meaning_filipino: Hindi lumulubog; nananatili sa ibabaw ng likido o sa himpapawid.
original_explanation: This is the state of being buoyant, either in water (like a beach body on a salbabida in Boracay) or in air (like dust particles you see in a sunbeam). Figuratively, it's how you feel after 3 cups of coffee and no sleep—your brain is just **nakalutang**. Or when you're so in love, "nakalutang sa alapaap" (floating in the clouds).
usage_notes: Can be used literally for objects in liquid/air, or figuratively for feelings of being dazed, spaced out, or euphoric.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang yelo ay **nakalutang** sa baso ng tubig.","translation":"The ice is **floating** in the glass of water."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam niya ay **nakalutang** siya sa saya nang manalo sa lotto.","translation":"He felt like he was **floating** with joy when he won the lottery."}]

translation: to pretend to be happy; to cause oneself to be pleased
meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang pagkilos o pagpapakita ng saya o katuwaan, na maaaring hindi tunay na nararamdaman, o ang paghahanap ng paraan upang sumaya.
original_explanation: This is your "itago sa ngiti" (hide it with a smile) moment. Like when your crush is talking about *their* crush, and you just have to sit there and **magpatuwa**, pretending you're happy for them. "Bes, okay ka lang?" "Oo naman! Super happy for you!" *cries internally*.
usage_notes: Can imply either genuinely trying to cheer oneself up or pretending to be happy for social reasons.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit malungkot siya, sinubukan niyang **magpatuwa** sa harap ng mga bata.","translation":"Even though she was sad, she tried to **act happy** in front of the children."},{"sentence":"Para malimutan ang problema, nagpunta siya sa mall para **magpatuwa**.","translation":"To forget her problems, she went to the mall to **cheer herself up**."}]

meaning_filipino: Pabayaan o sadyain na mahulog ang isang bagay nang may bigat at lakas; o bigyan ng bagsak na marka ang isang mag-aaral sa isang klase o pagsusulit.
etymology: From the prefix 'i-' (causative verb marker) and 'bagsak' (to fall; to fail).
original_explanation: Two meanings, both equally stressful. First, when you accidentally drop your phone (and your heart along with it). Second, the terror of every student: when your prof decides to **ibagsak** you in a subject. It's the ultimate 'game over' for the semester. Also applicable to governments.
usage_notes: Can be literal (dropping a physical object) or figurative (failing a student, overthrowing a government). The context determines the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ibagsak** ang mga prutas at baka magasgasan.","translation":"Don't **drop** the fruits as they might get bruised."},{"sentence":"Binalaan ng guro ang mga estudyante na **ibabagsak** niya ang sinumang mahuling nandadaya.","translation":"The teacher warned the students that she would **fail** anyone caught cheating."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng mariing pag-apak ng paa sa sahig o lupa, o ang pagtulak sa pedal gamit ang paa.
original_explanation: This is the move you make when you're super inis, like stomping your foot because the wifi is down again. It's also what you do to make the pedicab or your bike move—the forceful push on the pedal. It's the sound of frustration and the engine of leg-powered transportation rolled into one word.
usage_notes: Can refer to stomping in anger or frustration, or the act of pedaling a bicycle, tricycle, or similar vehicle.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang malakas na **pagpadyak** niya mula sa kabilang kwarto, mukhang galit.","translation":"I heard his loud **stomping** from the other room, it seems he's angry."},{"sentence":"Mabigat ang **pagpadyak** sa bisikleta kapag paakyat ng bundok.","translation":"The **pedaling** of the bicycle is heavy when going uphill."}]

translation: to be dragged along; to be pulled forcefully
meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang mahila o makaladkad nang may puwersa, karaniwan ay sa lupa o sahig.
original_explanation: Imagine being pulled somewhere you don't want to go. Like a kid having a tantrum being dragged by their mom out of the toy store, or you, being dragged by your friends to a third round of karaoke when you just want to go home. The `ma-` form means to be the one dragged. "Ayaw kong makadkad sa gulo."
usage_notes: This word describes being involuntarily dragged or pulled. The active form is `kumadkad` (to drag something). `Kinakadkad` (is being dragged), `kinadkad` (was dragged).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigla siyang **nakadkad** ng malakas na alon habang naliligo sa dagat.","translation":"He was suddenly **dragged along** by a strong wave while swimming in the sea."},{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang **makadkad** sa gulo kaya umalis na lang siya.","translation":"He didn't want to **be dragged** into the trouble so he just left."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghingi ng tulong pinansyal o materyal, tulad ng pagkain o pera, mula sa iba dahil sa kahirapan.
original_explanation: The "pa-victim" move, but for real. It's what you see on the streets when someone asks for "konting barya lang po." On a lighter note, it's what you jokingly do with your friends when you're broke before payday: "Penge 20, pang-jeep lang."
usage_notes: Can be used literally for begging on the streets, or hyperbolically among friends.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagbabawal ng ordinansa ang **pagpapalimos** sa mga lansangan.","translation":"The ordinance prohibits the **act of begging** on the streets."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapalimos** ay naging paraan niya para mabuhay araw-araw.","translation":"**Asking for alms** became his way to survive day by day."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong sumasailalim sa pagsasanay upang maging bihasa sa isang partikular na trabaho o kasanayan.
original_explanation: The 'newbie' in the office. The intern who gets the coffee. The padawan to the Jedi master. This is the person learning the ropes, making rookie mistakes, but hopefully on the path to becoming 'sanay' (the adjective).
usage_notes: This noun form is much less common than the adjective form or the verb 'sanayin'. The term 'nagsasanay' is more frequently used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga bagong **sanay** ay tinuturuan muna ng mga pangunahing alituntunin.","translation":"The new **trainees** are first taught the basic rules."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos o pananalitang nagpapakita ng matinding kawalan ng paggalang o pag-aalipusta sa Diyos, relihiyon, o anumang bagay na itinuturing na banal.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'walang galang' move against something holy. It's like posting a meme during the Simbang Gabi mass or making a joke that your lola would need holy water to recover from. Peak 'sacrilegious' behavior.
usage_notes: A formal and serious term, often used in legal or religious contexts. The root word 'lapastangan' means disrespectful or profane.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinuturing na isang malaking kasalanan ang **lapastangan sa relihiyon**.","translation":"**Blasphemy** is considered a grave sin."},{"sentence":"Kinasuhan siya ng **lapastangan sa relihiyon** dahil sa kanyang mga sinabi.","translation":"He was charged with **blasphemy** because of his statements."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, bagay, o pangyayari na nagdudulot ng abala, pagkainis, o gambala.
original_explanation: Yung kapitbahay mong nagvi-videoke ng "My Way" ng 3 AM. Yung kapatid mong pumapasok sa kwarto mo nang hindi kumakatok. Yung biglaang "urgent" meeting na sinet ng boss mo ng 4:55 PM on a Friday. Sila ang tunay na istorbo sa buhay.
usage_notes: Maaari ring gamitin bilang pandiwa (mang-istorbo) o pang-uri (nakaka-istorbo).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **istorbo** sa mga nag-aaral.","translation":"Don't be a **nuisance** to those who are studying."},{"sentence":"Malaking **istorbo** sa trapiko ang nasiraang trak.","translation":"The broken-down truck is a huge **disturbance** to the traffic."}]

meaning_filipino: Binaluktot ang katotohanan; hindi tapat o sadyang binago para manlinlang.
original_explanation: Think of it as 'fake news' before 'fake news' was a trending topic. When a story gets passed from one person to another and each one adds their own 'flavor', the final product is a **balikutsa** version of the truth. It's a twisted narrative, a misrepresentation for dramatic effect.
usage_notes: A formal and somewhat literary term for something that is intentionally twisted or distorted, especially information or truth.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang inilathalang kwento ay **balikutsa** at malayo sa tunay na nangyari.","translation":"The published story was **distorted** and far from what really happened."},{"sentence":"Iwinasto ng guro ang **balikutsa** na interpretasyon ng mag-aaral sa tula.","translation":"The teacher corrected the student's **misrepresented** interpretation of the poem."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging sanhi ng paghihintay ng isang tao; hindi pagdating o pag-aksyon sa takdang oras.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'Filipino time' power move. When you're running late, you text your friend, 'Pakisabi **papaghintayin** mo muna ako, 5 minutes pa!' even though you know it's 30. Also the favorite tactic of government agencies and slow Wi-Fi.
usage_notes: A very common causative verb. It implies causing someone else to be in a state of waiting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagalit siya dahil pinag-antay siya, pero hindi ko naman sinadyang **papaghintayin** siya.","translation":"He got mad because he was made to wait, but I didn't mean to **make him wait**."},{"sentence":"Pakiusap, huwag mo akong **papaghintayin** sa wala.","translation":"Please, don't **make me wait** for nothing."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pagkakaroon ng maraming maliliit na lubog, hukay, o butas sa isang ibabaw, tulad ng lupa o balat.
original_explanation: Describes a surface that looks like it has a bunch of mini-wells or craters. Think of a pockmarked face from past acne, the surface of the moon, or an unpaved 'lubak-lubak' road after a heavy rain. It's the 'before' picture in a skincare ad for acne scars.
usage_notes: Used to describe uneven surfaces, particularly skin or ground. 'Lubak-lubak' is a more common term for roads.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **balun-balon** ang kanyang mukha dahil sa bulutong-tubig noong bata pa siya.","translation":"His face became **pockmarked** because of chickenpox when he was young."},{"sentence":"**Balun-balon** ang daan papunta sa liblib na baryo.","translation":"The road to the remote village is **full of depressions**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong namumuhay sa labis na karalitaan at kadalasang umaasa sa limos mula sa ibang tao upang mabuhay.
etymology: Possibly from Spanish `pobre` (poor), which evolved in the local language.
original_explanation: The person you see on the street asking for 'barya lang po sa umaga'. It's the harsh reality of poverty personified. Can also be used hyperbolically when your friends ask you for money right before payday: 'Pasensya na, **pulubi** din ako ngayon.'
usage_notes: This is the standard and most common term for a beggar or an extremely poor person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagbigay ng pagkain ang ale sa batang **pulubi**.","translation":"The lady gave food to the young **beggar**."},{"sentence":"Mula sa pagiging **pulubi**, nagsikap siya at naging isang matagumpay na negosyante.","translation":"From being a **pauper**, he worked hard and became a successful businessman."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagliligtas mula sa kasalanan, pagkakamali, o isang mahirap na sitwasyon; ang pagbabayad para sa isang pagkukulang o pagkakautang.
original_explanation: This is what you're aiming for when you treat your friends to lunch after you messed up big time. It's the plot of every bida who starts as a kontrabida. In a religious sense, it's the ultimate "pag-ahon sa hirap." In a daily sense, it's that feeling of relief when you finally pay off your credit card debt or SpayLater balance. Freedom!
usage_notes: May matibay na konotasyong panrelihiyon (pagtubos mula sa kasalanan) ngunit ginagamit din sa mga sekular na konteksto (pagtubos mula sa utang, kabiguan, o masamang reputasyon).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para sa mga Kristiyano, ang pagkamatay ni Hesus sa krus ay para sa **katubusan** ng sangkatauhan.","translation":"For Christians, Jesus' death on the cross is for the **redemption** of mankind."},{"sentence":"Ang panalo niya sa huling laro ay tila **katubusan** para sa kanyang mga naunang pagkatalo.","translation":"His win in the final game felt like **redemption** for his previous losses."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat ng mga sasakyan o barko na sabay-sabay na naglalakbay, karaniwan para sa proteksyon o tulong sa isa't isa.
original_explanation: When a politician is late for a meeting and their fleet of black SUVs with wang-wang (sirens) parts the Red Sea of EDSA traffic. It's also what your barkada becomes when you go on a road trip with multiple cars, trying desperately not to lose each other at the toll gate.
usage_notes: Often associated with VIPs, military movements, or group travel.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang seguridad ng **komboy** ng presidente.","translation":"The president's **convoy** has tight security."},{"sentence":"Naiwan kami sa **komboy** dahil na-flat ang gulong namin.","translation":"We were left behind by the **convoy** because we got a flat tire."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang dahan-dahang pagmulat ng mga mata mula sa pagkakatulog; ang proseso ng paggising.
etymology: From 'pag-' (gerund prefix) + 'hi-' (intensive prefix) + 'himukas' (to awaken). 'Himukas' itself is from 'hi-' + 'mukas' (archaic term related to opening).
original_explanation: That groggy, blurry-eyed moment when you're not quite asleep but not fully awake yet. It's hitting the snooze button for the third time and your eyelids feel like they weigh 10 kilos each. The struggle between the dream world and the real world.
usage_notes: A more poetic or literary term for waking up. Not used in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kasabay ng **paghihimukas** ng araw ang kanyang pagbangon.","translation":"Along with the **awakening** of the day was his rising."},{"sentence":"Mabagal ang kanyang **paghihimukas** dahil sa sobrang pagod.","translation":"His **awakening** was slow due to extreme fatigue."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng muling pagbuo, pag-aayos, o pagbabalik sa dating kaayusan ng isang bagay na nasira o nawasak.
original_explanation: This is the 'bangon' (rise up) phase. After a super typhoon, a bad breakup, or a failed project, this is the act of picking up the pieces and starting over. It's the reconstruction of a city after a disaster or the rebuilding of trust in a relationship. It's the ultimate glow-up after a major setback.
usage_notes: A common phrase used in contexts of disaster recovery, infrastructure projects, and even personal or national recovery.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula na ang **pagtatayong muli** ng mga bahay na winasak ng bagyo.","translation":"The **rebuilding** of the houses destroyed by the typhoon has begun."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagtatayong muli** ng Marawi ay isang malaking hamon para sa gobyerno.","translation":"The **reconstruction** of Marawi is a big challenge for the government."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagkain na nagbibigay ng pakiramdam ng kaginhawaan o kasiyahan, kadalasan ay may kaugnayan sa mga alaala ng pagkabata o tahanan.
original_explanation: Pagkain na parang mainit na yakap. Ito 'yung hinahanap mo 'pag pagod ka, malungkot, o stressed galing sa trabaho. Hindi 'to pang-diet. Examples: sinigang na luto ni nanay, champorado 'pag umuulan, o 'yung paborito mong instant noodles.
usage_notes: Isang modernong konsepto na malawakang tinanggap sa kulturang Pilipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para sa akin, ang sinigang ang ultimate **comfort food**.","translation":"For me, sinigang is the ultimate **comfort food**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng **comfort food** ngayon, sobrang stressful ng araw ko.","translation":"I need **comfort food** right now, my day was so stressful."}]

meaning_filipino: Inapi, hinamak, o minaliit; nakararanas ng masamang pagtrato mula sa iba.
original_explanation: Feeling mo **alipusta** ka kapag ikaw na nga 'yung nag-organize ng group project, ikaw pa 'yung hindi sinama sa 'Thanks to' slide. It's that 'ginawa ko na lahat, pero ako pa rin ang masama' feeling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman niyang siya ay **alipusta** sa sarili niyang pamamahay.","translation":"She felt **scorned** in her own home."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging ganap, walang anumang kapintasan o pagkukulang. Lubos na perpekto.
original_explanation: This is that "perfect" level of something. Like, "pagkasakdal ng ganda," is beauty that's so flawless it could launch a thousand ships or at least get a million likes. It's the highest tier, the S-rank of qualities, the final form of 'galing'.
usage_notes: Often used to intensify an adjective, similar to 'very' or 'extremely', especially in a more formal or literary context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinahangaan niya ang **pagkasakdal** ng pagkakagawa ng obra maestra.","translation":"He admires the **perfection** of the masterpiece's creation."},{"sentence":"**Pagkasakdal** ganda ng tanawin sa Batanes.","translation":"The view in Batanes is **perfectly** beautiful."}]

meaning_filipino: Nakalatag o nakabuka; hindi nakatiklop o nakasara.
original_explanation: That feeling when you finally lay out your banig (mat) on the floor to sleep, or when you open a big map to see where you're going. 'Buklad' means laid open, flat, and exposed. It can be a book, a fan, a mat, or even your life story to your best friend after a few drinks.
usage_notes: Often used with objects that can be folded or rolled, like mats, maps, books, or fans. The verb form is 'ibuklad' (to spread out).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatulog siya sa sahig na **buklad** ang banig.","translation":"He fell asleep on the floor with the mat **spread out**."},{"sentence":"Laging **buklad** ang aklat sa kanyang mesa.","translation":"The book on his table is always **open**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkuha ng isang bagay o halaga bilang isang utang.
original_explanation: The verb for acquiring the actual thing you're borrowing. Kung ang 'utangan' ay 'yung tao (source), ang 'utangin' ay 'yung item (object). 'Plano kong utangin 'yung 5k mo.' This is the part where you specify what you need, from cash to your friend's Netflix password.
usage_notes: Focuses on the *object* or *amount* being borrowed. The object of the verb is the thing itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **utangin** ang librong hawak mo.","translation":"I want to **borrow** the book you're holding."},{"sentence":"Magkano ba ang kailangan mong **utangin**?","translation":"How much do you need to **borrow**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paraang nagpapanggap o hindi tunay; may pagkukunwari.
original_explanation: 'Yung sagot mong "Okay lang ako" pero deep inside, hindi talaga. You're answering pabalintiyak. It's the art of saying one thing but meaning the complete opposite, usually with a hint of sarcasm or drama. The official language of passive-aggressive people.
usage_notes: Often used to describe speech or actions that are not sincere.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"\"Sige, magpakasaya ka,\" sabi niya nang **pabalintiyak**.","translation":"\"Go on, have fun,\" she said **ironically**."},{"sentence":"Sumagot siya ng oo nang **pabalintiyak**, halata namang ayaw niya.","translation":"He answered yes **feignedly**, it was obvious he didn't want to."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa maraming bagay na may sukat na mas mababa kaysa karaniwan; kabaligtaran ng malalaki.
original_explanation: This is what you call your collection of Funko Pops, your many small utangs (debts), or the tiny pieces of your heart after a breakup. It's the plural form of 'maliit' (small). Perfect for describing a litter of puppies, a handful of coins, or the 'maliliit na bagay' that you shouldn't sweat.
usage_notes: The plural form of the adjective 'maliit' (small). It's used when describing multiple small things. It is often followed by 'na' when modifying a noun, e.g., 'maliliit na bata'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **maliliit** na isda ay mabilis lumangoy.","translation":"The **small** fish swim fast."},{"sentence":"Ingatan mo ang mga **maliliit** mong kapatid.","translation":"Take care of your **little** siblings."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang anyo ng enerhiya na nagreresulta mula sa pagkakaroon ng mga naka-charge na particle (tulad ng mga electron o proton).
original_explanation: The formal, science-class name for 'kuryente'. This is what you see on your Meralco bill. When there's a brownout, you don't have 'elektrisidad', which means no WiFi, no aircon, no Netflix. It's the invisible force that powers our modern lives and our rising blood pressure when the bill arrives.
usage_notes: While "elektrisidad" is the technically correct term, the word "kuryente" (from Spanish "corriente") is overwhelmingly more common in everyday spoken and written Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **elektrisidad** ay isang mahalagang bahagi ng modernong pamumuhay.","translation":"**Electricity** is an essential part of modern living."},{"sentence":"Nag-aaral sila kung paano makalikha ng **elektrisidad** mula sa solar power.","translation":"They are studying how to generate **electricity** from solar power."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panlabas na tuyong balat ng puno. Maaari ring tumukoy sa natutuklap na balat ng hayop o balat ng tao dahil sa paso o sakit.
original_explanation: The stuff you peel off a tree when you're bored. Also, the unfortunate result of forgetting to use sunscreen at the beach—that flaky, peeling stage of a sunburn. Or, when you're prepping fish for sinigang, the scales you scrape off are also a form of 'balakbak'.
usage_notes: Can refer to the bark of a tree, peeling skin (human or animal), or fish scales that have been removed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang **balakbak** ng puno bilang panggatong.","translation":"He used the **bark** of the tree as firewood."},{"sentence":"Natutuklap na ang **balakbak** ng kanyang balat dahil sa araw.","translation":"The **skin** on his back is already peeling because of the sun."}]

meaning_filipino: Suriing mabuti at ayusin ang isang makina o sistema upang maibalik sa pinakamainam na kondisyon.
original_explanation: This is what your tito does to the family's Tamaraw FX every weekend. It's the full-on, deep-clean, and repair of a machine, not just a quick fix. Think of it as a system-wide "reformat" for your car's engine or your company's entire workflow. "I-oberholin na natin 'tong project, bes, ang gulo na ng process."
usage_notes: Commonly used in automotive and mechanical contexts. The root word 'oberhol' is from the English 'overhaul'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **oberholin** ang makina ng dyip bago ito bumiyahe ulit.","translation":"The jeep's engine needs to be **overhauled** before it can travel again."},{"sentence":"Sabi ng mekaniko, mas mahal pa ang pagpapa-**oberholin** kaysa bumili ng bago.","translation":"The mechanic said that **overhauling** it would be more expensive than buying a new one."}]

translation: virginity; state of being a virgin
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging isang birhen; ang hindi pa nakakaranas ng pakikipagtalik.
original_explanation: In classic Filipino culture, this was treated like a rare, mythical treasure to be guarded at all costs, often discussed in hushed tones by titas at family gatherings. Today, it's a personal choice, but the cultural baggage is still there. It's the 'Maria Clara' ideal clashing with modern dating app realities. The word itself feels a bit formal and clinical, like something from a health class textbook.
usage_notes: A formal and somewhat clinical term. 'Pagiging birhen' is a more common conversational phrasing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa maraming konserbatibong kultura, binibigyan ng malaking halaga ang **pagkabirhen** ng isang babae.","translation":"In many conservative cultures, a woman's **virginity** is given great importance."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aatubili o pag-aalinlangan sa paggawa ng isang desisyon o aksyon; ang kawalan ng katiyakan kung itutuloy ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're about to click 'Add to Cart' on Lazada but your wallet is crying. That's you, `nagbabantulot`. It's the pause before you confess to your crush, or before you tell your mom you broke her favorite vase. It's the 'should I or shouldn't I?' dance in your head. Synonymous with 'mag-alinlangan' but with a more poetic, dramatic flair.
usage_notes: Conveys a sense of indecision or reluctance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magbantulot** na sabihin ang iyong tunay na nararamdaman.","translation":"Don't **hesitate** to say what you truly feel."},{"sentence":"**Nagbantulot** siyang tanggapin ang alok na trabaho dahil malayo ito sa kanyang pamilya.","translation":"She **hesitated** to accept the job offer because it was far from her family."}]

translation: to stake; to mark with a stake
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagbaon ng isang tulos o patpat sa lupa, karaniwan bilang pananda o suporta.
original_explanation: The OG way of claiming your territory. Before fences and 'No Trespassing' signs, you'd just stick a 'tulos' (stake) in the ground. It's what farmers do to guide their climbing plants, or what you do in your mind to claim that last piece of lechon at a party. 'That's mine. I've staked it.'
usage_notes: Related to agriculture, construction, or marking boundaries.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **tulusan** ang mga bagong tanim na kamatis para hindi ito bumagsak.","translation":"The newly planted tomatoes need **to be staked** so they don't fall over."},{"sentence":"**Tinulusan** niya ang apat na sulok ng lote bilang pananda.","translation":"He **marked with stakes** the four corners of the lot as a sign."}]

meaning_filipino: Kasalukuyang tumitindi ang kabilisan o nagiging mas matulin ang galaw.
original_explanation: Yung tibok ng puso mo kapag biglang nag-chat si crush. Or yung internet connection mo... never. This is the speed of gossip spreading in the office, or how fast your Grab fare increases during rush hour.
usage_notes: Present progressive tense of 'bilis' (speed). Indicates an ongoing increase in speed or rate.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumibilis** ang takbo ng sasakyan sa expressway.","translation":"The car **is accelerating** on the expressway."},{"sentence":"Habang papalapit ang deadline, **bumibilis** ang trabaho ng lahat.","translation":"As the deadline approaches, everyone's work **is getting faster**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkuha ng isang bagay mula sa sahig o sa mababang lugar gamit ang kamay.
etymology: Mula sa salitang "dampot" (pagpulot) at ang gitlaping "-um-".
original_explanation: Picking something up from the ground. Like when you drop your phone and your heart stops for a second before you dumampot to check for cracks. Or picking up chismis from the palengke.
usage_notes: Karaniwang tumutukoy sa pagkuha ng isang bagay mula sa ibaba.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dumampot** siya ng bato at ibinato ito sa ilog.","translation":"He **picked up** a stone and threw it into the river."},{"sentence":"Nakita niya ang nahulog na pitaka kaya agad siyang **dumampot** nito upang isauli.","translation":"She saw the fallen wallet so she immediately **picked it up** to return it."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ika-dalawampu't limang anibersaryo ng isang mahalagang kaganapan, karaniwan ay kasal o pagkakatatag ng isang organisasyon.
etymology: From kaarawan (anniversary/birthday, from 'araw' meaning 'day') + pilak (silver). A calque from the Western concept of a "silver anniversary".
original_explanation: The 25th-anniversary milestone. It's less about the silver and more about the "Wow, 25 years na kayo/tayo?" achievement unlocked. For couples, it's proof of surviving 25 years of choosing what to eat for dinner. For companies, it's 25 years of not going bankrupt. Either way, it calls for a celebration.
usage_notes: This is a set phrase. It specifically refers to the 25th anniversary. The root is 'araw' (day) for 'kaarawan', combined with 'pilak' (silver).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipagdiriwang ng aking mga magulang ang kanilang **kaarawang pilak** sa susunod na taon.","translation":"My parents will celebrate their **silver anniversary** next year."},{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng malaking salu-salo para sa **kaarawang pilak** ng aming kumpanya.","translation":"There was a big party for our company's **silver anniversary**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng lakas o kapangyarihan upang pilitin ang isang tao o bagay na gawin ang isang kilos, kadalasan labag sa kalooban nito.
original_explanation: When you try to make a size Small shirt fit, you pumuwersa it over your head. Also, when your mom makes you sing for the relatives at the party. You were forced. Pinilit.
usage_notes: This is the completed or past tense form of the verb. The infinitive is 'pumuwersa' and the present progressive is 'pumupuwersa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pumuwersa** ang magnanakaw na buksan ang pinto.","translation":"The thief **forced** the door open."},{"sentence":"**Pumuwersa** siyang pumasok sa kwarto kahit sarado.","translation":"He **forced** his way into the room even though it was closed."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng prutas na may kayumangging balat, bilog o hugis-itlog, at may matamis na laman.
etymology: From Spanish 'chico' or 'chicozapote', which itself is from Nahuatl 'tzapotl'.
original_explanation: That brown, gritty-skinned fruit that looks like a small potato. When you open it, it's super sweet and has a texture like a pear mixed with brown sugar. Don't eat the shiny black seeds unless you want an unexpected trip to the ER.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito ni lola ang **tsiko** bilang panghimagas.","translation":"Grandma's favorite dessert is **sapodilla**."},{"sentence":"Matamis ang mga **tsiko** na nabili ko sa palengke.","translation":"The **sapodillas** I bought from the market are sweet."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng kawalan ng kaayusan dahil sa pagkawala o hindi pagkilala sa awtoridad o pamahalaan. Isang teoryang pampulitika na nagtataguyod ng lipunang walang estado.
etymology: Hiram sa Espanyol na "anarquía," mula sa Griyegong "anarkhia" (kawalan ng pinuno).
original_explanation: The more formal, textbook version of anarki. This is the word your Araling Panlipunan teacher would use. It's the political theory that says we'd all be better off without a government, which sounds great until you remember you need someone to collect the garbage and fix the potholes.
usage_notes: Mas pormal at akademiko kaysa sa varyant na "anarki."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan sa pilosopiyang pampulitika ang konsepto ng **anarkya**.","translation":"The concept of **anarchy** is studied in political philosophy."},{"sentence":"Ang pagbagsak ng pamahalaan ay maaaring humantong sa **anarkya**.","translation":"The fall of the government could lead to **anarchy**."}]

translation: to be covered in wounds; to have multiple wounds
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng marami at kalat-kalat na sugat sa katawan.
etymology: From `magka-` + reduplication of `sugat`. The reduplication signifies plurality or intensity.
original_explanation: This is the leveled-up version of `magkasugat`. It's not just one wound, it's a whole collection. This is you after attempting a new TikTok dance challenge, falling down the stairs, or getting into a fight with a rose bush. You look like you just came from an action movie scene you didn't win.
usage_notes: The repetition of "sugat" emphasizes that there are many wounds, not just one.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagkasugat-sugat** ang kanyang mga binti dahil sa kagat ng mga lamok.","translation":"His legs **were covered in wounds** from mosquito bites."},{"sentence":"Dinala sa ospital ang biktima dahil **nagkasugat-sugat** ito sa buong katawan.","translation":"The victim was brought to the hospital because he **had multiple wounds** all over his body."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa dalawa o higit pang lokasyon o bagay na may parehong distansya mula sa isang punto ng reperensya.
original_explanation: Yung LDR niyo ng ka-chat mo sa Singapore at yung LDR ng friend mo sa ka-chat niya sa Dubai. Parehong malayo, parehong masakit. It means being equally far apart. Or when you realize that from your house, the nearest Jollibee and the nearest McDo are magkasinlayo. The struggle is real.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mula sa Maynila, ang Baguio at ang Naga ay hindi **magkasinlayo**.","translation":"From Manila, Baguio and Naga are not **of the same distance**."},{"sentence":"Ang bahay namin at ang bahay niya ay **magkasinlayo** mula sa paaralan.","translation":"Our house and his house are **equidistant** from the school."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbukas ng bibig, karaniwan upang magsalita, kumain, o magpakita ng pagkagulat.
original_explanation: The default state when you hear the latest chismis. It's what the dentist tells you to do, and what you do when you see the bill for your Grab ride during a surge. Also, the first step to eating a whole lechon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ngumanga** siya para subuan ng doktor ng gamot.","translation":"He **opened his mouth** for the doctor to give him medicine."},{"sentence":"Napa-**nganga** na lang ako sa ganda ng tanawin.","translation":"I was left with my **mouth agape** at the beauty of the scenery."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hayop na natural na nanghuhuli at kumakain ng ibang hayop (ang biktima nito) upang mabuhay.
etymology: From the root word "sila" (prey). The ma- and -n- prefix/infix combination creates an agent noun, "one who preys".
original_explanation: In the wild, it's the lion chasing the gazelle. In the office, it's that person who "borrows" your lunch from the fridge. A 'maninila' is a predator, something that hunts. It can also be used figuratively for someone who preys on the weak or unsuspecting, like a scammer or a political opportunist.
usage_notes: The root 'sila' in this context means 'prey' and is different from 'sila' (they).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang agila ay isang kilalang **maninila** na kumakain ng mga ahas at maliliit na mamalya.","translation":"The eagle is a known **predator** that eats snakes and small mammals."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa mga **maninila** sa internet na nambibiktima ng mga walang muwang.","translation":"Be careful of **predators** on the internet who victimize the naive."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng puno (Ceiba pentandra) na nagbubunga ng mga hiblang mala-bulak na ginagamit bilang palaman sa mga unan, kutson, at iba pa.
original_explanation: This is the OG memory foam. Before Uratex and Tempur-Pedic, our lolas had unan and kutson filled with kapok. It's the cotton-like fluff from a tree. Kinda lumpy, but hey, it was organic!
usage_notes: Refers to both the tree and its cotton-like fiber.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gawa sa **kapok** ang luma naming unan.","translation":"Our old pillow is made of **kapok**."},{"sentence":"Mataas ang puno ng **kapok** sa likod-bahay.","translation":"The **kapok** tree in the backyard is tall."}]

translation: the act of hammering; pounding; striking
meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit na paghampas o pagpalo sa isang bagay, karaniwang gamit ang martilyo o katulad na kagamitan.
etymology: From `pag-` + `pukpok`. `Pukpok` means to hammer or strike.
original_explanation: The sound your kapitbahay makes at 7 AM on a Sunday morning while fixing his roof. It’s the action you use on a stubborn crab shell, a nail that won't go in straight, or your keyboard when your code has a bug you can't find. It's a percussive expression of either creation or frustration.
usage_notes: Often implies a repetitive, forceful action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ingay ng **pagpukpok** mula sa ginagawang bahay ay rinig sa buong kalye.","translation":"The sound of **hammering** from the house under construction could be heard down the whole street."},{"sentence":"Kinakailangan ng maingat na **pagpukpok** upang mabuo ang tansong plake.","translation":"Careful **pounding** is required to form the bronze plaque."}]

meaning_filipino: May ugali o inklinasyon na mang-agaw o kumuha ng yaman ng iba sa pamamagitan ng dahas o puwersa.
original_explanation: Think pirates, but in the modern world. Ito 'yung mga corrupt na politiko, mga scammer na nang-aagaw ng ipon mo, o kahit 'yung kumpanyang sobrang baba magpasahod pero limpak-limpak ang kita. Sila 'yung mga **mapandambong** na legal (minsan).
usage_notes: A strong, formal word, often used in political or historical contexts to describe conquerors, corrupt officials, or exploitative entities.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **mapandambong** na mananakop ay kinuha ang lahat ng ginto sa bayan.","translation":"The **predatory** conquerors took all the gold in the town."},{"sentence":"Dapat parusahan ang mga opisyal na **mapandambong** sa kaban ng bayan.","translation":"Officials who are **prone to plundering** the nation's treasury must be punished."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matinding pagbabanggaan o sagupaan ng dalawa o higit pang bagay; maaari ring tumukoy sa isang awayan o rambulan.
original_explanation: That moment when two jeepneys try to occupy the same space at the same time. Also, the epic showdown you see in action movies, or that intense argument between Marites and her rival chismosa. It's a clash, a bang, a full-on 'Here comes the boom!' moment.
usage_notes: Salpukan emphasizes the intensity and impact of the collision or conflict, more so than the simpler 'banggaan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging viral ang video ng **salpakan** ng dalawang motorsiklo sa EDSA.","translation":"The video of the **collision** between two motorcycles on EDSA went viral."},{"sentence":"Inaasahan ang matinding **salpakan** ng mga bida at kontrabida sa finale ng teleserye.","translation":"An intense **clash** between the protagonists and antagonists is expected in the soap opera's finale."}]

meaning_filipino: Nangangahulugang kaawa-awa; isang ekspresyon ng pagkaawa o pagkalungkot para sa isang tao o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: Short for "kawawa." Ito yung sinasabi mo sa kaibigan mong na-ghost na naman, o sa sarili mo habang tinitingnan ang laman ng wallet mo bago mag-sweldo. "Hala, wawa naman."
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa kolokyal at impormal na pananalita. Kadalasan itong may kasamang 'naman'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naiwan siyang mag-isa sa party, **wawa** naman.","translation":"He was left alone at the party, **poor thing**."},{"sentence":"**Wawa** ka naman, basang-basa ka ng ulan.","translation":"You're so **pitiful**, you're soaked from the rain."}]

meaning_filipino: Salaping yari sa papel na may tiyak na halaga, na inisyu ng pamahalaan o bangko sentral.
etymology: From Spanish 'cuarta' (a former Spanish coin) which evolved into the Tagalog 'kuwalta' (money) + 'papel' (paper).
original_explanation: Literally 'paper money.' This is the stuff you hopefully get on payday, not the barya (coins) you use for pamasahe. The kind that folds, not jingles. The blue one (1000 pesos) is everyone's favorite color.
usage_notes: Compound noun. 'Kuwarta' is often used interchangeably with 'pera'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas gusto niyang magbayad gamit ang **kuwaltang papel** kaysa barya.","translation":"He prefers to pay with **paper money** rather than coins."},{"sentence":"Naubos agad ang mga bagong **kuwaltang papel** na inilabas niya sa ATM.","translation":"The new **banknotes** he withdrew from the ATM were spent immediately."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang biruan, komento, o pag-uugali na luma, hindi nakakatawa, at pilit.
etymology: From English 'corny', possibly reinforced by the word for corn, 'mais'. A form of code-switching that became a word.
original_explanation: The official term for your tito's jokes or that pickup line you heard from a 90s movie. It's when someone tries to be funny but it just lands with a thud. "Stop it with the puns, ang **mais** mo!" Derived from the English word 'corny', not the plant.
usage_notes: A slang term that has become mainstream.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumigil ka na nga sa mga pickup line mo, sobrang **mais**!","translation":"Stop with your pickup lines already, they're so **corny**!"},{"sentence":"Tawa na lang tayo sa joke niya kahit **mais**.","translation":"Let's just laugh at his joke even if it's **corny**."}]

translation: to be overturned; to be defeated (unexpectedly)
meaning_filipino: Mabaligtad o tumaob, lalo na ang mga sasakyang-dagat. Sa matalinhagang gamit, nangangahulugang matalo o malupig, lalo na ang isang itinuturing na mas malakas o nakalalamang.
etymology: ma- (unintentional/ability prefix) + pa- (causative prefix) + taob (overturned, upside down)
original_explanation: Literally, this is what happens to a boat in a storm. Figuratively, it’s the ultimate underdog story. It's when the "dehado" (underdog) team beats the defending champion in a basketball game. "Akala nila sigurado na ang panalo, pero napatáob sila ng baguhang team!" It’s the David vs. Goliath verb.
usage_notes: Used for both literal capsizing and figurative upsets in competitions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Napatáob** ng malalaking alon ang maliit na bangka.","translation":"The small boat **was overturned** by the big waves."},{"sentence":"Isang malaking sorpresa nang **mapatáob** ng Pilipinas ang mas malakas na koponan ng Tsina.","translation":"It was a big surprise when the Philippines **defeated** the stronger Chinese team."}]

translation: to be reduced; to be lessened
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbaba o pagliit ng dami, bilang, o tindi ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: 'Yung sweldo mo, parang magic. Isang bayad lang ng bills, mabawasan agad! It’s that feeling when your phone's battery life, your patience, or your bank account gets smaller.
usage_notes: The object being reduced is the subject of the sentence (actor-focus).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **mabawasan** na ang trapik sa EDSA.","translation":"I hope the traffic on EDSA will **be reduced**."},{"sentence":"**Nabawasan** ang aking mga alalahanin nang makausap kita.","translation":"My worries **were lessened** when I talked to you."}]

translation: to fit perfectly; to land on; to be flush against
meaning_filipino: Eksaktong tumama o dumikit sa isang ibabaw nang walang puwang; umayon nang husto.
original_explanation: That super satisfying feeling when a lid closes perfectly on a container, or when two pieces of a puzzle click together. It's the perfect fit. It can also mean to land on something, like how your back lumapat on your bed after a long day at work. Ah, a perfect match.
usage_notes: Can be used for physical objects fitting together, a hand landing on a surface, or even abstract ideas aligning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lumapat** nang husto ang takip sa lalagyan kaya hindi ito natapon.","translation":"The lid **fit perfectly** on the container so it didn't spill."},{"sentence":"Pagod na pagod siya kaya't pag-uwi ay agad **lumapat** ang likod niya sa kama.","translation":"He was so tired that as soon as he got home, his back immediately **landed on** the bed."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan kinakatay ang mga hayop tulad ng baka, baboy, at manok para sa konsumo ng tao.
original_explanation: The place where your lechon, crispy pata, and beef steak begin their journey to your plate. It's the animal kingdom's version of a final boss level. Not for the faint of heart, and definitely not a first date spot.
usage_notes: A direct loanword from Spanish. The native Tagalog term is 'katayan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala ang mga baboy sa **matadero** bago ipamahagi ang karne sa palengke.","translation":"The pigs were brought to the **slaughterhouse** before the meat was distributed to the market."},{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang inspeksyon ng gobyerno sa mga **matadero** para sa kaligtasan ng publiko.","translation":"Government inspection in **abattoirs** is strict for public safety."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang unang bahagi ng araw, mula sa pagsikat ng araw hanggang tanghali.
original_explanation: The time of day powered by pandesal and kape. It's when you promise yourself you'll be productive, before the EDSA traffic or a slow internet connection crushes your soul. It’s the 'Good morning, ma'am/sir!' energy before the 3 PM slump hits.
usage_notes: Often used in greetings like 'Magandang umaga' (Good morning).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaga akong gumising kaninang **umaga**.","translation":"I woke up early this **morning**."},{"sentence":"Kape at pandesal ang karaniwang almusal tuwing **umaga**.","translation":"Coffee and pandesal are the usual breakfast every **morning**."}]

translation: to pierce through, to meet at a point
meaning_filipino: Ang pagdaan nang tuluyan at paglabas sa kabilang dulo; ang pagtatagpo ng dalawang dulo upang magkabit.
original_explanation: Medyo deep 'to. Imagine sinulid na **tumagpos** sa butas ng karayom. O kaya dalawang tunnel na hinuhukay from opposite ends, tapos nagkita sa gitna—**tumagpos** sila. It has a sense of successful connection or penetration, reaching the other side. It’s like 'tumagos' but with a feeling of completion or meeting.
usage_notes: This is a very literary or archaic word, often used in poetry or classical literature. It is the completed aspect (past tense).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang palaso ay **tumagpos** sa kanyang dibdib.","translation":"The arrow **pierced through** his chest."},{"sentence":"Sa wakas ay **tumagpos** din ang sinulid sa karayom.","translation":"At last, the thread finally **went through** the needle."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sangay ng agham na sumasaklaw sa pag-aaral ng kalikasan, materya, enerhiya, at mga interaksyon nito.
original_explanation: The 'Filipinized' word for Physics. You'll probably only see this in a K-12 textbook or during a very formal Buwan ng Wika event. In real life, everyone just says 'Physics'. But hey, if you want to sound deep and patriotic while talking about gravity, **liknayan** is your word.
usage_notes: Isang salitang akademiko at pormal na bihirang gamitin sa pang-araw-araw na usapan. Ang salitang hiram na "pisika" (physics) ang mas karaniwan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan sa **liknayan** ang mga batas ng mosyon ni Newton.","translation":"Newton's laws of motion are studied in **physics**."},{"sentence":"Nahihirapan ako sa aming klase sa **liknayan**.","translation":"I am having a hard time in our **physics** class."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na isinilang at lumaki sa matinding kahirapan.
etymology: Mula sa "anak" (child) at "dalita" (matinding hirap o pagdurusa).
original_explanation: The protagonist of 90% of Filipino dramas. Born poor, probably selling sampaguita in the streets, but has a heart of gold and will eventually discover they're the long-lost heir to a hacienda. It's a very literary, dramatic term for someone from a humble background.
usage_notes: Lubhang pampanitikan at matulain. Hindi ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kuwento ni Cinderella ay tungkol sa isang **anak-dalita** na naging prinsesa.","translation":"The story of Cinderella is about **one born into poverty** who became a princess."}]

translation: to be able to cover or press against
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang takpan o idiin ang isang bagay, karaniwan gamit ang palad, sa isang partikular na lugar.
original_explanation: That reflex action when you hear a shocking chismis (gossip) and you 'makatutop' your mouth with your hand. Or when you have a sudden headache and you 'makatutop' your forehead. It's the ability to cover, press, or place a hand (or something similar) firmly against a surface.
usage_notes: 'Tutop' often implies using the palm of the hand. It's a very specific action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang gulat, 'di niya napigilang **makatutop** ng bibig.","translation":"Due to extreme shock, she couldn't help but **be able to cover** her mouth."},{"sentence":"Nang sumakit ang kanyang dibdib, agad siyang **nakatutop** dito.","translation":"When his chest hurt, he immediately **was able to press against** it."}]

translation: being cherished; being singled out (as special)
meaning_filipino: Pagbibigay ng natatanging pagtingin o pagpapahalaga sa isang tao o bagay; pagiging bukod-tangi.
original_explanation: This is how your lola sees her 'paboritong apo' (favorite grandchild). You are the 'itinatangi', the special one who gets extra allowance and the biggest piece of chicken. It's about being held in special regard, the chosen one, the MVP of the family or barkada.
usage_notes: Present progressive tense of 'itangi'. Carries a very positive and special connotation of being prized or held dear.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **itinatangi** kong kaibigan sa lahat.","translation":"She is my most **cherished** friend of all."},{"sentence":"Ang pagmamahal ng ina ay isang bagay na **itinatangi** habambuhay.","translation":"A mother's love is something **cherished** for a lifetime."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay o grupo ng mga bagay na pinagsama-sama at binalot, karaniwan sa papel o tela, upang madaling dalhin o itago.
original_explanation: Your takeout from the resto, your pasalubong from a trip, or the 'pabaon' your tita insists you take home after a fiesta. It's basically anything wrapped up to go. "Paki-balutan mo na lang 'yung afritada, 'nay."
usage_notes: Can also refer to a 'doggy bag' in a restaurant context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dala mo ba ang **balutan** ng mga damit para sa donasyon?","translation":"Did you bring the **bundle** of clothes for donation?"},{"sentence":"Iuwi mo itong **balutan** ng pagkain para sa pamilya mo.","translation":"Take this **package** of food home for your family."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang babae na may katangiang mapagmahal, sentimental, o nagpapakita ng pag-ibig sa paraang katulad ng sa mga kuwentong romansa.
etymology: From Spanish 'romántica', the feminine form of 'romántico'.
original_explanation: She's the type who cries during movie proposals, loves receiving flowers for no reason, and probably has a secret Pinterest board for her dream wedding. She believes in 'The One' and isn't afraid of a little drama for the sake of love. The female counterpart to 'romantiko'.
usage_notes: This is the feminine form. The masculine form is 'romantiko'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sadyang **romantika** si Maria, laging may dalang bulaklak para sa kanyang ina.","translation":"Maria is truly **romantic**, always bringing flowers for her mother."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na gumagabay, pumapatnubay, o umaalalay sa iba, lalo na sa paglakad sa pamamagitan ng paghawak sa kamay o braso.
original_explanation: Your human Waze. The person who holds your hand to cross the chaotic streets of Manila. Can also be a mentor who guides you in life, your 'tagaakay sa tamang landas'.
usage_notes: Ang unlaping 'taga-' ay nagpapahiwatig ng isang taong gumaganap ng aksyon. Ang 'akay' ay ang pag-alalay sa paglakad.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang matanda ay nangailangan ng **tagaakay** para makatawid sa kalsada.","translation":"The old person needed a **guide** to cross the street."},{"sentence":"Siya ang nagsilbing **tagaakay** ng mga bulag na bata.","translation":"She served as the **guide** for the blind children."}]

translation: to tilt; to lean; to take a side
meaning_filipino: Pagpanig o pagbigay-suporta sa isang tao, bagay, o pananaw; pagtagilid o paghilig ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: Eto 'yung moment na sa gitna ng away ng dalawa mong kaibigan, kailangan mong mamili kung kanino ka kakampi. 'Yung pagpili mo, 'yun ang pag-kiling mo. Pwede ring literal, like 'yung tore ng Pisa, kumikiling. Or 'yung puso mo, kumikiling sa taong 'di ka naman pinapansin. Hugot!
usage_notes: Can be used both literally for physical tilting and figuratively for taking a side in an argument or issue.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa huli, **kumiling** ang hurado sa panig ng nasasakdal.","translation":"In the end, the jury **sided** with the defendant."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa malakas na hangin, **kumiling** ang puno ng niyog.","translation":"Because of the strong wind, the coconut tree **tilted**."}]

translation: by jumping; in a jumping manner
meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pagkilos na ginagawa sa pamamagitan ng pagtalon o paglukso.
etymology: From pa- prefix + lukso (jump). The pa- prefix indicates manner.
original_explanation: How you cross a muddy street during rainy season to avoid the 'putik' splash. It's the adverb for your heart when you get a 'good morning' text from your crush.
usage_notes: Describes an action done by means of jumping. 'Lukso' is often a smaller jump than 'lundag'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinakasan niya ang aso nang **palukso** sa bakod.","translation":"He escaped the dog **by jumping** over the fence."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mensahe, balita, o utos na ipinapatala o ipinapasabi sa isang tao upang maiparating sa iba.
original_explanation: The OG "DM" (Direct Message) before the internet existed. It’s when you tell a friend, "Pakisabi kay ano..." (Please tell so-and-so...). A pasabi is the information that travels through the human-powered network of chismis, office assistants, or your younger sibling who you bribed with candy.
usage_notes: Refers to the message itself, not the act of telling. The verb form is `pasabihan`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **pasabi** si nanay, umuwi ka raw nang maaga.","translation":"Mom sent a **message**, she said you should come home early."},{"sentence":"Iniwan ko lang ang **pasabi** sa guwardiya.","translation":"I just left the **message** with the guard."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyon na nagpapahiwatig ng kawalan ng paniniwala, pagdududa, o pag-aalinlangan sa sinabi ng isang tao.
etymology: Pinaniniwalaang pinaikling anyo ng pariralang "hindi nga?".
original_explanation: The shortest and most effective way to call out someone's bluff. It's the Pinoy version of "Yeah, right" or "I call BS." Sagot mo sa kaibigan mong sinabing "magda-diet na ako bukas."
usage_notes: Highly colloquial. The full phrase is "Weh, 'di nga?". The tone is crucial in conveying the level of disbelief.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Manlilibre daw siya? **Weh**?","translation":"He said he'll treat us? **Really**?"},{"sentence":"A: 'Tapos ko na lahat ng trabaho ko.' B: '**Weh**!?'","translation":"A: 'I've finished all my work.' B: '**No way**!?'"}]

translation: to object; to protest; to oppose
meaning_filipino: Nagpapahayag ng hindi pagsang-ayon o pagkontra sa isang bagay, pasya, o ideya.
original_explanation: This is what you do when your parents say "bawal lumabas" but all your friends are going out. It's the verbal equivalent of a protest rally, often done during family meetings or when the team lead suggests another "urgent" weekend task. "I object, your honor!"
usage_notes: Past/Completed aspect of the verb. The present tense is 'tumututol'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumutol** ang mga empleyado sa bagong patakaran ng kumpanya.","translation":"The employees **objected** to the new company policy."},{"sentence":"Bakit ka **tumutol** sa mungkahi ko kahapon?","translation":"Why did you **oppose** my suggestion yesterday?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, bata man o matanda, na bininyagan o kinumpilan na mayroong ninong o ninang bilang espirituwal na gabay.
original_explanation: Ito yung reason kung bakit may aguinaldo ka tuwing Pasko. Sila yung mga bata (o 'di na masyadong bata) na kinuha ka ng magulang nila para maging second parent. Responsibilidad mo silang i-guide sa buhay... at bigyan ng regalo. Kapag nakita mo sila, ang unang tanong ay "Asan ang regalo ko, Ninong/Ninang?"
usage_notes: Refers to both godson and goddaughter. The person who acts as the godparent is the 'ninong' (godfather) or 'ninang' (godmother).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing Pasko, dinadalaw ako ng aking mga **inaanak**.","translation":"Every Christmas, my **godchildren** visit me."},{"sentence":"Malaki na ang **inaanak** ko, magtatapos na ng kolehiyo.","translation":"My **godchild** is all grown up, about to graduate from college."}]

translation: to be harmed; to meet with disaster
meaning_filipino: Maging biktima ng kapahamakan, sakuna, o anumang masamang pangyayari.
original_explanation: Basically, to get rekt. If you ignore the 'Bawal Tumawid, May Namatay na Dito' sign and a speeding bus comes at you, you are about to **maparool**. It’s the universe’s way of saying “I told you so.” It’s getting into an accident or any form of harm.
usage_notes: Often used in warnings or to describe unfortunate events. Synonymous with 'mapahamak'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa pagmamaneho nang hindi ka **maparool**.","translation":"Drive carefully so you won't **be harmed**."},{"sentence":"Sana'y walang **maparool** sa paparating na bagyo.","translation":"I hope no one gets **harmed** in the coming typhoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahabang kasuotan, karaniwang itim, na isinusuot ng mga pari at iba pang kleriko.
original_explanation: Yung long-sleeved, floor-length na damit ng pari, parang black version ng gown ni Elsa pero pang-simbahan. Hindi ito ang OOTD mo sa mall, unless may theme party na 'Holy Chic'.
usage_notes: Karaniwang tumutukoy sa kasuotan ng mga paring Katoliko.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malinis at plantsado ang **sutana** ng pari bago ang misa.","translation":"The priest's **cassock** was clean and ironed before the mass."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maanghang na bunga o gulay na karaniwang ginagamit bilang pampalasa sa pagluluto.
original_explanation: The official fruit of Bicol and the reason you keep asking for extra water. It's that kick in your sisig, the 'hot' in Bicol Express, and what your toxic ex is full of. Red sili for a fiery relationship, green for 'are we or are we not?'
usage_notes: The two most common types are 'siling labuyo' (small, very hot) and 'siling haba' or 'siling pangsigang' (long green chili).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagdagdag siya ng maraming **sili** sa Bicol Express kaya sobrang anghang.","translation":"She added a lot of **chili** to the Bicol Express, so it's extra spicy."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hawakan ang mata mo pagkatapos humawak ng **sili**!","translation":"Don't touch your eyes after handling **chili**!"}]

translation: the manner/act of having sold something
meaning_filipino: Ang paraan o resulta ng matagumpay na pagbebenta ng isang produkto o serbisyo.
etymology: A complex formation from the root 'bili' (buy/sell). 'Pagbili' is buying, 'pagbebenta' is selling. 'Pagkakapagbili' focuses on the successful completion and manner of the sale.
original_explanation: This is the feeling of relief when you finally sell that old phone on Carousell. It's not about the *act* of selling ('pagbebenta'), but the *fact* or *manner* that it has been sold. 'Kumusta ang pagkakapagbili mo ng kotse?' (How did the sale of your car go?). It's all about the outcome.
usage_notes: This word emphasizes the result and circumstances of a sale. It answers the question 'How was it sold?' or 'What was the result of the sale?'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis ang **pagkakapagbili** ng mga tiket para sa konsiyerto.","translation":"The **selling** of the tickets for the concert was fast."},{"sentence":"Ikinatuwa ng ahente ang **pagkakapagbili** niya ng mamahaling bahay.","translation":"The agent was pleased with **his act of having sold** the expensive house."}]

translation: to act beastly; to behave inhumanly
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkilos na walang pakundangan, marahas, o hindi makatao, na maihahalintulad sa gawi ng isang hayop.
original_explanation: When someone's behavior goes from 'walang modo' (no manners) to full-on savage. This is for actions that are cruel, wild, or completely uncivilized. Think of someone cutting a long queue, a politician's blatant corruption, or a fight breaking out over the last piece of lechon. It's a strong condemnation of someone's character.
usage_notes: A very strong and insulting term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula siyang **mag-asal-hayop** nang malasing siya sa party.","translation":"He started **to act beastly** when he got drunk at the party."},{"sentence":"Hindi makatao ang **mag-asal-hayop** sa kapwa mo.","translation":"It is inhumane **to behave inhumanly** towards your fellow person."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hugis ng buwan sa unang bahagi nito kung kailan ito'y manipis at kurbado na parang isang suklay o karit.
etymology: From 'buwan' (moon) and 'gasuklay' (sickle-shaped, like a 'suklay' or comb).
original_explanation: This is the 'diet' version of the moon, just a sliver. It's the emoji you use when you're feeling mysterious or sleepy (🌙). It's also a classic design for pendants and earrings, and the shape of that delicious 'pan de coco' sometimes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakagandang pagmasdan ang **buwang gasuklay** sa maaliwalas na kalangitan.","translation":"It's so beautiful to watch the **crescent moon** in the clear sky."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paraang hindi totoo at naglalayong manlinlang o magpanggap; pagkukunwari.
original_explanation: The official word for 'kunwari lang' or 'acting-acting lang.' It's your friend being 'pakunwari' na galit but is actually just joking. It's the 'I'm okay' you text when you're definitely not okay. It’s the art of the poker face, Filipino style.
usage_notes: Can also function as an adjective (pang-uri), as in 'isang pakunwaring ngiti' (a feigned smile).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pakunwari** siyang natutulog para hindi mautusan.","translation":"He **pretended** to be asleep so he wouldn't be asked to do errands."},{"sentence":"Ang paghingi niya ng tawad ay **pakunwari** lamang.","translation":"His apology was just **for show**."}]

translation: to be fond of each other
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita ng pagmamahal, pag-aaruga, at paglalambing sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang tao.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'sana all.' It's the vibe between a new couple who can't keep their hands off each other, or your lolo and lola who are still sweet after 50 years. It's mutual affection in action. Think of it as the verb form of #RelationshipGoals.
usage_notes: This is a reciprocal verb, implying the action is done between the subjects.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bagong kasal ay laging nakikitang **naggigiliwan** sa parke.","translation":"The newlyweds are always seen **being affectionate with each other** at the park."},{"sentence":"Sana'y matuto kayong **maggiliwan** bilang magkapatid.","translation":"I hope you learn to **be fond of each other** as siblings."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pariralang naglalarawan sa isang bagay na may sukat o laki na higit pa sa inaasahan o sa naunang nabanggit.
original_explanation: When you order "large" fries but what arrives is a bucket. That's lalong malaki. It's the feeling of seeing a problem you thought was manageable, only to discover its true, massive scale. "Akala ko utang lang, 'yun pala may interes pa, kaya lalong malaki ang problema." It's the "plus ultra" of size.
usage_notes: A comparative adjectival phrase.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bahay na ito ay malaki na, ngunit ang hardin sa likod ay **lalong malaki**.","translation":"This house is already big, but the garden at the back is **even bigger**."},{"sentence":"Ang responsibilidad ng isang manager ay **lalong malaki** kaysa sa isang staff.","translation":"A manager's responsibility is **much larger** than a staff's."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panlabas na anyo, istilo ng pananamit, o kabuuang ayos ng isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: Your OOTD (Outfit Of The Day). When someone says 'Ang ganda ng porma mo,' they're complimenting your whole look—the clothes, the shoes, the confidence. It's all about how you present yourself. Someone who is 'pumoporma' is trying to look good, often to impress someone. It's the physical manifestation of 'slay.'
usage_notes: Can also be a verb 'pumorma' (to get dressed up, to pose, to make a move on someone).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging ang ganda ng **porma** ni Anna kapag pumapasok sa opisina.","translation":"Anna's **outfit** is always great whenever she comes to the office."},{"sentence":"Simpleng **porma** lang ang gusto ko, T-shirt at maong.","translation":"I just want a simple **style**, a T-shirt and jeans."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagdagdag sa haba o sukat; ang pagiging mas mahaba kaysa sa dating kalagayan.
original_explanation: Yung kwentuhan niyo na "sandali lang" pero inabot na ng madaling araw. O kaya 'yung pila sa government office, parang walang katapusan, humaba nang humaba. Ganyan din yung listahan ng 'things to do' mo tuwing Lunes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Humaba** ang buhok niya matapos ang isang taon.","translation":"Her hair **lengthened** after a year."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa traffic, **humaba** ang aming biyahe papuntang probinsya.","translation":"Because of the traffic, our trip to the province **became longer**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng mineral na iron oxide (Fe2O3) na karaniwang kulay itim, pilak-abo, kayumanggi, o mamula-mulang kayumanggi, at pangunahing pinagkukunan ng bakal.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "hematites," mula sa Latin na "haematites," mula sa Griyegong "haimatitēs lithos" (batong kulay dugo).
original_explanation: This is the scientific name for a type of rock, not something you'd hear at the palengke unless you're buying a pampaswerte bracelet made of it. It's the rock that gives Mars its 'Red Planet' branding. Think of it as the Earth's rusty blush.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa mga akademikong konteksto, lalo na sa heolohiya at kemistri.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakahanap ang mga minero ng malaking deposito ng **hematites** sa kabundukan.","translation":"The miners found a large deposit of **hematite** in the mountains."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkuha ng sukat, laki, haba, o bigat ng isang bagay gamit ang isang pamantayan o instrumento.
original_explanation: This is what your nanay does to you with her eyes before she says "Tumaba ka na naman." It's also what a tailor does before making you a gown, or what you do to your patience level when your internet connection drops during a meeting. "Sukatin mo muna kung kasya pa ba 'yang damit" is the prelude to a diet.
usage_notes: The verb is in its object-focus form (-in). "Sinukat" is the past tense, "sinusukat" is the present, and "susukatin" is the future.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sukatin** mo nga kung ilang metro ang haba ng lamesang ito.","translation":"Can you **measure** how many meters long this table is."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **sukatin** ang temperatura ng pasyente.","translation":"The patient's temperature needs to be **measured**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marahas at mabilis na pagkalat o pagkasira ng isang bagay dahil sa panloob na presyon, na kadalasa'y may kasamang malakas na tunog.
etymology: From 'sabog' (explosion, scattered) with the actor-focus infix '-um-'.
original_explanation: The big boom! Literally, when a volcano, a bomb, or a tire **sumabog**. Figuratively, it’s what happens to your brain after a 12-hour shift ("**Sumabog** na ang utak ko!"). It's also what happens when a secret is revealed dramatically ("**Sumabog** ang balita"). It's the peak of intensity, the point of no return, the ultimate 'kaboom!'
usage_notes: Used both literally for explosions and figuratively for overwhelming feelings, sudden news, or looking disheveled ('Mukha kang sabog').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumabog** ang bulkan at nagbuga ng makapal na abo.","translation":"The volcano **erupted** and spewed thick ash."},{"sentence":"Halos **sumabog** ang dibdib niya sa kaba habang hinihintay ang resulta.","translation":"Her chest was about to **burst** from anxiety while waiting for the results."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, partikular na isang lalaki, na lumalahok sa isport ng boksing.
etymology: From Spanish "boxeador", adapted with influence from English "boxing".
original_explanation: The guy who gets punched for a living. From local gym heroes to the legendary Manny Pacquiao, a boksinero is a symbol of Filipino strength and resilience. Sila 'yung patunay na kahit anong suntok ng buhay ang matanggap mo, babangon ka pa rin.
usage_notes: The female equivalent is "boksinera".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang maging isang sikat na **boksinero** tulad ni Manny Pacquiao.","translation":"He dreams of becoming a famous **boxer** like Manny Pacquiao."},{"sentence":"Isang matapang na **boksinero** ang kumakatawan sa Pilipinas.","translation":"A brave **boxer** is representing the Philippines."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng tagapamahala o tagapagpadala ng mga kalakal, mensahe, o tao; maaari ding tumukoy sa isang babaeng nagbebenta sa isang tindahan.
original_explanation: This is your tita in the office who knows where everyone is and what everyone should be doing. In a retail setting, she's the one who can find that size 'medium' shirt in the stockroom faster than you can say 'add to cart'. The OG human Waze for logistics.
usage_notes: Often used in business, logistics, or retail contexts. The male counterpart is 'despatsador'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinawagan ng **despatsadora** ang lahat ng tsuper para sa mga bagong utos.","translation":"The **dispatcher** called all the drivers for new orders."},{"sentence":"Magaling ang **despatsadora** sa department store, nahanap niya agad ang hinahanap ko.","translation":"The **salesclerk** at the department store was excellent, she immediately found what I was looking for."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagkopya o pagtulad sa kilos, gawa, o anyo ng iba. Ito ang salitang-ugat.
original_explanation: Before 'copycat,' there was 'manggagaya.' This is what you do when your younger sibling mimics every word you say. It's also what happens when a new milk tea shop opens and suddenly ten more pop up on the same street with almost the same menu.
usage_notes: This is the root word for verbs like 'gumaya', 'gayahin', 'manggaya'. As a root word, it is often used in its inflected forms.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **gumaya** sa mga masasamang impluwensya.","translation":"Don't **imitate** bad influences."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **gumaya** ng mga sikat na sayaw sa TikTok.","translation":"She loves to **imitate** popular dances on TikTok."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o katangian ng pagiging walang katapusan o wakas; ang pamamalagi magpakailanman.
original_explanation: This is the 'forever' that's not just a romantic promise but a literal, mind-bending concept. It's like the length of a teleserye that refuses to end, the line at a government office, or the number of chismis about a celebrity. The ultimate 'walang katapusan'.
usage_notes: Often used in religious or philosophical contexts. Interchangeable with 'kawalang-katapusan' but 'kawalang-hanggan' often feels more profound or spiritual.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naniniwala siya sa buhay na may **kawalang-hanggan** pagkatapos ng kamatayan.","translation":"He believes in a life of **eternity** after death."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-ibig ng ina ay maihahambing sa **kawalang-hanggan**.","translation":"A mother's love can be compared to **infinity**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglalandian o pagpapalitan ng kilos o salitang may pahiwatig ng pag-ibig sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang tao.
original_explanation: This is the main event. 'Landi' is the skill, 'landian' is the game. It's the back-and-forth messaging, the 'accidental' bumping into each other, the shared laughter over a corny joke. It's the UAAP finals of flirting. May the best 'malandi' win.
usage_notes: The suffix '-an' makes it a noun referring to the reciprocal act/event (ang landian). The verb form is 'maglandian'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita ko ang **landian** nila sa coffee shop kanina.","translation":"I saw their **flirtation** at the coffee shop earlier."},{"sentence":"Huwag kayong mag-usap ng trabaho sa oras ng **landian**.","translation":"Don't talk about work during a **flirting session**."}]

translation: to run amok; to go on a rampage
meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang pagwawala o marahas na pag-atake sa galit, na walang pinipiling target.
etymology: From Spanish 'juramentado' (one who has taken an oath), referring to Moro warriors in Philippine history who took an oath to die fighting invaders. The meaning has since shifted to 'run amok'.
original_explanation: Ever felt so angry at your slow internet connection that you just want to flip the table? That's the feeling. It's when someone snaps and goes berserk. The word has a dark history, but now we use it (sometimes jokingly) for any extreme outburst of anger. "Naghuramentado si boss nung nalamang bagsak ang sales."
usage_notes: A very strong word describing a violent, uncontrolled outburst.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nang malasing ang lalaki, nagsimula siyang **maghuramentado** sa kalsada.","translation":"When the man got drunk, he started to **run amok** on the street."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong gagalitin 'yan, baka **maghuramentado**.","translation":"Don't anger him, he might **go on a rampage**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangkalahatang katawagan para sa karaniwang tao o mamamayan sa isang lipunan; ang malaking bilang ng populasyon na hindi kabilang sa mga elitista o naghaharing uri.
original_explanation: This is 'the people,' the 'madla,' the 'everyday Juan'. It's the target audience of noontime shows, budget-friendly products, and politicians during election season. When you say something is 'pang-**masa**', it means it's affordable, accessible, and relatable to the general public.
usage_notes: Often used in socio-political and marketing contexts. 'Pang-masa' is a very common derivative phrase.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pelikulang ito ay talagang sumikat sa **masa**.","translation":"This movie was really a hit with **the masses**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga pulitiko ay nagsisikap na makuha ang boto ng **masa**.","translation":"Politicians strive to get the vote of **the common people**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglalaro, pagbibiruan, o paglalambingan na malikot at masaya.
original_explanation: This is the noun form of 'harot'. It's the event, the session, the *ganap*. It’s the chaotic energy when you and your barkada are wrestling on the couch, or the 'kilig' back-and-forth messaging with your crush. It's the 'kulitan' session that can sometimes lead to 'aminan.' From innocent roughhousing to romantic teasing, **harutan** covers it all.
usage_notes: Often implies a physical but playful interaction. The suffix '-an' denotes a reciprocal or social action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natigil ang masayang **harutan** ng mga bata nang dumating ang kanilang ina.","translation":"The children's happy **horseplay** stopped when their mother arrived."},{"sentence":"Nauwi sa seryosong usapan ang kanilang **harutan** sa chat.","translation":"Their **playful banter** on chat led to a serious conversation."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pag-aalis ng sabon o dumi mula sa isang bagay gamit ang malinis na tubig pagkatapos itong labhan o sabunin.
original_explanation: The final boss battle in doing the laundry. After all the scrubbing (kuskos) and soaking (babad), you face the **banlaw**. This is the stage where you rinse out all the soap suds and your past mistakes. One **banlaw** is for beginners, two is standard, but the lola-approved method is three rinses (tatlong banlaw) until the water is crystal clear.
usage_notes: Often used as a root for the verb 'banlawan' (to rinse).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan pa ng isang **banlaw** para maalis lahat ng bula.","translation":"It needs one more **rinse** to remove all the suds."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng unang **banlaw**, marumi pa rin ang tubig.","translation":"After the first **rinse**, the water was still dirty."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na legal na may pananagutan sa pag-aalaga sa isang indibidwal na hindi kayang alagaan ang sarili, tulad ng isang menor de edad o isang taong may kapansanan.
original_explanation: This is the official term for your tita who signs your school forms because your parents are OFWs. On report card day, they're your savior. In parent-teacher meetings about your 'kalokohan', they're the judge. Spelled in Tagalog often as 'gwardiyan'.
usage_notes: Used primarily in legal, academic, and formal contexts. The Tagalized spelling 'gwardiyan' is more common in speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng pirma ng iyong magulang o **guardian** sa form na ito.","translation":"This form requires the signature of your parent or **guardian**."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang tiyahin ang itinalagang legal na **guardian**.","translation":"Her aunt was appointed as the legal **guardian**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paggamit ng puwersa upang mapaalis, mapagalaw, o maitaboy ang isang bagay o tao palayo sa sarili.
original_explanation: This is what you do to the MRT door when it's closing and you're late for work. It's also, unfortunately, the modern slang for a drug pusher. “Huwag kang basta-basta magpapa-**tulak** sa mga desisyon ng iba, bes. Stand your ground!”
usage_notes: Ang salitang 'tulak' ay may negatibong konotasyon sa modernong balbal, na tumutukoy sa isang nagbebenta ng ipinagbabawal na gamot. Ang konteksto ay mahalaga.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malakas na **tulak** lang ang kailangan para bumukas ang pinto.","translation":"Just one strong **push** is needed to open the door."},{"sentence":"Nahuli ang hinihinalang **tulak** ng droga sa kanilang lugar.","translation":"The suspected drug **pusher** in their area was caught."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang opisyal na itinalaga ng isang pamahalaan upang manirahan sa ibang bansa upang pangalagaan ang mga interes ng mga mamamayan nito.
original_explanation: Siya 'yung go-to person mo 'pag nagkaproblema ka abroad. Parang senior admin ng isang malaking group chat ng mga Pinoy sa ibang bansa. Nawalan ng passport? Kailangan ng legal advice? Hanapin si konsul.
usage_notes: Not to be confused with 'ambassador' (embahador), who is a higher-ranking diplomat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumunta sa embahada ang mga OFW para humingi ng tulong sa **konsul**.","translation":"The OFWs went to the embassy to ask for help from the **consul**."},{"sentence":"Ang **konsul** ng Pilipinas sa Japan ay nagbigay ng anunsyo.","translation":"The Philippine **consul** in Japan made an announcement."}]

translation: to make red; to cause to blush
meaning_filipino: Gawing pula o mamula ang isang bagay; maging sanhi ng pamumula ng pisngi dahil sa hiya, galit, o kilig.
original_explanation: Two meanings! 1) To make something red, like adding food coloring to your icing. 2) The more fun one: to make someone blush. That moment when your crush looks at you, or when your Tita asks 'Kailan ka ikakasal?' in front of everyone at the family reunion. Your cheeks suddenly turn into a red stoplight.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa literal na pagkulay o sa pisyolohikal na reaksyon ng pamumula. Ang konteksto ang susi.
