usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong biruin nang ganyan, **pinapamula** mo ako.","translation":"Don't joke with me like that, you're **making me blush**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **pamulahin** ang mga dekorasyon para sa Pasko.","translation":"We need **to make** the decorations **red** for Christmas."}]

translation: to make a faint line or mark on something
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o paggawa ng manipis na guhit o marka sa isang ibabaw.
original_explanation: The act of accidentally dragging your keys against the side of a car and creating that heart-stoppingly thin scratch. Or when you use a ruler and a pencil to make a super light guide line before cutting, praying it's straight.
usage_notes: The verb form of 'linggit'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **linggitan** ang bagong pintura ng pader.","translation":"Don't **make a faint mark on** the new paint of the wall."},{"sentence":"Nalinggitan ng pusa ang braso ng bata.","translation":"The cat **made a slight scratch** on the child's arm."}]

translation: to be the cause of joy; to delight in
meaning_filipino: Maging dahilan ng kagalakan, ligaya, o kasiyahan.
original_explanation: This is the feeling you get when your Shopee order arrives earlier than expected, or when your crush likes your old profile picture. It's the 'reason for your joy.' More formal than 'ikinatuwa.' You'd use this in a wedding vow, not when you find a 20-peso bill in your old jeans.
usage_notes: A more formal or profound way to express the cause of happiness compared to 'ikatuwa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ikinagagalak** naming ipaalam na ikaw ay natanggap sa trabaho.","translation":"We **are delighted to** inform you that you have been accepted for the job."},{"sentence":"Ang tagumpay ng kanyang anak ay labis niyang **ikinagalak**.","translation":"Her child's success was what she greatly **delighted in**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-alis o paglayo sa piling ng isa; ang pagputol ng ugnayan o relasyon.
original_explanation: Ah, the big one. The "breakup." The "it's not you, it's me." The source of a thousand hugot posts and countless tubs of ice cream. This is the official end of a relationship, the untagging on Facebook, the "babalik na ako sa pag-gym" phase. It's the painful but sometimes necessary fork in the road.
usage_notes: Can refer to any kind of separation, but is most commonly used to mean a romantic breakup.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging mahirap para sa kanila ang **paghiwalay** pagkatapos ng sampung taon.","translation":"The **separation** was difficult for them after ten years."},{"sentence":"Ang **paghiwalay** ng mag-asawa ay nakaapekto nang husto sa mga bata.","translation":"The **separation** of the couple greatly affected the children."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gas na bumabalot sa mundo at kailangan sa paghinga; ang paggalaw nito. Sa matalinhagang paraan, ito ay tumutukoy sa pagiging mayabang o palalo.
original_explanation: On a good day, it's the preskong 'hangin' from Tagaytay. On a bad day, it's the 'hangin' from your officemate who just got promoted and won't shut up about it. It's literally what we breathe, but figuratively, it's the stuff an arrogant person is full of. 'Puno ng hangin ang ulo' is the classic Pinoy diagnosis for a braggart.
usage_notes: The dual meaning is very common. Context is key to distinguish between literal wind/air and figurative arrogance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sarap ng sariwang **hangin** sa probinsya.","translation":"The fresh **air** in the province is so nice."},{"sentence":"Malakas ang **hangin** kaya lumipad ang mga papel.","translation":"The **wind** was strong so the papers flew away."},{"sentence":"Puro ka na lang **hangin**, wala namang gawa.","translation":"You're full of **hot air**, but no action."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pag-iisip, sining, o panitikan na naglalayong ilarawan ang mga bagay, tao, at pangyayari ayon sa kanilang tunay na kalagayan sa totoong buhay, nang walang halong idealismo.
original_explanation: This is when art and literature stop using filters. It’s the opposite of a Disney movie. It's the indie film showing the grit of Manila, the novel that doesn't shy away from poverty and corruption. It's accepting that your 'sana all' dreams might not happen and focusing on what's actually in front of you. It's the cold, hard truth, served on a platter.
usage_notes: Used in academic, artistic, and philosophical contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga nobela ni Lualhati Bautista ay nagpapakita ng **realismo** sa lipunang Pilipino.","translation":"Lualhati Bautista's novels show **realism** in Philippine society."},{"sentence":"Mas pinili ng pintor ang **realismo** kaysa sa abstraktong sining.","translation":"The painter chose **realism** over abstract art."}]

meaning_filipino: Pudpud o pulpol; nawalan ng talim o dulo dahil sa madalas na paggamit.
original_explanation: Yung dulo ng lapis mo na pinangsulat mo ng lahat ng notes mo for the whole sem, tapos ngayon ayaw mo nang tasahan kasi konti na lang ang natitira. Ganyan, upod na. O kaya 'yung tsinelas mong pudpod na sa kakalakad para sa pangarap.
usage_notes: Often used to describe pencils, crayons, knives, or any pointed/sharp object that has become blunt from use. Can also be used metaphorically for a person's patience or spirit being worn down.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Upod** na ang dulo ng lapis ko kaya hindi na maganda ang sulat ko.","translation":"The tip of my pencil is **worn down** so my handwriting isn't good anymore."},{"sentence":"Ilang beses mo nang ginamit 'yang kutsilyo, **upod** na tuloy.","translation":"You've used that knife so many times, now it's **blunt**."}]

meaning_filipino: Malaki, marangya, o kahanga-hanga sa sukat, itsura, o kahalagahan.
original_explanation: Ito yung size ng kape mo sa Starbucks. O kaya yung tawag sa party na sobrang bongga, 'Isang **grande**ng selebrasyon!' Parang pag-describe sa pangarap mo na dapat daw malaki. Or sa utang mo.
usage_notes: Kadalasang ginagamit upang magbigay-diin sa laki o karangyaan ng isang bagay, higit pa sa simpleng 'malaki'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghanda sila ng isang **grande**ng salu-salo para sa kanilang anibersaryo.","translation":"They prepared a **grand** feast for their anniversary."},{"sentence":"Isang **grande**ng hagdanan ang sasalubong sa iyo sa loob ng mansyon.","translation":"A **grand** staircase will greet you inside the mansion."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-iisang-katawan o pagsasagawa ng gawaing sekswal sa pagitan ng dalawang tao.
original_explanation: The formal, almost clinical, Filipino term for 'doing the deed.' It sounds more like a biology textbook entry than something you'd hear in a hugot line. It's the 'Netflix and chill' that results in the actual, uh, 'chilling'. Often found in classic literature or health class brochures.
usage_notes: A very formal and somewhat dated term. Colloquial or more direct terms are more common in everyday speech. Using this in a casual conversation might sound awkward or overly dramatic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paksa ng pagtatalik ay bihirang pag-usapan nang hayagan sa mga konserbatibong pamilya.","translation":"The topic of **having sex** is rarely discussed openly in conservative families."},{"sentence":"Ipinagbabawal ng simbahan ang **magtalik** bago ang kasal.","translation":"The church forbids **having sexual intercourse** before marriage."}]

translation: to be able to show; to be shown
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng pagkakataong maipakita o maipamalas ang isang bagay; maipakita nang hindi sinasadya.
original_explanation: This is about showing something, either intentionally ("Para mapakita ko sa'yo ang pagmamahal ko...") or unintentionally (like when your true colors are revealed, "Napakita rin ang tunay na ugali niya."). It's the verb for "show and tell," whether it's for your thesis defense or your hidden feelings.
usage_notes: The 'mapa-' prefix indicates ability or causation. It's object-focused, meaning the thing being shown is the focus.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gagawin ko ang lahat para **mapakita** sa iyo na seryoso ako.","translation":"I will do everything **to be able to show** you that I am serious."},{"sentence":"Sa wakas ay **napakita** na niya ang kanyang proyekto sa klase.","translation":"He was finally **able to show** his project to the class."}]

translation: to cause to protrude; to push out slightly
meaning_filipino: Bahagyang itulak, iusli, o palabasin ang isang bagay mula sa kinalalagyan nito.
original_explanation: Imagine trying to close an overstuffed maleta. That little bit of damit that keeps sticking out? You try to push it in, but your friend accidentally leans on the other side, causing it to 'iudlot' or stick out again. It’s a subtle pushing or bulging out. Not a full-on 'usli,' but a gentle protrusion.
usage_notes: A less common word, often describing a slight, often unintentional, pushing out or protrusion. Can also mean to pout by pushing the lips out.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang puno ng aparador, **naiudlot** palabas ang manggas ng damit.","translation":"The closet was so full, the sleeve of a shirt was **pushed out slightly**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **iudlot** ang iyong labi kapag nagagalit ka.","translation":"Don't **pout** (push out) your lips when you're angry."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng kakayahang matikman o maramdaman ang lasa ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is what you hope happens when your friend says 'Tikman mo 'to!' It's the ability to perceive flavor. Also used figuratively, like 'Sana malasahan mo ang hirap na pinagdadaanan ko,' which is pure hugot meaning 'I hope you get a 'taste' of the hardship I'm going through.'
usage_notes: Can be used both literally for food and figuratively for experiences.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit konti lang ang sahog, **malalasahan** mo pa rin ang linamnam ng sabaw.","translation":"Even with just a few ingredients, you can still **taste** the richness of the soup."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko **malasahan** ang pagkain dahil may sipon ako.","translation":"I can't **taste** the food because I have a cold."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghimok o paghikayat sa isang tao sa pamamagitan ng malambing na pananalita, papuri, o pangako.
original_explanation: This is your 'budol' moves. 'Yung niyayaya mo ang tropa na gumastos kahit wala sa budget, gamit ang matatamis na salita tulad ng 'deserve mo 'to'. It's the art of sweet-talking someone into doing something, often against their better judgment.
usage_notes: Can be positive (gentle persuasion) or negative (deceptive flattery). Often synonymous with 'pambobola'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa pamamagitan ng **pag-ulok**, nakumbinsi niya ang kapatid na ipahiram ang sasakyan.","translation":"Through **coaxing**, he convinced his sibling to lend the car."},{"sentence":"Hindi siya nadala sa **pag-ulok** ng tindera na bilhin ang mamahaling produkto.","translation":"She wasn't swayed by the seller's **flattery** to buy the expensive product."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang masakit na pamamaga sa balat na may nana, sanhi ng impeksyon sa isang hair follicle o glandulang sebaceous.
original_explanation: Ah, the dreaded pigsa. That painful, pus-filled bump that appears at the worst possible time, like before a major presentation or a first date. It's like your body's own little volcano, waiting to erupt. Everyone's lola has a 'secret' herbal remedy for this.
usage_notes: A common medical term understood by everyone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong piliting putukin ang **pigsa** dahil baka lumala ang impeksyon.","translation":"Don't try to pop the **boil** because the infection might worsen."},{"sentence":"Nilagyan niya ng mainit na bimpo ang kanyang **pigsa**.","translation":"She applied a warm compress to her **boil**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalantad o paghahayag sa tunay na katangian, pagkatao, o intensyon ng isang tao na dati ay nakatago.
etymology: From Spanish 'mascara' (mask), with Tagalog verb affix 'i-'.
original_explanation: This is the big reveal in a teleserye when the 'kontrabida' is finally exposed for all their evil deeds. It's when you find out your "supportive" friend was actually the one spreading chismis about you. To 'imaskara' someone is to pull off their metaphorical mask and show everyone the 'true-self' hiding underneath. The ultimate "Aha! Sabi ko na nga ba!" moment.
usage_notes: A dramatic word, often used in contexts of betrayal, investigation, and revelation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa huli, ang matapang na saksi ang naglakas-loob na **imaskara** ang mga tiwaling opisyal.","translation":"In the end, the brave witness dared to **unmask** the corrupt officials."},{"sentence":"Oras na para **imaskara** ang kasinungalingan sa likod ng kanyang mga pangako.","translation":"It's time to **expose** the lies behind his promises."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pribadong guro na nagbibigay ng karagdagang pagtuturo sa isang mag-aaral o maliit na pangkat, karaniwan sa labas ng paaralan.
original_explanation: Your academic lifesaver when Math starts looking like ancient hieroglyphics. They're the reason you passed algebra and your parents didn't ground you for a year.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng **tiyutor** sa Math dahil nahihirapan ako.","translation":"I need a **tutor** in Math because I'm having a hard time."}]

translation: to be embarrassed; to be humiliated
meaning_filipino: Makaranas ng matinding kahihiyan sa harap ng ibang tao dahil sa isang pangyayari o kilos.
original_explanation: That feeling when you wave back at someone, only to realize they were waving at the person behind you. Or when your crush sees you trip over nothing. It's public embarrassment, level 99. The ultimate 'lupa, kainin mo na ako' moment.
usage_notes: A very common feeling in Filipino culture, where 'hiya' (shame/face-saving) is a significant social concept.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Talagang **napahiya** ako nang tawagin ako sa entablado at hindi ko alam ang isasagot.","translation":"I was truly **embarrassed** when I was called on stage and I didn't know what to answer."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang masidhing damdamin ng kaligayahan o kasiyahan na nararanasan dahil sa isang magandang pangyayari o kaganapan.
original_explanation: This is the feeling you get when your Shopee/Lazada parcel arrives, when the traffic suddenly clears up on EDSA, or when your crush finally replies to your message. It's that pure, unadulterated happiness before reality (like your credit card bill) kicks in.
usage_notes: A very common word for happiness. Can be intensified by repetition ('tuwang-tuwa').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi maipinta ang kanyang **tuwa** nang makita ang kanyang pamilya.","translation":"His **joy** was immeasurable when he saw his family."},{"sentence":"Nakaramdam ako ng matinding **tuwa** nang manalo kami sa kompetisyon.","translation":"I felt intense **happiness** when we won the competition."}]

translation: law enforcer; officer of the law
meaning_filipino: Isang taong ang tungkulin ay ipatupad ang mga batas ng isang bansa o komunidad, tulad ng pulis o sundalo.
etymology: A Filipino calque (loan-translation) of 'officer of the law'. Composed of 'alagad' (follower/disciple) + 'ng' (of) + 'batas' (law).
original_explanation: The formal term for pulis, security guard, or anyone in uniform who makes you check if your car's registration is expired. They're the main characters in every Cardo Dalisay-style action movie.
usage_notes: A formal and respectful term for police and other law enforcement personnel. Used frequently in news reports and official statements.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Rumesponde agad ang mga **alagad ng batas** sa pinangyarihan ng krimen.","translation":"The **officers of the law** immediately responded to the crime scene."},{"sentence":"Dapat nating igalang ang mga tapat na **alagad ng batas**.","translation":"We should respect the honest **law enforcers**."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang bagay na may maraming tubig o likido, o may katangiang tulad ng tubig.
original_explanation: When your sinigang is more 'sabaw' than 'sahog,' that's matubig. It's what you call a watermelon that's perfectly juicy or a sauce that's too thin. Your crush's reply could also be 'matubig' if it's bland and lacks substance. Ouch. The opposite of 'malapot' (thick).
usage_notes: Used to describe the consistency of food, the quality of fruit, or a place with a lot of water.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayoko ng kape na masyadong **matubig**.","translation":"I don't like coffee that's too **watery**."},{"sentence":"Ang pakwan na ito ay napakatamis at **matubig**.","translation":"This watermelon is very sweet and **watery** (juicy)."}]

translation: state of being confused or disoriented
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkalito, pagkawala sa sarili, o hindi malinaw na pag-iisip, kadalasan dahil sa pagod, sakit, o isang nakagugulat na pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is you trying to figure out your SSS, PhilHealth, and Pag-IBIG contributions. Or when you wake up from a deep nap and don't know what year it is. That 'loading... please wait' feeling in your brain is pagkatuliro.
usage_notes: Describes a more intense or dizzying confusion than the simple 'pagkalito'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa kanyang **pagkatuliro**, hindi niya maalala kung saan niya inilagay ang kanyang mga susi.","translation":"In his **state of confusion**, he couldn't remember where he put his keys."},{"sentence":"Ang lagnat ay nagdulot ng kanyang **pagkatuliro**.","translation":"The fever caused his **disorientation**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinsala sa balat o laman na sanhi ng init, apoy, kuryente, kemikal, o radyasyon.
original_explanation: The painful reminder you get when you accidentally touch a hot pan while cooking adobo or when your hair straightener decides to kiss your forehead. Also, a 'paso sa puso' is what you get when you see your crush holding hands with someone else. Ouch.
usage_notes: Refers to the injury itself. The verb form is 'mapaso' (to get burned).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon siya ng **paso** sa braso nang matalsikan ng mainit na mantika.","translation":"She got a **burn** on her arm when hot oil splattered on it."},{"sentence":"Lagyan mo kaagad ng gamot ang **paso** mo.","translation":"Put medicine on your **burn** immediately."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking yunit ng pamahalaang lokal sa Pilipinas, na karaniwang binubuo ng mga bayan at lungsod.
etymology: From 'lawig' (duration, extent) + '-an' suffix, possibly meaning "an extended area."
original_explanation: Ito yung "probinsya." Yung lugar na pinupuntahan mo tuwing Holy Week o Pasko para makalanghap ng sariwang hangin at makakain ng tunay na masarap na pagkain (sorry, Manila!). Dito mo maririnig ang "Uwi ka na, 'di na kami galit" galing sa lola mo. It's the opposite of the concrete jungle.
usage_notes: Refers to the administrative division known as a province. "Probinsya" is the more common conversational term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming magagandang tanawin sa **lalawigan** ng Palawan.","translation":"There are many beautiful sights in the **province** of Palawan."},{"sentence":"Umuwi siya sa kanilang **lalawigan** para magbakasyon.","translation":"He went home to their **province** for a vacation."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang regular na pagbabayad na ginagawa ng isang indibidwal o kumpanya sa isang kompanya ng seguro para sa isang insurance policy.
original_explanation: This is that recurring payment that makes you feel like you're throwing money away... until you actually need it. It’s the adult version of paying for an umbrella you hope you'll never have to use. Your friendly neighborhood financial advisor will tell you this is "investing in peace of mind," but your wallet just sees another "bayarin."
usage_notes: The amount paid for an insurance policy to remain active.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong bayaran ang buwanang **bayad sa seguro** ng kotse.","translation":"I need to pay the monthly car **insurance premium**."},{"sentence":"Mababa lang ang **bayad sa seguro** kung bata ka pa kumuha ng life insurance.","translation":"The **insurance premium** is low if you get life insurance when you're still young."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtatrabaho nang lampas sa itinakdang regular na oras ng paggawa, karaniwang may kaakibat na karagdagang bayad.
original_explanation: The national sport of BPO agents and anyone trying to make 'extra-extra' for the 13th-month pay. It's that feeling when your shift ends at 6 PM but you're still at your desk at 8 PM, fueled by cheap coffee and the promise of 'OT pay'. Your body says 'uwi na,' but your wallet says 'isa pang ticket, Lord.'
usage_notes: A very common Taglish verb in the workplace.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **mag-obertaim** ngayong gabi para matapos ang report.","translation":"I need to **work overtime** tonight to finish the report."},{"sentence":"Laging napipilitang **mag-obertaim** si Ana dahil sa dami ng gawain.","translation":"Ana is always forced to **work overtime** because of the heavy workload."}]

meaning_filipino: Makakatanggap ng dagdag sa isang bagay, karaniwan ay sa sahod, sweldo, o bayarin.
original_explanation: The magic word every employee wants to hear from their boss, especially after a grueling performance review. It's the moment you can finally afford that extra milk tea or consider moving out of your parents' house. This is the opposite of 'for compliance lang po.' This is the real deal.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in the context of salary or price increases. It's in the contemplative aspect (future tense).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **maaumentuhan** na tayo ng sahod sa susunod na taon.","translation":"I hope we will **receive a salary raise** next year."},{"sentence":"Kapag **naaumentuhan** ang pamasahe, apektado ang budget ng lahat.","translation":"When the fare **is increased**, everyone's budget is affected."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng pamaypay o anumang bagay upang mahanginan ang isang tao, bagay, o lugar.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of what you do *to* someone. 'Ma, paypayan mo naman ako!' (Mom, fan me!) is a classic line from Pinoy kids feeling the heat. It's an act of service, love, or sometimes, a chore you're forced to do for your lola while she watches her favorite teleserye.
usage_notes: The focus of the action is the object or person being fanned. 'Paypayan mo ako' (Fan me).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**paypayan** mo naman ang mga uling para magbaga.","translation":"Please **fan** the charcoal to get it glowing."},{"sentence":"Habang nagkukwento si lola, siya ay aking pini**paypayan**.","translation":"While grandma was telling a story, I was **fanning** her."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang taong kapareha sa pagsasayaw.
original_explanation: Your Jowa On The Dancefloor (JOTD). The one you grab for the 'Cha-Cha' at a tita's birthday party, or your designated partner for the company Christmas presentation dance number. Can be a romantic partner or just a 'for-this-song-only' partner.
usage_notes: Can be used for a partner in any type of dance, from formal ballroom to informal street dancing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Marco ang naging **kasayaw** ko sa aming prom.","translation":"Marco was my **dance partner** at our prom."},{"sentence":"Naghahanap siya ng **kasayaw** para sa nalalapit na kumpetisyon.","translation":"She is looking for a **dance partner** for the upcoming competition."}]

meaning_filipino: (Kolokyal) Ang mabilis na pag-alis o pagtakas mula sa isang lugar.
etymology: A modern slang term, likely from the early 2000s, derived from the noun 'sibat' (spear), implying a swift, direct movement away from something.
original_explanation: This is Pinoy slang for 'I'm outta here!' It's when you need to make a quick exit. 'Uy, andyan na si boss, sibat na tayo!' (Hey, the boss is here, let's scram!). It’s the action you take to avoid getting caught, whether it's by your parents after curfew or by your TL for taking too long on your break.
usage_notes: Highly colloquial and used in informal settings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumibat** agad kami pagkatapos ng klase para hindi maabutan ng ulan.","translation":"We **fled** right after class so we wouldn't get caught in the rain."},{"sentence":"Pre, **sibat** na, may meeting pa ako.","translation":"Bro, I gotta **scram**, I still have a meeting."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking anyong tubig na napapaligiran ng lupa, karaniwang tubig-tabang.
original_explanation: It's a body of water that's bigger than your condo's swimming pool but smaller than the West Philippine Sea. Think Taal Lake or Laguna de Bay. Perfect for your next "unwind" post on IG, complete with a dramatic caption about its depth mirroring your feelings.
usage_notes: Can also refer to a large pool of any liquid, like spilled oil, but 'lawa' is more common for 'lake'. 'Lanaw' is more common in certain regions and literature.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **Lanaw** ng Lanao ay isa sa pinakamalaki sa Pilipinas.","translation":"Lake Lanao is one of the largest in the Philippines."},{"sentence":"May nabuong **lanaw** ng putik sa kalsada pagkatapos ng malakas na ulan.","translation":"A **lagoon** of mud formed on the road after the heavy rain."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang taong may likas na kasamaan, mapanlinlang, taksil, at walang konsensiya.
original_explanation: The final boss of kontrabidas. Not just bad, but creatively, spectacularly evil. A 'balakyot' person will steal your jowa, your project proposal, and your last piece of lechon, then ask you why you look so sad. Think of the most hated villain in your favorite teleserye—that's peak balakyot energy.
usage_notes: A strong, literary word. Not typically used in casual conversation, but carries a lot of weight when it is. Implies a deep-seated, almost cartoonish evil.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa mga pelikula, laging natatalo ang **balakyot** na kontrabida sa huli.","translation":"In movies, the **wicked** villain always loses in the end."},{"sentence":"Isang **balakyot** na plano ang nabuo sa kanyang isipan upang makuha ang yaman.","translation":"A **treacherous** plan formed in his mind to get the wealth."}]

translation: back and forth; to and fro
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpunta sa isang lugar at pagbalik mula roon nang paulit-ulit; paggalaw na walang tiyak na direksyon o patutunguhan.
etymology: Kontraksyon ng pariralang 'paroon at parito' (going there and coming here).
original_explanation: 'Yung lakad mo sa sala habang hinihintay mo 'yung reply niya. O 'yung ginagawa ng office messenger buong araw. It's the state of being busy but not really getting anywhere, parang traffic lang sa EDSA. You're moving, but are you really going forward?
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay **paroo't-parito** sa loob ng kwarto, hindi mapakali.","translation":"He was pacing **back and forth** inside the room, unable to stay still."},{"sentence":"Maghapon siyang **paroo't-parito** sa pag-aasikaso ng mga dokumento.","translation":"He was going **to and fro** all day processing documents."}]

translation: to peck at repeatedly; to mob
meaning_filipino: Tukain nang paulit-ulit at may puwersa ng isang ibon; pagtulungan o gulpihin ng isang grupo.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you're the only one with chicharon in a group of hungry friends. They'll 'pupugin' you. It's also what chickens do to corn, or what chismosas do to a juicy piece of gossip—pecking at it until nothing is left.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for birds or figuratively for a group of people attacking one person (verbally or physically).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinimulang **pupugin** ng mga manok ang natapong mais.","translation":"The chickens started to **peck at** the spilled corn."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi ka namin **pupupugin** ng tanong.","translation":"Don't worry, we won't **mob** you with questions."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, bagay, o entidad na nagbibigay ng proteksyon, pagtatanggol, o pag-iingat.
original_explanation: Ang 'sugar daddy' ng 2026. Charot! Ito yung 'knight in shining armor' mo, yung 'backer' mo, yung Ate o Kuya na handang makipag-away para sa'yo. Pwede ring literal na bagay, like a screen protector for your phone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinuring niyang **protektor** ng kanilang pamilya ang kanilang panganay na kapatid.","translation":"She considered their eldest sibling as the **protector** of their family."},{"sentence":"Ang sundalo ay isang **protektor** ng bayan.","translation":"A soldier is a **protector** of the nation."}]

translation: Go ahead!; Hit it!; Do it!
meaning_filipino: Isang hudyat o pampasigla na nagsasabing "sige" o "ituloy mo."
original_explanation: The ultimate "push mo 'yan, teh!" from a friend. It's what you shout when someone is hesitating to message their crush, take the last piece of lechon, or sing their heart out at karaoke. From the Spanish "Dale," meaning "Go ahead" or "Give it."
usage_notes: Used as a slang or colloquial encouragement. Very common in informal conversations. Often used with a gesture.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kakanta ka sa videoke? **Dale**!","translation":"You're going to sing at the karaoke? **Go for it**!"},{"sentence":"Tirahin mo na 'yang huling piraso ng pizza. **Dale**!","translation":"Go ahead and take that last slice of pizza. **Hit it**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Nagdudulot ng pakiramdam ng pagkasuklam o pagnanais na sumuka; lubhang kasuklam-suklam.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'nakaka-' (nagsasanhi ng kilos) at salitang-ugat na 'duwal' (pagsusuka).
original_explanation: That feeling you get when you smell spoiled food in the office pantry, or when you see your ex's super cheesy posts with their new partner. It's something that makes you want to physically or figuratively vomit. 'Ewww, nakakaduwal!'
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin para sa pisikal na pagduduwal o para sa matinding pandidiri sa isang sitwasyon o tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakakaduwal** ang amoy na nagmumula sa basurahan.","translation":"The smell coming from the trash can is **nauseating**."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang pagtataksil ay isang **nakakaduwal** na alaala.","translation":"His betrayal is a **sickening** memory."}]

translation: can be moved; is being moved (unintentionally)
meaning_filipino: May kakayahang gumalaw o maigalaw; o di-sinasadyang naigagalaw.
etymology: From "galaw" (move) with the prefix "na-" and reduplication of the root's first syllable ("na" + "ga" + "galaw").
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na may multo sa kwarto kasi may gamit na nagagalaw mag-isa. Or when you're trying to take a super steady video but your hand isn't cooperating, so the camera nagagalaw. It's about movement, whether you can do it ("Paki-check kung nagagalaw pa 'yung turnilyo") or it's happening against your will.
usage_notes: The "na-" prefix here implies ability or involuntary action, distinguishing it from "gumagalaw" (is moving) or "ginagalaw" (is being moved intentionally).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang malikot, **nagagalaw** tuloy ang lamesa.","translation":"Don't be fidgety, the table **is being moved** (unintentionally)."},{"sentence":"Tingnan mo kung **nagagalaw** pa ang pinto, baka naipit na sa kalawang.","translation":"See if the door **can still be moved**, it might be stuck with rust."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng marka o diyakritiko sa ibabaw ng isang patinig upang ipahiwatig ang tamang diin o pagbigkas ng isang salita.
original_explanation: This is what your Filipino teacher tells you to do but you probably forgot how. It's adding those little hats (pakupya, paiwa) or lines (pahilis) on letters, like in 'tubó' (sugarcane) vs 'tubo' (pipe/profit). It's the OG way of correcting someone's pronunciation, grammar-nazi style.
usage_notes: A technical term used in linguistics and formal Filipino writing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **magtuldik** sa mga salitang may malumay na diin.","translation":"Don't forget to **place an accent mark** on words with a gentle stress."},{"sentence":"Tinuruan kami ng guro kung paano **magtuldik** nang wasto.","translation":"The teacher taught us how to **place accent marks** correctly."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng kawalan ng pagkakabuklod o pagtutulungan sa isang pangkat o lipunan.
original_explanation: Eto 'yung nangyayari sa group project kapag kanya-kanya ang trip ng mga ka-grupo mo. Imbes na isa lang ang output, nagiging battle royale. Parang pamilya sa Pasko na nag-aaway kung anong uunahin, Noche Buena o 'yung chismis tungkol sa Tita na galing abroad.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa kontekstong pampulitika, panlipunan, o pang-organisasyon upang ilarawan ang salungatan o kawalan ng kooperasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **di-pagkakaisa** ng mga miyembro ang nagpabagsak sa kanilang kooperatiba.","translation":"The **disunity** of the members caused their cooperative to fail."},{"sentence":"Kitang-kita ang **di-pagkakaisa** sa kanilang mga opinyon tungkol sa bagong batas.","translation":"The **discord** in their opinions about the new law was very apparent."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang itlog na niluto sa mainit na mantika. Ito ay isang di-pamantayang pagbaybay ng 'pritong itlog'.
original_explanation: This is how you type 'pritong itlog' when you're super hungry and texting your mom what to cook. No time for spaces, just pure, unadulterated craving for that glorious fried egg. It's the digital, fast-paced version of the classic breakfast hero.
usage_notes: This is an informal, non-standard spelling of 'pritong itlog'. While common in text messages and social media, 'pritong itlog' (two words) is the grammatically correct form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ma, pabili **pritongitlog** sa karinderya!","translation":"Mom, please buy a **fried egg** at the eatery!"},{"sentence":"Ang order ko ay isang **pritongitlog** na may kanin.","translation":"My order is one **fried egg** with rice."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong may pagkiling o sumusuporta sa pamamahala ng isang hari o monarkiya.
original_explanation: Basically, you're Team King/Queen. You believe in the whole royalty setup. In a modern Pinoy context, it's like being a die-hard fan of a specific celebrity "dynasty" or a political family, believing they're destined to lead. It's giving "long live the king" energy.
usage_notes: This is a more political or historical term and not commonly used in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **makahari** ay nagnanais na ibalik ang monarkiya sa kanilang bansa.","translation":"The **monarchists** wish to restore the monarchy in their country."},{"sentence":"Isang kilusang **makahari** ang nabuo noong panahon ng rebolusyon.","translation":"A **pro-monarchy** movement was formed during the time of the revolution."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piling hiwa ng karne, karaniwan ay mula sa baka o baboy, na matatagpuan sa bandang likod at balakang, na kilala sa pagiging malambot.
original_explanation: Yung 'sosyal' na parte ng baka o baboy na ino-order mo sa steakhouse kapag bonus day. Ito yung hiwa na hindi mo basta-basta makikita sa karinderya. The 'don't chew, just let it melt in your mouth' cut.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkano ang isang kilo ng **solomilyo** ng baka?","translation":"How much is one kilo of beef **tenderloin**?"},{"sentence":"Ang paborito niyang lutuin ay inihaw na **solomilyo**.","translation":"His favorite dish to cook is grilled **sirloin**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglusot o pagbaon nang malalim sa isang bagay hanggang sa lumabas sa kabilang panig.
original_explanation: ‘Yung sakit na 'tagos hanggang buto.' It's not just on the surface level; it goes all the way through. Like when your crush's 'seen' message penetrates your very soul, or when your mom's sermon pierces your pride.
usage_notes: Implies complete penetration from one side to the other. Often used figuratively for emotions. A common synonym is 'tagos'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumagop** ang bala sa pader.","translation":"The bullet **penetrated** the wall."},{"sentence":"**Tagop** sa puso ang kanyang mga sinabi.","translation":"His words were **piercing** to the heart."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sentro o kabayanan ng isang munisipalidad o lungsod kung saan matatagpuan ang mga pangunahing gusali tulad ng munisipyo, simbahan, at palengke.
original_explanation: Basically "the bayan of the bayan." It's the downtown area, the poblacion, where all the action happens. It's where you find the city hall, the main church, the public market, and probably the only Jollibee for miles. If your lola tells you to go to the "**bayanan**," she means the main commercial district, not the entire country.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with "bayan" when referring to the town proper. Synonymous with 'poblacion' or 'sentro'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa **bayanan** ang bagong bukas na bangko.","translation":"The newly opened bank is in the **town center**."},{"sentence":"Magkita tayo sa plasa sa **bayanan**.","translation":"Let's meet at the plaza in **downtown**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinagsamang salita ng "wala" at "na," na ginagamit upang ipahiwatig ang kawalan ng isang bagay na kasunod nito.
etymology: Kontraksyon ng `wala` (none) at ng pang-angkop na `na`.
original_explanation: The prefix to many Filipino hugot lines. Walang forever. Walang tayo. Walang label. It's the contraction of `wala na`, but it functions as the starting point for describing what's missing. "Anong ulam?" "Walang ulam." It sets the stage for disappointment, or sometimes, just a simple fact.
usage_notes: Laging sinusundan ng isang pangngalan, panghalip, o pang-uri upang tukuyin kung ano ang wala. Ito ang pinakakaraniwang paraan upang ipahayag ang "without [something]".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umalis siyang **walang** paalam.","translation":"He left **without** saying goodbye."},{"sentence":"Isa siyang bayaning **walang** kapa.","translation":"He is a hero **with no** cape."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagkuha o pag-ako sa isang bagay na iniaalok o ibinibigay; pagkilala at hindi pagtutol sa isang katotohanan o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: Ito yung phase na 'di ka na galit na single ka pa rin. "It is what it is," sabi mo sa sarili mo habang umo-order ng family-size na pizza for one. It's also that glorious moment you receive your sahod or your online shopping parcel. From accepting your fate to accepting a package, it's all pagtanggap.
usage_notes: Can be both physical (receiving a gift) and emotional/psychological (accepting a situation).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **pagtanggap** sa sarili upang maging tunay na masaya.","translation":"Self-**acceptance** is important to be truly happy."},{"sentence":"Malugod ang kanyang **pagtanggap** sa mga panauhin.","translation":"Her **receiving** of the guests was warm."}]

translation: diversification, act of varying or changing frequently
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbabago nang madalas o pag-iiba-iba ng isang bagay, tulad ng desisyon, plano, o anyo.
etymology: From pa- + pa- + iba-iba (reduplication of iba), meaning "the act of causing to be different/varied."
original_explanation: Describes your crush's mood, the Philippine weather, or your career plans after watching an inspiring movie. One minute you want to be a lawyer, the next a vlogger. It's the state of being "pabago-bago."
usage_notes: The reduplication 'iba-iba' emphasizes the variety or frequency of change.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapaiba-iba** ng desisyon ng hepe ay nakakalito sa mga empleyado.","translation":"The boss's **frequent changing** of decisions confuses the employees."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **pagpapaiba-iba** ng pananim upang mapanatiling malusog ang lupa.","translation":"Crop **diversification** is important to keep the soil healthy."}]

translation: the act of being fooled; the state of being crazy
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging nalinlang o nadaya ng iba; maaari ring tumukoy sa pagkawala sa tamang pag-iisip.
original_explanation: Two meanings! 1) The 'sana all' feeling turning into 'sana ol' after you realize you've been played. It's the feeling after falling for a 'legit' online seller who sends you a bar of soap instead of an iPhone. 2) The more serious version of 'pagkaloka', like actual mental breakdown from too much adulting.
usage_notes: Can mean either being deceived or going insane. Context is key. 'Naloko ako' (I was fooled) vs. 'Naloloko na ako' (I'm going crazy).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang nawala sa kanya dahil sa kanyang **pagkaloko** sa investment scam.","translation":"He lost a lot because of his **being fooled** by the investment scam."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkaloko** niya ay nagsimula nang iwan siya ng kanyang asawa.","translation":"His **descent into madness** began when his wife left him."}]

translation: to be squashed (by stepping on), to be crushed underfoot
meaning_filipino: Ang mapisa o madurog dahil sa pagtapak o pag-apak dito.
etymology: From *ma-* (potential verb prefix) + *tiris* (to crush with the foot or finger).
original_explanation: That tragic moment when you step on a snail, an insect, or worse, your dropped phone screen. It's being crushed specifically by being stepped on. Parang puso mo nung nakita mong may kasamang iba si crush, 'di ba? Na-tiris ang feelings mo.
usage_notes: Specifically implies crushing by stepping on something or pressing with a finger.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-ingat siyang maglakad para walang **matiris** na halaman.","translation":"He walked carefully so as not **to squash** any plants."},{"sentence":"Ay, may **natiris** akong langgam!","translation":"Oops, I **stepped on** an ant!"}]

meaning_filipino: Manatili sa isang lugar o kalagayan hanggang sa dumating ang isang tao o mangyari ang isang bagay; maghintay.
original_explanation: The national pastime of the Philippines. You 'mag-antay' for your friend who is on 'Filipino time,' 'mag-antay' for your package from Shopee, 'mag-antay' in line at the government office, and 'mag-antay' for your crush to notice you. It’s the root of all 'hugot' about waiting for something or someone that may never arrive. Synonymous with 'maghintay'.
usage_notes: 'Maghintay' is also very common and completely interchangeable in most contexts. 'Mag-antay' can sometimes feel slightly more informal or conversational.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Mag-antay** ka lang diyan, parating na ako.","translation":"Just **wait** there, I'm on my way."},{"sentence":"Gaano katagal pa ba ako kailangang **mag-antay**?","translation":"How much longer do I have **to wait**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang may pinakamataas na halaga, kabuluhan, o importansya; higit sa lahat.
original_explanation: This is your 'non-negotiable.' Like Wi-Fi during a work-from-home setup or getting your 13th-month pay on time. It's the top priority, the main character, the one thing you can't do without. Ang pamilya ang **pinakamahalaga** sa lahat. Period.
usage_notes: Can refer to both material value and abstract importance. The '-ng' is a linker used to connect it to a following noun, as in 'pinakamahalagang bagay' (most important thing).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kalusugan ang **pinakamahalaga** nating yaman.","translation":"Health is our **most valuable** wealth."},{"sentence":"Ano ang **pinakamahalagang** aral na natutunan mo?","translation":"What is the **most important** lesson you've learned?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pariralang nagsasaad na mayroong isang bilang o yunit ng isang bagay, tao, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: The classic start to many chismis or warnings. "May isa diyan na plastic..." (There's one person there who's fake...). It's also used when counting or pointing something out, like when you're looking for a seat in a crowded food court and your friend triumphantly yells, "Uy, may isa dito!"
usage_notes: A very basic and common phrase for indicating the existence of a single item or person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Akala ko ubos na ang mansanas, pero **may isa** pa pala sa ref.","translation":"I thought the apples were all gone, but **there is one** more in the ref."},{"sentence":"Sa lahat ng magkakapatid, **may isa** talagang pasaway.","translation":"Among all the siblings, **there is** always **one** who is mischievous."}]

translation: to cause hesitation; to delay because of doubt
meaning_filipino: Ipagpaliban o antalahin ang isang gawain dahil sa pag-aalinlangan o kawalan ng desisyon.
original_explanation: This is the act of "procrastinating because of ~feels~." You know you have to do something, like reply to a risky text or accept a job offer, but you hesitate. You're not just delaying; you're delaying because you're unsure. "Huwag mo nang ipag-atubili ang pagsabi ng totoo." (Don't hesitate to tell the truth.) It’s the official word for 'mañana habit' fueled by doubt.
usage_notes: A formal word. In casual conversation, people are more likely to say "huwag ka nang mag-dalawang isip" (don't think twice) or "gawin mo na" (just do it).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang **ipag-atubili** ang paghingi ng tulong kung kinakailangan mo.","translation":"Don't **delay** asking for help if you need it."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-amin sa pagkakamali ay isang bagay na hindi dapat **ipinag-aatubili**.","translation":"Admitting a mistake is something that should not be **hesitated upon**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking kawani na ang pangunahing tungkulin ay tumulong sa mga gawaing pang-opisina o administratibo. Ginagamit din para sa pinuno ng isang kagawaran ng gobyerno (e.g., Kalihim ng Edukasyon).
original_explanation: The male counterpart of the all-knowing office gatekeeper. Also, this is the title for the big bosses in government departments, like the "Secretary of Health." So, it can mean "the guy who gets the coffee" or "the guy who runs the country's entire health system." Level up!
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa isang lalaking kalihim o sa isang pinuno ng kagawaran ng pamahalaan (katumbas ng "Kalihim").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinalaga si G. Cruz bilang bagong **sekretaryo** ng Department of Tourism.","translation":"Mr. Cruz was appointed as the new **secretary** of the Department of Tourism."},{"sentence":"Mahusay na **sekretaryo** si Mark, laging organisado ang kanyang mga file.","translation":"Mark is an excellent **secretary**; his files are always organized."}]

meaning_filipino: Isa pang malambing at impormal na tawag sa isang matalik na kaibigan, kahalintulad ng 'beshie'.
original_explanation: Alternative spelling ng 'beshie'. Pinili mo 'to kung mas aesthetic sa'yo ang 'y' kaysa sa 'ie'. Same energy, different font. Para sa mga kaibigang kasama mong mag-emote at mag-rant tungkol sa buhay.
usage_notes: Ginagamit nang palitan sa "beshie".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Miss na kita, **beshy** ko!","translation":"I miss you, my **bestie**!"},{"sentence":"Happy birthday, **beshy**! More chika to come!","translation":"Happy birthday, **bestie**! More gossip to come!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hindi sinasadyang paggalaw sa isang makinis o basang ibabaw na nagiging sanhi ng pagkawala ng balanse.
original_explanation: What happens when you walk confidently on a newly-mopped floor at the mall. It's also a metaphor for your grades when you start binge-watching a new K-drama series during finals week.
usage_notes: Can be used both literally for physical slipping and figuratively for a decline or mistake (e.g., 'pagdulas ng dila' or slip of the tongue).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa **pagdulas** dahil basa ang sahig.","translation":"Be careful of **slipping** because the floor is wet."},{"sentence":"Ang biglaang **pagdulas** ng kanyang mga grado ay ikinabahala ng kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"The sudden **sliding** of his grades worried his parents."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging pabaya, kawalan ng pag-iingat, o hindi pag-aasikaso sa isang tungkulin o gawain.
etymology: From a less common root "siwal" (neglect) with the circumfix "ka-...-an".
original_explanation: This is the 'bahala na si Batman' attitude but with negative consequences. It's when you forget to pay the Meralco bill, submit a report full of typos, or leave the sinigang boiling until it's dry. It's a deep-level carelessness, the formal term for being 'pabaya'.
usage_notes: A formal and somewhat rare word. "Kapabayaan" is much more common in everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kasiwalan** ng drayber ang sanhi ng aksidente.","translation":"The driver's **negligence** was the cause of the accident."},{"sentence":"Pinagsabihan siya dahil sa kanyang **kasiwalan** sa trabaho.","translation":"He was reprimanded for his **carelessness** at work."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang dalawang panlabas na butas ng ilong na daanan ng hangin sa paghinga.
original_explanation: Your personal air intake vents. The two portals on your face responsible for smelling your mom's adobo and for getting clogged up when you have a cold. Also, the target of many a childhood 'kulangot' excavation mission.
usage_notes: A very specific and literal noun phrase.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lumaki ang **butas ng ilong** niya sa galit.","translation":"His **nostrils** flared in anger."},{"sentence":"May dumi sa kaliwang **butas ng ilong** mo.","translation":"There's dirt in your left **nostril**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng prutas na kulay kahel, matamis, at malambot kapag hinog, na karaniwang inaangkat mula sa ibang bansa.
original_explanation: That fancy, orange, tomato-looking fruit you see in the grocery store that's not a tomato. It's sweet, a bit pricey, and makes you feel a little bit sosyal when you eat it. That's a kaki.
usage_notes: Refers to the fruit. Not to be confused with the color.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito niyang prutas ang matamis na **kaki**.","translation":"His favorite fruit is the sweet **persimmon**."},{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng isang kilong **kaki** sa palengke.","translation":"Mom bought a kilo of **persimmons** at the market."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng kawalan ng kaayusan, sistema, o epektibong estruktura.
original_explanation: It's not just one person being messy; it's the entire system collapsing into chaos. This is the root cause of a `desorganisado` event. It's when the "plan" is just a bunch of conflicting ideas in a Viber group chat. The `desorganisasyon` is strong with this one.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **desorganisasyon** sa opisina ang dahilan ng mabagal na trabaho.","translation":"The **disorganization** in the office is the reason for the slow work."},{"sentence":"Malinaw ang **desorganisasyon** sa pamamalakad ng ahensya.","translation":"The **disorganization** in the agency's management is clear."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malayang estado o pamayanan, lalo na isang demokratikong republika. Sa kasaysayan ng Pilipinas, ito ay tumutukoy sa panahon (1935-1946) kung kailan ang bansa ay isang komonwelt ng Estados Unidos.
original_explanation: For most Filipinos, this word means one thing: traffic. It's the name of a super long, super wide avenue in Quezon City notorious for its legendary traffic jams, earning it the nickname "killer highway." Historically, it was our "in-a-relationship-but-it's-complicated" status with the USA before full independence. Now, it's just a place where your patience and driving skills go to die.
usage_notes: Heavily associated with Commonwealth Avenue in Quezon City. The historical meaning refers to the Commonwealth of the Philippines (1935–1946).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Panahon ng **Komonwelt** ay isang mahalagang yugto sa kasaysayan ng Pilipinas.","translation":"The **Commonwealth** Period is an important chapter in Philippine history."},{"sentence":"Grabe ang trapik sa **Komonwelt** Avenue tuwing rush hour.","translation":"The traffic on **Commonwealth** Avenue is terrible during rush hour."}]

translation: to dress up; to get dolled up
meaning_filipino: Mag-ayos nang labis sa pananamit at itsura upang maging kaakit-akit.
etymology: From Spanish 'postura' meaning posture, figure, or appearance.
original_explanation: That feeling when you have a date or a big event, so you spend hours choosing your OOTD, doing your makeup, and fixing your hair. It's the 'extra' version of 'mag-ayos.' It's your 'glow-up' moment before heading out. Parang pupunta sa JS prom, pero ang totoo, bibili lang ng suka sa kanto.
usage_notes: Often implies dressing up in a stylish or fashionable, sometimes even flamboyant, way.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **mamustura** para sa party mamayang gabi.","translation":"You need to **dress up** for the party tonight."},{"sentence":"Bihira siyang **mamustura** kaya nagulat ang lahat nang dumating siya.","translation":"She rarely **dresses up**, so everyone was surprised when she arrived."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang serye ng magkakaugnay na mga post sa isang social media platform, na karaniwang nagsisimula sa isang pangunahing post at sinusundan ng mga kasunod na tugon o karagdagan mula sa orihinal na nag-post.
etymology: Hiram mula sa Ingles na "thread", na isang adaptasyon ng orihinal na kahulugan nito sa mga online forum at email chains.
original_explanation: The modern-day "mahaba-habang usapan." It's how you tell a long story, share a detailed 'chismis', or post a step-by-step recipe on Twitter or Facebook without cramming it all into one post. Usually starts with "(1/n)" and ends with a call to action like "RT to save a life" or a shameless plug for your Shopee affiliate links.
usage_notes: Ang salitang ito ay halos eksklusibong ginagamit sa konteksto ng social media (Twitter/X, Threads, Facebook, etc.).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May ginawa siyang **thread** sa Twitter tungkol sa kanyang nakakatakot na karanasan.","translation":"She made a **thread** on Twitter about her scary experience."},{"sentence":"Basahin mo yung buong **thread** para maintindihan mo ang isyu.","translation":"Read the whole **thread** so you can understand the issue."}]

meaning_filipino: Tuwid; hindi liko-liko o paligoy-ligoy.
original_explanation: How you wish your internet connection was. Also, how you wish people would be when they owe you money—no excuses, just payment. It describes a path without curves or a statement without sugarcoating.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **deretso** at malinis na linya ang kailangan sa disenyo.","translation":"A **straight** and clean line is needed for the design."},{"sentence":"Gusto ko ng **deretso** na sagot, oo o hindi lang.","translation":"I want a **direct** answer, just yes or no."}]

translation: to tie up; to bind; to restrain
meaning_filipino: Talìan nang mahigpit ang mga kamay o paa ng isang tao o hayop upang hindi makakilos.
original_explanation: Before handcuffs, there was igapos. It's what villains in old Pinoy action movies do to the damsel in distress. But in a modern 'hugot' sense, 'igapos' is what you feel when you're stuck in a toxic relationship or a dead-end job. You feel tied up, unable to move freely. 'Nais kong kumawala sa mga problemang gumagapos sa akin.' Boom.
usage_notes: Implies a more forceful and complete binding than just 'itali'. Often used for restraining a person or animal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Iginapos** ng mga tulisan ang bihag sa isang puno.","translation":"The bandits **tied up** the captive to a tree."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **igapos** ka ng iyong nakaraan.","translation":"Don't let your past **bind** you."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit at bilog na prutas na sitrus, kulay berde, na may maasim na lasa at karaniwang ginagamit bilang pampalasa sa pagkain at inumin.
original_explanation: The undisputed MVP of the Filipino kitchen. This tiny green orb is our answer to everything. Got a cold? *Kalamansi* juice. Is your pancit bland? Squeeze some *kalamansi*. Need to make sawsawan for your fried fish? *Kalamansi* with toyo. It's the sour-power that fuels the nation.
usage_notes: Also spelled 'calamansi' in English contexts. A staple ingredient in Filipino cuisine.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pigaan mo ng **kalamansi** ang pancit para sumarap.","translation":"Squeeze some **calamansi** on the pancit to make it taste better."},{"sentence":"Gumawa siya ng mainit na tsaang may pulot at **kalamansi** para sa ubo.","translation":"She made a hot tea with honey and **Philippine lime** for the cough."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang pagtapon o pag-apaw ng likido mula sa isang lalagyan, karaniwan dahil sa pag-alog o paggalaw.
original_explanation: That messy, sudden spill when you're carrying a full cup of coffee and you trip. It's the splash of soup from a bowl that's too full. Figuratively, it’s also what happens when you get eliminated from a contest or a team. 'Na-ligwak sa PBB' means they got kicked out of the Pinoy Big Brother house. From liquid spillage to being spilled out of a competition.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb (maligwak - to be spilled).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-ingat siya sa paglalakad upang maiwasan ang **ligwak** ng mainit na kape.","translation":"He walked carefully to avoid the **spillage** of the hot coffee."},{"sentence":"Maraming natalo sa unang round; malaki ang **ligwak** ng mga kalahok.","translation":"Many lost in the first round; the **elimination** of participants was huge."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng sunod-sunod at malakas na tunog na "kalabog" sa pamamagitan ng pagpukpok o pagbagsak ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is what your upstairs neighbor does at 3 AM. It's the sound of someone angrily dropping things, or a kid having a tantrum and banging doors. 'Huwag mong pakalabugin 'yung pinto!' is what your mom yells when you try to make a dramatic exit. It's the official verb for creating disruptive, noisy chaos.
usage_notes: Implies intentional or forceful action causing the noise.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinadyang **pakalabugin** ng bata ang mga takip ng kaserola.","translation":"The child intentionally **banged** the pot lids together."},{"sentence":"Nagalit si Aling Nena nang **pakalabugin** ng kapitbahay ang kanilang pader.","translation":"Aling Nena got angry when the neighbor **started banging** on their wall."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pag-uugali o hitsura na nagiging mas bata kaysa sa tunay na edad.
original_explanation: That tita who suddenly starts wearing crop tops and using Gen Z slang like "spill the tea, sis!" Or that tito who buys a sports car and starts dyeing his hair. It's when someone's vibe is going in reverse, age-wise. Can be a compliment ("Wow, pabata ka nang pabata!") or a slight diss ("Nagpapabata ka na naman.").
usage_notes: Often used in the phrase "pabata nang pabata" (getting younger and younger).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napansin ko, **pabataan** ka yata ngayon, anong sikreto mo?","translation":"I noticed you seem to be **getting younger** these days, what's your secret?"},{"sentence":"Hala, **pabataan** ang suot niya, parang hindi tumatanda.","translation":"Wow, her outfit is making her look **younger**, it's like she's not aging."}]

translation: to gather; to collect; to assemble
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-iipon o pagsasama-sama ng mga bagay o tao.
etymology: Nagmula sa salitang-ugat na 'tipon' at hulaping '-in'.
original_explanation: Ito yung command ng nanay mo na "Tipunin mo na yang mga laruan mo!" Or yung moment na you have to gather your strength (lakas ng loob) para mag-confess sa crush mo. It's the action of bringing scattered things—or your feelings—into one place.
usage_notes: Isang pandiwang nakapokus sa obheto (object-focused) ng salitang 'tipon'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **tipunin** ang lahat ng ebidensya laban sa kanya.","translation":"We need **to gather** all the evidence against him."},{"sentence":"Sinabihan ako ni Inay na **tipunin** ang mga tuyong damit sa sampayan.","translation":"Mom told me **to collect** the dry clothes from the clothesline."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang likas na espasyo o butas sa ilalim ng lupa o sa gilid ng bundok o dalampasigan.
original_explanation: A cave. Your bedroom before you decide to clean it up. The place where Batman hangs out. It's a natural hideout, perfect for explorers, bats, or for you when you're avoiding adult responsibilities.
usage_notes: The standard Filipino term for 'cave'. 'Kuweba' is a common synonym from Spanish 'cueva'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming paniki ang naninirahan sa madilim na **yungib** na iyon.","translation":"Many bats live in that dark **cave**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga sinaunang tao ay gumuhit sa mga pader ng **yungib**.","translation":"Ancient people drew on the walls of the **cave**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging lubos na pagod, walang lakas, at matamlay.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung itsura mo after ng 12-hour shift, plus 3 hours of traffic. 'Yung gusto mo na lang humilata at mag-scroll sa TikTok hanggang makatulog. You're not just tired, you're gulaylay. Your social battery is at -10%.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a state of extreme physical or mental fatigue. Synonymous with 'pagod na pagod'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Gulaylay** ang katawan ng mga manggagawa pagkatapos ng maghapong trabaho.","translation":"The workers' bodies were **exhausted** after a whole day of work."},{"sentence":"Napaupo na lang siya sa sahig dahil sa pagiging **gulaylay**.","translation":"He just sat on the floor from being so **worn out**."}]

translation: to expose to the sun; to sunbathe
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalantad ng isang bagay o ng sarili sa init at sikat ng araw, karaniwan upang matuyo o uminit.
original_explanation: What you do to your laundry after washing, or what you do to yourself in Boracay to get that "golden" tan (or a painful sunburn). Also what your mom does to daing (dried fish) in the backyard.
usage_notes: Can refer to drying things (laundry, fish) or to sunbathing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong **magbilad** sa arawan at baka masunog ang balat mo.","translation":"Don't **expose yourself to the sun** too much or your skin might get burned."},{"sentence":"Tinulungan ko si Nanay na **magbilad** ng mga nilabhang damit.","translation":"I helped Mom **put out** the washed clothes **to dry in the sun**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao sa isang kuwento, sitwasyon, o buhay ng iba na hindi pangunahing tauhan; isang taong may maliit o pansuportang papel lamang.
original_explanation: The feeling when you're in a group photo but you're the one holding the camera. You're essential to the plot of your friends' love lives (as the taga-payo or the driver), but you're not the 'bida'. You're the supportive bestie, the comic relief, the one who says 'Kaya mo 'yan, friend!' before the main character goes off to do something dramatic.
usage_notes: A loan phrase used in Taglish, especially by younger generations, to describe social roles or feelings of being unimportant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayoko nang maging **side character** sa love story ng iba, gusto ko na ng sarili kong bida.","translation":"I don't want to be a **side character** in someone else's love story anymore, I want to be my own main character."},{"sentence":"Sa teleserye ng buhay mo, ako ba 'yung best friend na laging napapahamak o 'yung random na **side character**?","translation":"In the TV series of your life, am I the best friend who's always in trouble or just a random **side character**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang Ingles na ginagamit bilang malambing na tawagan para sa isang minamahal o kasintahan.
original_explanation: The default term of endearment when you can't remember if you're "mahal," "bebe," "hon," or "labs" for the day. It's the universal password for Filipino couples. "Kumain ka na ba, babe?" is our "I love you."
usage_notes: Used interchangeably with "baby," "bebe," "bhie." Primarily used in romantic contexts but sometimes used casually between close friends.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uwi ka na, **babe**, hindi na ako galit.","translation":"Come home now, **babe**, I'm not mad anymore."},{"sentence":"Anong gusto mong kainin, **babe**?","translation":"What do you want to eat, **babe**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang puwersang patuloy na ipinapataw sa isang bagay; ang pakiramdam ng pagka-apura o stress dahil sa mga panlabas na salik.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na deadline na bukas pero nasa Episode 2 ka pa lang ng bagong K-drama. O 'yung tanong ng mga tita mo na 'Kailan ka ikakasal?'. Pwede ring literal, like high blood pressure dahil sa stress o sa dami ng kinain mong lechon.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa parehong literal (pisikal na puwersa) at metaporikal (mental o emosyonal na stress) na kahulugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nararamdaman ko ang **presiyon** na makapasa sa board exam.","translation":"I feel the **pressure** to pass the board exam."},{"sentence":"Dapat mong bantayan ang **presiyon** ng iyong dugo.","translation":"You should monitor your blood **pressure**."}]

translation: Proper (as in a noun); Specific; Exclusive
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na partikular, natatangi, o hindi pangkalahatan. Sa balarila, ito ay tumutukoy sa tiyak na ngalan ng tao, bagay, pook, o pangyayari.
etymology: From `pan-` (prefix indicating kind or type) + `tangi` (sole, only, special).
original_explanation: This is the VIP of grammar. While 'bansa' (country) is for everyone (pambalana), 'Pilipinas' is **pantangi**—it's special, it's specific. It's the difference between 'a man' and 'Daniel Padilla.' It's exclusive, one-of-a-kind, not for general admission. Your name is a pangngalang **pantangi**. You're special!
usage_notes: Most commonly encountered in grammar lessons as 'pangngalang pantangi' (proper noun).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang 'Maria' ay isang halimbawa ng pangngalang **pantangi**.","translation":"'Maria' is an example of a **proper** noun."},{"sentence":"Ang Palasyo ng Malakanyang ay isang pangalang **pantangi** para sa isang tiyak na lugar.","translation":"Malacañang Palace is a **proper** name for a specific place."}]

translation: to pout, to sob with pouting lips
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-iyak na may kasamang pagnguso o pagbaluktot ng labi, karaniwang ginagawa ng mga bata bilang pagpapakita ng pagtatampo.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'sadboi' face. Yung itsura ng bata na hindi nabigyan ng candy, magngunguso tapos mag-uumpisang maiyak. It's the 'pa-cute' or 'pa-awa' cry. Yung lower lip, nanginginig at naka-pout. The ultimate weapon of a toddler in distress.
usage_notes: Strongly associated with children's tantrums or pouting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Humihibi** ang bata dahil inagaw ang kanyang laruan.","translation":"The child is **sobbing with pouting lips** because his toy was taken."},{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang **humibi** diyan, hindi bagay sa'yo.","translation":"Stop **pouting** there, it doesn't suit you."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kondisyong medikal kung saan ang presyon ng dugo sa mga arterya ay patuloy na mataas; hipertensiyon.
original_explanation: This is the national sickness of people stressed out by traffic, bills, and chismis. When your tita tells you, 'Naku, aatakihin ako sa puso sa'yo!' she's probably feeling her 'alta-presyon' acting up. It's the physical manifestation of being 'high blood' (pikon). The cure? Less stress, more chill, and maybe less patis.
usage_notes: Isang napakakaraniwang termino sa Pilipinas, ginagamit kapwa sa medikal at pang-araw-araw na konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinayuhan ng doktor ang pasyente na iwasan ang maaalat na pagkain dahil sa kanyang **alta-presyon**.","translation":"The doctor advised the patient to avoid salty food because of his **high blood pressure**."},{"sentence":"Tumaas ang **alta-presyon** niya nang malaman ang masamang balita.","translation":"Her **blood pressure** rose when she heard the bad news."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na maingat at masigasig sa pag-aalaga o pagtanggap sa iba, lalo na sa mga bisita.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `mapag-` (na nagsasaad ng ugali o hilig) + `asikaso` (pag-aalaga o pag-aasikaso).
original_explanation: Ito 'yung tita mo na pagdating mo pa lang sa bahay nila, aalukin ka agad ng pagkain, tubig, at tatanungin kung kumportable ka. Sila 'yung "Feel at home!" ang motto sa buhay. Sa office, siya 'yung laging nag-ooffer ng kape o nagche-check kung okay ka lang. The ultimate host/hostess with the mostest.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit upang ilarawan ang katangian ng isang tao, lalo na sa konteksto ng pagtanggap ng bisita.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakaswerte mo sa biyenan mo dahil **mapag-asikaso** siya sa lahat ng tao.","translation":"You are very lucky with your mother-in-law because she is **accommodating** to everyone."},{"sentence":"Kilala ang mga Pilipino sa pagiging **mapag-asikaso** sa mga dayuhan.","translation":"Filipinos are known for being **hospitable** to foreigners."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aksyon ng pagpukol o pagbato ng isang bagay mula sa isang lugar patungo sa iba, karaniwang gamit ang kamay.
original_explanation: This is what you do to your ex's stuff when you finally move on. Or what your nanay does with the tsinelas when you've been naughty. It's the physical version of 'yeet.' 'Huwag kang maghagis ng basura kung saan-saan!' is the battle cry of every environmentalist and concerned citizen.
usage_notes: Maghagis is the infinitive/command form. Naghagis (past), Naghahagis (present), Maghahagis (future).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Maghagis** ka ng barya sa wishing well para matupad ang hiling mo.","translation":"**Throw** a coin into the wishing well so your wish will come true."},{"sentence":"Sinabihan siya ng nanay niya na huwag **maghagis** ng bato sa bubong.","translation":"His mother told him not to **throw** stones at the roof."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bahagi o dibisyon ng isang malaking sistema, lalo na sa lipunan, ekonomiya, o pamahalaan.
original_explanation: Parang sa society, may BPO sector, agricultural sector, at 'yung sector ng mga marites. It's a specific area or group within a bigger system. Kumbaga, 'yung pamilya niyo may 'sektor ng mga panganay na laging inuutusan' at 'sektor ng mga bunso na laging spoiled.'
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa pormal na usapan tungkol sa ekonomiya, gobyerno, o lipunan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **sektor** ng agrikultura ay mahalaga sa ekonomiya ng Pilipinas.","translation":"The agricultural **sector** is important to the Philippine economy."},{"sentence":"Maraming manggagawa sa pribadong **sektor** ang apektado ng pandemya.","translation":"Many workers in the private **sector** were affected by the pandemic."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maging sapat o husto upang matugunan ang isang pangangailangan o pamantayan.
original_explanation: When the portions at the unli-wings place finally defeat you. It’s when your sweldo is just enough to cover bills, luho, and a little bit for savings, and you say, "Puwede na." It’s the state of being 'sakto lang,' no more, no less. Hindi kulang, hindi sobra. It's the goal when you're trying to fit all your pasalubong into one balikbayan box.
usage_notes: Implies sufficiency or meeting a required amount or standard. Often used with 'para' to specify what it is enough for.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang isang libong piso ay hindi **makahuhusto** para sa lingguhang gastusin.","translation":"One thousand pesos will not **be enough** for the weekly expenses."},{"sentence":"Sana'y **makahusto** ang dala nating pagkain para sa lahat.","translation":"I hope the food we brought will **suffice** for everyone."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbaba ng antas ng tubig sa dagat o karagatan, na naglalantad sa bahagi ng dalampasigan na karaniwang nasa ilalim ng tubig.
etymology: Mula sa Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *taSik na nangangahulugang 'dagat' o 'tubig-alat'. Ang kahulugan sa Tagalog ay nagbago upang tumukoy sa 'pagbaba ng tubig'.
original_explanation: 'Yan yung time na 'umuurong' yung dagat, kaya ang lawak ng beach! Perfect time para mag-beach combing, maghanap ng shells, o maglakad-lakad sa basang buhangin. Kabaligtaran ng high tide. Parang sahod, minsan high tide (kakakuha lang), madalas tahik (petsa de peligro na).
usage_notes: Madalas na ipinagpapalit sa salitang "kati" na may kaparehong kahulugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming natuyong damong-dagat sa dalampasigan kapag **tahik**.","translation":"There is a lot of dried seaweed on the shore during **low tide**."},{"sentence":"Hintayin nating mag-**tahik** bago tayo mamulot ng mga kabibe.","translation":"Let's wait for the **tide to go out** before we collect seashells."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa liturhiya ng Simbahang Katoliko, ito ang bahagi ng misa kung saan inihahanda at iniaalay sa Diyos ang tinapay at alak na magiging Katawan at Dugo ni Kristo.
original_explanation: This is that part of the Catholic Mass where they pass around the collection basket. While the choir sings a nice, solemn song, you see people bringing the bread and wine to the altar. It's the "alay" portion. For many kids (and adults), it's also the time to subtly check your phone or wonder what's for lunch.
usage_notes: Isang terminong panrelihiyon na partikular na ginagamit sa konteksto ng Misa sa Simbahang Katoliko.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula nang kumanta ang koro para sa **Opertoryo**.","translation":"The choir has started to sing for the **Offertory**."},{"sentence":"Inihanda ng mga sakristan ang mga alay para sa **Opertoryo**.","translation":"The sacristans prepared the gifts for the **Offertory**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paggaya sa kilos, pananalita, o anyo ng iba, kadalasan sa paraang nakakatawa o mapanukso.
original_explanation: This is the core skill of every Filipino comedian and the annoying little cousin at family reunions. **Panggagagad** is the art of copying someone's walk, talk, or mannerisms, usually for laughs. Think Michael V impersonating a politician or you mocking how your friend says "shocks!".
usage_notes: Often implies a playful or mocking imitation. 'Panggagaya' is a more neutral synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa kanyang mahusay na **panggagagad** sa mga sikat na artista.","translation":"He is known for his excellent **imitation** of famous actors."},{"sentence":"Itigil mo na ang **panggagagad** mo sa boses ko.","translation":"Stop your **mimicking** of my voice."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalabas ng malakas at katangi-tanging tunog ng tandang, karaniwang naririnig sa madaling-araw.
original_explanation: This is what your neighbor's rooster does at 4 AM, ruining your sleep and making you question your life choices. It's nature's most annoying alarm clock, the OG 'good morning' that nobody asked for.
usage_notes: Specifically used for the sound a rooster makes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumalaok** na ang manok ngunit tulog pa rin si Juan.","translation":"The rooster has **crowed** but Juan is still asleep."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagpapahintulot, nagbubulag-bulagan, o kumukunsinti sa maling gawain ng iba.
etymology: From Spanish 'consentidor' (one who consents or allows).
original_explanation: The 'ride or die' friend who holds your beer while you make bad decisions. The parent who buys their kid a new gadget after they broke the last one in a tantrum. The manager who lets their favorite employee get away with anything. A **kunsintidor** is the silent (or not-so-silent) partner in crime, the enabler of bad habits.
usage_notes: Carries a strong negative connotation, implying that the person is complicit in another's faults or wrongdoing by allowing it to happen.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **kunsintidor** sa katamaran ng iyong anak.","translation":"Don't be an **enabler** of your child's laziness."},{"sentence":"Pinarusahan din ang mga **kunsintidor** sa krimen.","translation":"The **condoners** of the crime were also punished."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pampalasang ginagamit sa pagluluto na nagmula sa pinatuyong bunga ng Piper nigrum. Ito ay karaniwang dinudurog at nagbibigay ng bahagyang anghang sa pagkain.
original_explanation: The other half of the iconic salt-and-pepper tandem on every Filipino dining table. It's that dark, spicy powder you accidentally put too much of in your sinigang, and now you're sneezing for an hour. It's the 'paminta' for the conyo crowd.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with the Tagalog word 'paminta,' but 'blackpepper' might be used to specify the ground black kind versus whole peppercorns (pamintang buo).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiabot ng **blackpepper**, kulang sa lasa ang adobo ko.","translation":"Please pass the **black pepper**, my adobo lacks flavor."},{"sentence":"Lagyan mo ng konting **blackpepper** ang steak para mas masarap.","translation":"Add a little **black pepper** to the steak to make it more delicious."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging maluwag; pagkakaroon ng sapat na espasyo; o ang pakiramdam ng ginhawa mula sa isang suliranin o bigat.
original_explanation: That feeling you get when you finally unbutton your jeans after a buffet. That's luwag. It can also be the "space" you need in a relationship (yikes), or the relief you feel when your toxic manager finally resigns. It's the emotional or physical breathing room we all crave.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for physical space/fit (`maluwag`) or figuratively for emotional relief (`kaluwagan`).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman ko ang **luwag** sa aking dibdib nang malaman kong ligtas siya.","translation":"I felt a **relief** in my chest when I found out he was safe."},{"sentence":"May **luwag** pa ba sa jeep? Isang tao na lang.","translation":"Is there still **space** in the jeep? Just for one person."}]

translation: to grieve; to feel deep sorrow
meaning_filipino: Ang makaranas ng matinding kalungkutan, pighati, o hapis, karaniwan dahil sa isang pagkawala o kabiguan.
original_explanation: This is a "main character in a teleserye crying in the rain" level of sadness. It's not just "sad" or "lungkot." It's deep, soul-crushing anguish. You mamighati when you lose a loved one, or when your favorite K-drama couple breaks up in the final episode. It’s a very formal, poetic word for being utterly heartbroken.
usage_notes: A formal and literary term for deep sadness. Not typically used in casual conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Patuloy siyang **mamighati** sa pagkawala ng kanyang alagang aso.","translation":"He continues to **grieve** the loss of his pet dog."},{"sentence":"Hindi dapat hayaang **mamighati** nang mag-isa ang isang kaibigan.","translation":"A friend should not be left to **feel deep sorrow** alone."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging hindi malinaw, mahirap unawain, o hindi tiyak.
etymology: Pinagsamang `pagka-` (kalagayan ng) at `malabo`, na galing sa salitang `labo` (hindi malinaw).
original_explanation: Ito yung status ng relasyon niyo na 'M.U.' or 'it's complicated'. Yung instructions ng boss mo na parang abstract art. Yung CCTV footage ng isang krimen na parang kuha sa patatas. It's the 'ano daw?' and 'paki-ulit nga' feeling.
usage_notes: Ang gitling ay opsyonal ngunit madalas gamitin upang bigyang-diin ang dalawang bahagi ng salita. Maaaring gamitin para sa pisikal na kalabuan o konseptuwal na kalabuan.
