usage_notes: A very common, informal, and highly critical expression. It is a strong insult. The adjective form is 'makapal ang mukha'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **kapal ng mukha** siyang humingi ulit ng pabor matapos kang hindi bayaran.","translation":"He has the **nerve** to ask for another favor after not paying you."},{"sentence":"Anong **kapal ng mukha** mo para magpakita rito!","translation":"What **audacity** you have to show your face here!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging hindi inalagaan, binalewala, o hinayaang mangyari ang isang bagay nang walang pakikialam. Ito ay nasa anyong pangkasalukuyan.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "pina-" at hulaping "-an" na ikinabit sa salitang-ugat na "pabaya".
original_explanation: Ito yung status mo nung iniwan ka niya sa ere. Yung halaman na hindi mo diniligan for a week. Yung project na 'bahala na si Batman' ang naging motto. Basically, the official state of 'seen-zoned' people and things.
usage_notes: Past tense. Indicates something was neglected or someone was allowed to do something. The meaning depends heavily on context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pinabayaan** niya ang kanyang pag-aaral kaya siya bumagsak.","translation":"He **neglected** his studies, which is why he failed."},{"sentence":"**Pinabayaan** na lang ng nanay ang bata na maglaro sa ulan.","translation":"The mother just **allowed** the child to play in the rain."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pag-aalis o pagpatay sa lahat ng anyo ng mikroorganismo, tulad ng bacteria, virus, at fungi, mula sa isang bagay o ibabaw upang ito ay maging ganap na malinis at ligtas.
original_explanation: This is what you do to your baby's feeding bottle so they don't get sick. It's also what your dentist does to their scary-looking tools. `Mag-isterilisa` is basically giving germs the "you shall not pass!" treatment. Level-up sa paghugas lang.
usage_notes: Commonly used in medical, laboratory, and food preparation contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **mag-isterilisa** ng mga bote ng sanggol pagkatapos gamitin.","translation":"Don't forget to **sterilize** the baby bottles after use."},{"sentence":"Ang mga siruhano ay kailangang **mag-isterilisa** ng kanilang mga kagamitan bago ang operasyon.","translation":"The surgeons need to **sterilize** their instruments before the operation."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa katangian ng pagiging mabangis, malupit, o matapang sa paraang nakakatakot.
original_explanation: The vibe your mom gives you when you come home past curfew. It's that intense, no-nonsense fierceness. Think of a strict BPO team leader during crunch time, or a kontrabida in a teleserye giving that death glare. It's pure, unadulterated intensity.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun (kabagsikan) or an adjective (mabalasik). The root word itself often functions as an adjective.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kitang-kita ang **balasik** sa mga mata ng tigre.","translation":"The **fierceness** in the tiger's eyes was very visible."},{"sentence":"May **balasik** ang kanyang mga salita nang magalit siya.","translation":"His words were **fierce** when he got angry."}]

translation: to give a salary; to pay a wage
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbibigay ng sahod o sweldo sa isang manggagawa bilang kabayaran sa kanyang serbisyo.
original_explanation: Ito yung pinakahihintay na moment ng bawat empleyado tuwing ika-15 at ika-30 ng buwan. Yung action ng amo mo na i-release na ang sweldo para may pambayad ka na sa bills, pang-shopping sa Shopee, at pang-treat sa sarili. Kapag sinabing "pasahurin mo na 'yan," ibig sabihin, "ibigay mo na ang bayad, deserve niya 'yan!"
usage_notes: The command form is "Pasahurin mo na sila" (Pay them their salary now).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **pasahurin** ang mga empleyado sa tamang araw.","translation":"The employees must **be paid their salary** on the correct day."},{"sentence":"Iniutos ng manager na **pasahurin** na nang maaga ang lahat dahil sa parating na bagyo.","translation":"The manager ordered for everyone **to be paid their salary** early because of the coming typhoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang napakasamang pangyayari na nagdudulot ng malaking kalungkutan, pagdurusa, o pagkawasak.
original_explanation: That feeling when you drop your Jollibee Chickenjoy on the floor. Or on a more serious note, it's the plot of every Filipino drama where someone gets amnesia, finds out their long-lost sibling is their mortal enemy, or the bus scene in the final episode. It's life hitting you with a "plot twist" you never asked for.
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang ilarawan ang mga malulungkot na kaganapan, mula sa personal na problema hanggang sa malawakang sakuna.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malaking **trahedya** ang pagguho ng gusali na kumitil sa maraming buhay.","translation":"The collapse of the building that claimed many lives was a great **tragedy**."}]

translation: to persevere, to be patient, to endure
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita ng katatagan, pagtitiis, at kasipagan sa pag-abot ng isang layunin o sa pagharap sa isang mahirap na sitwasyon nang hindi sumusuko.
original_explanation: This is your life motto when the internet is slow, the MRT breaks down, and your sahod is still five days away. It's the art of "sige, keri lang" even when everything is testing your patience. The patron saint of call center agents on a toxic account and students finishing their thesis.
usage_notes: Often used to encourage someone to keep going despite difficulties.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magtiyaga** ka lang sa pag-aaral at makakamit mo rin ang iyong mga pangarap.","translation":"Just **persevere** in your studies and you will achieve your dreams."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **magtiyaga** sa mahabang pila para makakuha ng ayuda.","translation":"You need to **endure** the long line to get financial aid."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paunang taya o pusta sa isang laro, lalo na sa baraha, bago pa man magsimula ang paglalaro.
original_explanation: The 'pay to play' fee in a card game. It's the money you put in the pot before you even see your cards. In life, it's the risk you take before you know the outcome, like confessing to your crush. 'Sige, mag-ante ka na,' is what your tito says before taking all your money in pusoy dos.
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of gambling and card games.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bawat manlalaro ay kailangang maglagay ng sampung pisong **ante**.","translation":"Each player needs to put in a ten-peso **bet**."},{"sentence":"Tumaas ang **ante** sa huling round ng poker.","translation":"The **stake** went up in the final round of poker."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malaking isda sa dagat na may mahaba at matulis na nguso, karaniwang tinatawag na isdang-ispada.
etymology: Possibly from Malay 'sugi' meaning 'comb', referring to its dorsal fin.
original_explanation: The MVP of the palengke's 'pang-steak' section. This is the fish you buy when you want to feel a little fancy. It's big, meaty, and has a nose long enough to poke your ex's new partner from a safe distance. Perfect for grilling or making 'fish steak' with a lot of onions and toyo-mansi. Also known as swordfish or marlin.
usage_notes: Often sold in steaks or fillets in Philippine wet markets (palengke).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng **malasugi** sa palengke para i-ihaw mamaya.","translation":"Mom bought **marlin** at the market to grill later."},{"sentence":"Masarap gawing fish steak ang sariwang **malasugi**.","translation":"Fresh **swordfish** is delicious when made into fish steak."}]

meaning_filipino: Pilitin ang isang tao na makipagtalik nang labag sa kanyang kalooban; manlapastangan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "gahasa" na nangangahulugang puwersa o dahas.
original_explanation: This is a heavy, serious word with no witty explanation. It refers to the horrific act of violating someone sexually. It's the verb form of 'gahasa' (rape). There's no sugarcoating this. It's a crime, plain and simple.
usage_notes: Isang napakatindi at seryosong termino na ginagamit sa mga legal at pormal na konteksto upang ilarawan ang sekswal na pang-aabuso.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May mabigat na parusa sa sinumang mangangahas na **gahasain** ang isang tao.","translation":"There is a severe penalty for anyone who dares to **rape** a person."},{"sentence":"Naglakas-loob ang biktima na isumbong ang tangkang **gahasain** siya.","translation":"The victim gathered the courage to report the attempt to **sexually assault** her."}]

translation: to exchange for; to trade for; to cheat on (someone) for (someone else)
meaning_filipino: Ibigay ang isang bagay bilang kapalit ng iba; o, sa konteksto ng relasyon, palitan ang kasintahan o asawa para sa ibang tao.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `i-` (nagsasaad ng sanhi), `pag-` (nagsasaad ng kilos), at `palit` (change, exchange).
original_explanation: The ultimate "hugot" verb. This is what happens when your S.O. leaves you for someone else. "Saan ako nagkulang?" On a less dramatic note, it's also what you do when you trade your old phone for a new one, or when you swap your lunch with a co-worker's. "Huwag mo akong **ipagpalit** sa mas bata, ha?"
usage_notes: Ang bagay/tao na isinusuko ay ang tuwirang layon, at ang bagay/tao na ipinapalit dito ay ang di-tuwirang layon. Mayroon itong mabigat na emosyonal na kahulugan sa konteksto ng relasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ipinagpalit** niya ang kanyang kotse para sa isang motorsiklo.","translation":"He **traded** his car **for** a motorcycle."},{"sentence":"Masakit malaman na **ipinagpalit** ka niya sa matalik mong kaibigan.","translation":"It hurts to know that he **cheated on** you **with** your best friend."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mga katangian, kasanayan, o tagumpay na nagpapatunay na ang isang tao ay angkop o may kakayahan para sa isang partikular na trabaho o posisyon.
original_explanation: That long list under "Requirements" in a job posting that makes you question all your life choices. "Required kalipikasyon: 5 years experience for an entry-level job." It's the evidence you bring to prove you're not just faking it.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with the English word in Taglish. The native spelling 'kuwalipikasyon' is also accepted.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano-ano ang mga **kalipikasyon** na hinahanap ninyo para sa trabahong ito?","translation":"What are the **qualifications** you are looking for for this job?"}]

translation: to imitate; to copy; to mimic
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtulad o pagkopya sa isang partikular na tao, bagay, kilos, o katangian.
etymology: From 'gaya' (to imitate) + '-in' suffix, creating a transitive verb.
original_explanation: This is the command form of 'gaya'. It's what you tell someone NOT to do: 'Huwag mo akong gayahin!' (Don't copy me!). It's the act of doing a celebrity impression, copying your seatmate's answer, or trying to replicate a recipe you saw on YouTube.
usage_notes: A transitive verb that requires a direct object (the thing being copied). The user query included 'gayagin' which is a common but non-standard variant; 'gayahin' is the standard form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **gayahin** ang signature ni Michael Jackson.","translation":"He tried to **imitate** Michael Jackson's signature."},{"sentence":"Madaling **gayahin** ang istilo niya sa pananamit.","translation":"It's easy to **copy** her style of dressing."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagtitipon o salu-salo bilang pamamaalam sa isang taong aalis o lilipat ng lugar.
original_explanation: The official 'mamimiss ka namin' party for someone leaving for abroad, a new job, or getting married. It’s that one last blowout filled with food, kantahan, and promises to 'keep in touch' that you'll try your best to keep via Messenger.
usage_notes: Commonly associated with OFWs leaving the country or someone moving away.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghanda kami ng **dispedida** para kay Ana bago siya lumipad papuntang Canada.","translation":"We prepared a **farewell party** for Ana before she flew to Canada."}]

meaning_filipino: Alisin sa puwesto o kapangyarihan, lalo na ang isang pinuno o monarko.
original_explanation: This is some serious Game of Thrones level action. It's when you overthrow the king, or when the office votes out the ridiculously strict manager. It has major historical and political vibes, like what people power aims to do.
usage_notes: A very formal and somewhat archaic word, mostly used in historical, political, or literary contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaisa ang mga mamamayan upang **italungkas** ang mapang-aping diktador.","translation":"The people united to **oust** the oppressive dictator."},{"sentence":"Sa kuwento, ang masamang hari ay pinilit na **italungkas** ng kanyang mga nasasakupan.","translation":"In the story, the evil king was forced to be **dethroned** by his subjects."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manggagamot na dalubhasa sa pag-aalaga ng mga babaeng nagdadalang-tao, sa panganganak, at sa panahon pagkatapos manganak.
original_explanation: The doctor who's with you through the whole pregnancy journey, from the first ultrasound 'kilig' to the final 'push!' moment in the delivery room. They're the VIPs of childbirth. This is the English term, often used interchangeably with the Tagalog 'obstetrisyan'.
usage_notes: This is the direct English loanword. 'Obstetrisyan' is the Filipinized spelling and is also very common. Often shortened to 'OB' or 'O.B-Gyne'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong magpatingin sa aking **obstetrician** para sa buwanang check-up.","translation":"I need to see my **obstetrician** for my monthly check-up."},{"sentence":"Ang aking O.B., na isang **obstetrician**, ang nagpaanak sa akin.","translation":"My O.B., who is an **obstetrician**, was the one who delivered my baby."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang pangkusina na de-kuryente na ginagamit para sa paulit-ulit na mga gawain sa paghahanda ng pagkain tulad ng paghiwa, pagtadtad, paggiling, at paghahalo.
original_explanation: 'Yung appliance na best friend ng mga tamad maghiwa ng sibuyas at bawang. Isang pindot mo lang, durog na ang kalaban. Perfect para sa mga gustong magluto pero ayaw sa "manual labor" ng prep work. It's the "auto" mode of the kitchen.
usage_notes: Used in contexts of cooking and kitchen appliances.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang **foodprocessor** para gawing pino ang mga mani.","translation":"She used the **food processor** to finely grind the peanuts."},{"sentence":"Mas mabilis maghanda ng pesto gamit ang **foodprocessor**.","translation":"It's faster to prepare pesto using a **food processor**."}]

translation: to say to someone's face; to confront
meaning_filipino: Sabihin nang harapan, diretsahan, at walang paligoy-ligoy sa isang tao ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay isang akusasyon, puna, o katotohanan.
etymology: Mula sa 'pa-' + 'mukha' + hulaping '-an'. Literal na 'iharap ang isang bagay sa mukha ng iba'.
original_explanation: When you're done with the subtweets and the 'parinig' and you just say it directly to their face. 'Hoy, utang mo, bayaran mo na!' It's the verbal equivalent of a screenshot sent to the person in the screenshot. No more hiding, it's confrontation time. Prangkahan to the highest level.
usage_notes: Nagtataglay ng malakas na diwa ng komprontasyon at pagiging direkta.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **pamukhaan** ng mga pagkakamali ko sa harap ng maraming tao.","translation":"Don't **confront me with** my mistakes in front of many people."},{"sentence":"**Pinamukhaan** niya sa akin ang lahat ng tulong na ibinigay niya.","translation":"He **rubbed in my face** all the help he had given."}]

translation: is fixing; is arranging; is getting ready
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglalagay sa tamang kaayusan, pagkukumpuni ng sira, o paghahanda sa sarili para sa isang okasyon.
etymology: From "ayos" (order, fix, arrangement) with the prefix "nag-a-".
original_explanation: This has three main vibes. 1) The "Tito mode": nag-aayos ng sirang gripo. 2) The "Marie Kondo" mode: nag-aayos ng magulong kwarto. 3) The "Gandang-ganda sa sarili" mode: nag-aayos for a date, which can take anywhere from 15 minutes to 3 business days.
usage_notes: A very versatile word. Context is key to know if it means fixing something broken, arranging items, or grooming oneself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nag-aayos** ako ng mga gamit ko sa aparador.","translation":"I **am arranging** my things in the cabinet."},{"sentence":"Teka lang, **nag-aayos** pa ako ng sarili ko.","translation":"Wait a minute, I'm still **getting myself ready**."},{"sentence":"Si Tatay ay **nag-aayos** ng bubong na may butas.","translation":"Dad **is fixing** the hole in the roof."}]

translation: to feel, to perceive, to sense
meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang makaranas o makapansin ng isang pisikal o emosyonal na sensasyon.
etymology: From 'ma-' (potential/ability prefix) + 'ramdam' (a variant of damdam, meaning feeling/sensation) + '-an' (locative/referential suffix).
original_explanation: That gut feeling you get when your crush walks into the room, or the slight chill you feel when you think you're being watched. It's when you sense something is off with your friend even if they say 'okay lang ako.' Basically, your internal emotional/physical sensor is going off. 'May naramdaman ka ba?' (Did you feel that?) can be about an earthquake or about the kilig.
usage_notes: This verb is in the potential aspect, meaning 'to be able to feel' or 'to happen to feel'. The root is 'damdam', and a related verb form is 'damhin' (to intentionally feel something). 'Maramdaman' focuses on the experience of the sensation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula na niyang **maramdaman** ang epekto ng gamot.","translation":"He started to **feel** the effects of the medicine."},{"sentence":"Sana'y **maramdaman** mo ang tunay kong pagmamahal.","translation":"I hope you **feel** my true love."},{"sentence":"Wala akong **maramdaman** na sakit.","translation":"I don't **feel** any pain."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na piraso ng tinapay, biskwit, o pastry na may masarap na palamang sa ibabaw, at karaniwang inihahain bilang pampagana.
etymology: From French 'canapé' (appetizer). The name is a figurative comparison to a person sitting on a sofa.
original_explanation: The tiny, one-bite snack you see at fancy parties or hotel buffets. It's what you eat while trying to look sophisticated, holding a glass of wine in your other hand. You're supposed to eat it in one go, but you always try to nibble at it, only for the topping to fall off. The eternal struggle.
usage_notes: Used in culinary or catering contexts. This is a homonym of 'kanape' (sofa).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghanda siya ng iba't ibang **kanape** para sa mga bisita.","translation":"She prepared various **canapés** for the guests."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan, karaniwang natitiklop at yari sa papel, tela, o katutubong materyales, na iwinawasiwas upang lumikha ng hangin at magbigay-ginhawa sa init.
etymology: From "pan-" + "paypay" (to wave or fan). The "n" in the prefix "pan-" assimilates to "m" before a root word starting with 'p'.
original_explanation: The non-electric aircon of the Philippines. Your tita's best friend during church, your lola's weapon for getting your attention, and a must-have accessory when commuting via jeepney. Comes in many forms, from the elegant abaniko to the freebie fan from a local politician's campaign.
usage_notes: Can refer to a folding fan (abaniko) or a fixed fan (like those made of anahaw leaves).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa matinding init, hindi niya mabitawan ang kanyang **pamaypay**.","translation":"Because of the intense heat, she couldn't let go of her **hand fan**."},{"sentence":"Isang magandang **pamaypay** na gawa sa anahaw ang regalo niya sa akin.","translation":"A beautiful **hand fan** made of anahaw was her gift to me."}]

translation: to last; to take a long time
meaning_filipino: Manatili sa isang kalagayan, lugar, o gawain sa loob ng mahabang panahon; umabot nang matagal.
original_explanation: This is what you wish your sahod (salary) would do, but it never does. It's also what you tell your friend who's taking forever to get ready: "Huy, magtagal ka pa ba dyan?" It's the opposite of a 'quickie' meeting; it's the 3-hour meeting that could have been an email.
usage_notes: Often used to ask about duration or to describe something that endures.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **magtagal** ang ating pagsasama.","translation":"I hope our relationship will **last**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magtagal** sa palengke at baka maubusan tayo ng ulam.","translation":"Don't **take too long** at the market, or we might run out of dishes to cook."}]

translation: to be the cause of fulfillment/implementation
meaning_filipino: Ang maging sanhi ng pagsasakatuparan o pagganap sa isang pangako, plano, o tungkulin.
original_explanation: This is the "how" behind your "New Year's Resolution." If your resolution is to get fit, your 'ikatupad' might be finally using that gym membership you've been paying for. It's the reason something planned actually happens. The cause of the "action" in your "action plan."
usage_notes: The 'ika-' prefix highlights the reason or means by which something is fulfilled. The subject of the sentence is the cause of the fulfillment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagkakaisa ng grupo ang **ikătutupad** ng aming proyekto.","translation":"The group's unity will **be the cause of fulfillment** for our project."},{"sentence":"Sana ang panalo sa lotto ang **ikatupad** ng mga pangarap ko.","translation":"I hope winning the lottery will **be the cause of fulfillment** for my dreams."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaikling at kolokyal na salita para sa 'automobil' o kotse.
original_explanation: Your four-wheeled baby. The reason you're perpetually broke from gas price hikes. The status symbol you wash every Sunday. It's not a formal word like 'kotse' or 'sasakyan,' it's what you say when you're talking to your friends: 'Pre, gamitin ko auto mo, ha?' It's a very 90s Titos/Titas of Manila vibe.
usage_notes: Colloquial term for a car. 'Kotse' and 'sasakyan' are more common and standard.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipagawa mo na ang gasgas sa **auto** mo.","translation":"Have the scratch on your **car** fixed already."},{"sentence":"Ang ganda naman ng bago mong **auto**!","translation":"Your new **car** is so beautiful!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbibigay o paghahandog ng isang bagay, serbisyo, o maging ng sarili para sa isang partikular na layunin, tao, o diyos.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you write 'I dedicate this thesis to...' It's the 'alay-lakad' during Holy Week, the flowers you offer at a hero's monument, or the song you sing for your crush during a contest. It's giving something up, big or small, for a higher purpose or for someone you value.
usage_notes: May matinding konotasyon ng paggalang, sakripisyo, o malalim na pagmamahal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang tula ay isang **pag-aalay** sa mga bayani ng bansa.","translation":"Her poem is a **dedication** to the heroes of the country."},{"sentence":"Ang **pag-aalay** ng bulaklak sa altar ay bahagi ng kanilang ritwal.","translation":"The **offering** of flowers on the altar is part of their ritual."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang ginagamit upang tukuyin ang pinagmulan, pinanggalingan, o lugar ng kapanganakan o paninirahan ng isang tao.
original_explanation: The ultimate ice breaker question in the Philippines after 'Anong pangalan mo?' is 'Taga-saan ka?'. This little word tells people your origin story, whether you're a city slicker (taga-Manila) or a promdi (taga-probinsya).
usage_notes: Madalas na sinusundan ng gitling (-) kapag idinurugtong sa isang tiyak na pangalan ng lugar (hal. taga-Cebu), ngunit maaaring tumayong mag-isa sa mga tanong (hal. Taga saan ka?).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Taga**-Baguio ang pamilya ng nanay ko.","translation":"My mother's family is **from** Baguio."},{"sentence":"Tinanong niya ako kung **taga** saan ako.","translation":"He asked me where I am **from**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang damdamin ng hindi pagiging masaya o kontento sa isang sitwasyon, bagay, o kinalabasan.
original_explanation: The feeling you get when your online shopping order finally arrives and it looks nothing like the picture. It's the 'sana all' you mutter when you see your friends' travel photos. The general 'meh' feeling of adulting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroong pangkalahatang **kawalang-kasiyahan** sa mga empleyado dahil sa mababang sahod.","translation":"There is a general **dissatisfaction** among the employees due to the low wages."},{"sentence":"Ang **kawalang-kasiyahan** niya sa buhay ay halata sa kanyang mga kilos.","translation":"His **discontentment** with life is obvious in his actions."}]

translation: to have something consulted; to refer for consultation
meaning_filipino: Ang paghingi ng payo o opinyon mula sa isang tao o pangkat tungkol sa isang bagay; ang pagdulog sa isang eksperto o awtoridad.
original_explanation: This is the adulting version of "Ma, okay lang ba 'to?" You're basically taking a problem—be it a weird rash, a legal document, or a questionable life choice—and showing it to an expert. "Doc, pa-check up po." "Atty, pa-consult po." You're not just asking, you're formally seeking professional advice.
usage_notes: Commonly used in formal, medical, legal, or academic contexts. The prefix "magpa-" causes the action of "sangguni" (to consult).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magpasangguni** sa isang abogado tungkol sa kontratang iyan.","translation":"You need to **have** that contract **consulted** with a lawyer."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hindi gaanong karaniwan o makalumang anyo para sa bilang na siyamnapu.
etymology: A contracted form of 'siyam na pu'. A less common, somewhat archaic variant of 'siyamnapu'.
original_explanation: This is the OG, old-school way of saying 'siyamnapu' (ninety). It's the vintage version. If someone uses this, they're either a lolo from the province, a language purist, or trying to sound poetic. It's the vinyl record to 'siyamnapu's Spotify stream.
usage_notes: Considered archaic or poetic by most modern speakers. 'Siyamnapu' is overwhelmingly preferred in both speech and writing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa mga lumang aklat, mababasa ang salitang **siyampu**.","translation":"In old books, one can read the word **ninety** (siyampu)."},{"sentence":"Ang bilang ng mga taon ay umabot na sa **siyampu**.","translation":"The number of years has reached **ninety**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang inuming de-bote o de-lata na karaniwang may karbonasyon, asukal, at pampalasa, at hindi naglalaman ng alkohol.
original_explanation: The lifeblood of any Pinoy handaan. From the 'tindahan' staple Coke, Royal, and Sprite, to the iconic Zesto for baon. It's the go-to partner for everything from pizza to pancit. You know it's a real party when someone brings out the 1.5L bottle.
usage_notes: A fully assimilated English loanword, commonly used and understood throughout the Philippines. Often spelled as one word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Palamig ka muna, heto ang **softdrink**.","translation":"Cool down first, here's a **soft drink**."},{"sentence":"Bili ka nga ng dalawang litrong **softdrink** sa kanto.","translation":"Please buy a two-liter **soft drink** at the corner store."}]

translation: Hanger; rack; hook; place to hang things
meaning_filipino: Isang bagay o lugar kung saan maaaring isabit, ikawit, o ibitin ang mga gamit tulad ng damit, tuwalya, o bag.
original_explanation: The unsung hero of your messy room. It's the chair where you throw all your 'pambahay' and 'panlakad' clothes. Technically, it's supposed to be a proper hook, a clothes rack, or a hanger ('sabit' is the action, 'sabitan' is the object/place). But for many Pinoys, that one 'The Chair' is the ultimate sabitan.
usage_notes: Can refer to a single hook, a full rack, or a clothesline.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Wala na akong mapag-**sabitan** ng mga damit ko.","translation":"I have no more **place to hang** my clothes."},{"sentence":"Bumili siya ng bagong **sabitan** para sa mga susi.","translation":"She bought a new **hook rack** for the keys."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagluluto ng isang bagay sa mainit na mantika.
etymology: From 'prito' + '-hin' suffix, making it an object-focus verb.
original_explanation: The verb form of the national pastime. It's the command you give or receive when a delicious, crispy meal is on the horizon. 'Prituhin mo na 'yung isda!' is a call to action. It's the process that turns a simple tilapia into a golden, crunchy masterpiece.
usage_notes: This is an object-focus verb. The actor is in 'ng' form and the object is in 'ang' form (e.g., Prituhin mo ang isda).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **prituhin** ang manok para sa hapunan.","translation":"Don't forget **to fry** the chicken for dinner."},{"sentence":"Masarap **prituhin** ang tira-tirang adobo.","translation":"It's delicious **to fry** leftover adobo."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pambihira at di-pangkaraniwang pangyayari na pinaniniwalaang gawa ng isang higit na makapangyarihang puwersa o ng Diyos.
etymology: From Sanskrit 'hima' meaning 'snow, frost', possibly through a metaphorical extension of something rare and wondrous like snow in a tropical land.
original_explanation: When you survive a week of deadlines on just 3 hours of sleep per night, that's a himala. When you find a parking spot at the mall on a payday weekend, himala. When your crush finally replies to your message after 3-5 business days, "Walang himala!" (Just kidding, that's a himala too). It's any event that defies logic and makes you think a higher power intervened, or you just got incredibly, unbelievably lucky.
usage_notes: Famously used in the Nora Aunor movie "Himala" with the iconic line "Walang himala!" (There are no miracles!).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **himala** ang paggaling niya mula sa malubhang sakit.","translation":"His recovery from the serious illness was a **miracle**."},{"sentence":"Naghihintay ako ng **himala** para manalo sa lotto.","translation":"I'm waiting for a **miracle** to win the lottery."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng hindi pagbibigay o pagtanggi na ibigay ang isang bagay na hinihingi o nararapat.
etymology: From `pag-` (nominalizer) + `ka-` + `it` (from root `kait`, meaning 'to withhold, to deny').
original_explanation: This is the act of being "madamot" or selfish. It's when your friend asks for a piece of your chicharon and you say no. It's a company's `pagkakait` of a well-deserved promotion. On a deeper level, it can be the `pagkakait` of justice or rights. It’s the universe (or a person) telling you "access denied."
usage_notes: Often has a negative connotation, implying that what is being withheld is deserved or needed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkakait** ng tamang sahod ay labag sa batas.","translation":"The **withholding** of proper wages is against the law."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya maintindihan ang **pagkakait** sa kanya ng pagmamahal ng kanyang ama.","translation":"He couldn't understand the **denial** of his father's love for him."}]

meaning_filipino: Halagang ibinabayad bilang kabayaran para sa pinsalang nagawa, perwisyo, o pagkawala.
original_explanation: This is what you have to pay when you break the "you break it, you buy it" rule on a grand scale. Whether you bumped someone's car or broke a friend's heart, the **bayad-pinsala** is the price of making things right. Sometimes it's cash, sometimes it's a public apology, and sometimes it's treating them to a lifetime supply of milk tea.
usage_notes: A legal and social term. Can refer to monetary compensation awarded by a court or an informal settlement between parties. The synonym "danyos" is also commonly used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Humingi siya ng malaking **bayad-pinsala** mula sa kumpanyang nakasira sa kanyang ari-arian.","translation":"He asked for a large **indemnity** from the company that damaged his property."},{"sentence":"Ang paghingi ng tawad ay isang uri rin ng **bayad-pinsala**.","translation":"Asking for forgiveness is also a form of **compensation for damages**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malungkot at mahabang daing o panaghoy, karaniwang nagpapahayag ng matinding kalungkutan, sakit, o pagdadalamhati.
original_explanation: This isn't just a simple cry. This is the "MMK" theme song of sounds. It's the sound you make when you find out your favorite K-drama character died, or when you realize you left your wallet in the taxi. It's a deep, sorrowful sound, the official soundtrack for hugot moments and epic heartbreaks.
usage_notes: A highly evocative and literary word for a cry of deep sorrow. Often heard in poems, songs, and classic literature.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig sa buong kabahayan ang **taghoy** ng biyuda.","translation":"The widow's **lament** was heard throughout the house."},{"sentence":"Ang kaniyang tula ay puno ng **taghoy** para sa nawalang pag-ibig.","translation":"His poem was full of **wails** for a lost love."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng kasaganaan, kaginhawaan, at pagiging malaya sa hirap o tungkulin; luho.
original_explanation: This is the "sana all" life. Unlimited budget for Shopee, no traffic, 8 hours of sleep, eating whatever you want without gaining weight. It's the state of pure comfort and luxury, free from the daily grind. The opposite of "petsa de peligro."
usage_notes: Often implies a life of ease and pleasure, sometimes with a negative connotation of being spoiled.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lumaki siya sa **kalayawan** at hindi sanay sa hirap.","translation":"He grew up in **luxury** and is not used to hardship."}]

translation: shared with; gave a share to
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbibigay ng bahagi o parte ng isang bagay sa iba.
original_explanation: It's when you have one piece of Jollibee Chickenjoy left and your sibling gives you the 'pahingi' eyes. What you do next is 'kinahatian' mo siya. You split it. It’s sharing the bill, splitting the pizza, or giving your friend half of your baon because they 'forgot' theirs.
usage_notes: This is an object-focus verb form. 'Siya ay kinahatian ko' means 'I shared with him/her.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kinahatian** ko ng aking baon ang aking kaklase.","translation":"I **shared** my packed lunch **with** my classmate."},{"sentence":"Ang premyo ay **kinahatian** ng dalawang nanalo.","translation":"The prize was **shared by** the two winners."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pook-kalakalan kung saan maaaring magrenta ng computer na may internet access kada oras para sa paglalaro, pananaliksik, o pag-print.
original_explanation: Before everyone had WiFi and data, this was the temple for research, gaming (Dota!), and printing your thesis at 2 AM. Kilala rin bilang 'compshop'. Dito mo unang nalaman ang halaga ng 'piso-net'.
usage_notes: Madalas paikliin bilang 'compshop'. Bagama't nabawasan ang bilang dahil sa laganap na mobile data, nananatili itong mahalaga para sa mga gamer at sa mga nangangailangan ng printing services.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpaprint ako ng resume ko sa **computer shop** malapit sa amin.","translation":"I had my resume printed at the **computer shop** near our place."},{"sentence":"Puno na naman ng mga estudyanteng naglalaro ng online games ang **computer shop**.","translation":"The **computer shop** is once again full of students playing online games."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagputol sa isang bagay, tulad ng tela, papel, o damo, upang mabigyan ito ng hugis o nais na sukat.
original_explanation: The act of cutting with precision. Think of a sastre (tailor) about to magtabas of expensive cloth—no room for mistakes! It's also what your dad does to the lawn on a Saturday morning. Basically, it's 'gupit' but with a more constructive, shaping purpose.
usage_notes: Distinguished from 'pumutol' (to cut/snap) as 'magtabas' implies shaping or trimming to a desired form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magaling siyang **magtabas** ng tela para sa mga gown.","translation":"She is skilled at **cutting** fabric for gowns."},{"sentence":"Oras na para **magtabas** ng damo sa bakuran.","translation":"It's time to **trim** the grass in the yard."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi pa nasusuri o nabibigyan ng opisyal na halaga, marka, o pagtatasa.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'di-' (hindi) at salitang 'tasado' (mula sa Espanyol na 'tasado' - appraised).
original_explanation: That feeling when you apply for a loan and your property papers are still 'di-tasado'. Or when you're trying to sell your old phone and you have no idea how much it's worth. It's an unknown value, like your chances with your crush.
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of property, goods, or formal evaluation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi pa maaaring ibenta ang lupa dahil ito ay **di-tasado** pa ng gobyerno.","translation":"The land cannot be sold yet because it is still **unassessed** by the government."},{"sentence":"Ang mga alahas ay nananatiling **di-tasado** kaya't hindi malaman ang tunay na halaga.","translation":"The jewels remain **unappraised**, so their true value is unknown."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o kainan kung saan nagluluto at nagbebenta ng iba't ibang uri ng pansit.
original_explanation: The mothership. The holy ground. This is where you go when you have a specific pansit craving that mom's cooking can't satisfy. It's that corner eatery that's been there for decades, serving the best Pansit Malabon or the greasiest, most satisfying Pansit Canton in town. Your friendly neighborhood source for a "long life" fix.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to a place that sells pansit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Doon tayo kumain sa sikat na **pansitan** sa kanto.","translation":"Let's eat at the famous **noodle house** on the corner."},{"sentence":"Nag-order ako ng dalawang bilao ng pansit mula sa **pansitan** ni Aling Nena.","translation":"I ordered two large platters of pansit from Aling Nena's **pansit eatery**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng pagiging tulala, walang kamalay-malay, o nakanganga dahil sa pagtataka, pagkalito, o kawalan ng gagawin.
etymology: Reduplication of 'anga', which means to gape or be open-mouthed.
original_explanation: That look on your face when the prof calls you for recitation and you have zero idea what the topic is. Or when you're in a new city, looking up at the tall buildings with your mouth slightly open, making you a prime target for snatchers. "Huwag kang aanga-anga diyan!"
usage_notes: Carries a slightly negative and admonishing tone, implying that the person should be more aware or alert.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang tumayong **aanga-anga** diyan, tulungan mo ako!","translation":"Don't just stand there **gawking**, help me!"},{"sentence":"Naiwan siyang **aanga-anga** nang biglang umalis ang bus.","translation":"He was left **clueless** when the bus suddenly left."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagturo sa isang tao o bagay gamit ang daliri sa paraang mapanisi, galit, o nag-aakusa.
original_explanation: This isn't just regular pointing. This is the Marites-level pointing, full of accusation and drama. It's when you point your finger at someone like they stole the last piece of chicharon. It’s the physical gesture for 'Ikaw! Ikaw ang may kasalanan!' (You! It's your fault!).
usage_notes: Carries a strong negative connotation of accusation or blame, stronger than 'pagturo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagduro** niya sa akin sa harap ng lahat ay hinding-hindi ko malilimutan.","translation":"His **act of pointing at me accusingly** in front of everyone is something I will never forget."},{"sentence":"Itigil mo ang **pagduro** sa kapatid mo; hindi siya ang kumuha ng laruan mo.","translation":"Stop your **accusatory pointing** at your sibling; they didn't take your toy."}]

meaning_filipino: May hugis na tulad ng itlog o elipse; hugis-itlog.
original_explanation: A fancy, Spanish-sounding way to say 'oval.' You'd probably hear this from an old-school architect, a jeweler describing a gem, or your lola describing the shape of a fancy serving platter ('pinggan na obalado'). It's the more *sosyal* version of 'hugis-itlog'.
usage_notes: Hindi gaanong karaniwan kumpara sa 'obalo' o 'hugis-itlog'. May bahagyang teknikal o pormal na dating.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang salamin ay may **obalado** na kuwadro.","translation":"The mirror has an **oval-shaped** frame."},{"sentence":"Gusto niya ng mesang **obalado** para sa kanilang silid-kainan.","translation":"She wants an **oval-shaped** table for their dining room."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa lahat ng oras o pagkakataon; palagi; walang palya.
original_explanation: This is the more formal, slightly more poetic cousin of 'palagi'. You'd use it in a love song lyric ('Ikaw ang iibigin ko tuwina') or when you're trying to sound deep. It’s the 'forever and ever' of adverbs. It's the promise your internet provider makes about their connection speed, but rarely delivers.
usage_notes: Interchangeable with 'palagi' but carries a slightly more formal or literary tone. Can also be seen as 'tuwi-tuwina' for emphasis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tuwina**'y naaalala kita sa paglubog ng araw.","translation":"I **always** remember you at sunset."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-ibig ng ina ay naririyan **tuwina** para sa kanyang anak.","translation":"A mother's love is **always** there for her child."}]

translation: act of inviting or persuading (to come along)
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-anyaya o paghimok sa isa o higit pang tao na sumama sa isang gawain o lugar.
original_explanation: This is the official term for 'Tara, G!' or 'Sama ka?' It's the act of rounding up your friends for a coffee run, a road trip, or an ML session. It's less of a formal invitation and more of a friendly persuasion. The 'pagyayakag' is strongest when someone says, 'Libre ko!'
usage_notes: Implies a friendly, informal invitation to join an activity. The `pag-CV-` form suggests a more earnest or repeated invitation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang masayang **pagyayakag** niya ang dahilan kung bakit napasama ako sa kanilang lakad.","translation":"His/Her cheerful **act of inviting** was the reason I ended up joining their trip."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglala, pagtindi, o pag-igting ng isang damdamin, kalagayan, o pangyayari.
etymology: Root word 'sidhi' means intensity or severity.
original_explanation: That feeling when the 'kontrabida' in a teleserye goes from slapping to kidnapping. That's *pagsidhi*. It's when your crush not replying escalates to your crush being 'in a relationship' on Facebook. It's the intensification of feelings, drama, or even a typhoon's signal number. From bad to worse, or from good to great.
usage_notes: Often used to describe emotions, conflicts, weather, or situations that are becoming more extreme.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagsidhi** ng kanyang galit ay ikinabahala ng lahat.","translation":"The **intensification** of his anger worried everyone."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa **pagsidhi** ng bagyo, itinaas na sa Signal No. 3 ang aming lugar.","translation":"Due to the **worsening** of the typhoon, our area was raised to Signal No. 3."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pagkaing Italyano na binubuo ng isang patag, bilog na tinapay na nilalagyan ng sarsang kamatis, keso, at iba't ibang sahog, at niluluto sa hurno.
original_explanation: The ultimate group project food. Whether you're pulling an all-nighter for a thesis or just binge-watching a K-drama, a box of pizza solves everything. It's the national food of 'bahala na si Batman sa budget.' Bonus points for pineapple on pizza debates that can end friendships.
usage_notes: While the English word is used, the pronunciation is Filipinized.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-order tayo ng **pizza** para sa meryenda.","translation":"Let's order **pizza** for our snack."},{"sentence":"Hawaiian ang paborito kong **pizza**, kahit maraming may ayaw.","translation":"Hawaiian is my favorite **pizza**, even if many dislike it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang elektroniko na may iskrin na nagpapakita ng mga imahe o datos mula sa isang kompyuter.
original_explanation: That screen you're staring at right now, probably for way too long. For BPO agents, it's their window to the world (and to irate customers). For gamers, it's the portal to another universe. For your parents, it's 'the TV of the computer'.
usage_notes: A direct loanword from English. Used universally in the context of computers and technology.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng bagong **monitor** para sa aking setup.","translation":"I need a new **monitor** for my setup."},{"sentence":"Pakipunas ang alikabok sa **monitor** ng kompyuter.","translation":"Please wipe the dust off the computer **monitor**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang elektroniko na ginagamit upang mag-rekord at muling iparinig ang tunog, karaniwan sa pamamagitan ng magnetic tape.
original_explanation: The OG voice memo app. This was the high-tech gadget of your tito's generation, used for recording everything from family gatherings to their own singing voice for a "demo tape." Today, seeing a real grabador is like spotting a dinosaur. It's the ancestor of your smartphone's recording feature.
usage_notes: Now considered a dated or retro term. The verb form "i-record" is more common now.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ng lolo ko ang kanyang lumang **grabador** para i-record ang kasal namin.","translation":"My grandfather used his old **tape recorder** to record our wedding."},{"sentence":"May koleksyon siya ng mga cassette tape at isang gumaganang **grabador**.","translation":"He has a collection of cassette tapes and a working **recorder**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kabuuan ng mga kamag-anak o angkan; maaari ring tumukoy sa mga nakababatang miyembro ng pamilya.
etymology: From ka- + anak + -an suffix, denoting a collective group or the entirety of a lineage.
original_explanation: Think of it as the 'extended universe' of your family. It's not just the main cast (your immediate family), but all the spin-off characters (second cousins, grand-nephews) combined. Sometimes used to refer to all the 'bata' or younger folks in the clan.
usage_notes: While it can mean 'clan' or 'lineage', it's often used to refer to the collective nieces, nephews, and grandchildren of an elder.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagmamalaki ng lolo ang kanyang buong **kaanakan**.","translation":"The grandfather is proud of his entire **lineage**."},{"sentence":"Binigyan niya ng pamasko ang lahat ng kanyang **kaanakan**.","translation":"She gave Christmas gifts to all her **younger relatives** (nieces/nephews)."}]

translation: nowadays, in this era, at this time
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kasalukuyang yugto ng panahon, henerasyon, o kapanahunan.
original_explanation: The classic 'back in my day' starter pack, but for the present. 'Sa panahong ito, lahat nasa online na.' It's what your parents say when they're amazed or confused by TikTok, online banking, or the fact that you can have a full-time job talking to a computer. Also a great opening line for any 'state of the nation' type of rant.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit upang ikumpara ang kasalukuyan sa nakaraan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sa panahong ito**, napakadali nang kumalat ng pekeng balita.","translation":"**Nowadays**, it's so easy for fake news to spread."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang pinagbago ng teknolohiya **sa panahong ito** kumpara noong dekada nobenta.","translation":"Technology has changed a lot **in this era** compared to the nineties."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pang-abay na nagpapahiwatig ng pag-aalinlangan, kawalan ng katiyakan, o isang palagay tungkol sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: The official word for 'parang'. It's the verbal shrug you use when you're not 100% sure but you're making a calculated guess. 'Umuwi na siya **yata**.' (I think she went home already, but don't quote me on that). It's the ultimate get-out-of-jail-free card for chismis and assumptions. You're not stating a fact, just a 'yata'.
usage_notes: Usually placed after the word it modifies or at the end of a clause.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uulan **yata** mamaya kaya magdala ka ng payong.","translation":"**It seems** it will rain later, so bring an umbrella."},{"sentence":"Siya **yata** ang nanalo sa raffle.","translation":"**Perhaps** she was the one who won the raffle."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang matatag na paniniwala o tiwala sa kakayahan, katangian, o paghuhusga ng sarili o ng iba.
original_explanation: Ito yung energy na kailangan mo bago ka mag-ask for a raise sa boss mo, o bago ka umamin sa crush mo. Yung feeling na 'Kaya ko 'to!' kahit nanginginig ang tuhod. Lack of kompiyansa is why your brilliant idea stays in the drafts.
usage_notes: Can also mean trust in someone else ('may kompiyansa ako sa kanya').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mo ng **kompiyansa** sa sarili para magtagumpay.","translation":"You need self-**confidence** to succeed."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang **kompiyansa** ko sa kakayahan mong mamuno.","translation":"I have great **confidence** in your ability to lead."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging iniwan o tinapos ang relasyon ng isang kasintahan.
etymology: From the English verb "to dump" (discard), applied to romantic relationships.
original_explanation: The official relationship status when your jowa hits you with the classic "It's not you, it's me." You've been binned, bes. Time to queue up the Moira dela Torre playlist, grab a tub of ice cream, and prepare for a major 'hugot' session.
usage_notes: A very common slang term for being broken up with. It implies that the decision was one-sided.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kawawa naman si Anna, na-**dumped** siya ng boyfriend niya through text.","translation":"Poor Anna, she was **dumped** by her boyfriend through text."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos niyang ma-**dumped**, nag-makeover agad siya as a form of revenge glow-up.","translation":"After she got **dumped**, she immediately had a makeover as a form of revenge glow-up."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pariralang pang-abay na nagsasaad na ang isang kilos o pangyayari ay naganap nang dalawang ulit.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng 'dalawa' (two) at 'beses' (mula sa Espanyol na 'veces', na nangangahulugang 'times').
original_explanation: This is your classic 'second time's the charm'... or not. It's when you have to repeat your order at the drive-thru. It's checking your alarm **dalawang beses** to make sure it's set. It's the number of times your boss asks 'tapos na ba?' in one hour. Literally, two times. No more, no less.
usage_notes: Isang napakakaraniwang parirala na ginagamit upang bilangin ang mga pagkilos o pangyayari.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinabi ko na sa'yo nang **dalawang beses** na huwag kang pupunta doon.","translation":"I already told you **twice** not to go there."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong uminom ng gamot na ito nang **dalawang beses** sa isang araw.","translation":"You need to take this medicine **two times** a day."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang idyomatikong pahayag na nangangahulugang pagod na pagod o hingal na hingal, tulad ng isang aso na tumakbo nang malayo.
original_explanation: The feeling after climbing five flights of stairs because the elevator is broken, or after chasing the last jeep home. Your tongue feels like it's about to fall out of your mouth from exhaustion. "Friend, 5 minutes pa, **lawit na ang dila** ko sa pagtakbo!"
usage_notes: A very common expression to describe extreme physical exhaustion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagdating niya sa finish line, **lawit na ang dila** niya sa pagod.","translation":"When he reached the finish line, he was **panting from exhaustion**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng ilong na matulis o may mataas na bridge.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'ma-' at salitang ugat na 'tangos' (pointedness, prominence of the nose).
original_explanation: The nose that launched a thousand compliments (and maybe some insecurities). In the Philippines, having a 'matangos na ilong' is a prized beauty standard, often associated with Spanish or foreign ancestry. It's the opposite of 'pango' (flat-nosed). People with this nose are often told, 'Ang tangos ng ilong mo, pahingi naman!'
usage_notes: Halos eksklusibong ginagamit para ilarawan ang ilong ng isang tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marami ang nagsasabi na kamukha niya ang kanyang amang Kastila dahil sa **matangos** niyang ilong.","translation":"Many say she looks like her Spanish father because of her **high-bridged** nose."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang opisyal na pagbilang at pagtatala ng mga impormasyon tungkol sa populasyon ng isang bansa o lugar.
original_explanation: That time every few years when someone from the government knocks on your door to ask 'Ilan kayo dito?' and a bunch of other questions. It's how the government knows how many people to promise things to during the next election. Basically, a national attendance check.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayon sa huling **senso**, umabot na sa isandaang milyon ang populasyon ng Pilipinas.","translation":"According to the latest **census**, the population of the Philippines has reached one hundred million."},{"sentence":"Sumasailalim sa **senso** ang aming barangay ngayong linggo.","translation":"Our barangay is undergoing a **census** this week."}]

translation: to stick, to paste, to attach
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkabitin o pagdugtungin ang dalawang bagay sa pamamagitan ng isang malagkit na substansiya tulad ng pandikit o kola.
original_explanation: Basically, to make two things become one, using glue, tape, or even your feelings. Parang 'yung pag-attach ng resibo sa expense report, o pag-paste ng poster ng K-Pop idol mo sa pader. Can also be used for people who are inseparable, 'Para kayong pinagbiyak na bunga, laging **magkadikit**!'
usage_notes: Can refer to literally sticking objects together or figuratively for people being close to each other ('magkadikit').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **magdikit** ng mga anunsyo sa bulletin board.","translation":"Help me **paste** the announcements on the bulletin board."},{"sentence":"Ayaw **magdikit** ng tape dahil basa ang ibabaw.","translation":"The tape won't **stick** because the surface is wet."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hanay o saklaw ng mga magkakaibang posisyon, opinyon, o katangian sa pagitan ng dalawang sukdulan. Maaari ring tumukoy sa hanay ng mga kulay tulad ng sa bahaghari.
original_explanation: This is the official term for "it's complicated." Hindi lang black and white, may gray areas. Hindi lang masaya o malungkot, mayroon ding "okay lang." From political views to gender identity, the "ispektrum" shows us that life isn't a simple choice between A or B, but a whole rainbow of possibilities.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa mga akademik, siyentipiko, at panlipunang talakayan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan nila ang buong **ispektrum** ng mga opinyon ng publiko tungkol sa bagong batas.","translation":"They are studying the entire **spectrum** of public opinion regarding the new law."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang estado ng pagkawala ng malay o kamalayan, karaniwang dahil sa sakit, pinsala, o matinding pagkabigla.
etymology: Mula sa `ka-` + `wala` + `-an` (kawalan, "lack of"), `ng` ("of"), at `ulirat` (kamalayan o consciousness).
original_explanation: This is what happens when you see your crush holding hands with someone else, or when you check your bank account after a 12.12 sale. Biglang black out! It's the state of being "himatay" or knocked out, whether literally from a punch or figuratively from shock. Your brain just logs off.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa medikal na konteksto o sa paglalarawan ng matinding pisikal o emosyonal na kalagayan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala siya sa ospital dahil sa biglaang **kawalan ng ulirat**.","translation":"She was brought to the hospital due to a sudden **loss of consciousness**."},{"sentence":"Ang matinding init ay maaaring magdulot ng **kawalan ng ulirat**.","translation":"Extreme heat can cause a **loss of consciousness**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na naniniwalang mas nakatataas siya sa iba dahil sa kanyang katayuan sa lipunan, yaman, o kaalaman, at madalas ay minamaliit ang mga itinuturing niyang mas mababa.
original_explanation: Yung kakilala mong ayaw kumain sa karinderya kasi 'ew, it's so madumi'. Sila yung mga tipo na judge-mental sa brand ng damit mo at sa accent mo. Basically, the human version of a chihuahua in a designer bag.
usage_notes: Very common in both Filipino and Taglish. The pronunciation often adds an 'i-' sound at the beginning: /is-nob/.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **snob**, kausapin mo rin ang mga bagong kasamahan natin.","translation":"Don't be a **snob**, talk to our new colleagues too."},{"sentence":"Ayoko siyang kaibiganin dahil **snob** siya at matapobre.","translation":"I don't want to befriend her because she is **snobbish** and looks down on the poor."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na isinisingit o ipinapasok sa pagitan ng dalawang bagay upang magbigay-diin, suporta, o upang punan ang isang puwang.
etymology: From "singit" (groin, to insert), with the instrumental prefix "paN-".
original_explanation: That extra piece of paper you fold to stop a wobbly table? That's a paningit. It's the 'sige, isingit mo na lang' item sa budget plan. The friend who suddenly joins your duo and makes it a trio? Sila yung paningit sa friendship.
usage_notes: Can refer to a physical object or a person/thing inserted into a situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng piraso ng karton bilang **paningit** sa bintana para hindi ito umalog.","translation":"He used a piece of cardboard as a **wedge** for the window to stop it from rattling."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, **paningit** lang naman ang komento ko sa usapan ninyo.","translation":"Don't worry, my comment is just an **insert** in your conversation."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng puno (Casuarina equisetifolia) na kahawig ng puno ng pino dahil sa mga dahon nitong parang karayom, karaniwang tumutubo malapit sa mga baybayin.
original_explanation: The 'pine tree' of the Philippines, but it's a fraud! Hindi siya totoong pine tree. Siya 'yung friend mong nag-a-ala-foreigner pero taga-probinsya lang pala. Madalas makita sa beach, nagbibigay ng shade at 'Baguio feels' kahit nasa tabing-dagat ka.
usage_notes: Madalas mapagkamalang puno ng pino (pine tree) dahil sa mga dahon nitong parang karayom, ngunit hindi ito isang tunay na pino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakasarap magpahinga sa ilalim ng puno ng **aguho**.","translation":"It's so nice to rest under an **agoho tree**."},{"sentence":"Maraming **aguho** ang nakatanim sa baybayin ng Zambales.","translation":"There are many **agoho trees** planted along the coast of Zambales."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o establisyimento kung saan ginagawa at ibinebenta ang tinapay, keyk, at iba pang mga produktong galing sa hurno.
original_explanation: The happiest place on the corner of the street. It's where you go for your pandesal fix, your merienda of Spanish bread, or that birthday cake you forgot to order in advance. A **panaderya** is a core memory for every Filipino kid.
usage_notes: A staple in almost every Filipino neighborhood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumaan ka muna sa **panaderya** bago ka umuwi.","translation":"Please pass by the **bakery** before you go home."},{"sentence":"Amoy bagong lutong tinapay mula sa kalapit na **panaderya**.","translation":"It smells like newly baked bread from the nearby **bakery**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggalaw o pagpunta sa likuran ng isang tao o bagay; pagsubaybay sa galaw o pag-unlad ng isang bagay.
etymology: From 'sunod' (follow, next). The '-in-' infix and '-an' suffix with reduplication indicate the present progressive, object-focused tense.
original_explanation: What you do to your crush on Instagram. It's also what that creepy dude in the alley is doing. On a less dramatic note, it's what you do when you're following a recipe, a GPS route, or the latest chismis about your officemate.
usage_notes: Can be literal (physically following someone) or figurative (following a story, a trend, or instructions).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May pakiramdam akong may **sinusundan** sa akin pauwi.","translation":"I have a feeling someone is **following** me on my way home."},{"sentence":"**Sinusundan** ko ang bawat episode ng paborito kong serye.","translation":"I'm **following** every episode of my favorite series."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang masidhi at malalim na damdamin ng pagmamahal, pag-aaruga, at pagmamalasakit sa isang tao, bagay, o konsepto.
original_explanation: The national pastime. The reason for 99% of OPM songs, teleseryes, and hugot lines. It’s what makes you share your last piece of Jollibee Chickenjoy or wait for your BPO-worker partner to get home at 5 AM. It's more powerful than a typhoon signal #5 and more complicated than filing your taxes.
usage_notes: A very broad term for love, encompassing romantic love, familial love, love for country, etc. It's more profound than the simpler "mahal".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pag-ibig** sa bayan ay isang dakilang katangian.","translation":"**Love** for one's country is a noble characteristic."},{"sentence":"Maraming tula ang naisulat tungkol sa wagas na **pag-ibig**.","translation":"Many poems have been written about pure **love**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng paraan ng pagluluto, karaniwang hango sa lutuing Tsino, kung saan ang karne ay pinalalambot sa pamamagitan ng matagal na pagpapas蒸 (steaming) o pagpapakulo.
etymology: From Chinese Hokkien 燉 (tīm), meaning "to stew" or "to steam for a long time."
original_explanation: This 'tim' is that delicious, savory, fall-off-the-bone dish you order at a Chinese restaurant, like Pata Tim. It's slow-cooked to perfection, usually in a sweet and savory soy-based sauce. Think of it as the sophisticated, steamed cousin of adobo.
usage_notes: Almost always refers to a specific dish, like 'Pata Tim' (pork hock) or 'Manok na Tim' (chicken).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paborito kong orderin sa restawran ay ang pata **tim**.","translation":"My favorite thing to order at the restaurant is the pata **tim** (steamed pork hock)."},{"sentence":"Nagluto si Lola ng masarap na manok na **tim** para sa tanghalian.","translation":"Grandma cooked delicious steamed chicken (**tim**) for lunch."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o akto ng pagpapatunay na ang isang pahayag, paratang, o tao ay hindi totoo o nagsasabi ng kasinungalingan.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'receipts' move. It's when you expose the 'fake news' or call someone out on their lies with solid proof. Think of a lawyer discrediting a witness in court, or you showing your friend the screenshots that prove their ex was lying. 'Ayan, may ebidensya! This is pagpapasinungaling 101.'
usage_notes: A formal and strong term used when disproving a statement or accusation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang testimonya ay isang malinaw na **pagpapasinungaling** sa mga akusasyon laban sa kanya.","translation":"His testimony is a clear **refutation** of the accusations against him."},{"sentence":"Naglabas ng mga dokumento ang kumpanya para sa **pagpapasinungaling** sa mga maling balita.","translation":"The company released documents for the **disproval** of the fake news."}]

translation: to revive, to bring back to life, to support (a family)
meaning_filipino: Muling bigyan ng buhay ang isang bagay na patay o walang sigla; sustentuhan o suportahan ang pamilya.
original_explanation: The verb for when you're a necromancer, a first responder, or just trying to restart a dead conversation on a first date. Also, it's what OFWs do for their families back home—they 'buhayin' them by providing financial support. It can also mean reviving an old trend, like bringing back bell-bottoms.
usage_notes: Has a literal meaning (revive) and a figurative one (support financially, keep a family going).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng mga doktor na **buhayin** ang pasyente.","translation":"The doctors tried to **revive** the patient."},{"sentence":"Siya ang nag-iisang bumubuhay sa kanyang pamilya.","translation":"He is the only one supporting his family."},{"sentence":"Gusto nilang **buhayin** ang mga lumang awiting Pilipino.","translation":"They want to **revive** old Filipino songs."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng matamis na gawa sa pinakuluang katas ng tubo na inilagay sa bao ng niyog upang tumigas. Kilala rin bilang panutsa.
etymology: 'sang-' (one) + 'kaka' (a container, often a coconut shell half). So, 'one shell-full'.
original_explanation: This is the OG Filipino sweetener, the Lola's K-drama heartthrob before refined sugar became mainstream. It looks like a coconut shell filled with dark, hardened sugar. Perfect for 'taho' or just breaking a piece off to eat like candy when no one's looking.
usage_notes: Synonymous with 'panutsa' or 'panocha'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumagamit si Lola ng **sangkaka** para sa kanyang arnibal.","translation":"Grandma uses **panutsa** for her syrup."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mahikayat o mapaniwala sa isang ideya, argumento, o katotohanan.
original_explanation: That moment when your friend finally convinces you to buy that 10th milk tea of the week. "Sige na, last na 'to!" and you believe them. When you finally get your parents to say "yes" to a night out. When a "Maritess" tells you some chismis and you're like, "OMG, totoo nga?!" That's it. You've been *makumbinsi*.
usage_notes: The root word 'kumbinsi' is a direct borrowing. The Tagalog affix 'ma-' makes it a verb meaning 'to be able to convince' or 'to be convinced'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay **makumbinsi** ko si Inay na payagan akong sumama sa field trip.","translation":"I hope I can **convince** Mom to let me join the field trip."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi tumutubo, umuunlad, o lumalaki; nananatili sa isang kalagayan at walang pag-asenso.
original_explanation: Describes your savings account after a 12.12 sale. Also a perfect "hugot" for a dead-end job or a relationship that's going nowhere. "Nasa comfort zone ka pa rin? Stuck ka na, bes. Di-lumalago."
usage_notes: Can be used for plants, businesses, personal development, or relationships. Describes a state of being stagnant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang halaman ay **di-lumalago** dahil kulang sa sikat ng araw.","translation":"The plant is **not growing** because it lacks sunlight."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam niya ay **di-lumalago** ang kanyang karera sa kumpanyang iyon.","translation":"She feels her career is **stagnant** in that company."}]

meaning_filipino: Labis na paghanga sa kagandahan ng isang bagay, tao, o lugar; lubos na pagkagusto.
original_explanation: When someone is so beautiful it hits you twice. It's that feeling when you see your crush's new profile pic and you can't help but stare. 'OMG, gandang ganda ako sa bago mong haircut!' It's also used when you *really* like something, not just visually. 'Gandang ganda ako sa plot twist ng K-drama na 'to!'
usage_notes: The phrase expresses intense admiration or liking. The subject who feels this admiration is usually in the 'ako/siya/sila' form. For example, 'Gandang ganda *ako* sa'yo' (I find you extremely beautiful).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Gandang ganda** si Maria sa suot niyang bestida.","translation":"Maria is **extremely fond** of the dress she is wearing."},{"sentence":"**Gandang ganda** ang mga turista sa mga tanawin sa Palawan.","translation":"The tourists find the sights in Palawan **extremely beautiful**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang selyo o tatak na inilalagay sa mga dokumento, sulat, o produkto bilang tanda ng pagiging opisyal, pagbabayad ng buwis, o pagpapatunay.
original_explanation: Before email and DocuSign, there was 'timbre'. This is the official stamp that makes a document legit. Think of the notary public's seal, the 'selyo' on your diploma, or even the stamp on a package that says "PAID". It's the government's way of saying, "We see you, and this is official."
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin nang palitan sa salitang 'selyo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng **timbre** mula sa munisipyo para maging balido ang kasulatan.","translation":"A **seal** from the municipal hall is needed for the document to be valid."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang produkto na idinisenyo upang maglabas ng samyo at takpan o alisin ang mga hindi kanais-nais na amoy sa isang espasyo.
original_explanation: The magical spray or gel that tries to convince you your bathroom smells like 'Fresh Linen' or 'Ocean Breeze' instead of, well, a bathroom. It's the first thing taxi drivers hang on their rearview mirrors. That little cardboard tree is a cultural icon.
usage_notes: An English loanword used directly in Tagalog. No common Filipino equivalent is used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng bagong **airfreshener** para sa kotse.","translation":"I bought a new **air freshener** for the car."},{"sentence":"Amoy lavender ang buong banyo dahil sa **airfreshener**.","translation":"The whole bathroom smells like lavender because of the **air freshener**."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa parehong sandali; nang walang pagkaantala o pagpapaliban; agad-agad.
etymology: From ka- + agad. The prefix 'ka-' adds emphasis to the immediacy.
original_explanation: The most optimistic word in the Filipino vocabulary. When your mom says 'Linisin mo 'yan kaagad,' she means NOW, not after one more TikTok video. It's the opposite of 'mamaya na.' In the world of online shopping, it's what you hope for when you see 'sameday delivery.'
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'agad', but 'kaagad' can add a slight emphasis on the immediacy and is very common in commands.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumawag ka **kaagad** pagdating mo roon.","translation":"Call **immediately** when you get there."},{"sentence":"Ubusin mo **kaagad** ang pagkain habang mainit pa.","translation":"Finish the food **right away** while it's still hot."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pakiusap o magalang na paraan ng pagsasabi na nais bumili ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: The magic word you say at the sari-sari store. 'Pabili po!' is the national anthem of anyone needing anything from suka to phone load. It's the polite way of saying 'I want to buy...' and instantly gets the tindera's attention.
usage_notes: Extremely common in commerce, especially in small, local stores. Often followed by 'po' for politeness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pabili** po ng isang kilong bigas.","translation":"I'd like to **buy** one kilo of rice, please."},{"sentence":"Narinig ko siyang sumigaw ng '**pabili**!' sa tindahan.","translation":"I heard him shout '**I'd like to buy**!' at the store."}]

meaning_filipino: Maintindihan o maabot ng isip ang kahulugan, katwiran, o kalikasan ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: The goal of every "hugot" post, every cryptic tweet, and every parent's lecture. It's more than just hearing; it's about getting it, feeling it in your soul. "Sana'y umunawa ka kung bakit kailangan kong umalis." — a classic line from every Filipino movie breakup scene.
usage_notes: A deeper form of understanding than 'maintindihan'. It implies comprehension on an empathetic or intellectual level.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **umunawa** sa isang taong ayaw magpaliwanag.","translation":"It is difficult **to understand** a person who refuses to explain."},{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **umunawa** rin siya sa bigat ng kanyang responsibilidad.","translation":"Finally, he **understood** the weight of his responsibility."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pakikipag-ugnayan, pakikipag-usap, o pagiging bahagi ng isang grupo ng mga tao sa isang panlipunang pagtitipon.
original_explanation: That thing your tita tells you to do at family reunions instead of just staring at your phone. 'Uy, 'wag kang KJ (killjoy), makisalamuha ka naman!' It's about getting out of your shell and actually talking to people. The opposite of being a wallflower.
usage_notes: Strongly implies active social interaction and mingling within a group.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahiyain si Ana kaya nahihirapan siyang **makisalamuha** sa mga bagong kaklase.","translation":"Ana is shy, that's why she finds it difficult **to socialize** with new classmates."},{"sentence":"Pumunta ka sa party para **makisalamuha** at magkaroon ng mga bagong kaibigan.","translation":"Go to the party **to mingle** and make new friends."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang aparato na naglilipat ng mga tao o bagay sa pagitan ng mga palapag ng isang gusali.
original_explanation: The Tagalized, phonetic spelling of 'elevator'. This is how your lola might write it down. It's the magic box in the mall that saves you from the escalator when you're carrying a mountain of shopping bags.
usage_notes: This is a less common, phonetic spelling. The English word "elevator" is used much more frequently in conversation and writing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sira daw ang **elebeytor**, kaya sa hagdan tayo.","translation":"They said the **elevator** is broken, so we'll take the stairs."},{"sentence":"Pindutin mo ang para sa 5th floor sa **elebeytor**.","translation":"Press the button for the 5th floor in the **elevator**."}]

translation: Fare for a taxi; Money for a taxi
meaning_filipino: Perang nakalaan o ibabayad para sa pagsakay sa isang taksi.
original_explanation: This is your 'pamasahe' but specifically for a taxi. It's the budget you set aside for that Grab or taxi ride when you're running late for work, or when it's raining cats and dogs and the MRT is packed like a can of sardines. 'Ma, pahingi ng **pantaksi**, male-late na ako!'
usage_notes: A colloquial term formed using a standard Filipino word-formation pattern. While understandable, 'pamasahe sa taxi' is more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtabi ako ng saktong pera para **pantaksi** pauwi mamayang gabi.","translation":"I set aside the exact amount of money for **taxi fare** going home later tonight."},{"sentence":"Kulang pa ang naipon ko na **pantaksi** papuntang airport.","translation":"The money I saved for the **taxi ride** to the airport is still not enough."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malapad na ibabaw, karaniwang kulay itim o madilim na berde, na sinusulatan gamit ang tisa (chalk), at kadalasang matatagpuan sa mga silid-aralan.
original_explanation: Ah, the OG PowerPoint. The blakbord was the battleground of every Filipino student's childhood. It's where you solved math problems under pressure, where your teacher drew the map of the Philippines from memory, and where the 'cleaners' had to erase everything, creating a cloud of chalk dust that was probably bad for everyone's lungs. Synonymous with 'pisara'.
usage_notes: Used interchangeably with 'pisara'. 'Blakbord' feels slightly more informal or colloquial.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakibura ng mga sulat sa **blakbord** bago magsimula ang susunod na klase.","translation":"Please erase the writings on the **blackboard** before the next class starts."},{"sentence":"Isinulat ng guro ang aming takdang-aralin sa **blakbord**.","translation":"The teacher wrote our homework on the **blackboard**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng pagkakaroon ng hindi magandang damdamin, hinanakit, o galit sa isang tao na nag-ugat sa isang di-pagkakaunawaan o masamang karanasan.
etymology: Kombinasyon ng "sama" (masama) at "loob" (panloob na damdamin), na literal na nangangahulugang "kasamaan ng kalooban".
original_explanation: Ito yung state of being niyo ng dati mong bestie matapos niyang i-spill ang sikreto mo. Hindi kayo galit na nagsisigawan, pero ramdam mo yung bigat sa hangin, yung 'di na kayo nagpapansinan sa office pantry. Parang silent war, a cold war of emotions.
usage_notes: Isang malalim at madalas na magkabilang panig na damdamin ng hinanakit. Mas matindi kaysa sa 'tampo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **samaan ng loob** sa pagitan ng magkapatid ay tumagal nang maraming taon.","translation":"The **grudge** between the siblings lasted for many years."},{"sentence":"Dapat nating iwasan ang **samaan ng loob** upang mapanatili ang kapayapaan.","translation":"We should avoid having **ill feelings** to maintain peace."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng puno (Cananga odorata) na may mababangong dilaw na bulaklak na karaniwang ginagamit sa paggawa ng pabango.
etymology: From Tagalog 'ilang' (wilderness), possibly meaning "flower of the wilderness". The repetition signifies emphasis or distinction.
original_explanation: That super fragrant, star-shaped, yellowish flower that smells like the quintessential 'Pinoy garden' or what lola's house smells like. Its oil is used for fancy perfumes, but for us, it's the scent that reminds you of Flores de Mayo or a calm provincial afternoon.
usage_notes: Refers to both the tree and its flower. The name is internationally spelled as ylang-ylang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakabango ng mga bulaklak ng **ilang-ilang** sa kanilang bakuran.","translation":"The **ylang-ylang** flowers in their yard are very fragrant."},{"sentence":"Ang langis mula sa **ilang-ilang** ay sikat na sangkap sa mga pabango.","translation":"The oil from the **ylang-ylang** is a popular ingredient in perfumes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maliit na daga na may puting balahibo, karaniwang ginagamit sa mga eksperimento sa laboratoryo.
original_explanation: Literally 'white mouse.' This is what you call someone who's always the test subject for new things, like your friend who tried the new milk tea flavor first. 'Sige, ikaw na mauna, ikaw naman ang dagang-puti ng barkada.' Also, the actual lab animal.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for the animal or figuratively for a test subject.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginagamit ang mga **dagang-puti** sa pag-aaral ng mga bagong gamot.","translation":"**White mice** are used in studying new medicines."},{"sentence":"Para akong **dagang-puti** sa bagong sistema ng kumpanya; sa akin lahat tinetesting.","translation":"I feel like a **guinea pig** for the company's new system; they're testing everything on me."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa lupa na nabungkal, malambot, at buhaghag, karaniwang resulta ng pag-aararo o paghuhukay.
original_explanation: Yung lupa after paglaruan ng aso mong naghahanap ng buto. O yung lupa sa garden ni lola na ready na para tamnan ng pechay. Basically, soil that's been fluffed up and is no longer solid.
usage_notes: Primarily used in agricultural or gardening contexts. Describes the state of the soil.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Halimbukay** na ang lupa kaya't madali itong tamnan.","translation":"The soil is already **loose** so it's easy to plant on."},{"sentence":"Nag-iwan ng **halimbukay** ang mga naghukay sa kalsada.","translation":"The diggers left behind **turned-over soil** on the road."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na ginagawa, nangyayari, o natatanggap tuwing linggo; minsan sa isang linggo.
etymology: Mula sa salitang 'linggo' (week) at hulaping '-han' na nagpapahiwatig ng pagiging regular.
original_explanation: Ito yung allowance mo galing sa magulang, o kaya yung sahod mo sa part-time job na every Friday mo nakukuha. Pwede ring ito yung schedule ng team meeting niyo na laging Lunes ng umaga. Weekly basis, bes.
