usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pang-uri (e.g., 'lingguhang sahod' - weekly salary) o pang-abay (e.g., 'Lingguhan siyang umuuwi' - He goes home weekly).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumatanggap siya ng **lingguhang** sahod mula sa kanyang trabaho.","translation":"She receives a **weekly** salary from her job."},{"sentence":"**Lingguhan** ang aming pagpupulong sa opisina.","translation":"Our office meetings are held **weekly**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbigkas ng pangalan ng isang tao upang makuha ang kaniyang atensyon, o ang pag-anyaya sa kaniya na lumapit o dumalo.
original_explanation: This is what your mom does from the first floor when you're on the second, and it sounds like she's about to summon a demon, but really she just wants you to get the "toyo" from the sari-sari store. Also what you do to call a meeting, a taxi, or your dog who refuses to come inside.
usage_notes: Can be used for calling a person's name, calling for a meeting, or hailing a ride.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magtawag** ka ng mga bata dahil handa na ang hapunan.","translation":"**Call** the children because dinner is ready."},{"sentence":"Ang pangulo ay nagpasyang **magtawag** ng isang press conference.","translation":"The president decided to **call** a press conference."}]

meaning_filipino: Nakaangat, naka-alsa, o lumalabas mula sa isang patag na ibabaw.
original_explanation: Like that one pilit-na-pilit nail on the wall that you always snag your shirt on. Or your tiyan after a grand fiesta buffet. Anything that's sticking out when it should be flat is usli.
usage_notes: Commonly used to describe physical objects or body parts that are sticking out.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natusok ako sa pako na **usli** mula sa dingding.","translation":"I was pricked by the nail **sticking out** from the wall."},{"sentence":"Kitang-kita ang **usli** niyang buto sa balikat dahil sa kanyang kapayatan.","translation":"His shoulder bone was clearly **protruding** because of his thinness."}]

translation: to adapt; to fit; to make suitable
meaning_filipino: Isaayos o ibagay ang isang bagay upang maging angkop, wasto, o katugma sa iba pa.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "i-" at salitang-ugat na "agpang" (lapat, akma).
original_explanation: Similar to 'iakma' but feels a bit more technical, like fitting a puzzle piece. It's making two different things work together. For example, you iagpang the new software to the old computer system, or you iagpang the curriculum to the students' learning pace.
usage_notes: Medyo pormal at hindi kasing-karaniwan ng "iakma" sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinusubukan ng karpintero na **iagpang** ang bagong pinto sa lumang hamba.","translation":"The carpenter is trying to **fit** the new door to the old frame."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **iagpang** ang mga dayuhang tradisyon sa ating sariling kultura.","translation":"It's difficult to **adapt** foreign traditions to our own culture."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsukat sa isang bagay gamit ang dangkal, o ang distansya mula sa dulo ng hinlalaki hanggang sa dulo ng kalingkingan kapag nakaunat ang kamay.
original_explanation: This is the OG measuring tape before measuring tapes were cool. You know when your lola needs to measure something, like fabric sa palengke or the space for a new 'last supper' painting, and she uses her hand? That's 'dumangkal'. It's the ultimate 'bahala na' system of measurement. Close enough is good enough.
usage_notes: An informal and traditional method of measurement, not used for precise technical work.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dinangkal** niya ang mesa para malaman kung kasya sa pinto.","translation":"She **measured the table by handspan** to see if it would fit through the door."},{"sentence":"Sinabihan ako ni Nanay na **dumangkal** ng dalawang dangkal ng tela.","translation":"Mom told me to **measure by handspan** two spans of cloth."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong pinili at binigyan ng kapangyarihan upang magpasya sa isang alitan o hindi pagkakasundo.
original_explanation: The person in the middle. In sports, it's the referee. In law, it's the arbitrator. In a family squabble over the last piece of lechon, it's the lola whose decision is final and absolute. The 'arbitro' holds the power.
usage_notes: Can refer to a legal arbitrator or a sports referee.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **arbitro** ang nagbigay ng pinal na desisyon sa laban.","translation":"The **referee** gave the final decision in the match."},{"sentence":"Itinalaga siya bilang **arbitro** sa kaso ng dalawang malaking korporasyon.","translation":"He was appointed as the **arbitrator** in the case between the two big corporations."}]

meaning_filipino: Ipasok at iparada ang sasakyan sa loob ng isang garahe.
original_explanation: This is your dad yelling at you at 10 PM because you left the car on the street. 'Igarahe mo na 'yang kotse!' It's the official end of a road trip or a long day of driving. It's the verb form of putting something (usually a car) to its proper resting place for the night.
usage_notes: Specifically means to park in a garage, but can be used colloquially to mean 'to park' in general, especially at home.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **igarahe** mo nang maayos ang sasakyan para may madaanan.","translation":"Please, **park** the car properly in the **garage** so there's a path."},{"sentence":"Gabi na, oras na para **igarahe** ang motor.","translation":"It's late, time to **park** the motorcycle **in the garage**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging mabangis; kalupitan, karahasan, o pagiging suwail at walang awa.
original_explanation: This is villain-level cruelty. It's not just being mean; it's the savagery of a predator, the brutality of a dictator, or the ferocity of your mom when she finds out you failed a subject. It's the opposite of 'chill'.
usage_notes: A strong word used to describe extreme cruelty or wildness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ikinuwento ng mga biktima ang **kabangisan** na dinanas nila sa kamay ng mga kidnapper.","translation":"The victims recounted the **brutality** they experienced at the hands of the kidnappers."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay o pagpapahid ng pintura sa isang bagay o lugar.
original_explanation: The command you give someone (or yourself) when a surface looks sad and needs a splash of color. It's the 'verb' version of making things pretty. 'Uy, pinturahan mo naman 'yang pader, mukha nang luma.'
usage_notes: This is a verb in the object-focus form. The object being painted is the focus of the sentence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **pinturahan** ang buong bahay bago ang Pasko.","translation":"We need to **paint** the whole house before Christmas."},{"sentence":"**Pinturahan** mo ng puti ang pinto para magmukhang bago.","translation":"**Paint** the door white so it looks new."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyong balbal na nangangahulugang perpekto, walang mali, o kahanga-hanga ang pagkakagawa ng isang bagay, na walang iniiwang kahit katiting na kapintasan.
etymology: From English internet/AAVE slang, popularized on platforms like TikTok and Twitter, meaning someone did something so well they 'ate' it all up, leaving no crumbs behind.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate compliment for a performance. When someone sings a song perfectly, slays a dance routine, or delivers a presentation flawlessly, you say they 'left **no crumbs**.' It means they devoured the task, leaving nothing—no mistakes, no hesitations, no room for criticism. It's the 'pak, ganern!' of the Gen Z era.
usage_notes: Used to praise someone's excellent execution of a task. It's a high form of compliment in modern internet slang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Grabe ang performance ni Catriona Gray sa Miss Universe, **no crumbs** talaga!","translation":"Catriona Gray's performance in Miss Universe was amazing, truly **flawless**!"},{"sentence":"Yung sagot niya sa interview, clear and confident. Ate, **no crumbs**!","translation":"Her answer in the interview was clear and confident. Girl, **no crumbs**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos o damdamin ng pagbibigay-halaga, pagkilala, at pagpipitagan sa isang tao, bagay, o konsepto.
original_explanation: That thing your parents told you to show to your elders by saying 'po' and 'opo' and doing the 'mano.' It's also what you demand from your ex but sometimes forget to give yourself. Basic human decency, level 1.
usage_notes: Often used with 'sa' (to/for), e.g., 'paggalang sa nakatatanda' (respect for elders).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paggalang** sa watawat ay tanda ng pagmamahal sa bayan.","translation":"**Respect** for the flag is a sign of love for the country."},{"sentence":"Ipakita mo ang iyong **paggalang** sa pamamagitan ng pakikinig.","translation":"Show your **respect** by listening."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paggamit ng isang bagay na matalas upang hatiin o putulin ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: The verb form of `hiwa`. This is the command you give or receive. "Hiwain mo na 'yang cake!" is the official start of any Filipino birthday party after the song. It's the action that turns a whole into parts.
usage_notes: An object-focused verb. "Hiwain mo ang tinapay" (You slice the bread). The focus is on the thing being sliced.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **hiwain** mo ang litson para sa mga bisita.","translation":"Please, **slice** the roasted pig for the guests."},{"sentence":"Marunong ka bang **hiwain** ang isda nang tama?","translation":"Do you know how to **cut** the fish properly?"}]

translation: will make rope; will twist fibers
meaning_filipino: Isasagawa ang pag-ikid o pagpilipit ng mga hibla (tulad ng abaka o bunot) upang makalikha ng isang lubid. Ito ay nasa panahunang panghinaharap.
original_explanation: Literally, it means to make rope. Figuratively, it's what you do when you twist a story to get out of trouble. "Para makalusot sa boss, maglulubid na naman ng kwento si Peter kung bakit siya late."
usage_notes: This is the future tense of 'maglubid'. It can be used literally for making rope or metaphorically for fabricating stories. The user's spelling 'maglulubid' is treated as the future tense 'maglúlubid'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sila ay **maglulubid** ng abaka para gawing pisi para sa barko.","translation":"They **will make rope** from abaca to be used as cordage for the ship."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala diyan, **maglulubid** lang 'yan ng kasinungalingan.","translation":"Don't believe him, he **will just weave** a lie."}]

translation: to have someone finish or consume everything
meaning_filipino: Iutos o payagan ang isang tao na gamitin, kainin, o gastusin ang lahat ng natitira sa isang bagay hanggang sa ito ay maubos.
original_explanation: That moment at a party when there's only a little bit of lechon left and the host says, "Ipaubos na natin 'to!" It's a green light for a food free-for-all. Also your mom telling you to finish the food on the table so it doesn't spoil.
usage_notes: A causative verb indicating that the subject allows or instructs another to finish the entirety of something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ipaubos** mo na sa mga bata ang natirang spaghetti.","translation":"Have the children **finish off** the leftover spaghetti."},{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang masayang kaya **ipinapaubos** niya ang pagkain sa bisita.","translation":"He doesn't want it to go to waste, so he is having the visitors **consume all** the food."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang kilos ng pagtindig mula sa pagkahiga o pagkakaupo; ang pag-ahon mula sa isang mahirap na sitwasyon.
original_explanation: You, every Monday morning when the alarm rings. Also, that feeling when you fail an exam but you decide to fight back and study harder for the finals. It's the act of getting up, rising, or recovering. #BangonPilipinas
usage_notes: Can be literal (getting out of bed) or metaphorical (recovering from failure, disaster, or grief).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaga siyang **bumabangon** tuwing umaga para mag-ehersisyo.","translation":"He/She **gets up** early every morning to exercise."},{"sentence":"Unti-unti nang **bumabangon** ang bansa mula sa kalamidad.","translation":"The country **is** slowly **rising** from the calamity."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng pinong buhok o balahibo sa ibabaw ng balat o isang bagay, tulad ng sa prutas.
etymology: From ma- (adjective prefix) + bulo (fine hair, down, fuzz).
original_explanation: 'Yung texture ng peach, kiwi, o rambutan. Pwede ring braso ng lalaki na medyo balbon. Hindi kasing-kapal ng "mabalahibo," mas "fuzzy" lang. Parang 'yung static sa lumang TV, pero sa balat.
usage_notes: Often used to describe the texture of fruits or fine body hair.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang balat ng prutas na peach ay medyo **mabulo**.","translation":"The skin of a peach fruit is a bit **fuzzy**."},{"sentence":"May mga uri ng dahon na **mabulo** ang ilalim.","translation":"There are types of leaves that are **downy** underneath."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagtatanghal o panoorin na itinatanghal sa madla, tulad ng dula, pelikula, o programa sa telebisyon.
original_explanation: This is what you watch on Netflix, at the cinema, or the "drama" your kapitbahay creates for everyone to see. It can be anything from a high-budget teleserye to a low-budget "bardagulan" on the street. "Gawa-gawa lang 'yan, palabas lang!"
usage_notes: Can refer to a TV show, a stage play, a movie, or even a metaphorical performance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maganda ba ang **palabas** kagabi sa teatro?","translation":"Was the **show** at the theater last night good?"},{"sentence":"Paborito kong **palabas** ang tungkol sa mga dragon.","translation":"My favorite **show** is the one about dragons."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtrato sa isang tao bilang isang pag-aari o alipin; pag-alis ng kalayaan ng isang indibidwal o grupo.
original_explanation: This is what happens when your boss makes you work weekends without overtime pay. You feel mang-alipin-ed. It's taking control to the extreme, treating someone not as a person but as a tool. Think historical drama villains or that one toxic ex.
usage_notes: Often used in historical, political, or highly dramatic contexts. Carries a very strong, negative connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi tayo dapat pumayag na **mang-alipin** ang dayuhan sa ating sariling bayan.","translation":"We should not allow foreigners to **enslave** us in our own country."},{"sentence":"Ang layunin ng batas ay protektahan ang mga manggagawa, hindi para sila ay **mang-alipin**.","translation":"The purpose of the law is to protect workers, not to **enslave** them."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pag-aayos o pagpapangkat-pangkat ng mga bagay, ideya, o datos ayon sa kanilang pagkakatulad o pagkakaiba.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung ginagawa mo sa laundry mo: puti sa puti, de-kolor sa de-kolor. O 'yung pag-aayos mo ng friends list mo sa FB: "Acquaintances," "Work," at "Mga Uutangan Ko." You're sorting things into categories. Ang 'klasipikahin' ay ang pormal na termino para sa paglalagay ng mga bagay sa kanilang tamang kahon.
usage_notes: Ang pandiwang ito ay madalas gamitin sa pormal, akademiko, o siyentipikong konteksto. Ang ugat na 'klasipika' ay hindi isang nagsasariling salita sa Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **klasipikahin** ang mga dokumento ayon sa petsa.","translation":"The documents need **to be classified** according to date."}]

translation: to reveal, to expose, to show
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalantad o pagpapakita ng isang bagay na dating nakatago, natatakpan, o lihim.
original_explanation: This is the 'big reveal' moment. It's when the kontrabida in the teleserye finally shows their true colors, or when you open the curtains to 'magtambad' a beautiful sunrise. In modern slang, it's like dropping the 'receipts' in a group chat, exposing the tea for everyone to see.
usage_notes: Can be used for physical objects, secrets, or true intentions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **nagtambad** din sa madla ang katotohanan tungkol sa katiwalian.","translation":"Finally, the truth about the corruption was **revealed** to the public."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mahiya na **magtambad** ng iyong tunay na talento.","translation":"Don't be shy to **show** your true talent."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang umikot o gumalaw nang hindi mapakali at paikut-ikot, karaniwang dahil sa pananakit, pagkailang, o pagpupumiglas.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling mo kapag may nag-spoil ng series na pinapanood mo, gusto mong **kumislot** sa inis. Also, 'yung uod sa mangga, 'yan 'yung ginagawa niya. Ew, but accurate.
usage_notes: Describes a restless, twisting movement. Can be from discomfort, pain, or trying to escape a hold.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumislot** ang uod sa loob ng prutas.","translation":"The worm **wriggled** inside the fruit."},{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **kumislot** sa sakit ang lalaking natapakan ang paa.","translation":"The man whose foot was stepped on started **to squirm** in pain."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng alahas na isinusuot sa daliri, karaniwang pabilog at yari sa metal, na maaaring may palamuting hiyas.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'pampatagal ng relasyon' if it's an engagement ring, or just a pretty accessory you bought from Shopee. The thing your lola tells you to pawn when you're short on cash. Can be a symbol of love, or a sign that you need to moisturize your hands.
usage_notes: Can refer to any type of ring worn on the finger, from engagement rings ('singsing na pangkasal') to simple bands.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ibinigay niya ang **singsing** ng kanyang lola sa kanyang mapapangasawa.","translation":"He gave his grandmother's **ring** to his fiancée."},{"sentence":"Nawala ko ang paborito kong **singsing** sa dagat.","translation":"I lost my favorite **ring** at the sea."}]

translation: to use a towel; to dry oneself with a towel
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggamit ng tuwalya upang patuyuin ang sarili, karaniwan pagkatapos maligo.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `mag-` (pormang pandiwa) + `tuwalya`, na hango sa salitang Espanyol na 'toalla'.
original_explanation: That thing you do after a shower so you don't drip water all over the floor and get an earful from your nanay. It's the essential step between being 'basa' and being 'ready to face the world... or at least your bedroom.'
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang isang utos ('Magtuwalya ka!') o upang ilarawan ang kilos.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos mong maligo, **magtuwalya** ka kaagad para hindi ka ginawin.","translation":"After you bathe, **use a towel** immediately so you don't get cold."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang lalabas ng banyo nang hindi ka pa nagtuwalya.","translation":"Don't come out of the bathroom without having dried yourself with a towel."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang taunang pagdiriwang o paggunita sa isang mahalagang petsa o kaganapan.
original_explanation: The one day a year you absolutely cannot forget, unless you want a month of silent treatment. It's the yearly reminder of your 'monthsary' graduating to a 'big boy' level. Whether it's for a wedding, a company's founding, or the day you started stanning a K-Pop group, it's a date that calls for either a celebration or a thoughtful Facebook post.
usage_notes: Used for any kind of yearly commemoration.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagdiwang kami ng aming ika-sampung **anibersaryo** ng kasal.","translation":"We celebrated our tenth wedding **anniversary**."},{"sentence":"Malapit na ang founding **anibersaryo** ng aming kumpanya.","translation":"Our company's founding **anniversary** is near."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay, pangyayari, o kilos na hindi madalas mangyari o makita; pambihira.
etymology: Reduplication of the first syllable of "bihira" (rare) for intensification.
original_explanation: This is the "once in a blue moon" of Tagalog. A loyal politician? `Bibihira`. A day with zero traffic on EDSA? `Bibihira`. Your crush replying to your DM? `Bibihira`. It emphasizes extreme rarity.
usage_notes: The reduplication of "bi-" adds emphasis, making it mean "very rare" as opposed to just "rare" (bihira). Can function as both an adjective and an adverb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bibihira** ang pagkakataong makita ang isang shooting star.","translation":"The chance to see a shooting star is **very rare**."},{"sentence":"**Bibihira** na siyang umuwi sa probinsya mula nang magtrabaho siya sa Maynila.","translation":"He **seldom** goes home to the province anymore since he started working in Manila."}]

translation: to play with someone; to toy with someone's feelings
meaning_filipino: Gawing katuwaan o libangan ang isang tao o bagay; makipaglaro sa isang tao.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you're not serious about a relationship. You're just passing the time, parang laro lang. 'Huwag mo akong kalaruin, please. Seryoso ako sa'yo.' It can also mean to literally play with someone, like a kid playing with their sibling. But let's be real, the 'hugot' meaning is more common these days.
usage_notes: Often carries a negative connotation of toying with someone's feelings, making them a 'plaything'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hiling ko lang na huwag mo akong **kalaruin** at saktan ang damdamin ko.","translation":"My only wish is for you not to **toy with** me and hurt my feelings."},{"sentence":"Gusto niyang **kalaruin** ang bagong alagang tuta.","translation":"He wants to **play with** the new pet puppy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng tela na isinasabit sa bintana, pinto, o entablado upang magbigay ng pribasya, harangin ang liwanag, o bilang palamuti.
original_explanation: The ultimate shield against your neighborhood's number one marites. A good kortina is the difference between privacy and your chismosa neighbor knowing what you ate for lunch. It's also what makes a house feel like a home, especially if it's the fancy, heavy kind from Divisoria that your mom changes every Christmas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisara ng **kortina** dahil masyadong masilaw ang araw.","translation":"Please close the **curtain** because the sun is too bright."},{"sentence":"Nagpalit si nanay ng bagong **kortina** para sa sala.","translation":"Mom changed to a new **curtain** for the living room."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang kagamitan na ginagamit upang maglagay ng marka, tanda, o senyas sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is your trusty sidekick for leaving your mark, literally. It could be a Pentel Pen for your notes, the chalk a tailor uses on fabric, or even the 'pan-taya' you use for your lotto ticket. It's any tool you use to say 'I was here,' 'this goes here,' or 'this is mine.'
usage_notes: A general term for any marking instrument.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pahiram ng iyong permanenteng **pangmarka**.","translation":"May I borrow your permanent **marker**?"},{"sentence":"Gumamit ang karpintero ng lapis bilang **pangmarka** sa kahoy.","translation":"The carpenter used a pencil as a **marking tool** on the wood."}]

translation: to wear a coat; to take shelter
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsusuot ng abrigo o damit panlaban sa lamig; ang pagkilos ng pagsilong o paghanap ng kanlungan.
original_explanation: Something you do once a year when you go to Baguio or when the office aircon is set to "Antarctica." To **mag-abrigo** is to put on a jacket, but it also carries the dramatic weight of seeking shelter, like when you're caught in a sudden downpour and you run to the nearest 7-Eleven.
usage_notes: Can mean both to wear a coat and to seek shelter. The context usually clarifies the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **mag-abrigo** dahil malamig ang panahon sa Tagaytay.","translation":"Don't forget to **wear a coat** because the weather in Tagaytay is cold."},{"sentence":"Naghahanap sila ng lugar kung saan maaaring **mag-abrigo** mula sa malakas na ulan.","translation":"They are looking for a place where they can **take shelter** from the heavy rain."}]

translation: to bring up (an old issue), to dig up, to unearth
meaning_filipino: Ang muling pagbanggit o pagbuhay sa isang lumang usapin, isyu, o pangyayari na matagal nang nalimutan o ipinagsawalang-bahala.
original_explanation: This is what happens during a fight with your S.O. when they suddenly bring up that *one thing* you did back in 2019. "'Wag mo nang **ungkatin** 'yun!" is the classic defense. It's digging up old dirt, exhuming past mistakes for present-day ammo. The ultimate "resurrecting past issues" move.
usage_notes: Madalas na may negatibong konotasyon, na nagpapahiwatig na ang paksang binabalikan ay luma na, naayos na, o mas mabuting hayaan na lamang sa nakaraan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa tuwing nag-aaway kami, palagi niyang **inuungkat** ang mga nakaraang pagkakamali ko.","translation":"Every time we fight, he always **brings up** my past mistakes."},{"sentence":"Tapos na ang isyung iyan, huwag na nating **ungkatin** pa.","translation":"That issue is over, let's not **dig it up** anymore."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging madaling mainis o magalit habang naghihintay o dahil sa pagkaantala; kakulangan sa pasensiya.
etymology: From `ka-` (marker for abstract nouns) + `walang` ('without') + `pasyensiya` (from Spanish 'paciencia', 'patience'). Literally 'the state of being without patience'.
original_explanation: That feeling when the internet buffer icon is mocking you. Or when you're in a long queue at the bank and the person in front is asking a million questions. It's the urge to say "Bilisan mo, bes!" but you just sigh heavily instead.
usage_notes: This is a more formal or literary way of saying "walang pasensya" or "pagkainip".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa kanyang **kawalang-pasyensiya** sa mga tamad na empleyado.","translation":"He is known for his **impatience** with lazy employees."},{"sentence":"Ang **kawalang-pasyensiya** ay maaaring magdulot ng maling desisyon.","translation":"**Impatience** can lead to wrong decisions."}]

translation: to fall prostrate, to lie sprawled out
meaning_filipino: Pagbagsak o paghiga sa lupa nang walang ayos o kontrol dahil sa labis na pagod, sakit, o pagkalasing.
original_explanation: This is that 'I give up' pose. After a hell week at work, you get home, drop your bag, and just mahandusay on the sofa like a sack of potatoes. It's the physical manifestation of 'ayoko na.'
usage_notes: Often used to describe a dramatic fall or a state of complete exhaustion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nang makita ang resulta ng exam, halos **mahandusay** siya sa sahig.","translation":"When he saw the exam results, he almost **sprawled out** on the floor."},{"sentence":"Sa sobrang pagod, **nahandusay** na lang siya sa kama pag-uwi.","translation":"From extreme exhaustion, he just **fell prostrate** onto the bed when he got home."}]

meaning_filipino: Natanggal o nabali ang isang bahagi mula sa kabuuan nito, kadalasan sa paraang biglaan o marahas.
original_explanation: Parang braso ng laruan na biglang tinanggal ng pinsan mong makulit. O 'di kaya, 'yung sanga ng puno na hindi kinaya ang bigat ng mangga. It's that sudden, sharp break.
usage_notes: Implies a more forceful or sudden detachment than 'nabali' (broke).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nalagpi** ang isang paa ng antigong silya nang maupo ako.","translation":"One leg of the antique chair **snapped off** when I sat on it."},{"sentence":"Sa lakas ng bagyo, **nalagpi** ang malaking sanga ng puno ng akasya.","translation":"Due to the storm's strength, a large branch of the acacia tree **broke off**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang una at tunay na bersyon; hindi kopya, imitasyon, o huwad.
original_explanation: 'Yung sapatos na binili mo sa Greenhills vs. 'yung galing sa official store. 'Yung isa Class A, 'yung isa **orihinal**. Also, 'yung jowa mong hindi trying hard maging iba, 'yung totoong siya? That's an **orihinal** personality. No to fake news, no to fake people, no to fake products.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a noun to mean "the original copy/item".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawala ko ang **orihinal** na kopya ng birth certificate ko.","translation":"I lost the **original** copy of my birth certificate."},{"sentence":"Mas mahal talaga ang mga **orihinal** na piyesa ng sasakyan.","translation":"The **original** car parts are really more expensive."}]

translation: to prepare; to get ready; to adorn
meaning_filipino: Ang paghahanda sa sarili sa pamamagitan ng pag-aayos o pagbibihis para sa isang okasyon; maaari ring tumukoy sa paghahanda o pag-aayos ng isang lugar.
original_explanation: This is you getting ready for a big date or a party. It's more than just 'magbihis' (to get dressed). It involves the whole production: shower, makeup, choosing the perfect OOTD, doing your hair. You're not just getting ready, you're adorning yourself. 'Maggayak ka na, aalis na tayo!' is what your mom shouts when you've been in your room for an hour.
usage_notes: Often implies dressing up or preparing for a special event, more elaborate than simple preparation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula na siyang **maggayak** para sa kanyang kasal.","translation":"She started to **get ready** (adorn herself) for her wedding."}]

translation: to swindle; to extort money from someone
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkuha ng pera mula sa isang tao sa pamamagitan ng panlilinlang, pananamantala, o pamimilit.
etymology: Mula sa 'pera' (salapi) + hulaping '-han' (na nagsasaad ng kilos o lokasyon).
original_explanation: This is what happens when someone sees you as a walking ATM. To be 'perahan' means someone is trying to milk you for money, usually through dishonest means. It's the 'friend' who only messages you to borrow money, the online seller with a 'too good to be true' offer, or the subject of countless Raffy Tulfo episodes. It's the opposite of 'libre.'
usage_notes: Nagtataglay ng mabigat na negatibong konotasyon ng pagsasamantala o panloloko.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpapauto diyan, baka **perahan** ka lang niya.","translation":"Don't be fooled by him, he might just be trying to **swindle money** from you."},{"sentence":"Ginawa niyang negosyo ang **perahan** ang mga turista.","translation":"He made a business out of **extorting money** from tourists."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na may diperensya sa pag-iisip o kumikilos nang wala sa sarili, lalo na tuwing kabilugan ng buwan; isang taong naglalakad habang natutulog.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'lunático', na nangangahulugang 'apektado ng buwan'.
original_explanation: Basically, your friend who makes questionable life choices at 3 AM. Or that officemate who suddenly bursts into song during a serious meeting. The OG term for someone acting 'weird' or 'crazy', often linked to the full moon (luna). Also, the clinical term for a sleepwalker.
usage_notes: While it can mean a clinical sleepwalker, it's more often used figuratively to describe someone acting erratically or eccentrically.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para kang **lunatiko** kung maglakad ka sa gabi nang tulog!","translation":"You're like a **sleepwalker** when you walk at night while asleep!"},{"sentence":"Huwag mong pansinin, parang **lunatiko** lang 'yan kung magalit.","translation":"Don't mind him, he's like a **lunatic** when he gets angry."}]

translation: to make equal; to equalize; to level
meaning_filipino: Gawing pantay o balanse ang isang sitwasyon, laro, o kalagayan.
original_explanation: This is the 'habol' moment in any game, whether it's basketball or Mobile Legends. When the other team is leading and you score to tie it, you just **nagpatas** the game. It's the ultimate 'di kami papatalo' move. It can also mean making sure everyone gets an equal share of the pizza.
usage_notes: Commonly used in sports, games, and situations involving distribution or fairness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinikap ng koponan na **magpatas** ng iskor bago matapos ang laro.","translation":"The team tried to **level** the score before the game ended."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magpatas** sa hatian ng mga gawain sa bahay.","translation":"We need to **make** the division of household chores **equal**."}]

meaning_filipino: Maging dahilan ng matinding pagkabigla, pagkatakot, o pangingilabot.
etymology: Mula sa panlaping pangkasanhi na "ika-" at sa salitang-ugat na "sindak" (matinding takot o gulat).
original_explanation: This is what causes you to go into full-blown panic mode. Think seeing your ex with their new partner, but the new partner is your best friend. Or when you check your bank account after a Shopee 11.11 sale. The feeling is pure sindak, and this word is the *reason* for it.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang pandiwang sanhi na tumutukoy sa pinagmulan ng pakiramdam ng sindak o matinding takot.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang biglaang pagyanig ng lupa ang **ikasindak** ng marami.","translation":"The sudden shaking of the ground was what **caused terror** among many."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang gumawa ng bagay na **ikasindak** ng iyong mga magulang.","translation":"Don't do anything that will **cause shock to** your parents."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang artipisyal na daluyan ng tubig, gaya ng kanal, na ginagamit sa sistema ng patubig.
original_explanation: This is the actual canal or ditch that carries the water. It's the "highway" for the water in an irrigation system. You see these crisscrossing provinces. As kids, some people might have even swum in one (though maybe not the cleanest idea).
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa mismong istruktura o daluyan, hindi sa proseso.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malinis na ang **patubigan** kaya't mabilis ang daloy ng tubig papunta sa mga sakahan.","translation":"The **irrigation canal** is now clean, so the flow of water to the farms is fast."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang tao o hayop na may malaki at nakaumbok na tiyan, na maaaring sanhi ng labis na pagkain, sakit, o pagkabundat.
original_explanation: That feeling after a fiesta or Noche Buena when you've eaten your body weight in lechon and spaghetti. You look down and your tummy has expanded to its own barangay. 'Busog' is full. `Butod` is 'I've-made-a-huge-mistake-but-it-was-worth-it' full. Can also refer to a permanent pot-belly.
usage_notes: Can be considered slightly rude if used to describe a person directly, implying they are unhealthily large in the midsection.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **butod** ang tiyan ng aso sa dami ng nakain.","translation":"The dog's stomach became **bloated** from all the food it ate."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang magtagumpay sa isang laban, kompetisyon, o anumang uri ng paligsahan.
original_explanation: That feeling when your crush finally replies, or when you snag the last piece of chicken joy. It's the ultimate goal in any game, from Mobile Legends to the game of life (and love). #SanaAll
usage_notes: A very common word. The opposite is 'matalo' (to lose).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **manalo** tayo sa laro mamaya!","translation":"I hope we **win** the game later!"},{"sentence":"**Nanalo** siya ng malaking premyo sa lotto.","translation":"He **won** a big prize in the lottery."}]

translation: to make bigger; to take up space
meaning_filipino: Magdulot ng paglaki o pag-okupa ng malaking espasyo.
original_explanation: That one piece of furniture that just dominates the whole living room. Or when a small lie you told suddenly snowballs into a huge problem that takes up all your mental energy.
usage_notes: A causative verb indicating an increase in size or the occupation of a large area.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang bumili ng sofà na **makalaki** masyado sa sala.","translation":"Don't buy a sofa that will **take up too much space** in the living room."},{"sentence":"Ang utang na iyon ay **makalaki** sa ating buwanang badyet.","translation":"That debt will **make a big dent** in our monthly budget."}]

translation: to throw, to hurl, to fling
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpukol o pagbato ng isang bagay nang may pwersa at sa malayo-layong distansya.
original_explanation: More aggressive than 'ibato.' This is what you do to your phone when your game lags (but you don't actually let go). Or when you're so done with a relationship you want to ihagis all their stuff out the window. It's a throw with feeling, usually anger or frustration.
usage_notes: Implies a more forceful or less careful throw than 'ibato' or 'ipukol'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Galit na **inihagis** niya ang baso sa pader.","translation":"He angrily **threw** the glass against the wall."},{"sentence":"**Ihagis** mo sa akin ang bola!","translation":"**Throw** me the ball!"}]

translation: a temporary separation in a relationship
meaning_filipino: Isang pansamantalang panahon ng paghihiwalay o pagdistansya sa isang romantikong relasyon upang makapag-isip-isip ang bawat isa at mabigyan ng espasyo ang isa't isa.
etymology: Mula sa pariralang Ingles na "cool off", na literal na nangangahulugang "palamigin".
original_explanation: The pre-breakup stage. Eto yung sinasabi ng jowa mo na 'I need space' pero ayaw ka pang i-break. It's not a breakup, but it's not *not* a breakup. Parang 'on a break' ni Ross at Rachel. Yung moment na di mo alam kung single ka na ba o hihintayin mo lang siyang 'lumamig'.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng mga romantikong relasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-usap sila at napagdesisyunang mag-**cool off** muna.","translation":"They talked and decided to have a **cool off** period for now."},{"sentence":"Sabi niya **cool off** lang, pero may bago na siya after one week.","translation":"She said it was just a **cool off**, but she had someone new after one week."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtanggap ng ari-arian, katangian, o responsibilidad mula sa isang naunang tao, karaniwan ay mula sa isang yumaong kamag-anak.
original_explanation: What everyone hopes to do from a rich, long-lost relative. It can be money, land, or the old family house. But more often than not, what you 'magmana' from your parents is their nose, their temper, or their debt. "Kanino ka ba nagmana?" is the classic question when you do something weird.
usage_notes: Can refer to inheriting tangible assets (yaman), physical traits (itsura), or even personality traits (ugali).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Swerte siya dahil **magmamana** siya ng malaking lupain.","translation":"He is lucky because he **will inherit** a large piece of land."},{"sentence":"Saan ka ba **nagmana** ng ganyang katigasan ng ulo?","translation":"From whom did you **inherit** such stubbornness?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang parirala na nagpapahiwatig na ang isang bagay, tao, o konsepto ay katanggap-tanggap, nakaaaliw, o may mataas na kalidad ayon sa pamantayan ng komunidad ng mga bading.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate seal of quality for anything related to pop culture, fashion, or drama. If a movie, a song, or a new chismis is 'bading approved,' it means it's fabulous, entertaining, and worth your time. The gay community is often seen as the tastemaker, so this approval carries weight. Think of it as a 5-star rating from the experts of 'taray' and 'ganda'.
usage_notes: Used colloquially to denote something as fashionable, trendy, or entertaining according to perceived gay sensibilities.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bagong album ni Taylor Swift ay talagang **bading approved**.","translation":"Taylor Swift's new album is definitely **gay-approved**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan **bading approved** ang outfit mo para sa party mamaya.","translation":"Your outfit for the party later needs to be **gay-approved**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maikling pagtukoy o pagbanggit sa isang tao, bagay, o ideya.
etymology: From `paN-` + `banggit`. The `paN-` prefix (which becomes `pam-` before 'b') often creates a noun indicating a tool or means for the action of the root word.
original_explanation: This is the academic's "shoutout." When you're writing your thesis and you have to name-drop Foucault or a local historian, that's a 'pamanggit'. In casual talk, it's that quick mention: "Nagkaroon ng pamanggit tungkol sa 'yo sa meeting kanina." (You were mentioned in the meeting earlier.) It’s dropping a name or a fact into the conversation.
usage_notes: More formal than "banggit." Often used in literary or academic contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang aklat ay puno ng **pamanggit** sa mga naunang manunulat.","translation":"His book is full of **citations** of earlier writers."},{"sentence":"Isang simpleng **pamanggit** lang ng kanyang pangalan ay sapat na para mapangiti siya.","translation":"Just a simple **mention** of his name is enough to make her smile."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na tawagan para sa isang malapit na kaibigan o kasama, na pinaikling anyo ng salitang Ingles na 'partner'.
etymology: Mula sa pinaikling salitang Ingles na 'partner'.
original_explanation: The quintessential Filipino bro-term. It's the shortened, cooler version of 'partner'. You use this for your barkada, your drinking buddies, your workmates. 'Uy, pards, kamusta?' is the standard greeting. It's less formal than 'kaibigan', more friendly than 'pare'. It's the sound of camaraderie over a bucket of Red Horse.
usage_notes: Isang salitang balbal o slang na karaniwang ginagamit ng mga kalalakihan, ngunit maaari ring gamitin ng lahat sa impormal na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tara, inom tayo mamaya, **pards**!","translation":"Let's go for a drink later, **buddy**!"},{"sentence":"Salamat sa tulong mo, **pards**. Utang ko 'to sa'yo.","translation":"Thanks for your help, **pal**. I owe you one."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng pag-iisip na puno ng pag-aalala, hindi mapakali, at kawalan ng kapanatagan.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na 11:59 PM na pero 'di mo pa sinisimulan 'yung deadline mong 12:00 MN. Or when you sent a risky text and now you're staring at the 'seen' notification with no reply. That's being 'balisa'—anxious, restless, and overthinking everything. Welcome to the club.
usage_notes: A very common word to describe a state of anxiety or worry.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **balisa** siya habang hinihintay ang resulta ng kanyang medical exam.","translation":"She became **anxious** while waiting for the results of her medical exam."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **balisa**, malulutas din natin ang problemang ito.","translation":"Don't be **worried**, we will solve this problem eventually."}]

meaning_filipino: Bahagyang matamis; hindi gaanong katamisan.
etymology: Reduplication of matamis, indicating a lesser degree.
original_explanation: This is for the "healthy-ish" crowd. It's the "less sugar" option in your milk tea order. It's not full-blown sweet, just a hint, a suggestion, a "baka naman" kind of sweetness. Like a situationship—not quite a relationship, but not *not* sweet either.
usage_notes: The reduplication of the root word with a 'ma-' prefix often indicates a moderate or diminished quality.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko ang kape ko na **matamis-tamis** lang.","translation":"I like my coffee just **somewhat sweet**."},{"sentence":"May **matamis-tamis** na lasa ang hinog na kamatis.","translation":"A ripe tomato has a **sweetish** taste."}]

translation: to sign; to affix one's signature
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsulat ng sariling pangalan o pirma sa isang dokumento bilang tanda ng pagsang-ayon, pagpapatunay, o pag-ako ng responsibilidad.
original_explanation: The final step before you're officially 'in debt' for a new phone plan, a housing loan, or a marriage contract. It’s that moment of truth when your pen hits the paper. In the digital age, this is your "I have read and agree to the Terms and Conditions" click, but with more legal weight and a fancier scribble.
usage_notes: A formal term for 'pirmahan'. Used in legal, business, and official contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinihiling na **ilagda** ng pangulo ang bagong batas.","translation":"The president is being asked to **sign** the new law."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **ilagda** ang iyong pangalan sa tatlong kopya ng kontrata.","translation":"You need to **affix your signature** to the three copies of the contract."}]

meaning_filipino: Makipagpustahan; tumaya ng pera o anumang bagay sa isang kaganapan na hindi tiyak ang resulta.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping pandiwa na 'ma-' at ang salitang ugat na 'pusta' (bet), na hango sa salitang Espanyol na 'apostar'.
original_explanation: The act of putting your money where your mouth is. Whether it's on a basketball game, a boxing match, or whether your friend will finally get over their ex. It's the thrill of 'may the best (or luckiest) person win.' Every sabongero and NBA fan knows this verb by heart.
usage_notes: Ito ang pandiwang nakapokus sa aktor o gumagawa ng kilos. Ang 'pumusta' ay isa ring karaniwang anyo na may parehong kahulugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino sa tingin mo ang mananalo? Halika, **mamusta** tayo.","translation":"Who do you think will win? Come on, let's **bet**."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **mamusta** sa karera ng kabayo tuwing Linggo.","translation":"He likes to **bet** on horse races every Sunday."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng suporta, tulong, o pabor sa isang tao, produkto, o kilusan; pagiging suki.
original_explanation: This is the official term for being a 'suki'. It's your loyalty to your favorite milk tea shop, your unwavering support for local artists, or your mom's dedication to buying from only one specific stall in the palengke. It's the 'support local' energy that keeps small businesses alive.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of business, arts, and community support.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagtangkilik** sa sariling produkto ay tanda ng pagmamahal sa bayan.","translation":"The **patronage** of one's own products is a sign of love for the country."},{"sentence":"Salamat sa inyong walang sawang **pagtangkilik** sa aming munting kainan.","translation":"Thank you for your unending **support** for our small eatery."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang babae na masigla, maliksi, o palaging may ginagawa; hindi pasibo.
original_explanation: Siya yung friend mong babae na laging may ganap. Akyat bundok sa umaga, zumba sa hapon, tapos may online business pa sa gabi. Hindi nauubusan ng energy, parang laging naka-unli-Milo. The feminine form of 'laging go lang nang go!'
usage_notes: Ito ang pambabaeng anyo; "aktibo" ang panlalaki.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Lola Remedios ay **aktiba** pa rin sa edad na otsenta.","translation":"Grandma Remedios is still **active** at the age of eighty."},{"sentence":"Naging **aktiba** siya sa mga gawaing pampaaralan.","translation":"She became **active** in school activities."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sundalo o artilyero na namamahala sa paggamit at pagpapaputok ng kanyon.
original_explanation: Literally a 'cannon-er'. This is some serious historical warfare vocabulary. Think pirates, the Battle of Mactan, or that one hyper-competitive person in a video game who always picks the heavy artillery character. Not your everyday palengke term.
usage_notes: This is a rare word, mostly found in historical texts or literature about warfare from past centuries.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **manganganyon** ay naghanda para sa pag-atake ng mga pirata.","translation":"The **cannoneers** prepared for the pirate attack."},{"sentence":"Isang matapang na **manganganyon** ang nagligtas sa buong kuta.","translation":"A brave **gunner** saved the entire fort."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa paraan ng pagluto kung saan ang isang sangkap, karaniwan ay butil o buto, ay iniinit sa kawali nang walang mantika hanggang sa maluto o pumutok.
original_explanation: Think of making garlic bits for 'sinangag' (garlic fried rice) or toasting nuts for a recipe. You toss them in a hot, dry pan until they get fragrant and a little brown. 'Yan ang 'pagbusa'. It's the OG, no-oil-needed cooking method for that perfect crunch.
usage_notes: Commonly used for grains, nuts, and seeds. The verb form is "magbusa" or "busahin".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas masarap ang sinangag kung may sahog na maraming **binusang** bawang.","translation":"Garlic fried rice is more delicious if it has a lot of **toasted** garlic as an ingredient."},{"sentence":"Naglagay siya ng **binusang** mani sa ibabaw ng kanyang pansit.","translation":"He put **toasted** peanuts on top of his noodles."}]

translation: to endure something together; to make do with something
meaning_filipino: Pagtiiisan o pagtiyagaan ang isang bagay o sitwasyon, kadalasan ay dahil sa kakulangan o kawalan ng mas mainam na pagpipilian, na ginagawa nang sama-sama.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'tiis-ganda' or 'kapit-bisig' verb. It's when you and your officemates have to share the weak office Wi-Fi, or when a couple has to make do with a tiny studio apartment in the city. 'Pag-agwantahan na muna natin 'to.' It's the patron saint of budget trips and relationships surviving on a shoestring.
usage_notes: Often used in a shared context, implying mutual endurance or tolerance. The '-han' suffix indicates the object or person being collectively endured.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pag-agwantahan** na muna natin itong luma at mabagal na internet connection habang naghihintay ng upgrade.","translation":"Let's just **make do with** this old and slow internet connection while waiting for the upgrade."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **pag-agwantahan** ang isa't isa sa hirap at ginhawa.","translation":"We need to **endure with** each other through thick and thin."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pakiramdam ng lamig sa katawan, na maaaring sanhi ng mababang temperatura, sakit, o takot.
original_explanation: That feeling when the aircon in the office is set to 'Antarctica' mode. Or when you step out of a hot shower into a cold room. It's the kind of cold that makes you shiver and look for the nearest jacket or kumot.
usage_notes: Refers to the sensation of coldness on the body, not just the ambient temperature (which is 'lamig').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nararamdaman ko ang **ginaw** hanggang sa aking mga buto.","translation":"I can feel the **chill** down to my bones."},{"sentence":"Nanginginig siya sa **ginaw** dahil sa lagnat.","translation":"He is shivering from the **cold** because of the fever."}]

translation: to roll up repeatedly or playfully
meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit o walang-tiyak na layuning pagkilos ng pagrorolyo ng isang bagay.
etymology: Mula sa pag-uulit ng bahagi ng salitang-ugat na "rolyo" at pagdaragdag ng hulaping "-hin".
original_explanation: Ito 'yung ginagawa mo 'pag bored ka. You're not just rolling it once; you keep rolling and unrolling it. 'Rolyu-rolyuhin mo 'yang papel habang naghihintay ka.' It's the fidget spinner version of rolling something up. It implies a casual, repetitive, or maybe even a slightly careless action.
usage_notes: Ang pag-uulit ng unang dalawang pantig ng ugat ('ro-lyo' -> 'rolyu-') ay nagpapahiwatig ng isang paulit-ulit o hindi seryosong pagkilos.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **rolyu-rolyuhin** ang pera, baka masira.","translation":"Don't **repeatedly roll** the money, it might get damaged."},{"sentence":"Habang nag-iisip, kinagawian niyang **rolyu-rolyuhin** ang dulo ng kanyang manggas.","translation":"While thinking, he had a habit of **playfully rolling** the end of his sleeve."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malawak na lupain na sadyang tinatamnan ng mga halaman, bulaklak, puno, o anumang pananim.
original_explanation: Your mom's pride and joy, that ever-expanding collection of succulents, snake plants, and orchids taking over the balcony. It's also where your tita gets her new profile picture and selfie background. The modern version of 'hacienda' for city dwellers.
usage_notes: Often refers to a dedicated area for planting, which can range from a small garden plot to a large plantation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming kakaibang bulaklak sa **halamanin** ni Lola.","translation":"There are many exotic flowers in Grandma's **garden**."},{"sentence":"Pinaplano nilang gawing **halamanin** ng mga gulay ang bakanteng lote.","translation":"They are planning to turn the vacant lot into a vegetable **garden**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng katangiang kaakit-akit o kahali-halina sa paningin; karaniwang tumutukoy sa isang lalaki, anumang kasarian, o isang bagay.
original_explanation: The guy who makes you do a double-take. He's not just 'gwapo' (handsome), he has charisma. Think of the office heartthrob or your K-drama oppa. It's also used for non-people things, like an 'atraktibong' investment plan or a sale that's too good to pass up. It's the 'add to cart' impulse in adjective form.
usage_notes: The masculine/gender-neutral form. Can be used for people of any gender, objects, and concepts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay isang **atraktibo** at matalinong binata.","translation":"He is an **attractive** and intelligent young man."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa mababang presyo, naging **atraktibo** ang lupa sa mga mamimili.","translation":"Because of the low price, the land became **attractive** to buyers."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mataimtim na paghiling o pagsusumamo para sa isang pabor o biyaya.
original_explanation: This is a level-up from 'pakiusap'. This is the 'last-two-minutes' full-court press of asking for something. Imagine begging your prof to pass you, not just with words, but with your whole being. It's the 'I'm begging you' energy when you're trying to borrow money from a friend for the nth time.
usage_notes: A formal and deep word, often found in literature or religious contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa kanyang **pagluhog**, nakuha niya ang kapatawaran ng hari.","translation":"Through his **supplication**, he obtained the king's forgiveness."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sistema, kagamitan, o paraan para sa pagdaloy ng tubig, karaniwan para sa mga pananim o sakahan.
original_explanation: Think of this as the life support for your lola's garden or a vast rice field. It can be a simple 'tabo' and a pail, a garden hose, or a complex irrigation canal. It's the system that delivers the 'elixir of life' (H2O) to thirsty plants, ensuring we have rice on our plates and not just 'hugot' in our hearts.
usage_notes: More formal term is 'patubig' or 'irigasyon', but 'pampatubig' is understood as any device or system used for watering.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasira ang makinang **pampatubig** kaya nanganganib matuyo ang mga palay.","translation":"The **irrigation** machine broke, so the rice plants are in danger of drying out."}]

translation: for the wrist, worn on the wrist
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na idinisenyo upang isuot o ilagay sa pulso o galang-galangan.
original_explanation: Anything you wear on your wrist. Your smartwatch that counts your steps (or lack thereof), your pampaswerteng red string, or 'yung relo na bigay pa ng ex mo. It's your wrist accessory, your 'pampulso'.
usage_notes: Commonly used to describe accessories like watches or bracelets.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawala ang paborito niyang relong **pamulso**.","translation":"He lost his favorite **wrist**watch."},{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng bagong pulseras mong **pamulso**!","translation":"Your new **wrist** bracelet is beautiful!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malawak na lupain o plantasyon, karaniwang pagmamay-ari ng isang pamilya o korporasyon, na tinataniman ng mga pang-agrikulturang produkto.
original_explanation: The setting of every other teleserye. It's a massive piece of land owned by a ridiculously rich family, usually with a dark secret. Think of it as the ultimate landlord goals from the Spanish era, complete with a grand house, endless fields, and enough family drama to fuel 10 seasons.
usage_notes: Often associated with historical wealth, agriculture (like sugar or coconut plantations), and social class distinctions in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakalawak ng **asyenda** ng mga Dela Cruz sa probinsya.","translation":"The Dela Cruz's **hacienda** in the province is vast."},{"sentence":"Maraming manggagawa ang nagtatrabaho sa **asyenda** ng tubo.","translation":"Many workers are employed at the sugarcane **hacienda**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking kasintahan o karelasyon.
original_explanation: The official term for 'jowa' (male version). He's the reason you're always 'kilig', the subject of your "sana all" posts, and the person your titas always ask about during family reunions ("O, nasaan na ang boyfriend mo?"). The Filipino equivalent is 'kasintahan', but let's be real, almost everyone says boyfriend or 'jowa'.
usage_notes: Extremely common in spoken and informal written Tagalog (Taglish). The native Tagalog term "kasintahan" is more formal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipakilala mo naman kami sa **boyfriend** mo.","translation":"Introduce us to your **boyfriend**."},{"sentence":"Wala akong **boyfriend** ngayon, focus muna sa career.","translation":"I don't have a **boyfriend** right now, I'm focusing on my career first."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing mas malawak, mas malaki, o mas komprehensibo ang isang espasyo, saklaw, kaalaman, o impluwensya.
original_explanation: What you need to do to your vocabulary, your patience, and your pants after the holidays. It's the act of making something bigger, wider, or more comprehensive. 'Expand your horizons' is 'Palawakin ang iyong pananaw.'
usage_notes: A command or infinitive form. Conjugates as pinapalawak (is expanding), pinalawak (expanded), and papalawakin (will expand).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais ng kumpanya na **palawakin** ang kanilang operasyon sa ibang bansa.","translation":"The company wants **to expand** its operations to other countries."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **palawakin** ang iyong pang-unawa sa sitwasyon.","translation":"You need **to expand** your understanding of the situation."}]

translation: to be able to break free; to escape
meaning_filipino: Ang matagumpay na paglaya o pagkawala mula sa isang bagay na pumipigil, kumukulong, o nagpapahirap, tulad ng gapos, bilangguan, o masamang sitwasyon.
original_explanation: That feeling when you finally log off after a toxic day of back-to-back meetings. It's the bird escaping its cage, the prisoner finding freedom. On a less dramatic note, it's you finally getting out of a family gathering you didn't want to be at. "Sana makaalpas na ako sa toxic kong trabaho." is a common prayer.
usage_notes: Carries a strong sense of liberation from confinement or restraint, both literal and metaphorical.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng ibon na **makaalpas** mula sa hawla.","translation":"The bird tried **to break free** from the cage."},{"sentence":"Hindi siya **makaalpas** sa alaala ng kanyang nakaraan.","translation":"She cannot **escape** the memories of her past."}]

meaning_filipino: Payapain o bawasan ang tindi ng nararamdamang galit; magtimpi at huminahon.
etymology: A figurative use of "palamigin" (to cool) applied to "galit" (anger).
original_explanation: This is the emotional equivalent of putting ice on a burn. When you're fuming mad and about to send that risky text or confront your boss, someone wise (like your mom or a work friend) will tell you to do this first. It means 'chill ka lang muna, besh' before you do something you'll regret.
usage_notes: A very common idiom. Often used with 'ulo' (head) as in 'palamigin ang ulo.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas mabuting **palamigin ang galit** mo bago kayo mag-usap.","translation":"It's better to **cool down your anger** before you two talk."},{"sentence":"Umalis muna siya para **palamigin ang galit**.","translation":"He left for a while to **cool down his anger**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lalaking asawa ng tunay na ina ng isang tao, na hindi niya tunay na ama.
original_explanation: He's your mom's new husband. Not your biological dad, but hopefully he's the cool tito-type who gives you extra allowance and doesn't ask too many questions. The male counterpart of a 'madrasta'.
usage_notes: The female equivalent is 'madrasta' (stepmother).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabait ang aking **padrasto** at tinuturing niya akong tunay na anak.","translation":"My **stepfather** is kind and treats me like his own child."},{"sentence":"Ipinakilala ni Ana ang kanyang **padrasto** sa mga kaibigan niya.","translation":"Ana introduced her **stepfather** to her friends."}]

translation: to be persuaded, to be convinced
meaning_filipino: Ang makumbinsi o mapapaniwala na gawin ang isang bagay dahil sa panghihimok o magandang paliwanag ng iba.
original_explanation: When your friends successfully convince you to go out on a Friday night even though you swore you'd stay home. 'Sige na, isa lang.' And you go. You've been `mahikayat`. Also applies to budol deals online.
usage_notes: The person being persuaded is the subject of the verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana'y **mahikayat** kitang sumama sa aming proyekto.","translation":"I hope I can **persuade** you to join our project."},{"sentence":"Madali siyang **mahikayat** ng mga matatamis na salita.","translation":"She is easily **persuaded** by sweet words."}]

translation: someone one meets with; counterpart in a meeting
meaning_filipino: Ang isang tao na nakatakdang makipagkita o makipag-usap sa iyo sa isang partikular na oras at lugar.
etymology: From `tagpo` (encounter, scene) with the prefix `ka-` denoting a person with whom the action is shared.
original_explanation: Your "ka-meeting". The person you're supposed to see, whether for a client presentation, a blind date, or a "let's talk" session with your jowa. When you say, "May katagpo ako," it sounds more formal and mysterious than just "may imi-meet ako." It implies an appointment, a purpose, and maybe a little bit of drama.
usage_notes: Often used in formal or literary contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huli na ako sa usapan, naghihintay na ang aking **katagpo**.","translation":"I'm late for the appointment, the person I'm **meeting with** is already waiting."},{"sentence":"Ang pangulo at ang kanyang **katagpo** mula sa ibang bansa ay nag-usap tungkol sa kalakalan.","translation":"The president and his **counterpart** from another country discussed trade."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang koleksyon ng mga larawan sa social media, tulad ng Instagram, na may magkakabagay na kulay, tema, o istilo upang maging kaaya-aya sa paningin.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng 'aesthetic' at 'feed' mula sa Ingles.
original_explanation: The ultimate goal of every aspiring influencer. It's when all your Instagram posts match perfectly, creating a beautiful grid. It takes more effort than a thesis paper, involving apps like VSCO and Lightroom, and maybe even a color-coordinated calendar for your OOTDs.
usage_notes: Termino na partikular na ginagamit sa konteksto ng social media platforms tulad ng Instagram.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinagpapaguran niya talaga ang kanyang **aesthetic feed** sa Instagram.","translation":"She really works hard on her **aesthetic feed** on Instagram."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging padalos-dalos, walang pag-iingat, o hindi pinag-iisipan ang mga posibleng kahihinatnan ng isang kilos.
etymology: Nagmula sa `ka-` + `wala` + `-ng` + `taros`. Ang 'taros' ay nangangahulugan ng pag-iingat o maingat na pagsasaalang-alang.
original_explanation: This is your 'YOLO' friend who jumps into things without thinking. The one who spends their entire sahod on an 11.11 sale without a budget. It's the vibe of making decisions with pure 'bahala na' energy, no risk assessment whatsoever. It’s recklessness, but make it Filipino.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan ng isang aksyon o katangian na walang pag-iisip sa hinaharap o walang pag-iingat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kawalang-taros** niya sa pagmamaneho ang naging sanhi ng aksidente.","translation":"His **recklessness** in driving was the cause of the accident."},{"sentence":"Pinagsisihan niya ang **kawalang-taros** sa kanyang mga desisyon sa buhay.","translation":"He regretted the **imprudence** in his life decisions."}]

translation: to feel resentful towards each other
meaning_filipino: Ang sabay o parehong pagdaramdam ng sama ng loob ng dalawa o higit pang tao sa isa't isa.
etymology: From hinanakit (resentment), which comes from sakit (pain). The -an suffix makes the action reciprocal or done among a group.
original_explanation: This is when the whole barkada is giving each other the silent treatment. It's a group chat full of "seen" but no replies. It's the cold war between siblings over who gets the last piece of lechon. A multiplayer version of maghinanakit.
usage_notes: This is a reciprocal verb, indicating the action is done between two or more people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa hindi pagkakaunawaan, nagsimula silang **maghinanakitan**.","translation":"Because of a misunderstanding, they started to **feel resentful towards each other**."},{"sentence":"Hindi maganda na ang magkapatid ay **naghihinanakitan**.","translation":"It's not good for siblings to be **harboring grudges against each other**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong may ugaling madalas at malakas na sumigaw, lalo na kapag nagpapahayag ng damdamin.
original_explanation: Eto yung tita mo sa palengke na kahit katabi mo lang kausap, rinig hanggang sa kabilang kanto. Sila yung mga kaibigan na nanonood ng basketball sa TV na akala mo nasa Araneta Coliseum. Hindi kailangan ng microphone, natural na ang amplifier.
usage_notes: Describes a person's tendency or habit. Different from 'maingay' (noisy) which can describe a place or a situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala si Aling Nena sa pagiging **masigawin** tuwing nagagalit sa kanyang mga anak.","translation":"Aling Nena is known for being **prone to shouting** whenever she gets angry at her children."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtitiis ng hirap o sakit para sa isang layunin; ang masikap at matiyagang paggawa sa isang bagay.
etymology: From "sakit" (pain, illness). In this context, it takes on the meaning of enduring hardship, formed with the "pag- -an" affix and reduplication.
original_explanation: This is the "tiis-ganda" or "tiis-pogi" mindset applied to everything in life. It's the puyat for an exam, the overtime to meet a deadline, the OFW working abroad away from family. It’s that feeling of grinding and suffering now for a payoff later. It’s the hugot behind every success story: "Walang tagumpay na hindi pinaghirapan."
usage_notes: Different from "pagkakasakit" which means getting sick. "Pagsasakit" is about voluntary endurance of difficulty.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagsasakit** ng mga magulang ay para sa kinabukasan ng kanilang mga anak.","translation":"The **enduring of hardship** by parents is for the future of their children."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **pagsasakit** sa pag-aaral, nakamit niya ang pinakamataas na karangalan.","translation":"Because of his **painstaking effort** in his studies, he achieved the highest honors."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lubusang pagbabago ng pisikal na kaanyuan o hitsura.
original_explanation: The ultimate glow-up. This is what happens after a major breakup, a big promotion, or just getting a really good haircut. It's the 'New Year, New Me' post on Instagram. Think of a caterpillar becoming a butterfly, or your friend after they discover skincare. 'Wow, parang **nagbagong-anyo** ka!'
usage_notes: Implies a significant, often positive, change in physical appearance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matapos ang ilang buwang pag-eehersisyo, tila **nagbagong-anyo** si Marco.","translation":"After a few months of exercising, it seems Marco **has transformed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang silid sa isang bahay o gusali na pangunahing ginagamit para sa pagkain.
original_explanation: The room in the house that's only ever fully used during Noche Buena, fiestas, or when important guests come over. The rest of the year, it's a storage area for things that don't have a home, or where you dump your mail. Most Pinoys eat in the kitchen or in front of the TV anyway.
usage_notes: A traditional term; "dining area" is a more common modern equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakahain na ang pagkain sa mesa sa **komedor**.","translation":"The food is already served on the table in the **dining room**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aari o paghawak sa isang bagay. Maaari din itong tumukoy sa isang bagay na pagmamay-ari ng isang tao.
original_explanation: Hindi lang ito 'yung mga gamit mo. Posesyon din 'yung lupa na pinag-aawayan ng magkakamag-anak sa mga teleserye. It's anything you legally or physically own, from your cellphone to that piece of land na may 'No Trespassing' sign.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa mga legal na konteksto at pormal na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang titulo ng lupa ay patunay ng kanyang legal na **posesyon** sa ari-arian.","translation":"The land title is proof of his legal **possession** of the property."}]

translation: to sadden; to make someone sad
meaning_filipino: Ang maging dahilan ng kalungkutan o pighati ng isang tao.
original_explanation: The opposite of magpalugod. This is what happens when your internet connection dies during an online final exam, or when your favorite character gets killed off in a series. It's the act of causing sadness. Minsan, 'di mo kailangan ng kaaway, sapat na ang memories para magpalungkot sa'yo. Hugot!
usage_notes: A very common and direct way to express the act of causing sadness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw kong **magpalungkot** sa iyo, pero kailangan mong malaman ang totoo.","translation":"I don't want to **sadden** you, but you need to know the truth."},{"sentence":"Ang balitang iyon ay tiyak na **nagpalungkot** sa buong pamilya.","translation":"That news certainly **saddened** the whole family."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paglalaban, pagtatalo, o pag-aaway ng mga ideya, interes, o puwersa. Maaari itong maging pisikal, berbal, o sa antas ng kaisipan.
original_explanation: This is the official term for the drama in your favorite teleserye. The **tunggali** between the bida and the kontrabida. The **tunggali** between your desire to go to the gym and your desire to eat a whole pizza. It's the struggle, the clash, the main event.
usage_notes: Commonly found in literary analysis (e.g., 'tunggalian ng mga tauhan' - conflict of characters) and formal discourse.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **tunggali** sa pagitan ng kabutihan at kasamaan ay isang pangkaraniwang tema sa panitikan.","translation":"The **conflict** between good and evil is a common theme in literature."},{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng matinding **tunggali** ang dalawang panig sa pulong.","translation":"There was a heated **dispute** between the two sides at the meeting."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pagkain na gawa sa harina, tubig, at kung minsan ay itlog, na hinuhulma sa mahahabang piraso at niluluto sa kumukulong tubig.
etymology: Hiram na salita mula sa Ingles na 'noodles'.
original_explanation: The ultimate Pinoy comfort food, whether it's the 15-peso instant kind you eat during petsa de peligro, or the birthday pancit that promises long life. It's the stringy, carby goodness that holds our society together.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa pangkalahatan para sa lahat ng uri ng noodles, lokal man o dayuhan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong kainin ang instant **noodles** na may itlog kapag umuulan.","translation":"My favorite thing to eat is instant **noodles** with an egg when it's raining."},{"sentence":"Nag-crave ako sa **noodles**, kaya nagluto ako ng pancit canton.","translation":"I was craving for **noodles**, so I cooked pancit canton."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na paltos o pamamaga sa balat na karaniwang naglalaman ng likido, na sanhi ng paso, kiskis, o impeksyon.
original_explanation: It's that bubble on your skin that screams "Error 404: Skin Not Found." You get it from wearing new shoes that are "tiis-ganda," from accidentally touching a hot kawali, or from too much friction. The urge to pop it is real, but everyone says you shouldn't. Parang chismis, masarap ikalat pero masama ang epekto.
usage_notes: Often used to describe blisters from burns ('paso') or friction ('kiskis').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ako ng **lintog** sa paa dahil sa bago kong sapatos.","translation":"I got a **blister** on my foot because of my new shoes."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong putukin ang **lintog** para maiwasan ang impeksyon.","translation":"Don't pop the **blister** to avoid infection."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagsipsip o paghigop ng likido, hangin, o usok gamit ang bibig.
original_explanation: The sound you make when you're trying to get the last drop of your milk tea, boba pearls and all. It's that little sipsip action. Can also refer to taking a puff from a cigarette or vape.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa anyong pandiwa na 'humiphip' (sumipsip/humigop) o 'hiphipin' (sipsipin/higupin). Ang pangngalan ay tumutukoy sa mismong aksyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **hiphip** lang mula sa kaniyang sigarilyo ay kinalma na niya.","translation":"Just one **puff** from his cigarette calmed him down."},{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **hiphip** niya sa straw habang inuubos ang juice.","translation":"I heard his **sip** on the straw as he finished the juice."}]

translation: like a stone; very hard; unemotional
meaning_filipino: Isang paglalarawan sa isang bagay na napakatigas o sa isang taong manhid, walang emosyon, o hindi madaling makaramdam.
original_explanation: This is your heart after your 5th situationship. Or your pan de sal after leaving it out for a day. It can mean literally hard, or emotionally impenetrable. 'Pusong bato' is its final form.
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang simile na ginagamit upang ilarawan ang katigasan ng isang bagay o ang kawalan ng emosyon ng isang tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang puso niya ay **parang bato**, hindi na tinatablan ng pakiusap.","translation":"His heart is **like a stone**, no longer moved by pleas."},{"sentence":"Tumigas na ang sinaing na kanin, **parang bato** na!","translation":"The cooked rice has hardened, it's **like a stone** now!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang marka na tuldok; ang bantas na naghuhudyat ng katapusan ng isang pangungusap. Salitang may pinagmulang Bisaya.
etymology: From Visayan languages (e.g., Cebuano, Hiligaynon) 'tudlok' meaning 'point' or 'dot'.
original_explanation: 'Tudlok' is the Visayan cousin of the Tagalog 'tuldok'. It's the dot at the end of a sentence, the 'seen' at the end of your long message to your crush. Periodt. It's the final say, the end of the discussion. Walang kasunod.
usage_notes: While understood in many contexts, especially in areas with many Visayan speakers, the more common Tagalog term is 'tuldok'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang maglagay ng **tudlok** sa dulo ng bawat pangungusap.","translation":"Don't forget to put a **period** at the end of every sentence."},{"sentence":"Isang maliit na **tudlok** lamang ang pagkakaiba ng dalawang disenyo.","translation":"Just a small **dot** is the only difference between the two designs."}]

translation: to lend money; to give credit
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng pera sa isang tao na may kasunduang ito ay ibabalik, kadalasan ay may kasamang interes o tubo.
original_explanation: The quickest way to test a friendship. "Pwedeng magpautang?" is the start of many financial sagas. If you're the one lending, you're the 'nagpapautang'. If you're the one borrowing, you're the 'umutang'. Be careful, baka ma-5-6 ka.
usage_notes: The subject of the verb is the lender.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **magpautang** sa kaibigan dahil baka masira ang inyong pagsasamahan.","translation":"It's difficult to **lend money** to a friend because it might ruin your relationship."},{"sentence":"Nag-aalok siyang **magpautang** na may maliit na interes.","translation":"He offers to **give credit** with a small interest."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtingin sa labas mula sa isang bintana, balkonahe, o anumang mataas na lugar sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: This is what Marites and the gang will be doing when they hear the chismis siren (aka an ambulance or a couple fighting). It's the classic 'patingin nga' move from your window to see if the GrabFood rider has arrived. Future tense of being a professional neighborhood watcher.
usage_notes: Future tense of "dumungaw". The prefix "mag-" is also commonly used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mamaya, **magdudungaw** ako sa bintana para abangan ang prusisyon.","translation":"Later, I **will look out** the window to wait for the procession."},{"sentence":"Sino ba ang hindi **magdudungaw** kung may maingay sa kalsada?","translation":"Who wouldn't **look out** if there's noise on the street?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkawala ng kakayahang igalaw ang isa o higit pang bahagi ng katawan, na kadalasang sanhi ng pinsala sa nervous system o sakit.
original_explanation: This is a serious one. It refers to the medical condition of paralysis. Figuratively, it can also mean being completely unable to act or decide, like when you have so many tasks you end up doing none of them—that's 'analysis paralysis' or a form of 'pagkalumpo' ng isip.
usage_notes: Can be used both in a literal medical sense and a figurative sense to mean complete inaction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkalumpo** niya ay resulta ng isang malagim na aksidente sa sasakyan.","translation":"His **paralysis** was the result of a tragic car accident."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa takot, tila nakaranas siya ng **pagkalumpo** at hindi nakakilos.","translation":"Because of fear, it was as if he experienced **paralysis** and could not move."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o paghiling na buksan ang isang bagay na nakasara, tulad ng pinto, bintana, o kahon.
original_explanation: When you're carrying a mountain of groceries and can't open the door yourself, you shout, "Pabukas ng pinto!" That's the command form. The verb for that action is *magpabukas*. "Nagpabukas ako ng pinto kay kuya." It's the act of delegating the 'opening' task.
usage_notes: The meaning is dependent on the pronunciation of the root word 'bukas' as /bu-KAS/, with stress on the last syllable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masyadong masikip ang takip ng garapon kaya **nagpabukas** siya sa kanyang asawa.","translation":"The jar lid was too tight so she **had her husband open** it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na katangian na tumutukoy sa isang tao na karapat-dapat o may potensyal na maging kasintahan.
etymology: Isang modernong hibridong salita mula sa salitang balbal na "jowa" at ang Ingles na hulaping "-able".
original_explanation: The ultimate compliment in the modern Pinoy dating scene. It means you're not just for "fun," you're for keeps. You're the type they'd bring home to meet the titas and titos. You have good character, a stable job (or at least a plan), and you know how to peel a shrimp. You're wife/husband material, but make it slang.
usage_notes: Used to describe someone who possesses qualities desirable in a long-term partner.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabait siya, matalino, at may trabaho. Sobrang **jowable**!","translation":"He's kind, smart, and has a job. So **relationship material**!"},{"sentence":"Hindi lang itsura ang basehan para masabing **jowable** ang isang tao.","translation":"Looks aren't the only basis for saying a person is **relationship material**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagdami at pagpatong-patong ng mga bagay sa isang lugar na walang kaayusan.
