original_explanation: Your laundry chair. Your unread emails. Your Shopee parcels. Your 'sana all' moments. Anything that piles up until it becomes a mountain of either literal stuff or figurative 'feels'. 'Yan ang nagkakabuntun-bunton.
usage_notes: The repetition of 'bunton' emphasizes the messiness and large quantity of the pile.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagkakabuntun-bunton** na ang mga labahin sa kwarto niya.","translation":"The laundry is **piling up** in his room."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **magkabuntun-bunton** ang iyong mga gawain.","translation":"Don't let your tasks **accumulate in heaps**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang establisyimento kung saan inihahanda ang mga yumao para sa kanilang libing o kremasyon, at kung saan idinaraos ang burol o lamay.
original_explanation: The final boarding gate. The place for 'lamay' where you drink free coffee, play cards (tong-its, pusoy dos), and share stories about the dearly departed. It’s also where you see who among your titas is the most dramatic crier.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala ang kanyang labi sa isang kilalang **punerarya**.","translation":"His remains were brought to a well-known **funeral parlor**."},{"sentence":"Nagtipon ang pamilya sa **punerarya** para sa huling gabi ng lamay.","translation":"The family gathered at the **funeral parlor** for the last night of the wake."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkalagas o pagkahulog ng mga balahibo ng ibon o buhok ng tao, karaniwan ay dahil sa pagpapalit o sakit.
original_explanation: You know when your dog sheds all over the sofa? That's "paglulugon." Or when birds moult and leave feathers everywhere? That's `lugon`. For humans, it's when your hair is falling out at an alarming rate, either from stress or because you bleached it one too many times. "Grabe ang lugon ng buhok ko!" is the cry for help you say to your hairdresser.
usage_notes: Can refer to animals (moulting) or humans (hair fall). The verb form is 'maglugon' or 'nalulugon'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Panahon na naman ng **lugon** ng mga manok kaya maraming balahibong nagkalat.","translation":"It's the chickens' **moulting** season again, so there are many feathers scattered around."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa stress, napansin niyang dumami ang **lugon** ng kanyang buhok.","translation":"Due to stress, she noticed an increase in her hair **fall**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang makapal at masinsing pagtubo ng mga halaman, baging, at maliliit na puno na mahirap pasukin o daanan.
original_explanation: This is the part of the forest in horror movies you're not supposed to go into. A **dawag** is a jungle of thorny vines and tangled plants, the kind of place where duwendes and engkantos supposedly hang out. It’s the natural version of the mess in your 'bodega' or that one 'tambak' corner of your room.
usage_notes: Evokes a sense of wildness, impenetrability, and getting lost.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahirapan silang makalabas sa makapal na **dawag** ng gubat.","translation":"They had difficulty getting out of the dense **thicket** of the forest."},{"sentence":"May nakita raw silang anino sa gitna ng **dawag**.","translation":"They said they saw a shadow in the middle of the **undergrowth**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na nangangahulugang magaling, matapang, o kahanga-hanga.
original_explanation: The ultimate Pinoy compliment for anything cool, from a sick motorcycle to a friend who aces a final exam without studying. It's a word that survived decades, evolving from "tough guy" to "awesome." Originally from 'matigas' (hard) spelled backwards, 'astig' is the sound of pure, unadulterated Pinoy approval.
usage_notes: A very common slang term used across different age groups, though it originated as youth slang in the 1970s-80s.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Astig** 'yung bagong sapatos mo, saan mo nabili?","translation":"Your new shoes are **awesome**, where did you buy them?"},{"sentence":"Para sa akin, **astig** 'yung mga taong kayang ipaglaban ang tama.","translation":"For me, people who can fight for what's right are **cool**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging puno ng tiyan dahil sa sapat o labis na pagkain; hindi na nakakaramdam ng gutom.
original_explanation: The official feeling after conquering an 'unli-rice' or 'samgyupsal' promo. It's that glorious state of being where you can't possibly eat another bite, and all you want to do is find the nearest couch and enter a food coma. The opposite of 'gutom'.
usage_notes: Very common word used after eating. The stress is on the second syllable, distinguishing it from the noun 'busog' (bow).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Salamat sa pagkain, **busog** na **busog** na ako!","translation":"Thanks for the food, I'm very **full** now!"},{"sentence":"Huwag mo na akong alukin, **busog** pa ako mula sa tanghalian.","translation":"Don't offer me any more, I'm still **satiated** from lunch."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng tulong sa mga nangangailangan nang walang hinihintay na kapalit; gawaing pangkawanggawa o pagkakawanggawa.
etymology: Mula sa `awang` (pity, mercy) + `gawa` (work, deed). Literal na 'gawa ng awa'.
original_explanation: This is the spirit of 'Bayanihan' in action. It's donating to a community pantry, volunteering for a cause, or even just treating a friend who's broke before payday. It's doing good for others without expecting a 'thank you' post or anything in return. Pure, selfless giving.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa parehong akto ng pagkakawanggawa at sa konsepto mismo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming organisasyon ang nabubuhay dahil sa **kawanggawa**.","translation":"Many organizations subsist on **charity**."},{"sentence":"Ang pagtulong sa kapwa ay isang uri ng **kawanggawa**.","translation":"Helping others is a form of **philanthropy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mamahalin at matigas na batong hiyas na karaniwang walang kulay at binubuo ng purong karbon.
original_explanation: Not just a girl's best friend, but the source of all power in Encantadia. Before you ask for one for your engagement ring, make sure it's not the Brilyante ng Apoy, baka mag-away lang kayo. Pashnea!
usage_notes: Its popularity surged due to the fantasy TV series "Encantadia," where magical gems were called 'brilyante'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang singsing na may **brilyante** ay simbolo ng walang hanggang pag-ibig.","translation":"A ring with a **diamond** is a symbol of eternal love."},{"sentence":"Nawawala ang ika-limang **brilyante** ng Lireo.","translation":"The fifth **diamond** of Lireo is missing."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdurog o pagpino ng isang bagay gamit ang gilingan; maaari ring tumukoy sa pag-ikot ng katawan, lalo na ng balakang.
original_explanation: Two meanings, one word. 1) The serious one: what your lola does to rice to make 'galapong' for bibingka. 2) The fun one: what you do on the dance floor when the DJ plays that budots song or your favorite K-pop track. It’s the signature move of many a TikTok challenge. "Grabe **gumiling** si ate, parang walang buto!"
usage_notes: This word has a primary, literal meaning (to grind) and a very common secondary, figurative meaning (to dance sensually/gyrate). Both are widely understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Gumiling** siya ng kape para sa mga bisita.","translation":"She **ground** coffee for the guests."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula siyang **gumiling** sa saliw ng malakas na tugtog.","translation":"She started to **gyrate** to the beat of the loud music."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ugali ng pagiging sakim o hindi mapagbigay; labis na pag-iisip sa sarili at pagkakait sa iba.
original_explanation: This is the person who brings a single piece of candy to a party and eats it themselves. They won't share their Wi-Fi password, their fries, or their notes. The 'sana all' is never for them, because 'all' is for them. The opposite of 'libre' culture.
usage_notes: Isang matinding negatibong katangian na nagpapahiwatig ng kawalan ng pagkabukas-palad.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa kanyang **pagkamaramot** kaya walang gustong humingi ng tulong sa kanya.","translation":"He is known for his **stinginess**, so no one wants to ask for his help."}]

translation: to exchange with; to trade with
meaning_filipino: Ang sabay na pagbibigay at pagtanggap ng isang bagay mula sa isa't isa; ang pagpapalit ng pag-aari o posisyon.
etymology: From 'makipag-' (to mutually do something) and 'palit' (change, exchange).
original_explanation: This is the verb for your office Kris Kringle, swapping shifts with a co-worker, or trading your duplicate Pokémon card. It can be an exchange of things ('makipagpalitan ng regalo'), words ('makipagpalitan ng kuro-kuro'), or even something more intense, like angry words ('makipagpalitan ng masasakit na salita').
usage_notes: A very versatile word. The object of the exchange is often specified after the verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **makipagpalitan** ng aklat sa iyo.","translation":"I want to **exchange** books with you."},{"sentence":"Nag-**makipagpalitan** sila ng matatamis na ngiti.","translation":"They **exchanged** sweet smiles."},{"sentence":"Ang mga politiko ay nag-**makipagpalitan** ng maaanghang na salita sa debate.","translation":"The politicians **traded** sharp words during the debate."}]

translation: to have a dialogue, to converse
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagkakaroon ng pormal na pag-uusap o palitan ng kuro-kuro sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang tao.
original_explanation: Parang group chat sa Messenger, pero mas seryoso at walang stickers. Ito 'yung ginagawa ng mga magulang mo at ng principal kapag may kalokohan kang ginawa sa school. O kaya 'yung usapan niyo ng jowa mo na 'We need to talk.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magdialogo** upang malutas ang hindi pagkakaunawaan.","translation":"We need to **have a dialogue** to resolve the misunderstanding."},{"sentence":"**Nagdialogo** ang mga lider ng iba't ibang bansa sa summit.","translation":"The leaders of different countries **conversed** at the summit."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong may ugaling mang-abuso o manliit ng kapwa, lalo na sa mga mas mahihina o walang kalaban-laban.
original_explanation: The kontrabida in every teleserye. The office manager na power-tripper. The school bully who lives for your lunch money. Sila yung mga taong aangat lang kapag may tinatapakan. Basically, anyone who uses their power, whether real or imagined, to make others feel small.
usage_notes: A strong word used to describe a person who habitually mistreats or bullies others, especially those in a weaker position.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala ang amo bilang isang **mapang-api** na lider.","translation":"The boss is known as an **oppressive** leader."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **mapang-api** sa iyong mga kapatid.","translation":"Don't be **abusive** towards your siblings."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagaganap o umiiral nang paulit-ulit; siksik o malapit sa isa't isa, tulad ng buhok o halaman.
etymology: ma- (having the quality of) + dalas (frequency, density)
original_explanation: Same word, different context. Can describe your 'madalas' na pag-order ng milk tea (frequent). Or your friend's kilay na on fleek—'madalas' ang tubo (dense). It's about how close together things are, whether in time or in space.
usage_notes: As an adjective, it can mean 'frequent' (e.g., madalas na pagbisita) or 'dense' (e.g., madalas na buhok).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **madalas** na pag-ulan ay sanhi ng pagbaha.","translation":"The **frequent** rain is the cause of the flood."},{"sentence":"Mayroon siyang **madalas** at makapal na buhok.","translation":"She has **dense** and thick hair."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang hugis na may apat na tuwid na gilid at apat na tamang anggulo, kung saan ang magkakatapat na gilid ay magkapareho ng haba.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na "parejo" (parehas, pantay) at Tagalog na "haba" (length), na nagpapahiwatig ng magkaparehong haba ng magkabilang gilid.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung hugis ng smartphone mo, ng blackboard sa school, at ng pinto ng kwarto mo. Hindi bilog, hindi tatsulok. 'Pag sinabing "box-type", usually **parihaba** ang tinutukoy, hindi parisukat. Parang 'yung box na pinaglagyan ng pag-asa mong magkakabalikan kayo, pero empty na pala.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng isang **parihabang** mesa para sa aming kusina.","translation":"Mom bought a **rectangular** table for our kitchen."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkakaroon ng sapat o hustong dami ng isang bagay upang matugunan ang isang pangangailangan.
original_explanation: That "sakto lang" feeling. Not too much, not too little. It's when your sahod is just enough to cover bills, a little bit of luho, and some savings. Walang labis, walang kulang. It's the opposite of "sana all" and the reality of "eto lang." It's achieving budget balance, the adulting dream.
usage_notes: Often used in discussions about resources, budget, and needs.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat nating tiyakin ang **kasapatan** ng suplay ng pagkain para sa lahat.","translation":"We must ensure the **sufficiency** of the food supply for everyone."},{"sentence":"Ang **kasapatan** ng kanyang kita ay sapat lamang para sa kanilang pang-araw-araw na gastos.","translation":"The **adequacy** of his income is just enough for their daily expenses."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o institusyon na nagbibigay o nag-aambag ng isang bagay, tulad ng pera, ari-arian, o dugo, para sa isang layunin o kawanggawa.
original_explanation: This is the formal, Spanish-derived word for 'donor'. You'll see this on plaques in churches or schools: "Pinagawa ni Donador Juan Dela Cruz." It sounds more high-class than just "nagbigay." It's your tita from the US who sends a balikbayan box, but on a corporate or philanthropic level.
usage_notes: More formal and less common in everyday speech than its English counterpart "donor", which is also frequently used in Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghahanap ang ospital ng mga **donador** ng dugo.","translation":"The hospital is looking for blood **donors**."},{"sentence":"Nakatala ang pangalan ng mga **donador** sa isang plake.","translation":"The names of the **benefactors** are listed on a plaque."}]

translation: can be likened to; can be compared to
meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang maghambing o magturing na may pagkakatulad sa isang bagay, tao, o konsepto.
etymology: ma- (ability prefix) + i- (object-focus prefix) + wawá (reduplication of first syllable of root) + wangis (likeness)
original_explanation: This is a fancy, literary word you pull out to sound smart. It's like saying "pwede i-compare" but with more oomph. You use it when you're trying to explain something complex by relating it to something simple. "Ang pag-ibig ay maiwawangis sa isang laro ng chess." See? Instant poet.
usage_notes: This is a contemplative, future-tense verb. It's often used in formal writing, poetry, or deep conversations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang ganda ay **maiwawangis** sa isang bukang-liwayway.","translation":"Her beauty **can be likened** to a sunrise."},{"sentence":"Saan mo **maiwawangis** ang pakiramdam ng unang pagkabigo?","translation":"To what **can you compare** the feeling of your first failure?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalatag o paglalagay ng aspalto sa isang daan o ibabaw.
original_explanation: This is the action verb for road projects. When the local government promises to fix your street, they're going to 'aspaltuhan' it. It's a sign of progress, or an upcoming election. 'Sana bago mag-tag-ulan, ma-aspaltuhan na nila ang lubak-lubak na daan.'
usage_notes: Ang mga anyo nito ay inaaspaltuhan (paving), inaspaltuhan (paved), aaspaltuhan (will pave).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Aaspaltuhan** daw ng DPWH ang mga pangunahing kalsada sa susunod na buwan.","translation":"They say the DPWH **will pave with asphalt** the main roads next month."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtakas o pag-iwas mula sa isang mapanganib o hindi kanais-nais na lugar o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: That feeling when you finally get to log off after a toxic day of back-to-back meetings. It's your 'Friday 5 PM' moment, your great iskape from the demands of adulting. Also, what your Houdini-like cat does every time you open the door.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'takas'. 'Iskape' can sound slightly more formal or literary.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagplano ng **iskape** ang mga bilanggo mula sa mahigpit na kulungan.","translation":"The prisoners planned an **escape** from the high-security prison."}]

translation: to feel nauseated; to be disgusted
meaning_filipino: Makaranas ng pakiramdam ng pagkasuklam o pagkadiri na halos ikasuka, sanhi ng isang bagay na nakita, naamoy, o naramdaman.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping pandiwa na `ma-`, salitang-ugat na `alibadbad` (pagkarimarim), at hulaping `-an`.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling mo pag nakakita ka ng ipis na lumilipad papunta sa'yo. Or when you smell something expired from the back of the ref. It's that physical "eww" reaction that makes your stomach churn. "I can't even."
usage_notes: Inilalarawan ang matinding pakiramdam ng pisikal na pagkasuklam o pagkahilo. Mas matindi ito kaysa sa `mandiri` (to feel disgusted).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Naalibadbaran** ako sa amoy ng basura.","translation":"I **felt nauseated** by the smell of the garbage."},{"sentence":"Halos **maalibadbaran** siya sa kaniyang nakita.","translation":"She almost **got disgusted** by what she saw."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng mabilis at malakas na pag-apoy o pag-alab ng isang bagay; ang biglaang pagsiklab ng apoy.
original_explanation: That moment when a small spark becomes a full-on bonfire. It's the "on fire" emoji in verb form. Can be literal, like your barbecue grill going wild, or metaphorical, like the pagliliyab of your anger when your internet connection dies during an online game, or the pagliliyab of passion in a teleserye love scene.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for fire or metaphorically for strong emotions like anger or passion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagulat ang lahat sa biglaang **pagliliyab** ng tuyong damo.","translation":"Everyone was surprised by the sudden **flaring up** of the dry grass."},{"sentence":"Ramdam ko ang **pagliliyab** ng galit sa kanyang mga mata.","translation":"I could feel the **blazing** of anger in his/her eyes."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagbuo ng isang balangkas o plano ng mga ideya, karaniwang sa paraang nakasulat o nakalarawan, bago ang pinal na pagsulat o paggawa.
original_explanation: This is what your prof asks you to do before writing your thesis, but you skip it and go straight to writing, then realize halfway through that you're lost. It's the 'isipin mo muna bago ka kumuda' of academic writing. Parang pagplano ng attack sa Mobile Legends, kailangan may strategy.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa mga kontekstong akademiko, pampanitikan, o pormal na pagpaplano.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan ng guro ang mga mag-aaral na **ibanghay** ang mga pangunahing kaganapan sa nobela.","translation":"The teacher instructed the students to **outline** the main events of the novel."},{"sentence":"Mahalagang **ibanghay** muna ang mga gagawin upang maging organisado ang proyekto.","translation":"It's important to first **outline** the tasks to make the project organized."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkakaroon ng labis na yaman, kaginhawahan, at magagarang bagay na hindi lubos na kailangan.
original_explanation: That "sana all" feeling you get when you see a celebrity's house tour on YouTube. It's the land of branded bags, out-of-the-country trips every long weekend, and not having to check your bank account before ordering food. The opposite of "petsa de peligro" life.
usage_notes: Carries a sense of grandeur and sometimes excess. Often implies a lifestyle that is visibly and lavishly wealthy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nabubuhay sa **karangyaan** ang pamilya ng politiko.","translation":"The politician's family lives in **luxury**."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya ipinagmamalaki ang kanyang **karangyaan** sa harap ng mahihirap.","translation":"She does not flaunt her **opulence** in front of the poor."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabago ng tunog upang maging matinis o mataas.
original_explanation: This is the sound you make when you see a cockroach fly. It’s the sound of a microphone feeding back during an event. It's when your voice goes up several octaves out of fear, excitement, or 'kilig'. "Tuminis ang boses niya nang makita si crush." It's the auditory equivalent of a jump scare.
usage_notes: Refers to the action of a sound becoming sharp or high-pitched. Can describe a voice, a whistle, or an instrument.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tuminis** ang pito ng pulis, hudyat na kailangang huminto.","translation":"The policeman's whistle **became high-pitched**, a signal to stop."},{"sentence":"Biglang **tuminis** ang boses ng babae sa takot.","translation":"The woman's voice suddenly **shrieked** in fear."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lupain at mga gusali na bumubuo sa isang unibersidad, kolehiyo, o paaralan.
etymology: From English "campus," which is from Latin "campus" (field).
original_explanation: The place where you made the best and worst decisions of your young adult life. It's the land of instant noodles, puyat for exams, org activities, and that one terror prof. It's where your allowance magically disappears on milk tea and photocopies.
usage_notes: A direct loanword from English, fully integrated into Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkita-kita ang magkakaibigan sa loob ng **kampus**.","translation":"The friends met inside the **campus**."},{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang seguridad sa **kampus** ng unibersidad.","translation":"Security is tight on the university **campus**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao o pahayag na naglalatag ng mga prinsipyo bilang hindi mapag-aalinlanganang totoo, nang walang sapat na ebidensya o pagsasaalang-alang sa opinyon ng iba.
original_explanation: Ito yung tao sa comment section na feeling laging tama at isasampal sa'yo ang kanyang "facts" kahit galing lang sa isang unverified na blog. Sila yung tipo na hindi nakikinig sa argumento ng iba dahil para sa kanila, ang opinyon nila ay hindi opinyon, kundi batas. Walang "depende," walang "what if." Sila ang huling hurado.
usage_notes: Madalas may negatibong konotasyon, na nagpapahiwatig ng pagiging makitid ang isip.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masyadong **dogmatiko** ang kanyang pananaw kaya walang nakikinig sa kanya.","translation":"His views are too **dogmatic** that's why no one listens to him."},{"sentence":"Isang **dogmatiko**ng pahayag ang binitiwan ng lider.","translation":"The leader released a **dogmatic** statement."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malubhang sakit na sanhi ng abnormal at hindi makontrol na pagdami ng mga selula sa katawan, na maaaring kumalat sa ibang bahagi nito.
original_explanation: The Big C. It's a serious illness, but in Pinoy humor, it can also refer to a toxic person or situation that slowly drains the life out of you. "'Yung jowa mong selosa, parang kanser sa lipunan."
usage_notes: A medical term that has also entered figurative language to describe something extremely harmful or destructive.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng maagang pagsusuri upang maiwasan ang sakit na **kanser**.","translation":"Early detection is needed to prevent the disease of **cancer**."},{"sentence":"Itinuturing niyang **kanser** sa kanilang kumpanya ang katiwalian.","translation":"He considers corruption a **cancer** in their company."}]

meaning_filipino: Linisin ang mga ngipin gamit ang sipilyo at toothpaste.
original_explanation: Your dentist's favorite word. It's the daily ritual you do to fight off plaque, coffee stains, and the ghost of last night's garlic rice. The main reason your crush might actually talk to you up close.
usage_notes: A very common daily activity verb. Often used interchangeably with 'mag-toothbrush'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **magsipilyo** bago matulog.","translation":"Don't forget to **brush your teeth** before sleeping."},{"sentence":"Sinabihan ako ng dentista na kailangan kong **magsipilyo** nang tatlong beses sa isang araw.","translation":"The dentist told me I need to **brush my teeth** three times a day."}]

meaning_filipino: Kalat na kalat o laganap sa isang malawak na lugar, pangkat, o sakop ng panahon.
etymology: From 'laganap,' which means widespread. The 'ma-' prefix emphasizes the state of being widespread. 'Laganap' itself is a variation of 'ganap' (complete, full).
original_explanation: Parang chismis sa office, **malaganap**. One minute, it's a secret; the next, even the guard at the lobby knows. It describes something that has spread everywhere, like a viral meme, a new K-drama, or unfortunately, a new variant. It's everywhere!
usage_notes: Often used with social phenomena, news, diseases, or trends.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Malaganap** ang paggamit ng social media sa mga kabataan ngayon.","translation":"The use of social media is **widespread** among the youth today."},{"sentence":"Naging **malaganap** ang balita tungkol sa pagtaas ng presyo ng bilihin.","translation":"The news about the price hike of goods became **prevalent**."}]

translation: cannot be, not possible, not allowed
meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na imposible, ipinagbabawal, o labag sa alituntunin o batas ng kalikasan.
original_explanation: The more formal, dramatic older sibling of "bawal." This is what your boss says when you ask for a 1-month vacation. It's what teleserye characters scream when they find out they're related to their one true love. "Hindi! Hindi maaari!"
usage_notes: Stronger and more formal than "hindi puwede". It often implies a rule, a law, or a fundamental impossibility.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hindi maaari** na pumasok sa loob nang walang pahintulot.","translation":"It **is not allowed** to enter without permission."},{"sentence":"Sabi ng doktor, **hindi maaari** na kumain siya ng matatamis.","translation":"The doctor said, it **is not possible** for him/her to eat sweets."}]

translation: to crack; to cause something to crack
meaning_filipino: Magdulot ng lamat o biyak sa isang bagay; sirain sa pamamagitan ng paglikha ng mga bitak.
original_explanation: What happens to the road after a small earthquake, or your phone screen after you drop it for the nth time. "Nako, 'wag mong upuan 'yang plastic na upuan, baka bitakin mo." It's also what happens to your heart when you see your crush with someone else. Aray.
usage_notes: Refers to the action of creating cracks or fissures on a surface.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kaya mong **bitakin** ang nuez gamit lang ang iyong kamay?","translation":"Can you **crack** the nut using only your hand?"},{"sentence":"Ang matinding init ay maaaring **bitakin** ang lupa.","translation":"The intense heat can **cause the ground to crack**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahaba at makitid na daanan sa loob ng isang gusali na nag-uugnay sa iba't ibang silid o bahagi nito.
original_explanation: The long hallway in the office where you do the 'walk of shame' when you're late. Or the hospital passageway that feels like a horror movie set at night. This is also where quick gossip sessions with your work bestie happen on the way to the pantry. This is the more common spelling than 'koredor'.
usage_notes: This is the standard spelling in Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkita sila sa **koridor** ng hotel.","translation":"They met in the hotel **corridor**."},{"sentence":"Ang opisina ng prinsipal ay nasa dulo ng **koridor** na iyon.","translation":"The principal's office is at the end of that **hallway**."}]

translation: to enforce; to make something prevail; to implement
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapatupad o pagpapagana ng isang batas, patakaran, o prinsipyo upang ito ang masunod o mangibabaw.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `mag-` (gumanap ng kilos), `pa-` (sanhi), at salitang-ugat na `iral` (pag-iral, pagkabuhay, o paggana).
original_explanation: This is what strict parents, terror profs, and micromanager bosses do. They `magpairal` their rules, no questions asked. 'Bawal mag-cellphone sa klase!' 'Dapat on-cam sa Zoom meeting!' It's about making your will—or the system's will—the law of the land (or the office, or the house).
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa mga pormal na konteksto tulad ng batas, pamamahala, at pamamalakad ng organisasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat nating **magpairal** ng disiplina sa ating mga sarili.","translation":"We must **enforce** discipline upon ourselves."},{"sentence":"Ang bagong administrasyon ay nangakong **magpairal** ng mga batas laban sa korapsyon.","translation":"The new administration promised to **implement** laws against corruption."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpunta sa loob ng isang lugar; tumutukoy din sa regular na pagdalo sa trabaho o paaralan. Ito ay nasa pangkasalukuyang panahunan.
original_explanation: The daily grind. That 'Time to make the donuts' feeling every morning. 'Pre, pumapasok ka ba ngayon?' is the classic text you send a co-worker to see if you're the only one suffering today. It's the verb form of 'adulting'.
usage_notes: This is the present tense form. Past tense is 'pumasok'. Future tense is 'papasok'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pumapasok** na ang mga estudyante sa kanilang mga silid-aralan.","translation":"The students **are entering** their classrooms now."},{"sentence":"Maaga siyang **pumapasok** sa opisina araw-araw.","translation":"He **goes to** the office early every day."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malakas na sipa, karaniwang ginagamit ang sakong o talampakan, at madalas na patalikod o patagilid.
original_explanation: Yung sipa ng kabayo. O 'yung gusto mong gawin sa vending machine 'pag kinain 'yung bayad mo. Hindi ito ang 'sipa' na ginagamit sa laro; ito'y mas marahas at malakas.
usage_notes: Mas malakas at mas marahas kaysa sa karaniwang 'sipa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malakas na **tadyak** mula sa kabayo ang tumama sa pader.","translation":"A strong **kick** from the horse hit the wall."},{"sentence":"Nakatanggap siya ng **tadyak** sa likod habang naglalakad.","translation":"He received a **kick** in the back while walking."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kusang-loob na pinipiling manatiling walang asawa o kasintahan.
etymology: From the English phrase 'single by choice'.
original_explanation: The official relationship status of titas and titos who are tired of their relatives asking "Kailan ka ikakasal?". It's not that you can't get a jowa, it's that you'd rather spend your money on travel, skincare, and peace of mind. A power move.
usage_notes: A modern Taglish phrase used to assert independence in one's relationship status.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ako naghahanap ng jowa. **Single by choice** ako ngayon.","translation":"I'm not looking for a partner. I'm **single by choice** right now."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malaking hipon (Penaeus monodon) na karaniwang inaalagaan at kinakain, kilala sa laki at guhit sa katawan.
original_explanation: Yung aroganteng pinsan ng hipon. Mas malaki, mas mahal, at mas masarap. Eto yung special occasion seafood, yung handa kapag may bisitang taga-abroad o kapag nanalo ka sa lotto. The king of crustaceans sa palengke.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to the large tiger prawn, distinct from the smaller 'hipon' (shrimp).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-uwi si Tatay ng isang kilong sariwang **sugpo** mula sa palengke.","translation":"Dad brought home a kilo of fresh **prawns** from the market."},{"sentence":"Masarap gawing sinigang o butter-garlic ang **sugpo**.","translation":"**Prawns** are delicious in sinigang or as butter-garlic."}]

translation: to support; to promote; to advocate
meaning_filipino: Suportahan at itaguyod ang isang layunin, prinsipyo, o samahan; tulungan ang isang tao o pamilya na umunlad.
original_explanation: This is what OFWs do for their families back home—they magtaguyod. It's also what you do when you champion a cause, like "Save the Pawikans" or "Support Local Coffee". It’s more than just 'support'; it has a sense of building up, championing, and sustaining. It's being the main character of someone's success story.
usage_notes: A strong, formal word that encompasses financial support, promotion of a cause, and helping someone to get on their feet.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang layunin ay **magtaguyod** ng mga karapatan ng kababaihan.","translation":"Her goal is to **advocate** for women's rights."},{"sentence":"Nagsisikap siyang **magtaguyod** ng kanyang pamilya sa pamamagitan ng pagtatrabaho sa ibang bansa.","translation":"She works hard to **support** her family by working in another country."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyon na nangangahulugang hindi magbabago ang isang desisyon o damdamin sa kabila ng anumang posibleng maganap sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: Ito ang ultimate "bahala na" but with commitment. Pangako ng BFF, "Besh, anuman ang mangyari, 'di kita iiwan." O kaya, linya sa K-drama bago mag-enlist sa military yung lead, "I'll wait for you, anuman ang mangyari!"
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang ipahayag ang katatagan, pangako, o determinasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Anuman ang mangyari**, magkikita tayo sa Sabado.","translation":"**Whatever happens**, we will see each other on Saturday."},{"sentence":"Ipaglalaban kita, **anuman ang mangyari**.","translation":"I will fight for you, **come what may**."}]
related: ["kahit anong mangyari","sa ayaw at sa gusto","bahala na"]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uunat ng mga bahagi ng katawan, partikular na ang mga kalamnan, upang maging handa sa pisikal na gawain o upang maibsan ang paninigas.
original_explanation: What you promise yourself you'll do before a workout but never do. Also, that satisfying feeling of stretching your arms after sitting at your desk for 8 hours straight. "Magbanat ka muna ng buto!" is the tita way of saying "Stop being lazy and do something!"
usage_notes: "Magbanat ng buto" (literally "to stretch the bones") is a very common idiom meaning "to work hard" or "to get to work".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magbanat** bago ka mag-ehersisyo para hindi ka mapulikat.","translation":"You need to **stretch** before you exercise so you don't get cramps."},{"sentence":"Maaga siyang gumising para **magbanat** ng buto sa bukid.","translation":"He woke up early to **work hard** in the field."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng isang bagay nang walang pag-iingat, paggalang, o pagsasaalang-alang sa maaaring maging epekto nito sa iba.
etymology: From `ka-` (marker for abstract nouns) + `walang` ('without') + `pakundangan` ('regard', 'consideration'). Literally 'the state of being without regard'.
original_explanation: This is the 'bahala na si Batman' attitude but with negative consequences. It's cutting in line at the MRT, blasting loud music at 2 AM, or posting a spoiler moments after a movie premiere. Basically, acting without thinking if you're bothering anyone else.
usage_notes: A strong word implying a blatant disregard for rules, norms, or the feelings of others.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ikinagalit ng marami ang kanyang **kawalang-pakundangan** sa pagsasalita.","translation":"Many were angered by his **inconsiderateness** in speaking."},{"sentence":"Ang **kawalang-pakundangan** niya sa pagmamaneho ay nagdulot ng aksidente.","translation":"His **recklessness** in driving caused an accident."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manipis na suson ng tisyu sa likod ng mata na sensitibo sa liwanag, kung saan nabubuo ang mga imahe bago ipadala sa utak.
original_explanation: The "screen" at the back of your eyeball. It's the part that processes all the chismis you see on social media, the finale of your favorite K-drama, and the face of your crush, before sending the data to your brain. Kapag nasira 'to, goodbye HD vision, hello blurry life. So take care of your eyes!
usage_notes: A specific medical and scientific term. Used directly in Filipino without a native equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasira ang kanyang **retina** dahil sa isang aksidente.","translation":"His **retina** was damaged due to an accident."},{"sentence":"Sinusuri ng doktor ang **retina** mo para malaman kung may problema sa iyong paningin.","translation":"The doctor is examining your **retina** to see if there is a problem with your vision."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabago tungo sa isang mas maganda o mas maayos na kalagayan.
original_explanation: That moment when the WiFi signal goes from one bar to full. Or when your friend finally gets over their toxic ex. 'Bumuti' is the universe giving you a high-five, a sign that things are looking up, from your health to your love life (sana all).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumuti** na ang pakiramdam ko pagkatapos uminom ng gamot.","translation":"I **felt better** after taking the medicine."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagsagawa ng kilos upang alisin ang dumi, kalat, o anumang bagay na nagparungis sa isang lugar o bagay. Ito ay nasa panahunang pangnagdaan.
etymology: From "linis" (clean) with the "nag-" prefix for the past tense.
original_explanation: The completed action of #GeneralCleaning. You did the thing. The floor is shiny, the dust is gone, and you can finally sit down and watch Netflix. 'Ma, naglinis na po ako ng kwarto ko,' you say, hoping it's enough to earn you some screen time or a trip to the mall.
usage_notes: The past tense (perfective aspect) of the verb "to clean".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Naglinis** ako kahapon kaya 'wag ninyong kakalatan.","translation":"I **cleaned** yesterday so don't make a mess."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **naglinis** ng kusina? Ang galing!","translation":"Who **cleaned** the kitchen? It's amazing!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagiging mas makapal o pagbuo ng kalyo, tulad sa balat. Ginagamit din sa metaporikal na paraan para sa pagiging manhid o walang hiya.
original_explanation: Two meanings: 1) Literal: Yung kamay mo na nagiging parang papel de liha dahil sa pagbubuhat sa gym. 2) Figurative: Yung mukha ng kaibigan mong nangutang tapos siya pa galit. "Nangangapal na ang mukha," meaning they've become shameless. The ultimate "kapal muks" evolution.
usage_notes: Mayroon itong literal na kahulugan (pagkapal ng balat, bagay) at isang napakakaraniwang idyomatikong kahulugan (pagiging walang hiya).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nangangapal** na ang kalyo sa kanyang mga kamay dahil sa mabibigat na gawain.","translation":"The callouses on his hands are **thickening** due to heavy work."},{"sentence":"Hindi ka na nahiya? Talagang **nangangapal** na 'yang mukha mo!","translation":"Aren't you ashamed? Your face is really **becoming thick** (you're becoming shameless)!"}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng kawalan ng pag-iingat o pag-iisip sa posibleng panganib; padalos-dalos sa pagkilos o pagpapasya.
original_explanation: This is your friend who jumps into a get-rich-quick scheme without reading the fine print. Someone galgal is recklessly impulsive. It's the "Bahala na si Batman!" attitude, but without any superpowers to back it up. It's acting first and thinking... maybe never. "Huwag kang galgal sa pag-drive, baka maaksidente tayo!"
usage_notes: Has a strong negative connotation of foolishness and lack of foresight.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Galgal** ang desisyon niyang mag-resign nang walang ipon.","translation":"His decision to resign without any savings was **reckless**."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang pagiging **galgal**, palagi siyang napapahamak.","translation":"Because of his **rashness**, he always gets into trouble."}]

translation: distinction, act of being unique or separate
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o akto ng pagiging natatangi, naiiba, o hiwalay sa karamihan.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're the only one in the friend group who's single, or the only one wearing a formal outfit to a casual party. It's the act of being unique, whether by choice ('main character energy') or by circumstance ('OP' - out of place).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pamumukod** sa klase ay dahil sa kanyang pambihirang talino.","translation":"His **distinction** in class is due to his extraordinary intelligence."},{"sentence":"Nais niyang maranasan ang **pamumukod** sa isang malayong isla.","translation":"He wants to experience **seclusion** on a remote island."}]

translation: until, as long as, up to
meaning_filipino: Ginagamit upang tukuyin ang hangganan o limitasyon sa oras, lugar, o kalagayan.
original_explanation: The ultimate "wait lang" word. "Maghihintay ako hangga't 'di ka dumarating" (I'll wait until you arrive) - the national anthem of the martir friend. "Mag-aaral ako hangga't kaya ko" (I'll study as long as I can) - the battle cry during finals week. It sets the boundary, the finish line you're either waiting for or trying to avoid.
usage_notes: Often appears as 'hanggang' (most common form), or as 'hangga't' (contraction of 'hangga at'). 'Hangga' by itself is less common in modern speech but is the root.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mananatili ako rito **hangga**'t kailangan mo ako.","translation":"I will stay here **as long as** you need me."},{"sentence":"Kumain ka **hangga** gusto mo.","translation":"Eat **as much as** you want."}]

translation: Filipino ceviche; a dish of raw fish or meat cured in vinegar
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng ulam na gawa sa hilaw na isda, karne, o lamang-dagat na ibinabad at "niluto" sa suka na may halong mga pampalasa tulad ng sibuyas, luya, at sili.
original_explanation: The ultimate "pulutan" (bar chow). This is what happens when raw fish (or goat meat, if you're brave) takes a long bath in vinegar, ginger, and onions. It's the perfect partner for a cold beer on a hot day. It's sour, it's spicy, it's fresh, and it's proof that you don't always need fire to make something delicious.
usage_notes: Different regions in the Philippines have their own versions of kilawin. For example, in the north, "kinilaw" is more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghanda si tatay ng **kilawin** na tanigue para sa aming pananghalian.","translation":"Dad prepared **Filipino ceviche** made of tanigue for our lunch."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang **kilawin** kung maraming sili at sibuyas.","translation":"**Kilawin** is delicious with lots of chili and onions."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang siyentipiko na nag-aaral ng mga buhay na organismo, kabilang ang kanilang estruktura, paglaki, pinagmulan, ebolusyon, at distribusyon.
original_explanation: The person who actually understood what 'mitochondria is the powerhouse of the cell' meant. They study everything alive, from the tiniest bacteria to the largest whale. Sila yung tinatanong mo kung anong pangalan ng halaman sa bakuran o kung bakit kakaiba yung kulisap na nakita mo.
usage_notes: Ang pambabaeng anyo ay 'biyologa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng mga **biyologo** ang epekto ng climate change sa mga hayop sa Pilipinas.","translation":"The **biologists** are studying the effects of climate change on animals in the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Isang marine **biyologo** ang kapatid niya na nagtatrabaho sa Palawan.","translation":"Her sibling is a marine **biologist** who works in Palawan."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gawain o kilos na labag sa batas at may kaukulang parusa.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung mga bagay na 'pag ginawa mo, siguradong may kalalagyan ka sa kulungan o sa balita. From snatching to corruption, lahat 'yan **krimen**. Huwag tularan, bes.
usage_notes: A serious term for an illegal act.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagnanakaw ay isang malubhang **krimen**.","translation":"Theft is a serious **crime**."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan ng mga pulis na lutasin ang **krimen** na naganap.","translation":"The police are trying to solve the **crime** that occurred."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang instrumentong medikal na ginagamit ng mga doktor at nars upang pakinggan ang mga panloob na tunog ng katawan, tulad ng tibok ng puso at paghinga.
original_explanation: That cold, metallic thing your doctor hangs around their neck and presses against your chest, making you take a deep breath ('Hinga, malalim...'). It's the official accessory for anyone playing a doctor in a school play and the primary tool for listening to your heart—both literally and, if the doctor is cute, figuratively.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ng doktor ang kanyang **estetoskopyo** upang pakinggan ang tibok ng puso ng pasyente.","translation":"The doctor used his **stethoscope** to listen to the patient's heartbeat."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangunahing kumpanya at plataporma ng e-commerce sa Timog-silangang Asya, kung saan maaaring bumili at magbenta ng iba't ibang produkto online.
original_explanation: The orange-themed online shopping app that's your best friend on payday and your worst enemy for your savings account. It's the place you go to buy everything from a new phone to cat food at 2 AM. It's a source of joy (parcel's arriving!), anxiety (where's my parcel?), and the occasional "budol" (see: lazada budol). "Check out ko na 'to sa Lazada."
usage_notes: A household name in the Philippines, often used interchangeably with "online shopping".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tingnan mo muna sa **Lazada** kung may sale bago ka bumili sa mall.","translation":"Check on **Lazada** first if there's a sale before you buy at the mall."},{"sentence":"Araw-araw may dumarating na delivery mula sa **Lazada** sa bahay namin.","translation":"Every day a delivery from **Lazada** arrives at our house."}]

translation: to be able to join; to be able to participate
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng pagkakataong maging bahagi ng isang grupo, gawain, o kaganapan.
original_explanation: FOMO is real, and the goal is always to makasali. 'Yung may usapang gala ang barkada at nag-aabang ka ng "Sama ka?" para makasali ka. Or 'yung may contest sa office at gusto mong makasali para sa premyo. It's the ability or opportunity to be included, to be part of the in-crowd or an event.
usage_notes: "Maka-" emphasizes the opportunity or ability to join. It is often used when there are requirements or limitations to joining.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **makasali** ako sa dance troupe ng paaralan sa susunod na taon.","translation":"I hope I can **join** the school's dance troupe next year."},{"sentence":"Huli na akong dumating kaya hindi na ako **nakasali** sa palaro.","translation":"I arrived late so I wasn't **able to participate** in the games anymore."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbibigay ng suporta o asistensya sa isang tao o gawain sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: The future tense of being a hero (or just a decent human being). It's what you say when you see your friend struggling with their bags, their love life, or their thesis. "**Tutulong** ako." It's the verbal equivalent of a helping hand, a promise of bayanihan, even if it's just helping someone move a couch.
usage_notes: This is the actor-focus, future tense form of the verb 'tulong' (to help).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **tutulong** sa paglilinis ng bahay?","translation":"Who **will help** clean the house?"},{"sentence":"**Tutulong** ako sa paghahanda ng pagkain para sa mga bisita.","translation":"I **will help** prepare the food for the guests."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pang-abay na tumutukoy sa kasunod na panahon, kaganapan, o pagkakasunod-sunod ng mga pangyayari.
etymology: From `pag-` (prefix) + `tapos` (end, finish). Often used as a shortened form of `pagkatapos`.
original_explanation: This is the official word for 'after party' or 'after shift' or 'after this meeting that could have been an email.' It's the gateway to freedom. When your boss says 'Okay, pagtapos nito, lunch na,' you feel a level of hope you haven't felt all morning. It's the word that signals the start of your real life after your responsibilities.
usage_notes: Commonly used with 'ng' or 'na' (`pagkatapos ng...`, `pagkatapos na...`) to mean 'after...'. When used alone, it can mean 'afterwards'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pagtapos** ng trabaho, dumaan ako sa palengke.","translation":"**After** work, I passed by the market."},{"sentence":"Manonood kami ng sine **pagtapos** kumain.","translation":"We will watch a movie **after** eating."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang litratong kinunan nang hindi alam o hindi naghahanda ang paksa, na nagreresulta sa isang natural at hindi-pormal na imahe.
original_explanation: The 'official' term for a picture you take of your friend when they're not looking, usually when they're eating, sleeping, or making a weird face. The goal is to capture them 'au naturel', but it's often used to gather future blackmail material. On Instagram, it's the 'I wasn't posing, I swear' pose.
usage_notes: This English phrase is used directly in Tagalog and Taglish conversations. The direct translation 'ninakaw na kuha' is rarely used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng **stolen shot** mo habang tumatawa!","translation":"Your **candid photo** while laughing is beautiful!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang proyekto o gawain kung saan dalawa o higit pang tao o grupo ay nagtutulungan upang makamit ang isang partikular na layunin.
original_explanation: Short for collaboration. The lifeblood of YouTubers, TikTokers, and artists. 'Pag nakita mo 'yung paborito mong vlogger kasama ang isa pang sikat na vlogger, sure na may collab 'yan. Pwede ring gamitin sa office: 'Let's do a collab on this report.'
usage_notes: Ginagamit bilang pangngalan (a collab) at pandiwa (to collab/mag-collab).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **collab** sina Moira at Ben&Ben sa bagong kanta.","translation":"Moira and Ben&Ben have a **collab** on a new song."},{"sentence":"Gusto kong mag-**collab** sa'yo para sa isang TikTok video.","translation":"I want to **collab** with you for a TikTok video."}]

translation: to humble oneself; to act lowly
meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang pagpapakita ng kababaang-loob o pag-aalis ng sariling karangalan, kadalasan sa sukdulang paraan.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `mag-` (gumanap ng kilos), `paka-` (pagsisikap o pagpapanggap), at salitang-ugat na `aba` (lowly, humble).
original_explanation: This is the opposite of 'flex culture.' It's when you deliberately act humble, sometimes to an extreme degree. It's the 'sino ba naman ako' attitude. While humility is a virtue, `magpakaaba` can sometimes feel like you're putting yourself down too much, like a martyr in a teleserye. It’s about choosing the low road, not in a bad way, but in a self-effacing one.
usage_notes: Madalas na may bahagyang negatibo o malungkot na konotasyon, na nagpapahiwatig ng labis o hindi kinakailangang pagpapakababa sa sarili.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit mayaman na siya, marunong pa rin siyang **magpakaaba** at makisama sa mahihirap.","translation":"Even though he's rich, he still knows how to **humble himself** and associate with the poor."},{"sentence":"Hindi mo kailangang **magpakaaba** para lang matanggap ka nila.","translation":"You don't need to **act lowly** just for them to accept you."}]

meaning_filipino: May takip sa mga mata, kadalasan ay isang piraso ng tela, upang hindi makakita.
original_explanation: 'Yung state mo 'pag pinapalaro ka ng "Pin the Tail on the Donkey" sa birthday party. Or 'yung feeling mo sa love life mo, parang wala kang makita sa hinaharap pero sige ka pa rin. Justice is often depicted as nakapiring to symbolize impartiality.
usage_notes: Describes a state of being blindfolded.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakapiring** ang mga bihag habang dinadala sa hindi malamang lugar.","translation":"The captives were **blindfolded** while being taken to an unknown place."},{"sentence":"Naglalaro ang mga bata ng pabitin habang **nakapiring**.","translation":"The children are playing the pabitin game while **blindfolded**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paglalarawan na nagsasaad na ang isang bagay ay medyo malapit na, ngunit hindi pa eksakto sa destinasyon.
original_explanation: This is the official Filipino term for 'mga five minutes pa' when you're on your way but you're actually still 15 minutes away. It's close-ish. It gives a sense of progress without the commitment of being 'malapit na'. 'Nasaan ka na?' 'Eto, malapit-lapit na sa kanto!'
usage_notes: The reduplication of 'lapit' softens the meaning to 'somewhat' or 'getting' close.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Malapit-lapit** na ang Pasko kaya marami nang pailaw sa mga daan.","translation":"Christmas is **quite near**, so there are many lights on the roads already."},{"sentence":"Teka lang, **malapit-lapit** na akong matapos sa ginagawa ko.","translation":"Just a moment, I'm **somewhat close** to finishing what I'm doing."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang sistema ng edukasyon kung saan ang mga lalaki at babae ay magkasamang tinuturuan sa iisang institusyon o paaralan.
original_explanation: When boys and girls are in the same school. Hindi all-boys, hindi all-girls. This is the setup for most universities, and where many high school "crushes" and "first loves" begin. It’s the opposite of exclusive schools where you only see the opposite sex during mixers or school fairs.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa konteksto ng edukasyon at mga paaralan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming magulang ang mas gustong ipasok ang kanilang mga anak sa mga **koedukasyonal** na paaralan.","translation":"Many parents prefer to enroll their children in **co-educational** schools."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng nagtitinda o nagbebenta ng mga kalakal.
original_explanation: She's the queen of the `tindahan`, the maestra of the `palengke`. She knows the price of everything, can give you a "suki" discount, and probably knows more about your family than your own Tita. From the sari-sari store owner to the department store saleslady, she is the **tindera**.
usage_notes: The female form for a vendor or seller.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"\"Magkano po ito, ate?\" tanong ko sa **tindera**.","translation":"\"How much is this, miss?\" I asked the **saleswoman**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gusali o bahagi ng isang gusali na ginagamit na paradahan at sisilungan ng mga sasakyan.
original_explanation: The official bedroom of your family car. Also the unofficial 'bodega' for things you swear you'll use again but never do. In many Pinoy homes, it's also the default 'tambayan' and inuman spot.
usage_notes: A direct loanword from Spanish, commonly used in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakipasok mo na ang kotse sa **garahe** dahil mukhang uulan.","translation":"Please put the car in the **garage** because it looks like it will rain."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging mahigpit, marahas, o hindi maluwag; maaari ring tumukoy sa kalagayan ng kakulangan o pagiging limitado.
etymology: From `ka-`...`-an` (denoting quality or state) around `higpit` (tightness, strictness).
original_explanation: This is your parents' 10 PM curfew. It's your terror prof's 'no extension' policy. It's when the budget is so tight you can only afford instant noodles until the next payday ('gipit' is a cousin). **Kahigpitan** is that feeling of being squeezed, whether by rules or by finances.
usage_notes: Can refer to the strictness of rules, the tightness of a space or object, or financial difficulty (kagipitan).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa **kahigpitan** ng kanilang mga magulang, bihirang makalabas ang magkapatid.","translation":"Because of their parents' **strictness**, the siblings rarely get to go out."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang **kahigpitan** ng yakap ng kanyang ina.","translation":"She felt the **tightness** of her mother's hug."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang matuklasan, matagpuan, o malaman ang isang bagay na dati ay lihim, hindi alam, o nakatago.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling mo kapag may nakita kang bagong kainan na super sarap at mura pa, tapos ikaw ang unang nag-post sa social media. You want it to be madeskubre by others. Also, 'yung takot mo na madeskubre ng nanay mo 'yung mga tinago mong resibo ng online shopping.
usage_notes: More common is 'matuklasan' or 'malaman'. 'Madeskubre' carries a slightly more dramatic or significant connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming bagong talento ang maaaring **madeskubre** sa mga probinsya.","translation":"Many new talents can **be discovered** in the provinces."},{"sentence":"Inaasahan ng mga siyentista na may **madeskubre** silang gamot para sa sakit.","translation":"Scientists hope they can **discover** a cure for the disease."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi nagkukunwari; tapat at totoo sa sarili at sa iba.
original_explanation: That one friend who will tell you straight up if your outfit looks bad or if you have something between your teeth. They are di-mapagpanggap. They're the real ones, no filters, no BS. What you see is what you get. The opposite of a "plastikan" queen.
usage_notes: Isang positibong katangian na naglalarawan sa isang taong totoo at prangka.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko siyang kaibigan dahil siya ay **di-mapagpanggap** na tao.","translation":"I like him as a friend because he is a **genuine** person."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang ngiti ay **di-mapagpanggap**; ramdam mo ang kanyang tunay na saya.","translation":"Her smile is **sincere**; you can feel her genuine happiness."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkawala ng pagmamahal, paghanga, o pagkasabik sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: This is that "Sunday night feeling" but for a person or a hobby. Remember when you were super into that K-drama, tapos biglang na-realize mo na pare-pareho lang ang plot? 'Yun na 'yun. The magic is gone. The kilig has left the building. You're not mad, you're just... over it. It's the emotional equivalent of a flat soft drink.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of romantic relationships or fading passions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkawalang-giliw** niya sa kanyang trabaho ay halata sa kanyang mga kilos.","translation":"His **disenchantment** with his job was obvious in his actions."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang unti-unting **pagkawalang-giliw** ng kanyang kasintahan.","translation":"She felt the gradual **loss of affection** from her partner."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na pagbati na ginagamit sa umaga.
original_explanation: The OG Filipino greeting. The first thing you hear from the security guard, your BPO team lead, and the TV news anchor. It's the Pinoy version of coffee—you can't start your day without it. Replying with "umaga lang, walang maganda" is the official hugot response for people who haven't had their coffee yet.
usage_notes: Standard greeting from sunrise until noon. Often followed by "po" or "ho" for respect.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magandang umaga** po,\" bati ng estudyante sa kanyang guro.","translation":"**Good morning**,\" the student greeted his teacher."},{"sentence":"Isang masiglang \"**Magandang umaga**!\" ang salubong niya sa amin.","translation":"A cheerful \"**Good morning**!\" was her greeting to us."}]

translation: a specific sweet and savory stew
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng putahe, karaniwan ay baboy o manok, na niluto sa matamis at maalat na sarsa na may sangkap tulad ng toyo, asukal, at mga pampalasa.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na "asado" (roasted), bagaman ang putaheng Pilipino ay mas malapit sa pag-i-stew o pag-braise.
original_explanation: That reddish, sweet pork dish you often see in siopao fillings or as a standalone ulam. It's the sweeter, less fatty cousin of humba. It’s that familiar, comforting flavor that tastes like a fiesta or a handaan. Not to be confused with 'asada' the cooking method, asado is the name of the actual delicious dish.
usage_notes: Ang pork asado at chicken asado ay dalawang magkaibang putahe sa Pilipinas. Ang isa ay matamis na stew, at ang isa ay inihaw na may palaman (chicken asado).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong palaman sa siopao ang **asado**.","translation":"My favorite siopao filling is **asado**."},{"sentence":"Nag-order kami ng kanin at pork **asado** para sa tanghalian.","translation":"We ordered rice and pork **asado** for lunch."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng pahintulot sa isang tao na pumasok o manatili sa isang lugar, tulad ng bahay o gusali.
etymology: Nagmula sa salitang-ugat na "tuloy" (to enter, to proceed). Ang unlaping "pa-" at hulaping "-in" ay lumilikha ng isang pandiwang nagiging sanhi ng pagkilos (causative verb).
original_explanation: This is what you do when your friend shows up at your door at 2 AM after a breakup. Or when you tell the guard, "Manong, **patuluyin** niyo po, bisita ko 'yan." Figuratively, "Sige na, **patuluyin** mo na ako sa buhay mo," ang hugot line kapag gusto mong maging parte ng buhay niya.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang pandiwang nakapokus sa layon (object-focused). Ang layon ay ang taong pinapapasok o pinapatira.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Patuluyin** mo ang mga bisita sa sala.","translation":"**Let the visitors in** to the living room."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko siya maaaring **patuluyin** sa aking bahay nang walang pahintulot.","translation":"I cannot **let him stay** in my house without permission."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbuo ng isang hula, teorya, o opinyon na batay sa hindi kumpletong impormasyon o ebidensya.
original_explanation: This is the official term for being a 'Marites' (gossiper). When you see your ex with someone new and you start creating a whole backstory in your head, you're starting to **magsapantaha**. It's making assumptions or educated guesses, whether for a science project or for the latest chismis.
usage_notes: Has a more formal or intellectual tone than 'hulaan' (to guess).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **magsapantaha** tungkol sa tunay na motibo niya nang hindi siya kinakausap.","translation":"It's difficult to **speculate** about his true motives without talking to him."},{"sentence":"Ang mga siyentipiko ay nagsimulang **magsapantaha** na may buhay sa ibang planeta.","translation":"The scientists began to **hypothesize** that there is life on other planets."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging hindi matatag, hindi pantay, o umuuga-uga, tulad ng isang mesa o silya na may magkaibang haba ng paa.
original_explanation: You know that super annoying feeling when you're at a karinderya and the table keeps shaking every time you try to cut your food? That's 'kibang'. It's that wobbly, unstable state of a chair that feels like it's about to give up on life, or a tooth that's loose. The solution is usually a folded piece of paper or a tsinelas wedge.
usage_notes: Can refer to furniture, structures, or even loose teeth.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayusin mo 'yang mesa, **kibang** na naman.","translation":"Fix that table, it's **wobbly** again."},{"sentence":"Delikadong umupo sa silyang **kibang**.","translation":"It's dangerous to sit on a **wobbly** chair."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga biyak o siwang sa lupa na sanhi ng matinding pagkatuyo o init.
original_explanation: Picture a rice field during El Niño, or the skin on your heels after walking barefoot all summer. That's 'litak'. It's the earth so thirsty it literally cracks open. Also a good metaphor for your heart after seeing your crush with someone else. "Puso kong may litak." Hugot!
usage_notes: Primarily refers to cracks in the ground, but can be used metaphorically for skin or other surfaces.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **litak** ang bukirin dahil sa mahabang tagtuyot.","translation":"The field was full of **cracks** due to the long drought."},{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng mga **litak** ang kanyang sakong sa sobrang paglalakad.","translation":"His heels developed **cracks** from too much walking."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang de-kuryente na ginagamit sa awtomatikong paglalaba ng mga damit.
original_explanation: The savior of every Filipino household that's tired of 'kusot-kusot' and 'piga-piga'. We just say 'washing machine' as is, sometimes as one word. The alternative, 'makinang panlaba', sounds like something from a science textbook that no one actually says.
usage_notes: The English term is used almost exclusively. Often spelled as two words ("washing machine"), but the one-word form is also seen. The formal Filipino translation "makinang panlaba" is very rarely used in conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sira ang aming **washingmachine** kaya nagpa-laundry ako.","translation":"Our **washing machine** is broken so I went to a laundromat."},{"sentence":"Ilagay mo na ang mga puti sa **washingmachine**.","translation":"Put the whites in the **washing machine** now."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matalas na talim na gawa sa metal na ikinakabit sa paa ng manok na panabong.
original_explanation: This is the business end of a fighting cock. It's the deadly weapon that turns a 'sabong' from a simple chicken fight into a high-stakes, life-or-death duel. The 'tari' is meticulously sharpened and fitted by a 'mananari'. It's a symbol of both the sport's danger and the deep-rooted culture surrounding cockfighting in the Philippines. Not to be confused with a knife, this is specifically for the roosters.
usage_notes: Exclusively used in the context of cockfighting (sabong).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maingat na ikinabit ng mananari ang **tari** sa paa ng manok.","translation":"The gaff-fitter carefully attached the **gaff** to the rooster's leg."},{"sentence":"Namatay ang kalabang manok dahil sa tama ng **tari**.","translation":"The opposing rooster died from a strike by the **cockspur**."}]

meaning_filipino: Inilalarawan ang isang bagay na nasira o naitim dahil sa sobrang pagkakalantad sa apoy o matinding init.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your toast when you get distracted by a meme. Or your skin after a day trip to the beach without sunblock. "Ay, **sunog** na yung sinaing!" is a phrase that has caused panic in many Filipino households.
usage_notes: The pronunciation stress shifts to the last syllable (su-NOG) when used as an adjective, compared to the noun (SU-nog).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi na makakain ang kanin dahil **sunog** na ang ilalim.","translation":"The rice is no longer edible because the bottom is **burnt**."},{"sentence":"**Sunog** ang balat niya pagkatapos magbabad sa araw sa Boracay.","translation":"Her skin was **sunburnt** after soaking up the sun in Boracay."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gagawing paggalaw sa isang bagay palapit sa sarili sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng lakas.
original_explanation: This is the future tense of 'to pull.' It can be literal, like 'sino ang hihila ng pisi sa pabitin?' (who will pull the string for the pabitin game?). Or it can be figurative, like 'hihila ka pababa' (will pull you down), the favorite line of toxic friends and crab mentality champions.
usage_notes: This is the actor-focus future tense of 'hila'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **hihila** sa kariton bukas.","translation":"He **will pull** the cart tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Sana walang **hihila** sa paa ko habang natutulog ako.","translation":"I hope nothing **will pull** my foot while I'm sleeping."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdaan o paggalaw ng isang bagay, tulad ng kard o daliri, sa ibabaw ng isa pang bagay, karaniwan para sa pagbabayad o paggamit ng teknolohiya.
original_explanation: The official verb of modern dating (Tinder) and modern debt (credit card). You either magswipe right for a potential jowa or magswipe your credit card for that 12-months-to-pay gadget. Both can lead to either joy or immense regret.
usage_notes: A recently assimilated loanword that has been fully conjugated into the Tagalog verb system.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sige, **magswipe** ka na lang muna, wala akong cash.","translation":"Go ahead, just **swipe** (the card) for now, I don't have cash."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magswipe** nang **magswipe** sa Tinder kung hindi ka naman seryoso.","translation":"Don't keep **swiping** on Tinder if you're not serious."}]

translation: will be broken, will be destroyed
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay o sitwasyon na malapit nang masira, mawalan ng halaga, o hindi na gumana sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na kaka-charge mo lang ng phone tapos nahulog, at alam mong pag pulot mo, masisira ang araw mo. Or 'yung tiwala mo sa kanya, once broken, considered sold. Future tense ng pagka-wasak.
usage_notes: Ito ay nasa anyong panghinaharap o future tense ng pandiwang 'masira'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingatan mo 'yan, **masisira** kapag nabagsak.","translation":"Be careful with that, it **will break** if it falls."},{"sentence":"**Masisira** ang plano kung hindi tayo magtutulungan.","translation":"The plan **will be ruined** if we don't help each other."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay ng kandado sa isang bagay upang ito ay maisara nang ligtas at hindi mabuksan ng sinuman na walang pahintulot o susi.
original_explanation: It's what you frantically do when you hear a noise outside at 3 AM. It's also what your parents do to the snack cabinet when you're on a diet. "Hoy, sino'ng nag-utos sa'yo na kandaduhan ang ref?!"
usage_notes: The verb form. The object being locked is the focus.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **kandaduhan** ang gate pagkagabi.","translation":"Don't forget **to lock** the gate at night."},{"sentence":"Kinandaduhan niya ang kanyang diary para walang makabasa.","translation":"She locked her diary so no one could read it."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging sanhi ng pagbagal ng kilos, galaw, o proseso ng isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: This is the effect of that one person in your group project who doesn't do their part, forcing everyone else to slow down. Or the ancient office computer that takes 10 minutes to open a file. Anything that acts as a bottleneck or a drag is nagpapabagal. Even your "marupok" heart going back to your ex can magpabagal your moving-on process.
usage_notes: The subject of the verb is the one causing the slowness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang matinding trapik ay **nagpapabagal** sa biyahe ng lahat.","translation":"The heavy traffic **is slowing down** everyone's travel."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magpabagal** sa team, bilisan mo ang trabaho mo.","translation":"Don't **slow down** the team, speed up your work."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglilipat o pagpapahayag ng isang teksto o salita mula sa isang wika patungo sa iba. Sa agham, ito ay tumutukoy sa paggalaw ng isang bagay mula sa isang punto patungo sa iba nang walang pag-ikot.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "translación" at Ingles na "translation".
original_explanation: The formal, highfalutin' way of saying "pagsasalin" or "translation". You'd use this in a thesis about linguistics, not when asking your friend what "on fleek" means. It's the academic cousin of "Google Translate." It also has a meaning in physics and geometry, but let's be real, we're mostly using it for language.
usage_notes: Ang salitang "pagsasalin" ay mas karaniwan at malawakang ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na usapan para sa "translation". Ang "translasyon" ay mas madalas gamitin sa mga teknikal o akademikong konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **translasyon** ng mga akdang pampanitikan ay isang maselang gawain.","translation":"The **translation** of literary works is a delicate task."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan sa pisika ang paggalaw na may **translasyon**.","translation":"In physics, they study movement with **translation**."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing mas matibay, matatag, o permanente ang isang bagay, kasunduan, o relasyon.
original_explanation: This is what you do to a wobbly table by adding more nails. It's also what you do to a 'M.U.' (Mutual Understanding) by finally asking "What are we?". You're trying to **papagtibayin** the relationship. In a legal sense, it's what Congress does to a bill to make it a law. It's about making things official and solid.
usage_notes: Can be used for physical objects, relationships, laws, or beliefs. The simpler form 'pagtibayin' is more common in everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **papagtibayin** ang pundasyon ng bahay bago dumating ang bagyo.","translation":"We need **to strengthen** the house's foundation before the typhoon arrives."},{"sentence":"Ang mga pagsubok sa buhay ang siyang **nagpapatibay** sa aming pagsasama.","translation":"Life's challenges are what **strengthen** our relationship."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagpapahayag ng romantikong intensyon ng isang tao sa iba, na karaniwang kinapapalooban ng pagbibigay ng regalo, pagbisita, at pagpapakita ng pagmamahal at respeto.
etymology: From 'pan-' (prefix indicating action) + reduplication of the first syllable of 'ligaw' (to court).
original_explanation: The OG 'getting to know' stage, but with more effort. Before DMs, there was 'harana' (serenading). Before 'u up?' texts, there was fetching water ('pagsisibak ng kahoy'). It's the whole process of proving your worth to the person you like... and more importantly, to their parents. The ultimate 'Sana All' project.
usage_notes: A culturally significant term in the Philippines, representing a traditional and often formal period of courtship.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matagal din ang naging **panliligaw** ni Ben kay Ana bago siya sinagot.","translation":"Ben's **courtship** of Ana was quite long before she said yes."},{"sentence":"Bahagi ng tradisyonal na **panliligaw** ang paghingi ng pahintulot sa mga magulang.","translation":"Part of traditional **courtship** is asking for permission from the parents."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglilinis ng katawan sa pamamagitan ng pagpunas gamit ang basang tela o espongha, karaniwan ay ginagawa sa mga may sakit o hindi makapaligo.
etymology: From Spanish "baños" (baths), adapted to mean sponge bath.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'punas-punas lang' method. When you're sick with a fever and can't take a full shower, your mom will `magbanyos` you with a warm, wet towel. It's a hospital-approved way to stay fresh without getting out of bed. Think of it as a low-tech, manual shower for when you're not feeling 100%.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used for giving a sponge bath to a person, especially someone who is sick, elderly, or an infant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magbanyos** sa kapatid mong may lagnat para bumaba ang temperatura niya.","translation":"You need to **sponge-bathe** your sibling who has a fever to lower their temperature."},{"sentence":"Araw-araw siyang **nagbabanyos** sa kanyang lola na maysakit.","translation":"Every day, she **gives a sponge bath** to her sick grandmother."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng orasan na may mekanismo upang tumunog sa isang itinakdang oras, karaniwang ginagamit upang gumising sa umaga.
original_explanation: The original, non-digital enemy of every person who loves to sleep. Before your smartphone alarm, this was the loud, annoying thing on your bedside table that you either wanted to throw against the wall or frantically hit the snooze button on. Now, it's more of a vintage decor item.
usage_notes: Less common now due to smartphones, but still understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malakas ang tunog ng lumang **despertador** ni Lolo.","translation":"The sound of Grandpa's old **alarm clock** is loud."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na tumatagal o umiiral sa kabuuan ng buhay ng isang tao; walang hanggan sa konteksto ng buhay.
original_explanation: This is the "forever" in your "sana all" moments. It's for lifetime warranties, "best friends forever," and the kind of love you see in teleseryes. It’s also what a life sentence in prison is called (`panghabang-buhay na pagkabilanggo`), or that student loan you feel like you'll be paying off for the rest of your existence. The ultimate commitment level.
usage_notes: Often used to describe relationships, commitments, or sentences. Can also be a noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumpaan natin ang ating **panghabang-buhay** na pag-ibig.","translation":"Let's promise our **lifelong** love to each other."},{"sentence":"Ang produktong ito ay may **panghabang-buhay** na warranty.","translation":"This product has a **lifetime** warranty."}]

translation: to sell by retail; to sell in small quantities
meaning_filipino: Ipagbili nang paunti-unti o por piraso, hindi por dosena o bultuhan.
original_explanation: The "sachet economy" in verb form. This is the business model of every sari-sari store. Why buy a whole bottle of shampoo when you can buy one sachet? Why buy a whole pack of cigarettes when you can buy one stick? That's the magic of 'itingi'. Selling things piece by piece.
usage_notes: The opposite of 'bultuhan' (wholesale). It's a key concept in Philippine local commerce.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas malaki ang tubo kung **itingi** mo ang pagbenta ng bawang.","translation":"The profit is bigger if you **sell** the garlic **by retail**."},{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **itingi** ang isang sakong asukal sa kanyang tindahan.","translation":"She decided to **sell** the sack of sugar **in small quantities** at her store."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang pamamaraan, kilos, o katangian na tulad ng sa isang diktador; mapaniil, malupit, at may ganap na kapangyarihan.
original_explanation: When your team lead acts like they're the supreme ruler of the project and won't listen to anyone's input. "Bawal mag-leave? Ang diktatoryal naman ng boss mo!" It’s giving off major "my way or the highway" energy.
usage_notes: Used to describe a person, rule, or government that is oppressive and absolute.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinutulan ng mga mamamayan ang **diktatoryal** na pamumuno ng pangulo.","translation":"The citizens opposed the president's **dictatorial** leadership."},{"sentence":"May mga magulang na may **diktatoryal** na paraan ng pagpapalaki ng anak.","translation":"Some parents have a **dictatorial** way of raising children."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabalik o pagsasauli ng isang bagay na kinuha, ninakaw, o nawala sa tunay na may-ari; kabayaran para sa pinsala o pagkawala.
original_explanation: It's the legal and more 'sosyal' term for 'bayad-pinsala'. Imagine you accidentally break your friend's limited edition Funko Pop. 'Restitusyon' is you either buying them a new one (good luck!) or paying for its value. It's the court-ordered version of 'Sorry na, eto pambayad ko.'
usage_notes: Primarily used in legal, formal, or religious contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inatasan ng korte ang nasasakdal na magbigay ng **restitusyon** sa mga biktima.","translation":"The court ordered the accused to provide **restitution** to the victims."},{"sentence":"Ang **restitusyon** ay isang mahalagang bahagi ng paghingi ng kapatawaran.","translation":"**Restitution** is an important part of asking for forgiveness."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-uudyok o pagsulsul sa isang tao upang magalit o makipag-away.
original_explanation: What happens in a Filipino inuman session when someone says, "Ano, matapang ka?" It's the act of poking the bear, of starting drama for no reason. The verbal equivalent of "suntukan na lang, o!"
usage_notes: Specifically refers to provoking a conflict or fight, often in a boastful or challenging manner.
