usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na ang **paggiri** sa kanya bago pa magkasakitan kayo.","translation":"Stop your **provocation** of him before you two get hurt."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula ang gulo sa simpleng **paggiri** ng dalawang grupo.","translation":"The chaos started from a simple **instigation** between the two groups."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang beses lamang; minsan. Ito ay pinaikling anyo ng pariralang "isang beses".
original_explanation: The short, sweet, and slightly lazy way of saying "isang beses." It's what you tell your friend when they ask how many times you've rewatched that K-drama series, but you're lying. "Ah, **sambeses** ko pa lang napanood 'yan." (Spoiler: It was your fifth time).
usage_notes: Used to emphasize that an action occurred only a single time.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sambeses** lang sa isang taon kung umuwi siya mula sa abroad.","translation":"He only comes home from abroad **once** a year."}]

meaning_filipino: Mahirap nguyain, kagatin, o hiwain; matigas at makunat.
original_explanation: The ultimate disappointment at a fiesta or handaan. It's that piece of steak that feels like you're chewing on a leather shoe, or the 'liempo' that's more 'goma' (rubber) than pork. When you get a 'maganit' piece of meat, your jaw gets a full workout, and you start questioning the cook's life choices.
usage_notes: Primarily used to describe food, especially meat. It can also describe non-food items that are stiff or inflexible, like old leather.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Medyo **maganit** ang bistek na naluto ko.","translation":"The beef steak I cooked is a bit **tough**."},{"sentence":"Ayokong kumain diyan, laging **maganit** ang karne nila.","translation":"I don't want to eat there, their meat is always **tough to chew**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagdudulot ng pisikal na sugat o ng matinding sakit sa damdamin.
etymology: From `sugat` (wound). The affix `nakasu-` indicates the ability to cause the action of the root word.
original_explanation: Pwedeng literal, like a sharp object. Pero mas madalas, ito yung mga salitang binitawan ng ex mo na hanggang ngayon, ramdam mo pa rin. Yung "parang kapatid na lang kita" or "it's not you, it's me." Mga salitang mas matalas pa sa blade, **nakasusugat** ng puso't kaluluwa. Hugot level 99.
usage_notes: Can be used both literally for physical wounds and metaphorically for emotional pain.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa bubog, **nakasusugat** iyan.","translation":"Be careful with the broken glass, it is **wounding**."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang masasakit na salita ay tunay na **nakasusugat** ng damdamin.","translation":"Her harsh words are truly **hurtful** to one's feelings."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian o kalagayan ng pagiging madalang o bihirang mangyari o matagpuan.
original_explanation: This is the reason you get excited when your crush finally replies. It's the 'rarity' of a 5-minute commute on EDSA. It's the opposite of your daily dose of traffic and stress. It describes something that happens so infrequently, it's almost a special event. 'Minsan lang sa isang blue moon.'
usage_notes: 'Kadalangan' is the noun form, while 'madalang' (infrequent) is the more commonly used adjective.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa **kadalangan** ng ulan, natuyo ang mga pananim.","translation":"Due to the **infrequency** of rain, the crops dried up."},{"sentence":"Ang **kadalangan** ng kanyang pagdalaw ay nagpapahiwatig ng pagbabago sa aming pagkakaibigan.","translation":"The **rarity** of his visits hints at a change in our friendship."}]

meaning_filipino: Hiwalay sa pagkakakabit, pagkakabuhol, o pagkakabuo; bakbak, tanggal.
original_explanation: 'Yung state ng isang bagay na dapat buo pero nabakbak na. Parang 'yung upuan na binili mo online, isang upuan mo lang, **kalas** na agad ang paa. O 'yung tiwala mo sa kanya, dati buong-buo, ngayon **kalas-kalas** na.
usage_notes: Can be used for physical objects or abstract concepts like trust or unity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kalas** na ang isang paa ng mesa kaya kailangan nang kumpunihin.","translation":"One leg of the table is already **detached**, so it needs to be repaired."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng matinding away, tila **kalas** na ang kanilang pagkakaibigan.","translation":"After the intense fight, their friendship seemed to be **falling apart**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na kalat na kalat, umiiral sa maraming lugar, o karaniwan sa isang partikular na panahon o pangkat.
original_explanation: It’s that chismis that has reached every department in the office. It's the K-drama fever that has infected everyone you know. It's a trend, a disease, or a piece of news that has gone viral and is everywhere.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Laganap** ang paggamit ng social media sa mga kabataan ngayon.","translation":"The use of social media is **widespread** among the youth today."},{"sentence":"Naging **laganap** ang sakit na dengue noong tag-ulan.","translation":"Dengue became **rampant** during the rainy season."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagdudulot ng pinsala, pagkasira, o pagkawala ng integridad o kaayusan ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: When your little pamangkin gets ahold of your phone. When you spill coffee on your laptop. When a chismis ruins someone's reputation. It's anything that breaks, ruins, or corrupts something. Pwedeng bagay, pwedeng relasyon, pwedeng pangalan. **Nakasisira** 'yan, besh. Handle with care!
usage_notes: The 'nakasisi-' prefix indicates the ability or tendency to cause damage. Can be used for physical objects, relationships, or abstract concepts like reputation or trust.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang baha ay **nakasisira** ng mga pananim at kabahayan.","translation":"The flood is **damaging** to crops and houses."},{"sentence":"**Nakasisira** ng tiwala ang paulit-ulit na pagsisinungaling.","translation":"Constant lying is **destructive** to trust."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang matuklasan o mahanap ang isang bagay na hindi pa alam o nakikita noon.
original_explanation: That "Aha!" moment. It's when you find a new hole-in-the-wall resto with amazing sisig, a new series to binge-watch, or when you finally figure out who's been stealing your food from the office fridge. "Sana makadiskubre ako ng bagong coffee shop na hindi pa sikat."
usage_notes: The root `diskubre` is from Spanish. The native Tagalog equivalent is `tuklas`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino kaya ang susunod na **makadiskubre** ng gamot para sa malubhang sakit?","translation":"Who will be the next to **discover** a cure for the serious illness?"},{"sentence":"Habang naglilinis ng bodega, **nakadiskubre** siya ng mga lumang litrato.","translation":"While cleaning the storage room, she **discovered** old photographs."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang legal o panlipunang proseso ng pagtanggap at pag-aalaga sa isang bata na hindi tunay na anak, o sa isang hayop na walang nag-aalaga.
original_explanation: This is the "Adopt, Don't Shop" mantra in one word. It's the act of giving a forever home, whether to a child from an orphanage or a stray 'aspin' (Asong Pinoy) from the street. It's a formal process, but also a huge act of love.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming bata sa ampunan ang naghihintay ng **pag-ampon** mula sa isang mapagmahal na pamilya.","translation":"Many children in the orphanage are waiting for **adoption** by a loving family."},{"sentence":"Ang **pag-ampon** sa isang alagang hayop ay isang malaking responsibilidad.","translation":"The **adoption** of a pet is a big responsibility."}]

translation: to gut, to eviscerate, to empty the contents
meaning_filipino: Tanggalin ang mga laman-loob o ang nilalaman ng isang bagay, tulad ng isda, hayop, prutas, o sisidlan.
original_explanation: What you do to a fish before cooking it. Also what your wallet experiences during a 12.12 sale. Biglang **alisan ng laman** ang bank account mo.
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang parirala sa pagluluto at pagkatay. Maaari ring gamitin sa makabagong paraan para sa pag-ubos ng pera sa pitaka o bank account.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinuruan siya ng kanyang lola kung paano **alisan ng laman** ang isda nang mabilis.","translation":"His grandmother taught him how to **gut** a fish quickly."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **alisan ng laman** ang niyog para makuha ang gata.","translation":"You need to **empty the contents** of the coconut to get the milk."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang pangunahing hanapbuhay ay ang pagtatanim, pag-aalaga ng mga pananim, at pag-aani sa bukid.
original_explanation: The OG food source. A farmer. They are the reason you have rice on your plate and sinigang in your bowl. While city folks are busy with deadlines, magbubukid are busy with seasons and harvests. They're the backbone of the country, working under the hot sun. So next time you complain about the price of sibuyas, remember the magbubukid who grew it.
usage_notes: The noun is formed from the root "bukid" (field/farm) with the prefix "mag-". It literally means "one who farms".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ama niya ay isang masipag na **magbubukid** sa kanilang probinsya.","translation":"His father is a hardworking **farmer** in their province."},{"sentence":"Dapat nating suportahan ang mga lokal na **magbubukid**.","translation":"We should support our local **farmers**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng tela, katad, o ibang materyal na itinatapal sa butas ng damit o anumang bagay. Maaari ring tumukoy sa medikal na tapal para sa sugat.
original_explanation: Think of it as the OG 'Band-Aid' or the thing your lola sews onto your favorite butas na pantalon. It's a patch. From the Spanish word 'parche'. Nowadays you'd probably just say 'patch' or 'tapal', but 'patse' has that old-school, vintage vibe.
usage_notes: Hindi na gaanong karaniwan sa pang-araw-araw na usapan; mas madalas gamitin ang "tapal" o ang hiram na salitang "patch".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nilagyan ng sastre ng **patse** ang punit sa siko ng aking dyaket.","translation":"The tailor put a **patch** on the tear at the elbow of my jacket."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang medikal na proseso ng pagsisiyasat sa isang bangkay upang matukoy ang sanhi, paraan, at oras ng pagkamatay.
etymology: A compound phrase from 'pagsusuri' (examination) and 'pagkamatay' (after death).
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'pagsusuri'. It's what happens in every episode of a crime procedural when the medical examiner tries to find out 'whodunnit' or 'whatdunnit.' It's a post-mortem deep-dive, literally. The English word 'autopsy' is more common in everyday talk, though.
usage_notes: This is a specific medical and legal term. The English loanword 'awtopsiya' is more commonly used in casual conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinihiling ng pamilya na magkaroon ng **pagsusuri pagkamatay** upang malaman ang tunay na dahilan ng kanyang pagpanaw.","translation":"The family is requesting a **post-mortem examination** to determine the real cause of his passing."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaikling tawag para sa "call boy," na tumutukoy sa isang lalaking nag-aalok ng sekswal na serbisyo kapalit ng bayad.
etymology: Mula sa acronym ng Ingles na "call boy".
original_explanation: Acronym for 'call boy.' Medyo old-school na term, parang galing sa mga '90s B-movies starring a 'ST' (Sex Trip) queen. Nowadays, may mga bago nang terms, pero kung maririnig mo 'to, alam na this.
usage_notes: Isang slang na termino na may negatibong konotasyon. Itinuturing na bulgar at hindi ginagamit sa pormal na pag-uusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May mga pelikula noon na ang tema ay tungkol sa buhay ng mga **cb**.","translation":"There were movies before whose themes were about the lives of **call boys**."},{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang terminong '**cb**' sa isang lumang pelikula.","translation":"I heard the term '**cb**' in an old movie."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa ng mga kinakailangang hakbang o pag-aayos bilang paghahanda para sa isang paparating na kaganapan, gawain, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: What your family does for three days straight before Noche Buena, turning the kitchen into a war zone. Also, what you tell yourself you'll do before an exam ("maghahanda ako nang maaga") but end up cramming anyway. It's getting everything in order, from food for a fiesta to your "baon" for work.
usage_notes: Very common verb. "Handa ka na ba?" (Are you ready?) is a frequently asked question.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **maghanda** para sa darating na bagyo.","translation":"We need to **prepare** for the coming typhoon."},{"sentence":"Siya ang laging taya sa **maghanda** ng pagkain para sa aming barkada.","translation":"He's always in charge of **preparing** the food for our group of friends."}]

translation: to divide; to cut into parts
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabahagi o pagputol ng isang buo sa dalawa o higit pang parte.
original_explanation: This is what you do with the last piece of pizza when you're with your best friend. Or what you wish you could do with your sweldo to make it last 'til the next payday. Hatiin mo sa bills, sa luho, sa ipon... ay, kulang pa. It's the art of splitting things, whether it's food, money, or the bill on a group date.
usage_notes: This is an object-focused verb. The actor-focused form is `maghati`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **hatiin** ang kita sa tatlong magkakapatid.","translation":"The income needs to be **divided** among the three siblings."},{"sentence":"**Hatiin** mo sa gitna ang mansanas.","translation":"**Cut** the apple in the middle."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang babae na may masamang hangarin, layuning makasakit, o magdulot ng pinsala sa kapwa sa pamamagitan ng paninira o mapanirang-puri na mga salita o gawa.
original_explanation: Eto yung ahas sa office, yung kapitbahay na laging may "breaking news" tungkol sa'yo, or yung "frenemy" mo na nag-cocomment ng "Congrats! Naka-jackpot ka ah!" sa picture niyo ng jowa mong di kagwapuhan. She's the queen of side-eyes and backhanded compliments. The female equivalent of a troll, but IRL.
usage_notes: Specifically used for females. The male counterpart is 'malisyoso'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala sa kanya, **malisyosa** talaga ang mga sinasabi niya tungkol sa'yo.","translation":"Don't believe her, what she's saying about you is truly **malicious**."},{"sentence":"May **malisyosa** siyang ngiti nang makita niyang nag-aaway ang magkapatid.","translation":"She had a **malicious** smile when she saw the siblings fighting."}]

translation: to use as a basis; to rely on
meaning_filipino: Gamitin bilang batayan, pundasyon, o basehan para sa isang paniniwala, desisyon, o aksyon.
original_explanation: This is when you use your friend's 'pasalubong' promise as the main reason you're excited for them to come home. You are relying on that box of goodies. In arguments, this is your 'source?' moment. You're asking 'What are you basing this on?' or you're declaring what you're using as your foundation. 'Eto ang pinagsasaligan ko ng aking hugot.'
usage_notes: A locative verb. The object is what is being used as the basis. It is often used in the form 'pagbatayan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pagsaligan** ang mga sabi-sabi lamang.","translation":"Do not **rely on** mere hearsay."},{"sentence":"Ang Saligang Batas ang dapat nating **pagsaligan** sa pagpapatupad ng ating mga karapatan.","translation":"The Constitution is what we should **use as a basis** for implementing our rights."}]

translation: anointing of the sick; last rites
meaning_filipino: Isang sakramento ng Simbahang Katoliko kung saan binibigyan ng isang pari ng basbas ang isang taong may malubhang karamdaman o nasa bingit ng kamatayan sa pamamagitan ng pagpapahid ng banal na langis.
etymology: From pagpapahid (act of wiping/anointing) + ng (of) + Santo Oleo (Spanish for Holy Oil).
original_explanation: In Filipino culture, this is the ultimate 'call a priest' moment. When lola is very sick, someone will inevitably whisper, 'Tawagin na ang pari para sa pagpapahid ng Santo Oleo.' It's the Catholic sacrament for the sick, meant to give spiritual strength and healing. It's a very serious, solemn event, often mistakenly called just 'last rites,' but it's really about healing and peace for the person, not just for the dying.
usage_notes: A specific Catholic sacrament, also known as Anointing of the Sick. 'Santo Oleo' is sometimes spelled 'Santo Olyo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hiniling ng pamilya ang **pagpapahid ng Santo Oleo** para sa kanilang lolo na nasa ospital.","translation":"The family requested the **anointing of the sick** for their grandfather who is in the hospital."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapahid ng Santo Oleo** ay nagbibigay ng kapanatagan sa mga maysakit.","translation":"The **anointing of the sick** gives peace to the ill."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng hirap sa pagtulog o kawalan ng sapat na tulog, lalo na sa gabi.
original_explanation: Best friend ng mga BPO agent, estudyanteng nag-the-thesis, at ng mga taong nag-o-overthink sa gabi. Ito 'yung 3 AM na pero gising na gising ka pa rin kasi iniisip mo 'yung maling sinabi mo noong 2012. Ang official state of being ng mga mahilig sa kape at chismis.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa isang gabi ng hindi pagkatulog o sa malalang kondisyon ng insomnia.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inirereklamo niya ang madalas na **di-pagkakatulog** dahil sa stress sa trabaho.","translation":"She complains about frequent **sleeplessness** due to stress at work."},{"sentence":"Ang sobrang pag-inom ng kape ay maaaring magdulot ng **di-pagkakatulog**.","translation":"Drinking too much coffee can cause **insomnia**."}]

translation: a threat; an act of threatening
meaning_filipino: Isang salita, kilos, o pahayag na naglalayong magbigay ng babala, manakot, o magbanta.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "pan-" at salitang ugat na "bala" (threat). Tumutukoy sa akto ng pagbabanta.
original_explanation: That look your mom gives you when you're about to do something stupid in public. It's a non-verbal 'pambabala'. It’s the 'last warning' text from your jowa, or the 'HR would like to see you' email from your boss. It's the prelude to drama.
usage_notes: Madalas na mas matindi o direkta ang implikasyon nito kaysa sa 'babala' (warning).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatanggap siya ng liham na may lamang **pambabala** sa kanyang buhay.","translation":"He received a letter containing a **threat** on his life."},{"sentence":"Itigil mo na ang iyong **pambabala** dahil hindi ako natatakot sa iyo.","translation":"Stop your **threatening** because I am not afraid of you."}]

translation: to push someone towards another; to palm someone/something off on another
meaning_filipino: Ang sapilitang paglapit, pag-ugnay, o pagpasa ng responsibilidad ng isang tao o bagay sa iba, kadalasan laban sa kanilang kalooban.
original_explanation: When your friends try to set you up with their other single friend and literally push you towards them at a party. 'Huy, 'wag n'yo nga akong **ipagtulakan** diyan kay Mark, awkward kaya!' It's the physical or metaphorical act of being pushed onto someone or being made responsible for someone you didn't ask for.
usage_notes: This complex verb form combines 'ipag-' and '-an', indicating the action of pushing something/someone (the object) towards a recipient/direction (the locative part).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan nilang **ipagtulakan** sa akin ang lahat ng gawain.","translation":"They tried to **palm off** all the work **on me**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **ipagtulakan** sa taong hindi ko gusto.","translation":"Don't **push me towards** a person I don't like."}]

translation: to lighten, to alleviate, to make easier
meaning_filipino: Ang maging sanhi ng paggaan ng isang bagay, tulad ng pasanin, gawain, o damdamin.
original_explanation: That feeling of relief. It's when a friend helps you with your heavy workload, when you finally pay off a debt, or when you vent to your BFF and your emotional baggage feels lighter. It's the verb form of "Gumaan ang pakiramdam ko." "Salamat sa tulong mo, sana makagaan ito sa mga gawain ko."
usage_notes: Can be used for physical weight, workload, or emotional burdens.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-uusap ay maaaring **makagaan** ng iyong nararamdaman.","translation":"Talking can **alleviate** what you are feeling."},{"sentence":"Sana'y **makagaan** sa iyong pasanin ang kaunting tulong na ito.","translation":"I hope this little help can **lighten** your burden."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa posisyong nakaharap ang unahang bahagi sa ibaba; nakabaligtad.
original_explanation: The default position of your phone when your jowa is around. Or how you sleep after a long, tiring day. It's the opposite of `patihayà` (face up). Think of a cup or bowl on a dish rack to let the water drip out. That's `pataob`.
usage_notes: Can describe a person lying down or an object placed with its opening facing downwards.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ilagay mo nang **pataob** ang baso para tumulo ang tubig.","translation":"Place the glass **face down** so the water drips out."},{"sentence":"Natagpuan siyang natutulog nang **pataob** sa kama.","translation":"He was found sleeping **face down** on the bed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian o kalagayan ng hindi pagtupad sa mga tungkulin at obligasyon; kawalan ng pananagutan.
original_explanation: This is the groupmate who disappears on the day of the presentation. This is the person who borrows money and suddenly gets amnesia. It’s the "bahala na si Batman" attitude applied to serious duties. It’s ghosting not just a date, but your adult responsibilities. The root cause of "ako na naman" moments for the responsible ones.
usage_notes: Used in contexts of duty, accountability, and obligation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkawalang-pananagutan** ng ilang opisyal ay nagdulot ng galit sa mga mamamayan.","translation":"The **irresponsibility** of some officials caused anger among the citizens."},{"sentence":"Itinuturo sa mga bata ang kahalagahan ng pag-iwas sa **pagkawalang-pananagutan**.","translation":"Children are taught the importance of avoiding **irresponsibility**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkikita ng dalawa o higit pang tao o bagay, maaaring sinasadya o hindi inaasahan.
original_explanation: This is the stuff of teleseryes. The moment the bida and the kontrabida finally meet, or when long-lost siblings accidentally bump into each other at the mall. It's the "it's a small world" feeling when you see your ex at your new favorite coffee shop. Pwede ring planned, like "Saan tayo magkakatagpo?" (Where will we meet?). It's the universe conspiring for two paths to intersect.
usage_notes: Can refer to both planned meetings and chance encounters. The verb is often conjugated in the future tense (`magkakatagpo`) or past tense (`nagkatagpo`).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dito sa parke na ito unang **nagkatagpo** ang mga magulang ko.","translation":"It was in this park that my parents first **met**."},{"sentence":"Sana **magkatagpo** tayong muli sa hinaharap.","translation":"I hope we **cross paths** again in the future."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang taong madaling makalimot o may mahinang memorya.
original_explanation: Describes your friend who always forgets your birthday, where they put their keys, or the chismis you told them 5 minutes ago. 'Huwag mo akong utusan, palimot ako ngayon, puyat sa work.' It's the state of having a memory like a leaky sieve.
usage_notes: Synonymous with 'makakalimutin'. 'Palimot' might feel slightly more literary or old-fashioned to some speakers.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **palimot** si lola simula nang siya ay tumanda.","translation":"Grandma became **forgetful** ever since she got old."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **palimot** sa mga utang mo sa akin.","translation":"Don't be **forgetful** of your debts to me."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging maikli o hindi mahaba.
original_explanation: Basically a synonym for 'kaigsian'. It’s the quality of being short and sweet. If your love life has 'kaiklian', it means it was a flash in the pan—a summer fling. If your speech has 'kaiklian', you're everyone's hero at the graduation ceremony.
usage_notes: Interchangeable with 'kaigsian'. 'Iksi' and 'ikli' are dialectal variants, but both 'kaigsian' and 'kaiklian' are accepted in standard Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinahahalagahan ko ang **kaiklian** ng iyong paliwanag.","translation":"I appreciate the **conciseness** of your explanation."},{"sentence":"Sa kabila ng **kaiklian** ng aming pagsasama, marami akong natutunan.","translation":"Despite the **shortness** of our time together, I learned a lot."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking pangkat o hanay ng mga pulo. Ang kabuuan ng lahat ng pulo sa isang partikular na lugar.
original_explanation: Literally "one whole group of islands." This is the Philippines' official job title. It’s why our Grab delivery routes are sometimes... complicated. We're not just one place; we're a collection of over 7,000 islands, all connected by chismis, basketball, and a deep love for karaoke.
usage_notes: Often used to refer to the entire Philippine archipelago.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Pilipinas ay isang **sangkapuluan** na binubuo ng libo-libong isla.","translation":"The Philippines is an **archipelago** made up of thousands of islands."},{"sentence":"Layunin ng programa na pag-isahin ang buong **sangkapuluan**.","translation":"The program's goal is to unite the entire **archipelago**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkuha ng isang bagay mula sa isang tao o lugar, o ang pagrekord ng imahe o video gamit ang kamera.
original_explanation: This is a multi-purpose word. It can mean you're about to be the subject of a chismis photo ('Hala, kukunan tayo ng picture!'), or that your sweldo is about to get smaller because of SSS, Pag-ibig, and Philhealth deductions ('Kukunan na naman ng tax ang sahod ko.'). It’s the future tense of being 'taxed' by life, literally and figuratively.
usage_notes: Can refer to taking a physical object, a photo/video, or abstract things like a sample or a deduction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kukunan** ko ng litrato ang magandang tanawin.","translation":"I **will take** a picture of the beautiful scenery."},{"sentence":"**Kukunan** ka ba ng dugo para sa medical exam?","translation":"**Will they take** a blood sample from you for the medical exam?"}]

translation: night and day; day and night
meaning_filipino: Walang tigil; nagaganap sa buong maghapon at magdamag.
etymology: Contraction of "gabi at araw" (night and day).
original_explanation: The ultimate description of a 24/7 hustle. BPO agents work **gabi't-araw**. OFWs work **gabi't-araw**. A mother's love is **gabi't-araw**. It means non-stop, around the clock. It's the grind that never sleeps, just like the city of Manila.
usage_notes: An idiom meaning continuously or without stopping.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtrabaho siya nang **gabi't-araw** para matustusan ang kanyang pamilya.","translation":"She worked **day and night** to provide for her family."},{"sentence":"Binantayan niya ang maysakit na ina nang **gabi't-araw**.","translation":"He watched over his sick mother **night and day**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang instrumento para sa pagsukat at pagpapakita ng temperatura.
original_explanation: The gadget your mom points at your forehead that decides if you're "may lagnat ka, 'wag ka muna maligo" sick or "kaya pa pumasok 'yan" sick. Before the fancy digital ones, this was the glass stick of doom you had to keep under your tongue or armpit. Now, it's the gatekeeper at every mall and office entrance during a health crisis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ng nars ang **termometro** upang kunin ang temperatura ng pasyente.","translation":"The nurse used the **thermometer** to take the patient's temperature."},{"sentence":"Ayon sa **termometro**, tatlumpu't walong digri ang lagnat mo.","translation":"According to the **thermometer**, your fever is thirty-eight degrees."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lisensyadong propesyonal sa kalusugan na dalubhasa sa paghahanda, pag-iimbak, at pagbibigay ng mga iniresetang gamot. Ang katumbas nito sa Filipino ay parmasyutiko o botikaryo.
original_explanation: The person at Mercury Drug or Watsons who can actually read your doctor's handwriting. They're the gatekeepers of Biogesic, Neozep, and that antibiotic you need a prescription for. You ask them, 'Miss, may gamot ba para sa sakit ng puso?' and they'll either give you medicine or a reality check. Sila yung legit na 'ask the expert.'
usage_notes: Ang salitang 'pharmacist' ay mas karaniwang ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na usapan kaysa sa mga katumbas nitong Filipino na 'parmasyutiko' o 'botikaryo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtanong ako sa **pharmacist** kung ano ang generic na bersyon ng gamot na ito.","translation":"I asked the **pharmacist** what the generic version of this medicine is."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao, bagay, o lugar na may kaugnayan sa kabanalan, relihiyon, o sa Diyos; malinis sa espirituwal at walang bahid ng kasalanan.
original_explanation: This is your friend who goes to church every single Sunday without fail, never curses, and probably has a rosary in their car. The opposite of your other friend who lives for "Sana all." It's that level of purity and goodness that makes you think, "Wow, goals," but you also know you're too much of a marites to ever achieve it.
usage_notes: Often used in religious contexts. Can also be used sarcastically to describe someone who acts overly righteous.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **banal** na tungkulin ang maglingkod sa kapwa.","translation":"It is a **holy** duty to serve others."},{"sentence":"Ang Simbahan ng Quiapo ay isang **banal** na lugar para sa maraming deboto.","translation":"The Quiapo Church is a **sacred** place for many devotees."}]

translation: in addition to that; attached to that
meaning_filipino: Bilang karagdagan sa bagay na naunang nabanggit; kasama niyon.
original_explanation: A fancy way to say 'Also...' or 'And another thing...' It's the phrase you use in a formal report or a very serious chismis session to add another layer of information. 'He was late for the meeting. Kalakip niyon, he didn't bring the coffee he promised.'
usage_notes: A set phrase used as a transition to add related information. More formal than 'saka' or 'at saka'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinasa niya ang ulat nang huli. **Kalakip niyon**, marami pa itong mali.","translation":"He submitted the report late. **In addition to that**, it still had many errors."},{"sentence":"Ang proyekto ay nangangailangan ng malaking pondo; **kalakip niyon** ang pangangailangan para sa mas maraming tao.","translation":"The project requires a large fund; **attached to that** is the need for more people."}]

meaning_filipino: May kakayahang magdulot ng karamdaman o sakit.
original_explanation: Like eating street food from a questionable vendor, or reading the comments section on a political post. It can literally make you sick (food poisoning) or figuratively make you sick (from all the toxicity). Can also refer to a person who is "sakit sa ulo"—a real pain.
usage_notes: Formed from the root "sakit" (illness/pain) with causative affixes. Describes something with the potential to cause sickness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sobrang pag-inom ng alak ay **nakapagkakasakit**.","translation":"Excessive drinking of alcohol **causes illness**."},{"sentence":"**Nakapagkakasakit** ng damdamin ang kanyang masasakit na salita.","translation":"His harsh words **make one sick** at heart."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagbabago ng isang likido upang maging gas o singaw; ang paglabas ng amoy o hangin mula sa isang sisidlan.
original_explanation: Scientifically, it's evaporation. In real life, it's why the 'patis' on the table eventually makes the whole room smell like 'patis'. It's the reason you can smell your neighbor's adobo cooking. It’s the slow escape, whether it's water turning into vapor or a secret (amoy) getting out.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for scientific processes or figuratively for odors and information spreading.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa init ng araw, mabilis ang **pagsingaw** ng tubig sa kalsada.","translation":"Because of the sun's heat, the **evaporation** of water on the road is fast."},{"sentence":"May **pagsingaw** ng gas sa kusina kaya mag-ingat ka.","translation":"There is a gas **leak** in the kitchen, so be careful."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malalim na butas sa lupa na may takip o nakatago, ginawa upang mahulog at mabihag ang isang tao o hayop.
original_explanation: The classic cartoon trap. You dig a hole, cover it with leaves, and wait for the 'kontrabida' (villain) or your unsuspecting friend to fall in. It's a literal 'pitfall,' the kind you set for others, unlike the metaphorical pitfalls you create for yourself by maxing out your credit card on Shopee.
usage_notes: Used to describe physical traps in hunting or warfare, or metaphorically for a deceptive situation designed to ensnare someone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahulog ang baboy-ramo sa **hukay na patibong** na inihanda ng mga mangangaso.","translation":"The wild boar fell into the **trap pit** prepared by the hunters."}]

meaning_filipino: Pamahalaan, pigilin, o idirekta ang kilos o galaw ng isang tao, bagay, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: What you try to do with your 'add to cart' impulses during the 11.11 sale, but fail. Also what your friend tells you to do with your feelings for your crush who has a jowa. 'Try to get a grip!'
usage_notes: Ito ang anyong pandiwa na nakapokus sa layon (object-focus) para sa salitang 'kontrol'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **kontrolahin** ang pagdami ng tao sa Metro Manila.","translation":"It is difficult **to control** the population growth in Metro Manila."},{"sentence":"Dapat mong matutunang **kontrolahin** ang iyong galit.","translation":"You should learn **to control** your anger."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manipis at makintab na patong, karaniwan ay matamis, na ipinapahid sa pagkain tulad ng tinapay, karne, o donat.
original_explanation: That shiny, sticky, sweet stuff on your favorite donut that makes you lick your fingers. It's the magic sauce on a Christmas ham or the sweet coating on a donut from Krispy Kreme. It's the "look" that says "I'm delicious, eat me."
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in a culinary context. Can also be a verb ("i-glaze ang hamon").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito ko ang orihinal na donat na may simpleng sugar **glaze**.","translation":"My favorite is the original donut with a simple sugar **glaze**."},{"sentence":"Naglalagay siya ng honey **glaze** sa manok bago ito iluto sa oven.","translation":"She puts a honey **glaze** on the chicken before cooking it in the oven."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtutupi o paglilimpon ng isang bagay, tulad ng papel o damit, upang maging mas maliit o maayos.
original_explanation: This is what you do to your feelings when your crush is near—you fold them up neatly and hide them away. Also, what your mom yells at you to do with the mountain of laundry on your bed. "Kupiin mo na 'yang mga damit mo!"
usage_notes: Used for folding flexible objects like paper, cloth, or even plastic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **kupiin** mo ang mga bagong labang tuwalya.","translation":"Please **fold** the newly washed towels."},{"sentence":"Tinuruan niya akong **kupiin** ang papel para makagawa ng isang bangkang papel.","translation":"He taught me how to **fold** the paper to make a paper boat."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay na pagkilos ng paggamit ng abaniko upang paypayan ang isa't isa, karaniwan dahil sa matinding init.
original_explanation: This is what you and your chismosa friends do on a hot afternoon while waiting for the next scoop. Picture this: a group of Titas sitting on a bench, fanning each other, not just to beat the heat but to subtly signal, "Spill the tea, sis!" It's a social ritual powered by heat and gossip.
usage_notes: A reciprocal verb form, indicating the action is done by two or more people to each other. Often used to depict a quaint, communal scene.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa brownout, naglabas ng upuan ang magkakapitbahay at nagsimulang **mag-abanikuhan** sa labas ng kanilang mga bahay.","translation":"Because of the brownout, the neighbors brought out chairs and started to **fan each other** outside their houses."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pook na pinalilibutan ng matibay na pader o istruktura para sa depensa; isang muog o balwarte.
etymology: From Malay 'kota' (fort, city), which in turn is from Sanskrit 'koṭa' (fort, stronghold).
original_explanation: The original 'Walled City'. Think Intramuros. It's a fort built to keep enemies out, usually with cannons, high walls, and a great view of the sea for spotting incoming pirates or colonizers. In modern terms, your bedroom when you don't want to do chores is your personal **kota**.
usage_notes: Primarily used in historical contexts. 'Kuta' is a more common variant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Fort Santiago ay isang makasaysayang **kota** sa loob ng Intramuros.","translation":"Fort Santiago is a historic **fort** inside Intramuros."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang manatili o maging labi mula sa isang kabuuan matapos bawasan o alisin ang ilang bahagi.
original_explanation: This is the "sana all may natira" moment after sweldo. O yung feeling na ikaw na lang ang single sa barkada. It's what's left over. In a Pinoy party, "matira" is the food you take home as "baon." In a competition, it's the last one standing. "Matira ang matibay!" is the ultimate Pinoy survival motto.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of leftovers, survivors, or remaining items. The phrase "Matira ang matibay" (The strong will survive) is very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **matira** sa laro ang siyang panalo.","translation":"Whoever **remains** in the game is the winner."},{"sentence":"Kaunti na lang ang **matira** sa ulam, kaya mag-init na lang tayo ng iba.","translation":"There's only a little of the dish **left**, so let's just heat up something else."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng bahay kung saan kumakain ang mga tao, karaniwang kinaroroonan ng hapag-kainan.
etymology: Compound word from "silid" (room) and "kainan" (eating place, from root 'kain').
original_explanation: The stage for family drama and chismis during Noche Buena. It's where 'tumaba ka' is the standard greeting and where the last piece of lechon is fiercely contested. Also serves as a makeshift office or study area 90% of the year.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakahanda na ang hapunan sa **silid-kainan**.","translation":"Dinner is ready in the **dining room**."},{"sentence":"Pinalamutian nila ang **silid-kainan** para sa Pasko.","translation":"They decorated the **dining room** for Christmas."}]

meaning_filipino: Sama-samang lumapit at magdikit-dikit sa isang lugar, karaniwan ay bilang isang grupo.
original_explanation: This is the command you hear from photographers at every Pinoy party: 'Okay, maglapit-lapit po tayo for the group picture!' It's the physical act of 'siksikan' to fit into a frame, to share one umbrella during a downpour, or to huddle together to hear the latest chismis from one source. It implies a group action of coming together in a tight space.
usage_notes: The repetition of 'lapit' emphasizes the collective and close-knit nature of the gathering. It's a plural or group action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Maglapit-lapit** kayo para hindi kayo mabasa ng ulan.","translation":"**Huddle together** so you don't get wet from the rain."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula nang **maglapit-lapit** ang mga tao sa paligid ng entablado.","translation":"The people started to **gather closely** around the stage."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng katad na may malambot at gasgas na ibabaw, karaniwang gawa sa panloob na bahagi ng balat ng hayop.
original_explanation: The material of those fancy shoes or bags you're afraid to get wet. It feels soft and luxurious, but one drop of rain and it's drama. The high-maintenance cousin of regular leather. Also refers to the 'chamois' cloth for cleaning cars and glasses.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingatan mong matapunan ng tubig ang bago mong sapatos na **gamusa**.","translation":"Be careful not to spill water on your new **suede** shoes."},{"sentence":"Kumuha siya ng basahang **gamusa** para patuyuin ang sasakyan.","translation":"He got a **chamois** cloth to dry the car."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pariralang pang-ukol na nagpapakilala sa pinagmulan ng isang impormasyon, opinyon, o utos. Ang 'sa' ay ginagamit para sa mga karaniwang pangngalan at ang 'kay' para sa mga tiyak na pangalan ng tao.
original_explanation: The official way to start any chismis. "**Ayon kay** Marites..." is the Filipino equivalent of "A little birdy told me...". It gives your statement a veneer of authority, even if your source is just the tindera sa kanto. Use 'sa' for things/institutions (e.g., "ayon sa balita") and 'kay' for people (e.g., "ayon kay Mameh").
usage_notes: 'Ayon sa' precedes common nouns (e.g., ayon sa batas). 'Ayon kay' precedes personal names (e.g., ayon kay Jose). 'Ayon kina' is used for multiple people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ayon sa** batas, bawal magtapon ng basura dito.","translation":"**According to** the law, it is forbidden to throw trash here."},{"sentence":"**Ayon kay** Dr. Rizal, ang kabataan ang pag-asa ng bayan.","translation":"**According to** Dr. Rizal, the youth is the hope of the nation."}]

translation: an assayer's office; a place for testing quality
meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o tanggapan kung saan sinusuri ang kalidad, kadalisayan, o halaga ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay metal tulad ng ginto.
etymology: From pa- + kilatis + -an. 'Kilatis' means 'purity' or 'carat' (of gold), and the pa-...-an affix denotes a place where the action is done.
original_explanation: Before there were "legit checkers" on Facebook marketplace, there was the pakilatisan. It's the OG place you go to see if the "gold" necklace your ex gave you is real or just gilded heartbreak. Think of it as a physical "fact-check" for your alahas (jewelry).
usage_notes: A specific and somewhat dated term, strongly associated with jewelry and pawnshops.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala niya ang singsing sa **pakilatisan** upang malaman kung ilang karat ito.","translation":"She brought the ring to the **assayer's office** to find out how many carats it was."},{"sentence":"May malaking **pakilatisan** ng ginto sa bayan ng Meycauayan.","translation":"There is a large gold **assaying center** in the town of Meycauayan."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi nag-iiba o nananatiling pareho sa paglipas ng panahon; matatag at permanente.
original_explanation: Ito yung pagmamahal mo sa kanya, kahit ilang beses ka nang na-seen-zone. O yung presyo ng bilihin na sana all, di-nagbabago. Constant. As in, forever and ever, amen. Parang Wi-Fi signal na laging full bars, pero sa feelings.
usage_notes: Used to describe something that remains constant, stable, or consistent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Di-nagbabago** ang pagtingin ko sa iyo mula pa noon.","translation":"My feelings for you have been **unchanging** since then."},{"sentence":"Ang mga batas ng kalikasan ay **di-nagbabago**.","translation":"The laws of nature are **unchanging**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang alternatibong baybay o katawagan para sa balumbong, ang lalagyan na gawa sa kawayan.
original_explanation: A variant of `balumbong`. It's the same OG Filipino tumbler made of bamboo. The spelling difference is probably a regional thing, like the eternal debate between 'Filipino' and 'Pilipino'.
usage_notes: Interchangeable with `balumbong`, but both are rarely used in modern conversation. 'Bumbong' is the more prevalent term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga sinaunang Pilipino ay gumagamit ng **balungbong** para sa kanilang inumin.","translation":"Ancient Filipinos used **bamboo containers** for their drinks."},{"sentence":"May ukit ang **balungbong** na ginamit sa ritwal.","translation":"The **bamboo container** used in the ritual has carvings."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaikling anyo ng "wika mo" o "sabi mo," na ginagamit upang iulat ang sinabi ng isang tao.
original_explanation: The classic "he said, she said" but make it Pinoy. It's the shorthand for "sabi mo." Example: "Ika mo, mahal mo ako, pero bakit may ka-chat kang iba?" It's the verbal equivalent of pulling out the receipts.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa panitikan o sa medyo pormal na usapan upang sumipi sa sinabi ng iba. Mas bihira itong gamitin sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap kumpara sa "sabi mo."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ika** nga ng matatanda, 'Magsipag ka nang husto para sa iyong kinabukasan.'","translation":"As the elders **say**, 'Work very hard for your future.'"},{"sentence":"Maganda raw ang pelikula, **ika** ni Maria.","translation":"The movie is supposedly good, **said** Maria."}]

meaning_filipino: Nauukol o may katangian ng isang ina; may kaugnayan sa pagiging ina.
original_explanation: When your work supervisor packs you extra baon because you look thin, that's her maternal instincts kicking in. It's that 'motherly' vibe. Often used in English, but understood by most Filipinos.
usage_notes: A loanword used in formal, medical, or code-switching contexts. The native Tagalog equivalent is 'maka-ina' or 'pang-ina'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **maternal** instincts ng isang ina ay laging lumalabas.","translation":"A mother's **maternal** instincts always come out."},{"sentence":"Nag-file siya ng **maternal** leave para alagaan ang bagong silang niyang anak.","translation":"She filed for **maternal** leave to take care of her newborn child."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkukunwari o pagpapakita ng magkaibang pag-uugali o paniniwala sa iba't ibang tao o sitwasyon; pagkakaroon ng dalawang mukha.
original_explanation: This is the classic 'plastikan' but leveled up. It's that co-worker who's super nice to the boss but talks trash about them during lunch. It's the 'frenemy' in every teleserye. In short, #SanaTotooKa.
usage_notes: A strongly negative term for duplicity and insincerity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya matagalan ang **pagdadalawang-mukha** ng kanyang kaibigan.","translation":"She could not stand the **hypocrisy** of her friend."},{"sentence":"Itigil na ang **pagdadalawang-mukha** at magpakatotoo ka.","translation":"Stop **being two-faced** and be real."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng isang pagkakataon, sitwasyon, o kahinaan ng iba para sa sariling kapakinabangan, na kadalasa'y may negatibong konotasyon.
original_explanation: This is the noun form of being an 'opportunist,' but with a shady vibe. Like when someone uses your Netflix account without your permission. O yung 'friend' na lumalapit lang 'pag may kailangan. It's spotting a loophole and diving right in, whether it's ethical or not.
usage_notes: Almost always has a negative connotation of opportunism or exploitation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagsamantala** sa kalamidad para magtaas ng presyo ay ilegal.","translation":"The **act of taking advantage** of a calamity to raise prices is illegal."},{"sentence":"Biktima siya ng **pagsamantala** ng kanyang amo.","translation":"She was a victim of **exploitation** by her boss."}]

meaning_filipino: Dalawang supling na ipinanganak sa iisang pagbubuntis.
original_explanation: 'Yung magkapatid na pareho ng birthday at halos pareho ng mukha. Sila 'yung magkakambal. The classic "which one are you?" scenario. Also used to describe two things that are identical, like your matching shirts with your BFF. "Uy, magkakambal tayo ng sapatos!"
usage_notes: Primarily refers to human twins but can be used metaphorically for any two identical or closely related things.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **magkakambal** na sina Popoy at Basya ay laging magkasama.","translation":"The **twins**, Popoy and Basya, are always together."},{"sentence":"Hindi mo aakalaing hindi sila **magkakambal** dahil sa kanilang pagkakahawig.","translation":"You wouldn't think they aren't **twins** because of their resemblance."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o paraan ng paghimok o pag-akit sa isang tao upang sumang-ayon, maniwala, o gawin ang isang bagay.
etymology: From Malay 'hikayat', ultimately from Arabic 'ḥikāya' (story, tale).
original_explanation: This is the art of 'budol'. It's what your friend does to make you go out when you promised yourself you'd stay home. It's what Shopee and Lazada do with their flash sales. It's the power to make someone say 'yes' even when their brain says 'no'.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of convincing someone. The verb form 'hikayatin' is more common in everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang lahat ng paraan ng **hikayat** para makuha ang boto ng mga tao.","translation":"He used every method of **persuasion** to get the people's votes."},{"sentence":"Ang matamis na salita ay isang mabisang **hikayat**.","translation":"Sweet words are an effective **inducement**."}]

translation: act of residing; living (in a place)
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paninirahan o pag-okupa sa isang bahay, lugar, o tirahan.
original_explanation: This is your life's status. Are you team 'condo living' or team 'bahay at lupa'? It's the daily grind of staying in a place. 'Mahirap ang **pagtira** sa Maynila kung malayo ka sa trabaho, puro traffic ang aabutin mo.'
usage_notes: Refers to the act or condition of dwelling somewhere. The stress is on the second syllable of the root: ti-RA.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinili niya ang **pagtira** sa probinsya para sa mas tahimik na buhay.","translation":"He chose **living** in the province for a quieter life."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagtira** sa tabi ng riles ay mapanganib.","translation":"**Residing** beside the train tracks is dangerous."}]

translation: to waste (time, effort, resources) on someone/something
meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit o paggugol ng isang bagay na mahalaga, tulad ng oras, pera, o lakas, sa isang tao, bagay, o gawain na walang kabuluhan o hindi karapat-dapat.
original_explanation: This is the verb for all your 'sana all' moments that turn into 'sana 'di na lang.' You know, when you spend hours crafting the perfect reply to your crush, only to get 'seen-zoned.' That's you, 'pinag-aksayahan' mo ng effort. It's the hugot behind spending your 13th-month pay on something that breaks after a week. 'Don't waste your time on me.'
usage_notes: Used to denote the object or person on which something valuable is wasted. Often used with a sense of regret or admonishment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pag-aksayahan** ng luha ang taong hindi ka naman pinapahalagahan.","translation":"Don't **waste** your tears on a person who doesn't value you."},{"sentence":"Ayokong **pag-aksayahan** ng oras ang mga walang katuturang tsismis.","translation":"I don't want **to waste** time on pointless gossip."}]

translation: to use a lasso; to tie with a ribbon
meaning_filipino: Gumamit ng laso, na maaaring tumukoy sa lubid na may silo para sa paghuli ng hayop, o sa pampalamuting sintas para sa regalo o buhok.
original_explanation: This verb has a cool double life. On one hand, it's the cowboy move: 'maglaso ng baka' (to lasso a cow). Very ranchero. On the other hand, it’s what you do to a gift box: 'maglaso ng regalo' (to tie a ribbon on a gift). It's all about using that 'laso' (from Spanish 'lazo'), whether it's for wrangling cattle or for making something pretty. The context is your clue!
usage_notes: The meaning depends heavily on the object of the verb. 'Laso' can mean a cowboy's lasso or a decorative ribbon/bow.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sanay siyang **maglaso** ng mga kabayo sa kanilang rancho.","translation":"He is skilled at **lassoing** horses on their ranch."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **maglaso** sa kahon ng regalo para maging maganda.","translation":"Don't forget to **tie a ribbon** on the gift box to make it look nice."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang panlinis na binubuo ng isang bungkos ng makakapal na sinulid o espongha na nakakabit sa isang hawakan, ginagamit sa paglilinis ng sahig.
original_explanation: That thing your mom yells at you to use on a Saturday morning. The archenemy of spilled coffee and dusty floors. It has two states: wet and ready for cleaning, or crusty and forgotten in the corner of the CR.
usage_notes: May katumbas na salita sa Tagalog ("panlampaso") ngunit mas karaniwang ginagamit ang "mop" sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiabot ng **mop** at timba, lilinisin ko ang sahig.","translation":"Please hand me the **mop** and bucket, I will clean the floor."},{"sentence":"Basang-basa ang sahig kaya kailangan itong i-**mop**.","translation":"The floor is very wet so it needs to be **mopped**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang dayagram na gumagamit ng mga bilog na nagkakapatong upang ilarawan ang lohikal na ugnayan sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang mga pangkat ng bagay.
etymology: Salin-hiram mula sa Ingles na 'Venn Diagram', ipinangalan kay John Venn.
original_explanation: The official diagram of 'It's Complicated' relationships. You know, those overlapping circles from school that show what you and your crush have in common (the tiny middle part) and what you don't (the huge outer parts). Perfect for comparing 'Sana All' vs. 'Sana Oil'.
usage_notes: A direct translation/adaptation for the term 'Venn Diagram', used in academic and formal settings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gamit ang isang **Guhiting Venn**, ipakita ang pagkakatulad at pagkakaiba ng Noli Me Tángere at El filibusterismo.","translation":"Using a **Venn Diagram**, show the similarities and differences between Noli Me Tángere and El filibusterismo."},{"sentence":"Ipinagawa sa amin ng guro ang isang **Guhiting Venn** tungkol sa mga uri ng hayop.","translation":"The teacher made us create a **Venn Diagram** about types of animals."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bilang na lima (5); sa sistema ng pagmamarka ng ilang unibersidad tulad ng UP, ito ang kumakatawan sa bagsak na grado.
original_explanation: A word with a dual personality. On the streets, **singko** is the five-peso coin for your pamasahe. In the University of the Philippines, **singko** is the stuff of nightmares—the 5.0 grade that means you've failed the subject and have to face the 'walk of shame' to your professor's office. It's the ultimate "game over" in acads.
usage_notes: The meaning of a failing grade is specific to certain universities, most notably the University of the Philippines (UP).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May barya ka bang **singko** para sa jeep?","translation":"Do you have a **five**-peso coin for the jeepney?"},{"sentence":"Nalungkot ang estudyante nang makita niyang **singko** ang grado niya sa Math.","translation":"The student was sad when he saw that his grade in Math was a **failing grade** (5.0)."}]

meaning_filipino: Maliliit na piraso ng papel o metalikong materyal na isinasaboy sa mga pagdiriwang tulad ng parada, kasal, o Bagong Taon.
etymology: From Spanish 'confites' (sweets, which were originally thrown during carnivals). The standard Filipino spelling is 'kumpitis'.
original_explanation: The tiny, colorful pieces of paper that signal 'PARTY TIME!' at birthdays or New Year's Eve. It's super fun when it's flying in the air, but an absolute nightmare to clean up the next day. It gets everywhere—in your hair, in your clothes, in your food. The glitter version is its evil, more fabulous cousin.
usage_notes: 'Kumpites' is a common colloquial spelling and pronunciation. The more formal, dictionary-standard spelling is 'kumpitis'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-ulan ng **kumpites** nang manalo ang kanilang koponan.","translation":"It rained **confetti** when their team won."},{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutan ang **kumpites** para sa party mamaya.","translation":"Don't forget the **confetti** for the party later."}]

translation: feels like vomiting, is made to vomit
meaning_filipino: Nakakaramdam ng hindi mapigilang pagnanais na ilabas ang laman ng sikmura; nasusuka.
original_explanation: This is that 'I shouldn't have eaten that' feeling. It's the physical reaction to spoiled food, a bumpy bus ride, or sometimes, your ex's new profile picture. It's an involuntary urge to throw up, whether from something physical or something emotionally disgusting.
usage_notes: Describes the feeling or state of being about to vomit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Napapasuka** ako sa sobrang pag-ikot ng sasakyan.","translation":"The constant turning of the car **makes me feel like vomiting**."},{"sentence":"Sa sobrang sama ng lasa ng gamot, **napapasuka** ang bata.","translation":"The medicine tasted so bad, the child **felt like vomiting**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpunta sa mas mataas na lugar, posisyon, o lebel sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: What you tell your boss when you're gunning for a promotion: "Aakyat ako sa corporate ladder!" Also what you say when the LRT elevator is broken and you have to take the stairs to the platform.
usage_notes: The contemplative aspect of the future tense of 'akyat'. The more common spoken form is 'aakyatin' (for an object) or 'umakyat' (as an intransitive verb). 'Aakyat' implies intention.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bukas kami **aakyat** ng Bundok Pulag.","translation":"We **will climb** Mt. Pulag tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Dahil sira ang elevator, **aakyat** kami sa hagdan hanggang 10th floor.","translation":"Because the elevator is broken, we **will go up** the stairs to the 10th floor."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagkakaroon ng matalas, mabilis, at malinaw na pag-iisip; talino.
original_explanation: This is what you wish you had during a job interview or when your crush asks you a question. It's being 'quick on the uptake,' 'madiskarte,' or 'gets na gets agad.' Not just book smart, but street smart too. The opposite of 'loading...'
usage_notes: A noun phrase that functions as a single concept for intelligence and wit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinangaan siya dahil sa kanyang **katalasan ng isip** sa paglutas ng problema.","translation":"He was admired for his **sharpness of mind** in solving the problem."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ang **katalasan ng isip** sa larong chess.","translation":"Mental **acuity** is needed in the game of chess."}]

translation: to criticize, to notice, to point out a flaw
meaning_filipino: Magbigay ng puna o komento, karaniwan ay tumutukoy sa mga pagkukulang o kamalian ng isang bagay o tao.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping pandiwa na 'ma-' at ang salitang ugat na 'puna' (notice, criticism).
original_explanation: To give 'constructive criticism,' but let's be real, it's usually just criticism. It's what your boss does during your performance review, what your tita does to your life choices, and what netizens do in the comments section 24/7. 'Hilig mamuna' is a national pastime.
usage_notes: Maaaring maging neutral na pagpansin o matinding kritisismo depende sa konteksto at tono ng pagkakasabi.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mahiyang **mamuna** kung may makita kang mali sa aking gawa.","translation":"Don't be shy to **criticize** if you see something wrong with my work."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **mamuna** ng pananamit ng iba.","translation":"She likes to **criticize** how other people dress."}]

word: hayop na may supot sa tiyan
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng mamalyang hayop na karaniwang dinadala ang kanyang anak sa isang supot o lukbutan sa kanyang tiyan.
original_explanation: This is the long, descriptive way to say "marsupial." Think kangaroos and koalas. Sila yung mga nanay na may built-in baby bag. It's super specific, kaya madalas "kangaroo" na lang ang sasabihin ng mga tao instead of this mouthful.
usage_notes: Isang literal na paglalarawan. Ang salitang "marsupial" ay mas karaniwan sa siyentipikong konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kangaroo ay isang **hayop na may supot sa tiyan** na matatagpuan sa Australia.","translation":"The kangaroo is a **marsupial** found in Australia."}]

meaning_filipino: Gumamit ng gaod o sagwan upang paandarin o igiya ang isang bangka o sasakyang pantubig.
etymology: From the root 'gaod' (oar) with the infix '-um-'.
original_explanation: The OG way of moving a boat before motors were a thing. Metaphorically, it's what you feel you're doing when you're trying to move your group project forward while your groupmates are just dead weight. 'Ako na lang mag-isa ang gumagaod dito!'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinailangan naming **gumaod** nang malakas laban sa agos ng ilog.","translation":"We had to **row** hard against the river's current."},{"sentence":"Pagod na pagod ang kanyang mga braso sa maghapong **paggapod**.","translation":"His arms were very tired from **rowing** all day."}]

translation: purple rice cake steamed in bamboo tubes
meaning_filipino: Isang tradisyonal na kakaning Pilipino na gawa sa malagkit na bigas (pirurutong) na kulay lila, pinasisingawan sa loob ng tubong kawayan (bumbong), at inihahain kasama ng niyog at asukal na pula.
original_explanation: Ah, the smell of Christmas in the Philippines! This isn't just a snack; it's a whole Christmas morning vibe. It's a purple sticky rice cake cooked in bamboo tubes, served hot with a generous sprinkle of grated coconut, muscovado sugar, and sometimes a slab of butter or margarine. You'll see vendors pop up outside churches during Simbang Gabi. It's the ultimate post-mass treat.
usage_notes: Pangunahing iniuugnay sa panahon ng Pasko sa Pilipinas, lalo na tuwing Misa de Gallo o Simbang Gabi. Ang baybay na 'putubumbong' ay isang karaniwang baryasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng Simbang Gabi, kakain kami ng **puto-bumbong**.","translation":"After the Dawn Mass, we will eat **puto-bumbong**."},{"sentence":"Ang sarap ng **puto-bumbong** na may maraming niyog at asukal.","translation":"The **puto-bumbong** with lots of coconut and sugar is delicious."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay, lalo na ang negatibo, na laganap, malubha, o matagal nang umiiral at mahirap nang alisin.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung level ng problema na hindi na kaya ng "dasal lang". Parang chismis sa office, sobrang kumalat na. O 'yung utang mo sa credit card, hindi na basta utang, lifestyle na. It's when something bad has gone from a "phase" to a "feature."
usage_notes: Almost always used with a negative connotation, describing problems like corruption, addiction, or disease.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Talamak** na ang korapsyon sa ahensyang iyon.","translation":"Corruption is **rampant** in that agency."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa bisyo, naging **talamak** ang kanyang sakit sa baga.","translation":"Because of his vice, his lung disease became **chronic**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng malakas at dumadagundong na tunog sa kalangitan na kasunod ng isang kidlat. Ito ang anyong pangkaganapan ng 'kulog'.
original_explanation: The sound that makes you jump and your dog hide under the bed. It's the sky's bass drop after a flash of lightning. When it kumulog, it means a storm is nearby. It's also what your stomach does loudly in a quiet room when you're hungry, and you try to pretend it wasn't you.
usage_notes: Past tense/completed aspect of 'kulog'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malakas na **kumulog** kaya nagising ang sanggol.","translation":"It **thundered** loudly, so the baby woke up."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko munang kumidlat bago **kumulog**.","translation":"I saw it flash with lightning first before it **thundered**."}]

translation: to look out of (a window); to peer out
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtingin sa labas mula sa isang siwang o mataas na lugar, karaniwan mula sa bintana, habang ang katawan ay nasa loob.
original_explanation: This is the official verb for being a "Marites" from your window. When you hear a commotion outside and you just *have* to see what's up, you don't just "look," you "dumungaw." It's leaning out just enough to get the tea, but not enough to be fully involved. The classic "usyoso" move.
usage_notes: Almost always associated with windows, balconies, or other openings. Implies looking downwards or outwards from an enclosed space.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dumungaw** siya sa bintana para tingnan kung sino ang kumakatok.","translation":"She **looked out** the window to see who was knocking."},{"sentence":"Nang marinig ang sigaw, lahat kami ay **dumungaw** mula sa aming mga opisina.","translation":"When we heard the shout, all of us **peered out** from our offices."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng hindi pagdalo, hindi pagsipot, o hindi paggawa sa isang tungkulin o kaganapan. Pagtanggal o hindi pagsama ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is your go-to move when you're not feeling the 'petsa de peligro' vibe at work or school. It's the official term for 'absent po.' Also used when you conveniently 'forget' to include your ex in the group picture throwback.
usage_notes: Can mean both physical absence (not being present) and omission (leaving something out).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang madalas niyang **pagliban** sa klase ay nakaapekto sa kanyang mga grado.","translation":"His frequent **absence** from class affected his grades."},{"sentence":"May **pagliban** sa listahan ng mga sangkap kaya hindi naging masarap ang luto.","translation":"There was an **omission** in the list of ingredients, that's why the dish wasn't delicious."}]

translation: feeling a thrill of romantic excitement
meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang pandamdam ng matinding tuwa, pananabik, o nerbiyos na karaniwang may kaugnayan sa romantikong interes.
etymology: From 'kilig', the feeling of romantic excitement. 'Kinikilig' is its present progressive verb form.
original_explanation: Ah, *kilig*. The untranslatable. *Kinikilig* is the active state of feeling it. It's that giddy, butterflies-in-your-stomach, can't-stop-smiling feeling when your crush messages you "hi". It's the internal squealing when your favorite K-drama characters finally hold hands. It's a full-body blush and a sudden inability to form coherent sentences. The national emotion of the Philippines.
usage_notes: Often followed by 'ako' as in 'Kinikilig ako' (I'm feeling 'kilig').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kinikilig** ako sa tuwing ngumingiti siya sa akin.","translation":"I **get that giddy romantic feeling** every time he/she smiles at me."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maingay, **kinikilig** ang kaibigan natin habang nanonood ng teleserye.","translation":"Be quiet, our friend is **feeling 'kilig'** while watching the soap opera."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malakihang pagtitipon ng mga tao sa isang pampublikong lugar upang ipahayag ang kanilang mga saloobin, suporta, o pagtutol sa isang partikular na isyu, patakaran, o pinuno.
original_explanation: In the Philippines, this is what happens when people get fed up and take it to the streets. It's a public gathering, usually with placards, megaphones, and a whole lot of chanting, to protest or support a cause. From EDSA to your local university, a 'rally' is a staple of Pinoy activism. It’s democracy in its loudest, most traffic-inducing form.
usage_notes: Often associated with political activism and student movements in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng malaking **rally** sa Mendiola kahapon.","translation":"There was a big **rally** at Mendiola yesterday."},{"sentence":"Sumama ang mga estudyante sa **rally** upang ipanawagan ang mas mataas na badyet para sa edukasyon.","translation":"The students joined the **protest** to call for a higher budget for education."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkawala o panlalabo ng orihinal na kulay o ningning ng isang bagay dahil sa pagkaluma, pagkakabilad sa araw, o madalas na paggamit.
original_explanation: The reason you can't wear your favorite black t-shirt forever. It's what happens to old jeans, forgotten posters, and sometimes, feelings. 'Hugot' alert: 'Parang pag-ibig niyo, kupas na.' It's the visual representation of time passing and glory diminishing.
usage_notes: The verb form is 'kumupas' (to fade). Often used metaphorically for feelings, memories, or fame.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kupas** na ang kulay ng paborito kong damit.","translation":"The color of my favorite shirt has **faded**."},{"sentence":"Makikita sa mga litrato ang **kupas** na alaala ng nakaraan.","translation":"You can see the **faded** memories of the past in the photos."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginawang mas makapal ang isang bagay. Sa malalim na panitikan, maaari rin itong mangahulugang nilikha o nilalang.
etymology: From the root word `kapal` (thickness). The first meaning ('to thicken') is straightforward. The second meaning ('to create') is a metaphorical extension, as if shaping a thick mass of material into existence. Related to `Maykapal` (The Creator).
original_explanation: This word is a bit of a drama queen. In everyday life, it's what the make-up artist did to your foundation ("Kinapal niya 'yung base ko, mukha akong espasol!"). But in old poems and epic sagas, it's how the universe was made. "Ang mga bundok ay kinapal ng Bathala." So it's either about pancake-face makeup or divine creation. No in-between.
usage_notes: The 'to create' meaning is literary, religious, or archaic. The 'to thicken' meaning is more common in practical contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kinapal** ng karpintero ang pader gamit ang semento.","translation":"The carpenter **thickened** the wall with cement."},{"sentence":"Ang buong sanlibutan ay **kinapal** sa loob ng pitong araw, ayon sa Banal na Kasulatan.","translation":"The entire universe **was created** in seven days, according to the Holy Scripture."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o paghiling sa isang tao na buhatin o dalhin ang isang mabigat na bagay.
etymology: From the causative prefix `ipa-` and the root word `buhat` (to lift, to carry).
original_explanation: The official verb for when you buy a 50-kilo sack of rice at the palengke and you need someone else to do the heavy lifting. "Manong, paki-buhat." Or when you see your gym-fit brother doing nothing: "Hoy, 'wag kang pabebe diyan, **ipabuhat** ko sa'yo 'tong galon ng tubig!"
usage_notes: Commonly used for requesting help with heavy objects, from groceries to furniture.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ipabuhat** mo na lang sa mga kargador 'yang mga maleta.","translation":"Just **have** the porters **carry** those suitcases."},{"sentence":"Sino ang puwedeng **ipabuhat** ng lamesang ito papasok ng bahay?","translation":"Who can we **have carry** this table into the house?"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang panahon na hindi pa nagtatagal mula sa kasalukuyan; hindi pa natatagalan.
original_explanation: The formal way of saying "nung isang araw lang" or "very recent lang." It's what you use in official emails or when you're trying to sound smart while gossiping. "Kamakailan lamang, I saw him with someone else..." See? Instant class.
usage_notes: Often shortened to just 'kamakailan'. 'Lamang' adds emphasis on the recency.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kamakailan lamang** ay nag-anunsyo sila ng bagong patakaran.","translation":"**Just recently**, they announced a new policy."},{"sentence":"Nagkita kami **kamakailan lamang** sa isang coffee shop.","translation":"We met **only recently** at a coffee shop."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang empleyado na nagtatrabaho sa isang call center, na tumatanggap o gumagawa ng mga tawag sa telepono para sa isang kumpanya.
etymology: Mula sa pariralang Ingles na "call center agent".
original_explanation: The modern-day bayani working graveyard shifts, fueled by coffee and sheer will. They're the ones you talk to when your internet is down. A **call center agent** has more patience in one shift than most people have in a year. They're masters of the 'Sir/Ma'am, I understand your frustration...' line.
usage_notes: Madalas na pinaikli bilang "agent" o tinutukoy ang propesyon bilang "call center".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dating **call center agent** ang kapatid ko bago siya naging team lead.","translation":"My sibling was a former **call center agent** before becoming a team lead."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang sahod ng mga **call center agent** na may night differential.","translation":"The salary of **call center agents** with night differential is high."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bilang na kasunod ng labinsiyam at bago ang dalawampu't isa; katumbas ng 20.
original_explanation: The magic number for your pamasahe sa jeep (minsan kulang pa), a small bill you can easily break at the sari-sari store, or your age when you thought you had it all figured out (spoiler: you didn't). It's the Spanish-derived way of saying "dalawampu."
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa pagtukoy sa pera, edad, at sa impormal na pagbibilang. Ang katutubong katumbas nito ay "dalawampu".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pautang muna ng **beinte** pesos, pambili lang ng yosi.","translation":"Can I borrow **twenty** pesos, just to buy cigarettes."},{"sentence":"Mag **be-beinte** anyos na ako sa susunod na buwan.","translation":"I'll be turning **twenty** years old next month."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagbibigay o paggamit ng gamot para sa paggamot ng isang karamdaman; o ang gamot mismo.
original_explanation: It's what your doctor gives you and what your lola reminds you to take every 8 hours. "Uminom ka na ba ng medikasyon mo?" is the official love language of concerned Filipino family members. Whether it's for a simple headache or for maintenance, it's the stuff that keeps us going (or makes us sleepy).
usage_notes: Interchangeable with 'gamot' (medicine), but 'medikasyon' often implies a prescribed course of treatment or the act of medicating.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang pagsunod sa tamang **medikasyon** na inireseta ng doktor.","translation":"It is important to follow the correct **medication** prescribed by the doctor."},{"sentence":"Itinigil niya ang kanyang **medikasyon** nang walang pahintulot mula sa espesyalista.","translation":"He stopped his **medication** without permission from the specialist."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang espesyal na uri ng niyog na may malambot at malagkit na laman na halos pumupuno sa loob ng bao, at may kaunting sabaw lamang. Ito ay resulta ng isang abnormalidad sa pag-unlad ng endosperm ng bunga.
etymology: From 'niyog' (coconut) and 'makapuno' (from 'puno,' meaning full), literally 'coconut that is full.'
original_explanation: This is the 'sana all' version of coconuts. While a regular niyog has water and firm meat, the **niyog na makapuno** is packed to the brim with soft, jelly-like, glorious coconut goodness. It's a genetic anomaly that results in pure dessert magic. It's the special, rare, and more expensive cousin in the coconut family, perfect for ice cream and sweets.
usage_notes: Often shortened to just 'makapuno'. It's a prized ingredient for Filipino desserts like ice cream, pastillas, and halo-halo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paborito kong ice cream flavor ay **niyog na makapuno**.","translation":"My favorite ice cream flavor is **macapuno coconut**."},{"sentence":"Mahal ang isang lata ng minatamis na **niyog na makapuno** dahil bihira ito.","translation":"A can of sweetened **macapuno coconut** is expensive because it is rare."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng alahas na isinusuot sa tainga, na katumbas ng hikaw. Kadalasan, tumutukoy ito sa mga hikaw na hugis anilyo o argolla.
original_explanation: An old-school word for earrings, especially the hoop or ring type ('argolla'). Think of your lola's classic gold earrings. It's something that hangs on you, kinda like your responsibilities, but way more fashionable.
usage_notes: 'Hikaw' is the more common term for earring today. 'Pakaw' is still used, especially for traditional or hoop-style earrings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang pares ng gintong **pakaw** ang regalo niya sa kanyang ina.","translation":"A pair of golden **earrings** was his gift to his mother."},{"sentence":"Nawala ang isang **pakaw** ko habang nagsasayaw.","translation":"I lost one of my **earrings** while dancing."}]

meaning_filipino: Maging sanhi o dahilan ng galit o pagkagalit.
original_explanation: This is the reason you go from zero to 'Hulk smash' real quick. It could be someone spoiling the ending of a series you're watching, a 'Marites' spreading fake news about you, or a driver cutting you off in traffic. It's the trigger for your anger. The phrase 'nang labis' (greatly, excessively) just turns the volume up to 11.
usage_notes: The phrase 'ikagalit nang labis' means 'to cause extreme anger' or 'to infuriate'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga kasinungalingan ang **ikinagalit** ko nang labis.","translation":"His lies were what **caused my extreme anger**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang gumawa ng bagay na **ikagagalit** ng iyong ama.","translation":"Don't do things that will **cause your father's anger**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa direksyon o kilos na patungo sa labas ng isang lugar.
original_explanation: When you're finally clocking out from your BPO shift at 6 AM. "Pauwi na? Hindi, palabas pa lang ng office." It's the direction you're heading when you've had enough and just need to leave the room.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatayo siya sa may pinto, **palabas** na.","translation":"He was standing by the door, already **on his way out**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa tao, grupo, o kalahok na nagwagi sa isang kompetisyon.
etymology: Hiram sa salitang Espanyol na *ganado*, na nangangahulugang 'nanalo' o 'kumita'.
original_explanation: The winner, the champ, the bida! This is the person everyone wants to be. From the local karaoke contest winner to the grand lottery winner, ang **panalo** is the one who gets the prize, the bragging rights, and probably a congratulatory tarpaulin from a local politician.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa isang tao (ang panalo) o sa mismong resulta (ang panalo niya).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **panalo** ay mag-uuwi ng isang milyong piso.","translation":"The **winner** will take home one million pesos."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **panalo** sa laro ninyo kagabi?","translation":"Who was the **winner** of your game last night?"}]

meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng kasiyahan, pabuya, o gantimpala ang isang tao bilang pagkilala sa kanyang ginawa o serbisyo.
original_explanation: 'Yan 'yung ginagawa ng boss mo 'pag binigyan ka ng bonus kasi na-hit mo 'yung quota. O 'yung pag-treat mo sa sarili mo ng milk tea after a hell week. Basically, bigyan ng reward ang sarili o ang iba.
usage_notes: Isang pormal na salita na madalas makita sa mga legal na dokumento o pormal na anunsyo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat **gratipikahan** ang sinumang makapagbibigay ng impormasyon tungkol sa nawawalang alahas.","translation":"Anyone who can provide information about the missing jewelry should be **rewarded**."},{"sentence":"Nais ng kumpanya na **gratipikahan** ang kanilang mga tapat na empleyado.","translation":"The company wants to **gratify** its loyal employees."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal sa beki lingo o salitang bakla na tumutukoy sa isang lalaking homoseksuwal.
etymology: A playful alteration of 'bakla,' the Filipino word for a gay man.
