original_explanation: The self-referential term for a gay man in the Philippines, derived from 'bakla'. It's part of the colorful and ever-evolving world of 'beki lingo' (gay slang). If you hear someone say "Ay, 'di ko keri, Becky!", they're talking to a friend (or to themselves) in this fabulous dialect. It's a term of camaraderie and identity within the community.
usage_notes: Primarily used within the LGBTQ+ community and by those familiar with 'beki lingo.' Can also be spelled as 'beki'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tara na, mga **becky**, rumampa na tayo sa mall!","translation":"Let's go, **gays**, let's hit the mall!"},{"sentence":"Siya ang aming go-to **becky** para sa advice sa fashion.","translation":"He's our go-to **gay friend** for fashion advice."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nag-oorganisa at kadalasang nagpopondo ng mga konsiyerto, dula, o opera; isang negosyante.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung "big boss" na nagpapatakbo ng show, parang si Mr. Krabs ng Krusty Krab pero sa totoong buhay. Sila 'yung may vision at (importante) may puhunan para gawing reality ang isang project, concert, or business venture. Think of the producers behind your favorite K-Pop group's world tour or the owner of that new milk tea shop na laging puno.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kilalang **empresaryo** ay nag-invest sa isang bagong teknolohiya.","translation":"The well-known **entrepreneur** invested in a new technology."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **empresaryo** sa likod ng matagumpay na concert na iyon?","translation":"Who was the **impresario** behind that successful concert?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolektibong termino para sa mga pag-aari ng isang tao, korporasyon, o entidad, kabilang ang lupa, bahay, salapi, at iba pang mahahalagang bagay.
original_explanation: This is your 'stuff.' All of it. From your condo in BGC and your farm in the province down to your Funko Pop collection. When people fight over a will, they're fighting over the 'ari-arian.' It's the physical proof of your 'sana all' moments.
usage_notes: 'Ari' by itself can mean property, but also has a more common, delicate meaning (genitals), so 'ari-arian' is the preferred and safer term for assets.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aagawan ng mga magkakapatid ang **ari-arian** na naiwan ng kanilang mga magulang.","translation":"The siblings are fighting over the **properties** left by their parents."},{"sentence":"Lahat ng kanyang **ari-arian** ay nakapangalan sa kanyang asawa.","translation":"All of his **assets** are in his wife's name."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan kung saan ang isang tao o bagay ay hindi nagtamo ng anumang pinsala, sugat, o sakit, pisikal man o emosyonal.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng 'hindi' (not) at 'nasaktan' (was hurt), mula sa salitang-ugat na 'sakit' (pain, hurt).
original_explanation: When you fall down the stairs in public and immediately stand up and say "Okay lang ako!" even if your knee is screaming. It's also what you tell your friends after a breakup to look strong, "Promise, **hindi ako nasaktan**." It's the emotional equivalent of putting a band-aid on a bullet wound.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa parehong pisikal at emosyonal na kalagayan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa kabutihang palad, **hindi nasaktan** ang mga pasahero sa aksidente.","translation":"Fortunately, the passengers were **unharmed** in the accident."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang magpanggap na **hindi nasaktan** sa mga sinabi nito.","translation":"He tried to pretend he was **not hurt** by what she said."}]

translation: to pilot; to steer; to fly (an aircraft)
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagmamaneho o pagpapalipad ng isang sasakyang panghimpapawid.
original_explanation: The verb form of being a 'piloto'. It's what the pilot actually does. 'Sino ang mag-pi-pilotohan ng eroplano?' means 'Who will fly the plane?'. You can also use it figuratively for leading a project or a team, like you're the one in the cockpit. 'Ikaw na ang mag-pilotohan ng project na 'to, besh!'
usage_notes: The object of the verb is the aircraft being piloted.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kaya mo bang **pilotohan** ang maliit na eroplanong ito?","translation":"Can you **pilot** this small airplane?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maikli ngunit kawili-wiling salaysay tungkol sa isang tunay na insidente o tao.
original_explanation: Basically, a short chismis with a point. It’s that quick story you tell to illustrate something, like 'Speaking of traffic, may **anekdota** ako diyan...' and then you launch into your epic tale of getting stuck on EDSA for 3 hours. It's a story that's supposed to be true and usually a little bit funny or interesting.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa parehong pormal at impormal na konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig magbahagi ng mga **anekdota** tungkol sa kanyang kabataan ang lolo ko.","translation":"My grandfather loves to share **anecdotes** about his youth."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang isang personal na **anekdota** upang ipaliwanag ang kanyang punto.","translation":"He used a personal **anecdote** to explain his point."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paniniwala at pagpapahalaga sa sariling kakayahan, katangian, at paghuhusga.
original_explanation: This is your 'Kaya ko 'to!' energy. It's the belief in yourself that lets you walk into a job interview, sing your heart out at karaoke, or slide into someone's DMs, even if you're shaking on the inside. It's the main character energy everyone's trying to manifest.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of personal development, career, and relationships. Lack of it is often linked to being 'mahina ang loob' (weak-willed).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong buuin ang iyong **tiwala sa sarili** upang magtagumpay.","translation":"You need to build your **self-confidence** to succeed."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa papuri ng kanyang amo, lumakas ang kanyang **tiwala sa sarili**.","translation":"Because of his boss's praise, his **self-confidence** grew stronger."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao, bagay, o ideya na pumapabor o naaayon sa mga prinsipyo at paniniwala ng Kristiyanismo.
original_explanation: Describes an attitude or policy that's very much aligned with Christian values. Think of it as the 'What Would Jesus Do?' filter applied to actions, rules, or even a whole political platform.
usage_notes: The prefix 'maka-' when attached to a noun or proper noun often indicates alignment, support, or being in favor of that noun (e.g., maka-Marcos, makabayan).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanilang samahan ay may mga alituntuning **makakristiyano**.","translation":"Their organization has **pro-Christian** rules."},{"sentence":"Ipinapakita niya ang **makakristiyanong** pagpapatawad.","translation":"He is showing **Christian-like** forgiveness."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging magkatabi, magkasabay, o magkaagapay sa paggalaw o posisyon.
etymology: Possibly related to "abay" (to escort, to be beside).
original_explanation: "Agapay" is how you and your bestie walk through the mall, perfectly in sync. It's how motorcycles weave through EDSA traffic, side-by-side like a synchronized dance. It’s having someone beside you, literally or figuratively, facing the same direction. #SanaAll may ka-agapay.
usage_notes: Can also function as a noun. The verb form is "umagapay" (to go alongside) and the noun for a companion is "kaagapay".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglalakad silang **agapay** sa dalampasigan.","translation":"They were walking **side by side** on the shore."},{"sentence":"Ang motorsiklo ay umagapay sa aming sasakyan.","translation":"The motorcycle went **alongside** our car."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang damdamin, kaisipan, o karanasan na napakahirap o imposibleng isalin sa mga salita.
original_explanation: That feeling when you see your crush and your brain just short-circuits. It's the "words are not enough" moment. Used to describe overwhelming joy, deep sadness, or the beauty of a sunset that your phone camera can't capture. It's when the feels are too real for vocabulary.
usage_notes: Often used for deep emotions or profound experiences. "Hindi masabi" is a simpler, more common equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang saya na nararamdaman ko ay **hindi maipahayag** sa salita.","translation":"The joy I feel is **inexpressible** in words."},{"sentence":"May mga lungkot na **hindi maipahayag** pero dinadala sa puso.","translation":"There is a sadness that is **inexpressible** but is carried in the heart."}]

translation: to make ninety; to divide into ninety parts
meaning_filipino: Gawing siyamnapu ang bilang o dami ng isang bagay; hatiin sa siyamnapung bahagi.
original_explanation: The action of making something ninety. Imagine you're counting your coins for pamasahe and you're at 85. 'Siyampuhin ko na 'to para sakto,' you say, as you look for a 5-peso coin. Or when you're dividing a huge task into 90 tiny, soul-crushing sub-tasks for your project management app.
usage_notes: A rare verb form, but grammatically logical and perfectly understandable. Usually used in contexts of counting, dividing, or reaching a target of 90.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Siyampuhin** mo na ang bayad para masara na ang usapan.","translation":"**Make** the payment **ninety** so we can close the deal."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **siyampuhin** ang mga silya para sa mga bisita.","translation":"We need to **make it ninety** chairs for the guests."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging isang martir; ang pag-aalay ng buhay o pagdanas ng matinding hirap para sa isang paniniwala, prinsipyo, o pananampalataya.
etymology: From Tagalog affix "pagka-" (denoting state or manner) + Spanish "mártir" (martyr).
original_explanation: This is the 'Level Up' version of kamatayan. It’s not just dying; it's dying for a cause—like Jose Rizal, the Gomburza priests, or your favorite hero in a historical drama. It's when your death becomes an inspiration, a symbol. It's the ultimate sacrifice that ensures you're never 'seen-zoned' by history. This entry represents the concept of 'kamatayan bilang isang martir' (death as a martyr).
usage_notes: This is the proper noun for the concept of "death as a martyr" (kamatayan bilang isang martir).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkamartir** ni Dr. Jose Rizal ay gumising sa damdaming makabayan ng mga Pilipino.","translation":"The **martyrdom** of Dr. Jose Rizal awakened the patriotic spirit of the Filipinos."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagkamartir** ay nagbigay-inspirasyon sa marami na ipagpatuloy ang laban.","translation":"His **martyrdom** inspired many to continue the fight."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sukat na katumbas ng laman ng isang kutsara.
etymology: Contraction of 'isang kutsara' (one spoon). The prefix 'sang-' means 'one whole of'. 'Kutsara' is from Spanish 'cuchara'.
original_explanation: The official measurement when your mom says 'maglagay ka ng isang kutsara' but she really means one whole serving spoon (sandok). It's supposed to be a standard measure, but in a Filipino kitchen, it's more of a suggestion.
usage_notes: Used for measurements in cooking, medicine, etc. Often written as 'sang kutsara'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magdagdag ka ng **sangkutsara**ng asukal sa kape.","translation":"Add **one tablespoon** of sugar to the coffee."},{"sentence":"Isang **sangkutsara**ng gamot lang ang inumin mo tatlong beses sa isang araw.","translation":"Just drink **one tablespoon** of the medicine three times a day."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagbibigay ng kaalaman, nagtuturo ng kasanayan, o gumagabay sa pag-aaral ng iba.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'taga-' (tagagawa), 'pag-' (nagpapangalan), at salitang-ugat na 'turo' (teach, point).
original_explanation: More than just a teacher ('guro'). This is your instructor, your mentor, the one who shows you *how* to do things. Pwedeng sa gym (your fitness instructor), sa office (the one training the new hires), or even your friend who taught you how to play that online game. They're the 'how-to' guide in human form.
usage_notes: Bagaman maaaring kasingkahulugan ng 'guro', ang 'tagapagturo' ay madalas na nagbibigay-diin sa pagtuturo ng isang partikular na kasanayan o proseso.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aming **tagapagturo** sa sayaw ay napakagaling.","translation":"Our dance **instructor** is very good."},{"sentence":"Nakinig nang mabuti ang mga bagong empleyado sa kanilang **tagapagturo**.","translation":"The new employees listened carefully to their **instructor**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng pinaniniwalaang may angking kapangyarihang itim, nagsasagawa ng pangkukulam, o may kakayahang gumawa ng kababalaghan.
original_explanation: Ang OG "Marites" na may powers. Siya yung sinisisi sa lahat ng malas sa barangay, mula sa biglang pagkapanis ng kanin hanggang sa pagkawala ng manok. Sa modern times, "buruha" na rin ang tawag mo sa ka-team mo na parang may powers para laging makaiwas sa mahirap na task. From Spanish 'bruja'.
usage_notes: Kadalasang may negatibong konotasyon at nauugnay sa mga alamat at pamahiin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa mga lumang kuwento, kinatatakutan ang mga **buruha** na nakatira sa gubat.","translation":"In old stories, **witches** who live in the forest are feared."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkubli o pag-alis sa paningin ng iba upang hindi matagpuan o makita.
original_explanation: What you do when the 'maniningil ng utang' (debt collector) is outside your house. Or when you were a kid playing 'tagu-taguan'. In the adult world, it's what your ex does after ghosting you, or what you do after an embarrassing 'send to all' text message.
usage_notes: Past tense of "magtago". The present progressive is "nagtatago".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagtago** ang bata sa ilalim ng kama.","translation":"The child **hid** under the bed."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng iskandalo, **nagtago** muna siya sa publiko.","translation":"After the scandal, he **went into hiding** from the public for a while."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubhang kaibig-ibig, kaakit-akit, o kalugud-lugod sa isang romantikong paraan.
etymology: From `ka-` + reduplication of `irog` (beloved, dear). `Irog` itself is an old Tagalog word.
original_explanation: This is some next-level, harana-worthy "lovable." It's not just "cute" or "sweet," it's so endearing it makes you want to write a poem. You wouldn't use this for a baby, but for your "sinta," "irog," or "giliw." It's the kind of word you'd find in a Florante at Laura-era love letter. Super rare in 2026, but will definitely score you points for effort.
usage_notes: A very deep and archaic word for "lovable" or "endearing," almost exclusively used in literature or romantic poetry.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga ngiti ay tunay na **kairug-irog**.","translation":"Her smiles are truly **endearing**."},{"sentence":"Sinulatan niya ng tula ang kanyang **kairug-irog** na kasintahan.","translation":"He wrote a poem for his **very lovable** sweetheart."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sasakyang may dalawang gulong na pinapaandar sa pamamagitan ng pagpedal ng sakay nito.
original_explanation: The OG eco-friendly ride. Before Grab, Angkas, or even the MRT, the bisikleta was your ticket to freedom. It's what your tito used to court your tita, and what kids in the province use to race each other after school. Now, it's the ride of choice for weekend warriors in spandex and food delivery riders navigating EDSA traffic. Also known as a "bike".
usage_notes: "Bike" is a very common informal synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Araw-araw siyang pumapasok sa opisina gamit ang kanyang **bisikleta**.","translation":"He goes to the office every day using his **bicycle**."},{"sentence":"Niregaluhan ako ng bagong **bisikleta** noong Pasko.","translation":"I was gifted a new **bicycle** last Christmas."}]

translation: to make someone behave; to straighten out
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtuturo o pagdidisiplina sa isang tao upang umayos ang pag-iisip at pag-uugali nito.
original_explanation: The ultimate goal of every Filipino parent to their 'pasaway na anak'. It's the 'I brought you into this world, I can take you out' energy, but channeled into making you a decent human being. Also what you try to do to your friend who keeps making bad life choices.
usage_notes: Can range in meaning from gentle guidance to strict disciplining. 'Tino' refers to good sense, sanity, or proper behavior.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **magpatino** ng taong ayaw magbago.","translation":"It's hard to **straighten out** a person who doesn't want to change."},{"sentence":"Ipinasok siya sa military school ng kanyang ama para **magpatino**.","translation":"His father enrolled him in a military school to **make him behave**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maliit, tuyo, at malutong na tinapay o kraker.
original_explanation: In the Philippines, a biscuit is not the fluffy scone you eat with gravy. It's the SkyFlakes, Fita, or Marie that's your go-to merienda, your palaman partner, or your emergency rations during a typhoon. It's the thing you dip in coffee until it's dangerously soggy and about to collapse. The ultimate test of reflexes.
usage_notes: Refers to what Americans would call a "cracker" or a "cookie" depending on sweetness. It does not refer to the soft, scone-like American "biscuit".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakikuha mo nga ako ng **biscuit** at kape.","translation":"Can you please get me some **crackers** and coffee."},{"sentence":"Paborito kong **biscuit** ang Fita.","translation":"My favorite **biscuit** is Fita."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gagawing pagluha at pagpapakita ng matinding damdamin tulad ng kalungkutan, sakit, o kagalakan.
original_explanation: What you do after watching Hachiko for the nth time, or when you see your phone bill after a month of mobile data. "Pag 'di nanalo ang pusta ko sa game mamaya, mag-iiyak ako."
usage_notes: Future tense of 'umiyak'. The 'mag-' prefix can imply a more intense or prolonged crying session compared to 'iiyak'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siguradong **mag-iiyak** ang bata kapag hindi mo binili ng laruan.","translation":"The child **will surely cry** if you don't buy him a toy."},{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang **mag-iiyak** diyan, wala na tayong magagawa.","translation":"Don't **cry** there anymore, there's nothing we can do."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng paggamit ng mahika o kapangyarihang sobrenatural, karaniwang may masamang intensyon, upang manakit o makaimpluwensya sa ibang tao.
etymology: From `pang-` (prefix indicating means or instrument) + `kulam` (witchcraft, hex).
original_explanation: This is the OG 'bad vibes'. Before you could block someone on social media, there was 'kulam'. It's the act of putting a hex on someone, usually involving a 'mangkukulam' (sorcerer), a doll, and some seriously bad intentions. Think of it as the ultimate passive-aggressive move, but with more chanting and less subtweeting.
usage_notes: Often associated with folk beliefs and provincial stories. It is distinct from 'barang', which is another form of Filipino witchcraft often involving insects.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming kwento tungkol sa **pangkukulam** sa mga liblib na probinsya.","translation":"There are many stories about **sorcery** in remote provinces."},{"sentence":"Pinagbibintangan siyang gumagamit ng **pangkukulam** dahil sa biglaang pagkakasakit ng kanyang kaaway.","translation":"She is being accused of using **witchcraft** because of her enemy's sudden illness."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapakamatay sa pamamagitan ng pagsasabit sa sarili sa leeg gamit ang isang lubid o katulad na bagay.
original_explanation: A very dark and serious topic. This is the act of taking one's own life by hanging. It’s a word used in news reports or very somber discussions. It's a heavy word for a heavy reality. If you or someone you know is feeling this way, please reach out for help.
usage_notes: This term is very specific and refers only to suicide by hanging. The general term for suicide is 'pagpapakamatay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iniimbestigahan ng pulisya ang kaso ng **pagbigti** na natagpuan sa lumang bahay.","translation":"The police are investigating the case of **suicide by hanging** found in the old house."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar, karaniwang isang hukay sa lupa, kung saan inililibing ang isang yumaong tao.
original_explanation: Dito nagtatapos ang lahat ng "sana all" at "edi wow" mo. Ang final resting place. Madalas bisitahin 'pag Undas para magtirik ng kandila at mag-alay ng bulaklak, at para alalahanin na hindi forever ang mobile data plan mo, parang buhay.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'libingan' (cemetery/grave).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-alay sila ng mga bulaklak sa **puntod** ng kanilang yumaong lola.","translation":"They offered flowers at the **tomb** of their deceased grandmother."},{"sentence":"Nakatayo ang isang anghel na marmol sa ibabaw ng lumang **puntod**.","translation":"A marble angel stands atop the old **grave**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malawak na lupain, karaniwang ginagamit para sa pag-aalaga ng mga hayop tulad ng baka at kabayo.
original_explanation: Think of a hacienda, but make it more cowboy. It's a huge piece of land with cows, horses, and probably a guy in a hat who says 'Howdy, partner' but in Tagalog. It’s the setting for every other Pinoy action movie where the hero has to hide out.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May malaking **rantso** ang pamilya nila sa Batangas.","translation":"Their family owns a big **ranch** in Batangas."},{"sentence":"Nagtatrabaho siya bilang tagapangalaga ng mga kabayo sa isang **rantso**.","translation":"He works as a caretaker for horses on a **ranch**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang magiliw na katawagan para sa isang ama; tatay.
original_explanation: A more 'alta' or 'sosyal' way to say 'tatay'. Often used interchangeably with 'daddy'. If your dad drives you to school in an SUV, you probably call him 'papa'. Also, the default name for the dad in many Filipino teleseryes.
usage_notes: The stress is on the second syllable (/pa-PA/), which distinguishes it from 'Papa' (/PA-pa/) for the Pope. It is an informal term of endearment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"\"Aalis na po ako, **Papa**!\"","translation":"\"I'm leaving now, **Dad**!\""},{"sentence":"Binilhan ako ng bagong cellphone ng **papa** ko.","translation":"My **dad** bought me a new cellphone."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa Araw ng mga Puso (Pebrero 14) o sa isang taong minamahal na pinadadalhan ng kard o regalo sa araw na ito.
original_explanation: Araw ng gastos! It's Valentine's Day, the day of overpriced flowers, booked-out restaurants, and immense pressure to be romantic. Kung single ka, araw din ito ng "sana all" posts. Ang "balentayn" mo ay pwedeng yung jowa mo, crush mo, or even yourself (self-love, 'di ba?).
usage_notes: Colloquial spelling of "Valentine".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang ka-**balentayn** mo ngayong taon?","translation":"Who is your **valentine** this year?"},{"sentence":"Nakatanggap siya ng maraming bulaklak noong **Balentayn**.","translation":"She received a lot of flowers on **Valentine's** Day."}]

translation: to interpret; to give meaning to
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng kahulugan, paliwanag, o interpretasyon sa isang salita, pangyayari, o konsepto.
original_explanation: This is what you do when your crush gives you mixed signals and you ask your friends, "Ano kayang ibig sabihin nito?" You're asking them to **ipakahulugan** their actions. It's the intellectual version of overthinking.
usage_notes: A more formal or profound way of saying 'ibigay ang kahulugan' (give the meaning).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **ipakahulugan** ang malalim na tula, ngunit nahirapan siya.","translation":"He tried to **interpret** the profound poem, but he struggled."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking ang trabaho ay maghatid ng mga produkto, pagkain, o pakete sa mga customer.
etymology: Mula sa mga salitang Ingles na "delivery" at "boy".
original_explanation: The modern-day hero on a motorcycle. Rain or shine, traffic or not, they bring you your milk tea, pizza, or the 11.11 haul you forgot you ordered. Always greet your **deliveryboy** with a "Salamat, kuya! Ingat!"
usage_notes: Isang napaka-karaniwang termino. Ang "rider" ay isa na ngayong mas sikat at gender-neutral na kasingkahulugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-text na ang **deliveryboy**; malapit na raw siya.","translation":"The **delivery boy** has texted; he said he's near."},{"sentence":"Nagbigay ako ng tip sa **deliveryboy** dahil umuulan nang malakas.","translation":"I gave the **delivery boy** a tip because it was raining hard."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging hindi pormal; ang kawalan ng mahigpit na alituntunin, seremonya, o pormal na pamamaraan.
original_explanation: Ito yung company culture na pwedeng naka-shorts at tsinelas ka lang sa office. O yung meeting na nagsisimula sa 'Kamusta ang weekend?' imbes na 'Good morning, team.' Impormalidad is the opposite of being stiff and stuffy; it's the chill, relaxed vibe of Filipino gatherings where everyone is 'tropa'.
usage_notes: Ang pang-uri ay 'impormal'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala ang mga Pilipino sa kanilang **impormalidad** sa pakikitungo.","translation":"Filipinos are known for their **informality** in interactions."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa **impormalidad** ng pag-uusap, naging mas komportable ang lahat na magbahagi ng kanilang opinyon.","translation":"Because of the **informality** of the conversation, everyone became more comfortable sharing their opinion."}]

meaning_filipino: Hati sa dalawang pantay na bahagi.
original_explanation: The ultimate test of friendship and siblinghood. "Pahati tayo" means we're splitting this equally, whether it's the last piece of pizza or the bill at a restaurant. It’s the principle behind "walang lamangan." But be warned, someone is always watching to make sure your half isn't bigger.
usage_notes: Can function as an adjective or adverb depending on the sentence structure.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pahati** tayo sa bayad sa kuryente.","translation":"Let's go **half and half** on the electricity bill."},{"sentence":"Binili namin ang lupa nang **pahati**.","translation":"We bought the land, **sharing the cost equally**."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang tao, bagay, o gawain na karapat-dapat sa matinding galit o pagkasuklam.
original_explanation: This describes the ultimate kontrabida. The corrupt politician, the two-timing partner, the person who cuts in line at the ATM. It's not just that you hate them; it's that their actions are objectively, universally, 'nakakagigil'-ly awful. They are hate-worthy.
usage_notes: An adjective that describes something or someone as deserving of hatred. It's a very strong and judgmental word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagtataksil sa bayan ay isang **kamuhi-muhing** krimen.","translation":"Betraying the country is a **despicable** crime."},{"sentence":"**Kamuhi-muhi** ang ginawa niyang panloloko sa mga matatanda.","translation":"His act of deceiving the elderly was **loathsome**."}]

translation: like; in the style of; Oh!
meaning_filipino: Isang salitang nagpapahayag ng pagkukumpara o pagkakatulad. Sa diyalektong Batangueño, ito ay isang panimulang ekspresyon o muletilya na nagpapahiwatig ng pagtataka o pagdidiin.
etymology: From Spanish 'a la', meaning 'in the style/manner of'. The Batangueño usage is native to the dialect.
original_explanation: Two meanings! 1) The 'parang' of the sosyals, e.g., 'Dinner, ala Solaire.' 2) The signature word of every Batangueño, used like 'uhm' or 'hey' to start a sentence. 'Ala eh, ang layo naman nire!'
usage_notes: The Batangueño usage is very specific to the region and is a strong cultural marker. The 'in the style of' usage is more common in formal, culinary, or fashion contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagluto siya ng spaghetti **ala** carbonara.","translation":"She cooked spaghetti **in the style of** carbonara."},{"sentence":"**Ala** eh, pumarine ka nga!","translation":"**Oh**, come over here! (Batangueño expression)"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit sa isang bagay bilang unan o suporta sa ulo habang nakahiga.
original_explanation: 'Yung braso ng jowa mo, 'yung bag mo sa bus, 'yung tumpok ng mga libro noong college—anything can be a pillow if you're sleepy enough. To `paunanan` is to turn any object into a temporary headrest. The ultimate act of resourcefulness for the 'antukin'.
usage_notes: Can be a verb (to use as a pillow) or a noun (a place for a pillow, though this is less common). The verb form is more frequent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **paunanan** ang mga bagong labang damit!","translation":"Don't **use** the newly laundered clothes **as a pillow**!"},{"sentence":"Pinatulog niya ang bata at **pinaunanan** sa kanyang kandungan.","translation":"She put the child to sleep and let him **use** her lap **as a pillow**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malalim na pakiramdam ng pangamba, takot, o pag-aalala tungkol sa isang masamang bagay na maaaring mangyari sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: That feeling you get on a Sunday night when you remember you have a major presentation at 8 AM on Monday. 'Yung kaba na may kasamang lungkot at takot. It's the emotional background music to a horror movie, but your life is the movie.
usage_notes: A deep, literary word for a sense of impending doom or anxiety. Not commonly used in casual conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **gulimgim** ang bumalot sa kanyang puso habang papalapit ang bagyo.","translation":"A sense of **foreboding** enveloped her heart as the storm approached."},{"sentence":"May nararamdaman siyang **gulimgim** tuwing napapadaan siya sa lumang bahay na iyon.","translation":"He feels a sense of **dread** whenever he passes by that old house."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa konteksto ng social media, ito ay ang bilang ng beses na napanood o tiningnan ng mga tao ang isang video, larawan, o anumang online content.
original_explanation: The modern-day currency of influencers and content creators. 'Yung paramihan ng views ang labanan sa TikTok at YouTube. Kapag mababa ang views, parang na-reject ka. Kapag mataas, feeling mo sikat ka na at pwede nang mag-endorso ng sabon. 'Pa-view naman ng bago kong video, guys!'
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in the context of social media and online content. The traditional meaning of 'view' (like a scenic view) is usually translated as 'tanawin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umabot na sa isang milyon ang **views** ng bago niyang dance challenge.","translation":"The **views** on her new dance challenge have reached one million."},{"sentence":"Hindi mahalaga ang **views**, ang importante ay nag-enjoy ka sa paggawa ng content.","translation":"**Views** aren't important, what matters is you enjoyed making the content."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-aanyaya sa isang tao na pumunta o sumali sa isang okasyon.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you're planning a party and making a guest list. 'Sino-sino ang kukumbidahin natin?' is the ultimate question that can either make or break friendships. It's the active form of sending out that 'kumbida'.
usage_notes: Ito ang anyong pampandiwa ng 'kumbida'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumbidahin** mo naman kami sa binyag ng anak mo.","translation":"You should **invite** us to your child's baptism."}]

translation: to become tight; to feel tight
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging masikip o ang pagdama ng paninikip, tulad ng sa damit, espasyo, o sa dibdib.
etymology: From the verb-forming prefix 'maN-' and the root 'sikip' (tight). The 'n' sound is a result of phonetic assimilation.
original_explanation: That feeling in your jeans after an unli-samgyup session. Or that feeling in your chest when you see your crush holding hands with someone else. It can be about clothes, it can be about your heart. Both are signs that you need to let go—of either the rice or the feelings.
usage_notes: Often used in its progressive form 'naninikip' to describe an ongoing sensation, such as 'naninikip ang dibdib' (my chest is tightening).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **manikip** ang dibdib niya dahil sa kaba.","translation":"His chest began **to feel tight** due to anxiety."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong isuot 'yan, baka **manikip** sa iyo pagkatapos kumain.","translation":"Don't wear that, it might **become tight** on you after eating."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang miyembro ng simbahan na hindi bahagi ng kaparian; isang taong hindi dalubhasa sa isang partikular na larangan.
original_explanation: Basically, a non-expert. In church, it's anyone who isn't a priest, pastor, or nun. In real life, it's you trying to fix the Wi-Fi router and making it worse. You're a 'laiko' in the world of IT.
usage_notes: Primarily used in religious contexts but is gaining wider use to mean a non-specialist in any field.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang papel ng mga **laiko** sa pagpapalaganap ng salita ng Diyos.","translation":"The **laity** has a big role in spreading the word of God."},{"sentence":"Para sa isang **laiko**, mahirap intindihin ang mga teknikal na termino.","translation":"For a **layman**, it is difficult to understand the technical terms."}]

translation: to give way; to be magnanimous; to yield
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay-daan, pagpapaubaya, o pagpapakita ng kabutihang-loob sa pamamagitan ng hindi paggiit sa sariling karapatan o kagustuhan para sa kapakanan ng iba.
etymology: From magpa- (causative prefix) + paraya (to give way). The deeper root might be related to 'daya' (cheat), in the sense of allowing oneself to be 'cheated' out of something for the sake of another.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'sige, sa'yo na' move. It's when you let someone else take the last piece of chicken, or when you let your ex be happy with someone else even if it hurts. To 'magparaya' is to choose peace over being right, or to let go for a greater good (or just to end the argument).
usage_notes: While 'daya' means to cheat, 'magparaya' has a positive connotation of being selfless or yielding.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Minsan, kailangan mong **magparaya** para sa kapayapaan ng pamilya.","translation":"Sometimes, you need to **give way** for the peace of the family."},{"sentence":"Nagparaya siya sa kanyang pwesto upang bigyan ng pagkakataon ang mas bata.","translation":"He **yielded** his position to give the younger one a chance."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtupad, pagganap, o pag-iral sa isang plano, gawain, o tungkulin.
etymology: From "gawa" (to do, to make). The "pag- -an" affix with reduplication of the first syllable of the root ("sa") indicates the act or process of doing something.
original_explanation: This is the "Just Do It" part of any plan. After all the brainstorming, meetings, and unli-coffee, this is when you actually start working. It's moving from "drawing" to "doing". Sa BPO, ito yung "Go Live" phase. Sa group project, ito yung part na isang tao lang talaga ang gumagawa.
usage_notes: A formal term often used in business, government, and academic contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang tamang pagpaplano para sa matagumpay na **pagsasagawa** ng proyekto.","translation":"Proper planning is important for the successful **implementation** of the project."},{"sentence":"Pinuri ang mabilis na **pagsasagawa** ng rescue operations.","translation":"The swift **performance** of the rescue operations was praised."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang magdulot ng pagkawala ng kakayahang gumalaw o kumilos ng isang bahagi o ng buong katawan; ang maging sanhi ng paghinto ng isang gawain o sistema.
original_explanation: Can be literal, like in a medical sense. But more often, you hear this in a figurative way. 'Takot na magparalisa sa'yo.' (Fear that paralyzes you). It's what happens when you have so much work to do that you just stare at your screen, unable to start. Analysis paralysis, but make it Filipino.
usage_notes: Used both literally for medical conditions and figuratively for fear, inaction, or system-wide stoppage (e.g., a strike paralyzing transportation).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang matinding takot ay maaaring **magparalisa** sa isang tao.","translation":"Intense fear can **paralyze** a person."},{"sentence":"Ang welga ay nagbadyang **magparalisa** sa transportasyon sa buong lungsod.","translation":"The strike threatened to **paralyze** transportation across the city."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdaan o paglipas ng panahon.
original_explanation: This is a more poetic way of saying "lumipas." It’s how you describe time slipping away, often with a hint of nostalgia or regret. "Ang bilis tumipas ng panahon, parang kailan lang Pasko." It's the verb for when you're reminiscing about the good old days and wondering where all the years went. It's got that #throwbackthursday vibe.
usage_notes: A less common, more literary synonym for "lumipas." Used almost exclusively for the passage of time.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming taon na ang **tumipas** mula noong huli kaming nagkita.","translation":"Many years have **passed by** since we last saw each other."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya namalayan ang oras na **tumitipas** habang nagbabasa.","translation":"She didn't notice the time that was **elapsing** while she was reading."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng ilong na pango, hindi gaanong matangos, at may malapad na tulay.
original_explanation: The classic Pinoy 'pango' nose. While some might get insecure, many embrace their sarat na ilong. It's a common feature, often a subject of friendly teasing. It's the opposite of a 'matangos na ilong' that you see in commercials for glutathione or something. It's a nose that's cute, button-like, and unapologetically Filipino.
usage_notes: A common descriptive phrase. Often shortened to just 'sarat' when referring to a nose.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong pagtawanan ang kanyang **sarat na ilong**.","translation":"Don't laugh at his **flat nose**."},{"sentence":"Sabi nila, swerte daw ang mga taong may **sarat na ilong**.","translation":"They say people with a **snub nose** are lucky."}]

translation: sheath of a banana stalk; husk
meaning_filipino: Ang panlabas na tuyong balat o dahon na bumabalot sa puno o bunga ng ilang halaman, lalo na sa saging.
original_explanation: 'Yung part ng puno ng saging na tinatanggal bago mo makuha 'yung "puso." It's like the plant's old, dry clothes. Dati, ginagawa itong pang-slide sa damuhan. Kids today will never know.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to the dried outer layers of plants like banana and abaca.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ng mga bata ang **talupak** ng saging bilang laruang bangka.","translation":"The children used the banana stalk **sheath** as a toy boat."},{"sentence":"Tuyong-tuyo na ang mga **talupak** sa puno.","translation":"The **husks** on the tree are very dry."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga haka-haka, hinuha, o palagay na hindi batay sa matibay na ebidensya.
original_explanation: This is basically just guesswork or making assumptions. It's the stuff that fuels all the chismis in the barangay. "Ayon sa wari-wari ni Marites..." means "According to the speculations of Marites..." It's thinking without proof, just pure vibes and assumptions.
usage_notes: Often used to describe unconfirmed thoughts or gossip. Less common than 'haka-haka'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puro **wari-wari** lang ang naririnig ko, wala namang katotohanan.","translation":"I'm only hearing **speculations**, there's no truth to it."},{"sentence":"Itigil na natin ang **wari-wari** at alamin ang tunay na nangyari.","translation":"Let's stop the **guesswork** and find out what really happened."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-ako sa isang mabigat na tungkulin, responsibilidad, o gastusin.
original_explanation: This is a very 'panganay' (eldest child) word. 'Bumalikat' means to shoulder a burden or responsibility, taken from 'balikat' (shoulder). It's what the eldest child does for the family's finances, what a team leader does for a project, or what a superhero does for the world. It’s about stepping up and carrying the weight.
usage_notes: A formal, figurative verb. You don't "bumalikat" a sack of rice; you "pasan" it. You "bumalikat" the cost of your sibling's education.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **bumalikat** sa lahat ng gastusin sa pagpapagamot ng kanyang ina.","translation":"He **shouldered** all the expenses for his mother's medical treatment."},{"sentence":"Handa siyang **bumalikat** ng mas malaking responsibilidad sa kumpanya.","translation":"She is ready to **take on** a bigger responsibility in the company."}]

meaning_filipino: Yupi, pipi, o durog dahil sa pagkakadiin o pagkakabagsak. Sa ibang gamit, tumutukoy sa paglabas mula sa itlog.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your heart after seeing your crush with someone else—durog at pisa. Or more literally, what happens to a can of Coke after you step on it. It's that state of being completely flattened. It can also mean 'hatched' from an egg, which is the total opposite vibe, from destruction to birth.
usage_notes: Primarily means 'crushed' or 'flattened'. A secondary, less common meaning is 'hatched' (e.g., 'kapipisa pa lang na sisiw' - a newly hatched chick).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **pisa** ang kamatis nang aksidenteng maupuan.","translation":"The tomato became **crushed** when it was accidentally sat on."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong isama sa basket ang saging na **pisa** na.","translation":"Don't include the banana that's already **flattened** in the basket."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang nakausling bahagi ng mukha sa ibaba ng bibig.
original_explanation: Your chin. The thing you rest on your hand when you're bored in a meeting or daydreaming about your next meal. Also, the feature that becomes a "double **baba**" after too many holiday feasts. No judgment.
usage_notes: Pronounced with stress on the first syllable: BA-ba. This differentiates it from its homograph 'babà' (low).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang haba naman ng **baba** mo!","translation":"Your **chin** is so long!"},{"sentence":"Nakatukod ang kanyang siko sa mesa habang hawak ang kanyang **baba**.","translation":"His elbow was propped on the table while holding his **chin**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na pinaikli mula sa "suspicious" sa Ingles, ginagamit upang ipahiwatig ang pagdududa o na mayroong kahina-hinala.
etymology: Pagpapaikli ng salitang Ingles na "suspicious," na pinasikat ng online game na "Among Us."
original_explanation: Short for 'suspicious'. Yung feeling mo kapag biglang naging super bait ng jowa mo after mag-overtime. O kaya kapag sinabi ng tropa mong '5 minutes' na lang daw siya pero nasa bahay pa. Medyo **sus**.
usage_notes: Ginagamit bilang pandamdam o pang-uri. Karaniwan sa mga Gen Z at millennial.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bakit bigla siyang umalis? **Sus**.","translation":"Why did he leave so suddenly? **Suspicious**."},{"sentence":"Ang **sus** ng mga galaw niya, parang may tinatago.","translation":"His actions are so **suspicious**, like he's hiding something."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng gulay na hugis peras, may kulay na mapusyaw na berde, at karaniwang isinasahog sa mga lutuing tulad ng tinola at ginisang gulay.
etymology: From Spanish "chayote," which itself comes from Nahuatl "chayohtli."
original_explanation: The most misunderstood vegetable. It's the backup dancer in Tinolang Manok, always there but often overshadowed by the chicken. Some say it's bland, but really, it's just a team player, absorbing the flavor of whatever it's cooked with. It's the "pwede na" of vegetables—reliable, always available in the palengke, and won't break your budget.
usage_notes: A staple vegetable in Filipino cuisine.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghiwa si nanay ng **sayote** para sa tinola.","translation":"Mom sliced some **chayote** for the tinola."},{"sentence":"Masarap din ang ginisang **sayote** na may kasamang hipon.","translation":"Sautéed **chayote** with shrimp is also delicious."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabago ng kulay tungo sa pula, karaniwang tumutukoy sa pamumula ng mukha dahil sa hiya o galit.
etymology: From `mag-` + `sa-` + `pula` (red). The `sa-` infix here indicates a change towards the color.
original_explanation: That feeling when your crush says 'hi' and your face suddenly turns into a ripe tomato. It's the physical manifestation of a 'sana all' moment turning into an 'oh no' moment.
usage_notes: More poetic or literary than the common 'mamula'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nang purihin siya ng guro, hindi niya napigilang **magsapula** ang mga pisngi.","translation":"When the teacher praised her, her cheeks couldn't help but **turn red**."},{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **magsapula** ang langit habang papalubog ang araw.","translation":"The sky began to **turn red** as the sun was setting."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagtatrabaho sa pagmimina, karaniwang sa ilalim ng lupa, upang kumuha ng mga mineral, metal, karbon, o ibang mahahalagang materyales.
original_explanation: The real-life version of the guys in Minecraft, but with way more risk and less crafting of diamond swords. These are the hardworking folks who go deep into the earth to get the gold for your jewelry and the coal for energy. A tough and often thankless job.
usage_notes: The root 'mina' means 'mine' (the place).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tatay niya ay isang **minero** sa Benguet.","translation":"His father is a **miner** in Benguet."},{"sentence":"Mapanganib ang trabaho ng mga **minero**.","translation":"The work of **miners** is dangerous."}]

translation: Taal (referring to the volcano, lake, or town)
meaning_filipino: Isang pangngalang pantangi na tumutukoy sa isang bulkan, lawa, at bayan sa lalawigan ng Batangas, Pilipinas.
etymology: Ipinangalan sa bayan ng Taal, Batangas.
original_explanation: That famous volcano inside a lake, which is on an island inside another lake on an island. Yes, it's confusing. It's the ultimate 'picture-in-picture' of Philippine geography and a favorite background for pre-nups and tourist selfies. When it's angry, everyone pays attention.
usage_notes: Palaging isinusulat na may malaking titik sa unahan. Tumutukoy sa isang tiyak na heograpikal na lokasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maganda ang tanawin ng Bulkang **Taal** mula sa Tagaytay.","translation":"The view of **Taal** Volcano from Tagaytay is beautiful."}]

meaning_filipino: May katangian na nagpapahintulot na makita ang nasa kabila o loob nito; malinaw, hayag, at walang itinatago.
original_explanation: Two meanings. First, like the cellophane on your lumpia or the glass on a Jollibee counter - you can see through it. Second, it's what politicians promise to be during elections but rarely are. It means being open, honest, and having no hidden agenda. "What you see is what you get." Yung walang "hidden charges," kumbaga.
usage_notes: Ang salitang Ingles na "transparent" ay karaniwan ding ginagamit. Ang mga katutubong katumbas ay "aninao" o "malinaw," depende sa konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng **transparente** na tela para sa kurtina.","translation":"She used a **transparent** fabric for the curtain."},{"sentence":"Dapat maging **transparente** ang gobyerno sa paggamit ng pondo ng bayan.","translation":"The government should be **transparent** in its use of public funds."}]

meaning_filipino: Ibaba o iyuko ang ulo bilang tanda ng paggalang, kalungkutan, pag-iisip, o pagsuko.
original_explanation: This is the opposite of 'itunghay'. It's what you do when your crush passes by and you suddenly find the floor very interesting. Or when your boss asks who broke the coffee machine and everyone collectively bows their head. It's the physical manifestation of 'yuko'.
usage_notes: Often implies a sense of submission, sadness, shame, or respect.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Itungo** mo ang iyong ulo bilang paggalang sa watawat.","translation":"**Bow** your head in respect for the flag."},{"sentence":"Nang mapagalitan, **itinungo** na lang niya ang kanyang ulo at hindi na nagsalita.","translation":"When scolded, he just **bowed** his head and did not speak anymore."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging walang kaalaman, pagkatuto, o impormasyon.
original_explanation: That state of blissful unawareness before you found out the 'chismis' about your officemate. It's what leads people to share fake news on Facebook. As they say, 'ignorance is bliss,' but in the age of information, 'ignoransiya' is a choice.
usage_notes: A formal word. 'Kamangmangan' is a more native Tagalog equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **ignoransiya** sa batas ay hindi maaaring gawing dahilan.","translation":"**Ignorance** of the law excuses no one."},{"sentence":"Labanan natin ang **ignoransiya** sa pamamagitan ng tamang edukasyon.","translation":"Let's fight **ignorance** through proper education."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging masaya, maligaya, o pagkakaroon ng kagalakan at kasiyahan.
original_explanation: This is the goal. The 'Sana All' feeling. The opposite of 'sawi'. It's that payday, long weekend, 13th-month-pay, 'kinilig-kay-crush' kind of feeling. It's the 'saya' that makes life worth living, even with all the traffic and BPO night shifts. As a noun, it means happiness.
usage_notes: Pronunciation is key. /SA-ya/ is the skirt, /sa-YA/ is the feeling. The adjective form is 'masaya'. As a noun, it means 'happiness' or 'joy'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Anong laking **saya** ang nadarama ko ngayon!","translation":"What great **happiness** I feel right now!"},{"sentence":"Talagang **masaya** ang Pasko sa Pilipinas.","translation":"Christmas in the Philippines is truly **happy**."}]

translation: the act of striking or lashing
meaning_filipino: Ang malakas na pagpalo, pagtama, o pagpukpok ng isang bagay sa iba, na karaniwang lumilikha ng ingay.
original_explanation: Think of the sound of waves crashing on the shore ('paghampas ng alon') or your mom's hand getting dangerously close to the walis tingting when you've been a pasaway. It's that sharp, impactful strike. Can be literal (a whip) or metaphorical (the lash of fate).
usage_notes: Can refer to the action itself or the sound produced by the action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malakas ang **paghampas** ng alon sa dalampasigan.","translation":"The **crashing** of the waves on the shore is strong."},{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **paghampas** ng sinturon sa sahig.","translation":"I heard the **lashing** of the belt on the floor."}]

translation: the act of identifying; referring; specifying
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagkilala, pagbanggit, o pagturo sa isang partikular na tao, bagay, o konsepto.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `pag-` at sa salitang ugat na `tukoy` (pagturo o pagbanggit sa isang bagay).
original_explanation: When your friend says "yung ano..." and you have to play detective to figure out what "ano" they're talking about. That whole process is 'pagtukoy'. It's pointing someone out in a crowd, citing your sources in a thesis, or specifying which Jollibee branch you want to meet at. It's the opposite of being vague. Precision is key!
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang tamang **pagtukoy** sa sanhi ng problema.","translation":"The correct **identification** of the problem's cause is important."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng empleyado sa isang restawran o kainan na ang trabaho ay kumuha ng order ng mga kostumer at maghatid ng pagkain at inumin.
original_explanation: Siya yung "Ate" na tinatawag mo sa Jollibee o sa karinderya. Laging may dalang ballpen at maliit na notepad, at may ngiting handang tumanggap ng order mo kahit gaano pa ito kakomplikado ("extra rice, no onions, less salt, more sabaw, please"). Sila ang dahilan kung bakit kumpleto ang order mo. Pro tip: Maging mabait sa kanila, baka dagdagan nila ang gravy mo.
usage_notes: Tulad ng "waiter," malawakang ginagamit ang salitang Ingles. Ang katumbas na "tagapagsilbi" ay gender-neutral ngunit mas pormal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinanong ng **waitress** kung may order pa kami.","translation":"The **waitress** asked if we had any more orders."},{"sentence":"Mabibilis kumilos ang mga **waitress** sa sikat na kainang iyon.","translation":"The **waitresses** at that popular eatery move quickly."}]

meaning_filipino: Bawat isa sa labindalawang alagad na pinili ni Hesukristo upang ipalaganap ang kanyang mga aral. Sa malawak na kahulugan, isang masigasig na tagapagtaguyod ng isang partikular na patakaran, ideya, o layunin.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "apóstol", mula sa Latin na "apostolus", mula sa Griyegong "apóstolos" (pinadala).
original_explanation: Basically, Jesus's original boy band—the OG 12. Today, you can be an 'apostol' of something else, like being an 'apostle of K-Pop' because you converted your whole barkada to stan a new group, or an 'apostle of minimalist living' who preaches the gospel of Muji and Uniqlo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si San Pedro ay isa sa mga **apostol** ni Hesus.","translation":"Saint Peter is one of the **apostles** of Jesus."},{"sentence":"Itinuturing siyang isang **apostol** ng malinis na pamamahala.","translation":"He is considered an **apostle** of clean governance."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na proseso ng pagboto upang pumili ng mga opisyal ng pamahalaan.
original_explanation: That magical time in the Philippines when streets are plastered with faces, jingles are catchier than any pop song, and everyone suddenly becomes a political analyst on Facebook. It's the ultimate 'piliin mo ako' contest, but for the whole country.
usage_notes: The common, modern spelling. The native Tagalog equivalent is "halalan". "Eleksiyon" is an older spelling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang iboboto mo sa darating na **eleksyon**?","translation":"Who will you vote for in the upcoming **election**?"},{"sentence":"Naging mainit ang kampanya para sa lokal na **eleksyon**.","translation":"The campaign for the local **election** became heated."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng iskoba upang linisin, kuskusin, o alisin ang dumi sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: That intense cleaning action your mom does on the bathroom floor that sounds like she's fighting a mortal enemy. To iskobahin is not just to brush; it's to scrub with purpose, with vigor, with the power of a thousand angry ancestors, until the tiles are sparkling clean.
usage_notes: Refers to scrubbing with a coarse brush (iskoba), not a toothbrush (sepilyo) or hairbrush (suklay).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **iskobahin** nang maigi ang sahig para matanggal ang mantsa.","translation":"You need **to brush** the floor well to remove the stain."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan o kasangkapan na ginagamit sa paglalagay ng trangka o pagsasara nang mahigpit sa isang pinto, bintana, o tarangkahan.
original_explanation: This is your anti-Marites security system. It's the piece of wood, metal bar, or any random object you use to double-lock the door when you hear a spooky noise at 2 AM. It's the low-tech version of a deadbolt, but with more 'bahala na' energy. The prefix 'pan-' indicates it's 'for' or 'used for' something, in this case, 'trangka' (bolt).
usage_notes: 'Pan-' is a prefix meaning 'for the purpose of' or 'instrument for'. The root word is 'trangka' (latch/bolt).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng isang makapal na kahoy bilang **pantrangka** sa pinto ng bodega.","translation":"He used a thick piece of wood as a **latch** for the warehouse door."},{"sentence":"Nawala ang susi kaya **pantrangka** na lang muna ang inilagay nila.","translation":"The key was lost, so they just put a **latch** for now."}]

translation: Boiled dish (usually beef or pork with vegetables)
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng lutuing Pilipino na kung saan ang karne (karaniwang baka o baboy) ay pinakukuluan nang matagal kasama ang mga gulay tulad ng repolyo, patatas, at saging na saba.
etymology: From 'laga' (to boil), referring to the dish made by boiling.
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino comfort food for a rainy day. It's that simple, brothy, boiled meat dish that makes you feel like your lola is giving you a warm hug. It's what you cook when you're too lazy for a complicated recipe but still want something hearty.
usage_notes: As a noun, this refers to the dish itself. Common variations include 'Nilagang Baka' (Boiled Beef) and 'Nilagang Baboy' (Boiled Pork).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong ulam ang **nilaga** na may mainit na kanin at patis na may sili.","translation":"My favorite dish is **nilaga** with hot rice and fish sauce with chili."},{"sentence":"Nagpaluto si nanay ng **nilaga** dahil umuulan.","translation":"Mom had **nilaga** cooked because it's raining."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbababa o pag-aalis ng kargamento mula sa isang sasakyan; ang paglilipat ng datos mula sa isang malaking sistema patungo sa isang lokal na aparato.
original_explanation: This is what you do after a massive online shopping haul—`deskarga` all the boxes from the delivery kuya's motorcycle. It's also what happens when your phone memory is crying because you just downloaded a 10GB game. Unloading baggage, literal or digital.
usage_notes: Commonly used in contexts of shipping, logistics, and digital technology (downloading).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong mag-**deskarga** ng mga sako ng bigas mula sa trak.","translation":"Help me **unload** the sacks of rice from the truck."},{"sentence":"Ang bagal ng **deskarga** ko ng file na ito, mahina yata ang internet.","translation":"My **download** of this file is so slow, I think the internet is weak."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagyupi o paglukot sa isang bagay, tulad ng papel, sa pamamagitan ng pagpisil nito nang mariin.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa mo sa love letter galing sa ex mo. You kuyumusin it into a ball bago mo itapon sa basurahan with feelings. It's the act of angrily crumpling something.
usage_notes: Implies a more forceful and often emotional act of crumpling compared to 'lukutin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang inis, ginawa niyang **kuyumusin** ang papel at itinapon.","translation":"Out of extreme annoyance, he proceeded to **crumple** the paper and threw it away."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **kuyumusin** ang damit, bagong plantsa lang 'yan.","translation":"Don't **crush** the clothes, they were just newly ironed."}]

translation: full of holes; perforated; riddled with holes
meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang bagay na may maraming butas, sira, o mga puwang.
etymology: Nagmula sa pag-uulit ng salitang 'butas' (hole) upang ipahiwatig ang pagiging marami.
original_explanation: Parang kalsada sa EDSA after a long week, o yung paborito mong t-shirt na pantulog. It's something that has so many holes, it looks like it went through a cheese grater. Pwede ring estado ng wallet mo bago mag-sweldo.
usage_notes: The repetition of 'butas' emphasizes the multiplicity and distribution of holes throughout an object.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Butas-butas** na ang payong kaya't basang-basa kami sa ulan.","translation":"The umbrella was **full of holes**, so we got soaked in the rain."},{"sentence":"Ang keso ay **butas-butas**, na siyang katangian ng Swiss cheese.","translation":"The cheese is **riddled with holes**, which is a characteristic of Swiss cheese."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagtatrabaho at karaniwang naninirahan sa tahanan ng kanyang pinaglilingkuran upang tumulong sa mga gawaing-bahay.
etymology: Contraction of 'kasama sa bahay' (companion in the house).
original_explanation: Your home's COO (Chief Operating Officer). Sila ang dahilan kung bakit hindi mukhang disaster area ang kwarto mo at may pagkain ka pa rin kahit puro ka na lang 'add to cart'. Respect and fair wages are a must! Sila ang tunay na MVP.
usage_notes: The preferred and more respectful term over 'katulong' (helper) or 'muchacha' (maid). The "Batas Kasambahay" (Republic Act No. 10361) is a law that protects their rights.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabait ang aming **kasambahay** at itinuturing na namin siyang pamilya.","translation":"Our **house helper** is kind and we already consider her as family."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga na ibigay ang tamang sahod at benepisyo para sa mga **kasambahay**.","translation":"It's important to provide the correct salary and benefits for **domestic workers**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang hiram na bulalas na nagpapahayag ng pagkagulat, pag-aalala, o bahagyang pagkatakot, lalo na sa isang alanganing o hindi kaaya-ayang sitwasyon.
original_explanation: The go-to reaction when you see your ex with a new partner, check your bank account after a 12.12 sale, or accidentally send a screenshot back to the person you screenshotted it from. It’s the polite way of saying 'Oh, that's bad' or 'Awkward...'
usage_notes: Used extensively in informal Taglish conversations, both online and offline.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Yikes**, ang mahal pala ng bill natin sa kuryente!","translation":"**Yikes**, our electricity bill is so expensive!"},{"sentence":"Sinabi niya 'yun sa harap ng boss niya? **Yikes**.","translation":"He said that in front of his boss? **Yikes**."}]

translation: to stay permanently; to settle down
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapasya na manatili o manirahan sa isang lugar nang pangmatagalan at hindi na umalis.
original_explanation: This is the opposite of "wanderlust." It's when you finally find a place—or a person—and decide, "Dito na ako." It's the ultimate act of settling down, whether it's moving into your own house, accepting a permanent job, or finally updating your relationship status to "In a Relationship" and meaning it.
usage_notes: Often implies a conscious decision to end a period of moving or instability. Connotes stability and permanence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos maglakbay sa iba't ibang bansa, nagpasya siyang **magpapirmi** sa Pilipinas.","translation":"After traveling to different countries, she decided to **stay permanently** in the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Gusto na niyang **magpapirmi** sa isang trabaho para sa katatagan ng kanyang pamilya.","translation":"He wants to **settle down** in one job for the stability of his family."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kataga na nagpapahayag ng pagkagulat, pagkatuklas, o pagkaunawa sa isang bagay na hindi dati alam o inaasahan.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'plot twist' word. It's the sound of your expectations crashing into reality. 'Akala ko single siya, may asawa na **pala**.' (I thought he was single, it turns out he's married). Use this when something dawns on you.
usage_notes: This particle often appears after the subject or verb and conveys a sense of surprise or new realization. Its meaning is highly contextual.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ikaw **pala** ang nanalo sa raffle!","translation":"**So** it was you who won the raffle!"},{"sentence":"Ang hirap **pala** ng exam, hindi ako nakapag-aral nang maigi.","translation":"The exam was **apparently** hard, I wasn't able to study well."},{"sentence":"Nandito lang **pala** sa bulsa ko ang hinahanap kong susi.","translation":"The key I was looking for was in my pocket all along, **it turns out**."}]

translation: to file (with a tool); to smoothen
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggamit ng kikil (isang kasangkapang bakal) upang pakinisin, patalasin, o hubugin ang isang matigas na bagay tulad ng metal o kahoy.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'kilkil' (file, the tool).
original_explanation: This is the OG, literal meaning. Think of a 'panday' (blacksmith) or a 'karpintero' (carpenter) using a metal file to sharpen a blade or smoothen a piece of wood. It's a job that requires patience and precision, unlike its more infamous slang meaning.
usage_notes: Ito ang literal na kahulugan na nauugnay sa pagkakarpintero o paggawa ng metal. Huwag ipagkamali sa kolokyal na kahulugan nito na 'mangotong'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang karpintero ay **kumikil** ng kahoy upang maging makinis ito.","translation":"The carpenter is **filing** the wood to make it smooth."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagsasaad na kasisilang o kaikitatag lamang ng isang bagay, tulad ng isang organisasyon o pundasyon.
original_explanation: That "new business" smell. Like your friend's online shop that was just launched yesterday, or a new relationship that's still in the "honeymoon phase." It's the "just started" status of anything.
usage_notes: Part of the `ka-` + (reduplicated first syllable of root) verb form indicating a very recent action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Katatag** pa lang ng aming grupo, kaya nangangailangan kami ng suporta.","translation":"Our group was **just founded**, so we need support."},{"sentence":"Ang samahan ay **katatag** lamang noong isang buwan.","translation":"The organization was **just established** only last month."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng kakayahan, kapangyarihan, o pagkakataon na isakatuparan o tapusin ang isang gawain o kilos.
original_explanation: The ultimate answer to 'Kaya mo ba?' (Can you do it?). When you finally fix that leaky faucet using only YouTube tutorials and a prayer, you can proudly say, 'Nays! Na-`magawa` ko rin!' It's the feeling of accomplishment when you overcome a challenge, whether it's a work deadline or assembling IKEA furniture.
usage_notes: This verb combines the concept of 'doing' (gawa) with 'ability' (the 'ma-' prefix). Often used to express capability or success in completing a task.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **magawa** ko lahat ng takdang-aralin ko ngayong gabi.","translation":"I hope I'll **be able to do** all my homework tonight."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko **magawa** ang pinapagawa mo dahil kulang ang mga materyales.","translation":"I **can't do** what you're asking because the materials are insufficient."}]

translation: to conquer; to occupy; to cover
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-angkin, pagkontrol, o pag-okupa sa isang lugar, teritoryo, o tao sa pamamagitan ng lakas o kapangyarihan. Maaari ding tumukoy sa pagsaklaw sa isang paksa o espasyo.
etymology: Mula sa "sakop" (jurisdiction, territory, under one's power).
original_explanation: Parang yung ginawa ng Spain sa Pinas for 333 years. Or sa mas modernong take, yung ginagawa ng isang K-Pop group sa buong mundo—world domination! Pwede rin itong yung pag-take over ng isang tao sa buong kama, wala ka nang space matulog. That's being "sinakop".
usage_notes: Ang "sakop" (noun) ay ang teritoryo. Ang "sakupin" (verb) ay ang aksyon ng pag-angkin dito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matagal na panahong **sinakop** ng mga dayuhan ang Pilipinas.","translation":"The Philippines was **conquered** by foreigners for a long time."},{"sentence":"Layunin ng diskusyon na **sakupin** ang lahat ng mahahalagang paksa.","translation":"The discussion aims to **cover** all important topics."}]

meaning_filipino: Kumilos nang napakabilis; humagibis. Maaari ring tumukoy sa tunog ng mabilis na paggalaw sa hangin.
original_explanation: That feeling when the jeepney driver suddenly channels his inner F1 driver and 'pumaspas' to beat the red light. It's the sound of a whip, the blur of a motorcycle on the highway, or you frantically typing to meet a deadline. It's speed, baby!
usage_notes: Can refer to fast movement or the swishing sound produced by it.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pumaspas** ang motorsiklo sa EDSA kaya nahuli ng enforcer.","translation":"The motorcycle **sped** along EDSA so it was caught by the traffic enforcer."},{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **pumaspas** na hangin bago bumuhos ang malakas na ulan.","translation":"I heard the wind that **swished** by before the heavy rain poured."}]

translation: A person who is easily pleased or is happy with simple things.
meaning_filipino: Isang taong madaling mapasaya o kuntento na sa mga simpleng bagay.
original_explanation: The feeling you get when your Shopee/Lazada package arrives, when you get the window seat on the bus, or when there's free coffee at the office. You declare, 'I'm a happy kid!' It's the adult version of getting a lollipop. It signifies being happy with small, simple joys.
usage_notes: Used to express simple, immediate happiness, often over something small or unexpected.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binigyan lang ako ng libreng dessert, **happy kid** na ako.","translation":"They just gave me free dessert, I'm already a **happy kid**."},{"sentence":"Basta may milk tea, **happy kid** na 'yan.","translation":"As long as there's milk tea, she's a **happy kid**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kumpol ng mga bulaklak na magkakasamang itinali at karaniwang ginagamit bilang regalo o palamuti.
original_explanation: The Filipino way of saying "bouquet." It's what you give your crush on Valentine's Day, what the bride holds walking down the aisle, or what you buy for your mom on Mother's Day. Pro-tip: the price of a bukey magically triples in February.
usage_notes: A direct loanword, commonly used and understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatanggap siya ng isang malaking **bukey** ng mga rosas.","translation":"She received a large **bouquet** of roses."},{"sentence":"Magkano ang isang **bukey** para sa Araw ng mga Puso?","translation":"How much is a **bouquet** for Valentine's Day?"}]

translation: to cause to whiz or whistle through the air
meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng isang matinis at mabilis na tunog sa pamamagitan ng pagpapatama o pagpapadulas ng isang bagay sa hangin nang may bilis.
original_explanation: This is the sound effect verb you never knew you needed. When a superhero flies by really fast? Haginit! When you whip a 'latigo' (a whip)? That's pahaginitin. When a car speeds past you on SLEX and it makes that 'whoosh' sound? That's the sound of haginit. It’s the action of making that sharp, swift, cutting-through-the-air sound.
usage_notes: Onomatopoeic in nature. Used to describe the action that creates a whizzing sound.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **pahaginitin** ang latigo sa ere.","translation":"He tried to **make the whip whiz** in the air."},{"sentence":"Pinapangarap ng bata na **pahaginitin** ang kanyang saranggola sa himpapawid.","translation":"The child dreamed of **making his kite whiz** through the sky."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang magbigay ng paliwanag o klaripikasyon tungkol sa isang bagay sa hinaharap.
etymology: ma- (ability) + i- (object focus) + pa- (causative) + li- (future tense repetition) + liwanag (light/clarity)
original_explanation: This is what you say when you're caught in an awkward situation and need time to craft the perfect excuse. "Bakit late ka na naman?" "Uhm... **maipaliliwanag** ko 'to, promise!" It's the verbal equivalent of "It's a long story" or "I'll tell you later."
usage_notes: This is the future tense. 'Maipapaliwanag' is a more common, slightly less formal variant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, **maipaliliwanag** ko ang lahat pagdating ng tamang panahon.","translation":"Don't worry, I **will be able to explain** everything when the right time comes."},{"sentence":"Hindi mo **maipaliliwanag** ang iyong pagliban sa klase kung wala kang katibayan.","translation":"You **won't be able to explain** your absence from class if you don't have proof."}]

translation: clam (specifically, a type of small freshwater clam)
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maliit na molusko na may dalawang kabibe, karaniwang matatagpuan sa mga ilog at iba pang anyong-tubig-tabang.
original_explanation: Not the fancy-schmancy clams you get in a pasta vongole. This is the humble palengke clam. You buy a bag for cheap, throw it in a pot with some ginger, lemongrass, and maybe some malunggay, and you've got a simple, comforting soup. It's the comfort food of river towns.
usage_notes: Refers to a specific type of bivalve, Marsh Clam (Batissa violacea), often used in soups like 'sinabawang tulya'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si Nanay ng isang kilong **tulya** sa palengke para gawing sinabawan.","translation":"Mom bought a kilo of **clams** at the market to make a broth soup."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang **tulya** kapag sariwa at bagong huli.","translation":"**Clams** are delicious when they are fresh and newly caught."}]

meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng espesyal na pansin o gawing pangunahing atraksyon ang isang tao, bagay, o kaganapan.
original_explanation: To put something in the spotlight. Like when a vlogger features a new cafe, or when a news program highlights a person's success story. 'Itatampok sa MMK ang kwento ng buhay niya.' (His life story will be featured on MMK.)
usage_notes: Commonly used in media, arts, and marketing to mean 'to give prominence to'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pelikula ay naglalayong **itampok** ang kagandahan ng mga tanawin sa Palawan.","translation":"The film aims to **feature** the beauty of the scenery in Palawan."},{"sentence":"Napili siyang **itampok** sa susunod na isyu ng magasin.","translation":"She was chosen to be **featured** in the next issue of the magazine."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggawa sa isang tao o bagay na maging biktima; ang manakit, manlinlang, o manamantala.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you fall for a '2 gives' text scam or when your friend 'borrows' your charger and it magically disappears. Ikaw ang na-hassle, ikaw ang talo. You've been victimized. Ayan, **bumiktima** na naman 'yung scammer sa lola mo.
usage_notes: Actor-focus verb in the completed aspect. Present: bumibiktima. Future: bibiktima. The object-focus form 'biktamahin' is also common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumiktima** na naman ang mga magnanakaw sa aming barangay kagabi.","translation":"The thieves **victimized** our village again last night."},{"sentence":"Maraming Pilipino ang **bumiktima** sa investment scam na iyon.","translation":"Many Filipinos **fell victim** to that investment scam."}]

translation: to get a gash/scratch (on the face)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng gasgas o malalim na galos, partikular na sa mukha, na kadalasang resulta ng isang sakuna o away.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you lose a fight with a cat, or a toddler with sharp nails, or you trip and face-plant on the pavement. It's a very specific kind of "sugat" (wound) that's more of a scratch or gash, usually on your face. "Anyare sa'yo? Bakit ka may bangas? Nakipag-away ka na naman sa pusa?"
usage_notes: While it can refer to a gash anywhere, it's most strongly associated with one on the face.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-ingat ang bata sa pag-akyat ng puno para hindi siya **magbangas**.","translation":"The child was careful climbing the tree so he wouldn't **get a gash**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang makipag-away, baka **magbangas** ka lang sa mukha.","translation":"Don't get into a fight, you might just **get a scratch** on your face."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pariralang balbal na katumbas ng "biro lang," na kadalasang idinurugtong sa isang pahayag upang bawiin ito sa pabirong paraan, na may halong sarkasmo.
etymology: A hybrid of the Tagalog slang "eme" and the English word "not", popularized in online culture. It mirrors the structure of "charot not".
original_explanation: The classic "NOT!" from the 90s, but make it Pinoy Gen Z. You say something, then immediately take it back with "eme not". It’s the verbal equivalent of the uno reverse card. "I'll treat you all to dinner... eme not!" Used for maximum comedic effect and to crush your friends' hopes and dreams in a funny way.
usage_notes: Almost always used for humor or sarcasm.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-aaral na ako nang mabuti... **eme not**!","translation":"I'm going to study hard now... **just kidding, not**!"},{"sentence":"Libre ko na 'to... **eme not**, bayad-bayad din 'pag may time.","translation":"This is on me... **just kidding, not**, pay up when you have the time."}]

translation: to host a banquet; to have a banquet thrown
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-organisa o pagpondo ng isang malaking salu-salo o handaan para sa maraming tao.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "I'm treating everyone" move. You don't just buy lunch, you *magpabangkete*. It's for big celebrations like winning the lottery, getting a huge promotion, or your anak finally graduating. It’s a flex, fiesta-style.
usage_notes: Implies a large, formal, and often expensive feast.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagpabangkete** ang alkalde para sa mga bumisita mula sa sister city nila.","translation":"The mayor **hosted a banquet** for the visitors from their sister city."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malapad at mataas na pader na nagsisilbing depensa, karaniwang pumapalibot sa isang lungsod o kuta.
original_explanation: "Muralya" is like "muog" but specifically for the WALLS. Think the Great Wall of China or the walls of Intramuros. It's a big, defensive wall. In hugot terms, "muralya" is the emotional wall you've built around your heart, so high and thick that even a 5-star general (or a very persistent suitor) would have a hard time getting through.
usage_notes: A specific architectural and historical term. Often used interchangeably with 'pader' in literary contexts but 'muralya' implies a grander, defensive purpose.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga turista ay namamasyal sa ibabaw ng makasaysayang **muralya** ng Intramuros.","translation":"The tourists are walking on top of the historic **walls** of Intramuros."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng mga kaaway na sirain ang **muralya** ng lungsod.","translation":"The enemies tried to destroy the city's **rampart**."}]

translation: to be spilled; to be poured accidentally
meaning_filipino: Aksidenteng matapon o dumaloy palabas mula sa isang lalagyan, karaniwan ay tumutukoy sa likido o butil.
original_explanation: That mini-panic when you knock over your cup of coffee on your laptop. Or when you're carrying a bag of rice from the palengke and it has a hole. 'Ay, nabubo!' is the official cry. It's the reason why we say 'Sayang...' a lot.
usage_notes: Used for accidental spilling of liquids (water, coffee) or granular items (rice, salt).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka at baka **mabubo** ang mainit na sabaw.","translation":"Be careful or the hot soup might **be spilled**."},{"sentence":"**Nabubo** ang isang sakong bigas sa kalsada.","translation":"A sack of rice **was spilled** on the road."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mamula-mulang kayumangging patong na nabubuo sa ibabaw ng bakal o asero dahil sa oksihenasyon, lalo na kapag nababad sa hangin at halumigmig.
original_explanation: That reddish-brown stuff that appears on your gate after a rainy season, or on old tools you forgot in the garage. It's the metal equivalent of getting old and wrinkly. Parang 'yung feelings mo for your ex, nagkakalawang na, hindi na kasing-kinang ng dati.
usage_notes: Can also be used metaphorically to mean something has become dull, old, or out of practice (e.g., 'kinakalawang na ang utak').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno na ng **kalawang** ang lumang bisikleta ni Lolo.","translation":"Grandpa's old bicycle is full of **rust**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bansa na matatagpuan sa silangang Europa at hilagang Asya, na siyang pinakamalaking bansa sa buong mundo batay sa lawak ng lupain.
original_explanation: The largest country in the world, where it's so cold your tears can freeze. It's the place where the Kremlin is, and it's famous for its ballet, literature, and for being a major player on the world stage.
usage_notes: The standard Filipino name for the country Russia.
