usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglakbay sila sa **Rusya** noong nakaraang taglamig.","translation":"They traveled to **Russia** last winter."},{"sentence":"Ang Moscow ang kabisera ng **Rusya**.","translation":"Moscow is the capital of **Russia**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na pangako o kasiguruhan, karaniwang nakasulat, na ang isang bagay ay may tiyak na kalidad at kung masira ay aayusin o papalitan. Maaari rin itong tumukoy sa isang bagay na isinasanla bilang paniguro sa isang utang.
original_explanation: This is the 'resibo' or 'warranty card' you get when you buy a new appliance. It's your 'I-told-you-so' card when the item breaks down after a week. It’s the assurance you need, parang 'yung assurance na hinihingi mo sa kanya pero 'di maibigay-bigay. Pwede ring collateral, 'yung isasanla mo 'pag gipit.
usage_notes: Can mean 'warranty' for products or 'collateral' for loans.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May isang taong **garantiya** ang binili naming telebisyon.","translation":"The television we bought has a one-year **warranty**."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang titulo ng lupa bilang **garantiya** sa kanyang utang.","translation":"He used the land title as **collateral** for his loan."}]

translation: to be carried away by the current
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtangay o pagpapadala ng agos ng tubig.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your tsinelas when you swim in the river or at the beach. It's also a metaphor for life: "Huwag kang magpa-ianod sa masamang impluwensya." (Don't get carried away by bad influences). It’s the passive version of going with the flow, where the flow takes you somewhere you didn't plan.
usage_notes: This is an object-focus verb. The subject is the thing being acted upon by the current (agos).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **ianod** ng baha ang mga alaga mong hayop.","translation":"Don't let your pets **be carried away by the flood**."},{"sentence":"Maraming basura ang **iniaanod** patungo sa karagatan.","translation":"A lot of trash is **being carried away by the current** towards the ocean."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na isinama o inilakip sa isang sulat o dokumento.
etymology: From ka- + lakip + -an, meaning 'that which is enclosed with'.
original_explanation: It's the OG 'attachment' before email existed. That piece of paper you fold neatly inside a greeting card? That's the *kalakpan*. It's the physical version of `attachment.zip`.
usage_notes: Primarily used in formal writing, especially for physical letters or documents. It is less common in digital communication.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa loob ng sobre ang liham at ang **kalakpan** na litrato.","translation":"Inside the envelope are the letter and the **attached** photo."},{"sentence":"Pakihanap ang **kalakpan** na resibo para sa ating ulat.","translation":"Please find the **enclosed** receipt for our report."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang napakalaking mamalyang pandagat na kabilang sa orden ng Cetacea.
original_explanation: That giant sea creature from "Free Willy". Also, a term your brutally honest tita might use to describe someone who gained weight over the holidays. "Hala, tumaba ka! Para ka nang balyena!" Ouch.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakasuwerteng makakita ng isang **balyena** sa gitna ng karagatan.","translation":"It is very lucky to see a **whale** in the middle of the ocean."},{"sentence":"Ang butanding ay isang uri ng pating, hindi isang **balyena**.","translation":"The whale shark is a type of shark, not a **whale**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkakaroon ng kinikilingan o hindi pagiging patas sa paghatol o pagpapasya.
original_explanation: This is what you accuse the referee of when your favorite basketball team is losing. It's when your mom gives the bigger piece of chicken to your sibling. It's the state of not being objective, of having a favorite. #NoToFavoritism pero 'pag pabor sa'yo, okay lang.
usage_notes: A compound noun phrase often used in formal contexts like law, journalism, and academics to describe a lack of objectivity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inakusahan ang hukom ng **pagka-may-pinapanigan** dahil sa kanyang ugnayan sa akusado.","translation":"The judge was accused of **bias** because of his connection to the accused."},{"sentence":"Dapat iwasan ng mga mamamahayag ang anumang uri ng **pagka-may-pinapanigan** sa kanilang pag-uulat.","translation":"Journalists must avoid any form of **partiality** in their reporting."}]

translation: to have someone/something be run over
meaning_filipino: Hayaan o maging sanhi na masagasaan ng isang sasakyan ang isang tao, hayop, o bagay.
original_explanation: This is a dark, telenovela-level word. It's when the kontrabida tells her driver, "Ipasagasa mo 'yan!" referring to the poor bida. It means to deliberately cause someone to be run over. Not a word you use when asking for a ride.
usage_notes: This is a causative verb. The subject of the sentence is the one causing the action of running over, not the one doing the driving. Often used with the prefix 'i-' (ipasagasa).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May masamang-loob na nagtangkang **ipasagasa** ang aso sa kalsada.","translation":"An evil person attempted **to have the dog run over** on the street."},{"sentence":"Bakit mo **pinasagasa** ang bisikleta ko?","translation":"Why did you **have my bike run over**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kumukuha ng mga litrato o larawan, bilang isang propesyon o libangan.
original_explanation: The person you hire for your wedding, debut, or binyag who tells you to "smile!" a hundred times. In the modern era, it's also your friend who has a nice camera and an eye for the 'gram. Sila 'yung laging wala sa group picture kasi sila 'yung taga-kuha. "Paki-picture naman kami, paps!"
usage_notes: Ang termino ay karaniwang gender-neutral sa paggamit, ngunit maaaring tukuyin bilang "potograpo" (lalaki) at "potograpa" (babae) kung kinakailangan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang sikat na **potograpo** ang kinuha para sa kanilang kasal.","translation":"A famous **photographer** was hired for their wedding."},{"sentence":"Laging dala ng **potograpo** ang kanyang kamera saan man siya magpunta.","translation":"The **photographer** always brings his camera wherever he goes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, karaniwang babae, na nangingibabaw, umaagaw ng atensyon, o higit na magaling kaysa sa iba sa isang partikular na sitwasyon o pagtatanghal.
etymology: From Tagalog 'kabog' (to upstage) + Spanish suffix '-era' (feminine doer).
original_explanation: A 'kabogera' is that person who walks into a room and all eyes are on them. They effortlessly outshine everyone else, whether it's with their outfit, talent, or wit. Think Anne Curtis or Vice Ganda on any given day. They don't just join the party; they *are* the party. The male version is 'kabogero'. Derived from 'kabog'.
usage_notes: A modern slang term, very popular in pop culture, fashion, and LGBTQ+ circles. Can also function as a noun ('Siya ay isang kabogera').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Talagang **kabogera** ang nanalong Miss Universe sa kanyang pagrampa.","translation":"The Miss Universe winner was a total **showstopper** during her walk."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang papayag na matalbugan, maging **kabogera** ka!","translation":"Don't let them overshadow you, be a **scene-stealer**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng pagiging kalmado at hindi nakakaramdam ng kaba, lalo na sa isang sitwasyon na karaniwang nakakapagdulot nito.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng 'hindi' (not) at 'ninenerbiyos' (is getting nervous), isang pandiwang hango sa salitang Espanyol na 'nervios' (nerves).
original_explanation: This is the energy of a senior employee during a surprise client presentation. Habang 'yung mga bago nanginginig, siya chill lang, umiinom ng kape. It's that "been there, done that" vibe. You're so used to the pressure that it doesn't even register anymore. "Final exam bukas? Ay, **hindi ako ninenerbiyos**." (Famous last words).
usage_notes: Isang kolokyal at karaniwang paraan upang ipahayag ang pagiging kalmado sa ilalim ng presyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sanay na siyang magsalita sa harap ng maraming tao kaya **hindi na siya ninenerbiyos**.","translation":"He is used to speaking in front of many people, so he **doesn't get nervous** anymore."},{"sentence":"Kahit unang beses niyang sumabak sa kompetisyon, **hindi siya ninenerbiyos**.","translation":"Even though it was his first time to join the competition, he was **not getting nervous**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng butong-gulay na bilog at karaniwang ginagamit sa mga lutuin tulad ng callos at pochero.
original_explanation: It's the MVP of your lola's pochero and the star of every Mediterranean-themed potluck (hello, hummus!). These are those little beige balls you find in cans at the supermarket, waiting to be turned into something delicious. Think of them as the more sophisticated cousin of the munggo bean.
usage_notes: The spelling "garbansos" is a common Filipinized variant. It's a key ingredient in many Filipino dishes with Spanish influence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagdagdag si nanay ng isang lata ng **garbanzos** sa niluluto niyang callos.","translation":"Mom added a can of **chickpeas** to the callos she was cooking."},{"sentence":"Ang hummus ay gawa sa dinurog na **garbanzos**.","translation":"Hummus is made from mashed **chickpeas**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagbabasa ng mga banal na kasulatan sa isang serbisyo sa simbahan; isang guro o tagapagturo sa ilang institusyong pang-edukasyon.
original_explanation: You'll most often hear this in a Catholic church. The **lektor** is the person assigned to read from the Bible during mass, usually a layperson. They're the opening act before the priest's main performance (the homily). In a non-religious sense, it can also mean a lecturer, but it's much rarer. Think of your most pious tita who's active in church—she's probably a **lektor**.
usage_notes: Primarily used in a religious (specifically Catholic) context in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aking ama ay isang **lektor** sa aming parokya tuwing Linggo.","translation":"My father is a **lector** in our parish every Sunday."},{"sentence":"Malinaw at marahan ang pagbasa ng **lektor** sa mga salita ng Diyos.","translation":"The **lector**'s reading of the words of God was clear and gentle."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao o bagay na inanod ng alon, hangin, o agos patungo sa dalampasigan o ibang lugar.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you get lost at sea and end up on a random island, like in the movies. You're a castaway. Sa modern context, 'yan 'yung feeling mo pagkatapos ng isang linggong OT, tapos napunta ka sa maling department party. You're just... there. Washed up.
usage_notes: Often used to describe things or people carried by water currents or wind. The phrase 'padpad na pasahero' specifically means a castaway passenger or a passenger who has drifted.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natagpuan ang mga **padpad** na piraso ng kahoy sa dalampasigan.","translation":"**Drifted** pieces of wood were found on the shore."},{"sentence":"Siya ay isang **padpad** na manlalakbay na napunta sa aming bayan.","translation":"He is a **wandering** traveler who ended up in our town."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay o koleksyon ng mga bagay na binalot sa papel o inilagay sa isang kahon upang maipadala, maihatid, o ibigay.
etymology: Hiram na salita mula sa Ingles na 'parcel'.
original_explanation: The reason you get excited when you hear 'May nagpapabigay po!'. 'Yung box from Shopee or Lazada na inorder mo 3 days ago at nakalimutan mo na. The modern-day 'sulat' from your online shopping cart, na naglalaman ng budol finds mo.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng pagpapadala at pagtanggap ng mga bagay sa pamamagitan ng koreo o courier services.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May dumating na **parsel** para sa iyo galing sa probinsya.","translation":"A **parcel** arrived for you from the province."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong buksan ang **parsel** na hindi para sa iyo.","translation":"Don't open the **package** that isn't for you."}]

meaning_filipino: Agad-agad; sa isang iglap lamang. Ito ay salitang hindi karaniwan sa Katagalugan at mas madalas marinig sa mga wikang Bisaya.
original_explanation: This isn't your everyday Tagalog word. It's more of a Visayan (Cebuano) import, meaning 'right away' or 'pronto.' So if your Bisaya friend says 'Buhaton nako na kabud,' it means 'I'll do it right now.' It's like the 'ASAP' in a corporate email, but with a regional flavor.
usage_notes: Primarily used in Visayan languages. Its use in Tagalog is very rare and usually indicates a speaker with a Visayan background.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nang utusan siya, **kabud** siyang tumalima.","translation":"When he was ordered, he obeyed **at once**."},{"sentence":"Dumating **kabud** ang tulong na aming hinihintay.","translation":"The help we were waiting for arrived **immediately**."}]

translation: to cause annoyance; to be the source of frustration
meaning_filipino: Maging dahilan ng matinding inis, pagkainis, o pagkayamot.
etymology: From 'i-' (causative prefix) + 'ka-' (causative prefix) + 'buwisit' (annoyance, from Hokkien 'bo ui sit' meaning 'no clothes to wear').
original_explanation: From slow internet during a crucial Zoom meeting to that one person who types 'TY' instead of 'Thank you' after you wrote a whole novel for them. Anything that makes your blood boil just a little bit and makes you whisper 'Bwisit!' under your breath is the 'ikabubuwisit' mo.
usage_notes: A strong word for expressing the cause of annoyance or bad luck.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang gumawa ng ingay na **ikabubuwisit** ng mga kapitbahay.","translation":"Don't make noise that will **cause annoyance** to the neighbors."},{"sentence":"Ang walang katapusang traffic sa EDSA ang **ikinabubuwisit** ko araw-araw.","translation":"The endless traffic on EDSA is what **is the source of my frustration** every day."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga pandaigdigang institusyon o sistema na may kinalaman sa pananalapi, partikular na ang International Monetary Fund (IMF).
original_explanation: This is the big boss of world money. When you hear "Panalapiang Internasyonal" (usually referring to the IMF), you think of massive loans, economic policies, and news reports that make your head spin. It's like the ultimate bumbay, but for entire countries. They lend money, but with a lot of terms and conditions.
usage_notes: This is a formal term, often used in news and academic contexts as the Filipino translation for the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-ulat ang **Panalapiang Internasyonal** tungkol sa paglago ng ekonomiya ng Pilipinas.","translation":"The **International Monetary** Fund reported on the economic growth of the Philippines."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan, hukay, o patibong na idinisenyo upang makahuli o makasilo ng mga hayop.
original_explanation: Not the "it's a trap!" meme kind, but the literal one for catching pests. 'Yung panghuli ng daga na nilalagyan mo ng keso o kanin. Also, it can be a metaphor for a bad situation you can't escape, like getting stuck in an 'MLM' presentation from a high school batchmate.
usage_notes: While 'bitag' or 'patibong' are more traditional terms, 'trap' is commonly used, especially for modern devices like mouse traps or sticky traps.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating maglagay ng **trap** para sa mga daga sa kusina.","translation":"We need to set a **trap** for the mice in the kitchen."},{"sentence":"Nahulog ang kanyang paa sa isang **trap** na para sana sa baboy-ramo.","translation":"His foot fell into a **trap** that was meant for a wild boar."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na humahalili o pumapalit sa tungkulin ng iba, lalo na sa trabaho, pagkatapos ng isang takdang oras o shift.
original_explanation: Your work bestie at 2:00 AM. In the BPO world, security guard posts, or hospitals, the **relebo** is the angel who arrives to take over your shift. Seeing them walk in means you can finally log off, go home, and collapse. They are the human equivalent of the "end of shift" alarm.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng trabahong may shift, tulad ng sa mga call center, ospital, o pagbabantay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hintayin ko lang ang **relebo** ko bago ako umuwi.","translation":"I'll just wait for my **relief** before I go home."},{"sentence":"Sino ang naka-iskedyul na **relebo** ni Kuya Guard mamayang gabi?","translation":"Who is scheduled as the security guard's **substitute** tonight?"}]

translation: to be envious, to be jealous
meaning_filipino: Makaramdam ng inggit o selos sa tagumpay, pag-aari, o katangian ng ibang tao.
original_explanation: It's that feeling when you see your friend's IG story of their Euro trip while you're stuck in traffic on EDSA. It's the "sana all" that has a little bit of saltiness to it. It’s not quite hating, but it’s the intense desire for what someone else has, from their new gadget to their jowa.
usage_notes: A more formal or literary synonym for 'mainggit'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi mo kailangang **mangimbulo** sa iba, dahil may sarili kang landas na tinatahak.","translation":"You don't need to **be envious** of others, because you are treading your own path."},{"sentence":"May mga taong hindi mapigilang **mangimbulo** kapag nakakakita ng tagumpay ng kanilang kapwa.","translation":"There are people who can't help but **be jealous** when they see the success of their peers."}]

translation: to butter; to put butter on
meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng mantikilya ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay pagkain tulad ng tinapay o mais.
original_explanation: The action of slathering that golden goodness onto something. It's what you do to hot pandesal, grilled corn on the cob, or a boring piece of toast to make it 100x better. 'Mantikilyahan mo nang husto!' is a command for maximum flavor.
usage_notes: The '-han' suffix indicates applying something onto a surface.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Mantikilyahan** mo ang mainit na mais habang bagong luto.","translation":"**Put butter on** the hot corn while it's newly cooked."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **mantikilyahan** ang bawat piraso ng tinapay.","translation":"Don't forget to **butter** every piece of bread."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkuha, pagkain, o paglipat ng isang bagay gamit ang kutsara.
etymology: From 'kutsara' (spoon) + '-hin' suffix, indicating an action to be done with the object.
original_explanation: This is the action you do when you see that last bit of ube ice cream or that perfect spoonful of leche flan. It's the verb form of surrendering to your cravings, one spoonful at a time. 'Kutsarahin mo na 'yang kanin, 'wag nang mahiya.'
usage_notes: Can be used literally for food or figuratively for scooping up something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kutsarahin** mo na lang ang sorbetes para hindi matunaw.","translation":"Just **scoop the ice cream with a spoon** so it doesn't melt."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **kutsarahin** ang asukal nang direkta mula sa lalagyan.","translation":"Don't **scoop** the sugar directly from the container **with a spoon**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos o proseso ng pagkontrol, paghahari, o pagkakaroon ng kapangyarihan sa iba.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `pan-`, pag-uulit ng unang pantig ng salitang ugat `do-` (nagiging `du-`), at salitang hiram na `domina` (mula sa Espanyol na 'dominar').
original_explanation: The act of dominating. It's the energy you bring when you're the group leader who gets the project done right. It's the feeling of winning a Mobile Legends match after a 10-game losing streak. It's all about taking charge and being in control. The 'main character' energy in a power struggle.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa proseso o kilos ng paghahari. Ang 'dominasyon' ay mas karaniwang ginagamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pandudomina** sa laro ay halatang-halata.","translation":"His **domination** in the game was very obvious."},{"sentence":"Layunin ng imperyo ang **pandudomina** sa buong rehiyon.","translation":"The empire's goal is the **domination** of the entire region."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking propesyonal na nagtuturo; o isang dalubhasa at iginagalang na tao sa isang larangan ng sining o agham.
original_explanation: Si Sir. 'Yung teacher mong lalaki. Pero level-up din ito, 'pag tinawag kang "maestro," ibig sabihin master ka sa ginagawa mo, parang si Ryan Cayabyab sa musika o si FPJ sa action films.
usage_notes: Has a dual meaning: a male teacher (less common now than 'guro' or 'sir') and a master of an art or trade, which carries a high degree of respect.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bihira na ngayon ang mga lalaking **maestro** sa elementarya.","translation":"Male **teachers** in elementary are rare nowadays."},{"sentence":"Kinikilala si Lucio San Pedro bilang isang **maestro** ng musikang Pilipino.","translation":"Lucio San Pedro is recognized as a **master** of Filipino music."}]

meaning_filipino: Angkop, tama, o nababagay para sa isang partikular na layunin, tao, okasyon, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: That feeling when your outfit matches the party theme perfectly. Or when your 'hugot' line is perfectly timed for maximum dramatic effect. It's the universe giving you a thumbs up. When something is 'sakto,' 'swak,' or 'bagay,' it's akma.
usage_notes: Often used with 'sa' to indicate what it is suitable for (e.g., 'akma sa okasyon'). 'Angkop' is a close synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang suot niyang barong ay **akma** sa pormal na pagdiriwang.","translation":"The barong he is wearing is **appropriate** for the formal celebration."},{"sentence":"Hindi **akma** ang kanyang biro sa seryosong usapan.","translation":"His joke was not **suitable** for the serious conversation."}]

translation: to assign; to dedicate; to ordain
meaning_filipino: Italaga; bigyan ng katungkulan, layunin, o sagradong misyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang itinalaga bilang bagong pinuno.","translation":"He was appointed as the new leader."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagganap o pagsasabuhay ng isang karakter o papel sa isang partikular na sitwasyon, lalo na sa mga laro, pagsasanay, o libangan.
original_explanation: Ito yung pag-acting mo na ibang tao ka. Pwedeng sa Dungeons & Dragons, sa Roblox, o sa training niyo sa BPO (e.g., "Okay, I'll be the irate customer, you be the agent."). It's basically 'arte-artehan' with a purpose.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pangngalan o pandiwa ("mag-roleplay tayo").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kasama sa training namin ang **roleplay** ng iba't ibang customer scenarios.","translation":"Our training includes the **roleplay** of different customer scenarios."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang mag-**roleplay** bilang isang wizard sa online game.","translation":"He likes to **roleplay** as a wizard in the online game."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aapoy o ang kalagayan ng pagiging may apoy o ilaw; ang mismong pagsisimula ng apoy.
etymology: Possibly from a shortened form of Spanish 'encender' (to light).
original_explanation: The OG command before 'Netflix and chill' was 'Sindi na, manonood tayo.' It's the action of starting a fire, whether it's for a romantic candle, your Tito's yosi, or the gas stove when it's your turn to cook the sinangag. It's the spark that starts it all, the very moment of ignition.
usage_notes: Often used as a root word for verbs like 'sindihan' (to light something) or 'sumindi' (to be lit). As a noun, it refers to the act or state of being lit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **sindi** lang ng posporo, nasunog ang buong papel.","translation":"Just one **light** of the match, and the whole paper burned."},{"sentence":"Malakas ang **sindi** ng bagong lighter mo.","translation":"The **ignition** of your new lighter is strong."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglipat o pagtungo sa isang partikular na lugar o destinasyon.
original_explanation: The action you take when your friend messages "tara, kape!" and you're already halfway out the door. It's the opposite of "drawing" (a plan that doesn't happen). You actually pumunta.
usage_notes: This is the completed or past tense form of the verb. The infinitive form is 'pumunta' and the present progressive is 'pumupunta'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pumunta** kami sa mall kahapon.","translation":"We **went** to the mall yesterday."},{"sentence":"Bakit ka **pumunta** rito?","translation":"Why did you **come** here?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pandiwa na nangangahulugang ang pagbabago ng isang estado, katangian, o pagkakakilanlan patungo sa iba; o ang pag-iral sa isang partikular na kalagayan.
etymology: Considered a defective or irregular verb. It functions as a base form for expressing a future state or a command to be something.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "glow-up" verb. It's about transformation. From single to "in a relationship," from trainee to regular employee, from "just friends" to something more. `Maging` is the process, the journey. It's the verb for all your "sana all" moments and New Year's resolutions.
usage_notes: Often used in aspirations, commands, or stating a potential change of state. The past tense is 'naging' and the present progressive tense is 'nagiging'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pangarap niya ay **maging** isang tanyag na manunulat.","translation":"Her dream is **to become** a famous writer."},{"sentence":"**Maging** tapat ka sa lahat ng iyong ginagawa.","translation":"**Be** honest in everything you do."}]

translation: to make a fool of oneself; to act crazy (for someone)
meaning_filipino: Sadyain ang pag-aasal na parang wala sa katinuan, kadalasan dahil sa matinding damdamin tulad ng pag-ibig.
etymology: From the prefix `magpaka-`, which signifies an intense or deliberate effort to become or do something, and the root word `loko` (crazy).
original_explanation: The official sport of someone who's "marupok" (emotionally fragile). It's when you do things you'd normally never do, all for that one person who probably just sees you as a friend. It's when you let yourself be played, but you call it love. #Clownery
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Handa siyang **magpakaloko** para sa pag-ibig, kahit pa nasasaktan na siya.","translation":"She is ready to **make a fool of herself** for love, even if she's already getting hurt."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magpakaloko** sa mga pangako niyang laging napapako.","translation":"Don't **let yourself be fooled** by his promises that are always broken."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aalok, pagbibigay, o pagtanggap ng anumang bagay na may halaga upang maimpluwensyahan ang kilos ng isang tao na nasa posisyon ng kapangyarihan.
original_explanation: The OG act of "under-the-table" transactions. Ito 'yung pagbibigay ng "lagay" para mapabilis ang proseso sa gobyerno, o para makalusot sa traffic violation. It's the unofficial "express lane" fee of the Philippines. Very illegal, very tempting for some.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to the act or crime of bribery.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **panunuhol** ay isang krimen na may mabigat na parusa.","translation":"**Bribery** is a crime with a heavy penalty."},{"sentence":"Nasangkot ang opisyal sa isang iskandalo ng **panunuhol**.","translation":"The official was involved in a **bribery** scandal."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi para sa publiko; personal o pagmamay-ari ng isang partikular na tao o grupo.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "privada", ang pambabaeng anyo ng "privado".
original_explanation: 'Yung IG account mo na naka-lock, 'yung 'me time' mo na ayaw mong may istorbo, o 'yung resort na 'exclusive for guests only'. Ito 'yung opposite ng 'public,' 'yung espasyo o bagay na para sa'yo lang o sa iilang tao. 'Pag sinabing 'pribada,' bawal ang chismosa.
usage_notes: Ang panlalaking anyo ay "pribado". Ang "pribada" ay ginagamit kasama ng mga pangngalang pambabae (hal. pribadang paaralan, pribadang pag-uusap). Sa kolokyal na gamit, madalas na ang salitang Ingles na "private" ang ginagamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginanap ang kasal sa isang **pribada** na seremonya.","translation":"The wedding was held in a **private** ceremony."},{"sentence":"Ito ay isang **pribada**ng ari-arian kaya bawal pumasok ang hindi awtorisado.","translation":"This is **private** property so unauthorized entry is forbidden."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang impormal at hindi malinaw na ugnayan sa pagitan ng dalawang tao na may romantikong elemento ngunit walang malinaw na kasunduan, titulo, o pangako.
etymology: Hiram sa Ingles, mula sa pinagsamang "situation" at "relationship".
original_explanation: The M.U. (Mutual Understanding) of the 2020s, but with more anxiety. It's when you're more than friends, but less than a couple. You do couple things, you have couple feelings, but you don't have the label. It's the Schrödinger's cat of relationships—you're both together and not together until someone asks "Ano ba talaga tayo?"
usage_notes: Isang napakakaraniwang termino sa modernong pakikipag-date sa Pilipinas, lalo na sa mga lungsod at sa social media. Kadalasang nauugnay sa 'hugot' culture.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagod na ako sa **situationship**, gusto ko na ng tunay na jowa.","translation":"I'm tired of this **situationship**, I want a real partner now."},{"sentence":"Nasa **situationship** kami, kaya bawal magselos at bawal mag-demand.","translation":"We're in a **situationship**, so getting jealous and making demands are not allowed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis at malakas na pagtibok o pagkabog ng puso, karaniwang sanhi ng matinding damdamin tulad ng takot, kaba, o pananabik.
original_explanation: 'Yan 'yung nararamdaman mo 'pag biglang nag-pop up sa screen 'yung pangalan ng crush mo, o 'pag tinawag ka ng boss mo for a 'quick chat'. It's the 'kabog ng dibdib' moment. Pwedeng dahil sa kape, sa puyat, o sa pag-ibig. This is your heart doing the cha-cha against your will.
usage_notes: Partikular na tumutukoy sa mabilis o iregular na pagtibok ng puso, kadalasang may kasamang matinding emosyon tulad ng pagkabalisa o takot.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman ko ang **tahip** ng aking dibdib habang papalapit ang resulta ng exam.","translation":"I felt the **palpitation** of my chest as the exam results drew near."},{"sentence":"Ang malakas na **tahip** ng puso niya ay tanda ng matinding kaba.","translation":"The strong **throbbing** of his heart is a sign of intense nervousness."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis na pag-agaw o pagkuha sa isang bagay, karaniwang mula sa itaas o sa biglaang paraan.
original_explanation: This is what a hawk does to a chick, or what a snatcher does to your phone while you're texting on the jeepney. It's a swift, sudden, and often unwelcome takeover. 'Agila-move.'
usage_notes: Often used to describe birds of prey or the act of snatching/theft.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita ko ang **pagdagit** ng lawin sa sisiw.","translation":"I saw the hawk's **swooping** on the chick."},{"sentence":"Naging biktima siya ng **pagdagit** ng cellphone habang naglalakad.","translation":"She became a victim of cellphone **snatching** while walking."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang Ingles na katawagan para sa sampalok, isang tropikal na puno na may bunga na maasim na ginagamit sa pagluluto at paggawa ng kendi.
original_explanation: This is just the English word for sampalok. You'll see this on the packaging of instant sinigang mix or those sour candies you either love or hate. It's basically the English version of a Filipino flavor icon.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa mga kontekstong Ingles o kapag tumutukoy sa mga produkto na gumagamit ng pangalang Ingles. Ang katutubong salita sa Tagalog ay *sampalok*.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **tamarind** powder ang ginamit niya sa sinigang.","translation":"She used a lot of **tamarind** powder in the sinigang."}]

translation: in a tight spot; short of money; cornered
meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng kakulangan, lalo na sa pananalapi; nasa isang mahirap o alanganing sitwasyon.
original_explanation: That dreaded 'petsa de peligro' feeling right before payday. When your wallet is on life support and your ATM balance is judging you. You're 'gipit' when you have to choose between load and lunch. It's not just about money; you can also be 'gipit sa oras' (short on time) when you're stuck in EDSA traffic and your meeting starts in 5 minutes.
usage_notes: Most commonly refers to financial difficulty but can also describe being in a tight or difficult situation in general.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Gipit** ako sa pera ngayon, sa susunod na linggo na lang kita babayaran.","translation":"I'm **short of money** right now, I'll just pay you next week."},{"sentence":"Nang maramdaman niyang **gipit** na siya, sumuko ang magnanakaw sa mga pulis.","translation":"When he felt he was **cornered**, the thief surrendered to the police."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pansariling benepisyo o interes na nangingibabaw sa kapakanan ng iba o ng pangkalahatan.
original_explanation: This is the official motto of every "trapo" (traditional politician) and anyone who messages you with "Hi, friend! Musta? May business ako..." It's the "What's in it for me?" attitude. When someone does something "good" but you can smell the ulterior motive from a mile away, that's sariling kapakinabangan at work.
usage_notes: Often carries a negative connotation, implying selfishness or opportunism.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang desisyon niya ay para lamang sa kanyang **sariling kapakinabangan**.","translation":"His decision was only for his **own personal gain**."},{"sentence":"Isinantabi niya ang **sariling kapakinabangan** para sa kabutihan ng grupo.","translation":"She set aside her **self-interest** for the good of the group."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa sistema, proseso, o anumang may kaugnayan sa parlamento.
original_explanation: This is a high-level politics word. As an adjective, it's about anything related to a parliament, like "parliamentary procedure" (yung rules sa mga meeting na parang sa Congress). As a noun, it refers to a member of parliament. Basically, a fancy word for lawmaker na galing sa Spanish.
usage_notes: Maaari ring maging pangngalan na tumutukoy sa isang miyembro ng parlamento (parliamentarian). Ginagamit sa mga pormal na talakayan tungkol sa gobyerno at politika.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Pilipinas ay may sistemang presidensyal, hindi **parlamentaryo**.","translation":"The Philippines has a presidential system, not a **parliamentary** one."},{"sentence":"Kilala siyang mahusay na **parlamentaryo** dahil sa kanyang mga talumpati.","translation":"He is known as a great **parliamentarian** because of his speeches."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paraan ng paggamit ng mga salita upang ipahayag ang kaisipan o damdamin; maaari ring tumukoy sa isang pormal na pahayag o talumpati.
etymology: From the verb 'magsalita' (to speak). The noun is formed via `pan-` + reduplication of the first syllable of the root `salita`, resulting in `pananalita`.
original_explanation: It's not just *what* you say, but *how* you say it. This is your 'delivery'—your choice of words, your tone, your accent. Is your pananalita 'conyo,' 'jologs,' 'bekimon,' or straight out of a Balagtas poem? It's your verbal personality, the thing your friends make fun of or your boss praises during presentations.
usage_notes: Can refer to both the general act/manner of speaking and a specific utterance or formal speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingatan mo ang iyong **pananalita** kapag kaharap ang mga nakatatanda.","translation":"Watch your **words/manner of speaking** when you are with elders."},{"sentence":"Nagbigay ng mahalagang **pananalita** ang pangulo sa harap ng kongreso.","translation":"The president gave an important **speech** before the congress."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng miyembro ng banda na nagpapaikot-ikot ng baston (baton) sa saliw ng musika, karaniwang makikita sa mga parada.
etymology: From Spanish 'bastonera', the feminine form of 'bastonero' (cane-maker or keeper).
original_explanation: The star of every town fiesta parade, the one who can twirl a shiny stick better than you can handle your life's problems. She's got the high-knee march and the dazzling smile down pat, even under the scorching sun.
usage_notes: The feminine form of 'bastunero'. Refers specifically to female majorettes in a marching band.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napanood mo ba ang galing ng mga **bastonera** sa parada kahapon?","translation":"Did you see the skill of the **majorettes** at the parade yesterday?"},{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang maging pangunahing **bastonera** ng kanilang eskwelahan.","translation":"She dreams of becoming the lead **majorette** of their school."}]

meaning_filipino: Paglalagay ng sangkap upang magdagdag, magpasarap, o magbago ng lasa ng pagkain.
original_explanation: This is what you do when the sinigang isn't 'asim-kilig' enough or your adobo is lacking that 'alat-tamis' kick. It's the art of turning a bland dish into a flavor bomb, like adding the perfect filter to your food's profile picture before posting.
usage_notes: The prefix 'magpa-' in this context indicates causing something to have a certain quality, in this case, 'lasa' (taste/flavor).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magpalasa** pa ng sabaw para mas sumarap.","translation":"You need to **season** the soup more to make it tastier."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang matakot **magpalasa** gamit ang iba't ibang uri ng pampalasa.","translation":"Don't be afraid to **add flavor** using different kinds of spices."}]

translation: to strike flints together; to create a spark
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkiskis ng dalawang bagay, karaniwan ay bato o bakal, upang lumikha ng apoy o kislap.
etymology: Likely related to "pingkian," which means friction or clash.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate survival move you see in movies. Before lighters and matches, this was the Tinder of the old world—literally swiping stones together to get some fire. It’s the ancient way of saying, "Let's get this fire started!"
usage_notes: A very old and now rarely used word, mostly found in historical or literary contexts. The noun form "pingkian" is more common, often referring to a clash of ideas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sinaunang panahon, kailangang **magpingki** ng dalawang bato upang makagawa ng apoy.","translation":"In ancient times, one needed to **strike two stones** together to make fire."},{"sentence":"Tinuruan siya ng kanyang lolo kung paano **magpingki** gamit ang kawayan.","translation":"His grandfather taught him how to **create a spark** using bamboo."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng isang maikli at matinis na tunog, karaniwang ginagawa ng mga sisiw o maliliit na ibon, o ng isang taong biglang nasaktan o natuwa.
original_explanation: The sound a baby chick makes. Also, the sound you make when you accidentally step on a LEGO brick in the dark. It's that high-pitched, short 'Eep!' of surprise or pain. Not a full-blown scream, just a 'piyak'.
usage_notes: Usually associated with small animals like chicks or mice, but can be used for a person's short, high-pitched cry.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang mga sisiw na **pumiyak** sa loob ng kahon.","translation":"I heard the chicks **chirping** inside the box."},{"sentence":"**Pumiyak** siya sa sakit nang maipit ang daliri niya sa pinto.","translation":"She **squeaked** in pain when her finger got caught in the door."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lihim na pagmamanman o pag-eespiya sa mga kilos, galaw, o usapan ng isang tao o grupo.
etymology: From "tiktik" (spy, detective), with the prefix "paN-" and reduplication of the first syllable.
original_explanation: The work of a 'tiktik' or a spy. It's what your jealous ex does to your social media profiles. It's also what the neighborhood 'marites' does from her window. On a larger scale, it's James Bond stuff. The art of gathering intel without getting caught.
usage_notes: Can range from casual snooping to professional, state-level espionage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inakusahan ang dayuhang diplomatiko ng **paniniktik**.","translation":"The foreign diplomat was accused of **espionage**."},{"sentence":"Ang **paniniktik** sa pribadong buhay ng iba ay isang paglabag sa kanilang karapatan.","translation":"**Spying** on the private lives of others is a violation of their rights."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na namumuno at gumagabay sa isang grupo ng mga musikero o mang-aawit, tulad ng isang orkestra o koro, gamit ang mga senyas ng kamay.
original_explanation: The ultimate traffic enforcer of music. Sila 'yung may hawak na stick (baton) sa harap ng orchestra, parang nagcha-charge ng spirit bomb. They don't make a sound, pero sila ang may kontrol sa lahat. Sila ang dahilan kung bakit hindi nagkakagulo ang mga violin at trumpeta.
usage_notes: Refers to the leader of a musical ensemble like an orchestra or choir.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **konduktor** ng orkestra ay nagbigay ng hudyat upang magsimula.","translation":"The orchestra **conductor** gave the signal to begin."},{"sentence":"Si Ryan Cayabyab ay isang tanyag na kompositor at **konduktor**.","translation":"Ryan Cayabyab is a famous composer and **conductor**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbigkas ng isang bagay na isinaulo, karaniwan sa harap ng isang madla o klase.
original_explanation: The moment in class that gives everyone anxiety. Your teacher calls your name, you stand up, your mind goes blank, and you suddenly forget the entire Panatang Makabayan you've known since grade 1. Plus 5 points if you survive.
usage_notes: Primarily used in an academic or school context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinakabahan ako para sa aming **resitasyon** sa Araling Panlipunan bukas.","translation":"I'm nervous about our **recitation** in Social Studies tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Ang bawat tamang sagot sa **resitasyon** ay may katumbas na puntos.","translation":"Every correct answer in the **recitation** corresponds to points."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita ng isang bagay, katangian, o sarili sa isang paraan na may pagyayabang o labis na pagmamalaki.
original_explanation: This is 'flexing' before 'flex' was a thing. When you get a new phone and you 'accidentally' place it on the table screen up for everyone to see, you're **inilalandang** it. It's showing something off, but not in a subtle way. Parang rampa sa runway ng life.
usage_notes: Carries a slightly negative connotation of being boastful or ostentatious.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **ilandang** ang kanyang mga mamahaling alahas.","translation":"She loves to **flaunt** her expensive jewelry."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ilandang** ang iyong kayamanan sa harap ng mga nangangailangan.","translation":"Don't **show off** your wealth in front of those in need."}]

translation: to become loose; to ease up
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbawas ng higpit, sikip, o tensyon sa isang bagay, sitwasyon, o damdamin.
etymology: From 'luwag' (looseness, space). The '-um-' infix indicates a verb.
original_explanation: That magical feeling when your jeans finally fit again after a diet. Or when the traffic on EDSA finally moves after being stuck for an hour. It can also be emotional, like when your strict parents finally allow you to go on an overnight trip – lumuwag na sila. It's the feeling of "finally, some breathing room!"
usage_notes: Can be used for physical objects (a screw, clothes), abstract concepts (rules, traffic), or emotions (a heavy heart).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng Pasko, medyo **lumuwag** ang aking pantalon.","translation":"After Christmas, my pants became a bit **loose**."},{"sentence":"**Lumuwa**g ang daloy ng trapiko pagkalagpas ng alas-diyes ng umaga.","translation":"The flow of traffic **eased up** after ten in the morning."},{"sentence":"**Lumuwa**g ang dibdib ko nang malaman kong ligtas sila.","translation":"My chest **felt lighter** (I was relieved) when I found out they were safe."}]

translation: to base on; to found upon
meaning_filipino: Gamitin bilang pundasyon, basehan, o sanggunian sa paggawa ng isang desisyon, konklusyon, o akda.
original_explanation: The academic version of 'Sabi ni...' (According to...). It's what you do when you need to justify your opinion with facts, not just feelings. In a chismis context, it's checking if the rumor is based on a 'reliable source' or just 'sabi-sabi'. In short, it’s about having receipts for your claims.
usage_notes: Often followed by 'sa' (on/in). For example, 'magbatay sa ebidensya' (to base on evidence).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat tayong **magbatay** sa siyentipikong datos sa pagbuo ng ating mga patakaran.","translation":"We should **base** our policies on scientific data."},{"sentence":"Saan ka ba **nagbatay** para sabihing hindi siya mapagkakatiwalaan?","translation":"What did you **base** it on to say that he/she is not trustworthy?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ibabang bahagi ng panga ng tao o hayop, na naglalaman ng mga ngipin at gumagalaw kapag nagsasalita o kumakain.
original_explanation: This is your jaw, specifically the lower part that moves when you're chewing chicharon or talking smack. It's the part that drops when you see your electricity bill. It's a more specific, almost anatomical term than just "panga."
usage_notes: Not a very common word in daily conversation. "Panga" is used more often. "Bibigan" has a slightly more technical or literary feel.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malakas na suntok sa **bibigan** ang nagpatumba sa boksingero.","translation":"A strong punch to the **jaw** knocked the boxer down."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagluluto ng pagkain sa pamamagitan ng paglubog nito sa mainit na mantika.
original_explanation: The sound and smell of a Filipino household in the morning. Someone is always nagpiprito—whether it's hotdog, itlog, or tuyo. It's the official cooking method of the 'silog' breakfast empire. Similar to 'nagpiplantsa', the 'pr' blend means you just repeat the 'p' with an 'i'.
usage_notes: Present progressive tense. For root words starting with consonant blends like 'pr', the first consonant and 'i' are prefixed (nag-pi-).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Amoy pa lang, alam mo nang may **nagpiprito** ng isda.","translation":"From the smell alone, you know someone **is frying** fish."},{"sentence":"**Nagpiprito** si Kuya ng manok para sa aming pananghalian.","translation":"My older brother **is frying** chicken for our lunch."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagsasagawa ng isang opisyal na pagsusuri sa mga account ng isang organisasyon, kadalasan ay sa pananalapi.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your department's budget before the fiscal year ends. It's the corporate version of your mom checking your receipts after you go to the palengke. "Awditin mo nga kung saan napunta 'yung 13th-month pay ko."
usage_notes: Often used in business, finance, and government contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **awditin** ang lahat ng gastusin ng kumpanya para sa nakaraang taon.","translation":"All of the company's expenses for the past year need to **be audited**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na umuupa o nagbabayad para sa pansamantalang paggamit ng isang ari-arian, tulad ng bahay, apartment, o kwarto.
etymology: Mula sa "upa" na may panlaping "nang-" at "-han".
original_explanation: Sila yung mga "boarders", "bedspacers", o yung pamilyang umuupa sa apartment ni Aling Nena. Ito yung mga taong may "landlord" or "landlady" na kinakatok sila tuwing due date ng upa. Ang buhay ng isang nangungupahan ay isang cycle ng pagbabayad ng renta, pagtitipid sa kuryente at tubig, at pag-asang makabili ng sariling bahay balang araw.
usage_notes: Ginagamit din ang "arkilado" o ang salitang Ingles na "tenant".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May bagong **nangungupahan** sa apartment sa tabi namin.","translation":"There's a new **tenant** in the apartment next to us."},{"sentence":"Bilang **nangungupahan**, responsibilidad mong panatilihing malinis ang iyong tinitirhan.","translation":"As a **renter**, it's your responsibility to keep the place you live in clean."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mas matandang tao, kadalasan ay isang kamag-anak, na sumasama sa isang dalaga o magkasintahan sa isang pampublikong lugar o pagtitipon upang matiyak ang kanilang tamang asal at kaligtasan.
etymology: From French 'chaperon,' borrowed into English and then into Filipino.
original_explanation: The original 'third wheel,' but with parental approval. In classic Filipino courtship, the chaperon (usually a tita, lola, or younger sibling) was the human CCTV camera meant to keep things wholesome between young lovers. Today, the term is a bit retro, but the spirit lives on in any group hang-out where one friend is clearly just there to make sure nobody does anything stupid. 'Sama ka, para may chaperon kami.'
usage_notes: A concept more associated with traditional Filipino culture but still understood today, often in a humorous or historical context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ako pinayagan ng mga magulang ko na lumabas kasama ka kung walang **chaperon**.","translation":"My parents won't allow me to go out with you without a **chaperone**."},{"sentence":"Naging **chaperon** ako ng kapatid ko sa first date niya.","translation":"I became my younger sibling's **chaperone** on their first date."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pirasong bagay, karaniwang tatsulok ang hugis, na isinisingit sa siwang upang pigilan ang paggalaw o upang patagin ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: The unsung hero of wobbly tables everywhere. Got a table at the karinderya that moves every time you breathe? You need a 'tako'—a folded piece of cardboard or a piece of wood—to shut it up. It's the low-tech solution to life's unsteady problems.
usage_notes: Madalas na ipagkamali sa 'tako' ng bilyar, ang konteksto ang nagdidikta ng kahulugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagyan mo ng **tako** ang paanan ng mesa para hindi umuga.","translation":"Put a **wedge** under the table leg so it won't wobble."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawin ang mga kinakailangang hakbang o magbigay ng suporta upang matiyak ang tagumpay ng isang tao, plano, o adhikain.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate goal of every parent, mentor, or supportive friend. You want to **papagtagumpayin** your 'alaga'. It's about providing the tools, the 'diskarte', and the emotional support (or the startup capital) to help someone win at life. It's the opposite of the crab mentality.
usage_notes: A very positive and formal-sounding word, often used in speeches and inspirational messages.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gagawin ko ang lahat para **papagtagumpayin** ang iyong mga pangarap.","translation":"I will do everything **to make your dreams succeed**."},{"sentence":"Ang pagkakaisa ng grupo ang **nagpatagumpay** sa kanilang proyekto.","translation":"The group's unity **made their project triumph**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay o koleksyon ng mga bagay na ipinapakita sa isang eksibisyon; ebidensyang ipiniprisinta sa korte.
original_explanation: Pwedeng 'yung specific na item sa museum, like "Wow, ganda ng eksibit na 'yan!" Pwede ring pang-lawyer, 'yung "Exhibit A" na ebidensya sa kaso, tulad ng screenshot ng convo niyo ng ex mo na umaamin sa kasalanan niya.
usage_notes: May dalawang pangunahing gamit: bilang isang bagay na itinatanghal at bilang legal na ebidensya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pinakasikat na **eksibit** sa museo ay ang Spoliarium.","translation":"The most famous **exhibit** in the museum is the Spoliarium."},{"sentence":"Ipinakita ng piskal ang kutsilyo bilang **Eksibit** A.","translation":"The fiscal presented the knife as **Exhibit** A."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na paghiling sa isang mas mataas na kapangyarihan o hukuman na muling isaalang-alang ang isang desisyon; ang paghingi ng tulong, awa, o suporta.
original_explanation: When you fail a subject and you talk to the prof to reconsider your grade, that's you trying to mag-apela. It's the "Sir/Ma'am, baka naman po" move. Also used in legal terms, like appealing a court decision, or in basketball, when a player complains to the ref.
usage_notes: Used in both legal and everyday contexts to mean asking for reconsideration or help.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Plano ng abogado na **mag-apela** sa Korte Suprema.","translation":"The lawyer plans **to appeal** to the Supreme Court."},{"sentence":"Nag-**apela** ang mga residente sa gobyerno para sa agarang tulong pagkatapos ng bagyo.","translation":"The residents **appealed** to the government for immediate help after the storm."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maliit na ibon (Passer montanus) na karaniwang makikita sa Pilipinas, may kayumangging likod, puting pisngi na may itim na patak, at itim na tuka.
original_explanation: The OG 'maya.' For the longest time, everyone thought this was the national bird. It’s that small, brown bird you see everywhere in the city, from the mall parking lot to the Jollibee sign. It's the most common 'maya' you'll encounter. The 'bato' (stone/rock) in its name might refer to its preference for urban, rocky, or man-made structures.
usage_notes: This is the bird most Filipinos refer to when they simply say 'maya.' The actual national bird is the Philippine Eagle (Pithecophaga jefferyi).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **mayang-bato** ang mga kawad ng kuryente tuwing umaga.","translation":"The electrical wires are full of **Eurasian tree sparrows** every morning."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong itaboy ang mga **mayang-bato**, bahagi sila ng ating kalikasan.","translation":"Don't drive away the **sparrows**, they are part of our nature."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpunta sa mas mataas na lugar mula sa isang mababang posisyon; o ang pagtaas ng halaga o antas.
original_explanation: Yung ginagawa mo sa bundok pag weekend warrior ka, o yung ginagawa mo sa corporate ladder pero parang ang bagal ng usad. Also, yung presyo ng bilihin. 'Grabe ang akyat ng presyo ng gas!'
usage_notes: Often used as a root word for verbs like 'umakyat' (to climb) and 'akyatin' (to climb something). It can also refer to the increase in prices or status.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **akyat** sa bundok ay nakakapagod.","translation":"The **climb** up the mountain is tiring."},{"sentence":"Mabilis ang **akyat** ng presyo ng sibuyas.","translation":"The price **increase** of onions is fast."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggamit ng gunting upang putulin o hubugin ang isang bagay tulad ng papel, tela, o buhok.
original_explanation: The OG way to crop someone out of a photo before Photoshop existed. This is what your nanay does to your bangs when you're five, what the sastre does to the tela, or what you do to cut out coupons. If it involves scissors, you're *gumugupit*.
usage_notes: Specifically implies the use of scissors. For cutting with a knife, the word 'humiwa' is used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **gumupit** ng buhok ko noong isang linggo.","translation":"She was the one who **cut** my hair last week."},{"sentence":"**Gumupit** ako ng mga larawan mula sa lumang magasin.","translation":"I **cut** pictures from old magazines."}]

translation: a type of small, unglazed clay pot
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maliit na palayok na yari sa luwad, karaniwang ginagamit sa pagluluto o bilang sisidlan.
original_explanation: Before there were non-stick pans, there was the 'pali'. This is the OG clay pot, smaller than a 'palayok'. Imagine your lola cooking sinigang in this over a wood fire. It's rustic, it's traditional, it's the kind of thing you see in a historical diorama or a fancy Filipino restaurant trying to be authentic.
usage_notes: This is a more traditional and less common term. The stress is on the second syllable, distinguishing it from 'pali' (spleen).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagluto si lola ng sinaing sa isang maliit na **pali**.","translation":"Grandma cooked braised fish in a small **clay pot**."}]

translation: to clash; to have a heated argument
meaning_filipino: Ang pakikipagtalo o pakikipag-away nang may matinding damdamin at malalakas na salita; isang masidhing bangayan.
original_explanation: This is a level up from `makipag-away`. Think less of a physical brawl and more of a really intense, no-holds-barred verbal showdown. It's the kind of argument you see in teleseryes where family secrets are revealed, or in a condo board meeting about parking rules. It’s loud, it’s messy, and someone’s probably going to cry.
usage_notes: More intense and often more verbal than 'makipag-away'. It implies a direct, forceful confrontation of words and wills.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **makipagbabag** sa mga taong sarado ang isip.","translation":"Don't **clash** with people who are close-minded."},{"sentence":"Narinig ng buong kapitbahayan nang sila'y **makipagbabag** kagabi.","translation":"The whole neighborhood heard it when they **had a heated argument** last night."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tunog na nalilikha sa pamamagitan ng pagkaskas o pagkayod sa isang matigas na bagay, tulad ng ginagawa ng daga.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung pinsan ni 'kaluskos'. Kung si kaluskos ay rustling, si kalutkot ay gnawing or scraping. 'Yung tunog ng daga na nginangatngat 'yung pader. O 'yung tunog ng kutsara mo habang kinakayod 'yung tutong sa kaldero. It's a harder, more persistent sound. Nakakakilabot din minsan.
usage_notes: Often associated with pests like rats or the act of scraping something hard.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May naririnig akong **kalutkot** sa ilalim ng sahig.","translation":"I hear a **scraping sound** under the floor."},{"sentence":"Ang **kalutkot** ng mga kuko ng aso sa pinto ay gumising sa akin.","translation":"The **scraping** of the dog's claws on the door woke me up."}]

translation: to give a title to; to entitle
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagbibigay ng pamagat sa isang akda, sulatin, o anumang gawa.
original_explanation: This is what you do after you've written a long essay for school or a hugot-filled poem for your crush. You need to magpamagat—give it a title. A good title is like a good movie trailer; it should be catchy and make people want to read what you wrote. 'Ang Pagsuko ng Isang Martir' is a much better title than 'Essay #2'.
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of literature, writing, music, and art.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahihirapan akong **magpamagat** ng aking isinulat na tula.","translation":"I'm having a hard time **giving a title to** the poem I wrote."},{"sentence":"Siya ang **nagpamagat** sa pelikulang naging sikat.","translation":"He was the one who **entitled** the movie that became famous."}]

translation: myriads of years; tens of thousands of years
meaning_filipino: Isang napakahabang panahon na binubuo ng sampu-sampung libong taon; ginagamit upang ipahiwatig ang isang napakasinaunang panahon.
etymology: Ang 'Laksa' ay mula sa Sanskrit na 'lakṣa', na nangangahulugang 'isang daang libo' (100,000), bagama't sa Tagalog ay karaniwang nauunawaan bilang 'sampung libo' (10,000). Ang pag-uulit ay nagpapahiwatig ng napakaraming bilang.
original_explanation: This is how you say 'forever ago' in a really epic, 'Lord of the Rings' kind of way. It's not just 'matagal na panahon' (a long time ago), it's geological, biblical, 'since the dinosaurs' long. You use this when you want to sound dramatic about how long you've been waiting for your GrabCar. 'Pakiramdam ko **laksa-laksang taon** na akong naghihintay dito!'
usage_notes: A very literary and somewhat archaic phrase used for hyperbole or poetic effect. 'Libu-libong taon' (thousands of years) is more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga fossil na ito ay nabuo **laksa-laksang taon** na ang nakalilipas.","translation":"These fossils were formed **myriads of years** ago."},{"sentence":"Aabutin nang **laksa-laksang taon** bago maabot ng liwanag nito ang Daigdig.","translation":"It will take **tens of thousands of years** before its light reaches Earth."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi pagdalo o pagharap sa isang lugar, pagtitipon, o tungkulin; liban.
original_explanation: 'Yung status mo sa klase noong tinamad kang pumasok, o 'yung ka-team mo sa BPO na laging may "emergency" tuwing Lunes. From the English word "absent."
usage_notes: Commonly used in schools and offices. The more formal Tagalog term is "liban".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bakit ka **absen** kahapon sa klase?","translation":"Why were you **absent** from class yesterday?"},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-**absen** sa meeting, mahalaga 'yun.","translation":"Don't be **absent** from the meeting, it's important."}]

translation: to inflame; to ignite; to intensify (feelings)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapasiklab o pagpapaliyab ng apoy; o sa matalinghagang paraan, ang pagpapatindi ng isang damdamin, tulad ng galit, pag-ibig, o sigasig.
original_explanation: This verb has two modes: literal and hugot. Literal: What you do to the charcoal for the barbecue using a 'pamaypay' (hand fan). Hugot mode: What your ex does when they suddenly message you 'I miss you,' effectively re-igniting old feelings. It's also what a powerful speech does to a crowd—it inflames their passion and makes them want to rally for a cause.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for fire ('alab') or figuratively for emotions ('damdamin'). The 'magpa-' prefix is causative, meaning to cause something to burn or to cause a feeling to intensify.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng gasolina para **magpaalab** ng siga.","translation":"He used gasoline to **ignite** the bonfire."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga salita ay lalong nagpa**paalab** sa galit ng mga tao.","translation":"His words further **inflamed** the anger of the people."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagpapalipad ng sasakyang panghimpapawid; isang piloto.
original_explanation: The original Top Gun. A pilot. It sounds more classic and romantic than 'piloto'. It's what your lolo might have called pilots back in the day. Now, it's also a style of sunglasses. 'Pahiram ng abyador mo, bes, pang-profile pic lang.'
usage_notes: Less common than 'piloto' in modern everyday speech but still understood. Often used in a historical or literary context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang maging isang **abyador** balang araw.","translation":"His dream is to be an **aviator** someday."},{"sentence":"Ang mga unang **abyador** ay tunay na matatapang.","translation":"The first **aviators** were truly brave."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matinding damdamin ng kalungkutan, pighati, o pagkaawa para sa sarili o sa iba.
original_explanation: This isn't just regular 'lungkot'. This is 'sana all' level of sadness, the kind you feel when you've been ghosted after a 3-month 'getting to know' stage. It's a deep, heavy sorrow, like the feeling of dropping your last piece of Jollibee chicken on the floor. A tragic, profound sadness mostly found in poems and old songs.
usage_notes: A deep and literary word for sorrow. Not used in casual conversation. Can mean both personal anguish and deep pity for another.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **hambal** ang kanyang puso sa pagpanaw ng kanyang alagang aso.","translation":"His heart was full of **anguish** at the passing of his pet dog."},{"sentence":"Nakadama siya ng matinding **hambal** para sa mga naulila dahil sa bagyo.","translation":"She felt deep **pity** for those who were orphaned by the typhoon."}]

translation: to make someone happy; to delight
meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng galak o tuwa ang isang tao.
original_explanation: This is what your crush does to you with a single 'seen' message, but also what your mom does when you finally clean your room. It's the act of causing happiness, whether it's from a Jollibee treat or a surprise 13th-month pay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Layunin ng payaso na **pagalakin** ang mga bata sa kaarawan.","translation":"The clown's goal is to **delight** the children at the birthday party."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang **pagalakin** ang kanyang kasintahan matapos ang kanilang pagtatalo.","translation":"He is trying to **make** his girlfriend **happy** after their argument."}]

translation: to cause a commotion, to make a scene
meaning_filipino: Gumawa ng ingay, gulo, o kaguluhan; magpakita ng matinding galit o pagtutol sa paraang nakakagambala.
original_explanation: This is what happens when the WiFi dies during a crucial Netflix episode, or when your mom finds out you failed a subject. It's going full-on 'Hulk mode', making a scene, and letting everyone know you are NOT happy.
usage_notes: Implies a noisy and disruptive display of anger or protest.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **mag-alboroto** ang mga pasahero nang ipahayag na kanselado ang kanilang flight.","translation":"The passengers started **to cause a commotion** when it was announced that their flight was canceled."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mag-alboroto** dito sa ospital; may mga nagpapahinga.","translation":"Don't **make a scene** here in the hospital; there are people resting."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagpapatalas sa isang kagamitan, tulad ng kutsilyo o gunting, sa pamamagitan ng pagkiskis nito sa isang hasaan. Ginagamit din sa metaporikal na paraan para sa pagpapahusay ng isang kasanayan.
original_explanation: Literally, what you do to the kitchen knife before slicing the lechon. Figuratively, what you do to your brain before a board exam or to your basketball skills before a tournament. It's about honing and refining, making something dull into something sharp and effective.
usage_notes: Used for both literal sharpening of tools and figurative sharpening of skills or intellect.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinuha ni tatay ang hasaan para **maghasa** ng itak.","translation":"Dad got the whetstone to **sharpen** the bolo knife."},{"sentence":"Sumali siya sa mga paligsahan upang **maghasa** ng kanyang galing sa pagsulat.","translation":"She joined competitions to **sharpen** her writing skills."}]

translation: to be in agreement; to be in harmony
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng pagkakaisa sa opinyon, damdamin, o kilos; magkasundo.
etymology: From magka- (reciprocal state) + ayon (in accordance with).
original_explanation: The opposite of `magkaaway`. Ito 'yung goal sa group project, 'yung lahat kayo on the same page. To be **magkaayon** is to be in harmony or agreement. It's when your brain, heart, and wallet all agree na "deserve ko 'to" before checking out your online cart.
usage_notes: Can be used as a verb or an adjective to describe a state of mutual agreement or harmony.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **magkaayon** na rin ang kanilang mga pananaw tungkol sa proyekto.","translation":"Finally, their views on the project are now **in agreement**."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga na **magkaayon** ang mag-asawa sa pagpapalaki ng mga anak.","translation":"It is important for a married couple **to be in harmony** in raising their children."}]

meaning_filipino: Ipalaba ang isang tiyak na bagay o mga damit; ang partikular na aksyon ng pagpapalaba.
original_explanation: This is the more direct command form. When you hand over the specific pile of dirty clothes and say, '**Palabahin** mo na 'to, please.' It's more focused than the general request of 'palaba'. This is the 'get it done now' version.
usage_notes: This is a verb in the object-focus imperative mood. It commands or requests that the action of laundering be done to a specific object.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **palabahin** ang uniporme mo para bukas.","translation":"You need **to have** your uniform **laundered** for tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **palabahin** ang mga kurtina.","translation":"Don't forget **to have** the curtains **laundered**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, tao, o pangyayari na walang gaanong halaga, kabuluhan, o bigat.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na "importante" na may unlaping "di-" (hindi).
original_explanation: Eto yung mga bagay na "seen-zoned" mo lang sa buhay. Yung email na galing sa HR tungkol sa "optional" na webinar sa Sabado. Yung opinyon ng tita mong 'di mo naman close. Basically, if it doesn't spark joy, or more importantly, if it doesn't affect your sweldo, it's probably di-importante.
usage_notes: Ang "di-" ay isang kolokyal na pagpapaikli ng "hindi".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para sa kanya, **di-importante** ang mga materyal na bagay.","translation":"For him, material things are **unimportant**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong sayangin ang oras sa mga gawaing **di-importante**.","translation":"Don't waste time on **unimportant** tasks."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mga paniniwala o opinyon na karaniwang taglay ng mga tao tungkol sa isang tao o bagay; ang kabuuang kalidad o katangian na nakikita o hinuhusgahan ng iba.
original_explanation: Your reputasyon is your personal brand, your "resibo" sa mata ng publiko. Ito yung chismis na kumakalat tungkol sa'yo, good or bad. Ingatan mo 'yan, mas mahirap 'yan i-rebuild kaysa sa trust issues mo sa ex mo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga na panatilihing malinis ang iyong **reputasyon** sa trabaho.","translation":"It is important to maintain a clean **reputation** at work."},{"sentence":"Nasira ang **reputasyon** ng kumpanya dahil sa iskandalo.","translation":"The company's **reputation** was ruined because of the scandal."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagsasagawa o pakikilahok sa isang digmaan laban sa isang kaaway, bansa, o pangkat.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate `makipag-away`. We're talking large-scale, organized conflict. Armies, nations, factions. It's what happens when diplomacy fails spectacularly. While it literally means war, Filipinos also use it hyperbolically for any major, all-out conflict, like a corporate war between two rival companies or a full-blown family feud that spans generations.
usage_notes: More formal and grander in scale than 'makipag-away'. It refers to war. 'Makipagdigmaan' is a variant that emphasizes the state or process of being at war. 'Makipagdigma' can be seen as the act of initiating or engaging in that war.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang bansa na huwag **makipagdigma** at sa halip ay idaan sa diplomasya ang usapin.","translation":"The country decided not **to wage war** and instead use diplomacy to resolve the issue."},{"sentence":"Parang ayaw mong **makipagdigma** sa boss mo kung gusto mo pa ng promotion.","translation":"You probably don't want **to wage war against** your boss if you still want a promotion."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghuhukay o pag-aalis ng isang bagay mula sa isang sisidlan gamit ang daliri o isang kasangkapan. Maaari ring tumukoy sa pag-iingat o pagtatago ng isang bagay para sa sarili lamang.
original_explanation: Two meanings here! 1) The act of digging your finger into something, like getting the last bit of Nutella from the jar. 2) Figuratively, it means to hoard or keep something for yourself, like that one coworker who 'kinukulkol' all the good projects and leaves you with the boring ones.
usage_notes: The verb form is more common (e.g., 'kinukulkol', 'kulkolin'). As a noun, it refers to the act itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kinulkol** niya ang huling laman ng garapon ng palaman.","translation":"He **dug out** the last contents of the jar of spread."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **kulkolin** ang lahat ng biyaya para sa iyong sarili.","translation":"Don't **hoard** all the blessings for yourself."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng mineral na may regular na estrukturang atomiko, na nagreresulta sa isang anyong may patag na mga gilid. Ito ay maaaring malinaw o may kulay at madalas ginagamit bilang palamuti o alahas.
etymology: Mula sa "bato" (stone) at salitang Espanyol na "cristal" (crystal).
original_explanation: Your tita's aesthetic. These are the shiny, often colorful rocks people believe can cleanse your aura, attract good vibes, or just look pretty on a shelf. From quartz to amethyst, it's the kind of stone you buy for good juju, not for throwing.
usage_notes: Ginagamit para sa parehong hilaw na kristal at mga naprosesong hiyas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang mangolekta ng iba't ibang uri ng **batong kristal**.","translation":"She loves collecting different kinds of **crystals**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang heolohikong panahon sa Mesozoic Era, tinatayang 201 hanggang 145 milyong taon na ang nakalilipas, na kilala sa pangingibabaw ng mga dinosauro.
etymology: Salin ng pariralang Espanyol na "período Jurásico" o Ingles na "Jurassic period".
original_explanation: 'Yan 'yung ultimate TBT (Throwback Thursday). Panahon ng mga dinosaur, bago pa naimbento ang Wi-Fi, unli-rice, at traffic sa EDSA. Kung may marites noon, ang chismis siguro ay, "Nakita mo ba 'yung bagong T-Rex sa kabilang bundok? Ang laki!"
usage_notes: Isang teknikal na termino sa heolohiya at paleontolohiya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga dambuhalang dinosauro tulad ng Brachiosaurus ay nabuhay noong **Panahong Hurasiko**.","translation":"Giant dinosaurs like the Brachiosaurus lived during the **Jurassic Period**."}]

translation: to conquer, to vanquish, to subdue
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtalo o paggapi sa isang kalaban sa pamamagitan ng lakas o kapangyarihan; ang pagsupil sa isang pag-aalsa o kahirapan.
original_explanation: What you do to your deadlines on a Friday afternoon. Or what Manny Pacquiao does in the ring. It's the ultimate "Sino ka ba?" move. You didn't just win; you dominated. You **lumupig** the competition.
usage_notes: A strong, formal, and somewhat literary word. Often used in historical accounts, epics, or for dramatic effect.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang layunin ng bayani ay **lumupig** sa kasamaan at itaguyod ang katarungan.","translation":"The hero's goal is to **vanquish** evil and uphold justice."},{"sentence":"Nagawa nilang **lumupig** sa mga mananakop pagkatapos ng mahabang pakikibaka.","translation":"They managed to **conquer** the invaders after a long struggle."}]

meaning_filipino: Agwat o espasyo sa pagitan ng dalawang bagay; bakanteng lugar o patlang.
original_explanation: That empty space in your heart after a breakup? That's a 'puwang'. It's also the gap between your teeth, the space between parked cars, or the awkward silence during a family reunion when tita asks about your love life.
usage_notes: Can refer to both physical and metaphorical spaces. 'Patlang' is a close synonym, often used for gaps in text or time.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **puwang** pa ba sa puso mo para sa akin?","translation":"Is there still a **space** in your heart for me?"},{"sentence":"Mag-iwan ka ng sapat na **puwang** kapag pumarada ka.","translation":"Leave enough **space** when you park."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtitipon ng mga kamag-anak at kaibigan upang magbigay-galang at maglamay sa tabi ng kabaong ng isang yumaong tao bago ang libing.
original_explanation: The original Filipino social gathering. It's a sad occasion, pero dito mo rin makikita 'yung reunion ng buong angkan, 'yung mga kapitbahay na nagdadala ng kape at biskwit, at 'yung walang katapusang saklaan. It's where we say our goodbyes, share stories, and check if our crush from the neighborhood is also there.
usage_notes: Mahalaga ang diin (stress) sa pagbigkas upang maiba ito sa "burol" (hill), na may diin sa unang pantig. /bu-ROL/ (wake) vs /BU-rol/ (hill).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pupunta kami sa **burol** ng lolo ng kaibigan ko mamayang gabi.","translation":"We are going to the **wake** of my friend's grandfather tonight."},{"sentence":"Ang huling gabi ng **burol** ay karaniwang dinadaluhan ng maraming tao.","translation":"The last night of the **wake** is usually attended by many people."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang alagad ng sining na lumilikha ng mga karikatura, o mga larawang-guhit na nagpapalabis sa mga katangian ng isang tao o bagay para maging katawa-tawa.
original_explanation: Ito yung artist na kayang-kayang gawing cartoon character ang mukha mo in 5 minutes. Perfect for events, 'pag gusto mong magkaroon ng souvenir na pwedeng ipagyabang o itago depende sa kinalabasan. Sila 'yung nagpapatunay na 'yung ilong mo, pwedeng maging a whole new mountain range sa drawing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha kami ng isang **karikaturista** para sa aming company Christmas party.","translation":"We hired a **caricaturist** for our company Christmas party."},{"sentence":"Isang tanyag na **karikaturista** sa pahayagan ang gumuhit ng editoryal na iyon.","translation":"A famous newspaper **caricaturist** drew that editorial."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbibigay ng puna, opinyon, o reaksyon sa isang bagay, lalo na sa social media o internet. Ito ay nasa pangkasalukuyang panahunan.
original_explanation: The present tense of leaving your unsolicited (or solicited) opinion online. "Tingnan mo si Tita, nagcocomment na naman ng 'Amen' sa mga meme." It's the act of typing your thoughts on a Facebook post, a YouTube video, or a friend's IG photo.
usage_notes: A Taglish verb, present progressive tense. Often spelled as "nagko-comment".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bakit ka **nagcocomment** sa mga post ng ex mo?","translation":"Why **are you commenting** on your ex's posts?"},{"sentence":"Laging **nagcocomment** ang nanay ko sa lahat ng pictures ko sa Facebook.","translation":"My mom always **comments** on all my pictures on Facebook."}]

translation: romantic excitement, butterflies in the stomach
meaning_filipino: Ang pakiramdam ng biglaang, matinding tuwa at pananabik, karaniwang nauugnay sa mga romantikong sitwasyon, na nagdudulot ng bahagyang panginginig o pagngiti.
original_explanation: The Philippines' greatest emotional export, now officially in the Oxford English Dictionary. It's that giddy, butterflies-in-your-stomach feeling you get when your crush looks at you, when your favorite loveteam has a sweet moment on screen, or when you get a "Good morning" text from your BPO-night-shift-special-someone. It’s a full-body blush.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun ("May kilig factor sila.") or an adjective ("Kilig ako!").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Grabe ang **kilig** ko noong hinawakan niya ang kamay ko.","translation":"I felt so much **romantic excitement** when he held my hand."},{"sentence":"Nakakaramdam ka ba ng **kilig** kapag ka-chat mo siya?","translation":"Do you feel those **butterflies in your stomach** when you're chatting with him/her?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbibigay-pansin, paggalang, o pag-iisip sa kapakanan, damdamin, o kalagayan ng iba bago gumawa ng desisyon o aksyon.
etymology: Mula sa ugat na "alang-alang" na nangangahulugang 'for the sake of'.
original_explanation: This is the social skill you use to not play loud music at 2 AM in a condo, or not to post spoilers of the latest K-drama right after it airs. It's thinking 'What would other people feel?' before you act. It's the opposite of being 'bastos' or 'walang pakialam'. It's the core of 'pakikisama'.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin kasama ang "sa" tulad ng "pag-aalang-alang sa..." (consideration for...).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa **pag-aalang-alang** sa mga matatanda, ginawa niyang mas madali ang daanan.","translation":"Out of **consideration** for the elderly, he made the pathway easier to access."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang desisyon ay ginawa nang walang **pag-aalang-alang** sa aming opinyon.","translation":"His decision was made without **regard** for our opinion."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar na natatabunan o sagana sa buhangin.
