original_explanation: It's not just a beach, bes! It's any place that's basically a giant sandbox, like a construction site, a desert-themed resort, or your cat's litter box. The OG beach is the prime example, of course.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglaro ang mga bata sa **buhanginan** sa may dalampasigan.","translation":"The children played in the **sandy area** by the seashore."},{"sentence":"Ginawang **buhanginan** ang isang bahagi ng parke para sa mga bata.","translation":"A part of the park was turned into a **sandpit** for the children."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malambot na telang hinabi, karaniwang gawa sa lana o koton, na kadalasang ginagamit sa paggawa ng kumot, damit, at pamunas.
original_explanation: The OG "basahan" for everything. From wiping spills, cleaning the family car, to being the emergency baby blanket. A piece of pranela in a Filipino household has lived more lives than a cat. It's the ultimate multi-purpose cloth, the unsung hero of 'general cleaning'.
usage_notes: Madalas na tumutukoy sa telang pamunas sa kontekstong Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakikuha ng **pranela** at punasan mo ang mesa.","translation":"Please get the **flannel** cloth and wipe the table."},{"sentence":"Malambot ang tela ng **pranela** na kumot niya.","translation":"The fabric of her **flannel** blanket is soft."}]

meaning_filipino: Mabilis at magaang na ihagis o ihampas ang isang bagay, karaniwan gamit ang dulo ng daliri o isang maliit na instrumento.
etymology: From Tagalog 'i-' (causative/instrumental prefix) + 'paltik' (a flick, a snap; also refers to an unlicensed firearm).
original_explanation: Think of flicking a rubber band at your classmate, or how a horse trainer snaps a whip. It's a quick, sharp motion. It's the sound your finger makes when you snap it, but as a verb for an object. 'Ipaltik mo nga 'yang alikabok sa mesa.' (Flick the dust off the table.)
usage_notes: The word 'paltik' by itself can also mean an illegally manufactured firearm, but in this verb form, it usually refers to the flicking motion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marunong siyang **ipaltik** ang latigo nang hindi tumatama sa kabayo.","translation":"He knows how to **snap** the whip without hitting the horse."},{"sentence":"**Ipaltik** mo lang ang daliri mo para makuha ang atensyon niya.","translation":"Just **snap** your fingers to get his attention."}]

translation: to be laughed at; to be ridiculed
meaning_filipino: Maging paksa ng katatawanan, panunuya, o pangungutya mula sa ibang tao.
original_explanation: That feeling when you trip in the middle of the mall, or when you confidently answer the wrong thing in class. It’s that moment of pure awkwardness where you wish the ground would swallow you whole. The reason why you replay embarrassing moments in your head at 3 AM.
usage_notes: Often used to express the fear of being embarrassed or made fun of in a social situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang sumayaw sa entablado dahil takot siyang **mapagtawanan**.","translation":"He doesn't want to dance on stage because he's afraid of **being laughed at**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pagkaing-kalye na gawa sa giniling na karne o isda na hinaluan ng mga gulay at pampalasa, binalot sa balat na gawa sa arina (bean curd sheet), at karaniwang ipiniprito.
etymology: From Hokkien Chinese 雞捲 (koe-kńg) or Lán-nâng-ōe 五香 (ngó͘-hiong).
original_explanation: The OG street food before fishball became the star. That brown, elongated thingy swimming in hot oil, waiting to be drowned in sweet and spicy sauce. You're not sure what's in it, but for 10 pesos per stick, you're willing to take the risk. Best eaten with friends while standing on a sidewalk.
usage_notes: A popular Filipino street food. Often sold alongside fish balls, squid balls, and kwek-kwek.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pabili po ng sampung pisong **kikiam**, 'yung maraming sauce.","translation":"I'd like to buy ten pesos' worth of **kikiam**, with lots of sauce."},{"sentence":"Masarap isawsaw ang **kikiam** sa maanghang na suka.","translation":"It's delicious to dip **kikiam** in spicy vinegar."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng hayop na may hasang, kaliskis, at palikpik na karaniwang naninirahan sa tubig.
original_explanation: The main character of every Dampa and palengke. From the humble galunggong (GG) to the fancy salmon, it's the go-to ulam when you're tired of chicken or pork. Also, a term for a small-time player in a big game.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumunta si nanay sa palengke para bumili ng sariwang **isda**.","translation":"Mom went to the market to buy fresh **fish**."},{"sentence":"Maraming uri ng **isda** ang mahuhuli sa karagatan ng Pilipinas.","translation":"Many kinds of **fish** can be caught in the seas of the Philippines."}]

translation: defamation, slander, libel, damage to one's reputation
meaning_filipino: Ang pagyurak o pagdudungis sa dangal, karangalan, o mabuting reputasyon ng isang tao sa pamamagitan ng malisyosong pahayag o tsismis.
etymology: A set phrase literally meaning "damage of name".
original_explanation: This is what happens when Marites goes too far. It's the official term for getting your name dragged through the mud. It's not just chismis, it's career-ending, friendship-ruining, 'I'll see you in court!' level of reputation damage.
usage_notes: A specific legal and social concept often translated as libel (written) or slander (spoken). It is a more formal and serious term than "paninira".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaari kang kasuhan ng **kasiraan ng pangalan** dahil sa iyong mga paratang.","translation":"You can be sued for **defamation** because of your accusations."},{"sentence":"Iniiwasan niyang gumawa ng anumang bagay na magdudulot ng **kasiraan ng pangalan** sa kanyang pamilya.","translation":"He avoids doing anything that would cause **damage to his family's reputation**."}]

translation: to let subside; to cause to recede
meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng paraan o paghihintay upang mabawasan ang tindi, lakas, o dami ng isang bagay, tulad ng baha, galit, o lagnat.
etymology: From mag- (actor-focus verb prefix) + pa- (causative prefix) + hupa (subside, recede).
original_explanation: That feeling when you're super angry ("gigil") and you take deep breaths to calm down—that's pagpapahupa of your anger. It's also what you wait for after a typhoon: "Hintayin nating magpahupa ng baha." It's the act of letting things chill out, whether it's floodwaters, a fever, or your friend's drama.
usage_notes: Can be used for emotions, physical conditions (fever, swelling), or natural phenomena (flood, storm). The actor can be the one causing the subsiding, or it can be used intransitively meaning "to wait for it to subside".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uminom siya ng gamot para **magpahupa** ng lagnat.","translation":"He drank medicine to **make** the fever **subside**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magpahupa** muna ng galit bago tayo mag-usap.","translation":"We need to **let** our anger **subside** first before we talk."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pag-aani ng mga pananim, lalo na ng palay, sa pamamagitan ng pagputol gamit ang isang karit o lingkaw.
original_explanation: The OG 'reaping.' Before combine harvesters, this was how our ancestors got their rice. It's hard, back-breaking work under the sun, often done with a scythe. Think of the grim reaper, but for palay.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to harvesting grains like rice or wheat by cutting the stalks. It's a subset of the more general term 'pag-aani' (harvesting).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula na ang **paggapas** ng palay sa kanilang bukirin.","translation":"The **harvesting** of rice stalks has begun in their field."},{"sentence":"Tulung-tulong ang mga magsasaka sa **paggapas**.","translation":"The farmers are helping each other with the **reaping**."}]

translation: to have something happen to (a vague term)
meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na pandiwa na ginagamit bilang pamalit sa ibang pandiwa kapag hindi masabi o maalala ang eksaktong salita; magkaroon ng anuman, mapahamak.
original_explanation: The ultimate filler verb. It’s what you say when you don't know, can't remember, or don't want to say the actual verb. 'Anong nangyari sa'yo?' 'Na-ano kasi ako...' It's the verbal equivalent of a loading screen or a shrugged shoulder. It can mean anything from 'I tripped' to 'I got into a complicated situation.'
usage_notes: Highly colloquial and informal. Its meaning is almost entirely dependent on context and non-verbal cues. Can also be a euphemism for getting hurt or being in an accident.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingat ka sa pag-uwi, baka ka **maano** diyan sa daan.","translation":"Be careful on your way home, something **might happen to you** on the road."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi ako **maaano**.","translation":"Don't worry, **nothing will happen** to me."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang akronim mula sa Ingles na "laughing out loud" na ginagamit sa pasulat na komunikasyon upang ipahiwatig ang pagtawa o katuwaan.
etymology: Akronim mula sa Ingles na "laughing out loud".
original_explanation: The universal sign for "I'm mildly amused but too lazy to type 'hahaha'." It's the default reaction to a meme your tita sends in the family group chat. Sometimes used sarcastically. "Nag-reply siya after 3 days. Lol."
usage_notes: Ginagamit lamang sa di-pormal na pasulat na komunikasyon tulad ng text at social media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang cute ng aso mo, **lol**.","translation":"Your dog is cute, **lol**."},{"sentence":"Nahulog ako sa upuan. **Lol**.","translation":"I fell off my chair. **Lol**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa panlabinlimang posisyon o pagkakasunod-sunod sa isang serye.
original_explanation: Ah, the 15th of the month. A day of great importance. For some, 'petsa de peligro' is over, for others, it's just beginning. It’s the day the sweldo drops, the bills are due, and the chat group suddenly becomes active with "Kain sa labas?"
usage_notes: Used to denote the 15th item in a sequence. Can be written as "ika-15". The day of the month when many Filipinos get paid.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing **ikalabinlima** ng buwan ang aming sahod.","translation":"Our salary comes every **fifteenth** of the month."},{"sentence":"Siya ang **ikalabinlimang** aplikante na aming nainterbyu.","translation":"She was the **fifteenth** applicant we interviewed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang daanan sa loob ng ilong kung saan dumadaloy ang hangin at ang sipon o uhog.
original_explanation: Basically, ito 'yung "expressway" ng sipon mo. Kapag barado 'to, parang EDSA rush hour sa ilong mo. Diyan din dumadaan 'yung hangin na nilalanghap mo, kaya alagaan mo 'yan.
usage_notes: A very literal and somewhat clinical term. Not commonly used in everyday conversation. "Butas ng ilong" (nostril) is more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa sipon, barado ang kanyang **daluyang-uhog**.","translation":"Because of his cold, his **nasal passage** is blocked."},{"sentence":"Nililinis ng doktor ang **daluyang-uhog** ng pasyente.","translation":"The doctor is cleaning the patient's **nasal passage**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos o kalagayan ng paglabas ng sipon o uhog mula sa ilong.
original_explanation: That gross but unavoidable thing that happens when you have a cold, cry too hard, or eat something super spicy. 'Hala, nag-uuhog ka!' is the polite way of saying 'You've got a booger.' It's the body's way of oversharing.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang pandiwang naglalarawan ng kalagayan. Hindi mo ito aktibong 'ginagawa', kundi ito ay nangyayari sa iyo. Madalas gamitin sa anyong pangkasalukuyan na `nag-uuhog`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ako makahinga nang maayos dahil **nag-uuhog** ako.","translation":"I can't breathe properly because I **have a runny nose**."},{"sentence":"Pinunasan niya ang ilong ng bata dahil ito ay **nag-uuhog**.","translation":"She wiped the child's nose because it **was runny**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang masiglang sayaw na nagmula sa Bohemia noong ika-19 na siglo, na isinasayaw nang may dalawang hakbang at isang hop sa duple meter.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'polca' o Ingles na 'polka'.
original_explanation: This is your lolo and lola's jam! It's a bouncy, happy folk dance that was super popular back in the day. Think of fiestas and traditional gatherings. It's not the TikTok dance of today, but it's got its own classic charm. The music sounds like it belongs in a European carnival.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy rin sa musika para sa sayaw. Ang 'polka dots' (bilog-bilog na disenyo) ay isang kaugnay na konsepto ngunit ang salitang 'polka' mismo ay karaniwang nangangahulugang sayaw.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsayaw ng **polka** ang mga mag-aaral para sa kanilang presentasyon sa Araw ng Wika.","translation":"The students danced the **polka** for their presentation on Language Day."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagbabago, pagdaragdag, o pag-aalis sa isang panukalang batas, kontrata, o anumang opisyal na dokumento.
original_explanation: Parang yung 'final_final_v2_revised_FINAL.docx' mo sa thesis. Ito yung mga pagbabagong isinisingit sa batas o rules. Sa chismis, ito yung "update" sa kwento na binigay ni Marites. "May **susog** ako sa chismis kahapon..."
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa mga kontekstong legal, pambatasan, o pormal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpanukala ang senador ng isang **susog** sa kasalukuyang batas trapiko.","translation":"The senator proposed an **amendment** to the current traffic law."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan pa ng komite ang mga iminungkahing **susog**.","translation":"The committee is still studying the proposed **amendments**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang partikular na pagpapahayag ng kawalan ng pagnanais o interes sa pagkain.
etymology: Mula sa pariralang "walang gana" at dinugtungan ng pandiwang "kumain" (to eat).
original_explanation: This is the specific diagnosis when you're heartbroken. Your friends offer you Jollibee, milk tea, pizza... but you just shake your head sadly. Your stomach is in a knot, and not even your comfort food can fix it. Also happens when you have the flu or you're *sawi*.
usage_notes: A very common phrase that specifically refers to the lack of appetite for food, distinguishing it from the general lack of enthusiasm ('walang-gana').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Simula nang magkasakit siya, palagi siyang **walang-ganang kumain**.","translation":"Ever since she got sick, she's always had **no appetite to eat**."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa stress sa trabaho, ako ay **walang-ganang kumain**.","translation":"Because of work stress, I **have no appetite to eat**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang marka, linya, o drowing na nilikha sa isang ibabaw, karaniwang gamit ang panulat, lapis, o anumang kagamitang panulat.
original_explanation: It's a line. The one you draw on paper, the one you cross when you make your parents mad ('sumusobra ka na sa guhit!'), or the line you see in your crush's palm when you pretend to be a palm reader. Also, a drawing or sketch. It's the OG form of art before Canva.
usage_notes: Can refer to a simple line, a drawing, or a metaphorical boundary.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong matutong gumawa ng **guhit** na katulad ng mga nasa komiks.","translation":"I want to learn how to make **drawings** like the ones in comics."},{"sentence":"Naglagay sila ng **guhit** sa sahig upang malaman kung saan ang pila.","translation":"They put a **line** on the floor to show where the queue is."}]

translation: to be able to cross a narrow bridge or path
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang tumawid o maglakad sa isang makitid na daanan, tulad ng tulay na kawayan o alambre.
etymology: From "maka-" (ability prefix) + "panulay" (act of crossing a bridge, from "tulay").
original_explanation: This is your life skill test in the province. Can you walk across that shaky bamboo bridge without falling into the 'sapa' (creek)? If yes, you can 'makapanulay'. It's the original Filipino ninja warrior challenge.
usage_notes: This specifically refers to crossing on a narrow, often precarious, bridge or tightrope.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit madilim, **nakapanulay** pa rin siya sa tulay na kawayan.","translation":"Even if it was dark, he was still **able to cross the bamboo bridge**."},{"sentence":"Hindi lahat ay kayang **makapanulay** sa sirang tulay na iyon.","translation":"Not everyone can **cross that broken bridge**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na nakaayos nang paikot-ikot o nakapulupot, tulad ng lubid, alambre, o ahas.
original_explanation: That tangled mess your earphones become in your pocket? That's a 'likaw'. The way a snake rests, or how you roll up the garden hose or Christmas lights? That's also a 'likaw'. It's any circular, winding, looping formation. It's also a great way to describe the traffic on EDSA—a long, slow-moving 'likaw' of cars.
usage_notes: The verb form is "lumikaw" (to coil) or "ilikaw" (to coil something).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malaking **likaw** ng ahas ang nakita niya sa damuhan.","translation":"He saw a large **coil** of snake in the grass."},{"sentence":"Ayusin mo ang **likaw** ng alambre para hindi magkabuhol-buhol.","translation":"Fix the **winding** of the wire so it doesn't get tangled."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaikling salita para sa "delusional"; tumutukoy sa isang tao na may maling paniniwala o pantasya na malayo sa katotohanan, lalo na sa konteksto ng pag-ibig o paghanga.
etymology: Clipped form of the English word "delusional," popularized by K-Pop and internet fan culture.
original_explanation: Your friend who thinks their K-Pop bias is their soulmate? That's peak delulu. It's when your imagination is working overtime, creating scenarios that are, let's be real, never gonna happen. It's the state of being happily living in your own fantasy world.
usage_notes: Often used humorously and self-deprecatingly to describe one's own fantasies.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Medyo **delulu** ka na, bes, hindi ka pa nire-replyan pero kinikilig ka na.","translation":"You're getting a bit **delusional**, girl; he hasn't even replied but you're already feeling giddy."},{"sentence":"Okay lang maging **delulu** minsan, libre naman mangarap.","translation":"It's okay to be **delusional** sometimes, it's free to dream."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagdadala o paghahawak ng isang bagay mula sa isang lugar patungo sa iba.
original_explanation: This is your default "carry" verb. It's what you do with your bag, your payong, or your feelings for your crush. "Mag-**dala** ka ng jacket" is the official motto of Pinoy moms everywhere. It can also mean emotional baggage, like the 'hugot' you carry from your ex.
usage_notes: Ang 'dala' ay isang pangkalahatang termino para sa pagdadala ng isang bagay. Ang 'magdala' ay ang anyo ng pandiwa na nakapokus sa aktor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutan **dala**hin ang iyong mga libro.","translation":"Don't forget to **bring** your books."}]

translation: to become peaceful; to become calm/tranquil
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-abot sa isang kalagayan ng kapayapaan, katahimikan, o kapanatagan. Ito ay tumutukoy sa isang kilos na natapos na.
original_explanation: What you hope your life becomes after payday, but then the bills arrive. It’s that feeling of calm after a storm, or when you finally log off after a toxic day of Zoom meetings. The state of your soul after a good massage or a successful "Sana all" moment.
usage_notes: A more poetic or formal word for having become peaceful. Completed aspect (past tense).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumiwasay** ang kanyang kalooban matapos magdasal.","translation":"His inner self **became peaceful** after praying."},{"sentence":"Nang umalis ang maingay na bisita, **tumiwasay** din ang bahay.","translation":"When the noisy visitor left, the house finally **became tranquil**."}]

meaning_filipino: Magsalita nang pabulong at hindi malinaw, karaniwan bilang pagpapahayag ng pagtutol o reklamo.
original_explanation: This is what you do under your breath when your boss gives you another task at 4:59 PM. It’s the low-volume, "I'm complaining but I don't want you to *really* hear me" language. "May narinig akong umungot nung sinabi kong may meeting sa Sabado."
usage_notes: Similar to 'bumulong' (to whisper) but 'umungot' specifically carries a negative connotation of complaint or dissatisfaction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **umungot** diyan at gawin mo na lang ang pinapagawa sa iyo.","translation":"Don't just **grumble** there and do what you're told."},{"sentence":"Palihim siyang **umungot** tungkol sa dami ng kanyang takdang-aralin.","translation":"He secretly **mumbled** about the amount of his homework."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong labis na mapansinin sa mga maliliit na detalye; maselan o pihikan sa mga bagay-bagay.
original_explanation: Your boss who wants the report's font size to be 11.5 instead of 12. Your tita who rearranges the throw pillows every time you sit down. The client who has 101 "minor revisions." They are *makuriri*. It's being detail-oriented to the point of being fussy or difficult. It's the human embodiment of "the devil is in the details."
usage_notes: Can be positive (meticulous, thorough) or negative (fussy, nitpicky) depending on the context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Makuriri** ang kliyente kaya't dapat pulido ang bawat detalye ng proyekto.","translation":"The client is **meticulous**, so every detail of the project must be polished."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalapat o pag-eempleyo ng isang bagay, kasanayan, o ideya para sa isang partikular na layunin o gawain.
original_explanation: Parang feelings mo para sa kanya, 'gamitin' mo lang daw 'pag kailangan ka niya. This is the command form of 'to use something.' From your office ID to your 'special skills' on your resume, you need to know how to use them. It's the action of making something functional.
usage_notes: Often used in the imperative mood (as a command). The phrase 'gamitin sa masama' means 'to use for evil/bad purposes'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **gamitin** mo ang tamang paraan sa paghiwa ng sibuyas.","translation":"Please, **use** the correct method for slicing onions."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hahayaang **gamitin** ka ng ibang tao para sa kanilang pansariling interes.","translation":"Don't let other people **use** you for their own personal interests."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manggagawa na tumatangging sumali sa welga o unyon, o isang taong nagtatrabaho kapalit ng mga manggagawang nagwewelga.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'sipsip' or traitor in a workplace protest. When everyone's outside chanting for better pay, the iskirol is the one who crosses the picket line to go to work, earning the side-eye of all their co-workers. Not a good look.
usage_notes: A highly negative and politically charged term, used to refer to a strikebreaker.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinawag siyang **iskirol** ng mga kasamahan niya dahil pumasok siya sa trabaho sa gitna ng welga.","translation":"His colleagues called him a **scab** because he went to work in the middle of the strike."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing banal o sagrado ang isang bagay, lugar, o tao sa pamamagitan ng isang ritwal o seremonya.
original_explanation: This is what a priest does to water to turn it into holy water. It's the act of leveling something up from "regular" to "blessed." Think of it as the spiritual version of getting verified on Instagram—suddenly, it's official, it's special, it's #blessed.
usage_notes: Primarily used in a religious or ceremonial context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **banalin** ng pari ang bagong kapilya bago ito gamitin.","translation":"The priest needs **to sanctify** the new chapel before it can be used."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan o sistema na nagpapalamig at nag-aalis ng halumigmig sa hangin sa loob ng isang gusali o sasakyan.
original_explanation: The most important appliance in the Philippines, aka the savior of humanity from April to June. It's the reason your Meralco bill is sky-high but also the reason you can sleep at night without becoming a human puddle. The sound of the aircon is the modern Filipino lullaby.
usage_notes: This English loanword is used universally in the Philippines. The formal Filipino term, 'pampalamig,' is rarely used in this context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakibuksan mo ang **aircon**, sobrang init!","translation":"Please turn on the **aircon**, it's so hot!"},{"sentence":"Malakas ba sa kuryente ang **aircon** ninyo?","translation":"Does your **aircon** consume a lot of electricity?"}]

meaning_filipino: Pagiging hindi makapagsalita o makakibo, karaniwan ay dahil sa matinding hiya, pagkagulat, o pagkalito.
original_explanation: Yung moment na tinawag ka ni Ma'am para mag-recite pero wala kang maisagot. Or when your crush talks to you and your brain just blue-screens. You're not physically mute, you're just... shookt. That's being imid. Your tongue has left the group.
usage_notes: Nagpapahiwatig ng pansamantalang kawalan ng kakayahang magsalita, iba sa pagiging 'pipi' (mute).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **imid** siya nang mahuli sa kanyang kasinungalingan.","translation":"He became **speechless** when he was caught in his lie."},{"sentence":"Napahinto siya at nanatiling **imid** sa harap ng entablado.","translation":"She stopped and remained **speechless** in front of the stage."}]

translation: to ask for news; to catch up on news
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtatanong o pagkuha ng impormasyon tungkol sa mga kasalukuyang pangyayari o kaganapan.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "maki-" (paghiling) at salitang ugat na "balita" (news).
original_explanation: The polite term for 'Anong chismis?' It's what you do when you log back into Facebook after a week-long digital detox or when you bump into an old friend at the mall. 'Uy, makibalita nga, anong nangyari sa series finale?'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumawag siya sa probinsya para **makibalita** tungkol sa kalagayan ng kanyang mga kamag-anak.","translation":"He called the province to **ask for news** about the condition of his relatives."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangatnig na ginagamit upang ipakita ang pagkontra o pagkakaiba sa dalawang sugnay o ideya. Ito ay pormal na katumbas ng 'pero'.
etymology: Believed to be a contraction of "ngayon" (now) and "at" (and), evolving into its current meaning.
original_explanation: This is the formal, "nasa thesis defense ka" version of 'pero'. You use 'nguni't' when you want to sound smart and serious, like when you say "Mahal kita, nguni't kailangan ko munang unahin ang career ko." It’s the ‘but’ that carries weight, drama, and a hint of a classic Filipino movie monologue.
usage_notes: 'Nguni't' is more formal and literary than its common counterpart, 'pero'. The apostrophe is often omitted in modern writing ('ngunit').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais sana niyang sumama, **nguni't** may mahalaga siyang gagawin.","translation":"He wanted to come, **but** he had something important to do."},{"sentence":"Marami siyang pera, **nguni't** hindi siya masaya.","translation":"He has a lot of money, **however** he is not happy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan lumalapag at lumilipad ang mga sasakyang panghimpapawid tulad ng eroplano.
etymology: From 'lipad' (fly) + '-an' (locative suffix). Literally, "a place for flying."
original_explanation: The place of tearful goodbyes and joyful reunions. Home of overpriced coffee, terminal fees, and the constant fear of having an overweight baggage. For OFWs and their families, this place is a symbol of both sacrifice and hope. Also known as NAIA, where "patience is a virtue" is a required skill.
usage_notes: Can also refer to any airfield, not just a commercial airport.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pupunta kami sa **paliparan** para sunduin ang aking tiya.","translation":"We are going to the **airport** to pick up my aunt."},{"sentence":"Ang Ninoy Aquino International Airport ay ang pangunahing **paliparan** sa Pilipinas.","translation":"The Ninoy Aquino International Airport is the main **airport** in the Philippines."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tuyong sekresyon na namumuo sa sulok ng mga mata, lalo na habang natutulog.
original_explanation: That crusty stuff in the corner of your eyes when you wake up. The first thing your friends will point out in the morning with a 'Uy, may muta ka pa!' It's the universe's way of telling you to wash your face before you face your Zoom call.
usage_notes: A very common, everyday word. Also known as 'kulabat' in other dialects.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Punasan mo ang iyong **muta** bago ka lumabas ng bahay.","translation":"Wipe the **sleep** from your eyes before you leave the house."},{"sentence":"Nagising siyang maraming **muta** dahil sa mahabang tulog.","translation":"He woke up with a lot of **rheum** because of a long sleep."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglalakbay sa dagat o anumang anyong tubig gamit ang isang sasakyang pandagat, lalo na ang may layag.
original_explanation: The OG way of island hopping before Cebu Pacific piso fares. It's the act of traveling by sea, which sounds romantic until you get seasick. Today, it's more of a metaphor for life's journey, navigating the rough seas of adulting.
usage_notes: Often used in a literal sense for sea travel or metaphorically for a journey or adventure.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paglalayag** ni Magellan ay isang mahalagang bahagi ng kasaysayan.","translation":"Magellan's **voyage** is an important part of history."},{"sentence":"Naging mahirap ang kanilang **paglalayag** dahil sa malakas na bagyo.","translation":"Their **sailing** became difficult because of the strong typhoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan o kagamitan na ginagamit sa paghilis o pagkuha ng hibla mula sa mga halaman tulad ng abaka.
original_explanation: Imagine you're making a rope from a plant. You need a tool to scrape off all the non-fibrous gunk and get to the good stuff. That tool is a hagutan. It's the OG way of extracting fiber before fancy machines took over. It's the Tita of textile tools.
usage_notes: Specific to agriculture and traditional crafts, particularly related to abaca and other fiber-producing plants.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matibay ang **hagutan** na gawa sa matigas na kahoy at bakal.","translation":"The **fiber-stripping tool** made of hard wood and metal is durable."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng lakas sa paggamit ng **hagutan** para makuha ang hibla ng abaka.","translation":"One needs strength to use the **fiber-stripping tool** to extract abaca fibers."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nakikilahok sa isang laro, palakasan, o anumang uri ng kumpetisyon.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'mang-' at ang salitang-ugat na 'laro' (play/game), na may pag-uulit ng unang pantig ng ugat ('la').
original_explanation: Your MVP, your teammate, or that 'bida-bida' on the other team. A 'manlalaro' is anyone who plays a game—from basketball and Mobile Legends to the games of the heart (charot!). They're the ones who know the thrill of victory and the agony of a 'lag' connection.
usage_notes: A very general term covering anyone who plays a game, sport, or even a musical instrument.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bawat **manlalaro** sa koponan ay dapat magtulungan.","translation":"Every **player** on the team must cooperate."},{"sentence":"Siya ay isang propesyonal na **manlalaro** ng e-sports.","translation":"He is a professional e-sports **player**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang agwat o espasyo sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang punto, tao, o bagay.
original_explanation: It's the distance between you and your sweldo. It's the reason you need to book a Grab instead of walking. In relationships, 'layo' is the "I need space" conversation starter. It's the physical or emotional gap. "Ang layo ng tingin mo," means you're spacing out, probably thinking about your crush or your debts.
usage_notes: Very common root word used in various forms like "malayo" (far), "lumayo" (to move away). "Distansya" is a common Spanish-derived synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **layo** ng Maynila mula sa Baguio?","translation":"What is the **distance** of Manila from Baguio?"},{"sentence":"Kahit malaki ang **layo** natin sa isa't isa, hindi magbabago ang nararamdaman ko.","translation":"Even if our **distance** from each other is great, my feelings won't change."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking gumaganap ng isang papel o karakter sa isang dula, pelikula, o iba pang pagtatanghal.
original_explanation: Siya yung bida na lalaki sa paborito mong teleserye o pelikula. Sila yung mga pinagpapantasyahan mong maging jowa, tulad nina Piolo Pascual o Daniel Padilla. Sa totoong buhay, lahat tayo pwedeng maging aktor sa sarili nating drama.
usage_notes: Tiyak na tumutukoy sa lalaking gumaganap. Ang pambabae ay "aktres".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang maging isang sikat na **aktor** sa Hollywood.","translation":"He dreams of becoming a famous **actor** in Hollywood."},{"sentence":"Ang gumanap na **aktor** sa pelikula ay napakahusay.","translation":"The **actor** who performed in the movie was excellent."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasuotan o kombinasyon ng mga damit na ang lahat ng bahagi ay binili mula sa ukay-ukay.
etymology: From Tagalog 'ukay' (to dig, rummage) + English 'fit' (short for outfit).
original_explanation: Your OOTD (Outfit of the Day) but make it sustainable and budget-friendly. It's the art of looking like a million bucks while your whole ensemble costs less than a milk tea with extra pearls. The ultimate flex for the 'diskarte' fashionista.
usage_notes: Often used with hashtags like #UkayFit or #UkayChallenge on social media to showcase an outfit composed of thrifted clothes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng **ukay fit** mo ngayon, mukhang mamahalin!","translation":"Your **thrifted outfit** today is beautiful, it looks expensive!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang arko o kurbadong istruktura na nagsisilbing kisame o bubong ng isang gusali, karaniwan sa mga simbahan o malalaking bulwagan.
original_explanation: Think of the ceiling of a grand, old church or a bank's vault. It's that fancy, curved roof that makes you feel small and poor. It's the architectural equivalent of a 'sana all' moment when you look up. Not your typical condo ceiling.
usage_notes: A formal, architectural term. Not used in everyday conversation unless discussing architecture or old buildings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakamamangha ang pinta sa **bobeda** ng simbahan.","translation":"The painting on the church's **dome** is amazing."},{"sentence":"Ang mga alahas ay nakatago sa isang matibay na **bobeda**.","translation":"The jewels are kept in a strong **vault**."}]

meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang alisin sa isipan o alaala ang isang tao, bagay, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: 'Yung goal mo after ng isang masakit na breakup. "Sana all makalimot agad." Ito 'yung active process of trying to move on, unlike 'makalimutan' which is often accidental. The ultimate #MoveOnChallenge.
usage_notes: Implies the ability or capacity to forget, often used in a hopeful or aspirational sense. Focuses on the person doing the forgetting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paano kaya ako **makalilimot** sa lahat ng sakit na idinulot niya?","translation":"How can I **be able to forget** all the pain he caused?"},{"sentence":"Kahit anong gawin niya, hindi siya **makalimot** sa kanyang nakaraan.","translation":"No matter what he does, he cannot **forget** his past."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang akronim para sa "Kulang sa Pansin," na tumutukoy sa isang tao na labis na naghahanap ng atensyon mula sa iba.
original_explanation: The official term for that friend who posts "sad but not telling why" on Facebook. It stands for "Kulang sa Pansin" (Lacking in Attention). It's what you call someone who does dramatic, loud, or annoying things just so people will look at them. Think of it as the Filipino version of being "extra" for clout.
usage_notes: Isang kolokyal na termino na madalas gamitin sa social media at sa pang-araw-araw na usapan. Maaaring ituring na bahagyang mapanukso o mapanghusga.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang pansinin, **KSP** lang 'yan.","translation":"Don't mind him/her, they're just an **attention-seeker**."},{"sentence":"Nag-post na naman siya ng cryptic message. Ang **KSP** talaga.","translation":"He/She posted another cryptic message. Such an **attention-seeker**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na nangangahulugang kasinungalingan, imbento, o pagmamalabis.
etymology: Mula sa African-American Vernacular English (AAVE) na "cap", na pinaikli mula sa "capping" (to lie or exaggerate).
original_explanation: The Gen Z word for 'kasinungalingan' or 'bola'. If someone says something that sounds too good to be true, you say 'That's cap!'. The opposite is 'No cap', which is the modern way of saying 'Promise, cross my heart, hope to die' or 'Walang halong biro'. It's the ultimate lie detector test in a single word.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa pariralang "No cap" upang bigyang-diin ang katotohanan ng isang pahayag.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sabi niya, kaya niyang buhatin 'yun mag-isa? Malaking **cap** 'yun!","translation":"He said he can lift that by himself? That's a big **lie**!"},{"sentence":"No **cap**, ito na ang pinakamasarap na adobo na natikman ko.","translation":"**No lie**, this is the most delicious adobo I have ever tasted."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng matinding kahirapan o pagiging dukha; kakulangan sa mga pangunahing pangangailangan sa buhay.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'isang kahig, isang tuka' lifestyle, but make it chronic. It's when your wallet has more cobwebs than a horror movie set, and 'petsa de peligro' is every day. It's the level of broke that inspires teleseryes and political campaigns.
usage_notes: A more formal and intense word for poverty than 'kahirapan'. Often used in literary or formal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Layunin ng pamahalaan na wakasan ang **karukhaan** sa bansa.","translation":"The government's goal is to end **poverty** in the country."},{"sentence":"Maraming pamilya ang nagtitiis sa matinding **karukhaan**.","translation":"Many families are suffering from extreme **destitution**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ayusin o atasan ang mga tao na maghalinhinan sa paggawa ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'sharing is caring' verb. It's what your mom tells you and your siblings when you're fighting over the video game controller: 'Mag-turnuhan kayo!' Or in the office, when the workload is insane, the manager might have to **paturnuhin** the team for the night shift. It’s about fairness and not hogging all the fun (or the work).
usage_notes: A causative verb. It means to cause or arrange for people to take turns.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Paturnuhin** mo sila sa pagbabantay ng tindahan.","translation":"**Have them take turns** watching the store."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **paturnuhin** ang paggamit ng computer.","translation":"We need to **arrange turns** for using the computer."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkilos ng pagdugtong-dugtong sa mga tela o pag-ayos ng sira sa damit gamit ang sinulid at karayom.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa ng lola mo sa lumang damit mo para magamit ulit. Or 'yung ginagawa ng sastre para sa wedding gown mo. Kung marunong kang **tumahi**, malaki matitipid mo sa pagpapa-alter ng pantalon. It's the OG life skill before fast fashion took over.
usage_notes: This is the completed aspect (past tense). The more common verb forms are 'manahi' or 'magtahi'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **tumahi** ng sarili niyang bestida para sa party.","translation":"She was the one who **sewed** her own dress for the party."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **tumahi** sa butas ng medyas ko?","translation":"Who **sewed** the hole in my sock?"}]

translation: to taste like, to have a flavor of
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon o pagpapahiwatig ng isang partikular na lasa.
etymology: From the root word 'lasa' (taste, flavor) + the '-um-' infix.
original_explanation: When you're trying your friend's "experimental" adobo and you have to describe it. "Hmm, lumasa siyang... interesting." It's the polite way of saying something has a distinct, and not always good, taste. It's the flavor reveal.
usage_notes: Often used to describe the flavor profile that has emerged in a dish. Distinct from 'tikman' (to taste something) and 'lasahan' (to add flavor to something). 'Lumasa' is about the flavor *coming out*.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lumasa** ang pait ng ampalaya sa buong ginisado.","translation":"The bitterness of the bitter melon could be **tasted** throughout the entire stir-fry."},{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **lumasa** na rin ang tamis ng tagumpay.","translation":"Finally, the sweetness of success can be **tasted**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging malinis, walang dumi, o anumang bahid. Tumutukoy rin ito sa kadalisayan ng puso o isipan.
original_explanation: It's what your mom nags you about every Sunday morning. "Iyong kwarto, anong kalinisan ang pinagsasabi mo diyan?!" It's also the goal of every "new year, new me" post that involves decluttering, both physically and emotionally (goodbye, toxic ex!).
usage_notes: Can refer to physical cleanliness or moral/spiritual purity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kalinisan** ay kalahati ng kalusugan.","translation":"**Cleanliness** is half of health."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang kilos, pananalita, o anyo na itinuturing na katulad ng sa isang bakla, kadalasan sa paraang mapanukso o mapanghusga.
original_explanation: This is an old-school, often judgy way to describe someone's actions as stereotypically gay. It's the exaggerated hand gestures, the "maldita" tone, the "kikay" walk. While the LGBTQ+ community has reclaimed many terms, this one often still carries a negative, mocking tone, like saying "acting so gay." It's less about identity and more about performative stereotypes. Use with caution, besh.
usage_notes: Can be considered derogatory or pejorative depending on context and intent. Its usage has declined in more progressive circles but is still heard.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinuna ng marami ang kanyang **kabakla-bakla** na pagsasalita.","translation":"Many criticized his **effeminate** way of speaking."},{"sentence":"Tigilan mo nga 'yang **kabakla-bakla** mong pag-arte.","translation":"Stop your **flamboyant** acting."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa tanggapan o grupo ng mga kalihim na bumubuo sa isang sekretarya. Maaari ding tumukoy sa katangian ng pagiging lihim o kompidensyal.
etymology: From 'ka-' + 'lihim' + '-an', meaning 'the place of secrets/secretaries' or 'the state of being secret'.
original_explanation: This is the HQ, the nerve center where all the 'kalihims' work. Think of it as the office of the secretaries, the place where all the paperwork and secrets live. It can also mean the vibe of the place: 'confidentiality'. What happens in the kalihiman, stays in the kalihiman.
usage_notes: Has two main meanings: the physical office/body (secretariat) and the abstract concept (confidentiality). The context usually makes it clear.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipasa ninyo ang lahat ng dokumento sa **kalihiman** ng aming organisasyon.","translation":"Submit all the documents to the **secretariat** of our organization."},{"sentence":"Dapat panatilihin ang **kalihiman** ng bawat transaksyon.","translation":"The **confidentiality** of every transaction must be maintained."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasuotang isinusuot sa kamay, karaniwang may hiwalay na mga puwang para sa bawat daliri at hinlalaki.
original_explanation: The thing your tita from the US wears when washing dishes even though you use your bare hands. Also, what boxers wear, or what doctors and nurses have an unlimited supply of. Not to be confused with "grab," the app you use to get a ride.
usage_notes: A direct loanword, often used in contexts like sports (boxing gloves) or medical settings (latex gloves). The native word is 'guwantes'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong magsuot ng **glab** kapag naglilinis ng banyo.","translation":"You need to wear **gloves** when cleaning the bathroom."},{"sentence":"Pinirmahan ni Manny Pacquiao ang kanyang boxing **glab** at ibinigay sa isang tagahanga.","translation":"Manny Pacquiao signed his boxing **glove** and gave it to a fan."}]

meaning_filipino: Matunaw o maging likido mula sa pagiging solido, karaniwan dahil sa init o pagkahalo sa isang likido.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your ice cream under the Philippine sun in 5 seconds. It's also what happens to your heart when your crush finally smiles at you. 'Nalusaw ako, bes.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hayaan mong **malusaw** ang asukal sa mainit na tubig.","translation":"Let the sugar **dissolve** in the hot water."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula nang **malusaw** ang yelo sa baso.","translation":"The ice in the glass started to **melt**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babae, kadalasang mas bata, na paborito o labis na inaalagaan ng isang tao, partikular ng isang lalaki sa isang romantikong relasyon.
original_explanation: The female equivalent of 'babyboy'. It's what you call your girlfriend, your favorite 'inaanak', or even a male celebrity you find particularly cute and want to protect (e.g., 'He's so babygirl'). It's a term of endearment that screams 'I must protect this person at all costs.'
usage_notes: A very common term of endearment. Its usage has expanded online to describe men who are perceived as cute, vulnerable, or submissive.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong pagurin ang **babygirl** ko.","translation":"Don't tire out my **darling**."},{"sentence":"Para sa internet, si Keanu Reeves ay isang **babygirl**.","translation":"For the internet, Keanu Reeves is a **babygirl**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagkakaroon ng partikular na gusto o interes sa isang bagay; ang pagiging hilig o madalas na gawin ang isang aktibidad.
original_explanation: This is your Tito's obsession with karaoke, your Tita's addiction to Korean dramas, or your own personal relationship with milk tea. It's that thing you're 'into,' your go-to hobby, your favorite flavor of anything. It's the 'I can't help it, I just love it' feeling.
usage_notes: Usually followed by `sa` to indicate what the person is fond of (e.g., `pagkamahilig sa pagkain`).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa kanyang **pagkamahilig** sa pagbabasa ng mga libro.","translation":"She is known for her **fondness** for reading books."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagkamahilig** sa matatamis ang dahilan ng kanyang pagtaba.","translation":"His **fondness** for sweets is the reason for his weight gain."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat ng mga tao na may masamang hangarin o intensyon; mga kriminal o taong gumagawa ng labag sa batas.
etymology: From 'masama' (bad/evil) + '-ng' (linker) + 'loob' (inner self/will), literally 'people of bad inner will'.
original_explanation: The generic term for the bad guys in every TV news report or 'Magpakailanman' episode. They're the reason your parents tell you, 'Umuwi ka bago dumilim!' Always plural.
usage_notes: This is a plural noun, referring to two or more criminals or a group of them. The singular form 'masamang-loob' is less common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binalaan ng barangay ang mga residente tungkol sa mga **masasamang-loob** na nag-aabang sa dilim.","translation":"The barangay warned the residents about the **criminals** who wait in the dark."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang dasal na dinarasal ng mga Katoliko sa ganap na ika-6 ng umaga, ika-12 ng tanghali, at ika-6 ng gabi. Maaari ding tumukoy sa isang bulong o inkantasyon.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'oración' na nangangahulugang 'panalangin' o 'pangungusap'.
original_explanation: That 6 PM signal for you to stop playing outside and go home. You'd hear the church bells ring, and TV/radio stations would pause for a moment of prayer. It's the universe's daily reminder to "uwi na, may lamok na!" Also, the secret chant your albularyo cousin mutters to find a lost item.
usage_notes: Primarily refers to the Angelus prayer, especially the one at 6 PM. The 'incantation' meaning is more archaic or used in folklore contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumigil ang mga bata sa paglalaro nang tumunog ang kampana para sa **orasyon**.","translation":"The children stopped playing when the bell rang for the **Angelus prayer**."},{"sentence":"May binulong siyang **orasyon** para daw hindi kami maligaw.","translation":"He muttered an **incantation** so that we supposedly wouldn't get lost."}]

translation: to make an insinuation; to hint at something negatively
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpaparinig ng isang puna o akusasyon sa paraang hindi direkta o patagilid.
original_explanation: This is the official verb of Filipino passive-aggression. It's when you post "Sana all masipag" on Facebook when your groupmate isn't doing their part of the project. You're not naming names, but you're throwing shade so specific, the target feels the burn. It’s the art of hitting someone with a comment without actually looking at them. #Parinig
usage_notes: Often used with "ng" or "tungkol sa." The root "saring" is rarely used on its own. The action is almost always negative or critical.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **magpasaring** sa social media tungkol sa mga kaaway niya.","translation":"She likes to **make insinuations** on social media about her enemies."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtalsik ng maliliit na patak ng likido dahil sa isang puwersa o pagtama.
original_explanation: The reason you wear an apron when frying galunggong. It’s the sudden, aggressive splash of hot oil that seems to aim for your face. Also, what happens when a car speeds through a puddle next to you on a rainy day. Your all-white OOTD is now a masterpiece of **tumilamsik** na putik.
usage_notes: Describes the scattering of small droplets of liquid. 'Tumalsik' is a more general synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa pagpiprito, baka **tumilamsik** ang mainit na mantika.","translation":"Be careful when frying, the hot oil might **spatter**."},{"sentence":"**Tumilamsik** ang putik sa kanyang damit nang dumaan ang mabilis na sasakyan.","translation":"Mud **splashed** onto his clothes when the fast car passed by."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong hindi madaldal, matipid magsalita, o bihirang magbigay ng opinyon.
original_explanation: This is your friend who replies 'K.' to your long, emotional message. Not necessarily shy or angry, just... efficient with words. They're the opposite of the 'Marites' of the group. They listen more than they talk, and when they do speak, it's usually important.
usage_notes: An idiomatic expression used to describe a person's personality. It's not a literal physical description.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala si Juan bilang isang taong **maikling-dila**, kaya nagulat kami nang magsalita siya nang matagal.","translation":"Juan is known as a **taciturn** person, so we were surprised when he spoke for a long time."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong isiping galit siya, sadyang **maikling-dila** lang talaga siya.","translation":"Don't think he's angry, he's just really a man **of few words**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang damdamin ng pagkainggit o pagnanasa sa tagumpay, katangian, o pag-aari ng iba.
original_explanation: Ito yung feeling na nakita mo yung travel photos ng kaibigan mo sa Japan tapos ikaw, heto, nasa bahay lang at kumakain ng instant noodles. Hindi galit, pero parang may kirot. 'Sana all' pero may kasamang konting sama ng loob.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'inggit', but 'hili' can sometimes feel a bit milder or more internalized.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mahili** sa tagumpay ng iba; magsumikap ka para sa sarili mo.","translation":"Don't be **envious** of others' success; work hard for your own."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang **hili** nang malaman niyang na-promote ang kanyang katrabaho.","translation":"She felt a pang of **envy** when she found out her colleague got promoted."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lumang yunit ng panukat na katumbas ng lapad ng isang daliri, o sa modernong sistema, isang pulgada.
original_explanation: Before measuring tapes, there was the 'dali.' It's the OG Filipino unit of measurement, probably used by your lolo to check if the fish was big enough. "Mga dalawang dali na lang ang natitira sa softdrinks mo, ubusin mo na." It's imprecise, but it gets the job done, just like "Filipino time."
usage_notes: This is an older, more traditional unit of measurement. While "pulgada" (from Spanish) or "inch" are now more common, "dali" is still understood, especially by older generations. The stress is on the first syllable, unlike 'dalî' (quick).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kulang pa ng isang **dali** ang haba ng tela.","translation":"The length of the cloth is still short by one **inch**."},{"sentence":"Sinukat niya ang tubig gamit ang kanyang mga **dali**.","translation":"He measured the water using his **fingers' breadth**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pagiging magkapareho ng pinagmulan, pinanggalingan, o sanhi.
etymology: From `ka-` (denoting a companion or shared quality) + `ugat` (root).
original_explanation: Like how 'chismis' and 'chismosa' are family. Or how the words 'utang' and 'utang na loob' share a deep, complicated DNA. 'Kaugat' is about tracing things back to the same source, whether it's two words, two families from the same province, or two problems that stem from one bad decision.
usage_notes: Often used in linguistics, genealogy, or problem analysis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang salitang 'bahala' ay **kaugat** ng 'Bathala'.","translation":"The word 'bahala' is **of the same root** as 'Bathala'."},{"sentence":"Ang dalawang pamilya ay **kaugat** pala sa iisang ninuno.","translation":"The two families, it turns out, are **from the same origin** (share a common ancestor)."}]

meaning_filipino: Gamitin sa pagdakip o paghuli ng hayop, tao, o anumang bagay.
original_explanation: This is your trap or your tool for capture. It could be the 'lambat' (net) for catching fish, the 'pokeball' for catching Pokémon, or that witty 'banat' you use to catch someone's attention. It's the instrument of capture. 'Anong pain ang maganda nating ipanghuli ng isda?'
usage_notes: An instrumental verb where the focus is on the means or tool used for catching something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglagay siya ng bitag na **ipanghuli** ng daga.","translation":"He set up a trap **to use for catching** mice."},{"sentence":"Ang ebidensyang ito ang **ipanghuhuli** natin sa salarin.","translation":"This evidence is what we will **use to catch** the culprit."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang uri ng buhay na organismo na karaniwang tumutubo sa lupa, sumisipsip ng tubig sa pamamagitan ng ugat, at gumagawa ng sariling pagkain sa proseso ng photosynthesis.
original_explanation: The "alaga" of every Plantita and Plantito during the pandemic. These are your leafy children that require sunlight, water, and occasional "chika" to thrive. They range from the low-maintenance snake plant you can't kill to the dramatic Calathea that faints if you look at it wrong.
usage_notes: A general term for any kind of plant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig mag-alaga ng iba't ibang **halaman** ang lola ko.","translation":"My grandmother loves taking care of different **plants**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong legal na pinawalang-bisa ang kasal sa kanyang asawa.
original_explanation: This is the official "It's Complicated" status before Facebook made it cool. It's when the "forever" has an expiration date, and you've gone through the legal untangling. Not yet legal in the Philippines for most, so this usually applies to Filipinos married abroad or to foreigners.
usage_notes: Can be used as an adjective (e.g., "lalaking diborsyado") or a noun (e.g., "Siya ay isang diborsyado"). The feminine form is "diborsyada".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang lalaking **diborsyado** ang bagong kapitbahay namin.","translation":"Our new neighbor is a **divorced** man."},{"sentence":"Matagal na siyang **diborsyado** bago pa bumalik sa Pilipinas.","translation":"He has been **divorced** for a long time even before returning to the Philippines."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang nakausling ibabang bahagi ng bubong ng isang gusali. Maaari din itong tumukoy sa isang bahagyang pagbaba o paghilig ng lupa.
original_explanation: This is the part of your roof that juts out, perfect for 'tagay sa tag-ulan' moments while watching the rain without getting wet. It's also that slight downhill slope where your tsinelas might slide off if you're not careful. The architectural equivalent of bangs.
usage_notes: This word has two distinct meanings: one related to architecture (eaves) and the other to geography (slope). Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumutulo ang tubig-ulan mula sa **balisbis** ng aming bubong.","translation":"The rainwater is dripping from the **eaves** of our roof."},{"sentence":"Dahan-dahan siyang bumaba sa **balisbis** ng burol.","translation":"He slowly went down the **gentle slope** of the hill."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasama-sama ng dalawa o higit pang magkakaibang bagay, elemento, o katangian upang makabuo ng isang kabuuan.
original_explanation: That perfect mix, like your ulam and kanin, or the numbers for your lotto ticket. It's also that weird outfit your tita wears that somehow... works? Or that mix of emotions you feel when your ex gets engaged: a 'kumbinasyon' of sadness, relief, and a little bit of 'buti nga'. From Spanish 'combinación'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magandang **kumbinasyon** ang mangga at bagoong.","translation":"Mango and shrimp paste are a good **combination**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bansa sa Gitnang Europa na kilala sa opisyal na pangalan na Republikang Pederal ng Alemanya.
original_explanation: The country where your tito or tita who's a nurse wants to work. It's the land of beer festivals (Oktoberfest), autobahns with no speed limits, and world-class engineering. The official country name for 'Aleman'.
usage_notes: The standard Filipino term for the country Germany.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming Pilipinong nars ang nagtatrabaho ngayon sa **Alemania**.","translation":"Many Filipino nurses are now working in **Germany**."},{"sentence":"Ang Berlin ang kabisera ng **Alemania**.","translation":"Berlin is the capital of **Germany**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging mangmang; kawalan ng kaalaman, edukasyon, o kamalayan sa isang bagay.
etymology: From "ka-" + "mangmang" + "-an", a common Filipino nominal affixation pattern to denote a state or quality.
original_explanation: This is the state of being 'clueless' or 'living under a rock'. It's not about being stupid, but about not knowing something. Like when your friend doesn't know the latest trending meme, or when someone genuinely asks "Sino si Taylor Swift?" That's kamangmangan in action. It’s the opposite of being a ‘woke’ netizen.
usage_notes: Can have a strong, sometimes judgmental connotation, implying a preventable lack of knowledge.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kamangmangan** sa batas ay hindi maaaring gawing dahilan.","translation":"**Ignorance** of the law excuses no one."},{"sentence":"Layunin ng edukasyon na puksain ang **kamangmangan**.","translation":"The goal of education is to eradicate **ignorance**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng tela na malambot, makinis, at may maikling buhok na tulad ng pelus (velvet).
etymology: Literally 'cat's fur' (balahibo ng pusa), named for its soft, furry texture.
original_explanation: The fabric that feels like a hug from your lola. It's that soft, slightly fuzzy material used for old-school formal dresses, curtains in ancestral homes, or the cover of a fancy jewelry box. It screams vintage elegance.
usage_notes: Often used to describe velvet or velveteen cloth.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kurtina sa lumang bahay ay yari sa telang **balahibong-pusa**.","translation":"The curtain in the old house was made of **velvet-like fabric**."},{"sentence":"Ang lambot ng unan dahil **balahibong-pusa** ang punda nito.","translation":"The pillow is so soft because its case is made of **velvet-like fabric**."}]

translation: to be disowned, to be repudiated
meaning_filipino: Itakwil, talikuran, o hindi kilalanin bilang bahagi ng pamilya o grupo.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "You're not my child anymore!" moment in a teleserye, usually followed by dramatic music and someone fainting. It's when your family or community cuts you off, often because you broke a major rule or chose a path they don't approve of. It's the social version of being unfriended and blocked, but a thousand times more intense.
usage_notes: A very strong and formal word, often found in literature and dramatic contexts. The active form is 'itakwil'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nangamba siyang **matakwil** ng kanyang pamilya kapag nalaman nila ang kanyang lihim.","translation":"She feared she would **be disowned** by her family if they found out her secret."},{"sentence":"Ang sinumang lumabag sa sagradong batas ay maaaring **matakwil** ng kanilang tribo.","translation":"Anyone who violates the sacred law can **be repudiated** by their tribe."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos o paraan ng pagsuway o hindi pagsunod sa isang batas, tuntunin, o kasunduan.
original_explanation: This is the "oops, I did it again" moment but with rules. It's the reason you get a memo from HR, a ticket from the MMDA, or a sermon from your lola. Basically, the state of being *bawal pero ginawa pa rin*.
usage_notes: Describes the manner or circumstance of a violation that has occurred.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkakalabag** niya sa batas-trapiko ay nagdulot ng malaking multa.","translation":"His **violation** of the traffic law resulted in a hefty fine."},{"sentence":"Inimbestigahan ang **pagkakalabag** sa kontrata ng kumpanya.","translation":"The company's **breach** of contract was investigated."}]

meaning_filipino: Magkakatabi o magkakasama sa isang hilera o linya; magkakalapit.
original_explanation: This is how you and your bestie sit while watching a movie, or how jeepney passengers are packed during rush hour. It's the physical representation of 'siksikan'. When you arrange things tabi-tabi, you're putting them right next to each other with no personal space.
usage_notes: Used to describe the state of being adjacent to one another. Not to be confused with the phrase 'Tabi-tabi po,' which is used to ask permission from supernatural beings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatayo silang **tabi-tabi** habang naghihintay ng bus.","translation":"They were standing **side by side** while waiting for the bus."},{"sentence":"Ayusin mong **tabi-tabi** ang mga libro sa estante.","translation":"Arrange the books **side by side** on the shelf."}]

meaning_filipino: Humingi ng payo, opinyon, o kaalaman mula sa isang dalubhasa o taong may awtoridad hinggil sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: Before you make a major life decision (or even just pick a Netflix show), you 'ikonsulta' it with the group chat. It's what you do with your symptoms on Google before you finally 'ikonsulta' them to a real doctor. It means "to ask an expert (or your friends)."
usage_notes: An object-focus verb. The thing being consulted (e.g., the problem, the plan) is the grammatical object.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas mabuting **ikonsulta** mo muna sa abogado ang problemang iyan.","translation":"It's better if you **consult** a lawyer first about that problem."},{"sentence":"Balak kong **ikonsulta** sa doktor ang pananakit ng aking likod.","translation":"I plan to **consult** a doctor about my back pain."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mahinang pag-iyak o pag-atungal na tulad ng sa isang aso; isang paulit-ulit at nakakainis na pagsusumamo.
original_explanation: This is the sound a dog makes when it wants to go out for a walk NOW, or the sound your jowa makes when they *really* want to eat at Jollibee for the fifth time this week. It's a persistent, low-key, annoying sound of wanting something. Less dramatic than pagngangawa, more targeted than pagngangayngay.
usage_notes: Often associated with dogs, but can be applied to humans in a slightly derogatory way to imply annoying persistence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginigising ako tuwing umaga ng **pagngilngil** ng alaga kong aso.","translation":"The **whimpering** of my pet dog wakes me up every morning."},{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na ang **pagngilngil** mo, sinabi nang hindi pwede.","translation":"Stop your **whining pleas**, I already said no."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-alis o paghagis ng isang bagay na hindi na kailangan o gusto. Ito ay ang nakaraang anyo ng pandiwang 'magtapon'.
original_explanation: This is what you did to your ex's stuff after the breakup. Also, what you *should* have done with that leftover adobo from last week instead of letting it become a science experiment in the ref. You nagtapon your trash in the correct bin, right? *Right?*
usage_notes: Ito ang perpektibong aspekto (past tense) ng pandiwang 'magtapon'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagtapon** siya ng basura sa tamang lalagyan.","translation":"He **threw away** the trash in the proper bin."},{"sentence":"Saan mo **nagtapon** ang mga lumang diyaryo?","translation":"Where did you **dispose of** the old newspapers?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggamit ng tinig upang makuha ang atensyon ng isang tao, o ang paggamit ng telepono upang makipag-ugnayan. Ito ay ang kasalukuyang anyo ng pandiwang "tawag".
original_explanation: This is what your phone does when your boss calls you on your day off. Or what your mom does from the kitchen when she needs you to buy suka from the sari-sari store. "Sino'ng tumatawag?" is the default question when a phone rings. It's the act of reaching out, either vocally or digitally.
usage_notes: Present progressive tense of "tawag" (to call).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **tumatawag** sa telepono, sagutin mo muna.","translation":"Someone **is calling** on the phone, please answer it."},{"sentence":"**Tumatawag** ng pansin ang batang umiiyak.","translation":"The crying child **is calling** for attention."}]

translation: to ask for a hug; to be embraced
meaning_filipino: Ang paghiling o pagpapahintulot na mayakap ng isang tao.
original_explanation: That feeling when you've had a rough day, you see your favorite person, and you just open your arms and say this. It's a request for a human-sized emotional band-aid. The ultimate "pampalubag-loob."
usage_notes: Can be used as a command or request ("Payakap nga!") or as a descriptive verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagod na ako, **payakap** naman.","translation":"I'm tired, **let me hug you** / can I have a hug."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpili o paghanap ng isang bagay mula sa maraming opsyon, o ang gawain ng pagbili ng mga produkto sa isang pamilihan o tindahan.
original_explanation: This is your national sport every 12.12 sale. You add to cart for a week, then at midnight, you either check out or you 'mamili' which ones to sacrifice because your wallet is crying. Also, it's what you do in Divisoria, trying to decide between the 'Class A' and the 'OEM' version of the same thing.
usage_notes: Can mean both 'to choose' in a general sense and 'to shop/go shopping'. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **mamili** kung sino ang iboboto sa darating na halalan.","translation":"It's hard to **choose** who to vote for in the upcoming election."},{"sentence":"Araw ng sahod bukas, kaya plano naming **mamili** sa mall.","translation":"It's payday tomorrow, so we plan to **shop** at the mall."}]

translation: to establish (a business); to build up assets
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsisimula at pagpapalago ng isang negosyo, ari-arian, o anumang mahalagang bagay mula sa sariling pagsisikap at pag-iipon.
original_explanation: This is the OFW and entrepreneur's anthem. It's the act of hustling hard to build something from scratch—a sari-sari store, a house and lot, or a small business. It’s the opposite of 'one day millionaire.' It's about planting seeds (and your sahod) and watching them grow into something you can call your own. The ultimate Filipino dream.
usage_notes: Strongly associated with long-term financial goals, entrepreneurship, and the achievements of OFWs.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtrabaho siya sa abroad para **makapagpundar** ng bahay para sa kanyang pamilya.","translation":"She worked abroad to be able to **build up assets** (like a house) for her family."},{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **nakapagpundar** din ako ng maliit na coffee shop.","translation":"Finally, I was able to **establish** a small coffee shop."}]

translation: to gasp for air, to pant
meaning_filipino: Huminga nang malalim at mabilis, karaniwan ay dahil sa pagod, pagkagulat, o kakapusan ng hininga.
original_explanation: The sound you make after running up five flights of stairs because the elevator is broken. It's that sharp intake of breath when you see a shocking 'resibo' (receipt) or a juicy piece of 'chismis'. It's the physical reaction to 'OMG!'
usage_notes: Describes a single, sharp intake of breath, often involuntary.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumingap** siya nang makita ang dambuhalang ahas.","translation":"He **gasped for air** when he saw the giant snake."},{"sentence":"Pagod na **sumingap** ang mananakbo sa finish line.","translation":"The runner tiredly **panted** at the finish line."}]

translation: to be opposite; to be directly in front of
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging nasa tapat o katapat na posisyon ng isang bagay, lugar, o tao.
original_explanation: Parang sa jeep, 'pag sumigaw ka ng "para," tapos eksakto sa tapat ng bahay niyo huminto. 'Yun, **nanapat** 'yung jeep sa bahay niyo. Perfect timing, walang extra lakad. It's when things align perfectly in front of you.
usage_notes: Often used in its past tense 'nanapat' or future tense 'mananapat' to describe a precise alignment or positioning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nanapat** ang paghinto ng bus sa mismong hintayan.","translation":"The bus stopped **directly in front of** the waiting shed."},{"sentence":"Sana'y **manapat** ang ating mga landas sa tamang panahon.","translation":"I hope our paths **align** at the right time."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagpapakita ng kabutihan, habag, at paggalang sa kapwa tao; pagiging makatao.
etymology: Nagmula sa `pagka-` (katangian ng pagiging) at `makatao` (para sa tao), na buhat sa salitang `tao`.
original_explanation: This is the opposite of 'pagkamakasarili'. Ito yung pagiging 'tao sa kapwa tao.' Yung tipong mag-aabot ka ng payong sa kasabay mo sa jeep kahit hindi mo kilala. Yung magbibigay ng upuan sa matanda sa MRT. It's the 'sana all' of good character traits. The core of being a decent human being.
usage_notes: Isang mataas na positibong katangian, madalas gamitin sa mga talakayan tungkol sa katarungang panlipunan, etika, at simpleng kabutihang-asal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinamalas ng mga volunteer ang kanilang **pagkamakatao** sa pagtulong sa mga biktima ng bagyo.","translation":"The volunteers showed their **humanity** in helping the typhoon victims."},{"sentence":"Ang tunay na lider ay may **pagkamakatao**.","translation":"A true leader possesses **humaneness**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasalita nang walang katuturan o lohika, karaniwan ay dahil sa mataas na lagnat, sakit, o matinding emosyon.
original_explanation: Ito yung state mo kapag sobrang taas ng lagnat mo tapos kung anu-ano na ang sinasabi mo na parang galing sa ibang dimension. O kaya yung kaibigan mong sobrang in-love, humihibang na sa kakabanggit ng pangalan ng crush niya. Parang sirang plaka na may fever.
usage_notes: Often associated with fever, delirium, or being madly in love.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-umpisang **humibang** ang pasyente dahil sa taas ng kanyang lagnat.","translation":"The patient started to **talk deliriously** because of his high fever."},{"sentence":"Para kang **humihibang** sa pag-ibig sa kanya!","translation":"You seem to be **raving** madly in love with him!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-ikot o pagbaling ng isang bagay mula sa dati nitong posisyon, tulad ng sa isang bisagra o aksis.
original_explanation: It's the action of turning something, like when you're trying to find the right "angle" for your selfie, or when you twist a doorknob to escape an awkward conversation. It's the 'pihit' of the electric fan that decides who gets the breeze and who sweats it out.
usage_notes: Can refer to a physical turn, a change of direction in a plan, or turning a dial.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagpihit** ng manibela ang nagligtas sa kanila sa aksidente.","translation":"The **turning** of the steering wheel saved them from the accident."},{"sentence":"Isang **pagpihit** lang sa susi ay umandar na ang makina.","translation":"Just one **turn** of the key and the engine started."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagsasabit o paglalagay ng isang bagay sa isang mataas na lugar upang ito ay lumawit.
original_explanation: This is what you do with a 'sampayan' (clothesline), Christmas lights, or that picture frame you've been meaning to put up for months. It's the act of making things 'sabit'. Also, what your favorite K-drama does at the end of an episode, leaving you hanging. Cliffhanger!
usage_notes: Can also refer to the state of being left hanging or unsatisfied ('nabitin'). This entry focuses on the physical act of hanging an object.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan mo ako sa **pagbibitin** ng mga parol.","translation":"Help me with the **hanging** of the Christmas lanterns."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng isang direktiba, mandato, o kautusan na kailangang sundin o isakatuparan ng iba.
original_explanation: This is what bosses, senior officemates, and the government do. It's a command, not a suggestion. '**Ipinag-utos** ng Pangulo ang pagsusuot ng face mask.' The `ipag-` prefix makes it sound more formal, official, and absolutely non-negotiable compared to the simpler `iutos`.
usage_notes: A more formal and emphatic way to say 'to order' something to be done. The object of the verb is the action or thing being commanded.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ipinag-utos** ng manager na tapusin ang proyekto bago ang Biyernes.","translation":"The manager **ordered** that the project be finished before Friday."},{"sentence":"Ano ang **ipinag-utos** sa iyo ng iyong mga magulang?","translation":"What did your parents **command** you to do?"}]

meaning_filipino: May masamang amoy; katulad ng lantong, tumutukoy sa mabahong amoy ng ihi o nabubulok na bagay.
original_explanation: Basically a synonym or close cousin to 'lantong'. It’s that same category of "OMG, what died here?" smell. If 'lantong' is the specific foul smell of old pee, **lantot** is its slightly more general, equally disgusting buddy. Both will make you question your life choices that led you to smell them.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'lantong', though some speakers might perceive slight differences in the type of foul smell.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **lantot** na amoy sa ilalim ng lababo.","translation":"There's a **foul** smell under the sink."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong iwanan ang basang basahan diyan, magiging **lantot** 'yan.","translation":"Don't leave the wet rag there, it will turn **putrid**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang pag-iwas o pag-iba ng direksyon mula sa isang landas, tao, o paksa.
etymology: From root word "lihis" (deviated, off-course), with the object-focus suffix "-an".
original_explanation: When you see your tita who always asks "Kailan ka mag-aasawa?" at a family reunion and you suddenly make a hard turn towards the lechon. That's you, doing a 'lihisan'. It's the art of strategic avoidance, whether on the road to miss a pothole or in conversation to miss an awkward question.
usage_notes: "Lihisan" is the verb form. The root "lihis" is an adjective meaning 'off-course' or 'astray'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lihisan** mo ang mga masasamang impluwensya sa iyong buhay.","translation":"**Avoid** the bad influences in your life."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **lihisan** ang tanong tungkol sa kanyang lovelife.","translation":"She tried to **deviate from** the question about her lovelife."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mahigpit na paghawak sa isang bagay upang hindi mahulog o maalis.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'hugot' verb. 'Kumapit ka lang,' they say, which means 'Just hold on.' This is what you do when you're on a speeding jeepney, when you're scared during a horror movie, or when you're trying to get through a tough week. It’s about holding on for dear life, whether to a railing or to a hope.
usage_notes: Often used with 'sa' (to/on). 'Kumapit sa patalim' is an idiom meaning 'to resort to desperate measures' (literally 'to cling to a blade').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumapit** ka nang mahigpit!","translation":"**Hold on** tight!"},{"sentence":"Parang linta kung **kumapit** ang bata sa kanyang ina.","translation":"The child **clings** to his mother like a leech."}]

translation: was adapted; was derived; was extracted
meaning_filipino: Kinuha, isinalin, o ibinatay mula sa isang orihinal na akda, ideya, o pinagmulan.
original_explanation: It's like when a movie is 'based on a true story' or a song 'samples' an older tune. It's taking an existing thing and creating a new version of it. A chef might say, '**Hinalaw** ko ang recipe na ito mula sa luto ng lola ko.' (I adapted this recipe from my grandmother's cooking).
usage_notes: Commonly used in the context of literature, film, music, and recipes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pelikulang ito ay **hinalaw** mula sa isang sikat na nobela.","translation":"This movie **was adapted** from a famous novel."},{"sentence":"Maraming aral ang maaaring **hinalaw** mula sa kanyang mga karanasan.","translation":"Many lessons can be **derived** from his experiences."}]

meaning_filipino: Ipasok o isingit ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay sa baywang ng pantalon, palda, o sa sinturon.
original_explanation: That move you do when you tuck your phone into your waistband because your skinny jeans have no pockets. Or how a pulis tucks his gun into his belt. It's the 'I have no bag but I need my hands free' life hack.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin para sa mga bagay tulad ng pitaka, telepono, kutsilyo, o baril.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maingat niyang **isinukbit** ang kanyang pitaka sa likod ng kanyang pantalon.","translation":"He carefully **tucked** his wallet into the back of his pants."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **isukbit** diyan ang cellphone mo, baka mahulog.","translation":"Don't **tuck** your cellphone there, it might fall."}]

translation: to join forces; to merge with
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagsama o pag-iisa sa isang pangkat, puwersa, o entidad upang maging isang buo.
etymology: maki- (social verb prefix) + sanib (join, merge, possess)
original_explanation: This is more intense than just 'makisali.' It's like when two rival BPO companies merge, or when smaller political parties form a coalition. It's a formal, often strategic, joining of forces. Think Power Rangers forming the Megazord. 'Para matalo ang kalaban, kailangan nating makisanib-pwersa!'
