usage_notes: Has a more formal and serious tone than 'sumali.' 'Sanib' can also mean demonic possession, so context is key! 'Makisanib-pwersa' (to join forces) is a common collocation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang maliit na kumpanya na **makisanib** sa isang mas malaking korporasyon.","translation":"The small company decided **to merge with** a bigger corporation."},{"sentence":"Ang mga rebeldeng grupo ay **nakisanib** upang labanan ang gobyerno.","translation":"The rebel groups **joined forces** to fight the government."}]

translation: to be left behind; to stay behind
meaning_filipino: Manatili sa isang lugar habang ang iba ay umaalis; hindi sumama.
original_explanation: This is the "FOMO is real" verb. When your friends are all going out and you have to work, you say, "Maiwan na muna ako, guys." It can be by choice (you're tired) or by force (your boss is a monster). It's the state of staying put while the world moves on without you, even if it's just for a night.
usage_notes: This is intransitive. The subject is the one being left behind or choosing to stay. Contrast with `maiwanan`, which is transitive and often implies something was forgotten or someone was outpaced.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas pinili niyang **maiwan** sa bahay at magpahinga.","translation":"He chose **to stay behind** at home and rest."},{"sentence":"Ayokong **maiwan** mag-isa dito, natatakot ako.","translation":"I don't want **to be left** alone here, I'm scared."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng lumilipad na insekto na kilala sa paggawa ng pulot at pagkit, at sa mahalagang papel nito sa polinisasyon ng mga halaman.
original_explanation: The hardworking, underpaid, and unappreciated employee of the flower world. They're the ones responsible for honey, and more importantly, for making sure plants get... frisky with each other (pollination). They are the original 'busy bee'. Jollibee is their famous cousin.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'bubuyog', although 'pukyutan' (plural/collective) is more common for the species. 'Pukyot' can refer to a single bee.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **pukyot** ang dumapo sa bulaklak upang kumuha ng nektar.","translation":"A **honeybee** landed on the flower to get nectar."},{"sentence":"Ang pulot-pukyutan ay galing sa mga **pukyot**.","translation":"Honey is from **honeybees**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang dalagang hindi pa ikinakasal, lalo na ang mula sa isang marangal na pamilya; isang dalagang mahinhin at mayumi.
original_explanation: This is your classic "damsel in distress" from old Filipino epic poems and komiks. Think Maria Clara vibes. A young, unmarried, very proper lady, probably waiting for her prince or a 'harana'. In modern times, it's used mostly ironically or for costume parties. "Ang arte mo, para kang donselya!"
usage_notes: Archaic and literary. Not used in everyday conversation except for historical context or humorous effect.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa mga lumang kwento, ang prinsipe ay laging nagliligtas sa isang magandang **donselya**.","translation":"In old stories, the prince always saves a beautiful **damsel**."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang kilos ay parang isang **donselya** mula sa panahon ng Kastila.","translation":"Her movements are like a **maiden** from the Spanish era."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon o pagdanas ng sipon, isang karaniwang sakit na dulot ng virus na nagdudulot ng pagbahing, pag-ubo, at pagbara ng ilong.
original_explanation: That feeling when you start sneezing nonstop and your nose becomes a leaky faucet. It's the universe's way of telling you to log off from work, cancel your plans, and become a human lumpia wrapper under your blanket. "Sorry, can't make it, nagkasipon ako." is the ultimate get-out-of-jail-free card for any social event.
usage_notes: Refers to the act of getting or having a common cold.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpapaulan para hindi ka **magkasipon**.","translation":"Don't stay out in the rain so you don't **catch a cold**."},{"sentence":"**Nagkasipon** na naman ang bata dahil sa pabago-bagong panahon.","translation":"The child **has a cold** again because of the changing weather."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi nagtataglay ng anumang kahalagahan, saysay, o katuturan.
original_explanation: Yung effort mo sa kanya pero in-seen ka lang. Yung pinagpuyatan mong report na hindi naman pala gagamitin. Yung pag-ibig na one-sided. In short, walang-kabuluhan. It's the feeling of 'what was the point?' when something ends up being useless or a complete waste of time.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ipahayag ang pagkadismaya o pagkabigo sa isang bagay na walang saysay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para sa akin, **walang-kabuluhan** ang mga pangako niya.","translation":"For me, his promises are **meaningless**."},{"sentence":"Nagtatalo sila sa isang **walang-kabuluhan** na bagay.","translation":"They are arguing over a **pointless** matter."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglikha o pag-record ng isang video blog (vlog) na naganap na.
etymology: Hiram na salita mula sa Ingles na 'vlog' (video blog).
original_explanation: Past tense na 'to, bes. Tapos ka na mag-shoot, mag-edit, at mag-upload. Dasal-dasal na lang for the views and likes. 'Hi guys, welcome to my channel!' ang opening, 'Don't forget to like and subscribe!' ang ending. Tapos na ang trabaho.
usage_notes: Isang modernong hiram na salita. Ang unlaping 'nag-' ay nagpapahiwatig ng isang kilos na natapos na.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagvlog** si Erwan Heussaff tungkol sa mga pagkaing Pilipino.","translation":"Erwan Heussaff **vlogged** about Filipino food."},{"sentence":"Kahapon, **nagvlog** ako sa Divisoria para ipakita ang mga murang bilihin.","translation":"Yesterday, I **vlogged** at Divisoria to show the cheap finds."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na mahilig magsimula o makisangkot sa mga away, gulo, o anumang uri ng kaguluhan.
etymology: From `basag-ulo` ("head-breaking," a brawl) + the Spanish-derived agentive suffix `-ero`.
original_explanation: The guy in every inuman session who suddenly wants to fight everyone after two bottles of Red Horse. He's the reason why plastic chairs are used at fiestas—less damage. The neighborhood basag-ulero is the one who thinks "suntukan sa labas" is a valid debate tactic.
usage_notes: Carries a very negative connotation. Refers to a person known for instigating physical fights.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iwasan mo ang grupong iyan, puro **basag-ulero** ang mga kasama.","translation":"Avoid that group, they are all **troublemakers**."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya bilang **basag-ulero** sa kanilang barangay.","translation":"He is known as a **brawler** in their village."}]

translation: to turn, to rotate, to spin
meaning_filipino: Ang paggalaw sa paraang paikid o pag-inog sa isang sentro. Ginagamit din bilang salitang-ugat para sa mga kaugnay na pandiwa tulad ng 'umikot' at 'paikutin'.
original_explanation: The action version of 'ikot'. When your boss tells you to do something, then changes their mind, then changes it back. "Paikot-ikot lang tayo, sir." Also, what you do when you're looking for parking at SM on a payday weekend.
usage_notes: Often used in its root form for commands or in reduplicated forms like 'ikot-ikot' (to go around in circles). It's the base for affixed verbs like 'umikot' (to turn) and 'paikutin' (to make something turn).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **ikot** nang **ikot** diyan, nahihilo ako.","translation":"Don't **spin** around and around there, I'm getting dizzy."},{"sentence":"Sabi ng nanay, \"**Ikot**!\" at umikot nga ang aso.","translation":"The mother said, \"**Spin**!\" and the dog did spin."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang utos o gawain na gawing magkasing-antas, magkasintaas, o magkapareho sa halaga o katayuan ang dalawa o higit pang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the command you give when one side of the picture frame is higher than the other. Or when you're trying to divide the last piece of cake *perfectly* between you and your sibling to avoid World War III. In a more serious sense, it's the goal of social justice movements—to level the playing field.
usage_notes: This is in the imperative/infinitive form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **pagpantayin** ang mga paa ng mesa para hindi ito umuga.","translation":"You need **to make** the table's legs **level** so it doesn't wobble."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na termino para sa isang bagay na ginawa nang hindi maayos, may pagkakamali, o hindi umabot sa inaasahang kalidad.
etymology: From `pa-` (prefix, can indicate manner) + `sablay` (miss, fail, not aligned).
original_explanation: When you aimed for "perfect" but landed on "meh, pwede na." It's that moment of epic fail, like when you confidently submit a report only to realize you sent the wrong file. It’s a presentation that crashes, a joke that doesn't land, or a dance move that ends in a slip. It's the "A for effort" of failures.
usage_notes: Often used to describe an action or an outcome. Can be used as an adjective (e.g., "pasablay na GFX") or an adverb (e.g., "ginawa nang pasablay").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong gawin nang **pasablay** ang proyekto para hindi tayo mapagalitan.","translation":"Don't do the project **poorly** so we don't get scolded."},{"sentence":"Ang ending ng serye ay medyo **pasablay**, hindi nagustuhan ng mga manonood.","translation":"The series finale was a bit **botched**, the viewers didn't like it."}]

translation: a mythical creature in Filipino folklore
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng nilalang sa mitolohiyang Pilipino na may kakayahang magbago ng anyo, karaniwang kumakain ng tao, lalo na ng mga sanggol at buntis. Ito ay isang pangkalahatang tawag sa iba't ibang uri ng halimaw tulad ng manananggal, tiktik, at wakwak.
etymology: The more common spelling is 'aswang'. The term's origin is debated, but one theory links it to Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *asu-asu, meaning 'dog', due to its shapeshifting nature, often into a dog.
original_explanation: The OG Filipino monster that's the star of every lola's scary stories. It's a shapeshifting, liver-eating, fetus-snatching ghoul that's basically the reason you were told not to stay out too late. Think of it as a Pinoy vampire, werewolf, and witch all rolled into one terrifying package. It's the ultimate 'panakot sa mga pasaway na bata'.
usage_notes: A generic term for a wide range of evil, shape-shifting creatures in Philippine folklore. The spelling 'aswang' is more prevalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglagay sila ng bawang sa bintana upang itaboy ang **asuwang**.","translation":"They put garlic on the window to repel the **aswang**."}]

meaning_filipino: Halagang ibinabayad para sa paggamit ng isang ari-arian (tulad ng bahay o sasakyan) o para sa serbisyo ng isang tao.
original_explanation: The reason why petsa de peligro is a national mood. It's the monthly monster that eats a huge chunk of your sweldo. Whether it's for your condo in BGC or for the services of a plumber, 'upa' is the price of admission.
usage_notes: 'Upa sa bahay' for house rent, 'upa sa manggagawa' for a worker's wage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko nang magbayad ng **upa** para sa apartment bago matapos ang linggo.","translation":"I need to pay the **rent** for the apartment before the end of the week."},{"sentence":"Magkano ang **upa** sa karpintero para sa isang araw na trabaho?","translation":"How much is the **wage** for a carpenter for one day's work?"}]

translation: to be addicted; to be engrossed
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging labis na nahuhumaling o pagkahilig sa isang bagay, lalo na sa isang bisyo tulad ng droga, sugal, o alak.
etymology: From Tagalog `lulong` (addiction, obsession). The prefix `ma-` indicates an ability or state of being.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you "just try" something and end up selling your kidney for it. It's the "one more episode" on Netflix at 3 AM, the "last game lang" that turns into an all-nighter, or falling into a rabbit hole of conspiracy theories on YouTube. Basically, you've been consumed. You're in too deep.
usage_notes: Often used in a negative context, referring to addiction to vices.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming kabataan ang **nalulong** sa online games ngayong pandemya.","translation":"Many youths **became addicted** to online games during the pandemic."},{"sentence":"Pinayuhan siya ng doktor na itigil na ang paninigarilyo bago pa siya tuluyang **malulong** dito.","translation":"The doctor advised him to stop smoking before he becomes completely **addicted** to it."}]

meaning_filipino: Labis na nakasasawa o nakauumay, lalo na sa panlasa dahil sa sobrang tamis o sa isang kilos na labis na sentimental.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling after mo kumain ng isang buong box ng yema cake. Or 'yung ka-opisina mong sobrang OA mag-display ng affection sa jowa niya sa phone. Nakatutuya is when something is so excessively sweet or cheesy that it becomes unpleasant. It's the 'umay' factor cranked up to 100.
usage_notes: Primarily used for taste (sickeningly sweet) but also figuratively for overly sentimental or cheesy behavior. Can be confused with 'mapanuya' which means 'sarcastic' or 'mocking'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **nakatutuya** ang lasa ng keyk dahil sa sobrang tamis.","translation":"The taste of the cake became **cloying** because it was too sweet."},{"sentence":"Para sa iba, **nakatutuya** ang sobrang paglalambingan ng magkasintahan sa publiko.","translation":"For some, a couple's excessive display of affection in public is **sickeningly sweet**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na naglalakbay o bumibisita sa isang lugar para sa kasiyahan, libangan, o kultural na interes, na hindi naninirahan doon nang permanente.
original_explanation: The person wearing a sun hat, shorts, and a camera around their neck, looking slightly lost but very excited in the middle of Quiapo. They're the reason prices for buko juice suddenly go up. We love them, we need them for the economy, but we also love making fun of them (lovingly, of course).
usage_notes: A common loanword that is fully integrated into Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dagsaan ang mga **turista** sa Boracay tuwing tag-araw.","translation":"Swarms of **tourists** flock to Boracay during the summer."},{"sentence":"Tayo ay maging magalang sa mga dayuhang **turista**.","translation":"Let's be polite to foreign **tourists**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-aalis o pagbura na naganap na. Ito ay nasa pangnagdaang anyo.
original_explanation: The past tense of moving on. When you finally nagdelete ng number niya. It's the digital version of ripping up old photos. A moment of cleansing or a moment of regret, depende sa na-delete.
usage_notes: A Tagalized verb in the past tense, formed with the nag- prefix.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigla siyang **nagdelete** ng kanyang social media account.","translation":"He suddenly **deleted** his social media account."},{"sentence":"Sayang, **nagdelete** ako ng maling file.","translation":"Too bad, I **deleted** the wrong file."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalatag o paglalagay ng aspalto sa isang daanan o kalsada.
original_explanation: The favorite activity of DPWH, especially when elections are near. It's the verb for turning a lubak-lubak (pothole-ridden) road into a (temporarily) smooth one. The smell of progress... and hot tar.
usage_notes: A direct verb form created from the loanword 'aspalto'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang munisipyo na **mag-aspalto** ng mga pangunahing kalsada sa bayan.","translation":"The municipal office decided **to pave with asphalt** the main roads in town."},{"sentence":"Kailan kaya sila **mag-aaspalto** sa eskinita namin?","translation":"I wonder when they will **pave with asphalt** our alley?"}]

translation: to clang, to make a resonant sound
meaning_filipino: Paglikha ng isang malagong at umaalingawngaw na tunog, tulad ng isang kampana o isang malaking piraso ng metal na pinukpok o nahulog.
original_explanation: The sound of a church bell calling you to Simbang Gabi. Or the sound the empty Gasul tank makes when you tap it to check if it's *really* empty in the middle of cooking sinigang. It has a deep, resonant quality.
usage_notes: Describes a deep, ringing, or resonant sound, often from a large metal object.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumalaton**g ang malaking kampana sa lumang simbahan.","translation":"The large bell **clanged** in the old church."},{"sentence":"Nang mahulog ang takip ng kaldero, **kumalatong** ito sa sahig.","translation":"When the pot lid fell, it **clanged** on the floor."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang sistema ng tunog kung saan ang lahat ng audio signal ay pinagsasama sa iisang channel.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na "mono", pinaikli ng "monophonic".
original_explanation: Before stereo and surround sound, there was 'mono'. It's like listening to music with just one ear. Think of old radios or your lolo's vinyl records. It's the OG sound system. Also, sometimes used as a prefix for things that are 'one' or 'single'.
usage_notes: Primarily used in technical contexts related to audio and electronics.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lumang recording ay nasa **mono** format pa.","translation":"The old recording is still in **mono** format."},{"sentence":"Mas gusto niya ang stereo kaysa sa **mono** dahil mas buo ang tunog.","translation":"He prefers stereo over **mono** because the sound is fuller."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang propesyon, talento, o hilig ay ang pag-awit.
original_explanation: That friend who turns any road trip into a live concert. The one who belts out 'My Way' in the karaoke bar like their life depends on it. From professional biriteras like Regine Velasquez to your tito who's had one too many San Miguels.
usage_notes: Refers to both professional singers and anyone who is about to sing or enjoys singing. It's the future/contemplated tense of the actor-focus verb, used as a noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang sikat na **manganganta** ang panauhin sa piyesta.","translation":"A famous **singer** is the guest at the fiesta."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **manganganta** sa kasal ninyo sa susunod na buwan?","translation":"Who will be the **singer** at your wedding next month?"}]

translation: to wander; to roam; to stray
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalakad o paggala nang walang tiyak na direksyon o layunin; ang pagiging layas o palaboy.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you're 'walang magawa' (have nothing to do) and just want to walk around the mall ('mag-mall'). It's the verb for aimless wandering. It's what your parents accuse you of doing when you come home late: 'Saan ka na naman naglaboy?!' (Where have you been wandering off to again?!). Also applies to stray dogs and cats (mga asong/pusang laboy).
usage_notes: Often has a slightly negative connotation of being aimless or truant, but can also mean to wander in a more neutral sense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **maglaboy** pagkatapos ng klase at umuwi ka kaagad.","translation":"Don't **wander around** after class and go home immediately."},{"sentence":"Gusto ko lang **maglaboy** sa dalampasigan at mag-isip-isip.","translation":"I just want to **roam** on the beach and think."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa ilalim ng pamamahala, direksyon, o kapangyarihan ng isang tao o bagay; hindi malaya.
original_explanation: The opposite of 'bahala na si Batman.' Everything is planned, monitored, and probably has a spreadsheet. Also, how your parents think your love life should be. 'Under control.'
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa mga sitwasyon, emosyon, o tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kontrolado** ng gobyerno ang presyo ng bigas.","translation":"The price of rice is **controlled** by the government."},{"sentence":"Kahit galit na siya, nanatiling **kontrolado** ang kanyang mga salita.","translation":"Even though he was angry, his words remained **controlled**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang kilos ng paglalagay ng tagpi sa isang butas o sira. Ito ay ang kasalukuyang anyo ng pandiwang 'magtagpi'.
original_explanation: Your tita, right now, fixing your pants because you're clumsy. It's the process of making do with what you have. "Budget is tight this month, so I'm nagtatagpi our finances" is a mood. It's the act of trying to hold things together, literally and figuratively.
usage_notes: Ito ang imperpektibong aspekto (present tense) ng pandiwang 'magtagpi', na naglalarawan ng isang patuloy na kilos.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si nanay ay **nagtatagpi** ng aking uniporme.","translation":"Mom is **patching** my uniform."},{"sentence":"Habang **nagtatagpi** siya ng bubong, biglang umulan.","translation":"While he was **mending** the roof, it suddenly rained."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang damdamin ng matinding pagkabigo o pagkadismaya dahil sa hindi natupad na inaasahan o pangarap.
original_explanation: This is the feeling when you line up for hours for a limited-edition milk tea, only for them to announce "sold out" right when it's your turn. It's the heartbreak of a failed project, a cancelled trip, or finding out your online order was a total scam. Peak "sana all" but you got "sana 'wag na lang".
usage_notes: A deeper, more profound sense of disappointment than 'pagkabigo'. It carries a literary or formal tone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya maitago ang **pagkasiphayo** sa mukha nang malaman ang resulta ng pagsusulit.","translation":"He couldn't hide the **dismay** on his face when he learned the exam results."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkasiphayo** ay isang damdaming mahirap itago.","translation":"**Frustration** is a difficult emotion to hide."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang instrumentong siyentipiko na ginagamit sa pagsukat ng presyon ng atmospera, na nakakatulong sa pagtaya ng panahon.
original_explanation: Before the weather app on your phone, there was this thing. It's a science-y gadget that tells you if a storm is coming by measuring air pressure. Today, the real barometro of an incoming storm is when PAGASA starts using color-coded warnings and your office announces work-from-home.
usage_notes: Primarily used in scientific or meteorological contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumaba ang sukat sa **barometro**, senyales ng paparating na masamang panahon.","translation":"The reading on the **barometer** dropped, a sign of approaching bad weather."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan sa agham kung paano gumagana ang isang **barometro**.","translation":"They are studying in science class how a **barometer** works."}]

translation: was infected; was contaminated; was influenced
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon o paglipat ng sakit, katangian, o ugali mula sa isang tao o bagay patungo sa iba.
original_explanation: The OG 'pasa-load' ng sakit. Eto yung nangyari nung pumasok ka pa rin sa office kahit may ubo't sipon na, tapos after 3 days, buong team may sakit na. It's not just for germs, though. Pwede ring 'nahawa sa kabaitan niya' (influenced by his kindness) or 'nahawa sa pagka-Marites ng katabi' (contaminated by your neighbor's gossip-mongering).
usage_notes: Ang unlaping 'na-' ay nagpapahiwatig ng isang natapos na at hindi kusang-loob na kilos.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nahawa** ako ng ubo mula sa kasama ko sa bus.","translation":"I **was infected** with a cough by someone I was with on the bus."},{"sentence":"Sana ang kasipagan mo ay **mahawa** sa mga kapatid mo.","translation":"I hope your diligence **influences** your siblings."}]

translation: an old unit of measure for grains
meaning_filipino: Isang sinaunang yunit ng panukat para sa mga butil tulad ng bigas, na katumbas ng sampung salop.
original_explanation: This is your lolo's lolo's way of measuring rice, back when 'ganta' and 'salop' were the GigaBytes and MegaBytes of the palengke. You won't hear this at the grocery store unless you've time-traveled.
usage_notes: Extremely rare in modern usage. It is equivalent to ten 'salop'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili siya ng isang **sanghod** na palay.","translation":"He bought one **sanghod** of unhusked rice."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng matinding damdamin, pagiging padalus-dalos sa desisyon, o pag-uugaling walang pagpipigil.
original_explanation: The 'YOLO' or 'Bahala na si Batman' attitude in a person. Yung kaibigan mong biglang nag-book ng flight to Siargao after a breakup. Pwede ring sa love—'isang mapusok na halik'. It's high-energy, high-risk, and sometimes high-reward. It's the opposite of overthinking. Sometimes it's romantic, sometimes it's reckless. It's a fine line, bes.
usage_notes: Can have both positive (passionate) and negative (reckless) connotations depending on the context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **mapusok** na desisyon, nalagay siya sa alanganin.","translation":"Because of his/her **rash** decision, he/she was put in a precarious situation."},{"sentence":"Ibinigay niya ang isang **mapusok** na halik bago umalis.","translation":"He/She gave a **passionate** kiss before leaving."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tanda o palatandaan. Karaniwang ginagamit sa pariralang "signos ng sodyako" na tumutukoy sa mga simbolo ng astrolohiya.
original_explanation: "Ano signos mo?" is the Pinoy icebreaker right after "Anong pangalan mo?" and "Saan ka nag-work?". It refers to your zodiac sign. Knowing someone's signos is key to judging their personality based on cosmic alignments you read on Facebook. "Ah, Scorpio ka pala, kaya pala intense ka!"
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in the context of astrology and zodiac signs ("signos ng sodyako"). For other types of signs, "tanda" or the English "sign" are more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkatugma raw ang aming mga **signos** kaya kami nagkakasundo.","translation":"They say our zodiac **signs** are compatible, that's why we get along."},{"sentence":"Hindi ako naniniwala sa mga hula batay sa **signos** ng sodyako.","translation":"I don't believe in predictions based on zodiac **signs**."}]

translation: to cause to boil; to boil
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-utos na painitin ang isang likido o bagay na may likido hanggang sa ito ay kumulo.
original_explanation: Basically the same as 'pakuluan'. Think of it as the 'object-focus' version. While you 'pakuluan' the water in the pot (location focus), you 'pakuluin' the water itself (object focus). In real life? People use them interchangeably. Don't overthink it, just make sure the water is boiling for your pancit canton.
usage_notes: 'Pakuluin' (verb, object-focus) and 'Pakuluan' (verb, locative-focus) are often used interchangeably in everyday conversation when commanding someone to boil something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **pakuluin** ang mga itlog para sa almusal.","translation":"Don't forget **to boil** the eggs for breakfast."},{"sentence":"Mas madaling balatan ang kamote kapag ito ay **pinakulo** mo muna.","translation":"It's easier to peel sweet potatoes if you **boil** them first."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng isdang-alat na mayaman sa lasa at karaniwang inihahain sa mga espesyal na okasyon.
etymology: A local Philippine language term, referring to various species in the Lates genus.
original_explanation: The fancy fish you order at a restaurant to impress your date or your in-laws. It's the 'sosyal' na isda, often steamed with soy sauce and ginger. Definitely not your everyday galunggong.
usage_notes: Refers to various species of sea bass, barramundi, or similar fish found in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagluto si nanay ng steamed na **apahap** para sa Noche Buena.","translation":"Mom cooked steamed **sea bass** for Christmas Eve dinner."},{"sentence":"Mahal ang kilo ng sariwang **apahap** sa palengke.","translation":"The price per kilo of fresh **sea bass** at the market is expensive."}]

translation: to hope; to rely on; to expect
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng pag-asa o pananabik para sa isang bagay na mangyari; manalig o magtiwala sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: The national pastime. It's what you do when you're waiting for your crush to text back, when you buy a lottery ticket, or when you believe a politician's promise. Often leads to the famous hugot line, 'Pinaasa mo lang ako.' (You just led me on). It's the emotional investment you make with no guaranteed ROI.
usage_notes: Can have a positive meaning (to hope) or a slightly negative one (being overly dependent or being led on).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umasa** siyang mananalo sa raffle.","translation":"He **hoped** he would win the raffle."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **umasa** sa iba para sa iyong kaligayahan.","translation":"Don't **rely** on others for your happiness."},{"sentence":"Akala ko mahal niya ako, pero **umasa** lang pala ako sa wala.","translation":"I thought he loved me, but I was just **hoping** for nothing."}]

meaning_filipino: Madaling mailipat o maipasa sa iba, tulad ng sakit, gawi, o damdamin.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'nakaka-' at salitang-ugat na 'hawa'.
original_explanation: Like a common cold during 'ber' months, or that one TikTok dance craze everyone in the office suddenly knows. It can be a disease, but it can also be a good mood, a yawn, or even 'chismis'. 'Uy, 'wag kang tumawa, nakakahawa 'yan!'
usage_notes: Ginagamit para sa mga sakit, at malawakan ding ginagamit para sa mga emosyon, gawi, at kilos.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat dahil **nakakahawa** ang trangkaso.","translation":"Be careful because the flu is **contagious**."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang magandang ngiti ay tunay na **nakakahawa**.","translation":"Her beautiful smile is truly **infectious**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang magalang na tawag o pamagat para sa isang dalaga o babaeng hindi pa kasal.
original_explanation: The term for a young, unmarried woman, straight out of a historical drama. Think Maria Clara vibes. It's what you call the beautiful daughter of the haciendero. Today, it might sound a bit playful or even sarcastic if used on your modern, independent barkada. 'Wow, feeling sinyorita!'
usage_notes: 'Sinyurita' is a common alternative spelling. It implies youth and being unmarried, unlike 'Sinyora' which is for married or older women.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang kumpol ng mga bulaklak ang alay ng binata sa magandang **sinyorita**.","translation":"The young man offered a bouquet of flowers to the beautiful **young lady**."},{"sentence":"\"Paumanhin po, **Sinyorita**, saan po ang daan patungo sa simbahan?\"","translation":"\"Excuse me, **Miss**, which way to the church?\""}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng hindi pantay na pagtrato sa mga tao batay sa kanilang lahi, kasarian, relihiyon, o iba pang katangian; diskriminasyon.
original_explanation: This is the leveled-up, more intense version of 'pagtatangi'. It's not just having a favorite, it's actively treating people differently and unfairly. Think of it as the 'VIP vs. General Admission' of social interaction, but for all the wrong reasons. It's the reason we have HR policies and SOGIE bills.
usage_notes: Almost always has a negative connotation, referring to systemic or personal discrimination. The repetition of 'tangi' emphasizes the act of separating or singling out.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit na ipinagbabawal ang **pagtatangi-tangi** sa lahi sa lugar na ito.","translation":"**Discrimination** based on race is strictly prohibited in this place."},{"sentence":"Ang batas ay dapat para sa lahat at walang **pagtatangi-tangi**.","translation":"The law should be for everyone without any **unfair distinction**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matandang babae na mahina na at kuba dahil sa katandaan. Sa mitolohiyang Pilipino, isa siyang mangkukulam na may kapangyarihang magbigay ng sakit o kamatayan sa pamamagitan lamang ng pag-unat ng kamay.
etymology: From Proto-Philippine *hukluban, meaning 'sorceress'. In Tagalog folklore, she is one of the agents of Sitan.
original_explanation: Before 'cancel culture', we had the 'hukluban'. In mythology, she's a powerful witch who can end you just by pointing. In modern slang, it's a *very* rude way to call someone an old, decrepit hag. Use with extreme caution, or you might just get cursed, socially or otherwise.
usage_notes: The term carries strong negative and ageist connotations when used for a person. Its mythological meaning refers to a specific type of witch in Tagalog folklore.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa mga kwentong bayan, ang **hukluban** ay isang uri ng mangkukulam na dapat katakutan.","translation":"In folktales, the **hukluban** is a type of sorceress that should be feared."},{"sentence":"Tinawag siyang **hukluban** ng mga bata dahil sa kanyang kuba at kulubot na anyo.","translation":"The children called her a **hag** because of her hunched and wrinkled appearance."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng isang tao na may likas na pag-aatubili sa pakikisalamuha, madaling mahiya, at hindi palakibo.
original_explanation: The person at the party who is one with the wallpaper. They're not antisocial, they're just running on a different social battery—usually one that's at 5% and needs to be recharged by being alone with their phone. They're the ones who will bring a gift but leave before you even open it.
usage_notes: Describes a person's personality trait, as opposed to 'mahiya' which is the action or feeling in a moment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Noong bata ako, sobrang **mahiyain** ko at ayaw kong kumanta sa harap ng tao.","translation":"When I was a child, I was very **shy** and didn't want to sing in front of people."},{"sentence":"Kahit mukha siyang **mahiyain**, napakatalino niya sa klase.","translation":"Even though he seems **timid**, he is very intelligent in class."}]

meaning_filipino: May mga dumi o mantsa sa mukha o katawan na hindi gaanong kalat ngunit kapansin-pansin; hindi malinis tingnan.
original_explanation: A specific kind of 'dirty.' Not 'madumi' from rolling in mud, but 'madungis' from eating chocolate and having it all over your face. It's the look of a kid after playing outside all day, with little smudges of dirt here and there. Cute on a 5-year-old, not so much on a 30-year-old on a Zoom call.
usage_notes: Often refers specifically to dirt or smudges on the face or exposed skin. Implies a slightly unkempt or neglected appearance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Punasan mo ang mukha mo, ang **madungis** mong tingnan.","translation":"Wipe your face, you look so **grimy**."},{"sentence":"Umuwi ang bata na **madungis** at pawisan pagkatapos maglaro.","translation":"The child came home **smudged with dirt** and sweaty after playing."}]

translation: to put ash on; to cover with ash
meaning_filipino: Ang pandiwa ng paglalagay o pagpapatong ng abo sa isang bagay o lugar.
etymology: From 'abo' (ash) with the infix '-in-' and suffix '-an'.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your grilled tilapia or liempo when the charcoal gets a bit too excited. It's also a classic prank, or what you do to the fire to put it out. In a more figurative sense, it's like getting 'cancelledt' or having your bright idea shot down and covered in the 'ash' of negativity.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for covering something with ash or figuratively for ruining something. This is the completed action (past tense).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **inabuhan** ang isdang iniihaw, masusunog iyan.","translation":"Don't **cover** the fish being grilled **with ash**, it will get burnt."},{"sentence":"**Inabuhan** niya ang baga para mamatay ang apoy.","translation":"He **covered** the embers **with ash** to put out the fire."}]

translation: to lean something against; to rest something on
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapatong o pagpapatukod ng isang bagay sa iba upang hindi ito matumba.
original_explanation: When you're too tired to hold something up, you 'isandal' it. You lean the guitar against the wall, you lean the broom in the corner, or you lean your weary head on your crush's shoulder (if you're lucky). It's about finding support, literally.
usage_notes: 'Isandal' is used when making an object lean against something. To lean yourself against something, you would use the verb 'sumandal'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Isandal** mo na lang muna ang bisikleta sa pader.","translation":"Just **lean** the bicycle against the wall for now."},{"sentence":"Maingat niyang **isinandal** ang mamahaling kuwadro sa mesa.","translation":"She carefully **leaned** the expensive painting against the table."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katungkulan, kapangyarihan, at panahon ng panunungkulan ng Papa, ang pinakamataas na pinuno ng Simbahang Katoliko Romano.
etymology: Mula sa `pagka-` (estado ng pagiging) + `Papa` (mula sa Espanyol na 'Papa').
original_explanation: The ultimate #blessed job in the Catholic world. It's the state of being God's CEO on Earth. You get a cool hat (the mitre), a popemobile, and your own country (Vatican City). Your job is basically to lead over a billion people, and every word you say becomes a headline. It's the highest level of "paglilingkod" in the church.
usage_notes: Partikular na tumutukoy sa opisina ng Santo Papa ng Simbahang Katoliko Romano.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkapapa** ni Pope Francis ay kilala sa kanyang pagiging simple at makamasa.","translation":"The **papacy** of Pope Francis is known for his simplicity and connection with the masses."},{"sentence":"Mahaba at makasaysayan ang naging **pagkapapa** ni Saint John Paul II.","translation":"The **pontificate** of Saint John Paul II was long and historic."}]

meaning_filipino: Putulin ang ulo; isagawa ang pagpugot. Ito ay ang anyong pautos o obhetibo ng pandiwa.
original_explanation: This is the 'do it now' version of beheading. If 'pugutan' is the concept, 'pugutin' is the direct order. 'Pugutin mo ang ulo ng manok,' says lola before making tinola. It's the command form, the action you need to perform on a specific object (the head).
usage_notes: 'Pugutan' is often used as 'pugutan ng ulo' (to behead someone), while 'pugutin' is used as 'pugutin ang ulo' (to cut off the head). The focus shifts from the victim to the object (the head).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang utos ng reyna ay **pugutin** ang ulo ng traydor.","translation":"The queen's order was to **behead** the traitor."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pugutin** ang bulaklak na iyan, hayaan mong mamukadkad.","translation":"Don't **cut off the head** of that flower, let it bloom."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pang-abay na tumutukoy sa isang lugar na malayo sa nagsasalita at sa kinakausap.
original_explanation: The final boss of Tagalog directionals. 'Dito' is here, 'diyan' is there (near you), and 'doon' is way over there, somewhere in another barangay, or maybe just across the street. It's the 'over yonder' of Pinoy speech. Pro-tip: a 'd' often becomes an 'r' after a vowel, so you'll hear 'roon' a lot (e.g., 'nandoon' -> 'naroon').
usage_notes: Ginagamit kapag ang tinutukoy na lokasyon ay malayo sa parehong nagsasalita at kausap. Nagiging 'roon' kapag ang sinusundang salita ay nagtatapos sa patinig (vowel), 'w', o 'y'. Halimbawa: "Punta ka roon."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakilagay mo ang mga sapatos **doon** sa labas.","translation":"Please put the shoes **there**, outside."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko siya **doon** sa palengke kanina.","translation":"I saw him/her **there** at the market earlier."},{"sentence":"Malayo pa ba? Parang ang layo naman ng **doon**.","translation":"Is it still far? That '**there**' seems so distant."}]

translation: to have a rendezvous; to meet at an appointed time/place
meaning_filipino: Magkasundo na magkita sa isang tiyak na lugar at oras, karaniwang para sa isang romantikong layunin o lihim na pag-uusap.
original_explanation: The old-school, poetic version of 'let's meet up' or 'mag-date.' This is what Crisostomo Ibarra and Maria Clara did. In modern times, it's setting that 'Kita tayo sa [coffee shop name] at 3 PM' text. It has a slightly formal, almost romantic, 'may usapan tayo' vibe.
usage_notes: Has a more formal or romantic connotation than the more common 'magkita'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang magkasintahan ay nagkasundong **magtipan** sa ilalim ng puno ng mangga.","translation":"The lovers agreed to **have a rendezvous** under the mango tree."},{"sentence":"Saan ba tayo muling mag**titipan**?","translation":"Where shall we **meet** again?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang propesyon ay ang pagsukat ng mga lupain, kabilang ang mga hangganan, lawak, at elebasyon nito.
original_explanation: Sila 'yung mga nakikita mo sa daan na may parang camera na nakatayo sa tripod (theodolite 'yun, bes!), tinitingnan kung hanggang saan ang lupa mo at ng kapitbahay mong chismosa. Sila ang referee sa awayan sa lupa.
usage_notes: Isang pormal na termino para sa isang 'land surveyor'. Ang salitang Ingles na "surveyor" ay mas karaniwang ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating kumuha ng **agrimensor** upang sukatin ang ating lote.","translation":"We need to hire a **land surveyor** to measure our lot."},{"sentence":"Ang **agrimensor** ang nagtakda ng mga muhon sa hangganan ng aming ari-arian.","translation":"The **surveyor** placed the boundary markers on our property."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sanggol na kapapanganak pa lamang.
original_explanation: The newest member of the pamilya! Yung maliit na version ng tatay o nanay niya na ang trabaho lang ay umiyak, kumain, at matulog. Also the reason why your ninongs and ninangs suddenly go MIA during Christmas.
usage_notes: Literally 'new person'. While its primary meaning is a newborn baby, it can be used metaphorically for a reformed person, similar to 'bagong-buhay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroon silang **bagong-tao** sa kanilang pamilya.","translation":"They have a **newborn** in their family."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng pag-uugaling mahinhin, pino, at mayumi, kadalasan sa paraang tila may pag-aatubili o pag-iwas na mapansin.
etymology: From the adjective "mayumi" (demure, refined) with the "nag-ma-" prefix and reduplication.
original_explanation: This is that 'pabebe' energy, but the classic, dalagang Filipina version. It's acting shy and reserved, maybe talking softly or covering your mouth when you laugh. It's the opposite of being loud and aggressive. Think Maria Clara, but in a modern setting. 'Ay, nagmamayumi pa siya, pero gusto rin naman.'
usage_notes: Describes the act of behaving in a demure or refined manner. It can sometimes have a slightly negative or teasing connotation, implying the coyness is an act.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi na uso ngayon ang babaeng laging **nagmamayumi**.","translation":"It's no longer in style for a woman to always be **acting demurely**."},{"sentence":"Nung inalok siya ng pagkain, **nagmamayumi** pa kunwari pero gutom na talaga.","translation":"When she was offered food, she pretended to be **coy** but was actually very hungry."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tiyak na daanan o landas na tinatahak mula sa isang lugar patungo sa iba, lalo na ang regular na tinatahak ng mga sasakyan.
original_explanation: 'Yung daan ng jeep na sinasakyan mo araw-araw. Or 'yung path na sinet mo sa Waze para iwas-traffic. It's the designated path from Point A to Point B. Kung naligaw ka, ibig sabihin, wala ka sa tamang ruta.
usage_notes: Commonly used in transportation and travel contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **ruta** ng bus na ito?","translation":"What is the **route** of this bus?"},{"sentence":"Humanap tayo ng alternatibong **ruta** para makaiwas sa trapik.","translation":"Let's find an alternative **route** to avoid the traffic."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang babae na mahinhin kumilos, mayumi, may malinis na puri, at kagalang-galang sa pananalita at pananamit.
original_explanation: This is the classic "Maria Clara" stereotype. The girl who speaks softly, dresses conservatively, and probably blushes a lot. She's the opposite of a "Marites" – quiet, reserved, and doesn't get involved in drama. In old-school Filipino culture, this was the ultimate compliment for a woman. Today, it can sometimes feel a bit dated, but the core idea of being respectable and modest still holds.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used to describe women. Carries a traditional, sometimes old-fashioned, connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinahangaan siya ng lahat dahil sa kanyang pagiging **matimtiman**.","translation":"Everyone admires her for being **demure**."},{"sentence":"Ang dalagang Pilipina ay kilala sa pagiging **matimtiman** at mahinhin.","translation":"The Filipina maiden is known for being **modest** and gentle."}]

translation: to be implicated; to be involved (unwillingly)
meaning_filipino: Ang hindi sinasadyang pagkasangkot o pagkasali sa isang gulo, problema, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: Yung nanahimik ka lang sa isang corner, tapos biglang isinigaw ng kaibigan mo 'yung pangalan mo sa gitna ng away nila ng jowa niya. Ayun, napadamay ka. It’s being dragged into drama you didn't sign up for. The classic "wrong place, wrong time" scenario.
usage_notes: Always has a negative connotation, implying being dragged into trouble or a negative situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayokong **mapadamay** sa gulo ninyo kaya aalis na ako.","translation":"I don't want to **be involved** in your trouble, so I'm leaving."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na termino para sa isang taong may pambihirang ganda o karisma, na karapat-dapat sa isang beauty pageant tulad ng Miss Universe.
etymology: Isang pariralang Ingles na naging popular sa konteksto ng mga beauty pageant sa Pilipinas, lalo na sa social media.
original_explanation: The highest compliment you can give someone's looks on Pinoy social media. It's not just "maganda" or "pogi"—it's "pang-Miss Universe ang ganda." It's the level of beauty that makes you say, "Pang-international! I-pasok na sa Binibini 'yan!"
usage_notes: Commonly used on social media platforms like Twitter, Instagram, and TikTok to compliment someone's photo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Grabe ang ganda niya sa litrato, isang tunay na **universe cutie**!","translation":"She's so beautiful in the photo, a real **universe cutie**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Magbigay-anyo o porma sa isang bagay, karaniwang sa pamamagitan ng isang molde o gabay.
original_explanation: Similar to *humugis*, but this one emphasizes using a mold or a pattern. It's what a baker does with a cake mold, or what your parents/school/society tried to do to you. It’s the process of shaping something into a specific, predetermined form. 'Hinulma ako ng hirap' (I was molded by hardship) is a classic line.
usage_notes: Often used for physical molding (clay, dough) or figurative molding (character, personality).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga karanasan sa buhay ang **humulma** sa kanyang pagkatao.","translation":"Life experiences are what **molded** his/her personality."},{"sentence":"**Humulma** siya ng paso mula sa luwad.","translation":"He/She **molded** a pot from clay."}]

translation: a type of coarse grass; cogon grass (Imperata cylindrica)
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng mataas at magaspang na damo na karaniwang tumutubo sa mga bakanteng lote; kilala rin bilang kogon o talahib.
etymology: From "damo" (grass). The origin of the suffix "-hiya" is unclear, but it serves to specify a type of wild grass.
original_explanation: This isn't the nice, soft grass for picnics. This is the tall, sharp-edged talahib or kogon grass that gives you paper cuts on your legs if you run through it. It's the kind of grass that takes over abandoned lots and makes you think there might be snakes hiding in there. "Puro **damuhiya** na yung bakuran sa likod, kailangan nang linisin."
usage_notes: More specific than 'damo'. Often used interchangeably with 'talahib' or 'kogon', which are more common terms.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mataas pa sa tao ang tubo ng **damuhiya** sa bukid na iyon.","translation":"The **cogon grass** in that field grew taller than a person."},{"sentence":"Nag-ingat siyang dumaan sa matatalim na dahon ng **damuhiya**.","translation":"He was careful passing through the sharp leaves of the **coarse grass**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis at magaang na pagpalo o pagtama gamit ang dulo ng daliri, karaniwan ang hinlalato o hintuturo. Maaari ring tumukoy sa mabilis na pintig o tibok.
original_explanation: That small, annoying flick your sibling does to your ear. Or the sound your ballpen makes when you're bored in a meeting. Pwede ring 'yung biglaang 'pitik' ng idea sa utak mo habang naliligo. It's a small action with a surprisingly sharp effect.
usage_notes: Maaari ring mangahulugan ng biglaang tibok, tulad ng 'pitik ng pulso'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **pitik** lang sa tenga ang parusa sa matatalo sa laro.","translation":"Just one **flick** on the ear is the punishment for the loser of the game."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman ko ang mabilis na **pitik** ng aking pulso dahil sa kaba.","translation":"I felt the rapid **throb** of my pulse because of nervousness."}]

translation: to mow, to reap (with a scythe)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagputol ng damo, palay, o mga katulad na halaman gamit ang isang karit o katulad na kasangkapan.
original_explanation: The OG way of cutting grass or harvesting rice before lawnmowers and fancy machines. Picture a farmer in a rice field, under the hot sun, swinging a 'karit' (scythe). It's hard, back-breaking work. Today, you might hear it when someone needs to clear a vacant lot full of 'talahib'.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to cutting with a swinging motion using a tool like a scythe or sickle.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaga pa lang ay nasa bukid na si tatay para **manggapas** ng palay.","translation":"Father was in the field early **to reap** the rice stalks."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **manggapas** ng matataas na damo sa bakuran.","translation":"We need **to mow** the tall grass in the yard."}]

translation: midnight thoughts; mga iniisip sa kalaliman ng gabi
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga malalalim, personal, o kung minsan ay walang katuturang kaisipan na pumapasok sa isip ng isang tao tuwing hatinggabi, kadalasan kapag hindi siya makatulog.
original_explanation: Ito yung mga oras na bigla mong naaalala yung kahihiyan mo nung Grade 4, kinukwestyon lahat ng life choices mo, o biglang nag-crave ng Jollibee. It's your brain opening 27 tabs at 2 AM, ranging from "What is my purpose?" to "Saan kaya gawa ang chicharon?". The official fuel of hugot posts.
usage_notes: A popular phrase in social media, often used as a hashtag or a caption for introspective or emotional posts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Heto na naman ako sa aking mga **midnight thoughts**, hindi na naman makakatulog.","translation":"Here I am again with my **midnight thoughts**, I won't be able to sleep again."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babae na kinakasama ng isang lalaking mayroon nang asawa, ngunit hindi sila legal na kasal.
etymology: Ang ugat na 'yuyo' ay maaaring may kaugnayan sa pang-aakit o paglapit, ngunit ang buong salita ang karaniwang anyo.
original_explanation: The formal, almost archaic term for 'the other woman.' It's the word your lola might use when telling a story about the scandalous past of a distant relative. In today's world, we'd just say 'kabit' or 'kerida'. This one has a more literary, dramatic flair, like something out of a classic Filipino film.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang pormal at medyo makalumang termino. Ang salitang 'kabit' ay mas karaniwan sa modernong pag-uusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa lumang nobela, ang kontrabida ay ang **kayuyo** ng mayamang asendero.","translation":"In the old novel, the antagonist was the rich landowner's **concubine**."},{"sentence":"Isang malaking eskandalo noon ang pagkakaroon ng **kayuyo** ng isang opisyal ng gobyerno.","translation":"It was a huge scandal back then for a government official to have a **mistress**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao, kilos, o sitwasyon na gumagamit ng pisikal na puwersa upang manakit, makasira, o magdulot ng pinsala.
original_explanation: Think of that one character in an action movie who solves every problem with their fists. Or that scene in a teleserye where someone throws a vase against the wall. That's biolento. It's aggressive, forceful, and definitely not chill.
usage_notes: Used to describe actions or people that are physically aggressive.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw ng mga magulang na manood ng **biolento**ng palabas ang kanilang mga anak.","translation":"Parents don't want their children to watch **violent** shows."},{"sentence":"Naging **biolento** ang protesta nang magsimulang magbatuhan ang mga tao.","translation":"The protest turned **violent** when people started throwing things."}]

meaning_filipino: Handa sa anumang mangyayari; nakahanda o may sapat na paghahanda.
original_explanation: That feeling you have when you've reviewed for an exam, or when you've brought an umbrella and it suddenly rains. It's the opposite of 'bahala na'. When your crush suddenly talks to you and you actually have a coherent sentence ready, you are **preparado**. The Boy Scout motto 'Laging Handa' in its Spanish-loanword form.
usage_notes: The native Tagalog equivalent is 'handa'. 'Preparado' often implies a more thorough or formal state of readiness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging **preparado** ang mga rescuer para sa anumang sakuna.","translation":"The rescuers are always **prepared** for any disaster."},{"sentence":"Dapat laging **preparado** tayo sa pagdating ng bagyo.","translation":"We should always be **prepared** for the arrival of a typhoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng pahintulot, pagsang-ayon, o opisyal na pagpapatibay sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: The verb that holds the fate of your vacation leave, your loan application, or your thesis proposal. When your boss or the bank finally says yes, 'yan, nag-aproba na sila. It's the "Approved!" stamp in verb form. The opposite of "seen-zoned" by management.
usage_notes: A very common loanword used in business, academic, and government settings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **mag-aproba** ang manager sa aking request for leave.","translation":"I hope the manager **approves** my request for leave."},{"sentence":"Hindi pa nag-a-**aproba** ang komite sa bagong badyet.","translation":"The committee has not yet **approved** the new budget."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan na ginagamit upang buksan, patayin, o baguhin ang daloy ng kuryente sa isang sirkito.
original_explanation: Yung pinipindot mo para magkaroon ng liwanag ang buhay mo... literally. O 'yung bagay na laging pinag-aawayan ng magkakapatid kung sino ang magpapatay bago matulog. 'Ikaw na, mas malapit ka sa **switch**!'
usage_notes: Halos eksklusibong tumutukoy sa isang de-koryenteng switch.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakipatay ng ilaw, pindutin mo lang ang **switch** sa tabi ng pinto.","translation":"Please turn off the light, just press the **switch** beside the door."}]

translation: to strike with force; to bludgeon
meaning_filipino: Ang malakas na pagpalo o paghampas sa isang tao o bagay, karaniwan gamit ang isang mabigat na kagamitan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'hambalos' (malakas na palo) at ang gitlaping '-um-'.
original_explanation: Imagine your nanay getting the walis tambo and going full Thor on an ipis. That's **humambalos**. It’s not just a tap; it’s a forceful, heavy strike meant to cause damage. Parang 'yung impact ng realization na na-ghost ka na naman.
usage_notes: Nagpapahiwatig ng paggamit ng isang kasangkapan o sandata (tulad ng pamalo, patpat, o batuta) sa pagpalo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Galit na galit na **humambalos** ng pinto ang lalaki nang hindi siya pinagbuksan.","translation":"The man angrily **struck** the door with force when no one opened it for him."},{"sentence":"**Humambalos** siya gamit ang isang piraso ng kahoy para itaboy ang asong-gala.","translation":"He **struck** with a piece of wood to drive away the stray dog."}]

translation: to scrutinize, to appraise, to assess
meaning_filipino: Suriing mabuti ang kalidad, halaga, o katangian ng isang bagay o tao.
etymology: From Spanish 'quilates' (carats), referring to the measure of purity for gold and gems.
original_explanation: It's that look your tita gives your new boyfriend/girlfriend from head to toe. It's what you do to the ukay-ukay clothes before buying, checking for stains or tears. It's how you check the avocados in the palengke, squeezing them just right. To kilatisin is to judge with expert-level, almost forensic, detail.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of evaluating quality, value, or character.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bago bumili ng alahas, mahalagang **kilatisin** muna itong mabuti.","translation":"Before buying jewelry, it is important to **scrutinize** it well first."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpadala sa itsura; **kilatisin** mo muna ang kanyang pagkatao.","translation":"Don't be swayed by appearances; **assess** their character first."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapataw o pagpapatupad ng isang bagay, tulad ng buwis, batas, o tungkulin, na kadalasan ay hindi kanais-nais o pabigat sa pinapatawan.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung mga bagay na sapilitang ipinapagawa sa'yo. Parang 'yung biglaang O.T. na binigay ng boss mo kahit Biyernes na. O 'yung pagpapataw ng bagong tax sa online shopping mo. 'Yan ay isang **imposisyon**.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng batas, buwis, at awtoridad.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bagong **imposisyon** ng buwis ay ikinagalit ng maraming mamamayan.","translation":"The new tax **imposition** angered many citizens."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko matatanggap ang **imposisyon** ng iyong mga kagustuhan.","translation":"I cannot accept the **imposition** of your personal wants."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kanal o daanan sa ilalim ng lupa o sa gilid ng kalsada para sa maruming tubig o tubig-ulan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na 'imbornal' (scupper, drain).
original_explanation: The final destination of all things liquid and unwanted on the street. 'Yung pinagtatapunan ng pinaghugasan ng pinggan sa karinderya, 'yung dinadaluyan ng baha, at kung saan nahuhulog 'yung bente pesos mo. It's the city's plumbing system that we only notice when it's clogged (barado).
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa mga sistema ng daluyan para sa maruming tubig o tubig-ulan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Barado ang **imburnal** kaya bumaha sa kalsada.","translation":"The **sewer** is clogged, that's why the street flooded."},{"sentence":"Itapon mo ang basura sa tamang lalagyan, hindi sa **imburnal**.","translation":"Throw the trash in the proper bin, not in the **drainage canal**."}]

translation: to give a share to; to share with
meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng bahagi o parte ang isang tao o pangkat.
original_explanation: When your officemate brings a whole box of Krispy Kreme and you hold out your hand, you're asking them to '**bahaginan**' you. It's the verb form of 'pahingi!'
usage_notes: This is a verb in the object-focus '-an' form. The person or group being shared with is the focus of the sentence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bahaginan** mo naman kami ng biyaya mong natanggap.","translation":"Please **share with** us the blessings you have received."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pag-iipon at pagbubuo ng mga ideya o impormasyon upang makabuo ng isang buod o kabuuan.
original_explanation: This is the 'TL;DR' (Too Long; Didn't Read) of Filipino academia. When your teacher asks for a paglagom of a Noli Me Tángere chapter, they want the juicy highlights, not the whole novel. It's about taking a lot of info, like chismis from your tita, and boiling it down to the main point.
usage_notes: Primarily used in academic or formal writing to mean 'summarization' or 'synthesis'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paglagom** ng mga natutunan sa seminar ay mahalagang bahagi ng ulat.","translation":"The **synthesis** of the learnings from the seminar is an important part of the report."},{"sentence":"Mahusay ang kanyang ginawang **paglagom** sa mahabang kasaysayan ng Pilipinas.","translation":"Her **summary** of the long history of the Philippines was excellent."}]

meaning_filipino: Gumamit ng lakas, kapangyarihan, o impluwensya upang pilitin ang isang tao na gawin ang isang bagay na labag sa kanyang kalooban.
etymology: From Spanish 'fuerza' meaning force or strength.
original_explanation: Ever been 'volun-told' to do something at work or by your parents? That's mamuwersa. It's when someone uses their authority or sheer persistence to make you do things. Think of your tita insisting you sing at the family reunion even if you sound like a dying frog. That's her, mamumuwersa.
usage_notes: Carries a negative connotation of imposition or lack of consent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mamuwersa** ng tao kung ayaw niyang sumama.","translation":"Don't **force** someone if they don't want to come along."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng magnanakaw na **mamuwersa** para buksan ang pinto.","translation":"The thief tried to **use force** to open the door."}]

translation: the act of drinking liquor; boozing
meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pag-inom ng inuming nakalalasing, karaniwan sa isang sosyal na pagtitipon.
original_explanation: The official term for 'tagay session' with the barkada after a long week of adulting. Pagbabarik is the solution (or cause) of many of life's problems, usually involving a bottle of gin, a plate of pulutan, and endless kwentuhan until someone starts singing their heart out on the karaoke machine.
usage_notes: Generally colloquial and informal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napagalitan siya ng asawa dahil sa gabi-gabing **pagbabarik**.","translation":"He was scolded by his wife because of his nightly **boozing**."},{"sentence":"Nagplano ang magkakaibigan ng isang sesyon ng **pagbabarik** sa darating na Sabado.","translation":"The friends planned a **drinking session** for the coming Saturday."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa dumi, maliliit na basura, o mga pira-pirasong bagay na walang halaga. Sa malawakang gamit, ito ay tumutukoy sa isang batang palaboy na marumi ang pananamit at kaanyuan.
original_explanation: Originally means small bits of trash or debris, like what you sweep up with a *walis tingting*. But in classic Filipino drama, it's the go-to word for a poor, grimy, street-smart kid—the protagonist of a 'rags-to-riches' teleserye. Think of it as the opposite of a 'conyo kid'.
usage_notes: The meaning of 'street urchin' is more common in modern and literary usage than the literal 'debris' meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **yagit** sa lansangan ay nangangarap ng mas magandang buhay.","translation":"The **street urchins** on the streets dream of a better life."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng pista, puro **yagit** ng plastik ang naiwan sa plasa.","translation":"After the festival, only plastic **debris** was left in the plaza."}]

translation: to shake one's head (in refusal or disapproval)
meaning_filipino: Paggalaw ng ulo nang pakanan at pakaliwa bilang tanda ng pagtanggi, hindi pagsang-ayon, o pagkadismaya.
etymology: From the root "ilig" (to shake head) + infix "-um-".
original_explanation: The classic "no" gesture. It's what your mom does when you ask for money for the fifth time this week. Or your reaction when your friend suggests another "one last drink" at 3 AM. It's a slightly more obscure cousin of the more common 'umiling'.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with "umiling", but "umiling" is far more common in modern speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umilig** siya nang tanungin ko kung may gusto pa siyang kanin.","translation":"He **shook his head** when I asked if he still wanted rice."},{"sentence":"Basta na lang siyang **umilig** at umalis.","translation":"He just **shook his head** and left."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang hanapbuhay ay ang paggawa, pag-aayos, o pagbabago ng mga kasuotan, lalo na para sa mga lalaki.
original_explanation: Your go-to person when you gain "happy weight" and your pants suddenly don't fit. They're the magician who can turn a thrifted 'ukay' find into a custom-fit masterpiece. Also, the one who saves you a week before the wedding because your online order was a disaster. This entry is for 'sastre', the Tagalog word for 'tailor'.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to a male tailor. The female equivalent is 'modista' or 'mananahi'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipapabago ko ang haba ng pantalon ko sa **sastre**.","translation":"I'll have the length of my pants altered by the **tailor**."},{"sentence":"Magaling ang **sastre** sa kanto; pulido ang gawa.","translation":"The **tailor** on the corner is good; his work is neat."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalawakan na nakikita sa ibabaw ng mundo kapag araw; itinuturing ding tirahan ng Diyos at ng mga banal sa maraming relihiyon.
original_explanation: Literally the sky above. Figuratively, it's that feeling when your Shopee parcel finally arrives. "Nasa **langit** na ba ako?" you ask after tasting your crush's home-cooked sinigang. It’s the ultimate destination, both spiritually and for describing something that's just pure, blissful perfection.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng bughaw na **langit** ngayong umaga.","translation":"The blue **sky** is beautiful this morning."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam ko ay nasa **langit** ako kapag kasama kita.","translation":"I feel like I'm in **heaven** when I'm with you."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sangkap tulad ng sarsa o pampalasa na idinadagdag sa pagkain upang bigyan ito ng partikular na lasa, karaniwang pagkatapos itong maluto.
original_explanation: In the Philippines, this isn't just an addition, it's a requirement. We don't just have condiments, we have 'sawsawan'. Toyo, suka, patis, bagoong, banana ketchup... a meal is incomplete without its designated partner. The condiment station at a fast-food joint is a sacred space.
usage_notes: Bagama't ginagamit ang salitang 'condiment', mas karaniwan sa pang-araw-araw na usapan ang 'sawsawan' o ang pagtukoy mismo sa pangalan ng pampalasa (e.g., toyo, suka).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiabot ng mga **condiment** tulad ng ketchup at hot sauce.","translation":"Please pass the **condiments** like ketchup and hot sauce."},{"sentence":"Ang bawat rehiyon sa Pilipinas ay may kani-kaniyang paboritong **condiment**.","translation":"Each region in the Philippines has its own favorite **condiment**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang magalang na kataga na ginagamit sa pakikipag-usap, katulad ng 'po', ngunit karaniwang itinuturing na di-gaanong pormal o nagpapahiwatig ng mas malapit na ugnayan sa kausap.
original_explanation: It's like 'po', but for your cool tita, not your strict lola. It's the 'po' you use with your boss who's also your lunch buddy. It shows respect but with a little less formality and a bit more warmth. 'Opo' is a firm 'Yes, sir/ma'am.' 'Oho' is a friendly 'Yup, got it!'
usage_notes: Less formal than 'po' but more respectful than not using any honorific. Common in certain regions and social circles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"O**ho**, tapos na **ho** ang report.","translation":"Yes (polite, informal), the report is done."},{"sentence":"Salamat **ho** sa tulong ninyo.","translation":"Thank you (polite, informal) for your help."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katumbas na presyo sa pera ng isang bagay o serbisyo; ang kahalagahan o importansya ng isang tao, bagay, o konsepto.
original_explanation: This word has two major personalities. The first is the one you ask the tindera at the mall: "Magkano po ang halaga nito?" (How much is the price?). The second is the hugot one: "Sana malaman mo ang halaga ko bago ako mawala." (I hope you realize my value/importance before I'm gone). It's both about monetary cost and emotional worth. So, know your worth, but also check the price tag.
usage_notes: Can refer to both monetary price and abstract worth/importance. `Kahalagahan` is often used to specifically mean 'importance'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mataas ang **halaga** ng bilihin ngayong panahon.","translation":"The **price** of goods is high these days."},{"sentence":"Hindi matutumbasan ng anumang **halaga** ang pagmamahal ng isang ina.","translation":"A mother's love cannot be matched by any **value**."},{"sentence":"Ano ang **halaga** ng edukasyon sa iyong buhay?","translation":"What is the **importance** of education in your life?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan kung saan ang lahat ng tao ay may pare-parehong karapatan, oportunidad, at pagtrato nang walang kinikilingan.
etymology: From the reduplicated root 'pantay-pantay' (equal), with the 'pagkaka-' prefix to form a noun signifying the state or principle of being equal.
original_explanation: What we all fight for during team-building when the boss treats someone else to Starbucks. It's about fairness—same sahod for the same work, same rights for everyone regardless of who they are. It's the dream, both in society and when dividing the last slice of pizza.
usage_notes: A key term in social justice, politics, and law. The reduplication 'pantay-pantay' emphasizes the comprehensive and universal nature of the equality being described.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkakapantay-pantay** ay isang pundamental na karapatang pantao.","translation":"**Equality** is a fundamental human right."},{"sentence":"Ipinaglalaban ng grupo ang **pagkakapantay-pantay** sa harap ng batas.","translation":"The group is fighting for **equality** before the law."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang parirala na tumutukoy sa isang bagay, ideya, o pangyayari na hindi tiyak o hindi pinangalanan.
original_explanation: The go-to phrase for when you're feeling vague, indecisive, or just plain lazy. 'Bahala na kung ano,' is the national anthem of winging it. It's the verbal equivalent of a shrug. 'Ano'ng gusto mo?' '**Kung ano** na lang.'
usage_notes: Used to introduce a clause about an unknown or unspecified thing. It can mean 'whatever' or simply introduce an indirect question starting with 'what'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kainin mo na lang **kung ano** ang nasa mesa.","translation":"Just eat **whatever** is on the table."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya masabi **kung ano** talaga ang problema.","translation":"He can't say **what** the problem really is."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang kalagayan kung saan ang mga bagay ay magkakasama nang walang partikular na ayos o pagkakasunud-sunod.
original_explanation: Describes your emotions during a rollercoaster K-drama finale. O kaya yung laman ng 'junk drawer' niyo sa bahay—may lumang battery, resibo, ballpen na walang tinta, at isang random na turnilyo. It’s a beautiful mess. Not the dessert, but the feeling of being mixed up like one.
usage_notes: Note the difference in stress from the dessert 'halo-haló'. This adjective is stressed on the first syllable: 'hálu-halo'. Often used with 'na' (e.g., 'halu-halong emosyon').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Halu-halo** ang naramdaman ko nang manalo ako sa lotto.","translation":"I felt **mixed** emotions when I won the lottery."},{"sentence":"Isang kahon ng **halu-halong** tsokolate ang regalo niya.","translation":"His gift was a box of **assorted** chocolates."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghalungkat o paghahanap ng isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pagkakalkal o paglilipat-lipat ng mga gamit, lupa, o bunton.
etymology: The term "ukay-ukay" for thrift shopping is said to have originated from Cebuano, where "ukay" means to dig or sift.
original_explanation: The national sport of thrift shoppers in the Philippines. It's the act of diving into a mountain of pre-loved clothes (the "ukay-ukay") hoping to find a branded jacket for 50 pesos. Also applies to what your mom does to your room when she's "cleaning" but is actually looking for contraband.
usage_notes: Most famously used in the term "ukay-ukay" which refers to both the act of thrift shopping and the thrift store itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang mag-**ukay** ng mga damit sa Baguio.","translation":"She loves to **rummage** for clothes in Baguio."},{"sentence":"**Inukay** ng aso ang basurahan para maghanap ng pagkain.","translation":"The dog **dug through** the trash to look for food."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng hipon na partikular na nabubuhay at nahuhuli sa dagat o tubig-alat.
original_explanation: This is the boujee cousin of the regular hipon. The one that's been to the beach, got that salty flavor. Ito yung hipon na mas malasa daw sabi ng mga tita sa palengke, at medyo mas mahal. Hindi ito yung galing sa fishpond, galing 'to sa dagat, 'teh!
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang tukuyin ang pinagmulan o uri ng hipon, na iba sa "hipong-tabang" (freshwater shrimp).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas masarap daw igisa ang **hipong-alat** dahil sa taglay nitong lasa.","translation":"They say it's better to sauté **saltwater shrimp** because of its natural flavor."},{"sentence":"Magkaiba ang presyo ng **hipong-alat** at ng hipong galing sa palaisdaan.","translation":"The price of **saltwater shrimp** is different from shrimp from a fishpond."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaikling katawagan para sa larong "Valorant," isang sikat na first-person shooter na laro sa kompyuter.
original_explanation: Short for Valorant. Eto yung dahilan kung bakit puyat ang jowa mo o mga kaibigan mo. "Tara Valo!" is the new "Tara, kape tayo." It's where friendships are tested and 'trashtalk' is a love language. 'Pag sinabi niyang "last game na," expect mo na aabutin pa 'yan ng madaling araw.
usage_notes: Exclusively used in the gaming community as a slang term for the game Valorant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Yayain mo si Mark, mag-**Valo** tayo mamaya.","translation":"Invite Mark, let's play **Valorant** later."},{"sentence":"Na-addict na naman ako sa **Valo**.","translation":"I'm addicted to **Valorant** again."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sisidlang salamin na puno ng tubig kung saan inaalagaan ang mga isda at iba pang hayop at halamang pantubig.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na "aquarium", na mula sa Latin na "aquarius".
original_explanation: Basically, isang glass house para sa mga isda. Ito yung mini-version ng Manila Ocean Park na nasa sala niyo. Para sa mga isda, ito yung condo unit nila. Para sa'yo, ito yung bagay na nakaka-relax tingnan hanggang sa oras na para linisin.
usage_notes: Madalas na tumutukoy sa maliit na tangke sa bahay, ngunit maaari ring tumukoy sa malalaking pampublikong akwaryum.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili siya ng bagong isda para sa kanyang **akwaryum**.","translation":"He bought a new fish for his **aquarium**."},{"sentence":"Ang pagmamasid sa mga isda sa **akwaryum** ay nakakabawas ng stress.","translation":"Watching the fish in the **aquarium** reduces stress."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pahid o paglalagay ng pintura, semento, o barnis sa isang direksyon at sa isang galaw lamang.
original_explanation: This is a pro-level karpintero or painter term. It's that one smooth, perfect swipe of paint on a wall, or plaster on a ceiling. No streaks, no do-overs. It’s the satisfying "swoosh" of a master at work. The opposite of when you try to DIY paint your room and it looks like a blotchy mess.
usage_notes: A technical term used in construction and painting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan isang **saho** lang ang pagpahid ng masilya para maging makinis.","translation":"Applying the putty must be done in a **single, uniform stroke** to make it smooth."},{"sentence":"Tingnan mo ang galing ng pintor, tuloy-tuloy ang **saho** ng brush.","translation":"Look at the painter's skill, the **stroke** of the brush is continuous."}]

translation: to be overtaken by morning; to have something last until morning
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-abot ng umaga habang ginagawa ang isang bagay o habang nasa isang kalagayan.
original_explanation: This is what happens when your 'one episode lang' on Netflix turns into a whole season, and suddenly, may manok nang tumitilaok. Or when the chismisan with your barkada is so good, you don't realize the sun is already rising. Basically, you pulled an all-nighter. In BPO terms, ito yung shift mo.
usage_notes: Often used to describe activities that extend through the night, such as studying, working, or partying.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nangangamba siyang baka **umagahin** sila sa daan dahil sa traffic.","translation":"She's worried they might **be overtaken by morning** on the road due to traffic."},{"sentence":"Madalas kaming **umagahin** sa paglalaro ng video games.","translation":"We often play video games **until morning**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sapilitang pagkuha ng mga mahahalagang bagay mula sa isang lugar o tao, lalo na sa panahon ng digmaan o kaguluhan; mga bagay na nakuha sa ganitong paraan.
original_explanation: Think of pirates shouting 'Arrr!' and taking treasure chests. In modern terms, it's what corrupt politicians are accused of doing with public funds. It’s not just simple theft (pagnanakaw); it’s theft on a grand, often violent or systemic, scale. The 'haul' from a successful raid.
usage_notes: Carries a strong negative connotation, often associated with war, corruption, or large-scale robbery. The verb form is 'mandambong' and the act is 'pandarambong'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga kayamanang nakuha sa **dambong** ay isinumpa raw.","translation":"The treasures acquired through **plunder** were said to be cursed."},{"sentence":"Nahatulan ang opisyal dahil sa kasong pandarambong at pagkuha ng **dambong**.","translation":"The official was convicted for the case of plunder and acquiring **loot**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging bihasa o pag-alam sa isang gawain sa pamamagitan ng paulit-ulit na pagsasagawa; ang pagiging hirati sa isang sitwasyon.
original_explanation: It's the "git gud" verb of Tagalog. That feeling when you've done your BPO script so many times you can recite it in your sleep, or when you've commuted via EDSA so often that the traffic no longer fazes you. You've *sumanay* na. You've leveled up your tolerance skill.
usage_notes: This is the completed (past tense) actor-focus form. 'Nasanay' is a more common, object-focus equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumanay** na ang katawan ko sa puyatan dahil sa pag-aaral.","translation":"My body **has become accustomed** to staying up late because of studying."},{"sentence":"Dati siyang takot sa aso, pero **sumanay** na rin siya sa alaga namin.","translation":"He used to be afraid of dogs, but he eventually **got used to** our pet."}]

translation: Bicol Express (a spicy Filipino pork dish)
meaning_filipino: Isang maanghang na pagkaing Pilipino na gawa sa baboy, gata, at sili, na nagmula sa rehiyon ng Bicol.
etymology: Pinangalanan mula sa Bicol Express, isang serbisyo ng tren patungo sa rehiyon ng Bicol, kung saan sikat ang paggamit ng sili at gata sa pagluluto.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'kanin-killer'. It's that spicy, creamy pork dish that makes you sweat, cry, and ask for a second (or third) serving of rice. Perfect for when you need to feel something, even if it's just the burning sensation in your mouth.
usage_notes: The level of spiciness can vary greatly from mild to extremely hot.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-crave ako bigla ng **Bicol Express** kaya bumili ako ng gata at sili sa palengke.","translation":"I suddenly craved **Bicol Express**, so I bought coconut milk and chili at the market."},{"sentence":"Sobra ang anghang ng **Bicol Express** na niluto ni nanay, pero masarap!","translation":"The **Bicol Express** mom cooked is extremely spicy, but delicious!"}]
