translation: Lenten chanting of the Passion of Christ
meaning_filipino: Isang tradisyong panrelihiyon tuwing Kuwaresma kung saan inaawit o binibigkas nang may tono ang Pasyon, ang salaysay ng buhay, pagpapakasakit, at pagkamatay ni Hesukristo.
etymology: From Tagalog 'basa' (to read). The 'pa-' prefix indicates a request or a communal activity.
original_explanation: The OG Lenten soundtrack. It's that marathon chanting session you hear from a neighbor's house during Holy Week, usually fueled by endless coffee and tinapay. It's a religious tradition, a community gathering, and a test of vocal endurance all rolled into one. Think of it as a holy karaoke session that lasts for hours, sometimes days.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to the Catholic Holy Week tradition in the Philippines. Not to be confused with the verb 'pabasa' (to have someone read something).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naimbitahan kami sa **pabasa** sa bahay nina Aling Nena.","translation":"We were invited to the **pabasa** at Aling Nena's house."},{"sentence":"Naghanda sila ng meryenda para sa mga kalahok sa **pabasa**.","translation":"They prepared snacks for the participants of the **Lenten chanting**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao, karaniwan ay dating kasintahan, na muling naging karelasyon matapos ang isang panahon ng paghihiwalay.
original_explanation: The ex you're not supposed to text at 2 AM but you did, and now you're back together. This is your 'part 2,' your 'rebooted series,' the sequel nobody asked for but you're producing anyway. Your friends will either say 'Sabi ko na nga ba!' or 'Hay nako, 'yan na naman.' Good luck, you'll need it.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in the context of romantic relationships. It implies a reconciliation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Mark ang **kabalikan** ni Anna pagkatapos ng limang taon.","translation":"Mark is the one Anna got **back together with** after five years."},{"sentence":"Ayaw ng mga kaibigan niya sa kanyang **kabalikan**.","translation":"Her friends don't like her **reconciled partner**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gupit sa buhok na ginawa nang padalos-dalos o hindi pinag-isipan, na kadalasan ay may hindi magandang resulta.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you have a breakdown at 2 AM and the scissors start looking friendly. It's the "nag-break kami" haircut, the "bagsak ako sa exam" bangs, the "wala lang, trip ko lang" trim that you immediately regret. It's a cry for help, but in hairstyle form.
usage_notes: A common colloquial phrase often associated with emotional distress or impulsiveness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hala, nagpa-**biglang gupit** ka ba? Anong nangyari?","translation":"Oh my, did you get an **impulsive haircut**? What happened?"},{"sentence":"Mukhang resulta ng **biglang gupit** ang buhok niya, hindi pantay-pantay.","translation":"Her hair looks like the result of a **sudden haircut**; it's uneven."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggalaw pabalik-balik o pagyanig ng isang bagay, karaniwang dahil sa isang panlabas na puwersa tulad ng lindol o malakas na hangin.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na naramdaman mo 'yung lindol pero ikaw lang pala 'yung nahihilo sa stress. O 'yung upuan mo sa jeep na feeling mo nasa roller coaster ka. The act of shaking or wobbling, like a wobbly table leg that holds all your life's problems.
usage_notes: Often used to describe the shaking from an earthquake (lindol) or the swaying of a structure.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman namin ang malakas na **pag-uga** ng gusali noong lumindol.","translation":"We felt the strong **shaking** of the building during the earthquake."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa malakas na hangin, hindi mapigilan ang **pag-uga** ng tulay.","translation":"Because of the strong winds, the **swaying** of the bridge couldn't be stopped."}]

translation: to snatch; to grab or pull away forcefully
meaning_filipino: Ang sapilitang pag-agaw, paghila, o pagtanggal sa isang bagay mula sa kinalalagyan nito o sa pagkakahawak ng iba.
original_explanation: Yung ginagawa ng snatcher sa cellphone mo sa EDSA. O 'yung ginagawa mo sa last piece ng lechon sa handaan. It's a sudden, aggressive grab. The verb form of "Akin 'to!"
usage_notes: A very active and often aggressive verb. Synonymous with "agawin" but implies a more tearing or ripping motion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **labnutin** ang bag mula sa magnanakaw.","translation":"She tried to **snatch** the bag back from the thief."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **labnutin** ang laruan sa kapatid mo!","translation":"Don't **grab** the toy away from your sibling!"}]

translation: to graze, to glance off, to skim
meaning_filipino: Ang bahagyang pagtama o pagdagi sa isang bagay habang mabilis na gumagalaw, na hindi tumatama nang tuwiran o buo.
original_explanation: This is the 'muntik na' of hitting something. Imagine a speeding jeepney almost hitting you, but it just brushes against your backpack. That's 'dumaplis'. It's a near miss. In basketball, when the ball hits the rim but doesn't go in, 'dumaplis sa aro'. Sa chismis, when an accusation almost hits you but is really for the person next to you, 'dumaplis lang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dumaplis** lang sa braso ko ang bala kaya hindi ako gaanong nasaktan.","translation":"The bullet just **grazed** my arm, so I wasn't badly hurt."},{"sentence":"Mabuti na lang at **dumaplis** lang ang bola sa kanyang ulo.","translation":"It's a good thing the ball only **skimmed** his head."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagpapatulo ng laway sa isang bagay o tao.
original_explanation: What a baby does to your new shirt, or what you accidentally do to your seatmate on the bus when you fall asleep. "Huwag mo akong lawayan!" is a valid complaint.
usage_notes: Often used in an accidental or sometimes derogatory context. The action is 'nilawayan' (drooled on).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **lawayan** ang libro.","translation":"Don't **drool on** the book."},{"sentence":"**Nilawayan** ng sanggol ang kanyang laruan.","translation":"The baby **drooled on** its toy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, karaniwang pagkain, na sumailalim sa proseso ng pagluluto at hindi na hilaw.
original_explanation: The state of being ready to eat. When the rice is no longer hard and the meat is no longer pink, it's 'luto na!' It's the finish line of your culinary efforts. Also the state you wish your brain was in before a major exam (fully-cooked with knowledge) instead of being hilaw (raw) or sunog (burnt).
usage_notes: The stress is on the second syllable (/lu-TO/), distinguishing it from the noun 'lúto' (/LU-to/).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siguraduhin mong **luto** na ang kanin bago mo ito hanguin.","translation":"Make sure the rice is **cooked** before you take it off the heat."}]

translation: act of kneeling to beg or plead
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagluhod bilang tanda ng matinding pakiusap, pagsusumamo, o paghingi ng tawad.
etymology: From "sikluhod" (to kneel in pleading), which is a compound of "sikad" (a stamping of the foot) and "luhod" (kneel). The "paN-" prefix is added to form the noun.
original_explanation: This isn't just kneeling. This is telenovela-level begging. It's the 'patawarin mo ako, gagawin ko ang lahat' scene, usually done in the rain. It's the ultimate act of desperation, when you're willing to drop to your knees to ask for forgiveness or a huge favor.
usage_notes: Implies a deep sense of desperation, humility, or supplication. It's more intense than simply "pagluhod" (kneeling).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Walang nagawa ang kanyang **paninikluhod** upang ibalik ang tiwala ng kanyang asawa.","translation":"His **act of pleading on his knees** did nothing to win back his wife's trust."},{"sentence":"Sa kanyang **paninikluhod** sa harap ng altar, humingi siya ng himala.","translation":"In his **fervent kneeling** before the altar, he asked for a miracle."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sitwasyon sa merkado kung saan may iisang nagbebenta o prodyuser lamang na kumokontrol sa suplay ng isang partikular na produkto o serbisyo.
original_explanation: Not just the board game that ruins friendships and family gatherings. It's when one company is the 'bida' and owns everything, so you have no choice but to buy from them. Parang sa love life, pag 'monopoly' ka ng isang tao, bawal ka na tumingin sa iba. The Tagalog version is 'monopolyo'.
usage_notes: The English word is often used in formal business and economic discussions, interchangeably with 'monopolyo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng gobyerno kung paano babasagin ang **monopoly** sa industriya ng telekomunikasyon.","translation":"The government is studying how to break the **monopoly** in the telecommunications industry."},{"sentence":"Ang pagkakaroon ng **monopoly** ay maaaring magresulta sa mas mataas na presyo para sa mga konsyumer.","translation":"Having a **monopoly** can result in higher prices for consumers."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang elektroniko na nagpapalit ng signal na elektrikal upang maging tunog na naririnig. Ginagamit upang palakasin ang tunog mula sa isang audio source.
original_explanation: This is the source of your neighbor's videoke session at 2 AM. It's what you connect your phone to via Bluetooth to blast your 'sad girl' playlist. From the tiny ones you can fit in your pocket to the giant ones that shake the entire barangay during a fiesta, the speaker is the modern-day town crier.
usage_notes: Refers almost exclusively to the electronic device. To refer to a person who speaks, 'tagapagsalita' is used, although 'speaker' is also used in formal contexts like conferences. This entry focuses on the device.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakihinaan mo naman ang **speaker**, masyadong malakas.","translation":"Please turn down the **speaker**, it's too loud."},{"sentence":"May dala ka bang Bluetooth **speaker** para sa outing?","translation":"Did you bring a Bluetooth **speaker** for the outing?"}]

translation: to prop up; to support something
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng tukod o suporta sa isang bagay upang ito ay mapanatiling tuwid, matatag, o hindi gumuho.
original_explanation: The action verb version of 'tukod'. This is what you do when you put pillows behind your drunk friend to keep them from falling over. Or when you brace an old wall to keep it from collapsing. It's the act of being the support system.
usage_notes: The object-focused verb form of the root word 'tukod'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **tukuran** ang pader bago ito tuluyang gumuho.","translation":"The wall needs **to be propped up** before it completely collapses."},{"sentence":"**Tukuran** mo ang sanga para hindi mabali sa dami ng bunga.","translation":"**Support** the branch so it won't break from the weight of the fruit."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kusang-loob o di-kusang paglalabas ng laman ng sikmura sa pamamagitan ng bibig.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "suká" (pagsusuka) at panlaping -um-.
original_explanation: What happens after too much sisig and five bottles of Red Horse. Or that feeling you get when you see your ex with their new partner. It's your body's (or heart's) ultimate "nope" button. The aftermath of a bad decision, a bumpy bus ride, or a really cringey moment.
usage_notes: Anyong pangnagdaan. Ang diin ay nasa huling pantig ng salitang-ugat (suká), na iba sa súka (vinegar).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahilo siya sa byahe kaya siya **sumuka**.","translation":"He got dizzy during the trip so he **vomited**."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos uminom ng gamot, **sumuka** ang bata.","translation":"After taking the medicine, the child **threw up**."}]

meaning_filipino: Dalawang mahabang tikin o patpat na may tungtungan para sa paa, ginagamit upang makalakad nang mas mataas mula sa lupa.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung larong pambata na kailangan ng super balancing skills. Gawa sa kawayan, with a small step near the bottom. Parang pagsuot ng high heels for the first time, pero mas extreme version. You use tayakad to literally rise above the situation (or the mud). Sa corporate world, 'yung pag-angat mo sa career ladder, parang naglalakad ka sa tayakad—one wrong move, bagsak.
usage_notes: Pangunahing kilala bilang isang tradisyonal na larong Pilipino. Ang kilos ng paglakad sa tayakad ay "magtayakad".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpaligsahan ang mga bata sa paglalakad gamit ang **tayakad**.","translation":"The children competed in walking on **stilts**."},{"sentence":"Mahirap magbalanse sa **tayakad** lalo na kung maputik ang daan.","translation":"It's hard to balance on **stilts** especially if the path is muddy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sistema ng pagtatrabaho o pag-aaral kung saan ang isang tao ay pumapasok sa opisina o paaralan sa ilang mga araw at nagtatrabaho o nag-aaral mula sa bahay sa iba.
etymology: From English 'hybrid' + 'setup.' A loan phrase that became widespread globally in the 2020s.
original_explanation: The post-pandemic work arrangement that's the corporate world's version of "can't decide." It's part-WFH, part-on-site. You get the comfort of working in your pambahay clothes for a few days, but then you have to remember what actual pants feel like for your office days. It's the best (or worst) of both worlds, depending on the traffic on your "in-office" day.
usage_notes: A very modern term that became widespread after the COVID-19 pandemic. Usually used in the context of work (BPO, corporate) or education.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas gusto ko ang **hybrid setup** dahil nababalanse ko ang trabaho at buhay-pamilya.","translation":"I prefer the **hybrid setup** because I can balance work and family life."},{"sentence":"Ipinatupad ng kumpanya ang isang **hybrid setup** simula ngayong taon.","translation":"The company implemented a **hybrid setup** starting this year."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa bilis ng pagkilos, paggawa, o pag-unawa; hindi mahirap.
original_explanation: The speed at which you close a browser tab when your boss walks by. The opposite of the MRT during rush hour. It's that "1-day delivery" promise from Shopee that actually arrives in a week. "Ang dali lang pala niyan!" is what you say *after* someone shows you how to do it.
usage_notes: Can mean both "quick" (madali) and "easy" (madali). The root form "dali" is often used in commands or exclamations. The stress is on the last syllable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dali**! Aalis na ang bus!","translation":"**Quick**! The bus is about to leave!"},{"sentence":"Napakadali lang ng pagsusulit kung nag-aral ka.","translation":"The exam is very **easy** if you studied."}]

meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahan o pagkakataong ipagpatuloy ang isang nasimulang gawain, paglalakbay, o kalagayan.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `makapag-` (kakayahan) at `patuloy` (pagpapatuloy ng kilos), na nagmula sa salitang-ugat na `tuloy`.
original_explanation: This is what you tell yourself when you're on your 5th coffee just to finish a deadline: 'Kailangan kong makapagpatuloy.' It's the mantra for moving on from a past relationship, for finishing your degree despite the odds, or simply for getting to the next level of a game. It's the ability to keep going, to push forward. Go lang nang go!
usage_notes: Ang `makapagpatuloy` ay tumutukoy sa kakayahang ipagpatuloy ang isang bagay na nasimulan na.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng maikling pahinga, sana'y **makapagpatuloy** na tayo sa ating pagpupulong.","translation":"After a short break, I hope we can **continue** with our meeting."},{"sentence":"Hindi siya **makapagpatuloy** sa pag-aaral dahil sa problemang pinansyal.","translation":"He/She is not **able to continue** studying due to financial problems."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang estado sa isang relasyon kung saan may pagtitinginan ang dalawang tao ngunit walang pormal na kasunduan o titulo. Dinaglat mula sa pariralang Ingles na 'Mutual Understanding'.
etymology: From the English phrase 'Mutual Understanding', abbreviated to M.U.
original_explanation: 'Mag-Un,' 'Mutual Understanding,' or 'Malabong Usapan.' It's the relationship status before the *actual* relationship status. You're more than friends, but not quite lovers. You go on dates, have late-night calls, but if someone asks, 'Kayo na ba?' the answer is a complicated shrug. It's the Schrödinger's cat of Pinoy dating.
usage_notes: Pronounced as two letters, 'M.U.' but often written as 'MU' or 'mu'. It's a cornerstone of modern Filipino dating slang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano na ba kayo? **MU** pa rin?","translation":"What's your status? Still in **MU** (Mutual Understanding)?"},{"sentence":"Ayoko na sa **MU**, gusto ko ng commitment.","translation":"I'm tired of having a **Mutual Understanding**, I want commitment."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkakaroon ng nawawalang ngipin, lalo na sa harapan.
original_explanation: The state of your smile after a street basketball game gone wrong, or when you were a kid and your milk teeth started falling out. It's that awkward phase where you smile with your mouth closed in photos. Your dentist's potential nightmare... or business opportunity.
usage_notes: Describes a person who is missing one or more front teeth. It can be used as a noun ("isang bungal") or an adjective ("siya ay bungal").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **bungal** ang bata matapos matanggalan ng ngipin.","translation":"The child became **gap-toothed** after his tooth was extracted."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang tumawa nang malakas, makikita ang pagka-**bungal** mo.","translation":"Don't laugh too loud, your **missing front tooth** will show."}]

translation: I might as well; me too; I'll do it myself
meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyon na nagpapahiwatig ng pag-ako sa isang gawain o pagsang-ayon sa isang sitwasyon, kadalasan dahil wala nang ibang gagawa o bilang pagsunod sa iba.
etymology: A common Filipino phrase composed of 'ako' (I), 'na' (now/already), and 'rin' (also/too).
original_explanation: The official phrase of the 'pasan-ko-ang-daigdig' club. You say this with a sigh when you realize no one else is going to wash the dishes or finish the report. It's a mix of resignation, initiative, and a little bit of martyrdom. 'Sige na, ako na rin bibili ng yelo.'
usage_notes: The meaning changes with context. It can mean 'I'll do it' (initiative/resignation) or 'Me too' (joining in). 'Ako na lang' is a close alternative.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil walang ibang nagboluntaryo, sinabi niyang, \"**Ako na rin** ang magliligpit.\"","translation":"Since no one else volunteered, he said, \"**I'll do** the cleaning **myself**.\""},{"sentence":"\"Sasama ako sa party.\" \"Sige, **ako na rin**.\"","translation":"\"I'm going to the party.\" \"Okay, **me too**.\""}]
related: ["ako na lang","sige na nga","bahala na","pati ako"]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng tunog mula sa lalamunan upang alisin ang bara o upang makuha ang atensyon ng iba.
original_explanation: That awkward moment when you enter a room and no one notices you, so you let out a little cough. Or when the crush of your life passes by and you suddenly need to signal your presence without actually saying 'hi'. It's the OG 'ehem'.
usage_notes: Often used to get someone's attention subtly or to express awkwardness or disapproval.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumighim** ang guro para makuha ang atensyon ng maiingay na estudyante.","translation":"The teacher **cleared his throat** to get the attention of the noisy students."},{"sentence":"Bigla siyang **tumighim** nang makita niyang dumarating ang kanyang biyenan.","translation":"He suddenly **cleared his throat** when he saw his mother-in-law arriving."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pananggalang na isinusuot sa ulo upang maprotektahan ito mula sa pinsala o tama.
etymology: Hiram na salita mula sa Ingles na "helmet".
original_explanation: The non-negotiable accessory for motorcycle riders, cyclists, and construction workers. Para sa iba, ito yung "emotional helmet" na sinusuot mo para 'di ka maapektuhan sa mga sinasabi ng mga Marites. Safety first, both for your ulo and your feelings.
usage_notes: Mahalaga para sa kaligtasan sa maraming aktibidad. Ang pagsusuot nito ay ipinapatupad ng batas para sa mga nagmomotorsiklo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging magsuot ng **helmet** kapag nagbibisikleta para iwas-disgrasya.","translation":"Always wear a **helmet** when riding a bicycle to avoid accidents."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na hindi nagmula o hindi kabilang sa isang partikular na lugar, grupo, o komunidad.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "taga-" (nagmula sa) at salitang-ugat na "labas" (outside).
original_explanation: The new person in the office who doesn't get the inside jokes yet. The 'dayo' in a local basketball league. You feel like a tagalabas when your friends start talking about a shared memory you weren't there for. It's the feeling of not belonging, even for a moment.
usage_notes: Carries a stronger sense of not belonging than 'taga-ibang lugar' (from another place).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bilang isang **tagalabas**, ramdam niya na pinagtitinginan siya ng mga tao sa baryo.","translation":"As an **outsider**, he felt that the people in the village were staring at him."}]

meaning_filipino: Paraan ng pagsulat na ginagamitan ng kamay at panulat, salungat sa paggamit ng makinilya o kompyuter.
original_explanation: Before keyboards and touchscreens, this was the OG way to slide into someone's DMs—by actually sliding a handwritten letter. It's your personal font, the one that tells people if you're a doctor or just really, really rushed. The original "seen zone" was when you saw they read your letter but didn't write back.
usage_notes: Used to describe the physical act of writing by hand or the resulting script.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap basahin ang **sulat-kamay** niya.","translation":"His **handwriting** is hard to read."},{"sentence":"Mas personal ang regalong may kasamang liham na **sulat-kamay**.","translation":"A gift is more personal with an accompanying **handwritten** letter."}]

translation: to take revenge on; to retaliate against
meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng isang kilos bilang ganti o katumbas na kapinsalaan sa isang taong nakasakit o nakagawa ng mali.
original_explanation: This is the official verb of Pinoy teleserye plot twists. The "Aha! Akala mo tapos na tayo?" moment. It's when you plot your comeback after a friend eats your lunch from the office fridge. From petty office pranks to epic family sagas, higantihan is serving revenge, best served cold... or with a dramatic confrontation in the rain.
usage_notes: Implies a reciprocal action, often negative. It's the act of getting back at someone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binalaan niya ang mga kaaway na balang araw ay **hihigantihan** niya sila.","translation":"He warned his enemies that one day he would **take revenge on** them."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **higantihan** ang kasamaan ng kapwa kasamaan.","translation":"Do not **retaliate against** evil with more evil."}]

translation: to be chopped into pieces, to be splintered
meaning_filipino: Ang maputol o mahati sa maraming maliliit na piraso, karaniwan ay tumutukoy sa kahoy o kawayan sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng itak o katulad na kasangkapan.
etymology: From `ma-` (involuntary/ability prefix) + `tilad` (a chip or splinter of wood).
original_explanation: Imagine a lumberjack going wild on a log. The end result is that the log is matilad—chopped up into many pieces or splinters. It's more than just being 'cut'; it implies being broken down into smaller, often rough, segments. Parang puso mo after ng breakup, tilad-tilad.
usage_notes: Specific to materials like wood or bamboo being broken down. Can be used metaphorically for something shattered.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **matilad** ang mga kawayan para magawa ang pader.","translation":"The bamboos need **to be chopped into pieces** to make the wall."},{"sentence":"**Natilad** ang sanga ng puno dahil sa lakas ng hangin.","translation":"The tree branch **was splintered** by the strong wind."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pahayag kung saan ang isang ideya ay inuulit gamit ang magkaibang salita ngunit may parehong kahulugan, na kadalasang hindi na kailangan.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "tautología", na mula sa Griyegong "tautologia".
original_explanation: Ito 'yung sinabi mo na, inulit mo pa in another way. Example: "Libre ito, walang bayad!" or "Bumaba ka sa baba." Gets na namin the first time, bes! Parang 'yung friend mong paulit-ulit mag-kwento about sa ex niya. Yes, we know, nasaktan ka. It's a tawtolohiya of hugot.
usage_notes: Isang termino sa lohika, retorika, at linggwistika.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pangungusap na 'Ang mga biyuda ay mga babaeng namatayan ng asawa' ay isang halimbawa ng **tawtolohiya**.","translation":"The sentence 'Widows are women whose husbands have died' is an example of a **tautology**."},{"sentence":"Iwasan ang **tawtolohiya** sa pagsusulat upang maging mas malinaw ang iyong mensahe.","translation":"Avoid **tautology** in writing to make your message clearer."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagwawasto, pagtatama, o pag-aayos ng isang pagkakamali, kamalian, o depekto.
etymology: From English 'correct' + '-in' suffix (Filipino verbalizer). 'Korek' is a common Filipinized spelling/pronunciation of 'correct'.
original_explanation: A Taglish verb for 'to correct.' It's what your teacher does to your exam paper with a red pen. Or what your mom does when you cook the rice wrong. 'Hey, **korekin** mo nga 'yang grammar mo sa email bago i-send kay boss!' ('Hey, correct your grammar in that email before sending it to the boss!')
usage_notes: A very common Taglish verb used in both casual and semi-formal (like office) settings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **korekin** mo ang mga mali sa ulat na ito.","translation":"Please, **correct** the errors in this report."},{"sentence":"Hayaan mo na, ako na ang bahalang **korekin** ang mga papeles.","translation":"Don't worry about it, I'll be the one to **correct** the papers."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malalim na pagkahumaling o pananabik sa isang tao, bagay, o lugar na nag-iwan ng marka; ang hirap sa paglimot.
original_explanation: That feeling when you can't get over someone. It's more than just 'miss ko na siya'. It's a deep, lingering attachment. Parang hangover, pero sa feelings. Yung kahit wala na kayo, a part of them is still stuck with you. Classic 'sana ako pa rin' feels.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang malalim at makatang salita, hindi karaniwang ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nananatili ang **hawili** niya sa kanyang kabiyak kahit ito'y pumanaw na.","translation":"His **lingering affection** for his spouse remains even after their passing."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-angat o pagbalik ng isang bagay paitaas o patagilid matapos tumama sa isang matigas na ibabaw.
original_explanation: What a basketball does on the court, or what your check does when you have insufficient funds (yikes!). When you try to make a move on your crush and get rejected, tapos biglang may um-epal at sila ang nag-work out, na-**talbog** ka. It's the rebound, whether in sports or in love.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb root (e.g., tumalbog - to bounce). Metaphorically means being outshone or superseded.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malakas ang **talbog** ng bola kaya lumabas ito ng court.","translation":"The **bounce** of the ball was strong, so it went out of the court."},{"sentence":"Sa ganda ng boses niya, tiyak na **talbog** ang lahat ng ibang kalahok.","translation":"With the beauty of her voice, all other contestants will surely be **outshone**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gusali o estruktura na nagsisilbing tirahan ng isang tao o pamilya.
original_explanation: Your personal Batcave, charging station, and the only place where your 'pambahay' outfit is considered high fashion. It's where the Wi-Fi connects automatically and where you can ugly-cry in peace after a tough day. Basically, your personal headquarters.
usage_notes: Can refer to the physical structure (house) or the concept of a home, which is more accurately 'tahanan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umuwi ka na sa **bahay**, hinahanap ka na ng nanay mo.","translation":"Go **home** now, your mother is looking for you."},{"sentence":"Nagpapagawa kami ng bagong **bahay** sa probinsya.","translation":"We are having a new **house** built in the province."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pag-aalis ng manipis na bahagi ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay kahoy, gamit ang isang matalim na kasangkapan upang ito ay hubugin o pakinisin.
original_explanation: Think of your lolo making a toy for you from a piece of wood, slowly shaving off bits with a knife. That's pagkayas. It's the OG way of 3D printing, but with more splinters and patience. It's the meticulous work of shaping something from a rough block into something useful or beautiful.
usage_notes: Often used for wood, bamboo, or similar materials. Distinct from 'pagkayod' which is for grating.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkayas** ng kawayan para gawing patpat ay nangangailangan ng tiyaga.","translation":"The **shaving** of bamboo to make sticks requires patience."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko ang sining sa **pagkayas** ng eskultor sa kanyang obra.","translation":"I saw the art in the sculptor's **whittling** of his masterpiece."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagpapahid ng isang malagkit o makapal na substansya sa isang ibabaw sa paraang hindi pantay o walang kaayusan.
original_explanation: Imagine a kid getting their hands on a chocolate cake. 'Yan 'yung pag-smear ng icing sa mukha, sa damit, sa pader. It's messy, it's thick, and it's everywhere. Parang make-up ng nagmamadali.
usage_notes: Nagpapahiwatig ng makapal at madalas na magulong paglalagay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magkulapol** ng putik sa bagong pintura na pader.","translation":"Don't **smear** mud on the newly painted wall."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **magkulapol** ng foundation para takpan ang kanyang mga tigyawat.","translation":"She tried to **daub thickly** with foundation to cover her pimples."}]

meaning_filipino: Kumapit at bumitin sa isang bagay gamit ang mga kamay o paa, tulad ng sa sanga ng puno o sa mga rehas.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're riding the MRT during rush hour and you're just a human chandelier, hanging on for dear life. It's also what monkeys do, and what kids do on playground monkey bars before they discover TikTok.
usage_notes: Often used to describe the action of hanging playfully or precariously from something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig **maglambitin** sa mga sanga ng puno ang mga unggoy.","translation":"Monkeys love **to hang** from the branches of trees."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **maglambitin** diyan sa pinto, baka masira!","translation":"Don't **dangle** from the door, you might break it!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang akronim para sa "Sasakyan para sa Kalinangan ng Bansa," isang uri ng sasakyan na idinisenyo at binuo sa Pilipinas noong dekada '70.
etymology: A portmanteau of 'sasakyan' (vehicle) and 'bayan' (nation), officially an acronym for "Sasakyan para sa Kalinangan ng Bansa".
original_explanation: The OG Pinoy-made car! Before the Vios and the Fortuner, there was the Sakbayan. It was a local attempt at a national car, kind of like a jeepney but more "car-like." Ask your tito or lolo about it; it's a piece of Pinoy automotive history and a major throwback.
usage_notes: Refers to a specific historical vehicle model from the Marcos era, a product of an partnership between DMG Inc. and Volkswagen. Rarely used today except in historical or nostalgic contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang luma nilang **Sakbayan** ay nakatambak na lang sa garahe.","translation":"Their old **Sakbayan** is just gathering dust in the garage."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malakas at paulit-ulit na pag-alog o pagyugyog sa isang bagay.
etymology: Likely onomatopoeic, imitating the sound or motion of shaking.
original_explanation: Imagine you're trying to get the last drop of ketchup out of the bottle. That violent, desperate shaking? 'Yan ang pag-ug-og. It's what happens to you inside a jeepney running over a pothole-filled road. It's a more intense, more aggressive version of "yugyog" or "alog." Not a gentle rock, but a full-on, brain-rattling shake. The verb form is 'ug-ugin'.
usage_notes: The verb is 'ug-ugin' (to shake). The root word 'ug-og' itself can describe the act or the jolt. 'Na-ug-og' means was shaken/jolted.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ug-ugin** ang mesa, natatapon ang kape ko!","translation":"Don't **shake** the table violently, my coffee is spilling!"},{"sentence":"Naramdaman ko ang malakas na **ug-og** nang dumaan ang trak.","translation":"I felt a strong **jolt** when the truck passed by."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa anumang bagay, gamot, o pamamaraan na may kakayahang magligtas ng buhay ng isang tao mula sa tiyak na kamatayan.
etymology: A compound word from 'panligtas' (for saving) and 'buhay' (life).
original_explanation: This is the hardcore version of 'panligtas'. We're not just talking about getting out of a jam; we're talking about cheating death. Think CPR, a defibrillator, an EpiPen, or that last-minute project save that prevents your boss from firing you. It's the ultimate clutch play.
usage_notes: A specific and serious term used for things that literally prevent death.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang operasyon ay isang prosesong **panligtas-buhay** para sa pasyente.","translation":"The operation is a **life-saving** procedure for the patient."},{"sentence":"Marunong ka bang gumamit ng mga kagamitang **panligtas-buhay** tulad ng AED?","translation":"Do you know how to use **life-saving** equipment like an AED?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang arko ng mga kulay na makikita sa kalangitan, sanhi ng repraksyon at dispersyon ng liwanag ng araw sa mga patak ng ulan o tubig.
etymology: Compound of 'bahag' (g-string, loincloth) and 'hari' (king), literally 'the king's loincloth', a reference to folklore.
original_explanation: That magical arc in the sky that makes everyone stop and take a picture for their IG story. Legend says there's a pot of gold at the end, but in the Philippines, it's more like a sign that the bagyo is finally over and you can go outside. It's the original 'It gets better' meme, courtesy of Mother Nature. It's also a powerful symbol for the LGBTQ+ community, representing diversity and pride.
usage_notes: A beautiful and poetic word. The etymology is a subject of folklore.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang magandang **bahaghari** ang lumitaw sa langit pagkatapos ng ulan.","translation":"A beautiful **rainbow** appeared in the sky after the rain."},{"sentence":"Ang mga kulay ng **bahaghari** ay pula, kahel, dilaw, luntian, bughaw, indigo, at lila.","translation":"The colors of the **rainbow** are red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng patuloy na pagpapatak ng likidong gamot o sustansya sa ugat ng isang pasyente gamit ang isang tubo; karaniwang tumutukoy sa suwero.
original_explanation: Eto 'yung "naka-**drip**" o "naka-suwero." Picture mo 'yung kamay ng pasyente sa ospital na may nakatusok na karayom at may nakasabit na plastic bag ng Dextrose. 'Yan ang **drip**. Sa modern slang, **drip** also means you have great style or 'swag', pero sa Pinas, pag sinabing **drip**, ospital agad ang iisipin mo.
usage_notes: Sa kontekstong Pilipino, halos palaging tumutukoy ito sa IV drip o suwero sa ospital.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isinugod siya sa ospital at agad siyang nilagyan ng **drip** dahil sa dehydration.","translation":"He was rushed to the hospital and immediately put on a **drip** due to dehydration."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagtatama o pag-aayos ng isang kamalian o pagkukulang upang maging wasto o tama.
original_explanation: This is what you hope happens to your exam after your teacher realizes they made a mistake in the answer key. It's the "oops, my bad, let's fix it" moment, but for documents, calculations, or even a misguided life choice that needs a do-over. "Sana all pwedeng i-mawasto."
usage_notes: Often used in formal or written contexts, especially regarding errors in documents, accounts, or official records.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **mawasto** ang lahat ng mali sa listahan bago ito isumite.","translation":"All errors on the list need **to be corrected** before it is submitted."},{"sentence":"Umaasa siyang **mawasto** ang maling akala ng kaibigan tungkol sa kanya.","translation":"He hopes that his friend's wrong impression of him **will be rectified**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging malabnaw; kakulangan sa lapot o pagiging puro ng isang likido.
etymology: From `labnaw` (dilute, thin liquid) with `ka-` and `-an` affixes to form an abstract noun.
original_explanation: This is the sad state of your coffee when you put too much water, or the soup that tastes more like hot water than sinigang. It’s the lack of substance, the 'watered-down' feeling. 'Ay, ano ba 'tong juice, puro tubig! Grabe ang kalabnawan.'
usage_notes: The antonym is 'kalaputan' (thickness).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa **kalabnawan** ng pintura, kinailangan namin itong patungan ng ilang beses.","translation":"Because of the **thinness** of the paint, we needed to apply several coats."},{"sentence":"Reklamo ng customer ang **kalabnawan** ng tsokolateng inihain sa kanya.","translation":"The customer's complaint was the **wateriness** of the hot chocolate served to him."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang indibidwal na tanyag at kinikilala ng marami sa lipunan, karaniwan dahil sa kanilang tagumpay sa isang partikular na larangan tulad ng sining, politika, o isports.
original_explanation: Basically, your VIP, your "sikat" person, the "artista" or politician everyone knows. They're the ones you see on billboards along EDSA, in your social media feed, or causing traffic because of a movie shoot. They have more than 1M followers and probably a blue checkmark.
usage_notes: "Kilalang" is the linker form of "kilala" (known) modifying "tao" (person).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **kilalang tao** ang dumalo sa premiere night ng pelikula.","translation":"Many **celebrities** attended the movie's premiere night."},{"sentence":"Isang **kilalang tao** sa larangan ng medisina ang aming panauhing pandangal.","translation":"A **well-known person** in the field of medicine is our guest of honor."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang tela o materyal na ginagamit sa pagpunas ng dumi, likido, o alikabok.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'punas' (wipe) at panlaping 'pa-'.
original_explanation: Your trusty sidekick in the war against spills and messes. It's the basahan, the towel, the tissue, or even the sleeve of your shirt in a desperate moment. The official tool for "punas-punas lang 'pag may time." Every household has a designated (and usually grimy) papunas.
usage_notes: Karaniwang tumutukoy sa isang piraso ng tela.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha ka ng **papunas** at linisin mo ang natapong kape sa mesa.","translation":"Get a **rag** and clean the spilled coffee on the table."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang aparato na karaniwang inilalagay sa tabi ng pinto na gumagawa ng tunog kapag pinindot upang ipaalam sa mga nasa loob na mayroong tao sa labas.
original_explanation: The official "Tao po!" device for houses in subdivisions. If you don't have one, you just shout "Tao po!" or clap your hands. If you're a delivery rider, you press this like your life depends on it.
usage_notes: Karaniwang baybay at gamit sa Pilipinas. Ang katutubong katumbas ay maaaring "kampanilya ng pinto" ngunit hindi ito karaniwang ginagamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pindutin mo ang **doorbell** para malaman nilang nandito na tayo.","translation":"Press the **doorbell** so they know we're here."},{"sentence":"Sira yata ang **doorbell** nila, kumatok ka na lang.","translation":"I think their **doorbell** is broken, just knock instead."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan, posisyon, o ranggo ng isang tao o bagay sa lipunan, sa isang organisasyon, o sa isang partikular na sitwasyon.
etymology: From ka- + tayo + -an, literally "state of standing".
original_explanation: Your relationship status on Facebook: 'In a relationship', 'Single', or the ever-popular 'It's complicated'. Pwede rin itong tumukoy sa social standing mo—kung VIP ka ba o Gen Ad lang. O kaya sa work, kung rank-and-file ka ba o C-level exec na.
usage_notes: Often used in formal contexts like legal documents, social sciences, or when discussing one's role or position.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **katayuan** mo sa kumpanya?","translation":"What is your **position** in the company?"},{"sentence":"Pinag-uusapan nila ang **katayuan** ng ekonomiya ng bansa.","translation":"They are discussing the **condition** of the country's economy."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga na malinaw ang **katayuan** ng inyong relasyon.","translation":"It's important that the **status** of your relationship is clear."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o pangkat na kumokontra, tumututol, o lumalaban sa isang panig, ideya, o panukala.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "taga-" (pananda ng panig) at salitang-ugat na "salungat" (kontra).
original_explanation: The 'kontrabida' in your life story. The one who always clicks 'dislike' on your ideas during a meeting. In politics, they're the opposition party. In family reunions, they're the tita who asks, "Kailan ka mag-aasawa?"
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa mga pormal na konteksto tulad ng debate, politika, o panitikan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **tagasalungat** ay naghain ng kanilang mga argumento laban sa bagong batas.","translation":"The **opposition** presented their arguments against the new law."},{"sentence":"Handa siyang harapin ang sinumang **tagasalungat** sa kanyang mga prinsipyo.","translation":"He is ready to face any **opponent** of his principles."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tirahan o gusali na inaalok para sa pansamantalang paninirahan kapalit ng regular na bayad o upa.
original_explanation: The OG Airbnb. Ito 'yung business ng tita mo na maraming "For Rent" signs sa gate. Pwede itong apartment, condo, o isang buong bahay. Your landlord's prized possession and your source of "due date na naman ng renta" stress.
usage_notes: A very common term in real estate and everyday life. Often shortened to just "paupahan".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghanap kami ng **paupahang-bahay** na malapit sa aking trabaho.","translation":"We looked for a **house for rent** near my workplace."},{"sentence":"Ang kita niya sa **paupahang-bahay** ay sapat para sa kanyang mga gastusin.","translation":"Her income from the **rental property** is enough for her expenses."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang magpakita ng maliliit at mabilis na kislap ng liwanag; ang kumislap o magniningning.
etymology: From 'mang-' and the root 'kislap', meaning 'sparkle' or 'gleam'.
original_explanation: The OG 'Sparkle.' This is what your eyes do when the food delivery arrives. It's what the sea does at sunset in Boracay. It's the effect on a diamond ring in a jewelry ad. It’s the visual equivalent of a magical 'ting!' sound, perfect for describing anything that catches the light and your attention.
usage_notes: Often used in a poetic or descriptive manner to describe light reflecting off surfaces like water, eyes, gems, or polished objects.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nangislap** ang kanyang mga mata nang matanggap ang magandang balita.","translation":"Her eyes **sparkled** when she received the good news."},{"sentence":"Ang mga bituin ay **nangigislap** sa madilim na kalangitan.","translation":"The stars were **twinkling** in the dark sky."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagdudulot ng interes, kasiyahan, o pagkagusto dahil sa mga katangiang kaakit-akit o hindi karaniwan.
original_explanation: The feeling you get when you start a new K-drama and you can't stop watching. Or when you stumble upon a 'Marites' thread that's so juicy, you read all 200 comments. It's something that grabs your attention and doesn't let go. The opposite of a boring university lecture.
usage_notes: Describes experiences, stories, hobbies, or personalities that are captivating.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Talagang **nakawiwili** ang mga kuwento ng aking lolo tungkol sa kanyang kabataan.","translation":"My grandfather's stories about his youth are truly **engaging**."},{"sentence":"Para sa akin, **nakawiwili** ang pag-aaral ng mga bagong wika.","translation":"For me, learning new languages is **interesting**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malapot na likido na namumuo sa lalamunan o baga, karaniwang inilalabas sa pamamagitan ng pag-ubo.
original_explanation: Let's be real, it's that gross stuff you cough up when you have a cold or flu. It's the enemy you fight with Solmux or a good, hearty 'ehem!'. It's the body's way of saying, 'Hey, there's a party of germs in here and we need to evict them ASAP.'
usage_notes: The verb form is 'dumahak' (to cough up or spit phlegm).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May bahid ng dugo ang kanyang **dahak** kaya dinala siya sa ospital.","translation":"There was a trace of blood in his **phlegm** so he was taken to the hospital."},{"sentence":"Mahirap matulog kapag puno ng **dahak** ang lalamunan.","translation":"It's hard to sleep when your throat is full of **phlegm**."}]

translation: to take to heart; to take something seriously or personally
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-iisip nang malalim at pag-aalala nang labis tungkol sa isang bagay, na nagdudulot ng matinding emosyonal na epekto.
etymology: From `dibdib` (chest/heart) + `-in` (verb suffix). Literally "to put in the chest/heart".
original_explanation: This is what you do when your crush leaves you on 'seen'. You overthink, you replay scenarios, you make a whole teleserye in your head. Basically, 'wag mo masyadong **dibdibihin** ang life, beshie. It's the emotional equivalent of letting something live rent-free in your heart.
usage_notes: Often used as advice in the negative form ("Huwag mong dibdibihin") to mean "Don't take it so seriously" or "Don't be too affected by it."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinabi lang niyang mataba ka, **dinibdib** mo na agad.","translation":"She just said you were fat, and you immediately **took it to heart**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **dibdibihin** ang mga puna nila; ang mahalaga ay masaya ka.","translation":"Don't **take their criticisms to heart**; what's important is that you're happy."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng matinding pagmamahal, paggalang, at pagmamalasakit sa sariling bansa.
original_explanation: That feeling of pride when Hidilyn Diaz or Catriona Gray wins. It's choosing local brands, supporting OPM, or simply respecting the flag. It's having a deep love for the Philippines, warts and all.
usage_notes: A positive term for someone who loves their country. It is often used interchangeably with 'makabayan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagtangkilik sa sariling produkto ay isang gawaing **makabansa**.","translation":"Patronizing one's own products is a **patriotic** act."},{"sentence":"Kilala si Heneral Luna bilang isang bayaning may matatag na paninindigang **makabansa**.","translation":"General Luna is known as a hero with a strong **nationalistic** stance."}]

translation: to launch; to cause; to bring about
meaning_filipino: Maging sanhi o simula ng isang pangyayari, kilos, o proyekto; itulak o pasimulan.
original_explanation: Think of it as the "go" signal or the first domino to fall. The new chismis about the office manager could "maibunsod" a series of resignations. A viral TikTok video can "maibunsod" a new dance craze. It's the starting push that gets something big rolling.
usage_notes: Often used in formal contexts like news reports, academic papers, and official statements to mean 'to launch' a program or 'to be caused by' an event.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay **maibunsod** ng bagong batas ang tunay na pagbabago.","translation":"Hopefully, the new law will **bring about** real change."},{"sentence":"Ang kanilang pag-aaway ay maaaring **maibunsod** ng matagal nang samaan ng loob.","translation":"Their fight could be **caused** by long-held grudges."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong may propesyon na magpayo sa usaping legal at kumatawan sa kliyente sa korte.
original_explanation: 'Yung friend mo na laging may "objection!" kapag nag-aaway kayo sa kung anong movie ang panonoorin. Sila 'yung tatawagan mo kapag may problema ka sa batas, o kapag kailangan mo ng magaling mag-argue. From Spanish "abogado".
usage_notes: The feminine form 'abugada' is also common. 'Manananggol' is a more formal, native Tagalog equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating kumuha ng magaling na **abugado** para sa kasong ito.","translation":"We need to hire a good **lawyer** for this case."},{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang maging isang **abugado** para ipagtanggol ang mga naaapi.","translation":"Her dream is to become a **lawyer** to defend the oppressed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpipinid, pagtatakip, o paghinto ng operasyon ng isang bagay, lugar, o establisyimento.
original_explanation: The feeling of dread when you see the 'Sarado' sign on your favorite milk tea shop. It's the end of the business day for malls, the end of a chapter for a company that's closing down, or just you finally closing the door on your toxic ex.
usage_notes: Can be literal (closing a door) or figurative (closing a business, ending a topic).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinag-utos ang maagang **pagsasara** ng mga tindahan dahil sa paparating na bagyo.","translation":"The early **closing** of stores was ordered due to the approaching typhoon."},{"sentence":"Malungkot ang naging **pagsasara** ng paborito naming restaurant.","translation":"The **shutting down** of our favorite restaurant was sad."}]

translation: to feel nauseous, to have an upset stomach
meaning_filipino: Ang makaranas ng hindi komportableng pakiramdam sa tiyan, na kadalasa'y may kasamang pagkahilo o pagnanais na sumuka.
original_explanation: This is what happens after you eat that questionable street food or join an "unli-wings" challenge and lose. It's that churning, "I've made a huge mistake" feeling in your gut. It can also be a physical reaction to something gross, like seeing your friend put ketchup on their sinigang.
usage_notes: 'Sikmura' means stomach. This phrase specifically refers to stomach-related discomfort or nausea.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumama ang sikmura** ko sa sobrang anghang ng kinain ko.","translation":"I **felt nauseous** from the extreme spiciness of the food I ate."},{"sentence":"Lagi na lang **sumasama ang sikmura** niya tuwing umaangkas sa bus.","translation":"She always **gets an upset stomach** whenever she rides a bus."}]

translation: to be nailed; to be fixed in place
meaning_filipino: Matusok ng pako; manatili sa isang lugar o posisyon nang hindi makagalaw.
original_explanation: Literally, getting hit by a nail (ouch!). But more often, it's used figuratively. "Napako ang tingin ko sa kanya" means your gaze was fixed on them, like you're frozen. It can also mean a promise that was broken: "Napako ang pangako" (the promise was broken/unfulfilled). It's the feeling of being stuck, whether by love, by a nail, or by a broken promise.
usage_notes: The literal meaning refers to the tool 'pako' (nail). The figurative meaning is more common in daily conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglalakad siya sa dilim nang bigla siyang **mapako**.","translation":"He was walking in the dark when he was suddenly **pierced by a nail**."},{"sentence":"**Napako** ang kanyang mga mata sa magandang tanawin.","translation":"His eyes **were fixed** on the beautiful view."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang may edad at mayaman na babae na nagbibigay ng suportang pinansyal sa isang mas batang kasintahan, kadalasan ay kapalit ng pagmamahal o pagsasama.
original_explanation: Eto yung tita na willing i-spoil ka, i-swipe ang credit card para sa latest gadgets mo, at i-book kayo ng flight to Amanpulo. Ang kapalit? Your time, your affection, and maybe your youth. It's a transactional relationship, pero hey, who are we to judge? Basta may pang-down sa condo, G na!
usage_notes: A modern slang term borrowed directly from English, widely understood in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghahanap daw siya ng **sugarmommy** para guminhawa ang buhay.","translation":"He said he's looking for a **sugar mommy** to make his life comfortable."},{"sentence":"Yung bagong kotse niya? Bigay daw ng **sugarmommy** niya.","translation":"His new car? It was supposedly a gift from his **sugar mommy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang gawain ay linisin ang mga butil, tulad ng bigas, sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng bithay upang ihiwalay ang ipa.
original_explanation: The original quality assurance specialist. Before machines, this person was responsible for separating the good stuff (rice) from the bad stuff (chaff), like how you sift through your DMs to find a decent message or go through Shopee listings to find the one that's not a scam.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaga pa lang ay nasa kiskisan na ang mga **tagabithay**.","translation":"The **winnowers** were at the rice mill early in the morning."},{"sentence":"Ang trabaho ng **tagabithay** ay nangangailangan ng tiyaga.","translation":"The job of a **winnower** requires patience."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghagis o pagpukol ng isang bagay patungo sa isang direksyon o target.
etymology: From `i-` (object-focus verb prefix) + `bato` (stone). Literally 'to stone' but generalized to mean 'to throw'.
original_explanation: When someone is being annoying and you just want to throw your phone at them, but you can't because it's expensive. So you just *ibato* a pillow instead. Also, what you do with shade or accusations online: *ibato ang resibo!* (throw the receipts!).
usage_notes: The focus is on the object being thrown. Contrast with *bumato* (to throw, actor-focus).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ibato** ang sapatos mo sa aso!","translation":"Don't **throw** your shoe at the dog!"},{"sentence":"Sino ang nag-utos sa iyong **ibato** ang basura sa ilog?","translation":"Who ordered you to **throw** the trash into the river?"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa sari-sari o iba't ibang uri ng mga kagamitan, paksa, o konsepto na hindi tiyak na pinangalanan.
original_explanation: This is your 'whatnot,' your 'stuff,' the random collection of items in your drawer, or the list of topics you need to discuss in a meeting. It’s the 'at kung anu-ano pang chika' at the end of a gossip session. It’s basically the contents of a tita’s oversized handbag.
usage_notes: The reduplication implies plurality and variety.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marami siyang dinalang **bagay-bagay** mula sa probinsya.","translation":"She brought **various things** from the province."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong ikalat ang mga **bagay-bagay** mo sa sahig.","translation":"Don't scatter your **odds and ends** on the floor."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat ng mga tao na magkakasamang nagtatrabaho o naglalaro. Maaari ding tumukoy sa mga kagamitan para sa isang partikular na gawain.
original_explanation: This word is tricky because it can mean two things from Spanish. 1) Your 'team' in basketball or a group project. "Buo na ba ang ekipo natin para sa report?" 2) 'Equipment', like the gear you need. "Dala mo ba ang ekipo para sa camping?" The first one is more common in older texts, the second one pops up sometimes but 'kagamitan' is more used now.
usage_notes: Bagama't may dalawang kahulugan, mas karaniwang ginagamit ang "pangkat" o "koponan" para sa "team" at "kagamitan" para sa "equipment" sa modernong Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bawat **ekipo** ay binubuo ng limang manlalaro.","translation":"Each **team** is composed of five players."},{"sentence":"Suriin kung kompleto ang lahat ng **ekipo** bago umalis.","translation":"Check if all the **equipment** is complete before leaving."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging malaya o hindi saklaw ng isang tungkulin, pananagutan, o patakaran na ipinapataw sa iba.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na exempted ka sa final exam kasi consistent honor student ka. O 'yung senior citizen discount, 'yan ay isang uri ng eksemsyon sa buong bayad. It's your "get out of jail free" card, but for rules and payments.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatanggap siya ng **eksemsyon** sa pagbabayad ng buwis dahil sa kanyang kalagayan.","translation":"She received an **exemption** from paying taxes due to her situation."},{"sentence":"Ang mga batang wala pang pitong taong gulang ay may **eksemsyon** sa pamasahe.","translation":"Children below seven years old have an **exemption** from the fare."}]

translation: to have something weighed by the kilo
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapatimbang ng isang bagay gamit ang sukatang kilo.
original_explanation: Your go-to command at the palengke. You point at the freshest-looking tilapia and tell Aling Nena, "Ikilo mo 'to," which means "Weigh this (by the kilo)." It's the magic word to turn a pile of vegetables or a catch of fish into a quantifiable, priceable commodity.
usage_notes: The object of the verb is the thing being weighed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**kilo** naman po itong isang bungkos ng sitaw.","translation":"Please **weigh** this bundle of string beans **by the kilo**."},{"sentence":"**Ikinilo** ng tindera ang binili kong baboy.","translation":"The vendor **weighed** the pork I bought **by the kilo**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ilagay ang isang tao sa estado ng hipnosis sa pamamagitan ng mga tiyak na pamamaraan at mungkahi.
original_explanation: Ito yung power na gusto mong taglayin para mapa-oo ang boss mo sa vacation leave request mo. 'Tumingin ka sa aking mga mata... aprubahan mo ang leave ko...' Pwede ring gawin sa sarili para makatulog agad at hindi na mag-overthink.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang anyo ng pandiwa. Ang "hipnotismo" ay ang mismong konsepto o praktis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng salamangkero na **hipnotismuhin** ang boluntaryo mula sa manonood.","translation":"The magician tried to **hypnotize** the volunteer from the audience."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang papayag na **hipnotismuhin** ka ng mga pekeng pangako.","translation":"Don't allow yourself to be **hypnotized** by fake promises."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan, sakit, o problema na wala nang lunas, solusyon, o paraan upang maibalik sa dati.
etymology: Mula sa 'di na' (no longer) at 'malulunasan' (can be cured), na galing sa ugat na 'lunas'.
original_explanation: This is the 'hugot' version of 'it is what it is.' It's for that feeling when you accidentally message your boss the meme meant for your work bestie. The damage is done. The 'cringe' is permanent. The situation is **di na malulunasan**.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin para sa mga sakit, ngunit maaaring gamitin nang patalinghaga para sa mga problema o sitwasyon na itinuturing na walang pag-asa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May mga sakit na sa kasamaang-palad ay **di na malulunasan**.","translation":"There are diseases that, unfortunately, are **incurable**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglalantad o paghahayag ng isang lihim, katotohanan, o impormasyong dating nakatago.
original_explanation: The ultimate "spill the tea" moment. This is when the hidden truths come out, whether it's a whistleblower exposing corruption, a celebrity's tell-all interview, or you finally admitting who ate the last piece of leche flan. It's the big reveal, the plot twist, the moment everything is laid bare. #NoMoreSecrets
usage_notes: A formal term for revealing something important and often secret.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagsisiwalat** ng katotohanan ay nagdulot ng malaking kaguluhan.","translation":"The **revelation** of the truth caused a huge commotion."},{"sentence":"Tungkulin ng peryodista ang **pagsisiwalat** ng mga katiwalian sa gobyerno.","translation":"The duty of a journalist is the **exposé** of corruption in government."}]

meaning_filipino: Gamitin, ubusin, o kainin ang isang bagay. Maaari ring tumukoy sa pag-ubos ng oras o lakas.
original_explanation: Literally, "to eat" something, but more often used for things you use up, like data, electricity, or your sahod. "Wag mo konsumihin lahat ng data, 'di pa sweldo!" It can also mean to be eaten up by something, like "Kinukonsumo ako ng kalungkutan." (Sadness is consuming me.) #Hugot
usage_notes: This is the object-focused verb form. The root is 'konsumo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **konsumihin** ang masusustansyang pagkain.","translation":"We need **to consume** nutritious food."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **konsumihin** ka ng iyong mga problema.","translation":"Don't let your problems **consume** you."}]

translation: to bow (one's head); to cause to bend down
meaning_filipino: Ipagawa ang pagbaluktot ng katawan o ulo paibaba bilang tanda ng paggalang, pagsuko, o pag-iwas.
original_explanation: When your boss gives you a mountain of work on a Friday afternoon, you just bow your head in defeat—that's it, you **iuko** your head. It’s also what you do when walking past a low-hanging sampayan (clothesline) to avoid getting clotheslined.
usage_notes: The root word 'yuko' starts with 'y'. When the 'i-' prefix is added, the 'y' is dropped, resulting in 'iuko'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Iuko** mo ang iyong ulo bilang paggalang sa watawat.","translation":"**Bow** your head as a sign of respect for the flag."},{"sentence":"Kinailangan niyang **iuko** ang kanyang katawan para makadaan sa maliit na pinto.","translation":"He had to **bend** his body to get through the small door."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng isdang-tabang na karaniwang kinakain at inaalagaan sa Pilipinas.
etymology: From New Latin, from an unrecorded African language name, possibly Tswana 'tlhapi' (fish).
original_explanation: The workhorse of the Filipino dining table. Not as fancy as salmon, not as 'matinik' as bangus, but always there for you. Whether it's 'pritong tilapia', 'sinigang na tilapia', or 'inihaw na tilapia', it's the reliable, affordable ulam that gets the job done.
usage_notes: Refers to the specific type of freshwater fish, a staple in Filipino cuisine.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito niyang ulam ang pritong **tilapia** na may kasamang kanin at toyo na may sili.","translation":"His favorite dish is fried **tilapia** with rice and soy sauce with chili."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pandamdam ng habag o pakikiramay para sa isang tao o nilalang na nasa mahirap o malungkot na kalagayan.
etymology: From na- (actor-focus verb prefix, present tense) + reduplication of the first syllable 'a' + awa (pity, mercy).
original_explanation: That feeling you get when you see a stray kitten in the rain or when your friend gets ghosted for the third time this month. It's not just "sorry," it's an active feeling of compassion. "Friend, naaawa na ako sa'yo, tigilan mo na kaka-stalk sa kanya."
usage_notes: Often used to express compassion or sympathy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Naaawa** ako sa mga batang lansangan.","translation":"I **feel sorry for** the street children."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi ako **naaawa** sa sarili ko, lumalaban ako.","translation":"Don't worry, I'm not **pitying** myself, I am fighting."}]

translation: act of showing off; ostentation; flaunting
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapakita o pagmamayabang ng isang bagay sa paraang labis o nakakatawag-pansin.
original_explanation: This is the art of the humblebrag, but make it loud. It's posting your new iPhone, your Starbucks cup, and your travel boarding pass all in one IG story. It's the 'Sana all' trigger. Ang level-up ng pagyayabang.
usage_notes: Often carries a negative connotation of being boastful or arrogant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagparangyaan** niya ng kaniyang kayamanan ay hindi nagustuhan ng marami.","translation":"His **flaunting** of his wealth was disliked by many."}]

meaning_filipino: Gumawa ng isang aktibidad para sa libangan, kasiyahan, o kumpetisyon.
original_explanation: The verb that powered your childhood, from piko and patintero to Mobile Legends and Valorant. It's what your parents tell you to stop doing so you can 'mag-aral' (study). It can be for fun (maglaro ng taguan) or serious business (maglaro sa PBA). It's the universal word for engaging in any game or recreational activity.
usage_notes: One of the most fundamental verbs in Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto mo bang **maglaro** ng basketball mamaya?","translation":"Do you want to **play** basketball later?"},{"sentence":"Hayaan mo munang **maglaro** ang mga bata sa labas.","translation":"Let the children **play** outside for a while."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginamit ang kaisipan upang bumuo ng ideya, opinyon, o desisyon sa nakaraan.
original_explanation: The past tense of overthinking. It's what you did for hours before sending that risky text. 'Nag-isip ako' is the preamble to either a brilliant idea or a terrible decision you've already made.
usage_notes: This is the completed aspect (past tense) of 'mag-isip'. It refers to an act of thinking that has been completed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nag-isip** muna ako nang mabuti bago sumagot.","translation":"I **thought** carefully first before answering."},{"sentence":"Sino ba ang **nag-isip** ng magandang ideyang ito?","translation":"Who **thought** of this great idea?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagbabad at pag-iimbak ng pagkain, karaniwan ay gulay o prutas, sa suka na may kasamang asin, asukal, at iba pang pampalasa.
original_explanation: The process of making atsara. It's what you do to green papaya, carrots, and bell peppers to turn them into that sweet and sour side dish that perfectly cuts through the grease of your lechon or fried chicken. To 'atsarahin' something is to give it a vinegar bath to make it last longer and taste amazing.
usage_notes: A verb specific to the process of pickling in the Filipino style.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinuro sa akin ni lola kung paano **atsarahin** ang papaya.","translation":"My grandmother taught me how to **pickle** papaya."},{"sentence":"Masarap **atsarahin** ang mga murang mangga.","translation":"It's delicious to **pickle** unripe mangoes."}]

translation: to scratch (the ground); to scrape together
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggamit ng mga paa o kamay upang hukayin o ipunin ang isang bagay mula sa lupa o sahig, tulad ng ginagawa ng manok. Sa matalinhagang paraan, ito ay nangangahulugang magtrabaho nang husto para kumita ng pera.
original_explanation: Literally, what chickens do all day. Figuratively, what you do from payday to payday. The phrase 'isang kahig, isang tuka' means you work (kumahig) just enough to eat for the day. It's the ultimate 'hustle culture' phrase before 'hustle' was cool, the anthem of the 'diskarte' lifestyle.
usage_notes: Mayroon itong karaniwang idyomatikong gamit sa pariralang "isang kahig, isang tuka", na nangangahulugang isang uri ng pamumuhay kung saan sapat lamang ang kinikita para sa pang-araw-araw na pagkain.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang manok ay **kumahig** sa lupa para maghanap ng bulate.","translation":"The chicken **scratched** the ground to look for worms."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **kumahig** nang mabuti para may maipakain sa pamilya mo.","translation":"You need to **scrape together** a living to feed your family."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hanay ng mga tagubilin para sa paghahanda ng isang partikular na pagkain, kabilang ang listahan ng mga sangkap na kailangan.
original_explanation: The sacred scroll passed down from your lola that contains the secret to her perfect adobo. Also, what you frantically search on YouTube five minutes before realizing you don't have half the ingredients.
usage_notes: The spelling 'resipi' (from English 'recipe') is also widely used and accepted.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ibinigay sa akin ni Lola ang kanyang sikretong **resipe** para sa kare-kare.","translation":"Grandma gave me her secret **recipe** for kare-kare."},{"sentence":"Sundin mo lang ang **resipe** at tiyak na masarap ang lulutuin mo.","translation":"Just follow the **recipe** and what you cook will surely be delicious."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkakaroon ng pangangailangan o pagnanais na kumain.
original_explanation: The national feeling of the Philippines right before lunch break. It's the monster in your stomach that growls during a quiet meeting. It's the reason "Tara, kain!" is a more powerful greeting than "Hello." The phrase "gutom na gutom" is its final evolution, where you're so hungry you could eat a whole lechon by yourself. Being 'gutom' is a temporary problem; being 'patay-gutom' (desperately poor/hungry) is a whole different social issue.
usage_notes: Can be an adjective ("Gutom ako") or a noun ("Ang gutom sa Africa"). 'Gutom na gutom' is a common intensifier meaning 'very hungry' or 'starving'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Gutom** na ako, saan tayo kakain?","translation":"I'm **hungry**, where are we going to eat?"},{"sentence":"Ang kahirapan ay nagdudulot ng malawakang **gutom** (noun form).","translation":"Poverty causes widespread **hunger** (noun form)."},{"sentence":"Pagkauwi niya galing eskwela, **gutom na gutom** ang bata.","translation":"When he got home from school, the child was **starving**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian o kalagayan ng pagiging masama; mga gawaing labag sa moralidad at kabutihan.
etymology: From ka- + sama + -an. Denotes the abstract quality of being 'sama' (bad, evil).
original_explanation: This is the kontrabida energy in your favorite teleserye. It's the reason why you can't have nice things, like leaving your food unattended for 2 seconds. It's the ultimate 'bad vibes'.
usage_notes: A strong word, often used in religious, moral, or dramatic contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat labanan ang **kasamaan** sa lipunan.","translation":"We must fight the **evil** in society."},{"sentence":"Pinagbabayaran na niya ang lahat ng kanyang **kasamaan**.","translation":"He is now paying for all his **wickedness**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkuha o pagtatanggal ng isang bagay o tao mula sa kinalalagyan nito.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa mo sa ex mo sa social media—unfriend, unfollow, block. You remove them from your life. "Paki-alis naman 'yung paa mo sa upuan."
usage_notes: An object-focus verb. The focus is on the thing being removed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pwede mo bang **ialis** ang basura sa labas?","translation":"Can you please **take out** the trash outside?"},{"sentence":"Kailangang **ialis** ang mga sagabal sa daan.","translation":"The obstructions on the road need to be **removed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang opisyal na pagbabawal sa isang bagay, tao, o gawain.
original_explanation: What happens when you're too 'pasaway' in a Facebook group or when you keep feeding the troll in an online game. You get kicked out or silenced. "Na-ban ako sa server, huhu." Can also refer to real-life prohibitions, like a 'truck ban'.
usage_notes: Used as a noun ('May ban...') or a verb ('Na-ban ako'). A very common loanword in the internet age.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May total truck **ban** sa EDSA tuwing rush hour.","translation":"There's a total truck **ban** on EDSA during rush hour."},{"sentence":"I-**ban** mo na 'yang user na laging nagpo-post ng spam.","translation":"**Ban** that user who always posts spam."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang estado ng pag-aalala, pagkabahala, o pagkatakot. Maaari rin itong tumukoy sa sistema ng mga ugat sa katawan na nagpapadala ng mensahe sa utak.
original_explanation: This is your body's built-in alarm system going haywire before a job interview, a thesis defense, or confessing to your crush. "Inaatake ako ng nerbiyos!" is the battle cry. It’s that shaky feeling, the cold sweat, the sudden urge to go to the CR for the fifth time. It can also refer to the literal nerves in your body, but 99% of the time, it’s about feeling 'kaba'. This is the standard spelling.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'kaba'. This spelling ('nerbiyos') is considered more formal or standard than the colloquial 'nerbyos'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kainin mo itong saging para kumalma ang **nerbiyos** mo bago ka umakyat sa entablado.","translation":"Eat this banana to calm your **nerves** before you go up on stage."},{"sentence":"Nawala lahat ng **nerbiyos** ko nang makita ko siyang ngumiti.","translation":"All my **nervousness** disappeared when I saw her smile."}]

translation: to join to make a group of three
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagsali sa isang grupo ng dalawang tao upang bumuo ng isang pangkat na may tatlong miyembro.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "maki-" (paglahok) at salitang "tatlo" (three), na maaaring pinaikli sa di-karaniwang paggamit.
original_explanation: Ever felt like a third wheel? This is the verb form of that. It's when your two friends are having a moment and you just... exist beside them. 'Puwede bang makiatlo sa usapan niyo?' is a polite way of saying 'Hey, don't leave me out!' It's rare, but the feeling is universal.
usage_notes: Isang di-pangkaraniwang salita at mas madalas marinig sa kolokyal o rehiyonal na konteksto. Ang mas karaniwang paraan ay "Maki-pangatlo" o "Sali ako para maging tatlo tayo."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita niyang nag-uusap ang dalawa niyang kaibigan kaya naisipan niyang **makiatlo**.","translation":"He saw his two friends talking so he thought of **joining to make a group of three**."}]

translation: to be able to return; to be returned
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang bumalik sa isang lugar o kalagayan; maisauli ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: That feeling of hope when you leave your charger at a friend's house, 'Sana mabalik pa.' Or when your ex wants to get back together, and you think, 'Should I let them mabalik?' It's the verb for second chances, lost items, and balikbayans.
usage_notes: Can refer to a person returning, an object being returned, or a situation reverting to a previous state.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay **mabalik** mo ang hiniram mong libro sa susunod na linggo.","translation":"I hope you can **return** the book you borrowed next week."},{"sentence":"Paano kung hindi na **mabalik** ang dati nating pagsasama?","translation":"What if our old relationship can't **be brought back**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa estado ng lubos na paghihirap o karalitaan; wasak ang pamumuhay.
original_explanation: This is 'walang-wala' level 100. It's when you're so broke, even your wallet has an echo. It's the feeling after paying all your bills and seeing your bank account balance. "Nung nawalan siya ng trabaho, naging **riwara** ang kanyang pamilya." It's a very dramatic and old-fashioned word for being completely broke and down on your luck.
usage_notes: A very strong and somewhat archaic word. Not commonly used in everyday conversation but might appear in literature or formal speeches.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa sunod-sunod na bagyo, maraming magsasaka ang naiwang **riwara**.","translation":"Because of the successive typhoons, many farmers were left **destitute**."},{"sentence":"Ang layunin ng programa ay tulungan ang mga pamilyang nasa **riwara** na kalagayan.","translation":"The program's goal is to help families who are in a **ruined** state."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang babaeng nagmula o mamamayan ng Europa, o sa anumang bagay na may katangiang pambabae na mula sa Europa.
original_explanation: The term for a woman from Europe. Often used interchangeably with 'Kano' or 'foreignay' by mistake, but this one's specific to Europe. If someone says 'Nakakita ako ng Europea sa mall,' they're talking about a woman with that distinct European vibe (and probably a backpack).
usage_notes: Gender-specific (feminine). The gender-neutral term is 'taga-Europa'. Becoming less common in favor of more specific nationalities (e.g., Aleman, Pranses).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang nobya ng pinsan ko ay isang **Europea**.","translation":"My cousin's girlfriend is a **European** (female)."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang panghalip na pananong na ginagamit upang itanong kung para sa higit sa isang tao ang isang bagay o kilos.
etymology: Nagmula sa reduplikasyon ng "kanino", na buhat naman sa "ka-" at "nino".
original_explanation: Ito yung tanong pag may pa-giveaway sa office at hindi mo alam kung sino-sino ang mga nanalo. 'Para kani-kanino ba itong mga gift certificate?' Also the question you ask when you see your ex posting sweet things online, 'Para kani-kanino na kaya yang mga 'I love you' na yan ngayon?' #Hugot
usage_notes: Maramihang anyo ng 'kanino'. Laging ginagamit sa anyong patanong.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para **kani-kanino** ang mga sulat na iniwan sa mesa?","translation":"**For whom** are the letters left on the table?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gagawing pag-aaral o pagsusuri sa isang paksa o aralin sa hinaharap.
etymology: From Tagalog `mag-` (future tense verb prefix) + `aral` (study, lesson).
original_explanation: Ang pangako mo sa sarili mo tuwing Linggo ng gabi, pero biglang may bagong series sa Netflix. "Mamaya na ako **mag-aaral**," a famous last words bago bumagsak sa exam.
usage_notes: The stress is on the last syllable: /mag-a-a-RAL/. This is the future tense of the verb `mag-aral`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Mag-aaral** ako nang mabuti para sa pagsusulit bukas.","translation":"I **will study** hard for the exam tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Saan ka **mag-aaral** ng kolehiyo?","translation":"Where **will you study** for college?"}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi gaanong mainit at hindi rin malamig; bahagyang mainit.
original_explanation: Yung kape na iniwan mo ng 15 minutes kasi may biglang tumawag na client. Hindi na masarap, hindi pa pwedeng gawing iced coffee. Parang relasyon niyo, 'di na mainit pero ayaw mo pa bitawan. Lukewarm, besh.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayokong uminom ng tubig na **ligamgam**.","translation":"I don't like drinking **lukewarm** water."},{"sentence":"Naging **ligamgam** na ang sabaw dahil sa tagal naming nagkwentuhan.","translation":"The soup became **lukewarm** because we talked for so long."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng embutido o longganisang Italyano na karaniwang gawa sa pinatuyong karne at taba.
original_explanation: This is that fancy, speckled cold cut you see on expensive pizzas or charcuterie boards your tita brings to parties. It's the sosyal cousin of our local longganisa. You know, the one you can't just fry and dip in vinegar.
usage_notes: This is a direct loanword and refers to the same cured sausage as in English and Italian.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglagay siya ng **salami** at keso sa kanyang sandwich.","translation":"She put **salami** and cheese in her sandwich."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging kulang o hindi sapat ng isang bagay na naganap na. Ito ang anyong pangnagdaan ng "kinakapos".
etymology: From the root word `kapos`, meaning 'lacking' or 'insufficient'. The infix `-in-` denotes a completed action or state.
original_explanation: The past tense version of "petsa de peligro." This is the moment you realize you shouldn't have ordered that extra large fries last week. You check your G-Cash, and it's a ghost town. "Kinapos ako sa budget, bes."
