It can also be used for non-money situations, like when you're telling a story and you run out of breath or when your crush's height just wasn't enough to reach your standards. Ouch.
usage_notes: The past tense of `kinakapos`. Used for money, time, breath, height, etc.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kinapos** ako sa oras kaya hindi ko natapos ang pagsusulit.","translation":"I **ran short** of time, so I wasn't able to finish the exam."},{"sentence":"Maganda sana ang plano nila, ngunit **kinapos** sila sa pondo.","translation":"Their plan was good, but they **were insufficient** in funds."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing alipin ang isang tao o pangkat; sakupin at kontrolin ang kalayaan ng iba.
original_explanation: This is what toxic relationships and exploitative jobs do. They take your freedom, your time, your energy, until you feel like you're just living to serve them. It's the ultimate 'di ka na makahinga' situation, often fueled by 'utang na loob'.
usage_notes: A strong, literary word often used to describe historical oppression or figurative subjugation (e.g., enslaved by debt, fear, or vice).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi natin dapat hayaang **umalipin** sa atin ang teknolohiya.","translation":"We should not let technology **enslave** us."},{"sentence":"Ang layunin ng mga mananakop ay **umalipin** sa mga katutubo.","translation":"The goal of the colonizers was **to enslave** the natives."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging pormal o opisyal ng isang relasyon o anunsyo na idineklara sa social media platform na Facebook.
etymology: Mula sa "Facebook" (isang social media platform) at "official" (salitang Ingles para sa opisyal).
original_explanation: It's not real until it's 'FB official'. This is the modern-day *kasal* for Gen Z and Millennial relationships. If you haven't updated your relationship status from 'Single' to 'In a relationship' and tagged your jowa, are you even really together? It's the digital equivalent of shouting it from the rooftops, but with more potential for chismis from your Titas.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng mga romantikong relasyon, ngunit maaari ring tumukoy sa anumang pormal na anunsyo na ginawa sa Facebook.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailan niyo balak gawing **FB official** 'yang relasyon niyo?","translation":"When do you plan to make your relationship **FB official**?"},{"sentence":"Nag-post na sila ng pictures, pero hindi pa **FB official** kaya 'wag kang assuming.","translation":"They've posted pictures, but it's not **FB official** yet so don't be assuming."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, lalo na isang bata, na legal na kinupkop at pinalaki ng mga hindi niya tunay na magulang.
original_explanation: More than just an adopted child, it's anyone taken under someone's wing. It could be the new guy at work that the boss mentors, or that stray cat your family decided to keep. It's about being chosen and welcomed into a new family or group.
usage_notes: Maaari ring tumukoy sa isang alaga o taong nasa ilalim ng proteksyon ng iba.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahal na mahal nila ang kanilang nag-iisang **ampon**.","translation":"They love their only **adopted child** very much."},{"sentence":"Siya ay itinuturing na **ampon** ng kilalang politiko.","translation":"He is considered a **protégé** of the famous politician."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang yugto sa buhay ng isang lalaki kung saan siya ay nagkakaroon ng mga katangiang pisikal at sekswal ng isang adulto, karaniwang nagsisimula sa pagitan ng edad na 9 at 14.
etymology: From the root word 'binata', meaning 'young man' or 'bachelor'. The prefix 'pag-' and reduplication 'bi-' signifies the process of becoming one.
original_explanation: This is the 'awkward stage' for boys. When your voice starts cracking like a poorly-tuned radio, you get your first pimple, and you suddenly become super conscious of girls. It's the official level-up from 'bata' to 'binata'.
usage_notes: The female equivalent is 'pagdadalaga'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kasama sa **pagbibinata** ang pagbabago ng boses at pagtubo ng bigote.","translation":"Part of **puberty** includes the changing of the voice and the growing of a mustache."}]

meaning_filipino: Labis na pagmamalaki o pagpapahalaga sa sariling anyo, kakayahan, o ari-arian; kahambugan.
original_explanation: That feeling when you post 50 selfies and can't choose which one to make your profile pic because you look good in all of them. That's **banidad**. It's the "I woke up like this (after a 2-hour skincare routine and finding the perfect lighting)" energy. A little self-love is great, but too much **banidad** can make you look mayabang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puro salamin ang kanyang bahay dahil sa labis na **banidad**.","translation":"His house is full of mirrors because of excessive **vanity**."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-aayos sa sarili ay hindi laging tanda ng **banidad**; minsan, ito ay pag-aalaga lamang.","translation":"Fixing oneself up is not always a sign of **vanity**; sometimes, it's just self-care."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pagngiti kung saan nakikita ang mga ngipin, na maaaring magpahiwatig ng panunuya, katuwaan, o kung minsan ay kasamaan.
original_explanation: The smile of a kontrabida in a teleserye right after they've done something evil. It's that 'I know something you don't know' look. Not a pure smile, more like a smile with a hidden agenda or a punchline.
usage_notes: Often has a negative or mischievous connotation compared to 'ngiti' (smile).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May halong pang-aasar ang **ngisi** niya habang nakatingin sa akin.","translation":"There was a hint of teasing in his **smirk** while looking at me."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagnanakaw o kumukuha ng yaman ng iba sa malawakang paraan, lalo na kung may kaugnayan sa kapangyarihan o posisyon.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung level-up version ng magnanakaw. Hindi lang wallet mo ang target, kundi 'yung kaban ng bayan. Sila 'yung mga character sa balita na may 'plunder case.' Think pirates, but instead of a ship, they have a government office.
usage_notes: Isang mabigat na salita na halos eksklusibong ginagamit sa konteksto ng malawakang pagnanakaw, korapsyon, at mga iskandalong pampulitika.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nilitis ang politiko dahil sa pagiging isang **mandarambong**.","translation":"The politician was tried for being a **plunderer**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga **mandarambong** ay salot sa lipunan.","translation":"**Plunderers** are a plague on society."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng manipis at nababaluktot na yantok na ginagamit sa paggawa ng mga basket at muwebles.
original_explanation: Before there was plastic twine and zip ties, there was bukawe. It's that skinny but surprisingly strong rattan your lolo used to tie things up or that's woven into those classic, slightly scratchy chairs at your tita's house. The OG of natural binders.
usage_notes: Often used in basket weaving and making lightweight furniture.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gawa sa **bukawe** ang hawakan ng basket na ito.","translation":"The handle of this basket is made of **bukawe**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng matibay na **bukawe** para itali ang mga kawayan.","translation":"A strong **bukawe** is needed to tie the bamboos together."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lumang katawagan para sa isang uri ng araro o kasangkapang ginagamit sa paggawa ng tudling sa lupa.
original_explanation: Think of 'tudlingan' as the OG plow, the vintage farm equipment before John Deere became a thing. It's the tool that makes the 'tudling' (furrow). You won't hear this in everyday convo unless you're talking to a history buff or a time-traveling magsasaka.
usage_notes: This word is largely obsolete and found mainly in older texts or specialized dictionaries. The common word is 'araro'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa museo, nakita namin ang isang lumang **tudlingan** na gawa sa kahoy.","translation":"In the museum, we saw an old **plow** made of wood."},{"sentence":"Mahirap nang makahanap ng gumagawa ng tradisyonal na **tudlingan**.","translation":"It's hard to find anyone who makes a traditional **plow** anymore."}]

translation: to abuse; to take advantage of
meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng kapangyarihan o posisyon sa paraang hindi tama, mapagsamantala, o sobra sa itinakda.
original_explanation: Think of that boss who makes you do their personal errands, or a politician using public funds for a private party. That's 'magmalabis'. It's about crossing the line from using power to abusing it. It's the ultimate "with great power comes great irresponsibility" move.
usage_notes: Carries a strong negative connotation of injustice and exploitation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binalaan ang mga opisyal na huwag **magmalabis** sa kanilang kapangyarihan.","translation":"The officials were warned not to **abuse** their power."},{"sentence":"Hindi tama na **magmalabis** sa kabaitan ng isang tao.","translation":"It's not right to **take advantage** of a person's kindness."}]

translation: to be cloyed; to get tired of something
meaning_filipino: Magsawa o maramdaman ang labis na pagkainip o pagkasuya sa isang bagay, lalo na sa pagkain, dahil sa paulit-ulit na pagkonsumo o karanasan.
etymology: From 'umay', the state of being cloyed or satiated to the point of aversion.
original_explanation: That feeling when you've eaten your 5th piece of lechon and your body just says "STOP." It's the point of diminishing returns for pleasure. Pwede rin sa tao. "Nakakaumay na 'yang mga drama mo, bes." It's when too much of a good thing becomes a bad thing, like hearing the same song on repeat for a whole day on your commute.
usage_notes: Primarily used for food, but widely used metaphorically for anything one becomes tired of due to overexposure, such as a song, a topic, or a person's behavior.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo ubusin lahat 'yan, baka **maumay** ka.","translation":"Don't finish all of that, you might **get tired of the taste**."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula na akong **maumay** sa paulit-ulit niyang dahilan.","translation":"I've started to **get tired of** his repetitive excuses."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang matinding pagsiklab o pag-aalab ng damdamin, tulad ng galit, pag-ibig, o sigasig.
original_explanation: This is your feelings on overdrive. It's the 'all-in' emotional state. Think of the intense feels when your favorite K-pop group has a comeback, the burning passion to finish a thesis the night before the deadline, or the flare-up of 'kilig' when your crush replies to your story. It’s emotion level: 1000%.
usage_notes: Often used in literature to describe intense emotions, both positive (passion) and negative (rage).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nadama ko ang **pagdurubdob** ng galit sa kanyang mga salita.","translation":"I felt the **flare-up** of anger in his words."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagdurubdob** ng kanyang pag-ibig sa sining ay kitang-kita sa kanyang mga obra.","translation":"The **fervor** of his love for art is evident in his masterpieces."}]

translation: to block, to parry, to intercept
meaning_filipino: Salagin, harangin, o pigilan ang isang bagay na paparating, tulad ng isang suntok, salita, o atake.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'sangga' at hulaping '-hin'.
original_explanation: The act of blocking something directly. Like when your mom throws a 'tsinelas' and you use your sibling as a human shield. Or when someone throws shade and you have the perfect comeback. 'Sinubukan niya akong insultuhin, pero nasangga ko agad.'
usage_notes: Nagpapahiwatig ng isang direkta at nagtatanggol na aksyon laban sa isang paparating na bagay o atake (pisikal man o berbal).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **sanggahin** ang mga suntok ng kalaban.","translation":"You need to **block** the opponent's punches."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **sanggahin** ang lahat ng kritisismo ng tao.","translation":"It's hard to **parry** all of people's criticisms."}]

meaning_filipino: Tubig na binasbasan ng isang pari at ginagamit sa mga seremonyang panrelihiyon, tulad ng binyag at pagbabasbas.
etymology: Mula sa pariralang Espanyol na "agua bendita".
original_explanation: That blessed H2O you get from church. Used for everything from blessing a new car (para iwas-disgrasya) to splashing on someone you suspect is possessed by an evil spirit. It's the original spiritual cleanser bago pa nauso ang sage.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa konteksto ng Simbahang Katoliko. Ang mga bahagi nitong "agwa" (tubig) at "bendita" (binasbasan) ay hindi karaniwang ginagamit nang hiwalay sa ganitong anyo sa Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagwisik ng **agwa-bendita** ang pari sa mga tao.","translation":"The priest sprinkled **holy water** on the people."},{"sentence":"Kumuha siya ng **agwa-bendita** mula sa simbahan para sa kanyang altar.","translation":"She got **holy water** from the church for her altar."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagyupi o paggusot ng isang bagay, tulad ng papel, gamit ang mga kamay sa paraang marahas o mabilis.
original_explanation: Yung ginagawa mo sa test paper mo pagkatapos mong makita ang score mo. You **lapirot** it into a ball of shame and regret, tapos shoot mo sa basurahan, pero sablay pa rin. 3-points for effort, 0 for the exam.
usage_notes: Often used for paper, thin foil, or fabric. Implies a forceful, almost angry crumpling action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang inis, ni-**lapirot** niya ang sulat na galing sa kanyang manliligaw.","translation":"Out of extreme annoyance, she **crumpled** the letter from her suitor."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **lapirotin** ang resibo, baka kailanganin pa natin.","translation":"Don't **crumple** the receipt, we might still need it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng batong nabuo mula sa mabilis na paglamig ng lava ng bulkan; ito ay parang salamin, matalas, at karaniwang kulay itim.
original_explanation: The 'Goth' kid of gemstones. It's that sleek, black, volcanic glass that looks super cool and was historically used to make sharp tools and weapons. In video games, it's usually the high-tier material you need to craft that epic sword.
usage_notes: Primarily used in geological, archaeological, or fantasy contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakahanap ang mga arkeologo ng mga sinaunang talim na gawa sa **obsidiyana**.","translation":"The archaeologists found ancient blades made of **obsidian**."},{"sentence":"Makintab at kulay itim ang pulseras niyang gawa sa **obsidiyana**.","translation":"Her bracelet made of **obsidian** is shiny and black."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sukat ng dami ng isang bagay, lalo na ng mga butil o likido, gamit ang isang lalagyan bilang panukat; ang proseso ng pagsukat nito.
original_explanation: The palengke lifehack for measuring stuff without a weighing scale. 'Isang takal ng bigas' is usually one cup. It's how your mom tells you to cook rice. It's also used for 'taho', 'vinegar', and other things sold 'by the cup'. It's the Filipino metric system before the actual metric system.
usage_notes: Refers to measuring by volume, not weight. A "panakal" is the tool used for measuring (e.g., a cup, a ganta).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dalawang **takal** ng bigas ang isaing mo.","translation":"Cook two **measures** (cups) of rice."},{"sentence":"Pabili po ng isang **takal** ng suka.","translation":"I'd like to buy one **measure** (cup) of vinegar."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang manipis na bahagi ng katawan ng isda at iba pang hayop sa tubig na ginagamit sa paglangoy, pagbalanse, at pag-gabay sa direksyon.
original_explanation: That pointy thing on a fish's back that pops out of the water in horror movies. It's what helps Nemo swim and what you try to avoid when cleaning a fish for sinigang. 'Kita mo ba yung palikpik ng pating? Tara na, uwi na tayo!'
usage_notes: Can refer to dorsal, pectoral, caudal, or any fin on an aquatic animal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **palikpik** ng pating ay madalas ginagawang sangkap sa mamahaling sabaw.","translation":"A shark's **fin** is often used as an ingredient in expensive soup."},{"sentence":"Napakaganda ng kulay ng **palikpik** ng isdang iyon.","translation":"The color of that fish's **fin** is so beautiful."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagdudulot ng pagpigil o paghinto sa isang kilos, damdamin, o pag-usad. Maaari ding tumukoy sa isang bagay na lubhang kagila-gilalas na tila humihinto ang paghinga.
etymology: From naka- (causative prefix) + reduplication of first syllable of root pi- + pigil (control, restrain).
original_explanation: 'Yung tawa mo na gusto mong ilabas sa meeting pero 'di pwede, so you're just shaking. That's `nakapipigil`. Also used for things that are so amazing they take your breath away, like "Nakapipigil-hiningang ganda!" (Breathtakingly beautiful!).
usage_notes: Can mean either causing restraint or being so intense it causes one to hold their breath (e.g., nakapipigil-hininga).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakapipigil** ng galit ang kaniyang mahinahong pagsasalita.","translation":"His calm way of speaking is **restraining** one's anger."},{"sentence":"Ang tanawin mula sa tuktok ng bundok ay **nakapipigil**-hininga.","translation":"The view from the mountain top is **breathtaking**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbibigay ng isang bagay at pagtanggap ng iba bilang kapalit; ang mutual na pagpapalitan.
etymology: From pakiki- (reciprocal action) + pag- (action noun) + palitan (to exchange with one another). Root is palit (change, replace).
original_explanation: This isn't just about trading things, but also words, ideas, or even insults (like in a rap battle). It's the "exchange gift" during Christmas parties. It's the back-and-forth messaging with your crush. It's the "palitan ng maanghang na salita" (exchange of harsh words) in a heated argument. Basically, a two-way street of giving and receiving.
usage_notes: Can refer to the exchange of goods, words, ideas, or even blows. The context specifies what is being exchanged.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon sila ng **pakikipagpalitan** ng kuro-kuro sa pulong.","translation":"They had an **exchange** of opinions during the meeting."},{"sentence":"Ang **pakikipagpalitan** ng regalo ay tradisyon tuwing Pasko.","translation":"The **act of exchanging** gifts is a tradition during Christmas."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang istrukturang tulay na nagdadala ng isang kalsada o riles sa ibabaw ng isa pang kalsada, riles, o ibang hadlang upang maiwasan ang salubungan ng trapiko.
original_explanation: That giant concrete snake that's supposed to solve traffic but sometimes feels like it just moves the traffic jam 500 meters forward. It's your best friend during a carmaggedon-free day and your worst enemy when you're stuck on top of it with an empty gas tank. Also a great place to see the city lights, if you're into that 'romanticizing pollution' aesthetic.
usage_notes: A common term in Philippine urban areas. Used interchangeably with 'overpass'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumaan tayo sa **flyover** para iwasan ang traffic sa ilalim.","translation":"Let's take the **flyover** to avoid the traffic below."},{"sentence":"May bagong ginagawang **flyover** sa EDSA para daw mabawasan ang siksikan.","translation":"A new **flyover** is being built on EDSA to supposedly ease congestion."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahinang liwanag o kislap, lalo na ang nakikita sa dilim; sinag na bahagya lamang nakikita.
original_explanation: That faint glow from your phone screen under the blanket at 3 AM when you should be sleeping. It's not a full-on flashlight beam, just a weak, almost magical light, like the 'seen' notification on messenger—it's there, but you wish it wasn't. Also, tunog-engkanto.
usage_notes: A poetic or literary term. Not commonly used in daily conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tanging ang **alinagnag** ng buwan ang nagsilbing ilaw sa kanilang daan.","translation":"Only the **glimmer** of the moon served as the light on their path."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na kainan na karaniwang naghahain ng mga lutong-bahay na pagkain sa abot-kayang halaga.
etymology: Pinaniniwalaang nagmula sa "karihan" (isang lugar na nagbebenta ng kari), na kalaunan ay naghain na ng iba't ibang uri ng pagkain. Ang "karinderia" ay isang alternatibong baybay.
original_explanation: The Philippines' unofficial national restaurant. Your go-to place for a budget-friendly, delicious meal that tastes like your lola cooked it. Dito mo makikita ang magic ng "turo-turo" system. Perfect for when sweldo is a week away but you're craving sisig, adobo, and sinigang all at once. Life-saver ng mga estudyante at office workers.
usage_notes: "Karinderia" is an alternative, less common spelling. The term "turo-turo" (point-point) is often used to describe the way customers order by pointing at the displayed dishes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa **karinderya** na lang tayo kumain ng tanghalian para makatipid.","translation":"Let's just eat lunch at the **eatery** to save money."},{"sentence":"Puno ng tao ang **karinderya** ni Aling Tess tuwing tanghali.","translation":"Aling Tess's **eatery** is full of people at noon."}]

translation: to indulge oneself; to eat one's fill
meaning_filipino: Gawin o kainin ang isang bagay nang walang pagpipigil hanggang sa marating ang punto ng lubos na kasiyahan o pagkasuya.
etymology: From the prefix `magpaka-` (to deliberately cause oneself to be) and the root `sawa` (satiated, fed up).
original_explanation: The official command at any Pinoy buffet or handaan. "Sige, magpakasawa ka!" means "Eat until you can't breathe and have no regrets." It's the philosophy of unli-rice, unli-wings, and unli-samgyup. Live without limits, at least until the food runs out.
usage_notes: Commonly used in the context of food and eating, but can be applied to any activity one indulges in.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumunta kami sa buffet para **magpakasawa** sa pagkain.","translation":"We went to the buffet to **eat our fill**."},{"sentence":"Habang bakasyon, **magpakasawa** ka sa pagtulog at pamamahinga.","translation":"While on vacation, **indulge yourself** in sleeping and resting."}]

meaning_filipino: Nadagdagan ang timbang o bigat; naging mas mahirap o mas malubha ang isang sitwasyon o pakiramdam.
original_explanation: The feeling after a Christmas Noche Buena feast. Or the atmosphere in a Zoom call when the boss asks, 'Any volunteers for weekend work?' That sudden, deafening silence? That's the mood that just bumigat.
usage_notes: Past tense of 'bigat' (weight/heaviness). Can refer to literal weight or metaphorical burden/seriousness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumigat** ang daloy ng trapiko pagkatapos ng aksidente.","translation":"The flow of traffic **became heavy** after the accident."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam ko, **bumigat** ang aking katawan pagkatapos kumain.","translation":"I feel like my body **got heavier** after eating."}]

meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng mga sangkap o pampalasa ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay pagkain o inumin, upang ito ay magkalasa.
etymology: Nagmula sa salitang-ugat na 'timpla' at hulaping '-han'.
original_explanation: The action you do when the soup is bland. 'Timplahan mo pa,' your mom says, telling you to add more patis or magic sarap. It's the process of turning something boring into something delicious. It's a command, a request, a culinary call to action.
usage_notes: Isang pandiwa na madalas gamitin sa anyong pautos ('timplahan mo'). Ang obheto ng pandiwa ay ang bagay na nilalagyan ng lasa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyong **timplahan** mo ng asin at paminta ang sabaw.","translation":"Please **add seasoning** of salt and pepper to the soup."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **timplahan** nang tama ang adobo.","translation":"Don't forget **to add flavor to** the adobo correctly."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar, karaniwan sa ospital o punerarya, kung saan pansamantalang inilalagak ang mga bangkay upang kilalanin o bago ilibing.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na "morgue", na inangkop sa pagbaybay sa Filipino.
original_explanation: The coldest room in the hospital, and the setting for 90% of Filipino horror movies. It's the place you hope to never visit, either as a visitor or... a resident. In Pinoy films, this is where the ghost's body is, and the hero has to go there at midnight for some reason.
usage_notes: The English spelling "morgue" is also commonly used in writing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala ang bangkay sa **morge** para sa awtopsiya.","translation":"The body was brought to the **morgue** for an autopsy."},{"sentence":"Nakakatakot daw pumasok sa **morge** ng ospital kapag gabi.","translation":"They say it's scary to enter the hospital **morgue** at night."}]

meaning_filipino: (Pang-uri) Isang tao o bagay na pinahahalagahan at iniibig nang labis. (Pandiwa) Ang kasalukuyang kilos ng pagmamahal sa isang tao.
etymology: From Tagalog root "mahal" (love, expensive) with the "-in-" infix and "ma-" prefix, indicating an object of an action or a state.
original_explanation: The subject of every OPM love song. Your "Babe," "Love," "Pangga," or kung ano man ang call sign ninyo. It's the person you're currently loving, the one you text "kumain ka na ba?" three times a day. As a verb, it's the act of loving itself—the "in a relationship" status of your heart.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun (e.g., "aking minamahal" - my beloved) or as the present tense of the verb "mahalin" (to love someone).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ikaw ang aking nag-iisang **minamahal**.","translation":"You are my one and only **beloved**."},{"sentence":"**Minamahal** ko siya nang buong puso.","translation":"I am **loving** him/her with all my heart."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang akronim na karaniwang nangangahulugang "sana all," isang ekspresyon ng pagnanais na maranasan din ang magandang kapalaran ng iba. Maaari rin itong mangahulugang "seen back" sa konteksto ng social media.
etymology: Acronym for various phrases, most notably "Sana all."
original_explanation: The Swiss Army knife of Pinoy chat acronyms. Most famously, it means "Sana All," the national anthem of the inggit-pero-happy-for-you. See a friend's travel pic? "SB." Someone's in a happy relationship? "SB." It can also mean "Seen Back" (when you want someone to acknowledge they've seen your message) or even "Starbucks" ("Tara, sb?"). Context is key, beshie.
usage_notes: Heavily used in texting, social media comments, and informal online conversations. The meaning is highly dependent on context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng bago mong phone, **sb**! (sana all)","translation":"Your new phone is so nice, **if only everyone were so lucky**! (sana all)"},{"sentence":"Pa-**sb** naman ng message ko para alam kong nabasa mo. (seen back)","translation":"Please **\"seen back\"** my message so I know you've read it."}]

translation: a person of no consequence; a nobody
meaning_filipino: Isang tao na itinuturing na walang halaga, silbi, o importansya sa lipunan o sa isang partikular na sitwasyon.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'seen-zoned' person. The one who feels invisible in a group project, the one whose opinions are always ignored. It's the main character of a hugot song about feeling insignificant. 'Pakiramdam ko isa lang akong **taong bale-wala** sa buhay niya.'
usage_notes: A very strong and often hurtful phrase. Carries a heavy emotional weight.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong ituring na **taong bale-wala** ang iyong sarili dahil bawat isa ay may halaga.","translation":"Do not consider yourself a **person of no consequence** because everyone has value."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na ginagamit bilang tuntungan o sapin sa paanan.
original_explanation: Literally, something you're meant to step on. This could be the doormat that says "Welcome," the little stool to help you reach the top shelf, or even a person you use as a 'stepping stone' to get ahead in life (yikes, don't be that person).
usage_notes: Can be a literal object or used figuratively to mean a means to an end, often with a negative connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gamitin mo ang **patapakan** para maabot mo ang bumbilya.","translation":"Use the **footstool** to reach the lightbulb."},{"sentence":"Ayokong maging **patapakan** lamang para sa iyong tagumpay.","translation":"I don't want to just be a **stepping stone** for your success."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal o rehiyonal na varyant ng salitang 'tiyo' na tumutukoy sa kapatid na lalaki ng magulang.
etymology: Varyant ng "tiyo", mula sa Espanyol na "tío".
original_explanation: A more classic, sometimes provincial, way of saying 'Tiyo' or 'Tito'. If someone calls their uncle 'Tiyong', they might be from a specific region or just have a more traditional family vibe. It's the OG 'Tito'.
usage_notes: Less common in urban Manila but still widely used in other regions. It carries a slightly more dated or rural connotation compared to 'tiyo' or the more modern 'tito'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si **Tiyong** Berto ang paborito kong kamag-anak.","translation":"**Uncle** Berto is my favorite relative."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o establisyimento kung saan nag-aalok ng serbisyo ng paggugupit ng buhok.
etymology: From `pagupit` + `-an` (location marker). Literally "a place for getting a haircut".
original_explanation: The sacred place where all the neighborhood chismis is born. It's where you go in looking like a mess and come out either looking like a celebrity or crying internally. The air is a mix of hairspray, shampoo, and the latest tea.
usage_notes: Can refer to a male-focused barbershop (`barberya`) or a unisex/female-focused salon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumunta si tatay sa **pagupitan** para magpa-ahit.","translation":"Dad went to the **barbershop** to get a shave."},{"sentence":"Nagkita-kita ang magkakaibigan sa **pagupitan** bago ang party.","translation":"The friends met at the **salon** before the party."}]

translation: to be charmed; to be fascinated; to be captivated
meaning_filipino: Ang mabighani o maakit nang husto sa isang tao, bagay, o lugar dahil sa angkin nitong ganda, galing, o kakaibang katangian.
original_explanation: The OG "sana all" magnet. It's when someone or something is so captivating, you're instantly drawn in. It's that K-drama lead who makes you forget you have deadlines, or that beach in Palawan that makes you want to quit your job and sell coconuts. It’s a spell-binding attraction.
usage_notes: Nagtataglay ng diwa ng malalim na pagkaakit o pagkabighani. Madalas gamitin sa romantiko o patulang konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marami ang **nahalina** sa kanyang angking ganda at talino.","translation":"Many were **charmed** by her innate beauty and intelligence."},{"sentence":"Sino ba ang hindi **mahahalina** sa ganda ng El Nido?","translation":"Who wouldn't **be captivated** by the beauty of El Nido?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahinang kaluskos, tulad ng tunog ng tuyong dahon na tinatangay ng hangin. Maaari ring tumukoy sa palihim o biglaang pag-alis.
original_explanation: That spooky sound you hear at night when you're home alone watching a horror movie. 'Yung alis-is ng dahon sa labas, or worse, 'yung alis-is sa loob ng bahay. It can also mean "the great escape" or "Irish exit"—'yung bigla na lang siyang nawala sa party nang walang paalam. Nag-alis-is!
usage_notes: Can refer to both a sound and an action. The context determines the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **alis-is** ng mga dahon sa hardin.","translation":"I heard the **rustling sound** of the leaves in the garden."},{"sentence":"Sa isang iglap, nagkaroon ng **alis-is** ang magnanakaw at hindi na namin nakita.","translation":"In an instant, the thief made a **secret departure** and we never saw him again."}]

translation: to drop; to shed; to miscarry
meaning_filipino: Ang paghulog o pagbitaw sa isang bagay, sinasadya man o hindi. Ginagamit din ito para sa pagkawala ng bunga sa sinapupunan.
original_explanation: This is the 'oops' verb. You maglaglag your phone, a tree can maglaglag its leaves, or in a more serious, 'hugot' sense, someone can maglaglag you from their life. It's the action of something falling or being let go. It also has a very serious medical meaning: to have a miscarriage. So, context is super important.
usage_notes: The meaning can range from mundane (dropping an item) to serious (miscarriage). Be mindful of the context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-ingat siya na hindi **maglaglag** ng kahit anong basura sa daan.","translation":"He was careful not to **drop** any trash on the road."},{"sentence":"Ang puno ng mangga ay nagsimulang **maglaglag** ng mga dahon.","translation":"The mango tree started to **shed** its leaves."},{"sentence":"Isang malaking dagok sa kanya nang siya ay **maglaglag**.","translation":"It was a huge blow to her when she had a **miscarriage**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagpapatuyo ng isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pagbibilad o paglalantad nito sa sikat ng araw.
etymology: Proto-Philippine *balad, meaning "to spread out to dry".
original_explanation: What your mom does to the laundry on a sunny Saturday, making the whole neighborhood smell like fabric conditioner. It's also how they make tuyo (dried fish) and daing. Think of it as a natural, eco-friendly dryer powered by pure, scorching Philippine heat. Verb forms: 'magbalad', 'ibalad'.
usage_notes: Used as a root for verbs like 'ibinalad' (was sun-dried) and 'magbalad' (to sun-dry something).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **ibalad** ang mga isda upang maging daing.","translation":"The fish need to be **sun-dried** to become 'daing'."},{"sentence":"Nag-**balad** siya ng mga damit sa sampayan.","translation":"She **exposed** the clothes to the sun on the clothesline."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagnanakaw o gumagamit para sa sariling kapakanan ng perang ipinagkatiwala sa kanya.
original_explanation: The treasurer of your 'paluwagan' who suddenly goes on a "soul-searching" trip to Europe and can no longer be contacted. That's a `despalkador`. It’s a fancy word for a specific kind of magnanakaw who steals the money they were supposed to be watching.
usage_notes: A formal and legal term. 'Mandarambong' or 'magnanakaw' are more common in casual speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinahanap ng mga pulis ang **despalkador** na tumangay sa pondo ng kumpanya.","translation":"The police are looking for the **embezzler** who ran off with the company's funds."},{"sentence":"Nakasuhan ng pagiging **despalkador** ang dating ingat-yaman.","translation":"The former treasurer was charged with being an **embezzler**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, grupo, o ahensya na may kapangyarihang ipatupad ang mga batas, alituntunin, o patakaran.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'tagapagpa-' (agent) at 'tupad' (fulfill), na bumubuo sa salitang 'patupad' (to implement).
original_explanation: Think of the MMDA on EDSA, the barangay tanod doing their rounds, or your office HR making sure everyone follows the new 'no-Tiktok-during-work-hours' memo. They're the ones who make sure the rules aren't just suggestions.
usage_notes: Karaniwang tumutukoy sa mga awtoridad o ahensya ng gobyerno.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga pulis ang pangunahing **tagapagpatupad** ng batas sa ating bansa.","translation":"The police are the primary **enforcers** of the law in our country."},{"sentence":"Itinalaga ang isang komite bilang **tagapagpatupad** ng mga bagong patakaran sa kompanya.","translation":"A committee was assigned as the **implementer** of the new company policies."}]

translation: to make something last longer; to prolong
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapahaba sa durasyon o panahong ginugugol sa isang gawain, pangyayari, o kalagayan.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're on a good date and you wish you could 'itagal' the moment. Or when your client call is supposed to be 30 minutes but they 'itinagal' it for two hours. It's the act of extending time, for better or for worse. 'Huwag mo nang itagal ang pag-uusap, sabihin mo na.' (Don't prolong the conversation, just say it.) It's about stretching a moment, a task, or a feeling.
usage_notes: Used to describe the act of causing something to take more time. The focus is on the thing being prolonged.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **itagal** ang kanilang bakasyon kahit isang araw pa.","translation":"He tried to **prolong** their vacation for even just one more day."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo sanang **itagal** ang iyong paghihiganti; magpatawad ka na.","translation":"I hope you don't **prolong** your revenge; just forgive."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng kasiyahan o kaligayahan sa isang tao o sa Diyos sa pamamagitan ng salita o gawa.
original_explanation: This is your goal kapag may nililigawan ka or when you're trying to impress your future mother-in-law. It's the act of making someone happy, like giving them the last piece of chicken joy or letting them win at Mobile Legends. 'Happy wife, happy life' is the ultimate magpalugod life mission.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of pleasing someone important, including God.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang **magpalugod** sa kanyang mga biyenan.","translation":"He is trying to **please** his in-laws."},{"sentence":"Ang pagtulong sa kapwa ay isang paraan upang **magpalugod** sa Diyos.","translation":"Helping others is one way to **please** God."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang baryasyon sa pagbaybay ng salitang 'lengguwahe'. Tumutukoy sa sistema ng komunikasyon na ginagamit ng mga tao.
original_explanation: Spelling variation ng 'lengguwahe'. Medyo 'di na 'to ginagamit, parang pag-ibig ng ex mo, nag-exist pero laos na. Stick to 'lengguwahe' or 'lenggwahe' para 'di ka ma-call out ng grammar police.
usage_notes: Isang hindi gaanong karaniwang pagbaybay. Ang mas tinatanggap na mga anyo ay 'lengguwahe' at 'lenggwahe'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang pambansang **lenguwahe** ng bansang Hapon?","translation":"What is the national **language** of Japan?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging matingkad o matindi ng isang kulay; kalinawan o kasikatan.
etymology: From ka- (quality of) + tingkad (vividness, intensity of color).
original_explanation: This is the 'in your face' quality of a neon sign, the color of a ripe mango, or your friend's highlighter-yellow crocs. It's the visual equivalent of shouting. When a color is so bright it almost hurts your eyes but you can't look away, that's **katingkaran**.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used to describe the intensity or vividness of colors.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Namumukod-tangi ang **katingkaran** ng mga bulaklak sa hardin.","translation":"The **vividness** of the flowers in the garden stands out."},{"sentence":"Binawasan niya ang **katingkaran** ng pula sa kanyang ipininta.","translation":"He reduced the **intensity** of the red in his painting."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sistema ng komunikasyon na ginagamitan ng mga tunog, salita, at gramatika, na ginagamit ng isang partikular na bansa o komunidad.
etymology: Mula sa Sanskrit na "vākya" (वाक्य), na nangangahulugang "pananalita" o "pangungusap".
original_explanation: Ito yung dahilan kung bakit nagkakaintindihan (o nag-aaway) ang mga tao. Ito rin ang subject na ipinagdiriwang tuwing Buwan ng Wika, kung kailan lahat ay nagiging makata at nagsusuot ng baro't saya. Sa modernong panahon, ang 'wika' ay nag-evolve na rin sa emojis, memes, at gay lingo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Filipino ang ating pambansang **wika**.","translation":"Filipino is our national **language**."},{"sentence":"Mahalagang pag-aralan ang iba't ibang **wika** sa mundo.","translation":"It is important to study the different **languages** of the world."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbangon mula sa pagkakatulog sa hinaharap; ang pagiging mulat muli matapos ang pamamahinga.
original_explanation: That moment your 5th alarm for your 6 AM shift finally works. '5 more minutes' is a lie you tell yourself, pero gigising ka rin naman pala. This is the future tense of waking up, full of dread and responsibility.
usage_notes: This is the future tense of the verb 'gising' (to wake up).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Gigising** ako nang maaga bukas para sa flight natin.","translation":"I **will wake up** early tomorrow for our flight."},{"sentence":"Anong oras ka **gigising** para sa ating online meeting?","translation":"What time **will** you **wake up** for our online meeting?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang tungkulin ay maglagay ng marka, magtala ng puntos, o magsuri ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: The person in charge of the scoresheet. In sports, they're the one tracking the points. In school, they're your classmate who checks the quiz papers. In the palengke, they're the one who marks the 'suki' list. They hold the power of the 'check' or 'ekis'.
usage_notes: Can be used in various contexts like sports, academics, or any activity involving scoring or marking.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng **tagamarka** para sa ating laro ng basketball.","translation":"We need a **scorer** for our basketball game."},{"sentence":"Si Lisa ang itinalagang **tagamarka** ng mga dumadalo sa seminar.","translation":"Lisa was assigned as the **checker** for the seminar attendees."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging masalimuot, magulo, o mahirap unawain dahil sa maraming magkakaugnay na bahagi o detalye.
original_explanation: Relationship status: 'It's Complicated'. 'Yan ang kasalimuutan. Parang pag-intindi sa family tree ng mga Targaryen, sa rules ng TRAIN law, o sa plot ng isang Christopher Nolan film. Needs a diagram and a lot of coffee.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa **kasalimuutan** ng kaso, inabot ito ng maraming taon sa korte.","translation":"Because of the **complexity** of the case, it took many years in court."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagbibigay ng detalye, dahilan, o impormasyon upang gawing malinaw at mauunawaan ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: That moment when you have to explain to your parents why you got home at 3 AM. Or when your partner asks "Sino 'yang ka-chat mo?" and you have to present a whole PowerPoint presentation. That's pagpapaliwanag.
usage_notes: A very common word used in any situation requiring clarification, from school to relationships.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng malinaw na **pagpapaliwanag** kung bakit ka huli sa ating usapan.","translation":"I need a clear **explanation** as to why you were late for our meeting."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang aparato na gumagawa ng malakas at matining na tunog bilang babala, tulad ng sa ambulansya, trak ng bumbero, o patrol ng pulis.
original_explanation: That loud, ear-splitting "WEE-WOO-WEE-WOO" sound that makes you pull over to the side of the road. It's the official sound of "OMG, something's happening!" whether it's an ambulance rushing to the hospital, a fire truck, or the noon-time signal in some provinces. It's the sound of urgency.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa aparato na nagbibigay babala. Ang konteksto ng pangungusap ang naglilinaw ng kahulugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nang marinig namin ang **sirena** ng ambulansya, tumabi kami sa daan.","translation":"When we heard the **siren** of the ambulance, we moved to the side of the road."},{"sentence":"Ang **sirena** tuwing alas-dose ng tanghali ay hudyat para sa pananghalian.","translation":"The **siren** at twelve noon is the signal for lunch."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na salita na nagpapahiwatig ng paghanga sa paraan ng pagkilos, pagganap, o pagdadala ng isang tao sa sarili nang may kumpiyansa at kahusayan.
etymology: From African-American Vernacular English and ballroom culture, popularized globally.
original_explanation: When 'work' just isn't fabulous enough. This is what your friends scream when you finally post that perfectly angled selfie, or when someone aces a presentation at the office. It's the verbal equivalent of a slow clap and a hair flip. From the runway to the BPO floor, 'werk' means you're killing it.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tingnan mo ang OOTD niya, ang ganda! **Werk**!","translation":"Look at her OOTD, it's so beautiful! **Slay**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng pagkakaroon ng magandang ugnayan, pagkakasundo, at komportableng pakiramdam sa isang tao.
etymology: A phrase composed of 'kagaanan' (lightness) and 'ng loob' (of one's inner self).
original_explanation: This is when you just 'click' with someone. You meet a person and after five minutes, you're already sharing memes and complaining about the same things. It's that instant comfort and connection, the opposite of an awkward first date. You're 'on the same wavelength.'
usage_notes: This is a very important concept in Filipino interpersonal relationships (pakikipagkapwa). It signifies a smooth, easy-going relationship.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Agad kaming nagkaroon ng **kagaanan ng loob** sa isa't isa.","translation":"We immediately developed a **rapport** with each other."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **kagaanan ng loob** sa isang team para maging matagumpay ang proyekto.","translation":"Having **congeniality** in a team is important for a project to be successful."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na lubhang mahalaga, esensyal, at hindi maaaring mawala o hindi gawin.
etymology: From 'kailangan' (need, necessary), with the 'kina-' prefix indicating a present/progressive state of being needed.
original_explanation: This is the adulting version of 'gusto ko.' It's not what you want, it's what you NEED. It's the requirements for your visa application, the ingredients for adobo, or the stable internet connection for your WFH job. Non-negotiable. Mandatory. The 'must-haves' of life.
usage_notes: Often used as a verb ('Kinakailangan kong umalis') or an adjective ('mga kinakailangang dokumento').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang mga **kinakailangan** para makakuha ng pasaporte?","translation":"What are the **requirements** to get a passport?"},{"sentence":"**Kinakailangan** mong mag-aral nang mabuti para pumasa.","translation":"It is **necessary** for you to study well to pass."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sinasadyang pag-aalis ng isang sanggol mula sa sinapupunan ng ina bago ito maisilang.
etymology: From `pag-` + `pa-` + `laglag` (to fall, to drop). The `pa-` prefix indicates causation, hence 'to cause to drop/fall'.
original_explanation: A very serious and sensitive topic. This refers to the deliberate termination of a pregnancy. It's a subject of intense debate and is illegal in the Philippines, often discussed in whispers or in the context of health warnings and legal dramas.
usage_notes: This term specifically refers to an induced abortion, not a natural miscarriage ('pagkalaglag' or 'nakunan'). It is a highly sensitive and often controversial term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapalaglag** ay isang ilegal at mapanganib na gawain sa bansa.","translation":"**Induced abortion** is an illegal and dangerous act in the country."},{"sentence":"Maraming organisasyon ang tumututol sa pagsasabatas ng **pagpapalaglag**.","translation":"Many organizations oppose the legalization of **induced abortion**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pakikipagtunggali, pagkontra, o paghamon sa isang tao, bagay, o ideya.
original_explanation: This is the action form. It's what you do. Labanan mo ang tukso na i-chat ang ex mo. Labanan mo ang sistema. Labanan mo ang pagnanasang umorder ng milk tea kahit petsa de peligro na. It's actively resisting something.
usage_notes: Isang palipat na pandiwa na nangangailangan ng tuwirang layon na siyang kinakalaban.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat nating **labanan** ang pagkalat ng maling impormasyon.","translation":"We must **fight against** the spread of misinformation."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-anyaya o pagsama sa isang tao sa pagsasayaw.
original_explanation: When you're at a party and your tita forces you to dance with your cousin you haven't seen in 10 years. 'I-bayle mo ang pinsan mo!' she screams over the music. It's the command form of 'get on the dance floor with this person.'
usage_notes: Usually means to take someone as a dance partner.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto sana kitang **ibayle** ngunit nahihiya ako.","translation":"I wanted to **dance with you** but I'm shy."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **ibinayle** ng debutante sa kanyang cotillion?","translation":"Who did the debutante **dance with** in her cotillion?"}]

meaning_filipino: Daglat para sa pariralang Ingles na 'looking for,' na nangangahulugang 'naghahanap ng.'
etymology: Daglat ng pariralang Ingles na 'looking for.'
original_explanation: The three most important letters in any online marketplace or buy-and-sell group. It's the digital version of shouting in a crowded palengke what you need. 'LF: Jowa, 'yung seryoso.' is the ultimate final boss of all LF posts.
usage_notes: Ginagamit lamang sa digital na komunikasyon, tulad ng mga social media post, forum, at chat group.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**LF**: murang apartment, one month advance, one month deposit lang.","translation":"**Looking for**: a cheap apartment, just one month advance, one month deposit."},{"sentence":"Post niya sa group: '**LF** ka-duo sa ML, mythic rank.'","translation":"His post in the group: '**Looking for** a duo in ML, mythic rank.'"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging nasa pagitan ng pagiging gising at tulog; antukin.
original_explanation: "Agaw-tulog" is that state you're in during a 1 PM meeting after a heavy lunch. Your eyes are open, but your brain has logged off. It's when you're on a bus, your head keeps nodding, and you're trying to fight sleep but sleep is winning. Literally "sleep-snatching," but here, sleep is the one doing the snatching.
usage_notes: Describes the drowsy state just before falling asleep or just after waking up.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong kausapin, **agaw-tulog** pa ako.","translation":"Don't talk to me, I'm still **half-asleep**."},{"sentence":"Nahuli siyang **agaw-tulog** sa klase ng kanyang guro.","translation":"He was caught **drowsy** in class by his teacher."}]

translation: to grow; to flourish; to prosper
meaning_filipino: Umunlad, dumami, o tumubo nang malusog at masagana.
original_explanation: This is what you hope your savings account does, but it's usually what your hair does when you need a haircut. It's the glow-up word. From a small sari-sari store to a mini-mart, lumago ang negosyo. From a tiny seedling to a big tree, lumago ang halaman. It’s all about positive growth and getting thicc, whether it's your wallet or your plant collection.
usage_notes: Used for plants, businesses, hair, population, etc. Signifies healthy and abundant growth.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis **lumago** ang kanilang negosyong food cart.","translation":"Their food cart business **grew** quickly."},{"sentence":"**Lumago** nang husto ang mga tanim niyang gulay dahil sa ulan.","translation":"His vegetable plants **flourished** greatly because of the rain."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sanggol na umaasa pa sa gatas ng ina bilang pangunahing pagkain.
etymology: From 'bata' (child) and 'pasusuhin' (to be breastfed), from the root 'suso' (breast).
original_explanation: This refers to a baby who is still breastfeeding. It's that cute, chubby, "gigil-worthy" stage where their main job is to eat (suso), sleep, and poop. It's the most high-maintenance, low-contribution member of the household, but also the boss.
usage_notes: This is a descriptive phrase rather than a single word. 'Sanggol' is the more common term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang isang **batang pasusuhin** ay nangangailangan ng masusing pag-aaruga.","translation":"An **infant** requires meticulous care."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang gatas ng ina para sa kalusugan ng **batang pasusuhin**.","translation":"A mother's milk is important for the health of a **suckling child**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang batang inahing manok na hindi pa nagsisimulang mangitlog o kalalagpas pa lamang sa pagiging sisiw.
etymology: From 'dalaga' (unmarried young woman), applied to a young hen. The form is a fossilized verb form now used as a noun.
original_explanation: Basically, a teenage chicken. Not a baby chick ('sisiw'), not yet a full-blown egg-laying momma hen ('inahing manok'). She's in that awkward phase, finding her place in the coop. In human terms, she's the 'dalagita' of the poultry world. A 'dumalagang manok' is often cooked as tinola because its meat is tender.
usage_notes: 'Dumalaga' by itself refers to a pullet. It is almost always seen with 'manok' as in 'dumalagang manok' to be clear.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas masarap daw ang tinola kapag **dumalagang manok** ang ginamit.","translation":"They say tinola is more delicious when a **young hen** is used."},{"sentence":"Naghahanap si Mang Tonyo ng **dumalaga** para sa kanyang manukan.","translation":"Mang Tonyo is looking for a **pullet** for his poultry farm."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng araw sa pagitan ng tanghali at gabi.
original_explanation: That magical time between lunch and dinner. The official siesta time, merienda time, or 'antok-sa-opisina' time. 'Yung sinasabi mong 'mamayang hapon' na lang gagawin 'yung work, tapos biglang gabi na. Also, the first half of 'Magandang Hapon'.
usage_notes: Used in the common greeting 'Magandang hapon'. The stress is on the first syllable, which distinguishes it from Hapon (Japanese).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkita tayo mamayang **hapon** sa parke.","translation":"Let's meet this **afternoon** at the park."},{"sentence":"Inaantok ako tuwing **hapon** pagkatapos mananghalian.","translation":"I get sleepy every **afternoon** after eating lunch."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sangkap o bagay na idinadagdag upang magbigay ng kapal o lapot, tulad sa sarsa, buhok, o materyales.
etymology: From 'pang-' (instrumental prefix) + 'pa-' (causative prefix) + 'kapal' (thickness). Lit. 'that which is used to cause thickness'.
original_explanation: In cooking, it's the cornstarch that saves your watery sauce. For your hair, it's the shampoo that promises 'more volume.' For your face, it's the foundation you apply layer by layer. It can also refer to the 'lakas ng loob' you need to ask for a raise ('pampakapal ng mukha').
usage_notes: The meaning can be literal (thickening a liquid, hair) or figurative (as in 'pampakapal ng mukha', something that makes one shameless). This entry focuses on the literal sense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagdagdag siya ng arina bilang **pampakapal** ng sarsa.","translation":"She added flour as a **thickener** for the sauce."},{"sentence":"Mayroon bang shampoo na mabisang **pampakapal** ng buhok?","translation":"Is there a shampoo that is an effective **hair thickener**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagbibisikleta, para man sa transportasyon, ehersisyo, o libangan.
original_explanation: The modern-day kabayo. You see them in full Lycra gear conquering the hills of Rizal on a Sunday, or weaving through EDSA traffic like a pro. They are powered by determination, strong coffee, and an unli-rice diet. The mortal enemy of impatient bus drivers.
usage_notes: A direct loanword that has become very common, especially with the rise of cycling culture in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumarami ang mga **siklista** sa Maynila dahil sa pandemya.","translation":"The number of **cyclists** in Manila is increasing because of the pandemic."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa mga **siklista** sa daan.","translation":"Be careful of the **cyclists** on the road."}]

translation: to cause to stammer or stutter
meaning_filipino: Magdulot ng pautal-utal o hindi tuloy-tuloy na pagsasalita, karaniwan dahil sa kaba, takot, o pag-aalangan.
original_explanation: This happens when you're called for recitation and you didn't do the reading. Or when your crush asks you a question and your brain just blue-screens. Your mouth tries to form words, but they come out like a corrupted audio file.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sobrang kaba ay maaaring **mapautal-utal** sa isang tao habang nagsasalita sa publiko.","translation":"Extreme nervousness can **cause a person to stammer** while speaking in public."},{"sentence":"Nang makita niya ang multo, siya ay **napautal-utal** sa takot.","translation":"When he saw the ghost, he **started to stutter** in fear."}]

translation: to notice (someone/something), to pay attention to
meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng pansin o atensiyon ang isang tao, bagay, o pangyayari. Ito ay ang anyong pautos o pakiusap ng pandiwang "pansin".
original_explanation: This is the verb form of "notice me, senpai!" It's what you tell your friend when their crush walks by: "Pansinin mo, dali!" (Notice him/her, quick!). Or what you mutter to yourself when your boss is ignoring your brilliant idea in a meeting. It's the active command to give someone the time of day.
usage_notes: This is the object-focus verb form. The subject-focus form is "pumansin". "Pansinin mo siya" (You notice him). "Pumansin ka naman" (You should pay attention).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pansinin** mo ang pagbabago sa kanyang ugali.","translation":"**Notice** the change in his behavior."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang **pansinin** ang mga negatibong komento.","translation":"Don't **pay attention** to the negative comments anymore."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpunta sa direksyon o landas na tinatahak ng iba; ang paggaya sa isang gawain, halimbawa, o instruksyon.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you stalk someone's IG profile, clicking from one tagged photo to the next. It's also literally following someone on the street or following instructions in a recipe. 'Sundan mo ako' means 'Follow me,' whether you're leading them to a secret restaurant or just to the next room.
usage_notes: Object-focused verb from the root 'sunod'. The imperative form is also 'sundan'. It typically refers to following a physical path, a person, or a visual example.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**sundan** ang mga panuto sa pagsusulit.","translation":"Please **follow** the instructions on the exam."},{"sentence":"**Sundan** mo ang taong naka-pulang sumbrero.","translation":"**Follow** the person in the red hat."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalaro ng bilyar, isang laro na gumagamit ng tako upang itulak ang mga bola sa isang mesang may mga butas.
original_explanation: The classic 'tambay' activity with your barkada. It's the game you play while drinking beer and trying to look cool, even if you keep scratching. It’s about hitting balls with a stick into holes on a table.
usage_notes: A loanword that has been fully integrated into Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Niyaya ako ng mga kaibigan kong **magbilyar** pagkatapos ng trabaho.","translation":"My friends invited me to **play billiards** after work."},{"sentence":"Mahusay siyang **magbilyar** at madalas manalo sa pustahan.","translation":"He is good at **playing billiards** and often wins bets."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang yugto ng araw sa pagitan ng hapon at gabi, kung kailan papalubog na ang araw.
original_explanation: The golden hour for your IG feed. That magical, slightly melancholic time of day when the sun is setting, the sky is a mix of orange and purple, and you suddenly feel the urge to be sentimental or drink coffee. It's the universe's way of saying, 'Okay, pwede ka nang umuwi at mag-Netflix.'
usage_notes: A more poetic term than just 'hapon' or 'gabi'. Literally translates to 'the approach of the afternoon/evening'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakaganda ng tanawin sa dalampasigan tuwing **dapithapon**.","translation":"The view at the beach is so beautiful during **dusk**."},{"sentence":"Nagsisimula nang umilaw ang mga poste pagsapit ng **dapithapon**.","translation":"The lamp posts start to light up when **twilight** arrives."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-abot ng isang likido sa temperatura kung saan ito ay nagiging singaw (steam) at bumubuo ng mga bula. Ito ang anyong pangkaganapan ng 'kulo'.
original_explanation: Past tense of "boil." This is the first step to making instant noodles, coffee, or sinigang. When the water kumulo, it's go time. It's the state of bubbling liquid that's hot enough to cook something or, in the case of your temper (kumukulo ang dugo), hot enough to start an argument.
usage_notes: Past tense/completed aspect of 'kulo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nang **kumulo** na ang tubig, inilagay ko na ang mga pansit.","translation":"When the water **boiled**, I put in the noodles."},{"sentence":"Mabilis **kumulo** ang nilaga sa bagong kaldero.","translation":"The stew **boiled** quickly in the new pot."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong may karapatang bumoto sa isang halalan.
original_explanation: This is the official-sounding term for a voter. You're not just a 'botante', you are an 'elektor'! It sounds like something from a formal COMELEC document. It's the person who holds the power during an election, even if it's just for one day.
usage_notes: A formal term for "voter". "Botante" is more common in everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bawat **elektor** ay may responsibilidad na pumili ng karapat-dapat na lider.","translation":"Every **elector** has the responsibility to choose a worthy leader."},{"sentence":"Tumaas ang bilang ng mga rehistradong **elektor** ngayong taon.","translation":"The number of registered **voters** increased this year."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang araknida na may walong paa, isang pares ng sipit, at isang buntot na may nakalalasong tibo sa dulo.
original_explanation: That creepy-crawly desert creature that looks like a mini-lobster with a death-stinger on its tail. Also, the zodiac sign for your intense, passionate, and slightly vengeful friend born in November. Handle with care, both the animal and the person.
usage_notes: Ang katutubong salita para dito ay "alakdan", ngunit karaniwan ding gamitin ang "eskorpiyon".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa mga **eskorpiyon** kapag naglalakad sa disyerto.","translation":"Be careful of **scorpions** when walking in the desert."},{"sentence":"Ang kagat ng **eskorpiyon** ay maaaring makamatay.","translation":"A **scorpion**'s sting can be fatal."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pagtugtog ng kampana ng simbahan tuwing gabi (karaniwan ay ika-6 ng gabi) bilang panawagan sa pagdarasal ng Angelus; maaari ring tumukoy sa mga kaluluwa sa purgatoryo.
original_explanation: This is the sound of church bells ringing at 6 PM, signaling it's time for the Angelus prayer. For older generations, it meant everything stops. Kids had to go home, people would pause and pray. Today, it's that nostalgic sound you might hear in the province that reminds you to log off from work. It's also linked to the 'kaluluwa' or souls in purgatory, for whom the prayers are often offered.
usage_notes: Primarily used in a religious, specifically Catholic, context. The term is less common among younger, urban populations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing tumutunog ang **animas**, humihinto sa paglalaro ang mga bata para magdasal.","translation":"Whenever the **Angelus bell** rings, the children stop playing to pray."},{"sentence":"Nag-aalay sila ng panalangin para sa mga **animas** sa purgatoryo.","translation":"They offer prayers for the **souls** in purgatory."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng tela na may makinis at malambot na pakiramdam, na karaniwang may maikling buhok-buhok sa ibabaw nito.
etymology: From Spanish 'pelusa' (fuzz, fluff), though it means 'velvet' in Tagalog. The direct Spanish for velvet is 'terciopelo'. The Tagalog 'pelus' seems to have taken the sense of a fuzzy, plush fabric.
original_explanation: That fancy, smooth fabric that makes you feel like royalty, or at least a member of a 90s R&B group. It's what your lola's sofa might be made of, or that special occasion dress you're too scared to spill anything on. It's the texture of luxury, even if it's just a cheap scrunchie.
usage_notes: Often used to describe the texture of something, e.g., 'makinis na parang pelus' (smooth like velvet).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kurtina sa mansyon ay gawa sa mamahaling pulang **pelus**.","translation":"The curtain in the mansion is made of expensive red **velvet**."},{"sentence":"Malambot ang kanyang balat, parang **pelus**.","translation":"Her skin is soft, like **velvet**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang panulat o pangkulay na gawa sa may kulay na pagkit, karaniwang ginagamit ng mga bata sa pagguhit.
original_explanation: Ang sandata ng bawat batang artist. Ito yung unang-unang 'art materials' mo bago ka pa natutong gumamit ng Photoshop. At aminin mo, minsan naamoy-amoy mo pa 'to noong kinder ka.
usage_notes: Commonly associated with children's art materials.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binilhan niya ng isang kahon ng **kreyon** ang kanyang anak.","translation":"She bought a box of **crayons** for her child."},{"sentence":"Puno ng mga guhit ng **kreyon** ang pader ng kanyang kwarto.","translation":"The wall of his room is full of **crayon** drawings."}]

meaning_filipino: Pakiusapan ang isang tao sa isang malumanay, mapagkumbaba, at kaakit-akit na paraan.
original_explanation: This is the "puppy dog eyes" move in verb form. It's when you're begging for a favor, but you do it gently and with maximum pa-cute or pa-awa effect. You're not demanding, you're imploring. It's how you ask your boss for a day off after a long weekend, or how a child asks for one more piece of candy.
usage_notes: Less intense and desperate than 'magmakaawa'. It focuses on gentleness and charm.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagmamakaamo** ang bata sa kanyang ina na bilhan siya ng bagong laruan.","translation":"The child is **pleading gently** with his mother to buy him a new toy."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ko pang **magmakaamo** para lang payagan siyang lumabas.","translation":"I still had to **implore** just to get her permission to go out."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglapit sa isang tao upang humingi o kumuha ng isang bagay mula sa kanya.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'hingi' at hulaping '-an'.
original_explanation: The verb form of being a 'friend' during petsa de peligro. 'Pre, pwedeng hingan ka muna ng pang-kape?' It's the act of requesting something, from a piece of paper to a major life favor. It's the foundation of 'utang na loob' and the occasional 'seen zone.'
usage_notes: Nakatuon sa tao o pinagmumulan kung kanino hinihiling ang isang bagay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **hingan** ng pera dahil wala rin ako.","translation":"Don't **ask me for** money because I don't have any either."},{"sentence":"Maaari ba kitang **hingan** ng payo?","translation":"May I **ask you for** advice?"}]

translation: to value; to appreciate; to give importance
meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng importansya, paggalang, o mataas na pagtingin ang isang tao, bagay, o konsepto.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'hugot' word. This is what you tell your jowa when they're not giving you enough attention: "Pahalagahan mo naman ako!" It means to treat something or someone like they're a limited-edition Starbucks tumbler—precious and not to be taken for granted. It's the opposite of being 'dedma' (ignored). Value your time, your work, your friends, your data plan.
usage_notes: A very common verb used in contexts of relationships, personal values, and appreciation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat nating **pahalagahan** ang ating mga magulang habang sila'y nabubuhay.","translation":"We should **value** our parents while they are still alive."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya alam kung paano **pahalagahan** ang mga simpleng bagay sa buhay.","translation":"He doesn't know how to **appreciate** the simple things in life."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang produktong gawa sa gatas na pinakapal at pinapaasim sa pamamagitan ng bacterial fermentation.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na 'yogurt', na nagmula naman sa Turkish na 'yoğurt'.
original_explanation: That healthy stuff you buy from the grocery store when you promise yourself you'll start a diet. Comes in flavors like strawberry, blueberry, and that plain one that tastes like sad sour cream. Perfect for your "Tita/Tito" wellness journey.
usage_notes: Ginagamit bilang isang hiram na salita sa Filipino. Walang katutubong katumbas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang kumain ng **yogurt** na may prutas tuwing umaga.","translation":"She likes to eat **yogurt** with fruit every morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, bagay, o puwersa na nagbibigay ng proteksyon o pananggalang laban sa panganib, atake, o pinsala.
original_explanation: Your personal Darna or Captain Barbell. This could be the lawyer defending you in court, the antivirus protecting your laptop from malware, or your big brother who stood up to your bullies. They're your shield, your firewall, your human (or digital) body guard.
usage_notes: Isang pormal at matalinghagang salita. Mas karaniwan ang 'tagapagtanggol'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga sundalo ang nagsisilbing **tagapagsanggalang** ng ating teritoryo.","translation":"The soldiers serve as the **protectors** of our territory."},{"sentence":"Itinuring niyang **tagapagsanggalang** ang kanyang nakatatandang kapatid.","translation":"She considered her older sibling as her **protector**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglilinis ng isang bagay gamit ang tubig at (madalas) sabon.
original_explanation: The national sport of every Filipino household after a meal. It's the chore that magically becomes yours when you're the last one to finish eating. 'Hugas-kamay' is also what you call someone who evades responsibility.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit para sa mga kamay, pinggan, o iba pang maliliit na bagay. Iba sa 'laba' na para sa damit. Maaari ring gamitin bilang pandiwa (e.g., 'Maghugas ka ng kamay.')
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang taya sa **hugas** ng pinggan mamayang gabi?","translation":"Whose turn is it to do the **washing** of dishes tonight?"},{"sentence":"Ang nanay ay nag-aayos ng mga **hugas** na plato.","translation":"The mother is arranging the **washed** plates."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpilipit o pag-ikid ng isang bagay sa palibot ng isa pa; ang kalagayan ng pagiging nakapilipit o nakalingkis.
original_explanation: Like how a snake wraps around its prey, or how your earphones get impossibly tangled in your pocket. It can also be 'hugot' for a clingy ex: 'Grabe ang **pulupot** niya sa'yo, parang ahas.'
usage_notes: This is the root word. It can be used as a noun (the coil itself) or as a root for verbs like `pumulupot` (to coil) and `puluputan` (to coil around something).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap tanggalin ang **pulupot** ng baging sa puno.","translation":"It's hard to remove the vine's **coil** from the tree."},{"sentence":"Pumulupot ang ahas sa binti ng mangangaso.","translation":"The snake coiled around the hunter's leg. (showing verb form 'pumulupot')"}]

translation: to scamper; to move with quick, jerky steps
meaning_filipino: Gumalaw o tumakbo sa paraang mabilis, paigtad-igtad, at tila hindi mapakali, karaniwan dahil sa tuwa, takot, o pananabik.
original_explanation: That feeling when you hear the ice cream truck music getting closer. Or when your crush finally replies and you do that little happy dance in your seat. That's `magkandirit`. It's a sudden burst of excited, jumpy movement, like a cat with the zoomies or a kid who just got a new toy.
usage_notes: Often used to describe children, small animals, or someone extremely excited or anxious. It implies a light, almost comical movement.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagkandirit** sa tuwa ang bata nang makita ang regalong laruan.","translation":"The child **scampered** in joy upon seeing the toy gift."},{"sentence":"Parang manok na **nagkandirit** siya nang matapakan ang mainit na semento.","translation":"He **hopped around** like a chicken when he stepped on the hot cement."}]

meaning_filipino: Nauunawaan; malinaw na naiintindihan.
original_explanation: This is a bit of a throwback word, something your lolo might say. It's like saying "gets?" or "understood?" with a bit of a formal, old-school flair. "O, ang mga bilin ko, intendido?" It’s the verbal equivalent of a firm, knowing nod.
usage_notes: Madalas ginagamit bilang tanong na "Intendido?" (Naiintindihan ba?). Medyo luma na ang tunog nito at bihirang gamitin sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Intendido** ba ang lahat ng aking sinabi?","translation":"Is everything I said **understood**?"},{"sentence":"Matapos ang mahabang paliwanagan, sa wakas ay naging **intendido** rin ang lahat.","translation":"After the long explanation, everything was finally **understood**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang seremonya o ritwal ng paggawad ng banal na pabor, pagpapala, o pagtatalaga sa isang tao, bagay, o lugar.
original_explanation: It's what the priest does to your new car with holy water so you don't get into an accident. It's also what your lola does when you 'mano po' before you leave the house. Pagbabasbas is the official spiritual seal of approval.
usage_notes: Primarily used in a religious or spiritual context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isinagawa ang **pagbabasbas** ng bagong tayong gusali ng paaralan.","translation":"The **blessing** of the newly constructed school building was performed."},{"sentence":"Humingi siya ng **pagbabasbas** mula sa kanyang mga magulang bago siya ikinasal.","translation":"She asked for a **blessing** from her parents before she got married."}]

translation: to retrieve from water; to lift from a lower position
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-angat o pagkuha ng isang bagay mula sa pagkakababad sa tubig, sa pagkakabaon sa lupa, o mula sa isang mababang lugar.
original_explanation: That moment of truth when you pull your laundry from the washing machine, hoping you didn't mix the whites with the reds. Or when you're fishing and you finally pull something out of the water—could be a fish, could be an old boot. It's the 'angat' moment from any 'lubog' situation.
usage_notes: 'Ahon' is the root word, meaning to go up or ascend, especially from water or a low place. 'Ahunan' is the object-focus verb form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **ahunan** ang mga damit na nakababad sa batya.","translation":"Help me **retrieve** the clothes soaking in the basin."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan nilang **ahunan** ang lumubog na bangka.","translation":"They tried **to retrieve** the sunken boat."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o akto ng pagkontrol, pagsakop, o pag-angkin sa isang lugar, bansa, o teritoryo sa pamamagitan ng puwersa.
etymology: From the verb 'manakop' (to conquer). The noun is formed via `pan-` + reduplication of the first syllable of the root `sakop`, resulting in `pananakop`.
original_explanation: Think of it as the ultimate "hostile takeover" but on a national scale. It's what you study in history class about the Spanish, Americans, and Japanese. Today, it can also feel like the 'pananakop' of K-dramas in our streaming accounts or milk tea shops on every corner.
usage_notes: Primarily used in historical and political contexts to refer to the subjugation of one territory or people by another.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan sa kasaysayan ang epekto ng **pananakop** ng mga Espanyol sa Pilipinas.","translation":"The effects of the Spanish **colonization** in the Philippines are studied in history."},{"sentence":"Ang paglaban sa dayuhang **pananakop** ay tanda ng pagmamahal sa bayan.","translation":"Resisting foreign **invasion** is a sign of love for one's country."}]

translation: to cement; to cover with cement
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay o pagpapahid ng semento sa isang ibabaw o lugar.
original_explanation: The act of making something permanent, whether it's your driveway or your feelings. "Bes, sementuhan mo na yang puso mo para 'di na siya makabalik." In construction, it's making the floor smooth. In life, it's making sure your ex can't find a way back in.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang pandiwang banghay sa anyong 'object-focus'. Ang 'sinementuhan' (past), 'sinesementuhan' (present), at 'sesementuhan' (future) ay mga karaniwang anyo nito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Balak naming **sementuhan** ang garahe sa susunod na buwan.","translation":"We plan **to cement** the garage next month."},{"sentence":"Dahan-dahan mong **sementuhan** ang mga siwang para siguradong matibay.","translation":"Slowly **cover the cracks with cement** to ensure it's sturdy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghiling na timbangin ang isang bagay.
etymology: From pa- prefix indicating causation/request + timbang (weight).
original_explanation: Classic palengke or supermarket line. "Ate, **patimbang** nga po ng isang kilong baboy." It's the magic word to get the vendor to put your chosen goods on the weighing scale. Also used figuratively, like when you're asking friends to weigh in on a decision. "Guys, **patimbang** naman, jowain o trabaho?"
usage_notes: Often used as a command or request. The full verb form is `magpatimbang` or `ipatimba`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Patimbang** po ng dalawang kilong bigas.","translation":"**Please weigh** two kilos of rice."},{"sentence":"Pumunta siya sa health center para **magpatimbang**.","translation":"She went to the health center to **get weighed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kalagayan ng pagiging tuyo o wala nang katas matapos pigaan; lubos na naubos.
etymology: Mula sa 'piga' (squeeze). Ang hulaping -s ay isang karaniwang pagbabago sa ilang salitang Tagalog upang ipahiwatig ang resulta.
original_explanation: Kung ang 'piga' ay ang proseso, ang **pigis** ay ang resulta. Ito 'yung itsura ng wallet mo a day before sweldo. **Pigis** na. Walang-wala na. It's that feeling of being completely drained—emotionally, physically, financially. "After five straight days of OT, my brain is **pigis**."
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa matalinghagang paraan na nangangahulugang pagod na pagod o wala nang maibibigay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pigis** na ang mga damit nang alisin niya sa sampayan.","translation":"The clothes were already **wrung out** dry when she took them from the clothesline."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam ko ay **pigis** na ang utak ko matapos ang eksamen.","translation":"I feel like my brain is completely **squeezed dry** after the exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng paghingi ng tulong pinansyal, pagkain, o anumang bagay mula sa iba, karaniwan dahil sa kahirapan.
etymology: From `magpa-` (prefix meaning 'to ask for') and `limos` (alms), which is from Spanish 'limosna' (alms).
original_explanation: Literally, to beg. But in modern Pinoy context, it's also what you're doing when you send a GCash request to your friend for that ₱50 they owe you from three months ago. Or when you give your parents the 'paawa' eyes for extra baon. It's the act of asking for something, usually small, with a hint of desperation.
usage_notes: While the formal meaning is to beg for alms, it's often used hyperbolically among friends and family to mean asking for small favors or money.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napilitan siyang **magpalimos** sa kalye upang may maipakain sa kanyang mga anak.","translation":"He was forced **to beg** on the streets to feed his children."},{"sentence":"Para kang nagpa-**palimos** ng atensyon sa bawat post mo sa social media.","translation":"It's like you're **begging** for attention with every post you make on social media."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paraang tago, lihim, o hindi lantad sa kaalaman ng iba.
