original_explanation: This is how you eat the last piece of leche flan from the fridge at 2 AM, hoping no one finds out. It's the "pasimpleng sulyap" sa crush. Basically, any move you make that's "on the down low" or "under the radar."
usage_notes: Implies an action done without the knowledge of others, often with a hint of secrecy or even deception.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-usap sila nang **palingid** upang walang makarinig.","translation":"They talked **secretly** so no one would hear."},{"sentence":"**Palingid** niyang sinulyapan ang kanyang katabi sa pagsusulit.","translation":"He **stealthily** glanced at the person beside him during the exam."}]

translation: falsity; mendacity; state of being a liar
meaning_filipino: Ang katangian o kalagayan ng pagiging hindi totoo, sinungaling, o mapanlinlang.
original_explanation: This is the very essence of 'I'm on my way' when you're still in the shower. It's the 'Okay lang ako' when you're definitely not okay. It's the core characteristic of that friend who says 'libre kita' but always 'forgets' their wallet. The pure, unadulterated state of being a sinungaling.
usage_notes: Isang abstract noun na tumutukoy sa mismong katangian ng kasinungalingan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahayag sa korte ang **pagkabulaan** ng kanyang mga testimonya.","translation":"The **falsity** of his testimonies was revealed in court."},{"sentence":"Sa kabila ng ebidensya, iginiit pa rin niya ang kanyang **pagkabulaan**.","translation":"Despite the evidence, he still insisted on his **mendacity**."}]

translation: to be able to haul; to be transported (in bulk)
meaning_filipino: Magawang madala o maisakay ang maramihang bagay, tao, o kagamitan mula sa isang lugar patungo sa iba.
original_explanation: The official verb for 'Lipat Bahay' day, when you realize you own too much stuff. Also applies to hoarding during a 12.12 sale, or when a bus conductor tries to fit 100 people in a 50-seater bus ('Paki-usog lang po!'). If it can be moved en masse, it can be 'mahakot'.
usage_notes: Nangangahulugan ng paglipat ng malaking bilang o bulto ng isang bagay. Ito ay isang pandiwang nagpapahayag ng kakayahan (ma-).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng malaking trak para **mahakot** lahat ng gamit sa isang byahe lang.","translation":"We need a big truck to **be able to haul** all the things in just one trip."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o gusali kung saan ikinukulong ang mga taong nagkasala sa batas; bilangguan.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'timeout' corner for adults. Where you end up if you get caught in a 'buy-bust' operation in teleseryes. The final destination after 'Huli ka!'.
usage_notes: A common, slightly informal term for jail.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa **kalaboso** ang bagsak ng mga magnanakaw.","translation":"Thieves will end up in **jail**."},{"sentence":"Ikinulong siya sa **kalaboso** dahil sa kanyang mga kasalanan.","translation":"He was put in **jail** for his crimes."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdaan sa isang sitwasyon, karaniwan ay isang pagsubok, hirap, o mahalagang pangyayari.
original_explanation: What you tell your friend who's going through a tough breakup: "Kailangan mong magdanas ng sakit para matuto." It's to go through something, usually the hard stuff like heartbreaks, 5-hour traffic on EDSA, or a slow internet connection during a final exam. Character development, basically.
usage_notes: Often implies experiencing something difficult or significant, but can be neutral. 'Maranasan' is a more common conjugated form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lahat tayo ay kailangang **magdanas** ng mga pagsubok sa buhay.","translation":"All of us have to **undergo** trials in life."},{"sentence":"Sana hindi mo na maranasan ang hirap na aking **dinanas**.","translation":"I hope you don't experience the hardship that I **went through**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking uri ng lambat na ginagamit sa pangingisda, karaniwang hinihila ng dalawang bangka o mula sa dalampasigan upang makahuli ng maraming isda.
original_explanation: This isn't your tito's weekend fishing net. This is the 'go big or go home' net. A 'pukot' is a massive net that catches fish by the school, not one by one. It's the fishing equivalent of 'sana all.' In police lingo, a 'dragnet operation' can also be called 'operasyong pukot.'
usage_notes: Also used metaphorically for operations designed to catch many people at once, like a police dragnet.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumagamit ng **pukot** ang mga mangingisda para sa maramihang huli.","translation":"The fishermen use a **dragnet** for a large catch."},{"sentence":"Ipinagbawal ang paggamit ng **pukot** sa ilang santuwaryong-dagat upang maprotektahan ang mga korales.","translation":"The use of **dragnets** is prohibited in some marine sanctuaries to protect the corals."}]

translation: to speak to someone, to address someone
meaning_filipino: Ang pakikipag-usap o pagbigkas ng salita sa isang tao; kausapin.
original_explanation: This is a less common verb for "to talk to someone." Parang 'yung ginagawa ng boss mo kapag may mali ka sa report, he will salitan you. It's like 'kausapin' but feels a bit more formal or even confrontational. "I need to have a word with you."
usage_notes: The stress is on the last syllable: sa-li-TAN. This is a directional verb, indicating who is being spoken to.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **salitan** nang ganyan.","translation":"Don't **speak to** me like that."},{"sentence":"**Sinulitan** siya ng kanyang ina tungkol sa kanyang mga grado.","translation":"His mother **spoke to** him about his grades."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang rehiyon ng Daigdig na nakapalibot sa ekwador, na nasa pagitan ng Tropiko ng Kanser sa hilagang hemispero at Tropiko ng Kaprikorn sa timog hemispero.
original_explanation: Ito yung "zone" kung nasaan ang Pilipinas. Isipin mo na lang, ito yung VIP section ng Earth kung saan laging summer party. Dito mo mahahanap ang best beaches, pinakamasasarap na prutas, at ang walang katapusang reklamo na "Ang init!"
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa heograpikal na lokasyon. Ang "tropikal" ay ang pang-uri na naglalarawan dito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatira tayo sa **tropiko**, kaya sanay tayo sa mainit na panahon.","translation":"We live in the **tropics**, so we are used to hot weather."},{"sentence":"Ang mga bansa sa **tropiko** ay sagana sa likas na yaman.","translation":"Countries in the **tropics** are rich in natural resources."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang patag na bahagi sa ilalim ng bintana, na karaniwang ginagamit na patungan ng mga palamuti o halaman.
original_explanation: 'Yung ledge sa bintana kung saan mo pinapatong 'yung mga succulents mo na namamatay pa rin, or 'yung pusa mong mahilig tumunganga at mag-judge ng mga dumadaan. It's the balcony for your flowerpots and the stage for your cat's daily neighborhood watch.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May nakapatong na mga paso ng halaman sa **pasimano**.","translation":"There are pots of plants placed on the **windowsill**."},{"sentence":"Umupo ang pusa sa **pasimano** at nagbilad sa araw.","translation":"The cat sat on the **windowsill** and sunbathed."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang pambata para sa gatas, o tumutukoy din sa suso ng ina o sa bote ng gatas.
original_explanation: The universal code word for milk when you're a baby, or what you call the source of that milk. It's the first thing you ever 'ordered' in your life. 'Umiiyak si baby, gusto na mag-dede.'
usage_notes: Primarily used as baby talk or in informal contexts when referring to feeding a baby. Can also informally refer to the breast.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ihanda mo na ang **dede** ng bata, baka magising at umiyak.","translation":"Prepare the baby's **milk**, he might wake up and cry."},{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang dumede sa bote, gusto niya sa **dede** ng nanay niya.","translation":"He doesn't want to drink from the bottle, he wants his mother's **breast**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamaliit na yunit ng materya na bumubuo sa isang kemikal na elemento.
original_explanation: "Atomo" is what your science teacher tried to explain in high school. It's that super tiny building block of everything. You, your phone, the sisig you ate for lunch – lahat 'yan gawa sa "atomo". It's so small you can't see it, but a whole bunch of them together makes up the universe. Mind-blowing, 'di ba?
usage_notes: A scientific term borrowed from Spanish.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang isang molekula ng tubig ay binubuo ng dalawang **atomo** ng hydrogen at isang **atomo** ng oxygen.","translation":"A water molecule is composed of two **atoms** of hydrogen and one **atom** of oxygen."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng mga siyentipiko ang estruktura ng **atomo**.","translation":"Scientists study the structure of the **atom**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng sintetikong materyal na magaan, matibay, at maaaring hubugin sa iba't ibang anyo, karaniwang ginagamit sa paggawa ng mga lalagyan, supot, at iba pang kagamitan.
original_explanation: The default packaging for everything from your suka at the sari-sari store to your online shopping haul. It's the 'labo' (clear) or 'sando' bag you ask for at the palengke. Also, the main villain in every beach cleanup drive.
usage_notes: Refers to the physical material.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakilagay na lang sa **plastik** ang mga pinamili ko.","translation":"Please just put my groceries in a **plastic** bag."},{"sentence":"Ang mga bote ng softdrinks ay gawa sa **plastik**.","translation":"The softdrink bottles are made of **plastic**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang patalim na parang punyal o kutsilyo na ikinakabit sa dulo ng baril o riple para magamit sa malapitang labanan.
original_explanation: That pointy knife you attach to the end of a rifle. You see it in old war movies and historical reenactments. It's for when you run out of bullets and have to get 'up close and personal.' Basically, it turns your gun into a spear. Not something you see at the palengke.
usage_notes: A loanword from Spanish. The English spelling 'bayonet' is also understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ikinabit ng sundalo ang **bayoneta** sa kanyang riple.","translation":"The soldier attached the **bayonet** to his rifle."},{"sentence":"Ang mga lumang sandata ay may kasamang **bayoneta** para sa mano-manong labanan.","translation":"The old weapons came with a **bayonet** for hand-to-hand combat."}]

translation: to gain weight; to become plump
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagdagdag ng timbang o paglaki ng katawan, na karaniwang nagreresulta sa pagiging mas mabilog o mataba.
original_explanation: What happens after a month of non-stop Christmas parties and Noche Buena. 'Uy, nangangatawan ka!' is a classic Tita greeting that's 50% compliment ('You look healthy!') and 50% observation ('You got fat.'). It's the opposite of 'mangayayat'.
usage_notes: Generally implies a noticeable and significant weight gain, often viewed as becoming healthier or more robust, though it can also mean getting fat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Simula nang mag-asawa siya, halatang **nangatawan** siya dahil masarap magluto ang kanyang misis.","translation":"Ever since he got married, he noticeably **gained weight** because his wife is a good cook."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng karakter sa isang kuwento na masama ang ugali at kalaban ng pangunahing tauhan.
original_explanation: The female kontrabida in your favorite teleserye. Siya yung laging may hawak na baso ng red wine, mayaman, at laging may planong masama laban sa bida. Think Valentina, Selina (from Mara Clara), or yung officemate mong mahilig manira sa SMM.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng panitikan, pelikula, at teatro.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang galing gumanap ng aktres bilang isang **bilyaka**.","translation":"The actress is great at portraying a **villainess**."},{"sentence":"Sa bawat kuwento, laging may isang **bilyaka** na gumugulo sa buhay ng bida.","translation":"In every story, there is always a **villainess** who makes the protagonist's life difficult."}]

translation: to be able to be buried
meaning_filipino: Maidaos ang seremonya ng paglilibing; maihatid sa huling hantungan ang isang yumao.
original_explanation: A heavy but practical word. In the Philippines, this is a major community affair. When someone passes away, the whole barangay chips in ('abuloy') to ensure the family can afford the funeral, so their loved one can **mapalibing** with dignity. It's about giving a proper and respectful farewell.
usage_notes: Refers to the act and process of burial, often including the financial and logistical aspects.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglilimos ang pamilya upang **mapalibing** nila nang maayos ang kanilang yumaong ama.","translation":"The family is asking for donations so they can **properly bury** their deceased father."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa tulong ng mga kapitbahay, sa wakas ay **naipalibing** na si Lolo Berto.","translation":"Thanks to the help of the neighbors, Grandpa Berto was finally **able to be buried**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ikalawa sa pinakamalaking pulo sa Pilipinas at isa sa tatlong pangunahing pangkat ng mga pulo sa bansa, kasama ang Luzon at Visayas. Kilala rin ito bilang 'Lupang Pangako'.
etymology: Named after the Maguindanaon people, from 'maginged' (people) and 'danaw' (lake), meaning 'people of the lake'.
original_explanation: The 'Land of Promise' of the Philippines. It's that massive island down south on the map that's culturally rich, has amazing beaches, great coffee, and the majestic Philippine Eagle. It's more than just the headlines, it's a whole vibe of its own.
usage_notes: Always capitalized as it is a proper noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming magagandang tanawin sa **Mindanao**.","translation":"There are many beautiful sights in **Mindanao**."},{"sentence":"Nagmula ang prutas na durian sa isla ng **Mindanao**.","translation":"The durian fruit originates from the island of **Mindanao**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan na may maliliit na hibla na ginagamit kasama ng toothpaste upang linisin ang mga ngipin.
original_explanation: The one thing your dentist wishes you'd use more often. That essential tool for getting rid of coffee breath before a meeting or garlic breath after eating your lola's adobo. Also, the thing you always forget to pack on a trip.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng bagong **sipilyo** sa tindahan.","translation":"I bought a new **toothbrush** at the store."},{"sentence":"Nasa banyo ang **sipilyo** at toothpaste.","translation":"The **toothbrush** and toothpaste are in the bathroom."}]

translation: state of being lame or crippled; lameness
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkakaroon ng kapansanan sa paglalakad, karaniwan dahil sa pinsala sa paa o binti.
etymology: Mula sa ugat na "pilay" (lumpo, may kapansanan sa paglakad). Ang unlaping "pagka-" ay nagpapahiwatig ng estado o kondisyon.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling pagkatapos mong mag-leg day sa gym for the first time in months. The **pagkapilay** is temporary but feels eternal. O kapag sinubukan mong magsuot ng 5-inch heels sa isang party at kailangan mong maglakad pauwi.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa isang pansamantala o permanenteng kondisyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagkapilay** ay dahil sa pagkahulog niya sa hagdan.","translation":"His **lameness** is because he fell down the stairs."},{"sentence":"Ginamot niya ang pansamantalang **pagkapilay** ng kabayo.","translation":"He treated the horse's temporary **state of being lame**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang hanapbuhay ay ang pagtatanim at pag-aalaga ng mga halaman sa bukid.
original_explanation: More formal than just 'magsasaka'. This is the person who wakes up before the sun to feed the nation. They're the original 'plantito/plantita', but for survival, not just for aesthetics. They're the reason you have rice on your plate.
usage_notes: Bagaman tama, mas karaniwan ang paggamit ng 'magsasaka' sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **tagapagsaka** ay itinuturing na bayani ng ating ekonomiya.","translation":"The **farmers** are considered heroes of our economy."},{"sentence":"Maraming programa ang gobyerno para sa maliliit na **tagapagsaka**.","translation":"The government has many programs for small-scale **farmers**."}]

translation: act of being swarmed or flocked to
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagiging puntahan o pagtitipunan ng napakaraming tao nang sabay-sabay.
original_explanation: This is what happens to a celebrity during a mall show, or to a popular food stall in a weekend market. The place becomes the destination. The verb form 'dagsain' is more common, like 'Dagsain tayo ng mga customer!' (We will be swarmed by customers!).
usage_notes: This noun form is less common than the verb form 'dagsain' (to be swarmed) or the noun 'pagdagsa' (the act of swarming). It specifically refers to the act of a place being swarmed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagdagsaan** sa bagong bukas na tindahan ay nagdulot ng trapiko.","translation":"The **act of being swarmed** at the newly opened store caused traffic."},{"sentence":"Handa na ba kayo sa **pagdagsaan** ng mga turista ngayong tag-init?","translation":"Are you ready for the **flocking** of tourists this summer?"}]

translation: to be found out; to be exposed
meaning_filipino: Mahuli o malaman ang isang lihim, kasinungalingan, o itinatagong gawain.
original_explanation: That mini heart attack when you're talking about someone and they suddenly appear behind you. Or when your boss sees your screen and you have to switch from Shopee to your spreadsheet in 0.2 seconds. It's the 'Huli, pero 'di kulong' moment of your life.
usage_notes: This is distinct from 'buko' (young coconut). The root 'buko' in this context, meaning 'to be found out', is rarely used alone and almost always appears with the 'ma-' prefix.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Takot siyang **mabuko** ng kanyang mga magulang na may kasintahan na siya.","translation":"She's afraid **to be found out** by her parents that she already has a boyfriend."},{"sentence":"Sa huli, **nabuko** rin ang kanilang lihim na relasyon.","translation":"In the end, their secret relationship **was exposed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay, tao, o halaga na maliit, hindi mahalaga, o mababa ang kalidad.
etymology: From a colloquial understanding of 'pitsa' (a coin of small value), with the diminutive/pejorative suffix '-in'.
original_explanation: Eto yung sinasabi mo sa kalaban mo sa Mobile Legends na akala mo magaling, pero 'di naman pala. O kaya yung project na binigay sa'yo na ang budget, pang-isang kape lang. "Pipitsugin lang 'yan!" means it's easy money, not a real challenge.
usage_notes: Often used in a derogatory or dismissive way to belittle something or someone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong maliitin ang kalaban, kahit mukha siyang **pipitsugin**.","translation":"Don't underestimate the opponent, even if they look **small-time**."},{"sentence":"Barya lang ba ang tingin mo sa akin? **Pipitsugin** ba ang halaga ko sa'yo?","translation":"Do you just see me as loose change? Is my worth to you that **insignificant**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtulo o paglaglag nang paisa-isang butil ng likido.
original_explanation: That sound from a leaky faucet that keeps you up at night. The first few drops of rain that make you run for cover. The 'piso-piso' payment plan for your utang. It's the slow, steady, sometimes annoying, drip... drip... drip.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **pagpatak** ng ulan sa aming bubong.","translation":"I heard the **dripping** of the rain on our roof."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang landas na walang liko o balakid; sa metaporikal na kahulugan, isang buhay na matapat, tama, at walang katiwalian.
original_explanation: The "straight path" famously used in politics. It's the ideal road of honesty and good governance that everyone promises to take during elections. In real life, it’s that rare, glorious moment on SLEX when there are no cars, no construction, and you can just drive straight. A beautiful, often mythical, concept.
usage_notes: Carries a strong moral and ethical connotation, often used in political or religious discourse.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang panunungkulan ay nakatuon sa **daang tuwiran**.","translation":"His term in office was focused on the **straight path** (of righteousness)."},{"sentence":"Mahirap manatili sa **daang tuwiran**, ngunit ito ang tama.","translation":"It is difficult to remain on the **straight path**, but it is the right thing to do."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit na paglubog ng dulo ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay pagkain, sa isang likido o sarsa.
original_explanation: That satisfying moment when you repeatedly dip your chicharon into the vinegar. It's not just a single dip ('sawsaw'), it's a dedicated, rhythmic dipping session. Think of it as giving your food a little bath in flavor before you eat it.
usage_notes: Often confused with 'pagsawsaw', which is a single act of dipping. 'Pagtitiltil' implies a repeated action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sarap ng **pagtitiltil** niya ng mangga sa bagoong.","translation":"The way he **dips** his mango into the shrimp paste is so satisfying."},{"sentence":"Huwag masyadong magtagal sa **pagtitiltil** ng tinapay sa kape, baka lumubog.","translation":"Don't take too long **dipping** the bread in the coffee, it might sink."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong ang hanapbuhay ay ang paggawa o pagkukumpuni ng mga bagay na yari sa kahoy, tulad ng bahay, kasangkapan, at iba pang istruktura.
etymology: Posibleng hango sa salitang Kapampangan na 'aluagi' na may parehong kahulugan.
original_explanation: The OG "Mr. Fix-It" of the wood world. Sila 'yung gumagawa ng mga lamesa, silya, at aparador na pagmamay-ari pa ng lola mo. Think of them as the anluwage's more common cousin.
usage_notes: Ang salitang 'karpintero' (mula sa Espanyol) ay mas karaniwang ginagamit sa modernong Tagalog. Ang 'alwagi' ay naiintindihan pa rin ngunit hindi na gaanong ginagamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating tumawag ng mahusay na **alwagi** para ayusin ang sirang pinto.","translation":"We need to call a good **carpenter** to fix the broken door."},{"sentence":"Ang tatay ko ay isang **alwagi** sa aming probinsya.","translation":"My father is a **carpenter** in our province."}]

translation: to implement, to enforce, to execute
meaning_filipino: Isakatuparan o ipasunod ang isang batas, regulasyon, o plano.
original_explanation: This is the government's job after they announce a new rule, like the "Bawal Ang Maarte" ordinance. They have to `magpatupad` it. It's the difference between a plan on paper and a plan in action. Your office HR trying to `magpatupad` the 'return to office' policy is a prime example.
usage_notes: Commonly used in the context of laws, rules, policies, and plans.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pulisya ang naatasang **magpatupad** ng bagong batas trapiko.","translation":"The police are tasked to **enforce** the new traffic law."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **magpatupad** ng isang proyekto kung kulang sa pondo.","translation":"It's difficult to **implement** a project if it lacks funds."}]

translation: to try; to test; to sample
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa ng isang bagay upang malaman ang kalidad, bisa, o resulta nito; ang pagsubok sa lasa ng pagkain o ang pagsuot ng damit upang makita kung ito ay kasya.
original_explanation: "Probahan mo 'tong adobo ko!" is the ultimate test of friendship. It's the moment of truth before you commit, whether it's food, a new pair of shoes from the ukay-ukay, or a potential jowa. It's the free sample version of life decisions.
usage_notes: Often used for tasting food ('tikman') or trying on clothes ('isukat'). 'Probahan' has a broader sense of testing or trying something out.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Probahan** mo muna ang sapatos bago mo bilhin.","translation":"**Try on** the shoes first before you buy them."},{"sentence":"Gusto kong **probahan** ang bagong Korean restaurant sa kanto.","translation":"I want to **try** the new Korean restaurant on the corner."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat o lupon ng mga sasakyang-dagat, pandigma man o pangkalakalan, na magkakasamang naglalayag sa ilalim ng iisang pamunuan.
original_explanation: Think of it as the barkada of boats. It's a whole squad of ships rolling deep, either for trade (like the Galleons of yore) or for war. Today, you're more likely to see a 'plota' of Grab cars waiting for passengers outside a mall.
usage_notes: Primarily used in historical or military contexts. Not a word used in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **plota** ni Magellan ay binubuo ng limang barko.","translation":"Magellan's **fleet** was composed of five ships."},{"sentence":"Nagpadala ang hukbong-dagat ng isang **plota** sa pinag-aagawang teritoryo.","translation":"The navy sent a **fleet** to the disputed territory."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging labis na nahuhumaling o nalululong sa isang bagay, lalo na sa isang bisyo tulad ng droga, alak, o pagsusugal, na umaabot sa puntong nakakasama na.
original_explanation: Yung friend mo na hindi na natutulog dahil sa Mobile Legends o yung tita mong hindi makaalis sa casino. It's being hooked on something so bad it becomes your life's toxic, full-time job. From K-dramas to online shopping, we all have that one thing that makes us a little bit 'sugapa'.
usage_notes: May matinding negatibong konotasyon, kadalasang tumutukoy sa mapanirang pagka-adik.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **sugapa** siya sa paglalaro ng video games kaya napabayaan niya ang pag-aaral.","translation":"He became **addicted** to playing video games, so he neglected his studies."},{"sentence":"Maraming pamilya ang nasisira dahil sa pagiging **sugapa** sa sugal.","translation":"Many families are destroyed because of being **obsessed** with gambling."}]

meaning_filipino: Bawasan ang tapang o konsentrasyon ng isang likido sa pamamagitan ng pagdaragdag ng tubig o ibang pampalabnaw.
original_explanation: What you do to the instant coffee when it's too strong, or to the shampoo when you're on the last few drops but payday is still a week away. "Lagyan mo ng tubig para dumami." It's the art of stretching a resource, a classic Filipino life hack.
usage_notes: Primarily used for liquids.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **palabnawin** ang pintura bago ito gamitin.","translation":"You need **to dilute** the paint before using it."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng paggamit ng mahika o kapangyarihang sobrenatural upang makasakit, makontrol, o magdulot ng kamalasan sa ibang tao, na karaniwang iniuugnay sa isang manggagaway.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'cancel culture'. Bago pa mag-block sa social media, mayroon nang panggagaway. Kapag may kaaway ka, hindi mo siya i-ra-rant post, kukuha ka ng manika at karayom. It's the dark magic version of 'I'll make you regret it.'
usage_notes: Strongly associated with Philippine folklore and superstition.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinabintangan siyang nagsasagawa ng **panggagaway** sa kanyang kaaway.","translation":"She was accused of performing **sorcery** on her enemy."},{"sentence":"Ang kuwento ng **panggagaway** ay kinatatakutan sa kanilang baryo.","translation":"The story of **bewitchment** is feared in their village."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lamat o siwang sa isang matigas na bagay na sanhi ng pagkabagsak, pagtama, o puwersa.
original_explanation: The sound your mom hears from the kitchen that makes her yell your full name. It's the literal crack in the pavement you try to avoid, or the metaphorical basag in a friendship after a big fight.
usage_notes: Refers to the crack or fracture itself, as opposed to the state of being cracked.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **basag** ang screen ng cellphone mo.","translation":"There's a **crack** on your cellphone screen."},{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **basag** ng plato nang mahulog ito.","translation":"I heard the **shatter** of the plate when it fell."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paggamit ng isang matulis na bagay, tulad ng daliri o patpat, upang bahagyang itulak o diinan ang isang bagay o tao.
original_explanation: The 'kulit' move of your younger sibling who won't stop poking you. Or what you do with a stick to see if the fish on the grill is cooked. In basketball, it's a quick jab to steal the ball. In the digital world, it was the old Facebook 'Poke' feature, the original 'seen.'
usage_notes: Can be playful, annoying, or functional depending on context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natigil sa pagtulog ang bata dahil sa **pagsundot** ng kanyang kapatid.","translation":"The child's sleep was interrupted by his sibling's **poking**."},{"sentence":"Isang mahinang **pagsundot** lang sa fishball ay sapat na para makuha ito.","translation":"Just one gentle **poke** at the fishball is enough to get it."}]

translation: hard-earned thing; object of one's labor
meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, layunin, o gantimpala na pinagtutuunan ng matinding pagsisikap, pagod, at sakripisyo upang makamit o matamo.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung sahod mo na parang bula kung maglaho, pero dugo't pawis ang naging puhunan. The reason for your overtime, eyebags, and endless coffee refills. It's not just money; it can also be your degree, your 'body goals', or your jowa's approval. Basically, the 'hard' in 'work hard, play hard'.
usage_notes: Often used to emphasize the value of something due to the difficulty in obtaining it. It is the object form of the verb 'paghirapan' in the progressive aspect.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong sayangin ang perang iyan dahil **pinagkakahirapan** ko ang bawat sentimo.","translation":"Don't waste that money because I **work hard for** every centavo."},{"sentence":"Ang diploma na ito ang bunga ng lahat ng aking **pinagkakahirapan** sa loob ng apat na taon.","translation":"This diploma is the fruit of everything I **worked hard for** in four years."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na kayang magtiis ng sakit o hirap nang hindi nagpapakita ng emosyon o nagrereklamo.
original_explanation: Yung lolo mo na kahit anong problema, kalmado lang. O yung BPO agent na kahit sinisigawan na ng irate customer, ang sagot ay "I understand your frustration, ma'am/sir" with a deadpan voice. Emotionally unbothered. Poker face level: expert.
usage_notes: Gender-neutral sa modernong paggamit, bagaman nagmula sa pambabaeng anyo sa Espanyol.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nanatiling **istoika** ang kanyang mukha sa kabila ng masamang balita.","translation":"Her face remained **stoic** despite the bad news."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa pagiging **istoika** at hindi basta-basta nagpapadala sa emosyon.","translation":"He is known for being **stoic** and not easily swayed by emotion."}]

meaning_filipino: Itiklop paitaas ang dulo ng manggas ng damit o laylayan ng pantalon.
etymology: From the verb-forming prefix `i-` + `lilis` (to roll up).
original_explanation: The action you do before washing the dishes or when the floodwaters start rising. You **ililis** your pants so they don't get wet. It's the universal sign for 'Okay, let's get down to business' or 'Baha na naman, bes.' It's a less common synonym for 'ilislis'.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with `ilislis`, but `ilislis` is more common in modern usage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Inilis** niya ang manggas ng kanyang barong bago magbuhat ng mga kahon.","translation":"He **rolled up** the sleeves of his barong before lifting the boxes."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **ililis** ang iyong pantalon dahil maputik sa labas.","translation":"You need to **roll up** your pants because it's muddy outside."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na para lamang sa, nauugnay sa, o katangian ng isang partikular na lugar o rehiyon.
original_explanation: Basically, the opposite of 'pang-international'. It's for a specific area only. Think 'pampook na balita' (local news) that talks about the new footbridge in your barangay, not global politics. It's your city's specific version of a 'longganisa' or the chismis that only your neighborhood knows.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang balita, pamamahala, o mga paligsahan na limitado sa isang tiyak na heograpikal na lugar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng **pampook** na patimpalak sa pag-awit sa aming bayan.","translation":"There was a **local** singing contest in our town."},{"sentence":"Ang **pampook** na pamahalaan ang nangangasiwa sa proyektong ito.","translation":"The **local** government is managing this project."}]

translation: to use a two-way radio; to broadcast on the radio
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggamit ng radyo, partikular ang isang two-way radio (walkie-talkie), upang makipag-ugnayan o maghatid ng mensahe. Maaari ring tumukoy sa pag-ere sa radyo.
etymology: Mula sa salitang 'radyo' (mula sa Espanyol 'radio') + panlaping '-um-'.
original_explanation: From the root word 'radyo' (radio). This is what security guards, event organizers, and traffic enforcers do with their walkie-talkies. 'Alpha to Bravo, paki-check ng parking, over!' It can also mean to broadcast something on AM/FM radio, like when a breaking news story rumadyo across the nation. It's the OG way of sending a group message before Viber or Telegram existed.
usage_notes: Madalas na tumutukoy sa paggamit ng two-way radio.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Rumadyo** agad ang guwardiya sa kanyang mga kasama nang makita ang magnanakaw.","translation":"The guard immediately **radioed** his companions when he saw the thief."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **rumadyo** sa base para humingi ng tulong.","translation":"We need to **use the radio** to call base for help."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagyuko, pagbaluktot, o pag-urong ng katawan dahil sa matinding takot, hiya, o panliliit.
original_explanation: The feeling when you accidentally send a 'for your eyes only' message to the group chat. You just want to curl up into a little ball and disappear. That's the feeling of 'sumukot'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumukot** sa isang tabi ang aso nang marinig ang malakas na kulog.","translation":"The dog **cowered** in a corner when it heard the loud thunder."},{"sentence":"Nahihiya siyang humarap kaya **sumukot** na lang siya sa likod ng pinto.","translation":"He was too shy to face them so he just **crouched** behind the door."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kumpetisyon o kasunduan na paikliin ang isang bagay, tulad ng salaysay, pangalan, o ruta.
original_explanation: Parang laro sa group chat. "Okay guys, paiklian tayo ng pangalan ng movie." Or when you and your friend are telling the same long story to someone else and you say, "Paiklian na lang natin, bes."
usage_notes: This is a social verb form (-an suffix) implying a reciprocal or collective action. It's less common than 'paikliin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-usap ang magkapatid na **paiklian** na lang ang kanilang mga kuwento para hindi mainip ang mga bisita.","translation":"The siblings agreed **to shorten** each other's stories so the guests wouldn't get bored."},{"sentence":"\"Maglaro tayo ng **paiklian** ng mga pamagat ng kanta,\" mungkahi niya.","translation":"\"Let's play a game of **shortening** song titles,\" she suggested."}]

meaning_filipino: Dalawang supling na sabay na ipinanganak mula sa iisang pagbubuntis. Maaari ring tumukoy sa dalawang bagay na magkatulad na magkatulad.
original_explanation: The original "copy-paste." Yung laging tinatanong, "Sino si A at sino si B?" at napagpapalit ng mga tita. They have this secret telepathy na sila lang ang nakakaintindi. Minsan, parang may built-in best friend ka na, minsan naman, may kaagaw ka sa lahat ng bagay since birth.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pangngalan (hal., 'ang kambal') o pang-uri (hal., 'kambal na saging').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkamukhang-magkamukha ang **kambal** na sina Ana at Ani.","translation":"The **twins**, Ana and Ani, look very much alike."},{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng **kambal** na saging sa palengke.","translation":"I bought a **twin** banana (two bananas fused together) at the market."}]

translation: a contest of durability or strength
meaning_filipino: Isang paligsahan ng katatagan, tibay, o tatag, pisikal man o emosyonal.
etymology: From `pa-` + `tibay` + `-an`. The `-an` suffix denotes a place or event of action.
original_explanation: A showdown of endurance. Think "Patibayan ng aTAY" during an inuman session, or "patibayan ng pamilya" during a teleserye finale. It's the ultimate test of "Sino'ng mas matatag?"
usage_notes: Often used to describe a competition, whether formal or informal, that tests strength, endurance, or resilience.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **patibayan** ng loob ang kanilang pagsubok sa buhay.","translation":"Their life trials became a **test of fortitude**."},{"sentence":"Sumali sila sa **patibayan** ng pag-inom sa piyesta.","translation":"They joined the drinking **contest** at the festival."}]

meaning_filipino: (Balbal) Isang lalaking tanyag o kinikilala bilang pangunahing halimbawa ng kulturang "kanal," partikular sa pag-uugali, panlasa, o komedya.
etymology: Combination of Tagalog 'kanal' (gutter, low-brow) and English 'king'.
original_explanation: The guy who is the undisputed champion of all things 'kanal'. He's the master of green jokes, the icon of jologs fashion, and the face of a thousand relatable 'nagkamali ng send' memes. He's not trying to be classy; he's owning his 'kalye' credibility.
usage_notes: A title, often bestowed ironically or as a term of endearment within a specific community.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa mga video niya, tinagurian siyang **Kanal King** ng internet.","translation":"Because of his videos, he was dubbed the **Kanal King** of the internet."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng kikil upang pakinisin, hubugin, o bawasan ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: 'Yung action na ginagawa mo sa kuko mo bago ka mag-nail polish para pantay. O 'yung ginagawa ng karpintero sa kahoy para mag-fit sa frame. It's the verb form of making something 'smooth'. "Bes, kikilin ko lang 'tong mga rough edges ng life ko, charot!"
usage_notes: This is the object-focused verb form related to 'kikil' (the tool). The actor-focused form is 'kumikil'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **kikilin** ang dulo ng tubo para magkasya.","translation":"You need **to file** the end of the pipe so it will fit."},{"sentence":"Dahan-dahan niyang **kinikil** ang alahas upang kuminis.","translation":"He is slowly **filing** the jewelry to make it smooth."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bulwagan o kapulungan ng isang sangay ng lehislatura, tulad ng Mababang Kapulungan o Kamara de Representantes.
original_explanation: This is the 'Marites central' of Philippine politics. It's the House of Representatives, where congressmen and congresswomen (mga 'Tongressman') gather to make laws, deliver privilege speeches, and sometimes, create viral clips. It's one-half of Congress, the other being the Senado.
usage_notes: Often used as a shortened term for "Kamara de Representantes" (House of Representatives).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinagdedebatehan sa **Kamara** ang bagong panukalang batas.","translation":"The new bill is being debated in the **Chamber**."},{"sentence":"Iprinisenta ng kongresista ang kanyang argumento sa plenaryo ng **Kamara**.","translation":"The congressman presented his argument on the plenary floor of the **House**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit at manipis na piraso na natanggal mula sa isang mas malaking piraso, karaniwan ay kahoy.
original_explanation: That tiny piece of wood that gets stuck in your finger when you're trying to be a DIY king/queen. It's the universe's way of telling you to stop. Also, what you call the small pieces of wood you use to start a barbecue fire.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to a small, thin piece broken off a larger object, most commonly wood. 'Salubsob' is a more common synonym for a splinter in one's skin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May pumasok na **tilad** ng kawayan sa aking daliri.","translation":"A **splinter** of bamboo got into my finger."},{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng mga **tilad** ng kahoy para simulan ang apoy.","translation":"He used **slivers** of wood to start the fire."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapaputok ng baril, maaaring tumukoy sa isang insidente ng karahasan, isport, o pagsasanay.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'baril' (gun) at unlaping 'pamama-' na nagsasaad ng kilos o gawain.
original_explanation: Ito yung laging laman ng balita. From action movies to the 6 o'clock news, may eksena ng pamamaril. Pwede ring hobby 'to, like target shooting, pero mas madalas, negative ang connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nabulabog ang buong kapitbahayan dahil sa nangyaring **pamamaril** kagabi.","translation":"The whole neighborhood was disturbed by the **shooting** incident last night."},{"sentence":"Sumali siya sa isang kumpetisyon sa **pamamaril**.","translation":"He joined a **shooting** competition."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paghihiwalay ng butil, tulad ng bigas, mula sa ipa sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng bilao at pagpapahangin dito.
etymology: From `pag-` (prefix) + reduplication of the first syllable of `tahip` (to winnow).
original_explanation: This is a classic 'probinsya life' skill. It's the art of separating the rice from the chaff (ipa) using a 'bilao' (a flat woven basket). You toss the grains in the air with a specific wrist flick, letting the wind blow away the lighter, useless bits. It’s a metaphor for life, really: separating what's important from what's not. The OG way to 'filter' your life before social media even existed.
usage_notes: A traditional agricultural term, often depicted in cultural presentations to represent rural Filipino life. The root `tahip` can also mean 'palpitation', but `pagtatahip` exclusively refers to winnowing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagtatahip** ng palay ay nangangailangan ng kasanayan at tamang hangin.","translation":"The **winnowing** of rice grains requires skill and the right amount of wind."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko si Lola na abala sa **pagtatahip** sa likod-bahay.","translation":"I saw Grandma busy **winnowing** at the backyard."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghugot o pagtanggal ng isang bagay mula sa kinalalagyan nito, o ang pagpili sa pamamagitan ng palabunutan.
original_explanation: This is what you do at the dentist ('bunot ng ngipin'), what you do when you need to remove a stubborn weed, or what happens during the office Christmas party raffle. 'Bunutan na!' is the signal for everyone to hold their breath and hope their name gets picked for the grand prize flat-screen TV.
usage_notes: The verb form is often 'bumunot' (actor-focus) or 'bunutin' (object-focus). The root word 'bunot' is used as a command.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang nakabunot ng nanalong numero sa raffle?","translation":"Who **drew** the winning number in the raffle?"},{"sentence":"Magpa-**bunot** ka na ng masakit mong ngipin.","translation":"Go have your painful tooth **pulled out**."}]

translation: was torn apart; was ripped forcefully
meaning_filipino: Marahas na pinunit o hinati sa pamamagitan ng paghatak mula sa magkabilang dulo.
original_explanation: Imagine a photo of your ex. You don't just gently tear it. You hold both sides and pull with all your hugot and rage until it rips in two. 'Yan, binitad mo. It's more aggressive than 'pinunit'.
usage_notes: Implies a more forceful and often aggressive tearing action compared to "pinunit" (torn) or "ginisi" (torn slightly).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang galit, **binitad** niya ang sulat na naglalaman ng masamang balita.","translation":"In extreme anger, he **forcefully ripped apart** the letter that contained the bad news."},{"sentence":"Para silang mga asong nag-aagawan sa isang pirasong karne na kanilang **binitad**.","translation":"They were like dogs fighting over a piece of meat that they **tore apart**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabago ng kulay tungo sa pula; ang pamumula ng mukha dahil sa hiya, galit, o kilig.
original_explanation: This is your face's reaction when crush says "hi." It's the "kilig" effect in action. It can also be your face turning red from anger (galit) when someone cuts you in line, or your skin getting red from the sun. Basically, your body's built-in "red alert" system.
usage_notes: Can describe blushing, getting angry, or an object turning red.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya napigilang **mamula** nang purihin siya ng kanyang guro.","translation":"She couldn't help but **blush** when her teacher praised her."},{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **mamula** ang pisngi ng bata dahil sa matinding sikat ng araw.","translation":"The child's cheeks started to **turn red** because of the intense heat of the sun."}]

translation: tenth (in a series); for the tenth
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa ikasampu sa pagkakasunod-sunod; pang-bilang na ordinals para sa sampu.
original_explanation: This is the grand finale of a top ten list. Yung feeling na 'And for our tenth and final contestant...' Parang sa 13th month pay, 'pag 10th day na ng December at wala pa, nagiging 'pansampu' na ang araw na hinihintay mo. The last one to complete the set of ten.
usage_notes: 'Pansampu' and 'ikasampu' are often interchangeable, but 'pansampu' can sometimes imply completing a set of ten.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **pansampu** sa pila.","translation":"He is the **tenth** in line."},{"sentence":"Ito na ang **pansampu** kong subok na makapasa sa exam.","translation":"This is my **tenth** attempt to pass the exam."}]

translation: desirous; having a wish or ambition
meaning_filipino: Ang isang tao na may pagnanasa, mithiin, o ambisyon para sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: Eto 'yung friend mong laging nag-a-apply for a promotion o 'yung tita mong laging sumasali sa raffle. Sila 'yung may goal, may gustong maabot. They have that 'eye on the prize' energy.
usage_notes: Describes a person with a strong desire or ambition. It's a more formal way to say 'ambisyoso' but often with a more positive connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bilang isang taong **mayhangad**, hindi siya tumitigil hangga't hindi niya nakukuha ang gusto niya.","translation":"As a **desirous** person, she doesn't stop until she gets what she wants."},{"sentence":"Lahat tayo ay **mayhangad** ng magandang kinabukasan para sa ating pamilya.","translation":"We all **have a desire** for a good future for our family."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging manhid, ngalay, o pulikat ng isang bahagi ng katawan, karaniwan ay dahil sa matagal na pananatili sa isang posisyon.
original_explanation: That feeling when you've been binge-watching a K-drama for 5 hours straight without moving and your leg falls asleep. That tingling, pins-and-needles sensation? 'Yan ang kimay. It's the official state of being for anyone in a long meeting or a cramped bus ride.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin kasama ng 'ngalay' o 'manhid'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **kimay** ang aking mga binti sa haba ng biyahe.","translation":"My legs became **cramped** from the long trip."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang umupo nang ganyan, baka maging **kimay** ang paa mo.","translation":"Don't sit like that, your foot might get **benumbed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng matinding kalungkutan, panghihina ng loob, at kawalan ng pag-asa.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `pan-` (na nagiging `panl-`) + pag-uulit ng unang pantig (`lu`) + salitang-ugat na `lumo` (matinding lungkot).
original_explanation: Eto yung feeling mo after mong makita yung "Sent" sa Messenger tapos naging "Seen" pero walang reply. That deep, soul-crushing sadness na parang naubusan ka ng data sa gitna ng panonood ng K-drama finale. It's the 'sana all' feeling, but make it existential dread.
usage_notes: Isang mas matinding salita para sa kalungkutan, kadalasang tumutukoy sa isang estado ng pagkatao kaysa sa isang panandaliang damdamin lamang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dama sa kanyang mga mata ang **panlulumo** matapos mabalitaan ang masamang nangyari.","translation":"The **dejection** was palpable in his eyes after hearing the bad news."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpatalo sa **panlulumo**; laging may pag-asa.","translation":"Don't let **depression** defeat you; there is always hope."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay o palitan na pag-atake ng dalawa o higit pang panig sa isa't isa.
etymology: From 'atake' + '-an' suffix, indicating reciprocal or locative action.
original_explanation: This is the 'bardagulan' verb. It's not a one-way attack; it's a full-on brawl, a mutual exchange of fire. Think of two groups of fans arguing in a comments section, or your cats suddenly deciding the living room is a wrestling ring. "Nag-atakihan sila!" means the chaos is reciprocal.
usage_notes: The '-an' suffix here denotes reciprocal action. It implies multiple actors attacking each other.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-**atakihan** ang dalawang grupo sa social media.","translation":"The two groups **attacked each other** on social media."},{"sentence":"Huwag kayong mag-**atakihan** ng salita; mag-usap kayo nang maayos.","translation":"Don't **verbally attack each other**; talk to each other properly."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o entidad na nagbibigay ng suportang pinansyal o materyal sa isang tao, kaganapan, o proyekto. Sa kultural na konteksto, tumutukoy din ito sa ninong o ninang sa binyag o kasal.
original_explanation: Has two main flavors in the PH. The wholesome one: your ninong/ninang at your binyag or kasal, who's supposed to be a spiritual guide but is mostly known for giving aguinaldo (Christmas cash). The not-so-wholesome one: the "sponsor" (aka sugar daddy/mommy) who funds a lavish lifestyle in exchange for... well, "companionship." The term can shift from a family gathering to a gossip column topic in a heartbeat.
usage_notes: The meaning is heavily dependent on context. It can refer to a godparent (ninong/ninang), a financial backer for an event, or a sugar daddy/mommy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating maghanap ng **sponsor** para sa ating Christmas party.","translation":"We need to find a **sponsor** for our Christmas party."},{"sentence":"Siya ang kinuha naming **sponsor** sa binyag ng aming anak.","translation":"We chose him as a **godparent** for our child's baptism."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar na laan para sa paglilibing sa mga yumao; sementeryo.
original_explanation: The original 'final resting place.' It's where you visit your ancestors during Undas, armed with candles, flowers, and a deck of cards. It's the one place where everyone's quiet, except for that one tita who's broadcasting the family drama over your lolo's tombstone.
usage_notes: A more traditional or formal term for 'sementeryo.' Often heard in provinces or in literary contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpunta kami sa **kamposanto** noong Araw ng mga Patay.","translation":"We went to the **cemetery** on All Souls' Day."},{"sentence":"Ang lumang **kamposanto** ay sinasabing may mga kababalaghan.","translation":"The old **graveyard** is said to have supernatural occurrences."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-aalis ng dumi o pagpapanumbalik ng kalinisan sa isang bagay o lugar.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'linis' at hulaping '-in'.
original_explanation: The command you get every Saturday morning. Ito yung ginagawa mo sa history ng browser mo. O yung ginagawa mo sa pangalan mo after a major chismis. To make something clean, literally or figuratively.
usage_notes: Ito ang anyong pawatas na nakapokus sa layon. Halimbawa, 'Linisin mo ang kwarto'. Ang katumbas nitong pokus sa tagaganap ay 'maglinis'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **linisin** ang iyong sapatos bago pumasok sa bahay.","translation":"You need **to clean** your shoes before entering the house."},{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **linisin** mo ang mesa pagkatapos nating kumain.","translation":"Please, **clean** the table after we eat."}]

translation: to look at; to direct one's gaze toward
meaning_filipino: Ibaling o ituon ang paningin sa isang partikular na direksyon o bagay.
original_explanation: When your friend says "Uy, tingnan mo 'to!" and you don't know where to look, they'll say "Itingin mo sa kanan!" (Look to the right!). It's giving your eyes a specific target, like when you're trying to point out a chismis-worthy scene across the room without being too obvious.
usage_notes: Often used as a command. It's about directing someone else's (or your own) sight.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Itingin** mo ang iyong mga mata sa daan habang nagmamaneho.","translation":"**Keep** your eyes **on** the road while driving."},{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **itingin** mo kung sino ang kumakatok sa pinto.","translation":"Please, **go look** and see who is knocking at the door."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maipit o maiipit sa isang makitid na espasyo o sa pagitan ng dalawang bagay.
original_explanation: 'Yung daliri mo na naipit sa pinto. 'Yung braso mo na naipit sa siksikang MRT. 'Yung puso mo na naipit between "mahal ko" and "mahal ako". It's the feeling of being stuck and squeezed, literally or figuratively.
usage_notes: Can be used for both physical and metaphorical situations of being trapped or squeezed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka at baka **sumipit** ang daliri mo sa siper ng iyong bag.","translation":"Be careful or your finger might **get caught** in the zipper of your bag."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng makinilya na gumagamit ng koryente upang paganahin ang mga mekanismo nito, na nagpapagaan sa pagpindot ng tiklado at nagbibigay ng mas pare-parehong imprenta.
etymology: Pagsasama ng 'makinilya' at 'de-koryente' (mula sa Espanyol na 'de corriente', nangangahulugang 'de-kuryente').
original_explanation: The glow-up version of the classic typewriter. The 'makinilyang de-koryente' was the high-tech office equipment of its time. Less finger muscle needed, more consistent typing, and it made that cool electric hum. It was the bridge between the purely mechanical world and the computer age. The iPhone 3G of typewriters.
usage_notes: Isang partikular na termino na nagpapaiba dito mula sa isang manwal na makinilya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas mabilis mag-type sa **makinilyang de-koryente** kaysa sa mano-mano.","translation":"It's faster to type on an **electric typewriter** than a manual one."},{"sentence":"Naabutan ko pa sa opisina ang paggamit ng **makinilyang de-koryente** bago nagkaroon ng mga kompyuter.","translation":"I still experienced using an **electric typewriter** at the office before computers became available."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang unlapi na ikinakabit sa mga salitang-ugat upang bumuo ng pang-uri na nagsasaad ng katangian (hal. maganda), o pandiwa na nagpapahayag ng kakayahan o di-sinasadyang pagkilos (hal. makuha, mahulog).
original_explanation: The ultimate glow-up prefix. It takes a plain root word like 'ganda' (beauty) and turns it into `maganda` (beautiful). It's also the prefix for "oops" moments (`mahulog` - to accidentally fall) and "I can do it!" moments (`magawa` - to be able to do). It's the little engine that could, of prefixes.
usage_notes: One of the most common prefixes in Tagalog. `Ma-` + [root] often creates an adjective. `Ma-` + [root] can also form a potential verb (can be done). `Maka-` is for ability, `Ma-` is more about potential or accidental action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang 'ganda' ay nagiging '**ma**ganda' kapag nilapian.","translation":"'Ganda' (beauty) becomes '**ma**ganda' (beautiful) when the prefix is added."},{"sentence":"Sana ay **ma**kuha ko ang tamang sagot.","translation":"I hope I can **get** the right answer."}]

meaning_filipino: Suriin nang masusi at maingat ang isang bagay, pangyayari, o pahayag upang alamin ang katotohanan.
original_explanation: This is some next-level Sherlock Holmes stuff. When you 'sinsayin' something, you're not just looking, you're *investigating*. It's what you do to your partner's phone when your gut feeling is acting up, or what your boss does to your expense report. It's CSI: Manila level of checking.
usage_notes: A formal and somewhat archaic term. 'Siyasatin' or 'imbestigahan' are more common synonyms in modern use.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **sinsayin** nang mabuti ang bawat ebidensya bago magbigay ng hatol.","translation":"Each piece of evidence must be **scrutinized** carefully before giving a verdict."},{"sentence":"**Sinsayin** mo ang mga dokumento upang makita kung may mali.","translation":"**Examine** the documents to see if there is anything wrong."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kalangitan na walang anumang ulap; maliwanag at maaliwalas.
original_explanation: That perfect beach day sky. 'Yung tipong walang sagabal sa view, as in clear na clear, parang NBI clearance mo. Perfect for taking IG-worthy photos or just contemplating life without any 'clouds' of doubt.
usage_notes: Used literally to describe the sky. Can be used metaphorically to mean 'clear' or 'without trouble'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Walang-ulap** ang langit kaya't napakainit ng sikat ng araw.","translation":"The sky was **cloudless** so the sun's rays were very hot."},{"sentence":"Sana ang buhay ko ay kasing linaw ng isang **walang-ulap** na umaga.","translation":"I wish my life was as clear as a **cloudless** morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Kasalukuyang inaalis ang pagkakahawak sa isang bagay; sumusuko o humihinto sa isang gawain o ugnayan.
original_explanation: The 'it's not you, it's me' of actions. When you're holding on to your last bit of patience in EDSA traffic, or to that toxic situationship, and you finally decide, 'Ayoko na.' That's you, bumibitaw. A hugot anthem in verb form.
usage_notes: Present progressive tense of 'bitaw' (to let go). Can be used literally for physical grip or metaphorically for emotional attachments or responsibilities.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahan-dahan siyang **bumibitaw** sa pagkakahawak sa lubid.","translation":"He **is** slowly **letting go** of his grip on the rope."},{"sentence":"Nararamdaman kong **bumibitaw** na siya sa aming mga pangarap.","translation":"I feel that she **is letting go** of our dreams."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinuno o tagapamahala ng isang paaralan; punong-guro.
original_explanation: The final boss of the school. The person you only see when you're in deep trouble (in the `prinsipal's` office) or when you're getting an award. They have the power to suspend classes, which makes them a hero, or give a really long speech during the flag ceremony, which is... less heroic.
usage_notes: This is the common Filipinized spelling of the English 'principal'. 'Punong-guro' is the native Tagalog equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinatawag ako ng **prinsipal** dahil sa aking mga grado.","translation":"The **principal** called for me because of my grades."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay, tao, o pangyayari na nagdudulot ng gulo, pagkabalisa, o paggambala sa kapayapaan at kaayusan.
original_explanation: Eto 'yung kapitbahay na nagvi-videoke hanggang 3 AM on a Tuesday. O kaya 'yung issue sa trabaho na ayaw kang patulugin. It's anything that disrupts your zen and makes you say, "Hay, nako, eto na naman." It's the opposite of peace and quiet.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa isang tao, isang kaganapan, o isang sitwasyon na nagdudulot ng gulo o pagkabalisa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **mapanligalig** na balita ay nagdulot ng takot sa buong komunidad.","translation":"The **troublesome** news caused fear in the entire community."},{"sentence":"Sinaway ng pulis ang grupong **mapanligalig** sa kalye.","translation":"The police reprimanded the **disruptive** group on the street."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang mag-alok at magbenta ng isang produkto o serbisyo kapalit ng pera.
original_explanation: That feeling when you finally get rid of your pre-loved stuff online. "Yung sapatos na binili mo on a whim, tapos after one use, you realize you need the cash more. Sana **maipagbili** ko 'to agad sa Carousell!" It's the hustle of turning 'tambak' into 'pera'.
usage_notes: Often used when one wants or needs to sell something, implying a goal or necessity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay **maipagbili** ko ang mga lumang gamit para magkaroon ng ekstrang pera.","translation":"I hope I can **sell** my old things to have extra money."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **maipagbili** ang bahay sa panahon ngayon.","translation":"It's hard **to be able to sell** a house these days."}]

meaning_filipino: Nilagyan o kinulayan ng enamel, isang uri ng makintab at matibay na pintura o patong.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Ingles na "enamel" na nilapian ng "-an".
original_explanation: 'Yung process ng paglalagay ng shiny, protective coating sa isang bagay. Isipin mo 'yung paborito mong tasa na sobrang kinis at may design—malamang in-enamel 'yan. O 'yung lumang kadena ng lola mo na pinakintab at pinatibay ulit. Basically, giving something a glow-up and a shield.
usage_notes: Isang pandiwang nabuo mula sa isang hiram na salita.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Enamelahan** ang mga bagong gawang palayok upang maging mas matibay.","translation":"The newly made pots **were enameled** to make them more durable."},{"sentence":"Gusto niyang **enamelahan** ang kanyang lumang alahas.","translation":"She wants **to have** her old jewelry **enameled**."}]

translation: to gulp; to guzzle; to chug
meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis, malakas, at madalas ay maingay na pag-inom ng anumang likido, karaniwan sa isang lagukan.
original_explanation: This isn't just 'inom' (to drink). This is drinking on beast mode. It’s that sound you make when you're super thirsty and you **laklak** a whole bottle of water in 5 seconds. Or when your 'tito' at the fiesta starts to **laklak** the Emperador like it's a juice box. It's aggressive, no-nonsense drinking.
usage_notes: Often used informally to describe drinking a lot, especially alcohol, in a short amount of time. It has an onomatopoeic quality, mimicking the sound of gulping.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **laklakin** ang gamot, inumin mo nang dahan-dahan.","translation":"Don't **guzzle** the medicine, drink it slowly."},{"sentence":"**Nilaklak** niya ang isang buong pitsel ng malamig na tubig dahil sa sobrang uhaw.","translation":"He **chugged** a whole pitcher of cold water because he was so thirsty."}]

translation: to give someone provisions (for a trip/day); to have someone take something along
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng pagkain, pera, o anumang bagay na kakailanganin para sa isang paglalakbay, pagpasok sa paaralan, o pagtatrabaho.
etymology: From the causative prefix "ipa-" and "baon" (provisions, packed meal).
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino mom love language. It's not just 'to give food,' it's to command someone to bring food that you prepared. 'O, **ipabaon** mo 'to sa tatay mo para may pananghalian siya.' (Here, have your dad take this for his lunch.) It's an order rooted in care. Can also be used for non-food items, like advice: '**Ipabaon** mo ang mga pangaral ko.' (Take my advice with you.)
usage_notes: Strongly associated with acts of care, especially from a parent to a child or between family members. Refers to provisions for a specific day or journey away from home.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagluto si nanay ng adobo para **ipabaon** sa akin sa opisina.","translation":"Mom cooked adobo **to have me take** to the office as my packed lunch."},{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **ipabaon** sa mga bata ang kanilang pamasahe at meryenda.","translation":"Don't forget **to give the children** their fare and snacks **to take with them**."}]

translation: to rush something; to do something hastily
meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang pagmamadali sa paggawa ng isang bagay, na maaaring magresulta sa hindi gaanong magandang kalidad.
original_explanation: The verb for when you're trying to cook adobo in 15 minutes. You just dali-daliin everything. It's what students do with their thesis the night before the deadline. The result might be "pwede na," but definitely not "perfect."
usage_notes: Verb form of "dali-dali." Implies rushing an action or task, often with negative consequences to quality.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **dali-daliin** ang pagkain, baka mabilaukan ka.","translation":"Don't **rush** your food, you might choke."},{"sentence":"**Dinalidali** niya ang report kaya maraming mali.","translation":"She **rushed** the report, that's why it has many mistakes."}]

meaning_filipino: Maglagay ng panakip sa isang bagay o sa sarili upang ito ay maprotektahan, maitago, o hindi makita.
original_explanation: What you do to your laptop camera with a piece of tape because you're paranoid. Also, what your friend does to your mouth when you're about to spill a secret in public. 'Hoy, **magtakip** ka ng bibig!' can mean literally cover your mouth when you cough, or figuratively, 'shut up!'
usage_notes: A general verb for covering. 'Takpan' is the object-focused version, e.g., 'Takpan mo ang ulam' (Cover the food).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magtakip** ng ilong at bibig kapag bumabahing.","translation":"You need to **cover** your nose and mouth when you sneeze."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagdaragdag ng lakas, sigla, o tibay sa isang bagay, tao, o sistema.
original_explanation: Your "gym bro" phase. It's the act of drinking Cobra for that extra push, doing overtime to get in your boss's good graces (strengthening your position), or when a government official uses their influence for personal gain (pagpapalakas sa pwesto). Can be for your body, your WiFi signal, or your political connections.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical, mental, emotional, political, or structural strengthening.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ehersisyo ay mahalaga sa **pagpapalakas** ng katawan.","translation":"Exercise is important for **strengthening** the body."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapalakas** ng relasyon sa mga kliyente ay prayoridad ng kumpanya.","translation":"The **reinforcement** of relationships with clients is a company priority."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang wika o diyalekto na sinasalita ng mga ordinaryong tao sa isang partikular na bansa o rehiyon.
original_explanation: This is the language you actually speak at home, not the super-formal one you use for job interviews. It's your Cebuano, Ilocano, Hiligaynon, or even your everyday Taglish. It's the real, raw, 'palengke-level' talk of the people, not the stiff, textbook 'balarila' version. It's language in its 'pambahay' clothes.
usage_notes: An academic term used in linguistics, literature, and cultural studies.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang panitikang **bernakular** ay gumagamit ng pang-araw-araw na wika ng isang rehiyon.","translation":"**Vernacular** literature uses the everyday language of a region."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan nila ang pagkakaiba ng wikang pambansa at mga wikang **bernakular**.","translation":"They are studying the difference between the national language and the **vernacular** languages."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pampublikong anunsyo, karaniwang ginagawa sa simbahan sa loob ng tatlong magkakasunod na Linggo, na ipinapaalam ang intensyon ng isang pares na magpakasal.
original_explanation: This is the OG relationship status update, church edition. Before you can get married in a Catholic church, they announce your upcoming wedding for three straight Sundays. It's basically a public "speak now or forever hold your peace" to check if anyone has a valid objection, like if the groom is secretly already married. It's the tawag sa kasal.
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of Catholic wedding preparations in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nilang tapusin ang tatlong Linggong **tawag sa kasal** bago sila maikasal.","translation":"They need to finish the three-Sunday **wedding banns** before they can get married."},{"sentence":"Narinig mo na ba ang **tawag sa kasal** para kina Ana at Ben?","translation":"Have you heard the **marriage banns** for Ana and Ben?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamataas na bahagi ng ulo ng isang tao.
original_explanation: The part of your head that gets wet first when it rains and you don't have an umbrella. Or the spot where your mom gives you a 'kutos' (knuckle tap) when you've done something silly. It's the summit of your personal mountain.
usage_notes: A common phrase referring to the very top of the head.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinaplos niya ang **tuktok ng ulo** ng bata.","translation":"She caressed the **crown of the child's head**."},{"sentence":"Mainit ang sikat ng araw sa **tuktok ng ulo** ko.","translation":"The sun's rays are hot on the **top of my head**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawa ng panlilinlang, pandaraya, o hindi pagiging tapat sa isang kasunduan, laro, o relasyon.
original_explanation: That shady move. It’s copying your seatmate's answers, using cheat codes in a game, or telling your partner you're working overtime when you're actually at the mall. It's the reason for trust issues and the main plot of many teleseryes.
usage_notes: Can refer to cheating in games, exams, relationships, or business.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagdaraya** sa eleksyon ay isang malubhang krimen.","translation":"**Cheating** in the election is a serious crime."},{"sentence":"Nahuli siya sa akto ng **pagdaraya** sa kanilang pagsusulit.","translation":"He was caught in the act of **cheating** on their exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghiling o pag-uutos sa isang tao na magpalit ng damit o bihisan ang iba.
etymology: From `pa-` prefix indicating a request or cause + `bihis` (dress, clothes).
original_explanation: When your mom yells 'Pabihis ka na sa kapatid mo!' it means 'Get your sibling dressed!' It can also be the actual clothes you bring for a quick change, like your gym clothes after work. It's the command form of getting someone else ready.
usage_notes: Used as a command to get someone (else) dressed, or as a noun for the clothes themselves.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May dala akong **pabihis** para mamaya sa party.","translation":"I brought some **clothes for changing** for the party later."},{"sentence":"**Pabihis** mo na ang bata at aalis na tayo.","translation":"**Get** the child **dressed** now, we are leaving."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng panlilinlang, panloloko, o hindi patas na pamamaraan upang makakuha ng kalamangan sa isang laro, pagsusulit, o anumang sitwasyon.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you can't win fair and square. From peeking at your seatmate's test paper ('nangodigo'), to using cheat codes in a video game, to manipulating the rules in a friendly game of Uno. 'Dumaya' is the act of breaking the rules for your own benefit. In love, this is the ultimate betrayal. 'Akala ko tapat ka, pero nalaman kong dumaya ka.' Ouch.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **dumaya** sa laro para masaya ang lahat.","translation":"Don't **cheat** in the game so that everyone has fun."},{"sentence":"Inakusahan siyang **dumaya** noong nakaraang halalan.","translation":"He was accused of **cheating** during the last election."}]

meaning_filipino: Pilitin, atasan, o hikayatin ang isang tao na maging matipid sa paggastos o paggamit ng anumang bagay.
etymology: From pa- (causative) + pag- (causative/agentive) + tipid (thrifty). The pa- and pag- combination creates a complex causative verb, meaning "to make someone do the action of the root word."
original_explanation: This is your mom's superpower. It's when she tells you, "Anak, isang kilong bigas na lang 'to," to guilt-trip you into not buying that milk tea. It's the command form of "magtipid ka, uy!"
usage_notes: A causative verb used to command or request someone to make another person practice thriftiness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Papagtipirin** mo muna ang mga anak mo habang wala ka pang trabaho.","translation":"**Make** your children **be thrifty** for now while you are still jobless."}]

translation: to cause to subside; to placate; to calm down
meaning_filipino: Pababain o bawasan ang tindi o lakas ng isang bagay, tulad ng galit, sakit, lagnat, o baha.
original_explanation: What you try to do to your mom's anger after you forgot to defrost the chicken. 'Ma, kalma lang...' Or when you take paracetamol to pahupain the fever. It’s the act of making something less intense, from emotions to floodwaters.
usage_notes: A versatile word used for emotions, weather phenomena, physical symptoms, and conflicts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang **pahupain** ang galit ng kanyang kaibigan.","translation":"He is trying to **placate** his friend's anger."},{"sentence":"Uminom ka ng gamot para **pahupain** ang iyong lagnat.","translation":"Take medicine to **make** your fever **subside**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa kalagayan ng pagkalango dahil sa labis na pag-inom ng alak o anumang inuming nakalalasing.
original_explanation: The state you're in after one too many bottles of Red Horse. Suddenly, you're a philosopher, a karaoke star, or you're crying over your ex from 5 years ago. It's when you start sending 'u up?' texts at 2 AM or declaring 'I love you, guys!' to everyone at the table. Your balance is gone, your inhibitions are gone, and your Grab fare is about to be astronomical.
usage_notes: The most common term for being intoxicated.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang magmaneho kapag **lasing**.","translation":"Don't drive when you're **drunk**."},{"sentence":"**Lasing** na siya kagabi kaya kung ano-ano ang pinagsasabi.","translation":"He was **drunk** last night, that's why he was saying all sorts of things."}]

translation: to have mercy, to feel pity
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita ng habag o awa sa isang taong nagdurusa, nangangailangan, o nagkasala.
etymology: From 'dala' (to carry) and 'awa' (pity, mercy), literally "to carry pity".
original_explanation: This is the feeling you get when you see a stray kitten in the rain, or when your friend is crying over a breakup for the fifth time. It's the "aww, kawawa naman" emotion that compels you to help, or at least offer a shoulder to cry on. It’s the core of Filipino charity and compassion.
usage_notes: A compound verb that expresses a deep sense of compassion or pity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magdalang-awa** ka naman sa mga pulubing nanlilimos sa kalye.","translation":"**Have mercy** on the beggars asking for alms on the street."},{"sentence":"Kahit galit siya, sinubukan pa rin niyang **magdalang-awa** sa taong nanakit sa kanya.","translation":"Even though she was angry, she still tried to **feel pity** for the person who hurt her."}]

translation: to be peeled off, to flake off
meaning_filipino: Ang unti-unting pagtanggal o pagtuklap ng panlabas na bahagi o balat ng isang bagay, tulad ng pintura sa pader o balat matapos masunog sa araw.
etymology: From 'ma-' (potential prefix) + reduplication of the first syllable 'ba-' + 'bakbak' (to peel, to strip off a surface layer).
original_explanation: This is what happens to cheap paint, your skin after getting sunburnt at the beach, or the non-stick coating of your old frying pan. It's that process of flaking away. The 'true colors' of a wall, or a person, are revealed when the outer layer starts to 'mabakbak'.
usage_notes: The root 'bakbak' implies a flaking or peeling away of a surface layer. 'Mababakbak' is the potential form, meaning 'will be peeled off' or 'can be peeled off'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa matinding init, nagsimula nang **mabakbak** ang pintura ng aming pader.","translation":"Because of the intense heat, the paint on our wall has started to **peel off**."},{"sentence":"Mag-lotion ka, kung hindi ay **mababakbak** ang balat mo.","translation":"Put on lotion, otherwise your skin will **peel off**."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing dalawang beses ang dami, laki, o halaga ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: The act of making something double. It's what you tell the cashier at the milk tea shop: "Ate, dublihin mo 'yung pearls!" It's the verb form of getting twice as much.
usage_notes: The verb form of "duble". The more common spelling is "doblehin".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **dublihin** mo ang effort mo sa proyektong ito.","translation":"Please, **double** your effort on this project."},{"sentence":"Naisip kong **dublihin** ang ipon ko para sa kinabukasan.","translation":"I thought of **doubling** my savings for the future."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kilos o gawa na sinasadya, may layunin, at hindi nagkataon lamang.
original_explanation: When you 'accidentally' leave your crush on read, but you actually saw the message 5 hours ago. That, my friend, was intensyunal. It's the opposite of 'oops, nadulas lang.' It's a calculated move, like a chess grandmaster planning their endgame, or you planning how to get the last piece of chicken joy.
usage_notes: Often used to emphasize that an action was done on purpose, especially in arguments or legal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Intensyunal** ang ginawa niyang pagbasag sa baso dahil sa galit.","translation":"His breaking of the glass was **intentional** because of anger."},{"sentence":"Hindi aksidente iyon, **intensyunal** na hindi ka niya pinansin.","translation":"That wasn't an accident, he **intentionally** ignored you."}]

translation: will cause to spoil; will make something go stale
meaning_filipino: Ang maging sanhi ng pagkasira o pagkapanis ng pagkain sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you forget about the leftover adobo in the microwave for three days. The act of neglect that turns delicious food into a science experiment. "Huwag mong iwan sa labas 'yan, **magpapapanis** lang 'yan ng ulam."
usage_notes: Future tense of a causative verb. Refers to the act of causing food to spoil.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-iwan ng pagkain sa labas ng refrigerator ay **magpapapanis** dito.","translation":"Leaving food outside the refrigerator **will cause it to spoil**."},{"sentence":"Bakit ka pa bumili ng tinapay? **Magpapapanis** ka lang dahil marami pa tayo.","translation":"Why did you buy more bread? You **will just make it go stale** because we still have a lot."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat ng mga tao o panig na magkatunggali o magkasalungat sa isang kompetisyon, laban, o prinsipyo.
original_explanation: Sa Mobile Legends, 'yung team niyo at 'yung kabilang team, magkakalaban kayo. Sa office, 'yung ka-team mo na gusto ring ma-promote, magkakalaban kayo (lowkey lang). It's the "versus" in any situation, from sports to love triangles.
usage_notes: Can function as a noun (the opponents) or an adjective (being opponents). The plural noun form is 'mga magkakalaban'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit **magkakalaban** sa basketball court, magkakaibigan pa rin sila sa labas.","translation":"Even if they are **opponents** on the basketball court, they are still friends outside."},{"sentence":"Ang dalawang pamilya ay matagal nang **magkakalaban** sa pulitika.","translation":"The two families have long been political **rivals**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggalaw ng katawan kasabay ng ritmo ng musika.
etymology: From sum- (actor-focus infix) + sayaw (dance), with reduplication of the first syllable (sa-) to indicate progressive aspect.
