original_explanation: What Pinoys do at every party, fiesta, or just when a good song comes on the radio. From the traditional tinikling to the latest TikTok challenge, we're always sumasayaw. It's the present tense of busting a move. "Tingnan mo si Tito, sumasayaw na naman ng 'Otso-Otso'."
usage_notes: This is the progressive or present tense, indicating the ongoing action of dancing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga bata ay masayang **sumasayaw** sa gitna ng ulan.","translation":"The children are happily **dancing** in the middle of the rain."},{"sentence":"Sino ang lalaking **sumasayaw** mag-isa sa entablado?","translation":"Who is the man **dancing** alone on stage?"}]

translation: to use to support a living; to make a livelihood from
meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit sa isang bagay, kasanayan, o halaga bilang paraan para matustusan ang pang-araw-araw na pangangailangan.
original_explanation: This is the verb for your "hustle." It's what you do to put food on the table. A fisherman will ipagbuhay his catch. A writer will ipagbuhay his words. It's turning a skill, a resource, or even a small capital into your means of survival. "Yung sahod ko sa BPO, 'yun ang ipinagbubuhay ko sa pamilya ko."
usage_notes: Often used in the context of earning a living from a specific source or activity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kita mula sa maliit na tindahan ang kanilang **ipinagbubuhay** sa pamilya.","translation":"The income from the small store is what they **use to support** their family."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong matutong **ipagbuhay** ang iyong sarili gamit ang iyong mga talento.","translation":"You need to learn to **make a living for** yourself using your talents."}]

translation: A light touch; a slight nudge or tap
meaning_filipino: Isang marahan at bahagyang pagdikit o pag-abot sa isang bagay o tao, kadalasan gamit ang daliri o kamay.
original_explanation: It's that subtle "kalabit" from your friend when your crush walks by. Or the gentle tap on the jeepney ceiling to signal "para!". It's a touch so light, it's almost a suggestion. "Huy, kanti lang, 'wag manulak!"
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb root (e.g., 'kantihin', 'kinanti'). Often implies a playful or teasing touch.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **kanti** lang sa kanyang balikat ay sapat na para makuha ang atensyon niya.","translation":"Just a light **touch** on his shoulder was enough to get his attention."},{"sentence":"Nagalit siya dahil sa ginawang **kanti** ng bata sa kanyang bagong pintura na kotse.","translation":"He got mad because of the child's slight **tap** on his newly painted car."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing katangi-tangi o bukod-tangi ang isang bagay, tao, o kaganapan; pagtuunan ng pansin ang isang partikular na larangan.
original_explanation: This is what your favorite carinderia does when they create the 'Special of the Day'. It's also what you do when you're trying to impress someone: 'Mag-e-espesyal ako ng luto para sa bisita.' It’s the verb form of going the extra mile, whether it’s with adobo or with your love life.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Balak kong **mag-espesyal** ng pancit palabok para sa kaarawan mo.","translation":"I plan to **make a special** pancit palabok for your birthday."},{"sentence":"Hindi na siya tumatanggap ng ibang proyekto dahil gusto niyang **mag-espesyal** sa potograpiya.","translation":"He no longer accepts other projects because he wants to **specialize** in photography."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtiyak, pagpapatunay, o paggawa ng mga hakbang upang matiyak na ang isang bagay ay ligtas, tama, o mangyayari ayon sa plano.
original_explanation: This is your mom asking 'Naka-lock ba 'yung pinto?' five times before leaving the house. It's double-checking your alarm for a 6 AM flight, saving your work every 5 minutes, or asking your Grab driver 'Kuya, papunta po tayo sa Megamall, 'no?' just to be sure. It's the national pastime of the 'praning' (paranoid) but practical Pinoy.
usage_notes: Often used with 'paniniguro' or 'pagtitiyak.' Can also be spelled as `pagsisiguro`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bilang **pagseseguro**, dinala niya ang lahat ng kinakailangang dokumento.","translation":"As an **act of making sure**, he brought all the necessary documents."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na bahagi ng materya mula sa kalawakan na nagliliyab sa pagdaan nito sa atmospera ng daigdig.
original_explanation: That thing you see zipping across the night sky that makes you shout "Make a wish!" before you even realize what it is. It's the universe's version of a photobomber, gone in a flash. Perfect for your #aesthetic night sky photos, if you can even capture it.
usage_notes: Madalas iniuugnay sa mga pamahiin, tulad ng paghiling kapag nakakita nito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakita ako ng **bulalakaw** kagabi habang nakatingin sa mga bituin.","translation":"I saw a **shooting star** last night while looking at the stars."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao, wika, o anumang bagay na nagmula o may kaugnayan sa bansang Hapon (Japan).
original_explanation: Not the time of day, but the people and culture that gave us anime, ramen, and Uniqlo. When you say someone is 'Hapon', you mean they're Japanese. Note the different stress: HA-pon is afternoon, ha-PON is Japanese. Getting it wrong might just change your dinner plans.
usage_notes: The stress is on the second syllable (/ha-PON/) to differentiate it from 'afternoon' (/HA-pon/). It can be a noun (a Japanese person) or an adjective (Japanese food).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming turista na **Hapon** ang bumibisita sa Cebu.","translation":"Many **Japanese** tourists visit Cebu."},{"sentence":"Paborito kong kainin ang pagkaing **Hapon**.","translation":"My favorite food to eat is **Japanese** food."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagpapakinis o pag-aalis ng panlabas na balat ng kawayan, yantok, o kahoy gamit ang isang matalim na kasangkapan tulad ng itak o kutsilyo.
etymology: From mag- (verb-forming prefix) + kayas (to scrape or shave wood/bamboo).
original_explanation: It's the OG way of sanding wood or bamboo before papel de liha became a thing. Think of your lolo in the province, expertly peeling the skin off a bamboo pole to make a chair. It's a skill, not just scraping!
usage_notes: Typically used for making raw materials like bamboo, rattan, or wood smoother and more uniform by scraping off the outer layer.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magkayas** ng kawayan para gawing balag ng ampalaya.","translation":"You need **to shave the bamboo** to make a trellis for the bitter gourd."},{"sentence":"Maingat siyang nag-umpisang **magkayas** ng yantok para sa kanyang proyekto.","translation":"He carefully started **to shave the rattan** for his project."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng pagiging masiba, malakas, o labis kung kumain.
original_explanation: Describes your friend who orders their own food, then says "Penge, isang subo lang," and proceeds to eat half of yours. They have a separate stomach for dessert and are the first to attack the lechon at a fiesta. In the world of unli-wings, the matakaw is king.
usage_notes: Primarily refers to food but can be used figuratively for other forms of greed, e.g., 'matakaw sa kapangyarihan' (greedy for power).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa pagiging **matakaw** kaya laging ubos ang handa sa mga party.","translation":"He is known for being **gluttonous**, which is why the food always runs out at parties."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **matakaw** sa kapangyarihan.","translation":"Do not be **greedy** for power."}]

translation: to live together; to be in one household
meaning_filipino: Ang sama-samang paninirahan sa iisang tahanan o bubong.
etymology: From 'magka-' (denoting a shared state) + 'pisan' (to unite, to put together).
original_explanation: This is the adulting version of a group project, but for living arrangements. It's when you and your family, or maybe you and your partner, decide to share one roof, one electricity bill, and one battle over who gets the last piece of chicken.
usage_notes: Implies sharing a dwelling. More formal than 'live-in'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang magkapatid na **magkapisan** sa isang apartment para makatipid.","translation":"The siblings decided to **live together** in one apartment to save money."},{"sentence":"Matagal nang pangarap ni Ana na **magkapisan** silang muli ng kanyang mga anak.","translation":"It has long been Ana's dream for her and her children to **live together** again."}]

translation: a type of tall grass or weed
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng mataas na damo o talahib. Ito rin ang pinaniniwalaang pinagmulan ng pangalan ng lalawigan ng Tarlac.
etymology: Pinaniniwalaang orihinal na salitang Austronesian, kung saan hinango ang pangalan ng lalawigan ng Tarlac.
original_explanation: Before it was a province you drive through on SCTEX, 'tarlak' was just a humble weed, a kind of tall grass similar to talahib. The province was named after it! So next time you're stuck in traffic there, you can tell your friends, "Did you know we're in the land of tall grass?" It's a great fun fact that will make you sound smart (or like a nerd, depending on your friends).
usage_notes: This meaning is very rare and mostly known in the context of the etymology of Tarlac province.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mataas na ang mga **tarlak** sa bakanteng lote.","translation":"The **tarlak grass** in the vacant lot is already tall."},{"sentence":"Ang pangalan ng probinsya ay hango sa isang damo na kung tawagin ay **tarlak**.","translation":"The province's name is derived from a weed called **tarlak**."}]

meaning_filipino: Latak o burak na naiipon sa ilalim ng tubig, partikular sa mga ilog, lawa, o estero.
original_explanation: This is the mud and gunk at the bottom of a river or estero. It's the stuff that makes the water murky after a heavy rain. Parang 'yung mga unresolved issues sa isang relationship, 'yung mga latak na nasa ilalim lang, pero 'pag ginalaw, lumalabo lahat.
usage_notes: Refers to the physical sediment, not a metaphorical residue, though it can be used that way poetically.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **banlikan** ang ilog kaya mababaw na ito.","translation":"The river is full of **sediment**, which is why it is now shallow."},{"sentence":"Naging problema ang makapal na **banlikan** sa daluyan ng tubig.","translation":"The thick **silt** in the waterway became a problem."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing mas pino, makinis, o detalyado ang isang bagay. Pag-alis ng magaspang na bahagi.
original_explanation: Like when you're editing your thesis and your adviser says 'Pinuhan mo pa,' meaning you need to polish your arguments. Or when a carpenter sands a piece of wood until it's super smooth. It's the act of leveling up from 'good' to 'great.'
usage_notes: Can be used for physical objects (making them smoother) or for abstract concepts (refining an idea, a plan, or a skill).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat mong **pinuhan** ang iyong mga sagot para mas malaki ang makuha mong puntos.","translation":"You should **refine** your answers to get a higher score."},{"sentence":"**Pinuhan** mo ang pagkakahiwa ng sibuyas.","translation":"**Make** the chopping of the onions **finer**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-imbita o pag-anyaya sa isang tao na dumalo sa isang pagtitipon, kaganapan, o lugar.
original_explanation: This is the formal way of saying 'inviting someone.' It's the action behind that fancy, ribboned card for a wedding, or that mass-forwarded GC message for a birthday KTV session. It's the opposite of being a gatecrasher. A successful `pagpapaanyaya` means more food to prepare and more people to entertain.
usage_notes: More formal than `pag-imbita`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Salamat sa iyong **pagpapaanyaya** sa kasal ng iyong kapatid.","translation":"Thank you for your **invitation** to your sibling's wedding."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang dalubhasang tekniko na gumagawa, nag-aangkop, at naglalapat ng mga lente, salamin sa mata, at contact lens ayon sa reseta.
original_explanation: Basically, ito yung modern/English spelling ng 'optiko'. Siya ang go-to person mo sa optical shop para sa perfect fit ng salamin at para sagutin ang tanong na, 'Bagay ba sa'kin 'to?'
usage_notes: Ito ang mas karaniwang ginagamit na termino sa kasalukuyan kumpara sa 'optiko', lalo na sa mga urban na lugar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtanong ako sa **optisyan** kung aling frame ang pinakamaganda para sa hugis ng aking mukha.","translation":"I asked the **optician** which frame is best for my face shape."}]

translation: will be made to become thin/skinny
meaning_filipino: Magiging sanhi ng labis na pagbaba ng timbang o pagiging payat ng isang tao.
original_explanation: This is the effect of a "broken heart diet" or a "thesis diet." You're so stressed or sad you forget to eat. "Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi ka **papangyayatin** ng trabaho mo, papatabain ka ng stress-eating." (Don't worry, your job won't make you skinny; stress-eating will make you fat.)
usage_notes: This is the causative form of 'mangayayat' (to become thin). It implies that an external factor (like sickness, stress, or diet) will cause weight loss.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kung puro ka lang trabaho at hindi ka kakain, **papangyayatin** ka niyan.","translation":"If you only work and don't eat, that **will make you skinny**."},{"sentence":"Ang matinding kalungkutan ay maaaring **makapangayayat** sa isang tao.","translation":"Intense sadness can **make** a person **thin**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang pangkusina na may malapad at patag na dulo, ginagamit sa pagbabaligtad, paghahalo, o pag-aalis ng pagkain sa kawali. Ang katumbas nito ay 'siyansi'.
original_explanation: It's the kitchen utensil you use to flip pancakes, fry eggs, or scrape the last bit of adobo from the pan. While older folks might call it 'siyansi', everyone in the department store will know you're looking for a spatula. The rubber ones are great for baking, the metal ones for serious frying action.
usage_notes: 'Siyansi' (from Chinese) is the more traditional term, but 'spatula' is widely used and understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gamitin mo ang **spatula** para baligtarin ang isda.","translation":"Use the **spatula** to flip the fish."},{"sentence":"Nabili ko itong bagong set ng silicone **spatula** online.","translation":"I bought this new set of silicone **spatulas** online."}]

translation: to favor; to show preference for
meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng higit na atensyon, kalamangan, o pagtatangi ang isang tao o bagay kaysa sa iba.
etymology: From 'pabor' + '-an' (suffix indicating the object of an action).
original_explanation: This is what happens when your mom gives the last piece of fried chicken to your sibling. "Pinaboran mo na naman si bunso!" It's the act of playing favorites, whether it's the teacher's pet, the favorite child, or the BPO agent who always gets the best shifts. The root of all 'tampo'.
usage_notes: The object of the verb is the one being favored.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **paboran** ang isang anak mo; dapat pantay-pantay ang pagtingin mo sa kanila.","translation":"Don't **favor** one of your children; you should treat them equally."},{"sentence":"Mukhang **pinaboran** ng tadhana ang aming koponan ngayong gabi.","translation":"It seems fate **favored** our team tonight."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sistema ng isang bansa o rehiyon na may kinalaman sa paglikha, pamamahagi, at pagkonsumo ng yaman, produkto, at serbisyo.
original_explanation: The *ekonomiya* is the country's financial "vibe." Is it booming? Is it in a recession? Is everyone getting a job, or is everyone applying for a visa to work abroad? It's the giant, invisible machine powered by businesses, OFWs, the stock market, and your local sari-sari store. When the news says "bumagsak ang ekonomiya," it's basically the nation's wallet crying.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang naging epekto ng pandemya sa **ekonomiya** ng buong mundo.","translation":"The pandemic had a huge effect on the world's **economy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaki at mapaminsalang baha; isang malawakang kalamidad o sakuna.
original_explanation: What it feels like when it rains for 5 minutes in Metro Manila and EDSA turns into a parking lot slash swimming pool. It's the "end of the world" level of disaster, often used dramatically for heavy floods or any overwhelming catastrophe, like your inbox on a Monday morning.
usage_notes: A very strong, often biblical-sounding word for a massive flood or disaster.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang walang tigil na ulan ay nagdulot ng isang **dilubyo** sa buong probinsya.","translation":"The non-stop rain caused a **deluge** in the entire province."},{"sentence":"Parang **dilubyo** ang dami ng trabahong kailangan kong tapusin.","translation":"The amount of work I need to finish feels like a **cataclysm**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng lutuin kung saan ang karne, karaniwan ay baka o baboy, ay pinakuluan sa tubig kasama ang mga gulay tulad ng repolyo, patatas, at mais.
etymology: From 'laga' (boil) + '-in-' (denoting a completed action or the object of an action) + 'karne' (meat, from Spanish 'carne').
original_explanation: The ultimate rainy-day comfort food. It's basically a hug in a bowl. You have tender **linagang karne** (usually beef), a clear, savory broth, and chunky veggies like cabbage and potatoes. It's the simpler, less-sour cousin of Sinigang. Perfect for when you're feeling sick, sad, or just really, really hungry. Don't forget the sawsawan of patis, calamansi, and sili!
usage_notes: 'Nilagang baka' is a more common and specific term. 'Linagang karne' is a general term for any boiled meat dish of this type.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpaluto si Itay ng **linagang karne** para sa aming pananghalian.","translation":"Dad had **boiled meat** cooked for our lunch."},{"sentence":"Ang sarap humigop ng sabaw ng **linagang karne** kapag malamig ang panahon.","translation":"It's so good to sip the broth of **boiled meat** when the weather is cold."}]

translation: to be chipped off; to be sliced off
meaning_filipino: Ang hindi sinasadyang pagkatanggal ng isang maliit na bahagi mula sa isang bagay, karaniwan ay sa gilid, sa pamamagitan ng pagtama o paghiwa.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your sweldo on the 15th. You get your full pay, pero biglang matapyas for bills, utang, and your Shopee cart. It's that feeling when a piece of your sanity gets chipped away during a traffic jam on EDSA.
usage_notes: Refers to a small, often angled, piece being removed from a larger whole.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingat ka sa paghawak ng baso, baka **matapyas** ang gilid.","translation":"Be careful holding the glass, its edge might **get chipped off**."},{"sentence":"Malaking bahagi ng badyet ang **natapyas** para sa biglaang gastusin.","translation":"A large part of the budget was **sliced off** for emergency expenses."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng katangiang sumusubok sa kakayahan, pasensya, o lakas ng isang tao. Maaari ring tumukoy sa isang taong palaban o hindi takot sa komprontasyon.
original_explanation: Two flavors! 1. The 'challenging' one: Yung exam na parang isinulat ng kaaway mo. Yung project na may deadline na 'yesterday.' 2. The 'defiant' one: Yung kaibigan mong laging 'Tara, G!' sa anumang adventure. It's an attitude that says 'Bring it on!'
usage_notes: Can describe a situation (challenging) or a person (defiant, confrontational). Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bagong posisyon sa trabaho ay mas **mapanghamon**.","translation":"The new position at work is more **challenging**."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa kanyang **mapanghamon** na paninindigan laban sa katiwalian.","translation":"He is known for his **defiant** stance against corruption."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng mineral na silicate na may mahahabang hibla, hindi nasusunog, at ginagamit bilang insulasyon sa init.
original_explanation: Yan yung material sa mga lumang bahay na bawal na ngayon kasi daw nakaka-cancer. Parang ex mo, mukhang harmless pero toxic pala in the long run. Ingat sa pag-handle.
usage_notes: Isang teknikal na termino na mas madalas marinig sa larangan ng konstruksiyon o agham.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bawal nang gamitin ang **asbesto** sa pagtatayo ng mga bagong gusali.","translation":"The use of **asbestos** is no longer allowed in the construction of new buildings."},{"sentence":"Natuklasan na may **asbesto** sa kisame ng lumang bodega.","translation":"**Asbestos** was discovered in the ceiling of the old warehouse."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong nakakulong sa bilangguan bilang parusa sa isang krimen o habang naghihintay ng paglilitis.
original_explanation: 'Yung bida (o kontrabida) sa mga prison break movies. Sila 'yung nakasuot ng orange jumpsuit at nasa likod ng rehas. Metaphorically, 'yan din 'yung feeling mo 'pag 'di ka pinayagan ng magulang mong lumabas. 'Parang preso naman ako dito sa bahay!'
usage_notes: Ang pambabaeng anyo ay "presa", ngunit "preso" ay karaniwang ginagamit para sa parehong kasarian sa modernong pag-uusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatakas ang ilang **preso** mula sa pambansang bilangguan.","translation":"Several **prisoners** escaped from the national penitentiary."},{"sentence":"Dinalaw niya ang kanyang kamag-anak na **preso**.","translation":"He visited his relative who is an **inmate**."}]

translation: to attain happiness; to achieve bliss
meaning_filipino: Ang makamit ang sukdulang kaligayahan o kasiyahan, kadalasan sa kontekstong espirituwal o sa pag-ibig.
original_explanation: The ultimate #SanaAll goal. This isn't just about being happy; it's about achieving a state of pure bliss. It's the feeling you hope to get when your crush finally notices you, or the state of nirvana you reach after a long, hard-fought battle in life. Very poetic, very teleserye ending.
usage_notes: A literary and somewhat archaic phrase. It's a compound verb phrase.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dasal ng bawat magulang na sana'y **magtamong-ligaya** ang kanilang mga anak sa hinaharap.","translation":"It is every parent's prayer that their children will **attain happiness** in the future."},{"sentence":"Sa wakas, pagkatapos ng lahat ng pagsubok, sila ay **nagtamong-ligaya**.","translation":"At last, after all the trials, they **achieved bliss**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamataas na kapulungan ng hukuman sa Pilipinas, na may panghuling kapangyarihan sa paglilitis at pagpapasya sa mga usaping legal at konstitusyonal.
original_explanation: The final boss of Philippine courts. If your legal drama reaches this level, it's like the season finale of a teleserye where everything is on the line. It's where the most important legal battles are fought and where laws get their ultimate reality check. Think of them as the admins of the "Philippine Law" server.
usage_notes: Always capitalized as it is a proper noun referring to the specific judicial body.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Idinulog ng mga mambabatas ang petisyon sa **Kataas-taasang Hukuman**.","translation":"The lawmakers filed the petition before the **Supreme Court**."},{"sentence":"Ang desisyon ng **Kataas-taasang Hukuman** ay pinal at hindi na maaaring iapela.","translation":"The decision of the **Supreme Court** is final and executory."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang opisyal na pagbabawal o paghihigpit sa kalakalan o iba pang komersyal na aktibidad sa isang partikular na bansa.
original_explanation: This is the international version of 'I'm not talking to you.' When one country gets mad at another, they might do a pag-eembargo, basically saying, 'No more buying your stuff, and you can't buy our stuff either!' It's a political silent treatment that hits the economy.
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of international politics and economics.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pag-eembargo** sa langis ay nagdulot ng krisis sa enerhiya sa buong mundo.","translation":"The **imposing of an embargo** on oil caused an energy crisis worldwide."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng mga bansa ang posibleng **pag-eembargo** bilang parusa.","translation":"The countries are studying the possible **act of imposing an embargo** as a sanction."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malalim at magiliw na katawagan para sa isang minamahal; maaari ring tumukoy sa damdamin ng pag-ibig mismo.
etymology: From Malay 'cinta' (love), from Sanskrit 'cintā' (thought, care, anxiety).
original_explanation: The OG term of endearment before 'babe,' 'mahal,' or 'bebe ko.' This is Harana-level love. You hear 'sinta' and you imagine kundiman songs, balagtasan, and writing love letters instead of just sending a heart emoji. It's classic, it's poetic, it's the 'O, aking sinta' kind of vibe.
usage_notes: Often used in literature, songs, and poetry. Can be used as a term of address ('O, sinta ko') or to refer to the feeling of love ('puspos ng sinta').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ikaw ang aking natatanging **sinta**.","translation":"You are my one and only **beloved**."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang puso ay puno ng **sinta** para sa bayan.","translation":"His heart is full of **love** for the country."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian o kilos ng pag-unat o paghaba kapag hinihila at pagbalik sa orihinal na anyo kapag binitawan.
etymology: From na- + reduplication of the first syllable 'ba' + banat (stretch).
original_explanation: Describes anything that can be stretched, like a rubber band, your favorite garterized shorts after a fiesta, or your budget during "petsa de peligro" (days before payday). "Bes, 'wag mo nang isuot 'yan, nababanat na 'yung tela!"
usage_notes: Can refer to the physical act of stretching something or the property of being stretchable. Can also be used figuratively for things like patience or budget.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maganda ang tela ng damit na ito dahil **nababanat** ito nang maayos.","translation":"The fabric of this dress is good because it **is stretchable**."},{"sentence":"**Nababanat** na nang husto ang pasensya ko sa iyo.","translation":"My patience with you **is being stretched** to its limit."}]

translation: to be able to escape from
meaning_filipino: Magawang makawala o makaligtas mula sa isang tao, lugar, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: That feeling of pure, unadulterated joy when you successfully leave the office at exactly 5 PM on a Friday, avoiding your boss who's looking for "volunteers" for weekend work. You have successfully "matakasan" the overtime trap. It's also when the hero in a movie finally gets away from the bad guys.
usage_notes: The 'ma- -an' affix indicates the ability to escape *from* a specific person, place, or situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **matakasan** ang kanyang mga problema ngunit lalo lang itong lumala.","translation":"He tried **to escape from** his problems, but they only got worse."},{"sentence":"Sana'y **matakasan** natin ang matinding traffic sa EDSA ngayon.","translation":"I hope we can **escape from** the terrible traffic on EDSA today."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang miyembro ng aristokrasya; isang taong kabilang sa mataas na lipunan dahil sa kapanganakan o yaman.
original_explanation: The person who is part of the 'aristokrasiya.' This is your Don/Doña, the one who sips tea with a pinky up and probably has never commuted via jeepney in their life. They're the main characters in those historical dramas, often portrayed as either benevolent rulers or snobby antagonists.
usage_notes: Can be used for both male and female individuals.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Donya Victorina ay kumikilos na parang isang tunay na **aristokrata**.","translation":"Doña Victorina acts like a true **aristocrat**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga **aristokrata** noong unang panahon ay may malalawak na lupain.","translation":"The **aristocrats** of the olden times owned vast lands."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang madilim na hugis at balangkas ng isang tao o bagay na nakikita laban sa isang mas maliwanag na likuran.
original_explanation: Parang yung anino ng ex mo na kahit saan ka lumingon, nakikita mo pa rin. It's that dark outline of something or someone, usually against a light source like a sunset. Perfect for dramatic profile pics.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng **silweta** ng mga bundok tuwing dapit-hapon.","translation":"The **silhouette** of the mountains is beautiful at dusk."},{"sentence":"Isang misteryosong **silweta** ang nakita niyang nakatayo sa may bintana.","translation":"He saw a mysterious **silhouette** standing by the window."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging laya o malaya mula sa pagkaalipin, pagkakakulong, o anumang uri ng paghihigpit at pagkontrol.
original_explanation: This is the feeling you get on the last day of work before a long vacation. It's the ultimate "sana all" moment for anyone stuck in a bad situation, whether it's traffic, a toxic relationship, or a job you hate. It's not just independence; it's the exhale after being held underwater.
usage_notes: More abstract than `kalayaan` (freedom), focusing on the state or quality of having become free.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkamalaya** ng bansa ay ipinagdiriwang taon-taon.","translation":"The country's **attainment of freedom** is celebrated every year."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang tunay na **pagkamalaya** nang iwan niya ang mapang-abusong relasyon.","translation":"She felt a true **state of being free** when she left the abusive relationship."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang taong mapag-aksaya, bulagsak sa paggasta, o maluho nang walang pag-iingat sa yaman.
original_explanation: That friend who gets their sahod on the 15th and is already broke by the 17th because of Shopee hauls and GrabFood. They live by the motto 'YOLO' and 'pera lang 'yan,' while their wallet is crying. The opposite of a financial guru.
usage_notes: A formal and somewhat archaic word. 'Bulagsak' or 'gastador' are more common in modern speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **mariwara** na pamumuhay, mabilis na naubos ang kanyang mana.","translation":"Because of his **wasteful** lifestyle, his inheritance quickly ran out."},{"sentence":"Pinangaralan siya ng kanyang mga magulang na huwag maging **mariwara** sa pera.","translation":"His parents advised him not to be **extravagant** with money."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng pananampalataya o pagtitiwala sa katotohanan, pag-iral, o bisa ng isang bagay o tao.
original_explanation: The present tense of "I trust you." 'Yung state mo 'pag sinabi ng jowa mong "friends lang kami" at pinipilit mong paniwalaan. Or 'yung pag-asa mong may darating na 13th-month pay. It's the act of having faith or trust in something or someone, right now.
usage_notes: Pangkasalukuyang panahunan (present tense) ng pandiwang 'maniwala'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Naniniwala** ako sa lahat ng sinasabi mo.","translation":"I **believe** everything you are saying."},{"sentence":"**Naniniwala** ka ba sa multo?","translation":"Do you **believe** in ghosts?"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay o puwersa na may kakayahang magdulot ng malawakang pinsala, pagkawasak, o pagkasira.
etymology: Mula sa `mang-` + `salasa` (to ravage). Ang `mang-` ay nagiging `manan-` at inuulit ang unang pantig ng salitang-ugat.
original_explanation: Ito yung description sa bagyo bago pa mag-landfall, 'yung tipong "Signal No. 4 na, besh!" Or 'yung tita mo sa handaan na parang bagyo kung ubusin 'yung lechon—isang mananalasa ng buffet table.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang mga natural na kalamidad tulad ng bagyo. Maaari ding gamitin bilang pangngalan na tumutukoy sa ahente ng pagkawasak.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inaasahan ang pagdating ng **mananalasa** na bagyo bukas ng umaga.","translation":"The arrival of the **ravaging** typhoon is expected tomorrow morning."},{"sentence":"Ang apoy ay naging isang **mananalasa** na tumupok sa buong kabahayan.","translation":"The fire became a **devastating force** that consumed the entire block of houses."}]

meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng maliliit na pagbabago o pagwawasto upang mapabuti o mapaganda ang isang bagay, lalo na ang isang larawan o gawaing sining.
etymology: From Spanish 'retoque' (touch-up). The verb is formed with the suffix '-hin'.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung final touches sa project mo bago i-submit kay client. Akala mo tapos na, pero may "isang maliit na paki-adjust lang" pa pala. Pwede rin sa makeup, 'yung konting ayos lang bago ka rumampa ulit.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'retokihin', but 'retinihin' can sometimes imply even finer, more delicate adjustments.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **retinihin** ang anino sa ilalim ng mata para magmukhang mas natural.","translation":"You need to **touch up** the shadow under the eye to make it look more natural."},{"sentence":"**Retinihin** mo lang nang kaunti ang kulay ng kalangitan sa painting.","translation":"Just **refine** the color of the sky in the painting a little."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matibay at nababaluktot na himaymay sa katawan na nag-uugnay ng kalamnan sa buto. Sa kolokyal na gamit, tumutukoy din sa ugat na nakikita sa balat.
original_explanation: That thing that pops out on your neck, forehead, or arms when you're super stressed, angry, or lifting something heavy. 'Lumabas na ang litid ni Ma'am sa leeg sa sobrang inis sa klase.' It's the body's natural 'gigil' meter.
usage_notes: While the technical meaning is 'tendon', it's more commonly used to refer to prominent veins.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halatang galit siya dahil lumabas ang mga **litid** sa kanyang leeg.","translation":"It's obvious he's angry because the **veins** on his neck were popping out."},{"sentence":"Naputol ang **litid** sa kanyang paa kaya siya ay naoperahan.","translation":"The **tendon** in his foot was torn, so he had surgery."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong laging nakikisama o 'nakikibuntot' nang walang paanyaya. Maaari ring tumukoy sa pagkakadawit sa isang problema o krimen.
original_explanation: This is when you're 'damay' in a problem you didn't necessarily start. As a person, a 'sabit' is that friend-of-a-friend who always shows up to the party uninvited and eats all the lumpia. The ultimate freeloader or someone implicated in a scandal.
usage_notes: The pronunciation often shifts to /sa-BIT/ to distinguish it from the 'hanging' meaning (/SA-bit/). When used for a person, it is derogatory.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **sabit** siya sa kaso dahil sa maling akala.","translation":"He became **implicated** in the case due to a misunderstanding."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **sabit** sa lakad ng may lakad.","translation":"Don't be a **hanger-on** on someone else's trip."}]

translation: state of being saved or collected; savings
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o resulta ng pagtitipon o pag-iimbak ng mga bagay, lalo na ng pera, sa paglipas ng panahon.
original_explanation: Ito yung pinaghirapan mong i-save from your sweldo, yung "ipon-challenge" mo na nauwi sa tagumpay. It's the fruit of skipping milk tea for a month. The opposite of "one day millionaire". What you have after resisting the 11.11 sale.
usage_notes: Refers to the accumulated result of saving or gathering. Can be used for money, things, or even abstract concepts like knowledge.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinakita niya sa amin ang kanyang **pagkaipon** na pera sa alkansya.","translation":"He showed us his **saved-up** money in the piggy bank."},{"sentence":"Ang dami ng kanyang **pagkaipon** na libro ay kahanga-hanga.","translation":"The amount of his **collected** books is impressive."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagdudulot ng matinding pandidiri, pagkamuhi, o galit dahil sa kasamaan o karumihan nito.
etymology: From `suklam` (disgust, loathing). The `nakasu-` affix indicates something that causes this intense feeling.
original_explanation: This is a level up from "kadiri". This is for things that make you go "Ewww!" with your whole being. Think spoiled food with crawling things, or yung mga balita tungkol sa corruption na grabe. It’s so bad, it makes your stomach turn and your moral compass spin. **Nakasusuklam**!
usage_notes: A very strong word used to express extreme disgust, either moral or physical.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para sa kanya, **nakasusuklam** ang anumang uri ng karahasan.","translation":"For her, any form of violence is **abominable**."},{"sentence":"Isang **nakasusuklam** na krimen ang natuklasan sa lumang gusali.","translation":"A **loathsome** crime was discovered in the old building."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang ginagamit sa pagtatanong na nagpapahayag ng pagdududa, pagtataka, o kawalan ng paniniwala.
etymology: Hindi tiyak ang pinagmulan, ngunit posibleng nagmula sa sinaunang Tagalog.
original_explanation: The old-school, formal way of saying "Weh, 'di nga?". It's what characters in historical dramas say when they hear something shocking. Today, if you use this in a casual conversation, your friends might look at you funny, as if you just stepped out of a time machine. It's the 'forsooth' of Tagalog.
usage_notes: Medyo luma na at karaniwang maririnig o mababasa sa panitikan, pormal na pananalita, o mga dula na may makasaysayang tagpuan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Diyata**'t nagawa mo iyon sa iyong sariling kapatid?","translation":"**Is it really so** that you did that to your own sibling?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang teknolohiya na nagpapahintulot sa mga elektronikong kagamitan tulad ng kompyuter at smartphone na kumonekta sa internet o makipag-ugnayan sa isa't isa nang walang ginagamit na kable sa loob ng isang partikular na lugar.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na "Wi-Fi", isang trademark na pangalan para sa mga produkto ng IEEE 802.11x.
original_explanation: Ang pinakamahalagang elemento sa isang bahay, mas mahalaga pa minsan kaysa sa tubig. Ito ang dahilan kung bakit ang unang tanong sa mga coffee shop ay "Anong password ng wifi?" at hindi "Kamusta ka?". Kapag mabagal ito, parang end of the world na. Kapag nawala, national crisis.
usage_notes: Ginagamit nang walang pagbabago sa baybay o kahulugan sa Pilipinas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakitanong naman kung ano ang password ng **wifi** nila.","translation":"Can you please ask what their **Wi-Fi** password is."},{"sentence":"Mahina ang signal ng **wifi** dito sa kwarto ko.","translation":"The **Wi-Fi** signal is weak here in my room."}]

translation: The act of slipping; a slip
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng di-sinasadyang paggalaw o pagbagsak dahil sa madulas na ibabaw; maaari ding tumukoy sa di-sinasadyang pagbanggit ng isang bagay (slip of the tongue).
original_explanation: Two kinds! 1) The literal 'Wet Floor' sign moment. You're walking, then suddenly you're doing an unplanned split because of a slippery floor. That's 'pagkadulas'. 2) The figurative 'Oops, sinabi ko ba 'yon?' moment. A slip of the tongue. You accidentally reveal a secret or say something you shouldn't have. Your mouth was the slippery floor and the secret was you. 'Dahil sa pagkadulas ng dila niya, nalaman ng lahat.'
usage_notes: Can be literal (slipping on a surface) or figurative (slip of the tongue - 'pagkadulas ng dila').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa sahig para maiwasan ang **pagkadulas**.","translation":"Be careful on the floor to avoid **slipping**."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagkadulas** ng dila ang naglantad ng kanilang sikreto.","translation":"His **slip** of the tongue exposed their secret."}]

translation: to contemplate on something; to ponder deeply
meaning_filipino: Isipin nang malalim at paulit-ulit; bulay-bulayin ang isang bagay.
etymology: From the reduplicated root "muni-muni", with the prefix "pag-" and suffix "-hin" to create a passive verb.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of that 3 AM ceiling-staring session. It's what you do to a problem or a major life decision. "Should I resign from my BPO job to open a coffee shop?" You don't just think about it, you **pagmuni-munihin** it. You make a pros and cons list, ask the universe for a sign, and overthink it for a week.
usage_notes: A passive verb. It means to make something the object of deep thought. The object being contemplated is the focus.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **pagmuni-munihin** ang mga susunod mong hakbang sa buhay.","translation":"You need **to contemplate deeply on** your next steps in life."},{"sentence":"Ating **pagmuni-munihin** ang tunay na kahulugan ng kalayaan.","translation":"Let us **ponder deeply** on the true meaning of freedom."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pook na pinatibay ng mga pader, moog, at iba pang depensa upang maprotektahan ang mga nasa loob laban sa pagsalakay.
etymology: From Malay 'kota' (fort, town), from Sanskrit 'koṭa' (fort, stronghold).
original_explanation: Your bedroom when you don't want to do chores. It's your personal Batcave, your headquarters, your safe space. Historically, it's where heroes made their last stand. Today, it's where you hide from your responsibilities with a phone and a charger.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for a military structure (e.g., Intramuros) or figuratively for a personal sanctuary or a group's base.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Intramuros ay isang makasaysayang **kuta** sa Maynila.","translation":"Intramuros is a historical **fortress** in Manila."},{"sentence":"Ang silid-aklatan ang nagsisilbing **kuta** niya laban sa ingay ng mundo.","translation":"The library serves as his **stronghold** against the noise of the world."}]

translation: will be made to shudder; will be terrified
meaning_filipino: Dudulutan ng matinding takot o pandidiri na magiging sanhi ng panginginig ng katawan.
original_explanation: This is the goal of every Filipino horror movie. They want to scare you so much that you get goosebumps. "Sa kuwento pa lang niya tungkol sa multo sa opisina, **papangilabutin** ka na." (Just from his story about the office ghost, you will already be made to shudder.) It's the feeling you get when you see a huge ipis flying towards you.
usage_notes: Describes an intense reaction of fear, horror, or disgust that causes goosebumps or shudders.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tiyak na **papangilabutin** ang mga manonood sa bagong horror film.","translation":"The audience **will surely be made to shudder** by the new horror film."},{"sentence":"Sino ba namang hindi **papangilabutin** sa ganoong krimen?","translation":"Who wouldn't **be horrified** by such a crime?"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na lalong nagiging makapal o sa isang tao na nawawalan ng hiya.
original_explanation: Two meanings! 1. Physical: 'Yung makeup mong pakapal na nang pakapal habang tumatagal ang party. 2. Attitude: 'Yung ka-officemate mong pakapal na nang pakapal ang mukha, nanghihiram ng pera pero 'di nagbabayad. It's the gradual increase of either thickness or audacity.
usage_notes: Often used in the phrase 'pakapal nang pakapal.' The `pa-` prefix here denotes a process or direction ('becoming'). It is also often used with 'mukha' (face) to mean 'becoming more shameless'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pakapal** na ang usok mula sa nasusunog na gusali.","translation":"The smoke from the burning building is **getting thicker**."},{"sentence":"Grabe, **pakapal** na nang **pakapal** ang mukha niya sa pang-aabuso sa kabaitan mo.","translation":"Wow, his/her audacity is **getting more and more shameless** in abusing your kindness."}]

translation: to cause to miss or fail; to cause a blunder
meaning_filipino: Ang maging sanhi ng pagkabigo, pagkakamali, o hindi pagtama sa isang layunin o target.
original_explanation: Ever tried to help someone but ended up making things worse? That's you, *nagpasablay*. It's the vibe of that one groupmate who submits their part late, causing the whole project to get a lower grade. Or when you try to set up two friends, but your awkward introduction just makes it weird. You didn't mean to, but... *sablay*.
usage_notes: 'Sablay' colloquially means a miss, a failure, or an epic fail. 'Magpasablay' means to be the cause of that failure.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ingay mula sa labas ang **nagpasablay** sa kanyang konsentrasyon.","translation":"The noise from outside **caused his concentration to fail**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magpasablay** sa ating presentasyon bukas; mag-praktis kang mabuti.","translation":"Don't **cause our presentation to fail** tomorrow; practice well."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghila sa isang bagay o tao nang may puwersa sa isang ibabaw, na karaniwang nagdudulot ng hirap o pagtutol.
original_explanation: What you do with your friend who's had too much to drink at the party. You don't carry them, you kumaladkad them to the taxi. It's also what you do with a super heavy maleta at the airport when you refuse to pay for a cart. It implies difficulty, friction, and a lack of grace.
usage_notes: Ipinahihiwatig nito ang paghila ng isang bagay na mabigat o ayaw sumama sa lupa o sahig.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumaladkad** siya ng isang malaking sako ng bigas papasok ng bahay.","translation":"He **dragged** a large sack of rice into the house."},{"sentence":"Ayaw sumama ng bata kaya **kumaladkad** ito sa sahig habang nagmamaktol.","translation":"The child didn't want to go, so he **dragged** himself on the floor while throwing a tantrum."}]

translation: a light tap or knock on the head
meaning_filipino: Isang bahagya at magaan na pagpalo o pag-untog sa ulo, karaniwang gamit ang mga buko ng daliri (knuckles).
original_explanation: That playful little tap on the head your lola gives you when you're being 'makulit' (pesky). It's not a full-on 'batok' (hit on the nape), more like a 'kutusan' but gentler. It's a gesture of affectionate correction, like, 'You're being silly again.'
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb (dinukdok).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **dukdok** ang natanggap niya mula sa kanyang kuya.","translation":"He received a light **tap on the head** from his older brother."},{"sentence":"Dinukdok niya nang bahagya ang ulo ng kapatid niyang natutulog.","translation":"He lightly **tapped** the head of his sleeping sibling."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagbaba ng halaga, kalidad, o katayuan; paghina o pagbagsak.
etymology: Possibly related to 'dausdos', but referring to a more abstract decline.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your bank account after the 12.12 sale. It's the slow, sad slide from 'payday rich' to 'petsa de peligro broke.' It can also describe the **dausos** of a celebrity's career after a scandal, or the decline of your motivation on a Wednesday afternoon. It's a downward spiral, but in a more poetic, less dramatic way.
usage_notes: Often refers to a decline in quality, status, or economy, not a physical slide.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakikita natin ang unti-unting **dausos** ng moralidad sa lipunan.","translation":"We are seeing the gradual **decline** of morality in society."},{"sentence":"Ang pagbagsak ng stock market ay nagdulot ng **dausos** sa ekonomiya.","translation":"The stock market crash caused a **slump** in the economy."}]

translation: to eat leftover rice; to revive
meaning_filipino: Kainin ang natirang malamig na kanin (bahaw); o alisin ang pagiging luma o hindi na sariwa ng isang bagay o konsepto.
original_explanation: The act of finishing off last night's rice, usually by frying it into sinangag for breakfast. It's the ultimate 'walang tapon' (no waste) move in a Pinoy household. In a figurative sense, it means to 'revive' something old, like a forgotten friendship.
usage_notes: The primary meaning relates to 'bahaw' (stale, leftover rice). The secondary, more figurative meaning of reviving something is less common but poetic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gising na at **bahawin** na natin ang kanin para gawing sinangag.","translation":"Wake up and let's **use the leftover rice** to make fried rice."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan nilang **bahawin** ang dating sigla ng kanilang samahan.","translation":"They are trying **to revive** the old liveliness of their group."}]

meaning_filipino: Gumawa ng isang bagay na eksaktong katulad ng isa pa; gayahin o tularan.
original_explanation: The verb form. What you do during an exam when you didn't study (bad!). What you do to a recipe from a YouTube video (good!). What you do to a file on your computer (neutral!). The action of making a 'kopya'.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang pandiwang nakapokus sa layon (object-focus).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **kopyahin** mo ang lahat ng nasa pisara.","translation":"Please, **copy** everything on the board."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **kopyahin** ang sagot ng katabi mo.","translation":"Don't **copy** the answer of your seatmate."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng katawan sa pahalang na posisyon, karaniwan upang magpahinga o matulog.
original_explanation: Your body's default setting after a long day. Yung feeling na pagod ka na sa lahat—sa work, sa traffic, sa life—at ang gusto mo na lang ay ma-meet ang iyong one true love: ang kama. 'I just wanna lie down and not adult for a while.'
usage_notes: A very common verb for daily activities.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagod na pagod ako, gusto ko nang **humiga**.","translation":"I'm so tired, I just want to **lie down**."},{"sentence":"**Humiga** ka muna at magpahinga.","translation":"**Lie down** for a while and rest."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salita, parirala, o pangungusap na ginagamit bilang taguri, bansag, o motto na naglalarawan sa katangian ng isang tao, lugar, o pangkat.
etymology: From `paN-` + `bansag`. `Bansag` means nickname or title. The prefix `paN-` (which becomes `pam-` before 'b') creates a noun for the means or instrument.
original_explanation: It's a brand tagline or a superhero's title. "The People's Champ" for Manny Pacquiao? That's a 'pamansag'. "It's More Fun in the Philippines"? 'Pamansag' din 'yan. It’s that catchy phrase that sticks, your personal or group's hashtag for life.
usage_notes: Often associated with branding, historical figures, or formal titles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang '**Perlas ng Silanganan**' ay isang tanyag na **pamansag** para sa Pilipinas.","translation":"'**Pearl of the Orient**' is a famous **epithet** for the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Naging **pamansag** ng kanilang samahan ang 'Pagkakaisa at Pag-unlad'.","translation":"'Unity and Progress' became the **motto** of their organization."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng paraan upang ang isang bagay na nakatago o wala ay makita o lumabas.
etymology: From `magpa-` (causative prefix) and `litaw` (to appear, to surface).
original_explanation: The ultimate 'sana all' skill. It's what you wish your wallet could do with money during 'petsa de peligro'. Magicians do this with rabbits, ghosts do this in horror movies ('nagpapalitaw'), and your friend who suddenly shows up after someone mentions free food is an expert at this.
usage_notes: A causative verb. The subject causes something to appear. Can be used for physical objects, ghosts, or abstract things like feelings. Not to be confused with 'palitaw', the rice cake, though the food is named after the verb 'lumitaw' (to surface/appear) which it does when cooked.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang **magpalitaw** ng ebidensya para patunayan ang kanyang kaso.","translation":"He is trying **to bring forth** evidence to prove his case."},{"sentence":"Bigla siyang **nagpalitaw** ng pera mula sa kanyang bulsa.","translation":"He suddenly **made** money **appear** from his pocket."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lugar o bintana sa isang sinehan, teatro, o istadyum kung saan ibinebenta ang mga tiket. Tumutukoy din ito sa kabuuang kita ng isang palabas mula sa pagbebenta ng tiket.
original_explanation: This is where your movie date dreams begin (or end, if the movie is sold out). The **takilya** is that little window where you pay for a ticket to another world. It's also the showbiz term for a movie's earnings. 'Malakas sa takilya' means it's a blockbuster hit, and the producers are probably swimming in money.
usage_notes: Can refer to the physical ticket booth or to the overall ticket sales/revenue ('box office gross').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumila kami nang maaga sa **takilya** para makakuha ng magandang upuan.","translation":"We lined up early at the **ticket booth** to get good seats."},{"sentence":"Naging 'box office hit' ang pelikula at kumita nang malaki sa **takilya**.","translation":"The movie became a 'box office hit' and earned a lot at the **box office**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang wakas ng panahon o paggunaw ng daigdig. Ginagamit din bilang isang idyoma para sa isang matinding problema o sakuna.
original_explanation: Literally, the apocalypse. But for Pinoys, it's also any minor inconvenience that feels major. Failed an exam? Katapusan ng mundo na. Iniwan ka ng jowa? Katapusan ng mundo. Walang Wi-Fi? OMG, katapusan ng mundo na talaga! It's our go-to phrase for being dramatic about a crisis.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for the apocalypse or, more commonly, hyperbolically for a major personal crisis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi pa **katapusan ng mundo** kahit bumagsak ka sa pagsusulit.","translation":"Don't worry, it's not the **end of the world** even if you failed the exam."},{"sentence":"Maraming pelikula ang tungkol sa **katapusan ng mundo**.","translation":"There are many movies about the **end of the world**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang magdulot ng kalituhan o pagkalito sa isipan ng isang tao; gawing hindi malinaw o mahirap unawain ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you try to understand government agency procedures, or when your crush gives you mixed signals. One day they're hot, the next day they're cold. To 'manlito' is to intentionally or unintentionally scramble someone's brain until they go, 'Huh? Ano daw?' It's the favorite tactic of confusing instruction manuals.
usage_notes: Can be intentional (to confuse someone on purpose) or unintentional (the speech was confusing).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga pabago-bagong patakaran ay sadyang **nanlito** sa mga mamamayan.","translation":"The ever-changing rules truly **confused** the citizens."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **panlituhin** ang usapan, diretsuhin mo na.","translation":"Don't **confuse** the conversation, just get straight to the point."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghampas sa mukha ng isang tao gamit ang bukas na palad, na isasagawa sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: Future tense of 'sampal'. This is what your nanay threatens to do when you talk back, or what you want to do to your ex's new partner but you won't because you're a classy person. It's the physical manifestation of "how dare you?!"
usage_notes: This is the future tense of the verb 'sampal'. The 'sa-' prefix indicates future action for root words starting with 's'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kapag hindi ka tumigil, **sasampal**in kita!","translation":"If you don't stop, I **will slap** you!"},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong subukan, dahil **sasampal** talaga ako sa'yo.","translation":"Don't test me, because I really **will slap** you."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aayos o pagpapangkat-pangkat ng mga bagay o konsepto ayon sa kanilang katangian, klase, o uri.
original_explanation: Ito yung ginagawa mo sa mga ex mo. May "The One That Got Away" category, may "What Was I Thinking?" folder, at may "Never Again" archive. Ikaw na ang umuri sa kanila.
usage_notes: This is a more formal or literary term. In common speech, "pagbukud-bukurin" or "i-classify" are more frequent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng siyentipiko na **umuri** sa mga bagong tuklas na halaman.","translation":"The scientist tried **to classify** the newly discovered plants."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **umuri** sa mga tao batay lamang sa kanilang panlabas na anyo.","translation":"It is difficult **to categorize** people based only on their external appearance."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang antas ng alat ng tubig, partikular na ang tubig na bahagyang maalat dahil sa paghahalo ng tubig-tabang at tubig-dagat, na karaniwang matatagpuan sa mga bukana ng ilog.
original_explanation: This is that 'not quite fresh, not quite salty' water you find where a river meets the sea. It's the taste of a fishpond (palaisdaan) or a mangrove forest. If you've ever accidentally swallowed water while swimming near an estuary, you've tasted tabsing. It's nature's version of a mixed drink.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to the saltiness or brackishness, not just any salty taste. Often used in contexts of aquaculture and coastal geography.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasanay na ang mga isda sa **tabsing** ng tubig sa palaisdaan.","translation":"The fish have gotten used to the **brackishness** of the water in the fishpond."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa pagtaas ng dagat, tumaas din ang **tabsing** sa mga kalapit na ilog.","translation":"Due to sea-level rise, the **saltiness** in nearby rivers also increased."}]

translation: to take responsibility for; to claim ownership
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtanggap sa responsibilidad o pagkakasala para sa isang gawain, pangyayari, o bagay.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'ako' (I/me) at unlaping '-um-'.
original_explanation: The opposite of 'turo-turo' (pointing fingers). This is when you raise your hand and say, 'It was me.' It's owning up to your mistake, like when you accidentally CC'd the whole company on a private email. A true leader knows how to 'umako ng pagkakamali'. It's the 'sana all' of accountability.
usage_notes: Often followed by 'ng' or 'sa' to specify what is being taken responsibility for (e.g., umako ng kasalanan, umako sa responsibilidad).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Walang gustong **umako** sa basag na plorera.","translation":"No one wanted **to take responsibility** for the broken vase."},{"sentence":"Bilang lider, dapat kang **umako** sa resulta ng desisyon ng grupo.","translation":"As a leader, you should **take ownership** of the results of the group's decision."}]

translation: to pay in advance for someone; to cover a cost temporarily
meaning_filipino: Ang pansamantalang pagbabayad para sa gastos ng iba, na may inaasahang pagsasauli sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: The official verb of every team lunch. There's always that one person who says, "Sige, ako muna **mag-aabono**," and then spends the next week chasing people down with a G-Cash QR code. It's a gesture of generosity mixed with the mild anxiety of tracking who has and hasn't paid you back yet.
usage_notes: This meaning is distinct from its agricultural use (to fertilize). It implies a temporary covering of costs.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pwede bang ikaw muna ang **mag-abono** para sa pagkain? Naiwan ko ang wallet ko.","translation":"Can you **pay** for the food for now? I left my wallet."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdating sa isang lugar, panahon, o kalagayan; ang pag-abot sa isang tiyak na punto.
original_explanation: The more poetic, dramatic cousin of 'dumating'. You don't just *sumapit* at the mall. You *sumapit* at a destination after a long journey. A specific time, like midnight on New Year's Eve, also *sumasapit*. It’s arrival with a capital A.
usage_notes: Often used in a more formal, literary, or temporal context than the more common 'dumating'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nang **sumapit** ang takipsilim, nagsimula na silang maglakad pauwi.","translation":"When dusk **arrived**, they started walking home."},{"sentence":"Maligayang Pasko! **Sumapit** na ang araw na pinakahihintay nating lahat.","translation":"Merry Christmas! The day we've all been waiting for has **come**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bilang na katumbas ng sampung daan (1,000); ginagamit din bilang pang-uri upang tukuyin ang dami.
original_explanation: The number that makes your Shopee or Lazada cart feel heavy. 'Isang **libo**' is the blue bill, the Aguinaldo you hoped to get from your ninong, and the price of a decent buffet. It’s also used for exaggeration, as in '**Libo**-libong beses ko nang sinabi sa'yo!' (I've told you a thousand times!).
usage_notes: Often used with 'isang' (one) to mean 'one thousand' (sanlibo). Can be reduplicated as 'libo-libo' to mean 'thousands'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkakahalaga ng isang **libo**ng piso ang sapatos na iyon.","translation":"Those shoes cost one **thousand** pesos."},{"sentence":"**Libo**-libong tao ang nanood ng konsiyerto.","translation":"**Thousands** of people watched the concert."}]

translation: To dawn; for dawn to break
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsisimula ng araw kung kailan unang lumilitaw ang sinag ng araw sa abot-tanaw; pag-uumaga.
etymology: From `mag-` (verb-forming prefix) + `bukang-liwayway` (dawn), which is a compound of `buka` (open) and `liwayway` (dawn).
original_explanation: The official start time for BPO night-shifters going home, for early-bird joggers, and for your tita's "Good Morning" posts on Facebook with a picture of a coffee cup. `Magbukang-liwayway` is when the sky starts to lighten up, signaling the end of marathon Netflix sessions and the beginning of a new day full of possibilities (or just traffic).
usage_notes: This is a verb phrase. The noun is `bukang-liwayway` (dawn).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating umalis bago **magbukang-liwayway** para maiwasan ang trapik.","translation":"We need to leave before **dawn breaks** to avoid the traffic."}]

translation: for the twelfth; intended for the twelfth
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na para sa ikalabindalawa sa isang pagkakasunod-sunod, o bilang pamilang na panunuran.
original_explanation: For the 12th person in line, the 12th item on the list, or the 12th placer. "Ito ang premyo para sa **panlabindalawa**." It's that specific ordinal marker you rarely use unless you're organizing a race with lots of participants or listing down your 12 exes.
usage_notes: Part of a series of ordinal determiners formed with `pan-` + [number], e.g., `pampito` (for the seventh), `panwalo` (for the eighth).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tropeong ito ay para sa **panlabindalawa** na kalahok na makatapos sa karera.","translation":"This trophy is for the **twelfth** participant to finish the race."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sangay ng pamahalaan na namamahala sa paglilitis at pagbibigay-kahulugan sa mga batas; ang gusali o lugar kung saan isinasagawa ang mga paglilitis.
original_explanation: The place where dreams of a quick legal victory go to die in a mountain of paperwork. It's the ultimate "See you in court!" destination. If you end up here, you're either suing someone, being sued, or you're an abogado who lives on coffee and contempt of court citations.
usage_notes: Refers to the court system or the physical courthouse itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala ang akusado sa **husgado** para sa pagbasa ng sakdal.","translation":"The accused was brought to the **courthouse** for the arraignment."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang tiwala ng tao sa ating **husgado**.","translation":"The people have great faith in our **judiciary**."}]

translation: in a state of confused excitement; chaotic
meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng matinding kaguluhan, ingay, o pagkasabik kung saan hindi na magkaintindihan o magkarinigan ang mga tao.
etymology: Mula sa "di-" (not/unable) at "magkamayaw" (to agree or be in unison). Ang "mayaw" ay isang lumang salita na nangangahulugang pag-awat o pagpapatigil.
original_explanation: Imagine mo yung 12.12 sale ng Shopee o Lazada, tapos may piso flash deal. Yung aabangan mo tapos pag-click mo, sold out na. Yung reaction ng lahat? 'Yan ang di-magkamayaw. Pwede ring reaction ng fans sa concert ng K-Pop group. Sigawan to the max!
usage_notes: Often used to describe a crowd's reaction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Di-magkamayaw** ang mga tao sa panonood ng laban ni Pacquiao.","translation":"The people were in a **state of confused excitement** watching Pacquiao's fight."},{"sentence":"Nang lumabas ang banda, ang mga manonood ay **di-magkamayaw** sa pagsigaw.","translation":"When the band came out, the audience was **chaotically** screaming."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na instrumentong de-kuwerdas na kahawig ng gitara, na nagmula sa Hawaii.
etymology: Hiram sa Ingles na 'ukulele', na mula sa Hawaiian na 'ʻukulele' (tumatalon na pulgas).
original_explanation: The official instrument of beach trips, indie movie soundtracks, and that one tito who wants to serenade everyone at the family reunion. It's like a guitar that went on a diet. Smaller, cuter, and sounds like instant good vibes.
usage_notes: This is a direct loanword and is spelled and used similarly to its English counterpart.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinutugtog niya ang paborito niyang kanta sa kanyang **yukulele**.","translation":"He is playing his favorite song on his **ukulele**."},{"sentence":"Niregaluhan niya ako ng isang **yukulele** noong Pasko.","translation":"She gifted me a **ukulele** for Christmas."}]

meaning_filipino: Naaayon sa batas; ipinahihintulot o kinikilala ng batas.
etymology: Hiram sa salitang Ingles na "legal", na mula sa Latin na "legalis".
original_explanation: The opposite of "colorum." It's what you want your driver's license, your business permit, and your marriage to be. When someone says, "Let's make it legal," they're either talking about signing a contract or proposing marriage. Both involve a lot of paperwork.
usage_notes: Maaaring bigkasin na may diin sa unang pantig (/LI-gal/) na impluwensya ng Ingles, o sa ikalawang pantig (/le-GAL/) na impluwensya ng Espanyol.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siguraduhin mong **legal** ang lahat ng dokumento bago ka pumirma.","translation":"Make sure all the documents are **legal** before you sign."},{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **legal** na ang aming kasal!","translation":"Finally, our marriage is **legal**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang trabaho ay itala ang mga transaksyong pampinansyal ng isang negosyo.
original_explanation: The Filipinized spelling of "bookkeeper." This is the person in the office who actually knows where the money is going. They're the master of receipts, ledgers, and Excel sheets. Don't mess with the bukkiper, especially when it's time to file for reimbursement.
usage_notes: This is a phonetic spelling of the English word. In formal writing, 'bookkeeper' or the Spanish-derived 'tenedor de libros' might be preferred, but 'bukkiper' is common in spoken language.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating kumuha ng bagong **bukkiper** para sa kumpanya.","translation":"We need to hire a new **bookkeeper** for the company."},{"sentence":"Tinanong ng **bukkiper** kung nasaan ang mga resibo.","translation":"The **bookkeeper** asked where the receipts were."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang estado o kalagayan na kabaligtaran, salungat, o baligtad mula sa karaniwan o inaasahan.
original_explanation: This is when everything goes the opposite of how you planned. You expected a sunny day, but it rained. You thought you'd save money, but then the 11.11 sale happened. It's the universe playing a prank on you. "Ang nangyari ay tumbalik sa aming inaasahan." It's irony in one word. Like wanting to be productive but ending up binge-watching for 8 hours.
usage_notes: Often implies an ironic or unexpected reversal. It's a more literary or formal word than "kabaligtaran."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **tumbalik** ang resulta ng eleksyon sa mga hula ng mga survey.","translation":"The election result became the **inverse** of the survey predictions."},{"sentence":"Anong **tumbalik** na kapalaran, ang manggagamot ay siyang nagkasakit.","translation":"What an **ironic** (reversed) fate, the healer is the one who got sick."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis at malakas na pagtibok o pintig ng puso, karaniwan dahil sa takot, kaba, o matinding damdamin. Maaari ring mangahulugang pagdaig o paglamang sa iba.
original_explanation: This is that intense heartbeat you get right before a job interview, when you see your crush, or when your mom calls you using your full name. It's the 'dug-dug-dug' sound effect of your life's most dramatic moments. It can also mean to outshine or upstage someone. 'Kinabog niya ang lahat sa pageant!' means she totally slayed the competition.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for a heartbeat ('kabog ng dibdib') or figuratively to mean 'to defeat' or 'to upstage' ('kinabog').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang malakas na **kabog** ng dibdib ko nang tawagin ang pangalan ko.","translation":"I heard the loud **throb** of my chest when my name was called."},{"sentence":"Kinabog ng bagong singer ang mga dati nang sikat.","translation":"The new singer **upstaged** the already famous ones."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na ginagamit upang pagkabitin, iugnay, o pahabain ang dalawa o higit pang bagay.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `pan-` (gamit para sa) at salitang ugat na `dugsong` (to join/append).
original_explanation: That piece you need to connect or extend something. It's the extension cord for your phone charger, the 'Part 2' of a chismis, the 'continued...' at the end of a series, or the extra carriage on the MRT during rush hour. Anything that bridges a gap.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa isang pisikal na bagay (connector, link) o isang konsepto (addendum, continuation).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawawala ang **pandugsong** para sa hose kaya hindi natin magamit.","translation":"The **connector** for the hose is missing so we can't use it."},{"sentence":"Magsusulat ako ng **pandugsong** sa kwento dahil marami ang nag-request.","translation":"I will write a **continuation** to the story because many requested it."}]

meaning_filipino: Muling pumasok sa isipan; hindi nalimutan.
original_explanation: That "Aha!" moment when you finally remember where you left your keys. Or, the more painful version, when you suddenly remember the cringey thing you did in high school. It's the past tense of remembering something you previously knew. "Bigla kong natandaan na may exam pala kami ngayon!"
usage_notes: Past tense of the verb 'matandaan'. Often used interchangeably with 'naalala'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Natandaan** mo ba ang sinabi ko sa iyo kahapon?","translation":"Did you **remember** what I told you yesterday?"},{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **natandaan** din niya ang pangalan ko.","translation":"Finally, he **remembered** my name."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng mabilis na reaksiyong kemikal sa pagitan ng isang sangkap at isang oxidant, karaniwang oxygen, upang makabuo ng init at liwanag. Ang proseso ng pagsunog.
original_explanation: That science-y word for "pagsunog" or burning. It’s what happens inside your car's engine, or what happens to your brain cells when you're cramming for an exam. Also, "spontaneous human combustion" is what you jokingly threaten when your internet connection dies during a crucial online meeting.
usage_notes: Primarily a scientific or technical term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang internal **kombustyon** engine ay gumagamit ng pagsabog ng gasolina para paganahin ang sasakyan.","translation":"The internal **combustion** engine uses the explosion of gasoline to power the vehicle."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang serye sa telebisyon o streaming platform na paulit-ulit na pinapanood ng isang tao upang makaramdam ng kaginhawaan, pamilyaridad, at kasiyahan.
original_explanation: The TV show equivalent of comfort food. Ito 'yung series na kahit kabisado mo na ang bawat linya (e.g., Friends, The Office, Reply 1988), uulitin mo pa ring panoorin kasi parang bumibisita ka lang sa mga luma mong kaibigan. Perfect background noise habang nagtatrabaho o kumakain.
usage_notes: Isang konsepto na naging popular sa panahon ng streaming services tulad ng Netflix.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang *Friends* ang **comfort series** ko; pinapanood ko 'pag nalulungkot ako.","translation":"*Friends* is my **comfort series**; I watch it whenever I'm sad."},{"sentence":"Naghahanap ako ng bagong **comfort series** sa Netflix.","translation":"I'm looking for a new **comfort series** on Netflix."}]

translation: to grope for; to search for by feeling
meaning_filipino: Hanapin ang isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng kamay o pakiramdam, lalo na sa dilim o kapag hindi makakita.
original_explanation: This is what you do when the power goes out and you're trying to find your phone or a candle. It's the "kapay-kapay sa dilim" move. Also applies to that moment you're trying to find your keys in a bag that has become a black hole of receipts, old candy, and random stuff.
usage_notes: Often implies searching blindly or with difficulty.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nang mamatay ang ilaw, sinubukan niyang **apuhapin** ang kandila sa mesa.","translation":"When the lights went out, he tried to **grope for** the candle on the table."},{"sentence":"In**apuhap** niya ang switch ng ilaw sa madilim na silid.","translation":"He **searched by feeling** for the light switch in the dark room."}]

meaning_filipino: Magbigay ng basbas o pabor mula sa Diyos; magsagawa ng isang seremonya ng pagbabasbas.
original_explanation: What the priest does with holy water during fiestas, or what your lola does before you leave for a long trip. It’s asking for divine good vibes and protection, like a spiritual 'ingat!' or 'God bless.'
usage_notes: Primarily used in a religious or deeply respectful cultural context, like asking for a parent's or elder's blessing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumunta ang pamilya sa pari upang **magbendisyon** ng kanilang bagong sasakyan.","translation":"The family went to the priest to **bless** their new car."},{"sentence":"Ang lola ay laging handang **magbendisyon** sa kanyang mga apo.","translation":"The grandmother is always ready to **give a blessing** to her grandchildren."}]

translation: to find something beautiful; to be charmed by
meaning_filipino: Maging maganda sa paningin ng isang tao; maakit o humanga sa ganda ng isang bagay o tao.
original_explanation: This isn't just "to be beautiful" (that's 'maganda'). This is the *act of perceiving* beauty. It's when you're scrolling through IG and a post makes you stop and go, "Wow." That's you, 'nagagandahan'. It's that feeling when you see a perfect sunset, a stunning outfit, or your crush. "Nagandahan ako sa view sa Tagaytay." It's an internal reaction, a verb of appreciation.
usage_notes: Often used with "na-" (nagandahan) or in the actor-focus form "magandahan". It's a psychological verb. The structure is often "[Actor] ay nagandahan sa [Object]." (e.g., "Ako ay nagandahan sa damit mo.")
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay **magandahan** ka sa regalong pinili ko para sa iyo.","translation":"I hope you **will find** the gift I chose for you **beautiful**."},{"sentence":"Talagang **nagandahan** ang mga turista sa mga dalampasigan ng Palawan.","translation":"The tourists were truly **charmed by the beauty of** Palawan's beaches."}]

translation: to apply oil; to become oily
meaning_filipino: Magpahid o lagyan ng langis ang isang bagay; o kaya ay ang pagiging malangis ng isang bagay, tulad ng balat o buhok.
original_explanation: Two scenarios: 1) What you do to a squeaky door hinge or a rusty bike chain. 2) What your face does by 3 PM in the humid Philippine weather, giving you that "natural" highlighter look even if you didn't ask for it. Time to pull out the oil-blotting paper!
usage_notes: Can mean both the act of applying oil ('maglagay ng langis') and the state of becoming oily.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **maglangis** ng makina para hindi ito kalawangin.","translation":"You need **to apply oil** to the engine so it won't rust."},{"sentence":"Kapag mainit ang panahon, madaling **maglangis** ang aking mukha.","translation":"When the weather is hot, my face easily **becomes oily**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isinara nang mariin, ganap, o tuluyan ang isang bagay tulad ng pinto, bintana, o aklat.
original_explanation: More dramatic than just 'isinara'. This is closing something with feelings. You don't just 'isinara' the door on your ex, you **ipinid** it. It's also what you do to your wallet when your friend asks for 'utang' for the fifth time this month.
usage_notes: Carries a sense of finality or firmness compared to the more neutral 'isinara'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigla niyang **ipinid** ang pinto matapos ang aming mainit na pagtatalo.","translation":"He suddenly **slammed shut** the door after our heated argument."},{"sentence":"**Ipinid** niya ang aklat at nagpasiyang tapos na ang kabanatang iyon ng kanyang buhay.","translation":"She **closed** the book and decided that chapter of her life was over."}]

meaning_filipino: Putol o natanggal mula sa pinagkakabitan o kabuuan.
original_explanation: Imagine your Wi-Fi connection in the middle of a crucial online game or a Zoom presentation. That's 'utod'. Or when you're telling a juicy story and someone cuts you off. Your story is 'utod'. It's the feeling of being abruptly disconnected.
usage_notes: Less common than 'putol'. Often heard in provincial dialects.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Utod** ang isang daliri ng karpintero dahil sa aksidente.","translation":"One of the carpenter's fingers was **severed** due to an accident."},{"sentence":"Naging **utod** ang aming pag-uusap nang biglang mamatay ang telepono.","translation":"Our conversation was **cut off** when the phone suddenly died."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang detalyadong impormasyon o utos na nagsasabi kung paano gawin, gamitin, o isagawa ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: 'Yung manual ng IKEA na mas mahirap pa intindihin sa ex mo. O 'yung bilin ng nanay mo bago ka umalis ng bahay: "Mag-ingat ka, 'wag magpagabi, 'wag makipag-usap sa stranger, at iuwi mo 'yung sukli."
usage_notes: Madalas na ipinagpapalit sa salitang 'tagubilin' o 'panuto'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sundin mong mabuti ang bawat **instruksiyon** sa reseta.","translation":"Follow every **instruction** on the prescription carefully."},{"sentence":"Nakalimutan ko ang **instruksiyon** ng guro para sa aming takdang-aralin.","translation":"I forgot the teacher's **instruction** for our homework."}]

translation: to be named; to give a name to
meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng pangalan o bansag ang isang tao, bagay, o lugar.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'i-' at salitang-ugat na 'ngalan' (pangalan).
original_explanation: This is what your parents did when they decided to name you 'John' instead of the cool, unique name you wish you had. It's the act of slapping a label on something. 'Ingalan mo 'yung pusa,' means 'Name the cat,'—which you'll probably name 'Mingming' anyway.
usage_notes: Less common in casual conversation than 'pangalanan'. 'Ingalan' often appears in more formal or literary contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bagong panganak na sanggol ay **ingalan** nating Pag-asa.","translation":"Let's **name** the newborn baby Hope."},{"sentence":"Naisip mo na ba kung ano ang **iingalan** sa bago nating tuta?","translation":"Have you thought about what **to name** our new puppy?"}]

translation: to befriend; to make friends with
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagtatatag o pagbuo ng isang relasyon ng pagkakaibigan sa isang tao.
original_explanation: The adult version of "Do you want to be my friend?" at the playground. It's about finding your 'kumpare' for inuman sessions, your 'mare' for chismisan, or your 'beshie' to send memes to at 3 AM. It’s actively looking for your chosen family.
