translation: to invite, to persuade to come along
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-anyaya o paghikayat sa isang tao na sumama sa isang lugar o gawain.
original_explanation: This is the classic 'Tara, G!' move. When you kumayag your friends for a coffee run or a last-minute beach trip, you're inviting them to join. It’s more active than just a simple invite; there's a sense of persuasion, like 'Sama ka na, kj mo naman eh!'
usage_notes: More common in certain regions of the Philippines. Often interchangeable with 'nagyaya'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **kumayag** sa buong barkada na manood ng sine.","translation":"He was the one who **invited** the whole group to watch a movie."},{"sentence":"Sinong **kumayag** sa iyong sumama sa party?","translation":"Who **persuaded** you to come to the party?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paulit-ulit na pananakit o pagpalo sa isang tao o hayop; matinding bugbog.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung matatanggap mo 'pag 'di ka umuwi sa tamang oras at hinanap ka na ng nanay mo na may hawak na tsinelas. In sports, it's what happens when your favorite team loses by 50 points—gulpi sarado!
usage_notes: Refers to a severe physical beating. The verb form is 'gulpihin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakuha ng matinding **gulpi** ang magnanakaw mula sa mga taumbayan.","translation":"The thief received a severe **beating** from the townspeople."},{"sentence":"Inawat ng pulis ang lalaking gustong **gulpihin** ang kanyang kaaway.","translation":"The police stopped the man who wanted to **maul** his enemy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdadala ng isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pagpapatong nito sa ulo.
original_explanation: The original hands-free carrying method, perfected by palengke vendors and rural folks. You see someone with a "bilao" of kakanin or a basin of fish gracefully balanced on their head, navigating a crowd? That's **sunong**. It’s a skill that requires insane balance and a strong neck.
usage_notes: The action is "sumunong" (actor-focus) or "sunungin" (object-focus). The state of being carried is "nakasunong".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magaling **sumunong** ng banga ang mga katutubo sa aming probinsya.","translation":"The indigenous people in our province are skilled at **carrying** jars **on their heads**."},{"sentence":"Sanay si Aling Nena na **sunungin** ang mabigat na timba ng tubig mula sa poso.","translation":"Aling Nena is used to **carrying** the heavy pail of water from the well **on her head**."}]

translation: to cut something (e.g., fabric, grass) for someone
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa ng paggupit o pagputol ng tela, damo, o katulad na materyal para sa kapakanan o pakiusap ng ibang tao.
original_explanation: This is what you ask your tita who's a seamstress to do for your school project's costume. 'Tita, pa-cut po ng tela' becomes '**Ipagtabas** n'yo po ako ng tela.' It’s the act of cutting something, usually fabric or patterns, for someone else. A true pakiusap verb.
usage_notes: This is a benefactive verb, indicating the action is done for the benefit of someone else. The object being cut is the direct object, and the beneficiary is the indirect object.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakiusap si Ana sa kanyang ina na **ipagtabas** siya ng tela para sa kanyang bestida.","translation":"Ana asked her mother to **cut the fabric for her** for her dress."},{"sentence":"Sino ang pwedeng **ipagtabas** ng mga kartolinang ito para sa dekorasyon?","translation":"Who can I ask to **cut these pieces of cardstock for** the decorations?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-iimbak o pagtatabi ng isang bagay para sa hinaharap, lalo na ang datos sa kompyuter o pera.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na nagsave ka ng work mo bago mag-brownout. Life-saver! O kaya nagsave ka ng pera buong taon para sa 13th month pay, tapos isang 12.12 sale lang, ubos na. Relate?
usage_notes: Past tense of the verb. 'Nagsesave' is present tense, 'magse-save' is future tense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Buti na lang at **nagsave** ako ng kopya ng dokumento.","translation":"It's a good thing I **saved** a copy of the document."},{"sentence":"**Nagsave** siya ng malaking halaga para sa kanyang pagreretiro.","translation":"He **saved** a large amount for his retirement."}]

meaning_filipino: Maningning na kislap o kinang, lalo na mula sa isang bagay na makintab o pinakintab.
original_explanation: Eto yung kislap sa mata mo nung nakita mo yung 13th month pay mo. O kaya yung kinang ng bagong-linis na sahig na ayaw mong tapakan. Parang 'bling-bling' pero mas poetic.
usage_notes: Often used in literature to describe the sparkle of jewels, stars, or eyes. More poetic than 'kislap' or 'kinang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **dagilap** ng mga bituin ay nagsilbing gabay sa mga mangingisda.","translation":"The **sparkle** of the stars served as a guide for the fishermen."},{"sentence":"Nasisilaw ako sa **dagilap** ng kanyang diyamanteng singsing.","translation":"I am dazzled by the **brilliance** of her diamond ring."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawing buntis o magdalang-tao ang isang babae.
original_explanation: The verb that leads to 'buntis'. This is a very direct, and sometimes clinical or blunt, term. It's often used in serious contexts, like in news reports about social issues or in very dramatic telenovela plot twists where the kontrabida reveals a secret. 'Binuntis niya ako!' is a peak teleserye line.
usage_notes: An object-focus verb. The actor-focus counterpart is 'makabuntis' (to be able to impregnate) or 'mangbuntis' (to go around impregnating).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May pananagutan ang sinumang lalaki na **buntisin** ang isang babae.","translation":"Any man has a responsibility when he **impregnates** a woman."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaikling bersyon ng salitang Ingles na 'traditional,' na tumutukoy sa isang bagay, tao, o pag-iisip na nakaugalian, klasiko, o konserbatibo.
etymology: Mula sa pinaikling salitang Ingles na 'traditional'.
original_explanation: A term borrowed from English, often used online to describe someone with 'traditional' values, sometimes ironically. 'You want a harana? Ang trad mo naman, besh.' It's the opposite of 'woke'.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa mga moderno, impormal, at online na pag-uusap. Ito ay direktang hiram na salita at hindi taal na Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Medyo **trad** pa rin ang pananaw niya sa pag-aasawa.","translation":"Her views on marriage are still a bit **traditional**."},{"sentence":"Ayaw niya ng mga bagong gimik, mas gusto niya 'yung **trad** lang.","translation":"He doesn't like new gimmicks, he prefers the ones that are just **traditional**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpalo o paghampas nang may buong lakas, karaniwang gamit ang isang bagay tulad ng pamalo o kahoy.
original_explanation: This is not your friendly 'tapik.' This is the 'I'm-so-done-with-your-nonsense' kind of strike. Imagine your nanay seeing your report card and reaching for the walis tambo. That's a potential hambalusin moment. It's a strike with feeling, with gusto, with extreme prejudice.
usage_notes: The '-in' suffix makes it an object-focused verb, meaning the action is done *to* someone or something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binalaan niya ang magnanakaw na **hahambalusin** niya ito ng tubo kung hindi aalis.","translation":"He warned the thief that he would **strike** him with a pipe if he didn't leave."},{"sentence":"**Hambalusin** mo nga 'yang unan para lumabas ang alikabok.","translation":"**Whack** that pillow to get the dust out."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sasakyang pinalamutian nang marangya para sa mga parada, pista, o prusisyon, na kadalasang nagdadala ng mga tao o imahen.
original_explanation: The official vehicle of fiestas and parades. Whether it's for a beauty queen waving, a company mascot dancing, or a santo looking solemn, the 'karosa' is the star of the show. It's basically a truck disguised with a mountain of flowers, papier-mâché, and glitter.
usage_notes: While it can refer to a religious carriage like 'karos', 'karosa' is also widely used for secular parades (e.g., Flores de Mayo, Christmas parades).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng **karosa** ng aming reyna sa parada.","translation":"Our queen's **float** in the parade is beautiful."}]

translation: to hum; to buzz; to drone
meaning_filipino: Gumawa ng isang malakas, mababa, at tuloy-tuloy na tunog.
original_explanation: This is the sound of your old aircon unit working overtime, the collective *chismis* in the office when a new memo drops, or the sound of a drone flying overhead. It's a low, continuous noise that fills the space. Think of it as the background music to Manila traffic.
usage_notes: Describes a low-frequency, resonant sound.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Humugong** ang buong silid nang ipahayag ang nanalo.","translation":"The whole room **buzzed** when the winner was announced."},{"sentence":"Narinig kong **humugong** ang refrigerator bago ito tuluyang nasira.","translation":"I heard the refrigerator **drone** before it completely broke down."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng panunukso, panlalait, o pagbibirong mapang-inis sa isang tao.
original_explanation: This is the 'asar-talo' starter pack. 'Pagtudyo' is that playful (or sometimes not-so-playful) teasing among friends, siblings, or coworkers. It’s calling your friend 'puyat' because of their eye bags or teasing someone about their crush. It can be harmless fun, but cross the line and it becomes bullying.
usage_notes: Can range from lighthearted teasing to serious mockery.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang madalas na **pagtudyo** ay maaaring makasakit sa damdamin ng isang tao.","translation":"Frequent **teasing** can hurt a person's feelings."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya pinansin ang **pagtudyo** ng kanyang mga kaklase.","translation":"He ignored the **mockery** from his classmates."}]

translation: the act of having said goodbye
meaning_filipino: Ang akto o paraan ng pagsasabi ng paalam; ang sandali matapos magpaalam.
etymology: Mula sa `pagka-` (estado matapos ang kilos) + `pagpaalam` (ang akto ng pagsasabi ng paalam).
original_explanation: This is the "after" picture of saying goodbye. It's that awkward silence after you've said "sige, alis na ako" but you're both still standing there. It's the feeling after you've finally logged off from a toxic job or ended a messy relationship. The pagkapagpaalam is the beginning of the moving on process.
usage_notes: Isang kumplikadong anyo ng pangngalan na nagbibigay-diin sa pagtatapos o estado *matapos* gawin ang kilos ng pagpapaalam. Hindi ito kasing-karaniwan ng "pagpapaalam".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malungkot ang naging **pagkapagpaalam** niya sa kanyang pamilya bago siya umalis papuntang abroad.","translation":"The **way he said goodbye** to his family before leaving to go abroad was sad."},{"sentence":"Matapos ang kanyang **pagkapagpaalam**, hindi na siya muling nagpakita.","translation":"After his **act of saying goodbye**, he never showed up again."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos na gagawin kung saan isang bagay, karaniwan ay isang buton, ay didiinan gamit ang daliri.
etymology: Future tense of 'pindutin', from the root 'pindot'. The first syllable of the root is reduplicated.
original_explanation: Future tense of 'pindot'. It's what you will do to the elevator button, the remote control, or the 'send' button on that risky text message you've been typing for an hour. 'Huwag mong pipindutin 'yan, baka sumabog!'
usage_notes: Refers to the future action of pressing something, usually small like a button or a key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ako ang **pipindot** sa doorbell pagdating natin doon.","translation":"I **will press** the doorbell when we get there."},{"sentence":"Anong numero ang **pipindutin** ko para tawagan ka?","translation":"What number **will** I **press** to call you?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang yugto ng buwan kung saan ito ay hindi nakikita mula sa Daigdig dahil ang naliliwanagang bahagi nito ay nakatalikod sa atin.
original_explanation: That time of the month in the sky when the moon decides to go on 'private mode' or 'incognito'. It's the start of the lunar cycle, perfect for setting new intentions, starting a new project, or for werewolves (aswangs?) to plan their next move. It's the universe's 'new page' button.
usage_notes: Refers to the first lunar phase.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming naniniwala na magandang magtanim sa panahon ng **bagong buwan**.","translation":"Many believe that it is good to plant during the **new moon**."},{"sentence":"Madilim ang gabi dahil **bagong buwan** at walang mga bituin.","translation":"The night is dark because it's a **new moon** and there are no stars."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pagkakaroon ng maraming uri, klase, o anyo; hindi magkakatulad.
etymology: Daglat ng pariralang "iba at iba" (other and other).
original_explanation: The official adjective of a Filipino food court, a Divisoria stall, or the chismis about your neighbor. It's the Pinoy version of 'a wide array of choices.' From iba't ibang ulam sa karinderya to iba't ibang rason kung bakit late ka na naman sa work.
usage_notes: Palaging ginagamit upang ilarawan ang isang pangngalang maramihan, na nagbibigay-diin sa pagkakaiba-iba o variedad.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroong **iba't ibang** kulay ng bulaklak sa hardin.","translation":"There are **various** colors of flowers in the garden."},{"sentence":"Nagmula sa **iba't ibang** panig ng Pilipinas ang mga kalahok.","translation":"The participants came from **different** parts of the Philippines."}]

translation: to persuade; to urge; to induce
meaning_filipino: Ang manghikayat o mag-udyok sa isang tao na gawin ang isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pakiusap o panghihikayat.
original_explanation: This is next-level persuasion. It's not just asking ('humiling'), it's convincing. It's what your friend does to get you to go out on a Friday night when you just want to 'humilata'. It's what sales agents do to make you buy that "essential" item. It's the art of making your "no" a "maybe" and your "maybe" a "sige na nga!"
usage_notes: Stronger than 'makiusap' (to plead) and implies successful or attempted persuasion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinong **humimok** sa'yo na sumali sa paligsahan?","translation":"Who **persuaded** you to join the contest?"},{"sentence":"Kahit anong pilit, hindi niya ako nahimok na ibenta ang lumang bahay.","translation":"No matter how he tried, he couldn't **persuade** me to sell the old house."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paggamit ng suklay upang ayusin ang buhok.
original_explanation: The verb form of what your mom yells at you to do before you leave for school so you don't look like a walking *walis tingting*. "Suklayin mo yang buhok mo, mukha kang pinaglaruan ng pusa!"
usage_notes: This is the command form. The infinitive is "suklayin". The past tense is "sinuklay". The present tense is "sinusuklay". The future tense is "susuklayin".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Suklayin** mo ang buhok ng kapatid mo bago kayo umalis.","translation":"**Comb** your sibling's hair before you leave."},{"sentence":"Gusto kong **suklayin** ang buhok niya na parang sa commercial ng shampoo.","translation":"I want **to comb** her hair like in a shampoo commercial."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang makitid na daanan o kalye sa pagitan ng mga gusali o bahay.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na "esquinita", na nangangahulugang "maliit na kanto".
original_explanation: The shortcut you take to avoid traffic, or where the best street food is hiding. It's the place where your mom warned you not to go after dark, but also where all the neighborhood chismis happens. The lifeblood of a dense Manila barangay.
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang salita, lalo na sa mga lugar na urban.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumaan tayo sa **eskinita** para mas mabilis.","translation":"Let's pass through the **alley** so it's faster."},{"sentence":"May nagtitinda ng masarap na isaw sa **eskinita** malapit sa amin.","translation":"There's someone selling delicious isaw in the **alley** near our place."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghahanda ng pagkain sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng init. Ito ay nasa anyong pautos o pawatas.
original_explanation: The fundamental life skill that determines if you're eating gourmet adobo or just sad instant noodles for dinner. The verb that launches a thousand "Kain tayo!" invitations. "Gusto kong matutong magluto ng Bicol Express."
usage_notes: This is the infinitive form ('to cook') or imperative form ('Cook!'). It's the base from which other tenses like 'nagluto' (cooked) and 'magluluto' (will cook) are formed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magluto** ka na ng hapunan dahil parating na ang mga bisita.","translation":"**Cook** dinner now because the guests are arriving."},{"sentence":"Ang pangarap niya ay **magluto** sa isang sikat na restaurant.","translation":"Her dream is **to cook** in a famous restaurant."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang karaniwang palayaw sa lalaking may pangalang Santiago.
etymology: A diminutive of the Spanish name 'Santiago' (Saint James).
original_explanation: The go-to nickname for any Santiago. If you meet a Filipino named Santiago, there's a 90% chance everyone calls him Tiago. He's either the protagonist in a teleserye running from his past, or that friendly kuya in your barangay who's good at basketball. Think Kapitan Tiago from Noli Me Tángere, but the modern version probably has a vlog.
usage_notes: A very common male nickname in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si **Tiago** raw ang nanalo sa patimpalak sa pagkanta.","translation":"They said **Tiago** won the singing contest."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubos na napuno; wala nang maaaring isilid o idagdag; sagad na sa nilalaman.
original_explanation: Level 99 na pagiging puno. Parang MRT/LRT rush hour, parang jeep na "sampu pa, kasya pa," o parang pasensya mo sa ka-group mong walang ambag. 'Pag sinabi mong "punung-puno ka na," it's either a hugot line or a threat. Choose your fighter.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical space or emotional state. The hyphen is standard.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Punung-puno** na ang bus pero nagsasakay pa rin ang kundoktor.","translation":"The bus is **completely full** but the conductor is still letting people on."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo na akong kausapin, **punung-puno** na ako sa mga problema.","translation":"Don't talk to me anymore, I'm **fed up** with problems."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabayad o pag-abono muna gamit ang sariling pera para sa isang gastusin ng iba, na may inaasahang bayad o reembolso sa hinaharap.
etymology: From `pa-` (causative/request prefix) + `luwal` (out, outside). Literally "to cause to come out [of one's pocket]".
original_explanation: This is the official term for "abono". It’s when your boss asks you to buy office supplies and you use your own money first, expecting to be reimbursed later. "Paki-**paluwal** muna ng pambili ng kape, i-reimburse kita sa sahod." It's the foundation of many office expense reports and a test of trust.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of business expenses, errands, or group purchases. Synonymous with `abono`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakiusap si Ana na kung pwede ay **paluwal** muna ako para sa kanyang pamasahe.","translation":"Ana asked if I could please **advance the payment** for her fare."},{"sentence":"Laging may resibo para sa mga gastos na **paluwal** para sa kumpanya.","translation":"Always have a receipt for expenses **paid out-of-pocket** for the company."}]

translation: Stripped; shredded (e.g., fiber from a plant)
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paghihiwalay o pagtatanggal ng hibla (fiber) mula sa isang bagay, karaniwan sa halaman tulad ng abaka o pinya, sa pamamagitan ng pagkayod o paghila.
etymology: From 'laslas' (to rip, to tear into strips) with the infix '-in-'.
original_explanation: Imagine making a rope from a plant. The act of scraping and pulling the fibers out is 'nilalas'. It's like giving a plant a very rough, one-way haircut to get its strong, stringy bits. Very old-school, pre-Shopee way of getting thread.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of creating textiles, ropes, or native crafts from plant fibers.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabusisi ang paraan kung paano **nilalas** ang hibla ng abaka.","translation":"The way the abaca fiber is **stripped** is meticulous."},{"sentence":"Ang **nilalas** na dahon ng pinya ay ginagawang mamahaling tela.","translation":"The **shredded** pineapple leaves are made into expensive fabric."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagbabahagi ng impormasyon, balita, o mensahe; isang pinagmumulan ng sabi-sabi.
original_explanation: Your "source," your "marites," your "insider." This is the person who holds the information and decides to share it. They can be a formal spokesperson for a company, or your officemate who knows all the chismis. Sila ang nagpapakalat ng balita, for better or for worse.
usage_notes: The connotation (positive, negative, or neutral) depends heavily on the context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **tagasabi** ako na aalis na daw ang boss natin.","translation":"I have an **informant** who says our boss is leaving."},{"sentence":"Ikaw na ang maging **tagasabi** sa klase na walang pasok bukas.","translation":"You be the one to **tell** the class that there are no classes tomorrow."}]

meaning_filipino: Magbigay ng detalye, dahilan, o katwiran upang maging malinaw at maunawaan ang isang bagay.
etymology: From `i-` + `pa-` + `liwanag` (light). Literally, 'to use to make something clear' or 'to bring light to something.'
original_explanation: The classic line heard in every Filipino drama, classroom, and relationship argument: 'Ipaliwanag mo!' It's the demand for clarity when things are malabo (unclear). Whether you're explaining your thesis to a panel or explaining to your mom why you came home at 3 AM, you need to `ipaliwanag` your side. Make it make sense!
usage_notes: A fundamental verb for communication. The object being explained is the focus of the verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaari mo bang **ipaliwanag** kung bakit ka nahuli sa klase?","translation":"Can you **explain** why you were late for class?"},{"sentence":"Mahirap **ipaliwanag** ang nararamdaman ko ngayon.","translation":"It's hard **to explain** what I'm feeling right now."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging dakila, maringal, o kahanga-hanga na nagdudulot ng matinding pagkamangha o paggalang.
original_explanation: This is a very deep, very rare word. It's the feeling you get when you see a perfect Mayon Volcano cone, or when you finally understand a Jose Rizal novel. It's that "wow, ang galing/ganda, naiiyak ako" feeling, but make it intellectual. It's the grandeur of an idea or a view that's almost spiritual.
usage_notes: Extremely formal and literary. You're more likely to encounter this in old books or academic papers than in conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **sublimidad** ng kaniyang mga tula ay hindi matatawaran.","translation":"The **sublimity** of his poems is unparalleled."},{"sentence":"Namangha ang lahat sa **sublimidad** ng tanawin mula sa tuktok ng bundok.","translation":"Everyone was amazed by the **grandeur** of the view from the mountaintop."}]

meaning_filipino: Magpakita ng kilos o asal na mapaglaro at may pahiwatig ng romantikong interes sa isang tao.
original_explanation: The national pastime, charot! It's when you're being extra charming, witty, or pa-cute to someone you're interested in. It's the "How you doin'?" of the Philippines. Whether it's a subtle smile, a witty comment on their IG story, or a full-on harana, you're trying to catch their attention.
usage_notes: Can have a slightly negative or playful connotation depending on the context. "Malandi" (the adjective form) is often used more pejoratively, especially towards women, but is being reclaimed in modern slang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **lumandi** sa opisina, baka mapunta ka sa HR.","translation":"Don't **flirt** in the office, you might end up at HR."},{"sentence":"Napangiti siya nang makitang sinusubukang **lumandi** sa kanya ng torpeng binata.","translation":"She smiled when she saw the shy young man trying **to flirt** with her."}]

translation: to suppress, to quell, to stop
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpigil, pagpapatigil, o pagpapahinto sa isang gawain, kaguluhan, o pag-unlad ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the "Stop! In the name of love" ng mga Pinoy authorities. When a riot is about to break out or your two titas are fighting over the last piece of lechon, someone needs to 'sawatahin' the gulo. It's crowd control, but for everything from chismis to actual protests.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of controlling crowds, riots, or intense arguments. Verb forms include sinawata (past), sinasawata (present), sasawatain (future).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng mga pulis na **sawatahin** ang nagkakagulong mga raliyista.","translation":"The police tried to **quell** the rowdy protesters."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **sawatahin** ang pagkalat ng maling impormasyon sa social media.","translation":"It's difficult to **stop** the spread of misinformation on social media."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang kontrolin ang sariling damdamin, pagnanasa, o pag-uugali, lalo na sa mga mahihirap o mapanuksong sitwasyon.
original_explanation: This is the superpower you need when you see a 12.12 sale on Shopee but it's not payday yet. It's what you practice when your boss gives you 'for revision' feedback for the 5th time. It's the immense strength required not to eat the last piece of lechon at a party.
usage_notes: A compound concept from 'pagpipigil' (restraining) and 'sarili' (self).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng matinding **pagpipigil sa sarili** upang hindi magalit sa gitna ng trapiko.","translation":"Intense **self-control** is needed to not get angry in the middle of traffic."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagpipigil sa sarili** ay isang mahalagang katangian.","translation":"**Self-restraint** is an important trait."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang elementong kemikal na may simbolong Na at atomic number 11. Ito ay isang malambot, kulay-pilak na puting metal na lubhang reaktibo.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Ingles na "Sodium", na isina-Tagalog ang baybay.
original_explanation: The scientific name for "alat." Ito yung dahilan kung bakit masarap ang instant noodles, chichirya, at fries. It's the "S" in MSG that makes food addictive. Doctors and your nanay will tell you to cut down on Sodyum to avoid high blood pressure, but sometimes, a high-sodium life is a happy life (for your taste buds, at least).
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa kontekstong siyentipiko, pangkalusugan, o nutrisyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mataas sa **sodyum** ang mga pagkaing de-lata.","translation":"Canned goods are high in **sodium**."},{"sentence":"Pinayuhan siya ng doktor na bawasan ang pagkonsumo ng **sodyum**.","translation":"The doctor advised him to reduce his **sodium** intake."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking may sakit na ketong.
original_explanation: The male version of 'leprosa'. A term for a man with leprosy, usually heard in historical contexts or when reading Noli Me Tángere. Like its female counterpart, it’s a word loaded with historical baggage and stigma.
usage_notes: A dated and potentially offensive term. Modern medical terms are preferred.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inalagaan ni Maria Clara ang isang **leproso** sa isang kabanata ng Noli Me Tángere.","translation":"Maria Clara took care of a **male leper** in a chapter of Noli Me Tángere."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamataas na punto, antas, o kasidhian ng isang pangyayari, damdamin, o kuwento.
etymology: Nagmula sa salitang-ugat na `tukdol` ('rurok' o 'tuktok'), na kinabitan ng unlaping `pan-` at hulaping `-an`. Ang /t/ ng ugat ay nawala sa proseso. Ang 'kasukdulan' ay isang mas karaniwang kasingkahulugan.
original_explanation: That part in the teleserye where the bida finally confronts the kontrabida in the rain. It's the 'OMG' moment of any story, the peak of your 'kilig' or your anger. The highest point of the drama before the commercial break.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa **panukdulan** na ng kanyang galit ang ama.","translation":"The father was already at the **peak** of his anger."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-amin ng pangunahing tauhan ang **panukdulan** ng kwento.","translation":"The main character's confession is the **climax** of the story."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang panahon ng pagsubok o superbisyon na ipinapataw sa isang nagkasala bilang alternatibo sa pagkabilanggo, o sa isang bagong empleyado upang tasahin ang kanyang kakayahan.
original_explanation: That dreaded 6-month period in your BPO job where you have to be extra nice to everyone, can't be late, and have to prove you're not just there for the free coffee. Fail this, and it's back to updating your JobStreet profile. Also applies to the legal kind, but we hope you're more familiar with the office version.
usage_notes: Commonly heard in corporate/office settings ('probationary period') and legal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa ilalim pa rin ako ng anim na buwang **probasyon** sa bago kong trabaho.","translation":"I am still under a six-month **probation** at my new job."},{"sentence":"Pinalaya ang akusado sa ilalim ng **probasyon**.","translation":"The accused was released under **probation**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaki na mahilig makipag-ugnayan o magkaroon ng romantikong relasyon sa maraming babae nang sabay-sabay o sunod-sunod.
etymology: From `maN-` (agentive prefix) + `babae` (woman). The prefix `maN-` indicates someone who does the action habitually.
original_explanation: The guy your Tita warns you about. He's got a different 'ka-talking stage' for every day of the week. His motto is 'sana all,' but he applies it to girlfriends. A walking red flag with a collection of SIM cards.
usage_notes: Carries a strong negative connotation. The counterpart for a woman is `manlalalaki`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May reputasyon siyang **mambababae** kaya iniiwasan siya ng mga seryosong dalaga.","translation":"He has a reputation as a **womanizer**, so serious young women avoid him."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magtiwala sa kanya, kilalang **mambababae** 'yan sa buong barangay.","translation":"Don't trust him, he's a known **philanderer** in the whole village."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtirintas ng buhok; o ang pagkakabuhol o pagkakabit-kabit ng mga bagay tulad ng sinulid o alambre.
original_explanation: Literally, it's what you do to your hair to get that Katniss Everdeen look. Metaphorically, it's what happens to your life when you try to date two people from the same 'barkada'. Things get 'sumalapid'—tangled, complicated, and messy. Just like your earphones in your pocket.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for braiding or figuratively for becoming complicated or intertwined.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang nanay ay **sumalapid** sa mahabang buhok ng kanyang anak.","translation":"The mother **braided** her daughter's long hair."},{"sentence":"**Sumalapid** ang mga kuwento ng kanilang buhay sa isang hindi inaasahang paraan.","translation":"The stories of their lives **got entangled** in an unexpected way."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga materyales, partikular sa panitikan o sining, na may mahalay o malaswang nilalaman na naglalayong pukawin ang sekswal na pagnanasa.
original_explanation: Sa mundo ng fanfiction, ito yung chapter na inaabangan ng lahat pero nahihiya aminin. The 'Rated SPG' content you read on your phone at 2 AM, hoping your mom doesn't suddenly walk in. It's the 'secret spice' of many online reading platforms.
usage_notes: Primarily used in online communities, especially in the context of fanfiction and literature, to refer to sexually explicit content.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang magbasa ng **smut** sa office computer, baka ma-trace ng IT.","translation":"Don't read **smut** on the office computer, IT might trace it."},{"sentence":"Nagulat siya na may **smut** pala sa binabasa niyang fanfic.","translation":"She was surprised that the fanfic she was reading had **smut**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang hindi tiyak ngunit partikular na lugar o lokasyon.
original_explanation: The classic opening for a fairy tale or your lola's stories about her youth. "Sa isang dako ng Pilipinas..." It’s the vague, mysterious location of a chismis you heard, or where your missing Tupperware lid probably ended up. It's the GPS equivalent of "doon sa may ano."
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa pagkukuwento o kapag ang eksaktong lokasyon ay hindi alam o hindi mahalaga.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sa isang dako** ng gubat, may nakatirang isang ermitanyo.","translation":"**In a certain place** in the forest, there lived a hermit."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko siyang naglalakad **sa isang dako** ng parke.","translation":"I saw him walking **somewhere** in the park."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tuloy-tuloy at madalas na walang kabuluhang pagsasalita o pag-uusap, lalo na tungkol sa ibang tao.
original_explanation: This is the official sport of the Marites community. It's the endless chismisan with your kapitbahay, the non-stop chatter in a group chat, or what your teacher tells you to stop doing in class. It's talking for the sake of talking.
usage_notes: Often has a slightly negative connotation of being noisy or engaging in gossip, but can also mean harmless chit-chat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang kanilang **pagdadaldalan** mula sa kabilang kwarto.","translation":"I heard their **chattering** from the other room."},{"sentence":"Tigilan niyo na 'yang **pagdadaldalan** at magtrabaho na kayo.","translation":"Stop that **chit-chat** and get to work."}]

translation: to cage; to put in a cage
meaning_filipino: Ilagay o ikulong ang isang tao o hayop sa loob ng isang hawla.
original_explanation: What you do to your new pet lovebirds. Or, metaphorically, how you feel when your parents give you a 9 PM curfew. 'Parang nakakulong, parang ihinawla!' It’s the act of confining something or someone, taking away their freedom to roam.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for animals or figuratively for people to denote confinement or restriction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ihawla** ang ligaw na ibon; pakawalan mo ito.","translation":"Don't **cage** the wild bird; set it free."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam niya ay **ihinawla** siya sa kanyang sariling bahay.","translation":"She felt as if she was **caged** in her own house."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagpasok ng likidong gamot o bakuna sa katawan gamit ang isang heringgilya at karayom.
original_explanation: The 'turok' that made you cry as a kid (and maybe as an adult, too). From your baby vaccines to that anti-rabies shot, this is the quickest way to get medicine into your system. Sabi ng nurse, 'Parang kagat lang ng langgam,' pero iba ang sinasabi ng luha mo.
usage_notes: Madalas na kolokyal na pinapalitan ng salitang 'turok'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan niya ng **iniksiyon** para sa trangkaso.","translation":"He needs an **injection** for the flu."},{"sentence":"Medyo masakit ang **iniksiyon** ng doktor.","translation":"The doctor's **injection** was a bit painful."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumukoy sa paglikha ng malakas at magulong tunog dahil sa pagtama ng mga bagay sa isa't isa, karaniwan ay mga mas malalaking bagay kaysa sa 'kalansing'.
original_explanation: This is the sound of the water jug in the delivery tricycle hitting a pothole. Or the sound of your kaldero and kawali when you're angrily washing the dishes after a fight. It's a louder, more aggressive version of *kumalansing*.
usage_notes: Louder and heavier than 'kumalansing'. Often implies a hollow or loose object being shaken.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumalantog** ang mga bote sa likod ng trak.","translation":"The bottles **rattled** in the back of the truck."},{"sentence":"Sino ba 'yung **kumalantog** sa aming gate kaninang madaling araw?","translation":"Who was that **rattling** our gate in the early morning?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng may sakit na ketong.
original_explanation: The female counterpart of a 'leproso'. Historically, a term for a woman with leprosy, now thankfully a rare word as the disease is treatable. It carries a heavy, old-world stigma, like something out of a historical drama.
usage_notes: A dated and potentially offensive term. Modern medical terms are preferred.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa mga lumang nobela, ang **leprosa** ay madalas na itinatago sa lipunan.","translation":"In old novels, the **female leper** was often hidden from society."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubhang nagliliyab o nagniningas, maaaring tumukoy sa apoy o sa matinding damdamin tulad ng galit o pag-ibig.
original_explanation: This is your heart when you see your ultimate bias on stage. Or your anger when someone cuts you in line. It's passion turned up to 11. It's more than just "mainit," it's "sobrang init na may feelings." Puso mong nag-aalab para sa kanya, kahit seen-zoned ka lang.
usage_notes: Used both literally for fire and metaphorically for strong emotions. "Nagaalab" (without a hyphen) is a common but less formal spelling variant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nag-aalab** ang apoy sa aming sig-ang.","translation":"The fire in our bonfire is **blazing**."},{"sentence":"**Nag-aalab** sa galit ang kanyang mga mata.","translation":"His eyes were **burning** with anger."},{"sentence":"Isang pusong **nag-aalab** sa pag-ibig ang alay ko sa'yo.","translation":"A heart **fervent** with love is what I offer you."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lalaking sponsor na pinili upang maging gabay sa espirituwal na buhay ng isang bata sa sakramento ng binyag.
original_explanation: This is Level 1 Ninong. The OG. The one who was there when they poured water on your head as a baby. While you can have a 'ninong sa kasal' (wedding godfather), the 'ninong sa binyag' holds a special place as the one chosen by your parents to be your lifelong spiritual mentor (and, let's be real, Christmas cash dispenser).
usage_notes: Specifies the role of the godfather in the context of baptism, distinguishing him from a 'ninong sa kumpil' (confirmation godfather) or 'ninong sa kasal' (wedding sponsor).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aking **ninong sa binyag** ay kapatid ng tatay ko.","translation":"My **baptismal godfather** is my father's brother."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating maghanap ng responsableng **ninong sa binyag** para sa ating anak.","translation":"We need to find a responsible **baptismal godfather** for our child."}]

translation: to ensure; to make sure; to ascertain
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtiyak o pagsiguro na ang isang bagay ay totoo, tama, o magaganap ayon sa inaasahan.
original_explanation: The act of double-checking. It's when you text your friend "OTW na ako" but you're still in the shower, so they reply "Sure na 'yan, ha?" to **katiyakin**. It's the "paki-confirm" email you send five minutes after the meeting.
usage_notes: Isang anyong pautos o pawatas ng pandiwa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Katiyakin** mong nakasara ang lahat ng pinto bago ka umalis.","translation":"**Make sure** all the doors are locked before you leave."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **katiyakin** ang lahat ng detalye bago simulan ang proyekto.","translation":"We need to **ascertain** all the details before starting the project."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagiging sanhi ng pagbagsak o pagguho ng isang bagay o tao na dating nakatayo.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "tumba" (fall, topple), na may unlaping "pa-" at hulaping "-hin" upang bumuo ng isang pandiwang palipat na nangangahulugang 'maging sanhi ng pagkatumba'.
original_explanation: What Manny Pacquiao does to his opponents. Or what you do to the Jenga tower when you get nervous. Figuratively, ito yung ginagawa mo sa mga argumento ng ka-debate mo. You **patumbahin** their points one by one. O yung sandamakmak na deadlines, sinusubukan kang **patumbahin**.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang pandiwang nakapokus sa layon (object-focused). Ang layon ay ang bagay na pinapatumba.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malakas na hangin ang dahilan kung bakit kailangang **patumbahin** ang mga mahihinang poste.","translation":"The strong wind is the reason why the weak posts need to be **knocked down**."},{"sentence":"Kayang-kaya mong **patumbahin** ang lahat ng pagsubok na iyan.","translation":"You can easily **overcome** (knock down) all those challenges."}]

translation: pulp; soft, fleshy part of a fruit
meaning_filipino: Ang malambot at makatas na laman ng prutas, lalo na ng mga sitrus tulad ng dalandan o suha.
original_explanation: The good stuff inside a fruit. Think of the juicy bits of an orange or suha that you actually eat, minus the skin and seeds. It's the 'flesh' of the fruit. In some contexts, it can also mean any soft, pulpy mass.
usage_notes: Primarily used for fruits.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap kainin ang **lamukot** ng suha kapag malamig.","translation":"The **pulp** of a pomelo is delicious to eat when it's cold."},{"sentence":"Hiniwalay niya ang buto sa **lamukot** ng santol.","translation":"He separated the seeds from the **pulp** of the santol."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang muling pagkukulong o paglalagay sa bilangguan sa isang tao na dati nang nakalaya.
original_explanation: This is the sequel nobody wants. It's when someone who's been released from prison gets sent back, usually for committing another offense. The ultimate 'back to square one' in the legal system.
usage_notes: A formal term used in legal and news contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapabilanggong muli** ay isang malaking isyu sa sistema ng hustisya.","translation":"**Re-incarceration** is a major issue in the justice system."},{"sentence":"Hiniling ng piskal ang **pagpapabilanggong muli** sa akusado matapos itong lumabag sa kanyang parol.","translation":"The prosecutor requested the **re-imprisonment** of the accused after he violated his parole."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang daglat sa internet na nangangahulugang "Rolling On the Floor Laughing," ginagamit upang ipahayag ang matinding pagtawa.
etymology: Daglat mula sa pariralang Ingles na "Rolling On the Floor Laughing".
original_explanation: The upgrade to "LOL". Ito 'yung reply mo sa group chat kapag 'yung meme na sinend ng kaibigan mo ay sobrang funny, to the point na gusto mong humiga sa sahig at gumulong-gulong sa kakatawa. Usually, you're just smiling at your phone, but the sentiment is there.
usage_notes: Eksklusibong ginagamit sa digital na komunikasyon tulad ng text messages at social media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita mo ba 'yung video ng pusang nahulog? **ROFL**!","translation":"Did you see the video of the cat that fell? **ROFL**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagpapakita o pagpapaliwanag ng isang paksa sa isang grupo ng tao; isang ulat o pagtatanghal.
original_explanation: That thing you dread in school and at work that requires a PowerPoint deck and a lot of 'uhms' and 'ahs'. Mula sa book report ni bunso hanggang sa quarterly business review ng boss mo, lahat yan **presentasyon**. The source of sleepless nights and too much coffee.
usage_notes: Standard term for school reports and business presentations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinakabahan ako para sa aking **presentasyon** bukas.","translation":"I'm nervous about my **presentation** tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng mga makukulay na slide para sa kanyang **presentasyon**.","translation":"She used colorful slides for her **presentation**."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing mabangis, marahas, o mas matindi.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you add extra sili to your Bicol Express. You pabangisin the anghang. It's to make something more intense, wild, or fierce. Pwedeng sa ugali ng tao ("Huwag mo akong galitin, baka pabangisin ko ang trato ko sa'yo") or sa isang sitwasyon.
usage_notes: Used to describe the act of making a person, animal, or situation more aggressive or intense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang hirap ng buhay ang siyang **nagpabangis** sa kanyang puso.","translation":"The hardship of life is what **made** his heart **fierce**."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan ng kontrabida na **pabangisin** ang alaga niyang aso.","translation":"The villain is trying to **make** his pet dog **fiercer**."}]

translation: Parting; clearing a way (by pushing aside)
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghihiwalay o pag-aalis sa magkabilang gilid ng isang bagay, tulad ng buhok, kurtina, o mga tao, upang makagawa ng daan.
original_explanation: The dramatic parting of curtains before a show. The way you push people aside in a crowded Divisoria aisle. The 'Moses parting the Red Sea' effect, but for your bangs or a crowd.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malakas na **hawi** sa kurtina ang nagpapasok ng liwanag.","translation":"A strong **parting** of the curtains let the light in."}]

meaning_filipino: Gumawa ng isang bagay o sabihin ang isang bagay na magiging sanhi ng pagtawa ng ibang tao.
original_explanation: This is the main goal of a comedian, a class clown, or your friend who sends you memes at 3 AM. It's the art of cracking a joke, making a funny face, or telling a story so well that you get a laugh out of someone. "Kahit gaano ako kalungkot, nagagawang patawanin ako ng mga anak ko."
usage_notes: The object of this verb is the person who is made to laugh.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Subukan mong **patawanin** ang kapatid mong umiiyak.","translation":"Try to **make your crying sibling laugh**."},{"sentence":"Hindi mo ako **mapapatawa** sa mga luma mong biro.","translation":"You can't **make me laugh** with your old jokes."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi nagkasala o nakagawa ng kamalian; malinis sa anumang akusasyon.
original_explanation: The classic line in every Pinoy movie trial scene: 'Your honor, ang kliyente ko ay **walang-sala**!'. Also you, trying to explain to your mom who ate the last piece of leche flan.
usage_notes: Isang napakakaraniwang termino sa kontekstong legal, moral, at pang-araw-araw.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napatunayan sa korte na siya ay **walang-sala**.","translation":"It was proven in court that he is **not guilty**."},{"sentence":"Bakit ako ang sinisisi? **Walang-sala** ako!","translation":"Why am I being blamed? I am **innocent**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pag-iihaw o pagluluto ng pagkain sa isang grill.
original_explanation: Ang Tagalog nito ay "mag-ihaw". Pero sa Taglish, diretso na, "I-grill mo na 'yang manok." It also has a slang meaning: to interrogate someone intensely. "G-in-grill ako ng nanay ko kung saan ako galing kagabi."
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa Taglish. Mayroon ding kolokyal na kahulugan na "matinding pagtatanong" o interogasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang mag-i-**grill** ng mga isda para sa pananghalian?","translation":"Who will **grill** the fish for lunch?"},{"sentence":"G-in-**grill** ng mga reporter ang politiko tungkol sa isyu ng korapsyon.","translation":"The reporters **grilled** the politician about the corruption issue."}]

translation: to make something stick; to have someone hold on
meaning_filipino: Isang utos na paidikitin o ipahawak nang mahigpit ang isang bagay o tao sa isang lugar o posisyon.
original_explanation: That 'hugot' moment when you tell your friend, 'Pakapitin mo 'yang pag-asa mo, bes, baka sakaling mag-reply siya.' It's the act of making something cling, whether it's a poster on a wall, your faith in humanity, or your grip on the MRT handrail during rush hour.
usage_notes: A causative command. The actor of the verb is causing the object to 'kapit' (hold on/stick).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **pakapitin** ang pintura sa mamasa-masang pader.","translation":"It's hard **to make the paint stick** to a damp wall."},{"sentence":"**Pakapitin** mo muna itong hawak kong sako habang nagbabayad ako.","translation":"**Have (someone) hold on** to this sack I'm holding while I pay."}]

meaning_filipino: May kaugnayan sa kasaysayan o sa mga nakaraang pangyayari.
original_explanation: Anything labeled 'pangkasaysayan' is basically a #ThrowbackThursday that's so epic it made it into the textbooks. It's about events, places, or figures that are part of the national 'Maritest' (chismis) from long ago. Think of Rizal, the EDSA revolution, or your lola's stories about her first harana.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan ng isang bagay na may koneksyon o kahalagahan sa kasaysayan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Intramuros ay isang **pangkasaysayan** na pook sa Maynila.","translation":"Intramuros is a **historical** site in Manila."},{"sentence":"Marami tayong matututunan sa panonood ng mga pelikulang **pangkasaysayan**.","translation":"We can learn a lot from watching **historical** films."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paltos o pamamaga sa balat na may lamang tubig, karaniwang sanhi ng paso, kiskis, o impeksyon.
original_explanation: That bubble on your skin you get after touching a hot pan or wearing new shoes without socks. It's your skin's way of saying, 'I told you so!' Resisting the urge to pop the **lapnos** is a true test of character.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb 'malapnos' (to get a blister/scald).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ako ng **lapnos** sa daliri dahil sa mainit na mantika.","translation":"I got a **blister** on my finger because of the hot oil."},{"sentence":"Ang pagsuot ng masikip na sapatos ay maaaring magdulot ng **lapnos** sa paa.","translation":"Wearing tight shoes can cause **blisters** on the feet."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paraang salitan o halinhinan; paggawa ng isang bagay nang may kahalili o kapalit.
original_explanation: The rule for sharing the karaoke mic. You sing one song, then I sing one song—that's pahalili. It’s the system for 'bantay' at the hospital, for driving on a long road trip, or for using the one good charger in the house. It’s the foundation of fairness and teamwork, Tagalog-style. Turn-based strategy, but for everyday life.
usage_notes: Often used with "mag-" verbs, e.g., "magpahalili" (to take turns).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-usap ang magkapatid na magbantay nang **pahalili** sa kanilang maysakit na ina.","translation":"The siblings agreed to watch over their sick mother **in turns**."},{"sentence":"Gawin ninyo ang trabaho nang **pahalili** para hindi kayo mapagod agad.","translation":"Do the work **alternately** so you don't get tired quickly."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halaman (Euphorbia pulcherrima) na may malalaki at matingkad na pulang dahon na parang bulaklak, karaniwang nakikita at ginagamit bilang palamuti tuwing panahon ng Kapaskuhan.
etymology: From Spanish "poinsettia", named after Joel Roberts Poinsett, the first US minister to Mexico, who introduced the plant to the US in 1825.
original_explanation: The official plant of Filipino Christmas, right next to the plastic Christmas tree. You know it's the '-ber' months when these fiery red plants start popping up everywhere from mall lobbies to your tita's living room. Fun fact: the red parts aren't flowers, they're leaves! It's the plant world's version of putting on a festive outfit for the holidays.
usage_notes: Primarily used during the Christmas season.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglagay si Nanay ng mga **poinsetya** sa paligid ng aming belen.","translation":"Mom placed **poinsettias** around our nativity scene."},{"sentence":"Ang matingkad na pula ng **poinsetya** ay simbolo ng Pasko.","translation":"The bright red of the **poinsettia** is a symbol of Christmas."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinsala sa malambot na himaymay ng katawan na nagiging sanhi ng pagbabago ng kulay ng balat dahil sa pagdurugo sa ilalim nito, ngunit hindi ito nasusugatan.
etymology: From Spanish "pasar" (to pass), in the sense of something having 'passed over' or struck the skin.
original_explanation: That dark souvenir you get on your skin after bumping into a chair you swore wasn't there a second ago. It's your body's way of saying, "Oops, you messed up." A black eye (`pasa sa mata`) is the most dramatic version, often the subject of tall tales like "nakipag-away ako sa pinto" (I fought with the door).
usage_notes: Can be used for any kind of bruise on the body. A black eye is specifically 'pasa sa mata'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **pasa** ako sa braso dahil sa pagkakahulog ko sa bisikleta.","translation":"I have a **bruise** on my arm from falling off my bike."},{"sentence":"Kitang-kita ang **pasa sa mata** ng boksingero.","translation":"The boxer's **black eye** was very visible."}]

meaning_filipino: Gumawa ng isang bagay para sa kapakinabangan o para sa ibang tao.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'lambing' verb. When you ask your mom, 'Ma, igawa mo naman ako ng kape,' it's not just about the coffee, it's about the love. It's the BPO agent asking their partner, 'Igawa mo 'ko baon please?', a request packed with 'puyat' and 'pagod'. It's the act of creation, but with a specific beneficiary in mind.
usage_notes: The 'i-' prefix here indicates a benefactive focus, meaning the action is done for someone. 'Igawa mo ako' means 'Make for me'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pwede mo ba akong **igawa** ng isang tula?","translation":"Can you **make** a poem **for me**?"},{"sentence":"**Iginawa** ni Lola ng damit ang kanyang paboritong apo.","translation":"Grandma **made** a dress **for** her favorite grandchild."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gawain o pag-uusap na isinasagawa nang pribado, walang ibang taong kasama o nakikialam.
etymology: From 'sarili' (self) + '-an' suffix, denoting a place or manner of action.
original_explanation: This is the "Can we talk? Privately." of Tagalog. When your boss says "Mag-usap tayo nang sarilinan," you know it's either you're getting promoted or you're getting fired. No in-betweens. It's the opposite of a group chat; it's a one-on-one DM.
usage_notes: Can function as an adjective (e.g., 'usapang sarilinan' - a private conversation) or an adverb (e.g., 'nag-usap nang sarilinan' - talked privately).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon sila ng **sarilinan**g pag-uusap pagkatapos ng miting.","translation":"They had a **private** conversation after the meeting."},{"sentence":"Gusto kitang makausap nang **sarilinan**.","translation":"I want to talk to you **in private**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang marka o dumi na mahirap tanggalin, lalo na sa damit o anumang ibabaw, na nag-iiwan ng permanenteng o pansamantalang bakas.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na 'mancha', na nangangahulugang 'stain' o 'spot'.
original_explanation: Ito yung reason kung bakit laging may dalang Tide Pen ang mga Tita of Manila. Isang patak lang ng toyo sa puting blouse mo, ayan na, may **mantsa** ka na for life, or at least until the next laundry day. Parang sa reputasyon, isang maliit na pagkakamali, mahirap nang burahin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahihirapan akong tanggalin ang **mantsa** ng kape sa aking damit.","translation":"I'm having a hard time removing the coffee **stain** from my clothes."},{"sentence":"Naiwan ang **mantsa** ng putik sa sahig pagkatapos umulan.","translation":"A mud **stain** was left on the floor after it rained."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggalaw gamit ang mga paa sa pamamagitan ng paghakbang.
etymology: From mag- (verb prefix) + lakad (walk, step, errand).
original_explanation: The most basic form of Filipino cardio. You maglakad to the nearest sari-sari store, maglakad to the sakayan, or maglakad around the mall for 'window shopping'. It's also a verb for making things happen, as in 'I-lakad mo naman 'tong papers ko' (Can you process these papers for me?), turning a physical action into a metaphor for getting things done.
usage_notes: Can also be used figuratively to mean 'to process' or 'to facilitate' something, usually through personal connections.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap **maglakad** sa umaga kapag malamig ang hangin.","translation":"It's nice to **walk** in the morning when the air is cool."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **maglakad** ng kanyang visa application sa ahensya.","translation":"He tried to **facilitate** his visa application at the agency."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang makabagong ekspresyon na ginagamitan ng salitang 'yarn' (isang paglalaro sa 'iyan') upang magbigay-diin, madalas sa paraang may halong sarkasmo o pagbibiro, sa salitang 'pagod.'
etymology: Combination of 'pagod' and 'yarn,' a gay lingo/internet slang term derived from 'iyan.'
original_explanation: This is how you say 'I'm tired' with Gen Z flavor. The 'yarn' (a playful version of 'iyan') adds a layer of sass, irony, or dramatic flair. Friend: 'Nag-laundry ako, naglinis ng bahay, at nag-grocery today.' You: '**Pagod yarn**?' Can be self-directed ('Nag-reply lang sa isang email, pero pagod yarn?') or used to comment on someone else's minimal effort.
usage_notes: Highly contemporary and informal. The tone can be sincere, sarcastic, or playful depending on context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umattend lang ng isang meeting, pero **pagod yarn**?","translation":"Just attended one meeting, and you're **so tired** already?"},{"sentence":"Selfie pagkatapos mag-workout. Grabe, **pagod yarn**!","translation":"Selfie after a workout. Wow, **so tired**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na proseso ng pagpapatalsik o pag-aalis sa isang tao mula sa isang organisasyon, paaralan, o lugar.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you *really* mess up in school. Hindi lang suspension, this is the 'pack your bags, you're out' level of punishment. Parang na-evict ka sa PBB house for a major violation.
usage_notes: Primarily used in formal, academic, or disciplinary contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **ekspulsiyon** mula sa unibersidad ay dahil sa pandaraya.","translation":"His **expulsion** from the university was due to cheating."},{"sentence":"Nakatanggap siya ng babala ng posibleng **ekspulsiyon** kung uulit pa siya.","translation":"He received a warning of possible **expulsion** if he does it again."}]

translation: to moan, to complain, to lament
meaning_filipino: Pagpapahayag ng sakit, hinagpis, o reklamo sa pamamagitan ng tunog o salita.
original_explanation: Yung tunog na ginagawa mo kapag Lunes na naman at back to work/school ka na. Parang life's biggest plot twist, 'di ba? Pwede ring ito 'yung constant state mo kapag "seen" ka lang ng crush mo. Puro ka na lang **daing**.
usage_notes: Often used to express physical pain or emotional grievance. The stress is on the second syllable, distinguishing it from the noun for dried fish.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puro **daing** ang naririnig ko mula sa kanya dahil sa sakit ng ngipin.","translation":"All I hear from him are **moans** because of his toothache."},{"sentence":"Tumigil ka na sa pag**daing** at kumilos ka para masolusyunan ang problema.","translation":"Stop **complaining** and do something to solve the problem."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtuturo o pagbibigay-kaalaman sa isang tao; o ang proseso ng pag-aaral at pagsusuri sa isang bagay.
etymology: From 'aral' (lesson, study) with the infix '-in-' and suffix '-an'.
original_explanation: This is what happens when your mom catches you doing something stupid and gives you "the talk." It's also what you're doing to that online course you bought but haven't finished yet. It's the "studying in progress" status of your brain, whether it's a lesson from a teacher or a lesson from life (a.k.a. a mistake).
usage_notes: Can mean both "being taught" (by someone) and "being studied" (by someone). The context clarifies the agent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Inaaralan** ng guro ang mga bata kung paano magbasa.","translation":"The teacher is **teaching** the children how to read."},{"sentence":"Matagal na naming **inaaralan** ang kasong ito.","translation":"We have been **studying** this case for a long time."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sigaw o utos, karaniwang ginagamit sa mga hayop na humihila tulad ng kabayo o kalabaw upang umabante o bumilis.
etymology: Onomatopoeic, imitating the sound of a sharp cry or command.
original_explanation: Not to be confused with the feeling of shame! This is what you shout at a kabayo (horse) or kalabaw (carabao) to make it go faster. Think of it as the Filipino "Giddy-up!" or the sound effect you make when pretending to do karate chops. Hi-ya!
usage_notes: This is a homonym of 'hiya' (shame) and is differentiated by context, intonation (stress on the first syllable), and often hyphenation in writing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hi-ya**! bilisan mo, Bilis!\" sigaw ng kutsero sa kanyang kabayo.","translation":"**Giddy-up**! Hurry up, Bilis!\" shouted the coachman to his horse."},{"sentence":"Nagulat ako sa sigaw niyang '**Hi-ya**!' habang naglalaro.","translation":"I was surprised by his shout of '**Yah**!' while playing."}]

translation: to be the cause of progress/development
meaning_filipino: Ang maging dahilan o sanhi ng pag-unlad, pagbuti, o pagsulong ng isang tao, bagay, o kalagayan.
original_explanation: That upskilling course your BPO company paid for? That's para 'ikaunlad' ng career mo. That new expressway that cuts your travel time from 3 hours to 1? That's para sa 'ikaunlad' ng ekonomiya. It's the "why" behind the glow-up, whether it's for you or for the whole country.
usage_notes: The subject of the sentence with this verb is the cause of the progress.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang edukasyon ay sandatang **ikauunlad** ng bayan.","translation":"Education is a tool that will **be the cause of the nation's progress**."},{"sentence":"Ang sipag at tiyaga ay **ikauunlad** ng sinuman.","translation":"Hard work and perseverance will **be the cause of anyone's progress**."}]

translation: to go first; to be the first
meaning_filipino: Mauna sa pag-alis, paggawa, o pagdating sa isang lugar. Maging nangunguna sa isang pila o karera.
original_explanation: When you and your friend are leaving a party and you say, 'Mag-una na ako, ha?' meaning 'I'll go ahead, 'kay?' It's the polite way of ditching them. Also, what you do in a buffet line if you want to get the first crack at the lechon.
usage_notes: Can also mean to prioritize something when used with an object, e.g., 'Mag-una ka sa pag-aaral' (Prioritize your studies). However, the primary meaning is to go first.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sige, **mag-una** na kayo sa sinehan at susunod na lang ako.","translation":"Okay, you guys **go first** to the cinema and I'll just follow."},{"sentence":"Sino ang gustong **mag-una** sa pag-uulat?","translation":"Who wants to **be the first** to report?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtatago o paglalagay ng mga bagay, lalo na ang pagkain o suplay, sa isang ligtas na lugar para magamit sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: This is your tita's superpower. It's the art of buying things in bulk 'cause they're on sale and storing them for a rainy day (or a zombie apocalypse). It ranges from the practical (storing rice) to the questionable (hoarding empty ice cream tubs). During the pandemic, this was everyone's hobby with alcohol and toilet paper.
usage_notes: Can have a neutral meaning (storing) or a negative one (hoarding), depending on the context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pag-iimbak** ng pagkain ay mahalaga bilang paghahanda sa bagyo.","translation":"**Storing** food is important in preparation for a typhoon."},{"sentence":"Ipinagbabawal ang **pag-iimbak** ng gasolina sa mga bahay-bahay.","translation":"The **stockpiling** of gasoline in homes is prohibited."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagsagip o pagtulong sa mga tao o sasakyang-dagat na nasa panganib sa karagatan.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'sana all' moment for anyone stuck in the middle of the sea. It's the Coast Guard's version of a Grab rescue, but with more waves and less surge pricing. It's the dramatic scene in movies where the hero is plucked from the raging water by a helicopter.
usage_notes: A compound noun referring specifically to rescue operations at sea.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging matagumpay ang **pagliligtas sa dagat** ng mga mangingisdang nawala.","translation":"The **sea rescue** of the missing fishermen was successful."},{"sentence":"Pinangunahan ng Philippine Coast Guard ang malawakang operasyon ng **pagliligtas sa dagat**.","translation":"The Philippine Coast Guard led the massive **sea rescue** operation."}]

meaning_filipino: Durugin ang pagkain o anumang bagay sa bibig gamit ang mga ngipin.
original_explanation: The object-focus version of 'to chew'. This is what you do *to* the chicharon. "Nguyain mo nang maigi" is your mom's advice for everything from steak to life's problems. Sometimes, it also means to ponder or think deeply about something, like, "Kailangan kong nguyain ang offer na 'to."
usage_notes: Object-focus verb. The action is done *to* the object. Can also be used figuratively to mean 'to ponder' or 'to mull over'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **nguyain** nang mabuti ang karne bago lunukin.","translation":"You need **to chew** the meat well before swallowing."},{"sentence":"Hayaan mong **nguyain** ko muna ang mga sinabi mo.","translation":"Let me **chew on** what you said for a while."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong mayabang, mapusok, at laging naghahanap ng away; maton.
original_explanation: The 'siga-siga sa kanto' is a classic Pinoy character. He's the guy who walks around like he owns the place, maybe has a toothpick in his mouth, and thinks a loud voice wins every argument. Every barangay, classroom, and even office has one. He's one 'Ano, tinitingin-tingin mo diyan?' away from starting trouble.
usage_notes: Often carries a negative connotation of being an arrogant troublemaker.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong pansinin 'yang **siga** sa kabilang kalye.","translation":"Don't pay attention to that **bully** on the other street."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya bilang **siga** ng kanilang klase noong high school.","translation":"He was known as the **tough guy** of their class back in high school."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong wala sa tamang pag-iisip o katinuan; nagpapakita ng hindi pangkaraniwang pag-uugali o pag-iisip.
original_explanation: Can range from clinically insane to what you call your friend who wants to get back with their toxic ex for the 5th time. Also used to describe something amazing, like 'Baliw sa ganda!' (Crazy beautiful!). It's the emotional state of Metro Manila traffic personified.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for mental illness, but more commonly used informally or figuratively to mean 'wild', 'absurd', or 'intensely'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi ako **baliw** para gawin 'yon.","translation":"Don't worry, I'm not **crazy** enough to do that."},{"sentence":"Para siyang **baliw** sa pag-ibig.","translation":"He/She is like someone **mad** with love."}]

meaning_filipino: May lasang katulad ng asukal o pulot; kaaya-aya sa pandinig o paningin.
original_explanation: The official flavor of Filipino desserts, afternoon merienda, and your crush's smile. It's the taste of halo-halo on a summer day, the sound of a sweet promise ("babayaran na kita next week"), or the look in your dog's eyes. Warning: Too much can lead to diabetes or a "sana ol" moment.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for taste or figuratively for words, smiles, or memories.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para sa akin, masyadong **matamis** ang leche flan na ito.","translation":"For me, this leche flan is too **sweet**."},{"sentence":"Nagbigay siya ng isang **matamis** na ngiti bago umalis.","translation":"She gave a **sweet** smile before leaving."}]

translation: suicide; the act of killing oneself
meaning_filipino: Ang sinasadyang pagkitil sa sariling buhay.
etymology: From pag- (nominalizer) + pa- (causative, reflexive) + tiwakal (to commit suicide).
original_explanation: This is a heavy one. It's the act of taking one's own life. It's a topic that's often whispered about, but needs to be discussed openly with care and empathy. It's the ultimate act of hopelessness for some, and a reminder for the rest of us to always check in on our friends.
usage_notes: A very serious term. Used in news reports, psychological contexts, and formal discussions about mental health.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming organisasyon ang tumutulong upang maiwasan ang **pagpapatiwakal** sa mga kabataan.","translation":"Many organizations are helping to prevent **suicide** among the youth."},{"sentence":"Ang depresyon ay isang seryosong kondisyon na maaaring humantong sa **pagpapatiwakal**.","translation":"Depression is a serious condition that can lead to **the act of killing oneself**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging masaya matapos ang isang pangyayari o sa paglipas ng panahon.
original_explanation: This is you after a good cry, a chat with your best friend, or when you finally get over your ex. It's the completed action of becoming happy. "Okay na ako, sumaya na ako." It’s the "after" picture of sadness. The hugot has ended, and the happiness has begun.
usage_notes: This is the completed aspect of the verb, meaning the state of happiness has been achieved.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigla siyang **sumaya** nang makita niya ang kanyang mga kaibigan.","translation":"She suddenly **became happy** when she saw her friends."},{"sentence":"**Sumaya** ang buong pamilya sa balitang uuwi na siya.","translation":"The whole family **cheered up** at the news that he was coming home."}]

meaning_filipino: Buhatin o dalhin ang isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng balagwit.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of using the 'taho vendor stick'. When you 'balagwitin' something, you're not just carrying it, you're performing a feat of strength and balance. It's the action that defines the hustle of many Filipino workers.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan niyang **balagwitin** ang mga paninda papunta sa palengke.","translation":"He needs **to carry** the goods **with a pole** to the market."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan kong **balagwitin** ang dalawang banga ngunit napakabigat pala.","translation":"I tried **to carry** the two jars **with a yoke** but they were too heavy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis at biglaang pagtakbo, karaniwan dahil sa takot o pagmamadali.
original_explanation: This isn't just running; this is panic-running. Imagine seeing a giant 'ipis' (cockroach) fly. The chaotic, zig-zagging sprint you do to get away? That's 'kumarimot ng takbo'. It’s the kind of run that’s fueled by pure adrenaline and terror. Not graceful, just fast.
usage_notes: A verb phrase. 'Kumarimot' is the verb, and 'ng takbo' specifies the action. It's rarely used without 'ng takbo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumarimot ng takbo** ang mga bata nang makita nila ang asong galit.","translation":"The children **scampered away** when they saw the angry dog."},{"sentence":"Nang biglang kumulog, **kumarimot ng takbo** ang pusa papasok ng bahay.","translation":"When it suddenly thundered, the cat **ran hastily** into the house."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyong balbal mula sa Ingles na nangangahulugang gumawa ng isang bagay sa napakahusay at walang kapintasang paraan. Halimbawa: "She ate and left no crumbs."
etymology: Mula sa African-American Vernacular English (AAVE), na pinasikat sa pamamagitan ng internet at kultura ng drag. Ito ang anyong pangnagdaan ng pandiwang Ingles na "eat".
original_explanation: When someone says "she ate that" or "she ate and left no crumbs," it means she absolutely killed it. Think of a beauty queen's pasarela, a singer hitting a high note, or your friend's perfect comeback to a hater. It's the Gen Z version of "Ginalingan!" or "Pak!". No food is involved, just pure, unadulterated talent and excellence.
usage_notes: Halos eksklusibong ginagamit sa mga kontekstong Taglish o Ingles online o sa mga nakababatang henerasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Grabe 'yung performance ni Catriona, she really **ate** that!","translation":"Catriona's performance was amazing, she really **ate** that!"},{"sentence":"Nakita mo ba 'yung sagot niya sa pageant? She **ate** and left no crumbs!","translation":"Did you see her answer in the pageant? She **ate** and left no crumbs!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian na naglalarawan sa isang tao, bagay, o kilos na nagdudulot ng matinding kahihiyan o kawalan ng dangal.
etymology: Reduplication of 'kahiya' from ka- + hiya (shame), used to intensify the quality of being shameful.
original_explanation: This is the adjective form of maximum cringe. It's not just 'nakakahiya' (embarrassing), it's on a whole other level. It’s for scandals, epic fails, and moments that make you want the earth to swallow you whole. 'Ang ginawa niyang pagnanakaw ay isang **kahiya-hiyang** krimen.' It's the judgment your Tita gives you when you do something she doesn't approve of.
usage_notes: The repetition 'hiya-hiya' intensifies the meaning, making it stronger than 'nakakahiya' (embarrassing). It implies a moral judgment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **kahiya-hiyang** pangyayari ang naganap sa entablado kanina.","translation":"A **shameful** incident happened on stage earlier."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang asal sa harap ng mga bisita ay **kahiya-hiya**.","translation":"His behavior in front of the guests was **disgraceful**."}]

translation: to be able to move or speak
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang gumalaw, umimik, o tumugon, karaniwang ginagamit sa anyong negatibo.
etymology: From `maka-` (ability prefix) + `kibo` (a slight movement or utterance).
original_explanation: This word lives in its negative form: 'hindi makakibo.' It's what happens when your crush suddenly talks to you, or when your mom finds out you failed a subject. You're frozen, speechless, shookt. You are physically and verbally unable to function. You can't even.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in the negative (`hindi makakibo`) to mean 'to be speechless' or 'to be frozen in place'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang gulat, hindi siya **makakibo**.","translation":"From extreme shock, he/she **could not move or speak**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang matakot, kailangan mong **makakibo** at ipagtanggol ang sarili mo.","translation":"Don't be afraid, you need to be **able to speak up** and defend yourself."}]

translation: to make someone laugh; to be funny
meaning_filipino: Gumawa ng isang bagay na magdudulot ng katuwaan o pagtawa sa ibang tao.
original_explanation: This is the job description of your one friend who's the designated clown of the group. They're an expert in the art of **magpatawa**. It's the skill of dropping a perfectly timed joke during a serious meeting or sending a meme that makes everyone's day. The secret weapon of comedians and class clowns.
usage_notes: Can describe a deliberate act (telling a joke) or a general quality (being a funny person).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahusay talagang **magpatawa** si Vice Ganda.","translation":"Vice Ganda is really great at **making people laugh**."},{"sentence":"Huwag ka ngang **magpatawa**, seryoso ang usapan.","translation":"Don't **be funny**, this is a serious conversation."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na hindi naniniwala o kulang sa paniniwala sa pagkakaroon ng Diyos o mga diyos.
original_explanation: This is someone who, when asked "Anong religion mo?", answers "Wala po." In a country where there's a fiesta for a saint every other day, being an ateista can lead to some... interesting family dinner conversations, especially with your lola. They trust in science, logic, and a good adobo recipe, not necessarily a higher power.
usage_notes: Ang terminong "ateo" (panlalaki) ay ginagamit din ngunit ang "ateista" ay mas karaniwan at pangkalahatang neutral sa kasarian.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iginagalang niya ang paniniwala ng iba kahit isa siyang **ateista**.","translation":"He respects the beliefs of others even though he is an **atheist**."},{"sentence":"Nagkaroon sila ng malalim na talakayan tungkol sa pagiging **ateista**.","translation":"They had a deep discussion about being an **atheist**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng lalagyan ng tubig na yari sa isang malaking biyas ng kawayan, karaniwang may hawakan.
original_explanation: Before the age of Aquaflask and plastic water bottles, there was the 'sawing'. It's the OG, eco-friendly, provincial water jug. Imagine fetching water from the 'poso' (water pump) and carrying it back home in this giant bamboo tube. Very rustic, very classic Pinoy.
usage_notes: This term is more common in rural or historical contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumunta siya sa bukal upang punuin ng tubig ang kanilang **sawing**.","translation":"He went to the spring to fill their **bamboo water container** with water."},{"sentence":"Ang lumang **sawing** ay nakasabit pa rin sa dingding ng bahay-kubo.","translation":"The old **bamboo water container** is still hanging on the wall of the nipa hut."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang makamit o makuha ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay premyo o parangal, sa pamamagitan ng kompetisyon, sugal, o raffle.
etymology: Nagmula sa salitang 'panalo' na dinugtungan ng hulaping '-an'.
original_explanation: This is the verb for 'winning a thing'. It's what you do to the grand prize. When you join a contest, you hope na may **panalunan** ka. It's the action of securing the bag, the trophy, the title, or even just the free tumbler from a coffee shop promo.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang pandiwang pokus sa layon, kung saan ang pinag-uusapan ay ang bagay na napanalunan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang iyong **panalunan** sa sinalihan mong raffle?","translation":"What did you **win** from the raffle you joined?"},{"sentence":"Sana'y **panalunan** ko ang jackpot sa lotto ngayong gabi.","translation":"I hope I **win** the lotto jackpot tonight."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga pakinabang, karagdagang sahod, o pribilehiyo na natatanggap ng isang empleyado bukod sa kanyang regular na suweldo.
original_explanation: The magic word you look for in a job description after "salary." This includes HMO, 13th-month pay, de minimis, rice allowance, and free coffee. Having good benefits is the difference between "I love my job" and "I need a new job." It's the corporate world's version of a love language.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa konteksto ng trabaho at negosyo. Madalas baybayin at gamitin bilang salitang Ingles sa pangungusap na Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maganda ang **benefits** na ino-offer ng kompanya nila kaya marami ang nag-a-apply.","translation":"The company offers good **benefits**, which is why many people are applying."},{"sentence":"Kasama ba sa **benefits** mo ang health card para sa dependents?","translation":"Is a health card for dependents included in your **benefits**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o kumpanya na namamahagi ng mga produkto mula sa prodyuser patungo sa mga nagtitingi o sa mga mamimili.
original_explanation: Same as 'distribuidor', pero this is the more common, English-based spelling you'll see in business permits and job titles. Sila 'yung link sa supply chain. Without them, paano makakarating ang paborito mong chichirya sa suking tindahan mo?
usage_notes: This English-derived spelling is more common in modern business and everyday use than the Spanish-derived "distribuidor".
