usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating makipag-usap sa opisyal na **distributor** para makakuha ng diskwento.","translation":"We need to talk to the official **distributor** to get a discount."},{"sentence":"Nag-apply siya bilang sales **distributor** ng isang malaking kumpanya ng softdrinks.","translation":"He applied as a sales **distributor** for a large softdrink company."}]

translation: to oppress, to mistreat, to bully
meaning_filipino: Magsagawa ng hindi makatarungang pagtrato, pang-aabuso, o pagmamalupit sa isang tao o grupo, lalo na sa mga mas mahihina.
original_explanation: The villain's main job description in any teleserye. It's what bullies do in school, what abusive bosses do at work, and what kontrabidas do to the bida. To 'umapi' is to use your power to make someone else's life miserable.
usage_notes: A strong word with connotations of injustice and power imbalance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **umapi** ng iyong kapwa, lalo na ng mga mas mahihina sa iyo.","translation":"Do not **oppress** your fellow human beings, especially those who are weaker than you."},{"sentence":"Inakusahan ang gobyerno na **umapi** sa karapatan ng mga mamamayan.","translation":"The government was accused of **oppressing** the rights of the citizens."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalarawan sa isang hayop o bagay na mayroong sungay.
original_explanation: Literally, 'to have horns.' It's what you call a carabao, a goat, or that one friend who's always the kontrabida in every story. Metaphorically, it can also refer to a cuckolded husband, a very old and somewhat offensive term ('sinusungayan').
usage_notes: The metaphorical use for a cheated-on husband is archaic and can be offensive. The literal meaning is more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **sungayan** na usa ay mabilis na tumakbo paalis.","translation":"The **horned** deer quickly ran away."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alaga ng **sungayan** na hayop kung maliit ang iyong bakuran.","translation":"Don't raise a **horned** animal if your yard is small."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kawalan ng pisikal na pakiramdam sa isang bahagi ng katawan; maaari ring tumukoy sa kawalan ng emosyonal na reaksyon o pagiging walang pakialam.
original_explanation: Two types. 1) Literal: 'Yung feeling ng bibig mo after a dental procedure. 2) The "hugot" version: 'Yung ex mong paulit-ulit mong iniyakan pero parang wala lang sa kanya. Siya 'yun. Manhid. Walang pakiramdam. A rock. A stone. A wall.
usage_notes: Can be used for both physical numbness (e.g., from anesthesia or cold) and emotional insensitivity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **manhid** ang aking binti dahil sa matagal na pagkakaupo.","translation":"My leg became **numb** from sitting for a long time."},{"sentence":"Bakit ka ba ganyan ka-**manhid**? Hindi mo ba nakikita na nasasaktan na ako?","translation":"Why are you so **insensitive**? Can't you see that I'm already hurting?"}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng labis na interes o pag-uusisa sa mga bagay na hindi naman niya dapat pakialaman.
etymology: From Spanish 'ocioso' (idle, unoccupied), with its meaning shifting in Filipino to align more with 'curioso' (curious), likely because idle people were perceived as being nosy.
original_explanation: A lighter, more casual version of 'usisero'/'usisera'. It's more about being curious than being malicious. You're being usyoso when you slow down to see what the commotion is on the street. It's the 'chismis-in-the-making' vibe.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a male, but can be used for anyone. It is less formal and less negative than 'usisero'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **usyoso** ang mga tao nang may dumating na ambulansya.","translation":"The people became **curious** when an ambulance arrived."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong **usyoso** sa buhay ng may buhay.","translation":"Don't be too **nosy** about other people's lives."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sagradong lalagyan o kahon, lalo na sa mga simbahan, kung saan itinatago ang Banal na Sakramento. Sa kontekstong biblikal, ito ay ang portable na dambana ng mga Israelita.
original_explanation: This is the special, often golden, box you see in Catholic churches, usually near the altar. It's basically the VIP lounge for the Holy Eucharist. Think of it as God's holy treasure chest on Earth.
usage_notes: Primarily used in a religious (Christian/Catholic) context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **tabernakulo** ay matatagpuan sa pinakasagradong bahagi ng simbahan.","translation":"The **tabernacle** is located in the most sacred part of the church."},{"sentence":"Yumukod siya sa harap ng **tabernakulo** bago umupo.","translation":"He bowed before the **tabernacle** before taking a seat."}]

translation: to get a shave; to have someone shave you
meaning_filipino: Ang paghiling o pagpapahintulot sa ibang tao na alisin ang iyong buhok o balbas gamit ang labaha o pang-ahit.
original_explanation: This is what your Lolo does at the local barbershop on a Saturday morning. It's not just a shave, it's a ritual—complete with the hot towel, the straight razor, and all the local chismis. It's the act of letting someone else do the grooming, a small luxury. It can also mean getting your armpits or legs waxed/shaved at a salon.
usage_notes: The 'magpa-' prefix is causative, meaning you cause someone else to perform the action (shaving) on you. 'Mag-ahit' means to shave yourself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing Linggo, pumupunta si Tatay sa barbero para **magpaahit** ng bigote.","translation":"Every Sunday, Dad goes to the barber to **get his mustache shaved**."},{"sentence":"Nahihiya siyang **magpaahit** ng kilay sa salon sa unang pagkakataon.","translation":"She was shy to **have her eyebrows shaped** at the salon for the first time."}]

meaning_filipino: Isama o ilagay ang mga gamit sa bagahe upang isakay sa sasakyan, partikular sa eroplano o bus.
original_explanation: The most stressful part of any airport trip. It's the act of deciding which items are worthy of being checked in. "I-hand carry ko na lang 'to o ibagahe?" is the question that haunts every Pinoy traveler trying to avoid excess baggage fees. It's literally telling the airline, "Please take care of my life's possessions and don't lose them."
usage_notes: Specific to travel contexts, especially air travel.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ibagahe** ang iyong laptop at mahahalagang dokumento.","translation":"Do not **check in** your laptop and important documents **as luggage**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ko nang **ibagahe** itong maleta para makapila na tayo.","translation":"I need to **check in this luggage** so we can get in line."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang modernong balbal na ekspresyon ng matinding pagsang-ayon, kagalakan, o paghanga, na hinango sa salitang Ingles na 'yes'.
etymology: From English slang 'yass', a variant of 'yes'. Popularized by internet and LGBTQ+ culture.
original_explanation: This is how you say 'yes' when you REALLY mean it. It's the verbal equivalent of a slow-motion hair flip or getting your 13th-month pay. The more 's's you add, the more intense the feeling. 'Yasss, may bago na namang K-drama!' or 'Yasss, nakauwi bago mag-rush hour!' A staple in the Gen Z and Millennial vocabulary.
usage_notes: Purely informal and used in spoken language or online chats. Using this in a formal business email is a bold, and probably unwise, choice.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakuha mo 'yung promo sa concert? **Yasss** queen!","translation":"You got the promo for the concert? **Yasss** queen!"},{"sentence":"**Yasss**, sa wakas, Biyernes na!","translation":"**Yasss**, finally, it's Friday!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang magkaroon ng maraming maliliit na dumi, mantsa, o marka sa iba't ibang bahagi ng isang bagay o ibabaw.
original_explanation: Imagine a toddler after a solo mission with a chocolate cake. That's `magkabahid-bahid`. It's not just one stain; it's a constellation of smudges. Your white shirt after eating sisig with a leaky fork, or your reputation after a 'Maritess' is done with you. It means to be covered in multiple stains or blemishes.
usage_notes: The reduplication 'bahid-bahid' implies that the stains are multiple and scattered, covering a surface unevenly.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagkabahid-bahid** ng putik ang kanyang uniporme pagkatapos maglaro sa ulan.","translation":"His uniform **became stained all over** with mud after playing in the rain."},{"sentence":"Ayokong **magkabahid-bahid** ang pangalan ng ating pamilya dahil sa isang pagkakamali.","translation":"I don't want our family's name **to be tarnished** by one mistake."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sukat ng isang bagay mula sa ibaba pataas; ang bahaging nasa ibabaw o itaas ng isang lugar.
original_explanation: Yung lugar sa bahay na laging mas mainit. 'Nasa taas si Mama, natutulog.' Also, what you're trying to achieve in your career or in a video game level. The opposite of 'baba'.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical height, a higher location (like upstairs), or a metaphorical high level (e.g., 'taas ng pangarap' - height of one's dream).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-abot ng libro sa **taas** ng aparador.","translation":"Please get the book on **top** of the cabinet."},{"sentence":"Umakyat ka sa **taas** para tawagin ang kuya mo.","translation":"Go **upstairs** to call your older brother."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o kilos ng pagiging banal, paglilinis mula sa kasalanan, o pag-aalay ng isang bagay o tao para sa sagradong layunin.
original_explanation: This is the real deal, the genuine journey towards holiness. It's not just about posting Bible verses on Facebook. It's the quiet, consistent effort to be a better person, to help others without expecting a feature on 'KMJS', and to live a life of integrity. It's the opposite of pagbabanal-banalan. Think less PR, more GR (Grace).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagbabanal** ay isang habambuhay na paglalakbay ng pananampalataya.","translation":"**Sanctification** is a lifelong journey of faith."},{"sentence":"Bahagi ng ritwal ang **pagbabanal** sa tubig na gagamitin sa binyag.","translation":"Part of the ritual is the **consecration** of the water to be used for baptism."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng lason o isang substansiya na nakamamatay o nakakasama sa kalusugan kapag nakain, nalanghap, o nahawakan.
original_explanation: This is what your nanay warns you about when you see a brightly colored, unknown fruit in the province. 'Huwag mong kainin 'yan, baka **may-lason**!' It's also used to describe words that are meant to hurt—'marites' spreading 'chismis na may-lason'. Toxic, literally or figuratively.
usage_notes: Can refer to poisonous substances, venomous animals, or metaphorically to harmful words or intentions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ilang uri ng ahas ay **may-lason**.","translation":"Some types of snakes are **venomous**."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa mga salitang **may-lason** na maaaring makasakit ng damdamin.","translation":"Be careful of **poisonous** words that can hurt feelings."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sakramento sa relihiyong Kristiyano, partikular sa Katolisismo, na kumakatawan sa katawan at dugo ni Kristo sa anyo ng tinapay at alak.
etymology: From Spanish 'Eucaristía', from Latin 'eucharistia', from Greek 'eukharistia' (thanksgiving).
original_explanation: This is the holy communion, the part of the Mass where you get the 'ostia' or host. It's the ultimate spiritual snack, a wafer that's more than just a wafer. It's a central, super-solemn moment, so no chewing loudly or checking your phone.
usage_notes: A formal religious term. The more common, less formal term is 'Komunyon' (Communion).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **Eukaristiya** ay ang sentro ng Misa sa Simbahang Katoliko.","translation":"The **Eucharist** is the center of the Mass in the Catholic Church."},{"sentence":"Tinanggap niya ang Banal na **Eukaristiya** nang may taimtim na pananampalataya.","translation":"He/She received the Holy **Eucharist** with sincere faith."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang biglaan at malakas na pagbugso o pagsiklab ng damdamin, pagnanasa, o kilos.
original_explanation: That sudden urge you get at 3 AM to check your ex's IG stories. Or when you see a 12.12 sale and suddenly *need* that air fryer. It's the 'wala lang, naisipan ko lang bigla' energy that leads to either great memories or great regrets.
usage_notes: Often used with 'ng damdamin' to specify 'surge of emotion.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa **simbuyo** ng galit, nasigawan niya ang kanyang kaibigan.","translation":"Because of an **impulse** of anger, he shouted at his friend."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya napigilan ang **simbuyo** na bilhin ang mamahaling sapatos.","translation":"She couldn't resist the **urge** to buy the expensive shoes."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa kabuuan ng itagal ng pamumuhay o pag-iral ng isang tao.
original_explanation: The ultimate timeframe for drama and promises. "I've waited for you my whole life!" or "I will love you for the rest of my life!" It’s the duration of your parents' sermon when you mess up, and the length of a teleserye that just won't end.
usage_notes: Used to express the entirety of a person's existence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Buong buhay** siyang nagtrabaho para sa kanyang pamilya.","translation":"He worked his **entire life** for his family."},{"sentence":"Ikaw lang ang mamahalin ko **buong buhay**.","translation":"You're the only one I will love **all my life**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan kung saan ang isang bahagi o ang buong katawan ay walang pakiramdam o hindi maigalaw, karaniwan ay pansamantala.
etymology: Literally 'dead body' or 'the body is dead,' used idiomatically to mean loss of sensation.
original_explanation: When you've been sitting in the same position for a 4-hour Zoom call and your leg decides to log off before you do. That pins-and-needles feeling is your body saying 'BRB'. It's either that, or you're literally paralyzed, in which case, this explanation is probably not what you're looking for.
usage_notes: This is an idiom. It doesn't mean the person is literally dead, but that a part of their body has lost sensation or mobility, often temporarily.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng mahabang biyahe, **patay ang katawan** ko at hindi ako makatayo agad.","translation":"After the long trip, my body was **numb** and I couldn't stand up immediately."}]

translation: to act upon; to catch in the act
meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng isang bagay bilang tugon sa isang sitwasyon; ang paghuli sa isang tao habang ginagawa ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay mali.
etymology: Mula sa salitang "akto" (mula sa Espanyol na "acto") + hulaping "-han".
original_explanation: Two meanings, bes. First, yung "Let's do something about it!" moment mo. Nakita mong may injustice, so inaktuhan mo. Second, yung "Huli ka, balbon!" moment. Nahuli mo sa aktuhan yung jowa mong may ka-chat na iba. Ouch.
usage_notes: Maaaring mangahulugang "to take action on something" o "to be caught in the act". Ang konteksto ang magdidikta ng kahulugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **aktuhan** agad ang problema bago ito lumala.","translation":"We need to **act upon** the problem immediately before it gets worse."},{"sentence":"Na-**aktuhan** ng pulis ang mga magnanakaw habang nililimas ang bahay.","translation":"The police **caught** the thieves **in the act** of robbing the house."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaikling salita para sa 'outfit'; ang kasuotan o porma ng isang tao.
original_explanation: Your 'OOTD' (Outfit Of The Day). It's the whole ensemble, the porma, the look you carefully curated for your IG story or TikTok video. When someone says 'Nice fit!', they're complimenting your drip, not your gym progress.
usage_notes: A very modern slang term, popularized by social media. Often used in the phrase 'fit check'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng **fit** mo ngayon, saan mo nabili 'yang jacket?","translation":"Your **outfit** is great today, where did you buy that jacket?"},{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng bagong **fit** para sa party sa Sabado.","translation":"I need a new **outfit** for the party on Saturday."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panlabas na anyo o kaanyuan ng isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: Your overall look, your vibe, your "porma." It's how you present yourself to the world. "Ayusin mo nga 'yang hitsura mo!" is the classic line from your mom before you leave the house. It’s not just your face, it's the whole package—hair, clothes, and the "mukha kang pagod" expression.
usage_notes: A very common word, often spelled colloquially as 'itsura'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagbago ang kanyang **hitsura** mula noong huli kaming nagkita.","translation":"His **appearance** has changed since the last time we saw each other."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong husgahan ang tao batay sa kanyang panlabas na **hitsura**.","translation":"Don't judge a person based on their outward **looks**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bagay, katangian, o punto na nagpapaiba sa dalawa o higit pang tao, bagay, o konsepto.
etymology: From ka- + iba + -han. The suffix -han turns the concept into a noun.
original_explanation: The **difference** between "On my way" and "OTW." The first one means they're actually traveling. The second one means they're just getting out of the shower. It's the subtle distinction that matters.
usage_notes: The noun form of 'kaiba'. Used when pointing out the specific difference between things. See also the common contraction 'kaibhan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **kaibahan** ng 'ng' at 'nang'?","translation":"What is the **difference** between 'ng' and 'nang'?"},{"sentence":"Malaki ang **kaibahan** ng buhay sa probinsya kumpara sa siyudad.","translation":"There is a big **difference** between life in the province compared to the city."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang takdang halaga ng salapi na ibinabayad bilang kontribusyon o bayarin sa isang samahan, klub, o grupo.
original_explanation: That 'ambagan' you have to pay for your homeowners' association, your office 'paluwagan', or your barkada's beach trip fund. It's the fee that makes you an official member, the one you sometimes 'forget' to pay until the treasurer DMs you with a smiley face.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of organizations, clubs, or community groups for recurring payments.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakalimutan kong magbayad ng buwanang **butaw** sa aming kooperatiba.","translation":"I forgot to pay the monthly **dues** for our cooperative."},{"sentence":"Siningil na kami para sa **butaw** ng Christmas party.","translation":"We were already asked to pay the **contribution** for the Christmas party."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa anumang bagay, lalo na ang kasuotan, na ginagamit o isinusuot para sa isang burol o lamay.
etymology: From `pan-` (a prefix used to denote an instrument or purpose) + `burol` (wake, vigil for the dead). The `n` in `pan-` assimilates to `m` before `b`.
original_explanation: This is your 'outfit of the day' (#OOTD) for visiting a wake. Usually, it's something respectful and somber, like a black or white shirt. It's the kind of clothing you keep ready, but hope you don't have to use often. Parang emergency fund, pero para sa social obligation sa patay.
usage_notes: Can be used as an adjective ("damit na pamburol") or a noun ("May pamburol ka na ba?").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghanap siya ng damit na **pamburol** nang mabalitaan niyang namatay ang kanyang kaibigan.","translation":"She looked for clothes **for the wake** when she heard her friend had passed away."},{"sentence":"Itabi mo na 'yang itim na polo, gawin nating **pamburol**.","translation":"Set aside that black polo shirt, let's make it your go-to **funeral attire**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang pangkat o grupo ng mga indibidwal na kumikilos bilang isang yunit; isang samahan na may iisang layunin.
original_explanation: Parang group project sa school, lahat kayo dapat gumagalaw. Or, 'yung mga jeepney driver na may sariling association, 'yun ay isang kolektibo. It’s about teamwork making the dream work, pero sa mas pormal na paraan.
usage_notes: Can be used as both an adjective (e.g., 'pangkat na kolektibo') and a noun (e.g., 'ang kolektibo').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang desisyon ay ginawa ng buong **kolektibo**.","translation":"The decision was made by the entire **collective**."},{"sentence":"May **kolektibo** silang pagsisikap na linisin ang ilog.","translation":"They have a **collective** effort to clean the river."}]

translation: patrolling; the act of conducting a patrol
meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pag-ikot sa isang lugar upang mapanatili ang kaayusan, seguridad, at kapayapaan.
etymology: From pag- (nominalizer) + pa- (causative) + patrolya (patrol), which is from Spanish `patrulla`.
original_explanation: This is what the barangay tanod, the security guard sa mall, or the police do. It's the act of making the rounds ('ronda') to make sure everything's okay. Parang 'yung jowa mong laging chine-check 'yung phone mo, pagpapatrolya rin 'yun in a way, but the toxic kind.
usage_notes: Used in security, military, and law enforcement contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan ng kapitan ang mga tanod para sa gabi-gabing **pagpapatrolya** sa kanilang barangay.","translation":"The captain ordered the watchmen to conduct nightly **patrolling** in their village."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapatrolya** ng mga pulis ay nagbibigay ng pakiramdam ng seguridad sa komunidad.","translation":"The **patrolling** of the police gives a sense of security to the community."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng palitan ng pagbibigay sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang tao; pagpapakita ng pagiging bukas-palad sa isa't isa.
original_explanation: This is the spirit of Christmas, bayanihan, and potlucks in one word. It's about reciprocal giving. It's not just 'I give to you,' but 'we give to each other.' When the family does gift-giving, they 'magbigayan.' When your team is cramming for a deadline, you 'magbigayan' ng support (and coffee). It’s the verb for 'walang iwanan.'
usage_notes: Implies a mutual or group action. The focus is on the exchange and shared generosity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa Pasko, masaya ang mga pamilya na **magbigayan** ng regalo.","translation":"During Christmas, families are happy **to give gifts to each other**."},{"sentence":"Dapat tayong **magbigayan** sa oras ng pangangailangan.","translation":"We should **be generous to one another** in times of need."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ilegal na nagpapasok o naglalabas ng mga kalakal sa isang bansa.
original_explanation: Eto yung ninja moves ng pag-import ng goods. Sila yung dahilan kung bakit may "Class A" version ng paborito mong sapatos o bag sa tiangge. Parang "add to cart" pero on a whole other, highly illegal level.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng ilegal na kalakalan sa mga daungan o hangganan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahuli ng mga awtoridad ang kilabot na **ismagler** ng mga mamahaling sasakyan.","translation":"The authorities caught the notorious **smuggler** of luxury cars."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkawala ng talim o tulis ng isang bagay; ang pagiging pango ng ilong.
original_explanation: This is what happens to a pencil after you use it to write a 1000-word essay on why your ex was wrong. It lost its point. Or, according to lola, what happens to your nose if you keep telling lies.
usage_notes: This is a less common verb form. The adjective 'pango' is more frequently used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pumangos** ang dulo ng lapis dahil sa kakagamit.","translation":"The tip of the pencil **became blunt** from so much use."},{"sentence":"Sa kwento ng matatanda, **pumangos** daw ang ilong ni Pinocchio.","translation":"In old stories, they say Pinocchio's nose **became snub-nosed** (implying it shortened after being long)."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang trabaho ay magbantay o magprotekta sa isang lugar, gusali, o tao.
original_explanation: That person you greet with 'Good morning, manong guard!' every day. They're the gatekeepers of condos, malls, banks, and schools. They check your bag, ask for your ID, and are the first line of defense against any *kaguluhan*. They're often underappreciated but super essential. Also known as 'sekyu.'
usage_notes: Colloquially shortened to 'sekyu' from the English 'security'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang **guwardiya** sa entrada ng subdivision.","translation":"The **guard** at the subdivision entrance is strict."},{"sentence":"Pakiiwan po ng ID sa **guwardiya** bago pumasok.","translation":"Please leave your ID with the **guard** before entering."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong lisensyado at may kasanayang magpalipad ng sasakyang panghimpapawid, tulad ng eroplano o helikopter.
original_explanation: The person in charge of your Cebu Pacific or PAL flight. They're the reason you can get from Manila to Cebu in an hour instead of a day. Basically, the ultimate Grab driver of the skies. Also, a childhood dream job for many, right next to being a doctor or an astronaut.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to an aircraft pilot. For a ship's pilot, 'kapitan' is more common, though 'piloto' can also be used in a nautical context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang maging isang **piloto** ng komersyal na eroplano.","translation":"His dream is to become a commercial airplane **pilot**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging nasa ilalim ng impluwensya ng alak o anumang nakalalasing na inumin.
etymology: From the root word 'lasing' (drunk) + the '-um-' infix.
original_explanation: The verb form of your Friday night. It's the process, not the destination. Nagsimula sa "isang bote lang," tapos ayun, lumasing na. The transformation from a functioning adult to someone who thinks karaoke at 3 AM is a great idea.
usage_notes: The action of becoming drunk. The state is 'lasing'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis siyang **lumasing** dahil hindi siya kumain.","translation":"He **got drunk** quickly because he didn't eat."},{"sentence":"Nagplano silang mag-inuman pero hindi **lumasing**.","translation":"They planned to drink but not to **get drunk**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, pangyayari, o sitwasyon na hindi karaniwan at nagdudulot ng pagtataka, pagkamangha, o pagkalito.
etymology: From nakapag- (causative) + taka (wonder, surprise). It functions as an adjective describing something that causes wonder.
original_explanation: That 'sana all' moment but for weird stuff. When your friend who's always late arrives on time. When your internet is suddenly fast. When an appliance fixes itself. It's anything that makes you go 'Hala, paano nangyari 'yun?' or 'Wow, amazing!'. It's the universe glitching in a good (or just plain weird) way.
usage_notes: This very common word acts as an adjective to describe a situation or event that is surprising or puzzling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakapagtataka** kung paano niya nalaman ang sikreto natin.","translation":"It's **surprising** how he found out about our secret."},{"sentence":"**Nakapagtataka** ang bilis ng paglago ng kanilang negosyo.","translation":"The speed of their business's growth is **amazing**."}]

translation: pocket money, something for the pocket
meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na halaga ng salapi na inilalaan para sa maliliit na gastusin; maaari ring tumukoy sa suhol o lagay.
original_explanation: Your daily allowance or 'baon'. Pwede ring 'yung extra cash na binibigay ni Tito for 'ice cream'. Minsan, may darker meaning 'yan, 'yung 'lagay' para pabilisin ang proseso. 'Pampadulas' ika nga.
usage_notes: Can have a neutral meaning (allowance) or a negative one (bribe), depending on context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigyan mo ng pambili ng kendi ang bata, kahit pang-**pamulsa** lang.","translation":"Give the child money to buy candy, just something for his **pocket**."},{"sentence":"Humingi ako sa nanay ko ng **pamulsa** para sa field trip namin.","translation":"I asked my mom for **pocket money** for our field trip."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay, tulad ng kosmetiko o palamuti, na ginagamit upang mapabuti o mapatingkad ang pisikal na anyo o kagandahan.
etymology: From 'pang-' (instrumental prefix) + 'pa-' (causative prefix) + 'ganda' (beauty). Lit. 'that which is used to cause beauty'.
original_explanation: Your daily war paint. From the kikay kit essentials like lipstick and foundation to that filter you can't live without on Instagram. Anything that makes you go from 'puyat from work' to 'photoshoot-ready.' Also known as 'this month's budget.'
usage_notes: Often refers to makeup, but can also be used for clothing, accessories, or even actions that improve appearance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili siya ng mga bagong **pampaganda** para sa party.","translation":"She bought new **cosmetics** for the party."},{"sentence":"Ang isang magandang ngiti ay mabisang **pampaganda**.","translation":"A beautiful smile is an effective **beautifier**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na tumutukoy sa isang bagay o tao na pangit, hindi kaaya-aya sa paningin, o may mababang kalidad.
etymology: Origin is debated, but it's a prominent term in Swardspeak (gay lingo) that entered mainstream consciousness. Some theories suggest it's a portmanteau or simply an onomatopoeic-like word for disgust.
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino diss for anything visually offensive. Your outfit? Chaka. Your ex's new partner? Super chaka. The movie you just watched? Ang chaka! It's short, brutal, and universally understood. It's the opposite of 'pak!' or 'taray!'.
usage_notes: Can refer to people, things, situations, or outcomes. While informal, it is widely used and understood across different social groups.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ay, ang **chaka** ng nabili kong sapatos online, iba sa picture!","translation":"Oh, the shoes I bought online are so **ugly**, they look different from the picture!"},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi ka **chaka**, kailangan mo lang ng kumpiyansa.","translation":"Don't worry, you're not **ugly**, you just need confidence."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang palikpik ng isda na matatagpuan sa magkabilang gilid ng katawan, sa likod ng hasang, na katumbas ng braso sa mga bertebrado sa lupa.
etymology: Possibly from "pa-" prefix + "y-" infix + "pikpik" (to pat lightly), likening the fin's movement to patting.
original_explanation: Basically, the 'arms' or 'armpits' of a fish. It's the two fins on the side that help it steer. When you're eating a whole fried fish, it's that little fin near the head that gets extra crispy.
usage_notes: A specific anatomical term for fish. Not a common word unless you're a fisherman, a marine biologist, or very specific about your 'sinigang na isda'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinikik ako sa **payikpik** ng bangus.","translation":"A bone from the **pectoral fin** of the milkfish got stuck in my throat."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang kilos, pananamit, o lugar na itinuturing na mababa ang uri, magulo, o hindi kaaya-aya ayon sa pamantayan ng lipunan.
etymology: From English 'ghetto', which is originally from Italian 'ghetto'.
original_explanation: When your tita calls your ripped jeans "ghetto," she means it looks cheap or "iskwater." It's the Pinoy way of saying something lacks class or refinement, whether it's a place, a person's style, or their "asal" (behavior). It’s a borrowed word, but we use it with our own special brand of judgment.
usage_notes: Often used with a negative, classist connotation to describe behavior, style, or places deemed unrefined or of a lower social status.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang manirahan doon dahil masyadong **ghetto** daw ang lugar.","translation":"He doesn't want to live there because he says the place is too **ghetto**."},{"sentence":"Itigil mo 'yang pag-uugaling **ghetto**, nakakahiya sa mga bisita.","translation":"Stop that **crude** behavior, it's embarrassing in front of the guests."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maikling kurso o kilusan sa loob ng Simbahang Katoliko na naglalayong palalimin ang pananampalataya at pamumuhay Kristiyano.
original_explanation: A spiritual 'bootcamp' for Catholic adults. It's a three-day retreat that's a mix of intense talks, group sharing, and prayer, often leading to a profound spiritual renewal. It's where your parents might have gone and came back with a new perspective and a theme song.
usage_notes: Refers to the 'Cursillos in Christianity' movement, a specific type of religious retreat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumali siya sa **kursilyo** noong nakaraang linggo.","translation":"He joined the **Cursillo** last week."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang naging epekto ng **kursilyo** sa kanyang buhay-espiritwal.","translation":"The **Cursillo** had a big impact on his spiritual life."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng paghahanap at pagpatay o paghuli sa mga ligaw na hayop, karaniwan para sa pagkain, libangan, o kalakalan.
original_explanation: Before GrabFood, this was the original delivery service. It’s the act of hunting for game. Today, "pangangaso" is what you do at the mall during a 70% off sale, hunting for the best deals before someone else grabs them.
usage_notes: The root word 'aso' (to hunt) is different from 'aso' (dog). Context is key. 'Pangangaso' always refers to hunting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagbabawal ang **pangangaso** ng mga endangered species.","translation":"The **hunting** of endangered species is prohibited."},{"sentence":"Ang **pangangaso** ay isang tradisyonal na paraan ng pamumuhay para sa ilang mga katutubong tribo.","translation":"**Hunting** is a traditional way of life for some indigenous tribes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalagyan kung saan kumakain ang mga hayop; isang lugar na itinalaga para sa pagkain.
etymology: From 'pa-' (causative) + 'kain' (eat) + '-an' (locative suffix). Literally, "a place for causing eating".
original_explanation: This is the designated dining area, whether it's the fancy trough for your alagang baboy, the bird feeder for your tita's feathered friends, or even the mess hall in a BPO where everyone rushes for the free lunch. It's the 'chow zone'.
usage_notes: Often refers to animal feeders but can also be used for designated human eating areas, especially in institutional settings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nilinisan ni Mang Tonyo ang **pakainan** ng mga baboy.","translation":"Mang Tonyo cleaned the pigs' **trough**."},{"sentence":"Puno na ng butil ang **pakainan** ng mga manok.","translation":"The chickens' **feeder** is full of grain."}]

translation: to advise, to lecture, to preach to
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng payo o aral sa isang tao upang ituwid ang kanyang pag-uugali o kaisipan.
original_explanation: The verb form of "pangaral". It's what happens when you get caught coming home past curfew. Your dad sits you down and starts to **pangaralan** you about responsibility. It's the "we need to talk" of Filipino parenting.
usage_notes: Can be used in a gentle sense (to advise) or a more stern one (to reprimand or lecture).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **pangaralan** na parang bata pa ako.","translation":"Don't **lecture** me as if I'm still a child."},{"sentence":"Nais niyang **pangaralan** ang mga kabataan tungkol sa pag-iimpok.","translation":"He wants to **advise** the youth about saving money."}]

meaning_filipino: Nakaayos sa maraming hanay o linya sa isang organisadong paraan.
original_explanation: This is what your pantry looks like for 5 minutes after you've organized all the cans. It's `hanay` but make it plural and aesthetic. "Hanay-hanay ang mga produkto sa supermarket shelf." It implies order and multiplicity. It's the OCD version of `hanay`.
usage_notes: Describes how things are arranged. Can also function as an adjective ('mga bahay na hanay-hanay').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hanay-hanay** ang mga sasakyan sa parking lot.","translation":"The cars are **in neat rows** in the parking lot."},{"sentence":"Magtanim tayo ng mga halaman nang **hanay-hanay**.","translation":"Let's plant the seedlings **in rows**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao, bagay, o istilo na napapanahon at sumasabay sa kasalukuyang uso o popular na disenyo.
original_explanation: This is your friend who always has the latest iPhone, wears the "in" colors, and knows all the TikTok dances. Sila yung hindi pahuhuli sa uso, from their shoes to their choice of milk tea. Being **sunod sa moda** is a full-time job, bes!
usage_notes: A common phrase. "Moda" is from Spanish.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging **sunod sa moda** ang pananamit ni Cassandra.","translation":"Cassandra's style of dress is always **fashionable**."},{"sentence":"Kahit simple lang, mukha ka pa ring **sunod sa moda** dahil sa iyong bagong sapatos.","translation":"Even if you're just simple, you still look **trendy** because of your new shoes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na seremonya kung saan ang isang tao ay opisyal na binibigyan ng ranggo, karangalan, o kapangyarihan.
original_explanation: This is a super formal word for a ceremony that's basically a level-up. Think of a graduation, but for becoming a president, a new CEO, or a Knight of Rizal. It's the official event where they hand you the fancy robe, the medal, or the scepter of power. It's the academic or formal version of being sworn in. You'll see this word a lot in university event invitations or news reports about new officials.
usage_notes: A formal term used in academic, governmental, and organizational contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **imbestidura** ng bagong pangulo ng unibersidad ay gaganapin sa susunod na buwan.","translation":"The **investiture** of the new university president will be held next month."},{"sentence":"Isang marangyang **imbestidura** ang inihanda para sa mga bagong kasapi ng samahan.","translation":"A grand **investiture ceremony** was prepared for the new members of the organization."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalaan o pagtatabi ng isang bagay para sa isang partikular na tao, layunin, o okasyon.
original_explanation: This is what your mom does with the 'special' plates and silverware that only come out for fiestas or when a VIP (like the parish priest) visits. It's the act of setting something aside. Parang pag-magtaan ka ng feelings para sa 'the one' kahit marami nang nag-a-apply.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'maglaan' but 'magtaan' can have a stronger sense of reserving for a specific person or purpose.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magtaan** ng pagkain para sa mga bisitang darating mamaya.","translation":"We need to **set aside** food for the guests arriving later."},{"sentence":"Nag**taan** siya ng isang upuan para sa kanyang kaibigan.","translation":"She **reserved** a seat for her friend."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging magkasalungat sa panig, opinyon, o interes. Maaari ring tumukoy sa mga taong magkaribal.
etymology: From `mag-` + `ka-` (denoting a pair or group) + `kontra` (from Spanish 'contra', meaning 'against').
original_explanation: Sila 'yung bida at kontrabida sa teleserye ng buhay mo. 'Yung isa gusto ng aircon na 20 degrees, 'yung isa gusto 25 degrees. Sa politika, ito 'yung Dilawan vs DDS. Sa office, 'yung Team A vs Team B sa sales. Laging may banggaan.
usage_notes: Can describe people, ideas, or teams that are in opposition. Can also be used as a noun to mean 'rivals'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagi silang **magkakontra** sa opinyon pagdating sa pulitika.","translation":"They always have **opposing** opinions when it comes to politics."},{"sentence":"Ang dalawang koponan ay matagal nang **magkakontra**.","translation":"The two teams have long been **rivals**."}]

translation: to give way; to make way
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-urong o paghinto upang makaraan ang iba; maaari ring tumukoy sa pagiging sanhi o pagbubukas ng oportunidad para sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: Literally, 'to give road.' On the street, it's what you do for an ambulance, or what that slow car in the fast lane *should* do. Figuratively, it’s about paving the way for something or someone else. An older CEO might retire to 'magbigay-daan' for new leadership. A crisis can 'magbigay-daan' for new opportunities. It's the verb for both traffic courtesy and major life changes.
usage_notes: Has both a literal meaning (traffic) and a figurative one (opportunity, succession).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat tayong **magbigay-daan** sa mga ambulansya at bumbero.","translation":"We should **give way** to ambulances and fire trucks."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang pagreretiro ay **nagbigay-daan** sa mas batang lider.","translation":"His retirement **made way** for a younger leader."}]

translation: to radio; to contact via radio
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapadala ng mensahe o komunikasyon sa isang tao o lugar gamit ang radyo bilang midyum.
original_explanation: Bago mag-Viber or Messenger group chat, ito ang way ng mga pulis, sundalo, at BFP para mag-update. "Alpha-1 to base, pakiradyuhan mo si Bravo-2, may 2-piece chicken with rice dito, over." It's the original voice message.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Radyuhan** mo ang kabilang team at sabihing parating na tayo.","translation":"**Radio** the other team and tell them we are on our way."}]

translation: to be broken (brittle); to be shattered
meaning_filipino: Masira o magkapira-piraso, karaniwan para sa mga bagay na babasagin tulad ng salamin o plato.
original_explanation: The sound your heart makes when your crush posts 'in a relationship with...' someone else. Also, the literal sound of your mom's favorite 'plato' when it slips from your hand. It's the 'uh oh' moment for anything fragile, from glassware to feelings.
usage_notes: Specifically for brittle items that shatter, like glass, ceramic, or even a voice ('mabasag ang boses'). For things that tear or rip, use 'mapunit'. For things that snap, use 'mabali'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nanginginig ang kanyang kamay kaya nahulog at **nabasag** ang baso.","translation":"Her hand was shaking, so the glass fell and **shattered**."},{"sentence":"Sa sobrang kaba, halos **mabasag** ang kanyang boses habang nagsasalita.","translation":"From extreme nervousness, her voice almost **broke** while speaking."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghingi ng payo, opinyon, o impormasyon mula sa isang tao o pangkat na may sapat na kaalaman.
original_explanation: This is what you do when WebMD scares you into thinking you have a rare disease, so you finally decide to pagkonsultahan a real doctor. It's asking your team lead for advice, or huddling with your barkada to decide where to eat. Basically, it's 'getting a second opinion' from someone who (hopefully) knows better.
usage_notes: This is in the object-focus verb form, meaning 'to consult with someone/something'. The root 'konsulta' is more common as a noun ('consultation').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **pagkonsultahan** ang iyong mga magulang tungkol sa iyong mga plano.","translation":"You need **to consult with** your parents about your plans."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magdesisyon agad; **pagkonsultahan** muna natin ang mga eksperto.","translation":"Don't decide right away; let's **consult with** the experts first."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng masangsang at hindi kanais-nais na amoy, karaniwang iniuugnay sa ihi o hindi nalilinis na katawan o lugar.
original_explanation: If "anghit" is specific to armpits, "angis" is its less famous but equally offensive cousin. It's that stale, musky smell of a public toilet that hasn't seen water in a week, or the scent of unwashed clothes left in a corner for too long. It's a smell that makes your nose wrinkle involuntarily.
usage_notes: Less common than 'anghit' or 'baho'. Describes a specific type of foul, stale, or urinous odor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroong amoy **angis** sa eskinita na iyon.","translation":"There's a **musky odor** in that alley."},{"sentence":"Kailangang labhan ang mga kumot na ito dahil nangangamoy **angis** na.","translation":"These blankets need to be washed because they're starting to have a **stale, musky smell**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng mga kagamitan, kasangkapan, o sangkap na kailangan para sa isang tiyak na layunin o gawain.
original_explanation: It's when you're fully geared up. Parang 'yung condo unit na "fully furnished"—may kama, ref, at aircon na. O kaya 'yung gamer na kumpleto ang RGB setup. You're not just ready, you're **nakasangkapan** for battle... or for a chill movie night.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a place (like a house or kitchen) or a person being fully supplied with necessary tools or equipment for a task.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bagong kusina ay **nakasangkapan** na ng lahat ng modernong kagamitan.","translation":"The new kitchen is already **equipped** with all modern appliances."},{"sentence":"Dumating ang mga sundalo na **nakasangkapan** para sa isang mahabang laban.","translation":"The soldiers arrived, fully **equipped** for a long battle."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang kilos ng pagtalon o pag-angat ng katawan mula sa lupa gamit ang lakas ng mga paa.
original_explanation: What your heart does when you get a "Good morning" text from your crush. Also, what you do on New Year's Eve to supposedly get taller. "Hoy, 12 AM na, **lumulukso** na ang lahat!"
usage_notes: This is the present tense form (progressive aspect) of the verb. 'Lumukso' is the completed/infinitive form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lumulukso** sa tuwa ang bata tuwing nakikita ang kanyang tatay.","translation":"The child **is jumping** with joy whenever he sees his father."},{"sentence":"Bakit **lumulukso** ang kuryente sa metro?","translation":"Why **is** the electricity in the meter **jumping** (spiking)?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng aspili na may pananggalang o takip sa dulo upang maiwasan ang di-sinasadyang pagtusok.
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino life hack tool. Need to fix a broken zipper? **Emperdible**. Wardrobe malfunction during a presentation? **Emperdible**. Need to get the SIM card out of your phone? **Emperdible**. It's the low-tech, multi-tool that lives in every Pinay's kikay kit and every lola's sewing box.
usage_notes: The spelling 'imperdible' is also sometimes used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang **emperdible** para ayusin ang laylayan ng kanyang palda.","translation":"She used a **safety pin** to fix the hem of her skirt."},{"sentence":"Pahiram naman ng **emperdible**, nasira ang strap ng bag ko.","translation":"Can I borrow a **safety pin**? The strap of my bag broke."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pag-alam o pagtanggap sa pagkakakilanlan, halaga, o pagkakaroon ng isang tao, bagay, o konsepto.
original_explanation: This is what you crave after pulling an all-nighter for a project – pagkilala from your boss. It's when you see an old classmate and your brain buffers for 5 seconds before shouting their name. It's giving credit where credit is due, whether it's for an 'Employee of the Month' award or just admitting your mom was right all along.
usage_notes: A broad term covering everything from simple recognition of a face to formal awards and acknowledgment of rights.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumanggap siya ng parangal bilang **pagkilala** sa kanyang mga nagawa para sa komunidad.","translation":"She received an award in **recognition** of her achievements for the community."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkilala** sa sariling pagkakamali ay unang hakbang sa pagbabago.","translation":"The **acknowledgment** of one's own mistake is the first step towards change."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginagamit sa pagtukoy sa oras, nangangahulugang lumipas na ang isang takdang oras o minuto.
original_explanation: The Filipino time-telling flavor that means "a little bit past the hour." "Alas-dos pasado" means it's a bit past 2:00, but who's counting the exact minutes, right? It's the relaxed, non-specific way of telling time, perfect for "Filipino time" culture. It’s the verbal equivalent of shrugging and saying "around that time."
usage_notes: Always used with time, following the hour. For example, "ala-una pasado" (past one), "alas-singko pasado" (past five).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumating siya ng **pasado** alas-otso ng umaga.","translation":"He arrived **past** eight in the morning."},{"sentence":"Magkita tayo ng mga **pasado** ala-una, pagkatapos ng tanghalian.","translation":"Let's meet around **past** one, after lunch."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na lihim at ilegal na nagpapasok o naglalabas ng mga kalakal sa isang bansa upang maiwasan ang pagbabayad ng buwis o pagdaan sa legal na proseso.
original_explanation: The OG 'pasabuy' expert, but for illegal stuff. Sila yung nagpapasok ng mga bagay na bawal, parang yung kaibigan mong nagpuslit ng pagkain sa sinehan, pero on a national, highly illegal scale. From imported onions to luxury cars.
usage_notes: The goods being smuggled are called 'kontrabando'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahuli ng mga awtoridad ang isang kilalang **kontrabandista** ng mga sigarilyo.","translation":"The authorities arrested a known **smuggler** of cigarettes."},{"sentence":"Maraming opisyal ang iniimbestigahan dahil sa umano'y pagiging **kontrabandista**.","translation":"Many officials are being investigated for allegedly being **smugglers**."}]

translation: in a prone position; lying face down
meaning_filipino: Sa paraan ng paghiga na ang tiyan at dibdib ay nakadikit sa ibabaw at ang likod ay nasa itaas.
original_explanation: This is how you sleep after a long, stressful week at work. Or how you end up after a round of tequila shots. It's the official position of "I give up on today." Also the classic "Dapa!" command when someone is about to get hit.
usage_notes: Can describe a state (lying prone) or an action (falling or getting down into a prone position).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natagpuan siyang natutulog nang **padapa** sa sahig dahil sa sobrang pagod.","translation":"He was found sleeping **face down** on the floor due to extreme exhaustion."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang tao na ang kilos, salita, o paniniwala ay hindi taos-puso at salungat sa tunay na nararamdaman o pagkatao; pagkukunwari.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `mapag-` (pagkahilig) at `paimbabaw` (superficiality), na mula sa `ibabaw` (surface). "May pagkahilig na maging nasa ibabaw lamang."
original_explanation: The "plastic" friend. Sila yung ngingitian ka sa harap mo, pero pagtalikod mo, topic ka na sa ibang group chat. They say one thing but do another. Yung nagpo-post ng "Save the Earth" pero tapon naman nang tapon ng basura kung saan-saan. All for show, all for appearances. What you see is NOT what you get.
usage_notes: Kasingkahulugan ng `ipokrito` o `plastik` sa modernong salita. Ang `mapagpaimbabaw` ay ang mas pormal at pampanitikang termino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap pagkatiwalaan ang isang taong **mapagpaimbabaw**.","translation":"It's hard to trust a **hypocritical** person."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **mapagpaimbabaw** na kabaitan ay halata sa mga nakakakilala sa kanya.","translation":"Her **superficial** kindness is obvious to those who know her."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian o kilos ng hindi pagiging maingat na nagreresulta sa kapahamakan, pagkakamali, o pinsala.
original_explanation: This is the "Ah, sh*t" moment. It's texting while walking and bumping into a post. It's forgetting to hit 'save' on a 10-page document. It's accidentally sending a screenshot *to the person you're talking about*. It's the opposite of "think before you click," and it's the reason why we have warning labels and double-checking protocols in the BPO world.
usage_notes: Often used to describe the cause of an accident or mistake.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aksidente ay bunga ng kanyang **pagkawalang-ingat** sa pagmamaneho.","translation":"The accident was a result of his **carelessness** in driving."},{"sentence":"Pinagsisihan niya ang kanyang **pagkawalang-ingat** na naging sanhi ng pagkawala ng mahahalagang dokumento.","translation":"He regretted his **negligence** which caused the loss of important documents."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagkaing Pilipino na gawa sa sariwa at malambot na tokwa (silken tofu), arnibal (matamis na sarsang gawa sa tinunaw na asukal), at maliliit na sago.
etymology: Mula sa Hokkien 豆花 (tāu-hue), na nangangahulugang 'bulaklak ng tokwa'.
original_explanation: The ultimate morning comfort food delivered straight to your doorstep by a shouting manong. 'TAHOOOOO!' is the best alarm clock. It's that warm, sweet, silky goodness in a cup that can fix a bad morning. The sago pearls are the boba of our parents' generation. Pro tip: extra arnibal, always.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa partikular na pagkaing Pilipino na ito. Karaniwang inilalako ng mga nagtitinda sa kalye tuwing umaga.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng **taho** mula sa magtataho kaninang umaga.","translation":"I bought **taho** from the taho vendor this morning."},{"sentence":"Paborito ng mga bata ang matamis na **taho**.","translation":"Children's favorite is the sweet **taho**."}]

meaning_filipino: Gumamit ng walis upang linisin ang dumi o kalat sa sahig, bakuran, o anumang ibabaw.
original_explanation: The national pastime every Saturday morning. To **magwalis** is the OG Filipino workout before Zumba was even a thing. It's the act of using a 'walis tambo' (for indoors) or a 'walis tingting' (for outdoors) to assert dominance over dust, dried leaves, and all the 'resibo' of your bad decisions. Also, the first step in getting your mom to calm down when she's angry.
usage_notes: A very common verb for daily chores. The type of broom ('walis tambo' or 'walis tingting') is often implied by the context (indoors vs. outdoors).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan si Totoy na **magwalis** sa buong bakuran bago siya maglaro.","translation":"Totoy was ordered to **sweep** the entire yard before he could play."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **magwalis** dahil puno na ng alikabok ang sahig.","translation":"I need to **sweep** because the floor is full of dust."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasunduan sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang tao kung saan ang bawat isa ay tumataya ng pera o isang bagay sa isang kaganapan na hindi tiyak ang kalalabasan.
original_explanation: The national sport during any Pacquiao fight, beauty pageant, or basketball game. It's when your tito says "P1000 kay Catriona!" It can be for money, a case of beer, or just bragging rights. The verbal contract that turns any event into a high-stakes championship.
usage_notes: Can also function as a location or event ("sa pustahan" - at the betting place) or a verb command "Pustahan tayo!" (Let's bet!).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **pustahan** kami kung sino ang mananalo sa eleksyon.","translation":"We have a **bet** on who will win the election."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang nanalo niya sa **pustahan** sa sabong.","translation":"He won big from the **betting** at the cockfight."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong masayahin, palabiro, at may pagka-sira ang ulo sa positibong paraan.
etymology: ma- (having the quality of) + kalog (shake/jolt), figuratively "shaken brain" or "loose screw".
original_explanation: Ito 'yung kaibigan mong laging may energy, laging may kalokohan, at laging nagpapatawa sa group chat. Sila 'yung official "jester" ng barkada. "Si Alex talaga ang pinaka-makalog sa aming lahat, laging may baong hirit!"
usage_notes: Used informally to describe a person's personality. It's generally a positive or endearing term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa opisina bilang isang **makalog** pero mahusay na empleyado.","translation":"She is known in the office as a **wacky** but efficient employee."},{"sentence":"Ang saya kasama ng mga **makalog** mong kaibigan.","translation":"It's fun to be with your **wacky** friends."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang indibidwal na babae na may kaparehong mga magulang sa isa pa, o may isa man lang na magulang na kapareho.
original_explanation: Your 'ate' or 'bunso' that you either fight with over clothes or team up with against your parents. She's your forever frenemy, your first best friend, and the one who knows exactly how to push your buttons. In short, your ride-or-die, but will also 'sumbong' you to your nanay.
usage_notes: The standard way to specify a female sibling. Often shortened in speech or replaced by 'ate' (for older sister) or the person's name.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kapatid na babae** ko ang nagturo sa akin magbisikleta.","translation":"My **sister** taught me how to ride a bike."}]

translation: to form; to take the shape of
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbuo o pagkakaroon ng isang partikular na anyo o porma.
original_explanation: This is the verb for glow-ups and transformations. It's what clay does in a potter's hands, what a caterpillar does inside a chrysalis, and what your body does when you finally stick to your new year's resolution of going to the gym. It's the process of becoming, of taking on a new form, like your savings account that 'maghugis' negative balance after a 12.12 sale.
usage_notes: Often used with an object or a description of the new shape, for instance, 'maghugis-puso' (to take the shape of a heart). The phrase 'maghugis nang panibago' means 'to be reshaped' or 'to take a new form'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga ulap ay tila **naghugis** na isang malaking barko.","translation":"The clouds seemed to **take the shape of** a large ship."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan ng iskultor na **maghugis** ng mukha ng tao mula sa putik.","translation":"The sculptor is trying to **form** a human face from the clay."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng martilyo na karaniwang gawa sa kahoy o goma na ginagamit sa pagpukpok. Ginagamit din ito ng hukom sa korte.
original_explanation: The 'maseta' is that wooden hammer a judge bangs to say 'Order in the court!' or, in a more relatable scenario, what a carpenter uses to gently tap things into place without wrecking them. It's the 'persuader' tool. Also, it's what you wish you had to get everyone's attention during a chaotic Zoom meeting.
usage_notes: Can refer to a judge's gavel, a carpenter's mallet, or a meat tenderizer.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ng karpintero ang **maseta** upang ikabit ang paa ng lamesa.","translation":"The carpenter used the **mallet** to attach the table leg."},{"sentence":"Tatlong beses ipinukpok ng hukom ang kanyang **maseta**.","translation":"The judge banged his **gavel** three times."}]

translation: to summarize; to monopolize; to engulf
meaning_filipino: Kinuha ang lahat para sa sarili; binuod ang isang paksa o usapin; sinakop o nilamon nang buo.
original_explanation: This word is an overachiever with three personalities. 1) The student who lumagom (summarized) the entire book for a report. 2) The greedy business person who lumagom (monopolized) the whole market. 3) The dramatic cloud that lumagom (engulfed) the entire city. It's about taking it all in, whether it's information, profit, or physical space.
usage_notes: The 'summarize' meaning is common in academic contexts, while 'monopolize' or 'engulf' are also used. Context is key to understanding the intended meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lumagom** siya ng mga pangunahing punto mula sa mahabang talumpati.","translation":"He **summarized** the main points from the long speech."},{"sentence":"Tila **lumagom** ang dilim sa buong paligid.","translation":"It seemed as if the darkness **engulfed** the entire surroundings."}]

translation: to turn or direct (attention, gaze, etc.)
meaning_filipino: Ilipat ang direksyon ng tingin, atensyon, o isang bagay patungo sa iba.
original_explanation: That moment when you're talking to someone and a good-looking person walks by, and you subtly (or not so subtly) `ibaling` your eyes. It's what you do when you change the topic because the conversation is getting awkward. "Bes, ibaling mo na lang sa iba ang pagtingin mo, 'di ka na niyan babalikan."
usage_notes: Mostly used for intangible things like attention, gaze, conversation, or feelings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Subukan mong **ibaling** ang iyong atensyon sa pag-aaral.","translation":"Try to **direct** your attention to your studies."},{"sentence":"Bigla niyang **ibinaling** ang usapan nang tanungin siya tungkol sa kanyang ex.","translation":"She suddenly **changed** the topic when asked about her ex."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pag-uugaling masama, malupit, o walang kabutihan, na maihahalintulad sa isang demonyo.
original_explanation: This is next-level 'walang modo'. This is for the person who cuts in line, steals your parking spot, and then glares at you for it. It's for the chismosa who spreads fake news with a smile. Basically, anyone whose actions make you think, "Saan ka pinaglihi?" has **asal-demonyo**.
usage_notes: A very strong and insulting descriptor. It's a compound word that functions as an adjective.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itigil mo na ang iyong **asal-demonyo** at magpakabait ka.","translation":"Stop your **demonic behavior** and be good."},{"sentence":"Kinaiinisan siya ng lahat dahil sa kanyang **asal-demonyo**.","translation":"Everyone resents him because of his **ill-mannered** ways."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging dedikado; ang pag-aalay o pagtatalaga ng sarili, oras, o isang bagay para sa isang partikular na layunin o tao.
original_explanation: It's the 'why' behind the overtime, the 'reason' for the puyat. It's what you write in the first page of a book you're gifting to your jowa. It's the fuel for your passion project that's currently draining your bank account.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **dedikasyon** sa trabaho ay talagang kahanga-hanga.","translation":"His **dedication** to his work is truly admirable."},{"sentence":"May **dedikasyon** ang libro para sa kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"The book has a **dedication** to his parents."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghagis o pagbato ng isang bagay, karaniwang may puwersa.
etymology: Likely from Spanish "echar" (to throw, to cast).
original_explanation: It's the "Yeet!" of the Filipino vocabulary. It’s how you throw trash in the bin (or try to), how you pass the ball in piko, or how you dramatically toss your ex's stuff out the window. It's a throw with a bit of flair and intention.
usage_notes: Synonymous with "paghagis" and "pagbato". "Itsa" often implies a more casual or forceful underhand/overhand throw.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lakas ng **pag-itsa** niya ng bola kaya home run!","translation":"His **pitching** of the ball was so strong it was a home run!"},{"sentence":"Isang maling **pag-itsa** lang ng basura at may multa ka na.","translation":"Just one wrong **throw** of the trash and you'll get a fine."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na piraso ng tela, karaniwang parisukat, na ginagamit upang ipunas sa pawis, ilong, o bilang palamuti.
original_explanation: The OG face towel, tissue, and emergency palengke face mask all in one. Your lolo definitely has one in his pocket, probably smelling of Vicks VapoRub. In old Filipino movies, it's the thing you drop to get a cute guy's attention. Now, it’s mostly replaced by wet wipes, but the sentimental value is forever.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang kanyang **panyo** para punasan ang pawis sa noo.","translation":"He used his **handkerchief** to wipe the sweat from his forehead."},{"sentence":"Naiwan ko yata sa bahay ang puti kong **panyo**.","translation":"I think I left my white **handkerchief** at home."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging hindi mabilis o matagal sa pagkilos, pag-iisip, o pag-unlad.
original_explanation: The speed of your internet connection when you need it most. Also, the pace of the person in front of you at the ATM on payday. It’s the ultimate test of patience. "Ang bagal mo!" is the national anthem of the impatient.
usage_notes: Can function as a noun (slowness) or an adjective (slow). Often used in exclamations of frustration. The related form 'mabagal' is more common as a descriptive adjective.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakainis ang **bagal** ng serbisyo dito.","translation":"The **slowness** of the service here is annoying."},{"sentence":"**Bagal** kumilos! Mahuhuli na tayo sa klase.","translation":"So **slow**! We're going to be late for class."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, grupo, o kumpanya na nakikipagpaligsahan o karibal sa isang larangan, negosyo, o palakasan.
etymology: From `ka-` + `kompetensiya` (competition), which is from Spanish 'competencia'. The `ka-` prefix denotes a fellow participant in the competition.
original_explanation: Your BPO team's rival team for the highest CSAT score. The other sari-sari store across the street selling the same brand of suka. That officemate who's also gunning for the same promotion. They're the ones who keep you on your toes, the "kalaban" in a "friendly" competition.
usage_notes: Used in business, sports, and any competitive context. Can also be spelled as 'kakumpetensya'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Jollibee at McDonald's ay mahigpit na **kakompetensiya** sa Pilipinas.","translation":"Jollibee and McDonald's are tight **competitors** in the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Tiningnan niya ang kanyang **kakompetensiya** bago nagsimula ang takbuhan.","translation":"He looked at his **rival** before the race started."}]

translation: to get; to take; to obtain; to fetch
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkuha, pagdaklot, o pag-angkin sa isang bagay, tao, o konsepto mula sa isang lugar o pinagmulan.
original_explanation: The most versatile 'get' command. You can 'kunin' the remote, 'kunin' a course in college, 'kunin' a picture, or 'kunin' your package from the delivery rider. For ninongs and ninangs, it's the dreaded word from their inaanak: '**Kunin** mo na po ako!' (Sponsor me in marriage/baptism!).
usage_notes: A very common verb with a wide range of applications, from physical taking to abstract acquisition. The object of the verb is in the 'ang' case (e.g., kunin mo *ang* libro).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **kunin** mo ang baso sa kusina.","translation":"Please, **get** the glass from the kitchen."},{"sentence":"Anong kurso ang plano mong **kunin** sa kolehiyo?","translation":"What course do you plan to **take** in college?"},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **kunin** ang hindi sa iyo.","translation":"Do not **take** what is not yours."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay, karaniwang tela, na ginawa sa pamamagitan ng paghahabi gamit ang kamay at hindi makina.
original_explanation: The 'artisanal' or 'craft' version of fabric. It's the opposite of fast fashion. This is the stuff that costs more at Kultura because it was made with love, sweat, and possibly some tears by a real person, not a robot. Peak 'support local' energy.
usage_notes: A compound word from 'habi' (weave) and 'kamay' (hand).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagmamalaki niya ang suot niyang barong na **habing-kamay** mula sa Laguna.","translation":"He is proud of the barong he is wearing, which is **hand-woven** from Laguna."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bilang na kasunod ng labing-apat at bago ang labing-anim; katumbas ng 15.
original_explanation: The number 15. The most important day of the month for many employees: "A-kinse na!" (It's the 15th!), also known as PAYDAY. It's half of "kinse-trenta" (15th and 30th), the two holiest days in the corporate calendar. Also, the age you can't wait to leave behind for your debut at 18.
usage_notes: The Spanish-derived number is more common in everyday speech for dates and money than the native Tagalog 'labinlima'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sahod na naman sa a-**kinse**!","translation":"It's payday again on the **fifteenth**!"},{"sentence":"Bumili siya ng **kinse** pirasong itlog.","translation":"She bought **fifteen** pieces of eggs."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panahon sa pagitan ng hapon at gabi kung kailan unti-unting nawawala ang liwanag ng araw at nagsisimulang dumilim ang paligid.
etymology: Mula sa "pag-aagaw" (snatching) at "dilim" (darkness), na literal na nangangahulugang "ang pag-agaw ng dilim" sa liwanag.
original_explanation: This is that magical, often traffic-filled, time when the sun clocks out and the moon is about to clock in. Perfect for dramatic selfies with the sunset, or for rushing home before the 'lamig' gets you. It's the universe's 'last call' for daylight.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa panitikan at tula upang magpahiwatig ng pagbabago, pagtatapos, o romansa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula na ang prusisyon nang mag-umpisa ang **pag-aagaw-dilim**.","translation":"The procession began as **dusk** started to fall."},{"sentence":"Magandang pagmasdan ang paglabas ng mga bituin sa panahon ng **pag-aagaw-dilim**.","translation":"It's beautiful to watch the stars appear during **dusk**."}]

translation: to transcribe; to type; to set in type
meaning_filipino: Isulat o i-encode ang mga salita o simbolo; maglimbag gamit ang tipo.
original_explanation: Before "mag-type," there was "magtitik." This is the OG term for putting words into written form, whether by hand, typewriter, or printing press. It's the verb for creating the very text you're reading. Think of it as the formal, almost poetic, ancestor of "mag-encode ng data."
usage_notes: A more formal or literary term for "mag-type" or "magsulat".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga sinaunang eskriba ay matiyagang **nagtitik** ng mga banal na kasulatan.","translation":"The ancient scribes patiently **transcribed** the holy scriptures."},{"sentence":"Inutusan siyang **magtitik** ng lahat ng sinabi sa pulong.","translation":"He was ordered to **transcribe** everything said in the meeting."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malubhang sakit na nakakahawa na karaniwang umaatake sa mga baga, sanhi ng bakteryang Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'ubo na may kasamang dugo' plot device in classic Filipino dramas. Before COVID, TB was the airborne illness everyone was wary of. It's a serious lung disease that requires long-term treatment, often associated with the free DOTS (Directly Observed Treatment, Short-course) program from health centers.
usage_notes: Isang terminong medikal. Ang karaniwang tawag sa sakit na ito sa kolokyal na usapan ay 'TB'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang libreng gamutan para sa **tuberculosis** ay malaking tulong sa mga mahihirap.","translation":"The free treatment for **tuberculosis** is a big help to the poor."},{"sentence":"Pinayuhan siya ng doktor na magpa-X-ray upang matiyak kung mayroon siyang **tuberculosis**.","translation":"The doctor advised him to get an X-ray to confirm if he has **tuberculosis**."}]

translation: someone one gets along with; compatible
meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kaayon ng iyong ugali, pananaw, o interes; pagiging magaan ang loob o madaling pakisamahan.
original_explanation: Your 'vibes' person. That friend you can talk to for hours about anything or nothing. 'Yung hindi ka kailangang magpanggap. If you're into K-Pop, they're into K-Pop. If you hate pineapple on pizza, they hate it too. You just click. Antonym: 'yung ka-officemate mong laging kontra sa lahat ng suggestion mo.
usage_notes: Often used in the phrase 'mag-kasundo' (to get along) or 'di-magkasundo' (to not get along). Can be used as a noun ('Siya ang kasundo ko') or an adjective ('Kasundo kami').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Buti na lang at **kasundo** ko ang mga bago kong katrabaho.","translation":"Thankfully, I **get along with** my new colleagues."},{"sentence":"Si Maria ang tanging **kasundo** ni Pedro sa kanilang pamilya.","translation":"Maria is the only one Pedro **gets along with** in their family."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbaba o pagkawala sa paningin, tulad ng araw sa kanluran o isang bagay sa tubig.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na unti-unti kang nawawalan ng pag-asa, parang araw na nagpapaalam sa hapon. O 'yung moment na nahulog 'yung phone mo sa inidoro. That's the paglubog of your hopes and dreams (and your phone).
usage_notes: Often used metaphorically for the decline of fame, fortune, or hope.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paglubog** ng barko ay isang malaking trahedya.","translation":"The **sinking** of the ship was a great tragedy."},{"sentence":"Sinabayan ng ulan ang **paglubog** ng araw.","translation":"Rain accompanied the **setting** of the sun."}]

meaning_filipino: Inilalahad sa paraan ng pagkukuwento o kronolohikal na paglalarawan ng mga pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is how your friend tells you about their weekend—not just the facts, but a full **pasalaysay** with side comments, flashbacks, and sound effects. It's not just a story, it's a teleserye episode.
usage_notes: Can also function as an adjective (e.g., 'tulang pasalaysay' - narrative poem).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ikinuwento niya nang **pasalaysay** ang mga nangyari sa kanyang bakasyon.","translation":"He recounted the events of his vacation **in a narrative manner**."},{"sentence":"Ang epiko ay isang uri ng tulang **pasalaysay**.","translation":"An epic is a type of **narrative** poem."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaloob ng kapangyarihan o awtoridad sa isang tao upang kumatawan o gumawa ng desisyon para sa iba.
etymology: Tambalang salita mula sa "bigay" (give) at "bahala" (charge, care, responsibility).
original_explanation: This is the official 'bahala ka na' document. You're legally telling someone, 'I trust you to handle my stuff.' It's like giving a trusted friend your ATM card and PIN because you're out of the country. It's a high-level trust fall, but with legal papers and potentially your life savings on the line.
usage_notes: Isang pormal at legal na termino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumirma siya ng isang kasulatan ng **bigay-bahala** para sa kanyang abogado.","translation":"He signed a **power of attorney** document for his lawyer."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng palaman na gawa sa giniling na mani, karaniwang ipinapahid sa tinapay.
original_explanation: The ultimate palaman for Pinoy pandesal, especially the local kind that's oily, a bit gritty, and super sweet. It's the star of many a baon and the secret ingredient in a good Kare-Kare for some families. Don't forget the eternal debate: 'chunky or creamy?'
usage_notes: A common loanword used in everyday conversation, especially regarding food.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong almusal ang pandesal na may **peanut butter**.","translation":"My favorite breakfast is pandesal with **peanut butter**."},{"sentence":"Gagamitin natin ang **peanut butter** para sa sarsa ng Kare-Kare.","translation":"We will use the **peanut butter** for the Kare-Kare sauce."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang itim at medyo magnetikong mineral na titanato ng bakal, (FeTiO3), na siyang pangunahing pinagkukunan ng elementong titan.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'ilmenita', na ipinangalan sa Bundok Ilmen sa Russia kung saan ito unang natuklasan.
original_explanation: This is some next-level nerd stuff. Ilmenite is a mineral, basically a fancy rock that's the main source of titanium. Think of it as the raw material for those lightweight but super strong things, like high-end bike frames or parts for spaceships. It's the 'unprocessed' version of something very cool. Definitely not your everyday palengke item.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa mga teknikal o siyentipikong konteksto, lalo na sa heolohiya, kemistri, at metalurhiya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakahanap ang mga heologo ng malaking deposito ng **ilmenayt** sa kabundukan ng Zambales.","translation":"The geologists found a large deposit of **ilmenite** in the mountains of Zambales."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang anyo ng sining-biswal na gumagamit ng gumagalaw na larawan at tunog upang magkuwento o maglahad ng isang paksa.
original_explanation: Your escape from reality for two hours, powered by popcorn and soda. It's where you find your new celebrity crush, cry over fictional characters, and get inspired to have a 'training montage' moment in your own life (which usually just lasts for 5 minutes). From MMFF entries to the latest Marvel blockbuster, `pelikula` is our modern-day campfire story.
usage_notes: Synonymous with 'sine' (from Spanish 'cine'), but 'pelikula' often refers to the film itself, while 'sine' can also mean the cinema/theater.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napanood mo na ba ang bagong **pelikula** ni Kathryn Bernardo?","translation":"Have you seen the new **movie** of Kathryn Bernardo?"},{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng sinematograpiya ng **pelikula**ng iyon.","translation":"The cinematography of that **film** was beautiful."}]

translation: to engage in a heated debate or argument
meaning_filipino: Ang masigla at kung minsan ay mainit na pagpapalitan ng mga kuro-kuro, opinyon, o argumento ng dalawa o higit pang tao.
original_explanation: This isn't just a simple chat. This is the comments section of a political post on Facebook come to life. It's you and your friends arguing whether pineapple belongs on pizza, or the Tito and Tita arguing about politics at the family reunion. It’s passionate, loud, and everyone has a strong opinion.
usage_notes: Implies a rapid, back-and-forth exchange, not necessarily negative but always energetic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula na namang **magbalitaktakan** ang mga senador tungkol sa bagong batas.","translation":"The senators have again started to **engage in a heated debate** about the new law."},{"sentence":"Mahilig **magbalitaktakan** ang magkakaibigan tungkol sa basketball.","translation":"The friends love to **have a spirited argument** about basketball."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang taong ang trabaho ay magtimpla o maghalo ng mga inumin, kemikal, o iba pang likido.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na 'templador' (temperer, one who mixes).
original_explanation: The official 'taga-timpla'. In a fancy bar, they're a 'mixologist'. At a fiesta, they're the tito in charge of the Emperador-and-powdered-juice concoction. A chemist in a lab can also be a 'timplador'. Anyone whose job is to mix things precisely.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa isang propesyonal tulad ng bartender o kemiko, o impormal na sa taong nakatalagang maghalo ng inumin sa isang party.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magaling na **timplador** ang bartender sa hotel na iyon.","translation":"The bartender at that hotel is a great **mixer**."},{"sentence":"Si Kuya Jojo ang laging **timplador** ng inumin sa aming mga salu-salo.","translation":"Kuya Jojo is always the designated **drink mixer** at our gatherings."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapalabas ng pagkain mula sa tiyan pabalik sa bibig na hindi puwersado, karaniwan sa mga sanggol.
original_explanation: This is the baby version of vomiting. It's less of a violent spew and more of a gentle, milky "oops, I drank too much." The kind of thing that happens on your new shirt right before you leave the house. "Dahan-dahan lang sa pagpapakain sa sanggol para hindi siya maglungad."
usage_notes: Specifically used for babies or sometimes animals spitting up. For forceful vomiting in adults, 'suka' is the correct term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Normal lang sa sanggol na **maglungad** pagkatapos dumede.","translation":"It's normal for a baby to **spit up** after feeding."},{"sentence":"Binuhat niya ang pamangkin nang maingat upang hindi ito **maglungad** sa damit niya.","translation":"She carried her nephew carefully so he wouldn't **spit up** on her clothes."}]
