meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasabi ng katotohanan, lalo na tungkol sa isang pagkakamali o isang lihim.
original_explanation: The moment of truth. This is what you do when your mom asks who ate the last piece of leche flan and you can't lie anymore. It's the climax of every teleserye confrontation scene. 'Umamin ka! May iba ka na bang mahal?!'
usage_notes: Can be used for serious confessions (crimes, secrets) or trivial admissions (eating someone's food).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **umamin** din ang bata na siya ang nakabasag ng plorera.","translation":"Finally, the child **admitted** that he was the one who broke the vase."},{"sentence":"Kailan ka ba **aamin** na may gusto ka sa kanya?","translation":"When will you **admit** that you have feelings for her?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hudyat o sigaw na ginagamit upang utusan ang isang tsuper, karaniwan ng pampublikong sasakyan tulad ng dyipni, na huminto.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'parar', na nangangahulugang 'huminto'.
original_explanation: The single most powerful word in Philippine public transportation. Yell this in a jeepney or tricycle and the world (well, the vehicle) stops for you. It's often accompanied by the sound of coins tapping on the metal roof. Pro tip: say it with conviction, but not so loud that you startle Manong Driver into hitting the brakes too hard.
usage_notes: Eksklusibong ginagamit sa konteksto ng pagsakay sa pampublikong transportasyon upang magpahiwatig ng pagbaba.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Para** po sa tabi!","translation":"**Stop** by the side, please!"},{"sentence":"Manong, **para** na po!","translation":"Driver, **stop** here, please!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang huling halaga o kabuuan matapos ibawas ang lahat ng kaltas, buwis, o iba pang mga bagay.
original_explanation: The final, 'take-home' amount of your sahod after taxes, SSS, Pag-ibig, Philhealth, and that utang from your officemate have been deducted. It's the 'reality check' number, the one that dictates if you can afford extra rice or not. "Ang gross salary mo, pang-mayaman. Ang net pay mo, pang-aray."
usage_notes: Commonly used in business, finance, and salary discussions. Often used to refer to net income or net pay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkano ba ang **net** na sahod mo pagkatapos ng lahat ng kaltas?","translation":"How much is your **net** salary after all the deductions?"},{"sentence":"Ang **net** weight ng produkto ay 250 grams.","translation":"The **net** weight of the product is 250 grams."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang aksyon o relasyon kung saan ang bawat isa sa dalawang panig ay nagbibigay at tumatanggap nang pantay o pareho; ganti sa ganti.
original_explanation: The official term for 'I scratch your back, you scratch mine.' It's that unspoken agreement when your friend treats you to coffee, so you know you're getting the bill next time. The opposite of a one-sided love affair.
usage_notes: Often used in formal, academic, or technical discussions about relationships, mathematics, or agreements.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **resiprokal** na pag-unawa sa anumang relasyon.","translation":"**Reciprocal** understanding is important in any relationship."},{"sentence":"Mayroon silang **resiprokal** na kasunduan tungkol sa kalakalan.","translation":"They have a **reciprocal** agreement regarding trade."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapalipad o pagpapatalsik ng isang bagay sa isang direksyon gamit ang lakas ng braso.
original_explanation: The move you make when you're angry and you see a pillow. Or when you're trying to get the basura into the bin from across the room, NBA-style. It’s a more forceful and less precise 'pukol' or 'bato'.
usage_notes: A very common root word used in various verb forms (ihagis, maghagis, hagisan). 'Hagis' as a noun refers to the act or the manner of throwing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malakas na **hagis** ng bola ang nagpanalo sa kanila.","translation":"A strong **throw** of the ball won them the game."},{"sentence":"Ang **hagis** niya ng susi ay hindi ko nasalo.","translation":"I failed to catch the keys from his **toss**."}]

translation: to peddle, to vend, to hawk
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbebenta ng mga kalakal sa pamamagitan ng pag-iikot o paglalakad sa mga pampublikong lugar.
original_explanation: This is the hustle of the street vendor. Think of the taho vendor shouting "Tahooooo!", the guy selling ice cream from a cart, or someone walking through a bus selling mani (peanuts) and bottled water. They are all "naglalako". It's grassroots entrepreneurship on the move.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to selling goods while moving around, as opposed to selling from a fixed stall (`magtinda`).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaga siyang gumigising para **maglako** ng isda sa palengke.","translation":"She wakes up early **to peddle** fish at the market."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula siyang yumaman sa pamamagitan ng paglako.","translation":"He started to get rich by peddling."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malalim na damdamin ng kalungkutan o pighati.
original_explanation: This is the 'sana all' feeling when you see happy couples, but in a poetic, black-and-white-filter kind of way. It's the official mood of a rainy Sunday afternoon listening to sad OPM songs. Hindi lang siya basta lungkot, may kasamang pagmumuni-muni at pagka-miss sa isang bagay na wala na. Hugot level: expert.
usage_notes: Ang 'lumbay' ay mas matalinghaga at malalim kaysa sa karaniwang 'lungkot'. Madalas itong gamitin sa panitikan at mga awitin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga mata ay puno ng **lumbay** matapos mawalay sa kanyang minamahal.","translation":"Her eyes were full of **sorrow** after being separated from her beloved."}]

meaning_filipino: Manumbalik sa isipan o magawang alalahanin ang isang bagay, tao, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: That "aha!" moment when you finally remember where you left your keys. Or that "oh no" moment when you remember your ex's birthday. It's your brain's search function. Sometimes it works instantly, other times it lags worse than PLDT, and sometimes it just returns "404 Not Found."
usage_notes: Interchangeable with 'maalala' in many contexts. 'Matandaan' focuses on the ability to keep something in memory or recall it.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko **matandaan** kung saan ko inilagay ang aking salamin.","translation":"I can't **remember** where I put my glasses."},{"sentence":"Sana'y **matandaan** mo ako kahit sa paglipas ng panahon.","translation":"I hope you **remember** me even as time passes."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang kilos ng pag-unawa sa mga nakasulat na salita o simbolo; ang proseso ng pagkuha ng impormasyon mula sa teksto.
original_explanation: What you're doing right now. Or what you tell your boss you're doing ("nagbabasa po ng emails") when you're actually scrolling through memes. It's the progressive tense of the verb.
usage_notes: Refers to the act of reading. Not to be confused with its homograph 'nagbabasa' (/nag-ba-ba-SA/), which means 'making something wet'. Pronunciation is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **nagbabasa** ng mga libro tuwing gabi.","translation":"He likes **reading** books every night."},{"sentence":"Ano ang **binabasa** mo diyan sa cellphone mo?","translation":"What are you **reading** there on your phone?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ugali ng pag-aaksaya o hindi pagpapahalaga sa mga bagay, na nagreresulta sa labis na pagtapon.
original_explanation: This is the 'add to cart' champion who never uses half the stuff they buy. It's ordering more food than you can eat at a buffet. It's the 'one-time use' mentality for things that are perfectly reusable. Your lola would definitely scold you for this, saying 'sayang ang pera!'
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa katangian ng pagiging maaksaya, hindi lamang sa akto ng pagtatapon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkamapagtapon** ng pagkain ay isang malaking isyu sa ating lipunan.","translation":"The **wastefulness** of food is a big issue in our society."}]

meaning_filipino: May hugis na bilog o isinagawa sa paraang paikot.
etymology: From `pa-` prefix indicating shape or manner + `bilog` (circle, round).
original_explanation: The shape of your ube cheese pandesal, or the instruction your Zumba teacher shouts: 'Gawin nating pabilog ang formation!' It describes anything round or done in a circle, like how your argument with your jowa goes - paikot-ikot lang, pabilog.
usage_notes: Can describe a shape (adjective) or a manner of doing something (adverb).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gupitin mo ang kartolina nang **pabilog**.","translation":"Cut the cardboard in a **circular** shape."},{"sentence":"Umupo sila nang **pabilog** sa sahig.","translation":"They sat on the floor **in a circular manner**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking likhang sining na direktang ipininta o inilapat sa isang pader, kisame, o iba pang permanenteng ibabaw.
original_explanation: 'Yung dambuhalang painting sa pader na ginagawang background for the 'gram. Madalas may social commentary 'yan, o kaya naman, pang-beautify lang talaga ng isang lugar. Parang malaking version ng drawing mo sa likod ng notebook.
usage_notes: A direct loanword, used in the context of art and public spaces.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng bagong **miyural** sa pader ng city hall.","translation":"The new **mural** on the city hall wall is beautiful."},{"sentence":"Nag-volunteer siyang magpinta ng **miyural** para sa eskwelahan.","translation":"He volunteered to paint a **mural** for the school."}]

meaning_filipino: Isagawa o ipatupad ang isang batas, kautusan, o plano.
original_explanation: This is the 'make it happen' verb. When the government announces a new rule, this is the action that follows. It's the difference between a memo just sitting in your inbox and actually having to follow the new 'clean desk policy.' 'Pinapatupad na ang Bawal Umihi Dito.' Time to get serious.
usage_notes: A causative verb meaning 'to cause something to be fulfilled or implemented.' Often used in the context of laws, rules, promises, and plans. Synonymous with 'ipatupad'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **patupdin** ang mga bagong alituntunin sa komunidad.","translation":"The new community rules need to be **enforced**."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **patupdin** ang isang pangako kung ikaw lang ang gumagawa ng paraan.","translation":"It's hard to **implement** a promise if you're the only one making an effort."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marahang pag-usad o paggalaw sa isang tabi upang magbigay ng espasyo.
original_explanation: The official request in a crowded jeepney or on a church pew. It's the polite way of saying "Your personal space is invading my personal space." The opposite of 'social distancing' before we even knew what that was. "Isod, isod, para makaupo lahat!"
usage_notes: Very common in situations involving shared seating.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umisod** ka nang kaunti para makaupo ako.","translation":"**Move over** a little so I can sit."},{"sentence":"Dahan-dahang **umisod** ang pila sa sinehan.","translation":"The line at the cinema slowly **moved forward**."}]

meaning_filipino: Daglat ng salitang Ingles na 'please', na ginagamit sa pakiusap.
original_explanation: The official text-speak of Pinoys who are too lazy to type 'please' but still want to sound polite... or passive-aggressive. "Pakisend 'yung report, pls." It's the digital equivalent of a half-hearted 'paki-abot'.
usage_notes: Exclusively used in informal digital communication like text messages and social media posts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakibili ako ng pagkain pag-uwi mo, **pls**.","translation":"Please buy me food on your way home, **pls**."},{"sentence":"**Pls** paki-approve ng leave ko. Thanks.","translation":"**Pls** approve my leave. Thanks."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglapit o pag-atake nang sabay-sabay at maramihan sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: What fans do to their K-Pop idol at the airport. Or what you and your barkada do to the last piece of lechon at a fiesta. It's an "attack," but usually fueled by love (or extreme hunger).
usage_notes: Can be used in both literal (a physical swarm) and figurative (e.g., swarmed with questions) senses.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag ninyong **dumugin** ang buffet table, lahat naman tayo makakakain.","translation":"Don't **swarm** the buffet table, all of us will get to eat."},{"sentence":"Matapos ang laro, **dinumog** ng mga reporter ang nanalong manlalaro.","translation":"After the game, the winning player was **mobbed** by reporters."}]

translation: to pair up; to make a tandem
meaning_filipino: Pagsamahin ang dalawang tao o bagay bilang magkapareha.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate showbiz word. It's what producers do when they create a 'love team' like KathNiel or DonBelle. 'Sino kaya ang susunod na itatambal kay new actor?' It can also apply to food pairings, like 'itambal ang kape sa pandesal.'
usage_notes: Very common in the context of Philippine entertainment ('love teams') but can be used more broadly for any pairing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang direktor na **itambal** ang dalawang sikat na artista sa isang bagong pelikula.","translation":"The director decided to **pair up** the two famous actors in a new movie."},{"sentence":"Masarap **itambal** ang mainit na tsokolate sa ensaymada.","translation":"It's delicious to **pair** hot chocolate with ensaymada."}]

translation: setting a trap; cocking (a gun); aiming
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghahanda ng isang bitag o patibong; ang paglalagay sa posisyon ng isang bagay upang maging handa, tulad ng pag-kasa ng baril o pag-asinta.
original_explanation: This is the 'abangers' move. Yung tipong inihahanda mo na yung 'seen zone' para sa ka-chat mo, or when you're setting up the perfect 'gotcha!' moment for your prank. It's the act of preparing for the kill, whether it's a real trap, a witty comeback, or just setting up your friend for a funny fail video.
usage_notes: Can refer to literal traps for animals, figurative traps in social situations, or preparing a weapon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pag-uumang** ng bitag para sa daga ay kailangang gawin nang maingat.","translation":"The **setting** of the trap for the rat needs to be done carefully."},{"sentence":"Kitang-kita sa kanyang mga mata ang **pag-uumang** ng galit.","translation":"You could clearly see the **brewing** of anger in his eyes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang nilalang mula sa mitolohiyang Pilipino na pinaniniwalaang may kapangyarihang higit sa karaniwan at naninirahan sa mga punongkahoy, ilog, o iba pang likas na lugar.
original_explanation: Your friendly neighborhood supernatural entity. Think dwarves (nuno sa punso), fairies, or other elementals that lola warns you not to mess with. They're the reason you say "tabi-tabi po" when passing by a big old tree. They're the original land-owners, so show some respect or you might get "nainkanto" (bewitched).
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with "engkanto" or "engkantada" (for females).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naniniwala ang matatanda na may mga **inkanto** na nakatira sa malaking puno ng balete.","translation":"The elders believe that there are **supernatural beings** living in the large balete tree."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-iingay sa gubat, baka makagambala ka ng **inkanto**.","translation":"Don't be noisy in the forest, you might disturb an **elemental**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagbuo ng isang opinyon o teorya batay sa hindi kumpletong impormasyon; pag-aakala o paghihinuha.
etymology: From 'haka' (guess, assumption). The 'pag-ha-' prefix indicates a continuous or habitual action.
original_explanation: This is your brain on 'chismis'. It's what you do when you see your ex's IG story with someone new and you start connecting imaginary dots. It's the act of creating a whole teleserye plot in your head with zero evidence. 'Haka-haka mo lang 'yan!' is the national anthem against fake news.
usage_notes: Often used with 'lang' (haka-haka lang) to downplay the seriousness of the speculation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itigil mo na ang **paghahaka** at tanungin mo na lang siya nang direkta.","translation":"Stop the **speculation** and just ask him directly."},{"sentence":"Puro **paghahaka** ang naririnig ko, wala namang katotohanan.","translation":"I'm hearing nothing but **conjecture**, there's no truth to it."}]

translation: Wanderer, a person who loves to go out
meaning_filipino: Isang tao na mahilig maglakbay, lumabas ng bahay, o pumunta sa iba't ibang lugar nang walang tiyak na patutunguhan.
original_explanation: The 'Saan ang gala?' friend. Their feet are always itchy to go somewhere. Long weekend? They're already in La Union. Sweldo day? They're at a new cafe. They can't stay home for more than 24 hours without getting an existential crisis. Also known as 'layas' by their parents.
usage_notes: Maaaring maging neutral (isang manlalakbay) o bahagyang negatibo (isang palaboy, laging wala sa bahay). Ang konteksto ang susi.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa kanilang lugar bilang isang **taong gala** dahil palagi siyang wala sa bahay.","translation":"He's known in their area as a **person who loves to go out** because he's never at home."},{"sentence":"Bilang isang **taong gala**, natutunan kong mag-impake ng mabilis para sa mga biglaang biyahe.","translation":"As a **wanderer**, I learned to pack quickly for spontaneous trips."}]

translation: to be able to melt; to be able to digest
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang maging likido mula sa pagiging solido dahil sa init; o ang kakayahan ng tiyan na durugin ang pagkain.
original_explanation: Has two main uses. First, the literal: what the sun does to your ice cream. Second, the digestive: what your stomach is supposed to do after you eat at an unli-samgyup buffet. Also used figuratively for melting hearts: "Yung ngiti niya, nakakatunaw!" (His/Her smile is heart-melting!).
usage_notes: Context (food, heat, romance) determines the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mo ng matinding apoy para **makatunaw** ng bakal.","translation":"You need intense fire to **be able to melt** steel."},{"sentence":"Kumain ako ng papaya para mas madali akong **makatunaw** ng kinain ko.","translation":"I ate papaya so I could **digest** my food more easily."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang buhok sa ulo o sa isang bahagi ng katawan na karaniwang tinutubuan nito.
original_explanation: The look you get when you've stressed out too much about adulting. Or, you know, just a haircut choice. Think Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson or your tito who's very proud of his shiny head. Can also refer to a worn-out tire ('kalbo na ang gulong').
usage_notes: Can be used for people, animals, or even inanimate objects that are supposed to have a covering but don't, like a tire with no tread.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang maging **kalbo** ang kanyang ama sa edad na trenta.","translation":"His father started to go **bald** at the age of thirty."},{"sentence":"**Kalbo** na ang gulong ng bisikleta kaya kailangan nang palitan.","translation":"The bicycle tire is **bald** (worn out) so it needs to be replaced."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdausdos o mabilis na pagbaba sa isang makinis na ibabaw.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung ginagawa mo sa playground nung bata ka, or 'yung nangyayari sa'yo kapag basa ang sahig at naka-medyas ka. Pwede ring 'yung pag-dalusdos ng luha mo habang nanonood ng K-drama. Smooth but sometimes painful.
usage_notes: The verb form 'dumalusdos' (to slide) is more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasiyahan ang mga bata sa paglalaro sa **dalusdos**.","translation":"The children enjoyed playing on the **slide**."},{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **dalusdos** ng mga bato mula sa bundok.","translation":"I heard the **sliding** of rocks from the mountain."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging labis na madaldal o pagsasalita nang walang tigil, kadalasan tungkol sa mga bagay na hindi dapat ipagsabi.
original_explanation: This is the Tita who knows all the chismis in the family reunion, the officemate who gives a play-by-play of their weekend on Monday morning, and you after two cups of coffee. It's having a mouth that's faster than your brain's 'is this confidential?' filter. The OG source of 'sabi-sabi.'
usage_notes: Often has a slightly negative connotation, implying that the person talks too much or shares secrets.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nalagay siya sa alanganin dahil sa kanyang **pagkamatabil**.","translation":"He got into trouble because of his **talkativeness**."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa opisina sa kanyang **pagkamatabil** at pagiging masayahin.","translation":"She is known in the office for her **garrulousness** and cheerfulness."}]

translation: having main character energy; acting like the protagonist
meaning_filipino: Isang pariralang balbal na naglalarawan sa isang tao na kumikilos na para bang siya ang bida sa isang pelikula o kuwento, kadalasan ay may kasamang pagiging dramatiko, may tiwala sa sarili, o pakiramdam na ang mundo ay umiikot sa kanya.
etymology: Combination of the slang "giving" and the English phrase "main character," popularized by TikTok and internet culture to describe a specific type of self-centered or self-romanticizing behavior.
original_explanation: This is for that person who romanticizes their commute, thinks their minor inconvenience is a major plot point, and posts everything with a dramatic caption. They're not just living life; they're curating their own movie. Sometimes it's empowering (you go, girl!), other times it's just plain narcissistic. It's when your officemate treats a missed deadline like a season finale cliffhanger.
usage_notes: Used to describe someone who acts as if they are the central figure in every situation. Can be used admiringly, humorously, or critically.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-walk out siya sa meeting dahil lang di nagustuhan yung idea niya? Sobrang **giving main character**.","translation":"She walked out of the meeting just because her idea wasn't liked? That's so **main character energy**."},{"sentence":"Treat yourself today. Go on a solo date, buy that coffee. Be **giving main character** for a day.","translation":"Treat yourself today. Go on a solo date, buy that coffee. Be **the main character** for a day."}]

meaning_filipino: Maging sanhi ng pagkalanta o pagkatuyo ng isang halaman o bulaklak.
original_explanation: This is what extreme heat does to the plants on your balcony. Figuratively, it's what a harsh, soul-crushing comment can do to someone's spirit or enthusiasm. It just makes them wilt.
usage_notes: A causative verb, primarily used for plants, but can be used metaphorically for emotions, spirit, or beauty.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sobrang init ng araw ay **makalanta** ng mga bulaklak.","translation":"The intense heat of the sun can **cause the flowers to wither**."},{"sentence":"Ang masasakit na salita ay **makalanta** ng puso.","translation":"Harsh words can **cause a heart to wither**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpapakita, pagmamalaki, o pagpapahayag ng isang bagay, ideya, o tagumpay nang hayagan at buong pagmamalaki.
etymology: Mula sa salitang `bandila` (flag), na hango sa salitang Espanyol na `bandera`.
original_explanation: This is the art of the "humble brag" turned up to 11. It's posting your new iPhone, your Starbucks cup with your name misspelled, your travel pics with the caption #blessed. It's making sure everyone knows about your achievements, your new jowa, or your political stance. It's the social media equivalent of waving a giant flag that says "LOOK AT ME!"
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagbabandila** ng kanyang kayamanan ay kinaiinisan ng marami.","translation":"His **flaunting** of his wealth is disliked by many."},{"sentence":"Ipinagpatuloy niya ang **pagbabandila** sa karapatan ng mga kababaihan.","translation":"She continued **proclaiming** the rights of women."}]

translation: to be piled up; to accumulate
meaning_filipino: Maipon o magkapatong-patong hanggang sa maging isang malaking bunton o tambak, kadalasan nang hindi ginugusto.
etymology: ma- (unintentional state prefix) + pa- (causative prefix) + tambak (pile, heap)
original_explanation: This is your laundry chair. Or your desk at work before a long weekend. Or the unread messages in your work chat group. It’s when things pile up, usually because of procrastination or being overwhelmed. "Huwag mong hayaang mapatambak ang mga labahin." It’s the physical manifestation of "I'll do it later."
usage_notes: Often used to describe chores, work, or debt that has accumulated.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Napatambak** ang mga basura sa kalsada dahil hindi dumating ang trak.","translation":"The garbage **was piled up** on the street because the truck didn't arrive."},{"sentence":"Kung hindi mo uumpisahan ngayon, **mapapatambak** lang ang trabaho mo.","translation":"If you don't start now, your work will just **accumulate**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga bagay, tao, o ideya na kasunod sa isang listahan, pagkakasunod-sunod, o daloy ng usapan.
original_explanation: The most corporate-sounding Filipino word ever. "Pakibasa ang mga sumusunod na anunsyo." "Ang mga sumusunod ay ang mga nanalo sa raffle." Basically, it's the formal way of saying "eto na yung next..."
usage_notes: Often used to introduce a list or a series of items. It's a pseudo-verb acting as an adjective.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **sumusunod** ay ang mga sangkap para sa sinigang.","translation":"**The following** are the ingredients for sinigang."},{"sentence":"Pag-aralan natin ang **sumusunod** na talata.","translation":"Let's study **the following** paragraph."}]

meaning_filipino: Tubig na nasa solido at nagyeyelong estado dahil sa matinding lamig.
original_explanation: The official sponsor of summer in the Philippines. It's what makes your halo-halo a halo-halo and not just a weird fruit salad. Also the reason why sari-sari stores can charge P5 for a small plastic bag of it when you're desperate. The sound of an ice cream vendor's bell is basically the sound of solid, flavored yelo coming to save you from the heat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pabili po ng **yelo**, 'yung tig-lima.","translation":"Can I buy some **ice**, the five-peso one."},{"sentence":"Lagyan mo ng maraming **yelo** ang juice para malamig.","translation":"Put a lot of **ice** in the juice so it's cold."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na bagay na walang gaanong halaga o tiyak na gamit; mga abubot.
original_explanation: This refers to those little trinkets, gadgets, and miscellaneous small items cluttering up your tito's garage or your lola's aparador. It’s the hardware store's worth of screws, wires, and unidentifiable parts you keep 'just in case'. 'Ano ba 'yang mga butingting mo?' (What are all these knick-knacks of yours?)
usage_notes: Often used in plural form to refer to a collection of small, often unimportant, items.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng mga **butingting** ang kanyang lumang kahon.","translation":"His old box is full of **knick-knacks**."}]

meaning_filipino: Mayroong maraming gasgas o galos sa ibabaw dahil sa pagkakiskis o madalas na paggamit.
original_explanation: 'Yung itsura ng bumper ng kotse mo after mo i-park sa mall, or 'yung luma mong sapatos na pan-commute. It's seen better days, puno ng battle scars from the daily grind. Hindi na siya 'mint condition'.
usage_notes: Often refers to surfaces that have been scuffed or scratched up through use or friction. Can also be used metaphorically for a voice that is hoarse.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magasgas** na ang screen ng luma kong cellphone.","translation":"The screen of my old cellphone is already **scratched up**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong gamitin ang platong iyan, **magasgas** na ang ibabaw.","translation":"Don't use that plate, its surface is already **scuffed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ibigay o ikalat sa maraming tao o sa iba't ibang pangkat.
etymology: From Tagalog 'i-' (causative/instrumental prefix) + 'pamahagi' (act of distributing), which comes from 'bahagi' (part, share).
original_explanation: This is the official verb for 'ayuda' during a crisis, or for the free samples at the supermarket. It's about spreading the love (or the goods). When your friend brings back a giant box of pasalubong, the command is: 'Ipamahagi mo na 'yan!' (Distribute that now!). It feels more formal and large-scale than just 'ibigay'.
usage_notes: Often used in formal contexts like announcements, news reports, or charity work. Implies distribution to a group rather than giving to a single person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga relief goods ay handa nang **ipamahagi** sa mga nasalanta ng bagyo.","translation":"The relief goods are ready **to be distributed** to the typhoon victims."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **ipamahagi** ang mga gawain upang mas mabilis matapos.","translation":"We need **to distribute** the tasks so we can finish faster."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaki na malapit nang ikasal o nasa araw mismo ng kanyang kasal.
original_explanation: The guy who's about to end his 'single' subscription and sign up for a 'joint account' for life. He's probably sweating in his barong, thinking about the wedding bills, and practicing his "I do." The star of the bachelor party, and the co-star of the wedding day.
usage_notes: The direct equivalent of 'groom'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakagwapo ng **lalaking ikakasal** sa kanyang suot na Barong Tagalog.","translation":"The **groom** is very handsome in his Barong Tagalog."},{"sentence":"Naghihintay na sa altar ang **lalaking ikakasal**.","translation":"The **groom-to-be** is already waiting at the altar."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng hindi pagbibigay ng atensyon o pagwawalang-bahala sa isang tao, bagay, o pangyayari.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng "di-" (hindi) at "pagpansin" (ang akto ng pagbibigay-atensyon).
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "seen zone" move. When you slide into their DMs and they leave you on 'read'? That's di-pagpansin. It's the art of making someone feel like they're invisible, like a ghost in their own chat thread. The classic "dedma" lang.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang isang sinasadyang kilos ng pagwawalang-bahala sa isang tao o bagay. Ang katumbas nito sa usapang kolokyal ay "dedma".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **di-pagpansin** sa aking mga mensahe ay malinaw na senyales.","translation":"Her **disregard** for my messages is a clear sign."},{"sentence":"Ikinasama ng loob niya ang **di-pagpansin** ng kanyang mga kaibigan.","translation":"He was hurt by his friends' **neglect**."}]

translation: to cause to be stunned; to bewilder
meaning_filipino: Ang magdulot ng pagkatuliro, pagkabigla, o pagtigil dahil sa pagtataka o gulat.
etymology: From `mag-` (verb prefix) + `pa-` (causative prefix) + `lumagak` (to be stunned, to be still).
original_explanation: This is a deep cut, a very rare word. Imagine seeing your crush suddenly confess their feelings for you online, and you just stare at the screen, unable to type. That feeling of being frozen in shock or confusion is what magpalumagak causes. It's that 'buffering...' moment in your brain when reality hits you unexpectedly.
usage_notes: Very formal and literary. You're more likely to encounter this in old poems or novels than in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang biglaang pag-amin ay **nagpalumagak** sa lahat.","translation":"His sudden confession **stunned** everyone."},{"sentence":"Ang kagandahan ng tanawin ay sapat na upang **magpalumagak** sa sinumang makakita.","translation":"The beauty of the scenery is enough to **bewilder** anyone who sees it."}]

meaning_filipino: Putulin o tanggalin ang isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng biglaang paghila o puwersa.
original_explanation: This is the action of doing the snapping. 'Pigtasin mo na 'yang tag sa damit mo.' (Tear off that tag on your shirt.) Or more dramatically, it's what you want to do to the connection with your toxic ex. Pigtasin the cord, girl! Cut them off!
usage_notes: This is the command or infinitive form of the verb. The root word is 'pigtal'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pigtasin** ang pahina ng libro.","translation":"Don't **tear off** the page of the book."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **pigtasin** ang lubid ngunit napakatibay nito.","translation":"He tried **to snap off** the rope but it was too strong."}]

translation: A crush you admire from afar with no intention of pursuing a relationship.
meaning_filipino: Isang taong hinahangaan mo nang palihim o mula sa malayo na nagdudulot sa iyo ng kasiyahan, ngunit wala kang intensyong ligawan o magkaroon ng romantikong relasyon.
etymology: English loan phrase, widely adopted in Philippine slang.
original_explanation: This is your low-maintenance, zero-drama, purely-for-kilig-and-inspiration crush. Usually a celebrity, a senior from school, or that cute barista. You're happy just seeing them exist. Walang pressure, walang expectations, walang 'sana kami na lang'. Pure, unadulterated, low-risk admiration.
usage_notes: A very common term among Filipino youth and on social media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Daniel Padilla ang **happy crush** ng bayan.","translation":"Daniel Padilla is the nation's **happy crush**."},{"sentence":"Okay lang na 'di niya ako pansinin, **happy crush** ko lang naman siya.","translation":"It's okay if he doesn't notice me, he's just my **happy crush**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng labis na puwersa na nakakasakit o nakakasira; malupit at walang awa.
original_explanation: This is the energy you get when your internet dies during a Netflix finale. It's the opposite of 'marahan'. A 'marahas na action scene', a 'marahas na salita' from a toxic boss, or a 'marahas na pag-agaw sa huling piraso ng lechon'. It's intense, aggressive, and usually not in a good way.
usage_notes: Always has a negative connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi solusyon ang **marahas** na pamamaraan sa anumang problema.","translation":"A **violent** approach is not a solution to any problem."},{"sentence":"Umiwas sa mga taong may **marahas** na pag-uugali.","translation":"Avoid people with a **harsh** demeanor."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang estado o relasyon ng pagiging magkapatid.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "pagka-" (estado ng pagiging) at "magkapatid" (mga taong may iisang magulang).
original_explanation: The bond that lets you fight over the last piece of chicken but also makes you willing to fight anyone who messes with your sibling. It's a mix of "pahiram ako ng damit mo" (which means "I'm taking your clothes") and "ako bahala sa'yo."
usage_notes: Katulad ng 'pagkamagkaibigan', ang 'pagkamagkapatid' ay mas pormal kaysa sa mas karaniwang 'pagkakapatiran'. Nakatuon ito sa estado ng pagiging magkapatid.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinahahalagahan nila ang kanilang **pagkamagkapatid** higit sa anumang materyal na bagay.","translation":"They value their **siblinghood** more than any material thing."}]

translation: to be nauseated or dizzy from a strong smell
meaning_filipino: Mahilo o maduwal dahil sa matapang na amoy, tulad ng kemikal, pabango, o nabubulok na bagay.
original_explanation: Ever walked past a pile of garbage on a hot day and felt your soul try to leave your body? That's lumango. It's the feeling you get when someone bathes in their perfume inside a crowded elevator. Your nose gets KO'd and your brain feels like it's doing somersaults.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to dizziness or nausea caused by olfactory overload, not from motion sickness or intoxication from drinking (though "lango" can also mean drunk).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halos **lumango** ako sa tindi ng amoy ng durian.","translation":"I almost **got nauseated** from the strong smell of durian."},{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **lumango** ang mga trabahador dahil sa singaw ng kemikal.","translation":"The workers began **to get dizzy** from the chemical fumes."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang masigasig na paghabol sa isang tao, hayop, o bagay na nais hulihin o abutan. Ito ay tumutukoy sa kilos na naganap na.
original_explanation: This is more intense than just 'habol'. This is what cops do to robbers in action movies. It's what you do to the last bus at night. It's what your landlady does to you when the rent is three months late. It implies a determined, focused chase. Not just a jog, but a full-on sprint with a goal.
usage_notes: Implies a more intense and purposeful chase than 'humabol'. Completed aspect (past tense).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumugis** ang mga pulis sa mga magnanakaw.","translation":"The police **pursued** the thieves."},{"sentence":"Ang pusa ay **tumugis** sa daga hanggang sa makorner ito.","translation":"The cat **chased** the mouse until it was cornered."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pag-aalis ng balat sa dulo ng ari ng lalaki (foreskin), na isang kaugalian o ritwal sa maraming kultura at relihiyon.
original_explanation: The ultimate summer rite of passage for every Pinoy boy. Yung panahon na bigla kang maglalakad na parang penguin at may suot na maluwag na shorts o palda. Proof of manhood daw, pero actually, it's a minor surgical procedure na ginawang neighborhood event, kumpleto with a 'pukpok' master o libreng 'Operation Tuli' sa barangay health center.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa akto ng pagsasagawa ng pagtutuli.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala ni Mang Jose ang kanyang anak sa klinika upang **tuliin**.","translation":"Mang Jose brought his son to the clinic **to be circumcised**."},{"sentence":"Sino ang magtu**tuli** sa mga bata sa medical mission?","translation":"Who will **circumcise** the children at the medical mission?"}]

translation: to have a jumping contest; to jump over something together
meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng sabay-sabay o paligsahang pagtalon sa ibabaw ng isang bagay.
etymology: From 'lukso' (jump) + '-han' (suffix indicating a reciprocal or group action).
original_explanation: This is the verb for a group jumping activity. Think of it as a friendly competition, like who can jump over the most number of stacked slippers, or the group action in 'luksung-tinik'. The '-han' suffix implies a reciprocal action or a shared event, turning a solo jump into a party.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of games or challenges involving multiple participants.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tara, **luksuhan** natin kung sino ang mas mataas tumalon.","translation":"Come on, let's **have a jumping contest** to see who can jump higher."},{"sentence":"Huwag ninyong **luksuhan** ang mga halaman sa hardin.","translation":"Don't you all **jump over** the plants in the garden."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang taong namamahala at nagbibigay ng gabay sa isang proyekto, organisasyon, o produksiyon tulad ng pelikula o dula.
original_explanation: Yung taga-sigaw ng "CUT!" sa shooting. Sila 'yung may 'vision'—'yung nakikita na nila ang itsura ng pelikula habang lahat kayo nagkakagulo pa. Sa opisina, sila 'yung boss na laging may "urgent" meeting at kailangan ng "deck" ASAP.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bagong pelikula ng sikat na **direktor** ay umani ng maraming parangal.","translation":"The new film by the famous **director** reaped many awards."},{"sentence":"Kinausap ng **direktor** ng kumpanya ang lahat ng empleyado.","translation":"The company **director** spoke to all the employees."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maikling patalim na may dalawang talim at matulis na dulo, karaniwang ginagamit bilang sandata.
original_explanation: That short, pointy weapon you see in historical dramas or fantasy movies like Encantadia. It's not a knife for the kitchen; it's a knife for dramatic betrayals and epic fight scenes. Think of it as the more intense cousin of the kutsilyo.
usage_notes: Often found in literature, historical texts, and fantasy genres.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ng bayani ang kanyang **balaraw** upang ipagtanggol ang sarili.","translation":"The hero used his **dagger** to defend himself."},{"sentence":"Isang antigong **balaraw** na may palamuting ginto ang natagpuan sa baul.","translation":"An antique **dagger** with gold ornaments was found in the chest."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sigaw o pakiusap para sa tulong sa oras ng panganib o kagipitan. Tumutukoy din ito sa mismong tulong o pag-aalalay na ibinibigay.
original_explanation: The OG 'Help me!' before 911 was a thing on speed dial. It's what you scream when a dog is chasing you, when you're stuck in an elevator, or when your sibling is about to tell your mom you broke her favorite vase. It's a dramatic, high-stakes cry for immediate backup.
usage_notes: Often used as an exclamation: 'Saklolo!'. Can also be used as a noun to mean 'aid' or 'succor'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Saklolo**! May sunog!","translation":"**Help**! There's a fire!"},{"sentence":"Humingi siya ng **saklolo** sa mga kapitbahay.","translation":"He asked for **help** from the neighbors."},{"sentence":"Salamat sa iyong mabilis na pag**saklolo**.","translation":"Thank you for your quick **aid**."}]

translation: to report; to give an account
meaning_filipino: Magbigay ng pormal na salaysay o impormasyon tungkol sa isang kaganapan, gawain, o paksa.
original_explanation: What your boss asks you to do at the end of the day. What a news anchor does on TV. What you do to your best friend about your date last night ('chismis' is just an informal report, right?). It's giving the deets, formally or informally.
usage_notes: Can be used in formal contexts (news, school, work) or informal ones (gossip, storytelling).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **mag-ulat** ng reporter sa pinangyarihan ng aksidente.","translation":"The reporter needs **to report** from the scene of the accident."},{"sentence":"**Mag-ulat** ka sa akin kung ano ang napag-usapan ninyo.","translation":"**Give me an account** of what you talked about."}]

translation: to apply ink to; to ink something
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o paglalapat ng tinta sa isang bagay, tulad ng papel o selyo. Ito ay isang utos o kilos.
original_explanation: The action of putting ink on something. Like when you're using a rubber stamp and you press it onto an ink pad – you 'tintahan' the stamp. Or, in a more dramatic sense, when a contract is finally signed and 'inked'.
usage_notes: A command or a verb describing the action of inking a surface. Focus is on the location or surface where ink is applied.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tintahan** mo muna ang selyo bago itatak sa papel.","translation":"**Ink** the stamp first before pressing it on the paper."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **tintahan** ang mesa.","translation":"Don't get **ink** on the table."}]

translation: the act of transporting or hauling things in large quantities
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglilipat ng mga bagay, karaniwang maramihan, mula sa isang lugar patungo sa iba.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you're moving houses (lipat-bahay) and you try to carry 10 grocery bags at once to save trips. It’s also what happens during elections when people are 'transported' to polling places, or when a movie 'hauls' in all the awards. 'Grabe ang paghakot ng awards ng Parasite!'
usage_notes: Implies moving a large volume of items, often back and forth.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumulong ako sa **paghakot** ng mga donasyon para sa mga nasalanta ng bagyo.","translation":"I helped in **hauling** the donations for the typhoon victims."},{"sentence":"Buong araw silang abala sa **paghakot** ng mga gamit palabas ng lumang bahay.","translation":"They were busy the whole day **transporting** things out of the old house."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang punto o bahagi na may pantay na layo mula sa mga dulo o hangganan ng isang bagay; sentro.
original_explanation: That awkward phase in a project where you're past the exciting start but the deadline is still far away. Also, 'petsa de peligro' - the middle of the month, right between paydays. The 'gitna' of it all.
usage_notes: Can refer to the middle of a place, time, or event.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa **kalagitnaan** kami ng aming pagsusulit nang biglang bumagyo.","translation":"We were in the **middle** of our exam when a storm suddenly hit."},{"sentence":"Ang monumento ay nasa **kalagitnaan** ng plasa.","translation":"The monument is in the **center** of the plaza."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na nagkukunwaring marami o malalim ang kaalaman sa isang paksa kahit hindi naman totoo.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `mapag-` at `dunong-dunungan` (pagkukunwaring marunong), na pag-uulit ng salitang ugat na `dunong` (kaalaman, talino).
original_explanation: The "Actually..." guy in every conversation. You say the sky is blue, and they'll say, "Actually, it's the scattering of light through the atmosphere..." Sila yung laging may 'fun fact' na hindi naman fun, at expert sa lahat ng topic from cryptocurrency to the best way to cook adobo, kahit galing lang sa Google ang alam nila. The human equivalent of a Wikipedia article no one asked for.
usage_notes: Nagtataglay ng negatibong konotasyon ng pagiging mayabang o nakakainis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakainis kausap ang mga taong **mapagdunung-dunungan**.","translation":"It's annoying to talk to people who are **know-it-alls**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mapagdunung-dunungan**; aminin mo kung hindi mo alam.","translation":"Don't be **pretentious about your knowledge**; admit it if you don't know."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gagawing paghahanap sa hinaharap; ang kilos ng pagsisiyasat o paggagalugad upang matagpuan ang isang bagay, tao, o impormasyon.
original_explanation: The future tense of looking for something. This is you, every single day, looking for your keys, your wallet, or your will to go to work. 'Saan ka maghahanap ng jowa?' is the perennial question from your titas during family reunions. It's also the state of every fresh grad: 'maghahanap ng trabaho.'
usage_notes: This is the future tense form of the verb maghanap. The root hanap is reduplicated (ha-hanap).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Maghahanap** ako ng bagong apartment na mas malapit sa opisina.","translation":"I **will look for** a new apartment that is closer to the office."},{"sentence":"Bukas, **maghahanap** kami ng masarap na makakainan sa Poblacion.","translation":"Tomorrow, we **will search** for a delicious place to eat in Poblacion."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng pagiging pabago-bago o hindi permanente sa desisyon, isip, o bagay.
etymology: From reduplication of 'palit', with the 'pa-' prefix indicating a repetitive or frequent action.
original_explanation: Describes your friend who changes their "jowa of the year" every three months. Also applies to the weather in Baguio, your internet connection's stability, or your career plans when you were in college.
usage_notes: Describes something or someone that changes frequently or is inconsistent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Papalit-palit** ang isip niya kung saan kami kakain.","translation":"He/She **keeps changing** his/her mind about where we should eat."}]

meaning_filipino: Daglat para sa "group chat"; isang anyo ng komunikasyon sa mga messaging app kung saan maraming tao ang maaaring mag-usap sa iisang pag-uusap.
original_explanation: The modern-day 'tambayan' and source of all 'chismis' (gossip). It's where plans are made and then canceled ('drawing'), where memes are born, and where you get 'seen-zoned' by your entire barkada. 'Uy, add mo ako sa **GC** ng batch natin!' is the start of either beautiful friendships or endless notifications.
usage_notes: Extremely common in digital communication (Messenger, Viber, WhatsApp, etc.).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"I-send mo na lang sa **GC** ang mga detalye ng ating proyekto.","translation":"Just send the details of our project to the **group chat**."},{"sentence":"Ang ingay ng **GC** ng pamilya namin, laging may bagong chismis.","translation":"Our family's **GC** is so noisy, there's always new gossip."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mabilis at tuwid na pagsaksak gamit ang espada o patalim; maaari ring tumukoy sa isang matalas na puna o salita.
etymology: From Spanish 'estocada' (a thrust with a sword).
original_explanation: Originally a fencing term (the final 'touché!' move). But in the Philippines, it's more often a verbal attack. It's that sharp, witty comeback you think of 5 hours after the argument. Yung 'bardagulan' sa Twitter? Puno 'yan ng mga estokada.
usage_notes: Can be literal (in martial arts like arnis) or figurative (in arguments).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nailagan ng eskrimador ang biglaang **estokada** ng kalaban.","translation":"The fencer dodged the opponent's sudden **thrust**."},{"sentence":"Kilala si Miriam Defensor-Santiago sa kanyang mga matatalinong **estokada** sa mga debate.","translation":"Miriam Defensor-Santiago was known for her intelligent **verbal jabs** in debates."}]

meaning_filipino: Lumampas o humigit sa isang itinakdang hangganan, sukat, o pamantayan.
original_explanation: When you told yourself you'd only watch one episode on Netflix but it's suddenly 3 AM. You didn't just pass the time, you went way over the limit. It's also that moment in the jeepney when you miss your stop because you were too busy scrolling on your phone. "Manong, para! Naglampas na po!"
usage_notes: Often used with objects or concepts indicating a limit, like 'oras' (time), 'badyet' (budget), or 'lugar' (place). The actor-focus form is 'lumampas' while 'maglampas' implies a more deliberate or resulting action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **maglampas** sa itinakdang badyet para sa proyekto.","translation":"Do not **exceed** the set budget for the project."},{"sentence":"Nakatulog ako sa bus kaya ako'y **naglampas** sa aking bababaan.","translation":"I fell asleep on the bus that's why I **went beyond** my stop."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagmulat ng mga mata at pagkamit ng kamalayan mula sa pagkakatulog.
original_explanation: The daily struggle between your alarm clock and your desire for "5 more minutes." It's the moment you check your phone for notifications before you even get out of bed. It can also be metaphorical, like your "awakening" that you deserve better than your toxic ex.
usage_notes: Can be literal (waking from sleep) or metaphorical (a realization or awakening).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap ang **paggising** nang maaga kung gabi ka na natulog.","translation":"**Waking up** early is hard if you slept late at night."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang talumpati ay naging isang **paggising** sa natutulog na damdamin ng mga tao.","translation":"His speech became an **awakening** for the people's dormant feelings."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na pagpapahayag ng paumanhin o pagsisisi na ginagawa sa harap ng publiko, kadalasan sa pamamagitan ng media.
original_explanation: The national sport of celebrities and politicians after getting caught. It usually involves a crying selfie video, a carefully worded statement written by their PR team, and a promise to 'be better.' The comments section is where the real tea is.
usage_notes: Used as a set phrase in Taglish media and conversation. The Tagalog equivalent is 'pampublikong paghingi ng tawad.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglabas ng **public apology** ang influencer matapos ang kontrobersyal na post.","translation":"The influencer issued a **public apology** after the controversial post."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagpapakita ng pagtatampo o pagkayamot sa pamamagitan ng pananahimik, pag-ungot, o pag-iwas sa pakikipag-usap.
original_explanation: This is what you do when your parents don't buy you the latest iPhone, or when your Jollibee order is missing the extra gravy. It's the silent treatment with a side of dramatic sighs and maybe a slammed door. The adult version is called 'pagtatampo', but 'magmaktol' is for when you're feeling extra childish.
usage_notes: Often associated with childish behavior, but adults do it too, especially in relationships.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magmaktol** diyan, hindi bagay sa iyo.","translation":"Don't **sulk** there, it doesn't suit you."},{"sentence":"**Nagmaktol** ang bata nang hindi ibinili ng laruan.","translation":"The child **threw a tantrum** when they weren't bought a toy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong labis na nagbibigay ng layaw o anumang kagustuhan ng iba, lalo na sa isang bata o minamahal.
original_explanation: Describes the lola who will fight your parents for scolding you. She's the one who gives you extra baon, lets you eat dessert before dinner, and believes you are the most special apo in the world, even if you just spent 8 hours on TikTok.
usage_notes: Can have a slightly negative connotation, implying that the person being indulged might become spoiled ('laki sa layaw').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masyadong **mapagpalayaw** ang lola ni Ana kaya lumaki itong spoiled.","translation":"Ana's grandmother is too **indulgent**, which is why she grew up spoiled."},{"sentence":"Bilang isang magulang, mahirap iwasang maging **mapagpalayaw** sa bugtong na anak.","translation":"As a parent, it's hard to avoid being **doting** on an only child."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng mabilis na paggalaw gamit ang mga paa; ang daloy o direksyon ng isang pangyayari, usapan, o negosyo.
original_explanation: The default setting when you hear your Tita shouting your name to ask you to buy vinegar from the sari-sari store. Also, how your life is going ('ang takbo ng buhay'). It's both literal cardio and metaphorical panic.
usage_notes: Can refer to a physical run, a political race ('takbo sa pagkapangulo'), the flow of events ('takbo ng usapan'), or the running of a machine.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahaba-haba ang naging **takbo** niya kaninang umaga.","translation":"He had a pretty long **run** this morning."},{"sentence":"Ano na ang **takbo** ng negosyo mo?","translation":"How is the **course** of your business?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging mabango; ang amoy na kaaya-aya sa pang-amoy.
original_explanation: This is the quality of being 'mabango'. It's the scent of sampaguita garlands sold in church, the smell of your crush's perfume when they walk by, or the aroma of sinigang being cooked by your nanay. It's the official scent of 'good vibes'.
usage_notes: Refers to the quality or state of being fragrant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kabanguhan** ng mga bulaklak sa hardin ay umaabot hanggang sa loob ng bahay.","translation":"The **fragrance** of the flowers in the garden reaches inside the house."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pautos na ekspresyon na nangangahulugang 'umalis na' o 'simulan na ang pag-alis'; maaari ding mangahulugang 'ayós na ang usapan' o 'sarado na ang kasunduan'.
original_explanation: Has two main uses. 1) Your mom when you're late for school: 'Lakad na!' (Go now!). 2) When you finally agree on a price at the 'palengke' or Greenhills, the vendor says, 'Sige, lakad na!' (Okay, it's a deal!). It's the verbal equivalent of a firm handshake.
usage_notes: An idiomatic expression. The tone of voice is crucial in determining the meaning. It is considered colloquial.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Male-late na tayo! **Lakad na**!","translation":"We're going to be late! **Let's go**!"},{"sentence":"Sige, sa presyong iyan. **Lakad na**!","translation":"Okay, at that price. **It's a deal**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang pananong na ginagamit upang alamin ang halaga, presyo, o katumbas na bayad para sa isang bagay o serbisyo.
etymology: Possibly a contraction of 'may gaano' or derived from 'mag-' + 'ka-' + 'ano'.
original_explanation: The official opening line for any transaction in the Philippines, from the palengke to the mall. It's the question that determines if something is 'Ukay-worthy' or 'Ay, pang-mayaman.' Before you add to cart, you ask `magkano`. It's the ultimate test of your budget and your self-control.
usage_notes: The most common way to ask for the price of something. While 'gaano' asks about extent or quantity, 'magkano' is almost exclusively for cost.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magkano** po ang isang kilong bigas?","translation":"**How much** is one kilo of rice?"},{"sentence":"Tinanong niya kung **magkano** ang utang niya sa akin.","translation":"He asked **how much** he owed me."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi sinasadyang matapakan o maapakan ang isang bagay o tao.
etymology: From `ma-` (accidental action prefix) + `apak` (step) + `-an` (locative suffix), with a -y- infix.
original_explanation: That 'ay, sorry!' moment when you're navigating a crowded MRT and you accidentally step on someone's pristine white sneakers. Or worse, when you're walking barefoot at home and you step on a Lego. It's the verb for an unintentional foot-related mishap.
usage_notes: The prefix `ma-` here indicates an accidental or involuntary action. `Matapakan` is a common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa paglalakad sa dilim, baka may **mayapakan** kang bubog.","translation":"Be careful walking in the dark, you might **accidentally step on** broken glass."},{"sentence":"Pasensya na, hindi ko sinasadyang **mayapakan** ang paa mo.","translation":"I'm sorry, I didn't mean **to step on** your foot."}]

translation: to stomp one's feet in anger; to show frustration noisily
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita ng inis o galit sa pamamagitan ng malalakas na pagpadyak ng paa o pagbato ng mga bagay.
original_explanation: The national sport of the 'tampo.' It's when you're so annoyed you can't use words, so your feet and the random objects you slam do the talking. A classic move when your mom says 'no' or when your internet dies mid-game. The louder the magdabog, the deeper the inis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magdabog** diyan na parang bata dahil lang hindi ka pinayagan.","translation":"Don't **throw a tantrum** there like a child just because you weren't allowed."},{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **magdabog** ang dalaga nang malamang SINEEN lang siya.","translation":"The young lady started to **show frustration noisily** when she found out she was just SEEN-ZONED."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang magulang na lalaki; ang haligi ng tahanan na pinagmumulan ng gabay at suporta sa pamilya.
original_explanation: The original ATM, a.k.a. "Anak, teka, manghihiram ako." Sila 'yung unang magtuturo sa'yo kung paano mag-bike, at sila rin 'yung unang magagalit kapag 10 PM na wala ka pa sa bahay. The king of dad jokes and the silent provider. Also known as Tatay, Itay, Papa, Daddy.
usage_notes: Isang pangunahing katawagan sa pamilya. Ginagamit din bilang tawag sa pari ('amang pari') o bilang titulo para sa Diyos ('Amang nasa langit').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aking **ama** ay isang masipag na magsasaka.","translation":"My **father** is a hardworking farmer."},{"sentence":"**Ama** Namin, sumasalangit Ka...","translation":"Our **Father**, who art in heaven..."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong ang trabaho ay maghatid o magdala ng mga sulat at pakete sa mga tahanan at opisina; kartero.
original_explanation: The original human notification system. Before email, SMS, and Messenger, this person was the bringer of good news (love letters, checks) and bad news (bills, summons). They braved dogs, rain, and intense heat just to deliver your "pahatid." Today, they're the ones delivering your Shopee and Lazada hauls. A true hero.
usage_notes: A compound noun. The more common term in everyday speech is 'kartero'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inaabangan ko ang **pahatid-liham** tuwing umaga para sa sulat mo.","translation":"I wait for the **mail carrier** every morning for your letter."},{"sentence":"Ang trabaho ng isang **pahatid-liham** ay hindi madali.","translation":"The job of a **postman** is not easy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang opisyal na pahintulot o pagpayag sa isang bagay; pormal na pagsang-ayon.
original_explanation: The more formal, almost legal-sounding cousin of 'pahintulot'. This is what you need before you borrow your friend's charger, use their Netflix account, or, you know, more serious stuff. No kunsintimyento? No go. It's the opposite of 'ghosting' someone's request.
usage_notes: More formal than 'pahintulot' or 'payag'. Often used in legal, medical, or official contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ang **kunsintimyento** ng magulang bago ka makasali sa field trip.","translation":"Parental **consent** is needed before you can join the field trip."},{"sentence":"Ibinigay niya ang kanyang buong **kunsintimyento** sa kasunduan.","translation":"He gave his full **approval** to the agreement."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na pinili para sa isang partikular na posisyon, karangalan, o tungkulin; maaari ring tumukoy sa isang minamahal o kasintahan.
original_explanation: This is some next-level 'chosen one' stuff. Parang sa teleserye, ikaw ang 'Itinakda.' If someone calls you their 'hirang,' it's more poetic than 'jowa' or 'Babe.' It means you were selected, appointed, destined. It's the ultimate promotion, from applicant to 'the one.' Pwede rin sa politics, 'ang bagong hirang na kalihim.'
usage_notes: Has a formal and somewhat archaic or poetic feel, especially when used to mean "beloved." Commonly used in formal appointments.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang bagong **hirang** na embahador sa Japan.","translation":"He is the newly **appointed** ambassador to Japan."},{"sentence":"Ikaw ang aking **hirang**, ang tanging sinisinta.","translation":"You are my **chosen one**, my only beloved."}]

translation: to be orphaned, to be bereft
meaning_filipino: Ang mawalan ng isa o parehong magulang. Sa mas malawak na kahulugan, ang maiwang mag-isa dahil sa pagpanaw ng isang minamahal.
original_explanation: The ultimate teleserye trope starter pack. The main character is almost always **naulila** at a young age. In real life, it’s a deeply sad state of losing one's parents or, more broadly, being left alone by the death of a loved one. It’s the feeling of profound loss and being left behind.
usage_notes: A verb describing the state of becoming an orphan. The noun is 'ulila'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaga siyang **naulila** sa kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"She **was orphaned** by her parents at an early age."},{"sentence":"Nang mamatay ang kanyang asawa, pakiramdam niya ay **naulila** siyang muli.","translation":"When her husband died, she felt as if she **was bereft** once again."}]

translation: the state of being consumed by fire
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng lubusang pagkasunog o pagka-abo ng isang bagay dahil sa apoy.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you forget the 'sinaing' on the stove. It's the ultimate end-game for anything flammable that meets fire. More dramatic than just 'pagkasunog'—this is being burnt to a crisp. 'Yan ang pagkatupok.
usage_notes: Implies complete destruction by fire, more so than 'pagkasunog' (burning). Often used in literary or formal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakalulungkot ang **pagkatupok** ng makasaysayang gusali.","translation":"The **total burning** of the historic building is saddening."},{"sentence":"Pinanood nila nang walang magawa ang **pagkatupok** ng kanilang mga ari-arian.","translation":"They watched helplessly as their properties were **consumed by fire**."}]

translation: Monitoring; tracking; keeping an eye on
meaning_filipino: Ang patuloy na pagmamasid o pag-antabay sa galaw, pag-unlad, o kalagayan ng isang tao, bagay, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is you refreshing the Shopee/Lazada app every 5 minutes to see where your package is. It's also what your manager calls 'performance management,' but what you feel is them watching your every move. It's the official term for stalking, but for projects and parcels.
usage_notes: Can be used for people, projects, deliveries, or situations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **pagsubaybay** sa progreso ng mga mag-aaral.","translation":"**Monitoring** the progress of students is important."},{"sentence":"Salamat sa iyong walang sawang **pagsubaybay** sa aming programa.","translation":"Thank you for your tireless **following** of our program."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng katawan na nag-uugnay sa ulo at sa katawan.
original_explanation: The more poetic, dramatic word for 'leeg'. If your character in a story is being choked, you use **liig** for extra drama. If you're just complaining about a stiff neck from working OT, you use 'leeg'. It's the high-literature version of the body part that holds your heavy head up after a long day.
usage_notes: "Liig" is a more formal or literary synonym for the more common "leeg".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang gintong kuwintas ang nakapulupot sa kanyang makinis na **liig**.","translation":"A gold necklace was wrapped around her smooth **neck**."},{"sentence":"Hinawakan niya ang **liig** ng kalaban upang hindi ito makahinga.","translation":"He grabbed the enemy's **neck** so he couldn't breathe."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagtatrabaho sa pamamagitan ng pagpapakita ng damit o produkto; isang halimbawa o huwaran na dapat tularan; isang representasyon ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: 'Yung friend mong laging "pang-IG" ang OOTD at marunong mag-project sa camera. Pwede ring 'yung tito mong "role model" kasi successful. O 'yung "car model" na tinitingnan mo sa showroom kahit alam mong hanggang tingin ka lang. It's all about being the standard.
usage_notes: A direct English loanword with multiple senses: a fashion model, a role model, or a scale model/representation. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang maging isang sikat na **model**.","translation":"She dreams of becoming a famous **model**."},{"sentence":"Siya ang aking role **model** sa buhay.","translation":"He is my role **model** in life."},{"sentence":"Bumili siya ng **model** kit ng isang eroplano.","translation":"He bought a **model** kit of an airplane."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang lugar na may maraming tao.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `ma-` (na nagsasaad ng kasaganaan) + `tao` (person).
original_explanation: Picture mo ang Divisoria a week before Christmas. O kaya ang MRT-3 ng 7 AM on a Monday. 'Yan ang **matao**. 'Yung tipong wala ka nang personal space at amoy mo na 'yung pabango (o pawis) ng katabi mo. Social distancing is but a dream.
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang ilarawan ang mga lugar tulad ng palengke, mall, kalye, o siyudad.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **matao** ang Quiapo dahil sa Pista ng Itim na Nazareno.","translation":"Quiapo became **crowded** because of the Feast of the Black Nazarene."},{"sentence":"Mas gusto kong manirahan sa probinsya kaysa sa isang **matao** na siyudad.","translation":"I prefer to live in the province rather than in a **populous** city."}]

meaning_filipino: Eksakto o tamang-tama; walang labis, walang kulang.
original_explanation: That feeling when the Grab car arrives the *exact* second you step outside. Or when the last piece of the puzzle fits perfectly. It's the "chef's kiss" of measurements. "Yung terno mo? Ay, hustung-husto sa'yo, sis!"
usage_notes: The reduplication intensifies the meaning of 'husto'. Can also function as an adverb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hustung-husto** ang sukat ng damit sa kanya.","translation":"The size of the dress is a **perfect fit** for her."},{"sentence":"Ang sahod ko ay **hustung-husto** lang para sa mga bayarin.","translation":"My salary is **just enough** for the bills."}]

translation: to be able to ride; to be able to go along with
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng pagkakataong makasakay sa isang sasakyan; makaunawa o makasabay sa isang biro, usapan, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: Literally, it's being able to get a ride on the jeepney during rush hour. Figuratively, it's when you can keep up with your friends' inside jokes and memes. If you can't masakyan ang trip, you're the one left confused while everyone else is laughing. It's about being in sync, whether on the road or with the barkada's wavelength.
usage_notes: Has a very common figurative meaning of "to get" a joke or "go along with" a mood or plan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana may **masakyan** pa akong bus pauwi.","translation":"I hope I can still **catch a ride** on a bus going home."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko **masakyan** ang mga biro niya; masyadong malalim.","translation":"I can't **go along with** (understand) his jokes; they're too deep."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maliit na sepilyo na partikular na idinisenyo para sa paglilinis ng ngipin.
original_explanation: Your dentist's best friend and your first and last line of defense against bad breath after eating that garlic-heavy meal. This is the sepilyo you should be using at least twice a day, but let's be real, sometimes we forget. Don't forget, or your crush might notice.
usage_notes: The most common term for toothbrush.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang magdala ng **sepilyo sa ngipin** kapag mag-o-overnight ka.","translation":"Don't forget to bring a **toothbrush** when you're staying overnight."},{"sentence":"Pinalitan ko na ang luma kong **sepilyo sa ngipin**.","translation":"I already replaced my old **toothbrush**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o antas ng pagiging matalim ng isang bagay, tulad ng kutsilyo o anumang may talim.
etymology: From 'talim' (blade, sharp edge) + 'ka- -an' affix group, denoting quality or state.
original_explanation: This is the quality of the knife you use to slice your green mangoes perfectly. It's the 'sharpness' that makes the chismis from your kapitbahay so cutting. Can refer to a blade, or metaphorically, to sharp words. 'Yung kutsilyo, kasing talim ng dila niya.'
usage_notes: Distinct from 'katalasan' which can also refer to mental sharpness. 'Kataliman' is almost always about a physical edge or, by direct metaphor, sharp words.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubok niya ang **kataliman** ng bagong itak.","translation":"He tested the **sharpness** of the new bolo."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang **kataliman** ng mga salitang binitiwan nito.","translation":"She felt the **sharpness** of the words he uttered."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pananampalataya, mga aral, doktrina, at sistema ng Simbahang Katolika na pinamumunuan ng Papa.
original_explanation: It's the religion that gave us a month-long Christmas, countless holidays for saints you barely know, and the concept of "bahala na si Lord" after you've messed up. It's the spiritual backbone of the Philippines, influencing everything from politics to family dynamics.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa relihiyon at sistema ng paniniwala, kumpara sa "Katoliko" na tumutukoy sa tagasunod.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang naging impluwensya ng **Katolisismo** sa kultura at sining ng Pilipinas.","translation":"**Catholicism** has had a great influence on the culture and arts of the Philippines."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging nakatataas, nanginguna, o higit na may kapangyarihan o impluwensya.
etymology: From pangi- + ibabaw. A reduplication of the first syllable of the root word is added.
original_explanation: This is the noun form of "owning it." It's when one thing is clearly the winner or the most dominant force. Parang sa K-drama, yung pangingibabaw ng feelings ng lead actor para sa lead actress over the second lead. Or sa potluck, ang pangingibabaw ng lechon sa lahat ng ibang handa. It's the state of being on top.
usage_notes: A formal term used in discussions about power, influence, emotions, or ideas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pangingibabaw** ng kanyang pag-ibig sa bayan ang nagtulak sa kanya na maging bayani.","translation":"The **supremacy** of his love for the country pushed him to become a hero."},{"sentence":"Sa huli, ang **pangingibabaw** ng katotohanan ang siyang nagwagi.","translation":"In the end, the **prevalence** of truth is what won."}]

translation: to screw; to fasten with a screw
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkabit o paghigpit ng isang bagay gamit ang tornilyo.
original_explanation: Literally, to put a screw in something. It's what your Tatay does on a Sunday afternoon while fixing that wobbly chair you've been complaining about for months. Also a metaphor for "fixing" things, or sometimes, when someone's mind is a bit loose, you might joke, "Kailangan na atang magtornilyo niyan."
usage_notes: A very specific action verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **magtornilyo** ng bagong kabinet sa kusina.","translation":"Help me **to screw** in the new cabinet in the kitchen."},{"sentence":"Marunong siyang **magtornilyo**, magmartilyo, at maglagari.","translation":"He knows how to **use a screw**, hammer, and saw."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi totoo; huwad o imitasyon. Maaari ring tumukoy sa isang taong hindi tapat, mapagkunwari, o plastik.
original_explanation: From your 'brand new' bag from Greenhills to your 'friend' who only talks to you when they need something. 'Fake' is everywhere. If it's too good to be true, it's probably fake. If they're too nice to your face and talk behind your back, they're definitely **fake**. Also known as 'plastik'.
usage_notes: A very common loanword used in both literal (counterfeit items) and figurative (insincere people) senses.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang bibili diyan, **fake** ang mga produktong 'yan.","translation":"Don't buy from there, those products are **fake**."},{"sentence":"Ayoko sa kanya kasi feeling ko, **fake** ang pagiging mabait niya.","translation":"I don't like her because I feel her kindness is **fake**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng isang bagay na hindi na bago, matagal nang umiiral, o nagamit na sa loob ng mahabang panahon.
original_explanation: That shirt you've had since college? That's luma. The iPhone 6 you refuse to upgrade? Super luma. It's the opposite of "brand new" and often the reason why your nanay wants to throw your stuff away during general cleaning. "Itapon mo na 'yan, ang luma na!"
usage_notes: Primarily used for objects. For people, 'matanda' is used for 'old'. 'Dati' or 'dating' is used for 'former' (e.g., dating kasintahan - former girlfriend).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong bumili ng bagong sapatos dahil **luma** na ang gamit ko.","translation":"I want to buy new shoes because the one I'm using is already **old**."},{"sentence":"Mas matibay pa rin ang mga gamit na **luma** kaysa sa mga bago ngayon.","translation":"**Old** things are still more durable than the new ones today."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maliit na hayop na karaniwang may anim na paa, katawang nahahati sa tatlong bahagi, at kung minsan ay may pakpak.
original_explanation: The general term for any creepy-crawly that makes you go "Eww!" From the friendly langgam (ant) trying to steal your sugar to the annoying lamok (mosquito) singing in your ear at 3 AM. If it's small, has lots of legs, and probably shouldn't be in your house, it's a kulisap.
usage_notes: A general term. Specific insects have their own names (e.g., langgam, ipis, gamu-gamo). 'Insekto' is the direct Spanish loanword equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **kulisap** ang naaakit sa ilaw tuwing gabi.","translation":"Many **insects** are attracted to the light at night."},{"sentence":"Pinatay niya ang **kulisap** na dumapo sa kanyang braso.","translation":"He killed the **insect** that landed on his arm."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang anyo ng musikang popular sa Pilipinas na kadalasang kinabibilangan ng mga grupo ng mang-aawit at mananayaw, na may malaking impluwensya mula sa K-Pop.
original_explanation: It's what happens when you mix K-Pop visuals, OPM heart, and a whole lot of training. Think of it as the soundtrack to your commute, your TikTok dance challenge, and your 'sana all' moments. It's the genre that proves Filipinos can slay the stage, one perfectly synchronized dance move at a time.
usage_notes: Isang modernong katawagan na naging popular noong huling bahagi ng 2010s at unang bahagi ng 2020s. Ito ay isang portmanteau o pinagsamang salita.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paborito kong **ppop** group ay SB19.","translation":"My favorite **P-pop** group is SB19."},{"sentence":"Dumadami na ang mga sumisikat na **ppop** idols ngayon.","translation":"More and more **P-pop** idols are becoming famous now."}]

translation: to use as a lining or underlayer
meaning_filipino: Gamitin bilang panloob na patong o sapin sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: Like putting a placemat under a hot plate, or what you do with a fresh bedsheet. It's the act of adding a protective or decorative layer underneath something else. "Ma, isapin mo na yung diyaryo bago mo ipatong diyan yung kaldero!"
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaari mong **isapin** ang dahon ng saging sa plato bago maglagay ng kanin.","translation":"You can **use a banana leaf as a lining** on the plate before putting rice."},{"sentence":"**Isapin** mo itong kumot sa sahig para hindi malamig.","translation":"**Use this blanket as an underlayer** on the floor so it's not cold."}]

translation: to get married; to unite in marriage
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakasal o pag-aasawa; ang pormal na pagsasama ng dalawang tao sa ilalim ng batas o seremonyang panrelihiyon.
etymology: From 'makipag-' (to mutually do something), 'isa' (one), and 'dibdib' (chest/heart), literally "to become one in chest/heart".
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "sana all" moment. It's when you finally decide to change your Facebook status from "In a Relationship" to "Married" and make it legally binding. It's the grand finale of a love story, the final boss level of dating, where you agree to share not just your Netflix account but your entire life (and maybe your surname).
usage_notes: A formal and somewhat poetic term for getting married.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang **makipag-isang-dibdib** sa isang lalaking may takot sa Diyos.","translation":"Her dream is to **get married** to a God-fearing man."},{"sentence":"Nagpasya silang **makipag-isang-dibdib** sa simbahan sa susunod na taon.","translation":"They decided to **unite in marriage** at the church next year."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng higaan kung saan ipinapatong ang ulo; maaari ring tumukoy mismo sa unan.
etymology: From 'ulo' (head) + '-an' (a suffix indicating place or location).
original_explanation: Technically, it means the 'head of the bed' (where you put your 'ulo'). But in practice, people often use it to mean the pillow ('unan') itself. It's that soft thing you hug tight when you're single on Valentine's, cry into after a breakup, or use to muffle your screams during a horror movie.
usage_notes: While its primary meaning is the head of a bed or sleeping mat, it is often used as a synonym for 'unan' (pillow).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa **ulunan** ng kama ang kanyang telepono.","translation":"His phone is at the **head of the bed**."},{"sentence":"Pahiram muna ako ng malambot na **ulunan**.","translation":"Let me borrow a soft **pillow**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sistematikong serye ng mga aksyon o hakbang na isinasagawa upang makamit ang isang partikular na resulta, lalo na sa pag-asikaso ng mga dokumento, datos, o aplikasyon.
original_explanation: This is the official term for what happens to your soul (and your documents) at a government office. It's the endless waiting, the "pabalik-balik ka," the "Sir/Ma'am, kulang po ng isang photocopy." In the BPO world, it's handling calls or tickets. In the kitchen, it's what your food processor does.
