Basically, it’s the journey from "pending" to "approved" (or "rejected").
usage_notes: A modern, technical, and bureaucratic term borrowed from Spanish/English.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabagal ang **pagpopropeso** ng mga aplikasyon dahil sa dami ng tao.","translation":"The **processing** of applications is slow due to the number of people."},{"sentence":"Ang bagong sistema ay naglalayong pabilisin ang **pagpopropeso** ng datos.","translation":"The new system aims to speed up data **processing**."}]

translation: shade-loving plant; a type of fish (halfbeak)
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halaman na tumutubo sa malilim na lugar; o isang uri ng isda na may mahabang ibabang panga (halfbeak).
original_explanation: This word is a two-for-one deal, but both are kinda obscure. First, it's that plant in your tita's garden that thrives in the shade, the one that doesn't need the spotlight to grow. Second, it's a type of fish. Unless you're a botanist or an old-school fisherman, you probably won't hear this in your daily chismis session.
usage_notes: The meaning depends heavily on context (botany vs. ichthyology).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga halamang **talilong** ay mainam sa mga hardin na hindi gaanong nasisikatan ng araw.","translation":"**Shade-loving plants** are good for gardens that don't get much sun."},{"sentence":"Nakahuli ang mangingisda ng isang **talilong**.","translation":"The fisherman caught a **halfbeak fish**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit na pagsasagawa ng isang gawain o kasanayan upang mapabuti o mapanatili ang husay dito.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa mo bago ang presentation sa office, 'yung rehearsal ng sayaw para sa Christmas party, o 'yung pag-type mo ng message sa crush mo tapos buburahin mo rin. Praktis makes perfect, but sometimes, 'praktis' just leads to more 'kaba' (nervousness).
usage_notes: Maaari ring gamitin bilang pandiwa (mag-praktis).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng maraming **praktis** para sa darating na kompetisyon.","translation":"We need a lot of **practice** for the upcoming competition."},{"sentence":"Pumunta ka ba sa **praktis** ng basketball kahapon?","translation":"Did you go to basketball **practice** yesterday?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mahigpit na paghawak sa isang bagay gamit ang kamay.
original_explanation: This isn't just holding, it's *holding on for dear life*. Imagine you're on a speeding jeepney and the driver thinks he's in an action movie—that's when you magtaban sa bakal. It's a more intense, focused kind of 'hawak'.
usage_notes: Implies a stronger, more forceful, or more desperate hold than the common word 'humawak'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magtaban** ka nang mahigpit sa iyong pangarap.","translation":"**Hold on** tightly to your dream."},{"sentence":"Pinayuhan siyang **magtaban** sa baras para hindi siya mahulog.","translation":"He was advised to **grip** the rail so he wouldn't fall."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-uga o paggalaw nang mabilis at pabalik-balik; isang lindol.
original_explanation: That feeling when your crush walks by, or when you check your bank account after a 12.12 sale. It's the literal shaking, like an earthquake ('lindol'), but also the metaphorical kind that leaves you shookt. 'Pagyanig' sounds more dramatic, like something from a movie trailer.
usage_notes: Often used to describe earthquakes ('pagyanig ng lupa') or a strong, sudden shaking motion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman sa buong rehiyon ang malakas na **pagyanig**.","translation":"The strong **tremor** was felt throughout the entire region."},{"sentence":"Nagdulot ng **pagyanig** sa kanyang puso ang muli nilang pagkikita.","translation":"Their meeting again caused a **quaking** in his/her heart."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginagawa o ginagamit upang makalikha ng isang partikular na impresyon, damdamin, o resulta, na hindi laging tunay o taos-puso.
original_explanation: This is the "for the 'gram" of Tagalog. Crying in a music video? **Pang-epekto**. That dramatic slow-motion walk? **Pang-epekto**. That long, vague Facebook post about "challenges"? Pure **pang-epekto**. It's all about the presentation, the drama, the ✨aesthetic✨.
usage_notes: A Taglish/Filipinized term. Can be used as an adjective ("pang-epektong luha" - tears for effect) or as a noun ("puro ka pang-epekto" - you're all for show).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala sa iyak niya, **pang-epekto** lang 'yan.","translation":"Don't believe his crying, that's just **for effect**."},{"sentence":"Nagsuot siya ng salamin kahit hindi malabo ang mata, **pang-epekto** lang daw.","translation":"He wore glasses even though his vision isn't blurry, supposedly just **for show**."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paraang eksakto o salita-por-salita na katulad ng orihinal.
original_explanation: This is the call center agent's mantra: 'You must follow the script **berbeytim**.' It means word-for-word, no ad-libs, no shortcuts. It's quoting your friend's 'hugot' line exactly as they posted it, or when your mom repeats what your dad said, complete with his tone and gestures, just to prove a point. Copy-paste, but for spoken words.
usage_notes: A direct Tagalized spelling of the English word. Used in both formal (e.g., legal transcription) and informal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinuha niya nang **berbeytim** ang sinabi ng propesor para sa kanyang mga tala.","translation":"She took down what the professor said **verbatim** for her notes."},{"sentence":"Ang testimonya ng saksi ay itinala nang **berbeytim**.","translation":"The witness's testimony was recorded **verbatim**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng panahon na mainit at maalinsangan, kung saan ang pakiramdam ay mabigat at malagkit dahil sa halumigmig sa hangin.
etymology: From ka- + alinsangan + -an. Describes the state or quality of being 'maalinsangan' (sultry, humid).
original_explanation: The official weather report for the Philippines from March to May. It's that 'malagkit' (sticky) feeling the moment you step out of the shower. It's when your powder foundation melts off your face before you even get to the office. It’s the reason we have malls on every corner—not just for shopping, but for the free air-con.
usage_notes: Describes the oppressive, humid heat common in tropical climates, which feels heavy and sticky.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Grabe ang **kaalinsanganan** ngayong tanghali, parang ayaw kong lumabas.","translation":"The **sultriness** this noon is intense, I don't feel like going out."},{"sentence":"Ang **kaalinsanganan** ay nagpapalala sa aking pagod.","translation":"The **humidity** makes my exhaustion worse."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, sangkap, o pamamaraan na ginagamit upang maging mas maputi o magpaputi ng kulay ng isang bagay, lalo na ng balat.
original_explanation: The holy grail of many Pinoys, found in everything from sabon to lotion to gluta drips. This is the stuff that promises to make you look like your favorite K-drama star, even if it means avoiding the sun like a vampire. The official product of the "Sana all maputi" fan club.
usage_notes: Can be a noun (a whitening product) or an adjective (a whitening effect).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming sabon na **pampaputi** ang mabibili sa botika.","translation":"Many **whitening** soaps are available at the pharmacy."},{"sentence":"Naghahanap siya ng mabisang paraan na **pampaputi** ng ngipin.","translation":"She is looking for an effective method for teeth **whitening**."}]

translation: to sway gracefully; to swing rhythmically
meaning_filipino: Ang marahan at may ritmong paggalaw o pag-ugoy, tulad ng pagsayaw o pagsway ng mga sanga ng puno sa hangin.
original_explanation: That graceful sway you see in dance performances, or how a tall coconut tree moves in the breeze. It's the opposite of awkward, jerky movements. Think of a beauty queen doing her signature walk, or your lola swaying to a classic kundiman. It's movement with *soul*.
usage_notes: Implies a sense of rhythm, grace, and natural, flowing movement.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umindayog** ang mga mananayaw sa saliw ng malamyos na musika.","translation":"The dancers **swayed gracefully** to the tune of the gentle music."},{"sentence":"Nakakarelax panoorin ang mga dahon na **umindayog** sa ihip ng hangin.","translation":"It's relaxing to watch the leaves **sway rhythmically** with the blowing wind."}]

translation: to gesture repeatedly, to wave around
meaning_filipino: Paulit-ulit na igalaw ang kamay o mga kamay bilang senyas o upang magbigay-diin sa sinasabi.
original_explanation: What your tita does with her hands while telling a very dramatic story. Or what a conductor does with a baton. It's hand-gesturing level 99. "Huwag mong i-kumpas-kumpas 'yang kutsilyo, delikado!"
usage_notes: The reduplication ('kumpas-kumpas') implies a repetitive, continuous, or sometimes careless action, as opposed to a single gesture ('ikumpas').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hilig niyang **ikumpas-kumpas** ang kanyang mga kamay habang nagsasalita.","translation":"He likes to **gesture repeatedly** with his hands while talking."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ikumpas-kumpas** ang baso at baka mabasag.","translation":"Don't **wave** the glass **around** or it might break."}]

translation: to lay out; to expose to the sun/air
meaning_filipino: Ilapag o ilantad ang isang bagay sa isang bukas na lugar upang matuyo, maaarawan, o mahanginan.
original_explanation: A close cousin of 'ihayhay' but more general. This is what you do with palay (rice grains) after harvest, laying them out on the road to dry (watch out, motorists!). It's also for drying daing (dried fish) under the sun. It's the act of laying something flat and open to the elements, usually to dry it out.
usage_notes: Often used for agricultural products like grains or fish that need to be sun-dried. Less common in urban conversation compared to 'ibilad'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **ihayang** ang mga butil ng palay sa sikat ng araw.","translation":"The rice grains need to be **laid out** under the sun."},{"sentence":"Maingat niyang **inihayang** ang isda sa bilao.","translation":"She carefully **laid out** the fish on the woven tray."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malambot na himaymay na nakapalibot sa ngipin.
original_explanation: Your teeth's best friend and support system. It's what gets angry and bleeds when you haven't flossed since 2019. It's the pink frame for your pearly whites. When your dentist says 'Your gums look a little inflamed,' they're talking about your ngilngil.
usage_notes: A less common but more specific term for 'gums' than the Spanish-derived 'gilagid'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Namamaga ang kanyang **ngilngil** dahil sa impeksyon.","translation":"His **gums** are swollen because of an infection."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang pagsesepilyo upang mapanatiling malusog ang **ngilngil** at ngipin.","translation":"Brushing is important to keep the **gums** and teeth healthy."}]

translation: to do one's best; to improve something deliberately
meaning_filipino: Gawin ang isang bagay sa pinakamahusay na paraan; pag-igihan o husayan ang paggawa.
original_explanation: This is your boss's favorite word during performance reviews: "Pakabutihin mo ang trabaho mo." It means to level up, to do it better, to put your heart and soul (and maybe some overtime) into it. It's the opposite of "pwede na 'yan." It's the "galingan mo, besh!" of the corporate world.
usage_notes: Often used as a command or an exhortation to improve performance or effort.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pakabutihin** mo ang iyong pag-aaral para sa iyong kinabukasan.","translation":"**Do your best** in your studies for your future."},{"sentence":"Sinabi ng nanay na **pakabutihin** ko ang pagluto ng adobo.","translation":"My mom said to **improve** my adobo cooking."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng matinding pagnanais o ambisyon na makamit ang isang mataas o marangal na layunin.
original_explanation: The more poetic, "Rizal-level" way of saying "to have a goal." This isn't just wanting to buy a new phone; this is wanting to change the world, or at least pass your thesis. It's the verb for your big, lofty dreams that you put on your vision board. #SanaAllMayMithiin
usage_notes: A formal and literary word. In everyday conversation, "mag-ambisyon" or "pangarapin" might be more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay **nagmithi** na maging isang tanyag na manunulat.","translation":"She **aspired** to become a famous writer."},{"sentence":"Dapat tayong **magmithi** ng kapayapaan para sa ating bansa.","translation":"We should **aim for** peace for our country."}]

meaning_filipino: Acronym para sa "Closed-Circuit Television." Isang sistema ng mga video camera na ginagamit upang subaybayan ang isang lugar para sa seguridad.
etymology: Mula sa acronym ng Ingles na "Closed-Circuit Television".
original_explanation: Ang Big Brother ng barangay, 7-Eleven, at ng EDSA. Bawat galaw mo, captured. Ito ang dahilan kung bakit nahuhuli ang mga snatcher, mga um-extra rice na hindi nagbayad, at mga nag-violate ng traffic rules. Smile, you're on CCTV!
usage_notes: Palasak na ginagamit sa buong Pilipinas, lalo na sa mga urban na lugar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahuli sa **CCTV** ang magnanakaw.","translation":"The thief was caught on **CCTV**."},{"sentence":"Dapat lahat ng kanto may **CCTV** para ligtas.","translation":"Every corner should have a **CCTV** to be safe."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa dalawa o higit pang panig, ideya, o tao na imposibleng magkasundo o magkaunawaan.
etymology: Mula sa `hindi` (not) + `mapagkakasundo` (can be made to agree).
original_explanation: 'Yung away ng mag-ex na umabot na sa punto na kahit si Tulfo give up na. Irreconcilable differences kung sa legal terms. Parang 'yung opinyon mo sa pulitika at ng Tita mo sa Facebook—alam mong walang pupuntahan ang usapan.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa mga legal na konteksto (hal. 'irreconcilable differences' sa annulment) at para sa malalalim na hidwaan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa mga pagkakaibang **hindi mapagkakasundo**, nagpasya silang maghiwalay.","translation":"Because of **irreconcilable** differences, they decided to separate."},{"sentence":"Ang kanilang mga paniniwala ay sadyang **hindi mapagkakasundo**.","translation":"Their beliefs are simply **irreconcilable**."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagbuo ng isang balangkas o plano; sa linggwistika, ito ay ang pagbabago ng anyo ng pandiwa ayon sa panahunan, panagano, at aspekto.
original_explanation: This is the academic version of "G, gawa tayo ng plano!" Before you write your thesis or your hugot-filled novel, you need to **banhayin** the plot first. It's also what your Filipino teacher makes you do with verbs: "Ako ay kumakain," "Ikaw ay kumakain," "Sila ay kumakain" – that's conjugating, or pagbaban-hay. It's organizing your thoughts before you mess up.
usage_notes: Commonly used in academic, literary, and linguistic contexts. 'Balangkasin' is a more common synonym for 'to outline'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan namin kung paano **banhayin** ang mga pandiwa sa Filipino.","translation":"We are studying how **to conjugate** verbs in Filipino."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **banhayin** muna ang iyong mga ideya bago simulan ang pagsusulat ng sanaysay.","translation":"You need **to outline** your ideas first before starting to write the essay."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga maruruming damit at iba pang tela na kailangang labhan, o ang proseso ng paglalaba mismo.
original_explanation: The monster in your room that grows every week. It's the physical manifestation of your adulting responsibilities. You can ignore it, but it will only get bigger. Also, a common weekend "ganap" that competes with your social life. "Sorry, can't go out, may laundry ako."
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang tumukoy sa tambak ng maruruming damit. Ang pandiwa ay "mag-laundry". Ang lugar ay "laundry shop".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tambak na naman ang **laundry** ko ngayong linggo.","translation":"My **laundry** is piled up again this week."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malaking butiki o reptilya, na karaniwang kilala bilang bayawak (monitor lizard).
etymology: A regional or specific term for the monitor lizard.
original_explanation: This is the big lizard you sometimes see chilling by the river or crossing a rural road. It's the bigger, scarier cousin of the common house butiki. Not quite a crocodile, but big enough to make you jump. In some provinces, it's considered a delicacy. Think of it as the Philippines' mini-Godzilla.
usage_notes: 'Bayawak' is the more widely known and used term for monitor lizard. 'Banyas' might be more regional.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malaking **banyas** ang nahuli ng mga residente malapit sa ilog.","translation":"A large **monitor lizard** was caught by the residents near the river."},{"sentence":"Kinatatakutan ng mga manok ang pag-atake ng **banyas**.","translation":"The chickens are afraid of the **monitor lizard's** attack."}]

translation: leaning back with belly out, arched back
meaning_filipino: Nasa posisyon kung saan ang likod ay bahagyang nakabaluktot paatras at ang tiyan ay nakaliyad o nakausli pasulong.
original_explanation: That classic 'Tito' pose after a big Christmas dinner. You're full, you're happy, and you're leaning back in your chair with your stomach leading the way. It’s also the pose you strike when you're trying to stretch your back after sitting in front of a computer for 8 hours.
usage_notes: Describes a specific posture. Can be due to being full, pregnant, arrogant, or simply stretching.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos kumain, **nakahiyad** siyang naupo sa silya dahil sa kabusugan.","translation":"After eating, he sat **leaning back with his belly out** on the chair because he was so full."},{"sentence":"Madalas makitang **nakahiyad** ang mga buntis.","translation":"Pregnant women are often seen with their **backs arched**."}]

translation: credit to the owner (used as a phrase/attribution)
meaning_filipino: Isang parirala na ginagamit sa social media upang kilalanin ang orihinal na may-ari ng isang larawan, video, o anumang nilalaman na ibinahagi, lalo na kung hindi tukoy kung sino ang may-akda.
etymology: Mula sa pariralang Ingles na 'Credit To The Owner,' pinaikli bilang CTTO at nilagyan ng unlaping 'pa-' na nagpapahiwatig ng pag-amin o paglalagay ng atribusyon.
original_explanation: It's the internet's magic spell to avoid getting called out for content grabbing. You see a meme, you like it, you share it, but you have no idea who made it. Slap a 'pa-ctto' on it and you're *supposedly* clear. It's like saying, 'Hey, this isn't mine, don't sue me, just crediting the anonymous genius who created this.'
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa mga social media post tulad ng Facebook, Twitter, at Instagram. Itinuturing na isang impormal na paraan ng pagbibigay-kredito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng litratong ito, **pa-ctto** na lang po kasi hindi ko alam kung sino ang kumuha.","translation":"This picture is so beautiful, just putting **'credit to the owner'** since I don't know who took it."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng kulay na bahagyang dilaw o may pagkakahawig sa kulay dilaw.
etymology: From `ma-` (having the quality of) + reduplication of `dilaw` (yellow).
original_explanation: It's not full-on yellow, just... kinda yellow. Like your teeth after a coffee binge but before you brush. It's the color of a bruise that's starting to heal, or the sky during a hazy sunset. A subtle, 'hint of' yellow.
usage_notes: The reduplication `dilaw-dilaw` indicates a lesser or intermittent quality of the color.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Madilaw-dilaw** na ang mga pahina ng lumang libro.","translation":"The pages of the old book are already **yellowish**."},{"sentence":"May **madilaw-dilaw** na mantsa sa puting damit niya.","translation":"There's a **yellowish** stain on his white shirt."}]

meaning_filipino: Paulit-ulit na paglagpas o pagsobra sa isang hangganan, sukat, o limitasyon.
etymology: Reduplication of the root 'lampas' to indicate repetitive or intensified action.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa ng jeepney driver na nag-uunahan sa pasahero, lampas-lampasan sila sa mga designated stops. Pwede rin sa budget: 'Akala ko tipid month, pero lampas-lampasan na naman ang gastos ko sa Shopee.'
usage_notes: The reduplication implies a repeated or careless action of going beyond a limit. It can function as an adverb modifying an action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **lampas-lampasan** ang paggasta niya kaya siya nabaon sa utang.","translation":"His spending became **repeatedly excessive** which is why he got buried in debt."},{"sentence":"Sa sobrang bilis ng takbo, **lampas-lampasan** ang sasakyan sa mga kanto.","translation":"Because of the high speed, the vehicle was **overshooting** the corners."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagsisiksikan, pagtutulakan, o mahigpit na kompetisyon.
original_explanation: Welcome to EDSA during rush hour. That's **gitgitan**. Jeepneys, buses, and cars all trying to squeeze into one lane. It's also what happens in the MRT, sa palengke pag-sale, or when there's a piso fare promo. Figuratively, it's the intense rivalry between two BPO agents for the Top Performer award. "Grabe ang gitgitan sa pila ng ayuda!"
usage_notes: Ang hulaping '-an' ay nagpapahiwatig ng isang lugar o isang resiprokal na aksyon. Dito, ito ay nangangahulugan ng kilos ng pagtutulakan o pagsisiksikan sa isa't isa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging sanhi ng alitan ang **gitgitan** ng mga sasakyan sa kalsada.","translation":"The **jostling** of vehicles on the road caused a dispute."},{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang **gitgitan** para sa huling puwesto sa basketball team.","translation":"The **competition** is tight for the last spot on the basketball team."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan sa kusina na ginagamit upang durugin ang mga butil ng bawang sa pamamagitan ng pagpiga.
original_explanation: The MVP of your nanay's kitchen, right next to the mortar and pestle (almires). This little gadget saves you from smelling like you wrestled a garlic monster, perfect for making that killer sinangag or adobo.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa de-kamay na pampiga o sa maliit na almires na partikular sa bawang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakikuha nga ng **pandurog ng bawang** para mas madaling igisa ito.","translation":"Please get the **garlic press** so it's easier to sauté this."},{"sentence":"Nabasag ang luma naming **pandurog ng bawang** kaya kutsilyo na lang ang gamit ko.","translation":"Our old **garlic press** broke, so I'm just using a knife now."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagpapakita ng matinding pagnanasa o pagnanais sa isang bagay, lalo na sa pagkain, na kadalasan ay nagpapalaway.
original_explanation: That feeling when you see a food blogger post a close-up of crispy pata or a cheesy baked mac. You're not just hungry, you're *craving*. Your mouth waters, and you suddenly *need* it. That's `tumakam`. It's the opposite of being on a diet.
usage_notes: Primarily used for food cravings, but can be used figuratively for other strong desires.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumakam** siya sa manggang may bagoong na nakita niya sa palengke.","translation":"She **craved** the green mango with shrimp paste she saw at the market."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang tao, karaniwan ay babae, na labis na malandi, mapaglaro sa pakikipag-ugnayan, o nagpapakita ng labis na pagpapacute sa paraang hindi kaaya-aya.
original_explanation: Ito yung level up ng 'pabebe'. Yung aarte na parang helpless at super pa-cute para makuha ang gusto niya, lalo na sa mga lalaki. Medyo nega ang dating nito, parang 'flirt' na may halong 'annoying'. Think of the classic 'kontrabida' sa teleserye na nagpapa-baby talk sa harap ng bida.
usage_notes: Often has a negative connotation and is almost exclusively used to describe women. It implies an annoying or overly conspicuous type of flirtatiousness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw ng mga kaibigan niya sa kanyang bagong nobya dahil sa pagiging **makiri** nito.","translation":"His friends dislike his new girlfriend because of her **flirtatious** nature."},{"sentence":"Pilit siyang nagpapakabait para hindi masabihang **makiri**.","translation":"She tries to act demure so she won't be called **coquettish**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng matinding pagsisikap, sigla, at pagnanais na matapos ang isang gawain.
original_explanation: Eto yung empleyado na laging "Good morning!" sa group chat kahit 5 AM pa lang at nagse-send na ng unang report. Sila yung tipo na hindi nauubusan ng energy, parang laging naka-tatlong tasa ng kape. Yung ka-grupo mo sa project na siya lahat gumagawa. A true go-getter.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Masigasig** si Ana sa kanyang pag-aaral kaya siya laging nangunguna sa klase.","translation":"Ana is **diligent** in her studies, which is why she is always at the top of her class."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay, gawi, o katangian na panlabas o pang-ibabaw lamang at hindi totoo o malalim.
original_explanation: This is the perfect word for 'plastic.' It's that friend who is super nice to your face but talks trash behind your back. It's the politician's promise during election season. It's all for show, all surface-level, no substance. Like an Instagram post that looks perfect but the reality is a total mess. #NoFilter is the opposite of paimbabaw.
usage_notes: The 'pa-im-' prefix is less common and often implies a quality or characteristic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala sa kanyang **paimbabaw** na papuri.","translation":"Don't believe his **superficial** praise."},{"sentence":"Isang **paimbabaw** na kabaitan ang ipinapakita niya sa harap ng mga tao.","translation":"He shows a **hypocritical** kindness in front of people."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa dakong harapan ng isang bagay, lugar, o tao.
original_explanation: Your location when you're waiting for your Grab car. 'Nandito na po ako sa tapat ng 7-Eleven.' It's the strategic position for 'chismis', where you can see everything happening across the street.
usage_notes: Indicates location. The pronunciation shifts stress to the first syllable: /TA-pat/. Almost always used with 'sa' (sa tapat ng...).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkita tayo sa **tapat** ng simbahan mamayang hapon.","translation":"Let's meet **in front of** the church this afternoon."},{"sentence":"Ang bahay namin ay nasa **tapat** lang ng palengke.","translation":"Our house is just **across from** the market."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagnanakaw nang malakihan at may karahasan, lalo na sa panahon ng digmaan, kaguluhan, o mula sa kaban ng bayan.
original_explanation: This isn't just simple theft. This is next-level, big-time robbery. Think pirates looting a treasure ship, or more realistically, what some politicians are accused of doing with public funds. It's a word you hear a lot in the news, often paired with 'korapsyon'.
usage_notes: Strongly associated with corruption and large-scale theft from public funds, legally defined in the Philippines as 'plunder'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinasuhan ang senador ng **pagdambong** dahil sa di-umano'y pagnanakaw sa pondo ng gobyerno.","translation":"The senator was charged with **plunder** for allegedly stealing from government funds."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang muling mapili sa parehong posisyon o tungkulin sa pamamagitan ng kasunod na halalan.
original_explanation: "To be elected again." The sequel to `mahalal`. It's like your favorite Netflix series getting renewed for another season because the ratings (votes) were high.
usage_notes: Partikular na ginagamit sa kontekstong pulitikal kung saan ang isang kasalukuyang opisyal ay muling tumatakbo para sa parehong posisyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mababa ang tsansang **mahalal na muli** ang kasalukuyang meyor dahil sa mga kontrobersiya.","translation":"The current mayor has a low chance of **being re-elected** due to controversies."},{"sentence":"Nagsusumikap ang kongresista na **mahalal na muli** sa kanyang distrito.","translation":"The congresswoman is working hard to **be re-elected** in her district."}]

translation: entangled; caught up in many things
meaning_filipino: Pagiging gusot, pagkakabuhol-buhol, o pagkakasangkot sa maraming bagay o gawain nang sabay-sabay.
etymology: Reduplication of 'sabid' (to get caught or entangled).
original_explanation: This is the feeling when your earphones are a mess in your pocket. It's also your life when you've got projects, family drama, and a complicated love life all at once. You're not just busy, you're sabid-sabid—tangled up in everything. It's the physical and metaphorical state of being a mess.
usage_notes: Can describe both physical entanglement (like threads) and metaphorical entanglement (like in problems or tasks).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **sabid-sabid** ang sinulid kaya nahirapan siyang manahi.","translation":"The thread became **entangled** so she had a hard time sewing."},{"sentence":"**Sabid-sabid** ang isip ko sa dami ng problema.","translation":"My mind is **all tangled up** with so many problems."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng musikang popular na nagmula sa Hapon. Ito ay daglat para sa "Japanese Pop".
etymology: Loanword from English, short for "Japanese Pop".
original_explanation: Before K-pop took over the world, there was J-pop, the OG Asian pop sensation for many Pinoys in the 90s and early 2000s. Think anime theme songs from your childhood (Rurouni Kenshin, Sailor Moon), colorful music videos, and artists like Utada Hikaru. It's the cool tito/tita of the Asian pop music scene.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to Japanese popular music.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig akong makinig sa **J-pop** noong high school pa ako.","translation":"I loved listening to **J-pop** when I was still in high school."},{"sentence":"Ang theme song ng paborito kong anime ay isang sikat na **J-pop** na kanta.","translation":"The theme song of my favorite anime is a famous **J-pop** song."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paraan ng pagkakagawa, kalidad ng pagkakatapos, o ang kabuuang estruktura ng isang bagay na nilikha.
etymology: From `pag-` + `CV` (first syllable repetition) + `yari` (to make, to finish).
original_explanation: This is your inner quality control specialist speaking. It's how you judge the things you buy online vs. what you expected. 'Maayos ba ang pagyayari?' means 'Is it well-made?'. You use this for shoes, bags, furniture, or even a well-coded app. It's all about the craftsmanship.
usage_notes: 'Pagkakayari' is a more common and direct synonym for this meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinuri niya ang makinis na **pagyayari** ng mesang gawa sa narra.","translation":"He praised the smooth **workmanship** of the table made from narra."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng likas na galing o kasanayan sa sining. May kaugnayan sa mga alagad ng sining o sa sining mismo.
original_explanation: Yung kaibigan mong kahit simpleng coffee art lang sa latte niya, kailangan kunan ng 50 pictures from different angles. O kaya yung presentation niya sa work, akala mo album art ng K-Pop group. May "aesthetic" sa lahat ng bagay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **artistiko** niyang pagpinta ay hinangaan ng lahat.","translation":"His **artistic** painting was admired by everyone."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa kanyang **artistiko** na pananaw sa buhay.","translation":"She is known for her **artistic** perspective on life."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging madalang o hindi madalas mangyari; ang agwat o pagitan sa pagitan ng mga bagay o pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is about how often (or how rarely) something happens. 'Yung sweldo mo, "madalang" dumating. 'Yung pag-reply ng crush mo, "madalang". The opposite of "madalas". It describes things that are few and far between, like a quiet day on EDSA or a train that arrives on time.
usage_notes: Halos palaging ginagamit sa anyong pang-uri nitong "madalang" (infrequent, rare). Ang anyong pangngalan na "dalang" ay bihirang gamitin nang mag-isa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napansin niya ang **dalang** ng mga sasakyang dumaraan sa kalye.","translation":"He noticed the **sparseness** of vehicles passing on the street."},{"sentence":"Madalang na siyang dumalaw mula nang lumipat siya ng tirahan.","translation":"He visits **infrequently** ever since he moved residences."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng balani upang makahikayat ng metal; sa makasagisag na paraan, ang pag-akit o paghalina nang may malakas na puwersa.
original_explanation: To have that 'main character energy' that just pulls people in. It's when your crush walks into the room and suddenly they're the only person you see, like a human magnet. On a literal level, it's what Magneto does. On a personal level, it's what your charisma (or your bank account) does.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for magnets (bato-balani) or figuratively for personal charm and attraction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang bato-balani upang **magbalani** ng mga pako na nahulog sa sahig.","translation":"He used the magnet to **attract** the nails that fell on the floor."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang ngiti ay tila **nagbabalani** sa lahat ng tao sa silid.","translation":"Her smile seemed to **attract** everyone in the room."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakahuli sa isang serye o pagkakasunod-sunod; ang pangwakas.
original_explanation: This is the Spanish word for 'last' that we use for dramatic flair. It's not just 'huli' (last), it's *ultima*—the 'now or never', 'do or die' kind of last. Think 'ultima hantungan' (final destination) or 'ultima ora' (the last hour before a deadline). It adds a touch of telenovela drama to any finality.
usage_notes: Typically used in set phrases to convey a strong sense of finality or urgency.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ito na ang **ultima** pag-asa ng bayan.","translation":"This is the nation's **final** hope."},{"sentence":"Nasa **ultima** yugto na ang laban.","translation":"The fight is now in its **final** stage."}]

translation: A miss; failure; error; off the mark
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkabigo na tamaan ang isang puntirya; isang pagkakamali o hindi matagumpay na pagtatangka.
original_explanation: That feeling when you confidently answer a question in class, only to be totally wrong. When your joke doesn't land. When you try to shoot a crumpled paper into the trash can and miss. That's sablay. It's the universe telling you, 'Nice try, but no.' It's the opposite of 'saktong-sakto'.
usage_notes: Can be used as an adjective ('Sablay ang tira mo.') or a noun ('Isang malaking sablay ang proyekto.').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sablay** ang hula mo kung sino ang mananalo.","translation":"Your guess on who would win was **way off**."},{"sentence":"Laging **sablay** ang pag-timing niya sa pagdating ng bus.","translation":"His timing for the bus's arrival is always a **miss**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita ng matinding pagnanais o paggigiit na gawin o makuha ang isang bagay sa kabila ng mga hadlang o pagtutol.
original_explanation: This is peak Pinoy hospitality in reverse. It's your tita telling you 'Kain pa!' for the 5th time, and you finally give in. It's you trying to fit into your pre-pandemic jeans. It’s the energy of insisting, whether it's for someone to eat more or for yourself to finish that last-minute report. It's the art of 'kulit' but with a goal.
usage_notes: Can have a positive connotation (persistence) or a negative one (being pushy).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit pagod na, **nagpumilit** siyang tapusin ang kanyang trabaho.","translation":"Even though he was tired, he **persisted** to finish his work."},{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang **magpumilit** kung ayaw niya talaga.","translation":"Don't **insist** anymore if they really don't want to."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng katangiang hindi maipaliwanag ng agham o likas na batas; kahima-himala.
original_explanation: 'Yung tipong nakapasa ka sa exam kahit 'di ka nag-review. O kaya 'yung sahod mo na umabot pa hanggang sa susunod na kinsenas. It's that "how did that even happen?!" moment, powered by divine intervention or pure, unadulterated luck.
usage_notes: Often used in religious contexts or to describe highly improbable, fortunate events.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Milagroso** ang paggaling ng pasyente matapos ang matinding karamdaman.","translation":"The patient's recovery after a severe illness was **miraculous**."},{"sentence":"Isang **milagroso**ng pangyayari ang pagkapanalo niya sa lotto.","translation":"His winning the lottery was a **miraculous** event."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pang-abay na nagsasaad na ang isang kilos o kalagayan ay nangyayari sa panahon ngayon.
etymology: Pinaniniwalaang nagmula sa 'sa' + 'lukob' (to cover/encompass), na tumutukoy sa panahong sakop ng ngayon.
original_explanation: The professional way of saying 'ngayon'. Sounds more legit in office emails. 'Kasalukuyan po naming pinoproseso ang inyong request' is the corporate version of 'Wait lang, ginagawa na.'
usage_notes: Madalas makita sa unahan ng pangungusap, na sinusundan ng 'na' o 'ay'. Halimbawa: 'Kasalukuyan siyang natutulog.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kasalukuyan** siyang nag-aaral para sa darating na pagsusulit.","translation":"She is **currently** studying for the upcoming exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kakanin na gawa sa galapong o harina ng bigas, asukal, at tubig, na pinasisingawan upang maluto. Karaniwan itong kinakain bilang meryenda o kasama ng dinuguan.
etymology: Mula sa Malay na 'putu', na tumutukoy sa isang uri ng pinasisingawang keyk.
original_explanation: The OG Filipino cupcake. It's that fluffy, white, steamed rice cake you see everywhere from fiestas to your tita's merienda spread. It's the perfect partner-in-crime for dinuguan (pork blood stew). Don't ask why, just try it. It's a culinary love story better than most teleseryes.
usage_notes: Madalas itong nilalagyan ng keso, itlog na maalat, o kinudkod na niyog sa ibabaw. Ang kulay nito ay maaaring mag-iba depende sa lasa (hal. rosas para sa strawberry, lila para sa ube).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong **puto** ang may keso sa ibabaw.","translation":"My favorite **steamed rice cake** is the one with cheese on top."},{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng **puto** at dinuguan para sa almusal.","translation":"Mom bought **puto** and dinuguan for breakfast."}]

translation: to try (in court); to put on trial
meaning_filipino: Isailalim sa pormal na paglilitis sa hukuman.
original_explanation: This is the action verb for 'litis'. It's what the court does to a suspect. To be 'lilitisin' means you're going to face the judge and the legal system. It's the legal version of being put in the hot seat. 'Huwag kang gumawa ng masama kung ayaw mong litisin sa korte.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang akusado ay **lilitisin** sa susunod na buwan.","translation":"The accused will be **put on trial** next month."},{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang piskal na **litisin** ang suspek batay sa ebidensya.","translation":"The fiscal decided to **try** the suspect based on the evidence."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain o industriya ng pag-aalaga ng mga manok at iba pang katulad na ibon para sa kanilang karne o itlog.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `pag-`, salitang-ugat na `manok`, at hulaping `-an` (panandang pook o kolektibo).
original_explanation: Business ito ng tita mo sa probinsya. Amoy... opportunity. It's the art of raising chickens, whether for that sweet, sweet Jollibee-style fried chicken or for the eggs you need for your silog breakfast.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa industriya o sa lugar kung saan isinasagawa ang pag-aalaga ng manok.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Yumaman ang pamilya nila dahil sa negosyong **pagmamanukan**.","translation":"Their family got rich because of the **poultry farming** business."},{"sentence":"Nagtayo siya ng maliit na **pagmamanukan** sa likod-bahay.","translation":"He built a small **poultry farm** in the backyard."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lalaking haligi ng isang pamilya; ang padre de pamilya na responsable sa kapakanan at pagtataguyod ng kaniyang sambahayan.
etymology: Kombinasyon ng salitang Tagalog na 'ama' (father) at 'tahanan' (home).
original_explanation: Literally "father of the home." This is the OG provider, the guy who's supposed to fix the leaky faucet, kill the ipis, and provide the Netflix subscription. He's the "haligi ng tahanan" (post of the house), holding everything up. Think of him as the family's CEO.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa mga pormal o tradisyonal na konteksto upang tukuyin ang papel ng ama sa pamilya. Ang katapat nito ay 'ilaw ng tahanan' para sa ina.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bilang **ama ng tahanan**, tungkulin niyang magtrabaho para sa pamilya.","translation":"As the **head of the household**, it is his duty to work for his family."},{"sentence":"Iginagalang si Mang Jose bilang isang mabuting **ama ng tahanan**.","translation":"Mang Jose is respected as a good **head of the household**."}]
related: ["ilaw ng tahanan","haligi ng tahanan","padre de pamilya","pamilya"]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang paglalabas ng malakas na boses o tunog mula sa bibig, upang ipahayag ang matinding damdamin o para marinig sa malayo.
original_explanation: This is the current state of your mom when she finds out you haven't washed the dishes yet. It's also the sound of a crowd at an Araneta concert or a PBA game. 'Bakit ka sumisigaw? Nasa kabilang kwarto lang ako!' It's the default volume for vendors in Divisoria.
usage_notes: This is the present tense of the verb `sumigaw`. It describes the ongoing action of shouting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naririnig kong **sumisigaw** ang kapitbahay namin tuwing may laro ng basketball.","translation":"I can hear our neighbor **shouting** every time there's a basketball game."},{"sentence":"**Sumisigaw** siya sa sakit.","translation":"She is **shouting** in pain."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay na karaniwang tinatanggap bilang bayad para sa mga produkto at serbisyo at pagbabayad ng mga utang.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'perra,' isang kolokyal na termino para sa baryang mababa ang halaga (partikular, ang 'perra gorda' o 'perra chica').
original_explanation: The ultimate 'hugot' topic and the reason you wake up for your 8 AM Zoom call. In the Philippines, 'pera' is the magic word that can make you happy, stressed, motivated, and guilty all at once. It's what your ninong/ninang gives you on Christmas, what you use to buy milk tea, and what mysteriously vanishes a week before payday. As the saying goes, 'Pera na, naging bato pa.'
usage_notes: Ito ang pinakakaraniwan at pangkalahatang termino para sa pera sa wikang Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong mag-ipon ng **pera** para sa kinabukasan.","translation":"I need to save **money** for the future."},{"sentence":"Wala na akong **pera**, sa susunod na sahod na lang.","translation":"I have no **money** left, maybe next payday."}]

translation: to be annoyed; to get irritated
meaning_filipino: Makaramdam ng inis o pagkainis; mawalan ng pasensya o magalit nang bahagya.
original_explanation: The default emotional state of anyone commuting in Metro Manila. It's the feeling you get when the internet is slow, when someone spoils a series, or when your sibling "borrows" your clothes without asking. It's not full-blown rage, just that "konti na lang, sasabog na ako" feeling.
usage_notes: `Naiinis` is the common present tense form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang gagawa ng bagay na ikaw ay **maiinis** sa huli.","translation":"Don't do things that will make you **get annoyed** in the end."},{"sentence":"Naiinis ako sa bagal ng serbisyo nila.","translation":"I'm **annoyed** with their slow service."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang utos o pakiusap na pag-isipan nang malalim at mabuti ang isang partikular na bagay.
etymology: From 'nilay' (contemplation) with reduplication and the suffix '-in'.
original_explanation: This is what your parents tell you to do when you make a rash decision. 'Nilay-nilayin mo muna!' means 'Think it over, dude!' It's the command form of your 3 AM overthinking session. It's being told to activate your 'nilay-nilay' mode on a specific topic, like a major purchase or a relationship status change.
usage_notes: This is the imperative or infinitive form, used as a command or to express the action of contemplating.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bago ka magdesisyon, dapat mong **nilay-nilayin** ang lahat ng posibleng kahihinatnan.","translation":"Before you decide, you should **contemplate** all the possible consequences."},{"sentence":"**Nilay-nilayin** mo kung tama ba talaga ang gagawin mo.","translation":"**Reflect upon** whether what you're about to do is truly right."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sisidlan, karaniwang yari sa metal o porselana, na nilalagay sa sahig upang duraan, partikular na ng mga taong ngumunguya ng tabako o buyo.
original_explanation: The lolo's version of an ashtray, but for spit. This was the designated target for the red-orange spit from chewing 'nga-nga' (betel nut). Now mostly seen in museums or old houses, reminding us of a time before 'Bawal Dumura Dito' signs were everywhere.
usage_notes: An old-fashioned item, not common in modern households. Often made of brass.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa ilalim ng mesa ng matanda ay may isang antigong **kuspidor** na tanso.","translation":"Under the old man's table was an antique brass **spittoon**."},{"sentence":"Bawal dumura sa sahig; gamitin ang **kuspidor**.","translation":"It is forbidden to spit on the floor; use the **spittoon**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-iiwan ng tagubilin, bilin, o anumang bagay sa isang tao para sa kanyang pangangalaga o pagtupad.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "bahala ka na diyan" move, but with more responsibility. It's what your mom does before she leaves for the palengke: "Huwag mong kalimutan pakainin yung aso, hugasan mo yung plato, at 'wag kang mag-add to cart!" You're the one being left with the 'habilin'.
usage_notes: The verb form focuses on the person or place *receiving* the instruction or entrusted item. The object being entrusted uses the verb 'ihabilin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Paghabilinan** mo si ate ng mga dapat gawin habang wala tayo.","translation":"**Entrust** to your older sister the things that need to be done while we're away."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **paghabilinan** natin ng mga alaga nating pusa?","translation":"To whom shall we **entrust** our pet cats?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salita, parirala, o larawan sa isang elektronikong dokumento na kapag pinindot ay magdadala sa gumagamit sa ibang bahagi ng dokumento o sa ibang website.
etymology: A neologism (newly coined word) from 'ugnay' (connect) and the suffix '-an', created to serve as a local equivalent for 'hyperlink'.
original_explanation: This is the super formal, 'purist' Filipino word for a hyperlink. You know, the blue, underlined text you click to get to a Shopee budol, a Wikipedia rabbit hole, or a chismis thread. In real life, literally no one says 'Paki-click ang ulnayan.' We all just say 'link.' Use this to impress your Filipino teacher, not your friends.
usage_notes: A formal, academic term. 'Link' or 'kawing' are used in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa dulo ng artikulo ang **ulnayan** para sa mga sanggunian.","translation":"The **hyperlink** for the references is at the end of the article."},{"sentence":"I-klik ang **ulnayan** upang mapanood ang buong video.","translation":"Click the **link** to watch the full video."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagdudulot ng pagkagulat o pagkabigla; hindi inaasahan.
original_explanation: The feeling when your 'mahinhing' officemate suddenly belts out a rock song perfectly at karaoke. Or when you see the latest 'resibo' or 'chismis' about a celebrity. It's the 'OMG, for real?!' moment.
usage_notes: Can range from mild surprise to profound shock.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakagugulat** ang balitang nanalo siya sa lotto.","translation":"The news that he won the lottery is **surprising**."},{"sentence":"Isang **nakagugulat** na rebelasyon ang natuklasan ng mga imbestigador.","translation":"A **shocking** revelation was discovered by the investigators."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang panghalip paari sa ikalawang panauhan isahan na tumutukoy sa isang bagay na pag-aari ng kinakausap. Ito ang anyong 'sa' ng panghalip.
original_explanation: The more formal, almost poetic way of saying 'sayo'. You use this when you're writing a love letter, a formal document, or when you're trying to sound extra sincere. 'Ang puso ko ay iyo' hits different than 'Sayo puso ko.' In everyday chismisan, you'll just hear 'sayo'.
usage_notes: 'Iyo' is the 'sa' form (e.g., para sa iyo). The possessive form used before a noun is 'iyong' (e.g., iyong aklat), and the form after a noun is 'mo' (e.g., aklat mo). In modern colloquial speech, 'sayo' is much more common than 'iyo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aklat na ito ay **iyo**.","translation":"This book is **yours**."},{"sentence":"Ibinibigay ko sa **iyo** ang aking buong tiwala.","translation":"I am giving to **you** my full trust."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalakbay sa tubig gamit ang isang sasakyang-dagat, lalo na ang may layag na isinasakay sa hangin.
original_explanation: The OG way of travelling the seas before Cebu Pacific and Air Asia. It's about harnessing the wind and going on an adventure. Today, it's more of a romantic or "finding yourself" activity. "Gusto kong maglayag sa paligid ng Palawan balang araw."
usage_notes: Primarily refers to travelling by sailboat but can be used more broadly for any sea travel.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga ninuno natin ay matatapang na **naglayag** sa malawak na karagatan.","translation":"Our ancestors bravely **sailed** across the vast ocean."},{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang **maglayag** nang mag-isa sa buong mundo.","translation":"He dreams of **sailing** solo around the world."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa ng kilos ng pagsunod sa isang akawnt sa social media sa hinaharap.
etymology: From Tagalog prefix 'mag-' + English 'follow'. A Taglish verb conjugation.
original_explanation: The future tense of modern-day courtship and networking. This is the promise you make when you meet someone interesting: 'Ganda ng feed mo, **magfofollow** ako!' It's a low-stakes commitment that means 'I'll keep an eye on you... digitally.' Often followed by the hopeful question, 'Follow back?'
usage_notes: This is the future tense form. The infinitive is 'mag-follow'. Exclusively used in the context of social media (Instagram, Twitter, TikTok, etc.).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kapag gumawa ka na ng TikTok, **magfofollow** agad ako sa'yo.","translation":"When you finally make a TikTok, I **will follow** you immediately."},{"sentence":"Sabi niya **magfofollow** siya pero hindi naman.","translation":"He said he **will follow** but he didn't."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng metal na ikinakabit sa pinto na ginagamit bilang trangka o pangkakatok.
original_explanation: The old-school doorbell. It's that heavy, often ornate, piece of metal on your lola's ancestral house door that you use to announce your arrival. It's also the latch that makes a very satisfying 'clank' sound when you secure the door for the night.
usage_notes: Can refer to either the latch mechanism (trangka) or the knocker (pangkakatok). More common in older, traditional houses.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malakas niyang kinatok ang **aldaba** ng malaking pinto.","translation":"He knocked loudly on the **door knocker** of the large door."},{"sentence":"Siguraduhing nakakabit nang maayos ang **aldaba** para hindi makapasok ang magnanakaw.","translation":"Make sure the **latch** is properly secured so thieves cannot enter."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng kaalaman, kasanayan, o kakayahang gumawa o umunawa ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: More than just being 'smart' (matalino), this means you know *how* to do things. The friend who knows how to cook, fix your laptop, and give good life advice is **marunong**. It's practical intelligence, not just book smarts. 'Diskarte' is its best friend.
usage_notes: `Matalino` refers to intelligence (IQ), while `marunong` refers to skill and practical knowledge (know-how). You can be `matalino` in books but not `marunong` in life.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Marunong** siyang mag-gitara mula pa noong bata.","translation":"He has been **skilled** at playing the guitar since he was a child."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating kumuha ng taong **marunong** sa pag-aayos ng computer.","translation":"We need to get someone **knowledgeable** in fixing computers."}]

translation: to mediate; to intervene (to separate); to create a gap
meaning_filipino: Ang pagitan o pumagitna upang paghiwalayin ang dalawa o higit pang nag-aaway o bagay; ang paglikha ng espasyo o distansya.
etymology: From the root word 'agwat' (gap, interval) with the infix '-um-'.
original_explanation: This is the designated 'referee' friend who breaks up a fight between two other friends. 'Hoy, tama na 'yan!' Yan ang umagwat. It's also what you do when you put a pillow between you and your sibling on the bed to create a 'border'. It’s about stepping in to create space, literally or figuratively, to stop a conflict or just to separate things.
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of separating people who are fighting, but can also mean to create a physical or metaphorical gap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Walang nangahas na **umagwat** sa dalawang nag-aaway na lalaki.","translation":"No one dared to **intervene** between the two fighting men."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **umagwat** sa magkapatid ngunit siya pa ang napagbalingan ng galit.","translation":"He tried to **mediate** between the siblings but their anger was turned on him instead."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang halagang kinakailangang bayaran sa isang institusyong pang-edukasyon para sa pagtuturo at paggamit ng mga pasilidad.
original_explanation: Also known as 'tuition'. This is the final boss your parents have to defeat every semester. It's the reason why "Mag-aral ka nang mabuti" is often followed by a quiet, stressed sigh. When this gets paid, it’s a temporary victory until the next "miscellaneous fees" boss shows up.
usage_notes: The formal term for tuition. Informally, people just say "tuition". The synonym "matrikula" is also very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtaas na naman daw ang **bayad sa pag-aaral** para sa susunod na semestre.","translation":"They said the **tuition fee** will increase again for the next semester."},{"sentence":"Pinag-iipunan niya ang **bayad sa pag-aaral** ng kanyang mga anak.","translation":"She is saving up for her children's **tuition fees**."}]

translation: to do something at the same time as (someone/something)
meaning_filipino: Isagawa ang isang bagay sa parehong oras o panahon ng iba; samahan sa paggawa ng isang kilos.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of your 'sana all' moments. "Gusto ko siyang kasabayin kumain." It's the action of trying to sync your schedule with your crush's coffee break. It's what you tell your friend to do when you both need to hit 'send' on a risky text message. "Okay, kasabayin mo ako... 1, 2, 3, send!"
usage_notes: This is the verb form, commanding or stating the action of synchronizing with someone or something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Subukan mong **kasabayin** ang pagtibok ng musika.","translation":"Try **to go in time with** the beat of the music."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **kasabayin** sa pag-uwi, may dadaanan pa ako.","translation":"Don't **go home at the same time as** me, I still have to stop by somewhere."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang direksyong timog; ang rehiyon o mga lugar na matatagpuan sa gawing timog.
etymology: From ka- + timog (south) + -an, denoting a region or place.
original_explanation: For Metro Manila folks, this is the land of Alabang, Parañaque, and Las Piñas—the 'South'. It’s where life is supposedly more chill, the traffic is... well, still traffic, and where people say 'taga-South ka ba?' as if it’s a different country. Basically, it’s the southern part of any given area.
usage_notes: Refers to the direction or the region of the south. Often capitalized as 'Katimugan' when referring to a specific southern region (e.g., Katimugang Luzon).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming magagandang dalampasigan sa **Katimugan**.","translation":"There are many beautiful beaches in the **South**."},{"sentence":"Ang hangin ay umiihip mula sa **katimugan**.","translation":"The wind is blowing from the **south**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panginginig ng katawan dahil sa ginaw, lagnat, o takot.
original_explanation: The feeling when the office AC is set to 'Antarctica' mode and you forgot your jacket. Or that uncontrollable shaking when you have a high fever and your mom is wrapping you in three layers of blankets. It's your body's natural 'brrrr' response.
usage_notes: Often associated with being cold or sick with fever.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang **ngiki** sa buong katawan dahil sa lakas ng ulan.","translation":"He felt a **shiver** all over his body because of the strong rain."},{"sentence":"Ang mataas na lagnat ay may kasamang **ngiki**.","translation":"A high fever is accompanied by **chills**."}]

translation: to refute; to prove someone a liar
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapatunay na ang sinasabi ng isang tao ay hindi totoo o isang kasinungalingan.
original_explanation: This is the 'Objection, your honor!' move in a friendship. It's when someone tells a lie and you come in with the receipts, the screenshots, the 'actually...' to expose the truth. You're not just saying they're wrong, you're proving them a certified sinungaling.
usage_notes: A strong verb used to challenge a statement and prove it false.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit anong gawin mong **magpasinungaling** sa akin, hindi mo mababago ang katotohanan.","translation":"No matter what you do to **prove me a liar**, you cannot change the truth."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **magpasinungaling** sa testigo gamit ang mga pekeng ebidensya.","translation":"He tried to **refute** the witness using fake evidence."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtanggap sa isang bagay bilang totoo o umiiral, lalo na kung walang tiyak na katibayan; pagtitiwala sa katapatan o kakayahan ng isang tao.
etymology: Functions as a root word for terms like 'maniwala' (to believe) and 'paniniwala' (the act of believing). Its origin is complex but related to 'tiwala' (trust).
original_explanation: It's what you give your friend when they say "libre kita next time" (even if you have doubts). It's your faith in a higher power, in the universe, or simply in yourself. It's also what gets broken when you find out your "work from home" officemate was actually at the beach. It's the foundation of trust, easily given but hard to rebuild.
usage_notes: Can refer to religious faith, trust in a person, or acceptance of a fact.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang aking **paniwala** sa kakayahan mong magtagumpay.","translation":"I have great **faith** in your ability to succeed."},{"sentence":"Laban sa **paniwala** ng marami, hindi lahat ng ahas ay makamandag.","translation":"Contrary to popular **belief**, not all snakes are venomous."}]

translation: a rush job; something done in a hurry
meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, gawain, o sitwasyon na kailangang madaliin o tapusin kaagad.
etymology: From Spanish `apura` (to hurry). The `pag-a-` prefix and `-han` suffix turn the root into a noun denoting the thing or situation being rushed.
original_explanation: This is a "rush job." It's that project your client suddenly needs by EOD. It's the ulam you cook in 15 minutes because you forgot you had to bring food to the potluck. The result is often described as "pwede na 'yan" or "basta may maipasa." It's the noun form of something being subjected to `pag-aapura`.
usage_notes: Refers to the object or context of the rushing, not the act itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halata sa gawa na ito ay isang **pag-aapurahan** lamang.","translation":"It's obvious from the work that this was just a **rush job**."},{"sentence":"Naging **pag-aapurahan** ang paghahanda para sa biglaang bisita.","translation":"The preparation for the unexpected visitor became a **rushed affair**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggamit o paglalagay ng kulambo sa paligid ng higaan upang maprotektahan ang sarili laban sa kagat ng lamok.
original_explanation: The OG anti-dengue move before insect repellent lotions became a thing. It's like setting up your own personal fortress against the tiny, flying vampires of the night. Very probinsya life, very nostalgic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ugaliing **magkulambo** tuwing gabi lalo na kung tag-ulan.","translation":"Make it a habit to **use a mosquito net** every night, especially during the rainy season."},{"sentence":"Ayaw na ng mga bata ngayon na **magkulambo** dahil mainit daw.","translation":"Kids nowadays don't want to **use a mosquito net** because they say it's hot."}]

translation: to floor; to lay flooring on
meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng sahig ang isang lugar o istraktura.
original_explanation: The verb version of "sahig." This is what your friendly neighborhood karpintero does. It's the act of turning a patch of dirt or a concrete slab into a proper floor where you can finally do your TikTok dances without getting your socks dirty. "Boss, kailan po natin sasahigan itong kwarto?"
usage_notes: The suffix "-an" here denotes applying something (the floor) onto a surface.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan na nating **sahigan** ang itinatayong kubo bago umulan.","translation":"We need **to lay flooring on** the hut we're building before it rains."},{"sentence":"**Sinahigan** nila ng mamahaling tiles ang buong bahay.","translation":"They **floored** the entire house with expensive tiles."}]

translation: to be overcome by emotional weakness; to give in
meaning_filipino: Ang karanasan ng pagpapakita ng kahinaan, lalo na sa emosyonal na aspekto; ang hindi pagpigil sa damdamin o tukso.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of the 'hugot' adjective 'marupok'. It's the moment you actually give in. When you swore you wouldn't text your ex, but you did it anyway at 2 AM? 'Yan, **narupukan** ka. It’s the act of failing your 'don't be marupok' challenge.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in modern, informal, and 'hugot' contexts related to love and relationships.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinabi ko sa sarili ko na hindi na ako bibili ng milk tea, pero **narupukan** ako nang dumaan ako sa paborito kong tindahan.","translation":"I told myself I wouldn't buy milk tea anymore, but I **gave in** when I passed by my favorite shop."},{"sentence":"Ayan na naman siya sa mga sweet messages niya, huwag kang **marupukan**!","translation":"There he goes again with his sweet messages, don't **be emotionally weak**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang likidong ginagamit sa paglilinis ng bibig at lalamunan sa pamamagitan ng pagpapaikot nito sa loob ng bibig nang hindi nilulunok.
original_explanation: Ito yung liquid na ka-partner ng toothbrush mo para sa fresh breath, 'yung pang-final boss bago ka umalis ng bahay. The stuff you swish around your mouth while making that 'grrrr' sound to kill germs and bad vibes (and bad breath).
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa mismong likidong pangmumog o sa akto ng pagmumumog. Madalas na ipinagpapalit sa anyong pandiwa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit ka ng **mumog** pagkatapos magsipilyo para sa mas mabangong hininga.","translation":"Use **mouthwash** after brushing for fresher breath."},{"sentence":"Inirerekomenda ng dentista ang **mumog** na may fluoride.","translation":"The dentist recommends a **mouthwash** with fluoride."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang alternatibong baybay para sa "emulsyon." Tumutukoy sa isang pinong pagpapakalat ng maliliit na patak ng isang likido sa isa pang likido kung saan ito ay hindi natutunaw o naghahalo.
original_explanation: Same as 'emulsyon', just with an extra 'i'. Parang 'yung pangalan mo na may "h" sa dulo (e.g., Sarah vs. Sara). Same person, different spelling on the birth certificate. The more common spelling in modern Filipino is 'emulsyon'.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang variant spelling ng "emulsyon", na siyang mas ginagamit sa kasalukuyan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paggawa ng salad dressing ay nangangailangan ng tamang **emulsiyon**.","translation":"Making salad dressing requires the right **emulsion**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kulisap na may malalaki at karaniwang makukulay na pakpak; paruparo.
original_explanation: The Tagalog for butterfly that makes you sound a little fancy, a little *colegiala*. While everyone else is saying 'paruparo,' you drop a 'mariposa' and suddenly you're in a Spanish-era garden. Also, a famous motel chain, so... context is key.
usage_notes: 'Paruparo' is the more common and native term. 'Mariposa' can also refer to a butterfly knife ('balisong') or a type of lamp, but its primary meaning is butterfly.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang magandang **mariposa** ang dumapo sa bulaklak.","translation":"A beautiful **butterfly** landed on the flower."},{"sentence":"Ang hardin ay puno ng mga **mariposa** at tutubi.","translation":"The garden is full of **butterflies** and dragonflies."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pait na bakal na ginagamit sa pagputol o paghugis ng malamig na metal.
etymology: Hindi tiyak ang pinagmulan, posibleng mula sa Espanyol.
original_explanation: Parang pait para sa kahoy, pero ito pang-bakal. Yung tool na gagamitin ng tito mong mekaniko para tanggalin yung turnilyo na ayaw nang umikot. Hindi ito yung 'pa-fall' pero 'pa-cool'.
usage_notes: Isang teknikal na termino para sa kasangkapan, hindi karaniwan sa pang-araw-araw na usapan maliban kung ikaw ay mekaniko, panday, o manggagawa sa konstruksyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng **pasol** para biyakin ang kadena.","translation":"He used a **cold chisel** to break the chain."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating patalasin ang **pasol** bago gamitin.","translation":"We need to sharpen the **cold chisel** before using it."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang itaas na bahagi sa loob ng bibig, na naghihiwalay sa bibig at sa butas ng ilong.
original_explanation: That part of your mouth that gets brutally burned when you're too excited to eat hot pizza or lugaw. It's the ceiling of your bibig. You don't notice it until it's injured, then it's all you can think about.
usage_notes: A specific anatomical term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napaso ang **ngalangala** ko dahil sa mainit na sabaw.","translation":"My **palate** got burned because of the hot soup."},{"sentence":"May dumikit na pagkain sa kanyang **ngalangala**.","translation":"Some food got stuck on his **palate**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglilinis sa pamamagitan ng pag-alog ng isang bagay sa loob ng likido, o pagmumumog ng likido sa bibig at lalamunan.
etymology: From `pag-` + reduplication of the first syllable of the root `luglog` (`lu-`) + `luglog`.
original_explanation: Parang pag-shake ng Zesto para mahalo 'yung laman, or pag-banlaw ng bote bago lagyan ng tubig. It's also that weird sound your lolo makes in the morning when he's gargling with salt and water. A vigorous, noisy kind of cleaning.
usage_notes: Can refer to rinsing an object or gargling. `Pagmumog` is more specific to gargling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ang masusing **pagluluglog** ng mga bote bago ito gamitin muli.","translation":"Thorough **rinsing** of the bottles is needed before using them again."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa dalawang bagay o tao na halos magkapantay sa galing, lakas, o katangian kaya't mahirap matukoy kung sino ang mas nakalalamang.
original_explanation: Parang laban ng Jollibee at McDo sa Pinas. O kaya 'yung dalawang top student sa klase na laging 98.5 at 98.4 lang ang pagitan ng grades. Sila 'yung di-magkatalo. Close fight lagi!
usage_notes: Can also imply a very close friendship where two people are always together.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Di-magkatalo** sa ganda ang magkapatid na sina Anne at Jasmine.","translation":"The sisters Anne and Jasmine are **evenly matched** in beauty."},{"sentence":"Sa laro ng basketball, **di-magkatalo** ang dalawang koponan hanggang sa huling segundo.","translation":"In the basketball game, the two teams were **neck and neck** until the final second."}]

meaning_filipino: Magiging nasa gilid o malapit sa isa't isa.
original_explanation: How you and your crush sit in the movie theater in your dreams. In reality, it's how you are with a stranger in the MRT during rush hour—so close you can smell their breakfast.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa bus, **magkakatabi** ang upuan namin kaya nagkausap kami.","translation":"On the bus, our seats **were next to each other** so we got to talk."},{"sentence":"Ayusin ninyo ang mga silya para **magkakatabi** ang mga miyembro ng bawat pamilya.","translation":"Arrange the chairs so that members of each family **will be beside each other**."}]

meaning_filipino: Magbigay ng bahagi o parte para sa isang layunin o gawain.
original_explanation: The OG 'group project' verb. It's what you do when you chip in for the office pizza, give your share for the family reunion potluck, or (hopefully) add your brilliant ideas during a brainstorming session. If you don't 'umambag', you're a freeloader.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of group efforts, financial contributions, or sharing ideas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umambag** ako ng isang daang piso para sa regalo ni Ma'am.","translation":"I **contributed** one hundred pesos for Ma'am's gift."},{"sentence":"Lahat ay inaasahang **umambag** ng kanilang ideya para sa proyekto.","translation":"Everyone is expected to **contribute** their ideas for the project."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na may inklinasyon na laging tumutol, kumontra, o magreklamo sa mga mungkahi o sitwasyon.
etymology: From the affix 'pala-' (indicating fondness or habit) + 'tutol' (objection, protest).
original_explanation: The 'devil's advocate' in every group project. No matter what the suggestion is, they'll find a reason to say 'Pero...' or 'Actually...'. The human 'objection!' meme from Phoenix Wright.
usage_notes: Often carries a negative connotation, implying that the person is difficult to work with.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap siyang kausap dahil siya ay **palatutol** sa lahat ng bagay.","translation":"He is difficult to talk to because he is **argumentative** about everything."},{"sentence":"Hindi naman sa pagiging **palatutol**, ngunit may mas maganda akong ideya.","translation":"Not to be **argumentative**, but I have a better idea."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpapakita ng labis na pagmamalaki o kayabangan sa isang tao tungkol sa sariling mga nagawa, ari-arian, o katangian.
original_explanation: This is what you do on Instagram with your travel pics, your new gadget, or your a-bit-too-perfect-looking relationship. It's the act of subtly (or not-so-subtly) making someone feel, "Sana all." The verb form of "hambog."
usage_notes: Often used in a negative context, implying arrogance. The '-an' suffix indicates the person or audience being boasted to.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **paghambugan** ang iyong mga kaibigan dahil lang sa bago mong cellphone.","translation":"Don't **boast to** your friends just because you have a new cellphone."},{"sentence":"Ginawa niya lang iyon para **paghambugan** ang kanyang karibal.","translation":"He only did that to **show off to** his rival."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalaan o pagtatabi ng isang bagay, lugar, o serbisyo para sa isang partikular na tao o layunin sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: That thing you do when you want to make sure you have a seat at that trendy Samgyupsal place on a payday Friday. It's telling the world, "Hey, that's mine, don't touch it yet!" whether it's a hotel room in Boracay, the last piece of cake in the ref, or a bit of your patience for your chismosa tita.
usage_notes: Used for booking tables, tickets, rooms, or setting something aside for later use.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumawag ako sa restaurant para **magreserba** ng mesa para sa dalawang tao.","translation":"I called the restaurant to **reserve** a table for two people."},{"sentence":"Mas mabuting **magreserba** ka na ng tiket sa bus bago maubusan.","translation":"It's better if you **book** a bus ticket before they run out."}]

translation: the act of breaking free; wriggling out
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-alpas o pagkawala mula sa isang pagkakahawak, pagkakagapos, o mahigpit na sitwasyon sa pamamagitan ng mabilis at paikot-ikot na pagkilos.
original_explanation: This is the move you make when your tita tries to pinch your cheeks, or when a "snatcher" grabs your arm. It's that frantic, slippery escape. It's the fish wriggling off the hook, the prisoner breaking from his chains, or you trying to get out of an awkward conversation at a party. It's the physical manifestation of "Nope, I'm out!"
usage_notes: Describes a struggle to get free from a physical restraint or grasp.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa pamamagitan ng mabilis na **pagpulanggos**, nakatakas ang nahuling isda sa kanyang mga kamay.","translation":"Through a quick **wriggle**, the caught fish escaped from his hands."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng suspek ang **pagpulanggos** mula sa hawak ng pulis ngunit nabigo siya.","translation":"The suspect attempted to **break free** from the police officer's hold but he failed."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasapi ng isang maliit at malayang pangkat ng mga mandirigma na nakikipaglaban sa mas malaking regular na puwersa, karaniwang gumagamit ng mga taktikang hindi pangkaraniwan.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "guerrilla" (maliit na digmaan).
original_explanation: Think of them as the original "diskarte" masters of warfare. Hindi sila aatake nang harapan, parang 'yung kaibigan mong bigla na lang susulpot sa likod mo para manggulat. They use the element of surprise, like a pop quiz on a Monday morning.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng kasaysayan ng Pilipinas, lalo na noong Ikalawang Digmaang Pandaigdig.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming Pilipinong **gerilya** ang lumaban sa mga Hapon noong panahon ng digmaan.","translation":"Many Filipino **guerrillas** fought against the Japanese during the war."},{"sentence":"Ang mga taktika ng **gerilya** ay epektibo sa mga lugar na masukal.","translation":"**Guerrilla** tactics are effective in dense areas."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit at tuloy-tuloy na paglanghap sa pamamagitan ng ilong.
etymology: From pag- + si- + singhut-singhot (reduplication of the root singhot).
original_explanation: This is pagsisinghot in burst mode. It's not just one sniff, it's a whole series. It's the sound of someone trying not to cry in public, or that kid in class who perpetually has a runny nose but refuses to use a handkerchief. It's the passive-aggressive signal that you need a tissue, stat.
usage_notes: The repetition implies a continuous or frequent action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumigil ka na sa **pagsisinghut-singhot** at suminga ka na.","translation":"Stop your **continuous sniffling** and just blow your nose."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagsisinghut-singhot** niya ay tanda na malapit na siyang umiyak.","translation":"Her **constant sniffing** was a sign that she was about to cry."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa posisyong nakasabit o nakakabit sa pamamagitan ng isang kawit o anumang hugis-kawit na bagay.
original_explanation: 'Yung bag mong nakakawit sa likod ng pinto. O 'yung braso mo na nakakawit sa braso ng jowa mo habang naglalakad sa mall, para 'di mawala (o para 'di makatingin sa iba).
usage_notes: Describes something being hung or attached by a hook, or in a hook-like manner.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga isdang nahuli ay **nakakawit** sa isang mahabang alambre.","translation":"The caught fish are **hooked** on a long wire."},{"sentence":"Laging **nakakawit** ang kanyang braso sa akin tuwing kami ay naglalakad.","translation":"Her arm is always **latched on** to mine whenever we walk."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang pansining na may anyong patpat, na binubuo ng purong pulbos na pangkulay at isang pambigkis. Tumutukoy rin sa isang likhang sining na ginamitan nito.
original_explanation: Yung pinsan ng crayon na mas sosyal at mas magaling mag-blend. Ito yung ginagamit mo sa art class para gumawa ng mga obra na malalambot at dreamy ang kulay. Perfect for drawing sunsets, portraits, or anything that needs that soft-focus, 'sana all' vibe.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa konteksto ng sining at mga kagamitang pansining.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumuhit siya ng isang larawan gamit ang **pastel**.","translation":"She drew a picture using **pastels**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga kulay ng **pastel** ay karaniwang mas malambot kaysa sa oil paint.","translation":"**Pastel** colors are usually softer than oil paint."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian o paraan ng pagkilos na nagpapakita ng kawalan ng pag-iingat, pag-iisip, o pagsasaalang-alang sa posibleng masamang resulta.
original_explanation: Describes how you handle your phone after the 12th month of your 24-month plan. It's that friend who drives like they're in a video game or the one who spills coffee on your laptop. Basically, 'YOLO' as a lifestyle choice, but with more property damage.
usage_notes: Can be used as an adjective to describe a person (e.g., "walang-ingat na tao") or an adverb to describe an action (e.g., "gumalaw nang walang-ingat").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nabagsak niya ang baso dahil sa kanyang **walang-ingat** na pagkilos.","translation":"He dropped the glass because of his **careless** movement."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **walang-ingat** sa pagtawid sa kalsada.","translation":"Don't be **reckless** when crossing the street."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos o galaw ng pag-inog sa isang sentro o aksis; isang buong pag-ikid o pag-inog.
original_explanation: That feeling when you've had too much to drink and the whole room starts doing the 'ikot'. Also, what the jeepney driver does when he decides to take a 'shortcut' that feels longer than the original route. "Isang ikot pa," is the mantra of your tita at the casino slot machine.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **ikot** lang sa plaza at umuwi na kami.","translation":"Just one **round** at the plaza and we went home."},{"sentence":"Nahihilo ako sa **ikot** ng ferris wheel.","translation":"I'm getting dizzy from the **spin** of the ferris wheel."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpunta sa isang lugar na malayo sa nagsasalita at sa kausap.
original_explanation: This is the opposite of 'pagparito'. It's the 'going there' to a place you've been talking about. 'Tara, punta tayo sa bagong coffee shop.' The action of actually going is the 'pagparoon'. It’s the physical manifestation of 'G!'.
usage_notes: Like 'pagparito', this is more formal or literary than 'pagpunta doon'. The root verb is 'paroon' (go there).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binalak namin ang **pagparoon** sa probinsya ngunit hindi natuloy.","translation":"We planned the **act of going** to the province but it didn't push through."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paanyaya sa isang labanan, paligsahan, o pagsubok; isang bagay na nangangailangan ng malaking pagsisikap upang magawa o malampasan.
