original_explanation: What your BPO team lead gives you when they say 'Let's aim for 110% of the target this month!' It's also what your friend says when they dare you to eat a whole siling labuyo. A hamon can be a serious life obstacle (pagsubok) or a dare (hamunin). It's anything that makes you say, 'Game!' or 'Ayoko nga!'
usage_notes: Not to be confused with 'hamón' (cured ham). The stress on the first syllable (/HA-mon/) means 'challenge'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-akyat sa Bundok Apo ay isang malaking **hamon** para sa mga baguhang hiker.","translation":"Climbing Mount Apo is a big **challenge** for beginner hikers."},{"sentence":"Tinatanggap ko ang iyong **hamon** na maglaro tayo ng chess.","translation":"I accept your **challenge** to a game of chess."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking tinidor na ginagamit sa pagkuha at paghahain ng pagkain mula sa isang sisidlan patungo sa indibidwal na plato.
original_explanation: The "serving fork" is the giant fork that sits next to the serving spoon in the pancit or spaghetti. It's the official tool for "Operation: Kumuha ng Ulam." In its absence, any "kutsara" (spoon) will do, because Filipinos are resourceful like that. We don't let a missing serving fork get between us and the handa.
usage_notes: Often paired with a "serving spoon". The Tagalog equivalent is "panandok na tinidor" but the English term is far more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiabot ng **serving fork** para makuha ko 'yung ulam.","translation":"Please pass the **serving fork** so I can get some of the dish."}]

translation: to erect; to build; to stand up for
meaning_filipino: Itayo o ipatayo ang isang istruktura; manindigan para sa isang prinsipyo o karapatan.
original_explanation: Can be literal, like what construction workers do to a building: they 'itindig' the posts. Or it can be figurative, like when you stand up for your rights or your friend who's being bullied. You 'itindig' your principles. It's about making something stand, whether it's concrete or a belief.
usage_notes: Has both a physical (to build, to make stand) and a metaphorical (to uphold, to stand for) meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais nilang **itindig** ang isang bagong gusali sa loteng iyon.","translation":"They want to **erect** a new building on that lot."},{"sentence":"Dapat nating **itindig** ang ating karapatan bilang mamamayan.","translation":"We must **stand up for** our rights as citizens."}]

translation: got a share; received a cut (of profits)
meaning_filipino: Nakakuha ng bahagi, karaniwan ay sa pera o anumang pinaghatian, na kadalasa'y mula sa isang ilegal o di-karaniwang transaksyon.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you get your cut from the 'team building' budget that mysteriously had a surplus. Or when your friend sells something and gives you a commission. 'May na-close deal si beshie, may nahita ba tayo diyan pang-kape?' It has a slightly shady, under-the-table connotation.
usage_notes: Colloquial and often used in the context of money, commissions, or gains from a venture, sometimes illicit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang **nahita** niya sa proyektong iyon.","translation":"He **got a big share** from that project."},{"sentence":"Wala akong **nahita** sa pagtulong sa kanya, ni pasasalamat ay wala.","translation":"I **got** nothing from helping him, not even a thank you."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghithit at pagbuga ng usok mula sa isang sigarilyo.
original_explanation: This is the verb for taking a 'yosi break.' It's the five-minute escape from your BPO shift, the punctuation mark between classes, or the way you bond with the security guard downstairs. 'Tara, magsigarilyo muna tayo sa labas.'
usage_notes: Refers specifically to smoking cigarettes. The verb 'manigarilyo' is a common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinabihan siya ng doktor na tumigil nang **magsigarilyo**.","translation":"The doctor told him to stop **smoking cigarettes**."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko siyang **nagsisigarilyo** sa likod ng gusali.","translation":"I saw him **smoking a cigarette** behind the building."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglalagay o pagpapasya sa isang tiyak na bagay, tulad ng oras, petsa, limitasyon, o tungkulin.
etymology: From `pag-` (prefix) + reduplication of the first syllable of `takda` (allotted, destined, set).
original_explanation: This is the official word for 'setting a deadline' or 'drawing the line.' `Pagtatakda` ng deadline. `Pagtatakda` ng meeting. `Pagtatakda` ng boundaries sa isang toxic na relasyon. It’s about making things official and definite. When you tell your friend, 'Last na 'to,' but then you do a `pagtatakda` by blocking them, that's when you know it's for real. It’s the adulting version of 'no-take-backs'.
usage_notes: Commonly used in formal, academic, and professional contexts for planning and management.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagtatakda** ng malinaw na layunin ay mahalaga sa anumang proyekto.","translation":"The **setting** of clear goals is important in any project."},{"sentence":"May pulong bukas para sa **pagtatakda** ng mga bagong patakaran.","translation":"There is a meeting tomorrow for the **designation** of new rules."}]

translation: to be hit; to be struck
meaning_filipino: Ang direktang pagdama ng epekto ng isang bagay na bumangga o tumama, literal man o matalinhaga.
original_explanation: Can mean literally getting hit by a ball. But 99% of the time in 2026, it means a hugot post or a meme hit you right in the feels. "Ouch, relate much. Natamaan ako dun, bes." It's when a statement is so true for you, it feels like a personal attack.
usage_notes: Has a strong literal meaning (to be hit by an object) and an even more common figurative meaning (to be emotionally or mentally affected by a statement or situation).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umiwas siya para hindi **matamaan** ng bola.","translation":"He dodged so he wouldn't **be hit** by the ball."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, kahit **matamaan** ka sa sinabi ko, para din naman 'yun sa'yo.","translation":"Don't worry, even if you're **struck** by what I said, it's also for your own good."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng pagiging nakahilig, nakatagilid, o hindi tuwid na patayo o pahiga.
original_explanation: Yung font style na pinipili mo sa Word para kunwari artistic ka, 'yan yung *italic*. Parang 'yung postura mo rin 'pag napuyat sa kakapanood ng K-drama, pahilig ka na sa balikat ng katabi mo sa jeep.
usage_notes: Commonly used to refer to the italic font style in writing and publishing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakasulat sa **pahilig** na letra ang mga dayuhang salita.","translation":"Foreign words are written in **italicized** letters."},{"sentence":"**Pahilig** ang pagkakatayo ng poste matapos ang malakas na bagyo.","translation":"The post is **leaning** after the strong typhoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang posisyon ng katawan kung saan ang dalawang binti ay magkahiwalay o naka-ekis nang malayo sa isa't isa.
original_explanation: That "manspreading" pose you see on the MRT. Or 'yung pose mo 'pag sobrang pagod ka na at umupo ka na lang sa sahig na parang wala nang bukas. It's sitting or standing with your legs wide apart.
usage_notes: Can be seen as impolite or too casual depending on the context. Sometimes used as an adverb of manner.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang umupo nang naka-**bukaka** dahil masikip sa dyip.","translation":"Don't sit with your **legs spread apart** because it's crowded in the jeepney."},{"sentence":"Nahulog ang bata mula sa puno at bumagsak na naka-**bukaka**.","translation":"The child fell from the tree and landed **astride**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha o pag-anyo sa isang bagay ayon sa isang padron o hulmahan.
original_explanation: It's what you do with clay to make a pot, or with your kids' values to make them good people. Parang paggawa ng yema o polvoron, kailangan may hulmahan para perfect ang shape. Figuratively, society tries to maghulma you into what it wants you to be.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for physical objects or figuratively for character, ideas, or society.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto niyang **maghulma** ng mga banga gamit ang putik.","translation":"She wants to **mold** pots using clay."},{"sentence":"Ang mga magulang ang dapat **maghulma** sa pagkatao ng kanilang mga anak.","translation":"Parents are the ones who should **shape** the character of their children."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdadala o pagsama sa isang tao o bagay patungo sa isang partikular na lugar.
original_explanation: This is the official verb of Grab/Lalamove riders, your supportive parents dropping you off at school, or that special someone who insists on taking you home after a date. 'Ihahatid na kita' is the classic Filipino gentleman move. It's more than just a ride; it's a gesture of care.
usage_notes: Can mean delivering an object or escorting a person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **maghahatid** sa iyo sa airport?","translation":"Who will **take** you to the airport?"},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **maghatid** ng mga dokumento sa opisina.","translation":"I need to **deliver** some documents to the office."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawi ng pagkuha o pagnanakaw ng mga bagay na may maliit na halaga, karaniwan ay isinasagawa nang pailalim o hindi napapansin.
etymology: From `pang-` + reduplication of the first syllable `u-` + `umit` (to filch, to pilfer).
original_explanation: A direct synonym for 'pangungupit'. It's that sneaky move of taking something small that isn't yours. It's the office mate who 'borrows' your favorite pen and it's never seen again, or taking a handful of free candies when the sign says 'Take One'.
usage_notes: Interchangeable with 'pangungupit'. Both refer to petty theft.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pang-uumit** ng gamit ng iba ay masama.","translation":"The **filching** of others' belongings is bad."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya namalayan ang **pang-uumit** sa kanyang bag.","translation":"She didn't notice the **pilfering** from her bag."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagbabayad o obligadong magbayad ng buwis sa pamahalaan.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'mang-' na nagiging 'mam-' at ang pag-uulit ng unang pantig ng salitang ugat na 'buwis' (tax). Tumutukoy sa taong nagbabayad o magbabayad ng buwis.
original_explanation: That's you, me, and everyone with a job. We are all 'mamumuwis.' It's that moment you see the 'Withholding Tax' on your payslip and a single tear rolls down your cheek. We are the modern-day heroes funding the nation, one tax deduction at a time.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa isang nagbabayad ng buwis sa pangkalahatan o sa isang taong partikular na magbabayad ng kanyang buwis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bilang isang responsableng **mamumuwis**, dapat nating alamin kung saan napupunta ang ating buwis.","translation":"As a responsible **taxpayer**, we should know where our taxes go."},{"sentence":"Dumarami ang mga **mamumuwis** na gumagamit ng online system para magbayad.","translation":"The number of **taxpayers** using the online system to pay is increasing."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong kasarian ay lalaki, partikular na isang nasa hustong gulang na.
etymology: Possibly from a reduplication related to 'laki' (big), but its origin is ancient and considered a root word in modern usage.
original_explanation: The other half of the human species. Provider, protector, or professional gamer living in his mom's basement—the range is wide. In the palengke, they're the ones carrying the bayong. In a teleserye, they're either the rich heir or the poor but handsome 'probinsyano'.
usage_notes: The standard term for 'man' or 'male'. The counterpart of 'babae' (woman/female).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **lalaki** ang nagtanong kung nasaan ang istasyon ng tren.","translation":"A **man** asked where the train station is."},{"sentence":"Ang tatay ko ang pinakamabait na **lalaki** na kilala ko.","translation":"My father is the kindest **man** I know."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pamumuhay na may matinding pagpipigil sa sarili at pag-iwas sa mga luho o karangyaan, karaniwan dahil sa layuning espirituwal.
original_explanation: Ito yung extreme minimalist. Yung tipong isang plato, isang baso, dalawang damit lang ang gamit. Hindi dahil nagtitipid, kundi for spiritual or personal reasons. Sila yung kayang mag-survive sa tuyo at kanin lang, hindi dahil walang-wala, kundi by choice. Parang monghe.
usage_notes: Isang salitang hindi karaniwang ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap. Mas madalas itong mabasa sa mga aklat ng pilosopiya, relihiyon, o kasaysayan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **asetiko** ang kanyang naging pamumuhay sa loob ng monasteryo.","translation":"He lived an **ascetic** life inside the monastery."},{"sentence":"Mas pinili niya ang landas na **asetiko** kaysa sa karangyaan.","translation":"He chose the **ascetic** path over luxury."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na palaging nakakasama o nakakausap sa isang partikular na lugar o gawain, tulad sa trabaho o sa lipunan.
original_explanation: These are the people in your orbit. Your officemates you share coffee breaks with, your neighbors you exchange 'good mornings' with. Hindi sila necessarily your 'beshie,' but they're part of your daily grind. Sila 'yung mga kailangan mong i-small talk para lang 'di maging awkward sa elevator.
usage_notes: More formal than "kasama" or "kausap". It emphasizes social interaction. The verb form is "makisalamuha" (to socialize, to mingle).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Piliin mong mabuti ang iyong mga **kasalamuha**.","translation":"Choose the people you **interact with** carefully."},{"sentence":"Sa trabaho, marami siyang naging **kasalamuha** mula sa iba't ibang bansa.","translation":"At work, he had many **associates** from different countries."}]

translation: to go to a place for a purpose, to do intentionally
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpunta sa isang lugar o paggawa ng isang bagay na may tiyak na layunin o pakay; gawin nang may intensyon.
original_explanation: When you 'accidentally' bump into your crush at their favorite coffee shop. You didn't just happen to be there; nag-research ka, bes. You went there *on purpose*. That's pagsadya. It’s the opposite of ‘napadaan lang’.
usage_notes: Implies intention and purpose in an action or visit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magsadya** sa munisipyo para kumuha ng permit.","translation":"We need to **go to** the municipal hall **for the purpose of** getting a permit."},{"sentence":"Nag-abala ka pang **magsadya** rito, sana ay tumawag ka na lang.","translation":"You still went to the trouble of **coming here intentionally**, you could have just called."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kagamitan sa pangingisda na may mahabang tali at maraming kawil na may pain.
etymology: From `pa-` (prefix indicating method) + `ambaliwis` (a term related to fishing tackle).
original_explanation: The Tita of fishing methods. Instead of one fishing rod for one fish, you set one long line with multiple hooks for multiple fish. It's the 'work smarter, not harder' of the sea, maximizing your chances of getting a catch. Parang pag-post ng thirst trap, multiple hooks 'yan to catch anyone's attention.
usage_notes: Primarily a technical term used in fishing communities. It can also be used metaphorically to mean an indirect or multi-pronged approach.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas maraming nahuhuli si Mang Cardo dahil sa kanyang pamamaraang **paambaliwis**.","translation":"Mang Cardo catches more fish because of his **long-line fishing** method."},{"sentence":"Ang estratehiya niya sa negosyo ay parang **paambaliwis**; maraming sinusubukang paraan nang sabay-sabay.","translation":"His business strategy is like **long-line fishing**; trying out many methods at the same time."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang isang paglalakbay na isinasagawa dahil sa relihiyoso o espirituwal na kadahilanan, karaniwang patungo sa isang lugar na itinuturing na sagrado o banal.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'Visita Iglesia' but on a grander scale. It's a journey you take not for the 'gram, but for your soul (though a few pics won't hurt). Think of the Hajj to Mecca, a trip to the Vatican, or even just climbing a local holy mountain during Holy Week. It's a trip fueled by faith, devotion, and sometimes, a promise (panata).
usage_notes: The direct translation of "pilgrimage".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming Katoliko ang nagsasagawa ng **paglalakbay sa banal na lugar** tuwing Mahal na Araw.","translation":"Many Catholics undertake a **pilgrimage** during Holy Week."},{"sentence":"Ang kaniyang **paglalakbay sa banal na lugar** sa Jerusalem ay isang makabuluhang karanasan.","translation":"Her **pilgrimage** to Jerusalem was a meaningful experience."}]

translation: workmanship; the way something was made
meaning_filipino: Ang kalidad o paraan ng pagkakabuo o pagkakayari ng isang bagay.
etymology: From `pag-` + `kaka-` + `gawa` (to do, to make). Indicates the manner or quality of creation.
original_explanation: This is the 'Shopee review' word. 'Maganda ang pagkakagawa, mukhang matibay.' (The workmanship is good, it looks durable.) It’s the difference between a hand-stitched leather bag from Marikina and something that falls apart after one use. It's all about the craftsmanship, or lack thereof.
usage_notes: Used to comment on the quality of construction or creation of an object.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halata sa mesa na pulido ang **pagkakagawa** nito.","translation":"It's obvious from the table that its **workmanship** is refined."},{"sentence":"Reklamo ng customer ang pangit na **pagkakagawa** ng sapatos.","translation":"The customer complained about the poor **way the shoe was made**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay o paraan na matipid, hindi magastos, at mahusay sa paggamit ng salapi o yaman.
original_explanation: This is the slightly more formal, almost-obsolete cousin of "ekonomikal". You might see it in an old textbook. It's the same idea: being smart with money. Think of your mom who can make a 500-peso bill last for a week's worth of ulam. That's *ekonomika* in action. But honestly, most people just say "matipid" or "ekonomikal" now.
usage_notes: Mas karaniwang ginagamit ang salitang "ekonomikal" sa kasalukuyang panahon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghahanap siya ng solusyon na mas **ekonomika** para sa kanilang proyekto.","translation":"He is looking for a more **economical** solution for their project."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang bakal na may magaspang na ibabaw na ginagamit sa pagpapakinis, paghuhugis, o pagbabawas ng materyal tulad ng metal o kahoy.
original_explanation: 'Yung tool na ginagamit ng tatay mo para patalasin 'yung itak. Or 'yung ginagamit sa parlor para ayusin 'yung kuko mo. Basically, a tool for smoothing out rough edges, whether it's on steel or your ingrown toenail.
usage_notes: This entry is for the tool. For the act of extortion, see the other entry for 'kikil'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang **kikil** para pakinisin ang gilid ng metal.","translation":"He used the **file** to smoothen the edge of the metal."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang serye ng masasamang salita o pagmumura na ipinapatungkol sa isang tao o bagay bilang pagpapahayag ng matinding galit o pagkasuklam.
original_explanation: This isn't your simple 'P.I.' This is the full-blown, creative, multi-syllabic, generation-spanning curse-out you get from a truly angry tita at a family gathering or a jeepney driver who got cut off. It's a verbal machine-gun of insults.
usage_notes: A stronger and more descriptive term than 'mura' (curse). It implies a tirade or a long string of insults.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malutong na **tungayaw** ang pinakawalan niya nang matapunan ng kape ang kanyang damit.","translation":"He let out a string of **profanities** when coffee was spilled on his clothes."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko na natiis ang mga **tungayaw** niya kaya umalis na lang ako.","translation":"I couldn't stand his **vituperation** anymore so I just left."}]

translation: The act of boarding (a vehicle); loading passengers or cargo
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpasok o pag-akyat sa isang sasakyan; ang paglalagay ng mga tao o kargamento sa loob ng sasakyan.
etymology: From "sakay" (to ride, to board). The "pag- -an" affix with reduplication of the first syllable of the root ("sa") indicates the act or process of doing something.
original_explanation: The daily Filipino "Amazing Race" challenge. Whether it's squeezing into a jampacked MRT train, finding a spot in a jeepney during rush hour, or loading the entire family plus the rice cooker into the car for a road trip. It’s a test of speed, agility, and the ability to make yourself 50% smaller.
usage_notes: Can refer to people boarding or cargo being loaded.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap ang **pagsasakay** sa bus tuwing rush hour.","translation":"The **act of boarding** the bus is difficult during rush hour."},{"sentence":"Tinulungan niya ang matanda sa **pagsasakay** ng kanyang mga pinamili.","translation":"He helped the old woman with the **loading** of her groceries."}]

translation: to have a relapse (from an illness)
meaning_filipino: Ang muling pagbabalik o paglala ng sakit matapos ang isang panahon ng paunang paggaling.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'akala mo okay na, pero hindi pa pala' moment, but for sickness. You feel better, you go out, eat something you shouldn't, or get caught in the rain, and BAM! You're back in bed. Your nanay will definitely say, "Sabi ko sa'yo, magpahinga ka muna! Ayan, nabinat ka tuloy!"
usage_notes: The verb form of 'binat' (relapse). Usually used in the past tense 'nabinat' or as a command 'huwag kang magpabinat'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maligo agad pagkatapos lagnatin para hindi ka **binatin**.","translation":"Don't take a bath immediately after having a fever so you don't **have a relapse**."},{"sentence":"Mukhang na**binat** si Anna dahil nagtrabaho siya kaagad.","translation":"It looks like Anna **had a relapse** because she went back to work right away."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang una at pinakamahalagang titik sa alpabetong Griyego. Ginagamit din ito upang tukuyin ang nangingibabaw o dominanteng indibidwal sa isang grupo.
etymology: Mula sa Griyegong 'alpha', ang unang titik ng alpabeto.
original_explanation: This is a direct import, like your Shopee order from China. In the Philippines, we use 'alpha' to describe the leader of the pack, the 'bida' sa group project, or that one officemate who thinks they're the boss of everyone. It's the first, the best, the one who calls the shots.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa mga kontekstong siyentipiko, teknikal, o sa mga talakayan tungkol sa social dynamics. Madalas itong marinig sa mga code-switched na pag-uusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa pag-aaral ng mga lobo, laging may isang **alpha** na namumuno sa grupo.","translation":"In the study of wolves, there is always one **alpha** that leads the pack."},{"sentence":"Siya ang **alpha** sa aming team, lahat kami ay sumusunod sa kanyang mga desisyon.","translation":"She is the **alpha** of our team, we all follow her decisions."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahabang tulang pasalaysay na karaniwang tungkol sa kabayanihan ng isang pangunahing tauhan na may di-pangkaraniwang lakas o kapangyarihan, at kadalasang nagsasalaysay ng mahahalagang pangyayari sa kasaysayan o mitolohiya ng isang lahi.
original_explanation: Ito ang OG "cinematic universe" ng ating mga ninuno. Isipin mo ang "Avengers: Endgame" pero sa anyo ng tula at tungkol sa mga bayaning tulad nina Lam-ang, Indarapatra, at Sulayman. Ito yung kwentong sobrang haba at puno ng action, magic, at monsters, na kinakanta o binibigkas ng mga oras, o kahit araw, sa mga sinaunang pagtitipon.
usage_notes: Isang mahalagang bahagi ng Panitikang Pilipino na pinag-aaralan sa mga paaralan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang 'Biag ni Lam-ang' ay isang halimbawa ng **epika** ng mga Ilokano.","translation":"'Biag ni Lam-ang' is an example of an Ilocano **epic**."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan namin ang iba't ibang **epika** mula sa Mindanao.","translation":"We are studying the different **epics** from Mindanao."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagdiin, pagpiga, at paghalo sa isang bagay gamit ang mga kamay, karaniwan sa paghahanda ng pagkain.
original_explanation: That satisfying squish when you're mixing dough for pandesal or making lumpiang shanghai filling. It's a very hands-on, almost aggressive way of mixing things. Think of it as a massage, but for food. Or what you want to do to your stress ball during a hellish team meeting.
usage_notes: Primarily used in a culinary context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sikreto sa masarap na embutido ay nasa tamang **lamas** ng mga sangkap.","translation":"The secret to a delicious embutido is in the proper **kneading** of the ingredients."},{"sentence":"Isang mabilis na **lamas** lang ang kailangan para sa ensaladang ampalaya.","translation":"Just a quick **mashing** is needed for the bitter gourd salad."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kalagayan ng masaganang pagtubo o pagyabong, lalo na ng mga halaman.
original_explanation: Parang buhok mo after gumamit ng mamahaling conditioner, or 'yung plantita garden ng tita mo na sobrang healthy. It's that look of abundance and healthy growth. Pwede ring i-apply sa business na yumayabong.
usage_notes: Can also be used figuratively to describe something that is flourishing, like a business.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakaganda tingnan ng **lago** ng mga halaman sa hardin.","translation":"The **lushness** of the plants in the garden is beautiful to see."},{"sentence":"Ang **lago** ng kanyang buhok ay kinaiinggitan ng marami.","translation":"The **luxuriance** of her hair is envied by many."}]

translation: to be brought to ruin; to be in a state of misery
meaning_filipino: Maipatungo sa isang kalagayan ng matinding paghihirap, pagkabigo, o pagkasira.
etymology: From 'ma-' (potential) + 'rapa' (to fall flat on one's face, to be in dire straits).
original_explanation: This is what happens when you invest all your sahod in a crypto scam that your friend posted on Facebook. Your finances will be **maparapa**. It's like hitting rock bottom, but with more drama and less Dwayne 'The Rock' Johnson to save you. It’s the state of being financially and emotionally wrecked.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a fall from grace, whether financially, socially, or morally. Has a more severe connotation than just 'maghirap' (to suffer).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa sugal, **naparapa** ang kanyang pamilya.","translation":"Because of gambling, his family was **brought to ruin**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpapadala sa tukso upang hindi ka **maparapa**.","translation":"Don't give in to temptation so that you won't **be ruined**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng opisyal na dokumento o sertipiko na nagpapatunay sa isang kasanayan, kwalipikasyon, o katotohanan.
original_explanation: When you have the receipts to prove you're legit. "Sertipikado" kang public accountant, "sertipikado" kang IT professional, o "sertipikado" kang marites dahil may screenshot ka ng lahat. It means you're not just claiming it, you have the papers to back it up.
usage_notes: Can also be used figuratively to mean "confirmed" as in "sertipikadong sinungaling" (certified liar).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isa siyang **sertipikado** na mekaniko kaya sa kanya ko dinadala ang kotse ko.","translation":"He is a **certified** mechanic, which is why I bring my car to him."},{"sentence":"**Sertipikado** na siyang baliw sa pag-ibig sa'yo.","translation":"He is **certified** crazy in love with you."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging tapat, totoo, at hindi nandadaya sa kapwa, sa tungkulin, o sa sinumpaang pangako.
original_explanation: This is that rare trait you look for in a partner, a politician, and the tindera giving you your change. It's about not having a secret second family, not pocketing the people's money, and not shortchanging someone on their sukli. Basically, it's the adult version of not cheating on a test.
usage_notes: A core value in Filipino culture, emphasizing integrity in personal and professional relationships. The source 'pagiging-matapat' is sometimes hyphenated for clarity, but is more commonly written as two words.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagiging matapat** ay pundasyon ng tiwala.","translation":"**Honesty** is the foundation of trust."},{"sentence":"Iginagalang siya dahil sa kanyang **pagiging matapat** sa kanyang mga kaibigan.","translation":"He is respected for his **loyalty** to his friends."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kahilingan, papuri, o pasasalamat na taimtim na ipinararating sa isang sinasambang diyos o espirituwal na nilalang.
original_explanation: Your direct message (DM) to G (God). It's what you do before a major exam, when your Grab is stuck in EDSA traffic, or when you're hoping your online shopping order arrives on time. It can be a formal "Ama Namin" or a desperate "Lord, sana pumasa ako!" It's your spiritual Wi-Fi connection to the heavens.
usage_notes: `Dasal` is a more common synonym. `Panalangin` often implies a more personal, heartfelt, and specific prayer, while `dasal` can also refer to recited or formulaic prayers.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aking taos-pusong **panalangin** ay para sa kaligtasan ng aking pamilya.","translation":"My heartfelt **prayer** is for the safety of my family."},{"sentence":"Isama mo ako sa iyong mga **panalangin**.","translation":"Include me in your **prayers**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-usad pauna, pag-unlad, o pagpunta sa isang direksyon sa harapan.
original_explanation: The opposite of 'umurong' (to retreat). It's what you tell yourself when you're trying to move on from your ex. 'Sulong lang, besh!' It's also what happens when the jeepney driver finally finds a gap in EDSA traffic. The nation progresses one inch at a time.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit maraming pagsubok, patuloy na **sumulong** ang kanilang negosyo.","translation":"Despite many challenges, their business continued **to advance**."},{"sentence":"**Sumulong** ang mga sundalo patungo sa kampo ng kaaway.","translation":"The soldiers **advanced** towards the enemy camp."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng katawan ng isda at iba pang hayop sa tubig na ginagamit sa paghinga sa ilalim ng tubig.
original_explanation: It's the fish's version of lungs. When you're in the *palengke* buying fish, you check the **hasang** to see if it's fresh. If it's bright red, G! If it's brown and sad-looking, that fish has seen better days, probably like you after a long week of work.
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of fish and marine biology. A key indicator of a fish's freshness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tiningnan niya ang **hasang** ng isda upang matiyak na sariwa pa ito.","translation":"He looked at the fish's **gills** to make sure it was still fresh."},{"sentence":"Ang mga isda ay humihinga sa pamamagitan ng kanilang **hasang**.","translation":"Fish breathe through their **gills**."}]

translation: to become crumpled; to get wrinkled
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging kulubot o lukot ng isang bagay, karaniwan dahil sa pagkabasa, pagkakapiga, o pagkakakuyom.
original_explanation: 'Yung itsura ng papel na binasa mo tapos piniga. Or your clothes after sleeping in them. Or your soul after a really bad day. 'Yung puso kong lumamukot sa sakit.' This is deep cut Tagalog, pang-Makata level.
usage_notes: A more poetic or intense word for 'kumulubot' or 'nalukot'. Often implies being crumpled due to moisture or strong pressure.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa ulan, **lumamukot** ang mga papeles na naiwan sa labas.","translation":"Because of the rain, the papers left outside **became crumpled**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang relihiyon at pilosopiya na nagmula sa India na batay sa mga aral ni Siddhartha Gautama, na kilala bilang Buddha.
original_explanation: The religion and philosophy that gave us concepts like karma, reincarnation, and the ultimate life goal of achieving 'zen'. It's about finding inner peace, which is what we all desperately need after being stuck in EDSA traffic.
usage_notes: Capitalized as it is a proper noun referring to a religion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **Budismo** ay isa sa mga pangunahing relihiyon sa Asya.","translation":"**Buddhism** is one of the major religions in Asia."},{"sentence":"Marami siyang natutunan tungkol sa **Budismo** sa kanyang paglalakbay sa Thailand.","translation":"He learned a lot about **Buddhism** during his trip to Thailand."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang datu ng Mactan na kinikilalang unang bayaning Pilipino dahil sa kanyang paglaban at pagpaslang kay Ferdinand Magellan sa Labanan sa Mactan noong 1521.
original_explanation: The OG Filipino action star. Before Rambo, before John Wick, there was **Lapulapo**. He saw foreigners arriving uninvited on his beach and his response was basically 'Not on my watch.' The ultimate symbol of 'know your boundaries' and Philippine resistance.
usage_notes: Always capitalized as it is a proper name. He is the reason we have a holiday, and also the reason a delicious fish is named after him.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si **Lapulapo** ang kauna-unahang bayani ng Pilipinas.","translation":"**Lapulapu** is the very first hero of the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Ipinagdiriwang ang Araw ng Mactan upang gunitain ang tagumpay ni **Lapulapo**.","translation":"Mactan Day is celebrated to commemorate the victory of **Lapulapu**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng makapal at matigas na papel na karaniwang ginagamit sa paggawa ng mga kahon at iba pang lalagyan.
original_explanation: The ultimate multi-purpose material. It's the box for your online shopping delivery, the 'bed' when you need to sleep on the floor ('higang-karton'), and the main component of every kid's school project diorama.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ilagay mo ang mga lumang libro sa **karton** na iyan.","translation":"Put the old books in that **cardboard** box."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niyang panlatag ang isang pirasong **karton**.","translation":"He used a piece of **cardboard** as a mat."}]

translation: to mix, to add in, to blend
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasama ng isang sangkap sa iba pang mga bagay upang makabuo ng pinag-isang kabuuan.
original_explanation: The core instruction for making halo-halo, pancit, or any ulam that requires mixing things in a pan. It means 'to mix in.' But also used for people: 'Huwag mo akong ihalo sa gulo nila!' (Don't mix me up in their drama!). It’s about adding something to an existing mix.
usage_notes: A fundamental verb in cooking and also used metaphorically in social situations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ihalo** mo ang itlog sa harina.","translation":"**Mix** the egg into the flour."},{"sentence":"Sinabi niya sa akin na huwag daw akong **ihalo** sa kanilang problema.","translation":"He told me not to be **mixed** in with their problem."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkapanalo o pagtatagumpay sa isang laban, kompetisyon, o pagsubok.
original_explanation: The feeling when your crush finally notices you. Yung moment na "Panalo!" ka sa contest. O yung pakiramdam kapag ikaw ang nanalo sa argument niyo ng kapatid mo. **Wagi** is your victory pose moment. It's the fist pump, the happy dance, the "sa wakas!" sigh of relief and triumph. In short, #Wagi! #Slay!
usage_notes: Madalas ding gamitin bilang pang-uri (victorious).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinaas ng boksingero ang kanyang mga kamay bilang tanda ng kanyang pagka-**wagi**.","translation":"The boxer raised his hands as a sign of his **victory**."},{"sentence":"**Wagi** ang pambato ng Pilipinas sa katatapos na beauty pageant.","translation":"The Philippines' representative was **victorious** in the recently concluded beauty pageant."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa posisyong hindi tuwid o nakahilig sa isang gilid.
etymology: From `tagilid` (tilted, askew). `Naka-` indicates the resulting state.
original_explanation: Ito yung picture frame sa pader na konting-konti lang ang pagkaka-tilt pero sapat na para ma-trigger ang O.C. mo. O kaya yung jeep na dumaan, sobrang puno, **nakatagilid** na sa dami ng sakay. Pwede ring ikaw 'pag may kausap kang 'di mo bet, **nakatagilid** lang ulo mo habang nag-iisip ng escape plan.
usage_notes: Can also be used metaphorically to mean being in a precarious or disadvantageous situation (e.g., `tagilid sa negosyo` - the business is in trouble).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayusin mo ang litrato, **nakatagilid**.","translation":"Fix the picture, it's **tilted**."},{"sentence":"Maingat niyang ibinaba ang baso na **nakatagilid** sa gilid ng mesa.","translation":"He carefully put down the glass that was **sideways** at the edge of the table."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aalis o pagbabawas ng halaga, importansya, o kahulugan ng isang bagay, ideya, o damdamin.
etymology: From pag- (nominalizer) + pa- (causative) + walang-kabuluhan (meaningless). Lit. 'the act of making something meaningless'.
original_explanation: Yung ginagawa mo sa feelings ng ex mo by posting 'Thank u, next' memes. It's the art of making a big deal seem like no deal at all. 'Di ka minahal? 'Pagpapawalang-kabuluhan' mo lang 'yan, sis!
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of emotions, ideas, or efforts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapawalang-kabuluhan** sa kanyang mga sakripisyo ay labis na masakit.","translation":"The **trivialization** of his sacrifices is extremely painful."},{"sentence":"Itigil mo ang **pagpapawalang-kabuluhan** sa mga alalahanin ko.","translation":"Stop **making my concerns meaningless**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na pagkain na kinakain sa kalagitnaan ng gabi, karaniwan ay matapos ang hapunan at bago matulog o kapag nagising sa hatinggabi.
original_explanation: The reward you give yourself for surviving the day. Ito yung instant noodles, tirang kanin na may itlog, o yung biskwit na tinatago mo sa drawer mo. The reason why your diet starts "tomorrow." It's not a meal, it's a "secret happy moment."
usage_notes: A very common phrase used directly in Taglish.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tara, magluto tayo ng pancit canton para sa ating **midnight snack**.","translation":"Come on, let's cook some pancit canton for our **midnight snack**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tao na nakasakay sa likuran ng nagmamaneho ng motorsiklo, bisikleta, o kabayo. Tumutukoy din sa mismong gawain ng pagsakay sa likuran.
original_explanation: "Angkas" is your human backpack when you're on a two-wheeled vehicle. It's also the name of the ride-hailing app that became a verb: "Mag-Angkas na lang tayo para iwas-traffic!" Having an "angkas" means you're responsible for another life, so you drive extra carefully... unless you're trying to get to the airport in 15 minutes. It's the ultimate trust fall, but at 60 kph.
usage_notes: Can refer to the person riding at the back or the act itself. Now heavily associated with the ride-hailing service "Angkas". The verb is 'umangkas'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bawal ang dalawang **angkas** sa iisang motorsiklo.","translation":"Two **back-ride passengers** on a single motorcycle are not allowed."},{"sentence":"Kumapit ka nang mabuti, ikaw ang **angkas** ko.","translation":"Hold on tight, you are my **back-ride passenger**."}]

translation: to have something reduced or lessened
meaning_filipino: Ang paghiling o pagiging sanhi na bawasan ang dami, halaga, o tindi ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the official verb for "pahingi ng discount." When you're at the palengke and you ask the tindera, "Ate, wala na bang bawas?" you're essentially asking her to *magpabawa* ng presyo. It's the art of the haggle, or asking your boss to lessen your workload.
usage_notes: `Bawa` is less common than `bawas`, but `magpabawa` is used interchangeably with `magpabawas`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **magpabawa** sa bayarin sa kuryente sa pamamagitan ng pagtitipid.","translation":"He tried to **have the electricity bill reduced** by saving energy."},{"sentence":"**Nagpabawa** siya ng dalang bagahe para hindi mag-excess baggage.","translation":"She **had the weight of her luggage reduced** so as not to have excess baggage."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-aanunsyo o paglalathala ng impormasyon sa publiko, karaniwan sa pamamagitan ng midya.
etymology: From pag- (nominalizer) + pa- (causative prefix) + talastas (aware, known).
original_explanation: This is the act of putting something on blast for everyone to know. It's making an announcement, like when a company posts a job opening, or a brand launches a new commercial (the one you always skip on YouTube). It's basically shouting 'Hey, look at this!' to the world, but in a more formal, organized way.
usage_notes: A formal term for public announcements or advertisements. 'Patalastas' is the noun for the announcement/ad itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ahensya ay gumastos ng malaki para sa **pagpapatalastas** ng kanilang bagong produkto.","translation":"The agency spent a lot on **advertising** their new product."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **pagpapatalastas** ng mga pampublikong paalala sa panahon ng kalamidad.","translation":"The **act of announcing** public advisories is important during calamities."}]

meaning_filipino: Pormal na isumbong sa kinauukulan, lalo na ang isang krimen o ilegal na gawain.
etymology: From i- (object focus prefix) + pag- + suplong (denunciation).
original_explanation: This is the more formal, serious cousin of `ipagsumbong`. You don't ipagsuplong someone for stealing your pen. You ipagsuplong them for tax evasion or running a syndicate. It's whistleblowing. It has the weight of bringing down a whole operation, not just getting someone grounded.
usage_notes: A formal term, often used in legal, news, or historical contexts. It is a stronger synonym for 'isumbong' and implies reporting a serious crime or act of betrayal to the authorities.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tungkulin nating **ipagsuplong** sa mga awtoridad ang anumang katiwalian.","translation":"It is our duty to **report** any corruption to the authorities."},{"sentence":"Takot siyang **ipagsuplong** ang kanyang amo dahil sa mga banta nito.","translation":"He is afraid to **denounce** his boss because of his threats."}]

translation: to bellow, to howl, to moo
meaning_filipino: Maglabas ng isang malakas, malalim, at humahabang tunog, katulad ng sa baka o kalabaw; umiyak nang malakas at walang pigil.
original_explanation: This is not your cute, silent cry. This is the ugly cry. Yung parang kalabaw na nawalan ng anak. It's a loud, deep, gut-wrenching sound of crying or shouting, full of pain or anger. Think of a toddler's epic tantrum in the mall.
usage_notes: Used for the sound animals like cows/carabaos make, or for a very loud, deep human cry.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umatungal** sa iyak ang bata nang hindi makuha ang gusto niyang laruan.","translation":"The child **bellowed** in tears when he couldn't get the toy he wanted."},{"sentence":"Rinig sa buong bukid nang **umatungal** ang kalabaw.","translation":"The carabao was heard to **bellow** throughout the entire field."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang pagpapabalam o pagpapahinto sa isang gawain, proseso, o pag-alis ng isang tao.
original_explanation: What EDSA traffic does to your life every single day. It's what happens when your friend says 'On the way na!' but they're still in the shower. To intentionally cause a delay, like when a government office tells you to 'come back tomorrow' for a form that was ready today.
usage_notes: Object-focused verb. The root word 'antala' means delay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo sanang **antalahin** ang aming pag-alis.","translation":"I hope you don't **delay** our departure."},{"sentence":"In**antala** ng masamang panahon ang biyahe ng barko.","translation":"The bad weather **delayed** the ship's voyage."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng damit na isinusuot o nagsisilbing takip para sa braso.
original_explanation: The part of your shirt that covers your arms. Can be 'long-sleeved' for the office aircon or BPO night shift, 'short-sleeved' for the everyday Pinoy climate, or 'sleeveless' (walang manggas) for the beach. Also, a place to hide things, like a kodigo during an exam. 'May alas ka sa iyong manggas' means you have a hidden advantage.
usage_notes: A very common word in clothing and fashion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko ang damit na iyan, pero mas mahaba sana ang **manggas**.","translation":"I like that dress, but I wish the **sleeves** were longer."},{"sentence":"Itinupi niya ang **manggas** ng kanyang polo bago magtrabaho.","translation":"He rolled up the **sleeves** of his shirt before working."}]

translation: act of poking or nudging lightly
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng bahagyang pagdantay o pagtulak gamit ang daliri o anumang matulis na bagay upang makuha ang atensyon.
original_explanation: This is the OG "seen-zone" bypass. Before DMs, there was the pagkuhit. It's that gentle poke you give your friend to point out some chismis, or the subtle nudge to your sibling at the dinner table to pass the adobo. It's the physical version of a notification ping.
usage_notes: A very specific action, usually done to get someone's attention discreetly.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang magaan na **pagkuhit** sa braso ang ginawa niya para tawagin ako.","translation":"She gave a light **poke** on my arm to call me."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman ko ang **pagkuhit** ng bata sa laylayan ng aking damit.","translation":"I felt the child's **tugging/poking** at the hem of my dress."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malubhang sakit sa bituka na nakukuha sa kontaminadong pagkain o tubig, na nagdudulot ng matinding pagtatae at dehydration.
original_explanation: This is a serious disease, no hugot here. Parang 'yung friend mo na laging sinasabihan, "Hugas-hugas din ng kamay 'pag may time!" at "Don't drink the water!" lalo na sa mga lugar na 'di sigurado. Getting kolera is a major health crisis.
usage_notes: A medical term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng epidemya ng **kolera** sa lugar dahil sa maruming tubig.","translation":"There was a **cholera** epidemic in the area due to contaminated water."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-inom ng malinis na tubig ay panlaban sa **kolera**.","translation":"Drinking clean water is a defense against **cholera**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging sapat o tama lamang; hindi labis at hindi kulang.
etymology: From 'taman' (an archaic word for 'just right' or 'moderate') + 'ka- -an' affix group. It is the root of the more common word 'katamtaman'.
original_explanation: The Goldilocks principle. Not too much, not too little, just enough. It's having 'sakto lang' na sahod, 'sakto lang' na feelings for someone (para hindi masaktan), or 'sakto lang' na kanin. The art of 'pwede na 'yan.'
usage_notes: A very formal and rare word. 'Katamtaman' is the everyday equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **katamanan** sa pagkain upang maging malusog.","translation":"**Moderation** in eating is important to be healthy."},{"sentence":"Sa **katamanan** ng kanyang kita, simple lang ang kanyang pamumuhay.","translation":"With the **sufficiency** of his income, his lifestyle is simple."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong ang trabaho ay maghatid ng mga produkto, pagkain, o dokumento sa mga customer gamit ang motorsiklo o iba pang sasakyan.
original_explanation: Sila ang mga modern-day superheroes na sumusuong sa traffic at sama ng panahon para lang ma-receive mo na ang inorder mong milk tea o crispy pata. Tip your rider, bes! Sila ang dahilan kung bakit hindi ka nagugutom habang WFH.
usage_notes: Commonly used in the Philippines to refer to couriers for services like GrabFood, FoodPanda, Lalamove, etc.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumating na ba 'yung **delivery rider** na may dala ng inorder kong pagkain?","translation":"Has the **delivery rider** with the food I ordered arrived?"},{"sentence":"Bigyan mo ng tip 'yung **delivery rider**, ang lakas ng ulan.","translation":"Give the **delivery rider** a tip, the rain is really strong."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang patuloy at hindi matatag na paggalaw o paggewang-gewang; mas matindi at paulit-ulit na bersyon ng 'gumiray'.
original_explanation: This is 'gumiray' on steroids. It's not just one wobble; it's a whole series of them. Think of a Jenga tower seconds before it collapses. Or that feeling when you're on a bus driven by a Fast & Furious wannabe on a bumpy provincial road.
usage_notes: A reduplicated form of 'gumiray' that emphasizes the continuous or severe nature of the wobbling. This is the completed aspect (past tense).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **gumiray-giray** ang tulay na kawayan habang tumatawid kami.","translation":"The bamboo bridge started to **wobble unstably** as we were crossing."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng lindol, **gumiray-giray** ang mga gusali bago tuluyang huminto sa pag-uga.","translation":"After the earthquake, the buildings **swayed continuously** before finally stopping."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking uri ng artilerya o armas na nagpapaputok ng malalaking bala o projectile sa malalayong distansya.
original_explanation: Think old-school warfare, like the ones you see in Intramuros pointing out to sea. It's a giant gun. Nowadays, you might hear 'pang-kanyon' to describe something really powerful or explosive, like a spicy Bicol Express or your friend's angry rant. 'Kanyon ng baril' specifically means 'barrel of a gun'.
usage_notes: Ang pariralang 'kanyon ng baril' ay isang partikular na paggamit na tumutukoy sa mahabang tubo ng isang baril, isang metaporikal na pagpapalawig mula sa hugis ng isang kanyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga lumang **kanyon** sa Corregidor ay paalala ng kasaysayan ng digmaan.","translation":"The old **cannons** in Corregidor are a reminder of the history of war."},{"sentence":"Nilinis niya ang **kanyon** ng kanyang riple.","translation":"He cleaned the **barrel** of his rifle."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalapat ng init at bigat gamit ang plantsa upang mapatag o mapakinis ang isang bagay, tulad ng damit. Isang di-pangkaraniwang katumbas ng 'plantsahin'.
etymology: Mula sa salitang 'prinsa', na galing sa Espanyol na 'prensa' (press).
original_explanation: This is what you do to your school uniform the night before, or more realistically, 5 minutes before you leave the house. `Prinsahan` mo yung gusot para di ka mukhang tinakasan ng plantsa. It's the verb form of giving your clothes that crisp, 'bagong laba' look, but it's the more old-school term compared to 'plantsahin'.
usage_notes: A much more common term is 'plantsahin'. 'Prinsahan' is considered rare or archaic in many regions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Prinsahan** mo nga itong polo ko para sa interbyu ko bukas.","translation":"Please **iron** this polo shirt of mine for my interview tomorrow."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kuwento ng pag-iibigan na puno ng masidhing damdamin at kababalaghan, o isang relasyon na may matinding pagmamahalan.
original_explanation: This is the 'kilig' factor dialed up to 11. It's the stuff of K-dramas, Wattpad stories, and that one couple in the office who are so sweet it makes you sick. It's the whole 'sana all' package: harana, flowers, dramatic confessions in the rain, and maybe a little bit of 'Marites'-worthy drama.
usage_notes: Can refer to a love affair or a genre of literature/film.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang magbasa ng mga librong tungkol sa **romansa**.","translation":"She loves to read books about **romance**."},{"sentence":"Nagtapos na ang kanilang maikling **romansa**.","translation":"Their short **romance** has ended."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bahagi na pinutol mula sa isang kabuuan. Ginagamit din bilang metaporikal na tawag sa kapatid.
original_explanation: Literally, "a piece of." Like a "kaputol" of cake or a "kaputol" of wire for your DIY project. But in true Filipino fashion, we made it dramatic and use it to mean "sibling"—because they're a piece of you, or more accurately, a piece of your parents' patience that's now gone.
usage_notes: The meaning of "sibling" is more poetic or formal. "Kapatid" is the everyday term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pahingi naman ng **kaputol** na litson.","translation":"Can I have a **piece** of the roasted pig?"},{"sentence":"Itinuturing niyang tunay na **kaputol** ang kaniyang matalik na kaibigan.","translation":"She considers her best friend a true **sibling**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar na pansamantalang tinitirhan o tinutuluyan, na maaaring may bayad o wala, at kadalasa'y ipinagkaloob ng iba.
etymology: From pa- (locative prefix, 'place for') + tira (to live/stay) + -han (locative suffix).
original_explanation: Not quite your forever home. It's the Airbnb, the boarding house, the 'makikitulog muna ako sa inyo' spot. It’s a place to crash, whether you're a BPO agent renting a bedspace near the office or a probinsyano relative staying over for a month. It implies it's a place provided for you to stay in.
usage_notes: Distinct from 'tirahan' (residence), as 'patirahan' often implies a more temporary or provided lodging, like a shelter or dormitory.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-aalok ang kumpanya ng libreng **patirahan** para sa mga empleyado nito mula sa malalayong probinsya.","translation":"The company offers free **lodging** for its employees from distant provinces."}]

meaning_filipino: Naaayon sa eksakto at pangunahing kahulugan ng salita, nang walang pagtatalinghaga o idyoma.
original_explanation: When you tell your friend "Patay ako nito," because you forgot your assignment, and they start checking your pulse. They took you 'literal'. It's the opposite of figurative, the no-frills, no-hugot, "what you see is what you get" meaning of something. It's the ultimate "walang malisya" mode of interpretation.
usage_notes: Often used in Taglish sentences to emphasize that one is not exaggerating. For example, "Literal na bumaha sa loob ng bahay."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **literal** na kahulugan ng \"balat-sibuyas\" ay balat ng sibuyas, hindi isang taong maramdamin.","translation":"The **literal** meaning of \"balat-sibuyas\" is onion skin, not a sensitive person."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kunin sa **literal** na paraan ang lahat ng sinasabi ko; minsan, nagbibiro lang ako.","translation":"Don't take everything I say in a **literal** way; sometimes, I'm just joking."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging marupok, malutong, at madaling mabali o madurog.
original_explanation: This is the defining quality of your favorite chicharon or crispy pata. That satisfying crunch. It's also the quality of dried leaves, old plastic, or my patience on a Monday morning. One wrong move, and it shatters.
usage_notes: Used to describe the physical property of being brittle or crispy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubok niya ang **pagkalutos** ng bagong gawang kropek.","translation":"She tested the **crispiness** of the newly made crackers."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi pantay o tuwid; nakahilig o nakatagilid.
etymology: Possibly related to Spanish 'al bies' (on the bias, askew).
original_explanation: That feeling when you try to hang a picture frame and no matter what you do, it's just not straight. Or when you cut your own bangs and one side is higher than the other. "Ay, naging aldabis yung gupit!" It's the aesthetic of 'almost there, but not quite'.
usage_notes: Describes something that is not level or vertically/horizontally aligned. Synonymous with 'tabingi'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **aldabis** ang pagkakakabit ng salamin sa dingding.","translation":"The mirror was hung **askew** on the wall."},{"sentence":"Napansin niyang **aldabis** ang pagkakatayo ng poste.","translation":"He noticed that the post was standing **slanted**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang baryasyon sa pagbaybay ng salitang 'resina'. Tumutukoy sa malagkit na sangkap mula sa halaman o sa sintetikong bersyon nito na ginagamit sa mga craft.
original_explanation: The more common, English-based spelling you'll see on Shopee and Lazada for those DIY keychain or coaster kits. It's the same as 'resina', but this one sounds more... industrial and less probinsya.
usage_notes: This spelling is preferred in modern, informal contexts, especially online and in hobbyist circles. See 'resina' for the traditional term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkano ang isang set ng epoxy **resin** para sa mga baguhan?","translation":"How much is one set of epoxy **resin** for beginners?"},{"sentence":"Nag-order ako ng **resin** art kit online.","translation":"I ordered a **resin** art kit online."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang kilos o pagbabago na biglaan, malubha, o may matinding epekto.
original_explanation: Ito ang formal version ni 'drastik'. 'Yung pagtaas ng presyo ng bilihin, hindi lang basta pagtaas, kundi **drastiko**ng pagtaas. O 'yung pagbaba ng grades mo from 95 to 75, **drastiko** 'yun. Ito 'yung salitang ginagamit kapag gusto mong sabihing 'sobra' pero gusto mo ring mag-tunog matalino.
usage_notes: Mas pormal kaysa sa 'drastik'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinakailangan ng **drastiko**ng aksyon upang masugpo ang pagkalat ng sakit.","translation":"**Drastic** action is needed to stop the spread of the disease."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng diplomatiko na may pinakamataas na ranggo na ipinadadala ng isang bansa bilang opisyal na kinatawan nito sa isang banyagang bansa.
original_explanation: She's the ultimate Tita of the nation abroad. The female boss-level diplomat who represents the country with grace, intelligence, and probably a killer Filipiniana gown at state dinners.
usage_notes: Ang pambabaeng katawagan para sa isang embahador. Ang panlalaki ay 'embahador'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinalaga si Ginang Cruz bilang bagong **embahadora** ng Pilipinas sa Japan.","translation":"Mrs. Cruz was appointed as the new **ambassadress** of the Philippines to Japan."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto o proseso ng pagbibigay ng detalyadong impormasyon tungkol sa anyo, katangian, o kalagayan ng isang tao, bagay, lugar, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is your best friend hyping you up to their other friends. Or when you're trying to describe a meme to your parents who just don't get it. It's painting a picture with words. "Yung pagsasalarawan mo sa crush mo, parang perpekto. Sa personal, di pala."
usage_notes: A key term in literature and communication.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malinaw ang kanyang **pagsasalarawan** sa mga nangyari noong gabing iyon.","translation":"Her **description** of what happened that night was clear."},{"sentence":"Ang mahusay na **pagsasalarawan** ay mahalaga sa pagsulat ng maikling kuwento.","translation":"A good **portrayal** is important in writing a short story."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nangangakong managot sa pagbabayad ng utang o pagtupad sa isang obligasyon ng ibang tao kung sakaling hindi ito magawa ng pangunahing may-utang.
original_explanation: The official 'salo' person. Ito 'yung kaibigan mong pinakiusapan mong maging co-maker sa loan mo, tapos ngayon pareho na kayong ninenerbyos pag malapit na ang due date. Sila ang fall guy, the backup plan, the 'in case of emergency, break glass' person for financial obligations.
usage_notes: Primarily used in legal and financial contexts, such as loans and contracts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mo ng **garantisador** para maaprubahan ang iyong housing loan.","translation":"You need a **guarantor** for your housing loan to be approved."}]

translation: to be left speechless; to be at a loss for words
meaning_filipino: Isang idyomatikong pahayag na nangangahulugang hindi makapagsalita o makatugon, karaniwan dahil sa matinding pagkabigla, pagkagulat, o paghanga.
etymology: Idiomatic phrase: ma- (to experience) + tuyo (dry) + -an (locative) + ng (of) + laway (saliva).
original_explanation: Literally 'to have your saliva dry up.' This is what happens when you see your crush in person and they're 10x more gorgeous than their profile pic. Your brain short-circuits, your mouth goes dry, and all you can do is stare like a malfunctioning robot. Also applicable when you see the bill after a fancy dinner.
usage_notes: A very expressive idiom for being stunned into silence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halos **matuyuan ako ng laway** nang makita ko ang presyo ng bagong iPhone.","translation":"I was almost **left speechless** when I saw the price of the new iPhone."},{"sentence":"Sa sobrang ganda ng tanawin, lahat kami ay **natuyuan ng laway**.","translation":"The view was so beautiful, we were all **at a loss for words**."}]

translation: to have one's ear pulled; to get one's ear twisted
meaning_filipino: Makaranas ng paghila o pagpilipit sa tainga bilang isang paraan ng pagpaparusa o pagbibirong may kasamang pananakit.
etymology: From ma- (potential/involuntary action prefix) + pingol (act of pulling the ear).
original_explanation: The OG Filipino disciplinary action, pre-palo and pre-sinturon. This is what happens when your nanay or lola catches you stealing a piece of fried chicken before dinner. It's a quick, sharp reminder of who's boss. "Isa pang 'di pag-uwi nang maaga, mapipingol ka sa akin!"
usage_notes: This is a very specific verb related to a common form of physical punishment or jest in Filipino culture.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kapag hindi ka tumigil sa kakalaro, **mapipingol** ka ng tatay mo.","translation":"If you don't stop playing, you'll **get your ear pulled** by your father."},{"sentence":"**Napingol** ako dahil nahuli akong hindi natutulog sa tanghali.","translation":"I **had my ear twisted** because I was caught not taking a noon nap."}]

translation: to happen in the blink of an eye; to be able to blink
meaning_filipino: Mabilis na pagpikit at pagdilat ng mga mata; tumukoy sa isang pangyayaring naganap sa sandaling iglap.
original_explanation: Parang sweldo mo lang. Pagdating sa palad mo, hindi ka pa halos **napakakurap**, ubos na agad pambayad ng bills at Shopee checkouts. It describes something that happens so fast, you barely had time to process it.
usage_notes: Can be used literally (to blink) but more often used figuratively to mean 'in an instant'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa isang **pagkurap** lang, natangay na ng magnanakaw ang kanyang bag.","translation":"In just a **blink of an eye**, the thief had already snatched her bag."},{"sentence":"Sa sobrang pagod, hindi na siya halos **mapakurap** habang nagmamaneho.","translation":"From extreme fatigue, he could barely **keep his eyes open (blink)** while driving."}]

meaning_filipino: Magkakaroon ng kakayahang hindi na maalala ang isang bagay, tao, o pangyayari sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: The theme of 90% of hugot songs. It's the future tense of moving on. You tell yourself 'Balang araw, makakalimot din ako,' while scrolling through their profile for the 17th time today. It's the promise of future amnesia for a present heartache.
usage_notes: This is the future tense of `makalimot` (to be able to forget).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paano ako **makakalimot** kung lagi siyang nagpaparamdam?","translation":"How **will I be able to forget** if he/she always makes their presence felt?"},{"sentence":"Darating ang araw na **makakalimot** ka rin sa sakit na naramdaman mo.","translation":"The day will come when you **will be able to forget** the pain you felt."}]

translation: act of opening a book; turning a page
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbubukas ng isang aklat, magasin, o anumang may mga pahina.
etymology: From pag- (gerund prefix) + buklat (to open/turn pages).
original_explanation: The satisfying sound and feeling of opening a new book or flipping through a magazine at a doctor's office. It's the 'scroll down' of the analog world. Every time you open a book to find a specific page or just to start reading, that's 'pagbuklat'.
usage_notes: Specific to books, magazines, notebooks, and other items with pages.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa isang **pagbuklat** niya ng aklat, nakita niya ang isang lumang litrato.","translation":"In one **turn of the book's page**, he/she saw an old photograph."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siya sa **pagbuklat** ng mga lumang dyaryo sa silid-aklatan.","translation":"He/She loves the **act of opening/browsing through** old newspapers in the library."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangkalahatang komunidad ng mga tao; ang mamamayan sa kabuuan.
original_explanation: The 'madlang people'. Sila yung laging pinapasaya ni Vice Ganda, yung kailangan mong harapin kapag mag-cocommute ka, at yung laging may opinyon sa lahat ng bagay sa social media. The ultimate judge, jury, and 'Marites' rolled into one.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bukas sa **publiko** ang bagong tayong parke.","translation":"The newly built park is open to **the public**."}]

translation: to cut down, to chop off
meaning_filipino: Ang pagputol sa isang bagay, karaniwan ay halaman o sanga, sa pamamagitan ng isang matalim na kasangkapan tulad ng itak o machete.
original_explanation: This is what you do to tall grass (talahib) or sugarcane with a single, swift strike of a bolo. Imagine a warrior in a Filipino epic, **tumagpas** siya ng ulo ng kalaban. It's a very decisive, powerful cut. Not a delicate snip, but a full-on hack.
usage_notes: Completed aspect (past tense). Infinitive: tumagpas, Progressive: tumatagpas, Contemplative: tatagpas. Often implies a swift, single-stroke action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumagpas** siya ng mga sanga na nakaharang sa daan.","translation":"He **chopped off** the branches blocking the path."},{"sentence":"Isang malakas na hampas lang at **tumagpas** ang kawayan.","translation":"Just one strong strike and the bamboo was **cut down**."}]

translation: person one has a deal with; contracting party
meaning_filipino: Ang tao na kabilang sa isang kasunduan, kontrata, o transaksyon.
etymology: Mula sa "ka-" (nagpapahiwatig ng pagiging kasosyo) + "trato" (kasunduan, mula sa Espanyol na "trato").
original_explanation: This is the person on the other end of a deal. It could be the person you're buying a pre-loved item from on Carousell, the business partner for your milk tea franchise dream, or even just the friend you have a "no-spoilers" pact with for a new series. It's all about the agreement.
usage_notes: Maaari ding gamitin upang tumukoy sa isang taong may romantikong (ngunit hindi kinakailangang pormal) relasyon, bagaman ito ay hindi gaanong karaniwan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, mapagkakatiwalaan ang **katrato** natin sa negosyo.","translation":"Don't worry, the person we have a **deal** with in our business is trustworthy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong nag-aaral, nagsusulat, at dalubhasa sa kasaysayan. Maaari ring tumukoy sa isang tagapagsalaysay ng isang kuwento.
etymology: Mula sa `mang-` + `salaysay` (narrative). Ang `mang-` ay nagiging `manan-` at inuulit ang unang pantig ng salitang-ugat.
original_explanation: The OG storyteller. Sila 'yung nag-aaral ng mga "resibo" ng nakaraan para hindi na maulit ang mga epic fail ng history. Kung sa tropa, sila 'yung laging may "Alam niyo ba..." na intro. Think Ambeth Ocampo.
usage_notes: Maaaring mangahulugang "historian" sa pormal na konteksto o "narrator" sa pangkalahatang gamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayon sa mga **mananalaysay**, malaki ang naging papel ng mga kababaihan sa rebolusyon.","translation":"According to **historians**, women played a significant role in the revolution."},{"sentence":"Ang lolo ko ang **mananalaysay** ng aming pamilya, alam niya lahat ng kuwento.","translation":"My grandfather is the **narrator** of our family, he knows all the stories."}]

meaning_filipino: Inilalarawan ang isang tao na namumuhay sa karangyaan, kapangyarihan, o paggalang na tulad ng sa isang monarko.
original_explanation: How you feel when your 13th-month pay comes in. You walk into the mall **parang hari**, ready to buy everything, until you check your bank account the next day. Also describes someone who expects to be served hand and foot.
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang ilarawan ang isang marangyang pamumuhay o isang presensya na puno ng awtoridad at paggalang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang buhay niya ay **parang hari** mula nang manalo siya sa lotto.","translation":"His life is **like a king's** since he won the lottery."},{"sentence":"Kung umasta siya ay **parang hari** na dapat laging sundin.","translation":"He acts **like a king** who must always be obeyed."}]

meaning_filipino: Katumbas ng bilang na isandaan (100); isang daan.
etymology: Mula sa 'isang' at 'gatos', na hango sa salitang Espanyol na 'cientos' (hundreds). Isang varyant ng 'sandaan'.
original_explanation: What your pamasahe feels like during surge pricing. Also the grade you tell your parents you got, even if it was really a 75. A classic palengke term. 'Sanggatos na lang po, suki!'
usage_notes: Hindi kasing-karaniwan ng 'sandaan' ngunit malawakang naiintindihan, lalo na sa mga palengke o ng mga nakatatandang tagapagsalita.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigyan mo ako ng **sanggatos** na halaga ng bawang.","translation":"Give me **one hundred** pesos' worth of garlic."},{"sentence":"May utang pa siyang **sanggatos** sa akin.","translation":"He still owes me **one hundred**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-ugoy, pag-uga, o biglaang paggalaw ng isang bagay na nakabitin o hindi matatag.
original_explanation: The sudden sway or jolt. Imagine riding a jeepney that suddenly brakes—that's an 'abyog'. Or a hammock swinging a little too fast. It's the motion that makes you grab onto something for dear life. It can also describe the swing of a dancer's hips.
usage_notes: Often describes a sudden, sometimes violent, swinging motion. Not a very common word in urban areas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman namin ang malakas na **abyog** ng tulay nang dumaan ang malaking trak.","translation":"We felt the strong **sway** of the bridge when the big truck passed."},{"sentence":"Sa isang **abyog** ng kanyang balakang, nakuha niya ang atensyon ng lahat.","translation":"With one **sway** of her hips, she got everyone's attention."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na mabigat na kailangang buhatin o dalhin, literal man o metaporikal, tulad ng problema, responsibilidad, o tungkulin.
etymology: From `pasan` (to carry on the shoulder) + `-in` (noun-forming suffix).
original_explanation: This is the feeling when you're the panganay and a.k.a. the family retirement plan. It's the weight of your family's expectations, your unli-rice guilt, and your 10-year loan all rolled into one. It's not just a backpack; it's a spiritual backpack of 'utang na loob' and bills.
usage_notes: Very commonly used metaphorically to describe life's difficulties or responsibilities.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bawat isa ay may kani-kaniyang **pasanin** sa buhay.","translation":"Each person has their own **burdens** in life."},{"sentence":"Malaking **pasanin** sa kanya ang pag-aaral ng kanyang mga kapatid.","translation":"Sending his siblings to school is a great **responsibility** for him."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nag-aaral o nagsasanay ng astrolohiya, ang pag-aaral ng di-umano'y impluwensya ng mga bituin at planeta sa buhay at kapalaran ng tao.
original_explanation: The person your Tita consults before making any major life decision, from business ventures to the best date for a wedding. They're the original life coaches, but with more flair and cosmic charts. They read your fate in the stars, which is basically the ancient version of checking your daily horoscope on an app.
usage_notes: The person who practices 'astrolohia'. Not to be confused with an 'astronomo' (astronomer), who is a scientist.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpakonsulta si Aling Nena sa isang **astrologo** para sa kanyang kapalaran ngayong taon.","translation":"Aling Nena consulted an **astrologer** for her fortune this year."},{"sentence":"Ayon sa **astrologo**, magiging maganda ang takbo ng negosyo ko.","translation":"According to the **astrologer**, my business will do well."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkilala o pagtukoy sa pagkakaiba sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang mga bagay, tao, o ideya.
original_explanation: Yung skill na kailangan mo para malaman kung sino ang true friends at sino ang plastic. To 'distinggihin' means to tell things apart. Parang sa trabaho, kailangan mong i-distinguish ang urgent sa important, at sa lovelife, ang 'crush lang' sa 'the one'.
usage_notes: A verb in the object-focus, infinitive form. Often used in formal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **distinggihin** ang kambal dahil sa kanilang sobrang pagkakahawig.","translation":"It's hard **to distinguish** the twins because of their extreme resemblance."},{"sentence":"Dapat nating **distinggihin** ang tama sa mali sa lahat ng ating mga desisyon.","translation":"We must **differentiate** right from wrong in all our decisions."}]

translation: to ride, to get on (a vehicle)
meaning_filipino: Pumasok o umakyat sa isang sasakyan upang maglakbay.
original_explanation: The daily grind of every commuter. Yung tipong makikipagsiksikan ka sa MRT, hahabulin ang jeep na paalis na, o mag-aabang ng Angkas sa gitna ng rush hour. To sumakay is to hop on for a ride. Pwede ring 'sumakay sa trip,' which means to go along with a joke or a plan. 'Bes, sumakay ka na lang sa trip namin!'
usage_notes: Can also be used figuratively to mean 'to go along with' or 'to play along.' The -um- infix indicates a completed action (past tense).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaga siyang **sumakay** ng bus para hindi mahuli sa trabaho.","translation":"He **rode** the bus early so he wouldn't be late for work."},{"sentence":"**Sumakay** na lang ako sa biro niya para hindi na humaba ang usapan.","translation":"I just **played along** with his joke so the conversation wouldn't drag on."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng labis at walang-pakundangang pagnanasa o paglalandi, na maaaring ituring na malaswa o hindi kaaya-aya.
original_explanation: This is the extra, EXTRA level of landi. It's not just cute, subtle flirting. It's the in-your-face, aggressive, "walang preno" kind of flirtation that makes people uncomfortable. Think of it as the difference between a witty DM slide and sending unsolicited "good morning" selfies with a duck face. It's a bit much, bes.
usage_notes: Carries a strong negative connotation. A more intense version of 'malandi'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itigil mo na ang iyong **lantod** na pag-uugali sa harap ng mga bisita.","translation":"Stop your **lewd** behavior in front of the guests."},{"sentence":"Hindi nakakatuwa ang kanyang mga **lantod** na biro.","translation":"His **lascivious** jokes are not funny."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagluto ng bigas upang maging kanin.
original_explanation: The most fundamental life skill for any Filipino, more important than calculus or knowing how to change a tire. It's the sacred ritual of washing rice, measuring the water with your finger joints ('yung daliri method), and praying to the rice cooker gods that it doesn't turn into 'lugaw' (porridge) or 'tutong' (burnt rice). If you don't know how to do this, your Pinoy license is under review.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tamang **pagsaing** ay isang sining.","translation":"The proper **cooking of rice** is an art."},{"sentence":"Ituro mo sa akin ang tamang paraan ng **pagsaing** gamit ang kaldero.","translation":"Teach me the correct way of **cooking rice** using a pot."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o ahensya na nagsisilbing tagapamagitan sa mga transaksyon sa pagitan ng mamimili at nagbebenta, karaniwan para sa isang komisyon.
original_explanation: The middleman. The person who connects Person A with Person B and gets a cut. They sell you real estate, insurance, or stocks. Basically, a professional 'taga-lakad' or 'bridge' who helps you buy things you probably can't afford without them.
usage_notes: Used in business, finance, and real estate contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha kami ng **broker** para tulungan kaming maghanap ng bahay.","translation":"We hired a **broker** to help us find a house."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking pamilihan kung saan ang mga customer ay mismo ang kumukuha ng mga bilihin tulad ng pagkain at mga gamit sa bahay mula sa mga estante bago magbayad sa kahera.
original_explanation: The modern palengke with air-conditioning, shopping carts, and a 10% chance you'll run into a neighbor you're trying to avoid. You go in for one thing (e.g., suka) and come out with a cartful of snacks, toiletries, and that weird imported ice cream. It's where 'add to cart' happens in real life.
usage_notes: A direct loanword from English. Often used interchangeably with 'grocery'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumunta si nanay sa **supermarket** para mamili ng aming pagkain para sa isang linggo.","translation":"Mom went to the **supermarket** to buy our food for the week."},{"sentence":"Mas mahaba ang pila sa **supermarket** tuwing araw ng sahod.","translation":"The lines at the **supermarket** are longer during payday."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng hindi pagkaalala sa isang bagay; ang pagkawala ng isang impormasyon sa isipan.
original_explanation: The official sickness of someone who owes you money. It's why you suddenly remember your report at 11 PM the night before it's due. It's the classic 'hugot' fuel: 'Sana ang pagkalimot sa'yo ay kasing bilis ng pagkalimot ko sa pinag-aralan ko pagkatapos ng exam.' It's the brain's delete button, sometimes convenient, often a disaster.
usage_notes: Can refer to a single act of forgetting or the general state of being forgetful.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang madalas na **pagkalimot** ay maaaring sintomas ng pagod.","translation":"Frequent **forgetfulness** can be a symptom of fatigue."},{"sentence":"Humihingi ako ng tawad sa aking **pagkalimot** sa iyong kaarawan.","translation":"I apologize for my **act of forgetting** your birthday."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking pangkat ng mga sasakyang pandagat, lalo na ng mga barkong pandigma.
original_explanation: Imagine mo yung buong EDSA sa rush hour, pero imbes na kotse, mga barko ng military. O kaya 'yung squad mo 'pag rorolyo sa isang event, 'yun ang 'armada' niyo. It's a show of force, but on water.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa konteksto ng militar, pandagat, o sa paraang pahiwatig para sa isang malaking grupo ng anumang bagay na gumagalaw nang magkakasama.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinadala ng hari ang isang **armada** upang sakupin ang mga kalapit na isla.","translation":"The king sent an **armada** to conquer the nearby islands."},{"sentence":"Tila isang **armada** ng mga food delivery rider ang nasa labas ng condominium.","translation":"It seems like an **armada** of food delivery riders is outside the condominium."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gawain na napakadaling isagawa; mga literal na laro para sa bata.
original_explanation: That task your boss thought was difficult but you finished in 5 minutes. 'Akala mo naman kung ano, **larong-bata** lang pala.' It's the 'Ez' of the corporate world. It means the challenge level is so low, even a kid could do it.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin sa literal na kahulugan (games for children) o sa idyomatikong paraan (an easy task).
