usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para sa isang henyo sa matematika, ang pagsagot sa problemang ito ay **larong-bata** lamang.","translation":"For a math genius, answering this problem is just **child's play**."},{"sentence":"Miss na miss ko na ang mga **larong-bata** tulad ng patintero at piko.","translation":"I really miss **children's games** like patintero and piko."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang tungkulin ay itala o isulat ang mga mahahalagang impormasyon, kaganapan, o datos.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'taga-' (tagagawa), 'pag-' (nagpapangalan), at salitang-ugat na 'tala' (record, list).
original_explanation: The official 'taga-lista' of the group. Sila yung designated human version ng spreadsheet or logbook sa isang meeting, event, or even sa classroom para i-check ang attendance. The secretary, the registrar, the one who takes down minutes.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa mga pormal na konteksto tulad ng mga pagpupulong (kalihim), opisina ng gobyerno (registrar), o sa mga talaang pangkasaysayan (chronicler).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **tagapagtala** ng pulong ang siyang magsusumite ng ulat bukas.","translation":"The **recorder** of the meeting is the one who will submit the report tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Itinalaga si Maria bilang **tagapagtala** ng mga bagong miyembro.","translation":"Maria was assigned as the **registrar** for the new members."}]

translation: to get along with; to be a good sport
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng maganda at maayos na pakikipag-ugnayan sa ibang tao; ang pag-angkop sa kagustuhan ng grupo para sa kaayusan.
etymology: maki- (social verb prefix) + sama (to go with, accompany)
original_explanation: This is a cornerstone of Filipino culture, a.k.a. 'pakikisama.' It's about being a team player, not rocking the boat, and maintaining smooth interpersonal relationships (SIR). When your boss asks you to render OT on a Friday night, and you say yes with a smile (while crying inside), that's pag-marunong kang makisama. It's about going with the flow to keep the peace.
usage_notes: Deeply cultural. It can be positive (being cooperative) or negative (giving in to peer pressure). The noun form 'pakikisama' is a key Filipino social value.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit ayaw mo, **makisama** ka na lang para walang gulo.","translation":"Even if you don't want to, just **go along with it** to avoid trouble."},{"sentence":"Madaling **makisama** si Mario kaya marami siyang kaibigan.","translation":"It's easy **to get along with** Mario, that's why he has many friends."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglikas o pag-alis ng mga tao mula sa isang lugar na may panganib patungo sa isang mas ligtas na lokasyon.
original_explanation: The national sport during typhoon season. When the floodwaters rise or the volcano starts acting up, it's time for pag-eebakwet. It's the organized (or sometimes chaotic) 'Let's get out of here!' moment, usually involving packing your most important belongings: documents, a few clothes, and probably the rice cooker.
usage_notes: This is the noun form for the future/contemplated action of evacuating. 'Paglikas' is the more traditional Tagalog term. 'Pag-ebakweyt' is a common spelling variant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-anunsyo ang alkalde ng agarang **pag-eebakwet** ng mga residenteng malapit sa ilog.","translation":"The mayor announced the immediate **evacuation** of residents near the river."},{"sentence":"Ang plano para sa **pag-eebakwet** ay dapat laging handa.","translation":"The plan for the **evacuation** should always be ready."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na malikot, malandi, o labis kung makipaglaro at makipagbiruan.
original_explanation: The energy of a person who's extra playful, bordering on flirty. It's that friend who can't stop poking you, making silly jokes, or being touchy-feely. Pwedeng playful like a puppy (malikot), or playful with romantic intentions (malandi). 'Ang **harot** mo naman!' can be both an accusation and a term of endearment, depending on who's saying it.
usage_notes: The meaning can shift from innocent playfulness to flirtatiousness depending on the context and tone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan mo nga 'yang pagiging **harot** mo, para kang bata.","translation":"Stop being so **rowdy**, you're like a child."},{"sentence":"Napangiti siya sa **harot** na text ng kanyang manliligaw.","translation":"She smiled at the **flirtatious** text from her suitor."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpigil sa isang tao na makita ang iyong mga post o makipag-ugnayan sa iyo sa isang social media platform o sa pamamagitan ng telepono.
original_explanation: Eto yung ultimate power move mo sa social media kapag toxic na yung ex mo, yung tita mong laging may comment sa itsura mo, o yung online seller na ayaw kang tantanan. One click lang, poof! Hindi ka na nila makikita. Para kang naglagay ng digital harang. 'Peace out, you're blocked!'
usage_notes: Ginagamit nang malawakan sa konteksto ng social media at digital na komunikasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko nang i-**block** ang numerong iyon dahil puro scam text ang natatanggap ko.","translation":"I need to **block** that number because I keep receiving scam texts."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong i-**block** sa Facebook, mag-usap tayo.","translation":"Don't **block** me on Facebook, let's talk."}]

translation: to remain silent, to not say a word
meaning_filipino: Manatiling tahimik at hindi magsalita o kumibo, kadalasan bilang pagpapahayag ng isang damdamin tulad ng galit, pagtatampo, o malalim na pag-iisip.
etymology: From 'mag-' (verb prefix) + the phrase 'walang imik' (no utterance/speech).
original_explanation: The quiet part of 'quiet quitting'. When your friend asks 'Uy, anong problema?' and you just stare into the void, you are choosing to **magwalang-imik**. It's the ultimate passive-aggressive power move or a sign of deep 'tampo'. It's louder than any shout, proving that silence is indeed golden... and very, very stressful for everyone else in the room.
usage_notes: This verb implies a deliberate choice to be silent, often as a form of non-verbal communication.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinili niyang **magwalang-imik** sa gitna ng mainit na pagtatalo.","translation":"She chose to **remain silent** in the middle of the heated argument."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng sermon, ang bata ay **nagwalang-imik** sa isang sulok.","translation":"After the scolding, the child **remained silent** in a corner."}]

translation: a meal of tocino, fried rice, and egg
meaning_filipino: Isang pagkaing Pilipino na binubuo ng pinagsama-samang tocino (binurong karne), sinangag (sinangag na kanin), at itlog (pritong itlog).
etymology: A portmanteau of Tagalog 'tocino' (sweet cured meat), 'sinangag' (fried rice), and 'itlog' (egg).
original_explanation: The ultimate 'silog' breakfast for the sweet tooth. It's the combination of TOcino (sweet cured pork), SInangag (garlic fried rice), and itLOG (fried egg). If you can't decide what to eat at the karinderya, tocilog is always a safe and delicious bet.
usage_notes: One of the most popular "-silog" breakfast combinations in the Philippines, served any time of the day.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong almusal ang **tocilog** na may maraming sinangag.","translation":"My favorite breakfast is **tocilog** with lots of fried rice."},{"sentence":"Ate, isang order ng **tocilog**, 'yung itlog 'sunny-side up'.","translation":"Miss, one order of **tocilog**, with the egg sunny-side up."}]

translation: to report; to make an accounting of
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uulat o paglalahad ng mga detalye tungkol sa isang gawain, pananagutan, o pinagkatiwalaang pondo.
etymology: From 'magbigay' (to give) + 'sulit' (account, report). Note: This 'sulit' is different from the common adjective 'sulit' (worth it).
original_explanation: This is what you have to do after a team building event when you're the treasurer. You need to show the receipts for the 5000-peso 'miscellaneous' expense. To magbigay-sulit is to be accountable, to report back and prove that the company's money didn't just disappear into a black hole of milk tea and samgyupsal.
usage_notes: Primarily a formal, business, or organizational term. It implies accountability and reporting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inaatasan ang lahat ng puno ng departamento na **magbigay-sulit** sa kanilang mga gastusin.","translation":"All department heads are instructed to **make an accounting of** their expenses."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magbigay-sulit** sa iyong mga magulang kung saan napunta ang allowance mo.","translation":"You need to **report** to your parents where your allowance went."}]

translation: to cause an accident; to cause misfortune
meaning_filipino: Ang maging sanhi ng isang aksidente, kapahamakan, o di-kanais-nais na pangyayari.
original_explanation: To be the reason something bad happens, like accidentally spilling coffee on your boss's laptop or saying the wrong thing that starts a family drama. It's the "Oops, my bad, but now there's a huge problem" verb. "Mag-ingat sa pagmamaneho, baka ka pa makadesgrasya."
usage_notes: Can refer to both physical accidents and social or personal misfortunes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maglalaro ng apoy, baka ka **makadesgrasya** ng bahay.","translation":"Don't play with fire, you might **cause an accident** and burn the house."},{"sentence":"Ang tsismis na iyon ay maaaring **makadesgrasya** sa kanyang reputasyon.","translation":"That gossip could **cause misfortune** to his reputation."}]

translation: to remove; to detach; to take off
meaning_filipino: Alisin ang isang bagay mula sa kinalalagyan nito; hubarin ang kasuotan; ihiwalay ang isang bahagi.
original_explanation: This is your everyday 'take-it-off' verb. 'Magtanggal' ng sapatos pag-uwi. 'Magtanggal' ng makeup bago matulog. 'Magtanggal' ng takip ng bote. In the office context, it can also mean to fire someone ('nagtanggal sila ng mga empleyado'), which is a much less fun way to use the word.
usage_notes: A very common and versatile verb for any kind of removal or detachment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **magtanggal** ka ng sapatos bago pumasok sa bahay.","translation":"Please **remove** your shoes before entering the house."},{"sentence":"Nagdesisyon ang kumpanya na **magtanggal** ng ilang posisyon para makatipid.","translation":"The company decided to **remove** several positions to save money."}]

meaning_filipino: Hilingin o utusan ang isang tao na gunitain o ibalik sa isipan ng iba ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the "PS, don't forget" verb. Ito yung ginagawa ng alarm mo tuwing 5 AM. Ito rin yung passive-aggressive na "Gusto ko lang ipaalaala na may utang ka pa sa akin." It's the verbal nudge, the 'follow-up' action, the 'just circling back on this' of Filipino verbs.
usage_notes: Ang 'ipa-' dito ay nagpapahiwatig ng 'causative' o pagpapagawa ng kilos sa iba, ngunit sa kasong ito, madalas itong nangangahulugang 'to cause someone to remember'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **ipaalaala** mo sa akin ang meeting bukas.","translation":"Please, **remind** me about the meeting tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Gusto kong **ipaalaala** sa lahat ang kahalagahan ng pagkakaisa.","translation":"I want **to remind** everyone of the importance of unity."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang taas na naabot sa paglipad; ang kataasan ng lipad ng isang ibon, eroplano, o saranggola. Sa matalinhagang paraan, ito ay ang kataasan ng pangarap o ambisyon.
original_explanation: This is not just 'height' (taas), this is *flight* height. It's the altitude of a PAL flight to Cebu. Figuratively, it's about the 'height' of your dreams. "Ang taas ng layog ng mga pangarap niya" means their ambitions are soaring high. It's the opposite of being grounded. It's the 'reach for the stars' vibe.
usage_notes: Primarily used in literary or poetic contexts, both literally for flight and figuratively for ambition.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Humanga kami sa **layog** ng agila sa kalangitan.","translation":"We were amazed at the **flight height** of the eagle in the sky."},{"sentence":"Walang makakapigil sa **layog** ng kanyang mga pangarap.","translation":"Nothing can stop the **loftiness** of her dreams."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging malambing at magiliw sa paghipo, pagsasalita, o pagkilos.
original_explanation: This is the opposite of 'ghosting'. It's that gentle 'good morning' text, the soft hand-holding while walking in the mall, or the 'lambing' you give your pet cat. It's the ASMR of Filipino emotions. Pure, soft, and makes you feel all warm and fuzzy inside.
usage_notes: Describes a quality of gentleness and affection. Often paired with 'lambing'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nararamdaman ko ang **lamyos** ng kanyang mga daliri sa aking pisngi.","translation":"I feel the **gentle caress** of his fingers on my cheek."},{"sentence":"Puno ng **lamyos** ang kanyang bawat salita.","translation":"Every word of hers was full of **tenderness**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gitnang bahagi o punto ng isang bagay, lugar, o gawain.
original_explanation: It's the 'main character' of a location. Kung sa barkada, siya yung laging bida. Sa mall, ito yung activity center kung saan may mga pa-contest. Sa isang isyu, ito yung 'main point.' Basically, where all the action is. 'Meet tayo sa sentro ng plaza.'
usage_notes: Can be used literally for a physical center or figuratively for the focus of attention or activity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matatagpuan sa **sentro** ng lungsod ang munisipyo.","translation":"The municipal hall is located in the **center** of the city."},{"sentence":"Siya ang naging **sentro** ng usapan sa buong magdamag.","translation":"She became the **center** of conversation the whole night."}]

translation: to get a smudge on the face
meaning_filipino: Marumihan o malagyan ng dumi ang mukha.
etymology: From magka- (to have/acquire) + amos (smudge on the face).
original_explanation: Remember nung bata ka na kumain ng chocolate tapos 'yung buong mukha mo parang chocolate na rin? 'Yun 'yon. You **nagkaamos**. It's that specific brand of getting dirt, food, or anything messy smeared on your face. Cute sa bata, medyo awkward sa adult during a Zoom meeting.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to dirt, food, or any messy substance getting smeared on one's face.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tingnan mo ang iyong sarili sa salamin, **nagkaamos** ka ng tsokolate sa pisngi.","translation":"Look at yourself in the mirror, you **got a smudge** of chocolate on your cheek."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos maglaro sa labas, ang bata ay **nagkaamos** ng putik.","translation":"After playing outside, the child **got his face smudged** with mud."}]

translation: to raise; to lift up; to rebuild
meaning_filipino: Itindig o itayo mula sa pagkakabuwal o pagkakaratay; tumutukoy din sa pagpapanumbalik ng dangal, ekonomiya, o katayuan.
original_explanation: This is the national motto after every typhoon, earthquake, or major scandal. It's the 'get up, dust yourself off' energy of the Filipino people. Also what you tell yourself every Monday morning after a long weekend. 'Kailangan ko nang ibangon ang sarili ko sa kama.'
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin nang literal para sa isang pisikal na bagay o tao, o sa matalinghagang paraan para sa mga konsepto tulad ng ekonomiya, bansa, o dignidad.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **ibangon** ang natumbang aparador.","translation":"Help me **lift up** the fallen cabinet."},{"sentence":"Sama-sama nating **ibangon** ang ating ekonomiya mula sa pandemya.","translation":"Together, let's **rebuild** our economy from the pandemic."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi gaanong mahalaga; may kaunting kahulugan o kabuluhan lamang.
original_explanation: This is a gentler, more polite way of saying something is almost useless. It's for that meeting that could have been an email, but you can't say it was *totally* useless because your boss was there. "Kumusta ang seminar?" "Okay naman, pero walang-gaanong-saysay 'yung ibang topics." It's the "meh" of Filipino phrases. Not completely zero, but close.
usage_notes: A softer, more nuanced version of 'walang-saysay' (meaningless). It implies that there might be a little bit of value, but not much.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga tsismis na naririnig mo ay **walang-gaanong-saysay** kaya huwag mo nang pansinin.","translation":"The gossip you're hearing is **of little significance**, so just ignore it."},{"sentence":"Para sa kanya, **walang-gaanong-saysay** ang paghingi ng tawad kung uulitin lang din ang pagkakamali.","translation":"For him, an apology is **not very meaningful** if the mistake will just be repeated."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong lumalabag sa batas at karaniwang namumuhay sa labas ng lipunan, madalas sa mga kabundukan o liblib na lugar, at nabubuhay sa pamamagitan ng pagnanakaw o pamimilit.
etymology: From 'tulis' (sharp point), possibly referring to their sharp weapons (like bolos).
original_explanation: The classic Filipino Robin Hood... sometimes. He's the guy in historical dramas living in the mountains, fighting the Spanish or the government. To the authorities, he's a criminal. To the poor villagers he sometimes helps, he's a folk hero. The original 'rebelde.'
usage_notes: Historically significant figure in Philippine history and folklore.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming kuwento tungkol sa mga **tulisan** noong panahon ng mga Kastila.","translation":"There are many stories about **bandits** during the Spanish era."},{"sentence":"Itinuring na bayani ng ilan ang **tulisan** na si Nardong Putik.","translation":"The **outlaw** Nardong Putik was considered a hero by some."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marahang pagdampi o pagtapik sa isang bagay o tao gamit ang palad ng kamay, kadalasan upang aliwin, pakalmahin, o alisin ang alikabok.
original_explanation: This is that gentle tap on the back your lola gives you after a good meal, saying "Busog na ang alaga ko." It's also what you do to a baby's back to make them burp, or what you do to your crush's shoulder to get their attention, pretending it was an accident. "Ay, sorry!"
usage_notes: Often used to show comfort, affection, or to clean a surface lightly.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinabihan siya ng nanay niya na **magpikpik** ng harina sa mesa bago magmasa ng tinapay.","translation":"His mother told him to **tap** some flour onto the table before kneading the dough."},{"sentence":"“Huwag kang umiyak, andito lang ako,” sabi niya habang **nagpipikpik** sa likod ko.","translation":"'Don't cry, I'm just here,' he said while **patting** my back."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking kampana, karaniwang matatagpuan sa kampanaryo ng simbahan, na ginagamit upang ipahiwatig ang oras o magbigay ng babala.
original_explanation: This isn't your tiny 'tita's doorbell'. This is the G.O.A.T. of bells. The massive one in the church tower that rings for mass, weddings, or to warn the whole town that Godzilla is coming. Its sound can be heard from kilometers away. Think the Hunchback of Notre Dame's Quasimodo, but with an anting-anting.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively refers to large church bells or similar monumental bells.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Rinig sa buong bayan ang kalembang ng **batingaw**.","translation":"The ringing of the **large bell** could be heard throughout the town."},{"sentence":"Ang lumang **batingaw** sa simbahan ay isang pamanang pangkasaysayan.","translation":"The old **large bell** in the church is a historical heritage."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng pagdududa, kawalan ng tiwala, o pag-aagam-agam.
original_explanation: This is your default mode when someone slides into your DMs with "Hi, I'm a prince from a faraway land..." or when a networking friend says "Hindi 'to pyramiding, promise!" Being mapag-alinlangan is being skeptical. It's your inner lie detector going off. A useful survival skill in 2026.
usage_notes: The "mapag-" prefix turns the root ("alinlangan" - doubt) into a character trait, describing someone who is often doubtful or skeptical.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay likas na **mapag-alinlangan** sa mga alok na napakaganda para maging totoo.","translation":"She is naturally **skeptical** of offers that are too good to be true."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging siksik, masusi, o detalyado. Tumutukoy sa pagiging malapit-lapit ng mga bahagi ng isang bagay o sa kalaliman ng isang pagsusuri.
etymology: Mula sa kabilaang panlaping 'ka-...-an' at salitang-ugat na 'sinsin' (density, closeness).
original_explanation: This is a high-level word. Think of it as the quality of being super detailed and packed. It's the 'kasinsinan' of your Lolo's old-school handwriting, where every letter is perfectly formed. It's also the 'kasinsinan' (thoroughness) required to debug code at 3 AM or to survive a thesis defense.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical density (e.g., of a forest, population) or abstract thoroughness (e.g., of an investigation, analysis).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa **kasinsinan** ng gubat, mahirap itong pasukin.","translation":"Because of the **density** of the forest, it is difficult to enter."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng **kasinsinan** sa pagsusuri ng mga ebidensya.","translation":"Thoroughness is needed in the examination of evidence."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat ng mga sasakyan o barko na magkakasamang naglalakbay, karaniwan para sa proteksyon o pag-aalalay.
original_explanation: When the whole barkada decides to go to Tagaytay in separate cars, that's a 'kumboy'. The lead car is the designated Waze user, and everyone else just follows. It's also what politicians use, complete with 'wang-wang', to part the sea of EDSA traffic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naka-**kumboy** ang mga sasakyan ng presidente.","translation":"The president's vehicles were in a **convoy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na laging may negatibong sinasabi, kritisismo, o galit sa isang tao o bagay, kadalasan dahil sa inggit.
original_explanation: The Filipino definition is exactly the same as the English one, but we've adopted it with gusto. A **hater** is that person in your comments section saying 'Sana all' with a hint of bitterness, or that *tita* who asks 'Kailan ka mag-aasawa?' with a judgy look. They're the bashers, the critics, the ones who just can't be happy for you. The classic comeback? 'Haters gonna hate.'
usage_notes: A direct borrowing from English, commonly used in Taglish conversations, especially in the context of social media and celebrity culture.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong pansinin ang mga **hater**, inggit lang 'yan sila.","translation":"Don't pay attention to the **haters**, they're just envious."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang tagumpay, dumami ang kanyang mga **hater**.","translation":"Because of her success, her **haters** multiplied."}]

meaning_filipino: Banatin ang mga kalamnan ng katawan, karaniwan pagkatapos gumising o matagal na pag-upo. Maaari ring tumukoy sa pag-unat ng isang bagay na lukot o nakatupi.
original_explanation: The best feeling in the world after waking up or after sitting in front of your laptop for 4 hours straight. It's your body's way of saying 'Thank you, next (task)!' Also what you do to a crumpled 20-peso bill before handing it to the jeepney driver.
usage_notes: Can refer to stretching limbs (`mag-unat ng braso/binti`) or straightening a creased object (`mag-unat ng damit`).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap **mag-unat** pagkagising sa umaga.","translation":"It feels good to **stretch** after waking up in the morning."},{"sentence":"Tumayo ka muna at **mag-unat** para hindi mangalay ang likod mo.","translation":"Stand up for a while and **stretch** so your back won't get sore."}]

meaning_filipino: Nauukol sa o nagpapakita ng mga kahanga-hangang gawaing pampisikal na nangangailangan ng liksi, balanse, at koordinasyon.
original_explanation: Parang yung ex mong ang galing mag-juggle ng dalawang tao nang sabay. Yung mga galawan na 'wow, paano niya nagawa yun?' - yan ang akrobatik. Pwede sa circus, pwede sa relasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakagaling ng **akrobatik** na pagtatanghal ng mga sirkero.","translation":"The circus performers' **acrobatic** show was amazing."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng **akrobatik** na pag-iisip para masolusyonan ang problema sa traffic sa EDSA.","translation":"You need **acrobatic** thinking to solve the traffic problem on EDSA."}]

translation: to whiten; to make something white
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng kulay puti o paggamit ng paraan upang gawing puti ang isang bagay; maaari ring tumukoy sa pagpapaputi ng balat.
original_explanation: In the Philippines, this verb is a billion-peso industry. From laundry ('Paano magpaputi ng damit na may mantsa?') to skincare ('Anong sabon ang mabisang magpaputi?'). It's the act of making something white, whether it's your shirt, your teeth, or... well, you know.
usage_notes: Very common. Can refer to whitening clothes, teeth, skin, or painting something white.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto niyang **magpaputi** ng ngipin bago ang kanyang kasal.","translation":"She wants to **whiten** her teeth before her wedding."},{"sentence":"Nagdesisyon silang **magpaputi** ng pader ng kanilang bahay.","translation":"They decided to **paint** the walls of their house **white**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pautos na paraan upang hilingin sa isang tao na balutin ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: The official request of every Pinoy at a handaan or restaurant when the food is too good to leave behind. "Ate, pabalot po." It's the verbal command that activates 'take-out' mode. It's a polite imperative, the equivalent of "Can you wrap this for me?"
usage_notes: Used as a command or request, often in food establishments or after parties. The full verb form would be `magpabalot` (to ask someone to wrap) or `ipabalot` (to have something wrapped). `Pabalot` is the shortened, common command form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pabalot** po nitong natirang adobo,\" sabi niya sa serbidora.","translation":"**Please wrap** this leftover adobo,\" she told the waitress."},{"sentence":"Tumawag siya sa nanay niya, \"Nay, **pabalot** naman ng ulam para sa akin!\"","translation":"He called his mom, \"Mom, **please wrap** some food for me!\""}]

meaning_filipino: Ang isang mabilis at malaking pag-inom o paglunok ng likido.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa mo sa malamig na tubig after mag-jogging sa ilalim ng araw. Isang diretsong lunok, 'yung tipong ramdam mo 'yung lamig pababa ng lalamunan mo. It's the sound and action of chugging a drink.
usage_notes: Often used with "isang" (one) as "isang lagok" (one gulp). The verb form is "lagukin".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa isang **lagok**, inubos niya ang buong baso ng tubig.","translation":"In one **gulp**, he finished the whole glass of water."},{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **lagok** niya habang umiinom.","translation":"I heard his **swallow** as he was drinking."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na naipakita, naiharap, o naipakilala na.
original_explanation: This is the 'past tense' of presenting something. Kapag tapos na ang report mo sa klase, 'Na-**presentado** na po.' Kapag naipakilala mo na ang jowa mo sa pamilya mo, 'Na-**presentado** ko na siya.' It means the deed is done, the thing has been shown.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of formal presentations or introductions. It functions as a past participle.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahusay na **presentado** ang mga datos sa ulat.","translation":"The data in the report was well **presented**."},{"sentence":"**Presentado** na ba ang bagong miyembro sa grupo?","translation":"Has the new member been **introduced** to the group yet?"}]

meaning_filipino: Magsabi ng masasamang salita o mga paglapastangan, karaniwan dahil sa galit o pagkadismaya.
original_explanation: The national sport when you stub your toe, get stuck in traffic, or see your electricity bill. It's the verbal equivalent of a stress ball. Some people turn it into an art form, stringing curses together like poetry.
usage_notes: This refers to using profane language. The root word 'mura' (curse) is pronounced with stress on the second syllable: /mu-RA/.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magmura** sa harap ng mga bata.","translation":"Don't **curse** in front of the children."},{"sentence":"Napilitan siyang **magmura** nang malaman niyang nanakawan siya.","translation":"He couldn't help but **swear** when he found out he was robbed."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng paggawa ng isang bagay na ginagamitan ng lakas, puwersa, o pamimilit, at labag sa kalooban ng iba.
original_explanation: Think of your mom making you clean your room, or a security guard escorting a rowdy customer out. That's sapuwersahan. It's the 'you have no choice' move. Sa office, ito 'yung 'mandatory' team building na ayaw mo namang puntahan. It's done by force, whether physical or through sheer authority.
usage_notes: Can also be used as an adjective (e.g., 'sapuwersahang pagkuha' - forced taking).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sapuwersahan** siyang isinakay sa kotse ng mga dumukot sa kanya.","translation":"He was **forcibly** put into the car by his abductors."},{"sentence":"Isinagawa ang **sapuwersahang** pagpapaalis sa mga nakatira sa tabi ng ilog.","translation":"The **forced** eviction of the residents by the river was carried out."}]

translation: to embrace with; to use to embrace
meaning_filipino: Gamitin ang mga braso o kamay upang yumakap sa isang tao o bagay.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "i-" at salitang-ugat na "akap" (yakap).
original_explanation: This is the verb for when you're the one doing the hugging, specifically focusing on what you're using to hug. "Iakap mo ang mga braso mo sa kanya." It's a bit more poetic or specific than just saying "yakapin mo siya" (hug him/her). It's like saying "envelop them in your arms."
usage_notes: Ang "iakap" ay tumutukoy sa aksyon ng paggamit ng isang bagay (karaniwan ay braso) para yumakap, samantalang ang "yakapin" ay tumutukoy sa taong niyayakap. Hal: "Iakap mo ang iyong mga braso" (focus sa braso) vs. "Yakapin mo ako" (focus sa taong yayakapin).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit niyang **iakap** ang kanyang mga braso sa unan.","translation":"She tightly **embraced** the pillow **with** her arms."},{"sentence":"Gusto kong **iakap** sa'yo ang lahat ng pagmamahal ko.","translation":"I want to **embrace** you **with** all my love."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabantay o pagmamasid sa isang tao, bagay, o lugar upang ito ay protektahan o siguruhing nasa maayos na kalagayan.
original_explanation: This is what your nanay tells you to do with the nilaga on the stove so it doesn't boil over. Or what you do to your crush's IG stories, waiting for them to post. It's active surveillance, whether for your baby sibling or for your favorite pair of sneakers you left outside.
usage_notes: "Bantayan" implies a specific object or person to watch. "Magbantay" is more general, meaning "to be on guard."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bantayan** mo ang kapatid mo habang nasa palengke ako.","translation":"**Watch over** your sibling while I'm at the market."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **bantayan** ang mga boto upang maiwasan ang pandaraya.","translation":"The votes must be **guarded** to prevent fraud."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bilang na kasunod ng labing-anim at bago ang labing-walo; katumbas ng 17.
etymology: From "labi" (excess, remainder) + "-ng" + "pito" (seven), literally "excess of ten by seven".
original_explanation: The age you feel when you're listening to a 2000s rock playlist. Also, the number of unread messages from your group chat after being away for just one hour.
usage_notes: Can be written as "labimpito" or "labingpito". The Spanish-derived "disisiyete" is also used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay **labingpito** taong gulang na.","translation":"He/She is now **seventeen** years old."},{"sentence":"**Labingpito** lahat ang inorder nating pagkain.","translation":"We ordered **seventeen** dishes in total."}]

translation: to be fickle; to keep changing
meaning_filipino: Ang patuloy at madalas na pagpapalit ng isip, desisyon, o kalagayan; kawalan ng paninindigan.
original_explanation: Eto yung kaibigan mong "See you at 7 PM!" pero 7:30 na, "OTW na!" ang text, tapos 8 PM, "Sorry, 'di na pala ako tutuloy." O kaya yung jowa mong ngayon "I love you," bukas "I need space." It's the act of being inconsistent and unpredictable, like your internet connection during a typhoon. It's the ultimate source of trust issues.
usage_notes: Describes inconsistency in decisions, moods, or plans. Carries a slightly negative connotation of being unreliable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap magplano kasama si Ana dahil **nagpapabagu-bago** siya lagi ng isip.","translation":"It's hard to make plans with Ana because she always **keeps changing** her mind."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magpabagu-bago** ng desisyon kung ayaw mong malito ang mga tao.","translation":"Don't **be fickle** with your decision if you don't want to confuse people."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalathala o paglalagay ng mensahe, larawan, o video sa isang social media platform o website.
original_explanation: The national sport of the Philippines. If you didn't 'mag-post' about your lunch, your vacation, or your 'hugot' for the day, did it even happen? It's the act of sharing your life (or a highly curated version of it) for likes, shares, and comments. "Pa-like and share naman po."
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in the context of social media and the internet.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mag-post** ng mga personal na impormasyon online.","translation":"Don't **post** personal information online."},{"sentence":"**Nag-post** siya ng picture namin sa Boracay.","translation":"She **posted** our picture in Boracay."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang seryosong kalagayang medikal sa isipan na nagdudulot ng patuloy na pakiramdam ng kalungkutan, kawalan ng interes, at iba pang emosyonal at pisikal na mga problema.
original_explanation: That feeling when it's sahod day but you have zero pesos left after paying all your bills. But seriously, it's not just 'lungkot' or being 'emo'. It's a real and serious mental health issue that needs professional help. #MentalHealthMatters
usage_notes: While it can be used colloquially to mean 'sadness', there is a growing awareness in the Philippines of its clinical definition.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag balewalain ang mga sintomas ng **depresyon**; mahalagang kumonsulta sa isang propesyonal.","translation":"Do not ignore the symptoms of **depression**; it is important to consult a professional."},{"sentence":"Maraming kabataan ngayon ang mas bukas sa pag-uusap tungkol sa **depresyon** at mental health.","translation":"Many young people today are more open to talking about **depression** and mental health."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasukasuan sa gitna ng braso na nag-uugnay sa itaas na bahagi at ibabang bahagi nito.
original_explanation: The pointy part of your arm that's useless for kissing but perfect for poking someone to get their attention, or for making space in a crowded jeepney. It's also what you use to apply an ungodly amount of pressure on your friend's back during a massage. "Pasa-siko" is the art of subtly elbowing your way through a crowd.
usage_notes: The verb 'sikuhin' means 'to elbow someone'. 'Maniko' is the act of using one's elbows, often aggressively.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natamaan ang **siko** ko sa pader.","translation":"I hit my **elbow** on the wall."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniko kung nakikipagsiksikan ka sa pila.","translation":"Don't use your **elbows** when you're squeezing into a line."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang pagtalon, pag-unat, o pagbalik sa dating posisyon mula sa pagkakabaluktot o pagkakadiin.
etymology: Possibly related to Malay "bingkas" (to get up, to rise).
original_explanation: Parang yung bigla mong pagbangon sa kama kapag naalala mong may exam ka pala. O yung pagtalon ng takip ng kaldero kapag kumukulo na. That sudden, forceful spring into action. Pwedeng literal, pwedeng sa gulat. The verb form is 'bumingkas'.
usage_notes: Often used with 'bumingkas' (verb form) meaning 'to spring up'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa isang **bingkas**, tumayo siya at hinarap ang kalaban.","translation":"In one **spring**, he stood up and faced the enemy."},{"sentence":"Bumigkas ang bitag nang masagi ito ng usa.","translation":"The trap **sprang** when the deer touched it."}]

translation: to make famous; to publicize; to seek fame
meaning_filipino: Gawin ang isang bagay, tao, o serbisyo na maging kilala o sikat sa karamihan.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate goal of every aspiring influencer or TikToker. It's the act of doing something—anything—to go viral. From dance challenges to controversial statements, it's all in the name of trying to **magpatanyag**. The ultimate 'sana all mapansin' move.
usage_notes: Often implies a deliberate and sometimes strategic effort to gain fame or public recognition.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang social media para **magpatanyag** ng kanyang negosyo.","translation":"She used social media to **publicize** her business."},{"sentence":"May mga artistang gumagawa ng isyu para lang **magpatanyag**.","translation":"Some artists create issues just to **gain fame**."}]

meaning_filipino: Mag-asal na tila totoo ang isang bagay na hindi naman; magpanggap upang makalinlang o magtago ng tunay na nararamdaman.
original_explanation: The official verb for "acting lang." When you see your ex with a new partner and you smile and act happy for them, but deep inside you're plotting 101 ways to trip them. Or when you act like you're working hard when your boss walks by your desk. That's you, magpakunwari-ing.
usage_notes: Often carries a slightly negative connotation of deception, as opposed to simply 'acting' in a play.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magpakunwari** na hindi mo ako kilala.","translation":"Don't you **pretend** that you don't know me."},{"sentence":"**Nagpakunwari** siyang tulog para hindi mautusan.","translation":"He **feigned** sleep so he wouldn't be asked to run an errand."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tanda, bakas, o pahiwatig na maaaring sundan upang matuklasan ang isang bagay o malutas ang isang suliranin.
original_explanation: The chismis breadcrumbs you follow to get the full tea. It's the 'seen' on Messenger, the vague FB status, or the one friend who knows a little something. You piece these clues together like a detective trying to figure out 'kayo na ba?'
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng imbestigasyon o paghahanap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Walang naiwang anumang **tagunton** ang magnanakaw.","translation":"The thief left no **trace** whatsoever."},{"sentence":"Sinusundan ng mga pulis ang bawat **tagunton** upang mahanap ang nawawalang bata.","translation":"The police are following every **clue** to find the missing child."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng isang larawan o disenyo sa pamamagitan ng paglalagay ng pintura sa isang ibabaw.
original_explanation: The OG way of creating an image before Instagram filters. It's what artists do with a brush, canvas, and a lot of feelings. Also what you do to your face every morning with makeup, creating a masterpiece called "ready for my close-up."
usage_notes: This is a less common, more formal/literary term for 'to paint'. The more common term is 'magpinta'. Completed aspect (past tense). Present: `pumipintal`, Future: `pipintal`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Fernando Amorsolo ay **pumintal** ng maraming larawan na nagpapakita ng buhay sa kabukiran.","translation":"Fernando Amorsolo **painted** many pictures showing life in the countryside."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **pumintal** ng isang obra maestra para sa kaniyang minamahal.","translation":"He tried to **paint** a masterpiece for his beloved."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtaas o paglala ng isang sitwasyon, hidwaan, o problema.
original_explanation: 'Yung simpleng 'sana all' comment mo sa Facebook na naging World War III sa comment section. From a small misunderstanding to a full-blown barangay hearing, that's 'umiskala'. It's when things go from 0 to 100 real quick.
usage_notes: A loanword that has been fully integrated and conjugated as a Tagalog verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umiskala** ang simpleng away-trapiko hanggang sa nagkasuntukan na sila.","translation":"The simple traffic dispute **escalated** until they were punching each other."},{"sentence":"Pinipigilan ng mga lider na **umiskala** ang tensyon sa pagitan ng dalawang bansa.","translation":"The leaders are trying to prevent the tension between the two countries from **escalating**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng kinakailangang pondo, materyales, o suporta para sa isang tao, proyekto, o gawain; sustento.
original_explanation: Basically, your allowance from your parents or the budget your manager gives you for a project. It's the financial lifeline. When someone asks 'Sino ang nag-tustos sa pag-aaral mo?', they're asking who's paying your tuition.
usage_notes: A formal term, often related to finance, budget, or sustenance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang gobyerno ang nagbigay ng **tustos** para sa pagpapatayo ng bagong tulay.","translation":"The government provided the **funding** for the construction of the new bridge."},{"sentence":"Kulang ang **tustos** para sa lahat ng gastusin.","translation":"The **provision** is not enough for all the expenses."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng materyal na idinidikit o itinatapal sa butas o punit ng damit, sisidlan, at iba pa.
original_explanation: The original 'life hack' for your favorite jeans that are now 'holy' (but not in a good way). It's the band-aid for your clothes. In software, it's a 'patch' to fix a bug. In life, sometimes you just gotta patch things up and move on.
usage_notes: Can be a noun (the patch itself) or a verb root (to apply a patch, e.g., 'tagpian').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagyan mo ng **tagpi** ang butas sa iyong pantalon.","translation":"Put a **patch** on the hole in your pants."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **tagpian** ang gulong ng bisikleta.","translation":"I need to **patch** the bicycle tire."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa posisyon na kasunod ng ikatlo at bago ang ikalima sa isang pagkakasunod-sunod.
etymology: Mula sa panlaping 'ika-' (panandang pamilang na panunuran) at 'apat'.
original_explanation: The fourth one. In a barkada of five, you're not the leader (una), not the second-in-command (ikalawa), not the middle child (ikatlo), but you're not the baby either (ikalima). You're the ikaapat. The one who's just... there. Also, the ikaapat na kanto is where the jeepney driver is supposed to drop you off, but he always forgets.
usage_notes: Pamantayang paraan ng pagbuo ng mga pamilang na panunuran (ordinal numbers) sa Tagalog. Ikinakabit ang panlaping 'ika-' sa pamilang na patakaran (cardinal number). Maaari ring isulat bilang 'ika-4'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa **ikaapat** na palapag ang aming opisina.","translation":"Our office is on the **fourth** floor."},{"sentence":"Ito na ang **ikaapat** na beses na nanonood ako ng concert nila.","translation":"This is the **fourth** time I'm watching their concert."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng lubos na atensyon sa maliliit na bahagi o impormasyon; masusi.
original_explanation: This describes your friend who plans a trip down to the last centavo and minute, or that one tita who notices you gained 2 pounds. It's the Tagalog version of being 'OC' or a 'details person'. 'Napakamadetalye ng client, pati font size ng period pinapansin.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil **napakamadetalye** si Ana, siya ang laging taga-plano ng aming mga biyahe.","translation":"Because Ana is **very meticulous**, she is always the planner of our trips."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang dalubhasa sa agham; isang tao na may sistematikong kaalaman sa isa o higit pang sangay ng siyensya at nagsasagawa ng pananaliksik.
original_explanation: The person in a lab coat that your parents wanted you to be. They do research, experiments, and discover things that could either save the world or just prove a very specific theory about fruit flies. In the Philippines, they're often underfunded but overworked, the unsung heroes behind our weather forecasts, medical breakthroughs, and understanding of local biodiversity.
usage_notes: The Tagalog 'siyentipiko' or 'dalub-agham' exists but 'scientist' is understood and often used in formal and informal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang Pilipinong **scientist** ang nakatuklas ng bagong gamot.","translation":"A Filipino **scientist** discovered a new medicine."},{"sentence":"Ang mga **scientist** sa PAGASA ang nagbibigay ng babala tungkol sa bagyo.","translation":"The **scientists** at PAGASA are the ones who give warnings about typhoons."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng daliri, karaniwan ay ang hinlalato, upang biglaang pakawalan at patalsikin ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: It's that move you do to launch a rubber band at your unsuspecting classmate or sibling. Or flicking a bottle cap across the table. The OG fidget spinner move. 'pa-' (to cause) + 'labtik' (flick) + '-in' (object focus).
usage_notes: The action of using a finger (usually the thumb or middle finger) to build tension and then release it, causing something small to fly.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **palabtikin** ang goma sa loob ng klase.","translation":"Don't **flick** the rubber band inside the classroom."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **palabtikin** ang tansan papunta sa basurahan.","translation":"He tried to **flick** the bottle cap into the trash can."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga salitang mabulaklak, maligoy, o labis na papuri na kadalasan ay hindi taos-puso o may halong pagmamalabis.
original_explanation: This is what you call verbal fireworks. It's the language of 'mambobola'—sweet, fancy words that sound amazing but are probably as empty as your wallet before payday. Think of it as the 'sales talk' of love and life. "Ang ganda mo, para kang tala..." -- ayan, bulaklak ng dila 'yan.
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang ilarawan ang mabulaklak na pananalita, madalas na may pahiwatig ng kawalan ng katapatan o pagmamalabis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala sa kanya, puro **bulaklak ng dila** lang 'yan.","translation":"Don't believe him, those are just **flowery words**."}]

translation: Full of sharp points / Very pointy
meaning_filipino: May maraming bahaging matutulis o patusok; lubhang matulis.
original_explanation: Describes anything that looks like a punk rocker's jacket or a durian. It's the visual equivalent of stepping on a Lego. If something is tulis-tulis, you probably don't want to sit on it.
usage_notes: The reduplication emphasizes the quantity or intensity of the sharpness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bakod nila ay **tulis-tulis** kaya mahirap akyatin.","translation":"Their fence is **full of sharp points** so it's hard to climb."},{"sentence":"Mukhang masarap ang prutas pero **tulis-tulis** ang balat nito.","translation":"The fruit looks delicious but its skin is **very pointy**."}]

translation: digging out, scooping out (with a finger or tool)
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghuhukay o pagkuha ng isang bagay mula sa isang masikip na espasyo o lalagyan gamit ang daliri o isang kasangkapan.
etymology: From `pag-` (nominalizer) + `kulkol` (to dig out with a finger/tool).
original_explanation: ‘Yung ginagawa mo sa garapon ng peanut butter para makuha 'yung last bits. O 'yung pagkuha ng kulangot (let's be real). It's the act of digging into a nook or cranny to extract something. Can be satisfying or kinda gross, depending on the context.
usage_notes: Often implies using fingers or a small, curved tool. It has a slightly more specific meaning than 'paghuhukay' (general digging).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahirapan siya sa **pagkulkol** ng natirang ube jam sa bote.","translation":"He had difficulty **scooping out** the remaining ube jam from the bottle."}]

translation: to surpass, to overcome, to outdo
meaning_filipino: Ang paglampas o pag-angat sa iba sa isang kumpetisyon, kakayahan, o kalagayan; ang paggapi sa isang kalaban o pagsubok.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'I'm better than you' move. It's when you one-up someone. Your officemate got a promotion? You get a better offer from a competitor. Your ex has a new partner? You show up glowing up and unbothered. To 'dumaig sa subasta' (to outbid) is a classic example—you literally put more money where your mouth is to win. It's the spirit of 'Galingan mo, bes!'
usage_notes: Often used in competitive contexts. Can mean to defeat an opponent, overcome a challenge, or simply be better than someone/something. 'Dumaig sa subasta' is a common phrase meaning 'to outbid'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malaking korporasyon ang **dumaig sa subasta** para sa proyekto.","translation":"A large corporation **outbid** everyone in the auction for the project."},{"sentence":"Sa huli, ang kabutihan pa rin ang **dadaig** sa kasamaan.","translation":"In the end, goodness will still **prevail** over evil."},{"sentence":"Sinikap niyang **dumaig** sa lahat ng pagsubok na dumating sa kanyang buhay.","translation":"He strived to **overcome** all the challenges that came into his life."}]

translation: the act or manner of searching thoroughly; rummaging
meaning_filipino: Ang paraan ng masusing paghahanap o paghalungkat sa isang bagay o lugar.
etymology: From 'pagka-' (manner of) + 'balutbot' (to search thoroughly, to rummage).
original_explanation: This is you tearing your room apart looking for your keys, wallet, or will to live. It's the frantic energy of a customs officer checking a suspicious balikbayan box, or your mom looking for that *one* specific Tupperware lid.
usage_notes: Implies a very detailed, sometimes messy, search.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko gusto ang **pagkabalutbot** niya sa aking mga gamit.","translation":"I don't like his **manner of rummaging** through my things."},{"sentence":"Sa tindi ng kanyang **pagkabalutbot**, natagpuan din niya ang nawawalang singsing.","translation":"Due to his **thorough searching**, he finally found the missing ring."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o katangian ng pagiging salungat sa mga pamantayang moral o etikal ng isang lipunan.
original_explanation: The stuff that makes the marites in your neighborhood start whispering. It's the plot of every teleserye involving a third party, a secret family, or a corrupt politician. It's basically breaking the 'good conduct' rules of society.
usage_notes: A formal word used in discussions about ethics, religion, and social issues.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang korapsyon ay isang malinaw na halimbawa ng **imoralidad** sa gobyerno.","translation":"Corruption is a clear example of **immorality** in government."},{"sentence":"Ikinababahala ng mga magulang ang paglaganap ng **imoralidad** na nakikita ng mga kabataan sa media.","translation":"Parents are worried about the spread of **immorality** that the youth see in the media."}]

translation: to indulge in pleasure; to make something delicious
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakasawa sa kaligayahan o kaginhawaan; maaari ring tumukoy sa pagdaragdag ng sangkap upang gawing mas malasa ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: Two meanings here. First is "magpakasarap" mode: you just won the lottery (or just got your sahod) and you're going to treat yourself to a spa, a buffet, and everything nice. It's the "I deserve this" verb. Second is the literal cooking version: "Paano ko ba mapapasarap itong adobo ko?" You're asking how to make it more delicious. It's about leveling up the pleasure, whether for your life or for your taste buds.
usage_notes: Can be reflexive ("magpasarap sa buhay" - to indulge oneself in life) or transitive ("magpasarap ng ulam" - to make a dish delicious). Often used interchangeably with "magpakasarap".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng mahabang linggo sa trabaho, oras nang **magpasarap** at manood ng paborito mong serye.","translation":"After a long week at work, it's time to **indulge** and watch your favorite series."},{"sentence":"Magdagdag ka ng keso para **magpasarap** ng iyong spaghetti.","translation":"Add cheese to **make** your spaghetti **more delicious**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kumukuha ng mga litrato bilang isang propesyon o libangan. Ang katumbas sa Filipino ay maniniyot o potograpo.
original_explanation: The designated 'taga-picture' of the barkada, but make it pro. They're the ones who say 'Wait, the lighting is bad here' and make you pose for 10 minutes for that perfect 'candid' shot. Everyone has that one friend who became a photographer and now all your group outings look like a pre-nup shoot. They're the heroes who make our IG feeds look 100x better.
usage_notes: Mas karaniwang ginagamit kaysa sa mga katumbas nitong Filipino na 'maniniyot' o 'potograpo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha kami ng isang propesyonal na **photographer** para sa aming kasal.","translation":"We hired a professional **photographer** for our wedding."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagak ng kaukulang halaga o ari-arian sa hukuman bilang garantiya sa pansamantalang paglaya ng isang akusado.
original_explanation: This is what happens in teleseryes when the 'bida' gets framed and thrown in jail. Their rich tita or lawyer best friend will rush to the courthouse to 'pumiyansa' so they can be free while the case is ongoing. It's literally paying to get out of jail (for now).
usage_notes: A legal term used in the context of law and court proceedings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nilang mag-ipon ng malaking halaga para **pumiyansa** sa kanilang ama.","translation":"They need to raise a large amount of money **to post bail** for their father."},{"sentence":"Agad siyang **pumiyansa** matapos siyang arestuhin.","translation":"He immediately **posted bail** after he was arrested."}]

meaning_filipino: Bilang pang-uri, tumutukoy ito sa mga bagay na may kaugnayan sa edukasyon, pag-aaral, at iskolarsyip. Bilang pangalan, ito ay tumutukoy sa isang babaeng kasapi ng akademya o isang babaeng iskolar.
original_explanation: When something is so 'deep' and full of jargon, you need a PhD to understand it. 'Masyadong akademika ang sinabi niya.' It can also refer to a female professor or researcher who probably has a ton of books, drinks a lot of coffee, and uses words you have to Google later.
usage_notes: The masculine form is 'akademiko'. Often used to describe a style of writing or discussion that is formal and scholarly.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang sulatin ay may tonong napaka-**akademika**.","translation":"Her writing has a very **academic** tone."},{"sentence":"Isang kilalang **akademika** mula sa UP ang magiging tagapagsalita.","translation":"A well-known **female academic** from UP will be the speaker."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa balarila, isang yunit ng wika na binubuo ng isa o higit pang mga salita na may simuno at panaguri, at nagpapahayag ng isang buong kaisipan.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung pinapagawa sa'yo ni Ma'am noong elementary: 'Gamitin sa pangungusap ang...' Ang sentensya ay kumpletong chika—may subject (pinag-uusapan) at predicate (ang sinasabi tungkol sa subject). Dapat may period, question mark, o exclamation point sa dulo para kumpleto ang drama.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa konteksto ng wika, pagsulat, at gramatika. Ang 'pangungusap' ay ang mas katutubong katumbas nito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siguraduhing tama ang bantas sa bawat **sentensya** na iyong isusulat.","translation":"Make sure the punctuation in every **sentence** you write is correct."},{"sentence":"Ang isang talata ay binubuo ng magkakaugnay na mga **sentensya**.","translation":"A paragraph is composed of related **sentences**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng isang bagay na madaling mag-apoy, sumiklab, o masunog.
original_explanation: This is the warning label on your deodorant or alcohol spray. It's that thing that makes firefighters nervous. Also used figuratively for a person who is "madaling mag-init ang ulo" (hot-headed). Isang maling sabi mo lang, maliyab na agad. Handle with care!
usage_notes: Both 'flammable' and 'inflammable' are correct English translations, despite their confusing prefixes. The Tagalog word is unambiguous.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa paggamit ng gas dahil ito ay **maliyab**.","translation":"Be careful when using gas because it is **flammable**."},{"sentence":"Huwag itapon ang sigarilyo sa tuyong damuhan dahil ito ay **maliyab**.","translation":"Don't throw cigarettes on dry grass because it is **flammable**."}]

translation: to put into writing; to document
meaning_filipino: Ilipat o isalin sa anyong nakasulat o dokumento ang isang kasunduan, pahayag, o ideya.
original_explanation: Yung moment na sinabi ng boss mo, "Okay, great idea, now isapapel mo 'yan for the presentation." It's the official act of turning chismis into a formal complaint, or your brilliant shower thoughts into a business plan. From 'sabi-sabi' to black and white.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **isapapel** ang lahat ng napag-usapan sa pulong.","translation":"Everything discussed in the meeting needs to be **put into writing**."},{"sentence":"**Isinapapel** niya ang kanyang mga tula upang mabasa ng marami.","translation":"She **documented** her poems so that many could read them."}]

translation: to finish off one another; to eliminate each other
meaning_filipino: Mag-ubusan o magpuksain ng isa't isa hanggang sa wala nang matira.
original_explanation: This is Hunger Games, Filipino style. It's when a conflict gets so intense that the goal is for everyone to take each other down, like in a political dynasty feud or the last ten minutes of a battle royale game. "Bahala na, magtiwasan na tayo dito!" It's mutual destruction, a zero-sum game where nobody wins in the end.
usage_notes: Implies a mutual and often violent process of elimination among a group. A very strong and dramatic word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang tindi ng kanilang alitan, halos **magtiwasan** ang dalawang paksyon.","translation":"Their conflict was so intense, the two factions nearly **finished each other off**."},{"sentence":"Hinayaan ng hari na **magtiwasan** ang mga traydor sa kanyang kaharian.","translation":"The king let the traitors in his kingdom **eliminate each other**."}]

translation: to accustom; to get someone used to something
meaning_filipino: Sanayin o hayaang masanay ang isang tao sa isang partikular na gawain, sitwasyon, o kapaligiran.
original_explanation: It's like training your new officemate on the company's weird, unwritten rules. Or how your mom "trains" you to wake up early by blasting the radio. It's the process of making something abnormal feel normal through repetition. Parang pag-ibig, sa una naninibago ka, pero sa katagalan, nasasanay ka na rin sa topak niya.
usage_notes: Often implies accustoming someone to something difficult or undesirable, although it can be neutral.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pamihasahin** ang bata sa laging pagbili ng laruan.","translation":"Don't **accustom** the child to always buying toys."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **pamihasahin** ang mga aso sa pagkakaroon ng ibang tao sa bahay.","translation":"The dogs need to be **acclimated** to having other people in the house."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking makina na ginagamit sa pagbubuhat at paglilipat ng mabibigat na bagay, karaniwang makikita sa mga lugar ng konstruksiyon.
original_explanation: Yung dambuhalang bakal na may mahabang leeg sa mga construction site na nagbubuhat ng mga semento at bakal. Parang giraffe na bakal na tumutulong magtayo ng mga condo.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to the construction machine.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit sila ng **kreyn** para itaas ang mga materyales sa ikasampung palapag.","translation":"They used a **crane** to lift the materials to the tenth floor."},{"sentence":"Natumba ang **kreyn** dahil sa malakas na hangin.","translation":"The **crane** fell over because of the strong wind."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang balat ng hayop na pinroseso sa pamamagitan ng pagkulay at pagpapatuyo upang gawing materyales para sa sapatos, bag, sinturon, at iba pang produkto.
original_explanation: The stuff your dad's favorite "Marikina-made" shoes are made of. It's the material for that bag you saved up for, or the jacket that makes you feel like a rockstar. Real katad has that distinct smell and gets better with age, just like a good adobo or your favorite tito's jokes. Beware of 'katad-finish' – that's the impostor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala ang Marikina sa paggawa ng de-kalidad na sapatos na gawa sa **katad**.","translation":"Marikina is known for making high-quality shoes made of **leather**."},{"sentence":"Ang amoy ng bagong kotse ay dahil sa upuang **katad**.","translation":"The new car smell is because of the **leather** seats."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagdudulot ng matinding pananabik, interes, o kagalakan para sa isang bagay na inaasahan o paparating.
etymology: From nakapang- + duplicated first syllable of root sa- + sabik (eager). It functions as an adjective describing something that causes eagerness.
original_explanation: That feeling you get waiting for the 12.12 sale to start, the last 2 minutes of a close basketball game, or the cliffhanger ending of your favorite series. It's the 'Abangan!' of your life. It makes you sit on the edge of your seat, wanting to know what happens next.
usage_notes: Used to describe events, stories, or prospects that generate excitement and anticipation. Can be used interchangeably with 'kapanapanabik'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakapananabik** ang mga huling tagpo ng pelikula.","translation":"The final scenes of the movie are **exciting**."},{"sentence":"Isang **nakapananabik** na paglalakbay ang naghihintay sa atin.","translation":"A **thrilling** journey awaits us."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbaba mula sa isang mataas na lugar, tulad ng hagdanan, bundok, o entablado.
original_explanation: Basically, to go down. It's what you do when your mom calls you from the first floor for the 5th time. It sounds more formal and dramatic than just 'bumaba'. You can imagine a queen `pumanaog` from her throne or a beauty queen `pumanaog` from the stage.
usage_notes: A more formal or literary term for 'bumaba' (to go down). Often heard in formal speeches, literature, or religious contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang hari ay **pumanaog** mula sa kanyang trono upang salubungin ang mga bisita.","translation":"The king **descended** from his throne to greet the visitors."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng misa, **pumanaog** ang pari mula sa altar.","translation":"After the mass, the priest **went down** from the altar."}]

translation: manner of release; act of being released/shown
meaning_filipino: Ang paraan o sirkumstansya ng paglabas mula sa isang lugar o pagiging hayag sa publiko, tulad ng isang pelikula o produkto.
original_explanation: This is the "how" of something coming out. It could be how a prisoner was released, how a movie premiered (was it a blockbuster opening?), or how your secret *pagkain* stash in the office fridge was discovered. It's all about the grand reveal or the great escape.
usage_notes: Focuses on the circumstances or method of an exit, release, or publication.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-uusapan pa rin ang misteryosong **pagkakalabas** niya sa bilangguan.","translation":"His mysterious **release** from prison is still being talked about."},{"sentence":"Matagumpay ang naging **pagkakalabas** ng bagong album ng banda.","translation":"The **release** of the band's new album was successful."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian o kalagayan ng hindi pagkakatulad ng dalawa o higit pang bagay, tao, o ideya.
original_explanation: This is the classic "spot the difference" word. It's what makes Jollibee Chickenjoy different from McDo's. It's the `pagkakaiba` in your political views versus your Tito's. It’s the reason you say "iba 'to" (this is different) when you taste something unexpectedly good. The space between "what is" and "what is not."
usage_notes: Used to compare two or more things.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **pagkakaiba** ng \"ng\" at \"nang\"?","translation":"What is the **difference** between \"ng\" and \"nang\"?"},{"sentence":"Malaki ang **pagkakaiba** ng buhay sa probinsya at sa siyudad.","translation":"There is a big **difference** between life in the province and in the city."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpasok o pagkanlong sa ilalim ng isang bagay (tulad ng payong o silong) kasama ang iba, karaniwan upang maiwasan ang ulan. Sa ibang konteksto, tumutukoy sa pagdaraos ng kasal ng magkapatid sa loob ng iisang taon.
original_explanation: Like when you have to share one tiny payong with your crush during a downpour. Instant movie scene! Or when siblings get married in the same year, and the elders say it's bad luck because it's 'sukob'. This verb is the action of doing that.
usage_notes: Can refer to sharing physical shelter or to the superstition of siblings marrying within the same year, which is believed to bring bad luck.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumukob** muna kami sa ilalim ng puno habang hinihintay tumila ang ulan.","translation":"We first **took shelter** under a tree while waiting for the rain to stop."},{"sentence":"Pinayuhan sila ng matatanda na huwag **sumukob** sa taon ng kanilang kasal.","translation":"The elders advised them not to have their weddings **in the same year**."}]

translation: (sarcastic) "Oh, so you're a social media manager now?"
meaning_filipino: Isang sarkastikong ekspresyon na ginagamit upang tukuyin ang isang tao na nag-aasal na parang isang eksperto sa social media, o kapag ang isang post ay masyadong pinaghandaan o "curated".
etymology: Isang meme na nagmula sa kulturang online sa Pilipinas, na idinadagdag ang salitang beki na "yarn" sa "social media manager".
original_explanation: The ultimate clapback for that friend who posts everything with a perfectly crafted caption, 10 aesthetically pleasing photos, and a call-to-action. "Feeling social media manager yarn?" is how you jokingly call out someone for trying too hard online. The 'yarn' (from 'iyan') adds that iconic Pinoy gay lingo sass. It’s a meme, an attitude, a lifestyle.
usage_notes: Purong slang at ginagamit sa di-pormal at mapagbirong konteksto, lalo na sa social media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng caption mo sa IG post mo, teh! **Social media manager yarn**?","translation":"Your caption on your IG post is so good, sis! **Trying to be a social media manager, are we**?"},{"sentence":"Grabe, bawat galaw naka-story. **Social media manager yarn**?","translation":"Wow, every move is on your story. **Feeling like a social media manager now, huh**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpunta at pagiging parte ng isang pagtitipon, kaganapan, o pulong.
etymology: Mula sa salitang "dalo" (pagdalo) at ang gitlaping "-um-".
original_explanation: Showing up. What you do when there's free food at a party, a mandatory company meeting, or a Zoom call you could've just read in an email. It's the opposite of ghosting an event.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa pisikal o birtwal na presensya sa isang okasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigit isandaang katao ang **dumalo** sa kanyang kaarawan.","translation":"More than one hundred people **attended** his birthday party."},{"sentence":"Hindi ako nakapagtrabaho kahapon dahil **dumalo** ako sa isang seminar.","translation":"I wasn't able to work yesterday because I **attended** a seminar."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagmamadali sa isang tao o sa isang proseso upang mapabilis ito.
etymology: From Spanish `apura` (to hurry). The `pag-` prefix and reduplication of the first vowel `a` form a noun for the action of rushing someone.
original_explanation: This is what your mom does when the whole family is already 15 minutes late for church. It's the "Bilisan mo!" energy. In the office, it's your boss following up on a task 5 minutes after they gave it to you. The opposite of "chill lang".
usage_notes: Distinct from `pagmamadali` (the act of rushing oneself). `Pag-aapura` is often done *to* someone or something else.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi maganda ang resulta kapag may **pag-aapura** sa trabaho.","translation":"The result isn't good when there's **hurrying** in the work."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pag-aapura** sa mga empleyado ay nagdulot ng tensyon.","translation":"His **act of rushing** the employees caused tension."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paniniwala o konsepto ng isang diyos, espiritu, o di-pisikal na nilalang na nagkatawang-tao. Ang pagsasakatawan ng isang katangian o ideya.
original_explanation: Yung konsepto na ang isang diyos o espiritu ay nag-level up at nagkaroon ng physical body. Sa relihiyon, ito ang pagiging tao ni Kristo. Sa modern pop culture, 'pag sinabi mong "Siya ang engkarnasyon ng kasipagan," ibig sabihin, kung magiging tao ang salitang 'kasipagan', siya 'yun. The living, breathing embodiment of a concept.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa teolohiya at pilosopiya, ngunit ginagamit din sa matalinhagang paraan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **Engkarnasyon** ay isang mahalagang doktrina sa Kristiyanismo.","translation":"The **Incarnation** is an important doctrine in Christianity."},{"sentence":"Para sa akin, siya ang **engkarnasyon** ng tunay na kagandahan.","translation":"For me, she is the **incarnation** of true beauty."}]

translation: to be sarcastic, to mock with irony
meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng mga salitang kabaligtaran ng tunay na kahulugan upang manudyo, manlibak, o magpahiwatig ng pagkadismaya; sarkasmo.
original_explanation: This is the OG Filipino "sarcasm." It's saying "Ang galing mo naman!" when your friend trips on a flat surface. To mang-uyam is to use words that praise but your tone screams "You're an idiot." It's a more intellectual form of mangutya.
usage_notes: Carries a strong sense of irony or derisive wit, often more subtle than 'mangutya'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"\"Napakasipag mo naman,\" **pang-uuyam** niya sa kasamang laging huli.","translation":"\"You're so diligent,\" he said **sarcastically** to his colleague who is always late."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **mang-uyam** sa mga desisyon ng gobyerno.","translation":"He likes to **mock with irony** the government's decisions."}]

meaning_filipino: Ihiwalay o ibuklat nang malapad ang mga hita o binti.
etymology: i- (causative prefix) + bukaka (spread apart, usually legs)
original_explanation: That awkward moment in a PE class during stretching exercises. "Okay class, ibukaka ang mga binti!" It's all about creating space, whether you're doing yoga or trying to make room on a crowded jeepney bench.
usage_notes: Primarily refers to spreading the legs. Can be considered impolite to say in certain contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan ng gymnastics coach ang mga atleta na **ibukaka** ang kanilang mga binti para sa stretching.","translation":"The gymnastics coach instructed the athletes to **spread** their legs **apart** for stretching."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong masyadong **ibukaka** ang iyong mga paa habang nakaupo.","translation":"Don't **spread** your feet too far **apart** while sitting."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na palaging nangungutya, namimintas, o nagsasabi ng masasamang bagay tungkol sa iba upang sila ay maliitin.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'mang-' at ang salitang-ugat na 'lait' (insulto), na may pag-uulit ng unang pantig ng ugat ('la').
original_explanation: That's your basher, your hater, the troll in your comments section. The 'manlalait' is someone who gets their kicks from pointing out your flaws, whether real or imagined. They're the Marites who graduated to a professional level of negativity. Sila yung laging may 'pero...' sa bawat achievement mo.
usage_notes: A strongly negative term for a person who habitually belittles others.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **manlalait**; purihin mo na lang ang gawa ng iba.","translation":"Don't be an **insulter**; just praise the work of others."},{"sentence":"Puno ng mga **manlalait** ang comment section ng kanyang post.","translation":"The comment section of her post is full of **mockers**."}]

translation: wealth, richness, state of being rich
meaning_filipino: Ang katangian o kalagayan ng pagiging sagana sa salapi, ari-arian, o yaman.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate goal of your side hustles, the reason you play the lottery, and why your tita in the States keeps sending balikbayan boxes. It's not just about having money, it's the *state* of being rich—the 'sana all' moment when someone posts their European vacation.
usage_notes: "Pagka-" is a prefix that turns an adjective into a noun describing the state or quality of that adjective.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkamayaman** ay hindi laging sukatan ng tunay na kaligayahan.","translation":"**Wealth** is not always the measure of true happiness."},{"sentence":"Ipinakita niya ang kanyang **pagkamayaman** sa pamamagitan ng pagbili ng mamahaling sasakyan.","translation":"He showed off his **richness** by buying an expensive car."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal para sa 'maganda,' na karaniwang ginagamit sa swardspeak o gay lingo.
etymology: From 'ganda' (beauty), likely influenced by gay lingo's playful and often flamboyant word formations.
original_explanation: The fabulous, upgraded, and often pageant-esque version of 'ganda.' It's not just beautiful, it's *gandara*. Popularized by Vice Ganda, it's the go-to word when someone serves a look so fierce you have to give it a name. Think of it as beauty with extra sparkle and a hair flip. 'Pak! Ang gandara mo today, sis!'
usage_notes: Primarily used in informal, conversational settings, especially among younger generations and the LGBTQ+ community. It carries a fun, celebratory tone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-transform ka talaga! From simple to **gandara** park!","translation":"You really transformed! From simple to a **gorgeous** park! (play on words)"},{"sentence":"Kailangan maging **gandara** ako para sa party mamaya.","translation":"I need to be **gorgeous** for the party later."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pang-abay na nagpapahiwatig ng kawalan ng katiyakan o posibleng mangyari.
etymology: From Spanish 'seguro' (sure, certain), but ironically used in Tagalog to mean uncertainty.
original_explanation: The national anthem of the perpetually undecided. It's the 'seen-zone' of verbal commitments. 'Pupunta ka ba?' 'Siguro.' Translation: 'I'll go if I have no other options, the weather is perfect, my horoscope is aligned, and I feel like it.'
usage_notes: Very common in daily conversation. Its meaning can range from a slight doubt to a strong probability depending on intonation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Siguro** uulan mamaya kaya magdala ka ng payong.","translation":"**Maybe** it will rain later, so bring an umbrella."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko pa alam kung sasama ako, **siguro**.","translation":"I don't know yet if I'm coming, **maybe**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang matigas at manipis na panlabas na takip ng isang itlog.
original_explanation: The crunchy, fragile thing you have to break to get to the yummy yolk and white. It’s what you accidentally get in your sinangag when you’re not careful. Also, a metaphor for someone who is overly sensitive or easily offended—mababaw ang luha or balat-sibuyas, but for eggs.
usage_notes: A compound noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa pagpukpok para hindi mapunta ang **balat ng itlog** sa iyong niluluto.","translation":"Be careful with cracking it so the **eggshell** doesn't get into what you're cooking."},{"sentence":"Ginagamit niya ang dinurog na **balat ng itlog** bilang pataba sa halaman.","translation":"She uses crushed **eggshells** as fertilizer for the plants."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pandiwa para sa pagluto ng isang bagay hanggang sa ito ay maging tustado o malutong.
original_explanation: The command you give when you want someone to make your bread crispy. 'Pakidalian, tustahin mo na 'yang tinapay!' It's the action of turning something into its glorious, 'tustado' form.
usage_notes: This is a verb in the object-focus, command/infinitive form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong masyadong **tustahin** ang manok at baka pumait.","translation":"Don't **roast** the chicken too much or it might become bitter."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **tustahin** ang bawang bago ilagay ang sibuyas.","translation":"You need to **toast** the garlic before adding the onions."}]

translation: to dismantle; to dissolve; to break up
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkilos ng paghihiwa-hiwalay ng mga bahagi ng isang istruktura, pagwawakas sa isang samahan, o pagputol sa isang ugnayan.
original_explanation: The formal term for 'It's over.' It's what happens to K-Pop groups, political coalitions, and, yes, your situationship. Can also apply to dismantling the stage after a concert or the Lego castle your pamangkin spent hours building. Either way, something ends.
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of organizations, structures, and relationships.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang banda na **magbuwag** pagkatapos ng sampung taon.","translation":"The band decided to **break up** after ten years."},{"sentence":"Sila ang naatasang **magbuwag** ng entablado pagkatapos ng piyesta.","translation":"They were assigned to **dismantle** the stage after the festival."}]

translation: a flick or graceful curve (of the wrist/fingers); a lash
meaning_filipino: Isang mabilis at kurbadong kilos, karaniwan ng kamay, daliri, o latigo. Maaari ring tumukoy sa marka o sakit na dulot ng hagupit nito.
original_explanation: This is the graceful flick of the wrist in traditional Filipino dance. The 'angas' in how a 'bad-ass' character flicks a cigarette. It's a movement with attitude and finesse. It can also mean the sting of a whip or a sharp, witty comeback (a verbal lash). Parang 'Barda Queen' move.
usage_notes: Can refer to both the motion and the impact/mark left by the motion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng **pilantik** ng kanyang mga daliri habang sumasayaw.","translation":"The **graceful curve** of her fingers while dancing is beautiful."},{"sentence":"Masakit ang **pilantik** ng latigo sa kanyang likod.","translation":"The **lash** of the whip on his back was painful."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng matinding pagsubok, pagdurusa, o pasakit sa buhay.
etymology: A phrase composed of `malaki` (big) and `hirap` (difficulty, hardship).
original_explanation: This is the adulting mood. Yung pag-commute mo pa lang from Cavite to Makati, malaking hirap na. It's the struggle of trying to save money while Shopee and Lazada exist. The ultimate 'Lord, pa-exit' moment.
usage_notes: Used to emphasize the severity of a struggle, challenge, or suffering, whether physical, emotional, or financial.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Malaking hirap** ang dinanas ng pamilya matapos masunugan.","translation":"The family experienced **great difficulty** after their house burned down."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi angkop, wasto, o nararapat gawin o mangyari.
