usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May mga halaman sa gubat na nagsisilbing **panggatol** sa balat.","translation":"There are plants in the forest that act as a skin **irritant**."},{"sentence":"Iwasan mo ang alikabok kung iyan ang iyong **panggatol**.","translation":"Avoid dust if that is your **allergen** (that causes itchiness)."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na takip na isinusuot sa dulo ng daliri upang maiwasan ang pagtusok ng karayom habang nananahi.
original_explanation: This is your finger's personal bodyguard against the "tira-pasok" attack of a needle. It's that little metal or plastic hat for your fingertip that your lola uses when sewing. A true lifesaver for the clumsy mananahi.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang gamitin ang **didal** para hindi ka matusok.","translation":"Don't forget to use the **thimble** so you don't get pricked."},{"sentence":"Nawawala ang paboritong **didal** ni Lola.","translation":"Grandma's favorite **thimble** is missing."}]

translation: to move back; to retract; to postpone
meaning_filipino: Ilipat ang isang bagay sa dati nitong kinalalagyan o sa mas likod na posisyon; ipagpaliban ang isang gawain o kaganapan.
original_explanation: When you're about to send that risky text but your inner tita says "Wag, 'nak!" so you iurong your thumb. Also what happens to your salary increase proposal kapag "wala pang budget." It's the act of pulling something back, whether it's a chair, a decision, or your feelings.
usage_notes: Can mean physically moving something back, retracting a statement, or postponing an event. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **iurong** mo nang kaunti ang upuan para makadaan ako.","translation":"Please **move** the chair **back** a little so I can pass."},{"sentence":"Nagpasya silang **iurong** ang kasal dahil sa pandemya.","translation":"They decided to **postpone** the wedding due to the pandemic."},{"sentence":"Hindi na niya maaaring **iurong** ang kanyang sinabi.","translation":"He can no longer **retract** what he said."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na putol, kulang, o walang isa o parehong braso o kamay.
original_explanation: This is an old, somewhat dated term for someone who has lost a hand or an arm. It's not politically correct anymore; you'd use "person with a disability" or "amputee" in formal contexts. But in the province, you might still hear a tito refer to a character in a story as "pungkol."
usage_notes: Can be considered offensive or outdated. Use with caution. "Taong may kapansanan" is the preferred modern term. Can also be used as a noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa isang lumang pelikula, ang bida ay isang bayaning **pungkol**.","translation":"In an old movie, the hero was a **one-armed** hero."},{"sentence":"Tinulungan niya ang lalaking **pungkol** na tumawid sa kalsada.","translation":"He helped the **armless** man cross the street."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos sa isang tao na magbuhat o magsakay ng kargamento.
original_explanation: Pagod ka na galing grocery, so pag-uwi mo, sisigaw ka: 'Junior! Tulong! **Papagkargahin** mo 'yung kapatid mo ng ibang pinamili!' You're making someone else make another person do the heavy lifting.
usage_notes: Causative verb for making someone carry or load something. Common in contexts of moving items, logistics, or manual labor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **papagkargahin** natin ng mga sako ng bigas sa trak?","translation":"Who will we **have load** the sacks of rice onto the truck?"},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **papagkargahin** ng mabigat ang bata.","translation":"Don't **make** the child **carry** anything heavy."}]

translation: To talk animatedly (and spit while doing so)
meaning_filipino: Isang idyomatikong paglalarawan sa isang taong masiglang-masigla o galit na nagsasalita, na nagiging sanhi ng pagtalsik ng kaniyang laway.
original_explanation: We all have that one tito or tita. When they get super passionate about a topic—whether it's politics, sports, or the latest chismis—they talk so fast and so loud that you need a tiny umbrella. It's not just talking, it's a performance with special effects (i.e., saliva spray). When someone is 'sabog ang laway', you listen with your ears and dodge with your face.
usage_notes: A very descriptive and somewhat humorous idiom. Used to describe someone in a heightened emotional state of speaking.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Galit na galit si boss kanina, **sabog ang laway** habang nagsisigaw.","translation":"The boss was so angry earlier, he was **spitting while shouting**."},{"sentence":"Kapag nagkukuwento siya tungkol sa basketball, talagang **sabog ang laway** niya.","translation":"When he tells stories about basketball, he really **talks animatedly (and spits)**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marahas o biglaang paghila o pag-agaw sa isang bagay na nakakabit o nakasuksok.
original_explanation: That feeling when a snatcher on a jeepney grabs your phone—that's paglabnot. It's also the motion of angrily yanking out a weed from your garden or pulling a loose thread that unravels your whole sweater. It's a quick, forceful pull. Think 'Hala, na-snatch!'
usage_notes: Implies a sudden, forceful, and often violent pulling motion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang marahas na **paglabnot** sa kanyang kuwintas ay nag-iwan ng marka sa kanyang leeg.","translation":"The violent **snatching** of her necklace left a mark on her neck."},{"sentence":"Nainis siya sa damo kaya't sunod-sunod ang ginawa niyang **paglabnot** dito.","translation":"He was annoyed by the weeds, so he did a series of abrupt **pulling** on them."}]

translation: to mess up; to make into a mess
meaning_filipino: Gawing magulo, wasakin, o sirain ang ayos ng isang bagay; ihalintulad sa magulong itsura ng sampurado.
etymology: Mula sa "sampurado" at idinugtong ang hulaping "-hin". Ang makabagong kahulugan ay nagmula sa magulo at pinaghalong itsura ng lugaw.
original_explanation: Figuratively, this means to wreck something completely. Imagine your well-organized Excel sheet after your boss makes 'minor' changes. That's 'sinampurado'. It's turning something neat into a chaotic, sticky mess, much like the porridge it's named after. 'Huwag mo sampuraduhin ang plano!'
usage_notes: Ito ay isang kolokyal o impormal na pandiwa. Mayroon itong literal na kahulugan na "gawing sampurado" ngunit mas madalas na ginagamit sa makasagisag na paraan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ba ang nagsabi sa iyong **sampuraduhin** ang ayos ng mga gamit ko?","translation":"Who told you to **mess up** the arrangement of my things?"},{"sentence":"Nangialam na naman siya kaya **sinampurado** niya ang buong sistema.","translation":"He meddled again, so he **made a mess** of the whole system."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na sisidlan, karaniwang yari sa katad o tela, na ginagamit upang paglagyan ng pera, mga kard, at iba pang mahahalagang personal na gamit.
original_explanation: Your life's summary in a foldable rectangle. It holds your cash (or lack thereof), your expired IDs, and pictures of your loved ones. The state of your kartera at the end of the month is a valid 'hugot' line.
usage_notes: While it can mean purse, it's more commonly used for a wallet (for men or women). 'Pitaka' is a more native-sounding synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawala ang kanyang **kartera** sa loob ng jeep.","translation":"He/She lost his/her **wallet** inside the jeep."},{"sentence":"Puno ng resibo pero walang pera ang **kartera** ko.","translation":"My **wallet** is full of receipts but has no money."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-ilag o paglayo sa isang tao, bagay, o sitwasyon upang hindi ito makaharap o maranasan.
original_explanation: That ninja move you do when you see your tita who always asks 'Kailan ka ikakasal?' at a family reunion. Also, your strategy when you see someone you owe money to at the mall. Social distancing before it was cool.
usage_notes: Can also function as an adjective-like root, e.g., 'iwas-pusoy' (card-dodging game).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-**iwas** sa problema ay hindi solusyon.","translation":"**Avoidance** of the problem is not a solution."},{"sentence":"Mabilis ang kanyang pag-**iwas** sa paparating na sasakyan.","translation":"His **evasion** of the oncoming vehicle was quick."}]

meaning_filipino: Mag-alok ng isang produkto o serbisyo kapalit ng pera.
original_explanation: The official verb of the Filipino hustle. From the palengke vendor shouting 'Bili na kayo!', to your officemate who has a side hustle selling perfume, to your Facebook friend posting 'PM for price.' To sell is to survive, and sometimes, to thrive.
usage_notes: The basic, infinitive form of the verb 'to sell'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **magbenta** ng mga lumang gamit online para magkapera.","translation":"She decided to **sell** old things online to earn money."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **magbenta** ng ice cream kapag tag-ulan.","translation":"It's hard to **sell** ice cream during the rainy season."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglitaw o pagbuo ng isang bukol, umbok, o maga sa isang bahagi ng katawan o sa isang ibabaw.
original_explanation: The physical result of walking into a glass door. It's that lump that suddenly appears, screaming 'I'm clumsy!' It can also refer to the bulging of muscles, like 'yung pamumukol ng bicep ng gym-goer mong friend.
usage_notes: Can refer to a bump from an injury or the bulging of muscles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kitang-kita ang **pamumukol** ng kanyang mga braso dahil sa pagbubuhat ng mabibigat.","translation":"The **bulging** of his arms is very visible from lifting heavy weights."},{"sentence":"Pinatingnan niya sa doktor ang **pamumukol** sa kanyang likod.","translation":"She had the doctor check the **lump** on her back."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lihim na kasunduan o pagkakaisa ng dalawa o higit pang tao upang magsagawa ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay masama o labag sa batas.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "pakat" na may panlaping "sa- -an". Ang "pakat" mismo ay maaaring kaugnay ng "sangkat".
original_explanation: This is the chismis version of a corporate merger. It's when people team up on the down-low to do something shady. Think of politicians plotting, or your officemates having a secret "sapakatan" to all call in sick on the same day. It’s a conspiracy, but with a more local, "tayo-tayo lang" vibe.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng pulitika, krimen, o negosyo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nabunyag ang **sapakatan** ng mga opisyal upang itaas ang presyo ng bilihin.","translation":"The **collusion** of the officials to raise the price of goods was exposed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang kilos ng pagbuo ng isang katanungan upang makakuha ng impormasyon. Ito ay ang kasalukuyang anyo ng pandiwang 'magtanong'.
original_explanation: That nosy tita at the family reunion: "Kailan ka mag-aasawa?" "Magkano sahod mo?" She is perpetually nagtatanong. It's also you in a meeting, trying to sound smart by asking a "clarifying question" that you already know the answer to.
usage_notes: Ito ang imperpektibong aspekto (present tense) ng pandiwang 'magtanong', na naglalarawan ng isang patuloy na kilos.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagi siyang **nagtatanong** sa klase.","translation":"He is always **asking** questions in class."},{"sentence":"**Nagtatanong** lang po, saan ang pinakamalapit na istasyon ng tren?","translation":"Just **asking**, where is the nearest train station?"}]

translation: something that is mentally taxing (colloquial); something that causes bleeding
meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay na nagiging sanhi ng pagdurugo. Sa kolokyal na gamit, tumutukoy ito sa isang gawain na napakahirap sa pag-iisip, na parang 'nagpapadugo ng ilong.'
original_explanation: Literally, it's something that makes you bleed. But 99% of the time, you'll hear this used for something that gives you a 'nosebleed'—Filipino slang for struggling with a complex problem or difficult English. That advanced calculus exam? Pampadugo. Trying to understand a legal document? Pampadugo. Listening to your boss use corporate jargon for 30 minutes? Definitely pampadugo.
usage_notes: The colloquial meaning related to 'nosebleed' (pampadugo ng ilong) is extremely common and refers to mental exhaustion, not literal bleeding.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagsusulit sa abogasya ay tunay na **pampadugo** ng utak.","translation":"The bar exam is truly **mentally taxing** (lit. brain-bleeding)."},{"sentence":"Ayokong kausapin 'yan, **pampadugo** ng ilong kausap.","translation":"I don't want to talk to him, talking to him is **mentally exhausting** (lit. nosebleed-inducing)."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan, makina, o kagamitan na may partikular na tungkulin o gamit, lalo na sa agham o teknolohiya.
original_explanation: A formal word for 'gadget' or 'machine.' It's what your Tita calls the new air fryer she can't figure out how to use: 'Ano ba itong aparatong ito?' It's also used to refer to the complex machinery of government or an organization, like the 'aparato ng hustisya' (apparatus of justice).
usage_notes: Can refer to a single device or a complex system of equipment or bureaucracy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May bagong **aparato** sa laboratoryo para sa mas mabilis na pagsusuri.","translation":"There is new **equipment** in the laboratory for faster analysis."},{"sentence":"Ang buong **aparato** ng gobyerno ay kumilos upang tumugon sa kalamidad.","translation":"The entire government **apparatus** mobilized to respond to the calamity."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paggamot sa balat ng hayop gamit ang mga kemikal upang ito ay maging katad o leather.
original_explanation: This is the glow-up process for animal skin. It's the spa treatment that turns it from something raw into the durable leather for your shoes, bags, and belts. Think of it as the 'before and after' of leather goods.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang teknikal na termino na may kaugnayan sa paggawa ng katad at hindi para sa pagpapa-itim ng balat sa ilalim ng araw (magpa-araw).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natutunan niya kung paano **magkulti** ng balat ng baka mula sa kanyang lolo na isang sapatero.","translation":"He learned how to **tan** cowhide from his grandfather who was a shoemaker."},{"sentence":"Mahirap at matagal ang proseso ng pagkulti ng balat para maging de-kalidad na leather.","translation":"The process of tanning hide to become high-quality leather is difficult and long."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpunta sa isang lugar para mamasyal o ang pagdalaw sa isang tao.
original_explanation: This is the "action" version of `pasyal`. When your Tita from the US comes home, she'll say, "*Pasyalin* natin lahat ng kamag-anak!" (Let's visit all our relatives!). It can also mean to tour a place: "*Pasyalin* natin ang buong Intramuros." (Let's go see all of Intramuros). It's more goal-oriented than the aimless `mamasyal`.
usage_notes: Focuses on the object of the visit, whether it's a person or a place. Contrast with `pasyalan` (to visit AT a place).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bukas, plano naming **pasyalin** ang aming lola sa probinsya.","translation":"Tomorrow, we plan **to visit** our grandmother in the province."},{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **pasyalin** ang mga museo kapag nasa ibang bansa ka.","translation":"Don't forget **to visit** the museums when you're in another country."}]

translation: will not be allowed, not permissible
meaning_filipino: Hindi bibigyan ng pahintulot o permiso; isang pagbabawal sa isang gawain o kilos sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: Your mom's final answer when you ask to go on an overnight trip at 16. It's the bouncer at the club telling you your slippers are not proper attire. It's a hard 'no' that carries the weight of absolute authority, often followed by 'Habang nakatira ka sa pamamahay ko!'
usage_notes: This is a future tense verb form expressing prohibition. It's a strong and definitive 'no'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Di-mapapayagan** ang paggamit ng cellphone habang nagmamaneho.","translation":"Using a cellphone while driving **will not be allowed**."},{"sentence":"Sinabi ng guro na **di-mapapayagan** ang sinumang mahuhuli sa klase.","translation":"The teacher said that anyone who is late for class **will not be permitted**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maalat na sawsawan o pampalasa na gawa sa isda na pina-ferment. Kilala sa Tagalog bilang patis.
original_explanation: The Filipino's secret weapon in the kitchen. It's that 'what's that smell?' ingredient that magically makes everything taste better. Known locally as 'patis', it's the soulmate of calamansi and sili for the perfect sawsawan.
usage_notes: The native term 'patis' is overwhelmingly more common in all contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nilagyan niya ng **fish sauce** ang sinigang para lumasa.","translation":"She added **fish sauce** to the sinigang to enhance the flavor."},{"sentence":"In some restaurants, they ask if you want **fish sauce** or soy sauce.","translation":"Sa ibang restoran, tinatanong nila kung gusto mo ng **patis** o toyo."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang estado o teritoryo na pinamumunuan ng isang hari o reyna.
original_explanation: The OG "shared universe." Ito 'yung lugar kung saan nagaganap lahat ng drama sa mga fairytale at fantasy series. 'Yung kaharian sa Encantadia, 'yung Westeros, o 'yung bahay niyo kung saan ang nanay mo ang reyna.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa mga pormal na usapan, panitikan, at sa mga kuwentong-bayan o pantasya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **reyno** ng Berbanya ay isang tanyag na tagpuan sa Ibong Adarna.","translation":"The **kingdom** of Berbanya is a famous setting in Ibong Adarna."},{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang maglakbay sa iba't ibang **reyno** sa Europa.","translation":"He dreams of traveling to different **kingdoms** in Europe."}]

translation: to be confused; to become bewildered
meaning_filipino: Ang mawalan ng tamang pag-iisip o direksyon dahil sa pagkalito, pagkabigla, o labis na gawain; maguluhan nang husto.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling mo paggising mo, Lunes pala pero akala mo Sabado. O 'yung state mo after ka i-ghost ng ka-talking stage mo for 3 months. "Ano'ng nangyari?!" You're mentally scrambled, like your brain is buffering.
usage_notes: Describes a more intense state of confusion than 'malito'. It implies being disoriented or dazed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-panic para hindi ka **matuliro** sa gitna ng emergency.","translation":"Don't panic so you won't **get bewildered** in the middle of an emergency."},{"sentence":"**Natuliro** siya sa dami ng utos ng kanyang amo.","translation":"She **became confused** by the sheer number of her boss's commands."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na laging handa o may ugaling magbigay ng tulong sa kapwa, madalas nang kusa.
etymology: From the affix 'pala-' (indicating fondness or habit) + 'tulong' (help).
original_explanation: That one friend who will help you move apartments, lend you money before payday, and listen to your rants at 3 AM. The MVP of the friend group. They have a hero complex, but in a good way.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay isang lider na **palatulong** sa kanyang mga nasasakupan.","translation":"He is a leader who is **helpful** to his constituents."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa pagiging **palatulong**, marami ang nagmamahal kay Aling Nena sa kanilang komunidad.","translation":"Because of being **helpful**, many love Aling Nena in their community."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang kilos na ginagawa nang dahan-dahan, banayad, at walang pagmamadali.
original_explanation: This is the opposite of your Grab driver pag 5 minutes na lang late ka na sa work. It's the chill, 'bahala na' pace of life. Think of how lola stirs her coffee, or how you walk away from drama. That's `luway`.
usage_notes: Often used in literary or older contexts. Synonymous with 'dahan-dahan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglakad siya nang **luway** papalapit sa akin.","translation":"She walked **slowly** towards me."},{"sentence":"Gawin mo nang **luway** ang pag-aayos para hindi masira.","translation":"Do the arranging **gently** so it won't break."}]

translation: to give importance; to value; to appreciate
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng importansya, pagkilala sa kahalagahan, o pagpapakita ng pagtanaw ng utang na loob sa isang tao, bagay, o konsepto.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung 'sana all' moment. To **magpahalaga** is to see someone's worth. Yung tipong, 'Hindi ka niya pinahalagahan? Dito ka na lang sa'kin.' It's giving someone the value they deserve, 'di tulad ng ex mo. Charot. It's the opposite of taking things for granted.
usage_notes: This verb is crucial in expressing appreciation and value, both material and emotional.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat tayong **magpahalaga** sa ating kalikasan.","translation":"We should **give importance** to our environment."},{"sentence":"Matuto kang **magpahalaga** sa mga taong nagmamahal sa iyo.","translation":"Learn to **appreciate** the people who love you."}]

translation: to have something insured; to ensure
meaning_filipino: Kumuha ng seguro para sa isang tao o ari-arian; o tiyakin at siguruhin ang isang bagay.
etymology: From 'i-' (causative prefix) + 'pa-' (causative prefix) + 'seguro' (sure, insurance), from Spanish 'seguro'.
original_explanation: This has two main vibes. First, the adulting one: "Kailangan mo nang **ipaseguro** 'yang kotse mo." (Get your car insured). Second, the "praning friend" vibe: "Okay, aalis na ako. **Ipaseguro** mo lang na naka-lock ang pinto, ha?" (Just make sure the door is locked, okay?). It's about getting protection, either from an insurance company or from your own forgetfulness.
usage_notes: Can mean 'to insure' (formal financial context) or 'to make sure/ensure' (more common in everyday speech).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga na **ipaseguro** ang iyong bahay laban sa sunog.","translation":"It's important **to have** your house **insured** against fire."},{"sentence":"**Ipaseguro** mo na kumain ka na bago uminom ng gamot.","translation":"**Ensure** that you have eaten before taking medicine."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hindi pagdalo o pagpasok sa isang itinakdang pagtitipon, klase, o trabaho.
original_explanation: The opposite of "present!" It's what you do when you're "sick" (read: tinatamad), or when there's a new season of your favorite Netflix series. To **mag-absen** is a high-stakes game. Do it too often in school, and you'll fail. Do it too often at work, and you'll have a one-on-one with HR. Use your absences wisely.
usage_notes: A Taglish-derived verb, very common in schools and workplaces. The formal equivalent is 'lumiban'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mag-a-absen** bukas dahil may mahalagang pagsusulit tayo.","translation":"Don't **be absent** tomorrow because we have an important exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyon na nagpapahiwatig ng pagsang-ayon o pagkakaugnay sa isang sitwasyon o damdamin na ipinapakita ng iba.
etymology: Taglish slang na pinagsamang "mood" (Ingles) at "yarn" (isang kolokyal na bersyon ng "iyan").
original_explanation: The Gen Z version of "Same!" or "Relate much?". When your friend posts a meme about being tired and broke, and you feel it in your bones, you comment "mood yarn." It’s the official stamp of approval for a shared feeling or vibe. 'Yarn' is the cutesy, internet-speak version of 'iyan'.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa social media (Twitter, TikTok, Facebook) bilang komento o reaksyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Friend 1: \"Gusto ko lang humiga at kumain ng ice cream.\" Friend 2: \"**Mood yarn**!\"","translation":"Friend 1: \"I just want to lie down and eat ice cream.\" Friend 2: \"**That's the mood**!\""},{"sentence":"Nakita niya ang post tungkol sa pagod sa trabaho at nag-comment siya ng, \"**Mood yarn**.\"","translation":"She saw the post about being tired from work and she commented, \"**Same mood**.\""}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan kung saan ang isang tao, hayop, o halaman ay pinamumugaran o dinadapuan ng mga maliliit na insektong tinatawag na tungaw.
original_explanation: The ultimate horror story for anyone with a pet. It's when your dog starts scratching like crazy and you realize he's being attacked by tiny vampire-like pests. 'Kailangan na nating ipa-groom si Bantay, baka **tungawin** na 'yan sa sobrang kati!'
usage_notes: The root word 'tungaw' refers to a type of small mite or chigger, often found on poultry.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kapag hindi nilinis ang kulungan, maaaring **tungawin** ang mga alagang manok.","translation":"If the coop isn't cleaned, the pet chickens might **get infested with mites**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o takdang pook kung saan maaaring bumaba ang mga pasahero mula sa isang pampublikong sasakyan.
original_explanation: The place where you shout "Para po!" to the jeepney driver. It's the designated spot to get off, but let's be real, for jeepneys, anywhere is a **babaan** as long as you shout loud enough. The opposite is 'sakayan' (loading zone).
usage_notes: The stress is on the second syllable: ba-BA-an. Not to be confused with the verb 'babaan' (to lower something for someone), which has a different stress pattern.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dito lang po sa tamang **babaan**.","translation":"Just here at the proper **drop-off point**."},{"sentence":"Bawal magsakay at magbaba kung hindi sa tamang **babaan**.","translation":"It's forbidden to load and unload passengers if not at the proper **unloading zone**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang propesyon o gawain ay ang pagsusulat ng mga aklat, artikulo, kuwento, o iba pang akdang pampanitikan.
original_explanation: From the content creator scripting their next vlog to the journalist chasing a deadline, to the novelist building worlds in a coffee shop—they are all a manunulat. They are powered by coffee, anxiety, and the fear of a blank page. Sila yung laging may 'what if' sa isip at kayang gawing nobela ang isang simpleng 'Hi.'
usage_notes: A general and widely used term for anyone who writes, professionally or as a hobby.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang sikat na **manunulat** ng mga nobelang romansa si Martha.","translation":"Martha is a famous **writer** of romance novels."},{"sentence":"Ang mga **manunulat** ay may mahalagang papel sa paghubog ng kultura.","translation":"**Writers** have an important role in shaping culture."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto o proseso ng pagiging iba; isang alterasyon o modipikasyon sa dating kalagayan.
original_explanation: The only constant thing in the world, sabi nila. It's what politicians promise every election, what you tell yourself every New Year's ('magda-diet na talaga ako'), and what happens to your feelings for your crush after you find out their toxic tweets.
usage_notes: A very common and versatile word for any kind of change, from personal to societal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Handa ka na ba para sa mga **pagbabago** sa iyong buhay?","translation":"Are you ready for the **changes** in your life?"},{"sentence":"Ang **pagbabago** ng klima ay isang seryosong isyu.","translation":"Climate **change** is a serious issue."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagpapaandar ng bangka o sasakyang pantubig sa pamamagitan ng paggaod.
original_explanation: The original engine. Before outboard motors, the 'tagagaod' was your human-powered Uber for crossing rivers. They have arms of steel and can probably give you the latest chismis from the other side of the water. In group work, they're the ones doing all the heavy lifting to move the project forward.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **tagagaod** ay nagsimula nang pumalaot pagsikat ng araw.","translation":"The **rowers** started heading to sea at sunrise."},{"sentence":"Upang manalo sa karera, kailangang maging sabay-sabay ang mga **tagagaod**.","translation":"To win the race, the **oarsmen** need to be synchronized."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkayod o pagpino sa isang bagay, karaniwan ay pagkain, gamit ang isang kudkuran.
original_explanation: The command you give when you need more cheese for the pichi-pichi. "Bes, gadgarin mo pa 'tong keso, kulang pa eh." It's the verb form of making things small and ready for mixing.
usage_notes: The verb form of 'gadgad'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **gadgarin** ang niyog para makagawa ng gata.","translation":"You need **to grate** the coconut to make coconut milk."},{"sentence":"**Gadgarin** mo na ang mga karot para sa salad.","translation":"**Grate** the carrots for the salad."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ikinulong sa bilangguan bilang parusa sa isang krimen o habang naghihintay ng paglilitis. Maaari ring tumukoy sa kalagayan ng pagkakakulong.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "bilango" (isang pangalan na ibinigay sa mga taong ipinatapon sa Pilipinas mula sa Vilanova de Arousa, Galicia). Ang modernong kahulugan ay naiimpluwensyahan ng "bilangguan" (prison).
original_explanation: The OG term for someone 'in a relationship' with the Bilibid. Sila 'yung mga taong ang status ay 'It's Complicated... with the Justice System.' Pwede ring adjective para i-describe 'yung feeling mo 'pag 'di ka pinayagan ng nanay mo lumabas ng bahay. 'Feeling bilanggo ako dito sa kwarto ko!'
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pangngalan (isang preso) o pang-uri (nakakulong).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatakas ang **bilanggo** mula sa kulungan kagabi.","translation":"The **prisoner** escaped from the jail last night."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman niyang siya ay **bilanggo** sa sarili niyang tahanan.","translation":"She felt **imprisoned** in her own home."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng isang ibabaw na magaspang, hindi makinis, at may hindi pantay na tekstura.
original_explanation: This is the texture of your siko (elbow) when you forget to put on lotion. It's the feeling of un-sanded wood or a cheap, low-thread-count bedsheet. In a person, it can describe a rough, unrefined character, like a "brusko" tito from the province.
usage_notes: Primarily refers to physical texture but can be used metaphorically for behavior.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dama ko ang **pagkamaligasgas** ng pader na hindi pa napipinturahan.","translation":"I could feel the **roughness** of the unpainted wall."},{"sentence":"Inireklamo niya ang **pagkamaligasgas** ng tela ng damit.","translation":"She complained about the **coarseness** of the dress's fabric."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tuluy-tuloy na paggalaw ng isang likido, gas, kuryente, o maging ng mga ideya at impormasyon.
original_explanation: Think of the EDSA traffic, but the opposite. It's that smooth, uninterrupted movement. It's the 'daloy' of your internet connection when you're streaming Netflix in HD without buffering. It's the 'daloy' of conversation with your BFF na walang preno. It's the ideal state of everything, from traffic to chismis.
usage_notes: Used for liquids (water, blood), traffic, electricity, and abstract concepts (story plot, conversation).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahina ang **daloy** ng tubig sa gripo.","translation":"The **flow** of water from the faucet is weak."},{"sentence":"Sinusundan niya ang **daloy** ng kuwento.","translation":"He is following the **flow** of the story."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang taong walang hiya, makapal ang mukha, at hindi tinatablan ng panunumbat o kritisismo.
original_explanation: This is a level-up from "makapal ang mukha". It's for that person who has the audacity of a cockroach surviving a nuclear blast. They'll borrow money and never pay, cut in line at the MRT, and still have the nerve to ask you for another favor with a smile. Their face isn't just thick, it's as thick as the earth's crust.
usage_notes: A very strong and insulting term. Use with caution.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Talagang **kapal-lupa** ang taong iyon, siya na ang may utang, siya pa ang galit.","translation":"That person is truly **shameless**; they're the one in debt, yet they're the one who's angry."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **kapal-lupa** at akuin mo ang iyong pagkakamali.","translation":"Don't be **thick-skinned** and own up to your mistake."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang damdamin ng pakikiisa, pagkaunawa, o pagkagusto sa isang tao o bagay; pagkakaroon ng magandang ugnayan.
original_explanation: This isn't just 'pity' (awa). It's more like having good vibes or chemistry with someone. When you meet a new officemate and you just... click. That's simpatya. It's the opposite of having your 'santo not matching' (hindi magkasundo ang santo).
usage_notes: Often confused with 'awa' (pity), but 'simpatya' implies a sense of liking or positive connection, not just feeling sorry for someone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis niyang nakuha ang **simpatya** ng mga botante dahil sa kanyang pagiging makamasa.","translation":"He quickly won the **rapport** of the voters because of his pro-people stance."},{"sentence":"Wala akong **simpatya** sa mga taong nanlalamang sa kapwa.","translation":"I have no **sympathy** for people who take advantage of others."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lugar kung saan naganap ang isang bangga; o ang akto ng pagbabanggaan ng dalawa o higit pang partido.
original_explanation: This is the 'TKP' (Teka, Kuha Picture) or crime scene of a car crash. The 'bangga' is the event, the 'banggaan' is often the result or the location. It can also mean a mutual crash, like when two people with opposite opinions clash in the comments section. 'Nagkaroon ng banggaan ng opinyon.'
usage_notes: The suffix '-an' can denote a place where an action occurs (collision site) or a reciprocal action (mutual collision).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinalibutan ng mga pulis ang lugar ng **banggaan**.","translation":"The police surrounded the **collision site**."},{"sentence":"Naganap ang **banggaan** ng dalawang motorsiklo dahil sa madulas na kalsada.","translation":"The **mutual collision** of two motorcycles happened because of the slippery road."}]

translation: to become like this; for things to turn out this way
meaning_filipino: Ang pagdating sa ganitong kalagayan, sitwasyon, o resulta.
original_explanation: The official verb of "Sana all" and "Paano tayo napunta dito?" It's the word you use when you're reflecting on a situation, good or bad. "Hindi ko inakalang magkakaganito tayo" can either be a hugot line for exes or a proud moment for a successful startup team. It's the "How it started vs. How it's going" of the Tagalog language.
usage_notes: Often used in reflective, dramatic, or explanatory contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko akalain na **magkakaganito** ang sitwasyon.","translation":"I didn't expect the situation **to become like this**."},{"sentence":"Bakit ba tayo **nagkaganito**? Dati naman masaya tayo.","translation":"Why did **things turn out this way** for us? We used to be happy."}]

meaning_filipino: Mayroong mga marka o tuldok na iba ang kulay sa kabuuang ibabaw.
etymology: From 'batik', meaning 'spot' or 'stain'. Reduplication 'batik-batik' intensifies this to mean 'full of spots'.
original_explanation: Parang damit na pinintahan ng toddler, o 'yung mukha mo nung high school dahil sa tigyawat. It's a pattern, usually random dots or splotches. Think dalmatian, but make it Pinoy.
usage_notes: Often used to describe patterns on animals (like a cat), fabric, or even skin conditions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pusa niya ay puti na may mga **batik-batik** na itim.","translation":"Her cat is white with black **spots**."},{"sentence":"Nagustuhan ko ang **batik-batik** na disenyo ng tela.","translation":"I liked the **spotted** design of the fabric."}]

meaning_filipino: Regalo, salapi, o anumang bagay na ibinibigay sa panahon ng Kapaskuhan.
etymology: From `paN-` + `Pasko`. `Pasko` is from Spanish 'Pascua' (originally Easter, but in the Philippines refers to Christmas). The `paN-` prefix (`pam-` before 'p') indicates something intended for or related to the root word.
original_explanation: The most awaited word from September to December. This is your 13th-month pay, the aguinaldo from your ninongs and ninangs, or the Christmas bonus you've been dreaming of to fund your holiday shopping. "Ma'am/Sir, pamasko po!" is the official line of carolers and anyone hoping for a little Christmas cheer (in cash form).
usage_notes: Can refer to a gift, money (aguinaldo), or a bonus given specifically for Christmas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natanggap mo na ba ang iyong **pamasko** mula sa kumpanya?","translation":"Have you received your **Christmas bonus** from the company?"},{"sentence":"Nag-iipon ang mga bata ng kanilang natanggap na **pamasko**.","translation":"The children are saving the **Christmas money** they received."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kabuuang hanay ng mga pangyayari, katangian, o sirkumstansya sa isang partikular na oras; estado o kondisyon.
original_explanation: Your Facebook relationship status but for everything else in life. 'It's complicated.' Can refer to your financial status ('alipin ng salapi'), emotional state ('marupok'), or the traffic on EDSA (always 'malala').
usage_notes: A very versatile word used to describe the state of almost anything.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano na ang **kalagayan** ng pasyente?","translation":"What is the patient's **condition** now?"},{"sentence":"Mahirap ang **kalagayan** ng buhay ngayon.","translation":"The **situation** of life is difficult nowadays."}]

translation: by the hundreds; in groups of a hundred
meaning_filipino: Pangkat-pangkat na tig-iisang daan; maramihan sa bilang na isang daan.
original_explanation: When 'sandaan' is not enough. This is how you describe things coming in bulk. Think Shopee parcels during a 12.12 sale, likes on a viral post, or ants heading to a dropped piece of candy. It implies a large, almost uncountable quantity grouped in hundreds.
usage_notes: Denotes distribution or grouping. It answers the question 'how?' or 'in what manner?' regarding quantity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sandaanan** ang dating ng mga turista tuwing summer.","translation":"The tourists arrive **by the hundreds** every summer."},{"sentence":"Ibinenta nila ang mga mangga nang **sandaanan**.","translation":"They sold the mangoes **in groups of a hundred**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng tiwala sa isang tao o bagay; ang pag-asa sa isang tao para sa isang gawain o responsibilidad.
etymology: From i- (causative prefix) + katiwala (steward, trustee), from root 'tiwala' (trust).
original_explanation: This is what you do when you give your friend your ATM card and PIN for "safekeeping" during a night out. Or when you tell your work bestie the *real* reason you took a sick leave. You're entrusting them with something valuable, whether it's your money or your juicy secrets.
usage_notes: The 'i-' prefix here indicates that the object of the verb is the thing being entrusted.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ikatiwala** mo sa akin ang iyong mga alalahanin.","translation":"**Entrust** your worries to me."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **ikatiwala** ang pera sa taong hindi mo kilala.","translation":"It's hard to **entrust** money to someone you don't know."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na hinahangaan dahil sa kaniyang pambihirang katapangan, tagumpay, o marangal na katangian, lalo na kung ito ay para sa kapakanan ng bayan.
etymology: Possibly from Proto-Austronesian *baRani ("brave, fearless"). In old Tagalog, 'bayani' meant someone who leads warriors in battle or a member of a community working together.
original_explanation: A **bayani** isn't just someone in a cape. It's Jose Rizal, it's the OFW sending money home, it's the frontliner during the pandemic, it's the Grab driver navigating EDSA traffic to get you your milk tea. It's anyone who shows courage and makes a sacrifice for the greater good, whether it's for the whole country or just for their family. The ultimate "sana all" of character traits.
usage_notes: Can refer to historical national heroes or modern-day everyday heroes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Jose Rizal ay isang pambansang **bayani** ng Pilipinas.","translation":"Jose Rizal is a national **hero** of the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Para sa marami, ang mga OFW ay maituturing na mga makabagong **bayani**.","translation":"For many, OFWs can be considered modern-day **heroes**."}]

translation: a hint, an allusion, an insinuation (archaic)
meaning_filipino: Isang pahiwatig o parunggit na hindi direktang sinasabi ang tunay na kahulugan; pagpaparamdam.
original_explanation: This is the ancestor of "pasaring". It's the OG "parinig". Think of your lola saying "Naku, ang mga kabataan ngayon..." while looking at you playing on your phone. It's a hint, but with the subtlety of a history book. It's so old-school, it's almost a museum piece.
usage_notes: Very rarely used in modern conversation. `Pasaring` is the common term now.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puro **pasari** ang kanyang mga sinasabi, wala man lang diretsahan.","translation":"His words are full of **allusions**, nothing is ever direct."},{"sentence":"Sa pamamagitan ng isang **pasari**, ipinahiwatig niya ang kanyang pagkadismaya.","translation":"Through an **insinuation**, he showed his disappointment."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang boluntaryong pag-alis sa isang posisyon, tungkulin, o trabaho. Maaari rin itong mangahulugan ng pagpapakawala sa isang bagay na hawak.
original_explanation: The corporate version of "I'm breaking up with you." It's what you do when the toxicity levels at work are higher than your salary. Also, literally letting go of something you're holding, like your ex's hand. #LetGoNaBes
usage_notes: Has two common meanings: resigning from a job ('magbitiw sa tungkulin') and physically letting go of an object ('magbitiw sa hawak'). Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **magbitiw** sa kanyang trabaho para mag-aral muli.","translation":"He decided **to resign** from his job to study again."},{"sentence":"**Magbitiw** ka na sa galit mo sa kanya; hindi iyon makakatulong.","translation":"**Let go** of your anger towards him; it won't help."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing pangunahin o sentro ng atensyon; bigyan ng natatanging puwang o pagkilala.
original_explanation: Think of it as giving someone or something the 'main character' energy. When a TV show features a special guest, they 'magtampok' that guest. When your group report highlights your best-researched section, you are 'nagtatampok' that part. It's about putting something in the spotlight.
usage_notes: Commonly used in media, arts, and presentations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pelikula ay **magtatampok** sa mga bagong artista ng henerasyon ngayon.","translation":"The movie will **feature** the new actors of today's generation."},{"sentence":"Nais naming **itampok** ang mga nagawa ng aming organisasyon sa nakaraang taon.","translation":"We want to **highlight** our organization's achievements from the past year."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mabigat na sasakyang pangkonstruksiyon na may malaki at mabigat na roler sa harap, ginagamit upang patagin at siksikin ang lupa, aspalto, o graba.
original_explanation: That giant, slow-moving beast you see at road construction sites that looks like it's giving the asphalt a deep-tissue massage. It's the real-life version of what you feel when you're overwhelmed with deadlines—napipison ka.
usage_notes: Often used metaphorically to mean being run over or overwhelmed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahan-dahan ang usad ng trapiko dahil sa **pison** na gumagawa sa kalsada.","translation":"The traffic is moving slowly because of the **steamroller** working on the road."}]

translation: to build; to erect; to establish
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbuo o pagtatatag ng isang estruktura, negosyo, o organisasyon.
original_explanation: This is the verb for making things stand up. You can "magtayo" a building, a sari-sari store, or a new branch of your milk tea empire. It's about establishing something from the ground up, whether it's a condo in BGC or just your tent at the beach.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical construction (build a house) or conceptual creation (establish a business).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Plano nilang **magtayo** ng bagong ospital sa aming probinsya.","translation":"They plan to **build** a new hospital in our province."},{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **magtayo** ng sarili niyang coffee shop pagkatapos mag-resign.","translation":"She decided to **establish** her own coffee shop after resigning."}]

translation: to name; to call; to dub
meaning_filipino: Magbigay ng isang partikular na pangalan, bansag, o katawagan sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you give your friend group a name ("Team Sawi"), or call your suki at the palengke "Boss". It's the act of officially or unofficially dubbing someone or something. Jose Rizal was tinaguriang "Pambansang Bayani." Your office bestie might be tinaguriang "HR" because they know all the chismis.
usage_notes: Often used in the passive form 'tagurian' or 'itinaguri'. It implies giving a title or a descriptive name, not just a personal name.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **nagtaguri** sa Pilipinas bilang 'Perlas ng Silanganan'?","translation":"Who **named** the Philippines the 'Pearl of the Orient'?"},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang kabaitan, **tinagurian** siyang 'anghel' ng kanilang komunidad.","translation":"Because of her kindness, she was **dubbed** the 'angel' of their community."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang kurbada o liko; tuwid. Maaari ring tumukoy sa pagiging prangka o tapat sa pananalita.
original_explanation: Describes a line that passed geometry class, or a person who doesn't use paligoy-ligoy (beating around the bush). A 'diretso' person will tell you if you have something between your teeth. Brutally honest, no filter, parang 'di dumaan sa HR.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang pisikal na pagiging tuwid, tulad ng linya o buhok.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumuhit ka ng isang linyang **diretso**.","translation":"Draw a **straight** line."},{"sentence":"Gusto ko siya kasi **diretso** siyang kausap.","translation":"I like him because he is a **direct** person to talk to."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging marumi dahil sa malagkit na dumi, grasa, o langis.
original_explanation: Yung feeling ng kamay mo pagkatapos kumain ng lechon o crispy pata gamit ang kamay. O yung sahig ng kusina na hindi nalinis ng isang linggo. It's that specific kind of icky, sticky dirt that makes you want to take a bath immediately.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan ng isang partikular na uri ng dumi - malagkit at mamantika.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nanggigitata** sa mantika ang kanyang mga kamay pagkatapos magprito.","translation":"His hands were **greasy** with oil after frying."},{"sentence":"Linisin mo nga 'yang mesa, **nanggigitata** na sa dumi.","translation":"Clean that table, it's already **sticky with grime**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkuha o pagdala sa isang bagay nang biglaan at mabilisan, kadalasan nang walang pahintulot.
original_explanation: The classic 'snatcher' move. Imagine a bird swooping down to grab a fish, or a thief grabbing a phone and running. That's 'tangay' (usually as 'tinangay'). It's not just 'kinuha' (taken); it has the drama of being swiftly carried away. 'Tinangay ng agos' (carried away by the current) or 'Tinangay ng magnanakaw' (snatched by a thief). It's the official word for when your wig gets snatched, literally.
usage_notes: Madalas ginagamit sa anyong pandiwa na 'tinangay' (was carried away/snatched).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tinangay** ng malakas na hangin ang mga sinampay na damit.","translation":"The strong wind **carried away** the clothes on the line."},{"sentence":"Ang cellphone ko ay **tinangay** ng snatcher sa Divisoria.","translation":"My cellphone was **snatched** by a thief in Divisoria."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang linyang iginuhit sa ibabaw ng isang salita, simbolo, o numero, karaniwan sa larangan ng matematika o tipograpiya.
original_explanation: You know that line you put on top of a letter in math to mean it's a segment, or on top of a repeating decimal? That's a 'guhit sa tuktok'. It's the crown a number wears to show it's special (or infinitely annoying).
usage_notes: Primarily a technical term in mathematics and typography.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagyan mo ng **guhit sa tuktok** ang mga numerong paulit-ulit sa desimal.","translation":"Put an **overline** on the repeating numbers in the decimal."},{"sentence":"Ang **guhit sa tuktok** ng AB ay nangangahulugang 'line segment AB'.","translation":"The **line on top** of AB means 'line segment AB'."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaki na may ugaling mapagmataas, mayabang, at hindi palakausap o palangiti.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "chiflado" (crazy, conceited), na naging "suplado" sa Filipino.
original_explanation: The male version of suplada. He's that guy in the office who never joins the "kain tayo" lunch invites, communicates only through one-word emails, and seems to think he's too cool for everyone. He might be your "terror" prof from college or the quiet, handsome guy in the corner who everyone's afraid to talk to.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to a male. The female counterpart is "suplada".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Akala ko **suplado** ang bago naming boss, pero marunong pala siyang magbiro.","translation":"I thought our new boss was **snobbish**, but he actually knows how to joke."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa pagiging **suplado** niya, walang nag-ayang lumabas sa kanya.","translation":"Because he's a **snob**, no one invited him to go out."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pahayag na nagsasabing mayroong isang tao o mga tao sa isang lugar; ginagamit din upang ipahiwatig na ang isang lugar, tulad ng banyo, ay kasalukuyang ginagamit.
original_explanation: The universal Filipino response when someone knocks on the public restroom door you're in. You don't say "Occupied!" or "Someone's in here!" You panic-shout "**May tao**!" It can also be a warning, like when you're about to gossip and your friend whispers, "Shhh, **may tao** sa likod."
usage_notes: Context is key. It can mean "someone's here" in a general sense, or "this is occupied" in the specific context of a private space like a toilet or fitting room.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumatok ako sa pinto ng banyo at may sumagot ng, '**May tao**!'","translation":"I knocked on the bathroom door and someone answered, '**It's occupied**!'"},{"sentence":"Akala ko walang nakakarinig, pero **may tao** pala sa kabilang kwarto.","translation":"I thought no one was listening, but **there was someone** in the other room."}]

translation: to be splashed on, to be spattered with
meaning_filipino: Ang aksidenteng mapatakan o tamaan ng maliit na tilamsik ng likido, putik, o anumang katulad na bagay.
etymology: From `ma-` (involuntary action prefix) + `tilabsik` (a small splash or spatter) + `-an` (location/object suffix).
original_explanation: That super annoying moment when a car speeds through a puddle and you get a free, unwanted shower of murky water. 'Yan 'yung matilabsikan. Or when you're frying hotdogs and the oil decides to attack you.
usage_notes: The `-an` suffix indicates that the subject is the one receiving the splash.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naka-puting uniporme pa naman ako nang **matilabsikan** ng putik.","translation":"I was even wearing my white uniform when I **was spattered with** mud."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa pagpiprito at baka **matilabsikan** ka ng mainit na mantika.","translation":"Be careful when frying so you won't **be splashed on** by hot oil."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang lugar na sarado, walang sapat na bentilasyon, at karaniwang may maalinsangang hangin.
original_explanation: That feeling when you enter a room that hasn't been opened in weeks. The air is thick, warm, and smells like... old air. It’s the opposite of 'presko'. Think of a packed jeepney in traffic with all the windows closed, or your cabinet full of clothes you haven't worn since 2019. That's the essence of kulob.
usage_notes: Also refers to a cooking method where food is cooked in an enclosed container, trapping heat and steam.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Amoy **kulob** ang kwarto dahil laging sarado ang mga bintana.","translation":"The room smells **stuffy** because the windows are always closed."},{"sentence":"Ang init at sobrang **kulob** sa loob ng bus.","translation":"It's hot and very **unventilated** inside the bus."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang parirala na tumutukoy sa masama, hindi kaaya-aya, o nakakahiya na pag-uugali o asal. Ang 'kapangitan' dito ay hindi pisikal kundi sa kilos o gawa.
etymology: A modern phrase combining the swardspeak term 'chararat' (hideously ugly) with the English word 'behavior.' Popularized in social media.
original_explanation: This is when the ugliness isn't on the face, but in the attitude. It's the 'ugaling chaka.' Spreading gossip? Chararat behavior. Being rude to service crew? Super chararat behavior. Not returning the money you borrowed? The ultimate chararat behavior. It's a social violation, an offense against decency and good vibes.
usage_notes: Used to call out negative or toxic actions, separate from physical appearance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya binalik ang hiniram niyang damit. Grabe, **chararat behavior**.","translation":"She didn't return the dress she borrowed. Wow, such **awful behavior**."},{"sentence":"Ang paninira sa kaibigan para lang umangat ay isang uri ng **chararat behavior**.","translation":"Putting down a friend just to get ahead is a form of **trashy conduct**."}]

translation: to be hit; to crash into
meaning_filipino: Ang maranasang mabangga o matamaan nang may lakas ng isang bagay na gumagalaw.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you're texting while crossing the street and don't see the incoming e-trike. Or when your feelings for your crush suddenly hit a wall because you found out they're 'taken'. Ouch, na-salpok ka, beshie.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of vehicular accidents or any forceful collision. The verb form is 'nasalpok' (was hit).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa pagtawid, baka ka **masalpok** ng mabilis na motor.","translation":"Be careful crossing, you might **get hit** by a fast motorcycle."},{"sentence":"Para akong **nasalpok** ng ten-wheeler truck nang malaman kong may iba na siya.","translation":"I felt like I was **hit** by a ten-wheeler truck when I found out he has someone else."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan o lugar na pinaglulutuan ng pagkain, na maaaring gumagamit ng kahoy, uling, gas, o kuryente.
original_explanation: The OG kitchen appliance. Bago pa nagkaroon ng air fryer at induction cooker, si kalan ang bida. Pwedeng de-gasul na kailangan mo pang katukin at tapikin para malaman kung may laman pa, o 'yung lumang version na de-uling na amoy pa lang, alam mong may nag-iihaw na. The throne where adobo and sinigang are born.
usage_notes: Isang pangkaraniwang gamit sa bahay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakalimutan niyang patayin ang **kalan** pagkatapos magluto ng almusal.","translation":"She forgot to turn off the **stove** after cooking breakfast."},{"sentence":"Mas gusto pa rin ni Lola ang magluto sa tradisyonal na **kalan** na de-kahoy.","translation":"Grandma still prefers to cook on a traditional wood-fired **stove**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabago ng kalagayan mula sa maliwanag patungo sa madilim; ang pagkawala ng liwanag.
original_explanation: This is what happens when the sun sets, when the power goes out (brownout!), or when the movie is about to start in the cinema. Figuratively, it’s when your world turns upside down after a breakup: "*Dumilim ang aking mundo*." It's the transition from light to its absence.
usage_notes: Can refer to literal darkness (like nightfall) or figurative darkness (like despair).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Biglang **dumilim** ang kalangitan at nagsimulang umulan.","translation":"The sky suddenly **darkened** and it started to rain."},{"sentence":"**Dumilim** ang kanyang paningin nang marinig niya ang masamang balita.","translation":"His vision **darkened** (His world went dark) when he heard the bad news."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ina ng lolo o lola ng isang tao; ang lola ng magulang ng isang tao.
etymology: Isang idyomatikong pariralang Filipino. Ang "sa tuhod" ay maaaring tumukoy sa henerasyon na sumunod sa mga anak (na nasa kandungan), kung saan ang mga apo ay madalas umupo sa tuhod.
original_explanation: Literally "grandmother on the knee." This is the lola of your mom or dad. She's the source of the *really* old stories, the ones that start with "Noong panahon pa ng Hapon..." If your lola is the final boss, your lola sa tuhod is the secret DLC character with legendary loot (stories and wisdom).
usage_notes: Isang tiyak na termino para sa relasyon sa pamilya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Buhay pa ang **lola sa tuhod** ni Ana at mag-iisang daang taong gulang na siya.","translation":"Ana's **great-grandmother** is still alive and is almost one hundred years old."},{"sentence":"Ipinakita niya sa akin ang litrato ng kanyang **lola sa tuhod**.","translation":"He showed me a picture of his **great-grandmother**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na ginawa ng sariling sikap o paraan, hindi ipinagawa sa iba.
original_explanation: This is the DIY King/Queen's motto. From baking your own pandesal to building your own PC rig. It's the product of YouTube tutorials, a lot of trial and error, and the satisfaction of saying, 'Ako gumawa niyan!' (I made that!).
usage_notes: Hyphenated compound adjective. Can refer to both objects and abstract things like a 'self-made man' (taong yaring-sarili).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagmamalaki niya ang kanyang **yaring-sarili** na bookshelf.","translation":"He is proud of his **self-made** bookshelf."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kutsilyo na partikular na idinisenyo para sa paghiwa ng mga pagkain tulad ng karne, tinapay, o gulay.
original_explanation: This isn't just any kutsilyo; it's the specialist. The chef's knife, the bread knife, the paring knife—they all fall under this category. Ito yung kutsilyo na 'I have a very particular set of skills,' and that skill is to slice things perfectly, whether it's for your sinigang na baboy or your pang-Instagram na fruit platter.
usage_notes: A compound noun, more commonly written as 'kutsilyong panghiwa' or with a hyphen 'kutsilyong-panghiwa'. The single-word form is less common in formal writing but understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iba ang **kutsilyongpanghiwa** ng tinapay sa pangkarne.","translation":"A bread **slicing knife** is different from a meat one."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong gamiting pambukas ng lata ang **kutsilyongpanghiwa**.","translation":"Don't use the **slicing knife** to open cans."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang gawain ay habulin o hulihin ang isang tao, hayop, o bagay na tumatakas.
original_explanation: Sila 'yung bida sa action movie na humahabol sa kontrabida. Sa office, sila 'yung taga-collections na humahabol sa'yo para sa bayad. Sa love life, sila 'yung hindi tumitigil manligaw kahit na-seen-zoned na. The official 'habol' officer.
usage_notes: Often found in legal, criminal, or dramatic contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga pulis ay nagsilbing **tagatugis** sa mga magnanakaw na tumakas.","translation":"The police acted as the **pursuers** of the thieves who escaped."},{"sentence":"Sa kwento, isang matapang na **tagatugis** ng dragon ang bida.","translation":"In the story, the hero is a brave **chaser** of dragons."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang de-kuryente para sa paghahalo ng mga sangkap. Ginagamit din ito upang tukuyin ang isang pagtitipong panlipunan na idinisenyo upang makilala ng mga tao ang isa't isa.
original_explanation: In the kitchen, it's the appliance that saves your arm from cramping when you're making Dalgona coffee or baking a cake. In social life, it's that awkward "get to know you" party where you stand in a corner with your one friend, pretending to be interested in small talk.
usage_notes: The meaning depends on context—kitchen appliance or social event. The pronunciation is Anglicized.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hiram muna ako ng **mixer** mo para sa gagawin kong cake.","translation":"Can I borrow your **mixer** for the cake I'm going to make?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang akronim para sa "Overseas Filipino Worker," isang mamamayang Pilipino na nagtatrabaho sa ibang bansa.
original_explanation: Short for 'Overseas Filipino Worker,' but really it means 'Our Family's Walang-katapusang source of balikbayan boxes.' They are the modern-day heroes who brave loneliness and culture shock for a better future... and for the latest iPhone model for their pamangkins.
usage_notes: A very common and important term in modern Philippine society, economics, and culture.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tatay ko ay isang **OFW** sa Saudi Arabia.","translation":"My father is an **OFW** in Saudi Arabia."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang naitutulong ng mga **OFW** sa ekonomiya ng Pilipinas.","translation":"The **OFWs** contribute greatly to the Philippine economy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking nasa hustong gulang na ngunit wala pang asawa.
original_explanation: The male equivalent of a 'dalaga'. He's single and (maybe) ready to mingle. In Pinoy culture, once you hit your late 20s and you're still a `binata`, expect your titas to ask at every family gathering, "O, iho, kailan ka mag-aasawa?" It's the ultimate 'pressure cooker' status.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a young, unmarried man. The female counterpart is 'dalaga'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **binata** pa rin si Kuya Mark kahit trenta anyos na siya.","translation":"Kuya Mark is still a **bachelor** even though he's already thirty."},{"sentence":"Lahat ng mga **binata** sa aming baryo ay sumali sa palaro.","translation":"All the **unmarried men** in our village joined the games."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paraang mabilis, walang pagkaantala, at sa sandaling iyon din.
original_explanation: This is the 'ASAP' of Tagalog. When your boss emails you and marks it 'urgent,' they want it done 'kagyat'. It's faster than 'mamaya,' more urgent than 'agad-agad.' It's the speed of light for tasks and actions.
usage_notes: Often used in formal or literary contexts. 'Agad' is more common in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinakailangan nating umalis **kagyat** upang hindi mahuli sa biyahe.","translation":"We need to leave **immediately** so we won't be late for the trip."},{"sentence":"Tumugon siya **kagyat** sa tawag ng tulong.","translation":"He responded **instantly** to the call for help."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng baging na may malaki at mabilog na bunga na karaniwang ginagawang minatamis o isinasahog sa mga lutuin tulad ng sabaw.
original_explanation: 'Yung gulay na mukhang green na kalabasa pero hindi. Ito yung bida sa hopia at sa pampalamig na winter melon milk tea! It's the Zelig of the food world—pwede siyang ulam, pwede siyang dessert, pwede siyang inumin. Low-key, but versatile.
usage_notes: The scientific name is Benincasa hispida.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paborito niyang palaman sa hopia ay **kundol**.","translation":"Her favorite filling in hopia is **winter melon**."},{"sentence":"Nagluto si nanay ng sabaw na may **kundol** at baboy.","translation":"Mom cooked a soup with **winter melon** and pork."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na umuupa ng isang bahay, apartment, o silid mula sa may-ari nito.
original_explanation: The person paying rent to their landlord/landlady. The professional "bedspacer" or "apartment-dweller" who knows the struggle of "due date na naman ng renta." They're the reason your tita with a spare room can say, "May bago kaming boarder."
usage_notes: A formal term for a renter. "Umuupa" or "nangungupahan" are more common in everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **inkilino** sa apartment sa itaas ay maingay tuwing gabi.","translation":"The **tenants** in the apartment upstairs are noisy every night."},{"sentence":"Tumaas ang bayad sa upa ng mga **inkilino** ngayong taon.","translation":"The rent for the **renters** increased this year."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahabang upuan na may palaman at karaniwang may sandalan at patungan ng braso, na dinisenyo para sa dalawa o higit pang tao.
original_explanation: The throne of the house where the remote control king/queen reigns. It's the battlefield for the best spot during movie night, the designated napping area for titos, and the place where you find loose change and a month-old chip. It's a loanword, obviously. We just spell it like it sounds.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umupo ka muna sa **supa** habang naghahanda ako ng meryenda.","translation":"Please sit on the **sofa** for a while as I prepare a snack."},{"sentence":"Nakatulog siya sa **supa** kagabi dahil sa pagod.","translation":"He fell asleep on the **couch** last night due to exhaustion."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang opisyal ng pamahalaan na nagsasagawa ng paunang imbestigasyon sa mga kasong kriminal at kumakatawan sa estado sa pag-uusig ng mga nasasakdal.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na "fiscalía" (prosecutor's office) o "fiscal" (prosecutor).
original_explanation: The person in a legal drama who says "Objection, your Honor!" for the government. They're the lawyer for the people, tasked with proving a case against a suspect. If you've been watching too many teleseryes, you'd think their main job is to have intense stare-downs with the defense attorney.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghain ng mosyon ang **piskalya** upang pigilan ang pagpiyansa ng akusado.","translation":"The **prosecutor** filed a motion to prevent the accused from posting bail."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na naniniwala at nagsusulong ng kapitalismo; isang indibidwal na nagmamay-ari ng malaking puhunan o yaman na ginagamit sa pagnenegosyo.
original_explanation: The 'Tito' or 'Tita' in the family who owns multiple businesses, drives a European car, and tells you to 'think like a businessman'. Also, the villain in your friend's political science rants. They're all about that 'return on investment'.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun (a capitalist person) or an adjective (a capitalist system). Often carries a neutral to negative connotation in modern discourse, depending on the speaker's political leanings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang isang tunay na **kapitalista** ay laging naghahanap ng pagkakataong kumita.","translation":"A true **capitalist** is always looking for an opportunity to earn."},{"sentence":"Marami ang tumutuligsa sa mga **kapitalista**ng patakaran ng gobyerno.","translation":"Many are criticizing the **capitalist** policies of the government."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagwawasto, pagtutuwid, o pag-aayos ng isang pagkakamali, depekto, o kamalian.
original_explanation: A very formal way of saying 'pagtatama' or 'fixing your mess.' It's what you do when you file the wrong BIR form, or what a company does when they send you the wrong Lazada order. It’s 'sorry, mali kami, eto 'yung tamang gawin.'
usage_notes: Isang pormal na termino na ginagamit sa mga legal, teknikal, o administratibong konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghain sila ng mosyon para sa **rektipikasyon** ng mga mali sa dokumento.","translation":"They filed a motion for the **rectification** of the errors in the document."},{"sentence":"Ang **rektipikasyon** ng listahan ng mga botante ay isinasagawa bago ang eleksyon.","translation":"The **rectification** of the voters' list is done before the election."}]

translation: to summon; to have someone called
meaning_filipino: Iutos o ipakiusap na tawagin ang isang tao upang humarap o dumalo.
original_explanation: This is what your boss does when they need to see you, and you get that dreaded email: 'HR wants to see you.' That's your boss who decided to **magpatawag**. It can also be less scary, like when your lola decides to **magpatawag** ng family meeting kasi may bagong chismis. It’s an act of power, summoning your minions (or family members).
usage_notes: Often implies that the person summoning is in a position of authority.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagpatawag** ng pulong ang manager para sa lahat ng empleyado.","translation":"The manager **called** a meeting for all employees."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **magpatawag** ng tubero para ayusin ang gripo.","translation":"I need to **call for** a plumber to fix the faucet."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagkuha o paggamit ng isang bagay na pag-aari ng iba na may kasunduang ibabalik ito sa takdang panahon.
original_explanation: This is the official sport of every Pinoy household. It's the "Can I borrow your charger?" that becomes a permanent adoption. It's asking your kapitbahay for a cup of sugar, or your officemate for 100 pesos 'til payday. The golden rule is: always return it... eventually. The unspoken rule: if you don't return it, utang na loob forever.
usage_notes: The noun form of the verb "humiram" (to borrow).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paghiram** ng pera ay dapat may kasamang responsibilidad na magbayad.","translation":"The **act of borrowing** money should come with the responsibility to pay it back."},{"sentence":"Naging sanhi ng kanilang alitan ang **paghiram** niya ng damit na hindi ipinapaalam.","translation":"Her **borrowing** of clothes without permission became the cause of their argument."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pasilidad na pang-industriya para sa pagbuo ng koryente o lakas-elektrikal.
original_explanation: Ito yung building na pinanggagalingan ng kuryente para makapag-charge ka ng phone at makapag-scroll sa TikTok. Kapag nag-brownout, sila ang either sinisisi o inaasahan mong umayos agad. Think Meralco's giant, noisy cousin.
usage_notes: Madalas na pinaikli bilang "planta" sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May malaking **planta elektrika** na malapit sa aming bayan.","translation":"There is a large **power plant** near our town."},{"sentence":"Ang suplay ng koryente ay nagmumula sa **planta elektrika** sa Batangas.","translation":"The electricity supply comes from the **power plant** in Batangas."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangkalahatang diwa, kahulugan, o takbo ng isang bagay, tulad ng isang talumpati, sulat, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: This is the ~vibe~ or the general mood of a conversation or situation. When your boss calls for a meeting and the `tenor` is serious, you know it's not about the upcoming company outing. It's the 'ano kayang meron?' feeling you get from the overall tone.
usage_notes: Mas pormal at di-gaanong karaniwan kaysa sa katumbas nitong "diwa" o "tono".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagbago ang **tenor** ng usapan nang dumating ang manager.","translation":"The **tenor** of the conversation changed when the manager arrived."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko nagustuhan ang **tenor** ng kanyang sulat ng reklamo.","translation":"I did not like the **tenor** of his complaint letter."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking gusali o lugar na may mga upuan para sa mga manonood, karaniwang ginagamit para sa mga palaro, konsiyerto, at iba pang malalaking pagtitipon.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'estadio', na mula sa Latin na 'stadium'.
original_explanation: The place where you scream your lungs out for your favorite basketball team or K-Pop group. It's the modern-day coliseum, but instead of gladiators, we have athletes and idols. Think Philippine Arena or Araneta Coliseum levels of energy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ang **istadyum** para sa laban ng Gilas Pilipinas.","translation":"The **stadium** is full for the Gilas Pilipinas game."},{"sentence":"Gaganapin ang konsiyerto sa pinakamalaking **istadyum** sa bansa.","translation":"The concert will be held in the biggest **stadium** in the country."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga kagamitan sa pagsulat at pang-opisina, tulad ng papel, sobre, panulat, at iba pa.
original_explanation: Your back-to-school shopping haul. Lahat ng cute na notebook, makukulay na ballpen, at scented paper na binili mo sa National Book Store na minsan ayaw mo na ngang gamitin sa sobrang ganda. Basically, the official currency of a 'tita's' desk.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang mangolekta ng mga magagandang **istesyoneri**.","translation":"She loves to collect beautiful **stationery**."},{"sentence":"Pumunta kami sa bookstore para bumili ng **istesyoneri** para sa opisina.","translation":"We went to the bookstore to buy **stationery** for the office."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal at legal na kasunduan sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang partido na may kaakibat na mga karapatan at obligasyon.
original_explanation: That piece of paper you sign without reading the fine print. Dito nakasulat lahat ng promises (at threats). From your 5-month job as a BPO agent to your 30-year housing loan. It's the 'sana all' ng mga usapan, kasi may pirmahan at may habol ka 'pag di tinupad.
usage_notes: A fundamental term in business, law, and employment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Basahin mong mabuti ang lahat ng nakasulat sa **kontrato** bago ka pumirma.","translation":"Read everything written in the **contract** carefully before you sign."},{"sentence":"Nagtapos na ang kanyang **kontrato** sa kumpanya noong nakaraang buwan.","translation":"His **contract** with the company ended last month."}]

translation: to justify; to give a reason; to rationalize
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalahad ng dahilan o basehan upang ipaliwanag o patunayan ang isang kilos, desisyon, o pahayag.
original_explanation: This is what you do when your boss asks why you were late, or when your partner asks why you bought another pair of sneakers. You're trying to build a logical bridge from 'what you did' to 'why it was okay'. Sometimes it's a valid reason ('May accident po sa EDSA'), sometimes it's an excuse ('It was on sale!'). To magbigay-katwiran is to present your case.
usage_notes: Can have a neutral tone (to explain) or a slightly negative one (to make excuses). The context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hiningan siya ng korte na **magbigay-katwiran** sa kanyang mga aksyon.","translation":"The court asked him to **justify** his actions."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **magbigay-katwiran** kung alam mong mali ka talaga.","translation":"It's hard to **give a reason** when you know you're truly wrong."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maliit na lambat na may mahabang hawakan, ginagamit sa paghuli ng isda, hipon, o iba pang maliliit na hayop-tubig.
original_explanation: Think of it as a giant "siyanse" (slotted turner) but for fishing. It's the net you use to scoop up fish from a small pond, or what kids use to try and catch tadpoles in a canal. It's for small-time fishing, not the big hauls you see on "Deadliest Catch".
usage_notes: A specific term used in fishing and rural communities.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng **sigpaw** para manghuli ng maliliit na isda sa ilog.","translation":"He used a **scoop net** to catch small fish in the river."},{"sentence":"Puno ng hipon ang kanyang **sigpaw** pagkatapos ng isang umaga.","translation":"His **hand net** was full of shrimp after one morning."}]

translation: to hex, to cast a spell on
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa ng itim na mahika o pangkukulam upang magdulot ng pinsala, sakit, o kamalasan sa isang tao. Ito ang anyong pangkaganapan ng 'kulam'.
original_explanation: This is the past tense of 'kulam' (witchcraft/hex). It's what you jokingly threaten to do to your ex. "Sana all kinukulam." It's the act of using supernatural means, often involving a doll and some creepy chants, to cause someone harm. In modern terms, it's like leaving a 1-star review on their soul.
usage_notes: Past tense/completed aspect of 'kulam'. Refers to Filipino witchcraft.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayon sa matatanda, may kakayahan daw ang mangkukulam na **kumulam** ng tao.","translation":"According to the elders, a sorcerer supposedly has the ability **to cast a spell on** people."},{"sentence":"Pinagbintangan siyang **kumulam** kaya siya pinalayas sa baryo.","translation":"She was accused of having **cast a hex**, which is why she was driven out of the village."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng butiki (Gekko gecko) na malaki, karaniwang naninirahan sa mga bahay at puno, at kilala sa malakas at natatanging tunog na "tuk-ko" na pinagmulan ng pangalan nito.
etymology: Onomatopoeic, from the sound the gecko makes.
original_explanation: Your friendly (or terrifying) neighborhood wall-crawler. He's the guy who randomly screams "TUK-KOOO!" in the middle of the night, making you jump. Urban legends say they're worth a fortune, but in reality, they're just pro-bono pest control, eating mosquitoes for free.
usage_notes: The sound of a 'tuko' is often associated with superstitions, such as counting the calls to predict something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May malaking **tuko** na nakadikit sa kisame ng aming kusina.","translation":"There's a big **gecko** stuck to the ceiling of our kitchen."},{"sentence":"Narinig mo ba ang huni ng **tuko** kagabi?","translation":"Did you hear the call of the **gecko** last night?"}]

meaning_filipino: Maliliit na batik o patse ng mas maitim na kulay sa balat, karaniwang lumalabas sa mukha dahil sa pagkabilad sa araw o pagbabago sa hormon.
original_explanation: Those little brown spots on your face that some people try to hide with concealer and some people think are super cute. In the Philippines, it's often associated with getting older or too much sun exposure ('bilad sa araw'). Titas will recommend all sorts of creams for your 'pekas', but hey, they're just your skin's unique constellations. Can also refer to melasma.
usage_notes: Can refer to both freckles (common in youth) and melasma/age spots (more common in adults).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon siya ng **pekas** sa mukha dahil palagi siyang nagbibilad sa araw.","translation":"She got **freckles** on her face because she's always out in the sun."},{"sentence":"May mga pampaputi ba kayong mabisa para sa **pekas**?","translation":"Do you have any effective whitening products for **melasma**?"}]

translation: to take turns; to substitute; to relieve (someone of duty)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapalit o pagsasalin sa isang gawain, posisyon, o tungkulin.
original_explanation: This is the more formal 'take turns.' When your co-worker's shift ends and yours begins, you maghalili. When a king dies and his son takes the throne, the son naghahalili (present tense) sa kanyang ama. It’s less about continuous back-and-forth like 'maghali-halili' and more about a single, official substitution or shift change.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of work shifts, duties, or succession of roles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pwede ba tayong **maghalili** sa pagbabantay? Inaantok na ako.","translation":"Can we **take turns** on watch? I'm already sleepy."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **maghalili** sa kanya bilang pangulo ng organisasyon?","translation":"Who will **substitute** for him as president of the organization?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagdurog o paggiling ng isang bagay, lalo na ng mga butil tulad ng palay o mais, upang maging mas pino.
etymology: From 'ligi' (to grind, to mill) with the infix '-in-'.
original_explanation: This is what happened to the rice before it became bigas. It's the process of taking the grains and grinding them to remove the husk. Think of it as the rice's spa day where it gets a full-body exfoliation to become the pretty white grain you know and love.
