usage_notes: Primarily used in an agricultural or food processing context, especially for grains like rice or corn. It is less common than 'giniling'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Niligi** na ang mga palay para maging bigas.","translation":"The rice stalks have been **milled** to become rice grains."},{"sentence":"Dati, mano-mano kung paano **niligi** ang kape.","translation":"Before, the coffee was **ground** by hand."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagtatagpo ng dalawa o higit pang tao na hindi plinano o inaasahan na mangyari.
etymology: Isang parirala na binubuo ng "di-", "inaasahan" (mula sa ugat na "asa"), at "pagkikita" (mula sa ugat na "kita").
original_explanation: Ito yung moment na akala mo safe ka nang mag-mall na pambahay lang ang suot, tapos biglang makakasalubong mo yung ex mo kasama yung bago niya. Or when you bump into your boss at a concert you called in sick for. It's the universe's way of saying, "Gotcha!" Serendipity with a side of panic.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa mga kuwento, pelikula, at dula bilang isang mahalagang tagpuan sa banghay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanilang **di-inasasahang pagkikita** sa isang coffee shop ang naging simula ng kanilang pag-iibigan.","translation":"Their **unexpected meeting** at a coffee shop was the beginning of their romance."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katawagang balbal para sa isang lalaki na nagpapakita ng labis na kalungkutan o pagiging emosyonal, kadalasan upang makakuha ng simpatya o atensyon, lalo na mula sa mga babae.
etymology: Mula sa salitang balbal sa Ingles na 'sad boy'.
original_explanation: The guy who posts black and white photos, listens to The Smiths, and slides into your DMs with 'U up? I'm sad.' He weaponizes his emotions to get attention. He's not just sad, he performs sadness. Beware the sadboy aesthetic. Also spelled 'sadboi'.
usage_notes: Isang termino sa kulturang pop at internet na naging popular sa mga kabataan. Maaaring gamitin nang mapanukso o bilang isang kritisismo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na 'yang ka-**sadboy**-han mo, hindi na 'yan uso.","translation":"Stop with your **sadboy** antics, that's not in style anymore."},{"sentence":"Akala ko malalim siyang tao, pero isa lang pala siyang **sadboy** na mahilig magpaawa.","translation":"I thought he was a deep person, but he's just a **sadboy** who likes to play the victim."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malawak at tuloy-tuloy na masa ng lupa, na karaniwang itinuturing na isa sa mga pangunahing dibisyon ng mundo (e.g., Asya, Europa). Maaari ring tumukoy sa isang napakalayo o liblib na lugar.
original_explanation: Literally, a continent. But when your tita says, "Saan lupalop ka na naman nanggaling?", she's not asking if you've been to Antarctica. She's asking what god-forsaken, far-flung corner of the city you've been to that made you come home so late. It's a dramatic word for any place that feels a million miles away.
usage_notes: Used to mean "continent" in a geographical context, but more commonly used hyperbolically to mean a very distant, remote, or unfamiliar place.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Asya ang pinakamalaking **lupalop** sa mundo.","translation":"Asia is the largest **continent** in the world."},{"sentence":"Anong **lupalop** ng Maynila 'yan at sobrang traffic papunta diyan?","translation":"What **remote part** of Manila is that for the traffic to be so bad going there?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang prinsipyo ng pagiging makatarungan; ang pagkakaloob ng nararapat na parusa o gantimpala; katarungan.
original_explanation: What everyone screams for in TV news interviews and protest rallies. It’s what you demand when your sibling eats the last piece of leche flan that you were saving. "Hustisya para sa leche flan ko!" On a serious note, it's the goal of every legal battle and the hope of the oppressed. Sometimes it's swift, but in the Philippines, it's often stuck in EDSA traffic.
usage_notes: A very common and emotionally charged word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sigaw ng mga biktima ay katarungan at **hustisya**.","translation":"The cry of the victims is for fairness and **justice**."},{"sentence":"Nakamit din niya ang **hustisya** matapos ang mahabang panahon.","translation":"He finally obtained **justice** after a long time."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagkamit ng tagumpay; matagumpay sa isang layunin, gawain, o laban.
etymology: From `ma-` (adjective-forming prefix) + `panagumpay` (a variant of tagumpay, often used in compounds).
original_explanation: This is your graduation photo caption, your LinkedIn status after getting that promotion, or how you feel after finally paying off your credit card debt. It’s that "I made it!" moment. Ang pagiging **mapanagumpay** ay ang ultimate "in your face" sa lahat ng 'di naniwala sa'yo.
usage_notes: Often used in formal contexts to describe a person, an endeavor, or an outcome.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **mapanagumpay** ang kanilang misyon na tulungan ang mga nasalanta.","translation":"Their mission to help the victims was **successful**."},{"sentence":"Isang **mapanagumpay** na negosyante ang nagsalita sa aming klase.","translation":"A **triumphant** entrepreneur spoke to our class."}]

translation: a press (of a button); a click
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagdiin sa isang buton, teklado, o anumang katulad na bagay gamit ang daliri.
original_explanation: The official sound and action of the digital age in the Philippines. From ordering food delivery, to liking a crush's photo, to sending that risky "u up?" text. It's the cause of and solution to many of life's problems, one 'pindot' at a time. Also, what your lola tells you to do to the TV remote.
usage_notes: Used as a noun for the action itself. It also serves as the root for the verb 'pindutin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **pindot** lang sa app, may pagkain ka na.","translation":"Just one **press** on the app, and you have food."},{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **pindot** ng kamera.","translation":"I heard the **click** of the camera."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang propesyonal na tagapagluto, karaniwang punong tagapagluto sa isang restawran o hotel.
original_explanation: The person who makes your food look and taste like it's worth the 'service charge'. Hindi lang basta tagaluto, artist din. Sila 'yung dahilan kung bakit may #FoodPorn sa Instagram feed mo.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to a professional, often trained, cook, as opposed to the more general 'kusinero' or 'tagapagluto'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong maging isang sikat na **chef** balang araw.","translation":"I want to be a famous **chef** someday."},{"sentence":"Ang **chef** sa hotel na iyon ay galing pa sa France.","translation":"The **chef** at that hotel is from France."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagmamasid, nanonood, o nag-oobserba sa mga pangyayari, tao, o bagay sa paligid.
original_explanation: The professional 'chismoso/chismosa', but in a more formal setting. They're the people who just watch things unfold, whether it's a UN observer, a poll watcher during elections, or you, quietly watching the drama in your group chat. They're paid (or not) to just look.
usage_notes: Often used in formal contexts like politics, science, or sociology. More formal than 'nanonood' (one who is watching).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpadala ang United Nations ng mga **tagamasid** sa halalan.","translation":"The United Nations sent **observers** to the election."},{"sentence":"Bilang isang **tagamasid**, napansin ko ang unti-unting pagbabago sa komunidad.","translation":"As an **observer**, I noticed the gradual change in the community."}]

translation: to moan; to wail softly; to lament
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-iyak o pagdaing nang mahina at may pananangis, karaniwang nagpapahiwatig ng matinding kalungkutan o sakit.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'haluyhoy' (isang mahinang daing o panaghoy) at ang gitlaping '-um-'.
original_explanation: This is that low, sad sound you make when you see your electricity bill. It's not a full-on breakdown, just a sad, quiet 'huhuhu'. Parang tunog ng kaluluwang ligaw sa horror movie, pero 'yung sa'yo dahil sa bills at deadlines.
usage_notes: Isang salitang pampanitikan o patula. Hindi karaniwan sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig sa dilim ang isang babaeng **humahaluyhoy** dahil sa pagkawala ng kanyang anak.","translation":"A woman was heard in the dark, **wailing softly** over the loss of her child."},{"sentence":"**Humaluyhoy** ang makata habang binibigkas ang tula tungkol sa sawimpalad na pag-ibig.","translation":"The poet **lamented** while reciting the poem about ill-fated love."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga bantas ( " " o ' ' ) na ginagamit sa simula at dulo ng isang sinipi na salita, parirala, o pangungusap upang ipahiwatig na ito ay direktang sipi o may espesyal na kahulugan.
original_explanation: The punctuation you use when you're quoting someone, or when you're being sarcastic. It's the text equivalent of doing "air quotes" with your fingers. When you see something in **komilyas**, it means "sabi ng iba, hindi ako" or "I 'allegedly' ate the last piece of cake."
usage_notes: Also known as 'panipi'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang lagyan ng **komilyas** ang mga direktang sinabi ng tauhan.","translation":"Don't forget to put **quotation marks** on the character's direct quotes."},{"sentence":"Ang salitang 'kaibigan' ay nasa loob ng **komilyas**, na nagpapahiwatig ng pagdududa.","translation":"The word 'friend' was in **quotation marks**, implying doubt."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng makamandag na ahas (Naja philippinensis); sa matalinhagang kahulugan, isang taong taksil o mapanganib.
original_explanation: Literally, it's a Philippine cobra – super dangerous, don't touch! But in everyday chismis, it's that 'friend' who smiles at you but talks trash behind your back. The classic 'ahas,' but leveled up. If a regular 'ahas' is a backstabber, an 'ulupong' is the one who masterminded the whole betrayal plot.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin nang literal para sa ahas o patalinghaga para sa isang taksil na tao. Ang makasagisag na kahulugan ay karaniwan sa kolokyal na pag-uusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa taong iyan, isa siyang **ulupong**.","translation":"Be careful with that person, they are a **traitor**."},{"sentence":"May nakitang **ulupong** sa bukirin.","translation":"A **cobra** was seen in the field."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtikim at paglasap nang may lubos na kasiyahan upang maramdaman ang buong linamnam. Sa matalinhagang paraan, ito ay ang pagdanas nang malalim sa isang karanasan.
original_explanation: This is more than just tasting; it's 'slow-mo' eating. You know when you take a bite of that perfectly cooked adobo or that life-changing leche flan, and you close your eyes to let the flavor explode? That's 'namnamin'. It's not just for food; you can also 'namnamin ang tagumpay' (savor the victory). It's about fully appreciating the moment, whether it's a flavor or a feeling.
usage_notes: This is a command or infinitive form. It implies a deliberate and appreciative act of tasting or experiencing something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Namnamin** mo ang bawat sandali ng iyong tagumpay.","translation":"**Savor** every moment of your victory."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong madaliin ang pagkain; **namnamin** mo ang luto ni Lola.","translation":"Don't rush your food; **savor** Grandma's cooking."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang biglaang pagkilos o paggalaw upang makawala sa pagkakatali, pagkakagapos, o anumang pumipigil.
original_explanation: This is that 'I've had enough!' moment. Yung bigla kang aalis sa toxic relationship or magre-resign sa trabahong ayaw mo na. It's the sudden, forceful act of breaking free. The ultimate 'bahala na si Batman' escape.
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of rebellion, escape, or breaking from physical or metaphorical constraints.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa isang **piglas**, nakawala ang bilanggo sa mga tanod.","translation":"In one forceful **struggle**, the prisoner broke free from the guards."},{"sentence":"Ang **piglas** ng mamamayan laban sa katiwalian ay hindi mapipigilan.","translation":"The people's **uprising** against corruption cannot be stopped."}]

translation: to understand each other; to have a mutual understanding
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng reciprokal na pag-intindi o pagkakaintindihan sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang tao.
original_explanation: The goal of every couple's fight, every team meeting, and every family discussion about politics. It's when you finally get why your friend is 'marupok' or why your mom keeps sending you chain messages. It's a rare achievement, so when it happens, it's magic. The `-an` suffix implies it's a two-way (or multi-way) street.
usage_notes: This is a reciprocal verb, meaning the action is done between two or more subjects. You can't `mag-unawaan` by yourself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **mag-unawaan** para malutas ang problemang ito.","translation":"We need to **understand each other** to solve this problem."},{"sentence":"Sa wakas, nagkausap sila at nagsimulang **mag-unawaan**.","translation":"Finally, they talked and began to **have a mutual understanding**."}]

translation: to be able to support (financially); to make a living
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang tustusan ang mga pangangailangan sa pamumuhay, lalo na sa aspetong pinansyal.
original_explanation: 'Kahit anong trabaho papasukin ko, basta **makabuhay** lang ng pamilya.' The ultimate Filipino parent mantra. It's about being able to provide, to put food on the table, and pay for the WiFi subscription.
usage_notes: This is the 'maka-' actor-focus, potential aspect of the verb 'buhay' (to live/support). It focuses on the ability to provide for oneself or others.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sapat na ba ang sahod mo para **makabuhay** ng isang pamilya?","translation":"Is your salary enough **to be able to support** a family?"},{"sentence":"Nag-abroad siya para **makabuhay** at makapag-ipon para sa kinabukasan.","translation":"He went abroad **to make a living** and save for the future."}]

translation: to be involved; to be implicated
meaning_filipino: Masama o madawit sa isang pangyayari, usapin, o gulo, kadalasan nang hindi sinasadya.
original_explanation: The 'nadamay lang' verb. When your officemate is doing something shady and you just happened to be in their screenshot, you might get **mapasangkot** in the HR investigation. It’s being dragged into drama, whether you're a willing participant or just an innocent bystander. The favorite word of every politician in a scandal: 'Hindi po ako sangkot!'
usage_notes: Often carries a negative connotation, implying involvement in trouble, crime, or controversy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang **mapasangkot** sa gulo ng mag-asawa.","translation":"He doesn't want **to be involved** in the couple's troubles."},{"sentence":"**Napasangkot** ang pangalan niya sa isang malaking iskandalo.","translation":"His name **was implicated** in a huge scandal."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglikha o paggawa ng mga kalakal at serbisyo. Tumutukoy din ito sa kabuuang bilang o halaga ng mga bagay na nagawa.
original_explanation: Ito yung dahilan kung bakit may OT (overtime) sa trabaho. Kapag sinabi ng boss mo, "Kailangan nating habulin ang produksyon," ibig sabihin, maghanda ka nang hindi umuwi on time. Sa pelikula, ito yung buong proseso mula sa shooting hanggang sa editing.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng negosyo, pagmamanupaktura, agrikultura, at sining tulad ng pelikula at teatro.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumaas ang **produksyon** ng bigas ngayong taon dahil sa magandang panahon.","translation":"Rice **production** increased this year due to good weather."},{"sentence":"Ang **produksyon** ng bagong pelikula ay aabutin ng anim na buwan.","translation":"The **production** of the new movie will take six months."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-aalis ng legalidad, pagiging epektibo, o kapangyarihan ng isang bagay tulad ng kasunduan, batas, o dokumento.
etymology: From pa- prefix + wala (none) + -ng linker + bisa (effect, validity).
original_explanation: The official term for 'cancel culture' but for documents and contracts. It's when you make something 'null and void,' like your ex's promises, a parking ticket you successfully contested, or that free trial you forgot to cancel before they charged your card.
usage_notes: This is the infinitive form. It is often conjugated as 'pinawalang-bisa' (past) or 'papawalang-bisain' (future). The root verb is 'pawalang-bisain'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **pawalang-bisa** ang lumang kontrata bago gumawa ng bago.","translation":"The old contract needs **to be nullified** before making a new one."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan nilang **pawalang-bisa** ang resulta ng eleksyon.","translation":"They tried **to invalidate** the election results."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-apaw ng tubig na nagdudulot ng paglubog sa karaniwang tuyo na lupa.
original_explanation: The unwanted sequel to a 'bagyo'. Baha is when the streets of Manila turn into a temporary Venice, but way less romantic. It's when your commute becomes an extreme water sport, and 'hanggang bewang' (waist-deep) becomes a standard unit of measurement. It's the reason why Filipinos are experts at lifting their feet inside a jeepney.
usage_notes: Often occurs after heavy rains or typhoons.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umabot hanggang tuhod ang **baha** sa aming kalye.","translation":"The **flood** on our street reached knee-deep."},{"sentence":"Maraming sasakyan ang nasira dahil sa biglaang pagtaas ng **baha**.","translation":"Many vehicles were damaged due to the sudden rise of the **flood**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pariralang nagbibigay-diin sa pinakamahalaga o nangingibabaw na punto, ideya, o bagay kumpara sa iba.
original_explanation: This is your main character energy phrase. When you list down all your priorities, this is the one that gets the top spot. "Gusto kong yumaman, mag-travel, at maging masaya, pero lalo sa lahat, gusto ko ng peace of mind." It's the ultimate "This is the most important thing" clarifier.
usage_notes: Used to emphasize the most important point in a series.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka palagi, at **lalo sa lahat**, huwag kang magpapagabi sa daan.","translation":"Always be careful, and **above all**, don't stay out late on the streets."},{"sentence":"Mahal ko ang aking mga kaibigan, pamilya, at trabaho, ngunit **lalo sa lahat**, mahal ko ang aking sarili.","translation":"I love my friends, family, and job, but **most of all**, I love myself."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahabang hanay o serye ng mga bundok na magkakadugtong.
original_explanation: The squad goals of mountains. It's not just one mountain, but a whole barkada of them standing together. Think Sierra Madre. It's the kind of view you see from a plane or on a postcard that makes you say, "Wow, ang ganda ng Pilipinas!"
usage_notes: Isang deskriptibong parirala. Ang mas karaniwang termino ay `kabundukan` o `hanay ng mga bundok`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Makikita mula sa itaas ang kahabaan ng **tagudtod ng mga bundok**.","translation":"From above, you can see the length of the **mountain range**."},{"sentence":"Ang Sierra Madre ay isang mahalagang **tagudtod ng mga bundok** sa Luzon.","translation":"The Sierra Madre is an important **mountain range** in Luzon."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sapilitang pagkuha ng ari-arian bilang kabayaran sa isang pagkakautang o bilang parusa alinsunod sa batas; kumpiskasyon.
original_explanation: The act of getting your stuff taken away legally. When you can't pay your credit card debt, the bank might start the process of **ilit** on your property. It's the formal term for 'hatak' (to pull/tow). The moment the repo man shows up, that's **ilit** in action.
usage_notes: This noun refers to the act of confiscation. The verb form is `ilitin` (to confiscate).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **ilit** sa kanilang bahay at lupa ay isang malaking dagok sa pamilya.","translation":"The **confiscation** of their house and lot was a huge blow to the family."},{"sentence":"Inutos ng korte na **ilitin** ang lahat ng ari-arian ng nasasakdal.","translation":"The court ordered to **confiscate** all the properties of the accused."}]

translation: to lose something unintentionally; to misplace; to get rid of (from mind)
meaning_filipino: Mawala ang isang bagay nang hindi sinasadya; alisin sa isipan o kalimutan.
original_explanation: That feeling when you check your pocket and your phone is gone. You've just naiwaglit it. It's more than just 'nawala' (lost); it has a nuance of carelessness or of something slipping away. Also used for feelings: "Sana'y ma-iwaglit ko na siya sa isip ko." (I hope I can get him out of my mind.) — a classic hugot line.
usage_notes: Often used for misplacing small items or for trying to forget memories or feelings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingatan mo ang singsing na iyan at huwag mong **iwaglit**.","translation":"Take care of that ring and don't **lose** it."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang **iwaglit** sa isipan ang masasakit na alaala.","translation":"She is trying to **get rid of** the painful memories from her mind."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang akronim para sa 'One True Pairing', na tumutukoy sa paboritong tambalan ng dalawang karakter sa isang kuwento (libro, pelikula, serye) ng isang tagahanga.
etymology: Akronim sa Ingles para sa 'One True Pairing', nagmula sa mga komunidad ng fanfiction.
original_explanation: Your 'One True Pairing'. The two characters in a series you ship so hard you'd write a 50-chapter fanfiction about them. It's your ideal love team, the one you believe is endgame, and you're ready to fight anyone on Twitter who disagrees.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa mga konteksto ng fandom at pop culture. Madalas na isinusulat sa malalaking titik bilang OTP.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para sa akin, si Popoy at Basha ang ultimate **OTP** ng Philippine cinema.","translation":"For me, Popoy and Basha are the ultimate **OTP** of Philippine cinema."},{"sentence":"Nag-away sila dahil magkaiba sila ng **OTP** sa paborito nilang K-drama.","translation":"They fought because they had a different **OTP** in their favorite K-drama."}]

translation: to scoop up with one's hand, to grab a handful
meaning_filipino: Kunin ang isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pagsalok o pagsakop gamit ang kamay.
original_explanation: Imagine you're at a kid's party and there's a mountain of candy. That motion of grabbing as much as you can with one cupped hand? That's 'dakutin'. It’s a bit greedy, a bit messy, and very effective. You can 'dakutin' popcorn, coins, or even sand at the beach.
usage_notes: Implies using the hand as a scoop to get a large quantity of something small and numerous.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinabihan siya na huwag **dakutin** ang kanin kundi gumamit ng kutsara.","translation":"He was told not to **scoop up** the rice with his hand but to use a spoon."},{"sentence":"Gusto kong **dakutin** lahat ng barya sa mesa.","translation":"I want to **grab a handful** of all the coins on the table."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng gulay na may mahahaba at berdeng bunga na karaniwang isinasahog sa mga lutuing Pilipino tulad ng sinigang o ginisa.
original_explanation: The OG healthy-ish sidekick in your sinigang or ginisa. It's that long, green veggie that gives a satisfying crunch, often mistaken for Baguio beans, but who's really checking? It’s the vegetable you buy from the suking tindera sa palengke.
usage_notes: 'Abitswelas' and 'Baguio beans' are often used interchangeably in the Philippines, although they can refer to slightly different varieties.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagdagdag si nanay ng **abitswelas** sa niluluto niyang pochero.","translation":"Mom added **green beans** to the pochero she was cooking."},{"sentence":"Ginisang baboy na may **abitswelas** ang paborito kong ulam.","translation":"Sautéed pork with **string beans** is my favorite dish."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalipunan o sistema ng mga makina o mga bahagi nito na magkakasamang gumagana upang isagawa ang isang partikular na gawain. Ginagamit din ito sa matalinghagang paraan para sa isang organisadong sistema ng mga tao o proseso.
original_explanation: Think of 'makinarya' as the squad goals of machines. It's not just one machine, it's the whole system—the conveyor belts, the robotic arms, the big crushy things—all working together in a factory. It can also be used figuratively for any complex system, like the 'political machinery' that gets activated during elections to get votes.
usage_notes: Can refer to literal machines or a figurative system of people and processes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagpapatakbo ng malaking pabrika ay nangangailangan ng modernong **makinarya**.","translation":"Running a large factory requires modern **machinery**."},{"sentence":"Gumalaw na ang **makinarya** ng partido para sa darating na halalan.","translation":"The party's **machinery** has started to move for the upcoming election."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng suklay upang ayusin, alisin ang buhol, o i-istilo ang buhok.
original_explanation: What you do when you wake up looking like a 'bruha' and need to look presentable for a Zoom meeting. 'Magsuklay ka nga, para kang pusang nag-away!' is a classic mom-ism. It's the basic act of taming your wild hair.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to using a comb ('suklay'). For a hairbrush ('sepilyo'), the verb 'magsipilyo' (or 'mag-brush') is used, though 'magsuklay' is often used generically for any hair-tidying action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **magsuklay** bago umalis ng bahay.","translation":"Don't forget to **comb your hair** before leaving the house."},{"sentence":"Nahihirapan siyang **magsuklay** dahil sobrang buhol-buhol ng kanyang buhok.","translation":"She's having a hard time **combing** because her hair is so tangled."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katawagan para sa isang taong mahilig sa tsismis o pagkalat ng balita tungkol sa buhay ng ibang tao.
etymology: A modern portmanteau of the Filipino phrase 'Mare, ano ang latest?' (Friend, what's the latest?).
original_explanation: The official name for the designated chismosa of the group. She's the one who always starts with 'Mare, ano'ng latest?' and has the tea on everyone from your neighbor to that celebrity breakup. The patron saint of neighborhood gossip circles and FB comment sections.
usage_notes: A very popular slang term that emerged around the 2020s. It is used humorously to refer to a gossipmonger, regardless of gender (the male equivalent is sometimes called 'Tolits' from 'Tol, ano'ng latest?').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naku, andiyan na si Aling Nena, ang reyna ng mga **Marites** sa ating kalye.","translation":"Oh no, here comes Aling Nena, the queen of the **gossips** on our street."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala diyan, gawa-gawa lang 'yan ng mga **Marites** sa Facebook.","translation":"Don't believe that, it's just made up by the **rumormongers** on Facebook."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang daanan para sa mga sasakyan o tao na nasa ilalim ng isa pang daan, tulay, o riles ng tren.
original_explanation: The tunnel of hope you dive into when EDSA traffic is a parking lot. It's that slightly gloomy, sometimes smelly, but often faster way to get to the other side. 'Dumaan tayo sa anderpas sa Quiapo para iwas-traffic.'
usage_notes: A Filipinized spelling and pronunciation of the English word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging binabaha ang **anderpas** sa EDSA tuwing malakas ang ulan.","translation":"The **underpass** on EDSA always floods whenever it rains hard."},{"sentence":"May mga nagtitinda sa loob ng **anderpas** ng Quiapo.","translation":"There are vendors inside the Quiapo **underpass**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang muling pagbabalik ng isang bagay, damdamin, alaala, o kalagayan sa dati nitong estado.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'hugot' verb. It's when an old feeling, memory, or even your ex suddenly comes back. 'Manumbalik ang feelings.' It’s also used when you want something good from the past to be restored, like the good old days when 100 pesos could buy you a full meal. It’s the official verb of #ThrowbackThursday.
usage_notes: Often has a nostalgic or emotional connotation. Can refer to feelings, memories, health, or a former state.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay **manumbalik** ang dating sigla ng aming lungsod.","translation":"I hope the former vibrancy of our city will **be restored**."},{"sentence":"Sa tuwing naririnig ko ang kantang iyon, tila ba **nanunumbalik** ang lahat ng alaala.","translation":"Every time I hear that song, it's as if all the memories **return**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng tulong o suporta sa isang tao sa paggawa ng isang gawain; pagdalo sa isang pagtitipon o klase.
etymology: Tagalog verb infix '-um-' + 'asistí' (from Spanish 'asistir' meaning 'to assist' or 'to attend')
original_explanation: This is the Tagalized version of 'assist'. It's what the sidekick does for the hero, or what you do for your boss when they ask you to 'pretty please' help them with their PowerPoint. It can also mean just showing up, like 'attending' a class or a meeting.
usage_notes: A formal or slightly academic-sounding word. 'Tumulong' is the more common, everyday equivalent for 'to help'. 'Umasisti' is often used in the context of formal duties or attendance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umasisti** ang nars sa doktor habang nag-oopera.","translation":"The nurse **assisted** the doctor during the operation."},{"sentence":"Inaasahan ang lahat ng mag-aaral na **umasisti** sa seminar.","translation":"All students are expected to **attend** the seminar."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapaligid sa isang lugar, tulad ng isang lungsod o kuta, ng isang hukbo upang pilitin itong sumuko.
original_explanation: Imagine you and your barkada surrounding the last piece of lechon on the table. That's a `kubkob`. It’s a military term for a siege, where an army surrounds a place to cut off supplies and force a surrender. It’s a total lockdown, medieval style.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa kontekstong militar o pangkasaysayan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kubkob** sa Marawi ay tumagal ng ilang buwan.","translation":"The **siege** of Marawi lasted for several months."},{"sentence":"Naghanda ang mga sundalo para sa isang mahabang **kubkob**.","translation":"The soldiers prepared for a long **siege**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang matatag na paniniwala sa katapatan, kakayahan, o katangian ng isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: Ah, **tiwala**. The most expensive thing in the world. Easy to lose, hard to earn back. It's what you give your friend when they borrow money, what you have in your Grab driver to get you there safely, and what gets broken in every 'hugot' movie. 'Sira na ang **tiwala** ko sa'yo' is the ultimate relationship-ending line.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb with affixes (e.g., 'magtiwala' - to trust, 'pagkakatiwalaan' - trustworthy).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **tiwala** ang pundasyon ng isang matatag na relasyon.","translation":"**Trust** is the foundation of a strong relationship."},{"sentence":"Mayroon akong buong **tiwala** sa kakayahan mo.","translation":"I have full **confidence** in your abilities."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manipis na piraso ng papel, plastik, o metal na may butas na disenyo, na ginagamit upang maglipat ng disenyo sa isang ibabaw sa pamamagitan ng paglalagay ng tinta o pintura.
original_explanation: The original 'copy-paste'. It's that plastic sheet with letters and shapes you used for your project titles in elementary school to make your handwriting look perfect. Also used by street artists for quick, repeatable graffiti. It's the cheat code for perfect lettering.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng **istensil** para maging pantay-pantay ang mga letra sa karatula.","translation":"She used a **stencil** to make the letters on the sign even."},{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng **istensil** na may disenyo ng mga bulaklak para sa aking kwarto.","translation":"I bought a flower-designed **stencil** for my room."}]

translation: to get cracked; to develop a crack
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng isa o higit pang maliliit na bitak o guhit sa ibabaw ng isang matigas na bagay, ngunit hindi pa tuluyang basag.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your phone screen after you drop it for the nth time. It's not totally shattered, but it's got that spiderweb pattern. It's also your heart after seeing your crush with someone else—not broken, just `nagkalamat`. #hugot
usage_notes: Describes the initial stage of damage before something completely breaks.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingatan mo ang salamin at baka **magkalamat**.","translation":"Be careful with the mirror, it might **get cracked**."},{"sentence":"**Nagkalamat** ang pader dahil sa lindol.","translation":"The wall **developed cracks** because of the earthquake."}]

translation: to fall off (hair, feathers), to shed
meaning_filipino: Pagkalaglag o pagkatanggal ng buhok, balahibo, o butil mula sa pinagkakabitan nito.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your pet dog during shedding season—the whole house becomes a carpet of fur. Or that alarming moment in the shower when you see more hair on the drain than on your head. "Hala, **nalulugas** na buhok ko!" is the battle cry of the stressed-out. It's the process of things falling off when they're supposed to be attached.
usage_notes: Commonly used for hair loss in humans and animals, or grains falling from a stalk. The verb form is often `malugas` (infinitive) or `nalulugas` (present tense).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Normal lang na **malugas** ang balahibo ng aso.","translation":"It's normal for a dog's fur to **fall off**."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa stress, nagsimulang **malugas** ang kanyang buhok.","translation":"Due to stress, her hair started to **fall out**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang propesyonal na dalubhasa sa pagpapaganda ng hitsura ng isang tao, na karaniwang nagbibigay ng serbisyo tulad ng pag-aayos ng buhok, pagme-makeup, manikyur, at pedikyur.
original_explanation: The magical person, often your friendly neighborhood 'parlorista', who can transform you from 'puyat na puyat' to 'ready for my close-up'. They are the keepers of gossip, the masters of the haircut, and the high priests and priestesses of the rebond. A good beautician is more trusted than a politician.
usage_notes: The word is used directly in Tagalog/Taglish. The local term 'parlorista' is also very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magaling ang **beautician** sa salon na iyon; siya ang laging nag-aayos sa akin.","translation":"The **beautician** at that salon is great; she's the one who always styles me."},{"sentence":"Nag-aral siya para maging isang lisensyadong **beautician**.","translation":"She studied to become a licensed **beautician**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsakay o paglalakbay sa pamamagitan ng isang bapor o malaking sasakyang-dagat.
original_explanation: Before Cebu Pacific and AirAsia, this was the way to go island-hopping across the Philippines. To `magbapor` is to take a ship, like the 2GO or a SuperFerry. It's slower, you can feel the waves, and you might get seasick, but you can bring a ton of baggage. It's the classic 'probinsya' travel experience.
usage_notes: While 'barko' is more common for ship, 'bapor' and 'magbapor' are still understood, often with a slightly older or more traditional connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Noong araw, kailangan mong **magbapor** nang ilang araw para makarating mula Maynila hanggang Mindanao.","translation":"In the old days, you had to **travel by ship** for several days to get from Manila to Mindanao."},{"sentence":"Nagpasya silang **magbapor** pauwi sa kanilang probinsya para makatipid.","translation":"They decided to **travel by ship** going home to their province to save money."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na binaligtad mula sa salitang Ingles na "power," na nangangahulugang lakas, kapangyarihan, o bilang isang sigaw ng pagbibigay-sigla.
etymology: Baliktad (reversed) slang from the English word 'power' (pa-wer -> wer-pa).
original_explanation: The battle cry of a tito or your cool dad trying to sound hip. It's 'power' but make it '80s Pinoy slang. You shout this when your friend finally gets their crush's number, or when the wifi is surprisingly fast. Petmalu! Lodi! Werpa!
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa wakas, natapos din ang project! **Werpa**!","translation":"Finally, the project is finished! **Power**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong gumagamit ng panlilinlang o hindi tapat na impluwensya upang kontrolin ang iba.
etymology: From English "manipulator". A common loanword in Taglish.
original_explanation: The final boss of toxic people. Sila yung mga taong ang galing magpaikot ng kwento, at sa huli, ikaw pa ang lalabas na masama. They'll make you question your own sanity. Ingat sa mga manipulator!
usage_notes: A Taglish term for a person who manipulates. The formal Tagalog is 'mapagmanipula' (as a noun/adjective).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpapaloko sa kanya, isa siyang expert na **manipulator**.","translation":"Don't be fooled by him/her, he/she is an expert **manipulator**."},{"sentence":"Narealize ko na isa pala siyang **manipulator** after all these years.","translation":"I realized that he/she was a **manipulator** after all these years."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hudyat o pahiwatig upang magsimula, magpatuloy, o isagawa ang isang kilos; pagpapahayag ng pagsang-ayon.
original_explanation: The ultimate "G!" signal. Short for "Game!" or "Let's do it!" 'Pag sinabi ng barkada mo, "Tara, Inuman?" at ang sagot mo ay "Go!" ibig sabihin, on the way ka na. It's the green light for any plan, from a coffee run to a spontaneous beach trip.
usage_notes: An extremely common English loanword used as a standalone interjection in Tagalog to mean "yes," "let's do it," or "I'm in."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto mo bang sumama sa mall? **Go**!","translation":"Do you want to come to the mall? **Go**!"},{"sentence":"Okay, sa bilang ng tatlo, **go**!","translation":"Okay, on the count of three, **go**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Bawat isang piraso o bahagi ng bungang sitrus tulad ng dalandan, o ng ulo ng bawang.
original_explanation: The reason why your mom says 'kumuha ka ng isang bawang' but actually means 'kumuha ka ng isang siha ng bawang.' It's that single piece of suha or pomelo you painstakingly peel, only for your sibling to steal it.
usage_notes: Specific to segments of fruits like citrus or cloves of garlic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maghiwa ka ng tatlong **siha** ng bawang para sa ginisang kangkong.","translation":"Chop three **cloves** of garlic for the sauteed water spinach."},{"sentence":"Ang sarap kainin ng matamis na **siha** ng suha.","translation":"It's delicious to eat a sweet **segment** of pomelo."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tela na ipinapatong sa ibabaw ng mesa bilang palamuti o proteksyon.
original_explanation: That fancy cloth you only bring out during fiestas, Christmas, or when important visitors are coming over. For everyday use, it's probably that plastic, easily-wipeable 'mantel' with fruit or flower designs that has been on your dining table since the 90s.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakilagay mo nga itong bagong **mantel** sa lamesa.","translation":"Please put this new **tablecloth** on the table."},{"sentence":"Natapunan ng kape ang puting **mantel**.","translation":"The white **tablecloth** was spilled on with coffee."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing maluwag ang pagkakatali o pagkakabuhol ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung pag-untie mo ng shoelaces mo after a long day. O kaya 'yung pagluwag ng feelings mo para sa kanya kasi narealize mong toxic pala. Let go, beshie!
usage_notes: Often used for ropes, knots, or anything tied.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **magkalos** ng buhol sa lubid.","translation":"Help me **untie** the knot in the rope."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **magkalos** ng sinturon para makahinga siya nang maayos.","translation":"The belt needs to be **loosened** so he can breathe properly."}]

translation: to adapt; to fit in; to make something fit
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-ayon o paglapat sa isang bagay, sitwasyon, o kapaligiran; ang pagiging angkop o akma.
etymology: From the root word 'agpang' (fit, suitable) with the infix '-um-'.
original_explanation: Like a chameleon changing colors, 'to umagpang' is to adjust yourself to fit the situation. It’s what you do when you move to a new city and learn the local culture. It’s also what a programmer does to make two different systems talk to each other. It’s about finding the perfect fit, whether it's social, emotional, or technical.
usage_notes: Can be used for social adaptation, as well as for physically or technically making things fit together.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap para sa kanya na **umagpang** sa bagong kultura ng kumpanya.","translation":"It was difficult for him to **adapt** to the new company culture."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng karpintero na **umagpang** ang pinto sa lumang hamba.","translation":"The carpenter tried to **make the door fit** the old frame."}]

translation: to cause, to bring about, to result in
meaning_filipino: Maging sanhi o dahilan ng isang pangyayari, kalagayan, o resulta.
original_explanation: This is what happens when your 'marupok' self decides to text your ex at 2 AM. Kung anuman ang gulo na idulot niyan, 'yan ang tinatawag na 'consequences'. It's the effect your actions bring, whether it's a good grade from studying or a food coma from an unli-samgyup session.
usage_notes: The 'i-' prefix here indicates a causative focus, meaning the action causes something to happen or come into being.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Anong kabutihan ang **idudulot** ng iyong paghihiganti?","translation":"What good will your revenge **bring about**?"},{"sentence":"Sana ay kaligayahan ang **idulot** ng bagong taon sa ating lahat.","translation":"I hope the new year **brings** happiness to us all."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang idyomatikong pahayag para sa isang taong madaldal, mahilig magsiwalat ng sikreto, o hindi mapigilang magsalita tungkol sa ibang tao.
etymology: From makati (itchy) + ang (the) + dila (tongue). A literal "itchy tongue."
original_explanation: This is the official diagnosis for your neighborhood Marites. Someone who literally can't keep a secret. The moment you tell them "secret lang natin 'to ha," you've basically broadcasted it to the entire barangay. Their tongue is "itchy" to spill the tea. "Huwag kang magkwento diyan, makati ang dila niyan, bukas alam na ng lahat 'yan."
usage_notes: A very common idiom to describe a gossipmonger.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa opisina bilang taong **makati ang dila**.","translation":"She is known in the office as someone who is **gossipy**."},{"sentence":"Pinagsabihan ko siyang huwag ipagkalat ang sikreto, pero **makati ang dila** niya talaga.","translation":"I told him not to spread the secret, but he's just really **talkative** (can't keep a secret)."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kakulangan sa karangalan, integridad, o kagalang-galang na katayuan, na kadalasa'y bunga ng isang kahiya-hiyang gawa.
original_explanation: This is when you lose your "diskarte" and your "pride" in one go. 'Yung nahuli kang nangongopya sa exam, or 'yung politiko na nangako tapos biglang nag-corrupt. It's the opposite of having delicadeza. It's the act of doing something that makes your lola shake her head in disappointment.
usage_notes: Isang mabigat na salita na nagpapahiwatig ng malalim na pagkawala ng respeto sa sarili o mula sa iba dahil sa isang moral na paglabag.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagsisinungaling sa bayan ay isang gawa ng **kawalang-dangal**.","translation":"Lying to the nation is an act of **dishonor**."},{"sentence":"Mas gugustuhin pa niyang mamatay kaysa mabuhay sa **kawalang-dangal**.","translation":"He would rather die than live in **dishonor**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang opisyal na titulo para sa asawa ng halal na pangulo ng isang bansa.
original_explanation: She's the wife of the President, the nation's 'First Tita'. While not an elected official, her role is often focused on social causes, hosting events, and generally looking graceful beside the most powerful person in the country. Her fashion choices are always a hot topic.
usage_notes: Mahalaga ang malaking titik dahil ito ay isang pormal na titulo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **Pangunang Ginang ng bansa** ay nanguna sa isang proyektong pangkawanggawa.","translation":"The **First Lady of the country** led a charity project."}]

translation: to cause pain, to inflict suffering
meaning_filipino: Ang magdulot ng sakit, hirap, o pighati sa isang tao, sa pisikal man o emosyonal na paraan.
original_explanation: This is the verb for all the *hugot* feels. It's what that person who left you on 'read' did. It can be physical, like when you eat something that gives you a stomachache, or emotional, like reminiscing about 'the one that got away.' It's the act of causing an 'ouch' to the body or the heart.
usage_notes: Can refer to both physical pain ('magpasakit ng tiyan' - to cause a stomachache) and emotional pain ('magpasakit ng damdamin' - to hurt feelings).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw kong **magpasakit** ng ulo sa mga problemang hindi ko naman kontrolado.","translation":"I don't want to **cause myself a headache** over problems I can't control."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga salita ay **nagpasakit** sa damdamin ng marami.","translation":"His words **caused pain** to the feelings of many."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan kung saan ang isang ibabaw ay natakpan o tinubuan ng lumot dahil sa katagalan o palagiang pagkabasa.
original_explanation: Basically, something that's been left alone for so long that moss started growing on it. It's the aesthetic of ancient ruins, forgotten garden statues, or that water bottle you lost under your bed for a year. "Nilumot na sa tagal" is the Filipino way of saying something is old, neglected, or has been waiting forever, like your crush finally noticing you.
usage_notes: Can be used as a verb (nilumot - was covered in moss) or more commonly as an adjective (nilumot na bato - a moss-covered stone).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga batong malapit sa talon ay **nilumot** na at madulas.","translation":"The stones near the waterfall are **moss-covered** and slippery."},{"sentence":"**Nilumot** na ang mga pangako mong napako.","translation":"Your broken promises have been left for so long they've **gathered moss**."}]

translation: to feel unwell, to feel sick
meaning_filipino: Ang makaranas ng hindi magandang kondisyon sa katawan; ang pagkakaroon ng sintomas ng sakit.
original_explanation: The universal excuse to get out of anything. "Boss, di ako makakapasok, sumama ang pakiramdam ko." It's the Monday morning feeling, the post-buffet regret, or the start of a real flu. It’s your body sending a notification: "System error. Please reboot with Paracetamol and lots of sleep."
usage_notes: A common and polite way to say one is feeling sick. 'Pakiramdam' means 'feeling' or 'sensation'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos magpaulan, **sumama ang pakiramdam** niya kinabukasan.","translation":"After playing in the rain, he **felt unwell** the next day."},{"sentence":"Kapag **sumama ang pakiramdam** mo, magpahinga ka kaagad.","translation":"When you **feel sick**, rest immediately."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng mabilis na pag-iwas sa isang bagay na paparating o sa isang panganib upang hindi matamaan o masaktan.
original_explanation: When someone asks "Kailan ka magbabayad ng utang mo?" and you suddenly pretend to see a long-lost friend across the street. That's an expert-level pag-ilag. It's the national sport when dodging awkward questions, responsibilities, or a flying tsinelas.
usage_notes: Can refer to both physical dodging (like in sports) and metaphorical evasion (like avoiding a topic).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bilis ng **pag-ilag** ni Manny Pacquiao sa suntok ng kalaban.","translation":"Manny Pacquiao's **dodging** of the opponent's punch was so fast."},{"sentence":"Dalubhasa siya sa **pag-ilag** sa mga tanong tungkol sa kanyang lovelife.","translation":"She is an expert at the **evasion** of questions about her lovelife."}]

translation: detached skin or bark; flayed piece
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa balat ng kahoy, prutas, o hayop na natanggal o natuklap mula sa pinagkakabitan nito, karaniwan sa malaking piraso.
original_explanation: Think of a sunburn so bad your skin starts peeling off in sheets. That's **lapnis**. Or the bark of a tree that's coming off. It's the 'ghosting' equivalent for skin and surfaces—bigla na lang bumibitaw.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'lapnit', but 'lapnis' can imply a larger, more significant piece that has been detached.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **lapnis** ng balat sa kanyang braso dahil sa pagkakapaso.","translation":"There's a **detached piece of skin** on his arm from the burn."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang **lapnis** ng puno ng saging bilang panali.","translation":"He used the **detached bark** of the banana tree as a tie."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mababang bundok, burol, o lambak.
original_explanation: Not the mountain that will move for you, but a small, manageable one. Think of it as a 'bundok-bundukan' or a big hill. It's a geographical term you're more likely to find in a textbook or a place name (like 'Banaue') than in a daily convo.
usage_notes: This meaning is very rare in modern spoken Tagalog and is mostly encountered in place names or literature.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Makikita ang isang maliit na kapilya sa ituktok ng **bana**.","translation":"A small chapel can be seen at the top of the **hillock**."},{"sentence":"Ang pangalang 'Banaue' ay pinaniniwalaang nagmula sa salitang **bana**.","translation":"The name 'Banaue' is believed to have originated from the word **bana**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging lubhang nababad sa tubig o anumang likido.
etymology: Reduplication of `basa` (wet), which intensifies the meaning.
original_explanation: You after walking for 2 minutes under the August rain without an umbrella. It's the state of your shirt after a water gun fight or after riding the Log Jam at Enchanted Kingdom. "Friend, basang-basa ka! Umuwi ka na, baka magkasakit ka pa." Also used metaphorically when someone is caught red-handed: "Basang-basa sa ebidensya!"
usage_notes: The repetition of the root word `basa` serves as an intensifier.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumating siya sa opisina na **basang-basa** dahil sa malakas na ulan.","translation":"He arrived at the office **soaking wet** because of the heavy rain."},{"sentence":"**Basang-basa** na ang sahig, mag-ingat ka at baka madulas.","translation":"The floor is **soaking wet**, be careful you might slip."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pakiramdam ng matindi at kumikirot na sakit, tulad ng dulot ng sugat na nilagyan ng alkohol o ng maanghang na sili.
original_explanation: This is the pain you feel when you put alcohol on a fresh wound. It's the sharp, burning sensation when calamansi juice gets into a paper cut. It's also the emotional 'ouch' when your crush's reply is just a 'k.' or a thumbs-up emoji. Kahapdian is that specific, sharp, 'aray ko po' kind of pain, both literal and hugot.
usage_notes: Describes a specific type of pain—sharp and stinging, as opposed to a dull ache (`kirot`) or general pain (`sakit`).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya natiis ang **kahapdian** ng sugat kaya napasigaw siya.","translation":"He couldn't endure the **stinging pain** of the wound, so he shouted."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman ko ang **kahapdian** ng kanyang mga salita sa aking puso.","translation":"I felt the **sting** of his words in my heart."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng gamot na ginagamit upang puksain o pigilan ang pagdami ng mga mikroorganismo tulad ng bakterya.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung reseta sa'yo ng doktor kapag matindi na ang ubo't sipon mo at hindi na kaya ng Vicks. Kailangan mo 'tong tapusin, 'di tulad ng series sa Netflix na pwede mong iwanan 'pag 'di mo na trip. Incomplete dosage is a big no-no, parang ghosting lang.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa kontekstong medikal. Mahalagang sundin ang reseta ng doktor at tapusin ang buong kurso ng gamutan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Reseta ng doktor na uminom ako ng **antibayotik** sa loob ng pitong araw.","translation":"The doctor prescribed that I take **antibiotics** for seven days."},{"sentence":"Huwag basta-basta iinom ng **antibayotik** nang walang konsulta sa doktor.","translation":"Do not just take **antibiotics** without consulting a doctor."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbabantay o pag-eespiya sa isang tao o bagay nang palihim.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `pag-` (panandang pandiwari) at `manman` (pagmasid nang malapitan).
original_explanation: Ito yung ginagawa mo sa social media profile ng ex mo o ng crush mo. Stalking, pero 'di mo aaminin. Parang undercover agent lang ang peg, naghahanap ng ebidensya o chismis. "Sino 'tong kasama niya sa picture?!"
usage_notes: Madalas may negatibong konotasyon ng pag-eespiya, ngunit maaari ring gamitin sa neutral na konteksto tulad ng pagbabantay ng isang detektib.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang **pagmamanman** ng mga pulis sa pinaghihinalaang pugad ng mga kriminal.","translation":"The police's **surveillance** of the suspected criminal den is tight."},{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na ang **pagmamanman** sa bawat galaw niya online.","translation":"Stop your **spying** on his every move online."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng hindi pag-aplay o pag-empleyo ng isang bagay; ang kawalan o pagtigil ng paggamit.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng 'hindi' (not) at 'paggamit' (the act of using), mula sa salitang-ugat na 'gamit' (use).
original_explanation: This is the fate of the treadmill you bought for your new year's resolution, now a very expensive clothes hanger. It’s also the "leave on read" of the physical world. The **hindi paggamit** of your brain cells during a Monday morning meeting.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa mga pormal o teknikal na konteksto, tulad ng mga manwal o legal na dokumento.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **hindi paggamit** ng seatbelt ay labag sa batas.","translation":"The **non-use** of a seatbelt is against the law."},{"sentence":"Ang madalas na **hindi paggamit** sa makina ay maaaring magdulot ng sira nito.","translation":"Frequent **disuse** of the machine can cause it to break down."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang likhang-sining na tatlong-dimensyonal na karaniwang nililok mula sa bato, kahoy, o metal, na kumakatawan sa isang tao o bagay.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "bulto," na maaaring mangahulugang "volume" o "figure."
original_explanation: Ito yung mga estatwa sa Luneta o sa plaza. Minsan, ito rin yung feeling mo sa group project—ikaw lahat gumawa, pero kasama sila sa picture. O kaya 'yung itsura mo kapag nag-freeze ang Zoom call mo sa very unflattering angle. Statue mode!
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **rebulto** ni Jose Rizal ay makikita sa Luneta Park.","translation":"The **statue** of Jose Rizal can be seen in Luneta Park."},{"sentence":"Maraming turista ang nagpapakuha ng litrato sa tabi ng **rebulto** ng Lapu-Lapu.","translation":"Many tourists take pictures beside the **statue** of Lapu-Lapu."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang maintindihan o maabot ng isipan ang kahulugan, katotohanan, o kahalagahan ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: That "Aha!" moment when the math problem finally makes sense, or when you finally get why your friend is giving you the silent treatment. It's more than just knowing; it's deep comprehension. In office jargon, it's "managing expectations" and "alignment." Sa love life, ito yung level na hindi mo na kailangan ng long message, gets mo na agad.
usage_notes: Madalas na ipinagpapalit sa `pag-unawa`, ngunit ang `pagkaunawa` ay maaaring magbigay-diin sa resultang estado o lalim ng pag-intindi.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malinaw ang kanyang **pagkaunawa** sa mga kumplikadong isyu ng bansa.","translation":"His **understanding** of the country's complex issues is clear."},{"sentence":"Ang susi sa maayos na relasyon ay ang tamang **pagkaunawa** sa isa't isa.","translation":"The key to a good relationship is proper **comprehension** of each other."}]

translation: to cause to lose consciousness; to knock out
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasanhi sa isang tao na mawalan ng ulirat o kamalayan, maaaring dahil sa gamot, suntok, o iba pang dahilan.
original_explanation: What a boxer does to his opponent with a good punch, or what anesthesia does to you before surgery. In dramas, it's what the kidnapper's chloroform-soaked panyo does to the bida. "Isang malakas na suntok lang, sapat na para magpawalang-malay sa kalaban."
usage_notes: Can also be used to mean 'to feign unconsciousness' ('nagpawalang-malay').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamitan siya ng pampatulog para **magpawalang-malay** bago ang operasyon.","translation":"He was given an anesthetic to **cause him to lose consciousness** before the operation."},{"sentence":"Nagpanggap siyang nahimatay at **nagpawalang-malay** para takasan ang sitwasyon.","translation":"She pretended to faint and **feigned unconsciousness** to escape the situation."}]

translation: to go for it; rock on; hustle
meaning_filipino: Isang impormal na salita na nangangahulugang "sige lang," "ituloy mo," o tumutukoy sa pagtatrabaho o pagkilos nang may sigasig.
etymology: Mula sa pinaikling Ingles na "rock" o "rock and roll", na may kaugnayan sa salitang "raket" (sideline/gig).
original_explanation: The ultimate Pinoy battle cry. Short for 'rock on'. Gusto mong mag-resign? Rak! Gusto mong mag-start ng business? Rak! Gusto mong umorder ng extra rice? Rak na 'yan! It's the verbal equivalent of a Nike check mark: Just do it. Pwedeng verb ("Rakenrol to the world!"), pwedeng noun ("Kailangan ko ng raket/rak.").
usage_notes: Isang napaka-versatile na salitang-kalye. Ang ugat nito ay "raket" (sideline/gig), na naging "rak" bilang pandiwa o pangngalan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Rak** na 'to, mga besh! Huling kembot na lang para sa deadline!","translation":"Let's **go for it**, guys! This is the final push for the deadline!"},{"sentence":"Kahit pagod, tuloy lang ang **rak** para sa pamilya.","translation":"Even if tired, the **hustle** continues for the family."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katawagang balbal para sa isang babae na niyayakap ang isang estetika ng kalungkutan at melankoliya, kadalasang ipinapakita sa pamamagitan ng musika, pananamit, at presensya sa social media.
etymology: Mula sa salitang balbal sa Ingles na 'sad girl', ang katapat ng 'sadboy'.
original_explanation: She's the one listening to Taylor Swift's 'All Too Well (10 Minute Version)' on repeat, romanticizing her pain, and posting teary-eyed selfies with poetic captions. The sadgirl finds beauty in melancholy, whether it's genuine or just for the 'gram.
usage_notes: Tulad ng 'sadboy', ito ay isang termino sa kulturang pop na maaaring tumukoy sa isang tunay na estado ng pag-iisip o isang piniling 'aesthetic' lamang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puro Lana Del Rey ang nasa playlist niya, nasa **sadgirl** era yata siya ngayon.","translation":"Her playlist is all Lana Del Rey, I think she's in her **sadgirl** era right now."},{"sentence":"Ang pagiging **sadgirl** ay hindi lang tungkol sa kalungkutan, kundi isang buong aesthetic.","translation":"Being a **sadgirl** isn't just about sadness, it's a whole aesthetic."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangatnig na nagpapahayag ng dahilan o katuwiran, kadalasang may pahiwatig ng pagkadismaya, paghamak, o pagbibigay-katwiran sa isang hindi kanais-nais na sitwasyon.
etymology: From 'pa-' + 'libhasa' (to be accustomed to something, often negative).
original_explanation: This is the "because" you use when you're about to throw shade or make an excuse. It's not a neutral "kasi" or "dahil." It's the "because" that comes with a side of judgment. "Late na naman siya, palibhasa puyat sa kaka-ML." See? It's got attitude. It's the conjunction equivalent of an eye-roll.
usage_notes: Carries a slightly critical or judgmental tone compared to 'dahil' or 'sapagkat'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi na siya nag-aral, **palibhasa** mayaman na ang pamilya niya.","translation":"He didn't study anymore, **precisely because** his family is already rich."},{"sentence":"**Palibhasa** sanay sa hirap, hindi siya nagrereklamo.","translation":"**Since** he is used to hardship, he doesn't complain."}]

meaning_filipino: Utusan o atasan ang isang tao na magsagawa ng isang gawain, tungkulin, o trabaho.
original_explanation: What your manager does when they see you watching YouTube during office hours. It's the official term for "Hoy, 'di ka bayad para tumunganga!" Can also be used for that tamad na jowa you need to motivate to wash the dishes.
usage_notes: A complex causative verb, often used in a context of authority, like a boss to an employee or a parent to a child.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **papagtrabahuhin** ang mga bago mong tauhan para masubok ang kanilang kakayahan.","translation":"You need to **make** your new staff **work** to test their abilities."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa buhok na sobrang kulot o sa isang bagay na kakaiba, lalo na sa kontekstong sekswal.
original_explanation: This is a direct loanword from English. It can mean "kinky" hair (super kulot, like an afro) or "kinky" in the... ahem... spicy bedroom sense. Context is everything here. You use it for hair, you're a hairstylist. You use it for anything else, you're probably sharing a meme your lola shouldn't see.
usage_notes: A direct adaptation of the English word with the same dual meanings (hair texture and unconventional preferences).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto niyang ipa-unat ang kanyang **kingki** na buhok.","translation":"She wants to have her **kinky** hair straightened."},{"sentence":"Medyo **kingki** ang mga biro niya kaya hindi lahat natatawa.","translation":"His jokes are a bit **kinky** so not everyone finds them funny."}]

translation: each to his own; individually; separately
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa paraan ng paggawa o pag-aari nang paisa-isa o hiwa-hiwalay; walang pakialaman.
original_explanation: The official motto of potluck parties and splitting the bill. "KKB" (Kanya-Kanyang Bayad) is a sacred Filipino text. It means "you do you." It's the social contract that says, "Let's all eat together, but we're all paying for our own orders." It can also describe a situation where everyone is just minding their own business, for better or for worse.
usage_notes: Very common in both spoken and written Filipino. The acronym "KKB" (Kanya-Kanyang Bayad) is extremely popular. Can function as both an adverb and an adjective.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng pulong, **kanya-kanya** na silang umuwi.","translation":"After the meeting, they went home **separately**."},{"sentence":"Sa panahong ito, **kanya-kanya** tayo ng diskarte para mabuhay.","translation":"In these times, we **each have our own** strategy to survive."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang labis na masigasig o masugid na tagahanga ng isang partikular na sikat na tao, grupo, o palabas.
etymology: From the 2000 Eminem song 'Stan', about an obsessive fan.
original_explanation: Hindi ka lang basta fan, you're a stan. Alam mo birthday ng bias mo, paboritong pagkain niya, at handa kang makipag-away sa Twitter para ipagtanggol siya. It's a lifestyle. Inspired by the Eminem song 'Stan.'
usage_notes: Used to describe a very dedicated fan. Can also be used as a verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isa siyang certified **stan** ng SB19.","translation":"She is a certified **stan** of SB19."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa susunod na araw pagkatapos ng kasalukuyang araw.
original_explanation: The most powerful and dangerous word in the procrastinator's vocabulary. It's where all your diet plans, workout routines, and life goals live. 'Mamaya na' is its younger sibling.
usage_notes: Pronounced with stress on the first syllable (BU-kas) to mean 'tomorrow'. Contrast with 'bukás' (open).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkita tayo **bukas** sa may mall.","translation":"Let's meet **tomorrow** at the mall."},{"sentence":"Saka na natin gawin 'yan, **bukas** na lang.","translation":"Let's do that later, maybe just **tomorrow**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katawagan para sa isang tao na may kakulangan sa pag-iisip, hangal, o tanga.
original_explanation: This is your classic 'shunga' or 'engot'. It's not just making a mistake; it's that state of being where your brain feels like it's on airplane mode during a crucial Zoom call. It's more of a playful insult among friends, but can be genuinely offensive if said with malice. Think of someone trying to push a 'pull' door with all their might. 'Yan ang bang-aw.
usage_notes: Often used as a lighthearted insult, but context is key. Its tone is similar to 'engot' or 'shunga'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **bang-aw**, alam mo namang bawal 'yan.","translation":"Don't be an **idiot**, you know that's forbidden."},{"sentence":"Natawa na lang kami sa pagka-**bang-aw** niya nang maling pinto ang pinasok.","translation":"We just laughed at his **foolishness** when he entered the wrong door."}]

translation: was cornered; was in a tight spot; was short on cash
meaning_filipino: Nasa isang kalagayan na mahirap o walang malabasan; naipit sa isang sitwasyon; kinapos sa pananalapi.
original_explanation: That feeling a week before payday. You're 'financially challenged' or, in Pinoy terms, nagipit. It's also when you're stuck between two arguing friends. You are, quite literally, in a tight spot. The universal signal to message a friend, 'Pautang, besh.'
usage_notes: Can refer to a financial, physical, or emotional state of being constricted or pressured.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagipit** ako sa pera noong nakaraang linggo kaya nangutang muna ako.","translation":"I **was short on cash** last week so I had to borrow money."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam niya ay **nagipit** siya sa desisyon ng kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"He felt **cornered** by his parents' decision."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing matalas o mas matalas ang isang bagay; hasain. Maaari ring tumukoy sa pagpapatalas ng isip o pandama.
original_explanation: The action you do when your kitchen knife is as dull as your love life. 'Pa-**talasan** mo naman 'tong kutsilyo, parang 'di na makahiwa ng sibuyas.' It's also what you do to your brain before a big exam—you sharpen it with review sessions and lots of coffee.
usage_notes: The command form is 'Talasan mo!' (Sharpen it!).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **talasan** ang lapis bago gamitin sa pagguhit.","translation":"The pencil needs **to be sharpened** before being used for drawing."},{"sentence":"**Talasan** mo ang iyong pandinig upang marinig ang ibinubulong niya.","translation":"**Sharpen** your hearing so you can hear what he is whispering."}]

meaning_filipino: Bumuo ng mga pangkat na may tiglilimang miyembro.
etymology: From mag- (verb prefix) + lima (five), with reduplication to indicate distribution.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na group project tapos sinabi ng teacher, "Okay class, maglima-lima kayo." Tapos ikaw 'yung pang-anim na walang ka-grupo. The ultimate social anxiety trigger in a Filipino classroom.
usage_notes: The reduplication lima-lima indicates a distributive action, meaning the grouping into fives happens across a set of items or people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Maglima-lima** tayo para magkasya sa bawat bangka.","translation":"Let's **group ourselves by fives** so we can fit in each boat."},{"sentence":"Pinapabasa sa amin ang libro at pagkatapos ay kailangang **maglima-lima** para sa talakayan.","translation":"We were told to read the book and then we had to **form groups of five** for the discussion."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdaan mula sa isang panig patungo sa kabilang panig ng isang lugar, tulad ng ilog, kalye, o anumang hadlang.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "tawid" at hulaping "-in".
original_explanation: Parang pag-move on sa ex mo. Kailangan mong lakasan ang loob mo para makarating sa "other side" kung saan single ka na ulit at ready to mingle. O kaya 'yung feeling na tatawid ka ng EDSA, 'di ka sure kung aabot ka sa kabilang side. Life is a risk, parang pag-tawid sa highway.
usage_notes: Ito ang anyong pokus sa layon ng pandiwa. Ang "tumawid" naman ang pokus sa tagaganap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **tawirin** ang ilog para makarating sa susunod na baryo.","translation":"We need to **cross** the river to get to the next village."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **tawirin** ang tulay na nasira ng bagyo.","translation":"It's difficult **to cross** the bridge that was destroyed by the typhoon."}]

translation: to be saved; to be rescued
meaning_filipino: Ang makaiwas o makalaya mula sa panganib, kapahamakan, o kamatayan.
original_explanation: That feeling when your Grab driver arrives just as it starts to rain. Or when you thought you failed a subject but the prof curved the grades. "Maligtas" is being rescued, whether it's from a burning building, a toxic relationship, or a "petsa de peligro" situation where your friend treats you to lunch. A true blessing!
usage_notes: Can be used in physical, emotional, financial, or spiritual contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nanalangin siya na sana'y **maligtas** ang lahat sa paparating na bagyo.","translation":"He/She prayed that everyone would **be saved** from the coming typhoon."},{"sentence":"Buti na lang may naipon ako, kung hindi, hindi ako **maliligtas** sa gastusin.","translation":"It's a good thing I had savings, otherwise, I wouldn't have **been saved** from the expenses."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng kalinga, proteksyon, at atensyon sa isang tao, hayop, o bagay.
original_explanation: What your mom tells you to do with your younger sibling. What your friend tells you to do with your new iPhone. What your heart tells you to do with your jowa, pero minsan napapabayaan. 'Please alagaan mo ang puso ko.'
usage_notes: An object-focused verb. The object is the one being cared for. The actor is usually marked by 'ng' or a possessive pronoun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tungkulin nating **alagaan** ang ating kalikasan.","translation":"It is our duty **to take care of** our environment."},{"sentence":"Sino ang mag-a**alaga** sa aso habang nasa bakasyon tayo?","translation":"Who will **take care of** the dog while we are on vacation?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtalon sa ibabaw ng isang bagay o hadlang.
original_explanation: From the hugot line "Lundagin mo, baby!" popularized by a movie. It means to take a leap of faith, to go for it despite the obstacles. Literally, it's what you do to cross a puddle ('kanal') or a sleeping dog on the sidewalk. Figuratively, it’s what you do when you apply for that job you think you're not qualified for.
usage_notes: The object-focused verb form of 'lundag'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kaya mo bang **lundagin** ang bakod na 'yan?","translation":"Can you **jump over** that fence?"},{"sentence":"Huwag kang matakot, **lundagin** mo ang mga hamon sa buhay.","translation":"Don't be afraid, **jump over** life's challenges."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapahiwatig ng pagkilos nang labag sa kalooban, may pag-aalinlangan, o hindi buong-puso.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung "pilit" version. Parang 'yung paghuhugas mo ng plato. Gagawin mo pero **ayaw-ayaw**. O 'yung pagsama mo sa lakad ng barkada kahit gusto mo lang matulog. Sumama ka nga, pero 'yung mukha mo parang pinagsakluban ng langit at lupa. It's doing something while broadcasting to the world that you'd rather be anywhere else.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin bilang pang-abay (adverb) para ilarawan ang isang kilos. (e.g., "Sumama siya nang ayaw-ayaw.")
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ayaw-ayaw** man, napilitan siyang maglinis ng kanyang kwarto.","translation":"**Reluctantly**, he was forced to clean his room."},{"sentence":"Tinanggap niya ang alok nang **ayaw-ayaw** dahil kailangan niya ng pera.","translation":"He accepted the offer **unwillingly** because he needed the money."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang latak o dumi na naiiwan matapos tunawin ang metal; anumang uri ng basura o bagay na walang halaga.
original_explanation: That gunk or residue left over after you melt something down, like in a metal shop. Figuratively, it's used to describe something worthless or the scum of society. Parang yung mga natitirang feelings mo para sa ex mong 'di kawalan. Charot.
usage_notes: Isang salitang hindi na gaanong ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na usapan. Madalas maririnig sa mga kontekstong teknikal o sa mas matatandang panitikan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinapon ng panday ang **escoriya** mula sa kanyang gawaan.","translation":"The blacksmith threw away the **slag** from his workshop."},{"sentence":"Para sa kanya, **escoriya** lamang ng lipunan ang mga taong iyon.","translation":"For him, those people were just the **dross** of society."}]

translation: to be overtaken, to be caught in (a situation)
meaning_filipino: Ang maabutan o marating ng isang tao, bagay, o pangyayari; ang maranasan ang isang partikular na oras o kaganapan habang nasa isang lugar o gawain.
original_explanation: This is when you get caught by something. 'Inabutan ng ulan' means the rain caught you. 'Inabutan ng deadline' means the deadline caught up to you. It's that 'Oh no, it's here!' moment, whether it's the 5 PM traffic, your boss, or a closing mall.
usage_notes: The stress shifts to the second syllable /a-BU-tan/ for this meaning. It implies being caught or surprised by an event or time.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Inabutan** kami ng malakas na ulan sa daan.","translation":"We were **caught** by the heavy rain on the road."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpuyat para hindi ka **abutan** ng antok sa klase.","translation":"Don't stay up late so you won't **be overcome** by sleepiness in class."}]

translation: to park (a vehicle); to stop (a vehicle)
meaning_filipino: Itigil ang takbo ng isang sasakyan at ilagay sa isang partikular na lugar.
original_explanation: The magic word you shout inside a jeepney when you're about to miss your stop. "Manong, para po!" The verb form is 'ipara', used for bringing a vehicle to a halt, whether it's parking your car neatly or frantically telling the bus driver to stop *right here, right now*.
usage_notes: While 'para' is the common interjection to tell a driver to stop, 'ipara' is the formal verb form used when instructing someone to stop or park a vehicle.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Saan ko pwedeng **ipara** ang kotse ko?","translation":"Where can I **park** my car?"},{"sentence":"**Ipara** mo ang jeep sa tapat ng palengke.","translation":"**Stop** the jeep in front of the market."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang nagpapahayag ng matinding pag-asam o pagnanais na maganap ang isang bagay. Katumbas ng "sana."
etymology: Mula sa pagsasama ng mga salitang "hari" at "nawa," na nangangahulugang "nawa'y mangyari ang kalooban ng hari" o "may it happen."
original_explanation: The OG 'sana all.' It's the formal, almost poetic way of saying 'I hope,' like when you're wishing for your crush to finally notice you, or for the traffic on EDSA to magically disappear. It's got that old-school, wishing-on-a-star vibe. You'd probably hear this in a historical drama, not so much in a text message.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa mga pormal o pampanitikang konteksto. Bihira na itong marinig sa pang-araw-araw na usapan at karaniwang napapalitan na ng "sana."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Harinawa**'y maging mapayapa ang darating na halalan.","translation":"**Hopefully**, the upcoming election will be peaceful."},{"sentence":"Ipinapanalangin kong **harinawa** ay makapasa ka sa pagsusulit.","translation":"I am praying that **you may** pass the exam."}]

translation: to browse; to flip through pages
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbubukas o paghahanap ng isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng paglilipat ng mga pahina ng isang aklat, magasin, o anumang katulad nito.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung ginagawa mo sa menu ng restaurant kahit alam mo nang Chickenjoy with extra rice ang o-orderin mo. It's the act of flipping through pages, whether you're seriously looking for something or just pretending to be busy while waiting for your friend.
usage_notes: Specifically used for items with pages like books, notebooks, magazines, and menus. For doors, windows, or containers, 'buksan' is the correct term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**buklat** mo ang aklat sa kabanata lima.","translation":"Please **open** the book to chapter five."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **buklatin** ang mga lumang photo album tuwing umuulan.","translation":"She loves to **browse** through old photo albums whenever it rains."}]

translation: to retreat, to back out, to move backward
meaning_filipino: Gumalaw paurong; bumalik sa pinanggalingan; o bawiin ang isang naunang desisyon o pangako.
original_explanation: Yung nag-YES ka sa outing, tapos nakita mo yung bank account mo, so bigla kang nag-chat ng "Guys, sorry, 'di pala ako makakasama." That's you, backing out. It can be literal (backing up a car) or figurative (backing out of a deal).
usage_notes: Can be used for physical movement or for changing one's mind or commitment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigla siyang **umatras** sa kasal ilang araw bago ang seremonya.","translation":"He suddenly **backed out** of the wedding a few days before the ceremony."},{"sentence":"\"**Umatras** ka nang kaunti, mababangga mo 'yung pader,\" sigaw niya.","translation":"**Move backward** a little, you're going to hit the wall,\" he shouted."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang koleksyon ng mga litrato at video na ipino-post sa social media upang gunitain ang kaarawan, karaniwang pagkatapos ng mismong araw ng selebrasyon.
etymology: From English "birthday" + "dump" (as in a photo dump).
original_explanation: This is the social media ritual you do *after* your actual birthday. It's the "eto, tingnan niyo lahat ng ganap ko" post. You unload all the unposted, semi-blurry, but still cute photos from your celebration because sayang naman kung 'di makikita ng lahat. It's the digital version of showing the family album, but for your 1,000+ followers.
usage_notes: A very recent slang term, exclusively used in the context of social media platforms like Instagram.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Late post: my **birthday dump** from last week's salubong!","translation":"Late post: my **birthday dump** from last week's celebration!"},{"sentence":"Mag-aabang ako ng **birthday dump** mo, beshie!","translation":"I'll wait for your **birthday dump**, bestie!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaikling anyo ng 'kaibahan'; ang bagay, katangian, o punto na nagpapaiba sa dalawa o higit pang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the "tayo na lang mag-adjust" version of 'kaibahan'. It's the same word, just shorter, like your patience in traffic. It's the **difference**, but make it snappy. "Ano'ng **kaibhan** niyan dito?"
usage_notes: A common colloquial contraction of 'kaibahan'. Less formal and very common in spoken language.
