usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Wala namang **kaibhan** ang luma sa bago.","translation":"There's no **difference** between the old and the new."},{"sentence":"Ipaliwanag mo ang **kaibhan** ng dalawa.","translation":"Explain the **difference** between the two."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malambot na bagay na ginagamit na patungan ng ulo habang natutulog o nagpapahinga.
original_explanation: Your best friend after a long day. The silent witness to your late-night thoughts and the absorber of your tears during a hugot movie marathon. A good unan is a non-negotiable for quality sleep. It can also be a weapon during a pillow fight or a makeshift lap desk.
usage_notes: A basic, essential household item.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Niyakap niya ang kanyang **unan** habang umiiyak.","translation":"She hugged her **pillow** while crying."},{"sentence":"Ang lambot ng bagong **unan** ko!","translation":"My new **pillow** is so soft!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto o kalagayan ng pagkawala o paglalaho nang tuluyan.
etymology: Mula sa ugat na "param" (mawala). Ang unlaping "pagka-" ay tumutukoy sa estado o paraan ng pagkawala.
original_explanation: Parang feelings niya para sa'yo, bigla na lang naglaho. The **pagkaparam** is real. O parang 13th-month pay mo dalawang araw matapos mo itong makuha. Sandaling nandiyan, tapos... poof!
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ikinagulat ng lahat ang biglaang **pagkaparam** ng mahikero sa entablado.","translation":"Everyone was surprised by the sudden **disappearance** of the magician on stage."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkaparam** ng kanyang pag-asa ay unti-unting nangyari.","translation":"The **vanishing** of his hope happened gradually."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang partikular na tono ng kulay-kayumanggi, karaniwan ay tumutukoy sa balat na bahagyang umitim at nagkaroon ng ginintuang kulay dahil sa pagkabilad sa araw.
etymology: Mula sa 'kayumanggi' (brown) at 'kaligatan' (isang salitang naglalarawan sa pagiging makintab o nasinagan ng araw).
original_explanation: This isn't just brown skin. This is that *glowing*, post-beach trip, 'I just spent a week in Siargao' kind of brown. It's the 'Morena and proud' skin tone that has a healthy, golden sheen. The kind of color that looks amazing in sunset photos. It's the aesthetic.
usage_notes: Isang mas makata at tiyak na termino kaysa sa 'kayumanggi' lamang. Binibigyang-diin nito ang ginintuang aspekto ng balat na nasikatan ng araw.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng bakasyon niya sa Palawan, naging **kayumangging-kaligatan** ang kanyang balat.","translation":"After her vacation in Palawan, her skin became a **sun-kissed brown**."},{"sentence":"Ipinagmamalaki niya ang kanyang kulay na **kayumangging-kaligatan**.","translation":"She is proud of her **golden-brown** complexion."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na may maliit na sukat o laki; hindi kalakihan.
original_explanation: "Munti" is the more poetic, "makata" way of saying something is small. You'd use it in a song or a poem about your "munting pangarap" (small dream). It's the opposite of the "go big or go home" mindset; it's the small, quiet wins, like finding a 20-peso bill in your old jeans. The reduplicated form, "munting-munti," means *very* small, like your patience on a Monday morning in EDSA traffic.
usage_notes: Often used in literary or formal contexts, but also in expressing endearment. The form 'munting-munti' is an intensifier meaning 'very small'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroon siyang isang **munting** pangarap na maging isang manunulat.","translation":"She has a **small** dream of becoming a writer."},{"sentence":"Ang kanilang tirahan ay isang **munting** kubo sa tabi ng dagat.","translation":"Their home is a **tiny** hut beside the sea."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sining ng pagdidisenyo sa tela gamit ang karayom at sinulid.
original_explanation: This is your lola's favorite hobby, and now a trendy Gen Z pastime thanks to social media. It's the art of 'drawing' with thread. From the intricate floral designs on a Barong Tagalog to a snarky 'Live, Laugh, Leave Me Alone' quote on a hoop, pagbuburda is proof that patience and a sharp needle can create beautiful things.
usage_notes: A craft often associated with traditional Filipino clothing like the Barong Tagalog and Baro't Saya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagbuburda** ay isang libangan na nangangailangan ng tiyaga at pokus.","translation":"**Embroidery** is a hobby that requires patience and focus."},{"sentence":"Kilala ang bayan ng Lumban, Laguna sa masining na **pagbuburda**.","translation":"The town of Lumban, Laguna is known for its artistic **embroidery**."}]

meaning_filipino: Lahat; buo; walang pag-aalinlangan o pagtitira; sagad o hanggang sa sukdulan.
original_explanation: When you give it your all. Think "beast mode" during the last 5 minutes of your shift, or when you blast the karaoke sound system to the max. "Todo na 'to!" is the battle cry before doing something epic (or stupid).
usage_notes: Often used to mean "maximum" or "full effort". Can be reduplicated as 'todo-todo' for emphasis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Todo** ang effort niya sa pag-decorate para sa party.","translation":"His/Her effort in decorating for the party was **all-out**."},{"sentence":"Naka-**todo** ang volume ng speaker kaya nagising ang mga kapitbahay.","translation":"The speaker volume was at **full-blast**, so the neighbors woke up."}]

meaning_filipino: Tubig na binasbasan ng isang pari at ginagamit sa mga ritwal ng Simbahang Katoliko.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na '(agua) bendita' na nangangahulugang 'blessed (water)'.
original_explanation: That special water you see at the entrance of a Catholic church. You dip your fingers in it, make the sign of the cross, and hope it washes away your minor sins from the past week. Also known as "Agua Bendita." It's like spiritual hand sanitizer.
usage_notes: Karaniwang pinaikling anyo ng "Agua Bendita".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagwisik ng **bendita** ang pari sa mga dumalo sa misa.","translation":"The priest sprinkled **holy water** on the mass attendees."},{"sentence":"Kumuha siya ng kaunting **bendita** bago umalis ng simbahan.","translation":"She took a little **holy water** before leaving the church."}]

translation: to chug, to gulp down (a drink)
meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis at tuloy-tuloy na pag-inom ng isang likido, karaniwan ay alak o anumang inumin, direkta mula sa bote o malaking lalagyan.
original_explanation: Ito yung ginagawa mo sa malamig na softdrinks after mag-basketball sa ilalim ng araw. O kaya sa inuman session with barkada kapag "tagay" na. It's not sipping delicately; it's a full-on, no-holds-barred chug. The sound is almost part of the word: "tungga-tungga-tungga".
usage_notes: Informal and often associated with drinking alcoholic beverages, but can be used for any drink consumed quickly.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang uhaw, **tumungga** siya ng isang buong bote ng tubig.","translation":"Being so thirsty, he **chugged** a whole bottle of water."},{"sentence":"Bawal **tumungga** ng alak habang nagmamaneho.","translation":"It's forbidden to **chug** alcohol while driving."}]

meaning_filipino: Humiram ng isang bagay para sa kapakanan o gamit ng ibang tao.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'paki-utang' verb. This is when your friend has no more 'mukhang ihaharap' to the lender (or to their suking tindahan), so you step in to borrow on their behalf. You're the middleman in this transaction of trust (and debt). 'Bes, pwede mo ba akong ipanghiram ng 100 pesos kay Aling Nena? Babayaran ko agad sa sahod.'
usage_notes: This is a benefactive verb, meaning the action of borrowing is done for someone else's benefit. It can also have an instrumental meaning ('to use something to borrow'), but the benefactive sense is more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ipinanghiram** ako ni Maria ng aklat sa library dahil naiwan ko ang aking ID.","translation":"Maria **borrowed** a book **for** me from the library because I left my ID."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang basta-basta pumapayag na **ipanghiram** ng pera ang mga kaibigan mo.","translation":"Don't just agree to **borrow** money **for** your friends."}]

translation: sanctifying; that which makes one holy
meaning_filipino: May kakayahang gawing banal o dalisay ang isang tao o bagay; nagdudulot ng kabanalan.
original_explanation: That feeling of purity after you've deep-cleaned your entire house and decluttered your life, Marie Kondo style. Or, more traditionally, what prayer, sacrifice, and good deeds are supposed to do. It's the process of turning a 'marupok' soul into a saintly one.
usage_notes: A word used in religious or highly moral contexts. It describes an action or thing that has a sanctifying effect.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagtulong sa kapwa ay isang gawaing **nakapagpapabanal**.","translation":"Helping others is a **sanctifying** act."},{"sentence":"Naniniwala sila na ang pag-aayuno ay **nakapagpapabanal** ng kaluluwa.","translation":"They believe that fasting **makes the soul holy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pamamaga, karaniwan sa mga mata, dahil sa labis na pag-iyak, kakulangan sa tulog, o alerhiya.
etymology: From "mang-" + "pukto". 'Pukto' itself is an archaic word for swelling.
original_explanation: The official look after a K-drama marathon, a major "iyak" session over a breakup, or pulling an all-nighter for a deadline. Your eyes go from normal to "puffy." When someone asks "Umiyak ka ba?" and you say no, but your eyes are screaming "namumukto ako!"
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used to describe swollen eyes from crying or lack of sleep.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halatang umiyak siya buong gabi dahil **namumukto** ang kanyang mga mata.","translation":"It's obvious she cried all night because her eyes **are swollen**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpuyat nang husto para hindi **mamukto** ang mata mo bukas.","translation":"Don't stay up too late so your eyes won't **get swollen** tomorrow."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang magalang na pakiusap upang makakuha o makahiling ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: The magic word that turns you into a professional food sampler. Ito 'yung linya mo 'pag nakita mong may chichirya 'yung katabi mo: "Pahingi naman!" It's the polite Filipino way of asking for something, which is usually followed by "isa lang" (just one) but never really means just one.
usage_notes: A very common, polite imperative form. Often used with 'po' or 'ho' for politeness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pahingi** po ng isang basong tubig.","translation":"**May I have** a glass of water, please."},{"sentence":"Wow, ang sarap niyan! **Pahingi** ako!","translation":"Wow, that looks delicious! **Give me** some!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang masinsinang paghahanap sa isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pag-aalis o paggalaw sa mga nakaharang na gamit, madalas sa medyo magulong paraan.
original_explanation: This is you trying to find your other sock in the morning. It's the frantic search inside your bag for your beep card when the bus is already there. It's less intense than a police raid ('paghalughog') and more of a personal, desperate search for something you know is *somewhere* in that pile of mess.
usage_notes: Implies a more focused but still messy search compared to 'paghalughog'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa kanyang **paghahalikwat** sa lumang baul, nakita niya ang mga litrato ng kanyang lola.","translation":"In her **rummaging** through the old chest, she found her grandmother's photos."},{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na ang **paghahalikwat** sa bag ko, wala akong tinatagong pagkain.","translation":"Stop **rummaging** through my bag, I'm not hiding any food."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay, tao, o pangyayari na nagiging hadlang o balakid sa isang layunin o daloy ng gawain.
original_explanation: That one friend who keeps asking "malayo pa ba tayo?" on a road trip. Or the slow internet connection during a crucial Zoom meeting. Basically, anything or anyone that gets in your way and makes you want to scream "excuse me, dadaan ang reyna/hari!" A human or situational roadblock.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical objects, people, or abstract concepts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang matinding trapik ay malaking **sagabal** sa mga manggagawa.","translation":"The heavy traffic is a major **obstacle** for workers."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang maging **sagabal** ang takot sa iyong mga pangarap.","translation":"Don't let fear become a **hindrance** to your dreams."}]

translation: to flare up; to blaze; to become inflamed
meaning_filipino: Ang marahas at biglaang paglaki ng apoy; ang matinding pag-aalab ng damdamin.
original_explanation: This is for feelings that are too big for regular words. It's not just 'galit' (angry), it's your anger flaring up like a dragon. It's not just 'in love', it's your passion blazing. It's the fire emoji in verb form. Perfect for describing your feelings when someone cuts you in line or when you see your crush.
usage_notes: Can be used for literal fire or for intense emotions like anger, passion, or love.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Biglang **naglaab** ang tuyong damuhan dahil sa init ng araw.","translation":"The dry grass suddenly **blazed up** because of the sun's heat."},{"sentence":"**Naglaab** ang galit niya nang marinig ang masamang balita.","translation":"His anger **flared up** when he heard the bad news."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang larawan o marka na inililimbag sa isang bagay; isang maliit na piraso ng papel na may disenyo na idinidikit sa mga sulat bilang bayad sa selyo.
original_explanation: This can be the 'selyo' you put on a love letter (if people still send those), or the cool design on your t-shirt. It's the mark you leave, whether it's the official 'LBC' stamp on a package or the potato stamp you made in Grade 1 art class.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa 'postage stamp' (selyo) o sa 'print/design' (limbag/disenyo).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawawala ang **istampa** ng Mahal na Birhen sa kanyang pitaka.","translation":"The **image** of the Blessed Virgin is missing from her wallet."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mo ng dalawang **istampa** para sa sulat na iyan papuntang Amerika.","translation":"You need two **stamps** for that letter to America."}]

translation: to be made to laugh; to laugh involuntarily
meaning_filipino: Hindi sinasadyang tumawa o biglang magpakita ng kagalakan dahil sa isang bagay na nakatutuwa.
original_explanation: When you're trying to be serious in a meeting, but your work bestie sends you a meme and you just can't hold it in. That sudden burst of laughter you try to disguise as a cough. It's an uncontrollable reaction to peak comedy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko napigilan at **napatawa** na lang ako sa kanyang kwento.","translation":"I couldn't help it and I just **laughed** at his story."},{"sentence":"Kahit sino ay **mapapatawa** sa galing ng komedyante.","translation":"Anyone **would be made to laugh** by the comedian's skill."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglalagay ng proteksiyon na patong ng sink sa bakal o asero upang maiwasan ang kalawang.
original_explanation: This is a word you'd probably hear more in a hardware store than in a coffee shop. It's the process that gives our 'yero' (GI sheets) their superpower to resist rust. When you 'maggalbanisa', you're coating metal with zinc. It’s a very specific, industrial-strength verb for making things last longer against the elements.
usage_notes: A technical term used in construction, manufacturing, and hardware.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **maggalbanisa** ng mga tubo para hindi agad kalawangin.","translation":"The pipes need **to be galvanized** so they don't rust quickly."},{"sentence":"Nag-order ang kumpanya ng bakal na ipapa-**maggalbanisa** pa.","translation":"The company ordered steel that still needs **to be galvanized**."}]

translation: to surround; to encircle; to corner
meaning_filipino: Palibutan o kulungin ang isang lugar o tao upang hindi makatakas.
original_explanation: Imagine a SWAT team cornering a suspect, or your group of friends blocking the exit so your other friend can't escape a surprise birthday song. That's 'palikmuin'. 'Pinalikmuan ng mga tsismosa si Aling Nena para alamin ang sikreto niya.' You're basically creating a human wall.
usage_notes: Less common than 'palibutan' or 'kubkubin'. Tends to appear in more formal or literary contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan ng heneral ang kanyang mga kawal na **palikmuin** ang kuta ng mga kalaban.","translation":"The general ordered his soldiers to **surround** the enemy's fortress."},{"sentence":"Nagplanong **palikmuin** ng mga pulis ang hideout ng sindikato.","translation":"The police planned to **encircle** the syndicate's hideout."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng banig na magaspang na yari sa mga dahon ng palmang talak.
etymology: From the 'talak' palm, whose leaves are used to make the mat.
original_explanation: The OG, low-tech sleeping mat. Before memory foam and Tempur-Pedic, there was the 'talakan'. It's a coarse mat that probably smells like dried leaves and the province. Not exactly comfy, but it gets the job done. More likely to be seen in a museum or a lola's baul (storage chest) these days.
usage_notes: This meaning is very rare and mostly archaic or localized. Most Filipinos would only know the 'argument' meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natulog siya sa sahig gamit ang isang lumang **talakan**.","translation":"He slept on the floor using an old **coarse mat**."},{"sentence":"Ang paggawa ng **talakan** ay isang tradisyonal na sining.","translation":"The making of a **talakan mat** is a traditional art."}]

translation: to cause something to become dirty; to be able to defecate
meaning_filipino: Magdulot ng dumi o maging sanhi ng pagiging marumi ng isang bagay; magkaroon ng kakayahang maglabas ng dumi mula sa katawan.
original_explanation: This has two main uses. First, the literal, TMI one: 'yung hirap na hirap ka sa CR, tapos finally, success! "Naka-dumi na ako!" The second one is to make something dirty. For example, 'yung aso mong bagong paligo, tapos nagpagulong-gulong sa putik. "Huwag kang papasok, makarurumi ka ng sahig!" It's the potential to cause dirtiness.
usage_notes: The context usually makes the meaning clear, whether it's about making something unclean or the bodily function. The stress is important: /ma-ka-DU-mi/.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong ipasok ang sapatos mong maputik dahil **makarurumi** iyan sa sahig.","translation":"Don't bring in your muddy shoes because they will **make** the floor **dirty**."},{"sentence":"Uminom siya ng gamot para **makarumi** nang maayos.","translation":"He drank medicine so he could **defecate** properly."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging nasa ilalim ng isang bagay o kapangyarihan; ang pagiging nasasakupan.
original_explanation: This is the feeling of being an "under de saya" husband, or a junior associate in a company where the boss is a micromanager. It's being under someone's thumb, whether it's a person, a system, or a heavy workload. You're not on top, you're at the bottom of the food chain, just trying to survive.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin nang literal (pisikal na nasa ilalim ng isang bagay) o matalinhaga (pagiging mas mababa sa kapangyarihan ng isang tao o bagay).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya nagustuhan ang kanyang **pagkapailalim** sa bagong manager.","translation":"He did not like his **subordination** to the new manager."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkapailalim** ng Pilipinas sa mga dayuhan ay tumagal nang daan-daang taon.","translation":"The **subjugation** of the Philippines to foreigners lasted for hundreds of years."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na umuupa ng isang silid o bahagi ng isang bahay upang tirahan; isang kasama sa bahay na nagbabayad ng upa.
original_explanation: The person who rents a room in your house. Your 'bedspacer'. They pay you rent, use your bathroom, and sometimes 'borrow' your food from the fridge. It's a common setup for students and young professionals who move to the city for school or work.
usage_notes: The feminine form is 'kuwartera'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May bakanteng silid kami para sa isang **kuwartero**.","translation":"We have a vacant room for a **boarder**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga **kuwartero** sa itaas ay mga estudyante.","translation":"The **tenants** upstairs are students."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang propesyonal na may lisensya at karapatang magbigay ng legal na payo at kumatawan sa isang kliyente sa korte.
original_explanation: The person your parents wanted you to be. The one you call when you're in trouble, or when you need to understand the terms and conditions you never read. They're the masters of 'objection!' and 'it depends.' Also known as 'Attorney' or 'Atty.'
usage_notes: The feminine form 'abogada' is also used. It is common to address a lawyer as 'Attorney' or its abbreviation 'Atty.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha sila ng magaling na **abogado** para sa kanilang kaso.","translation":"They hired a good **lawyer** for their case."},{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang maging isang **abogado** balang araw.","translation":"His dream is to become a **lawyer** someday."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng bagay na madaling mabasag o masira.
etymology: From "basag" (break) with the "-in" suffix indicating a quality and the repeated first syllable "ba-" indicating a characteristic.
original_explanation: The official label on your LBC box that you pray the delivery guy actually reads. Also, your heart after seeing your crush's 'in a relationship' status update. Handle with care, bes.
usage_notes: Often used for glass, ceramics, and delicate items. Can also be used metaphorically for a person's feelings or trust.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingatan mo ang kahon na iyan dahil **babasagin** ang laman.","translation":"Be careful with that box because the contents are **fragile**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong paglaruan ang puso niya, hindi mo ba alam na **babasagin** 'yan?","translation":"Don't play with her heart, don't you know it's **fragile**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kapatiran o samahan ng mga Mason, na nakabatay sa mga prinsipyo ng kapatiran, kawanggawa, at paghahanap sa katotohanan.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung pangalan ng "club" ng mga Mason. Isipin mo na lang na ito 'yung "Hogwarts" para sa mga tito na gustong maging better men at tumulong sa community, minus the magic wands and plus more aprons and secret meetings.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa mismong organisasyon o sistema ng Freemasonry.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang naging impluwensya ng **Masoneria** sa Kilusang Propaganda.","translation":"**Freemasonry** had a great influence on the Propaganda Movement."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-aaral sa kasaysayan ng **Masoneria** sa Pilipinas ay napaka-interesante.","translation":"Studying the history of **Freemasonry** in the Philippines is very interesting."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis at malakas na pagkain na halos walang pagnguya; pagkain nang may katakawan.
original_explanation: This isn't just eating. This is unli-wings, samgyupsal, post-breakup-ice-cream-binge level of eating. It's what happens when you're "lamon-tado" (a pun on 'lamentado' or lamenting). It's eating with gusto, passion, and zero table manners. Can also be used metaphorically, like when the "sistema" (system) devours your hopes and dreams.
usage_notes: Has a slightly negative or gluttonous connotation compared to the neutral 'pagkain' (eating).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahan-dahan lang sa **paglamon**, baka mabilaukan ka.","translation":"Go easy on the **gobbling**, you might choke."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng mahabang araw, **paglamon** ng pizza ang gusto niya.","translation":"After a long day, **devouring** pizza is what he wants."}]

translation: to be able to enter; to get into (a place, situation, or trouble)
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang pumasok; makapasok sa isang lugar o kalagayan, na maaaring hindi sinasadya.
original_explanation: This can mean literally getting into a place, like "Sana mapasok ko yung sinehan kahit late na ako." But more often, it's used for getting into a situation, especially trouble. "Ayaw kong mapasok sa gulo." It's like accidentally walking into a meeting you weren't invited to, or getting dragged into office drama.
usage_notes: Can denote ability ('can enter') or accidental entry ('happened to enter'). Context is crucial.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-aral siyang mabuti para **mapasok** sa unibersidad na pangarap niya.","translation":"He studied hard to **be able to enter** his dream university."},{"sentence":"Ingat sa paglalakad, baka **mapasok** ka sa putikan.","translation":"Be careful where you walk, you might **get into** the mud."}]

translation: to scorn, to insult, to belittle
meaning_filipino: Magsabi ng masasamang salita laban sa isang tao na may layuning hamakin, maliitin, o ipahiya siya.
original_explanation: This is what happens in a classic Pinoy telenovela confrontation scene. The rich 'matapobre' character verbally destroys the poor 'bida'. It's weaponizing words to make someone feel worthless. The verbal equivalent of stepping on someone.
usage_notes: A strong word that denotes intense verbal abuse and contempt.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masakit para sa kanya na **mag-alimura** ang sarili niyang kaibigan.","translation":"It was painful for him **to be insulted** by his own friend."},{"sentence":"Hindi tama na **mag-alimura** ng kapwa dahil lang sa kanilang estado sa buhay.","translation":"It is not right **to scorn** others just because of their status in life."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pag-uusap sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang mga tao, lalo na bilang bahagi ng isang dula, aklat, o pelikula.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung script niyo ni crush sa isip mo. It's the back-and-forth conversation, whether it's in a movie, a teleserye, or that 'we need to talk' moment with your partner. The lines that make or break a story.
usage_notes: Maaari ring tumukoy sa isang pormal na talakayan sa pagitan ng dalawang grupo na may magkasalungat na pananaw, tulad ng 'peace dialogue'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahusay ang pagkakasulat ng **dialogo** sa pelikulang iyon.","translation":"The **dialogue** in that movie was well-written."},{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng **dialogo** ang mga manggagawa at ang management.","translation":"The workers and the management had a **dialogue**."}]

translation: to run short of; to be insufficient
meaning_filipino: Ang maranasan ang kakulangan o hindi sapat na dami ng isang bagay, lalo na ang salapi o panustos.
original_explanation: That feeling five days before sweldo. You check your wallet, you check your Gcash, and you realize you're about to be "kapusin" for your milk tea budget. It's the official state of being for "petsa de peligro."
usage_notes: Often used in the context of money, resources, or time. The actor-focus form is "kumapos."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay hindi tayo **kapusin** sa budget para sa proyekto.","translation":"I hope we don't **run short** of budget for the project."},{"sentence":"Nang **kapusin** sila ng bigas, agad silang tinulungan ng kanilang kapitbahay.","translation":"When they **ran short** of rice, their neighbor immediately helped them."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng papel, plastik, o tela na nakakabit sa isang bagay upang magbigay impormasyon tungkol dito, tulad ng pangalan, presyo, o nilalaman.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung nakadikit sa bote ng toyo na nagsasabing 'Brand X' ito, o 'yung price tag sa damit na tinatago mo sa jowa mo. 'Yung 'Made in China' sa likod ng halos lahat ng gamit mo? Etiketa 'yun.
usage_notes: Refers to a physical tag or label on a product. Homonym with 'etiketa' (etiquette).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Basahin mo ang **etiketa** para malaman kung kailan ito mag-e-expire.","translation":"Read the **label** to know when it will expire."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malakas na sigaw o boses, karaniwang nagpapahayag ng matinding damdamin tulad ng galit, tuwa, o takot.
original_explanation: The sound you make when you see a cockroach flying towards you. Or when your favorite band finally comes on stage. Or when you hit the jackpot. It's a raw, loud vocal expression—a shout, a yell, a scream. Not just a sigaw (shout), a hiyaw has more passion and volume.
usage_notes: Often implies a more emotional or primal sound than 'sigaw' (shout).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malakas na **hiyaw** ang narinig mula sa kabilang kwarto.","translation":"A loud **scream** was heard from the other room."},{"sentence":"Napuno ng **hiyaw** ng mga tagahanga ang buong istadyum.","translation":"The whole stadium was filled with the **shouts** of fans."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang relasyon kung saan ang dalawang magkaibigan ay may kasunduang sekswal nang walang romantikong ugnayan. Akronim para sa "friends with benefits."
original_explanation: Stands for "Friends With Benefits." It's the "best of both worlds" situationship where you have a friend you can hang out with and also sleep with, minus the drama of a real relationship. Spoiler alert: someone almost always catches feelings and it gets complicated. It's the plot of 90% of rom-coms for a reason.
usage_notes: Used as an acronym in text and speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayoko na ng **fwb** setup, nakakapagod.","translation":"I don't want an **fwb** setup anymore, it's tiring."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis na pagbaba o pag-agos sa isang pahilis na lugar o ibabaw.
etymology: Mula sa salitang "dalisdis" (dalusdos o slope) at ang gitlaping "-um-".
original_explanation: Imagine water flowing down a slide, or your motivation level sliding down as the work week progresses. It's that smooth, downward movement. Pwede ring luha na dumalisdis sa pisngi mo nung nalaman mong sold out na 'yung concert tickets.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa panitikan upang ilarawan ang paggalaw ng likido o ng isang bagay sa isang dalisdis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dumalisdis** ang mga luha sa kanyang pisngi nang marinig ang malungkot na balita.","translation":"Tears **flowed down** her cheeks when she heard the sad news."},{"sentence":"Ang tubig-ulan ay **dumalisdis** mula sa bubong patungo sa kanal.","translation":"The rainwater **slid down** from the roof to the canal."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kulungan, karaniwang yari sa kawayan, kahoy, o alambre, na partikular na ginagamit para sa mga manok o ibang uri ng ibon.
etymology: Maaaring hiram sa salitang Espanyol na `jaula` (kulungan).
original_explanation: This is NOT the English 'haul' (like a shopping haul). In Tagalog, it's a cage, specifically for chickens. You see this in the palengke or in backyards in the province. It's the chicken's temporary condo before... well, you know. 'Ilagay mo muna 'yung manok sa haul.' It's a very specific, traditional Filipino object.
usage_notes: Pronounced /ha-UL/, not like the English word 'hall'. Primarily used in rural or agricultural contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinuha niya ang manok na pansabong mula sa **haul**.","translation":"He took the fighting cock from the **cage**."},{"sentence":"Gawa sa yantok ang luma nilang **haul**.","translation":"Their old **chicken cage** is made of rattan."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit at pansamantalang tirahan na yari sa magagaang at mga patapong materyales, karaniwang itinayo sa mga pook-iskwater.
etymology: Mula sa pag-uulit ng isang malamang na sinaunang salita na "barong" na nangangahulugang isang simpleng kubo o istraktura.
original_explanation: It’s the OG tiny house, but not the aesthetic, minimalist kind you see on Pinterest. This is the makeshift home built out of whatever you can find—yero, kahoy, tarpaulin. It's a stark symbol of urban poverty, but also of Filipino resilience and the ability to make a home anywhere.
usage_notes: Ang "barongbarong" (walang gitling) ay isang karaniwang variant ng baybay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming pamilya ang nawalan ng tirahan nang masunog ang mga **barung-barong**.","translation":"Many families lost their homes when the **shanties** burned down."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bilang na katumbas ng isandaang libo; 100,000.
original_explanation: This is the salary you want to receive, but the company only gives you minimum wage. 'Sana all sandaanlibo ang sahod.' Also, the price of the latest iPhone that makes you question your life choices.
usage_notes: Ginagamit bilang isang tiyak na bilang (cardinal number).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkakahalaga ng **sandaanlibong** piso ang singsing na iyon.","translation":"That ring costs **one hundred thousand** pesos."},{"sentence":"Mayroong **sandaanlibong** tao na dumalo sa konsiyerto.","translation":"There were **one hundred thousand** people who attended the concert."}]

translation: to persuade earnestly; to convince thoroughly
meaning_filipino: Pilitin o kumbinsihin ang isang tao sa masigasig at puspusang paraan.
original_explanation: This is the level of persuasion needed to get your barkada to go on a spontaneous beach trip even though everyone's broke. It's more than just asking; it's presenting a PowerPoint, showing a budget spreadsheet, and appealing to their FOMO. It’s sales talk on steroids.
usage_notes: Implies a greater degree of effort and earnestness than the simpler 'hikayatin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **pakahikayatin** ang komite na aprubahan ang kanyang proyekto.","translation":"He tried to **persuade earnestly** the committee to approve his project."},{"sentence":"**Pakahikayatin** mo si Ana na sumama sa atin.","translation":"Try your best to **convince** Ana to come with us."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang panghimagas mula sa Korea na gawa sa pinong yelo (shaved ice) na may iba't ibang sahog tulad ng prutas, matamis na gatas, at red bean paste.
original_explanation: Yung sosyal na version ng halo-halo na in-adopt natin from our K-drama overlords. Perfect pang-Instagram at pang-palamig sa ulo mo after makipag-away sa Grab driver. It's the dessert you eat when you want to feel fancy but also just want a mountain of ice and sugar.
usage_notes: A very popular food item, especially in urban areas with many cafes and Korean restaurants.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tara, mag-**bingsu** tayo mamaya pagkatapos ng klase.","translation":"Let's go eat **bingsu** later after class."},{"sentence":"Ang paborito kong flavor ng **bingsu** ay yung mango cheese.","translation":"My favorite flavor of **bingsu** is mango cheese."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita ng matinding galit o poot, kadalasan sa paraang marahas o nakakatakot.
original_explanation: This isn't just being 'pikon' or 'inis'. This is full-on, tables-flipping, 'Darna!' shouting level of anger. It's the rage you feel when the internet goes out during a ranked game, or when someone spoils the finale of your favorite K-drama. It's an epic, cinematic kind of fury.
usage_notes: Stronger than 'magalit' (to be angry). 'Magngalit' implies a more intense, possibly destructive rage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tila isang bulkan na sasabog, nagsimulang **magngalit** ang ama sa nalamang kataksilan.","translation":"Like a volcano about to erupt, the father began to **rage** upon learning of the betrayal."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hintaying **magngalit** ang iyong ina dahil sa kalat mo.","translation":"Don't wait for your mother to **be furious** because of your mess."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahan o katangian ng pagiging malikhain; ang abilidad na bumuo o gumawa ng mga bago at orihinal na bagay.
original_explanation: This is the Pinoy 'diskarte' superpower. It's turning a lata of sardines into a gourmet meal, making a parol out of recycled bottles, or writing a viral TikTok script. It's the ability to make something amazing out of, well, almost nothing. The spirit of every artist, content creator, and lola who can fix anything with a rubber band.
usage_notes: Isang mataas na pinahahalagahang katangian sa sining, inobasyon, at kahit sa pang-araw-araw na paglutas ng problema.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinamalas ng mga estudyante ang kanilang **pagkamapanlikha** sa ginanap na art exhibit.","translation":"The students showcased their **creativity** at the art exhibit."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng laruang hinihipan na gawa sa karton o plastik na lumilikha ng malakas na tunog, karaniwang ginagamit sa mga pagdiriwang tulad ng Bagong Taon.
etymology: Onomatopoeic, imitating the sound it makes.
original_explanation: The official noisemaker of every Filipino New Year's Eve party. It's that colorful paper or plastic horn you blow until you're out of breath to scare away bad spirits (and annoy your neighbors). The sound of Dec 31, 11:59 PM.
usage_notes: Also spelled as 'turutot'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng maraming **torotot** para sa Bagong Taon.","translation":"Mom bought a lot of **party horns** for New Year's."},{"sentence":"Ang ingay ng mga **torotot** ay nakakabingi!","translation":"The noise from the **party horns** is deafening!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar na mayroong maraming puno at halaman; makahoy o masukal.
original_explanation: That part of the province where the phone signal disappears and the only network available is the 'chismis network' from the local titas. It's where you go for hiking, soul-searching, or to get lost if you're not careful. Think of a horror movie setting, but also a beautiful nature reserve.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan sa isang lugar, hindi sa isang tao o bagay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magubat** ang daan papunta sa liblib na talon.","translation":"The path to the remote waterfall is **forested**."},{"sentence":"Dati raw ay isang **magubat** na lugar ang kinatatayuan ng mall na ito.","translation":"They say the place where this mall stands used to be a **woody** area."}]

translation: to harden; to be stubborn; to stand firm
meaning_filipino: Gawing matigas ang isang bagay; o manindigan nang matatag sa isang desisyon o paniniwala, na kung minsan ay nagiging katumbas ng katigasan ng ulo.
original_explanation: This has two meanings. The literal one is for cement: **magpatigas** ng semento. The more common, 'hugot' one is when you refuse to give in during an argument with your jowa. You **nagpapatigas**, even if you know you're a little bit wrong. It's the 'pride' move, standing your ground like a rock, for better or for worse.
usage_notes: Can be literal (physical hardening) or figurative (emotional or psychological hardening/stubbornness).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magpatigas** ng ulo at makinig ka sa payo ng iyong mga magulang.","translation":"Don't **be stubborn** and listen to your parents' advice."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magpatigas** ng loob para malampasan ang mga pagsubok.","translation":"We need to **toughen** ourselves up (literally: harden our inner self) to overcome the challenges."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay na idinaragdag sa pagkain o inumin upang magbigay ng lasang matamis; maaari ring tumukoy sa panghimagas.
original_explanation: Your reward after eating all your veggies. It's the 'something sweet' you crave after a meal, whether it's a fancy cake or just a piece of Choc-Nut. Also, the general term for anything you add to make your coffee less bitter, just like how a compliment from your crush can sweeten a bad day.
usage_notes: Can refer both to a sweetener (like sugar or honey) and a dessert. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagyan mo ng **patamis** ang kape para hindi masyadong mapait.","translation":"Add some **sweetener** to the coffee so it's not too bitter."},{"sentence":"Ano ang **patamis** natin mamayang gabi?","translation":"What's our **dessert** for tonight?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng bahagyang pagngiti kung saan ang mga labi ay kumukurba nang kaunti, na nagpapahiwatig ng kagalakan, pag-aliw, o pagkilala.
original_explanation: This is not your full-blown, teeth-showing grin. It's that subtle, pa-cute smile you give your crush when you pass by them. Yung 'di halata pero kinikilig. A Mona Lisa smile, Pinoy version.
usage_notes: Describes a subtle, often involuntary smile, which is different from the more deliberate 'pagngiti'. It's considered a more poetic or literary term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya napigilan ang **paggiti** nang mabasa ang text mula sa kanya.","translation":"She couldn't stop **smiling slightly** when she read the text from him."},{"sentence":"May isang munting **paggiti** sa kanyang mga labi habang natutulog.","translation":"There was a small **smile** on her lips as she slept."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na nangangahulugang handa, payag, o sang-ayon na sumama o gumawa ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino 'yes'. When your friend asks, 'Kain tayo sa labas?' and you reply with a firm 'Game!', it means you are 100% down for it. It's the verbal equivalent of a thumbs-up emoji and the battle cry for any spontaneous food trip, road trip, or questionable life choice.
usage_notes: Used as an enthusiastic affirmative response to an invitation or suggestion. Often abbreviated to just 'G'. As in, 'Tara? G!'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tara, mag-videoke! **Game** ka ba?","translation":"Let's go sing karaoke! Are you **game**?"},{"sentence":"Mag-beach tayo sa Sabado. **Game**!","translation":"Let's go to the beach on Saturday. **I'm in**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Lugar na kinalalagyan; tungkulin o posisyon sa trabaho; maliit na tindahan o espasyo sa palengke.
original_explanation: Your 'puwesto' could be your cubicle at your BPO job, your tita's vegetable stall in the palengke, or your designated spot on the couch. It's your place, your station, your small kingdom. 'Paki-bantay muna ng puwesto ko,' is the national anthem of market vendors taking a bathroom break.
usage_notes: A very versatile word that can mean a physical spot, a job position, or a market stall.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May bakanteng **puwesto** para sa manager sa aming kumpanya.","translation":"There is an open **position** for a manager in our company."},{"sentence":"Ang **puwesto** ni Aling Nena sa palengke ay nasa bandang gitna.","translation":"Aling Nena's **stall** in the market is near the middle."},{"sentence":"Humanap ka ng magandang **puwesto** para makita natin ang entablado.","translation":"Find a good **spot** so we can see the stage."}]

translation: Act of making something bear fruit; bringing about results.
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o paraan upang ang isang halaman o puno ay mamunga; o ang pagkakaroon ng magandang resulta o kinalabasan mula sa isang pagsisikap.
original_explanation: Literally, making your mango tree finally give you mangoes. Figuratively, it’s when all your 'pagod' and 'puyat' finally pay off. Your side hustle starts making money, your thesis gets approved, your hard work gets you that promotion. It’s the 'reap what you sow' moment.
usage_notes: Can be literal (agriculture) or figurative (efforts leading to success).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tamang pataba ay mahalaga sa **pagpapabunga** ng mga halaman.","translation":"The right fertilizer is important in **making plants bear fruit**."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapabunga** ng kanyang mga sakripisyo ay ang tagumpay ng kanyang mga anak.","translation":"The **fruition** of his sacrifices is the success of his children."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malakas at tuloy-tuloy na pag-iyak o pag-ingay, katulad ng sa isang pusa o sanggol na gutom o nasasaktan.
etymology: From `pag-` (gerund prefix) + `ngawa` (to meow loudly, to wail).
original_explanation: This is that next-level iyak. Not just a simple whimper, but a full-on, 'buong barangay makakarinig' kind of wail. Think of a cat in heat at 3 AM or a baby who just discovered the power of their lungs. It's the sound of pure, unadulterated demand or drama.
usage_notes: Often associated with the sound cats make, but can be used hyperbolically for a person's loud crying or complaining.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko matiis ang **pagngangawa** ng pusa sa bubong tuwing hatinggabi.","translation":"I can't stand the **wailing** of the cat on the roof every midnight."},{"sentence":"Itigil mo na 'yang **pagngangawa** mo, hindi ka na bata.","translation":"Stop your **wailing**, you're not a child anymore."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng parehong bigat, halaga, o sukat.
etymology: From magka- (denoting similarity or relationship) + timbang (weight).
original_explanation: This is the goal for your work-life balance. Or when you and your jowa split the bill 50/50. It's about being equal. Sa palengke, this is what you want the scale to show. "Ate, paki-check nga kung magkatimbang." It can also be used for abstract things, like "magkatimbang na pagmamahal" (equal love).
usage_notes: Can be used for literal weight or figurative balance and equality.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat **magkatimbang** ang trabaho at personal na buhay.","translation":"Work and personal life should be **balanced**."},{"sentence":"Siguraduhin mong **magkatimbang** ang bigas at asukal na bibilhin mo.","translation":"Make sure the rice and sugar you will buy are **of equal weight**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang distrito o rehiyong eklesiastikal na nasa ilalim ng hurisdiksyon ng isang obispo.
original_explanation: Basically, a bishop's area of responsibility. Think of it like a barangay, but for the Catholic Church, and the kapitan is a bishop. "Sino ang obispo sa diosesis ng Cubao?"
usage_notes: A specific term used primarily within the context of the Catholic Church. The standard Filipino spelling is 'diyosesis'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aming parokya ay bahagi ng **diosesis** ng Malolos.","translation":"Our parish is part of the **diocese** of Malolos."},{"sentence":"Nagpulong ang mga pari mula sa iba't ibang **diosesis**.","translation":"The priests from different **dioceses** held a meeting."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong nagtatrabaho sa isang tanggapan, otel, o gusali, na ang pangunahing tungkulin ay batiin at tulungan ang mga bisita, sagutin ang telepono, at mag-iskedyul ng mga appointment.
etymology: Hiram na salita mula sa Ingles na "receptionist".
original_explanation: The first friendly (or sometimes, intimidating) face you see when you walk into an office for a job interview or a condo to visit a friend. They are the gatekeepers of the lobby, the masters of the logbook, and the voice on the other end of the line that says, "For whom is the call?" Be nice to them; they probably know where the good office chismis is.
usage_notes: Malawakang ginagamit sa Taglish, lalo na sa mga propesyonal at urban na setting. Ang pormal na katumbas ay "tagatanggap ng panauhin" ngunit bihirang gamitin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiiwan na lang po ng package sa **receptionist** sa lobby.","translation":"Please just leave the package with the **receptionist** in the lobby."},{"sentence":"Magalang na nagtanong ang **receptionist** kung may appointment ako.","translation":"The **receptionist** politely asked if I had an appointment."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagliligtas o tumutubos sa iba mula sa kasalanan, pagkakaalipin, o kapahamakan.
original_explanation: The OG 'sana all' provider. In religious contexts, this is the ultimate hero who pays for everyone's debt (kasalanan). In modern terms, it's that one friend who pays for your Grab ride when your Gcash is empty, or the one who covers your shift when you're 'sick.' Sila ang tagapagligtas ng budget at ng attendance record mo.
usage_notes: Primarily used in a religious or highly formal context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinikilala ng mga Kristiyano si Hesus bilang kanilang **Manunubos**.","translation":"Christians recognize Jesus as their **Redeemer**."},{"sentence":"Ang bayani ay itinuring na **manunubos** ng bayan mula sa paniniil.","translation":"The hero was considered the **savior** of the nation from oppression."}]

translation: To present; to lay out; to state.
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalatag, pagpapakita, o pagsasabi ng isang bagay sa paraang malinaw at organisado, tulad ng isang plano, ideya, o damdamin.
original_explanation: It's the 'Okay, let's talk' moment. When your boss asks you to **ilahad** the project plan, you're not just showing it, you're presenting it step-by-step. Parang sa teleserye, when the main character finally decides to **ilahad** their true feelings. It's about revealing something in an open, organized way.
usage_notes: Can refer to presenting physical objects (like goods on a mat) or abstract concepts (like a plan or feelings).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ilahad** mo ang iyong mga ebidensya sa korte.","translation":"**Present** your evidence in court."},{"sentence":"Mangyaring **ilahad** ang iyong saloobin nang mahinahon.","translation":"Please **state** your opinion calmly."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bukal ng tubig na natural na umaagos mula sa ilalim ng lupa; balon.
original_explanation: Before NAWASA and Maynilad, this was your source of fresh water. It's the OG water dispenser of the province. In literature, it’s the place where the 'dalaga' is washing clothes when the 'binata' first sees her. A classic meet-cute spot in rural Philippines.
usage_notes: This meaning is less common in modern urban speech. The pronunciation with stress on the first syllable is key to distinguishing it from the adverb 'talagá'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha sila ng malinis na tubig mula sa **talaga**.","translation":"They got clean water from the **spring**."},{"sentence":"May isang matandang puno sa tabi ng **talaga** sa aming baryo.","translation":"There is an old tree beside the **well** in our village."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa dalawa o higit pang bagay, tao, o konsepto na may parehong antas ng kahalagahan o presyo.
original_explanation: This is the "hugot" entry. Yung feeling na sana all magkasinghalaga sa'yo ang trabaho at ang jowa mo. Or when you realize your 1,000-peso bill and two 500-peso bills can buy the same amount of milk tea. It's about equal worth, whether it's in pesos or in feelings.
usage_notes: Can refer to monetary value or abstract importance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para sa akin, **magkasinghalaga** ang pamilya at ang mga kaibigan.","translation":"For me, family and friends are **of the same importance**."},{"sentence":"Ang ginto at ang platino ay hindi **magkasinghalaga** sa merkado.","translation":"Gold and platinum are not **of the same value** in the market."}]

translation: To suffer, to experience, to befall
meaning_filipino: Ang pagdanas o pagtanggap ng isang kalagayan, karaniwan ay isang paghihirap, kamalasan, o kapahamakan.
original_explanation: This is a dramatic word. It’s what happens *to* you, usually something bad. It's not just 'to experience,' it's 'to end up with' or 'to be met with' a certain fate. 'Ano kaya ang sasapitan ng bida sa finale?' (What fate will the protagonist suffer in the finale?). It’s the punchline of karma, the result of your actions (or someone else's).
usage_notes: Often has a negative connotation, implying a consequence or fate that one arrives at. The past tense 'sinapit' is very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay hindi masamang kapalaran ang **sapitan** ng ating mga bayani.","translation":"I hope a bad fate does not **befall** our heroes."},{"sentence":"Anuman ang iyong **sapitan**, mananatili akong nasa iyong tabi.","translation":"Whatever you may **suffer/experience**, I will remain by your side."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halaman (Sesamum indicum) na may maliliit at nakakain na buto na pinagkukunan din ng langis.
original_explanation: That tiny seed that gets stuck in your teeth after eating buchi. It's the magic ingredient in sesame oil that makes your siomai dip level up, and the crunchy topping on palitaw. Small but terrible... in flavor!
usage_notes: The seeds are called 'buto ng linga'. The English word 'sesame' is also widely understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap ang kare-kare kapag may giniling na **linga**.","translation":"Kare-kare is delicious when it has ground **sesame**."},{"sentence":"Nilagyan niya ng buto ng **linga** ang ibabaw ng tinapay.","translation":"She put **sesame** seeds on top of the bread."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging malusog, matipuno, at masigla sa paglaki o pag-unlad, partikular sa mga halaman o kabataan.
original_explanation: The glow-up of a person, plant, or even a business. It's that "Wow, ang laki ng pinagbago mo!" energy. For people, it means they look healthy and well-built. For plants, it means they're thriving, not dying a slow, sad death on your condo balcony.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin para sa tao, hayop, o halaman upang ilarawan ang masiglang pag-unlad.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kitang-kita ang **bulas** ng kanyang katawan dahil sa pag-eehersisyo.","translation":"The **robustness** of his body is very evident because of exercising."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang yunit ng masa sa sistemang metriko, katumbas ng ika-1000 na bahagi ng isang kilogramo.
original_explanation: Ito yung madalas mong marinig sa palengke o grocery. 'Ate, isang daang **gramo** po ng giniling.' Hindi mo sasabihing 'one hundred grams', 'di ba? Mas Pinoy pakinggan. Parang mas magaan din ang 100 **gramo** sa bulsa kaysa 1 kilo.
usage_notes: Mas karaniwang ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na usapan sa Pilipinas kaysa sa katumbas nitong Ingles na 'gram'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magdagdag ka ng limampung **gramo** ng keso sa spaghetti.","translation":"Add fifty **grams** of cheese to the spaghetti."},{"sentence":"Tumitimbang lamang ng ilang **gramo** ang bagong silang na sisiw.","translation":"The newborn chick weighs only a few **grams**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na tagabantay o namamahala sa isang karsel o bilangguan.
original_explanation: The person holding the keys to the 'kulungan'. Basically, the bouncer of the city jail. You see them in movies, usually looking stern while walking down a long, dim hallway.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **karselero** ang nagbigay ng pagkain sa mga bilanggo.","translation":"The **jailer** gave food to the prisoners."},{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang bilin ng **karselero** na bawal ang anumang uri ng gulo.","translation":"The **jailer** gave strict orders that any kind of trouble was forbidden."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na nangyari nang walang anumang babala, hudyat, o pag-aakala; hindi inaasahan.
original_explanation: Yung biglaang quiz ng prof mo on a Monday morning. Yung 13th-month pay na pumasok nang maaga. Yung ex mong biglang nag-chat ng 'kamusta?'. It's the universe throwing a plot twist at your life's teleserye.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang mga pangyayari, bisita, o kinalabasan. Ang 'biglaan' ay isang malapit na kasingkahulugan. Ang pariralang 'di asahan' ay isang di-pormal na baryasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **di-inaasahang** bisita ang dumating kagabi.","translation":"An **unexpected** visitor arrived last night."},{"sentence":"Ang panalo niya sa lotto ay isang **di-inaasahang** biyaya.","translation":"His lottery win was an **unexpected** blessing."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging banat, mahigpit, o maigting.
original_explanation: Yung feeling kapag mag-e-exam ka na pero 'di ka nag-review. O 'yung moment na nag-uusap 'yung parents mo sa kabilang kwarto at alam mong may kasalanan ka. 'Yan ang agting. The kind of tension you can cut with a knife, or maybe just a very stressed side-eye.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa pisikal na tensyon (tulad ng sa isang lubid) o emosyonal/sosyal na tensyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nararamdaman ko ang **agting** sa pagitan ng dalawang magkaaway.","translation":"I can feel the **tension** between the two enemies."},{"sentence":"Sinuri ng gitarista ang **agting** ng bawat kuwerdas.","translation":"The guitarist checked the **tautness** of each string."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sikat na pandaigdigang fast-food chain na kilala sa mga hamburger, french fries, at manok; kolokyal na tawag para sa McDonald's.
etymology: Colloquial shortening of the brand name "McDonald's".
original_explanation: The go-to place for Chicken McDo with rice, the cure for hangovers (large fries and coke float combo!), and the emergency meeting place for barkadas. It's where you first learned the meaning of 'extra rice, please' and where 'pa-deliver tayo' becomes a solution to adulting problems.
usage_notes: A very common colloquial term used by virtually everyone in the Philippines to refer to the McDonald's fast-food chain.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gutom na ako, daan muna tayo sa **McDo**.","translation":"I'm hungry, let's drop by **McDonald's** first."}]

translation: to burn (something); to set on fire
meaning_filipino: Ang sinasadyang pag-aapoy o pagtupok sa isang bagay gamit ang apoy.
original_explanation: The verb for when you're done with something. "I-burn the ships!" "Burn the evidence!" "Sunugin ang mga lumang love letters ng ex mo!" It's the act of intentionally setting something ablaze, whether it's trash (basura), a field for farming (kaingin), or your 'kilay' because you got too close to the gas stove.
usage_notes: This is the object-focus form. The actor-focus form is "sumunog".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **sunugin** ang lahat ng lumang litrato nila.","translation":"She decided to **burn** all of their old photos."},{"sentence":"Ipinagbabawal na **sunugin** ang mga basura sa bakuran.","translation":"It is forbidden to **burn** trash in the yard."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ponemang kinakatawan ng isang titik sa alpabeto na hindi patinig. Ito ay ang mga tunog na nalilikha sa pamamagitan ng bahagya o kumpletong pagharang sa daloy ng hangin sa bibig.
etymology: Mula sa 'ka-' (kasama) + 'tinig' (tunog). Literal na 'kasamang-tunog' ng patinig.
original_explanation: Ito yung mga letra sa alphabet na hindi A, E, I, O, U. Sila yung B-squad, C-team, D-group, atbp. na kailangan ng isang patinig para makabuo ng solidong tunog, parang sa love team, kailangan mo ng ka-partner para may 'spark'.
usage_notes: Ang kabaligtaran ng 'patinig' (vowel).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang letrang 'B' ay isang **katinig**.","translation":"The letter 'B' is a **consonant**."},{"sentence":"Mahirap bigkasin ang mga salitang puro **katinig** at walang patinig.","translation":"It's hard to pronounce words that are all **consonants** and have no vowels."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpunta sa isang lugar upang samahan o kunin ang isang tao; o ang taong nagsasagawa nito.
original_explanation: This is the Filipino version of Uber, but it's your dad, jowa, or friend. 'Sino sundo mo?' (Who's picking you up?) is a standard question after a night out. A 'sundo' is a love language. If someone offers to be your sundo, especially in Manila traffic, they're a keeper. It can also refer to the person doing the picking up ('Nasaan na ang sundo ko?').
usage_notes: Often used with verbs like 'may' (may sundo - has someone picking them up) or 'nasaan ang' (where is the). The verb form is 'sunduin' (to fetch someone).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ma, darating na po ba ang **sundo** ko?","translation":"Mom, is the person **picking me up** coming soon?"},{"sentence":"Hintayin mo ako, may **sundo** ako mamayang alas-singko.","translation":"Wait for me, I have a **pick-up** later at five o'clock."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasunduan o pagkikita ng dalawang tao, lalo na ng magkasintahan, sa isang tiyak na lugar at oras, na kadalasa'y lihim.
original_explanation: The old-school term for a romantic 'meet-up' or 'date', but with more drama and secrecy. Think Maria Clara and Ibarra planning to see each other by the river, away from prying eyes. Today, it’s like telling your crush "See you at the milk tea shop at 3 PM," but whispering it so your clingy friends don't hear.
usage_notes: Has a formal and somewhat archaic or literary feel.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ilalim ng puno ng mangga ang lugar ng kanilang **pagtitipan**.","translation":"The spot under the mango tree is the place of their **rendezvous**."},{"sentence":"Lihim ang naging **pagtitipan** ng dalawang magsing-irog.","translation":"The two lovers had a secret **tryst**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang panghalip paari na nagmula sa Espanyol, katumbas ng "aking" o "ko".
original_explanation: This is the conyo/old-school Spanish-influenced way of saying "my". You'd hear this in phrases like "Mi amor" (my love) or from your lola saying "Mi Hija" (my daughter). It's a bit formal, a bit romantic, and a bit vintage. Not for everyday use unless you're feeling extra charming or quoting a telenovela.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa mga pariralang hiram sa Espanyol na naging bahagi na ng wikang Filipino, tulad ng "mi amore" o "casa mi". Hindi ito malayang ginagamit bilang kapalit ng "ko" o "aking".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"\"O, **mi** amore,\" ang sabi niya sa kanyang kasintahan.","translation":"\"Oh, **my** love,\" he said to his girlfriend."},{"sentence":"Ang tawag sa kanya ng lola niya ay \"**mi** unica hija.\"","translation":"Her grandmother calls her \"**my** only daughter.\""}]

meaning_filipino: Isang talaan ng mga pangalan, bagay, o gawain na nakaayos nang sunud-sunod.
original_explanation: Your 'utang' (debt) list at the sari-sari store. Your grocery list that you always forget at home. The list of your ex's red flags that you only saw in hindsight. Basically, any enumeration of things, from a to-do list for your BPO shift to a kill list in an action movie.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisulat ang pangalan mo sa **listahan**.","translation":"Please write your name on the **list**."},{"sentence":"May mahabang **listahan** ng mga bibilhin si nanay para sa Noche Buena.","translation":"Mom has a long **list** of things to buy for Christmas Eve dinner."}]

meaning_filipino: (Kolokyal) Isang estado ng pag-iisip kung saan ang isang tao ay labis na naghihinala, natatakot, o nag-aalala nang walang sapat na batayan.
etymology: Pinaniniwalaang nanggaling sa salitang Ingles na "paranoid".
original_explanation: That feeling you get when your boss says "Can we talk?" in a Slack message. Or when you hear a noise at 3 AM and you're convinced it's a multo and not the cat. Praning is the national mood after sending a risky text and seeing "..." for too long. It's your brain's overacting, teleserye-level drama queen mode.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pang-uri (e.g., "praning ako") o pangngalan (e.g., "para kang praning").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **praning**, walang multo dito.","translation":"Don't be **paranoid**, there are no ghosts here."},{"sentence":"Nagiging **praning** ako kapag hindi siya nagre-reply agad.","translation":"I get **paranoid** when he/she doesn't reply immediately."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang damdamin ng inggit o pagnanasa sa tagumpay, katangian, o pag-aari ng iba.
original_explanation: That feeling you get when you see your friend's travel photos on Instagram while you're stuck in traffic on EDSA. It's the 'sana all' moment that turns a little bit bitter. The root of many kontrabida origin stories.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'inggit', but 'paghihili' can sometimes imply a more intense, consuming jealousy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paghihili** ay maaaring sumira sa isang magandang pagkakaibigan.","translation":"**Envy** can destroy a good friendship."},{"sentence":"Walang maidudulot na mabuti ang **paghihili** sa kapwa.","translation":"**Jealousy** towards others will bring no good."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang tao na may tamang pag-iisip, mabuting pag-uugali, at nasa wastong katinuan.
original_explanation: This is your parents' ultimate relationship goal for you: 'Maghanap ka ng matino!' It means someone who's got their life together, isn't a 'red flag,' and won't give you a headache. Can also mean 'sane' or 'sober,' as in, 'Wala nang matino sa inuman kagabi.'
usage_notes: A very common adjective used to describe a person's character, state of mind, or the quality of a conversation/idea.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong magkaroon ng isang **matino** at seryosong kausap.","translation":"I want to have a **sensible** and serious conversation partner."},{"sentence":"Sa wakas, nakahanap din siya ng **matinong** trabaho.","translation":"Finally, he/she found a **decent** job."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na may pambihirang ganda, kaningningan, at kadakilaan; maningning at kahanga-hanga.
original_explanation: If 'marikit' is exquisite beauty, 'marilag' is magnificent beauty. It’s grand, splendid, and majestic. It’s the kind of beauty that inspires national anthems (the line 'may dilag ang tula' in Lupang Hinirang comes from the same root). Marilag is beauty that commands respect, like a perfect Mayon Volcano view or a queen in her full regalia.
usage_notes: Highly formal and poetic, similar to 'marikit' but often implying a grander or more majestic scale of beauty.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **marilag** na pagtatanghal ang ipinamalas ng mga mananayaw.","translation":"The dancers put on a **magnificent** performance."},{"sentence":"Ang **marilag** na Bulkang Mayon ay isang pambansang yaman.","translation":"The **splendid** Mayon Volcano is a national treasure."}]

meaning_filipino: Makamit ang tagumpay o panalo; magwagi laban sa isang pagsubok, kalaban, o hamon.
original_explanation: This is the goal of every student during finals week, every BPO agent trying to hit their quota, and every person swiping right on a dating app. It's the "Sana all!" moment when you see someone else's success. To magtagumpay is to win at life, or at least, win this particular round. It's the opposite of "na-seen zone."
usage_notes: A formal and powerful word for success. 'Manalo' (to win) is more common for games and competitions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsikap siya nang husto upang **magtagumpay** sa buhay.","translation":"He worked very hard in order to **succeed** in life."},{"sentence":"Dasal ko na **magtagumpay** ka sa iyong mga pangarap.","translation":"I pray that you will **succeed** in your dreams."}]

translation: will make someone believe; to convince
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkilos upang makumbinsi o mahikayat ang isang tao na tanggapin ang isang bagay bilang totoo sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: This is the verb for when you're trying to explain to your mom why you came home at 3 AM ("May group project po kami, super important"). It's the art of convincing someone, whether you're telling the truth, a white lie, or a full-blown "chismis". It's the core skill of politicians and marketing agents.
usage_notes: Future tense of the causative verb "magpaniwala".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Anong kwento ang sasabihin mo na **magpapapaniwala** sa kanila?","translation":"What story will you tell that **will make them believe**?"},{"sentence":"Kahit anong gawin mo, hindi ka na **magpapapaniwala** sa akin.","translation":"Whatever you do, you **will no longer convince** me."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis at malakas na pag-inom ng likido, karaniwang direkta mula sa sisidlan at sa maraming dami.
original_explanation: This is how you drink when you're super uhaw after playing basketball, or when it's 'tagay' time with your barkada. Paglaklak isn't sipping; it's chugging. It's the sound of you downing a whole bottle of water in one go. Not to be confused with a dainty sip from a teacup. This is the 'walang bukas' style of drinking.
usage_notes: Colloquial and often used to describe drinking large amounts of liquid, especially water or alcoholic beverages, quickly and with gusto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa matinding uhaw, isang **paglaklak** lang ay naubos niya ang isang bote ng tubig.","translation":"Due to extreme thirst, he finished a bottle of water in just one **gulping** session."},{"sentence":"Pinagsabihan siya ng doktor na iwasan ang **paglaklak** ng alak.","translation":"The doctor advised him to avoid **chugging** alcohol."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kondisyon kung saan ang mga mata ay hindi magkahanay at tumitingin sa magkaibang direksyon.
original_explanation: When your eyes are playing multiplayer but are on different servers. It's sometimes used jokingly when someone's trying to look at two things at once, like their phone and the person they're talking to. "Saan ka ba nakatingin, sa kausap mo o sa chismis sa kabilang table?"
usage_notes: Can be considered offensive if used to mock a person's medical condition (strabismus). Often used interchangeably with 'duling'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong pagtawanan ang batang **sulipat**.","translation":"Don't laugh at the **cross-eyed** child."},{"sentence":"Nagkunwari siyang **sulipat** para magpatawa.","translation":"He pretended to be **cross-eyed** to be funny."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang lugar na maliwanag, maluwag, at walang sagabal; o sa isang pakiramdam na magaan at walang bumabagabag.
original_explanation: The opposite of your cramped condo unit. It's that feeling of a wide open space, lots of natural light, and good ventilation. Think of a beach on a clear day, a minimalist cafe, or even a clear, uncluttered mind. If your life is 'maaliwalas', you're probably stress-free and have your finances in order. We can only dream.
usage_notes: Can describe a physical space, the weather (clear sky), or a person's mood or facial expression.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko ng bahay na **maaliwalas** at maraming bintana.","translation":"I want a house that is **spacious and bright** with many windows."},{"sentence":"Naging **maaliwalas** ang kanyang mukha nang makita ang mga anak.","translation":"Her face became **serene** when she saw her children."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kasama o katrabaho sa propesyon ng pagtuturo.
original_explanation: Your work-BFF, but specifically for teachers. The one you share lesson plans, tsismis in the faculty room, and eye-rolls with when the principal announces another last-minute meeting. 'Ma'am, pahiram po ng chalk, naubusan ako.'
usage_notes: The prefix 'ka-' is used to denote a companion or someone in the same group.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Gng. Reyes ay aking **kaguro** sa asignaturang Filipino.","translation":"Mrs. Reyes is my **fellow teacher** in the Filipino subject."},{"sentence":"Nagpulong ang mga **kaguro** upang planuhin ang darating na school festival.","translation":"The **fellow teachers** met to plan the upcoming school festival."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpapalit ng kasuotan o pag-aayos ng sarili sa pamamagitan ng pananamit. Ito ay nasa aspektong panghinaharap.
etymology: From `mag-` (verb prefix) + `bi-` (future tense repetition of the first syllable of the root) + `bihis` (dress, attire).
original_explanation: Future tense of getting your drip right. It's that moment before a date, a party, or even just a Zoom call where you transform from your 'pambahay' self to your 'present-to-the-world' self. 'Wait lang, magbibihis lang ako!' is the national anthem of people who are chronically 5 minutes late.
usage_notes: Can mean both 'will change clothes' and 'is changing clothes' depending on context, as the contemplative aspect in Tagalog can cover both future and progressive tenses.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magbibihis** muna ako bago tayo umalis.","translation":"I **will change my clothes** first before we leave."},{"sentence":"Teka, **magbibihis** lang siya para sa party.","translation":"Wait, he/she **is just getting dressed** for the party."}]

meaning_filipino: Paglalarawan sa isang tao na likas na masayahin, palangiti, at madaling maging maligaya.
original_explanation: This is your friend who is 'happy lang, walang ending'. They're the human equivalent of a golden retriever. Kahit gaano kabigat ang problema, they find a reason to laugh. They're the one who starts the karaoke, tells the corny jokes, and brings the good vibes. The designated 'bibo' of the barkada.
usage_notes: Describes a person's disposition or personality. 'Masayahin' is a more common variant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sayahin** siyang tao kaya marami siyang kaibigan.","translation":"She is a **cheerful** person that's why she has many friends."},{"sentence":"Kilala ang mga Pilipino sa pagiging **sayahin** sa kabila ng mga problema.","translation":"Filipinos are known for being **jolly** despite the problems."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglunok ng anumang likido, tulad ng tubig, gatas, o gamot. Ito ay nasa anyong pangnagdaan.
original_explanation: What you did with your coffee this morning, your water after jogging, or that suspiciously strong "juice" at the party last night. It's the past tense of 'to drink'. "Ininom ko lahat ng bubble tea, wala nang natira."
usage_notes: The most common past-tense form for 'to drink'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ininom** mo ba ang gamot na inireseta ng doktor?","translation":"Did you **drink** the medicine prescribed by the doctor?"},{"sentence":"Bigla siyang nahilo matapos **ininom** ang alak.","translation":"He suddenly felt dizzy after he **drank** the liquor."}]

translation: to cut off for someone; to trip someone
meaning_filipino: Putulin ang isang bagay tulad ng tali para sa isang tao, o sinadyang ipatid ang paa ng iba upang matumba.
original_explanation: This is a bit old-school. It's like when you're flying a kite (saranggola) and someone asks you to cut the string for them, you "patdan" it. Or, more mischievously, when you stick your foot out to make your friend fall over during a game of habulan, that's also "patdan". The original prank.
usage_notes: Can mean both cutting a string/rope for someone or deliberately tripping someone. Context is key to differentiate between the two meanings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Patdan** mo nga ako ng sinulid para sa saranggola ko.","translation":"Please **cut** a piece of string for my kite."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **patdan** ang kapatid mo habang tumatakbo!","translation":"Don't **trip** your sibling while they're running!"}]

translation: to make an excuse, to give a reason
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng katuwiran o paliwanag, na maaaring totoo o hindi, upang ipaliwanag ang isang kilos o pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is the national sport when you're late for work ("Grabe ang traffic, Ma'am/Sir!"), when you forgot to do a chore ("Biglang sumakit ulo ko eh."), or when you don't want to go to a reunion ("May prior commitment na kasi ako, sorry!"). It's the art of creative storytelling to get out of trouble.
usage_notes: Can have a neutral meaning (to give a reason) but often carries a negative connotation (to make an excuse).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang **magdahilan**, aminin mo na lang na nakalimutan mo.","translation":"Don't **make excuses** anymore, just admit you forgot."},{"sentence":"Kailangan niyang **magdahilan** sa kanyang amo kung bakit siya nahuli sa trabaho.","translation":"He needed to **give a reason** to his boss for why he was late for work."}]

translation: To tell on someone; to gossip about
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uulat o paghahatid ng impormasyon, karaniwan ay negatibo, tungkol sa isang tao sa iba. Ang pagiging paksa ng usap-usapan.
etymology: From 'sabi' (to say) with reduplication and the '-an' suffix, indicating the recipient or topic of the action.
original_explanation: The verb form of being a Marites. When your officemate is late, and you 'casually' mention it to the boss, you're doing the 'pagsasabi'. When you become the topic of everyone's chismis, you're the one being 'pinagsasabi-sabihan'. It's the act of turning a person into a 'sabi-sabi'.
usage_notes: Can mean 'to tell on' (magsabi) or 'to be the subject of gossip' (pag-sabi-sabihan). The form 'sabi-sabihan' is often used in the passive voice, as in 'pag-sabi-sabihan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang lumabas dahil **pinagsasabi-sabihan** siya ng mga kapitbahay.","translation":"She doesn't want to go out because the neighbors are **gossiping about** her."},{"sentence":"Itigil mo na ang **pagsasabi-sabi** ng mga bagay na hindi totoo.","translation":"Stop **gossiping about** things that are not true."}]

translation: prolific; fecund (tending to have many children)
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao o hayop na madalas o maraming magkaanak.
original_explanation: That one tita in every clan who has a dozen kids and somehow still looks amazing. Also, rabbits. Rabbits are very **palaanakin**. It's the opposite of a fur-parent.
usage_notes: The prefix 'pala-' indicates a fondness for or a tendency towards the root word. In this case, 'anak' (child).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala ang pamilya nila sa pagiging **palaanakin**.","translation":"Their family is known for being **prolific**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga kuneho ay itinuturing na **palaanakin** na hayop.","translation":"Rabbits are considered to be **fecund** animals."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manunulat na regular na nag-aambag ng isang artikulo o kolum sa isang pahayagan, magasin, o website.
original_explanation: Sila yung mga professional na Marites sa dyaryo o online news. May sarili silang space para isulat ang opinyon nila sa lahat ng bagay, from politics to showbiz chismis. Parang OG vlogger, pero in writing.
usage_notes: Often refers to opinion writers in print or digital media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala ang **kolumnist** na iyon sa kanyang matapang na mga pananaw sa pulitika.","translation":"That **columnist** is known for his bold political views."},{"sentence":"Binabasa ko ang kolum niya tuwing Linggo; magaling na **kolumnist** si G. Reyes.","translation":"I read his column every Sunday; Mr. Reyes is a great **columnist**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng puno (Annona reticulata) o ang bunga nito na may matamis at mamasang laman. Ito ay kahawig ng atis at guyabano.
original_explanation: Yung prutas na kamag-anak ng atis at guyabano. Siya yung pinsan na medyo low-key pero masarap din. Hindi kasing sikat, pero 'pag natikman mo, mapapa- "Uy, not bad!" ka.
usage_notes: Bagaman ang 'guyabano' (soursop) at 'atis' (sugar apple) ay mas karaniwan, ang 'anunas' (custard apple) ay kabilang sa parehong pamilya (Annona). Sa ilang rehiyon, maaaring magkapalitan ang paggamit ng mga terminong ito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap gawing ice cream ang hinog na **anunas**.","translation":"Ripe **custard apple** is delicious when made into ice cream."},{"sentence":"Namitas kami ng **anunas** sa likod-bahay ni lola.","translation":"We picked **custard apples** at grandma's backyard."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pakiramdam ng pagkabigo na nagmumula sa pagkatuklas na ang isang bagay o tao ay hindi kasing-husay tulad ng unang pinaniniwalaan.
original_explanation: That feeling when you finally get your dream job, only to realize it's full of toxic bosses and endless OT. Or when you meet your hero and find out they're a jerk. It's the "akala ko" moment that shatters your "sana all" dreams. Reality check, level: expert. Hugot material 'to, bes.
usage_notes: Isang salitang tumutukoy sa isang malalim na pagkadismaya o pagkabigo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **disilusyon** sa politika ay nagsimula nang makita niya ang talamak na katiwalian.","translation":"His **disillusionment** with politics began when he saw the widespread corruption."},{"sentence":"Nagdulot ng matinding **disilusyon** sa kanya ang pagtataksil ng kanyang kaibigan.","translation":"His friend's betrayal caused him great **disillusionment**."}]

translation: the state of being Catholic; catholicity
