original_explanation: 'Yung kaibigan mong single na nag-comment ng 'Sana all' sa lahat ng wedding post sa Facebook. 'Yung tipong handa nang mag-download ng lahat ng dating apps. Pero in a serious note, it's that feeling of hopelessness, like waiting for your Shopee delivery on the last possible day. The male version is 'disesperado'.
usage_notes: Feminine form. The masculine form is 'disesperado'. Can be used as both an adjective ('She is desperate') and a noun ('She is a desperate person').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Disesperada** na siyang makahanap ng trabaho kaya tinanggap niya kahit mababa ang sahod.","translation":"She was **desperate** to find a job so she accepted it even with a low salary."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **disesperada**; darating din ang tamang tao para sa iyo.","translation":"Don't be **desperate**; the right person for you will come eventually."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalakbay o paggala sa iba't ibang lugar nang walang tiyak na patutunguhan.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'travel without a plan.' Before 'wanderlust' became a thing on Instagram, our ancestors were already doing the *langlang*. It's like walking around the mall aimlessly just looking at stuff, or when your Grab driver takes a 'shortcut' and you end up seeing parts of the city you've never seen before.
usage_notes: Often implies a sense of aimlessness or exploration. The verb form is often 'maglanglang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **maglanglang** sa mga lansangan ng Maynila tuwing gabi.","translation":"He likes **to roam** the streets of Manila at night."},{"sentence":"Nag-**langlang** ang magkakaibigan sa buong probinsya sakay ng kanilang motor.","translation":"The friends **wandered** throughout the province on their motorcycle."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng napakaliit na kulisap na kahawig ng lamok at kilala sa makating kagat, karaniwang matatagpuan malapit sa tubig o dalampasigan.
original_explanation: The *kalukati* is that tiny, almost invisible ninja insect that attacks you during your beach trip at dusk. You don't see it, you don't hear it, but the next day you have 20 itchy red spots that make you question all your life choices. They're the uninvited guests at every provincial outing.
usage_notes: More commonly known as 'niknik' in many regions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng kagat ng **kalukati** ang kanyang mga binti pagkatapos mamasyal sa dalampasigan.","translation":"His legs were full of **gnat** bites after strolling on the beach."},{"sentence":"Naglagay sila ng kulambo upang hindi mapasok ng **kalukati**.","translation":"They put up a mosquito net so the **midges** could not enter."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng lutuing Italyano na gawa sa pasta, itlog, keso, at bacon o guanciale. Sa Pilipinas, madalas itong may kasamang cream at kabute.
original_explanation: The "white spaghetti" that's always present at Pinoy parties, right next to the red spaghetti. The Filipino version is super creamy, often with mushrooms and ham, and is the ultimate comfort food. It's the opposite of the "authentic" Italian one, but who cares? Masarap eh.
usage_notes: Ang bersyon ng carbonara sa Pilipinas ay naiiba sa orihinal na Italyano, dahil karaniwang gumagamit ito ng all-purpose cream.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-crave ako ng **carbonara** kaya nagluto si nanay.","translation":"I was craving **carbonara**, so my mom cooked some."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkakaroon ng utang o pananagutan sa pananalapi sa isang tao o institusyon.
etymology: From pagka- (manner/state of) + ka- (state of) + utang (debt).
original_explanation: The official status of your wallet every 'petsa de peligro'. It's that awkward feeling when you see the friend you owe money to at the mall. It's the reason why you suddenly become a minimalist and say "hindi ko kailangan niyan" when your friends want to eat out. Your credit card bill is the monthly report of your 'pagkakautang'.
usage_notes: Often used in a financial context, but can also be used for "utang na loob" (debt of gratitude).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa malaking **pagkakautang**, kinailangan niyang isanla ang kanilang bahay.","translation":"Because of his huge **indebtedness**, he had to mortgage their house."},{"sentence":"Paano mo babayaran ang iyong **pagkakautang** sa bangko?","translation":"How will you pay your **debt** to the bank?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-abot sa isang lugar o destinasyon; ang pagwawakas ng isang paglalakbay. Ito ay nasa panahong pangnagdaan.
original_explanation: The OG 'arrival' word. This is your everyday, all-purpose verb for when something or someone gets to a place. Your visitor? 'Dumating'. Your online order? 'Dumating'. The bill from Meralco? 'Dumating' din. It's the past tense, the completed action. The waiting is over, for better or for worse. 'Finally, the package I ordered last 11.11 has arrived!'
usage_notes: This is the completed or past tense form. For ongoing arrival, use 'dumarating'. For future arrival, use 'darating'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahapon pa **dumating** ang mga bisita mula sa probinsya.","translation":"The guests from the province **arrived** yesterday."},{"sentence":"**Dumating** ka sa puntong pagod ka na sa lahat.","translation":"You **came** to a point where you're tired of everything."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapahid o pagkalat ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay malagkit o basa, sa isang ibabaw na nag-iiwan ng marka o dumi.
original_explanation: Imagine a kid eating champorado without a spoon. 'Yung kalat ng chocolate sa mukha niya? That's hilahid. Or your makeup after crying while watching a K-drama. The smudge is real.
usage_notes: Can also be a verb: ihilahid (to smear), maghilahid (to smear something on oneself).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **hilahid** ng putik ang kanyang mga binti pagkatapos maglaro sa ulan.","translation":"His legs were full of **smears** of mud after playing in the rain."},{"sentence":"Ayusin mo ang **hilahid** ng lipstick mo sa iyong pisngi.","translation":"Fix the lipstick **smudge** on your cheek."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng hindi mapakali o hindi mapalagay sa pagtulog, na kadalasang nagreresulta sa paggagalaw o pagbaling-baling.
original_explanation: This is you at 3 AM, staring at the ceiling, replaying that awkward thing you said in 2012. Pagkabilasa is when your body wants to sleep but your brain, fueled by coffee and anxiety about your bills, decides to host a marathon of your greatest mistakes. You toss, you turn, you check your phone for the 50th time.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to restlessness during sleep or when trying to sleep. Not to be confused with 'bilasa' meaning stale fish.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa sobrang pag-aalala, puro **pagkabilasa** ang naranasan niya buong gabi.","translation":"Due to extreme worry, he experienced nothing but **restlessness** the whole night."}]

translation: will become slow; will slow down
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging marahan o hindi mabilis sa pagkilos, pag-unlad, o pagganap. Ito ay nasa aspektong panghinaharap ng pandiwang 'bumagal'.
etymology: Pag-uulit ng unang pantig ng salitang-ugat na "bagal" (ba-) at idinugtong sa buong salitang-ugat (bagal) upang mabuo ang aspektong panghinaharap.
original_explanation: The future tense of "bumagal" (to slow down). This is what happens to your internet connection right when you're about to win a game or in the middle of a crucial Zoom call ("Huwag sanang **babagal** ang internet!"). It's also what happens to traffic when someone rubbernecks at a minor accident on the highway.
usage_notes: Stress is on the second syllable: ba-BÁ-gal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kapag napagod ka, siguradong **babagal** ang iyong takbo.","translation":"When you get tired, your running **will surely slow down**."},{"sentence":"Tila **babagal** ang usad ng pila dahil may problema sa sistema.","translation":"It seems the line **will slow down** because there's a problem with the system."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mag-aaral na kinikilala para sa kanyang natatanging tagumpay sa akademya at pagkamit ng matataas na marka.
original_explanation: The one whose parents actually have something to post on Facebook after Recognition Day. The 'bibo kid' who always sits in front, asks all the questions, and probably has a laminating machine at home for their certificates. The reason you hear 'Bakit si [insert honor student's name] kaya niya?' from your parents.
usage_notes: The phrase is adopted directly from English and is the standard term used in the Philippine education system. Often seen as 'with honors'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isa siyang **honor student** mula elementarya hanggang kolehiyo.","translation":"She has been an **honor student** from elementary to college."},{"sentence":"Ipinagmamalaki ng kanyang mga magulang na isa siyang **honor student**.","translation":"Her parents are proud that she is an **honor student**."}]

translation: to be able to make sure; to ensure
meaning_filipino: Ang magkaroon ng katiyakan o kumpirmasyon tungkol sa isang bagay; ang alisin ang anumang pag-aalinlangan.
original_explanation: The classic 'double-check' verb. It's what you do before you leave the house ('Did I lock the door?'), before you send a risky text, or before you finalize a GCash payment. 'Tawagan mo siya para makasiguro kang darating siya.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tingnan mo ulit ang iyong mga sagot para **makasiguro** kang tama lahat.","translation":"Check your answers again **to ensure** they are all correct."},{"sentence":"Paano ako **makakasiguro** na ligtas ang aking pera sa bangko?","translation":"How can I **be sure** that my money is safe in the bank?"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pagkain, lalo na ang tinapay, na hindi na sariwa, tumigas na, o nagsisimula nang masira dahil sa katagalan.
original_explanation: This is what happens to the pandesal you bought three days ago and forgot to eat. It's hard, dry, and just sad. The opposite of "bagong luto." It's that loaf of bread that's one step away from becoming a science experiment.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit para sa tinapay at iba pang produktong panaderya. Iba sa "panis" na para sa kanin at ulam.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Panis** na ang kanin, pero **panig** pa lang ang tinapay.","translation":"The rice is already **spoiled**, but the bread is just **stale**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang kainin 'yan, **panig** na.","translation":"Don't eat that anymore, it's **stale**."}]

translation: to celebrate a golden wedding anniversary
meaning_filipino: Ang pagdiriwang ng ikalimampung anibersaryo ng kasal ng isang mag-asawa.
original_explanation: The ultimate #RelationshipGoals. It's when lolo and lola have been married for 50 years and the whole clan throws a party that's bigger than most weddings. Proof that 'sana all' can come true.
usage_notes: A very specific term used only for the 50th wedding anniversary. The silver anniversary (25th) is 'boda de plata'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa susunod na taon ay **magbo-boda-de-oro** na ang aking mga lolo at lola.","translation":"Next year, my grandparents will **celebrate their golden wedding anniversary**."},{"sentence":"Isang malaking salu-salo ang inihanda para sa mag-asawang **nagboda-de-oro**.","translation":"A big feast was prepared for the couple who **celebrated their golden wedding anniversary**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang daglat sa internet na nangangahulugang "Want to Buy" o "Nais Bumili," na ginagamit sa mga online forum, laro, at social media upang ipahayag ang intensyong bumili ng isang partikular na aytem.
etymology: Daglat mula sa pariralang Ingles na "Want To Buy".
original_explanation: Acronym ng mga naghahanap ng rare item sa online games, specific na piyesa ng PC, o limited edition na sapatos. "Guys, wtb PS5, budget meal price lang po, willing to add my undying loyalty." Makikita mo 'to sa mga Facebook group at Discord server.
usage_notes: Halos eksklusibong ginagamit sa mga online na platform ng kalakalan at komunidad.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Post sa FB group: \"**WTB** secondhand na iPhone 12, 'yung good as new sana.\"","translation":"Post on an FB group: \"**Want to buy** a secondhand iPhone 12, hopefully one that's good as new.\""},{"sentence":"Sa chat ng laro: \"**WTB** Legendary Sword of Valor, name your price!\"","translation":"In the game chat: \"**Want to buy** the Legendary Sword of Valor, name your price!\""}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghahanap o pagsunod sa mga bakas o palatandaan upang matagpuan ang isang tao, bagay, o pinagmulan ng isang pangyayari.
original_explanation: The act of going full FBI-mode on someone's social media. You're not just stalking, you're *researching*. You're connecting the dots, following the trail of tagged photos, old comments, and shared posts to get the full story. 'Saan kaya galing 'tong chismis? Let's trace it back.'
usage_notes: Anyong pandiwa ng 'tagunton'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **taguntunin** ang pinagmulan ng pekeng balita.","translation":"It is difficult **to trace** the origin of fake news."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **taguntunin** ang kanyang mga ninuno sa Espanya.","translation":"He tried **to track down** his ancestors in Spain."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang uod na yugto ng isang paruparo o gamugamo, na karaniwang may mabalahibong katawan na maaaring magdulot ng pangangati sa balat kapag nadikit.
original_explanation: The OG itchy frenemy of your childhood garden. You see this fuzzy little guy crawling on a leaf and your skin already starts to feel tingly. Touching one is a rite of passage that teaches you the valuable life lesson: "Not all cute, fluffy things are for cuddling."
usage_notes: Specifically refers to the hairy, often itchy kind of caterpillar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa puno ng mangga, maraming **higad** diyan.","translation":"Be careful near the mango tree, there are many **caterpillars** there."},{"sentence":"Nangati ang braso ko dahil nadikitan ako ng **higad**.","translation":"My arm got itchy because a **caterpillar** touched it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nag-aalok ng serbisyong sekswal kapalit ng kabayaran o pera.
etymology: The root 'tutot' is obscure and not commonly used on its own, but is believed to be related to the act of selling or offering oneself.
original_explanation: This is a harsh, often derogatory old-school term for a sex worker. It's the kind of word you'd hear in a classic Filipino drama movie, usually delivered with a lot of angst. Nowadays, more respectful or neutral terms are preferred.
usage_notes: This is a strong and often offensive term. 'Sex worker' is the more neutral term in English. In Filipino, euphemisms like 'babaeng-aliw' or 'kalapating mababa ang lipad' are sometimes used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang karakter na ginampanan niya sa pelikula ay isang **patutot** na may ginintuang puso.","translation":"The character she played in the movie was a **prostitute** with a heart of gold."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging tulala, karaniwang may bahagyang bukas na bibig, at walang kamalayan sa paligid.
original_explanation: That moment when your crush finally talks to you and you just... freeze. Hindi ka makasagot, nakatingin ka lang sa kawalan. That's you, 'nakatanga'. Parang nag-buffer 'yung utak mo. It's the default face when you see your Meralco bill.
usage_notes: Describes a state of being stunned or absent-minded, not necessarily indicating a lack of intelligence, but rather being caught off-guard or lost in thought.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bakit ka **nakatanga** diyan? May multo ka bang nakita?","translation":"Why are you **staring blankly** over there? Did you see a ghost?"},{"sentence":"Naiwan siyang **nakatanga** matapos marinig ang balita.","translation":"He was left **dumbfounded** after hearing the news."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng lutuing Italyano na gawa sa mga patong-patong na lapad na pasta, sarsa, keso, at kung minsan ay karne.
original_explanation: That cheesy, meaty, saucy pasta bake that makes you forget your diet. It's the go-to potluck dish for titas and the ultimate comfort food after a rough week. You know, the one from that famous fast-food chain with the bee? Peak handaan food.
usage_notes: Used directly as a loanword. Spelling and pronunciation are adapted from English/Italian.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-order ako ng isang buong tray ng **lasagna** para sa party.","translation":"I ordered a whole tray of **lasagna** for the party."},{"sentence":"Paborito niya ang **lasagna** na may maraming keso.","translation":"Her favorite is **lasagna** with lots of cheese."}]

translation: to make someone get tired of something
meaning_filipino: Maging sanhi ng pagkasawa o pagkaumay ng isang tao sa isang bagay, karaniwan dahil sa labis na pagkakalantad o pagkonsumo nito.
original_explanation: This is what happens when your mom cooks adobo for a week straight. She will **papagsawain** you until you never want to see adobo again (for a few days, at least). It's also that song on the radio that's played every 5 minutes until you hate it. The goal is to reach the 'umay' factor.
usage_notes: The root 'sawa' (fed up) is stressed on the last syllable /sa-WA/. This is different from 'sawa' /SA-wa/ (snake, python).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong araw-arawin ang pagkain ng prito, baka **papagsawain** mo ang mga anak mo.","translation":"Don't serve fried food every day, you might **make your children get tired of it**."},{"sentence":"**Pinagsawa** na niya ako sa paulit-ulit niyang mga pangako.","translation":"He **made me get tired** of his repetitive promises."}]

translation: uselessness; state of being useless or inept
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging walang silbi, walang kakayahan, o hindi epektibo sa isang gawain o layunin.
etymology: From 'pagka-' (state of being) + 'inutil' (useless), which is from Spanish 'inútil'.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're in a group project and you have no idea what's going on, so you just offer to buy snacks. It's the state of being a "pabigat" or feeling like you're not contributing anything useful. The opposite of "diskarte".
usage_notes: A strong word describing a state of complete ineffectiveness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang **pagkainutil** nang hindi niya matulungan ang kaibigang may problema.","translation":"He felt a sense of **uselessness** when he couldn't help his friend in need."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkainutil** ng sistema ang dahilan ng pagbagal ng progreso.","translation":"The **ineptness** of the system is the reason for the slow progress."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa anumang bagay, wika, o kultura na nagmula o may kaugnayan sa bansang Sweden (Suwesya).
original_explanation: The adjective for things from the land of IKEA, ABBA, and Spotify. Describes a design that's probably minimalist, functional, and comes with a tiny Allen key. 'That's a very Swedish meatball.'
usage_notes: Isinusulat sa maliit na titik (lowercase) kapag ginagamit bilang pang-uri para sa mga bagay o konsepto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang disenyo ng muwebles na iyon ay estilong **suweko**.","translation":"The design of that furniture is of the **Swedish** style."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bilang na kasunod ng tatlumpu't siyam at sinusundan ng apatnapu't isa; katumbas ng apat na sampu (40).
original_explanation: The big 4-0. The age when your Titos and Titas start complaining about their back pain and say 'in my time...'. It's also the number of days in Lent (Kuwaresma). From the Spanish 'cuarenta'. We also say 'apatnapu'.
usage_notes: Used interchangeably with the native Tagalog term 'apatnapu'. Spanish-derived numbers are often preferred for counting money, telling time, and stating age.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magdiriwang na siya ng kanyang ika-**kuwarenta** na kaarawan sa susunod na buwan.","translation":"She will be celebrating her **fortieth** birthday next month."},{"sentence":"**Kuwarenta** pesos po ang isang kilo ng kamatis.","translation":"**Forty** pesos is the price for one kilo of tomatoes."}]

translation: to decant; to transfer a liquid
meaning_filipino: Ang maingat na paglilipat ng likido mula sa isang sisidlan patungo sa isa pa, karaniwan upang ihiwalay ito sa mga latak o namuong bagay.
original_explanation: This is what your tita does with the expensive wine, or what you do when you transfer the last drops of suka from the big bottle to a smaller one for the dining table. It's the art of pouring something carefully so you don't get the 'tira-tira' or 'latak' at the bottom. Think of it as liquid decluttering.
usage_notes: Commonly used in the context of liquids like vinegar, soy sauce, wine, or oil.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magsalong** ng mantika sa mas maliit na bote.","translation":"You need to **transfer** the oil into a smaller bottle."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa literal na kahulugan, tumutukoy sa isang tao na kuba o may baluktot na likod. Sa makasagisag na kahulugan, ito ay nangangahulugang masama, buhong, o tiwali.
original_explanation: Originally means hunchbacked, like Quasimodo. But in modern Pinoy teleseryes, it's the go-to adjective for a kontrabida. A 'buktot na tao' is someone with a twisted soul, 'yung palihim na nagnanakaw ng Tupperware sa office pantry or 'yung nang-iiwan sa ere sa group project. It's evil with a capital E.
usage_notes: The metaphorical meaning (wicked/corrupt) is more common in modern usage, especially in media and literature. The literal meaning (hunchbacked) is often replaced by the more common word 'kuba'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **buktot** na opisyal ay nagnakaw mula sa kaban ng bayan.","translation":"The **corrupt** official stole from the nation's treasury."},{"sentence":"Inilalarawan siya bilang isang taong may **buktot** na hangarin.","translation":"He is described as a person with **wicked** intentions."}]

meaning_filipino: Biglaang paghila o pag-agaw sa isang bagay nang may puwersa.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'haltak' (isang biglaang paghila) at ang gitlaping '-um-'.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na may biglang humaltak ng bag mo sa daan. O kaya 'yung eksenang hinahaltak ka ng nanay mo palayo sa toy store kasi wala na kayong pera. It's a sudden, forceful pull, often with a hint of violence or desperation.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang isang marahas o biglaang kilos ng pagkuha.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **humaltak** sa kanyang kuwintas habang siya ay naglalakad sa Divisoria.","translation":"Someone **snatched** her necklace while she was walking in Divisoria."},{"sentence":"**Humaltak** ng isang pirasong damit ang bata mula sa sampayan.","translation":"The child **pulled** a piece of clothing from the clothesline."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalapat ng diin sa isang bagay gamit ang mga daliri; gawin ang aksyon ng pagpisil.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "pisil" at hulaping "-in".
original_explanation: The command form of 'pisil'. Ito yung sinasabi mo sa sarili mo kapag nakakita ka ng bubble wrap: "Pisilin mo 'yan!" It's also what you do to the last bit of toothpaste in the tube or the calamansi for your pancit. A fundamental life skill for maximizing resources.
usage_notes: This is the object-focused verb form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pisilin** nang masyadong mahigpit ang kamatis at baka madurog.","translation":"Don't **squeeze** the tomato too hard or it might get crushed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpunta kasama ng isang tao o grupo; pagiging bahagi ng isang gawain o samahan.
original_explanation: Ito yung 'Sama ako!' moment mo kapag narinig mong may lakad ang barkada. It's the fear of missing out (FOMO) in verb-form-turned-noun. From joining a friend to the canteen, to joining a protest, it's all about not being left behind.
usage_notes: Derived from 'sama' meaning 'to go with' or 'to join'. Pronunciation stress is on the last syllable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagsama** niya sa amin sa Bicol ay nagbigay ng ibayong saya.","translation":"Her **joining** us in Bicol brought extra joy."},{"sentence":"Salamat sa iyong **pagsama** sa aking kaarawan.","translation":"Thank you for **accompanying** me on my birthday."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong may lisensya at kwalipikadong magbigay ng legal na payo at kumatawan sa iba sa usaping pambatas; isang abogado.
original_explanation: "Atorni" is how Pinoys say "attorney." They're the people you call when you get into trouble, or when you need a contract checked so you don't get scammed. They're masters of "palusot" (excuses), but the legal kind. Having an "atorni" in the family is a source of pride, and they're often the designated person to argue with the waiter when there's a mistake in the bill. The more formal term is 'abogado'.
usage_notes: A very common loanword. It is used interchangeably with 'abogado', which is from Spanish. 'Attorney' or 'Atty.' is also used as a title before a lawyer's name.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating kumonsulta sa isang **atorni** tungkol sa kasong ito.","translation":"We need to consult an **attorney** regarding this case."},{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang maging isang tanyag na **atorni** balang araw.","translation":"She dreams of becoming a famous **lawyer** someday."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng isang matining na tunog sa pamamagitan ng pagbuga ng hangin mula sa mga labing bahagyang nakaawang o gamit ang isang silbato.
original_explanation: What the traffic enforcer does when you're blocking the pedestrian lane. What you do to call your dog (or sometimes, a cute person walking by). It's making that sound with your lips or an actual whistle. Tandaan: Huwag kang 'pumito' sa gabi, baka may sumunod na hindi mo kilala, sabi ng matatanda.
usage_notes: The root 'pito' can mean 'whistle' or the number 'seven'. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pumito** ang pulis upang patigilin ang mga sasakyan.","translation":"The police officer **whistled** to stop the vehicles."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **pumito** habang naglalakad.","translation":"He likes **to whistle** while walking."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng isang likido, lalo na ang tubig, kapag umabot sa temperatura kung saan ito ay nagiging singaw at bumubuo ng mga bula.
original_explanation: That moment your instant noodles are almost ready. It's the bubbles and steam that signal something is cooking. Figuratively, it’s also your temper reaching its peak. 'Kumukulo na ang dugo ko' is the classic 'I'm about to lose it' line, usually heard before a mom unleashes the ultimate sermon.
usage_notes: Often used in the verb form 'kumukulo' (boiling). The idiom 'kumukulo ang dugo' (blood is boiling) is a common expression for intense anger.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hintayin mong umabot sa **kulo** ang tubig bago ilagay ang kape.","translation":"Wait for the water to reach a **boil** before adding the coffee."},{"sentence":"Nararamdaman kong malapit nang umabot sa **kulo** ang galit niya.","translation":"I can feel his anger is about to reach its **boiling point**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao, karaniwan ay bata, na magulo, malikot, at mahirap sawayin o disiplinahin.
original_explanation: This is your pamangkin who treats your living room like a WWE ring. They're the 'pasaway' kid who runs around during mass, or the one who draws on the walls with crayons. It's chaotic energy in human form, but often in a playful, not malicious, way. Lovable but requires a lot of patience and a first-aid kit.
usage_notes: Often used to describe children, but can also apply to playful adults, pets, or any boisterous group.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang batang iyon ay sadyang **haragan**, laging nagtatakbuhan sa loob ng bahay.","translation":"That child is really **rowdy**, always running inside the house."},{"sentence":"Sawayin mo nga ang mga alaga mong aso, masyadong **haragan**!","translation":"Please control your pet dogs, they're too **unruly**!"}]

translation: to be born into; to find upon waking
meaning_filipino: Ang madatnan o maranasan ang isang kalagayan o pangyayari sa pagmulat, pagdating, o pagsilang.
original_explanation: That feeling when you wake up and find out na may pasok pala kahit holiday (because your boss declared it a working holiday). It can also be more profound, like "Ito na ang mundong magisnan ko" – the world you were born into, with all its traffic and political drama.
usage_notes: This is a more literary or formal verb form. It has two main senses: 1) literally finding something upon waking up, and 2) figuratively being born into a certain situation or reality. The '-an' suffix makes the root word the location or circumstance of the action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang hirap ng buhay ang kanyang **magisnan**.","translation":"The hardship of life was the reality he was **born into**."},{"sentence":"Pagmulat niya, isang masaganang almusal ang kanyang **magisnan** sa mesa.","translation":"When he opened his eyes, a bountiful breakfast was what he **found** on the table."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat ng tatlo o higit pang mga nota ng musika na sabay-sabay na tinutugtog.
original_explanation: This is what you try to learn on the guitar to serenade your crush. You start with G-C-D, and suddenly you can play half of the Eraserheads' discography. It's the building block of 'harana' and the reason your fingers hurt when you first start playing.
usage_notes: Used in musical contexts. The English word 'chord' (spelled 'kord') is also very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinuturuan niya ako ng mga pangunahing **akorde** sa gitara.","translation":"He is teaching me the basic **chords** on the guitar."},{"sentence":"Mahirap isagawa ang **akorde** na F major para sa mga baguhan.","translation":"The F major **chord** is difficult to perform for beginners."}]

meaning_filipino: Malapatan o malagyan ng saliw, karaniwan ay akompanyamentong musikal o tunog.
original_explanation: When your dramatic life moment gets its own background music. Crying over a breakup? Suddenly a sad song plays on the radio. That's your moment being 'masaliwan'. It's turning a regular scene into a movie scene by adding a soundtrack.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in the context of music, sound, or performance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tula ay mas magiging madamdamin kung ito ay **masasaliwan** ng malamyos na tunog ng biyolin.","translation":"The poem will be more emotional if it can **be accompanied by** the gentle sound of a violin."},{"sentence":"Hiniling ng mang-aawit na **masaliwan** ng piano ang kanyang pag-awit.","translation":"The singer requested for her singing to **be accompanied** by a piano."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang pagpapakita ng kayamanan, kakayahan, o anumang pag-aari sa paraang mapagmataas o upang hangaan ng iba.
original_explanation: The art of 'flexing.' When someone posts their new iPhone, their Starbucks drink, their plane ticket, and their new shoes all in one IG story, they are trying to magparangya. It's the act of showing off, sometimes subtly (humble bragging), sometimes not-so-subtly. 'Pabili po, hindi po magpaparangya.'
usage_notes: Carries a slightly negative connotation of ostentatious display.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **magparangya** ng kanyang mga bagong gamit sa social media.","translation":"She loves to **flaunt** her new things on social media."},{"sentence":"Kahit mayaman na sila, hindi sila kailanman natutong **magparangya**.","translation":"Even though they are rich, they never learned to **show off**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maikling panahon ng pagtigil sa isang gawain, karaniwan ay para magpahinga, kumain, o maglibang.
original_explanation: That 15-minute window your boss gives you to escape your BPO duties. Pwedeng coffee break, yosi break, or mental breakdown break. It's the pause button on adulting. Also, what happens to couples who are "not on the same page anymore." #Hiwalayan
usage_notes: Commonly used in Taglish in work, school, and relationship contexts. Often spelled phonetically as 'breyk'. The verb form is usually 'mag-break'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tara, mag-**break** muna tayo, pagod na ako.","translation":"Let's take a **break**, I'm tired."},{"sentence":"Mahirap mag-move on pagkatapos ng **break**-up ninyo.","translation":"It's hard to move on after your **break**-up."}]

meaning_filipino: Kasuotang espesyal na idinisenyo para isuot sa pagtulog.
etymology: From 'bata' (a colloquial term for clothes, possibly from Spanish 'bata' meaning robe/dressing gown) and 'pantulog' (for sleeping).
original_explanation: Literally "clothes for sleeping." These are your PJs, your duster, your oversized t-shirt from a fun run you never joined, or your comfy shorts with a garter that's given up on life. Your "pambahay" can level up to "batang pantulog" status once it's too worn out for public viewing but too comfy to throw away.
usage_notes: While 'bata' can mean child, in this context it refers to a robe or gown. The more common term is 'pajama' or 'pantulog'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatanggap siya ng bagong **batang pantulog** bilang regalo.","translation":"She received new **pajamas** as a gift."},{"sentence":"Masarap matulog kapag malambot ang iyong **batang pantulog**.","translation":"It's nice to sleep when your **sleepwear** is soft."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang serbisyo, karaniwan ay sa transportasyon tulad ng taxi, na mayroong nakatakdang singil o bayad batay sa taripa o metro.
etymology: Combination of 'de' (Spanish for 'of' or 'with') and 'taripa' (from Spanish 'tarifa', meaning 'tariff' or 'rate').
original_explanation: The opposite of 'kontrata' or 'dagdag' when riding a taxi. This is what you pray for when you get a taxi from the airport—a driver who actually uses the meter. It's the sign of an honest transaction, a rare gem in the urban jungle.
usage_notes: Primarily used for taxis to distinguish from those who negotiate a fixed price ('kontrata'). 'Metered' is a common English equivalent in this context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas gusto kong sumakay sa taxi na **de-taripa** para makasiguro sa bayad.","translation":"I prefer to ride a taxi that is **metered** to be sure of the fare."},{"sentence":"Swerte, **de-taripa** ang nasakyan naming taxi mula sa airport.","translation":"Luckily, the taxi we got from the airport was **using a fixed rate**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang layunin, hangarin, o plano na nasa isip ng isang tao bago isagawa ang isang kilos.
original_explanation: 'Yung rason sa likod ng ginagawa mo. "Sorry, hindi ko intensyon na saktan ka" is the classic line when you mess up. It's the 'why' behind the 'what'. Pwedeng good, pwedeng bad. Sa ligawan, mahalagang malaman kung ano ang intensyon ng nanliligaw—for keeps ba o for fun lang?
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maganda man ang iyong **intensyon**, mali pa rin ang paraan na ginawa mo.","translation":"Even if your **intention** was good, the method you used was still wrong."},{"sentence":"Ano ba talaga ang **intensyon** mo sa paglapit sa kanya?","translation":"What really is your **intention** in getting close to her?"}]

translation: to let oneself fall; to throw oneself down
meaning_filipino: Ang kusang pagpapaubaya sa sarili na mahulog mula sa isang mataas na lugar o posisyon.
original_explanation: When you see a 12.12 sale and you just let yourself fall into the temptation of spending. Or more literally, when you finally give in and just free-fall onto your bed after a long day. Can also be used for 'nahulog sa'yo' hugot lines.
usage_notes: Often has a dramatic or deliberate connotation, implying a conscious decision to fall, as opposed to 'mahulog' which is often accidental.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tila isang bayani sa pelikula, **nagpatihulog** ang stuntman mula sa gusali papunta sa isang malaking kutson.","translation":"Like a hero in a movie, the stuntman **threw himself down** from the building onto a large mattress."},{"sentence":"Sa sobrang pagod, **nagpatihulog** na lang ako sa sofa pag-uwi.","translation":"From extreme exhaustion, I just **let myself fall** onto the sofa when I got home."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapakamatay sa pamamagitan ng pagsabit sa leeg gamit ang lubid o anumang tali.
original_explanation: This is a heavy one. It's the act of ending one's life by hanging. In a less literal, more modern 'hugot' sense, it's what you feel like doing when your thesis adviser rejects your draft for the fifth time. 'Mag-bigti na lang ako' is a common, though dark and hyperbolic, expression of extreme frustration or despair. (Note: This is a serious topic. If you or someone you know is struggling, please seek help.)
usage_notes: Isang seryosong termino para sa pagpapakamatay sa pamamagitan ng pagbitin. Ang paggamit nito sa balbal na paraan ("magbigti") ay nagpapahayag ng matinding pagkadismaya ngunit dapat gamitin nang may pag-iingat dahil sa kabigatan ng paksa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malagim na balita ang natuklasang kaso ng **bigti** sa lumang bahay.","translation":"The discovered case of **suicide by hanging** in the old house was grim news."}]

translation: to reverse; to invert; to turn over
meaning_filipino: Ilagay sa kabaligtarang ayos o posisyon; baguhin ang pahayag o katotohanan.
original_explanation: The signature move of a 'Marites' (gossiper). They take a simple story and **baliktarin** the facts until the hero becomes the villain. It's also what you do to your pillow at 2 AM to find the cold side for better sleep. One is for drama, the other is for comfort.
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of twisting facts or stories. Can also be spelled 'baligtarin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **baliktarin** ang sinabi ko; hindi iyan ang punto ko.","translation":"Don't **twist** what I said; that wasn't my point."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **baliktarin** ang kutson kada anim na buwan.","translation":"We need to **flip** the mattress every six months."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapakita ng pakikiramay, pagdamay, o pakikiisa sa kalungkutan o pagdadalamhati ng ibang tao.
etymology: From pakikipag- (prefix for mutual social action) + damay (empathy, involvement) + -an (mutual action suffix).
original_explanation: This is the Filipino spirit of 'bayanihan' applied to grief. It's showing up at a wake ('burol') even if you only vaguely knew the person, just to be there for the family. It's the envelope ('abuloy') you give, the shared stories, the quiet presence. It's the community wrapping its arms around someone who's hurting. It's more than just saying "condolences"; it's the act of sharing the burden of sorrow.
usage_notes: Often seen in obituaries as "Nakikipagdamayan" (We sympathize). Strongly associated with funerals and times of tragedy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpaabot kami ng aming taos-pusong **pakikipagdamayan** sa pamilya ng yumao.","translation":"We extended our heartfelt **condolences** to the family of the deceased."},{"sentence":"Sa panahon ng sakuna, nangingibabaw ang diwa ng **pakikipagdamayan** ng mga Pilipino.","translation":"In times of disaster, the Filipino spirit of **mutual sympathy** prevails."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos o pananalita na nagpapahayag ng layuning manakit, magdulot ng pinsala, o magparusa sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: This is your mom giving you "the look" and saying "Umuwi ka bago mag-alas diyes, kundi..." That's a low-level threat. A high-level one is from your landlord: "Bayad o layas!" It's the verbal warning shot before things get real, the promise of negative consequences if you don't comply. It's the "You'll be sorry!" of the Filipino world.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatanggap siya ng **pagbabanta** sa kanyang cellphone.","translation":"He received a **threat** on his cellphone."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagbabanta** sa buhay ng isang tao ay isang seryosong krimen.","translation":"The **act of threatening** a person's life is a serious crime."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging nakagapos o nakakabit sa pamamagitan ng isang lubid, tali, o anumang katulad na bagay.
original_explanation: The feeling when you're stuck in a 'situationship' you can't get out of. You're not officially together, but you're definitely tied down. Also, literally what happens to your shoes if you don't double-knot.
usage_notes: Often used in the passive voice to describe the state of being tied.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **matali** ang aso sa ilalim ng araw.","translation":"Don't let the dog **be tied** up under the sun."},{"sentence":"Ayokong **matali** sa isang trabahong hindi ko gusto.","translation":"I don't want **to be tied** to a job I don't like."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nasa murang edad, mula pagkapanganak hanggang bago maging dalaga o binata.
original_explanation: A young human. The reason for 90% of your expenses and 100% of your 'puyat'. Also, what your parents will call you even when you're 40 years old with a mortgage. "Ang laki mo na, pero para sa amin, bata ka pa rin."
usage_notes: The stress is on the first syllable /BA-ta/. Compare with the adjective 'bata' /ba-TA/ (young).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **bata** ay naglalaro sa labas.","translation":"The **children** are playing outside."},{"sentence":"Mananatili kang **bata** sa paningin ng iyong mga magulang.","translation":"You will always remain a **child** in the eyes of your parents."}]

meaning_filipino: Kumain ng agahan; ang unang pagkain sa umaga.
etymology: From "almusal", which is a corruption of the Spanish "almorzar" (to have lunch), but shifted in meaning to breakfast in Filipino.
original_explanation: This is the more formal, almost poetic way to say "eat breakfast." You'd probably hear your lola say this more than your barkada. While everyone else says "kain na tayo ng breakfast" or "mag-agahan tayo," using 'mag-amusal' is like wearing a barong to a casual brunch. Classy, but a bit extra.
usage_notes: A more formal or literary synonym for "mag-agahan". "Almusal" is the noun, "mag-amusal" is the verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"\"Gising na, mga anak, at tayo'y **mag-amusal** na,\" ang tawag ni Lola.","translation":"\"Wake up, children, and let's **eat breakfast** now,\" called Grandma."},{"sentence":"Maaga siyang gumising upang **mag-amusal** bago pumasok sa trabaho.","translation":"He woke up early to **eat breakfast** before going to work."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang nagpapahayag ng pagtutol, pagsalungat, o pagiging kabaligtaran ng isang bagay, ideya, o tao.
original_explanation: Ito yung laging 'G' sa debate, kahit walang sense yung pinaglalaban. The official 'epal' or 'killjoy' of the group. Kung lahat pro-pineapple on pizza, siya lang ang **kontra**. 'Contra-flow' sa traffic? Ganyan. Siya rin yung laging nega sa group chat.
usage_notes: Can be used as a standalone word ('kontra ako'), a prefix (e.g., 'kontrabida'), or in phrases like 'kontra sa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kontra** ako sa panukalang iyan dahil dehado ang mga manggagawa.","translation":"I am **against** that proposal because it is disadvantageous to the workers."},{"sentence":"Laging may **kontra** sa bawat desisyon ng grupo.","translation":"There's always someone who goes **against** every decision of the group."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang simula o panimulang bahagi ng isang bagay, pangyayari, o yugto ng panahon.
original_explanation: That first day of the 'Ber' months when everyone starts playing Jose Mari Chan. It's the first five seconds of a new K-drama episode, the first day of your diet (again), or the first sahod of a new job. Everything feels possible sa umpisa.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb with prefixes, like 'mag-umpisa' (to start).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap talaga sa **umpisa**, pero masasanay ka rin.","translation":"It's really hard at the **start**, but you'll get used to it."},{"sentence":"Nasa **umpisa** pa lang tayo ng ating paglalakbay.","translation":"We are just at the **beginning** of our journey."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang dalubhasa na nagbibigay ng propesyonal na payo sa isang partikular na larangan tulad ng negosyo, edukasyon, batas, o teknolohiya.
original_explanation: 'Yung tao na binabayaran ng malaki para sabihin sa kumpanya mo kung ano ang mga mali sa ginagawa ninyo. Minsan, sila rin 'yung tito o tito mong laging may 'advice' sa family reunion, pero this time, may Powerpoint presentation at bayad.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa mga propesyonal at teknikal na konteksto. Ang katumbas nitong Filipino na 'tagapayo' ay mas pangkalahatan ang saklaw.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha ang kumpanya ng isang marketing **consultant** para mapalakas ang kanilang benta.","translation":"The company hired a marketing **consultant** to boost their sales."},{"sentence":"Nagtatrabaho siya bilang isang IT **consultant** sa isang malaking korporasyon.","translation":"She works as an IT **consultant** in a large corporation."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-ikot o pagbaling sa ibang direksyon; ang pagpapaikot sa isang bagay tulad ng seradura o takip.
original_explanation: Like when you turn a doorknob, twist open a bottle cap, or when a character in a teleserye slowly turns around for a dramatic reveal. 'Dahan-dahan siyang pumihit paharap sa akin.' It's a controlled turn or twist.
usage_notes: `Pihitin` is the object-focus form. `Pumihit` is the actor-focus form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pumihit** siya pakaliwa sa kanto.","translation":"He **turned** left at the corner."},{"sentence":"Subukan mong **pumihit** ng takip para mabuksan ang bote.","translation":"Try to **twist** the cap to open the bottle."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng hindi pagsasalita o pag-imik, kadalasan dahil sa pagkagulat, pagkalungkot, o malalim na pag-iisip.
original_explanation: This is the deafening silence in the room after someone drops a major chismis bomb. It's you staring at your phone, unable to type a reply because 'seen' is already a message in itself. It’s not just being quiet; it’s a silence that speaks volumes, louder than any shouting match. The ultimate "walang masabi" moment.
usage_notes: Describes a heavy or significant silence, not just the absence of noise.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagkawalang-imik** ay mas nakabibingi pa kaysa sa malakas na sigaw.","translation":"His **speechlessness** was more deafening than a loud shout."},{"sentence":"Sa harap ng balita, tanging **pagkawalang-imik** ang naging tugon ng lahat.","translation":"In the face of the news, the only response from everyone was a **state of silence**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na pag-aari, ginagamit, o ibinabahagi ng lahat sa isang grupo o komunidad.
original_explanation: Parang 'common sense,' na minsan hindi na ganoon ka-common. O kaya yung Wi-Fi password sa co-working space—pang lahat, para sa lahat. It's for public use.
usage_notes: Less common than 'pangkaraniwan' for 'common' but specific when referring to shared resources.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang hardin sa gitna ng subdibisyon ay gamit na **komun** ng lahat ng residente.","translation":"The garden in the middle of the subdivision is for the **common** use of all residents."},{"sentence":"Mayroon silang **komun** na banyo sa dormitoryo.","translation":"They have a **shared** bathroom in the dormitory."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang panimulang pahayag upang bigyang-diin na ang susunod na sasabihin ay isang tapat, prangka, at seryosong opinyon o katotohanan, kahit pa ito ay hindi magandang pakinggan.
original_explanation: The verbal equivalent of 'brace yourself.' When your friend says this, they're about to drop a truth bomb. It's the signal to stop joking around and listen. 'Realtalk, besh, hindi ka na niya babalikan.' It's the modern version of 'Sa totoo lang...' but with more punch.
usage_notes: Used to preface a frank or serious statement. A very common internet and conversational slang, often used as an adverbial phrase.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Realtalk**, kailangan mo nang mag-ipon para sa kinabukasan mo.","translation":"**Real talk**, you need to start saving for your future."},{"sentence":"Okay, **realtalk** lang tayo, ha? Hindi bagay sa'yo 'yang kulay ng buhok.","translation":"Okay, let's have some **real talk**, okay? That hair color doesn't suit you."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mapabilang o madawit sa isang pangyayari, usapin, o gulo, kadalasan nang hindi sinasadya.
original_explanation: That "nadamay lang po" feeling. When you were just minding your own business and suddenly you're part of the *chismis* or, worse, the group project drama. It's being dragged into a situation, often a messy one.
usage_notes: Carries a slightly negative connotation of being dragged into something, often trouble. The object-focus counterpart is 'nasangkot'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May mga pulitiko na **sumangkot** sa malaking iskandalo.","translation":"There were politicians who **were implicated** in a big scandal."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko sinasadya, pero **sumangkot** ako sa kanilang pag-aaway.","translation":"I didn't mean to, but I **got involved** in their fight."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging lukot, gusot, o hindi makinis ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay tela o papel.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung itsura ng damit mong isang linggo nang nasa laundry basket. Or 'yung noo ng nanay mo 'pag nalamang hindi ka pa naliligo at 12 PM na. "Hala, ang kulungkot ng uniform mo, plantsahin mo 'yan!"
usage_notes: Synonymous with 'lukot' or 'gusot', but is less common in everyday speech than 'lukot'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayusin mo ang **kulungkot** sa iyong damit bago ka umalis.","translation":"Fix the **wrinkle** on your clothes before you leave."},{"sentence":"Naging **kulungkot** ang papel matapos itong makulob sa bag.","translation":"The paper became **wrinkled** after being stuck inside the bag."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging walang-hiya; ang kawalan ng pakiramdam ng kahihiyan o paggalang sa iba.
original_explanation: This is the official term for someone with 'kapal ng mukha' (thick face). It's that person who cuts in line, sings karaoke loudly at 2 AM on a Tuesday, or asks 'Tumataba ka yata?' as a greeting. The ultimate lack of 'delicadeza'.
usage_notes: A very strong term used to denote a severe lack of propriety or respect.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko matiis ang **kawalang-hiyaan** ng taong iyon sa pila.","translation":"I cannot stand the **shamelessness** of that person in the queue."},{"sentence":"Tunay na **kawalang-hiyaan** ang ginawa niyang pag-post ng pekeng balita.","translation":"What he did by posting fake news was an act of true **impudence**."}]

translation: To apply, to fit closely, to administer
meaning_filipino: Idikit o ilagay nang mahigpit at walang puwang; magbigay ng paunang lunas.
original_explanation: This is what you do with a Band-Aid on a cut, or foundation on your face to cover up the fact you only got 3 hours of sleep. It's about making things fit perfectly, whether it's a theory to a problem ('**ilapat** ang teorya') or first aid ('**ilapat** ang paunang lunas'). The goal is a perfect, seamless fit.
usage_notes: Can mean to physically apply something (like medicine), or to apply a concept or theory. Also used for administering first aid.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ilapat** mo ang yelo sa bukol para hindi mamaga.","translation":"**Apply** ice to the bump so it won't swell."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan nilang **ilapat** ang natutunan nila sa klase sa totoong buhay.","translation":"They tried to **apply** what they learned in class to real life."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi nakakalimutan; nananatili sa isipan o alaala.
original_explanation: This is your brain's current activity when your friend asks, "Uy, 'yung utang mo sa'kin last year?" It's the active process of recalling something. "Wait lang, natatandaan ko pa... " is the verbal equivalent of a loading screen in your head. It's the present tense, the ongoing state of having something in your memory.
usage_notes: Present tense of 'matandaan'. Often used interchangeably with 'naaalala'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Natatandaan** mo pa ba noong una tayong nagkita?","translation":"Do you still **remember** when we first met?"},{"sentence":"Hanggang ngayon, malinaw ko pa ring **natatandaan** ang lahat.","translation":"Until now, I still clearly **remember** everything."}]

meaning_filipino: May hugis na tulad ng isang apa o kono; patulis mula sa isang pabilog na base.
original_explanation: Describes anything shaped like a birthday party hat, an ice cream cone, or the 'sombrero' you see on farmers in old paintings. It's that pointy shape you learned in geometry but now only associate with traffic cones or 'dirty ice cream'.
usage_notes: Isang teknikal o pormal na termino. Mas karaniwan sa pang-araw-araw na salita ang 'hugis-apa' o 'hugis-kono'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bubong ng tore ay may **koniko** na disenyo.","translation":"The roof of the tower has a **conical** design."},{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng isang **koniko** na sisidlan para sa eksperimento.","translation":"He used a **conical** flask for the experiment."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang damdamin ng pag-asam o pananabik na mangyari ang isang bagay na ninanais; tiwala na may magandang kahihinatnan ang isang sitwasyon.
original_explanation: That feeling you get on the 14th and 29th of the month, waiting for sahod. Or when you send a risky text and wait for a reply. It's the "sana all" energy converted into a noun. It's the reason why we still bet on lotto, join raffles, and believe our crush will notice us someday. Asa is the ultimate kapit-bisig move against uncertainty.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa anyong "pag-asa".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mawalan ng **pag-asa**.","translation":"Don't lose **hope**."},{"sentence":"Siya ang tanging **asa** ng kanyang pamilya.","translation":"She is the only **hope** of his family."}]

translation: to be allied; to be affiliated
meaning_filipino: Magkasama o magkasapi sa isang pangkat, samahan, o layunin.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung dalawang K-Pop fandoms na **magkaanib** para i-boost 'yung streams ng kanilang faves. It means being united, allied, or part of the same group. You're on the same team, fighting for the same cause, whether it's politics, business, or just getting your group project done.
usage_notes: Can function as a verb (to be allied) or an adjective (allied). Describes a formal or informal alliance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang dalawang kumpanya ay **magkaanib** ngayon upang palakasin ang kanilang negosyo.","translation":"The two companies are now **allied** to strengthen their business."},{"sentence":"Sila ay **magkaanib** sa iisang paniniwalang pampulitika.","translation":"They are **affiliated** by the same political belief."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbuga ng isang bagay mula sa bibig, tulad ng laway, pagkain, o anumang hindi sinasadyang naisubò.
etymology: From `dura` (spit), with a common d-l sound shift.
original_explanation: What you do when you accidentally drink spoiled milk. Or when you have to spit out bitter truths. It's the opposite of "lunukin" (to swallow). Minsan kailangan mong ilura yung sama ng loob para gumaan ang pakiramdam.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for spitting something from the mouth, or figuratively for expressing something held back, often with anger or disgust.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ilura** mo 'yang buto ng pakwan.","translation":"**Spit out** that watermelon seed."},{"sentence":"Nais niyang **ilura** ang lahat ng kanyang sama ng loob.","translation":"She wants **to spit out** all her grievances."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malaking isda sa dagat na karaniwang matatagpuan sa malamig na tubig ng Hilagang Atlantiko, at mahalaga bilang pagkain.
original_explanation: Yung isda na sikat sa fish and chips, pero hindi kasing sikat ng galunggong o tilapia sa palengke. Pang-special occasion o pang-fancy restaurant lang ang datingan.
usage_notes: Hindi ito karaniwang isda sa mga palengke sa Pilipinas. Mas kilala bilang sangkap sa mga pagkaing Kanluranin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatikim ka na ba ng **cod** fish and chips?","translation":"Have you ever tasted **cod** fish and chips?"},{"sentence":"Mahal ang presyo ng **cod** sa supermarket.","translation":"The price of **cod** at the supermarket is expensive."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o bagay na naliwanagan, nagkaroon ng malalim na kaalaman, o may sapat na ilaw.
original_explanation: When the lightbulb in your brain finally turns on after your friend explains a meme for the 5th time. It also literally means well-lit, like a mall during Christmas season. Or that feeling of deep understanding after watching a really good documentary. You're now "enlightened."
usage_notes: Can be used literally for light or figuratively for knowledge/enlightenment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **iluminado** ang entablado nang lumabas ang bida.","translation":"The stage became **illuminated** when the star came out."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang mga nabasa, tila **iluminado** ang kanyang isipan sa mga bagong ideya.","translation":"Because of what he read, his mind seems **enlightened** with new ideas."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang estado ng kawalan ng katiyakan o pag-aalinlangan; paghihinala.
original_explanation: That feeling you get when your partner says "may overtime ako" on a Friday night. It's the "benefit of the doubt" you're NOT giving. It's the official sport of marites everywhere. "May duda ako sa kanya."
usage_notes: Can also be used as an adjective informally (e.g., "Duda ako" meaning "I am doubtful").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawala ang lahat ng **duda** ko nang makita ko ang ebidensya.","translation":"All my **doubts** disappeared when I saw the evidence."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magtanim ng **duda** sa iyong kaibigan.","translation":"Don't plant **doubt** in your friend."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang opisyal na may kapangyarihang magpasya sa mga usaping legal; sinumang nagbibigay ng hatol, pagsusuri, o kritikal na opinyon.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "taga-" (tagagawa ng kilos) at salitang-ugat na "husga" (paghatol), na hiram sa Espanyol na "juzgar".
original_explanation: The official judge in a courtroom, or unofficially, your chismosang kapitbahay judging your life choices from her window. On social media, everyone's a self-appointed tagahusga. The line 'Judge me when you are perfect' was made for them.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **tagahusga** sa beauty pageant ay mga kilalang personalidad.","translation":"The **judges** in the beauty pageant are well-known personalities."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paraang nagmamadali at halos hindi na makahinga dahil sa pagod o pag-aapura.
original_explanation: This is you running to catch the MRT before the doors close, or rushing to clock in at your BPO job with 30 seconds to spare. You arrive at your destination, gasping for air, looking like you just wrestled a jeepney. "Bakit ka dumating nang pahangos?" is the classic "what's the emergency?" question.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumating siyang **pahangos** sa opisina dahil na-late siya ng gising.","translation":"He arrived **hurriedly** at the office because he woke up late."},{"sentence":"**Pahangos** na tumakbo ang bata papalayo sa aso.","translation":"The child ran away from the dog, **out of breath**."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa literal na kahulugan, ito ay ang kasalukuyang kilos ng pagpisil sa balat gamit ang mga daliri. Sa matalinhagang kahulugan, ito ay naglalarawan ng isang damdaming nakakaantig o nakapagpapadama ng kirot sa puso.
original_explanation: Literally, it's "pinching," like what your tita does to your cheeks. But the real 'hugot' meaning is "heart-wrenching." It's that feeling you get watching a sad movie or a viral video of a lolo working hard. It's not a full-blown cry; it's that sharp, sudden pang of sadness or empathy that "pinches" your heart. "Kumukurot sa puso."
usage_notes: Can be used literally (pinching skin) or figuratively (emotionally touching/painful). The figurative use, often as 'kumukurot sa puso', is very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Talagang **kumukurot** sa puso ang mga eksena sa pelikulang iyon.","translation":"The scenes in that movie are truly **heart-wrenching**."},{"sentence":"Bakit ka ba **kumukurot** sa tagiliran ko?","translation":"Why **are you pinching** my side?"}]

translation: is delivering; is escorting; is conveying
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagdadala o pagsasama sa isang tao o bagay patungo sa isang partikular na lugar o destinasyon. Maaari ring tumukoy sa pagpapahayag ng isang damdamin o mensahe.
original_explanation: That sweet gesture of walking someone home ('ihahatid kita') to make sure they're safe. It's also what Grab, Lalamove, and FoodPanda riders do all day. On a 'hugot' level, it's what a sad song does—it 'naghahatid ng kalungkutan' (delivers sadness). So, it can be literal delivery or emotional delivery.
usage_notes: The 'ha-' is the reduplication of the first syllable of the root 'hatid', indicating the present tense. It can mean physical delivery or conveying a message/feeling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang rider ay **naghahatid** ng pagkain kahit umuulan.","translation":"The rider is **delivering** food even though it's raining."},{"sentence":"Ang balitang ito ay **naghahatid** ng pag-asa sa marami.","translation":"This news **brings** hope to many."}]

translation: to unite; to make as one; to combine
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsamahin ang dalawa o higit pang bagay, tao, o konsepto upang maging isang buo.
original_explanation: This is what you try to do with your different friend groups at your birthday party. It's what a project manager does with different departments to meet a deadline. It's also what you do when you have leftover sinigang and adobo and you decide to pag-isahin them in one bowl. #FusionCuisine
usage_notes: Command form. The infinitive is "pag-isahin," the past tense is "pinag-isa," the present is "pinag-iisa," and the future is "pag-iisahin."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sikaping **pag-isahin** ang lahat ng sangkap bago ito ilagay sa oven.","translation":"Try **to combine** all the ingredients before putting them in the oven."},{"sentence":"Nais ng lider na **pag-isahin** ang mga nag-aaway na paksyon.","translation":"The leader wants **to unite** the warring factions."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging malagkit, makunat, o mahirap nguyain.
original_explanation: Ito yung 'chewiness level' ng paborito mong biko o sapin-sapin. The more na kailangan mong i-effort ang pag-nguya, the more na 'maligat'. Perfect for describing kakanin, or that one friend who is super clingy.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin ang anyong "maligat" (adjective).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko ang **ligat** ng bagong lutong kalamay.","translation":"I like the **chewiness** of freshly cooked rice cake."},{"sentence":"Sinusubok niya ang **ligat** ng nilulutong pandikit.","translation":"He is testing the **viscosity** of the glue he is making."}]

translation: to leave alone, to stop bothering
meaning_filipino: Utos na tigilan ang pang-iistorbo, panggugulo, o pag-abala sa isang tao o pagpapatuloy sa isang gawain.
original_explanation: The Tagalog equivalent of "Get off my back!" or "Leave me alone!" It's what you want to scream when someone keeps pestering you about your love life, your weight, or why you're still single. It's a command to cease and desist, often said with a hint of desperation or major annoyance. "Please lang, lubayan niyo na ako sa tanong na 'kailan ka mag-aasawa?'"
usage_notes: Used as a command. The tone can range from playful pleading to serious anger.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lubayan** mo ako! Nag-aaral ako para sa exam.","translation":"**Leave me alone**! I'm studying for the exam."},{"sentence":"Sinabihan ng pulis ang mga usisero na **lubayan** ang crime scene.","translation":"The police told the onlookers to **stay away from** (stop bothering) the crime scene."}]

translation: to have someone argue/debate about something
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o paghiling na ipagtanggol o ipaglaban ang isang panig o opinyon sa pamamagitan ng debate o diskusyon.
original_explanation: This is what lawyers do. You hire them to **ipakipagtaltalan** your case in court. It's also what happens when you post a controversial opinion on Facebook and let your friends battle it out in the comments section. You're basically telling them, "Go, argue about this for me."
usage_notes: Implies engaging in a formal or intense argument on behalf of someone or for a certain cause.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Handa siyang **ipakipagtaltalan** ang kanyang karapatan hanggang sa huling sandali.","translation":"She is ready to **debate for** her rights until the very last moment."}]

meaning_filipino: Makaranas ng panginginig ng katawan, karaniwan dahil sa lagnat o matinding ginaw.
original_explanation: The verb form of that 'Antartica AC' feeling. This is what happens when you decide to take a bath at 4 AM. 'Ngingikiin ka' is what your lola warns you about when you go out with wet hair. It's the active state of your body doing the cha-cha against its will because of cold or fever.
usage_notes: A verb describing the state of having chills, usually from cold or sickness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula siyang **ngikiin** kaya't agad siyang nagkumot.","translation":"He started **to have chills** so he immediately used a blanket."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magbabad sa ulan at baka ka **ngikiin**.","translation":"Don't stay too long in the rain or you might **get chills**."}]

meaning_filipino: Lantad, hayag, o kalat na sa kaalaman ng marami; hindi na lihim.
original_explanation: This is when the tea is not just spilled, it's been broadcasted on a national town hall meeting. When a secret is so out in the open, it might as well have its own billboard on EDSA. Think of a 'blind item' where everyone already knows who the subject is. The opposite of 'keep it lowkey'.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng mga sikreto, balita, o impormasyon na naging pampubliko. Mayroon itong pormal at medyo malalim na tono.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Siwalat** na sa buong barangay ang tungkol sa kanilang sikretong relasyon.","translation":"Their secret relationship is now **widespread** knowledge throughout the whole village."},{"sentence":"Nang dahil sa social media, naging **siwalat** ang katiwalian sa gobyerno.","translation":"Because of social media, the corruption in the government became **exposed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isinasagawa o isinaayos ayon sa isang tiyak na plano, pamamaraan, o sistema; organisado at may kaayusan.
original_explanation: Parang pag-aayos ng files sa computer or pag-aayos ng damit sa aparador by color. Hindi 'yung "bahala na si Batman" approach. 'Yung friend mong may Excel sheet para sa lahat ng bagay? Sobrang sistematiko niya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating magkaroon ng **sistematiko** na paraan sa paglutas ng problemang ito.","translation":"We need to have a **systematic** way of solving this problem."}]

translation: a type of Filipino noodle dish (Pancit Luglog)
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pansit na may makapal na noodles at malapot na sarsang kulay kahel, na hinahango ang pangalan sa paraan ng pagluto ng noodles nito.
etymology: From the verb `luglog`, referring to the cooking method.
original_explanation: Pancit Luglog is the cousin of Pancit Palabok. It gets its name from the cooking process where the thick rice noodles are "ni-lu-luglog" (dipped and shaken) in hot broth. It's topped with a savory orange shrimp sauce, crushed chicharon, tinapa flakes, and hard-boiled eggs. It's a fiesta on a plate.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with Pancit Palabok, though technically the noodle thickness differs (Luglog uses thicker noodles).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-uwi si tatay ng isang bilao ng pansit **luglog** para sa meryenda.","translation":"Dad brought home a tray of pancit **luglog** for our afternoon snack."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malambot na himaymay sa katawan ng tao o hayop na may kakayahang umikli at humaba upang makagawa ng paggalaw.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'laman' (flesh, content) at panlaping 'ka- -an'.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung pino-flex mo sa salamin after ng workout. 'Yung dahilan kung bakit masakit ang buong katawan mo the day after mag-decide kang mag-gym for the first time in years. Sa Tagalog, hindi lang abs ang meron ka, may kalamnan ka.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa konteksto ng anatomiya, ehersisyo, at kalusugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumasakit ang kanyang mga **kalamnan** dahil sa pagbubuhat ng mabibigat na bagay.","translation":"His **muscles** are sore from lifting heavy things."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang stretching upang maiwasan ang pinsala sa **kalamnan**.","translation":"Stretching is important to avoid **muscle** injury."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ina ng ama o ina ng isang tao; isang babaeng nakatatanda na may mga apo.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na "abuela", na pinaikli at inangkop sa ponolohiyang Tagalog.
original_explanation: The OG source of unconditional love, unsolicited advice about your weight, and a seemingly endless supply of food and stories about "noong panahon namin." She's the one who will defend you from your parents' scolding. Also, the final boss in a Filipino family hierarchy.
usage_notes: Isang magalang na tawag sa lahat ng matatandang babae, kahit hindi kamag-anak.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap magluto ng adobo ang **lola** ko.","translation":"My **grandmother** cooks delicious adobo."},{"sentence":"Mano po, **Lola**.","translation":"Bless me, **Grandma**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang taong hindi tapat, pakitang-tao, at nagkukunwari lamang sa ipinapakitang ugali o pakikitungo.
etymology: From English 'plastic', used metaphorically to mean artificial or not genuine.
original_explanation: The person who's super nice to your face but talks trash behind your back. They're the 'frenemy' in your office or barkada. You know, the one who'll praise your new haircut then screenshot your photo for the group chat with the caption 'ano na naman 'to?' Classic backstabber.
usage_notes: A very common colloquial term to describe insincerity. Can also be used as a noun to refer to a person ('Huwag kang maniwala diyan, plastik 'yan.').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong magtiwala sa kanya, **plastik** daw 'yan sabi ng marami.","translation":"Don't trust her too much, many say she's **two-faced**."},{"sentence":"Ayoko ng mga kaibigang **plastik**; masakit silang katraydor.","translation":"I don't like **fake** friends; they are painful traitors."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang natatanging kasuotan na isinusuot ng ikakasal, lalo na ng babae, sa araw ng kasal.
original_explanation: The most expensive 'damit' a person might ever wear for just one day. It's the subject of countless Pinterest boards, family arguments ('Dapat may sleeves!'), and 'Say Yes to the Dress' marathon dreams. For men, it's usually a Barong Tagalog or a suit. This is the ultimate 'pang-aura' outfit.
usage_notes: Can refer to the bride's gown (traje de boda) or the groom's suit/barong.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakaganda ng kanyang **damit pangkasal** na gawa sa piña.","translation":"Her **wedding dress** made of piña cloth was so beautiful."},{"sentence":"Nag-iipon sila para sa pangarap nilang **damit pangkasal**.","translation":"They are saving up for their dream **wedding attire**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamababang tono sa musika, para sa boses ng lalaki o sa instrumentong pangmusika.
original_explanation: In music, this is the deep, low-pitched sound that gives a song its foundation. Think of the lowest male voice in a choir or the sound of a bass guitar or double bass. It's the 'dug-dug-dug' that you feel in your chest.
usage_notes: Pareho ang bigkas sa 'baho' (stench), ngunit nililinaw ng konteksto ang kahulugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maganda ang timbre ng kanyang boses na **baho**.","translation":"The timbre of his **bass** voice is beautiful."},{"sentence":"Siya ang tumutugtog ng **baho** sa kanilang banda.","translation":"He plays the **bass** in their band."}]

translation: to be hidden from one's knowledge; to be unaware of
meaning_filipino: Hindi malaman o mapansin; maitago sa kaalaman o paningin ng isang tao.
etymology: Mula sa "lingid," na nangangahulugang tago o lihim.
original_explanation: Hindi nalingid sa kaalaman ng nanay mo na um-order ka na naman sa Shopee kahit sabi mo 'last na 'to'. Mother's instinct is the best CCTV. Nothing escapes her.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa mas pormal o pampanitikang paraan. Ang estruktura ay madalas na "hindi nalingid sa [kaniyang] kaalaman".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi **nalingid** sa kanya ang mga lihim na kilos ng kanyang mga kasamahan.","translation":"The secret actions of his colleagues were not **hidden from his knowledge**."},{"sentence":"Marahil ay may mga detalyeng **nalingid** sa mga imbestigador.","translation":"Perhaps there are details that the investigators **were unaware of**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang pangkusina na may talim na ginagamit sa pagbabalat ng mga prutas at gulay.
original_explanation: The kitchen gadget that saves you from the risky business of balatan-ng-kutsilyo. It's the MVP when making potato salad, fruit salad, or anything that requires removing the skin of a fruit or vegetable. Every Filipino household has at least one of these, probably bought from a street vendor or Daiso. It's a small tool that prevents big 'sugat'.
usage_notes: A direct English loanword. The Tagalog equivalent is 'pambalat'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiabot ng **peeler**, babalatan ko lang itong mga patatas.","translation":"Please hand me the **peeler**, I'm just going to peel these potatoes."},{"sentence":"Mas mabilis gumamit ng **peeler** kaysa kutsilyo para sa mangga.","translation":"It's faster to use a **peeler** than a knife for mangoes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking nasa hustong gulang na ngunit hindi pa ikinakasal.
original_explanation: This is the classic term for a bachelor, an unmarried dude. Your tita's favorite question during family reunions is probably, "O, iho, kailan ka mag-aasawa? Baka tumandang **sultero** ka niyan!" It's the male equivalent of a 'dalagang Pilipina' who's taking her sweet time. In modern terms, he's 'single and not-so-ready-to-mingle' according to your relatives.
usage_notes: The female equivalent is 'sultera'. Sometimes used with a slightly teasing or worried tone by older relatives.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masaya siya sa pagiging **sultero** at wala pang planong mag-asawa.","translation":"He is happy being a **bachelor** and has no plans to get married yet."},{"sentence":"Lahat ng magkakapatid ay may asawa na, maliban sa bunso na nananatiling **sultero**.","translation":"All the siblings are married, except for the youngest who remains a **bachelor**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglipat ng mga tao mula sa isang lugar na mapanganib patungo sa isang mas ligtas na lokasyon.
original_explanation: Yung mandatory "vacation" na ayaw mo, sponsored by a typhoon, flood, or a nearby volcano acting up. Dito mo isasalba ang TV, ang aso, at ang picture niyo ng ex mo (bakit?!), bago ang sarili mo. The national past-time during rainy season.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng sapilitang **ebakwasyon** dahil sa pagtaas ng tubig-baha.","translation":"There was a forced **evacuation** due to the rising floodwaters."},{"sentence":"Handa na ang mga **ebakwasyon** center para sa paparating na bagyo.","translation":"The **evacuation** centers are ready for the coming typhoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng hindi pagkaalala; pagkawala ng isang bagay sa isipan o alaala.
original_explanation: That feeling when you walk into a room and completely forget why you're there. Or when your ex asks 'Naalala mo pa ba ako?' and you hit them with a 'Sino ka ulit?' That's limot. It's the brain's delete button, sometimes helpful, sometimes the reason you failed an exam. The classic 'Nasa dulo ng dila ko!' moment.
usage_notes: Often used in its verb forms: 'nakalimutan' (forgot), 'malimutan' (to forget), 'kalimutan' (forget it). The noun 'limot' itself is a bit more poetic or formal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nalbaon na sa **limot** ang kanilang nakaraan.","translation":"Their past has been buried in **oblivion**."},{"sentence":"Sana ay may gamot para sa **limot**.","translation":"I wish there was a cure for **forgetfulness**."}]

translation: to make someone happy; to please
meaning_filipino: Magdulot ng saya o ligaya sa isang tao; bigyan ng kasiyahan.
original_explanation: This is your love language if you're the type to buy your friend milk tea after a tough day or send a funny meme to your group chat just to lift the mood. It's the goal of every 'pasalubong' from a vacationing tita.
usage_notes: This is an object-focused verb. The person being made happy is the object of the sentence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang **pasiyahin** ang kanyang inang may sakit.","translation":"He is trying **to make** his sick mother **happy**."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **pasiyahin** ang mga taong laging may reklamo.","translation":"It's hard **to please** people who always have a complaint."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kutsara na may tiyak na sukat (hal. teaspoon, tablespoon) na ginagamit sa pagtakal ng maliliit na dami ng sangkap.
etymology: Direct loan phrase from English "measuring spoon".
original_explanation: The smaller, more elusive cousin of the measuring cup. It's that set of spoons on a ring that you always lose one piece from. Is it a teaspoon or a tablespoon? Who knows! Your mom's 'isang kutsarita' is probably more accurate anyway. It's all about 'tantsa-tantsa' (estimation) in a Filipino kitchen.
usage_notes: The English term is used almost exclusively. The Tagalog equivalent "panakal na kutsara" is very rare.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng isang **measuring spoon** para sa baking powder.","translation":"I need a **measuring spoon** for the baking powder."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang impormal at magiliw na tawag sa mga taong kabilang sa "rainbow community" o LGBTQIA+ community.
etymology: Mula sa pinaikling Ingles na "rainbow family".
original_explanation: The more casual, more 'barkada' way of saying 'Rainbow Community'. Parang, "Uy, part ka ba ng rainbow fam?" It's less formal, more intimate, like a secret handshake for the kids. It’s giving 'squad goals' but make it ✨fabulous✨.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin ng mga nakababatang miyembro ng komunidad.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Happy Pride sa lahat ng ating **rainbow fam**!","translation":"Happy Pride to all of our **rainbow fam**!"}]

translation: to frisk; to search by patting down
meaning_filipino: Ang paghalughog o paghahanap ng isang bagay sa katawan o kasuotan ng isang tao sa pamamagitan ng pagdama o paghipo.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa ng sekyu sa'yo bago ka pumasok sa mall o sa MRT. It's a full-body pat-down to check for... well, things you're not supposed to bring in. It's the 'wala po akong dala, manong' moment.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of security checks. The base form 'kapkap' can also function as a noun meaning 'the act of frisking'.
