original_explanation: Think of that resume and cover letter you put in one brown envelope. Or when you send an email and you click "attach file" – a digital version of `magkalakip`. It's two things that are meant to be together, like french fries and ketchup.
usage_notes: Often used in formal or written communication, like describing documents in an envelope. Can also be used figuratively for things that are inseparable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magkalakip** sa sobre ang sulat at ang litrato.","translation":"The letter and the photo are **attached together** in the envelope."},{"sentence":"Ang kanilang mga kamay ay **magkalakip** habang naglalakad.","translation":"Their hands were **held together** while walking."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglapat o naglalapat ng mga labi sa isang tao o bagay bilang tanda ng pagmamahal, paggalang, o pagbati.
original_explanation: The present tense of 'Naks, may something sila!' This is what's happening when your friend says 'BRB' and you spot them with their crush sa may madilim na corner. The action that fuels the 'Sana all' comments.
usage_notes: Present progressive tense of 'humalik'. Describes the ongoing action of kissing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa pelikula, laging **humahalik** ang bida sa kanyang katambal sa ilalim ng ulan.","translation":"In movies, the protagonist **is** always **kissing** his partner under the rain."}]

translation: to take turns; to relieve someone
meaning_filipino: Ang paghalili o pagpalit sa isang tao sa isang gawain o posisyon, karaniwan ay para magbigay ng pahinga o tulong.
original_explanation: Parang sa BPO, 'pag end of shift mo na, may darating na ka-team para pulihan ka. Or sa love life, 'pag 'di ka na niya mahal, may papalit sa'yo... ay, hugot! It's basically a tag-in, tag-out system for tasks or duties. Your reliever "takes your post."
usage_notes: Often used in the context of work shifts, guard duty, or any task that requires continuous attention where people need to take breaks.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pulihan** mo muna ako sa pagbabantay ng tindahan, kakain lang ako.","translation":"**Take over** for me in watching the store, I'm just going to eat."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **pupulih** sa kanya kapag nag-leave siya sa trabaho?","translation":"Who will **relieve** her when she goes on leave from work?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na namamahala, nangangasiwa, o nagpapatakbo ng isang organisasyon, proyekto, o ari-arian.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'taga-' (tagagawa) at 'pangasiwa' (to manage, administer), mula sa ugat na 'asiwa'.
original_explanation: The boss. The manager. The person in charge. Sila yung taga-approve ng leave, taga-delegate ng tasks, at taga-sermon 'pag may mali. From the BPO team leader to the building admin to the manager of your favorite fast-food chain, sila ang 'bahala' sa lahat.
usage_notes: Isang pangkalahatang termino para sa sinumang nasa posisyong manedyeryal o administratibo. Karaniwan sa konteksto ng negosyo at organisasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kausapin mo ang **tagapangasiwa** ng gusali kung may problema ka sa iyong unit.","translation":"Talk to the building **administrator** if you have a problem with your unit."},{"sentence":"Ang **tagapangasiwa** ng proyekto ang nagbigay ng mga bagong alituntunin.","translation":"The project **manager** gave the new guidelines."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagtatalaga ng mga tao upang gampanan ang isang tungkulin o trabaho sa isang partikular na lugar o posisyon.
original_explanation: This is what your manager does when they create the weekly shift schedule. It's assigning people to their battle stations—who's on cashier duty, who's on the floor, who's in charge of the BGC branch. It’s the strategic placement of 'tao' (people) to get the job done.
usage_notes: Related to the verb 'magpatao' (to assign people). Not to be confused with 'pagkatao' (personality, humanity).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang tamang **pagtao** sa bawat istasyon para maging maayos ang operasyon.","translation":"Proper **manning** of each station is important for the operation to be smooth."},{"sentence":"Inihahanda na ng komite ang listahan para sa **pagtao** ng mga presinto.","translation":"The committee is now preparing the list for **assigning personnel** to the precincts."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pag-aatubili o kawalan ng desisyon, na nagreresulta sa pabalik-balik na kilos o isipan sa pagitan ng pag-urong at pagsulong.
original_explanation: This is the official term for 'Should I text them? No. Yes. No. Maybe tomorrow.' It's that endless back-and-forth in your head when deciding on something, like choosing between two Jollibee meal combos or finally resigning from your toxic job. It's the paralysis of analysis, Filipino style.
usage_notes: Describes a state of indecisiveness or wavering.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **pag-urung-sulungan**, naunahan na siya ng iba sa pag-apply para sa posisyon.","translation":"Because of his **hesitation**, others got ahead of him in applying for the position."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang makitid na daanan sa loob ng isang gusali, bahay, o sasakyan na nag-uugnay sa iba't ibang silid o bahagi.
original_explanation: That narrow space in the office or school where all the chismis happens. Dito ka rin naglalakad nang dahan-dahan para i-delay ang pagbalik sa desk mo. Sa sinehan, ito yung daanan na ayaw mong madadaanan ng may dalang popcorn kasi baka matapunan ka. In short, the runway of everyday life.
usage_notes: While 'hallway' is understood, 'pasilyo' is the correct and common term in Filipino. The user requested 'hallway', and this is the direct Filipino equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-abang siya sa **pasilyo** ng ospital habang inooperahan ang kanyang asawa.","translation":"He waited in the hospital **corridor** while his wife was being operated on."},{"sentence":"Huwag kayong magtakbuhan sa **pasilyo** ng paaralan.","translation":"Don't run in the school **hallway**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malakas at magaspang na tunog na nalilikha sa paghinga habang natutulog, sanhi ng bahagyang pagbara sa daluyan ng hangin.
original_explanation: The official soundtrack of your Tito's siesta. It’s that chainsaw-like sound that can shake the entire house and proves someone is in a deep, *deep* sleep. If your roommate does this, good luck getting any sleep yourself.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used to describe the sound of snoring. 'Hilik' is a more common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lakas ng **hagok** ni Tatay kagabi!","translation":"Dad's **snore** was so loud last night!"},{"sentence":"Hindi ako makatulog dahil sa **hagok** ng katabi ko sa bus.","translation":"I couldn't sleep because of the **snoring** of the person next to me on the bus."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pampublikong anunsyo o paunawa, karaniwan sa pahayagan, tungkol sa pagkamatay ng isang tao, na kadalasa'y may kasamang maikling talambuhay.
original_explanation: The one part of the newspaper you hope you're not featured in anytime soon. The obitwaryo is the formal 'chismis' about someone's passing. It's a public notice that someone has died, often with a short bio and details about the wake and funeral. It’s basically the final Facebook status update, but in print.
usage_notes: Found in the classified ads or a dedicated section of a newspaper.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nalungkot siya nang makita ang pangalan ng kanyang kaibigan sa **obitwaryo**.","translation":"He was saddened when he saw his friend's name in the **obituary**."},{"sentence":"Naghahanap kami ng impormasyon tungkol sa burol sa seksyon ng **obitwaryo** ng dyaryo.","translation":"We are looking for information about the wake in the **obituary** section of the newspaper."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang akda, likha, o gawa ng isip, lalo na sa larangan ng panitikan, musika, o sining. Maaari rin itong tumukoy sa isang bagay na inimbento o hindi totoo.
original_explanation: Anything you make up. Pwedeng isang award-winning novel, pwedeng kanta, or pwedeng excuse mo sa boss mo kung bakit ka na-late. "Kathang-isip" is your imagination's playground. If someone says "pawang katha lang 'yan," they're calling your story a lie, a fabrication, pure chismis.
usage_notes: Often seen as "kathang-isip" (fiction/product of imagination). Can also mean an excuse or fabrication.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Noli Me Tángere ay isang di-malilimutang **katha** ni Jose Rizal.","translation":"Noli Me Tángere is an unforgettable **work** by Jose Rizal."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala sa kanya, puro **katha** lang ang mga sinasabi niya.","translation":"Don't believe him, what he says are all just **fabrications**."}]

translation: to be able to mislead; to be able to deceive
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang ilihis ang isang tao o bagay mula sa tamang landas, direksyon, o pag-unawa.
original_explanation: This is what fake news does. Or that friend who gives you "shortcut" directions that get you stuck in EDSA for three hours. It's the ability to lead someone astray, intentionally or not. "Ang maling impormasyon ay maaaring makapagligaw ng maraming tao."
usage_notes: Used for both literal getting lost and figurative deception or confusion. The stress on the syllable 'GAW' distinguishes it from its homonym related to courtship.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga pekeng karatula sa daan ay maaaring **makapagligaw** sa mga turista.","translation":"Fake signs on the road can **mislead** the tourists."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala sa sabi-sabi, baka **makapagligaw** lang iyan sa katotohanan.","translation":"Don't believe in rumors, they might just **lead you away** from the truth."}]

meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahan o pagkakataong ipahayag ang isang bagay, ideya, o nararamdaman sa pamamagitan ng salita.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `makapag-` (kakayahan) at salitang-ugat na `sabi`.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're bursting to tell your friend the latest chismis but they're not picking up the phone. The moment you finally get to talk, you can say 'Hay, salamat! May kailangan akong makapagsabi sa'yo!' It's about having the chance or the courage to finally say what's on your mind, whether it's a secret, a confession, or just piping hot tea.
usage_notes: Madalas itong nagpapahiwatig ng pagkakaroon ng pagkakataon, lakas ng loob, o awtoridad na sabihin ang isang partikular na bagay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **makapagsabi** ako ng totoo sa kanya balang araw.","translation":"I hope I can **be able to tell** him/her the truth someday."},{"sentence":"Hindi siya **makapagsabi** ng 'hindi' dahil ayaw niyang makasakit ng damdamin.","translation":"She can't **bring herself to say** 'no' because she doesn't want to hurt feelings."}]

meaning_filipino: Mapagkakatiwalaan; matatag at maaaring sandigan o pagkunan ng suporta.
original_explanation: Your one friend who actually shows up on time when you agree to meet. The Wi-Fi connection that doesn't die in the middle of your Zoom presentation. It's something or someone you can bet your last load on. The human equivalent of a power bank.
usage_notes: A formal and somewhat rare word. 'Mapagkakatiwalaan' or 'maaasahan' are more common synonyms.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng isang lider na **masalig** at tapat sa kanyang tungkulin.","translation":"We need a leader who is **trustworthy** and true to his duty."},{"sentence":"Ang Saligang Batas ay dapat maging isang dokumentong **masalig** para sa lahat ng mamamayan.","translation":"The Constitution should be a **dependable** document for all citizens."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na hindi propesyonal o kulang sa kasanayan sa isang partikular na gawain; isang baguhan.
original_explanation: 'Yung tropa mong sumali sa singing contest pero sintunado. O 'yung nag-volunteer mag-ayos ng computer mo pero mas lalo lang nasira. Basically, someone doing it for the "love of the game" (or just for fun), not for a paycheck. Not a pro. Amatyur level pa lang.
usage_notes: Often used with a slightly derogatory or humorous tone to describe a lack of skill. Can also function as a noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Amatyur** pa lang ako sa pagluluto kaya pasensya na kung hindi masarap.","translation":"I'm still an **amateur** at cooking, so I'm sorry if it's not delicious."},{"sentence":"Kitang-kita sa gawa niya na **amatyur** pa lang siya.","translation":"It's obvious from his work that he is still an **amateur**."}]

translation: to give a percentage to; to calculate the percentage of
meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng isang tiyak na bahagdan o porsiyento; kalkulahin ang porsiyento ng isang kabuuan.
original_explanation: 'Yung usapan niyo ng ahente mo sa commission. "Okay, **porsiyentuhan** mo na lang ako sa benta." o 'yung ginagawa ng boss mo sa performance bonus niyo. Basically, the act of getting or giving a cut based on a percentage.
usage_notes: Often used in business, sales, or commission-based contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **porsiyentuhan** ang bawat ahente batay sa kanilang benta.","translation":"You need to **give a percentage to** each agent based on their sales."},{"sentence":"**Porsiyentuhan** natin ang kabuuang kita para malaman ang buwis.","translation":"Let's **calculate the percentage of** the total income to determine the tax."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian na napakalinaw, hayag, o madaling mapansin; nangingibabaw.
original_explanation: When something is so obvious it might as well be floating in front of your face with a neon sign. 'Lutang na lutang ang pagka-in love niya sa'yo, 'di mo lang makita.' It means something is prominent, conspicuous, and undeniable. It’s not just visible; it’s practically screaming for attention.
usage_notes: This is a reduplication of 'lutang' but carries a different common meaning from the 'distracted' sense. It emphasizes prominence or obviousness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lutang na lutang** ang galing niya sa pagkanta kumpara sa ibang kalahok.","translation":"Her skill in singing is **very prominent** compared to the other contestants."}]

translation: to bow, to stoop, to duck
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbaba ng ulo o pagbaluktot ng katawan bilang tanda ng paggalang, pag-iwas, o pagkuha ng isang bagay na mababa.
original_explanation: This is your everyday bow. You do this to say 'po' to your lola, to duck under a low-hanging sampayan, or when you drop your phone for the nth time. It can be a sign of respect, or just a physical action to not bump your head. Parang 'pag nakita mo 'yung ex mo with their new partner, biglang **yumuko** ka at nag-pretend na may tinitingnan sa phone.
usage_notes: A very common verb. Can be used literally (physical action) or figuratively (to bow to pressure).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Yumuko** siya bilang paggalang sa mga nakatatanda.","translation":"He **bowed** as a sign of respect to the elders."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **yumuko** para hindi mauntog ang ulo mo sa pinto.","translation":"You need to **duck** so you don't hit your head on the door."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain o isport ng pagdulas sa ibabaw ng yelo o sa isang patag na ibabaw gamit ang sapatos na may gulong (roller skates) o talim (ice skates).
original_explanation: That graceful (or not-so-graceful) activity you do at the mall's ice rink or along the seaside baywalk. Isketing is 50% gliding like a pro and 50% trying not to fall on your butt in front of your crush.
usage_notes: Can refer to both ice skating and roller skating. Context usually clarifies which.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Niyaya niya akong mag-**isketing** sa bagong bukas na rink.","translation":"He/She invited me to go **skating** at the newly opened rink."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marka o hugis ng isang bagay na nakikita o nararamdaman sa ibabaw ng isa pang bagay; pagiging kitang-kita ng isang bagay sa ilalim ng damit.
original_explanation: That awkward moment when the outline of your underwear is visible through your leggings (VPL - Visible Panty Line). Or the mark your watch leaves on your wrist after a long day. It’s an imprint, a trace that’s clearly visible, whether you want it to be or not. 'Uy, bakat!' is the friendly warning you get from a true friend.
usage_notes: Can also function as a noun meaning 'an imprint' or 'a mark'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bakat** ang tahi ng unan sa kanyang pisngi.","translation":"The seam of the pillow was **imprinted** on her cheek."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa isusuot mo, baka maging **bakat**.","translation":"Be careful with what you wear, it might **show through**."}]

translation: having a torn or clipped earlobe
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tainga na may punit, gupit, o kakulangan sa bahagi, lalo na sa ibabang bahagi nito (earlobe).
original_explanation: You know when an earring gets snagged and rips your earlobe a little? That's `pingod`. Or when someone has a part of their earlobe missing from a fight or an accident. It's a very specific kind of 'tenga' situation. Not to be confused with `pingot`, which is the action of pulling the ear.
usage_notes: Describes the state of an ear, usually as a result of an injury.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **pingod** ang kanyang tainga dahil sa aksidente.","translation":"His ear became **torn at the lobe** because of the accident."},{"sentence":"Kilala ang aso sa pagiging **pingod** ng kaliwang tainga nito.","translation":"The dog is known for its **clipped** left ear."}]

translation: to be bruised; to get a contusion
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng pasa o galos sa balat dahil sa pagkakabangga o pagkahampas, na nagreresulta sa pamumuo ng dugo sa ilalim nito.
original_explanation: That moment when you bump into a table corner and a day later, you have a souvenir. It's your skin's way of keeping a colorful, painful memory of your 'lampa' moments.
usage_notes: Refers to the process of a bruise forming. More common to just say 'magkapasa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siguradong **mamumugo** ang binti niya matapos matamaan ng bola.","translation":"His leg will surely **get bruised** after being hit by the ball."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa pag-akyat, baka ka mahulog at **mamugo**.","translation":"Be careful climbing, you might fall and **get bruised**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagkakaroon ng matatag na pasya o layunin; ang pagiging desididong makamit ang isang bagay sa kabila ng mga hadlang.
original_explanation: That 'Walang makakapigil sa akin!' (Nobody can stop me!) feeling. It's what fuels you to finish your thesis, to lose weight for summer, or to line up for 8 hours for a K-Pop concert ticket. The power source of every aspiring Pinoy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **determinasyon**, natapos niya ang pag-aaral kahit mahirap ang buhay.","translation":"Because of her **determination**, she finished her studies despite life's hardships."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng matinding **determinasyon** para manalo sa kumpetisyon.","translation":"You need strong **determination** to win the competition."}]

translation: to string (an instrument); to put strings on
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng mga kuwerdas sa isang instrumentong pangmusika, tulad ng gitara.
original_explanation: This is what you do to your guitar after you've played 'Wonderwall' so many times one of the strings snaps in protest. It's the act of replacing or installing the very things that make the music happen. Also, a metaphor for getting things in order or preparing something, like 'magkuwerdas ng plano' (to string a plan together).
usage_notes: Primarily used for musical instruments like guitars, violins, and ukuleles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko nang **magkuwerdas** ng bago sa gitara ko dahil naputol ang isa.","translation":"I need to **put new strings** on my guitar because one broke."},{"sentence":"Marunong ka bang **magkuwerdas** ng ukelele?","translation":"Do you know how to **string** a ukelele?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagbabahagi ng teksto, larawan, o video sa isang social media platform o website.
original_explanation: The modern-day "chismis" but with receipts (screenshots). If it wasn't posted, did it even happen? From your OOTD, to your "woke up like this" selfie, to your rant about traffic—if you share it online, you "post" it. Remember: think before you post, the internet is forever.
usage_notes: Extremely common in the digital age. Often conjugated using Filipino affixes, e.g., "nag-post", "i-post", "pino-post".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong i-**post** 'yang picture na 'yan, ang pangit ko diyan!","translation":"Don't **post** that picture, I look ugly there!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapatigil sa operasyon o pag-access; ang paglalapat ng takip, pinto, o bintana upang hindi na ito bukas.
original_explanation: What every store does at 9 PM, and what you wish your chismosa neighbor would do with her mouth. Also the command form you yell at your sibling: 'Magsara ka ng pinto!'
usage_notes: Can refer to closing a physical object (door, window) or a business/operation. This is the infinitive/imperative form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan na nating **magsara** ng tindahan dahil gabi na.","translation":"We need to **close** the store now because it's already night."},{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **magsara** ka ng bintana dahil lumalamig.","translation":"Please, **close** the window because it's getting cold."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking sundalo na binabayaran upang lumaban para sa isang dayuhang hukbo o grupo. Sa malawak na kahulugan, isang taong gumagawa ng isang bagay para lamang sa pera.
original_explanation: A soldier of fortune. This guy fights for whoever signs the check. In modern slang, you might call someone a 'mersenaryo' if their loyalty is purely transactional, like a basketball player who jumps to whichever team offers the biggest contract, regardless of team history.
usage_notes: Can be used for both the literal soldier-for-hire and figuratively for someone motivated solely by money. It is also used as a general term for mercenary regardless of gender.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha sila ng mga **mersenaryo** upang palakasin ang kanilang puwersa.","translation":"They hired **mercenaries** to strengthen their forces."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **mersenaryo** sa pag-ibig.","translation":"Don't be a **mercenary** in love."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pag-uugnay o pagkakabit ng dalawa o higit pang bagay upang maging isa o magkaroon ng karugtong.
original_explanation: Parang pag-assemble ng DIY furniture from Shopee, but for stories. It's what you do when you're trying to make sense of all the chismis from different Marites sources. "Teka, i-connect natin ang mga pangyayari..."
usage_notes: Refers to the act of physically or figuratively connecting things, such as wires, pieces of a story, or ideas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahusay siya sa **pagdudugtong** ng mga putol na kable ng kuryente.","translation":"He is skilled at **joining** broken electrical cables."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagdudugtong** sa mga nakaraang kaganapan ang susi sa paglutas ng misteryo.","translation":"The **linking** of past events is the key to solving the mystery."}]

translation: to buy for someone; to buy from someone/somewhere
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa ng pagbili ng isang bagay para sa kapakanan ng iba, o ang pagbili mula sa isang partikular na tao o lugar.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "pasabuy" verb. When your friend goes to Japan, you say "Bilhan mo ako ng KitKat!" (Buy me some KitKat!). It's also used for the source: "Bilhan natin si Aling Nena ng isda." (Let's buy fish from Aling Nena). It's a verb of transaction focused on the beneficiary or the source, not just the item.
usage_notes: The focus of the action is on the person being bought for (beneficiary) or the place/person being bought from (locative). Contrast with 'bilhin' which focuses on the object being bought.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bilhan** mo naman ako ng kape pagdaan mo sa coffee shop.","translation":"**Buy** me some coffee when you pass by the coffee shop."},{"sentence":"Saan ba puwedeng **bilhan** ng murang gulay?","translation":"Where can one **buy** cheap vegetables **from**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Minamahal nang lubos; ang taong pinag-uukulan ng matinding pagmamahal o pagtingin. Ginagamit din bilang pandiwa na nangangahulugang 'minamahal'.
original_explanation: This is some next-level 'lodi' or 'crush'. It's what your lolo called your lola in his harana days. If you call someone your 'ginigiliw,' you're not just 'in a relationship,' you're in a full-blown kundiman love song. It's the OG term for 'bae.'
usage_notes: Often found in classic songs, poems, and formal declarations of love. 'Ginigiliw kita' means 'I cherish you' or 'I adore you'. It can be used as an adjective (aking ginigiliw - my beloved) or a verb (siya ay ginigiliw ng lahat - he is loved by all).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ikaw ang aking **ginigiliw**, O aking sinta.","translation":"You are my **beloved**, oh my love."},{"sentence":"Siya ay **ginigiliw** ng kanyang mga lolo at lola dahil sa kanyang kabaitan.","translation":"She is **cherished** by her grandparents because of her kindness."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malawak at patag na kalupaan sa ilalim ng dagat.
etymology: A compound phrase from `kapatagan` (plain, flatland) and `dagat` (sea).
original_explanation: Basically, the Earth's underwater 'semento'. It's where Spongebob's pineapple is located, where sunken treasures are rumored to be, and where all your deep, dark secrets (and maybe that phone you dropped on a boat trip) go to rest. The ultimate 'ilalim'.
usage_notes: A descriptive, somewhat technical term. 'Sahig ng dagat' (floor of the sea) is a more common equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-aaral ang mga siyentipiko tungkol sa mga nilalang na nabubuhay sa **kapatagan ng dagat**.","translation":"Scientists are studying the creatures that live on the **seabed**."},{"sentence":"Maraming misteryo ang nakatago sa malalim na **kapatagan ng dagat**.","translation":"Many mysteries are hidden on the deep **ocean floor**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaki na mahilig sa mga abentura, o isang lalaki na naghahanap ng kapalaran o tagumpay sa pamamagitan ng mapangahas na mga gawain.
original_explanation: The guy version of the abenturera. He's got a well-worn backpack, a tan line that never fades, and a collection of stories that usually start with "This one time in Sagada...". He's your 'Indiana Jones' or 'Nathan Drake' ng Pinas. In the world of love, he's the guy who's afraid of commitment because he's "not ready to settle down yet" and has "more mountains to climb." #wanderlust
usage_notes: The male counterpart to 'abenturera'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga sinaunang mandaragat ay mga tunay na **abenturero**.","translation":"The ancient sailors were true **adventurers**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala sa **abenturero** na 'yan, puro salita lang 'yan.","translation":"Don't believe that **adventurer**, he's all talk."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang kagamitan na ginagamit sa paglalagay ng kulay.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `pang-` at `kolor` (mula sa Espanyol na *color*).
original_explanation: This is anything you use to make life less black and white. Your kid's crayons, your hair dye, the food coloring for your ube cake, the felt-tip pens for your adult coloring book to de-stress from work. If its purpose is to add color, it's 'pangkolor'.
usage_notes: Maaari ring gumana bilang pang-uri ("lapis na pangkolor"). Ang salitang 'pangkulay' ay mas karaniwang ginagamit at itinuturing na mas pormal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng bagong set ng **pangkolor** para sa proyekto ko.","translation":"Mom bought a new set of **coloring materials** for my project."},{"sentence":"Pahiram naman ako ng **pangkolor** mo, naiwan ko kasi ang sa akin.","translation":"Can I borrow your **coloring materials**? I left mine behind."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng daan na naka-angat at nakalaan para sa mga taong naglalakad.
original_explanation: The Philippines' version of a multi-purpose hall. It's a walkway, a parking spot for motorcycles, a dining area for street food vendors, a playground for kids, and the prime spot for the neighborhood chismisan. Walking on it is an obstacle course.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap maglakad sa **bangketa** dahil puno ito ng mga paninda.","translation":"It's hard to walk on the **sidewalk** because it's full of vendors' stalls."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katawagan para sa isang lalaking itinuturing na kaakit-akit, may tiwala sa sarili, at matagumpay; hango sa isang sikat na internet meme.
etymology: From the English internet slang 'Chad,' which originated from online forums like 4chan and Reddit.
original_explanation: The internet's ultimate alpha male, now imported into Pinoy slang. A 'Chad' is the guy who's conventionally handsome, probably has a gym membership, and doesn't get left on 'seen.' He's the guy your tita wishes you were dating instead of your e-boy boyfriend. The opposite of an 'incel'.
usage_notes: A relatively new addition to Filipino slang, primarily used by younger, internet-savvy generations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang maging isang **Chad** na habulin ng mga babae.","translation":"He dreams of becoming a **Chad** who is chased by women."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mahiya, mag-effort ka para maging **Chad** ng buhay niya.","translation":"Don't be shy, make an effort to be the **Chad** of her life."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging mapagtanong at may pagnanais na matuto o malaman ang mga bagay-bagay.
original_explanation: This is the official term for being a 'chismoso/chismosa,' but with a diploma. It's the urge that makes you click on 'link in bio,' read the comments section of a viral post, or ask your friend 'so anong nangyari?' It can lead to great scientific discoveries or just finding out who your neighbor's new visitor is. The energy of a true 'Marites.'
usage_notes: Can be neutral (intellectual curiosity) or slightly negative (being nosy).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagkamausisa** ang nagtulak sa kanya na maging isang siyentipiko.","translation":"His **curiosity** is what pushed him to become a scientist."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko mapigilan ang aking **pagkamausisa** kung ano ang laman ng kahon.","translation":"I can't stop my **inquisitiveness** about what's inside the box."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng dinamita upang pasabugin, wasakin, o sirain ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: Ang action-movie version ng pag-solve ng problema. May malaking bato sa daan? Dinamitahin! May building na kailangang gibain? Dinamitahin! Pero sa totoong buhay, 'wag basta-basta mag-dinamitahin ng feelings ng iba. Explosive results, promise.
usage_notes: A verb indicating the action of using dynamite.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Plano nilang **dinamitahin** ang lumang gusali para magtayo ng bago.","translation":"They plan **to dynamite** the old building to construct a new one."},{"sentence":"Ilegal na **dinamitahin** ang mga bahura para sa pangingisda.","translation":"It is illegal **to dynamite** coral reefs for fishing."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-iwan ng isang mahalagang bagay bilang kolateral o garantiya para sa isang utang.
original_explanation: The national sport during 'petsa de peligro' (the days before payday). When your wallet is crying and your ATM is judging you, you **magsangla** your lola's necklace at the nearest pawnshop. It's basically a short-term loan from a place with a name like 'Cebuana' or 'Palawan'.
usage_notes: Commonly associated with pawnshops and financial hardship.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napilitan siyang **magsangla** ng kanyang singsing para sa matrikula ng anak.","translation":"She was forced to **pawn** her ring for her child's tuition."},{"sentence":"Babalik ako bukas para **magsangla** nitong laptop, kailangan ko lang ng pera ngayon.","translation":"I will come back tomorrow to **pawn** this laptop, I just need money now."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang di-pormal na termino para sa isang kapansin-pansin at positibong pagbabago sa pisikal na anyo, kumpiyansa, o pangkalahatang estado ng isang tao.
original_explanation: 'Yung transformation mo from "duckling" to "swan." Dati laging napagkakamalang pamangkin, ngayon tinititigan na. It's that major upgrade in looks, confidence, and overall vibe, usually after a difficult period. The ultimate "look at me now" moment.
usage_notes: Isang napakatanyag na modernong salitang balbal, lalo na sa mga nakababatang henerasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita mo ba 'yung **glow up** ni Liza Soberano mula pagkabata?","translation":"Have you seen Liza Soberano's **glow up** since she was a child?"},{"sentence":"Ang pag-aalaga sa sarili ang sikreto sa aking **glow up**.","translation":"Self-care is the secret to my **glow up**."}]

translation: a Filipino dish cooked in vinegar
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng lutuing Pilipino kung saan ang karne o isda ay niluluto sa suka, bawang, at paminta, at kung minsan ay may kasamang luya o sili.
etymology: Isang katutubong paraan ng pagluluto sa Pilipinas; hindi tiyak ang pinagmulan ng salita.
original_explanation: The ultimate "pampagana" dish! It’s that sour, savory ulam that makes you get extra rice. Whether it’s 'Paksiw na Isda' (fish) or 'Lechon Paksiw' (roasted pork), it's the magical dish that transforms leftovers into a whole new level of deliciousness. The signature sour kick from the vinegar is what makes it uniquely Pinoy.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa paraan ng pagluluto at sa mismong ulam. Iba sa 'adobo' na gumagamit din ng suka ngunit may toyo bilang pambalanse.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-uwi si nanay ng **paksiw** na bangus mula sa palengke.","translation":"Mom brought home **paksiw** na bangus (milkfish cooked in vinegar) from the market."},{"sentence":"Ang natirang lechon ay ginawang **paksiw** para hindi masira.","translation":"The leftover roasted pig was made into **lechon paksiw** so it wouldn't spoil."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahabang tungkod, karaniwang yari sa kahoy, yantok, o metal, na ginagamit bilang suporta sa paglakad o bilang sandata sa arnis.
original_explanation: Your lolo's walking accessory, which doubles as a pointer, a dog-shooer, and a threat when you're being makulit. In the world of Arnis, it's not for support, it's for delivering a world of hurt.
usage_notes: Can refer to a medical walking cane, a conductor's baton, or the rattan stick used in Filipino martial arts (arnis/eskrima).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumagamit ng **baston** ang aking lolo para makalakad nang maayos.","translation":"My grandfather uses a **cane** to walk properly."},{"sentence":"Mabilis magpaikot ng **baston** ang mga nagsasanay ng Arnis.","translation":"The Arnis practitioners can twirl the **stick** quickly."}]

meaning_filipino: Patigilin ang pagdurugo o pag-agos ng likido, karaniwan sa pamamagitan ng pagdiin o paglalagay ng gamot.
original_explanation: Before there were Band-Aids and first aid kits, you had to `ampatin` the wound. It’s the old-school way of saying 'stop the bleeding!' – something you'd hear from a village elder, not a modern doctor. The O.G. first aid verb.
usage_notes: Isang luma at hindi na gaanong ginagamit na salita, karaniwang matatagpuan sa mga lumang panitikan o sa mga malalim na diyalekto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha siya ng dahon ng bayabas upang **ampatin** ang sugat sa kanyang tuhod.","translation":"He got a guava leaf to **stanch** the wound on his knee."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng nars na **ampatin** ang malakas na pagdurugo ng pasyente.","translation":"The nurse tried to **stop the bleeding** of the patient."}]

translation: to do a somersault; to tumble
meaning_filipino: Isagawa ang pag-ikot ng katawan nang pauna o patalikod, karaniwang nagsisimula sa paa at nagtatapos sa paa.
original_explanation: That cool trick you tried to do as a kid and probably ended up with a bump on your head. Gymnasts do this gracefully; the rest of us look like a sack of potatoes falling down the stairs.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kaya pa rin ng matanda na **magbabalintong** na parang bata.","translation":"The old man can still **do a somersault** like a child."}]

translation: to be able to touch or hold
meaning_filipino: Magawang mahawakan, masakop, o makapa ang isang bagay. Ito ay isang anyo ng pandiwa na nagmula sa salitang-ugat na 'kapa'.
etymology: From 'ma-' prefix + 'kapa' (to grope, feel for) + '-an' suffix.
original_explanation: That moment when you're fumbling in the dark for the light switch, and you finally feel it. 'Ayun! Mekapan ko na!' Also what your lola says when she finally gets to hold her apo (grandchild) for the first time. It's about finally making contact.
usage_notes: This is an archaic or dialectal form. The more common modern equivalent is 'makapa' or 'mahawakan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa dilim ng kuwarto, buti na lang at **mekapan** niya ang kaniyang salamin.","translation":"In the darkness of the room, it's a good thing he was **able to feel for** his glasses."},{"sentence":"Napakaliit ng butas kaya hindi **mekapan** ng kaniyang daliri ang turnilyo.","translation":"The hole is so small that his finger **can't touch** the screw."}]

translation: to inflame; to intensify; to arouse passion
meaning_filipino: Palakasin o pataasin ang sidhi ng isang damdamin, tulad ng galit, pag-ibig, o sigasig. Ito ay ang pagpapaliyab o pagpapasiklab sa isang bagay na dati nang naroroon.
original_explanation: This is what a good motivational speaker does to a sleepy audience. It's what a 'Marites' does to a small issue, turning it into a full-blown barangay-level drama. It's when a sweet gesture from your crush turns your simple 'like' into a blazing 'I-must-have-you' inferno. It's the 'extra rice' of feelings.
usage_notes: Used figuratively for emotions and abstract concepts like nationalism or anger. The root 'alab' means blaze or ardor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ng lider ang kanyang talumpati upang **pag-alabin** ang diwang makabayan ng mga tao.","translation":"The leader used his speech to **inflame** the patriotic spirit of the people."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong lalong **pag-alabin** ang galit ko.","translation":"Don't further **inflame** my anger."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao, bagay, o kilos na nagpapakita ng katangian ng isang aristokrata o maharlika; marangya, elegante, at may mataas na katayuan sa lipunan.
original_explanation: Yung friend mong ayaw kumain sa karinderya at gusto lagi sa fine dining. Medyo "conyo" at parang laging naka-aircon ang kilos. They have that "old money" vibe, kahit minsan utang lang sa credit card.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit upang ilarawan ang pamumuhay, pananamit, o kilos ng mayayamang tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahahalata sa kanyang pananalita at kilos ang kanyang **aristokratikong** pinagmulan.","translation":"You can tell his **aristocratic** origins from his speech and actions."},{"sentence":"Nagsuot siya ng damit na may **aristokratikong** disenyo para sa party.","translation":"She wore a dress with an **aristocratic** design for the party."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang simbolo (+) na ginagamit sa matematika upang ipahiwatig ang operasyon ng adisyon o pagsasama-sama ng mga bilang.
original_explanation: The 'plus sign' in math. It’s that little cross that tells you to add things up, whether it's your expenses for the month, the number of tasks your boss gave you, or the reasons why you should probably just stay in bed.
usage_notes: This is a specific mathematical term. `Pagdaragdag` is from the root `dagdag` (add).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isulat mo ang **tanda ng pagdaragdag** sa pagitan ng dalawang numero.","translation":"Write the **plus sign** between the two numbers."},{"sentence":"Ang 2 + 2 ay gumagamit ng **tanda ng pagdaragdag**.","translation":"2 + 2 uses the **plus sign**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng tela na inilalatag sa ibabaw ng kutson ng isang kama. Karaniwang tinatawag ding kobrekama.
original_explanation: The final boss of laundry day. That thin piece of fabric you fight with every morning when you try to make your bed, only to mess it up again at night. In the Philippines, we often just say "bedsheet" instead of "kobrekama" because, let's be real, it's faster.
usage_notes: Bagama't may salitang Filipino na "kobrekama", mas madalas gamitin ang salitang Ingles na "bedsheet" sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakipalitan naman ang **bedsheet** sa kuwarto, marumi na.","translation":"Please change the **bedsheet** in the room, it's already dirty."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na bangka o sasakyang pantubig na walang katig, karaniwang ginagamit sa mga ilog o lawa.
original_explanation: Before GrabCar, there was the lunday. It's a small, simple boat, like a canoe. Think of the boats you see in paintings of old Philippine riversides. It's the acoustic, unplugged version of a speedboat.
usage_notes: A more traditional or literary term. 'Bangka' is more common in everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ng mangingisda ang kanyang **lunday** upang tumawid sa ilog.","translation":"The fisherman used his **small boat** to cross the river."},{"sentence":"Payapang umaagos ang **lunday** sa gitna ng lawa.","translation":"The **canoe** peacefully glides in the middle of the lake."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa kalagayan ng mga bagay o tao na magkakalapit o halos walang pagitan.
original_explanation: The state of things in the MRT during rush hour. Your house, your neighbor's house, and their neighbor's house in a typical Manila subdivision. Also, kanin na hindi nabuhaghag nang maayos.
usage_notes: Emphasizes the closeness or lack of space between multiple items or people, often with a sense of being cluttered or crowded.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dikit-dikit** ang mga bahay sa lugar na iyon.","translation":"The houses in that area are **packed together**."},{"sentence":"Ayusin mo ang sinaing, **dikit-dikit** pa ang kanin.","translation":"Fix the steamed rice, the grains are still **clumped together**."}]

meaning_filipino: (Balbal) Isang salitang walang pormal na kahulugan na tumutukoy sa kalipunan ng mga bagay na nakakainis, walang kwenta, o pagyayabang.
etymology: Likely a humorous or slang formation from `ka-` + `burot` (slang for 'annoying', 'boastful', or 'bloated') + `-an`.
original_explanation: "Ang dami mong kaburutan!" is like saying "You're full of it!" or "Stop with all your nonsense!". It's a made-up-sounding word that means 'a collection of annoying/boastful acts'. You'd use it with friends when someone is being extra 'mahangin' or telling a story that's clearly exaggerated.
usage_notes: Highly informal and not a standard dictionary word. Its meaning is derived entirely from context and the slang usage of its root "burot".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na nga 'yang mga **kaburutan** mo, wala namang naniniwala sa'yo.","translation":"Just stop with all your **nonsense**, no one believes you anyway."},{"sentence":"Puro **kaburutan** lang ang alam ng taong 'yan, mahilig magyabang.","translation":"That person is only full of **boastful talk**, loves to brag."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang gawain ay durugin o pulbusin ang isang bagay, tulad ng bigas o pampalasa, gamit ang pandikdik at lusong.
original_explanation: The original human food processor. Before blenders, you had the 'tagadikdik' with their trusty mortar and pestle ('lusong at pandikdik'). They're the reason your lola's adobo has perfectly crushed garlic, not just sliced. The rhythmic sound of their work was the original kitchen ASMR.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magaling ang **tagadikdik** ng paminta sa palengke.","translation":"The pepper **pounder** at the market is good."},{"sentence":"Kinakailangan ng lakas ng braso ng isang **tagadikdik**.","translation":"A **pounder** needs arm strength."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa posisyong nakayuko ang ulo, karaniwang nagpapahiwatig ng kalungkutan, hiya, o paggalang.
original_explanation: 'Yung itsura mo kapag napagalitan ka ng boss mo sa harap ng lahat. Or when you're trying to avoid eye contact with someone you owe money to. Nakatungo is the universal sign for "I'm shy," "I'm sad," or "Please don't talk to me right now." It's having your head bowed down.
usage_notes: The context determines if it's due to shyness, sadness, respect, or shame.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nanatili siyang **nakatungo** habang pinapagalitan.","translation":"He remained with his **head bowed** while being scolded."},{"sentence":"Naglakad siyang **nakatungo** dahil sa hiya.","translation":"He walked while **looking down** because of shame."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging hindi mapakali, balisa, o pagkabalisa dahil sa isang bagay o sitwasyon.
etymology: Mula sa 'di' (not) at 'pagkapalagay' (state of being at ease).
original_explanation: That feeling when you've sent a risky text and it's been 'seen' for an hour with no reply. The social anxiety you get when you're the first one to arrive at a party. 'Yan ang di pagkapalagay. Parang laging may utang.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang pakiramdam ng pag-aalala, pag-aalinlangan, o pangkalahatang pakiramdam na mayroong mali.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **di pagkapalagay** akong nararamdaman tungkol sa bagong kasosyo niya.","translation":"I feel a sense of **uneasiness** about her new business partner."},{"sentence":"Kitang-kita sa mukha niya ang **di pagkapalagay** habang hinihintay ang resulta ng exam.","translation":"His **anxiety** was evident on his face while waiting for the exam results."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang koleksyon ng mga litrato at video na sabay-sabay na ipino-post sa social media, kadalasan sa Instagram, na walang iisang tema o caption, upang ibahagi ang mga sandali mula sa isang partikular na panahon.
original_explanation: The official term for 'I have too many random pics from the weekend and my camera roll is full.' It's the social media equivalent of throwing all your laundry on a chair. You post a mix of selfies, food pics, blurry concert videos, and a random shot of your cat. The caption is almost always just 'photo dump,' 'late post,' or an emoji. Zero effort, maximum content.
usage_notes: Isang popular na trend sa Instagram at iba pang visual social media platforms.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-post siya ng isang **photodump** mula sa kanilang bakasyon sa La Union.","translation":"She posted a **photo dump** from their vacation in La Union."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa Rotary International, isang pandaigdigang organisasyon ng serbisyo na ang layunin ay pagsama-samahin ang mga lider sa negosyo at propesyonal upang magbigay ng serbisyong pangkawanggawa.
original_explanation: This is the club where the Rotarians hang out. When you see a big wheel logo on a welcome arch to a town or on a waiting shed, that's a project by the local Rotary Club. It's like the Avengers, but for community service projects instead of fighting aliens.
usage_notes: Almost always refers to the Rotary Club International.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumali siya sa **Rotary** upang makatulong sa kapwa.","translation":"He joined **Rotary** to help others."},{"sentence":"Ang proyektong ito ay pinondohan ng **Rotary** Club of Manila.","translation":"This project was funded by the **Rotary** Club of Manila."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian o kalagayan ng pagiging isang diyos; pagka-diyos o kabanalan.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate level-up. It's not just being good, it's having that divine, god-tier energy. Think Zeus, Bathala, or that feeling you get when your crush finally replies. It's the highest form of 'Sana all.'
usage_notes: A very formal and literary word. Not used in daily conversation, primarily found in religious or philosophical texts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan sa teolohiya ang **kadiyusan** ni Hesukristo.","translation":"Theology studies the **divinity** of Jesus Christ."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang kagandahan ay tila may taglay na **kadiyusan**.","translation":"Her beauty seemed to possess a certain **godliness**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sasakyang pang-transportasyon na may dalawang gulong at hinihila ng isang kabayo, na karaniwang ginagamit noong unang panahon at ngayon ay pangunahing atraksyon para sa mga turista.
original_explanation: The original GrabCar of the Spanish colonial era. Now, it's the ride you take in Intramuros or Vigan to feel like a character from a historical drama. The ride is slow, a bit bumpy, and smells faintly of horse, but hey, it's for the 'gram.
usage_notes: Mostly found in tourist spots like Intramuros (Manila) and Vigan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasiyahan ang mga turista sa kanilang pagsakay sa **kalesa** sa Vigan.","translation":"The tourists enjoyed their **horse-drawn carriage** ride in Vigan."},{"sentence":"Ang tunog ng mga kabayong humihila ng **kalesa** ay bahagi ng kagandahan ng Intramuros.","translation":"The sound of the horses pulling the **kalesa** is part of the charm of Intramuros."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na pag-anib o pagiging kasapi sa isang samahan, grupo, o asosasyon.
original_explanation: It's like clicking the 'Join Group' button on Facebook, but in real life. When you decide to **magsapi** in a school club, a religious organization, or even a secret society (ooh, mysterious!), you're officially becoming a member. It's about committing to a group.
usage_notes: More specific than 'sumama' (to go with). 'Magsapi' implies formal membership.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming kabataan ang gustong **magsapi** sa aming organisasyon para sa kalikasan.","translation":"Many young people want to **join** our organization for the environment."},{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **magsapi** sa isang kooperatiba upang makakuha ng benepisyo.","translation":"He decided to **become a member** of a cooperative to get benefits."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumigil sa pag-iyak o pagluha.
etymology: From `ma-` (ability/involuntary action prefix) + `tahan` (stop, cease, specifically crying).
original_explanation: That moment when your friend finally stops ugly-crying over their ex after you've bribed them with milk tea and fries. "Ayan, na-matahan din sa wakas." It's the calm after the emotional storm, the ceasefire of tears.
usage_notes: Often used to comfort a crying child or person. The 'ma-' prefix suggests an ability or a state being achieved.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi **matahan** sa pag-iyak ang bata kahit anong gawin ng ina.","translation":"The child couldn't **stop crying** no matter what the mother did."},{"sentence":"Bigyan mo ng laruan para **matahan** na siya.","translation":"Give him a toy so he will **stop crying**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagdudulot ng pinsala, kapahamakan, o negatibong epekto sa kalusugan, kalagayan, o reputasyon.
original_explanation: Like eating instant noodles for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. Or doomscrolling on social media until 3 AM. Or hanging out with "toxic" friends. Anything that's bad for your physical, mental, or emotional health is **nakasasama**. It's the opposite of what your nanay would recommend.
usage_notes: The 'nakasasa-' prefix indicates the ability or tendency to cause something bad or harmful. Can refer to health, well-being, or morality.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang labis na pag-inom ng alak ay **nakasasama** sa atay.","translation":"Excessive drinking of alcohol is **harmful** to the liver."},{"sentence":"Ang pagkakalat ng maling impormasyon ay **nakasasama** sa lipunan.","translation":"Spreading false information is **bad for** society."}]

translation: to harden one's heart; to be resolute
meaning_filipino: Panindigan ang sariling desisyon o damdamin at hindi magpadala sa pakiusap o emosyon ng iba; magmatigas.
etymology: Compound word from 'tigas' (hard) and 'loob' (inside, will, spirit).
original_explanation: This is you when your friend asks to borrow money for the 5th time this month and you finally say no. It's that 'pasensya na, pero hindi na talaga pwede' moment. It's not about being mean, it's about setting boundaries, even if it feels tough. You **harden your heart** for your own sanity (and wallet).
usage_notes: Can have both a positive connotation (being resolute, firm) and a negative one (being unfeeling, stubborn). Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit anong pakiusap, pinili niyang **magtigas-loob** at hindi magpatawad.","translation":"Despite all the pleas, he chose **to harden his heart** and not forgive."},{"sentence":"Kinailangan niyang **magtigas-loob** para malampasan ang mga pagsubok sa buhay.","translation":"She needed **to be resolute** to overcome the challenges in life."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbabantay o pagmamasid sa isang tao, bagay, o lugar upang maprotektahan ito o tiyaking nasa maayos na kalagayan.
original_explanation: This is what the security guard at the mall is doing, even if he looks like he's just scrolling on his phone. It's what your overprotective jowa does when you go out with friends. "Sino kasama mo? Saan kayo pupunta? Anong oras uwi mo?" That's a form of "pagtatanod." It's the continuous action of watching over something or someone. Parang CCTV na may feelings.
usage_notes: Present progressive tense of the verb "tanuran" (to guard). The root "tanod" means guard.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga sundalo ay mahigpit na **tinatanuran** ang hangganan ng bansa.","translation":"The soldiers are strictly **guarding** the country's border."},{"sentence":"Siya ang **tinatanuran** ng mga pulis dahil isa siyang mahalagang saksi.","translation":"He is being **watched over** by the police because he is an important witness."}]

translation: to divide among several people; to share something
meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay o sama-samang pagbabahagi ng isang bagay sa maraming tao o pangkat.
original_explanation: This is the group project version of 'paghati'. It's when you and your barkada get one large pizza and everyone has to share. "Paghati-hatian natin 'tong bayarin sa kuryente, besh, para 'di masakit." It implies a collective action of dividing something for everyone to get a piece.
usage_notes: Verb in the infinitive form. It focuses on the group of people who will receive the shares of the divided object.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **paghati-hatian** ang mga natirang pagkain.","translation":"We need **to share** the leftover food among ourselves."},{"sentence":"Pinaghati-hatian ng mga magnanakaw ang kanilang mga nakuha.","translation":"The thieves **divided** their loot among themselves."}]

translation: (the one/place) from which something was bought
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa tao, pook, o entidad kung saan nagmula ang isang bagay na binili.
original_explanation: The suki tindera at the palengke, the Shopee store you got your latest budol, or the friend you bought that pre-loved item from. It's the source of your purchase, the origin story of your new 'kagamitan'.
usage_notes: A locative/benefactive-focus verb in the completed aspect. It points to the source of the transaction, not the item bought.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Suki na namin ang tindahan na **napagbilhan** ko nitong bigas.","translation":"The store from which I **bought** this rice is already our regular."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **napagbilhan** mo ng masarap na longganisang ito?","translation":"From whom **did you buy** this delicious sausage?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang buong baboy na niluto sa ibabaw ng nagbabagang uling, dahan-dahang iniikot sa isang kawayan o metal na tuhugan hanggang sa maging malutong ang balat.
original_explanation: The undisputed king of any Filipino fiesta, Noche Buena, or major celebration. If you see a letson at a party, you know it's a legit blowout. The goal is to get the first crack at that crispy, glistening skin. The mere smell of it can cause traffic jams and unite warring family members. It's not just food; it's a cultural event.
usage_notes: While 'lechón' in Spanish refers to a suckling pig, Filipino 'letson' can refer to a pig of any age. Also used for other roasted animals like 'letson manok' (roast chicken) or 'letson baka' (roast calf/cow). The spelling 'litson' is also very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Walang tatalo sa malutong na balat ng bagong luto na **letson**.","translation":"Nothing beats the crispy skin of a newly cooked **roast pig**."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubhang maganda; nagtataglay ng pambihirang ganda.
etymology: Combination of the slang intensifier `apaka-` and the root word `ganda` (beauty). `Apaka-` is a playful corruption of the standard intensifier `pagka-` or `napaka-`.
original_explanation: This is not just 'maganda.' This is next-level, jaw-dropping, 'sana all' beauty. It's what you'd say when you see a sunset in El Nido, or when your crush finally posts a new profile picture. The 'apaka-' is a modern slang intensifier, a funnier version of 'napaka-'.
usage_notes: A very informal and modern way to say 'very beautiful'. Common in social media and casual conversations among younger generations. The prefix 'apaka-' can be attached to many adjectives (e.g., apakasarap, apakagaling).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Apakaganda** ng tanawin mula sa tuktok ng bundok!","translation":"The view from the top of the mountain is **so beautiful**!"},{"sentence":"Uy, **apakaganda** ng bago mong sapatos!","translation":"Hey, your new shoes are **very beautiful**!"}]

translation: the act of blocking; interception; holdup
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpigil, pagharang, o pagbalakid sa daan o sa isang gawain; maaari ring tumukoy sa isang insidente ng pagnanakaw sa daan.
etymology: From `pang-` + reduplication of the first syllable of the root `ha-` + `harang` (to block).
original_explanation: This is what happens on EDSA every single day. But it's also what your sibling does when you're about to get the last piece of chicken. It's the act of blocking something or someone, whether it's a basketball shot, a text message you're trying to read over someone's shoulder, or a highway robbery. Context is key!
usage_notes: Can refer to a simple act of blocking or a more serious crime like a holdup.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging biktima sila ng **panghaharang** sa madilim na kalsada.","translation":"They became victims of a **holdup** on a dark road."},{"sentence":"Mahusay ang kanyang **panghaharang** sa bola kaya hindi naka-iskor ang kalaban.","translation":"His **blocking** of the ball was excellent, which is why the opponent didn't score."}]

translation: to exchange news with each other
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapalitan ng impormasyon o balita ng dalawa o higit pang tao; ang pag-uulat sa isa't isa ng mga pinakabagong pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is the OG "spill the tea" session. It's the act of catching up with friends, family, or the neighborhood 'Maritess' to exchange the latest chismis or life updates. Before group chats, there was `magkabalitaan` over the bakod (fence).
usage_notes: Implies a mutual, reciprocal exchange of information, not just one person reporting to another.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tawagan mo ako mamaya para **magkabalitaan** tayo.","translation":"Call me later so we can **update each other**."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga sa magkakalayong magkapatid ang palaging **magkabalitaan**.","translation":"It's important for siblings who are far apart to always **exchange news with each other**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay o palitang pagbibigay ng ngiti ng dalawa o higit pang mga tao sa isa't isa.
etymology: `mag-` + `ngiti` + `-an`. The `-an` suffix indicates a reciprocal or collective action.
original_explanation: That moment when you and your bestie see something funny and you just look at each other and know. It's the silent communication that happens in a crowded room. It's the awkward moment when you pass an acquaintance and you both do that little half-smile, half-nod thing. It’s a group chat, but with faces.
usage_notes: Implies a reciprocal or mutual action. It's not one person smiling, but people smiling *at each other*.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkatinginan muna sila bago **magngitian** nang makahulugan.","translation":"They looked at each other first before **smiling at each other** meaningfully."},{"sentence":"Tuwing nagkikita ang magkakaibigan, hindi nila maiwasang **magngitian** at magbatian.","translation":"Whenever the friends see each other, they can't help but **smile at each other** and greet one another."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi kasapi o kumikiling sa anumang partido, pangkat, o grupo, lalo na sa politika.
etymology: Mula sa "wala" (none) + "-ng" (linker) + "lapi" (join a group) + "-an" (suffix na tumutukoy sa isang grupo).
original_explanation: This is that one friend in your barkada who refuses to take sides during a group fight. "Kayo bahala, basta ako, neutral." In politics, this is the candidate who runs as an "Independent," not allied with the big red, yellow, or blue teams. They're the Switzerland of the group chat.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa konteksto ng pulitika, mga organisasyon, o pormal na grupo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumakbo siya bilang isang **walang-lapian** na kandidato sa pagka-senador.","translation":"He ran as a **non-partisan** candidate for senator."},{"sentence":"Ang isang hukom ay dapat manatiling **walang-lapian** upang maging patas ang kanyang desisyon.","translation":"A judge must remain **non-partisan** for his decisions to be fair."}]

translation: having the same taste; of the same flavor
meaning_filipino: Pagkakaroon ng parehong lasa o timpla ng dalawa o higit pang pagkain o inumin.
original_explanation: When you and your friend order the same milk tea flavor and it tastes exactly the same. Or when your mom cooks adobo today and it tastes just like the one she cooked last week. Consistency is key! Can also be used to say two different things surprisingly taste similar. "Uy, `magkalasa` pala ang mangga at kamatis na may bagoong!"
usage_notes: Used to compare the flavors of two or more items.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko malaman kung alin ang Coke at Pepsi dahil para sa akin ay **magkalasa** lang sila.","translation":"I can't tell which is Coke and which is Pepsi because for me, they **have the same taste**."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan nilang gawing **magkalasa** ang luto nilang sinigang.","translation":"They tried to make their sinigang dishes **taste the same**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang larawan o disenyo na nilikha sa isang patag na ibabaw, karaniwan sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng lapis, pluma, o krayola.
original_explanation: The OG meaning. This is what you did in your MAPEH class back in grade school. Stick figures, mountains with a sun in between, a bahay kubo—that's a drowing. It's the art of making lines on paper to create a picture.
usage_notes: The Filipinized spelling of the English word. "Guhit" is the native Tagalog equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinasa niya ang kanyang **drowing** para sa art contest.","translation":"She submitted her **drawing** for the art contest."}]

translation: the act of stepping or taking a step
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-angat ng isang paa at paglalagay nito sa ibang lugar, karaniwan bilang bahagi ng paglakad o pagsulong.
original_explanation: This is the literal 'first step' you take, whether it's walking into a new job, moving on from a toxic ex, or finally deciding to go to the gym. It's the moment you decide to move forward, one step at a time. 'Ang paghakbang palayo sa ref pagkatapos ng hatinggabi ang pinakamahirap.'
usage_notes: Often used metaphorically for starting something new or making a significant life change.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang unang **paghakbang** sa entablado ang pinakamahirap para sa isang baguhang mang-aawit.","translation":"The first **step** onto the stage is the hardest for a new singer."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang kanyang **paghakbang** tungo sa pagbabago.","translation":"His **step** towards change is important."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga bagay, ideya, o pamamaraan na naaayon sa kasalukuyang panahon o nagpapakita ng pagiging bago at progresibo.
original_explanation: Anything that's 'new gen' or 'updated.' From the latest smartphone model to your lola finally learning how to use TikTok, that's *makabago*. It's being up-to-date with the trends, technology, or even just a new way of thinking.
usage_notes: Can also mean 'pro-new', describing a person who favors new things and change.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumagamit sila ng **makabago** at mabisang teknolohiya sa kanilang pabrika.","translation":"They use **modern** and effective technology in their factory."},{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng mga **makabago** na solusyon sa mga lumang problema.","translation":"We need **innovative** solutions to old problems."}]

translation: to encircle; to trap by circling
meaning_filipino: Palibutan o paligiran sa pamamagitan ng pag-ikot upang hindi makawala o upang makorner.
original_explanation: Think of a spider spinning a web around its prey. That's 'ikitan'. It's the strategic move in 'agawan base' where you and your friends circle an opponent to tag them. It’s a tactical encirclement, whether in games or in life.
usage_notes: This verb suggests a dynamic, circling action with the intent to trap or corner something or someone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan nilang **ikitan** ang pusang kalye pero mabilis itong nakatakas.","translation":"They tried to **encircle** the stray cat but it quickly escaped."},{"sentence":"Sa laro, kailangang **ikitan** ang kalaban para makuha ang kanilang bandila.","translation":"In the game, you need to **trap by circling** the opponent to get their flag."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng lala o paghahabi ng yantok na karaniwang ginagamit sa mga muwebles tulad ng upuan at kama, na nagtatampok ng butas-butas na disenyo.
etymology: From Spanish 'rejilla' (grille, grating), adapted to refer to the specific weaving style.
original_explanation: That iconic, breezy pattern on your lola's rocking chair or bed frame. It's the OG air-conditioning system for furniture, perfect for the Philippine heat. You know you're a true Pinoy if you have a memory (or a scar) from a broken strand of solihiya.
usage_notes: Refers to the specific woven pattern, not just the material (rattan/yantok).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang upuang **solihiya** ay simbolo ng tradisyonal na disenyong Pilipino.","translation":"The **solihiya** chair is a symbol of traditional Filipino design."},{"sentence":"Nasira ang **solihiya** sa likod ng silya kaya kailangang ipaayos.","translation":"The **caning** on the back of the chair broke so it needs to be repaired."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng kilos upang himukin o kumbinsihin ang isang tao na gawin ang isang bagay o maniwala sa isang ideya.
original_explanation: This is the active verb form of 'budol'. It's when you're actively trying to convince your boss you need a raise, or trying to get your friends to chip in for a surprise party. It's the Team Lead trying to get the team to render OT on a Friday night.
usage_notes: This is the action of persuading. It's a transitive verb requiring an object (the person being persuaded).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan kong **hikayatin** si Maria na sumama sa ating lakad.","translation":"I tried to **persuade** Maria to join our trip."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **hikayatin** ang mga taong sarado na ang isip.","translation":"It is difficult to **convince** people who are already close-minded."}]

meaning_filipino: Bumalik sa pinagmulan, lalo na ang isang masamang salita, plano, o gawa na orihinal na para sa iba.
original_explanation: When you throw shade at someone, but it ends up hitting you back harder. 'Inaway mo si beshie, now the whole barkada is mad at you. Ayan, bumerang tuloy.' It's Karma's younger, sassier sibling that works in real-time.
usage_notes: A colloquial verb derived from the English noun 'boomerang', used to describe situations that backfire.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lahat ng paninira niya sa akin ay **bumerang** lang sa kanya.","translation":"All the slander he threw at me just **boomeranged** back at him."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa iyong mga sinasabi, baka **bumerang** iyan sa'yo.","translation":"Be careful with your words, they might **backfire** on you."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang damdamin ng kasiyahan o pagiging kontento sa sariling mga nagawa, katangian, o pag-aari. Maaari rin itong tumukoy sa kahambugan o kayabangan.
etymology: From pag- + the first syllable of mag- (ma-) + mag- + laki (big, great). The sense of 'pride' comes from 'thinking big of oneself'.
original_explanation: This has two flavors. 1) The good kind: The feeling Hidilyn Diaz gave us when she won the Olympic gold. That's pagmamalaki for the country. 2) The not-so-good kind: Your friend who just got a promotion and won't stop talking about their new salary. That's also pagmamalaki, but the mayabang version. It's the line between 'I'm proud of my achievement' and 'Look at me, I'm better than you.'
usage_notes: Can be positive (pride) or negative (arrogance), depending on context. The modifier 'labis na' (excessive) usually pushes it to the negative side.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **pagmamalaki** sa kanyang tinig habang ikinukwento ang tagumpay ng anak.","translation":"There was **pride** in her voice as she told the story of her child's success."},{"sentence":"Ang labis na **pagmamalaki** ay humahantong sa kayabangan.","translation":"Excessive **pride** leads to arrogance."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang aparato na ginagamit upang mag-imbak ng tunog, video, o datos sa isang midyum upang muling mapakinggan o mapanood sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: That thing your tita from the US brings home as pasalubong in the 90s, the one you use to record your voice singing 'My Heart Will Go On.' Today, it's just an app on your phone. Also, that plastic flute from elementary school that sounded like a dying bird when everyone played it at the same time.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa isang aparato para sa audio/video o sa instrumentong pangmusika. Ang konteksto ang magdidikta ng kahulugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ng reporter ang kanyang **rekorder** para sa panayam.","translation":"The reporter used his **recorder** for the interview."},{"sentence":"Natututo siyang tumugtog ng **rekorder** sa klase sa musika.","translation":"He is learning to play the **recorder** in music class."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangmatagalang kondisyong medikal na kinakikitaan ng mataas na antas ng asukal sa dugo.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol 'diabetes', mula sa Latin 'diabetes', mula sa Griyego 'diabētēs'.
original_explanation: The reason your tita tells you to stop drinking too much milk tea with 100% sugar. It's the 'bawal sa matamis' sickness. Basically, your body's relationship with sugar becomes... complicated.
usage_notes: Isang direktang hiram na salita, ginagamit katulad ng katumbas nito sa Ingles sa mga kontekstong medikal at pang-araw-araw.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan niyang mag-ingat sa pagkain dahil sa kanyang **diabetes**.","translation":"He needs to be careful with his food because of his **diabetes**."},{"sentence":"Ang regular na ehersisyo ay makakatulong upang maiwasan ang **diabetes**.","translation":"Regular exercise can help prevent **diabetes**."}]

translation: to put someone in a tight spot; to pressure someone
meaning_filipino: Ilagay ang isang tao sa isang mahirap na kalagayan o sitwasyon; pilitin o idiin.
original_explanation: The act of being a 'user-friendly' friend, but in a bad way. It's when someone takes advantage of your kindness, especially when they know you're already struggling. 'Huwag mo naman akong gipitin' is the polite way of saying 'Bro, back off, I have my own problems.' It's the verb form of putting someone in that 'gipit' state.
usage_notes: The verb form of 'gipit'. The action of causing someone to be 'gipit'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **gipitin** ang mga taong may utang sa'yo, bigyan mo sila ng sapat na panahon.","translation":"Don't **pressure** the people who owe you money, give them enough time."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan siyang **gipitin** ng kanyang mga kalaban sa negosyo.","translation":"His business rivals are trying **to put him in a tight spot**."}]

translation: to give importance; to value; to appreciate
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng importansya, pagpapahalaga, o pagkilala sa isang tao, bagay, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is your love language if it's 'acts of service' or 'quality time'. It's when you finally put down your phone during dinner to actually listen to your partner. To magbigay-halaga is to treat something or someone like they're the last piece of chicken joy, not just some random 'seen-zoned' message.
usage_notes: Very common concept. Can be used for people, objects, or abstract ideas like time or effort.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat tayong **magbigay-halaga** sa sakripisyo ng ating mga bayani.","translation":"We should **give importance** to the sacrifices of our heroes."},{"sentence":"Nagsisisi siyang hindi niya **binigyan-halaga** ang kanilang relasyon.","translation":"He regrets not **valuing** their relationship."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babae o batang babae na malikot, mapagbiro, at kung minsan ay may pagka-pasaway ngunit sa paraang hindi nakakasakit o masama.
original_explanation: The female version of 'pilyo'. She's the tita who makes witty, slightly naughty jokes at family reunions. She's the little girl who puts makeup on the dog. It's a term of endearment for a girl who's a playful troublemaker, a lovable rascal. 'Ang pilya mo talaga, kung anu-ano ang sinasabi mo!'
usage_notes: The masculine form is 'pilyo'. It carries a lighthearted, often affectionate connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa pagiging **pilya** noong kanyang kabataan.","translation":"She was known for being **mischievous** in her youth."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala diyan, **pilya** lang talaga ang batang 'yan.","translation":"Don't believe that, that child is just a real **rascal**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging maikli o hindi mahaba, na maaaring tumukoy sa sukat, distansya, o tagal ng panahon.
original_explanation: The 'ikli' of your sweldo—it's gone before you know it. The 'ikli' of your patience when the WiFi is slow. The 'ikli' of a summer romance. It's the official state of things that end too soon. The opposite of 'haba'.
usage_notes: This is the root word and noun form. 'Maikli' is the adjective (short). 'Kaiklian' is a more formal noun for 'brevity'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa **ikli** ng oras, hindi namin natapos ang lahat ng gawain.","translation":"Because of the **shortness** of time, we weren't able to finish all the tasks."},{"sentence":"Nainis ako sa **ikli** ng kanyang pasensya.","translation":"I was annoyed by the **shortness** of his patience."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lipon ng mga pangungusap na magkakaugnay at tumatalakay sa isang partikular na paksa o ideya.
etymology: Possibly from Sanskrit *lata* (creeper, vine), referring to a line or string of words, though this is not confirmed.
original_explanation: That block of text you have to read for school, or the one you write in a long, dramatic text message to your jowa explaining your feelings. A good **talata** is like a well-made sandwich: may intro (top bread), may laman (the juicy details), at may conclusion (bottom bread).
usage_notes: Commonly used in schools and in writing. The Spanish-derived 'parapo' is also used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binubuo ng limang pangungusap ang bawat **talata** sa sanaysay na ito.","translation":"Each **paragraph** in this essay is composed of five sentences."},{"sentence":"Pakibasa ang ikatlong **talata** ng balita.","translation":"Please read the third **paragraph** of the news report."}]

translation: state of being scattered or ruined; disarray
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging kalat-kalat, sira-sira, o wasak.
etymology: Mula sa 'pagka-' (estado o paraan ng) + 'walat' (destroyed, scattered).
original_explanation: This is your room after trying on your entire wardrobe. This is your brain during finals week. This is what happens to a group project when there's no leader. It’s a state of total chaos, mess, and destruction. If your life was a car, "pagkawalat" is when it's been totaled, stripped for parts, and left in a ditch. Also a popular slang for being extremely drunk or wasted. "Walat na ako, pre."
usage_notes: Can be used literally for physical mess or figuratively for a person's mental/emotional state. Also has a common slang usage meaning 'wasted' or 'drunk'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko malaman kung saan magsisimula sa **pagkawalat** ng aking kwarto.","translation":"I don't know where to start with the **disarray** of my room."},{"sentence":"Grabe ang **pagkawalat** niya kagabi dahil sa dami ng ininom.","translation":"He was extremely **wasted** last night because of how much he drank."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyon na nagpapahiwatig ng pagkakatulad, paghahambing, o pag-aalinlangan; katumbas ng "tila" o "animo".
etymology: Pagsasama ng 'para' (tulad) at 'baga' (isang panandang nagpapahiwatig ng tanong o pagdududa).
original_explanation: This is the Tagalog way of saying "as if" or "it's like...". It adds a bit of drama or uncertainty, often used in more literary or formal contexts. You use it when describing something that looks like something else, or when you're being poetic. "Para bagang artista siya kung maglakad." (She walks as if she's a celebrity.) The everyday version is just "parang".
usage_notes: Medyo pormal o pampanitikan ang dating nito. Mas karaniwan sa pang-araw-araw na usapan ang "parang".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga ulap ay **para baga**ng bulak na nakakalat sa langit.","translation":"The clouds are **like** cotton scattered across the sky."},{"sentence":"Nagsalita siya na **para baga**ng walang anumang nangyari.","translation":"He spoke **as if** nothing had happened."}]

meaning_filipino: Itago o ikubli ang isang bagay o impormasyon upang hindi malaman ng iba.
original_explanation: That 'It's Complicated' relationship status on Facebook. You're trying to **ilihim** the fact that you don't know if you're officially together or just in an M.U. (Mutual Understanding). It's the act of keeping something on the down-low, like your office romance or the fact that you ate the last piece of cake.
usage_notes: The `i-` prefix indicates that the direct object of the verb is the thing being kept secret.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pilit niyang **inihim** ang tunay na nararamdaman para sa kaibigan.","translation":"He tried to **keep secret** his true feelings for his friend."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ilihim** sa amin ang iyong mga problema.","translation":"Don't **conceal** your problems from us."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang post sa social media na sadyang idinisenyo upang makapukaw ng galit o matinding reaksyon mula sa mga mambabasa para sa engagement.
original_explanation: You know those FB posts that start with 'Unpopular opinion, but...' and then say something super controversial? That's a bait post. It's designed to make people angry and start a war in the comments section. The goal isn't to have a real discussion, but to get clicks, shares, and reactions. Don't fall for it, 'wag kang magpa-bait!
