usage_notes: A very modern, internet-specific term. It is a loan phrase treated as a single noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halata namang **bait post** lang 'yun para dumami ang followers niya.","translation":"It's obviously just a **bait post** to increase his followers."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang patulan 'yang **bait post** na 'yan, sinasayang mo lang oras mo.","translation":"Don't engage with that **bait post**, you're just wasting your time."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkilos na nagpapakita ng labis o huwad na kabanalan; pagpapanggap na mas relihiyoso o moral kaysa sa tunay na katangian.
etymology: From root 'banal' (holy) with reduplication and suffix '-an' to denote pretense or imitation.
original_explanation: The act of being "holier-than-thou". 'Yung kakilala mong laging may quote galing sa bible sa Facebook post pero number one chismosa sa inuman. Sila 'yung nagbabanal-banalan. They post "God bless" on a post that's throwing shade at someone else. It's the performance of piety, not the real thing.
usage_notes: Carries a negative connotation of hypocrisy. The structure (reduplication of the root + -an) is a common way in Tagalog to mean "to pretend to be X".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala diyan, **nagbabanal-banalan** lang iyan para makuha ang tiwala ng mga tao.","translation":"Don't believe them, they're just **pretending to be holy** to get people's trust."},{"sentence":"Mahirap makisama sa taong **nagbabanal-banalan** at laging hinuhusgahan ang iba.","translation":"It's hard to get along with a person who is **sanctimonious** and always judges others."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pag-eespiya o pagmamanman nang lihim upang makakuha ng impormasyon, karaniwan ay para sa isang pamahalaan o organisasyon.
etymology: Mula sa 'espiya' (mula sa Espanyol na 'espía') + hulaping '-han'.
original_explanation: What your kapitbahay na chismosa does from her window. It's the corporate version of trying to get the secret recipe for Jollibee Chickenjoy. Basically, next-level stalking with higher stakes, like a government budget or a trade secret.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inakusahan ang diplomatiko ng **espiyahan**.","translation":"The diplomat was accused of **espionage**."}]

meaning_filipino: Mahigpit na nakabigkis o nakapalibot sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: Parang ahas sa sanga, o extension cord na ginulo ng pusa. It's also how your clingy jowa holds onto your arm in public. "Bakit ganyan 'yang earphones mo?" "Nakapulupot na naman, 'di ko na maayos!"
usage_notes: Can be used for literal coiling (like a snake or rope) or figurative clinging (like a person).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May ahas na **nakapulupot** sa sanga ng puno.","translation":"There is a snake **coiled** around the tree branch."},{"sentence":"Ang bata ay mahigpit na **nakapulupot** sa braso ng kanyang ina.","translation":"The child was tightly **wrapped around** his mother's arm."}]

translation: to stay at home; to build a house
meaning_filipino: Manatili o mamalagi sa loob ng tahanan. Maaari ring mangahulugan ng pagtatayo ng isang bahay.
original_explanation: During the pandemic, we all became experts at this. "Magbahay" means to just stay home, be a homebody. It's the opposite of 'gumala'. In another context, it's the more ambitious version: to literally build a house, like what your OFW relative dreams of doing.
usage_notes: The meaning (stay home vs. build a house) is highly dependent on context. "Magbahay ka na lang" usually means "Just stay home." "Magbahay tayo sa probinsya" could mean "Let's build a house in the province."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa malakas na ulan, minabuti naming **magbahay** na lang muna.","translation":"Because of the heavy rain, we decided to just **stay at home** for now."},{"sentence":"Plano nilang **magbahay** sa kanilang bagong lupang binili.","translation":"They plan to **build a house** on their newly bought land."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng isang bagay na nararanasan sa pamamagitan ng panlasa. Ang sensasyon na nalilikha sa dila kapag ang isang pagkain o inumin ay tinikman.
etymology: From Malay 'rasa', from Sanskrit 'rasa' (रस), meaning 'juice, essence, flavor, taste'.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'flavor profile.' Is your sinigang maasim enough? Is your coffee too matamis? Is your ex's apology too bland? It's all about the lasa. It's the difference between a 5-star meal and your sad desk lunch.
usage_notes: Can also be used metaphorically to describe the 'flavor' or 'feel' of an experience.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sarap ng **lasa** ng adobo ni lola.","translation":"The **taste** of grandma's adobo is delicious."},{"sentence":"Ano kayang **lasa** ng tagumpay?","translation":"I wonder what the **flavor** of success is?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang yugto ng buhay mula sa pagiging sanggol hanggang sa bago maging dalaga o binata; ang panahon ng pagiging bata.
original_explanation: The era of your life powered by Treetop, Yakult, and a diet of '90s cartoons. It's that magical time before bills, back pain, and existential dread kicked in. The time when your biggest problem was getting home before the streetlights came on. #Nostalgia
usage_notes: A very common word referring to the period of one's life as a child.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masaya ang kanyang **pagkabata** sa probinsya.","translation":"His **childhood** in the province was happy."},{"sentence":"Naalala ko noong aking **pagkabata**, naglalaro kami ng tumbang preso.","translation":"I remember during my **childhood**, we used to play tumbang preso."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay o tao na nagsisilbing huwaran o modelo. Isang partikular na kaso na nagpapakita ng isang pangkalahatang tuntunin.
original_explanation: This is the classic "For example..." you hear in class. "Magbigay ng ehemplo ng pang-uri." It's also what your parents want you to be: a good example to your younger siblings. "Maging mabuting ehemplo ka sa mga kapatid mo."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Jose Rizal ay isang magandang **ehemplo** ng pagmamahal sa bayan.","translation":"Jose Rizal is a good **example** of love for one's country."},{"sentence":"Magbigay ka ng **ehemplo** ng pandiwa sa pangungusap.","translation":"Give an **example** of a verb in a sentence."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi totoo, huwad, o mapanlinlang; peke.
original_explanation: This is the classic "peke" or fake. Parang 'yung "I love you" niya, bogus pala. Or that online seller who sends you a bar of soap instead of the iPhone you ordered. It's the ultimate scam, the "expectations vs. reality" meme in word form.
usage_notes: Commonly used in contexts of scams, fake items, or insincere actions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingat sa mga **bogus** na text message na nagsasabing nanalo ka sa raffle.","translation":"Be careful of **fraudulent** text messages saying you won a raffle."},{"sentence":"Nalaman niyang **bogus** pala ang alok na trabaho sa kanya.","translation":"He found out that the job offer to him was **bogus**."}]

meaning_filipino: Buburahin o aalisin ang isang bagay, lalo na ang datos o impormasyon sa isang elektronikong kagamitan. Ito ay nasa anyong panghinaharap.
original_explanation: The future tense of regret. This is what you tell yourself you'll do to that embarrassing photo, that angry comment, or your ex's number. 'Mamaya, **magdedelete** na talaga ako.' Spoiler: sometimes, 'mamaya' never comes.
usage_notes: This is the future tense form of the Tagalized verb 'mag-delete'. The 'de-' is repeated to indicate future action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magdedelete** ako ng mga lumang files para lumuwag ang memory ng computer ko.","translation":"I **will delete** old files to free up my computer's memory."},{"sentence":"Sabi niya **magdedelete** na siya ng social media, pero online pa rin siya.","translation":"He said he **will delete** his social media, but he's still online."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng hindi pagsunod o pagsuway sa isang umiiral na batas, utos, o alituntunin.
etymology: From the root 'labag' (against, contrary to) with the infix '-um-'.
original_explanation: When you cross the street even if the pedestrian light is red, you lumabag sa batas trapiko. When you break your diet on the first day, you lumabag sa promise mo sa sarili mo. It's basically breaking the rules, whether it's the law of the land or the law of your diet plan.
usage_notes: This is the actor-focus past tense form (naganap). The infinitive is 'lumabag' and the present/progressive is 'lumalabag'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lumabag** siya sa mga patakaran ng paaralan kaya siya naparusahan.","translation":"He **violated** the school rules, which is why he was punished."},{"sentence":"Sinabihan siyang huwag **lumabag** sa tiwala na ibinigay sa kanya.","translation":"He was told not to **transgress** the trust that was given to him."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na ekspresyon na nangangahulugang hindi natitinag, walang epekto, o hindi magawang saktan o abalahin ang isang tao.
etymology: From "hindi" (not) and "ma-ano" (literally 'can't be what-ed'), a versatile placeholder verb indicating an action cannot be successfully done to the subject.
original_explanation: The ultimate "unbothered" state of being. When someone throws shade at you and you just sip your milk tea. "Pinagalitan siya ng boss niya, pero hindi maano." It's the power of not letting anything ruin your vibe. You can't be... 'what-ed'.
usage_notes: Highly colloquial and context-dependent. The meaning is derived from the situation. It implies that an action (the "ano") cannot be successfully done to the person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan nilang inisin si Maria, pero **hindi maano**.","translation":"They tried to annoy Maria, but she was **unfazed**."},{"sentence":"Kahit anong tukso sa kanya, **hindi maano** ang kanyang pokus sa pag-aaral.","translation":"No matter how they tempted him, his focus on studying **couldn't be bothered**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang matigas na bahagi ng kalansay ng mga bertebrado, kasama ang tao, na nagbibigay-suporta at hugis sa katawan.
original_explanation: This is the reason you drink your milk. It's the framework of your body, the thing your dog loves to chew on, and what makes up the deliciousness of Bulalo. It's what's left when all the 'hugot' is gone. The 'buto' in 'buto't balat'.
usage_notes: This is one of two primary meanings for 'buto'. The other is 'seed'. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masakit ang mga **buto** niya sa pagod sa trabaho.","translation":"His **bones** ache from work fatigue."},{"sentence":"Ang sarap sipsipin ng **buto** ng bulalo.","translation":"The **bone** marrow of the bulalo is delicious to sip."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal o impormal na pagpapalitan ng kuro-kuro, opinyon, at impormasyon tungkol sa isang partikular na paksa.
original_explanation: A more civilized version of a 'talakan'. This is the group chat, the forum thread, the panel discussion, the brainstorming session. It's where ideas are shared, not just insults. Think of it as a collaborative effort, unlike a 'talakan' which is a competitive sport.
usage_notes: 'Talakayan' is the event or venue for discussion, while 'talakay' is the topic being discussed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng isang mainit na **talakayan** tungkol sa bagong batas.","translation":"There was a heated **discussion** about the new law."},{"sentence":"Bukas ang **talakayan** para sa lahat ng gustong magbigay ng suhestiyon.","translation":"The **forum** is open to everyone who wants to give a suggestion."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng kuwadro o balangkas sa paligid ng isang bagay, tulad ng litrato, pinta, o sertipiko.
original_explanation: The verb form of making something look important. You get your diploma? I-kuwadrohan mo. That one good photo where you don't look like a potato? I-kuwadrohan mo rin. It's the act of putting a border around something to make it official, presentable, or just to hang it on the wall for your Titas to see.
usage_notes: Object-focus verb. The root word "kuwadro" means "frame".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipapagawa ko sa karpintero na **kuwadrohan** ang aming family picture.","translation":"I will have the carpenter **frame** our family picture."},{"sentence":"Dapat mong **kuwadrohan** ang iyong diploma at isabit sa pader.","translation":"You should **frame** your diploma and hang it on the wall."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang partikular na anyo ng isang wika na sinasalita sa isang tiyak na rehiyon o ng isang partikular na pangkat ng mga tao.
original_explanation: Ito yung dahilan kung bakit iba ang Tagalog ng taga-Batangas ('Ala e!') sa Tagalog ng taga-Maynila. It's like a flavor of a language. Parehong kape, pero isa ay barako, isa ay 3-in-1. Gets?
usage_notes: Mahalagang tandaan na ang dialekto ay isang baryasyon ng isang wika, at hindi isang 'mababang' uri ng wika. Ang Cebuano at Ilocano ay mga wika, hindi mga dialekto ng Filipino/Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayaman sa iba't ibang **dialekto** ang rehiyon ng Bikol.","translation":"The Bicol region is rich in different **dialects**."},{"sentence":"Kahit parehong Tagalog, may kaibahan ang **dialekto** ng taga-Bulacan at taga-Quezon.","translation":"Even though they're both Tagalog, the **dialect** of someone from Bulacan and someone from Quezon has differences."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang pagkakasunod-sunod kung saan ang mga elemento o tao ay nagpapalitan ng posisyon o tungkulin sa isang regular na paraan.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung shift niyo sa BPO, day shift tapos night shift, magkakahalili kayo. O kaya sa paborito niyong K-drama, 'yung mga bida, magkakahalili sa pagiging masaya at pagiging sawi. It’s a cycle, a rotation, a turn-based system.
usage_notes: Often implies a cycle or a roster.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magkakahalili** ang pagbabantay ng mga sundalo sa kampo.","translation":"The soldiers' guard duty at the camp is **alternating**."},{"sentence":"Ang araw at gabi ay **magkakahalili** sa pagbibigay-liwanag at dilim.","translation":"Day and night **take turns** in giving light and darkness."}]

translation: to make easier, to expedite, to simplify
meaning_filipino: Gawing mas madali, mas mabilis, o mas simple ang isang gawain, proseso, o sitwasyon.
etymology: From 'mag-' (verb prefix) + 'pa-' (causative prefix) + 'dali' (easy, quick). 'To cause to be easy/quick.'
original_explanation: Life hacks! This is the verb for finding shortcuts or ways to make a difficult task simpler. 'Gagamit ako ng app para magpadali sa pag-budget.' (I'll use an app to make budgeting easier.) It's what you wish government offices had a button for. The opposite of 'magpahirap' (to make difficult).
usage_notes: Often used in the context of processes, technology, and problem-solving.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang teknolohiya ay nilikha upang **magpadali** sa ating pang-araw-araw na buhay.","translation":"Technology was created to **make** our daily lives **easier**."},{"sentence":"May shortcut ba para **magpadali** sa prosesong ito?","translation":"Is there a shortcut to **expedite** this process?"}]

meaning_filipino: Nauukol sa kalakalan, komersyo, o pagpapalitan ng mga produkto at serbisyo.
original_explanation: When your hobby of baking cookies suddenly becomes a business, you're now producing them for 'pangkalakal' purposes. It's the difference between a pet pig and a pig being raised for lechon. This is business, not personal. Think stocks, exports, imports, and that 'For Sale' sign.
usage_notes: Often used in formal business and economic discussions. "Komersyal" is a common Spanish-derived synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga barkong **pangkalakal** ay dumaong sa pier.","translation":"The **commercial** ships docked at the pier."},{"sentence":"May kasunduang **pangkalakal** ang Pilipinas at Japan.","translation":"The Philippines and Japan have a **trade** agreement."}]

meaning_filipino: Mawalan ng sigla at pananariwa, karaniwan sa mga halaman na natutuyo dahil sa kakulangan sa tubig o sobrang init.
original_explanation: What happens to your houseplant when you forget to water it for a week. Also, what happens to your energy levels by Thursday afternoon. Metaphorically, it's that feeling of losing your spark or enthusiasm, like when your crush leaves you on 'seen'. "Ay, lumanta na ang pag-asa kong mag-leave bukas, may urgent meeting daw."
usage_notes: Used for plants, flowers, and metaphorically for people's spirits, beauty, or hopes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis na **lumanta** ang mga bulaklak dahil sa matinding sikat ng araw.","translation":"The flowers **wilted** quickly because of the intense heat of the sun."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **lumanta** ang iyong pangarap dahil lang sa isang pagkabigo.","translation":"Don't let your dream **wither** just because of one failure."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang tao, ideya, o kilos na nagpapakita ng paglaban o pagtutol sa isang umiiral na kapangyarihan, sistema, o awtoridad.
original_explanation: Think Katipunan vibes. This is the spirit of Andres Bonifacio. In modern terms, it's the artist whose work challenges the status quo, the student activist fighting for a cause, or even just you deciding to quit your toxic job to follow your passion. It's about fighting the power.
usage_notes: A very strong word with historical and political connotations. It implies a deep-seated opposition to an established order.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga tula ay may **mapanghimagsik** na mensahe.","translation":"His poems carry a **revolutionary** message."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **mapanghimagsik** na pananaw, itinuring siyang banta ng pamahalaan.","translation":"Because of his **rebellious** views, he was considered a threat by the government."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na marka, dumi, o bakas na naiwan sa isang ibabaw; maaari ding tumukoy sa kaunting palatandaan ng isang katangian o damdamin.
original_explanation: That little smudge of chocolate on your white shirt that you didn't notice until someone pointed it out. It can also be used figuratively, like a 'bahid ng kalungkutan' (a trace of sadness) on someone's face, trying to hide their true feelings. It's the subtle evidence left behind, whether it's lipstick on a collar or the lingering feeling after a sad movie.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa matalinghagang paraan upang mangahulugang 'dungis' o 'stigma' (hal., bahid sa pangalan - a stain on one's name).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **bahid** ng putik ang kanyang sapatos.","translation":"There's a **smear** of mud on his shoes."},{"sentence":"Kahit nakangiti siya, may **bahid** ng pag-aalala sa kanyang mga mata.","translation":"Even though she was smiling, there was a **trace** of worry in her eyes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang nakalimbag na dokumento na naglalarawan at nag-aanunsyo ng isang partikular na bagay, tulad ng isang paaralan, kumpanya, o isang bagong produkto, upang makaakit ng mga kliyente o mag-aaral.
original_explanation: Ito yung pamphlet o brochure na binibigay sa'yo sa mga college fair o kapag may nag-aalok ng condo. Puno ng magagandang pictures at promises. Basically, ito ang marketing material na nagsasabing, "Enroll here!" or "Invest now!". The paper version of a sales pitch.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakalagay sa **prospekto** ng unibersidad ang lahat ng kursong inaalok nila.","translation":"The university's **prospectus** lists all the courses they offer."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng mga mamumuhunan ang **prospekto** ng bagong kumpanya.","translation":"The investors are studying the new company's **prospectus**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na matagumpay na nakaahon o naka-move on mula sa isang masalimuot o masakit na 'situationship'.
original_explanation: This person went through the emotional roller coaster of a "what are we?" dynamic and came out the other side, maybe a little bruised, but definitely wiser. They've learned the hard way that "vibes" don't pay the emotional bills. Now they're either happily single or in a relationship with a clear DTR (Define The Relationship) moment. They wear their past as a badge of honor.
usage_notes: Isang termino na ginagamit para sa pagpapalakas ng loob pagkatapos ng isang malabong romantikong ugnayan. Madalas makita sa mga online forum at social media posts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Proud **situationship survivor** here! Never again sa mga paasa.","translation":"Proud **situationship survivor** here! Never again to those who lead people on."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panloob na bahagi ng kamay ng tao, mula sa pulso hanggang sa puno ng mga daliri.
etymology: Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *palaj₁ (palm of hand, sole of foot).
original_explanation: The part of your hand you use for high-fives, facepalms, and for checking if you have enough cash for milk tea. It's also where your lola 'reads' your future, right before telling you to get a real job.
usage_notes: This is the literal, anatomical meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pawisan ang kanyang **palad** dahil sa kaba.","translation":"His **palm** was sweaty due to nervousness."},{"sentence":"Ipinatong niya ang barya sa **palad** ng bata.","translation":"She placed the coin on the child's **palm**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga numerong buo, na walang bahaging desimal o praksyon, kasama ang positibo, negatibo, at sero.
original_explanation: This is math that doesn't give you a headache with decimals or fractions. Just clean, whole numbers like 1, 2, 3... like the number of cups of rice you *should* eat vs. the 4.5 you actually do. It's the 'walang butal' of mathematics.
usage_notes: A technical term used in mathematics. The English equivalent is 'integer'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **pambuong-numero** ay maaaring positibo, negatibo, o zero.","translation":"**Integers** can be positive, negative, or zero."},{"sentence":"Pag-aralan natin ang operasyon sa mga **pambuong-numero**.","translation":"Let's study the operations on **whole numbers**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pook o pagawaan kung saan ginagawa, itinitinda, o kinukumpuni ang mga sapatos.
original_explanation: This is the OG shoe store, not the cool sneaker shops in the mall, but the place where your lolo would get his leather shoes fixed. Think of it as the 'talyer' (workshop) for your kicks. It's now a bit of a vintage term.
usage_notes: This term is less common in modern conversation, often replaced by 'tindahan ng sapatos' (shoe store) or the specific name of a shop. It specifically implies a place for making or repairing shoes, not just selling them.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala ni tatay ang luma niyang sapatos sa **sapatirya** para kumpunihin.","translation":"Father brought his old shoes to the **cobbler's shop** to be repaired."},{"sentence":"May kilala ka bang magaling na **sapatirya** sa Marikina?","translation":"Do you know a good **shoe maker/shop** in Marikina?"}]

translation: to fit each other; to be just right for each other
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging sapat o tamang-tama ng dalawang bagay para sa isa't isa, maaaring sa sukat, halaga, o katangian.
original_explanation: That Cinderella moment when the shoe fits perfectly. Or when your salary is *sakto lang* for your monthly bills (walang labis, walang kulang). In relationships, it's finding someone who just *gets* you. You click. You fit. #SanaAll
usage_notes: Can refer to physical fit, financial balance, or compatibility between people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **nagkahusto** rin ang takip at ang kaldero.","translation":"Finally, the lid and the pot **fit each other**."},{"sentence":"Sana **magkahusto** ang sweldo ko para sa lahat ng bayarin ngayong buwan.","translation":"I hope my salary will **be just enough** for all the bills this month."}]

translation: to be able to be taught; to be disciplined
meaning_filipino: Ang makatanggap ng turo o aral; ang mapasunod sa pamamagitan ng pagtuturo o pagdidisiplina.
original_explanation: This is what parents hope for their kids. "Sana **maturuan** na ng leksyon ang batang 'yan." It means someone is teachable or can be disciplined. It's the opposite of "matigas ang ulo" (hard-headed). It's the goal of every training, seminar, or "sermon" from your lola. It's not just about teaching, but about the lesson actually *landing* and sticking.
usage_notes: Can mean simply "to be taught something" or carry the stronger connotation of "to be taught a lesson" or "to be disciplined."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **maturuan** ang isang taong sarado ang isip.","translation":"It's difficult **to teach** a person who is close-minded."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng insidente, sana'y **maturuan** na siya ng leksyon.","translation":"After the incident, hopefully he will finally **be taught** a lesson."}]

translation: to be sipped; to be slurped; to be sucked in
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-inom o pagkuha ng likido sa pamamagitan ng pagsipsip, o ang di-sinasadyang pagpasok sa isang bagay dahil sa malakas na puwersa.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're drinking milk tea and you accidentally slurp up a boba pearl. Also, a metaphor for getting sucked into a black hole of K-Drama or online shopping. 'Nahigop na ako ng sistema.'
usage_notes: Can be literal (sipping soup) or figurative (being drawn into something).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingat ka, baka **mahigop** mo ang mainit na sabaw.","translation":"Be careful, you might **slurp** the hot soup."},{"sentence":"Para siyang **mahigop** ng kadiliman.","translation":"It's as if he will **be sucked in** by the darkness."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagkakaroon ng kawalan ng tiwala o katiyakan sa isang bagay, pahayag, o tao.
original_explanation: That feeling when your jowa says "may sasabihin ako sa'yo mamaya." It's the "seen-zone" of emotions—you're left hanging, wondering what's up. It's also the national sport when a new online scam pops up.
usage_notes: Often used to express a lack of trust or a feeling of uncertainty, particularly in relationships or when assessing the truthfulness of a statement.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko mapigilan ang **pagdududa** ko sa kanyang mga sinabi.","translation":"I can't stop my **suspicion** about the things he said."},{"sentence":"Ang labis na **pagdududa** ay maaaring makasira sa isang relasyon.","translation":"Excessive **doubting** can destroy a relationship."}]

translation: to put inside; to place in a container
meaning_filipino: Ilagay ang isang bagay sa loob ng isang sisidlan o nakasarang espasyo.
original_explanation: The magical act of trying to fit all your pasalubong into one already-overweight Balikbayan box. It's what you tell your kid to do with their toys, and what you wish you could do with all your problems—just put them in a box and close the lid.
usage_notes: Implies putting something into an enclosed space, like a room ('silid'), box, or cabinet.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**isilid** mo na ang mga damit sa aparador.","translation":"Please **put** the clothes **inside** the cabinet."},{"sentence":"Saan ko pwedeng **isilid** itong mga aklat?","translation":"Where can I **put** these books **inside**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Nauukol sa o ginagamit para sa pagpapadala ng sulat o pakete sa pamamagitan ng koreo.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `pang-` at `koreo` (mula sa Espanyol na *correo*).
original_explanation: This is anything related to the post office or sending snail mail. Think 'selyong pangkoreo' (postage stamp) or 'kahong pangkoreo' (mailbox). In the age of email, DMs, and Lalamove, 'pangkoreo' stuff feels almost vintage, like waiting for a love letter instead of a 'seen' notification.
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang ilarawan ang mga item o serbisyong nauugnay sa sistema ng koreo o post office.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong lagyan ng selyong **pangkoreo** ang sulat mo.","translation":"You need to put a **postal** stamp on your letter."},{"sentence":"Ihulog mo ang sobre sa kahong **pangkoreo**.","translation":"Drop the envelope into the **mail**box."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng kakayahang pigilin o kontrolin ang sariling damdamin, pagnanasa, o kilos.
original_explanation: This is your inner strength when you see a 12.12 sale but your credit card is crying. It's the power you summon to not clap back at a rude comment online. It's biting your tongue during a meeting when a colleague presents your idea as their own. The ultimate 'tiis ganda' but for your emotions.
usage_notes: Refers to the ability to control one's emotions and impulses.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinakailangan ang **pagkamatimpi** upang maiwasan ang gulo.","translation":"**Self-control** is needed to avoid trouble."},{"sentence":"Ipinamalas niya ang kanyang **pagkamatimpi** sa kabila ng mga panunukso.","translation":"He showed his **restraint** despite the taunts."}]

translation: to tear off, to rip off
meaning_filipino: Ang sapilitang pagtanggal o pag-alis sa isang bagay na nakadikit sa pamamagitan ng paghila o pagbabalat, tulad ng langib o sticker.
original_explanation: It's that irresistible urge to peel off a scab, a sticker, or the plastic film on a new appliance. That satisfying (or sometimes painful) rip? That's 'pumuknat'. Your mom told you not to do it to your 'sugat', but you did it anyway.
usage_notes: Implies something was adhered or attached and is now being forcefully peeled or ripped away.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong piliting **pumuknat** ng langib at baka magkasugat muli.","translation":"Don't force yourself to **tear off** the scab or you might get wounded again."},{"sentence":"**Pumuknat** ang bata ng poster na nakadikit sa pader.","translation":"The child **ripped off** the poster stuck to the wall."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pagkaing meryenda sa Pilipinas na gawa sa kamote na hiniwa, pinirito, at binalutan ng tinunaw na pulang asukal, at karaniwang tinutuhog sa patpat na kawayan.
etymology: Isang portmanteau ng salitang Tagalog na "kamote" (sweet potato) at Ingles na "barbecue" (tumutukoy sa pagiging nakatuhog nito).
original_explanation: The healthier (or so we tell ourselves) cousin of banana cue. It's that bright orange, super sweet, and sticky merienda you buy on the street. That moment when you get a piece of **camote cue** and the caramelized sugar is perfectly crunchy? Pure bliss. It's the ultimate budget-friendly pamatid-gutom.
usage_notes: Ang pagbaybay na "camoteque" ay isang karaniwang baryasyon, ngunit ang "camote cue" o "kamote-cue" ay ang mas pamantayan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pabili po ng dalawang **camote cue**.","translation":"Can I buy two **camote cues**, please?"},{"sentence":"Amoy pa lang ng nilulutong **camote cue** ay nakakagutom na.","translation":"Just the smell of **camote cue** being cooked is enough to make you hungry."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mawalan ng malay o panandaliang ulirat, karaniwan dahil sa matinding emosyon, pagod, o sakit.
original_explanation: That feeling when you stand up too fast after a long meeting. Or when your crush finally talks to you and your soul briefly leaves your body. "Bes, muntik na akong `desmayahin` sa kilig!" Can also be used for actual medical fainting, but the dramatic version is more fun.
usage_notes: The verb form `mahilo` (to get dizzy) is more common in everyday speech, while `desmayahin` or `himatayin` implies a full loss of consciousness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halos **desmayahin** ang babae sa sobrang init sa loob ng tren.","translation":"The woman almost **fainted** from the extreme heat inside the train."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi ako madaling **desmayahin**.","translation":"Don't worry, I don't **faint** easily."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga pagkain na nagmula sa dagat, kabilang ang mga isda, hipon, alimango, talaba, at iba pang lamang-dagat.
original_explanation: Anything you can eat that once lived in the sea. This is the star of the show at any Dampa-style restaurant. From inihaw na pusit to sinigang na hipon and baked tahong, pagkaing-dagat is the reason you're willing to get your hands dirty and maybe risk an allergy attack. Worth it.
usage_notes: A very common compound noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig ako sa lahat ng klase ng **pagkaing-dagat**.","translation":"I love all kinds of **seafood**."},{"sentence":"Sariwa ang mga **pagkaing-dagat** na tinda sa palengke tuwing umaga.","translation":"The **seafood** sold at the market every morning is fresh."}]

translation: prostrate; fallen flat on the ground
meaning_filipino: Nakahandusay o nakadapa sa lupa, karaniwan dahil sa matinding pagod, sakit, pagkatalo, o kawalan ng malay.
etymology: Hindi tiyak ang pinagmulan, ngunit ito ay isang salitang matatagpuan sa iba't ibang rehiyonal na wika sa Pilipinas.
original_explanation: This is you after a full week of OT, lying face down on your bed. It's the state of a boxer after a knockout punch. It's the ultimate 'I give up' physical position. 'Pagod na pagod ako, **bulaid** ako sa sahig pag-uwi.'
usage_notes: Isang napaka-deskriptibong salita ngunit hindi pangkaraniwan sa pang-araw-araw na usapan. Ang 'handusay' ay isang mas karaniwang kasingkahulugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natagpuan siyang **bulaid** sa tabi ng ilog.","translation":"He was found **prostrate** beside the river."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa matinding pagod, ang manlalaro ay **bulaid** sa damuhan.","translation":"Due to extreme exhaustion, the player was **fallen flat** on the grass."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawing biktima ang isang tao; manakit, manloko, o mang-abuso sa isang tao.
original_explanation: Ito yung action na ginagawa ng mga scammer, manggagantso, at mga pa-fall. 'Pag may kumuha ng pera mo via a fake text message, na-biktimahin ka. 'Pag may nang-ghost sa'yo after ng 3 months na landian, na-biktimahin ka rin. Basically, the act of making someone a 'biktima'.
usage_notes: Isang pandiwa na nabuo mula sa pangngalang 'biktima'. Ito ay pandiwang palipat, na nangangailangan ng tuwirang layon (ang binibiktima).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag nating hayaang **biktimahin** ng mga manloloko ang mga matatanda.","translation":"Let's not allow scammers to **victimize** the elderly."},{"sentence":"Maraming turista ang nabibiktima ng mga pekeng tour guide.","translation":"Many tourists are being victimized by fake tour guides."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kilos, panukala, o gawain na isinasagawa upang makamit ang isang layunin o malutas ang isang suliranin.
etymology: From `hakbang` (step) + `-in` (suffix indicating an object or action).
original_explanation: This is the corporate or government version of "making a move." When your boss says, "Anong mga hakbangin ang gagawin natin para ma-hit ang quota?" they're asking for a game plan, not just random ideas. It's the "what's the next step?" but with more PowerPoint slides.
usage_notes: Often used in formal contexts like government, business, and planning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpanukala ang gobyerno ng mga bagong **hakbangin** upang labanan ang kahirapan.","translation":"The government proposed new **initiatives** to combat poverty."},{"sentence":"Anong **hakbangin** ang dapat nating gawin para mapabuti ang ating serbisyo?","translation":"What **steps** should we take to improve our service?"}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi makatwiran; laban sa lohika o sentido komon; katawa-tawa dahil sa kawalan ng katuturan.
etymology: Posibleng mula sa salitang Malay na 'baligh' na nangangahulugang pagbibinata o pagdadalaga, ngunit hindi malinaw ang pagbabago ng kahulugan nito sa Tagalog patungo sa 'absurdo'. Ipinapahiwatig nito ang kamangmangan o kawalang-gulang ng pag-iisip.
original_explanation: Ito yung mga argumentong parang 'earth is flat' o yung ex mong nagsasabing 'nagbago na ako' for the 10th time. Yung tipong mapapakamot ka na lang sa ulo at masasabing, 'Seryoso ba 'to?' Isang ideyang so out there, it's not even in the same universe as common sense.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang isang argumento, pahayag, o sitwasyon na lubos na walang katuturan. Mas matindi ang kahulugan nito ng pagiging di-lohikal kaysa sa pagiging katawa-tawa o nakakatuwa lamang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Baligho** ang kanyang paniniwala na lilipad siya kung tatalon mula sa gusali.","translation":"His belief that he would fly if he jumped from the building is **absurd**."},{"sentence":"Isang **balighong** ideya ang subukang magbenta ng yelo sa mga Eskimo.","translation":"It's a **ridiculous** idea to try to sell ice to Eskimos."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginagawa o nangyayari nang may pagitan o palitan; hindi magkakasunod o sabay-sabay.
original_explanation: This is your A-B-A-B pattern. Parang 'yung pag-inom niyo ng soju at pagkain ng samgyup, salitan dapat. It's the adjective form of taking turns. Imagine black and white tiles on a floor.
usage_notes: The stress is on the second syllable: sa-LI-tan. Often used interchangeably with 'salisi' and 'halinhinan'. The hyphenated spelling 'sal-itan' is sometimes used to distinguish it from the verb form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Salitan** ang puti at itim na teklado ng piano.","translation":"The white and black keys of the piano are **alternating**."},{"sentence":"Dapat **salitan** ang pag-aaral at paglalaro.","translation":"Studying and playing should be done **by turns**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng matibay na tela o lona na karaniwang gawa sa koton o linen, ginagamit sa paggawa ng tolda, layag, sapatos, at para sa pagpipinta.
original_explanation: This is the OG heavy-duty fabric. Before there were high-tech polymers, there was *kanyamaso*. It's the tough stuff your Converse shoes, your tote bag, and the painter's canvas are made of. It's the fabric that says, "I'm not fancy, but I will not break on you."
usage_notes: Often used to refer to the material for shoes (like sneakers), bags, and painting canvases. "Lona" is a more common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sapatos niya ay yari sa **kanyamaso**.","translation":"His shoes are made of **canvas**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng pintor ng bagong **kanyamaso** para sa kanyang obra.","translation":"The painter needs a new **canvas** for his masterpiece."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang huling bahagi, punto, o hangganan ng isang bagay, pangyayari, o panahon.
etymology: From `ka-` + `wakas` + `-an`, forming a noun that means 'the end'.
original_explanation: The final episode of your favorite K-drama. The moment you finally pay off your credit card debt. The "The End" screen of your life's chapters. It can be sad, happy, or just plain "Hay, salamat, tapos na!"
usage_notes: More formal and literary than the simpler 'wakas' or 'katapusan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lahat ay umaasa sa isang masayang **kawakasan** ng kuwento.","translation":"Everyone is hoping for a happy **ending** to the story."},{"sentence":"Sumapit na ang **kawakasan** ng kanyang paghahari.","translation":"The **end** of his reign has come."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagmulat ng mga mata at pagkakaroon ng ulirat mula sa pagtulog.
original_explanation: That moment of panic when you wake up and realize it's Monday. Or worse, you check your phone and see a dozen missed calls from your boss. "Uy, magising ka na sa katotohanan, hindi ka na niya babalikan."
usage_notes: Can be used literally for waking from sleep or figuratively for 'waking up' to a certain reality.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **magising** nang maaga bukas para sa flight ko.","translation":"I need to **wake up** early tomorrow for my flight."},{"sentence":"Oras na para **magising** sa katotohanan na kailangan mo nang mag-budget.","translation":"It's time to **wake up** to the reality that you need to start budgeting."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng kasagutan o katumbas na reaksyon sa isang stimuli, tanong, o panawagan.
original_explanation: Basically a synonym for `tugunan`, but sometimes feels more direct, like answering a call or a direct question. When someone calls your name in a crowded mall, you `tugunin` them. When a survey asks for your opinion, you `tugunin` it. It's the act of completing the communication loop.
usage_notes: Verb, object focus. Often interchangeable with `tugunan`, but `tugunin` can feel more focused on a single, direct reply to a call or question.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **tugunin** mo ang aking tawag.","translation":"Please, **answer** my call."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **tugunin** ang mga katanungang walang malinaw na sagot.","translation":"It is difficult to **answer** questions that have no clear answers."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng tradisyonal na telang hinabi sa kamay mula sa rehiyon ng Kanlurang Visayas, lalo na sa Iloilo, na karaniwang gawa sa pinya, abaka, o bulak.
original_explanation: Not just any woven cloth, this is the signature textile of Iloilo. It's the fabric equivalent of La Paz Batchoy – a proud product of the region. Wearing **hablon** is like wearing a piece of Filipino heritage, and it's making a huge comeback in modern fashion.
usage_notes: A specific, culturally significant textile. Not a generic term for woven cloth.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **hablon** ay isang patunay ng mayamang kultura ng paghahabi sa Pilipinas.","translation":"**Hablon** is a testament to the rich weaving culture in the Philippines."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang indibidwal, grupo, o institusyon na nagmamay-ari ng kahit isang share ng stock sa isang kumpanya. Sila ay maituturing na isa sa mga may-ari.
original_explanation: Ito yung mga taong may hawak ng 'share'. Sila yung mga umaasa na tataas ang value ng stocks para yumaman, o kinakabahan kapag bumabagsak ito. Sila ang mga totoong 'boss' ng mga CEO, at sila ang pinapakinggan sa mga annual meetings.
usage_notes: Used in formal business and legal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **shareholder** ay boboto para sa bagong board of directors.","translation":"The **shareholders** will vote for the new board of directors."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain, industriya, o negosyo ng pag-oorganisa ng mga paglalakbay para sa kasiyahan, pag-aaral, o libangan, lalo na ang pag-aasikaso sa mga turista.
original_explanation: This is the industry that powers all your beach trips to Boracay and mountain adventures in Sagada. It's the reason for overpriced souvenirs and the 'It's More Fun in the Philippines' slogan. Basically, it's the business of showing off how beautiful our country is to both locals and foreigners.
usage_notes: Directly equivalent to the English word 'tourism'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang naitutulong ng **turismo** sa ekonomiya ng Pilipinas.","translation":"**Tourism** contributes greatly to the Philippine economy."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating isulong ang responsableng **turismo** para mapangalagaan ang ating kalikasan.","translation":"We need to promote responsible **tourism** to protect our environment."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang nagpapahiwatig ng pagkakatulad, pagwawangis, o pag-aakala; katumbas ng tila, para, o wari.
original_explanation: This is the 'thou' and 'hath' of Tagalog. You'd use this if you were writing the next 'Florante at Laura' or trying to sound super deep and poetic for a spoken-word piece. In normal conversation, using 'anaki' is like showing up to a beach party in a full suit of armor. Just use 'parang' or 'tila'.
usage_notes: Makaluma at pampanitikan. Pangunahing matatagpuan sa mga klasikong panitikan at pormal na tula.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang ganda, **anaki**'y bituin sa kalangitan.","translation":"Her beauty, **it seems**, is like a star in the heavens."}]

translation: act of uprooting or pulling out
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagbunot o pag-alis ng isang bagay mula sa pagkakabaon o pagkakakabit nito, karaniwan ay mga damo o buhok.
original_explanation: The official term for what you do to your underarm hair with tweezers, or what your lola does to the weeds in her garden with extreme prejudice. It's a very satisfying, if sometimes painful, act of removal.
usage_notes: More specific than 'pagbunot'. Often implies pulling out something undesirable, like weeds or stray hairs, by hand.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakapagod ang **paggalbot** ng damo sa buong hardin.","translation":"The **act of pulling out** weeds in the entire garden is tiring."},{"sentence":"Ang **paggalbot** ng kilay ay bahagi ng kanyang beauty routine.","translation":"The **plucking** of eyebrows is part of her beauty routine."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking sakuna o kapahamakan na nagdudulot ng malawakang pinsala, pagdurusa, o pagkawala.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung level-up version ng malas. Hindi lang 'to simpleng 'bad day,' ito 'yung buong Pilipinas sabay-sabay nag-post ng '#PrayFor...'. Bagyo, lindol, baha—mga superstar sa kategoryang ito. Basically, when Mother Nature decides to drop her new, devastating single.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa balita at opisyal na anunsyo, lalo na tuwing panahon ng bagyo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagdeklara ng state of calamity ang gobyerno dahil sa pinsala ng bagyo at **kalamidad**.","translation":"The government declared a state of calamity due to the damage from the storm and **calamity**."},{"sentence":"Dapat laging handa ang bawat pamilya para sa anumang **kalamidad**.","translation":"Every family should always be prepared for any **calamity**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang parirala na tumutukoy sa mga kilos, gawi, o pananalita na karaniwang iniuugnay sa mga homoseksuwal na lalaki, madalas na may halong pagkatuya o pagmamaliit.
etymology: From the English slang "fruity," used to describe gay men.
original_explanation: When someone says your behavior is "fruity," they're not talking about your diet. They mean you're acting in a way that's stereotypically gay—think limp wrists, a certain way of talking, or being overly dramatic. It can be used playfully among friends but can also be a low-key insult, so read the room, sis!
usage_notes: Often used within and outside the LGBTQ+ community. Its connotation can range from playful and descriptive to derogatory, depending on the speaker and context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinuna ng tita niya ang **fruity behavior** daw ng pamangkin niya.","translation":"His aunt commented on her nephew's supposedly **fruity behavior**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa dalawang taong mayroong lihim at kadalasang imoral na relasyon ng pag-iibigan, lalo na kung ang isa o pareho ay mayroon nang ibang kinakasama.
etymology: From `mag-` + `ka-` (denoting a pair or group) + `laguyo` (paramour). The root word itself is rarely used.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung mga bida sa 'The World of the Married' Pinoy version. 'Yung relasyong tinatago, puno ng text na 'asan ka?' at 'delete mo 'to after.' Hindi sila 'yung jowang pinopost sa FB with matching #blessed, sila 'yung rason bakit may nag-aaway sa FB. The official term for 'kabitserye' protagonists.
usage_notes: Carries a strong negative and secretive connotation, implying an illicit or adulterous affair. It's not used for regular, open couples.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nabulgar ang lihim na relasyon ng dalawang **magkalaguyo**.","translation":"The secret relationship of the two **lovers** was exposed."},{"sentence":"Maraming tsismis tungkol sa politiko at sa kanyang diumano'y **kalaguyo**.","translation":"There are many rumors about the politician and his alleged **paramour**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang siyentipikong pag-aaral ng mga tungkulin at mekanismo sa isang buhay na sistema, tulad ng sa tao, hayop, o halaman.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung science subject na nagpapaliwanag kung bakit ka kinikilig (hello, endorphins!), bakit ka gutom (hello, ghrelin!), at bakit ka antok (hello, melatonin!). Basically, the 'how it works' manual of your body.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan sa klase ng **pisyolohiya** kung paano gumagana ang katawan ng tao.","translation":"The class on **physiology** studies how the human body functions."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapatalsik ng maliliit na patak ng likido gamit ang mga daliri o isang kagamitan.
original_explanation: This is the OG way of blessing something (or someone). Picture the priest flicking holy water during a house blessing, or your lola sprinkling water on clothes before ironing them with a flat iron that uses charcoal. It's a delicate, flicking motion, not a full-on drench. It's the "salt bae" of liquids.
usage_notes: Implies a light, flicking motion to disperse liquid, often done with the fingertips.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagwisik** ng holy water ang pari sa mga deboto.","translation":"The priest **sprinkled** holy water on the devotees."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magwisik** ng tubig sa akin, mababasa ang cellphone ko!","translation":"Don't **flick** water at me, my cellphone will get wet!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hawakan ng isang tasa, basket, o anumang sisidlan, karaniwang hugis arko o bilog.
original_explanation: The thing you grip for dear life on your 'But first, coffee' mug on a Monday morning. It's the difference between a useful cup and just a ceramic cylinder. Without a pakaw, your mug is just a pen holder.
usage_notes: 'Hawakan' is a more general and common term. 'Pakaw' often refers specifically to a looped or curved handle.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka, mainit ang **pakaw** ng takure.","translation":"Be careful, the **handle** of the kettle is hot."},{"sentence":"Nabali ang **pakaw** ng paborito kong tasa.","translation":"The **handle** of my favorite cup broke."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na hindi kayang matanaw o maaninag ng mga mata dahil sa kalikasan nito, sa distansya, o sa anumang harang.
original_explanation: The status of your crush's feelings for you, or your sweldo two days after payday. It's the "404 Not Found" of your eyesight. Also, the official description of air, ghosts, and the effort you put in that your boss somehow misses.
usage_notes: A literal description of invisibility or being out of sight. The single word "di-makita" is a common, shorter equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga mikrobyo ay **hindi maaaring makita** ng ating mga mata lamang.","translation":"Microbes **cannot be seen** by our eyes alone."},{"sentence":"Nakatago siya sa lugar na **hindi maaaring makita**.","translation":"He hid in a place where he **could not be seen**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagwasak, pagtanggal, o pagwawakas sa isang estruktura, organisasyon, o samahan.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'It's over.' It's what happens to a loveteam that breaks up, a government task force that gets dissolved, or that illegal food stall the barangay officials take down. It's the end of an era, big or small.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical structures (demolition) or abstract entities like groups or laws (dissolution).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagbuwag** sa aming grupo ay ikinalungkot ng marami.","translation":"The **dissolution** of our group saddened many."},{"sentence":"Naging mabilis ang **pagbuwag** sa lumang gusali.","translation":"The **dismantling** of the old building was quick."}]

translation: to enter a rooster into a cockfight
meaning_filipino: Ipaglaban o ilahok ang isang manok na panabong sa isang labanan o sabong.
original_explanation: It's literally putting your prized fighting rooster into the ring. Metaphorically, it's when you throw a friend into a debate or a risky situation they're surprisingly good at. "Isinabong ko si Mark sa karaoke battle, ayun, nanalo!"
usage_notes: Specific to the culture of cockfighting in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-alaga siya ng manok para **isabong** sa darating na pista.","translation":"He raised a rooster to **enter into the cockfight** during the upcoming fiesta."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghingi ng tulong o saklolo, lalo na sa oras ng panganib o kagipitan.
original_explanation: Ito yung "Help!" moment mo. Yung bigla kang sumisigaw ng tulong kapag may ipis na lumilipad o kapag na-trap ka sa elevator. Sa social media, ito yung post mong "Pa-share naman po, need funds for..." The act of raising the distress signal.
usage_notes: Often used as a verb-like noun in statements, e.g., "Nagpasaklolo siya." (He asked for help.) The root word itself is "saklolo" (help/aid).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Agad siyang nag-**pasaklolo** sa mga pulis nang makita ang sunog.","translation":"He immediately **asked for help** from the police when he saw the fire."},{"sentence":"Isang malakas na sigaw ng **pasaklolo** ang narinig mula sa lumulubog na bangka.","translation":"A loud **call for help** was heard from the sinking boat."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na grupo ng mga tao na may magkakatulad na interes, layunin, o propesyon na nagsasama-sama para sa isang partikular na adhikain.
original_explanation: The official term for your 'barkada' if your barkada had meeting minutes and a treasurer. It's a club, an organization, or a brotherhood. Think Knights of Columbus, your college org, or the 'samahan ng mga senior citizen' in your barangay. It's where you find your 'ka-vibes' with a formal structure.
usage_notes: Mas pormal ang tunog kaysa sa 'samahan' o 'grupo'. Madalas gamitin para sa mga propesyonal o sibikong organisasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumali siya sa isang **kapisanan** ng mga manunulat sa kanilang lungsod.","translation":"He joined an **association** of writers in their city."},{"sentence":"Ang **kapisanan** ng mga inhenyero ay magdaraos ng kanilang taunang kumperensya.","translation":"The **society** of engineers will hold their annual conference."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maayos at kaaya-ayang galaw o tunog na may tiyak na kumpas, tulad ng sa sayaw, musika, o tula.
original_explanation: It's the groove, the sway, the vibe. 'Yung pag-indak mo sa kantang 'Raining in Manila' kahit tirik ang araw. O 'yung paggalaw ng mga puno ng niyog sa probinsya kapag mahangin. It's the natural, graceful rhythm of things, from dancing to poetry.
usage_notes: Often used in literary or artistic contexts to describe movement or sound.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakasarap pakinggan ang **indayog** ng mga alon sa dalampasigan.","translation":"The **rhythm** of the waves on the shore is so pleasant to hear."},{"sentence":"Sumabay siya sa **indayog** ng musika.","translation":"She moved along with the **rhythm** of the music."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang elementong kemikal na gas na nagbibigay ng maningning na mapula-pulang kulay-kahel na ilaw kapag ginamit sa mga ilaw at karatula. Ginagamit din upang tukuyin ang anumang matingkad na kulay.
original_explanation: That super bright, attention-grabbing color that screams '80s party, K-pop music video, or the sign of your favorite late-night lugawan. If your OOTD is neon, you're not trying to blend in. You're the human highlighter pen.
usage_notes: Refers to both the element/light and the bright, fluorescent colors. The user provided 'Neyon' which is a common phonetic spelling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng mga ilaw na **neon** sa Poblacion sa gabi.","translation":"The **neon** lights in Poblacion are beautiful at night."},{"sentence":"Bumili siya ng sapatos na kulay **neon** green.","translation":"She bought shoes that are **neon** green in color."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pambansang kapulungan ng mga mambabatas sa isang bansa, na karaniwang binubuo ng Senado at Kapulungan ng mga Kinatawan.
original_explanation: The place where laws are made... and also where marathon hearings and viral soundbites are born. It's like a massive group project where the deadlines are flexible, the arguments are televised, and the final output affects 100+ million people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinasa na sa **Konggreso** ang bagong panukalang batas.","translation":"The new bill has been passed in **Congress**."},{"sentence":"Mainit ang naging debate sa **Konggreso** tungkol sa pambansang badyet.","translation":"The debate in **Congress** about the national budget was heated."}]

translation: layered; stacked; one on top of another
meaning_filipino: Inilalarawan ang mga bagay na nakaayos nang magkakapatong o magkakasunod sa isang paraan na parang baitang.
original_explanation: Like your dirty laundry on "the chair." Or the layers of a good sans rival cake. Or the susun-suson na problema that life throws at you right before payday. It’s organized chaos, Filipino style.
usage_notes: Reduplication of the root 'suson' (layer) to indicate plurality or intensity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakaayos nang **susun-suson** ang mga libro sa estante.","translation":"The books on the shelf are arranged **in stacks**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, **susun-suson** man ang problema, malalampasan din natin 'yan.","translation":"Don't worry, even if the problems are **piled one on top of another**, we will get through them."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng mga dahilan o sagot na tila matalino ngunit walang laman, mapanlinlang, o sadyang nagpapahirap sa usapan.
etymology: From "pilosopo" (philosopher, but often used to mean smart-aleck), which is from Spanish "filósofo". The "pan-" prefix becomes "pam-" and the first syllable of the root is reduplicated.
original_explanation: This is the art of answering back with 'logic' that's designed to annoy, not to enlighten. It's what kids do when you tell them to clean their room and they ask, "What is the philosophical definition of 'clean'?" It's the verbal equivalent of an eye-roll. Pilosopo Tasyo-core.
usage_notes: Almost always has a negative connotation of being a wise-guy or being intentionally difficult.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na ang iyong **pamimilosopo** at sagutin mo nang maayos ang tanong.","translation":"Stop your **smart-alecky reasoning** and just answer the question properly."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa klase dahil sa kanyang galing sa **pamimilosopo** sa tuwing may debate.","translation":"He is known in class for his skill in **sophistry** whenever there's a debate."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na hindi pa ikinakasal o wala nang kabiyak sa buhay.
original_explanation: The default status your titas will point out at every family reunion. "Uy, 30 ka na, walang asawa?" It's not a bug, it's a feature! More time for hobbies, friends, and not having to share the remote control. Also known as being in your "single and ready to get my own condo" era.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa isang taong hindi pa kailanman ikinasal (binata/dalaga), o sa isang biyudo/biyuda o diborsiyado.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay isang ina na **walang-asawa**.","translation":"She is a **single** mother."},{"sentence":"Marami sa aking mga kaibigan sa trabaho ay **walang-asawa** pa.","translation":"Many of my friends at work are still **unmarried**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang opisyal na pagsusuri ng mga talaang pampinansyal ng isang organisasyon, kadalasang isinasagawa ng isang independiyenteng katawan.
original_explanation: BPO-speak for "auditing." This is that dreaded time of year when someone from QA or a client listens to your calls or checks your work with a fine-toothed comb. It's the corporate version of your parents checking your report card. The goal is to find errors, but everyone just hopes they pass without any major findings.
usage_notes: A clear loanword from English, commonly used in business and finance contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang isinasagawang **pag-aawdit** sa mga ahensya ng gobyerno.","translation":"The **auditing** being conducted on government agencies is strict."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating maghanda para sa taunang **pag-aawdit**.","translation":"We need to prepare for the annual **auditing**."}]

translation: wiper; rag; something to wipe with
meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay, karaniwang tela o papel, na ginagamit upang linisin o alisin ang dumi, likido, o anumang marka sa isang ibabaw.
original_explanation: Your designated "basahan". That old t-shirt from a failed political candidate that is now used to wipe up spilled coffee. From the root 'pahid' (to wipe), 'pamahiran' is the tool for the job. It could be a fancy microfiber cloth or the sleeve of your shirt in an emergency.
usage_notes: Can refer to a cloth, paper towel, or even a doormat. It's the instrument used for wiping. 'Pamunas' is a close synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha ka ng **pamahiran** at linisin mo ang natapong tubig.","translation":"Get a **rag** and wipe up the spilled water."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang panyo bilang pansamantalang **pamahiran** ng kanyang pawis.","translation":"He used his handkerchief as a temporary **wiper** for his sweat."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang nababanat na sisidlan na karaniwang yari sa goma o latex, pinapapintog sa pamamagitan ng hangin o gas tulad ng helium, at ginagamit bilang laruan o palamuti.
original_explanation: The official symbol of every Filipino birthday party, fiesta, or mall opening. A lobo is happiness you can hold until it either pops dramatically or slowly withers in a corner, much like your enthusiasm for work on a Monday. Its greatest tragedy is flying away, a classic 'sana di na lang kita binitawan' moment for every kid.
usage_notes: A very common word, especially in contexts of celebrations and childhood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumutok ang **lobo** nang matusok ng karayom.","translation":"The **balloon** popped when it was pricked by a needle."},{"sentence":"Nagpalipad ng mga puting **lobo** sa kasal.","translation":"They released white **balloons** at the wedding."}]

translation: to record; to list; to note down
meaning_filipino: Isulat o irekord ang mga impormasyon, pangyayari, o datos sa isang listahan o talaan para sa paggunita o opisyal na layunin.
original_explanation: What you do in your phone's notes app or a spreadsheet. You **magtala** your expenses to figure out where your sweldo went. You **magtala** your 'utang na loob' list for future reference. It's adulting 101: listing things down so your brain doesn't have to.
usage_notes: 'Magtala' is the action, 'talaan' is the list/record itself. 'Itala' is the object-focused version.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan ng guro ang mga estudyante na **magtala** ng mahahalagang detalye mula sa lektura.","translation":"The teacher instructed the students to **note down** important details from the lecture."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan isinasagawa ang pagharang, pagsalubong, o pag-atake sa isang gumagalaw na target.
original_explanation: The designated spot for a 'tambangan' (ambush), but not the fun kind. In action movies, this is where the hero gets cornered. In real life, it's where your friend waits to surprise you for your birthday, or where your mom waits to ask where her Tupperware is.
usage_notes: Often associated with military or strategic contexts, but can be used metaphorically.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghanda ang mga gerilya ng **sabatan** sa makitid na daan.","translation":"The guerillas prepared an **ambush point** on the narrow road."},{"sentence":"Ang kanto na iyon ang naging **sabatan** ng mga magkakalabang grupo.","translation":"That corner became the **place of interception** for the rival groups."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng pagiging pabaya, hindi pagtupad sa tungkulin o responsibilidad, at kawalan ng sapat na pag-iingat o atensyon.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `mapag-` (pagkahilig) at salitang-ugat na `pabaya` (neglect).
original_explanation: This is the groupmate who goes MIA (Missing In Action) until the day of the presentation, then asks, "Ano'ng part ko?" It's the "Bahala na si Batman" attitude applied to responsibilities. They leave things undone, forget important dates, and generally cause stress to everyone around them. Their life motto is "pwede na 'yan."
usage_notes: Isang napakalakas na negatibong katangian na nagpapahiwatig ng pagkabigo sa pagtupad ng mga tungkulin o pangangalaga sa isang bagay/tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **mapagpabaya** na magulang ang nag-iiwan sa kanyang mga anak nang walang nag-aalaga.","translation":"A **negligent** parent is one who leaves their children without a guardian."},{"sentence":"Sinisi siya sa pagiging **mapagpabaya** kaya nasunog ang gusali.","translation":"He was blamed for being **neglectful**, which is why the building burned down."}]

meaning_filipino: Alisin, tanggalin, o linisin ang isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pagkaskas o pagkayod.
original_explanation: The command form. 'Scrape it!' This is what your lola tells you to do with the coconut meat for 'gata', or what you do to get the burnt 'tutong' off the bottom of the 'kaldero'. Also applies to scraping old paint or mud off your shoes.
usage_notes: A transitive verb indicating the action of scraping is being done *to* an object. It's often used as a command.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **kaskasin** ang lumang pintura bago magpinta ulit.","translation":"You need **to scrape** the old paint off before painting again."},{"sentence":"Pakisuyong **kaskasin** mo ang niyog para sa bibingka.","translation":"Please **scrape** the coconut for the rice cake."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tumpok o bunton ng mga bagay, karaniwan ay lupa, buhangin, o basura.
original_explanation: Imagine your laundry chair—that mountain of clothes you swear you'll fold "later." That's a 'timbon'. Or the 'timbon ng hugasin' in the sink after a fiesta. It's a pile of anything that's just waiting to be dealt with, a physical manifestation of your procrastination.
usage_notes: Ang 'tambak' ay isang mas karaniwang kasingkahulugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **timbon** ng mga tuyong dahon sa ilalim ng puno ng mangga.","translation":"There is a **heap** of dry leaves under the mango tree."}]

translation: to turn over suddenly; to flip
meaning_filipino: Mabilis at biglaang ibaliktad o itaob ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: Imagine you're frantically looking for your missing AirPods. You start flipping over pillows, books, and piles of laundry. That chaotic flipping action is 'balikwasin'. You **balikwasin** everything in your path until the lost item is found. It's organized chaos in verb form.
usage_notes: This verb implies a more forceful and sometimes less careful flipping action compared to 'baliktarin'. It's often used when searching for something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **balikwasin** ang lupa para makahanap ng bulate.","translation":"You need to **turn over** the soil to find worms."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **balikwasin** ang mga papel sa mesa ko!","translation":"Don't **flip over** the papers on my desk!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging hindi mapakali, pag-aalala, o pagkabahala.
original_explanation: That feeling when you've sent a risky text and they're typing... and then they stop. That's pagkabalino. It's your inner Marites waiting for the chismis to drop, or your anxiety kicking in because your Shopee order is 'out for delivery' but it's already 9 PM.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'pag-aalala' or 'pagkabahala', but 'pagkabalino' can imply a more physical restlessness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi siya makatulog dahil sa **pagkabalino** kung papasa ba siya sa board exam.","translation":"He couldn't sleep due to his **anxiety** about whether he would pass the board exam."},{"sentence":"Nawala ang kanyang **pagkabalino** nang dumating na ang kanyang hinihintay.","translation":"His **restlessness** disappeared when the one he was waiting for finally arrived."}]

meaning_filipino: Pasanhiin o utusan ang isang tao o hayop na lumukso o tumalon.
etymology: From pa- prefix + lukso (jump) + -hin suffix, a causative verb form.
original_explanation: What a PE teacher does to students during warm-ups ('Okay class, jumping jacks!'). Also, what you do to your friend by suddenly shouting 'Boo!' from behind a door. It's the act of causing a sudden upward movement, whether for fitness or for fun.
usage_notes: Similar to 'palundagin' but 'lukso' often implies a shorter, quicker jump compared to 'lundag'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **paluksuhin** ang pusa sa ibabaw ng mesa.","translation":"He tried to **make** the cat **jump** on top of the table."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi kaagad nakikita, napapansin, o nauunawaan; tago o mahirap matukoy.
etymology: From 'di-' (not) + 'halata' (obvious, from Spanish 'halar' - to pull, which evolved into a sense of 'drawing out' or 'making apparent').
original_explanation: The art of being low-key. It's that 'subtle' post you make about being happy right after your ex posts their new partner. It's the way you try to check your crush out without them noticing. 'Di-halata, promise!' you say, while being as obvious as a flashing neon sign.
usage_notes: A very common compound adjective. Can be written with or without a hyphen ('di halata' or 'di-halata').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lungkot sa kanyang mga mata ay **di-halata** sa unang tingin.","translation":"The sadness in her eyes was **not obvious** at first glance."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang gawing **di-halata** ang kanyang pagkagulat.","translation":"He tried to make his surprise **unnoticeable**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagbabawas o pag-aalis ng isang bahagi mula sa isang kabuuan; pagpapaliit ng dami o halaga.
original_explanation: This is what you wish your boss would do to your workload, or what you try to do with your rice intake when you're "on a diet". Pagbabawa is the opposite of 'add to cart'. It's the painful but necessary act of cutting back.
usage_notes: Synonymous with 'pagbabawas', but 'pagbabawas' is more commonly used in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagbabawa** ng asukal sa diyeta ay mabuti para sa kalusugan.","translation":"The **act of reducing** sugar in one's diet is good for the health."},{"sentence":"Nagpatupad ang kumpanya ng **pagbabawa** sa mga hindi kinakailangang gastos.","translation":"The company implemented a **lessening** of unnecessary expenses."}]

translation: to be made to flinch or twitch
meaning_filipino: Hindi sinasadyang mapagalaw o manginig nang bigla dahil sa gulat, takot, o kiliti.
original_explanation: That sudden, involuntary little jump you do when someone tickles you or when a creepy-crawly touches your skin. "Huwag mo 'kong gulatin, mabilis akong mapakislot." It's the body's mini-panic attack.
usage_notes: Refers to a quick, sudden, involuntary movement.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Napakislot** siya nang biglang may humawak sa kanyang balikat.","translation":"He **flinched** when someone suddenly touched his shoulder."},{"sentence":"Madali siyang **mapakislot** kahit sa mahinang kiliti lang.","translation":"She is easily **made to twitch** even with just a light tickle."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglabas ng hangin mula sa tiyan sa pamamagitan ng bibig, na karaniwang may kasamang tunog.
original_explanation: That sound you make after chugging a whole bottle of Coke Zero. It's your stomach's way of saying "Salamat, 'teh!" or "Excuse me po." In a formal dinner, you try to suppress it, but like your feelings for your crush, it just comes out.
usage_notes: Often used with the verb 'dumighal' (to burp).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malakas na **dighal** ang pinakawalan ng sanggol pagkatapos dumede.","translation":"The baby let out a loud **burp** after feeding."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang basta-basta dumidighal sa harap ng pagkain, wala kang modo!","translation":"Don't just **burp** in front of food, you have no manners!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng pagiging hindi nagdaramot; mapagbigay at bukas-palad sa kapwa.
original_explanation: That friend who always says 'Kain tayo!' and actually means it, sharing their food without you even asking. The opposite of someone who counts the number of fries you take from their plate. A true treasure, protect them at all costs.
usage_notes: A positive attribute describing a generous personality. The simple negation 'hindi maramot' is also very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala si Aling Nena sa pagiging **di-maramot** sa kanyang mga kapitbahay.","translation":"Aling Nena is known for being **generous** to her neighbors."},{"sentence":"Salamat sa tulong mo, tunay kang **di-maramot** na kaibigan.","translation":"Thanks for your help, you are truly a **not selfish** friend."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal at malalim na kasunduan sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang panig; maaari ring tumukoy sa isang takdang pagkikita o usapan.
original_explanation: This is a promise with a capital P. Not just a simple "I promise," but a solemn, binding agreement. Think "Luma at Bagong Tipan" (Old and New Testament). On a less serious note, it's the old-school word for a date or appointment. "May tipan kami mamaya" sounds way more dramatic than "We have a date later." It's like you're meeting for a secret treaty negotiation, not just for milk tea.
usage_notes: May dalawang pangunahing kahulugan: (1) isang seryosong kasunduan (covenant), at (2) isang takdang pagkikita (appointment/date). Ang konteksto ang magdidikta ng kahulugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kasal ay isang banal na **tipan** sa harap ng Diyos.","translation":"Marriage is a holy **covenant** before God."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, darating ako sa ating **tipan**.","translation":"Don't worry, I will come to our **agreed meeting**."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa pagkain na mayaman at masarap ang lasa.
original_explanation: The highest compliment you can give to your tita's cooking. It's when the adobo isn't just salty, but has that perfect blend of soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, and pepper. It's the opposite of 'matabang.' It's food that makes you say 'extra rice, please!'
usage_notes: A universal compliment for good food.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Wow, ang **malasa** ng luto mong sinigang!","translation":"Wow, the sinigang you cooked is so **flavorful**!"},{"sentence":"Mas **malasa** ang pagkain kapag bagong luto.","translation":"Food is **tastier** when freshly cooked."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit at makipot na daanan o kalye, karaniwang nasa pagitan ng mga gusali o bahay.
original_explanation: The shortcut you take to avoid traffic or your neighbor you owe money to. The iskinita is that narrow pathway where motorcycles magically fit, where kids play patintero, and where you're never quite sure if that's a cat or a giant rat in the shadows.
usage_notes: The '-ita' suffix denotes its small size, literally 'small corner' or alleyway leading from a corner.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumaan kami sa madilim na **iskinita** para mas mapabilis ang aming lakad.","translation":"We passed through a dark **alley** to make our walk faster."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga maliliit at makukulay na butil, karaniwang gawa sa mga tunay na korales o sa imitasyon nito, na ginagamit sa paggawa ng alahas tulad ng kuwintas o pulseras.
original_explanation: Not the animal pen ('kural'), but the bling! These are the red or pink beads your lola might have on her fancy rosary or necklace. It's old-school accessory, often believed to ward off 'usog' (evil eye/hex). So it's both fashion and a spiritual life hack.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively refers to coral beads used in jewelry or rosaries, not the living coral reefs (which are 'bahura').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Regalo ng lola niya ang kuwintas na gawa sa **kurales**.","translation":"Her necklace made of **corals** was a gift from her grandmother."},{"sentence":"Pinaniniwalaang nagtataboy ng masamang espiritu ang pulseras na may **kurales**.","translation":"A bracelet with **coral beads** is believed to ward off evil spirits."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapanggap o pagkukunwari sa isang bagay na hindi totoo; pag-aarte.
original_explanation: The OG 'acting busy' move. When your boss walks by, you `magbalabala` by typing furiously on your keyboard, even if you were just watching cat videos. It's pretending to be sick to skip school, or acting like you didn't hear your mom calling you to do chores. The art of the fake-out.
usage_notes: Often used with a clause explaining what is being feigned. Synonymous with 'magkunwari'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagbalabala** siyang tulog para hindi mautusan.","translation":"He **pretended** to be asleep so he wouldn't be asked to do an errand."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magbalabala** na hindi mo alam ang nangyari.","translation":"Don't **feign** ignorance about what happened."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sinaunang wikang Italic na ginamit sa Imperyong Romano; tumutukoy din sa mga taong mula sa Latium o sa mga kultura at bansang gumagamit ng mga wikang Romans.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na "Latin", na mula sa Latin na "Latīnus".
original_explanation: The original "nosebleed" language. Before there was English, there was Latin. It's the language of science, law, and the Catholic Mass back in the day. Basically, the ultimate "ma, pa-recite ako ng scientific name" language.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa mga kontekstong akademiko, siyentipiko, at relihiyoso sa Pilipinas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga siyentipikong pangalan ng mga halaman at hayop ay madalas nasa wikang **Latin**.","translation":"The scientific names of plants and animals are often in the **Latin** language."}]

translation: to skim from, to take a portion from
meaning_filipino: Kumuha ng bahagi mula sa isang mas malaking kabuuan, karaniwan ay mula sa ibabaw ng isang likido o bunton.
original_explanation: What you do to the *latik* forming on top of the coconut milk you're cooking. It's also what you do when you 'borrow' a few fries from your friend's Large Fries. 'Pahingi ako' is the request, but the action is mang-**halawan**.
usage_notes: Often used in cooking contexts, like skimming fat from broth, or in a more general sense of taking a small amount from a larger source.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **halawan** ng taba ang sabaw habang kumukulo ito.","translation":"You need to **skim** the fat from the broth while it is boiling."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **halawan** ang kanin habang hindi pa luto.","translation":"Don't **take a portion from** the rice while it's not yet cooked."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng pagiging hindi mapakali, balisa, o hindi matahimik ang kalooban o katawan.
etymology: From 'di-' (not) + 'mapalagay' (to be at ease, to be placed).
original_explanation: This is that feeling when you're waiting for a text back from your crush, or when you've submitted your resignation and are waiting for your boss to read the email. You keep checking your phone, pacing around... 'yan ang di-mapalagay. It's your body's 'seen-zoned' status.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a state of anxiety or anxious anticipation about a specific event or outcome.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Di-mapalagay** si Ana habang hinihintay ang resulta ng kanyang exam.","translation":"Ana was **restless** while waiting for the results of her exam."},{"sentence":"Mula nang mag-away sila, **di-mapalagay** ang kanyang loob.","translation":"Ever since they fought, his heart has been **uneasy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang santong itinuturing na taga-ingat at tagapagtanggol ng isang tao, lugar, o pangkat. Maaari ring tumukoy sa isang taong nagbibigay ng suportang pinansyal o iba pang tulong sa isang artista o institusyon.
original_explanation: Your town's patron saint, the reason why there's a fiesta every year. It's the 'official' heavenly protector of your city. It can also mean a sponsor or a rich tito/tita who funds your art project or small business. "Sino ba ang patron ng fiesta natin?" is a classic question.
usage_notes: Malaki ang kaugnayan nito sa kulturang Katoliko sa Pilipinas, lalo na sa mga pista.
