usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **patron** ng aming bayan ay si San Isidro Labrador.","translation":"The **patron saint** of our town is Saint Isidore the Laborer."}]

translation: to deliberately act slow; to slow down intentionally
meaning_filipino: Sadyain ang pagiging mabagal sa pagkilos o paggawa upang maantala ang isang gawain.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you're about to be asked to do another chore after finishing the first one. You suddenly move in slow motion, hoping the person who's about to give the order gets impatient and just does it themselves. It's weaponized slowness. Or that one person in the group project who takes forever to do their part.
usage_notes: This implies intentionality, as opposed to just 'bumagal' (to slow down).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magmabagal** diyan at baka maiwan tayo ng bus.","translation":"Don't **deliberately act slow** over there or we might miss the bus."},{"sentence":"Parang sinasadyang **magmabagal** ng serbisyo para mapilitan kang bumili ng inumin.","translation":"It seems the service is **intentionally slowing down** to force you to buy a drink."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aaral ng wika sa mga nakasulat na makasaysayang batis; ito ay isang kumbinasyon ng kritisismo sa panitikan, kasaysayan, at linggwistika.
etymology: From Spanish 'filología', from Latin 'philologia', from Ancient Greek 'φιλολογία' (philología, 'love of speech').
original_explanation: The high-level, academic study of language and literature. It's like being a detective, but instead of solving crimes, you're figuring out the history and structure of words. Think of it as the ultimate 'word nerd' field. Not to be confused with philosophy (pilosopiya), though they might both hang out in the same university coffee shop.
usage_notes: A very specific academic term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dalubhasa siya sa **pilolohiya** at pag-aaral ng mga sinaunang teksto.","translation":"She is an expert in **philology** and the study of ancient texts."}]

translation: a shake of the head (in disapproval or negation)
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggalaw ng ulo pakanan at pakaliwa bilang tanda ng pagtanggi, hindi pagsang-ayon, o pagkadismaya.
original_explanation: The non-verbal 'No.' The classic parent move when you ask for a new gadget. It’s what you give your friend when they're about to make a bad decision. A single, powerful **iling** can say more than a thousand words, like 'Ayoko,' 'Hindi pwede,' or 'Sinasabi ko na nga ba.'
usage_notes: The noun for the action. The verb form is `umiling` (to shake one's head).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **iling** lang ang sagot niya sa aking tanong.","translation":"Just a **shake of the head** was his answer to my question."},{"sentence":"Makikita mo sa kanyang mga **iling** ang labis na pag-aalala.","translation":"You could see in the **shakes of his head** his extreme worry."}]

translation: to cause chaos or confusion; to make a mess
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging sanhi ng kawalan ng kaayusan, pagkalito, o kaguluhan sa isang sitwasyon o lugar.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung specialty ng 'pasaway' sa pamilya o barkada. Siya 'yung expert **magpagulo** ng plano. O 'yung little pamangkin mo na dumaan sa sala, one minute malinis, next minute parang dinaanan ng bagyo. Expert magpagulo!
usage_notes: Can refer to creating physical mess or causing social/mental confusion and trouble.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumasok lang siya sa kwarto para **magpagulo** ng gamit ko.","translation":"He only entered the room to **make a mess** of my things."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magpagulo** ng isip ko, diretsuhin mo na ang sasabihin mo.","translation":"Don't **cause my thoughts to get jumbled**; just say what you need to say directly."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkulong sa isang tao sa bilangguan o selda bilang parusa sa isang krimen o habang naghihintay ng paglilitis.
original_explanation: The next level after 'iposas'. This is when the court says "Guilty!" and you get a long-term, government-sponsored staycation with free, albeit terrible, food. "Huwag kang gagawa ng masama kung ayaw mong ma-ipreso."
usage_notes: Often used in the passive form 'maipreso' (to be imprisoned).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sinumang mapatunayang nagkasala ay dapat **ipreso**.","translation":"Anyone proven guilty must be **imprisoned**."},{"sentence":"Binalaan niya ang anak na **ipapapreso** niya ito kung hindi titino.","translation":"He warned his child that he would have him **jailed** if he didn't straighten up."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng kaaya-ayang anyo; malinis, maayos, at angkop tingnan para iharap sa publiko o sa isang okasyon.
original_explanation: Your mom's favorite word before you leave the house. 'Mag-ayos ka para **presentable** ka naman.' It's the minimum requirement for meeting your jowa's parents, attending a job interview, or taking a new profile pic. Hindi kailangang artistahin, basta malinis at maayos.
usage_notes: Widely used in Taglish and informal conversations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siguraduhin mong **presentable** ang iyong sarili sa job interview.","translation":"Make sure you are **presentable** for the job interview."},{"sentence":"Kahit simpleng polo at pantalon lang, basta malinis ay **presentable** na.","translation":"Even just a simple polo and pants, as long as it's clean, is already **presentable**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malambot at matamis na tinapay o keyk na gawa sa itlog, harina, at asukal, na may magaang na pagkayari.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na 'mamón', isang uri ng sponge cake.
original_explanation: The ultimate Pinoy comfort food. That soft, fluffy, slightly sweet cake you get from Goldilocks or Red Ribbon. It's the go-to pasalubong and the star of every merienda. Sometimes with cheese on top. Also used as a 'hugot' term for someone who is soft-hearted, "pusong mamon".
usage_notes: Maaari ring gamitin bilang talinghaga para ilarawan ang isang taong napakalambot ng puso o madaling masaktan ('pusong mamon').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong kainin ang **mamon** na may kasamang mainit na kape.","translation":"My favorite thing to eat is **sponge cake** with hot coffee."},{"sentence":"Para siyang **mamon** sa lambot ng kanyang puso.","translation":"He/She is like a **sponge cake** for having such a soft heart."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpilit na ituloy ang isang bagay sa kabila ng mga hadlang; ang pagpupumilit na gawin o makamit ang isang layunin.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Ingles na "push," ngunit may pagbabago sa kahulugan sa Taglish upang mangahulugang "ituloy" o "ipilit."
original_explanation: The Pinoy battle cry for "Go for it!" or "Make it happen!" When your friend is hesitant to apply for that dream job, you say "I-**push** mo 'yan, mars!" It's the verbal equivalent of a supportive shove in the right direction. Use it when you're trying to convince yourself to buy that 12.12 sale item you don't really need.
usage_notes: Isang napaka-karaniwang pandiwang balbal sa Taglish. Madalas itong nilalapian ng mga panlaping Filipino tulad ng "i-push" o "pinu-push."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit mahirap, i-**push** natin itong project hanggang matapos.","translation":"Even if it's hard, let's **push through** with this project until it's finished."},{"sentence":"Gusto mo ba talaga? Sige, **push** mo lang!","translation":"Do you really want it? Go on, just **go for it**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o akto ng pagbibigay ng kahulugan, paliwanag, o interpretasyon sa isang salita, konsepto, o pangyayari.
etymology: From pag- (gerund prefix) + papaka- (causative/intensive prefix) + kahulugan (meaning).
original_explanation: This is what you do when your crush gives you a one-word reply. You analyze it, consult your friends, and try to find the 'deep meaning' behind that 'K.' It's the act of defining things, from a word in a dictionary to your 'what are we?' relationship status.
usage_notes: A formal term used in academic, literary, and legal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iba-iba ang **pagpapakahulugan** ng mga kritiko sa tula.","translation":"The critics have different **interpretations** of the poem."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang tamang **pagpapakahulugan** sa mga batas upang maiwasan ang kalituhan.","translation":"The correct **giving of meaning** to laws is important to avoid confusion."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang batayang yunit ng haba sa sistemang metriko, katumbas ng 100 sentimetro. Ginagamit din bilang pinaikling tawag sa "Metro Manila".
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagamit ni manong karpintero o manang mananahi para sukatin kung gaano kahaba ang gagawin niyang lamesa o gaano kaikli ang ipapuputol mo sa pantalon mo. One metro is roughly the distance from your shoulder to your opposite fingertip. Also, 'yung "Metro Manila," pero dito, unit of measurement muna tayo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng tatlong **metro** ng tela para sa aking bestida.","translation":"I bought three **meters** of cloth for my dress."},{"sentence":"Siksikan palagi sa mga daan sa **Metro** Manila tuwing rush hour.","translation":"The roads in **Metro** Manila are always congested during rush hour."}]

meaning_filipino: May kakayahang magdulot ng kalasingan o pagkalango.
original_explanation: Obvious 'to, 'yung alak nakalalasing. Pero pwede ring gamitin sa ibang bagay. 'Yung boses niya? Nakalalasing. 'Yung titig niya? Nakalalasing. 'Yung power? Sobrang nakalalasing. Anything that makes you feel dizzy, giddy, and makes you do stupid things can be described as nakalalasing.
usage_notes: Used for alcoholic beverages and metaphorically for anything that can overwhelm the senses or judgment, like love, power, or perfume.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa pag-inom ng lambanog dahil ito ay tunay na **nakalalasing**.","translation":"Be careful drinking coconut wine because it is truly **intoxicating**."},{"sentence":"May **nakalalasing** na ganda ang tanawin mula sa tuktok ng bundok.","translation":"The view from the mountain top has an **intoxicating** beauty."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagkonsumo ng pagkain; ang pagpasok ng pagkain sa bibig upang magbigay sustansya sa katawan. Ito ay nasa anyong pautos o obhektibong pokus ng pandiwang "kain".
original_explanation: This is the command form of "to eat." It's what your mom yells when the food is ready, or what you tell yourself when you see that box of pizza after a long day at work. "Kainin mo na 'yan!" means "Just eat it already!" It's the action of devouring something specific, like your feelings... or a whole lechon.
usage_notes: This is the object-focus form of the verb. The actor-focus form is "kumain". For example, "Kainin mo ang kanin" (You eat the rice) vs. "Kumain ka ng kanin" (You eat some rice).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kainin** mo na ang almusal mo bago ka umalis.","translation":"**Eat** your breakfast before you leave."},{"sentence":"Masarap **kainin** ang mangga kapag malamig.","translation":"It's delicious to **eat** mangoes when they're cold."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagputol o paghiwalay ng isang matigas na bagay sa dalawa o higit pang piraso, tulad ng patpat o buto, sa pamamagitan ng pwersa.
original_explanation: 'Bumali' is that sharp *snap* sound. It's what you do to a stick of barbecue before throwing it away. It's what happens to your bone if you fall off a bike the wrong way. Figuratively, it's also what someone does to a promise ('bumali sa usapan'). It's a clean, forceful break.
usage_notes: Used for long, thin, rigid objects like sticks, bones, pencils, etc. Differentiated from "basag" (for glass, plates) and "punit" (for paper, cloth).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **bumali** ng patpat gamit ang kanyang tuhod.","translation":"He tried to **break** a stick using his knee."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa pag-akyat, baka may **bumali** na sanga.","translation":"Be careful climbing, a branch might **snap**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghinto sa pagtatrabaho o paglilingkod, karaniwan dahil sa pag-abot sa takdang edad o haba ng serbisyo.
original_explanation: The ultimate life goal after decades of 'pagpupuyat' and dealing with Manila traffic. It's the time when your main job becomes tending to your plants, playing with your apos, and forwarding 'good morning' chain messages on Viber. The finish line.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinaghahandaan na niya ang kanyang **pagriritiro** sa susunod na taon.","translation":"She is already preparing for her **retirement** next year."},{"sentence":"Maraming benepisyo ang kasama sa kanyang **pagriritiro**.","translation":"Many benefits are included in his **retirement**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagsipsip o paglanghap ng usok, singaw, o likido sa pamamagitan ng bibig.
original_explanation: The action of inhaling something, like smoke from a cigarette or vape ('hithit-buga'). It can also mean sipping a drink through a straw. It’s that sharp inhale, the "shloooorp" sound you make with a good iced coffee or the puff you take during a smoke break.
usage_notes: The meaning depends heavily on context. As a verb 'humithit', it can mean 'to puff a cigarette', 'to sip soup', or 'to inhale drugs'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **hithit** lang sa kanyang kape at gising na agad siya.","translation":"Just one **sip** of his coffee and he's immediately awake."},{"sentence":"Iwasan ang **hithit** ng ipinagbabawal na gamot.","translation":"Avoid the **inhalation** of illegal drugs."}]

translation: gentle touch; not leaving a mark when hitting
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na kapag namalo o humampas (lalo na sa pagdidisiplina) ay hindi nag-iiwan ng marka o hindi gaanong masakit.
original_explanation: The *good* version of 'gaan ng kamay'. This refers to someone, usually a parent disciplining a child, whose hand is "light." When they spank, it's just enough to say "I mean business" but not hard enough to actually cause injury or leave a mark. It's the old-school way of saying "I'm doing this for your own good, but I'm not a monster."
usage_notes: This positive meaning is less common today and often used by older generations to describe a specific style of physical discipline. The adjective form is 'magàan ang kamay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit pinapalo kami ni lola, **magàan ang kamay** niya at hindi kami nasasaktan nang todo.","translation":"Even if grandma would spank us, she had a **gentle touch** and we wouldn't get hurt badly."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng katangian ng batubalani; may kakayahang umakit ng metal o magkaroon ng magnetic field.
original_explanation: Literally, it has a magnet. But more often, it's used to describe someone with an irresistible charm or charisma. That person who walks into a room and everyone just gravitates towards them? 'Yan, 'yan ang may-batubalani. They have that magnetic personality, the 'it' factor. Parang BINI lang, ang lakas maka-akit ng Blooms.
usage_notes: Can be literal or figurative. The figurative sense is more poetic and less common in casual conversation but well-understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang dulo ng distornilyador na ito ay **may-batubalani** para dumikit ang turnilyo.","translation":"The tip of this screwdriver is **magnetic** so the screw will stick."},{"sentence":"Tila **may-batubalani** ang kanyang mga ngiti, lahat ay napapalingon.","translation":"Her smile seems to be **magnetic**, everyone turns to look."}]

translation: to make dirty; to get grimy
meaning_filipino: Ang pagdudulot ng dumi o pagiging marungis sa isang tao, bagay, o lugar.
etymology: From magpa- (causative prefix) + rungis (a variant of 'dungis', meaning 'grime' or 'smudge').
original_explanation: This is what kids do best after you've just given them a bath. They go outside and play in the mud, effectively 'magparungis'-ing themselves. It’s the act of making something clean into something dirty. 'Huwag kang magparungis ng damit mo, kadarating lang natin sa party!' (Don't get your clothes dirty, we just arrived at the party!).
usage_notes: The 'magpa-' prefix makes this a causative verb, meaning 'to cause to become 'marungis' (dirty/grimy).'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinabihan ng ina ang anak na huwag **magparungis** habang kumakain ng tsokolate.","translation":"The mother told her child not to **get messy** while eating chocolate."},{"sentence":"Ang paglalaro sa putikan ay tiyak na **magpaparungis** sa kanilang mga uniporme.","translation":"Playing in the mud will surely **make** their uniforms **dirty**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na gulong, karaniwang nakakabit sa ilalim ng isang kasangkapan upang madali itong maigalaw o maitulak.
etymology: Posibleng mula sa salitang "gilid" (side), na tumutukoy sa isang bagay na gumagalaw sa gilid o pa-gilid.
original_explanation: ‘Yan ‘yung maliit na gulong sa ilalim ng office chair mo na laging nasasabitan ng buhok at alikabok. O ‘yung nasa ilalim ng maleta na nagpapadali ng pag-travel mo sa NAIA, hanggang sa masira ang isa at kailangan mo nang bitbitin ang buong bagahe ng buhay mo.
usage_notes: Karaniwang tumutukoy sa mga gulong ng muwebles, kariton, o maleta.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasira ang isang **parigilid** ng silya kaya hindi na ito magamit nang maayos.","translation":"One **caster** of the chair broke, so it can't be used properly anymore."},{"sentence":"Palitan mo na ang mga **parigilid** ng lumang kabinet para madaling itulak.","translation":"Replace the **casters** of the old cabinet so it's easier to push."}]

translation: to compete against each other; to clash
meaning_filipino: Maglaban o magpaligsahan nang mahigpit; magkaroon ng salungatan ng interes o opinyon.
original_explanation: This is the main event! Think rival K-drama leads fighting for the girl, two bida-kontrabidas in a teleserye finale, or your team versus your rival in the UAAP finals. It's more than just a game; it's a clash of titans, a battle of wills, a 'dapat manalo ang bet ko' moment.
usage_notes: Implies a serious or intense conflict or competition.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatakdang **magtunggalian** ang dalawang pinakamagaling na manlalaro sa kampeonato.","translation":"The two best players are set to **compete against each other** in the championship."},{"sentence":"Madalas **magtunggalian** ang kanilang mga ideya sa pulong.","translation":"Their ideas often **clash** during meetings."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paligsahan o paglalaban sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang panig para sa isang gantimpala, karangalan, o pangingibabaw.
original_explanation: The reason why your tita asks 'Kailan ka ikakasal?' at family reunions—she's competing with your other tita whose kid just got married. It's Jollibee vs. McDo. It's what happens when there's only one parking spot left at the mall. It's the Hunger Games, but with more chismis.
usage_notes: While it can also mean 'competence' or 'skill', the word 'kumpetisyon' is more specific for 'competition' or 'contest'. 'Kompetensiya' often implies a broader sense of rivalry.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang **kompetensiya** sa pagitan ng mga kandidato.","translation":"The **competition** between the candidates is tight."},{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang may **kompetensiya** sa pag-ibig.","translation":"She doesn't want any **rivalry** in love."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na varyant ng salitang 'parati' o 'palagi'; nangangahulugang sa lahat ng oras o pagkakataon.
original_explanation: A casual, slightly shortened version of 'parati'. Think of it as the lazy person's 'palagi'. 'Parating ganyan 'yan.' (He's always like that.) It flows a bit quicker in fast-paced chismisan. It's less formal than 'parati' and definitely more for everyday convo.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang kolokyalismo at mas karaniwan sa pasalitang pakikipag-usap kaysa sa pormal na pagsulat. Magkaiba ang diin nito sa pandiwang 'parating' (/pa-ra-TING/).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Parating** masaya sa bahay namin tuwing Pasko.","translation":"It's **always** happy in our house during Christmas."},{"sentence":"Bakit **parating** ikaw ang paborito ni nanay?","translation":"Why are you **always** mom's favorite?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay o palitang pagbibiro o pagtukso sa isa't isa.
original_explanation: This is the group chat dynamic when someone has a new crush. It's the reciprocal act of teasing. 'Uy, si ano...' followed by 'Ikaw nga diyan, nakita ko kayo kahapon!' That back-and-forth is 'magtudyuhan'. It's the national sport of barkadas.
usage_notes: Implies a mutual, often playful, act of teasing among two or more people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkakatuwaan ang magkakaibigan habang sila ay **nagtutudyuhan** tungkol sa kanilang mga lovelife.","translation":"The friends were having fun while they were **teasing each other** about their lovelives."},{"sentence":"Tigilan n'yo na ang **pagtutudyuhan** at kumain na tayo.","translation":"Stop **teasing one another** and let's eat."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagpapahayag ng paghanga, paggalang, o pagkilala sa kabutihan o kagalingan ng isang tao, bagay, o gawa.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'puri' (praise) at panlaping 'pa-'.
original_explanation: It's the "sana all" you receive from others. It’s what you get from your boss during performance reviews (if you're lucky), from your lola for finishing your food, or from your friends when your OOTD is on point. A papuri is verbal validation, the "good job!" that fuels the Filipino soul.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa pormal o seremonyal na konteksto, ngunit maaari ring sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatanggap siya ng maraming **papuri** para sa kanyang natatanging pagganap.","translation":"She received a lot of **praise** for her outstanding performance."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paraan o proseso ng paglutas sa isang problema o suliranin; ang resulta ng paghahanap ng sagot.
original_explanation: This is the "Aha!" moment after a long, stressful problem. 'Yung sagot sa math problem na ilang oras mong tinitigan. 'Yung pag-uusap ninyo ng jowa mo para ayusin ang L.Q. (lover's quarrel). 'Yung naisip mong paraan para umabot ang sahod mo hanggang sa susunod na kinsenas. Yan ang kalutasan. The answer, the fix, the way out.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Humanap tayo ng **kalutasan** sa problemang ito.","translation":"Let's find a **solution** to this problem."},{"sentence":"Ang mapayapang diyalogo ang tanging **kalutasan** sa kanilang hindi pagkakaunawaan.","translation":"Peaceful dialogue is the only **resolution** to their misunderstanding."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o akto ng paglampas sa isang tiyak na antas, bilang, o kalidad; pagiging mas mataas o nakahihigit.
etymology: pag- (prefix indicating action/process) + higit (more than, to exceed)
original_explanation: This is what "extra" literally means. When the bill is P950 but you give P1000, that's with paghigit. It's going above and beyond. It can refer to talent ("Ang galing niya, may paghigit sa inaasahan!"), quantity, or even drama ("Yung reaction niya, may paghigit sa sitwasyon.").
usage_notes: Can be used to mean 'more than' or 'the act of being more than'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang galing sa pagkanta ay may **paghigit** sa lahat ng sumali.","translation":"Her singing talent **surpassed** all the other contestants."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **paghigit** sa tungkulin, siya ay nabigyan ng promosyon.","translation":"Because of his **act of exceeding** his duties, he was given a promotion."}]

translation: small bamboo twig; fine fish bone
meaning_filipino: Isang maliit at matulis na sanga ng kawayan; o isang maliit na tinik ng isda.
original_explanation: That tiny, treacherous fish bone that gets stuck in your throat and turns a delicious meal into a life-or-death situation. Also, those annoying little bamboo splinters that get into your finger when you're trying to be artsy with a 'walis tingting'.
usage_notes: Can refer to a bamboo splinter or a very fine fish bone. The context usually clarifies the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natusok ang daliri ko ng **siit** ng kawayan.","translation":"My finger was pricked by a bamboo **twig**."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa pagkain ng isda, maraming maliliit na **siit**.","translation":"Be careful eating the fish, it has many fine **bones**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang kilos ng paglilimpon o pag-aayos ng isang bagay, tulad ng damit o papel, sa pamamagitan ng paglalapat ng mga gilid nito. Ito ang anyong pangkasalukuyan ng pandiwang 'magtupi'.
original_explanation: What you're doing when your friend calls and asks "Ano gawa mo?" and you want to sound productive. "Nagtutupi lang ng damit." It's the therapeutic (or tedious) process of turning chaos into neat little squares. The perfect background activity for listening to a podcast about unsolved mysteries or chismis.
usage_notes: Present progressive tense of 'magtupi'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong istorbohin, **nagtutupi** ako ng mga bagong laba.","translation":"Don't bother me, I'm **folding** the newly washed clothes."},{"sentence":"Habang nanonood ng TV, **nagtutupi** ng papel si Ana para sa kanyang origami.","translation":"While watching TV, Ana is **folding** paper for her origami."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang gamot, karaniwang nasa anyong krema o langis, na ipinapahid sa balat upang maibsan ang sakit, pamamaga, o iba pang karamdaman.
original_explanation: Your lola's go-to solution for everything from muscle pain to a broken heart. Think Vicks, Efficascent Oil, or that sketchy herbal concoction from a palengke stall. If it smells strong and feels either hot or cold on your skin, it's probably a `panghaplas`.
usage_notes: Madalas na iniuugnay sa mga tradisyonal o halamang gamot.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha ka ng **panghaplas** sa botikina para sa likod ni Lolo.","translation":"Get some **liniment** from the medicine cabinet for Grandpa's back."},{"sentence":"Mabisa ang dahon ng bayabas bilang **panghaplas** sa mga galos.","translation":"Guava leaves are effective as a **poultice** for scratches."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing mas malakas ang isang bagay, tao, o tunog; dagdagan ang puwersa, kapangyarihan, o bisa nito.
original_explanation: The verb for "power up!" This is what you do at the gym ('nagpapalakas ng katawan' - strengthening the body). It's also what you do to the TV when your favorite song comes on ('magpalakas ng volume' - make the volume louder). It's all about increasing 'lakas' (strength/loudness), whether it's your muscles, your immune system (by drinking vitamins), or your WiFi signal by moving closer to the router.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical strength, health, volume of sound, or power/influence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong kumain ng gulay para **magpalakas** ng resistensya.","translation":"You need to eat vegetables **to strengthen** your resistance."},{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **magpalakas** ka ng boses, hindi kita marinig.","translation":"Please, **make** your voice **louder**, I can't hear you."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kalagayan ng pagiging nakatigil o nakapuwesto sa isang partikular na lugar, karaniwang ginagamit para sa mga sasakyan, barko, o tropa ng militar.
original_explanation: Like your Grab driver waiting patiently outside your condo, or the jeepneys lined up at the terminal waiting for passengers. It's a state of being parked and ready, but not moving just yet. Think of it as 'standby mode.'
usage_notes: Commonly used in contexts of transportation, military, or any situation involving being stationary at a post.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May mga bus na **nakahimpil** sa terminal habang naghihintay ng pasahero.","translation":"There are buses **parked** at the terminal while waiting for passengers."},{"sentence":"Ang mga sundalo ay **nakahimpil** sa kampo.","translation":"The soldiers are **stationed** at the camp."}]

translation: getting drunk, the act of getting intoxicated
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o kilos ng pag-inom ng alak hanggang sa malasing o mawala sa sarili.
original_explanation: This is the official sport of Titos on a Friday night. It's the journey, not the destination (which is usually a massive hangover). It's the process of consuming alcoholic beverages until you start sending "u up?" texts to your ex.
usage_notes: The gerund form of 'maglasing'. Refers to the act of drinking to get drunk.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Walang mabuting naidudulot ang madalas na **paglalasing**.","translation":"Frequent **getting drunk** brings nothing good."},{"sentence":"Itigil na natin ang **paglalasing** at umuwi na tayo.","translation":"Let's stop **getting drunk** and go home."}]

translation: to be the cause of happiness
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging dahilan o sanhi ng kasiyahan o ligaya ng isang tao.
etymology: i- (causative prefix) + ka- (nature/ability prefix) + ligaya (joy, happiness)
original_explanation: 'Yung moment na natanggap mo na 'yung 13th month pay, 'yun ang ikaliligaya mo. Or a simple "I love you" from your special someone. Ito 'yung trigger ng "sana all" moments. The reason for your "inner peace" kuno.
usage_notes: Often used in the future tense (ikaliligaya) or past tense (ikinaligaya). Expresses what brings someone joy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagdating ng apo niya ang **ikinaligaya** ng matanda.","translation":"The arrival of his grandchild was the **cause of the old man's happiness**."},{"sentence":"Tiyak na **ikaliligaya** ni nanay ang mga bulaklak na ito.","translation":"Mother will surely **be made happy by** (lit: these flowers will be the cause of her happiness) these flowers."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkilos ng pagkuha o pagkopya ng isang digital na file mula sa isang server patungo sa isang lokal na aparato.
original_explanation: The infinitive form of our favorite modern-day activity. This is what you do to get apps, movies, music, and... 'research material.' It's a command: 'Mag-download ka na ng ticket para sa concert!' or a statement of ability: 'Hindi ako makapag-download, mahina ang signal.' The foundation of our digital lives.
usage_notes: A Taglish verb conjugation (mag- + root). This is the infinitive form, also used for commands.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **mag-download** ng app para makasali sa laro.","translation":"You need **to download** the app to join the game."},{"sentence":"**Mag-download** ka ng antivirus para protektahan ang computer mo.","translation":"**Download** an antivirus to protect your computer."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mag-aaral na tumatanggap ng tulong-pinansyal, tulad ng scholarship, upang makapag-aral. Maaari ring tumukoy sa isang taong dalubhasa sa isang partikular na larangan ng pag-aaral.
original_explanation: The student whose tuition is sponsored, either because they're super smart (academic scholar) or they're good at a sport (athletic scholar). They're the ones who can't afford to get a grade of 3.0 or they'll lose their funding. The "bawal bumagsak" life is their reality. Sila ang tunay na "student-athlete" or "student-achiever."
usage_notes: The native word 'iskolar' is also used interchangeably.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isa siyang **scholar** ng gobyerno kaya libre ang kanyang pag-aaral.","translation":"She is a government **scholar**, so her education is free."},{"sentence":"Kailangan niyang i-maintain ang mataas na grado para sa kanyang **scholarship**.","translation":"She needs to maintain high grades for her **scholarship**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang namumuong abo sa dulo ng sigarilyo, tabako, o anumang nasusunog na bagay na may baga.
original_explanation: That gray, fragile thing at the end of a lit cigarette that you need to tap off into an ashtray. 'Paki-tap naman 'yang **titis** ng yosi mo, baka mahulog sa damit ko.' It's the physical manifestation of something being slowly consumed. Ang hugot!
usage_notes: Primarily used for cigarettes or cigars. For general ash, 'abo' is more common. For a glowing coal, 'baga' is also used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahulog ang **titis** ng kanyang sigarilyo sa sahig.","translation":"The **ash** from his cigarette fell on the floor."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa **titis** ng kandila para hindi masunog ang mantel.","translation":"Be careful with the candle's **ember** so the tablecloth doesn't burn."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahalaga at tiyak na tungkulin o layunin na ipinagkatiwala sa isang tao o pangkat.
original_explanation: Your life's "mission" is that thing you keep telling your friends you're passionate about, but you're still working a BPO job to pay the bills. It's your "Why" in life, or just the next task your boss gives you on a Monday morning.
usage_notes: Used both in the grand sense (life mission) and the practical sense (a specific task or assignment).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **misyon** ng mga bayani ay ipaglaban ang kalayaan ng bansa.","translation":"The **mission** of the heroes was to fight for the country's freedom."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng malalim at magaslaw na tunog na karaniwang ginagawa ng mga palaka.
etymology: Onomatopoeia, from the sound a frog makes.
original_explanation: Sound effect ng mga palaka sa probinsya kapag umuulan. Kapag 'di ka makatulog sa gabi dahil sa ingay sa labas, baka hindi 'yan multo, baka mga palaka lang na **kumokak**. Ribbit ribbit!
usage_notes: Onomatopoeic word, directly imitating the sound it describes. Can be used humorously to describe a person with a hoarse voice.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Rinig na rinig ang mga palakang **kumokak** sa may sapa tuwing gabi.","translation":"The frogs **croaking** by the stream could be heard clearly every night."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **kumokak** diyan na parang palaka, uminom ka ng salabat.","translation":"Don't **croak** there like a frog, drink some ginger tea."}]

translation: to feel sleepy, to become drowsy
meaning_filipino: Ang pagdama ng pagnanais na matulog; ang unti-unting pagbigat ng talukap ng mata at paghina ng katawan dahil sa pagod o kakulangan sa tulog.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're in a 1 PM meeting after lunch, and your boss's voice starts sounding like a lullaby. You try to keep your eyes open, but the spirit is willing, and the flesh is weak. Yan ang mag-antok. It's the universe telling you, "Bes, kailangan mo na ng kape o kama."
usage_notes: Used to describe the state of becoming sleepy. `Inaantok` is the present tense ("I am sleepy").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mag-antok** sa klase kung ayaw mong mapagalitan ng guro.","translation":"Don't **get sleepy** in class if you don't want to be scolded by the teacher."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula na akong **mag-antok** pagkatapos kong kumain ng tanghalian.","translation":"I started to **feel sleepy** after eating lunch."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang marahan at magaan na pagdampi o paghimas, karaniwang nagpapahayag ng pagmamahal, pag-aalaga, o pag-alo.
original_explanation: The opposite of 'haplit'. This is the gentle, comforting touch from your lola, your jowa, or even your pet cat rubbing against your leg. It's the physical version of 'it's okay, you're safe now.' Parang 'yung feeling 'pag pumasok 'yung sahod sa bank account mo—nakakakalma.
usage_notes: Often used in romantic or familial contexts. The verb form is 'haplusin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **haplos** ng ina ay gamot sa anumang sakit.","translation":"A mother's **gentle touch** is a cure for any ailment."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang **haplos** ng hangin sa kanyang pisngi.","translation":"She felt the **caress** of the wind on her cheek."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na nasa dulo ng isang serye o pagkakasunod-sunod; hindi na sinusundan pa ng iba.
original_explanation: The grand finale! The last episode of your favorite K-drama, the last piece of lechon on the plate, your "last na 'to" promise before taking another shot. It's the end of the line. The final boss. The panghuli is often the most memorable, or the most painful.
usage_notes: Can also function as a noun, meaning "the last one."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ito na ang **panghuli** kong babala sa iyo.","translation":"This is my **final** warning to you."},{"sentence":"Siya ang **panghuli** sa pila.","translation":"He is the **last** one in line."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pagtutulad o paghahambing ng dalawa o higit pang tao, bagay, pook, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: The official term for what your parents do when they compare you to your overachiever cousin. "Pahambing" is the grammar-nerd word for comparison. "Mas matangkad" (taller), "di-gaanong masarap" (not as delicious)—these are all examples of the pahambing degree. It's the language of 'which is which' and 'who is better', a national pastime both in grammar class and at family reunions.
usage_notes: A grammatical term for the comparative degree of adjectives and adverbs. The other degrees are 'Lantay' (Positive) and 'Pasukdol' (Superlative).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang \"mas maganda\" ay isang halimbawa ng pang-uring nasa kaantasang **pahambing**.","translation":"\"More beautiful\" is an example of an adjective in the **comparative** degree."},{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng **pahambing** na pagsusuri upang ipakita ang pagkakaiba ng dalawang produkto.","translation":"He used a **comparative** analysis to show the difference between the two products."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang biglaan at malakas na pag-unos ng hangin at ulan, karaniwan ay sa dagat.
etymology: Possibly from Spanish 'galope' (gallop) or related nautical terms, combined with a local root.
original_explanation: This is the ocean's version of a sudden mood swing. One minute you're chilling on a boat, the next, sigalbo hits—a surprise party of wind and rain that nobody asked for. It's a sudden, violent storm at sea, the kind that makes sailors go, 'Ah, here we go again.'
usage_notes: Primarily used in a nautical or maritime context to describe a sudden, localized storm.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahuli ang mga mangingisda sa isang **sigalbo** sa gitna ng karagatan.","translation":"The fishermen were caught in a **squall** in the middle of the ocean."},{"sentence":"Nagbabala ang PAGASA tungkol sa posibleng **sigalbo** sa mga baybaying-dagat.","translation":"PAGASA warned about possible **squalls** along the coastlines."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na nagbibigay ng lakas, sigla, o enerhiya sa katawan o isipan.
original_explanation: Your legal drug of choice to survive the daily grind. Usually comes in the form of kape, energy drink, or a quick workout. It's the "pampagising" you need for that 9 AM meeting after binge-watching a series until 3 AM. The official fuel of the BPO industry and college students during finals week.
usage_notes: Can refer to drinks, food, activities, or even music that boosts energy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng kape bilang **pampasigla** sa umaga.","translation":"I need coffee as an **energizer** in the morning."},{"sentence":"Ang ehersisyo ay mabisang **pampasigla** ng katawan at isip.","translation":"Exercise is an effective way to **invigorate** the body and mind."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang babaeng mayroong hika, isang malalang sakit sa baga na nagdudulot ng pamamaga at pagkitid ng mga daanan ng hangin.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "asmática," ang pambabaeng anyo ng "asmático" (asthmatic).
original_explanation: Your tita who can't be near dust, smoke, or intense family drama without reaching for her inhaler. 'Asmatika' is the feminine form for someone with asthma. The masculine form is 'asmatiko'. It's a reminder that some people's 'hininga' needs extra care.
usage_notes: This is the feminine form. The masculine form is "asmatiko". The general, non-gendered term is "may hika".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil **asmatika** si Maria, lagi siyang may dalang inhaler.","translation":"Because Maria is **asthmatic**, she always carries an inhaler."},{"sentence":"Iwasan ang maalikabok na lugar kung ikaw ay **asmatika**.","translation":"Avoid dusty places if you are **asthmatic**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kahon, karaniwang yari sa kahoy, na pinaglalagyan ng bangkay ng isang yumaong tao para sa libing o kremasyon.
original_explanation: The final condo unit. The ultimate GrabCar ride. It's the one box you can't unbox. In Pinoy teleseryes, this is where the dramatic crying scenes happen, usually with someone shouting "Bakit mo kami iniwan?!" while shaking the occupant who, spoiler alert, won't wake up.
usage_notes: Ang "kabaong" ay isang mas karaniwang kasingkahulugan. Ang "ataul" ay medyo pormal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inilagak ang mga bulaklak sa ibabaw ng **ataul**.","translation":"The flowers were placed on top of the **casket**."},{"sentence":"Mahal ang presyo ng mga magagarang **ataul** ngayon.","translation":"The price of fancy **coffins** is expensive nowadays."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sining ng pagbuo ng tula; isang kalipunan ng mga akdang patula.
etymology: Nagmula sa salitang-ugat na `tula` ('poem'), na kinabitan ng unlaping `pan-` at hulaping `-an`, na tumutukoy sa isang sining o kalipunan. Ang /t/ ng ugat ay nawala sa proseso.
original_explanation: The entire world of 'roses are red, violets are blue.' It's the subject in Filipino class that made you write about your feelings in rhyming stanzas. From Balagtas to modern spoken word artists performing their hugot pieces in a coffee shop.
usage_notes: Isang pormal at akademikong termino para sa larangan ng tula.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayaman ang Pilipinas sa larangan ng **panulaan**.","translation":"The Philippines is rich in the field of **poetry**."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aralan namin ang iba't ibang anyo ng **panulaan** sa klase sa Filipino.","translation":"We studied the different forms of **poetry** in our Filipino class."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pambalot na naglalaman ng pulbura at bala para sa baril; maaari ding tumukoy sa lalagyan ng tinta para sa printer.
original_explanation: Back in the day, this was the 'bala' for a gun. Now, it's more known as the 'bala' for your printer—that super expensive little box of ink that always runs out when you're printing your thesis at 2 AM.
usage_notes: Has both a military/weaponry context and a modern technology (ink cartridge) context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naubusan ng **kartutso** ang printer kaya hindi ako makapag-print.","translation":"The printer ran out of its ink **cartridge** so I can't print."},{"sentence":"Nakapulot sila ng mga basyong **kartutso** ng baril sa lugar ng krimen.","translation":"They found empty gun **cartridge** casings at the crime scene."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na nangangahulugang "wala," partikular na tumutukoy sa kawalan ng pera.
etymology: Borrowed from the Waray-Waray language where "waray" means "nothing" or "none".
original_explanation: This is what you call yourself a week before payday. "Bes, libre mo muna ako, waray na ako eh." It's slang for being broke or having nothing, borrowed from the actual Waray word for "nothing." It's the financial status of many during "petsa de peligro."
usage_notes: Very common slang, especially when talking about money. The stress is often on the second syllable (/wa-RAY/) in slang use, distinguishing it from the ethnic group name (/WA-ray/).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pasensya na, hindi ako makakasama, **waray** ako ngayon.","translation":"Sorry, I can't join, I'm **broke** today."},{"sentence":"Tinanong niya kung may natira pa, sabi ko **waray** na.","translation":"He asked if there was any left, I said there's **nothing** left."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging kulang o hindi sapat ng isang bagay, tulad ng pera, oras, o hininga. Ito ay isang proseso na kasalukuyang nangyayari.
etymology: From the root word `kapos`, meaning 'lacking' or 'insufficient'. The affix `kina-` denotes an ongoing state or action, often involuntary.
original_explanation: This is the official feeling of every "petsa de peligro" (the days before payday). When your wallet is on its last legs, your patience is wearing thin, and you're literally short of breath from running to catch the bus because you can't afford a Grab—lahat 'yan, kinakapos ka. It’s the universe telling you, "Besh, budget-ing is a skill you haven't unlocked yet."
usage_notes: Often used to describe a shortage of money, time, or breath.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Palagi na lang akong **kinakapos** sa pera bago pa man dumating ang sahod.","translation":"I'm always **running short of** money even before payday arrives."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula siyang **kinakapos** ng hininga pagkatapos umakyat ng hagdan.","translation":"He started **getting short of** breath after climbing the stairs."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-alis o pagbabago sa mga bahagi ng isang akda, pelikula, o anumang uri ng midya na itinuturing na hindi kanais-nais.
original_explanation: 'Pag may sinabi sa'yo 'yung kaibigan mo na, 'Uy, 'wag mong ikwento 'yung part na 'yon,' sinensura niya 'yung chika. Ito 'yung act ng pag-cut, pag-bleep, o pag-blur ng mga bagay na 'di dapat makita o marinig ng madla.
usage_notes: Isang pandiwang tumutukoy sa aksyon ng pagsasagawa ng sensura.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng komite kung dapat bang **sensurahin** ang ilang eksena sa pelikula.","translation":"The committee is studying whether they should **censor** some scenes in the movie."},{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang **sensurahin** ang kanyang sining para lang magustuhan ng lahat.","translation":"He doesn't want **to censor** his art just to be liked by everyone."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng katapatan at hindi nagbabago ng suporta o pagtingin sa isang tao, grupo, o prinsipyo.
original_explanation: That friend who still defends you even after you've made a questionable life decision. Or your dog. Your dog is the ultimate definition of 'loyal'. In relationships, this is the bare minimum, but sometimes, it's the first thing to go missing. "Sana all loyal."
usage_notes: Commonly used in Taglish conversations, especially regarding relationships, friendships, and politics.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit anong mangyari, **loyal** ako sa paborito kong basketball team.","translation":"Whatever happens, I'm **loyal** to my favorite basketball team."},{"sentence":"Humanap ka ng partner na **loyal**, hindi yung parang Wi-Fi, laging naghahanap ng ibang connection.","translation":"Find a partner who is **loyal**, not like Wi-Fi that's always looking for another connection."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng mga bagay o tao sa paligid ng isang sentrong punto o bagay; ang pagkulong sa isang lugar sa pamamagitan ng pag-ikot dito.
etymology: From 'pa-' + 'libot' (to roam, to go around) + '-an' (locative/directional suffix).
original_explanation: When the chismosas in your neighborhood see you with someone new, they'll "palibutan" you to get the details. It means to surround something or someone. It can be literal, like "Pinalibutan ng mga pulis ang gusali" (The police surrounded the building), or figurative, like "Palibutan mo ang sarili mo ng mga taong positibo" (Surround yourself with positive people).
usage_notes: The object of the verb is the thing being surrounded.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **palibutan** ng bakod ang buong lote.","translation":"The entire lot needs **to be surrounded** by a fence."},{"sentence":"Bigla siyang **pinalibutan** ng mga tagahanga para magpa-picture.","translation":"He was suddenly **surrounded** by fans asking for a picture."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hiram na salita mula sa Ingles na tumutukoy sa matinding pagsisikip ng daloy ng trapiko sa daan.
original_explanation: The default state of EDSA. That moment you realize your Waze ETA is more of a suggestion than a reality. It's the ultimate test of patience, a free-for-all concert of car horns, and the reason why '5 minutes away' actually means 30-45 minutes.
usage_notes: Often used with 'trapik' as in 'traffic jam'. The word 'trapik' by itself is more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naku, sobrang **jam** sa C5, male-late na ako!","translation":"Oh no, the traffic is so **jammed** on C5, I'm going to be late!"},{"sentence":"Halos isang oras kaming naipit sa **jam** kanina.","translation":"We were stuck in the traffic **jam** for almost an hour earlier."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng katahimikan, katiwasayan, at kawalan ng gulo, hidwaan, o digmaan.
etymology: Mula sa "payapa" (peaceful) na may mga panlaping "ka-" at "-an", na bumubuo ng isang basal na pangngalan.
original_explanation: That rare, magical moment when there's no traffic on EDSA, your internet connection is stable, and your family isn't fighting over the remote control. It’s what you wish for during your commute and what you pray for after a long day at the BPO. It's the opposite of "sana all" drama; it's "sana peace" for real.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa panloob na kapayapaan (kapayapaan ng isip), kapayapaang panlipunan, o ang kawalan ng digmaan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tanging hiling niya ay **kapayapaan** sa kanyang kalooban.","translation":"Her only wish is **peace** within herself."},{"sentence":"Nagkakaisa ang mga bansa para sa pandaigdigang **kapayapaan**.","translation":"The nations are uniting for world **peace**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang takdang mangyayari sa buhay ng isang tao, bagay, o lugar; ang guhit ng palad.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na kahit anong gawin mong "diskarte moves" sa buhay, mayroon pa ring script na sinusunod ang universe para sa'yo. Parang sa love life mo, kahit ilang beses kang na-ghost, if it's your kapalaran to find "The One," mahahanap mo 'yan... sa tamang panahon, after ng ilang failed talking stages.
usage_notes: Often used in fortune-telling contexts or philosophical discussions about life.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano kaya ang **kapalaran** ko sa susunod na taon?","translation":"I wonder what my **fate** will be next year?"},{"sentence":"Iginuhit na sa ating mga palad ang ating **kapalaran**.","translation":"Our **destiny** is written on our palms."},{"sentence":"Tinanggap niya nang buong puso ang kanyang **kapalaran**.","translation":"He/She accepted his/her **fate** wholeheartedly."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging huli o dakip ng mga awtoridad.
original_explanation: This is the headline you see when a drug bust is successful or when a corrupt official finally gets caught. "Huli sa akto! Timbog ang suspek!" It's the moment the game of cat and mouse ends, and someone's about to have a very bad day involving handcuffs.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa mga balita. Ang anyong pandiwa nito ay 'tinimbog' (inaresto).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Timbog** ang magnanakaw matapos ang mahabang habulan sa EDSA.","translation":"The thief was **captured** after a long chase on EDSA."}]

translation: act of pulling each other's hair
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng sabay-sabay o gantihang paghila sa buhok ng isa't isa, karaniwan sa gitna ng isang away.
original_explanation: The iconic scene in every Pinoy teleserye. When words are no longer enough, and the drama escalates to a physical catfight, this is what happens. It's the ultimate 'palengke' fight move. One person pulls hair, the other pulls back. It's messy, dramatic, and guaranteed to draw a crowd.
usage_notes: The `-an` suffix here indicates a reciprocal action, meaning two or more people are doing it to each other.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang simpleng alitan ay nauwi sa **pagsasabunutan** sa gitna ng kalsada.","translation":"The simple argument led to an **act of pulling each other's hair** in the middle of the street."},{"sentence":"Inawat ng mga guwardiya ang **pagsasabunutan** ng dalawang babae.","translation":"The guards stopped the **act of pulling each other's hair** between the two women."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na may matatayog na mithiin, ambisyon, o pangarap sa buhay.
original_explanation: The person who says 'Laban lang!' even when their bank account is crying. They have a vision board, listen to motivational podcasts, and probably have a startup idea that will 'change the world.' The official title of every aspiring artist, entrepreneur, and OFW.
usage_notes: Generally has a positive and hopeful connotation, referring to someone with ambitions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bilang isang **mangangarap**, hindi siya tumitigil na magsumikap para sa kanyang pamilya.","translation":"As a **dreamer**, she never stops working hard for her family."},{"sentence":"Ang Pilipino ay likas na **mangangarap**.","translation":"The Filipino is a natural **dreamer**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga matang tila laging inaantok, malumanay, o may banayad na anyo.
original_explanation: Yung mga mata mong parang 'I woke up like this' pero in a sleepy, sexy way. Hindi puyat sa work, hindi rin galing sa iyak. It's the 'come hither' look na effortless. Perfect for dramatic monologues sa teleserye or just looking cute while waiting for your Grab.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used to describe eyes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahuhumaling ako sa kanyang mga **mapungay** na mata.","translation":"I am captivated by his/her **languid** eyes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na ginagamit bilang sisidlan o lalagyan ng iba't ibang uri ng laman.
original_explanation: It's the Tupperware your mom insists you return. It's the balikbayan box that holds all the pasalubong. It's any object whose primary purpose in life is to hold other stuff. Basically, the physical embodiment of 'it's what's inside that counts.'
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'lalagyan' or 'sisidlan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakilagay ang mga prutas sa **lamanan** na iyan.","translation":"Please put the fruits in that **container**."},{"sentence":"Ang baul ay isang uri ng **lamanan** para sa mga damit at gamit.","translation":"A chest is a type of **receptacle** for clothes and things."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, lalo na isang kabataan, na nakagagawa ng mga pagkakasala o krimen; may sala o nagkasala.
original_explanation: The person who commits the dilingkuwensiya. It's what your tita calls your cousin who's always getting into trouble. "Hala, 'yan na naman si pinsan, 'yung dilingkwente."
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun to refer to a person or an adjective to describe them.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinuturing siyang **dilingkwente** ng kanilang komunidad.","translation":"He is considered a **delinquent** by their community."},{"sentence":"Dinala sa DSWD ang mga nahuling **dilingkwente**.","translation":"The arrested **delinquents** were brought to the DSWD."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matinding paglalarawan ng pag-iyak na may kasamang malakas na sigaw o daing, na nagpapahiwatig ng sukdulang sakit o kalungkutan.
original_explanation: This is the telenovela-level of crying. 'Yung eksena na namatay 'yung bida or nalaman niyang ampon siya. It's not just tears; it's a full-on scream-cry. Think of a child having a massive tantrum in the mall, but the adult version with 1000x more emotional baggage and drama.
usage_notes: A very dramatic and literary phrase. 'Humiyaw' means to scream or shout. 'Pananangis' is a deep form of weeping. This emphasizes the vocal aspect of grieving.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang buong kabahayan ay nagising sa kanyang **naghuhumiyaw sa pananangis**.","translation":"The entire household was awakened by her **wailing** (screaming while crying)."},{"sentence":"Sa sobrang sakit, halos **maghumiyaw sa pananangis** ang babae sa loob ng ospital.","translation":"From so much pain, the woman was almost **screaming while crying** inside the hospital."}]

translation: according to a plan; in a planned manner
meaning_filipino: Sa paraang ayon sa isang plano; sa paraang naka-plano.
etymology: From 'plano' (plan, from Spanish 'plano') and the prefix 'pa-', which here denotes manner or likeness.
original_explanation: This isn't a very common word. It's like saying something is "plan-ish" or "done in the style of a plan." You'd more likely hear "naka-plano" (planned) or "ayon sa plano" (according to the plan). Using 'paplano' might sound a bit academic or even awkward in casual conversation. It’s like describing the *method* as being plan-like. "The project was executed paplano." It's a bit formal.
usage_notes: This word is quite rare in modern spoken Filipino. 'Ayon sa plano' or 'planado' are much more common substitutes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lahat ng hakbang ay isinagawa nang **paplano** upang maiwasan ang anumang pagkakamali.","translation":"All steps were executed **according to a plan** to avoid any mistakes."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan nilang ayusin ang gusot sa paraang **paplano**, ngunit nabigo pa rin.","translation":"They tried to fix the mess in a **planned** manner, but still failed."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang instrumentong medikal na binubuo ng isang tubo, karayom, at émbolo na ginagamit sa pag-iniksyon o pagkuha ng likido mula sa katawan.
original_explanation: That pointy thing the nurse uses that makes grown men cry. It's your frenemy during flu season and your worst nightmare during a blood test. 'Relax lang,' they say. Sure.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ng doktor ang **heringgilya** para sa bakuna.","translation":"The doctor used the **syringe** for the vaccine."},{"sentence":"Takot ako sa **heringgilya** mula pa noong bata ako.","translation":"I've been afraid of **syringes** since I was a child."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng takbo ng kabayo na mas mabilis kaysa paglakad ngunit mas mabagal kaysa pagtakbo nang mabilis (gallop), kung saan ang mga paang magkasalungat sa dayagonal ay sabay na gumagalaw.
original_explanation: Ito yung parang jog ng mga kabayo, hindi yung todo-karipas. Parang ikaw lang 'pag nagmamadali pero ayaw mong pagpawisan—brisk walking with a purpose. Sa kalesa, ito yung "chill ride" mode ng kabayo.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng mga kabayo o pangangabayo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula sa marahang **trote** ang kabayo bago ito tumakbo nang mabilis.","translation":"The horse started with a slow **trot** before it galloped."},{"sentence":"Sanay sa **trote** ang mga kabayong humihila ng kalesa sa Vigan.","translation":"The horses pulling carriages in Vigan are used to the **trot**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapanggap o pagpapakita ng isang katangian, damdamin, o kalagayan na hindi totoo.
original_explanation: This is the OG "acting-actingan". Yung kunwari hindi ka apektado na na-seen ka niya, pero deep inside, wasak. That's you, trying to magkunuwa that you're okay. It's pretending to be busy when your boss walks by, or pretending you like your tita's super sweet fruit salad.
usage_notes: Interchangeable with "magkunwari". "Magkunuwa" can sound slightly more formal or literary.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **magkunuwa** na masaya siya para sa kaibigan, ngunit bakas sa kanyang mukha ang lungkot.","translation":"She tried to **pretend** she was happy for her friend, but sadness was visible on her face."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magkunuwa** na hindi mo alam ang nangyari.","translation":"Don't **pretend** you don't know what happened."}]

translation: To drag forcefully to the limit
meaning_filipino: Ang marahas na paghila o pagkaladkad sa isang bagay o tao hanggang sa pinakadulo o hangganan nito, kadalasan sa lupa o sa isang magaspang na ibabaw.
etymology: From `pa-` (causative) + `sagad` (limit, to the very end) + `-in` (object focus suffix), with reduplication of the root's first syllable (`sa-gad` -> `sa-gad-sad`) for intensity.
original_explanation: This is not your friendly "hila" or "kaladkad." This is dragging with extreme prejudice. Imagine pulling a heavy sack of rice across a rough floor until it tears, or how villains in old action movies drag the hero's friend. It’s an intense, almost cruel action. It’s taking "sagad" (to the limit/max) and turning it into a violent verb. Not a word you use when asking someone to move a chair.
usage_notes: A very strong and somewhat rare word. More common synonyms are `kaladkarin` or `hilahin nang pilit`. The `-sad-` infix implies a scraping, grating motion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pasagadsarin** ang sako sa semento at baka mabutas.","translation":"Don't **drag** the sack **forcefully** on the cement or it might get a hole."},{"sentence":"Sa galit ng lalaki, halos **pasagadsarin** niya ang upuan palabas ng bahay.","translation":"In his anger, the man nearly **dragged the chair forcefully** out of the house."}]

translation: being run over; being crushed by rolling
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging nasagasaan o napisa ng isang bagay na gumugulong, tulad ng gulong ng sasakyan.
original_explanation: This is the tragic fate of a random tsinelas left on the driveway or an ipis that didn't scurry away fast enough. It's the state of being completely flattened by something rolling over you. The noun form of your worst road-crossing nightmare.
usage_notes: Often used to describe roadkill or objects flattened by vehicles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging sanhi ng trapiko ang isang malaking kahon na biktima ng **ligis** sa gitna ng kalsada.","translation":"A large box that was **run over** in the middle of the road caused traffic."},{"sentence":"Iwasan ang **ligis** sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng tamang tawiran.","translation":"Avoid **being run over** by using the proper pedestrian lane."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kabilang dako, panig, o bahagi ng isang lugar, bagay, o sitwasyon.
etymology: From ka- + ibayo + -han. 'Ibayo' itself means 'the other side'.
original_explanation: 'Yung kabilang kalsada. 'Yung kabilang team sa Mobile Legends. 'Yung kapitbahay na laging nakatingin. Basically, "the other side" of anything—a street, an argument, or the MRT platform during rush hour.
usage_notes: A more formal or literary word for 'kabila'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatira sila sa **kaibayuhan** ng ilog.","translation":"They live on the **other side** of the river."},{"sentence":"Maririnig mo ang tawanan mula sa **kaibayuhan** ng pader.","translation":"You can hear the laughter from the **other side** of the wall."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kilos o serye ng mga kilos na nangangailangan ng kasanayan at pag-iingat. Sa matalinhagang kahulugan, isang tusong plano o pakana upang makamit ang isang layunin.
original_explanation: On the road, it's that skillful swerve to avoid a pothole or a tricycle that suddenly stopped. In life or office politics, it's that 'diskarte' move you make to get what you want. "Galing ng manyobra mo para 'di ka mahuling late!" It can be a legit strategy or a shady scheme, depending on the context.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin nang literal para sa pisikal na pagkilos o patalinghaga para sa mga estratehikong hakbang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinailangan ng tsuper ng isang mabilis na **manyobra** para maiwasan ang aso.","translation":"The driver needed a quick **maneuver** to avoid the dog."},{"sentence":"May hinala akong may **manyobra** sa likod ng biglaan niyang promosyon.","translation":"I suspect there's a **scheme** behind his sudden promotion."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglakad nang may pare-parehong hakbang at ritmo, karaniwang ginagawa ng mga sundalo, miyembro ng banda, o mga nagpoprotesta.
original_explanation: What you do during graduation, whether on stage to get your diploma or in the streets for a rally. It’s walking with a purpose and in unison. From ROTC drills to street protests, magmartsa is the verb for synchronized steps.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsanay **magmartsa** ang mga kadete para sa parating na parada.","translation":"The cadets practiced **marching** for the upcoming parade."},{"sentence":"Libo-libong tao ang **nagmartsa** sa kalsada upang ipanawagan ang kanilang mga karapatan.","translation":"Thousands of people **marched** in the streets to call for their rights."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng paghuhugas ng mga pinggan, baso, kubyertos, at iba pang gamit sa pagkain.
original_explanation: The sequel to 'kainan'. After a glorious fiesta or handaan, ito yung part na lahat nagtuturuan kung sino'ng taya. It's the less glamorous cousin of pagluluto. Synonymous with 'paghuhugas ng pinggan.' You know you're an adult when a clean sink brings you immense joy.
usage_notes: "Paglalabon" is a less common, more regional, or older term for "paghuhugas ng pinggan". "Paghuhugas ng pinggan" is the more standard and widely understood term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ako ang nakatokang gumawa ng **paglalabon** pagkatapos ng hapunan.","translation":"I am assigned to do the **washing of dishes** after dinner."},{"sentence":"Marami ang **paglalabon** dahil sa dami ng bisita.","translation":"There is a lot of **dishwashing** to do because of the many guests."}]

translation: to leave a mark on; to trace
meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng bakas o marka ang isang bagay o lugar.
original_explanation: The verb form of leaving your mark. This is what you do when you write your name on wet cement, or when a traumatic ex 'bakasans' your heart. It means to imprint, to leave a trace, for better or for worse.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **bakasan** ng putik ang bagong linis na sahig.","translation":"Don't **leave a mark** of mud on the newly cleaned floor."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **bakasan** ang papel upang makopya ang guhit.","translation":"He is trying to **trace** on the paper to copy the drawing."}]

translation: to be able to object to; to be able to oppose
meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang magpahayag ng pagtutol, pagkontra, o hindi pagsang-ayon sa isang bagay, ideya, o pasya.
etymology: From ma- (ability prefix) + duplicated first syllable of root tu- (future tense) + tutol (object) + -an (locative suffix).
original_explanation: This is your inner 'Objection, your honor!' moment. It's the feeling you get when your parents make a new house rule you don't agree with, or when your boss suggests a 'fun' team-building activity on a Saturday. It's the potential to disagree, whether you actually voice it out or just scream internally.
usage_notes: Future tense form, indicating a potential or future objection.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang desisyon ng korte ay hindi na **matututulan** pa.","translation":"The court's decision can no longer **be objected to**."},{"sentence":"Sa ganda ng kanyang argumento, wala kang **matututulan**.","translation":"With the quality of his argument, there's nothing you can **object to**."}]

translation: to trim (hair/plants); to cut off the top/end
meaning_filipino: Ang pagputol sa dulo ng buhok, halaman, o anumang bagay upang ito ay pumantay, umikli, o maging malinis tingnan.
original_explanation: Before there was 'pa-trim,' there was `magpungos`. It's what your lola does to her plants to make them grow better. It's also what your mom did to your bangs with the kitchen scissors, resulting in a questionable haircut you had to live with for a month. It’s a very specific, no-frills kind of cutting.
usage_notes: Refers to cutting the very end or tip of something, like hair, a plant's stem, or a wick. More specific than 'magputol' (to cut).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nang **magpungos** ng buhok ni David dahil masyado nang mahaba.","translation":"David needs to **trim** his hair because it's gotten too long."},{"sentence":"Inutusan ako ni Lola na **magpungos** ng mga tuyong sanga ng rosas.","translation":"Grandma told me to **cut off the ends** of the dry rose branches."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-angat at pagdadala ng isang bagay na karaniwang mabigat.
original_explanation: This is "carry" but with more effort, like you're lifting weights at the gym. You **buhat** a sack of rice, a gasul tank, or your sleepy toddler. If someone asks you to **buhat** their baggage, they're not your friend. They're using you.
usage_notes: Ang 'buhat' ay partikular na tumutukoy sa pag-angat at pagdadala ng isang mabigat na bagay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **buhat**in ang kahon na ito.","translation":"Help me **lift/carry** this box."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang punong tagapangasiwa o katiwala sa isang malaking sambahayan, na namamahala sa ibang mga katulong.
original_explanation: 'Yung parang si Alfred kay Batman. Siya 'yung head ng mga kasambahay sa isang mansyon, 'yung pinagkakatiwalaan ng 'señorito' at 'señorita'. Sa modern times, baka siya 'yung may hawak ng SSS at Pag-IBIG records ng lahat ng staff sa bahay. Very Tita levels of management.
usage_notes: This term feels a bit dated and is often associated with old, wealthy families or historical dramas (teleseryes).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan ng **mayordomo** ang mga hardinero na diligan ang mga halaman.","translation":"The **butler** instructed the gardeners to water the plants."},{"sentence":"Sa mga lumang pelikula, laging istrikto ang itsura ng **mayordomo**.","translation":"In old movies, the **major-domo** always looks strict."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang makitid na anyong-tubig na nag-uugnay sa dalawang mas malaking anyong-tubig.
original_explanation: Think of it as the SLEX or NLEX of the sea. It's a narrow waterway where ships pass through, connecting two bigger bodies of water. Kinda like that one narrow hallway in the office that connects the pantry and the main workspace, where everyone awkwardly passes each other.
usage_notes: A specific geographical term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang San Juanico Bridge ay tumatawid sa **dagat-kipot** sa pagitan ng Samar at Leyte.","translation":"The San Juanico Bridge crosses the **strait** between Samar and Leyte."},{"sentence":"Mapanganib ang paglalayag sa **dagat-kipot** na iyon kapag masama ang panahon.","translation":"Sailing in that **channel** is dangerous during bad weather."}]

translation: to have something covered or wrapped; to pretend
meaning_filipino: Una, ang paglalagay ng pabalat o takip sa isang bagay. Ikalawa, ang pagpapanggap o pagkukunwari.
original_explanation: This word has two vibes. Vibe 1: The back-to-school rush. You go to the bookstore to magpabalat your new textbooks with plastic cover para 'di magusot. It's literally "to have something put in a cover." Vibe 2: The "plastic" friend. Yung kunwari bati kayo, pero sa likod, sinisiraan ka. That's magpabalat-kayo, or "to put on a facade." It's about covering something up, whether it's a book or your true intentions.
usage_notes: The meaning "to pretend" or "to put on a show" is often used in the form `magpabalat-kayo`. The literal meaning is to have something wrapped or book-covered.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **magpabalat** ng mga bago kong aklat bago magsimula ang klase.","translation":"I need **to have** my new books **covered** before class starts."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala sa kanya, sanay siyang **magpabalat-kayo**.","translation":"Don't believe him, he's used to **pretending**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahinang sinag o bahagyang liwanag, lalo na ang namamanaag sa pagbubukang-liwayway.
original_explanation: That first hint of light before the sun actually rises. It's the 'may pag-asa pa' glow on the horizon after you've pulled an all-nighter for a deadline or after a long, dark night of 'senti'. It’s the universe telling you, "Good morning, you made it."
usage_notes: A poetic and literary term. Synonymous with 'bukang-liwayway' or 'madaling-araw'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa paglitaw ng **banag** sa silangan, nagsimula nang magtrabaho ang mga magsasaka.","translation":"With the appearance of **dawn** in the east, the farmers started to work."},{"sentence":"Isang **banag** ng pag-asa ang sumilay sa kanyang mga mata.","translation":"A **glimmer** of hope shone in her eyes."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang taong mapagkunwari, na nagpapakita ng magkaibang pag-uugali o pananaw depende sa kung sino ang kaharap.
etymology: Tambalang salita mula sa "doble" (double) at "kara" (mula sa Espanyol na "cara", mukha).
original_explanation: Parang kaibigan mo na mabait sa harap mo, pero pagtalikod mo, siya pala ang admin ng "Confessions" page ng office niyo. Sila yung mga taong may front cam (yung pa-sweet) at back cam (yung totoong kulay). Master of disguise, pero sa ugali.
usage_notes: Madalas na may negatibong konotasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap magtiwala sa taong **doble-kara**.","translation":"It's hard to trust a **two-faced** person."},{"sentence":"Nalaman niyang **doble-kara** pala ang kanyang itinuturing na kaibigan.","translation":"She found out that the one she considered a friend was actually **two-faced**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kulay na nasa pagitan ng bughaw at lila sa ispektrum ng liwanag. Isa ring uri ng tina na nagmula sa halamang Indigofera.
original_explanation: That deep, dark blue-purple color. 'Yung kulay ng maong (denim) bago pa malabhan nang maraming beses. Or 'yung kulay ng langit bago tuluyang dumilim. In new age circles, 'indigo children' are said to be special, but for most of us, it's just a really nice, moody color.
usage_notes: Used to describe the specific dark blue-purple color.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinili niya ang kulay **indigo** para sa kanyang bagong bestida.","translation":"She chose the color **indigo** for her new dress."},{"sentence":"Ang **indigo** ay isa sa mga kulay ng bahaghari.","translation":"**Indigo** is one of the colors of the rainbow."}]

translation: to fall or lie prone on someone/something
meaning_filipino: Ang pagdapa sa ibabaw ng isang tao o bagay, kadalasan upang takpan o protektahan ito.
original_explanation: When you're so tired you just plop face-down on the bed. Or when a wrestler pins another wrestler down. It's the act of becoming a human blanket, whether intentionally (for a hug), protectively (like a bodyguard), or accidentally (you tripped).
usage_notes: The locative/benefactive form of 'dapa' (to fall prone). It implies doing the action *onto* something or *for* someone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nang makita ang papalapit na aso, agad na **dapaan** ng ina ang kanyang anak upang protektahan ito.","translation":"Upon seeing the approaching dog, the mother immediately **lay prone on** her child to protect them."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **dapaan** ang mga damit na bagong plantsa!","translation":"Don't **lie prone on** the newly ironed clothes!"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumumba o nawalan ng balanse; Pagkalugi sa negosyo o kawalan ng pera.
original_explanation: Parang puno na tinamaan ng bagyo, or parang negosyo mo after mag-invest sa crypto at bumagsak ang market. 'Yung literal na bagsak, either physically or financially. Game over.
usage_notes: Can refer to a physical object falling over or a business/person becoming financially insolvent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hapay** ang mga poste ng ilaw pagkatapos ng malakas na bagyo.","translation":"The light posts have **fallen over** after the strong typhoon."},{"sentence":"Maraming negosyo ang **hapay** dahil sa pandemya.","translation":"Many businesses went **bankrupt** because of the pandemic."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapahayag o pag-aanunsyo sa publiko ng isang bagay sa isang pormal at opisyal na paraan.
original_explanation: This is a very formal word. You don't just 'magproklama' that you're hungry. It's used for big, official stuff, like when a president 'nagproklama' of a new law, or when COMELEC 'nagproklama' ng winners sa election. It's the verbal equivalent of a giant tarpaulin and a marching band.
usage_notes: Usually used in formal, legal, or political contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pangulo ay **magpoproklama** ng isang bagong holiday.","translation":"The president will **proclaim** a new holiday."},{"sentence":"**Iprinoklama** na ang mga nanalo sa halalan.","translation":"The winners of the election have been **proclaimed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalapat ng kilos o pagtugon sa isang partikular na bagay, suliranin, o kahilingan.
original_explanation: Ito yung utos ng boss mo sa'yo 'pag may email na 'For your action.' Meaning, 'wag mo lang basahin, 'wag mo lang i-seen, gawin mo! It's the verb form of 'stop being a "drawing".'
usage_notes: Ginagamit bilang isang pandiwang palipat na nangangailangan ng tuwirang layon (ang bagay na aaksyunan).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyong **aksyunan** agad ang reklamo ng kliyente.","translation":"Please **act on** the client's complaint immediately."},{"sentence":"Hindi pa rin niya **inaaksyunan** ang mga papeles na pinapirmahan ko kahapon.","translation":"He still hasn't **taken action on** the papers I had him sign yesterday."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng tuldik na may anyong bubong (^) na inilalagay sa ibabaw ng huling patinig ng isang salita. Ito ay nagpapahiwatig na ang diin ay nasa huling pantig at may kasamang impit na tunog o glottal stop sa dulo.
original_explanation: This is the 'little hat' or 'bahay kubo roof' accent (^). It means you stress the last syllable AND you end it abruptly, like you suddenly ran out of breath. Think 'dugô' (blood) or 'pusò' (heart). It's the most dramatic of all the tuldiks, full of stress and a sudden stop. Parang ‘yung feelings mo for him, biglang napatid.
usage_notes: Tinatawag ding 'maragsa'. Ito ay kombinasyon ng diin sa huling pantig at isang impit na tunog sa dulo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **tuldik na pakupya** sa salitang 'sinû' ay nagpapahiwatig ng impit na tunog sa dulo.","translation":"The **circumflex accent** in the word 'sinû' (who) indicates a glottal stop at the end."},{"sentence":"Maraming salitang may **tuldik na pakupya** ang nagtatapos sa patinig.","translation":"Many words with a **circumflex accent** end in a vowel."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng mga organismo na nagpapakita ng paglago, pagtugon sa kapaligiran, metabolismo, at pagpaparami, na naghihiwalay sa kanila sa mga bagay na walang buhay.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'sana all'. It's the reason you're grinding in the BPO, the thing you question during traffic on EDSA, and what you celebrate with Tanduay on a Friday night. It’s complicated, messy, and beautiful. Ganyan talaga ang **buhay**.
usage_notes: A foundational concept in Filipino culture, often discussed in contexts of fate (kapalaran), struggle, and resilience. The stress is on the first syllable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **buhay** ay parang gulong, minsan nasa ibabaw, minsan nasa ilalim.","translation":"**Life** is like a wheel, sometimes you're on top, sometimes you're at the bottom."},{"sentence":"Ibinuwis niya ang kanyang **buhay** para sa bayan.","translation":"He gave his **life** for the country."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagyakap sa isang tao o bagay sa hinaharap bilang pagpapahayag ng pagmamahal, kaginhawahan, o pagbati.
original_explanation: The future tense of 'hug'. It's that thing you promise your friend who's going through a tough time: "Pag nagkita tayo, aakap ako sa'yo nang mahigpit." It's the LDR couple's most awaited action upon arrival at the airport.
usage_notes: This is the contemplative aspect of the future tense. The more common form used in conversation is 'yayakap'. 'Aakap' is often used to express a decision or a strong intention.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkauwi niya mula sa abroad, **aakap** ako nang mahigpit sa aking ina.","translation":"When she comes home from abroad, I **will hug** my mother tightly."},{"sentence":"Sino kaya ang unang **aakap** sa tropeo kapag nanalo sila?","translation":"Who do you think **will be** the first to **hug** the trophy when they win?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kondisyon kung saan ang isang tao ay naglalakad o gumagawa ng iba pang kumplikadong gawain habang natutulog.
