etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "sonambulismo". Tandaan na may varyant itong "sonambulismo".
original_explanation: Ito 'yung parang eksena sa horror movie na bigla na lang may naglalakad sa bahay niyo nang tulog. O baka ikaw 'yun, 'yung nag-rereply sa chat ng ex mo tapos a-claim mo kinabukasan, "Sorry, sleepwalking ako." Ito ang teknikal na tawag sa sleepwalking at magandang dahilan para sa midnight snacking.
usage_notes: Ang "sonambulismo" ay isang mas karaniwang varyant sa pagbaybay, na mas malapit sa ugat na Espanyol. Parehong naiintindihan ngunit bihira sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap. Mas karaniwang ginagamit ang salitang Ingles na "sleepwalking".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **somnambulismo** ay isang uri ng parasomnia.","translation":"**Somnambulism** is a type of parasomnia."},{"sentence":"Pinatingnan niya sa doktor ang kanyang anak dahil sa madalas na **somnambulismo** nito.","translation":"She had her child checked by a doctor because of frequent **sleepwalking**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na ginaya o kinopya mula sa orihinal; hindi tunay o peke.
original_explanation: The official term for your 'Adibas' shoes and 'Guchi' bag from Greenhills. It's the art of looking sosyal on a Divisoria budget. It's not fake, it's 'Class A'.
usage_notes: Used for counterfeit goods or anything that is a copy of an original.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap matukoy kung ang alahas ay tunay o **imitasyon** lamang.","translation":"It's hard to tell if the jewelry is real or just an **imitation**."},{"sentence":"Bumili siya ng bag na **imitasyon** dahil mas mura ito.","translation":"She bought an **imitation** bag because it was cheaper."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng inuming pampalamig na may carbonasyon, karaniwang may lasa mula sa nuwes ng kola at iba pang pampalasa.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na "Cola", na pangalan ng isang brand, na naging pangkalahatang tawag.
original_explanation: The generic term for Coke, Pepsi, RC, etc. 'Yung pampatanggal-umay after kumain ng lechon. Your go-to drink kapag "isang regular" lang ang order sa karinderya. Perfect partner for pizza, fried chicken, and movie nights.
usage_notes: Pangkalahatang tawag sa mga inuming "cola" o softdrink.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pabili po ng isang litrong **kola** at yelo.","translation":"Please buy one liter of **cola** and ice."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang opisyal na awitin ng isang bansa na kumakatawan sa kasaysayan, tradisyon, at pakikibaka ng mga mamamayan nito.
original_explanation: The song you have to stand still for at the movie theater before the trailers. It's 'Lupang Hinirang' for the Philippines. You put your right hand over your chest, sing with pride, and silently judge people who don't know the lyrics.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to a country's official anthem.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat nating igalang ang ating **awit na pambansa** sa tuwing ito ay tinutugtog.","translation":"We should respect our **national anthem** whenever it is played."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maikli at bahagyang pagtulog o pag-idlip, karaniwan habang nakaupo o hindi nakahiga nang maayos.
original_explanation: That moment in a boring meeting or a hot afternoon class when your head starts to feel heavy and your eyes close for a second. It's not a full-on nap; it's a power-fail. The head-bobbing struggle is real. The perfect word for when you're trying to fight sleep but sleep is winning.
usage_notes: A very specific and somewhat poetic word for dozing off. 'Pag-idlip' is more common and less formal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya namalayan ang kanyang **paggupiling** habang nagbabasa ng libro.","translation":"He didn't notice himself **dozing off** while reading a book."},{"sentence":"Isang saglit na **paggupiling** lang ang kailangan niya para manumbalik ang lakas.","translation":"Just a moment of **light napping** was all he needed to regain his energy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglikha ng malakas o magulong tunog.
original_explanation: That moment when your neighbor decides to start their karaoke session at 2 AM. It's the collective sound of chismis in the palengke, the MRT during rush hour, or your family group chat when someone posts a controversial meme. It's the opposite of "silent mode."
usage_notes: "Pag-iingay" (with reduplication) often implies a more continuous or deliberate act of making noise.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinagsabihan ng guro ang mga mag-aaral na itigil ang kanilang **pag-ingay**.","translation":"The teacher told the students to stop their **noise-making**."},{"sentence":"Ang **pag-ingay** ng mga sasakyan sa EDSA ay nakakabingi.","translation":"The **clamor** of vehicles on EDSA is deafening."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang nararamdamang pagsisisi o panghihinayang sa isang nagawang pagkakamali o desisyon.
original_explanation: Yung feeling mo after mo ubusin yung isang buong box ng pizza mag-isa. No regrets! O kaya yung ex mong di-nagsisisi na iniwan ka, so move on na, bes. #SorryNotSorry ang peg.
usage_notes: Describes a person's state of mind of not feeling sorry for their actions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit nahuli na siya, nanatili siyang **di-nagsisisi** sa kanyang ginawa.","translation":"Even after being caught, he remained **unrepentant** for what he did."},{"sentence":"**Di-nagsisisi** akong pinili ko ang kursong ito.","translation":"I **do not regret** choosing this course."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong mapagkawanggawa na nagbibigay ng malaking halaga ng salapi o tulong sa mga nangangailangan o para sa kapakanan ng publiko.
etymology: Hiram sa Espanyol na 'filántropo', mula sa Griyegong 'philanthropos' (mapagmahal sa sangkatauhan).
original_explanation: Yung mayaman na hindi lang pang-IG stories ang yaman, kundi talagang tumutulong sa kapwa. Sila yung mga totoong "sana all" dahil sa kanilang generosity. Hindi lang sila nag-a-abuloy, nagtatayo sila ng foundations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala ang yumaong negosyante bilang isang dakilang **pilantropo**.","translation":"The late businessman is known as a great **philanthropist**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-alis o paghagis ng isang bagay na hindi na kailangan o gusto; pagwawaksi.
original_explanation: What you do with your ex's stuff after a breakup. Also, the daily chore your mom reminds you of. "It's time to declutter. I will throw away everything that doesn't spark joy... or that reminds me of my 2025 self."
usage_notes: Future tense of "magtapon".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magtatapon** na ako ng basura sa labas.","translation":"I **will throw away** the trash outside now."},{"sentence":"Bakit mo **magtatapon** ng pagkaing pwede pang kainin?","translation":"Why **will you discard** food that can still be eaten?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na mungkahi o plano na inihaharap para sa pagsasaalang-alang, pag-aaral, o pagpapatibay, lalo na sa isang lehislatibong kapulungan.
etymology: Nagmula sa unlaping `pan-` at sa bihirang salitang-ugat na `sukala` ('plano' o 'panukod'). Ang /s/ ng ugat ay nawala sa pagkakabitan ng unlapi.
original_explanation: That 'great idea' you present to your boss that might get you a promotion, or that 'great idea' a politician presents that might get them elected. It's a formal 'What if...?' that comes with a PowerPoint presentation.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa pormal na konteksto tulad ng gobyerno, negosyo, at akademya. Kapag naging batas, ito ay tinatawag nang 'batas' at hindi na 'panukalang-batas'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iniharap ng senador ang kanyang **panukala** para sa mas mataas na sahod.","translation":"The senator presented his **proposal** for a higher wage."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan pa ng komite ang mga isinumiteng **panukala**.","translation":"The committee is still studying the submitted **proposals**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaikling anyo ng "palibhasa ay," na ginagamit upang iugnay ang isang dahilan sa kasunod nitong resulta o paglalarawan.
original_explanation: The shorter, more poetic, and slightly more dramatic version of 'palibhasa'. It's like upgrading your chismis from a text message to a spoken word performance. "Palibhasa'y pagod, natulog siya agad." It just flows better, perfect for when you're telling a story with flair. It's the 'it's' to 'it is'.
usage_notes: Functions identically to "palibhasa ay". More common in written or formal speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Palibhasa'y** anak-mayaman, hindi siya marunong maglaba.","translation":"**Because he is** a rich kid, he doesn't know how to do laundry."},{"sentence":"Madali siyang napaniwala, **palibhasa'y** mabait.","translation":"He was easily convinced, **because he is** kind."}]

translation: to have something blessed (with holy water)
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghingi na wisikan ng bendita o banal na tubig ang isang bagay o lugar bilang tanda ng pagbabasbas.
etymology: From `pa-` (to ask someone to do) + `bendita` (holy water), from Spanish `(agua) bendita`.
original_explanation: The more specific, "on-the-go" version of 'pabendisyunan'. This is the quick blessing. You bring your new Sto. Niño statue or your car to the church office, and the priest does a quick sprinkle of 'bendita' (holy water). It's the "express lane" for blessings. Less formal than a full house blessing ceremony.
usage_notes: Synonymous with `pabendisyunan` in many contexts, but specifically implies the use of holy water (`bendita`).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng misa, marami ang nagpunta sa opisina ng pari para **pabenditahan** ang kanilang mga rosaryo.","translation":"After the mass, many went to the priest's office **to have** their rosaries **blessed with holy water**."},{"sentence":"Dapat nating **pabenditahan** ang kotse bago gamitin sa mahabang byahe.","translation":"We should **have the car blessed** before using it for a long trip."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan ginagawa, kinukumpuni, o pinananatiling nasa mabuting kondisyon ang mga barko at iba pang sasakyang pandagat.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na *varadero* ("pagawaan ng barko," "dike seko").
original_explanation: This is the 'talyer' (workshop) for ships. Where a 'bapor' goes for its spa day—a fresh coat of paint, engine check-up, and barnacle removal. It's a place of heavy machinery and skilled workers, not your typical tourist spot unless you're really into big boats.
usage_notes: Isang teknikal na termino, hindi karaniwang ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap maliban kung nagtatrabaho sa industriya ng maritima.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala ang lumang barko sa **baradero** upang kumpunihin.","translation":"The old ship was taken to the **shipyard** for repairs."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang laruang pampalipad na yari sa papel at patpat na tinatalian ng sinulid; o isang uri ng ibon na kilala sa mabilis na paglipad at mahabang buntot.
original_explanation: This word is a 2-for-1 deal! It can be the kite you used to fly as a kid, na laging napupunta sa puno ng kapitbahay. Or it can be the bird (swallow) that looks like it's dancing in the sky. Both are symbols of freedom, parang ikaw nung payday.
usage_notes: The meaning (bird or kite) is usually clear from context. 'Saranggola' is a more common term for 'kite'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga bata ay masayang nagpapalipad ng **layang-layang** sa parang.","translation":"The children are happily flying a **kite** in the field."},{"sentence":"Isang kawan ng **layang-layang** ang dumaan sa aming bintana kaninang umaga.","translation":"A flock of **swallows** passed by our window this morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong naniniwala o sumusunod sa Hinduismo, ang pangunahing relihiyon sa India.
etymology: Mula sa Sanskrit na 'Sindhu', na tumutukoy sa Ilog Indus. Hango sa Kastilang 'hindú'.
original_explanation: A follower of Hinduism. Not to be confused with 'Hindi,' which is a language, or 'hindi,' the Tagalog word for 'no.' Getting this wrong is like calling a BPO agent a 'call boy.' Detail-oriented, please.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa isang tagasunod ng pananampalatayang Hindu. Karaniwang isinusulat na nagsisimula sa malaking titik.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming diyos at diyosa ang sinasamba sa relihiyong **Hindu**.","translation":"Many gods and goddesses are worshipped in the **Hindu** religion."},{"sentence":"Ang kaibigan kong **Hindu** ay nag-imbita sa amin para sa pagdiriwang ng Diwali.","translation":"My **Hindu** friend invited us for the Diwali celebration."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang babaeng uri ng lobo, isang mabangis na hayop na kahawig ng aso.
original_explanation: The female counterpart of a 'lobo'. Think of the alpha female in a wolf pack, or in office politics. She's fierce, she's a leader, and you don't want to be on her bad side during the performance review. Sometimes used to describe a powerful, intimidating woman.
usage_notes: Hindi gaanong karaniwan sa pang-araw-araw na usapan maliban kung tumutukoy sa hayop o ginagamit sa paraang matalinghaga.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **loba** ang namumuno sa grupo ng mga lobo sa kagubatan.","translation":"The **she-wolf** leads the pack of wolves in the forest."}]

translation: to be redeemed; to be able to redeem
meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang mabawi o makuha muli ang isang bagay na isinanla o ipinagbili sa pamamagitan ng pagbabayad ng katumbas na halaga.
original_explanation: Parang pag-claim mo sa phone mo sa pawnshop after mong sumahod. O kaya 'yung feeling na nabawi mo na 'yung self-respect mo after ng isang toxic relationship. You've been redeemed! Pwede ring kapag na-achieve mo na 'yung 13th-month pay mo, finally, matutubos mo na 'yung mga naka-add to cart sa Shopee.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of finance (pawning, debt) or religion (redemption from sin). The actor-focus form is 'makatubos'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay **matubos** ko na ang isinangla kong alahas bago ito maremata.","translation":"I hope I can **redeem** the jewelry I pawned before it gets foreclosed."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang halagang kailangan para **matubos** ang kanilang pagkakautang.","translation":"A large amount is needed to **redeem** them from their debt."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi nagdudulot ng kaluguran o satispaksyon; hindi kaaya-aya.
original_explanation: ‘Yung feeling na nag-order ka ng "large" na fries pero ‘yung laman parang "small". O ‘yung performance review mo na parang sinabi lang, "Ayan, pumasok ka." It's the official term for "meh." Hindi masama, pero hindi rin maganda. It's just... not satisfying.
usage_notes: Isang tambalang pang-uri na nabuo sa pamamagitan ng pagtanggi sa salitang "kasiya-siya".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Di-kasiya-siya** ang naging resulta ng kanilang proyekto.","translation":"The result of their project was **unsatisfactory**."},{"sentence":"Nakatanggap siya ng **di-kasiya-siya**ng serbisyo sa restawran.","translation":"He received **disagreeable** service at the restaurant."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghahalo-halo ng mga baraha o anumang bagay upang mag-iba ang kanilang pagkakasunod-sunod. Ginagamit din sa pagbabago ng posisyon o tungkulin sa isang organisasyon.
original_explanation: This is what your tito does to the deck of cards before a serious game of pusoy dos. 'Bumalasa' means to shuffle. But in the grown-up world, it's also what happens in government or a company when a new boss comes in and 'shuffles' the team—firing some, promoting others, and moving everyone around. It's a corporate/political reshuffle.
usage_notes: Primarily for shuffling cards, but also used figuratively for reorganizing personnel or a system.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang taya kaya siya ang **bumalasa** ng mga baraha.","translation":"It's his turn to deal, so he **shuffled** the cards."},{"sentence":"**Bumalasa** ng mga hepe ng departamento ang bagong pangulo ng kumpanya.","translation":"The new company president **shuffled** the department heads."}]

meaning_filipino: Sadyang sirain o durugin ang isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pagpukpok, pagbagsak, o paggamit ng puwersa.
original_explanation: What you want to do to the alarm clock on a Monday morning. In arguments, it can also mean to destroy someone's point: "Basagin mo ang argumento niya!" Or, more literally, it's what happens in a "basag-ulo" (brawl). The -in suffix makes it an action done *to* something, like, "Huwag mong basagin ang tiwala ko."
usage_notes: This is a transitive verb, meaning it requires an object that is being broken.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinadya niyang **basagin** ang bintana.","translation":"He intentionally **broke** the window."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **basagin** ang katahimikan sa loob ng library.","translation":"It's hard **to break** the silence inside the library."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa ayos na tiniklop o pinagpatong-patong ang mga bahagi.
original_explanation: How your mom wants you to leave your clothes after laundry, but you just dump them on 'the chair'. It means folded. Your new 1000-peso polymer bill is best kept **nakalupi** in a long wallet, not crumpled in your pocket.
usage_notes: Refers to anything that can be folded, like paper, clothes, or blankets.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iniwan niya ang mga damit na **nakalupi** sa ibabaw ng kama.","translation":"He left the clothes **folded** on top of the bed."},{"sentence":"Maayos na **nakalupi** ang liham sa loob ng sobre.","translation":"The letter was neatly **folded** inside the envelope."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa ng isang masusing medikal na pagsusuri sa isang bangkay upang matukoy ang sanhi, paraan, at oras ng pagkamatay.
original_explanation: What happens in every crime procedural show like *CSI* or *SOCO*. When the detectives are clueless, they turn to the medical examiner and say, 'Kailangan nating `mag-autopsiya`.' It's the ultimate way to make the dead tell their story.
usage_notes: A technical term used in medical and legal fields. The root word is sometimes spelled 'awtopsiya'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang pamilya na huwag nang **mag-autopsiya** sa labi ng kanilang kaanak.","translation":"The family decided not to **perform an autopsy** on the remains of their relative."},{"sentence":"Inutusan ng korte ang mga mediko legal na **mag-autopsiya** sa biktima.","translation":"The court ordered the medical legal team to **perform an autopsy** on the victim."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sistema ng komunikasyon na binubuo ng mga salita, tunog, at tuntunin sa gramatika, na ginagamit ng isang partikular na bansa o komunidad.
original_explanation: Ito yung dahilan kung bakit may 'Google Translate' at kung bakit minsan 'nosebleed' ka na sa ka-chat mo. From your native tongue to the 'love language' you're trying to figure out with your crush, lahat 'yan lengguwahe. Ito rin ang dahilan kung bakit may Tagalog, Bisaya, Ilocano, at bekimon sa Pinas.
usage_notes: Ito ang estandardisadong baybay ayon sa Komisyon sa Wikang Filipino. Ang mga baryasyon tulad ng 'lenggwahe' at 'lengwahe' ay karaniwan din sa paggamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalagang pag-aralan ang iba't ibang **lengguwahe** sa Pilipinas.","translation":"It's important to study the different **languages** in the Philippines."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang taong hindi nakararamdam ng emosyon, hindi sensitibo sa damdamin ng iba, o sa isang bahagi ng katawan na manhid.
original_explanation: Two meanings! 1) The literal one: When your leg falls asleep after sitting on it for too long while scrolling through TikTok. It's **numb**. 2) The 'hugot' one: Your ex. The one who ghosted you and acts like you never existed. **Insensitive**. Manhid. Someone who cracks a joke right after you shared something serious. Sila 'yun.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa literal (pisikal na pamamanhid) o piguratibong (emosyonal na kawalan ng pakialam) kahulugan. Ang konteksto ang susi. Mas karaniwang gamitin ang 'manhid' para sa parehong kahulugan, ngunit malawak ding ginagamit ang 'walang-pakiramdam', lalo na para sa emosyonal na kahulugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **walang-pakiramdam** sa hirap na dinaranas ng iyong kapwa.","translation":"Don't be **insensitive** to the hardship your fellow people are experiencing."},{"sentence":"Naging **walang-pakiramdam** ang paa ko dahil sa tagal ng pagkakaupo.","translation":"My foot became **numb** from sitting for so long."}]

meaning_filipino: Ibigay bilang isang regalo o alaala sa isang tao.
original_explanation: The act of giving something you probably got for free or are re-gifting from last Christmas. "Uy, ang ganda ng mug mo!" "Sayo na lang, iregalo mo sa iba." Also, the verb form of what your ninongs and ninangs are supposed to do every Pasko.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Plano kong **iregalo** sa kanya ang librong ito sa kaarawan niya.","translation":"I plan to **give** this book **as a gift** to her on her birthday."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang **iregalo** 'yan, gamitin mo na lang.","translation":"Don't **give** that **as a gift** anymore, just use it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tanyag na panghimagas sa Pilipinas na binubuo ng kinaskas na yelo, gatas, at iba't ibang pinaghalong sangkap tulad ng minatamis na prutas, beans, sago, at gulaman, na karaniwang nilalagyan ng leche flan o ube sa ibabaw.
original_explanation: The ultimate Pinoy summer survival kit in a glass. It's a chaotic mix of everything sweet and wonderful, just like a Filipino family reunion. You've got your beans, jellies, fruits, shaved ice, milk, and a crown of leche flan. The national symbol of 'Kahit ano, basta masarap!' (Anything, as long as it's delicious!).
usage_notes: The name is both a noun and an instruction: you have to mix it all up ('haluin') before eating. Spelling can be 'halo-halo' or 'haluhalo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sarap kumain ng **halo-halo** kapag tag-init.","translation":"It's delicious to eat **halo-halo** during the summer."},{"sentence":"Paki-order mo ako ng isang special na **halo-halo**.","translation":"Please order me one special **halo-halo**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kaparusahan na sukdulan sa tindi, kalupitan, at nagdudulot ng matinding takot o pagdurusa.
original_explanation: This isn't just getting grounded. This is 'no internet for a month' level of punishment. A parusang kahila-hilakbot is a punishment so severe it sounds like something from a horror movie or a medieval history book. Like being forced to listen to your parents' old love songs on repeat. Truly horrific.
usage_notes: A very strong and descriptive phrase used to emphasize the severity of a punishment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ipatapon sa isang malayong isla ay isang **parusang kahila-hilakbot** noong unang panahon.","translation":"Being exiled to a remote island was a **horrific punishment** in the old days."},{"sentence":"Para sa kanya, ang mawalan ng tiwala ng pamilya ay isang **parusang kahila-hilakbot**.","translation":"For him, losing his family's trust is a **terrible punishment**."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi maihahambing sa iba dahil sa pagiging natatangi o superior.
original_explanation: A close cousin of 'walang-kahalintulad'. You use this when you've seen it all, but this one thing just hits different. Think of the traffic in EDSA on a payday Friday—walang-kahambing sa tindi! Or the flavor of a perfectly ripe mango from Guimaras.
usage_notes: Kasingkahulugan ng `walang-kahalintulad` ngunit marahil ay mas karaniwan sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng tanawin sa Batanes ay **walang-kahambing**.","translation":"The beauty of the scenery in Batanes is **without comparison**."},{"sentence":"Ang kabaitan na ipinakita niya ay **walang-kahambing**.","translation":"The kindness he showed was **incomparable**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng pagiging madaling mainis, magalit, o mawalan ng pasensya.
original_explanation: That feeling you get when you haven't had your morning coffee, you're stuck in EDSA traffic, and the internet is slow. It's being 'pikon' but for life in general. The default mood of many people during a hot summer day without aircon.
usage_notes: Describes a person's temporary state or general disposition.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagiging **iyamutin** ako kapag kulang ako sa tulog.","translation":"I become **irritable** when I lack sleep."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa pagiging **iyamutin** kaya iniiwasan siya ng mga kasamahan niya.","translation":"He is known for being **grumpy**, so his colleagues avoid him."}]

translation: let me borrow; may I borrow
meaning_filipino: Isang pakiusap na pansamantalang gamitin ang isang bagay na pag-aari ng iba, na may intensyong ibalik ito.
original_explanation: The national anthem of every Filipino student looking for a ballpen. "Pahiram ng ballpen!" It's the magic word to get something temporarily, from your friend's charger to your sibling's clothes. Just remember the unspoken rule: you have to actually give it back. Otherwise, "pahiram" becomes "pa-kinam" (let me own it).
usage_notes: A very common expression used in the imperative form to ask to borrow something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pahiram** muna ng payong mo, umuulan kasi sa labas.","translation":"**May I borrow** your umbrella for a moment, it's raining outside."},{"sentence":"Sabi niya, '**Pahiram** ng P500, babayaran kita sa sahod.'","translation":"He said, '**Let me borrow** P500, I'll pay you back on payday.'"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng malapit at malalim na ugnayan o pagkakaibigan.
original_explanation: This is the bond you have with your 'Beshie,' your 'Sis,' or your 'Parekoy.' It's the level of friendship where you can show up at their house unannounced, raid their fridge, and talk about anything from career goals to the weirdest thing you saw on TikTok. It's the 'alam na this' look you give each other across a crowded room.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to the quality of a close, platonic relationship.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanilang **pagkamatalik** na magkaibigan ay hinahangaan ng marami.","translation":"Their **closeness** as best friends is admired by many."},{"sentence":"Sinubok ng panahon ang kanilang **pagkamatalik**.","translation":"Time tested their **intimacy** (as friends)."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng isang bagay nang may lubos na katapatan, sigasig, at walang pag-aalinlangan.
original_explanation: This is how you should do things you're passionate about. You accept an apology "buong puso." You serve the people "buong puso." You sing karaoke "buong puso" (even if you're out of tune). It means doing something with 100% sincerity and effort, holding nothing back. It's the opposite of half-assing it.
usage_notes: Can describe the sincerity of an action, an emotion, or an apology.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Buong puso** siyang nagpapasalamat sa lahat ng tumulong sa kanya.","translation":"She **wholeheartedly** thanks everyone who helped her."},{"sentence":"Tinatanggap ko **buong puso** ang iyong paumanhin.","translation":"I accept your apology **with all my heart**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maranasan ang pagkasawa o pagkaumay sa isang partikular na bagay, tao, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: That moment when you realize you can't eat another bite of lechon, no matter how glorious it is. 'Pagsawaan mo muna 'yang laro mo bago ka humingi ng bago.' (Get tired of your current game first before you ask for a new one.) It's the object-focused version of getting fed up.
usage_notes: This is the object-focused verb form. The subject of the sentence is the one causing the feeling of being 'fed up.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong hintaying **pagsawaan** ka niya bago mo ayusin ang inyong relasyon.","translation":"Don't wait for him/her **to get tired of** you before you fix your relationship."},{"sentence":"Tila hindi niya **pinagsasawaan** ang pagkain ng sinigang araw-araw.","translation":"It seems he doesn't **get tired of** eating sinigang every day."}]

meaning_filipino: Tiyakin o siguruhin ang isang bagay upang magkaroon ng katiyakan at mawala ang pag-aalinlangan.
original_explanation: The verb form of "sure ka na ba diyan?" It's what you do before you click 'submit' on an online form or before you send that risky text. You double-check, you triple-check, you maniyak. "Bago tayo umalis, maniyak muna tayo na nakasara ang lahat ng pinto."
usage_notes: Often used in the form 'makatiyak' or 'matiyak' (to be able to make sure). 'Maniyak' is less common in everyday speech than its other forms but is grammatically correct.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **maniyak** kung tama ang direksyon natin.","translation":"We need to **ascertain** if we are going in the right direction."},{"sentence":"Para **maniyak** ang kaligtasan ng lahat, sundin ang mga alituntunin.","translation":"To **ensure** everyone's safety, follow the rules."}]

translation: to author; to compose (a literary piece)
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglikha o pagsulat ng isang akdang pampanitikan, tulad ng tula, kwento, o nobela.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'akda' (literary work) at unlaping '-um-'.
original_explanation: Basically, to write something and be its official creator. It's what Jose Rizal did with Noli Me Tángere. It's what your favorite Wattpad author does. If you've ever written a whole dramatic 'script' in your head for an argument that will probably never happen, you've technically 'umakda' a one-act play.
usage_notes: Used primarily in formal, academic, or literary contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **umakda** ng sikat na nobelang 'Banaag at Sikat'?","translation":"Who **authored** the famous novel 'Banaag at Sikat'?"},{"sentence":"Nais niyang **umakda** ng isang tula para sa kanyang minamahal.","translation":"He wants **to compose** a poem for his beloved."}]

translation: to make someone happy; to bring joy
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay o pagdudulot ng kaligayahan o kagalakan sa isang tao.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate goal of every GrabFood delivery, every surprise party, every corny joke your dad tells. It's the act of causing happiness. Whether you're a comedian making an audience laugh, or you're just bringing home your partner's favorite milk tea, you are actively trying to "magpasaya". It's the verb form of "Sana all happy."
usage_notes: A very common causative verb. The subject causes the object to feel "saya" (happiness).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Simple lang ang gusto niya: ang **magpasaya** ng kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"His wish is simple: to **make** his parents **happy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-angat mula sa isang mababang lugar patungo sa mas mataas, o ang pagbangon mula sa isang mahirap na kalagayan, tulad ng kahirapan, sakit, o trahedya.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'bangon' moment. Literally, it’s what happens after a typhoon when you move to higher ground. Figuratively, it's the plot of every inspiring teleserye: the main character, after being oppressed and downtrodden, finally succeeds. It’s your career after leaving a toxic job. It's getting over a breakup. It's the opposite of 'lugmok'.
usage_notes: Can be literal (rising from water, coming up from a dive) or figurative (recovering from hardship, poverty, or illness).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging mahirap ang **pag-ahon** ng pamilya mula sa pagkalubog sa utang.","translation":"The family's **recovery** from being buried in debt was difficult."},{"sentence":"Ang **pag-ahon** mula sa baha ay isang malaking hamon para sa buong komunidad.","translation":"The **act of rising** from the flood was a huge challenge for the whole community."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbigkas ng isang panunumpa o pangako nang may kabigatan. Maaari rin itong tumukoy sa paggamit ng masasamang salita o paglalagay ng isang malédisyon sa isang tao.
original_explanation: This word has a split personality. On one hand, it's what politicians do during their oath-taking ('nanunumpa ako...'). On the other hand, it's what you do when you stub your toe in the middle of the night. It can also mean to put a curse on someone, like the old witch in a fairy tale. So, it can be formal, angry, or magical. Choose your 'sumpa' wisely.
usage_notes: The meaning of 'sumumpa' is highly dependent on context. It can mean 'to take an oath' (formal), 'to curse' or 'to swear' (informal/angry), or 'to put a curse on' (supernatural).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumumpa** ang bagong pangulo sa harap ng mamamayan.","translation":"The new president **took an oath** in front of the citizens."},{"sentence":"**Sumumpa** siyang hindi na babalik sa dati niyang bisyo.","translation":"He **swore** that he would never return to his old vice."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa galit, **sumumpa** siya na maghihiganti.","translation":"Because of anger, he/she **swore** to get revenge."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagiging maaga o nauuna sa iba sa isang gawain, lugar, o pila.
original_explanation: The opposite of 'Filipino time'. This is the act of being the first one to arrive at a meeting, the first to pass a project, or the first to get the chismis. Being ahead of the pack.
usage_notes: Refers to the action of being first, as opposed to 'una' which is an adjective (first) or adverb (before).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang maagang **pag-una** sa pila ay nagsisiguro na makakakuha ka ng tiket.","translation":"The **act of going first** in line ensures you will get a ticket."},{"sentence":"Pinuri ng boss ang kanyang **pag-una** sa pagtapos ng proyekto.","translation":"The boss praised his **precedence** in finishing the project."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyong alhebraiko na binubuo ng mga baryable at koepisyente, na gumagamit lamang ng mga operasyon ng adisyon, subtraksyon, multiplikasyon, at hindi-negatibong intedyer na exponent ng mga baryable.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'polinomial', na hango sa Ingles na 'polynomial'.
original_explanation: This is that thing from your high school math class that made you question all your life choices. Yes, the one with all the x's and y's and numbers raised to a power. It's basically a chain of terms added or subtracted together, like a mathematical version of a train.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa mga kontekstong pang-akademiko at matematikal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paglutas sa **polinomyal** na ekwasyon ay bahagi ng aming pagsusulit sa Algebra.","translation":"Solving the **polynomial** equation is part of our Algebra exam."}]

translation: To do better; to improve upon
meaning_filipino: Gawin ang isang bagay nang mas mahusay o mas may pagsisikap; pagbutihin.
etymology: From 'igi' (a variant of 'buti' meaning good/well) + '-han' suffix.
original_explanation: It's the 'Galingan mo pa!' (Do it better!) command from your parents, your boss, or your inner critic when your first attempt just wasn't good enough. It's the upgrade from 'pwede na' (it'll do) to 'wow, ang galing!' (wow, amazing!).
usage_notes: 'Igi' itself is rarely used now, but the verb form 'igihan' is still common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Igihan** mo ang iyong pag-aaral para sa kinabukasan mo.","translation":"**Do better** in your studies for your future."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **igihan** ang paghahanda para sa parating na bagyo.","translation":"We need to **improve upon** our preparations for the coming typhoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gagawing pagtigil sa paggalaw, pagkilos, o paggawa ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: The future tense of 'stop.' This is what the jeepney driver hopefully does when you shout 'Para!'. It's the promise of a pause, whether it's a bus at a stoplight, your heart when you see your crush, or your Netflix marathon at 3 AM (spoiler: it usually doesn't).
usage_notes: This is the actor-focus future tense of 'hinto'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sabi ng tsuper, **hihinto** tayo sa susunod na kanto.","translation":"The driver said we **will stop** at the next corner."},{"sentence":"Hindi ako **hihinto** hangga't hindi ko natatapos ang trabaho.","translation":"I **will not stop** until I finish the work."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang pagsira, pagpinsala, o paghadlang sa isang bagay, lalo na para sa kapakinabangang politikal o militar.
original_explanation: That feeling when your groupmate 'forgets' to do their part of the report right before the deadline. Or when your 'frenemy' tells your crush you have a weird laugh. It's the act of deliberately messing things up for someone else. In the office, it's the person who 'accidentally' unplugs the router during a critical Zoom meeting. Classic sabotahe.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb root, e.g., 'sinabotahe' (sabotaged).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May hinala silang **sabotahe** ang dahilan ng pagkasira ng makina.","translation":"They suspect that **sabotage** was the reason the machine broke down."},{"sentence":"Ang pagpapakalat ng maling impormasyon ay isang uri ng **sabotahe**.","translation":"Spreading false information is a form of **sabotage**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglikha ng mga titik, salita, o simbolo sa isang papel o anumang ibabaw gamit ang panulat.
original_explanation: What you do when you slide into someone's DMs. You're technically 'sumusulat'. From love letters to resignation letters, from coding to writing your thesis, it's all a form of this. The OG form of communication before voice notes took over.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumulat** si Jose Rizal ng dalawang tanyag na nobela.","translation":"Jose Rizal **wrote** two famous novels."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang kalimutang **sumulat** sa akin pagdating mo sa Amerika.","translation":"Don't forget **to write** to me when you arrive in America."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagwiwisik o pagkakalat ng mga maliliit na bagay tulad ng butil, pulbos, o asin sa isang ibabaw.
original_explanation: Parang paglalagay ng cheese powder sa French fries, o sprinkles sa ice cream. You just bulubod it all over. Ganun din sa chismis, 'di ba? Kinakalat, binubulubod kung saan-saan.
usage_notes: Often used in a cooking context. A common synonym is 'budbod'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**bulubod** naman ng asukal sa ibabaw ng biko.","translation":"Please **sprinkle** some sugar on top of the rice cake."},{"sentence":"**Binulubod** niya ng asin ang isdang ihawin.","translation":"She **scattered** salt on the fish to be grilled."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa kasalukuyang panahon; sa oras na ito; sa araw na ito.
original_explanation: The ultimate deadline. Whether it's for a project, a life decision, or just deciding what to eat for lunch, 'ngayon na' is the Pinoy's way of saying 'the pressure is ON.' It's the opposite of 'mamaya na,' the siren song of procrastination.
usage_notes: Can mean both "now" (at this moment) and "today" (this current day). Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang tapusin ang trabaho **ngayon**.","translation":"The work needs to be finished **today**."},{"sentence":"Kumain na tayo **ngayon**.","translation":"Let's eat **now**."},{"sentence":"**Ngayon** ko lang nalaman ang totoo.","translation":"I only found out the truth just **now**."}]

translation: to be able to meet; to encounter; to find
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng pagkakataong makita o masalubong ang isang tao o bagay, nang hindi sinasadya o sa pamamagitan ng paghahanap.
original_explanation: That serendipitous moment when you bump into your crush at the milk tea shop. Or when you finally find that one specific brand of chili oil at the grocery after searching for weeks. It's the universe saying, 'Here you go, I gotchu.'
usage_notes: Can refer to meeting people or finding things. Often implies a chance encounter but can also be the result of a search.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Saan kaya ako **makakatagpo** ng tunay na pag-ibig?","translation":"Where will I be able **to find** true love?"},{"sentence":"Nagulat siya nang **makatagpo** niya ang kanyang dating guro sa mall.","translation":"She was surprised when she **encountered** her former teacher at the mall."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uugali ng pagiging maramot o hindi mapagbigay; pag-iimbot ng isang bagay para sa sarili lamang.
original_explanation: The opposite of 'libre.' A person who is 'madamot' is that friend who never shares their food, won't let you borrow a pen, and splits the bill down to the last centavo. They're the human embodiment of the 'This is mine!' meme. Don't be that person. Share your chichirya.
usage_notes: The adjective form is 'madamot'. 'Damot' itself is often used as a noun to mean 'selfishness' (e.g., "Ang damot mo!" - "Your selfishness!").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **madamot** sa pagkain, ibahagi mo sa iyong kapatid.","translation":"Don't be **stingy** with the food, share it with your sibling."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa kanyang **pagkadamot** kaya kaunti lang ang kanyang kaibigan.","translation":"He is known for his **selfishness**, which is why he has few friends."},{"sentence":"Ang **damot** mo naman! Pahingi lang ng isang piraso e.","translation":"You're so **selfish**! I'm just asking for one piece."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na may pananagutang pinansyal o pagkakautang sa iba.
original_explanation: The default status of every Filipino adult during 'petsa de peligro'. It's that person who suddenly becomes an expert at 'seen-zone' when you message them about the money they borrowed. Also, the reason why some friendships have an expiration date. "Sana all, walang utang."
usage_notes: Can function as an adjective describing a person ("taong may-utang") or a noun referring to the debtor themselves ("ang may-utang").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging malungkot ang taong **may-utang** tuwing araw ng sahod.","translation":"A person who is **indebted** is always sad on payday."},{"sentence":"Hinahanap ng nagpautang ang **may-utang**.","translation":"The lender is looking for the **debtor**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging tulala; isang estado ng kawalan ng malay o malalim na pag-iisip dahil sa pagkabigla, pagkamangha, o matinding damdamin.
etymology: From 'ka-' + 'tulala' (stunned, dazed) + '-an' (suffix indicating a state or condition).
original_explanation: That moment when your brain just blue-screens. It's the 'loading...' icon in your head after hearing shocking chismis, seeing your crush, or finding out your sweldo for the month is already gone. It's the blank stare, mouth slightly open, as the world moves in slow motion around you.
usage_notes: A more formal and less common word than 'pagkatulala'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nananatili siya sa isang **katulalaan** matapos marinig ang balita.","translation":"He remained in a **stupor** after hearing the news."},{"sentence":"Bigla siyang natauhan mula sa kanyang **katulalaan** nang may tumapik sa kanyang balikat.","translation":"He was suddenly brought back to his senses from his **daze** when someone tapped his shoulder."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng langis na mineral na madaling magliyab, karaniwang ginagamit bilang panggatong sa mga ilawan o kalan.
original_explanation: Before Meralco and Solane, there was pitrolyo. This is the stuff that powered your lola's gasera (kerosene lamp) during brownouts. It has a very distinct smell that instantly transports you to a time before WiFi and unlimited data. Now, it's mostly used for cleaning greasy machine parts or for starting a stubborn charcoal grill. The OG fuel.
usage_notes: While it technically means petroleum, in common Philippine usage it almost always refers to kerosene.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng **pitrolyo** para sa aming gasera.","translation":"Mom bought **kerosene** for our lamp."},{"sentence":"Maamoy ang **pitrolyo** sa lumang bodega.","translation":"The old warehouse smells of **kerosene**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pandama o persepsyon ng isang tao, pisikal man o emosyonal; kutob o hinala.
etymology: From paki- (a complex prefix, here related to feeling/sensing) + ramdam (a variant of damdam, meaning feel).
original_explanation: This is the OG Filipino 'vibe check.' It's more than just a feeling; it's your soul's Wi-Fi signal picking up on things your eyes can't see. It's the reason you feel weird about a person for no reason, or why you suddenly miss someone. It's your internal Marites, but for emotions.
usage_notes: A very versatile word covering physical sensations (sakit), emotions (lungkot), and intuition (kutob).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May masama akong **pakiramdam** tungkol dito.","translation":"I have a bad **feeling** about this."},{"sentence":"Ano ang **pakiramdam** mo ngayong nanalo ka?","translation":"What is your **feeling** now that you've won?"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa sangay ng medisina na may kinalaman sa pag-iwas, pag-diagnose, at paggamot sa mga pinsala at karamdaman ng sistemang musculosketal, kasama ang mga buto, kasukasuan, litid, at kalamnan.
original_explanation: This is the less common spelling variant. It's like the difference between 'color' and 'colour'. Still means the same thing. Think of that special, expensive mattress you buy for your back pain, or the weird-looking shoes the doctor tells you to wear. If it's for your bones, joints, or muscles, it's **ortopedik**.
usage_notes: The spelling 'ortopediko' is more common and aligned with modern Filipino orthography.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan niya ng espesyal na sapatos na **ortopedik**.","translation":"He needs special **orthopedic** shoes."},{"sentence":"Ang kama ay may **ortopedik** na kutson para sa masarap na tulog.","translation":"The bed has an **orthopedic** mattress for good sleep."}]

translation: fickle; one who easily gets tired of things
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na madaling magsawa, mawalan ng interes, o magbago ng gusto sa isang bagay, gawain, o maging sa isang tao.
etymology: From 'sawa' (to be tired of/satiated) + '-in' (suffix indicating a tendency or nature).
original_explanation: This describes your friend who changes hobbies faster than they change their profile picture. One week they're a 'plantita,' the next they're learning to bake, and by Friday they're suddenly into crypto. Applies to relationships too, but that's a different 'hugot'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bilang isang **masawain** na tao, marami siyang nasimulan na hindi natapos.","translation":"As a **fickle** person, she started many things that she never finished."}]

translation: to cause trouble; to make a mess
meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng kawalan ng kaayusan, pagkalito, o kaguluhan.
original_explanation: What a toddler does to a clean living room in 5 seconds. What happens to your life when your ex decides to text you 'I miss you.' It's the act of disrupting the peace, whether it's a neat stack of papers or your emotional stability. "Pakiusap, 'wag ka nang gumulo sa buhay ko."
usage_notes: Can refer to a physical mess (gumulo ang kwarto) or a non-physical one (gumulo ang isip, gumulo ang sitwasyon).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Gumulo** ang sitwasyon nang dumating ang mga pulis.","translation":"The situation **became chaotic** when the police arrived."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **gumulo** sa mga gamit ko sa mesa?","translation":"Who **messed up** my things on the table?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang estado o relasyon ng pagiging magkaibigan.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "pagka-" (estado ng pagiging) at "magkaibigan" (dalawa o higit pang tao na may ugnayang pangkaibigan).
original_explanation: This is the official term for your bond with your "beshie," "mars," or "barkada." It's built on shared memes, late-night food trips, and being each other's unpaid therapist. It's what you have with someone before one of you "catches feelings" and ruins it. Charot!
usage_notes: Ito ay bahagyang mas pormal o pampanitikan kaysa sa karaniwang 'pagkakaibigan'. Binibigyang-diin ng 'pagkamagkaibigan' ang estado ng pagiging magkaibigan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanilang **pagkamagkaibigan** ay nasubok ng maraming pagsubok.","translation":"Their **friendship** was tested by many trials."}]

translation: having a fit, being moody, acting up
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagdanas ng biglaan at hindi maipaliwanag na pagbabago sa damdamin o pag-uugali, o ang muling paglitaw ng isang karamdaman.
etymology: From 'sumpong' (whim, caprice, fit of temper). The '-in-' infix and reduplication of the first syllable ('su-') indicate the present progressive tense.
original_explanation: This is the official state of being when you're suddenly angry or sad for no apparent reason. It's the human equivalent of a computer that suddenly lags. It can refer to a kid's tantrum, an adult's mood swing ('topak'), or an illness flaring up, like 'sinusumpong ng hika' (having an asthma attack).
usage_notes: Can refer to a recurring illness (e.g., 'sinusumpong ng rayuma' - arthritis is acting up) or a mood swing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo munang kausapin si Ana, **sinusumpong** na naman yata.","translation":"Don't talk to Ana for now, it seems she's **being moody** again."},{"sentence":"Tuwing malamig ang panahon, **sinusumpong** ang aking asthma.","translation":"Whenever the weather is cold, my asthma **acts up**."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay tulad ng pagkain, inumin, ehersisyo, o gamot na nagbibigay o nagdaragdag ng lakas, sigla, o enerhiya sa katawan o isipan.
etymology: From 'pang-' (instrumental prefix) + 'pa-' (causative prefix) + 'lakas' (strength). Lit. 'that which is used to cause strength'.
original_explanation: Your morning kape, the energy drink you chug before a deadline, the gym session that makes you feel like a superhero, or even the playlist that gets you through a tough workout. Anything that boosts your physical, mental, or emotional power.
usage_notes: A very broad term covering anything from food and drink (e.g., 'pampalakas na pagkain') to activities and emotional support.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinuturing niyang **pampalakas** ang pag-eehersisyo tuwing umaga.","translation":"He considers his morning exercise as an **energizer**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng kape bilang **pampalakas** bago magtrabaho.","translation":"I need coffee as a **booster** before work."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maikli at biglaang paghinga nang malalim, karaniwan ay dahil sa pagkabigla, pagod, o kakulangan sa hangin.
original_explanation: That feeling when you see your electricity bill for the summer months. It's the sound you make when you've just run up five flights of stairs because the elevator is broken, or when you hear the latest shocking showbiz chismis. It's a physical "OMG."
usage_notes: Often used to describe a reaction of shock or physical exertion. Differentiated from 'paghingal' which is more prolonged panting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang kanyang **pagsingap** nang makita niya ang ahas.","translation":"I heard her **gasp** when she saw the snake."},{"sentence":"Puro **pagsingap** na lang ang naririnig mula sa manlalaro dahil sa pagod.","translation":"Only **panting** could be heard from the player due to exhaustion."}]

translation: to tilt; to place on its side
meaning_filipino: Ilagay sa posisyong nakahilig o nakatagilid.
original_explanation: The official command when you're trying to fit one last, oversized Tupperware in the ref. Or what you do to your phone when you switch from scrolling to watching a video. "Bes, itagilid mo 'yung galon, baka may matira pang tubig."
usage_notes: Can be used literally for objects or figuratively, as in "itagilid ang laban" (to turn the tide of a fight, often in a desperate way).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Itagilid** mo ang kahon para magkasya sa ilalim ng kama.","translation":"**Tilt** the box on its side so it will fit under the bed."},{"sentence":"Nang makitang dehado na, sinubukan niyang **itagilid** ang usapan.","translation":"When he saw he was at a disadvantage, he tried **to steer** the conversation **to the side**."}]

translation: to scoop up; to gather with a net
meaning_filipino: Kunin o kolektahin ang isang bagay, karaniwang isda o maliit na bagay, sa pamamagitan ng panahod, lambat, o salok.
original_explanation: Imagine you're trying to get all the pearls from your milk tea with a straw, or scooping up small fish from an aquarium with a tiny net. That's 'sahulin'. It's the act of trying to gather everything in one go, usually from a liquid. "Bes, sahulin mo na lahat ng chismis bago ka umuwi!"
usage_notes: Distinct from 'kunin' (to get), as 'sahulin' implies using a tool like a net or scoop.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **sahulin** ang lahat ng maliliit na isda sa batis.","translation":"He tried to **scoop up** all the small fish in the stream."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **sahulin** ang mga natapong butil ng bigas.","translation":"The spilled grains of rice need to be **gathered up**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halaman o bahagi nito, tulad ng dahon, bunga, o ugat, na kinakain bilang pagkain.
original_explanation: 'Yung laging sinasabi ng nanay mo na kainin mo para humaba ang buhay mo, pero mas gusto mo pa rin ng fried chicken. Also, an expression for being tired or exhausted, "Lutang na 'ko, gulay na gulay na." Parang overcooked na pechay.
usage_notes: Can also be used colloquially in a reduplicated form 'gulay na gulay' to mean 'very tired' or 'worn out'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang pagkain ng **gulay** para sa kalusugan.","translation":"Eating **vegetables** is important for health."},{"sentence":"Pumunta si nanay sa palengke para bumili ng sariwang **gulay**.","translation":"Mom went to the market to buy fresh **vegetables**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging payak, hindi kumplikado, o walang labis na palamuti.
original_explanation: This is the "less is more" aesthetic. Think of a clean, minimalist condo vs. a house full of "good morning" towels. It's the beauty of a simple white shirt and jeans, or a problem with a straightforward solution. No drama, no fuss, just pure, unadulterated "simple lang".
usage_notes: Can describe the quality of an object, a person's lifestyle, or a concept.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko ang **pagkasimple** ng kanyang pamumuhay sa probinsya.","translation":"I like the **simplicity** of his life in the province."},{"sentence":"**Pagkasimple** lang ng solusyon sa problema, masyado mo lang ginagawang kumplikado.","translation":"The solution to the problem is **very simple**, you're just overcomplicating it."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagkabitin o pagdugtungin ang mga bagay gamit ang isang panali tulad ng lubid o sinulid.
original_explanation: Literally, to tie your shoelaces or a ribbon on a gift. Figuratively, it's what your tita does when she tries to set you up with her friend's son: 'Itinali ka na naman niya!' (She tried to tie you up/set you up again!).
usage_notes: An object-focus verb. The object being tied is the focus of the sentence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **itali** mo ang aso sa poste.","translation":"Please **tie** the dog to the post."},{"sentence":"Mas maganda kung **itali** natin ang mga kahon para hindi magkahiwa-hiwalay.","translation":"It would be better if we **tie** the boxes so they don't fall apart."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumingin nang may pag-asinta at pagkatapos ay tumira, bumaril, o pumalo patungo sa isang target.
original_explanation: Parang sa billiards, 'yung moment na tinitira mo 'yung cue ball para ma-shoot 'yung 8-ball. O sa DOTA, 'yung pag-cast mo ng skill shot sa kalaban. "Sakto 'yung pag-timing niya, kumana siya ng tres para manalo sa huling segundo!"
usage_notes: Often used in the context of games like billiards, basketball, or target shooting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magaling siyang **kumana** sa bilyaran.","translation":"He is good at **hitting the ball** in billiards."},{"sentence":"Nang makita ang target, agad siyang **kumana**.","translation":"When he saw the target, he immediately **struck**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bata na nasa murang edad pa lamang; maliit na bata.
original_explanation: A cute, tiny human who's just learned how to walk and say 'no' to everything. They're the reason you have Cocomelon songs stuck in your head and why you can't have nice, clean white walls. The source of both extreme cuteness and extreme stress.
usage_notes: Carries a connotation of being small and young, often between the ages of 2 and 5.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang katuwaan ng isang **paslit** ay simple lang, bigyan mo lang ng laruan.","translation":"A **small child's** happiness is simple, just give them a toy."},{"sentence":"Nagkalat ang mga laruan sa sahig dahil sa makulit na **paslit**.","translation":"The toys are scattered on the floor because of the playful **toddler**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagwawasto o pagbabawal sa isang tao, karaniwan ay sa mas banayad na paraan kaysa sa paggalit, upang ituwid ang isang maliit na pagkakamali o hindi angkop na kilos.
etymology: From `pag-` (verbal noun prefix) + `saway` (to forbid, to reprimand lightly).
original_explanation: This is the 'uy, bawal 'yan' move. It's gentler than a full-blown sermon from your mom. Think of a librarian shushing you, or your friend gently telling you, 'Bes, 'wag mo na i-text 'yung ex mo.' It's a light scolding, a friendly correction.
usage_notes: Milder than `pagagalit` (scolding angrily). It implies correction or prohibition.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang mahinhing **pagsaway** lang mula sa kanyang ina ang kailangan niya upang tumigil.","translation":"Just a gentle **reprimand** from his mother was what he needed to stop."}]

translation: will be useful; will be of benefit
meaning_filipino: Magkakaroon ng gamit o kapakinabangan sa hinaharap; magiging isang bagay na may halaga o silbi.
original_explanation: This is what you tell yourself when you buy something from Shopee/Lazada that you don't really need right now. "Okay lang 'to, mapakikinabangan ko rin 'to balang araw." It's the future tense of usefulness, the hope that your junk will one day become a treasure.
usage_notes: This is the future tense, object-focus form of the verb. The past/present tense is 'napakikinabangan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itago mo iyang lumang kahon, baka **mapakikinabangan** pa natin.","translation":"Keep that old box, it **might still be useful** to us."},{"sentence":"Ang mga natutunan mo sa eskwela ay tiyak na **mapakikinabangan** mo sa iyong trabaho.","translation":"The things you learned in school **will surely be of benefit** to you in your job."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kemikal na solusyon, karaniwang naglalaman ng sodium hypochlorite, na ginagamit bilang pampaputi ng damit, panlinis, at disimpektante.
original_explanation: The ultimate weapon of every Pinoy household's 'labandera'. Got a stubborn 'mantsa' on your favorite white shirt? Bleach. Need to disinfect the whole bathroom until it smells like a hospital? Bleach. It's the magic potion that promises to make everything sparkling white, but one wrong move and you've got a new, unwanted tie-dye shirt. Also, a popular anime that has nothing to do with laundry.
usage_notes: Sometimes pronounced as 'blits'. The Tagalog equivalent 'lihiya' is also used but is less common for commercial liquid bleach.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa paggamit ng **bleach** para hindi masira ang kulay ng ibang damit.","translation":"Be careful when using **bleach** so you don't ruin the color of other clothes."},{"sentence":"Ibabad mo sa tubig na may **bleach** ang puting tuwalya.","translation":"Soak the white towel in water with **bleach**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pampublikong paghingi ng paumanhin, karaniwang sa pamamagitan ng video o social media post, na ginagawa ng isang influencer matapos makatanggap ng kritisismo o masangkot sa isang kontrobersiya.
etymology: Mula sa pariralang Ingles na 'influencer apology'.
original_explanation: The inevitable sequel to an influencer's 'cancellation.' It's a video, usually with bad lighting, a plain background, no makeup, and a lot of deep sighs. The classic formula includes 'I'm only human,' 'I will do better,' and 'I'm taking a break from social media.' The success rate varies.
usage_notes: A very specific cultural phenomenon of the late 2010s and 2020s. Often carries a cynical connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-upload na naman ng **influencer apology** video 'yung na-cancel kahapon.","translation":"The one who got canceled yesterday has uploaded an **influencer apology** video again."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **influencer apology** ay hindi tinanggap ng marami dahil hindi raw ito sinsero.","translation":"Her **influencer apology** was not accepted by many because they said it wasn't sincere."}]

translation: to attack (a place); to swarm (a place)
meaning_filipino: Sabay-sabay na paglusob o pagdaluhong sa isang tiyak na lugar o kinalalagyan.
original_explanation: This is when the whole barangay shows up at a free-lumpia event. It's the 'sugod' part of 'Sugod Bahay Gang' but directed at a *place*. Think of a mob rushing a concert gate or an online flash sale crashing a website. The location is the target.
usage_notes: Focuses on the location being attacked or swarmed, as opposed to `sugurin` which focuses on the person/object.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Suguran** natin ang bahay nila para sa pa-birthday!","translation":"Let's **swarm** their house for the birthday party!"},{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang mga sundalo na **suguran** ang kuta ng mga kalaban.","translation":"The soldiers decided to **attack** the enemy's fortress."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng guhit o serye ng mga guhit, na kadalasan ay nakakatawa, na naglalarawan ng isang partikular na paksa; maaari ring tumukoy sa isang animated na pelikula.
original_explanation: The reason you woke up early on Saturday mornings as a kid. From 'Tom and Jerry' to your favorite anime, 'kartun' is the umbrella term for animated goodness. It's also that funny drawing in the newspaper that roasts politicians.
usage_notes: Can refer to both animated shows/films and comic strips/editorial cartoons.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig manood ng **kartun** ang mga bata tuwing umaga.","translation":"The kids love to watch **cartoons** every morning."},{"sentence":"Ang **kartun** sa diyaryo ngayon ay tungkol sa pagtaas ng presyo ng gasolina.","translation":"The **cartoon** in today's newspaper is about the rise in gas prices."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang padamdam na utos o hiling na gawin muli ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: The one-word command that fuels concerts, encores, and your mom making you redo your chores because you did a terrible job the first time. It’s what the crowd chants for their favorite band, and what your karaoke-loving tita shouts after a power ballad. 'Isa pa!' is its equally demanding cousin.
usage_notes: Often shouted or said with emphasis. Can be a request or a command.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng kanta! **Ulit! Ulit!** sigaw ng mga manonood.","translation":"The song is beautiful! **Again! Again!** shouted the audience."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tatsulok na may tatlong magkakasinghabang gilid at tatlong magkakaparehong anggulo.
etymology: Mula sa salitang "sulok" (corner) na may panlaping "pa-" at gitlaping "-ri-" na nagpapahiwatig ng regular o pare-parehong anyo batay sa mga sulok/anggulo nito.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung triangle na walang favoritism; lahat ng sides at angles, equal. Parang barkada na pantay-pantay ang ambagan sa inuman. Hindi 'yung isa lang laging taya.
usage_notes: Isang tiyak na uri ng tatsulok. Ang pangkalahatang tawag ay 'tatsulok'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bubong ng ilang bahay-kubo ay hugis **parisulok**.","translation":"The roof of some nipa huts is shaped like an **equilateral triangle**."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan namin sa klase ang mga katangian ng isang **parisulok**.","translation":"We are studying the properties of an **equilateral triangle** in class."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang butas sa mukha na ginagamit sa pagkain at pagsasalita, kadalasang tumutukoy sa bibig ng hayop o ginagamit bilang isang magaspang na salita para sa bibig ng tao. Maaari ring tumukoy sa bukana ng isang butas, tulad ng sa bulkan o kweba.
original_explanation: A more vulgar term for "bibig" (mouth). It's what your mom tells you to shut ("Itikom mo 'yang bunganga mo!") when you're being too loud or sassy. Also used to describe the mouth of a volcano or a cave. Basically, any large opening, including the one that gets you into trouble.
usage_notes: Considered rude or informal when referring to a person's mouth. 'Bibig' is the polite term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinakpan niya ang kanyang **bunganga** para pigilan ang pagtawa.","translation":"She covered her **mouth** to stop herself from laughing."},{"sentence":"Nakakatakot tingnan ang **bunganga** ng bulkan.","translation":"The **crater** (mouth) of the volcano is scary to look at."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaki at mabigat na itak na karaniwang ginagamit sa pagpuputol ng mga sanga, paghahawan ng damo, o bilang sandata.
original_explanation: The original multi-tool of the Filipino farmer and the lolo in the province. Pwedeng pang-taga ng niyog, pang-hawan ng talahib, pang-depensa sa aswang. It's the star in many Filipino action films and the reason you behave when your tatay is cleaning the garden.
usage_notes: A common tool in rural and agricultural settings in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang **gulok** para hawanin ang makapal na damo.","translation":"He used the **machete** to clear the thick grass."},{"sentence":"Matulis ang **gulok** na pamana pa ng kanyang lolo.","translation":"The **bolo knife** inherited from his grandfather is sharp."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pakiramdam ng matinding pagkadiri o pagkasuya na halos umabot sa puntong ng pagduduwal, kadalasan dahil sa labis na pagkain ng isang bagay o paulit-ulit na karanasan.
etymology: From `pagka-` (state of) + `sunok` (a feeling of surfeit or nausea).
original_explanation: You know that feeling when you've eaten way too much lechon and the mere thought of another bite makes you want to hurl? That's pagkasunok. It's 'umay' level 99. It can also apply to non-food things, like when you've heard the same cheesy pickup line so many times you feel sick.
usage_notes: More intense than 'umay' or 'suya'. It implies a physical reaction of revulsion bordering on nausea.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa araw-araw na pagkain ng matamis, nakaramdam siya ng **pagkasunok**.","translation":"Because of eating sweets every day, he felt a sense of **nausea**."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkasunok** ko sa amoy na iyon ay hindi maipaliwanag.","translation":"My **revulsion** to that smell is inexplicable."}]

meaning_filipino: Kalipunan ng mga impormasyon, katotohanan, o bilang na ginagamit sa pagsusuri o bilang batayan ng mga konklusyon.
original_explanation: This is what your team lead in a BPO is always asking for. 'Where's the **datos** to support your claim?' It's the lifeblood of researchers, marketers, and anyone trying to win an argument online. Without **datos**, you're just another opinion. It's the Tagalog version of 'pics or it didn't happen,' but for spreadsheets.
usage_notes: A direct loanword from Spanish, used widely in academic, professional, and technical contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating suriin ang lahat ng **datos** bago tayo magdesisyon.","translation":"We need to analyze all the **data** before we make a decision."},{"sentence":"Ang ulat na ito ay batay sa **datos** na nakalap mula sa census.","translation":"This report is based on **data** gathered from the census."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang alternatibong baybay para sa 'romansa'; isang ugnayan ng pag-iibigan.
etymology: From Spanish 'romance', a spelling variation in Filipino.
original_explanation: Basically 'romansa' but with a slightly more old-school, telenovela vibe. It's like how your lola might spell it. It's the same kilig, just with a different, more classic font. Both get the 'sana all' point across.
usage_notes: A less common variant of 'romansa'. 'Romansa' is the preferred and standard spelling in modern Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanilang **romanse** ay parang isang pelikula.","translation":"Their **romance** is like a movie."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkasira o pagkakahiwa-hiwalay ng isang bagay na dating buo at organisado.
etymology: Mula sa `ma-` + `lansag` (gibain, buwagin). Ang `ma-` dito ay maaaring magpahiwatig ng isang estado o potensyal na mangyari ang kilos.
original_explanation: What happens to your group project when the leader quits. What happens to a political alliance a month before elections. What happens to a Lego creation when a toddler finds it. It's not just broken; it's completely taken apart, dismantled, and scattered. Total system failure.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin para sa mga organisasyon, istruktura, plano, o alyansa. Nagpapahiwatig ng tuluyang pagbagsak.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nanghina ang pundasyon kaya't madaling **malansag** ang gusali sa lindol.","translation":"The foundation was weak, so the building could be easily **dismantled** by the earthquake."},{"sentence":"Ang dati'y matatag na samahan ay **nalansag** dahil sa alitan sa pera.","translation":"The once strong organization was **destroyed** because of a dispute over money."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang estado ng pagiging kilala o tanyag ng maraming tao; ang rurok o pinakatanyag na panahon.
etymology: From ka- + sikat + -an. 'Sikat' literally means 'ray' or 'shine,' so 'kasikatan' is the state of being in the spotlight.
original_explanation: This is what happens when your TikTok video goes viral. It's the 'sikat' moment—your 15 minutes of fame, or if you're a true celebrity, a lifetime supply. It's being the 'Marites' topic of the town, for better or for worse. It's the peak, like the sun at high noon ('kasikatan ng araw').
usage_notes: Can refer to the state of being famous or the peak period of something (e.g., 'kasikatan ng araw' - high noon).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming artista ang nalulungkot matapos malimutan sa kanilang **kasikatan**.","translation":"Many artists become sad after being forgotten beyond their **fame**."},{"sentence":"Noong dekada '90 ang **kasikatan** ng mga bandang alternative rock.","translation":"The 90s was the **peak** of alternative rock bands."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang gawa sa kahoy na ipinapatong sa batok ng kalabaw o baka upang makahila ng araro o kariton.
original_explanation: The **singkaw** is the carabao's version of a work harness or an office ID lanyard. It's the wooden accessory that says, "Time to get to work." Metaphorically, it's anything that binds you to your labor, be it a plow, a desk, or a mountain of deadlines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maingat na inilagay ng magsasaka ang **singkaw** sa batok ng kanyang kalabaw.","translation":"The farmer carefully placed the **yoke** on his carabao's neck."},{"sentence":"Mabigat ang **singkaw** na humihila sa araro.","translation":"The **yoke** that pulls the plow is heavy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hugis na pahaba at bilugan sa mga dulo, katulad ng itlog; isang elipse.
original_explanation: The noun version of `obalado`. It's the shape itself. Think of the track and field where you run, the shape of a rugby ball, or the face of someone your tita calls 'mukhang obalo' (which could be a compliment... or not).
usage_notes: Mas karaniwan kaysa 'obalado'. Ginagamit upang pangalanan ang hugis mismo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumuhit siya ng isang perpektong **obalo**.","translation":"He drew a perfect **oval**."},{"sentence":"Ang disenyo ng plaza ay isang malaking **obalo**.","translation":"The design of the plaza is a large **oval**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkuha o pagpayag sa isang bagay na iniaalok o ibinibigay. Ito ay ang kasalukuyang anyo ng pandiwang "tanggap".
original_explanation: This is you when your sahod finally comes in. "Tumatanggap na po ng bayad sa Gcash!" It's the moment you say 'yes' to that Shopee delivery, a compliment, or even a friend request. It's the opposite of being seenzoned. You're actively taking in what's being given.
usage_notes: This is the present progressive tense of the verb "tanggap" (to accept/receive).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumatanggap** na ba kayo ng aplikante para sa bagong posisyon?","translation":"Are you **accepting** applicants for the new position already?"},{"sentence":"Siya ay **tumatanggap** ng maraming papuri para sa kanyang trabaho.","translation":"He/She is **receiving** a lot of praise for his/her work."}]

translation: to be able to fool/trick someone
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang manlinlang o mandaya ng kapwa.
original_explanation: 'Yung skill ng isang budol-budol gang member, o 'yung kaibigan mo na ang galing mag-bluff sa Tong-its. "Akala niya makakaloko siya ng marami, pero nahuli rin siya." It's the power to pull a fast one on someone.
usage_notes: Implies a deliberate act of deception. The root 'loko' means 'crazy' or 'fool', so 'makaloko' is literally 'to make a fool out of someone'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-isip na **makaloloko** ka sa akin.","translation":"Don't you think you can **fool** me."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang kanyang ganda para **makaloko** ng mga dayuhan.","translation":"She used her beauty to **be able to trick** foreigners."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang patuloy, paulit-ulit, o propesyonal na gawain ng paghabi. Ito ay tumutukoy sa sining o industriya ng paggawa ng tela.
etymology: From "pag-" + reduplication of the first syllable of the root "ha-" + "habi". This form indicates a more intense, prolonged, or professional action.
original_explanation: This is the leveled-up version of 'paghabi'. It's not just a one-time thing; it's a craft, a livelihood, a continuous process. Think of the T'boli dreamweavers or the artisans in Ilocos making inabel. It's weaving as a professional gig or a deep cultural practice.
usage_notes: This is the more common form used when referring to the craft or industry of weaving, compared to the simple act of "paghabi".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paghahabi** ay ang pangunahing ikinabubuhay ng mga kababaihan sa kanilang tribu.","translation":"**Weaving** is the main livelihood of the women in their tribe."},{"sentence":"Itinuturo sa mga kabataan ang tradisyonal na paraan ng **paghahabi**.","translation":"The youth are taught the traditional method of **weaving**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng kilos o pagsasabi ng mga salita na nagiging sanhi ng paglamig o pagkasira ng magandang relasyon o samahan.
original_explanation: This is when your actions make someone 'seen-zone' you in real life. It's that awkward phase when a friend starts avoiding you because of something you said or did. You didn't just create distance; you built a whole NLEX between your feelings.
usage_notes: A phrasal verb combining 'magpalayo' (to cause to be distant) and 'damdamin' (feelings).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang kayabangan ay siyang **nagpalayo ng damdamin** ng kanyang mga kaibigan.","translation":"His arrogance was what **alienated** his friends."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang gumawa ng bagay na maaaring **magpalayo ng damdamin** natin sa isa't isa.","translation":"Don't do things that might **cause estrangement** between us."}]
related: ["magtanim ng sama ng loob","ikasira ng loob","magkagalit"]

translation: to have a bone fractured; to have a bone broken
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng bali o lamat sa buto dahil sa isang aksidente o pinsala.
etymology: ma- (potential verb prefix) + bali (break, fracture) + -an (locative/referential suffix)
original_explanation: The feeling when you jump off the jeepney too early and land wrong. 'Yung literal na 'na-broken' ka, pero sa buto, hindi sa puso. It's that sharp pain that tells you, 'Oops, should've waited for the full stop.'
usage_notes: Refers to the unfortunate event of someone getting a fracture, not the act of breaking something. 'Nabalian ako' (I got a fracture) vs. 'Binali ko' (I broke it).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingatan mong huwag madulas sa basang sahig at baka ka **mabalian**.","translation":"Be careful not to slip on the wet floor, you might **get a fracture**."},{"sentence":"**Nabalian** ng braso ang bata matapos mahulog sa puno.","translation":"The child **had his arm fractured** after falling from the tree."}]

translation: to beg on one's knees, to implore
meaning_filipino: Pagmamakaawa o paghiling ng isang bagay nang buong pagpapakumbaba, na para bang nakaluhod.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "sana all" level of begging. It's when you're so desperate for forgiveness, a favor, or for them to not break up with you, that you'd literally get on your knees. It's the physical manifestation of "Please, I'm begging you."
usage_notes: This is a very dramatic and intense verb, often used in literature or highly emotional situations. It is formed from the prefix 'man-' (a variation of 'mang-') and the root 'luhod' (knee/kneel), with an '-ik-' infix suggesting an intense or encompassing action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halos **manikluhod** siya sa kanyang amo para lang hindi matanggal sa trabaho.","translation":"He almost **begged on his knees** to his boss just to not get fired from his job."},{"sentence":"\"Hindi mo kailangang **manikluhod** para sa pag-ibig na para sa'yo talaga,\" ang sabi ng kaibigan niya.","translation":"\"You don't need to **implore** for a love that's truly meant for you,\" his friend said."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-aalis ng balat ng isang prutas, gulay, o hayop.
original_explanation: What you do to a banana before you eat it, or to a potato before you make fries. It’s the act of removing the outer layer. Figuratively, it’s what chismosas do to your life story—they peel away every layer and expose everything. 'Binalatan nila ang buong pagkatao ko!'
usage_notes: The verb form of 'balat' (skin/peel).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **balatan** mo ang mga mangga para sa ating panghimagas.","translation":"Please, **peel** the mangoes for our dessert."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **balatan** ang kamote kapag mainit pa.","translation":"It's hard **to peel** a sweet potato when it's still hot."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagsisimula o pagpapakilala ng isang bagay na bago, tulad ng isang proyekto, produkto, o programa.
etymology: From pag- (nominalizing prefix) + lunsad (to launch, to alight).
original_explanation: This is the grand opening, the product drop, the big reveal. It's when your startup finally goes live, or when a new flavor of milk tea is finally available. It's the 'Ready, get set, GO!' moment for any new endeavor. Think of a rocket launch, but for a new business or a political campaign.
usage_notes: Commonly used in business, technology, publishing, and governance contexts to refer to the official start or introduction of something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging matagumpay ang **paglulunsad** ng bagong aklat ng sikat na manunulat.","translation":"The **launch** of the famous author's new book was successful."},{"sentence":"Pinaghahandaan na ng gobyerno ang **paglulunsad** ng bagong programa para sa mga magsasaka.","translation":"The government is preparing for the **launch** of a new program for farmers."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglakad o paggalaw na hindi matatag, pasuray-suray, o tila matutumba.
original_explanation: That walk you do after a few too many bottles of Red Horse. Also, how a building moves during a lindol (earthquake), or how a lola with arthritis might walk. It's the opposite of a stable, confident stride.
usage_notes: Often associated with drunkenness, dizziness, weakness, or structural instability.
