usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kitang-kita ang **paggiray** ng lasing na lalaki habang naglalakad pauwi.","translation":"The **staggering** of the drunk man was very visible as he walked home."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman namin ang **paggiray** ng gusali noong lumindol.","translation":"We felt the **wobbling** of the building when the earthquake hit."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pang-abay na katumbas ng salitang "din" o "rin", ginagamit upang magdagdag ng impormasyon o ipakita ang pagkakatulad, karaniwang sa pormal o patulang paraan.
original_explanation: "Ring" is the formal, slightly old-fashioned cousin of "din" and "rin". It's the version you use in formal writing or when you're trying to sound poetic. Think of it as the "din/rin" that went to a private school. "Ako ring" sounds more dramatic than "Ako rin".
usage_notes: An archaic or poetic variant of 'rin' or 'din'. Used after words ending in vowels, glottal stops, or the consonants 'n' and 'w'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kung aalis ka, aalis na **ring** ako.","translation":"If you are leaving, I will leave **also**."},{"sentence":"Masaya ako't nakarating ka, at masaya **ring** kasama mo siya.","translation":"I'm happy that you arrived, and happy **too** that she is with you."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gamot, substansiya, o pamamaraan na ginagamit upang mawala o mabawasan ang pakiramdam, lalo na ang sakit, sa isang bahagi o sa buong katawan.
original_explanation: Literally, the stuff the dentist gives you so you don't feel the pain. Metaphorically, it's anything you use to numb the feels—alak, Netflix binge-watching, shopping, or even working too much. It's your emotional anesthesia para 'di masyadong ramdam ang sakit ng life.
usage_notes: Can be used in both a literal medical context and a figurative emotional context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-iniksyon ng **pampamanhid** ang dentista bago bunutin ang ngipin ko.","translation":"The dentist injected an **anesthetic** before pulling my tooth."},{"sentence":"Para sa kanya, ang alak ay **pampamanhid** sa kalungkutan.","translation":"For him, alcohol is a **numbing agent** for sadness."}]

translation: act of stuffing oneself with food; gluttony
meaning_filipino: Ang labis na pagkain hanggang sa mabusog nang husto o lumaki ang tiyan; pagpapakabusog.
etymology: From pag- (gerund prefix) + papaka- (intensive prefix) + bundat (stuffed, bloated from eating).
original_explanation: That state of being you achieve after a Pinoy fiesta or hitting an 'eat-all-you-can' buffet. You undo the top button of your jeans, lean back, and swear you'll never eat again... until the next meal. It's the food-coma-inducing finale to a great meal.
usage_notes: Informal and slightly pejorative, implying overindulgence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itigil mo na ang **pagpapakabundat** mo, baka sumakit ang tiyan mo.","translation":"Stop **stuffing yourself with food**, your stomach might hurt."},{"sentence":"Handang-handa na ako para sa **pagpapakabundat** sa Noche Buena mamaya.","translation":"I am so ready for the **gluttony** at the Christmas Eve feast later."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal para sa isang lalaking homoseksuwal. Ginagamit din bilang pang-uri upang ilarawan ang isang bagay na may kaugnayan sa kultura ng mga homoseksuwal na lalaki.
etymology: Isang paglalaro sa salitang 'bakla', na pinalitan ang 'a' at 'la' ng 'e' at 'ki' para sa mas malambing o mas nakakatuwang tunog, isang karaniwang proseso sa pagbuo ng Beki language.
original_explanation: A colloquial, often affectionate term for a gay man in the Philippines. They're the life of the party, your go-to for fashion advice, and the friend who will give you the most brutally honest (but loving) "sermon" about your life choices. The term has been reclaimed and is now a staple of Pinoy pop culture. From 'bakla', it evolved into the cuter-sounding **beki**.
usage_notes: Itinuturing na mas impormal at kung minsan ay mas magiliw kaysa sa salitang "bakla".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kaibigan kong si Paolo ay isang proud na **beki**.","translation":"My friend Paolo is a proud **gay man**."},{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng ayos mo, ang **beki** ng dating!","translation":"Your style is great, it has a very **gay** vibe!"}]

translation: to be able to be converted; to be made to return to God's fold
meaning_filipino: Mailalapit o maibabalik sa pananampalataya sa Diyos.
etymology: Complex verb form from ma- (ability) + papag- (causative) + balik-loob (return of will/spirit).
original_explanation: This is the ultimate goal of your lola for her apo who's always out partying. It's the 'sana magtino ka na' energy, but on a spiritual level. It's the belief that no matter how far someone has strayed, they can still be brought back to the right path, often through prayer, pangaral, or a life-changing event.
usage_notes: A deeply religious and specific phrase. The structure `mapapag-` indicates a causative ability - 'to be *made* to do something'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naniniwala si Aling Nena na sa tulong ng dasal ay **mapapagbalik-loob sa Diyos** ang kanyang anak na naligaw ng landas.","translation":"Aling Nena believes that with the help of prayer, her child who has lost his way **can be made to return to God's fold**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o gawain na sumasalungat sa prinsipyo ng hustisya, pagkakapantay-pantay, at karapatan.
original_explanation: This is when your sibling gets away with something you'd definitely be grounded for. On a larger scale, it's the feeling you get stuck in EDSA traffic while a convoy with "wang-wang" speeds past. It's the system favoring the rich and powerful. It's the core "hugot" of every protest and every social media rant about corruption. It's the ultimate "That's not fair!"
usage_notes: A strong, formal word used in legal, social, and political contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkawalang-katarungan** sa lipunan ay isang malaking hamon na dapat harapin.","translation":"**Injustice** in society is a huge challenge that must be faced."},{"sentence":"Lumalaban sila upang wakasan ang **pagkawalang-katarungan** na dinaranas ng kanilang komunidad.","translation":"They are fighting to end the **injustice** experienced by their community."}]

meaning_filipino: Daglat para sa 'subtitles' (mga sulat sa ilalim ng screen) o 'subscribers' (mga tagasubaybay sa isang online channel).
original_explanation: A word with two main personalities in Pinoy internet culture. 1) The 'subs' on Netflix that you argue about whether to turn on or off. 2) The '**subs**' (subscribers) that vloggers thank profusely at the beginning and end of every video: "Thank you sa lahat ng **subs** natin diyan!" It's the currency of YouTube and Twitch fame.
usage_notes: Used in very specific, modern, and online contexts. Not a traditional Tagalog word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-on ng English **subs**, hindi ko maintindihan.","translation":"Please turn on the English **subs**, I can't understand."},{"sentence":"Malapit na siyang umabot ng 1 million **subs** sa YouTube.","translation":"He's close to reaching 1 million **subs** on YouTube."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na walang pakundangan, hindi marunong mahiya, at walang galang sa kapwa.
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino insult. This is the person who cuts in line, sings karaoke badly at 3 AM, or borrows money and then ghosts you. They operate on a different plane of existence where 'dyahe' or shame doesn't exist. The final boss of 'kakapalan ng mukha'.
usage_notes: A very strong and common insult. Can be used as an adjective ('walang-hiya kang tao') or as a noun/exclamation ('Walang-hiya!').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Walang-hiya** ka! Bakit mo kinuha ang pera ko?","translation":"You're **shameless**! Why did you take my money?"},{"sentence":"Ang taong sumisingit sa pila ay **walang-hiya**.","translation":"A person who cuts in line is **impudent**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng matamis na arnibal o sirup na nagmumula sa dagta ng puno ng sasa o nipa.
etymology: From the combination of Tagalog `pulot` ('honey' or 'molasses') and `sasa` ('nipa palm').
original_explanation: The OG local sweetener before coco sugar became cool. It's the thick, dark syrup your lola uses for kakanin. Think of it as the rustic cousin of maple syrup, but with more island vibes and a deeper, slightly smoky flavor.
usage_notes: Commonly used as a topping for traditional Filipino rice cakes (kakanin) like suman and bibingka.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap ipares sa suman ang **pulot-sasa**.","translation":"**Nipa palm syrup** is delicious with rice cakes."},{"sentence":"Ang paggawa ng **pulot-sasa** ay isang tradisyonal na kabuhayan sa mga baybaying-ilog.","translation":"Making **nipa palm syrup** is a traditional livelihood in riverside communities."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng pag-iingat, pagiging masusi, at pag-iwas sa panganib o pagkakamali.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung pag-type mo ng message sa crush mo, binabasa mo ng sampung beses bago i-send. O 'yung pagtawid mo sa EDSA na parang may level-up sa bawat lane na malampasan mo. Ang opposite nito ay 'yung "bahala na si Batman" attitude. Ang pagiging maingat ay pag-iwas sa "Ay, sh*t!" moments.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maging **maingat** sa pagmamaneho lalo na't madulas ang kalsada.","translation":"Be **careful** when driving, especially since the road is slippery."},{"sentence":"Siya ay **maingat** sa kanyang mga salita upang walang masaktan.","translation":"She is **cautious** with her words so as not to hurt anyone."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maliit at bilog na butong-gulay na kulay berde, karaniwang sangkap sa mga ulam tulad ng menudo at arroz a la valenciana.
original_explanation: Those little green balls of disappointment you used to pick out from your menudo when you were a kid. Now as an adult, you realize they're actually okay. It's the 'pampakulay' and 'pampadami' ng sahog. You buy them in small cans from the grocery.
usage_notes: Almost always refers to canned or frozen green peas used in cooking.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang maglagay ng **gisantes** sa menudo para kumpleto ang sahog.","translation":"Don't forget to add **green peas** to the menudo to complete the ingredients."},{"sentence":"Bumili ka ng isang latang **gisantes** sa tindahan.","translation":"Buy one can of **green peas** at the store."}]

translation: short on time; pressed for time
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkakaroon ng hindi sapat na panahon upang gawin ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the national anthem of every employee during rush hour, every student during finals week, and everyone stuck in EDSA traffic. 'Sorry, I'm late, kapos sa oras!' It's the ultimate Filipino excuse for when time itself is the kontrabida.
usage_notes: A very common fixed phrase.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pasensya na, hindi ako makakapunta. **Kapos sa oras** eh.","translation":"Sorry, I can't go. I'm **short on time**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating bilisan dahil **kapos na tayo sa oras**.","translation":"We need to hurry because we're already **pressed for time**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kataga mula sa Ingles na tumutukoy sa kumpiyansa sa sarili, karisma, at kakaibang istilo sa pananamit at pagkilos.
etymology: Mula sa salitang balbal (slang) sa Ingles na 'swag'.
original_explanation: Circa 2012 vibes. The ancestor of 'rizz.' It's not just about what you wear, but how you carry yourself. Think Justin Bieber in his 'Baby' era or any K-pop idol at the airport. May kasamang porma, angas, at confidence. 'Ang **swag** naman ng porma mo, pre!'
usage_notes: Itinuturing na medyo luma na ang salitang ito sa kasalukuyan, ngunit naiintindihan pa rin ng marami.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **swag** ang kanyang paglakad papunta sa entablado.","translation":"His walk to the stage was full of **swag**."},{"sentence":"Para sa kanya, ang **swag** ay nasa pananamit at salitang may angas.","translation":"For him, **swag** is in the clothes and confident speech."}]

translation: to be able to approach; to get near
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng pagkakataon o kakayahang pumunta sa malapit na distansya sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: That feeling when you see your crush across the room, but there's a sea of titas blocking your way. You're trying your best to *makalapit* but the universe (and your relatives) won't let you. It's the opposite of social distancing.
usage_notes: The "maka-" prefix indicates ability or opportunity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **makalapit** ako sa kanya mamaya para magpakilala.","translation":"I hope I can **get near** him later to introduce myself."},{"sentence":"Hindi siya **makalapit** sa aso dahil takot siyang makagat.","translation":"He couldn't **approach** the dog because he was afraid of being bitten."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng patalim na natitiklop na nagmula sa bayan ng Taal sa Batangas. Ito ay binubuksan at isinasara sa pamamagitan ng pag-ikot ng dalawang hawakan.
etymology: Pinaniniwalaang mula sa mga salitang 'baling sungay' (broken/folded horn), dahil sungay ng kalabaw ang dating ginagamit sa puluhan nito, at mula sa Baryo Balisong sa Taal, Batangas.
original_explanation: The OG fidget spinner from Batangas. Before it became a cool trick item in action movies, it was the province's iconic pocketknife, also known as a fan knife. Handle with care, or you'll get more than just a paper cut. The term '29' or 'veinte-nueve' is a popular slang for it.
usage_notes: Strongly associated with Batangas province and Filipino martial arts. It is a regulated weapon in many places.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagmamalaki ng mga taga-Batangas ang kanilang dekalidad na **balisong**.","translation":"The people of Batangas are proud of their high-quality **butterfly knives**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagbibigay ng tulong o suporta, lalo na sa mga nangangailangan, nang walang hinihintay na kapalit.
etymology: From pagka- (prefix indicating manner or quality) + kawanggawa (charity), which is from ka- + awa (mercy) + ng + gawa (deed).
original_explanation: This is your "pahingi po ng 5-star review" heart. It's the act of donating to a G-Cash QR code you saw on Facebook for a cause, or joining a community pantry. It's the corporate social responsibility (CSR) part of a company's yearly plan. Basically, it's doing good deeds, whether for genuine kindness or for the 'gram.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala ang pamilya nila sa kanilang **pagkakawanggawa** sa komunidad.","translation":"Their family is known for their **philanthropy** in the community."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkakawanggawa** ay isang mahalagang bahagi ng kanilang misyon.","translation":"**Charity** is an important part of their mission."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang parirala na ginagamit upang ipahayag ang pinakamababa o pinakasimpleng inaasahan o hinihiling sa isang sitwasyon.
original_explanation: This is the official phrase of 'sana all' but with lower expectations. It's the 'hugot' of asking for the bare minimum. 'Sana tinawagan mo man lamang ako.' (You could have at least called me.) It's what you say when your crush doesn't like you back, but you wish they'd at least seen your IG story. It's the sigh of a disappointed heart.
usage_notes: Expresses a sense of longing, disappointment, or a plea for a minimal action or acknowledgment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kung hindi ka makakapunta, sana nagsabi ka **man lamang**.","translation":"If you couldn't come, you could have **at least** told me."},{"sentence":"Bigyan mo naman ako ng isa **man lamang**.","translation":"Give me **even just** one."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang masira nang husto; gumuho. Sa matalinhagang kahulugan, ang makaramdam ng matinding kalungkutan o pagkasiphayo.
original_explanation: When your heart feels like it's been through a blender because of some serious hugot. That feeling of being utterly devastated, like when you find out your favorite milk tea shop closed down. Your heart is mabagbag. It can also literally mean for something to be wrecked, like a ship in a storm.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for physical destruction or figuratively for emotional devastation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayokong **mabagbag** ang puso mo dahil sa maling tao.","translation":"I don't want your heart **to be crushed** because of the wrong person."},{"sentence":"Maaaring **mabagbag** ang lumang bahay sa lakas ng lindol.","translation":"The old house might **be wrecked** by the strength of the earthquake."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na ipinagkakaloob sa isang tao nang walang inaasahang kapalit; regalo.
original_explanation: The noun form. The actual thing you give, whether it's a gift, a chance, or your heart. Parang 'Ano'ng bigay mo sa Pasko?' (What gift did you give for Christmas?). It's also used for effort, like 'Ibigay mo ang lahat,' meaning 'Give it your all.' It's the 'pasalubong' from your tita from the US, the 'ayuda' from the government, or the unsolicited advice from your marites na kapitbahay.
usage_notes: Maaari ring maging salitang-ugat para sa pandiwang 'ibigay' (to give).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng **bigay** mong relo!","translation":"The watch you **gave** is beautiful!"},{"sentence":"Todo **bigay** siya sa kanyang performance kagabi.","translation":"He went **all out** in his performance last night."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pangkat demograpiko ng mga taong ipinanganak mula sa mga unang taon ng 2010 hanggang sa kalagitnaan ng 2020. Sila ang henerasyong sumunod sa Generation Z.
original_explanation: The kids who were born with an iPad in one hand and a TikTok account in the other. Sila yung mga pamangkin mong mas magaling pa sa'yo mag-navigate ng settings ng phone mo. Basically, the future, and they're already cooler than us.
usage_notes: Isang modernong katawagan na hiram sa Ingles, karaniwang ginagamit sa mga usapang sosyolohikal at marketing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **genalpha** ay lumalaking bihasa sa digital na teknolohiya.","translation":"**Generation Alpha** is growing up well-versed in digital technology."},{"sentence":"Paano kaya mag-isip ang mga **genalpha** paglaki nila?","translation":"I wonder how **Generation Alpha** will think when they grow up?"}]

translation: to be spotted or seen (by someone)
meaning_filipino: Makita o mapansin ng isang tao mula sa isang partikular na lokasyon o pananaw.
original_explanation: This is the opposite of `matanaw`. You are the object being seen. It's that mini-panic when you're doing something silly in public and you realize someone from a high-rise window might be watching you. "Hala, baka may makatanaw sa atin dito!" It's being visible from a vantage point.
usage_notes: The focus is on the person or object being seen from afar. The -an suffix shifts the focus. Compare: Matanaw ko ang isla (I can see the island). Matatanawan ako sa isla (I can be seen from the island).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit nasa malayo ka, **matatanawan** ka pa rin dahil sa suot mong matingkad na damit.","translation":"Even if you're far away, you **can still be spotted** because of the bright clothes you're wearing."},{"sentence":"Tago tayo dito para hindi tayo **matanawan** ng guwardiya.","translation":"Let's hide here so we won't **be seen** by the guard."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat na binubuo ng apat na tao o bagay; isang gawain na para sa apat.
original_explanation: The squad size for a classic mahjong game, a road trip in a small car, or that group project where only two people actually do the work. "Apatan tayo sa Grab, para mas mura!"
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang tukuyin ang isang grupo o pagsasaayos na may bilang na apat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Apatan** ang pag-upo sa bawat mesa sa restaurant.","translation":"The seating at each table in the restaurant is for a **group of four**."},{"sentence":"Naglaro kami ng tong-its na **apatan**.","translation":"We played a **foursome** game of tong-its."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tindahan o puwesto na ang pangunahing paninda ay mga sariwang prutas.
original_explanation: The designated spot for all things fruity. It's the stall in the market with the most vibrant colors, or that roadside stand you stop at on the way to Tagaytay for pineapples. Think of it as a fruit-only 7-Eleven.
usage_notes: Hindi gaanong karaniwan kumpara sa "tindahan ng prutas" ngunit naiintindihan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili kami ng isang basket ng iba't ibang prutas sa **pruteriya**.","translation":"We bought a basket of assorted fruits at the **fruit store**."},{"sentence":"May bagong bukas na **pruteriya** malapit sa aming bahay.","translation":"A new **fruit stand** opened near our house."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing mas maikli ang isang bagay, tulad ng haba, oras, o teksto.
original_explanation: What your boss tells you to do with your 10-page report: "Paikliin mo." What you wish you could do to the EDSA traffic. Also, what happens to your salary—ang bilis paikliin ng bills.
usage_notes: A very common verb used for text, hair, clothes, speeches, time, etc.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **paikliin** mo ang iyong talumpati para hindi antukin ang mga tao.","translation":"Please, **shorten** your speech so people don't get sleepy."},{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **paikliin** ang kanyang buhok para sa tag-init.","translation":"She decided **to shorten** her hair for the summer."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na termino mula sa Ingles na tumutukoy sa isang tao na lubos na tapat at susuporta sa iyo sa anumang sitwasyon, kahit na ito ay mahirap o mapanganib.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na "ride or die".
original_explanation: Your ultimate beshie, tropa, or jowa. Sila 'yung sasamahan kang kumain ng isaw sa kanto, pero kaya ka ring samahan sa fine dining. 'Yung hindi ka lang dadamayan sa tagumpay, kundi pati sa pag-cram ng thesis at 3 AM. Sila 'yung "walang iwanan" in its purest, most modern form.
usage_notes: Isang modernong slang na popular sa mga kabataan at sa social media. Maaaring gamitin bilang pang-uri (e.g., "ride-or-die friend") o pangalan (e.g., "You are my ride-or-die").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **rideordie** ko, kasama ko sa lahat ng kalokohan.","translation":"She's my **ride or die**, with me through all the crazy stuff."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mo ng isang **rideordie** na kaibigan sa buhay.","translation":"You need a **ride or die** friend in life."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babasahin na binubuo ng serye ng mga iginuhit na larawan na may kasamang teksto o diyalogo, na nagsasalaysay ng isang kuwento.
original_explanation: The original Filipino graphic novel. Before Netflix and YouTube, this was the go-to entertainment, bought from the corner sari-sari store. It's where legends like Darna, Captain Barbell, and Lastikman were born. It's the reason why your lolo's imagination is probably more colorful than your Instagram feed.
usage_notes: Refers to the traditional Filipino comic books, often printed on newsprint, which were extremely popular from the mid to late 20th century.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig akong magbasa ng **komiks** noong bata pa ako.","translation":"I loved reading **comics** when I was young."},{"sentence":"Maraming sikat na pelikula ang hango sa mga kuwento sa **komiks**.","translation":"Many famous movies are based on stories from **comic books**."}]

meaning_filipino: Higit sa karaniwan, wasto, o kinakailangang antas; labis o sobra.
etymology: Hiram sa salitang Espanyol na "demasiado," na nangangahulugang "labis" o "sobra."
original_explanation: The official word for being "extra." Yung kaibigan mong nag-makeup para lang bumili sa sari-sari store? Masyadong nag-effort. Yung presyo ng sibuyas? Masyadong mahal. Yung feelings mo para sa kanya na 'di ka naman gusto? Masyado kang umasa. It's the amplifier for everything that's just... a lot.
usage_notes: Palaging ginagamit upang baguhin ang isang pang-uri, pandiwa, o isa pang pang-abay upang ipahiwatig ang kalabisan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Masyado** kang maingay, natutulog ang sanggol.","translation":"You are **too** noisy, the baby is sleeping."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **masyado** mag-alala, malulutas din natin ito.","translation":"Don't worry **too** much, we will solve this."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtungo o pagpunta sa bukid o kanayunan, karaniwan upang magsaka o mamahinga.
original_explanation: When you're tired of the city life, the traffic, and your toxic boss, you tell your friends, "Tara, mamukid muna tayo!" It's the act of escaping to the province, swapping your laptop for a carabao, and your Starbucks for fresh buko juice. The ultimate "probinsya life" fantasy.
usage_notes: Often used to mean going to the province or countryside in general, not just a specific farm.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Plano naming **mamukid** sa darating na bakasyon para makalanghap ng sariwang hangin.","translation":"We plan to **go to the countryside** during the upcoming vacation to breathe fresh air."},{"sentence":"Tuwing tag-araw, umuuwi si Lolo sa Batangas para **mamukid**.","translation":"Every summer, Grandpa goes home to Batangas to **spend time at the farm**."}]

translation: if paired with; if matched with
meaning_filipino: Isang pariralang nagpapahayag ng kondisyon ng pagtatambal o pagsasama ng isang bagay sa isa pa upang makabuo ng magandang resulta.
etymology: Combination of 'kung' (if) and 'ipaparis' (will be paired), from the root 'paris' (pair).
original_explanation: The ultimate foodie and fashionista phrase. It's how you justify that extra cup of rice ('Masarap 'to **kung ipaparis** sa kanin!') or that questionable outfit choice ('Gaganda 'to **kung ipaparis** sa tamang sapatos.'). It's the logic of combination.
usage_notes: Often used in culinary, fashion, or design contexts to describe good combinations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap ang kape **kung ipaparis** sa pandesal.","translation":"Coffee is delicious **if paired with** pandesal."},{"sentence":"Ang blusang iyan ay babagay **kung ipaparis** sa itim na palda.","translation":"That blouse will look good **if matched with** a black skirt."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang kilos ng pagpapadala ng isang mensahe, email, o anumang bagay sa isang patutunguhan.
etymology: Tagalog prefix 'nag-' + duplicated first syllable of root 'se-' + English 'send'.
original_explanation: Yung tropa mong nagsesend ng memes sa'yo at 2 AM. Alam mong gising pa kayo pareho at walang ginagawa sa buhay. A true sign of friendship.
usage_notes: Present progressive tense. The past tense is 'nagsend' and the future tense is 'magse-send'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maingay, **nagsesend** ako ng mahalagang text.","translation":"Be quiet, I'm **sending** an important text."},{"sentence":"Palagi siyang **nagsesend** ng 'good morning' sa akin.","translation":"He is always **sending** 'good morning' messages to me."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng manggagawa na ang trabaho ay magbenta ng mga produkto o serbisyo sa isang tindahan o establisyimento.
original_explanation: The omnipresent figure in every SM Department Store who magically appears when you touch an item, asking "Ma'am/Sir, ano pong hanap nila?" They are the guardians of the retail floor, masters of inventory, and can fold a shirt faster than you can say "May small po nito?". A highly respected and common job in the Philippines.
usage_notes: A very common English loanword fully integrated into Tagalog. The male equivalent is 'salesman'. 'Sales associate' or 'sales staff' are more gender-neutral terms but 'saleslady' remains extremely common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinulungan ako ng **saleslady** na mahanap ang tamang sukat ng sapatos.","translation":"The **saleslady** helped me find the right shoe size."},{"sentence":"Nag-apply siya bilang **saleslady** sa isang malaking mall.","translation":"She applied as a **saleslady** in a big mall."}]

meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kahalili o kapalit sa isang posisyon, bagay, o relasyon.
original_explanation: The 'hugot' version: 'Yung ang bilis mong **mapalitan** ng ex mo, parang nag-add to cart lang siya ng bago. The practical version: 'Yung ilaw sa kusina na kailangan nang **mapalitan** kasi fundido na. It's the universal experience of being swapped out for something or someone new.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **mapalitan** na ang luma kong cellphone.","translation":"I want my old cellphone **to be replaced** already."},{"sentence":"Masakit para sa kanya na malaman na agad siyang **napalitan** sa puso ng kanyang dating nobyo.","translation":"It was painful for her to find out she was quickly **replaced** in her ex-boyfriend's heart."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtatama sa isang kamalian, pagkukulang, o depekto upang ito ay maging wasto, tama, o angkop.
original_explanation: This is what your high school teacher did to your test papers with a red pen. It's editing your friend's caption to fix their grammar, or your mom adjusting the `timpla` of your adobo. In the world of fake news, `pagwawasto` is the act of dropping the truth bombs and fact-checking receipts in the comments section.
usage_notes: Commonly used in academic, editorial, and formal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagwawasto** sa mga maling impormasyon ay responsibilidad ng bawat isa.","translation":"The **correction** of wrong information is everyone's responsibility."},{"sentence":"Ipinasa ng mag-aaral ang kanyang sanaysay para sa **pagwawasto** ng guro.","translation":"The student submitted his essay for the teacher's **correction**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na mamamayan o katutubo ng Alemanya; ang wika ng Alemanya; o anumang tumutukoy o may kaugnayan sa Alemanya.
original_explanation: Refers to anything from Germany. That high-quality beer, the car that costs a fortune to maintain, or the tourist with socks and sandals. Also, the language that sounds like you're angry but you're just asking for bread. "Yung kotse niya, Aleman. Mahal."
usage_notes: Can function as a noun (a German person) or an adjective (of German origin).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakapangasawa siya ng isang **Aleman**.","translation":"She married a **German** (person)."},{"sentence":"Mahirap pag-aralan ang wikang **Aleman**.","translation":"The **German** language is difficult to study."},{"sentence":"Kilala ang mga sasakyang **Aleman** sa kalidad nito.","translation":"**German** cars are known for their quality."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangalan o katawagan na ibinibigay sa isang tao, lugar, o bagay bilang kapalit o karagdagan sa tunay na pangalan nito, na kadalasang batay sa isang katangian.
original_explanation: This is your alias, your AKA. It's what your barkada calls you, which might be a shortened version of your name, a description of your looks ("Tisoy"), or a reminder of that one embarrassing thing you did in high school. Jose Rizal had 'Laong Laan', your tito has 'Boy Bawang', and you probably have one you don't want your parents to know.
usage_notes: Can be a term of endearment, a neutral descriptor, or an insult. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang 'El Mago' ang **bansag** sa sikat na manlalaro ng basketball.","translation":"'The Magician' is the **moniker** of the famous basketball player."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang katangkaran, 'Tangkad' ang naging **bansag** sa kanya.","translation":"Because of his height, 'Tangkad' (Tall) became his **nickname**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng isdang-alat na may mahaba at manipis na katawan, na kilala rin bilang ladyfish.
original_explanation: Not the most popular fish in the palengke, kind of an underdog. It's bony, so it's a bit of a challenge to eat. Think of it as the fish you buy when the galunggong and tilapia are sold out. Often dried or used in fish balls.
usage_notes: Known for having many fine bones, making it difficult to eat fresh for some.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming tinik ang isdang **bidbid** kaya kailangang mag-ingat sa pagkain nito.","translation":"The **ladyfish** has many bones, so you need to be careful when eating it."},{"sentence":"Gawing daing na **bidbid** ang mga nahuli ni tatay.","translation":"Let's turn the **ladyfish** that dad caught into dried fish."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang magpatuloy sa isang gawain o layunin sa kabila ng mga paghihirap, pagkaantala, o hadlang nang hindi sumusuko.
original_explanation: This is the fuel that runs the Philippines. It's lining up for hours at a government office, studying for the board exams while working full-time, or enduring a 3-hour commute on EDSA every single day. It’s the ‘tiis-ganda’ for your soul. It’s the belief that all the suffering will be worth it in the end. A true Filipino superpower.
usage_notes: A core Filipino value, often associated with hard work and resilience.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakamit niya ang tagumpay dahil sa kanyang **pagtitiyaga**.","translation":"He achieved success because of his **perseverance**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng matinding **pagtitiyaga** para matuto ng bagong wika.","translation":"You need a lot of **patience** to learn a new language."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng mananayaw ng ballet.
original_explanation: A ballerina. The epitome of grace and discipline, like Lisa Macuja-Elizalde. Also, what your mom wanted you to be when you were 5, forcing you into a pink tutu and ballet classes you probably hated. Now, it's a term for anyone who seems to move with effortless grace, or someone who's just really, really flexible.
usage_notes: The male counterpart is less common but would be 'mananayaw ng ballet'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang maging isang sikat na **baylerina** balang araw.","translation":"She dreams of becoming a famous **ballerina** someday."},{"sentence":"Ang galing ng mga galaw ng pangunahing **baylerina** sa palabas.","translation":"The movements of the lead **ballerina** in the show were excellent."}]

translation: the manner/way of leaving or removal
meaning_filipino: Ang paraan o sirkumstansya ng pag-alis, pagtatanggal, o pagkawala ng isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: This is about the "how" of the leaving. Was it a dramatic "I'm leaving and I'm taking the dog!" exit, or a quiet ghosting? "Ang ganda ng pagkakaalis niya sa kumpanya, may pa-despedida at bonus pa." It describes the circumstances surrounding a departure or removal.
usage_notes: The 'pagkaka-' affix emphasizes the manner, reason, or circumstance of the action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-uusapan pa rin ang biglaang **pagkakaalis** ng dating CEO.","translation":"The sudden **departure** of the former CEO is still being talked about."},{"sentence":"Maayos ang **pagkakaalis** ng mantsa sa damit.","translation":"The **removal** of the stain from the clothes was done well."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang magalang na paraan ng paghingi ng paumanhin o kapatawaran para sa isang pagkakamali.
etymology: From `patawad` (forgiveness) + `po` (politeness marker). `Patawad` itself is from `pa-` (request prefix) + `tawad` (pardon, discount).
original_explanation: The ultimate "I messed up and I respect you" phrase. You use this when you bump into an elder on the MRT, when you're late for a meeting with your boss, or when you accidentally delete a shared file. The "po" is the magic word that dials the politeness and sincerity up to 11. It's the verbal equivalent of a respectful bow.
usage_notes: A set phrase used to apologize politely. The 'po' indicates respect towards the person being addressed, who is typically older or of higher status.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Patawad po**, lola, hindi ko po sinasadya na mabangga kayo.","translation":"**I'm sorry**, grandma, I didn't mean to bump into you."},{"sentence":"Sir, **patawad po** sa aking pagkahuli.","translation":"Sir, **I apologize** for being late."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ranggo sa militar o pulisya na mas mataas sa pribado ngunit mas mababa sa sarhento.
etymology: From Spanish 'cabo', meaning 'end' or 'cape,' also used for 'corporal.'
original_explanation: This is a military or police rank, like a corporal. In old movies, the 'kabo' is usually the right-hand man of the main 'kontrabida' or the tough but fair squad leader. Think of them as the team lead in your BPO company—not quite the manager, but the one you go to when the system crashes.
usage_notes: Primarily used in military, police, or historical contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inatasan ng **kabo** ang kanyang mga tauhan na maghanda para sa inspeksyon.","translation":"The **corporal** ordered his men to prepare for inspection."},{"sentence":"Si **Kabo** Tasyo ang pinakamatapang sa kanilang platun.","translation":"**Corporal** Tasyo was the bravest in their platoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Gumagamit ng isang mainit na kasangkapan, ang plantsa, upang alisin ang mga lukot sa damit.
original_explanation: That Sunday night feeling when you realize you have nothing to wear for work tomorrow, kaya heto ka, nagpiplantsa at 11 PM. It's the chore that smells like steam and responsibility. The 'p' is duplicated (nag-pi-plantsa) to show it's a current, ongoing action.
usage_notes: Present progressive tense. For root words starting with a consonant blend like 'pl', the first syllable is not repeated. Instead, the first consonant 'p' and the vowel 'i' are used: nag-pi-plantsa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Habang nanonood ng TV, **nagpiplantsa** ng damit si nanay.","translation":"While watching TV, mom **is ironing** clothes."},{"sentence":"Ayoko maistorbo kapag ako ay **nagpiplantsa** dahil baka masunog ang damit.","translation":"I don't want to be disturbed when I **am ironing** because the clothes might get burned."}]

meaning_filipino: Sobrang pagpuri sa isang tao, na kung minsan ay hindi na tapat at may kaakibat na pansariling interes.
original_explanation: 'Yung papuri ng officemate mo sa bago mong buhok, pero a few minutes later, "Uy, baka pwede mo 'ko i-cover sa shift ko mamaya?" It's the "sipsip" starter pack. It's when someone calls you "gwapo" and you know they need to borrow money.
usage_notes: Often used to describe insincere compliments or adulation. Synonymous with "bola" (flattery).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala agad sa **labis na papuri**; baka mauto ka lang.","translation":"Don't immediately believe in **flattery**; you might just get fooled."},{"sentence":"Ang **labis na papuri** ay paraan niya para makuha ang loob ng amo.","translation":"**Excessive praise** is his way of getting on the boss's good side."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto o kilos ng paglilibang sa pamamagitan ng isang laro o aktibidad na nakakaaliw.
original_explanation: This is what you tell your mom you're doing when you're actually grinding in Mobile Legends for 8 hours straight. It's the general term for any form of play, from patintero in the streets to "playing" with someone's feelings. Charot.
usage_notes: The gerund form of the verb 'maglaro' (to play). Refers to the action itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itigil mo na ang **paglalaro** ng video games at mag-aral ka na.","translation":"Stop **playing** video games and study now."},{"sentence":"Ang **paglalaro** ay mahalaga sa pag-unlad ng isang bata.","translation":"**Playing** is important for a child's development."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagkain, inumin, gamot, o anumang bagay na pinaniniwalaang nakapagpapasigla o nakapagpapataas ng pagnanasang sekswal.
etymology: From 'pang-' (instrumental prefix) + 'pa-' (causative prefix) + 'libog' (lust, libido). Lit. 'that which is used to cause libido'.
original_explanation: This is the 'talaba' (oysters), the dark chocolate, or the 'Fifty Shades of Grey' movie marathon. It's anything that supposedly gets you 'in the mood.' Often whispered about in markets ('Suki, bili ka nitong talaba, pampalibog!') and subject to much debate and placebo effect.
usage_notes: The root word 'libog' is often considered vulgar or overly direct in polite conversation. 'Pampalibog' is used more clinically or jokingly.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinasabing ang mga talaba ay isang mabisang **pampalibog**.","translation":"It is said that oysters are an effective **aphrodisiac**."},{"sentence":"Para sa ilan, ang alak ay nagsisilbing **pampalibog**.","translation":"For some, alcohol serves as an **aphrodisiac**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang paggawa o di-sinasadyang pagdudulot ng bingal o sira sa gilid ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: The action that *causes* your favorite mug to become `bingal`. This is the verb form. "Hoy, dahan-dahan sa paghugas! Baka **bingalin** mo 'yang mga plato!" (Hey, be careful with the washing! You might **chip** those plates!) It's the sound of your mom's voice echoing in your head every time you handle expensive dinnerware.
usage_notes: Verb form of 'bingal'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinadya niyang **bingalin** ang dulo ng lapis.","translation":"He intentionally **chipped** the tip of the pencil."},{"sentence":"Nanghihinayang siya dahil naaksidente niyang na**bingal** ang antigong plorera.","translation":"She regrets accidentally **chipping** the antique vase."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang regular at paulit-ulit na paggalaw o tunog, lalo na ng puso o ng isang orasan.
original_explanation: It's the rhythm of life, literally. It's the beat you feel in your chest after running to catch the jeep, the throb in your head after a night out, or the fluttery beat of your heart when your crush's chat bubble goes "is typing...".
usage_notes: Most commonly associated with the heart ('tibok ng puso'), but can be used for other rhythmic beats.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Rinig na rinig ko ang **tibok** ng aking puso dahil sa kaba.","translation":"I could clearly hear the **beat** of my heart due to nervousness."},{"sentence":"Sinusukat ng nars ang **tibok** ng kanyang pulso.","translation":"The nurse is measuring the **pulse** of his wrist."}]

meaning_filipino: Magkalapit na magkalapit; halos magkadikit.
original_explanation: 'Yung moment na sobrang siksikan sa MRT, wala ka nang choice kundi maging **dait** sa katabi mo, kahit 'di mo siya kilala. Pwede ring 'yung upo niyo ng bestie mo habang nagtsi-tsismisan, halos walang space sa pagitan. Social distancing's worst enemy.
usage_notes: Often used with a prefix like "magka-" (magkadikit) or "pagka-" (pagkakadait) to describe the state of being close to each other.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dait** ang kanilang mga balikat habang nanonood ng sine.","translation":"Their shoulders were **close together** while watching the movie."},{"sentence":"Magka**dait** ang aming mga bahay.","translation":"Our houses are **adjacent** to each other."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagpapakita ng pagmamahal o paglalambing sa pamamagitan ng salita, haplos, o kilos.
original_explanation: 'Yung maliliit na acts of service at lambing. 'Yung pag-akbay ng jowa mo, 'yung pag-text ng "kumain ka na?", o 'yung pag-headpat ng nanay mo. It's the physical or verbal expression of "I care about you" na hindi kailangang grand. The opposite of "seen."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpakita siya ng **karinyo** sa pamamagitan ng paghawak sa aking kamay.","translation":"She showed **affection** by holding my hand."},{"sentence":"Hinahanap-hanap ng bata ang **karinyo** ng kanyang ina.","translation":"The child longs for his mother's **affection**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katawagan para sa isang tao na labis na naghahanap o nagnanasa ng atensyon mula sa iba.
original_explanation: The Filipino equivalent of "clout-chaser" or "extra." That person in your feed who posts cryptic statuses, vague sad stories, or 100 selfies a day, just waiting for someone to comment, "What happened?" or "Ganda naman!" Can be shortened to "UP."
usage_notes: A modern, informal, and often pejorative term. Often abbreviated as KSP (Kulang Sa Pansin).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang patulan, **uhawpansin** lang 'yan.","translation":"Don't mind him/her, they're just **attention-seeking**."},{"sentence":"Minsan, ang mga taong **uhawpansin** ay may malalim na pinagdadaanan.","translation":"Sometimes, people who are **attention-seeking** are going through something deep."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa o pagganap ng isang gawain, partikular na bilang isang hanapbuhay, upang kumita ng pera o makamit ang isang layunin.
original_explanation: The daily grind. The reason you can't go to the beach on a Wednesday. It's the "para sa ekonomiya" hustle, whether you're WFH in your pajamas or commuting for 3 hours. It's the verb that pays the bills, the milk tea cravings, and the Shopee checkout.
usage_notes: One of the most common verbs in Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **magtrabaho** nang mabuti para sa kinabukasan ng pamilya ko.","translation":"I need to **work** hard for the future of my family."},{"sentence":"Saan ka nagtatrabaho ngayon?","translation":"Where do you work now?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang pananong na ginagamit upang tukuyin ang sukat, kantidad, antas, o digri ng isang bagay, katangian, o kilos.
original_explanation: The ultimate "How much?" question. From asking the price of chichirya sa tindahan ("Gaano po ito?") to asking your ex "Gaano ba kasakit?" after seeing their new IG story. It's the interrogative word for when you need to measure something, whether it's the length of a rope or the depth of your *feels*.
usage_notes: Often used with adjectives, like "gaano kalaki" (how big), "gaano kalayo" (how far), or "gaano kahalaga" (how important).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Gaano** karaming asukal ang ilalagay ko sa kape?","translation":"**How much** sugar should I put in the coffee?"},{"sentence":"Hindi niya alam kung **gaano** kahirap ang pinagdaanan ko.","translation":"She doesn't know **how** difficult what I went through was."}]

translation: to be disturbed; to be bothered
meaning_filipino: Ang maabala o magambala sa ginagawa dahil sa isang panlabas na salik.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling mo kapag WFH ka tapos biglang nag-videoke 'yung kapitbahay mo. O 'yung natawag sa'yo 'yung kaibigan mo para lang mag-rant, at kailangan mo nang mag-CR. "Friend, sorry, baka maestorbo kita..." ay madalas na intro bago mang-istorbo.
usage_notes: Often used in polite expressions to preface a potential interruption, e.g., "Pasensya na kung maestorbo kita." (Sorry if I'm bothering you.)
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw kong **maestorbo** ang tulog mo kaya hindi na ako tumawag.","translation":"I didn't want **to disturb** your sleep, so I didn't call anymore."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi ka **maestorbo** dito.","translation":"Don't worry, you won't **be bothered** here."}]

meaning_filipino: Daglat para sa "Rhythm and Blues," isang genre ng musika na nagmula sa mga komunidad ng Aprikano-Amerikano noong 1940s.
etymology: Acronym for the English music genre 'Rhythm and Blues'.
original_explanation: The official soundtrack of your 'senti' moments, your late-night drives, or when you're trying to be smooth. Think Jay-R, Kyla, Usher. "Pang-**RnB** 'yung boses niya, 'no? Ang lambing."
usage_notes: Standard abbreviation for the music genre, widely understood in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig akong makinig sa mga lumang **RnB** songs noong 90s.","translation":"I love listening to old **R&B** songs from the 90s."},{"sentence":"May bagong album 'yung paborito kong **RnB** artist.","translation":"My favorite **R&B** artist has a new album."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging nakahanda, nakaayos, o may sapat na kaalaman at kagamitan para sa isang partikular na gawain, sitwasyon, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is the 'laging handa' Boy Scout motto applied to everyday life. It's having a power bank for your phone, an umbrella when it looks cloudy, and your resume updated just in case your toxic boss finally pushes you over the edge. It's the opposite of 'bahala na si Batman.'
usage_notes: Frequently used in discussions about disaster preparedness, planning, and personal readiness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **pagiging handa** sa anumang sakuna.","translation":"**Preparedness** for any disaster is important."},{"sentence":"Ipinakita niya ang kanyang **pagiging handa** sa pagsusulit sa pamamagitan ng pag-aaral nang mabuti.","translation":"She showed her **readiness** for the exam by studying well."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng lamat, sira, o pira-pirasong bahagi dahil sa pagkabagsak o matinding puwersa.
original_explanation: Like your phone screen after it slips from your hand. Or that favorite mug you can't use anymore. Figuratively, it can also mean someone is a little 'off' or 'crazy'—'may basag sa ulo' (has a crack in the head). It's the state of things before they become 'wasak.'
usage_notes: Used for objects. 'May basag sa ulo' is a common idiom.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ibinalik niya ang salamin dahil **may-basag** ito sa gilid.","translation":"He returned the mirror because it **had a crack** on the side."},{"sentence":"Ingatan mo ang plorera, baka magka-**basag**.","translation":"Be careful with the vase, it might get **cracked**."}]

meaning_filipino: Habulin sa pamamagitan ng batas; parusahan o pahirapan dahil sa paniniwala, lahi, o iba pang katangian.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you get sued. Or, on a more dramatic level, it's that feeling when your conscience won't leave you alone about something you did wrong. 'Inuusig ng konsensya,' as they say. It's the legal or moral version of 'habulin mo ako!'
usage_notes: Often used in legal contexts (prosecute) or moral/psychological contexts (persecuted by conscience).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga taong sangkot sa katiwalian ay dapat **usigin** at managot sa batas.","translation":"The people involved in corruption should be **prosecuted** and be held accountable by the law."},{"sentence":"Simula nang magsinungaling siya, inu**usig** na siya ng kanyang konsensya gabi-gabi.","translation":"Ever since he lied, his conscience has been **persecuting** him every night."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manipis na pisi o alambre na karaniwang ginagamit sa mga instrumentong pangmusika tulad ng gitara; maaari ring tumukoy sa litid ng katawan.
original_explanation: The thing that makes your guitar go 'twang!' It’s the string you pluck. Metaphorically, it can also be the 'bagting ng puso' (heartstring) that gets pulled when you watch a sad movie, or the 'bagting sa leeg' (tendon on the neck) that pops out when you're really angry or stressed. It's all about tension.
usage_notes: Used for musical instruments, bows (pana), or in anatomy for tendons/ligaments. 'Kuwerdas' is a more common synonym for musical instrument strings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naputol ang isang **bagting** ng kanyang gitara habang tumutugtog.","translation":"One **string** of his guitar broke while he was playing."}]

translation: to bewitch; to cast a spell on
meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng kulam upang magdulot ng pinsala o sakit sa isang tao; ang pagiging target ng isang pangkukulam.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'kulam.' This is what you threaten to do when you're feeling extra vengeful (jokingly, of course... or not?). 'Sa sobrang inis ko sa kanya, parang gusto ko siyang ipakulam!' The receiving end is 'kinulam' (was bewitched). It's the ultimate 'curse you!' in the Filipino context.
usage_notes: An object-focused verb. The person being bewitched is the object of the verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May kakayahan daw ang mangkukulam na **kulamin** ang sinumang nais niya.","translation":"They say a sorcerer has the ability **to bewitch** anyone they want."},{"sentence":"Binalaan siya na baka **kulamin** siya ng kanyang kaaway.","translation":"He was warned that his enemy might **cast a spell on** him."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hindi inaasahang at mabilis na pagpapakita o pagdating ng isang tao, bagay, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: That moment when someone you were just gossiping about suddenly walks into the room. Or when a pimple makes a `biglang paglitaw` the night before a big date. It's the universe's jump scare. The Tagalog equivalent of "and then, out of nowhere..."
usage_notes: A common descriptive phrase, not a fixed idiom.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **biglang paglitaw** ng multo sa pelikula ay ikinagulat ng lahat.","translation":"The **sudden appearance** of the ghost in the movie surprised everyone."},{"sentence":"Kinabahan ako sa **biglang paglitaw** ng boss ko sa likod ko.","translation":"I got nervous at the **sudden appearance** of my boss behind me."}]

translation: to list; to make a list
meaning_filipino: Gumawa ng isang talaan o listahan ng mga pangalan, bagay, o gawain nang sunud-sunod.
original_explanation: Before you go to the palengke or S&R, you 'maglista' so you don't forget the toyo and the suka. It's the act of making a list, whether it's your grocery list, your list of 'sana all' goals for 2026, or the list of exes you'd rather not run into at the mall.
usage_notes: A very common verb used in daily life for planning and organization.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **maglista** ng mga bibilhin ko para sa Noche Buena.","translation":"I need to **make a list** of things I'll buy for Christmas Eve dinner."},{"sentence":"**Maglista** ka ng mga pro at con bago ka magdesisyon.","translation":"**List** down the pros and cons before you decide."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kapaligiran, mga kaugalian, o mga aral na nakagisnan mula sa pagkabata hanggang sa paglaki. Ito ang pundasyon ng pagkatao na nabuo sa murang edad.
etymology: From the root word `mulat`, meaning 'to open one's eyes' or 'to become aware'. The `kina-an` affixation points to the place or circumstance where one 'opened their eyes' to the world.
original_explanation: This is your "origin story" environment. The values, the TV shows (Batibot, anyone?), the brand of hotdog, the level of spiciness in the adobo—these are the things you kinamulatan. It's the stuff you absorbed as a kid that now makes you say, "Ganito kami sa pamilya namin, e." It’s your cultural factory setting.
usage_notes: Often used with "kahirapan" (poverty), "kasaganaan" (prosperity), or a specific culture/tradition.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagiging masipag ay isang katangiang **kinamulatan** niya sa kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"Hard work is a trait he **grew up with** from his parents."},{"sentence":"Iba ang pagpapalaki sa mga batang **kinamulatan** ang teknolohiya.","translation":"Raising children who **were brought up on** technology is different."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos na padalus-dalos, hindi pinag-isipan, o biglaan na maaaring magdulot ng hindi magandang resulta.
etymology: From `pag-` + `bi-` (reduplication) + `bigla` (sudden). The `pag-` + reduplication form turns the adjective/adverb `bigla` into a noun for the action/tendency.
original_explanation: This is the "add to cart" on 12.12 without checking your bank account. It's resigning from your job because of one bad day. It's confessing your feelings via a drunk text at 3 AM. Pagbibigla is your brain's "YOLO" moment that your future self will probably regret. It's the enemy of "pag-isipan mo muna."
usage_notes: Describes the tendency or act of being sudden or impulsive. `Pagkabigla` refers to the state of being shocked, while `pagbibigla` refers to the act of doing something suddenly.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iwasan ang **pagbibigla** sa paggawa ng mahahalagang desisyon.","translation":"Avoid **acting hastily** when making important decisions."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagbibigla** sa pagsagot ang nagpahamak sa kanya.","translation":"His **impulsiveness** in answering is what got him into trouble."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay o paraan na ginagamit sa marahang pagdampi o paghimas; maaari ring tumukoy sa isang kilos na nagpapahiwatig ng pag-aalaga o paglalambing.
original_explanation: This is less about medicine and more about emotion. It's the gentle touch that says "I'm here for you." It could be your mom's hand on your forehead when you're sick, your partner's hand on your back, or even the soft fur of your doggo. It's the physical form of "there, there."
usage_notes: Samantalang ang `panghaplas` ay para sa pisikal na sakit, ang `panghaplos` ay madalas para sa emosyonal na kaginhawahan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang malambing na salita ng ina ay nagsilbing **panghaplos** sa kanyang nalulungkot na puso.","translation":"The mother's sweet words served as a **soothing touch** for her sad heart."},{"sentence":"Walang anumang materyal na bagay ang makakatumbas sa **panghaplos** ng isang tunay na kaibigan.","translation":"No material thing can equal the **comforting gesture** of a true friend."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o bagay na nagbibigay o nagsusuplay ng isang bagay na kailangan, tulad ng serbisyo o pinansyal na suporta.
original_explanation: Kung ikaw ang breadwinner, ikaw ang 'provider.' Kung Globe o Smart ang SIM mo, 'yan ang 'network provider.' Kung Meralco ang nagbibigay ng kuryente, 'yan ang 'service provider.' Basically, sila yung 'taga-bigay' ng needs mo.
usage_notes: An English loanword used commonly in Tagalog, especially in contexts of family (breadwinner), telecommunications (network provider), and business (service provider).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bilang ama, siya ang pangunahing **provider** ng kanilang pamilya.","translation":"As the father, he is the main **provider** for their family."},{"sentence":"Anong network **provider** ang may pinakamalakas na signal sa inyo?","translation":"Which network **provider** has the strongest signal in your area?"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa balbas o buhok na magulo, hindi inalagaan, at marumi tingnan.
original_explanation: Yung itsura mo after ng isang linggong WFH na walang video call. Parang hermit in the making. 'Uy, mag-ahit ka naman, ang yangot na ng balbas mo!' It's the 'I give up on grooming' look.
usage_notes: Primarily used to describe messy facial hair.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa lockdown, naging **yangot** ang kaniyang itsura.","translation":"Because of the lockdown, his appearance became **disheveled**."}]

translation: to imagine; to ponder; to assess
meaning_filipino: Isipin o suriing mabuti ang isang bagay; bigyan ng pansin at pag-aralan sa isip; gunigunihin.
etymology: From the root word "wari" meaning "it seems" or "assessment".
original_explanation: This is a deep-cut, literary word for "to think about something really hard." It's not just 'isipin' (to think), it's more like pondering or trying to figure something out. Like when you're trying to wariin kung saan napunta 'yung 13th-month pay mo two weeks after you got it. It has a sense of deep introspection.
usage_notes: A more formal or literary term. Not commonly used in casual conversation. The verb is often conjugated, e.g., 'winari', 'winawari'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Subukan mong **wariin** ang tunay na kahulugan ng kanyang mga sinabi.","translation":"Try to **ponder** the true meaning of what he said."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **wariin** ang mangyayari sa hinaharap.","translation":"It's difficult to **fathom** what will happen in the future."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga bagay, gawain, o kasuotan na may kaugnayan sa o ginagamit para sa pag-aaral at eskwelahan.
original_explanation: This refers to your 'pang-school' things. Your uniform, your backpack, that one pair of black shoes you're forced to wear every day. It’s the mode you switch into when you need to be serious for class. The opposite of your 'pambahay' (for home) or 'pang-gala' (for going out) stuff. 'Di ako pwede, may project akong pampaaralan.'
usage_notes: Similar in structure and usage to 'pamista' and 'pambahay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si Nanay ng mga gamit na **pampaaralan** para sa darating na pasukan.","translation":"Mom bought supplies **for school** for the upcoming school year."},{"sentence":"Ang uniporme ay isang kasuotang **pampaaralan**.","translation":"A uniform is **school** attire."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sanhi, motibo, o pinagmulan ng isang bagay; katumbas ng salitang "dahilan".
original_explanation: This is the old-school, more poetic version of 'reason'. You won't hear this in everyday chismis. You'll find it in deep OPM songs or classic Filipino literature. 'Ikaw ang dahil ng aking pagluha' (You are the reason for my tears). It's the dramatic, 'hugot' version of 'dahilan'. The pronunciation is key here: da-HIL, not DA-hil.
usage_notes: Pronunciation shifts to /da-HIL/ with stress on the second syllable. Less common in modern spoken language than 'dahilan'. Primarily used in literary or formal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang malalim na **dahil** ng kanyang kalungkutan ay hindi pa rin malinaw.","translation":"The deep **reason** for his sadness is still not clear."},{"sentence":"Ano ang **dahil** at siya'y nagkaganito?","translation":"What is the **cause** for him becoming like this?"}]

translation: to stick to; to get attached to
meaning_filipino: Hindi sinasadyang dumikit o kumapit sa isang bagay o tao.
original_explanation: Like when you're walking through the palengke and suddenly a piece of plastic bag is stuck to your leg. Or when you meet someone new and you just instantly click, napadikit ka na sa kanya. It can be literal (like glue) or figurative (like a new bestie or a clingy ex).
usage_notes: Can be used physically for objects sticking together, or emotionally/socially for people becoming close. The "mapa-" implies it happened somewhat unintentionally or naturally.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang siksikan sa MRT, hindi mo maiiwasang **mapadikit** sa ibang pasahero.","translation":"It's so crowded in the MRT, you can't avoid **sticking to** other passengers."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng namatayan ng asawang lalaki at hindi pa muling nag-aasawa.
original_explanation: A woman whose husband has passed away. In Pinoy teleseryes, she's often portrayed as the strong matriarch who takes over the family business, or the dramatic character in black who delivers a powerful 'hugot' line at a funeral. The male version is 'biyudo'.
usage_notes: Ang katumbas nito para sa lalaki ay 'biyudo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ilang taon nang **biyuda** si Aling Rosa ngunit nanatili siyang matatag para sa kanyang mga anak.","translation":"Aling Rosa has been a **widow** for several years but she remained strong for her children."},{"sentence":"Ang **biyuda** ng yumaong sundalo ay tumanggap ng parangal.","translation":"The **widow** of the deceased soldier received an honor."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o pagawaan kung saan isinasagawa ang pananahi ng mga damit o anumang kasuotan.
etymology: From `pinag-` + `tahi` + `-an`. The `-an` suffix indicates a place where the action of the root word (tahi/sew) is done.
original_explanation: The OG 'pasadya' place. Before Zara and Uniqlo, this was where you got your prom gown or your school uniform made. It's the local atelier, the kingdom of the mananahi, filled with the sound of sewing machines and the smell of new fabric. Also, the place that saves you when you rip your pants.
usage_notes: Can also refer to the discarded fabric scraps from sewing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala ko sa **pinagtahian** ni Aling Nena ang aking uniporme.","translation":"I brought my uniform to Aling Nena's **sewing shop**."},{"sentence":"Maraming retaso sa sahig ng **pinagtahian**.","translation":"There are many fabric scraps on the floor of the **sewing shop**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kulay na dilaw.
original_explanation: The Spanish-derived word for "yellow." It sounds fancier than "dilaw." If you're painting your room, you might say "dilaw." If you're a fashion designer describing a gown, you'd say "amarillo" to sound more *sosyal*.
usage_notes: Ang 'dilaw' ay ang mas karaniwan at katutubong salita sa Tagalog. Ang 'amarilyo' ay ginagamit para sa mas pormal, pampanitikan, o teknikal na dating.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang bestido ay kulay **amarilyo**.","translation":"Her dress is the color **yellow**."},{"sentence":"Gumamit ang pintor ng tonong **amarilyo** para sa bukang-liwayway.","translation":"The painter used a **yellow** tone for the sunrise."}]

translation: will be caught with a net
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghuli sa isda o iba pang bagay gamit ang lambat sa hinaharap. Ito ang hinaharap na anyo ng pandiwang "lambatin".
original_explanation: The future of the fish who didn't see the net coming. Figuratively, it's what happens when you get caught in a group project where you're the only one working – nalambat ka. Or when a recruiter "lalambatin" all the good candidates from a rival company.
usage_notes: Future tense, object-focus verb for 'to net' or 'to catch with a net'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga isdang iyon ay **lalambatin** ng mga mangingisda mamayang gabi.","translation":"Those fish **will be caught with a net** by the fishermen tonight."},{"sentence":"Sa basketball, **lalambatin** ng player ang bola.","translation":"In basketball, the player **will net** the ball."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o pamilya na naninirahan sa katabing bahay, gusali, o lote.
etymology: From 'kapit' (to hold on, to be next to) + 'bahay' (house).
original_explanation: Your source of the latest chismis, the one you borrow a cup of sugar or an egg from, and the reason you can't sing karaoke at 2 AM on a Tuesday. They can be your best friend or your worst enemy, sometimes on the same day.
usage_notes: A very common word in daily life.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakibigay itong ulam sa ating **kapitbahay**.","translation":"Please give this dish to our **neighbor**."},{"sentence":"Maingay na naman ang aso ng **kapitbahay** namin.","translation":"Our **neighbor's** dog is noisy again."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang babaeng katumbas ng "fuccboi." Isang babae na mapaglaro sa damdamin ng iba, hindi seryoso sa relasyon, at ginagamit ang mga lalaki para sa sariling kapakinabangan nang walang emosyonal na pananagutan.
etymology: Derived from the term "fuccboi" to create a female equivalent.
original_explanation: The female counterpart to the fuccboi. She'll make you feel like you're the only one, then ghost you after you've bought her milk tea three times. She has a rotation of guys on her phone and her motto is "Thank U, Next" before Ariana Grande even made it a song. Equal opportunity heartbreaker.
usage_notes: Less common than "fuccboi" but gaining traction as a term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Akala mo biktima siya, pero siya pala ang tunay na **fuckgirl**.","translation":"You thought she was the victim, but she was the real **fuckgirl** all along."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng kanin na bahagyang nasunog at dumikit sa ilalim ng kaldero.
original_explanation: The best part (or worst, depending on who you ask) of the rice. It's the crispy, sometimes-a-bit-too-burnt layer at the bottom of the pot that siblings fight over. You can eat it with sugar, salt, or just pour coffee over it. It’s the original rice crispy.
usage_notes: A common term in Filipino households, often considered a delicacy or a simple snack.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito ni lolo na papakin ang **tutong** pagkatapos mananghalian.","translation":"Grandpa's favorite thing to snack on is the **scorched rice** after lunch."},{"sentence":"Inalis niya ang **tutong** sa kaldero para makapagsaing ulit.","translation":"She removed the **scorched rice** from the pot to cook rice again."}]

translation: an insinuation, a sarcastic remark, a pointed comment
meaning_filipino: Isang matalinhaga o mapanuyang pahayag na may pinatatamaan o pinupuntiryang tao, ngunit hindi direktang binabanggit ang pangalan.
etymology: A modern variant of the archaic `pasari`.
original_explanation: The official language of Filipino social media drama. It’s a "subtweet" in real life. When your friend posts "Sana lahat loyal" on Facebook after seeing their ex's new post, that's a pasaring. It's a guided missile of shade, expertly launched to hit a specific target without naming them. The art of "patama."
usage_notes: A very common word in modern Filipino, especially in the context of social interactions, conflicts, and social media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **pasaring** ang kanyang social media post tungkol sa mga pekeng kaibigan.","translation":"Her social media post was full of **pointed comments** about fake friends."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko na lang pinansin ang **pasaring** niya tungkol sa mga tamad na empleyado.","translation":"I just ignored his **sarcastic remark** about lazy employees."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kalagayan ng pagiging gulat o tulala kung saan malaki ang pagkaka-bukas ng mga mata.
original_explanation: Yung itsura mo kapag nakita mo 'yung ex mo na may kasamang iba, tapos dumaan sa harap mo. Or when you check your bank account after a Shopee 11.11 sale. Your eyes are wide open, but your brain has left the chat. Ganern.
usage_notes: Often implies shock, surprise, or being caught off-guard.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakamulaga** si Maria nang biglang sumulpot ang multo sa lumang litrato.","translation":"Maria was **staring wide-eyed** when a ghost suddenly appeared in the old photograph."},{"sentence":"Naiwan siyang **nakamulaga** sa ganda ng tanawin mula sa tuktok ng bundok.","translation":"He was left **dumbfounded** by the beauty of the view from the mountaintop."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkuha ng pera mula sa iba sa pamamagitan ng panlilinlang, pamimilit, o iba pang hindi tapat na paraan.
etymology: From Spanish 'cuarta', a unit of currency, which became 'kwarta' or 'kuwarta' for money in general.
original_explanation: 'Yung modus ng mga "dugo-dugo" gang, or 'yung "friend" mo na biglang nag-message para sa isang "amazing investment opportunity" na pyramiding scheme pala. To manguwarta is to hustle people for their cash, often illegally. It's the dark side of "diskarte."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binalaan ng pulisya ang publiko laban sa mga sindikatong **nangungu-warta** gamit ang text messages.","translation":"The police warned the public against syndicates that **swindle money** using text messages."},{"sentence":"Ang layunin lang niya ay **manguwarta** sa mga mayayamang dayuhan.","translation":"His only goal is to **extort** money from rich foreigners."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbibigay ng kapatawaran sa isang taong nagkasala; paglimot sa kasalanan o pagkukulang ng iba.
original_explanation: This is the emotional counterpart to haggling. Instead of asking for a lower price, you're asking for or giving a lower sentence for an emotional debt. It's the act of letting go of a grudge, saying 'I forgive you' (or hoping to hear it). It's much harder than getting a discount in Divisoria and the price is your pride.
usage_notes: This usage is less common than 'pagpapatawad' or 'kapatawaran' for 'forgiveness'. It is often understood through context, especially when paired with words like 'kasalanan' (sin) or 'pagkakamali' (mistake). The phrase 'paghingi ng tawad' (the act of asking for forgiveness) is very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tunay na **pagtawad** ay nagmumula sa puso.","translation":"True **forgiveness** comes from the heart."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **pagtawad** upang maghilom ang mga sugat ng nakaraan.","translation":"The act of **forgiving** is important for the wounds of the past to heal."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging mabilis kumilos, mag-isip, o makalito sa iba; katusuhan.
original_explanation: Ito yung skill mo kapag kailangan mong mag-explain sa nanay mo kung bakit late ka na naman umuwi. Yung mabilis kang makahanap ng palusot. O kaya yung pagiging alerto mo sa pag-iwas sa mga chismosa sa kanto. Agility level: expert.
usage_notes: Can have a slightly negative connotation, implying slyness or cunning, not just speed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinamalas niya ang kanyang **kalistuhan** nang maiwasan niya ang lahat ng tanong tungkol sa kanyang lovelife.","translation":"She showed her **slyness** when she avoided all questions about her lovelife."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng **kalistuhan** sa pagtawid sa EDSA tuwing rush hour.","translation":"You need **agility** to cross EDSA during rush hour."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa estado ng pagkalito, pagka-tuliro, o kawalan ng tamang ulirat, sanhi ng paggamit ng ipinagbabawal na gamot, kakulangan sa tulog, o matinding pagod.
original_explanation: The feeling you get after a 12-hour BPO shift, pulling an all-nighter for an exam, or just waking up on a Monday. Your brain is buffering, your eyes are half-closed, and you're not quite sure what planet you're on. It's the official state of being for the 'puyat' nation. Also known as 'sabaw'.
usage_notes: While it can mean "high on drugs," it's more commonly used in a colloquial, non-drug-related sense to mean extremely tired, groggy, or dazed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo muna akong kausapin, **bangag** pa ako sa puyat.","translation":"Don't talk to me yet, I'm still **groggy** from lack of sleep."},{"sentence":"Mukha siyang **bangag** pagkatapos ng mahabang biyahe.","translation":"He looked **dazed** after the long trip."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na kulisap na parasitiko na naninirahan sa anit ng tao at sumisipsip ng dugo.
original_explanation: The OG school problem bago pa nauso ang bullying. Ito yung dahilan kung bakit may suyod ang nanay mo at bakit bawal manghiram ng suklay. Getting 'kuto' is a childhood rite of passage that nobody wants. The ultimate uninvited guest sa buhok mo.
usage_notes: The eggs are called 'lisa'. The tool to remove them is 'suyod'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong gumamit ng espesyal na shampoo para mawala ang iyong mga **kuto**.","translation":"You need to use a special shampoo to get rid of your **head lice**."},{"sentence":"Nagkamot siya nang nagkamot dahil sa makating **kuto**.","translation":"He kept scratching because of the itchy **head louse**."}]

translation: to stay up late for something
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalaan ng gabi o pag-aalay ng oras ng tulog para sa isang partikular na gawain, bagay, o tao.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'pagpupuyat'. This is what you do when you decide that a certain task (finishing a report), a certain person (waiting for their chat reply), or a certain show (the season finale) is worth sacrificing your precious sleep for. "Bes, worth it ba **pagpuyatan** 'yan?"
usage_notes: This is a verb, often used in the imperative form ("Huwag mong pagpuyatan 'yan!") or to describe a past or future action ("Pinagpuyatan ko ang thesis ko.").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang **pagpuyatan** ang paghihintay sa text niya.","translation":"Don't **stay up late for** waiting for his text anymore."},{"sentence":"Talagang pinagpuyatan namin ang proyektong ito para matapos sa tamang oras.","translation":"We really **stayed up late for** this project to finish it on time."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng panloloko o panlilinlang upang makakuha ng pera o benepisyo mula sa isang tao sa hindi tapat na paraan.
original_explanation: 'Yung friend mo na nangutang para sa 'emergency' pero a week later may post sa IG na nasa beach. That's a con. It's the art of the 'budol-budol' but sometimes with more finesse. Also, 'con artist' is the practitioner of this dark art.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng mga scam o panloloko. Ang taong gumagawa nito ay tinatawag na 'con artist'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa mga online **con** kung saan hinihingi ang iyong personal na impormasyon.","translation":"Be careful of online **cons** where they ask for your personal information."},{"sentence":"Ang buong investment scheme ay isa palang malaking **con**.","translation":"The whole investment scheme turned out to be a big **con**."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagsabihan o bigyan ng impormasyon, paalala, o utos ang isang tao.
original_explanation: The act of giving someone a piece of your mind, a friendly reminder, or the latest chismis. 'Bes, sabihan mo ako kung on the way ka na.' It's more about directing the information *to a person*. It can be a gentle 'FYI' or a stern 'I'm telling you for the last time!'
usage_notes: Focuses on the person being told. 'Sabihan mo si Juan' (Tell Juan). Contrasts with 'sabihin', which focuses on the message itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sabihan** mo na lang ako kung may pagbabago sa plano.","translation":"Just **tell me** if there are any changes to the plan."},{"sentence":"Pinagsa**sabihan** ako ng nanay ko dahil gabi na akong umuwi.","translation":"My mom was **scolding** (repeatedly telling) me because I came home late."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapakawala mula sa pagkakahawak; tumutukoy din sa isang laban ng mga manok na pansabong.
original_explanation: Can mean two things: 1) The moment you finally let go of that toxic ex, 'Nag-bitaw na ako sa pag-asa.' 2) The main event in a sabong (cockfight) where the two roosters are released to fight. It's the 'Let's get ready to rumble!' moment for feathered warriors.
usage_notes: The cockfighting sense is very common in rural areas and among enthusiasts. The 'letting go' sense is more general and often used as the root for 'bitawan' or 'bitiwan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula na ang **bitaw** ng mga manok sa sabungan.","translation":"The **cockfight** has started at the cockpit."},{"sentence":"Sa isang iglap, naramdaman niya ang **bitaw** ng kamay nito.","translation":"In an instant, she felt the **release** of his hand."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa sinaunang Gresya, isang lungsod-estado, na binubuo ng isang lungsod at ng teritoryong nakapalibot dito.
etymology: Mula sa Sinaunang Griyego na πόλις (pólis, 'lungsod-estado').
original_explanation: Think of this as the OG barangay but on a much grander scale, like in ancient Greece. It's not just a city, it's a whole political unit with its own government and army. Athens and Sparta were famous frenemy polises. It's the root word for 'politics', 'politician', etc.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa mga talakayang pangkasaysayan at pang-akademiko tungkol sa sinaunang Gresya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Athens ay isang tanyag na **polis** sa sinaunang Gresya na kilala sa demokrasya.","translation":"Athens was a famous **polis** in ancient Greece known for democracy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglalagay ng mga braso sa paligid ng isang tao o bagay bilang pagpapahayag ng pagmamahal, pag-aliw, o pagtanggap.
original_explanation: A hug. The universal cure for a bad day, a failed exam, or a heartbreak. It's what you want from your mom after a tough day at work, or what you give a friend who's going through something. A `pagyakap` can be a tight, "I missed you" hug from a balikbayan relative, or a gentle, comforting one. It's a non-verbal "I'm here for you."
usage_notes: A very common and emotionally charged word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Walang hihigit pa sa mahigpit na **pagyakap** ng isang ina.","translation":"Nothing beats the tight **embrace** of a mother."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagyakap** ay nagbigay sa akin ng kapanatagan.","translation":"His **hug** gave me a sense of peace."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng malakas na tunog mula sa ilong, tulad ng ginagawa ng isang hayop na galit, o ang tunog ng singaw na lumalabas mula sa isang maliit na butas.
original_explanation: Think of a carabao that's not having a good day, or that sound your rice cooker makes when it's about to be done. It's an aggressive exhale, either from an angry animal or from pent-up steam pressure. It's the "I'm about to blow" sound.
