usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magtisa** ng manok para sa afritada para maging mas maganda ang kulay.","translation":"You need to **color the chicken with annatto** for the afritada to have a better color."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magtisa** sa pader, sa pisara ka magsulat.","translation":"Don't **mark with chalk** on the wall, write on the blackboard."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na kasunduan upang makipagkita o bumisita sa isang tao sa partikular na oras at lugar.
original_explanation: The official term for 'may lakad'. It can be for a visa interview, a dental check-up, or a client meeting. In the Philippines, having an appointment at 10 AM often means you'll actually start at 10:30 AM. Welcome to Filipino time. Also, the thing you set on Calendly so you don't have to do 10 email back-and-forths just to schedule a 'quick call'.
usage_notes: Malawakang ginagamit sa Taglish, lalo na sa mga propesyonal at pormal na konteksto. Ang mga katumbas sa Filipino ay "tipanan" o "takdang pakikipagkita".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **appointment** ako sa doktor mamayang alas tres.","translation":"I have an **appointment** with the doctor later at three o'clock."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, nakapag-set na ako ng **appointment** sa NBI.","translation":"Don't worry, I already set an **appointment** at the NBI."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang pagputol ng lahat ng komunikasyon sa isang tao (karaniwan sa isang romantikong kasama) nang walang anumang paliwanag.
etymology: From the English verb 'to ghost', which gained popularity in the 2010s to describe a phenomenon in online dating.
original_explanation: In the Philippines, to "ghost" someone is the national sport of modern dating. It's when the person you've been talking to 24/7 suddenly disappears like a bubble, leaving you on 'seen'. Walang paalam, walang "babye," parang multo na lang na naglaho sa ere.
usage_notes: Used as a verb in Taglish. The base word 'ghost' is used, but it implies the action. Often inflected with Tagalog affixes like 'i-ghost' (to ghost someone) or 'na-ghost' (was ghosted).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong i-**ghost** ha, mag-reply ka.","translation":"Don't **ghost** me, okay? Reply."},{"sentence":"Balak niya atang i-**ghost** 'yung ka-date niya kagabi.","translation":"I think he plans to **ghost** his date from last night."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkakaroon ng maraming uri o pagkakaiba sa loob ng isang grupo; baryasyon.
original_explanation: This is `pagkakaiba` on steroids. It's not just one difference, it's a whole buffet of them. Think of the food court in a mall—that's `pagkakaiba-iba` of cuisines. Or the mix of personalities in your friend group. It's the "unity in diversity" concept. It celebrates variety, like having different flavors of milk tea to choose from.
usage_notes: Emphasizes multiple, varied differences, often implying a collection or group with diverse elements.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkakaiba-iba** ng kultura sa Pilipinas ay isang yaman ng bansa.","translation":"The **diversity** of cultures in the Philippines is a treasure of the nation."},{"sentence":"Ipinakita ng pag-aaral ang **pagkakaiba-iba** ng opinyon ng mga tao tungkol sa isyu.","translation":"The study showed the **variety** of people's opinions on the issue."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking mamamayan ng Espanya, o ang wikang opisyal ng Espanya.
original_explanation: The OG colonizers. Sila yung dahilan kung bakit may siesta tayo, kung bakit apelyido mo ay Cruz o Santos, at kung bakit masarap ang lechon. Can also refer to the language itself, na parang Tagalog na may lisp at mas maraming 'r' na pinapa-roll.
usage_notes: Ginagamit bilang pangngalan (tao) o pang-uri (bagay na mula sa Espanya). Ang "Kastila" ay isang mas tradisyonal na katumbas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marunong siyang magsalita ng **Ispanyol** dahil nag-aral siya sa Madrid.","translation":"He knows how to speak **Spanish** because he studied in Madrid."},{"sentence":"Ang lolo niya ay isang **Ispanyol** na nanirahan sa Pilipinas.","translation":"His grandfather was a **Spaniard** who lived in the Philippines."}]

translation: to cause fatigue; to be tiring
meaning_filipino: Ang magdulot o maging sanhi ng pagod o panlalambot ng katawan.
original_explanation: That feeling after a whole day of adulting—paying bills, sitting in traffic, dealing with your boss's "urgent" requests. 'Yung energy level mo, pang-power nap na lang. It's the official state after a long commute on EDSA or a marathon online shopping checkout.
usage_notes: Often used to describe an activity or a condition that is physically or mentally draining.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Talagang **makahapo** ang pag-akyat sa bundok na iyon.","translation":"Climbing that mountain is really **tiring**."},{"sentence":"Naging **makahapo** ang maghapong pagtatrabaho sa bukid.","translation":"A whole day's work in the field **was tiring**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o negosyo na nakatuon sa pag-aalaga ng mga hayop para sa produksyon ng pagkain o iba pang produkto.
original_explanation: This is where your future fried chicken, lechon, and bulalo come from. A **maghayupan** is a farm dedicated to raising animals. It's a business, but also a lifestyle. Think of a hacienda with lots of cows, or a backyard piggery. Basically, an animal-centric enterprise.
usage_notes: This term is more specific than 'bukid' (farm), as it specifically refers to livestock farming.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May malawak na **maghayupan** ng baka ang kanilang pamilya sa Batangas.","translation":"Their family owns a wide cattle **ranch** in Batangas."},{"sentence":"Ang pagpapatakbo ng **maghayupan** ay nangangailangan ng sipag at tiyaga.","translation":"Running a **livestock farm** requires diligence and perseverance."}]

translation: to be able to do something; to manage; to handle
meaning_filipino: Ang pandiwa na nangangahulugang subukang gawin o isakatuparan ang isang bagay na maaaring mahirap; ang paggamit ng kakayahan upang harapin ang isang gawain.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of "Kaya 'to!". It's what you tell yourself when facing a seemingly impossible task, like assembling IKEA furniture or understanding your phone bill. "Kakayanin ko 'to." (I will be able to do this). It's the mantra of every Filipino trying to make ends meet or survive EDSA traffic.
usage_notes: A verb focused on the effort to be able to do something. Different verb conjugations: kinaya (past), kinakaya (present), kakayanin (future).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit mahirap ang exam, pilit niyang **kinaya** na sagutan lahat.","translation":"Even though the exam was hard, he forced himself **to manage** to answer everything."},{"sentence":"Sa tingin mo ba ay **kakayanin** natin ang lahat ng gastusin ngayong Pasko?","translation":"Do you think we will **be able to handle** all the expenses this Christmas?"}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng malalim na pananampalataya at paggalang sa Diyos.
original_explanation: Describes a person who's genuinely religious and lives by it. Your lola who goes to church every single day, your officemate who prays before eating their baon, or a politician who actually lives up to the "maka-Diyos, makabayan, makatao" motto. It's about walking the talk of faith.
usage_notes: The "D" in Diyos is often capitalized. It's one of the core values in the Philippine national motto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa kanilang komunidad bilang isang taong **maka-Diyos**.","translation":"He is known in their community as a **God-fearing** person."},{"sentence":"Ang pagiging **maka-Diyos** ay isa sa mga itinuturo sa mga paaralan.","translation":"Being **godly** is one of the values taught in schools."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maputi at esponghadong bahagi sa pagitan ng balat at ng mismong laman ng mga prutas na sitrus tulad ng dalandan, kahel, o suha.
original_explanation: It's that bitter white stuff on an orange or pomelo that you try to peel off but never fully can. It’s the clingy, bitter ex of the fruit world—it just won't let go of the good part. Some people eat it, most people avoid it.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to the spongy white layer in citrus fruits.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinanggal niya ang lahat ng **kalibkib** bago kainin ang suha.","translation":"He removed all the **pith** before eating the pomelo."},{"sentence":"Mapait ang lasa ng **kalibkib** ng dalandan.","translation":"The **pith** of an orange tastes bitter."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang alinlangan; sigurado; tiyak.
original_explanation: This is that feeling when you're 101% sure na s'ya na talaga ang the one, only to find out you were wrong all along. Or when you're 'piho' that you'll get your 13th-month pay on time, tapos na-delay. It's the confidence before the plot twist.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'sigurado' and 'tiyak'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Piho** akong darating siya mamaya.","translation":"I am **certain** he will arrive later."},{"sentence":"Hindi ako **piho** kung tama ang desisyon ko.","translation":"I am not **sure** if my decision is correct."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang doktrina o paniniwalang pilosopikal na nagtuturing sa sansinukob bilang manipestasyon ng Diyos, at ang Diyos ay ang kabuuan ng lahat ng bagay at hindi isang hiwalay na persona.
original_explanation: The belief that God isn't just some guy in the clouds, but is *in* everything—the trees, the mountains, the sea, and yes, even in the traffic along EDSA. It's finding the divine in your sisig. It's the 'the universe is my church' vibe.
usage_notes: A philosophical and theological term, not used in everyday conversation but important in academic or religious discussions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **panteismo** ay isang pananaw na iba sa mga tradisyonal na relihiyon.","translation":"**Pantheism** is a worldview that is different from traditional religions."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aralan nila ang konsepto ng **panteismo** sa kanilang klase sa pilosopiya.","translation":"They studied the concept of **pantheism** in their philosophy class."}]

translation: to code-switch; to speak in a mixed language
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapahayag gamit ang pinaghalong mga salita mula sa dalawa o higit pang wika sa loob ng isang pangungusap.
original_explanation: This is the official sport of every Filipino abroad, BPO agent, and coño kid. It's when your brain can't decide between English and Tagalog, so it just says 'Why not both?' The result is 'Make tusok-tusok the fishball' or 'I'm so pagod na, I need to make tulog.' It's the linguistic equivalent of a halo-halo dessert—a sweet, chaotic, but ultimately understandable mix.
usage_notes: Often used to describe Taglish (Tagalog-English) or any form of code-switching. It is a very common phenomenon in modern Philippine society.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magsalita nang halu-halo** para maintindihan ka ng lola mo.","translation":"Don't **speak in a mixed language** so your grandmother can understand you."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang sala o kasalanan; walang malisya o masamang hangarin; hindi pa mulat sa mga bagay na pang-matanda.
original_explanation: That friend who doesn't get your green jokes. Or a person wrongly accused of a crime. It means pure, naive, or legally not guilty. It's the "wala akong alam diyan" vibe, whether it's genuine or just an act. "Pa-inosente effect."
usage_notes: Can describe legal status (not guilty), a naive personality, or a lack of malice.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napatunayang **inosente** ang akusado sa lahat ng paratang.","translation":"The accused was proven **innocent** of all charges."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magkunwaring **inosente**, alam kong naintindihan mo ang biro ko.","translation":"Don't pretend to be **innocent**, I know you understood my joke."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matalas at masidhing pagpuna, pag-atake, o pagbatikos sa isang tao, ideya, o gawa, na karaniwang ipinapahayag sa paraang pasalita o pasulat.
original_explanation: Ito yung 'bardagulan' in essay form. Yung rants sa social media na may all caps, maraming exclamation points, at resibo. Kapag ang isang politiko ay nag-privilege speech para bumatikos ng kalaban, 'yan ay isang tuligsa.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa isang malakas, at kadalasan ay pampublikong, pasulat o pasalitang pag-atake.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglabas ng **tuligsa** ang grupo laban sa bagong batas.","translation":"The group released a **diatribe** against the new law."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang talumpati ay isang matapang na **tuligsa** sa katiwalian sa gobyerno.","translation":"His speech was a brave **tirade** against corruption in the government."}]

translation: to be able to wound; to cause injury
meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang magdulot ng pinsala o sugat sa katawan ng isang tao o hayop, o sa damdamin.
original_explanation: What your words can do when you're in a fight with someone you love. It can be a literal 'ouch' from a sharp object, or a figurative 'ouch' from a 'sana all' comment when you're single. It's the kind of hurt that needs more than just a band-aid.
usage_notes: Can be used for both physical and emotional wounds.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa bubog, baka ka **makasugat**.","translation":"Be careful with the broken glass, you might get **wounded**."},{"sentence":"Ang masasakit na salita ay maaaring **makasugat** ng damdamin.","translation":"Harsh words can **wound** feelings."}]

meaning_filipino: Nauukol sa o umiiral sa kasalukuyang panahon.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `pang-` at salitang `kasalukuyan` (the present).
original_explanation: This is the stuff that's happening *right now*. It's your current relationship status, the latest trending topic on X (formerly Twitter), the 'now playing' in your life's movie. It's not about the past (throwback) or the future (sana all), it's about the 'now na'.
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang ilarawan ang mga bagay na may kaugnayan o kahalagahan sa kasalukuyang panahon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **pangkasalukuyan** na isyu sa bansa ay dapat nating pagtuunan ng pansin.","translation":"We should focus our attention on the **current** issues in the country."},{"sentence":"Ito ang **pangkasalukuyan** na disenyo ng kanilang logo.","translation":"This is the **present-day** design of their logo."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay ng embargo o pagpigil sa mga kalakal o ari-arian sa pamamagitan ng legal na kapangyarihan.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'embargar' at hulaping Tagalog na '-hin'.
original_explanation: The action version of 'embargado.' It's what the authorities *do* to your stuff. 'I-e-embargo namin 'yan!' is the threat you hear when you've been a very naughty debtor.
usage_notes: Ang anyong pandiwa, na nagsasaad ng kilos ng pagsamsam ng ari-arian.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagbanta ang korte na **embarguhin** ang kanyang bahay kung hindi siya magbabayad.","translation":"The court threatened to **seize** his house if he did not pay."}]

meaning_filipino: Puno ng balakubak; pagkakaroon ng kapansin-pansing dami ng balakubak sa buhok o anit.
original_explanation: When it's snowing on your shoulders, but it's 30 degrees Celsius outside. This is the reason you have a complicated relationship with black shirts. It's the state of being that anti-dandruff shampoos promise to save you from.
usage_notes: A very specific and descriptive word. The '-in' suffix denotes being afflicted with or having a lot of the root word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahihiya siyang magsuot ng itim na damit dahil siya ay **balakubakin**.","translation":"He is shy to wear black clothes because he **has a lot of dandruff**."},{"sentence":"Gumamit ka ng espesyal na shampoo para sa iyong **balakubakin** na anit.","translation":"Use a special shampoo for your **dandruff-ridden** scalp."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagmumula sa kalooban; totoo, tapat, at walang pagkukunwari.
original_explanation: When your 'sorry' isn't just a 'sorry' to end the fight, but a 'sorry' that comes with tears, snot, and a promise to change. It's the 'thank you' you give to someone who paid for your Grab when you left your wallet. It's 100% genuine, no preservatives, straight from the heart. The opposite of plastic.
usage_notes: Commonly used in formal letters ('Taos-pusong nagpapasalamat,'), expressions of gratitude, apologies, and love.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Taos-puso** ang aking pasasalamat sa lahat ng tumulong sa akin.","translation":"My gratitude is **heartfelt** to everyone who helped me."},{"sentence":"Humihingi ako ng **taos-puso**ng paumanhin.","translation":"I offer a **sincere** apology."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasunduan o prinsipyo ng pagkakaisa sa isang grupo na tinitiyak na walang sinuman ang maiiwan, mapapabayaan, o kakalimutan.
etymology: Mula sa "walang" (no/none) at "iwanan" (the act of leaving someone/something).
original_explanation: The ultimate 'barkada' motto. It's the promise you make before a night out, a group project, or climbing a mountain. It means 'we're all in this together,' whether it's passing an exam or making sure everyone gets home safe after too much Red Horse. The foundation of true friendship and teamwork.
usage_notes: Often used as a rallying cry, a motto, or a promise among a group. It embodies loyalty and solidarity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang usapan ng magkakaibigan, **walang-iwanan** hanggang sa huli.","translation":"The friends' pact was **no one gets left behind** until the very end."},{"sentence":"Sa aming team, ang patakaran ay **walang-iwanan**.","translation":"In our team, the rule is **leave no one behind**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging bangkarote; ang pagkaubos ng yaman o kawalan ng kakayahang magbayad ng obligasyon sa pananalapi.
etymology: From 'pagka-' (state of being) + 'bangkarote' (bankrupt), a variant of Spanish 'bancarrota'.
original_explanation: Same as pagkabangkarota, but this is the more common, 'everyday' spelling you'd hear in the chismis. 'Nako, Mars, malapit na sa pagkabangkarote 'yan, panay pa ang travel!' It's the state of your finances after paying for your friend's Grab because they 'forgot' their wallet again.
usage_notes: A common variant of 'pagkabangkarota'. Both are widely understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa sugal, humantong siya sa **pagkabangkarote**.","translation":"Because of gambling, he ended up in **bankruptcy**."},{"sentence":"Paano maiiwasan ang **pagkabangkarote** ng isang maliit na negosyo?","translation":"How can a small business avoid **bankruptcy**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paghubog o paglikha ng isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng molde o hulmahan.
etymology: Mula sa `pag-` + `magmolde` (humubog), na hiram sa Espanyol na `molde` (hulmahan).
original_explanation: Parang paggawa ng yelo sa ice tray o leche flan sa llanera. You pour something liquid or soft into a container (the molde) and it takes that shape. Figuratively, ito rin yung ginagawa ng parents mo sa'yo, trying to shape you into the person they want you to be.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa literal na konteksto (paggawa ng palayok, pagmamanupaktura) at sa matalinghagang konteksto (paghubog ng karakter o isipan).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagmomolde** ng luwad ay isang sining na nangangailangan ng pasensya.","translation":"The **molding** of clay is an art that requires patience."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang papel ng mga guro sa **pagmomolde** ng kaisipan ng mga kabataan.","translation":"Teachers play a big role in the **shaping** of the youth's minds."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagkain na may matapang na lasa na nagdudulot ng init o hapdi sa bibig, karaniwang mula sa sili.
original_explanation: "Anghang" is that feeling when you eat Bicol Express and suddenly need a fire extinguisher for your mouth. It's the kick that separates the brave from the "extra rice, no sili" crowd. It's also a 'hugot' term: "Yung anghang ng sinabi mo, parang sili... nakakaiyak."
usage_notes: Often used as a noun to refer to the quality of being spicy. The adjective form is 'maanghang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko kinaya ang **anghang** ng pagkain kaya napainom ako agad ng tubig.","translation":"I couldn't handle the **spiciness** of the food so I immediately drank water."},{"sentence":"Gusto ko 'yung may tamang **anghang** lang, hindi 'yung nangingibabaw.","translation":"I like it with just the right amount of **spiciness**, not the overpowering kind."}]

translation: to close something for someone; to close on someone
meaning_filipino: Isara ang isang bagay (tulad ng pinto) para sa kapakanan ng isang tao, o biglaang isara ang isang daanan habang may dumaraan.
original_explanation: This has two fun meanings. 1) The nice one: When you see your crush coming, you hold the elevator door, then you close it for them after they get in. Smooth. 2) The 'savage' one: When your annoying officemate is running for the elevator, and you "accidentally" press the close button. You just got them closed on. Oops.
usage_notes: The context determines if it's a kind or unkind act. Differentiated from `pasarahan` (/pa-sa-ra-HAN/) by the placement of the stress, which changes the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigla na lang siyang **pinasarhan** ng pinto ng taxi.","translation":"The taxi door was suddenly **closed on** him."},{"sentence":"Puwede mo ba akong **pasarhan** ng gate pag-alis ko?","translation":"Can you **close** the gate **for me** when I leave?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbuo ng isang balangkas o sistema ng mga hakbang upang makamit ang isang layunin.
original_explanation: The official verb of your barkada's travel goals that never push through. "Guys, iplano na natin yung beach trip!" is the opening line to a story that ends with everyone staying home.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **iplano** nang mabuti ang ating badyet para sa susunod na buwan.","translation":"We need to **plan** our budget carefully for next month."},{"sentence":"**Iplano** mo na ang isasagot mo sa boss mo kapag tinanong ka tungkol sa proyekto.","translation":"Plan what you're going to say to your boss when he asks you about the project."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pilit na pagngiti o pag-asim ng mukha na nagpapahiwatig ng sakit, pagkadismaya, o pag-iwas.
original_explanation: That face you make when you taste something super sour, like unripe manga. Or your smile when your Tita asks, 'May boyfriend/girlfriend ka na?' at a family reunion. It's a smile that's halfway between a cringe and an actual smile.
usage_notes: A facial expression, distinct from 'ngiti' (smile) or 'ngisi' (smirk).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **ngiwi** ang naisagot niya nang matanong tungkol sa kanyang ex.","translation":"A **grimace** was her response when asked about her ex."}]

translation: a game of timing; an instance requiring perfect timing
meaning_filipino: Isang sitwasyon, laro, o gawain na nakasalalay nang malaki sa tamang tiyempo o pagkakataon.
original_explanation: Crossing a Manila street during rush hour is a masterclass in 'patiyempuhan'. So is trying to get the last piece of lechon kawali at a party. It's all about timing. One second too early or too late and you miss your chance. It’s the art of the perfect timing, like confessing your feelings on Valentine's Day or logging into the Piso Fare website the moment the sale starts.
usage_notes: The suffix '-han' turns 'tiyempo' (timing) into a context or event centered around timing. A more common spelling is 'tyempuhan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paghabol sa paalis na bus ay isang tunay na **patiyempuhan**.","translation":"Chasing after a departing bus is a real **game of timing**."}]

meaning_filipino: Panghalip na pananong na tumutukoy sa pag-aari o sa taong pinatutungkulan ng isang kilos o bagay.
original_explanation: The ultimate "marites" question. When you see your friend with a new phone, you don't ask "what," you ask "Kanino galing 'yan?" (Who gave you that?). It's the interrogative form of 'sa' + 'sino', basically asking "to whom" or "for whom" the chismis is about.
usage_notes: Used in questions to ask about ownership or the recipient of an action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kanino** po itong naiwang payong?","translation":"**Whose** umbrella is this that was left behind?"},{"sentence":"**Kanino** mo ibibigay ang huling piraso ng cake?","translation":"**To whom** will you give the last piece of cake?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggana o pag-andar ng isang makina, sasakyan, o anumang mekanismo. Ito ay nasa pangkasalukuyang anyo.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na 'andar' (to walk, to function).
original_explanation: This is what your car, the office aircon, or your brain (hopefully) on a Monday morning is doing. It means 'it's working!' or 'it's running!' When the internet is slow, you complain, 'Hindi umaandar nang maayos ang WiFi!' It's the state of being operational.
usage_notes: Anyong pangkasalukuyan ng pandiwang 'umandar'. Ginagamit para sa mga makina, sasakyan, at minsan para sa mga plano.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **umaandar** na ulit ang lumang kotse.","translation":"Finally, the old car is **running** again."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghahatid, paglilingkod, o pagbibigay ng isang bagay, partikular sa konteksto ng pag-arte o pagganap nang may kumpiyansa at kahusayan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Ingles na "serve," pinasikat sa ballroom culture at drag.
original_explanation: When you're not just doing something, you're *slaying* it. It's giving your best look, your best walk, your best performance. Parang sa volleyball, pero ang isine-serb mo ay looks, talent, o pure unadulterated confidence. 'Anong ulam? We serb looks today.'
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa impormal na usapan, lalo na sa mga kabataan at sa LGBTQ+ community.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Grabe, nag-**serb** talaga siya ng high fashion realness sa party kagabi!","translation":"Wow, she really **served** high fashion realness at the party last night!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isinasagawa sa paraang lihim, tago, o hindi ipinaaalam sa iba.
original_explanation: This is how you eat the last piece of cake at midnight, hoping no one notices. It's the 'PM is the key' of actions. When you're sliding into someone's DMs, you're doing it 'pasekreto'—on the down-low.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pasekreto** siyang kumuha ng pagkain mula sa ref.","translation":"He **secretly** got food from the fridge."},{"sentence":"May ibinulong siya sa akin nang **pasekreto**.","translation":"He whispered something to me **secretly**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng magkatulad na anyo, hitsura, o katangian.
original_explanation: When you see two people and you think, "Kambal ba 'yan?" They're magkawangis. It's the polite way of saying they look so alike, they could be doppelgängers. This applies to people, things, or even situations that look eerily similar. It's like seeing your ex's new partner and realizing... they look just like you. Awkward.
usage_notes: A more formal or poetic term than 'magkamukha'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang magkapatid ay **magkawangis**; mahirap silang pag-ibahin.","translation":"The siblings are **identical**; it's hard to tell them apart."},{"sentence":"Ang tadhana nila ay **magkawangis** sa isang lumang nobela.","translation":"Their fates are **similar** to an old novel."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na may likas na kakayahang humila o umakit ng mga partikular na metal, tulad ng bakal, dahil sa katangian nitong magnetismo; kilala rin bilang bato-balani.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "pan-" at salitang ugat na "balani" (magnetism, charm). Ang /n/ sa "pan-" ay nagiging /m/ dahil sa kasunod na tunog na /b/.
original_explanation: The OG 'attraction'. Before 'rizz', there was 'balani'. A 'pambalani' is a literal magnet you used in science class. Metaphorically, it’s that mysterious charm or 'lakas ng dating' that pulls people in. Your crush has a 'pambalani' effect on you.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin nang literal para sa pisikal na magnet o sa matalinghagang paraan para sa isang bagay na may pang-akit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit kami ng **pambalani** sa aming eksperimento sa agham.","translation":"We used a **magnet** in our science experiment."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang ngiti ay tila isang **pambalani** na nakakaakit sa lahat.","translation":"Her smile is like a **magnet** that attracts everyone."}]

translation: to have something lent to someone
meaning_filipino: Utos na payagan ang isang tao na pansamantalang gamitin ang isang bagay na pagmamay-ari ng iba.
original_explanation: This is the verb for when you're the middleman in a lending situation. Your friend wants to borrow your sibling's bike. You tell your sibling, "**Ipahiram** mo na sa kanya yung bike mo." You're not the one lending, but you're facilitating the loan. It’s being the enabler for your friend who always forgets their ballpen.
usage_notes: This is a causative form. The subject of the verb is the person being asked to do the lending, not the person who is lending.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puwede mo bang **ipahiram** ang aklat na ito kay Ana?","translation":"Can you **lend** this book to Ana? (Literally: Can you **have this book lent** to Ana?)"},{"sentence":"**Ipahiram** mo muna ang payong sa bisita dahil umuulan.","translation":"**Lend** the umbrella to the guest for a while because it's raining."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malalim na damdamin ng pag-aalala, takot, o pangamba tungkol sa isang bagay na maaaring mangyari sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: It's that feeling when you see 'We need to talk' in your inbox from your boss, or when your mom uses your full name. It’s the low-key background music of dread playing in your head before something potentially bad happens. A professional level of 'kaba'.
usage_notes: More formal and intense than 'kaba' (nervousness). Often used in literature and formal speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **ngamba** ang kanyang puso habang hinihintay ang resulta ng medical exam.","translation":"His heart was full of **apprehension** while waiting for the results of the medical exam."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang pawiin ang **ngamba** sa pamamagitan ng panalangin.","translation":"He tried to erase the **dread** through prayer."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang de-kuryente na may mga umiikot na talim upang makalikha ng hangin para sa pagpapalamig.
original_explanation: A non-negotiable appliance in every Filipino household. Your best friend during summer, your worst enemy when your mom says 'itututok mo lang sa'yo'. Also the source of the robot voice when you talk into it. Often shortened to 'e-fan'.
usage_notes: The English term is used directly as a loanword. The Spanish-derived "bentilador" is also common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakitapat mo sa akin ang **electricfan**, ang init!","translation":"Please point the **electric fan** at me, it's so hot!"},{"sentence":"Nililinis niya ang alikabok sa **electricfan** tuwing linggo.","translation":"She cleans the dust from the **electric fan** every week."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang nakasanayang pagkakasunod-sunod ng mga gawain o kilos na regular na isinasagawa.
original_explanation: The more classic, tita-approved version of "rutin". Ito 'yung daily grind mo. 'Yung skincare rutina mo na 10 steps, 'yung pag-check ng emails bago mag-kape, 'yung pag-scroll sa socmed bago matulog. It's your personal, unwritten daily script.
usage_notes: More common and standard than its English-derived counterpart "rutin".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinusunod niya ang mahigpit na **rutina** sa umaga.","translation":"She follows a strict morning **routine**."},{"sentence":"Ang buhay niya ay isang walang katapusang **rutina** ng trabaho at bahay.","translation":"His life is an endless **routine** of work and home."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging matigas, mahirap nguyain o baluktutin.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "pagka-" (estado ng pagiging) at "maganit" (matigas nguyain).
original_explanation: That feeling when you order a "well-done" steak and it fights back. It's like trying to chew on old leather shoes or that ube pandesal that's been sitting out for three days. The opposite of "fall-off-the-bone".
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit upang ilarawan ang tekstura ng pagkain, katad, o iba pang materyales na hindi kaaya-ayang tigas o kunat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inireklamo ng customer ang **pagka-maganit** ng karneng inihain sa kanya.","translation":"The customer complained about the **toughness** of the meat served to him."}]

translation: to hurl; to throw with force
meaning_filipino: Ang marahas at malakas na paghahagis o pagpupukol ng isang bagay.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "i-" at "banting" (a forceful throw).
original_explanation: The action you want to do to your phone when it lags in the middle of a ranked game. It's not just 'ihagis'; it's 'ihagis with feelings.' The kind of throw that says, 'Wala na, tapos na ang usapan!'
usage_notes: Bihira na itong gamitin sa modernong pag-uusap at mas matatagpuan sa mga lumang panitikan. Mas karaniwan ang mga kasingkahulugang 'ihagis' o 'ipukol'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang galit, muntik na niyang **ibanting** ang plorera sa pader.","translation":"In so much anger, he almost **hurled** the vase against the wall."},{"sentence":"Para siyang nagwawala, kung anu-ano ang kinukuha at **ibinabanting**.","translation":"He was on a rampage, grabbing and **throwing** things forcefully."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng kalamangan o mas magandang posisyon kumpara sa iba.
original_explanation: Kapag WFH ka tapos umuulan, sobrang mabentaha ang sitwasyon mo kumpara sa mga commuter. It's having an advantage, a leg up, or a better deal than everyone else. Like getting the window seat on a bus.
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of competition, business, or strategy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **mabentaha** para sa aming koponan ang paglalaro sa sarili naming court.","translation":"Playing on our home court became **advantageous** for our team."},{"sentence":"Mas **mabentaha** kung maaga kang mag-book ng flight.","translation":"It's more **advantageous** if you book your flight early."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pautos na paraan na nangangahulugang talian o ikabit ang isang bagay, tulad ng bangka, gamit ang isang lubid o panali. Ito ay anyong pautos ng pandiwang 'higutin'.
original_explanation: This is deep cut Tagalog, like something a fisherman from a remote province would say. It means to tie something down, like securing a boat to a dock. It's the ancestor of 'i-connect mo na 'yan'. Think of it as the original 'tethering'.
usage_notes: Considered a rare or dialectal term. 'Talian' is the more common equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Higtan** mo ang bangka sa poste para hindi anurin.","translation":"**Tie** the boat to the post so it doesn't drift away."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **higtan** nang maigi ang mga kargamento.","translation":"The cargo needs to be **tied down** securely."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat ng mga tao na binuo para sa isang partikular na layunin o gawain, karaniwan ay may kinalaman sa serbisyong pampamayanan.
original_explanation: Think "Brigada Eskwela" - that time of year when your parents were guilt-tripped into painting your classroom for free. It's the spirit of 'bayanihan' but with a specific to-do list, usually involving paint, brooms, and donated snacks.
usage_notes: Strongly associated with "Brigada Eskwela," a Department of Education program encouraging community participation in preparing schools for the opening of classes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumali ang mga magulang sa **brigada** upang ayusin ang mga sira-sirang upuan.","translation":"The parents joined the **work crew** to fix the broken chairs."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng manok na tandang na inaalagaan at sinasanay para partikular na ilaban sa sabong.
etymology: From 'sabong' (cockfighting) + '-in' suffix, indicating the object of the action.
original_explanation: Not your average 'manok'. This is a feathered gladiator, a 'tinali'. It's bred, trained, and fed better than some people, all for the cockpit. This is the main character in the world of 'sabong', the source of both fortune and 'talong' (loss) for many pintakasi.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to the rooster designated for a cockfight.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maingat na inaalagaan ni Mang Teban ang kanyang mga **sasabungin**.","translation":"Mang Teban carefully takes care of his **fighting cocks**."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang taya sa manok na **sasabungin** na galing sa Texas.","translation":"The bet is high on the **fighting cock** that came from Texas."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso at mga gawain na may kinalaman sa paghahanda at pagsasagawa ng paglilibing sa isang yumaong tao.
etymology: From `pag-` + `pa-` + `libing` (burial). The `pa-` indicates causing or arranging for the burial to happen.
original_explanation: The final project management task. It involves everything from choosing a coffin, coordinating with the funeral parlor (punerarya), planning the wake (lamay), and the actual burial. It's a stressful, sad, and expensive process that brings the whole clan together.
usage_notes: Refers to the entire process managed by the living, not just the act of burial itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sila ang namamahala sa lahat ng gastusin para sa **pagpapalibing**.","translation":"They are in charge of all the expenses for the **burial arrangements**."},{"sentence":"Naging maayos ang **pagpapalibing** sa yumaong alkalde.","translation":"The **interment** of the late mayor was orderly."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglabas ng hangin, usok, o anumang bagay mula sa bibig o isang butas.
original_explanation: This is what dragons do with fire, what volcanoes do with ash, and what your tito does with smoke after a long drag on his yosi. It's the forceful 'whoosh' of something coming out. Can also be used for your friend who won't shut up, 'Walang tigil ang pagbubuga niya ng chismis.'
usage_notes: Can refer to air, smoke, fire, words, etc.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mapanganib sa kalusugan ang **pagbubuga** ng makapal na usok ng mga sasakyan.","translation":"The **emission** of thick smoke from vehicles is hazardous to health."},{"sentence":"Kinilabutan ako sa **pagbubuga** ng apoy ng dragon sa pelikula.","translation":"I got goosebumps from the dragon's **spewing** of fire in the movie."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang anyong lupa na mas mataas kaysa sa nakapaligid na lupain ngunit mas maliit at hindi gaanong matarik kaysa sa isang bundok.
original_explanation: "Mountain-lite." Yung version ng bundok na kaya mong akyatin kahit hindi ka prepared. Perfect for pre-nup shoots or 'yung mga "hike" na pang-Instagram lang. Isipin mo na lang ang Chocolate Hills, mga cute na burol sila.
usage_notes: Mahalaga ang diin (stress) sa pagbigkas upang maiba ito sa "burol" (wake), na may diin sa huling pantig. /BU-rol/ (hill) vs /bu-ROL/ (wake).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maganda ang tanawin mula sa tuktok ng **burol**.","translation":"The view from the top of the **hill** is beautiful."},{"sentence":"Ang Chocolate Hills ay binubuo ng higit sa isang libong **burol**.","translation":"The Chocolate Hills are made up of more than a thousand **hills**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng labis na tiwala sa sarili na may kasamang paghamak o pagmamaliit sa iba; mayabang o astang siga.
original_explanation: The guy in the bar who picks a fight for no reason, or the driver who cuts you off and then glares at you. It's an attitude that screams 'Ako ang bida dito.' It's confidence that has crossed the line into douchebaggery. Think 'astig' but with a bad, unlikeable attitude.
usage_notes: Carries a strong negative connotation. It is not a compliment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw siyang kausapin ng mga tao dahil sa kanyang **maangas** na pag-uugali.","translation":"People don't want to talk to him because of his **cocky** attitude."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **maangas** dito, baka mapahamak ka.","translation":"Don't act so **tough** here, you might get into trouble."}]

translation: to soothe; to alleviate; to calm
meaning_filipino: Pagaanin, pahupain, o bawasan ang tindi ng sakit, galit, o anumang matinding damdamin o kalagayan.
etymology: From `pa-` (causative prefix) + `tighaw` (abatement, subsidence) + `-in` (object-focus suffix). The root 'tighaw' is rarely used on its own.
original_explanation: This is what a good massage does to your stress, what Vicks VapoRub does to your cough, or what a friend's comforting words do to your "sakit ng loob" (heartache). It's the act of making a bad situation less intense. "Uminom ka ng tsaa para **patighawin** ang sakit ng lalamunan mo."
usage_notes: Often used for pain, suffering, anger, or thirst. It implies reducing the intensity of something unpleasant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang malamig na panyo sa noo ay nakatulong upang **patighawin** ang kanyang lagnat.","translation":"The cold compress on his forehead helped **to alleviate** his fever."},{"sentence":"Walang makapag**patighaw** sa kanyang galit kundi isang tapat na paghingi ng tawad.","translation":"Nothing can **soothe** his anger except a sincere apology."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkuha o pag-angkin ng isang bagay kapalit ng pera sa hinaharap. Ito ang anyong pangkasalukuyan ng pandiwang 'bili'.
original_explanation: The future tense of "bili". This is your mindset when you get your sahod and you see that 12.12 sale on Shopee or Lazada. "Bibili ako ng bagong sapatos!" you declare, tapos biglang may darating na Meralco bill. Life happens.
usage_notes: Future tense of 'bili'. The actor is in the 'ang' form (e.g., *Bibili ako...*).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bibili** ako ng bigas mamaya sa palengke.","translation":"I **will buy** rice later at the market."},{"sentence":"Saan ka **bibili** ng pasalubong para sa kanila?","translation":"Where **will you buy** souvenirs for them?"}]

meaning_filipino: Pawalang-sala sa isang akusasyon o kaso sa korte; palayain mula sa isang paratang.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "absuelto" (acquitted) at dinagdagan ng hulaping Tagalog na "-hin".
original_explanation: 'Yung "Not Guilty!" moment sa isang courtroom drama. Ito 'yung gusto mong marinig ng abogado mo kapag nasabit ka sa isang gulo. From Spanish "absuelto" + Tagalog suffix "-hin".
usage_notes: A legal term. The root 'absuwelto' is the past participle/adjective form, meaning 'acquitted'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inaasahan ng nasasakdal na siya ay **absuweltuhin** ng hukom.","translation":"The defendant hopes that the judge will **acquit** him."},{"sentence":"Nagdiwang ang kanyang pamilya nang **absuweltuhin** siya sa lahat ng kaso.","translation":"His family celebrated when he was **acquitted** of all charges."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaki at malambot na unan, karaniwang ginagamit bilang suporta sa pag-upo sa sahig o bilang pandekorasyon sa sopa.
original_explanation: Think of that big, comfy cushion you grab from the sofa when you're about to marathon a K-drama series. It's not the one for your head when you sleep; it's the one you hug, sit on, or throw at your sibling. It's the decorative pillow that your mom says "wag upuan!" but you do it anyway.
usage_notes: Madalas na ipinagpapalit sa 'kutsón' o sa varyant nitong 'almuhada', bagaman ang 'almohadon' ay karaniwang tumutukoy sa mas malaking unan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naupo siya sa sahig gamit ang isang malaking **almohadon**.","translation":"She sat on the floor using a large **cushion**."},{"sentence":"Puno ng mga makukulay na **almohadon** ang kanilang sala.","translation":"Their living room is full of colorful **cushions**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang likhang-isip na isinulat o kinatha, tulad ng tula, maikling kuwento, nobela, o sanaysay.
etymology: Possibly from a root word related to creation or forming.
original_explanation: This is the final output after countless sleepless nights fueled by coffee and self-doubt. It's your thesis, your Wattpad story, your spoken-word piece about your ex. Every 'akda' is a piece of the author's soul, served on paper (or a screen) for everyone to judge.
usage_notes: A formal term used in literary and academic contexts. 'May-akda' means 'author'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Noli Me Tángere ay isang tanyag na **akda** ni Jose Rizal.","translation":"Noli Me Tángere is a famous **literary work** by Jose Rizal."},{"sentence":"Sumali siya sa isang paligsahan sa pagsulat ng **akda**.","translation":"He joined a competition for writing a **composition**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang biglaan at malakas na paghila o pagbatak sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: Imagine trying to start an old lawnmower or a stubborn generator—that sharp, forceful pull is kalsot. It's also the feeling when your friend suddenly yanks you out of the way of a speeding motorcycle. It’s a sudden, "uy, teka!" kind of pull.
usage_notes: A less common word for pulling. 'Hila' or 'batak' are more frequently used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **kalsot** lang sa pisi ay umandar na ang makina.","translation":"Just one **pull** on the cord and the engine started."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang malakas na **kalsot** sa kanyang braso.","translation":"He felt a strong **yank** on his arm."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang reaksyon sa social media, partikular sa Facebook, na nagpapahiwatig ng galit o pagkainis sa isang post.
etymology: From the Facebook "Reactions" feature introduced in 2016.
original_explanation: The digital version of a death glare. It's what you give to a post about traffic, a fake news article from a tito, or your ex's new happy relationship photo. A small, red, furious emoji that says 'I disapprove!' without typing a single word. The ultimate passive-aggressive tool online.
usage_notes: Used colloquially in Taglish. Not a formal Filipino word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puro **angry react** ang inabot ng post ng politiko.","translation":"The politician's post received nothing but **angry reacts**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong i-**angry react**, mag-comment ka kung may problema ka!","translation":"Don't just give me an **angry react**, comment if you have a problem!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang personal na kuru-kuro, hinuha, o paniniwala na hindi pa napapatunayan at batay lamang sa sariling pag-iisip o damdamin.
original_explanation: Your personal "Marites" theory. It's that chismis you cooked up in your head based on incomplete data. "In my opinion..." ka pa, pero pala-palagay mo lang naman pala. It's the official term for your "feeling ko..." statements.
usage_notes: Mahalaga ang gitling upang maiba ito sa ibang salita. Nagpapahiwatig ito ng espekulasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pala-palagay** ko lang naman, pero baka may gusto siya sa iyo.","translation":"It's just my **assumption**, but I think he/she likes you."},{"sentence":"Ang mga sinabi niya ay pawang **pala-palagay** at walang matibay na ebidensya.","translation":"His statements are all pure **surmise** and have no solid evidence."}]

translation: to eat everything up, to devour
meaning_filipino: Ubusin ang lahat ng pagkain sa isang paraan na tila nagpapakita ng malaking gutom o kasakiman.
etymology: From 'bangkay' (corpse). A morbidly humorous and colloquial term suggesting to 'finish off' the food as if killing it.
original_explanation: This is what happens during a 'mukbang' challenge or when your family finally opens the Noche Buena feast. It's not just 'kain' (eat), it's 'kain with a vengeance'. You see a table full of food, and your only mission is to leave no survivors. 'Bangkain mo na 'yang natirang pizza.'
usage_notes: Colloquial and highly informal. It carries a humorous, almost gluttonous connotation. The root is 'bangkay', not 'bangkain'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **bangkain** lahat, magtira ka para sa iba!","translation":"Don't **devour** everything, leave some for the others!"},{"sentence":"Nagugutom talaga siya, kaya niyang **bangkain** ang isang buong manok.","translation":"He's really hungry, he can **eat up** a whole chicken."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbawi o pag-delete ng isang naipadalang mensahe sa isang digital na platform bago pa man ito mabasa ng tatanggap, o kahit nabasa na.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na "unsend", isang salitang naging popular sa pag-usbong ng mga messaging app.
original_explanation: The digital version of "sabi ko nga, joke lang." It's the panic button you press after sending a risky text to your crush at 3 AM or accidentally sending a rant about your boss to your boss. The 'unsend' feature is a modern miracle, the savior of careers and relationships. "I-unsend mo na 'yan, bago pa niya makita!"
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamitan ng panlaping Filipino tulad ng 'i-unsend' (to unsend it) o 'in-unsend' (unsent it).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Buti na lang at na-**unsend** ko agad 'yung maling mensahe na naipadala ko.","translation":"Good thing I was able to **unsend** the wrong message I sent right away."}]

translation: peak of heat; height (of an event)
meaning_filipino: Ang pinakasukdulan o pinakamatinding punto ng init, galit, o isang pangyayari.
original_explanation: Literally the "peak of heat," like high noon in a Philippine summer when you feel like a walking chicharon. But it's also used for the peak of anything intense: the `kainitan` of an argument (the shouting part), the `kainitan` of a basketball game (the last 2 minutes), or the `kainitan` of the chismis (the juiciest part of the story).
usage_notes: Can refer to literal temperature or the figurative intensity of a situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang lumabas sa **kainitan** ng sikat ng araw.","translation":"Don't go out during the **peak heat** of the sun."},{"sentence":"Sa **kainitan** ng kanilang pagtatalo, biglang may sumigaw mula sa labas.","translation":"At the **height** of their argument, someone suddenly shouted from outside."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtigil sa paglaban o pagtutol at pagpayag na mapailalim sa kapangyarihan o kontrol ng iba.
original_explanation: That moment in a relationship argument when you just say 'Okay, fine, you win!' even if you don't believe it. It's also that #hugot feeling when you're tired of chasing your dreams (or your crush) and just want to say 'ayoko na.' Pagsuko na ba or laban pa?
usage_notes: Commonly used in contexts of conflict (war, arguments) and personal struggles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagsuko** ay hindi laging tanda ng kahinaan.","translation":"**Surrender** is not always a sign of weakness."},{"sentence":"Matapos ang mahabang negosasyon, napilitan ang mga rebelde sa **pagsuko**.","translation":"After long negotiations, the rebels were forced into **surrender**."}]

meaning_filipino: Magsasagawa ng isang pagkilos upang malaman kung ano ang kahihinatnan; gagawin ang isang bagay sa unang pagkakataon o bilang isang eksperimento.
original_explanation: The official motto of everyone's New Year's Resolution to go to the gym. "Sige, susubok ako." Also what you say before tasting the spiciest dish on the menu, or before applying for that job you're not sure you're qualified for. It's the battle cry of the brave, the curious, and the "bahala na" crowd.
usage_notes: Future tense of "sumubok". The 'su-' prefix indicates the future tense of an '-um-' verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Susubok** akong magluto ng adobo sa unang pagkakataon.","translation":"I **will try** to cook adobo for the first time."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **susubok** na sagutin ang napakahirap na tanong?","translation":"Who **will attempt** to answer the very difficult question?"}]

meaning_filipino: Mga alitan o hidwaan sa pagitan ng mga grupo ng tagahanga (fandoms) ng magkakaibang artista, grupo, o love team. Karaniwan itong nangyayari online, lalo na sa mga social media platform.
etymology: Direktang hiram mula sa Ingles na "fan wars."
original_explanation: Ito yung online "bardagulan" o awayan ng mga fandom. "Mas sikat idol ko!" "No, mas magaling idol ko!" Minsan tungkol sa music chart positions, awards, o kung sino ang naunang nag-sold out ng concert. Dito nasusubok ang pagiging "marites" at keyboard warrior mo, pero in the end, talo lahat kasi aawayin kayo ng mga "multi-stan".
usage_notes: Isang negatibong aspekto ng fan culture na kadalasang nagaganap sa Twitter, Facebook, at iba pang social media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iwasan na natin ang **fanwars** at suportahan na lang natin ang isa't isa.","translation":"Let's avoid **fan wars** and just support each other."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula ang **fanwars** dahil sa isang post na nagkukumpara sa dalawang grupo.","translation":"The **fan wars** started because of a post comparing the two groups."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng pabor, posisyon, o pagkakataon sa mga kamag-anak o kaibigan, lalo na sa larangan ng politika at negosyo, sa halip na batay sa kanilang kwalipikasyon.
etymology: From Spanish 'nepotismo', from Italian 'nepotismo', from Latin 'nepos' ('nephew').
original_explanation: Ah, nepotismo. The unofficial national sport of Philippine politics and sometimes, even in the office. It's when an official gets their underqualified 'pamangkin' (nephew/niece) a high-paying government job, or the boss hires his 'inaanak' (godchild) as a manager despite them only knowing how to use TikTok. It's the "it's not what you know, it's who you know" principle turned up to eleven, with a side of 'utang na loob'.
usage_notes: A formal term used frequently in discussions about politics, corruption, and business ethics.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Talamak ang **nepotismo** sa gobyerno kaya maraming hindi kuwalipikadong opisyal.","translation":"**Nepotism** is rampant in government, which is why there are many unqualified officials."},{"sentence":"Ipinagbabawal ng batas ang **nepotismo** upang maiwasan ang pang-aabuso sa kapangyarihan.","translation":"The law prohibits **nepotism** to prevent the abuse of power."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan o tao na ginagamit upang ihiwalay ang mga hindi kanais-nais na bahagi; isang komite o tao na pumipili ng mga kuwalipikadong kandidato.
original_explanation: This is your coffee filter in the morning, the strainer for your pancit palabok sauce, or even the HR department screening resumes. It's anything or anyone that separates the 'g' from the 'not g', the essentials from the 'marites' (chismis). It removes the unnecessary baggage.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa isang bagay (sieve, strainer) o sa isang tao/grupo (screening committee).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang **tagapagsala** upang makuha ang purong katas ng niyog.","translation":"She used the **filter** to get the pure coconut milk."},{"sentence":"Ang board of judges ang nagsilbing **tagapagsala** ng mga kalahok sa timpalak.","translation":"The board of judges served as the **screener** of the contestants in the competition."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking unggoy na may mahahabang braso at kulay-kapeng-pula na balahibo, na katutubo sa mga kagubatan ng Borneo at Sumatra.
etymology: Mula sa Malay na "orang hutan" na nangangahulugang "tao ng gubat".
original_explanation: Ito yung kamag-anak nating taga-gubat na 'person of the forest' ang meaning ng pangalan. Sila yung chill lang na nakasabit sa puno, nag-iisip ng malalim. Huwag malito sa ex mo, kahit pareho silang mahilig mag-monkey around.
usage_notes: Isang biyolohikal na termino. Huwag gamitin bilang panlait sa tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakita kami ng **oranggutang** sa zoo.","translation":"We saw an **orangutan** at the zoo."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga palamuti o anumang bagay na isinusuot o inilalagay upang mapaganda ang isang tao, bagay, o lugar, lalo na para sa isang espesyal na okasyon.
original_explanation: All the glitz and glamour. Ito 'yung bonggang-bonggang decorations tuwing Pasko, 'yung mga pailaw sa plaza. Ito rin 'yung kumpletong set: the gown, the jewelry, the makeup—the whole package for a big event like a wedding or a debut. 'Yung 'extra' a.k.a. the bells and whistles. Less is NOT more when it comes to kagayakan.
usage_notes: Refers to the collective set of decorations or attire, often implying extravagance or being dressed up for an occasion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakaganda ng **kagayakan** ng simbahan para sa kasal.","translation":"The **decorations** of the church for the wedding were so beautiful."},{"sentence":"Ang buong pamilya ay dumating na suot ang kanilang mararangyang **kagayakan**.","translation":"The whole family arrived wearing their luxurious **finery**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga impormasyon o salaysay na nauukol sa buhay ng isang partikular na tao.
original_explanation: Basically, anything that's 'based on a true story' about someone's life. Think of it as the adjective for movies like 'Heneral Luna' or 'Goyo'. It's the long-form version of someone's 'My Day' or IG story, but made into a film or a book.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pelikulang 'Heneral Luna' ay isang **biyograpiko**ng obra na nagpapakita ng kanyang katapangan.","translation":"The film 'Heneral Luna' is a **biographical** masterpiece that shows his bravery."},{"sentence":"Kinokolekta niya ang mga **biyograpiko**ng datos para sa kanyang isusulat na aklat.","translation":"She is collecting **biographical** data for the book she will write."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kabuuang halaga ng salapi na natatanggap bilang kapalit ng serbisyo, trabaho, o mula sa isang negosyo.
original_explanation: Your sahod, your sweldo, your earnings. It's the reason you brave EDSA traffic or work the graveyard shift in a BPO. It's what you budget for bills, luho, and padala for the family. When someone asks "Magkano ang kinikita mo?", they're asking about your salary.
usage_notes: While derived from a verb, this form is commonly used as a noun to mean 'income' or 'revenue'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang **kinikita** niya sa kanyang online business.","translation":"Her **income** from her online business is large."},{"sentence":"Sapat lang ang aking **kinikita** para sa aming pang-araw-araw na gastusin.","translation":"My **earnings** are just enough for our daily expenses."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalaan ng salapi o pondo para sa isang partikular na layunin, tao, o bagay.
etymology: From Spanish "gastos" (expenses). The affixes `pa-` and `-an` turn it into a verb meaning 'to have someone spend on something' or 'to finance something'.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of "gastos." It's what you do when your friend says "Libre mo naman ako!" and you actually do it. You're the one who will "pagastusan" the whole barkada's milk tea craving. It's the financial equivalent of being the designated martyr.
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of budgeting, family expenses, or treating someone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pagastusan** ang mga bagay na hindi mo naman kailangan.","translation":"Don't **spend on** things you don't really need."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **pagagastusin** mo para sa proyekto?","translation":"Who will you have **finance** the project?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malakas at madamdaming pag-iyak na may kasamang paghagulgol o pagdaing, karaniwang dahil sa matinding kalungkutan, sakit, o pighati.
etymology: From pa- + N (nasal assimilation of t) + tangis. The act or manner of wailing.
original_explanation: This isn't just simple crying (iyak). This is full-on, teleserye-level breakdown. The kind with matching hagulgol, singhot, and dramatic pauses. It's what you do when your favorite character dies, when you get ghosted, or when you see your credit card bill after a 12.12 sale. The soundtrack to major life drama.
usage_notes: A more intense and poetic word for crying. It implies a deep, sorrowful, and often audible expression of grief.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig sa buong kabahayan ang kanyang malakas na **panangis**.","translation":"Her loud **weeping** was heard throughout the entire house."},{"sentence":"Ang **panangis** ng isang ina para sa nawalang anak ay nakakadurog ng puso.","translation":"The **lamentation** of a mother for her lost child is heartbreaking."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbibigay ng babala sa isang tao o grupo sa hinaharap upang maipaalam ang isang panganib o kahihinatnan.
original_explanation: It's what your work BFF does when the scary boss is approaching your cubicle: 'Psst, babalaan kita, mainit ulo ni Sir.' It's the future tense of giving a heads-up, the verbal equivalent of a flashing red light before someone gets into trouble.
usage_notes: Future tense, object-focused verb. The person being warned is the object of the verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Babalaan** ko sila tungkol sa mga pekeng balita sa internet.","translation":"I will **warn** them about the fake news on the internet."}]

meaning_filipino: Bawasan ang bigat, dalahin, o pasanin ng isang bagay o tao; gawing mas magaan.
original_explanation: When your bag is too heavy, you 'gaanan' it by giving stuff to your friends. When your workload is killing you, you ask your boss to 'gaanan' it. When your heart is heavy with 'hugot', you 'gaanan' it by talking to a friend. It's the act of reducing a burden, whether it's physical, professional, or emotional.
usage_notes: Can be used for literal weight or metaphorical burdens like work, problems, or feelings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Gaanan** mo naman ang bag mo, baka magkasakit ka sa likod.","translation":"**Lighten** your bag, you might hurt your back."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang **gaanan** ang loob ng kaibigang may problema.","translation":"She is trying to **lighten** the burden of her friend who has a problem."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang tao na may mga matang bahagyang nakapikit dahil sa antok o kagigising lang.
original_explanation: That look you have during the 9 AM Zoom meeting when you only had 3 hours of sleep. Your eyes are half-closed, you're not really there, and you're just trying to nod at the right moments. "Gising ka na ba talaga o pungat ka pa?"
usage_notes: Often used to describe someone who has just woken up or is very sleepy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halata sa mga mata niyang **pungat** na kulang siya sa tulog.","translation":"It's obvious from his **drowsy-eyed** look that he lacks sleep."},{"sentence":"Pumasok siya sa opisina na **pungat** pa ang mga mata.","translation":"He entered the office with his eyes still **half-awake**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtutol, pagkontra, o hindi pagsang-ayon sa isang ideya, utos, o daloy.
original_explanation: This is the official term for being 'that guy' in a meeting who says 'I object!' It's the act of pushing back, resisting, or contradicting. When your parents tell you to be a doctor but you want to be an artist, your choice is an act of 'pagsalansang'. It's the core of any debate, argument, or rebellion. You're not just disagreeing quietly; you're actively opposing something.
usage_notes: This is the more standard and common spelling compared to 'pagsalangsang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaisa sila sa **pagsalansang** sa panukalang batas.","translation":"They united in **opposition** to the proposed law."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagsalansang** sa utos ng magulang ay madalas na nagiging sanhi ng alitan.","translation":"The **defiance** of a parent's command often becomes a cause of conflict."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtiklop ng isang bagay, tulad ng damit o papel, na isasagawa sa hinaharap.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `mag-` (pormang pandiwa) + pag-uulit ng unang pantig ng salitang ugat `tu-` (panahong panghinaharap) + `tupi` (fold).
original_explanation: This is what your mom tells you to do with the mountain of laundry that's been sitting on 'the chair' for a week. 'Magtutupi ka na ng damit mo!' is the battle cry against bedroom clutter. It's the future tense of folding, full of hope and procrastination.
usage_notes: Ginagamit para sa mga bagay na maaaring itiklop nang maayos, tulad ng damit, papel, o kumot.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magtutupi** ako ng mga damit mamayang gabi.","translation":"I **will fold** the clothes later tonight."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **magtutupi** ng mga bagong labang kumot?","translation":"Who **will fold** the newly washed blankets?"}]

translation: to light a candle; to erect
meaning_filipino: Magtayo o magpatayo ng isang bagay sa posisyong patindig, tulad ng kandila o poste.
original_explanation: This is what you do in church when you're praying for a miracle, like passing your board exams or for your crush to finally notice you. "Magtirik ng kandila." It can also mean to build or set something upright, like a tent. But mostly, it’s for candles and prayers.
usage_notes: Often used in a religious or spiritual context when referring to candles. Can also mean to erect or build something vertically.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumunta siya sa simbahan upang **magtirik** ng kandila para sa kanyang yumaong lola.","translation":"She went to church to **light a candle** for her deceased grandmother."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magtirik** ng poste para sa bakod.","translation":"We need to **erect** a post for the fence."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na nagdudulot ng pag-aalala o pagkabahala; isang bagay na dapat tandaan.
original_explanation: Your credit card bill, your thesis deadline, your toxic officemate, your "sana all" moments on IG—these are all your `alalahanin`. It's the mental load you carry every day, the stuff that makes you want to just "unplug" and go to the beach.
usage_notes: Ang diin sa huling pantig ang nagpapaiba rito mula sa anyong pandiwa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pinakamalaki kong **alalahanin** ngayon ay ang aking mga bayarin.","translation":"My biggest **worry** right now is my bills."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagluluto ng pagkain, karaniwan ay karne, sa istilong asado na may matamis at maalat na sarsa.
etymology: From Spanish 'asado' (roasted). In the Philippines, the meaning evolved into a specific braised dish.
original_explanation: This is a specific cooking verb! It's not just roasting; it's cooking something in that classic sweet and savory, often reddish, 'asado' sauce (think soy sauce, star anise, sugar). It's the action that results in the delicious ulam called Asado, whether it's pork, chicken, or even siopao filling.
usage_notes: Refers to a specific Filipino cooking method, distinct from the general 'mag-asada' (to roast).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ituro mo sa akin kung paano **mag-asado** ng baboy na katulad ng luto ni Lola.","translation":"Teach me how **to cook pork asado-style** just like Grandma's cooking."},{"sentence":"Masarap **mag-asado** ng manok para gawing palaman sa siopao.","translation":"It's delicious **to cook chicken asado-style** to use as filling for steamed buns."}]

translation: was jailed, was trapped, was confined
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging hindi makaalis sa isang lugar, maaaring sa bilangguan o dahil sa isang hadlang.
original_explanation: The literal meaning is "jailed," like in Bilibid. But it's also what you feel during a 4-hour meeting that could have been an email. "Help, nakulong ako sa elevator!" Or for Pinoys abroad, "Nakulong kami sa bahay dahil sa snowstorm." It's the feeling of being stuck, literally or figuratively.
usage_notes: The phrase 'nakulong ng niyebe' is a specific application meaning 'snowed in' or 'trapped by snow'. The general word 'nakulong' means trapped or imprisoned.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa lakas ng blizzard, **nakulong** sila sa kanilang bahay.","translation":"Because of the strong blizzard, they were **trapped** in their house."},{"sentence":"Ang magnanakaw ay **nakulong** ng sampung taon.","translation":"The thief **was jailed** for ten years."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi pa hustong gulang, karanasan, o pag-iisip; mura pa.
original_explanation: Describes a fruit that's not ready to be eaten, or a person whose brain is still buffering. When someone gives you terrible, unsolicited advice, you can think "ang pahat ng isip nito." It's the state of being green, both literally for a mango and figuratively for someone who still thinks "Ipon-challenge" means they can buy a condo in a year.
usage_notes: Often used to describe thinking or judgment ('pahat na pag-iisip').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong pitasin ang mangga, **pahat** pa.","translation":"Don't pick the mango, it's still **unripe**."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **pahat** na pag-iisip, madali siyang nalinlang.","translation":"Because of his **immature** thinking, he was easily deceived."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa sistema, katangian, o kaugaliang may kaugnayan sa peudalismo, kung saan ang kapangyarihan ay nakasalalay sa pagmamay-ari ng lupa.
original_explanation: Describes a system that feels like it's straight out of the Middle Ages, even if it's happening now. Think of a hacienda owner who controls the entire town, or a political dynasty that treats their province like a personal kingdom. When someone says the system is "peudal," they're saying it's old-fashioned, unfair, and based on who your lolo is, not what you can do.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng kasaysayan, agham panlipunan, at pampulitikang kritisismo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga magsasaka ay nag-aklas laban sa **peudal** na sistema ng kanilang panginoong maylupa.","translation":"The farmers revolted against the **feudal** system of their landlord."},{"sentence":"Marami pa ring bakas ng kulturang **peudal** sa ilang probinsya sa Pilipinas.","translation":"There are still many traces of **feudal** culture in some provinces in the Philippines."}]

meaning_filipino: Papunta sa labas o patungo sa ibang lugar; malapit nang umalis.
original_explanation: The standard Filipino excuse to get out of a party or family gathering you don't want to be in. "Ma, **paalis** na po kami." Also the state of your salary 5 minutes after you receive it. It's always on its way out.
usage_notes: Can also function as an adjective describing a noun (e.g., "tren na paalis" - departing train).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nang dumating ka, **paalis** na ako.","translation":"When you arrived, I was already **about to leave**."},{"sentence":"Sumakay siya sa bus na **paalis** patungong Bicol.","translation":"He boarded the **departing** bus bound for Bicol."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging mabagal; ang kakulangan sa bilis sa pagkilos, pag-iisip, o pag-unlad.
original_explanation: The official state of your internet connection, the traffic on a payday Friday, and the government service you're trying to apply for. It's the reason you're late for work. It's the loading screen of life that never seems to finish.
usage_notes: Can describe the slow speed of a person, object, or process.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naiinis ako sa **kabagalan** ng serbisyo nila.","translation":"I'm annoyed by the **slowness** of their service."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa **kabagalan** ng trapiko, nahuli siya sa pulong.","translation":"Because of the **slowness** of the traffic, he was late for the meeting."}]

translation: to be able to make use of; to benefit from
meaning_filipino: Magamit ang isang bagay sa paraang may kapakinabangan o benepisyo.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of "resourcefulness" or "making the most of something." It's when you find a way to use something, even if it's not for its intended purpose. "Paano ko kaya mapapakinabangan itong mga lumang bote?" It's also used in a negative way, like when someone feels they are just being used: "Ayokong maramdaman na pinapakinabangan mo lang ako." Ouch, hugot.
usage_notes: This is a more general/infinitive form compared to 'mapakikinabangan' (future tense). It's object-focused.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay **mapakinabangan** mo ang regalong ito.","translation":"I hope you can **make use of** this gift."},{"sentence":"Maraming paraan para **mapakinabangan** ang teknolohiya sa pag-aaral.","translation":"There are many ways **to benefit from** technology in studies."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na mahilig uminom ng alak o madalas na lasing; palainom. Ang panlalaking anyo nito (lasinggera para sa babae).
original_explanation: That tito or friend who's always the first to suggest 'tagay na!' and the last one standing (or sleeping on the sofa). They have a high tolerance, a story for every occasion, and probably a collection of beer-branded t-shirts. The male version is **lasinggero**, the female is **lasinggera**.
usage_notes: Gendered term. The female equivalent is 'lasinggera'. Can be used playfully or as a serious label for an alcoholic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa baryo bilang isang **lasinggero**.","translation":"He is known in the village as a **drunkard**."},{"sentence":"Noon, **lasinggero** siya pero nagbago na siya ngayon.","translation":"He used to be a **heavy drinker**, but he has changed now."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng muling pag-aayos o pagbubuo ng isang sistema, organisasyon, o istruktura upang ito'y mapabuti o maging mas epektibo.
original_explanation: This is what happens when a company is 'right-sizing' (a.k.a. may layoffs). It's also what a government agency undergoes after a huge scandal. On a personal level, it's rebuilding your life after a major setback. It's 'pagbabago' with a blueprint and a goal of making things stronger.
usage_notes: Commonly used in the context of organizations, governments, or systems needing structural reform.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpapatupad ang kumpanya ng **pagbabagong-tatag** upang makabangon sa pagkalugi.","translation":"The company is implementing a **reorganization** to recover from its losses."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kilos o tugon na katumbas ng isang naunang ginawa, maaaring mabuti o masama.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'resbak.' When someone does you dirty, and you just can't let it go. It's the plot of every teleserye where the bida comes back rich and fabulous to make the kontrabida's life miserable. It can also be a good thing, like returning a favor ('gantihan ng pabor'), but let's be real, we usually think of the juicy, dramatic kind.
usage_notes: Often has a negative connotation of vengeance, but can be neutral (gantihan ng tulong - return of help) or positive (gantimpala - reward).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang magtanim ng sama ng loob at maghangad ng **ganti**.","translation":"Don't harbor ill feelings and seek **revenge**."},{"sentence":"Ang pagtulong niya sa akin ay may **ganti** ring kabutihan mula sa akin.","translation":"His help for me will have a **requital** of goodness from me."}]

translation: to turn upside down, to invert
meaning_filipino: Gawing baligtad o patiwarik ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is what you want to do to your life sometimes—just pabalintuwarin and start over. Or when you're looking for something in your bag and you dump everything out, turning it upside down. Parang "world turned upside down" sa Hamilton, ganern.
usage_notes: The object is the thing being turned upside down.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pabalintuwarin** ang baso at matatapon ang tubig.","translation":"Don't **turn** the glass **upside down** or the water will spill."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **pabalintuwarin** ang argumento ng kanyang kalaban.","translation":"He tried to **invert** his opponent's argument."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghahayag, pagpapakita, o pagsisiwalat ng isang bagay na dating nakatago, lihim, o hindi alam ng publiko.
original_explanation: This is the "tea-spilling" moment. The grand reveal. It's what happens in a "Raffy Tulfo in Action" episode, or when a celebrity finally does a "coming out" vlog. It can be about exposing a secret, a scandal, or just finally showing your true, unfiltered self to the world (or your IG close friends).
usage_notes: Can be used for secrets, truths, or physically exposing something to the elements (e.g., paglalantad sa araw - exposing to the sun).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paglalantad** niya ng katotohanan ay nagdulot ng malaking kontrobersiya.","translation":"His/Her **disclosure** of the truth caused a huge controversy."},{"sentence":"Matapang ang kanyang naging **paglalantad** tungkol sa kanyang pagkatao.","translation":"His/Her **act of revealing** his/her identity was brave."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paglalarawan sa isang tao na may mataas na tindig at may mabuting kalusugan.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'anak, kumain ka ng gulay' achievement. It's the physical state every Filipino mother wishes for their child. You're not just tall, you've got the healthy glow to match. Think of a basketball player who also happens to be a health and wellness endorser.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit na papuri o paglalarawan sa pisikal na anyo at kalagayan ng isang tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lahat ng anak niya ay **matangkad at malusog**.","translation":"All of her children are **tall and healthy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tindahan kung saan nagbebenta ng sapatos, o isang pagawaan kung saan gumagawa o nagkukumpuni ng sapatos.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "zapatería" (shoe shop), mula sa "zapato" (sapatos).
original_explanation: Your friendly neighborhood shoe store. Before SM and an online cart, you went to the `sapateria` to get your school shoes or have your dad's leather shoes repaired. It's the place that smells of new leather and shoe polish. While "shoe store" is more common now, `sapateria` has that classic, Marikina-made vibe.
usage_notes: Medyo luma na ang termino at mas karaniwang ginagamit ang "tindahan ng sapatos" o "shoe store" ngayon, ngunit naiintindihan pa rin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpagawa siya ng sapatos sa sikat na **sapateria** sa Marikina.","translation":"He had shoes made at a famous **shoemaker's shop** in Marikina."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang hayop na palaboy-laboy at walang nag-aalaga.
original_explanation: This is your friendly neighborhood 'askal' (asong kalye) or 'pusakal' (pusang kalye). A 'gala' dog or cat is a free spirit, a wanderer with no master. They know all the secret shortcuts and where the best leftovers are. It's the animal version of the human 'gala' (noun), but with more fleas and less budget planning.
usage_notes: Ang diin ay nasa huling pantig (/ga-LA/). Pangunahing ginagamit upang ilarawan ang mga hayop.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming asong **gala** sa aming subdibisyon.","translation":"There are many **stray** dogs in our subdivision."},{"sentence":"Pinakain niya ang pusang **gala** na laging nasa tapat ng kanilang bahay.","translation":"She fed the **wandering** cat that was always in front of their house."}]

translation: to spread throughout, to become widespread in
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkalat o pag-iral sa isang malawak na lugar o sa kabuuan ng isang espasyo o pangkat.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of 'laganap'. It's the action of something *becoming* widespread. Imagine a single spark (chismis) that starts a fire (office-wide drama). The fire *spreading* is 'nilaganapan'. The state of the office being on fire is 'laganap'.
usage_notes: This is the object-focus verb form related to 'laganap'. The location or area being filled/spread over becomes the subject of the sentence. E.g., 'Nilaganapan ng balita ang bayan' (The town was spread over by the news).
