original_explanation: 'Yung friend mong laging nasusunod ang gusto sa group project, or 'yung Bida Kontrabida sa teleserye na laging agaw-eksena. It's the alpha in the pack, the loudest voice in the room, the main character energy.
usage_notes: Can describe a person, trait, or even a gene.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroon siyang **dominante** na personalidad.","translation":"She has a **dominant** personality."},{"sentence":"Ang pulang kulay ay **dominante** sa kanyang obra maestra.","translation":"The color red is **dominant** in his masterpiece."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng lutuing Pilipino na gawa sa nudels, karaniwang inihahalo sa iba't ibang sahog tulad ng gulay, karne, at pagkaing-dagat.
etymology: From Hokkien 'pian e sit' (便ê食), meaning 'something conveniently cooked.'
original_explanation: The official dish of every Filipino birthday party, office meeting, and general gathering. Believed to grant long life, but mostly grants a happy tummy. Comes in more varieties than there are political opinions in your family group chat (Bihon, Canton, Malabon, etc.).
usage_notes: Often followed by the type, e.g., pancit canton, pancit bihon, pancit malabon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutan mag-order ng **pancit** para humaba ang buhay ng may kaarawan.","translation":"Don't forget to order **pancit** for the birthday celebrant to have a long life."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang **pancit** na niluto ni lola, kumpleto sa sahog.","translation":"The **noodle dish** that grandma cooked is delicious, with complete ingredients."}]

translation: a person who fishes using a 'bunsol' (fish trap)
meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang hanapbuhay o gawain ay ang paghuli ng isda gamit ang bunsol, isang uri ng patibong sa isda.
etymology: From `man-` (doer prefix) + `bunsol` (a type of fish trap). The `n` assimilates to `m` before `b`.
original_explanation: This is your super-specialized, OG fisherman. Not the one with a fancy rod, but the one who knows the river's secrets and uses a 'bunsol'—a kind of fish trap. They're the real-life 'Finding Nemo' villain from the fish's perspective, but a hero to their family come dinner time. A very specific job title from the province.
usage_notes: A very specific and rare term, usually known only in fishing communities where this method is used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lolo ko ay isang bihasang **mambubunsol** sa aming ilog.","translation":"My grandfather is a skilled **person who fishes with a 'bunsol'** in our river."},{"sentence":"Kakaunti na lamang ang mga **mambubunsol** ngayon dahil sa modernong paraan ng pangingisda.","translation":"There are very few **'bunsol' fishermen** now because of modern fishing methods."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkawala ng hangin o laman sa loob ng isang bagay, na nagiging sanhi ng pag-urong o pagliit nito.
original_explanation: Parang wallet mo bago sumahod. O yung lobo pagkatapos ng birthday party. O yung tiyan mo pagkagising sa umaga bago mag-kape. 'Yan ang impis. It's that state of being flat, empty, or having lost all its air.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit para sa mga bagay na may hangin (gulong, bola) o sa tiyan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **impis** ang gulong ng kanyang sasakyan.","translation":"The tire of his car became **flat**."},{"sentence":"Pagkagising niya, **impis** pa ang kanyang tiyan.","translation":"When she woke up, her stomach was still **flat**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng umiibig o in love; isang kasintahan o minamahal na babae.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "enamorada", ang pambabaeng anyo ng "enamorado" (in love).
original_explanation: This is the classic, old-school term for a girl who is deeply in love. Parang 'yung bida sa isang harana scene, looking out the window, sighing for her man. It’s very telenovela, very Maria Clara. Hindi lang 'to "crush," ito 'yung "head-over-heels, isusulat-ko-pangalan-mo-sa-notebook-ko" level of in love.
usage_notes: Kadalasang ginagamit sa panitikan o sa pormal at romantikong konteksto. Medyo luma na para sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tila isang **enamorada** ang dalaga sa tuwing nakikita ang kanyang sinisinta.","translation":"The young lady seems like a **woman in love** whenever she sees her beloved."},{"sentence":"Siya ang naging **enamorada** ng sikat na makata.","translation":"She became the **beloved** of the famous poet."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkawala ng puhunan o salapi sa isang negosyo o transaksyon.
etymology: Mula sa Hokkien 豬 (ti o tu, 'baboy', ngunit ginagamit sa mga parirala tungkol sa pagsusugal/pagkatalo) + 錢 (chîⁿ, 'pera').
original_explanation: Yung feeling ng online seller na mas malaki pa 'yung shipping fee kaysa sa kita. O kaya 'yung nag-invest ka sa crypto tapos biglang nag-dip. Basically, you're losing money, honey. It's the opposite of "profit."
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng negosyo, pananalapi, o anumang sitwasyon kung saan may kabuuang pagkalugi. Maaari ring gamitin sa metaporikal na paraan para sa pagkawala ng isang pagkakataon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nalulugi** na ang tindahan ni Aling Nena dahil sa sunod-sunod na pagtaas ng presyo ng bilihin.","translation":"Aling Nena's store is **incurring losses** due to the continuous increase in the price of goods."},{"sentence":"Kung palagi kang huli sa trabaho, **nalulugi** ka sa sahod at sa tiwala ng iyong amo.","translation":"If you're always late for work, you're **losing out** on salary and your boss's trust."}]

meaning_filipino: Tuntungan o ilagay ang paa sa ibabaw ng isang bagay, lugar, o tao.
original_explanation: Literally, to step on something. Figuratively, it's what you feel your boss is doing to your dignity, or what happens in a crowded MRT train during rush hour. 'Huwag mo akong apakan' can mean 'Don't step on my shoes' or 'Don't undermine me.' Context is key.
usage_notes: Can be used both literally (to step on a physical object) and figuratively (to oppress or demean someone).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, huwag mong **apakan** ang bagong linis na sahig.","translation":"Please, do not **step on** the newly cleaned floor."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman niyang **inaapakan** na ang kanyang karapatan bilang manggagawa.","translation":"He felt that his rights as a worker were being **stepped on**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbabawas, pagtatanggal ng bahagi mula sa isang kabuuan, o paglilipat ng karga.
etymology: From `pag-` (gerund prefix) + `a` (euphonic liaison) + `awas` (to deduct, to unload).
original_explanation: This is what happens to your sahod on payday: may pag-aawas for SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, and tax. It's also the term for unloading goods from a truck, or when the jeepney conductor yells "May bababa ba?" to make space. It's basically "making less" of something, whether it's your take-home pay or the number of people in a vehicle.
usage_notes: Can refer to financial deductions, physical unloading of cargo, or reduction in quantity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang **pag-aawas** sa sahod niya dahil sa mga utang.","translation":"The **deduction** from his salary was large because of his debts."},{"sentence":"Sinimulan na ng mga trabahador ang **pag-aawas** ng semento mula sa trak.","translation":"The workers have started the **unloading** of cement from the truck."}]

meaning_filipino: Inilalarawan ang isang tao na labis na masunurin at walang sariling pag-iisip o paninindigan, na sumusunod na lamang sa lahat ng utos o nais ng iba.
original_explanation: This is the "yes man" of the group. Yung kaibigan mong "under de saya" or yung officemate na kahit anong ipagawa ng boss, kahit di na job description niya, go lang nang go. To be **sunud-sunuran** is to lack a backbone, to be a puppet. It's cute if it's a loyal dog, not so much in a person.
usage_notes: Carries a slightly negative connotation, implying a lack of personal will.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **sunud-sunuran** sa lahat ng gusto niya; magkaroon ka ng sariling desisyon.","translation":"Don't be **blindly obedient** to everything he wants; have your own decisions."},{"sentence":"Tinatawag siyang **sunud-sunuran** dahil hindi siya marunong tumanggi.","translation":"He is called a **pushover** because he doesn't know how to say no."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit na pag-ikot o pagparoo't parito sa isang partikular na lugar o sa paligid ng isang tao, na kadalasan ay may hinihintay o binabantayan.
original_explanation: Like a foodpanda driver waiting for the customer to come down, or that suitor who's always 'coincidentally' in the same places you are. It’s also what flies do to your plate of sinigang.
usage_notes: The root 'aligid' means 'around' or 'surrounding'. The repetition 'ali-aligid' emphasizes a persistent, circling, or loitering motion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kanina pa **umali-aligid** ang aso sa lamesa, nag-aabang ng pagkain.","translation":"The dog has been **hovering around** the table for a while, waiting for food."},{"sentence":"Bakit ka ba **umali-aligid** sa akin? May kailangan ka ba?","translation":"Why are you **hovering around** me? Do you need something?"}]

translation: To soothe; to stop someone from crying
meaning_filipino: Patigilin sa pag-iyak o paggawa ng isang bagay, karaniwang sa pamamagitan ng pag-alo o pagbibigay ng atensyon.
original_explanation: This is what you do when your pamangkin starts a dramatic performance in the middle of the mall. You give them a toy, some candy, or the good old 'para kang kiti-kiti' stare to make them stop. The verb form of 'shhh, tahan na.'
usage_notes: Often used in the context of pacifying a crying child or stopping a tantrum. 'Itihin' is a common alternative spelling/pronunciation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **itiin** ang sanggol sa pamamagitan ng isang kanta.","translation":"She tried to **soothe** the baby with a song."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matinding alab o apoy na mabilis ding mamatay o mawala, tulad ng pagkasunog ng tuyong bao ng niyog.
original_explanation: This is the slightly more intense, but equally short-lived, cousin of 'ningas-kugon'. Think of the flame from a burning coconut husk ('bao'): it flares up BRIGHTLY and intensely, then poof, it's gone. It describes a passion or anger that is fierce and furious but burns out very quickly. Like a Twitter war that's all the rage for an hour and then completely forgotten.
usage_notes: Similar to 'ningas-kugon' but implies a more intense, rather than just a quick-starting, flame. Often used to describe anger or a sudden, fierce but temporary burst of effort.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang galit niya ay parang **ningas-bao**, malakas sa simula pero madaling humupa.","translation":"His anger is like a **strong but short-lived flame**, intense at the start but easily subsides."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, **ningas-bao** lang 'yan. Bukas, bati na ulit kayo.","translation":"Don't worry, that's just a **flash in the pan**. You'll be friends again tomorrow."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibirong may kasamang panunukso o pang-aasar, karaniwan ay sa isang mapagkaibigang paraan ngunit maaaring maging sanhi ng inis.
etymology: From Hokkien 姦譙 (kàn-kiāu), meaning "to curse" or "to scold vehemently," but has evolved in Tagalog to a lighter sense of teasing.
original_explanation: This is the national sport of Filipino *barkadas*. It's that friendly (or sometimes not-so-friendly) teasing you get when you finally show up with a "special someone" or when you trip on a flat surface. "Uy, 'di na-inform!" is a classic *kantiyaw* opening. It's the sound of your friends lovingly roasting you.
usage_notes: Often done in a group setting, like during sports games or friendly gatherings. It's a form of social bonding, but can cross the line into bullying if not careful.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi na niya pinansin ang **kantiyaw** ng mga kaibigan niya tungkol sa bago niyang gupit.","translation":"He ignored his friends' **heckling** about his new haircut."},{"sentence":"Napuno na siya sa walang tigil na **kantiyaw** kaya umalis na lang siya.","translation":"He got fed up with the relentless **teasing**, so he just left."}]

translation: irritant; provocateur; something that causes anger
meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, salita, o kilos na nagiging sanhi ng matinding galit o pagkainis sa isang tao.
original_explanation: Ito yung ka-opisina mong panay ang 'for compliance' sa email kahit 5 PM na ng Biyernes. Yung classmate na nagpapaalala sa teacher na may homework. Basically, anything or anyone that activates your inner beast mode. Sila ang panggagalit sa payapa mong buhay.
usage_notes: Can refer to a person, an object, or an action that causes anger or irritation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ingay ng kapitbahay tuwing madaling araw ay isang tunay na **panggagalit**.","translation":"The neighbor's noise at dawn is a real **irritant**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **panggagalit** sa usapan.","translation":"Don't be a **provocateur** in the discussion."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa may pinakamatinding kalagayan ng karukhaan o kawalan ng yaman at mga pangunahing pangangailangan.
original_explanation: This refers to the most financially vulnerable in a community. The family with the least access to resources, opportunities, and basic needs. It’s a serious term used in socio-economic discussions, a far cry from just being 'broke' before payday.
usage_notes: Refers to a state of poverty. To be more specific and formal, 'pinakadukha' or 'pinakamaralita' are often used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang gobyerno ay may programa para tulungan ang mga pamilyang kabilang sa **pinakamahirap** na sektor ng lipunan.","translation":"The government has a program to help families belonging to the **poorest** sector of society."},{"sentence":"Sila ang itinuturing na **pinakamahirap** na komunidad sa buong rehiyon.","translation":"They are considered the **poorest** community in the entire region."}]

translation: to do a sideline job, to hustle
meaning_filipino: Gumawa ng mga karagdagang trabaho o paraan upang kumita ng pera sa labas ng pangunahing hanapbuhay.
etymology: Tagalog na anyong pandiwa ng salitang Ingles na "racket" (sa konteksto ng sideline o trabaho).
original_explanation: The verb form of 'diskarte'. It's selling baked goods at the office, doing freelance graphic design after your 9-to-5, or driving for a ride-sharing app on weekends. It's the Filipino spirit of finding extra income streams because, let's be real, the bills won't pay themselves. The hustle is real!
usage_notes: Isang salitang balbal o kolokyal. Nagmula sa salitang Ingles na "racket" ngunit may positibong konotasyon sa Pilipinas, na tumutukoy sa mga lehitimong sideline.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **manraket** para sa pambayad ng tuition fee ng kapatid ko.","translation":"I need **to do a sideline job** to pay for my sibling's tuition fee."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **manraket** tuwing bakasyon para may extra siyang pera.","translation":"He likes **to hustle** during vacations to have extra money."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng ulam na gawa sa giniling na baboy o manok na may mga hiniwang gulay, itlog, at pasas, na niluluto sa isang liyanera.
etymology: From Spanish 'jardinera,' which refers to a dish with a mix of garden vegetables ('a la jardinera' - garden style). This was applied to the meatloaf because of the colorful mixed vegetables inside.
original_explanation: That festive meatloaf you only see during fiestas, Christmas, or special occasions. It's cooked in an oval-shaped tin can (liyanera), packed with pork, carrots, peas, and raisins, then topped with a slice of hard-boiled egg. It's basically the more 'extra' cousin of embutido. The Lucban, Quezon version is legendary.
usage_notes: A well-known dish, especially from the Quezon province. Often mistaken for embutido, but hardinera is typically steamed then fried, while embutido is usually just steamed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sarap ng luto niyang **hardinera**; paborito ko tuwing Pasko.","translation":"Her **hardinera** is delicious; it's my favorite every Christmas."},{"sentence":"Nag-uwi siya ng dalawang liyanerang **hardinera** mula sa Lucban.","translation":"He brought home two tins of **hardinera** from Lucban."}]

translation: To work hard for something; to suffer for something
meaning_filipino: Ang pagdanas ng hirap, pagod, o sakripisyo upang makamit o makuha ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of 'no pain, no gain.' It’s what your parents tell you they did to send you to school. It's the blood, sweat, and tears you pour into a project, a goal, or even a relationship. It's the 'hugot' behind every success story. 'Lahat ng ito, pinaghirapan at pinagpuyatan ko!' is the battle cry.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **pagsakitan** ang iyong mga pangarap.","translation":"You need to **work hard for** your dreams."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong balewalain ang bahay na ito; **pinagsakitan** iyan ng mga magulang mo.","translation":"Don't take this house for granted; your parents **suffered to acquire** it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kulisap na may mahabang katawan, malalaking mga mata, at dalawang pares ng malinaw na pakpak. Karaniwang matatagpuan malapit sa anyong tubig.
etymology: Isang varyant ng salitang 'tutubi'. Ang unlaping 'hin-' ay hindi karaniwan at maaaring nagmula sa isang rehiyonal na diyalekto o mas lumang anyo ng wika.
original_explanation: The OG drone. That helicopter-looking bug that zips around ponds and sometimes your laundry line. Kids used to catch these for fun, which is probably why we have trust issues now. A more poetic, less common version of 'tutubi'.
usage_notes: Madalas na ipinagpapalit sa 'tutubi', bagaman mas karaniwan ang 'tutubi' sa modernong pananalita. Ang 'hintutubi' ay maaaring ituring na mas makaluma o pampanitikan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga makukulay na **hintutubi** ay nagliliparan sa ibabaw ng sapa.","translation":"The colorful **dragonflies** are flying over the creek."},{"sentence":"Nahuli niya ang isang asul na **hintutubi** gamit ang kaniyang kamay.","translation":"He caught a blue **dragonfly** with his hand."}]

translation: to trust; to have faith in
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng tiwala o pananampalataya sa isang tao, bagay, o ideya.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you give your phone to a friend to take a picture, hoping they don't scroll through your messages. It's giving your heart to someone and praying they don't break it (spoiler: sometimes they do, #hugot). It's the foundation of any relationship, from your suking tindera to your jowa. "Mahirap magkatiwala ulit pagkatapos masaktan."
usage_notes: Often used with "sa" (in/to). `Magtiwala` is a more common synonym. `Magkatiwala` can sometimes imply a mutual or reciprocal trust, but it is often used interchangeably with `magtiwala`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magkatiwala** sa iyong sariling kakayahan.","translation":"You need **to trust** in your own abilities."},{"sentence":"**Nagkatiwala** ako sa kanya ng aking mga sikreto.","translation":"I **entrusted** my secrets to him/her."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na walang paniniwala o tiwala, lalo na sa isang mas mataas na kapangyarihan o Diyos. Maaari ring tumukoy sa kawalan ng tiwala sa isang tao, ideya, o sistema.
original_explanation: This can mean two things. First, someone who is an atheist or agnostic—they have **no religious faith**. Second, and more commonly in a 'hugot' way, it's someone who has lost all trust, maybe in 'forever' or in the government. Sila yung tipo na, 'Huwag ka nang umasa, masasaktan ka lang.' They are **unbelieving** not just in a god, but in promises.
usage_notes: Maaaring partikular na tumukoy sa kawalan ng pananampalataya sa relihiyon (ateismo/agnostisismo) o sa mas pangkalahatang kawalan ng tiwala o paniniwala sa isang bagay o tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa sunod-sunod na kabiguan, siya ay naging isang taong **walang-pananampalataya** sa pag-ibig.","translation":"Because of successive heartbreaks, she became a person who was **faithless** in love."},{"sentence":"May mga taong pinipili ang landas na **walang-pananampalataya** sa anumang relihiyon.","translation":"There are people who choose the path of being **unbelieving** in any religion."}]

meaning_filipino: Inilalarawan ang isang ibabaw na hindi pantay, na may maraming lubak, butas, o marka, tulad ng mukhang may pekas ng bulutong o kalsadang sira-sira.
original_explanation: This describes a surface that looks like the moon, but not in a romantic way. Think of Metro Manila roads after a rainy season, or a face that lost a battle with teenage acne. It's uneven, full of craters, and generally a rough ride. It's the opposite of "flawless."
usage_notes: The word 'lipak' by itself means a pockmark or depression. The repetition 'lipak-lipak' emphasizes the multiplicity of these marks.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **lipak-lipak** ang mukha niya dahil sa tigdas.","translation":"His face became **pockmarked** because of measles."},{"sentence":"Mahirap magmaneho sa daang **lipak-lipak** at lubak-lubak.","translation":"It's hard to drive on a road that is **full of depressions** and potholes."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapakita o pagpapamalas ng isang bagay; paglitaw o paglantad.
etymology: From pa- (causative prefix) + kita (see). Literally 'to make see'.
original_explanation: This word has two main vibes. Vibe 1: 'Show me.' Like when you get a new phone and your friend says, 'Pakita!' Vibe 2: 'To make an appearance.' This is what ghosts do ('nagpakita'), or what your crush does when they finally show up to the party, making your heart stop. It's the verb for revealing something, whether it's a new tattoo or a supernatural entity.
usage_notes: Can be a command ('Pakita mo!') or a statement ('Nagpakita siya'). The verb form changes with focus: magpakita (to show), ipakita (to show something), pakitaan (to show to someone).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pakita** mo sa akin ang bago mong sapatos.","translation":"**Show** me your new shoes."},{"sentence":"Bigla siyang nag**pakita** sa party kagabi.","translation":"He suddenly **appeared** at the party last night."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-atras o pagbawi sa isang naunang sinabi, ginawa, o posisyon. Maaari ring tumukoy sa pisikal na pag-atras.
original_explanation: That awkward moment when you say something then immediately wish you could un-say it. It's the verbal equivalent of hitting 'undo'. Also applies to promises ('urong-sulong' means indecisive) or when a turtle pulls its head back into its shell. 'Bigla siyang nag-urong sa kasunduan.'
usage_notes: Often used in the context of decisions, statements, or legal cases. The phrase 'urong-sulong' (indecisive) is derived from this meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napilitan siyang **mag-urong** ng kanyang kandidatura.","translation":"He was forced to **withdraw** his candidacy."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mag-urong** sa iyong mga ipinangako.","translation":"Do not **go back on** your promises."}]

translation: very pretty in one's own eyes; conceited
meaning_filipino: Pagdadaglat para sa "gandang-ganda sa sarili." Tumutukoy sa isang tao na labis ang paghanga sa sariling itsura o hitsura, na maaaring totoo o biro lamang.
etymology: Acronym ng pariralang Tagalog na "gandang-ganda sa sarili".
original_explanation: Acronym for "Gandang-Ganda Sa Sarili." That feeling you get after taking the perfect selfie on the 178th try. You post it with the caption #GGSS. It's celebrating self-love, sometimes with a hint of "I know, I'm fabulous, you don't have to tell me." Can be used as a compliment or a lighthearted insult.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa social media at sa mga biruan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-post siya ng selfie na may caption na '**GGSS**'.","translation":"She posted a selfie with the caption '**GGSS**'."},{"sentence":"Feeling **GGSS** ako ngayon dahil sa bago kong gupit.","translation":"I'm feeling **very pretty in my own eyes** today because of my new haircut."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na pagtatanghal o paglalaban-laban ng galing, kaalaman, o kakayahan, karaniwang may mga hurado at premyo.
original_explanation: The national pastime. From barangay beauty pageants to 'birit' singing contests on noontime shows, Filipinos love a good 'timpalak'. It's where you prove your 'galing' and hope to win some cash prize or at least a sack of rice.
usage_notes: Madalas na ipinagpapalit sa 'paligsahan' o 'kompetisyon'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumali siya sa **timpalak** sa pag-awit sa kanilang piyesta.","translation":"She joined the singing **contest** at their fiesta."},{"sentence":"Ang premyo para sa mananalo sa **timpalak** sa pagtula ay isang tropeo at sampung libong piso.","translation":"The prize for the winner of the poetry **competition** is a trophy and ten thousand pesos."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o tindahan kung saan nagbebenta ng mga segunda-manong damit, sapatos, at iba pang gamit.
original_explanation: The battlefield. The treasure island. The place where your patience, hygiene standards, and allergic rhinitis are all put to the test. It can be a cramped stall in Baguio or a multi-story air-conditioned building in the city, but the mission is always the same: find the gold.
usage_notes: Can refer to a single stall or a whole building full of thrift shops.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumunta kami sa **ukayan** sa Cubao para maghanap ng mga murang pantalon.","translation":"We went to the **thrift store area** in Cubao to look for cheap pants."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging nakalantad sa init, gaya ng sa apoy o sikat ng araw, o sa hangin upang matuyo.
original_explanation: Like a barbecue skewer being cooked over hot coals, or your laundry hanging on the line under the scorching noon sun. It's being directly exposed to the elements, usually heat or air. Also, how you feel when you have to present your report first thing in the morning with no coffee.
usage_notes: Can mean exposed to heat (like fire) or exposed to air/sun for drying.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iniwan niyang **nakayangyang** sa araw ang basang sapatos para matuyo agad.","translation":"He left the wet shoes **aired out** in the sun to dry quickly."},{"sentence":"Ang lechon ay dahan-dahang iniikot habang **nakayangyang** sa nagbabagang uling.","translation":"The roasted pig is slowly turned while **exposed to the heat** of the glowing embers."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa dalawa o higit pang bagay, ideya, o salita na may pagtutugma, pagkakatulad, o pag-aangkop sa isa't isa.
etymology: From `mag-` (prefix indicating relationship/reciprocity) + `ka-` (prefix indicating being part of a pair/group) + `ugma` (rhyme, harmony).
original_explanation: Yung para kayong perfect couple, lahat ng trip n'yo, same. Mula sa paboritong kape hanggang sa ayaw n'yong politiko, swak na swak. Sa tula, ito 'yung mga salitang may parehong tunog sa dulo, parang jingle ng Shopee.
usage_notes: Often used in literary contexts for rhyming words, or in relationships to describe compatibility.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga salitang \"mahal\" at \"araw\" ay hindi **magkakaugma** sa isang tula.","translation":"The words \"love\" and \"sun\" do not **rhyme** in a poem."},{"sentence":"Buti pa sila, **magkakaugma** ang mga ugali kaya hindi nag-aaway.","translation":"Good for them, their personalities are **compatible** so they don't fight."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sona sa kalangitan na hinahati sa labindalawang bahagi, na ang bawat isa ay may pangalan ng konstelasyon at simbolo, na pinaniniwalaang nakakaimpluwensya sa kapalaran ng tao.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Ingles na "zodiac", na isina-Tagalog ang baybay.
original_explanation: Your cosmic alibi for your toxic traits. "Sorry, Scorpio ako eh" is the new "Ganon talaga ako." Ito yung dahilan kung bakit ka nagbabasa ng horoscope sa dyaryo o sa Co-Star app, hoping the universe will tell you na yayaman ka na o makikita mo na si The One. Ang sodyak ang go-to topic 'pag naubusan na ng chismis.
usage_notes: Karaniwang baybay sa Tagalog para sa "zodiac".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **sodyak** sign mo? Ako ay isang Leo.","translation":"What's your **zodiac** sign? I'm a Leo."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong maniwala sa sinasabi ng iyong **sodyak**.","translation":"Don't believe too much in what your **zodiac** says."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng malaking paggalang, pagpapahalaga, at tamang asal sa kapwa, lalo na sa mga nakatatanda o may awtoridad.
original_explanation: The ideal 'apo' or grandchild. This is the kid who always says 'po' and 'opo', does the 'mano po', and doesn't talk back to their lola. It's being respectful to the highest level. In modern terms, it's not looking at your phone while someone's talking to you. It's a trait that's becoming a rare Pokémon.
usage_notes: A formal word for respectful. 'Magalang' is the more common, everyday equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Manatili tayong **mapitagan** sa loob ng simbahan.","translation":"Let us remain **reverent** inside the church."},{"sentence":"Isang **mapitagan** na pagbati ang iginawad niya sa mga panauhing pandangal.","translation":"He gave a **respectful** greeting to the guests of honor."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maliit na isdang-alat, na karaniwang pinapatuyo, inaasinan, o ginagawang bagoong.
original_explanation: The unsung hero of the Filipino breakfast table. That small, crispy, salty fish that's perfect with sinangag (garlic fried rice) and a fried egg. Also a great "pulutan" when fried and coated in a sweet and spicy sauce. Don't underestimate its power!
usage_notes: Refers to the fish, which can be fresh, dried (tuyo), or fermented (bagoong).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito niyang almusal ang pritong **dilis** na may sukang maanghang.","translation":"His favorite breakfast is fried **anchovies** with spicy vinegar."},{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng isang kilong sariwang **dilis** sa palengke.","translation":"Mom bought a kilo of fresh **anchovies** at the market."}]

translation: to be able to overcome; to be able to surpass
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang lampasan, talunin, o higitan ang isang tao, bagay, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na na-promote ka at tinalo mo 'yung office rival mo. Nakadaig ka, bes! O 'yung moment na you finally overcome a personal struggle. You didn't just survive, you conquered. 'Yan ang **makadaig**.
usage_notes: The 'maka-' prefix indicates the ability to perform the action of 'daig' (to surpass, to beat). It implies overcoming a challenge or besting a competitor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Walang problemang hindi mo kayang **makadaig** kung magsisikap ka.","translation":"There is no problem you won't **be able to overcome** if you persevere."},{"sentence":"Sa paligsahan, sino kaya ang **makadaig** sa kasalukuyang kampeon?","translation":"In the competition, who will **be able to surpass** the current champion?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagdiin o paghawak nang mahigpit gamit ang mga daliri.
original_explanation: That gentle squeeze your tita gives your cheeks when she says "Ang laki mo na, iho/iha!" Can also be the angry squeeze you give a stress ball when your internet connection dies mid-meeting. It's a versatile action, from affection to frustration.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang mahigpit na **pisil** sa kamay ang ibinigay niya bilang tanda ng suporta.","translation":"She gave a tight **squeeze** on the hand as a sign of support."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gusali na nag-aalok ng upahang kuwarto, at kung minsan ay pagkain, para sa mga nangungupahan o estudyante.
etymology: From "bahay" (house) + "pang-asera" (for renting/boarding) + "-han" (place suffix). The root "kasera" (landlady) comes from Spanish 'casera'.
original_explanation: The 'starter pack' for adulting. It's where you learn to live with strangers, budget your allowance, and discover that instant noodles are a valid food group. The landlady is the final boss, and 'lights out' is a real rule. Think of it as a pre-condo, post-parents' house phase of life.
usage_notes: Synonymous with the more common loanword "boarding house" or the simpler term "paupahan".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatira siya sa isang **bahay-pangaserahan** na malapit sa unibersidad.","translation":"She lives in a **boarding house** near the university."}]

translation: to hit; to strike; to criticize
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtama, pagpalo, o pagpukol nang malakas sa isang bagay o tao; maaari ring tumukoy sa matinding pagpuna o pag-atake sa salita.
etymology: From Spanish 'virar' (to turn, tack). The meaning has shifted significantly in Tagalog to mean 'hit' or 'strike'.
original_explanation: This word has layers. On one hand, it's literally 'to hit,' like in a boxing match. But more often, you'll hear it used to mean 'to roast' or 'to drag' someone online. When a politician gets called out for their mistakes, 'binibira sila ng netizens.' It's to attack, either with your fists or with your savage words.
usage_notes: Can be literal (physical) or figurative (verbal/written criticism).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **birahin** ang pinto, masisira iyan!","translation":"Don't **slam** the door, it will break!"},{"sentence":"Laging **binibira** ng mga kritiko ang bagong pelikula.","translation":"The new movie is always being **hit** by critics."},{"sentence":"**Birahin** mo nang malakas ang bola!","translation":"**Hit** the ball hard!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maranasan o pagdaanan ang isang partikular na pangyayari, damdamin, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: 'Yung nangyari sa'yo na naging "learning experience" o "character development" ang peg. Pwedeng good (ma-promote sa work) o bad (ma-ghost ng ka-talking stage).
usage_notes: A common verb derived from the loanword 'eksperyensya' (experience).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana hindi mo **maeksperyensya** ang matraffic sa EDSA nang limang oras.","translation":"I hope you don't **experience** being stuck in traffic on EDSA for five hours."},{"sentence":"Masarap **maeksperyensya** ang buhay sa probinsya.","translation":"It's nice **to experience** life in the province."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi gumagalaw, matatag, o permanente sa isang posisyon o kalagayan; itinakda at hindi na mababago.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung presyo ng bilihin na may "fixed price" na sticker, 'di na pwedeng tawaran. Or 'yung status mo sa friendzone, for life na. Your salary after tax and deductions feels nakapirme, no matter how much you want it to grow.
usage_notes: Often used for prices, positions, or things that are not moving. A variant of 'nakapirmi'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakapirme** na ang presyo ng bigas sa palengke ngayong linggo.","translation":"The price of rice in the market is now **fixed** for this week."},{"sentence":"Ang mga poste ng ilaw ay **nakapirme** sa gilid ng kalsada.","translation":"The light posts are **stationary** on the side of the road."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang magpigil sa sarili; pagiging katamtaman at hindi labis sa kilos, pananalita, o pag-uugali.
original_explanation: This is the superpower you need during a 12.12 sale. It's saying 'no' to that third cup of milk tea or stopping yourself from sending that 'kainis ka' text at 2 AM. **Katimpian** is the adulting skill of choosing 'add to wishlist' instead of 'buy now.' It's your inner voice whispering 'hinay-hinay lang, bes.'
usage_notes: A virtue related to controlling one's desires, emotions, and actions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipakita mo ang **katimpian** sa harap ng tukso.","translation":"Show **self-control** in the face of temptation."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang pagsasalita ay may **katimpian** at paggalang.","translation":"His/Her speech has **moderation** and respect."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mga materyales, impormasyon, at ideya na bumubuo sa isang akda, publikasyon, o anumang anyo ng midya tulad ng website, video, o social media post.
original_explanation: The new 'raket'. Ito 'yung mga video, picture, at article na ini-scroll mo buong araw. From TikTok dance challenges to 'unboxing' videos to political vlogs, it's all content. Kung may camera ka at opinyon, pwede ka nang maging 'content creator'.
usage_notes: Isang modernong paggamit ng salita na sumikat dahil sa internet at social media. Ang taong gumagawa nito ay tinatawag na 'content creator'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang paggawa ng de-kalidad na **content** para dumami ang iyong followers.","translation":"Creating high-quality **content** is important to grow your followers."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang YouTube channel ay may iba't ibang uri ng **content**, mula sa pagluluto hanggang sa paglalakbay.","translation":"Her YouTube channel has various types of **content**, from cooking to travel."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matinding pagnanais o layunin na makamit ang isang bagay; mithiin.
original_explanation: This is your #goals in life. Your "Sana next year, nasa Japan na ako" or "Sana ma-promote na ako." It’s the thing you daydream about during a boring meeting. It’s the fuel for your hustle, the reason you drink kapeng matapang para ipaglaban ang pangarap mong matamis.
usage_notes: Often used in the verb form 'hangarin' (to desire something) or as 'kahangaran' (the object of desire).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tanging **hangad** niya ay magkaroon ng mapayapang buhay.","translation":"His only **desire** is to have a peaceful life."},{"sentence":"Mataas ang **hangad** ng mga magulang para sa kanilang mga anak.","translation":"Parents have high **aspirations** for their children."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay, konsepto, o lugar na banal, puro, at hindi dapat lapastanganin o yurakan.
etymology: Possibly from Sanskrit `vatsala` (affectionate), but the semantic shift is significant. Its origin is debated among linguists.
original_explanation: This is a deep cut. Think of it as the original "do not touch." It’s not just clean, it's spiritually, conceptually clean. A virgin forest can be basal. A sacred ground is basal. It's the kind of word you'd find in old poems or a philosophy textbook, not in a group chat. It's the "premium, high-level, VIP" version of 'bawal'.
usage_notes: An archaic and literary term. Often used in contexts of religion, nature, or abstract principles like virginity or purity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinuturing na **basal** ang kabundukang iyon ng mga katutubo.","translation":"That mountain is considered **sacred** by the indigenous people."},{"sentence":"Ang pagiging birhen ay isang konseptong **basal** sa maraming kultura.","translation":"Virginity is a **sacred/inviolable** concept in many cultures."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kabuuan ng mga personal na gamit o kargamento na dinadala ng isang tao, lalo na sa paglalakbay.
original_explanation: This is your 'dala' (baggage) but on steroids. It's not just one bag; it's ALL your stuff. It's the balikbayan box, two maletas, a backpack, and a hand-carry. When someone says 'Ayusin mo na ang mga dala-dalahan mo,' they mean 'Pack all your worldly possessions, we're leaving.'
usage_notes: The reduplication implies a multitude or variety of items being carried, often in a slightly cumbersome way.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naiwan niya sa bus ang lahat ng kanyang **dala-dalahan**.","translation":"He left all his **belongings** on the bus."},{"sentence":"Tulungan mo si lola sa kanyang mga **dala-dalahan**.","translation":"Help grandma with her **luggage**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kemikal na elemento na karaniwang ginagamit bilang antiseptiko para sa mga sugat, na may kulay kayumanggi o mamula-mula.
original_explanation: The orange stuff your mom would put on your scraped knees that stung more than the actual fall. It was the original 'tiis-ganda' but for wounds. Seeing a bottle of this meant someone had a bad day on their bike. Modern equivalent is Betadine, which is basically branded yodo.
usage_notes: Often refers to povidone-iodine, the common brown antiseptic solution.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pahiran mo ng **yodo** 'yang sugat mo para hindi maimpeksyon.","translation":"Apply **iodine** to your wound so it doesn't get infected."},{"sentence":"May amoy ng **yodo** ang first-aid kit.","translation":"The first-aid kit smells like **iodine**."}]

translation: To crush; to pound into fine pieces.
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpino o pagdurog sa isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng paulit-ulit na pagpukpok o pagbayo, karaniwan gamit ang pandikdik o almires.
original_explanation: Think of your lola in the kitchen with her mortar and pestle (almires), *dinidikdik* yung bawang at paminta. It's the process of turning something solid into powder or a paste through relentless pounding. In a figurative sense, it's what your prof does to a difficult topic—they *dinidikdik* it into your brain until you get it.
usage_notes: Often associated with cooking and preparing ingredients.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dumikdik** siya ng bawang para sa ginisang ulam.","translation":"He **crushed** garlic for the sauteed dish."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **dumikdik** ng mani para sa kare-kare.","translation":"You need to **pound** peanuts for the kare-kare."}]

translation: to know very well; fully aware
meaning_filipino: Lubos na nauunawaan o batid; may ganap na kaalaman sa isang bagay o paksa.
etymology: From Tagalog "alam" (know), reduplicated with "na" for emphasis.
original_explanation: This is when you know something so well, it's practically tattooed on your brain. Like when your friend asks, "Sure ka na ba sa desisyon mo?" and you reply, "Alam na alam ko na 'to, besh. I've run the numbers, consulted the stars, and overthought this for three straight nights." It's knowing something with the certainty of a marites finding the latest chismis.
usage_notes: The repetition of 'alam' emphasizes certainty and complete, unquestionable knowledge. It's stronger than just saying 'alam ko'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Alam na alam** niya ang pasikot-sikot sa Divisoria kaya hindi sila naligaw.","translation":"She **knows very well** the ins and outs of Divisoria, which is why they didn't get lost."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong subukang utuin, **alam na alam** ko ang mga palusot mo.","translation":"Don't try to fool me, I **know your excuses very well**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kabuuang halaga o timbang bago bawasan ang anumang kaltas (tulad ng buwis o tara). Maaari ding tumukoy sa isang taong magaspang ang pag-uugali.
original_explanation: This is a two-for-one deal from Spanish. First, it's your 'bruto' salary – the big number on your payslip before PhilHealth, SSS, Pag-IBIG, and tax come for their share, leaving you with the 'net' which is just enough for milk tea. Second, it's that guy who cuts in line, doesn't say 'excuse me', and generally acts like a caveman. A 'brute'.
usage_notes: The context determines the meaning. 'Brutong sahod' (gross salary) vs. 'Ang bruto mo naman!' (You're such a brute!). It can function as both a noun and an adjective.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **bruto** niyang kita ay isang daang libong piso, ngunit ang net ay mas mababa.","translation":"His **gross** income is one hundred thousand pesos, but the net is lower."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **bruto** sa pakikitungo sa mga babae.","translation":"Don't be a **brute** when dealing with women."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa direksyon ng isang lugar, kalagayan, o layunin.
original_explanation: This is your Waze or Google Maps status. 'Patungo na ako,' you text your friend, even if you're still just getting out of the shower. It signifies movement in a specific direction, whether it's towards your office, your favorite milk tea place, or your 'one great love.'
usage_notes: Often followed by 'sa' to indicate the destination (e.g., patungo sa Maynila).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bus ay **patungo** sa Cubao.","translation":"The bus is **heading towards** Cubao."},{"sentence":"Saan ka **patungo** pagkatapos ng trabaho?","translation":"Where are you **going to** after work?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng parehong pangalan ng dalawa o higit pang tao, lugar, o bagay.
original_explanation: That awkward moment in class when the teacher calls 'John!' and three people look up. That means `magkapangalan` sila. It's the reason why some people get nicknames like 'Junior,' 'Baby,' or get called by their last name. It's the universe's way of creating minor identity crises in group settings.
usage_notes: The adjective form is 'kapangalan' (namesake). 'Magkapangalan' is the verb form describing the state of sharing a name. 'Tokayo' is the colloquial term for a person with the same name.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Aksidenteng **nagkapangalan** ang magkaibigan.","translation":"The two friends coincidentally **have the same name**."},{"sentence":"Hindi na ako nagulat na **magkapangalan** sila; popular ang pangalang iyon noong dekada '90.","translation":"I wasn't surprised they **have the same name**; that name was popular in the '90s."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang serbisyo ng paghahanda at paghahatid ng pagkain para sa isang partikular na kaganapan, pagtitipon, o institusyon.
original_explanation: Essential sa bawat handaan—mula binyag hanggang lamay. Sila ang dahilan kung bakit may masarap na buffet at may bitbit ka pang naka-styro na 'take-out' pag-uwi. Ang tunay na MVP ng mga party na ayaw mong magluto.
usage_notes: Ginagamit nang direkta sa mga usapang may kinalaman sa pag-organisa ng mga event at pagdiriwang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkano ang pakete ng **catering** para sa 100 na tao?","translation":"How much is the **catering** package for 100 people?"},{"sentence":"Masarap ang pagkain sa **catering** na kinuha nila para sa kasal.","translation":"The food from the **catering** they got for the wedding is delicious."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang kalagayan na walang hirap, sagabal, o alalahanin; nagdudulot ng kaginhawahan sa katawan, isipan, o pamumuhay.
etymology: From the prefix `ma-` (indicating a quality) and the root `ginhawa` (comfort, ease, relief).
original_explanation: The opposite of "siksikan sa MRT." It's that feeling of having enough space, money, and peace of mind. A `maginhawa` life is the #SanaAll goal: no financial stress, a comfy home, and a stable internet connection. It's the sigh of relief you let out when you finally sit down after a long day.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical comfort (like a soft chair), a state of life (well-off), or convenience (an easy process).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas **maginhawa** ang biyahe kung hindi siksikan sa bus.","translation":"The trip is more **comfortable** if the bus is not crowded."},{"sentence":"Nagsisikap siya para magkaroon ng **maginhawang** buhay ang kanyang pamilya.","translation":"He is working hard so his family can have a **comfortable** (well-off) life."}]

translation: act of gaping or staring blankly
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging nakatingin sa isang bagay o direksyon nang walang imik at malayo ang isip.
original_explanation: Your face when the screen freezes during a Zoom presentation and the boss is calling your name. It's the default expression when you see the total on the grocery bill. The official state of being 'shookt'.
usage_notes: Often carries a slightly negative or comical connotation of being idle or clueless.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itigil mo na ang **pagtunganga** diyan at tulungan mo ako.","translation":"Stop **gaping blankly** there and help me."},{"sentence":"Napansin ng guro ang kanyang **pagtunganga** sa klase.","translation":"The teacher noticed his **staring blankly** in class."}]

translation: to rush something; to be the subject of a rush
meaning_filipino: Gawin o tapusin ang isang bagay sa paraang apurado o mabilis; mag-unahan sa pagkuha o pagpunta sa isang bagay o lugar.
etymology: From pag- + the first syllable of mag- (ma-) + mag- + dali (hurry) + -an.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of the Manila commute. It's what you do to your report when the deadline is in an hour. 'Uy, pagmamadalian na natin 'to, malapit na ang cut-off!' It's the art of cramming, perfected by Filipino students and office workers alike.
usage_notes: This is the verb form, indicating the action of rushing something. It can also mean a place or thing becomes the focus of a rush (e.g., 'pinagmadalian ang buffet table').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag nating **pagmamadalian** ang proyektong ito para masigurong maganda ang kalalabasan.","translation":"Let's not **rush** this project to ensure a good outcome."},{"sentence":"Laging **pinagmamadalian** ang mga huling upuan sa bus.","translation":"The last seats on the bus are always **rushed for**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpalo o paghampas sa mukha gamit ang bukas na palad.
original_explanation: The ultimate teleserye confrontation move. "How dare you!" *pak!* That's *sumampal*. It’s the physical manifestation of "you crossed the line." It's more dramatic than blocking someone on social media and delivers a much clearer message.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to a slap on the face.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa galit niya, hindi niya napigilang **sumampal**.","translation":"In her anger, she couldn't stop herself from **slapping** (him/her)."},{"sentence":"Parang gusto kong **sumampal** ng katotohanan sa mga taong ayaw maniwala.","translation":"I feel like I want to **slap** some truth into people who refuse to believe."}]

meaning_filipino: May malinaw, mataas, at umaalingawngaw na tunog, tulad ng sa metal, barya, o kampana.
original_explanation: The sound of a perfectly tuned bell, a coin dropping on a tile floor, or the voice of a classical singer hitting that high note. It's the ASMR of clear, metallic sounds. The opposite of a muffled, 'kalabog' sound.
usage_notes: Describes a specific quality of sound, usually high-pitched, clear, and metallic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **mataginting** na tunog ng mga barya sa kanyang bulsa.","translation":"I heard the **ringing** sound of the coins in his pocket."},{"sentence":"May **mataginting** siyang boses na laging nangingibabaw sa koro.","translation":"She has a **sonorous** voice that always stands out in the choir."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kulay na mapusyaw na puti na may bahid ng dilaw, katulad ng kulay ng garing o pangil ng elepante.
original_explanation: This is the color of your tita's elegant furniture, the fancy wedding invitation you just received, or the classic Barong Tagalog. It's not quite white, not quite beige. It's the "old money" of colors – subtle, classic, and screams sophistication without being loud. It's the color you choose when you want to look clean but not as basic as pure white.
usage_notes: A compound adjective.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang damit pangkasal niya ay **kulay-garing**.","translation":"Her wedding dress is **ivory-colored**."},{"sentence":"Pininturahan nila ang mga pader ng **kulay-garing** para magmukhang maluwag.","translation":"They painted the walls **off-white** to make it look spacious."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian, kalikasan, o estado ng pagiging isang Diyos.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate level-up. It's the state of being God. In theology, it's a big deal, discussing the nature of Jesus's divinity. In everyday chat, you might use it sarcastically for someone who acts like they know everything and can do no wrong. 'Wow, ang taas ng tingin sa sarili, ramdam na ramdam ang pagka-Diyos.'
usage_notes: Primarily used in religious and theological contexts. Capitalization of 'Diyos' is important.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinaniniwalaan ng mga Kristiyano ang **pagka-Diyos** ni Hesus.","translation":"Christians believe in the **divinity** of Jesus."},{"sentence":"Ang debate tungkol sa **pagka-Diyos** ay isang malalim na teolohikal na usapin.","translation":"The debate about **godhood** is a deep theological issue."}]

meaning_filipino: Nakakaramdam ng inggit, pagdududa, o sama ng loob dahil sa takot na maagaw ang pagmamahal o atensyon ng isang tao.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung Tagalog term for 'jealous,' pero 'yung luma, classic version. 'Yung tipong nababasa mo sa mga lumang nobela o naririnig sa lola mo. Bago pa nauso ang 'sana all,' may 'huwag kang manibugho' at 'tigilan ang iyong pagka-selang' muna.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang mas pampanitikan o lumang termino. Ang mas karaniwang salita ngayon ay 'selos' o 'nagseselos'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **selang** na asawa ang ayaw na may ibang kumakausap sa kanyang kabiyak.","translation":"A **jealous** spouse does not want anyone else talking to their partner."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **selang** na pag-uugali, madalas silang mag-away.","translation":"Because of his **jealous** attitude, they often fight."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng ibon na mabilis lumipad, karaniwang may mahahabang pakpak na hugis-karit, at kumakain ng mga kulisap habang nasa himpapawid.
original_explanation: These are the fighter jets of the bird world. They're the ones you see doing crazy aerial acrobatics at sunset, probably catching their dinner (lamok) on the fly. They're so fast, parang naka-5G sa himpapawid.
usage_notes: Often seen in provinces, especially near fields or open water. The term is sometimes used interchangeably for swifts and swallows.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang gaganda ng mga **langaylangayan** na lumilipad tuwing dapit-hapon.","translation":"The **swallows** flying at dusk are so beautiful."},{"sentence":"Isang kawan ng **langaylangayan** ang dumaan sa ibabaw ng palayan.","translation":"A flock of **swifts** passed over the rice field."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na ipinagkakaloob bilang gantimpala para sa isang tagumpay, kahusayan, o pagkapanalo sa isang paligsahan.
original_explanation: The reason you join 'Bring Me' contests in office Christmas parties or suffer through a company raffle draw. It can be anything from a crisp 1000-peso bill to a branded rice cooker. 'Ano'ng **premyo** sa grand finals?' is the most important question for any Pinoy game show contestant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang nanalong kalahok ay tumanggap ng malaking **premyo** na salapi.","translation":"The winning participant received a huge cash **prize**."},{"sentence":"Pinapangarap niya ang grand **premyo** na kotse.","translation":"He dreams of the grand **prize**, which is a car."}]

meaning_filipino: Maranasan ang kapahamakan, sakuna, o anumang masamang pangyayari.
original_explanation: Ito yung state of being mo kapag nag-motor ka nang walang helmet tapos umuulan, o kaya nung nag-reply ka sa 'Hi/Hello' ng tropa mong scammer. It's when you're on the verge of getting into trouble or an accident. 'Delikado' pero with a hint of bad luck.
usage_notes: This is a potential verb form, indicating something bad might happen or has happened to the subject. Often used in warnings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa pag-uwi baka ka **mapanganyaya** sa daan.","translation":"Be careful on your way home, you might **be harmed** on the road."},{"sentence":"Marami ang **napanganyaya** dahil sa biglaang pagbaha.","translation":"Many **met with misfortune** because of the flash flood."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nabuhay sa kaparehong panahon o henerasyon ng isa pang tao.
original_explanation: Your lolo and the Beatles? They're 'kapanahon'. You and Taylor Swift? 'Kapanahon'. It's the term for people who shared the same timeline, breathed the same-ish air, and probably vibed to the same hit songs. It's basically the OG "same batch" but for an entire era.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun (a contemporary) or an adjective (contemporary with).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sina Jose Rizal at Andres Bonifacio ay mga bayaning **kapanahon**.","translation":"Jose Rizal and Andres Bonifacio are heroes who were **contemporaries**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga awiting ito ay sikat noong **kapanahon** ko.","translation":"These songs were popular during my **time/era**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o paghiling sa isang tao na basahin ang isang bagay para sa iba.
etymology: From the causative prefix `ipa-` and the root word `basa` (read).
original_explanation: That moment when you're too lazy to read a long text, a contract, or even the menu. You hand your phone to your friend and say, "Bes, **ipabasa** ko sa'yo, paki-summarize na lang." It's the ultimate delegation of reading duties, perfect for avoiding fine print or long, dramatic messages from an ex.
usage_notes: Used to command or request someone to read something aloud or on one's behalf.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ipabasa** mo sa abogado ang kontrata bago ka pumirma.","translation":"Have the lawyer **read** the contract before you sign."},{"sentence":"Puwede bang **ipabasa** sa iyo itong reseta? Hindi ko maintindihan ang sulat ng doktor.","translation":"Can I have you **read** this prescription? I can't understand the doctor's handwriting."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng baril na may mahabang kanyon at karaniwang nagpapaputok ng maraming maliliit na bala (pellets) nang sabay-sabay.
original_explanation: The weapon of choice for security guards at the mall, farmers scaring away pests, and action movie heroes making a grand entrance. It's the "bahala na kayong lahat" version of a firearm. Not for precision, but for making a big, loud statement.
usage_notes: Karaniwang tawag para sa ganitong uri ng baril.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May dalang **eskopeta** ang guwardiya sa bangko.","translation":"The guard at the bank is carrying a **shotgun**."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang **eskopeta** para itaboy ang mga ligaw na hayop.","translation":"He used the **shotgun** to drive away the wild animals."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang impormal na termino para sa isang apartment, bahay, o lugar kung saan ang isang tao ay naninirahan o madalas tumatambay.
etymology: Hango sa salitang Ingles na 'pad,' na slang para sa tirahan o apartment.
original_explanation: Your 'pad' is your personal space, your Batcave, your headquarters. It's the place you crash after a long day at work or a long night out. When a friend says, 'Tara sa pad ko,' it's an invitation to chill, play video games, watch Netflix, or just hang out without the formalities of a 'bahay.' It's your turf.
usage_notes: Lubos na impormal at karaniwan sa mga nakababatang henerasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May inuman mamaya sa **pad** ni Marco.","translation":"There's a drinking session later at Marco's **pad**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pandiwa ng paghuli, pagdakip, o pagsakop sa isang tao, bagay, o lugar.
original_explanation: Like when your mom "captures" your phone because you've been on TikTok for 5 hours straight. Or when the traffic enforcer "captures" your driver's license for a violation. It's the act of taking something (or someone) forcefully. In gaming, it's what you do to the enemy's flag.
usage_notes: Often used in its inflected forms like 'kinaptura' (captured), 'kakapturahin' (will capture).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais ng mga pulis na **kaptura**hin ang pugante bago ito makalayo.","translation":"The police want **to capture** the fugitive before he gets far."},{"sentence":"**Kinaptura** ng mga sundalo ang kampo ng mga rebelde.","translation":"The soldiers **captured** the rebels' camp."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging ayaw kumilos, magtrabaho, o mag-isip; kakulangan sa sipag o sigasig.
original_explanation: The official spirit animal of Monday mornings. It's that feeling when your bed has a stronger magnetic pull than your responsibilities. Parang 'yong friend mong puro "Sana all" pero ayaw naman kumilos.
usage_notes: Maaari ring gamitin bilang isang pangngalan upang tumukoy sa isang taong tamad.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **tamad**, bumangon ka na diyan at maglinis ng bahay.","translation":"Don't be **lazy**, get up and clean the house."},{"sentence":"Pinagalitan siya ng nanay niya dahil **tamad** siyang mag-aral.","translation":"His mother scolded him because he is **lazy** when it comes to studying."}]

meaning_filipino: Pansamantalang tumitigil sa paggalaw, pag-andar, o paggawa ng isang aksyon.
original_explanation: What the world does when your crush looks at you. O 'yung bus na humihinto sa gitna ng EDSA for no apparent reason. Also, your brain when someone asks 'Saan napunta sweldo mo?'. Biglang freeze.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging **humihinto** ang sasakyan dito dahil sa matinding trapiko.","translation":"The car always **stops** here because of the heavy traffic."},{"sentence":"Bakit **humihinto** ang relo mo?","translation":"Why **is** your watch **stopping**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kolokyal at mas karaniwang tawag sa ninong ng anak ng isang tao. Ginagamit din bilang pangkalahatang tawagan sa matalik na kaibigang lalaki.
original_explanation: The official term for your kid's godfather, but more often used for your go-to drinking buddy or barkada. 'Pare' is the short version. Your kumpare is the guy you call for a 'tagay,' to help you move a couch, or to complain about your boss. It's a bond forged by San Miguel beer and shared secrets.
usage_notes: The more common, colloquial form of 'kumpadre'. The shortened version 'pare' is extremely common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"\"Hoy **kumpare**, kamusta na ang inaanak ko?\"","translation":"\"Hey **kumpare**, how is my godchild?\""},{"sentence":"Inimbitahan niya ang lahat ng kanyang **kumpare** sa kanyang kaarawan.","translation":"He invited all his **close friends (kumpare)** to his birthday."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagiging magaslaw, hindi sanay, o hindi maayos sa pagkilos; laging natitisod o nakakabangga.
etymology: Posibleng isang pag-uulit o pagpapatindi ng isang salitang-ugat na may kaugnayan sa 'balikaw' (swagger), ngunit ginamit nang kabalintunaan upang mangahulugan ng kabaligtaran.
original_explanation: This is your friend who can't walk five steps without tripping over their own feet. Yung tipong 'graceful as a baby giraffe on ice.' They're not just clumsy, they're awkwardly clumsy. Yung kilos na parang laging may mali, laging alanganin.
usage_notes: Inilalarawan nito ang pangkalahatang paraan ng pagkilos ng isang tao. Ito ay higit pa sa isang kilos ng pagiging lampa; ito ay isang katangian.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Balikawkaw** siyang kumilos kaya palagi siyang may nababasag na gamit.","translation":"She moves **clumsily**, that's why she always breaks things."},{"sentence":"Mula pagkabata ay **balikawkaw** na talaga siya, lalo na sa pagsayaw.","translation":"Since childhood, she has always been **awkward**, especially in dancing."}]

translation: Jokingly; deceitfully; in a teasing manner
meaning_filipino: Isang kilos o pahayag na ginawa bilang isang biro, panlilinlang, o hindi sineseryoso.
original_explanation: Yung akala mo seryoso na siya sa'yo, 'yun pala paloko lang lahat. Parang 'yung "I love you" na may kasamang "charot!" sa dulo. It's when an action is done not with serious intent, but as a prank, a joke, or to mislead. Basically, the official mode of your friendly neighborhood 'loko-loko'.
usage_notes: Can be used to describe an action (adverb) or a person/thing (adjective). For example, 'sumagot nang paloko' (answered jokingly) or 'isang ngiting paloko' (a deceitful smile).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumagot siya nang **paloko**, kaya hindi ko alam kung totoo ang sinasabi niya.","translation":"He answered **jokingly**, so I don't know if what he's saying is true."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala diyan, mga pangakong **paloko** lang 'yan.","translation":"Don't believe that, those are just **deceitful** promises."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng mineral na asin, ang potassium nitrate, na ginagamit sa paggawa ng pulbura, pataba, at sa pagpreserba ng pagkain.
original_explanation: This is the stuff that goes 'BOOM!'. Historically, it's a key ingredient for gunpowder. Think of the Katipuneros making their own ammo. Today, it’s more known in food preservation, like for making tocino or ham, giving it that distinct reddish color and cured taste. It's the secret ingredient that keeps your breakfast meat looking fresh, even when it's not.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa mga kontekstong siyentipiko, historikal, o kulinaryo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ang **salitre** sa paggawa ng mga paputok para sa Bagong Taon.","translation":"**Saltpeter** was used to make fireworks for New Year."},{"sentence":"Naglalagay sila ng kaunting **salitre** sa karne upang mapreserba ito.","translation":"They put a little **saltpeter** in the meat to preserve it."}]

meaning_filipino: Bilang pangngalan, ito ay tumutukoy sa pagkakataon o kapalaran na maaaring maging mabuti. Bilang pang-uri, ito ay naglalarawan sa isang taong mapalad.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'suerte' na nangangahulugang 'kapalaran'.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na nakasakay ka agad ng jeep kahit rush hour. O kaya nung nag-12.12 sale, ikaw lang nakakuha nung last stock. Kapag **suwerte** ka, parang umaayon sa'yo ang universe. Kapag malas, well... try again next life.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Suwerte** mo naman, nanalo ka sa raffle!","translation":"You're so **lucky**, you won the raffle!"},{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng **suwerte** para manalo sa laro mamaya.","translation":"We need **luck** to win the game later."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging abala o pagkakaroon ng maraming gawain; isang bagay na pinagkakaabalahan o nangangailangan ng atensyon.
etymology: From ka- + abala + -han. Denotes the state or quality of being 'abala' (busy).
original_explanation: This is the official state of being for every working adult in Metro Manila. 'May kaabalahan ako' is the polite way of saying 'Huwag mo akong kausapin, may deadline ako.' It's your ever-present to-do list, your back-to-back Zoom meetings, and your unread emails all rolled into one stressful word.
usage_notes: Can refer to the general state of being busy or the specific tasks/activities that make one busy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pasensya na sa aking **kaabalahan**, marami lang talagang tinatapos sa trabaho.","translation":"My apologies for my **busyness**, I just have a lot to finish at work."},{"sentence":"Anu-ano ang iyong mga **kaabalahan** ngayong linggo?","translation":"What are your **affairs/preoccupations** this week?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagbibigay ng payo, gabay, o opinyon, lalo na sa isang pinuno o sa isang larangan ng kadalubhasaan.
original_explanation: The official "taga-payo." Think of them as the human version of a "pros and cons" list. Whether for a king, a CEO, or your friend who needs relationship advice, the konsehero is the one you run to when your own brain cells are on vacation.
usage_notes: Can refer to a formal adviser in politics or business, or informally to anyone who gives advice.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang hari ay may isang tapat na **konsehero** na laging kasangguni.","translation":"The king has a loyal **adviser** whom he always consults."},{"sentence":"Nagsilbi siyang **konsehero** sa mga bagong empleyado ng kumpanya.","translation":"He served as a **counselor** to the company's new employees."}]

translation: to snatch with the mouth, to grab greedily
meaning_filipino: Kunin o kagatin nang buo at mabilisan gamit ang bibig; kunin nang may kasakiman.
original_explanation: Imagine a buwaya (crocodile) snapping its jaws on its prey. 'Yan ang sumakmal. Pwede rin itong gamitin for people. Yung friend mong gutom na gutom na parang ilang taong di kumain, tapos sumakmal ng isang buong slice ng pizza. It's a very aggressive and greedy way of grabbing something, usually with the mouth or hands.
usage_notes: Often used to describe animals hunting or people eating/grabbing voraciously. This is the completed action (past tense) form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis na **sumakmal** ng pain ang malaking isda.","translation":"The big fish quickly **snatched** the bait with its mouth."},{"sentence":"Para siyang leon na **sumakmal** sa pagkain dahil sa matinding gutom.","translation":"He was like a lion who **grabbed greedily** at the food due to extreme hunger."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pansamantalang pagtira o pagtigil sa isang lugar, tulad ng bahay ng iba, otel, o anumang tirahan na hindi sarili.
original_explanation: It's the official term for when you crash at a friend's place after a late-night gimmick or when your relatives from the province suddenly appear at your doorstep with maletas. It’s not moving in, it’s just “for the meantime.” Also, it's the verb for the traditional "Panunuluyan," the reenactment of Mary and Joseph looking for an inn during Christmas.
usage_notes: Often implies a temporary stay. Can also refer to the Christmas tradition "Panunuluyan".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Saan kami maaaring **manuluyan** ngayong gabi?","translation":"Where can we **lodge** for tonight?"},{"sentence":"Nagpasya silang **manuluyan** muna sa isang murang hotel habang naghahanap ng apartment.","translation":"They decided to **stay temporarily** at a cheap hotel while looking for an apartment."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang imitasyon ng istilo ng isang partikular na manunulat, artista, o genre na may sadyang pagmamalabis para sa epektong komiko. Ang Filipinized na baybay ay 'parodiya'.
etymology: Hiram na salita mula sa Ingles na 'parody'.
original_explanation: Yung ginagawa ni Michael V. sa Bubble Gang sa mga sikat na kanta. It's like taking a serious movie trailer and turning it into a funny meme video. The art of 'gaya-gaya, puto maya' but for laughs and sometimes, social commentary.
usage_notes: Bagama't ang 'parody' ay ginagamit sa Taglish, ang 'parodiya' ang mas pormal na anyo sa wikang Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanta nila ay isang **parody** ng sikat na pop song.","translation":"Their song is a **parody** of a famous pop song."},{"sentence":"Galing siyang gumawa ng **parody** ng mga pulitiko.","translation":"He is good at making a **parody** of politicians."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sistema ng pamahalaan kung saan ang kapangyarihan ay hawak ng isang tao na may ganap at walang takdang kontrol.
original_explanation: Imagine a group project where only one person makes all the decisions, and everyone else just has to follow or fail. Now, make that a country. That's an autocracy. It's the "my way or the highway" of government.
usage_notes: A term from political science.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinamumunuan ng isang diktador ang bansang nasa ilalim ng **awtokrasya**.","translation":"The country under an **autocracy** is led by a dictator."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bahagi ng pananalita na naglalarawan o nagbibigay-turing sa isang pangngalan o panghalip.
etymology: From `pang-` (for) + `uri` (type, kind, class). Literally 'for describing the type/kind'.
original_explanation: This is the 'chismis' of grammar. It's the word that adds all the juicy details. Is the person 'maganda' or 'pangit'? Is the food 'masarap' or 'matabang'? The pang-uri gives the flavor, the color, the tea! Without it, sentences would be as boring as a meeting that could have been an email.
usage_notes: A fundamental term in Filipino grammar, taught in elementary school.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang salitang 'maganda' ay isang halimbawa ng **pang-uri**.","translation":"The word 'beautiful' is an example of an **adjective**."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan namin ang tungkol sa mga **pang-uri** sa klase ng Filipino.","translation":"We are studying about **adjectives** in our Filipino class."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang itinakdang kapalaran o kinabukasan ng isang tao; maaari ding tumukoy sa lugar kung saan itinalaga o na-assign ang isang tao para magtrabaho.
original_explanation: The universe's grand script for your life. It's that 'tadhana' feeling when you meet someone special in a crowded MRT. It can also be your job assignment, like when a cop or a teacher gets a new 'destino' in a far-flung province. So it's either your soulmate or your next workplace. The universe works in mysterious ways.
usage_notes: Has two common meanings: fate and work assignment. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naniniwala siyang **destino** niya ang maging isang guro.","translation":"She believes it is her **destiny** to be a teacher."},{"sentence":"Malayo ang bagong **destino** ng pulis kaya malulungkot ang kanyang pamilya.","translation":"The police officer's new **assignment** is far away, so his family will be sad."}]

translation: a place for drying things under the sun
meaning_filipino: Isang lugar, karaniwang patag at bukas, kung saan ibinibilad o pinatutuyo sa sikat ng araw ang mga bagay tulad ng palay, isda, o damit.
etymology: Mula sa "bilad" (to expose to the sun) + "-an" (hulaping nagpapahiwatig ng lugar).
original_explanation: The original, eco-friendly Pinoy dryer. Ito yung basketball court ng barangay 'pag tanghaling tapat na nagiging higanteng sampayan ng palay. O 'yung sementadong espasyo sa tabing-dagat kung saan nagiging daing at tuyo ang mga isda. It's where the sun does all the work.
usage_notes: Karaniwang makikita sa mga lugar na rural o malapit sa baybayin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatambak ang mga palay sa **bilaran** para matuyo.","translation":"The rice grains are piled in the **drying place** to dry."},{"sentence":"Amoy isdang-alat sa buong **bilaran**.","translation":"The whole **sun-drying area** smells of salted fish."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal para sa isang lalaking homoseksuwal. Maaaring ituring na nakakainsulto depende sa konteksto ng paggamit.
etymology: Mula sa salitang balbal na 'bading', na posibleng korapsyon ng 'babae' at 'lalaki', at dinagdagan ng hulaping '-s' na nauso sa mga salitang balbal.
original_explanation: A slang term for a gay man. It can range from playful banter among friends ("Hoy, badings!") to a straight-up insult. The more accepted, modern term is 'beki'. Think of it as the tito version of 'beki'.
usage_notes: This term is considered outdated by many and can be offensive. 'Beki' is a more modern and generally preferred term within the LGBTQ+ community.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tawanan sila nang tawanan, para silang mga **badings** na nagkikilitian.","translation":"They were laughing so hard, like a bunch of **gay friends** tickling each other."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo siyang tawaging **badings**, hindi iyon magandang biro.","translation":"Don't call him **badings**, that's not a nice joke."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagkakasunod-sunod ng mga nota ng musika na kaaya-aya sa pandinig; ang himig.
original_explanation: Ito yung main tune ng kanta na madaling kantahin o i-hum. Isipin mo yung LSS ka sa isang kanta, malamang yung melodia ang tumatak sa utak mo, hindi yung bass line o yung drum solo. Parang theme song ng buhay mo.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'himig' or 'tono'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng **melodia** ng bagong kanta ng Ben&Ben.","translation":"The **melody** of the new Ben&Ben song is beautiful."},{"sentence":"Madaling tandaan ang **melodia** ng pambansang awit.","translation":"The **melody** of the national anthem is easy to remember."}]

translation: to put in a stable; to stable (an animal)
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o paglalagak ng hayop, karaniwan ay kabayo, sa isang kuwadra o silungan.
original_explanation: This is a word you'd use if you were a haciendero/haciendera in a teleserye. "Gaston, magkuwadra mo na si Furia!" you'd say about your prized stallion. For the rest of us non-hacienderos, it's the verb for putting a horse in its house. A very specific, slightly fancy word.
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of horses and stables.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan ng amo ang kanyang tauhan na **magkuwadra** na ng mga kabayo dahil papalubog na ang araw.","translation":"The master ordered his worker to **stable** the horses already because the sun was setting."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng mahabang biyahe, oras na para **magkuwadra** at pakainin ang pagod na kabayo.","translation":"After the long journey, it's time to **put the tired horse in the stable** and feed it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paunawa, babala, o pabatid na ibinibigay upang ipaalam sa mga tao ang isang mahalagang impormasyon.
original_explanation: The official Filipino term for "FYI." It's that piece of paper taped to the office pantry door saying "Please wash your own mugs." It's the text from your landlady saying the water will be out. It's the "PAALALA" before a "BABALA." Basically, it's the heads-up you get before something happens, giving you just enough time to prepare (or complain).
usage_notes: Very common in public announcements, office memos, and formal notifications.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatanggap kami ng **abiso** na walang pasok bukas dahil sa bagyo.","translation":"We received a **notice** that there are no classes tomorrow due to the typhoon."},{"sentence":"Mag-iwan ka ng **abiso** kung aalis ka.","translation":"Leave a **notice** if you're going to leave."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamalalim o pinakasentro na bahagi ng isang bagay, damdamin, o diwa.
etymology: From `ka-` + `-an` with an intensified root, possibly related to `buto` (bone, seed), signifying the very core or marrow of something.
original_explanation: This is the "deepest, darkest secret" part of something. The core. When someone says "mula sa kaibuturan ng puso ko," they're not just saying "from my heart," they're saying "from the very bottom, the Mariana Trench of my feelings." It's the hugot level of deep.
usage_notes: Almost always used in a figurative or poetic sense, especially with "puso" (heart) or "kaluluwa" (soul).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman ko sa **kaibuturan** ng aking puso ang lungkot.","translation":"I felt the sadness in the **depths** of my heart."},{"sentence":"Ang pagmamahal niya ay nagmumula sa **kaibuturan** ng kanyang pagkatao.","translation":"Her love comes from the very **core** of her being."}]

translation: to go back and forth; to keep coming back
meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit na pagpunta at pag-alis sa isang lugar; ang madalas na paglitaw o pag-ulit ng isang bagay o pangyayari.
original_explanation: Ito yung LBM mo, nagpapabalik-balik ka sa CR. O yung customer na tanong nang tanong pero hindi naman bumibili, nagpapabalik-balik lang sa tindahan. Pwede rin sa ex na on-again, off-again kayo, nagpapabalik-balik lang sa buhay mo. It implies a repetitive, sometimes annoying, cycle of returning. The "Marites" of verbs.
usage_notes: Implies repetition and frequency. Can have a slightly exasperated or annoyed tone depending on context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na ang **magpabalik-balik** sa nakaraan, mag-move on ka na.","translation":"Stop **constantly going back** to the past, just move on."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng doktor kung bakit **nagpapabalik-balik** ang lagnat ng pasyente.","translation":"The doctor is studying why the patient's fever **keeps coming back**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagbibigay ng puna, kritisismo, o komento, kadalasan ay upang suriin ang isang gawa o kilos.
original_explanation: That one tita sa family reunion who comments on your weight. Or your boss during a performance review. Or basically half of the people in any online comments section. They find flaws for a living... or for fun.
usage_notes: Can have a negative connotation (fault-finder) or a neutral/professional one (critic).
