original_explanation: This is a deep, dramatic word. It's not just 'poor,' it's living 'wretchedly.' Imagine a telenovela character, crying in the rain, clothes tattered, after being kicked out of the hacienda. That's living **pabusabos**. It’s drama with a capital D.
usage_notes: A very strong and literary word, not typically used in casual conversation. It implies a state of extreme poverty and misery.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Namatay siyang **pabusabos** sa isang sulok ng siyudad.","translation":"He died **wretchedly** in a corner of the city."},{"sentence":"Ginawa niya ang lahat upang hindi mamuhay nang **pabusabos** ang kanyang pamilya.","translation":"She did everything so that her family would not live **in a destitute manner**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkampi o pagsuporta sa isang partikular na grupo, tao, o opinyon sa isang hindi pagkakasunduan o debate.
original_explanation: Choosing your fighter in the latest showbiz chismis or family drama. Are you Team Marites or Team Karen? You have to pick a side. That's 'pumanig'. It's like choosing between Jollibee and McDo, but with more emotional stakes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa lahat ng aming pagtatalo, lagi siyang **pumanig** sa kanyang kapatid.","translation":"In all our arguments, he always **sided with** his sibling."},{"sentence":"Mahirap magdesisyon kung kanino ka **papanig** sa sitwasyong ito.","translation":"It's hard to decide who you will **side with** in this situation."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng isang tiyak na gawain o responsibilidad sa isang tao; ang pagiging nakatalaga sa isang tungkulin.
etymology: From Spanish 'tocar', meaning 'to touch' or 'to be one's turn'.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're in a group project and everyone looks at you for the presentation part. 'Sino'ng matotoka sa pag-encode?' is the office equivalent of 'Who's on dishwashing duty tonight?'. It means it's your turn in the barrel, bes. The universe has chosen you, for better or for worse.
usage_notes: Commonly used in the context of being assigned a task, duty, or shift, often by a group or a superior.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ako na naman ang **natoka** na maghugas ng mga pinagkainan.","translation":"I was **assigned** to wash the dishes again."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **matotoka** sa night shift sa Biyernes?","translation":"Who will be **assigned** to the night shift on Friday?"}]

translation: to give a souvenir to someone
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng pasalubong sa isang tao; ang pag-aalay ng regalo sa isang taong sinasalubong o sa pagbabalik mula sa isang paglalakbay.
original_explanation: This is what you do for your officemates when you come back from vacation. You don't want them to think you forgot about them while you were sipping cocktails on a beach, so you **pasalubungan** them with keychains or local delicacies. It's the verb form of the national debt you owe everyone after a trip.
usage_notes: Often confused with the noun 'pasalubong' (gift/souvenir). This is the action of giving that gift. The '-an' suffix here directs the action towards a person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **pasalubungan** ang iyong mga kapatid pag-uwi mo.","translation":"Don't forget to **give a souvenir to** your siblings when you get home."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pan-siyamnapung posisyon o ranggo sa isang pagkakasunod-sunod.
etymology: Mula sa panlaping panunuran na "ika-" at sa salitang "siyamnapu" (ninety).
original_explanation: The 90th one. Like your lola's 90th birthday party, which is a bigger production than a K-Pop concert. Or the 90th time you've promised yourself you'll start going to the gym. It's the one before the 91st.
usage_notes: Ginagamit bilang isang pang-uring pamilang na panunuran upang ipakita ang ika-90 na puwesto sa isang serye.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipagdiriwang natin ang **ikasiyamnapu** na anibersaryo ng pagkakatatag ng ating bayan.","translation":"We will celebrate the **ninetieth** anniversary of the founding of our town."},{"sentence":"Nasa **ikasiyamnapu** na pahina na ako ng aklat.","translation":"I am now on the **ninetieth** page of the book."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paggawa sa isang bagay na maging bago muli, o pagpapasigla sa isang kalagayan, kontrata, o pangako.
original_explanation: It's that "New Year, New Me" vibe. Or when you renovate your room to make it look fresh. It's also what you do when your driver's license or passport is about to expire. You hit the refresh button.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical renovation, renewing contracts/licenses, or spiritual/personal renewal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapanibago** ng aming bahay ay aabutin ng tatlong buwan.","translation":"The **renovation** of our house will take three months."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang taunang **pagpapanibago** ng lisensya sa pagmamaneho.","translation":"The annual **renewal** of the driver's license is important."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga likas na yamang mineral na may ekonomikong halaga at maaaring minahin o kunin mula sa lupa para sa kapakinabangan.
original_explanation: This isn't a common phrase you'd hear daily. It sounds like something straight out of a HeKaSi textbook or a DENR report. It literally translates to 'used mineral' which is weird. More likely, it's a formal, slightly awkward way of saying 'yamang mineral' (mineral wealth). You'd use it to sound smart in a school paper, but never to order at Jollibee.
usage_notes: This is a very formal and somewhat unnatural-sounding phrase. 'Yamang mineral' is the more common and natural term for 'mineral resources.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Pilipinas ay mayaman sa iba't ibang **gamit na mineral** tulad ng ginto at tanso.","translation":"The Philippines is rich in various **mineral resources** like gold and copper."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng gobyerno ang responsableng pagmimina ng mga **gamit na mineral**.","translation":"The government is studying the responsible mining of **mineral deposits**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na nagkataon lamang, hindi sinasadya, o may kaugnayan ngunit hindi pangunahin sa isang pangyayari.
original_explanation: 'Yung nagkita kayo ng ex mo sa mall. Hindi plinano, sadyang nagkasabay lang. 'Yan ay insidental. Parang 'yung gastos sa Grab papunta sa party—hindi kasama sa budget ng party mismo, pero kailangan para makarating ka. It's the side quest you didn't plan for.
usage_notes: Often used to describe minor, unplanned, or secondary occurrences or costs.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aming pagkikita ay pulos **insidental**; hindi namin ito pinlano.","translation":"Our meeting was purely **incidental**; we did not plan it."},{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutan isama sa budget ang mga **insidental** na gastos tulad ng pamasahe at pagkain.","translation":"Don't forget to include **incidental** expenses like fare and food in the budget."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging matalim at patusok sa dulo; ang mismong dulo na matalim.
original_explanation: It's the 'ouch' part of a pencil, the business end of a 'kikiam' stick, or the reason you don't run with scissors. If it can poke you, it's got tulis. Also, a 'matulis' mind is a sharp mind, but a 'matulis na dila' is a sharp tongue—use with caution.
usage_notes: Often used with 'ma-' to form the adjective 'matulis' (sharp/pointed). As a noun, it refers to the point itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingatan mo ang **tulis** ng bagong tasa na lapis.","translation":"Be careful with the **sharp point** of the newly sharpened pencil."},{"sentence":"Ang **tulis** ng tore ng simbahan ay tanaw mula sa malayo.","translation":"The **spire** of the church tower is visible from afar."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos sa isang tao na magsagawa ng pagdidilig, karaniwan sa mga halaman.
etymology: From `pa-` (causative prefix) + `pag-` + `dilig` (to water plants) + `-in` (object focus suffix).
original_explanation: Utos ni lola sa'yo para utusan mo 'yung bunso mong kapatid. 'Hoy, **papagdiligin** mo nga ng halaman si Junior!' Basically, delegating the delegation.
usage_notes: A causative verb used to command someone to have another person perform the action of watering.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Papagdiligin** ko si Ana ng mga rosas sa hardin.","translation":"I will **have Ana water** the roses in the garden."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **papagdiligin** mo mamayang hapon?","translation":"Who will you **get to water** (the plants) this afternoon?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lenteng pampalaki na ginagamit upang palakihin ang anyo ng isang bagay para sa mas malinaw na pag-inspeksyon.
original_explanation: 'Yung gamit ng lola mo para basahin 'yung mga text message mo sa phone niya. Or 'yung ginagamit ng mga chismosa para palakihin ang maliliit na isyu. "Sino ka-chat mo?" *whips out magnifier*
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit ang Tagalog na "lenteng pampalaki" o "salaming pampalaki". Ang "magnifier" ay ginagamit sa mga teknikal o siyentipikong konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng **magnifier** para makita ang maliliit na detalye sa selyo.","translation":"He used a **magnifier** to see the small details on the stamp."}]

translation: to nail; to affix with a nail
meaning_filipino: Ikabit o idikit ang isang bagay sa isang lugar sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng pako.
original_explanation: The OG "nailed it," but literally. It's what you do to that calendar you bought from the suking tindahan or that 'Live, Laugh, Love' sign you got for your room. It's also used figuratively, like when you're stuck on one thought ('ipako ang pag-iisip') or when someone is being crucified ('ipako sa krus').
usage_notes: Often used in the context of carpentry. The phrase "ipako sa krus" means "to crucify." The idiom "ipako ang pag-iisip" means to fixate or focus one's thoughts on something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ipako** mo nang maayos ang larawan sa pader.","translation":"**Nail** the picture properly on the wall."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ipako** ang iyong pag-iisip sa mga problema lamang.","translation":"Don't just **fixate** your thoughts on problems."},{"sentence":"Ayon sa Bibliya, si Hesus ay **ipinako** sa krus.","translation":"According to the Bible, Jesus was **nailed** to the cross."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao, partikular na babae, na may kayumangging kulay ng balat.
original_explanation: The beautiful, sun-kissed skin tone that many Filipinos have. It's the color that thrives under the tropical sun, the one that beauty standards are *finally* starting to appreciate. If someone calls you 'morena', it's a compliment on your natural Pinay beauty. #MorenaExcellence
usage_notes: The male counterpart is "moreno". Can also be used as a noun to refer to a brown-skinned woman.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagmamalaki niya ang kanyang pagiging **morena**.","translation":"She is proud of being **brown-skinned**."},{"sentence":"Maraming humahanga sa ganda ng mga babaeng **morena**.","translation":"Many admire the beauty of **brown-skinned** women."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang idyoma na tumutukoy sa isang tao na nahihirapang bigkasin nang wasto ang mga salita sa isang partikular na wika, na kadalasan ay dahil sa impluwensya ng kanyang unang wika.
original_explanation: This describes someone trying to speak Tagalog (or English) but their native accent is so strong, it's like their tongue is a rock. Think of your foreign friend trying to say "ng" or your probinsyano tito with a very distinct regional accent. It's not a bad thing, just a description. "Pasensya na, dilang matigas ako sa Tagalog."
usage_notes: An idiomatic expression. It describes the difficulty in pronunciation, not a physical attribute of the tongue.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halata sa kanyang pananalita na siya ay **dilang matigas** at hindi sanay mag-Tagalog.","translation":"It's obvious from his speech that he **has a strong accent** and is not used to speaking Tagalog."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo siyang pagtawanan, natural lang na **dilang matigas** siya dahil dayuhan.","translation":"Don't laugh at him, it's only natural that he is **hard-tongued** because he's a foreigner."}]

translation: to collect bets; to have someone place a bet
meaning_filipino: Pahintulutan o utusan ang isang tao na tumaya para sa iyo; mangolekta ng taya mula sa iba.
original_explanation: This is what the friendly neighborhood 'kobrador' does for jueteng or what you do when you're too lazy to go to the lotto outlet. You give your friend money and your numbers and ask them, 'Pwede bang **magpataya**?' It's outsourcing your hopes and dreams of becoming a millionaire.
usage_notes: Associated with gambling, lotteries, and other games of chance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bawal **magpataya** ng jueteng sa lugar na ito.","translation":"It is forbidden to **collect bets** for jueteng in this area."},{"sentence":"**Nagpataya** siya sa kaibigan niya ng kanyang mga paboritong numero sa lotto.","translation":"He **had his friend place a bet** on his favorite numbers in the lotto."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng hindi pagkamatay o pamumuhay magpakailanman.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate life goal for vampires, highlanders, and maybe your lola's favorite Tupperware. It's the state of being 'unkillable', like a Nokia 3310 or the cockroach in your kitchen. The opposite of 'one day-old' siopao.
usage_notes: Often used in fantasy, mythology, and religious contexts. 'Imortalidad' is a common Spanish-derived synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinahanap ng mga sinaunang hari ang sikreto sa **kawalang-kamatayan**.","translation":"Ancient kings searched for the secret to **immortality**."},{"sentence":"Nakamit niya ang **kawalang-kamatayan** sa pamamagitan ng kanyang mga obra maestra.","translation":"He achieved **immortality** through his masterpieces."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang poligon na may tatlong gilid at tatlong anggulo.
original_explanation: Sa math, shape ito. Sa chismis, ito yung love life ng kaibigan mo na may ka-something, na may ka-something din pala. The original 'sana all' is now a 'sana dalawa lang'. Also, a musical instrument na pinapalo sa school band.
usage_notes: The native term 'tatsulok' is more common in general and elementary education, while 'triyangulo' might be used in more technical or higher-level math discussions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aralan namin ang iba't ibang uri ng **triyangulo** sa klase ng Geometry.","translation":"We studied the different types of **triangles** in Geometry class."},{"sentence":"Ang Bermuda **Triyangulo** ay isang misteryosong lugar.","translation":"The Bermuda **Triangle** is a mysterious place."}]

translation: rooted in; having the same root
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa dalawa o higit pang bagay na may iisang pinagmulan o sanhi.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung problema niyo ng ex mo—magkaugat sa communication issues. It means sharing the same source or origin, like how all the chismis in the office are rooted in that one Marites.
usage_notes: Often used to describe abstract concepts like problems, traditions, or beliefs that share a common origin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kahirapan at kawalan ng edukasyon ay mga problemang **magkaugat**.","translation":"Poverty and lack of education are problems that are **rooted in each other**."},{"sentence":"Ang ating mga tradisyon ay **magkaugat** sa paniniwala ng ating mga ninuno.","translation":"Our traditions are **rooted in** the beliefs of our ancestors."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halamang gulay na may bahagyang anghang ang mga dahon. Tumutukoy din ito sa sarsang dilaw na gawa mula sa buto nito.
original_explanation: Pwedeng 'yung green, leafy vegetable na kasama sa sinigang o burong mustasa. Pwede ring 'yung yellow na palaman sa hotdog sandwich. So pag sinabing 'pahingi ng mustasa,' linawin mo kung dahon o 'yung nasa bote para 'di magka-gulo.
usage_notes: The context usually clarifies whether it refers to the plant (mustard greens) or the condiment (mustard).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magluto ka ng sinigang na may **mustasa**.","translation":"Cook sinigang with **mustard greens**."},{"sentence":"Pakiabot ng **mustasa** para sa hotdog ko.","translation":"Please pass the **mustard** for my hotdog."}]

translation: to bring ashore; to run aground
meaning_filipino: Itulak o dalhin ang isang sasakyang-dagat patungo sa pampang o dalampasigan; sumadsad.
original_explanation: Imagine you're on a bangka and the engine dies. The boatman has to idahik the boat, meaning, manually get it to the shore. It's the nautical equivalent of pushing a car that's run out of gas. It can also mean when a project or plan gets 'beached'—it gets stuck and can't move forward. "Na-idahik yung project proposal natin, 'di inaprubahan."
usage_notes: Primarily used in coastal or fishing communities. Can also be used figuratively to mean getting stuck.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinailangan nilang **idahik** ang bangka dahil sa papalakas na alon.","translation":"They had to **bring the boat ashore** because of the strengthening waves."},{"sentence":"Nagulat ang mga mangingisda nang may balyenang na-**idahik** sa kanilang dalampasigan.","translation":"The fishermen were surprised when a whale was **beached** on their shore."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang likas na akumulasyon o konsentrasyon ng mga mineral sa balat ng daigdig na may sapat na dami at halaga upang maging kapaki-pakinabang sa ekonomiya.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng 'deposito' (mula sa Espanyol na 'depósito') at 'mineral' (mula sa Espanyol na 'mineral').
original_explanation: This is Earth's version of a hidden treasure chest. It's where miners find the good stuff—gold, nickel, copper. Basically, it's the reason why some places become mining hotspots and why there are so many debates about environmental protection. It's nature's G-spot for geologists and mining companies.
usage_notes: Isang teknikal na termino na ginagamit sa heolohiya, pagmimina, at agham pangkapaligiran.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayaman sa **depositong mineral** tulad ng ginto at tanso ang kabundukan ng Cordillera.","translation":"The Cordillera mountains are rich in **mineral deposits** like gold and copper."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng mga heologo ang lokasyon ng mga bagong **depositong mineral**.","translation":"Geologists are studying the location of new **mineral deposits**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang pagtalon o paglundag pasugod upang sunggaban ang isang bagay o nilalang.
original_explanation: Think of a cat seeing a laser pointer. That sudden, focused jump? That's *pagdamba*. It's also what you do when the last piece of fried chicken is on the table and you and your sibling make eye contact. Game on.
usage_notes: Implies a sudden, predatory, or aggressive leap towards a target.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagulat ang daga sa biglaang **pagdamba** ng pusa.","translation":"The mouse was startled by the cat's sudden **pounce**."},{"sentence":"Muntik na siyang mahulog sa **pagdamba** ng malaking aso.","translation":"He almost fell from the big dog's **lunge**."}]

translation: to smile involuntarily; to happen to smile
meaning_filipino: Hindi sinasadyang pagngiti dahil sa isang partikular na dahilan, sitwasyon, o alaala.
original_explanation: That feeling when you suddenly remember a funny meme, or your crush messages you "good morning". You're in a jeep, trying to look serious, but you can't help it. 'Yan ang mapangiti. It’s the "bigla na lang" smile, the unplanned kilig-inducer.
usage_notes: This is an involuntary action verb. `Ngumiti` is the voluntary action. Common forms are `napangiti` (past) and `mapapangiti` (future).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko maiwasang **mapangiti** tuwing naaalala ko ang aming mga biruan.","translation":"I can't help but **smile** whenever I remember our jokes."},{"sentence":"Napatingin siya sa akin kaya ako'y biglang **napangiti**.","translation":"He looked at me, so I suddenly **smiled**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pang-abay na pananggi na nagpapahayag ng pagtanggi, pagtutol, o kawalan ng isang katangian o aksyon.
original_explanation: The ultimate conversation ender and a Pinoy's favorite way to politely say "no" even when they mean "maybe," "I'll think about it," or "ask me again after merienda." It’s the foundation of the friendzone ("**Hindi** kita gusto...") and the start of many negotiations at the palengke ("**Hindi** ba pwedeng 100 na lang?").
usage_notes: The primary word for negation in Tagalog. Often shortened to 'di in informal speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hindi** ako aalis hangga't **hindi** ka bumabalik.","translation":"I will **not** leave until you come back."},{"sentence":"Tinanong ko siya kung galit siya, sabi niya '**hindi**'.","translation":"I asked him if he was angry, he said '**no**'."}]

translation: to sue each other; to accuse one another
meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay o resiprokal na paghahain ng kaso ng dalawa o higit pang panig laban sa isa't isa.
original_explanation: The legal drama when two ex-business partners or feuding neighbors decide to air their dirty laundry in court by filing cases against each other. It's the ultimate 'you sue me, I sue you' telenovela plot.
usage_notes: Implies a reciprocal legal battle between two or more parties.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng mainit na pagtatalo, nagsimulang **magsakdalan** ang magkapitbahay.","translation":"After the heated argument, the neighbors started to **sue each other**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagkakaloob o pamamahagi ng mga bagay sa maraming tao, kadalasan nang walang bayad.
original_explanation: This is the official verb of campaign season, Christmas, and your balikbayan relative's arrival. It’s the act of handing things out, whether it's flyers, relief goods, or pasalubong. If someone is planning to mamigay ng pera, you better be first in line.
usage_notes: Implies giving to multiple recipients.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Plano ng aming grupo na **mamigay** ng mga laruan sa mga bata sa ampunan.","translation":"Our group plans to **give away** toys to the children in the orphanage."},{"sentence":"Tuwing Pasko, ugali na niyang **mamigay** ng aginaldo sa kanyang mga inaanak.","translation":"Every Christmas, it's his habit to **distribute** cash gifts to his godchildren."}]

translation: to cause to fall; to bring down; to cause to fail
meaning_filipino: Ang maging sanhi ng pagbagsak, pagguho, o pagkabigo ng isang bagay, tao, o sistema.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you pull a Jenga block from the wrong spot. Or when you vote for the wrong person and the economy goes brrr. Sa school, ito yung terror prof na kayang mapabagsak ang kalahati ng klase sa final exam.
usage_notes: Can be literal (to make something fall) or figurative (to cause failure, to overthrow a government, to fail a student).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang maling galaw mo lang ay maaari mong **mapabagsak** ang lahat ng domino.","translation":"Just one wrong move and you could **cause** all the dominoes **to fall**."},{"sentence":"Layunin ng mga rebelde na **mapabagsak** ang gobyerno.","translation":"The rebels' goal is to **bring down** the government."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi kita hahayaang **mapabagsak** sa klase ko.","translation":"Don't worry, I won't let you **fail** my class."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o katangian ng pagiging mabuti; ang paggawa ng mabuti sa kapwa; benepisyo o kapakinabangan.
original_explanation: This is the general 'goodness' that your lola hopes you have. It's the opposite of kasamaan. It's the reason you give up your seat on the MRT, help an old lady cross the street, or share your chichirya with your friends. It’s the positive karma points you rack up.
usage_notes: Often used in a general sense to refer to moral goodness or a positive outcome.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kabutihan** ng kanyang puso ay hindi matatawaran.","translation":"The **goodness** of his/her heart is immeasurable."},{"sentence":"Walang naidulot na **kabutihan** ang kanyang desisyon.","translation":"His/her decision brought no **benefit**."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang gawain o tao na nagpapakita ng malaking atensyon sa detalye; maingat at kumpleto.
etymology: ma- (adjective-forming prefix) + susi (key). The connection is figurative, as in "unlocking" all the details.
original_explanation: How your tita inspects your new boyfriend/girlfriend from head to toe. It's the level of detail a chismosa needs before spreading the news. In the BPO world, this is 'attention to detail'—no shortcuts, every corner checked, every 'i' dotted and 't' crossed.
usage_notes: Can describe a person, an investigation, a plan, or any process that requires careful attention.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng **masusi** na pag-iimbestiga sa kasong ito.","translation":"A **thorough** investigation is needed for this case."},{"sentence":"**Masusi** siyang nagtrabaho kaya walang naging pagkakamali.","translation":"She worked **meticulously** so there were no mistakes."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng biglaan at hindi sinasadyang paggalaw ng katawan o bahagi nito, karaniwang dahil sa sakit, takot, o matinding emosyon.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung puso mo noong nakita mong nag-reply si crush sa story ng iba. Biglang **kumisay** sa selos at kirot. O, 'yung reaction ng lola mo kapag nanalo sa bingo. Bigla na lang nag-spasm sa tuwa.
usage_notes: Often used to describe involuntary muscle movements due to medical conditions, strong emotions (like fear or shock), or being electrocuted.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumisay** ang pasyente bago ito binawian ng buhay.","translation":"The patient **convulsed** before he passed away."},{"sentence":"Biglang **kumisay** sa takot ang pusa nang makakita ng malaking aso.","translation":"The cat suddenly **twitched** in fear when it saw a large dog."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit at pansamantalang kapilya o dambana, na karaniwang yari sa mga katutubong materyales tulad ng kawayan at nipa, at itinayo para sa isang partikular na pagdiriwang o okasyon.
original_explanation: The original pop-up church. It's a temporary chapel you see in barrios during fiestas, often made of bamboo and coconut leaves. It's where the image of the patron saint chills before the big procession. Very rustic, very Filipino.
usage_notes: Strongly associated with rural religious festivities like Flores de Mayo or barrio fiestas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-alay sila ng mga bulaklak sa **tuklong** na itinayo para sa pista.","translation":"They offered flowers at the **makeshift chapel** built for the fiesta."},{"sentence":"Ang prusisyon ay magsisimula mula sa **tuklong** at iikot sa buong baryo.","translation":"The procession will start from the **temporary altar** and go around the whole village."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian o kalagayan ng pagiging puti.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate goal when you're washing your white uniforms, using all the *pampaputi* products you can find. It's the "kaputian" of a fresh sheet of bond paper, a brand new pair of sneakers, or the clouds on a perfect day.
usage_notes: Can refer to the color white, fairness of skin, or purity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Namangha ako sa **kaputian** ng kaniyang mga ngipin.","translation":"I was amazed by the **whiteness** of her teeth."},{"sentence":"Ang **kaputian** ng buhangin sa Boracay ay sikat sa buong mundo.","translation":"The **whiteness** of the sand in Boracay is famous worldwide."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang karwahe o sasakyan, kadalasang maganda ang palamuti, na ginagamit sa mga prusisyon, parada, o para paglagyan ng kabaong.
original_explanation: The OG pimped-out ride. During fiestas and Holy Week, it's the ornate float carrying a saint's statue, covered in flowers and lights. At a funeral, it's the hearse. Basically, it's a special vehicle for VIPs – Very Important Persons or Very Important Patay.
usage_notes: Ang kahulugan ay nag-iiba depende sa konteksto: prusisyon (float), libing (hearse), o pangkalahatang karwahe (carriage).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakaraming bulaklak ang palamuti sa **karo** ng Mahal na Birhen.","translation":"The **float** of the Blessed Virgin was decorated with so many flowers."},{"sentence":"Dahan-dahang umusad ang **karo** na naglalaman ng kabaong.","translation":"The **hearse** containing the coffin moved slowly."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pandiwa ng hindi pag-alala o pagkabigong isaisip ang isang bagay o isang tao. Ang pokus ay sa taong gumawa ng pagkilos.
original_explanation: This is the active form of forgetting. 'Yung ikaw mismo ang gumawa ng krimen. 'Sino ang nakalimot mag-off ng ilaw?' is a classic mom question. This is also the ultimate 'kasalanan' in a relationship. 'Nakalimot ka na ba sa mga pangako mo?' Cue the dramatic music.
usage_notes: Actor-focus verb. The person who forgot is the subject. Contrasts with 'nakalimutan' which is object-focus.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **nakalimot** na magdala ng payong kaya siya nabasa ng ulan.","translation":"She was the one who **forgot** to bring an umbrella, that's why she got wet in the rain."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi ako **nakalimot** sa ating usapan.","translation":"Don't worry, I have not **forgotten** our agreement."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng ayos ng buhok kung saan ang mahabang buhok ay tinitipon, iniikot, at itinatali sa likod o itaas ng ulo.
etymology: Possibly a semantic extension of "pusod" (navel/center), as the hair is gathered to a central point. Pronunciation often differs from its homonym.
original_explanation: The official hairstyle for "I need to get things done." It's the look for studying for an exam, cleaning the house, or when it's just too hot in the Philippines (so, every day). A perfectly messy pusod is an art form. The higher the bun, the closer to finishing your deadlines.
usage_notes: Pronunciation can distinguish this meaning from 'navel'. Stress is often on the second syllable for 'hair bun' (/pu-SOD/) and the first for 'navel' (/PU-sod/).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naka-**pusod** ang buhok ni Maria dahil mainit ang panahon.","translation":"Maria's hair is in a **bun** because the weather is hot."},{"sentence":"Gawa mo naman ng magandang **pusod** ang buhok ko.","translation":"Can you make a nice **bun** with my hair?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matalinhagang paglalarawan sa isang tao na walang kahihiyan, matakaw, o labis ang pagnanasa sa isang bagay, na inihahalintulad sa isang hayop.
original_explanation: Describes that one person at the all-you-can-eat buffet who piles their plate so high it looks like the Leaning Tower of Pisa, and then goes back for more. Walang hiya, parang **halhal**.
usage_notes: This is a figurative and very strong pejorative term, deriving its imagery from a panting, slobbering animal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinuturing siyang **halhal** sa pera ng kanyang mga kaaway.","translation":"He is considered **greedy** for money by his enemies."},{"sentence":"Kumilos siya nang parang **halhal** sa harap ng pagkain.","translation":"He acted like a **glutton** in front of the food."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagluto ng pagkain sa mainit na mantika o langis.
original_explanation: In the Philippines, "fry" is a love language. From the humble pritong itlog to the glorious crispy pata, we "fry" everything. It's the verb that launches a thousand carinderias and fills every Filipino kitchen with that "amoy-ulam" scent that sticks to your clothes.
usage_notes: Used as a verb root in Tagalog, often with affixes like 'i-' (i-fry), '-in' (frinay), or 'mag-' (mag-fry).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**fry** na lang itong isda para sa hapunan.","translation":"Please just **fry** this fish for dinner."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang manok kapag deep-**fry**.","translation":"Chicken is delicious when deep-**fried**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-inog o pag-ikot sa paligid ng isang sentral na punto o aksis.
original_explanation: This is what the Earth does around the sun. It's what the giant ferris wheel does at the perya. It's you, walking around the mall for the fifth time because you can't decide where to eat. It implies a revolution or a spin around something else, not just spinning in place.
usage_notes: Often used for celestial bodies, machinery, or movement in a circular path. Differentiated from `ikot` which is more general; `ikit` emphasizes orbiting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan nila ang **pag-ikit** ng mga planeta sa ating solar system.","translation":"They are studying the **revolution** of the planets in our solar system."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pandiwang-ugat para sa pagkilos ng pag-aanyaya o pag-imbita sa isang tao na sumama sa isang gawain, lugar, o kaganapan.
original_explanation: This is the action of asking 'Tara?' (Let's go?). It's the root word for that moment you ask your friends to go for milk tea ('**Yaya**in mo sila'), or when your officemate invites you to lunch ('Nagyaya siya'). Not to be confused with the nanny, this **yaya** is all about getting people to join in.
usage_notes: This is a verb root. It is almost always used with affixes, e.g., yayain, nagyaya, yumaya, nag-yayaan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang laging nag-**yaya** sa aming kumain sa labas.","translation":"He's always the one who **invites** us to eat out."}]

meaning_filipino: May katandaan na o marami nang edad; hindi na bata.
original_explanation: Describes someone who has collected many birthdays. They have more stories than you have IG posts, and their knees probably make more noise than your notifications. They've earned their senior citizen discount and the right to say "noong panahon namin..."
usage_notes: Primarily used for people and animals. For inanimate objects, the word is 'luma'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aso namin ay **matanda** na kaya palagi na lang natutulog.","translation":"Our dog is **old** now so it's always sleeping."},{"sentence":"Mas **matanda** siya sa akin ng limang taon.","translation":"He is five years **older** than me."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi napakinabangan; nauwi sa wala; natapon o nasira nang walang kabuluhan.
original_explanation: The ultimate sin in any Filipino household, especially when it comes to rice. It's the reason your mom tells you to finish your food ('Daming nagugutom!'). Also applies to time spent in traffic, a data plan you didn't use, or your effort on someone who just 'seen-zoned' you.
usage_notes: Often confused by learners with 'masaya' (happy). Note the different root word, pronunciation (stress on SA), and meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nanghinayang siya dahil baka **masayang** lang ang kanyang pinaghirapan.","translation":"He felt regret because his hard work might just **go to waste**."},{"sentence":"Itago mo ang natirang ulam para hindi **masayang**.","translation":"Keep the leftover food so it won't **go to waste**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapatigil ng operasyon o paglalapat ng harang sa isang daanan o bukasan sa hinaharap.
etymology: From `mag-` + reduplication of the first syllable of the root `sa-` + `sara` (close). Future tense of `magsara` (infinitive form).
original_explanation: The reason you panic-buy at the grocery store at 8:55 PM. It's the future tense of 'magsara'. 'Anong oras magsasara ang mall?' is a question that dictates your entire evening plan.
usage_notes: Future tense of the verb `magsara`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bangko ay **magsasara** nang alas-tres ng hapon.","translation":"The bank **will close** at three in the afternoon."},{"sentence":"**Magsasara** na ang pinto sa loob ng isang minuto.","translation":"The door **will close** in one minute."}]

translation: to fill with stars; to stud with stars
meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng mga palamuting hugis-bituin o anumang bagay na kumikinang na parang bituin.
original_explanation: To 'star-ify' something. It's the verb form of making something starry. Think of a graphic designer being told, 'Bitunan mo nga 'yang design para magmukhang magical.' Or what God does to the sky every night. It's adding sparkle and twinkle to an otherwise plain canvas.
usage_notes: A rare, poetic, or literary word. Not used in everyday conversation. It implies decorating something with many star-like objects.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang madilim na langit ay tila **bitunan** ng libu-libong alitaptap.","translation":"The dark sky seemed to be **studded with stars** by thousands of fireflies."},{"sentence":"Nais ng bata na **bitunan** ang kanyang buong kwarto.","translation":"The child wants **to fill** her entire room **with stars**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang espasyo o guhit sa gilid ng isang papel na walang sulat; ang agwat o palugit.
original_explanation: This is a direct English loanword. It's the space on the side of your notebook where your teacher writes "See me!" or "Good work!". In business, it's the difference between your puhunan and your benta. "Maliit lang ang margin ko diyan," says every vendor at Greenhills. It's your buffer, your extra space, your profit.
usage_notes: Used in both its literal (stationery) and figurative (business, finance) English senses. The Tagalog word 'marhen' is the Filipinized spelling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang susulat sa **margin** ng iyong test paper.","translation":"Don't write on the **margin** of your test paper."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating taasan ang profit **margin** sa susunod na quarter.","translation":"We need to increase the profit **margin** next quarter."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking gusali o silid na dinisenyo para sa mga manonood, karaniwang may entablado para sa mga pagtatanghal, seminar, o pagtitipon.
etymology: Mula sa Latin sa pamamagitan ng Ingles na "auditorium".
original_explanation: The place in school where you suffered through boring graduation speeches but also cheered your heart out during the battle of the bands. It's the 'event place' before event places were cool. Think a bigger, more formal version of your classroom.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginanap sa **oditoryum** ng unibersidad ang seremonya ng pagtatapos.","translation":"The graduation ceremony was held in the university **auditorium**."},{"sentence":"Puno ang **oditoryum** ng mga manonood para sa konsiyerto.","translation":"The **auditorium** was full of spectators for the concert."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tiyak na sukat o dami ng gamot na inireseta o inirerekomenda para sa isang partikular na paggamit.
original_explanation: Ilang tabletas ng Biogesic ang kailangan mo para sa lagnat mo? 'Yan ang dosis. Parang sa landi, dapat may tamang dosis din—'pag sumobra, overdose at nakaka-umay; 'pag kulang, baka ma-friendzone.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa kontekstong medikal ngunit maaari ring gamitin sa metaporikal na paraan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sundin mo ang tamang **dosis** ng gamot na inireseta ng doktor.","translation":"Follow the correct **dose** of medicine prescribed by the doctor."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng araw-araw na **dosis** ng kape para magising ang diwa ko.","translation":"I need a daily **dose** of coffee to awaken my senses."}]

translation: a boatload, a huge number of
meaning_filipino: Isang malaki at hindi tiyak na dami o bilang; napakarami.
etymology: From `sang-` (one) + `ka-` + `tutak` (an unspecific large quantity). The origin of 'tutak' is unclear.
original_explanation: The slightly more "proper" cousin of 'sangkaterba'. It's the amount of requirements your prof gives you the week before finals. It's the number of people lining up for milk tea on a payday Friday. It means "a lot," but with a hint of exasperation.
usage_notes: Informal and colloquial, similar to 'sangkaterba'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **sangkatutak** na tanong ang mga reporter sa press conference.","translation":"The reporters had a **boatload** of questions at the press conference."},{"sentence":"Bakit ba **sangkatutak** ang dala mong gamit para sa isang weekend trip?","translation":"Why did you bring a **huge number of** things for just a weekend trip?"}]

translation: to cause worry; to be disturbing
meaning_filipino: Ang magdulot ng matinding pag-aalala, pagkabalisa, o hindi mapakaling damdamin.
original_explanation: That feeling you get at 3 AM when you remember an embarrassing thing you did in high school. Or when you see a "We need to talk" message from your boss or jowa. That's *nakakabagabag*. It's something that really messes with your peace of mind.
usage_notes: Often used in its conjugated form 'nakakabagabag' (is disturbing). It implies a deep sense of unease or turmoil.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang balitang iyon ay tunay na **makabagabag** sa sinumang makarinig.","translation":"That news is truly **disturbing** to anyone who hears it."},{"sentence":"Nakakabagabag ang katahimikan niya matapos ang aming pag-uusap.","translation":"His silence after our conversation is **worrying**."}]

translation: to cause to wither; to let dry up
meaning_filipino: Pabayaan o hayaang matuyo nang husto, malanta, o maubos ang tubig, lalo na ang mga halaman, ilog, o balon.
etymology: From the causative prefix "pa-", the root word "tuyot" (withered, completely dry), and the object-focus suffix "-in".
original_explanation: This is a more intense version of 'patuyuin'. It's what happens to your houseplant when you forget about it for two weeks. It's also what your crush does to your hopes and dreams when they leave you on 'seen'. It implies a slow, complete drying out, often leading to decay or death.
usage_notes: While 'patuyuin' is for general drying of wet things, 'patuyutin' implies causing something (usually organic or a body of water) to wither or dry out completely due to neglect or natural forces.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **patuyutin** ang mga halaman sa hardin.","translation":"Don't **let the plants in the garden wither**."},{"sentence":"Ang matinding tag-araw ay maaaring **patuyutin** ang mga ilog.","translation":"The intense summer heat can **cause the rivers to dry up**."}]

translation: to be extorted; to have something forcibly taken from
meaning_filipino: Makuhaan ng pera o ari-arian sa pamamagitan ng pamimilit, pananakot, o panloloko.
etymology: From 'huthot', meaning 'to siphon' or 'to extort'. The '-an' suffix makes the subject the one being extorted from.
original_explanation: Imagine a 'corrupt traffic enforcer' scenario. Or that 'friend' who always 'borrows' money but never pays back, and you can't say no. You're being slowly drained of your resources. **Nahuhuthutan** ka. It's like being a human ATM for someone else's benefit, usually against your will.
usage_notes: Strongly implies coercion, threat, or deception is used to get something (usually money) from the victim.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming negosyante ang takot na **mahuthutan** ng mga buwayang opisyal.","translation":"Many business owners are afraid of being **extorted** by corrupt officials."},{"sentence":"Ayaw na niyang magpahiram ng pera dahil ayaw na niyang **mahuthutan**.","translation":"He doesn't want to lend money anymore because he doesn't want to be **extorted from**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng isang bagay na may lamat, sira, o hati ngunit hindi pa ganap na nagkahiwa-hiwalay ang mga bahagi.
original_explanation: Your phone screen after it falls face down. Your voice after a karaoke marathon singing Aegis songs. Your heart after seeing your crush with someone else. "Bes, basag na naman ang puso ko."
usage_notes: Can describe physical objects (glass, mirror) or abstract concepts (voice, heart, trust).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka, **basag** ang salamin sa sahig.","translation":"Be careful, the mirror on the floor is **broken**."},{"sentence":"**Basag** ang boses niya matapos ang konsiyerto.","translation":"His voice was **hoarse/cracked** after the concert."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkaramdam ng matinding hiya o kahihiyan, karaniwang dahil sa isang pagkakamali o sitwasyong nakakababa ng dangal sa harap ng publiko.
original_explanation: That "sana lamunin na ako ng lupa" moment. It's when you confidently wave at someone who wasn't actually waving at you. Or when your audio is unmuted during a Zoom meeting and you're talking to your cat. It's the emotional damage you feel after a major "epic fail." The feeling is so intense you wish you could just turn invisible.
usage_notes: Inilalarawan ang estado o pakiramdam ng pagiging napahiya. Ang "kahihiyan" ay ang mismong konsepto ng 'shame', habang ang "pagkapahiya" ay ang karanasan o estado ng pakiramdam nito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya malimutan ang **pagkapahiya** niya nang matapilok siya sa entablado.","translation":"She couldn't forget her **embarrassment** when she tripped on stage."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa **pagkapahiya**, hindi muna siya nagpakita sa mga kaibigan.","translation":"Because of the **humiliation**, he didn't show his face to his friends for a while."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng gulay na pahaba at kulay berde, na nagiging malagkit kapag niluto.
etymology: From English 'okra', ultimately from a West African language (e.g., Igbo 'ọ́kụ̀rụ̀').
original_explanation: The vegetable that divides the nation. You either love its slimy texture in sinigang and pinakbet, or you think it's an alien pod that has no business being in food. There is no in-between. It's the 'pasaway' but healthy kid in the bahay kubo song.
usage_notes: A common vegetable in Filipino cuisine.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong sahog sa sinigang ang **okra**.","translation":"My favorite ingredient in sinigang is **okra**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong i-overcook ang **okra** para hindi masyadong lumagkit.","translation":"Don't overcook the **okra** so it doesn't get too slimy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isa pang baryasyon ng salitang balbal na 'paps', na ginagamit bilang tawag sa isang kaibigang lalaki.
etymology: Isang baryasyon ng salitang balbal na 'paps'.
original_explanation: It's 'paps' but with a little extra flair. Think of it as the slightly more playful, sometimes more endearing version. If 'paps' is a nod, 'papsi' is a friendly pat on the back. "Papsi, ang galing mo kanina sa laro!"
usage_notes: Katulad ng 'paps', ito ay napaka-impormal at ginagamit sa mga kaibigan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Salamat sa tulong mo, **papsi**!","translation":"Thanks for your help, **dude**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panahon ng pag-aagaw ng liwanag at dilim sa paglubog ng araw; dapit-hapon. Maaari ring tumukoy sa isang panahon ng kahirapan, kamangmangan, o kasamaan.
original_explanation: It's that spooky time of day when the sun has clocked out but the moon hasn't clocked in yet. Your lola would tell you to get inside the house "dahil tagdilim na, baka may magpakita." It's the golden hour for aswangs and the primetime for ghost stories. Metaphorically, it's the "dark ages" or a tough phase in life, like the week before sahod.
usage_notes: Can be used both literally for twilight and metaphorically for a period of hardship or ignorance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umuwi ka na bago mag-**tagdilim**.","translation":"Go home before **dusk**."},{"sentence":"Ang bansa ay dumanas ng panahon ng **tagdilim** sa ilalim ng diktador.","translation":"The country experienced a **period of darkness** under the dictator."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matibay at pinalakas na istraktura o lugar, karaniwang may pader, na nagsisilbing pananggalang laban sa kaaway.
original_explanation: Think Intramuros. A "muog" is a fortress, a stronghold. It's what you build to protect yourself from invaders. Emotionally, your "muog" is that wall you put up after a bad breakup. It's your "I'm not crying, you're crying" defense mechanism, fortified with sarcasm and a "seen" zone.
usage_notes: Often used in historical or literary contexts to refer to fortified structures. Metaphorically, it can refer to a stronghold of belief or emotion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Intramuros ay isang makasaysayang **muog** na itinayo noong panahon ng mga Espanyol.","translation":"Intramuros is a historical **fortress** built during the Spanish era."},{"sentence":"Nananatiling matatag ang kanilang pananampalataya bilang kanilang **muog** sa gitna ng pagsubok.","translation":"Their faith remains strong as their **stronghold** amidst trials."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtama nang direkta at may katiyakan sa isang target o layunin.
original_explanation: Imagine playing darts and hitting the bullseye – that's it! Or when you're arguing and you deliver a point so perfectly that the other person goes silent. 'Sapul!' they say. To **magsapol** is to hit something dead on, whether it's a physical target or a verbal zinger.
usage_notes: Often used in its root form 'sapul' as an interjection ('Bullseye!'). As a verb, it is less common but understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **magsapol** ng ibon gamit ang kanyang tirador.","translation":"He tried to **strike** a bird directly using his slingshot."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang patutsada ay tila **nagsapol** sa lahat ng may kasalanan.","translation":"His sarcastic remark seemed to **hit the mark** on everyone who was guilty."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gilid o dulo ng isang bagay, lalo na ng isang bangin o anumang matarik na lugar; ang punto kung kailan malapit nang mangyari ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: Ito yung state mo bago mag-sweldo, nasa bingit ka na ng kahirapan. O kaya yung feeling mo sa jowa mong red flag, nasa bingit ka na ng hiwalayan. It's that 'one more push and I'm over the edge' moment.
usage_notes: Often used metaphorically to describe a critical or dangerous point.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa **bingit** siya ng kamatayan nang matagpuan ng mga rescuer.","translation":"He was on the **brink** of death when the rescuers found him."},{"sentence":"Isang maling hakbang lang at mahuhulog ka sa **bingit** ng bangin.","translation":"One wrong step and you'll fall over the **edge** of the cliff."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang proteksiyon o harang na inilalagay sa bintana upang maiwasan ang pagpasok ng mga insekto o bilang seguridad.
etymology: From 'panangga' (from pan- + sangga, 'something used to block/parry') + 'sa' ('at/for the') + 'bintana' ('window').
original_explanation: That metal grill or mesh screen on your window that stops two things: 1) lamok and other flying chismosas from entering your room, and 2) akyat-bahay gangs. It's the original, low-tech security system of Filipino homes.
usage_notes: This is a descriptive phrase. 'Panangga' is the core noun, meaning 'shield/guard'. The specific type is clarified by 'sa bintana'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpakabit kami ng bagong **panangga sa bintana** para sa dagdag na seguridad.","translation":"We had a new **window guard** installed for added security."},{"sentence":"Butas na ang **panangga sa bintana** kaya nakakapasok ang mga lamok.","translation":"The **window screen** has a hole, which is why mosquitoes can get in."}]

translation: to connect; to link; to relate
meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagdudugtong o paglalapat ng dalawa o higit pang bagay, tao, o ideya upang magkaroon ng relasyon o koneksyon.
original_explanation: Parang trabaho ng HR, kailangang i-connect ang management at employees. O parang ikaw na nagiging tulay sa dalawang magkaibigang nag-away. It's the act of linking things together, whether it's wifi, people, or ideas for your thesis.
usage_notes: A command or infinitive form. The root 'ugnay' means connection or relation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinusubukan ng guro na **pag-ugnayin** ang aralin sa totoong buhay.","translation":"The teacher tries **to connect** the lesson to real life."},{"sentence":"**Pag-ugnayin** mo ang dalawang wire na ito para gumana ang ilaw.","translation":"**Connect** these two wires for the light to work."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pagkakaroon ng pagkakahawig o pagkakapareho sa katangian, anyo, o kalagayan ng isang tao, bagay, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: ‘Yung feeling na nakita mo ‘yung ex mo may kasamang iba, tapos sabi ng friend mo, “Huy, tulad mo manamit ‘yung bago niya!” Awts. Also used to compare things, like “Ang traffic sa EDSA ay tulad ng isang toxic relationship, mahirap umusad.”
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa paghahambing, kasingkahulugan ng 'gaya' o 'para'. Maaari ring maging pangngalan na nangangahulugang 'kopya' o 'katapat'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tulad** ng isang agila, malaya siyang lumipad.","translation":"**Like** an eagle, she flew freely."},{"sentence":"Wala siyang **tulad** sa galing.","translation":"He has no **equal** in skill."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manipis, mahaba, at malambot na bahagi ng katawan ng ilang hayop, tulad ng pugita o pusit, na ginagamit sa paghawak, paggalaw, o pandama.
original_explanation: That creepy, wiggly arm of an octopus or squid. Also used figuratively to describe the far-reaching influence of something, usually something negative, like corruption or a powerful corporation. 'May mga tentakulo ang sindikato sa gobyerno.' Sounds like a movie plot, right?
usage_notes: Maaari ring gamitin sa matalinhagang paraan upang ilarawan ang malawak na impluwensya o kapangyarihan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahuli ng **tentakulo** ng pugita ang maliit na isda.","translation":"The octopus's **tentacle** caught the small fish."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang impluwensya ay parang mga **tentakulo** na umaabot sa lahat ng sangay ng pamahalaan.","translation":"His influence is like **tentacles** reaching into all branches of government."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng karangyaan, kagaraan, o pagiging marangya sa pananamit, palamuti, o pagdiriwang.
original_explanation: When something is extra, but in a good, high-class way. Think of a debutante's ball, a fiesta queen's gown, or that one tita who shows up to a family reunion looking like she's going to the Met Gala. It's not just 'maganda,' it's 'magarbo'—it has production value.
usage_notes: Often used to describe events, clothing, or decorations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakagarbo ng kasal nila, parang eksena sa pelikula.","translation":"Their wedding was so **lavish**, like a scene from a movie."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang magsuot ng **magarbo** na damit kahit sa simpleng okasyon lang.","translation":"She likes to wear **fancy** clothes even for simple occasions."}]

translation: a smile; the act of smiling
meaning_filipino: Ang akto o kilos ng pag-angat ng mga sulok ng bibig upang ipahiwatig ang saya, pagkalugod, o pagbati.
original_explanation: The universal Filipino language. It can mean 'hello,' 'thank you,' 'excuse me,' or 'I'm secretly judging your outfit but I'm too polite to say anything.' It's the default facial expression when you make eye contact with a stranger or when your Tita asks if you have a jowa.
usage_notes: A very common and positive word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang matamis na **pagngiti** ang kanyang isinukli sa aking pagbati.","translation":"She returned my greeting with a sweet **smile**."},{"sentence":"Ang simpleng **pagngiti** ay makapagpapasaya na ng araw ng iba.","translation":"A simple **act of smiling** can already brighten someone else's day."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang masusing pagtatanong o pagsisiyasat upang malaman ang katotohanan o mga detalye tungkol sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: The official term for being 'usi' or 'usyosero/usyosera'. It's what your tita does at family reunions when she asks, 'Kailan ka ikakasal?' It's the difference between asking 'How are you?' and asking 'So, how are you... *really*? Spill the tea!' It's investigation on a personal, sometimes annoying, level.
usage_notes: Can have a slightly negative connotation of being nosy or prying, but can also mean a formal inquiry.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **pag-uusisa**, nalaman niya ang lihim ng pamilya.","translation":"Because of her **prying**, she discovered the family's secret."},{"sentence":"Ang **pag-uusisa** ng pulisya ay nagdulot ng mga bagong ebidensya.","translation":"The police's **investigation** yielded new evidence."}]

translation: to be good; to behave well
meaning_filipino: Kumilos nang may kabaitan, ayon sa mabuting asal at pamantayan ng lipunan.
etymology: From `mag-` + `paka-` + `bait`. The `paka-` prefix intensifies the quality of the root word.
original_explanation: This is what your parents tell you before leaving you with your tita for the weekend. It's the command to activate your "good kid" mode, stop being a pasaway, and generally act like a decent human being, at least until they get back. "Magpakabait ka diyan, ha? May pasalubong ka pag-uwi ko."
usage_notes: Often used as a command or advice.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sabi ni Nanay, **magpakabait** daw ako sa eskwela.","translation":"Mom said I should **be good** at school."},{"sentence":"**Magpakabait** ka na para matuwa naman sa iyo ang mga magulang mo.","translation":"**Behave well** now so your parents will be happy with you."}]

translation: to form a lump; to bud
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbuo ng isang bukol o umbok; sa halaman, ito ay ang pagsisimulang lumabas ng usbong o bulaklak.
original_explanation: Like when you get a "bukol" on your head after walking into a glass door. Or for plants, it's that "getting ready to bloom" stage, like a rosebud about to show off. It's the physical manifestation of "may namumuong something."
usage_notes: Can refer to a lump on the body, a bud on a plant, or even a gathering of something into a mass.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsisimula nang **mamukol** ang mga usbong ng sampaguita sa hardin.","translation":"The sampaguita buds are starting to **form** in the garden."},{"sentence":"Nangati ang braso niya at nagsimulang **mamukol** dahil sa kagat ng lamok.","translation":"His arm itched and began to **form lumps** due to mosquito bites."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang manipis na bahagi ng katawan ng isda na ginagamit nito sa paglangoy, pagbalanse, at pagmamaneobra sa tubig.
etymology: Ang salitang-ugat na 'ligpig' mismo ay tumutukoy sa palikpik. Ang unlaping 'pa-' ay bahagi na ng salita sa karaniwang gamit.
original_explanation: 'Yung parang pakpak ng isda. Ito 'yung tinatanggal mo 'pag naglilinis ka ng isda para iprito, o 'yung matulis na parteng iniiwasan mo sa sinigang na baka tumusok sa lalamunan mo. It's the fish's steering wheel and propellers.
usage_notes: Isang espisipikong terminong biyolohikal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matulis ang **paligpig** ng isdang-espada.","translation":"The **fin** of a swordfish is sharp."},{"sentence":"Inalis niya ang mga **paligpig** at kaliskis bago lutuin ang isda.","translation":"She removed the **fins** and scales before cooking the fish."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi tuwid, baluktot, o liko. Sa moral na aspeto, ito ay nangangahulugang hindi makatarungan o hindi tama.
original_explanation: When someone says 'daang matuwid' (the straight path), this is the opposite. It's the crooked path, the sketchy deal, the politician's promise that sounds too good to be true. Yung kaibigan mong laging may 'shortcut' sa lahat ng bagay? Medyo di-matwid ang galawan.
usage_notes: Used both literally for physical straightness and metaphorically for moral or ethical correctness. The moral sense is more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinondena ng mga mamamayan ang **di-matwid** na pamamalakad ng gobyerno.","translation":"The citizens condemned the **unjust** governance of the administration."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang ruler para ayusin ang linyang **di-matwid**.","translation":"He used the ruler to fix the **crooked** line."}]

translation: to cause to shake; to rattle
meaning_filipino: Maging sanhi ng pagyanig o paggalaw nang pabalik-balik at mabilis.
original_explanation: What you do to a bottle of salad dressing, a can of spray paint, or your sibling when they won't wake up. It's also what a 7.2 magnitude earthquake does to your entire life and what chismis does to a peaceful friend group.
usage_notes: Distinct from `yugyugin` which is often more vigorous. `Paalugin` can be gentler.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **paalugin** ang bote bago ito inumin.","translation":"You need to **shake** the bottle before drinking it."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **paalugin** ang mesa, natatapon ang kape ko.","translation":"Don't **shake** the table, my coffee is spilling."}]

translation: to take a picture of (at a place/of a person)
meaning_filipino: Kunan ng larawan ang isang tao, bagay, o pook. Ang diin ay nasa lokasyon o sa taong binibigyan ng aksyon.
original_explanation: This is the verb you use when you're the designated photographer of the barkada. "Guys, ritratuhan niyo ako dito sa may wall art, pang-IG!" It focuses on *who* or *where* the photo is being taken, as opposed to just the object itself.
usage_notes: The suffix '-an' often implies the location or the recipient of the action. So, 'ritratuhan' means to take a picture *of* someone or *at* a certain place.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ritratuhan** mo naman ako habang maganda ang ilaw.","translation":"Please **take a picture of** me while the lighting is good."},{"sentence":"Ang simbahan sa Paoay ay paboritong **ritratuhan** ng mga turista.","translation":"The Paoay Church is a favorite place for tourists **to take pictures at**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na pagpapatalsik o pagpapaalis sa isang tao mula sa isang lugar, organisasyon, o paaralan bilang parusa.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'You can't sit with us!' It's what happens when you break the rules so bad that your school or organization gives you a permanent 'See you never.' It's like getting unfriended and blocked by an entire institution.
usage_notes: Mas karaniwang ginagamit ang salitang Ingles na 'expulsion' sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **espulsyon** mula sa unibersidad ang pinakamabigat na parusa.","translation":"**Expulsion** from the university is the most severe punishment."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na walang galang, mapusok, at padalus-dalos sa pagkilos o pananalita.
etymology: Posibleng mula sa Espanyol na "barrumbada," na nangangahulugang pagyayabang o isang hangal at magarbo na gastos, na nagbago upang mangahulugang isang padalus-dalos o mayabang na tao.
original_explanation: That jeepney driver who cuts you off without signaling? Barumbado. That guy who talks loudly on his phone inside the cinema? Barumbado. It’s a mix of reckless, rude, and having zero chill. It's the kind of person your mom warned you about.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang mga tsuper, basagulero, o sinumang kumikilos nang walang pagsasaalang-alang sa iba.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinagsabihan ng pulis ang **barumbado** na tsuper ng bus.","translation":"The police reprimanded the **reckless** bus driver."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa pagiging **barumbado** sa kalsada.","translation":"He is known for being **aggressive** on the road."}]

translation: by the way; to change the subject
meaning_filipino: Isang pahayag na ginagamit upang mag-umpisa ng bagong paksa o biglang palitan ang pinag-uusapan.
etymology: Literally 'may I be different,' it functions as a polite way to signal a topic shift.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'segway' phrase in Filipino chismisan. Your friends are talking about politics and it's getting heated. You jump in: '**Maiba ako**, nakita niyo na ba 'yung bagong Netflix series?' Boom. Subject changed, world saved. It's the conversational CTRL+ALT+DEL.
usage_notes: Used to smoothly (or abruptly) change the topic of conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Maiba ako**, kumusta na pala ang project na pinapagawa sa atin?","translation":"**By the way**, how's that project that was assigned to us?"},{"sentence":"Ang init ng usapan nila tungkol sa basketball. Sabi ko, '**Maiba ako**, anong oras na ba?'","translation":"Their conversation about basketball was so heated. I said, '**To change the subject**, what time is it?'"}]

translation: suddenly, all of a sudden, abruptly
meaning_filipino: Sa paraang biglaan, hindi inaasahan, at walang anumang babala.
etymology: Mula sa 'ka-' at pag-uulit ng 'ginsa', isang lumang salita para sa 'gulat' o 'bigla'.
original_explanation: That moment when you're just chilling, scrolling through TikTok, then kaginsa-ginsa your boss messages you with an "Urgent" task. It's the "out of nowhere" plot twist of your day. Parang biglang pag-ulan nang wala kang dalang payong.
usage_notes: Madalas itong sinusundan ng pariralang "na lamang" upang bigyang-diin ang pagiging biglaan, hal. "kaginsa-ginsa na lamang". Ito ay kasingkahulugan ng "bigla-bigla" o "walang anu-ano".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kaginsa-ginsa** na lamang ay sumulpot ang isang pusa mula sa ilalim ng mesa.","translation":"**All of a sudden**, a cat appeared from under the table."},{"sentence":"Tahimik ang gabi nang **kaginsa-ginsa** ay may narinig kaming malakas na sigaw.","translation":"The night was quiet when **suddenly** we heard a loud shout."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng mabilis at hirap na paghinga, karaniwan ay dahil sa matinding pagod, takot, o sakit.
original_explanation: That feeling after you run to catch the MRT right before the doors close, or after climbing five flights of stairs because the elevator is broken. You're bent over, hands on your knees, trying to get your life back. It's the physical manifestation of 'pagod na 'ko,' whether from a literal chase or a metaphorical one (like chasing deadlines).
usage_notes: This is an idiomatic phrase.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Naghabol ng hininga** ang bata matapos takbuhin ang buong basketball court.","translation":"The child was **gasping for breath** after running the entire basketball court."},{"sentence":"Huminto muna kami sa pag-akyat ng bundok para hindi **maghabol ng hininga**.","translation":"We paused our mountain climb for a bit so we wouldn't be **out of breath**."}]

translation: to text; to send a text message
meaning_filipino: Gumamit ng cellphone upang magpadala ng mensaheng text (SMS).
original_explanation: The infinitive form of the national past-time. It's the action of sending a short message instead of making a full call, usually to say 'OTW na' (even when you just got out of the shower) or to ask 'Wer u na?'
usage_notes: The infinitive form. Extremely common. It has completely replaced older, more formal phrases.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang tumawag, **mag-text** ka na lang dahil nasa meeting ako.","translation":"Don't call, **just text** because I'm in a meeting."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **mag-text** sa akin tuwing madaling araw.","translation":"He/She likes **to text** me during the early morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking mag-aaral na naninirahan sa loob ng isang paaralan o isang kaakibat na dormitoryo.
original_explanation: The male counterpart to the 'interna'. This is the boy who lives in the school dorm, probably in a seminary or an exclusive all-boys' school from a bygone era. He's the character in a classic film who's either a bookworm or the leader of a gang planning to sneak out for the town fiesta.
usage_notes: A dated term, less common than its medical counterpart. The female equivalent is 'interna'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Noong panahon ng mga Kastila, maraming kabataang lalaki ang naging **interno** sa mga seminaryo.","translation":"During the Spanish era, many young men became **boarders** in seminaries."},{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang mga patakaran para sa mga **interno** sa aming paaralan.","translation":"The rules are strict for the male **boarders** in our school."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salita o gawa na naglalayong saktan ang damdamin, mang-uyam, o magpakita ng kawalan ng galang sa isang tao.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na sinabihan ka ng "parang tumaba ka," pero with matching side-eye. It's the verbal equivalent of a slap, often delivered by a marites or a frenemy. Sa social media, ito yung mga comments na gusto mong i-delete, i-block, at i-report.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko matatanggap ang **insulto** mo sa aking pamilya.","translation":"I will not accept your **insult** to my family."},{"sentence":"Para sa kanya, biro lang iyon, pero para sa akin, isang malaking **insulto**.","translation":"For him, it was just a joke, but for me, it was a big **insult**."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa kultura ng mga tagahanga (fandom), ito ang tawag sa paboritong miyembro ng isang grupo, lalo na sa K-Pop.
original_explanation: "Sino'ng bias mo sa BTS?" is the modern-day "What's your sign?". It's your absolute favorite, the one you'd save all your photocards for, the one whose solo career you're already funding in your head. You can have a bias, and a bias-wrecker (the one who makes you question your loyalty to your bias).
usage_notes: Pronounced with an English accent. Used almost exclusively in fandom contexts, especially K-Pop, P-Pop, and other idol groups.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Jungkook ang **bias** ko, pero si V ang bias-wrecker ko!","translation":"Jungkook is my **bias**, but V is my bias-wrecker!"}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang bagay o bahagi ng katawan na maraming bikat o peklat.
original_explanation: Eto yung description sa tuhod ng bawat batang 90s. Kung ang balat mo ay parang mapa ng Pilipinas sa dami ng isla ng peklat, 'yan ay bikatan. Parang balat ng warrior na galing sa maraming laban... o sa maraming laro ng patintero at tumbang-preso.
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang ilarawan ang isang ibabaw, karaniwan ay balat, na puno ng mga peklat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bikatan** ang kanyang mga binti dahil sa mga kagat ng insekto noong bata pa.","translation":"His legs are **scarred** from insect bites when he was a child."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa giyera, **bikatan** ang katawan ng sundalo.","translation":"Because of the war, the soldier's body was **full of scars**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang pag-iwas na bigyan ng atensyon ang isang tao o bagay; pagpapanggap na hindi nakikita o naririnig.
original_explanation: The ultimate "snub" move. When you see your ex at the mall and you suddenly become intensely interested in the floor tiles. Or when a client you're avoiding calls and you stare at your phone until it stops ringing. That's you trying to magkunwang di-pansin. The art of strategic ignorance.
usage_notes: A very common and specific phrase describing a social action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita niya ang utang sa kanya pero **nagkunwang di-pansin** na lang siya para iwas-gulo.","translation":"He saw the person who owed him money but he just **pretended not to notice** to avoid trouble."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **magkunwang di-pansin** kapag ang crush mo ay nasa harap mo na.","translation":"It's hard to **pretend not to notice** when your crush is already in front of you."}]

meaning_filipino: Maaaring tumukoy sa isang patag na kagamitan na may butas para sa hinlalaki na pinagtitimplahan ng pintor ng mga kulay; isang maliit na pala na ginagamit sa konstruksyon; o isang uri ng matamis na pinalamig na pagkain na nakatusok sa patpat.
etymology: From Spanish 'paleta', meaning 'small shovel', 'palette', or 'shoulder blade'.
original_explanation: This word is a multi-tasker. It can be the artist's mixing board for their next masterpiece, the construction worker's tool for applying semento (the "dulos"), or—most importantly—that cheap, delicious ice drop you buy from a street vendor on a hot day. The avocado or monggo flavor? A core childhood memory.
usage_notes: The meaning depends heavily on context. The "ice pop" meaning is very common in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ng pintor ang kanyang **paleta** upang paghaluin ang asul at dilaw.","translation":"The painter used his **palette** to mix blue and yellow."},{"sentence":"Paborito ko ang **paleta** na may lasang mangga.","translation":"My favorite **ice pop** is the mango-flavored one."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malubhang impeksyon sa baga na nagdudulot ng pamamaga sa mga air sac (alveoli), na maaaring mapuno ng likido o nana.
original_explanation: This is that serious lung sickness that your lola always warns you about when you go out with wet hair or sleep in front of the electric fan. "Magkaka-pulmunya ka!" It's the leveled-up version of a bad cold or flu, and you definitely need a doctor for it. Not to be confused with 'pulmon', which is just the Spanish word for lung.
usage_notes: A medical term commonly used in households. The formal medical term is 'niyumonya' from English 'pneumonia', but 'pulmunya' is very widespread.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala siya sa ospital dahil sa **pulmunya**.","translation":"He was brought to the hospital because of **pneumonia**."},{"sentence":"Ang pagpapabakuna ay makakatulong upang maiwasan ang **pulmunya**.","translation":"Getting vaccinated can help prevent **pneumonia**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagdaan ng isang kard (gaya ng credit card o key card) sa isang aparato; sa balbal na kahulugan, ito ay pagnanakaw o pagkuha ng isang bagay na hindi sa iyo.
original_explanation: Can mean two very different things. 1) The sound your credit card makes when you buy something you can't afford ('I-**swipe** mo na, besh!'). 2) What happens to your phone if you leave it unattended in Quiapo ('Na-**swipe** yung phone ko!'). Context is everything!
usage_notes: Ang kahulugan ay lubos na nakadepende sa konteksto. Ang kahulugang 'magnakaw' ay balbal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**swipe** na lang po ng credit card ko para sa bayad.","translation":"Please just **swipe** my credit card for the payment."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa Divisoria, baka ma-**swipe** ang wallet mo.","translation":"Be careful in Divisoria, your wallet might get **swiped** (stolen)."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng isip na namamagitan sa kamalayan at sa panlabas na katotohanan; ang pagtingin ng isang tao sa kanyang sariling kahalagahan.
etymology: Mula sa Latin na "ego", na nangangahulugang "ako".
original_explanation: Your 'ego' is that little voice in your head that gets hurt when someone leaves you on 'seen'. It's what makes you post 15 IG stories when you're on vacation. When a Pinoy says "tinapakan mo ang ego ko," it means you've deeply offended their pride, probably by beating them at karaoke.
usage_notes: Used in the same psychological and common sense as in English.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masyadong mataas ang **ego** niya kaya ayaw niyang aminin ang pagkakamali.","translation":"His **ego** is too big, that's why he doesn't want to admit his mistake."},{"sentence":"Nasaktan ang **ego** ko noong hindi niya ako pinansin.","translation":"My **ego** was hurt when they ignored me."}]

translation: drenched, soaked (of the lower part of clothing)
meaning_filipino: Pagkabasa ng ibabang bahagi ng damit, tulad ng laylayan ng pantalon o saya, dahil sa paglusong sa tubig, putik, o paglakad sa matataas at basang damo.
original_explanation: The feeling of your pants' cuffs being wet and clingy after walking through a flooded Manila street or a dewy field. It's that uncomfortable dampness that slowly creeps up your leg. The mortal enemy of anyone wearing brand-new white pants during rainy season.
usage_notes: Describes a specific type of wetness, usually from the ground up. The verb form is 'masaog'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Saog** ang laylayan ng pantalon ko dahil sa baha.","translation":"The hem of my pants is **soaked** because of the flood."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa paglalakad sa damuhan, baka ma**saog** ang bestida mo.","translation":"Be careful walking on the grass, your dress might get **drenched** at the bottom."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis na pagtingin o pagtanaw sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: The classic move when your crush walks by. You can't stare (baka mahalata), so you just 'sumulyap'. It's that quick, almost-didn't-happen look. Also what you do to your seatmate's paper during an exam, but you know, don't.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigla siyang **sumulyap** sa akin kaya napaiwas ako ng tingin.","translation":"He/she suddenly **glanced** at me so I looked away."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **sumulyap** sa katabi mo habang may pagsusulit.","translation":"Don't **glance** at your seatmate during an exam."}]

translation: to flutter about; to fly around
meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit at walang tiyak na direksyong paglipad sa isang lugar, tulad ng ginagawa ng paruparo o ibon.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung galaw ng paruparo sa garden o 'yung lamok sa kwarto mo na ayaw kang patulugin. Hindi siya straight-line flight from point A to B; it's more like flying around aimlessly, enjoying the vibe. Parang 'yung isip mo kapag nagde-daydream ka sa gitna ng klase.
usage_notes: The repetition of 'lipad' indicates a continuous, often erratic or leisurely, flying motion, not a purposeful flight.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masayang **lumipad-lipad** ang mga paruparo sa hardin.","translation":"The butterflies happily **fluttered about** in the garden."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng sayaw na panlipunan na isinasagawa ng apat na pares sa isang parisukat na pormasyon. Maaari ring tumukoy sa isang pangkat ng mga tao, lalo na ang mga armado o may partikular na layunin.
original_explanation: The original squad goals. In old Filipino movies, it's that fancy Spanish dance at the governor's ball (the Rigodon de Honor is a type of this). But it can also mean a posse or gang, like a 'kuwadrilya ng mga bandido.' So it's either you're dancing gracefully or you're about to cause some trouble.
usage_notes: Has two main meanings: a formal dance and a group/squad, often with a slightly negative or rough connotation for the latter.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kuwadrilya** ay isang tanyag na sayaw noong panahon ng mga Espanyol.","translation":"The **quadrille** was a popular dance during the Spanish era."},{"sentence":"Hinahanap ng mga pulis ang **kuwadrilya** ng mga magnanakaw na nanloob sa bangko.","translation":"The police are looking for the **posse** of thieves who robbed the bank."}]

translation: to wilt something (by heat); to scald
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapalambot o pagpapalanta ng dahon o gulay sa pamamagitan ng pagdaraan nito sa apoy o mainit na tubig.
original_explanation: This is a classic kitchen prep move. You *languhin* the banana leaves over a flame to make them pliable for wrapping suman or bibingka. It's like giving the leaves a quick spa treatment so they don't tear. In life, sometimes you feel *nilalango* by stress—heated up and softened until you're about to break.
usage_notes: Primarily used in a culinary context, especially with leaves for wrapping food. Do not confuse with 'langu-languhin' (to fool).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **languhin** ang dahon ng saging bago gamitin pangbalot.","translation":"You need **to wilt** the banana leaf before using it as a wrapper."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahabang piraso ng kahoy na may lapad na dulo, ginagamit upang itulak ang tubig at paandarin ang isang bangka.
original_explanation: The manual engine of a small boat. Before outboard motors, this was your arm day at the gym. It's the thing you use to move your bangka across the river, or what you threaten your lazy kasama with if they don't help paddle. 'Sagwan' is a more common term, but gaod is the classic.
usage_notes: 'Sagwan' is a more common synonym. 'Gaod' can also be used as a verb (gumagaod - paddling).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawala ang isang **gaod** kaya paikot-ikot na lang ang aming bangka.","translation":"One **oar** was lost, so our boat was just going in circles."}]
