meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan o pangkat na mayroong pangkalahatang pagkainggit o paghihilian sa isa't isa. (Lubhang bihirang gamitin)
etymology: From `ka-` + `hili` (envy) + `-an`. A theoretical construction denoting a collective or abstract state.
original_explanation: This is that group chat where everyone is secretly jealous of everyone else's travel pics and job promotions. It's the 'Maritess' headquarters where envy is the main topic. A very rare word, you're more likely to use 'inggitan'.
usage_notes: This word is not in common use and its meaning is inferred from its morphemes. `Inggitan` or `pagkainggit` are the standard terms.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kahilian** sa kanilang departamento ay nagdulot ng hindi magandang samahan.","translation":"The **mutual envy** in their department resulted in a toxic environment."}]

translation: to memorize; to scold/lecture someone by bringing up past mistakes
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagsasaulo ng isang bagay. Sa kolokyal na paggamit, ito ay ang panunumbat o pagpapaalala sa isang tao ng kanyang mga nakaraang pagkakamali o utang na loob.
original_explanation: This word has two personalities. Yung una, yung student mode: "Kailangan kong memoryahin lahat ng 'to for the exam!" Yung pangalawa, a.k.a. the "Sumbat Mode" ng mga magulang o jowa: "Nagsimula lang sa 'di mo paghugas ng plato, na-memorya na sa'kin lahat ng kasalanan ko since birth!" It's when someone recites your entire history of failures like a pro.
usage_notes: The colloquial meaning of 'scolding by bringing up the past' is very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **memoryahin** sa lahat ng nagawa kong mali dati!","translation":"Don't **lecture me** by bringing up all the mistakes I made in the past!"},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **memoryahin** ang mga linya mo para sa dula.","translation":"You need to **memorize** your lines for the play."}]

meaning_filipino: Magbibigay ng tugon o kasagutan sa isang tanong, tawag, o sitwasyon. Ito ay nasa aspetong panghinaharap.
original_explanation: That moment of truth when your boss asks 'Who's responsible for this?'. Or when your phone rings with an unknown number and you debate whether to pick up. 'Sasagot' ka ba? It's the future tense of taking accountability, responding to a call, or finally replying to that 3-week-old chat.
usage_notes: Standard future tense conjugation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sasagot** ako sa tanong ng guro mamaya.","translation":"I **will answer** the teacher's question later."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **sasagot** sa telepono kung wala tayo sa bahay?","translation":"Who **will answer** the phone if we're not at home?"}]

translation: suited for each other; fitting together
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa dalawang bagay na magkatugma, magkabagay, o akma sa isa't isa.
original_explanation: When the lid perfectly fits the Tupperware container after a long search in the kitchen drawer. When your skills are the exact match for a job description. When two puzzle pieces click into place. That satisfying feeling of a perfect fit is `magkaagpang`. It's the universe saying, "Bagay!"
usage_notes: `Agpang` means fit or suitable. `Magkaagpang` emphasizes the mutual or reciprocal fitness between two or more things.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **magkaagpang** ang takip at ang kahon para maisara ito nang maayos.","translation":"The lid and the box need to **fit together** to close it properly."},{"sentence":"Hindi **magkaagpang** ang kanilang mga pananaw kaya sila laging nagtatalo.","translation":"Their views are not **suited for each other** which is why they always argue."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hukuman na may kapangyarihang dinggin at pagpasyahan ang mga apela mula sa mga desisyon ng mga mababang hukuman. Ito ang pangalawang pinakamataas na tribunal sa Pilipinas, sunod sa Korte Suprema.
etymology: Combination of "hukuman" (court) and "paghahabol" (the act of appealing/chasing).
original_explanation: This is the "Sana All May Second Chance" court. If you lost your case in a lower court (like the RTC), you can 'appeal' or 'habol' your case here. It's like asking for a manager review when the first customer service rep can't solve your problem.
usage_notes: This is the official name of the Philippine Court of Appeals.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inakyat ng kanyang abogado ang kaso sa **Hukuman sa Paghahabol**.","translation":"His lawyer elevated the case to the **Court of Appeals**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pagluluto kung saan piniprito ang mga sangkap tulad ng bawang, sibuyas, at kamatis sa kaunting mainit na mantika.
original_explanation: The holy trinity of Filipino cooking: bawang, sibuyas, kamatis. 'Igisa' is the first step to almost every ulam. It's the official sound and smell that tells everyone in the house, 'Ulam is coming!' The foundation of flavor that separates a sad meal from a fiesta.
usage_notes: A fundamental cooking term in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Igisa** mo muna ang bawang at sibuyas hanggang sa maging golden brown.","translation":"**Sauté** the garlic and onions first until they turn golden brown."},{"sentence":"Mas masarap ang monggo kapag **ginisa** sa maraming sahog.","translation":"Mung bean soup is more delicious when **sautéed** with many ingredients."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay, tao, o pangyayari na nagiging sanhi ng pagkalimot o pagkawala ng isang alaala sa isipan.
original_explanation: This is your 'amnesia' trigger. It could be a new crush that makes you forget your ex, a really good K-drama that makes you forget your deadlines, or a shot of tequila. Anything that helps you press the 'delete' button on a memory or a problem, even temporarily.
usage_notes: Used to describe something that induces forgetfulness, often in the context of emotional pain, worries, or responsibilities.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang alak ay hindi solusyon; pansamantala lang itong **nakapagpapalimot** ng problema.","translation":"Alcohol is not a solution; it only temporarily **makes one forget** their problems."},{"sentence":"Ang pagiging abala sa trabaho ay **nakapagpapalimot** sa akin ng kalungkutan.","translation":"Being busy at work **makes me forget** my sadness."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsuot ng bakya, isang uri ng tradisyonal na sapin sa paa na yari sa kahoy.
original_explanation: Channeling your inner old-school Pinoy. It's the act of wearing those iconic, noisy wooden sandals. Perfect for making a grand entrance (everyone will hear you coming) or for when you want to feel like a character in a classic Filipino film. Clack-clack-clack!
usage_notes: 'Bakya' can also be used pejoratively to mean something is of low-class taste or 'Jejemon', but 'magbakya' specifically refers to the act of wearing the footwear.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Noong araw, karaniwang makikita ang mga taong **nagbabakya** sa probinsya.","translation":"In the old days, it was common to see people **wearing wooden clogs** in the province."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **magbakya** sa unang pagkakataon at nahirapan siyang maglakad.","translation":"She tried to **wear wooden clogs** for the first time and found it difficult to walk."}]

translation: to treat someone like a child
meaning_filipino: Pakitunguhan ang isang tao na para bang siya ay isang bata pa, kadalasan sa paraang minamaliit o hindi isinasaalang-alang ang kanyang edad o kakayahan.
original_explanation: When your parents still talk to you like you're 12, even though you're 32 and paying your own bills. It’s that condescending tone someone uses, implying you don't know any better. 'Huwag mo akong magbataan; alam ko ang ginagawa ko.' is the classic comeback of every adult-in-progress.
usage_notes: Carries a negative connotation of condescension or belittling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw ng mga tinedyer na sila ay laging **minamagbataan** ng kanilang mga magulang.","translation":"Teenagers don't like it when their parents always **treat them like children**."},{"sentence":"Kahit ako ang bunso, huwag mo akong **magbataan** dahil may sarili na akong isip.","translation":"Even if I'm the youngest, don't **treat me like a child** because I have my own mind."}]

translation: to grope for; to fumble for
meaning_filipino: Hanapin ang isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng kamay o pakiramdam, lalo na kapag hindi ito makita.
original_explanation: This is what you do when the power goes out and you're trying to find your phone or a candle. It's that frantic, blind patting motion on your bedside table. It's also used figuratively for trying to grasp a difficult idea.
usage_notes: Often implies searching for something in the dark or without the sense of sight.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umapuhap** siya ng switch ng ilaw sa dilim.","translation":"He **groped** for the light switch in the dark."},{"sentence":"Tila siya'y **umapuapuhap** ng tamang salita na sasabihin.","translation":"It seems he was **fumbling** for the right words to say."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paraang nanunukso, nang-aakit, o nang-iinis nang bahagya.
original_explanation: That look your friend gives you when they know your crush is walking by. Or how a food vlogger describes a lechon belly—patukso. It's doing something in a way that's meant to tease or tempt, like dangling a piece of chicharon in front of someone on a diet.
usage_notes: Often implies a playful or mischievous intent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ngumiti siya nang **patukso** habang inaalok ang huling piraso ng cake.","translation":"She smiled **teasingly** while offering the last piece of cake."},{"sentence":"Tumingin siya sa akin nang **patukso**, na para bang may alam siyang hindi ko alam.","translation":"He looked at me **teasingly**, as if he knew something I didn't."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kawalan ng interes, pag-aalala, o atensyon sa isang tao, bagay, o sitwasyon na karaniwang nangangailangan nito.
etymology: From 'pag-' (gerund prefix) + 'walang-bahala' (indifferent), which is from 'wala' (none) and 'bahala' (care, responsibility).
original_explanation: The official term for 'seen-zoning' someone's crisis. It's when you know you have a deadline but you watch 'one more episode' anyway. It's the 'Bahala na si Batman' attitude but without the heroic part. It's the ultimate 'dedma' move, the art of pretending you don't care, even when maybe you should.
usage_notes: A compound noun that is always hyphenated. Carries a negative connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagwawalang-bahala** sa pag-aaral ay nagdulot ng mababang marka.","translation":"His **neglect** of his studies resulted in low grades."},{"sentence":"Hindi katanggap-tanggap ang **pagwawalang-bahala** ng gobyerno sa mga mahihirap.","translation":"The government's **apathy** towards the poor is unacceptable."}]

meaning_filipino: Maramihang anyo ng bota; mga sapatos na mataas na tumatakip sa paa at bukong-bukong o binti.
original_explanation: Plural form of 'bota'. When you have more than one, or you're talking about the pair. 'Saan mo nabili 'yang botas mo?' is asking about the pair you're wearing. Ito ang go-to word for rain boots, combat boots, or any pair of boots you own.
usage_notes: While 'mga bota' is the grammatically standard plural, 'botas' is very common in spoken language, directly borrowing the Spanish plural form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magsuot ka ng **botas** dahil maputik sa labas.","translation":"Wear **boots** because it's muddy outside."},{"sentence":"Ang bigat ng **botas** na suot ng sundalo.","translation":"The **boots** worn by the soldier are heavy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbuo o pagkakaroon ng sapot o bahay ng gagamba sa isang lugar.
original_explanation: When you haven't cleaned your room for so long that it looks like Spider-Man's secret HQ. 'Hala, nag-magsapot na 'yung lumang gitara sa bodega.'
usage_notes: Often used to describe old, neglected, or abandoned places.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong pabayaang **magsapot** ang mga libro mo sa estante.","translation":"Don't let your books on the shelf get **covered in cobwebs**."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula nang **magsapot** ang kisame dahil matagal nang walang nakatira.","translation":"The ceiling has started to **get covered in cobwebs** because it has been uninhabited for a long time."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggalaw ng katawan kasabay ng musika na naganap na.
original_explanation: This is the past tense of that TikTok dance you tried to learn. "Sumayaw ako sa party kagabi, pero sa isip ko lang" (I danced at the party last night, but only in my head). It's the action of dancing, completed. The memory of you busting a move, whether gracefully or like a malfunctioning robot.
usage_notes: This is the completed aspect of the verb, indicating that the action of dancing has finished.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumayaw** siya ng tinikling sa pagtatanghal.","translation":"She **danced** the tinikling at the performance."},{"sentence":"Lahat kami ay **sumayaw** hanggang mag-umaga.","translation":"All of us **danced** until morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang takdang halaga ng salapi na inilaan para sa isang partikular na layunin o panahon.
etymology: Hango sa wikang Ingles na 'budget', mula sa Lumang Pranses na 'bougette' (maliit na sisidlang balat).
original_explanation: The mortal enemy of every "add to cart" impulse. It's the plan you make for your sweldo that you almost never follow. When someone says "Wala sa badyet," it means "I'm broke until the next payday."
usage_notes: A very common Filipinized spelling of the English word 'budget'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating maghigpit ng sinturon dahil maliit lang ang **badyet** natin ngayong buwan.","translation":"We need to tighten our belts because we only have a small **budget** this month."},{"sentence":"Magkano ang **badyet** mo para sa proyekto?","translation":"How much is your **budget** for the project?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pandiwa na tumutukoy sa pagkilos o proseso ng pagiging maputla o pamumutla.
original_explanation: This is the verb form. It's what happens *to you* when you see a ghost, or more realistically, your ex with their new partner. You don't just *have* paleness (putla), you *become* pale (**putlain** ka).
usage_notes: Ang pandiwang ito ay madalas gamitin sa anyong balintiyak (passive) tulad ng 'pinutla' (was made pale). Mas karaniwan ang paggamit ng 'mamutla' para ipahayag ang 'to become pale'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tila **puputlain** siya sa sobrang nerbiyos bago ang kanyang presentasyon.","translation":"It seems she **will become pale** from so much nervousness before her presentation."},{"sentence":"**Pinutla** siya ng matinding takot.","translation":"Extreme fear **made her pale**."}]

meaning_filipino: Mag-alaga, magparami, o magtinda ng mga baka.
original_explanation: Basically, being a Filipino cowboy or rancher. It's all about that moo-lah. You're not just selling beef, you're in the 'baka' business.
usage_notes: This refers to the business or occupation of dealing with cattle, not to be confused with the expression 'baka' (maybe).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May malawak na rantso ang pamilya nila kung saan sila **nagbabaka**.","translation":"Their family has a wide ranch where they **raise cattle**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang pandamdam na nagpapahayag ng pagtataka, pagkalito, o bahagyang pagkadismaya.
original_explanation: The sound you make when your friend cancels plans last minute, or when the chismis you heard turns out to be fake news. It's a milder, more confused version of 'Hala!' or 'Anyare?'. It’s the verbal equivalent of the blinking white guy meme.
usage_notes: Often used in informal, spoken conversations or text messages.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nge**, akala ko ba tuloy tayo?","translation":"**Huh?**, I thought we were pushing through?"},{"sentence":"Wala na daw stock. **Nge** naman.","translation":"They said there's no more stock. **Eh?** That's a bummer."}]

meaning_filipino: Patayin at hiwa-hiwain ang isang hayop para sa konsumo. Sa makabagong gamit, maaari ring tumukoy sa pagtanggal o pagwawakas sa isang bagay nang biglaan.
original_explanation: The command form of "katay." It's the order given to the butcher: "Katayin mo na 'yang manok." Figuratively, it's what your strict manager does to your poorly-written report, or what happens to a project when the budget gets pulled. "Kinatay yung proposal ko."
usage_notes: The verb form of 'katay'. Can be used literally and figuratively.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang mag-**kakatay** ng manok para sa tinola?","translation":"Who will **slaughter** the chicken for the tinola?"},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **katayin** ang budget para sa mahalagang proyektong ito.","translation":"Don't **butcher** the budget for this important project."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan ibinababa o dinadala ang mga kalakal, karaniwan ay mga produktong agrikultural, para sa malawakang pagbebenta.
original_explanation: The OG Lazada/Shopee hub. This is where farmers drop off their produce in bulk before it gets distributed to your local palengke. It's chaotic, busy 24/7, and smells like fresh vegetables and hard work. In modern slang, it can also mean a beat drop in music. 'Ang tindi ng bagsakan ng bass!'
usage_notes: The stress on the last syllable /bag-sa-KAN/ distinguishes it from the verb /BAG-sa-kan/ (to drop something on).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala ng mga magsasaka ang kanilang ani sa **bagsakan** sa Divisoria.","translation":"The farmers brought their harvest to the **wholesale market** in Divisoria."}]

translation: container for transferring liquids; transfusion area
meaning_filipino: Isang sisidlan na ginagamit upang paglipatan ng likido; lugar kung saan isinasagawa ang pagsasalin, partikular ng dugo.
original_explanation: That extra 'tabo' or pitcher you grab when you're trying to move water from a big drum to a smaller pail. In a hospital, it's the room or station where you get a blood transfusion. It's the middleman container or location.
usage_notes: The suffix '-an' denotes a place or an instrument used for the action of the root word 'salin' (transfer).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gamitin mo ang malinis na **pasalinan** para sa gatas.","translation":"Use the clean **container** to transfer the milk."},{"sentence":"Dinala siya sa **pasalinan** para sa dugo.","translation":"She was brought to the **transfusion area** for blood."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang makapal at malamig na sarsa o pampalasa na karaniwang gawa sa langis, itlog, at suka o lemon juice.
original_explanation: Ang lifeblood ng chicken sandwich at macaroni salad. 'Yung palaman na akala mo healthy pero 'pag nalaman mo kung paano gawin, parang pure taba lang pala. Essential sa handaan, lalo na 'pag Pasko.
usage_notes: Spelled "mayonnaise" in English, but the Spanish spelling "mayonesa" is common in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiabot ng **mayonesa** para sa sandwich ko.","translation":"Please pass the **mayonnaise** for my sandwich."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang fruit salad kapag maraming **mayonesa** at condensed milk.","translation":"The fruit salad is delicious when it has a lot of **mayonnaise** and condensed milk."}]

meaning_filipino: Hayag at walang takip; lantad sa paningin ng lahat at hindi na lihim.
original_explanation: Kapag nakalantad ka, you are out in the open. Walang tago-tago. Puwedeng 'yung pagkain sa buffet table, nakalantad at ready to be eaten. Puwede ring 'yung sikreto mong matagal nang tinago, biglang nakalantad dahil sa isang chismosa. It's the state of being "out there" for everyone to see. Very similar to "nakaladlad" but more on exposure than spreading out.
usage_notes: Emphasizes the state of being unconcealed or public. Often used for secrets, truths, or vulnerabilities that are brought into the open.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga paninda ay **nakalantad** sa ilalim ng sikat ng araw.","translation":"The goods are **exposed** under the heat of the sun."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa social media, ang kanyang pribadong buhay ay **nakalantad** sa lahat.","translation":"Because of social media, her private life is **exposed** to everyone."}]

translation: pair, set of two; a beef stew dish
meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat na binubuo ng dalawang magkatulad o magkaakmang bagay. Tumutukoy din ito sa isang tanyag na lutuing Pilipino na binubuo ng karneng baka na may sabaw at kanin.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'pares' (pairs, plural of 'par').
original_explanation: Can mean a 'pair' of shoes, socks, or lovers. But let's be real, 99% of the time, it refers to that glorious braised beef stew served with garlic rice ('sinangag') and a bowl of clear broth. The ultimate 'after-inuman' or rainy day comfort food. 'Tara, mag-pares tayo!' is a love language.
usage_notes: While it literally means 'pair', its culinary meaning is extremely prominent in modern Filipino culture. The dish is called 'pares' because the beef is 'paired' with rice.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng bagong **pares** ng sapatos.","translation":"I bought a new **pair** of shoes."},{"sentence":"Gutom na ako, kain tayo sa paborito kong **pares**-an.","translation":"I'm hungry, let's eat at my favorite **pares** diner."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na may ugaling labis na ipagmalaki ang kanyang mga ari-arian, kakayahan, o nagawa, kadalasan sa paraang nakakainis o nakakainsulto.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `mapag-` (pagkahilig), `ma-`, at salitang-ugat na `yabang` (arogance, boastfulness).
original_explanation: This is the person who unboxes their new iPhone on IG Live. Yung tipong kahit bumili lang ng kape sa Starbucks, kailangan naka-post with the logo perfectly angled. They love to "flex." Lahat ng bagay, achievement man o gamit, kailangan ipangalandakan sa buong mundo.
usage_notes: Bagaman katulad ng `mapagmataas`, ang `mapagmayabang` ay mas tumutukoy sa pagpapakitang-gilas ng mga ari-arian o nagawa, habang ang `mapagmataas` ay mas tungkol sa panloob na pakiramdam ng pagiging superior sa iba.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay **mapagmayabang**; laging ipinapakita ang kanyang mga bagong gamit.","translation":"He is **boastful**; always showing off his new things."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **mapagmayabang** sa iyong mga tagumpay.","translation":"Don't be **boastful** about your successes."}]

translation: to make or sell bagoong (fermented paste)
meaning_filipino: Tumukoy sa gawain ng paggawa o pagtitinda ng bagoong.
original_explanation: To be the person responsible for creating that pungent, umami-rich condiment that defines many Filipino dishes. They are the unsung heroes of kare-kare and mangga't bagoong. A true artisan of funk.
usage_notes: Refers to the occupation or act of being a bagoong maker or vendor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lola niya ay kilala sa buong bayan dahil masarap siyang **magbagoong**.","translation":"His grandmother is known throughout the town because she is good at **making bagoong**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging hindi magkatumbas o magkapareho, lalo na sa katayuan, karapatan, at oportunidad.
etymology: Mula sa 'di' (not) at 'kapantayan' (equality), na nagmula sa ugat na 'pantay'.
original_explanation: It’s when your sibling gets the bigger piece of chicken, the latest iPhone, and no curfew, while you get chores and a 9 PM deadline. That, my friend, is a classic case of **di-kapantayan** in the household. The OG 'sana all' moment.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa mga talakayan tungkol sa lipunan, ekonomiya, at politika.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **di-kapantayan** sa lipunan ay isang malaking isyu na dapat tugunan.","translation":"Social **inequality** is a major issue that must be addressed."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang subkultura na nakasentro sa isang uri ng musikang rock na may emosyonal na liriko. Tumutukoy rin sa taong bahagi ng subkulturang ito, na kadalasang mayroong partikular na istilo ng pananamit at buhok.
etymology: From English "emo," short for "emotive hardcore," a genre of rock music.
original_explanation: Flashback to the mid-2000s: black eyeliner, side-swept bangs covering one eye, skinny jeans, and a steady diet of My Chemical Romance and The Used. An emo was that kid in your high school class who wrote deep poetry in their notebook and probably had a blog full of angsty song lyrics. They felt things... deeply.
usage_notes: Refers to the music genre, the fashion, and the people associated with the subculture.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang makinig sa mga bandang **emo** noong high school.","translation":"He loved listening to **emo** bands during high school."},{"sentence":"Yung pormahan niya, parang **emo** pa rin hanggang ngayon.","translation":"His style is still like an **emo** kid's until now."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga patpat, karaniwang yari sa kawayan o metal, na ginagamit sa pagtuhog ng pagkain tulad ng karne upang ihawin.
original_explanation: The unsung hero of Filipino street food. Without skewers, there would be no isaw, betamax, adidas, or pork barbecue. It's the magical stick that transforms random meat parts into 15-peso treasures. Also, the official pointing device at the "turo-turo" section of the palengke. Just be careful not to poke your eye out after dipping it in the communal suka container.
usage_notes: Ang Tagalog na katumbas ay "tuhog" o "pantuhog," ngunit ang "skewers" ay karaniwang ginagamit, lalo na sa mga menu o sa urban na konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pabili po ng sampung **skewers** ng isaw.","translation":"I'd like to buy ten **skewers** of isaw (chicken intestine)."},{"sentence":"Maingat niyang tinuhog ang baboy sa mga **skewers** na kawayan.","translation":"He carefully threaded the pork onto the bamboo **skewers**."}]

translation: hardship; burden; something that causes difficulty
meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, tao, o sitwasyon na nagdudulot ng paghihirap, pasanin, o balakid.
original_explanation: Your 5-hour commute in EDSA? That's a pahirap. The groupmate who doesn't contribute but gets the same grade? Pahirap. Unstable internet connection during a crucial online meeting? Super pahirap. It's anything or anyone that makes your life feel like it's on hard mode.
usage_notes: Can refer to a person, thing, or situation. Often used to express frustration.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagtaas ng presyo ng bilihin ay isang malaking **pahirap** sa mga mamamayan.","translation":"The increase in the price of goods is a huge **burden** to the citizens."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **pahirap** sa iyong mga magulang.","translation":"Don't be a **hardship** to your parents."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi naapektuhan o nasasaktan ng anumang bagay, tulad ng hiwa, sakit, o masamang salita.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'di-' (hindi) at pandiwang 'tinatablan' (is affected by).
original_explanation: Like your Tita who gets all the chismis thrown at her but just sips her coffee and smiles. She's 'di-tinatablan'. Also applies to superheroes or that one Nokia phone from 2002.
usage_notes: Stronger than 'di-apektado'. Implies a natural or magical resistance. Often used interchangeably with 'di-tinatalaban'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May mga anting-anting daw na nagiging dahilan kung bakit **di-tinatablan** ng bala ang isang tao.","translation":"They say some amulets are the reason why a person becomes **invulnerable** to bullets."},{"sentence":"Sa sobrang pagod, tila **di-tinatablan** na ako ng kape.","translation":"From being too tired, it seems I've become **impervious** to coffee."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maikling bahagi sa dulo ng isang akdang pampanitikan, na naglalahad ng mga huling pangyayari o nagbibigay ng komento sa mga naganap.
original_explanation: 'Yung part sa dulo ng libro o movie na sinasabi kung anong nangyari sa mga characters after ng "The End". Parang post-credits scene pero sa libro, or 'yung final chismis tungkol sa kanila. "Ano na kayang nangyari sa kanila after ng project?" 'Yan ang epilogo ng BPO life mo.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa mga kontekstong pampanitikan at akademiko.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakalagay sa **epilogo** ng nobela na nagkatuluyan ang dalawang bida.","translation":"It was stated in the novel's **epilogue** that the two protagonists ended up together."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong basahin ang **epilogo** kung ayaw mo ng spoiler.","translation":"Don't read the **epilogue** if you don't want spoilers."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghirang o pagpili sa isang partikular na tao, bagay, o opsyon mula sa iba pa.
etymology: Nagmula sa salitang-ugat na 'pili' at hulaping '-in'.
original_explanation: The object-focused version of 'pili'. This is what you do to your GrabFood order, your next travel destination, or your 'the one'. It's the hugot line: "Sa dinami-dami ng tao sa mundo, bakit siya pa ang pinili ko?" It's also a prayer: "Sana ako ang piliin."
usage_notes: Ito ay isang pandiwa na nakapokus sa layon (object-focused). Ang pinipili ang siyang tuon ng pangungusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **piliin** kung ano ang mas mahalaga sa iyo.","translation":"You need **to choose** what is more important to you."},{"sentence":"Siya ang **pinili** kong makasama habangbuhay.","translation":"She is the one I **chose** to be with for the rest of my life."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pakiusap na maghintay; o ang akto ng pagpapahintay sa isang tao.
original_explanation: What your friend texts you when you're already at the meeting place and they just woke up. 'Pahintay' means 'wait,' but in Filipino time, it could mean anything from 5 minutes to 5 business days. It's a polite request for patience, even when you've lost all of it.
usage_notes: Commonly used as a shortened, polite command or request.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pahintay** sandali, may tinatapos lang ako.","translation":"**Please wait** a moment, I'm just finishing something."},{"sentence":"Sabi niya **pahintay**, pero isang oras na akong nandito.","translation":"He said to **wait**, but I've been here for an hour."}]

meaning_filipino: Tubig na inilipat mula sa isang lalagyan patungo sa iba sa pamamagitan ng isang tubo o hose, gamit ang prinsipyo ng grabidad at presyon ng hangin.
etymology: Parirala na binubuo ng mga salitang Tagalog.
original_explanation: The technique every Pinoy learns when transferring gasoline from a car's tank or cleaning a fish tank. You stick a hose in, suck on the other end until the liquid starts flowing (and pray you don't get a mouthful), then quickly put it in the lower container. A classic life skill. This refers to the water that has been moved using that method.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan sa tubig na sumailalim sa proseso ng pagsipsip gamit ang tubo (siphoning).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maingat niyang inilipat ang **tubig na sinipsip** mula sa drum papunta sa mga timba.","translation":"He carefully transferred the **siphoned water** from the drum to the pails."},{"sentence":"Ito ang **tubig na sinipsip** mula sa aquarium para palitan ng bago.","translation":"This is the **water siphoned** from the aquarium to be replaced with new water."}]

meaning_filipino: Maglibot sa isang lugar upang magbantay, magmasid, at panatilihin ang kaayusan at seguridad.
original_explanation: What the barangay tanod does at 2 AM, armed with a flashlight and a 'batuta'. It's what the security guard at the mall does, walking the same route a hundred times a day. It’s the act of making 'ronda' to make sure everything is A-OK and no 'Marites' is causing trouble.
usage_notes: A direct loanword adaptation into a verb using the '-um-' infix. 'Magpatrolya' is a more common conjugation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gabi-gabi, **pumapatrolya** ang mga pulis sa aming lugar.","translation":"Every night, the police **patrol** our area."},{"sentence":"Inutusan ang mga sundalo na **pumatrolya** sa hangganan.","translation":"The soldiers were ordered to **patrol** the border."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang opisyal na titulo ng pinuno ng Kapulungan ng mga Kinatawan sa Pilipinas o ibang katulad na lehislatibong kapulungan.
original_explanation: This is the official title for the boss of Congress. Think of them as the class president of all the representatives, the one who bangs the gavel and says "Order in the court!"—except it's not a court. They're the one you see on the news when there's a big debate about a new law.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa isang partikular na posisyong pampulitika, karaniwan ay ang Ispiker ng Kapulungan ng mga Kinatawan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inanunsyo **ng Ispiker** ang pagsisimula ng sesyon.","translation":"**The Speaker** announced the start of the session."},{"sentence":"Nahalal bilang bagong **Ispiker** si Congressman Reyes.","translation":"Congressman Reyes was elected as the new **Speaker**."}]

meaning_filipino: Magsagawa ng matinding pagpuna o pagbatikos laban sa isang tao, bagay, o kaisipan.
original_explanation: Ang action form ng 'bardagulan'. Kapag may nakita kang mali at hindi ka na nakatiis, you post about it, you call it out, you make a stand. Ito yung ginagawa ng mga 'cancel culture' warriors at investigative journalists. To put someone or something on blast, pero in a more formal, righteous-anger kind of way.
usage_notes: Ang kilos ng paghahatid ng isang 'tuligsa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat nating **tuligsain** ang anumang uri ng pang-aabuso at kawalang-katarungan.","translation":"We must **denounce** any form of abuse and injustice."},{"sentence":"Walang takot niyang **tinuligsa** ang mga tiwaling opisyal sa kanyang artikulo.","translation":"He fearlessly **criticized** the corrupt officials in his article."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ehersisyo sa mukha na kinabibilangan ng tamang pagpoposisyon ng dila sa ngalangala upang mapabuti diumano ang linya ng panga (jawline).
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na "mewing", ipinangalan sa orthodontist na si John Mew.
original_explanation: This is the Gen Z secret to getting that chiseled jawline without surgery. It's basically resting your tongue on the roof of your mouth. Nag-scroll ka sa TikTok, nakita mo 'yung mga "looksmaxxing" tutorials, tapos bigla mo na lang ginagawa habang nag-aaral o nasa jeep. The ultimate silent workout for your face. 🤫
usage_notes: Isang modernong salitang balbal na naging popular sa social media, lalo na sa TikTok.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Subukan mo raw ang **mewing** para mas maging defined ang jawline mo.","translation":"They say you should try **mewing** to make your jawline more defined."},{"sentence":"Palagi siyang naka-**mewing** kahit sa mga litrato.","translation":"He's always **mewing**, even in photos."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bagay, halaga, o konsepto na kapareho o katapat ng isa pa sa bigat, sukat, halaga, o kahulugan.
etymology: From 'ka-' (denoting equality) + 'tumbas' (equal in weight or value).
original_explanation: This is the word you use when you're talking about a fair trade or an equal exchange. What's the peso equivalent of 100 dollars? 'Ano ang katumbas sa piso ng 100 dolyar?' It's not just about money, though. It can be about effort, love, or sacrifice. 'Ang pagod ko ay walang katumbas na sahod.' (My exhaustion has no salary equivalent.) It's the ultimate word for 'equal value.'
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun ('ang katumbas') or an adjective ('katumbas na halaga').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang isang oras na ehersisyo ay **katumbas** ng isang malusog na puso.","translation":"One hour of exercise is **equivalent** to a healthy heart."},{"sentence":"Magkano ang **katumbas** sa dolyar ng isang libong piso?","translation":"How much is the **equivalent** in dollars of one thousand pesos?"}]

translation: to save up; to conserve; to be thrifty
meaning_filipino: Ang maingat na paggamit o pag-iipon ng yaman, pera, o anumang bagay upang hindi maubos o masayang.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'OFW parent' verb. It's about being super thrifty and saving every last peso. It's not just 'mag-ipon' (to save); it has a deeper sense of scrimping and making sacrifices for a future goal, like sending a kid to college or buying a house and lot. The art of making one can of sardines last for three meals.
usage_notes: A more formal and intense version of 'magtipid' or 'mag-ipon'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **mag-arimuhunan** para sa kinabukasan ng mga anak.","translation":"One must **be thrifty** for the future of the children."},{"sentence":"Sinikap niyang **mag-arimuhunan** sa kabila ng maliit na sahod.","translation":"He tried **to save up diligently** despite his small salary."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kariton na may dalawa o apat na gulong at isang hawakan, na itinutulak ng kamay upang maglulan at maglipat ng mga bagay, karaniwang ginagamit sa pamilihan, paliparan, o bodega.
original_explanation: The official vehicle of the palengke tita and the hardworking kargador. It's the grocery store chariot you use to haul a week's worth of chichirya, or the reason you have a job if you're selling fishballs on the street. In airports, it's the luggage throne for the balikbayan box.
usage_notes: Used directly in Tagalog conversations without translation. 'Troli' is a common synonym in grocery store contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakilagay na lang lahat ng pinamili sa **pushcart**.","translation":"Please just put all the groceries in the **pushcart**."},{"sentence":"Nirentahan niya ang isang **pushcart** para sa kanyang mga panindang gulay.","translation":"He rented a **pushcart** for his vegetable wares."}]

translation: to attend to, to take care of, to focus on
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng buong pansin, panahon, at pagsisikap sa isang partikular na gawain, tungkulin, o bagay.
original_explanation: Yung sinabi ng nanay mo na 'Anak, atupagin mo muna pag-aaral mo bago 'yang jowa-jowa na 'yan.' It means to focus on something, to make it your priority. Your boss wants you to atupagin the report that's due EOD.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **atupagin** ang mga labahin bago umulan.","translation":"I need to **attend to** the laundry before it rains."},{"sentence":"Mas mabuting **atupagin** mo ang iyong kinabukasan.","translation":"It's better to **focus on** your future."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang Metro Rail Transit, isang sistema ng pampublikong transportasyon sa Metro Manila na gumagamit ng tren na bumibiyahe sa kahabaan ng EDSA.
original_explanation: The 'Minsan Rito, Tatlong oras sa pila' experience. A love-hate relationship for every Manila commuter. It's either your savior from EDSA traffic or the reason you're sweating buckets in a human sardine can during rush hour. You pray the aircon works and it doesn't stop mid-track.
usage_notes: Always referred to by its acronym. Refers specifically to the MRT-3 line along EDSA.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sasakay ako ng **MRT** para iwas-traffic.","translation":"I will ride the **MRT** to avoid traffic."},{"sentence":"Mahaba na naman ang pila sa **MRT** North Avenue station.","translation":"The line at the **MRT** North Avenue station is long again."}]

translation: to hide in a tight place; to insert into a nook/crevice
meaning_filipino: Ipasok, isingit, o itago ang isang bagay sa isang maliit, masikip, o tagong lugar.
original_explanation: This is what you do with your phone when the teacher says 'No gadgets!' You find the tightest, most hidden spot in your bag. It's also how you hide the last piece of choco-butternut donut for yourself. 'Isalingit mo muna diyan sa ilalim ng unan.'
usage_notes: Suggests hiding or storing something in a very small, often hidden, space.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Isinalingit** niya ang sulat sa pagitan ng mga pahina ng libro.","translation":"He **inserted** the letter between the pages of the book."},{"sentence":"Paki-**isalingit** na lang itong susi sa ilalim ng paso.","translation":"Please just **hide** this key in the tight space under the flowerpot."}]

meaning_filipino: Magsagawa ng pagpili para sa kapakanan o bilang kinatawan ng ibang tao.
original_explanation: When you're too indecisive to choose from a menu and you tell your friend, "Ipili mo na lang ako." It's the ultimate act of trust (or laziness). You're basically saying, "My fate is in your hands, please don't order ampalaya."
usage_notes: This verb implies the action of choosing is done on behalf of another person. The focus is on the person doing the choosing for someone else.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puwede mo ba akong **ipili** ng magandang damit para sa party?","translation":"Can you **choose** a nice dress **for me** for the party?"},{"sentence":"Siya ang **ipinili** kong lider ng ating grupo.","translation":"He is the one I **chose for** our group as leader."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o katangian ng pagiging matilos o pagkakaroon ng matulis na dulo.
original_explanation: This is the quality that makes a pencil, a tsismis, or a 'hugot' line effective. It's all about the sharp point. Think of the **katilusan** of a freshly sharpened Mongol pencil ready for an exam, or the **katilusan** of a well-aimed sarcastic comment that hits just right.
usage_notes: Used to describe the physical property of having a sharp point.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinahangaan ko ang **katilusan** ng dulo ng lapis na ito.","translation":"I admire the **pointedness** of the tip of this pencil."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang likas na pagkagusto, interes, o tendensiya sa isang partikular na gawain, bagay, o larangan.
original_explanation: Ito yung 'passion' mo na hindi mo pa napagkakakitaan. Yung bagay na ginagawa mo para 'di ka mabaliw sa trabaho—manood ng K-drama, mag-alaga ng halaman, o mag-scroll sa TikTok hanggang 3 AM. It's your default setting for fun.
usage_notes: Often used to describe hobbies or strong interests. 'Mahilig' is the adjective form ('fond of').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ba ang iyong mga **hilig** sa buhay?","translation":"What are your **hobbies/interests** in life?"},{"sentence":"May **hilig** talaga siya sa pagtugtog ng gitara.","translation":"He really has a **liking** for playing the guitar."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa lokasyon ng isang bagay o tao na nasa mas mataas na lebel, posisyon, o lugar.
original_explanation: Yung sagot mo kapag tinanong kung nasaan si kuya na naglalaro ng video games: "Nasa itaas, sa kwarto niya." O kaya, kung nasaan yung bago mong funko pop na ayaw mong magalaw: "Nasa itaas ng cabinet." It can also be used figuratively for someone in a higher position, like "the one above" or the boss.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga damit na hindi na ginagamit ay **nasa itaas** ng aparador.","translation":"The clothes that are no longer used are **on top** of the cabinet."},{"sentence":"Umakyat ka, **nasa itaas** ang banyo.","translation":"Go up, the bathroom is **upstairs**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na pagbati o pagbibigay-galang sa isang tao, lalo na sa pamamagitan ng salita o sulat.
original_explanation: This is the formal, almost old-school word for a greeting. Not your casual 'Hi!' or 'Uy!'. Think 'Maligayang Pasko' card greetings, or the opening of a formal letter: 'Isang malugod na bating pampasko sa iyo!' It’s got a bit of a classic, respectful vibe.
usage_notes: Often found in the phrase 'bating pampasko' (Christmas greeting) or in formal correspondence. Less common in everyday speech compared to 'bati'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpadala siya ng **bating** pangkumpleanyo sa kanyang lola.","translation":"He sent a birthday **greeting** to his grandmother."},{"sentence":"Ang liham ay nagsimula sa isang pormal na **bating**.","translation":"The letter began with a formal **greeting**."}]

translation: shoddy work; done deceitfully; a prank
meaning_filipino: Isang trabaho o kilos na ginawa nang hindi maayos, may pandaraya, o bilang isang biro lamang.
etymology: Mula sa `gawang` (isang anyo ng `gawa`, 'work of') at `paloko` (sa paraang mapanlinlang/mapagbiro, mula sa 'loko' - crazy/fool).
original_explanation: That time your contractor used substandard materials for your house renovation? That's gawang-paloko. Yung group project na ikaw lang gumawa tapos yung iba pangalan lang ang ambag? Gawang-paloko din 'yun sa part nila. It's work that's either a joke, a scam, or just plain lazy.
usage_notes: Maaaring ilarawan ang kalidad ng trabaho (hindi pulido) o ang intensyon sa likod ng isang kilos (mapanlinlang, isang biro).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasira agad ang pader dahil **gawang-paloko** lang pala ng kontratista.","translation":"The wall broke immediately because it was just **shoddy work** by the contractor."},{"sentence":"Akala ko seryoso siya, **gawang-paloko** lang pala ang lahat.","translation":"I thought he was serious, but it was all just a **prank**."}]

translation: to become frustrated; to be dismayed
meaning_filipino: Ang makaranas ng matinding pagkabigo, pagkasawi, o pagkasira ng loob dahil sa hindi pagkamit ng isang inaasahan.
original_explanation: That feeling when you studied all night for an exam, only to find out it was postponed. Or when you lined up for hours for concert tickets, and it sold out right when you got to the counter. It's the "sana 'di na lang" and "bakit ganun" feeling. The official emotion of every commuter during rush hour.
usage_notes: A deep, literary word for disappointment or frustration. "Nabigo" is the more common equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumiphayo** ang kanyang puso nang malaman niyang may iba nang mahal ang kanyang iniirog.","translation":"His heart **was dismayed** when he found out his beloved loves someone else already."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang legal o seremonyal na pagsasama ng dalawang tao bilang magkabiyak; ang kalagayan ng pagiging kasal.
etymology: From root `asawa` (spouse). The `pag-` prefix and reduplication of the first vowel `a` create a noun meaning 'the act of marrying' or 'the state of marriage'.
original_explanation: The ultimate "sana all" for some, and the reason for the endless "Kailan ka ikakasal?" from your titas. It's the act of tying the knot, getting hitched, and moving from "me" to "we." It's a lifelong commitment that starts with a lot of planning and expenses and continues with a lot of compromise and shared bills. It's not just a relationship status update; it's a whole new level of adulting.
usage_notes: Can refer to the wedding ceremony itself or the entire institution of marriage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pag-aasawa** ay isang sagradong sakramento para sa kanila.","translation":"**Marriage** is a sacred sacrament for them."},{"sentence":"Pinaplano na nila ang kanilang **pag-aasawa** sa susunod na taon.","translation":"They are already planning their **act of getting married** (wedding) for next year."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking masugid na tagahanga o may malaking hilig at kaalaman sa isang partikular na gawain, sining, o libangan.
original_explanation: He's the guy who spends his whole sahod on a new bike part because he's a cycling **apisyunado**. The basketball **apisyunado** who can recite player stats from the 90s. The male version of the ultimate fan, deeply passionate about his hobby.
usage_notes: Panlalaking anyo ng 'apisyunada'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **apisyunado** ng sabong ang aking lolo.","translation":"My grandfather is a cockfighting **aficionado**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging kaaya-aya, pino, at may mataas na kalidad sa kilos, pananamit, o anyo.
original_explanation: The 'tita' version of 'elegansya'. It sounds more formal, like something you'd hear in a classic Filipino movie or from your lola describing a debutante's gown. It’s class with a capital 'C' and a slightly more vintage vibe.
usage_notes: An older, more formal spelling of "elegansya". The latter is more common in modern usage. Can function as both a noun (elegance) and an adjective (elegant).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kitang-kita ang **elegansiya** ng kanyang mga kilos.","translation":"The **elegance** of her movements was very apparent."},{"sentence":"Napaká-**elegansiya** ng suot niyang baro't saya.","translation":"The baro't saya she's wearing is very **elegant**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng mga matang may makitid o pahilis na siwang, isang katangiang karaniwan sa mga taga-Silangang Asya.
original_explanation: The physical trait that makes people automatically assume you're good at math or have a Chinese ancestor. Having **singkit** eyes means you've mastered the "smize" since birth but also face the eternal struggle of making your eyeliner visible.
usage_notes: While often used descriptively, its use can be sensitive. Tone and context are crucial to avoid causing offense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa kanyang magagandang mata na medyo **singkit**.","translation":"She is known for her beautiful, slightly **almond-eyed** eyes."},{"sentence":"Lahat silang magkakapatid ay **singkit** ang mga mata.","translation":"All the siblings have **slant-eyed** eyes."}]

meaning_filipino: Iangat ang paningin upang pagmasdan ang isang bagay na nasa itaas.
original_explanation: This is the literal "look up" command. 'Pag sinabi ng nanay mo, "Tingalain mo 'yung bubong kung may butas," 'yan 'yun. Or 'pag tinuturo mo sa kaibigan mo 'yung shooting star na ikaw lang ang nakakita.
usage_notes: This is the object-focus form of the verb, directing the action of looking up towards a specific object.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **tingalain** ang langit paminsan-minsan.","translation":"Don't forget to **look up at** the sky once in a while."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang detalyadong pagpapaliwanag o paglalarawan ng isang teorya o ideya. Maaari rin itong tumukoy sa isang malaking pampublikong pagtatanghal ng mga likhang-sining o produkto.
original_explanation: This is the 'tell-all' part of a story, yung inilalatag lahat ng background info para hindi ka maligaw. Think of it as the opening scene of a teleserye where they explain who's who and why the bida is poor but has a secret rich relative. It's also that big trade show sa Megamall or World Trade Center where you get tons of freebies.
usage_notes: Used in both literary/academic contexts (exposition of a topic) and general contexts (trade exposition).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **eksposisyon** ng kanyang mga argumento ay malinaw at nakakakumbinsi.","translation":"The **exposition** of his arguments was clear and convincing."},{"sentence":"Pumunta kami sa isang **eksposisyon** ng mga bagong kotse sa SMX.","translation":"We went to a new car **exhibition** at SMX."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing matulis o matilos ang dulo ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is what you do to your pencil before a major exam, or to a bamboo stick before making isaw. 'Tilusan' is the act of making something pointy. It's the 'verb' version of 'tilos'. It's the glow-up your kilay pencil needs.
usage_notes: The object being sharpened is the direct object of the verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **tilusan** ang mga lapis ko bago magsimula ang klase.","translation":"I need to **sharpen** my pencils before class starts."},{"sentence":"**Tinilusan** niya ang kahoy para gawing panusok sa barbekyu.","translation":"He **sharpened** the wood to make a barbecue skewer."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagguho o pagbagsak ng lupa, bato, o isang istruktura.
original_explanation: What happens when too much rain meets a weak mountain. It's the land giving up, like you after a long week of deadlines. Also, the state of your carefully built Jenga tower after a wrong move.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of natural disasters. Synonymous with 'guho'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng **huho** ng lupa sa gilid ng bundok dahil sa malakas na ulan.","translation":"There was a **landslide** on the mountainside because of the heavy rain."},{"sentence":"Nangangamba ang mga residente sa posibleng pag-**huho** ng kanilang mga bahay.","translation":"The residents are worried about the possible **collapse** of their houses."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang espasyo, pook, o puwesto na maaaring puntahan o kinalalagyan ng isang tao o bagay. Tumutukoy rin sa posisyon o katayuan.
original_explanation: Your "lugar" is your spot. It can be a physical place like "Saan ang lugar ng party?" (Where's the party place?) or your figurative place in the world, like when you tell someone "Alamin mo ang lugar mo!" (Know your place!). It's the G in Waze's "You have arrived at your destination."
usage_notes: A very common word. Can also refer to one's social standing or role.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maghanap tayo ng magandang **lugar** para magpiknik.","translation":"Let's find a good **place** for a picnic."},{"sentence":"Ibalik mo 'yan sa tamang **lugar**.","translation":"Put that back in its proper **spot**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang mekanikal na ginagamit upang magbuhat ng mabibigat na bagay, karaniwan ay sasakyan.
original_explanation: The best friend you never knew you needed when you get a flat tire on EDSA. It's that tool in your car's trunk that lifts the vehicle so you can change the tire. For non-car people, it's the thing that goes "krik-krik-krik" and magically lifts a 1-ton hunk of metal.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to a mechanical lifting device.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang **diyak** para palitan ang gulong ng kotse.","translation":"He used the **jack** to change the car's tire."},{"sentence":"Pakikuha mo nga ang **diyak** sa likod ng sasakyan.","translation":"Can you please get the **jack** from the back of the car."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o estado ng sukdulang kaligayahan, kaluguran, at kapayapaan; paraiso.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol 'paraíso', na mula sa Latin 'paradīsus'.
original_explanation: It's the Tagalized version of 'paradise'. Think of it as that feeling when your 13th-month pay finally comes in, or when you find a parking spot in Greenbelt on a Saturday night. Ultimate bliss.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa kontekstong relihiyoso o sa paglalarawan ng isang napakagandang lugar. Isang baryasyon ng mas karaniwang 'paraiso'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang isla ng Palawan ay tila isang **paradais** sa lupa.","translation":"The island of Palawan is like a **paradise** on earth."},{"sentence":"Naniniwala sila na mapupunta ang mabubuting kaluluwa sa **paradais**.","translation":"They believe that good souls will go to **paradise**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-alis ng mga sagabal, damo, o tao sa isang lugar upang ito ay maging malinis at madaling daanan.
original_explanation: Imagine your messy room finally getting cleaned, or that feeling when EDSA is miraculously empty during a long weekend. That space has been `mahawan`. It's clearing the path, literally and figuratively.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of clearing land, paths, or crowds.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **mahawan** ang daan para makadaan ang ambulansya.","translation":"The road needs to **be cleared** so the ambulance can pass."},{"sentence":"Nang **mahawan** ang mga tao, nakita ko siya sa malayo.","translation":"When the crowd **cleared**, I saw him from afar."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain o hanapbuhay ng pakikipagtalik sa ibang tao kapalit ng pera o bayad.
original_explanation: The 'oldest profession in the world'. Isang mabigat at kumplikadong isyu sa lipunan kung saan ang sex ay nagiging serbisyo kapalit ng bayad. It's a harsh reality for many, often driven by poverty and lack of opportunities.
usage_notes: Isang sensitibong paksa na may malalim na implikasyong panlipunan at moral.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kahirapan ay isa sa mga ugat ng **prostitusyon** sa maraming bansa.","translation":"Poverty is one of the roots of **prostitution** in many countries."},{"sentence":"May mga batas na naglalayong sugpuin ang **prostitusyon** at tulungan ang mga biktima nito.","translation":"There are laws that aim to curb **prostitution** and help its victims."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang bagay o sitwasyon na wala sa ayos, magulo, o buhol-buhol. Ang karaniwang anyo nito bilang pang-uri ay 'magulo'.
original_explanation: 'Yung buhok mo pagkagising sa umaga. 'Yung plot ng isang teleserye na may amnesia, kambal na nawawalay, at sampalan scenes. 'Yung love life mo na hindi mo alam kung kayo pa ba o hindi na. Complicated.
usage_notes: The stress shifts to the last syllable when used as an adjective, though 'magulo' is the more common adjectival form. 'Gulo' as an adjective is often heard in exclamations like "Ang gulo ng buhok mo!"
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakagulo ng kwarto niya, parang dinaanan ng bagyo.","translation":"His room is so **messy**, it looks like a storm passed through."},{"sentence":"Ang **gulo** ng sinasabi mo, hindi kita maintindihan.","translation":"What you're saying is **chaotic**, I can't understand you."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagiging dilat na dilat ng mga mata, karaniwan dahil sa pagkabigla, takot, o pagkamangha.
original_explanation: The look you have when you accidentally open your phone's front camera. Or when you see your ex with their new partner. Or when your boss says 'May I see you in my office?' on a Friday afternoon. Your eyes are open, but the brain has left the building.
usage_notes: Madalas na nagpapahiwatig ng pagkabigla, pagkagulat, o pagkatulala.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napatingin siya sa akin nang **mulagat** ang mga mata nang marinig ang balita.","translation":"He looked at me with **wide-eyed** shock upon hearing the news."},{"sentence":"Bakit ka nakatayo diyan na **mulagat**? May multo ka bang nakita?","translation":"Why are you standing there **staring blankly**? Did you see a ghost?"}]

translation: to make something shiny; to polish
meaning_filipino: Gawing makintab o maningning ang isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pagpunas o paggamit ng pampakintab.
original_explanation: This is the command form of 'to polish.' It's what your mom tells you to do to the floor before the relatives arrive for Christmas, or what you do to your shoes before a job interview. It's the action of transforming something from 'meh' to 'wow, ang shiny!'.
usage_notes: Often used as a command or in infinitive form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pakintabin** mo ang sahig para sa bisita.","translation":"**Polish** the floor for the visitor."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang basahan upang **pakintabin** ang kanyang sapatos.","translation":"He used the rag to **make** his shoes **shiny**."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubos na nakalantad, walang takip, at kitang-kita ng lahat.
original_explanation: When your whole life's mess is on display for your surprise visitor to see. The bag of chips, the unwashed clothes, the three-day-old pizza box—lahat nakabuyangyang. It can also mean being indecently exposed. It's the state of being completely, and often messily, out in the open. No filter, no hiding.
usage_notes: Carries a slightly negative or messy connotation. It's not just 'exposed' but 'messily exposed'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iniwan niyang **nakabuyangyang** ang lahat ng gamit niya sa sahig.","translation":"He left all his things **exposed** on the floor."},{"sentence":"Ikinagulat ng lahat ang mga lihim na **nakabuyangyang** sa publiko.","translation":"Everyone was shocked by the secrets that were **laid bare** to the public."}]

meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng papuri, parangal, o paghanga ang isang tao, bagay, o diyos dahil sa taglay nitong kabutihan o kagalingan.
original_explanation: To gas someone up, but make it sincere. It's what you do when your friend's OOTD is on point ("Ganda mo, sis!"), or when your team lead actually does a good job. It's the opposite of 'cancel culture'. The verbal equivalent of a 'heart' react.
usage_notes: Object-focus verb. The object is the one being praised.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat nating **purihin** ang mga taong gumagawa ng mabuti sa kapwa.","translation":"We should **praise** people who do good to others."},{"sentence":"Gusto kitang **purihin** sa iyong mahusay na pagtatanghal.","translation":"I want to **praise** you for your excellent presentation."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na nakasabit at hindi sumasayad sa ibaba; maaari ring tumukoy sa isang sitwasyon na walang kasiguraduhan o resolusyon.
original_explanation: Literally, your laundry on the clothesline. Metaphorically, your relationship status with your crush. 'Ano na tayo?' is the official question of the nakabitin generation. It's being left hanging, whether it's a cliffhanger in a Netflix series, waiting for your exam results, or waiting for a 'yes' or 'no' from someone. It's the feeling of uncertainty.
usage_notes: Widely used both literally and metaphorically.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming parol ang **nakabitin** sa mga bintana tuwing Pasko.","translation":"Many Christmas lanterns are **hanging** on the windows during Christmas."},{"sentence":"**Nakabitin** ang desisyon ng boss tungkol sa aking promotion.","translation":"The boss's decision about my promotion is left **hanging**."}]

translation: to wonder about; to be amazed by
meaning_filipino: Ang makaranas ng pagkamangha, pagtataka, o pag-aalinlangan tungkol sa isang bagay, tao, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is what you feel when your friend who's always late arrives on time. "Nakaka-**pagtakha** naman!" Or when you see the price of onions and you just have to wonder why. It’s the verb for "Wow, really?!"
usage_notes: The focus is on the object or cause of the wonder or amazement.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi mo dapat **pagtakhan** kung bakit siya nagalit; kasalanan mo naman talaga.","translation":"You shouldn't **wonder** why they got mad; it was really your fault."}]

translation: to become trendy; to be in fashion
meaning_filipino: Maging popular o kalat na gawain, istilo, o bagay sa isang partikular na panahon.
original_explanation: The reason why everyone was suddenly making Dalgona coffee or dancing on TikTok. It's when something explodes in popularity, and you see it everywhere—from your feed to the mall. Milktea shops, samgyupsal places, hugot lines... they all had their moment 'na mauso'. It's the cycle of cool, and just as quickly as it comes, it can go.
usage_notes: 'Uso' is the noun (trend), 'mauso' is the verb (to become a trend).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana hindi **mauso** ang masasamang ugali.","translation":"I hope bad habits don't **become trendy**."},{"sentence":"Noong dekada '90, **nauso** ang maluluwag na pantalon.","translation":"In the 90s, baggy pants **were in fashion**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagawaran sa isang kumpanya na nangangasiwa sa mga empleyado, mula sa pagkuha, pamamahala, at pagtiyak sa kanilang kapakanan.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung department na pupuntahan mo 'pag may reklamo ka sa boss mo, 'pag hihingi ka ng leave, o 'pag tatanungin mo kung kelan ang sweldo. Sila rin ang nag-o-organize ng Christmas party na may pa-raffle ng electric fan. Basically, the principal's office of the corporate world.
usage_notes: Ginagamit bilang isang kolokyal na pagdadaglat sa mga opisina at propesyonal na kapaligiran. Binibigkas ang mga letra sa Ingles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isumite mo ang iyong medical certificate sa **hr**.","translation":"Submit your medical certificate to **HR**."},{"sentence":"Tinanong ko si Ma'am ng **hr** kung may bakante pa sila.","translation":"I asked the lady from **HR** if they still have a vacancy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malaking langgam, karaniwang kulay pula o itim, na kilala sa paninirahan sa kahoy at sa masakit nitong kagat.
original_explanation: The heavyweight champion of ants. Not your everyday tiny sugar ant. This is the big, bad red ant that makes you jump and yelp. If you see a trail of these, you don't mess with them. They're the bouncers of the insect world, and their bite feels like a tiny injection of fire.
usage_notes: Madalas ipagkamali sa 'hantik', na isa ring malaking langgam ngunit karaniwang mas malaki at mas agresibo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Aray! Nakagat ako ng **kayumad** sa paa habang nagdidilig.","translation":"Ouch! A **large red ant** bit me on the foot while I was watering the plants."},{"sentence":"May pugad ng **kayumad** sa lumang poste ng bakod.","translation":"There's a **carpenter ant** nest in the old fence post."}]

translation: to clash, to confront each other, to collide
meaning_filipino: Ang marahas na pagtatagpo o paglalaban ng dalawang magkasalungat na puwersa, panig, o bagay.
original_explanation: The ultimate showdown. Think rival K-Pop fandoms in the comments section, or two drivers arguing over a parking spot in a crowded mall. It’s more intense than a simple argument; there's action, there's drama, there's a sagupaan.
usage_notes: Used for more intense or physical confrontations, not just simple arguments.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatakdang **magsagupaan** ang dalawang pinakamagaling na koponan sa finals.","translation":"The two best teams are scheduled to **clash** in the finals."},{"sentence":"Nag-init ang ulo ng dalawang motorista at sila'y nagbantang **magsagupaan** sa gitna ng kalsada.","translation":"The two motorists got angry and threatened to **confront each other** in the middle of the road."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagturing o pagkilala sa isang tao o bagay bilang kasapi ng isang grupo; maaari ring tumukoy sa pagbibilang ng numero.
original_explanation: When you're making a list for the group lunch order and someone yells, '**Ibilang** mo ako diyan!' (Count me in!). It also means to consider someone as something. 'Sana **ibilang** mo akong kaibigan.' (I hope you consider me a friend.) — a classic line for the friend-zoned.
usage_notes: Has two main meanings: to literally count something for someone, or to figuratively count/include/consider someone/something as part of a group.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong kalimutang **ibilang** sa listahan ng mga bisita.","translation":"Don't forget to **include** me on the guest list."},{"sentence":"**Ibinilang** niya ang sarili sa mga tagahanga ng banda.","translation":"She **counted** herself among the band's fans."},{"sentence":"Maaari mo bang **ibilang** ang mga barya para sa akin?","translation":"Can you **count** the coins for me?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang metal na tabla na may nakaukit na numero at letra na ikinakabit sa harap at likod ng isang sasakyan para sa pagkakakilanlan nito.
original_explanation: The ID of your car. The reason you get pulled over by an MMDA officer on a Monday if your number ends in 1 or 2. Having a "low-numbered" or "vanity" plaka is a status symbol, basically the automotive equivalent of a blue checkmark.
usage_notes: Refers almost exclusively to a vehicle's license plate.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi pa rin dumadating ang bagong **plaka** ng kotse ko galing LTO.","translation":"My car's new **license plate** from the LTO still hasn't arrived."},{"sentence":"Tandaan mo ang numero ng **plaka** ng sasakyang bumangga sa atin.","translation":"Remember the **license plate** number of the vehicle that hit us."}]

translation: to pierce repeatedly; to stick something onto
meaning_filipino: Ang paglagay o pagbaon ng isang matulis na bagay sa isa pa, o ang kilos ng paulit-ulit na pagtusok.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'tusok'. This is what you do to the kikiam at the street food stall. 'Sige, tusukan mo na ng stick 'yan!' It can also mean to pierce something multiple times.
usage_notes: Can mean to pierce something (object focus) or to put a pointed object into something (locative focus).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **tusukan** ang lobo at baka pumutok.","translation":"Don't **pierce** the balloon or it might pop."},{"sentence":"Dito mo **tusukan** ng pako ang dingding.","translation":"This is where you should **stick** the nail into the wall."}]

meaning_filipino: Malapit nang matapos o nasa huling yugto ng paggawa o kaganapan.
etymology: From `pa-` (denoting movement towards a state) + `tapos` (end, finish).
original_explanation: That feeling at 5:50 PM on a Friday when you're just staring at the clock. It's the "last two minutes" of a basketball game, the final episode of a K-drama, or that thesis you're *almost* done with. "Guys, focus! Patapos na ang project!"
usage_notes: Often used to describe projects, events, or periods of time that are concluding.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Patapos** na ang klase kaya magligpit na kayo.","translation":"The class is **about to end** so pack up your things."},{"sentence":"Nasa **patapos** na yugto na ang konstruksyon ng bagong gusali.","translation":"The construction of the new building is now in its **finishing** stages."}]

translation: Burden; something that makes things difficult
meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay, sitwasyon, o tao na nagdudulot ng kahirapan, pasanin, o dagdag na kumplikasyon.
etymology: From 'pang-' (instrumental prefix) + 'pa-' (causative prefix) + 'hirap' (difficulty). Lit. 'that which is used to cause difficulty'.
original_explanation: That one groupmate who doesn't contribute but gets the same grade. The 'system is down' notification when you're about to clock out. The unexpected bill that ruins your 13th-month pay. Basically, anything that adds unnecessary difficulty to your life, also known as 'adulting.'
usage_notes: Can describe a person, object, or situation that complicates things. Often used with a negative connotation, implying an unnecessary complication.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang maging **pampahirap** sa buhay ng may buhay.","translation":"Don't be a **burden** in other people's lives."},{"sentence":"Ang biglaang pagtaas ng presyo ay isang **pampahirap** sa mga mamamayan.","translation":"The sudden price increase is something that **makes life difficult** for the citizens."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar, lalo na ang isang bahay o gusali, na walang naninirahan.
original_explanation: This is the real estate version of 'single and available.' It means a house, apartment, or condo is vacant. It's the sign you want to see when you're apartment hunting. But if it's a creepy old house, 'walang-nakatira' might just mean... walang *buhay* na nakatira. *cue horror music*
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matagal nang **walang-nakatira** sa lumang bahay na iyon.","translation":"That old house has been **uninhabited** for a long time."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang hanapbuhay ay ang pagputol ng mga puno sa gubat upang gawing tabla o troso.
etymology: mag- (prefix indicating occupation) + troso (log/lumber, from Spanish 'trozo')
original_explanation: The original lumberjack. Before "lumbersexual" was a thing, these guys were the real deal, working in forests. It's a tough job, often seen as both a source of livelihood and a cause of deforestation, making it a complicated topic in the Philippines.
usage_notes: The mag- + root + -o pattern is common for occupations (e.g., magtataho, magbabalut), although this word is formed slightly differently, it follows the occupational 'mag-' prefix.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ama ni Berto ay isang **magtotroso** sa kanilang probinsya.","translation":"Berto's father is a **logger** in their province."},{"sentence":"Ipinagbabawal na ang mga ilegal na **magtotroso** sa protektadong kagubatan.","translation":"Illegal **loggers** are now banned from the protected forest."}]

translation: to cause to be repeatedly turned upside down or inside out
meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang pagpapagulong-gulong o pagpapabalik-balik ng isang bagay sa magkabilang panig nito nang paulit-ulit.
original_explanation: Picture a kid having a tantrum on the floor, rolling around. That's magpabali-baligtad. Or when you're frying fish and you keep flipping it over and over, hoping it gets crispy but not burnt. It can also be used for stories or alibis: "Huwag mong pagbali-baligtarin ang kwento!" (Don't keep twisting the story!). It's the act of causing constant flipping and turning.
usage_notes: Implies a repeated, sometimes frantic or chaotic, turning action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwang-tuwa ang bata na **magpabali-baligtad** sa malambot na kama.","translation":"The child was happily **rolling over and over** on the soft bed."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **pagbali-baligtarin** ang pahayag upang malito ang mga imbestigador.","translation":"He tried **to keep twisting** the statement to confuse the investigators."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pandiwa na nangangahulugang gawing matatag, patibayin, o palakasin ang isang bagay, lalo na ang kalooban o determinasyon.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'tatag' at hulaping '-an'.
original_explanation: This is what your friend tells you when you're about to face your terror professor, or when your internet dies during a crucial online meeting. "Tatagan mo ang loob mo!" means "Brace yourself! Be strong!" It's about summoning your inner Darna and facing the challenge head-on.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin kasama ng 'loob' (kalooban) tulad ng sa pariralang 'tatagan ang loob'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tatagan** mo ang iyong loob; malalampasan mo rin ang pagsubok na iyan.","translation":"**Strengthen** your resolve; you will also overcome that trial."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ipinahayag, binigkas, o isinalita ng isang tao; ang nakaraang pandiwa ng 'sabihin'.
original_explanation: The root of all chismis. "Ano'ng sinabi niya?" is the question that launches a thousand screenshots. It's also the classic parent defense: "Sinabi ko na sa'yo, 'di ba?" (I told you so, right?). The past tense of "sabi," which means it's already out there and you can't take it back.
usage_notes: Past tense, object-focused form of "sabi". Refers to what was said.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **sinabi** sa iyo ng doktor?","translation":"What did the doctor **tell** you?"},{"sentence":"**Sinabi** niyang mahal niya ako, pero sa chat lang.","translation":"He **said** he loves me, but only in chat."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang likido na may halimuyak, karaniwang mula sa mga esensyal na langis, na ipinapahid sa katawan upang magbigay ng kaaya-ayang amoy.
original_explanation: Your secret weapon for date night, job interviews, or just feeling fresh after commuting. From Bench cologne to Jo Malone, it's all pabango. It's the "ambango mo naman, ano'ng pabango mo?" conversation starter. Also, the thing you spray generously to hide the smell of last night's samgyupsal.
usage_notes: Universal term for any kind of perfume or scent applied to the body.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-spray siya ng kaunting **pabango** bago umalis ng bahay.","translation":"She sprayed a little **perfume** before leaving the house."},{"sentence":"Regalo ko sa kanya ang paborito niyang **pabango**.","translation":"My gift to him is his favorite **cologne**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng uod (larva ng gamugamo) na may makakapal at makikinis na buhok na nagdudulot ng matinding pangangati kapag nadikit sa balat.
original_explanation: Nature's little scam artist. It looks fluffy and cute like a cat's fur, tempting you to pet it. But DON'T. One touch and you'll be scratching like you have a major life crisis. It's the ultimate 'look but don't touch' creature of the Philippines.
usage_notes: The name refers to its appearance, not its texture.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa mga dahon, baka may **balahibong-pusa**.","translation":"Be careful with the leaves, there might be a **stinging caterpillar**."},{"sentence":"Namula ang braso niya dahil nadikitan ng **balahibong-pusa**.","translation":"His arm reddened because a **stinging caterpillar** touched it."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangunahing diwa o pinag-uusapan sa isang sulatin, talakayan, o anumang anyo ng komunikasyon.
etymology: Maaaring mula sa Sanskrit पक्ष (pakṣa), nangangahulugang "panig" o "punto de bista".
original_explanation: This is the "So, what are we?" in a relationship, the main point of a chismis, or the title of your thesis that you've been procrastinating on for a year. It's the central idea, the "about what?" of any conversation or piece of writing.
usage_notes: Isang pangunahing salita sa mga talakayang akademiko, pormal, at maging sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paksa** ng ating pagpupulong ngayon ay tungkol sa bagong proyekto.","translation":"The **topic** of our meeting today is about the new project."},{"sentence":"Mahirap humanap ng magandang **paksa** para sa aking tesis.","translation":"It's hard to find a good **subject** for my thesis."}]

translation: to pretend to be holy; to sanctify
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkilos na tila banal o relihiyoso; ang paggawang banal sa isang bagay o lugar.
original_explanation: This is what you call that officemate who's super judgy and acts morally superior, but you know their weekend secrets. They love to *magpabanal-banalan* (a more intense form) at work. It's the "holier-than-thou" vibe, PH edition.
usage_notes: Often used with a slightly negative connotation, implying pretense (magpabanal-banalan). Can also be used in a literal religious context (to sanctify).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing Mahal na Araw, maraming tao ang sinusubukang **magpabanal**.","translation":"During Holy Week, many people try to **act holy**."},{"sentence":"Ang obispo ang **nagpabanal** sa bagong kapilya.","translation":"The bishop **sanctified** the new chapel."}]

translation: please get along with; please adapt to
meaning_filipino: Isang pakiusap na makisama, umayon, o iangkop ang sarili sa isang tao, sitwasyon, o kapaligiran.
original_explanation: This is what your mom tells you before dropping you off at a family party full of relatives you barely know. "Pakibagayan mo 'yung Tita mo," means "Please just laugh at your Auntie's corny jokes and don't start a political debate." It's a request to activate your 'pakikisama' mode for the sake of peace.
usage_notes: A command form of the verb 'makibagay'. It's a request for someone to make an effort to conform or socialize, often for social harmony.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pakibagayan** mo na lang ang mga bago mong kasama sa trabaho.","translation":"**Please just try to get along with** your new colleagues."},{"sentence":"Anak, **pakibagayan** mo ang pinsan mo galing probinsya.","translation":"Child, **please adapt to** and be nice to your cousin from the province."}]

meaning_filipino: Pera na itinabi o inilaan para sa isang tiyak na layunin.
original_explanation: Very similar to 'laang-gugulin' but more general. It's the 'pondo' or 'funds'. Ito yung emergency fund mo na ginagalaw mo kapag may 12.12 sale. The money you set aside but somehow never stays there.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'pondo'. It is slightly less formal than 'laang-gugulin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May sapat na **laang-salapi** ang proyekto para matapos sa takdang oras.","translation":"The project has enough **funds** to be completed on time."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagkaing Hapones na binubuo ng mga pagkaing-dagat o gulay na isinawsaw sa batter at pinirito nang malutong.
etymology: Mula sa Hapones na 天ぷら (tenpura), na nagmula naman sa Portuges na "têmpora".
original_explanation: Ito yung sosyal na version ng camaron rebosado. Hipon na binalutan ng light, crispy batter na masarap isawsaw sa special sauce. Paborito sa mga Japanese restaurant at food court. Pag kumakain ka nito, feeling mo nasa Japan ka, kahit nasa gitna ka lang ng SM food court.
usage_notes: Pangalan ng isang partikular na uri ng pagkain.
