usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kostante** ang pag-ulan sa aming probinsya tuwing buwan ng Agosto.","translation":"The rain is **constant** in our province during the month of August."},{"sentence":"Ang pagmamahal ng isang ina ay **kostante** at walang kapantay.","translation":"A mother's love is **persistent** and unequaled."}]

translation: to place close together; to press against
meaning_filipino: Ilapit o ipagdikit nang husto ang dalawang bagay upang magkadikit o magkasanib.
original_explanation: Think of sitting in a jeepney during rush hour. The way you have to **idait** your body to the person next to you just to fit? That's it. It’s about closing any and all personal space, whether it's two pieces of wood you're gluing or two people in a tight spot.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maingat niyang **inidait** ang dalawang piraso ng basag na plorera.","translation":"He carefully **pressed together** the two pieces of the broken vase."}]

translation: to pretend to be an expert; to act like a know-it-all
meaning_filipino: Magkunwaring marunong o may sapat na kaalaman sa isang bagay kahit hindi naman.
etymology: From 'tanda' (to know, remember), reduplicated with infix '-ng-' to imply pretense or imitation.
original_explanation: We all know that one person in the group project or in a meeting who acts like they know everything, even when they're just pulling 'facts' out of thin air. That's 'magtandang-tandangan'. It’s the art of faking it 'til you make it, but in a really obvious and sometimes annoying way. It's the 'Actually...' guy in every comments section.
usage_notes: Carries a negative connotation of arrogance or pretense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magtandang-tandangan** kung hindi mo naman talaga alam ang sagot.","translation":"Don't **act like a know-it-all** if you don't really know the answer."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **magtandang-tandangan** tuwing may bagong topic sa klase.","translation":"He likes to **pretend to be an expert** whenever there's a new topic in class."}]

translation: to cause to crack or split
meaning_filipino: Utusan o hilingin na magkaroon ng lamat o biyak ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay isang matigas na ibabaw tulad ng lupa o pader.
original_explanation: This is the command you give when you want something to crack open, like telling the earth to split during an earthquake scene in a movie, or what you wish would happen to your phone screen after dropping it for the nth time (just kidding... mostly). It's the 'make it crack' button.
usage_notes: This is a command form of the verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pabitakin** mo ang tuyong lupa sa pamamagitan ng pagbuhos ng maraming tubig at pagpapatuyo muli.","translation":"**Cause the dry land to crack** by pouring a lot of water and letting it dry again."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pabitakin** ang pader, kakatapos lang pinturahan.","translation":"Don't **cause the wall to crack**; it was just painted."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng manipis at malutong na biskwit na inikid na parang tubo, karaniwang gawa sa harina, asukal, itlog, at gatas.
etymology: From Spanish 'barquillo' (little boat), named for its shape.
original_explanation: This is that super delicate, cylindrical pasalubong from Iloilo that shatters into a million delicious pieces the moment you look at it. You try to eat it without making a mess, but you always fail. It's the official snack of "Oops, I ate the whole can."
usage_notes: Almost always used in its plural Spanish form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang bumili ng **barkilyos** pag-uwi mo galing Iloilo.","translation":"Don't forget to buy **barquillos** when you come home from Iloilo."},{"sentence":"Masarap isawsaw sa sorbetes ang **barkilyos**.","translation":"It's delicious to dip **crispy wafer rolls** in ice cream."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging bali o putol ng isang matigas na bagay, lalo na ang buto.
original_explanation: The result of trying to be a superhero and jumping off the second-floor veranda. It's when something, usually a bone, goes 'snap!' instead of 'bend'. This is what your mom warned you about when you were climbing trees or playing patintero too aggressively. The bill from the hospital is the second-degree pain.
usage_notes: Primarily used in a medical context for bone fractures.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon siya ng **kabalian** sa braso matapos mahulog sa bisikleta.","translation":"He sustained a **fracture** in his arm after falling from his bicycle."},{"sentence":"Ang X-ray ay nagpakita ng maliit na **kabalian** sa kanyang bukung-bukong.","translation":"The X-ray showed a small **fracture** in his ankle."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging angkop, wasto, o bagay sa isang partikular na layunin, sitwasyon, o pamantayan.
etymology: From `pagka-` (state or manner of being) + `akma` (to fit, to be suitable).
original_explanation: This is the "saktong-sakto" or "swak na swak" feeling. When your outfit matches the party's theme, that's pagkaakma. When the new hire is a perfect fit for the team's toxic-but-fun dynamic, that's also pagkaakma. It's the universe telling you, "Yes, girl, that's the one."
usage_notes: Often used to describe how well something fits, either literally (like clothes) or figuratively (like a job or a role).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinuri ng lahat ang **pagkaakma** ng kanyang kasuotan sa tema ng pagdiriwang.","translation":"Everyone praised the **suitability** of her attire to the celebration's theme."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkaakma** ng solusyon sa problema ay agad na napansin.","translation":"The **appropriateness** of the solution to the problem was immediately noticed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pakiramdam ng pagkainis, pagkayamot, o pagkainip dahil sa isang tao, bagay, o sitwasyon.
etymology: From Spanish 'azar' (bad luck, chance). The meaning shifted in Philippine Spanish and later in Tagalog to mean annoyance or irritation.
original_explanation: That feeling when the internet dies during your Zoom presentation. Or when someone keeps chew-talking. That's **asar**. It's the low-key, simmering anger that makes you want to roll your eyes so hard they get stuck. It’s the 'pikon' starter pack.
usage_notes: Extremely common in informal speech. The verb form is 'asarin' (to annoy) and the state is 'naaasar' (being annoyed).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko mapigilan ang aking **asar** sa mabagal na serbisyo.","translation":"I couldn't hide my **annoyance** at the slow service."},{"sentence":"Tanggal ang **asar** ko nang makita ko siyang ngumiti.","translation":"My **irritation** disappeared when I saw him/her smile."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng sandatang pampasabog na may sariling sistema ng paggabay upang tamaan ang isang partikular na target.
etymology: Mula sa pariralang Ingles na "guided missile."
original_explanation: This is what happens when English military terms take a vacation in the Philippines. It's a 'guided missile,' but said with a Pinoy accent. You'll hear this on the news when they're talking about military hardware. It's also a great metaphor for a 'marites' (gossiper) who has a very specific target for her chismis. Lock-on target!
usage_notes: Isang ponetikong pagbaybay ng pariralang Ingles. Pangunahing ginagamit sa pag-uulat ng balita o mga talakayan tungkol sa teknolohiyang militar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpakawala ng isang **gaided misil** ang barkong pandigma.","translation":"The warship launched a **guided missile**."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng militar ang pagbili ng mga bagong **gaided misil**.","translation":"The military is studying the purchase of new **guided missiles**."}]

translation: will be made to wrinkle; will be made to frown
meaning_filipino: Pipilitin o magiging sanhi upang kumunot o magkaroon ng mga guhit, lalo na ang noo o balat.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your forehead (`noo`) when you're trying to understand your PAG-IBIG statement. The confusing numbers will make you frown. "Sa sobrang stress sa trabaho, tiyak na **papangunutin** ang noo mo." (With so much stress at work, your forehead will surely be made to wrinkle.)
usage_notes: Often used specifically in the context of frowning ('kunot-noo'). A more common term for causing wrinkles in skin or fabric is 'papakulubutin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mahihirap na tanong sa pagsusulit ay **papangunutin** ang noo ng mga estudyante.","translation":"The difficult questions on the exam **will make** the students' foreheads **wrinkle** (frown)."}]

translation: to board, to ride, to embark
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagsakay sa isang sasakyan tulad ng barko, eroplano, bus, o tren.
original_explanation: The OG "Tara, G!" before it was cool. It's what you do when the MRT door opens and you have 0.5 seconds to get in. "Game, **lumulan** na tayo sa adventure!"
usage_notes: Often used in a more formal or literary context than 'sumakay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga pasahero ay maagang pumila upang **lumulan** sa barko.","translation":"The passengers lined up early to **board** the ship."},{"sentence":"Handa na siyang **lumulan** sa eroplano para sa kanyang unang paglalakbay sa ibang bansa.","translation":"She is ready to **board** the plane for her first trip abroad."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paunang at agarang tulong na ibinibigay sa isang taong may sakit o pinsala bago dumating ang propesyonal na tulong medikal.
original_explanation: Basically the same as 'pangunahing lunas', but this one sounds a bit more... urgent and initial. It's the 'first' in 'first aid'. It's what your Scoutmaster taught you, like how to make a splint from a branch or how to stop bleeding with a clean cloth. The very first response.
usage_notes: Madalas na ipinagpapalit sa "pangunahing lunas", ngunit ang "pangunang" ay partikular na nagbibigay-diin sa 'pauna' o 'unang' aksyon na ginawa. Minsan ay isinusulat din bilang "paunang lunas".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha siya ng kurso sa **pangunang lunas** sa Red Cross.","translation":"He took a course in **first aid** at the Red Cross."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapahayag ng matinding paghamak, pag-alipusta, o pagmamaliit sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: The national sport of Marites and online bashers. Panglait is when your tita comments on your weight gain during a family reunion. It's the 'roast me' session you never signed up for. It's more than just criticism; it's meant to sting and belittle. The classic 'Anong ambag mo?' can be a form of paglait.
usage_notes: A strong word for verbal abuse or severe mockery.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi maganda ang **paglait** sa kapwa, anuman ang kanyang itsura o estado sa buhay.","translation":"It is not good to **mock** others, whatever their appearance or status in life may be."},{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na ang **paglait** sa kanyang mga ginagawa.","translation":"Stop your **scorning** of his actions."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi mainit at hindi rin malamig; katamtaman ang temperatura, karaniwang tumutukoy sa tubig.
original_explanation: The temperature of coffee that you forgot about because you were scrolling on TikTok. It's not hot, not cold, just... meh. It's also used to describe a relationship that's lost its spark. "Yung pagmamahal niya, maligamgam na lang." It's that awkward in-between state of existence.
usage_notes: Primarily used for liquids. Can be used metaphorically for feelings or relationships.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit ka ng **maligamgam** na tubig para sa iyong lalamunan.","translation":"Use **lukewarm** water for your throat."},{"sentence":"Naging **maligamgam** ang pagtanggap ng madla sa bagong pelikula.","translation":"The public's reception of the new movie was **tepid**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng tinig o telepono upang makipag-ugnayan sa isang tao.
original_explanation: The command form. This is what your boss tells you: "Tawagan mo ang kliyente." (Call the client.) Or what your friend messages you when they're too lazy to type: "Tawagan mo ako." (Call me.)
usage_notes: Focus is on the person/place being called. Contrast with 'tumawag' (actor-focus) and 'itawag' (thing-being-called-focus).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **tawagan** mo si nanay at sabihin mong pauwi na ako.","translation":"Please, **call** mom and tell her I'm on my way home."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan kong **tawagan** ang opisina pero laging abala.","translation":"I tried **to call** the office but it's always busy."}]

translation: to all be the same; to be uniform
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng pagkakapareho o pagkakaisa sa katangian ng lahat ng miyembro ng isang grupo.
etymology: From mag- (verb-forming prefix) + pare-pareha (reduplication of pareha, indicating plurality).
original_explanation: This is 'magpareho' but on a group level. It's when the whole barkada decides to wear white for a beach trip, or when all the answers in a multiple-choice test are suspiciously 'C'. 'Para iwas gulo, dapat magpare-pareha na lang ang uniform sa opisina.' (To avoid trouble, the office uniforms should just all be the same.) It implies uniformity across more than two items.
usage_notes: The reduplication of 'pare-' from 'pareho' indicates that the similarity applies to all members of a group (three or more).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinadya nilang **magpare-pareha** ng suot para sa family picture.","translation":"They intentionally made their outfits **all the same** for the family picture."},{"sentence":"Hindi pwedeng **magpare-pareha** ang disenyo; kailangan may konting pagkakaiba.","translation":"The designs can't **all be the same**; there needs to be some slight difference."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng matinding pagkalito, pagkabalisa, o kaguluhan ng isip na dulot ng isang malaking suliranin.
original_explanation: That feeling when you have five deadlines, your internet is down, your boss is calling, and you just remembered you forgot to pay your Meralco bill. It's the mental equivalent of EDSA traffic at 6 PM on a payday Friday. Pure chaos in your brain.
usage_notes: A deep, literary word for mental distress.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang biglaang pagkawala ng trabaho ay nagdulot sa kanya ng matinding **linggatong**.","translation":"The sudden loss of his job caused him great **mental anguish**."},{"sentence":"Nababalot ng **linggatong** ang kanyang isipan dahil sa mga problema sa pamilya.","translation":"His mind is filled with **distress** because of family problems."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghila sa tainga bilang paraan ng pagpaparusa o pagbibiro.
original_explanation: A classic Pinoy disciplinary action, second only to the dreaded `tsinelas`. Your nanay or lola would `pingol` you for being naughty. It's that sharp, twisting pull on the ear that instantly makes you regret what you just did. A variation of the more common `pingot`.
usage_notes: Synonymous with `pingot`. The verb form is `pingulin`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang malikot diyan at baka kita **pingulin**.","translation":"Don't be rowdy there or I might **pull your ear**."},{"sentence":"Napangiwi siya sa sakit nang **pingulin** siya ng kanyang ina.","translation":"He winced in pain when his mother **pulled his ear**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang opisyal na pagtatala ng pangalan o impormasyon sa isang listahan o aklat para sa isang tiyak na layunin.
original_explanation: What you have to do to get your SIM card working, to vote, or to create an account for a new online game. It's the adulting version of 'attendance please!'—lots of forms, lots of waiting in line, and questioning your life choices while filling up 'Mother's Maiden Name'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumunta siya sa COMELEC upang **magrehistro** bilang botante.","translation":"He went to COMELEC to **register** as a voter."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magrehistro** online para makasali sa webinar.","translation":"You need to **register** online to join the webinar."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malawak na lupain na may damo kung saan kumakain ang mga alagang hayop tulad ng baka, kambing, at tupa.
etymology: From Spanish 'pastor' (shepherd). The '-an' suffix denotes a place.
original_explanation: Basically the all-you-can-eat buffet for cows and goats. It's their version of a picnic spot, minus the checkered blanket and plus a lot more... natural fertilizers.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala ng pastol ang mga tupa sa luntiang **pastulan**.","translation":"The shepherd brought the sheep to the green **pasture**."},{"sentence":"Malawak ang **pastulan** sa aming probinsya.","translation":"The **pastureland** in our province is vast."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pormal at sistematikong proseso ng pagsisiyasat o pag-aaral upang matuklasan at masuri ang mga katotohanan ng isang insidente, isyu, o krimen.
etymology: From 'pag-' (nominalizer) + 'imbestiga', which is a Hispanism from Spanish 'investigar' (to investigate).
original_explanation: This is what happens when your mom asks 'Saan ka galing?' and 'Sino kasama mo?'. It's also what you do when you suspect your partner is cheating and you start checking their DMs. On a serious note, it's the official job of the police, journalists, and every 'Marites' in the neighborhood. The goal: to find the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the chismis.
usage_notes: A formal term borrowed from Spanish, commonly used in legal, police, and journalistic contexts. 'Imbestigasyon' is a common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsasagawa ng masusing **pag-iimbestiga** ang mga pulis sa nangyaring krimen.","translation":"The police are conducting a thorough **investigation** into the crime that occurred."},{"sentence":"Ang resulta ng **pag-iimbestiga** ay ilalabas sa susunod na linggo.","translation":"The result of the **investigation** will be released next week."}]

translation: to lift up; to bring up from a lower place
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkuha o pag-angat ng isang bagay mula sa isang mababang lugar patungo sa isang mataas na lugar, o mula sa ilalim ng tubig. Ginagamit din ito sa metaporikal na kahulugan ng pagtulong sa isang tao na makaahon sa kahirapan.
original_explanation: Literally, pulling something up from below, like getting a bucket of water from a well ('balon'). Figuratively, it's the ultimate 'sana all' for someone struggling. It's when you help someone get out of a tough spot, like poverty, debt, or a bad breakup. It's the ultimate act of 'bayanihan' or friendship—to pull someone up with you.
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of floods (pagbaha) when people move things to higher ground, or in a socio-economic context of uplifting someone from poverty.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumulong siyang **mag-ahon** ng mga gamit mula sa binahang bahay.","translation":"He helped **lift** the things from the flooded house."},{"sentence":"Ang edukasyon ay isang paraan upang **mag-ahon** sa kahirapan.","translation":"Education is a way to **rise** from poverty."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkaalis o pagkatanggal ng isang buto mula sa normal nitong posisyon sa isang kasukasuan.
original_explanation: When your shoulder pops out of its socket after a failed TikTok dance move. It’s a physical 'diskompasado' for your bones. The reason why you shouldn't try those 'extreme' yoga poses you saw on Instagram without a professional.
usage_notes: A medical or technical term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon siya ng **dislokasyon** sa balikat habang naglalaro ng basketball.","translation":"He suffered a shoulder **dislocation** while playing basketball."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng agarang lunas ang **dislokasyon** upang maiwasan ang permanenteng pinsala.","translation":"A **dislocation** needs immediate treatment to avoid permanent damage."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lihim na pag-uunawaan o kasunduan ng dalawa o higit pang tao upang gumawa ng isang bagay na labag sa batas o masama.
etymology: From "sabwat" (conspiracy). The "pag- -an" affix with reduplication of the first syllable of the root ("sa") indicates the act or process of doing something.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "group project" from hell. When your team secretly plots to overthrow the boss, or when your friends conspire to surprise you on your birthday (but the evil version is more dramatic). It's the "us against the world" vibe, but make it illegal or shady. The OG "Team Building" for villains.
usage_notes: Often carries a negative and serious connotation, implying illegal or harmful activities.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nabunyag ang **pagsasabwatan** ng mga opisyal upang nakawin ang pondo ng bayan.","translation":"The **conspiracy** of the officials to steal the nation's funds was exposed."},{"sentence":"May hinala ang guro na may **pagsasabwatan** ang mga estudyante para mandaya sa pagsusulit.","translation":"The teacher suspects there is a **collusion** among the students to cheat on the exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang kasangkapan o instrumento na ginagamit sa pagputol, paghiwa, o pagtabas ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: Your go-to tool when you need to make a cut. It could be a 'gunting' (scissors) for your art project, a 'kutsilyo' (knife) for the onions that make you cry about your life choices, or a 'lagari' (saw) for that tree branch (or toxic relationship) you need to get rid of.
usage_notes: Isang pangkalahatang termino. Karaniwang tinutukoy ang partikular na kasangkapan, ngunit ginagamit ito kapag humihingi ng 'anumang bagay na magagamit sa pagputol'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiabot ng **pamputol** ng kuko.","translation":"Please hand me the nail **cutter**."},{"sentence":"Wala akong mahanap na matinong **pamputol** ng papel.","translation":"I can't find a decent paper **cutter**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalabas ng itlog mula sa katawan, karaniwang ginagawa ng mga ibon at reptilya.
original_explanation: The daily grind for a manok. Also, a slang term in the BPO world for getting a zero score on a call or survey. "Nako, na-QA ako, baka umitlog ako nito." It means you failed spectacularly.
usage_notes: Can be literal (for animals) or slang for getting a zero or failing completely.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Araw-araw **umitlog** ang alaga naming manok.","translation":"Our pet chicken **lays an egg** every day."},{"sentence":"Naku, **umitlog** ako sa exam sa Math, wala akong nasagot!","translation":"Oh no, I **laid an egg** (got a zero) on the Math exam, I couldn't answer anything!"}]

translation: to rummage through; to dig into
meaning_filipino: Ang masinsinang paghalungkat o paghahanap sa loob ng isang lalagyan, bag, o anumang siksikang espasyo.
original_explanation: The act of desperately searching for something in your messy bag, like looking for your keys or that one specific lipstick. Or when a customs officer decides your 'pasalubong' box needs a 'deep dive'. Parang paghahanap mo ng jowa sa dating app, 'butbot' lang nang 'butbot' sa mga profile.
usage_notes: Used as a root word for verbs like 'butbutin' or in verb phrases like 'mag-butbot'. It implies a somewhat frantic and messy search.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, mag-**butbot** lang ako sandali sa bag ko at hahanapin ko ang susi.","translation":"Don't worry, I'll just **rummage through** my bag for a moment and look for the key."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang mag-**butbot** ng mga lumang gamit sa baul ng lola niya.","translation":"He likes to **dig into** the old things in his grandmother's chest."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang patungan na may apat na paa, karaniwang gawa sa kahoy o metal, na ginagamit bilang suporta sa pagpuputol ng kahoy o bilang pansamantalang lamesa.
etymology: From 'pa-' + 'lagari' + '-an'. A locative noun, 'a place for sawing ('lagari')'.
original_explanation: That X-shaped wooden thingy your tatay or the neighborhood karpintero uses to chop wood or hold up a sheet of plywood. It's the unsung hero of every home construction project and garage DIY. Basically a low-tech, portable workbench.
usage_notes: A specific piece of equipment used in carpentry.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipatong mo ang tabla sa **palagarian** bago mo lagariin.","translation":"Place the plank on the **sawhorse** before you saw it."},{"sentence":"Gumawa sila ng pansamantalang mesa gamit ang dalawang **palagarian** at isang pinto.","translation":"They made a temporary table using two **trestles** and a door."}]

translation: to rummage through something; to search thoroughly
meaning_filipino: Ang paghalungkat nang husto sa isang bagay o lalagyan upang mahanap ang isang partikular na kagamitan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'butbot' at hulaping pandiwa na '-in'.
original_explanation: The command or action form of 'butbot'. It's what your mom tells you not to do to the freshly folded laundry. It's the act of going through someone's stuff, like a detective trying to find clues or a jealous partner checking a phone. 'Wag mo butbutin phone ko!'
usage_notes: A transitive verb, similar to 'halungkatin' or 'kalkalin'. It implies a more focused and intentional rummaging compared to the general act of 'mag-butbot'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **butbutin** ang buong aparador para mahanap ang aking birth certificate.","translation":"I need **to rummage through** the entire closet to find my birth certificate."},{"sentence":"Pinagalitan siya dahil sa ugali niyang **butbutin** ang bag ng iba.","translation":"He was scolded for his habit of **rummaging through** other people's bags."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng puwersa upang mapaalis o mapagalaw ang isang bagay palayo sa sarili.
original_explanation: What you do to a door that says "PUSH". Or what your friend does to you to get you to go talk to your crush. It's the opposite of 'hila' (pull).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumulak** siya ng kariton na puno ng gulay.","translation":"He **pushed** a cart full of vegetables."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **tumulak** sa pila.","translation":"Don't **push** in the line."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang supling o bunga ng pagsasama ng mga magulang; isang tao kaugnay sa kanyang mga magulang.
original_explanation: The original 'investment' of Filipino parents. Also, the person who gets asked 'Kailan ka mag-aasawa?' at every family reunion. Can refer to your actual offspring, or what your boss calls you when they want you to do overtime: 'Anak, pa-extend naman ng konti.' It's a term of endearment, a statement of fact, and sometimes, a call to duty.
usage_notes: A fundamental kinship term. Can be used gender-neutrally, or specified with 'na lalaki' (son) or 'na babae' (daughter). Also used as a term of endearment by elders to younger people, not necessarily their own child.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahal na mahal ng mga magulang ang kanilang kaisa-isang **anak**.","translation":"The parents dearly love their only **child**."},{"sentence":"Tawag sa akin ng ale, '**Anak**, pakiabot naman ng bayad ko.'","translation":"The lady called to me, '**Child**, please pass my fare.'"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging maramdamin, madaling maantig ang damdamin, o labis na pagpapahalaga sa mga bagay na may kaugnayan sa nakaraan.
original_explanation: This is your "throwback Thursday" mood personified. It's when you can't throw away that movie ticket from your first date, or you cry while watching a Jollibee commercial. It's being ruled by the heart and memories, often with a side of "hugot."
usage_notes: Used to describe a person's nature or to intensify the quality of being sentimental.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya maitapon ang mga lumang sulat dahil sa kanyang **pagkasentimental**.","translation":"She can't throw away the old letters because of her **being sentimental**."},{"sentence":"**Pagkasentimental** ng kantang iyan, naaalala ko tuloy ang ex ko.","translation":"That song is **so sentimental**, it makes me remember my ex."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng pagiging malaki at nakausli ang tiyan.
original_explanation: This is the 'dad bod' before 'dad bods' were cool. It's the tiyan that proudly announces, 'I have survived many fiestas and Noche Buenas.' It's not just fat; it's a trophy of a thousand lechon servings and countless bottles of San Mig.
usage_notes: Often used humorously or in a slightly teasing manner to describe someone with a large belly.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **butyog** si Mang Kanor dahil sa araw-araw na pag-inom ng beer.","translation":"Mang Kanor became **pot-bellied** from drinking beer every day."},{"sentence":"Pinagtawanan niya ang sarili niyang **butyog** na tiyan sa salamin.","translation":"He laughed at his own **paunchy** stomach in the mirror."}]

translation: to have something taken/fetched; to have a picture taken
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o paghiling sa iba na kunin ang isang bagay para sa iyo; ang pagpapahintulot na kunan ka ng litrato.
original_explanation: The official verb of delegating errands. 'Paki-abot' is for things within reach; magpakuha is for when you need someone to go and get something. 'Magpakuha ka ng tubig sa ref' (Have someone get water from the fridge). It's also the go-to verb for photoshoots: 'Tara, magpakuha tayo ng picture!' (Let's go have our picture taken!). It’s the verb for when you are the subject, not the actor.
usage_notes: Very common in two main contexts: asking someone to fetch something, and asking someone to take a photo of you.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puwede ba akong **magpakuha** sa iyo ng pagkain sa baba?","translation":"Can I **have you get** me food from downstairs?"},{"sentence":"Gusto naming **magpakuha** ng family picture sa tapat ng simbahan.","translation":"We want to **have a family picture taken** in front of the church."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mitolohikal na ibon sa isang sikat na Pilipinong korido (metrical romance) na may pamagat na "Ibong Adarna." Kilala ang ibon sa kanyang makulay na balahibo at mahiwagang awit na may kakayahang magpagaling ng anumang karamdaman.
etymology: The name's origin is debated, but some scholars link "Adarna" to a variation of the name "Adelfa" or suggest a connection to the Spanish word "adornar" (to adorn), referencing the bird's beautiful plumage. It is the central figure in the epic poem "Ibong Adarna."
original_explanation: The OG magical creature of Filipino lit before Pokémon even existed. The Ibong Adarna is that elusive, high-maintenance bird that changes colors and whose song is literally the cure for everything. But be careful! If you're not worthy, its poop can turn you to stone. It's the ultimate quest item in Filipino folklore, sought after by princes in what is basically a 16th-century version of a very difficult video game side quest.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to the bird from the epic poem, which is a required reading in Philippine high schools. The name can also be used metaphorically to refer to something beautiful but elusive and difficult to obtain.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang awit ng Ibong **Adarna** ang tanging lunas sa sakit ng hari.","translation":"The song of the **Adarna** bird is the only cure for the king's illness."},{"sentence":"Hinahanap niya ang kanyang 'Ibong **Adarna**,' ang pangarap na matagal na niyang inaasam.","translation":"He is searching for his '**Adarna** Bird,' the dream he has long been hoping for."}]

translation: to become sunny; for the sun to come out
meaning_filipino: Pagsikat o paglabas ng araw, na nagiging sanhi ng pagliwanag at pag-init ng paligid.
original_explanation: The ultimate plot twist after a week of non-stop rain. When the sun finally shows up, everyone suddenly wants to go to the beach or finally do their laundry. 'Sana all maarawan.'
usage_notes: A meteorological verb. Often used in contrast to 'umulan' (to rain).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **umaraw** bukas para matuloy ang ating lakad.","translation":"I hope it **will be sunny** tomorrow so our trip can proceed."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng malakas na bagyo, sa wakas ay **umaraw** din.","translation":"After the strong typhoon, the sun finally **came out**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtalon nang may higit na lakas, taas, o layo kumpara sa karaniwang paglukso.
original_explanation: This is the upgraded version of 'lukso'. It's not just a jump; it's a leap. Like when you **lumundag** to a conclusion, or **lumundag** from one career to a completely different one. #LeapOfFaith.
usage_notes: Implies a more forceful or farther jump than 'lumukso'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mula sa mataas na bato, **lumundag** siya patungo sa malamig na tubig ng ilog.","translation":"From the high rock, he **leaped** into the cold water of the river."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **lumundag** para maabot ang nakasabit na prutas.","translation":"You need to **jump high** to reach the hanging fruit."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang punong ehekutibo o pinakamataas na opisyal ng isang lungsod o munisipalidad.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "mayor" (mas malaki, mas mataas).
original_explanation: 'Yung pinakasikat na tao sa city hall. Sila 'yung nag-aapruba ng mga proyekto, nagbibigay ng anunsyo kapag may bagyo ('Walang pasok!'), at 'yung mukha nila laging nasa tarpaulin tuwing Pasko at Fiesta. Kapag may problema sa barangay na hindi na kaya ng kapitan, sa opisina ni Meyor ang takbo.
usage_notes: Ang "Mayor" (capital M) ay madalas gamitin bilang titulo, e.g., "Mayor Isko". Ang "meyor" (lowercase) ay tumutukoy sa posisyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **meyor** ng aming lungsod ay nag-anunsyo ng bagong programa para sa mga kabataan.","translation":"The **mayor** of our city announced a new program for the youth."},{"sentence":"Sino ang iboboto mong **meyor** sa darating na halalan?","translation":"Who will you vote for as **mayor** in the upcoming election?"}]

translation: to build a bonfire, to burn something in a pile
meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng malaking apoy sa labas, karaniwang ginagamit para sunugin ang mga basura, tuyong dahon, o para magpainit.
original_explanation: Your provincial cousin's version of a party. It's the OG 'lit'. You gather around, maybe roast some marshmallows (or hotdogs on a stick), and tell ghost stories. Also what you do with your ex's love letters. 'Tara, magsiga tayo ng basura at ng mga masasamang alaala.'
usage_notes: Usually refers to an open-air fire, not a controlled one like in a stove or fireplace. It can be for warmth, cooking, or burning refuse. Often associated with rural or outdoor settings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bawal **magsiga** ng basura sa loob ng siyudad.","translation":"It is forbidden **to burn** trash in a pile within the city."},{"sentence":"Nagplano ang magkakaibigan na **magsiga** sa dalampasigan.","translation":"The friends planned **to build a bonfire** on the beach."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging madali, mabilis, at hindi kumplikadong gawin o maunawaan.
etymology: From ka- + dali + -an, signifying the quality of being easy or quick.
original_explanation: Ito yung promise ng mga 'life hacks' sa TikTok. Yung pag-asa na sana lahat ng bagay sa buhay, kasing dali lang i-solve ng pag-scan ng QR code para sa GCash payment. The opposite of 'pahirapan'.
usage_notes: Used to describe the simplicity or speed of a task or concept.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagulat ako sa **kadalian** ng pagsusulit.","translation":"I was surprised by the **ease** of the exam."},{"sentence":"Ang **kadalian** ng paggamit ng app ang dahilan kung bakit ito sikat.","translation":"The **ease** of use of the app is the reason why it's popular."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay na ginagamit upang takpan ang isang butas, sisidlan, o anumang mayroong bukasan.
etymology: From `pan-` + `takip` (cover). The `n` in `pan-` assimilates to the `t` sound, becoming `pana-`.
original_explanation: The `panakip` is your ultimate tool for "ghosting" a problem. May utang na naniningil? `Panakip` ng pinto. May chismis sa office? `Panakip` ng tenga. But literally, it's the lid for your Tupperware, the cover for your pot of adobo, or even the panyo you use to cover your face when you see your ex with their new jowa. It's a tool for concealment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawawala ang **panakip** ng kaldero.","translation":"The **lid** of the pot is missing."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang libro bilang **panakip** sa kanyang mukha.","translation":"She used the book as a **cover** for her face."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginawa o sinabi sa paraang naglalayong magbigay-aliw o katatawanan.
original_explanation: When you say something wild and your friend gives you a look, you say, "Joke lang!" This is the word for that vibe. It's the tone of a stand-up comedian, your tito's corny jokes, or a sarcastic comment delivered with a smile. "Sabi ko, 'Ang ganda mo ngayon,' pero patawa lang." (Be careful with this one, it can backfire!)
usage_notes: Often used to clarify that a statement was not meant to be taken seriously.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinabi niya iyon nang **patawa**, kaya huwag mong seryosohin.","translation":"He said that **jokingly**, so don't take it seriously."},{"sentence":"May mga **patawa** siyang hirit sa gitna ng seryosong pulong.","translation":"He has some **comical** quips in the middle of the serious meeting."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malawak na lugar na may makakapal na puno at halaman.
original_explanation: Not just a place with trees, but a place with engkanto, diwata, and probably no phone signal. It's where horror movie characters go to die and where your lola warns you not to make loud noises. Also, what the city feels like during a 12.12 sale.
usage_notes: A fundamental word. Can be used metaphorically to mean a chaotic place (e.g., 'gubat ang siyudad'). 'Kagubatan' refers to a larger, denser forest area.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naligaw sila sa gitna ng madilim na **gubat**.","translation":"They got lost in the middle of the dark **forest**."},{"sentence":"Maraming hayop ang naninirahan sa **gubat** ng Amazon.","translation":"Many animals live in the Amazon **jungle**."}]

translation: to maintain (something) in a place; to cause to remain
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapanatili o pag-iingat sa isang bagay, kalagayan, o posisyon sa isang partikular na lugar o estado.
etymology: Mula sa `pa-` + `tili` (isang bihirang salitang-ugat na nangangahulugang 'manatili') + `-han`.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of "stay put." When your boss tells you to "panatilihan ang kalinisan sa office," it means "maintain the cleanliness." It's the act of making sure something doesn't change or leave. Parang 'yung effort mong i-maintain 'yung "sparks" sa relationship niyo.
usage_notes: Isang pandiwang nakapokus sa obheto. Halimbawa: "Panatilihan mo ang katahimikan." (Maintain the silence.)
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Panatilihan** natin ang kalinisan ng ating kapaligiran.","translation":"Let us **maintain** the cleanliness of our environment."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **panatilihan** ang magandang reputasyon sa mundong mapanghusga.","translation":"It's difficult **to maintain** a good reputation in a judgmental world."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malakas, matinis, at tuloy-tuloy na pagtahol ng aso.
etymology: Isang salitang onomatopeik, na hango sa tunog ng pagtahol.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung concert ng aso ng kapitbahay mo tuwing 3 AM. Hindi 'yung cute na 'arf arf', ito 'yung 'KANGKANG!' na parang may kaaway na multo at gigisingin ang buong barangay. The official soundtrack of sleepless nights.
usage_notes: Ito ay naglalarawan ng isang partikular na uri ng malakas at paulit-ulit na pagtahol, iba sa karaniwang 'tahol' o 'kahol'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gabi-gabi ay naririnig namin ang **kangkang** ng asong kalye sa labas.","translation":"Every night, we hear the **incessant barking** of the street dog outside."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pahayag o kilos na walang katuturan, kahangalan, o lubos na kalokohan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na "disparate" (nonsense, foolish remark).
original_explanation: When someone says something so out of this world, so illogical, na mapapa-"Huh?" ka na lang. It's not just a simple mistake; it's a statement that's completely bonkers. Parang 'yung sinabi ng tito mo na "ang paglalaro ng video games ay nakakabobo" habang nanonood siya ng fake news sa Facebook. That's a disparate.
usage_notes: Isang malalim na salita na bihirang gamitin sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pawang **disparate** lamang ang mga binitawan niyang salita.","translation":"The words he uttered were pure **nonsense**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala sa kanya, puro **disparate** ang alam niyan.","translation":"Don't believe him, he's full of **absurdities**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaki na madalas tumatambay sa kanto ng kalye, karaniwang walang ginagawa.
etymology: From Spanish *cantonero*, meaning a man who hangs around street corners.
original_explanation: The classic "kanto boy." He's the guy leaning against a wall, watching the world go by, and has an opinion on everything from basketball to politics. He's the unofficial security guard, traffic director, and news anchor of the block.
usage_notes: Like its female counterpart, this can be used neutrally to mean "loiterer" or can carry a slightly negative connotation of being idle or unproductive.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-iinuman ang mga **kantonero** sa tapat ng tindahan.","translation":"The **street corner guys** are drinking in front of the store."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halamang-ugat na may puting laman, karaniwang pahaba, at madalas gamiting sangkap sa mga lutuin tulad ng sinigang.
original_explanation: The unsung hero of Sinigang. It's that white vegetable that absorbs all the sour, savory goodness of the broth. Some people hate it, some people love it. It's the culinary equivalent of that one friend who's a bit bland on their own but makes the whole 'barkada' better.
usage_notes: Sa konteksto ng Pilipinas, halos palaging tumutukoy ito sa puting labanos o 'daikon radish'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakihiwa ng **labanos** para sa sinigang.","translation":"Please slice the **radish** for the sinigang."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging sunog o nasunog nang bahagya, lalo na sa pagkain, na nag-iiwan ng maitim na kulay at mapait na lasa.
original_explanation: It's that fine line between 'perfectly toasted' and 'oh no, my pandesal is now a charcoal briquette.' It's the smell of sinangag (fried rice) that was left on the pan for 30 seconds too long. It has that distinct, slightly bitter taste of a minor kitchen tragedy.
usage_notes: Specifically used for food that has been over-cooked, toasted, or roasted to the point of being partially burnt. Less severe than 'sunog' (completely burnt).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Medyo **bangi** ang ilalim ng sinaing, pero masarap pa rin.","translation":"The bottom of the cooked rice is a bit **scorched**, but it's still delicious."},{"sentence":"Ayoko ng tinapay na **bangi** ang lasa.","translation":"I don't like bread that tastes **burnt**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang laman na nakukuha mula sa isang usa, na itinuturing na "game meat" o karne mula sa hayop na hinuhuli sa ligaw.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "carne" (karne) at Tagalog na "usa" (deer).
original_explanation: This is Bambi meat, a.k.a. venison. It's not something you'd find in a regular supermarket. You usually get this from hunters or in specialty restaurants, especially in provinces. It has a stronger, "gamey" taste. Think of it as the indie artist of meats – not mainstream, but has a dedicated following.
usage_notes: Karaniwang niluluto bilang tapa, adobo, o caldereta. Itinuturing na exotic na pagkain sa maraming lugar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap gawing tapa ang **karne ng usa**.","translation":"**Venison** is delicious when made into tapa."},{"sentence":"May kilala ka bang nagbebenta ng **karne ng usa**?","translation":"Do you know anyone who sells **venison**?"}]

translation: will vlog; will create a video blog
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos sa hinaharap ng paglikha at pag-publish ng isang video blog o 'vlog'.
etymology: A Tagalog verb formation (`mag-` + duplicated first syllable `vo-` for future tense) applied to the English clipped compound 'vlog' (video log).
original_explanation: This is the future tense of turning your life into content. It's the promise you make to your followers: "Magvovlog ako sa Baguio next week, abangan n'yo!" It's the game plan for your next YouTube upload. The content creator's version of "I will write in my diary later."
usage_notes: The future tense of the Taglish verb `magvlog`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa susunod na linggo, **magvovlog** ako ng isang 'a day in my life' video.","translation":"Next week, I **will vlog** a 'day in my life' video."},{"sentence":"**Magvovlog** ka ba sa concert mamaya?","translation":"**Will** you **vlog** at the concert later?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ideya o panukala na inihaharap para sa pagsasaalang-alang o pagpapasya ng iba.
original_explanation: That thing your boss asks for in a meeting but might not actually listen to. Or what your friends give you about your love life that you also might not listen to. A mungkahi can range from "Mag-Jollibee na lang tayo" to a full-blown business proposal. It's the polite Filipino way of saying "Hey, I have an idea, hear me out..."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **mungkahi** ako para mapabuti ang ating proyekto.","translation":"I have a **suggestion** to improve our project."},{"sentence":"Tinatanggap namin ang anumang **mungkahi** mula sa inyo.","translation":"We accept any **recommendations** from you."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mamamayan ng Republika ng Pilipinas. Ginagamit din ito upang tukuyin ang pambansang wika ng Pilipinas na batay sa Tagalog.
etymology: Mula sa pangalang "Felipe", na ipinangalan sa Hari ng Espanya na si Haring Felipe II (King Philip II), kung saan hinango ang pangalan ng bansa, "Las Islas Filipinas".
original_explanation: A 'Filipino' is someone who points with their lips, says 'psst' to get your attention, and has a 'good morning' towel that's been around since the Marcos era. We're a people powered by rice, chismis, and resilience. Being Filipino is also about the 'Filipino Time' struggle, the extreme hospitality of making a guest eat even if they're full, and the magical ability to fit a whole family on one tricycle. It's a whole vibe.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa mga tao (isang Filipino, mga Filipino) o sa wika (ang wikang Filipino). Madalas na ipinagpapalit sa 'Pilipino', bagaman ang 'Filipino' ang opisyal na termino para sa wika at mamamayan ayon sa konstitusyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagmamalaki kong ako ay isang **Filipino**.","translation":"I am proud to be a **Filipino**."},{"sentence":"Ang **Filipino** ang pambansang wika ng Pilipinas.","translation":"**Filipino** is the national language of the Philippines."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang banayad na pagdaramdam o pagtatampo na ipinapahiwatig sa pamamagitan ng hindi pagkibo, paglayo, o pagbabago sa pakikitungo, karaniwang sa isang taong malapit sa iyo, na naghihintay ng suyò.
original_explanation: It's not anger, it's not sadness, it's... tampo. It's when you're upset with your jowa but you don't wanna say it, so you just go quiet and wait for them to ask "Babe, okay ka lang?" with a peace offering of milk tea. It's a silent protest fueled by a desire for affection. The cure? Lambing.
usage_notes: Isang salitang kultural na naglalarawan ng isang uri ng hindi pasalita at pasibong pagdamdam upang makakuha ng paghingi ng tawad o paglalambing ('suyo' o 'lambing').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **tampo** yata sa akin si Maria dahil hindi ako sumipot sa usapan namin.","translation":"I think Maria is **sulking** with me because I didn't show up for our appointment."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang talaan ng mga halagang kailangang bayaran ng isang kumpanya o indibidwal sa mga nagpapautang o tagapagtustos.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "cuenta" (account) at salitang Tagalog na "utang" (debt).
original_explanation: This is the official list of everyone you owe money to. Your "utang list" but with a corporate glow-up. If this list gets too long, you might need to start selling your Funko Pop collection or mag-instant noodles until the next sahod.
usage_notes: Isang terminong karaniwang ginagamit sa larangan ng accounting at pagnenegosyo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inaasikaso ng accountant ang **kuwenta ng pagkakautang** ng kumpanya bago matapos ang buwan.","translation":"The accountant is handling the company's **accounts payable** before the end of the month."}]

translation: to be bewildered; to be confused
meaning_filipino: Ang malito o mawala sa sarili dahil sa pagkalito, pagtataka, o pagkagulat.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na sinabihan ka ng "we need to talk" at bigla kang nag-rewind ng lahat ng kasalanan mo sa isip mo. You're stunned, confused, and your brain just blue-screens. Para kang na-disconnect sa Zoom meeting ng buhay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay **nabigaw** sa dami ng taong dumating sa kanyang handaan.","translation":"She was **bewildered** by the number of people who came to her party."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mabigaw** sa mga kumplikadong tagubilin.","translation":"Don't get **confused** by the complicated instructions."}]

meaning_filipino: Iluto ang bigas upang maging kanin.
etymology: From `i-` (verb prefix) + `saing` (the act of cooking rice).
original_explanation: The most important command in any Filipino household. If you don't know how to do this, your Pinoy license might be revoked. It's the foundation of every meal, the real MVP. Forgetting to do this is a level 10 crisis. 'Nak, paki-**isaing** na, gutom na ako.'
usage_notes: Refers specifically to cooking rice.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maghugas ka muna ng bigas bago mo ito **isaing**.","translation":"Wash the rice first before you **cook** it."},{"sentence":"Sino ang nakalimot na mag-**isaing**?","translation":"Who forgot to **cook rice**?"}]

translation: wake (venue); place where a wake is held
meaning_filipino: Ang lugar kung saan nakalagak ang isang yumaong tao upang paglamayan bago ang libing.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'burol' (wake), na may mga panlaping 'kina-' at '-an'.
original_explanation: This is the place for the lamay. It's where family and friends gather to pay their last respects, play card games like tong-its to stay awake, eat free coffee and biscuits, and reminisce about the person who passed. It’s a sad but also deeply communal Filipino experience. The 'burol' is the wake itself, and the kinabuburulan is the specific venue.
usage_notes: More specific than 'burol'. 'Burol' can mean the event, while 'kinabuburulan' refers to the location of the event.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumunta kami sa **kinabuburulan** ni Lolo para mag-alay ng dasal.","translation":"We went to the **place of Lolo's wake** to offer a prayer."},{"sentence":"Ang **kinabuburulan** ay sa isang kapilya malapit sa kanilang bahay.","translation":"The **wake is being held** at a chapel near their house."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang marahas na pag-aalsa o pagtutol laban sa isang umiiral na pamahalaan, awtoridad, o sistema.
etymology: Possibly a blend or related to *sik* meaning 'to rise' or 'to throb'.
original_explanation: Think Katipunan-level drama. This isn't just complaining on Twitter; this is a full-blown, take-up-arms, "para sa bayan" kind of revolt. It's the ultimate "I've had enough!" against an oppressive system. In modern terms, it's the feeling you get when your internet provider cuts off your service during a crucial Zoom meeting, but scaled up by a million.
usage_notes: Often used in historical or literary contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **himagsik** ng mga Pilipino laban sa mga mananakop ay tanda ng kanilang pagmamahal sa kalayaan.","translation":"The **rebellion** of the Filipinos against the colonizers is a sign of their love for freedom."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula ang isang **himagsik** sa mga manggagawa dahil sa hindi makatarungang sahod.","translation":"A **revolt** started among the workers due to unjust wages."}]

translation: to refute, to deny, to disprove
meaning_filipino: Itanggi o patunayan na hindi totoo ang isang pahayag, paratang, o paniniwala.
etymology: From `pa-` + `bulaan` (false, liar) + `-an`. To declare something as false.
original_explanation: This is what you do when your friend posts an old, unflattering photo of you. You slide into the comments to **pabulaanan** the chismis that you ever looked like that. It's the official verb of damage control. "I object, your honor!"
usage_notes: A formal word often used in legal, academic, or journalistic contexts to mean 'to formally deny' or 'disprove'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **pabulaanan** ang mga akusasyon laban sa kanya sa harap ng korte.","translation":"He tried to **refute** the accusations against him in front of the court."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **pabulaanan** ang isang katotohanan na may matibay na ebidensya.","translation":"It is difficult to **disprove** a fact that has strong evidence."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang trabaho ay ang pag-type ng mga dokumento gamit ang isang makinilya (typewriter).
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "tagapag-" (doer/agent of action) at sa salitang ugat na "makinilya" (typewriter).
original_explanation: The ancestor of the modern-day Data Entry Specialist. Before keyboards and backspace keys, they were the masters of the clack-clack-ding, using Tipp-Ex as their undo button. Ask your lolo or lola about them.
usage_notes: Isang lipas na termino dahil sa pagkawala ng paggamit ng mga makinilya. Ang modernong katumbas ay 'typist' o 'data encoder'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Noong araw, isang marangal na trabaho ang pagiging **tagapagmakinilya** sa isang opisina ng gobyerno.","translation":"Back in the day, being a **typist** in a government office was a respectable job."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang damdamin ng pagkadismaya, hinanakit, o sama ng loob na kinikimkim laban sa isang tao o sitwasyon.
etymology: A compound word, possibly from 'sala' (fault, miss) and 'hati' (disposition, feeling), implying a 'flaw in one's feelings'.
original_explanation: It's that low-key 'sama ng loob' you feel when your friend sees your message but doesn't reply. It's not full-blown anger, just a silent, simmering 'tampo'. The feeling of being 'sawi' in a small, poetic way. You won't hear this at the palengke, but you'll read it in a Florante at Laura meme.
usage_notes: This is a deep, literary word. Not used in everyday conversation, but found in classic literature and poetry.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **salaghati** ang kanyang puso dahil sa pagtataksil ng kaibigan.","translation":"His heart was full of **resentment** because of his friend's betrayal."},{"sentence":"Dapat iwasan ang pagkikimkim ng **salaghati** upang maging magaan ang buhay.","translation":"One should avoid harboring **ill feelings** to have a lighter life."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pahayag, kwento, o sitwasyon na itinuturing na positibo, malinis, at nakakabuti sa kalooban.
etymology: Isang pariralang Taglish na pinagsasama ang Ingles na "wholesome" at ang Filipino slang na "yarn" (mula sa "iyan").
original_explanation: Kapag may nag-share ng good news or a cute story, tapos sasabihin ng kaibigan mo, "Wholesome yarn!" Ito ay paraan ng pagsang-ayon sa isang kwento na nagbibigay ng good vibes. 'Yarn' is gay lingo for 'iyan' or a confirmation, so this means "That's a wholesome story right there!"
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa mga impormal na usapan, lalo na sa social media, bilang reaksyon sa isang bagay na nakakatuwa o nakakataba ng puso.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-post siya ng picture kasama ang lola niya. **Wholesome yarn**!","translation":"She posted a picture with her grandma. **That's a wholesome story**!"},{"sentence":"Friend: 'Tinulungan ko yung pusang kalye kanina.' Ikaw: '**Wholesome yarn**!'","translation":"Friend: 'I helped a stray cat earlier.' You: '**What a wholesome story**!'"}]

meaning_filipino: Iparanas o hayaang maranasan ng isang tao ang isang partikular na kalagayan, damdamin, o pangyayari, kadalasan ay may negatibong konotasyon.
original_explanation: This is the verb for when you want someone to get a taste of their own medicine. 'Sana *pagdanasin* ka ng karma ng triple!' is a classic hugot line. It's about inflicting an experience on someone, like a villain making the hero go through a series of trials.
usage_notes: Used in the imperative or subjunctive mood, often to wish or cause a (usually difficult) experience upon someone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong hilinging **pagdanasin** ang iba ng hirap na dinanas mo.","translation":"Do not wish for others **to experience** the hardship you went through."},{"sentence":"Ang layunin ng kontrabida ay **pagdanasin** ng matinding pagdurusa ang bida.","translation":"The villain's goal is **to make** the hero **experience** intense suffering."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang dokumento na may mga nakalaang espasyo para sulatan ng mga kinakailangang impormasyon.
original_explanation: That thing you have to fill out a million times when applying for a job, a bank account, or a government ID. 'Yung sandamakmak na papel na kailangan ng pangalan, address, birthday, at blood type mo. Ang official term sa "fill-up-an."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisagutan nang maayos ang **pormularyo** ng aplikasyon.","translation":"Please fill out the application **form** properly."},{"sentence":"Kumuha ako ng tatlong kopya ng **pormularyo** para sa pagpaparehistro.","translation":"I got three copies of the registration **form**."}]

meaning_filipino: Gagawa o bubuo ng mga teksto, simbolo, o salita sa isang ibabaw, karaniwan ay papel o screen, gamit ang isang panulat o keyboard.
original_explanation: What you tell your professor you'll do with your thesis, but you end up binge-watching a K-drama instead. "Susulat na po, mamser!" It's the future tense of procrastination. From love letters to resignation letters, this is the verb that starts it all.
usage_notes: Future tense of "sumulat". The 'su-' prefix indicates the future tense of an '-um-' verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Susulat** ako ng liham para sa aking lola sa probinsya.","translation":"I **will write** a letter for my grandmother in the province."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **susulat** ng minutes ng meeting natin ngayon?","translation":"Who **will write** the minutes of our meeting today?"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pagiging pinakamababa o pinakakaunti sa halaga, antas, o sukat.
original_explanation: Describes something that is at the lowest acceptable level. 'Minimum wage' is the classic example. 'Minimum effort' is what you call it when your groupmate adds one slide to the 50-slide presentation... and it's the 'Thank You' slide.
usage_notes: Used interchangeably with the English 'minimum' in modern Taglish. Often precedes a noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumaas na ang **minimo** na sahod sa Metro Manila.","translation":"The **minimum** wage in Metro Manila has increased."},{"sentence":"May **minimo** na bilang ng mga dadalo para matuloy ang event.","translation":"There is a **minimum** number of attendees for the event to proceed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na pagpapatawad sa kasalanan na ipinagkakaloob ng isang pari sa sakramento ng kumpisal.
original_explanation: 'Yung "You are forgiven, my child" moment mo sa loob ng kumpisalan pagkatapos mong aminin lahat ng kasalanan mo, mula sa pagtsismis sa kapitbahay hanggang sa pag-ubos ng ulam na para dapat sa lahat. From Spanish "absolución".
usage_notes: Strictly a religious term within Catholicism.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Humingi siya ng **absulusyon** mula sa pari para sa kanyang mga kasalanan.","translation":"He asked for **absolution** from the priest for his sins."},{"sentence":"Ang sakramento ng kumpisal ay nagtatapos sa pagbibigay ng **absulusyon**.","translation":"The sacrament of confession ends with the giving of **absolution**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kasalukuyang panahon o sa mga pangyayaring nagaganap ngayon.
etymology: Mula sa "sa" (at) + "kasalukuyan" (ang ngayon, mula sa sinaunang salitang-ugat na "salukoy" na nangangahulugang 'mangyari nang sabay').
original_explanation: The more formal cousin of "ngayon." It's the term reporters use on TV Patrol: "Sa kasalukuyan, nagpapatuloy ang imbestigasyon." It's how you start an update to your boss to sound more professional. It’s the official time zone for your problems and your blessings.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa pormal na pagsulat at pagsasalita, tulad ng sa mga balita, akademikong papel, at opisyal na pahayag.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sa kasalukuyan**, siya ang tumatayong CEO ng kumpanya.","translation":"**Currently**, he is the acting CEO of the company."},{"sentence":"Maraming hamon ang kinakaharap ng bansa **sa kasalukuyan**.","translation":"The country is facing many challenges **at present**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng isang parte o piraso mula sa isang kabuuan; ang pakikibahagi sa isang gawain o bagay.
original_explanation: The opposite of "sana all." This is when you actually do something about it. Like when your officemate brings chicharon and you ask them to bumahagi (share). It’s the spirit of "libre" and "balato," the core of Pinoy friendship. "Friend, bumahagi ka naman ng blessings mo diyan!"
usage_notes: Ito ang pandiwang nasa anyong pangkasalukuyan o pangnagdaan (actor-focus) ng salitang-ugat na 'bahagi'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumahagi** siya ng kanyang pagkain sa mga batang lansangan.","translation":"He **shared** his food with the street children."},{"sentence":"Ang bawat miyembro ay inaasahang **bumahagi** sa mga gastusin.","translation":"Every member is expected to **partake** in the expenses."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng dula, pelikula, o palabas na naglalayong magpatawa. Maaari din itong tumukoy sa isang katawa-tawang sitwasyon sa buhay.
original_explanation: Anything that makes you laugh, from a Vice Ganda movie to your love life. "My life is a komedya," you say, when things are so absurdly tragic it becomes funny. It's the genre of Filipino resilience—finding the humor in hardship.
usage_notes: Can refer to the genre or a funny situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong panoorin ang mga pelikulang **komedya** ni Dolphy.","translation":"I love watching Dolphy's **comedy** films."},{"sentence":"Naging isang malaking **komedya** ang nangyari sa party kagabi.","translation":"What happened at the party last night turned into a huge **comedy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang institusyon o tahanan na nagbibigay ng kalinga at tirahan para sa mga ulila o mga batang inabandona.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'ampon' na may hulaping '-an', na nagsasaad ng lugar.
original_explanation: The place where kids without parents are cared for. It's a word loaded with teleserye plotlines, but in reality, it's a place of refuge and hope. A real-life `ampunan` is a community built to give children a chance for a better future.
usage_notes: Ang mas pormal na termino ay 'bahay-ampunan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-donate sila ng mga laruan at pagkain sa lokal na **ampunan**.","translation":"They donated toys and food to the local **orphanage**."},{"sentence":"Lumaki siya sa isang **ampunan** bago siya kinupkop ng isang mabait na pamilya.","translation":"He grew up in an **orphanage** before he was adopted by a kind family."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahan ng katawan at isipan na makaramdam, umunawa, o tumugon sa mga panlabas na estimulo; alinman sa limang pandama.
original_explanation: Your built-in sensor suite. It's the reason you can smell the bagoong from a mile away, feel the 'kilig' when crush messages you, and taste the difference between Coke and Pepsi. It's your entire sensory toolkit for navigating the world... and for avoiding your tita's unsolicited advice.
usage_notes: Refers to the general faculty of sense/feeling. The specific five senses are paningin (sight), pandinig (hearing), pang-amoy (smell), panlasa (taste), and pansalat (touch).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matibay ang **pandamdam** ng mga aso kaya mahusay silang bantay.","translation":"Dogs have a strong **sense** of perception, which is why they are excellent guards."},{"sentence":"Nawalan siya ng **pandamdam** sa kaliwang braso pagkatapos ng aksidente.","translation":"He lost **sensation** in his left arm after the accident."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katawagang Ingles na tumutukoy sa isang bagay na nagkaroon na ng naunang may-ari; segunda-mano.
original_explanation: This is 'preloved's' more formal, car-dealership-sounding cousin. It's what you call a second-hand car to make it sound less like a potential headache and more like a 'certified' bargain. Both mean the same thing: hindi na brand new, but 'preowned' sounds like it comes with a warranty.
usage_notes: Often used for high-value items like cars, watches, and gadgets to imply good condition despite being second-hand.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas mura ang mga **preowned** na sasakyan kumpara sa mga bago.","translation":"**Pre-owned** cars are cheaper compared to new ones."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang larawan na kinuha mula sa kung ano ang kasalukuyang nakikita sa screen ng isang kompyuter, telepono, o iba pang elektronikong aparato.
original_explanation: The official resibo (receipt) of the digital world. The ultimate weapon in any online argument. "Delete mo lang, may screenshot ako." Used to capture tea, gossip, or proof that your friend saw your message at 3:17 PM and still hasn't replied.
usage_notes: Often used as a verb as well, 'i-screenshot mo' (take a screenshot of it).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpadala siya ng **screenshot** ng kanilang pag-uusap bilang ebidensya.","translation":"She sent a **screenshot** of their conversation as proof."},{"sentence":"Pakikuha ng **screenshot** 'yung error message para makita ko.","translation":"Please take a **screenshot** of the error message so I can see it."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpunta o pagdalaw sa isang tao o lugar.
original_explanation: The verb form of "bisita." This is the action you do when you miss your lola, need to borrow money from a friend, or want to check if the chismis about your kapitbahay is true. It's the "pasyal" with a specific destination and person in mind. "Tara, bisitahin natin si Tita, baka may pasalubong."
usage_notes: This is an object-focused verb. The subject-focused counterpart is "bumisita".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **bisitahin** ang iyong lola sa probinsya.","translation":"Don't forget **to visit** your grandmother in the province."},{"sentence":"Plano naming **bisitahin** ang National Museum sa susunod na linggo.","translation":"We plan **to visit** the National Museum next week."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pag-iwan o pagkamatayan ng isang mahal sa buhay; ang maranasan ang pagpanaw ng isang tao.
original_explanation: This is that heavy, empty feeling when someone important in your life passes away. It's the 'iniwan na ako' but on a whole different, permanent level. The ultimate ghosting, but make it existentially devastating.
usage_notes: Often used in a passive voice, as in 'panawan ng asawa' (to be left by a deceased spouse). It's a very formal and literary word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Labis ang kaniyang lumbay mula nang siya ay **panawan** ng kaniyang kabiyak.","translation":"His sorrow has been immense since he was **bereft by the death** of his spouse."},{"sentence":"Ayaw kong **panawan** ng pag-asa sa gitna ng mga pagsubok.","translation":"I don't want **to be left by** hope in the midst of trials."}]

translation: to torpedo; to hit with a torpedo
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapatama o pag-atake gamit ang isang torpido.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'torpido'. Literally, to sink something with a torpedo. Figuratively, it means to completely destroy or ruin something, like an argument or a plan. 'Torpiduhin mo ang argumento niya!' (Destroy his argument!).
usage_notes: Can be used literally for naval warfare or figuratively for destroying a plan, argument, or reputation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Planong **torpiduhin** ng mga kaaway ang kanilang barkong pandigma.","translation":"The enemies plan to **torpedo** their warship."},{"sentence":"Sinubukang **torpiduhin** ng oposisyon ang bagong panukalang batas.","translation":"The opposition tried to **destroy** the new bill."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, karaniwang lalaki, na propesyonal na sumasayaw, lalo na sa ballet o ibang pormal na sayaw.
original_explanation: This is the male counterpart of a 'bailarina'. Think of the guys in tights doing those incredible leaps and turns in shows like The Nutcracker. It's a Spanish loanword, so it sounds a bit fancy, like something you'd see at the CCP (Cultural Center of the Philippines).
usage_notes: While it can mean any male dancer, it's strongly associated with ballet or formal dance. The more general term is 'mananayaw'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang maging isang sikat na **bailarin** sa Europa.","translation":"He dreams of becoming a famous **male dancer** in Europe."},{"sentence":"Ang galing ng mga **bailarin** sa pagtatanghal ng 'Swan Lake'.","translation":"The male **dancers** in the 'Swan Lake' performance were amazing."}]

meaning_filipino: Biglaan at mabilis na pag-atake, pagtakbo, o paggalaw patungo sa isang direksyon.
etymology: From Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *səbad, meaning a sudden rush or attack.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung bigla kang tatakbo papunta sa pinto ng bus para makakuha ng upuan, o 'yung pag-atake ng aso sa nahulog na chichirya. It's a sudden, forceful burst of movement. Think of it as the 'sugod' but with more speed and less planning.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a sudden attack or a quick, forceful movement.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumibad** ang magnanakaw nang makita ang pulis.","translation":"The thief **dashed** away upon seeing the police."},{"sentence":"Ang aso ay **sumibad** sa pusa sa bakuran.","translation":"The dog **rushed** at the cat in the yard."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mas bata sa dalawang taong may parehong pangalan, karaniwan ay anak na isinunod sa pangalan ng ama. Ginagamit din upang tukuyin ang isang posisyong mas mababa sa ranggo.
original_explanation: The Filipinized spelling of 'Junior' or 'Jr.' It's what you call the son who's basically a carbon copy of his dad's name. In the office, it's you, the new hire. You're the 'junior' developer, 'junior' accountant, 'junior' everything. It means you get the coffee. Kidding... mostly.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pangngalan ('Siya ay isang diyunyor.') o pang-uri ('Siya ang diyunyor na senador.').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinangalan niya ang kanyang anak sa kanya, kaya ito ay isang **diyunyor**.","translation":"He named his son after himself, so he is a **junior**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsalo o pagtanggap sa isang bagay na inihagis, ibinato, o nahuhulog mula sa itaas.
original_explanation: When someone throws you the keys, your phone, or their trust issues. Your job is to sambutin it. It's like 'salo' but feels a bit more... formal? Or maybe just more dramatic. "Bes, andyan na 'yung responsibilities, **sambutin** mo!"
usage_notes: Synonymous with "saluhin." The "-in" suffix marks it as an object-focused verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**sambot** naman ng unan na ihahagis ko.","translation":"Please **catch** the pillow I'm going to throw."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi na nahiwalay mula sa isang kabuuan; isang piraso.
original_explanation: That shorter piece of the rope after you've cut it. The part of the cake that's been sliced off. It's the result of the action 'putulin'. Think of it as the 'offcut.'
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa resultang piraso matapos may maputol na isang bagay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ibigay mo sa akin ang isang **putol** ng kawayan.","translation":"Give me one **piece** of the bamboo."},{"sentence":"Nakatanggap siya ng dalawang **putol** ng tela.","translation":"She received two **cuts** of fabric."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtanggi o hindi pag-amin sa isang bagay, pahayag, o responsibilidad.
original_explanation: This is the official 'It wasn't me!' or 'I didn't say that!' move. It's what politicians do when a scandal breaks, or what you do when your friend asks if you ate the last piece of leche flan. It's the formal act of distancing yourself from something. The legal version is a 'disclaimer.'
usage_notes: 'Pagtatatuwa' is more formal than a simple 'pagtanggi' (denial/refusal). It implies disowning a statement or connection.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagtatatuwa** sa mga paratang ay hindi kapani-paniwala.","translation":"His **denial** of the accusations was not believable."},{"sentence":"Naglabas ang kumpanya ng isang **pagtatatuwa** hinggil sa mga maling balita.","translation":"The company issued a **disclaimer** regarding the fake news."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manipis na tubo na karaniwang gawa sa plastik, papel, o metal, na ginagamit sa paghigop ng inumin mula sa isang lalagyan.
original_explanation: The official tool for sipsip-ing your milk tea with extra pearls. Once a plastic villain, now it has paper, metal, and bamboo versions for the eco-conscious. It's how you get to the good stuff at the bottom of the glass without committing.
usage_notes: The English word 'straw' is often used directly. 'Istraw' is the common Tagalized spelling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pahingi naman ng **istraw** para sa softdrinks ko.","translation":"Can I have a **straw** for my softdrinks?"},{"sentence":"Maraming coffee shop ngayon ang gumagamit ng papel na **istraw**.","translation":"Many coffee shops now use paper **straws**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maasim na likido na resulta ng permentasyon ng ethanol, karaniwang ginagamit bilang pampalasa o preserbatibo sa pagluluto. Sa Pilipinas, ang suka na gawa sa niyog, tubo, o nipa ay pangkaraniwan.
original_explanation: The English word for 'suka'. You don't really say 'vinegar' unless you're reading a recipe from a foreign cookbook or trying to sound fancy when asking for sawsawan. 'Pahingi ng soy sauce and vinegar' sounds like you're in a high-end restaurant, while 'Pahingi ng toyo't suka' is for the real, everyday Pinoy kainan.
usage_notes: The native word 'suka' is far more common. 'Vinegar' is used in specific contexts like branding (e.g., 'apple cider vinegar') or when speaking in English/Taglish.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap ang adobo kung may tamang balanse ng soy sauce at **vinegar**.","translation":"Adobo is delicious when it has the right balance of soy sauce and **vinegar**."},{"sentence":"Gagamit ako ng apple cider **vinegar** para sa salad dressing.","translation":"I will use apple cider **vinegar** for the salad dressing."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang batas, regulasyon, o kautusan na ipinatutupad ng isang lokal na pamahalaan. Ang mas laganap na baybay ay "ordinansa".
original_explanation: Parang local version ng batas. Kung sa national level may Republic Act, sa city or municipality level, may **ordenansyon**. Ito 'yung nagsasabi na bawal magtapon ng basura kung saan-saan o 'yung number coding sa mga sasakyan. Think of it as the 'house rules' of a city.
usage_notes: Madalas na ipinagkakamali sa "ordinasyon" na tumutukoy sa seremonyang panrelihiyon. Ang "ordinansa" ay ang mas karaniwang baybay at anyo na ginagamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasa ang konseho ng bagong **ordenansyon** laban sa paggamit ng plastik.","translation":"The council passed a new **ordinance** against the use of plastic."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang samahan o kapatiran ng mga tao, lalo na sa konteksto ng relihiyon o pagka-kabalyero, na namumuhay sa ilalim ng isang partikular na hanay ng mga alituntunin.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'orden', na tumutukoy sa isang relihiyoso o militar na kapatiran.
original_explanation: Think of this as an exclusive club with very specific rules, usually involving religion or chivalry. The Franciscans, Dominicans, and Jesuits are all examples of a religious 'Orden'. It’s like a barkada, but with vows and a formal hierarchy. Not to be confused with the 'orden' you give to the waiter.
usage_notes: Usually capitalized when referring to a specific Order (e.g., Orden ng mga Agustino).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga paring Dominikano ay kabilang sa **Orden** ng mga Manggagaral.","translation":"The Dominican priests belong to the **Order** of Preachers."},{"sentence":"Sumapi siya sa isang **orden** ng mga madre sa Europa.","translation":"She joined a religious **order** of nuns in Europe."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kalagayan ng pagiging mahigpit na nakasara o nakatikom, karaniwan para sa kamao o bibig.
original_explanation: How your fist looks when you're trying to control your anger at a slow-walking person in the mall. Or how your lips get when your tita asks, 'Kailan ka mag-aasawa?' for the fifth time. It's the physical manifestation of 'pigil na pigil.'
usage_notes: Used specifically for body parts like hands (fist) or mouth (lips).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakaikom** ang kanyang kamao sa tindi ng galit.","translation":"His fist was **clenched** in intense anger."},{"sentence":"Nanatiling **nakaikom** ang kanyang mga labi at hindi nagsalita.","translation":"Her lips remained **pursed** and she did not speak."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng sakit o kirot na parang nasusunog o tinutusok ng maliliit na karayom, karaniwang nararamdaman sa sugat na nalagyan ng alkohol o sa mata na napuwing.
original_explanation: That feeling when you put alcohol on a fresh papercut. Ouch! Or when you're chopping sili and you accidentally rub your eye. That's mahapdi. It's the universe telling you, 'You messed up.'
usage_notes: Describes a specific type of sharp, stinging pain, different from a dull ache (kirot) or throbbing pain (kumikirot).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Mahapdi** ang sugat ko nang lagyan ng betadine.","translation":"My wound was **stinging** when I applied betadine."},{"sentence":"Naiiyak siya dahil **mahapdi** sa mata ang usok.","translation":"She was tearing up because the smoke was **stinging** her eyes."}]

translation: to shoulder; to take upon oneself (a responsibility)
meaning_filipino: Angkinin o akuin ang isang mabigat na tungkulin, gawain, o responsibilidad.
etymology: From `i-` (causative/benefactive prefix) + `balikat` (shoulder). Literally "to put on the shoulder".
original_explanation: This is what you do when your boss suddenly dumps a new project on you at 5 PM on a Friday. You just have to "shoulder" the responsibility. It's the adulting version of carrying your team in Mobile Legends. You take the burden, for better or for worse. 'Sige, ako na ang bahala,' ang sigaw ng pusong inibalikat ang lahat.
usage_notes: Often used figuratively to mean taking on a heavy responsibility, not just literally carrying something on one's shoulders.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ibalikat** mo ang responsibilidad bilang panganay na anak.","translation":"**Shoulder** the responsibility of being the eldest child."},{"sentence":"Inako at **inibalikat** ng pangulo ang lahat ng kritisismo.","translation":"The president took on and **shouldered** all the criticism."}]

translation: to reform; to turn over a new leaf
meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng kilos upang lubusang baguhin ang sarili o ang pamumuhay tungo sa mas mabuting kalagayan.
