meaning_filipino: Pagbabalumbon ng isang bagay, tulad ng papel o banig, upang maging bilog at pahaba. Maaari ring tumukoy sa paglunok ng isang bagay nang buo at mabilisan.
original_explanation: Two meanings here. First, it's what you do to your yoga mat or a poster after use. You roll it up nice and tight. Second, it's how a snake eats its prey—swallowing it whole. Parang 'yung paglunok mo sa pride mo para mag-sorry, ganun.
usage_notes: Can mean "to roll up" (like a mat or paper) or "to swallow whole" (like a pill or food). Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **ilulon** mo ang banig pagkatapos gamitin.","translation":"Please, **roll up** the mat after using it."},{"sentence":"Parang ahas na **inilulon** ang biktima nito.","translation":"Like a snake that **swallowed** its victim **whole**."}]

meaning_filipino: Magbibigay ng kaukulang halaga bilang kabayaran para sa isang produkto, serbisyo, o utang.
original_explanation: This is the future tense of every adult's life. 'Sino'ng **magbabayad**?' is the most stressful question after a group dinner. It's what you promise your suking tindera when you're short on cash: 'Bukas na po ako **magbabayad**.' The ultimate test of friendship and character.
usage_notes: Future tense of the verb "magbayad".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **magbabayad** ng ating mga kinain?","translation":"Who **will pay** for the food we ate?"},{"sentence":"**Magbabayad** ako ng kuryente bukas ng umaga.","translation":"I **will pay** the electricity bill tomorrow morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang marahas na pangyayari kung saan maraming tao ang nasusugatan o namamatay, na nagreresulta sa pag-agos ng dugo.
original_explanation: The most metal phrase in Tagalog. It's used for anything from historical battles to intense action movies. When you hear '*pagdanak ng dugo*', you know things just got serious. It's the difference between a simple 'away' (fight) and an all-out war.
usage_notes: A fixed phrase used to describe violence, war, or intense conflict resulting in death or injury.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais ng lahat na matigil na ang **pagdanak ng dugo** sa kanilang bayan.","translation":"Everyone wants the **bloodshed** in their town to stop."},{"sentence":"Ang rebolusyon ay humantong sa malawakang **pagdanak ng dugo**.","translation":"The revolution led to widespread **bloodshed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tunog na nalilikha ng mabilis at paulit-ulit na paggalaw, tulad ng pagkampay ng pakpak ng ibon, pagwagayway ng bandila, o pagaspas ng dahon sa hangin.
original_explanation: The sound effect for a bird taking flight, a flag waving dramatically in the wind, or the pages of a book being flipped through quickly. It's the 'whoosh-whoosh' sound of something thin and flat cutting through the air. Also, the sound of your palengke suki's pamaypay on a hot day.
usage_notes: An onomatopoeic word, the sound itself is described by the word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **pagaspas** ng mga pakpak ng paniki sa gabi.","translation":"I heard the **flapping sound** of the bat's wings at night."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdadala o paglilipat ng isang bagay o tao mula sa isang lugar patungo sa iba.
original_explanation: What your mom tells you to do with the baon, the payong, and the jacket "just in case." Also, what you do with all the 'hugot' and emotional baggage from your ex. You just **dalhin** it everywhere.
usage_notes: This is the object-focus form of the root "dala." "Magdala" is the actor-focus form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **dalhin** mo itong mga aklat sa silid-aklatan.","translation":"Please, **bring** these books to the library."},{"sentence":"Saan mo **dadalhin** ang mga bisita nating galing ibang bansa?","translation":"Where will you **take** our guests from overseas?"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na kinayod o pinino gamit ang isang kudkuran.
original_explanation: The state of cheese before it goes on your spaghetti, or a coconut before it becomes gata. Also, a good description for your knees after tripping on an unpaved road. "Yung tuhod ko, gadgad sa semento!"
usage_notes: Can be a noun (the act of grating, though less common) or an adjective (the state of being grated). The verb form is 'gadgarin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas masarap ang spaghetti kung maraming **gadgad** na keso sa ibabaw.","translation":"Spaghetti is more delicious with a lot of **grated** cheese on top."},{"sentence":"Naging **gadgad** ang gulong dahil sa biglaang pagpreno.","translation":"The tire became **shredded** due to the sudden braking."}]

meaning_filipino: Ituring na iba o hindi kabilang; ihiwalay o itakwil mula sa isang grupo.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of being left out. When your officemates go for a milk tea run and 'forget' to ask you, 'pinupuwera' ka nila. It's the high school drama of being intentionally excluded from the cool kids' table. The act of making someone feel 'fuera' or outside.
usage_notes: Carries a negative connotation of deliberate exclusion or making someone an outcast.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag nating **puwerahin** ang mga bagong kasamahan.","translation":"Let's not **exclude** the new colleagues."},{"sentence":"Masakit maramdaman na **pinuwera** ka ng sarili mong mga kaibigan.","translation":"It hurts to feel that you were **ostracized** by your own friends."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasama-sama ng mga kasangkapan, makina, pamamaraan, at proseso na ginagamit upang malutas ang mga suliranin, mapabuti ang mga gawain, o makamit ang mga layunin, lalo na sa larangan ng agham at industriya.
original_explanation: The reason you can order food without talking to anyone, watch your favorite series anytime, and argue with strangers on the internet. It's the magic (and sometimes the curse) that runs our modern lives, from your smartphone to the LRT.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang naitulong ng makabagong **teknolohiya** sa ating pang-araw-araw na buhay.","translation":"Modern **technology** has greatly helped our daily lives."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-aaral ng **teknolohiya** ay mahalaga para sa kinabukasan.","translation":"The study of **technology** is important for the future."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng isang bagay na nakikita ng mata, na resulta ng paraan ng pagpapakita o pagpapadala nito ng liwanag, gaya ng pula, bughaw, o dilaw.
original_explanation: Kulay is the spice of life, the reason your IG feed pops, and the basis for deciding which milk tea to get. It's what separates a boring day from a vibrant one. Sometimes, it's also used to describe someone's "true colors" (tunay na kulay) when the drama unfolds. "Anong paborito mong kulay?" is the ultimate icebreaker.
usage_notes: Can be used metaphorically to mean 'nature' or 'character' (e.g., 'tunay na kulay').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang paborito mong **kulay**?","translation":"What is your favorite **color**?"},{"sentence":"Nagbibigay-buhay sa silid ang matingkad na **kulay** ng mga pader.","translation":"The bright **color** of the walls brings the room to life."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagtataksil o pagiging hindi tapat sa isang tao, grupo, o prinsipyo na pinagkakatiwalaan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na "traidor" (traydor) na nangangahulugang taksil, na nilagyan ng panlaping Tagalog na "-in".
original_explanation: The ultimate "Sana all" gone wrong. When your best friend starts dating your ex, or when your groupmate removes your name from the project you stayed up all night for. It's the act of being a "Marites" with confidential info or the reason for most hugot songs. To be "traidurin" is to be backstabbed, Judas-style.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang pandiwa na nangangailangan ng tuwirang layon (ang taong tinraidor). Halimbawa: "Huwag mo akong traidurin." (Don't betray me.)
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya akalain na kaya siyang **traidurin** ng kanyang pinakamatalik na kaibigan.","translation":"He/She never thought that his/her best friend was capable of **betraying** him/her."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malakas na paglabas ng hangin, usok, likido, o anumang bagay mula sa bibig.
original_explanation: What a dragon does with fire, what a vaper does with smoke, and what your tito does after drinking a very cold Coke on a hot day ('Aaah!'). It can also mean to brag or spew nonsense. 'Pura buga ka lang ng salita, wala namang gawa.'
usage_notes: Can be used for literal exhalation/spraying or figuratively for speaking boastfully.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **bumuga** ng usok sa mukha ko.","translation":"Don't **spew** smoke in my face."},{"sentence":"Ang bulkan ay nagsimulang **bumuga** ng abo.","translation":"The volcano started to **spew** ash."}]

translation: to be able to feed; to cause someone to eat
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang magbigay ng pagkain sa isa o higit pang tao; maging sanhi ng pagkain ng iba.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate Filipino parent verb. "Kailangan kong magtrabaho para mapakain ang pamilya ko." It's about providing, hustling so everyone gets to eat. It can also mean you managed to make a picky eater *actually* eat something. "Success! Napakain ko ng gulay ang anak ko!"
usage_notes: The 'mapa-' prefix here implies ability or success in making someone eat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sahod niya ay sapat lang para **mapakain** ang kanyang mga anak.","translation":"His salary is just enough **to be able to feed** his children."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **mapakain** ng ampalaya ang bata.","translation":"It's difficult **to make a child eat** bitter gourd."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na pinapagana, gumagamit, o may kaugnayan sa elektrisidad.
original_explanation: This is the adjective form you barely hear anymore, like the 'donna' to the 'don' of electricity words. You might find it in an old physics book: 'silya elektrika' (electric chair) or 'gitarang elektrika' (electric guitar). Nowadays, we just say 'electric' chair or 'electric' guitar.
usage_notes: This is a dated, formal adjective. In modern Tagalog, it is much more common to use the English word "electric" or phrases like "de-kuryente" (powered by electricity).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang gitarang **elektrika** ay naging popular noong dekada sisenta.","translation":"The **electric** guitar became popular in the sixties."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aralan nila ang daloy ng kuryenteng **elektrika**.","translation":"They studied the flow of **electric** current."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang unlapi na ikinakabit sa isang salita upang ipahiwatig ang negasyon o ang kawalan ng katangian ng salitang-ugat.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'no, u' of the Filipino language. It's the prefix you use to turn something positive into its opposite. Mabait (kind)? Di-mabait (unkind). Maintindihan (understandable)? Di-maintindihan (incomprehensible). It's the simple, powerful tool for when you're just not feeling it.
usage_notes: Ito ay pagpapaikli ng 'hindi'. Kapag ang salitang-ugat ay nagsisimula sa patinig, 'di-' ang karaniwang ginagamit. Kapag sa katinig, mas karaniwan ang 'hindi' ngunit ginagamit din ang 'di-'. Isinusulat ito na may gitling kapag ginagamit bilang unlapi.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sagot niya ay **di-**tiyak kaya naguguluhan ako.","translation":"His answer is **un**certain so I'm confused."},{"sentence":"Ito ay isang pangyayaring **di-**malilimutan.","translation":"This is an **un**forgettable event."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pagiging nasa labas. Sa isang pormal o makalumang konteksto, ito ay nangangahulugang isinilang o inianak.
original_explanation: The old-school, dramatic way of saying something is "out." You wouldn't say your friend is "luwal" of the closet, but you might read in a historical text that a hero was "luwal sa kahirapan" (born into poverty). It’s a bit extra, like using "henceforth" in a text message. Its most common modern use is in the word "pagluwal" (childbirth).
usage_notes: A more formal and somewhat archaic term. Most commonly encountered in the compound form "pagluwal" (birth) or the verb form "iniluwal" (was born).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay **luwal** sa isang pamilya ng mga magsasaka.","translation":"He was **born** into a family of farmers."}]

translation: to initial; to put one's initials on
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay ng mga unang titik ng pangalan sa isang dokumento o bagay bilang tanda ng pagpapatunay o pag-aari.
original_explanation: That thing your boss asks you to do on every single page of a 50-page contract to prove you've read it. It's the verb form of putting your initials on something. "Paki-inisyalan mo na lang sa bawat pahina, thank you." - every BPO team lead, probably.
usage_notes: Commonly used in office or legal settings. The command form is 'inisyalan'. Past tense is 'inisyalanan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **inisyalan** ang bawat pahina ng kontrata.","translation":"You need **to initial** every page of the contract."},{"sentence":"**Inisyalan** mo ang dokumento bilang patunay na nabasa mo ito.","translation":"**Initial** the document as proof that you have read it."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa sukdulan o pinakamatinding antas ng kasamaan o pagiging seryoso.
etymology: Full reduplication of the adjective `malala` to create an intensified, superlative-like meaning.
original_explanation: This is 'malala' on steroids. This is when the WiFi isn't just slow, it's been down for 3 days and the telco's support line is a robot. This is when your 'situationship' isn't just complicated, it's malalang-malala because you found out you're one of three. It's the final boss level of 'grabe.'
usage_notes: An intensified form of 'malala' used for strong emphasis. It signifies that a situation or condition has reached a critical, extreme, or almost hopeless state.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Malalang-malala** na ang korapsyon sa ahensyang iyon.","translation":"The corruption in that agency is **very severe**."},{"sentence":"Dinala siya sa ospital dahil **malalang-malala** na ang kanyang kondisyon.","translation":"He was brought to the hospital because his condition was **extremely serious**."}]

translation: recovery; act of getting back or reclaiming
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos o proseso ng muling pagkuha sa isang bagay na nawala o naibigay; ang pagpapanumbalik ng lakas o kalusugan.
original_explanation: That 'bawi' moment. You lost in Mobile Legends, but then you get a Savage in the next game—that's pagkabawi. You failed a quiz, but you aced the final exam. It's the comeback, the redemption arc, whether it's recovering your money, your health, or your dignidad after a 'marupok' moment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis ang kanyang **pagkabawi** mula sa malubhang sakit.","translation":"His **recovery** from the serious illness was fast."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkabawi** sa natalong puhunan ay ang kanyang pangunahing layunin.","translation":"The **reclamation** of the lost investment is his main goal."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa kabaligtarang ayos o paraan; ang ugnayan o epekto ay pareho sa kabilang direksyon.
etymology: From English "vice versa", which is from Latin "vice versā" (the position being turned).
original_explanation: The fancy way of saying "the other way around" or "ganun din pabalik." You use this when you're trying to sound smart in a meeting or a school report. "I respect my boss, and bise bersa." It saves you the effort of repeating the entire sentence in reverse. Efficiency is key!
usage_notes: A formal-sounding phrase often used in writing and formal speech. It is a direct phonetic borrowing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahal niya ako, at **bise bersa**.","translation":"He loves me, and **vice versa**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga empleyado ay dapat maging tapat sa kumpanya, at **bise bersa**.","translation":"The employees should be loyal to the company, and **vice versa**."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi sinasadyang sumigaw o makapagpalabas ng malakas na tinig dahil sa gulat, takot, sakit, o matinding tuwa.
etymology: ma- (unintentional action prefix) + pa- (causative prefix, here intensifying) + sigaw (shout)
original_explanation: This is your reaction when you see a cockroach fly. Or when you check your bank account after payday. Or when your K-pop bias winks at the camera. It’s that scream you can’t hold back. "Nung nakita ko yung presyo ng bilihin, napasigaw na lang ako sa palengke."
usage_notes: The 'mapa-' prefix highlights the involuntary nature of the shout.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Napasigaw** siya sa takot nang may biglang gumulat sa kanya.","translation":"She **shouted involuntarily** in fear when someone suddenly startled her."},{"sentence":"**Mapapasigaw** ka sa sarap ng bagong chicken-joy flavor!","translation":"You'll **involuntarily scream** with delight at the new chicken-joy flavor!"}]

translation: Negrito (member of a specific ethnolinguistic group)
meaning_filipino: Isang miyembro ng isa sa mga pangkat etniko sa Timog-silangang Asya, kabilang ang Pilipinas, na karaniwang may maitim na balat, kulot na buhok, at hindi gaanong katangkaran.
original_explanation: This refers to the indigenous peoples of the Philippines like the Aeta, Ati, and Batak. The name literally means "little black person" in Spanish, which is pretty on-the-nose and a bit cringe by today's standards. They are considered some of the earliest inhabitants of the archipelago. Think of them as the OG Pinoys, living here way before the Austronesian migrations.
usage_notes: While the term is the established anthropological name, it's a Spanish exonym (a name given by outsiders). It is often considered more respectful to refer to the specific group name if known (e.g., Aeta, Ati, Batak).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **Negrito** ay kilala sa kanilang malalim na kaalaman tungkol sa kagubatan.","translation":"The **Negrito** people are known for their deep knowledge of the forest."},{"sentence":"Isang mahalagang bahagi ng kasaysayan ng Pilipinas ang kultura ng mga pangkat **Negrito**.","translation":"The culture of the **Negrito** groups is an important part of Philippine history."}]

meaning_filipino: Panahon ng taon na may mababang temperatura at malamig na hangin.
original_explanation: The 'Ber' months in the Philippines. It's not really winter, more like 'aircon weather' everywhere. This is the season when you can finally wear that jacket you bought on sale and not look crazy. It's the official excuse to cuddle and drink hot chocolate.
usage_notes: While it translates to 'winter,' in the Philippine context, it refers to the cooler months (September to February), not a season with snow.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap matulog kapag **taglamig**.","translation":"It's nice to sleep during the **cold season**."},{"sentence":"Naglalabas na sila ng mga palamuting pamasko dahil **taglamig** na.","translation":"They are already putting out Christmas decorations because the **cold season** is here."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pansamantalang pagkawala ng pakiramdam o pagkakaroon ng parang mga tusok ng karayom sa isang bahagi ng katawan, lalo na sa mga kamay o paa, dahil sa matagal na pagkakadiin.
original_explanation: That 'pins and needles' feeling you get when you sit on your leg for too long while doomscrolling, or when your arm falls asleep after you used it as a pillow. Your limb is basically rebooting and sending you error messages.
usage_notes: The verb form 'nangingimay' (is becoming numb) is very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman ko ang **ngamay** sa aking mga binti matapos umupo nang matagal sa sahig.","translation":"I felt the **numbness** in my legs after sitting on the floor for a long time."},{"sentence":"Nangingimay ang kamay ko, hindi ko mai-type nang maayos ang password!","translation":"My hand is **numb**, I can't type the password correctly!"}]

translation: to be the cause of shame/embarrassment
meaning_filipino: Maging dahilan ng pagdama ng hiya o kahihiyan.
original_explanation: That moment your mom shows your baby pictures to your new partner. When you wave back at someone who wasn't waving at you. It's the reason for your 'cringe attack' at 2 AM when you remember something dumb you did ten years ago.
usage_notes: Used to identify the source of one's embarrassment or shame.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ikahiya** ang iyong pinanggalingan.","translation":"Don't **be ashamed** of where you came from. (Literally: Don't let your origins be the cause of your shame.)"},{"sentence":"**Ikinahiya** niya ang suot niyang butas na medyas.","translation":"The hole in his sock **was the cause of his embarrassment**."}]

translation: an attack; the act of attacking
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pananalakay, paninira, o pagpuna nang may masamang layunin laban sa isang tao, bagay, o ideya.
etymology: From Spanish "ataque" (attack). The prefix `pag-` nominalizes the root word, turning it into the act or process of doing it.
original_explanation: This isn't just a physical fight. It can be your tita's "pag-atake" on your love life during a family reunion ("Wala ka pa ring jowa?!"). It's also that sudden urge to raid the fridge at midnight. Or, in gaming, it's literally the "pag-atake" on the enemy's base.
usage_notes: Can be physical, verbal, or even digital (e.g., cyber-attack).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang biglaang **pag-atake** sa puso ay isang seryosong kondisyong medikal.","translation":"A sudden heart **attack** is a serious medical condition."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko nagustuhan ang kanyang **pag-atake** sa aking pagkatao.","translation":"I did not like his **attack** on my character."}]

translation: to hand over; to pass; to reach for
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbibigay ng isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng kamay; ang pag-abot sa isang bagay na may kalayuan.
original_explanation: The universal Filipino gesture for "paki-abot." You say "**mag-abot** ka ng bayad" to the jeepney driver, and a chain of helpful hands passes your fare to the front. It's a beautiful display of bayanihan in public transport. It's also what you do when you're too lazy to stand up and ask someone to pass the remote control.
usage_notes: Can mean both "to hand over" and "to reach for" depending on context. The actor-focus form `mag-abot` emphasizes the giving/handing over.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **mag-abot** ka naman ng kanin.","translation":"Please, can you **pass** the rice."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **mag-abot** sa prutas na nasa tuktok ng puno.","translation":"He tried to **reach for** the fruit at the top of the tree."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang estado ng pagiging mahigpit, banat, o matindi. Tumutukoy din sa sidhi ng damdamin o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're watching the last 2 minutes of a tied basketball game, or when you're waiting for your crush to reply to your 'hi'. That's igting. It's the emotional or physical tension na parang anytime, may puputok.
usage_notes: Often used to describe dramatic tension in stories, movies, or relationships.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ramdam ang **igting** sa pagitan ng dalawang magkatunggali.","translation":"The **tension** between the two rivals can be felt."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa **igting** ng sitwasyon, walang nangahas na magsalita.","translation":"Because of the **intensity** of the situation, no one dared to speak."}]

translation: to be able to untie; to come loose
meaning_filipino: Magawang matanggal ang pagkakatali o pagkakabuhol ng isang bagay; maging maluwag.
original_explanation: Like when your shoelaces decide to betray you in the middle of a crowded MRT station. Or when you finally *makalas* from a toxic relationship. Either way, something that was tied up is now free. Freedom!
usage_notes: Can refer to literal knots or figurative bonds.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **makalas** ang buhol sa sinulid na ito.","translation":"Help me **untie** the knot in this thread."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **makalas** sa masamang bisyo.","translation":"It's hard to **break free** from a bad habit."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtamo ng sira, pinsala, o kapahamakan, lalo na dahil sa isang sakuna o masamang pangyayari.
original_explanation: The aftermath of a super typhoon, a bad breakup, or when your laptop crashes the night before a deadline. It means something has been wrecked, ruined, or seriously messed up. It's the 'after' picture you don't want to see.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of disasters, accidents, or significant negative events. Can function as a verb (was damaged) or an adjective (damaged).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming bahay ang **napinsala** ng malakas na bagyo.","translation":"Many houses were **damaged** by the strong typhoon."},{"sentence":"**Napinsala** ang kanyang reputasyon dahil sa maling akusasyon.","translation":"His reputation was **harmed** due to the false accusation."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lalaking uri ng usa, karaniwang mas malaki at may mga sungay na sanga-sanga.
original_explanation: The king of the forest, the one with the impressive antlers (sungay). This is the animal kingdom's version of the gym bro who's proud of his 'gains.' In stories, he's often the majestic, powerful leader of the herd.
usage_notes: 'Barako' is often used to describe male animals (e.g., kambing na barako) or a macho man.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **usang barako** ay may malalaking sungay na ginagamit nito sa pakikipag-away.","translation":"The **stag** has large antlers that it uses for fighting."},{"sentence":"Tila isang **usang barako** ang dating niya, matipuno at mayabang.","translation":"He had the air of a **stag**, sturdy and proud."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao, bagay, o sitwasyon na labis na nakakainis, nakakagambala, o nagdudulot ng matinding perwisyo.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng "parang" (like/as if) at "peste" (pest, mula sa Espanyol na 'peste').
original_explanation: The perfect description for slow internet during an online meeting, a mosquito in your room at 3 AM, or that one officemate who keeps asking 'Tapos ka na?'. It's anything that's super annoying and you wish would just disappear.
usage_notes: Isang matinding ekspresyon ng pagka-inis o pagka-irita.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang trapik sa EDSA ay **parang peste** tuwing Biyernes.","translation":"The traffic on EDSA is **like a pest** (a huge nuisance) every Friday."},{"sentence":"Umalis ka na nga, **parang peste** ka sa buhay ko!","translation":"Just leave, you're **like a pest** in my life!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paraan ng pagtayo o ang ayos ng katawan habang nakatayo; maaari ring tumukoy sa paninindigan sa isang prinsipyo o isyu.
original_explanation: It's more than just standing up straight. It's your vibe, your presence, the way you carry yourself. "May dating ang **tindig** niya." It can also mean your "stand" on an issue, your principles. In 2026, your **tindig** on a political issue is as important as your profile picture.
usage_notes: Can also be a verb root. `Tumindig` (to stand up), `Paninindigan` (principle, conviction).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahanga-hanga ang kanyang matatag na **tindig** sa gitna ng mga pagsubok.","translation":"Her firm **stance** in the midst of challenges is admirable."},{"sentence":"Ayusin mo ang iyong **tindig** para hindi ka magmukhang kuba.","translation":"Fix your **posture** so you don't look hunched."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aalay o pagbibigay ng isang bagay na mahalaga para sa isang mas mataas na layunin o para sa kapakanan ng iba.
original_explanation: Ito yung ginagawa ng mga OFW na tinitiis ang homesickness para sa pamilya. Ito rin yung paggising mo ng 4 AM para mag-commute papasok sa trabaho. Or yung pag-give up mo sa milk tea para makapag-ipon. The ultimate "tiis-ganda" or "tiis-pogi" para sa future.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang **sakripisyo** ng mga magulang para sa kanilang mga anak.","translation":"Parents make great **sacrifices** for their children."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-abot sa pangarap ay nangangailangan ng tiyaga at **sakripisyo**.","translation":"Reaching a dream requires perseverance and **sacrifice**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa sa isang bagay na maging malambot, gaya ng pagkain sa pamamagitan ng pagpapakulo; o ang pagpapabago sa matigas na damdamin ng isang tao.
original_explanation: Primarily a cooking term, like when you boil pork for sinigang until it's tender. 'Kailangan mong magpalambot ng karne.' But it's also used for people! When someone is angry or has a 'pusong bato' (heart of stone), you try to 'soften' them up with kind words, a thoughtful gift, or a really good apology.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical texture (especially food) or an emotional state (people's hearts or feelings).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng pressure cooker para **magpalambot** ng baka.","translation":"She used a pressure cooker to **tenderize** the beef."},{"sentence":"Subukan mong **magpalambot** ng puso niya sa pamamagitan ng sulat.","translation":"Try to **soften** his heart with a letter."}]

meaning_filipino: (Balbal) Isang alternatibong baybay para sa "kanal humor"; isang uri ng katatawanan na magaspang, bastos, o nakasentro sa mga paksang itinuturing na mababang-uri.
etymology: A compound word from Tagalog 'kanal' and English 'humor'.
original_explanation: Basically 'kanal humor' but you typed it faster without the space, probably because you were laughing too hard at a meme about a monobloc chair. It's the hashtag you use when you know the content is pure, unadulterated, 24-karat kanal.
usage_notes: Primarily functions as a hashtag (#kanalhumor) on social media to categorize content.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **kanalhumor** ang feed ko ngayon.","translation":"My feed is full of **gutter humor** right now."}]

translation: to hurt, to ache, to become painful
meaning_filipino: Makaramdam ng sakit o kirot sa isang bahagi ng katawan.
original_explanation: Ito yung feeling after a whole day of sitting in front of your laptop—sumakit ang likod mo. O kaya yung puso mo noong nalaman mong 'friends lang pala kayo'. It's the physical or emotional pain that suddenly hits you. From a simple headache to a major heartache.
usage_notes: The -um- infix with the root 'sakit' (pain/illness) creates the past tense verb 'became painful' or 'started to hurt'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Biglang **sumakit** ang ulo ko kaninang hapon.","translation":"My head suddenly **started to hurt** this afternoon."},{"sentence":"**Sumakit** ang dibdib niya nang makita niyang may kasamang iba ang kanyang mahal.","translation":"His chest **ached** when he saw his beloved with someone else."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal at medyo bastos na tumutukoy sa isang taong matanda na sa edad.
original_explanation: A not-so-nice slang term for an old person. It's what your rebellious teenage self might have muttered about your parents or any authority figure who just 'doesn't get it.' 'Ano ba 'yan, ang gurang na ng sound trip mo!' Use with caution, it can be offensive.
usage_notes: Often considered derogatory or disrespectful. 'Matanda' is the neutral and polite term. Can also be used as a noun to refer to an old person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinawag niyang **gurang** ang kanyang lolo kaya napagalitan siya.","translation":"He called his grandfather **old** (derogatory) so he got scolded."},{"sentence":"Para sa mga **gurang** na raw ang musikang iyan.","translation":"That music is supposedly for **old folks** already."}]

translation: to make someone research; to have something researched
meaning_filipino: Atasan o utusan ang isang tao na magsagawa ng isang masusing pag-aaral o pagsisiyasat tungkol sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is what your thesis adviser does to you. They don't do the research themselves; they make *you* do it. 'Okay, class, for your assignment, `pagsaliksikin` ninyo ang history of Filipino memes.' It's the act of delegating the 3 AM, 50-tab-browser-session struggle to someone else.
usage_notes: A causative verb. The subject of the verb is the one ordering or causing the research to be done. Not to be confused with 'saliksikin' (to research something). The `pag-` prefix here makes it causative.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-utos ng propesor na **pagsaliksikin** ang mga estudyante tungkol sa mga bayani ng Pilipinas.","translation":"The professor ordered to **have the students research** about the heroes of the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **pagsaliksikin** ng buhay niya; stalker ka ba?","translation":"Don't **make me research** his life; are you a stalker?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lupon o pangkat ng mga tao na itinalaga o inihalal upang magsagawa ng isang partikular na tungkulin o pag-aralan ang isang isyu.
original_explanation: The official term for a "barkada project" in the corporate or government world. It's a group of people formed to do something specific, like plan the Christmas party (the most important committee) or investigate a problem. Basically, a group that proves that multiple heads are... more complicated than one.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ako ang napiling mamuno sa **komite** para sa pagpaplano ng anibersaryo ng kumpanya.","translation":"I was chosen to lead the **committee** for planning the company's anniversary."},{"sentence":"Nagpulong ang **komite** upang talakayin ang mga bagong patakaran.","translation":"The **committee** met to discuss the new rules."}]

translation: to apply perfume; to have something scented
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng pabango sa sarili o sa iba; ang pagiging sanhi na magkaroon ng mabangong amoy ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: Two modes: 1) The verb form of "freshen up," usually before a date or an important meeting. "Wait lang, *magpapabango* lang ako." 2) The causative version, like asking the laundry shop to add extra fabric conditioner, para *magpabango* ng mga damit. It's the act of making things smell less like struggle and more like success.
usage_notes: Can be reflexive (applying to oneself) or causative (having something else scented).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bago umalis ng bahay, ugali niyang **magpabango**.","translation":"Before leaving the house, it's his habit to **apply perfume**."},{"sentence":"**Nagpabango** siya ng kotse sa carwash.","translation":"He **had his car scented** at the carwash."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang modernong katawagan na tumutukoy sa estetika o "aesthetic" ng kulturang Jejemon, na muling sumisikat bilang isang anyo ng moda o sining na may halong nostalgia at kabalintunaan.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng "jeje" at ng Ingles na hulapi na "-core," na ginagamit upang tukuyin ang isang kilusang estetiko.
original_explanation: It's what happens when Gen Z discovers their parents' Friendster accounts. It's taking the "jeje" aesthetic (the fashion, the typography) and ironically rebranding it as a cool, retro "core" like cottagecore or normcore. Think of it as a curated, high-fashion version of what we used to call "baduy."
usage_notes: A very recent slang term, popular among younger generations on social media like TikTok.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang outfit niya ay parang **jejecore**; may side-swept bangs at malaking cap.","translation":"Her outfit is very **jejecore**; she has side-swept bangs and a big cap."},{"sentence":"Nag-revive ang **jejecore** trend sa TikTok.","translation":"The **jejecore** trend was revived on TikTok."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal, partikular sa swardspeak, na katumbas ng 'ano'.
etymology: Mula sa 'ano' na nilagyan ng swardspeak/beki suffix na '-ech'.
original_explanation: The beki (gay lingo) version of 'ano?' (what?). It adds a little bit of flair and fabulousness to your confusion. Instead of a boring 'Ano?', you get a sassy '**Anech**?!' It's the sound you make when you see your friend's questionable fashion choice or hear the latest chismis. Also used for 'whatever' or 'whatchamacallit'.
usage_notes: Mahigpit na impormal at bahagi ng isang tiyak na sociolect. Ang paggamit nito ay nagpapahiwatig na kasama ka sa biruan o bahagi ng kultura.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Anech** ang ganap mamaya, mga mars?","translation":"**What's** the plan for later, girls?"},{"sentence":"Hala, **anech** itey? Bakit may pa-flowers si Mayor?","translation":"Whoa, **what** is this? Why are there flowers from the Mayor?"}]

translation: to tear into pieces; to shred
meaning_filipino: Paggisi o pagwasak sa isang bagay nang paulit-ulit hanggang maging maliliit na piraso.
original_explanation: This isn't just a simple tear. This is a "I'm so done with this" level of destruction. It's what you do to the evidence, the photo of your ex, or the 15th draft of your thesis that your adviser rejected. It’s tearing, but with passion and a little bit of rage.
usage_notes: The repetition of "punit" indicates a more intense or thorough action of tearing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pagpunit-punitin** ang libro, mahalaga iyan.","translation":"Don't **tear the book into pieces**, it's important."},{"sentence":"Gusto kong **pagpunit-punitin** ang mga bayarin ko, pero kailangan ko pa rin silang bayaran.","translation":"I want to **shred** my bills, but I still have to pay them."}]

translation: to get dirty; to be soiled
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagiging marumi o ang aksidenteng paglalagay ng dumi sa isang bagay, lugar, o sa sarili.
original_explanation: When your white sneakers suddenly meet a puddle of mud during a rainy commute. It's also what happens to your reputation when chismis spreads. 'Huwag kang dumaan diyan, baka marumihan 'yang sapatos mo.'
usage_notes: Often used to describe something getting accidentally dirty. The actor-focus form is `dumihan` (to make something dirty).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingatan mong huwag **marumihan** ang bagong pintura ng pader.","translation":"Be careful not to **get** the newly painted wall **dirty**."},{"sentence":"Nangyari na ang kinatatakutan ko, **narumihan** ang puting damit ko ng kape.","translation":"What I feared happened, my white dress **was soiled** with coffee."}]

translation: to make permanent; to fix; to finalize
meaning_filipino: Gawing pirmi o hindi nagbabago; patatagin; gawing pinal.
original_explanation: Similar to "pirmihan," but often used with more abstract concepts like decisions or plans. Think of it as hitting the "save and lock" button on a decision. "Pirmihin mo na ang isip mo, aalis ba tayo o hindi?" means "Make up your mind for good, are we leaving or not?"
usage_notes: Focuses on the object being made permanent. Often interchangeable with 'pirmihan' but can feel more direct, especially for decisions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat mong **pirmihin** ang iyong sagot bago ipasa ang papel.","translation":"You should **finalize** your answer before submitting the paper."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang **pirmihin** ang kaniyang posisyon sa kumpanya.","translation":"He is trying to **solidify** his position in the company."}]

meaning_filipino: Manood o mag-broadcast ng video o audio content sa internet nang live o on-demand.
original_explanation: The 21st-century version of "manood ng TV." It's what you do when you want to watch a movie without leaving your bed, or when your favorite gamer goes live to shout at pixels. Whether you're on Netflix, YouTube, or Twitch, you're streaming. "Tara, **magsistream** tayo ng K-drama hanggang umaga!"
usage_notes: A very modern loanword. The future tense is 'mag-iistream'. This is a prime example of Taglish verb formation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **magsistream** ng mga laro sa Facebook.","translation":"He likes **to stream** games on Facebook."},{"sentence":"Gusto kong **magsistream** ng bagong season ng paborito kong serye ngayong gabi.","translation":"I want to **stream** the new season of my favorite series tonight."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng manika o pigura na pinagagalaw sa pamamagitan ng mga tali, kamay, o ibang mekanismo. Maaari ring tumukoy sa isang tao na kontrolado ng iba.
etymology: From English 'puppet', possibly influenced by Spanish 'papel' (paper), referring to early paper puppets.
original_explanation: This is what you call someone who just follows orders without thinking. Parang sa gobyerno, 'pag sunud-sunuran lang sa mas mataas, "papet ng administrasyon" ang tawag. Or in a toxic relationship, kung anong sabihin ng jowa mo, 'yun ang gagawin mo. Don't be a papet!
usage_notes: Can be used literally for a toy puppet or figuratively for a person being controlled. The figurative sense is very common in political discourse.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginagamit ng mga pulitiko ang mga **papet** para isulong ang kanilang pansariling interes.","translation":"Politicians use **puppets** to advance their personal interests."},{"sentence":"Natuwa ang mga bata sa palabas ng mga **papet**.","translation":"The children were delighted by the **puppet** show."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng isda na kilala bilang hitò. Sa modernong konteksto, tumutukoy din ito sa isang tao na lumilikha ng pekeng pagkakakilanlan online upang manlinlang o manloko ng iba.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Ingles na "catfish", na naging popular ang slang na kahulugan dahil sa isang dokumentaryo noong 2010.
original_explanation: Hindi lang ito 'yung isdang hitò na masarap iprito. Sa mundo ng social media, ito 'yung ka-chat mo na ang ganda ng profile pic pero sa totoong buhay, iba pala ang itsura. Sila 'yung rason sa trust issues mo online. 'Yung akala mo si Chris Hemsworth, 'yun pala si Mang Cris na tambay sa kanto.
usage_notes: Ang slang na kahulugan ay mas karaniwan na ngayon sa mga nakababatang henerasyon, lalo na sa konteksto ng online dating at social media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingat ka diyan sa ka-chat mo, baka **catfish** 'yan.","translation":"Be careful with that person you're chatting with, they might be a **catfish**."},{"sentence":"Napanood mo na ba yung palabas tungkol sa mga biktima ng **catfish** sa internet?","translation":"Have you seen the show about the victims of **catfish** on the internet?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglilinis ng mukha gamit ang tubig, at kung minsan ay may kasamang sabon o panlinis.
original_explanation: The first thing you do to feel human in the morning, and the last thing you do to wash away the stress of the day (and your makeup). A sacred ritual. "Friend, maghilamos ka muna, 'yung eyebags mo may sarili nang zip code."
usage_notes: A very common verb related to daily hygiene.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gising na! **Maghilamos** ka na at mag-almusal.","translation":"Wake up! Go **wash your face** and eat breakfast."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **maghilamos** para mahimasmasan ako.","translation":"I need to **wash my face** to feel refreshed."}]

translation: the act of having someone sell something
meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pag-uutos o pagbibigay-pahintulot sa isang tao na magbenta ng mga produkto o kalakal.
etymology: From pag- (nominalizer) + pa- (causative) + tinda (goods for sale).
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "paki-benta mo naman 'to" move. When you ask your friend to sell your pre-loved clothes for you, that's pagpapatinda. It's the business of consignment, palengke-style. You're not the one selling, you're the one *making* someone sell.
usage_notes: Common in business, especially small-scale or informal economies.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapatinda** ng ice candy ang naging hanapbuhay niya ngayong tag-init.","translation":"**Having someone sell** ice candy became her livelihood this summer."},{"sentence":"Ipinagkatiwala niya sa kanyang kapatid ang **pagpapatinda** ng mga ani sa palengke.","translation":"She entrusted her sibling with **having the harvest sold** at the market."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging buwisit o nakakainis; isang bagay o tao na nagdudulot ng matinding inis o pagkayamot.
etymology: From ka- + buwisit + -an. 'Buwisit' is from Hokkien 'bo' (no) + 'ui-sit' (luck/clothing), meaning 'bad luck'.
original_explanation: That feeling when the internet dies during a crucial Zoom meeting. The person in front of you at the ATM who's checking their balance ten times. The 'seen' on Messenger with no reply. Basically, anything that makes you want to scream 'Bwisit!' is a source of kabuwisitan. It’s the ultimate 'peste' in your life.
usage_notes: A very common and expressive word for frustration. Can be used to describe the feeling or the source of the feeling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko na matiis ang **kabuwisitan** na dulot ng mabagal na trapiko.","translation":"I can no longer stand the **frustration** caused by the slow traffic."},{"sentence":"Ano na namang **kabuwisitan** ito?","translation":"What **annoyance** is this now?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang magaang pagkain na kinakain sa pagitan ng mga pangunahing kainan tulad ng agahan, tanghalian, at hapunan.
original_explanation: This is the 4th, 5th, and sometimes 6th meal of the day for a Filipino. It's the sacred afternoon ritual, usually around 3-4 PM, to power through the rest of the workday or before the commute home. Think banana cue, pancit, or even just a pack of Chippy with a Zesto. It's not just a snack; it's a social institution.
usage_notes: The spellings 'merienda' and 'meriyenda' are also widely used and accepted, though 'meryenda' is most aligned with Tagalog phonetic spelling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **meryenda** natin mamaya?","translation":"What's our **snack** for later?"},{"sentence":"Nagdala ako ng fishball para sa **meryenda**.","translation":"I brought fishballs for our **snack**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pampahid sa buhok, karaniwang may amoy at ginagamit upang ayusin at patingkarin ang buhok.
original_explanation: Your lolo's secret weapon for that classic, shiny, slicked-back hair that could withstand a typhoon. Now it's been rediscovered by hipsters and barbershop aficionados for that 'effortlessly styled' look that actually took 20 minutes to perfect.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng **pomada** para maayos ang ayos ng buhok ko para sa party.","translation":"I need **pomade** to fix my hairstyle for the party."},{"sentence":"Ang bango ng **pomada** na gamit mo.","translation":"The **pomade** you're using smells good."}]

translation: to chip off; to break off a piece
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkabakli o pagkatanggal ng isang maliit na piraso mula sa isang mas malaking bagay, lalo na sa matitigas na materyales tulad ng kahoy o bato.
original_explanation: You know that feeling when you accidentally hit the edge of your favorite mug and a small piece breaks off? That's it. The mug *tumilad*. It’s the universe's way of reminding you that nothing is perfect, not even your "World's Best Boss" mug. It's a small, tragic break.
usage_notes: Refers to a small piece breaking or chipping off a larger, solid object. 'Bumiyak' is for a larger crack or break.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumilad** ang isang piraso ng pinggan nang mabitawan ko ito.","translation":"A piece of the plate **chipped off** when I dropped it."},{"sentence":"Sa katagalan, ang pintura sa pader ay nagsimulang **tumilad**.","translation":"Over time, the paint on the wall began to **chip off**."}]

translation: the legal profession, law (as a field)
meaning_filipino: Ang propesyon ng pagiging abogado; ang larangan ng pag-aaral ng batas.
original_explanation: This is what you call the entire world of lawyers, law schools, and courtrooms. It's the field your parents push you into if you're good at arguing. 'Nag-aaral siya ng abogasya' means they're on the long, difficult, but prestigious path to becoming 'Atty.'
usage_notes: This is the modern, standard term for the law profession, distinct from the archaic and negative 'abogasia'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap ngunit marangal ang propesyon ng **abogasya**.","translation":"The **legal profession** is difficult but honorable."},{"sentence":"Pumasok siya sa larangan ng **abogasya** upang ipagtanggol ang mga naaapi.","translation":"She entered the field of **law** to defend the oppressed."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang lalaki na may magandang asal, magalang, at may paggalang sa kababaihan; kilos-ginoo.
etymology: From "ginoo" (gentleman) + "-hin" (suffix indicating a tendency or quality).
original_explanation: The type of guy your lola wishes you'd bring home. He opens doors, pulls out chairs, and probably says "po" and "opo" even to his pets. In short, the opposite of a f*ckboy. The "Sana All" of boyfriends.
usage_notes: Describes a man's character and behavior, often in a positive, traditional sense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **maginoohin** na ginoo si G. Reyes, laging magalang sa lahat.","translation":"Mr. Reyes is a **gentlemanly** man, always respectful to everyone."}]

translation: to be intricately tangled; to be disheveled
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng labis na pagkakabuhol-buhol o pagkakasalungat ng mga direksyon sa paraang napakagulo.
original_explanation: This is 'magsâla-salâ' on steroids. This is your headset after one second in your pocket. It's the state of your life plans when Mercury is in retrograde. It’s an absolute, chaotic mess where everything is tangled with everything else. Think of a bird's nest made of wires, strings, and bad decisions.
usage_notes: Stronger and more chaotic than 'magsâla-salâ'. Often used to describe something in extreme disarray.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-**magsâla-salabát** ang sinulid kaya hindi na magamit.","translation":"The thread **became intricately tangled** so it can no longer be used."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **magsâla-salabát** ang mga problema mo sa buhay.","translation":"Don't let your life's problems **get completely entangled**."}]

translation: to flourish; to soar; to show off
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-angat, pag-unlad, o pagpapakita ng galing at karangyaan; maaari ring tumukoy sa pagaspas ng pakpak ng isang ibon.
etymology: From `payagpag` (flapping of wings, showing off) with the infix `-um-`.
original_explanation: That's your friend who just got promoted and is now 'flexing' their new success. 'Aba, pumapayagpag na si kumpare!' It's like a bird spreading its wings and soaring high, showing everyone its beautiful feathers. It can mean to flourish or, in some contexts, to show off a bit.
usage_notes: Can have a slightly negative connotation of being boastful, but can also be used positively to mean thriving or succeeding.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pumayagpag** ang kanyang karera matapos siyang manalo sa kompetisyon.","translation":"His career **flourished** after he won the competition."},{"sentence":"Tila isang agila na **pumayagpag** sa himpapawid ang kanyang pangarap.","translation":"His dream **soared** in the sky like an eagle."}]

translation: to enslave, to treat as a servant
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtrato sa isang tao na parang alila o alipin; ang pagsasamantala o pagmamaltrato sa kapwa.
original_explanation: This is what you feel when your boss gives you work at 4:59 PM on a Friday. It's the ultimate "ginawa mo akong katulong" hugot. To be treated with less dignity than the office printer.
usage_notes: A strong word implying exploitation and disrespect. Often used hyperbolically to complain about being overworked.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi tama na **alilain** mo ang iyong mga kasambahay.","translation":"It is not right for you to **treat** your house helpers **like servants**."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam niya ay **inaalila** siya sa sarili niyang pamamahay.","translation":"She feels like she is being **treated like a slave** in her own home."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang impormal na tawag sa isang kaibigang lalaki o kapatid na lalaki.
original_explanation: The universal greeting for any male person whose name you've forgotten. It's the shorter, cooler, less formal cousin of 'kuya' and 'pare'. Usage: "What's up, bro?", "Thanks, bro!", "Bro, ang traffic!"
usage_notes: Extremely common informal address for males, regardless of actual familial relationship.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bro**, pahiram naman ng charger mo.","translation":"**Bro**, can I borrow your charger?"}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi baluktot, nakakiling, o may kurbada. Tumutukoy din sa tamang tindig o sa pagiging matapat at marangal.
original_explanation: The opposite of your scoliosis. It's how your lola tells you to sit. It can also mean being on the 'straight and narrow' path, as in not being corrupt or doing anything shady. The 'daang matuwid' everyone talks about but is harder to find than a parking spot in Greenhills during Christmas.
usage_notes: Often used to describe physical posture or moral character. While it can mean 'straight' like a line, 'diretso' is more common for that. 'Tuwid' is better for posture and morality.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Panatilihing **tuwid** ang iyong likod habang nakaupo.","translation":"Keep your back **straight** while sitting."},{"sentence":"Hangad nating lahat ang isang pamahalaang **tuwid** at tapat.","translation":"We all aspire for a government that is **upright** and honest."}]

translation: to load a gun with bullets
meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng bala ang isang baril o anumang uri ng sandatang-apoy.
original_explanation: This is NOT about giving a warning (see other 'magbabala'). This is literally loading a firearm. Action movie stuff. 'Huwag kang kikilos, nagbabala na ako ng baril!' is a line you hear in films, not something you say when you see a 'Wet Floor' sign.
usage_notes: This homonym is less common in everyday conversation but is understood in contexts involving firearms. The pronunciation is identical to its 'warning' counterpart.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita sa CCTV ang suspek na **nagbabala** ng kanyang baril bago pumasok sa bangko.","translation":"The suspect was seen on CCTV **loading** his gun with bullets before entering the bank."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalakad-lakad o pagpunta sa isang lugar para sa libangan, pagliliwaliw, o pagtingin-tingin sa paligid.
original_explanation: 'Yung "Tara, gala!" ng tropa mo. It's going out for leisure—window shopping sa mall, walking sa park, beach trip. It’s the opposite of being a "taong-bahay." Basically, any trip that isn't for work or errands.
usage_notes: Pangkasalukuyang anyo ng 'mamasyal'. Nagpapahiwatig ng isang patuloy na kilos ng paglalakad o pamamasyal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing Linggo, **namamasyal** kami sa Luneta Park.","translation":"Every Sunday, we **stroll** in Luneta Park."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko si Maria na **namamasyal** sa mall kasama ang kanyang mga kaibigan.","translation":"I saw Maria **sightseeing** at the mall with her friends."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglapat ng buong katawan sa isang patag na ibabaw, tulad ng sa kama o sahig, upang magpahinga o matulog.
original_explanation: The official action of the tamad, the pagod, and everyone on a Sunday afternoon. It's what you do after a long day at work, after eating too much, or when you just can't even. The ultimate act of "pahinga". Higa is a lifestyle.
usage_notes: Can be used as a command ('Higa!') or as a root for verbs like 'humiga' (to lie down) and adjectives like 'nakahiga' (in a lying position).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Higa** ka muna sa kama at magpahinga.","translation":"**Lie down** on the bed for a while and rest."},{"sentence":"Pagod na pagod ako, gusto ko na lang **humiga**.","translation":"I'm so tired, I just want to **lie down**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglabag sa isang batas, tuntunin, kasunduan, o karapatan ng isang tao.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you cross the yellow line on the MRT platform, or when your officemate steals your lunch from the pantry fridge. It's breaking the rules, whether it's a traffic rule or an unwritten social contract.
usage_notes: Often used in legal or formal contexts, such as 'traffic violation'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May multa ang anumang **biolasyon** sa batas trapiko.","translation":"Any **violation** of traffic laws has a fine."},{"sentence":"Ang ginawa niya ay isang malinaw na **biolasyon** ng aming kasunduan.","translation":"What he did was a clear **violation** of our agreement."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sangay ng sandatahang lakas na pangunahing kumikilos at lumalaban sa kalupaan.
etymology: A compound of 'hukbo' (army) and 'kati' (land, as opposed to sea).
original_explanation: The 'army of the land.' These are the soldiers with boots on the ground, the infantry. They're the main force you see in war movies, marching through jungles and cities. Basically, if 'hukbong-dagat' owns the water, 'hukbong-kati' owns the dry land.
usage_notes: Largely interchangeable with 'hukbong-katihan', though the latter is more common in official contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **hukbong-kati** ang bumubuo sa pinakamalaking bahagi ng militar.","translation":"The **land army** comprises the largest part of the military."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng payo, gabay, o rekomendasyon sa isang tao hinggil sa isang partikular na suliranin o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: This is what you do when your friend has a major "what do I do with my life?" crisis or is deep in a "hugot" moment about their love life. You sit them down, probably with coffee or beer, and `pagpayuhan` mo sila. It's the act of giving advice, solicited or not. Your tita who always asks when you're getting married is a master of this, in her own special way.
usage_notes: The verb `payuhan` means "to advise someone" (object-focused), while `magpayo` means "to give advice" (actor-focused). `Pagpayuhan` is the object-focused imperative/infinitive form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaari mo ba akong **pagpayuhan** kung ano ang dapat kong gawin?","translation":"Can you **advise me** on what I should do?"},{"sentence":"Laging handa si Lola na **pagpayuhan** ang kanyang mga apo.","translation":"Grandma is always ready **to advise** her grandchildren."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahina at pigil na pagtawa, na karaniwang nagpapahiwatig ng katuwaan, hiya, o panunukso.
original_explanation: The official sound of your friends when your crush walks by. It's that suppressed giggle you can't control, the kind that makes your shoulders shake. Not a full-blown 'halakhak' (laughter), but a quiet, often mischievous **halikhik**. The sound of high school corridors and chismis sessions.
usage_notes: Can also be a verb (humalikhik). It implies a certain coyness or secrecy in the laughter.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi mapigilan ng mga dalaga ang kanilang **halikhik** nang dumaan ang binatang kanilang hinahangaan.","translation":"The young ladies couldn't stop their **giggles** when the young man they admire passed by."},{"sentence":"Isang **halikhik** ang narinig mula sa sulok ng silid.","translation":"A **giggle** was heard from the corner of the room."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o damdamin ng pagiging galit; matinding sama ng loob o inis.
original_explanation: That feeling when the internet dies in the middle of your Netflix binge or when someone eats your Jollibee order from the office fridge. It's the 'gigil' level turned up to 11. The emotion that fuels many a dramatic teleserye confrontation.
usage_notes: Denotes the state or instance of anger. 'Kagalitan' is the act of scolding, while 'pagkagalit' is the emotion itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya maitago ang kanyang **pagkagalit** nang makita ang resulta.","translation":"He couldn't hide his **anger** when he saw the results."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkagalit** ay isang emosyong kailangang kontrolin.","translation":"**Anger** is an emotion that needs to be controlled."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay ng gamot o anumang likido sa katawan ng isang tao o hayop gamit ang heringgilya. Ito ay nasa anyong pangnagdaan.
original_explanation: This is what happened to you at the clinic when you got your anti-rabies shot after your neighbor's dog thought your leg was a chew toy. It's the past tense of 'to inject'. "Iniksiyunan ako ng nurse, ang sakit, besh!"
usage_notes: Often used in medical contexts. The root word is 'iniksyon'. This is the object-focused past tense form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Iniksiyunan** ng doktor ang pasyente ng gamot laban sa lagnat.","translation":"The doctor **injected** the patient with medicine for the fever."},{"sentence":"**Iniksiyunan** mo na ba ang manok para hindi magkasakit?","translation":"Have you **injected** the chicken so it won't get sick?"}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing malinaw o maliwanag ang isang bagay, ideya, o pahayag upang maunawaan nang husto.
original_explanation: This is what your partner asks you to do when they say "We need to talk." It's the opposite of "bahala na." You're basically being asked to turn on the lights in a dark room of misunderstandings. "Pakilinaw, besh. Anong status natin?"
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of explaining rules, feelings, or complex topics.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **liwanagin** ang iyong mga sinabi para maiwasan ang gulo.","translation":"You need to **clarify** what you said to avoid trouble."},{"sentence":"**Liwanagin** mo nga kung ano talaga ang gusto mong mangyari.","translation":"**Make it clear** what you really want to happen."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit at mababaw na hiwa o marka sa balat o sa ibabaw ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: That tiny scratch you get from your cat, a sharp piece of paper, or when you accidentally scrape your phone against your keys. It's not a full-blown 'sugat' (wound), just a 'konting gurlis lang.' It's the papercut of injuries.
usage_notes: Refers to a superficial scratch, not a deep wound.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ako ng **gurlis** sa braso dahil sa pusa.","translation":"I got a **scratch** on my arm from the cat."},{"sentence":"Ingatan mo 'yang kotse, baka magkaroon ng **gurlis**.","translation":"Be careful with that car, it might get a **scratch**."}]

translation: to have something axed; to use an axe
meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng palakol sa pagputol, partikular sa kahoy; o ang pag-utos sa iba na gumamit ng palakol.
original_explanation: Literally, it's about getting an axe to chop something, like firewood for your lola's dirty kitchen. Figuratively, in the corporate world, 'mapalakol' means to get fired or laid off. 'Nagpalakol ang boss' means the boss went on a firing spree. It's the less subtle version of 'downsizing'.
usage_notes: Can be literal (chopping wood) or figurative (getting fired, 'sibakin'). The context determines the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-utos ang magsasaka na **magpalakol** ng mga tuyong sanga ng puno.","translation":"The farmer ordered to **have the dry tree branches axed**."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa pagbaba ng kita, kailangang **magpalakol** ng empleyado ang kumpanya.","translation":"Due to the decrease in profit, the company needs to **lay off** employees."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mahaba at natatanging balahibo sa buntot ng isang tandang o ibang uri ng ibon.
original_explanation: The glorious, flowing feather on a rooster's tail. It's the bird's version of having fabulous, long hair. In sabong (cockfighting), a good 'lawi' is a sign of a strong chicken. It's the ultimate flex in the poultry world.
usage_notes: Primarily associated with roosters (tandang).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng **lawi** ng tandang na alaga ni Lolo.","translation":"The **long tail feather** of Grandpa's rooster is beautiful."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pahabang prutas na karaniwang kulay dilaw kapag hinog, na nagmumula sa halamang saging. Ito ay isang pangunahing pagkain at sangkap sa maraming lutuing Pilipino.
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino fruit. It's our breakfast (with sinangag), our merienda (banana cue, turon), our dessert (saging con yelo), and our go-to "pang-tawid gutom". It's the fruit that's always there for you, reliable and versatile, like a good friend. Also, the reason you slip in cartoons.
usage_notes: The Philippines has many varieties like Lakatan, Latundan, Saba, and Señorita. 'Saging' is the general term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong meryenda ang turon na gawa sa **saging** na saba.","translation":"My favorite snack is turon made from saba **bananas**."},{"sentence":"Magdala ka ng **saging** para may makain tayo sa biyahe.","translation":"Bring some **bananas** so we have something to eat on the trip."}]

meaning_filipino: (Kolokyal) Nagpapahayag ng matinding paghanga sa isang pambihirang galing, gawa, o kakayahan.
etymology: From `napaka-` (superlative prefix) + `hayop` (animal). The meaning evolved in slang usage.
original_explanation: The highest praise you can get from your barkada after you do something incredibly cool, like a perfect three-point shot or acing a presentation. It's like "awesome" or "beast mode" but with a distinct Pinoy flavor.
usage_notes: Used informally among peers to express intense admiration for a skill or achievement. Intonation is key to distinguish it from the insult.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita mo 'yung ginawa niyang guitar solo? **Napakahayop**!","translation":"Did you see that guitar solo he did? It was **freaking awesome**!"},{"sentence":"Tumakbo siya ng 10 kilometro sa loob ng 30 minuto, **napakahayop** ng tibay!","translation":"He ran 10 kilometers in 30 minutes, his endurance is **badass**!"}]

translation: to cause anguish; to afflict with sorrow
meaning_filipino: Magdulot ng matinding sakit ng damdamin, pighati, o pagdurusa.
original_explanation: A synonym for `bigyang-dalamhati`, but maybe with a more poetic, old-school flavor. It's the kind of word you'd find in a Florante at Laura-esque text. It’s deep, profound sadness, the kind that makes you want to stare at the rain with a sad OPM song playing in the background.
usage_notes: Extremely formal and literary. Almost never used in modern, everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang masamang balita ay **nagbigay-hapis** sa buong kaharian.","translation":"The bad news **caused anguish** throughout the kingdom."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang pagtataksil ay **nagbigay-hapis** sa puso ng dalaga.","translation":"His betrayal **afflicted with sorrow** the young lady's heart."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kondisyon sa balat na may mga mapupula, makakati, at nakaumbok na pantal, karaniwang sanhi ng allergy.
original_explanation: That annoying skin reaction you get after eating something you're allergic to, like shrimp or an ex's lies. It's super itchy and makes you want to scratch your skin off. "Hala, nagka-tagulabay ako sa kinain kong hipon!"
usage_notes: Isang partikular na terminong medikal, bagaman karaniwang ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinayuhan siya ng doktor na uminom ng antihistamine para sa kanyang **tagulabay**.","translation":"The doctor advised him to take an antihistamine for his **hives**."},{"sentence":"Ang alikabok ay maaaring magdulot ng **tagulabay** sa mga taong may allergy.","translation":"Dust can cause **hives** in people with allergies."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalagyan o kabinet para sa mga baso. Maaari ring tumukoy sa isang koleksyon o pangkat ng mga baso.
etymology: From "baso" (glass) + "-han" (suffix indicating a place or collection).
original_explanation: It's either that fancy crystal glass cabinet your tita only opens for Christmas, or just the part of the dish rack where you put all the... well, baso. The designated home for your drinking vessels.
usage_notes: The stress on the second syllable /ba-SU-han/ distinguishes it from /BA-su-han/ (a verb meaning 'to put something in a glass').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-ayos ang mga bagong baso sa **basuhan**.","translation":"Please arrange the new glasses in the **glass cabinet**."},{"sentence":"Nabagsak niya ang buong **basuhan**.","translation":"He dropped the entire **set of glasses**."}]

translation: Act of making something heavier; exacerbation; being a burden.
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagdaragdag ng bigat o timbang sa isang bagay; o ang paglala ng isang sitwasyon, problema, o pasanin.
original_explanation: Two meanings here. Literal: adding more stuff to your baggage para mag-excess. Figurative: being the 'pabigat' in the group—the one who complicates things, adds to the drama, or makes the problem worse. It's turning a simple issue into a teleserye-level crisis.
usage_notes: Can be literal (adding weight) or figurative (worsening a situation, being a burden).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itigil mo na ang **pagpapabigat** sa sitwasyon sa pamamagitan ng mga tsismis.","translation":"Stop **exacerbating** the situation with rumors."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapabigat** sa damdamin ng iba ay hindi magandang ugali.","translation":"Being a **burden** on others' feelings is not a good trait."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng babala o tanda ng posibleng kapahamakan o parusa sa isang tao upang siya ay mapasunod o matakot.
original_explanation: When you tell your sibling, "Isusumbong kita kay Mama!" That's the PG-13 version. The R-18 version involves HR and a formal complaint.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pagbantaan** ang iyong kapwa.","translation":"Do not **threaten** your fellow person."},{"sentence":"**Pinagbantaan** ng masamang panahon ang planong pag-akyat sa bundok.","translation":"The planned mountain climb was **threatened** by bad weather."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan na may butas-butas na ginagamit upang ihiwalay ang mga solido mula sa likido, o para salain ang mga hindi kanais-nais na bagay.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "taga-" (pananda ng gamit o gawain) at salitang-ugat na "sala" (salain).
original_explanation: That thing in your kitchen sink na laging nawawala 'pag kailangan mo para sa pancit canton. It separates the noodles from the hot water, just like how you separate your feelings from your work para 'di ka ma-HR.
usage_notes: Ito ay tumutukoy sa kasangkapan. Ang salitang "makasalanan" ang ginagamit para sa taong may sala o kasalanan, hindi "tagasala".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gamitin mo ang **tagasala** para hindi sumama ang buto ng calamansi sa juice.","translation":"Use the **strainer** so the calamansi seeds don't get mixed into the juice."},{"sentence":"Naiwan ang mga pansahog sa **tagasala** matapos ibuhos ang sabaw.","translation":"The ingredients were left in the **colander** after the broth was poured out."}]

translation: to charge interest, to lend money with interest
meaning_filipino: Magpataw ng karagdagang bayad o interes sa perang ipinautang.
original_explanation: This is the business model of your friendly neighborhood '5-6'. You borrow 5, you pay back 6. That extra '1' is because they `magpatubo`. It's the financial version of "there's no such thing as a free lunch." Banks do it legally, others do it... differently.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to finance and lending, often with a slightly negative connotation when referring to usury (e.g., '5-6'). Distinct from 'magpatubo' which means to grow something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bawal sa kanilang relihiyon ang **magpatubo** sa pautang.","translation":"It is forbidden in their religion to **charge interest** on loans."},{"sentence":"Malaki siyang **magpatubo**, kaya iwasan mong umutang sa kanya.","translation":"He **charges high interest**, so avoid borrowing money from him."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na laging salungat o iba ang ginagawa sa karaniwan o inaasahan; mapanlaban sa nakagawian.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "saliwa" (kabaligtaran, salungat) at hulaping "-in".
original_explanation: This is your friend who, when everyone says "let's go left," insists on going right just because. The one who orders a salad at a samgyupsal place. They're not necessarily bad, just hardwired to go against the flow. Sila yung tipo na sasabihan mo ng "huwag mong pindutin," at pipindutin talaga nila. The ultimate 'kontrabida' in group decisions.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan ng isang katangian ng pagkatao. Maaaring magkaroon ng negatibong konotasyon, na nagpapahiwatig ng pagiging mahirap pakisamahan o matigas ang ulo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang magtaka kung hindi siya sumang-ayon, talagang **saliwain** ang taong iyan.","translation":"Don't be surprised if he doesn't agree, that person is naturally **contrary**."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang pagiging **saliwain**, madalas siyang napapaaway.","translation":"Because of his **perverse** nature, he often gets into fights."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing mas mabilis ang isang kilos, proseso, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: What your boss tells you at 4:59 PM on a Friday. 'Pabilisin mo 'yang report!' means 'Hurry up that report!' It's the verb for when the internet is lagging and you're praying to the PLDT gods, or when you're stuck in EDSA traffic and wishing you could just teleport.
usage_notes: A causative verb. It means to cause something or someone to become fast.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **pabilisin** ang pag-aproba ng proyekto.","translation":"We need to **speed up** the approval of the project."},{"sentence":"**Pabilisin** mo ang takbo, male-late na tayo!","translation":"**Hasten** your pace, we're going to be late!"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay o pangyayari na tuluy-tuloy, hindi napuputol, o walang hinto.
original_explanation: Like your chismosa kapitbahay's storytelling—it just goes on and on, walang-lagot! Or that unli-rice promo where the server keeps coming back. It’s also the ideal state of your internet connection during a crucial online game or a Netflix binge. The opposite of your salary, which definitely has a "lagot" (break/end).
usage_notes: Maaaring ilarawan ang mga kilos, tunog, o proseso na tuluy-tuloy. Madalas gamitin sa paraang hyperbole.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-iyak ng sanggol ay **walang-lagot** buong magdamag.","translation":"The baby's crying was **incessant** all night."},{"sentence":"**Walang-lagot** ang buhos ng ulan kaya bumaha sa aming lugar.","translation":"The rain poured **uninterrupted**, which is why our area flooded."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdampi ng mga labi sa isang tao o bagay bilang pagpapahayag ng pagmamahal, paggalang, pagnanasa, o pagbati.
original_explanation: The official seal of a relationship status update, the 'mano po' gesture to your lola, or that smack on the cheek you get from a tita you haven't seen in ages. From "beso-beso" to a full-on teleserye-ending **halik**, it's a gesture with a thousand meanings.
usage_notes: Can be a romantic kiss, a respectful one (like on an elder's hand), or a friendly one (beso-beso).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang matamis na **halik** sa noo ang ibinigay niya sa kanyang anak bago ito matulog.","translation":"She gave a sweet **kiss** on her child's forehead before they slept."},{"sentence":"Ang unang **halik** nila ay napanood sa ilalim ng kalangitan na puno ng bituin.","translation":"Their first **kiss** was witnessed under a sky full of stars."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang biglaang pagkapilay o pinsala sa kasukasuan, lalo na sa bukung-bukong, na nagdudulot ng pamamaga at sakit.
original_explanation: That 'aray!' moment when your ankle decides to go sideways while you're running to catch the jeep or wearing heels on uneven pavement. The result is a painful, swollen ankle that makes you walk like a penguin. 'Ingat ka sa hagdan, baka ma-pilok ka.'
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun (sprain) or an adjective (sprained). The verb form 'napilok' means 'got sprained'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **pilok** ang kanyang kanang paa kaya hindi siya makalakad nang maayos.","translation":"He has a **sprain** on his right foot so he can't walk properly."},{"sentence":"Ang **pilok** na paa ay dapat ipahinga.","translation":"A **sprained** foot must be rested."}]

translation: to have someone catch; to make someone take the blame
meaning_filipino: Iutos o hayaan ang isang tao na saluhin ang isang bagay na inihagis o nahuhulog. Sa matalinghagang paraan, ito ay ang pagpasa ng responsibilidad o sisi sa iba.
original_explanation: Literally, it's when you toss your keys and yell "catch!" so you ask someone to **pasaluhin**. Figuratively, it's what your boss does when a project fails and they need a scapegoat. You're made to "catch" the blame. "Sino'ng may kasalanan?" "Siya po, pinasaluhan lang sa akin."
usage_notes: Has both a literal and a very common figurative meaning related to blame or responsibility. The context determines the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pasaluhin** mo kay Juan ang bola.","translation":"**Have Juan catch** the ball."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang papayag na ikaw ang **pasaluhin** sa kasalanan ng iba.","translation":"Don't allow them to **make you take the blame** for someone else's mistake."}]

meaning_filipino: Bilang pang-uri, tumutukoy sa pagkakaroon ng apat na magkakaparehong haba ng gilid at apat na tamang anggulo. Bilang pangalan, ito ang hugis mismo.
original_explanation: The shape of your crush's jawline if you're lucky, or the shape of a table you keep bumping into. It's basic geometry, but in Filipino culture, it can also mean old-fashioned or rigid, like a 'kuwadrado' way of thinking. 'Be there or be square' but make it Tagalog.
usage_notes: Can be a noun (the shape) or an adjective (describing something as square).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko ng mesang **kuwadrado** para sa aming maliit na kusina.","translation":"I want a **square** table for our small kitchen."},{"sentence":"Ang sahig ay may mga baldosa na hugis **kuwadrado**.","translation":"The floor has tiles shaped like a **square**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang posisyon o lokasyon na mas mataas kaysa sa isang punto ng reperensya.
etymology: Mula sa "sa" (at) + "itaas" (ang bahaging mas mataas, sa ibabaw).
original_explanation: Where your upstairs neighbor who loves dropping things at 3 AM lives. It's also where you point when someone asks where God is ("Nasa itaas"). In a corporate ladder, it's where the bosses are. In a double-decker bed, it's the more desirable spot (until you have to go to the CR).
usage_notes: Ang direktang kasalungat ng "sa ibaba" (below).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatira sila **sa itaas** ng aming apartment.","translation":"They live **above** our apartment."},{"sentence":"Pakikuha ng libro **sa itaas** ng mesa.","translation":"Please get the book **on top** of the table."}]

translation: mouthful (of food); act of putting food into the mouth
meaning_filipino: Ang dami ng pagkaing isinusubo sa bibig sa isang pagkakataon; ang akto ng paglalagay ng pagkain sa bibig.
original_explanation: Your mom shouting "Isang **subo** na lang, anak!" when you were a kid. It's that perfect spoonful of rice and ulam you put in your mouth. In the age of samgyupsal and food vlogs, it's also the "Akin na, isang **subo** lang!" you say to your friend's food, which you know will turn into five more.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb 'sumubo' (to eat/put in the mouth) or 'isubo' (to put something in the mouth).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **subo** pa bago ka umalis.","translation":"One more **mouthful** before you go."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong punuin ang bibig mo; maliliit na **subo** lang.","translation":"Don't fill your mouth; just small **mouthfuls**."}]

translation: to solicit, to collect (for a cause)
meaning_filipino: Maghanap o humingi ng abuloy o donasyon para sa isang tiyak na layunin.
etymology: From root "kilak," meaning to gather or collect.
