original_explanation: This is what your org's treasurer does when there's a project but no budget. It's the official term for "pasa lata" or "tokhang for a cause" where you approach people for donations, hoping they have more than just barya in their pockets.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of fundraising for charities, churches, or community projects.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang klase na **mangilak** ng pondo para sa mga nasalanta ng bagyo.","translation":"The class decided to **solicit** funds for the typhoon victims."},{"sentence":"Tuwing Pasko, sila ay umiikot sa mga bahay upang **mangilak** ng donasyon para sa ampunan.","translation":"Every Christmas, they go around the houses to **collect** donations for the orphanage."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salaysay, pasulat man o pelikula, na naglalahad ng mga kaganapan sa buhay ng isang tunay na tao.
original_explanation: The biopic of your life. Is it an indie film full of hugot, a blockbuster action flick, or a comedy of errors? Ito 'yung pelikula tungkol sa isang historical figure na pinapanood for school, tulad ng 'Heneral Luna' o 'Goyo'.
usage_notes: Isang tambalang salita. Maaari itong tumukoy sa isang libro (talambuhay) o sa isang pelikula (biopic).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **larawang-buhay** ni Jose Rizal ay nagpapakita ng kaniyang pagiging bayani.","translation":"The **biography** of Jose Rizal shows his heroism."},{"sentence":"Naging matagumpay sa takilya ang **larawang-buhay** ng sikat na mang-aawit.","translation":"The **motion picture** about the famous singer was a box-office success."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng suwerte, mabuting kapalaran, o biyaya.
original_explanation: Ikaw 'yung nakakuha ng last piece ng lechon sa handaan. Ikaw 'yung natawag sa recitation pero sakto alam mo 'yung sagot. Ikaw 'yung hindi na-stuck sa EDSA traffic today. You are **mapalad**. Basically, the universe is on your side. Sana all.
usage_notes: Root word 'palad' means 'palm of the hand', linked to palm reading and fate.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Mapalad** ang mga batang nakapag-aaral sa magandang eskwelahan.","translation":"The children who can study in good schools are **fortunate**."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam ko ay **mapalad** ako ngayong araw dahil nanalo ako sa raffle.","translation":"I feel **lucky** today because I won the raffle."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbuo ng isang pangkat, kumpol, o grupo.
etymology: From `pag-` + reduplication of the first syllable of the root `lumpon` (`lu-`) + `lumpon`.
original_explanation: 'Yung biglaang meeting ng mga chismosa sa kanto kapag may bagong issue. O 'yung pag-dikit-dikit ng mga tao sa MRT kahit may space pa naman. It's the act of forming a tight-knit group, whether it's for gossip, safety, or just because you're all waiting for the same thing.
usage_notes: Describes the formation of a cluster or group of people or things.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paglulumpon** ng mga tao sa plasa ay para sa isang protesta.","translation":"The **gathering** of people in the plaza is for a protest."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang walang saysay o labis na pagsasalita; daldal.
etymology: Posibleng mula sa Espanyol na "cuidar" (to care), na nag-evolve ang kahulugan patungo sa labis na pag-aalala o pagsasalita tungkol sa isang bagay, na naging 'chatter'.
original_explanation: This is the art of talking a lot without saying anything important. It's mindless chatter, yapping, or ranting. "Puro ka **kuda**, wala namang gawa" is the Filipino equivalent of "All talk, no action." It's what you do when you're complaining about your boss, gossiping about a celebrity, or just filling the air with noise.
usage_notes: Isang salitang kolokyal na may bahagyang negatibong konotasyon, na nagpapahiwatig na ang sinasabi ay walang kabuluhan. Ginagamit din bilang pandiwa (verb) na 'kumuda'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tama na ang **kuda**, simulan na natin ang trabaho.","translation":"Enough with the **chatter**, let's start working."},{"sentence":"Hayaan mo siyang kumuda nang **kuda**, mapapagod din 'yan.","translation":"Let him/her blab on and on, they'll get tired eventually."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang lugar na maraming tumutubong halamang pako (fern).
original_explanation: Describes a place that looks like the set of Jurassic Park—ferns everywhere! If your backyard is mapako, you can probably just forage for your next 'gising-gising' or 'ensaladang pako' right there. It's a very specific kind of green and lush.
usage_notes: The root word 'pako' refers to the edible fiddlehead fern (Athyrium esculentum). The pronunciation is the same as the verb form, so context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang gilid ng sapa ay **mapako** kaya madali kaming nakahanap ng ulam.","translation":"The side of the stream **was abounding in ferns** so we easily found something for our meal."},{"sentence":"Gusto ko ng hardin na **mapako** at malumot.","translation":"I want a garden that is **full of ferns** and moss."}]

translation: to put an end to; to terminate
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtatapos o paghinto sa isang bagay, proseso, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: This is what you want to do to your toxic situationship, your mountain of debt, or the never-ending group chat notifications. To magbigay-wakas is to declare 'The End,' to drop the mic, to finally close the tab. It's the ultimate 'it's over.'
usage_notes: A formal and somewhat dramatic way of saying 'to end'. 'Tapusin' is the more common equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Panahon na upang **magbigay-wakas** sa hidwaang ito.","translation":"It is time to **put an end to** this conflict."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang kamatayan ang **nagbigay-wakas** sa isang panahon ng sining.","translation":"His death **terminated** an era of art."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagpapaikli para sa "get-together" o "pasyal," na tumutukoy sa isang kaswal na pagtitipon o pamamasyal ng magkakaibigan.
etymology: Mula sa pagpapaikli ng mga pariralang Ingles na "Get-together" at Tagalog na "Pasyal".
original_explanation: Stands for "General Patronage" sa concert tickets, pero sa barkada chat, it means "Get-together Pasyal!" or simply "Gala, Please!" It's the two-letter question that determines your weekend plans. "GP tayo?" is the modern Filipino's mating call for friendship and gimmick.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa text messages at social media group chats.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uy, long weekend! **GP** naman tayo dyan.","translation":"Hey, it's a long weekend! Let's have a **get-together**."},{"sentence":"Sino'ng free for a coffee **GP** next week?","translation":"Who's free for a coffee **get-together** next week?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ayusin ang tono ng isang instrumentong may kuwerdas, tulad ng gitara, upang ito ay tumunog nang tama at kaaya-aya.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "cuerdas" (strings) na may panlaping Tagalog na "-an".
original_explanation: The act of making your guitar sound less like a dying cat and more like music. It's that moment before a performance where the musician gets all serious, twisting pegs and plucking strings, trying to get everything "in sync." Parang sa relationship, kailangan i-tune para hindi sintunado ang pagsasama.
usage_notes: Ginagamit para sa mga instrumentong pangmusika na may kuwerdas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bago tumugtog, kailangan mo munang **kuwerdasan** nang maayos ang iyong gitara.","translation":"Before playing, you first need **to tune** your guitar properly."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbibigay ng tulong o paggawa nang sama-sama kasama ang isa o higit pang tao upang makamit ang isang layunin.
etymology: From maki- (social prefix) + pag- (action prefix) + tulong (help) + -an (locative/social suffix).
original_explanation: Ito yung group project sa school na isa lang ang gumagawa, pero sa ideal world, lahat kayo nag-aambagan. 'Teamwork makes the dream work,' ika nga. Sa office, ito yung ginagawa niyo para humabol sa deadline, kahit puyat at puno ng kape ang sistema.
usage_notes: The 'maki-' prefix indicates a social or reciprocal action, asking for or joining in the act of helping each other.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **makipagtulungan** sa isa't isa upang malutas ang problemang ito.","translation":"We need to **cooperate** with each other to solve this problem."},{"sentence":"Pumayag siyang **makipagtulungan** sa proyekto ng gobyerno.","translation":"He agreed to **collaborate** on the government's project."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagdikit ng kamay sa isang bagay upang ito ay mapigilan, masuportahan, o makontrol; kapangyarihan o kontrol sa isang sitwasyon.
original_explanation: Ito yung ginagawa mo sa manibela ng jeep, sa strap ng bag mo sa MRT, at sa puso niya (sana all). It's not just holding, it's about control. 'Hawak ko ang oras ko,' says the freelancer. 'Hawak niya ako sa leeg,' says the person who is 'under the saya'.
usage_notes: Maaaring literal (pisikal na paghawak) o matalinhaga (kontrol, pag-aari).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang **hawak** niya sa kamay ng kanyang anak.","translation":"Her **hold** on her child's hand was tight."},{"sentence":"Nasa kanya ang **hawak** sa buong kumpanya.","translation":"He has **control** over the entire company."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga pinagbagsakan o mga tira-tirang materyales mula sa isang giniba o nasirang istruktura.
original_explanation: 'Yung mga pinagtibagan ng pader after a breakup... charot. It's the messy pile of broken concrete, wood, and metal you see after a building is demolished or after an earthquake. Basically, the physical manifestation of "wasak."
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa mga ulat-balita tungkol sa konstruksyon, demolisyon, o mga natural na kalamidad.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkalat ang mga **eskombro** sa daan matapos ang malakas na lindol.","translation":"**Debris** was scattered on the road after the strong earthquake."},{"sentence":"Inaalis ng mga construction worker ang **eskombro** mula sa ginigibang gusali.","translation":"The construction workers are clearing the **rubble** from the demolished building."}]

translation: to create, to invent, to fabricate
meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha, pag-imbento, o pagbuo ng isang bagay mula sa imahinasyon, tulad ng isang kuwento, tula, o kasinungalingan.
original_explanation: The verb form of "katha." Ito yung action of making something up. Pwedeng kathain mo ang pinakamagandang tula for your crush, or pwede mong kathain ang pinaka-creative na dahilan para 'di makasama sa family reunion. The power is in your hands (and your imagination).
usage_notes: Can be used for both creative works and for fabricating lies. The context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **kathain** ang isang awit tungkol sa kanyang karanasan.","translation":"She tried **to create** a song about her experience."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **kumatha** ng kuwento para lang makalusot.","translation":"Don't **fabricate** a story just to get away with it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking anyong tubig na napapaligiran ng lupa.
etymology: Mula sa Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *lawaq ("kalawakan, bukas na espasyo").
original_explanation: Nature's giant swimming pool, but with more mystery and potential for folklore creatures. It's where you go for a chill weekend getaway when you're tired of the beach's saltiness. Think Taal Lake, but with less volcanic activity and more "Ah, ang kalma."
usage_notes: Isang pangunahing katawagang heograpikal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Namingwit kami ng isda sa **Lawa** ng Laguna.","translation":"We fished in Laguna de Bay (**Lake** of Laguna)."},{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng tanawin sa paligid ng **lawa**.","translation":"The scenery around the **lake** is beautiful."}]

translation: to be able to consume/use up
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang ubusin o tapusin ang isang bagay, tulad ng pagkain, pera, o pasensya.
original_explanation: That feeling when you see a whole box of pizza and think, 'Challenge accepted.' It's your ability to finish something completely. Pwedeng pagkain, data allowance, or even pasensya ng magulang mo. 'Kahit isang buong lechon, kaya kong makaubos niyan!' The 'maka-' prefix here implies you have the potential or ability to do the 'ubos'-ing.
usage_notes: The `maka-` prefix here denotes ability or potential. 'Nakaubos' is the completed form (e.g., 'Nakaubos ako ng isang galon ng ice cream' - I was able to finish a gallon of ice cream).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ka **makakaubos** ng isang galon ng ice cream nang mag-isa!","translation":"You won't be **able to finish** a whole gallon of ice cream by yourself!"},{"sentence":"Ang bagong video game ay **makakaubos** ng iyong oras at pera.","translation":"The new video game will be **able to use up** your time and money."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang matindi at sakim na pagnanasa na magkamit o magmay-ari ng isang bagay, lalo na ang yaman o pag-aari ng iba.
original_explanation: This is that feeling when you see your friend's new iPhone and you suddenly *need* it, even if yours is working fine. It's the 'sana all' that has turned dark and obsessive. The opposite of 'contentment.'
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa mga kontekstong panrelihiyon o moral. Mas matindi ang kahulugan kaysa sa simpleng 'pagnanasa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang labis na **imbot** sa kayamanan ay nagdudulot ng kasamaan.","translation":"Excessive **greed** for wealth leads to evil."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa **imbot**, siniraan niya ang kanyang katrabaho.","translation":"Because of **covetousness**, he slandered his co-worker."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa paulit-ulit at marahang paggalaw o pag-indayog, karaniwan ng isang bagay na nakabitin o hindi matatag.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're in a hammock by the beach, or when you're in a bus on EDSA and it feels like the driver is trying to rock you to sleep... or to death. It's that gentle (or not-so-gentle) back-and-forth movement.
usage_notes: The repetition of "ugoy" emphasizes the continuous or repeated nature of the swaying.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Uguy-ugoy** ang tulay na kawayan kaya maingat kaming tumawid.","translation":"The bamboo bridge was **swaying** so we crossed carefully."},{"sentence":"Nakatulog ang sanggol sa **uguy-ugoy** ng duyan.","translation":"The baby fell asleep from the **swaying** of the cradle."}]

translation: every other; every second (day, week, etc.)
meaning_filipino: Isang pariralang pang-abay na nagsasaad ng pag-uulit sa bawat pangalawang yunit ng panahon, tulad ng araw, linggo, o buwan.
etymology: Isang parirala na binubuo ng 'tuwing' (bawat) at 'ikalawa' (pangalawa).
original_explanation: This is for things that don't happen every day, but also not just once a month. Like how often you *actually* go to the gym after your New Year's resolution. 'Every other week lang.' Or that payday schedule that isn't the 15th/30th. It's the rhythm of 'on again, off again' but for schedules.
usage_notes: The specific time unit (day, week, month) is usually understood from the context. 'Tuwing ikalawang araw' means every other day.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglalabas sila ng bagong episode **tuwing ikalawa** ng linggo.","translation":"They release a new episode **every other** week."},{"sentence":"Ang ulat ay kailangang isumite **tuwing ikalawa** ng buwan.","translation":"The report must be submitted on the **second** of every month."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng sinanay na tumulong sa mga ina sa panahon ng panganganak.
original_explanation: Sila yung original 'delivery service' bago pa nauso ang Grab at Lalamove. Noong wala pang malalaking ospital sa bawat kanto, ang komadrona ang superhero ng mga buntis sa probinsya. Sila ang unang nakakakita sa baby, armed with experience, tapang, at mainit na tubig.
usage_notes: The traditional term for a midwife, often associated with home births, especially in rural areas. The modern, professional term is simply 'midwife'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lola ko ay isang rispetadong **komadrona** sa aming bayan.","translation":"My grandmother was a respected **midwife** in our town."},{"sentence":"Tinawag nila ang **komadrona** nang magsimula nang mag-labor ang buntis.","translation":"They called the **midwife** when the pregnant woman started going into labor."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malawak at bukas na lugar sa isang bayan o lungsod, karaniwang napapaligiran ng mga gusali tulad ng simbahan at munisipyo, na nagsisilbing pook-tagpuan ng mga tao.
etymology: From `liwas` (to go around, to pass through) + `-an` (location suffix), referring to a central place people go to or pass through.
original_explanation: Before malls, this was the original "tambayan." It's the town plaza where everything happens – the fiesta, the political rally, the free Zumba class for titas, and the spot where teens go for their first awkward date. Think Luneta Park or Plaza Miranda.
usage_notes: A very common feature in Philippine town planning, inherited from Spanish colonial era design. The church, municipal hall, and main market are typically located around the liwasan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkita-kita ang magkakaibigan sa **liwasan** ng bayan.","translation":"The friends met up at the town **plaza**."},{"sentence":"Maraming nagtitinda ng street food sa gilid ng **liwasan** tuwing gabi.","translation":"Many street food vendors sell at the edge of the **square** every evening."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian o kalidad ng isang tunog o tinig na nagpapaiba nito sa iba, kahit na pareho ang tono at lakas.
original_explanation: This is what makes Regine Velasquez's voice different from Moira Dela Torre's. It’s not just the notes they hit, but the *quality* of the sound. It's the 'boses-ipis' vs 'boses-anghel' debate. It’s the texture of a voice—is it husky, breathy, clear, or raspy? That unique flavor is the 'timbre'.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa konteksto ng musika o tunog. Isang direktang hiram na salita.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kakaiba ang **timbre** ng boses ng mang-aawit na iyon.","translation":"The **timbre** of that singer's voice is unique."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manipis na piraso ng metal o ibang materyal na ipinapatong sa ibabaw ng isang bagay, karaniwan para sa proteksyon o palamuti.
original_explanation: Think of it like the "skin" or "case" you put on your phone. Hindi siya 'yung phone mismo, but it's the protective or decorative layer. Pwede ring parang 'yung gold plating sa alahas na peke – 'yung panlabas lang ang maganda, 'yun ang kalupkop.
usage_notes: Often refers to metal plating, inlay, or any thin decorative or protective covering.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang dibdib ng santo ay may **kalupkop** na pilak.","translation":"The saint's chest has a silver **overlay**."},{"sentence":"Natutuklap na ang **kalupkop** ng lumang baul.","translation":"The **veneer** of the old chest is already peeling."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pakiramdam ng labis na pagka-inaantok o pagnanais na matulog.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na 3 PM na sa office, tapos katatapos lang ng lunch, at biglang bumibigat ang talukap ng iyong mga mata. Ito yung kalaban mo sa pang-gabing shift o sa morning class pagkatapos mag-puyat sa K-drama. "Bes, kape tayo, tinatamaan na ako ng antok."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko mapigilan ang **antok** ko habang nagle-lecture ang propesor.","translation":"I couldn't fight my **sleepiness** while the professor was lecturing."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa gamot, nakaramdam siya ng matinding **antok**.","translation":"Because of the medicine, he felt extreme **drowsiness**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagpapaikli para sa pariralang Ingles na "be right back," na nangangahulugang "babalik ako kaagad." Ginagamit sa mga text o chat.
etymology: Acronym for the English phrase 'be right back'.
original_explanation: The classic chat message you send when your mom suddenly calls you to wash the dishes while you're in the middle of an intense online game. It's the digital version of "Sandali lang." "Guys, brb, tinatawag ako ni ermats."
usage_notes: Exclusively used in digital communication like texting, chatting, and gaming.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Wait lang, **brb**, oorder lang ako ng pagkain.","translation":"Wait, **brb**, I'm just going to order some food."}]

translation: the day after tomorrow; in a few days
meaning_filipino: Sa susunod na mga araw; sa araw pagkatapos ng bukas.
etymology: From `bukas` (tomorrow) and `makalawa` (after two days, a variant). Literally "tomorrow-after-two-days," but used to mean "the day after tomorrow" or more vaguely "in the near future."
original_explanation: The official deadline for things you keep procrastinating. "I'll do it bukas-makalawa" is the slightly more committed version of "I'll do it tomorrow," but let's be real, it's probably not happening then either. It's the 'mañana' habit, but stretched over a couple of days.
usage_notes: While it literally means "the day after tomorrow", it's often used more loosely to mean "in a few days" or "sometime soon."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magbabayad ako ng utang ko **bukas-makalawa**, pramis!","translation":"I'll pay my debt **the day after tomorrow**, I promise!"},{"sentence":"Darating ang order mo mula sa Shopee **bukas-makalawa**.","translation":"Your order from Shopee will arrive **in a few days**."}]
related: ["sa isang araw","sa susunod na araw","balang araw","bukas"]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagiging hindi matapat o paglabag sa tiwala ng isang tao, pangkat, o bansa.
original_explanation: That moment in your favorite teleserye when the best friend steals the boyfriend. Or when your officemate takes credit for your work. It's the ultimate "Et tu, Brute?" moment, Filipino style. The highest form of backstabbing.
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of personal relationships (infidelity), friendships, or national loyalty (treason).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagtataksil** sa bayan ay isang mabigat na krimen.","translation":"**Treason** against the country is a grave crime."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya mapapatawad ang **pagtataksil** ng kanyang kaibigan.","translation":"She cannot forgive her friend's **betrayal**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging apurado o mabilis sa pagkilos dahil sa kakulangan sa oras o kagustuhang matapos agad.
etymology: From pag- + the first syllable of mag- (ma-) + mag- + dali (hurry).
original_explanation: This is the official state of being for anyone commuting in Metro Manila during rush hour. It's that feeling when your Grab is 5 minutes away, you haven't finished your coffee, and your boss is already online on Teams. The opposite of 'chill lang'. It's the noun for 'dalian mo!'
usage_notes: Describes the state or act of rushing. Often carries a slightly negative connotation that mistakes can be made because of it.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa kanyang **pagmamadali**, naiwan niya ang kanyang wallet.","translation":"In his **haste**, he left his wallet."},{"sentence":"Walang mabuting idudulot ang **pagmamadali** sa paggawa ng mahahalagang desisyon.","translation":"Nothing good comes from **rushing** important decisions."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagpayag o pag-atas sa isang tao na bumalik o umuwi sa kanyang tahanan o pinagmulang lugar.
etymology: From pag- (nominalizer) + pa- (causative) + pa- (progressive aspect) + uwi (go home). Lit. 'the act of causing someone to go home'.
original_explanation: Yung moment na sinabi ng boss mo, 'Okay, uwian na!' after a long day of OT. O 'yung ginagawa ng gobyerno sa mga OFW na na-stranded sa ibang bansa. Pwede ring 'yung pag-aya mo sa lasing mong kaibigan na umuwi na kasi nagwawala na sa bar.
usage_notes: Can range from letting someone go home from work to formal government repatriation programs.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging mabilis ang proseso ng **pagpapauwi** sa mga na-stranded na turista.","translation":"The process of **repatriation** for the stranded tourists was quick."},{"sentence":"Ang maagang **pagpapauwi** sa mga empleyado ay dahil sa paparating na bagyo.","translation":"The early sending home of employees was due to the approaching typhoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay o palitan na pagtawag ng dalawa o higit pang tao sa isa't isa, kadalasan sa pamamagitan ng telepono.
original_explanation: The official sport of long-distance relationships and chismosa Titas coordinating their outfits for the next reunion. It's the reciprocal act of calling – "I call you, you call me." Before group chats, there was "magtawagan tayo mamaya."
usage_notes: This is a reciprocal verb, indicating that the action is done by the subjects to one another.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magtawagan** mamaya para planuhin ang ating bakasyon.","translation":"We need to **call each other** later to plan our vacation."},{"sentence":"Lagi silang **nagtawagan** noong nasa ibang bansa pa ang isa sa kanila.","translation":"They always **called each other** when one of them was still abroad."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng biglaang paggalaw o pag-urong at pagsulong, karaniwang may mabilis at maigsing puwersa.
etymology: Mula sa salitang ugat na "kadyot" na nangangahulugang biglaang pag-urong-sulong.
original_explanation: This is the motion your car makes when a newbie is learning stick shift. That sudden, embarrassing lurch forward? That's the car that kumadyot. It can also have... other, more vulgar connotations, but let's stick to the jeepney driver who suddenly brakes and sends everyone flying.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang pabigla-biglang galaw ng mga sasakyan. Mayroon itong bahagyang bastos o nakakatawang konotasyon depende sa konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Biglang **kumadyot** ang sinasakyan naming dyip kaya napasubsob kami.","translation":"The jeep we were riding suddenly **jerked**, causing us to fall forward."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong biglain ang preno para hindi **kumadyot** ang sasakyan.","translation":"Don't slam on the brakes so the car won't **jerk**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panghihina ng mga tuhod o katawan dahil sa matinding takot, gulat, o pagod, na parang isang malambot na gulay.
etymology: From `mang-` + `gulayin` (related to `gulay`, 'vegetable'), evoking the image of a limp vegetable.
original_explanation: That feeling when you almost trip down the stairs and your legs turn to instant ramen noodles. Or when your crush finally talks to you and you forget how to stand properly. Your body basically says 'Error 404: Bones not found.'
usage_notes: A very descriptive and somewhat informal term. It vividly captures the physical sensation of weakness or shock.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nanggulayin** ang mga tuhod niya nang makita ang multo.","translation":"His knees **turned to jelly** when he saw the ghost."},{"sentence":"Halos **manggulayin** ako sa pagod pagkatapos ng marathon.","translation":"I almost **felt my legs give way** from exhaustion after the marathon."}]

translation: with reservations; conditional; with a proviso
meaning_filipino: Naglalaman ng kondisyon o pag-aalinlangan; hindi lubos o walang pasubali.
original_explanation: This is how you say 'yes, but...' without actually saying 'but'. It's the 'I'll go to the party... *if* I finish my work' energy. Perfect for non-committal people. It's the fine print in your emotional contract.
usage_notes: Often used in legal, formal, or serious discussions to indicate that an agreement or statement is not absolute.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-apruba niya ay **may-pasubali**, kaya't basahin natin ang mga kondisyon.","translation":"His approval is **conditional**, so let's read the conditions."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtigil sa pag-iyak o paghikbi.
etymology: Maaaring kaugnay ng salitang-ugat ng 'tahanan', na nagpapahiwatig ng pagbabalik sa estado ng kapayapaan.
original_explanation: The magic word every parent, sibling, or jowa says to a crying person. 'Tahan na...' It's the verbal equivalent of a pat on the back, a hug, or being handed a tub of ice cream. It's the first step to 'Okay, now tell me the chismis.'
usage_notes: Halos palaging ginagamit bilang isang utos o pakiusap: 'Tahan na.' Ang anyong pawatas nito ay 'tumahan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pilit niyang pinatatahan ang sanggol, ngunit ayaw nitong **tumahan**.","translation":"He tried to make the baby stop crying, but it wouldn't **stop**."},{"sentence":"**Tahan** na, andito lang ako para sa'yo.","translation":"**Stop crying** now, I'm just here for you."}]

translation: to ask for a ride; to ride along
meaning_filipino: Ang paghiling na sumabay o sumakay sa likod ng isang sasakyan, karaniwan ay motorsiklo, o sa loob ng isang pribadong sasakyan.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "maki-" (paghiling ng pakikisali) at salitang ugat na "angkas" (pagsakay sa likod).
original_explanation: The ultimate 'save pamasahe' move. It's asking your officemate with a car, 'Pa-sabay naman hanggang kanto,' or yelling 'Maki-angkas!' to a friendly habal-habal driver. The currency is usually friendship, a shared Jollibee meal, or just plain kapal ng mukha.
usage_notes: Kadalasang tumutukoy sa pagsakay sa motorsiklo, ngunit maaari ring gamitin sa kahit anong uri ng pribadong sasakyan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pwede bang **makiangkas** sa motor mo hanggang sa palengke?","translation":"Can I **ride along** on your motorcycle to the market?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sukat ng pagiging malalim ng isang bagay, lugar, o kaisipan; ang pinakamalalim na bahagi.
original_explanation: This isn't just about how deep the swimming pool is. It's also for those 'deep talks' you have at 3 AM. *Kalaliman* can be the scary, dark part of the ocean, or the profoundness of a poem, or the depth of your *hugot* after a breakup. It's 'deep' in every sense of the word.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for physical depth or figuratively for emotional or intellectual depth.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natatakot siyang lumangoy sa **kalaliman** ng dagat.","translation":"He is afraid to swim in the **depths** of the sea."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko maabot ang **kalaliman** ng kanyang mga salita.","translation":"I cannot grasp the **profundity** of his words."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng isang matunog at matinis na tunog, karaniwan mula sa isang kampana o katulad na bagay kapag tinamaan.
etymology: From mag- (verb prefix) + bagting (a sharp, resonant sound).
original_explanation: Think of the church bell ringing for Simbang Gabi, or that old-school school bell signaling recess. 'Magbagting' is the action of making that distinct, sharp, reverberating sound. It's the OG notification sound before smartphones existed.
usage_notes: Often associated with bells, especially church bells.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **magbagting** ang kampana ng simbahan, hudyat na mag-uumpisa na ang misa.","translation":"The church bell began to **toll**, signaling that the mass was about to start."},{"sentence":"Naririnig mo bang **magbagting** ang telepono sa kabilang kwarto?","translation":"Do you hear the telephone **ringing** in the other room?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kultura at anyo ng sining na nagsimula noong dekada 1970 sa mga African American, na binubuo ng mga elemento tulad ng rap, DJing, breakdancing, at sining-graffiti.
etymology: Hiram na salita mula sa Ingles na 'hip-hop'.
original_explanation: What happens when poetry meets a sick beat. It's the culture that gave us rap battles (FlipTop!), breakdancing, cool graffiti art, and a whole lot of drip. It's more than just music; it's a whole vibe, from Gloc-9 to Shanti Dope.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa kontekstong Filipino upang tukuyin ang parehong pandaigdigang genre ng musika at kultura.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang makinig sa musikang **hiphop** mula pa noong bata siya.","translation":"He has loved listening to **hip-hop** music since he was a child."},{"sentence":"Sumali siya sa isang kompetisyon ng sayaw na **hiphop**.","translation":"He joined a **hip-hop** dance competition."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng maingat na pagtingin o pagsusuri sa isang bagay na malabo o nakikita sa pamamagitan ng repleksyon; maaari ding tumukoy sa malalim na pag-iisip o pagninilay.
original_explanation: That moment you stare at your reflection in a puddle after it rains, feeling all dramatic and full of hugot. It's about seeing something faintly or through a medium, like trying to see the fish below the water's surface. Metaphorically, it's 'discernment' – trying to see the truth in a murky situation, like figuring out if your crush's 'seen' was intentional or accidental.
usage_notes: Carries a dual meaning of literal, faint visibility and metaphorical, deep understanding or introspection.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa **pag-aninaw** sa tubig, nakita niya ang kanyang anino.","translation":"In **looking at the reflection** in the water, he saw his shadow."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng malalim na **pag-aninaw** upang maunawaan ang tunay na isyu.","translation":"Deep **discernment** is needed to understand the real issue."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng pahintulot na gamitin ang isang ari-arian, karaniwan ay lupa, kapalit ng regular na bayad sa loob ng isang takdang panahon.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate Tita move when you have a vacant lot. Instead of selling it, you **ipaarenda** it to a company for their parking lot or to a farmer. It's passive income, 'ika nga. It's more formal and long-term than 'ipaarkila,' which is for your condo or car.
usage_notes: Primarily used for leasing agricultural land or large plots of property for a significant period, often involving a formal contract.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Plano nilang **ipaarenda** ang kanilang bukirin sa isang malaking korporasyon.","translation":"They plan **to lease out** their farmland to a big corporation."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng nagmula sa o mamamayan ng ibang bansa; dayuhan.
original_explanation: The female version of 'estranghero'. This is what you call a foreign woman. She could be a tourist asking for directions to the nearest Jollibee, an expat who's been living in BGC for years, or the leading lady in a teleserye who just arrived from America to claim her inheritance. The male counterpart is 'estranghero'.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to a female. The gender-neutral term is 'dayuhan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **estranghera** ang nagtatanong kung saan ang pinakamalapit na palengke.","translation":"A **female foreigner** is asking where the nearest market is."},{"sentence":"Maraming **estranghera** ang nahuhumaling sa ganda ng mga isla sa Pilipinas.","translation":"Many **foreign women** are captivated by the beauty of the islands in the Philippines."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pahiwatig o paramdam na hindi tuwirang sinasabi; isang parunggit.
original_explanation: This is the art of 'parinig.' It's when your mom says, 'Ang dumi naman ng sahig,' when she really means, 'Magwalis ka na!' It's that FB status from your friend that's *totally* not about you, but you know it is. A *pahibat* is a sniper shot in a conversation—indirect but aimed.
usage_notes: Often carries a slightly negative or critical connotation, similar to 'parinig'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **pahibat** ang kanyang mga sinabi tungkol sa dati niyang kasama.","translation":"His words were full of **insinuations** about his former colleague."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko nakuha agad ang **pahibat** niya na kailangan na naming umalis.","translation":"I didn't immediately get his **hint** that we needed to leave."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging mabait; ang pagpapakita ng kagandahang-loob, habag, at pag-unawa sa kapwa.
original_explanation: This is the lola who gives you extra ulam, the security guard who greets you with a smile every morning, or the stranger who tells you your zipper is down. Kabaitan is goodness in action, the "Pusong Pinoy" spirit. It's the reason you say "Salamat, po" even when the jeepney driver is grumpy. It's a core value, the opposite of "kasamaan" or "pagka-Marites."
usage_notes: A fundamental concept in Filipino values.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinamalas niya ang kanyang **kabaitan** sa pagtulong sa mga nangangailangan.","translation":"She showed her **kindness** by helping those in need."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong abusuhin ang **kabaitan** ng iyong mga magulang.","translation":"Do not abuse the **kindness** of your parents."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manunulat na dalubhasa sa paglikha ng mga sanaysay, na siyang pormal o di-pormal na pagtalakay sa isang partikular na paksa.
etymology: Mula sa `mang-` + `sanaysay` (essay). Ang `mang-` ay nagiging `manan-` at inuulit ang unang pantig ng salitang-ugat.
original_explanation: Ito yung pinsan ni `mananalaysay` (historian) na mas focused sa "hugot" at opinion. Sila 'yung nagsusulat ng mga long post sa Facebook na may sense, o 'yung mga columnists sa dyaryo na binabasa mo habang nagkakape. They make a living out of their well-structured opinions.
usage_notes: Ito ay iba sa `mananalaysay` (historian/narrator). Ang `mananaysay` ay partikular na nagsusulat ng mga `sanaysay` (essays).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinilala ang **mananaysay** dahil sa kanyang matalas na kritisismo sa lipunan.","translation":"The **essayist** was recognized for his sharp social criticism."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalapat ng labatiba o enema sa isang tao o hayop upang linisin ang bituka.
original_explanation: This is a medical procedure, but in Pinoy humor, it's a threat. When someone's full of... well, you know... someone might joke, "Gusto mo **labatibahin** kita?" It's the ultimate 'cleanse your soul' (and your intestines) threat.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa kontekstong medikal, ngunit maaaring gamitin nang pasobra o bilang isang biro.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **labatibahin** ang pasyente bago ang operasyon.","translation":"The patient needs **to be given an enema** before the surgery."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasabit ng mga damit o anumang tela sa sampayan upang matuyo.
original_explanation: The final boss of laundry day. After washing and rinsing, you need to 'isampay' everything on the 'sampayan' (clothesline). It's a race against the sun, hoping everything dries before it rains again. This is a core memory for every Filipino kid who's been told 'Isampay mo na 'yang mga nilabhan!'
usage_notes: Specifically used for hanging items, usually clothes, on a line or rack to dry.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakitapos **isampay** ang mga tuwalya bago umulan.","translation":"Please finish **hanging** the towels to dry before it rains."},{"sentence":"Maingat niyang **isinampay** ang barong na isusuot niya bukas.","translation":"He carefully **hung** the barong he will wear tomorrow."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagdudulot ng pagkabalisa, pag-aalala, o hindi mapakaling pakiramdam; nasa anyong pangnagdaan.
original_explanation: That feeling you get at 3 AM when you remember an embarrassing thing you did in high school. Or when a vague text from your boss ('We need to talk.') ruins your whole weekend. It's the past tense of something causing you anxiety or worry.
usage_notes: Often refers to something that weighs on one's mind or conscience. The noun 'bagabag' itself means anxiety or deep worry.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumagabag** sa kanyang isipan ang masamang panaginip.","translation":"The bad dream **troubled** his mind."},{"sentence":"Ang sinabi mo kanina ay **bumagabag** sa aking kalooban.","translation":"What you said earlier **bothered** my conscience."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng gawgaw na mula sa mais, karaniwang ginagamit bilang pampalapot sa mga sarsa, sabaw, at panghimagas.
original_explanation: Yung puting powder na magic ingredient ni nanay para lumapot yung sauce ng ulam o yung gravy ng fried chicken. Akala mo harina pero hindi. Eto rin yung sikreto sa malutong na coating ng calamares.
usage_notes: Often pronounced locally as "kon-starch".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagyan mo ng **cornstarch** na tinunaw sa tubig para lumapot ang sarsa.","translation":"Add some **cornstarch** dissolved in water to thicken the sauce."},{"sentence":"Kulang tayo sa **cornstarch** para sa Bicol Express.","translation":"We don't have enough **cornstarch** for the Bicol Express."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang panlabas na balot o takip na nagsisilbing proteksyon sa isang bagay, tulad ng sa buto, prutas, o talim.
original_explanation: Think of it as nature's packaging. The husk of corn, the sheath of a blade, or the protective covering of a seed. It's the 'balat' but for specific natural things. Parang 'yung shell mo, 'yung panlabas na anyo na nagtatago sa tunay mong nararamdaman. Hugot!
usage_notes: Kadalasan itong ginagamit kasama ng isa pang pangngalan upang maging tiyak, halimbawa, 'talukap ng mais'. Ang pinakakaraniwang paggamit nito ay sa pariralang 'talukap ng mata'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maingat niyang inalis ang **talukap** ng mais bago ito inihaw.","translation":"He carefully removed the **husk** of the corn before grilling it."},{"sentence":"Ang **talukap** ng espada ay gawa sa mamahaling kahoy.","translation":"The **sheath** of the sword is made of expensive wood."}]

translation: a call (in card games), a bid
meaning_filipino: Sa mga laro ng baraha, ito ang tawag o hudyat ng isang manlalaro upang ipahiwatig ang kanyang gagawing galaw, taya, o deklarasyon.
original_explanation: This is what your tito shouts during a heated game of 'tong-its' or 'pusoy dos' after a few beers. It's the moment of truth, the "All in!" of the Pinoy card table. The more dramatic the liyamada, the more intense the game.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in the context of card games or similar bidding games.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malakas na **liyamada** ang kanyang binitawan bago ilapag ang mga baraha.","translation":"He made a loud **call** before laying down the cards."},{"sentence":"Ano ang **liyamada** mo? Tatawag ka ba o tatalon?","translation":"What's your **bid**? Are you going to call or fold?"}]

translation: to be able to go first; to get ahead
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng pagkakataon o kakayahang mauna sa isang pila, karera, o anumang sitwasyon.
original_explanation: Your superpower during a 12.12 sale. It's the ability to check out your cart before everyone else, or to be the first one in the jeepney to get the best seat. In life, it's about getting that first-mover advantage. 'Sana makauna ako sa pila para sa libreng pa-kape.'
usage_notes: The `maka-` prefix denotes ability or opportunity. 'Nakauna' is the completed form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumising ka nang maaga para **makauna** ka sa pagpila.","translation":"Wake up early so you can **be first** in line."},{"sentence":"Sino kaya ang **makakauna** sa pag-solve ng puzzle?","translation":"I wonder who will be **able to be the first** to solve the puzzle?"}]

meaning_filipino: 1. Lagyan ng sabon ang isang tao o bagay. 2. (Idyomatiko) Pagsabihan o pagalitan nang matindi.
original_explanation: Literal meaning: what you do to a dog on bath day. Figurative meaning: what your boss does to you when you mess up a big project. It's a verbal 'washing' or 'cleansing' that is NOT refreshing at all. 'Naku, sinabunan ako ni Ma'am kanina!' means you got an epic lecture, not a free bath.
usage_notes: The context determines whether the literal (to apply soap) or figurative (to scold) meaning is intended. The figurative sense is very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **sabunan** maigi ang iyong mga kamay para matanggal ang mikrobyo.","translation":"You need to **soap** your hands well to remove the germs."},{"sentence":"**Sinabunan** siya ng kanyang ina dahil gabi na siyang umuwi.","translation":"His mother **scolded** him because he came home late at night."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng isang lalaki na pakikipag-ugnayan sa maraming babae, lalo na kung siya ay mayroon nang kasintahan o asawa.
original_explanation: The act of collecting '2-gives' like they're Funko Pops. It's when a guy's side-chick has a side-chick. This is the verb form of being a walking red flag.
usage_notes: Refers to the act of cheating on a partner with other women or generally pursuing multiple women romantically. The completed form is `nambabae`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nangako siyang hindi na **mambababae** matapos silang magkabalikan ng asawa niya.","translation":"He promised not to **womanize** anymore after he and his wife got back together."},{"sentence":"Nabalitaan kong **nambabae** na naman daw ang asawa ni Aling Nena.","translation":"I heard that Aling Nena's husband is **womanizing** again."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa bawat indibidwal sa loob ng isang grupo; bawat isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: The more emphatic version of "bawa't". It’s like when the teacher says "Class, listen!" and no one does, so she switches to "Okay, **bawa't isa** sa inyo, makinig!" You know it's serious now. It singles everyone out, together. The ultimate paradox.
usage_notes: Functions as a pronoun phrase. Emphasizes individuality within a group more strongly than just "bawa't".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bawa't isa** sa kanila ay nagsumite ng proyekto.","translation":"**Each one** of them submitted a project."},{"sentence":"Mananagot ang **bawa't isa** sa kanilang mga ginawa.","translation":"**Everyone** will be held accountable for their actions."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o ahente ng awtoridad na may kapangyarihang kumpiskahin o kunin ang mga bagay na ilegal o ipinagbabawal.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "taga-" (tagagawa) at salitang-ugat na "samsam" (kumpiska).
original_explanation: The MMDA officer who takes your license, the customs agent checking for undeclared pasalubong, or your mom who confiscates your phone 'pag 'di ka pa natutulog at 2 AM. They take things, legally or... with motherly authority.
usage_notes: Madalas itong may negatibong konotasyon o tumutukoy sa isang taong may awtoridad.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinatakutan ng mga tindero ang pagdating ng mga **tagasamsam** ng paninda.","translation":"The vendors feared the arrival of the merchandise **confiscators**."},{"sentence":"Nagtago ang mga bata dahil may mga **tagasamsam** daw ng alagang hayop sa lugar.","translation":"The children hid because there were supposedly pet **seizers** in the area."}]

meaning_filipino: Itutok o iasinta ang isang bagay, tulad ng baril o tingin, sa isang partikular na target o layon.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're playing Mobile Legends and you lock onto the enemy hero with the lowest HP. That's `ipuntirya`. It can also be figurative, like when a marites ipupuntirya ka at gagawan ng chismis. "Focus, guys! Ipuntirya natin ang ADC nila!"
usage_notes: Can be used literally for aiming a weapon or camera, or figuratively for targeting a person or goal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ipuntirya** mo nang maigi ang kamera sa ibon bago mo kunan ng litrato.","translation":"**Aim** the camera carefully at the bird before you take a picture."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ipuntirya** sa akin ang sisi.","translation":"Don't **target** me with the blame."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang propesyon o gawain ng pag-aalaga sa mga maysakit, sugatan, o matatanda, lalo na sa ilalim ng pangangasiwa ng isang doktor.
original_explanation: The profession that has probably sent half of the Philippines abroad. It's the art and science of caring for the sick, which every Filipino family has at least one practitioner of. It's a career path, a calling, and for many, a ticket to a better life.
usage_notes: Halos palaging tumutukoy sa propesyong medikal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha siya ng kursong **Nursing** para makapagtrabaho sa ibang bansa.","translation":"She took a **Nursing** course to be able to work abroad."},{"sentence":"Ang tamang pag-aalaga ay mahalaga sa larangan ng **nursing**.","translation":"Proper care is important in the field of **nursing**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang marka o mantsa na dulot ng pagpahid ng isang bagay na marumi.
original_explanation: That random smudge you get on your shirt after squeezing into a crowded jeepney. It can also be metaphorical, like the stain on your reputation after some juicy 'chismis' makes the rounds. 'May lahid na,' as they say.
usage_notes: Often used for literal stains but can also be used metaphorically for a stain on one's reputation or character.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **lahid** ng tsokolate ang kaniyang pisngi.","translation":"There's a **smear** of chocolate on his cheek."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang linisin ang **lahid** sa kanyang pangalan.","translation":"He is trying to clear the **stain** on his name."}]

meaning_filipino: Pilitin o himukin ang isang tao o grupo na sumuko o tumigil sa paglaban.
original_explanation: The ultimate goal in any conflict, from a police standoff to arguing with your mom. You want to make the other party wave the white flag. 'Pinapasuko na kita, umamin ka na lang na ikaw umubos ng ulam!' It's about breaking their will to fight, whether through force, logic, or an overwhelming barrage of 'I told you so.'
usage_notes: This is the object-focused verb. The person being made to surrender is the object.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng mga pulis na **pasukuin** ang mga magnanakaw.","translation":"The police tried to **make the robbers surrender**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpatalo; huwag kang papayag na **pasukuin** ka nila.","translation":"Don't lose; don't allow them to **make you surrender**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gumagalaw na hagdanan na mekanikal na nagdadala ng mga tao pataas o pababa sa pagitan ng mga palapag ng isang gusali.
original_explanation: The moving stairs in the mall you were probably scared of as a kid. It's the lazy person's alternative to taking the actual stairs. Also, the place where you awkwardly try not to make eye contact with the person coming from the opposite direction. "Dito tayo sa escalator, bes, tinatamad ako mag-hagdan."
usage_notes: Walang katumbas na salita sa Tagalog kaya direktang hiniram mula sa Ingles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging puno ng tao ang **escalator** tuwing Sabado sa mall.","translation":"The **escalator** is always full of people every Saturday at the mall."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa pag-apak sa **escalator** para hindi maipit.","translation":"Be careful when stepping onto the **escalator** to avoid getting stuck."}]

translation: a probe; act of scooping with a pointed object
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagdukot o pagkuha ng isang bagay mula sa isang masikip na butas o espasyo gamit ang isang matulis na instrumento.
original_explanation: Think of getting that last bit of *ulam* stuck in the corner of a *tupperware*, or trying to fish out a piece of meat stuck between your teeth with a toothpick. That action of digging/prying/scooping something out of a tight spot is *sungkad*. It’s a precision operation, often done with intense focus.
usage_notes: Often associated with using a stick, fork, or finger to get something out. The verb form is 'sungkarin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **sungkad** lang ng tinidor, nakuha na niya ang karne sa loob ng buto.","translation":"With just one **probe** of the fork, he got the meat from inside the bone."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang palito para sa **sungkad** ng tinga sa kanyang ngipin.","translation":"He used the toothpick to **scoop** out the food particle from his teeth."}]

translation: to put a dot or mark on; to punctuate
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng tuldok, bantas, o anumang maliit na marka sa isang bagay, lalo na sa pagsusulat.
original_explanation: This is the act of putting a dot on it, literally. Like putting the dot on the 'i' or the 'j'. In a broader sense, it's about adding punctuation. It's the grammar police's favorite verb. 'Hoy, **titikan** mo 'yang dulo ng pangungusap mo!'
usage_notes: Related to 'tuldok' (period/dot). Less common in everyday speech than 'lagyan ng tuldok' or 'lagyan ng bantas'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **titikan** ang letrang 'i' at 'j'.","translation":"Don't forget to **dot** the letters 'i' and 'j'."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **titikan** nang maayos ang iyong sanaysay para madaling basahin.","translation":"You need to **punctuate** your essay properly so it's easy to read."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang karamdaman na malubha, mapanganib, o may malaking epekto sa kalusugan at buhay ng isang tao.
original_explanation: This isn't your 'a-sip-of-flat-soda-will-fix-it' kind of sakit. This is the teleserye-level illness, the one that requires a family meeting, selling the carabao, and a lot of crying scenes. It's the 'Stage 4' of illnesses, both literally and figuratively.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang parirala, hindi iisang salita. Ang 'mabigat' ay literal na nangangahulugang 'heavy'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming nag-alala nang malaman nilang may **sakit na mabigat** ang kanilang lola.","translation":"Many were worried when they found out their grandmother has a **serious illness**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng malaking pondo para sa pagpapagamot ng isang **sakit na mabigat**.","translation":"A large fund is needed for the treatment of a **grave disease**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kondisyong medikal kung saan naninilaw ang balat, mga mata, at mucous membranes dahil sa mataas na antas ng bilirubin sa dugo.
etymology: From "paninilaw" (yellowing), which comes from "dilaw" (yellow), and the phrase "ng balat" (of the skin).
original_explanation: Literally 'yellowing of the skin.' This is what happens to newborns sometimes, or when someone has a liver problem. It's a medical symptom, not a fashion statement. Your body is basically turning into a human highlighter pen, and it's a sign you need to see a doctor ASAP.
usage_notes: A specific medical term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paninilaw ng balat** ay maaaring sintomas ng sakit sa atay.","translation":"**Jaundice** can be a symptom of liver disease."},{"sentence":"Dinala sa ospital ang sanggol dahil sa **paninilaw ng balat**.","translation":"The baby was brought to the hospital because of **yellowing of the skin**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagdudulot ng pagkasawa o umay, lalo na sa labis na katamisan o paulit-ulit na karanasan.
etymology: From `suya` (satiation, being fed up). `Nakasusu-` indicates the ability to cause this feeling.
original_explanation: Alam mo yung dessert na sa unang subo, "Wow, sarap!" pero sa pangatlong subo, "Suko na 'ko, teh"? That's **nakasusuya**. Pwede ring sa tao. Yung sobrang sweet na couple sa feed mo, na sa una kinikilig ka pa pero 'pag araw-araw na, **nakasusuya** na. Parang "Okay, we get it, you're in love." Too much of a good thing.
usage_notes: Often associated with overly sweet food (`umay`) but also very commonly used for tiresome or annoying situations/people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masyadong matamis ang cake, **nakasusuya** nang kainin.","translation":"The cake is too sweet, it's become **cloying** to eat."},{"sentence":"**Nakasusuya** na ang kanyang paulit-ulit na mga dahilan.","translation":"His repetitive excuses have become **tiresome**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking domestikadong mamal na may kuko sa paa (ungulate), ginagamit sa pagsakay, paghila ng kargada, at karera.
original_explanation: Before GrabCar, there was the 'kabayo'. Now, it's a term of endearment for your friend with a long face (just kidding... mostly), or what you call someone who works tirelessly ('parang kabayo'). Also, the star of every town fiesta's 'kalesa'.
usage_notes: Can be used metaphorically to describe someone who is hardworking or has a long face.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marunong siyang sumakay sa **kabayo**.","translation":"He knows how to ride a **horse**."},{"sentence":"Nagtratrabaho siya na parang **kabayo** para sa kanyang pamilya.","translation":"She works like a **horse** for her family."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing maamo o sanay sa tao ang isang hayop; paamuin.
original_explanation: This is what you try to do to your fierce-looking but actually sweet-hearted boss. It's also what pet owners do to their new furbabies, training them not to bite the new furniture or the guests. 'Mansahin' is the verb form of making something 'manso' or tame.
usage_notes: Often used for animals. Can be used figuratively for people, meaning to win over or make someone more agreeable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **mansahin** ang pusang kalye na sanay na sa labas.","translation":"It's difficult to **tame** a street cat that's used to the outdoors."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang **mansahin** ang kanyang biyenan sa pamamagitan ng masarap na pagkain.","translation":"She's trying to **win over** her mother-in-law with delicious food."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa karne o anumang sangkap na idinaan sa proseso ng paggiling upang maging pino.
original_explanation: The ultimate ulam starter pack. Pork giniling, beef giniling... it's the foundation of Pinoy favorites like lumpia, arroz a la cubana, and that picadillo your tita brings to every party. It's the 'pwede na 'to' meal for a busy day, but also the star of the handaan. Versatile like a true Pinoy.
usage_notes: Usually refers to meat (pork or beef) but can be used for other ground ingredients. The word itself is the past participle of 'giling' (to grind), but it's most commonly used as a noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili ka ng kalahating kilong **giniling** na baboy sa palengke.","translation":"Buy half a kilo of **ground** pork at the market."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang tortang talong kung may palamang **giniling**.","translation":"Eggplant omelette is delicious if it has a **ground meat** filling."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bahagi ng isang makina, kasangkapan, o anumang mas malaking kabuuan.
original_explanation: 'Yung kulang na piyesa ng makina ng kotse mo kaya ayaw umandar, parang 'yung kulang sa buhay mo kaya 'di ka maka-move on. It's that specific spare part you have to hunt for in Banawe or Quiapo just to get something working again.
usage_notes: Commonly used for mechanical or electronic parts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap hanapin ang **piyesa** para sa lumang modelong iyon ng sasakyan.","translation":"It's hard to find the **part** for that old model of car."},{"sentence":"Nasira ang isang mahalagang **piyesa** ng computer kaya hindi ito gumagana.","translation":"An important **component** of the computer broke, which is why it's not working."}]

translation: to let someone smoke; to cause someone to smoke
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng pagkakataon o pag-udyok sa isang tao na humitit o suminghot ng usok, karaniwan mula sa sigarilyo o anumang katulad nito.
etymology: From mag- (actor-focus verb prefix) + pa- (causative prefix) + hitit (to puff, to smoke).
original_explanation: This is when you offer a cigarette to a friend, "Yosi break muna tayo, pre." Or, more negatively, it's when someone pressures another person to start smoking. It's the verb form of "share a stick" or "peer pressure in a puff."
usage_notes: Often used in the context of smoking cigarettes, but can also refer to other inhaled substances.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magpahitit** sa mga bata.","translation":"Don't **let** the children **smoke**."},{"sentence":"**Nagpahitit** siya ng isang stick sa kanyang kaibigan na stressed.","translation":"He **let** his stressed friend **have a puff** from a stick (of cigarette)."}]

translation: to force; to compel; to insist
meaning_filipino: Gawin ang isang bagay nang labag sa kalooban ng isang tao; igiit ang isang bagay sa kabila ng pagtutol.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'pilit'. This is what your nanay does when she wants you to sing for the guests, or what you do to your friend para samahan ka sa K-pop concert. It's the art of 'convincing' someone against their will, often with a mix of emotional blackmail and the promise of libre. 'Sige na, please? Pilitin mo na siyang sumama!'
usage_notes: Often used to express coercion or strong persuasion. The object of the verb is the person being forced.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pilitin** ang bata na kumain kung ayaw niya.","translation":"Don't **force** the child to eat if they don't want to."},{"sentence":"**Pilitin** mo siyang sabihin ang totoo.","translation":"**Compel** him to tell the truth."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalagyan ng tabako o sigarilyo; isang babaeng gumagawa o nagbebenta ng tabako.
etymology: From Spanish 'tabaquera' (cigar case, or a woman who works with tobacco).
original_explanation: Before vaping became a thing, this was the accessory. It's either the fancy case for your lolo's cigars, or the woman rolling them expertly, probably gossiping with the other tabakeras.
usage_notes: This word has two distinct but related meanings. Context is key to differentiate between the object and the person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inilabas niya ang gintong **tabakera** mula sa kanyang bulsa.","translation":"He took out the golden **cigar case** from his pocket."},{"sentence":"Isang tanyag na **tabakera** sa kanilang bayan si Aling Nena.","translation":"Aling Nena was a famous **female cigar maker** in their town."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain o propesyon ng pagsusulat para sa mga pahayagan, magasin, o pagbabalita sa radyo at telebisyon. Ito rin ay ang akto ng pagpapahayag o paglalathala ng impormasyon sa publiko.
etymology: From pa- + mam- (from ma- + hayag) + hayag. The root word is 'hayag', meaning 'to reveal' or 'proclaim'.
original_explanation: This is the world of journalism, news reporting, and broadcasting. Think of your favorite chismosa tita, but make it professional with a press ID. From hard-hitting news that topples governments to the latest showbiz scoop, if it's being reported, it's pamamahayag. It's the 'Freedom of the Press' you hear about.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of press freedom ('kalayaan sa pamamahayag') and media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang malayang **pamamahayag** ay haligi ng isang matatag na demokrasya.","translation":"A free **press** is a pillar of a strong democracy."},{"sentence":"Kumuha siya ng kursong **pamamahayag** sa unibersidad.","translation":"She took up a course in **journalism** at the university."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahan o kilos ng paggamit ng bibig at tinig upang makabuo ng mga salita at makipag-usap.
original_explanation: It's that thing you have to do in meetings even when it could have been an email. It's the "daldal" with your friends, the "sermon" from your parents, and the "presentation" for your boss. Basically, any time you open your mouth to make words come out.
usage_notes: A fundamental human action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahihirapan siya sa **pagsasalita** sa harap ng maraming tao.","translation":"He has difficulty with **speaking** in front of many people."},{"sentence":"Ang malayang **pagsasalita** ay isang karapatang pantao.","translation":"Free **speech** is a human right."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-alis ng dumi, basa, o alikabok sa isang ibabaw o sa sarili gamit ang tela, papel, o kamay.
original_explanation: The go-to action for almost any mess in the Philippines. Spilled coffee? Magpunas ka. Pawis? Magpunas ka. Dusty table? Magpunas ka. It's the universal solution, usually involving a basahan (rag) of questionable origin. Also, what you do to your face with a tissue after eating at Jollibee.
usage_notes: Can mean wiping a surface ('magpunas ng mesa') or wiping oneself ('magpunas ng pawis').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"\"Pakisabi sa bata na **magpunas** ng kanyang bibig pagkatapos kumain.\"","translation":"\"Please tell the child to **wipe** his mouth after eating.\""},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **magpunas** ng alikabok sa mga gamit.","translation":"I need to **wipe** the dust off the furniture."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay o paulit-ulit na paggalaw ng mga pakpak, kamay, o anumang katulad nito.
etymology: From `mag-` (actor-focus prefix) + `ka-` (repetitive/sudden action prefix) + `kawag` (to flap, wag).
original_explanation: Yung eksena sa concert ng paborito mong banda, lahat kayo sabay-sabay magkakawag ng kamay sa ere. O 'yung mga ibon na sabay-sabay lumilipad, parang synchronized swimmers ng kalangitan.
usage_notes: The `magka-` prefix here implies a sudden, collective, or repeated action rather than a state of being.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **magkakawag** ang mga manonood nang lumabas ang artista.","translation":"The audience started to **wave their hands repeatedly** when the celebrity came out."},{"sentence":"Nang marinig ang putok, nag-unahan sa paglipad at **pagkakawag** ng pakpak ang mga ibon.","translation":"When they heard the bang, the birds scrambled to fly, **flapping their wings**."}]

meaning_filipino: Kalagayan ng matinding hirap, pagdurusa, o karukhaan; pagiging kahabag-habag.
original_explanation: This isn't just 'petsa de peligro' level of broke. This is rock bottom. It's the feeling of having ₱20 left and your next sahod is still a week away, but times a thousand. It's a state of utter misery and hardship you wouldn't wish on your worst enemy (or maybe you would, depends on the ex).
usage_notes: A very strong, literary, and formal word for suffering. Often found in classic literature and formal speeches.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais nilang makaahon mula sa **kaduhaginan**.","translation":"They want to rise from **misery**."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga akda ay sumasalamin sa **kaduhaginan** ng mga naaapi.","translation":"His works reflect the **wretchedness** of the oppressed."}]

translation: to crumple; to tangle; to mess up
meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang paglukot o paggulo sa isang bagay, tulad ng papel o damit, upang mawala ang kinis at kaayusan nito.
original_explanation: The official verb for what happens to your earphones in your pocket, your bedsheets after a nap, and your freshly ironed uniform two seconds after putting it on. It can also be used for complicating things. "Huwag mo nang gusutin ang isyu" means "Don't complicate the issue," or basically, "Stop making things messy!"
usage_notes: The root word 'gusot' (adj.) means crumpled or tangled. 'Gusutin' is the act of making something crumpled or tangled.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, huwag mong **gusutin** ang mga damit na bagong plantsa.","translation":"Please, don't **crumple** the newly ironed clothes."},{"sentence":"Sinadya niyang **gusutin** ang buhok niya para magmukhang 'effortless'.","translation":"She intentionally **messed up** her hair to look 'effortless'."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat o kalipunan ng mga tao, bagay, o ideya na mayroong pagkakatulad o magkakaugnay na layunin.
original_explanation: 'Yung mga kaibigan mo sa group chat na laging present sa kalokohan pero 'seen' lang 'pag may kailangan kang tulong. From project groupmates to your 'tropa' sa inuman, 'yan ang grupo.
usage_notes: Widely used in all contexts, both formal and informal. Often used interchangeably with the native word 'pangkat'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumali ako sa isang **grupo** ng mga manunulat.","translation":"I joined a **group** of writers."},{"sentence":"Ang aming **grupo** ang nanalo sa patimpalak.","translation":"Our **group** won the contest."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang proseso ng pagkuha ng sampol mula sa ilong o lalamunan gamit ang isang mahaba at malambot na pamunas para sa medikal na pagsusuri, partikular na para sa COVID-19.
original_explanation: The most iconic accessory of the 2020s. That long cotton bud that goes way up your nose and makes your ancestors feel it. Getting a **swab** test became the new 'are you clean?' for travel, work, and even family gatherings.
usage_notes: Ang salitang ito ay naging pang-araw-araw na termino sa Pilipinas dahil sa pandemya ng COVID-19.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng negatibong resulta ng **swab** test bago makapasok sa opisina.","translation":"A negative **swab** test result is required before entering the office."},{"sentence":"Nakakakiliti ang pakiramdam ng **swab** sa ilong.","translation":"The feeling of the **swab** in the nose is ticklish."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangatnig na ginagamit upang magpakita ng konsesyon o pag-amin na ang isang bagay ay totoo o maaaring mangyari, ngunit hindi nito binabago ang kasunod na pahayag.
etymology: Possibly from Sanskrit 'kacit' (कचित्), meaning 'somewhere, anywhere, perhaps'.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'no excuses' word. It's what you say to push through. '**Kahit** umuulan, tutuloy ako sa concert.' It's the official word of the martyr, the determined, and the person who just really wants that milk tea. '**Kahit** malayo, pupuntahan kita.' #Hugot
usage_notes: Often followed by 'na' (kahit na) without a significant change in meaning. It can also mean 'any' when combined with interrogative words, such as 'kahit sino' (anyone), 'kahit ano' (anything), or 'kahit saan' (anywhere).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kahit** pagod na ako, tatapusin ko pa rin ang trabahong ito.","translation":"**Even if** I'm already tired, I will still finish this work."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang pagkain **kahit** simple lang ang luto.","translation":"The food is delicious **although** it was cooked simply."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpunta at pagiging naroroon sa isang pagtitipon, kaganapan, o lugar.
original_explanation: "Present po!" That's 'dalo'. It’s showing up. Whether it's for a Zoom meeting you could've skipped, a kasal you're attending for the free food, or that family reunion where titas will ask "Kailan ka ikakasal?". Your physical presence is your 'dalo'.
usage_notes: The root word `dalo` refers to the act or concept of attending. The most common verb form is `dumalo` (to attend) and the noun for attendance is `pagdalo`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **pagdalo** mo sa pulong mamaya.","translation":"Your **attendance** at the meeting later is important."},{"sentence":"Marami ang **dumalo** sa kanyang kaarawan.","translation":"Many people **attended** his birthday party."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos o gawain ng paggalaw sa tubig gamit ang mga braso at binti.
original_explanation: Your favorite summer activity! It's what you do to escape the Metro Manila heat. Whether it's in a resort pool, a pristine beach in Palawan, or in a 'baha' (kidding!), *langoy* is the Filipino's answer to a hot day. The verb form, *lumangoy*, is what you do when you see your crush coming and you try to act cool in the water.
usage_notes: The verb form is 'lumangoy' (to swim) or 'languyin' (to swim across something).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **langoy** ay isang mahusay na ehersisyo.","translation":"**Swimming** is a great exercise."},{"sentence":"Tara, **langoy** tayo sa dagat!","translation":"Come on, let's go for a **swim** in the sea!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng reptilya na mayroong matigas na bahay-bahayan o 'shell' sa likod, at kilala sa mabagal na pagkilos.
original_explanation: The OG symbol for 'mabagal.' If your internet connection is slow, it's 'usad-**pagong**.' If a friend is always late, they're a '**pagong**.' Also, the wisest-looking animal in any cartoon, probably because they've seen it all and are in no hurry to get anywhere. They carry their house on their back, which is the ultimate WFH setup.
usage_notes: Used literally for the animal and figuratively to describe slowness. The term covers both land (tortoise) and sea/freshwater (turtle) varieties in common parlance, though 'pawikan' is specific to sea turtles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagong** ay dahan-dahang tumawid sa kalsada.","translation":"The **turtle** slowly crossed the road."},{"sentence":"Bakit ang bagal mo? Para kang **pagong** kumilos!","translation":"Why are you so slow? You move like a **tortoise**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na nangangahulugang talo, bigo, o walang nakuha.
original_explanation: Galing sa binaliktad na 'talo.' Ito 'yung feeling mo kapag na-seen ka lang niya, natalo team mo sa basketball, o isa ka na lang sa 500+ na nag-apply sa trabaho. As in, 'Sorry, olats ka.'
usage_notes: Impormal na salitang kalye o balbal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Olats** na naman tayo sa pustahan!","translation":"We're **defeated** in the bet again!"},{"sentence":"Sinubukan kong makuha 'yung promo, pero **olats**, naunahan ako.","translation":"I tried to get the promo, but **I lost**, someone beat me to it."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamataas na bahagi o dulo ng isang bagay, lalo na ng bundok, burol, o gusali.
original_explanation: It's the very top of anything, like the peak of Mt. Pulag where you take your 'sea of clouds' profile pic. It's also the 'tuktok' of your career before you realize you're burnt out. In short, the highest point.
usage_notes: 'Tuktok' is far more common. 'Tukatok' might be considered poetic or archaic by some speakers.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natanaw nila mula sa **tukatok** ng bundok ang buong kapatagan.","translation":"From the **peak** of the mountain, they could see the entire plain."},{"sentence":"Inabot nila ang **tukatok** ng tagumpay dahil sa kanilang pagsisikap.","translation":"They reached the **apex** of success because of their hard work."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan ng sukdulang kagandahan, kariktan, o pagiging kaakit-akit sa paningin.
original_explanation: The default reaction to seeing a sunset at Manila Bay, your crush walking by, or a perfectly plated sisig. It's the highest form of aesthetic appreciation, Filipino style. When 'maganda' just doesn't cut it.
usage_notes: A very common compliment used for people, places, and things that are exceptionally beautiful.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Napakaganda** ng tanawin mula sa tuktok ng bundok.","translation":"The view from the top of the mountain is **very beautiful**."},{"sentence":"Sa lahat ng nakita ko, siya ang **napakaganda**.","translation":"Of all I have seen, she is the most **gorgeous**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang anibersaryo ng araw ng kapanganakan ng isang tao. Karaniwang ginagamit ang salitang Ingles na ito sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
original_explanation: The one day a year you're legally allowed to demand a handa, get a free cake from your office, and post 100 photos of yourself with a caption that starts with 'Chapter [your age]'. It's the annual performance review of your life, celebrated with spaghetti and hotdogs on a stick.
usage_notes: While "kaarawan" is the formal Filipino term, "birthday" is used far more frequently in casual conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Anong handa natin sa **birthday** mo?","translation":"What food are we having for your **birthday**?"},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutan ang **birthday** ko, ha!","translation":"Don't forget my **birthday**, okay!"}]

translation: act of charming (with a potion); love spell
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paggamit ng gayuma o isang uri ng mahika upang mapaibig o maakit ang isang tao nang labag sa kanyang kalooban.
original_explanation: Before dating apps, there was gayuma. This is the ultimate 'slide into your DMs' but with magic potions. Yung tipong pinainom mo si crush ng something-something tapos bigla ka na lang niyang naging 'My only one.' It's a magical, and very questionable, way to get someone's affection.
usage_notes: Part of Philippine folklore and superstition. Can be used figuratively for someone who is irresistibly charming.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May mga naniniwala pa rin sa bisa ng **panggayuma**.","translation":"Some people still believe in the effectiveness of a **love spell**."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga matatamis na salita ay tila isang **panggayuma**.","translation":"His sweet words are like a **love charm**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagkuha ng kaalaman, kasanayan, o pag-unawa sa pamamagitan ng pagbabasa, pagsasanay, o pagtuturo. Maaari rin itong tumukoy sa isang partikular na pagsusuri o pananaliksik.
etymology: From root `aral` (lesson, study). The `pag-` prefix and reduplication of the first vowel `a` create a noun meaning 'the act of studying' or 'the concept of education'.
original_explanation: The reason for all the puyat, coffee, and "sanaol tapos na" posts during finals week. It can mean the act of hitting the books ("Mag-aaral muna ako"), or your entire educational journey ("Mahalaga ang pag-aaral"). It can also be a formal research paper, like a "case study." Basically, it's the official term for anything that requires you to use your brain, whether you want to or not.
usage_notes: A very versatile word. Can mean 'studying', 'education', or 'a study/report'. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pag-aaral** nang mabuti ang susi sa magandang kinabukasan.","translation":"**Studying** well is the key to a good future."},{"sentence":"Isang bagong **pag-aaral** ang nagsasabing masama sa kalusugan ang sobrang asukal.","translation":"A new **study** says that too much sugar is bad for your health."},{"sentence":"Ipagpapatuloy niya ang kanyang **pag-aaral** sa kolehiyo.","translation":"She will continue her **education** in college."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng malalim na pag-iisip, katapatan, o kawalan ng pagbibiro; hindi naglalaro o pabagu-bago.
original_explanation: When your friend stops joking and says, 'Pre, seryoso...', you know the chismis is real. It's the opposite of 'charot lang.' It's your boss's face during performance reviews, or how you feel about your Shopee cart during the 12.12 sale.
usage_notes: Can also be used as an adverb ('seryosong nag-usap') or an interjection to express disbelief or sincerity ('Seryoso?').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mukhang **seryoso** ang usapan nila kaya hindi ako lumapit.","translation":"Their conversation looked **serious** so I didn't approach them."},{"sentence":"**Seryoso** ka ba sa sinasabi mo tungkol sa pag-alis mo?","translation":"Are you **serious** about what you're saying about your departure?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian o kalagayan ng pagiging hindi angkop, baligtad, o labag sa karaniwang pamantayan, na nagdudulot ng pagkailang.
original_explanation: That moment when you tell a joke and no one laughs. Crickets. Or when you show up to a wake wearing a beach party outfit. 'Yung level of cringe na gusto mo na lang magpalamon sa lupa. That's kasaliwaan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **kasaliwaan** sa kaniyang mga kilos kaya pinaghihinalaan siya ng mga pulis.","translation":"There was an **incongruity** in his actions, which is why the police suspected him."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pariralang tumutukoy sa isang lugar o direksyon na malapit sa kinaroroonan ng nagsasalita.
etymology: Mula sa "sa", "gawi" (direction/area), at "rito" (here, variant of dito).
original_explanation: This is the more formal, slightly poetic way of saying "dito sa amin" or "dito sa lugar namin." Kapag may nagtanong, "Saan ba maganda kumain?" at sumagot ka ng, "**Sa gawi rito**, sikat ang lugawan ni Aling Nena." You're basically saying "in this neck of the woods." Sounds a bit more established, like you're a local guide.
usage_notes: Ang "rito" ay karaniwang ginagamit kapag ang sinusundang salita ay nagtatapos sa patinig (vowel), tulad ng "gawi".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming bagong gusali ang itinatayo **sa gawi rito**.","translation":"Many new buildings are being constructed **in this area**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aalis ng mga kaliskis mula sa balat ng isda bilang paghahanda sa pagluto.
