meaning_filipino: Anumang pagkain na kinakain pansamantala upang maibsan o mawala ang pakiramdam ng pagkagutom, karaniwang hindi isang buong pagkain.
original_explanation: That 3 PM snack you grab to survive until dinner. It's the fishball, the turon, the half-eaten bag of chips in your drawer. Not a full meal, just something to silence your protesting stomach. The "pangtawid-gutom" for the working class hero.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with "pantawid-gutom".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng biskwit bilang **pamawing-gutom** habang naghihintay sa bus.","translation":"I bought some biscuits as a **snack to appease my hunger** while waiting for the bus."},{"sentence":"Saging lang ang kinain niya, sapat na **pamawing-gutom** daw.","translation":"He only ate a banana, saying it's enough to **appease his hunger**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang libangan o propesyon ay ang pag-iipon o pangongolekta ng mga partikular na bagay.
original_explanation: The formal term for someone who collects things. Sila yung mga taong seryoso sa pag-iipon ng K-Pop photocards, vintage toys, o kahit mga bato. Their house is basically a museum for one specific thing.
usage_notes: Formal spelling. 'Kolektor' is a more common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang kilalang **koleksiyonista** ng sining ang bumili ng obra.","translation":"A well-known art **collector** bought the masterpiece."},{"sentence":"Bilang isang **koleksiyonista** ng selyo, lagi siyang naghahanap ng mga pambihirang piraso.","translation":"As a stamp **collector**, he is always looking for rare pieces."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pook, gusali, o establisyimento kung saan isinasagawa ang paggawa o produksyon ng mga bagay; isang pagawaan o pabrika.
etymology: Mula sa `gawa` (work) at hulaping `-an` (locative suffix, na tumutukoy sa lugar).
original_explanation: This is your 9-to-5 prison, este, office. The factory, the workshop, the BPO floor. Kung saan man nangyayari ang 'magic' ng production. Basically, the place where 'gawa' happens on a massive scale. Think 'assembly line,' but it could also be a small talyer (mechanic's shop).
usage_notes: Kasingkahulugan ng `pagawaan` o `pabrika`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming manggagawa sa **gawaan** ng sapatos sa Marikina.","translation":"There are many workers in the shoe **factory** in Marikina."},{"sentence":"Dinala niya ang sirang sasakyan sa **gawaan**.","translation":"He brought the broken car to the **workshop**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na namamahala sa trabaho o gawain ng iba sa isang organisasyon o kumpanya.
original_explanation: The more modern, English-spelled version of 'superbisor'. This is your Team Lead, your Floor Supervisor, your BPO god who can grant you an early out. They're the ones you send a G-chat to when your internet dies mid-shift. Basically, the person you have to be nice to if you want a good performance review.
usage_notes: This English spelling is more common in modern business and corporate settings in the Philippines compared to the hispanized 'superbisor'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Please submit your leave requests to your immediate **supervisor**.","translation":"Please submit your leave requests to your immediate **supervisor**."},{"sentence":"Our **supervisor** called for an emergency team meeting.","translation":"Our **supervisor** called for an emergency team meeting."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtingin sa salamin; ang pagpapakita o paglalarawan ng isang bagay sa paraang tapat at malinaw, tulad ng imahe sa isang salamin.
original_explanation: This is what you do for 30 minutes before a Zoom call, checking if your 'no-makeup' makeup look is on point. It's also that deep, introspective moment when you realize your actions are a reflection of your character. "Ang social media feed mo ay isang pagsasalamin ng iyong pagkatao."
usage_notes: Can be literal (looking in a mirror) or figurative (reflection of a quality or state).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mahabang **pagsasalamin** niya sa harap ng aparador ay tanda na may lakad siya.","translation":"Her long **act of looking in the mirror** in front of the wardrobe is a sign that she's going somewhere."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga nobela ay isang **pagsasalamin** ng lipunang Pilipino.","translation":"His novels are a **reflection** of Philippine society."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubhang malapit ang ugnayan; matalik.
original_explanation: A more intense version of 'dait'. This is not just physically close, but emotionally, too. 'Yung level ng friendship n'yo na alam n'yo na ang iniisip ng isa't isa without even talking. The kind of closeness where you can finish each other's... sandwiches.
usage_notes: Synonymous with 'dait' but can imply a deeper, more intimate connection rather than just physical proximity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkaibigang **daiti** sila mula pa noong pagkabata.","translation":"They have been **intimate** friends since childhood."}]

translation: nest (specifically, of a swiftlet, used in soup)
meaning_filipino: Ang pugad ng ibong langay-langayan (swiftlet) na ginagamit bilang pangunahing sangkap sa paggawa ng sabaw na 'nido soup'.
original_explanation: Not to be confused with the powdered milk brand your titas probably fed you as a kid. This is the OG nido—an expensive bird's nest that's the main event in a fancy Chinese soup. It's basically saliva hardened into a nest. Delicious, right? It's the kind of food you eat at a lauriat for a wedding or a big birthday.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used to refer to the edible bird's nest for 'nido soup'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahal ang isang mangkok ng sabaw na may **nido**.","translation":"A bowl of soup with **nido** is expensive."},{"sentence":"Kinukuha ang **nido** mula sa mga kuweba.","translation":"The **nido** (bird's nest) is harvested from caves."}]

translation: to find abundant; to be blessed with plenty
meaning_filipino: Maranasan o makita na mayroong kasaganaan o labis na dami ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: When you open the fridge after payday and it's overflowing with food, you can say `masaganaan` mo ang laman. It's the feeling of seeing abundance. It's the opposite of 'petsa de peligro' vibes. It's the feeling of having more than enough, whether it's food, blessings, or chismis.
usage_notes: This is a slightly formal and less common verb form. More common is 'masagana ang...' (e.g., 'Masagana ang ani'). This form implies perception or discovery of abundance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa pag-uwi niya sa probinsya, **nasaganaan** niya ang hapag-kainan ng kanyang lola.","translation":"Upon returning to the province, he **found abundant** his grandmother's dining table."},{"sentence":"Sana'y **masaganaan** tayo sa biyaya ngayong taon.","translation":"I hope we will **be blessed with abundance** this year."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na insektong lumilipad na may mahabang proboscis, kung saan ang babae ay sumisipsip ng dugo ng mga tao at hayop.
original_explanation: The national bird of the Philippines every summer. The uninvited guest that sings a B-flat lullaby in your ear at 3 AM right before it bites you. The main reason for the existence of katol, Off! lotion, and that electric tennis racket.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisara ang bintana, baka may pumasok na **lamok**.","translation":"Please close the window, a **mosquito** might get in."},{"sentence":"Ang kagat ng **lamok** ay maaaring magdulot ng dengue.","translation":"A **mosquito** bite can cause dengue."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-imbay o pag-indayog ng balakang habang naglalakad.
original_explanation: The graceful, sometimes flirty, sway of the hips when walking. Think beauty queen walk or that confident stride someone has. It's walking with rhythm and a little bit of attitude. The verb form is 'kuminding'.
usage_notes: The verb form 'kuminding' (to sway the hips while walking) is more common in speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng **kinding** ng mga kalahok sa beauty pageant.","translation":"The **sway of the hips** of the beauty pageant contestants is beautiful."},{"sentence":"Siya ay **kumikinding** habang naglalakad sa pasilyo.","translation":"She is **swaying her hips** while walking down the hallway."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaikling salita para sa "fan fiction," na tumutukoy sa mga kuwentong kathang-isip na nilikha ng mga tagahanga (fans) na gumagamit ng mga tauhan at tagpuan mula sa isang umiiral na gawa ng panitikan, pelikula, o serye.
etymology: Pinaikling anyo ng pariralang Ingles na "fan fiction".
original_explanation: Short for fan fiction. This is where your favorite love teams *actually* get together, where the villain gets a redemption arc, or where characters from different universes meet. It's the literary version of 'what if...?' written by fans, for fans. Before Wattpad became a thing, there were forums and LiveJournals filled with 'fics' about everything from Harry Potter to local showbiz pairings.
usage_notes: Malawakang ginagamit sa mga online na komunidad ng mga tagahanga (fandoms).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpupuyat ako kagabi sa pagbabasa ng isang magandang **fic**.","translation":"I stayed up late last night reading a good **fan fic**."},{"sentence":"Sumusulat siya ng K-pop **fic** sa Wattpad.","translation":"She writes K-pop **fic** on Wattpad."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng anghang o lasang parang sili na nagdudulot ng bahagyang init o paso sa dila.
original_explanation: The official feeling when you eat Bicol Express or Samyang noodles and suddenly question all your life choices. It's the 'Kaya pa ba?' of flavors. Can also describe a spicy take or a sharp tongue, like your tita's 'tumaba ka' comments.
usage_notes: Distinct from 'mainit' which means hot in temperature. 'Maanghang' is strictly for taste. It can also be used figuratively to mean 'sharp' or 'biting' when describing words or a person's tongue.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong ubusin ang sili, baka maging sobrang **maanghang** ang luto mo.","translation":"Don't use up all the chili, your dish might become too **spicy**."},{"sentence":"**Maanghang** ang dila ng ale, lahat na lang ay pinupuna.","translation":"The woman has a **sharp** tongue, she criticizes everyone."}]

translation: to act elegantly; to carry oneself with poise
meaning_filipino: Kumilos o magpakita nang may bikas, tikas, o karangyaan sa tindig at pananamit.
original_explanation: It's what you do when you're wearing a brand new Barong Tagalog or a stunning Filipiniana dress. You walk a little straighter, you move more gracefully. It’s carrying yourself like you’re on a pageant stage, even if you’re just walking to the office pantry. Projecting!
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinabihan siyang **magmabikas** sa kanyang paglakad dahil kinatawan siya ng kumpanya.","translation":"She was told to **carry herself with poise** in her walk because she was a representative of the company."},{"sentence":"Kahit simpleng damit lang, kaya niyang **magmabikas**.","translation":"Even in simple clothes, he can **act elegantly**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglalagay ng sabon. Sa matalinhagang kahulugan, ito ay ang matinding pagagalit o pagsermon sa isang tao.
original_explanation: Literally, it's just lathering up with soap. But the real tea is its slang meaning: getting a severe scolding. When your boss "sermons" you for being late, or your mom goes full-on dragon mode because of your grades, that's 'pagsasabon'. You're getting "cleaned" with harsh words. It's a verbal beatdown that leaves you feeling... well, not so fresh.
usage_notes: The figurative meaning (scolding) is very common in informal speech. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang tamang **pagsasabon** ng kamay upang maiwasan ang sakit.","translation":"Proper **soaping** of hands is important to avoid sickness."},{"sentence":"Nakatikim siya ng matinding **pagsasabon** mula sa kanyang ina dahil sa pag-uwi nang gabi.","translation":"He received a severe **scolding** from his mother for coming home late."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o akto ng pag-agos o paglabas ng dugo mula sa katawan, karaniwang sanhi ng sugat o karamdaman.
original_explanation: The literal 'sana all' that you don't want. This is when blood decides to make an exit, whether from a paper cut or something more serious. It's the body's alarm system screaming 'May butas!' (There's a hole!). Also, a metaphor for when your wallet is 'bleeding' cash during a 12.12 sale.
usage_notes: A common medical term. Can also be used metaphorically for financial loss.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Agad nilapatan ng paunang lunas ang sugat upang matigil ang **pagdurugo**.","translation":"First aid was immediately applied to the wound to stop the **bleeding**."},{"sentence":"Ang matinding **pagdurugo** ng ilong ay dapat ikonsulta sa doktor.","translation":"Severe **bleeding** of the nose should be consulted with a doctor."}]

translation: to recover, to take back, to retract
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkuha muli ng isang bagay na naibigay, nawala, o ipinahiram; ang pag-urong sa isang sinabi o ginawa.
original_explanation: That feeling when you give your friend the last piece of chicharon, then immediately regret it. "Uy, bawiin ko na lang pala!" It's also the battle cry after a major "palpak" moment at work or in a game. "Babawi ako bukas!" (I'll make up for it tomorrow!). It's the official word for second chances and take-backsies.
usage_notes: Can be used for physical objects (to recover), statements (to retract), or making up for a loss/failure (to redeem oneself).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **bawiin** ang perang ipinautang niya.","translation":"He tried to **recover** the money he lent."},{"sentence":"**Binabawi** ko na ang sinabi ko kanina.","translation":"I'm **taking back** what I said earlier."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **bumawi** sa pagkatalo namin kahapon.","translation":"I need to **make up for** our loss yesterday."}]

translation: to feel like vomiting, to be nauseous
meaning_filipino: Ang maramdaman ang pagnanais o ang pisikal na pangangailangang ilabas ang laman ng sikmura.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling mo after sumakay sa Viking sa Star City, o kapag nakita mo 'yung jowa mo na may ka-holding hands na iba. Pwedeng literal, pwedeng figurative. "Napasuka ako sa pinagsasabi niya." It's the ultimate physical reaction to something disgusting, whether it's bad food or bad behavior.
usage_notes: Ang 'napasuka' ay nasa anyong naganap na (past tense), na nangangahulugang hindi sinasadyang pagsusuka. 'Magsuka' ay ang anyong pautos/pawatas. Ang 'masuka-suka' ay isang anyong nagpapahiwatig ng matinding pakiramdam.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahihilo ako at parang **masuka**.","translation":"I feel dizzy and **nauseous**."},{"sentence":"**Napasuka** siya dahil sa sobrang kalasingan.","translation":"He **vomited** due to extreme drunkenness."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na nangyayari, ginagawa, o ipinagdiriwang isang beses sa bawat taon.
original_explanation: Your annual performance review. The yearly family reunion where someone always brings up your love life. The 'piso sale' that happens every year. Anything that happens once a year, like clockwork. It's the more formal cousin of 'taun-taon'.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'taun-taon', but 'taunan' can sound slightly more formal, as in 'taunang ulat' (annual report).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **taunan** na pagpupulong ng mga shareholder ay gaganapin sa Disyembre.","translation":"The **annual** shareholders' meeting will be held in December."},{"sentence":"Nakatanggap siya ng **taunan**g bonus mula sa kumpanya.","translation":"He/She received an **annual** bonus from the company."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtindig at pagpilit sa sariling pananaw, karapatan, o katwiran sa isang usapin.
original_explanation: That moment in a meeting when you know you're right, so you keep repeating your point until everyone gets it. 'As per my last email...' pero in Tagalog. It's the energy of someone who won't take 'no' for an answer, whether you're asking for a raise or just trying to prove your friend wrong about a movie's ending.
usage_notes: "Igiit" is the object-focused form, meaning to assert something specific (e.g., "Igiit mo ang iyong karapatan."). "Maggiit" is actor-focused.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **maggiit** sa iyong mga karapatan bilang isang manggagawa.","translation":"You need to **insist** on your rights as a worker."},{"sentence":"Kahit maraming tumutol, patuloy siyang **naggiit** sa kanyang plano.","translation":"Even though many objected, he continued to **assert** his plan."}]

meaning_filipino: May kaugnayan sa paggamot ng sakit o karamdaman; may kakayahang magpagaling, magpakalma, o magpaginhawa.
original_explanation: Describes anything that makes you feel better and de-stressed. For some, it's a massage. For others, it's washing the dishes while listening to a podcast. For many, it's adding to cart on Shopee. If it calms your soul and makes you forget your problems even for a while, 'yan ay terapeutiko.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paghahardin ay may **terapeutiko** na epekto sa akin.","translation":"Gardening has a **therapeutic** effect on me."},{"sentence":"Ang mainit na paliligo ay maaaring maging **terapeutiko** para sa nananakit na mga kalamnan.","translation":"A hot bath can be **therapeutic** for sore muscles."}]

translation: treatment (of others); manner of treating someone
meaning_filipino: Ang paraan ng pakikitungo, pakikisama, o pakikipag-ugnayan sa isang tao o kapwa.
original_explanation: Your 'pagtrato' is your vibe check on others. Are you treating them like a VIP, or are you giving them the 'seen zone' treatment? It's how you handle people. A good 'pagtrato sa kapwa' is basic human decency, while a bad one is a one-way ticket to getting cancelled.
usage_notes: Often followed by 'sa' (to) to specify who is being treated, e.g., 'pagtrato sa kapwa' (treatment of others), 'pagtrato sa hayop' (treatment of animals).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang maayos na **pagtrato** sa lahat ng tao, anuman ang kanilang estado sa buhay.","translation":"Proper **treatment** of all people is important, regardless of their status in life."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko nagustuhan ang **pagtrato** niya sa mga serbidor.","translation":"I didn't like his **treatment** of the servers."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kasuotan para sa ibabang bahagi ng katawan na may dalawang butas para sa mga binti. Sa modernong gamit, madalas itong tumutukoy sa damit panloob (underwear).
original_explanation: Technically, this means pants. But in real talk, this is the old-school, formal, or sometimes funny word for 'underwear' or 'briefs'. You wouldn't tell your friend "Nice salawal!" unless you're trying to be funny. But your lola might ask you if you've changed your salawal.
usage_notes: Can mean 'pants' in a more traditional or literary context, but colloquially it often refers to underwear. 'Pantalon' is the more common word for pants.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakalimutan niyang magdala ng ekstrang **salawal** sa kanyang biyahe.","translation":"He forgot to bring extra **underwear** on his trip."},{"sentence":"Sa lumang larawan, nakasuot ng maluwag na **salawal** ang mga magsasaka.","translation":"In the old photograph, the farmers are wearing loose **pants**."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang tungkulin o responsibilidad na gawin ang isang bagay; hindi sapilitan.
original_explanation: The perfect response when your tita asks why you're still single. "Di-ubligado, Tita." It means you're not required or forced to do something. It's the freedom to not reply to a work email after 6 PM or to say "no" to another "ambagan" for a coworker's birthday. You're off the hook.
usage_notes: A loanword combination used in more formal or legalistic contexts, but also understood in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Di-ubligado** ang mga empleyado na pumasok sa araw ng holiday.","translation":"Employees are **not obligated** to come to work on a holiday."},{"sentence":"Tandaan mo, **di-ubligado** kang magpaliwanag sa lahat ng tao.","translation":"Remember, you are **not required** to explain yourself to everyone."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang patakaran o katangian ng isang tao o institusyon na hayagang tumatangging magpahiram ng salapi.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng 'hindi' (not) at 'nagpapautang' (lends money), mula sa salitang-ugat na 'utang' (debt).
original_explanation: The ultimate sign you see in a sari-sari store: "Bawal umutang." This is the mantra of someone who's been burned one too many times by friends who suddenly get amnesia on payday. It's a financial boundary, the "seen-zone" of lending. "Sorry, bes, **hindi nagpapautang** ang lola mo ngayon."
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang parirala sa mga usaping pampinansyal at personal na relasyon, lalo na sa mga maliliit na negosyo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang patakaran ng tindahan; **hindi nagpapautang** kahit sa mga suki.","translation":"The store's policy is strict; it **does not lend money** even to regular customers."},{"sentence":"Mula nang maloko siya, **hindi na nagpapautang** si Aling Nena.","translation":"Ever since she was tricked, Aling Nena **no longer lends money**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang silid, gusali, o espasyo para sa pagtatanghal ng mga likhang-sining.
original_explanation: It's the Spanish word for 'gallery', making it sound 10x more sosyal than just saying 'gallery'. You'll see this in the names of art spaces, like "Galeria de las Islas." It's where you go to look at paintings, feel cultured, and pretend you understand abstract art.
usage_notes: Interchangeable with the English word 'gallery', but 'galeria' often implies a more formal or traditional setting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May bagong eksibit sa **galeria** sa tapat ng simbahan.","translation":"There's a new exhibit at the **gallery** across from the church."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa hapon ng araw na iyon o sa sumunod na hapon pagkatapos ng isang tiyak na pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is the 'later that day' transition in a movie, but specifically for the afternoon. It's when you make plans in the morning and say 'mamayang hapon,' and then when that afternoon comes, you're living in the 'kinahapunan.' It's the time for merienda, a quick nap, or the start of rush hour traffic.
usage_notes: Indicates a specific afternoon, either the same day or the next, in the context of a past event.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-usap kami sa umaga, at **kinahapunan** ay nagkita kami muli.","translation":"We talked in the morning, and **that afternoon** we met again."},{"sentence":"Dumating ang bagyo **kinahapunan** noong Martes.","translation":"The typhoon arrived on the **afternoon** of Tuesday."}]

translation: to desire; to aspire; to wish for
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng matinding pagnanasa o layunin na makamit o makuha ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: That feeling when you see your friend's travel pics from Japan and you start dreaming of your own trip. It's a level up from 'gusto'. This is about ambition, aspiration, and deep-seated desires. Like wanting to be the next CEO, or just wanting to finally get 8 hours of sleep. To want something you don't have.
usage_notes: Implies a strong, often long-term desire for something significant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lahat tayo ay dapat **maghangad** ng kapayapaan para sa ating bansa.","translation":"We should all **aspire** for peace for our country."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **maghangad** ng bagay na hindi para sa iyo.","translation":"Don't **desire** something that is not meant for you."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng inumin o gamot na pinaniniwalaang nagpapalakas at nagpapasigla ng katawan.
original_explanation: Parang yung gin and tonic ng mga tito, pero sa sinaunang bersyon. Ito yung iniinom mo para "lumakas ang katawan," parang energy drink ng lolo mo. Puwede ring hair tonic, na parang conditioner para sa mga gustong maging kamukha ni FPJ.
usage_notes: Madalas tumutukoy sa "hair tonic" (toniko sa buhok) o "tonic water" (tubig-toniko).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpapahid siya ng **toniko** sa buhok para kumapal ito.","translation":"He applies hair **tonic** to make his hair thicker."},{"sentence":"Ang 'tonic water' ay isang uri ng **toniko** na may quinine.","translation":"'Tonic water' is a type of **tonic** that contains quinine."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang isa sa apat na pangunahing direksiyon o punto ng kumpas, katapat ng hilaga.
original_explanation: When someone from Manila says they're going "South," they usually mean Alabang, Laguna, or Cavite—the land of subdivisions and (formerly) less traffic. It's a direction, but in the Philippines, it's also a lifestyle. "Taga-South ka ba?" often implies a more laid-back vibe compared to the hustle of the North (QC, etc.).
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin kasama ng panandang 'sa', halimbawa, 'sa timog'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Mindanao ay nasa **timog** na bahagi ng Pilipinas.","translation":"Mindanao is in the **southern** part of the Philippines."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babae na mahilig sa mga abentura, o isang babae na sumusubok makamit ang yaman o posisyon sa lipunan sa pamamagitan ng mapangahas na paraan.
original_explanation: The 'dalagang Pilipina' who traded her 'baro't saya' for hiking boots and a passport. She's the 'travel goals' queen on your feed, always posting from a new mountain or beach. In classic teleseryes, she's the mysterious woman from the province who comes to the city with a big dream and an even bigger secret, ready to shake things up.
usage_notes: Can have a slightly negative connotation in older contexts, implying a social climber, but is now more commonly used to mean a female adventurer.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala si Dora bilang isang sikat na **abenturera** sa mga bata.","translation":"Dora is known to children as a famous **adventuress**."},{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang maging isang **abenturera** at libutin ang buong mundo.","translation":"She dreams of becoming an **adventuress** and traveling the whole world."}]

translation: to manage; to operate; to make someone walk
meaning_filipino: Pamahalaan ang operasyon o takbo ng isang negosyo, organisasyon, o gawain; o utusan o sanayin ang isang tao na maglakad.
original_explanation: The boss verb. It can mean 'to make someone walk' (e.g., a physical therapist helping a patient). But more often, it means 'to run' or 'to manage' something. If you run a business, you 'nagpapalakad ng negosyo'. If you manage a household, you 'nagpapalakad ng bahay'. It's being the person in charge of making things move forward, literally and figuratively.
usage_notes: Has two distinct common meanings: 1) to manage/run something (like a business) and 2) to make someone/something walk.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **nagpapalakad** ng aming pampamilyang negosyo.","translation":"She is the one who **manages** our family business."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **magpalakad** sa sanggol sa unang pagkakataon.","translation":"She tried **to make** the baby **walk** for the first time."}]

translation: Chorizo; a type of pork sausage.
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng longganisa na karaniwang maanghang o matamis, na nagmula sa Espanya at Portugal, at may mga lokal na bersyon sa Pilipinas.
original_explanation: The king of Filipino breakfast sausages, especially the ones from Cebu (sweet) or Vigan (garlicky). It's that fatty, flavorful, and sometimes intensely red sausage that makes your sinangag (garlic fried rice) glorious. The rendered fat is liquid gold you drizzle over your rice.
usage_notes: While it refers to a specific type of sausage, it's often used more broadly to refer to local longganisa with a chorizo-like flavor profile.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong almusal ang **tsoriso** na may sinangag at itlog.","translation":"My favorite breakfast is **chorizo** with fried rice and egg."},{"sentence":"Nag-uwi siya ng sikat na **tsoriso** de Cebu bilang pasalubong.","translation":"He brought home the famous Cebu **chorizo** as a souvenir."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa matematika, isang numero na kumakatawan sa isang bahagi ng isang kabuuan.
original_explanation: Your good old math class nightmare (or delight): fractions. That 1/2, 3/4, 5/8 thing. It's literally 'divided number.' Just like how you calculate your share of the Netflix subscription with your siblings. 'Okay, ₱549, hating-bilang tayo sa apat.'
usage_notes: A technical term used mostly in academic or mathematical contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan namin ang tungkol sa **hating-bilang** sa klase ng sipnayan.","translation":"We are studying about **fractions** in math class."},{"sentence":"Ang isang-kapat (1/4) ay isang halimbawa ng **hating-bilang**.","translation":"One-fourth (1/4) is an example of a **fraction**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao, bagay, o lugar na kilala, tanyag, at hinahangaan ng marami.
original_explanation: This is your "influencer" or "artista" status. If you're sikat, everyone knows you, from the BPO agent on their break to the lola buying pan de sal. You're the topic of chismis, the star of the show, the "pabebe wave" recipient.
usage_notes: Can be used for people, places, or brands. The opposite is 'laos' (faded from popularity).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sikat** na artista ang bida sa bagong pelikula.","translation":"A **famous** actor is the star of the new movie."},{"sentence":"Gusto niyang maging **sikat** na vlogger balang araw.","translation":"She wants to be a **popular** vlogger someday."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng tubo, partikular ang itaas na dulo o isang piraso nito, na ginagamit bilang pananim o binhi.
original_explanation: This is some deep-level farmer talk. It's the starter kit for a sugarcane plant. Think of it as the 'cutting' you plant to grow a new plant, but specifically for tubo. If you know this word, you're probably from a sugar-producing province or your lolo is a farmer.
usage_notes: Isang tiyak na terminong pang-agrikultura. Hindi ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap sa kalunsuran.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghanda ang mga magsasaka ng libu-libong **taad** para sa susunod na taniman.","translation":"The farmers prepared thousands of **sugarcane cuttings** for the next planting season."}]

translation: to move to the side; to step aside
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-usog o pagpunta sa gilid upang magbigay-daan o lumayo sa isang bagay o tao.
original_explanation: The standard operating procedure when you see your ex with their new partner walking towards you in the mall. Also, what you do in a crowded MRT when someone shouts "dadaan po!". It's the polite way of saying "get out of my way" or "I'm getting out of your way."
usage_notes: Often used as a command: "Tumabi ka!" (Move aside!). This is the completed aspect of the verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumabi** siya para makadaan ang ambulansya.","translation":"He **moved to the side** so the ambulance could pass."}]

translation: to compete in having the most
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalaban o pagpapaligsahan sa pagkakaroon ng pinakamaraming bilang o dami ng isang bagay.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "pa-" (nagpapahiwatig ng kumpetisyon o paggawa), salitang-ugat na "dami" (many), at hulaping "-han" (nagpapahiwatig ng sosyal na aksyon).
original_explanation: The official sport of Filipino family reunions—paramihan ng apo, paramihan ng napagtapos, paramihan ng handa sa Noche Buena. It's the unspoken competition of 'who has more?' Be it followers on IG, unread messages from your boss, or chismis about the neighbor.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng kumpetisyon o paghahambing tungkol sa dami o bilang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpa-**paramihan** sila ng likes sa kanilang mga post sa social media.","translation":"They are **competing to get the most** likes on their social media posts."},{"sentence":"Sa halip na mag-**paramihan** ng sisi, dapat tayong magtulungan.","translation":"Instead of **competing on who has more** blame, we should help each other."}]

translation: to be compromised; to be put in a compromising situation
meaning_filipino: Mailagay sa isang alanganing sitwasyon kung saan maaaring masira ang reputasyon, prinsipyo, o seguridad.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na napasubo ka sa isang sitwasyon na alam mong delikado o labag sa kalooban mo. For example, your work data gets hacked dahil nag-click ka ng phishing link, so the company's security is now **mapakompromiso**. Or sa love life, 'yung may 'resibo' o ebidensya laban sa'yo na pwedeng gamitin para ma-blackmail ka. You're in a tight spot.
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of security, integrity, or reputation being at risk.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingatan mo ang iyong password upang hindi **mapakompromiso** ang iyong mga online account.","translation":"Safeguard your password so your online accounts won't **be compromised**."},{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang **mapakompromiso** ang kanyang prinsipyo para lamang sa pera.","translation":"She doesn't want her principles **to be compromised** just for money."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aapoy, pagtupok, o pagkasira ng isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng apoy.
original_explanation: This is what happened to the toast you forgot in the toaster. It's the action of setting something on fire, whether intentionally (like burning old love letters for ~drama~) or accidentally (like when your sinangag becomes tutong). It’s the verb for when things get literally heated.
usage_notes: 'Sumunog' is the actor-focus verb (someone burned something), while 'nasunog' means 'was burned' (often accidentally).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **sumunog** sa sinaing? Amoy tutong sa buong bahay.","translation":"Who **burned** the rice? The whole house smells burnt."},{"sentence":"**Sumunog** sila ng mga tuyong dahon sa likod-bahay.","translation":"They **burned** dry leaves in the backyard."}]

translation: to be in danger; to be at risk
meaning_filipino: Malagay sa isang kalagayan na may panganib, kapahamakan, o alanganin.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung ginagawa mo 'pag nag-reply ka sa message ng ex mo. You are choosing to 'mamiligro.' Or when you eat the street food that's been sitting under the sun for 5 hours. Lakas ng loob, but your stomach is about to mamiligro.
usage_notes: A verb form derived from the noun 'peligro'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-motor nang walang helmet, baka **mamiligro** ang buhay mo.","translation":"Don't ride a motorcycle without a helmet, your life might **be in danger**."},{"sentence":"**Mamiligro** ang ating proyekto kung hindi tayo susunod sa plano.","translation":"Our project will **be at risk** if we don't follow the plan."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kaganapan o pagtitipon kung saan mayroong pagtatanghal ng musika; isang sesyon ng pagtugtog ng mga instrumento.
original_explanation: This is the gig, the jam session, the 'tara, soundtrip tayo' moment with the barkada. It's where you find your friend who thinks they're a rockstar after two beers, or that quiet officemate who suddenly shreds on the guitar. Think Battle of the Bands, a music festival, or just chilling with a guitar at a beach bonfire.
usage_notes: Refers to the event or place of music playing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **tugtugan** mamaya sa bar, gusto mo sumama?","translation":"There's a **musical event** at the bar later, want to come?"},{"sentence":"Nagsimula na ang **tugtugan** ng banda.","translation":"The band's **jam session** has started."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagbabawal, pagpigil, o hadlang sa isang gawain o kilos.
original_explanation: This is that thing your parents do when you want to go out with your friends on a Friday night. "Bawal" is the everyday word, but `sansala` is the formal, almost legalistic version. It's the official "NO" stamped on your plans. It can also mean an obstacle, like the EDSA traffic is a `sansala` to you getting to your date on time.
usage_notes: Primarily found in literary works, legal documents, or very formal speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Walang anumang **sansala** ang makahahadlang sa kanyang mga pangarap.","translation":"No **obstacle** can hinder his dreams."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi maluwag; kulang sa espasyo o sukat.
original_explanation: Describes three classic Manila experiences: 1) Ang pantalon mo pagkatapos ng holiday season. 2) Ang MRT pag rush hour. 3) Ang schedule mo kapag hell week sa school/work. Basically, the feeling of having no breathing room, literally or figuratively.
usage_notes: Can be used for physical spaces, clothing, or abstract concepts like schedules and traffic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **masikip** na ang lumang damit para sa kanya.","translation":"The old clothes have become too **tight** for him."},{"sentence":"Sobrang **masikip** sa loob ng bus tuwing umaga.","translation":"It's very **cramped** inside the bus every morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang marka na naiiwan sa balat matapos maghilom ang isang sugat o pinsala.
etymology: The exact origin is uncertain, but it is a native Austronesian term. It is not a Spanish loanword.
original_explanation: The permanent reminder of that time you fell off your bike, tried to cook something ambitious, or got into a fight. It's the body's version of 'Remember when...?' Some are battle scars, others are just... well, scars from being clumsy. It's your personal history written on your skin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **peklat** siya sa noo na nakuha niya noong bata pa siya.","translation":"He has a **scar** on his forehead that he got when he was a child."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kamutin 'yan, baka maging **peklat**.","translation":"Don't scratch that, it might become a **scar**."}]

translation: I wish everyone could have that; hope all
meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyon na nagpapahiwatig ng pag-asa na ang isang magandang karanasan, bagay, o katangian na tinatamasa ng iba ay mapasa-lahat din.
etymology: Isang pariralang Taglish (Tagalog-English) na pinagsasama ang "sana" (I wish, hopefully) at ang salitang Ingles na "all". Sumikat sa pamamagitan ng social media.
original_explanation: The national anthem of the 'inggit'. When your friend posts their travel pics, new gadget, or jowa reveal, this is the mandatory comment. It's a mix of 'congrats' and 'Lord, kailan naman ako?'. The modern 'sana ako rin'. The 'yiee' part is just extra kilig seasoning.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin bilang komento sa mga social media post na nagpapakita ng mga tagumpay, masayang relasyon, o magandang kapalaran. Ang mga baryasyon ay kinabibilangan ng "sana all talaga" (para sa diin) at "sana all yiee" (para sa romantikong konteksto).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May bagong iPhone na naman siya. **Sana all**!","translation":"She has a new iPhone again. **I wish everyone could have one**!"},{"sentence":"Ang sweet naman ng jowa mo, laging may flowers. **Sana all**!","translation":"Your significant other is so sweet, always bringing flowers. **Hope all** (have someone like that)!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtanggap ng salapi o kabayaran bilang kapalit ng serbisyo, pagtatrabaho, o bilang bunga ng isang negosyo.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'sahod'. This is the 'grind' part of the hustle. It's what you do to get the 'kita'. 'Kailangan kong kumayod para may kitain' is the mantra of every working Pinoy, from the BPO agent on night shift to the online seller packing orders at 2 AM.
usage_notes: This is the object-focus verb form. The actor-focus form is 'kumita'. Example: 'Kumita ako ng pera' (I earned money) vs. 'Pera ang kinitain ko' (Money is what I earned).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang **kinita** niya sa pagbebenta ng mga halaman noong pandemya.","translation":"She **earned** a lot from selling plants during the pandemic."},{"sentence":"Ano ang dapat kong gawin para **kitain** ang tiwala mo?","translation":"What should I do to **earn** your trust?"}]

translation: to be humane; to act with humanity
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o paghiling sa isang tao na kumilos nang may dignidad, kabutihan, at paggalang sa kapwa, alinsunod sa mga katangiang inaasahan sa isang mabuting tao.
etymology: From magpa- (causative prefix) + ka- (relational prefix) + tao (person/human). Literally 'to make oneself be a person'.
original_explanation: This is what your lola tells you when you're acting like a total monster. It's the ultimate 'check yourself before you wreck yourself' but on a spiritual, human level. It means to act like a decent human being, not some savage who cuts in line or ghosts their Tinder date.
usage_notes: Often used in a command or appeal for someone to show compassion or act morally.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magpakatao** ka naman, tulungan mo yung matandang nahihirapan.","translation":"Be **humane**, help that old person who is struggling."},{"sentence":"Sa gitna ng gulo, pinili niyang **magpakatao** at unawain ang magkabilang panig.","translation":"In the midst of chaos, he chose to **act with humanity** and understand both sides."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang karagdagang dosis ng bakuna na ibinibigay upang palakasin o pahabain ang bisa ng mga naunang bakuna.
original_explanation: In the post-pandemic Philippines, 'booster' doesn't mean a rocket engine or a fan. It means one thing: the follow-up vaccine shot. It's the topic of conversation in the office pantry, the reason for the long lines at the barangay hall, and the key to getting that updated VaxCertPH for your travel plans. 'Nagpa-booster ka na?' is the new 'Kumain ka na?'.
usage_notes: A direct loanword that became extremely common during and after the COVID-19 pandemic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating lahat magpa-**booster** para sa dagdag na proteksyon.","translation":"We all need to get a **booster shot** for added protection."},{"sentence":"May lagnat ako pagkatapos ng aking pangalawang **booster** shot.","translation":"I had a fever after my second **booster shot**."}]

translation: to get dusty; to be covered in dust
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkapuno o pagkatakpan ng alabok o alikabok.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping pandiwa na `ma-`, salitang-ugat na `alabok` (alikabok), at hulaping `-an`.
original_explanation: 'Yung nangyayari sa mga gamit mo na naka-tambak lang sa bodega. O 'yung itsura ng paa mo after maglakad sa probinsya wearing tsinelas. It's what happens to your forgotten gym membership card.
usage_notes: Ang `alabok` ay kasingkahulugan ng `alikabok`. Ang pandiwang `maalabukan` ay nangangahulugang mapuno ng alikabok.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong iwanang bukas ang bintana at baka **maalabukan** ang mga kasangkapan.","translation":"Don't leave the window open or the furniture might **get dusty**."},{"sentence":"**Naalabukan** ang lumang libro sa ibabaw ng estante.","translation":"The old book on top of the shelf **was covered in dust**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagpapalitan ng mga produkto o serbisyo sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang partido.
original_explanation: This is what countries do to keep their economies running, like the Philippines exporting mangoes and importing K-Pop merch. It's basically a giant, global "barter" system, but with more paperwork and less direct swapping of chickens for rice.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of economics, business, or international relations. Refers to a mutual or reciprocal act of trading.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **magkalakalan** ang mga sinaunang Pilipino at mga Tsino bago pa man dumating ang mga Espanyol.","translation":"The ancient Filipinos and the Chinese began to **trade with each other** long before the Spaniards arrived."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga para sa mga bansa na **magkalakalan** upang umunlad ang kanilang ekonomiya.","translation":"It is important for countries to **trade with each other** to grow their economies."}]

translation: to be trusted; to be confided in
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging karapat-dapat pagkalooban ng tiwala; ang maging sisidlan ng lihim o responsibilidad ng ibang tao.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate friendship/relationship level-up. When someone can tell you their secrets, their problems, or their ATM PIN (kidding!), you have been 'pagtiwalaan'. It's being the 'bes' someone runs to after a breakup, or the officemate who can cover for you, no questions asked. It's a heavy responsibility, so don't be a marites and spill the tea.
usage_notes: The 'pag-' and '-an' affixes turn the root 'tiwala' (trust) into a verb indicating the person or entity that is the recipient or location of the trust.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **pagtiwalaan** ang isang taong minsan ka nang niloko.","translation":"It's hard **to trust** a person who has already fooled you once."},{"sentence":"Siya ang tanging kaibigan na **pinagkakatiwalaan** ko ng aking mga sikreto.","translation":"She is the only friend **I confide** my secrets in."}]

translation: to aggrieve; to put at a disadvantage; to treat unfairly
meaning_filipino: Gawin o tratuhin ang isang tao sa paraang hindi makatarungan, na nagdudulot sa kanya ng pinsala, pagkalugi, o sama ng loob.
original_explanation: This is what you feel when you were promised a promo, but the new guy got it instead. Or when you paid for a large fries and got a medium. It’s the act of making someone feel cheated or wronged. Kapag na-agrabyado ka, you're not just sad, you're ready to file a formal complaint with HR or, at the very least, write a strongly-worded post online.
usage_notes: Commonly used in legal, formal, or dramatic contexts to express being wronged or treated unjustly.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **agrabyaduhin** ang iyong kapwa para lang sa sarili mong kapakanan.","translation":"Do not **treat your fellow person unfairly** just for your own benefit."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman niyang **inagrabyado** siya sa hatian ng mana.","translation":"He felt that he was **put at a disadvantage** in the division of the inheritance."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamataas na antas ng pagmamahal o pagpapahalaga; pinakaiibig. Maaari ring tumukoy sa napakataas na presyo.
original_explanation: This word has two vibes. 1) The 'sana all' vibe: what you call your one true love, your "kamahal-mahalang asawa." 2) The 'sana oil' vibe: what you call that ridiculously priced coffee or gadget, your "kamahal-mahalang bilihin." It's either about your heart or your wallet breaking.
usage_notes: The meaning (beloved vs. expensive) is determined by context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinakilala niya ang kanyang **kamahal-mahalan** na nobya sa pamilya.","translation":"He introduced his **most beloved** girlfriend to the family."},{"sentence":"Bakit ba **kamahal-mahalan** ang presyo ng sibuyas ngayon?","translation":"Why is the price of onions **so very expensive** nowadays?"}]

meaning_filipino: Nakaangat o nakahilig nang pataas ang isang dulo o bahagi.
original_explanation: Imagine a road going up a mountain, like the ones in Baguio. That's 'pasipa'. It's also the feeling of your career trajectory when you finally get that promotion you've been working overtime for. The opposite of 'downhill'.
usage_notes: Often used to describe terrain, roads, or ramps that go upwards.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pasipa** ang daan patungo sa tuktok ng burol kaya medyo mahirap akyatin.","translation":"The road to the top of the hill is **sloping upwards**, so it's a bit difficult to climb."},{"sentence":"Ginawang **pasipa** ang dulo ng rampa para mas madaling umakyat ang mga sasakyan.","translation":"The end of the ramp was made **inclined** so vehicles could go up more easily."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang baryasyon ng 'pagtatatuwa'; ang akto ng pagtanggi o hindi pag-amin sa isang bagay, pahayag, o responsibilidad.
original_explanation: This is the shorter, slightly less common cousin of 'pagtatatuwa'. Think of it like 'color' vs 'colour'. It means the same thing—denial, disavowal—but you might hear it less often. It's still that 'nope, wasn't me' energy.
usage_notes: Often considered a less formal or a spoken variant of 'pagtatatuwa'. Both are understood to mean the same.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa kabila ng ebidensya, ipinagpatuloy niya ang kanyang **pagtatatwa**.","translation":"Despite the evidence, he continued his **denial**."},{"sentence":"Malinaw ang kanyang **pagtatatwa** sa anumang kinalaman sa krimen.","translation":"His **disavowal** of any connection to the crime was clear."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na nabuo mula sa "wala akong pakialam." Ito ay nagpapahayag ng kawalan ng interes o pag-aalala sa isang bagay o sitwasyon.
etymology: Portmanteau of Tagalog "wala akong pakialam" (I don't have a care / I don't care).
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino mantra for self-preservation. It's the Tagalog version of "IDGAF" (I don't give a f*ck). When your tita asks why you're still single, or when there's new office chismis, you just go "wapakels" and sip your milk tea. It's a portmanteau of "Wala akong pakialam."
usage_notes: Highly informal and considered slang. Used to express indifference, sometimes defiantly or humorously.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Wapakels** ako sa opinyon nila basta masaya ako.","translation":"I **don't care** about their opinion as long as I'm happy."},{"sentence":"Sinabihan siyang tumigil pero **wapakels** lang siya.","translation":"He was told to stop but he was just **unconcerned**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdudulot ng pagod o kapagalan sa isang tao o bagay; gawing pagod.
original_explanation: What your toxic boss does to you by giving you work at 5:59 PM. What a toddler does to their parents by running around the mall for 3 hours straight. It's the goal of every workout, but the unintended consequence of every long, pointless meeting.
usage_notes: This is a verb. The noun form is 'pagod' (tiredness/fatigue).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pagurin** ang iyong sarili sa kaiisip sa kanya.","translation":"Don't **tire** yourself **out** by constantly thinking about him/her."},{"sentence":"Talagang pinagod ako ng biyahe, huwag mo na akong **pagurin** pa sa mga tanong mo.","translation":"The trip really tired me out, don't **fatigue** me further with your questions."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang parangal, karaniwang isang tasa o pigurin na gawa sa metal, na ibinibigay bilang simbolo ng tagumpay sa isang kompetisyon.
original_explanation: Yung premyo na napanalunan mo sa sportsfest o quiz bee na pinapangalandakan mo sa sala para makita ng mga bisita. Proof na may pinagkakaabalahan ka maliban sa pag-scroll sa TikTok. Minsan, ito rin yung jowa mong 'trophy wife' or 'trophy husband'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagmamalaki niya ang kanyang mga **tropeo** sa paglalaro ng chess.","translation":"He is proud of his **trophies** from playing chess."},{"sentence":"Ang bawat **tropeo** ay may kwento ng pagsisikap at tagumpay.","translation":"Every **trophy** has a story of effort and success."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sama-samang pagbibigay ng matinding puna o pagtuligsa sa isang tao o pangkat.
original_explanation: This is the verb form, like a group project of criticizing someone. 'Tara, batikusan natin yung finale ng series!' It’s the act of dishing out the 'batikos'. Often implies a collective or sustained criticism.
usage_notes: The '-an' suffix here points to the target of the criticism. It's often used when the criticism is widespread or coming from multiple sources.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sabay-sabay na **binatikusan** ng mga netizen ang kontrobersyal na pahayag ng artista.","translation":"The netizens simultaneously **criticized** the controversial statement of the celebrity."},{"sentence":"Huwag nating **batikusan** ang isang tao nang hindi nalalaman ang buong kwento.","translation":"Let's not **criticize** a person without knowing the whole story."}]

meaning_filipino: Marahan at mabagal na paggalaw o pag-abante, karaniwan sa pamamagitan ng pag-urong o pag-gapang.
original_explanation: This is the official speed of EDSA traffic at 5 PM on a Friday. It's how a turtle wins the race. It's also the progress you feel on your thesis after writing one paragraph in three hours. 'Usad pagong' (turtle's pace) is the national anthem of waiting.
usage_notes: Often used to describe traffic, a slow person, or a slow process. The verb form is umusad. 'Usad-pagong' is a very common idiom.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Usad**-pagong ang trapik sa SLEX tuwing long weekend.","translation":"The traffic on SLEX moves at a **turtle's pace** during long weekends."},{"sentence":"Isang **usad** lang ang nagawa ng pila sa loob ng isang oras.","translation":"The line only **inched forward** once in an hour."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang komposisyong musikal para sa isang solo instrumentista, kadalasan ay may kasamang piyano, na karaniwang binubuo ng tatlo o apat na magkakahiwalay na bahagi o movement.
etymology: Mula sa Italyano na "sonata", sa pamamagitan ng Espanyol na "sonata".
original_explanation: This is a fancy musical piece, usually for piano. Think of it as the musical equivalent of a three-course meal. It's not your usual LSS-inducing pop song; this is the kind of music your rich tita plays in her mansion or what you hear in classic Koreanovelas during dramatic moments.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa konteksto ng musikang klasikal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paborito niyang piyesa ay ang Moonlight **Sonata** ni Beethoven.","translation":"His favorite piece is Beethoven's Moonlight **Sonata**."},{"sentence":"Nag-aral siyang tumugtog ng isang kumplikadong **sonata** sa biyolin.","translation":"She studied how to play a complex **sonata** on the violin."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paggamit ng salapi o yaman para sa isang bagay o serbisyo.
original_explanation: That thing you do on the 15th and 30th, tapos sa 1st and 31st, puro ka na lang reklamo na wala ka nang pera. It's the "add to cart" impulse followed by the "Oh no, my wallet!" reality. The art of making your sweldo disappear.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of personal finance, budgeting, and shopping.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating bawasan ang ating **paggastos** sa mga hindi importanteng bagay.","translation":"We need to reduce our **spending** on non-essential things."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang naging **paggastos** para sa kasal niya.","translation":"The **expenditure** for her wedding was huge."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na lihim na nagnanakaw ng mga bagay mula sa bulsa o bag ng iba, karaniwan sa mga matataong lugar.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `man-` (tagagawa ng kilos) + pag-uulit ng unang pantig `du` + `dukot` (pagkuha mula sa sisidlan).
original_explanation: 'Yung kaaway mo sa jeep, sa MRT, at sa Divisoria. Sila 'yung may magic hands na bigla na lang nawawala ang cellphone o wallet mo. Sila ang dahilan kung bakit niyayakap mo ang bag mo na parang unan sa byahe. 'Keep your friends close, and your belongings closer' ang motto 'pag may mandurukot sa paligid.
usage_notes: Ang tamang anyo ay `mandurukot` dahil sa panuntunang pangwika kung saan ang `n` ng `man-` ay nagiging `r` bago ang ugat na nagsisimula sa `d`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa **mandurukot** sa loob ng bus.","translation":"Beware of **pickpockets** inside the bus."},{"sentence":"Nahuli ng pulis ang isang kilalang **mandurukot**.","translation":"The police caught a known **pickpocket**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pagpasok ng gamot sa katawan sa pamamagitan ng isang karayom at heringgilya; ang gamot na itinuturok.
original_explanation: That thing you dread getting at the doctor's office, but you know you need it. It's either the shot itself or the liquid inside the syringe. It's the reason kids suddenly develop a fear of doctors. "Takot ako sa iniksyon!"
usage_notes: Can refer to the act of injecting or the substance being injected.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan niya ng **iniksyon** ng anti-tetanus.","translation":"He needs an anti-tetanus **injection**."},{"sentence":"Masakit ba ang **iniksyon** para sa COVID-19 vaccine?","translation":"Is the **injection** for the COVID-19 vaccine painful?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang karga o lakas na elektrikal na taglay ng isang bagay; maaari ding tumukoy sa anting, bisa, o enerhiya ng isang bagay sa metaporikal na paraan.
original_explanation: The 'juice' in your phone's battery. Before power banks, this was a more magical concept, like the 'bisa' of an anting-anting. Now, it's the reason for our collective anxiety when the battery icon turns red. The root word for 'tablayan' (to charge).
usage_notes: While it technically means 'charge', it's less commonly used in everyday speech than 'karga'. It has a slightly more technical or literary feel.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nauubos na ang **tablay** ng aking selpon.","translation":"My cellphone's **charge** is running out."},{"sentence":"Tila may kakaibang **tablay** ang mga salita ng makata.","translation":"The poet's words seem to have a unique **potency**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtakip o natakpan ng isang lambong, belo, o anumang manipis na tela; o tumakip na parang isang lambong.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung ginagawa mo sa mukha mo gamit 'yung kumot 'pag ayaw mo pang bumangon. More formally, 'yung sa mga bride bago i-reveal ang kanilang "I do" face. Figuratively, "Friend, parang may kumambong na ulap sa isip ko, 'di ako makapag-isip nang maayos."
usage_notes: Can be used literally for veils or figuratively for things like fog, smoke, or sadness that cover something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang makapal na ulap ang **kumambong** sa tuktok ng bundok.","translation":"A thick cloud **shrouded** the mountain's peak."},{"sentence":"Ang lungkot na tila **kumambong** sa kanyang mga mata ay hindi maikakaila.","translation":"The sadness that seemed to **veil** her eyes was undeniable."}]

meaning_filipino: Gumamit ng payong bilang proteksyon sa ulan o init ng araw.
original_explanation: The most practical advice your nanay will ever give you. "Magpayong ka!" is the Philippine equivalent of "I love you, please don't get sick or turn 5 shades darker." It's a survival skill for both rainy season and high-noon UV rays.
usage_notes: Can also be used figuratively to mean "to give advice" (`magpayo`), but the literal meaning of using an umbrella is more common for this specific word form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **magpayong** dahil napakainit ng sikat ng araw ngayon.","translation":"Don't forget to **use an umbrella** because the sun is very hot today."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula na siyang **magpayong** nang biglang bumuhos ang malakas na ulan.","translation":"She started to **use an umbrella** when the heavy rain suddenly poured."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na pinino o hinimay sa pamamagitan ng pagkaskas sa isang kudkuran. Maaari ring tumukoy sa anyong pangnagdaan ng pandiwang 'kudkurin'.
original_explanation: This is what happens to coconut before it becomes gata (coconut milk) or that bukayo your lola makes. It's the result of some serious arm workout using a 'kudkuran'. Think of it as shredding, but for tropical ingredients. 'Kinudkod na yelo' is halo-halo's best friend.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pandiwa sa anyong pangnagdaan ('Kinudkod niya ang niyog') o bilang pang-uri na naglalarawan sa isang bagay na kinayod ('Ginamit niya ang kinudkod na niyog').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap ang bibingka na may **kinudkod** na niyog sa ibabaw.","translation":"The rice cake is delicious with **grated** coconut on top."},{"sentence":"**Kinudkod** niya ang buong melon para gawing palamig.","translation":"She **grated** the whole melon to make a cold drink."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi katulad ng karaniwan; may pagkakaiba o natatangi.
etymology: From ka- + iba. The ka- prefix here denotes being of the same kind, but in combination with iba (other/different), it forms an adjective meaning 'different from'.
original_explanation: 'Yung friend mong naglalagay ng ketchup sa ice cream. O 'yung feeling mo sa ex mo ngayon vs. dati. "Parang **iba** ka na." Can be a compliment (unique) or a red flag (strange). It's all about the delivery.
usage_notes: Can be used to mean 'different from' (kaiba sa/kay) or 'unusual'/'strange' on its own.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kaiba** talaga ang panlasa niya sa musika.","translation":"His/Her taste in music is really **different**."},{"sentence":"**Kaiba** siya sa lahat ng lalaking nakilala ko.","translation":"He is **different** from all the men I have met."}]

translation: to be thrown off; to splash; to be fired
meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis at biglaang pag-angat o paglipad ng isang bagay mula sa kinalalagyan nito dahil sa puwersa; maaari ring tumukoy sa pagkatanggal sa trabaho.
original_explanation: Ever fried hotdogs and the oil attacked you? That's it, tumalsik. Or when your boss says 'You're fired!' and you get booted out of the office. It's the 'yeet' of the Filipino language, whether it's oil, water, or a person from their job.
usage_notes: Has a common slang meaning of 'to be fired from a job' (natalsik sa trabaho).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumalsik** ang mantika mula sa kawali at napaso ako.","translation":"The oil **splashed** from the pan and I got burned."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa lagi siyang huli, **tumalsik** siya sa kanyang trabaho.","translation":"Because he was always late, he **was fired** from his job."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan o muwebles na karaniwang tinutulugan o pinagpapahingahan.
original_explanation: Your best friend after a long day of adulting. It's the silent witness to your late-night scrolling, Netflix binges, and existential crises. Also, the final boss when you need to get up in the morning. "5 more minutes" is its favorite spell.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko nang humiga sa **kama** at matulog.","translation":"I want to lie down on the **bed** and sleep."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang tumalon sa **kama**, baka masira.","translation":"Don't jump on the **bed**, it might break."}]

meaning_filipino: Isama, ihalo, o ipasok ang isang bagay sa isa pang bagay upang maging bahagi ng isang kabuuan.
original_explanation: It's what you do when you're making a group project and you have to **ilangkap** your lazy groupmate's half-baked contribution into the final presentation. Or when you're cooking adobo and you decide to throw in some potatoes and hard-boiled eggs. 'Ihalo mo na rin 'yan!'
usage_notes: Often used in formal or technical contexts, like in recipes, chemical processes, or legal documents.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ilangkap** mo ang harina nang paunti-unti sa basang sangkap.","translation":"**Incorporate** the flour gradually into the wet ingredients."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **ilangkap** ang mga bagong ideya sa lumang sistema.","translation":"New ideas need to be **incorporated** into the old system."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging hindi mapakali, magalaw, o mapaglaro sa paraang maaaring makagambala.
original_explanation: The energy of a kid who just ate a whole bag of candy. It's that 'di mapakali' feeling when you're waiting for a very important text message. Toddlers are the grandmasters of likot.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi mapigilan ang **likot** ng bata.","translation":"The child's **restlessness** cannot be stopped."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **likot**, nahulog siya sa upuan.","translation":"Because of his **fidgetiness**, he fell off the chair."}]

translation: to mock; to scorn; to insult
meaning_filipino: Magsalita nang may paghamak o pag-insulto sa kapwa, kadalasan ay tungkol sa kanilang anyo, katayuan, o kakayahan.
original_explanation: The act of body-shaming, poverty-shaming, or basically any kind of shaming. It's looking down on someone and making them feel small. It's a low-blow move. "Ang hilig mong manlait, perfect ka ba?"
usage_notes: A strong word that implies contempt and looking down on someone. Stronger than 'mang-asar' (to tease).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **manlait** ng kapwa dahil lang sa kanilang pananamit.","translation":"Don't **mock** others just because of how they dress."},{"sentence":"Masakit marinig ang mga salitang ginamit niya para **manlait**.","translation":"It's painful to hear the words he used to **insult**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na pamilihan o merkado, karaniwang pansamantala o mas maliit kaysa sa pangunahing palengke, kung saan nagbebenta ng mga sariwang produkto tulad ng isda, karne, at gulay.
original_explanation: It's the mini-me version of a 'palengke' (wet market). The 'talipapa' is your neighborhood go-to for fresh fish, veggies, and meat when you're too lazy to go to the main market. It's smaller, more convenient, and probably where your mom sends you for a last-minute errand to buy onions or garlic. It's the sari-sari store of fresh goods.
usage_notes: A very common term for a small, local wet market.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng sariwang tilapia sa **talipapa** kaninang umaga.","translation":"I bought fresh tilapia at the **small market** this morning."},{"sentence":"Mas mura ang gulay sa **talipapa** kaysa sa supermarket.","translation":"Vegetables are cheaper at the **satellite market** than at the supermarket."}]

meaning_filipino: May kakayahang magtimpi, magpigil sa sarili, at mag-isip nang mabuti bago gumawa ng isang desisyon o aksyon, lalo na kapag nasa ilalim ng matinding emosyon.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `mapag-` at `hunusdili` (pagpipigil sa sarili, pagtitimpi).
original_explanation: Ito yung taong hindi agad-agad nagre-reply sa angry email. They take a deep breath, drink water, maybe walk around the block, bago sila gumanti. The opposite of being 'marupok'. Sila yung hindi nag-a-add to cart sa 12.12 sale kahit andaming vouchers, kasi they practice self-control. A rare and valuable skill.
usage_notes: Isang pormal at pampanitikang salita. Ipinahihiwatig nito ang mataas na antas ng kontrol sa emosyon at pag-iisip.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Manatiling **mapaghunusdili** sa lahat ng oras, lalo na sa gitna ng kaguluhan.","translation":"Remain **self-controlled** at all times, especially in the midst of chaos."},{"sentence":"Isang lider na **mapaghunusdili** ang kailangan ng bayan.","translation":"The country needs a **temperate** leader."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o paghimok sa isang tao na maging kalmado; ang pagpapakalma sa isang sitwasyon o damdamin.
original_explanation: This is what your friend tells you when you're about to send a very angry email to your boss at 2 AM. 'Bes, **magpahinahon** ka muna. Chill.' It's the act of de-escalating, whether it's your own anger, a heated argument, or a crying child. It's the verbal equivalent of a cup of chamomile tea.
usage_notes: Can be used reflexively ('magpahinahon ka' - calm yourself down) or to mean pacifying others ('sinubukan niyang magpahinahon sa nag-aaway' - he tried to pacify the fighters).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinusubukan ng ina na **magpahinahon** sa kanyang umiiyak na anak.","translation":"The mother is trying to **pacify** her crying child."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magpahinahon** bago ka magdesisyon.","translation":"You need to **calm down** before you make a decision."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng kapangyarihan o lakas sa paraang mapanira, di-makatarungan, o labis.
original_explanation: This is what happens when someone gets a little bit of power and suddenly thinks they're the final boss in a video game. From corrupt officials to that one micromanaging team lead, 'mag-abuso' is the act of using your position to make others miserable. It's the ultimate 'with great power comes great irresponsibility' move.
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of power dynamics, such as domestic violence ('pang-aabuso sa tahanan'), substance abuse ('pag-abuso sa droga'), or abuse of authority ('pag-abuso sa kapangyarihan').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mag-abuso** sa kabaitan ng iyong mga kaibigan.","translation":"Don't **abuse** the kindness of your friends."},{"sentence":"Ang sinumang opisyal na napatunayang nag-abuso sa pwesto ay dapat maparusahan.","translation":"Any official proven to have abused their position must be punished."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdarasal ng rosaryo, isang serye ng mga panalangin sa relihiyong Katoliko na ginagamitan ng isang kuwintas ng mga butil.
original_explanation: That moment at 6 PM when your lola calls everyone to the living room to pray. It's a spiritual marathon of Hail Marys and Our Fathers. For many Pinoys, it's a core memory from childhood, often done for special intentions, like passing an exam or hoping your crush notices you.
usage_notes: Specific to the Catholic practice of praying the rosary.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gabi-gabi, sama-samang **nagrorosaryo** ang pamilya nila.","translation":"Every night, their family **prays the rosary** together."},{"sentence":"Nagpunta sila sa simbahan upang **magrosaryo** para sa kaluluwa ng kanilang yumaong kamag-anak.","translation":"They went to the church to **pray the rosary** for the soul of their deceased relative."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng nagpapaupa ng bahay, silid, o gusaling apartment.
original_explanation: Siya yung tita na buwan-buwan mong ka-chat sa Messenger para sa bayad ng renta. Minsan, mas updated pa siya sa lovelife mo kaysa sa nanay mo. 'Hija, may bisita ka na namang lalaki kagabi?'
usage_notes: Used for women who rent out property, from a single room to an entire house. The male equivalent is 'kasero'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtaas na naman ng upa ang **kasera** namin.","translation":"Our **landlady** raised the rent again."},{"sentence":"Mabait ang **kasera** ko, pinapahiram pa ako ng bigas.","translation":"My **landlady** is kind, she even lends me rice."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kending prutas na pinatuyo at inasnan, karaniwang mula sa prunelas o iba pang katulad na prutas. Ito ay may maalat-alat at maasim-asim na tamis.
etymology: Mula sa Hokkien na "tsiam-pué" (鹹梅), na nangangahulugang "inasnang prunelas".
original_explanation: That red, salty, sour, and slightly sweet dried plum candy that makes your face scrunch up but you can't stop eating it. It's the 'pampagising' snack you buy in small plastic packs. From Hokkien.
usage_notes: Often red or orange in color. Also known as kiamoy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong kutkutin ang **tsampoy** habang nanonood ng pelikula.","translation":"Eating **preserved sour plums** is my favorite snack while watching a movie."},{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng isang pakete ng **tsampoy** sa tindahan ni Aling Nena.","translation":"I bought a pack of **kiamoy** from Aling Nena's store."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na instrumento na lumilikha ng matining na tunog kapag hinipan, karaniwang ginagamit ng pulis, tanod, o reperi.
original_explanation: The ultimate tool of authority for barangay tanods, traffic enforcers, and PE teachers. One sharp toot from a 'silbato' can stop traffic, halt a basketball game, or make you feel like you're in trouble even if you did nothing wrong.
usage_notes: Refers to the physical object. The sound or act is 'pito' or 'sipol'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumito nang malakas ang pulis gamit ang kanyang **silbato**.","translation":"The policeman blew his **whistle** loudly."},{"sentence":"Nawala ng reperi ang kanyang **silbato** sa kalagitnaan ng laro.","translation":"The referee lost his **whistle** in the middle of the game."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang bagay, karaniwang papel o tela, na gusot, lukot, o hindi na makinis dahil sa pagkakakuyumos.
original_explanation: Describes the state of your shirt after a 12-hour flight, or that P20 bill you found in your jeans pocket after laundry. It's the physical manifestation of stress on an object. The opposite of 'plantsado' (ironed flat).
usage_notes: This meaning refers to physical texture. It is a homonym of 'yamutmot' (grumbling).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Yamutmot** na ang liham nang matagpuan niya ito.","translation":"The letter was already **crumpled** when he found it."},{"sentence":"Ayusin mo ang damit mong **yamutmot** bago ka umalis.","translation":"Fix your **wrinkled** clothes before you leave."}]

translation: to collect payment, to charge, to dun
meaning_filipino: Ang paghingi o pagkolekta ng bayad para sa isang utang, produkto, o serbisyo.
original_explanation: The act of transforming from a friend into a collections agent. To **singil** someone is a delicate art. You can go subtle with a "Uy, musta na?" or go full-on telenovela villain mode. It’s the high-stakes social maneuver that tests the very foundation of your friendship.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa mga anyong 'sumingil', 'siningil', 'sisingilin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailan mo ba ako **sisingilin** sa pinahiram mong pera?","translation":"When are you going to **charge** me for the money you lent?"},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi kita **sisingilin** agad.","translation":"Don't worry, I won't **collect** from you right away."}]

translation: act of joking or jesting; kidding
meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagbibiro o paggawa ng isang bagay na hindi seryoso upang magdulot ng katatawanan.
etymology: From pag- + si- + siste, from Spanish chiste (joke).
original_explanation: The art of the 'charot' or 'joke lang'. It's when you say something outrageous and then immediately follow it up with a laugh to signal that you're not serious. "Crush kita... charot!" That's pagsisiste. It's a social lubricant, a way to test the waters, or just plain having fun. From the Spanish word 'chiste' (joke).
usage_notes: Often used to describe playful teasing or making light of a situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napikon siya sa **pagsisiste** ng kanyang mga kaibigan.","translation":"He got annoyed by his friends' **jesting**."},{"sentence":"Hilig niya ang **pagsisiste** kaya marami ang natutuwa sa kanya.","translation":"He is fond of **joking around**, which is why many people like him."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pantukoy na ginagamit sa pagtukoy sa isang tiyak na pangngalang pambalana (isahan). Ito ay katumbas ng 'the' sa Ingles.
original_explanation: The OG article. The Beyoncé of Filipino grammar – a single word that commands attention. It's the spotlight you put on a noun. It's not just 'babae' (a woman), it's '**ang** babae' (THE woman). It's the difference between being 'a' choice and being 'THE' choice. It marks the subject of the sentence, the main character of your chika.
usage_notes: Ang pinakasalin at mahalagang pantukoy sa Tagalog para sa isahang pangngalang pambalana. Ang pangmaramihang katumbas nito ay 'ang mga'. Minamarkahan nito ang 'paksa' o 'tuon' ng pangungusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabait **ang** bata.","translation":"**The** child is kind."},{"sentence":"Nawawala **ang** pusa ko.","translation":"My cat is missing."},{"sentence":"**Ang** ganda ng Pilipinas!","translation":"**The** Philippines is beautiful!"}]

translation: to fence; to enclose with a fence
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagtatayo ng bakod sa paligid ng isang lugar o ari-arian upang magsilbing harang o pananda ng hangganan.
original_explanation: It's what you do to your property when the chismosa next door is getting too interested in your life. You're not just building a fence; you're building a 'minding my own business' barrier. Also what a subdivision developer does first before anything else.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of property, land, or creating a physical boundary for security or privacy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya silang **magbakood** sa kanilang bagong lupain para sa seguridad.","translation":"They decided to **fence** their new land for security."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magbakood** para hindi makapasok ang mga asong-gala.","translation":"We need to **put up a fence** so stray dogs can't get in."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng isang gawain, sitwasyon, o konsepto na nangangailangan ng malaking pagsisikap, kaalaman, o kasanayan upang magawa o maunawaan.
original_explanation: The state of your life during finals week. 'Yung math problem na mas complicated pa sa love life mo. Trying to assemble IKEA furniture without the manual. Or simply trying to get a Grab at 5 PM on a Friday payday. Mahirap is the default setting for adulting.
usage_notes: One of the most common adjectives in Tagalog. Can describe tasks, concepts, situations, etc.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Mahirap** ang pagsusulit sa Matematika kanina.","translation":"The Math exam earlier was **difficult**."},{"sentence":"**Mahirap** kalimutan ang unang pag-ibig.","translation":"It's **hard** to forget your first love."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapang pansaka o panghardin na may ngipin o tulis sa dulo, ginagamit sa pag-iipon ng mga tuyong dahon, damo, o sa pagpapantay ng lupa.
original_explanation: The official tool of every subdivision's maintenance crew and your dad on a Sunday morning. It's that long stick with a comb at the end used to gather all the dead leaves (and neighborhood chismis). The verb form, *kalaykayin*, is the act of raking.
usage_notes: The tool itself. The verb is "magkalaykay" or "kalaykayin".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinuha ni Tatay ang **kalaykay** upang linisin ang mga tuyong dahon sa bakuran.","translation":"Dad got the **rake** to clean the dry leaves in the yard."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi esensyal, hindi kinakailangan para sa isang layunin; maaaring isantabi o alisin.
etymology: Mula sa salitang "kailangan" na may unlaping "di-".
original_explanation: The official status of your college minor subject. Also, the 10th bag you bought this month, the extra chismis you shared that started a fight, and that meeting that could have been an email. If it adds clutter and not value, it's di-kailangan. Marie Kondo would have a field day.
usage_notes: Ang "di-" ay isang kolokyal na pagpapaikli ng "hindi".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinanggal niya ang mga **di-kailangan** na gamit sa kanyang bag para gumaan ito.","translation":"She removed the **unnecessary** items from her bag to make it lighter."},{"sentence":"Iwasan ang paggastos sa mga bagay na **di-kailangan**.","translation":"Avoid spending on things that are **not needed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panlabas na takip sa pinakatuktok ng isang gusali o bahay na nagsisilbing proteksyon laban sa ulan at araw.
original_explanation: The roof over your head. The thing that turns into a percussion instrument during a typhoon, making you wonder if your 'yero' (galvanized iron sheet) will suddenly fly to the next barangay. Having a solid 'bubong' is a life goal, literally meaning you have a home.
usage_notes: A fundamental word in housing and construction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang kumpunihin ang butas sa **bubong** bago dumating ang tag-ulan.","translation":"The hole in the **roof** needs to be repaired before the rainy season arrives."},{"sentence":"Ang pangarap niya ay magkaroon ng sariling bahay at **bubong**.","translation":"His dream is to have his own house and **roof**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng panloloko, pagbibiro nang labis, o paggawa sa isang tao na magmukhang hangal.
etymology: From `pang-` + reduplication of the first syllable `u-` + `ulol` (crazy, rabid, foolish).
original_explanation: This is when the 'prank' goes too far. It's not just a simple joke; it's making someone look like a complete 'tanga'.
