usage_notes: Used both for an actual infant and as a term of endearment, similar to "babe". It's more common than the traditional Tagalog word "sanggol" in casual conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulog na ang **baby**, huwag kayong maingay.","translation":"The **baby** is asleep, don't be noisy."},{"sentence":"Hi **baby**, miss na kita.","translation":"Hi **baby**, I miss you already."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng isang bagay upang maging bago o sariwa muli ang isang alaala, kaalaman, o damdamin.
original_explanation: Like hitting F5 on your brain. It's what you do when you need to review your notes before an exam, or when you tell your friend the whole story of your breakup for the 5th time just to 'refresh' their memory of why your ex is trash.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of memories (`pasariwain ang alaala`), knowledge, or even physical things like food, though less common for the latter.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **pasariwain** ang mga alaala natin sa lugar na ito.","translation":"I want to **refresh** our memories in this place."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **pasariwain** ang usapan tungkol sa mga patakaran ng kumpanya.","translation":"The discussion about the company policies needs to be **renewed**."}]

translation: to sway, to stagger, to reel
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkawala ng balanse at bahagyang pagewang-gewang, karaniwang dahil sa pagkahilo, kalasingan, o biglaang pagtulak.
original_explanation: Ito yung lakad mo pauwi galing sa inuman with friends. Feeling mo straight line lang tinatahak mo, pero sa CCTV mukha kang nag-interpretive dance. Pwede ring mangyari 'to 'pag sobrang puyat sa K-drama o sa pag-render ng video.
usage_notes: This is the completed action (past tense) form. The infinitive is 'sumuray'. The present tense is 'sumusuray'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumuray** ang matandang lalaki dahil sa matinding pagod.","translation":"The old man **staggered** due to extreme fatigue."},{"sentence":"Bigla siyang **sumuray** nang marinig ang balita.","translation":"He suddenly **reeled** upon hearing the news."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang likidong nagmumula sa bibig; laway na inilabas o idinura.
original_explanation: It's the stuff you spit out. Gross, but a daily reality. Seeing *lura* on the sidewalk is a classic Pinoy street experience. It's also what you metaphorically do to someone you despise (duraan sa mukha). In the age of COVID, it became public enemy number one.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with `dura`. `Lura` is the noun, `lumura` or `ilura` is the verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bawal magtapon ng **lura** sa sahig ng bus.","translation":"It is forbidden to dispose of **spit** on the bus floor."},{"sentence":"May bakas ng **lura** sa kanyang damit.","translation":"There was a trace of **spittle** on his shirt."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa paraan ng paggawa o pagbili nang maramihan, pangkalahatan, o hindi isinasaalang-alang ang bawat isa.
original_explanation: The Divisoria mindset. Bakit ka bibili ng isang piraso kung pwede namang isang dosena for a cheaper price? It's buying in bulk, thinking collectively. Parang sa team building, dapat palansak ang pag-iisip, walang iwanan.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng komersyo (hal., 'bentang palansak') o balarila (hal., 'pangngalang palansak').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas mura kung **palansak** ang pagbili ng bigas.","translation":"It's cheaper if you buy rice **in bulk**."},{"sentence":"Ang salitang 'kawan' ay isang halimbawa ng pangngalang **palansak**.","translation":"The word 'flock' is an example of a **collective** noun."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglilinis gamit ang walis na naganap na.
original_explanation: Tapos na. Clean na ang floor, pero ang sakit pa rin ng likod mo. Eto yung ginawa mo bago dumating yung mga bisita para hindi ka mapagalitan ni Mama. Past tense ng national household chore.
usage_notes: Ang unlaping 'nag-' ay nagpapahiwatig ng kilos na natapos na.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagwalis** ako ng buong bahay kaninang umaga.","translation":"I **swept** the whole house this morning."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **nagwalis** ng mga tuyong dahon sa bakuran?","translation":"Who **swept** the dry leaves in the yard?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang taunang kapistahan ng mga Kristiyano na ginugunita ang kapanganakan ni Hesukristo, na ipinagdiriwang tuwing ika-25 ng Disyembre.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "Pascua," na orihinal na tumutukoy sa Pasko ng Pagkabuhay (Easter) ngunit ginagamit na ngayon para sa Pasko ng Kapanganakan (Christmas).
original_explanation: In the Philippines, this isn't just a day, it's a whole season that starts the moment the '-ber' months hit. It's the season of Jose Mari Chan, Simbang Gabi, bibingka, puto bumbong, 13th-month pay, and endless family reunions where your titas ask, "Kailan ka ikakasal?"
usage_notes: Often used with 'Maligayang' to mean 'Merry Christmas.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maligayang **Pasko** sa inyong lahat!","translation":"Merry **Christmas** to you all!"},{"sentence":"Nagsisimula na ang Simbang Gabi kapag malapit na ang **Pasko**.","translation":"Simbang Gabi starts when **Christmas** is near."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bulalas na nagpapahayag ng pagkagulat, pagkabigla, pagkadismaya, o matinding damdamin. Ito ay pinagsamang pangalan nina Hesus, Maria, at Jose.
etymology: Isang portmanteau ng mga pangalang Espanyol na "Jesús, María y José" (Hesus, Maria, at Jose).
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino exclamation for when things go wrong, from dropping your phone to seeing your Meralco bill. It's the holy trinity of Pinoy frustration. Your lola's favorite word. **Susmaryosep**, ang mahal na ng bilihin!
usage_notes: Isang napakakaraniwang ekspresyon na ginagamit ng lahat ng edad, bagaman mas madalas iugnay sa mga nakatatandang henerasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Susmaryosep**! Bakit ang kalat ng kwarto mo?","translation":"Good heavens! Why is your room so messy?"},{"sentence":"Nanalo ako sa lotto? **Susmaryosep**!","translation":"I won the lottery? **Oh my God**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na sukat ng inuming may alkohol, karaniwang iniinom nang isang lagukan.
original_explanation: The start of many great stories and 'di ko na matandaan' moments. Inuman culture's 'one small step for man.' Also what you get from the doctor, but that's a different kind of 'aray'. 'Tara, shot!' is the national anthem after 5 PM on a Friday.
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of drinking alcoholic beverages. Can also refer to a vaccine shot (e.g., 'booster shot').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isa pang **shot** ng tequila, pakiusap!","translation":"One more **shot** of tequila, please!"},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng mahabang linggo, kailangan ko ng **shot**.","translation":"After a long week, I need a **shot**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang aktibong proteksyon laban sa sunog; isang koneksyon kung saan maaaring kumuha ng suplay ng tubig ang mga bumbero.
original_explanation: 'Yung pulang bakal na nakatayo sa kanto na parang laging naghihintay lang. Bawal i-park-an, bawal tambayan. Pag may sunog, ito ang VIP. Ito ang source ng 'unli-water' para sa mga bumbero. Sa mga pelikula, ito yung nababangga ng kotse tapos biglang may fountain.
usage_notes: Isang deskriptibong parirala. Ang salitang 'hydrant' ay naiintindihan din.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagbabawal ang pagparada sa tapat ng **bomba sa sunog**.","translation":"Parking in front of a **fire hydrant** is prohibited."},{"sentence":"Mabilis na ikinabit ng mga bumbero ang kanilang hose sa **bomba sa sunog**.","translation":"The firefighters quickly connected their hose to the **fire hydrant**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang panggitnang palapag sa pagitan ng mga pangunahing palapag ng isang gusali, karaniwang mas mababa ang kisame kaysa sa mga regular na palapag.
original_explanation: That 'half-floor' in a building, like a loft. It's the spot in the coffee shop with the comfy couches that's always taken. In a house, it's often the mini-library or TV area that overlooks the living room. It's basically the architectural equivalent of 'It's complicated'—not quite the ground floor, not quite the second floor.
usage_notes: Used in architecture and real estate contexts. 'Entresuwelo' is a synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa **mesanin** ang opisina ng tagapamahala.","translation":"The manager's office is on the **mezzanine**."},{"sentence":"May maliit na aklatan sila sa **mesanin** ng kanilang bahay.","translation":"They have a small library on the **mezzanine** of their house."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi gumagamit ng panlilinlang o pandaraya; tapat at matuwid.
original_explanation: This is the ideal state of your weighing scale in the morning. Or a game of Uno where no one is hiding a Draw 4 card. In relationships, it's open communication, no secret DMs. Basically, what you see is what you get, no hidden agenda, no "scam."
usage_notes: Often used to describe games, competitions, transactions, or people's intentions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko ng isang relasyong **walang-daya** at puno ng tiwala.","translation":"I want a relationship **without deceit** and full of trust."},{"sentence":"Siguraduhin nating **walang-daya** ang botohan sa darating na eleksyon.","translation":"Let's ensure the voting in the upcoming election is **fair**."}]

meaning_filipino: Makapal at maitim na usok, karaniwang mula sa pagsunog ng isang bagay na hindi ganap na natutupok.
original_explanation: That thick, choking smoke you get from your neighbor's burning basura, a busted jeepney, or a really intense inihaw session. It's the kind of smoke that makes you cough and wave your hand in front of your face like you're trying to clear your life's problems.
usage_notes: Often has a negative connotation, implying thick, unpleasant, or toxic smoke. More intense than 'usok'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **asuos** ang kalsada dahil sa nasusunog na gusali.","translation":"The road was full of **dense smoke** because of the burning building."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga gawain, kagamitan, o lupain na may kaugnayan sa pagsasaka.
original_explanation: This is the adjective for all things bukid-related. It's less common than 'pansaka' but has the same vibe. Think 'masakang lupain' (farmland) or 'kagamitang masaka' (farming tools). It's the OG 'farm-to-table' aesthetic before it was cool. This is the lingo of the DA (Department of Agriculture), not usually the city slicker.
usage_notes: 'Pansaka' is a more common synonym for 'agricultural'. 'Masaka' is a bit more formal or literary.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang rehiyon na ito ay kilala sa malawak na **masakang** lupain.","translation":"This region is known for its vast **agricultural** lands."},{"sentence":"Marami pa ring pamilya ang umaasa sa mga gawaing **masaka**.","translation":"Many families still depend on **agricultural** work."}]

translation: to climb, to clamber, to scale
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-akyat sa isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng paggapang o paggamit ng kamay at paa, lalo na sa matarik o mahirap na lugar.
original_explanation: This isn't just a simple 'akyat'. Kumatkat implies a struggle. It's what a cat does to get on your roof, or what you do to climb a coconut tree without a ladder. It’s the action of scrambling up something, using all your limbs. Think Spider-Man, but maybe less graceful and with more 'aray!'.
usage_notes: Emphasizes difficulty and the use of hands and feet in climbing, as opposed to simply walking up stairs.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bata ay mabilis na **kumatkat** sa puno ng mangga para kumuha ng bunga.","translation":"The child quickly **clambered** up the mango tree to get some fruit."},{"sentence":"Hirap siyang **kumatkat** sa bakod dahil sa taas nito.","translation":"He had a hard time **scaling** the fence because of its height."}]

meaning_filipino: Karne, karaniwang baka, na minarinado sa toyo, suka, bawang, at iba pang pampalasa, at pagkatapos ay pinatuyo o pinirito.
etymology: From Spanish 'tapa', which means 'lid' or 'cover', but in the Philippines, it evolved to mean cured meat, possibly from the method of preserving.
original_explanation: The undisputed king of the -silog breakfast empire (Tapsilog = Tapa + Sinangag + Itlog). It's that savory, slightly sweet, garlicky beef that makes you forget you have an 8 AM meeting. The perfect cure for a hangover or just a regular morning.
usage_notes: When someone says 'tapa' in a food context, they almost always mean beef tapa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong almusal ang **tapa** na may sinangag at itlog.","translation":"My favorite breakfast is **cured beef** with fried rice and egg."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-alis o pag-iwan sa isang lugar, tao, o kalagayan.
original_explanation: The noun form of 'ghosting.' It's the act of leaving, the departure itself. More poetic and dramatic than simply 'pag-alis.' This is the word you use for break-up songs or when a hero leaves their hometown for an adventure.
usage_notes: A literary and formal word. Often found in poems, songs, and formal speeches. More commonly used as a verb 'lisanin' or 'lumisan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang biglaang **lisan** ay nag-iwan ng maraming tanong.","translation":"His sudden **departure** left many questions."},{"sentence":"Ang **lisan** sa sariling bayan ay isang mapait na karanasan para sa maraming OFW.","translation":"The **act of leaving** one's own country is a bitter experience for many OFWs."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan pinalalaki at ibinebenta ang mga halaman, puno, at iba pang pananim.
original_explanation: Ito yung 'happy place' ng mga Plantita at Plantito. Dito sila bumibili ng mga bagong 'anak' na succulents, herbs, o ornamental plants. Parang shopping mall, pero para sa mga halaman.
usage_notes: Karaniwang tumutukoy sa isang lugar para sa mga halaman, hindi sa isang lugar para sa mga bata (na tinatawag ding "nursery" sa Ingles).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumunta kami sa **narseri** para bumili ng mga bagong bulaklak para sa hardin.","translation":"We went to the **plant nursery** to buy new flowers for the garden."}]

meaning_filipino: Paligiran o gipitin ang isang tao o bagay upang hindi makatakas o makakilos; sukulin.
etymology: `pa-` + `sukob` + `-in`. 'Sukob' can mean to take cover together, but in this context, it is related to 'sukol' (to corner).
original_explanation: When the deadlines, bills, and your boss's follow-ups all hit you at the same time. You feel cornered, like a character in a fighting game with no health left. That's 'pasukubin'. It's being trapped with no easy way out, whether by enemies, problems, or your tita asking when you're getting married.
usage_notes: This is a less common word. 'Sukulin' is more frequently used and synonymous.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan nilang **pasukubin** ang takas sa isang eskinita.","translation":"They tried to **corner** the fugitive in an alley."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi tayo papayag na **pasukubin** ka ng iyong mga problema.","translation":"Don't worry, we won't let you be **overwhelmed** by your problems."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang hiram na tumutukoy sa isang bagay o tao na may katangiang masining, o nagpapakita ng interes sa sining, kadalasan sa isang impormal o modernong paraan.
original_explanation: When your feed is full of museum visits, indie film posters, and latte art. It's the aesthetic of Escolta or Cubao Expo. Less formal than 'artistiko', more about the vibe and the lifestyle. "Gusto ko yung cafe, ang artsy ng pader."
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa impormal na pakikipag-usap at social media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **artsy** ng mga kuha mo sa Instagram!","translation":"Your shots on Instagram are so **artsy**!"},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang magsuot ng mga damit na **artsy**.","translation":"She likes to wear **artsy** clothes."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang di-sinasadyang mahulog mula sa isang kinalalagyan; ang hindi makapasa sa isang pagsusulit o kurso.
original_explanation: Two kinds of lagapak moments. First, when you accidentally drop your phone and your soul leaves your body for a second. Second, the academic version: when your grade is a solid singko and you mabagsak the subject. Both are painful, but one might cost you your graduation.
usage_notes: Can mean literally falling/being dropped, or figuratively failing in an academic context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka at baka **mabagsak** mo ang mga baso.","translation":"Be careful or you might **drop** the glasses."},{"sentence":"Kung hindi ka mag-aaral, tiyak na **mabagsak** ka sa pagsusulit.","translation":"If you don't study, you will surely **fail** the exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa dalawa o higit pang bagay na may parehong sukat ng haba.
original_explanation: Yung traffic sa EDSA at sa C5 tuwing rush hour—magkasinghaba. Or when you and your bestie get the same haircut and your hair is now of equal length. It's about having the same measurement from end to end.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang dalawang lubid ay **magkasinghaba**.","translation":"The two ropes are **of the same length**."},{"sentence":"Dapat **magkasinghaba** ang mga kurtinang ilalagay mo sa bintana.","translation":"The curtains you will put on the window should be **of the same length**."}]

translation: to die (plural); for many to die
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpanaw o pagkawala ng buhay ng maramihang tao, hayop, o bagay.
etymology: From `mang-` + `ka-` + `patay` (dead). The `ka-` infix often implies a collective or group action/state.
original_explanation: This is the plural form of 'dead.' Not just one person, but a group. Think the ending of a Shakespearean tragedy, or what happens to your houseplants when you go on a two-week vacation. 'Namatay' is for one, 'nangamatay' is for many. It’s a word used for epic-level failures, like when your whole team gets wiped out in Mobile Legends. 'Nangamatay na naman tayong lahat!'
usage_notes: The subject is always plural. It implies a collective or widespread death.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming isda ang **nangamatay** dahil sa polusyon sa ilog.","translation":"Many fish **died** because of the pollution in the river."},{"sentence":"**Nangamatay** ang lahat ng halaman ko dahil sa sobrang init.","translation":"All my plants **died** because of the extreme heat."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalakbay o lumilibot nang walang tiyak na patutunguhan; palibut-libot.
original_explanation: The official term for "laagan" or "layas". This is you on a weekend, hopping from mall to cafe to park. It's your cat at 3 AM. It’s the "R" in "BRB" (be right back), but the roaming part takes 3 hours. "Saan ka na naman **gumagala**?" is the default greeting from your mom when you get home late.
usage_notes: Present tense form. Describes an ongoing action of wandering or roaming.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May asong **gumagala** sa kalye tuwing gabi.","translation":"There's a dog **roaming** the street every night."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **gumagala** sa iba't ibang bansa.","translation":"She loves **wandering** in different countries."}]

meaning_filipino: Katulad ng 'kire', ito ay tumutukoy sa isang taong, karaniwan ay babae, na malikot ang kilos at mahilig magpakita ng pagka-mapang-akit sa paraang hindi direkta.
original_explanation: 'Kiri' is the twin sister of 'kire'. It's basically the same vibe: playful, attention-seeking flirtatiousness. If 'kire' is the glance, 'kiri' is the giggle that follows. It's the 'hehe, stop it!' while playfully hitting someone's arm.
usage_notes: Tulad ng 'kire', ito ay isang lumang termino at hindi na gaanong karaniwan kumpara sa 'malandi'. Ito rin ay halos eksklusibong ginagamit para sa mga babae.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa pagiging **kiri** noong dalaga pa.","translation":"She was known for being **flirtatious** when she was still single."},{"sentence":"Ang mga kilos niyang **kiri** ay ikinaiinis ng ibang babae.","translation":"Her **coquettish** actions annoy the other women."}]

translation: to offer, to present, to serve
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aalay, pag-aabot, o paghahandog ng isang bagay sa isang tao, diyos, o altar.
original_explanation: This is a very formal, almost ceremonial word. Think of priests offering something at the altar, or in olden times, presenting a gift to a king. Today, you might use it sarcastically when you serve your friend food with extra effort: 'Heto na po, Kamahalan, nag-**hayin** na po ako ng agahan mo.' It's 'to serve' with a side of reverence.
usage_notes: Often used in religious, ceremonial, or very formal contexts. Less common in casual conversation than 'maghanda' or 'magbigay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga deboto ay **naghayin** ng mga bulaklak sa altar.","translation":"The devotees **offered** flowers at the altar."},{"sentence":"Ang pamilya ay **naghayin** ng masaganang pagkain para sa kanilang mga bisita.","translation":"The family **served** a bountiful meal for their guests."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng ibang sangkap o elemento; hindi puro.
original_explanation: Like your feelings for your ex—hindi pure hate, may konting 'what if' pa. Or like that drink na may kung anong chemical aftertaste. 'This coffee has a weird taste, parang may-halo.' It suggests something isn't pure, for better or for worse.
usage_notes: Often used to describe something that is not pure or has an additional, sometimes unexpected, element. Can be used for food, drinks, feelings, or intentions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang papuri ay tila **may-halo**ng sarkasmo.","translation":"His praise seems to be **mixed** with sarcasm."},{"sentence":"Sigurado ka bang puro itong ginto? Baka **may-halo**.","translation":"Are you sure this gold is pure? It might be **mixed** with something else."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagtitipon o kaganapan kung saan ang pagsasayaw ang pangunahing gawain, kadalasan ay para sa isang layunin o pagdiriwang.
original_explanation: The OG social gathering in the province. Before clubs and bars, there was the **pasayaw** at the town plaza during the fiesta. It's where your lolo and lola probably had their first date. The entrance fee might be 'P20 para sa ilaw' and the music is a mix of cha-cha and whatever's on the radio.
usage_notes: Often refers to a public or community dance event, sometimes for fundraising (`pasayaw para sa pondo`).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **pasayaw** sa plasa mamayang gabi para sa pista.","translation":"There's a **dance party** at the plaza tonight for the fiesta."},{"sentence":"Nag-organisa sila ng **pasayaw** upang makalikom ng pondo para sa simbahan.","translation":"They organized a **benefit dance** to raise funds for the church."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang may pinakamalawak na sukat, sakop, o dami; higit sa lahat sa laki.
original_explanation: This is the 'grande' size when you wanted 'venti'. It's the share of the bill that your friend who ordered the most has to pay. It's the SM Mall of Asia of malls. When something is the **pinakamalaki**, it's the absolute unit, the one that dwarfs all others.
usage_notes: Refers to size, scale, or magnitude. Can be used literally for physical size or figuratively for the scale of a problem or achievement.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Asya ang **pinakamalaki** na kontinente sa mundo.","translation":"Asia is the **largest** continent in the world."},{"sentence":"Iyan ang **pinakamalaki** kong pagkakamali.","translation":"That is my **biggest** mistake."}]

meaning_filipino: Alisin ang pagkabasa o halumigmig sa isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pagpunas, pagpapatama sa araw o hangin, o paggamit ng init.
original_explanation: The action you do with a towel after a shower, with a hairdryer for your hair, or with a cloth to wipe a wet table. In a more dramatic, 'hugot' sense, it's what you do to your tears. 'Tuyuin mo na ang luha mo, 'di siya worth it.'
usage_notes: This is the object-focused verb. The actor-focused version is 'magtuyo' (e.g., 'Magtuyo ka ng buhok' - You dry your hair). 'Tuyuin mo ang buhok mo' - Dry your hair.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **tuyuin** mabuti ang iyong buhok bago ka matulog.","translation":"You need to **dry** your hair well before you go to sleep."},{"sentence":"**Tuyuin** mo ang mga basang pinggan gamit ang basahang iyan.","translation":"**Dry** the wet plates using that rag."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o akto ng paghimok, pag-akit, o pagpapapaniwala sa isang tao na gawin o sang-ayunan ang isang bagay.
etymology: Mula sa `pang-` + pag-uulit ng unang pantig ng salitang-ugat (`hi-`) + `hikayat`.
original_explanation: This is your power to make someone say "yes." It's what sales agents use to sell you a condo, what your friend uses to get you to go out on a Friday night ("isa lang!"), and what politicians use during campaign season. It's the art of making your idea sound like the best idea ever.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa pormal, pangnegosyo, o akademikong konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang lahat ng kanyang galing sa **panghihikayat** upang makuha ang kontrata.","translation":"He used all his skills in **persuasion** to get the contract."},{"sentence":"Ang epektibong **panghihikayat** ay mahalaga sa larangan ng marketing.","translation":"Effective **persuasion** is important in the field of marketing."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabad o paggulong-gulong sa putik o anumang malapot at maruming likido, tulad ng ginagawa ng kalabaw.
original_explanation: Think of a carabao chilling in a mud pit on a hot day. That's 'maglubalob' in its purest form. It's getting down and dirty, literally. Figuratively, it's what you do after a breakup: you 'maglubalob' in sadness, binge-watching sad movies with a gallon of ice cream. It's about immersing yourself completely in something, usually mud or misery.
usage_notes: Strongly associated with carabaos (water buffaloes) and mud. The figurative sense of 'wallowing in self-pity' is also a common usage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing tanghali, paborito ng mga kalabaw na **maglubalob** sa putikan.","translation":"At noon, the carabaos' favorite thing to do is to **wallow** in the mud."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos niyang mabigo, halos isang linggo siyang **naglulubalob** sa kalungkutan.","translation":"After he failed, he **wallowed** in sadness for almost a week."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang akronim para sa 'A Foreigner Assigned in Manila.' Karaniwang tumutukoy sa isang dayuhan, partikular na isang lalaking Kanluranin (Caucasian).
etymology: Akronim ng pariralang Ingles na 'A Foreigner Assigned in Manila'.
original_explanation: The slang for that foreigner, usually a white guy, you see in BGC or Poblacion. Originally meant 'A Foreigner Assigned in Manila,' but now it's just the go-to term for any Caucasian dude, whether he's a tourist, an expat, or someone's boyfriend. 'Uy, 'yung taga-HR, afam pala ang jowa.'
usage_notes: Bagama't orihinal na tumutukoy sa mga expat sa Maynila, ginagamit na ito ngayon para sa halos anumang dayuhang Kanluranin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **afam** ang mahilig mamasyal sa mga isla ng Pilipinas.","translation":"Many **foreigners** love to travel around the islands of the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Ang nobyo ng kapatid ko ay isang **afam** na taga-Europa.","translation":"My sister's boyfriend is a **foreigner** from Europe."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malakas na damdamin na nagmumula sa mga pangyayari, kalooban, o relasyon sa iba, tulad ng saya, lungkot, galit, o takot.
original_explanation: These are the "feels." The whole spectrum, from the kilig you get when your crush messages you, to the gigil when your internet dies during a crucial Zoom meeting, to the inis when someone cuts you in line. Managing your emosyon is basically adulting 101. "Pigilan mo 'yang emosyon mo," is what your friend tells you before you confront your ex.
usage_notes: A general term for feelings. Can be used in both formal psychological contexts and everyday conversations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap itago ang tunay na **emosyon** kapag masaya ka.","translation":"It's hard to hide your true **emotion** when you're happy."},{"sentence":"Dapat matuto tayong kontrolin ang ating mga **emosyon**.","translation":"We should learn to control our **emotions**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang institusyon para sa pagtuturo at pag-aaral ng mga mag-aaral; paaralan.
original_explanation: Ang dating 'prison' mo for 10+ years, pero pagka-graduate mo, bigla mong nami-miss. Dito mo natutunan ang Pythagorean theorem na hindi mo naman nagamit sa pagbili ng suka sa tindahan. Dito rin nagsimula ang mga first crush at first heartbreak.
usage_notes: Maaaring ipagpalit sa salitang "paaralan", bagaman ang "iskuwela" ay mas kolokyal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumasok ka na sa **iskuwela** at baka mahuli ka sa klase.","translation":"Go to **school** now or you might be late for class."},{"sentence":"Saan ka nag-aral noong elementarya? Saang **iskuwela**?","translation":"Where did you study during elementary? At which **school**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing puro, malinis, o walang anumang halo na nakasisira; alisin ang anumang karumihan o kasamaan.
original_explanation: It's like detoxing your life. Removing all the toxic people, bad vibes, and maybe even that ex's number you still have saved. It's the Marie Kondo method for your soul: if it doesn't spark joy (or isn't pure), thank it and let it go. #selfcare
usage_notes: Often used in a figurative sense, referring to purifying one's intentions, spirit, or love.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Layunin ng proseso na **dalisayin** ang ginto mula sa ibang mineral.","translation":"The process aims to **purify** the gold from other minerals."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **dalisayin** ang iyong puso at isipan bago ka magmahal muli.","translation":"You need to **purify** your heart and mind before you love again."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking pangkat o grupo ng mga tao, hayop, o insekto na sama-samang kumikilos.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung mga tao sa MRT pag rush hour, isang kuyog na siksikan. O kaya 'yung mga kaibigan mo na biglang dumarating sa bahay n'yo kapag nalamang may handa. A mob, a swarm, a posse.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a large group of small creatures (like fish or insects) or a disorderly crowd of people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **kuyog** ng mga isda ang aming nahuli.","translation":"We caught a **school** of fish."},{"sentence":"Dinumog siya ng isang **kuyog** ng mga tagahanga paglabas niya ng gusali.","translation":"He was mobbed by a **crowd** of fans when he exited the building."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabara sa lalamunan dahil sa pagkain o anumang bagay na hindi sinasadyang malunok, na nagiging sanhi ng hirap sa paghinga.
original_explanation: That moment when you're laughing too hard while eating sisig tapos biglang may bumara sa lalamunan mo. It's the universe telling you to slow down, bes. It's not just food, pwede ring "mahirinan sa sariling kasinungalingan" – choking on your own lies.
usage_notes: Often used in a literal sense but can also be used figuratively to mean being overwhelmed by something one has said or done.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahan-dahan sa pagkain ng kanin para hindi ka **mahirinan**.","translation":"Eat your rice slowly so you don't **choke**."},{"sentence":"Halos **mahirinan** siya sa dami ng trabahong ibinigay sa kanya.","translation":"He was almost **overwhelmed** (figuratively choked) by the amount of work given to him."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang hiram na nangangahulugang maganda o kaakit-akit, karaniwang ginagamit para sa isang babae.
original_explanation: It's the Spanish word for 'pretty,' but when Pinoys use it, it feels a little more... telenovela. It's what you call the haciendera's daughter or the new girl in school who looks like a movie star. It has a slightly more classic, less common feel than 'maganda.'
usage_notes: Used less frequently than 'maganda' but is universally understood. Often used to sound more sophisticated or in a playful, dramatic way.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"“Hola, **bonita**!” bati ng binata sa dalaga.","translation":"“Hello, **beautiful**!” the young man greeted the lady."},{"sentence":"Lumaki siyang isang tunay na **bonita**, tulad ng kanyang ina.","translation":"She grew up to be a true **beauty**, just like her mother."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng prutas na karaniwang itinuturing na gulay, bilog, kulay pula kapag hinog, at maasim-asim na matamis ang lasa. Ginagamit sa pagluluto at paggawa ng sarsa.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'tomate', na galing sa Nahuatl na 'tomatl'.
original_explanation: The OG fruit na nagpapanggap na gulay sa sinigang at ginisang ulam. Ito yung laging kasama ng itlog na maalat. Sa Pinoy spaghetti, siya ang bida, pero sa presyuhan sa palengke, minsan parang ginto, minsan parang wala lang. The ultimate "it's complicated" relationship status ng prutas at gulay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong pang-agahan ang sinangag na may kasamang **kamatis** at itlog na maalat.","translation":"My favorite breakfast is fried rice with **tomato** and salted egg."},{"sentence":"Nagmamahal na naman ang presyo ng **kamatis** sa palengke.","translation":"The price of **tomatoes** in the market is increasing again."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kabuuan ng lahat ng tao sa mundo; ang lahi ng tao.
original_explanation: The entire human race. It's everyone in the world, from your crush to your mortal enemy to that K-Pop idol you stan. When someone says "para sa sangkatauhan," they're talking about a goal so big, it's for all of us—like finding a cure for traffic or creating unlimited data plans.
usage_notes: A formal and grand term for all people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagtuklas ng apoy ay isang malaking hakbang para sa **sangkatauhan**.","translation":"The discovery of fire was a great leap for **mankind**."},{"sentence":"Dapat nating pangalagaan ang planeta para sa kinabukasan ng **sangkatauhan**.","translation":"We must care for the planet for the future of **humanity**."}]

translation: to be able to have something formed or shaped
meaning_filipino: Magawang mabigyan ng tiyak na anyo, hugis, o porma ang isang bagay. Ito ay tumutukoy sa kakayahang isakatuparan ang paglikha o pag-aayos ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is a deep, formal word. Think of a sculptor trying to form a statue from a block of marble, or a writer trying to shape a story from a chaotic mess of ideas. It's the "making it happen" verb for artists and creators. You wouldn't use this when talking about your lunch, unless your lunch is a work of art. "Sana maipaanyo ko nang maayos ang thesis na ito."
usage_notes: This is a very formal and literary word, not used in everyday conversation. It implies a complex process of shaping or forming something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa pamamagitan ng masusing pagpaplano, umaasa siyang **maipaanyo** ang kanyang pangarap na negosyo.","translation":"Through careful planning, he hopes **to be able to form** his dream business."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **maipaanyo** ang isang matatag na republika kung watak-watak ang mga mamamayan.","translation":"It is difficult **to be able to shape** a stable republic if the citizens are divided."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang lugar, tulad ng bundok o kalsada, na may mataas at biglaang anggulo ng pag-akyat o pagbaba.
original_explanation: Describes the road to Baguio, the last few flights of stairs to your condo unit, and the learning curve for your new job. It's anything that makes you say, 'Hinga-hinga muna, besh!' Also describes the price of onions these days.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for physical inclines or figuratively for prices or challenges.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sobrang **matarik** ang daan paakyat sa tuktok ng bundok.","translation":"The road to the mountain's peak is very **steep**."},{"sentence":"Naging **matarik** ang pagtaas ng presyo ng gasolina ngayong buwan.","translation":"The increase in gas prices this month has been **steep**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, pangkat, o kumpanya na lumilikha, gumagawa, o nagpoprodyus ng isang bagay o produkto.
original_explanation: The person or company behind the product. The 'Made in China' tag? They're the 'tagagawa'. The credits at the end of a movie? A list of the 'tagagawa'. In your barkada, the 'tagagawa' is the friend who makes the plans, makes the food, and basically makes everything happen. The unsung hero of 'drawing' plans.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **tagagawa** ng masarap na keyk na ito?","translation":"Who is the **maker** of this delicious cake?"},{"sentence":"Ang aming kumpanya ang pangunahing **tagagawa** ng sapatos sa bansa.","translation":"Our company is the leading **manufacturer** of shoes in the country."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kawali na may mga nakaalsang guhit (ridges) na ginagamit sa pag-ihaw ng pagkain sa loob ng bahay.
original_explanation: That thing you bought from Shopee to make samgyupsal at home. It's the key to pretending you're a chef, getting those perfect sear marks on your liempo or hotdog without needing a full-blown ihawan.
usage_notes: Commonly used as is in Tagalog conversations, especially in cooking and shopping contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakihugas ng **grillpan** pagkatapos mong gamitin.","translation":"Please wash the **grill pan** after you use it."},{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng bagong **grillpan** para sa ating Korean BBQ night.","translation":"I bought a new **grill pan** for our Korean BBQ night."}]

translation: to shine; to gleam; to become glossy
meaning_filipino: Pagpapakita ng liwanag o kislap dahil sa pagtama ng ilaw sa isang makinis na ibabaw.
original_explanation: 'Yung noo mo after mag-commute sa Pinas ng 1 PM. Charot! Eto 'yung effect ng floor wax, ng bagong carwash, o ng lip gloss. It’s that "shine bright like a diamond" moment for inanimate objects... or your oily T-zone. It's the goal of every floor polisher and car detailer.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumintab** ang sahig matapos itong bunutin.","translation":"The floor **shone** after being polished."},{"sentence":"Gusto kong **kumintab** ang sapatos ko para sa okasyon.","translation":"I want my shoes to **be shiny** for the occasion."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdurog o pagpino ng isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng paulit-ulit na pagpukpok o pagdiin, karaniwan ay gamit ang pandikdik at lusong.
original_explanation: To pound something into submission. Like how you crush garlic with the flat side of a knife, or how your lola pounds rice to make 'pinipig'. Metaphorically, it's what your heart feels like during a 'hugot' moment, or what you want to do to your slow laptop. 'Binayo sa dibdib' = chest-pounding anxiety.
usage_notes: Often performed with a mortar and pestle ('lusong at pandikdik' or 'almires').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **bayuhin** nang maigi ang mga mani para sa kare-kare.","translation":"You need to **pound** the peanuts well for the kare-kare."},{"sentence":"**Binayo** niya ang bigas hanggang sa maging galapong.","translation":"She **pounded** the rice until it became flour."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng suporta o pagtataguyod sa isang produkto, serbisyo, tao, o adhikain.
original_explanation: Ito yung 'support local' movement mo. Instead of buying that overpriced foreign brand, you choose the one made in Marikina. It's giving your business to someone or something you believe in. Parang pag-stan sa isang P-pop group, you stream their music, buy their merch, and defend them from bashers.
usage_notes: Often used in campaigns promoting local products or culture. The root 'tangkilik' means patronage or protection.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tangkilikin** natin ang sariling atin.","translation":"Let's **patronize** our own."},{"sentence":"Maraming salamat sa patuloy na pag**tangkilik** sa aming munting negosyo.","translation":"Thank you very much for continuously **patronizing** our small business."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang elementong kemikal na may simbolong Sr at atomic number 38. Ito ay isang malambot na metal na kulay pilak-puti na mabilis mag-oxidize sa hangin.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol 'estroncio' o Ingles na 'Strontium'.
original_explanation: Isa sa mga less-famous na pinsan ni Calcium sa periodic table. Siya yung dahilan kung bakit kulay pula ang mga fireworks. So next time na manood ka ng fireworks display sa New Year, pasalamatan mo si Istrontiyum for the fiery red spectacle.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng agham, partikular sa kimika.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **Istrontiyum** ay ginagamit upang makagawa ng matingkad na pulang kulay sa mga paputok.","translation":"**Strontium** is used to produce a vibrant red color in fireworks."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng mga siyentipiko ang mga katangian ng **Istrontiyum-90**.","translation":"Scientists are studying the properties of **Strontium-90**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kapatid na may iisang ina ngunit magkaibang ama.
original_explanation: This is your sibling from the same mother but a different father. It's like being in the same 'team nanay' but with a different player-coach on the 'tatay' side. The family tree gets a bit more complex, just like the plot of a teleserye.
usage_notes: Maaaring tukuyin sa pamamagitan ng pagdaragdag ng "na babae" para sa maternal half-sister o "na lalaki" para sa maternal half-brother. Ang katumbas nito ay "kapatid sa ama" (paternal half-sibling).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit **kapatid sa ina** lang kami, napakalapit namin sa isa't isa.","translation":"Even if we are only **maternal half-siblings**, we are very close to each other."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang tao na may angking talino sa pagpapatawa o pagbibiro sa paraang hindi nakakasakit ng damdamin.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na 'chiste' na nangangahulugang biro.
original_explanation: Ito yung tropa mong laging may banat o hirit, kahit sa seryosong usapan. Hindi corny, hindi trying hard. Natural comedian. Sila 'yung nag-iisip ng a-attend-an na "inuman" sa group project "planning". The opposite of a killjoy.
usage_notes: Ang 'siste' ay nangangahulugang biro o talas ng isip. Ang 'masiste' ay tumutukoy sa pagkakaroon ng katangiang ito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Masiste** talaga si Juan kaya masarap siyang kasama.","translation":"Juan is really **witty**, that's why he's fun to be with."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng **masiste** na host para maging masaya ang party.","translation":"A **humorous** host is needed to make the party lively."}]

translation: to show a sample; to demonstrate
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpapakita ng isang halimbawa o huwaran sa isang tao; turuan sa pamamagitan ng pagpapakita.
original_explanation: The action version of 'mustra'. Ito 'yung sinasabi mo sa kaibigan mong 'di marunong magluto, 'Sige, mustrahan kita kung paano.' It means to give a demo, a tutorial, or a walkthrough. Parang live YouTube tutorial.
usage_notes: 'Mustrahan (mo ako)' means 'Show me (how)'. The verb can be conjugated, e.g., 'minustrahan' (past tense).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**mustrahan** mo ako kung paano gamitin ang bagong software.","translation":"Please **demonstrate** to me how to use the new software."},{"sentence":"**Minustrahan** ng karpintero ang baguhan sa tamang pagpuputol ng kahoy.","translation":"The carpenter **showed** the newbie the proper way to cut wood."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pariralang pang-ugnay na ginagamit sa paghahambing kung saan ang ikalawang paksa ay isang pangngalang pambalana, lugar, o konsepto na ipinakikilala ng panandang 'sa'.
etymology: Isang konstruksyong panggramatika na pinagsasama ang pang-ugnay na 'kaysa' at ang pantukoy na 'sa'.
original_explanation: The general-purpose 'than' for comparing non-persons. 'Mas masarap ang adobo ko kaysa sa adobo mo.' It's the default comparator for everything that isn't a person's proper name. Use this when debating which is better: working from home or working in the office.
usage_notes: Bagama't maaaring gamitin ang 'kaysa' nang mag-isa, ang 'kaysa sa' ay mas karaniwan at malinaw sa pang-araw-araw na usapan para sa mga bagay at konsepto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas malamig sa Baguio **kaysa sa** Maynila.","translation":"It is colder in Baguio **than in** Manila."},{"sentence":"Mas gusto niya ang aso **kaysa sa** pusa.","translation":"She likes dogs more **than** cats."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paraang may kasaganaan o maraming biyaya; hitik sa bunga o ani.
original_explanation: This is how you describe the handaan for your tita who just came back from abroad. The food is flowing, the drinks are overflowing. It's the opposite of 'petsa de peligro' vibes. It's the 'bonus has been credited' feeling, but in food form.
usage_notes: Often used to describe harvests, blessings, or feasts. Can be used as an adjective modifying a noun or an adverb modifying a verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghanda sila ng pagkain nang **pasagana** para sa mga bisita.","translation":"They prepared food **abundantly** for the guests."},{"sentence":"Isang **pasagana** na ani ang kanilang natanggap ngayong taon.","translation":"They received a **bountiful** harvest this year."}]

translation: to acknowledge a debt of gratitude
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita ng pagpapahalaga at pagtanaw sa tulong o kabutihang ipinagkaloob ng isang tao.
etymology: Mula sa 'kilala' (to know/recognize) at 'utang-na-loob' (debt of gratitude).
original_explanation: This is a core Filipino value. It's more than just saying 'thank you.' It's about never forgetting the person who helped you when you were down, the one who lent you money for tuition, or the tita who let you crash at her place for a month. Not doing this makes you 'walang utang-na-loob', one of the worst insults you can get.
usage_notes: Isang mahalagang konsepto sa kulturang Pilipino na tumutukoy sa pagkilala at pagbabayad (hindi kinakailangang pampinansyal) sa kabutihang-loob na natanggap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat tayong **kumilala ng utang-na-loob** sa ating mga magulang.","translation":"We should **acknowledge our debt of gratitude** to our parents."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal at mapanlait na tumutukoy sa isang babaeng itinuturing na hangal, tanga, o walang isip.
original_explanation: The feminine form of 'istupido.' It's what your tita might call the kontrabida in a teleserye. It's a harsh word, so use it wisely, or better yet, don't. Unless you're describing someone who willingly falls for the same 'Hi, kamusta? Pa-load naman' scam for the fifth time.
usage_notes: Isang mapanirang-puri at nakakasakit na termino. Ang katumbas nito sa lalaki ay 'istupido'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala sa kanya, para kang **istupida** kung magpapaloko ka ulit.","translation":"Don't believe him, you'd be **stupid** if you let yourself be fooled again."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit at walang halagang bagay o usapin; mga mumo o durog na piraso.
original_explanation: Parang yung mga small talk na walang patutunguhan, o yung mga butil ng chichirya na naiwan sa ilalim ng pakete. "Huwag mo nang pansinin 'yan, mga yamuyam lang 'yan sa buhay." It's the small stuff you shouldn't sweat.
usage_notes: A very rare word, almost poetic or literary in use.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga alitan nila ay tungkol lamang sa mga **yamuyam**.","translation":"Their conflicts are only about **trifles**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkilos bilang isa; may iisang layunin o damdamin; pagiging magkasundo.
original_explanation: That rare, beautiful moment when the whole barkada finally agrees on where to eat. Or when Filipinos unite for a Manny Pacquiao fight. When we're nagkakaisa, we're a force to be reckoned with... until someone brings up politics.
usage_notes: Can function as a verb (uniting) or an adjective (united).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang buong barangay ay **nagkakaisa** para sa proyektong paglilinis.","translation":"The whole village is **uniting** for the clean-up project."},{"sentence":"Dapat tayong **magkaisa** laban sa katiwalian.","translation":"We must **be united** against corruption."}]

translation: to silence; to make someone be quiet
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-utos, paghiling, o pagpwersa na tumahimik ang isang tao o isang maingay na kapaligiran.
original_explanation: The classic 'shhh' move, but in verb form. It's what the librarian does with a death stare, what a mom does to noisy kids during an online meeting, or, in action movies, a more sinister way to 'silence' a witness. 'Pakiusap, magpatahimik muna kayo, may nagsasalita sa harap.'
usage_notes: Can range from a gentle request for quiet to a forceful or even threatening command to be silent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng guro na **magpatahimik** ng kanyang maingay na klase.","translation":"The teacher tried to **silence** her noisy class."},{"sentence":"Isang senyas lang mula sa lider ay sapat na para **magpatahimik** sa lahat.","translation":"Just one signal from the leader is enough to **make everyone quiet**."}]

meaning_filipino: 1. (Sa tao o batas) Sukdulan sa pagpapatupad ng mga alituntunin; hindi maluwag. 2. (Sa bagay) Sobrang sikip o mahirap tanggalin.
original_explanation: Can refer to your terror professor who requires Times New Roman, size 12, double-spaced, with a 1-inch margin. Or that pair of jeans you're trying to squeeze into after the holidays. It means no wiggle room, literally or figuratively.
usage_notes: Dual meaning: can refer to strictness of rules/people or the physical tightness of an object.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga magulang niya ay **napakahigpit**; kailangan niyang umuwi bago mag-alas-sais.","translation":"Her parents are **very strict**; she needs to be home before six."},{"sentence":"**Napakahigpit** ng pagkakatali ng buhol kaya hindi ko matanggal.","translation":"The knot was tied **very tightly** so I couldn't undo it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat o grupo ng mga tao na nagtutulungan upang makamit ang isang partikular na layunin, lalo na sa larangan ng palakasan o trabaho.
original_explanation: This 'tim' is your squad, your crew, your barkada for a specific purpose. It's your Mobile Legends 'tim', your BPO 'tim', or the group you were forced into for a school project. "Team Bahay" is the official 'tim' for people who'd rather stay home on a Friday night.
usage_notes: A direct loanword from English, used interchangeably with 'team'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-usap ang buong **tim** kung paano mananalo sa laro.","translation":"The whole **team** discussed how to win the game."},{"sentence":"Kasama ako sa **tim** ni Manager Cruz.","translation":"I'm on Manager Cruz's **team**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na idinisenyo para sa iisang gamitan lamang at pagkatapos ay itinatapon na; o tumutukoy sa pagiging libre o may bakanteng oras.
original_explanation: The millennial/Gen Z abbreviation for 'disposable.' 'Uy, may extra dispo vape ka ba diyan?' It also has a new meaning: being available. 'Gala tayo? Dispo ako mamaya.' It can mean a disposable item or, in a newer slang sense, being available or 'disposable' for a plan.
usage_notes: Primarily used in informal, spoken contexts. Has a dual meaning of a disposable item (like a vape) or being available/free.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bili tayo ng **dispo** na camera para sa beach trip.","translation":"Let's buy a **disposable** camera for the beach trip."},{"sentence":"Friend, **dispo** ka ba sa Friday? Kasi ako, hindi.","translation":"Friend, are you **available** on Friday? Because I'm not."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malakas at walang ingat na paghagis o pagpukol ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: Hindi lang 'to basta 'tapon' (throw). This is throwing with feeling! Yung galit ka, tapos ibinalibag mo yung pinto. O kaya 'yung asawa mong pagod galing work, ibinalibag lang 'yung bag sa sofa. It's a throw powered by stress, anger, or pure 'walang pakialam' energy.
usage_notes: Can be used as a root for verbs like "ibinalibag" (hurled), "binabalibag" (is hurling).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang galit, **ibinalibag** niya ang telepono sa pader.","translation":"Out of extreme anger, he **hurled** the phone against the wall."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **balibagin** ang mga gamit mo.","translation":"Don't **throw** your things around forcefully."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamalaki at pinakamataong pulo sa Pilipinas, at isa sa tatlong pangunahing pangkat ng mga pulo sa bansa, kasama ng Visayas at Mindanao.
etymology: Possibly from the Tagalog word "lusong," a large wooden mortar used for pounding rice, which was a common sight in early coastal communities.
original_explanation: The "main character" island of the Philippines. It's where Manila is, where the traffic is, and where most of the country's drama happens. If the Philippines were a TV show, `Luzon` would be the bustling, chaotic, and always-interesting main setting.
usage_notes: Always capitalized as it is a proper noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Maynila, ang kabisera ng Pilipinas, ay matatagpuan sa pulo ng **Luzon**.","translation":"Manila, the capital of the Philippines, is located on the island of **Luzon**."},{"sentence":"Maraming magagandang tanawin sa iba't ibang probinsya ng **Luzon**.","translation":"There are many beautiful sights in the different provinces of **Luzon**."}]

meaning_filipino: Paikliin ang isang mahabang salaysay, akda, o teksto sa pamamagitan ng paglalahad ng mga pangunahing ideya o pinakamahalagang punto.
original_explanation: When your friend asks what happened in the latest K-drama episode and you don't have an hour to explain. You **magbuod** it: 'He's rich, she's poor, the evil mother-in-law is at it again.' You give them the TL;DR version for school reports, movies, and chismis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinakiusapan ng guro ang mga mag-aaral na **magbuod** ng Noli Me Tángere.","translation":"The teacher asked the students to **summarize** Noli Me Tángere."},{"sentence":"Sige, **magbuod** ka na lang ng kuwento para mas mabilis.","translation":"Okay, just **summarize** the story to make it faster."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghiwa nang manipis o pino gamit ang isang matalas na kasangkapan tulad ng kutsilyo.
original_explanation: What your mom asks you to do with the onions and garlic, and you end up crying (not because of hugot, but because of the onions... probably). It's the first step to almost every Filipino ulam. The difference between julienne and just, you know, 'hiniwa'.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to slicing thinly or shredding, common in cooking contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis lang sa kanya ang **paggayat** ng repolyo para sa pancit.","translation":"The **slicing** of cabbage for pancit is quick for her."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa **paggayat** ng karne upang maiwasan ang aksidente.","translation":"Be careful when **slicing** the meat to avoid accidents."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagiging marangal, kagalang-galang, at may mataas na puri.
etymology: From "dangal" (honor) + "-in" (suffix used here to form an adjective).
original_explanation: This describes a person who has *dangal*. Think of Jose Rizal, a respected lola in the community, or that one officemate who is always fair and professional. They are "dangalin". They carry themselves with dignity. They're the opposite of a *damuho*. This is a high-level compliment you don't just throw around.
usage_notes: A formal and respectful term. 'Marangal' is a more common synonym in both spoken and written language.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya bilang isang **dangalin** na pinuno ng bayan.","translation":"He is known as an **honorable** leader of the town."},{"sentence":"Isang **dangalin** na pamilya ang kanilang pinagmulan.","translation":"They come from a **reputable** family."}]

translation: to burn out (light bulb); to get exasperated
meaning_filipino: Para sa isang bumbilya, ang masira o mawalan ng ilaw. Sa matalinhagang paraan, ang mawalan ng pasensya o mainis nang husto.
etymology: From Spanish 'fundir' (to melt, to blow a fuse).
original_explanation: This is you after your 5th Zoom meeting of the day, or when the internet dies during your Netflix finale. Literally, it's for a lightbulb that gives up on life. Figuratively, it's when your patience bar hits zero and you're about to rage-quit. 'Konting-konti na lang, mapupundi na ako.'
usage_notes: Very common in both its literal and figurative senses.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan na nating palitan ang ilaw dahil **mapundi** na ito.","translation":"We need to change the light because it's about **to burn out**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong kulitin, malapit na akong **mapundi** sa iyo!","translation":"Don't keep bugging me, I'm close **to getting exasperated** with you!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maingay at matinding pagtatalo o awayan sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang tao.
original_explanation: This isn't just a simple disagreement. This is the 'Marites-level' awayan na rinig ng buong barangay. It's the loud, dramatic fight that makes you pause your Netflix to listen. Think of two people shouting over the last piece of lechon at a fiesta. That's a bangay.
usage_notes: Implies a verbal, noisy conflict, more intense than a simple 'talo' (argument).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Rinig sa buong kapitbahayan ang **bangay** ng mag-asawa.","translation":"The couple's **loud quarrel** could be heard throughout the neighborhood."},{"sentence":"Itigil n'yo na ang walang kwentang **bangay** na 'yan.","translation":"Stop that pointless **argument**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katayuan ng pagiging may pananagutan; ang obligasyong sagutin at managot para sa sariling mga kilos, desisyon, at resulta.
etymology: From English "accountability." Its usage in Filipino is widespread, especially in corporate, legal, and political discourse.
original_explanation: This is that thing your boss keeps talking about during performance reviews. It’s the grown-up version of "aminin mo na, kasalanan mo!" (just admit it, it's your fault!). In politics, it’s what everyone demands but rarely gets. In a relationship, it's saying "sorry, my bad" instead of "kasalanan mo 'to, 'di ka nag-remind!" (this is your fault, you didn't remind me!). It’s owning your mess.
usage_notes: While "pananagutan" is the direct Tagalog equivalent, "accountability" is often preferred in formal and business settings for its specific nuance of being answerable for outcomes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **accountability** sa serbisyo publiko.","translation":"**Accountability** is important in public service."},{"sentence":"The team leader emphasized the need for personal **accountability** for the project's failure.","translation":"Binigyang-diin ng lider ng pangkat ang pangangailangan para sa personal na **pananagutan** sa pagkabigo ng proyekto."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga akda, sulatin, o anumang bagay na may kaugnayan sa panitikan.
original_explanation: This is the English word itself, often used by students and academics when they're talking about books, poems, or essays. It's the 'for-da-highbrow' version of saying something is about literature. 'Ang ganda ng pagkakasulat, very literary ang approach.'
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa mga pormal na talakayan o sa 'code-switching' sa mga usapang akademiko.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang magbasa ng mga **literary** journals.","translation":"She likes to read **literary** journals."},{"sentence":"May **literary** contest sa unibersidad.","translation":"There's a **literary** contest at the university."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng isda sa dagat (Filimanus xanthonema) na may malaking bibig at kilala sa mga lokal na pamayanan ng mangingisda.
etymology: Unknown, likely a local or indigenous name for the fish species.
original_explanation: A fish you've probably never heard of unless you're a fisherman from Palawan or your lolo is really into exotic marine life. It's not your everyday tilapia or galunggong. Finding this at the palengke is like finding a rare Pokémon.
usage_notes: This is a very specific and technical term, primarily used in ichthyology or by fishing communities in certain regions of the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakahuli ang mangingisda ng isang malaking **balabalan**.","translation":"The fisherman caught a large **four-finned filimanus**."},{"sentence":"Ang isdang **balabalan** ay masarap daw isigang.","translation":"They say the **balabalan** fish is delicious in a sour soup (sinigang)."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinuno ng isang pangkat, departamento, o organisasyon, lalo na sa konteksto ng pulisya o militar.
original_explanation: The one in charge. Your boss sa office, the barangay captain, or the chief of police you see in action movies. Basically, the person you don't want to get on the wrong side of, unless you want your life to be a teleserye drama.
usage_notes: Commonly used for police chiefs, but can be used colloquially for any boss or person in charge.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tawagin mo ang **hepe** ng pulisya!","translation":"Call the police **chief**!"},{"sentence":"Sabi ng **hepe** namin, kailangan tapusin ang report bago mag-uwian.","translation":"Our **boss** said we need to finish the report before going home."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpunta o pagtayo sa gitnang bahagi ng isang lugar o espasyo.
original_explanation: This is what you do when the photographer says 'Okay, birthday celebrant, sa gitna!' It's literally moving to the center stage. Whether it's for a group picture, a dance battle, or just trying to get the best view, to pumagitna is to claim the spotlight (or at least the geographical center).
usage_notes: Refers to physical positioning. Different from 'pumagitan' which means to mediate a conflict.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pumagitna** ka sa entablado para mas marinig ka ng lahat.","translation":"**Go to the center** of the stage so everyone can hear you better."},{"sentence":"Ang mananayaw ay **pumagitna** at nagsimulang umikot.","translation":"The dancer **went to the middle** and started to spin."}]

meaning_filipino: Gumawa ng musikal na tunog gamit ang tinig; bumigkas ng mga salita sa paraang may tono at ritmo.
original_explanation: The official sport of every Filipino family gathering. Whether you're in a legit competition or just murdering a song on the karaoke machine at 2 AM, you are 'umawit'-ing. It simply means to sing.
usage_notes: While its primary meaning is 'to sing', in colloquial or criminal contexts, 'umawit' can be slang for 'to confess' or 'to snitch' on accomplices.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **umawit** sa banyo tuwing umaga.","translation":"He loves **to sing** in the bathroom every morning."},{"sentence":"Matapos mahuli, **umawit** din ang suspek at itinuro ang kanyang mga kasabwat.","translation":"After being caught, the suspect finally **squealed** and pointed out his accomplices."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng isang bagay sa mabilis na paraan o sa mas maikling panahon kaysa sa karaniwan.
original_explanation: That feeling when your boss DMs you "urgent" at 4:59 PM. You need to magdali to finish your report before you can log off. It's the official state of being for anyone trying to catch the last MRT trip home.
usage_notes: Often used as a command "Magdali ka!" (Hurry up!).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magdali** kung ayaw mong mahuli sa klase.","translation":"You need to **hurry** if you don't want to be late for class."},{"sentence":"**Magdali** tayong tapusin ito para makauwi na.","translation":"Let's **rush** to finish this so we can go home."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lipas at hindi na gaanong ginagamit na termino para sa isang tagasunod ng relihiyong Islam, o anumang bagay na may kaugnayan sa kanila.
etymology: From Spanish "mahometano", meaning follower of Mohammed.
original_explanation: This is the Tita/Tito-level, history-book term for a Muslim. It's like calling a smartphone a "cellular device." It's technically not wrong, but it sounds like it came from a 1950s encyclopedia. The preferred and correct term is "Muslim." Using "Mahometano" today might get you a side-eye because it's outdated and centers the religion on the prophet rather than the submission to God (Islam).
usage_notes: This term is now considered archaic and often offensive or inaccurate by many Muslims, who prefer the term 'Muslim'. It's more likely to be encountered in historical texts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa mga lumang aklat ng kasaysayan, tinatawag na **Mahometano** ang mga tagasunod ng Islam.","translation":"In old history books, followers of Islam were called **Mohammedans**."},{"sentence":"Ang arkitekturang **Mahometano** ay makikita sa ilang bahagi ng Espanya.","translation":"**Mohammedan** architecture can be seen in some parts of Spain."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bahagi ng isang serye ng mga pangyayari, partikular sa isang programa sa radyo o telebisyon, o sa isang akdang pampanitikan.
original_explanation: Ito yung isang part ng paborito mong K-drama o Netflix series na pinagpupuyatan mo. 'Yung dahilan kung bakit nasasabi mong "Isang episodyo na lang," pero 3 AM ka na matutulog. Pwede ring isang chapter sa buhay mo, like "yung episodyo na umasa ako sa wala." Ouch.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng media at entertainment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Panoorin natin ang huling **episodyo** ng serye mamayang gabi.","translation":"Let's watch the final **episode** of the series tonight."},{"sentence":"Ang bawat **episodyo** ay may cliffhanger kaya hindi ka makakatulog.","translation":"Every **episode** has a cliffhanger so you won't be able to sleep."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagdakip o pag-akit sa isang tao sa hinaharap, sa paraang pisikal man o sa pamamagitan ng pag-uugali o karisma.
original_explanation: That person with the killer smile or an amazing voice. They have the power to be a 'mambibihag ng puso' (captivator of hearts). They'll capture your attention and feelings without even trying. This is the future tense of 'mamihag'.
usage_notes: This is the future tense of 'mamihag'. It can mean to literally capture someone (like an enemy in war) or to metaphorically capture someone's heart or attention.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang angking ganda ay tiyak na **mambibihag** sa puso ng binata.","translation":"Her innate beauty will surely **captivate** the young man's heart."},{"sentence":"Ang mga sundalo ay may planong **mambihag** sa mga kalaban sa dilim.","translation":"The soldiers have a plan to **capture** the enemies in the dark."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga matang malaki, bilog, at tila lumuluwa o nakausli, kadalasan dahil sa gulat, takot, o isang kondisyong medikal.
original_explanation: This is your eyes when you see your ex with a new partner. Or when you check your bank account after a Shopee 11.11 sale. Your eyes are wide, round, and practically popping out of your head. It's the physical manifestation of "SHOOKT!"
usage_notes: Describes the appearance of the eyes, often due to strong emotion or a physical trait.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **busilig** ang kanyang mga mata sa takot nang makita niya ang multo.","translation":"His eyes became **bulging** in fear when he saw the ghost."},{"sentence":"May lahi silang may **busilig** na mata.","translation":"Their family has a trait of having **wide** eyes."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubos na inosente; walang kaalaman o kabatiran sa mga bagay-bagay, lalo na sa kasamaan o malisya.
etymology: Mula sa 'walâ' (none) + 'muang' (knowledge, understanding, especially of worldly matters).
original_explanation: This is a deeper, more profound kind of innocence than 'walang-malay.' It’s the innocence of a very young child who doesn't understand malice or adult problems. It's pure, guileless, and completely unaware of the world's complexities. It's that 'bless your heart' energy.
usage_notes: Nagtataglay ng mas malalim na kahulugan ng pagiging inosente na parang bata kumpara sa 'walang-malay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa kanyang **walang-muang** na isipan, ang lahat ng tao ay mabuti.","translation":"In her **naive** mind, all people are good."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng malalim, taos-puso, at tunay na damdamin; walang pagkukunwari.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `ma-` (na bumubuo ng pang-uri) + `taos` (sinsero, mula sa puso).
original_explanation: This is not your typical "Thank you" sa cashier. This is the "Thank you" you say to your parents after graduation. It's that deep, genuine emotion. 'Yung "I love you" na hindi lang dahil Valentine's Day, kundi dahil 'yun talaga ang nararamdaman mo. No scripts, no pretense, just pure feels.
usage_notes: Isang pormal at medyo pampanitikang salita. Madalas ipares sa mga pangngalan tulad ng "pasasalamat", "pagmamahal", o "pagsisisi".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-abot siya ng isang **mataos** na pasasalamat sa lahat ng tumulong sa kanya.","translation":"He extended his **sincere** gratitude to everyone who helped him."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **mataos** na panalangin ay dininig ng Maykapal.","translation":"Her **heartfelt** prayer was heard by the Creator."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng manipis, tuyo, at malutong na biskwit.
etymology: From English 'cracker'. The spelling is Filipinized.
original_explanation: The default 'pampalipas-gutom' or the loyal partner of your instant pancit canton. Whether it's SkyFlakes, Fita, or Rebisco, this is the go-to snack when you're on a budget, sick, or just need something to dip in your morning coffee. It's the plain, reliable friend in your pantry.
usage_notes: The English spelling 'cracker' is also very common in informal writing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isinawsaw niya ang **kraker** sa mainit na kape.","translation":"He dipped the **cracker** in the hot coffee."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng isang bagay na nahiwa o natagpas, karaniwan ay manipis at patag.
original_explanation: When you ask for 'one slice' of pizza, you're asking for a **talyada**. Also applies to cake, watermelon, or even chismis na pa-slice-slice lang ang dating.
usage_notes: Commonly used for food items. Can also be used metaphorically for a share or portion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigyan mo ako ng isang **talyada** ng pakwan.","translation":"Give me one **slice** of watermelon."},{"sentence":"Ang bawat **talyada** ng keyk ay nagkakahalaga ng isandaang piso.","translation":"Each **slice** of cake costs one hundred pesos."}]

translation: to pull out; to draw out
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkuha o pagbunot ng isang bagay mula sa kinalalagyan nito.
original_explanation: The literal meaning. It's what you do to a stubborn weed, a drawer, your wallet from your tight jeans, or a sword from a stone. The OG action before it became all about feelings.
usage_notes: This is the root verb. Common forms are 'humugot' (actor-focus, to pull out) and 'hugutin' (object-focus, to pull a specific thing out).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **hugutin** ang masamang damo hanggang sa ugat.","translation":"You need to **pull out** the weed by its roots."},{"sentence":"**Humugot** siya ng baril mula sa kanyang baywang.","translation":"He **drew out** a gun from his waist."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit at parihabang piraso ng matigas na papel o plastik na ginagamit para sa iba't ibang layunin, tulad ng pagkakakilanlan, pagbati, o transaksyon.
original_explanation: The old-school term for 'card'. Before beep cards and QR codes, there was the 'tarheta'. Think of your lolo's collection of business cards, the Christmas 'tarheta' with glitter that sheds everywhere, or even the 'tarheta' for your library loan. Today, you're more likely to hear 'card' (credit card, ID card), but 'tarheta' still has that classic, slightly formal vibe. From Spanish 'tarjeta'.
usage_notes: While "card" is more common now for things like credit cards, "tarheta" is still understood and used, especially for greeting cards or calling cards.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-abot siya ng kanyang **tarheta** pagkatapos ng aming pag-uusap.","translation":"He handed over his business **card** after our conversation."},{"sentence":"Nakatanggap ako ng isang magandang **tarheta** para sa aking kaarawan.","translation":"I received a beautiful greeting **card** for my birthday."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tanong o suliranin na walang tiyak na kasagutan o hindi kayang tugunan.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `di-` (hindi) at `masasagot` (aspektong panghinaharap ng 'masagot'), na galing sa salitang ugat na `sagot`.
original_explanation: The ultimate "seen-zone" energy. It's that question from your crush, "Mahal mo pa ba ex mo?" that you just leave on read. Some things are better left **di-masasagot**. Also applies to philosophical questions like "Bakit ako single pa rin?"
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa mga tanong, problema, o hamon na hindi masagot o malutas. Ang gitlaping `-sa-` ay nagpapahiwatig ng hinaharap o potensyal na kalagayan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para sa kanya, ang tanong kung may buhay sa ibang planeta ay **di-masasagot**.","translation":"For him, the question of whether there is life on other planets is **unanswerable**."},{"sentence":"May mga problemang sa ngayon ay **di-masasagot** ng siyensya.","translation":"There are problems that, for now, are **unanswerable** by science."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pahayag na nagpapahiwatig ng pagkakaroon ng isa o higit pang pagkakamali, kamalian, o depekto sa isang bagay, gawain, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: This is your life's status update after checking your exam results or your GCash balance after a 12.12 sale. It's the polite way your boss tells you your report is a mess. "Sir, okay po ba yung presentation?" "Hmm, **may mga mali**. Let's revise this." It's the universe telling you, "Try again, beshie."
usage_notes: A very common and direct phrase used in various contexts, from academics to work to personal relationships.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinuri ng guro ang aking sanaysay at sinabing **may mga mali** sa gramatika.","translation":"The teacher checked my essay and said **there are mistakes** in the grammar."}]

translation: to delouse; to pick lice from hair
meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng masusing pag-aalis ng kuto at lisa mula sa buhok ng isang tao.
etymology: From mang- + hing- (a variant prefix meaning 'to search for') + kuto (louse).
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino bonding experience. It's not just about hygiene; it's about catching up on the latest *chismis* while your *nanay* or *lola* meticulously searches your scalp with a *suyod*. This is the original social network, powered by patience and really good eyesight.
usage_notes: A very specific cultural practice, often done among close family members as a sign of care and a way to spend time together.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita ko si Aling Nena na **manghinguto** sa kanyang apo sa ilalim ng puno ng mangga.","translation":"I saw Aling Nena **delousing** her grandchild under the mango tree."},{"sentence":"Noong bata pa ako, madalas akong hingutuan ng nanay ko habang nanonood kami ng TV.","translation":"When I was young, my mother would often **pick lice from my hair** while we watched TV."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit at matulis na piraso ng kahoy, metal, o salamin na bumaon o pumasok sa balat.
etymology: Unknown origin, but likely related to other words for piercing like 'subo' or 'tusok'.
original_explanation: That tiny, evil sliver of wood that gets under your skin and causes a disproportionate amount of pain. It's the reason your mom kept a sewing needle and a pair of 'tiyani' (tweezers) handy. The ultimate tiny nemesis.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb 'masalubsuban' (to get a splinter).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **salubsob** sa daliri ko kaya ang sakit.","translation":"There's a **splinter** in my finger, that's why it hurts."},{"sentence":"Ingat sa paghawak sa lumang kahoy at baka ka masalubsuban.","translation":"Be careful holding that old piece of wood, you might get a **splinter**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nauugnay sa politika o pamahalaan ng isang bansa.
original_explanation: The adjective form. If something is 'politikal,' it has something to do with power, government, or politicians. Your choice of coffee isn't politikal, but your opinion on who should be president definitely is. It's the flavor you add to a noun to make it about government drama.
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang ilarawan ang anumang bagay na may kaugnayan sa larangan ng politika.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May malalim na **politikal** na kahulugan ang kanyang mga pahayag.","translation":"His statements have a deep **political** meaning."}]

meaning_filipino: Mapanganib; maaaring magdulot ng pinsala, kapahamakan, o masamang pangyayari. Maselan o nangangailangan ng ibayong pag-iingat.
etymology: From Spanish "delicado" meaning 'delicate' or 'sensitive'. Its meaning in Tagalog has shifted more towards 'dangerous' or 'risky'.
original_explanation: It's that feeling when you're walking in a dark alley in Manila at 2 AM. Or when you tell your mom "mamaya na" when she asks you to do a chore. Basically, anything that puts you in a tight spot, from a sketchy investment to an "it's complicated" relationship status.
usage_notes: Often used to describe situations, places, or even people that pose a threat. Can also mean 'delicate' in a medical or sensitive context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dilikado** ang daan na iyon kapag gabi.","translation":"That road is **dangerous** at night."},{"sentence":"Nasa **dilikado** siyang kalagayan sa ospital.","translation":"He is in a **delicate** condition at the hospital."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng kawalan ng interes, sigla, o pagnanais na gawin ang isang bagay, kasama na ang pagkain.
etymology: Mula sa "wala" (none) at "gana" (appetite, enthusiasm), na hiram sa Espanyol na "gana".
original_explanation: The feeling you get on a Monday morning when your boss calls for an "urgent" meeting. It's also that "meh" feeling when your favorite food is served, but you're just not feeling it, maybe because of stress, sickness, or *hugot*. It’s your inner battery running on 1%.
usage_notes: Can refer to lack of appetite for food or lack of enthusiasm for an activity. The context clarifies the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mukhang **walang-gana** si Ana na sumali sa laro.","translation":"Ana seems **unenthusiastic** about joining the game."},{"sentence":"May sakit yata siya kaya **walang-gana**.","translation":"He might be sick, that's why he has **no appetite**."}]

translation: Young girl; a common nickname for girls
meaning_filipino: Isang karaniwang palayaw para sa mga babae o isang mas malambing na bersyon ng 'Nene'. Ito ay may diin sa ikalawang pantig.
etymology: A diminutive or affectionate form of 'Nene', from Spanish 'nena'.
original_explanation: 'Neneng' is the slightly more personal, often nickname-y version of 'Nene'. If 'Nene' is what strangers call you, 'Neneng' is what your Tita who sees you once a year calls you. It's also a very common Filipino nickname, to the point where you probably know at least three 'Nenengs'. It's the "Jennifer" of Pinoy nicknames.
usage_notes: Often used as a proper nickname. The stress is on the second syllable /ne-NENG/, unlike 'Nene' which is /NE-ne/.
