meaning_filipino: Isang pinuno na may hawak ng ganap at walang takdang kapangyarihan; isang diktador.
original_explanation: That one person in the group project who decides everything without asking for anyone's opinion. Or your boss who thinks 'collaboration' means everyone agreeing with them. On a larger scale, it's a leader who has absolute power and isn't a big fan of democracy or other people's suggestions. The 'ako lang ang masusunod' type of leader.
usage_notes: A very formal and strong term, often used in political science and history.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kasaysayan ay puno ng mga kuwento tungkol sa pagbagsak ng mga **autokrat**.","translation":"History is full of stories about the downfall of **autocrats**."},{"sentence":"Inakusahan siyang isang **autokrat** dahil sa kanyang paraan ng pamumuno.","translation":"He was accused of being an **autocrat** because of his leadership style."}]

translation: to fall flat on one's face; to trip and fall forward
meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang pagbagsak nang padapa, karaniwang dahil sa pagkadapa o pagkatumba.
etymology: From ma- (involuntary action prefix) + tuwad (to bend over with buttocks up, but in this context, implies falling forward).
original_explanation: That clumsy moment when you're walking confidently, maybe checking your phone, and suddenly you're kissing the pavement. It's the 'epic fail' of walking. Everyone has a matuwad story, usually involving a perfectly smooth floor and zero obstacles.
usage_notes: Describes an involuntary, often embarrassing, forward fall.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa madulas na sahig at baka ka **matuwad**.","translation":"Be careful on the slippery floor, you might **fall flat on your face**."},{"sentence":"Halos **matuwad** ako sa pagmamadali kong habulin ang bus.","translation":"I almost **tripped and fell forward** in my rush to catch the bus."}]

meaning_filipino: Kasalukuyang nagpapalitan ng salita o kuro-kuro.
original_explanation: What your boss thinks you're doing when you're on a 'very important call' (but you're actually just ordering milk tea with your officemate). It's the live, uncensored chismisan session. 'Huy, wag kang maingay, **nag-uusap** yung mga manager!'
usage_notes: Present progressive tense of 'mag-usap'. Implies a reciprocal action that is currently happening.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tila seryoso ang pinag-uusapan nila dahil kanina pa sila **nag-uusap**.","translation":"It seems they are discussing something serious because they **have been talking** for a while."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo silang istorbohin, **nag-uusap** sila.","translation":"Don't disturb them, they **are talking**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katayuan na nagsasabing nakasara o nakakandado gamit ang isang tarangka.
etymology: From "tarangka" + "-ado" (Spanish suffix indicating a state or quality).
original_explanation: The state of being locked with a 'tarangka'. When the gate is tarangkado, you're either safe inside or locked out. It's that moment you realize you forgot your keys and you have to do the "Akyat-Bakod" Challenge.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siguraduhin mong **tarangkado** ang lahat ng pinto bago ka umalis.","translation":"Make sure all the doors are **bolted** before you leave."},{"sentence":"Hindi ako makapasok dahil **tarangkado** ang gate.","translation":"I can't get in because the gate is **latched**."}]

translation: state of being chosen or selected
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o katotohanan ng pagiging napili o nahirang para sa isang posisyon, gawain, o parangal.
etymology: Mula sa ugat na "pili" (pumili). Ang unlaping "pagka-" dito ay tumutukoy sa estado ng pagiging pinili.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na ikaw 'yung natawag sa recitation kahit 'di ka nag-aral. Or worse, ikaw 'yung napili para mag-present ng group project kahit wala kang ambag. The **pagkapili** can be a blessing or a curse.
usage_notes: Iba sa "pagpili" (ang akto ng pagpili). Ang "pagkapili" ay ang resulta o estado matapos mapili.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagdiwang ng buong bayan ang kanyang **pagkapili** bilang bagong alkalde.","translation":"The whole town celebrated his **selection** as the new mayor."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya inaasahan ang kanyang **pagkapili** bilang kinatawan ng klase.","translation":"She did not expect her **state of being chosen** as the class representative."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pamilang na tumutukoy sa kabuuang bilang na kasunod ng dalawa at bago ang apat; ang simbolo nito ay 3.
original_explanation: The number 3. Famous for being in 'tres Marias' (gossip buddies), the 'love triangle' in every teleserye, and the number of installments you can pay for that Shopee purchase. The '(ng -)' in the source list indicates its linker form, 'tatlong'.
usage_notes: When followed by a noun, it often uses the linker 'ng', becoming 'tatlong'. For example, 'tatlong pusa' (three cats).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng **tatlo**ng mansanas.","translation":"I bought **three** apples."},{"sentence":"Mayroon siyang **tatlo**ng kapatid.","translation":"He/She has **three** siblings."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pampang o gilid ng isang ilog.
original_explanation: The slightly less glamorous cousin of 'tabindagat' (seashore). This is where you go for picnics, fishing, or washing your clothes 'provincial-style'. It’s the setting for many classic Filipino folk songs and the occasional horror movie scene.
usage_notes: A common descriptive noun for a location.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming naglalaba sa **tabing-ilog** tuwing umaga.","translation":"Many people are washing clothes at the **riverside** every morning."},{"sentence":"Nagtayo sila ng bahay malapit sa **tabing-ilog**.","translation":"They built a house near the **riverbank**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hayop, lalo na ang isang ibon, na nanghuhuli ng ibang hayop para kainin.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `man-` (tagagawa ng kilos) + `dagit` (agawin nang mabilisan).
original_explanation: Ito yung mga animal sa food chain na laging nasa 'top'. Parang 'yung officemate mong laging nang-aagaw ng credit sa project. Sila ang mga agila, lawin, at kung minsan, 'yung chismosang kapitbahay na laging nag-aabang ng mabibiktima.
usage_notes: Madalas tumutukoy sa malalaking ibon tulad ng agila at lawin, ngunit maaaring gamitin para sa anumang hayop na nanghuhuli.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang agila ay isang uri ng **mandaragit**.","translation":"The eagle is a type of **predator**."},{"sentence":"Kinatatakutan ng maliliit na hayop ang mga **mandaragit** sa gubat.","translation":"Small animals fear the **predators** in the forest."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang panlinis na binubuo ng mga pinong hibla (tulad ng tingting o buhok ng tambo) na nakakabit sa isang hawakan, ginagamit sa pagwawalis ng dumi.
original_explanation: The ultimate weapon of every Filipino nanay, second only to the tsinelas. It's not just a cleaning tool; it's a disciplinary tool, a way to reach things on high shelves, and a spider-killer. There are two main types: the `walis tingting` (made of coconut midribs) for outdoors, and the `walis tambo` (soft broom) for indoors. A Filipino household isn't complete without both.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb `magwalis` (to sweep). The two main types are `walis tingting` (hard broom) and `walis tambo` (soft broom).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinuha ni nanay ang **walis** at nagsimulang maglinis ng sahig.","translation":"Mom took the **broom** and started cleaning the floor."},{"sentence":"Gamitin mo ang **walis** tingting para sa mga tuyong dahon sa bakuran.","translation":"Use the stick **broom** for the dry leaves in the yard."}]

translation: the act of falling over; collapse
meaning_filipino: Ang akto o pangyayari ng pagbagsak o pagguho ng isang bagay o tao mula sa pagkakatayo.
original_explanation: What happens to your Jenga tower when your clumsy tito bumps the table. Also, what happens to your will to live after seeing your Meralco bill. That sudden, dramatic fall is pagkatumba.
usage_notes: Used for both literal falling of objects/people and figurative collapse (e.g., of a business or a plan).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagulat ang lahat sa biglaang **pagkatumba** ng puno.","translation":"Everyone was surprised by the sudden **collapse** of the tree."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagkatumba** sa entablado ay naging viral.","translation":"His **act of falling over** on stage went viral."}]

translation: to curse; to put a hex on
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbigkas ng isang masamang hangarin, parusa, o kamalasan laban sa isang tao, bagay, o lugar, na may kasamang matinding galit o poot.
original_explanation: This is what villains in teleseryes do. 'Isinusumpa ko, babalik ako at maghihiganti!' It's the ultimate verbal weapon when you've been wronged. Also used hyperbolically when you're extremely frustrated, like when your internet goes out during a final exam: 'Sumpain ka, PLDT!'
usage_notes: This is an object-focused verb. The person or thing being cursed is the direct object. The actor-focused form is `sumumpa` (to make an oath or to curse).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto niyang **sumpain** ang taong nanloko sa kanya.","translation":"She wants **to curse** the person who cheated her."},{"sentence":"**Sumpain** nawa ang sinumang magnakaw dito!","translation":"**Cursed** be whoever steals from here!"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa panahong darating o susunod.
etymology: Mula sa pariralang "sa" (in/at) at "hinaharap" (ang panahong darating, mula sa salitang-ugat na "harap").
original_explanation: This is the official address of your "sana all" and "manifesting" posts. It's the place where all your delayed Shopee orders, life plans, and romantic prospects are supposed to arrive. "Sana sa hinaharap, mayaman na ako."
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang pag-usapan ang mga pangyayari, plano, o kondisyon na hindi pa nangyayari.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming pagbabago ang inaasahan **sa hinaharap**.","translation":"Many changes are expected **in the future**."},{"sentence":"Sino kaya ang magiging pangulo **sa hinaharap**?","translation":"I wonder who will be the president **in the future**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa kalagayan ng pagiging preparado o nakahanda para sa isang gawain, pangyayari, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: This is you before an exam (hopefully), before a job interview, or before you confess to your crush. It's the state of being "G!" or "Game!". The opposite of "Bahala na si Batman." The phrase "Handa ka na ba?" (Are you ready?) can be exciting (before a trip) or terrifying (before a major presentation).
usage_notes: Pronounced with stress on the second syllable /han-DA/. Often followed by 'na' to indicate the state is now complete ('handa na').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Handa** na ako sa anumang pagsubok na darating.","translation":"I am **ready** for any challenge that may come."},{"sentence":"Lagi siyang **handa** sa hirap.","translation":"He is always **prepared** for hardship."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sikat na larong video na multiplayer online battle arena (MOBA) na kilala bilang Defense of the Ancients.
etymology: Mula sa acronym sa Ingles na 'Dota' (Defense of the Ancients).
original_explanation: Short for 'Defense of the Ancients'. Ito 'yung laro na dahilan kung bakit napupuyat ang jowa mo at biglang sumisigaw ng 'Pudge, Pudge!'. Classic na pampalipas oras sa computer shop bago pa sumikat ang Mobile Legends. Ang OG 'sampung piso, isang oras' na bisyo.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa serye ng video game. Kadalasang naka-kapital.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maglalaro kami ng **Dota** mamayang gabi sa computer shop.","translation":"We're going to play **Dota** tonight at the computer shop."},{"sentence":"Na-late siya sa klase dahil naglaro ng **Dota** buong magdamag.","translation":"He was late for class because he played **Dota** all night long."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng pag-uyam, pag-aglahi, o mababang pagtingin sa isang tao o bagay, kadalasan sa paraang pasarkastiko.
etymology: From ma- (adjective-forming prefix) + pan- (instrumental prefix) + tuya (mockery, sarcasm).
original_explanation: Ito yung tita mong laging may comment sa lahat. 'Uy, tumaba ka,' with a smile. O yung ka-team mo sa work na pag nag-present ka, sasabihin 'Wow, galing,' pero alam mong sa isip niya, 'Sus, kaya ko 'yan in 5 minutes.' The master of the backhanded compliment.
usage_notes: Carries a negative connotation of mockery or belittling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi nakakatuwa ang kanyang **mapanuyang** ngiti.","translation":"His **mocking** smile is not amusing."},{"sentence":"Sumagot siya sa isang **mapanuyang** tono.","translation":"She answered in a **sarcastic** tone."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng blog kung saan ang midyum ay video. Ito ay isang personal na journal o talaarawan na ibinabahagi sa publiko sa pamamagitan ng mga platform tulad ng YouTube.
original_explanation: Dati, sinusulat mo sa diary ang buhay mo. Ngayon, vini-video mo na tapos upload sa YouTube. From 'What's in my bag?' to 'A day in my life,' lahat pwedeng i-vlog. Ito na rin ang naging career path ng maraming artista at ordinaryong tao na gustong sumikat. 'Hi guys, welcome to my vlog! Don't forget to like and subscribe!'
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb, often with 'mag-' (mag-vlog) to mean 'to create a vlog'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bagong **vlog** niya ay tungkol sa kanyang paglalakbay sa Japan.","translation":"Her new **vlog** is about her trip to Japan."},{"sentence":"Naisipan niyang mag-**vlog** para ibahagi ang kanyang mga recipe.","translation":"She decided to create a **vlog** to share her recipes."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghahanap sa isang tiyak na bagay, tao, o lugar. Ito ang pagtukoy sa kung ano ang nais matagpuan.
original_explanation: This is the command your GPS gives you when it says "Searching for signal..." It's the active verb for `hanap`. When you lose your phone, you tell your friend, "Hanapin mo nga!" (Please look for it!). It’s the object-focused version of searching. You're not searching a place (`hanapan`), you're searching *for the thing* (`hanapin`).
usage_notes: Focuses on the object being searched for. Often used in the imperative mood (as a command).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **hanapin** ang nawawala kong singsing.","translation":"Help me **look for** my missing ring."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **hanapin** ang tunay na pag-ibig.","translation":"It's hard **to find** true love."}]

translation: to become chaotic; to become disorderly
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkawala ng kaayusan at pagiging magulo ng isang sitwasyon, lugar, o grupo ng mga tao.
original_explanation: This is what happens when there's a seat sale announcement, when the last piece of lechon is up for grabs at a fiesta, or when your extended family tries to decide where to eat. It's the moment everything descends into beautiful, glorious chaos. The "gulu-gulo" part emphasizes that it's not just a little messy—it's a full-blown free-for-all.
usage_notes: The duplication of "gulo" intensifies the meaning, implying a greater degree of chaos.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **magkagulu-gulo** ang mga tao nang may sumigaw ng 'Sunog!'","translation":"The people started **to become chaotic** when someone shouted 'Fire!'"},{"sentence":"Huwag nating hayaang **magkagulu-gulo** ang ating plano.","translation":"Let's not let our plan **become disorderly**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan kung saan ang isang tao, bagay, o kilos ay hindi nakikita o nabibigyan ng atensyon.
etymology: Mula sa `hindi` (not) + `mapansin` (to be able to be noticed).
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na nag-effort ka mag-ayos for 3 hours tapos pagdating mo sa party, dumaan ka lang na parang hangin. You're there, but you're not *there*. The ghosting experience before ghosting was even a thing. 'Yung effort mo sa work na **hindi mapansin** ng boss mo. Saklap.
usage_notes: Maaaring ilarawan ang isang tao, bagay, o kilos. May malakas na konotasyon ng pagiging binalewala o hindi pinapahalagahan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumaan siya sa aking tabi ngunit **hindi mapansin** dahil sa dami ng tao.","translation":"He passed by my side but went **unnoticed** because of the crowd."},{"sentence":"Laging **hindi mapansin** ang pagod ng mga magulang.","translation":"The exhaustion of parents often goes **unnoticed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking nagtitinda o nagbebenta ng mga kalakal.
original_explanation: The male counterpart to the `tindera`. He could be the friendly kuya selling you taho in the morning, the guy at the tiangge who convinces you that you *definitely* need another pair of pants, or the fish vendor shouting "Bili na, sariwa!" at the market.
usage_notes: The male form for a vendor or seller.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **tindero** ng isda ay sumisigaw para maubos ang kanyang paninda.","translation":"The fish **vendor** is shouting to sell all his goods."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa gawain, tungkulin, o anumang bagay na pinagtutuunan ng pansin o pagsisikap.
original_explanation: Ang dami mong atupag sa buhay, pero 'yung pag-reply sa chat ko hindi mo magawa? This is your to-do list, your business, the stuff you're busy with. 'Wag puro atupag sa work, mag-break ka rin.
usage_notes: Commonly used in its verb form `atupagin`. As a noun, it's often seen in phrases like "walang ibang atupag kundi..." (has nothing else to do but...).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Wala siyang ibang **atupag** kundi ang maglaro ng video games buong araw.","translation":"He has no other **concern** but to play video games all day."}]

meaning_filipino: Paglalarawan sa isang tao na may abnormal na kurbada sa likod, na nagiging sanhi ng pagkakayukod o pagkakaroon ng umbok sa likuran.
original_explanation: Like Quasimodo from "The Hunchback of Notre Dame." It describes a person with a hunchback. While it's a medical term (kyphosis), in the Philippines, it's often used casually, sometimes unkindly, to describe someone with a stooped posture. Laging sinasabi ng mga lola, "Umupo ka nang diretso, para hindi ka maging **kuba**!"
usage_notes: Maaaring ituring na hindi magalang o nakakasakit kung gagamitin bilang pang-asar. Madalas ding gamitin bilang pangngalan (noun) para tukuyin ang tao mismo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang scoliosis, unti-unti siyang nagiging **kuba**.","translation":"Because of her scoliosis, she is slowly becoming **hunchbacked**."},{"sentence":"Ang pangunahing tauhan sa nobela ay isang **kuba** na nagtatrabaho sa kampanaryo.","translation":"The main character in the novel is a **hunchback** who works in the bell tower."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpasok o paglalagay sa isang tao o bagay sa isang kulungan o saradong lugar kung saan hindi ito makalalabas.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you get caught doing something you shouldn't, and you end up in a place with bars. It can also be your dog when you leave for work, or you, emotionally, when your crush leaves you on 'seen'. You're trapped, bes.
usage_notes: Can refer to literal imprisonment or figurative confinement.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumulong** ang pulis sa mga suspek sa pagnanakaw.","translation":"The police **imprisoned** the suspects in the robbery."},{"sentence":"**Kumulong** ako sa kwarto buong araw para tapusin ang project.","translation":"I **confined** myself in my room the whole day to finish the project."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagbebenta o pagbili ng mga produkto sa maliliit na yunit o paunti-unting dami, sa halip na bultuhan.
original_explanation: The "Sachet Economy" in one word. Ito ang dahilan kung bakit pwede kang bumili ng isang yosi, dalawang pirasong bawang, o shampoo na kasya lang sa isang ligo. The ultimate life hack for the 'petsa de peligro'. "Pabili po ng tingi."
usage_notes: Often used in the context of sari-sari stores. Can function as a noun ('pagbebenta ng tingi') or an adjective ('bilihang tingi').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas nakakatipid daw siya kung bumibili nang **tingi** sa tindahan ni Aling Nena.","translation":"She says she saves more if she buys in **piecemeal** at Aling Nena's store."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng malalim na pag-iisip o pagninilay-nilay sa isang bagay.
etymology: From the root "muni" (reflect, ponder), with the prefix "pag-" and reduplication of the first syllable "mu-".
original_explanation: This is the shorter, less dramatic version of `pagmumuni-muni`. It's that quick moment you stare into space, thinking about your life choices, what to eat for dinner, or if you turned off the iron before leaving the house. It's the loading screen of your brain.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with "pagmumuni-muni," but can imply a shorter or less intense period of reflection.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sandaling **pagmumuni** ang kailangan niya bago magdesisyon.","translation":"A moment of **contemplation** is what he needs before deciding."},{"sentence":"Nahinto ang kanyang **pagmumuni** nang may kumatok sa pinto.","translation":"His **reflection** was interrupted when someone knocked on the door."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o bagay na nang-aakit o humihimok sa iba na gumawa ng isang bagay na karaniwang itinuturing na mali, imoral, o hindi kanais-nais.
original_explanation: This could be the devil on your shoulder whispering 'i-checkout mo na 'yan,' or the friend who keeps offering you cake when you're on a diet. A manunukso tests your self-control. It's that 11.11 sale notification, your ex's 'kamusta?' message at 2 AM, or the smell of Jollibee Chickenjoy when you promised yourself you'd eat healthy. Sila ang dahilan kung bakit napapa-'Lord, give me a sign' ka, and the sign is 'Sale.'
usage_notes: Can range from a playful 'teaser' to a more serious 'tempter' in a moral or religious sense. The context determines the severity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpadala sa **manunukso** na iyan; masama ang kanyang intensyon.","translation":"Don't give in to that **tempter**; his intentions are bad."},{"sentence":"Ang masarap na pagkain ang aking pinakamalaking **manunukso** kapag ako'y nagda-diet.","translation":"Delicious food is my biggest **tempter** when I'm on a diet."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang angkop na panahon o kalagayan upang gawin ang isang bagay; isang tsansa.
original_explanation: This is your big break! Your 'one shot, do not miss your chance to blow' moment. Whether it's the chance to apply for that dream job abroad, the perfect timing to confess to your crush, or just seeing the jeepney is empty during rush hour. When you get a pagkakataon, you grab it. Huwag nang pakawalan!
usage_notes: A very common and important word. Often used with verbs like 'bigyan ng' (to be given a), 'samantalahin ang' (to take advantage of), or 'palampasin ang' (to let pass).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binigyan niya ako ng pangalawang **pagkakataon** upang itama ang aking pagkakamali.","translation":"He gave me a second **chance** to correct my mistake."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong sayangin ang **pagkakataon** na makapag-aral sa ibang bansa.","translation":"Don't waste the **opportunity** to study abroad."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghinto at pag-iwan ng sasakyan sa isang lugar; maaari ring tumukoy sa pagmartsa o paglakad sa kalsada bilang bahagi ng isang selebrasyon o demonstrasyon.
original_explanation: Has two main meanings! 1) The daily struggle in Manila: finding a spot to magparada your car. 'Bawal magparada dito!' is a sign you see everywhere. 2) The festive version: when a celebrity, a beauty queen, or a winning sports team goes around town on a float. 'Manonood kami magparada si Catriona Gray.'
usage_notes: The meaning is highly context-dependent. 'Magparada ng kotse' is to park a car. 'Magparada sa kalye' could be to parade in the street.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Saan ba puwedeng **magparada** ng motor dito?","translation":"Where can I **park** a motorcycle here?"},{"sentence":"Ang mga nanalong atleta ay **magpaparada** bukas sa EDSA.","translation":"The winning athletes will **hold a parade** tomorrow on EDSA."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kawalan ng kakayahang sekswal ng isang lalaki; sa malawak na kahulugan, ito ay tumutukoy sa kawalan ng kapangyarihan, lakas, o bisa.
original_explanation: Medically, it's about a man's 'junior' not reporting for duty. Figuratively, it's feeling powerless. Parang 'yung feeling mo kapag ang bagal ng internet at may hinahabol kang deadline—you feel **impotent**, walang magawa.
usage_notes: Isang salitang hiram na may dalang medikal at metaporikal na kahulugan. It's Taglish.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May mga gamot na maaaring magdulot sa isang lalaki na maging **impotent**.","translation":"There are medicines that can cause a man to become **impotent**."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman niyang siya ay **impotent** sa harap ng malaking problema ng kumpanya.","translation":"He felt **impotent** in the face of the company's huge problem."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang grupo ng mga bagay na magkakasamang tinalian o pinagsama-sama.
original_explanation: The palengke unit of measurement. Isang 'bungkos' ng sitaw, isang 'bungkos' ng kangkong. It's a bundle of things tied together, whether it's vegetables, firewood, or even a bundle of love letters from your ex. It's the OG "add to cart" but with a rubber band or a piece of string.
usage_notes: Commonly used for vegetables, flowers, or other items that can be tied together.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng isang **bungkos** ng pechay sa palengke.","translation":"Mother bought a **bunch** of pechay at the market."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggabay, pagkontrol, o pangangasiwa sa isang pangkat, organisasyon, o proyekto.
original_explanation: The verb form of being the 'puno' or the boss. It's what your team lead does during a project, what the barangay captain does for the community, or what you do when you're in charge of ordering the group's lunch. 'Ikaw na ang **pamunuan** mo ang meeting, besh!'
usage_notes: This is the object-focus form of the verb. The actor-focus form is 'mamuno'. The stress is on the last syllable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hiniling sa kanya na **pamunuan** ang bagong departamento.","translation":"He was asked **to lead** the new department."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **pamunuan** ang isang pangkat na watak-watak ang opinyon.","translation":"It's difficult **to manage** a group with divided opinions."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang bagay na may mataas na antas, lakas, o kalubhaan; malubha o mabigat.
original_explanation: The 'extra rice' of adjectives. It's not just hot, it's 'matinding init' (like Manila in May). It's not just traffic, it's 'matinding traffic' (like EDSA on a payday Friday). It's the word you use when 'very' just isn't enough to capture the drama.
usage_notes: The linker -ng is often attached when it modifies a following noun (e.g., matinding gutom, matinding galit). This word is the root of phrases like 'matinding pagkapoot' (intense hatred) and 'matinding sakit' (intense pain).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakaramdam siya ng **matinding** sakit ng ulo.","translation":"He felt a **severe** headache."},{"sentence":"Mayroon siyang **matinding** pagkapoot sa mga taong umapi sa kanya.","translation":"He has **intense** hatred for the people who oppressed him."},{"sentence":"Nag-iwan ng **matinding** pinsala ang nakaraang bagyo.","translation":"The last typhoon left **severe** damage."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit at mabilis na pag-ilaw at pagdilim, o pagbukas at pagsara ng mga mata.
original_explanation: 'Yung ilaw ng Christmas lights na sira-sira na. O 'yung fluorescent light sa office niyo na malapit nang bumigay, giving your horror movie ambitions some real-world practice. It's that unstable, on-again, off-again glow, parang 'yung feelings ng ex mo.
usage_notes: Describes a weak or intermittent blinking or flickering. Often used for stars, lights, or eyes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kikisap-kisap** ang mga bituin sa madilim na kalangitan.","translation":"The stars are **twinkling** in the dark sky."},{"sentence":"Alam kong pagod na siya dahil **kikisap-kisap** na ang kanyang mga mata.","translation":"I know he's tired because his eyes are **flickering** shut."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking reptilya na naninirahan sa tubig. Sa matalinghagang kahulugan, ito ay tumutukoy sa isang taong sakim, mapagsamantala, o kurakot, lalo na sa gobyerno.
original_explanation: Literally, a crocodile. The kind you see in Palawan. Figuratively, it's that politician with the expensive watch and suspiciously large belly who keeps asking for 'donations.' Anyone greedy, especially in a position of power, gets called a 'buwaya'. So when you hear 'Daming buwaya sa gobyerno,' they're not talking about a zoo in Congress.
usage_notes: The metaphorical meaning is extremely common in political and social commentary.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May nakitang malaking **buwaya** sa ilog.","translation":"A large **crocodile** was seen in the river."},{"sentence":"Dapat mawala na ang mga **buwaya** sa pamahalaan.","translation":"The **corrupt officials** (crocodiles) in government should be eliminated."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapang metal na ginagamit upang buksan o isara ang isang kandado. Sa matalinhagang kahulugan, ito ay tumutukoy sa solusyon o paraan sa isang problema.
etymology: Mula sa Malay na 'kunci', na nagmula sa Sanskrit na 'kuñcikā' (susi).
original_explanation: The most important thing you forget when you're already late for work. It can be a physical key for your pinto, or the 'key' to your crush's heart (spoiler: it's probably money or good looks, charot). Ang **susi** sa tagumpay? Sipag at tiyaga.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin sa literal o matalinhagang paraan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naiwan ko ang **susi** ng bahay sa loob ng kotse.","translation":"I left the house **key** inside the car."},{"sentence":"Ang edukasyon ang **susi** sa magandang kinabukasan.","translation":"Education is the **key** to a good future."}]

meaning_filipino: Makipaglaban o manindigan para sa isang tao, bagay, karapatan, o paniniwala.
original_explanation: The official theme song of every Pinoy teleserye love team. 'Kahit ayaw sa 'yo ng parents ko, **ipaglalaban** kita!' It's what you do for your rights, for your 'ship', or for the last seat on the MRT during rush hour. It's about standing your ground for something or someone you believe in.
usage_notes: Can be used for abstract concepts (rights, love) or concrete things. The focus is on fighting *for* something/someone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Handa niyang **ipaglaban** ang kanyang karapatan bilang isang mamamayan.","translation":"He is ready to **fight for** his rights as a citizen."},{"sentence":"**Ipaglaban** mo ang pag-ibig ninyo!","translation":"**Fight for** your love!"}]

translation: to get tired of; to be fed up with
meaning_filipino: Ang maramdaman ang pagkasuya o pagkaumay sa isang bagay, tao, o sitwasyon dahil sa labis o paulit-ulit na pagkakalantad dito.
original_explanation: That feeling when you've eaten adobo for five straight days. Or when you've heard the same song on the radio for the 100th time. It's the 'umay' factor. 'Hindi ako makakasawa sa'yo' is a classic cheesy line, basically saying 'I'll never get tired of you.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Araw-araw na lang ulam namin ay isda, baka **makasawa** na ang mga bata.","translation":"We have fish for our meal every day, the children might **get tired of** it."},{"sentence":"Paano ka hindi **makakasawa** sa trabaho mo kung paulit-ulit lang ang ginagawa mo?","translation":"How can you not **be fed up with** your job if you just do the same thing over and over?"}]

meaning_filipino: Sa balarila, ito ang anyo ng pandiwa na hindi nagbabago batay sa aspekto o panahunan. Ito ang batayang anyo, karaniwang nagsisimula sa mga panlaping makadiwa, at madalas ginagamit bilang pangngalan.
etymology: Mula sa "panagano" (mood) at "watas" (command, decree, base form).
original_explanation: Ito yung 'base form' ng verb, yung parang 'raw' na version niya. 'Yung "to verb" sa English. Halimbawa, "Gusto kong *matulog*." 'Yung 'matulog' ay pawatas. Hindi pa siya nagsasabi kung kailan (natulog, natutulog, matutulog), basta 'yun 'yung action mismo. Parang 'yung plano mo sa group project bago pa mag-assign ng deadlines.
usage_notes: Isang mahalagang konsepto sa gramatikang Filipino. Ang anyong pawatas ay madalas ginagamit kasunod ng mga salitang tulad ng "gusto," "kailangan," "ayaw," at "puwede."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang \"kumain\" ay isang halimbawa ng pandiwang nasa **panaganong pawatas**.","translation":"\"To eat\" is an example of a verb in the **infinitive mood**."}]

translation: will end; will finish; will graduate
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagdating sa huling bahagi o wakas ng isang gawain, pangyayari, o yugto; pagkumpleto ng pag-aaral.
original_explanation: The light at the end of the tunnel for every student dreaming of their graduation picture. Also the feeling you get at 4:59 PM on a Friday. "Kailan ba magtatapos ang episode na ito ng buhay ko?" (When will this episode of my life end?).
usage_notes: Future tense of "magtapos". Can refer to finishing a task, ending a period, or graduating from school.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magtatapos** na ang pelikula sa loob ng sampung minuto.","translation":"The movie **will end** in ten minutes."},{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **magtatapos** na rin ako sa kolehiyo sa susunod na Marso.","translation":"Finally, I **will graduate** from college next March."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyon o tunog na nagpapahiwatig ng katuwaan, pananabik, o pagiging masigla. Madalas itong ginagamit bilang isang masayang hiyaw.
etymology: Onomatopoeic. Popularized by Filipino celebrity Kim Chiu.
original_explanation: The sound of pure, unadulterated, chaotic fun. It's the victory screech you make when your Shopee order arrives. It's the sound of your friend getting a 'yes' from their crush. It's the 'Yasss!' of the titas and titos of Manila. Popularized by a celebrity, it’s now a national treasure of an expression. WITITIT!
usage_notes: Used as a standalone exclamation to express joy, excitement, or to be playful.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nanalo ako sa raffle! **Wititit**!","translation":"I won the raffle! **(Expression of joy)**!"},{"sentence":"Nakita niya ang kanyang idol sa mall, kaya napasigaw siya ng \"**Wititit**!\"","translation":"She saw her idol at the mall, so she shouted \"**Wititit**!\""}]

translation: to spread by rumor; to whisper about
meaning_filipino: Ikalat ang isang balita o impormasyon sa pamamagitan ng pabulong o lihim na pag-uusap; pag-usapan nang patago.
original_explanation: This is the plural form of chismis. When it's not just one whisper, but a whole network of whispers. It's the office grapevine in action. "Uy, ibinu-bulong na magre-resign na daw si Manager." It’s the sound of a rumor mill grinding away.
usage_notes: The reduplication of 'bulong' indicates a continuous, repeated, or widespread action of whispering or rumoring.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matagal nang **ibinu-bulong** na mayroon silang lihim na relasyon.","translation":"It has long been **rumored** that they are in a secret relationship."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala sa mga **ibinu-bulong** ng mga taong inggit sa iyo.","translation":"Don't believe the things being **whispered about** by people who are envious of you."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga bagay na nagdudulot ng dumi o pagiging magulo ng isang lugar; laganap na usap-usapan o tsismis.
original_explanation: The state of your room after a long week. 'Yung sandamakmak na damit sa silya, 'yung mga pinagkainan sa mesa, 'yung mga papel kung saan-saan. Ito rin ang tawag sa chismis: 'May bagong **kalat** si Marites tungkol sa kapitbahay.'
usage_notes: Can refer to physical mess or, colloquially, to gossip/rumors.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang daming **kalat** sa sahig pagkatapos ng party.","translation":"There was so much **mess** on the floor after the party."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala diyan, **kalat** lang 'yan ng mga walang magawa.","translation":"Don't believe that, it's just **gossip** from people with nothing to do."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng kahoy, metal, o anumang matibay na bagay na inilalagay upang suportahan o patatagin ang isang istruktura upang hindi ito gumuho o tumagilid.
original_explanation: Your 'suhay' is your emotional support system personified. It's the friend who holds you up when you're about to collapse from a breakup, the parent who props up your dreams, or literally, the piece of bamboo holding up your laundry line. It's anything that stops something else from falling apart.
usage_notes: Can be used both literally for physical structures and figuratively for emotional or financial support.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglagay sila ng **suhay** sa lumang pader upang hindi ito bumagsak.","translation":"They placed a **brace** against the old wall so it wouldn't collapse."},{"sentence":"Ang aking mga magulang ang nagsilbing **suhay** sa lahat ng aking mga pangarap.","translation":"My parents served as the **support** for all of my dreams."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubhang marumi, lalo na dahil sa malagkit na dumi o grasa.
original_explanation: This isn't just 'marumi'. This is next-level dumi. Imagine a kid who just played in the mud after eating a melted chocolate bar. 'Yan ang **gitata**. It's that sticky, grimy, "eww, don't touch me" kind of dirty. Parang 'yung sahig ng jeep na natapunan ng softdrinks tapos inapakan ng buong barangay.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan ng isang kalagayan ng pagiging sukdulang marumi, kadalasan may kasamang malagkit o mamantikang katangian.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **gitata** ang damit ng bata matapos maglaro sa putikan.","translation":"The child's clothes became **filthy** after playing in the mud."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o akto ng pagpapadala o paghahatid ng mga kalakal, sulat, o mensahe.
original_explanation: This is the 'padala' part of LBC's 'Hari ng Padala'. It's the official act of sending something out, whether it's your Shopee order leaving the warehouse or the text message you nervously sent to your crush. 'Sent!'
usage_notes: Often used in business, logistics, and official communications.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating ihanda ang **dispatso** ng mga order para bukas.","translation":"We need to prepare the **dispatch** of orders for tomorrow."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bagay, tao, o lugar na tinutuklas o pinagsisikapang matagpuan.
original_explanation: This is what you do on Shopee at 3 AM for things you don't really need. It's also your "type" in a partner. "Ano bang hanap mo sa isang tao?" (What are you looking for in a person?) is the national anthem of your Titas at every family reunion.
usage_notes: Often used as a verb stem for 'maghanap' (to search) or 'humanap' (to search). As a noun, it refers to the object of the search.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ba ang **hanap** mo dito sa kwarto ko?","translation":"What are you **looking for** here in my room?"},{"sentence":"Ang **hanap** ko ay isang tapat na kaibigan.","translation":"What I'm **looking for** is a loyal friend."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagdaragdag ng bilis o tulin sa isang kilos, proseso, o sasakyan.
original_explanation: When you're running late for work and you tell the Grab driver, 'Manong, pa-dagdag po!' That's pagpapabilis. It's also what you wish the internet connection would do during a critical Zoom meeting or when you're downloading a huge file. The opposite of 'buffering.'
usage_notes: Used for both literal speed (vehicles) and figurative speed (processes).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bagong sistema ay para sa **pagpapabilis** ng proseso ng aplikasyon.","translation":"The new system is for the **acceleration** of the application process."},{"sentence":"Ipinagbabawal ang biglaang **pagpapabilis** ng sasakyan sa lugar na ito.","translation":"Sudden **speeding up** of vehicles is prohibited in this area."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bilog at karaniwang itim na butas sa gitna ng iris ng mata na nagpapahintulot sa pagpasok ng liwanag patungo sa retina.
etymology: Possibly a portmanteau of 'kaluluwa ng mata' (soul of the eye).
original_explanation: This is the black hole in the center of your crush's eyes that you get lost in. It's what gets super tiny when you walk out into the Manila sun, and what gets huge when you see the bill after a fancy dinner date. The window to the soul, or at least to the retina.
usage_notes: A more poetic or literary term. The more common and scientific term is 'balintataw'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lumaki ang kanyang **kalumata** dahil sa dilim.","translation":"Her **pupils** dilated because of the darkness."},{"sentence":"Tinitigan niya ang **kalumata** ng dalaga at doon nakita ang buong mundo niya.","translation":"He stared into the young woman's **pupils** and saw his whole world."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mas mapaglaro at pinalawak na bersyon ng "keri". Ipinapahiwatig nito ang parehong kahulugan ng kakayahan o pagiging katanggap-tanggap, ngunit may kasamang dagdag na sigla o kumpiyansa.
etymology: An embellished form of "keri", which is from English "carry". Common in Filipino gay lingo.
original_explanation: This is 'keri' with extra ~*pizzazz*~. It's the fun, flamboyant, and slightly more powerful older sister of 'keri'. You don't just say 'keribels'; you declare it. It implies you can handle the situation with style and maybe even a hair flip. It's the "I got this" for the fabulous.
usage_notes: Very informal and playful.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-present sa harap ng buong kumpanya? **Keribels**!","translation":"Present in front of the whole company? **Totally doable/I can handle it**!"},{"sentence":"Walang-wala ako ngayon pero **keribels** lang, makakaraos din.","translation":"I'm completely broke right now but it's **all good**, I'll get through it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, kaalaman, o lugar na natagpuan o nalaman sa unang pagkakataon.
original_explanation: That 'Eureka!' moment. It's when you find a new 'kainang-tago' with the best sisig, or when scientists discover a new species. It’s the 'what' that was discovered. The noun form of your "OMG, I just found out..."
usage_notes: Often used in scientific, academic, or formal contexts. It is the root word for 'tuklasin' (to discover).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagkadiskubre ng apoy ay isang mahalagang **tuklas** sa kasaysayan ng sangkatauhan.","translation":"The discovery of fire is an important **discovery** in human history."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang bagong **tuklas** ay maaaring magbago sa larangan ng medisina.","translation":"His new **discovery** could change the field of medicine."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na naglalakbay o palaging nasa paglalakbay; pasahero.
original_explanation: Yung kaibigan mong laging may travel goals at #wanderlust sa feed. Sila 'yung patunay na hindi lahat ng nawawala ay naliligaw; minsan, naghahanap lang ng murang ticket. Puwede ring tumukoy sa ordinaryong pasahero ng jeep o bus.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa isang propesyonal na manlalakbay o sa isang simpleng pasahero.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bilang isang **biyahero**, sanay na siyang matulog kahit saan.","translation":"As a **traveler**, he is used to sleeping anywhere."},{"sentence":"Puno na ang bus ng mga **biyahero**.","translation":"The bus is already full of **passengers**."}]

translation: to be pleased with; to delight in
meaning_filipino: Makadama ng kasiyahan, galak, o paghanga sa isang tao, bagay, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is what your Lola feels when you finally graduate, get a job, and stop asking her for money. It's the feeling of seeing your GrabFood order arrive earlier than expected. 'Ikinagagalak' is for formal events, 'kaluguran' is for when your heart genuinely does a little happy dance.
usage_notes: A more formal and deeper version of 'gustuhin' (to like). Often used in literature and formal speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana'y **kaluguran** mo ang munting handog na ito.","translation":"I hope you **will be pleased with** this small gift."},{"sentence":"Hindi lahat ng mayaman ay **kinakaluguran** ng taumbayan.","translation":"Not all rich people **are looked upon with pleasure** by the public."}]

translation: a type of dried, salted fish (rabbitfish)
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng isdang pinatuyo at inasinan, karaniwang mula sa isdang kilala bilang 'rabbitfish' o 'spinefoot'.
original_explanation: The king of breakfast fish! That crispy, salty, umami bomb you pair with sinangag (garlic fried rice) and suka (vinegar). It's the smell that wakes up the whole neighborhood, letting them know you're having a good morning. Your go-to pasalubong from Cebu.
usage_notes: Primarily known as a delicacy from the Visayas region, especially Cebu. The smell when frying is notoriously strong but beloved by many.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sarap ng **danggit** na may kasamang sinangag at itlog para sa almusal.","translation":"The **danggit** with fried rice and egg is delicious for breakfast."},{"sentence":"Nag-uwi si nanay ng isang balot na **danggit** mula sa kanyang bakasyon sa Cebu.","translation":"Mom brought home a pack of **danggit** from her vacation in Cebu."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang marka, tulad ng tuldok o maliit na linya, na inilalagay sa itaas o ibaba ng isang simbolo sa Baybayin upang baguhin ang tunog ng patinig nito.
original_explanation: The 'special character' of Baybayin, the OG Filipino script. It's the small mark you add to a character that's like choosing between 'e/i' or 'o/u'. Getting your kudlit right is the difference between writing 'bata' (child) and 'bato' (stone). It's the ancestor of the accent mark on your keyboard.
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of the ancient Filipino script, Baybayin. It can also mean a small incision or mark, similar to 'kudlis', but the Baybayin meaning is more specific and common in modern discourse.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kudlit** ang nagpapabago sa tunog ng patinig sa mga titik ng Baybayin.","translation":"The **diacritical mark** changes the vowel sound of the letters in Baybayin."},{"sentence":"Inilalagay sa itaas ang **kudlit** para sa tunog na 'e' o 'i', at sa ibaba para sa 'o' o 'u'.","translation":"The **diacritical mark** is placed above for the 'e' or 'i' sound, and below for 'o' or 'u'."}]

translation: to hit lightly; to take a small portion
meaning_filipino: Ang bahagyang pagtama o pagpalo sa isang bagay; o ang pagkuha ng maliit na bahagi o piraso, karaniwan ay pagkain.
original_explanation: Two meanings! 1) That gentle tap your friend gives you when they want your attention, or a playful smack. Parang "psst!" but with your hand. 2) When you see a plate of chicharon and you "accidentally" grab a tiny piece. It's not *stealing*, it's just... *kumanti*. A strategic sampling.
usage_notes: Can refer to a light physical touch/hit or taking a small amount of something, usually food.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **kumanti** ng pagkain sa plato ko!","translation":"Don't **take a small piece** of food from my plate!"},{"sentence":"**Kumanti** lang siya sa braso ko para makuha ang atensyon ko.","translation":"He just **tapped** me lightly on the arm to get my attention."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapanggap o kumikilos na parang mayaman; mahilig sa magagarang bagay na karaniwang pag-aari ng mga mayayaman.
etymology: From `mayaman` (rich) + suffix `-in`, implying a quality or tendency.
original_explanation: Ito yung friend mo na laging naka-Starbucks kahit 13th month pay pa lang ang inaabangan. They have the *aura* of wealth, whether it's real or just 'fake it 'til you make it.' It's less about actual bank accounts and more about the lifestyle they project. Think 'conyo' culture or someone who collects limited-edition sneakers on a BPO salary.
usage_notes: Often used with a slightly judgmental or humorous tone. It can describe a person, a place, or a thing that looks expensive.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **mayamanin** niyang bag ay peke lang pala.","translation":"Her **ostentatious** bag turned out to be a fake."},{"sentence":"Puro **mayamanin** ang mga kliente sa coffee shop na iyon.","translation":"The clients at that coffee shop are all **the rich-type**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay, lalo na ang isang sasakyan, na may lulang kargamento o pasan.
original_explanation: 'Yung jeep na puno na pero may sumisigaw pa ring "kasya pa isa diyan sa dulo!" 'Yan ay kargada. Or 'yung truck na nagde-deliver ng Shopee/Lazada parcels sa area niyo, kargada 'yun ng mga inorder mong 'di mo naman kailangan.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin para sa mga sasakyan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kargada** ng mga sako ng bigas ang trak na paakyat ng Baguio.","translation":"The truck going up to Baguio was **loaded** with sacks of rice."}]

translation: to fool, to trick, to deceive
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng panlilinlang, pandaraya, o pagbibiro sa isang tao upang maniwala sa isang bagay na hindi totoo. Ang pandiwang anyo nito ay "lokohin".
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na "loco" na nangangahulugang "baliw". Ang paggamit bilang pandiwa (hal. lokohin) ay isang pag-unlad sa Filipino.
original_explanation: What your officemate does when they tell you the boss is looking for you, but they're not. It's the verb form of being a "loko." Think of it as the national sport during April Fools' Day. "Naloko mo ako doon ah!" is the standard response.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamitan ng mga panlaping -in, ma-, mang- (e.g., niloko, maloko, manloko). Ang diin ay nasa huling pantig kapag ginamit bilang utos o sa anyong pandiwa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **lokohin**; alam ko ang totoo.","translation":"Don't **fool** me; I know the truth."},{"sentence":"**Niloko** siya ng kasintahan niya.","translation":"She was **tricked** by her partner."}]

meaning_filipino: Magsagawa ng legal na aksyon laban sa isang tao; o tratuhin nang malupit at walang-awa ang isang tao o grupo.
original_explanation: This is the action form of `pag-usig`. It's what your conscience does to you after you eat the last piece of pizza that was for your sibling ('Inuusig ako ng konsensya ko!'). In a more serious sense, it's the verb for taking someone to court or systematically oppressing a group.
usage_notes: The verb form corresponding to the noun 'pag-usig'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinag-utos ng korte na **pag-usigin** ang lahat ng sangkot sa krimen.","translation":"The court ordered to **prosecute** all those involved in the crime."},{"sentence":"Patuloy siyang **pinag-uusig** ng kanyang budhi dahil sa kanyang kasinungalingan.","translation":"He is continuously **being tormented (persecuted)** by his conscience because of his lie."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang keyk na inihahanda at inihahain bilang bahagi ng pagdiriwang ng kaarawan.
original_explanation: The center of every Pinoy birthday party, aside from the karaoke machine. It's usually a Red Ribbon or Goldilocks creation that you take a million pictures with before blowing out a trick candle that refuses to die. The best part? Fighting with your cousins over who gets the piece with the most icing.
usage_notes: Almost universally used instead of a Filipino equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hipan mo na ang kandila sa **birthday cake** mo!","translation":"Blow out the candle on your **birthday cake** now!"},{"sentence":"Sino ang bumili ng **birthday cake**?","translation":"Who bought the **birthday cake**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing matalim ang isang bagay na may talim, tulad ng kutsilyo o gunting, sa pamamagitan ng paghasa nito sa isang hasaan.
etymology: From the root 'asa' (sharpen) + '-in' suffix (object-focus verb suffix).
original_explanation: Before you can slice that green mango for your bagoong, you need to make sure the knife is sharp. The act of sharpening it on a whetstone ('hasaan') or any sharpening tool is **asasin**. It's what you do to your kitchen knives, your bolo, and sometimes, your wit.
usage_notes: The root word 'asa' is rarely used on its own. The verb forms 'asasin' (to sharpen something) or 'mag-asa' (to sharpen) are the common usages. Synonymous with 'hasain'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **asasin** ang gunting bago mo gamitin sa tela.","translation":"You need **to sharpen** the scissors before you use them on the fabric."},{"sentence":"Inutusan niya akong **asasin** ang lahat ng kutsilyo sa kusina.","translation":"He ordered me **to sharpen** all the knives in the kitchen."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang istrukturang karaniwang gawa sa kahoy o metal na isinasara at binubuksan upang makapasok o makalabas sa isang silid, gusali, o sasakyan.
original_explanation: The original 'seen zone.' Pwede kang kumatok, pero 'di sure kung pagbubuksan ka. It's also a metaphor for opportunity ('pagbukas ng pinto') or for being dense ('sarado ang isip na parang pinto').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisara ang **pinto** paglabas mo.","translation":"Please close the **door** on your way out."},{"sentence":"Isang bagong **pinto** ng oportunidad ang nagbukas para sa kanya.","translation":"A new **door** of opportunity opened for him."}]

meaning_filipino: May kakayahang magbigay-daan o isakripisyo ang sariling interes para sa kapakanan ng iba.
original_explanation: This is you letting your sibling get the last piece of chicken joy even if you really want it. It's the ultimate 'sige, sa'yo na lang' move. In love, it's the person who lets go because they know it's what's best for the other, even if it breaks their own heart. The patron saint of martyrs and 'it's complicated' relationships.
usage_notes: A deep and often admired trait, though sometimes seen as a weakness if it leads to being taken advantage of. It's about willingly giving way.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **mapagparaya** na puso, hinayaan niyang sumaya ang mahal niya sa piling ng iba.","translation":"Because of her **selfless** heart, she let her loved one be happy with someone else."},{"sentence":"Ang pagiging **mapagparaya** ay hindi kahinaan, kundi tanda ng lakas ng loob.","translation":"Being **yielding** is not a weakness, but a sign of fortitude."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay o palitan na pagsipa ng dalawa o higit pang tao sa isa't isa.
original_explanation: The plural, reciprocal form of kicking. This is what happens when a friendly game of street soccer gets too heated, or when siblings fight over the remote control. It implies a chaotic, mutual kicking frenzy. Hindi lang isa ang naninipa, a war of the feet has broken out.
usage_notes: The '-an' suffix indicates a reciprocal or collective action. It means the action of kicking is happening between two or more subjects.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-umpisa silang **magtadyakan** sa gitna ng init ng laro.","translation":"They started to **kick each other** in the heat of the game."},{"sentence":"Tigilan niyo 'yang pag**tadyakan**, baka masaktan kayo!","translation":"Stop **kicking each other**, you might get hurt!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagsisimula o pag-uumpisa ng isang gawain, proyekto, o pangyayari.
etymology: From pag- (nominalizer) + pa- (causative prefix) + simula (start, beginning).
original_explanation: This is the official 'Let's get this party started!' moment. It's the kickoff meeting for a new project at work, the first day of class, or that moment you decide to finally start your diet (again). It's the act of causing something to begin.
usage_notes: Often used in formal contexts like ceremonies, projects, or legal proceedings. More formal than 'pagsisimula'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapasimula** ng bagong negosyo ay nangangailangan ng malaking puhunan.","translation":"The **initiation** of a new business requires a large investment."},{"sentence":"Pinangunahan ng punong-guro ang **pagpapasimula** ng programa.","translation":"The principal led the **commencement** of the program."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbaba mula sa isang mataas na lugar patungo sa isang mas mababa; o ang pagpasok sa tubig.
etymology: From pag- (nominalizing prefix) + lusong (to go down, to descend).
original_explanation: This has two main vibes. First, it's literally going down, like descending a mountain or getting off a bus. Second, it's taking the plunge, like getting into a swimming pool or the sea. It's the opposite of 'ahon' (ascent). Think of it as the starting point of your beach trip—that first step into the cool water. It can also mean going into a difficult situation, like 'paglusong sa baha' (wading into the flood).
usage_notes: Has a dual meaning of physical descent and entering water. Context is key to differentiate.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging maingat sila sa **paglusong** sa matarik na bundok.","translation":"They were careful in their **descent** down the steep mountain."},{"sentence":"Ang sarap sa pakiramdam ng **paglusong** sa malamig na tubig ng ilog.","translation":"The feeling of **going down into** the cold river water is great."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kabuluhan, diwa, o saysay ng isang salita, parirala, pangungusap, o anumang simbolo.
etymology: From ka- + hulog + -an, literally 'the result of dropping/falling', metaphorically 'what falls out' or 'the essence'.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung hinahanap mo sa actions niya, sa mga "seen" messages mo, at sa buong relasyon niyo. Ano ba talaga tayo? What's the **meaning** of this? Parang pag-decode ng ancient text, pero sa feelings.
usage_notes: Often used when discussing the meaning of words, concepts, or actions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **kahulugan** ng salitang 'malaya' para sa iyo?","translation":"What is the **meaning** of the word 'free' for you?"},{"sentence":"Malalim ang **kahulugan** ng kanyang mga ngiti.","translation":"There is a deep **meaning** behind his/her smiles."}]

meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng palakpak ang isang tao o bagay bilang paghanga o pagkilala.
original_explanation: What you do when someone gives a great performance, or when the pilot lands the plane safely. It's the action of giving applause. 'Palakpakan natin ang nagwagi!'
usage_notes: This is a verb in the object-focus form, meaning to applaud a specific person or thing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Palakpakan** natin ang lahat ng nagsipagtapos ngayong araw!","translation":"Let's **applaud** all of today's graduates!"}]

translation: to obtain, to acquire, to gain
meaning_filipino: Ang makamit o makuha ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay resulta ng pagsisikap, tulad ng karunungan, karangalan, o gantimpala.
original_explanation: This is a more formal way of saying 'to get.' It's not what you use for getting groceries, but for getting things like a degree ('magtamo ng diploma'), an award ('magtamo ng parangal'), or wisdom ('magtamo ng karunungan'). It's 'get' with a college degree and a LinkedIn profile.
usage_notes: More formal than "kumuha" or "makakuha". Often used in formal speeches, literature, and academic contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsikap siya sa pag-aaral upang **magtamo** ng mataas na karangalan.","translation":"She studied hard in order to **obtain** high honors."},{"sentence":"Sana'y **magtamo** ka ng sapat na kaalaman mula sa iyong mga karanasan.","translation":"I hope you **gain** enough knowledge from your experiences."}]

translation: To give a speech; to discourse.
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbibigay ng isang pormal na talumpati o pahayag sa harap ng mga tao; ang pagtalakay sa isang paksa nang malawakan.
original_explanation: When someone starts talking and just won't stop, parang nag-speech sa SONA. "Huy, *dumidiskurso* ka na naman!" It's a more formal, slightly dramatic way of saying "to give a speech." It can be used seriously for a politician speaking, or jokingly for a friend who's giving you a long, unsolicited lecture about your life choices.
usage_notes: Can have a slightly negative or sarcastic connotation when used informally, implying a long-winded or preachy talk.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dumiskurso** ang pangulo sa harap ng libu-libong mamamayan.","translation":"The president **gave a speech** in front of thousands of citizens."},{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang **dumiskurso** diyan, sabihin mo na lang kung ano ang kailangan mo.","translation":"Don't **give a long speech** there, just say what you need."}]

meaning_filipino: Katulad; kapareho; hindi iba. Ginagamit sa Taglish upang ipahiwatig ang pagkakapareho.
original_explanation: The ultimate one-word reply when you relate so hard to a friend's rant about traffic, toxic workmates, or being broke before payday. It's a full sentence: "I feel you, I understand, I've been there, and I am also dead inside." Just say "**same**."
usage_notes: Used extensively in informal, online, and spoken Taglish. It can stand alone as a response.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagod na ako sa life. || Friend: **Same**.","translation":"I'm tired of life. || Friend: **Same**."}]

translation: exit; start of a performance; winnings
meaning_filipino: Ang paglabas o simula ng isang palabas. Sa pagsusugal, ito ay tumutukoy sa paunang taya o panalo.
original_explanation: Galing sa Spanish. Kung sa sinehan, ito yung sign na hahanapin mo 'pag tapos na ang movie o 'pag nasusunog na ang building. Sa sabong o sugal, ito 'yung panalo mo na pwede mo nang i-cash out at ipang-Jollibee. 'First blood' sa winnings.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng palabas, sugal (lalo na sa sabong), at minsan bilang literal na 'labasan' o 'exit'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang **salida** niya sa sabong kanina.","translation":"He had big **winnings** at the cockfight earlier."},{"sentence":"Abangan natin ang grandiyosong **salida** ng mga artista sa entablado.","translation":"Let's watch for the grand **entrance** of the actors on stage."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapang ginagamit sa pagsusulat, tulad ng bolpen, pluma, o lapis. Maaari ring tumukoy sa paraan o istilo ng pagsulat.
etymology: From pan- + titik (letter of the alphabet).
original_explanation: Your trusty ballpen, the G-Tech 0.3 you guard with your life, or even the fancy fountain pen your boss uses. It's any tool you use to write things down, from your grocery list to your deepest hugot lines in a journal. The OG tool for leaving a paper trail.
usage_notes: A more formal or literary word for 'panulat' (writing instrument) or 'bolpen' (ballpen).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang kanyang paboritong **panitik** upang isulat ang tula.","translation":"She used her favorite **pen** to write the poem."},{"sentence":"Ang **panitik** ay mas makapangyarihan kaysa sa espada.","translation":"The **pen** is mightier than the sword."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit at matulis na instrumentong pang-opera na may dalawang talim, ginagamit sa paghiwa o paggawa ng maliit na butas sa balat.
original_explanation: That tiny, scary needle thingy they use to prick your finger for a blood sugar test or blood typing. It's the 'ouch, sandali lang' tool of nurses and medtechs. Small but makes a point, literally.
usage_notes: Primarily used in medical contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ng nars ang **lanseta** upang kumuha ng patak ng dugo mula sa aking daliri.","translation":"The nurse used a **lancet** to get a drop of blood from my finger."}]

translation: to set an example for; to pioneer; to be a model for
meaning_filipino: Ang pangunahan ang isang gawain o kilos upang maging huwaran o tularan ng iba.
etymology: From pa- + sim- (from sin-, a variant of un-) + sunod (follow) + -an. It implies "to be the first one to be followed".
original_explanation: Ito 'yung act of being the "sample". Ikaw 'yung unang sasayaw sa dance floor para hindi na mahiya 'yung iba. Ikaw 'yung unang magvo-volunteer sa presentation. Basically, to be the guinea pig, the trailblazer, the one who sets the trend that others will follow. Ginagawa mo para may "pattern" na ang iba.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of leadership and setting precedents. The root is 'sunod' (follow), but the construction makes it about leading so others can follow.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat **pasimundan** ng mga lider ang tamang pag-uugali.","translation":"Leaders should **set an example** of good behavior."},{"sentence":"Siya ang nag-umpisa at dapat lang na siya ang **pasimundan** natin.","translation":"He started it and it's only right that we **follow his lead**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagkawala o pagtakas mula sa pagkakatali, pagkakakulong, o anumang paghihigpit.
original_explanation: This is that feeling when you finally log off after a toxic shift, or when you leave a relationship that's been holding you back. It's to break free, to be unleashed. Imagine a dog finally getting off its leash at the park—that's pure 'alpas' energy. The verb is 'makalpas' (to be able to break free).
usage_notes: Maaari ring gamitin bilang pang-uri (hal. 'alpas na hayop'). Ginagamit para sa literal (hal. pagtakas ng hayop) at matalinghagang (hal. paglaya sa problema) sitwasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naka-**alpas** ang aso mula sa kulungan nito.","translation":"The dog **broke free** from its cage."},{"sentence":"Hangad ng lahat ang maka-**alpas** sa kahirapan.","translation":"Everyone desires to **break free** from poverty."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang estado ng hindi pagkakaroon o pagkaubos ng isang bagay; ang pagkawala ng isang tao o bagay na mahalaga.
etymology: From `ka-` + `wala` + `-an`, forming a noun describing the state of 'nothingness' or 'absence'.
original_explanation: That feeling when your WiFi suddenly dies mid-binge watch. Or when you open the fridge and the leftover pizza is gone. It's the empty space, the "wala na," the "naubos na." Can be as trivial as losing your pen or as deep as losing a loved one.
usage_notes: A very versatile word that often forms part of a compound noun to specify what is lacking (e.g., kawalan ng pag-asa).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kawalan** ng disiplina sa sarili ang dahilan ng kanyang pagkabigo.","translation":"The **lack** of self-discipline was the reason for his failure."},{"sentence":"Malungkot ang Pasko dahil sa **kawalan** ng isang miyembro ng pamilya.","translation":"Christmas is sad because of the **loss** of a family member."}]

translation: to have something brought down; to have the price lowered
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos na ilagay ang isang bagay sa mas mababang posisyon; o ang paghiling na bawasan ang presyo o halaga ng isang bagay.
etymology: From the causative prefix "ipa-" and "baba" (down, low).
original_explanation: Two main uses: 1) The command you give your younger sibling, 'Paki-**ipababa** mo nga 'yung maleta sa taas.' (Please have the suitcase upstairs brought down.) 2) The magic words at the palengke or Greenhills, 'Ate, wala na bang tawad? **Ipababa** mo naman kahit konti.' (Miss, is there no discount? Please lower it a bit.)
usage_notes: Can refer to physical location (bring down from upstairs) or abstract concepts like price (lower the price), volume (turn down the volume), or standards.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **ipababa** mo ang mga kahon mula sa aparador.","translation":"Please, **have the boxes brought down** from the cabinet."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **ipababa** ang presyo ng bilihin sa tindera.","translation":"He tried **to have the price of the goods lowered** by the seller."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na madaling maniwala o magtiwala sa sinasabi ng iba, kahit na walang sapat na batayan o ebidensya.
etymology: Mula sa `ma-` + `paniwala` + `-in` (hulaping pang-uri na nagpapahiwatig ng tendensiya).
original_explanation: Eto 'yung friend mo na maniniwala sa "pikit-mata, may surprise" tapos ang surprise ay batok pala. Sila 'yung laging nabibiktima ng fake news sa Facebook at 'yung unang mag-se-send ng chain message para hindi magka-bad luck. Bless their trusting hearts.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan ng isang personal na katangian. Iba ito sa `mapaniwalaan` (to be able to believe) kumpara sa `mapaniwalain` (tends to believe easily).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging masyadong **mapaniwalain** sa mga alok na 'get rich quick'.","translation":"Don't be too **gullible** with 'get rich quick' offers."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang pagiging **mapaniwalain**, madalas siyang maloko.","translation":"Because of his being **credulous**, he often gets fooled."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang utos o pakiusap na alamin o tiyakin ang katotohanan ng isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng masusing pagsusuri.
original_explanation: This is your boss telling you, 'Find out why the client is angry, and don't come back until you have a solution.' It's the imperative form of 'chismis with a purpose.' You're not just gathering info, you're on a mission to confirm the facts, like trying to figure out if your crush is *really* single or just 'it's complicated.'
usage_notes: 'Pagsiyahin' is a non-standard or regional conjugation of the verb. The more common and standard form is 'siyasatin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pagsiyahin** mo nga kung totoo ang balitang iyan.","translation":"**Ascertain** if that news is actually true."},{"sentence":"Inutusan siya ng hepe na **pagsiyahin** ang pinagmulan ng sunog.","translation":"The chief ordered him to **investigate** the origin of the fire."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagluto ng sinigang, isang tanyag na pagkaing Pilipino na kilala sa maasim nitong sabaw.
etymology: From 'sigang', a verb root related to 'sinigang' (the name of the sour soup dish).
original_explanation: The ultimate act of Filipino comfort cooking. Feeling down? Magsigang ka. Raining outside? Magsigang ka. Your team at work just won a big project? Magsigang ka. It's the culinary equivalent of a warm hug and the perfect 'asim-kilig' moment.
usage_notes: A very specific verb for cooking a specific dish, which shows the cultural importance of sinigang in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang marunong **magsigang** ng baboy dito?","translation":"Who here knows how **to cook pork sinigang**?"},{"sentence":"Umuulan, masarap **magsigang** ng hipon.","translation":"It's raining, it would be nice **to cook shrimp sinigang**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga bagay, kaganapan, o produkto na nangyayari o available lamang sa tiyak na panahon o season ng taon.
original_explanation: This is why you can't get the perfect, sweet mangoes in December. It's why 'Bibingka' and 'Puto Bumbong' suddenly appear everywhere when the '-ber' months hit. It's the law of the palengke and the tiangge. Some things are just not available 24/7, 365 days a year. They're special because they're may-sapanahon.
usage_notes: A more formal or literary way to say "seasonal". "Pana-panahon" is a more common conversational equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang trangkaso ay isang sakit na **may-sapanahon**, karaniwan tuwing tag-ulan.","translation":"The flu is a **seasonal** illness, common during the rainy season."},{"sentence":"Ang mangga ay isang prutas na **may-sapanahon**.","translation":"The mango is a **seasonal** fruit."}]

translation: To stain; to put a stain on
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagdudulot ng mantsa sa isang bagay, sinasadya man o hindi.
etymology: Nagmula sa salitang-ugat na 'mantsa' at idinugtong ang hulaping '-han'.
original_explanation: The act of accidentally (or intentionally, kung may kaaway ka) getting something dirty. 'Wag mong **mantsahan** yung white shirt ko!' is a national emergency, especially kung bagong laba. It can also be used figuratively, like 'mantsahan ang pangalan' (to tarnish a name), which is the ultimate social death sentence.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin nang literal para sa pisikal na mantsa o patalinghaga para sa pagsira sa reputasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **mantsahan** ang bagong pintura sa pader.","translation":"Don't **stain** the new paint on the wall."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan nilang **mantsahan** ang kanyang magandang reputasyon.","translation":"They tried to **stain** his good reputation."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagbabago, pag-aayos, at pagpapahusay sa isang rekording ng tunog, tulad ng pagtanggal ng ingay, pagputol ng mga bahagi, at pagdaragdag ng mga epekto.
original_explanation: This is the magic trick podcasters and musicians use to sound flawless. It's removing your awkward pauses, your dog's barking in the background, and that "ummm" you said 50 times. Basically, it's autotune for your speaking voice. "Pa-edit naman ng audio, tanggalin mo yung ubo ko."
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa anyong 'mag-edit ng audio' o 'i-edit ang audio'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natuto siyang **mag-edit ng audio** para sa kanyang podcast.","translation":"He learned to **edit audio** for his podcast."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong i-**edit ang audio** para mas malinaw ang boses ng nagsasalita.","translation":"You need to **edit the audio** to make the speaker's voice clearer."}]

translation: to desecrate; to profane; to disrespect
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa ng kawalan ng paggalang sa isang tao, bagay, o lugar na banal o dapat igalang.
original_explanation: To commit the act of 'lapastangan.' It's when you deliberately disrespect something sacred. Think of someone vandalizing a church, or more commonly, when you use your Lola's prized 'Good Morning' towel to wipe your feet. 'Huwag mong **lapastanganin** ang alaala niya!'
usage_notes: This is the verb form, meaning 'to make something subject to disrespect'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang krimen ang **lapastanganin** ang watawat ng bansa.","translation":"It is a crime **to desecrate** the country's flag."},{"sentence":"Huwag nating **lapastanganin** ang mga pook-sambahan.","translation":"Let us not **profane** the places of worship."}]

translation: to boast about; to show off
meaning_filipino: Ipakita o ipangalandakan ang sariling kakayahan, kaalaman, o pag-aari sa paraang may halong pagyayabang.
original_explanation: This is the 'bida-bida' verb. It's what that one officemate does during meetings, trying to answer every question even if it's not for them. It's posting your new iPhone with the caption 'blessed' but really just wanting to **show it off**. It's the act of making 'galing' into 'mayabang.'
usage_notes: Carries a negative connotation of boastfulness or arrogance. It's different from `ipagmalaki`, which can be positive (pride). `Ipagmagaling` is almost always negative (bragging).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ipagmagaling** ang mga bagay na hindi naman ikaw ang gumawa.","translation":"Don't **boast about** things that you didn't even do."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **ipagmagaling** ang kanyang mga koneksyon sa gobyerno.","translation":"He likes to **show off** his connections in the government."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkawala sa sarili o tamang pag-iisip, na maaaring dulot ng matinding lagnat, pag-ibig, o pagnanasa.
original_explanation: This is what happens when your 'pagkagusto' levels up to 9000. It's being 'lasing sa pag-ibig'—drunk in love. You're smiling at your phone, re-reading messages, and your friends are telling you, 'Teh, kalma.' It can also mean literally going nuts, like when the Wi-Fi is down during a crucial online meeting.
usage_notes: Often hyperbolic, used to describe intense infatuation, but can also refer to a state of mental confusion or delirium from fever.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa tindi ng lagnat, nagsimula siyang magsalita nang may **pagkahibang**.","translation":"With the high fever, he started to speak in a state of **delirium**."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagkahibang** sa sikat na artista ay labis na.","translation":"Her **infatuation** with the famous actor is excessive."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matamis na palamuti o pantakip para sa mga keyk, tinapay, at biskwit, na karaniwang gawa sa asukal na may kasamang likido tulad ng tubig o gatas.
original_explanation: The best part of the birthday cake that kids fight over. It's the sweet, sugary goodness that covers up a possibly dry mamon. Figuratively, it's the 'icing on the cake,' like getting your 13th-month pay and then winning the office raffle on the same day.
usage_notes: Used in its English form, especially in baking contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw niya ng masyadong matamis na **icing** sa cupcake.","translation":"She doesn't like overly sweet **icing** on her cupcake."},{"sentence":"Tinuruan niya ako kung paano gumawa ng simpleng **icing** para sa keyk.","translation":"He taught me how to make simple **icing** for the cake."}]

translation: to make (someone) understand; to explain to
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagpapaliwanag o pagbibigay-linaw sa isang tao upang maunawaan niya ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: 'Yung moment na kailangan mong i-explain sa nanay mo for the 5th time kung paano gumamit ng Shopee. You're trying to make her understand. "Ma, ganito po, i-click niyo lang 'yung 'Add to Cart'..." That whole process is 'paunawaan'. It's a communication challenge, a test of patience.
usage_notes: Implies a process of making someone understand, often with patience and detail.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **paunawaan** ang mga bata sa kahalagahan ng pag-iipon.","translation":"The children need **to be made to understand** the importance of saving."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **paunawaan** ang kanyang mga magulang tungkol sa pinili niyang kurso.","translation":"He tried **to explain to** his parents about the course he chose."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang marangal na titulo para sa isang pinuno o hari sa mga sinaunang pamayanang Tagalog, katumbas ng Rajah o Sultan.
etymology: An Old Tagalog title of nobility for a ruler.
original_explanation: The OG King of a pre-colonial Tagalog kingdom. Think of Lakan Dula of Tondo. It's a title of nobility, like a duke or paramount chieftain. Today, you mostly see it used in beauty pageants ('Lakambini' for the queen and 'Lakan' for the king) or as a cool, historic-sounding brand name.
usage_notes: A historical term. Its modern usage is often ceremonial, especially in pageantry, where 'Lakan' refers to the male winner.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si **Lakan** Dula ay isang tanyag na pinuno ng Tondo bago dumating ang mga Espanyol.","translation":"**Lakan** Dula was a famous ruler of Tondo before the Spanish arrived."},{"sentence":"Sino ang pambato ninyo para sa titulong **Lakan** ng Kalikasan 2026?","translation":"Who is your bet for the title of **Lakan** of Nature 2026?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagsasagawa ng ilegal na pagdakip at pagtago sa kapwa tao laban sa kalooban nito.
original_explanation: The villain in every action movie starring Lito Lapid or a younger FPJ. They always wear a black bonnet, drive a white van, and have a ridiculously easy-to-trace hideout. In real life, they're just criminals. Don't be a kidnaper.
usage_notes: Also spelled as 'kidnapper'. A direct loanword.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahuli ng mga pulis ang mga **kidnaper**.","translation":"The police caught the **kidnappers**."},{"sentence":"Nagpanggap siyang biktima para matakasan ang kanyang **kidnaper**.","translation":"She pretended to be a victim to escape her **kidnapper**."}]

meaning_filipino: Paglalarawan sa isang bagay na nakabitin o bumabagsak dahil sa kabigatan, pagod, o kalungkutan.
