original_explanation: Similar to 'nakalawlaw' but with more *drama*. Think of a wilting flower after you forgot to water it, or your shoulders after your boss rejects your leave request. It's the physical manifestation of 'pagod na me.'
usage_notes: Often implies a sense of weakness, sadness, or weight. Used for plants, body parts (shoulders, head), or fabric.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakalaylay** ang mga balikat niya tanda ng matinding pagod at pagkabigo.","translation":"His shoulders were **drooping**, a sign of extreme exhaustion and disappointment."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa init, **nakalaylay** ang mga dahon ng halaman.","translation":"Because of the heat, the plant's leaves are **hanging down limply**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging mahusay; mataas na antas ng kasanayan, galing, o kalidad sa isang gawain.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung goal mo sa life, 'yung level of **excellence** na pang-"With High Honors" o "Employee of the Month". 'Yung galing mo sa paggawa ng PowerPoint presentation na akala mo TED Talk na.
usage_notes: Refers to a high degree of skill or quality in performance or craftsmanship.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinilala ang kanyang **kahusayan** sa pagpipinta sa buong mundo.","translation":"Her **excellence** in painting was recognized worldwide."},{"sentence":"Ang **kahusayan** sa serbisyo ay mahalaga sa anumang negosyo.","translation":"**Excellence** in service is important in any business."}]

meaning_filipino: Karagdagang oras ng pagtatrabaho na lampas sa regular na takdang oras, na kadalasang may kasamang karagdagang bayad.
original_explanation: The national sport of BPO agents and corporate slaves. It's that magical time after 5 PM when you're still at your desk, fueled by free coffee and the burning desire to pay your bills. The reason you miss family dinners and your friends' birthdays. "Mag-o-OT ako, bes" is the modern Filipino's cry for help and financial stability.
usage_notes: Often shortened to 'OT'. The verb form is 'mag-obertaym'. 'Obertaim' is a less common spelling variant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang nakuha niyang **obertaym** pay noong nakaraang buwan.","translation":"He got a big **overtime** pay last month."},{"sentence":"Puyat na naman ako dahil sa **obertaym** sa opisina.","translation":"I'm sleep-deprived again because of **overtime** at the office."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang magalang na tawag o pamagat para sa isang lalaki, partikular na kung siya ay may edad, may mataas na katungkulan, o bilang tanda ng paggalang.
original_explanation: The old-school, classy way to say 'Sir' or 'Mister.' You'd use this for the hacienda owner in a teleserye, a respected elder in the community, or maybe your Lolo when he's dressed up. It's got a bit of a Spanish colonial vibe. The female equivalent is Sinyora or Sinyorita.
usage_notes: Capitalized when used as a title before a name (e.g., Sinyor Cruz). Less common in everyday casual conversation today but still understood and used in formal or historical contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"\"Magandang umaga po, **Sinyor**,\" bati ng hardinero.","translation":"\"Good morning, **Sir**,\" the gardener greeted."},{"sentence":"Si **Sinyor** Alfredo ang pinakamayamang tao sa kanilang bayan.","translation":"**Mister** Alfredo is the richest person in their town."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng malaking bilis o tulin sa pagkilos, pag-iisip, o paggawa.
original_explanation: How fast your internet *should* be, but isn't. How fast chismis spreads in the neighborhood. How fast your sahod disappears after paying bills. It's the opposite of EDSA traffic on a Friday payday.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **mabilis** na pag-aksyon ng mga bombero ay nakapagligtas ng maraming buhay.","translation":"The **quick** action of the firefighters saved many lives."},{"sentence":"**Mabilis** ka namang kumain, may lakad ka ba?","translation":"You're eating so **fast**, are you going somewhere?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-upo sa isang partikular na lugar o bagay sa hinaharap; ang lugar na paglalagyan ng puwit.
etymology: From 'upo' (sit) + '-an' suffix, in future tense form.
original_explanation: This is the spot you're eyeing in a crowded MRT train. 'Yan ang uupan ko pag bumaba na si ate.' It's the specific chair, bench, or floor space that will soon be graced by your behind. Can also be a warning: 'Wag mong uupan 'yan, basa!'
usage_notes: This is the object-focused future tense of 'upo'. The subject is the thing being sat on. Compare with 'uupo' where the subject is the one sitting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Alin sa mga silyang ito ang **uupan** mo?","translation":"Which of these chairs **will you sit on**?"},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **uupan** ang mesa.","translation":"Do not **sit on** the table."}]

meaning_filipino: Simulan o pasimulan ang isang gawain, proyekto, o kilusan; itaguyod upang sumulong o umunlad.
original_explanation: The official verb for a product launch, a campaign kickoff, or starting a new advocacy. "We are here to ibunsod the new 'Bayanihan sa Paglilinis' program!" It's a very formal, corporate, or governmental way of saying "Let's get this thing started!" It sounds more impressive than "simulan".
usage_notes: Used in formal contexts like business, government, or social movements. It means to be the cause or starting point of something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pamahalaan ay mag-i-**ibunsod** ng isang bagong programa laban sa kahirapan.","translation":"The government will **launch** a new program against poverty."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang talumpati ang nag-**bunsod** sa mga tao na kumilos.","translation":"His speech **prompted** the people to take action."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng hayop na kahawig ng pusa na karaniwang naninirahan sa mga puno sa Timog-Silangang Asya, kilala sa paggawa ng Kape Alamid.
original_explanation: Ito yung hayop na mukhang pusa na may halong daga na mahilig sa kape. Sila yung original baristas ng pinakamahal na kape sa mundo, yung Kopi Luwak. Yes, kinakain nila yung coffee cherries tapos... you know the rest. The OG 'processed' coffee.
usage_notes: Kilala rin bilang "alamid" sa Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakita kami ng isang **mosang** na tumatakbo sa sanga ng puno kagabi.","translation":"We saw a **civet cat** running on a tree branch last night."}]

translation: to look down on, to belittle
meaning_filipino: Maliitin, hamakin, o bigyan ng mababang pagtingin ang isang tao o bagay.
etymology: From `mata` (eye) + `-hin` (object-focus verb suffix). Literally "to eye something/someone" in a diminutive way.
original_explanation: This is what happens when someone gives you the "side-eye" because of your P100 ukay-ukay OOTD, not knowing it looks better than their branded outfit. It's the act of underestimating someone's worth, like when they don't think you can hit your sales quota but then you end up being the top agent. Don't let them matahin you!
usage_notes: Carries a strong negative connotation of condescension and disrespect.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **matahin** ang kakayahan ng iyong kapwa.","translation":"Do not **belittle** the abilities of your fellow person."},{"sentence":"Madalas siyang **minamata** ng mga kaklase niya dahil sa kanyang kahirapan.","translation":"He was often **looked down upon** by his classmates because of his poverty."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginawang tatlo o pinarami nang tatlong beses. Ito ay nasa anyong pangkasalukuyan o pangnagdaan.
original_explanation: It's what happens to your workload when two colleagues go on an "emergency leave" on a Friday. Your single task suddenly becomes three. "Sir, **tinatlo** po 'yung reports na kailangan kong tapusin today."
usage_notes: This is the completed or past tense form of the verb `tatluhin` (to triple).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tinatlo** niya ang bayad dahil nagustuhan niya ang serbisyo.","translation":"He **tripled** the payment because he liked the service."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na labis na umasa at nasaktan dahil sa isang malabong ugnayan o 'situationship' kung saan siya ay hindi nabigyan ng kasiguraduhan.
original_explanation: The one who caught feelings, big time. This is the person who was hoping for a label, who thought all the sweet gestures meant something more, only to be hit with "Let's just be friends" or "I'm not looking for anything serious." They are the casualties of ambiguity, the ones left to wonder "Saan ako nagkulang?"
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin nang may halong biro at tunay na kalungkutan upang ilarawan ang masakit na karanasan sa isang walang-label na relasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang paasa, marami nang **situationship victim** sa mundo.","translation":"Don't lead people on, there are already too many **situationship victims** in the world."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan lumalapag at lumilipad ang mga sasakyang panghimpapawid, at kung saan nag-aantay ang mga pasahero; isang paliparan. Ito ay ang Filipinisadong pagbaybay ng salitang Ingles na "airport."
original_explanation: The place where you either cry because someone's leaving (OFW drama) or get excited for a vacation. It's basically the English word 'airport' but spelled the way your tita from the province would say it. The gateway to either Boracay or a 12-hour shift in Dubai.
usage_notes: Isang kolokyal na pagbaybay. Ang mas pormal na salita ay "paliparan".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sundo tayo sa **erport**, darating na si Tita galing Canada.","translation":"Let's go to the **airport** to pick someone up, Auntie is arriving from Canada."},{"sentence":"Maaga kaming pumunta sa **erport** para hindi mahuli sa flight.","translation":"We went to the **airport** early so we wouldn't be late for the flight."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na tumutukoy sa isang taong may kakulangan sa pag-iisip, o gumagawa ng mga bagay na walang katuturan; hangal.
original_explanation: 'Timang' is what your friend calls you when you do something ridiculously silly, like texting your ex at 2 AM or tripping over flat ground. It's a playful (or sometimes not-so-playful) way to say "idiot" or "goofball." It's less harsh than 'gago' but definitely gets the point across. "Huy, timang ka ba? Bakit mo ginawa 'yun?"
usage_notes: This is considered slang or colloquial. Its harshness depends heavily on the tone and relationship between the speakers.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para kang **timang** na tawa nang tawa mag-isa.","translation":"You look like an **idiot** laughing all by yourself."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala diyan, **timang** lang 'yang kausap mo.","translation":"Don't believe him, the person you're talking to is just a **fool**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang honoraryong titulo na iginagawad ng Santo Papa sa isang paring Katoliko bilang pagkilala sa kanyang serbisyo o posisyon sa simbahan.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "monseñor", na mula naman sa Italyanong "monsignore" na nangangahulugang "aking panginoon".
original_explanation: It's like a promotion for a priest. Not quite a bishop, but definitely a VIP (Very Important Priest). You know they're a big deal when people stop calling them 'Father' and start calling them 'Monsenyor'. It's the church's version of getting a 'Senior' in your job title.
usage_notes: A formal title of address and reference for a priest who has been granted this honor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinangunahan ni **Monsenyor** Cruz ang banal na misa.","translation":"**Monsignor** Cruz led the holy mass."},{"sentence":"Iginawad sa kanya ang titulong **Monsenyor** dahil sa kanyang mahabang paglilingkod sa diyosesis.","translation":"He was granted the title of **Monsignor** for his long service to the diocese."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang impormal na katawagan o pamansag sa isang kaibigang lalaki, katumbas ng 'pare' o 'tol'.
original_explanation: Short for 'brother'. The universal term of endearment for any male person whose name you don't know, from the Grab driver to the guy you're playing Mobile Legends with. It's the friendlier, more chill version of 'kuya'. "Brah, pa-assist naman dito sa lane."
usage_notes: Used informally among friends, particularly younger generations. It's a very casual term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uy **brah**, kamusta na? Tagal nating 'di nagkita.","translation":"Hey **bro**, how have you been? It's been a while since we last saw each other."},{"sentence":"Salamat sa tulong, **brah**!","translation":"Thanks for the help, **dude**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng hugis na bilog o parang bola.
original_explanation: Describes the moon, a basketball, or your face after the holidays. Also used to describe someone who is easily fooled or swayed ("mabilog ang ulo"). "Don't be 'mabilog ang ulo', 'wag basta-basta maniwala sa fake news."
usage_notes: Can also mean "gullible" when used in the idiomatic expression "mabilog ang ulo" (literally 'round head').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili kami ng **mabilog** na keso para sa Noche Buena.","translation":"We bought a **round** cheese for Christmas Eve dinner."},{"sentence":"Ang buwan ay **mabilog** na naman ngayong gabi.","translation":"The moon is **round** again tonight."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang eksaktong oras o panahon ng tanghali, karaniwang tumutukoy sa alas-dose ng tanghali.
original_explanation: That magical hour when your brain cells officially check out for lunch. It's when the sun is at its most savage, your stomach starts rumbling louder than the office AC, and the most important question of the day is 'Saan tayo kakain?' Peak traffic, peak heat, peak gutom.
usage_notes: Katanghalian specifically refers to the peak of noon, around 12 PM. Tanghali is more general (e.g., 11 AM to 1 PM).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tirik na tirik ang araw sa tapat ng **katanghalian**.","translation":"The sun is at its highest right at **noontime**."},{"sentence":"Magkita tayo sa **katanghalian** para mananghalian.","translation":"Let's meet at **midday** to have lunch."}]

translation: to us; for us; in our place
meaning_filipino: Isang panghalip na tumutukoy sa lugar, pagmamay-ari, o direksyon na nauukol sa mga nagsasalita, ngunit hindi kasama ang kausap.
etymology: Mula sa "sa" (preposition) at "amin" (first-person plural exclusive pronoun).
original_explanation: This is the 'exclusive' version of "us". Kapag sinabi mong "Punta ka **sa amin**," iniimbita mo siya sa bahay ninyo. Kapag sinabi mong "Para **sa amin** 'to," it means it's for your group, and sorry, hindi kasama si 'you'. It's the subtle art of Filipino inclusion and exclusion. Contrast this with 'sa atin' which is 'inclusive' (kasama ka).
usage_notes: Ang "sa amin" ay 'exclusive' (hindi kasama ang kausap), samantalang ang "sa atin" ay 'inclusive' (kasama ang kausap). Ito ay isang karaniwang pinagkakamalian ng mga nag-aaral ng Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maligayang Pasko mula **sa amin**!","translation":"Merry Christmas from **us**!"},{"sentence":"Umuwi ka na **sa amin**, hindi na ako galit.","translation":"Come home **to our place** now, I'm not angry anymore."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapahinto sa paggana o pag-andar ng isang bagay, tulad ng ilaw, apoy, o makina.
original_explanation: What you do to the lights before 'Netflix and chill', or what your mom yells at you to do when you leave a room. It's also what Meralco does to your power when there's a scheduled maintenance. The act of making something 'patay' (dead/off).
usage_notes: Context is key to differentiate this from the 'killing' meaning. Usually refers to electronics, fire, or engines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutan ang **pagpatay** ng ilaw bago umalis.","translation":"Don't forget the **act of turning off** the lights before you leave."}]

translation: to use soap; to soap oneself or something
meaning_filipino: Gamitan ng sabon ang katawan o anumang bagay upang linisin.
etymology: From `mag-` (verb prefix) + `sabon` (soap), which is from Spanish `jabón`.
original_explanation: The first step to not being "amoy araw." It's what you do in the shower to get clean, or when you're washing your hands for the 10th time today because you're a germaphobe. Also, the first step in the epic 'labada' journey of every Filipino household.
usage_notes: Commonly used for personal hygiene and cleaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magsabon** nang mabuti para matanggal ang dumi.","translation":"You need **to soap** yourself well to remove the dirt."},{"sentence":"Tinuruan niya ang bata kung paano **magsabon** ng kamay nang tama.","translation":"She taught the child how **to soap** their hands correctly."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang rolyo ng mga pinatuyong dahon ng tabako na sinisindihan upang hithitin ang usok. Mas malaki at mas makapal ito kaysa sa sigarilyo.
original_explanation: This is the 'boss level' of smoking. The sigaro is what the kontrabida in a '90s action film or the rich haciendero smokes while plotting something evil. It's thick, it's strong, and it screams 'I have money and/or I am the final boss.' Not to be confused with its skinny cousin, the sigarilyo.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to a cigar, not a cigarette.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig mag-**sigaro** ang lolo ko pagkatapos mananghalian.","translation":"My grandfather loves to smoke a **cigar** after lunch."},{"sentence":"Amoy **sigaro** ang buong kwarto ng Don.","translation":"The Don's entire room smells of **cigar**."}]

meaning_filipino: Itali nang mahigpit sa paraang nagkakaroon ng buhol; paglapitin at pagdugtungin sa pamamagitan ng tali.
original_explanation: This is what you do to your shoelaces, the plastic bag of suka from the palengke, or your feelings for your crush para hindi na kumalat. 'Wag mo nang ibuhol ang buhay mo sa taong 'di ka naman priority.
usage_notes: Used for tying things like strings, ropes, or even figurative things like problems.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**ibuhol** mo nang mahigpit ang tali para hindi makawala ang aso.","translation":"Please **tie** the rope tightly so the dog can't get away."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **ibuhol** ang sinulid sa karayom.","translation":"She tried to **knot** the thread onto the needle."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa presyo ng isang produkto o serbisyo na hindi na maaaring tawaran o babaan pa. Maaari ring isulat na 'fixprice'.
original_explanation: The three saddest words you can hear in a tiangge or from a Divisoria vendor when you're trying to haggle. It's the seller's final answer, the end of negotiations. Kapag narinig mo 'to, it means 'wala nang tawad, besh.'
usage_notes: Often written as one word ('fixprice') colloquially. The opposite of 'tawad' (haggle).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan kong tawaran pero **fix price** daw.","translation":"I tried to haggle but they said it's a **fixed price**."},{"sentence":"Lahat ng items dito, **fix price** na po.","translation":"All items here are already at a **fixed price**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos o galaw mismo ng pagwagayway ng kamay bilang pagbati o pamamaalam.
original_explanation: It's the gesture itself. 'Isang kaway lang, sapat na.' (Just one wave is enough.) It's the noun form of the action. You give a 'kaway', you don't just 'kaway'. Like how a beauty queen perfects her 'kaway' for the parade.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa mismong kilos o galaw.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang matamis na **kaway** ang kanyang isinukli sa aking pagbati.","translation":"She returned my greeting with a sweet **wave**."},{"sentence":"Ang huling **kaway** niya ay hindi ko malilimutan.","translation":"I will never forget his last **wave**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng prutas na bilog, may kulay lila o berde na balat, at may malagatas na laman. Kapag hiniwa nang pahalang, ang mga buto ay bumubuo ng hugis bituin.
original_explanation: That purple (or sometimes green) fruit that's super sweet and milky inside. You know you've eaten one when your lips get all sticky. It's called a star apple because when you slice it crosswise, the seeds make a perfect star pattern. It's a childhood favorite, often picked straight from a neighbor's tree (with permission, of course... hopefully).
usage_notes: Ang baybay na 'caimito' ay karaniwan ding ginagamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong prutas ang matamis na **kaimito**.","translation":"My favorite fruit is the sweet **star apple**."},{"sentence":"Umakyat si kuya sa puno para kumuha ng mga hinog na **kaimito**.","translation":"My older brother climbed the tree to get some ripe **star apples**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pampublikong lugar kung saan nagaganap ang bentahan at bilihan ng mga sariwang produkto tulad ng isda, karne, gulay, at prutas.
etymology: From Mexican Spanish 'palenque', meaning 'a site of public gathering'.
original_explanation: The original "add to cart" experience. It's where your mom becomes a financial genius, haggling for the best "tawad" on everything from galunggong to kangkong. The air is a mix of fresh produce, questionable smells, and the latest chismis from the suki vendors. Forget the supermarket, this is where the real deals and drama happen.
usage_notes: Often refers to a wet market (bagsakan).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maagang pumunta sa **palengke** si nanay para makabili ng sariwang isda.","translation":"Mom went to the **market** early to buy fresh fish."},{"sentence":"Ang ingay sa **palengke** tuwing umaga.","translation":"It's so noisy in the **public market** every morning."}]

translation: to tell a story; to narrate
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasalaysay ng isang kuwento o pangyayari, pasalita man o pasulat.
original_explanation: This is the official verb for 'chismis' (gossip) but in a more socially acceptable form. When your tita asks you to 'magkwento ka naman,' she's really asking for the latest tea on your love life, career, or that cousin you both don't like. It's the foundation of Filipino social gatherings.
usage_notes: `magkwento` is the more common and modern spelling. `magkuwento` is an older, alternative spelling but is still understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig si Lola na **magkwento** tungkol sa kanyang kabataan.","translation":"Grandma loves to **tell stories** about her youth."},{"sentence":"**Magkwento** ka naman tungkol sa bakasyon mo sa Palawan.","translation":"**Tell us a story** about your vacation in Palawan."}]

translation: to become fibrous; to form fibers
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbuo o pagkakaroon ng mga hibla o sinulid, karaniwan sa mga bagay na naluto nang matagal tulad ng karne.
original_explanation: 'Yung manok na tinola na sobrang lambot, nagma-maghibla na siya. Parang puso mong paulit-ulit nasaktan, durog at hibla-hibla na lang. It describes something, usually overcooked meat, that separates easily into strands.
usage_notes: Often used to describe overcooked meat, especially chicken or beef, that easily separates into strands.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa tagal ng pagpapakulo, nagsimula nang **maghibla** ang karneng baka.","translation":"Because of the long boiling time, the beef started to **become fibrous**."},{"sentence":"Gusto ko 'yung adobo na halos **maghibla** na sa lambot.","translation":"I like the adobo when it's so tender it's almost **falling into strands**."}]

translation: to cause to soar; to launch
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapalipad o pagpapatalsik ng isang bagay paitaas nang may bilis at lakas.
etymology: From mag- (actor-focus verb prefix) + pa- (causative prefix) + imbulog (to soar).
original_explanation: This is a very dramatic, almost poetic word. It's what you do with a rocket ship, a kite, or your dreams. "Magpaimbulog tayo ng saranggola!" It’s not just "paliparin" (to make fly); `magpaimbulog` has a sense of power, majesty, and soaring to great heights. Think of it as the verb for launching your career to the next level.
usage_notes: A more literary or formal term than `magpalipad`. It implies a powerful upward motion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ahensya ay **nagpaimbulog** ng isang satellite sa kalawakan.","translation":"The agency **launched** a satellite into space."},{"sentence":"Tulungan nating **magpaimbulog** ang mga pangarap ng kabataan.","translation":"Let us help the youth's dreams **soar**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng katawan sa pagitan ng tadyang at balakang; ang gilid na bahagi ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: Your body's 'side-chick' area, perfect for tickling (kiliti) or getting a stitch (paninikip) after running to catch the jeep. Sa usapang pwesto sa higaan, ito 'yung unang sumusuko kapag nakikipagsiksikan ka sa mga kapatid mo.
usage_notes: Refers to the side of the body or the side surface of an object.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masakit ang aking kanang **tagiliran**.","translation":"My right **side** hurts."},{"sentence":"Isinandal niya ang hagdan sa **tagiliran** ng bahay.","translation":"He leaned the ladder against the **side** of the house."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagtitipon, karaniwang tumatagal nang magdamag, upang magbigay-parangal at samahan ang mga naulila ng isang yumaong tao.
original_explanation: The Pinoy version of a wake. It's a social gathering fueled by coffee, biscuits, endless rounds of card games (tong-its, pusoy dos), and a whole lot of chismis to keep everyone awake. It's a sad occasion, but it's also a testament to Filipino community, where you literally stay up with the grieving family so they're not alone.
usage_notes: Also can be used more generally to mean 'staying up all night' for a purpose (e.g., to study, to work), but its primary meaning is a funeral wake. When used for other purposes, it's often phrased as 'maglamay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pupunta kami sa **lamay** ng lola ni Marco mamayang gabi.","translation":"We are going to the **wake** of Marco's grandmother tonight."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong mag-**lamay** para tapusin ang thesis ko.","translation":"I need to pull an **all-nighter** (lit. hold a vigil) to finish my thesis."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babae na kinikilala dahil sa kaniyang katapangan, natatanging mga nagawa, o marangal na katangian.
original_explanation: The female version of a 'bayani'. Think Gabriela Silang, Melchora Aquino (Tandang Sora), or your own nanay who can juggle a full-time job, manage the household, and still know where you left your keys. She's the Darna in real life, a true **bayaning babae**.
usage_notes: The direct equivalent of the English word 'heroine'. The Spanish-derived 'heroina' is also sometimes used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Melchora Aquino, o Tandang Sora, ay isang dakilang **bayaning babae** ng Himagsikang Pilipino.","translation":"Melchora Aquino, or Tandang Sora, is a great **heroine** of the Philippine Revolution."},{"sentence":"Ang bawat ina na nagsasakripisyo para sa kanyang mga anak ay isang **bayaning babae**.","translation":"Every mother who sacrifices for her children is a **heroine**."}]

translation: to be able to forbid or prohibit
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahan o karapatan na magpatupad ng pagbabawal sa isang gawain o kilos.
original_explanation: This is what your parents do when they say 'Bawal lumabas!' It's the power to lay down the law and say 'nope, you can't do that.' Think of a security guard telling you 'bawal pumarada dito' or your diet app telling you 'bawal ang extra rice.'
usage_notes: While 'bawal' is the common word for 'prohibited', 'makapagbawa' is the verb form indicating the ability to enforce that prohibition. The root 'bawa' is archaic and 'bawal' is more commonly used in its place.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga magulang lamang ang **makapagbawa** sa kanilang mga anak na maglaro sa labas.","translation":"Only the parents **can forbid** their children from playing outside."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **makapagbawa** sa akin na tuparin ang aking mga pangarap?","translation":"Who **can prohibit** me from fulfilling my dreams?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng panghimagas o meryenda na gawa sa saging (karaniwang saba) na hiniwa, binabalutan sa galapong, at piniprito. Karaniwang nilalagyan ng asukal sa ibabaw.
etymology: Possibly from Spanish, but its exact origin is uncertain. It refers specifically to this Filipino dish.
original_explanation: The OG Filipino afternoon snack. It's what happens when a 'saba' banana decides to level up by taking a dip in some batter and jumping into hot oil, then getting a nice shower of white sugar. It's the cousin of banana cue, but with more flair. Perfect with black coffee on a rainy day.
usage_notes: A popular street food and homemade meryenda in the Philippines. Variations exist, sometimes using sweet potato.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito ni lola na magprito ng **maruya** tuwing hapon.","translation":"It's grandma's favorite thing to fry **banana fritters** every afternoon."},{"sentence":"Magkano po ang isang piraso ng **maruya**?","translation":"How much is one piece of **maruya**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang itinalagang lugar kung saan maaaring sumakay o mag-abang ng sasakyan ang mga pasahero.
original_explanation: The official waiting shed, bus stop, or jeepney terminal. It's where you play the "paramihan ng tao" game while waiting for a ride during rush hour. "Doon tayo sa sakayan ng bus sa may kanto magkita."
usage_notes: Can refer to any place where one boards a vehicle, from a simple street corner for jeepneys to a large, formal terminal for buses or a pier for ships.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahaba ang pila sa **sakayan** ng tricycle tuwing umaga.","translation":"The line at the tricycle **loading area** is long every morning."},{"sentence":"Saang **sakayan** po ang bus na papuntang Baguio?","translation":"At which **terminal** is the bus going to Baguio?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging bastos, magaspang, o walang pinong asal sa pananalita o kilos.
original_explanation: This is the opposite of being "classy." It's the loud, offensive talk, the crass jokes, or the behavior that makes your lola shake her head and whisper "Walang modo." Think of it as the R-18 version of public behavior. It's the reason why some comments on social media get deleted. Masyadong mataas ang level ng bulgaridad.
usage_notes: A loanword that is well-integrated into Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi katanggap-tanggap ang **bulgaridad** sa isang pormal na pagtitipon.","translation":"**Vulgarity** is not acceptable in a formal gathering."},{"sentence":"Sinita siya ng guro dahil sa **bulgaridad** ng kanyang pananalita.","translation":"The teacher reprimanded him for the **coarseness** of his language."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng alternatibong rock music na sumikat noong dekada '90, na kilala sa tunog na pinagsasama ang punk rock at heavy metal; tumutukoy din sa istilo ng pananamit na nauugnay dito, tulad ng mga flanel na damit at punit na maong.
original_explanation: The official uniform and soundtrack of your cool tito's youth. Think flannel shirts, ripped jeans, combat boots, and the angsty-yet-awesome sounds of Nirvana, Pearl Jam, and Soundgarden. It's the 'I don't care but I secretly care a lot' vibe that defined the '90s.
usage_notes: Refers to both the music genre and the associated fashion style.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paboritong banda ng kuya ko ang Nirvana, puro **grunge** ang pinapakinggan niya.","translation":"My older brother's favorite band is Nirvana, he listens to nothing but **grunge**."},{"sentence":"Bumalik sa uso ang **grunge** fashion, 'di ba?","translation":"The **grunge** fashion style is back in trend, right?"}]

translation: To drop with force; to slam down.
meaning_filipino: Ang marahas o biglaang pagbaba o pagbagsak ng isang bagay mula sa itaas, na karaniwang may kasamang malakas na tunog.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung phone mo nung nalaman mong na-seen ka lang. You don't just drop it, you **ilagpak** it. It's dropping something with feelings, usually negative ones like anger or frustration. The sound is part of the definition.
usage_notes: Often used to express anger or frustration. Implies a loud sound upon impact.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ilagpak** ang telepono, baka masira.","translation":"Don't **slam** the phone down, it might break."},{"sentence":"**Inilagpak** niya ang mga libro sa mesa dahil sa inis.","translation":"He **slammed** the books on the table out of annoyance."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bulalas na nagpapahayag ng pagkagulat, pagkamangha, o kung minsan ay pagkadismaya.
etymology: From Spanish `¡caramba!`, an exclamation of surprise or annoyance.
original_explanation: Your lola's version of "OMG!" or "Shookt!" It's an old-school exclamation you blurt out when you're surprised, amazed, or slightly annoyed. Nakakita ka ng dambuhalang ahas? "Karamba!" Nanalo ka sa lotto? "Karamba!" Nakalimutan mo wallet mo? "Ay, karamba!" It's a classic for a reason.
usage_notes: Sounds somewhat dated or theatrical today, but is widely understood. Often used for humorous or dramatic effect.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Karamba!** Ang laki naman ng isdang nahuli mo!","translation":"**Good heavens!** That's a huge fish you caught!"},{"sentence":"**Karamba!** Naiwan ko na naman ang aking salamin.","translation":"**Gosh!** I left my glasses again."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na lumikas o inilikas mula sa isang mapanganib na lugar.
original_explanation: The official term for people na "nag-bakasyon" sa covered court ng barangay dahil sa baha. You'll find them playing tong-its, sharing chismis, and waiting for the relief goods to arrive. Sila ang bida sa 24 Oras tuwing may bagyo.
usage_notes: Ito ang tawag sa tao, habang ang "ebakwasyon" ay ang proseso.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Namahagi ng relief goods ang DSWD sa mga **ebakwet**.","translation":"The DSWD distributed relief goods to the **evacuees**."},{"sentence":"Pansamantalang nakatira ang mga **ebakwet** sa paaralan.","translation":"The **evacuees** are temporarily living in the school."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagmumumog na may kasamang tunog sa lalamunan, karaniwan ay gamit ang tubig o gamot.
original_explanation: The sound you make when you're trying to get rid of a sore throat with salt and water. It's like a mini-yodel in your throat. Your dentist's favorite verb after 'sipilyo'.
usage_notes: A less common synonym for 'mumog'. Its usage for 'gargle' might be regional.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinayuhan siya ng doktor na mag-**kalagkag** ng maligamgam na tubig na may asin.","translation":"The doctor advised him to **gargle** with warm salt water."},{"sentence":"Naririnig ko siyang nag-**kakalagkag** sa banyo tuwing umaga.","translation":"I hear him **gargling** in the bathroom every morning."}]

translation: to bear fruit; to result in
meaning_filipino: Ang pagluluwal ng bunga ng isang halaman. Sa malarawang kahulugan, ito ay ang pagkakaroon ng resulta o kinalabasan ng isang gawain o pagsisikap.
original_explanation: When a plant literally grows a fruit. Figuratively, it's when your hard work finally pays off. Your late nights studying 'nagbunga' in high grades. Your savings 'nagbunga' in a new iPhone. It's the 'finally!' moment after all the effort.
usage_notes: Very common in both its literal (agriculture) and figurative (results, consequences) senses.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula nang **magbunga** ang aming tanim na mangga.","translation":"Our mango tree has started to **bear fruit**."},{"sentence":"Sana ay **magbunga** ang lahat ng ating paghihirap.","translation":"I hope all our hardships will **bear fruit**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hindi pagbibigay ng atensyon o pagwawalang-bahala sa isang tao, bagay, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'seen zone' move. When your crush walks past you like you're invisible, or when your boss conveniently forgets your suggestion in a meeting. It's the art of making someone feel like they're just part of the background. Ouch.
usage_notes: Ang anyong 'di pansinin' ay ang pawatas o pautos. Sa pangungusap, madalas itong nagiging 'hindi pinansin' (past tense) o 'hindi pinapansin' (present tense).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **di pansinin** ang malaking problema sa basura.","translation":"It's hard **to ignore** the huge garbage problem."},{"sentence":"Pinili niyang **di pansinin** ang mga tsismis tungkol sa kanya.","translation":"She chose **to ignore** the rumors about her."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mapanlait na salitang balbal na naglalarawan sa isang bagay, tao, o pag-uugali na itinuturing na mababang-uri, baduy, o walang sapat na kagandahang-asal.
etymology: A diminutive/adjectival form derived from the English word 'squatter', which has a strong socio-economic connotation in the Philippines.
original_explanation: A modern, slightly classist slang for anything considered "jologs," "baduy," or low-class. Derived from "squatter." It's what you'd call that weird font with too many curls, a ridiculously loud outfit, or someone causing a scene in public. It's the aesthetic opposite of "sosyal." Use with caution, as it can be quite offensive.
usage_notes: A derogatory slang term. Its use can be seen as offensive and classist. Often spelled as 'isquami'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **squammy** naman ng ugali niya, naninigaw sa gitna ng mall.","translation":"Her behavior is so **trashy**, shouting in the middle of the mall."},{"sentence":"Pinalitan niya ang case ng phone niya dahil masyado daw **squammy** tingnan.","translation":"She changed her phone case because she said it looked too **tacky**."}]

meaning_filipino: Mahigpit na nakatali, karaniwan sa pamamagitan ng lubid, kadena, o posas, upang hindi makakilos.
original_explanation: Like a character in an action movie captured by the villains. Or figuratively, how you feel when you're stuck in a dead-end job or a toxic relationship—you're bound and can't escape. It's about being physically or emotionally restrained.
usage_notes: Can be literal (physically tied) or metaphorical (emotionally or socially constrained).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iniligtas ng pulis ang biktimang **nakagapos** sa isang silya.","translation":"The police rescued the victim who was **tied up** to a chair."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam niya ay **nakagapos** siya sa mga utang na kailangan niyang bayaran.","translation":"He feels **shackled** by the debts he needs to pay."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng mutwal na pag-unawa o pagkakaunawaan sa pagitan ng mga tao.
etymology: From `mag-` + `ka-` + `intindi` (from Spanish 'entender') + `-han`, denoting a reciprocal or mutual understanding.
original_explanation: The goal of every couple's argument, every team meeting, and every time you try to explain a meme to your parents. "Para magkaintindihan tayo..." is the opening line to either a very productive conversation or a very long lecture. It's about being on the same page, finally getting the signal when the WiFi of your brains connects.
usage_notes: A crucial verb in communication and relationships. It signifies mutual comprehension.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga sa isang relasyon na **magkaintindihan** ang dalawang tao.","translation":"It is important in a relationship for two people to **understand each other**."},{"sentence":"Mabuti't **nagkaintindihan** din tayo sa wakas.","translation":"It's a good thing we finally **came to an understanding**."}]

translation: to have something boiled; to instigate
meaning_filipino: Ang pagluluto ng isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pagpapakulo nito sa tubig; maaari ring tumukoy sa pagsisimula o pag-uudyok ng gulo o intriga.
original_explanation: This word has two flavors, one for the kitchen and one for the chismis. The literal one is 'to boil something,' like magpakulo ng tubig for coffee or magpakulo ng itlog. The juicy one is 'to stir up trouble' or 'to start drama.' When someone is spreading rumors to see what happens, they're nagpapakulo. It’s the culinary and social equivalent of turning up the heat.
usage_notes: The context determines whether it's literal (cooking) or figurative (instigating trouble). The figurative sense is quite common in colloquial speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang nag-utos na **magpakulo** ng manok para sa sopas?","translation":"Who ordered to **have the chicken boiled** for the soup?"},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala diyan, gusto lang niyang **magpakulo** ng intriga.","translation":"Don't believe that, he just wants to **instigate** intrigue."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang palihim na pagmamasid o pag-eespiya sa galaw ng isang tao, grupo, o kalaban; ang pag-alam sa sitwasyon ng isang lugar.
original_explanation: This is the verb for the certified 'Marites' or 'chismoso'. To 'magbakay' is to secretly observe, to scout the area, to gather intel. It's what you do before entering a family reunion to see who's already there, or what basketball teams do to check out their opponents' strategies. It's low-key espionage.
usage_notes: Implies secrecy and observation for a specific purpose, which could be for gossip, military strategy, or simple curiosity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan ang mga sundalo na **magbakay** sa kuta ng mga kalaban.","translation":"The soldiers were ordered to **scout** the enemy's camp."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko si Aling Nena na nagbabakay sa bintana, inaabangan kung sino ang bisita mo.","translation":"I saw Aling Nena **spying** from the window, waiting to see who your visitor was."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sapilitang pagkuha o pag-embargo ng mga ari-arian o bagay-bagay, karaniwang isinasagawa ng may kapangyarihan.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you try to bring a whole lechon into another country and customs says 'Nope.' It’s the official act of taking something away, usually by an authority figure like the police seizing evidence, or your mom confiscating your phone for not doing chores.
usage_notes: Has a strong legal or authoritative connotation. Implies that the taking is forceful or official. 'Pagkumpiska' is a common Spanish-derived synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinag-utos ng korte ang **pagsamsam** sa mga ilegal na pag-aari ng suspek.","translation":"The court ordered the **confiscation** of the suspect's illegal properties."},{"sentence":"Naging mabilis ang **pagsamsam** ng mga pulis sa mga kontrabando.","translation":"The police's **seizure** of the contraband was swift."}]

translation: a clearing of a path; a slash or graze
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aalis ng mga sagabal tulad ng damo o sanga upang makagawa ng daan; ang marka o hiwa na resulta nito.
original_explanation: Imagine you're in a horror movie, lost in a jungle. The act of frantically chopping away at vines and tall grass with a bolo knife to make a path? That's 'pag-dasdas'. The resulting cleared path is also the 'dasdas'. It’s the OG 'clearing my path' before it became a self-help mantra.
usage_notes: Can refer to both the act of clearing and the resulting path. It can also mean a superficial cut, scratch, or graze on the skin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumawa sila ng **dasdas** sa kagubatan para mas mabilis makarating sa ilog.","translation":"They made a **clearing** in the forest to get to the river faster."},{"sentence":"May **dasdas** ng kalmot ng pusa sa braso niya.","translation":"There's a **graze** from a cat's scratch on his arm."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking sisidlan, karaniwang gawa sa kahoy o bato, na ginagamit na pandikdik o pambayo ng mga butil tulad ng palay o mais, kasama ng halo o pestle.
original_explanation: The OG food processor. It's that giant wooden or stone bowl where your lola pounds rice or garlic with a huge pestle (halo). The sound of it is the provincial alarm clock. Before blenders and Magic Bullets, there was the mighty 'lubang'.
usage_notes: Often paired with 'halo' (pestle). Not to be confused with 'lusong', which is a more common term for the same object.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang **lubang** at halo upang magbayo ng palay.","translation":"She used the **mortar** and pestle to pound rice grains."},{"sentence":"Ang lumang **lubang** na gawa sa bato ay pamana pa ng kanyang lolo.","translation":"The old stone **mortar** is an heirloom from his grandfather."}]

meaning_filipino: Hayag, lantad, o kitang-kita; walang takip o hindi nakatago.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na na-seen ka na pero 'di pa nagrereply. Your secret is out in the open, fully visible. Like when your messy room is suddenly visible on a Zoom call because your virtual background failed. 'Huli ka, balbon!' Your scheme is tambad na!
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin kasama ang panlaping na- (natambad) o i- (itambad) upang bumuo ng pandiwa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tambad** sa lahat ang kanyang mga kasinungalingan.","translation":"His lies were **exposed** to everyone."},{"sentence":"Natambad ang sikreto niya nang may mag-post sa social media.","translation":"Her secret was **revealed** when someone posted on social media."}]

translation: to leave, to depart, to remove
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-alis, paglisan, o pag-iwan sa isang lugar; o ang pagtanggal ng isang bagay mula sa kinalalagyan nito.
original_explanation: The magic word you whisper to your friend kapag nasa isang boring na party kayo: 'Tara, **alis** na tayo.' It's also what your salary does two days after payday. It just... leaves.
usage_notes: Isang salitang-ugat na nagiging 'umalis' (to leave), 'alisin' (to remove), 'alisan' (to remove from). Ang 'Alis!' ay isang pautos na nangangahulugang 'Leave!' o 'Get out!'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Alis** na ako, baka mahuli pa ako sa trabaho.","translation":"I'm **leaving** now, I might be late for work."},{"sentence":"Pakitingnan kung may **alis** na ang mantsa sa damit.","translation":"Please check if the stain on the clothes has been **removed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pulbos na materyales na gawa sa apog at luwad, na kapag hinaluan ng tubig at buhangin ay tumitigas at ginagamit sa konstruksiyon.
original_explanation: The gray powder that built the Philippines, one hardware store at a time. It's what your dad mixes for that DIY project he started 5 years ago. It's the stuff that gets on your new shoes when you walk past a construction site. The foundation of every SM mall and condo unit.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'kongkreto' (concrete) in casual conversation, though technically cement is an ingredient of concrete.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si Tatay ng isang sakong **semento** sa hardware.","translation":"Dad bought a sack of **cement** at the hardware store."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng mas maraming **semento** para tumibay ang pader.","translation":"More **cement** is needed to make the wall stronger."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkain sa bandang tanghali, ang pangunahing pagkain sa gitna ng araw.
etymology: Mula sa `mang-` + `tanghali` (noon). Ang `mang-` ay nagiging `man-` at ang `t` ng salitang-ugat ay nawawala.
original_explanation: The sacred Filipino ritual between 12 PM and 1 PM. Ito 'yung oras na biglang tumatahimik ang office, naglalabasan ang mga baon, at nagiging ghost town ang kalsada (maliban sa paligid ng mga karinderya). The verb form of "tanghalian". "Tara, mananghali na tayo!" is the best invitation you can get at work.
usage_notes: Ito ay ang pandiwa o kilos ng pagkain. Ang mismong pagkain ay tinatawag na `tanghalian`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Saan niyo balak **mananghali** mamaya?","translation":"Where do you plan **to eat lunch** later?"},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **mananghali** nang maaga dahil may miting ako.","translation":"I need **to eat lunch** early because I have a meeting."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang elementong metaliko na may simbolong 'Ni' at atomikong bilang na 28; isang matigas at kulay-pilak na puting metal na ginagamit sa paggawa ng barya at iba pang haluang metal.
original_explanation: It's that shiny metal that's not quite silver, not quite steel. You see it in coins (like the old 25-centavo coin), batteries, and sometimes in cheap jewelry that turns your skin green. It's also a huge mining export for the Philippines, making it a hot topic in both business and environmental news.
usage_notes: A technical or scientific term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Pilipinas ay isa sa mga pangunahing prodyuser ng **nikel** sa mundo.","translation":"The Philippines is one of the world's top producers of **nickel**."},{"sentence":"Gawa sa **nikel** at tanso ang ilang barya.","translation":"Some coins are made of **nickel** and copper."}]

translation: to have a drinking session with; to get drunk with others
meaning_filipino: Ang sama-samang pag-inom ng alak kasama ang ibang tao, na kadalasan ay humahantong sa kalasingan.
original_explanation: The formal term for "tagay" or "inuman." This is the sacred Filipino ritual of solving the world's problems (or creating new ones) over bottles of beer or gin, accompanied by pulutan and a shared "tagayan" glass. It's where friendships are forged and secrets are (drunkenly) revealed.
usage_notes: Often has a slightly negative or informal connotation compared to the more neutral "makipag-inuman."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinagalitan siya ng nanay niya dahil gabi na siyang umuwi matapos **makipaglasingan**.","translation":"His mom scolded him because he came home late after **having a drinking session**."},{"sentence":"Tuwing Biyernes, ang magkakatrabaho ay nagkikita upang **makipaglasingan**.","translation":"Every Friday, the coworkers meet up to **get drunk together**."}]

translation: to transport to the city; to bring upstream
meaning_filipino: Ang pagdadala o pagbiyahe ng mga produkto o tao mula sa probinsya o isang mas mababang lugar patungo sa siyudad o sentro ng kalakalan.
original_explanation: This is the opposite of 'iuwi sa probinsya'. It's when you bring goods, produce, or even your newly-arrived relative from the province to the big city, usually Manila. Think of farmers bringing their fresh harvest to be sold in Divisoria or Balintawak. "Iluwas mo na 'yang mga mangga para kumita na tayo!"
usage_notes: Often used in the context of commerce and travel, contrasting the province ('probinsya') with the city ('siyudad' or 'Maynila').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **iluwas** ang mga sariwang gulay sa Maynila bago pa masira ang mga ito.","translation":"The fresh vegetables need to be **brought to Manila** before they spoil."},{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **iluwas** ang kanyang buong pamilya para sa mas magandang oportunidad.","translation":"He decided to **bring** his whole family **to the city** for better opportunities."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng isang bagay na hindi mahahawakan o mararamdaman sa pamamagitan ng pandama ng paghipo.
etymology: Mula sa "di-" (hindi) at "nasasalat" (nahahawakan), mula sa ugat na "salat" (hawakan; kakulangan).
original_explanation: Ito yung mga bagay na parang 'feelings' mo para sa kanya—alam mong nandiyan, pero hindi mo mahawakan. Parang Wi-Fi signal, ramdam mo ang presence pero hindi mo makikita. O kaya yung bonus na pinangako, hanggang salita lang, di-nasasalat.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin para sa mga abstraktong konsepto tulad ng pag-ibig, karangalan, o mga digital na produkto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-ibig ay isang damdaming **di-nasasalat** ngunit makapangyarihan.","translation":"Love is an **intangible** but powerful feeling."},{"sentence":"Ang mga ideya at konsepto ay mga kayamanang **di-nasasalat**.","translation":"Ideas and concepts are **intangible** treasures."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng malambot na materyal na ginagamit upang takpan at protektahan ang isang sugat o pinsala sa katawan.
original_explanation: Ito yung nilalagay mo sa sugat after mong linisin. Parang temporary solution din sa mga problema sa buhay, tinatakpan mo lang pero andyan pa rin. "Bes, kailangan ko ng bendahe para sa puso kong sugatan."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nilagyan ng nars ng **bendahe** ang braso ng pasyente.","translation":"The nurse put a **bandage** on the patient's arm."},{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng isang kahon ng **bendahe** para sa first aid kit.","translation":"I bought a box of **bandages** for the first aid kit."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghingi ng tulong pinansyal o materyal, karaniwan ay dahil sa kahirapan.
original_explanation: This is the act of asking for alms or donations, usually on the street. It's a serious social issue. On a lighter, 'hugot' note, sometimes it feels like you're doing this for your crush's attention: "Nagpapalimos ng pansin."
usage_notes: Specifically refers to begging for money or food, not begging in a general sense (which would be 'nagmamakaawa').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May mga batang **nagpapalimos** sa kanto tuwing Pasko.","translation":"There are children **begging** at the corner every Christmas."},{"sentence":"Para kang **nagpapalimos** ng pag-ibig sa kanya.","translation":"It's like you're **begging** for love from him."}]

translation: to have something be finished or completed
meaning_filipino: Utos o pakiusap na dalhin sa katapusan o kumpletuhin ang isang nasimulang gawain, proyekto, o trabaho.
original_explanation: The magic words a project manager says to the team on a Friday afternoon. Also what you tell the repairman about the leaky faucet before you pay him. 'Ipatapos mo na 'yan para makauwi na tayo.' It's the finish line in verb form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **ipatapos** ang report na ito bago mag-uwian.","translation":"I need to **have** this report **finished** before dismissal."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng kumot sa isang tao o bagay upang takpan ito.
original_explanation: Ito yung action na ginagawa mo sa jowa mong nilalamig, o sa sarili mo pag nanonood ng Netflix at umuulan. The ultimate act of care, or self-care. "Tara, kumutan na kita ng pagmamahal ko... charot, kumot lang talaga."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kinomutan** ng ina ang kanyang natutulog na anak.","translation":"The mother **covered** her sleeping child **with a blanket**."},{"sentence":"Paki-**kumutan** mo nga ako, nilalamig ako.","translation":"Please **cover me with a blanket**, I'm cold."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging labis na nakatuon sa sariling kapakanan, pangangailangan, at kagustuhan nang hindi isinasaalang-alang ang iba.
etymology: Nagmula sa `pagka-` (katangian ng pagiging) at `makasarili` (nakatuon sa sarili), na buhat sa salitang `sarili`.
original_explanation: Ito yung 'Me, Myself, and I' ang national anthem. Sila yung uubos ng huling piraso ng pizza nang hindi nagtatanong, o yung laging late sa BPO shift pero unang-unang mag-o-out. Classic main character syndrome. Sa group project, sila yung taga-print lang pero feeling leader.
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang salita upang ilarawan ang isang negatibong katangian ng isang tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **pagkamakasarili**, iniwan siya ng kanyang mga kaibigan.","translation":"Because of his **selfishness**, his friends left him."},{"sentence":"Isantabi muna natin ang **pagkamakasarili** para sa ikabubuti ng lahat.","translation":"Let's set aside **self-centeredness** for the good of everyone."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tapat ngunit kadalasang sunud-sunurang tagasunod o alalay ng isang makapangyarihang tao, na karaniwang may negatibong konotasyon.
etymology: From Spanish 'olvidados' (the forgotten ones), but the meaning has shifted significantly in Filipino.
original_explanation: The squad of a kontrabida. The 'yes men' or 'goons' of a corrupt politician or an evil CEO in a teleserye. They're the ones who do the dirty work, the 'utusan', the 'bata'. If the main villain is the final boss, the 'ulipores' are the minions you have to defeat first.
usage_notes: Almost always used with a negative connotation, implying blind or subservient following. Often used interchangeably with 'alipores'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinalibutan ang bida ng mga **ulipores** ng kontrabida.","translation":"The protagonist was surrounded by the villain's **henchmen**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinuno ng isang sasakyang-dagat, sasakyang-panghimpapawid, o isang pangkat ng mga tao, tulad ng koponan sa palakasan o barangay.
original_explanation: The leader of the pack. Could be the 'Kap' of your barangay who settles disputes about noisy karaoke, the captain of your favorite PBA team, or the pilot who says 'cabin crew, please be seated for take-off'. Basically, the boss.
usage_notes: Most commonly refers to the Barangay Captain ('Kapitan ng Barangay').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isumbong mo kay **Kapitan** ang magnanakaw na iyan!","translation":"Report that thief to the **Captain**!"},{"sentence":"Siya ang **kapitan** ng aming koponan sa basketball.","translation":"He is the **captain** of our basketball team."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking sasakyang de-motor na ginagamit sa paghahatid o paglilipat ng mabibigat na kargamento.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na "truck". Ang karaniwang baybay sa Filipino ay "trak".
original_explanation: Yung hari ng kalsada na laging nasa unahan mo 'pag late ka na. Mas malaki pa sa bus, at 'pag bumusina, feeling mo katapusan mo na. Sila ang dahilan kung bakit may "Keep Distance" na sign sa likod ng mga sasakyan. Common sight sa SLEX at NLEX.
usage_notes: Bagama't ang baybay na "truck" ay ginagamit, ang "trak" ang mas tinatanggap na Filipino na baybay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumaan ang isang malaking **truck** na may kargang buhangin.","translation":"A big **truck** carrying sand passed by."},{"sentence":"Ingat sa pag-overtake sa mga **truck** sa highway.","translation":"Be careful when overtaking **trucks** on the highway."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na mahirap paniwalaan dahil ito ay pambihira, kagila-gilalas, o taliwas sa karaniwang karanasan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "paniwala" na inuulit at nilalagyan ng unlaping "ka-" at "di-".
original_explanation: This is your reaction when your friend who's always late arrives on time. It's the plot of your favorite K-drama. It's the chismis from your kapitbahay that's too wild to be true (but you secretly hope it is). It can be good ('Nanalo ako sa lotto!') or bad ('Yung aso ang kumain ng project ko!'). It's the official motto of "Wow, Mali!".
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin upang ipahayag ang pagkamangha (positibo) o pagdududa (negatibo).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Di-kapani-paniwala** ang ganda ng tanawin mula sa tuktok ng bundok.","translation":"The view from the top of the mountain is **unbelievably** beautiful."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang kuwento ay **di-kapani-paniwala**, ngunit totoo.","translation":"His story is **incredible**, but true."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na para lamang sa personal na paggamit at hindi para ipagbili o ipahiram sa iba.
original_explanation: This is the official label for that really nice pen you don't want your officemates to borrow, or the "good" towel you hide when visitors come over. "Pang-sariling-gamit lang" is a polite way of saying "Get your own!" It’s the opposite of “for sharing.”
usage_notes: Used to specify that an item is not for public, commercial, or shared use.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga gamot na ito ay para sa **sariling-gamit** lamang.","translation":"These medicines are for **personal use** only."},{"sentence":"Mayroon siyang sasakyan na **sariling-gamit**, at isa para sa negosyo.","translation":"He has a car for **personal use**, and one for business."}]

translation: is starting to like; is fond of
meaning_filipino: Ang unti-unting pagkakaroon ng pagkagusto o paghanga sa isang tao, bagay, o ideya. Ito ay tumutukoy sa isang proseso o damdamin na nabubuo sa kasalukuyan.
etymology: Tagalog prefix 'na-' + 'gusto' + suffix '-han', with reduplication of the first syllable 'gu-'.
original_explanation: The "getting there" stage of feelings. Hindi mo pa "love," pero hindi na rin "like" lang. It's when you find yourself smiling at their texts. "OMG bes, feeling ko nagugustuhan ko na siya." It can also apply to things, like that K-drama you were hesitant to watch or the bitter taste of ampalaya you now find... tolerable. It's the slow burn of affection.
usage_notes: This is a complex verb form. The '-an' suffix makes it object-focused. The 'na-...' + reduplication indicates an ongoing, developing, or involuntary state. It means "is coming to be liked (by the actor)."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mukhang **nagugustuhan** na ng pusa ang bago niyang pagkain.","translation":"It seems the cat **is starting to like** its new food."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko alam kung bakit, pero **nagugustuhan** ko na ang mga kanta niya.","translation":"I don't know why, but I'm **starting to like** his/her songs."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi mapakali sa isang lugar; palaging gumagalaw o kumikilos. Tumutukoy din sa isang batang puspos ng enerhiya at kung minsan ay mahirap patigilin.
original_explanation: This is your pamangkin who just had three cups of Coke. They can't stay still, always touching things, climbing furniture, and generally causing cute chaos. It's also used for that person in a meeting who keeps shaking their leg or tapping their pen. 'Yung kamay na malikot sa wallet mo, iba na 'yun.
usage_notes: Often used to describe children, but can also describe restless movements in adults or even animals. Can have a slightly negative or endearing connotation depending on context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **malikot** na bata ay nahulog sa kama.","translation":"The **restless** child fell from the bed."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **malikot** habang ginugupitan kita ng buhok.","translation":"Don't be **fidgety** while I'm cutting your hair."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay na nakapagpapagaling ng sakit, nakalulunas sa isang suliranin, o nagwawasto sa isang kamalian.
original_explanation: Your lola's go-to solution for everything. May lagnat? Vicks. Ubo? Salabat. Broken heart? "Marami pang isda sa dagat, apo." A remedyo isn't just medicine; it's any fix, from a quick-fix solution at work to a life hack you saw on TikTok. It's the answer to "Paano 'to?"
usage_notes: Can be used for health, problems, or any kind of issue needing a solution.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang pinakamabisang **remedyo** sa sakit ng ulo?","translation":"What is the most effective **remedy** for a headache?"},{"sentence":"Wala na siyang makitang **remedyo** sa problema nila sa pera.","translation":"He can no longer find a **solution** to their money problems."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang krimen ng sapilitang pakikipagtalik o paggamit ng karahasan at pananakot upang mapasunod ang isang tao sa gawaing sekswal laban sa kanyang kalooban.
original_explanation: This is a heavy, serious word. There's no witty way to put it. **Panggagahasa** is the act of rape. It's a violent crime, a violation, and a topic that requires gravity and respect for the victims. It's not a punchline; it's a legal and social issue that we must confront seriously.
usage_notes: A very serious and formal term used in legal and news contexts. The verb is "gahasin" (to rape).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **panggagahasa** ay isang karumal-dumal na krimen na walang lugar sa ating lipunan.","translation":"**Rape** is a heinous crime that has no place in our society."},{"sentence":"Siya ay kinasuhan ng **panggagahasa** at nahatulan ng habambuhay na pagkakakulong.","translation":"He was charged with **rape** and sentenced to life imprisonment."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpipigil sa isang tao o bagay sa isang espasyo kung saan wala na itong matatakasan; paligiran upang hindi makawala.
original_explanation: What happens in an action movie when the hero is surrounded by goons in a dead-end alley. It's also what your boss does to you by the water cooler to ask about that report you haven't finished. "Nako, **susukulin** ako ni Ma'am tungkol sa O.T. ko." You're trapped, with no escape.
usage_notes: The root word "sukol" means cornered or trapped.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng mga pulis na **sukulin** ang magnanakaw sa isang eskinita.","translation":"The police tried **to corner** the thief in an alley."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi kita **susukulin** sa mga tanong.","translation":"Don't worry, I won't **trap** you with questions."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng pagkakaiba-iba sa katangian, anyo, o uri; hindi magkakatulad.
original_explanation: You and your siblings. One is a doctor, one is an artist, and you're still figuring things out—magkakaiba kayo ng landas. It’s like the flavors in a halo-halo; they're all in one glass but they're all magkakaiba. Diversity is the key!
usage_notes: A very common word to describe diversity or differences among a group.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magkakaiba** man ang ating mga opinyon, dapat pa rin tayong magkaisa.","translation":"Even if our opinions are **different**, we should still unite."},{"sentence":"Nag-aalok sila ng **magkakaiba**ng uri ng pagkain sa kanilang restawran.","translation":"They offer **various** kinds of food in their restaurant."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na kagamitang nabibitbit na lumilikha ng apoy, karaniwang ginagamit sa pagsisindi ng sigarilyo o kandila.
original_explanation: The most borrowed and never returned item in the Philippines, second only to ballpens. Essential for birthday candle emergencies, pang-sindi ng katol, at syempre, sa yosi break ng mga ka-officemate mo. 'Pahiram ng lighter, balik ko mamaya.' (Spoiler: hindi na babalik).
usage_notes: Isang napakakaraniwang hiram na salita.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawawala na naman ang **lighter** ko.","translation":"My **lighter** is missing again."},{"sentence":"Mayroon ka bang **lighter**? Magsisindi lang ako ng kandila.","translation":"Do you have a **lighter**? I'm just going to light a candle."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halaman na may mahahaba at makikitid na dahon, karaniwang tumutubo nang saganà sa mga parang, hardin, at bakuran.
original_explanation: The green stuff on your lawn you have to cut, or the unwanted plants your mom asks you to pull out from her garden ('bunutin mo ang mga damo!'). It's everywhere, from the side of the road to the football field. Also, a very common, very outdated slang for marijuana, but let's stick to the plant you see in parks, okay?
usage_notes: Can refer to both lawn grass and unwanted weeds. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko nang gupitin ang matataas na **damo** sa bakuran.","translation":"I need to cut the tall **grass** in the yard."},{"sentence":"Puno ng ligaw na **damo** ang hardin kaya kailangan itong linisin.","translation":"The garden is full of wild **weeds** so it needs to be cleaned."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-asinta, pagtuon, o pagpokus sa isang partikular na target, tao, o layunin.
etymology: Mula sa salitang "puntirya" (aim), na hango sa Espanyol na "puntería" (aim, marksmanship), na may hulaping "-hin".
original_explanation: When you set your sights on something. It could be a basketball hoop, a promo fare ticket, or the last piece of lechon at a party. It's the act of focusing all your energy and attention to hit a specific goal. 'Puntiryahin mo 'yung bullseye!' or 'Puntiryahin mo 'yung promotion this year!' Can also mean to single someone out.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for physical aiming or figuratively for goals, ambitions, or even singling someone out for criticism.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **puntiryahin** nang mabuti ang target para manalo sa laro.","translation":"You need **to aim** well at the target to win the game."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong laging **puntiryahin** sa mga biro mo.","translation":"Don't always **target** me in your jokes."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis na pagpapatama ng dulo ng daliri (karaniwan ay ang hinlalato) na binitawan mula sa pagkakaipit sa hinlalaki.
original_explanation: The OG way to get someone's attention from across the room before texts and DMs. It's also what you do to a bug on your desk, or what your grade school teacher did to your ear when you weren't listening. A low-tech, high-impact action.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa pagpitik ng isang bagay, pagpitik sa isang tao (isang magaang na tapik), o pagpitik ng mga daliri.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mamitik** ng gagamba kung ayaw mong magalit ang nanay mo.","translation":"Don't **flick** the spider if you don't want to make your mom angry."},{"sentence":"**Namitik** siya ng daliri para makuha ang atensyon ng weyter.","translation":"He **snapped** his fingers to get the waiter's attention."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang di-materyal na bahagi ng isang tao o nilalang; kaluluwa, sigla, o ang natatanging katangian ng isang bagay o gawain.
original_explanation: This is the 'ghost' in your 'ghosting' stories. It's the vibe you feel when someone enters the room, or the energy you need to survive another Monday morning meeting. Also, the main ingredient in your tita's favorite horror movies.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang **espiritu** ng Pasko sa mga ilaw at awitin.","translation":"He felt the **spirit** of Christmas in the lights and songs."},{"sentence":"Malakas ang **espiritu** ng pakikipaglaban ng mga atleta.","translation":"The fighting **spirit** of the athletes is strong."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pagkasira, pagguho, o paghina ng isang istruktura o bagay dahil sa bigat o presyon.
original_explanation: This is the 'hugot' version of 'nagbigay'. It's not about giving a gift; it's about something giving up. Like when a bridge collapses, it '**nagbigay**'. When your diet finally breaks after seeing a box of donuts, your self-control '**nagbigay**'. It’s the moment something reaches its breaking point. Sumuko na, bes.
usage_notes: This is a specific, idiomatic use of 'nagbigay' where it means to collapse, break, or give way under pressure. It is almost always followed by 'ang' and the subject that collapsed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa lakas ng lindol, **nagbigay** ang lumang gusali.","translation":"Due to the strength of the earthquake, the old building **collapsed**."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa bigat ng mga libro, **nagbigay** ang estante.","translation":"Because of the weight of the books, the shelf **gave way**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang damdamin ng pagkapahiya, pagkawala ng dangal, o pag-aalala sa opinyon ng iba dahil sa isang nagawang kamalian o di-kaaya-ayang sitwasyon.
etymology: From ka- + hiya (shame) + -an, forming an abstract noun representing the state or event of shame.
original_explanation: That feeling when you trip in public, call your teacher 'mom', or your crush sees you with a pimple patch on. It's the core of Filipino 'hiya' culture. 'Nako, anong **kahiyaan** ang sinapit ko!' means you just experienced something mortifying and will probably replay it in your head for the next 5 years.
usage_notes: 'Kahiyaan' is the abstract noun for the state or event of being embarrassed. 'Hiya' is the feeling itself. 'Pagkapahiya' is a close synonym focusing on the experience of being shamed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Upang maiwasan ang **kahiyaan**, inihanda niyang mabuti ang kanyang talumpati.","translation":"To avoid **embarrassment**, he prepared his speech well."},{"sentence":"Malaking **kahiyaan** ang idinulot ng iskandalo sa kanilang pamilya.","translation":"The scandal brought great **shame** to their family."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa teolohiyang Abrahamiko, ang katauhan na kumakatawan sa kasamaan, tukso, at pagiging kaaway ng Diyos.
etymology: From Spanish 'Satanás', from Latin 'Satanas', from Greek 'Σατανᾶς' (Satanâs), from Hebrew 'שָּׂטָן' (Sátan, "adversary").
original_explanation: The ultimate 'kontrabida' in the grand teleserye of life. Blamed for everything from traffic and missing Tupperware lids to actual temptation. "Naku, tinukso ako ni Satanas!" is the classic excuse when you give in to buying that 10th milk tea of the week.
usage_notes: Often used as a strong expletive or to describe a very evil person. The capitalization varies but is generally capitalized as a proper name.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpadala sa tukso ni **Satanas**.","translation":"Do not give in to the temptations of **Satan**."},{"sentence":"Para siyang si **Satanas** sa kasamaan.","translation":"He is like the **devil** in his wickedness."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pang-ugnay na nagpapahiwatig ng pagpapatuloy ng isang kilos o kalagayan sa kabila ng isang hadlang o salungat na kondisyon.
etymology: Mula sa pariralang Espanyol na 'mas que' (higit pa sa).
original_explanation: The official phrase of the "sige, push natin 'to" squad. "Maski na umuulan, tutuloy tayo sa beach." "Maski na wala nang pera, o-order pa rin sa Shopee." It's the Filipino spirit of 'bahala na' but with more determination. Synonymous with 'kahit na'.
usage_notes: Maaaring ipagpalit sa 'kahit na'. Ang 'maski' ay maaari ring gamitin nang mag-isa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Maski na** pagod, pumasok pa rin siya sa trabaho.","translation":"**Even though** he was tired, he still went to work."},{"sentence":"Mahal kita, **maski na** magulo ang kuwarto mo.","translation":"I love you, **although** your room is a mess."}]

translation: to debate about something; a debate session
meaning_filipino: Bilang pandiwa, ito ay ang pagtalakay o pagtatalo sa isang paksa. Bilang pangalan, ito ay tumutukoy sa isang pagtitipon o kaganapan kung saan nagaganap ang isang debate.
etymology: Mula sa salitang ugat na 'debate' at hulaping '-han'.
original_explanation: This is the "let's get ready to rumble!" version of the word debate. As a verb, it's an action: "pag-debatihan natin 'yan" (let's debate that). As a noun, it's the event itself, the whole shebang. It’s like turning a simple 'debate' into a full-blown session, complete with an audience, maybe some snacks, and definitely a lot of opinions.
usage_notes: The '-an' suffix can turn the root word into a verb (to do the action towards something/someone) or a noun (a place or event where the action happens). Context determines the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag na nating **debatihan** pa ang maliliit na bagay.","translation":"Let's not **debate** about the small things anymore."},{"sentence":"Naging sikat ang **debatihan** ng mga mag-aaral sa social media.","translation":"The students' **debate session** became famous on social media."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon o paglalabas ng masamang amoy.
original_explanation: What happens to the basurahan when you forget to take it out for three days. Or your gym clothes after a workout. Or when someone spills durian inside a closed van. That smell that hits you and makes you go "Ugh, ano 'yun?! Bumaho!" It's an assault on the senses.
usage_notes: Ito ang pandiwang nasa anyong pangkasalukuyan o pangnagdaan (actor-focus) ng salitang-ugat na 'baho'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumaho** ang buong kusina dahil sa nasunog na sinaing.","translation":"The whole kitchen **stank** because of the burnt rice."},{"sentence":"Naiwan niya ang isda sa labas kaya ito **bumaho**.","translation":"He left the fish outside that's why it **became smelly**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pananakal o pagpigil sa hininga ng isang tao gamit ang kamay sa leeg; maaari ding tumukoy sa isang sitwasyon kung saan nagkakasakalan ang mga tao.
original_explanation: That feeling when the deadline is tomorrow, you have 5 more tasks, your boss is messaging you, and your internet dies. That's 'sakalan'. It's being choked, literally or figuratively. It's what happens in action movies, wrestling, and during the MRT rush hour. "Grabe ang siksikan sa tren kanina, parang nag-sakalan kami."
usage_notes: Can be a noun ('sakalan') or a verb ('sakalin' - to choke someone, 'magsakalan' - to choke each other). Refers to a state of being choked or a mutual choking event.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nauwi sa **sakalan** ang mainit nilang pagtatalo.","translation":"Their heated argument ended in a **choking match**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang makipaglaro ng **sakalan**, delikado iyan.","translation":"Don't play by putting each other in a **chokehold**, that's dangerous."}]

translation: act of meeting or fetching someone; reception
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpunta sa isang lugar upang tagpuin at samahan ang isang taong paparating.
etymology: From the root 'salubong', meaning 'to meet' or 'to go against'.
original_explanation: That feeling when you go to the airport with a giant 'Welcome Home!' banner for your balikbayan relative. It's the act of meeting someone, fetching them, or just being there when they arrive. It's the opposite of 'hatid,' which is seeing someone off. 'Salubong' is pure Filipino hospitality in noun form.
usage_notes: Often used with a verb, e.g., 'Sasalubungin kita sa airport' (I will meet you at the airport). As a noun, it refers to the act itself. The 'Salubong' is also a famous Easter pre-dawn ritual reenacting the meeting of the risen Christ and his mother.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatanggap siya ng mainit na **salubong** mula sa kanyang pamilya.","translation":"He received a warm **reception** from his family."},{"sentence":"Ang **salubong** sa airport ang isa sa mga pinaka-nakakaiyak na eksena.","translation":"The **act of meeting someone** at the airport is one of the most emotional scenes."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtama ng paa sa isang bagay na nagiging sanhi ng pagkawala ng balanse o pagkadapa.
original_explanation: That clumsy moment when your foot catches on an uneven part of the sidewalk, a random wire, or your own two feet. "Aray, tumisod ako!" It's the prequel to 'nadapa' (fell down). It can also be used figuratively, like when you 'trip up' on a question during an exam or an interview. "Tumisod siya sa tanong tungkol sa work experience niya."
usage_notes: Describes the action of hitting one's foot against an obstacle, which may or may not result in a full fall ("dapa").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa paglalakad, baka ka **tumisod** sa nakausling bato.","translation":"Be careful when you walk, you might **stumble** on the protruding rock."},{"sentence":"Habang tumatakbo, **tumisod** siya at muntik nang madapa.","translation":"While running, he **tripped** and almost fell."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa gawing gilid o panggilid na bahagi ng isang bagay, lugar, o katawan.
original_explanation: This is where you get poked in a crowded MRT ('Aray, siko mo sa tagiliran ko!'). It's the side of your body where the 'bilbil' (love handles) loves to hang out. It can also mean the side of a building, a car, or anything with a side. Basically, not the front, not the back, but the 'sam-where in between'.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa gilid o panggilid na bahagi ng isang tao, hayop, o bagay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May naramdaman siyang kirot **sa tagiliran** pagkatapos magbuhat ng mabigat.","translation":"He felt a sharp pain **on his side** after lifting something heavy."},{"sentence":"Iparada mo ang sasakyan **sa tagiliran** ng bahay.","translation":"Park the car **on the side** of the house."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pandiwang pananong na tumutukoy sa kung ano ang dapat gawin sa isang bagay o sitwasyon. Katumbas ng "anong gagawin sa".
etymology: Contraction of "ano" (what) and the verb suffix "-hin".
original_explanation: The ultimate question of 'So... what now?'. It's what you ask when you're holding a weird kitchen gadget someone gave you, or when you get a job offer you're not sure you want. It's the verbal equivalent of the 🤔 emoji. "Aanhin mo 'yan?" is the polite way of saying "Why do you have that useless thing?".
usage_notes: A very common interrogative verb. Often appears in its future tense form, "aanhin".
