usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Aanhin** mo ang pera kung hindi ka naman masaya?","translation":"**What will you do with** the money if you aren't happy?"},{"sentence":"Hindi ko alam kung **aanhin** ko itong mga lumang damit.","translation":"I don't know **what to do with** these old clothes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal para sa 'babae', na karaniwang ginagamit sa social media at text messaging.
original_explanation: Internet slang for 'babae'. Why? Because 'x' looks cool, I guess? It's the Gen Z way of typing 'girl' quickly, often seen in online communities, fanfiction, and gaming chats. It's like 'lodi' for 'idol' or 'werpa' for 'pawer'.
usage_notes: Purely slang and informal, used almost exclusively in digital communication. Pronounced either as the letters 'B-X-B' or simply read as 'babae'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May kilala ka bang **bxb** na magaling mag-code?","translation":"Do you know a **girl** who's good at coding?"},{"sentence":"Sino 'yung **bxb** na kasama ni Mark kahapon?","translation":"Who was that **girl** with Mark yesterday?"}]

meaning_filipino: Barya o perang metal na may maliit na halaga.
etymology: From Spanish 'sencillo' (simple, easy), which came to mean small change.
original_explanation: The collective sound of your financial struggles clinking in your pocket. It's what you use to pay for jeepney fare ('Bayad po!'), what you hunt for when the 'taho' vendor passes by, and what mysteriously disappears from your coin bank. Also known as 'barya'.
usage_notes: Interchangeable with 'barya'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng **sensilyo** para sa panukli.","translation":"I need **coins** for change."},{"sentence":"Puno na ng **sensilyo** ang aking alkansya.","translation":"My piggy bank is full of **coins**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagpapalago, pagpapaunlad, o paglikha ng isang bagay, ideya, o kasanayan.
original_explanation: This is the Tagalized version of 'to develop'. Parang 'yung pag-evolve ng Pokémon mo, o 'yung pag-build mo ng career mo from entry-level to manager. Ginagamit din sa photography, 'yung pag-process ng film para lumabas 'yung picture, kung naabutan mo pa 'yun. 'Magdibelop ka naman ng skills, 'wag puro ML.'
usage_notes: Often used in the context of film photography or skills development. It's a Tagalized loanword.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **magdibelop** ng bagong app para sa mga mag-aaral.","translation":"I want to **develop** a new app for students."},{"sentence":"Saan ba pwedeng magpa-**dibelop** ng film roll dito?","translation":"Where can I get a film roll **developed** here?"}]

meaning_filipino: Daglat para sa 'blood pressure'; ang presyon ng dugo na dumadaloy sa mga ugat, isang mahalagang sukatan ng kalusugan.
original_explanation: The two letters that can make any tito or tita nervous. "Ano BP mo?" is the standard greeting in a family reunion after "Tumaba ka!" It's the number that tells you if you've had too much lechon or sisig. High BP? That's your body telling you to calm down and maybe skip the chicharon for a while.
usage_notes: Used as an initialism. Pronounced as two separate letters, "B-P".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumaas na naman ang **BP** ni Tatay dahil sa stress.","translation":"Dad's **blood pressure** went up again because of stress."},{"sentence":"Dok, paki-check po ang **BP** ko.","translation":"Doc, please check my **BP**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pabrika o lugar kung saan isinasagawa ang proseso ng distilasyon, lalo na sa paggawa ng mga inuming may alkohol tulad ng lambanog o rum.
original_explanation: The magical place where sugarcane juice, coconut sap, or grains go to glow up and become your favorite gin, rum, or lambanog. It's the birthplace of 'tagay' culture and the source of many 'kwentong lasing' (drunk stories).
usage_notes: Used in the context of alcohol production.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sikat ang **destileria** sa aming probinsya dahil sa kanilang de-kalidad na lambanog.","translation":"The **distillery** in our province is famous for its high-quality coconut wine."}]

meaning_filipino: Maging sanhi ng pagtataka o pagkamangha sa isang tao.
original_explanation: This is what that quiet guy in IT does when he suddenly busts out a perfect 'birit' at the company karaoke night. He will **papagtakhin** everyone. It's the 'sana all' moment when you see someone's travel pics from a place you can't even pronounce. It's about causing a 'wow' or a 'ha?!' moment.
usage_notes: Often used with 'lahat' (everyone). Can mean to amaze, surprise, or even perplex. A more common form is 'pagtakhin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang angking galing sa pag-awit ay talagang **nakapagpapatakha** sa lahat.","translation":"Her natural talent in singing truly **amazes** everyone."},{"sentence":"Gusto niyang **papagtakhin** ang madla sa kanyang kakaibang talento.","translation":"He wants **to amaze** the crowd with his unique talent."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagbuo ng mga hakbang o pag-iisip ng mga detalye para sa isang gagawing aktibidad o proyekto.
original_explanation: Ito yung verb form ng "drawing". Yung action na ginagawa ng barkada niyo sa group chat for 3 weeks, para sa isang get-together na hindi naman matutuloy. Sa work, ito yung ginagawa sa kickoff meeting. "Okay team, let's plan our next steps."
usage_notes: Ito ang pandiwang nakapokus sa layon. Ang "magplano" ay nakapokus sa tagaganap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **planuhin** nang mabuti ang ating budget para sa buong buwan.","translation":"We need **to plan** our budget for the whole month carefully."},{"sentence":"**Planuhin** na natin ang susunod na team outing habang maaga pa.","translation":"Let's **plan** the next team outing while it's still early."}]

translation: to come true; to be realized
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasakatuparan o pagiging tunay ng isang bagay na inaasahan, pinapangarap, o hinuhulaan.
original_explanation: Yung wish mo sa 11:11 na sana mag-reply na si crush. Pag nag-chat siya, masasabi mong, 'Sana magkatotoo na ito!' It's the universe finally logging into your server and approving your request.
usage_notes: Often used for dreams, wishes, prophecies, and plans.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **magkatotoo** ang lahat ng pangarap mo.","translation":"I hope all your dreams **come true**."},{"sentence":"Nangangamba siya na baka **magkatotoo** ang masamang panaginip niya.","translation":"She is worried that her bad dream might **be realized**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang muling pagkabuhay mula sa mga patay; ang pagpapanumbalik o pagbabalik sa dating kalagayan, gamit, o kasikatan.
original_explanation: The ultimate "bounce back" story. It's what happens on Easter Sunday. In modern terms, it's when your favorite 90s band suddenly has a reunion tour, or when your dead landline phone suddenly gets a dial tone. It's the career resureksiyon of an actor who was 'laos' na. The greatest comeback of all time.
usage_notes: The spelling 'resureksyon' is a more common, simplified variant. This spelling is more formal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **Resureksiyon** ni Hesus ang sentro ng pananampalatayang Kristiyano.","translation":"The **Resurrection** of Jesus is the center of the Christian faith."},{"sentence":"Tila isang **resureksiyon** ang muling pagsikat ng kanyang karera sa pagkanta.","translation":"The resurgence of her singing career seems like a **resurrection**."}]

translation: to attempt (something on someone); to make an attempt on
meaning_filipino: Isagawa ang isang pagsubok o balak, karaniwan ay may masamang layunin, laban sa isang tao, bagay, o lugar.
original_explanation: This is the verb for when someone tries to do something, usually shady. Think of a snatcher trying to grab your phone ('pagtangkaan ang cellphone mo'), or worse, someone making a move on your life ('pagtangkaan ang buhay niya'). It's the action of a 'tangka,' an attempt, and it's rarely for a good reason.
usage_notes: This is a verb in the object-focus, locative form (`-an` suffix). It implies an attempt directed *at* or *on* something or someone. The noun form is 'pagtatangka'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binalaan ng pulisya ang publiko na huwag **pagtangkaan** ang sinumang lumabag sa batas nang mag-isa.","translation":"The police warned the public not to **make an attempt on** anyone who breaks the law by themselves."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pagtangkaan** ang kanyang pasensya.","translation":"Do not **attempt to test** his patience."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ari-arian o anumang bagay na may halaga na isinasanla o ipinapangako bilang garantiya sa isang pagkakautang.
original_explanation: Ito yung 'panagot' mo kapag uutang ka sa bangko o sa 5-6. Yung alahas ni lola, titulo ng lupa, o kahit yung OR/CR ng motor mo. Pag 'di ka nakabayad, bye-bye kolateral.
usage_notes: Primarily used in finance and lending contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang titulo ng kanilang bahay bilang **kolateral** sa pautang.","translation":"He used their house title as **collateral** for the loan."},{"sentence":"Anong pwedeng gawing **kolateral** para sa business loan?","translation":"What can be used as **collateral** for a business loan?"}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng kulay na lunti o berde; may katangian ng pagiging sariwa at masigla tulad ng kalikasan.
original_explanation: This is the slightly more common, but still classy, cousin of 'lunti'. If 'berde' is the color you tell the Grab driver, 'luntian' is the color you use to describe the perfect matcha latte for your Instagram story. It evokes nature, freshness, and all things organic.
usage_notes: Can be used as both an adjective (luntiang dahon) and a noun (ang kulay luntian). More formal than 'berde'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanilang hardin ay isang **luntiang** paraiso.","translation":"Their garden is a **green** paradise."},{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang manirahan sa isang lugar na may **luntiang** kapaligiran.","translation":"He dreams of living in a place with a **green** environment."}]

meaning_filipino: Magbenta ng mga produkto nang paisa-isa o sa maliliit na dami.
original_explanation: This is the business model of every sari-sari store in the country. Can't afford a whole bottle of shampoo? Sachet. Need just one clove of garlic? Pwede. "Magtitingi" is the art of breaking down bulk items into bite-sized, budget-friendly pieces for the community. It's the backbone of the neighborhood economy.
usage_notes: The opposite of "magbenta nang bultuhan" (to sell in bulk). The person who does this is a "tindera/o" or "nagtitinda."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya si Aling Nena na **magtitingi** ng mga de-lata sa kanyang tindahan.","translation":"Aling Nena decided to **sell canned goods in retail** at her store."},{"sentence":"Mas malaki ang kita kung **magtitingi** ka ng bigas kaysa ibenta mo nang sako-sako.","translation":"The profit is bigger if you **sell rice in retail** instead of selling it by the sack."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang kagamitan o materyales na ginagamit upang makapagsimula ng apoy, tulad ng posporo, lighter, o tuyong dahon.
original_explanation: Your go-to for starting a fire, whether it's for the kalan de uling, the ihawan for your weekend barbecue, or that scented candle for your "me time." Could be a lighter, a matchstick (posporo), or even crumpled up newspaper. Basically, the spark that gets things going.
usage_notes: A general term for any fire-starting tool.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawawala ang aking **pansindi**, hindi ako makapagluto.","translation":"My **lighter** is missing, I can't cook."},{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng tuyong papel bilang **pansindi** sa uling.","translation":"He used dry paper as **kindling** for the charcoal."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa tinapay o ibang pagkain na pinainit at pinatuyo hanggang sa maging malutong at bahagyang kulay-kape.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your pandesal when you pop it in the oven toaster for a few minutes. Perfect with butter or as a side for your pancit canton. Also, a very, *very* mild way to say someone's drunk ('lasing'). "Medyo toasted na si kuya."
usage_notes: Primarily used for bread and other food items. The slang usage for 'slightly drunk' is less common but understood in casual conversations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko ng **toasted** na tasty para sa almusal.","translation":"I want **toasted** sliced bread for breakfast."},{"sentence":"Mas masarap ang sabaw kung may kasamang **toasted** na bawang sa ibabaw.","translation":"The soup is more delicious with **toasted** garlic on top."}]

translation: to be early; to do something earlier than planned
meaning_filipino: Ang maging mas mauna sa itinakdang oras o panahon; ang paggawa ng isang bagay nang mas maaga kaysa sa inaasahan.
original_explanation: Two scenarios: 1) Yung sinabi mong 7 PM ang call time pero 6 PM pa lang anjan ka na. Congrats, na-mapaaga ka! 2) Yung due date ng project mo next week pa, pero dahil sa anxiety at kape, natapos mo na ngayon. Na-mapaaga ang pagpupuyat mo.
usage_notes: Can be used for a person arriving early or for an event happening earlier than scheduled.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Napaaga** yata ang dating mo, wala pa ang iba.","translation":"It seems you arrived **early**, the others aren't here yet."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa bagyo, **mapaaga** ang pag-uwi ng mga empleyado.","translation":"Because of the storm, the employees will get to go home **earlier**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mag-aaral o bagong gradweyt na nagtatrabaho, madalas na may mababang sahod o walang bayad, upang makakuha ng praktikal na karanasan sa isang partikular na larangan.
original_explanation: The official 'taga-timpla ng kape' who's secretly running the company's social media accounts. An intern is powered by hope, free office coffee, and the dream of one day getting a real paycheck. They're the future CEO who's currently mastering the art of the photocopy machine.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with OJT (On-the-Job Trainee). Not to be confused with 'interno' which is more specific to the medical field.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghahanap ang kumpanya namin ng mga bagong **intern**.","translation":"Our company is looking for new **interns**."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula siya bilang **intern** bago naging regular na empleyado.","translation":"She started as an **intern** before becoming a regular employee."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng pagkakaroon ng hindi pantay o may puwang na ngipin. Ang mas karaniwang gamit ngayon ay para sa bungi o may sira sa gilid ng ngipin.
original_explanation: Okay, let's be real. In modern context, *sungi* almost always means having a chipped or broken tooth, especially a front one. It's that 'oh no' moment when you bite into something hard and a piece of your tooth goes with it. While it has an older, more offensive meaning related to a cleft lip, nowadays it's more about dental mishaps.
usage_notes: The term for cleft lip is now more clinically and respectfully referred to as 'bibig na may biyak' or 'cleft lip'. 'Sungi' is now predominantly used for a chipped or broken tooth.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **sungi** ang ngipin niya matapos makagat ang isang bato sa kanin.","translation":"His tooth became **chipped** after biting a stone in the rice."},{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang ngumiti nang malaki dahil **sungi** ang isa niyang ngipin sa harap.","translation":"She doesn't want to smile widely because one of her front teeth is **chipped**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapang pangkusina na ginagamit sa paghurno, pag-ihaw, o pagpapainit ng pagkain sa loob ng isang saradong espasyo.
original_explanation: That magic box where you put in raw pandesal dough and get out heavenly bread. Or where you reheat last night's pizza. For many Filipino households, the "oven" is actually the small, countertop "oven toaster," which is the MVP of the kitchen.
usage_notes: A direct loanword. The pronunciation is anglicized.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakilagay mo nga itong manok sa **oven**.","translation":"Please put this chicken in the **oven**."},{"sentence":"Nasunog ang cake kasi nakalimutan sa loob ng **oven**.","translation":"The cake got burnt because it was forgotten inside the **oven**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kondisyon ng balat na kinatatangian ng pamamaga ng mga sebaceous gland, na nagreresulta sa mga taghiyawat, lalo na sa mukha.
etymology: From English 'acne', from New Latin, from a misreading of Greek 'akmē' (point, peak).
original_explanation: The uninvited guest that always shows up on your face right before a big date, a job interview, or any event where you need to look your best. The mortal enemy of teenagers and the reason the skincare industry is booming. The more common term is 'taghiyawat' (pimple).
usage_notes: A more clinical or formal term. 'Taghiyawat' (pimple) is far more common in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpatingin siya sa isang dermatologo para sa kanyang **akne**.","translation":"She consulted a dermatologist for her **acne**."},{"sentence":"May mga gamot na mabisa laban sa matinding **akne**.","translation":"There are effective medicines against severe **acne**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pansara, karaniwang gawa sa metal, na ginagamit upang pagkabitin ang dalawang dulo ng sinturon, strap, o laso.
original_explanation: 'Yan 'yung metal part ng belt mo na sumasabit sa lahat ng bagay. Ito rin 'yung nag-iiwan ng marka sa tiyan mo pagkatapos ng isang malupit na "unli-rice" session. The struggle is real.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin para sa mga sinturon, bag, at sapatos.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumintab ang gintong **hebilya** ng kanyang sinturon.","translation":"The golden **buckle** of his belt shone."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matalik na kaibigan, kapanalig, o kasama na pinagkakatiwalaan. Madalas itong ginagamit sa mga pormal o makalumang konteksto.
original_explanation: This sounds like something your lolo would call his drinking buddy from the old days. It's like 'tropa' or 'barkada' but with a vintage, almost noble, feel. Think of it as your OG ally, your ride-or-die before those terms even existed.
usage_notes: More common in historical or literary contexts. Not typically used in modern everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang aking **rakan** sa lahat ng laban sa buhay.","translation":"He is my **ally** in all of life's battles."},{"sentence":"Ang mga tapat na **rakan** ay mahirap hanapin.","translation":"Loyal **confidants** are hard to find."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang trabaho ay pagdugtungin ang mga piraso ng metal sa pamamagitan ng pagtunaw sa mga ito gamit ang matinding init.
original_explanation: Yung tito mong laging may suot na parang helmet sa Star Wars at naglalaro ng apoy para ayusin yung gate niyo. Sila ang dahilan kung bakit buo pa rin ang sidecar ng tricycle kahit lubak-lubak ang daan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng magaling na **soldador** para sa proyektong ito.","translation":"We need a skilled **welder** for this project."},{"sentence":"Maingay at mainit sa talyer ng mga **soldador**.","translation":"It's noisy and hot in the **welders'** workshop."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na pag-anyaya o pakiusap na dumalo o makilahok sa isang okasyon.
etymology: From `pa-` (prefix indicating request or purpose) + `unlak` (an archaic word for consent or favor).
original_explanation: This is the formal, almost 'ninuno-level' way of saying 'invitation'. Hindi ito 'yung "G na ba?" sa group chat. Ito 'yung may calligraphed card na may wax seal pa. "Isang marangal na paunlak para sa kasal nina..." Very classy.
usage_notes: Highly formal and somewhat archaic. Often seen in formal written invitations for weddings, debuts, or official functions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang karangalan na matanggap ang iyong **paunlak** sa aming munting salu-salo.","translation":"It is an honor to receive your **invitation** to our small gathering."},{"sentence":"Nakatanggap kami ng **paunlak** mula sa Malacañang para sa isang pagtitipon.","translation":"We received a formal **invitation** from Malacañang for a gathering."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kulay na sumisipsip ng lahat ng liwanag at walang ipinapakitang anumang kulay. Ito rin ay maaaring tumukoy sa isang bagay na may ganitong kulay.
original_explanation: The official color of your closet, your coffee, and your soul on a Monday morning. It's the go-to color when you want to look chic, slim, or are just too lazy to coordinate outfits. Also, the color of your friend's 'dark' humor.
usage_notes: Can be used as an adjective (e.g., 'itim na pusa' - black cat) or a noun (e.g., 'Gusto ko ng itim' - I like black).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paborito niyang kulay ay **itim**.","translation":"His favorite color is **black**."},{"sentence":"Nakasuot siya ng **itim** na bestida sa pagdiriwang.","translation":"She wore a **black** dress to the celebration."}]

translation: to scrape clean, to use up completely
meaning_filipino: Kunin o ubusin ang lahat hanggang sa wala nang matira, karaniwan sa pamamagitan ng pagkayod o pag-ipon ng mga huling piraso.
original_explanation: That move you make with the spoon to get the very last bit of condensed milk from the can. It's scraping the 'tutong' from the rice cooker because that's the best part. On a sadder note, it's what happens to your sahod by the 14th and 29th of the month—na-simot na, ubos na. Leaving no crumbs, literally and financially.
usage_notes: Implies thoroughness in taking or consuming everything, leaving nothing behind.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sinimot** ng bata ang huling butil ng kanin sa kanyang plato.","translation":"The child **scraped clean** the last grain of rice on his plate."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **simutin** ang ulam, magtira ka para sa iba!","translation":"Don't **use up all** the food, leave some for the others!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahinang liwanag o bahagyang sinag, lalo na kung nakikita mula sa malayo o sa dilim.
original_explanation: That little bit of hope (or light) you see at the end of a very long, dark tunnel—like the 'available' light on the Grab app after 30 minutes of searching. It's the faint glow of your phone screen under the blanket at 2 AM, or the first glimmer of sunrise after an all-nighter.
usage_notes: Often used metaphorically to mean a glimmer of hope.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa gitna ng kadiliman, may nakita siyang **anag-ag** ng kandila.","translation":"In the middle of the darkness, he saw the **glimmer** of a candle."},{"sentence":"Ang tagumpay na ito ay isang **anag-ag** ng pag-asa para sa lahat.","translation":"This victory is a **gleam** of hope for everyone."}]

meaning_filipino: Naguguluhan ang isip at kilos dahil sa pagmamadali, takot, o pagkagulat. Nawawala sa sarili.
original_explanation: You, when your boss messages "Can we talk?" with no context. Or when you realize your wallet isn't in your bag five minutes after leaving the restaurant. It's that headless chicken mode where you're flustered, confused, and making frantic but unproductive movements. "Kalma lang, 'wag kang mataranta!" is easier said than done.
usage_notes: Present tense of 'mataranta'. Describes a state of panic or confusion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mataranta**; hahanapin natin ang nawawala mong telepono.","translation":"Don't **panic**; we will look for your missing phone."},{"sentence":"**Natataranta** na ang lahat dahil malapit na ang deadline.","translation":"Everyone **is panicking** because the deadline is near."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng pagmamahal, pag-aaruga, o lambing sa kilos, salita, o gawa.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `ma-` (nagpapakita ng katangian) + salitang ugat na `suyo` (panunuyo o paglalambing).
original_explanation: This is your "sana all" energy. Yung pag-aalaga na parang sa K-drama, yung tipong pupunasan yung dumi sa gilid ng labi mo, o kaya aayusin yung buhok mo. It's the opposite of "ghosting." This is peak "alaga" and "lambing" vibes.
usage_notes: Madalas na naglalarawan sa kilos o ugali ng isang tao, lalo na sa konteksto ng pag-ibig o pamilya. Ang "masuyong halik" ay isang karaniwang parirala.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **masuyo** na yakap ang kailangan ko ngayon.","translation":"An **affectionate** hug is what I need right now."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa pagiging **masuyo** sa kanyang mga apo.","translation":"She is known for being **caring** towards her grandchildren."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong may labis na pagnanasa sa yaman o kapangyarihan; sakim.
original_explanation: This is the person who takes the last piece of lechon, the biggest slice of cake, and still eyes your plate. In the corporate world, it's the boss who wants all the credit. In politics... well, you know. It's the 'mine, mine, mine!' attitude, but for adults. The ultimate opposite of 'sharing is caring.'
usage_notes: Isang mabigat na negatibong paglalarawan sa karakter ng isang tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **gahaman** na mangangalakal ay hindi nagbabayad ng tamang buwis.","translation":"The **greedy** merchant does not pay the correct taxes."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **gahaman** sa pagkain; magtira ka para sa iba.","translation":"Don't be **greedy** with the food; leave some for the others."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na taksil, hindi tapat, o mapagkanulo sa tiwala ng iba.
original_explanation: Not the Disney character with Stitch. This is that 'friend' who spills your secrets, the politician who breaks their campaign promises, or your teammate in Mobile Legends who feeds the enemy. It's the ultimate 'Sana all' but in reverse: 'Sana all loyal', because this person is the exact opposite. Ahas in the grass, basically.
usage_notes: A formal and literary word, often found in older texts and songs. 'Taksil' is the more common modern equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **lilo** niyang kaibigan ang naglaglag sa kanya sa mga pulis.","translation":"His **traitorous** friend was the one who snitched on him to the police."},{"sentence":"Pinarusahan ang mga **lilo** sa kaharian.","translation":"The **treacherous** ones in the kingdom were punished."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay, kaganapan, o konsepto na sumasaklaw sa buong daigdig o may pandaigdigang sakop at kalidad.
original_explanation: "World-class" ang peg. Hindi lang pang-barangay, hindi lang pang-Pinas, kundi pang-buong planeta. Parang ganda ni Catriona Gray o ang boses ni Lea Salonga. It's something that can compete or be recognized on a global stage.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang mga kaganapan (hal. Pangmundong Palaro), pamantayan, o katangian na may pandaigdigang antas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang talento sa pagkanta ay tunay na **pangmundo**.","translation":"Her singing talent is truly **world-class**."},{"sentence":"Sumali siya sa isang **pangmundo**ng kumpetisyon sa sining.","translation":"She joined a **global** art competition."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malawak na lugar na sagana sa mga puno; gubat.
etymology: From kahoy + -an, a locative suffix indicating a place abundant in something.
original_explanation: Hindi lang 'yung sa Baguio o Tagaytay. Ito rin 'yung lugar kung saan ka "nawawala" kapag tinatanong ka kung nasaan ka na. "Papunta na, malapit na sa **kahuyan** (pero kakagising lang)." Also, where Filipino horror movie characters make bad decisions.
usage_notes: Interchangeable with 'gubat' but 'kahuyan' can sometimes imply a smaller, less dense area of trees (woods/grove) compared to a large, dense 'gubat' (forest/jungle).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglakad-lakad sila sa may **kahuyan** upang magpahangin.","translation":"They walked through the **woods** to get some fresh air."},{"sentence":"Ang malawak na **kahuyan** ay nagsisilbing tahanan ng maraming hayop.","translation":"The vast **forest** serves as a home for many animals."}]

translation: to measure by fathom; to stretch out one's arms
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsukat sa haba o lalim gamit ang dipa, o ang pag-unat ng dalawang braso nang magkabilaan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang "dipa" (isang tradisyonal na yunit ng sukat na katumbas ng haba sa pagitan ng dulo ng mga daliri ng dalawang kamay kapag nakaunat).
original_explanation: This is the OG "social distancing" measurement. Before we had meter sticks, we had "isang dipa." It's when you stretch your arms out wide like you're about to give the world a big hug, but you're actually measuring something, like the size of a fish or how far you need to stay away from your chismosang kapitbahay.
usage_notes: Ang salitang-ugat na "dipa" ay isang tradisyonal na yunit ng panukat. Ang anyong pandiwa nito ay hindi na gaanong karaniwan sa modernong pananalita ngunit naiintindihan pa rin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dipahin** mo nga kung gaano kalapad ang bintana.","translation":"Can you **measure with your arms** how wide the window is?"},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **dipahin** ang lalim ng ilog bago tumawid.","translation":"He tried to **fathom** the depth of the river before crossing."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na ekspresyon na may halong pang-aasar o pagdududa, na ginagamit bilang tugon sa isang pahayag na tila engrande, hindi kapani-paniwala, o masyadong pormal.
etymology: From English 'statement' and a stylized, gay lingo pronunciation of 'iyan' (that).
original_explanation: Gay lingo response to something that sounds too serious, dramatic, or like a prepared speech. The 'yarn' (a stylized 'iyan?') adds a playful, dismissive, or questioning tone. Friend: 'I've decided to disconnect from worldly attachments and find my inner peace.' You: 'Statement yarn?'
usage_notes: Used to playfully question or mock a declaration. It implies 'Oh really? Is that your official statement?'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Friend 1: 'Hindi na ako iinom ng alak simula ngayon.' Friend 2: '**Statement yarn?** Tingnan natin sa Biyernes.'","translation":"Friend 1: 'I won't drink alcohol starting today.' Friend 2: '**Is that a statement?** Let's see on Friday.'"},{"sentence":"Nag-post siya ng 'I deserve to be happy.' Sabi ko sa isip ko, '**statement yarn?**'","translation":"She posted 'I deserve to be happy.' I thought to myself, '**what a statement, huh?**'"}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa estado ng pagtulog; hindi gising.
original_explanation: When your friend is unresponsive in the group chat at 2 AM, they're probably tulog. When the security guard is sitting but his head is nodding forward, he's definitely tulog. It's the status you wish you were in during a long, boring meeting.
usage_notes: Describes a person or animal that is currently sleeping. It is distinct from the verb 'matulog' (to sleep).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maingay, **tulog** na ang bata.","translation":"Don't be noisy, the child is already **asleep**."},{"sentence":"Naabutan ko siyang **tulog** sa sofa.","translation":"I found him **asleep** on the sofa."}]

translation: to become murky, to become turbid
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging malabo o marumi ng isang likido dahil sa pagkahalo ng mga latak o maliliit na piraso ng dumi.
etymology: From the root 'labusaw' (turbidity) with the infix '-um-'.
original_explanation: Imagine you're at the beach and someone runs past you, kicking up all the sand in the water. The water just lumabusaw. It's like `lumabo` but specifically for liquids that get stirred up with sediment. It's the state of your 'sinigang' broth right after you mash the gabi. It’s a more specific, almost poetic, way to say water got dirty.
usage_notes: A less common synonym for 'lumabo' when referring to liquids becoming turbid due to suspended particles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa malakas na ulan, **lumabusaw** ang dating malinaw na tubig sa sapa.","translation":"Because of the heavy rain, the once clear water in the stream **became murky**."},{"sentence":"Nang haluin niya ang putik, **lumabusaw** ang tubig sa timba.","translation":"When he stirred the mud, the water in the bucket **became turbid**."}]

meaning_filipino: Gamitin bilang kagamitan sa pagpapakintab o paglilinis ng isang bagay.
etymology: From Tagalog 'ipang-' (instrumental prefix, becomes 'ipam-' before 'b') + 'buli' (to polish).
original_explanation: This is the verb for making things shiny. It's what you do with the floor wax, the Brasso for your military belt buckle, or the banana peel on the wooden floor (old school!). The sentence subject is the thing you use for polishing. 'Anong magandang ipambuli sa sahig?' (What's good to use for polishing the floor?).
usage_notes: This is an instrumental verb. The focus is on the instrument or tool used for the action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lumang dyaryo ay mabisang **ipambuli** ng salamin.","translation":"Old newspaper is effective **to use for polishing** glass."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang isang malambot na tela na **ipambuli** sa kanyang sapatos na katad.","translation":"He used a soft cloth **to polish** his leather shoes."}]

translation: to name someone; to mention by name
meaning_filipino: Tukuyin o banggitin ang tiyak na pangalan ng isang tao, lalo na sa isang listahan o sa pag-akusa.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'spill the tea' verb. When your friend says 'may chika ako' and you reply 'Sino? Dali!', you're asking them to *mangalanan*. It's the act of dropping names, whether for credit on a group project or pointing out who didn't wash the dishes.
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of identification, accusation, or giving credit. The more common form is 'pangalanan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya magawang **mangalanan** kung sino ang kumuha ng kanyang pitaka.","translation":"She couldn't **name** who took her wallet."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi kita **mangangalanan** sa report ko.","translation":"Don't worry, I won't **mention you by name** in my report."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng kaalaman o kamalayan tungkol sa isang bagay; alam.
original_explanation: This is the more formal, almost poetic way of saying 'alam.' It's not just 'I know,' it's 'It is known to me.' Sounds like something a news anchor or a character in a historical teleserye would say. If 'alam' is a text message, 'batid' is a calligraphed letter. 'Batid ko ang iyong mga sekreto,' sounds way more dramatic than 'Alam ko.'
usage_notes: Often used in formal writing, literature, and news reporting. Interchangeable with 'alam' but carries a more formal and profound tone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Batid** ng lahat ang kanyang kabutihan.","translation":"His kindness is **known** to everyone."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko **batid** na darating ka pala.","translation":"I was not **aware** that you were coming."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang halaga ng pera na kinakailangang ilabas o bayaran para sa isang bagay; mga gugulin.
etymology: Mula sa salitang 'gastos' na hango sa Espanyol na 'gastos'.
original_explanation: Your 'sahod' minus everything else. This is the list of things draining your wallet: Meralco, Maynilad, rent, GrabFood, Shopee 'add to cart' moments, and your monthly 'ambag' for the office birthday party. It's the reason why 'petsa de peligro' is a real thing.
usage_notes: Ito ang anyong pangngalan na tumutukoy sa mga bagay na pinagkakagastusan. Iba ito sa pandiwang 'gastusin' (to spend).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating bawasan ang ating mga buwanang **gastusin**.","translation":"We need to reduce our monthly **expenses**."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang **gastusin** sa pagpapaaral ng mga anak.","translation":"The **expenses** for children's education are high."}]

translation: to hit; to strike; to throw (at)
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapatama, paghampas, o pagbato ng isang bagay. Ginagamit din sa pag-atake, pisikal man o berbal.
original_explanation: This is the action. Pwedeng sa sports, like "Tira na!" sa billiards. Pwede ring verbal, "Binanatan niya ng isang malupit na tira." Or, in a more 'kanto' way, it's the act of hitting something or someone. The root for "tirahin" and "tirador".
usage_notes: Salitang-ugat para sa 'tirahin'. Maaaring gamitin para sa pisikal o berbal na pag-atake.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malakas na **tira** ng bola ang nagpanalo sa kanila.","translation":"A strong **hit** of the ball made them win."},{"sentence":"Sige na, **tira** na! Ikaw na ang susunod sa bilyaran.","translation":"Go on, **hit** it! You're next at the billiard table."}]

translation: to make pale; to lighten a color
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabawas ng sidhi o tingkad ng isang kulay upang ito ay maging mas maputla o mapusyaw.
original_explanation: This is what you do in Photoshop when the color is too loud. 'Bes, masyadong matapang yung red, magpapusyaw ka ng konti.' It's the opposite of saturation. It can also describe someone's face when they see their credit card bill after the 12.12 sale.
usage_notes: Primarily used in contexts of color, art, design, and sometimes to describe a pale complexion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinabihan niya ang pintor na **magpapusyaw** ng kulay asul sa pader.","translation":"She told the painter to **lighten** the blue color on the wall."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong labhan nang matagal 'yan, baka **magpapusyaw** ang kulay ng damit.","translation":"Don't wash that for too long, the color of the clothes might **become pale**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang impormal at kolokyal na tawag sa isang matalik na kaibigan o ginagamit na pantawag sa sinuman.
etymology: Pinaikling anyo ng salitang Ingles na "best friend".
original_explanation: Short for 'best friend'. Pero sa Pinas, tinatawag mo nang **bes** kahit 'yung katabi mo lang sa jeep o 'yung tindera sa suking karinderya. "Bes, pakiabot ng bayad." It's the universal term of endearment for anyone you need a small favor from.
usage_notes: Ginagamit bilang pantawag sa kausap, kahit hindi ito matalik na kaibigan. Kadalasang ginagamit sa mga kabataan at sa social media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bes**, kumusta ka na? Tagal nating hindi nagkita!","translation":"**Bes**, how are you? It's been a while since we last saw each other!"},{"sentence":"Excuse me, **bes**, anong oras na?","translation":"Excuse me, **friend**, what time is it?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kamiseta na may kuwelyo, isang placket na karaniwang may dalawa o tatlong butones, at opsyonal na bulsa.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na 'polo shirt'. Isang direktang paghiram batay sa ponetika.
original_explanation: The official uniform of dads, call center agents on a Friday, and anyone who wants to look 'smart casual' without trying too hard. It's the middle ground between a t-shirt and a long-sleeved button-down. Perfect for when you're not sure if the event is chill or formal.
usage_notes: Madalas na pinaikli bilang 'polo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong magsuot ng **polosirt** para sa company outing.","translation":"You need to wear a **polo shirt** for the company outing."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malaking isda sa dagat na karaniwang ginagawang de-lata o kinakain bilang sashimi o steak.
original_explanation: The MVP of the pantry. Whether it's in a can (hot & spicy or in oil?), in your sushi, or grilled as a steak, `tuna` is a Filipino staple. It's the go-to `ulam` for busy people, the star of tuna-pandesal, and the reason why General Santos City is the "Tuna Capital of the Philippines."
usage_notes: Refers to the fish. A different, much rarer, 'tuna' (from Spanish) refers to the prickly pear cactus fruit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong palaman sa tinapay ang de-latang **tuna**.","translation":"Canned **tuna** is my favorite bread filling."},{"sentence":"Sariwa ang mga **tuna** na huli sa General Santos.","translation":"The **tuna** caught in General Santos are fresh."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang halaw, kopya, o bahagi ng isang orihinal na kasulatan, aklat, o anumang akda.
original_explanation: Before screenshots, there was 'sipi'. It's a copy of something, like the 'sipi' of your birth certificate you can never find when you need it, or the 'sipi' of a chismis that gets forwarded in a group chat. Also, that inspirational quote you 'sipi' from the internet for your IG caption.
usage_notes: Can refer to a full copy or just a part (excerpt/quote).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng isang **sipi** ng iyong resume.","translation":"I need a **copy** of your resume."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang isang **sipi** mula sa Noli Me Tángere para sa kanyang talumpati.","translation":"He used a **quotation** from Noli Me Tángere for his speech."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang obispo na may mataas na ranggo na namumuno sa isang mahalagang diyosesis o arkidiyosesis.
original_explanation: The big boss bishop. In the Catholic Church hierarchy, if a regular bishop is a branch manager, the archbishop is the regional director. They've got a bigger hat (mitre) and a bigger area of responsibility.
usage_notes: The feminine form is "arsobispa," though it is not used in the context of the Catholic Church.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **arsobispo** ng Maynila ay nagbigay ng mensahe para sa mga mananampalataya.","translation":"The **archbishop** of Manila gave a message for the faithful."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katawagan para sa isang aso na nasa kasariang pambabae.
original_explanation: The literal, no-malice translation for a female dog. Before the English word 'bitch' got its other, more colorful meanings, this was its simple, biological definition. In Tagalog, 'asong babae' is purely descriptive and doesn't carry the negative connotation it does in English. It's just a girl doggo, the future nanay of cute tuta (puppies).
usage_notes: This is a neutral, descriptive term. It is not used as an insult in the same way its English equivalent is.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nanganak na ang aming **asong babae**; lima ang tuta niya.","translation":"Our **female dog** has given birth; she has five puppies."},{"sentence":"Paano malalaman kung ang isang tuta ay **asong babae** o lalaki?","translation":"How do you tell if a puppy is a **female dog** or a male one?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagsakay o pagiging lulan ng isang sasakyan.
etymology: From sum- (actor-focus infix) + sakay (ride), with reduplication of the first syllable (sa-) to indicate progressive aspect.
original_explanation: The daily struggle of every commuter in EDSA. Whether you're sumasakay sa jeep, bus, or MRT, it's an extreme sport. Also used for "going along with" a trip or a joke. "Sumasakay ka na lang sa trip ng barkada mo."
usage_notes: This is the progressive or present tense, indicating the ongoing action of riding or boarding a vehicle.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming tao ang **sumasakay** sa MRT tuwing umaga.","translation":"Many people are **riding** the MRT every morning."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang basta-basta **sumasakay** sa sasakyan ng hindi mo kakilala.","translation":"Don't just **get into** the vehicle of someone you don't know."}]

translation: is being appointed; is being designated
meaning_filipino: Itinatalaga o inilalagay sa isang partikular na posisyon, tungkulin, o lugar.
original_explanation: This is when your team leader says, "Okay, ikaw ang OIC (Officer-in-Charge) habang naka-leave ako." You are being assigned a specific role or task. It's formal. You don't just 'fall into' a role; you are officially placed there. It’s what happens when someone becomes a department head, a project manager, or the designated taga-bili ng kape.
usage_notes: Present progressive tense of 'matalaga'. Often used in formal or official contexts like government and corporate settings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay **natatalaga** bilang bagong kalihim ng kagawaran.","translation":"He **is being appointed** as the new secretary of the department."},{"sentence":"Isang malaking responsibilidad ang nakaatang sa sinumang **natatalaga** sa posisyong iyan.","translation":"A great responsibility rests on anyone who **is designated** to that position."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sisidlan na hugis-kono, karaniwang yari sa papel, dahon, o anumang malambot na materyal na binaluktot upang maglaman ng maliliit na bagay.
original_explanation: That paper cone your friendly neighborhood street vendor uses to hold your P20 worth of mani or kasoy. It's the original, biodegradable Filipino take-out container before eco-bags were cool. Also what you make when you're bored in class with a piece of paper.
usage_notes: Commonly associated with street food. Often made from materials like old newspaper or banana leaves.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng isang **balisungsong** ng nilagang mani sa labas ng simbahan.","translation":"I bought a **cone** of boiled peanuts outside the church."}]

translation: crossroads; site of a cross; junction
meaning_filipino: Isang lugar, karaniwang isang sangandaan o panulukan ng daan, kung saan may nakatayong krus bilang pananda, alaala sa isang trahedya, o bilang gabay sa mga manlalakbay.
original_explanation: The original 'X marks the spot.' Before Waze and Google Maps, this was your landmark for giving directions: 'lumagpas ka lang sa pinagkurusan, tapos kanan.' Also, a place where you might hear ghost stories about white ladies, or where people leave offerings. It's a landmark with a hint of folklore and a dash of spookiness.
usage_notes: 'Pinagkrusan' is a common spelling variant. The term can mean a literal intersection with a cross or a metaphorical crossroads in life.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkita tayo sa may **pinagkurusan** sa tapat ng lumang simbahan.","translation":"Let's meet at the **crossroads** in front of the old church."},{"sentence":"May alay na mga bulaklak sa **pinagkurusan** kung saan nangyari ang aksidente.","translation":"There are flower offerings at the **site of the cross** where the accident happened."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamataas na ranggo ng opisyal sa hukbong-dagat.
original_explanation: The boss of the seas. The 'General' of the Navy. Kung sa BPO pa, sila 'yung site director ng buong fleet. You'll mostly encounter this word in history books about naval battles or in movies with epic ship fights.
usage_notes: A formal military rank.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinamunuan ni **Almirante** Dewey ang hukbong-dagat ng Amerika sa Labanan sa Look ng Maynila.","translation":"**Admiral** Dewey led the American navy in the Battle of Manila Bay."},{"sentence":"Isang malaking karangalan ang maging **almirante** ng Philippine Navy.","translation":"It is a great honor to become an **admiral** in the Philippine Navy."}]

translation: A friendly term of address for a female friend, short for 'mare'.
meaning_filipino: Isang impormal na katawagan para sa isang babaeng kaibigan, pinaikling anyo ng 'kumare' (comadre).
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'comadre' na naging 'kumare', na pinaikli bilang 'mare' at naging kolokyal na 'mars'.
original_explanation: The ultimate Tita-level term of endearment. Before 'beshie' or 'sis,' there was 'mars.' It's what your mom calls her best friend when they're about to spill the tea (chismis) over coffee. It's the 'girl, let me tell you' of the previous generation, but now it's a chic, retro way to call your friends.
usage_notes: Primarily used between women as a term of address, but can be used humorously by anyone. It implies a close, sister-like friendship.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Mars**, kumusta na ang bagong trabaho mo?","translation":"**Mars**, how's your new job?"},{"sentence":"Tara, kape tayo, **mars**! Dami kong chika.","translation":"Let's go for coffee, **mars**! I have so much gossip."}]

meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng sapak o isang malakas na sampal/suntok ang isang tao.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "sapak" na may hulaping "-in".
original_explanation: The verb form of `sapak`. This is what you do when you deliver that hard slap. It's a very common threat, especially among siblings or exasperated parents. "Huwag kang maingay, baka sapakin kita!" is the Filipino equivalent of "Be quiet, or I'll smack you!"
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **sapakin** ang sinumang kumain ng lunch ko sa ref.","translation":"I want **to punch** whoever ate my lunch from the fridge."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi na gumagana, wasak, o may depekto.
original_explanation: The default status of public infrastructure, your phone after it falls, your diet after seeing a lechon, and your heart after a breakup. 'Sira na naman ang LRT.' 'Sira na ang phone ko.' 'Sira na ang diet ko.' 'Sira na ang buhay ko.' It's a very versatile word for anything that's not working as it should.
usage_notes: Can be used for physical objects, abstract concepts (like plans or diets), and even people (though that's more colloquial/rude).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sira** ang zipper ng bag ko kaya hindi ko maisara.","translation":"The zipper on my bag is **broken** so I can't close it."},{"sentence":"Paumanhin, **sira** po ang aming credit card machine sa ngayon.","translation":"Sorry, our credit card machine is **out of order** right now."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malawak na lupain, karaniwang nasa labas ng lungsod, na ginagamit sa agrikultura o pag-aalaga ng hayop. Tumutukoy rin sa pangkalahatang pook-rural.
original_explanation: The opposite of the concrete jungle. It's where the air is (supposedly) fresher, the traffic is caused by cows crossing the road, and your phone signal goes to die. For city dwellers, "pumunta sa bukid" is the dream weekend escape. For people living there, it's just... home.
usage_notes: Can refer to a specific farm or the countryside in general.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lumaki siya sa **bukid** kaya sanay sa simpleng buhay.","translation":"He grew up in the **countryside**, so he's used to a simple life."},{"sentence":"Mayroon silang malawak na **bukid** ng mangga sa probinsya.","translation":"They have a wide mango **farm** in the province."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking may ugaling pagiging hambog; taong mayabang at mapagmalaki.
etymology: From Tagalog 'hambog' + Spanish suffix '-ero' indicating a person who does something.
original_explanation: The personification of 'hambog.' This is the guy who cuts you in line, revs his engine too loudly, and talks about his salary on the first date. He's the main character in his own movie, and everyone else is just an extra. The female version is 'hambugera'.
usage_notes: The '-o' ending typically denotes masculine, while '-a' (hambugera) denotes feminine.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa kanilang lugar bilang isang **hambugero** na laging naghahanap ng away.","translation":"He is known in their area as an **arrogant person** who is always looking for a fight."},{"sentence":"Umalis na lang kami dahil sobrang ingay ng **hambugero** sa kabilang mesa.","translation":"We just left because the **arrogant guy** at the next table was so noisy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na gumagamit ng panlilinlang o pandaraya upang makalamang sa iba.
original_explanation: That person in a game of Uno who keeps drawing cards but "forgets" to say "Uno!". Or someone who promises "I'll change" but never does. A magdaraya is a master of deception, whether in card games, exams, or relationships. Ingat!
usage_notes: Refers to a person who deceives. The verb 'to cheat' is 'mandaya', and its future tense is also 'mandaraya'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw kong makipaglaro sa iyo dahil isa kang **magdaraya**.","translation":"I don't want to play with you because you are a **cheater**."},{"sentence":"Nahuli ang **magdaraya** sa kanyang mga kasinungalingan.","translation":"The **deceiver** was caught in his lies."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng isang tao, karaniwang lalaki, na nahihiyang ipahayag ang kanyang damdaming pag-ibig sa taong kanyang nagugustuhan.
original_explanation: You know that guy who's been crushing on someone for years but can't even say 'hi'? That's him. He's got all the feelings but none of the guts. The classic 'torpe' is a staple of Filipino rom-coms, needing a makeover montage and a pushy best friend to finally confess. He's all 'sana all' but no 'sana ako'.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used to describe men who are too shy to court or confess their feelings to a woman. It's a key concept in Filipino courtship culture.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakatorpe ni David, hindi niya masabi kay Anna na gusto niya ito.","translation":"David is so **shy**, he can't tell Anna that he likes her."},{"sentence":"Kung hindi ka naging **matorpe**, baka kayo na sana ngayon.","translation":"If you hadn't been so **romantically shy**, maybe you two would be together now."}]

translation: to gush forth, to flow profusely
meaning_filipino: Malakas at tuloy-tuloy na pag-agos o paglabas ng likido, tulad ng tubig o dugo, mula sa isang siwang o butas.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'bulubod' at gitlaping '-um-'.
original_explanation: Imagine nasugatan ka tapos ‘yung dugo, parang gripo na hindi maisara. O ‘yung baha na biglang pumasok sa bahay niyo galing sa ilalim ng pinto. It's a strong, continuous flow, and usually, it's not a good thing.
usage_notes: Kadalasang naglalarawan ng malakas at hindi makontrol na pag-agos ng likido. Mas matindi kaysa sa 'umagos'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumulubod** ang dugo mula sa malalim na sugat sa kanyang braso.","translation":"Blood **gushed forth** from the deep wound on his arm."},{"sentence":"Nang masira ang tubo, **bumulubod** ang tubig sa kalsada.","translation":"When the pipe broke, water **flowed profusely** onto the street."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang baryant na pagbaybay para sa 'kapiterya'.
original_explanation: The slightly more 'Español' way to spell 'kapiterya'. It's the same place, just with a different spelling that might get you a red mark from your Filipino teacher. Most people use 'kapiterya' now.
usage_notes: This is a variant spelling of 'kapiterya', which is the more standard and common form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lumang karatula ay nagsasabing '**kapiteria**'.","translation":"The old sign says '**cafeteria**'."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bansa o teritoryo na nasa ilalim ng kontrol at pamamahala ng ibang mas makapangyarihang bansa.
original_explanation: The ultimate historical hugot. 'Yung feeling na 333 years kang nasa 'under de saya' ng Spain. Ang Pilipinas ay dating kolonya, kaya apektado pa rin ang kultura, apelyido, at pagkain natin hanggang ngayon.
usage_notes: Refers to a political or territorial colony.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **kolonya** ng Espanya ang Pilipinas sa loob ng mahigit tatlong daang taon.","translation":"The Philippines became a **colony** of Spain for more than three hundred years."},{"sentence":"Maraming bansa sa Africa ang dating **kolonya** ng mga Europeo.","translation":"Many countries in Africa were former **colonies** of Europeans."}]

translation: to step on; to tread on
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng paa sa isang bagay o lugar; ang pagyapak.
original_explanation: The OG way of saying you stepped on something. Like when you accidentally tumapak on your friend's brand new white sneakers. It's the physical version of 'seen-zoning' someone's heart. Ingat sa pagtapak, baka may maapakan kang feelings.
usage_notes: Often used literally, but can be used figuratively to mean entering a new phase or place (e.g., 'tumapak sa bagong yugto' - to step into a new chapter).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka, baka **tumapak** ka sa basang sahig.","translation":"Be careful, you might **step on** the wet floor."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **tumapak** sa damuhan.","translation":"Don't **tread on** the grass."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maingat at palihim na pagmamasid o pag-espiya sa isang tao, bagay, o lugar.
etymology: Possibly from Spanish 'atisbar' (to watch, to spy on), adapted into Tagalog.
original_explanation: The act of being a low-key 'Marites'. It's watching something or someone with intense focus, like how you stalk your ex's new partner on social media, or how you watch the Grab delivery guy's icon move on the map. It’s observation with a purpose.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of spying, detective work, or simply keen observation. The verb form is 'magmatyag' or 'matyagan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pulis ay naglagay ng **matyag** sa bahay ng suspek.","translation":"The police placed the suspect's house under **surveillance**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng masusing **matyag** upang malaman ang kanilang mga galaw.","translation":"Close **observation** is needed to know their movements."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na kahon o sisidlan, karaniwang gawa sa kahoy o metal, na ginagamit sa pagtatago ng maliliit at mahahalagang bagay tulad ng alahas.
original_explanation: This is a deep cut. Think of it as the lola's baul, but for your tiny treasures. It's the old-school version of a jewelry box. You'd probably find this word in a Florante at Laura-era text, not in a conversation about Shopee deliveries. It's like the vintage, more ✨classy✨ cousin of 'kahon'.
usage_notes: This word is very rare in modern conversation and is considered archaic or literary.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinago ng lola ang kanyang mga alahas sa isang antigong **kahita**.","translation":"Grandmother kept her jewelry in an antique **jewelry box**."},{"sentence":"Isang lumang **kahita** na puno ng mga liham ang natagpuan sa ilalim ng kama.","translation":"An old **small box** full of letters was found under the bed."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa panloob na kasuotan na direktang isinusuot sa katawan, tulad ng kamiseta o salawal. Maaari din itong mangahulugang unang patong o suson ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: Literally the 'first layer'. This is your underwear, your sando, your undershirt. It's the foundation of your OOTD. Before the branded shirt, before the jacket, there is the unang sapin. It's the unsung hero that absorbs your pawis on a hot day.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin nang literal para sa damit o sa matalinhagang paraan para sa isang pundasyong patong.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging magdala ng extrang **unang sapin** kapag mainit ang panahon.","translation":"Always bring extra **underwear** when the weather is hot."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-ibig sa bayan ang **unang sapin** ng pagiging isang tunay na mamamayan.","translation":"Love for the country is the **first layer** of being a true citizen."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kulisap (Gryllotalpidae) na naninirahan sa ilalim ng lupa, karaniwang may malalaking pang-unang paa na ginagamit sa paghuhukay.
original_explanation: That weird-looking bug you sometimes see after the rain that looks like a cross between a cricket and a tiny lobster. Kids in the province sometimes play with them. For city dwellers, it's the stuff of nightmares you see on a 'What is this bug?' Facebook group.
usage_notes: Not a common word in urban areas unless discussing insects specifically. Also known as 'suhong' or 'ararawan' in other dialects.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May nahuling **tatuwa** ang pusa sa hardin.","translation":"The cat caught a **mole cricket** in the garden."},{"sentence":"Ang mga **tatuwa** ay peste sa mga pananim na ugat.","translation":"**Mole crickets** are pests to root crops."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng paggala-gala o paglalakwatsa nang walang tiyak na patutunguhan o layunin.
original_explanation: Yung ginagawa mo pagkatapos ng shift o klase na ayaw mo pang umuwi. You're not going anywhere specific, just... out. Ito ang national sport ng mga 'tambay' at ng 'gala' mong kaibigan. The opposite of having a productive day.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa mga anyong pandiwa tulad ng 'lumaboy' (to wander) o bilang pang-uri/pangngalan na 'palaboy' (a wanderer, vagrant).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang hilig mo sa **laboy**, umuwi ka na at gabi na.","translation":"You love **loitering** so much; go home now, it's already late."},{"sentence":"Itigil mo na ang pagla**laboy** at maghanap ka ng trabaho.","translation":"Stop your **wandering** and look for a job."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging walang anumang gawain, trabaho, o pinagkakaabalahan.
etymology: Mula sa `kawalan` (lack) at `ginagawa` (doing), na mula sa ugat na `gawa` (work, act).
original_explanation: That glorious state of "nakatunganga." It's the Sunday afternoon vibe when you've finished all your chores, watched everything on Netflix, and are now just staring at a butiki on the ceiling. It can be relaxing (tambay mode) or stressful (unemployed ka 'teh?). The official term for doing nothing.
usage_notes: Maaaring maging positibo (pagpapahinga) o negatibo (katamaran, kawalan ng trabaho).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang matagal na **kawalang-ginagawa** ay maaaring humantong sa depresyon.","translation":"Prolonged **idleness** can lead to depression."},{"sentence":"Nababagot na ako sa **kawalang-ginagawa** dito sa bahay.","translation":"I'm getting bored with the **inactivity** here at home."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagkain na inihahanda at kinakain sa umaga bilang unang salo-salo sa buong araw.
etymology: From `pang-` (for the purpose of) + `almusal` (breakfast). `Almusal` itself is from Spanish `almorzar` (to have lunch), which shifted meaning in Filipino.
original_explanation: The most important meal of the day, featuring the holy trinity: SInangag (garlic fried rice), itlog (egg), and your choice of 'silog' partner (tapa, tocino, longganisa). It's the fuel for your morning commute, your 9 AM meeting, and your first "sana Biyernes na" thought of the day.
usage_notes: While `almusal` is the meal or act of eating, `pang-almusal` specifically refers to the food intended for breakfast. It can also be used as an adjective.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng pandesal at keso na **pang-almusal**.","translation":"Mom bought pandesal and cheese for **breakfast**."},{"sentence":"Ang paborito kong **pang-almusal** ay tapsilog.","translation":"My favorite **breakfast food** is tapsilog."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagsapi, pagsama, o pagiging bahagi ng isang grupo, organisasyon, o samahan.
original_explanation: This is when you finally click 'Join Group' on Facebook, or sign up for that gym membership you'll only use once. It's the official act of becoming part of a barkada, a fraternity, a political party, or even a cult. The 'initiation' process. 'Yung **pag-anib** niya sa kabilang team ang simula ng drama.'
usage_notes: Often implies a formal or significant act of joining, more so than 'pagsali'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pag-anib** sa mga makabuluhang organisasyon ay nagpapalawak ng kaalaman.","translation":"The **act of joining** meaningful organizations expands one's knowledge."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan niya ang mga benepisyo bago ang kanyang **pag-anib** sa kooperatiba.","translation":"He is studying the benefits before his **affiliation** with the cooperative."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang biglaan at di-mapigilang pagpapahayag ng salita o damdamin, karaniwang may kasamang lakas ng boses.
original_explanation: That moment when you see the latest chismis and you just shout, 'OMG, 'DI NGA?!' to an empty room. It's the unfiltered, spontaneous sound you make when you stub your toe. It's the verbal equivalent of a spit-take.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa mismong akto ng pagsasabi o pagsigaw nang biglaan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malakas na **pagkabulalas** ang narinig mula sa kusina.","translation":"A loud **exclamation** was heard from the kitchen."},{"sentence":"Sa kanyang **pagkabulalas**, nalaman ng lahat ang lihim na kanyang itinatago.","translation":"In his **outburst**, everyone learned the secret he was keeping."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang balbal na katawagan para sa 'ate,' na ginagamit bilang pantawag sa isang babae, kaibigan man o hindi, karaniwan sa paraang impormal o sa internet.
etymology: A clipped, stylized, or shortened form of 'ate' (older sister/term of respect for a woman). Popularized through text messaging and social media.
original_explanation: 'Teh' is the short, sassy, and sometimes passive-aggressive version of 'Ate'. It's what you call your friend when you're about to spill some tea ('Teh, may chika ako!'), or what you type online when you disagree with someone ('Mali ka yata, teh.'). It's the Swiss Army knife of casual address for Filipino women.
usage_notes: Highly informal. Can be used affectionately, neutrally, or sometimes confrontationally depending on tone and context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Teh**, pahiram naman ng ballpen mo.","translation":"**Sis**, can I borrow your pen?"},{"sentence":"Ano ba 'yan, **teh**? Umayos ka nga.","translation":"What's with you, **girl**? Get it together."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa anyong panghinaharap ng pandiwa; tumutukoy sa kilos ng pagkuha o pagpayag sa isang bagay na ibibigay o iaalok.
etymology: Mula sa "tanggap" na may pag-uulit ng unang pantig (ta-) bilang panandang panghinaharap.
original_explanation: The future tense of receiving something. This is you on the 15th and 30th of the month ('Swerte, tatanggap na ng sahod!'). Or when you're waiting for that Shopee delivery ('Sana bukas tatanggap na ako ng parcel.'). It's the verb of hope and expectation, whether it's for a salary, a package, or an apology you know you deserve.
usage_notes: Ito ang anyong panghinaharap ng salitang-ugat na "tanggap".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tatanggap** ka ba ng bisita bukas?","translation":"**Will you be accepting** visitors tomorrow?"},{"sentence":"Siya ang **tatanggap** ng parangal para sa buong klase.","translation":"He **will receive** the award for the whole class."}]

translation: to be a nuisance; to annoy; to pester
meaning_filipino: Magdulot ng inis, pagkainis, o abala sa isang tao sa paraang paulit-ulit.
etymology: From Hokkien Chinese 'bú-i-sī' (無意思), meaning 'senseless, meaningless' or 'unlucky'.
original_explanation: This is the specialty of a younger sibling, a persistent telemarketer, or that one fly in your room at 3 AM. It’s the act of being so incredibly annoying that the other person just wants to scream 'Bwisit!'. It's not just a one-time annoyance; it's a dedicated, sustained campaign of irritation.
usage_notes: A very common, informal word used to express annoyance. The root 'bwisit' is a mild curse word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na ang **mamuwisit** sa kapatid mo!","translation":"Stop **pestering** your sibling!"},{"sentence":"Hilig talaga ng batang iyan na **mamuwisit** ng mga natutulog.","translation":"That kid really loves to **be a nuisance** to people who are sleeping."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mabagal na takbo ng negosyo o kalakalan; mahina ang benta.
original_explanation: The official mood of every tindera sa palengke when it's not payday weekend. It's when your online shop gets zero checkouts for the day. "Friend, **matumal** ang benta ngayon, puro 'how much po?' lang." It's the economic equivalent of a traffic jam on EDSA at 3 AM – surprisingly and disappointingly slow.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in the context of business, sales, or economic activity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Matumal** ang benta ng mga parol ngayong taon kumpara noong nakaraan.","translation":"The sale of Christmas lanterns is **sluggish** this year compared to last."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa bagyo, naging **matumal** ang daloy ng turista sa Boracay.","translation":"Because of the typhoon, the flow of tourists in Boracay became **slow**."}]

meaning_filipino: Mayroong bagay na nakaharang o nakasagabal sa daluyan, na nagiging sanhi ng pagtigil ng daloy.
original_explanation: When your sink becomes a swimming pool for dirty dishes because the drain won't drain. Or when your nose is so stuffed during a cold that you can't breathe. It's the EDSA of your plumbing system—completely gridlocked and nothing is moving.
usage_notes: Commonly used for plumbing, drains, and nasal passages.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumawag ka ng tubero dahil **may-bara** ang lababo.","translation":"Call a plumber because the sink is **clogged**."},{"sentence":"Hindi ako makahinga nang maayos kasi **may-bara** ang ilong ko.","translation":"I can't breathe properly because my nose is **blocked**."}]

translation: to have food removed from teeth; to have a dental cleaning
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghiling na alisin ang tinga o dumi sa pagitan ng mga ngipin.
etymology: From pa- prefix indicating causation/request + tinga (food particle stuck between teeth).
original_explanation: When you go to the dentist and say, "**Patinga** po, doc." You're asking for a cleaning, to have all that gunk (tinga) removed from your teeth. It's the "pa-" prefix working its magic again, like in "patimbang" (have weighed) or "pagupit" (have a haircut).
usage_notes: Used as a request, often in the context of a dental visit. The more complete verb form is `magpatinga`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magpatinga** sa dentista kada anim na buwan.","translation":"You need to **have a dental cleaning** every six months."},{"sentence":"**Patinga** nga ako,\" sabi niya habang inaabot ang palito.","translation":"**Let me get this food out of my teeth**,\" he said while reaching for a toothpick."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang panghalip panao sa ikalawang panauhan na isahan. Ito ang anyo ng "ikaw" na ginagamit pagkatapos ng pandiwa o sa gitna ng pangungusap.
original_explanation: This is the "you" that's always in the middle of the action. It's the clingy version of "ikaw." You can't start a sentence with "ka," but it's everywhere else. "Kumain ka na?" (Have you eaten?) is the national anthem of Filipino care, and "ka" is the star of that show. It's short, sweet, and gets the job done.
usage_notes: Used in place of "ikaw" when it does not start the sentence. It is one of the most common words in Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Saan **ka** pupunta?","translation":"Where are **you** going?"},{"sentence":"Masaya ako para sa iyo, mahalaga **ka** sa akin.","translation":"I'm happy for you, **you** are important to me."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pampalasa na mula sa pinatuyong balat ng kahoy ng puno ng Cinnamomum. Ito ay may matamis at maanghang na lasa at aroma, at karaniwang ginagamit sa mga panghimagas at inumin.
original_explanation: The spice that makes your cinnamon rolls, champorado, and coffee taste like Christmas morning. It's that warm, cozy flavor that's both sweet and a little bit spicy, just like your favorite tita's chismis.
usage_notes: Refers to both the cinnamon stick and the ground powder.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglagay siya ng isang pirasong **kanela** sa kanyang mainit na tsokolate.","translation":"She put a stick of **cinnamon** in her hot chocolate."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na bahagi ng isang subkultura sa Pilipinas na sumikat noong huling bahagi ng 2000s, na kilala sa kanilang natatanging paraan ng paggamit ng wika sa text messaging (Jejebet) at sa kanilang moda.
etymology: Mula sa "jeje" (kumakatawan sa pagtawa) + "-mon" mula sa sikat na prangkisang "Pokémon," na nagpapahiwatig na sila ay ibang "uri" o "halimaw" na kokolektahin o kikilalanin.
original_explanation: A cultural phenomenon from the late 2000s. A Jejemon is someone who types lYk dIs, mixing capital and small letters with numbers (e.g., "iMiszU_pFoUh!"). They were the masters of the Nokia keypad. The fashion involved colorful skinny jeans, oversized hoodies, and trucker hats. Basically, the final boss of early Pinoy social media.
usage_notes: The term was once controversial and even prompted discussions in government and education. Now, it's mostly used with nostalgia.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang certified **Jejemon** ang kuya ko noong high school.","translation":"My older brother was a certified **Jejemon** in high school."},{"sentence":"Nahirapan ang mga magulang na intindihin ang text ng mga anak nilang **Jejemon**.","translation":"Parents had a hard time understanding the texts of their **Jejemon** children."}]

translation: To cause to burst; to crack open
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpapaputok o pagpapasabog sa isang bagay na may laman, tulad ng pigsa, upang lumabas ang nana o likido sa loob.
original_explanation: The verb for when you can't resist popping that pimple. It's the act of making something burst, usually something that's swollen or filled with pressure. 'Huwag mong puknatin 'yan, magkakapeklat ka!' is the classic line from your mom. Applies to boils, blisters, and other things you shouldn't be touching.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used for popping pimples, boils, or blisters.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinabihan siya ng doktor na huwag **puknatin** ang kanyang pigsa.","translation":"The doctor told him not to **pop** his boil."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya natiis at sinubukan pa ring **puknatin** ang tagihawat sa kanyang ilong.","translation":"He couldn't resist and still tried to **pop** the pimple on his nose."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa anumang kasangkapan, materyales, o binhi na ginagamit sa proseso ng pagtatanim.
etymology: From the prefix 'pan-' (instrumental) and the root word 'tanim' (to plant).
original_explanation: This is everything you need for your 'plantita' or 'plantito' phase. It can be the seeds you bought online, the special soil mix, or the cute little shovel from the hardware store. It's the starter pack for your urban gardening dreams.
usage_notes: Can function as a noun (e.g., 'mga pantanim' - planting materials) or an adjective describing something used for planting (e.g., 'lupang pantanim' - soil for planting).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si Lola ng mga bagong butong **pantanim** para sa kaniyang hardin.","translation":"Grandma bought new seeds **for planting** for her garden."},{"sentence":"Magdala ka ng palang **pantanim** para makatulong ka sa bukid.","translation":"Bring a shovel **for planting** so you can help at the farm."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa posisyong nakabaluktot ang mga binti at nakatukod ang isa o dalawang tuhod sa sahig o lupa.
original_explanation: The default position when proposing marriage, begging for forgiveness from a Pinay mom after breaking her favorite vase, or doing the 'penitensya' walk in Quiapo. It's the physical act of being on your knees.
usage_notes: Often implies humility, prayer, begging, or proposing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakaluhod** siyang nagdasal sa harap ng altar.","translation":"He was **kneeling** while praying in front of the altar."},{"sentence":"\"Patawarin mo na ako,\" sabi niya habang **nakaluhod**.","translation":"\"Please forgive me,\" he said while **kneeling**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paggiling sa tubo upang makuha ang katas nito para gawing asukal o iba pang produkto.
original_explanation: This is an old-school, industrial-level juicing process for sugarcane. Think of those giant machines in haciendas that squeeze the life (and sweetness) out of sugarcane stalks to make our beloved panutsa and sugar for our 3-in-1 coffee. It's the OG way of getting a sugar rush.
usage_notes: A specific agricultural/industrial term related to sugarcane processing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Noong unang panahon, mano-mano ang pag-**magkabyaw** ng mga manggagawa sa asukarera.","translation":"In the old days, workers used to **mill sugarcane** manually at the sugar mill."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magkabyaw** ng isang toneladang tubo bago matapos ang linggo.","translation":"We need to **mill** a ton of sugarcane before the week ends."}]

translation: will do at the same time; simultaneously
meaning_filipino: Mangyayari o gagawin sa iisang oras o panahon.
original_explanation: The ultimate multitasking challenge. Like trying to join a Zoom meeting while cooking adobo and replying to your jowa's text. When it works, you're a genius. When it doesn't, sunog ang adobo mo at seenzoned ka.
usage_notes: Can also function as an adverb ('magkakasabay na dumating' - arrived simultaneously).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Plano naming **magkakasabay** na umuwi pagkatapos ng party.","translation":"We plan to go home **all at the same time** after the party."},{"sentence":"Hindi pwedeng **magkakasabay** ang lahat ng proyekto; kailangan nating mag-prioritize.","translation":"All the projects cannot happen **simultaneously**; we need to prioritize."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsisimula ng pagliwanag sa umaga; ang paghiwalay ng araw sa gabi.
etymology: Mula sa `mang-` at `bitak` (crack), na tumutukoy sa 'pagbibitak' o paghiwalay ng liwanag sa dilim.
original_explanation: This is what BPO agents and night-shifters see after their shift ends. It's the moment the sky starts to get a bit of light, signaling "Uwian na!" It's the universe's way of saying, "Good morning!" or "Good night!" depending on your lifestyle. Also, the title of a classic OPM song.
usage_notes: Matalinghaga at pampanitikan. Mas karaniwan sa panitikan kaysa sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bago pa **mamitak** ang umaga, gising na ang mga magsasaka.","translation":"Before the morning **dawns**, the farmers are already awake."},{"sentence":"Nag-usap sila hanggang sa **mamitak** ang sikat ng araw.","translation":"They talked until the sunlight **broke** (at dawn)."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahina at pigil na pagtawa, karaniwang nagpapahiwatig ng katuwaan o pagkasabik na itinatago.
original_explanation: That sound you make when your crush walks by and your friend starts teasing you. It's the "silent mode" of laughter, perfect for when you're trying not to get caught laughing at a meme during a serious meeting.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb stem (umalik-ik). The sound is high-pitched and often associated with children or feelings of secret amusement.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **alik-ik** ng mga dalaga mula sa kabilang kwarto.","translation":"I heard the **giggle** of the young ladies from the other room."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya napigilan ang isang **alik-ik** nang mabasa ang text message.","translation":"She couldn't suppress a **giggle** when she read the text message."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang bagay na may disenyo, guhit, o teksturang katulad ng sa isang banig.
original_explanation: Describes something with a crosshatch or woven pattern, like a banig. Think of those fancy native bags, the surface of a pineapple, or even the waffle cone for your ice cream. If it looks like it was woven, you can describe it as **banigin**. "Wow, ang ganda ng pattern ng bag mo, parang **banigin**!"
usage_notes: This is a descriptive term, less common in everyday conversation but useful for describing patterns.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang balat ng pinya ay may itsurang **banigin**.","translation":"The skin of a pineapple has a **mat-like** appearance."},{"sentence":"Gusto ko ang **banigin** na disenyo ng iyong pitaka.","translation":"I like the **mat-like** design of your wallet."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kalagayan ng isang tao o pamilya na may kakulangan sa mga pangunahing pangangailangan tulad ng pagkain, tirahan, at salapi.
original_explanation: This isn't about a hard exam, this is about a hard life. 'Yung petsa de peligro at wala pang sahod. 'Yung kailangan mong mag-instant noodles for a week straight. It's the reason why many Filipinos become OFWs, working hard to escape the state of being mahirap. It's a serious word that reflects a major social issue.
usage_notes: This is the other primary meaning of "mahirap." Context is key to differentiate it from "difficult." It usually describes a person or a family's economic status.
