usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming pamilyang **mahirap** ang natulungan ng kanilang programa.","translation":"Many **poor** families were helped by their program."},{"sentence":"Laking **mahirap** si Manny Pacquiao kaya't nagsikap siyang maabot ang kanyang mga pangarap.","translation":"Manny Pacquiao grew up **poor**, which is why he strove to reach his dreams."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na uri ng loro (parrot) na katutubo sa Pilipinas, kilala sa makulay na luntiang balahibo at sa ugali nitong matulog nang nakabitin nang patiwarik.
original_explanation: A tiny, super cute, and very green parrot native to the Philippines. They're the acrobats of the bird world, famous for sleeping upside down like a bat. They're cute, but don't get them confused with the *other* meaning of kulasisi...
usage_notes: This is the primary, zoological meaning of the word, referring to the bird species Loriculus philippensis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakita kami ng isang kawan ng **kulasisi** sa puno ng mangga.","translation":"We saw a flock of **Philippine hanging parrots** in the mango tree."},{"sentence":"Ang **kulasisi** ay isa sa pinakamaliit na loro sa Pilipinas.","translation":"The **Philippine hanging parrot** is one of the smallest parrots in the Philippines."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang heometrikal na pigura na may dalawang magkatulad na pabilog na base at isang kurbadong gilid; maaari ring tumukoy sa isang bahagi ng makina ng sasakyan.
original_explanation: The geometric shape your high school math teacher tortured you with (volume = πr²h). Also, what your friendly neighborhood 'mekaniko' is talking about when he says your car's engine has a problem. 'Sir, may tama ang silindro mo,' which is code for 'Maghanda ka nang gumastos.'
usage_notes: Used for the geometric shape, mechanical parts (like an engine cylinder or a gas cylinder), and sometimes a rolling pin ('rodilyo' is more common). Differentiated from 'silinder' (top hat).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinakalkula ng mga estudyante ang bolyum ng isang **silindro**.","translation":"The students are calculating the volume of a **cylinder**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan palitan ang **silindro** ng makina para umandar ulit ang kotse.","translation":"The engine **cylinder** needs to be replaced for the car to run again."}]

translation: snapping; breaking off (of a string, rope, etc.)
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos o estado ng biglaang pagputol o pagkatanggal ng isang bagay na nakatali o nakakabit, tulad ng lubid o sinulid.
original_explanation: This is that "snap!" moment. Not the cool Thanos kind, but the sad, frustrating kind. Like when your earphones suddenly die mid-podcast, your tsinelas strap gives up on life in the middle of the street, or your patience with your slow internet connection finally experiences pagkalagot. It's the point of no return for anything tied, connected, or even your sanity.
usage_notes: Often used figuratively to mean the snapping of patience or temper.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkalagot** ng tali ng saranggola ang dahilan kung bakit ito lumipad palayo.","translation":"The **snapping** of the kite's string was the reason it flew away."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko na napigilan ang **pagkalagot** ng aking pasensya sa kanya.","translation":"I could no longer prevent the **snapping** of my patience with him."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong madaling maawa, maramdamin, at malambot ang puso.
etymology: Compound of "puso" (heart) and "mamon" (a type of soft, fluffy Filipino cake), metaphorically linking the heart's softness to the cake's texture.
original_explanation: Literally "heart of a mamon (chiffon cake)". This is the friend who cries during a Jollibee commercial. They are a certified "marupok" who will forgive their cheating ex for the 5th time. They're sweet and soft, but you also kinda want to shake them and say "Tumigil ka na!"
usage_notes: Describes a person's character. Often used with a mix of affection and slight exasperation. Its antonym is 'pusong-bato' (heart of stone).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi ka niya matatanggihan. **Pusong-mamon** 'yon.","translation":"Don't worry, she won't be able to refuse you. She's **soft-hearted**."},{"sentence":"Dahil **pusong-mamon** si Ana, pinatawad niya agad ang nagkasala sa kanya.","translation":"Because Ana is **overly sentimental**, she immediately forgave the one who wronged her."}]

meaning_filipino: Magsagawa ng isang gawaing pagpapakasakit o pagsisisi bilang kabayaran sa mga nagawang kasalanan, karaniwang may kinalaman sa relihiyon.
original_explanation: What you do during Holy Week, either by literally joining the flagellants in Pampanga or by giving up softdrinks for 40 days. In modern terms, it's like deactivating your social media accounts to 'cleanse' yourself after a toxic online fight.
usage_notes: Primarily associated with the Catholic observance of Lent (Mahal na Araw) in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing Mahal na Araw, may mga debotong naglalakbay sa mga simbahan para **magpenitensya**.","translation":"Every Holy Week, some devotees travel to churches to **do penance**."},{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **magpenitensya** sa pamamagitan ng pag-aayuno at pananalangin.","translation":"He decided to **do penance** through fasting and prayer."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng mahabang pantalon na karaniwang isinusuot sa mga pormal o semi-pormal na okasyon, hindi gawa sa maong.
original_explanation: Yung office uniform mo from Monday to Thursday bago mag-casual Friday. Ito yung pantalon na kailangan mong plantsahin maigi para 'di ka magmukhang gusgusin sa presentation mo sa boss. Partner ng leather shoes at polo shirt.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong magsuot ng **islaks** para sa interview mo bukas.","translation":"You need to wear **slacks** for your interview tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Hindi pinapayagan ang maong sa opisina, kaya **islaks** ang isinusuot ko.","translation":"Jeans are not allowed in the office, so I wear **trousers**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang simbolo sa isang alpabeto na kumakatawan sa isang tunog; maaari ring tumukoy sa mga salita ng isang awit.
original_explanation: 'Titik' is a double agent. It can be the letters A, B, C... you know, the building blocks of your 'Marites' group chat messages. But it's also the 'lyrics' of that LSS-inducing song you can't get out of your head. 'Anong **titik** ng kantang 'yan?' is how you ask for the lyrics, not which letter of the alphabet it starts with.
usage_notes: Context determines whether it means 'letter' or 'lyrics'. 'Titik ng awit' explicitly means 'lyrics of the song'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang salitang 'pag-ibig' ay may pitong **titik**.","translation":"The word 'pag-ibig' has seven **letters**."},{"sentence":"Kinabisado niya ang **titik** ng paborito niyang kanta.","translation":"She memorized the **lyrics** of her favorite song."}]

meaning_filipino: Alisin ang damit o takip ng isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: What you do to a crying toddler who needs a diaper change, or what a villain in a teleserye does to a treasure chest to reveal its contents. It's an action done *to* someone or something. Don't get any ideas, ha.
usage_notes: Ang pokus ng pandiwang ito ay ang tao o bagay na hinuhubaran (object focus). Halimbawa, 'Hubaran mo *ang bata*.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hubaran** mo na ng sapatos ang bata bago matulog.","translation":"**Take the shoes off** the child before they sleep."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **hubaran** ng balat ang mangga kung gagawin mong shake.","translation":"Don't **strip** the skin off the mango if you're going to make it into a shake."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa estado ng pagiging mulat at hindi natutulog.
original_explanation: Your default status when you're scrolling through TikTok at 3 AM. It's the opposite of 'tulog.' It's also the state your 'Marites' neighbor is in 24/7, always aware of the latest chismis. 'Pre, gising ka pa?'
usage_notes: Can be a state (adjective: 'Gising ako.') or a command (verb root: 'Gising!'). The verb 'to wake someone up' is 'gisingin'. The verb 'to wake up by oneself' is 'gumising'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Gising** ka na ba? Tanghali na!","translation":"Are you **awake** already? It's already noon!"},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong manatiling **gising** para tapusin ang aking trabaho.","translation":"I need to stay **awake** to finish my work."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong kasama o kabilang sa isang grupo ng mga magnanakaw; kasabwat sa pagnanakaw.
original_explanation: The squad you definitely don't want to be a part of. This is the term for someone's partner-in-crime, literally. In modern PH context, it's often thrown around to describe corrupt politicians and their cronies. It's 'tropa' but for illegal withdrawals.
usage_notes: Has a very strong negative and often political connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahuli ang lider ng sindikato kasama ang kanyang mga **kamagnanakaw**.","translation":"The syndicate leader was caught along with his **fellow thieves**."},{"sentence":"Tinawag niyang mga **kamagnanakaw** ang mga opisyal na sangkot sa korapsyon.","translation":"He called the officials involved in corruption **corrupt associates**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng karayom at sinulid upang pagdugtungin ang mga tela o kumpunihin ang mga damit.
original_explanation: What your lola does to your ripped jeans, or what that sastre in the palengke does for 50 pesos. It's the OG way of 'DIY' fashion before Shopee and TikTok hacks. Before fast fashion, there was just 'manahi'.
usage_notes: A common verb for the action of sewing by hand or machine.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natuto siyang **manahi** mula sa kanyang ina.","translation":"She learned **to sew** from her mother."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangunahing tauhan sa isang kuwento, dula, o pelikula, na karaniwang siyang bayani.
etymology: From Spanish 'vida' meaning 'life', but usage shifted in Filipino to mean the 'life' of the story.
original_explanation: The main character energy. In a teleserye, they're the one who gets slapped, cries in the rain, but eventually gets the guy and the inheritance. In real life, it's you, thinking you're the main character while stuck in EDSA traffic.
usage_notes: Can also be used to refer to someone who is the center of attention in a positive way.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **bida** sa paborito mong pelikula?","translation":"Who is the **protagonist** in your favorite movie?"},{"sentence":"Siya lagi ang **bida** sa mga party dahil sa galing niyang kumanta.","translation":"She's always the **star** of the parties because of her great singing."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging marangya; labis na karangyaan, pagpapakitang-gilas sa yaman o luho.
etymology: From Spanish 'rancia', which originally meant 'stale' or 'old', but the meaning in Tagalog evolved to signify old-money pomp and eventually, any form of luxury or ostentation.
original_explanation: It's the 'flex' culture. Showing off your new iPhone, your branded bag, or your trip to Amanpulo. It's the opposite of 'simple lang'. Think of those grand fiesta celebrations or debut parties na parang concert ni Taylor Swift sa production value. 'Yan ang rangya.
usage_notes: Often used with a slightly negative connotation, implying unnecessary showing off.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **rangya** ang kanyang pamumuhay, pero hindi naman siya masaya.","translation":"His lifestyle is full of **luxury**, but he is not happy."},{"sentence":"Hindi kailangan ng **rangya** para maging engrande ang kasal.","translation":"You don't need **pomp** for the wedding to be grand."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na hindi nauubos o tila walang katapusan ang dami o suplay nito.
original_explanation: This is like the chismis in your neighborhood—it's **inexhaustible**. Just when you think it's over, a new 'episode' drops. It's also the feeling you get with your credit card debt sometimes, parang **walang-pagkaubos**.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa paraang hyperbole upang ilarawan ang isang malaki o tila walang-hanggang suplay ng isang bagay, maging ito man ay nahahawakan (tulad ng pagkain) o hindi (tulad ng problema).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tila **walang-pagkaubos** ang problema na dumarating sa kanya.","translation":"It seems the problems coming her way are **endless**."},{"sentence":"Salamat sa **walang-pagkaubos** na suporta ng aking mga magulang.","translation":"Thanks for the **inexhaustible** support of my parents."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gawain o proseso upang malaman ang kalidad, kakayahan, o katotohanan ng isang bagay o tao.
original_explanation: This is the "try mo lang" moment. A **subok** can be tasting a new milk tea flavor, trying to see if your old jeans still fit, or even testing a relationship's strength. "Pagsubok" is the heavier, more dramatic version (the trials of life). But "subok" is the everyday trial-and-error. "Subukan mo kaya mag-apply sa BPO?"
usage_notes: The verb form 'subukan' (to try) is extremely common. As a noun, it's often seen in compounds like 'panahon ng pagsubok' (time of trial).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ito ay isang **subok** lamang para malaman kung epektibo ang gamot.","translation":"This is only a **test** to see if the medicine is effective."},{"sentence":"Ang buhay ay puno ng **subok**.","translation":"Life is full of **trials**."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa matematika, ito ang bilang na nasa ilalim ng linya sa isang praksyon, na nagsasaad kung sa ilang pantay na bahagi hinati ang isang buo.
original_explanation: 'Yung number sa ilalim ng fraction. Kung ang fraction ay 3/4, 'yung 4 ang denominador. Isipin mo 'yung pizza. Kung hinati sa 8, 'yung '8' ang denominador. Siya 'yung nagsasabi kung gaano karami ang "total slices" ng problema mo bago mo pa malaman kung ilan ang para sa 'yo (the numerator).
usage_notes: Primarily used in a mathematical context. Can be used metaphorically as "common denominator" (karaniwang denominador).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa praksyon na 1/2, ang 2 ang **denominador**.","translation":"In the fraction 1/2, 2 is the **denominator**."},{"sentence":"Para mapagsama ang mga praksyon, kailangan nilang magkaroon ng parehong **denominador**.","translation":"To add the fractions, they need to have the same **denominator**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagtutugma o paghahanap ng kapareha para sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: This is your tita's favorite hobby at family reunions, trying to match you with her friend's single anak. It's also what you do with your socks after laundry, or finding the perfect 'ka-terno' for your OOTD. The ultimate goal of every 'ship' in a teleserye.
usage_notes: This is the noun form for the action. The verb command form is 'pagparisin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapares** ng tamang alak sa pagkain ay isang sining.","translation":"The **pairing** of the right wine with food is an art."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkakaroon ng malaking kita o tubo mula sa isang negosyo o transaksyon; ang pagdagdag ng timbang o pagiging mataba. Ito ay nasa panahunang pangnagdaan.
original_explanation: This word has two moods: 'Yay, money!' or 'Oh no, weight gain!' You can 'tumiba' (profited) from a good investment in stocks or crypto. You can also 'tumiba' (got fat) after a month-long series of holiday parties and samgyupsal nights. Both involve getting 'thicc'—either your wallet or your waistline.
usage_notes: Past tense verb. The root 'tiba' means profit. The usage for 'got fat' is a common colloquialism, a playful corruption of 'tumaba' (from root 'taba'). Context determines the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumiba** siya nang malaki sa pagbebenta ng mga face mask noong pandemya.","translation":"He **gained a huge profit** from selling face masks during the pandemic."},{"sentence":"Hala, parang **tumiba** ako ngayong bakasyon!","translation":"Oh my, it seems I've **gotten fat** this vacation!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o pakiramdam ng pagiging inaantok o pagnanais na matulog.
etymology: From root `antok` (sleepy). The `pag-` prefix and reduplication of the first vowel `a` form a noun describing the state or feeling.
original_explanation: That feeling you get at 2 PM after a heavy lunch, during a boring meeting, or while stuck in EDSA traffic. It's your body's low-batt warning. Your eyelids feel like they have weights on them, and your head starts doing that slow, involuntary nod. The mortal enemy of students in afternoon classes and BPO agents on a graveyard shift.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko mapigilan ang aking **pag-aantok** habang nanonood ng pelikula.","translation":"I can't fight my **sleepiness** while watching the movie."},{"sentence":"Uminom siya ng kape para labanan ang **pag-aantok**.","translation":"He drank coffee to fight the **drowsiness**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbuka ng mga hita o binti nang malayo sa isa't isa habang nakatayo o nakaupo.
original_explanation: The classic "tito" pose when sitting down, or how you sit on a motorcycle. It's the ultimate power stance for asserting dominance over the armrest in a jeepney. "Manspreading" before it was even a word. "Huy, 'wag ka masyadong bumakaka, wala na kaming maupuan!"
usage_notes: Ito ang pandiwang nasa anyong pangkasalukuyan o pangnagdaan (actor-focus) ng salitang-ugat na 'bakaka'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumakaka** siya para maging matatag ang kanyang tayo.","translation":"He **spread his legs apart** to make his stance stable."},{"sentence":"Pinagsabihan ng nanay ang bata na huwag **bumakaka** kapag naka-palda.","translation":"The mother told the child not to **sit with her legs spread** when wearing a skirt."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghihiwalay o pagtatanggal ng isang bahagi mula sa kabuuan sa pamamagitan ng isang matalim na kasangkapan.
original_explanation: What your kapitbahay did to your internet connection while trimming their trees. Or what you did to your toxic ex. You pumutol the connection. Cut off, literally or figuratively.
usage_notes: This is the completed or past tense form of the verb. The infinitive is 'pumutol' and the present progressive is 'pumumuputol'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **pumutol** ng puno sa bakuran?","translation":"Who **cut** the tree in the yard?"},{"sentence":"**Pumutol** siya ng ugnayan sa kanyang mga kaibigan.","translation":"He/She **severed** ties with his friends."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang kasangkapan na ginagamit sa paghampas, pagpalo, o pagtama sa isang bagay.
etymology: From paN- (becomes pam-) + palo. 'Palo' means 'to hit' or 'strike'.
original_explanation: The ultimate "you're gonna get it" tool from your childhood. This could be a slipper (tsinelas), a rolled-up newspaper, a belt (sinturon), or an actual paddle. It's the physical manifestation of "Wait 'til your father gets home." In a non-disciplinary context, it's a bat for baseball or a stick for hitting a palayok.
usage_notes: The specific type of pamalo is often understood from context. It carries a strong connotation of discipline or punishment but can also be neutral (e.g., in sports).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha ng **pamalo** ang nanay dahil nabasag ko ang banga.","translation":"Mother got a **paddle** because I broke the jar."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang sanga ng puno bilang **pamalo** sa ahas.","translation":"He used the tree branch as a **striking stick** for the snake."}]

translation: state of being completely broken or dilapidated
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging lubos na wasak, gutay-gutay, o nasa napakasamang kondisyon dahil sa katagalan, kapabayaan, o matinding pinsala.
etymology: From `pagka-` (state of) + `sira-sira` (reduplication of 'sira' to indicate intensity or plurality of damage).
original_explanation: This isn't just 'sira' (broken), this is 'sira na, sira pa'. It's the state of that one road in your barangay that's more potholes than pavement. It's your favorite t-shirt that's now full of holes but you can't let go. It implies a level of disrepair that's almost impressive in its thoroughness.
usage_notes: The repetition of 'sira' intensifies the meaning, indicating a widespread or severe state of disrepair. It suggests something is broken in multiple places or in a state of decay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa kalumaan, kitang-kita na ang **pagkasira-sira** ng lumang bahay.","translation":"Due to its age, the **dilapidation** of the old house was very evident."},{"sentence":"Inireklamo ng mga residente ang **pagkasira-sira** ng kanilang kalsada.","translation":"The residents complained about the **state of disrepair** of their road."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi nagtatapos o walang katapusan; walang takdang dulo o limitasyon.
original_explanation: Like your crush's list of excuses for not replying, or the EDSA traffic on a payday Friday. It just goes on and on and on. Also, the love your parents have for you, which is a nice thought.
usage_notes: Often used to describe abstract concepts like love, time, or space. The hyphen is common but it can also be written as two words 'walang hangganan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagmamahal ng isang ina ay **walang-hangganan**.","translation":"A mother's love is **endless**."},{"sentence":"Naniniwala sila sa buhay na **walang-hangganan** pagkatapos ng kamatayan.","translation":"They believe in **infinite** life after death."}]

translation: to have money; to acquire money
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon o pagtatamo ng salapi o pera.
etymology: From 'magka-' (to have/acquire) + 'pilak' (silver, used colloquially for money).
original_explanation: Eto yung state mo after sahod day. Biglang may pang-Starbucks ka na at kaya mo nang i-treat ang barkada. Pero usually, sandali lang ito bago dumating ang mga bayarin. "Sana all laging magkapilak."
usage_notes: Often used colloquially to mean having money, not literally having silver.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kapag **nagkapilak** ako, bibili ako ng bagong sapatos.","translation":"When I **get some money**, I will buy new shoes."},{"sentence":"Swerte niya, **nagkapilak** siya sa lotto.","translation":"He's lucky, he **got money** from the lottery."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa pook o lugar na ito na kinaroroonan ng nagsasalita.
etymology: Mula sa salitang 'dito' na isang salitang-ugat. May kaugnayan sa 'diyan' (there, near listener) at 'doon' (there, far from both).
original_explanation: The default answer when your Grab driver calls and asks "Nasan na po kayo?" - "Nandito na po!" even if you're still 5 minutes away. 'Dito' is the place to be, the 'X' that marks the spot, the location pin of your life.
usage_notes: Changes to 'rito' if the preceding word ends in a vowel, 'w', or 'y'. For example, "Halika rito" (Come here) instead of "Halika dito".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkita tayo **dito** sa may coffee shop mamayang alas-tres.","translation":"Let's meet **here** at the coffee shop later at three."},{"sentence":"Pakilagay mo na lang **dito** sa mesa ang mga pinamili mo.","translation":"Please just put your groceries **here** on the table."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pag-upo kung saan ang bigat ng katawan ay nakasalalay sa mga sakong, at ang mga tuhod ay lubos na nakabaluktot.
original_explanation: The classic Filipino 'tambay' pose. You see it everywhere: waiting for a jeep, talking to a neighbor, or just chilling. It's that energy-efficient squat that your lolo can hold for an hour while reading the newspaper. Foreigners call it the 'Asian Squat,' we just call it being comfortable.
usage_notes: Describes a manner of sitting or resting. Often associated with informal settings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita ko si Mang Kiko na **patingkayad** na naghihintay sa pagdating ng bus.","translation":"I saw Mang Kiko **squatting** while waiting for the bus to arrive."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang portable na aparato na maaaring mag-imbak ng enerhiyang elektrikal at gamitin upang kargahan ang ibang mga elektronikong kagamitan tulad ng cellphone o tablet.
etymology: Direktang hiram mula sa salitang Ingles na "power bank".
original_explanation: The ultimate lifesaver for every Filipino who's always "lowbatt." This is your phone's best friend, especially during long commutes, brownouts, or when you're at a coffee shop where all the outlets are taken. Having a fully charged powerbank is a sign of a responsible adult in 2026. Not having one is a recipe for anxiety.
usage_notes: Isang direktang hiram na salita mula sa Ingles, malawakang ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap. Walang karaniwang katumbas sa Tagalog na ginagamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pahiram naman ng **powerbank** mo, 1% na lang ako.","translation":"Can I borrow your **power bank**, I'm at 1%."},{"sentence":"Laging puno ang aking **powerbank** bago ako umalis ng bahay.","translation":"My **power bank** is always full before I leave the house."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagpatungin ang mga bahagi ng isang bagay, tulad ng damit o papel, upang ito ay lumiit at maging maayos.
original_explanation: The household chore that never ends. After you 'maglaba' (wash clothes), you have to **magtiklop**. It's the act of folding your laundry, your love letters from high school, or even your hand in a game of poker when you know you're beat.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for folding objects or figuratively for giving up or 'folding' in a game ('tumiklop').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinuruan ako ng nanay ko kung paano **magtiklop** ng damit nang maayos.","translation":"My mother taught me how **to fold** clothes neatly."},{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **magtiklop** ng banig pagkagising sa umaga.","translation":"Don't forget **to fold** the sleeping mat after waking up in the morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang nagpapahayag ng pagkakaroon o presensya sa lugar na kinalalagyan ng nagsasalita. Ito ay pinaikling anyo ng 'narito'.
etymology: A syncopated form of "nandito", which comes from "narito".
original_explanation: The official Filipino 'I have arrived!' announcement. It’s what you text your friends when you're finally at the milk tea shop. It's the contraction of 'narito' that makes it more casual. 'Ma, andito na po ako!' is the password to get inside the house after a late night out.
usage_notes: A more common, informal contraction of 'narito' or 'nandito.' It is used when the object/person is right where the speaker is. Contrast with 'andiyan' (is there, near the listener) and 'andoon' (is over there, far from both).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, **andito** lang ako para sa'yo.","translation":"Don't worry, I **am just here** for you."},{"sentence":"**Andito** na ang inorder mong pagkain.","translation":"The food you ordered **is here**."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing maamo o hindi mailap ang isang hayop; suyuin upang bumait.
original_explanation: What you do to a stray cat so it will finally let you pet it. It's a game of patience, treats, and not making sudden movements. Also, what you try to do to your strict boss before you ask for a leave. It's the art of turning a 'wild beast' into a purring kitten.
usage_notes: Used for animals, but also frequently and metaphorically for people, especially in the context of persuasion or calming someone down.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang **paamuin** ang ligaw na aso sa kanilang lugar.","translation":"He is trying to **tame** the stray dog in their area."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **paamuin** ang iyong nobya bago ka magpaalam na lalabas kasama ang barkada.","translation":"You need to **placate** your girlfriend before asking for permission to go out with your friends."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na ginagamit bilang tawagan ng pagmamahal sa isang kasintahan, asawa, o malapit na kaibigan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Ingles na 'love', na pinaikli at ginawang parang pangmaramihan para sa paglalambing.
original_explanation: A cutesy, modern evolution of 'love.' It's what you call your jowa when 'babe' or 'mahal' feels too mainstream. Sounds like a text message from 2008 that just refused to die. 'Hi labs, kumain ka na?' is the modern Filipino's 'How do I love thee? Let me count the ways.'
usage_notes: Purong impormal at ginagamit bilang tawagan. Minsan, binabaybay na 'labz'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uwi ka na, **labs**. Hinihintay na kita.","translation":"Come home now, **my love**. I'm waiting for you."},{"sentence":"Happy anniversary, **labs**! I love you!","translation":"Happy anniversary, **love**! I love you!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na ginagamit upang paglagyan o maglaman ng iba pang mga bagay, karaniwan ay pagkain o maliliit na kagamitan.
etymology: From "silid" (room) + "-an" (locative suffix), literally "a place to put things in".
original_explanation: This is your Tupperware, your lunch box, your generic ice cream tub that now holds frozen fish. It's any object whose life purpose is to hold stuff, from your baon to your feelings (charot!). The ultimate 'lalagyan'.
usage_notes: While often used for food containers ('baunan'), it can refer to any kind of container or vessel. The root 'silid' means 'room', so a 'sisidlan' is conceptually a small 'room' for things.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakilagay na lang ng natirang ulam sa **sisidlan** at ilagay sa pridyeder.","translation":"Please just put the leftover food in the **container** and place it in the refrigerator."},{"sentence":"Nawawala ang takip ng paborito kong **sisidlan**.","translation":"The lid of my favorite **container** is missing."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang organisadong samahan ng mga manggagawa na binuo upang isulong at protektahan ang kanilang mga karapatan at interes.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na "union". Mas karaniwang binabaybay bilang "unyon".
original_explanation: The more common spelling is 'unyon'. This is your work barkada that's legally recognized. Sila 'yung taga-reklamo sa HR for you, demanding better pay, more benefits, and maybe even unli-coffee. They're the 'we' in 'we deserve better!'
usage_notes: The spelling "unyon" is far more common in formal and informal Filipino writing. "Union" is often seen in code-switching.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumali ang mga manggagawa sa **union** upang ipaglaban ang mas mataas na sahod.","translation":"The workers joined the **union** to fight for higher wages."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng paglilinis ng katawan gamit ang tubig at sabon.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'pa-' (nagpapahiwatig ng kaganapan o gawain) at salitang-ugat na 'ligo' (paghuhugas ng katawan).
original_explanation: That magical ritual that turns you from a zombie into a functioning human being in the morning. Ito 'yung 'saglit lang ako' na nagiging 30-minute concert sa banyo. The sacred act of washing away yesterday's problems (and today's B.O.).
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa mga pariralang tulad ng 'oras na ng paligo' (it's time for a bath).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aga naman ng **paligo** mo ngayon.","translation":"Your **bath** is quite early today."},{"sentence":"Isinama niya ang aso para sa lingguhang **paligo** nito.","translation":"He brought the dog for its weekly **bath**."}]

translation: to tremble with intense emotion (e.g., anger, delight)
meaning_filipino: Ang makaramdam ng matinding panginginig o paninikip ng panga dahil sa sobrang galit, tuwa, o pagkasabik.
original_explanation: That feeling when you see a super cute baby and you just want to pinch its cheeks so hard, but you can't. It's also the feeling when your internet connection dies mid-game. It's 'gigil,' but in verb form. The emotion is so strong, your body just has to react.
usage_notes: The context determines whether the emotion is positive (cute aggression) or negative (suppressed rage).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula siyang **manggigil** sa galit nang makita ang kalat.","translation":"He started to **tremble with rage** when he saw the mess."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko mapigilang **manggigil** sa kaputian ng tuta.","translation":"I can't help but **feel that overwhelming cuteness** for the white puppy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang aral na natutunan; maaari ring tumukoy sa isang mahabang pangaral o sermon dahil sa isang pagkakamali.
original_explanation: This isn't your typical school lesson. A 'lisyon' is the 30-minute "talk" you get from your parents when you come home past curfew, complete with historical references to all your past mistakes. It's a lecture powered by love, disappointment, and a desire for you not to mess up again. "Na-late ka na naman? O, heto na ang lisyon ng nanay mo."
usage_notes: Has a stronger connotation of being lectured or scolded than the more neutral 'aral' (lesson).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binigyan siya ng mahabang **lisyon** ng kanyang lola dahil sa pag-uwi nang gabi.","translation":"His grandmother gave him a long **scolding** for coming home late."},{"sentence":"Sana ay may natutunan kang **lisyon** sa nangyari.","translation":"I hope you learned a **lesson** from what happened."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangatnig na nagpapahayag ng pag-ayon o pagpayag sa isang kondisyon na may kasamang pasubali o pagtutol sa inaasahang resulta. Katumbas ng 'kahit na' o 'bagaman'.
etymology: Possibly from `ka` + `hi` + `man`, related to `bagaman` or `kahit man`.
original_explanation: The official word for "Okay, fine, but...". It's the classic "I'll go with you, **even if** I don't really want to." It’s the literary, old-school way of saying 'kahit'. You'd use this to sound poetic while reluctantly agreeing to something.
usage_notes: Primarily used in literary or formal writing. `Kahit na` is the modern, everyday equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kahiman** siya ay pagod, nagpatuloy pa rin siya sa pagtatrabaho.","translation":"**Although** he was tired, he still continued to work."},{"sentence":"**Kahiman** mahirap ang buhay, hindi siya nawawalan ng pag-asa.","translation":"**Even if** life is hard, he does not lose hope."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gusali ng pamahalaang lokal ng isang munisipalidad o bayan; ang sentro ng administrasyon ng isang bayan.
original_explanation: The ground zero for all your government-related adulting needs in your town—getting a business permit, paying taxes, or complaining to the mayor. It's the place your parents sent you to get a cedula. Basically the town's main office, often located right beside the church and the plaza.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumunta ako sa **munisipyo** para kumuha ng business permit.","translation":"I went to the **municipal hall** to get a business permit."},{"sentence":"Nasa gitna ng bayan ang bagong tayong **munisipyo**.","translation":"The newly built **town hall** is in the center of the town."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat ng mga delegado o kinatawan na ipinadala para sa isang partikular na layunin; ang akto ng pagde-delega.
original_explanation: Ito yung buong tropa na pupunta sa seminar, hindi lang isang tao. The whole squad representing the company or country. Sila yung sabay-sabay naka-uniporme or matching jackets sa airport, ready for the group picture.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa grupo ng mga tao o sa mismong akto ng pamamahagi ng gawain.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mainit na tinanggap ang **delegasyon** mula sa Japan.","translation":"The **delegation** from Japan was warmly welcomed."},{"sentence":"Ang epektibong **delegasyon** ng mga gawain ay mahalaga sa pamumuno.","translation":"The effective **delegation** of tasks is important in leadership."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglunok ng isang bagay nang buo at walang pagnguya, karaniwan ay malaki.
original_explanation: Like how you swallow your pride ('pride' is the 'something whole') to text them first. Or how a snake eats its food. Or how you **lumulon** a whole pill because you can't stand the taste.
usage_notes: Differs from 'lunok' (swallow) by emphasizing swallowing something whole or in large gulps.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinanood nila kung paano **lumulon** ng isang buong itlog ang ahas.","translation":"They watched how the snake **swallowed** a whole egg."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong subukang **lumulon** ng pagkain nang hindi nginunguya.","translation":"Don't try to **swallow** food **whole** without chewing."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ilegal na paggamit o pagnanakaw ng pera o ari-arian na ipinagkatiwala sa isang tao para sa pansariling kapakinabangan.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `pan-` (nagiging `panl-`) + pag-uulit ng unang pantig (`lu`) + salitang-ugat na `lustay` (pagwaldas o pag-aksaya).
original_explanation: This is the official term for when the class treasurer uses the class fund to buy milk tea for themselves. It's taking something you're supposed to be watching over—like money or resources—and using it for your own "budol." A classic move in politics, sadly.
usage_notes: Isang pormal at legal na termino para sa krimen ng paglustay ng pondo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahaharap sa kasong **panlulustay** ng pondo ng bayan ang dating opisyal.","translation":"The former official is facing charges of **embezzlement** of public funds."},{"sentence":"Ang **panlulustay** ay isang malaking kasalanan sa tiwalang ibinigay sa iyo.","translation":"**Misappropriation** is a huge betrayal of the trust given to you."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtutol o pagkontra sa isang bagay, tao, o pangyayari.
etymology: From pag- (nominalizer) + laban (fight) + -an (object focus suffix), referring to the act of fighting something.
original_explanation: This is your 'It's complicated' status with your feelings. You know you shouldn't catch feelings for that person, so you try to paglabanan the urge to slide into their DMs. It's the internal struggle between your heart and your brain, or your diet and that last piece of lechon.
usage_notes: Often used to describe resisting a temptation, an urge, or fighting against an oppressor or a difficult situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **paglabanan** ang antok pagkatapos mananghalian.","translation":"It's hard to **fight against** sleepiness after having lunch."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **paglabanan** ang anumang uri ng katiwalian sa gobyerno.","translation":"It is necessary to **fight against** any form of corruption in the government."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang payak na anyo ng isang salita na walang kasamang panlapi. Ito ang pinakapuso ng salita kung saan nabubuo ang iba't ibang anyo nito.
etymology: Isang tambalang salita mula sa "salita" (word) at "ugat" (root).
original_explanation: The 'salitang-ugat' is the main character, the bida of a word family. All the other forms are just spin-offs. For example, 'kain' (eat) is the root word. Then you have the sequels and prequels: 'kumain' (ate), 'kakain' (will eat), 'kainan' (eating place), 'pagkain' (food). It's the core, the OG, the source of it all.
usage_notes: Isang pangunahing konsepto sa gramatika at morpolohiyang Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **salitang-ugat** ng 'maganda' ay 'ganda'.","translation":"The **root word** of 'maganda' (beautiful) is 'ganda' (beauty)."},{"sentence":"Upang malaman ang kahulugan ng isang salita, mahalagang hanapin muna ang **salitang-ugat** nito.","translation":"To know the meaning of a word, it's important to first find its **root word**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mabilis at biglaang palo, hampas, o hagupit, karaniwang gamit ang isang manipis na bagay tulad ng sinturon o patpat.
original_explanation: The sound and feeling of your nanay's 'walis tingting' making contact with your legs because you were playing outside too long. It's that quick, stinging strike. Parang 'yung sakit 'pag na-seen zone ka—mabilis pero ramdam na ramdam.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb 'humaplit' (to strike) or 'haplitin' (to strike someone/something).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang **haplit** ng sinturon sa kanyang likod.","translation":"He felt the **lash** of the belt on his back."},{"sentence":"Isang **haplit** ng hangin ang dumampi sa kanyang mukha.","translation":"A swift **whip** of the wind touched his face."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pag-imbita o pag-alok sa isang tao na dumalo sa isang pagtitipon, lugar, o okasyon.
etymology: From root `anyaya` (invite). The `pag-` prefix and reduplication of the first vowel `a` create a noun meaning 'the act of inviting'.
original_explanation: The formal "Tara!" or "G!". It's the act of asking someone to come to your party, wedding, or even just for a quick 'kain tayo' session. In the digital age, this is the GC add, the event invite on Facebook, or the "sent you a link" for a Zoom call. It's the prelude to either a great time or a lot of social anxiety.
usage_notes: Can also refer to the invitation itself (the card or message), though "imbitasyon" is more common for that.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming salamat sa iyong **pag-aanyaya** sa kaarawan mo.","translation":"Thank you very much for your **invitation** to your birthday."},{"sentence":"Isang karangalan na tanggapin ang kanilang **pag-aanyaya** na magsalita sa kumperensya.","translation":"It is an honor to accept their **invitation** to speak at the conference."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maliit, lapad, at pilak-kulay na isdang-alat na karaniwang ginagawang paksiw o prito.
original_explanation: The **sapsap** is that humble, everyday fish you see in the palengke. It's not as glamorous as lapu-lapu, but it's a reliable, budget-friendly ulam. Perfect for frying until crispy or simmering in vinegar. The go-to fish when petsa de peligro is near.
usage_notes: A very common table fish in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap iprito hanggang maging malutong ang **sapsap**.","translation":"It's delicious to fry **ponyfish** until it becomes crispy."},{"sentence":"Bumili si Aling Nena ng isang kilong **sapsap** sa palengke para sa pananghalian.","translation":"Aling Nena bought a kilo of **slipmouth** at the market for lunch."}]

translation: to become fixed; to stay permanently
meaning_filipino: Manatili sa isang lugar o kalagayan sa loob ng mahabang panahon; maging permanente o hindi na magbago.
etymology: From ma- (potential/involuntary action prefix) + pirmi (fixed, constant, from Spanish 'firme').
original_explanation: The opposite of a 'nomad'. This is when you finally find a place to settle down, whether it's a job, a home, or a relationship. "After years of job hopping, gusto ko na sanang mapirmi sa isang kumpanya." It's the goal of someone tired of 'ghosting' and wants something stable. From "pirmi," meaning 'fixed' or 'always'.
usage_notes: Can mean to settle down in a location, or for a situation to become fixed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais na niyang **mapirmi** sa probinsya at mamuhay nang simple.","translation":"He wants **to settle permanently** in the province and live a simple life."},{"sentence":"Sana **mapirmi** na ang presyo ng gasolina.","translation":"I hope the price of gasoline **becomes fixed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng balakubak o maliliit at puting kaliskis ng patay na balat sa anit.
original_explanation: The horrifying moment you wear a black shirt and it suddenly looks like a snowy landscape on your shoulders. It means "to get dandruff." The universe's way of telling you to switch shampoos or to stop stressing about your deadlines.
usage_notes: A very specific and commonly understood term related to hair and scalp hygiene.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Madalas siyang **magkabalakubak** kapag mainit ang panahon.","translation":"He often **gets dandruff** when the weather is hot."},{"sentence":"Gumamit ka ng anti-dandruff shampoo para hindi ka **magkabalakubak**.","translation":"Use an anti-dandruff shampoo so you don't **get dandruff**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkaubos nang lubusan; wala nang natira.
original_explanation: It's the 29th of the month and you check your wallet. That empty feeling? That's pagkasaid. It's the state of your data allowance after binge-watching a K-drama series. It's the shampoo bottle you keep adding water to. The state of being totally, completely, utterly ubos.
usage_notes: Often used for resources like money, food, water, or patience. 'Naubos' is more common, but 'nasaid' implies a more thorough and often frustrating depletion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkasaid** ng pondo ang pangunahing problema ng proyekto.","translation":"The **depletion** of funds is the main problem of the project."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa tagtuyot, naramdaman ang **pagkasaid** ng tubig sa mga dam.","translation":"Due to the drought, the **depletion** of water in the dams was felt."}]

translation: to be splashed on; to be spattered with
meaning_filipino: Mabasaan o madumihan dahil sa tumilamsik na likido, putik, o anumang katulad na bagay.
original_explanation: That tragic moment when you're wearing all white and a bus speeds through a puddle next to you. You've been 'matalsikan'. It can also be figurative, like when your friend is in deep drama and some of it splashes onto you. "Ayoko nang madamay, baka **matalsikan** pa ako ng gulo n'yo."
usage_notes: The focus is on the person or object that *receives* the splash.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka at baka ka **matalsikan** ng kumukulong mantika.","translation":"Be careful or you might **be splashed on** by the boiling oil."},{"sentence":"Puti pa naman ang uniporme ko tapos **natalsikan** ako ng putik.","translation":"My uniform was white and then I **was spattered with** mud."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang daanang pampubliko, karaniwang sementado o aspaltado, na ginagamit ng mga sasakyan at tao.
original_explanation: The stage for all Philippine dramas: epic traffic jams, jeepneys packed like a can of sardines, street vendors selling everything from mani to face shields, and the occasional "manong, bayad po." It's where you question your life choices during rush hour and where "5 minutes away" actually means an hour. Welcome to the kalsada life.
usage_notes: A very common word for any paved road, from a small street to a major highway.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa pagtawid sa **kalsada**.","translation":"Be careful when crossing the **road**."},{"sentence":"Ma-traffic na naman sa **kalsada** ng EDSA.","translation":"The EDSA **road** is traffic-jammed again."}]

meaning_filipino: Iniluto sa mainit na mantika; isang pagkaing dumaan sa proseso ng pagpiprito.
etymology: Mula sa salitang hiram sa Espanyol na `frito` (pinirito), na naging `prito` sa Tagalog, at nilagyan ng gitlaping `-in-`.
original_explanation: The adjective describing the glorious state of being fried. `Piniritong` manok, `piniritong` isda, `piniritong` itlog—it's the foundation of the classic Pinoy breakfast, lunch, and dinner. If you can cook it in a sizzling pan of oil, it can be `pinirito`. It's the sound of happiness in a Filipino kitchen.
usage_notes: Functions as a past-tense verb (`Pinirito niya ang isda`) or an adjective (`Kumain ako ng piniritong manok`).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap ang **piniritong** galunggong na may kasamang kamatis at suka.","translation":"The **fried** mackerel scad is delicious with a side of tomatoes and vinegar."},{"sentence":"**Pinirito** ni nanay ang paborito kong longganisa para sa almusal.","translation":"Mom **fried** my favorite longganisa for breakfast."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa isang kalagayan na walang kamalayan sa sarili o sa paligid; hindi gising ang diwa.
original_explanation: This is you after a long night out with friends, or after a particularly brutal BPO night shift. You're physically there, but your brain has logged off. Also describes someone so drunk they passed out. 'Natagpuan siyang natutulog sa sofa *nang walang-malay-tao*.'
usage_notes: Describes a state of unconsciousness, often due to fainting, heavy intoxication, or deep sleep.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natagpuan siyang nakahandusay sa sahig **nang walang-malay-tao**.","translation":"He was found lying on the floor, **unconscious**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mapanirang termino para sa isang politiko na itinuturing na makaluma, tiwali, at inuuna ang pansariling interes kaysa sa kapakanan ng bayan. Ito ay isang portmanteau ng "traditional politician".
etymology: Isang portmanteau o pinagsamang salita mula sa Ingles na "**tra**ditional **po**litician".
original_explanation: Ah, the **trapo**. Not the rag for wiping spills, but the politicians who make you want to wipe them from the ballot. It's a portmanteau of "**tra**ditional **po**litician," but everyone knows it really means the politicians who only show up during elections, have their faces on every lamppost, and whose promises are as disposable as a wet tissue. They are the final bosses of Philippine politics.
usage_notes: Used as a noun to refer to the person (e.g., 'Siya ay isang trapo') or an adjective to describe a style of politics (e.g., 'mga trapo-style na kampanya'). It is always pejorative.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sawa na ang mga tao sa mga **trapo** na walang ginawa kundi mangurakot.","translation":"The people are tired of **traditional politicians** who do nothing but engage in corruption."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang plataporma ay laban sa **trapo** politics.","translation":"His platform is against **traditional, self-serving politics**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na ginagamit upang takpan ang isang butas, sugat, o anumang sira upang ito ay maayos o maprotektahan.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `pan-` (pang-instrumento) + `tapal` (paglalagay ng gamot o takip sa sugat o butas).
original_explanation: Ito yung "band-aid solution" mo sa buhay. May problema? Takpan mo lang muna. Sira 'yung pader? Lagyan mo ng poster. Butas bulsa mo? Stapler lang, katapat niyan. 'Yung puso mong wasak? Ay, 'di kaya ng panapal 'yan, kailangan diyan closure.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa pisikal na pantakip sa butas, gamot sa sugat (poultice), o sa metaporikal na kahulugan bilang isang pansamantalang solusyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng **panapal** na putik sa butas ng bubong.","translation":"He used a mud **patch** on the hole in the roof."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-inom ng alak ay hindi mabisang **panapal** sa kalungkutan.","translation":"Drinking alcohol is not an effective **remedy** for sadness."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na namamahala, nagbabantay, o gumagabay sa gawain ng iba, lalo na sa isang lugar ng trabaho.
original_explanation: The OG spelling before 'supervisor' became more common. This is your boss's boss, or maybe just your direct boss. They're the one who approves your vacation leave, listens to your call recordings in the BPO, and asks 'Kumusta na ang metrics mo?' The reason you can't just watch Netflix all day at work.
usage_notes: This is the Filipinized spelling of the English word 'supervisor', influenced by Spanish pronunciation. 'Supervisor' (the English spelling) is now more common in formal business writing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinausap ako ng aking **superbisor** tungkol sa aking performance.","translation":"My **supervisor** talked to me about my performance."},{"sentence":"Ipapasa ko ang report na ito sa **superbisor** ng aming departamento.","translation":"I will pass this report to the **supervisor** of our department."}]

meaning_filipino: Mapuno o maapawan ng tubig-baha ang isang lugar.
original_explanation: The verb form of every Filipino's rainy season nightmare. When your street turns into a river and you have to cancel all your plans, your area is being '**bahain**'. It's the official reason for 'walang pasok'.
usage_notes: Verb in the object-focus '-in' form. The place being flooded is the focus. Often used in its past tense 'binaha' (was flooded) or present tense 'binabaha' (is being flooded).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tiyak na **babahain** na naman ang kalsada dahil sa malakas na ulan.","translation":"The road will surely **be flooded** again because of the heavy rain."},{"sentence":"Laging **binabaha** ang aming lugar tuwing may bagyo.","translation":"Our area is always **flooded** whenever there's a typhoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Mapili sa pagkain, kasuotan, o sa anumang bagay; hindi basta-basta nasisiyahan.
original_explanation: This is your friend who takes 30 minutes to decide what to order, only to get the same thing they always get. A pihikan person is picky. They have high standards, whether it's for food ('Ayoko niyan, may sibuyas'), friends, or jowa. They're the 'hindi pwede ang pwede na' type of person.
usage_notes: Often used to describe someone's eating habits, but can apply to any choice.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Medyo **pihikan** ang anak ko sa pagkain kaya nahihirapan akong magluto.","translation":"My child is a bit **picky** with food so I have a hard time cooking."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong maging **pihikan** sa pagpili ng manliligaw.","translation":"Don't be too **choosy** when selecting a suitor."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang buwanang pagdaloy ng dugo mula sa matris ng isang babae na hindi buntis.
original_explanation: The monthly 'dalaw' (visitor) that arrives uninvited, makes you crave chocolate and junk food, and makes you want to curl up with a hot compress (or 'paso'). The official reason for a sudden 'pagsusungit' and the frantic 'Penge napkin!' moments.
usage_notes: Often used with euphemisms like 'dalaw,' 'meron,' or 'period'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masakit ang puson niya dahil sa kanyang **regla**.","translation":"She has abdominal cramps because of her **menstruation**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbaba o pagyuko sa gitnang bahagi ng isang bagay dahil sa bigat o kakulangan ng suporta.
original_explanation: The sad curve of your shoulders after a 12-hour shift. The dip in the middle of an old mattress. The 'sampayan' (clothesline) heavy with wet laundry. That's lundo. It's the physical manifestation of being weighed down, whether by gravity or the burdens of life, charot.
usage_notes: Can describe a physical sag or be used metaphorically for a dip in spirits or energy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **lundo** na sa gitna ang lumang kama.","translation":"The old bed already has a **sag** in the middle."},{"sentence":"Nawala ang **lundo** ng sampayan nang maalis ang mga basang damit.","translation":"The **droop** of the clothesline disappeared when the wet clothes were removed."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng may kapangyarihang mahiwaga o supernatural, karaniwang naninirahan sa mga kagubatan, ilog, o bundok at itinuturing na tagapangalaga ng kalikasan.
original_explanation: The original OG diwata. She's the magical girlboss of the forest who might give you a blessing or curse you for throwing your trash anywhere. Think Maria Makiling, but maybe with a more mysterious, less mainstream vibe. She's not your Disney princess; she's the queen of her own mystical domain.
usage_notes: Often used in folklore and mythology. The feminine form of 'enkantado'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayon sa alamat, isang magandang **enkantada** ang nagbabantay sa talon.","translation":"According to legend, a beautiful **enchantress** guards the waterfall."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-iingay sa gubat at baka magalit ang mga **enkantada**.","translation":"Don't be noisy in the forest, you might anger the **enchantresses**."}]

meaning_filipino: Pakintabin ang isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pagkuskos, karaniwang may kasamang pampakintab na materyal.
original_explanation: A very modern, likely BPO or office slang, for "to polish" something. "Uy, paki-isapol naman nitong report ko, i-check mo grammar bago ko isubmit." It's taking something rough and making it shine, whether it's a shoe, a presentation, or your English accent.
usage_notes: This is a neologism or slang and not standard Filipino. Its usage is confined to specific, modern contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Isinapol** niya ang sapatos hanggang sa kumintab.","translation":"He **polished** the shoes until they shone."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **isapol** ang presentasyon bago ipakita sa kliyente.","translation":"We need to **polish** the presentation before showing it to the client."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking mahilig gumawa o magkalat ng tsismis.
original_explanation: The male counterpart to the tsimosa. He's often found at the kanto (street corner) sari-sari store, holding court and delivering the 'balita' (news) with the same enthusiasm as a news anchor. Proof that gossip isn't just for the girls.
usage_notes: A derogatory term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang barbero ay naging **tsimoso** at ikinalat ang sikreto ng customer niya.","translation":"The barber became a **gossiper** and spread his customer's secret."},{"sentence":"Akala mo mga babae lang, pero ang dami ring **tsimoso** sa opisina.","translation":"You'd think it's only women, but there are also a lot of **male gossipers** in the office."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng ibon (Oriolus chinensis) na may katamtamang laki, na kilala sa matingkad na dilaw at itim na balahibo at magandang huni. Tinatawag ding kilyawan.
original_explanation: Ito yung ibon na mukhang naka-highlighter. Sobrang dilaw, tapos may itim na accent. Sila yung mga original na 'golden voice' ng kagubatan. Kung may 'The Voice: Birds Edition', baka sila ang laging champion.
usage_notes: Isang partikular na pangalan ng ibon, hindi gaanong karaniwan sa pang-araw-araw na usapan maliban kung tungkol sa kalikasan o ornitolohiya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakita ako ng isang magandang **salindayaw** na dumapo sa puno ng mangga.","translation":"I saw a beautiful **oriole** perch on the mango tree."},{"sentence":"Ang huni ng **salindayaw** ay kaaya-ayang pakinggan sa umaga.","translation":"The song of the **oriole** is pleasant to hear in the morning."}]

translation: to place over fire; to expose to heat; to put on the spot
meaning_filipino: Ilagay ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay pagkain, sa ibabaw ng apoy o init upang maluto. Sa matalinhagang paraan, ilagay sa isang mahirap na sitwasyon.
original_explanation: This is what your mom does to the kawali before frying the hotdog. It's also what your boss does to you during a meeting when they ask, 'Any questions?' and then immediately call your name. 'Isinalang ako sa hot seat!'
usage_notes: Can be literal (cooking) or figurative (putting someone in a difficult situation).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Isalang** mo na ang sinaing para makakain na tayo.","translation":"**Place** the rice **over the heat** so we can eat already."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **isalang** sa harap ng mga magulang mo, hindi ako handa.","translation":"Don't **put me on the spot** in front of your parents, I'm not ready."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o paghikayat sa isang tao na magsagawa ng pagsasanay o pag-eensayo.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung trabaho ng dance coach, choir master, o nanay mo bago ka sumali sa declamation contest. 'Sige, **papag-insayuhin** kita hanggang ma-perfect mo 'yan!' It's forcing someone to do drills until they get it right.
usage_notes: A causative verb related to training or rehearsal. 'Insayo' itself is less common now than 'praktis' or 'ensayo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **papag-insayuhin** ang mga bagong miyembro ng banda.","translation":"You need to **make** the new band members **rehearse**."},{"sentence":"Sila ay pinapunta sa training camp upang sila ay **papag-insayuhin** nang husto.","translation":"They were sent to a training camp to be **made to practice** thoroughly."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging masungit; isang estado ng pagiging magagalitin, madaling mainis, o hindi palangiti.
etymology: From ka- + sungit (grumpy, surly) + -an (state or quality of).
original_explanation: The 'RBF' (Resting B*tch Face) in noun form. 'Yung aura ng terror prof mo, o 'yung mood ng nanay mo 'pag hindi ka pa naghuhugas ng plato. It's that vibe of 'don't talk to me' before they've even said anything. The reason why you hesitate to ask the tindera at the sari-sari store if you can pay with GCash.
usage_notes: Refers to the quality or state of being grumpy, not the grumpy person themselves (who would be 'masungit').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko maintindihan ang **kasungitan** niya tuwing umaga.","translation":"I can't understand his **grumpiness** every morning."},{"sentence":"Nawala ang **kasungitan** sa kanyang mukha nang makita niya ang mga bulaklak.","translation":"The **surliness** on her face disappeared when she saw the flowers."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagtataglay ng matatag na pasya o determinasyon na gawin ang isang bagay; buo na ang loob.
original_explanation: When you've made up your mind and no amount of 'weh, 'di nga?' from your friends can change it. You're desidido to go on that diet (starting tomorrow, probably). You're desidido to resign from your job (after you find a new one). It's that firm 'Game!' feeling before you do something major.
usage_notes: Bagaman may anyong pambabae na 'desidida', karaniwang 'desidido' na ang ginagamit para sa lahat ng kasarian sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Desidido** na siyang mag-aral sa ibang bansa kahit tutol ang kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"He is **determined** to study abroad even if his parents are against it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang koleksyon ng nilalaman, tulad ng mga post sa social media o balita, na maingat na pinili at inayos para sa isang partikular na manonood o layunin.
original_explanation: Your social media feed when you've meticulously blocked your toxic titas, unfollowed annoying exes, and muted all political rants. What's left is pure, unadulterated content you actually want to see—mostly cats and food pics. It's your digital zen garden.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of social media (Instagram, TikTok, Facebook) and content platforms.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng **curated feed** mo sa Instagram, puro travel photos!","translation":"Your **curated feed** on Instagram is beautiful, it's all travel photos!"},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan kong ayusin ang aking **curated feed** para mas maging positibo ang mga nakikita ko.","translation":"I'm trying to fix my **curated feed** so I see more positive things."}]

translation: to be able to adapt; to be able to fit something in
meaning_filipino: Magawang iakma, ibagay, o ilapat ang isang bagay sa isa pa, o sa isang partikular na sitwasyon.
etymology: From the root 'agpang', meaning 'to fit' or 'to adapt'. The 'ma-i-' prefix denotes ability.
original_explanation: This is the skill you use when your client suddenly has a 'small' revision with a big impact. You need to **maiagpang** the new design into the old layout. It's also trying to fit your oversized luggage into a GrabCar's tiny trunk. It's about making things fit, whether it's a schedule, a budget, or a physical object.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of adjusting, fitting, or adapting something to a new situation or constraint.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinusubukan ng karpintero na **maiagpang** ang pinto sa hindi pantay na hamba.","translation":"The carpenter is trying to **fit** the door into the uneven frame."},{"sentence":"Sana ay **maiagpang** natin ang ating badyet sa biglaang pagtaas ng presyo.","translation":"I hope we can **adapt** our budget to the sudden price increase."}]

translation: act of hissing at each other; group whispering/hissing
meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay o palitan ng pagsitsit ng dalawa o higit pang tao, karaniwan upang magbulungan o magtawag ng pansin nang hindi hayagan.
etymology: pag- + si- + sitsit + -an. The -an suffix here implies a reciprocal or group action.
original_explanation: This is the sound of 'chismis' brewing. It's when a group of 'Marites' huddle together and start making that "psst... psst..." sound to share the latest tea. It's the human equivalent of a snake convention. It can be to call someone's attention secretly, or more often, to talk about someone who's just within earshot.
usage_notes: Implies a group activity, where multiple people are hissing or whispering.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **pagsisitsitan** ng mga babae nang dumaan ako.","translation":"I heard the women's **group hissing/whispering** when I passed by."},{"sentence":"Itigil niyo na 'yang **pagsisitsitan** at magsalita kayo nang maayos.","translation":"Stop that **mutual hissing** and speak properly."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapalaganap o pamamahagi ng isang bagay sa malawak na lugar o sa maraming tao, tulad ng impormasyon, sakit, o gamit.
etymology: From pag- (gerund prefix) + papaka- (causative prefix) + kalat (scattered, mess). 'The act of causing something to be scattered'.
original_explanation: This is the official sport of Marites. It's the spreading of anything from chismis (gossip) to a new meme, or even just your laundry all over the living room. In the digital age, hitting 'share' is the ultimate act of pagpapakalat.
usage_notes: Can be neutral (spreading information), negative (spreading rumors, disease), or literal (spreading things around).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapakalat** ng maling impormasyon ay isang seryosong problema sa social media.","translation":"The **spreading** of false information is a serious problem on social media."},{"sentence":"Inutusan niya ang mga bata na itigil ang **pagpapakalat** ng kanilang mga laruan sa sahig.","translation":"She ordered the children to stop **spreading** their toys on the floor."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kilusan ng pagtutol o paghihimagsik; isang rebelyon o pag-aaklas.
original_explanation: When you've had enough of your micromanaging boss and the whole team decides to file a group resignation—that's an 'alsa'. It's the noun form of revolting. From the historical 'Pag-aalsa ni Dagohoy' to a simple 'alsa-balutan' (packing up and leaving abruptly), it's the result of reaching your breaking point.
usage_notes: Karaniwang tumutukoy sa isang malawakang pag-aaklas o rebelyon. Madalas itong gamitin sa anyong 'pag-aalsa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **alsa** ng mga manggagawa ay humihingi ng mas mataas na sahod.","translation":"The workers' **uprising** demands higher wages."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan sa kasaysayan ang iba't ibang **pag-aalsa** sa Pilipinas.","translation":"Various **revolts** in the Philippines are studied in history."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang uri ng sasakyan na ginagamit sa paglalakbay sa ibabaw ng dagat, ilog, o lawa.
original_explanation: Anything that floats and gets you across water. From the humble bangka that takes you island hopping in El Nido, to the RORO ferry that carries buses and your 'pasalubong', to the massive container ships at the port. If it's on water and it moves people or things, it's a 'sasakyang-dagat'.
usage_notes: A general term covering all forms of water transportation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **sasakyang-dagat** ang nakadaong sa pantalan.","translation":"Many **sea vessels** are docked at the port."},{"sentence":"Ang barko ay isang malaking uri ng **sasakyang-dagat**.","translation":"A ship is a large type of **watercraft**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang nag-uutos o naglalarawan ng pag-usad o paggalaw patungo sa unahan.
original_explanation: What the jeepney barker shouts to the driver when it's time to go. 'Abante! Puno na!' It's the opposite of 'atras' (reverse). Can also be used figuratively, like when you're telling your friend to move on from their ex. 'Girl, abante na, 2026 na!'
usage_notes: Can be used as a command (verb-like) or as a description of movement (adverb). It is also the name of a popular tabloid.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumigaw ang konduktor, '**Abante** na!'","translation":"The conductor shouted, 'Move **forward** now!'"},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating mag-isip ng mga paraan para umabante ang ating proyekto.","translation":"We need to think of ways for our project to move **forward**."}]

meaning_filipino: Mayroong natatanging bigat, silbi, o kabuluhan; lubhang pinahahalagahan.
original_explanation: How you describe your SSS number, your phone's charger, or that last piece of Chickenjoy. It's something you absolutely cannot lose, or you'll have a life crisis. 'Napakamahalaga ng a-attend-an kong meeting, andoon si crush.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang edukasyon ay isang **napakamahalaga** na pamana na hindi mananakaw ninuman.","translation":"Education is a **very valuable** inheritance that no one can steal."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis at hindi makontrol na paggalaw o pagyanig ng katawan o bahagi nito, dulot ng takot, kaba, galit, o ginaw.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your hands when you're about to present your thesis, or when you're holding a cup of coffee after pulling an all-nighter. It's your body's physical reaction to extreme emotions like fear ('nginig sa takot'), excitement, or just too much caffeine. More general than 'ngiki' which is usually from cold/fever.
usage_notes: A general term for shaking or trembling, which can be caused by various factors like cold, fear, nervousness, or anger.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halata ang **nginig** sa kanyang boses habang nagsasalita sa harap ng maraming tao.","translation":"The **trembling** in her voice was obvious while speaking in front of many people."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya mapigilan ang **nginig** ng kanyang mga kamay dahil sa matinding kaba.","translation":"She couldn't stop the **shaking** of her hands due to extreme nervousness."}]

meaning_filipino: Paulit-ulit at mabilis na pagtibok ng puso, karaniwang sanhi ng kaba, pagod, o pananabik.
original_explanation: This is the upgraded version of 'sumikdo'. It's not just one beat; it's a series of them, like your heart is doing the cha-cha. It's what happens when you're waiting for that 'We need to talk' text to be followed up, or after running to catch the last MRT train. Continuous kaba.
usage_notes: The repetition of 'sikdo' indicates a continuous or repeated action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumisikdu-sikdo** ang dibdib ng manlalaro habang hinihintay ang huling busina.","translation":"The player's chest was **palpitating** as he waited for the final buzzer."},{"sentence":"Pagod na pagod siya kaya **sumikdu-sikdo** ang kanyang puso.","translation":"He was so tired that his heart **throbbed repeatedly**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglabas mula sa sinapupunan; ang pagsilang ng isang sanggol.
etymology: From 'luwal' (exterior, outside), referring to coming out into the world. The '-um-' infix indicates a verb.
original_explanation: This is the OG "coming out" story. The ultimate grand entrance. It's the verb for being born, for making your world debut. Before your first cry, first steps, or first IG post, you first had to lumuwal. It’s the most dramatic and profound exit from a nine-month staycation.
usage_notes: A more formal or literary term for "to be born" compared to the more common 'ipinanganak'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Noong ika-19 ng Hunyo 1861 **lumuwal** sa Calamba, Laguna, ang pambansang bayani.","translation":"On June 19, 1861, the national hero **was born** in Calamba, Laguna."},{"sentence":"Ligtas na **lumuwal** ang malusog na sanggol na lalaki.","translation":"The healthy baby boy **emerged** safely."}]

translation: to walk to a destination; to process something (an errand)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtahak o pagpunta sa isang tiyak na lugar sa pamamagitan ng paglalakad. Sa metaporikal na gamit, ito ay ang pagsasagawa o pag-aasikaso ng isang gawain o transaksyon.
original_explanation: Has two major vibes. First, literally walking to a specific place: "Lakarin mo na lang 'yan, isang kanto lang naman." The second, and more common adulting version, is to run an errand or process documents. "Kailangan kong lakarin ang business permit ko sa city hall." It's the ultimate 'asikaso' verb.
usage_notes: Ang ikalawang kahulugan (i-proseso/asikasuhin ang isang gawain) ay napakakaraniwan sa mga kontekstong burukratiko o opisyal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahaba ang pila, pero kailangan kong **lakarin** ang pagkuha ng NBI clearance.","translation":"The line is long, but I need to **process** my NBI clearance application."},{"sentence":"Mula dito, kaya mong **lakarin** ang simbahan sa loob ng sampung minuto.","translation":"From here, you can **walk to** the church in ten minutes."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang unang iyak o sigaw ng isang bagong silang na sanggol.
original_explanation: It's the official sound that says, "Hello, world! Ready or not, here I come with my cuteness and my bills!" It’s the cry that makes every new parent's heart melt and their wallets weep simultaneously.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to the cry of a newborn.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nang marinig nila ang unang **uha** ng sanggol, napaiyak sa tuwa ang mag-asawa.","translation":"When they heard the baby's first **cry**, the couple cried with joy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng maraming maliliit na batik o marka sa balat, karaniwang dulot ng pagkabilad sa araw.
original_explanation: When the sun decides to play connect-the-dots on your face. It's that 'I've been to the beach' look without the expensive resort bill. Some people pay to have this, others get it for free from walking to the sari-sari store.
usage_notes: Describes a person's skin, particularly the face.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **mapekas** ang kanyang ilong matapos ang bakasyon sa dagat.","translation":"Her nose became **freckled** after the vacation at the sea."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya itinatago ang kanyang **mapekas** na mukha.","translation":"She doesn't hide her **freckled** face."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbaba ng ulo o pagbaluktot ng katawan pauna, kadalasan bilang tanda ng paggalang o upang abutin ang isang bagay na mababa.
original_explanation: The everyday action of bowing. This is what you do when you pass in front of older people talking ("Excuse me po, makikiraan lang po"). It's also the action you do when you drop your phone and have to pick it up under a table. A gesture of both respect and practicality.
usage_notes: Ang ugat na 'yuko' ay nagiging pandiwa sa pamamagitan ng mga panlapi, tulad ng 'yumuko' (aspektong perpektibo/pangnakaraan) at 'yuyuko' (aspektong kontemplatibo/panghinaharap).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Yumuko** siya upang pulutin ang nahulog na barya.","translation":"He **stooped** to pick up the dropped coin."},{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **yumuko** bilang paggalang sa mga nakatatanda.","translation":"Don't forget to **bow** as a sign of respect to elders."}]

translation: to guide by the hand; to lead
meaning_filipino: Ang paggabay sa isang tao sa paglalakad sa pamamagitan ng paghawak sa kamay o braso, karaniwan upang tulungan ang bata, matanda, o may kapansanan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'akay' (to lead by hand) at unlaping '-um-'.
original_explanation: This is what you do for your lola when she's crossing a busy street. It's holding a toddler's hand so they don't run off in the mall. Metaphorically, it's what a good mentor does for you in your career—guiding you, but not carrying you. 'Sana all may umakay sa landas ng tagumpay.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **umakay** sa bulag na matanda patawid ng kalsada.","translation":"He was the one who **guided** the blind old man across the road."},{"sentence":"Ang ina ang dapat **umakay** sa kanyang mga anak sa tamang landas.","translation":"The mother should be the one **to lead** her children on the right path."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panloob na pagnanais, hilig, o kusa ng isang tao.
original_explanation: This is your inner "gusto." The vibe your spirit is giving off. Kung may **dakong loob** kang gawin ang isang bagay, it means you're genuinely willing and motivated to do it, walang pilitan. Parang 'yung desisyon mong mag-order ng milk tea—'yan ay purong **dakong loob**, walang pumilit sa'yo.
usage_notes: A compound term literally meaning "direction of one's inner self." It's a deep concept related to will and voluntariness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Walang sinuman ang makakapigil sa kanya kung iyon ang kanyang **dakong loob**.","translation":"No one can stop him if that is his **inclination**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng ugnayan kung saan ang isang tao ay nakararamdam ng matinding takot sa pag-abandona at labis na nangangailangan ng pagpapatunay at paglalambing mula sa kanyang kapareha.
original_explanation: Ito yung attachment style na laging nagtatanong ng "Mahal mo pa ba ako?" every 5 minutes. Yung tipong kailangan ng constant reassurance para maniwala na hindi sila iiwan. Sila yung mabilis mag-reply, mabilis mag-overthink, at laging nag-iisip, "Galit ka ba?" kapag "K." lang ang reply mo. Trending 'to sa TikTok psychology.
usage_notes: Isang terminong teknikal mula sa 'attachment theory' sa sikolohiya na naging popular sa usapang pang-relasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan niya ang kanyang **anxious attachment** style sa therapy.","translation":"She is working on her **anxious attachment** style in therapy."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **anxious attachment**, kailangan niya ng palagiang komunikasyon sa kanyang partner.","translation":"Because of his **anxious attachment**, he needs constant communication with his partner."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-utos o paghiling sa isang tao na magtungo o pumunta sa kinaroroonan ng nagsasalita.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping pangkauusalan na "pa-" at sa salitang "parito" (pumunta rito).
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "boss" move. It’s not just asking someone to come, it's *causing* them to come. Think of a CEO summoning an employee, or your lola telling you to come to the living room *right now*. It has a stronger sense of authority than just saying "halika dito".
usage_notes: Ang "paparituhin" ay ang anyong pangkauusalan ng "parito". Ang mas karaniwang kasingkahulugan nito ay "papunahin".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Paparituhin** mo ang lahat ng miyembro para sa isang mahalagang anunsyo.","translation":"**Have** all the members **come here** for an important announcement."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **paparituhin** ang mekaniko para ayusin ang kotse.","translation":"I need to **have the mechanic come here** to fix the car."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng puno o palumpong na karaniwang matatagpuan sa mga baybaying-dagat, na may malalapad na dahon at malalaking dilaw na bulaklak.
original_explanation: Ito yung puno na madalas mong makita sa beach, na parang ayaw magpa-araw. Yung mga dahon niya, hugis puso. Hindi siya kasing sikat ng Narra or Acacia, pero mahalaga siya sa coastal ecosystem. Marami ring lugar sa Pilipinas na ipinangalan sa punong ito, like Balibago, Angeles City. Parang low-key but important.
usage_notes: Also a common place name in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May malaking puno ng **balibago** sa tabi ng aming bahay sa probinsya.","translation":"There is a big **sea hibiscus** tree beside our house in the province."},{"sentence":"Ang mga hibla mula sa **balibago** ay ginagamit sa paggawa ng lubid.","translation":"The fibers from the **sea hibiscus** are used in making rope."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng pag-iral na pabago-bago; minsan ay nakikita o naroroon, at minsan ay nawawala.
etymology: A compound word from 'lubog' (to sink) and 'litaw' (to surface).
original_explanation: The official term for your internet connection during a typhoon. It's your 'friend' who only shows up when they need something. It's that on-again, off-again relationship status. One moment they're there (litaw), the next they're gone (lubog). The ultimate 'seen-zone' state of being.
usage_notes: Describes anything that is inconsistent or not constant.
