original_explanation: This is another way to say "eastern," but it feels a bit more poetic or descriptive than just saying "sa silangan." It's like the difference between "the eastern wind" and "the wind from the east." The first one, `hanging silanganin`, just sounds more dramatic.
usage_notes: Often used to describe winds ('hanging silanganin'), areas, or things located in the east.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman namin ang malamig na hanging **silanganin**.","translation":"We felt the cold **eastern** wind."},{"sentence":"Ang mga lalawigang **silanganin** ay madalas daanan ng bagyo.","translation":"The **eastern** provinces are often in the path of typhoons."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang dulo, katapusan, o guhit na nagtatakda ng saklaw ng isang bagay, lugar, o konsepto.
original_explanation: This is the 'hanggang dito na lang tayo' line. It's the boundary, whether it's the edge of your property, the end of the month before sweldo, or the emotional wall you put up when someone starts asking 'may aaminin ka ba?'. It’s the finish line you're desperate to cross during a marathon, or the end of the free data promo.
usage_notes: Often used to refer to physical borders (e.g., of a country) or abstract limits (e.g., of patience).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pasensya ko ay may **hangganan**.","translation":"My patience has a **limit**."},{"sentence":"Nakarating sila sa **hangganan** ng bayan bago gumabi.","translation":"They reached the town **border** before nightfall."},{"sentence":"Walang **hangganan** ang pagmamahal ng isang ina.","translation":"A mother's love has no **limit**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manipis na piraso ng metal, tulad ng yero. Maaari din itong tumukoy sa isang plaka na ginagamit sa pag-imprenta o isang tsapa na nagpapakita ng awtoridad o pagkakakilanlan.
original_explanation: That metal sheet your tito uses to patch the roof. Or the thing they used to print old newspapers. In street slang, it can also mean a police badge. 'May chapa 'yan' means 'That person is a cop/has authority.' It's a word with a very industrial, old-school feel.
usage_notes: Has multiple related meanings all stemming from a flat piece of metal. The specific meaning is derived from context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating palitan ang **chapa** ng bubong bago dumating ang tag-ulan.","translation":"We need to replace the metal **sheet** of the roof before the rainy season arrives."},{"sentence":"Ipinakita ng pulis ang kanyang **chapa** bago pumasok sa gusali.","translation":"The police officer showed his **badge** before entering the building."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na pagpili o pagtatalaga sa isang tao para sa isang posisyon, tungkulin, o karangalan.
original_explanation: This is what the boss does when they choose the new team lead (sana all!). It's the official "you're the one" in a corporate or political setting. Parang sa pageant, when they **humirang** ng Miss Universe. It’s a very formal way of saying "Ikaw na."
usage_notes: A formal term used in official contexts like government, organizations, and ceremonies.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pangulo ay **humirang** ng bagong kalihim para sa kagawaran.","translation":"The president **appointed** a new secretary for the department."},{"sentence":"**Humirang** ang komite ng tatlong mananalo para sa patimpalak.","translation":"The committee **designated** three winners for the contest."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang porma, hugis, o kalagayan na hindi katulad ng dati o ng karaniwan.
original_explanation: This is the glow-up, the transformation, the "Power Rangers, morph!" moment. It's when your quiet officemate suddenly becomes a rockstar on weekends. Or when a caterpillar becomes a butterfly. It's the "before and after" picture, but in two words. It can also refer to something taking on a new state, like water turning to ice.
usage_notes: A common phrase used to describe transformation or a change in state or appearance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpakita ang halimaw sa kanyang tunay at **ibang anyo**.","translation":"The monster showed its true and **different form**."},{"sentence":"Ang tubig ay maaaring magkaroon ng **ibang anyo**, tulad ng yelo o singaw.","translation":"Water can take on a **different form**, like ice or steam."}]

translation: to be able to get a signature on
meaning_filipino: Magawa na lagdaan ng isang tao ang isang dokumento.
etymology: From ma- (ability) + pa- (causative) + pirma (signature, from Spanish 'firma') + -han (locative/object focus).
original_explanation: The ultimate goal of every BPO agent closing a sale or anyone dealing with government offices. 'Sir, isang pirma na lang po.' It's the thrilling quest to get that autograph on a contract, a clearance form, or a parent's excuse letter. The final boss of bureaucracy.
usage_notes: 'To be able to cause a signature to be put on something.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **mapapirmahan** itong clearance sa lahat ng department heads.","translation":"I need **to get** this clearance **signed** by all the department heads."},{"sentence":"Sana **mapapirmahan** ko si Mayor para sa ating proyekto.","translation":"I hope I'll be **able to get** the Mayor **to sign** for our project."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa sentido ng ulo (bahagi sa gilid ng noo) o sa kakayahang makaramdam o umunawa; katinuan.
original_explanation: 'Pag sobrang stress mo sa work at sa lovelife, 'yung part ng ulo mo sa gilid ng mata na pumipintig? 'Yan ang sintido. Pwede ring "sense" or "logic," 'yung bagay na nawawala sa'yo 'pag nakita mo ang 11.11 sale. "Wala ka na ba sa iyong sintido?"
usage_notes: Can refer to both the physical temple of the head and the abstract concept of sense or consciousness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masakit ang **sintido** ko dahil sa puyat.","translation":"My **temples** hurt because of lack of sleep."},{"sentence":"Nawala siya sa kanyang **sintido** nang malaman ang balita.","translation":"He lost his **senses** when he heard the news."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng mapang-abuso o mapagsamantala sa kapwa.
original_explanation: The noun version of 'abusada'. She's the final boss Karen. The one who will ask to speak to the manager over a minor inconvenience. She's the 'kontrabida' in the teleserye everyone loves to hate.
usage_notes: Noun form for a female who is habitually abusive.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinawag siyang **abusera** ng mga kapitbahay dahil sa palagi niyang pagwawala.","translation":"The neighbors called her an **abusive woman** because of her frequent tantrums."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapakita ng kagalakan o libangan sa pamamagitan ng tunog at ekspresyon ng mukha; ang paghalakhak.
original_explanation: The best medicine, daw. It's that sound you make when you see a funny meme, hear your tita's corny joke, or watch a stand-up comedian. From a slight chuckle ('pfft') to a full-blown 'halakhak' that makes your stomach hurt, it's all a form of pagtawa. It's the sound of 'HA-HA-HA-sana-all'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko mapigilan ang aking **pagtawa** sa kanyang biro.","translation":"I couldn't stop my **laughter** at his joke."},{"sentence":"Ang malakas na **pagtawa** ay umalingawngaw sa buong silid.","translation":"Loud **laughter** echoed throughout the room."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking estruktura na may bubong at mga pader, tulad ng isang bahay, opisina, o paaralan, na itinayo para sa iba't ibang layunin.
original_explanation: Any big building. Your office in BGC, the mall where you hang out, your condo unit, or that creepy abandoned building you and your friends dared each other to enter. If it has multiple floors and makes you feel small, it's a 'gusali.'
usage_notes: A general term for any large, permanent structure.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang BPO company na pinagtatrabahuhan ko ay nasa isang mataas na **gusali** sa Makati.","translation":"The BPO company I work for is in a tall **building** in Makati."},{"sentence":"Luma na ang **gusali** ng aming paaralan ngunit matibay pa rin.","translation":"Our school **building** is old but still sturdy."}]

translation: to meet someone upon arrival; to welcome with
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtatagpo o pagtanggap sa isang taong dumarating. Maaari ring tumukoy sa bagay na inihahandog o ipinapakita sa pagsalubong.
original_explanation: That feeling when you see your family at the airport holding a 'Welcome Home!' sign after your 5-year OFW contract. 'Yan ang 'pag-isalubong'. It can also refer to what you're met WITH. Your mom might 'isalubong' you with a slipper for coming home late, or your manager might 'isalubong' you with a pile of new tasks on a Monday morning.
usage_notes: When using 'isalubong', the focus is on the thing being used to welcome, or the action of welcoming itself. Compare with 'salubungin', which focuses on the person being welcomed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **isinalubong** niya sa mga bisita ay isang masayang ngiti.","translation":"What she **welcomed** the visitors with was a happy smile."},{"sentence":"Tuwing Pasko, maligaya niyang **isinasalubong** ang mga balikbayan.","translation":"Every Christmas, he happily **welcomes** the returning Filipinos."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng sawsawan na kulay kayumanggi, maalat, at gawa sa isda na binuro sa asin sa loob ng mahabang panahon.
etymology: From Malay 'petis', which refers to a thick shrimp or fish paste.
original_explanation: The liquid soulmate of calamansi. It's the salty, funky, umami bomb that levels up everything from tinolang manok to fried fish. It's the one condiment whose smell will either make you hungry or make your non-Filipino friends ask if something died in your kitchen.
usage_notes: A staple condiment in Filipino cuisine, used for both cooking and as a dipping sauce (sawsawan).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas sumarap ang manok na tinola dahil sa isang kutsarang **patis**.","translation":"The chicken tinola became more delicious because of a spoonful of **fish sauce**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matinding damdamin ng pag-ayaw, pagkasuklam, o pagkasuya sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na 'di mo ma-explain pero 'di mo talaga feel 'yung isang tao. 'Yung tipong pagpasok pa lang niya sa kwarto, gusto mo na mag-log out sa buhay. It's a low-key, deep-seated "I don't like you," and you don't even need a reason. Basta, bad vibes.
usage_notes: Ang "antipatya" ay isang karaniwang baryant sa pagbaybay at pagbigkas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroong **antipatiya** sa pagitan ng dalawang magkaribal sa pulitika.","translation":"There is **antipathy** between the two political rivals."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tao o lahi na pinagmulan ng isang katangian, ari-arian, o kaugalian na naipasa sa mga sumunod na henerasyon sa pamamagitan ng herencia.
original_explanation: The answer to the national question at every family reunion: 'Kanino ka ba nagmana?' This word is the 'who' in that question. It's the reason why you have your tita's nose, your lolo's temper, or your nanay's talent in cooking. Your genetic (and sometimes financial) benefactor or culprit.
usage_notes: Refers to the source from which something (a trait, property, or skill) was inherited.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malinaw na ang lola niya ang kanyang **pinagmanahan** ng talento sa pag-awit.","translation":"It is clear that her grandmother is the **source of her inherited** singing talent."},{"sentence":"Sino kaya ang **pinagmanahan** niya ng ugali niyang iyan?","translation":"I wonder from whom he **inherited** that attitude of his?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kabuuang sukat sa paligid ng isang bilog o anumang espasyo; ang gilid o hangganan ng isang lugar.
original_explanation: Before Waze told you to 'turn right,' your lolo would tell you to go around the **libid** of the plaza. It means the whole way 'round, the perimeter. It’s that feeling of taking the scenic route, circling the entire subdivision just to avoid one traffic light.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb root 'libirin' (to go around). Not to be confused with 'libido'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinukat nila ang **libid** ng buong lawa.","translation":"They measured the **circumference** of the entire lake."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa paglalakad sa **libid** ng bangin.","translation":"Be careful when walking on the **periphery** of the cliff."}]

meaning_filipino: Iguhit o ilikha ang isang imahen o larawan sa isang ibabaw gamit ang pintura; maaari ring tumukoy sa masining na paglalarawan gamit ang mga salita.
original_explanation: Literally, to paint a picture. But also, it's how you describe something vividly. 'Friend, **ipinta** mo nga sa'kin ang itsura niya nung nalaman niyang may bago ka na.' You're asking them to paint a picture with words, to give you all the juicy details.
usage_notes: Often implies artistic creation ('ipinta ang isang tanawin') or vivid description, as opposed to 'ipintura' which is more about the physical act of applying paint.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **ipinta** ang magandang tanawin mula sa aming bintana.","translation":"I want **to paint** the beautiful view from our window."},{"sentence":"Subukan mong **ipinta** sa iyong isipan ang isang mapayapang lugar.","translation":"Try **to paint** a peaceful place in your mind."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lipas nang format ng magnetic videotape para sa pag-record at pag-playback ng analog na video at audio, na popular noong dekada '70 at '80.
original_explanation: The original Netflix-and-chill device for your parents. It fought a war with VHS and lost, becoming the ultimate 'hugot' story of tech formats. Now it's just a dusty relic in the attic that reminds you of a time before streaming.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa isang laos na teknolohiya. Madalas gamitin upang tukuyin ang isang bagay na luma o hindi na uso.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May koleksyon pa ng mga pelikula sa **Betamax** ang tatay ko.","translation":"My father still has a collection of movies on **Betamax**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang damdamin ng pangamba o pag-aalala na dulot ng panganib, sakit, o banta. Bilang pang-uri, ito ay naglalarawan sa isang tao na nakakaramdam nito.
original_explanation: The feeling you get when your phone is at 1% and there's no charger in sight. Or when your boss messages you "Can we talk?" with no context. Or when it's 3 AM and you hear a noise but you live alone. "Takot ako sa multo, pero mas takot akong ma-seen-zone."
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pangngalan ("ang takot ko" - my fear) o pang-uri ("takot ako" - I am afraid).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nangingibabaw ang **takot** niya sa dilim.","translation":"His **fear** of the dark is overwhelming."},{"sentence":"**Takot** siyang mag-isa sa bahay.","translation":"She is **afraid** to be alone in the house."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginagamit upang ipahayag ang mas mataas na antas o kantidad; lampas sa isang tiyak na bilang, sukat, o pamantayan.
etymology: From Proto-Philippine *higət (tight, taut). The meaning shifted to 'exceeding' or 'more'.
original_explanation: The word that fuels all competition, from school honors to office promotions. "Mas higit ang effort niya." (His effort is greater.) It's the +1 in life. It's what you want your salary to be, what you want your vacation days to be, and what you tell your friend when they ask if you like their new partner more than the ex. It's the ultimate upgrade word.
usage_notes: Often used in comparative phrases, like 'higit na' (more) or 'higit sa' (more than).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para sa akin, **higit** na mahalaga ang kalusugan kaysa kayamanan.","translation":"For me, health is **more** important than wealth."},{"sentence":"Ang bilang ng mga dumalo ay **higit** sa isang daan.","translation":"The number of attendees was **greater** than one hundred."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagyuko o pagbaluktot ng katawan, partikular ng likod; pagiging kuba.
original_explanation: This is Lolo's posture after years of hard work, or your posture after 8 hours hunched over a laptop answering emails. It’s that curve in your back that your mom always tells you to straighten up. "Ayusin mo yang hutok mo, para kang kinukuba!"
usage_notes: Often associated with old age or poor posture.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dala ng katandaan ang **hutok** ng kanyang likod.","translation":"The **stoop** of his back is due to old age."},{"sentence":"May bahagyang **hutok** ang kanyang tindig.","translation":"His posture has a slight **bend**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang resulta ng paggamit ng matalas na bagay upang hatiin o sugatan ang isang bagay; isang piraso o bahagi na nakuha sa pamamagitan ng pagputol.
original_explanation: That thin slice of mango you give your sibling when you really don't want to share. Also, what happens to your puso (heart) after a breakup—puro hiwa. It can also be a physical cut, like from a kitchen knife accident while trying to be a Masterchef.
usage_notes: Often used for food preparation but can also refer to wounds.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa **hiwa** sa iyong daliri.","translation":"Be careful with the **cut** on your finger."},{"sentence":"Pahingi naman ng isang **hiwa** ng pizza.","translation":"Can I have a **slice** of pizza?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang balbal na salita na nabuo sa pamamagitan ng pagbabaliktad ng mga pantig ng salitang "pare," na tumutukoy sa isang kaibigang lalaki.
etymology: Syllabic inversion of the word 'pare' (pa-re -> re-pa).
original_explanation: The OG "what's up bro?" but make it Pinoy. It's 'pare' scrambled ('er-ap'), but smoother and became 'repa'. Your go-to word for the guy you share chicharon and life problems with. The foundation of Pinoy bromance.
usage_notes: Highly informal and traditionally used among male friends, but now widely used by everyone regardless of gender. A staple of colloquial Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uy, **repa**, kamusta na? Tagal nating 'di nagkita!","translation":"Hey, **pal**, how are you? It's been a while since we saw each other!"},{"sentence":"Salamat sa tulong, **repa**. Utang ko 'to sa'yo.","translation":"Thanks for the help, **dude**. I owe you one."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kemikal na likido na sumisira sa mga mikrobyo at bakterya, karaniwang ginagamit sa paglilinis ng mga ibabaw o bagay.
original_explanation: Ito yung alas mo laban sa mga germs na mas makapit pa sa ex mo. Panlinis sa sahig, banyo, o kahit saang maduming surface na kailangang maging 'clinically clean.' Isipin mo na lang, ito ang Lysol o Domex ng buhay mo.
usage_notes: Madalas ding gamitin ang salitang Ingles na "disinfectant" sa pang-araw-araw na usapan, lalo na sa mga urban na lugar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maglagay ka ng **disimpektante** sa basahan para pamatay ng mga mikrobyo.","translation":"Put some **disinfectant** on the rag to kill the germs."},{"sentence":"Amoy **disimpektante** ang buong ospital.","translation":"The whole hospital smells like **disinfectant**."}]

translation: to be able to be invaded; will be stormed
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng posibilidad o kakayahang mapasok o masakop sa pamamagitan ng puwersa o biglaang pagdagsa ng marami.
etymology: From Tagalog `lusob` (raid, invasion, assault). The prefix `ma-` indicates potential or ability. This is the future tense form.
original_explanation: Future tense of getting raided or stormed. Think of it as what might happen to your pantry if your titas and cousins arrive unannounced for merienda. Or what happens to a concert venue when the gates finally open. "Malulusob ang buffet table mamaya!"
usage_notes: Future tense of `malusob`. Often used in the context of war, raids, or a sudden overwhelming rush of people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghanda ang mga sundalo dahil may balitang **malulusob** ang kanilang kampo.","translation":"The soldiers prepared because there was news that their camp **would be invaded**."},{"sentence":"Kapag nag-sale, tiyak na **malulusob** ng mga mamimili ang mall.","translation":"When there's a sale, the mall will surely **be stormed** by shoppers."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paraang walang ingat, walang-kabuluhan, o bilang pagkukunwari lamang.
etymology: Possibly a reduplication of a root related to pretense or superficiality.
original_explanation: Acting 'dedma' or unbothered, but you're really not. It's doing something just for the sake of doing it, without any real effort or heart. Like when you 'clean' your room by just throwing everything in the closet. That's balabala cleaning. It's the energy of 'bahala na si Batman'.
usage_notes: This word is not very common in modern conversation and might be considered literary or dated.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong gawin nang **balabala** ang iyong mga tungkulin.","translation":"Do not perform your duties **superficially**."},{"sentence":"**Balabala** lamang ang kanyang paghingi ng tawad, hindi ito taos-puso.","translation":"His apology was just a **pretense**, it wasn't sincere."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbibigay ng atensyon sa pamamagitan ng pandinig; ang pag-unawa sa mga tunog o salitang naririnig.
etymology: From pakiki- (social participation prefix) + kinig (to listen).
original_explanation: More than just hearing; it's the active version. It's what you *should* be doing during a meeting but instead you're just nodding while thinking about what to eat for lunch. It's also what your bestie does at 2 AM when you're having a breakdown over a text message. It's the difference between hearing noise and understanding a message, a song, or a friend's 'hugot'.
usage_notes: The verb form is 'makinig' (to listen). 'Pakikinig' is the noun form, the act itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang epektibong komunikasyon ay nagsisimula sa mabuting **pakikinig**.","translation":"Effective communication starts with good **listening**."},{"sentence":"Naantig ang aking puso sa kanyang **pakikinig** sa aking mga problema.","translation":"My heart was touched by his/her **listening** to my problems."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagsagawa ng mga organisadong gawain upang makamit ang isang partikular na layunin, lalo na sa pulitika, adbertismo, o adbokasiya.
original_explanation: Ginagawa ng mga politiko 'pag malapit na eleksyon. Biglang babait, mamimigay ng t-shirt, at mangangako ng kung anu-ano. Or 'yung ginagawa mo para i-promote 'yung small business ng kaibigan mo sa social media. "Todo siyang kumampanya para sa paborito niyang kandidato."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaga siyang nagsimulang **kumampanya** para sa pagka-alkalde.","translation":"He started to **campaign** early for the mayorship."},{"sentence":"Ang grupo ay **kumampanya** para sa mas malinis na kapaligiran.","translation":"The group **campaigned** for a cleaner environment."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian o bahagi na nagpapababa sa kalidad o nagiging sanhi ng pagiging hindi perpekto; isang kakulangan o depekto.
etymology: Mula sa 'ka-' (unlaping nagsasaad ng katangian) + 'pintas' (puna, sira).
original_explanation: This is the 'sana all' counter-attack. It's the flaw your judgmental tita points out ("Ang taba mo na!"), the bug in your code, or the reason you say "walang perpektong tao" in your hugot posts. It's the chismis ammo.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa pisikal, pag-uugali, o materyal na depekto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa kabila ng kanyang mga **kapintasan**, mahal pa rin siya ng kanyang pamilya.","translation":"Despite his **flaws**, his family still loves him."},{"sentence":"Walang perpektong produkto; lahat ay may kani-kaniyang **kapintasan**.","translation":"There is no perfect product; all have their own **defects**."}]

meaning_filipino: Kumikislap o kumikinang nang paulit-ulit at mabilis; patay-sindi.
original_explanation: Parang Christmas lights na sira, or yung signal ng WiFi mo kapag malapit ka nang ma-disconnect sa Zoom call. It's there, then it's not. On and off, just like your ex's feelings for you.
usage_notes: Describes something that flashes or sparkles intermittently, often used for lights or shiny objects.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ilaw ng kandila ay **padiklap-diklap** dahil sa malakas na hangin.","translation":"The candle's flame was **flickering** because of the strong wind."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko ang **padiklap-diklap** na mga alitaptap sa dilim.","translation":"I saw the **intermittently sparkling** fireflies in the dark."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng musika na partikular na nilikha o angkop para sa pagsasayaw.
etymology: Combination of `tugtugin` (music to be played, from `tugtog` + `-in`) and `pansayaw` (for dancing, from `pang-` + `sayaw`).
original_explanation: The official soundtrack for your 'budots' moments, your TikTok dance challenges, or that awkward swaying you do at weddings. From disco to K-Pop to the latest club banger, if it makes you move your feet, it's tugtuging pansayaw.
usage_notes: A descriptive phrase. `Tugtugin` is the object-focus noun form of `tugtog`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magpatugtog ka naman ng **tugtuging pansayaw** para masaya.","translation":"Please play some **dance music** to liven things up."},{"sentence":"Puro **tugtuging pansayaw** ang nasa playlist niya.","translation":"His playlist is full of **dance music**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa sukdulang kataksilan, pagiging baluktot ng prinsipyo, o pagiging hindi mapagkakatiwalaan.
original_explanation: This is for that one character in a teleserye who's smiling at the bida while secretly plotting to steal their inheritance, their jowa, and their parking spot. The ultimate backstabber. The human version of a snake emoji.
usage_notes: A strong and formal word to describe profound moral corruption or treachery. Not common in casual conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isiniwalat ng bayani ang **napakabuktot** na plano ng mga kalaban.","translation":"The hero revealed the **very treacherous** plan of the enemies."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang ginawang pagtataksil ay isang **napakabuktot** na gawain.","translation":"His act of betrayal was an **extremely crooked** deed."}]

translation: to be pulverized; to be crushed into powder
meaning_filipino: Maging durog na durog hanggang sa maging parang pulbos.
original_explanation: What happens to your heart after a breakup, or what you do to Oreo cookies to make a cheesecake crust. It's the process of being broken down into a fine, powdery substance. Sometimes delicious, sometimes devastating.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for food or materials, and figuratively for emotions or arguments.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **mapulbos** nang pino ang mga mani para sa sarsa.","translation":"The peanuts need **to be pulverized** finely for the sauce."},{"sentence":"Sa debateng iyon, tila **mapulbos** ang kanyang mga argumento.","translation":"In that debate, it seemed his arguments would be **crushed into powder**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang balangkas na kahoy na ipinapatong sa batok ng dalawang hayop, karaniwang baka o kalabaw, upang pag-isahin ang mga ito sa paghila ng araro o kariton.
etymology: From "pan-" + "patok" (to place on top). The "n" in the prefix "pan-" assimilates to "m" before a root word starting with 'p'.
original_explanation: The OG "group project" tool for carabaos. It's a wooden neck-hug that forces two individuals to work together, whether they like it or not. It's the agricultural symbol for "we're in this together," or more accurately, "wala kang choice, hihilahin natin 'to."
usage_notes: Primarily used in agricultural contexts. Can also be used metaphorically to mean a burden or oppression.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inilagay ng magsasaka ang **pamatok** sa dalawang kalabaw bago mag-araro.","translation":"The farmer placed the **yoke** on the two carabaos before plowing."},{"sentence":"Nais nilang makawala mula sa **pamatok** ng kahirapan.","translation":"They want to break free from the **yoke** of poverty."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagdampi ng mga labi sa isang tao o bagay sa hinaharap; ang gagawing paghalik.
etymology: From the root word 'halik' (kiss) with the future tense prefix 'ha-' (repetition of the first syllable).
original_explanation: This is the future tense of 'kiss'. It's the promise in a romantic movie's climax, the threat your tita gives to your chubby cheeks, or what you tell yourself you'll do to your pillow after a long day. 'Pag nanalo ako sa lotto, hahalik ako sa sahig!'
usage_notes: Standard future tense form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hahalik** siya sa noo ng kanyang ina bago umalis.","translation":"He **will kiss** his mother's forehead before leaving."},{"sentence":"Sabi ng prinsipe, **hahalik** siya kay Snow White upang magising ito.","translation":"The prince said he **will kiss** Snow White to awaken her."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang nasa pinakailalim na posisyon, antas, halaga, o kalidad kumpara sa iba.
original_explanation: This can be your score in an exam you didn't study for, the price of an item during a 12.12 sale, or your self-esteem after being left on 'seen.' It's the rock bottom, the lowest tier, the 'bagsak' grade. But hey, when you're at the 'pinakamababa,' the only way to go is up... hopefully.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical height, price, rank, quality, or score.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakuha niya ang **pinakamababa** na marka sa pagsusulit.","translation":"He got the **lowest** score on the exam."},{"sentence":"Sa kanila ka bumili, sila ang may **pinakamababa** na presyo sa palengke.","translation":"Buy from them, they have the **lowest** price in the market."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa mga relihiyong Abrahamiko, ito ang ipinangakong tagapagligtas o manunubos ng sangkatauhan.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol 'Mesías', na mula sa Hebreo 'māšīaḥ' (ang pinahiran).
original_explanation: The original 'The One.' Bago pa man si Neo sa The Matrix, mayroon nang inaabangang Mesiyas. Siya yung ultimate savior na hinihintay ng lahat para ayusin ang gulo ng mundo.
usage_notes: Isang sentral na pigura sa Kristiyanismo (si Hesus) at Hudaismo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naniniwala ang mga Kristiyano na si Hesus ang **Mesiyas**.","translation":"Christians believe that Jesus is the **Messiah**."},{"sentence":"Hinihintay ng mga Hudyo ang pagdating ng kanilang **Mesiyas**.","translation":"The Jewish people await the coming of their **Messiah**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging marangal, kagalang-galang, o pag-aari sa uring maharlika; ang pagkakaroon ng dangal at mataas na katayuan sa lipunan.
etymology: From `pagka-` (quality of) + `maharlika` (noble, freeman in pre-colonial Philippines).
original_explanation: This is the vibe of someone who walks into Jollibee with the grace of a queen, or your lola who insists on using the 'special' plates for guests. It’s not about being rich, but about carrying yourself with dignity, class, and a certain royal-like finesse. Think Heart Evangelista at the palengke.
usage_notes: Historically refers to the feudal warrior class. In modern usage, it refers to a sense of nobility, dignity, or high-mindedness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit sa gitna ng kahirapan, napanatili niya ang kanyang **pagkamaharlika**.","translation":"Even in the midst of poverty, she maintained her **nobility**."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkamaharlika** ay hindi lamang sa dugo, kundi nasa gawa.","translation":"**Nobility** is not just in blood, but in deeds."}]

translation: to title; to secure a land title
meaning_filipino: Maglagay ng pamagat sa isang akda; o kumuha ng legal na dokumento (titulo) na nagpapatunay ng pagmamay-ari sa isang lupain.
original_explanation: When you finish your masterpiece thesis, you "magtitulo" it (give it a title). More importantly for Filipino families, "magtitulo" is the ultimate adulting goal of securing the land title for your property. It’s the difference between "amin 'to" and having the papers to prove it. One is for art, the other is for avoiding family drama over inheritance.
usage_notes: The context (writing vs. real estate) is crucial for understanding the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **magtitulo** sa iyong sanaysay.","translation":"Don't forget to **put a title** on your essay."},{"sentence":"Maraming taon silang nagsumikap bago nila napa-**magtitulo** ang kanilang lupa.","translation":"They worked hard for many years before they were able to **secure a title** for their land."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang pambilang na binubuo ng isang kuwadro na may mga baras kung saan nakahanay ang mga butil o bola na maaaring galawin.
original_explanation: Ito yung calculator ng mga lolo't lola natin. The OG spreadsheet. Bago pa nauso ang Microsoft Excel at Casio calculators, ito ang sandata ng mga tindera sa palengke at mga Chinese businessman para sa mabilisang kwentahan. Satisfying pakinggan yung 'clack-clack' ng beads.
usage_notes: Ang salita ay hindi gaanong kilala ng mga nakababatang henerasyon, na karaniwang tinatawag itong 'abacus'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ng matandang tindera ang **bilahan** upang kwentahin ang kabuuang bayarin.","translation":"The old vendor used an **abacus** to calculate the total payment."},{"sentence":"Sa museo, nakakita kami ng isang lumang **bilahan** na gawa sa kahoy.","translation":"In the museum, we saw an old **abacus** made of wood."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang modelong hugis-bola ng Daigdig, o anumang bagay na pabilog o mala-bola.
original_explanation: The thing in your school library you'd spin to randomly choose your "future" travel destination. It's the Earth, but mini and you can hold it. Also, the name of a major telco, so when someone says "Walang signal ang Globo," they're not talking about the planet having a bad day.
usage_notes: Refers to a spherical model of the Earth or a sphere in general. Also a very common brand name for a telecommunications company in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinuro ng guro sa **globo** kung nasaan ang Pilipinas.","translation":"The teacher pointed on the **globe** where the Philippines is."},{"sentence":"Ang snow **globo** ay isang tanyag na subenir.","translation":"The snow **globe** is a popular souvenir."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghahalungkat o pagbubungkal sa isang tumpok ng mga bagay o sa lupa upang may mahanap.
original_explanation: This is you at an ukay-ukay store, diving into a mountain of clothes hoping to find a vintage gem for 50 pesos. It's the art of rummaging, whether it's in your messy closet for that one missing sock or digging up old issues (chismis).
usage_notes: The term 'ukay-ukay' (thrift store) is derived from this word, literally 'dig-dig'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pag-ukay** sa lumang baul ay nagbunyag ng mga lihim ng nakaraan.","translation":"The **rummaging** through the old chest revealed secrets of the past."},{"sentence":"Naiinis ako sa **pag-ukay** ng aso sa aming hardin.","translation":"I'm annoyed by the dog's **digging up** of our garden."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian kung saan ang mga ngipin sa itaas na panga, lalo na ang mga nasa harap, ay nakausli o mas abante kaysa sa mga ngipin sa ibabang panga.
original_explanation: The dental situation where your front teeth enter the room before you do. It's a descriptive term, though not always used kindly, so maybe don't call your date this. Think of a cartoon beaver, and you've got the picture.
usage_notes: Can be considered impolite or an insult. Use with caution.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Madalas siyang tuksuhin noong bata dahil siya ay **ngayngayin**.","translation":"He was often teased as a child because he was **buck-toothed**."},{"sentence":"Nagpa-brace siya para maitama ang kanyang pagiging **ngayngayin**.","translation":"She got braces to correct her **protruding upper teeth**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng tabako na binalumbon mula sa mga pinatuyong dahon nito at sinisindihan para hithitin.
etymology: From Spanish 'habano', referring to something from Havana, Cuba, famous for its cigars.
original_explanation: The rich kontrabida's favorite accessory in old Filipino movies. It's the Titos' version of a vape. You don't just smoke it, you brandish it while planning your evil takeover of the bida's hacienda.
usage_notes: A specific term for a cigar, as opposed to 'sigarilyo' (cigarette).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig mag-**abano** ang lolo ko pagkatapos mananghalian.","translation":"My grandfather likes to smoke a **cigar** after lunch."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na may katangiang biglaang sumabog o maglabas ng matinding enerhiya.
original_explanation: 'Yung ugali ng ka-opisina mong tahimik lang pero 'pag ginalit mo, parang granada. Pwede ring tumukoy sa performance ng isang atleta, 'Wow, ang eksplosibo ng laro niya!'
usage_notes: Can describe both literal potential for explosion and figurative ones (e.g., personality, performance, situation). The form 'eksplosib' is a less common variant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **eksplosibo** ang talakayan nang pag-usapan ang pulitika.","translation":"The discussion became **explosive** when they talked about politics."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng paggana o pag-usad ng isang makina, sasakyan, o anumang mekanismo.
etymology: From Spanish "andar" (to walk, to go, to function).
original_explanation: The 'go' button for anything with an engine. When your car is working, 'maganda ang andar.' When your brain isn't working on a Monday morning, 'mahina ang andar.' It's the life force of your aircon during summer.
usage_notes: Often used with a verb like 'umandar' (to run/function) or 'paandarin' (to make something run).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahina ang **andar** ng sasakyan paakyat ng Baguio.","translation":"The car's **performance (running state)** was weak going up to Baguio."},{"sentence":"Paandarin mo na ang motor, male-late na tayo!","translation":"Start the motorcycle's engine, we're going to be late!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang parirala na naglalarawan sa isang bagay o sitwasyon na mas kaakit-akit, mas gugustuhin, o mas mainam kumpara sa iba.
etymology: From "lalong" (more so) and "kanais-nais" (desirable, from root "nais" - want/desire).
original_explanation: This is the "upgrade" you're looking for. Comparing two job offers? The one with the higher salary and free coffee is "lalong kanais-nais." It's choosing between good and better. Parang sa love life, you meet someone nice, then you meet someone who's nice AND funny and loves the same weird memes as you—siya yung lalong kanais-nais.
usage_notes: A comparative adjectival phrase. "Lalong" is a ligatured form of "lalo na" or "lalo + -ng".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang alok na may kasamang benepisyo ay **lalong kanais-nais**.","translation":"The offer that includes benefits is **more desirable**."},{"sentence":"Mas tahimik dito, kaya **lalong kanais-nais** na lugar para mag-aral.","translation":"It's quieter here, making it a **more preferable** place to study."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na kontrata o kasulatan, lalo na sa seguro, na naglalahad ng mga tuntunin at kundisyon ng isang kasunduan.
original_explanation: This is the piece of paper (or PDF) you get from an insurance agent that you probably didn't read completely. It's the contract that says 'We'll give you money if something bad happens, IF you follow all these rules.' Parang terms and conditions ng life.
usage_notes: Tiyak na tumutukoy sa isang kontrata ng seguro. Para sa pangkalahatang patakaran (rules), mas karaniwang ginagamit ang 'patakaran'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Basahing mabuti ang lahat ng nakasulat sa **polisa** bago ka pumirma.","translation":"Read everything written on the **policy** carefully before you sign."}]

translation: Stale; stuffy; overripe (due to being kept enclosed)
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay, karaniwan ay prutas, na naging sobrang hinog o nagsimulang masira dahil sa pagkakakulob o pagkakatago sa isang saradong lugar. Maaari ring tumukoy sa mabigat at hindi sariwang hangin.
original_explanation: You know that smell in a room that hasn't been opened in weeks? That's `maluom`. Or when you forget you have bananas in your bag for three days under the hot sun? They become **luom**. It's the opposite of fresh, the vibe of being trapped and getting funky.
usage_notes: Often found in its verb or adjective form `naluom` or `maluom`. Describes something that has ripened or spoiled in an enclosed space.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **luom** ang mga saging dahil naiwan sa loob ng kotse.","translation":"The bananas became **overripe** because they were left inside the car."},{"sentence":"Ang amoy sa loob ng baul ay malúom.","translation":"The smell inside the chest is **stuffy**."}]

translation: to defecate; to make something dirty
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalabas ng dumi mula sa katawan; maaari ring tumukoy sa pagkakalat o pagpaparumi sa isang lugar o bagay.
original_explanation: Two meanings, one word. 1) The polite, almost clinical way of saying 'tumae' or 'to poop.' What a doctor might ask you. 2) What your mom yells when you walk into the newly mopped house with muddy shoes: 'Huwag kang magdumi dito!' It's the act of introducing chaos (dumi) into a clean space.
usage_notes: Context is key to differentiate between the biological function (a euphemism) and the act of soiling something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng pasyente na **magdumi** araw-araw para maging malusog.","translation":"The patient needs to **defecate** daily to be healthy."},{"sentence":"Pakiusap, huwag po kayong **magdumi** sa parke.","translation":"Please, do not **make a mess** in the park."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing tirintas ang buhok o anumang may hibla. Ang pandiwang ito ay tumutukoy sa bagay o tao na nilalagyan ng tirintas.
original_explanation: The verb form of your elementary school memories. Ito 'yung ginagawa sa buhok mo, sa extension cord na magulo, o sa friendship bracelet para sa bestie mo. A true test of patience and finger dexterity.
usage_notes: Ang pokus ng pandiwang ito ay sa tao o bagay na tinirintas. Hal: **Tirintasan** mo si Ana. (Braid Ana's hair).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marunong ka bang **magtirintas** ng buhok?","translation":"Do you know how to **braid** hair?"},{"sentence":"**Tirintasan** mo ang buhok ko, parang awa mo na.","translation":"Please **braid** my hair, I'm begging you."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamababang antas ng pagsisikap o kontribusyon na kinakailangan sa isang sitwasyon, gawain, o relasyon.
original_explanation: Yung effort na 'at least may ginawa' level lang. Parang pag-review mo sa exam, binasa mo lang yung headings. Sa relationships, ito yung 'good morning' text tapos a-absent na buong araw. It's the 'pwede na' that's not really 'pwede na'.
usage_notes: A very common Taglish phrase used to critique low levels of effort in work, school, and especially romantic or social relationships.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang masanay sa **bare minimum** na pagtrato sa'yo.","translation":"Don't get used to being treated with the **bare minimum**."},{"sentence":"Yung report na pinasa niya, halatang **bare minimum** lang ang effort.","translation":"The report he submitted, it's obvious only the **bare minimum** effort was put in."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng komunikasyon gamit ang internet kung saan ang dalawa o higit pang tao ay nag-uusap habang nagkikita sa pamamagitan ng video sa kani-kanilang mga screen.
original_explanation: Ito yung LDR-saver at WFH essential. Dati, kailangan mo pang mag-load para lang marinig boses niya. Ngayon, makikita mo na kung totoo bang 'natutulog' na siya o nasa labas pa kasama ang 'friends' niya. Perfect din para sa team meeting na pwede namang email lang.
usage_notes: Commonly spelled as 'video call' or 'videocall'. Used interchangeably in spoken and written Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-**videocall** tayo mamaya para makita ko ang mga pamangkin ko.","translation":"Let's have a **video call** later so I can see my nieces and nephews."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng malakas na internet para hindi putol-putol ang **videocall**.","translation":"You need a strong internet connection so the **video call** isn't choppy."}]

translation: to live; to dwell; to lead a life
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng buhay; ang paraan ng pag-iral o paggugol ng buhay sa isang partikular na lugar o kalagayan.
original_explanation: It's not just about breathing (huminga), it's about the whole package deal—the grind, the drama, the 'sana all' moments. To mamuhay is to exist with purpose, or at least to try and find one between coffee breaks and bill payments.
usage_notes: Implies a manner or style of living, not just the state of being alive.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais niyang **mamuhay** nang simple sa probinsya.","translation":"He wants **to live** a simple life in the province."},{"sentence":"Paano tayo **mamumuhay** kung palaging ganito ang presyo ng bilihin?","translation":"How will we **live** if the prices of goods are always like this?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng pabalat, padding, at bukal sa mga muwebles tulad ng silya o sopa.
original_explanation: That thing your parents do to the 30-year-old living room sofa to give it a "new look" instead of just buying a new one. To mag-apholster is to give furniture a makeover, usually involving lots of foam, fabric, and a staple gun. It's the ultimate thrift-flip for your sala set.
usage_notes: This is a direct Tagalized loanword. `Mag-upholster` is also a common variant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan na nating **mag-apholster** ng mga upuan sa dining room dahil luma na ang tela.","translation":"We need **to upholster** the dining room chairs because the fabric is old."},{"sentence":"Magkano ang singil para **mag-apholster** ng isang buong sofa set?","translation":"How much is the charge **to upholster** an entire sofa set?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang mahulaan o maramdaman ang isang bagay bago pa ito mangyari; isang kutob o pangitain.
original_explanation: It's that gut feeling you have that your friend is about to message you for a loan. Or when you just *know* your boss will call for an 'urgent' meeting at 4:59 PM on a Friday. It's the mind's ability to see a spoiler for your own life.
usage_notes: A somewhat literary or formal term. 'Kutob' is a more common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Wala siyang kahit katiting na **hinagap** sa planong sorpresa para sa kanya.","translation":"She didn't have the slightest **inkling** about the surprise plan for her."},{"sentence":"May **hinagap** akong hindi magtatagal ang kanilang relasyon.","translation":"I have a **premonition** that their relationship won't last."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang magkakasunod at halos walang patid na pagdating o pag-iral ng mga bagay o pangyayari.
original_explanation: When problems arrive one after the other with no break, parang BPO calls on a queueing night—that's 'sagunson'. Or when you get a 'sagunson' of good news, like your salary coming in, a bonus, and a refund all on the same day. It's the Tagalog for 'when it rains, it pours', for better or for worse.
usage_notes: Often used adverbially to mean 'consecutively' or 'in succession', frequently as 'magkasagunson' or in the phrase 'sunud-sunod na sagunson'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **sagunson** ng mga trahedya ay nagpaluhod sa buong bayan.","translation":"The **succession** of tragedies brought the whole town to its knees."},{"sentence":"Magka**sagunson** na dumating ang magandang balita.","translation":"The good news arrived in quick **succession**."}]

translation: to commentate; to make a commentary
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng mga puna, opinyon, o paliwanag tungkol sa isang paksa, pangyayari, o palabas.
etymology: From `mag-` (verb prefix) + `komentaryo`, which is from Spanish `comentario`.
original_explanation: What everyone on Facebook thinks they are: a professional analyst. To 'magkomentaryo' is to give your unsolicited (or solicited) opinion on everything from basketball games and political issues to your friend's new relationship status. 'Pahingi ng popcorn' is the battle cry before the 'komentaryo' begins.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of sports, news, or social media. A more common, less formal verb is `mag-comment`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang napiling **magkomentaryo** para sa laban ni Pacquiao.","translation":"He was chosen **to commentate** for Pacquiao's fight."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magkomentaryo** kung hindi mo alam ang buong kuwento.","translation":"Don't **make a commentary** if you don't know the whole story."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kemikal o sangkap na idinaragdag sa mga produkto tulad ng pagkain, gamot, o pampaganda upang maiwasan ang pagkasira o pagkabulok.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'pam-' (pang-instrumento) + 'preserba', na hango sa salitang Espanyol na 'preservar' (panatilihing sariwa).
original_explanation: The magic ingredient that makes your instant noodles, canned goods, and hotdogs last longer than your last relationship. It's the reason that snack from 2022 still looks edible. Basically, the food's version of formalin.
usage_notes: Maaari ring gamitin sa makasagisag na paraan para sa isang bagay na nagpapanatili ng isang alaala o tradisyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinitingnan ko kung mayroong maraming **pampreserba** ang binibili kong de-lata.","translation":"I check if the canned goods I'm buying have a lot of **preservatives**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sinasadyang pagpapatid o pagpapatisod sa isang tao gamit ang paa upang siya ay matumba.
etymology: From the root 'sabid', a less common term for tripping, related to 'sabit'.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'kontrabida' move in a Pinoy teleserye. It's when you subtly stick your foot out to make your office rival, who's carrying a tray of coffee, fall flat on their face. It's a low-key, physical form of sabotage. Not to be confused with 'matapilok' (accidental tripping on your own feet).
usage_notes: This is a less common term than 'patirin'. It specifically implies using one's foot to trip another person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **sabirin** ang kapatid mo, baka masaktan siya.","translation":"Don't **trip** your sibling, they might get hurt."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko kung paano niya **sinabid** ang kaklase namin.","translation":"I saw how he **tripped** our classmate."}]

meaning_filipino: Tanggapin o kolektahin ang sahod bilang kabayaran sa serbisyo o paggawa.
original_explanation: The best part of being an 'alipin ng salapi' (slave to money). 'Sahurin' is the action of finally getting your paycheck. When your friend texts you "Tara, shot puno!" on the 15th, you know exactly what they just did. They just 'sahurin'-ed their sweldo.
usage_notes: This is the verb form of 'sahod' (salary/wage). Refers to the act of receiving it.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Oras na para **sahurin** ang pinaghirapan nating pera.","translation":"It's time to **collect** the money we worked hard for."},{"sentence":"Babalik ako mamaya para **sahurin** ang bayad sa akin.","translation":"I will come back later to **collect** my payment."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay o magkakatuwang na pagkilos ng pagtatakip sa pagkakamali, kakulangan, o sekreto ng isa't isa.
original_explanation: This is the unwritten rule of 'Walang laglagan!' in a team or barkada. When the boss asks who made the mistake, everyone suddenly has amnesia. That's true **magtakipan**. It's a group effort in plausible deniability.
usage_notes: Implies a mutual, reciprocal action of covering up, usually for mistakes or secrets.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkasundo ang magkakaibigan na **magtakipan** para walang mapagalitan sa kanilang guro.","translation":"The friends agreed to **cover for each other** so that no one would get scolded by their teacher."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasuotang isinusuot sa ibabaw ng damit upang maprotektahan ito mula sa dumi, lalo na sa pagluluto o pagtatrabaho.
original_explanation: The official uniform of titas who cook, chefs, and baristas. It's that piece of cloth you tie around your waist that says, "I'm about to do something messy, and my OOTD will not be a victim."
usage_notes: The English word is used directly in Tagalog. No common native equivalent is in wide use.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isuot mo ang **apron** para hindi madumihan ang damit mo habang nagluluto.","translation":"Wear the **apron** so your clothes don't get dirty while cooking."}]

translation: to ambush; to lie in wait for
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-abang sa isang tao o hayop sa isang tago na lugar upang biglaang salakayin o sorpresahin.
original_explanation: The act of surprising someone, not always in a good way. Parang 'yong ginagawa ng boss mo 'pag bigla siyang susulpot sa likod mo habang nag-fe-Facebook ka. Or when your chismosa tita is waiting for you by the door, ready to ask, 'Kailan ka mag-aasawa?'
usage_notes: Nagmula sa ibang salitang-ugat (*tambang*) kumpara sa pangngalang *tambalan* (mula sa *tambal*).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binalak ng mga rebelde na **tambalan** ang mga sundalo sa bundok.","translation":"The rebels planned to **ambush** the soldiers in the mountains."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **tambalan** sa madilim na eskinita, natatakot ako.","translation":"Don't **lie in wait for** me in a dark alley, I'm scared."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong kabilang sa henerasyong ipinanganak sa pagitan ng unang bahagi ng dekada 1980 at kalagitnaan ng dekada 1990.
original_explanation: Ah, the "Titos and Titas of Manila" in training. Sila yung generation na naabutan pa ang dial-up internet pero expert na sa TikTok. They're obsessed with coffee, work-life balance, and secretly miss the 90s. Sila rin ang laging sinisisi sa lahat ng bagay, from killing industries to loving avocado toast too much.
usage_notes: A very common loanword in modern Filipino, used interchangeably with the English term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **millennial** ngayon ang mahilig mag-travel at mag-explore ng iba't ibang kultura.","translation":"Many **millennials** today love to travel and explore different cultures."},{"sentence":"Bilang isang **millennial**, sanay siya sa paggamit ng teknolohiya sa trabaho.","translation":"As a **millennial**, she is used to using technology at work."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang uri ng karne na niluto sa pamamagitan ng pagpiprito sa mainit na mantika.
original_explanation: Your go-to ulam when you're lazy or in a hurry. Just grab some meat, season it, and throw it in a hot pan. It's the "pwede na 'to" of Filipino cooking. The ultimate comfort food that pairs perfectly with rice and a sawsawan of toyo't kalamansi.
usage_notes: Ang "karneng pinirito" ay isang pangkalahatang termino at maaaring tumukoy sa piniritong baboy, baka, o manok.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito niyang almusal ang **karneng pinirito** na may kasamang sinangag at itlog.","translation":"His favorite breakfast is **fried meat** with garlic rice and egg."},{"sentence":"Amoy pa lang ng **karneng pinirito** ay nakakagutom na.","translation":"Just the smell of **fried meat** is enough to make you hungry."}]

meaning_filipino: May kakayahang makakumbinsi o mag-udyok sa iba na maniwala, sumang-ayon, o gawin ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: The skill of your friend who convinces you to go out on a Friday night even if you're broke and tired. Also, the skill of every online seller sa live selling: 'Mine na, mga sis! Last piece na 'to!' They can sell ice to an Eskimo. It's the power to make people say 'yes'.
usage_notes: Describes a person, speech, or argument that is good at convincing others.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Mapanghikayat** ang kanyang talumpati kaya marami ang bumoto sa kanya.","translation":"His speech was **persuasive**, which is why many voted for him."},{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng **mapanghikayat** na tono upang makuha ang gusto niya.","translation":"She used a **persuasive** tone to get what she wanted."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay na ginagamit upang isara o takpan ang isang butas, sisidlan, o ibabaw.
original_explanation: Your Tupperware is useless without its **pantakip**. It's the thing you use to cover something up, whether it's the lid for your kaldero, a piece of cardboard over a hole, or the 'seen' message you use to cover up the fact that you don't know how to reply to your ex.
usage_notes: A general term for any kind of covering.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasaan na ang **pantakip** ng kaldero? Kumukulo na ang sinaing!","translation":"Where is the **lid** for the pot? The rice is already boiling!"},{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng panyo bilang pansamantalang **pantakip** sa kanyang sugat.","translation":"She used a handkerchief as a temporary **cover** for her wound."}]

translation: state of being scalded or blistered
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkakaroon ng paltos o pinsala sa balat dahil sa pagkakadikit sa mainit na bagay, likido, o singaw.
original_explanation: This is the "ouch, tumalsik yung mantika!" moment when you're frying tilapia. It's the result of accidentally touching the "plantsa" or getting hit by steam from the rice cooker. The painful blister that forms after is the trophy of your 'pagkalabnos'.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to burns from hot liquids, steam, or brief contact with a hot surface, resulting in blisters.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Agad niyang binuhusan ng malamig na tubig ang kanyang kamay dahil sa **pagkalabnos**.","translation":"He immediately poured cold water on his hand after **getting scalded**."},{"sentence":"Nag-iwan ng peklat ang **pagkalabnos** niya noong bata.","translation":"The **blistering** he got as a child left a scar."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking salu-salo o piging na idinaraos upang ipagdiwang ang isang espesyal na okasyon.
original_explanation: The main event. The reason why your Tita from the US sent a Balikbayan box. It's the gathering where the lechon is the star, the karaoke machine is the supporting actor, and the chismis is the script. It's where "take out" is not just allowed, it's expected.
usage_notes: Often used for birthdays, fiestas, baptisms, and other celebrations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming bisita ang dumating sa **handaan** para sa kanyang kaarawan.","translation":"Many guests came to the **feast** for her birthday."},{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang magdala ng lalagyan para sa mga natira sa **handaan**.","translation":"Don't forget to bring a container for leftovers from the **party**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng magaspang na batong ígnea na maitim at binubuo pangunahin ng plagioclase at pyroxene.
original_explanation: This is a geology term. It's not your everyday 'bato-bato sa langit'. Think of it as the cool, underground cousin of basalt. You won't find this in your typical hugot line unless you're dating a geologist.
usage_notes: This is a technical, scientific term and is extremely rare in daily conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng mga heologo ang komposisyon ng **gabro** na natagpuan sa bundok.","translation":"The geologists are studying the composition of the **gabbro** found on the mountain."},{"sentence":"Ang **gabro** ay isang halimbawa ng intrusive igneous rock.","translation":"**Gabbro** is an example of an intrusive igneous rock."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tayutay na gumagamit ng salita o parirala sa isang bagay o ideya kung saan ito ay hindi literal na tumutukoy, upang magmungkahi ng pagkakatulad.
original_explanation: This is the secret language of 'hugot.' When you say, 'Ang pag-ibig ay parang investment, kailangan mong mag-risk,' that's a metapora. You're not actually calling your stockbroker about your crush. It’s making things sound deep and complicated, just like your feelings.
usage_notes: Isang mahalagang kasangkapan sa panitikan at tula.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pariralang 'pusong bato' ay isang karaniwang **metapora** para sa isang taong walang awa.","translation":"The phrase 'heart of stone' is a common **metaphor** for a merciless person."},{"sentence":"Mahilig gumamit ng **metapora** ang makata upang ipahayag ang kanyang damdamin.","translation":"The poet loves to use **metaphors** to express his feelings."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hanging hilagang-silangan na nagdadala ng malamig at tuyong panahon sa Pilipinas, karaniwan mula Oktubre hanggang Marso.
original_explanation: This is the Philippines' version of 'winter is coming'. It's that glorious '-ber months' wind that signals cooler weather, bibingka season, and the start of endless Christmas songs in malls. It's the reason you can finally wear that jacket you bought on sale. The opposite of 'habagat', which is the hot, humid, and rainy season.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to the cool, dry northeast monsoon, not just any wind. Its counterpart is 'habagat' (southwest monsoon).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap mamasyal kapag panahon ng **amihan** dahil hindi masyadong mainit.","translation":"It's nice to go out during the **northeast monsoon** season because it's not too hot."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula nang umihip ang **amihan**, hudyat na malapit na ang Pasko.","translation":"The **northeast monsoon** has started to blow, a sign that Christmas is near."}]

translation: the act of watching multiple episodes of a series in one sitting
meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng walang-tigil na panonood ng maraming yugto (episode) ng isang serye sa telebisyon o online sa isang upuan lamang.
original_explanation: The official sport of long weekends and 'sick' days. Ang binge watching ay ang sining ng pag-convince sa sarili mo na mas importante ang plot twist ng serye kaysa sa tulog, pagkain, at deadlines.
usage_notes: Used interchangeably with the verb form "mag-binge watch".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **binge watching** ang naging libangan ko noong lockdown.","translation":"**Binge watching** became my pastime during the lockdown."},{"sentence":"Naubos ang data ko dahil sa **binge watching**.","translation":"My data ran out because of **binge watching**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na piraso, karaniwang bilog at yari sa plastik o metal, na ikinakabit sa damit at isinusuot sa butas upang maisara ito.
original_explanation: From the Spanish 'botón'. It's that little circle on your polo shirt that always seems to pop off at the worst possible moment, like during a job interview. For your lola, it's a treasure to be collected in a tin can of Danish butter cookies.
usage_notes: Distinct from the English 'button' used for electronics (which is often just called 'button' in Taglish or 'pindutan'). 'Butones' is a common pluralized variant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakitahi ang natanggal na **buton** sa aking polo.","translation":"Please sew the button that came off my polo shirt."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglilinis ng damit o tela gamit ang tubig at sabon. Ito ay ang anyong pangnagdaan ng pandiwang 'labhan'.
etymology: From 'laba' (to do laundry) with the infix '-in-' and suffix '-han'.
original_explanation: This is what you did to that pile of clothes that's been sitting in the corner of your room for two weeks. The 'chair-drobe' finally got its day off. You've **nilabhan** the evidence of your procrastination.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to washing clothes or fabric, as opposed to 'hinugasan' which is for dishes or hands.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nilabhan** ko na ang mga damit na isusuot mo bukas.","translation":"I already **washed** the clothes you will wear tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Sino ang nag-iwan ng basang medyas na hindi naman **nilabhan**?","translation":"Who left these wet socks that weren't even **washed**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mga buto sa dibdib na bumabalot at nagpoprotekta sa puso at baga; tumutukoy din sa parte ng karne mula sa hayop na kasama ang mga butong ito.
original_explanation: The part of your body you hold when you laugh too hard at a meme. Also, the star of the show at every Filipino barbecue party. Whether it's pork or beef, when you hear 'kustilyas,' you know it's going to be a good (and messy) time. Extra rice, please!
usage_notes: Used both anatomically and culinarily. 'Tadyang' is a common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap ang adobong **kustilyas** na luto ni Nanay.","translation":"Mom's adobo **spare ribs** are delicious."},{"sentence":"Nabasag ang kanyang **kustilyas** sa aksidente.","translation":"His **ribs** were broken in the accident."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang istruktura na binubuo ng bubong na sinusuportahan ng mga haligi, karaniwang nakakabit bilang pasukan sa isang gusali.
original_explanation: 'Yung magarbong version ng "balkonahe" o "terrace" na kadalasan mong makikita sa mga lumang simbahan, munisipyo, o bahay na bato. Parang grand entrance na may mga poste. Dito nagaganap 'yung dramatic entrance mo sa isang party, kung may **portiko** man 'yung venue.
usage_notes: Primarily used in architecture and historical contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpatayo sila ng eleganteng **portiko** sa harap ng kanilang mansiyon.","translation":"They built an elegant **portico** in front of their mansion."},{"sentence":"Sumilong muna kami sa **portiko** ng simbahan habang umuulan.","translation":"We took shelter in the church's **portico** while it was raining."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa maraming pagkakataon; nang may regularidad o paulit-ulit.
original_explanation: 'Yung "seen" sa Messenger, 'yung traffic sa EDSA, 'yung unli-rice sa Mang Inasal—lahat 'yan nangyayari **madalas**. It's the opposite of "minsan lang." It's your life's recurring theme, for better or for worse.
usage_notes: One of the most common adverbs of frequency in Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Madalas** siyang pumunta sa library para mag-aral.","translation":"She **often** goes to the library to study."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit at siksik na piraso ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay metal tulad ng ginto o pilak; isang maliit na bloke.
original_explanation: Think of a tiny gold bar or a perfectly pressed cube of sugar. It’s a small, compact, and often valuable piece of something. It implies that something has been compressed or molded into a neat little block. "Isang tipil na ginto" is like a pirate's pocket change.
usage_notes: Madalas na tumutukoy sa mga mahahalagang metal. Bihira itong gamitin sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakahanap sila ng isang **tipil** ng ginto sa minahan.","translation":"They found an **ingot** of gold in the mine."},{"sentence":"Binigyan niya ako ng isang **tipil** ng tsokolateng mula sa ibang bansa.","translation":"He gave me a small **block** of imported chocolate."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking espasyo, karaniwan sa loob ng isang shopping mall, kung saan magkakatabi ang iba't ibang kainan at mayroong isang komunal na lugar para sa mga customer na kumain.
original_explanation: The promised land sa loob ng mall kung saan nagkakasundo ang buong barkada. 'Yung isa gusto ng Jollibee, 'yung isa gusto ng Chinese food, 'yung isa gusto ng Sbarro. Sa foodcourt, walang away, lahat masaya. It's the DMZ of dining choices.
usage_notes: Direct English loanword, universally understood in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkita na lang tayo sa **foodcourt** ng SM para mananghalian.","translation":"Let's just meet at the SM **food court** for lunch."},{"sentence":"Maingay at laging puno ng tao ang **foodcourt** tuwing Sabado.","translation":"The **food court** is noisy and always full of people on Saturdays."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na may sakit na rayuma o madalas makaranas ng pananakit na may kaugnayan dito.
original_explanation: This is the adjective you use to describe someone who has 'reuma'. It's their official title. "Reumatika si Tita, kaya laging may dalang Efficascent Oil." It's a medical-sounding term that has become common in the household.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lola kong **reumatika** ay hindi maaaring mapagod nang husto.","translation":"My **rheumatic** grandmother cannot get too tired."},{"sentence":"Nagrereklamo na naman ang **reumatika** kong tuhod.","translation":"My **rheumatic** knee is complaining again."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng sapin sa paa na bukas, magaan, at karaniwang gawa sa goma o katulad na materyales, na isinusuot sa loob ng bahay o para sa kaswal na paglakad.
original_explanation: The official footwear of the Filipino household. The weapon of choice for mothers chasing naughty kids (the dreaded 'flying sinelas'). It's what you wear for a quick trip to the sari-sari store. Not to be confused with its more common cousin 'tsinelas', 'sinelas' is the Spanish-derived version. Same comfort, different colonial origin story.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'tsinelas', though 'tsinelas' is far more common in colloquial speech. 'Sinelas' can sound slightly more formal, literary, or old-fashioned.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magsuot ka ng **sinelas** sa loob ng bahay para hindi madumihan ang paa mo.","translation":"Wear **slippers** inside the house so your feet don't get dirty."},{"sentence":"Naiwan ko ang aking paboritong pares ng **sinelas** sa beach.","translation":"I left my favorite pair of **flip-flops** at the beach."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-alis ng isang bahagi mula sa isang kabuuan; ang halaga o bilang na inalis; diskuwento.
original_explanation: This is what you hope for during a 12.12 sale. It's the "less" in "buy more, pay less". It could be a bawas in your workload (yay!), a bawas sa presyo (double yay!), or a bawas in your sahod (a nightmare). It's the opposite of 'dagdag' (addition).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **bawas** ba ito kung maramihan ang bibilhin?","translation":"Is there a **discount** if I buy in bulk?"},{"sentence":"Malaki ang **bawas** sa timbang niya mula nang mag-ehersisyo siya.","translation":"There was a big **reduction** in his weight since he started exercising."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa panlabas na bahagi, anyo, o katangian ng isang bagay; hindi panloob. Karaniwang ginagamit para sa mga pangngalang panlalaki sa kontekstong Espanyol.
original_explanation: Same as 'eksterna,' but for the boys. This is the 'outside' or 'external' adjective. Again, super formal and not something you'd hear at the palengke. 'Panlabas' is the everyday go-to word. Using 'eksterno' is like wearing a full barong to a beach party.
usage_notes: Very rare in modern Tagalog. Usually replaced by 'panlabas' or the English 'external'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating isaalang-alang ang mga salik na **eksterno**.","translation":"We need to consider the **external** factors."},{"sentence":"Ang kumpanya ay kumuha ng auditor na **eksterno**.","translation":"The company hired an **external** auditor."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lugar, kalagayan, o resulta na layuning marating o kahihinatnan ng isang bagay, tao, o pangyayari.
etymology: From the structure pa- + (reduplication of first syllable of root) + root + -han. Specifically: pa- + tu- + tungo + -han. 'Tungo' means 'towards'.
original_explanation: This is the 'Saan ba tayo pupunta?' of life, relationships, and Grab rides. It can be a literal destination like 'Ayala Triangle,' or the figurative destination of your confusing 'M.U.' (mutual understanding) status. 'Ano ba'ng patutunguhan nito?' is the official question of people who need to DTR (define the relationship).
usage_notes: A very common and versatile word for both literal destinations (places) and figurative ones (future, consequences, goals).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi natin alam ang **patutunguhan** ng ating bansa.","translation":"We do not know what the **outcome** for our country will be."},{"sentence":"Ang terminal na ito ang **patutunguhan** ng lahat ng bus galing probinsya.","translation":"This terminal is the **destination** for all buses from the province."}]

translation: something used for beating; a club or cudgel
meaning_filipino: Anumang kasangkapan o bagay na ginagamit sa pananakit o paghampas nang malakas sa isang tao, hayop, o bagay.
original_explanation: This is the weapon of choice for angry moms: the tsinelas, the walis tambo, the sinturon. Anything that can be used to deliver a good old-fashioned 'palo'. It's the 'instrument of disciplinary action' in a Filipino household, or in a more serious context, any blunt object used in a fight.
usage_notes: Can refer to any object used for beating, not just a formal weapon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang isang piraso ng kahoy bilang **pambugbog**.","translation":"He used a piece of wood as a **cudgel**."},{"sentence":"Nahanap ng pulisya ang **pambugbog** na ginamit sa krimen.","translation":"The police found the **weapon used for beating** in the crime."}]

meaning_filipino: Lisanin ang isang pook; tumulak patungo sa ibang lugar.
original_explanation: The classic Filipino 'ghosting' move. One minute they're there, the next, 'Paalam!'. Also what you want to do 5 minutes into a mandatory 3-hour meeting. The most common excuse to get out of anything: 'Sige, alis na 'ko.'
usage_notes: One of the most fundamental and frequently used verbs in Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umalis** siya nang walang paalam.","translation":"He/She **left** without saying goodbye."},{"sentence":"Kailangan na nating **umalis** para hindi tayo ma-traffic.","translation":"We need **to leave** now so we don't get stuck in traffic."}]

translation: to make hungry; to starve someone
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-udyok o pagdulot ng pakiramdam ng gutom sa isang tao o hayop; hindi pagbibigay ng sapat na pagkain.
original_explanation: This is what happens when your friend promises 'libre' but then suddenly has 'amnesia.' You get *gutumin*. It's the act of intentionally or unintentionally making someone starve. It can also refer to the state of being easily made hungry. 'Gutom na 'ko, 'wag mo 'kong gutumin sa kwento mo.'
usage_notes: Can be used as a command ('Huwag mo siyang gutumin!') or to describe a person's tendency ('Madali akong gutumin.').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **gutumin** ang alaga mong aso.","translation":"Don't **starve** your pet dog."},{"sentence":"Mukhang planong **gutumin** ng kontrabida ang buong bayan.","translation":"It looks like the villain plans to **make** the whole town **hungry**."}]

translation: to lose one's mind, to go crazy
meaning_filipino: Mawalan ng tamang pag-iisip o katinuan; maging baliw.
etymology: Idiomatic phrase, literally "to be broken of one's sanity/good judgment".
original_explanation: What your mom threatens will happen to her if you don't clean your room. It’s what you feel during a final exam you didn't study for, or when the WiFi dies in the middle of an important Zoom call. It can be a serious term for a mental breakdown or a hyperbolic way to say you're extremely stressed or frustrated.
usage_notes: Can be used seriously to refer to insanity or hyperbolically for extreme stress or anger. Past tense is 'nasiraan ng bait'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang problema, tila siya ay **masisiraan na ng bait**.","translation":"With so many problems, it seems like he is about **to lose his mind**."},{"sentence":"**Nasisiraan ka na ba ng bait**? Bakit mo ginawa iyon?","translation":"Are you **going crazy**? Why did you do that?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang makaramdam ng pagkabagot o pagkainip dahil sa kawalan ng interes o gawain.
original_explanation: That feeling you get during a 3-hour meeting that could have been an email. Or when you've scrolled through your entire social media feed and there's nothing new. You're starting to mabagot. It's the official state of being when there's a brownout and your phone is at 1%.
usage_notes: A very common verb to express boredom.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula na akong **mabagot** sa kahihintay sa iyo.","translation":"I'm starting **to be bored** from waiting for you."},{"sentence":"Para hindi ka **mabagot**, magbasa ka ng libro.","translation":"So that you won't **be bored**, read a book."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal at mapaglarong paraan ng pagtawag sa isang kaibigang babae o sa isang kaibigang bading, na hango sa salitang Ingles na "sister".
etymology: Isang pagbabago sa baybay (spelling) ng salitang balbal na "sis," na pinaikling anyo ng "sister" sa Ingles. Karaniwang ginagamit sa social media at chat.
original_explanation: The Gen Z evolution of "sis" or "bes." It's what you call your work bestie when you're about to spill some major tea (chismis). "Sissszt, may balita ako!" It's the "psst" of the modern marites. The 'zt' at the end just adds that extra ✨spice✨.
usage_notes: Kadalasang ginagamit sa online chat at social media. Itinuturing na napaka-impormal at pambeki (gay lingo) o Gen Z slang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hoy **siszt**, nakita mo ba 'yung bagong post ni crush?","translation":"Hey **sis**, did you see crush's new post?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kabuuan o panahon ng isang pag-aalsa o rebolusyon; ang mismong pangyayari ng paghihimagsik.
original_explanation: If 'himagsik' is the act of revolt, 'himagsikan' is the whole event. It's the "Philippine Revolution" event on your historical Facebook timeline. It's the entire era, the whole chaotic, history-making season finale, not just a single episode. Think of the 1896 Himagsikan—it wasn't just one fight, it was the whole revolutionary period.
usage_notes: Refers to the event or period of rebellion, often a specific historical one, like the Philippine Revolution of 1896.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming bayani ang nagbuwis ng buhay noong panahon ng **Himagsikan**.","translation":"Many heroes gave their lives during the time of the **Revolution**."},{"sentence":"Ang Sigaw ng Pugad Lawin ang hudyat ng pagsisimula ng **himagsikan**.","translation":"The Cry of Pugad Lawin was the signal for the start of the **revolution**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lubos na pagwasak, paglipol, o pag-alis sa isang bagay, tao, o grupo upang ito ay tuluyang maglaho.
etymology: From `pag-` + `puksa`. `Puksa` means to destroy or eradicate.
original_explanation: This is what you want to do to cockroaches in your kitchen, a computer virus, or fake news on your feed. It's not just defeating; it's wiping them off the face of the earth. It's the "no mercy" button. Think Thanos snap, but for ipis, corruption, or your ex's memories.
usage_notes: A very strong word implying total destruction or elimination.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng programa para sa **pagpuksa** ng mga peste sa palayan.","translation":"There was a program for the **eradication** of pests in the rice fields."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagpuksa** sa katiwalian ang pangunahing layunin ng kanyang administrasyon.","translation":"The **annihilation** of corruption is the main goal of his administration."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan naghihiwalay o nagtatagpo ang dalawa o higit pang mga daan.
original_explanation: That moment in your life (or on Waze) where you have to make a big decision. 'Should I go for Jollibee or McDo?' is a daily sangang-daan. It's the physical manifestation of 'Saan ba 'ko lulugar?'
usage_notes: Madalas ding gamitin sa matalinhagang paraan para ilarawan ang isang punto sa buhay kung saan kailangang gumawa ng mahalagang desisyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkita kami sa **sangang-daan** papuntang bayan.","translation":"We met at the **intersection** on the way to town."},{"sentence":"Nasa isang **sangang-daan** ang kanyang karera ngayon; kailangan niyang pumili.","translation":"His career is at a **crossroads** now; he needs to choose."}]
