meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halaman na kahawig ng luya (Curcuma zedoaria), ngunit may ibang katangian at gamit, kadalasang tumutubo nang ligaw.
original_explanation: The 'dupe' or 'inspired by' version of ginger you find in the wild. It looks like `luya`, smells kinda like `luya`, but it's not quite the `luya` you use for tinola. It's the plant equivalent of seeing someone who looks exactly like your ex from a distance. Close, but no cigar.
usage_notes: Refers to a different species of plant that resembles ginger. The repetition of the root word often implies "imitation" or "resemblance".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ugat ng **luya-luyahan** ay ginagamit din sa tradisyonal na panggagamot.","translation":"The root of the **wild ginger** is also used in traditional medicine."},{"sentence":"May nakita akong tumutubong **luya-luyahan** sa likod-bahay.","translation":"I saw some **wild ginger** growing in the backyard."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halaman na may bungang bungkos-bungkos (bulb) na ginagamit bilang pampalasa sa pagluluto at may halagang medikal.
original_explanation: The holy grail of Filipino cooking, alongside onion and tomato. If you're not starting a dish by sautéing bawang, are you even cooking Pinoy food? It's also the legendary weakness of the aswang (vampire-like creature), so it's both a kitchen staple and a supernatural repellent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-gisa ka ng maraming **bawang** para sa adobo.","translation":"Sauté a lot of **garlic** for the adobo."},{"sentence":"Nagsabit sila ng **bawang** sa bintana para itaboy ang masasamang espiritu.","translation":"They hung **garlic** on the window to ward off evil spirits."}]

translation: a piece of land, a plot of land
meaning_filipino: Isang partikular na sukat o bahagi ng lupain, na karaniwang may pagmamay-ari o partikular na gamit.
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino dream, second only to a US visa. It's the goal of every OFW, the subject of every teleserye where the hacienderos fight. Owning a 'kapirasong lupa' means you've made it – you can finally build your dream house or plant some kamote.
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang parirala na may malaking bigat sa kultura na nauugnay sa pagmamay-ari, pamilya, at pamana.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap ng bawat Pilipino ang magkaroon ng sariling **kapirasong lupa**.","translation":"It is the dream of every Filipino to own their own **piece of land**."},{"sentence":"Ipinaglaban nila ang kanilang karapatan sa **kapirasong lupa** na minana pa sa kanilang mga ninuno.","translation":"They fought for their right to the **plot of land** inherited from their ancestors."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na hindi maaaring mangyari o magawa; hindi kayang maisakatuparan.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na mag-commute sa EDSA nang hindi nat-traffic. O 'yung pag-asa mong mag-reply si crush. 'Yan, **imposible**. But as they say, 'Walang imposible sa taong may pangarap... at maraming pera.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Imposible** na makarating tayo doon sa loob ng sampung minuto.","translation":"It's **impossible** for us to get there in ten minutes."},{"sentence":"Para sa kanya, walang bagay na **imposible** kung magsisikap ka.","translation":"For him/her, nothing is **impossible** if you work hard."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng labis at hindi tapat na pagpupuri o pagpapakita ng paggalang sa isang tao, karaniwan ay para makakuha ng pabor.
etymology: Mula sa `pagka-` (katangian ng) at `malambis`. Ang `lambis` ay nangangahulugang paglalambing, ngunit ang anyong `malambis` ay nagkaroon ng negatibong konotasyon ng hindi totoong pagpapakitang-gilas.
original_explanation: Ito yung art of being a 'sipsip' or a 'tuta'. Yung kaklase mong laging nagbubuhat ng bag ng teacher. Yung officemate na taga-timpla ng kape ng boss at laging tumatawa sa mga corny na jokes niya. It's exaggerated flattery with a hidden agenda. Level 99 'sipsip'.
usage_notes: Isang matinding at negatibong termino para sa isang taong sumusubok na makakuha ng pabor sa pamamagitan ng labis na papuri.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halata ang kanyang **pagka-malambis** sa boss para ma-promote.","translation":"His **sycophancy** towards the boss is obvious for him to get promoted."},{"sentence":"Hindi nadadala sa **pagka-malambis** ang matalinong lider.","translation":"A wise leader is not swayed by **fawning**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sangay ng heolohiya na nakatuon sa pag-aaral ng mga materyales na bumubuo sa Daigdig at sa pag-unawa sa mga heolohikong proseso na nagaganap sa ibabaw at sa ilalim nito.
original_explanation: This is the 'how it works' manual for Planet Earth. It explains the nitty-gritty of *how* volcanoes erupt, *how* mountains are formed, and *how* earthquakes happen. It's the physics behind all the planet's dramatic moments. Think of it as the 'now' of geology, while historical geology is the 'then.'
usage_notes: Isang pangunahing kurso sa pag-aaral ng heolohiya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-aaral ng mga mineral at bato ay isang pangunahing bahagi ng **heolohiyang pisiko**.","translation":"The study of minerals and rocks is a fundamental part of **physical geology**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sangay ng heolohiya na tumutukoy sa pag-aaral ng kimika, istrukturang kristal, at pisikal na katangian ng mga mineral.
original_explanation: The science of rocks and shiny things. It's what geologists do when they're not just hitting rocks with hammers. They're actually studying the crystal structure, asking 'What are you made of?' like a jowa, but to a piece of quartz.
usage_notes: A technical, scientific term. Not used in everyday conversation unless discussing geology.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-aaral siya ng **mineralohiya** sa unibersidad.","translation":"He/She is studying **mineralogy** at the university."},{"sentence":"Ayon sa **mineralohiya**, ang diyamante ay isa sa pinakamatitigas na materyales.","translation":"According to **mineralogy**, diamond is one of the hardest materials."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang indibidwal na lalaki na may kaparehong mga magulang sa isa pa, o may isa man lang na magulang na kapareho.
original_explanation: Your 'kuya' or 'bunso' who is your partner in crime for DOTA or basketball, but also the first one to eat the last piece of lechon. He's the one you can count on for protection, but also the one who'll tease you mercilessly about your crush. 'Lalake' is a common spoken variant of 'lalaki'.
usage_notes: Madalas na pinaikli sa 'kapatid'. Ang 'Kuya' ay ginagamit para sa nakatatandang kapatid na lalaki. Ang 'lalake' ay isang karaniwang alternatibong baybay/pagbigkas para sa 'lalaki'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagtanggol ako ng aking **kapatid na lalaki** mula sa mga nambubully.","translation":"My **brother** defended me from the bullies."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagmamasid sa paligid nang walang partikular na layunin; ang paglibot ng paningin.
original_explanation: This is the official verb for "window shopping." You go to the mall with no money, and when the sales associate asks, "May I help you, ma'am/sir?" you reply, "Tumingin-tingin lang." It's looking without the intention to buy, searching without knowing what you're looking for, or simply observing your surroundings. It's the 'explore' mode of the eyes.
usage_notes: The repetition of "tingin" indicates a casual, non-focused, or repeated action of looking.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko lang **tumingin-tingin** sa mga bagong labas na libro.","translation":"I just want to **browse** the newly released books."},{"sentence":"**Tumingin-tingin** ka muna sa paligid bago ka tumawid ng kalsada.","translation":"**Look around** first before you cross the street."}]

translation: to attract; to entice; to charm
meaning_filipino: Gumamit ng panghalina o daya upang mahikayat o mapalapit ang isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: This is the art of 'landi' but with more effort. It’s what you do to get your crush's attention, what a sales agent does to make you buy something you don't need, or what a new K-pop group does to make you join their fandom. It's the power to pull people in.
usage_notes: Can be used for romantic attraction, commercial persuasion, or even luring animals.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang **mang-akit** ng mga bagong kliyente para sa kanyang negosyo.","translation":"He is trying to **attract** new clients for his business."},{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng kanyang ngiti ay sapat na para **mang-akit** ng kahit sino.","translation":"Her beautiful smile is enough to **charm** anyone."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan na yari sa lona o ibang matibay na tela na may dalawang poste sa magkabilang gilid, ginagamit sa pagbuhat at paglipat ng mga maysakit o sugatan.
original_explanation: Yung parang portable bed na dinadala ng mga medics kapag may emergency. Hopefully, hindi mo kailanganin, pero ito yung sinasakyan ng mga bida sa teleserye papasok ng ER, usually in slow motion with dramatic music.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis na isinakay sa **istretser** ang pasyenteng walang malay.","translation":"The unconscious patient was quickly placed on the **stretcher**."},{"sentence":"Nagbuhat sila ng **istretser** papunta sa ambulansya.","translation":"They carried a **stretcher** towards the ambulance."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga ari-arian na pansamantalang kinuha o pinigil ng may kapangyarihan alinsunod sa batas, karaniwan dahil sa hindi pagbabayad ng utang o bilang bahagi ng isang legal na proseso.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you don't pay your bills and the bank says 'Akin na 'yan!' to your car or house. It's the government or a court putting a giant 'DO NOT TOUCH' sign on your stuff. Parang na-hold sa customs 'yung gamit mo, but for legal reasons.
usage_notes: Isang legal at pampinansyal na termino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Embargado** ang mga ari-arian ng kumpanya dahil sa malaking pagkakautang sa buwis.","translation":"The company's assets were **seized** due to massive tax debts."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng sapat o libreng oras upang gawin ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: 'Yung status mo 'pag hindi ka naghahabol ng deadline at pwede ka pang mag-scroll sa TikTok. 'Yung sagot mo sa kaibigan mong nag-aaya, "Sige, G! May-panahon ako." Kabaliktaran ng "busy ako," ang pambansang excuse ng Pilipinas.
usage_notes: This is a very common phrase used to indicate availability. The opposite is "walang panahon".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kung **may-panahon** ka, daanan mo naman ako sa bahay.","translation":"If you **have time**, please drop by my house."},{"sentence":"Gusto ko sanang mag-aral ng bagong wika pero hindi ako **may-panahon**.","translation":"I would like to learn a new language but I don't **have the time**."}]

translation: to claim; to possess; to own
meaning_filipino: Sabihin o ideklarang sa iyo ang isang bagay; ariin o kamkamin ang isang pag-aari o katangian.
etymology: From Tagalog 'mag-' (verb prefix) + 'angkin' (to claim as one's own).
original_explanation: This is the 'dibs' verb. When you see the last piece of pizza and shout 'Akin 'yan!', you're trying to 'mag-angkin'. It can be about physical things (claiming land), abstract concepts (claiming a title), or even feelings, like that 'hugot' line, 'Huwag mong angkinin ang isang taong hiniram mo lang.' (Don't claim someone you only borrowed).
usage_notes: Can have a neutral meaning (to possess a quality) or a slightly negative one (to wrongfully claim something).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mag-angkin** ng bagay na hindi sa iyo.","translation":"Do not **claim** something that is not yours."},{"sentence":"Siya ay nag-a**angkin** ng pambihirang talino sa musika.","translation":"He **possesses** an extraordinary talent for music."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mesa o patag na istraktura na ginagamit para sa mga seremonya at pag-aalay sa relihiyon, karaniwan sa loob ng simbahan.
original_explanation: The main stage of any Filipino church. It's where the priest does his thing during mass. It's also the final destination for couples who say 'I do'—'sa harap ng altar' is the ultimate romantic goal for your lola. At home, it’s that small table in the corner with Sto. Niño, Mama Mary, and maybe some sampaguita.
usage_notes: Isang pangunahing salita sa konteksto ng relihiyon, lalo na sa Katolisismo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglakad ang nobya patungo sa **altar** kung saan naghihintay ang kanyang mapapangasawa.","translation":"The bride walked towards the **altar** where her groom was waiting."},{"sentence":"Naglagay si Lola ng mga bulaklak sa aming maliit na **altar** sa bahay.","translation":"Grandma placed flowers on our small **altar** at home."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang establisyimento kung saan ang mga tao ay nagbabayad upang kumain ng mga pagkaing inihanda sa lugar na iyon.
original_explanation: The most common way Filipinos actually spell 'restaurant' when they're not just using the English word. It's the middle ground between the 'deep Tagalog' 'restawran' and the English 'restaurant'. This is what you'd text your friend: 'Saang restoran tayo magkikita?' It's practical, understood by everyone, and gets the job done.
usage_notes: A very common spelling variant, often used interchangeably with the English 'restaurant' in informal and semi-formal writing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghahanap kami ng isang murang **restoran** na masarap ang pagkain.","translation":"We are looking for a cheap **restaurant** with delicious food."},{"sentence":"Ipinagdiwang nila ang kanilang anibersaryo sa isang mamahaling **restoran**.","translation":"They celebrated their anniversary at an expensive **restaurant**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay o substansiya na may kakayahang maging sanhi ng pagkalaglag o hindi planadong pagtatapos ng pagbubuntis.
original_explanation: This is a serious, old-school term you might hear from your lola when she warns you not to eat too much pineapple or drink a certain herbal tea when you're pregnant. It refers to anything believed to cause a miscarriage. It's a heavy word, not for everyday chika.
usage_notes: A very specific and formal/medical term. "Agas" itself means miscarriage. The complex affixation indicates a strong causative effect.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May mga halamang-gamot na pinaniniwalaang **nakapagpapaagas**.","translation":"There are herbal medicines that are believed to be **abortifacient**."},{"sentence":"Mahigpit na ipinagbabawal ng doktor ang anumang gamot na **nakapagpapaagas** sa mga buntis.","translation":"The doctor strictly forbids any medicine that **causes miscarriage** for pregnant women."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang nakakahawang sakit sa baga na nagdudulot ng matinding pag-ubo, karaniwang nararanasan ng mga bata.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'tos ferina' (mabangis na ubo).
original_explanation: This is the formal, medical term for 'ubong-dalahit'. It's that super intense cough that makes you sound like you're trying to start a stubborn two-stroke motorcycle. It's not just a simple 'ubo'; it's the final boss of coughs that requires a doctor's visit, not just a glass of water.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa mga kontekstong medikal o pormal. Ang karaniwang tawag dito sa pang-araw-araw na usapan ay 'ubong-dalahit'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang bakuna laban sa **tosperina** para sa mga sanggol.","translation":"The vaccine against **whooping cough** is important for babies."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging malago, masagana, at mayabong, karaniwang tumutukoy sa mga halaman o pananim.
original_explanation: Imagine a plant so happy, it's practically throwing a party with its leaves. That's kayabungan. It's the thicc-ness of a jungle, the vibrant green of your Lola's well-cared-for garden after a summer rain. It's the opposite of that sad, dying succulent on your windowsill. #PlantitaGoals
usage_notes: Primarily used for plants, forests, or hair. Can be used metaphorically for a flourishing culture or economy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakamangha ang **kayabungan** ng mga puno sa gubat ng Palawan.","translation":"The **lushness** of the trees in the Palawan forest is amazing."},{"sentence":"Ipinagmamalaki niya ang **kayabungan** ng kanyang buhok.","translation":"She is proud of the **luxuriance** of her hair."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang modernong kaisipan o pilosopiya, karaniwang laganap sa internet, na nagpapahayag ng isang pesimistikong pananaw sa buhay, relasyon, o lipunan, at naniniwalang ang tagumpay ay paunang natutukoy ng mga hindi nababagong katangian tulad ng itsura.
etymology: From English 'black pill', an internet subculture term.
original_explanation: This isn't a vitamin. It's a dark, doomer mindset you find in the weird corners of the internet. It's the ultimate 'wala na, finish na' philosophy, believing that some people are just destined to lose in life, especially in dating, because of things they can't change. It's the final boss of hugot, but without any of the poetry.
usage_notes: A very specific internet slang term. Not used in general conversation by most Filipinos.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong magbabad sa mga forum na iyan, baka ma-**blackpill** ka.","translation":"Don't spend too much time on those forums, you might get **blackpilled**."},{"sentence":"Ang paniniwala sa **blackpill** ay isang anyo ng matinding pesimismo.","translation":"Believing in the **blackpill** is a form of extreme pessimism."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi tuloy-tuloy; paputol-putol o may mga pagitan sa daloy o koneksyon.
original_explanation: This is your PLDT internet connection during a typhoon. It's that one friend who replies to your chat one message at a time, with 5-minute intervals. It's the audio on a Zoom call when someone has bad signal. "Bakit **patid-patid** ang salita mo? Naka-data ka lang?"
usage_notes: Describes anything that is not continuous, whether it's a signal, a sound, a supply, or even speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Patid-patid** ang signal ng Wi-Fi kaya nahihirapan akong magtrabaho.","translation":"The Wi-Fi signal is **intermittent**, so I'm having a hard time working."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa ubo, **patid-patid** ang kanyang pagsasalita.","translation":"Because of his cough, his speech was **choppy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kawalan ng tiwala o pananalig sa isang tao, bagay, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: That feeling you get when someone says 'On the way na ako' but you know they're still in the shower. It's the reason why you double-check the 'sukli' from the tindera. The foundation of most 'praning' moments.
usage_notes: Can refer to distrust in others or a lack of self-confidence, though the former is more common. Often used interchangeably with the adjective 'diskompiyado'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **diskumpyansa** ako sa kanyang mga sinasabi.","translation":"I have **distrust** in what he is saying."},{"sentence":"Nawala ang **diskumpyansa** niya nang patunayan ng kaibigan ang katapatan nito.","translation":"His **distrust** disappeared when his friend proved his loyalty."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagpapaputi ng damit o tela gamit ang isang kemikal na substansya, karaniwang klorina.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa ng nanay mo sa mga puting damit para tanggalin ang mga mantsa na parang mga pagkakamali mo sa buhay—mahirap tanggalin pero pilit pa ring sinusubukan. From 'kula', the bleaching agent itself.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy lamang sa pagpapaputi ng labada, hindi ng buhok.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **magkula** ng mga uniporme para sa susunod na linggo.","translation":"I need to **bleach** the uniforms for next week."},{"sentence":"Tinuruan siya ng kanyang lola kung paano **magkula** nang hindi nasisira ang tela.","translation":"Her grandmother taught her how to **bleach** without damaging the fabric."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtanaw o pagmamasid sa isang palabas, pelikula, o anumang kaganapan bilang isang manonood.
original_explanation: Ang paboritong hobby ng Pinoy. From Netflix series marathon hanggang sa chismis sa kapitbahay, basta may mapapanood, game! 'Tara, nood tayo sine.' is the ultimate low-effort date invitation.
usage_notes: Ito ay ang salitang-ugat. Mas madalas gamitin ang anyong pandiwa nito tulad ng 'manood' o 'nanonood'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puro ka na lang **nood** ng TV, wala ka nang ginawang iba.","translation":"All you do is **watch** TV, you haven't done anything else."},{"sentence":"Yayain mo siyang mag-**nood** ng sine sa Sabado.","translation":"Ask him/her to **watch** a movie on Saturday."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aani o pagkuha ng mga produkto mula sa mga pananim, tulad ng palay, prutas, at gulay. Tumutukoy rin ito sa mismong mga produktong inani.
original_explanation: The payday for farmers. It's the result of all the hard work under the sun, the literal fruit (or grain) of your labor. In modern terms, it's that feeling of finally getting your 13th-month pay after a long year of grinding. Reap what you sow, literally.
usage_notes: Can refer to the act of harvesting or the harvested crops themselves.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masagana ang **ani** ng palay ngayong taon.","translation":"The rice **harvest** is bountiful this year."},{"sentence":"Panahon na ng **ani** ng mangga sa aming probinsya.","translation":"It's the season for the mango **harvest** in our province."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyon na nagpapahiwatig ng matinding pagkahumaling, paghanga, o pag-ibig sa isang tao.
etymology: Reduplication of 'patay' (dead) for emphasis, used figuratively for intense emotion.
original_explanation: This is that level of crush where you'd willingly go through Manila traffic on a payday Friday just to see them for 5 minutes. You're so into them, your brain cells have stopped functioning normally. You're 'patay na patay', and your friends are tired of hearing about it. It can also mean 'completely dead,' but that's less romantic.
usage_notes: The meaning (love vs. literally dead) is highly dependent on context. 'Patay na patay si Maria kay Juan' means she's in love. 'Patay na patay ang ipis' means the cockroach is very, very dead.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halata sa mga ngiti niya na **patay na patay** siya sa kanyang kasintahan.","translation":"It's obvious from her smiles that she is **head over heels** for her boyfriend."},{"sentence":"Siguraduhin mong **patay na patay** ang apoy bago umalis ng kampo.","translation":"Make sure the fire is **completely out** before leaving the camp."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang magkabilang panig na paghihiganti o pagbibigay ng ganti sa isa't isa.
etymology: `pag-` + reduplication of the first syllable of the root `ga-` + `ganti` + `-han`. The structure implies a reciprocal or mutual action.
original_explanation: This is the plot of every teleserye ever. It's the 'you wronged me, so I'll wrong you back, then you'll wrong me again' cycle. It's when you and your workmate keep hiding each other's coffee mugs. A never-ending cycle of 'Akin ang huling halakhak!' (The last laugh is mine!).
usage_notes: Emphasizes the reciprocal nature of the revenge, a back-and-forth action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Walang katapusan ang **paggagantihan** ng dalawang pamilya.","translation":"The **mutual retaliation** between the two families is endless."},{"sentence":"Itigil na natin ang **paggagantihan** na ito para magkaroon na ng kapayapaan.","translation":"Let's stop this **cycle of revenge** so there can be peace."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagkaing Hapones na binubuo ng mga sariwa at hilaw na isda o karne na hiniwa nang manipis at karaniwang isinasawsaw sa toyo na may wasabi.
original_explanation: That fancy Japanese food you order to show you're a foodie. It’s basically 'kinilaw' but with a Japanese passport and a higher price tag. The true test of a legit Japanese restaurant is the freshness of its sashimi. If it tastes fishy, 'yun na ang sign para 'di na bumalik.
usage_notes: A loanword from Japanese, widely understood in the Philippines, especially in urban areas and among food enthusiasts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umorder tayo ng tuna **sashimi** at salmon **sashimi**.","translation":"Let's order tuna **sashimi** and salmon **sashimi**."},{"sentence":"Sariwa ba ang **sashimi** dito?","translation":"Is the **sashimi** here fresh?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paligsahan o pagtatanghal ng pagbigkas ng tula nang may angkop na damdamin at kilos.
original_explanation: Before rap battles, there was `bigkasan`. This is the OG spoken word event you were forced to join during Buwan ng Wika. It's declaiming "Ang Magsasaka" with so much drama, you'd think you actually planted a grain of rice in your life. It's performance art with a very specific, and often very loud, Filipino flavor.
usage_notes: Refers to the event or contest itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumali siya sa **bigkasan** noong Buwan ng Wika at nanalo ng unang gantimpala.","translation":"She joined the **poetry recital** during the National Language Month and won first prize."},{"sentence":"Naghahanda ang mga mag-aaral para sa taunang **bigkasan** sa kanilang paaralan.","translation":"The students are preparing for the annual **elocution contest** in their school."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hindi kanais-nais na amoy na nagmumula sa katawan ng tao, partikular sa kili-kili, dulot ng pawis at bakterya.
original_explanation: Ah, "anghit." The official scent of a crowded MRT at 5 PM. It’s that specific, pungent underarm aroma that makes you question your life choices and your proximity to other humans. The fear of having it is why the deodorant aisle is a war zone. If someone tells you "May naamoy ako," you discreetly check if it's you.
usage_notes: Very specific to armpit odor. Often used in a teasing or insulting manner, but also as a self-deprecating joke. A related term is 'putok'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakalimutan kong mag-deodorant, baka amoy **anghit** na ako mamaya.","translation":"I forgot to put on deodorant, I might have **armpit odor** later."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang tumabi sa akin, malakas ang **anghit** mo!","translation":"Don't stand next to me, your **armpit odor** is strong!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na nangangahulugang 'wala'. Ginagamit din upang ipahiwatig na ang isang bagay ay hindi nakakatawa, walang bisa, o hindi nagustuhan.
etymology: From Tagalog `wala` (none), popularized through Swardspeak (Filipino gay lingo).
original_explanation: The Swardspeak (gay lingo) version of 'wala'. It's more than just 'nothing'. It's a whole mood. When a joke falls flat? 'Waley.' When your crush doesn't notice your new haircut? 'Waley.' When your grand plan fails spectacularly? 'Mega-waley!' It's the sassy, slightly disappointed, and infinitely more expressive cousin of the boring old 'wala'.
usage_notes: Highly informal and colloquial. Often used to express disappointment or that something is not funny.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-joke siya pero **waley**, walang tumawa.","translation":"He told a joke but it was **lame**, no one laughed."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan ko siyang suyuin pero **waley** pa rin, galit pa rin siya.","translation":"I tried to win her over but still **nothing**, she's still mad."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang idyomatikong pahayag na nangangahulugan ng matinding galit o pagkainis sa isang tao o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: Literally "blood is boiling." This is the feeling you get when the internet connection dies during a crucial online meeting, or when someone spoils the ending of the K-drama you're binge-watching. It's not just 'galit' (angry), it's next-level, thermal-meltdown angry. You can feel the rage bubbling up inside you.
usage_notes: An idiomatic expression for intense anger. The verb `kumukulo` is in the present progressive form, indicating an ongoing state of anger.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumukulo ang dugo** ko sa tuwing nakikita ko ang taong nanloko sa akin.","translation":"My **blood boils** whenever I see the person who cheated me."},{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **kumukulo ang dugo** ng mga mamamayan dahil sa walang-tigil na korapsyon.","translation":"The citizens' **blood began to boil** because of the relentless corruption."}]
related: ["galit na galit","nag-iinit ang ulo","poot","sukdulan ang galit"]

meaning_filipino: Ang pakiramdam ng pag-ikot ng paligid, pagkawala ng balanse, o panlalabo ng paningin.
original_explanation: This is what you feel after riding the Viking at the 'perya', or after your third bottle of Red Horse. It's also the feeling you get when you see your credit card bill after a 12.12 sale. It can be literal (biya-hilo) or metaphorical (hilo sa dami ng trabaho).
usage_notes: Can refer to literal dizziness, motion sickness (bya-hilo), or a feeling of being overwhelmed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uminom siya ng gamot para sa kanyang **pagkahilo** tuwing bumibiyahe.","translation":"She took medicine for her **dizziness** whenever she traveled."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang biglaang **pagkahilo** kaya napaupo siya.","translation":"She felt a sudden **dizziness** so she had to sit down."}]

translation: at that very moment, right then
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa eksaktong sandali o panahon sa nakaraan na binanggit; kaagad-agad sa oras na iyon.
original_explanation: The 'samedt' of the past. When something happens right at the very moment you're talking about. 'Nakarating ako sa office, at noon din, biglang bumuhos ang ulan. Saved by the bell!'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinabi kong darating ako, at **noon din** ay tumawag siya.","translation":"I said I was coming, and **at that very moment** she called."},{"sentence":"Nang matanggap niya ang balita, **noon din** ay umalis siya papuntang ospital.","translation":"When he received the news, **right then** he left for the hospital."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-aangkop o pagbabagay ng sariling kilos at gawi sa ugali o kultura ng iba.
original_explanation: This is "When in Rome, do as the Romans do," but in the Philippine context. It's taking off your shoes before entering a house, eating with your hands at a "boodle fight," or learning to say "po" and "opo" when you're with your partner's family. It's social camouflage to show respect and get along.
usage_notes: Implies a conscious effort to adapt one's behavior to fit in with a group or social situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mabilis niyang **pakikiugali** sa aming pamilya ay hinangaan ng lahat.","translation":"His quick **adaptation to our family's ways** was admired by everyone."},{"sentence":"Bahagi ng pagiging dayuhan ang matutunan ang **pakikiugali** sa bagong kultura.","translation":"Part of being a foreigner is learning how to **conform to the customs** of a new culture."}]

translation: to engage in combat; to join a fight
meaning_filipino: Sumali o makipaglaban sa isang gulo, digmaan, o anumang uri ng tunggalian.
original_explanation: This is some next-level, epic movie stuff. Not just a simple "away" or "suntukan." This is when you join a massive battle, like something out of an RPG or a historical film. You don't just "makihamok" over the last piece of lechon; this is for serious, life-or-death conflicts.
usage_notes: A more formal and literary term for joining a battle or large-scale conflict.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga mandirigma ay handang **makihamok** para sa kalayaan ng kanilang bayan.","translation":"The warriors are ready to **engage in combat** for their country's freedom."},{"sentence":"Nag-atubili siyang **makihamok** dahil alam niyang walang maidudulot na mabuti ang digmaan.","translation":"He hesitated to **join the fight** because he knew war would bring nothing good."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maingat at matamang pagtingin sa mga pangyayari, kilos, o kapaligiran upang matuto o makakuha ng impormasyon.
original_explanation: This is the SFW (safe for work) version of 'magmanman'. It's what scientists, security guards, and curious cats do. You magmasid to understand, not to snoop. It's paying close attention to your surroundings, like when you're people-watching at a coffee shop or waiting for your Shopee delivery to arrive.
usage_notes: A general term for observation, more neutral than 'magmanman' and more focused than just 'tumingin' (to look).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong umupo lang dito at **magmasid** sa mga taong dumadaan.","translation":"I just want to sit here and **observe** the people passing by."},{"sentence":"Pinayuhan ng doktor ang nars na maiging **magmasid** sa kondisyon ng pasyente.","translation":"The doctor advised the nurse to closely **watch** the patient's condition."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katotohanan, pangyayari, o bagay na maoobserbahan, lalo na kung ito ay pambihira o mahirap ipaliwanag.
original_explanation: That thing that happens that makes everyone go 'Woah!' and pull out their phones to record it. It could be a supermoon, the rise of an AlDub-level love team, or the fact that your internet is suddenly fast. It's something remarkable, unusual, or just plain weird that gets everyone talking. A 'viral' event before 'viral' was a word.
usage_notes: The 'f' in the original Spanish 'fenómeno' is changed to 'p', which is common in older Tagalog borrowings. The modern, more direct borrowing 'phenomenon' is also used in educated circles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Aldub ay isang malaking **penomeno** sa social media noong 2015.","translation":"Aldub was a huge social media **phenomenon** in 2015."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng mga siyentista ang kakaibang **penomeno** sa kalangitan.","translation":"Scientists are studying the strange **phenomenon** in the sky."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapatunay o paglalahad ng personal na kaalaman tungkol sa isang pangyayari, lalo na sa isang pormal na pagdinig o sa ilalim ng panunumpa.
original_explanation: This is what a 'Marites' does, but in court. Instead of just gossiping at the sari-sari store, you're formally telling a judge what you saw. To magbigay-saksi is to be the official human dashcam, recounting the events as they happened, hopefully without the dramatic sound effects.
usage_notes: Primarily used in legal, religious, or very formal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Handa siyang **magbigay-saksi** sa korte laban sa akusado.","translation":"She is ready to **testify** in court against the accused."},{"sentence":"Ang mga bituin ay tila **nagbibigay-saksi** sa kanilang pag-iibigan.","translation":"The stars seem to **bear witness** to their love."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kopya ng isang nalathalang aklat, magasin, o pahayagan. Isang bagay na tipikal o huwaran ng isang partikular na uri.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung isang piraso ng libro o komiks na binili mo. "Ilang ehemplar ng bagong manga ang dumating?" Parang sa science, ito 'yung sample na kinuha mo to represent the whole group, 'yung specimen.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroon akong sampung **ehemplar** ng unang edisyon ng librong iyon.","translation":"I have ten **copies** of the first edition of that book."},{"sentence":"Ang natagpuang halaman ay isang pambihirang **ehemplar** ng uri nito.","translation":"The plant found is a rare **specimen** of its kind."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pook o tindahan kung saan naghahanda at nagbebenta ng mga gamot at iba pang kagamitang medikal.
original_explanation: Your go-to place when you have a headache from work or a heartache from your ex. Dito ka bumibili ng Biogesic para sa lagnat at Alaxan para sa 'sakit ng katawan.' It's the S.O.S. station for both physical and sometimes, emotional (chocolate section) emergencies.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng gamot sa **botika**.","translation":"I bought medicine at the **pharmacy**."},{"sentence":"May 24-hour na **botika** ba malapit dito?","translation":"Is there a 24-hour **drugstore** near here?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng isang partikular na bagay o mga bagay sa loob ng isang lalagyan. Ito ay isang pandiwang tumutukoy sa obheto ng pag-eempake.
original_explanation: This is the more specific 'what to pack' version. While 'mag-empake' is the general action, 'empakihin' is you telling your brain what specific items need to make it into the luggage. 'Empakihin mo na yang mga de lata!' is what your mom says when the balikbayan box is 90% full but she spots more stuff.
usage_notes: This is an object-focused verb. The action is being done *to* something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Empakihin** mo na ang lahat ng damit na dadalhin natin.","translation":"**Pack** all the clothes we are bringing."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **empakihin** ang charger ng telepono mo.","translation":"Don't forget to **pack** your phone charger."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging sanhi ng pag-antala o paghihintay ng isang tao.
original_explanation: The national pastime, also known as 'Filipino time.' This is what your friend does when they say 'On the way na!' but they're actually still in the shower. It's the act of causing someone else to wait for you. Whether it's a late doctor, a slow government process, or a perpetually tardy friend, someone is 'nagpapahintay.'
usage_notes: Often carries a negative connotation, implying inconsiderateness. The object-focus form is 'paghintayin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw na ayaw niyang **magpahintay** ng mga tao, kaya palagi siyang maaga.","translation":"He really dislikes **making people wait**, so he is always early."},{"sentence":"**Nagpahintay** ang bus ng tatlumpung minuto bago umalis.","translation":"The bus **made (us) wait** for thirty minutes before leaving."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na pagpapaikli at pagsasama ng mga salitang Ingles na "for the," na ginagamit upang magpahiwatig ng layunin, dahilan, o pagiging bahagi ng isang bagay.
etymology: Mula sa beki/swardspeak, na hinango sa Ingles na pariralang "for the."
original_explanation: Gen Z's version of "para sa." It's the swardspeak/beki-speak that crossed over to the mainstream. "Forda ferson" means it's for a specific person. "Forda go" means it's for going somewhere. It's like adding a ✨sparkle✨ to your sentence's purpose. The ultimate linguistic shortcut.
usage_notes: Highly informal and trendy slang, popular on social media platforms like TikTok and Twitter. Often used with other slang words.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang outfit na 'to ay **forda** OOTD post sa Instagram.","translation":"This outfit is **for the** OOTD post on Instagram."},{"sentence":"Okay, ready na ako. **Forda** rampa na!","translation":"Okay, I'm ready. This is **for the** catwalk/strutting now!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng pagiging mabilis makapuna o makakita ng mga detalye, pagbabago, o mga bagay na hindi karaniwang nakikita ng iba.
etymology: Mula sa `ma-` + `pansin` + `-in` (hulaping pang-uri na nagpapahiwatig ng tendensiya).
original_explanation: This is your friend who will notice your new haircut even if you only had a one-inch trim. Sila din 'yung unang makakapansin kung may something "off" sa'yo. They're the human equivalent of a magnifying glass. Great for finding your lost keys, bad if you're trying to hide a new pimple.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan ng isang personal na katangian ng pagiging mapagmasid. Huwag ipagkamali sa "kapansin-pansin" na nangangahulugang "noticeable".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil siya ay **mapansinin**, nakita niya agad ang mali sa dokumento.","translation":"Because she is **observant**, she immediately saw the error in the document."},{"sentence":"Ang pagiging **mapansinin** ay isang magandang katangian para sa isang imbestigador.","translation":"Being **observant** is a good quality for an investigator."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng nagbibigay ng regular na suporta, tulong, o pagbili sa isang tao, negosyo, o samahan.
original_explanation: She's the ultimate Tita-supporter. Not just a customer, but a *suki*. The one who promotes your small business on her socmed, brings all her amigas to your restaurant, or funds your art project. The female version of a patron, your business's fairy godmother.
usage_notes: A formal term. In everyday conversation, 'suki', 'sponsor', or 'patron' (as a loanword) are more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Donya Victoria ang aming matapat na **babaing tagatangkilik** sa teatro.","translation":"Doña Victoria is our loyal **patroness** at the theater."}]

translation: to serve; to act as a servant
meaning_filipino: Ang gampanan ang tungkulin ng isang alila; ang maglingkod o magsilbi sa isang tao o pamilya.
original_explanation: Before there were interns, there were 'alilas'. To 'umalila' is to do the bidding of a master, like being the designated 'taga-kuha ng tubig' for your demanding lola or being the one who has to do all the work in a group project.
usage_notes: This is a less common verb form than 'mag-alila' or 'alilain'. It can carry a historical or literary tone. It is important not to confuse this with 'ulila', which means 'orphan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Handa siyang **umalila** sa pamilyang kumupkop sa kanya.","translation":"He is ready **to serve** the family that took him in."},{"sentence":"Hindi tamang **umalila** sa kapwa kapalit ng utang na loob.","translation":"It is not right **to act as a servant** to someone in return for a debt of gratitude."}]

meaning_filipino: Mapangahas; walang takot o hiya sa paggawa o pagsasabi ng isang bagay na maaaring ituring na walang galang.
original_explanation: Someone with 'no filter' and zero chill. This is the person who'll ask your tita 'tumataba po yata tayo?' at a family reunion. It can be positive (a daring hero) but is more often negative (a sassy, disrespectful kid). It's boldness that borders on being rude. The '-a' version, 'atrebida', is for females. Think of a feisty telenovela kontrabida.
usage_notes: Often carries a negative connotation of being impudent or disrespectful. The feminine form is 'atrebida'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumasagot ka pa sa nanay mo, napaka-**atrebido** mong bata!","translation":"You're talking back to your mother, you **insolent** child!"},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng **atrebido** na lider para ipaglaban ang ating mga karapatan.","translation":"A **daring** leader is needed to fight for our rights."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mababang temperatura na nagdudulot ng lamig sa pakiramdam, lalo na sa hangin o panahon.
etymology: From the prefix `ma-` (indicating a quality) and the root `ginaw` (coldness, chill).
original_explanation: That feeling when you're in an air-conditioned office and you forgot your jacket. Or when you're in Baguio in December. It's not freezing like winter abroad, but it's that "kailangan ko ng kape at kumot" kind of cold. Also, your ex's heart. Charot.
usage_notes: Often used to describe weather, a breeze, or the temperature of a room or water. It is slightly less intense than 'malamig'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Maginaw** ang simoy ng hangin tuwing Pasko.","translation":"The breeze is **chilly** during Christmas."},{"sentence":"Pakihinaan ang aircon, medyo **maginaw** na dito.","translation":"Please turn down the aircon, it's getting a bit **chilly** in here."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagbili at pagbebenta ng mga produkto o serbisyo upang kumita; isang pangkalakal na establisyimento.
original_explanation: From your suking tindahan sa kanto, to the BPO company you work for, to the food cart you're dreaming of putting up. It's any activity where you exchange goods or services for cash. Pwede ring "Wag mo kong kausapin, may negosyo ako" (I'm busy).
usage_notes: Maaari ring gamitin sa kolokyal na paraan upang tukuyin ang 'usapin' o 'bagay' (hal. "Wala kang pakialam sa negosyo ko." - "It's none of your business.")
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtayo siya ng maliit na **negosyo** sa kanilang garahe.","translation":"He started a small **business** in their garage."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang pag-aaral ng merkado para sa tagumpay ng isang **negosyo**.","translation":"Studying the market is important for the success of a **business**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng isda (Siyentipikong pangalan: Decapterus macarellus) na kahawig ng galunggong, karaniwang nahuhuli sa mga karagatan ng Pilipinas.
etymology: The name might be related to its nature of staying far ("layo") or schooling behavior.
original_explanation: A fish that's part of the 'GG' (Galunggong) family. You'll see this in the palengke, chilling on ice next to its cousins, the galunggong and matambaka. It's an everyday fish, perfect for a simple 'prito' (fried) or 'paksiw' (stewed in vinegar) kind of meal. Not as famous as GG, but still a staple.
usage_notes: Primarily used in markets and kitchens.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas mura ang **layu-layo** kaysa sa galunggong ngayon.","translation":"The **mackerel scad** is cheaper than the round scad today."},{"sentence":"Nag-uwi si nanay ng isang kilong sariwang **layu-layo** mula sa palengke.","translation":"Mom brought home a kilo of fresh **mackerel scad** from the market."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging paksa ng mapilit at paulit-ulit na paghingi o pagtatanong; ang pilit na hingin ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is what you do TO someone. When you're the one doing the 'ukilkil'. Like when you 'ukilkilin' your boss for a raise after hitting all your KPIs, or when you 'ukilkilin' your friend to pay you back the 100 pesos they borrowed for a jeepney ride last week.
usage_notes: The focus of the verb is on the person or thing being pestered or the thing being insistently asked for.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Walang tigil niyang **inukilkil** sa kanyang nanay ang bagong cellphone hanggang sa ibili siya nito.","translation":"He relentlessly **pestered** his mom for a new cellphone until she bought him one."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang posisyon kung saan ang mga binti ay magkahiwalay o nakaarko palabas, na karaniwang makikita sa pag-upo o pagtayo nang nakabukaka.
etymology: Origin uncertain, possibly a portmanteau or a specific regional term that became widespread.
original_explanation: Ever seen someone ride a carabao or a horse? That's the OG bisaklat pose. In modern terms, it's how you sit on a motorcycle, especially if you're the passenger. It's the opposite of sitting "de-kwatro" (legs crossed). It's a power stance for some, and for others, it's just how their legs are built. No judgment.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a way of sitting or standing, or the physical characteristic of being bow-legged.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umupo siya nang **bisaklat** sa sahig.","translation":"He sat on the floor with his **legs apart/straddling**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong maging **bisaklat** kapag sumakay ka sa motor.","translation":"You need to **straddle** when you ride a motorcycle."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng matingkad na kulay pula na may bahid ng kahel.
original_explanation: Yung kulay ng red lipstick na pang-awra talaga, parang kontrabida sa teleserye na rich and powerful. Hindi basta pula, *eskarlata*. The color of drama and expensive things.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa panitikan o pormal na konteksto upang ilarawan ang isang partikular at matingkad na klase ng pula.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang damit ng reyna ay kulay **eskarlata**.","translation":"The queen's dress is colored **scarlet**."},{"sentence":"Namumula ang langit sa kulay **eskarlata** tuwing takipsilim.","translation":"The sky turns a **scarlet** color during twilight."}]

meaning_filipino: Mayroong malakas na hangin at ulan; naglalarawan sa isang panahon na may bagyo.
original_explanation: Ah, the official "walang pasok" weather. When PAGASA raises the signal and you start seeing memes about flying roofs and floating monobloc chairs, that's a mabagyo day. It's nature's way of telling you to stay home, drink coffee, and binge-watch.
usage_notes: Describes weather conditions characterized by a typhoon or storm.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **mabagyo** ang hapon kaya kinansela ang mga byahe ng barko.","translation":"The afternoon became **stormy** so the ship trips were cancelled."},{"sentence":"Asahan ang **mabagyo** na panahon sa mga susunod na araw.","translation":"Expect **stormy** weather in the coming days."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang taong kumikilos nang padaskul-daskol, hindi sigurado, o tila nangangapa, karaniwan dahil sa kaba o kawalan ng kasanayan.
etymology: Reduplication of 'apa', a root word related to groping or fumbling.
original_explanation: Describes how you act on a first date when you're super nervous, dropping your utensils and stuttering. "Bakit ka ba aapa-apa diyan?" It's the physical manifestation of anxiety when you're asked to do a presentation you didn't prepare for.
usage_notes: Often used to describe actions done under pressure or nervousness. It focuses more on the ineptness of movement rather than just being vacant (like aanga-anga).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **aapa-apa** ang sagot niya sa tanong ng panel.","translation":"His answer to the panel's question became **fumbling**."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kaba, naging **aapa-apa** ang kanyang mga kamay habang nagpipiyano.","translation":"Due to nervousness, his hands became **clumsy** while playing the piano."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay o paglalahad ng isang bagay, serbisyo, o tulong sa isang tao, na may kalayaang tanggapin ito o hindi.
original_explanation: The classic Filipino gesture of hospitality. When someone visits, you **mag-alok** ng food, even if it's the last piece of Skyflakes. It's what vendors in the *palengke* do ('Suki, bili na!'), what BPO agents do ('Ma'am, I can **mag-alok** you a 10% discount'), and what your friend does when they offer you a ride.
usage_notes: A fundamental verb in social and commercial interactions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nag-alok** siya ng tulong sa kanyang kapitbahay na nasalanta ng baha.","translation":"He **offered** help to his neighbor who was affected by the flood."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mahiyang **mag-alok** ng iyong mga ideya sa pulong.","translation":"Don't be shy to **offer** your ideas during the meeting."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pag-aalis ng mga lukot sa damit gamit ang isang pinainit na plantsa.
etymology: Mula sa `mang-` + `pirinsa`. Ang 'pirinsa' ay hango sa salitang Espanyol na 'prensa' (press).
original_explanation: The ultimate "adulting" chore. Yung kailangan mo nang gawin para hindi ka magmukhang gusgusin sa office o sa Zoom call. Ito yung dahilan kung bakit mataas ang bill nyo sa kuryente. "Sino'ng nakatoka mamirinsa this week?"
usage_notes: Isang mas pormal o tradisyonal na termino para sa 'magplantsa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko pang **mamirinsa** ng uniporme ko para bukas.","translation":"I still need to **iron** my uniform for tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Tinatamad akong **mamirinsa** ngayong gabi.","translation":"I feel lazy to **iron clothes** tonight."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay ng arko sa isang lugar o istruktura.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "arko" at hulaping "-han".
original_explanation: Action word ito. 'Pag sinabing "arkuhan niyo 'yan," ibig sabihin, lagyan niyo ng arko. Karaniwang utos 'to ng barangay captain o ng event organizer bago mag-fiesta. "Arkuhan ang entablado! Arkuhan ang kalsada!"
usage_notes: Ginagamit bilang pandiwa na nangangahulugang lagyan ng arko.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan ng meyor na **arkuhan** ang lahat ng pangunahing daan patungo sa plasa.","translation":"The mayor ordered to **put an arch on** all the main roads leading to the plaza."},{"sentence":"\"Paki-**arkuhan** na ang stage bago magsimula ang programa,\" sabi ng direktor.","translation":"\"Please **put an arch on** the stage before the program starts,\" said the director."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang anak na babae ng tiyuhin o tiyahin ng isang tao.
original_explanation: Your `prima` is your Tita's daughter who you either see every family reunion or you only know exists through Facebook tags. She's your automatic kakampi against your parents and your first-ever bestie (or rival).
usage_notes: The male counterpart is 'primo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kadarating lang ng **prima** ko mula sa Amerika.","translation":"My **female cousin** just arrived from America."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pariralang Ingles na nangangahulugang 'kung alam mo, alam mo,' na ginagamit upang ipahiwatig ang isang bagay na mauunawaan lamang ng isang partikular na grupo ng mga tao na may parehong karanasan o kaalaman.
etymology: Acronym for the English phrase 'If you know, you know'.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'bahala na kayo umintindi' online. It's the caption you put when the chismis is too hot to spell out, but you want your fellow marites to get the hint. The digital version of a meaningful look between friends.
usage_notes: Primarily used in digital communication like social media captions, chats, and comments.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Yung tingin niyo sa isa't isa ng bestie mo 'pag may dumaang chismis. **IYKYK**.","translation":"That look between you and your bestie when some gossip walks by. **If you know, you know**."},{"sentence":"Bakit ako pagod? Monday pa lang? **IYKYK**.","translation":"Why am I tired? It's only Monday? **If you know, you know**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bakod o kulungan, karaniwang gawa sa kahoy o alambre, para sa mga alagang hayop tulad ng baka, kabayo, o baboy.
original_explanation: Basically, a parking lot for farm animals. It's where you keep the goats from eating your laundry or the pigs from running off to the neighbor's palengke stall. Think of it as a low-tech, high-stakes playpen.
usage_notes: A general term for an animal enclosure. Specific types can be mentioned, like 'kural ng manok' (chicken coop) or 'kural ng baka' (cattle corral).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inilipat ng magsasaka ang mga baka sa mas malaking **kural**.","translation":"The farmer moved the cows to a bigger **corral**."},{"sentence":"Tumakas ang kambing mula sa **kural** kagabi.","translation":"The goat escaped from the **pen** last night."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalahad o pagkukuwento ng isang pangyayari, karanasan, o kuwento sa isang maayos at detalyadong paraan.
original_explanation: This is the formal way of saying 'i-kwento mo' or 'spill the tea.' When your friend comes back from a date, you demand, "Salaysayin mo ang lahat ng detalye!" It’s narrating, giving a full report, from start to finish, with no commercial breaks.
usage_notes: This is a verb. The noun form is 'salaysay' (narrative).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hayaan mong **salaysayin** ko ang tunay na nangyari.","translation":"Allow me **to narrate** what really happened."},{"sentence":"Mahusay niyang na**salaysay** ang kasaysayan ng aming bayan.","translation":"He was able to expertly **recount** the history of our town."}]

meaning_filipino: I-unat ang katawan o mga bahagi nito; gawing tuwid ang isang bagay na nakabaluktot.
original_explanation: That glorious feeling when you wake up in the morning and do a full-body stretch. Also what you need to do to your crumpled 100-peso bill before feeding it to the vending machine. "Pagkatapos ng walong oras sa harap ng computer, kailangan mo talagang umunat."
usage_notes: Can refer to stretching one's body or straightening a physical object.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap **umunat** pagkatapos ng mahabang pagkakaupo.","translation":"It feels good **to stretch** after sitting for a long time."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **umunat** ang gusot na damit gamit ang kanyang mga kamay.","translation":"He tried **to straighten** the wrinkled clothes with his hands."}]

translation: joker (in cards); jester; someone not to be taken seriously
meaning_filipino: Sa baraha, ito ang kard na may larawan ng isang payaso. Sa malawak na kahulugan, ito ay isang taong mapagpatawa, o isang tao na hindi sineseryoso o hindi mapagkakatiwalaan.
original_explanation: In the Philippines, a "joker" isn't just a playing card or a Batman villain. It's that one person in your barkada who's always making jokes. But it can also be a low-key insult. If someone says "Huwag mo nang seryosohin 'yan, joker 'yan," it means that person is unreliable, all talk, and probably won't show up to the group project.
usage_notes: The meaning shifts heavily with context, from a lighthearted "comedian" to a more serious "unreliable person."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mo ng dalawang **joker** para sa larong ito.","translation":"You need two **jokers** for this game."},{"sentence":"Akala ko seryoso siya sa alok niya, **joker** lang pala.","translation":"I thought he was serious with his offer, turns out he was just a **joker** (not to be taken seriously)."}]

meaning_filipino: (Pang-uri) May kaugnayan sa musika o may likas na kakayahan sa musika. (Pangalan) Isang dula, palabas, o pelikula na ang malaking bahagi ng diyalogo ay kinakanta.
original_explanation: As a noun, it's a show where people randomly burst into song and dance to express their feelings, parang 'High School Musical' o 'Rak of Aegis'. As an adjective, it describes your friend who can play the guitar, piano, and ukulele, tapos singer pa. Sila 'yung laging request-an sa parties.
usage_notes: Can function as both an adjective ('taong musikal' - musical person) and a noun ('manood ng musikal' - watch a musical).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **musikal** na palabas ang itatanghal sa teatro para sa anibersaryo.","translation":"A **musical** show will be staged at the theater for the anniversary."},{"sentence":"Talagang **musikal** ang pamilya nila; lahat ay mahusay umawit.","translation":"Their family is truly **musical**; everyone sings well."}]

translation: sense of regret over a loss or missed opportunity; what a waste
meaning_filipino: Ang pakiramdam ng panghihinayang o pagsisisi dahil sa isang bagay na nasayang, nawala, o isang pagkakataon na pinalampas.
etymology: A variant of `panghihinayang`, derived from `sayang` (waste, pity). The `-in-` infix denotes the feeling or state.
original_explanation: This is the official feeling of "Sayang!". It's the ghost of the 1-piece-chicken-with-rice you could have upsized to 2-piece. It's the "what if" when you see your ex looking good. It’s the pain of dropping your ice cream, the regret of not buying that shirt on sale. **Hinayang** is the patron saint of missed shots and wasted opportunities.
usage_notes: Often used as a noun ('ang hinayang ko') or in the verb form 'nanghihinayang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang **hinayang** ko sa perang nawala.","translation":"I feel a great **sense of loss** for the money that was lost."},{"sentence":"Nanghihinayang siya sa pinalampas na pagkakataon.","translation":"He **regrets** the opportunity he missed."}]

translation: to proceed, to continue; to stay (at a place)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapatuloy sa isang gawain, direksyon, o plano; o ang pansamantalang paninirahan o pagtigil sa isang lugar.
original_explanation: This word has two vibes. Vibe 1: "Go lang nang go!" Kahit umulan, the show must go on. Vibe 2: "Dito ka muna." It's when your friend from the province crashes at your condo for a few days. It's about continuing something or checking in somewhere.
usage_notes: The meaning depends heavily on context. "Tumuloy ka" can mean "Come in" or "Continue".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit malakas ang ulan, **tumuloy** pa rin ang parada.","translation":"Despite the heavy rain, the parade still **proceeded**."},{"sentence":"Sa bahay ng kanyang tiyahin siya **tumuloy** noong nag-aral siya sa Maynila.","translation":"She **stayed** at her aunt's house when she studied in Manila."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng labis na pagpapahalaga sa sarili at pagmamaliit sa iba; mayabang.
original_explanation: The kind of person who posts 'Haters are my motivators' on social media after flexing their new iPhone. They think they're the main character and everyone else is just an extra. It's a step above 'mayabang'—it has a classic, almost biblical feel of pride.
usage_notes: A more formal and stronger word than 'mayabang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **palalo** na ugali, iniwasan siya ng kanyang mga kaibigan.","translation":"Because of his **arrogant** attitude, his friends avoided him."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pampalasa na mula sa pinatuyong buto ng halamang Cuminum cyminum, na karaniwang ginagamit sa pagluluto upang magdagdag ng kakaibang lasa at amoy.
original_explanation: That spice you buy for one specific recipe you saw on TikTok, and then it just sits in your pantry for the next five years. It has a strong, earthy flavor often found in Middle Eastern, Indian, and Mexican dishes. Not to be confused with kasubha or atsuete, though they all live in the same forgotten corner of the spice rack.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa mga konteksto ng pagluluto. Hindi gaanong karaniwan sa tradisyonal na lutuing Pilipino ngunit nagiging kilala na dahil sa mga pandaigdigang trend sa pagkain.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglagay siya ng isang kutsaritang **komino** sa nilulutong kari.","translation":"She added a teaspoon of **cumin** to the curry she was cooking."},{"sentence":"Mabibili ang durog na **komino** sa mga malalaking pamilihan.","translation":"Ground **cumin** can be bought in large markets."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng senyas o hudyat sa isang tao o bagay upang maghatid ng mensahe o utos.
etymology: From the English loanword "signal" + Tagalog suffix "-an".
original_explanation: This is what you do to the jeepney driver when you want to get off. You don't just magically teleport to the sidewalk; you signalan mo siya by shouting "Para!" or knocking on the roof. It's the verb form of getting someone's attention for a specific purpose.
usage_notes: A verb created from a common English loanword.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Signalan** mo ako kapag handa ka na.","translation":"**Signal** me when you're ready."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **signalan** ang tsuper bago ka bumaba.","translation":"You need to **signal** the driver before you get off."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahaba at matulis na ngipin, karaniwan sa mga hayop na kumakain ng karne o sa mga ahas, na ginagamit sa pagkagat o pag-iniksyon ng kamandag.
original_explanation: Ito yung ngipin na pang-action star. Sa aso, sa ahas, kay Dracula. Yung extra pointy at dangerous-looking. Minsan, ginagamit din 'to para i-describe yung "hidden weapon" o "hidden danger" ng isang tao or situation. "Don't be fooled by her smile, may pangil 'yan."
usage_notes: Can be used literally for animals or figuratively for a person's hidden maliciousness or power.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinakita ng tigre ang matatalim nitong **pangil**.","translation":"The tiger showed its sharp **fangs**."},{"sentence":"Sa wakas, inilabas na ng pulitiko ang kanyang tunay na **pangil**.","translation":"Finally, the politician revealed his true **fangs** (malicious nature)."}]

meaning_filipino: Malapit nang magsara o isara. Nagpapahiwatig ng nalalapit na pagtatapos ng operasyon para sa isang araw o panahon.
original_explanation: That frantic feeling when you're running to the mall and the guards are already pulling down the steel gates. "Kuya, sandali lang, bibili lang ng milk tea!" That's the 'pasara na' rush. Also applies to your heart when you've had enough of someone's drama.
usage_notes: Often heard in the phrase "Pasara na!" (It's closing now!) to indicate urgency.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Habulin natin ang bangko, baka **pasara** na.","translation":"Let's rush to the bank, it might be **closing** already."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa pagkalugi, **pasara** na ang paborito naming kainan.","translation":"Due to losses, our favorite eatery is now **about to close** (for good)."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita ng kawalan ng katiyakan o pag-aalinlangan; pagdududa.
original_explanation: This is that moment you're about to click 'Add to Cart' on Lazada but then you remember your credit card bill. It's the 'should I or shouldn't I?' dance in your head. It's also what your friend does when you ask them for a straight answer about your new haircut, causing you to doubt everything.
usage_notes: Can mean to cause someone else to doubt, or to show hesitation oneself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magpaalinlangan** sa iyong kakayahan.","translation":"Don't **hesitate** or doubt your abilities."},{"sentence":"Ang pabago-bago niyang sagot ay nagawa akong **magpaalinlangan**.","translation":"His changing answers **caused me to doubt**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na may matinding pagnanais o ambisyon na makamit ang isang bagay, posisyon, o layunin.
original_explanation: This is every Pinoy with a dream. The BPO agent aspiring to be a Team Lead, the student burning the midnight oil to pass the board exams, the content creator hoping to hit 100k subscribers. They are fueled by ambition, coffee, and a 'kakayanin ko 'to' mindset. They are the opposite of 'pwede na.'
usage_notes: Karaniwang positibo, na nagpapahiwatig ng ambisyon at pagtatakda ng mga layunin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang isang **taong naghahangad** na umunlad ay laging naghahanap ng paraan para matuto.","translation":"A **person who aspires** to improve is always looking for ways to learn."},{"sentence":"Maraming **taong naghahangad** sa posisyong iniwan ng dating pangulo.","translation":"Many **people are aspiring** for the position left by the former president."}]

translation: a drink; a drinking session (non-standard spelling of 'toma')
meaning_filipino: Isang di-pamantayang baybay para sa 'toma', na tumutukoy sa pag-inom ng alak o sa isang sesyon ng inuman.
etymology: Di-pamantayang baybay ng "toma", na mula sa salitang Espanyol na "tomar" (kunin, inumin).
original_explanation: This is likely a typo for 'toma', the act of drinking alcohol ('tumoma' - to drink). It's the "Tara, shot!" moment. 'Toma' is what happens before the hugot, the karaoke, and the "Tol, I love you, man!" declarations. If someone texts "tomo na," they're probably already tipsy and can't spell 'toma' correctly.
usage_notes: Ang "toma" ang tama at mas karaniwang termino. Ang "tomo" ay bihirang makita at karaniwang itinuturing na isang pagkakamali.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto mo bang **tomo** mamaya?","translation":"Do you want to have a **drink** later?"},{"sentence":"Nagkayayaan ang barkada para sa isang **tomo**.","translation":"The friends decided to get together for a **drinking session**."}]

meaning_filipino: Anyayahan ang isang tao sa isang paglalaban, paligsahan, o anumang pagsubok ng kakayahan o tapang.
original_explanation: When you dare your friend to a spicy noodle challenge or when your rival in a video game taunts you. It’s the act of throwing down the gauntlet. 'Huwag mo akong **manghamon**, hindi kita uurungan!' (Don't challenge me, I won't back down!) It's the 'bring it on' verb.
usage_notes: Not to be confused with 'hamon' (ham). The context makes the meaning clear. The 'mang-' prefix suggests that the subject is initiating the challenge.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **manghamon** ng debate tungkol sa politika.","translation":"He likes **to challenge** people to debates about politics."},{"sentence":"Sino ang maglalakas-loob na **manghamon** sa kasalukuyang kampeon?","translation":"Who will be brave enough **to challenge** the current champion?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalipunan ng mga mito na nabibilang sa isang partikular na relihiyon o kultura.
original_explanation: The whole cinematic universe of ancient gods and heroes. Think of it as the original Avengers or Justice League, but with more confusing family trees and questionable morals. The Greek one has Zeus, the Pinoy one has Bathala and a whole squad of anitos and diwatas.
usage_notes: Refers to the entire system or collection of myths from a culture.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayaman ang Pilipinas sa **mitolohiya** na nagpapakita ng ating sinaunang kultura.","translation":"The Philippines is rich in **mythology** that shows our ancient culture."}]

translation: to lie around lazily; to lounge about
meaning_filipino: Ang paghiga o paghiga-higa sa isang lugar nang walang ginagawa; pagiging tamad o pagpapalipas ng oras sa pagpapahinga.
etymology: From `magpa-` + reduplication of `hilata` (lying down sprawled). The `hila-hilata` form emphasizes the continuous, lazy nature of the action.
original_explanation: This is the official sport of the weekend. It's when you just lie on the sofa, bed, or floor, scrolling through your phone, binge-watching a series, and generally just existing. No ambitions, no plans, just pure, unadulterated 'tamad mode.' Your body is in a state of 'ayaw ko muna gumalaw, please.'
usage_notes: Carries a strong connotation of laziness or idleness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Buong araw lang siyang **nagpahila-hilata** sa kama.","translation":"He just **lounged about** in bed the whole day."},{"sentence":"Masarap **magpahila-hilata** sa duyan kapag Linggo ng hapon.","translation":"It's nice to **lie around lazily** in a hammock on a Sunday afternoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na tumutugtog ng instrumentong pangmusika o umaawit bilang suporta sa isang pangunahing mang-aawit o manunugtog.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "taga-" (tagagawa) at salitang-ugat na "saliw" (akompanya sa musika).
original_explanation: The person who plays the guitar while you're singing your hugot song sa videoke. They're the 'support system' of the performance, like your best friend who holds your hair back when you've had too much to drink. The ultimate backup.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng mahusay na **tagasaliw** sa piano para sa darating na kompetisyon.","translation":"We need a skilled piano **accompanist** for the upcoming competition."},{"sentence":"Siya ang naging **tagasaliw** ko sa lahat ng aking pagtatanghal.","translation":"He was my **accompanist** in all of my performances."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagdudulot ng matinding pagkapagod sa katawan o isipan.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'nakaka-' at salitang-ugat na 'hapo' (pagod).
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling after a whole day of commuting on EDSA, plus 8 hours of work, plus another 3 hours of OT. Or just trying to explain technology to your parents. It's more than just 'pagod'; it's bone-deep, soul-crushing tiredness.
usage_notes: Naglalawaran ng isang gawain, karanasan, o bagay na nagdudulot ng matinding pagod.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakakahapo** ang maghapong pag-akyat sa bundok.","translation":"The whole day of climbing the mountain was **exhausting**."},{"sentence":"Minsan, ang pakikipagtalo sa social media ay **nakakahapo**.","translation":"Sometimes, arguing on social media is **wearying**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang impormal o pinaikling paraan ng pagsasabi ng 'pagod' o pagkaramdam ng kapaguran.
original_explanation: The lazy person's way of saying 'pagod.' It's what you text your friend when you're too tired to even type the last letter. 'Tara, inom?' 'Sorry, **pago** na.' It's the official mood after a long commute on EDSA.
usage_notes: Highly informal, used mostly in text messages and casual online conversations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Suko na ako, bes. Sobrang **pago**.","translation":"I give up, bestie. So **tired**."},{"sentence":"Gusto ko nang umuwi, **pago** na ako sa work.","translation":"I want to go home already, I'm **tired** from work."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang may pinakamataas na antas ng kahusayan, kasanayan, o galing; nangunguna sa lahat.
original_explanation: This isn't just 'good,' it's 'the GOAT' (Greatest Of All Time). It's that top-performing agent in your BPO team who gets all the awards. It's the lola who cooks the adobo that no one else can replicate. When you're the **pinakamagaling**, you're the undisputed champion in that skill.
usage_notes: Often used to describe skill, talent, or performance, whereas 'pinakamabuti' can describe moral goodness or the best option.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang kinikilalang **pinakamagaling** na manlalaro ng basketbol sa kasaysayan.","translation":"He is recognized as the **best** basketball player in history."},{"sentence":"Para sa akin, ikaw ang **pinakamagaling** kumanta.","translation":"For me, you are the **most excellent** singer."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang pansanitaryo na may upuan at inodoro para sa pagdumi at pag-ihi ng tao, na konektado sa sistema ng paagusan; kilala rin bilang kubeta.
original_explanation: The throne room. The place where you have your best ideas, scroll endlessly on your phone, or contemplate your life choices. Also known as CR (Comfort Room), banyo, or 'yung-lugar-na-pinupuntahan-mo-pag-tinawag-ka-ng-kalikasan'.
usage_notes: The word 'toilet' itself usually refers to the bowl (inodoro). 'CR' or 'banyo' is more commonly used to refer to the entire room.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong i-flush ang tissue sa **toilet**, baka bumara.","translation":"Don't flush the tissue in the **toilet**, it might get clogged."},{"sentence":"Sira ang **toilet** sa banyo ng mga lalaki.","translation":"The **toilet** in the men's restroom is broken."}]

translation: to make something fixed; to place permanently
meaning_filipino: Ilagay sa isang tiyak at permanenteng posisyon upang hindi maalis o gumalaw; gawing matatag o hindi nababago.
original_explanation: It's like when you finally find the perfect angle for your WFH setup and you tell everyone, 'Wag niyong gagalawin 'yan, **ipirmi** niyo na 'yan diyan!' It means to make it stay, make it fixed. Can also be used for decisions. 'Okay, final answer na 'to, **ipirmi** na natin.'
usage_notes: Commonly used in informal speech to mean 'to fix in place' or 'to finalize'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **ipirmi** mo ang estanteng ito sa pader para hindi matumba.","translation":"Please **fix** this shelf to the wall so it won't fall over."},{"sentence":"**Ipirmi** na natin ang petsa ng ating kasal sa susunod na buwan.","translation":"Let's **set** our wedding date **permanently** for next month."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa modernong gamit, ito ay tumutukoy sa tsismis, balita, o isang kawili-wiling impormasyon na ipinapasa-pasa. Literal din itong nangangahulugang isang inumin.
etymology: From English 'tea', influenced by international internet slang where 'T' stands for truth.
original_explanation: Literally, it's the drink you get from a teabag. But in 2026, 'tea' is the juicy gossip, the chismis, the 'spill the tea' moment. It's what Marites lives for. 'Ano'ng tea?' is the new 'Ano'ng balita?'.
usage_notes: Used both for the literal drink and for the slang meaning 'gossip'. The slang usage is very common among younger generations and on social media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto mo ba ng mainit na **tea**?","translation":"Do you want some hot **tea**?"},{"sentence":"Spill mo na ang **tea**, ano'ng nangyari sa party kagabi?","translation":"Spill the **tea** (gossip), what happened at the party last night?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang idyoma na tumutukoy sa isang taong hindi madaling maantig ang damdamin, walang awa, o sadyang matatag at hindi nagpapakita ng kahinaan.
original_explanation: Eto 'yung ex mong hindi ka binalikan kahit anong iyak at drama mo. Parang bato, bes. Walang pakiramdam, hindi marunong maawa. Minsan, ito rin 'yung tita mong ayaw kang pautangin kasi 'rules are rules' daw.
usage_notes: An idiomatic expression. It describes a person's character, not a physical condition of the heart.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Matigas ang puso** ng amo niya kaya hindi siya pinayagang umuwi kahit may sakit ang anak.","translation":"Her boss is **hard-hearted**, so she wasn't allowed to go home even though her child was sick."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **matigas ang puso** sa mga taong humihingi ng tulong.","translation":"Don't be **hard-hearted** to people asking for help."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi makagalaw o walang pakiramdam dahil sa pinsala sa nerbiyos o sakit; walang kakayahang kumilos o mag-isip nang maayos.
original_explanation: The state of being after seeing your Meralco bill during summer. Also, the traffic on EDSA during a payday Friday rain. Literally, cannot move.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa kondisyong medikal o sa isang sitwasyong hindi umuusad.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **paralisado** ang kalahati ng kanyang katawan matapos ang atake sa puso.","translation":"Half of his body became **paralyzed** after the heart attack."},{"sentence":"**Paralisado** ang gobyerno dahil sa matinding korapsyon.","translation":"The government is **paralyzed** due to severe corruption."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng pagiging malaya sa hirap, sakit, o anumang pasanin; kaginhawahan o payapang pakiramdam.
original_explanation: That feeling you get when the aircon is on full blast after walking under the Manila sun. It's the opposite of being stressed about bills, traffic, or that 'seen' message with no reply. It's your state of being after payday, before the 'bayarin' attack. Ultimate #SanaAll feeling.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a state of well-being, both physical and financial. 'Maginhawang buhay' (a comfortable life) is a common aspiration.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakaramdam siya ng **ginhawa** nang matapos ang lahat ng kanyang gawain.","translation":"He felt a sense of **relief** after finishing all his tasks."},{"sentence":"Ang hangad ng bawat magulang ay ang **ginhawa** ng kanilang mga anak.","translation":"The wish of every parent is the **comfort** of their children."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtingin nang mabilis, patago, o sa pamamagitan ng isang maliit na siwang o butas.
original_explanation: The OG 'seen zone.' Yung ginagawa mo sa social media profile ng crush mo, scroll ka nang scroll pero ingat na ingat na wag may ma-like. Or yung pagtingin mo sa katabing upuan sa jeep kung bababa na ba siya para makaupo ka na. A quick, stealthy look.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pandiwa (sumilip, silipin) o pangngalan (isang silip - one peek).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumilip** siya sa bintana para tingnan kung sino ang kumakatok.","translation":"He **peeped** through the window to see who was knocking."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **silipin** ang sagot ng katabi mo tuwing may pagsusulit.","translation":"Don't **peek** at your seatmate's answers during an exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Bilang pangalan, isang lalaking may kapangyarihang mahiwaga. Bilang pang-uri, tumutukoy sa isang bagay o lugar na nasa ilalim ng isang salamangka o hiwaga.
original_explanation: The male counterpart of the enkantada. He's the mysterious guy living in the old balete tree. Can also mean a place is 'enchanted,' like that one spot in the office where the WiFi mysteriously dies, or a person who seems to be under a spell (like when you're so in love, you're 'enkantado').
usage_notes: Masculine form of 'enkantada'. Can also be used as an adjective.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroong **enkantado** na naninirahan sa punong iyon.","translation":"There is an **enchanter** living in that tree."},{"sentence":"Ang buong kaharian ay naging **enkantado** dahil sa sumpa.","translation":"The entire kingdom became **enchanted** because of the curse."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katawagan para sa isang bagay na mura, mababa ang kalidad, o hindi gaanong maganda ang pagkakagawa.
etymology: Filipino gay slang, possibly a playful alteration of the English word 'cheap'.
