usage_notes: Can refer to the general act of thinking or a specific mindset/ideology (e.g., 'makalumang pag-iisip' - old-fashioned thinking).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malalim ang kanyang **pag-iisip** tungkol sa kinabukasan ng bansa.","translation":"His **thinking** about the country's future is deep."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggalaw o pag-indayog nang maluwag at paulit-ulit dahil sa ihip ng hangin, tulad ng isang bandila.
original_explanation: The state of the Philippine flag during the national anthem every morning assembly. Or your hair when you're riding a jeepney and you stick your head out (don't do it!). It's a majestic, free-flowing movement.
usage_notes: Mostly used for flags, banners, cloth, or even long hair.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bandila ng Pilipinas ay marilag na **nakawagayway** sa tuktok ng poste.","translation":"The Philippine flag is majestically **waving** at the top of the pole."},{"sentence":"Gusto ko ang pakiramdam ng hangin sa aking buhok na **nakawagayway**.","translation":"I like the feeling of the wind in my **fluttering** hair."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat ng mga tao na naninirahan sa isang tiyak na lugar o lokalidad, na may magkakatulad na interes, kultura, o pamahalaan.
etymology: From the circumfix "pa-...-an" and the root word "bayan" (town, country).
original_explanation: Your barangay, your subdivision, your online gaming guild, or your chismis group chat. It's any group of people with a shared space (physical or digital) and a shared interest, like complaining about the slow internet or celebrating a neighbor's lotto win. It's where the bayanihan spirit lives... or where the homeowners' association fines you for uncut grass.
usage_notes: A broader term than "barangay" (village) or "nayon" (hamlet). It can encompass social, cultural, and even virtual groups.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang pagtutulungan sa isang **pamayanan**.","translation":"Cooperation is important in a **community**."},{"sentence":"Nag-organisa ng clean-up drive ang aming **pamayanan**.","translation":"Our **community** organized a clean-up drive."}]

translation: To delouse someone; to pick lice from hair
meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pag-aalis ng kuto at lisa sa buhok ng ibang tao.
original_explanation: The ultimate bonding experience for a Pinoy mother and child, or between mag-kumare while waiting for the latest teleserye. It's a meticulous search-and-destroy mission against tiny invaders, often done in the afternoon sun. 'Pahinguto' is an act of love, hygiene, and sometimes, a source of juicy neighborhood gossip.
usage_notes: A very specific cultural activity, often done manually.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan ni nanay si ate na **pahinguto** ang bunsong kapatid.","translation":"Mother instructed older sister to **delouse** their youngest sibling."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng klase, nag-**pahinguto** ang magkakaibigan sa ilalim ng puno ng mangga.","translation":"After class, the friends **picked lice from each other's hair** under the mango tree."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan sa isang laro, kompetisyon, o paligsahan kung saan walang nanalo o natalo dahil pareho o pantay ang nakuha ng magkabilang panig.
etymology: From Spanish 'tablas', meaning 'a draw' in a game.
original_explanation: That moment in a basketball game when it's 98-98 with 3 seconds left. It's the 'walang nanalo, walang natalo, bati na tayo' of sports. The ultimate cliffhanger that leads to a thrilling overtime or a shared pot in a bet.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tabla** ang laro, kaya magkakaroon ng overtime.","translation":"The game is a **tie**, so there will be an overtime."},{"sentence":"Nagtapos sa **tabla** ang kanilang laban sa chess.","translation":"Their chess match ended in a **draw**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong naglalakad, lalo na sa isang lugar na ginagamit din ng mga sasakyan.
original_explanation: A fancy English word for 'taong naglalakad sa kalsada.' You're a pedestrian when you're walking to the nearest 7-Eleven, crossing the street to catch a jeep, or just strolling through BGC. Basically, anyone on foot navigating the urban jungle.
usage_notes: This is a direct borrowing from English and is often used in news reports or formal announcements about traffic. 'Taong-lakad' is a less common Tagalog equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat laging mag-ingat ang mga **pedestrian** sa pagtawid.","translation":"**Pedestrians** should always be careful when crossing."},{"sentence":"May bagong batas para sa kaligtasan ng mga **pedestrian**.","translation":"There is a new law for the safety of **pedestrians**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang kilos ng pagpunta o paggalaw sa likuran ng isang bagay o tao, o ang pagtupad sa isang utos, tuntunin, o payo.
original_explanation: Ito yung ginagawa mo sa Waze o Google Maps para hindi maligaw. Ito rin yung (sana) ginagawa mo sa instructions ng IKEA furniture. Pagdating sa social media, ito yung pag-stalk—este, pag-keep up—sa updates ng isang tao.
usage_notes: Present tense of 'sumunod'. Can mean physically following or metaphorically following rules or advice.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumusunod** ang aso sa kanyang amo saan man ito magpunta.","translation":"The dog is **following** its master wherever he goes."},{"sentence":"Dapat kang **sumunod** sa batas trapiko.","translation":"You should **obey** the traffic laws."}]

meaning_filipino: Isulat o bigkasin ang mga titik na bumubuo sa isang salita sa tamang pagkakasunod-sunod.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-hiram na "ispeling" (Ingles: spelling) na nilagyan ng hulaping "-in".
original_explanation: 'Yung action na ginagawa mo kapag tinanong ka ng kaibigan mo, "Paano i-spell yung 'necessary'?" Tapos pareho kayong mag-iisip at aasa sa autocorrect. The ultimate test of friendship is when you ask someone to spell a word and they don't judge you.
usage_notes: Isang Tagalized na bersyon ng Ingles na "to spell". Ang mas pormal na katumbas ay "baybayin".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyong **ispelingin** mo ang iyong buong pangalan.","translation":"Please **spell** your full name."}]

translation: to reconcile with someone; to make amends
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbabalik-loob o pagpapanumbalik ng mabuting ugnayan sa isang tao matapos ang isang di-pagkakaunawaan.
original_explanation: This is the "Sorry na, please?" phase after the `makipag-away`. It's the act of fixing a relationship, whether it's with your jowa, your bestie, or your boss. It involves swallowing your pride, admitting fault (maybe), and trying to get back to a good place. The opposite of ghosting.
usage_notes: Often used after a conflict or misunderstanding to restore harmony.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Panahon na para **makipag-ayos** ka sa kapatid mo.","translation":"It's time for you **to reconcile** with your sibling."},{"sentence":"Mas pinili niyang **makipag-ayos** kaysa palakihin pa ang gulo.","translation":"He chose **to make amends** rather than escalate the conflict."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang yugto o panahon sa buhay ng isang tao kung saan ang pangunahing pokus ay ang pagtanggap, pagpapahalaga, at pag-aalaga sa sarili.
etymology: Mula sa pariralang Ingles na 'self-love era'.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung phase sa buhay mo na ang mantra mo ay 'Ako muna.' After a breakup, a burnout, or just a major realization, you enter your self-love era. Dito mo natututunang i-prioritize ang peace of mind mo over toxic people, mag-set ng boundaries, at i-celebrate ang sarili mong achievements, malaki man o maliit. Hindi ito selfishness, it's a revolutionary act of choosing yourself.
usage_notes: Isang kontemporaryong parirala na sumikat sa social media, lalo na sa mga usapin tungkol sa mental health at personal growth.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng lahat ng pinagdaanan niya, nasa **self-love era** na siya ngayon.","translation":"After everything she's been through, she's in her **self-love era** now."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-eehersisyo at pagkain ng masustansya ay bahagi ng aking **self-love era**.","translation":"Exercising and eating healthy are part of my **self-love era**."}]

translation: suitability; appropriateness; the way something fits
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o paraan ng pagiging angkop, bagay, o tama para sa isang partikular na layunin, sitwasyon, o tao.
original_explanation: It's how well your witty caption fits your IG post. It's the "bagay" factor. When your outfit is perfect for the occasion, that's good pagkakaangkop. When you use a meme in a work presentation and the boss actually laughs, that's perfect pagkakaangkop. It's all about the right fit.
usage_notes: Refers to the quality of being suitable or the manner in which something is made to fit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinuri ng guro ang **pagkakaangkop** ng mga salitang ginamit niya sa tula.","translation":"The teacher praised the **appropriateness** of the words she used in the poem."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aralan nila ang **pagkakaangkop** ng bagong polisiya sa mga empleyado.","translation":"They studied the **suitability** of the new policy for the employees."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghinto o pagtigil sa isang gawain, kilos, o damdamin.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `pag-` (na bumubuo ng pangngalang-diwa) at sa salitang ugat na `tugot` (huminto, tumigil).
original_explanation: This is the "Ayoko na, pagod na ako" moment. It's when you finally decide to stop chasing someone who's not interested, stop working overtime for a company that doesn't appreciate you, or just stop arguing on social media. It's the act of quitting, but with a sense of finality. The ultimate "pag-let go" para sa inner peace mo.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa pormal o pampanitikang konteksto. Ang 'pagtigil' o 'paghinto' ay mas karaniwan sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagtugot** sa paninigarilyo ang pinakamabuting desisyon na ginawa niya.","translation":"The **cessation** of smoking was the best decision he ever made."}]

translation: to dodge; to parry; to evade a blow
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-iwas sa isang bagay na tatama, karaniwan ay sa pamamagitan ng mabilis na paggalaw ng katawan o bahagi nito.
original_explanation: It's what you do when your Tita asks, "Kailan ka mag-aasawa?" You mentally iplag the question and change the topic to the food. It's the physical version of "seen-zoning" a flying object.
usage_notes: The prefix 'i-' indicates that the action is done to or for something/someone, or the action involves moving something. Here it implies moving oneself away from something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis niyang **inilag** ang mukha niya nang may biglang lumipad na bola.","translation":"He quickly **dodged** with his face when a ball suddenly flew by."},{"sentence":"Subukan mong **iplag** ang mga responsibilidad mo, hahabulin ka pa rin niyan.","translation":"Try to **evade** your responsibilities, they will still chase after you."}]

translation: to press one's lips together; to be silent
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtitikom ng mga labi dahil sa pagpipigil ng damdamin, pag-iisip nang malalim, o sadyang pananahimik.
etymology: From the root "imid" (to press lips) + infix "-um-".
original_explanation: That moment you want to say something savage during a meeting but you remember you need the job. You just press your lips together and channel your inner peace. It's the physical manifestation of "if you don't have anything nice to say..."
usage_notes: Describes a specific action of closing the mouth tightly, often out of suppressed emotion or deep thought.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umimid** na lamang ang bata sa takot nang mapagalitan ng ama.","translation":"The child just **pressed his lips together** in fear when his father scolded him."},{"sentence":"Nang marinig niya ang tsismis, **umimid** siya at hindi na nagsalita.","translation":"When she heard the gossip, she just **clamped her mouth shut** and didn't speak anymore."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang akda o materyales na inilimbag at ipinamahagi sa publiko, tulad ng aklat, pahayagan, o magasin.
original_explanation: The official term for your school paper, that magazine you flip through at the salon, or even the academic journal you have to cite for your thesis. It's basically any printed stuff that's been made 'official' for everyone to see.
usage_notes: Commonly used in academic, literary, and formal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang tula ay napili para sa isang pambansang **palathala**.","translation":"His poem was chosen for a national **publication**."},{"sentence":"Naghahanap ang editor ng mga bagong manunulat para sa susunod na **palathala** ng magasin.","translation":"The editor is looking for new writers for the magazine's next **publication**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halamang-ugat na may kulay lilang laman, sikat na sangkap sa mga panghimagas tulad ng halaya at ice cream.
original_explanation: The undisputed king of Filipino desserts. Before 'ube' became a global hipster food trend in lattes and donuts, it was the heart of our lola's halaya, the star of ice cream, and the purple goodness in our halo-halo. It's the OG Pinoy flavor that went international.
usage_notes: The spelling "ube" is now more common than "ubi" in commercial and everyday contexts, but both are correct.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paborito kong panghimagas ay halayang **ubi**.","translation":"My favorite dessert is **purple yam** jam (halaya)."},{"sentence":"Sikat sa buong mundo ang lasa ng **ubi** mula sa Pilipinas.","translation":"The flavor of **purple yam** from the Philippines is famous worldwide."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pagkaing Pilipino na gawa sa manipis na hiwa ng baka na niluto sa toyo, kalamansi, at sibuyas.
original_explanation: The Pinoy's answer to fancy steak. It's that thinly sliced beef swimming in a soy sauce-calamansi-onion gravy that makes you ask for extra rice. It's the 'I want steak but on a budget' meal that tastes like home.
usage_notes: Often referred to as "Bistek Tagalog" to distinguish it from Western-style beef steak.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong ulamin ang **bistek** na luto ni nanay.","translation":"My favorite dish is the **Filipino beef steak** that my mom cooks."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang laruang yari sa magaang balangkas na may papel o tela, na pinapalipad sa himpapawid sa pamamagitan ng isang mahabang tali.
original_explanation: The original Pinoy drone. Before gadgets, the ultimate summer afternoon flex was having the best bolador (or saranggola) in the neighborhood. It's a symbol of carefree childhood days, running in an open field, and the simple joy of watching something you made soar. Just watch out for power lines and rival kite-flyers trying to cut your string!
usage_notes: "Saranggola" is a more common and native-sounding synonym. "Bolador" has a slightly more classic or literary feel.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naggawa kami ng **bolador** gamit ang patpat ng kawayan at papel de hapon.","translation":"We made a **kite** using bamboo sticks and Japanese paper."},{"sentence":"Mataas ang lipad ng kanyang **bolador** sa maaliwalas na kalangitan.","translation":"His **kite** flew high in the clear sky."}]

meaning_filipino: May pahintulot o opisyal na kapangyarihan na gawin ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na ikaw lang ang **autorisado** na humawak ng phone ni jowa. 'Authorized personnel only' kumbaga. Kapag hindi ka autorisado, bawal kang pumasok, parang sa puso niya na may iba nang nagmamay-ari.
usage_notes: Madalas makita sa mga karatula at sa mga pormal na dokumento.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tanging mga **autorisado** na tauhan lamang ang maaaring pumasok sa lugar na iyon.","translation":"Only **authorized** personnel may enter that area."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maikling pahinga o paghinto sa gitna ng isang pagtatanghal, tulad ng dula, pelikula, o konsiyerto.
original_explanation: The official CR and popcorn break during a movie or play. It's that 15-minute window where you sprint to the restroom, debate whether another P200 for popcorn is worth it, and check your phone for messages you missed. The intermisyon is the 'pause' button of live entertainment.
usage_notes: Mostly used in the context of theater, concerts, and sometimes older films.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili tayo ng pagkain habang **intermisyon**.","translation":"Let's buy food during the **intermission**."},{"sentence":"Magkakaroon ng sampung minutong **intermisyon** pagkatapos ng unang akto ng dula.","translation":"There will be a ten-minute **intermission** after the first act of the play."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pabilog na palamuti sa ulo, karaniwang gawa sa ginto at mga mamahaling bato, na isinusuot ng mga hari, reyna, o nagwagi sa isang patimpalak.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'sana all' accessory. Whether you're winning Miss Universe or just being the 'reyna' of your group chat, the korona is the symbol of victory. Also, what your dentist puts on your tooth after you've eaten too much chicharon and it gives up on life.
usage_notes: Maaari ring tumukoy sa dental crown.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinutong sa nanalo ang mamahaling **korona**.","translation":"The expensive **crown** was placed on the winner."},{"sentence":"Kailangan lagyan ng **korona** ang ngipin kong sira.","translation":"My damaged tooth needs to be fitted with a **crown**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mabango at mamahaling dagta o resin na nagmumula sa isang uri ng puno, karaniwang ginagamit bilang insenso, pabango, o gamot noong sinaunang panahon. Isa ito sa mga handog ng Tatlong Mago sa sanggol na si Hesus.
original_explanation: This is that fancy, expensive perfume stuff that one of the Three Kings gave to baby Jesus. It's like the OG essential oil, the kind of gift you give when you want to show you're not just rich, you're *ancient* rich. Think of it as the luxury brand of biblical times.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa mga kontekstong panrelihiyon o pangkasaysayan, lalo na kapag tinatalakay ang kuwento ng Kapanganakan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-alay ang isa sa Tatlong Hari ng ginto, kamanyang, at **mira**.","translation":"One of the Three Kings offered gold, frankincense, and **myrrh**."},{"sentence":"Ang **mira** ay may kakaibang amoy na ginagamit sa mga ritwal.","translation":"**Myrrh** has a unique scent used in rituals."}]

translation: to add fuel; to stoke a fire
meaning_filipino: Ang pagdaragdag ng panggatong, tulad ng kahoy o uling, sa apoy upang mapanatili o palakasin ang liyab nito.
original_explanation: Literally, it's adding wood to a bonfire. Figuratively, it's what your 'Marites' friend does to an argument. When two people are fighting and she whispers, 'Uy, narinig ko sabi niya...', she's 'nanggagatong'. She's adding fuel to the fire, making the drama bigger and hotter.
usage_notes: Often used figuratively to mean 'to instigate' or 'to provoke further conflict.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang **maggatong** sa away nila; hayaan mo na silang mag-usap.","translation":"Don't **add fuel** to their fight; let them talk it out."}]

translation: to burn with intense emotion; to rage
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng matinding damdamin, karaniwang galit o pagnanasa, na halos hindi mapigilan.
original_explanation: That feeling when the internet goes out during your online game's final boss, or when someone spoils the ending of your favorite K-drama. You're not just angry, you're *fuming*. Your inner volcano is about to erupt. It's the silent, seething rage before the 'Hulk smash!' moment.
usage_notes: Often used to describe intense, internal anger or passion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagpupuyos** sa galit ang kanyang dibdib nang malamang niloko siya.","translation":"His chest was **burning** with anger when he found out he was cheated on."},{"sentence":"Sa loob-loob niya, **nagpupuyos** ang pagnanasang makamit ang katarungan.","translation":"Inside, the desire to achieve justice was **raging**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, karaniwang lalaki, na nagpapakita ng romantikong interes at nagsisikap na makuha ang pag-ibig ng isang babae sa pamamagitan ng pagdalaw, pagbibigay ng regalo, at iba pang paraan ng panunuyo.
original_explanation: The OG 'Nasa 'yo na ang lahat' guy. He's the one who brings flowers, chocolates, and sometimes even a whole harana crew. In modern times, he's the one who sends good morning texts, fetches you from work, and pays for your milk tea. He's in the 'getting to know you' stage, hoping to level up from 'suitor' to 'jowa.'
usage_notes: Traditionally refers to a male suitor, but can be used more broadly in modern contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marami siyang **manliligaw** dahil sa kanyang kabaitan at ganda.","translation":"She has many **suitors** because of her kindness and beauty."},{"sentence":"Ang **manliligaw** ng kapatid ko ay laging may dalang pasalubong.","translation":"My sister's **suitor** always brings a gift."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng panghalip na ginagamit sa pagtatanong tungkol sa tao, bagay, lugar, o pangyayari.
etymology: Mula sa panlaping `pang-` (gamit sa) + `halip` (kapalit) at `na` (pang-ugnay) + `pananong` (mula sa `tanong`).
original_explanation: Ito yung mga words na ginagamit mo para mag-imbestiga sa chismis. 'Sino' ang kasama niya? 'Ano' ang ginawa nila? 'Saan' sila nagpunta? Basically, the building blocks of a full-blown "Marites" investigation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **panghalip na pananong** na 'sino' ay tumutukoy sa isang tao.","translation":"The **interrogative pronoun** 'who' refers to a person."},{"sentence":"Gamitin mo ang tamang **panghalip na pananong** sa iyong talata.","translation":"Use the correct **interrogative pronoun** in your paragraph."}]

meaning_filipino: Maraming balahibo; natatakpan ng makapal na balahibo.
original_explanation: Used to describe anything with a generous amount of hair or fur. That tito who looks like he's wearing a sweater even when shirtless? Balahibuhin. Your super fluffy doggo? Balahibuhin. The fruit rambutan? Balahibuhin din. It's the go-to word for all things hairy.
usage_notes: Can be used for people, animals, and even some fruits or plants.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang alaga niyang aso ay maliit pero **balahibuhin**.","translation":"Her pet dog is small but **furry**."},{"sentence":"Kilala ang mga lalaki sa kanilang pamilya sa pagiging **balahibuhin**.","translation":"The men in their family are known for being **hairy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang opisyal na kinatawan o sugo ng isang bansa o pinuno sa ibang bansa, na may pinakamataas na ranggo.
original_explanation: Imagine the ultimate "representative" ng Pilipinas sa ibang bansa. Hindi lang sila basta tourist, sila 'yung may dalang "pasabi" from the President. Think of them as the original influencers, but for international relations.
usage_notes: Isang pormal at medyo makalumang termino. Mas karaniwang ginagamit ang "ambasador" sa kasalukuyan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinadala ang **lakansugo** sa Tsina upang ayusin ang usaping pangkapayapaan.","translation":"The **ambassador** was sent to China to settle the peace talks."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi nagpapakita ng anumang hiya o pagkailang sa paggawa ng isang bagay na maaaring ituring na di-kanais-nais.
original_explanation: This describes someone with the 'kapal ng mukha' of a titan. The person who cuts in line, sings loudly and out of tune in the videoke, or asks for your Netflix password without batting an eye. They operate walang-kahiya-hiya, completely unbothered by social norms or what other people think.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan sa isang tao o kilos na walang hiya. Ito ay may negatibong konotasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay isang **walang-kahiya-hiya** na tao.","translation":"He is a **shameless** person."},{"sentence":"**Walang-kahiya-hiya** siyang umamin sa kanyang pagkakamali sa harap ng lahat.","translation":"He **unashamedly** admitted his mistake in front of everyone."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mag-aaral sa isang akademya militar, pulisya, o pandagat na nagsasanay upang maging isang opisyal.
etymology: From English 'cadet', which is from French 'cadet'.
original_explanation: The future PMA or PNPA graduate. They're the ones marching in perfect sync under the hot sun, with uniforms so crisp you could cut yourself on them. They're training to be the next leaders, and you know they're disciplined because their haircut hasn't changed in four years.
usage_notes: A direct loanword used specifically in the context of military, police, or maritime academies.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pangarap niya ay maging isang **kadet** sa Philippine Military Academy.","translation":"His dream is to become a **cadet** at the Philippine Military Academy."},{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang pagsasanay ng mga **kadet** sa barko.","translation":"The training of the **cadets** on the ship is strict."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang biglaan at walang-ingat na pag-upo o paghiga, karaniwan sa sahig, dahil sa matinding pagod o kawalan ng gana.
original_explanation: You know that feeling after a hellish commute or a long day at work? The moment you get home, you just drop your bag and flop onto the nearest surface—the sofa, the bed, or even the floor. That's 'pagsalampak'. It's not a graceful sitting down; it's a heavy, tired, 'I give up' kind of slump.
usage_notes: Conveys a sense of exhaustion, frustration, or casualness. It's a heavy, often noisy, way of sitting or lying down.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang pagod, isang **pagsalampak** sa sahig ang una niyang ginawa pag-uwi.","translation":"Due to extreme tiredness, **flopping down** on the floor was the first thing he did upon arriving home."},{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **pagsalampak** niya sa kama mula sa kabilang kwarto.","translation":"I heard his **slumping** onto the bed from the other room."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang unang yugto sa buhay ng isang palaka, na nabubuhay sa tubig at may buntot. Tumutukoy rin ito sa isang uri ng isda (pufferfish) na lumolobo kapag nasa panganib.
original_explanation: As a tadpole, it's the baby version of a frog, 'yung parang sperm cell na may mata na lumalangoy sa kanal. As a pufferfish, it's that cute-but-deadly fish that inflates itself when it feels threatened—parang ikaw 'pag may nag-comment sa weight mo. It's also used to describe someone with a big, round belly.
usage_notes: The meaning (tadpole or pufferfish) is usually clear from the context. It can also be used metaphorically to describe a pot-bellied person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming maliliit na **butete** sa sapa pagkatapos ng ulan.","translation":"There are many small **tadpoles** in the creek after the rain."},{"sentence":"Delikadong kainin ang isdang **butete** kung hindi marunong maghanda nito.","translation":"It's dangerous to eat **pufferfish** if it's not prepared by an expert."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging sanhi ng pag-iyak o pagdaloy ng luha ng isang tao.
original_explanation: The specialty of Korean dramas and sad Pinoy movies. It's what happens when you watch Hachiko, read your ex's old messages, or see your phone bill after being on data all month. To magpaluha is to cause tears, whether from sadness, happiness (iyak-tawa), or from chopping onions.
usage_notes: Can be intentional (like a villain's goal) or unintentional (like accidentally saying something hurtful).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang magsalita ng ganyan, ayokong **magpaluha** ng tao.","translation":"Don't speak like that, I don't want to **make people cry**."},{"sentence":"Ang pelikulang iyon ay siguradong **magpapaluha** sa mga manonood.","translation":"That movie will surely **make the audience cry**."}]

meaning_filipino: Itlog ng pato na inimbak sa asin at putik, na nagreresulta sa maalat na lasa at mapulang kulay ng pula ng itlog. Ang balat nito ay karaniwang tinina ng pula (fuchsia) upang matukoy.
original_explanation: That bright red (okay, fuchsia) egg you see in the palengke. It's the best friend of kamatis and sibuyas in a classic ensalada. Don't be fooled by the name, the shell is dyed red, the "pula" (yolk) inside is just a very rich orange. It's also called "itlog na maalat."
usage_notes: The term "itlog na pula" is synonymous with "itlog na maalat." The red dye is a traditional marker to distinguish it from regular eggs.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap ang ensaladang kamatis na may hiniwang **itlog na pula**.","translation":"Tomato salad with sliced **salted duck egg** is delicious."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hindi pagtagumpay sa isang layunin; paghinto sa paggana o hindi pag-andar nang maayos ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: Your Wi-Fi's favorite activity during a crucial Zoom meeting. It's the universal reason for being late, missing a deadline, or failing a subject. 'Boss, 'di ako makapasok, pumalya po 'yung MRT.' Basically, it's the more socially acceptable cousin of 'I messed up.'
usage_notes: A very common word for any kind of failure, from mechanical (pumalya ang makina) to personal (pumalya siya sa exam).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pumalya** ang preno ng bus kaya ito naaksidente.","translation":"The bus's brakes **failed**, which is why it got into an accident."},{"sentence":"Nangako siyang tutulong, pero sa huli ay **pumalya** rin siya.","translation":"He promised to help, but in the end he also **failed** (to deliver)."}]

translation: to calm down; to become composed
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabalik sa kalmadong estado mula sa pagiging galit, balisa, o magulo ang isip.
original_explanation: This is what your friend tells you when you're about to send that angry text. "Bes, 'huminahon' ka muna!" It's the verb form of taking a deep breath, counting to ten, and not making a decision you'll regret later. The ultimate "chill ka lang" action.
usage_notes: Used to describe the process of becoming calm or to command someone to calm down.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nang makita niya ang mga pulis, agad siyang **huminahon**.","translation":"When he saw the police, he immediately **calmed down**."},{"sentence":"**Huminahon** ka muna bago mo siya kausapin para hindi kayo mag-away.","translation":"**Calm down** first before you talk to him so you two won't fight."}]

translation: to like something; to find something pleasing
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkaroon ng pagkagiliw o pagkasaya sa isang bagay, tao, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is that feeling when you swipe right on someone's profile, or when you finally taste that milk tea you've been craving. It's the "sana all" moment but for a specific thing. "OMG, na-fall na yata ako sa'yo," says your heart. That's magustuhan. It's the start of something, whether it's a new favorite food or a new crush.
usage_notes: Often used to express a newfound liking or preference for something or someone. The -an suffix makes the object of the liking the focus of the sentence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **magustuhan** mo ang regalo ko para sa'yo.","translation":"I hope you **like** my gift for you."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko inakala na **magugustuhan** ko ang lasa ng ampalaya.","translation":"I never thought I would **like** the taste of bitter gourd."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabayad o pag-aayos ng utang upang maging patas; tabla o patas sa isang laro o labanan.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "a manos" (sa pamamagitan ng mga kamay), na ginagamit sa konteksto ng pag-aayos ng bagay sa pagitan ng dalawang panig.
original_explanation: When you and your friend treat each other to lunch on different days and decide "Okay, quits na tayo," that's amanos. It's the "KKB" (kanya-kanyang bayad) of past debts. In a game, it means it's a tie. No winner, no loser, no asaran.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa mga usapang pinansyal (utang) o sa mga laro.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Amanos** na tayo sa utang, bayad ka na.","translation":"We're **settled** on the debt, you're already paid up."},{"sentence":"Nagtapos sa **amanos** ang laro ng chess.","translation":"The chess game ended in a **draw**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalagyan para sa asukal, karaniwang ginagamit sa hapag-kainan.
original_explanation: That little jar on the dining table that's either completely full or disappointingly empty when you need it for your kape. It's the throne where the king (asukal) resides. Sometimes, you'll find ants have staged a coup and taken over.
usage_notes: A common household item for serving sugar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naubusan na ng laman ang **asukarera**, kailangan nang salinan.","translation":"The **sugar bowl** is empty, it needs to be refilled."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang uri ng pagtatrabaho na ginagawa nang malaya, hindi de-kontrata sa iisang kumpanya, at kadalasan ay per-proyekto.
original_explanation: Ito yung sagot mo kapag tinanong ka ng tita mo kung anong work mo at ayaw mong mag-explain. "Nag-fe-freelance po." It's the gig economy lifestyle. You trade the stability of a 9-to-5 job for the flexibility of managing your own time and projects.
usage_notes: Used to refer to the act or profession of freelancing. Often used with 'nag-' to form a verb-like action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan kong mag-**freelance** para may dagdag kitain.","translation":"I tried doing **freelance work** for extra income."},{"sentence":"Ang **freelance** ang naging daan para makapag-travel ako habang kumikita.","translation":"**Freelancing** became the way for me to travel while earning."}]

translation: to hack; to chop; to strike with a bolo/machete
meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng isang matalim na kasangkapan, tulad ng itak o palakol, upang putulin o hiwain nang may puwersa ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: The action movie verb. This is what the hero does to chop down bamboo to build a raft, or what the kontrabida does in a classic Pinoy action flick. It's a forceful, powerful chop. On a more metaphorical, 'hugot' level, 'Itaga mo sa bato!' means 'Mark my words!' or 'Carve this in stone!'—a promise so certain you could hack it into rock.
usage_notes: The root 'taga' refers to a chop or hack. The idiom 'itaga sa bato' (to carve in stone) is very common and means to make a firm, unbreakable promise.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Itaga** mo sa bato, babalik ako para sa'yo.","translation":"**Mark my words** (lit: Carve it in stone), I will come back for you."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **itaga** ang mga sanga ng puno upang hindi makasagabal sa daan.","translation":"The tree branches need to be **chopped** so they don't block the way."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang kakayahang magsalita o magbigkas ng mga salita, kadalasan dahil sa matinding emosyon tulad ng gulat, takot, o pagkamangha.
original_explanation: That feeling when your crush finally talks to you and your brain just blue-screens. You want to say something witty, but all that comes out is... nothing. Or when your boss asks you for that report you forgot about. Biglang mute ang lola mo. Ayan, di-makapagsalita.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang isang estado ng pagkabigla, sorpresa, o matinding damdamin na pansamantalang nagpapatahimik sa isang tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Di-makapagsalita** siya sa sobrang gulat nang makita ang resulta ng pagsusulit.","translation":"He was **speechless** from so much shock when he saw the exam results."},{"sentence":"Naiwan siyang **di-makapagsalita** matapos ang maalab na pagtatapat.","translation":"She was left **unable to speak** after the passionate confession."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang pagbibigay ng biglaang gulat o takot sa isang tao.
original_explanation: This is what your annoying sibling does when they hide behind a door and shout "BOO!" as you walk past. To **gitlahin** someone is to intentionally startle them. It's a classic prank move. "Huwag mo akong **gitlahin**, may sakit ako sa puso!" (Don't startle me, I have a heart condition!).
usage_notes: Ang hulaping '-in' ay ginagawang pandiwa ang pangngalang 'gitla', na nangangahulugang maging sanhi ng pagka-gitla ng isang tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **gitlahin** ang kanyang mga kaibigan.","translation":"He loves to **startle** his friends."}]

translation: will be made into tapa (cured meat)
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paghahanda ng karne sa pamamagitan ng pagbabad nito sa mga pampalasa at pagpapatuyo o pagluluto upang maging tapa; nasa anyong panghinaharap at pokus sa layon.
etymology: Mula sa "tapa" (cured meat) na may hulaping "-hin" at pag-uulit ng unang pantig (ta-) para sa anyong panghinaharap, pokus sa layon.
original_explanation: The future tense of turning meat into the glorious Filipino breakfast staple, tapa. This is what happens to that block of beef in the freezer before it becomes your beloved tapsilog. It's a promise of a delicious, savory future. 'Huwag mo muna gagalawin 'yan, tatapahin ni nanay 'yan para bukas.'
usage_notes: Ito ay pandiwa sa anyong panghinaharap at pokus sa layon (object-focus).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang karneng binili ko sa palengke ay **tatapahin** ko mamaya.","translation":"The meat I bought from the market **will be made into tapa** by me later."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang kalalabasan niyan kapag **tatapahin** mo nang maayos.","translation":"The result will be delicious if you **will cure it into tapa** properly."}]

translation: state of lying in state; being at a wake
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng isang yumaong nakahimlay para sa isang lamay o paglalamay bago ang libing.
original_explanation: This refers to the actual state of the deceased being presented for the wake. It’s that solemn period where friends and family gather, play cards, drink 3-in-1 coffee, and share stories. It's the final 'viewing party' before the closing credits roll.
usage_notes: Tiyak na tumutukoy sa kalagayan ng katawan ng namatay habang nasa burol o lamay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang huling gabi ng **pagkaburol** ay karaniwang dinadaluhan ng napakaraming tao.","translation":"The last night of **lying in state** is usually attended by so many people."},{"sentence":"Maayos ang kanyang anyo sa kanyang **pagkaburol**.","translation":"He looked peaceful during his **wake viewing**."}]

translation: to abuse (someone); to take advantage of
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtrato sa isang tao o bagay nang may kalupitan, karahasan, o di-makatarungang paraan; ang pagsamantala sa kahinaan o kabaitan ng iba.
etymology: From the `pag-…-han` circumfix + `abuso` (from Spanish 'abuso' meaning abuse).
original_explanation: This is when you misuse power or kindness. It's the boss who makes you do their personal errands, the 'friend' who only calls when they need money, or the jowa who takes your patience for granted. Basically, it's crossing the line from 'paggamit' (using) to 'pananamantala' (exploiting). Don't let them pag-abusuhan your kindness!
usage_notes: A verb in the infinitive/imperative form, object-focused. The root 'abuso' is more common as a noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pag-abusuhan** ang kabaitan ng iyong mga magulang.","translation":"Do not **abuse** the kindness of your parents."},{"sentence":"Bawal **pag-abusuhan** ang mga hayop.","translation":"It is forbidden **to abuse** animals."}]

translation: to insert; to wedge in; to tuck in
meaning_filipino: Ipasok, ilagay, o isiksik ang isang bagay sa isang masikip na puwang.
original_explanation: The art of squeezing yourself into a full jeepney or the MRT during rush hour. It's also what you do when you have 'one last thing' to say in a meeting that's already over. "Pa-isingit lang po ng question!"
usage_notes: Carries a connotation of inserting into a tight or already full space.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **isingit** ang kanyang kotse sa maliit na paradahan.","translation":"He tried to **wedge** his car into the small parking space."},{"sentence":"Maaari ko bang **isingit** ang aking komento?","translation":"May I **insert** my comment?"}]

meaning_filipino: Angkop o itinalaga para sa isang pormal na okasyon, ritwal, o seremonya.
original_explanation: This is the 'for display only' or 'special occasions lang' category of your life. That Barong Tagalog you only wear to weddings? Pangseremonya. The fine china your lola never lets you use? Pangseremonya. It's the opposite of your 'pambahay' clothes; it's you on your best, most formal, and probably most uncomfortable behavior.
usage_notes: Used to describe clothes, objects, or even actions reserved for formal events.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itago mo na iyang **pangseremonya** mong damit at baka magusot pa.","translation":"Put away your **ceremonial** clothes now before they get wrinkled."},{"sentence":"Ang mga espadang ito ay hindi panlaban, kundi **pangseremonya** lamang.","translation":"These swords are not for fighting, but are only **ceremonial**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking labis na magastos, maluho, o walang patumangga sa pagwaldas ng pera.
original_explanation: This is your tito who treats the whole barangay to drinks on payday and is broke by Monday. He's the guy who buys the latest iPhone on a 24-month installment plan but has no savings. He lives by the mantra "YOLO" and "add to cart," much to the horror of his Ipon Challenge-obsessed friends.
usage_notes: The '-or' suffix indicates a male subject. The female counterpart is 'gastadora'. Can be used as a noun (a spendthrift) or an adjective (wasteful).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siyang **gastador** dahil laging bago ang kanyang mga gamit kahit maliit lang ang sahod.","translation":"He's known as a **spendthrift** because his things are always new even if his salary is small."}]

translation: to reverse a statement; to twist facts; to turn against
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-iiba ng sinabi, salaysay, o panig; ang pagbaluktot sa katotohanan o pagtalikod sa isang kasunduan.
original_explanation: What a chismosa does to a story to make it more dramatic. It's when your friend promises to pay you back on payday, but on payday, they suddenly `magbaliktad` and act like they don't owe you anything. The ultimate 'change team' or 'change story' move, often with a hint of betrayal.
usage_notes: While often used interchangeably with 'magbaligtad' (with a 'g') for physical actions, 'magbaliktad' is more strongly associated with changing one's story, testimony, or allegiance. It carries a connotation of twisting facts or betrayal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigla siyang **nagbaliktad** ng testimonya sa korte.","translation":"He suddenly **reversed** his testimony in court."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **baliktarin** ang usapan, alam ko ang sinabi mo.","translation":"Don't **twist** the story, I know what you said."}]

meaning_filipino: Katapangan, tiwala sa sarili, o kahandaang harapin ang panganib, hirap, o hamon nang walang takot.
original_explanation: Literally "strength of the inside." This is the "hugot" you need to confess to your crush, to resign from a toxic job, or to speak up in a meeting. It’s not about muscle; it's about mental and emotional fortitude. When someone says "Wala akong lakas ng loob," they're saying they can't bring themselves to do it. It's the fuel for every "bahala na" moment.
usage_notes: Isang idyomatikong pahayag. Ang kasalungat nito ay "hina ng loob" (kahinaan ng kalooban, kakulangan sa tapang).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng matinding **lakas ng loob** para aminin ang iyong pagkakamali.","translation":"It takes great **courage** to admit your mistake."},{"sentence":"Nagkaroon siya ng **lakas ng loob** na mag-apply sa bagong trabaho.","translation":"She gathered the **confidence** to apply for a new job."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang makapal na takip sa sahig na yari sa tela, karaniwang may disenyo, na ginagamit para sa dekorasyon o upang magbigay-init.
original_explanation: This is what your lola calls a carpet. It's that fancy, sometimes itchy, floor covering na bawal tapakan kapag bagong vacuum. It's the centerpiece of the sala during Christmas reunions, where all the little pamangkins are forced to sit while the adults take the sofa. Think of it as the 'red carpet' of the Filipino household.
usage_notes: Isang salitang medyo luma na ngunit naiintindihan pa rin ng marami, lalo na ng mga nakatatanda. Ang mas karaniwang salita ngayon ay 'carpet'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka at baka matapunan ng kape ang bagong **alpombra** ni Nanay.","translation":"Be careful not to spill coffee on Mom's new **rug**."},{"sentence":"Ang mamahaling **alpombra** mula sa Persia ay regalo ng kanyang tiyahin.","translation":"The expensive **carpet** from Persia was a gift from her aunt."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng panunuyo na hindi seryoso, madalas ay biruan lamang o walang malinaw na intensyon na magkaroon ng pormal na relasyon.
original_explanation: This is the 'M.U.' or 'Mutual Understanding' stage's chaotic cousin. It's like courtship on 'trial mode'. You do the sweet stuff, but without the commitment. Parang laro-laro lang, hanggang sa may isang ma-fall. Usually, isa lang.
usage_notes: Nagpapahiwatig ng hindi seryoso o walang-pananagutang uri ng panunuyo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko alam kung seryoso siya o **ligaw-ligawan** lang ang ginagawa niya.","translation":"I don't know if he's serious or if what he's doing is just a **pretend courtship**."},{"sentence":"Natapos sa **ligaw-ligawan** ang kanilang kwento nang may dumating na iba.","translation":"Their **playful wooing** ended when someone else came along."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahan na magsalita o magsulat nang matatas, malinaw, at may kahusayan.
etymology: From `ka-` + `tatas` (fluency) + `-an`, referring to a high level of skill. The root `tatas` is related to `taas` (height).
original_explanation: The skill of your BPO friend who can switch from deep Tagalog to a perfect American accent in 0.5 seconds. It's that smooth, 'walang sabit' way of speaking that makes people say "Wow, galing!" whether you're delivering a report or a killer comeback.
usage_notes: Often refers to linguistic skill. `Katatasan sa pagsasalita` (fluency in speaking).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinahangaan siya dahil sa kanyang **katatasan** sa wikang Ingles.","translation":"He is admired for his **fluency** in the English language."},{"sentence":"Ang **katatasan** ng kanyang pananalita ay nagpapakita ng kanyang malawak na kaalaman.","translation":"The **eloquence** of his speech shows his vast knowledge."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, tao, o sitwasyon na nagsisilbing pang-akit o panghalina sa isang tao upang gumawa ng isang bagay na karaniwang ipinagbabawal o hindi kanais-nais.
original_explanation: It's that one slice of lechon staring at you when you're on a diet. It's the 'add to cart' button during the 12.12 sale. It's your friend messaging 'shot puno?' on a Wednesday night. Anything that tests your self-control is a pantukso. The devil on your shoulder probably uses this a lot.
usage_notes: From 'pan-' (for/instrument of) + 'tukso' (temptation).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang masasarap na pagkain ang nagsisilbing **pantukso** sa kanyang dieta.","translation":"The delicious food serves as a **temptation** to his diet."},{"sentence":"Iniwasan niya ang mga masasamang kaibigan na nagsisilbing **pantukso** sa kanya.","translation":"He avoided the bad friends who serve as a **lure** to him."}]

meaning_filipino: Daglat para sa "Light Rail Transit," isang sistema ng pampublikong transportasyon sa Metro Manila na gumagamit ng tren.
original_explanation: Light Rail Transit. The metal snake that slithers above Manila's traffic nightmare. It's where you learn the art of "siksikan," personal space becomes a myth, and your bag is worn on your chest like a shield. Cheaper and faster than Grab during rush hour, if you're willing to become a human sardine.
usage_notes: Refers to LRT Line 1 (Yellow Line) and Line 2 (Purple Line). The MRT (Line 3, Blue Line) is a different system but often grouped with it in general conversation about Manila's train systems.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sasakay ako ng **LRT** mula Baclaran hanggang Monumento.","translation":"I will ride the **LRT** from Baclaran to Monumento."},{"sentence":"Laging puno ang **LRT** tuwing rush hour.","translation":"The **LRT** is always full during rush hour."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagsipsip o pag-inom nang may kasamang tunog, karaniwan ay sa maiinit na sabaw o inumin.
original_explanation: That satisfying sound you make when the sinigang is just too good. It's the opposite of a delicate sip; it's a full-on, 'I'm-enjoying-this' slurp. Parang vacuum cleaner ng sabaw.
usage_notes: Often used to describe the audible drinking of soup or hot beverages.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **higop** lang ng kape ay sapat na para magising ako.","translation":"Just one **sip** of coffee is enough to wake me up."},{"sentence":"Ang sarap pakinggan ng **higop** niya sa noodles, alam mong nag-eenjoy siya.","translation":"His **slurp** of the noodles sounds so good, you know he's enjoying it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang daanan na binubuo ng dalawang magkahilerang riles na bakal kung saan dumadaan ang tren.
original_explanation: The OG land transportation system before Grab, Angkas, MRT, and LRT traffic. This is what your lolo and lola rode to go to the province. Today, you mostly hear about it in history books or when the PNR (Philippine National Railways) is in the news. It's the iron path that connects towns, one 'choo-choo' at a time.
usage_notes: A more formal or historical term. 'Riles' is the more common, everyday word for railway track. 'Tren' is for the train itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lumang **perokaril** ay bahagi na ngayon ng kasaysayan ng aming bayan.","translation":"The old **railroad** is now part of our town's history."},{"sentence":"Itinayo ng mga Kastila ang unang **perokaril** sa Pilipinas.","translation":"The Spanish built the first **railway** in the Philippines."}]

meaning_filipino: Nangangahulugang tapos na, kumpleto na, o pinal na ang isang desisyon o bagay.
original_explanation: This is the status of your day-13 salary: 'buo na' (and gone by day 15). It's also what you tell your friend when they try to change your mind about your 'marupok' decisions: 'Friend, buo na ang isip ko. Babalikan ko siya.' It’s the sound of finality, whether for better or for worse.
usage_notes: A very common phrase used to indicate completion or finality of a decision, object, or situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Buo na** ang desisyon kong mag-resign at mag-travel.","translation":"My decision to resign and travel is **already final**."},{"sentence":"Pakitingin kung **buo na** ang bayad niya.","translation":"Please check if his payment is **already complete**."}]

translation: to smell (like something); to give off an odor
meaning_filipino: Ang paglabas o pagkalat ng isang partikular na amoy, mabuti man o masama.
original_explanation: This is what your gym clothes do after a workout. Or what the kitchen does when your tita is cooking adobo. It's the verb for emitting a smell. Unlike 'amuyin' (to smell something), mangamoy is about *being* the source of the smell. 'Bakit nangangamoy usok dito?' (Why does it smell like smoke here?)
usage_notes: The verb for something emitting a smell. It's often followed by 'ng' or 'na' to describe the smell (e.g., mangamoy ng isda, mangamoy na bulaklak).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **mangamoy** sunog sa kusina.","translation":"It started **to smell** like something burning in the kitchen."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong iwan ang basura sa loob ng bahay dahil ito ay **mangangamoy**.","translation":"Don't leave the trash inside the house because it will **start to smell**."}]

meaning_filipino: Lagyan o patungan ng nikel ang isang bagay. Ito ay halos kapareho ng 'nikeladuhin'.
original_explanation: Basically the same as 'nikeladuhin'. It's the command form: 'Go nickel-plate this!' It's a more direct Tagalog construction (root + -hin) compared to the Spanish-derived 'nikeladuhin'. Both mean the same thing: to give something that shiny, protective metal coating.
usage_notes: Synonym for 'nikeladuhin', though the latter might be slightly more common due to the influence of the adjective 'nikelado'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Balak kong **nikelahin** ang mga riles ng aking motorsiklo.","translation":"I plan **to nickel-plate** the rims of my motorcycle."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **nikelahin** 'yan para hindi agad masira.","translation":"Don't forget **to nickel-plate** that so it won't get damaged quickly."}]

translation: to become a young woman, to reach adolescence (for a female)
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-abot sa yugto ng pagbibinata o pagiging dalaga ng isang babae; ang pagbabago mula sa pagiging bata patungo sa pagiging isang kabataang babae.
original_explanation: This is the stage when a girl starts getting the "dalaga ka na" speech from every tita at the family reunion. It means she's transitioning from a kid to a young lady. Suddenly, there are new rules, more chores, and a lot of unsolicited advice about boys. It's the Filipina's coming-of-age story, minus the Hollywood budget.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to the female transition into adolescence. The male equivalent is 'magbinata'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis lumipas ang panahon, parang kailan lang ay **nagdalaga** na ang aking pamangkin.","translation":"Time flies so fast, it seems like just yesterday my niece **became a young woman**."},{"sentence":"Kapag **nagdalaga** na ang isang babae, maraming pagbabago sa kanyang katawan at isipan.","translation":"When a girl **reaches adolescence**, there are many changes in her body and mind."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng simpleng asukal na nagsisilbing pangunahing panggatong para sa metabolismo ng katawan.
original_explanation: The more common term for 'glukos'. Ito yung "blood sugar" na tinetest sa mga may diabetes. Kapag bagsak, hihimatayin ka. Kapag sobra, iba na 'yan. It's the energy currency of your body.
usage_notes: Ang standard at mas karaniwang pagbaybay para sa glucose sa Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng utak ng sapat na **glukosa** upang gumana nang maayos.","translation":"The brain needs enough **glucose** to function properly."},{"sentence":"Mataas ang kanyang blood sugar, kaya kailangang kontrolin ang paggamit ng **glukosa**.","translation":"Her blood sugar is high, so her **glucose** intake needs to be controlled."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapahayag ng kawalang-kasiyahan, hinanakit, o pagtutol tungkol sa isang bagay o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: The national sport of Pinoys, right next to basketball. From slow internet, to a plot twist in a teleserye, to the intense heat. If there's something to be unhappy about, someone is probably going to **magreklamo**. 'Huwag ka nang magreklamo, gawin mo na lang.' - Every Pinoy mom, probably.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging **nagrereklamo** ang aking kapitbahay tungkol sa ingay.","translation":"My neighbor is always **complaining** about the noise."},{"sentence":"May karapatan kang **magreklamo** kung hindi maganda ang serbisyo.","translation":"You have the right to **complain** if the service is not good."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang kilos ng pagbabahagi ng isang bagay, tulad ng impormasyon, pagkain, o isang post sa social media.
etymology: Tagalog prefix 'nag-' + duplicated first syllable of root 'se-' + English 'share'.
original_explanation: Siya 'yung tipo na nagseshare ng lahat ng bagay sa social media—mula sa kinain sa almusal hanggang sa latest chismis. Oversharer ang lola mo. Pero okay lang kung pagkain ang sineshare, 'di ba?
usage_notes: Present progressive tense. The past tense is 'nag-share' and the future tense is 'mag-she-share'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging **nagseshare** si Tita ng mga fake news sa Facebook.","translation":"My aunt is always **sharing** fake news on Facebook."},{"sentence":"**Nagseshare** kami ng bayad sa upa.","translation":"We are **sharing** the rent payment."}]

translation: to shout at, to yell at, to berate
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasalita nang malakas at may galit o inis sa isang tao; ang pag-sermon o paggalit nang pasigaw.
original_explanation: This is when a regular 'sermon' gets a volume boost. It's what happens when your mom finally finds the Tupperware you lost a year ago. It's not just talking loudly; it's shouting with the full force of parental or managerial disappointment. 'Huwag mo akong sininghalan!' is the classic comeback of a defiant teenager.
usage_notes: 'Maninghal' carries a strong connotation of anger and scolding, more intense than simply 'sumigaw' (to shout). The completed aspect is 'sininghalan' (someone was yelled at).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Madalas **maninghal** ang galit na manager sa kanyang mga empleyado.","translation":"The angry manager often **yells at** his employees."},{"sentence":"**Sininghalan** niya ang bata dahil sa pagbasag nito ng plorera.","translation":"She **shouted at** the child for breaking the vase."}]

translation: to feel numb or tingly; to have pins and needles
meaning_filipino: Makaranas ng pamamanhid o pagkirot sa isang bahagi ng katawan dahil sa matagal na pananatili sa isang posisyon.
etymology: From `ma-` (stative verb prefix) + `ngalay` (numbness, fatigue in a limb).
original_explanation: This is the feeling you get in your butt after a 4-hour meeting that could've been an email, or in your arm after your partner uses it as a pillow all night. It's that 'asleep' limb sensation, the body's way of saying 'Hoy, galaw-galaw din 'pag may time!'
usage_notes: 'Ngalay' is the noun form for the sensation itself. 'Mangalay' is the verb 'to experience ngalay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang umupo nang matagal diyan, baka ka **mangalay**.","translation":"Don't sit there for too long, you might **get pins and needles**."},{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **mangalay** ang braso ko sa kakabuhat ng mga sako ng bigas.","translation":"My arm started to **feel numb** from carrying the sacks of rice."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hanay ng mga prinsipyo, aral, o paniniwala na itinuturo, lalo na sa relihiyon, pilosopiya, o moralidad.
original_explanation: This isn't just any lesson, like how to cook adobo. This is the heavy stuff. The katuruan of a religion, the principles your lolo passed down, or the core values of an organization. It's the 'Gospel Truth' of a certain group or belief system.
usage_notes: Often used in religious, moral, or philosophical contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **katuruan** ni Rizal ay buhay pa rin hanggang ngayon.","translation":"The **teachings** of Rizal are still alive today."},{"sentence":"Sumusunod siya sa **katuruan** ng kanilang relihiyon.","translation":"He follows the **doctrines** of their religion."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na sinanay at may trabahong pumatay ng mapanganib na sunog at magligtas ng mga tao at ari-arian.
etymology: Hiram sa salitang Espanyol na 'bombero' (firefighter, literal na 'pumper').
original_explanation: Ang mga totoong superhero kapag may sunog. Sila yung dumarating na may malakas na sirena at malaking red truck. Hindi lang apoy ang kalaban nila, pati na rin mga usisero sa daan. Sila rin ang nagliligtas ng pusang na-stuck sa puno. Salute to the bomberos!
usage_notes: Ang karaniwang tawag sa isang bumbero sa Pilipinas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis na rumesponde ang mga **bombero** sa nasusunog na gusali.","translation":"The **firefighters** quickly responded to the burning building."},{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang maging **bombero** paglaki niya.","translation":"He dreams of becoming a **firefighter** when he grows up."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging inalis o itinakwil mula sa isang grupo, organisasyon, o posisyon.
original_explanation: The formal version of getting kicked out. It's what happens when you break Rule #1 of the group. Think being removed from your BPO job for too many lates, getting excommunicated from a church, or being impeached. It's a very official "You're fired!" or "You're out!"
usage_notes: Often used in formal contexts like employment, religious organizations, or political parties. Carries a stronger and more official weight than 'pagtanggal'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagkatiwalag** sa kumpanya ay dahil sa malubhang paglabag sa patakaran.","translation":"His **dismissal** from the company was due to a serious violation of policy."},{"sentence":"Ikinagulat ng marami ang balita tungkol sa **pagkatiwalag** ng miyembro sa kanilang simbahan.","translation":"Many were surprised by the news about the member's **expulsion** from their church."}]

translation: to find, to discover, to come across
meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na salita para sa matagpuan, makita, o madiskubre ang isang bagay o tao, kadalasan nang hindi sinasadya.
etymology: ma- (potential verb prefix) + sumpungan (to find). While related to 'sumpong' (whim), its usage evolved separately.
original_explanation: The formal, dramatic way of saying 'nakita'. It's what you say when you finally find the matching sock after a month. "Sa wakas, ika'y aking nasumpungan!" You don't just find something; you *discover* it, like finding your Jollibee Funko Pop that's been missing.
usage_notes: More common in literature, formal speech, and songs than in everyday conversation where 'makita' or 'matagpuan' is preferred.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay **masumpungan** mo ang tunay na kaligayahan.","translation":"I hope you **find** true happiness."},{"sentence":"Sa aming paglalakbay, isang lumang simbahan ang aming **nasumpungan**.","translation":"In our travels, we **came across** an old church."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng itim na mahika o pangkukulam na pinaniniwalaang nagdudulot ng pinsala, sakit, o kamalasan sa isang tao sa pamamagitan ng mga ritwal na isinasagawa ng isang mangkukulam.
original_explanation: This is Pinoy-style voodoo. When something bad happens to a person who wronged someone, the chismis is: 'Naku, baka nakulam 'yan!' It involves a doll, a picture, and a 'mangkukulam' (sorcerer) on speed dial. It's the ultimate, supernatural revenge plot in Filipino folklore.
usage_notes: A central concept in Philippine folklore and superstition, distinct from 'barang' which often involves insects.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naniniwala pa rin ang ilang tao sa probinsya sa bisa ng **kulam**.","translation":"Some people in the province still believe in the power of **witchcraft**."},{"sentence":"Ang biglaang pagkakasakit niya ay ipinapalagay ng iba na dahil sa **kulam**.","translation":"His sudden illness is assumed by others to be because of a **hex**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nag-iisa; walang kapatid.
original_explanation: This is the Pinoy version of "only child." If you're the 'bugtong na anak', you're the solo flight, the one-man team, the sole heir to the family's collection of Tupperware and the remote control. You get all the attention, all the pressure, and all the 'pasalubong'.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in the set phrase "bugtong na anak" (only child). The noun form 'bugtong' means 'riddle'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bilang **bugtong** na anak, lahat ng atensyon ng magulang ay nasa kanya.","translation":"As the **only** child, all of the parents' attention is on him/her."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang opisyal na pagpapatawad mula sa pamahalaan para sa mga taong nakagawa ng mga krimen, lalo na ang mga kasong politikal.
etymology: From Spanish 'amnistía', adapted to Tagalog orthography.
original_explanation: The glow-up version of 'amnistia'. This is the spelling you'll see in modern news reports. It's a government-level "seen-zone" for past offenses. Basically, the state says, "We'll forget your crime if you promise to be good now." A clean slate, but on a national scale.
usage_notes: This is the modern, standard Filipino spelling for amnesty. It is more common than the Spanish 'amnistia'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng Kongreso ang panukalang batas para sa **amnistya**.","translation":"The Congress is studying the proposed bill for **amnesty**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang unti-unting pagkawala ng linaw o kaliwanagan ng isang bagay, tulad ng paningin o isang larawan.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na kailangan mo nang mag-salamin kasi 'di mo na mabasa 'yung text ng ka-talking stage mo. Or 'yung future niyo, biglang 'di mo na maaninag. It's when things start getting unclear, hazy, or blurry.
usage_notes: Kasalukuyang anyo (present progressive) ng 'lumabo'. Ang 'nanlalabo' ay nagpapahiwatig ng mas matindi o tuloy-tuloy na proseso.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nanlalabo** na ang aking paningin dahil sa pagod.","translation":"My vision is **becoming blurry** due to fatigue."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa ulan, **nanlalabo** ang kuha ng kamera.","translation":"Because of the rain, the camera's shot is **getting dim**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang damdamin ng habag o simpatiya para sa paghihirap o kasawian ng iba.
original_explanation: It's that "awww, kawawa naman" feeling. You feel this when you see a stray kitten in the rain, or when your friend tells you their sad "sawi sa pag-ibig" story for the fifth time this week. It's the emotion that makes you want to give your last piece of chicken joy to someone who looks hungrier.
usage_notes: A deep emotion, often leading to acts of kindness or help.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa **pagkaawa**, tinulungan niya ang pulubing umiiyak.","translation":"Out of **pity**, he helped the crying beggar."},{"sentence":"Nakadama ako ng matinding **pagkaawa** sa mga biktima ng bagyo.","translation":"I felt deep **compassion** for the victims of the typhoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang isang babae, bagay, o konsepto na higit na kinagigiliwan, pinipili, o itinatangi kaysa sa iba.
original_explanation: She's the "chosen one." The 'paborita' is the female favorite—the favorite daughter, the teacher's pet (girl version), or your go-to 'paborita'ng ulam' (sinigang, obviously). It's the feminine form of 'paborito'.
usage_notes: Used for female persons or grammatically feminine nouns (though Tagalog doesn't have grammatical gender, the Spanish origin implies it). Can also be an adjective.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **paborita** ng kanilang lola kaya lahat ng gusto niya ay ibinibigay.","translation":"She is the **favorite** of their grandmother, so she gets everything she wants."},{"sentence":"Ang adobo ang **paborita** kong lutuin.","translation":"Adobo is my **favorite** dish to cook."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagpasok ng teksto sa isang aparato tulad ng kompyuter o makinilya gamit ang keyboard.
original_explanation: This is what you do when your boss emails you at 10 PM. It's the sound of deadlines, BPO agents finishing their spiels, and you, furiously crafting the perfect "seen-zoned" reply to your crush. The modern-day "sulat-kamay."
usage_notes: A very common Taglish verb used in both formal and informal settings, especially in offices and schools.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **magtatype** ng sanaysay para sa klase ko sa Filipino.","translation":"I need to **type** an essay for my Filipino class."},{"sentence":"Ang bilis niyang **magtatype** sa keyboard.","translation":"She can **type** so fast on the keyboard."}]

translation: to make do with; to fit
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsisikap na pagkasyahin o gawing sapat ang isang bagay na limitado o kulang.
etymology: `Mapag-` + `kasya` (to fit, be enough). Verb form indicating an effort or ability to make something fit.
original_explanation: This is the art of "budgeting". Yung 500 pesos mo na kailangan mong mapagkasiya for the rest of the week until sahod. It's also about fitting 15 people in a 10-seater jeepney. The ultimate Filipino skill of making things work, no matter how limited the resources. "Diskarte" is its best friend.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of budgets, space, or resources. It implies ingenuity and resourcefulness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **mapagkasiya** ang natirang pagkain para sa hapunan.","translation":"We need to **make** the leftover food **do** for dinner."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang **mapagkasiya** ang lahat ng gamit niya sa isang maliit na maleta.","translation":"She is trying to **fit** all her things into one small suitcase."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng superyor o pinuno sa isang kumbento ng mga madre; ang katumbas na babae ng priyor.
original_explanation: The female counterpart of the priyor. She's the head nun in charge, the 'Mother Superior' you see in movies like 'Sister Act'. She runs the convent, makes the rules, and keeps everything in order. Again, a term you're more likely to read in Noli Me Tángere than hear in a TikTok video.
usage_notes: The female equivalent of 'priyor'. Used in religious and historical contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang **priyora** sa pagpapatupad ng mga alituntunin sa kumbento.","translation":"The **prioress** is strict in implementing the rules in the convent."},{"sentence":"Ang mga madre ay may malaking paggalang sa kanilang **priyora**.","translation":"The nuns have great respect for their **prioress**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-alis o pagtanggal ng abo mula sa isang bagay o lugar, tulad ng kalan o sigarilyo.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "abo" (ash) at hulaping "-hin".
original_explanation: 'Yung utos sa'yo pagkatapos mag-ihaw ng barbecue: "Pakitanggal naman 'yung mga abo." O 'yung ginagawa mo sa yosi mo bago ka ulit humithit. Different stress, different meaning! Huwag malito.
usage_notes: The pronunciation stress shifts to the last syllable to indicate the verb form, differentiating it from the adjective.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Abuhin** mo muna ang sigarilyo mo bago itapon.","translation":"**Remove the ashes** from your cigarette before throwing it away."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **abuhin** ang kalan bago magluto ulit.","translation":"We need to **remove the ashes** from the stove before cooking again."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pagkakaroon ng kulay berde o luntian.
etymology: From "ma-" (prefix indicating "having the quality of") + "berde" (from Spanish "verde" meaning green).
original_explanation: Yung utak ng kaklase mong laging may "joke" na bastos? Medyo maberde. It means "green," but colloquially, it means having a "green mind" or being perverted. But it can also literally mean greenish, like unripe fruit or a lush field.
usage_notes: Has a common colloquial meaning related to having a "dirty mind." The literal meaning is "greenish."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Maberde** pa ang mga mangga kaya huwag mo munang pitasin.","translation":"The mangoes are still **greenish**, so don't pick them yet."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa klase sa pagkakaroon ng **maberde** na pag-iisip.","translation":"He is known in class for having a **green** (perverted) mind."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghawak o pagkontrol sa isang sasakyan; maaari ring tumukoy sa pangkalahatang pangangasiwa o pagpapatakbo ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: Literally, the steering wheel of a car ('Hawakan mo ang maneho'). But figuratively, it's how you handle a situation. 'Ikaw na bahala sa maneho' means 'You're in charge now, you handle it.' It’s your strategy, your way of doing things. When your mom leaves you in charge of your younger siblings, you've got the 'maneho.'
usage_notes: Can refer to the physical steering wheel or the abstract concept of control or management. The verb form is 'manehohin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bago pa lang siyang marunong mag-drive kaya mahigpit ang hawak niya sa **maneho**.","translation":"He's just learning how to drive, so his grip on the **steering wheel** is tight."},{"sentence":"Ang galing ng **maneho** niya sa proyekto, natapos agad.","translation":"His **handling** of the project was excellent; it was finished quickly."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang simbolo, salita, o mga salita na legal na nakarehistro o itinatag sa pamamagitan ng paggamit bilang kumakatawan sa isang kumpanya o produkto.
original_explanation: This is the official 'brand' of a product. Think Jollibee's bee, Nike's swoosh, or even your favorite milk tea shop's logo. It's the reason why you pay more for something that has a specific name on it, kahit pareho lang naman ang lasa sa iba. It's the 'resibo' of a company's reputation.
usage_notes: Madalas na pinaikli sa "tatak" sa pang-araw-araw na usapan (hal. "Anong tatak ng sapatos mo?").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinarehistro ng kumpanya ang kanilang **tatak-pangkalakal** upang maprotektahan ito laban sa mga peke.","translation":"The company registered their **trademark** to protect it against counterfeits."},{"sentence":"Kilala ang **tatak-pangkalakal** na iyon sa buong mundo.","translation":"That **trademark** is known all over the world."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang kilos ng pagdating o pag-abot sa isang destinasyon. Ito ay nagpapahiwatig ng isang proseso o paggalaw na hindi pa natatapos.
original_explanation: This is the present tense of arrival. It's the feeling of anticipation. 'Dumarating' na yung Shopee delivery mo. 'Dumarating' na yung sweldo. It's that 'on the way' status. It's also used for things you can't control, like 'dumarating na ang katapusan ng buwan' (the end of the month is coming), which means bills are also 'dumarating'.
usage_notes: This is the present progressive tense of 'dumating', indicating an ongoing or imminent arrival.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naririnig ko na ang bus, **dumarating** na!","translation":"I can hear the bus, it's **arriving** now!"},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, ang tulong ay **dumarating** na.","translation":"Don't worry, help **is coming**."}]

meaning_filipino: Paggamit ng isang matalim na kasangkapan, tulad ng itak o palakol, upang putulin o hiwain nang may puwersa ang isang bagay.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "taga" (pagputol gamit ang itak) at hulaping "-in".
original_explanation: What you do to a coconut when you're thirsty on a provincial beach trip. Also, a 'hugot' term for what your ex did to your heart. 'Tinaga niya ang puso ko.' The more dramatic version of 'hiwain'.
usage_notes: Implies using a heavy blade like a bolo, machete, or axe with forceful downward strokes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **tagain** ang mga damo sa bakuran gamit ang itak.","translation":"You need **to chop** the weeds in the yard using the bolo."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubos na pagod; sumuko na; walang nang lakas o kakayahang lumaban.
original_explanation: That feeling after a 12-hour shift, back-to-back meetings, and a 2-hour commute. You're not just tired, you're **rendido**—drained, defeated, at gusto mo na lang humilata at mag-scroll sa phone hanggang makatulog. It's the 'ayoko na, suko na ako' level of pagod.
usage_notes: Describes a state of extreme physical or emotional exhaustion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Rendido** na ang mga sundalo matapos ang maghapong labanan.","translation":"The soldiers were **exhausted** after the whole day of fighting."},{"sentence":"Pagdating ng Biyernes, **rendido** na ako sa dami ng trabaho.","translation":"By the time Friday arrives, I'm already **rendered** exhausted from so much work."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaikling at impormal na tawag para sa restoran o restawran.
original_explanation: The short, chic, and slightly conyo way to say 'restaurant'. 'Tara, food trip tayo sa bagong resto sa kanto!' is the battle cry of barkadas everywhere. It's faster to type, easier to say, and makes you sound like you know the latest food spots. It's the 'kain tayo labas' upgrade.
usage_notes: Highly colloquial and used in informal spoken and written language, especially among younger generations and in urban areas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Saan 'yung bagong **resto** na sinasabi mo?","translation":"Where's that new **resto** you were talking about?"},{"sentence":"Puno lahat ng **resto** dito, sa iba na lang tayo kumain.","translation":"All the **restos** here are full, let's just eat somewhere else."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nanloloko o nandaraya sa iba, karaniwang sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng pekeng ginto o metal, o sa pamamagitan ng pangingikil ng pera.
etymology: Mula sa `mang-` + `tanso` (copper, brass). Ang `mang-` ay nagiging `manan-` at inuulit ang unang pantig ng salitang-ugat.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung original "scammer". Bago pa magkaroon ng online investment scams, andyan na sila, nagbebenta ng "gold" bar na gawa pala sa tanso. Sila 'yung dahilan kung bakit kinakagat ng mga lola 'yung alahas para i-check kung totoo.
usage_notes: Nagmula ang termino sa mga manloloko na nagpapanggap na ginto ang tanso. Ngayon, tumutukoy na ito sa pangkalahatang manloloko o mangingikil.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa mga **manananso** na naglipana sa Quiapo.","translation":"Be careful of the **swindlers** that are rampant in Quiapo."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang paggalaw o pag-urong ng katawan dahil sa gulat, takot, o sakit.
original_explanation: This is that mini-jump or twitch you do when someone surprises you from behind, or when you're watching a horror movie and the jump scare gets you. It's your body's "OMG!" reaction before your brain even processes what's happening. A physical manifestation of being *nagulat*.
usage_notes: Similar to *umigkas* but almost exclusively used for a person's or animal's reflexive body movement in response to surprise, fear, or pain.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umigtad** siya nang bigla siyang tapikin sa balikat.","translation":"She **flinched** when she was suddenly tapped on the shoulder."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang malikot, baka **umigtad** ako at masugatan ka ng gunting.","translation":"Don't move around, I might **jerk back** and cut you with the scissors."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tinapay na walang lebadura na ginagamit sa sakramento ng Banal na Eukaristiya sa Simbahang Katoliko, na sinasabing nagiging Katawan ni Kristo.
original_explanation: The super thin, flavorless wafer you get in Catholic Mass that you're not supposed to chew. It's the holiest "snack" you'll ever have. Just don't let it stick to the roof of your mouth, or you'll have an awkward moment with God. The alternate spelling 'ostia' is also used.
usage_notes: Mahigpit na ginagamit sa kontekstong relihiyoso, partikular sa Katolisismo. Ang 'Ostya' ay ang mas karaniwang Filipinisadong baybay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumila ang mga tao para tumanggap ng **Ostya**.","translation":"The people lined up to receive the **Host**."},{"sentence":"Sagrado ang **Ostya** para sa mga Katoliko.","translation":"The **Host** is sacred for Catholics."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa paggawa ng isang bagay nang palitan o halinhinan; paputol-putol o hindi tuloy-tuloy.
etymology: Pag-uulit ng salitang "salit", na nangangahulugang isingit o pagpalitin.
original_explanation: It's the "you go, then I go" system. Like sharing one pair of earphones with your jowa, one earbud each. Or when the internet connection is so bad, it's 'meron, wala, meron, wala'—that's salit-salit. It's the traffic light of actions: stop, go, stop, go.
usage_notes: Maaaring gumanap bilang pang-uri na naglalarawan sa isang bagay bilang paputol-putol, o pang-abay na naglalarawan sa isang kilos na ginagawa nang palitan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Salit-salit** ang ulan at araw buong hapon.","translation":"The rain and sun were **intermittent** all afternoon."},{"sentence":"Magbabantay tayo sa tindahan nang **salit-salit**.","translation":"We will watch the store by **taking turns**."}]
