meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis at biglaang pagkuha ng isang bagay gamit ang kamay, madalas sa paraang marahas o sakim.
etymology: From 'dakma' (a quick, forceful grab) with the -um- infix.
original_explanation: It's the move you make when there's only one piece of lechon left on the table. It’s a fast, desperate grab. Not a gentle 'abot', but a forceful, 'Akin 'to!' snatch. Think of a snatcher grabbing a phone, or you grabbing the last item on sale during 11.11.
usage_notes: Implies speed, force, and sometimes greed or desperation. Different from a gentle 'kumuha' (to get).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dumakma** ng pagkain ang gutom na bata.","translation":"The hungry child **grabbed** for food."},{"sentence":"Bigla na lang may **dumakma** sa bag ko habang naglalakad ako.","translation":"Suddenly someone **snatched** my bag while I was walking."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagong mag-aaral, karaniwan sa unang taon ng kolehiyo o hayskul.
etymology: From English slang 'freshie', a diminutive of 'freshman'.
original_explanation: The new kid on the block, usually in college. They're the ones walking around campus with a map, looking both excited and terrified. They haven't been broken by the system... yet. Bless their innocent hearts.
usage_notes: Primarily used in academic settings, especially universities.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan natin 'yung mga **freshie** na mahanap ang building nila.","translation":"Let's help the **freshmen** find their building."},{"sentence":"Noong **freshie** pa ako, naligaw ako sa campus.","translation":"When I was still a **freshman**, I got lost on campus."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sisidlan o lalagyan na karaniwang gawa sa tela, balat, o plastik, na ginagamit sa pagdadala ng mga gamit.
original_explanation: The essential accessory for carrying your whole life around. From your kikay kit and payong to your baon and laptop, the bag is the modern-day bahay-kubo you can sling over your shoulder.
usage_notes: The English word 'bag' is used universally in the Philippines. The native Tagalog word 'supot' (for smaller bags) or 'bayong' (for native woven bags) are also used but 'bag' is more general.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naiwan ko yata ang **bag** ko sa taxi.","translation":"I think I left my **bag** in the taxi."},{"sentence":"Ang bigat ng **bag** mo! Ano ba'ng laman niyan?","translation":"Your **bag** is so heavy! What's inside it?"}]

meaning_filipino: Gamitin bilang pamagat o titulo ng isang akda, kanta, o anumang likhang-sining.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you have a stroke of genius for your thesis or your next viral blog post. You take a concept or a line and make it THE title. 'Yung hugot line mo, pwede nang ipamagat sa isang teleserye!' (That dramatic line of yours could be used as a title for a TV series!).
usage_notes: The root word 'pamagat' itself comes from 'ba-gat', a now-obsolete root related to naming or invoking.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kantang \"Huling El Bimbo\" ay **ipinamagat** sa isang sikat na musical.","translation":"The song \"Huling El Bimbo\" was **used as the title** for a famous musical."},{"sentence":"Napagdesisyunan niyang **ipamagat** ang kanyang libro na \"Mga Tala ng Isang Manlalakbay\".","translation":"He decided **to title** his book \"Notes of a Traveler\"."}]

meaning_filipino: Marumi sa sukdulan; hindi malinis sa katawan o kapaligiran.
original_explanation: The ultimate word for "unhygienic" or "filthy." It's not just dirty, it's disgustingly so. It's the state of your room after a week-long gaming marathon, or that one friend who double-dips the lumpia in the shared sawsawan. "Kadiri, ang dugyot mo!"
usage_notes: A strong, often insulting word. Use with caution.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang kumain sa karinderyang iyon dahil mukha raw **dugyot**.","translation":"He doesn't want to eat at that eatery because it looks **filthy**."},{"sentence":"Pinagsabihan ng ina ang anak na huwag maging **dugyot** sa sarili.","translation":"The mother told her child not to be so **slovenly**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglalagay sa kaayusan, pag-aareglo, o pagwawasto sa isang bagay o sitwasyon.
etymology: From `pag-` (gerund prefix) + `sa-` (reduplication of first syllable) + `ayos` (order, arrangement). The reduplication implies a more deliberate or extensive process.
original_explanation: This is the official term for getting your life together. From Marie Kondo-ing your closet ('pagsasaayos ng gamit'), to fixing a bug in your code ('pagsasaayos ng system'), to settling a dispute with your chismosa neighbor ('pagsasaayos ng gulo'). It’s the act of turning chaos into order. Your mom probably yells this at you every weekend.
usage_notes: A very versatile word covering physical arrangement, fixing problems, and settling disputes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagsasaayos** ng mga dokumento ay tumagal nang buong araw.","translation":"The **arrangement** of the documents took the whole day."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula na ang **pagsasaayos** ng gusaling nasira ng bagyo.","translation":"The **fixing** of the building damaged by the typhoon has begun."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pagkaing Pilipino na karaniwang tumutukoy sa pritong mani na may bawang at asin, na kinakain bilang kutkutin.
etymology: From 'buto' (seed/bean) with a Spanish-style diminutive suffix '-itos'.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate pampulutan or movie snack. Forget popcorn, `butitos` is that crunchy, garlicky peanut goodness that you can't stop eating once you start. The name might sound like 'little boots' in Spanish, but it's all about the peanuts, baby.
usage_notes: While it can mean 'small beans', it almost exclusively refers to the peanut snack in modern usage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito niyang papakin ang **butitos** habang nanonood ng basketball.","translation":"His favorite snack is **fried peanuts with garlic** while watching basketball."}]

translation: to gasp repeatedly, to pant heavily
meaning_filipino: Paulit-ulit at hirap na paghinga, tulad ng isang taong nalulunod o sobrang pagod.
original_explanation: This isn't just one gasp, it's a whole series. Think of a fish out of water. Or you, after your team lead gives you three urgent tasks due EOD on a Friday. It's the physical manifestation of being overwhelmed, exhausted, or literally struggling to breathe. Hiningal level 99.
usage_notes: The reduplication indicates intense, continuous, and difficult breathing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumisingap-singap** ang biktima nang matagpuan siya ng mga rescuer.","translation":"The victim was **gasping repeatedly** when the rescuers found him."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko siyang **sumingap-singap** sa pagod matapos ang marathon.","translation":"I saw him **panting heavily** from exhaustion after the marathon."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang masinsinang pagtatanong sa isang tao upang makakuha ng tiyak na impormasyon, karaniwang sa isang pormal o seryosong paraan.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you come home at 2 AM and your parents ask, 'Saan ka galing?' It's not a simple question; it's a full-blown investigation. It's a rapid-fire Q&A session where you're the star witness and you're definitely guilty of something.
usage_notes: A compound verb from 'sulit' (to account for) and 'tanong' (question). It implies a formal and demanding line of questioning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula nang **magsulit-tanong** ang mga pulis sa nahuling suspek.","translation":"The police began **to interrogate** the captured suspect."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magsulit-tanong** na parang isa akong kriminal!","translation":"Don't **question me intensely** as if I were a criminal!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang liwanag na nagmumula sa araw; ang pag-angat ng araw sa umaga.
original_explanation: Literally "the fame of the sun," which is the most poetic way to say sunlight or sunrise. It's the natural alarm clock that makes you pull the blanket over your head for five more minutes. Also the reason your black shirt feels like an oven in May.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably for both 'sunrise' and 'sunlight'. Context is key. 'Pagsikat ng araw' more specifically means sunrise.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iwasan mong magbabad sa matinding **sikat ng araw**.","translation":"Avoid staying too long under the intense **sunlight**."},{"sentence":"Napakaganda ng **sikat ng araw** sa tuktok ng bundok.","translation":"The **sunrise** is so beautiful at the top of the mountain."}]

meaning_filipino: Dumaan sa mga liku-liko, makitid, o masalimuot na daanan.
original_explanation: This is what your Grab driver does to avoid EDSA traffic, taking you through mysterious side streets you never knew existed. It's navigating the labyrinth of Quiapo or Divisoria to find the best deals. It's not a straight path; it's the scenic, 'shortcut' route that sometimes feels longer.
usage_notes: Describes movement through a complex, winding path. The root 'sikot' itself is not commonly used alone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumikut-sikot** ang motorista sa mga eskinita para makaiwas sa trapik.","translation":"The motorist **meandered** through the alleyways to avoid the traffic."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **sumikut-sikot** sa palengke para mahanap ang tindahan ni Aling Nena.","translation":"You need to **wind through** the market to find Aling Nena's store."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o proseso ng pagiging lasing dahil sa labis na pag-inom ng alak o anumang inuming nakalalasing.
original_explanation: That Friday night state of mind after a hell week at work. It's the journey from "isa pa" to "sino ka?" to "bakit may traffic cone sa kwarto ko?" It's the official sport of many titos during reunions. The goal is to forget your problems, but the side effect is you also forget your ATM pin.
usage_notes: Refers to the process or act of becoming intoxicated. 'Kalasingan' refers to the state of being drunk.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang madalas na **paglalango** ay masama sa kalusugan.","translation":"Frequent **getting drunk** is bad for one's health."},{"sentence":"Iwasan ang **paglalango** upang makaiwas sa gulo.","translation":"Avoid **inebriation** to stay out of trouble."}]

translation: to take something home; to bring home
meaning_filipino: Dalhin ang isang bagay o tao patungo sa tahanan.
original_explanation: The ultimate goal after a long day at the office or a fun night out. It's what you do with your take-out, your sweldo, or your new jowa. "Pre, iuwi na natin 'to," can mean "let's take this food home" or "let's finish this drinking session and go home."
usage_notes: Very common verb. The object of the verb is the thing being brought home.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **iuwi** ang payong mo.","translation":"Don't forget to **bring** your umbrella **home**."},{"sentence":"Maaari ko bang **iuwi** ang natirang pagkain?","translation":"May I **take home** the leftover food?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging walang laman, hindi okupado, o bukas para sa isang bagong papalit o maninirahan.
etymology: From 'pagka-' (state of being) + 'bakante' (vacant), which is from Spanish 'vacante'.
original_explanation: The "For Rent" or "Now Hiring" sign of life. It could be a vacant position in your BPO team after someone got pirated, an empty apartment unit you're eyeing, or even the state of your love life. It’s a space waiting to be filled.
usage_notes: Used for job openings, empty rooms/properties, or any unoccupied position.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inanunsyo ng kumpanya ang **pagkabakante** ng posisyong manager.","translation":"The company announced the **vacancy** for the manager position."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa **pagkabakante** ng apartment, naghahanap sila ng bagong uupa.","translation":"Because of the **vacancy** of the apartment, they are looking for a new tenant."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagpupulong ng mga miyembro ng isang partidong pampulitika o pangkat upang pag-usapan ang mga patakaran, nominado, o estratehiya.
original_explanation: Parang group chat ng mga politiko bago ang main event. Dito sila nag-uusap-usap kung sino ang iboboto nila, anong bill ang susuportahan, o sino ang i-o-oust sa committee. It's the pre-game huddle for politicians, where they align their strategies before facing the public (or their rivals).
usage_notes: A direct loanword used in political and organizational contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng biglaang **kawkus** ang mga senador bago ang botohan.","translation":"The senators had a sudden **caucus** before the voting."},{"sentence":"Napagdesisyunan sa **kawkus** ng mayorya na suportahan ang panukalang batas.","translation":"It was decided in the majority **caucus** to support the bill."}]

translation: burnt smell (especially of rice or grains)
meaning_filipino: Amoy ng nasusunog na kanin, sinangag, o iba pang butil.
original_explanation: That 'oh no' smell when you get distracted by a TikTok video and forget you were cooking rice. It's the specific scent of culinary failure, the ghost of tutong past. Not quite 'sunog' (burnt), but the warning sign that you're about to get there.
usage_notes: Very specific to the smell of scorching grains, particularly rice.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naamoy ko ang **angot** ng kanin mula sa kusina.","translation":"I smelled the **burnt scent** of rice from the kitchen."},{"sentence":"Ayaw na ayaw ni nanay ang **angot** sa sinaing.","translation":"Mother really dislikes the **scorched smell** of cooking rice."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na umaasa sa iba para sa kanyang pagkain, tirahan, at iba pang pangangailangan; walang sariling hanapbuhay at binubuhay ng iba.
etymology: From "pa-" (causative prefix) + "lamon" (to eat voraciously, colloquial) + "-in" (object suffix, here nominalized). It means "one who is to be fed."
original_explanation: Ah, the 'pabigat.' The adult sibling who still lives at home, doesn't pay rent, and their only contribution is eating the food and using the Wi-Fi. It's a harsh term for someone who is completely dependent on others for sustenance. The ultimate 'tambay sa bahay.'
usage_notes: Carries a negative and often derogatory connotation, implying laziness or being a burden.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang maging **palamunin** lamang sa kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"He doesn't want to be just a **dependent** of his parents."},{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na ang pagiging **palamunin** at maghanap ka ng trabaho!","translation":"Stop being a **freeloader** and find a job!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan na ginagamit sa pagsukat ng bigat o timbang ng isang bagay.
etymology: Nagmula sa 'panimbang' at hulaping '-an', na tumutukoy sa lugar o kasangkapan kung saan ginagawa ang pagtitimbang.
original_explanation: This is the actual device, the weighing scale. The one in the palengke that the vendor uses for your kilo of tilapia. The one in your bathroom that you have a love-hate relationship with, especially after the holidays. The panimbangan tells the truth, whether you like it or not.
usage_notes: Ang 'timbangan' ay ang mas karaniwan at pang-araw-araw na termino. Ang 'panimbangan' ay medyo mas pormal o teknikal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inilagay ng tindera ang mga isda sa **panimbangan**.","translation":"The vendor placed the fish on the **weighing scale**."},{"sentence":"Sira yata ang **panimbangan** dahil hindi nagbabago ang timbang ko.","translation":"I think the **weighing scale** is broken because my weight isn't changing."}]

translation: short and direct; concise; to the point
meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pagpapahayag na hindi maligoy, walang labis na salita, at direktang tumutukoy sa pinupunto.
original_explanation: Basically, 'no BS.' It's how your manager wants your report, how your crush *should* reply to your 'kamusta?', and how Google Maps should give directions. Less 'hugot', more 'eto na 'yon'. Straight to the point, walang paligoy-ligoy.
usage_notes: An adjectival phrase describing a manner of speaking, writing, or communication.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko ang sagot na **maikli at tuwiran**.","translation":"I want a **short and direct** answer."},{"sentence":"Naging **maikli at tuwiran** ang kanyang talumpati, ngunit puno ng kahulugan.","translation":"His speech was **concise**, but full of meaning."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing pantay o lapad ang isang ibabaw o lugar, na inaalis ang anumang umbok o lubak.
original_explanation: Like what you wish your love life was—smooth and without any bumps. Or what you do to the dough for pandesal before baking. It's the act of turning a chaotic, uneven surface into something flat and manageable, parang pag-ayos ng gusot sa buhay.
usage_notes: Often used in construction, landscaping, or even cooking (flattening dough).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **patagin** ang lupa bago magtayo ng bahay.","translation":"The land needs to be **flattened** before building a house."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **patagin** ang gusot sa damit gamit ang kanyang kamay.","translation":"He tried to **flatten** the wrinkle on the clothes with his hand."}]

translation: To increase the amount of; to make more
meaning_filipino: Ang pagdaragdag sa bilang o sukat ng isang bagay upang ito ay maging mas marami.
original_explanation: This is what your tita tells the server at a samgyupsal place: 'Damihan mo ang side dish, iho!' It's the command you give your friend pouring the drink, 'Uy, damihan mo!' It's the verb form of 'dami' - the act of making something 'marami'.
usage_notes: Often used as a command or a request. The opposite is 'kauntian' (to lessen).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Damihan** mo ang asukal sa kape ko, pakiusap.","translation":"**Add more** sugar to my coffee, please. (Literally: Make the sugar in my coffee more in amount)"},{"sentence":"Sabi ni nanay, **damihan** ko raw ang kanin para mabusog ako.","translation":"Mom said I should **increase the amount** of rice so I'll be full."}]

translation: to harvest or deal with snow peas
meaning_filipino: Isang gawain sa agrikultura na tumutukoy sa pag-ani o pag-aalaga ng apina (sitsaro).
etymology: From `apina`, a local term for snow pea (sitsaro), possibly of Ilocano or Cordilleran origin.
original_explanation: This is a deep cut. If you know this word, you probably live near Baguio or have a farm. Mag-apina is the verb for harvesting snow peas (sitsaro/apina). It's the kind of word you'd hear in a palengke up north, not in a BGC coffee shop.
usage_notes: Very specific and regional term. The more common term for snow pea is 'sitsaro'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaga silang pumunta sa bukid para **mag-apina**.","translation":"They went to the farm early **to harvest snow peas**."},{"sentence":"Nais ni Inay na **mag-apina** para may maisahog sa chopsuey.","translation":"Mother wants **to get some snow peas** to include in the chopsuey."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian na nagdudulot ng pakiramdam ng hiya, pagkailang, o pandidiri dahil sa pagiging pilit, korni, o hindi angkop.
original_explanation: The adjective version of cringe. Ito yung description para sa mga bagay na nagpaparamdam sa'yo ng cringe. Your boss trying to use Gen Z slang? Cringey. Yung mga pilit na 'sweet' moments sa public? Cringey. Yung pag-propose na na-reject? Super cringey.
usage_notes: Essentially the same as using "cringe" as an adjective, but is more formally an adjective. Often preceded by 'ang' or 'sobrang' to intensify it.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **cringey** ng mga pickup lines na ginagamit niya.","translation":"The pickup lines he uses are so **cringey**."},{"sentence":"Napanood mo ba yung **cringey** na interview? Nakakahiya para sa kanya.","translation":"Did you see that **cringey** interview? It's embarrassing for him."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na naghahatid ng mensahe, sulat, o pakete bilang isang trabaho o atas.
original_explanation: The original Grab/Lalamove driver. Sila yung mga taga-deliver ng balita, chismis, o package bago pa nauso ang internet. Sa opisina, sila yung inuutusan mong, 'Pakidala naman nito sa kabilang department.' Today, your favorite food delivery rider is a modern-day mensahero.
usage_notes: Ang katumbas para sa babae ay 'mensahera', bagaman 'mensahero' ay madalas gamitin sa pangkalahatan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinadala ng hari ang kanyang pinagkakatiwalaang **mensahero** sa kabilang kaharian.","translation":"The king sent his trusted **messenger** to the other kingdom."},{"sentence":"Nagtatrabaho siya bilang **mensahero** sa isang malaking kumpanya.","translation":"He works as a **messenger** for a large company."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamaliit na daliri sa kamay ng tao.
original_explanation: The smallest and seemingly weakest finger, but you'll definitely miss it when it's gone. It's the finger you use for a 'pinky promise' (sumpaan sa kalingkingan), the one that always hits the corner of the table, and the one you raise with class while drinking tea (or coffee from a fancy mug). The unsung hero of your hand.
usage_notes: Minsan, ginagamit din ang salitang-ugat na 'kalingking' lamang, ngunit mas karaniwan at pamantayan ang 'kalingkingan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsilbing tanda ng kanilang pangako ang magkadugtong nilang mga **kalingkingan**.","translation":"Their intertwined **little fingers** served as a sign of their promise."},{"sentence":"Masakit kapag naipit ang daliring **kalingkingan** sa pinto.","translation":"It hurts when your **pinky finger** gets caught in the door."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagkaing Hapones na binubuo ng kanin na tinimplahan ng suka (shari), karaniwang may kasamang pagkaing-dagat, tulad ng isda, at iba pang sahog.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Hapones na 寿司 (sushi).
original_explanation: That fancy Japanese food you crave on payday. It's basically glorified rice with raw fish, but we love it. Perfect for a date night or when you want to feel a bit 'sosyal'.
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang hiram na salita na nauunawaan ng halos lahat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tara, kumain tayo ng **sushi** sa bagong bukas na restaurant.","translation":"Let's go eat **sushi** at the newly opened restaurant."},{"sentence":"Paborito kong **sushi** ang may salmon sa ibabaw.","translation":"My favorite **sushi** is the one with salmon on top."}]

translation: a light poke or touch (with a finger)
meaning_filipino: Ang marahan o mabilis na pagdaiti sa isang tao gamit ang dulo ng daliri upang makuha ang pansin. Ginagamit din ito para sa paghila sa gatilyo ng baril.
original_explanation: That quick little poke you do with your finger to get someone's attention without shouting. 'Psst!' in physical form. You give your friend a kalabit in church to show them some chismis on your phone. It can also mean pulling a trigger, so context is key!
usage_notes: As a root word, 'kalabit' is a noun referring to the action. It is frequently used as a verb: 'kalabitin' (to poke/pull), 'kinalabit' (poked/pulled). 'Kalabitin ang gatilyo' means 'to pull the trigger'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman ko ang **kalabit** niya sa aking likod.","translation":"I felt his **poke** on my back."},{"sentence":"**Kinalabit** niya ako para sabihing bababa na siya sa jeep.","translation":"She **poked** me to say she was getting off the jeep."}]

translation: to uproot, to pull out forcefully
meaning_filipino: Pilit na bunutin, tanggalin, o alisin ang isang bagay mula sa pagkakakabit o pagkakatanim nito sa pamamagitan ng malakas na puwersa.
original_explanation: Imagine trying to start a stubborn, old generator or pulling a deeply-rooted weed from the garden with all your might. That's 'hiklatin'. It's a more aggressive, forceful 'hila' or 'bunot'. It’s what you want to do to your Wi-Fi router when the internet dies during a critical online meeting.
usage_notes: Implies a sudden, forceful pull, often against strong resistance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **hiklatin** ang pako na iyan gamit ang martilyo.","translation":"You need to **pull that nail out forcefully** using a hammer."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **hiklatin** ang halaman, dahan-dahanin mo lang.","translation":"Don't **uproot** the plant, do it gently."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasapi ng parehong pangkat o koponan.
original_explanation: Your 'teammate' is your kakampi. Your work wife/husband. The one you share the office chismis with, the one who covers for you when you're late, and the one you compete with for that promotion. It's a complex relationship of camaraderie and low-key rivalry.
usage_notes: Very common in corporate and sports contexts. Used interchangeably with 'ka-team'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Anna ang paborito kong **teammate** dahil lagi siyang tumutulong.","translation":"Anna is my favorite **teammate** because she always helps."},{"sentence":"Nag-away ang mag-**teammate** sa gitna ng laro.","translation":"The **teammates** fought in the middle of the game."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagdaragdag ng mga kinakailangang sangkap, kagamitan, o elemento sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: Before you cook Adobo, you need to `magsangkap`—prepare the soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, etc. It's also what you do when you're building a PC (equipping it with a GPU, RAM) or preparing your emergency go-bag (equipping it with essentials). It's the act of putting all the necessary components together.
usage_notes: Used both in cooking (to add ingredients) and in a more general sense of equipping something with necessary parts or components.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magsangkap** ng lahat ng rekado bago ka magsimulang magluto.","translation":"You need to **include all the ingredients** before you start cooking."},{"sentence":"Ang pamahalaan ay **nagsangkap** ng mga bagong kagamitan sa mga pampublikong ospital.","translation":"The government **equipped** the public hospitals with new equipment."}]

meaning_filipino: Makatanggap ng papuri, paghanga, o pagkilala para sa isang nagawang mabuti o kahanga-hanga.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na na-recognize ka ng boss mo sa team meeting, or sinabihan ka ng nanay mo ng 'Proud ako sa'yo, anak.' It's the validation we all secretly (or not-so-secretly) crave. The opposite of being 'napagalitan'. This is your 'main character moment' fuel.
usage_notes: Object-focus verb. The actor-focus form is 'makapuri'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lahat tayo ay umaasa na **mapuri** sa ating mga pinaghirapan.","translation":"All of us hope **to be praised** for our hard work."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang palitan ng magkasalungat na pananaw o opinyon, na maaaring maging pormal (tulad ng debate) o impormal (tulad ng away).
etymology: From "pag-" (verbal noun prefix) + "talo" (defeat, but in this context, it forms the basis for arguing).
original_explanation: This is what happens when you bring up politics at a family reunion. It's the verbal version of a boxing match. It can be a formal debate club showdown or just you and your sibling arguing over who gets the last piece of chicken. It's the core of every comments section on the internet.
usage_notes: Can range from a friendly debate to a heated argument. The context determines the severity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula sa isang simpleng hindi pagkakaunawaan ang kanilang **pagtatalo**.","translation":"Their **argument** started from a simple misunderstanding."},{"sentence":"Nanalo ang aming grupo sa **pagtatalo** tungkol sa bagong batas.","translation":"Our group won the **debate** about the new law."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita o nakakaramdam ng matinding kagalakan, kasiyahan, o ligaya.
original_explanation: That feeling when your Shopee parcel finally arrives, when the long weekend is announced, or when you see your crush smile back at you. It's a pure, unadulterated state of happiness. The default setting for every "Maligayang Pasko!" greeting.
usage_notes: A common and standard word for "happy."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Maligaya** ako para sa iyong tagumpay.","translation":"I am **happy** for your success."},{"sentence":"Isang **maligaya** at masaganang Bagong Taon sa inyong lahat!","translation":"A **joyful** and prosperous New Year to you all!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sabay o palitang pagkilos ng dalawa o higit pang tao kung saan kinikiliti nila ang isa't isa.
etymology: From mag- (reciprocal action prefix) + kiliti (tickle) + -an (suffix indicating reciprocal action).
original_explanation: The ultimate test of friendship or a relationship. It starts with one person tickling another, then it escalates into a full-blown "kilitian" war. It's fun and games until someone who is "sobrang kilitiin" accidentally kicks you in the face. It’s a mutual, playful act.
usage_notes: The 'mag-'-...'-an' construction strongly denotes a reciprocal action done by two or more people to each other.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghabulan ang magkapatid sa sala at nauwi ito sa **magkilitian**.","translation":"The siblings chased each other in the living room and it ended with them **tickling each other**."},{"sentence":"Ang saya nilang panoorin habang sila'y **nagkikilitian** at nagtatawanan.","translation":"It's fun to watch them while they are **tickling each other** and laughing."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagdiin o pagsisiksik sa isang bagay upang ito ay maging masinsin o siksik, karaniwan upang magkasya sa isang lalagyan.
original_explanation: Think of trying to close an overstuffed maleta after a long vacation. That last-ditch effort to sit on it and force everything in? That's pagikpik. It's the art of making 'kasya' what is clearly 'hindi na kasya'. The official move of anyone packing for a trip or sending a balikbayan box.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of packing things tightly, like clothes in a suitcase or goods in a sack. It's a more specific term than 'pagsisiksik'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ang mahusay na **pagikpik** ng mga damit para magkasya sa maliit na bag.","translation":"Good **compression** of the clothes is needed to fit them into the small bag."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga pagkaing pang-meryenda na karaniwang maalat o matamis at nakabalot, tulad ng 'chips' o 'crackers'.
etymology: From Spanish 'chuchería' (tidbit, sweet), which refers to sweets and knick-knacks.
original_explanation: The official food group of Filipino movie marathons, inuman sessions, and long bus rides. From the sari-sari store staple PEE-WEEnner to the high-end truffle-flavored potato chips you feel guilty buying. Your mom probably warned you about eating too much of this.
usage_notes: Refers to a wide range of packaged snack foods, both savory and sweet.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili ka ng maraming **chichirya** para sa party.","translation":"Buy a lot of **snacks** for the party."},{"sentence":"Bawal sa akin ang **chichirya** sabi ng doktor.","translation":"The doctor told me I'm not allowed to eat **junk food**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit at matigas na butil ng mga halamang tulad ng trigo, mais, o bigas.
original_explanation: 'Yan yung maliliit na butil, 'teh. Parang butil ng kape, mais, o bigas. Pwede ring tumukoy sa texture ng isang bagay, like 'fine-**grano**' na buhangin. Sa photography, 'pag malabo ang picture, sasabihin mo 'Ang **grano** naman nito,' referring to the film grain.
usage_notes: Hindi kasing-karaniwan ng 'butil' sa pang-araw-araw na usapan, ngunit naiintindihan sa mga konteksto ng agrikultura o teknikal na paglalarawan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bawat **grano** ng bigas ay mahalaga sa panahon ng taggutom.","translation":"Every **grain** of rice is precious during a famine."},{"sentence":"Sinuri niya ang kalidad ng mga **grano** ng kape.","translation":"He examined the quality of the coffee **grains** (beans)."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat ng mga manunugtog na gumagamit ng mga instrumentong may kwerdas tulad ng bandurya, laud, oktabina, gitara, at baho de arko.
original_explanation: The Philippines' OG string ensemble, but way cooler. It's the sound of fiestas, school foundation days, and Christmas caroling taken to the next level. Think of a group of titos and titas (or students in barong) making beautiful music with instruments you can't easily pronounce, like the 'bandurya' and 'oktabina'.
usage_notes: Refers to a traditional Filipino plucked-string orchestra.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsasanay ang **rondalya** ng aming paaralan para sa darating na patimpalak.","translation":"Our school's **rondalla** is practicing for the upcoming competition."}]

meaning_filipino: Umiiral o nagaganap sa maikling panahon lamang; hindi pangmatagalan.
etymology: From pa- + N (nasal assimilation of s) + sandali + -an. Indicates something that is for a moment or temporary.
original_explanation: Parang yung 'feelings' niya para sa'yo, a fleeting moment. It's the 'for a while' that hurts. Think of a pop-up store, a summer fling, or the WiFi signal when you're in a moving bus. It's there one moment, gone the next. #WalangForever
usage_notes: Describes things that are not permanent or long-lasting. Often used to contrast with 'pangmatagalan' (long-term).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kasiyahan na dulot ng materyal na bagay ay **panandalian** lamang.","translation":"The happiness brought by material things is only **temporary**."},{"sentence":"Nagkaroon kami ng **panandalian** na pag-uusap bago siya umalis.","translation":"We had a **brief** conversation before he left."}]

translation: to ponder deeply; to speculate about
meaning_filipino: Pag-isipang mabuti at paulit-ulit; suriin ang iba't ibang anggulo o posibilidad ng isang bagay sa isipan.
original_explanation: If 'wariin' is to ponder, 'wari-wariin' is to overthink. It's you at 3 AM, replaying a conversation from 2015 and thinking of a better comeback. It implies a more prolonged, and perhaps more anxious, state of pondering or speculation.
usage_notes: Even more literary and rare than 'wariin'. The reduplication implies a more intensive or repetitive action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gabi-gabi niyang **winawari-wari** kung tama ba ang kanyang naging desisyon.","translation":"Every night, he **ponders deeply** if he made the right decision."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang **wari-wariin** 'yan, tapos na ang lahat.","translation":"Don't **speculate about** that anymore, it's all over."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao, karaniwan ay babae, na mahilig magpakitang-gilas, kumilos nang may kahanginan, o maging mapanligaw sa paraang hindi direkta.
original_explanation: Describes someone who's got that extra 'swish' in their walk and a twinkle in their eye. They're not just walking; they're making an entrance. It's the subtle hair flip, the playful laugh, the 'accidentally' brushing against your arm. It's the analog version of sliding into someone's DMs.
usage_notes: Often has a slightly negative or judgmental connotation. Can also refer to the rustling sound of a skirt or leaves.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa pagiging **waliswis** dahil sa kanyang paraan ng pananamit at pagkilos.","translation":"She is known for being **flirty** because of the way she dresses and acts."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong **waliswis** at baka kung ano ang isipin ng mga tao.","translation":"Don't be too much of a **show-off** or people might think something else."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong may kasariang pambabae; ang katapat ng lalaki.
original_explanation: A woman. A girl. A lady. From your lola, to your nanay, to your ate, to your tita-tita, to the "girl, tama na" friend who stops you from making bad life choices. "Babae kami, hindi babae lang." (We are women, not *just* women.)
usage_notes: Can also be used as an adjective, e.g., "pusong babae" (heart of a woman) or "damit pambabae" (women's clothing).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **babae** sa may bintana ay ang aking ina.","translation":"The **woman** by the window is my mother."},{"sentence":"Siya ay isang matapang at matalinong **babae**.","translation":"She is a brave and intelligent **woman**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng ibon (pamilya Cardinalidae) na kilala sa matingkad na pulang balahibo ng mga lalaki.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "cardenal" (cardinal), dahil sa kulay ng balahibo na kahawig ng kasuotan ng isang kardinal ng simbahan.
original_explanation: The bird version of a celebrity on a red carpet. Super flashy, all red, and definitely stands out. Think of it as the original "Angry Bird," but way more majestic.
usage_notes: Hindi katutubong ibon sa Pilipinas ngunit kilala sa kultura.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakita ako ng isang magandang **kardenal** sa hardin.","translation":"I saw a beautiful **cardinal** in the garden."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagsasabing may kakayahang malaman o hulaan ang mga mangyayari sa hinaharap, kadalasan sa pamamagitan ng baraha, bolang kristal, o pagbasa ng palad.
etymology: From mang- (doer prefix) + reduplication of the first syllable of the root (hu) + hula (guess, predict).
original_explanation: Your go-to person in Quiapo when you're desperate to know if you'll pass the board exams or if your crush will finally notice you. They're the original life coaches, but with more flair, a deck of tarot cards, and a much cheaper consultation fee.
usage_notes: The prefix 'mang-' here denotes a profession or a habitual doer of the action. The person who 'hula's.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagbayad siya sa isang **manghuhula** para malaman ang kanyang kapalaran.","translation":"She paid a **fortune teller** to know her fate."},{"sentence":"Sabi ng **manghuhula**, makikilala ko raw ang aking 'the one' ngayong taon.","translation":"The **soothsayer** said that I would supposedly meet 'the one' this year."}]

translation: to pretend, to feign, to pose as
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-arte o pagkukunwari na ikaw ay isang bagay o isang tao na hindi naman totoo, upang makapanlinlang o magtago ng tunay na katauhan.
original_explanation: That feeling when you see your crush and you try to act cool, calm, and collected, but inside you're screaming. Or that officemate who acts busy but is actually just scrolling through Shopee all day. "Fake it 'til you make it," but make it Tagalog.
usage_notes: Often has a negative connotation, implying deception.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magpanggap** na hindi mo alam ang katotohanan.","translation":"Don't **pretend** that you don't know the truth."},{"sentence":"**Nagpanggap** siyang pulis para makatakas sa trapiko.","translation":"He **posed as** a cop to escape the traffic."}]

translation: profound concept; abstract idea; deep thought
meaning_filipino: Isang malalim at masusing pag-iisip o pagkaunawa sa isang konsepto, ideya, o teorya.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung level of thinking na pang-philosopher o 'yung kaibigan mong biglang humuhugot ng malalim at 3 AM. Hindi lang basta "iniisip," ito 'yung "pinagninilayan" to the max. 'Yung mga dalumat ni Rizal, pang-exam 'yan.
usage_notes: A highly academic or literary term. 'Madalumat' is the adjective form, meaning 'profound' or 'abstract'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **dalumat** ng pag-ibig ay isang paksang hindi nauubos talakayin.","translation":"The **profound concept** of love is a topic that is endlessly discussed."},{"sentence":"Kinakailangan ng malalim na **dalumat** upang maunawaan ang kanyang tula.","translation":"A deep **understanding** is needed to comprehend his poem."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng mahilig magbiro, madalas magsabi ng "charot," o hindi seryoso sa mga sinasabi.
original_explanation: She's the friend who can't go five minutes without cracking a joke or saying something wild followed by a quick "charot!". She's fun, witty, and you can't always tell if she's being serious, which is part of her charm. The male version is "charotero."
usage_notes: The male counterpart is 'charotero'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong seryosohin 'yan, **charotera** 'yan.","translation":"Don't take her seriously, she's a **joker**."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa grupo bilang ang pinaka-**charotera** sa lahat.","translation":"She's known in the group as the biggest **joker** of all."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang balat ng butil ng palay na nahihiwalay sa bigas sa proseso ng paggiling.
original_explanation: Eto yung "dust" ng palay. Parang relationship, kailangan tanggalin yung ipa (mga problema, mga chismis) para makuha mo yung bigas (yung pure love). Madalas ginagamit na panggatong o pagkain ng hayop. Basically, the by-product you have to deal with to get to the good stuff.
usage_notes: Karaniwang maririnig sa mga probinsya o lugar na may palayan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginagamit nila ang **ipa** bilang panggatong sa pagluluto.","translation":"They use **rice chaff** as fuel for cooking."},{"sentence":"Puno ng **ipa** ang sahig ng gilingan.","translation":"The floor of the mill is full of **rice husks**."}]

meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang magbigay ng sapat at katanggap-tanggap na dahilan o paliwanag para sa isang kilos, desisyon, o paniniwala.
etymology: From "ma-" (potential verb prefix) + "pangatwiranan" (to justify, from root "katwiran" - reason).
original_explanation: Yung moment na kailangan mong i-explain sa nanay mo kung bakit 3 AM ka na umuwi. Or sa boss mo kung bakit na-late ka na naman. It's the ability to defend your actions with logic (or at least, what you hope sounds like logic). 'To justify.' Your success rate may vary.
usage_notes: A potential verb form. 'Mapangatwiranan' means something *can be* justified.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **mapangatwiranan** ang malaking gastos kung hindi naman ito kailangan.","translation":"It's difficult **to be able to justify** a large expense if it's not necessary."},{"sentence":"Paano mo **mapangangatwiranan** ang iyong pagliban sa klase?","translation":"How will you **be able to justify** your absence from class?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gusali o bahay na nahahati sa dalawang magkahiwalay na tirahan.
original_explanation: It's a house with a built-in 'marites' barrier (a wall). You and your neighbor share one building but have separate doors. Perfect for when you want your in-laws close, but not 'can-I-borrow-your-suka-at-6-AM' close.
usage_notes: A direct borrowing used in real estate and architecture.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghahanap sila ng uupahang **dupleks** na malapit sa eskwelahan.","translation":"They are looking for a **duplex** for rent near the school."},{"sentence":"Hinati ang malaking lote para pagtayuan ng isang **dupleks**.","translation":"The large lot was divided to build a **duplex**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halamang-gamot (herb) na may mabango at kakaibang lasa, karaniwang ginagamit bilang pampalasa sa mga lutuin tulad ng lugaw, sopas, at mga sawsawan.
original_explanation: The herb that divides friendships. You either think it tastes like a fresh, zesty fiesta in your mouth (like in your Vietnamese pho or Mexican salsa), or you think it tastes like soap. No in-between. In the Philippines, it's the 'special something' in your lugaw or gotong Batangas.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'wansoy', which is the Chinese-Filipino term for the same plant (coriander).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglagay siya ng tinadtad na **kulantro** sa ibabaw ng kanyang lugaw.","translation":"She put chopped **cilantro** on top of her rice porridge."},{"sentence":"Ang **kulantro** ay nagbibigay ng kakaibang bango sa sarsa.","translation":"**Cilantro** gives a unique aroma to the sauce."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-angat sa isang bagay, pagdaragdag sa halaga o bilang, o pag-akyat sa mas mataas na posisyon o antas.
etymology: From `pag-` (prefix) + reduplication of the first syllable of the root `taas` (high, up). The reduplication indicates a continuous, prolonged, or significant action.
original_explanation: The moment everyone is waiting for! `Pagtataas` ng sahod (salary increase). `Pagtataas` ng presyo (price hike) - the one we all dread. `Pagtataas` ng kilay (raising an eyebrow) - the ultimate Filipino side-eye. `Pagtataas` ng bandila (raising the flag) during flag ceremony. It’s all about going up, whether it's your salary, your blood pressure from seeing the new Meralco bill, or your rank at work.
usage_notes: A very versatile word used in economic, social, and physical contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inaprubahan na ang **pagtataas** ng minimum wage.","translation":"The **increase** in the minimum wage has been approved."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagtataas** ng watawat ay isang sagisag ng paggalang sa bansa.","translation":"The **raising** of the flag is a symbol of respect for the country."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng katas mula sa isang pinigang bagay sa ibabaw ng o sa loob ng iba pa.
etymology: Mula sa 'piga' (squeeze) + '-an' (hulaping nagpapahiwatig ng lugar o benepisyaryo).
original_explanation: Ito 'yung command ng nanay mo pag nagluluto ng sinigang: "**Pigaan** mo ng calamansi 'yang isda!" It's the act of squeezing something *for* something else. Like when you squeeze out your last bit of energy to finish your shift, pinipigaan mo 'yung sarili mo para sa kumpanya. Char.
usage_notes: Ang diin ay nasa patutunguhan ng likidong piniga. Iba ito sa 'pigain' na nakatuon sa bagay na pinipiga.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pigaan** mo ng lemon ang tsaa para mas masarap.","translation":"**Squeeze** lemon **into** the tea to make it more delicious."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **pigaan** ng calamansi ang pancit bago kainin.","translation":"Don't forget to **squeeze** calamansi **onto** the pancit before eating."}]

translation: act of pulling out; act of drawing lots
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghila o pagkuha ng isang bagay mula sa kinalalagyan nito, tulad ng damo, ngipin, o papel sa isang palabunutan.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung ginagawa niyo sa Christmas party para malaman kung sino'ng makakatanggap ng mug. O 'yung pagtanggal mo ng isang pirasong uban at pag-realize na may sampu pang kasunod. It's less dramatic than 'pagbunlot'. This is the standard 'pulling out' action, from weeds to raffle tickets.
usage_notes: A general term for pulling something out. 'Pagbunlot' is a more sudden and forceful version.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula na ang **pagbunot** ng mga pangalan para sa raffle.","translation":"The **drawing** of names for the raffle has begun."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagbunot** ng ngipin ay masakit kung walang anesthesia.","translation":"The **extraction** of a tooth is painful without anesthesia."}]

translation: to use a place for a vacation
meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit sa isang lugar bilang destinasyon para sa pamamahinga o pagliliwaliw sa panahon ng bakasyon.
original_explanation: This is what you dream of doing to Boracay, Palawan, or even just Tagaytay during a long weekend. When a place is so nice you want to make it your temporary home for R&R, you want to 'pagbakasyunan' it. 'Tara, pagbakasyunan natin ang Baguio sa December!'
usage_notes: An object-focus verb (-an suffix) where the object is the place being used for vacation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais naming **pagbakasyunan** ang Palawan sa susunod na taon.","translation":"We want **to have our vacation in** Palawan next year."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hindi inaasahang pagharap sa isang kasong legal o demanda sa korte.
original_explanation: Yung akala mo chismis lang, pero biglang may natanggap ka nang sulat galing sa abogado. Congrats, you might "mapademanda"! This is the adulting version of being sent to the principal's office. It's the legal trouble nobody wants.
usage_notes: A specific legal term. The "mapa-" prefix suggests that this is an unwanted or unexpected event happening to the subject.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa mga pinopost online, baka ka **mapademanda** ng libel.","translation":"Be careful with what you post online, you might **be sued** for libel."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggalaw gamit ang mga paa; isang gawain o tungkulin na kailangang tapusin; isang usapan o plano.
original_explanation: A super versatile word. Can be a literal 'lakad' (walk) in the park. Can be an errand ('May lakad ako sa bangko'). Can be a plan ('Tuloy ba ang lakad natin?'). Can be a shady deal ('May lakad ka ba sa LTO?' meaning, 'Do you have a fixer?'). It’s all about what needs to get done.
usage_notes: Extremely versatile. Context is key to understanding its specific meaning. 'Maglakad' is the verb 'to walk'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahaba-habang **lakad** ang papunta sa talon.","translation":"It's a long **walk** to the falls."},{"sentence":"Pasensya na, may importante akong **lakad** mamaya.","translation":"Sorry, I have an important **errand/appointment** later."},{"sentence":"Ituloy natin ang **lakad** natin bukas.","translation":"Let's push through with our **plan** tomorrow."}]

translation: to revolt; to rise up; to leaven (dough)
meaning_filipino: Tumayo at lumaban laban sa isang kapangyarihan o awtoridad; umangat ang masa (tulad ng tinapay).
original_explanation: This word has two vibes. First, it's the Katipunero spirit: "Enough is enough! Mag-aalsa tayo!" It's the ultimate act of protest, from staging a rally on EDSA to just refusing to do the dishes. Second, it's what your pandesal dough does before it becomes breakfast. If your dough doesn't 'mag-alsa', you get a rock, not bread. So, whether you're a revolutionary or a baker, you need things to rise.
usage_notes: The meaning depends heavily on context. "Mag-alsa laban sa gobyerno" (to revolt against the government) vs. "Hayaang mag-alsa ang masa" (Let the dough rise).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang mga manggagawa na **mag-alsa** laban sa hindi makatarungang sahod.","translation":"The workers decided to **revolt** against unfair wages."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong hintayin na **mag-alsa** ang masa bago ito iluto.","translation":"You need to wait for the dough to **rise** (leaven) before baking it."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang matinding paghamak, pag-alipusta, o pag-insulto sa isang tao sa paraang nakakababa ng kanyang pagkatao o dignidad.
etymology: From `dusta` (scorn, grave insult) + `-um-` (actor-focus infix). Possibly from Sanskrit दुष्ट (duṣṭa, “wicked, corrupt”).
original_explanation: This isn't your everyday "asar" or "lait." This is verbal demolition. It's when someone doesn't just make fun of you, they try to crush your soul with words. Think of a villain's monologue belittling the hero, or a really, *really* toxic argument where someone says things designed to destroy your self-worth. It's insult on hard mode.
usage_notes: A very strong word, often found in literature, formal speeches, or describing very serious verbal abuse.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi makatarungan na **dumusta** ng kapwa dahil lamang sa kanilang katayuan sa buhay.","translation":"It is unjust **to scorn** others just because of their status in life."},{"sentence":"Sa kanyang galit, **dinusta** niya ang lahat ng tumulong sa kanya.","translation":"In his anger, he **gravely insulted** everyone who helped him."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging kulay luntian; ang kasaganaan ng mga halaman o pananim sa isang lugar.
original_explanation: Ito yung view na hinahanap mo kapag pagod ka na sa city life at sa computer screen. The greenness of Tagaytay, the rice fields of Banaue, o kahit yung park sa kanto. It's the visual equivalent of a deep, relaxing breath. It's the color of "sana ganito na lang lagi."
usage_notes: Often used in a poetic or literary context to describe nature.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakabighani ang **kaluntian** ng mga bukirin sa probinsya.","translation":"The **greenness** of the fields in the province is captivating."},{"sentence":"Pinapanatili nila ang **kaluntian** ng parke para sa susunod na henerasyon.","translation":"They preserve the **verdure** of the park for the next generation."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar, karaniwan sa loob ng isang paaralan, opisina, o pabrika, kung saan maaaring bumili at kumain ng pagkain.
etymology: Mula sa Italyano "cantina" sa pamamagitan ng Espanyol "cantina".
original_explanation: Ah, the high school kantina. The place of overpriced soft drinks, legendary siomai, and chismis during recess. It's where you spent your baon, made friends over a shared bag of chips, and learned the art of 'pa-utang muna, bayad bukas'.
usage_notes: Primarily used for school or office cafeterias.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkita-kita ang magkakaibigan sa **kantina** tuwing tanghalian.","translation":"The friends met at the **canteen** every lunch break."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang fishball na tinda sa **kantina** ng aming paaralan.","translation":"The fishball sold at our school's **canteen** is delicious."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng bitag, karaniwang gawa sa lubid o alambre na may paikot na buhol, na ginagamit sa panghuli ng mga hayop. Ito rin ay maaaring tumukoy sa anumang uri ng patibong o panlilinlang.
original_explanation: Yung pa-fall moves ng crush mo na akala mo totoo na, pero silo lang pala. It's a trap! Pwedeng literal na panghuli ng manok sa probinsya, o figurative na panghuli ng puso ng marupok. Admiral Ackbar warned us about this.
usage_notes: Maaaring maging literal (para sa hayop) o matalinghaga (isang patibong o pakana).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakahuli ng mailap na ibon ang mangangaso gamit ang kanyang **silo**.","translation":"The hunter caught an elusive bird using his **snare**."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa mga **silo** ng kasakiman at huwag magpadala sa tukso.","translation":"Beware of the **traps** of greed and do not give in to temptation."}]

meaning_filipino: Ipagbigay-alam sa isang may kapangyarihan, tulad ng magulang, guro, o pulis, ang isang maling ginawa ng iba.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'sipsip' or 'Bida Bida' move from your childhood. 'Mama, si kuya kinuha yung chocolate ko!' That's you using 'isumbong'. As an adult, it's what you do when your chismosang kapitbahay is breaking quarantine rules again. You screenshot the evidence and 'isumbong' them to the barangay captain. #Sumbongera
usage_notes: Ang unlaping 'i-' ay nakapokus sa tao o gawang isinusumbong.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi kita **isusumbong** sa ating guro.","translation":"Don't worry, I won't **tell on** you to our teacher."},{"sentence":"**Isumbong** mo sa pulis ang anumang kahina-hinalang gawain sa inyong lugar.","translation":"**Report** any suspicious activity in your area to the police."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kabuuan ng mga bansang Kristiyano o ang lipunan ng mga Kristiyano sa buong mundo.
etymology: From circumfix `ka- -an` + `Kristiyano` (Christian), from Spanish 'Cristiano'. The circumfix denotes a collective group or territory.
original_explanation: This refers to the entire global community of Christians. It's the collective noun for everyone from the Pope in the Vatican to your lola who insists you go to Simbang Gabi. It's the worldwide "group chat" for followers of Christianity.
usage_notes: A formal term, often used in religious, historical, or academic contexts. Note the capitalization.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Pasko ay isang mahalagang pagdiriwang para sa buong **Kakristiyanuhan**.","translation":"Christmas is an important celebration for all of **Christendom**."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang naging impluwensiya ng Roma sa kasaysayan ng **Kakristiyanuhan**.","translation":"Rome had a great influence on the history of **Christendom**."}]

translation: act of hitting; striking; taking a shot
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtama, pagpalo, o paghampas sa isang target; pagpapakawala ng bala o pag-atake.
original_explanation: In basketball, this is your 'shot'. In a 'bardagulan' (online fight), this is your witty comeback that lands perfectly. 'Grabe yung **pagtira** niya ng three-points, panalo na sana kami!'
usage_notes: Often used in sports (basketball, billiards) or in a combative sense. The stress is on the first syllable of the root: TI-ra.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malakas na **pagtira** sa bola ang nagpanalo sa kanila.","translation":"One strong **hit** of the ball made them win."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aralan niya ang tamang **pagtira** sa bilyar.","translation":"He studied the correct way of **taking a shot** in billiards."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang rolyo o bilot ng anumang bagay, tulad ng banig o papel.
original_explanation: The 'thing' that you rolled up. 'Yung banig na ni-roll mo? That is now a **likit** of banig. Yung diploma mo na naka-rolyo? That's a **likit** too. It's the finished product of the verb 'likit'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iabot mo sa akin ang isang **likit** ng lumang mapa.","translation":"Hand me that **roll** of old maps."},{"sentence":"Bumili siya ng tatlong **likit** ng wallpaper.","translation":"She bought three **rolls** of wallpaper."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan na may patag na ibabaw at isa o higit pang mga paa, ginagamit upang pagpatungan ng mga bagay tulad ng pagkain, aklat, o iba pang kagamitan.
original_explanation: The OG flat surface. Where meals are shared, chismis is served, and where your parents put your report card for a 'serious talk'. In the office, it's where your laptop, 2-day-old coffee mug, and dreams of an early dismissal reside. The Filipino 'mesa' is the center of family life.
usage_notes: An extremely common word. The native Tagalog term 'hapag' or the more common 'lamesa' (from Spanish 'la mesa') are also used, with 'hapag' often being more poetic or formal (e.g., 'hapag-kainan').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-ayos ang mga plato sa **mesa**.","translation":"Please arrange the plates on the **table**."},{"sentence":"Naiwan ko ang aking susi sa ibabaw ng **mesa**.","translation":"I left my keys on top of the **table**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa anumang bagay, kasangkapan, o substansiya na ginagamit sa akto ng pagligo.
original_explanation: This is your 'ligo kit.' The sabon, shampoo, bimpo, tabo, anything you use to wash away the day's stress (or the evidence of your commute sa MRT). It's the arsenal you bring to the bathroom battlefield to feel 'fresh na fresh'.
usage_notes: Often used to describe items like soap, shampoo, or even the water itself intended for a bath.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng bagong sabong **pampaligo** na amoy sampaguita.","translation":"I bought a new soap **for bathing** that smells like sampaguita."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong ubusin ang tubig na **pampaligo**.","translation":"Don't use up all the water **for bathing**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkain nang may malaking gana, mabilis, at kadalasan ay marami.
etymology: Filipino slang, origin uncertain but popularized in the late 20th century.
original_explanation: This isn't just 'kain.' This is 'kain' on beast mode. It's what you do at a buffet, a fiesta, or when your officemate brings free pizza. No poise, just pure, unadulterated enjoyment of food. "Tara, lafang na!" is the battle cry.
usage_notes: Primarily used in informal, spoken language. Often used with 'nang' (e.g., 'lafang nang lafang') to denote continuous, enthusiastic eating.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mahiya, **lafang** lang nang **lafang**!","translation":"Don't be shy, just **devour** all you can!"},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng exam, nag-**lafang** kami sa Samgyupsal.","translation":"After the exam, we **pigged out** on Samgyupsal."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paghihiwalay ng mga latak o dumi sa isang likido hanggang sa ito ay maging malinaw; ang pagkalma ng isang sitwasyon o damdamin.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your 'sinigang' broth after you let it rest and all the 'sahog' bits sink. Figuratively, it's that moment of calm after a huge fight with your jowa, when emotions have settled and you can finally talk properly. 'Hintayin natin ang **pagtining** ng isyu bago tayo magdesisyon.'
usage_notes: Used for both liquids becoming clear and situations/emotions becoming calm.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng ilang oras na **pagtining**, luminaw ang tubig-baha sa bote.","translation":"After a few hours of **settling**, the floodwater in the bottle became clear."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng **pagtining** ng damdamin bago sila magkausap muli.","translation":"A **calming** of emotions is needed before they can talk again."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa anyong yelo o nanigas dahil sa sobrang lamig; hindi gumagalaw dahil sa takot o gulat.
original_explanation: Two meanings: 1) The state of your hotdog, tapa, and tocino in the freezer. 2) The state of your brain during an exam when you suddenly forget everything. Also, that one Disney movie your pamangkin has been singing 'Let It Go' from for the past decade.
usage_notes: Can refer to food, a state of being immobile, or the popular Disney movie.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nabili ko ang manok na **frozen** pa.","translation":"I bought the chicken while it was still **frozen**."},{"sentence":"Na-**frozen** ako sa takot nang makita ko ang multo.","translation":"I was **frozen** in fear when I saw the ghost."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maingat at masusing pagmamasid, pagsisiyasat, o pag-aaral sa isang bagay o pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is a deep cut. Imagine a detective in a noir film, meticulously checking every single clue at a crime scene. That's 'himat'. It's not just looking; it's *scrutinizing*. It's the kind of intense focus your boss gives your report right before your performance review. It's the OG "seen-zoning" with extreme prejudice.
usage_notes: A very formal and literary term. Not used in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinakailangan ng masusing **himat** ang mga ebidensya sa kaso.","translation":"The evidence in the case requires careful **scrutiny**."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **himat**, natuklasan niya ang mali sa kontrata.","translation":"Because of his **investigation**, he discovered the error in the contract."}]

translation: being talked about; the topic of conversation
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagiging paksa ng isang usapan o talakayan ng dalawa o higit pang tao.
etymology: From `pinag-` + `usap` (reduplicated first syllable `u-`) + `-an`. The progressive aspect of the verb.
original_explanation: The tea. The chismis. The main topic in the group chat. When you're the 'pinag-uusapan,' you're either famous, infamous, or someone just posted your old Friendster photo. It's being the 'talk of the town,' for better or for worse.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of gossip, news, or important discussions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang laging **pinag-uusapan** sa opisina dahil sa bago niyang kotse.","translation":"He is always **being talked about** at the office because of his new car."},{"sentence":"Ano ang **pinag-uusapan** ninyo at mukhang seryoso kayo?","translation":"What are you **talking about** that you look so serious?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangatnig na nag-uugnay ng mga salita o sugnay; nagpapahiwatig ng karagdagan o pagkasunod-sunod. Nangangahulugang 'at saka', 'pati'.
original_explanation: 'Saka' is the "wait, there's more!" of Tagalog conversations. It's how you add another item to your chismis, another task to your to-do list, or another order at Jollibee. "Kumain kami, tapos nanood ng sine, saka nag-kape." It's the verbal version of hitting the '+' button.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'at saka' or 'tsaka'. It connects sequential actions or adds items to a list.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-aral ka muna, **saka** ka na maglaro.","translation":"Study first, **and then** you can play."},{"sentence":"Bumili siya ng tinapay, palaman, **saka** gatas.","translation":"She bought bread, spread, **and also** milk."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng paggawa o pagkilos na walang sapat na pag-iisip, paghahanda, o pag-iingat; padalos-dalos.
etymology: From Spanish 'basta' meaning 'enough' or 'stop', reduplicated to mean 'just any which way' or 'without consideration'.
original_explanation: That thing your mom warns you not to do when making life decisions, like falling in love with a 'red flag' or spending your entire sahod on 11.11. 'Huwag kang basta-basta magtitiwala!' is the national anthem of protective parents.
usage_notes: The reduplication of 'basta' intensifies the meaning to imply a severe lack of care, thought, or preparation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **basta-basta** pumapasok sa isang relasyon.","translation":"Don't just **carelessly** enter into a relationship."},{"sentence":"Ang proyekto ay gumuho dahil ginawa ito nang **basta-basta**.","translation":"The project collapsed because it was done **haphazardly**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagiging mas maliit sa sukat, bilang, o halaga.
original_explanation: What happens to your favorite shirt after a wrong washing machine setting. It's also what happens to your sahod after taxes, SSS, and Pag-IBIG contributions. That feeling when your 1-liter ice cream tub now looks like 800ml for the same price? That's shrinkflation, a form of pagliit.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical size, quantity, or value.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napansin niya ang unti-unting **pagliit** ng kanyang ipon sa bangko.","translation":"She noticed the gradual **reduction** of her savings in the bank."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagliit** ng suplay ng sibuyas ang dahilan ng pagtaas ng presyo nito.","translation":"The **decrease** in the supply of onions is the reason for its price increase."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hindi sinasadyang pagbagsak o pagkawala ng balanse dahil sa pagkasabit o pagkatama ng paa sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: That moment when you're walking confidently, tapos biglang may 'ghost' na humila sa paa mo. You know, when the pavement suddenly decides it hates you. It's the universe's way of saying, "Hoy, 'wag masyadong mayabang sa paglakad."
usage_notes: Often used to describe a physical action but can be used metaphorically for failing or making a mistake. The prefix 'ma-' indicates an involuntary or accidental action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingat sa paglalakad para hindi ka **madapa** sa mga bato.","translation":"Be careful walking so you don't **trip** on the rocks."},{"sentence":"Halos **madapa** ako sa pagmamadali papuntang MRT.","translation":"I almost **stumbled** while rushing to the MRT."}]

meaning_filipino: Maliliit at malalambot na hibla o himulmol na karaniwang natitipon sa damit, tela, o sa mga sulok ng bahay.
original_explanation: The tiny, annoying fluff balls that magically appear on your black shirt right after you leave the house. It's the stuff you find in your pocket along with an old receipt and a single peso coin. It’s the universe's way of reminding you that nothing is ever perfectly clean.
usage_notes: Distinct from 'pelus' (velvet). 'Pelusa' is the unwanted fluff, while 'pelus' is the luxurious fabric.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **pelusa** ang filter ng washing machine.","translation":"The filter of the washing machine is full of **lint**."},{"sentence":"Alisin mo muna ang mga **pelusa** sa itim mong pantalon.","translation":"First, remove the **fuzz** from your black pants."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaki at matibay na piraso ng materyal na hindi tinatablan ng tubig, karaniwang ginagamit bilang pantakip.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "trapa" (basahan) at posibleng hinalo sa Ingles na "tarpaulin".
original_explanation: The unsung hero of the Philippines. It's the roof of a sari-sari store, the wall of a temporary shelter, the floor for a picnic, and the face of a politician during election season. This waterproof sheet is more versatile than a Swiss Army knife. Also known as "tarpaulin."
usage_notes: Universally understood and used for the blue, orange, or white plastic-like sheets. Also commonly refers to printed tarpaulins for events and advertisements.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit nila ang **trapal** bilang pansamantalang bubong pagkatapos ng bagyo.","translation":"They used a **tarpaulin** as a temporary roof after the typhoon."},{"sentence":"May malaking **trapal** sa gate na may mukha ng kandidato.","translation":"There's a big **tarp** on the gate with the candidate's face."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na mahilig sa musikang rock, o isang musikero na tumutugtog ng rock music.
etymology: A blend of the English word 'rock' and the Spanish suffix '-ista', which denotes a person associated with a particular field or ideology.
original_explanation: The person in your barkada who wears a black band shirt, probably has long hair (or used to), and knows all the lyrics to every Eraserheads and Bamboo song. They live for guitar solos and mosh pits. Their life's motto is probably 'Rakenrol!'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang maging isang sikat na **rakista**.","translation":"He dreams of becoming a famous **rocker**."},{"sentence":"Puno ng mga **rakista** ang concert ng paborito nilang banda.","translation":"The concert of their favorite band was full of **rock music enthusiasts**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ugnayan o koneksyon sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang tao, bagay, o konsepto.
original_explanation: The subject of 99% of all hugot posts. It's the "It's Complicated" status on Facebook, the "sana all" comment on a sweet couple's photo, and the reason why you're either listening to Moira dela Torre or upbeat pop songs. A **relasyon** can be with your jowa, your family, your friends, or even your toxic job. It's the source of both our greatest joys and our most "malamig ang Pasko" moments.
usage_notes: Ginagamit para sa romantiko at di-romantikong ugnayan. Ang 'relationship reveal' ay isang modernong kaganapan sa social media na may kinalaman dito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang tiwala sa isang matatag na **relasyon**.","translation":"Trust is important in a strong **relationship**."},{"sentence":"Hindi naging maganda ang **relasyon** niya sa kanyang dating boss.","translation":"He did not have a good **relationship** with his former boss."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paraan ng pagluluto sa pamamagitan ng paglubog o pagluluto ng pagkain sa mainit na mantika o langis.
original_explanation: The solution to 99% of Filipino food problems. Got leftover adobo? Iprito mo. Got a fish? Iprito mo. Got hotdog, longganisa, or tocino? Iprito mo. It's the national cooking method, powered by a kawali and a gallon of cooking oil.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**iprito** mo na ang isda para sa ating pananghalian.","translation":"Please **fry** the fish for our lunch."},{"sentence":"Mas masarap ang manok kapag **priniprito** hanggang maging golden brown.","translation":"Chicken is more delicious when **fried** until golden brown."}]

translation: to probe; to sound out; to survey
meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng isang instrumento o pamamaraan upang alamin ang lalim, katangian, o opinyon ng isang bagay. Pagsusuri o pagtatanong upang makakuha ng impormasyon.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you're trying to figure out if your crush likes you back, but you're too torpe to ask directly. You 'probe' for info from their friends. 'Magsonda ka muna kung single pa siya.' In a more literal sense, it's what surveyors do to land or what doctors do with a probe.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for physical probing or figuratively for gauging opinions or feelings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magsonda** sa mga residente para malaman ang kanilang saloobin sa bagong proyekto.","translation":"We need to **survey** the residents to know their opinion on the new project."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **magsonda** kung ano ang nararamdaman ng kaibigan niya tungkol sa isyu.","translation":"He tried to **sound out** how his friend felt about the issue."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malakas na tunog o huni na nililikha ng tandang, karaniwan sa madaling araw.
etymology: Onomatopoeic, mimicking the sound of a rooster.
original_explanation: The original Filipino alarm clock. Before your iPhone, there was the 'tilaok' of the neighbor's rooster, letting the whole barangay know it's 4 AM and time to make pandesal, go to the palengke, or just curse the noisy bird.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to the sound a rooster makes. The verb form is 'tumilaok' (to crow).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagising ako sa sunod-sunod na **tilaok** ng mga tandang.","translation":"I was awakened by the successive **crows** of the roosters."}]

translation: to cross; to traverse a path
meaning_filipino: Ang pagdaan o pagtawid sa isang landas, karaniwan ay isang maikli o di-pangkaraniwang daan.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'life hack' for commuting. When you know a shortcut through an eskinita to avoid the main road traffic, you 'bumabagtas'. It’s about taking a direct path, cutting across a field, or finding a quicker route. Think of it as crossing a level in a video game.
usage_notes: A bit archaic or literary. 'Tumawid' is more common for crossing a street. 'Bagtasin' is the more common verb form used in sentences.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **bagtasin** ang gubat upang makarating sa talon.","translation":"We need **to cross** the forest to get to the waterfall."}]

translation: to utter, to say, to express in words
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbigkas o pagsambit ng mga salita; ang pagpapahayag ng isang kaisipan o damdamin sa pamamagitan ng pagsasalita.
original_explanation: This is the more formal, almost dramatic way of saying "to say something." 'Yung moment na aamin ka na kay crush, you gather all your courage para salitain ang "mahal kita." It's not just talking; it's *uttering* something significant.
usage_notes: Often used in formal or literary contexts. It is the object-focus form, where the thing being said is the object.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **salitain** ang mga bagay na matagal mo nang kinikimkim.","translation":"It's hard **to utter** the things you've kept inside for so long."},{"sentence":"Ano ba ang gusto mong **salitain**?","translation":"What is it that you want **to say**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghuli sa isang tao, lalo na ang isinasagawa ng may awtoridad, dahil sa paglabag sa batas.
etymology: From 'dakip' (act of seizing/arresting) with the -um- infix.
original_explanation: This is what happens when your 'raket' is not exactly legal. It's the moment the pulis show up and say 'Freeze!'. It's the act of getting caught, cuffed, and taken away. The official term for 'nahuli ng pulis.'
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of law enforcement arresting a suspect.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga pulis ay **dumakip** sa mga suspek sa pagnanakaw.","translation":"The police **arrested** the suspects in the robbery."},{"sentence":"May utos ang korte na **dumakip** sa tumakas na bilanggo.","translation":"The court has an order to **apprehend** the escaped prisoner."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pekeng social media account na nilikha para sa layuning manloko, manggulo, o magpakalat ng propaganda, kadalasan ay sa paraang hindi nagpapakilala.
original_explanation: Yung profile na ang picture ay itlog, anime character, o random na artista, tapos 0 friends pero ang tapang mag-comment. Ginagamit para maghasik ng lagim online nang hindi nahuhuli kung sino talaga sila. The modern-day maskara.
usage_notes: A specific type of account used by trolls. Very common term in discussions about social media and politics.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"I-report na natin 'yang **troll account** na 'yan para ma-ban.","translation":"Let's report that **troll account** so it gets banned."},{"sentence":"Gumagamit sila ng libo-libong **troll account** para magmukhang marami sila.","translation":"They use thousands of **troll accounts** to make it seem like there are many of them."}]

translation: to arrest, to capture, to seize
meaning_filipino: Hulihin o arestuhin ang isang tao o hayop, karaniwan nang may paggamit ng puwersa.
original_explanation: The action movie scene where the police finally catch the bad guy. "Freeze! Pulis 'to!" 'Yan ang cue para **dakipin** ang kontrabida. In a less dramatic sense, ito 'yung ginagawa sa'yo ng nanay mo kapag ayaw mong maligo—bigla ka na lang dadakipin papuntang banyo. The command form is "Dakpin!"
usage_notes: This is the object-focus command/infinitive form of the root word 'dakip' (to catch/seize).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan ng hepe ang kanyang mga pulis na **dakipin** ang suspek.","translation":"The chief ordered his police officers to **arrest** the suspect."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan nilang **dakipin** ang pusang kalye ngunit ito'y mabilis na nakatakas.","translation":"They tried to **capture** the stray cat but it quickly escaped."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lugar sa isang hotel, opisina, o gusali kung saan tinatanggap at binibigyan ng impormasyon ang mga bisita, kliyente, o pasyente.
original_explanation: Ito yung front desk. Ang unang checkpoint mo pagpasok sa isang building, hotel, o BPO company. Dito ka mag-log in, kukuha ng visitor's pass, at magtatanong sa ate o kuya kung, "Andyan po ba si Ma'am/Sir...?". Sila ang gatekeepers ng corporate world.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa front desk area. Ang 'resepsiyonista' (receptionist) ay ang taong nagtatrabaho dito. Ang baybay na 'resepsyon' (walang 'i') ay karaniwan ding ginagamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-iwan ka ng mensahe sa **resepsiyon** para sa akin.","translation":"Leave a message at the **reception** desk for me."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong magparehistro sa **resepsiyon** pagdating mo.","translation":"You need to register at the **reception** when you arrive."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng kawalan ng katapatan, katotohanan, o paninindigan sa isang tao, kasunduan, o prinsipyo.
etymology: Mula sa "di-" (hindi) at "pagkamatapat" (state of being faithful/honest).
original_explanation: Ito 'yung "may ka-chat siyang iba" moment. O 'yung kaibigan mong sinabihan mong "secret lang natin 'to," pero after 5 minutes, alam na ng buong barangay. It's the ultimate betrayal, whether in love, friendship, or politics.
usage_notes: Isang matinding salita na nagpapahiwatig ng paglabag sa tiwala.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **di-pagkamatapat** ang sumira sa kanilang mahabang pagsasama.","translation":"**Unfaithfulness** destroyed their long relationship."},{"sentence":"Ipinakita ng politiko ang kaniyang **di-pagkamatapat** sa bayan nang siya ay nagnakaw sa kaban.","translation":"The politician showed his **disloyalty** to the country when he stole from its coffers."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtanggap o paghahayag sa isang bagay na totoo, lalo na kung ito ay isang pagkakamali o kasalanan.
original_explanation: The "It's me, hi, I'm the problem, it's me" verb. It's what you do when you finally confess you ate the last piece of leche flan. In hugot culture, it's that moment you finally tell yourself, "Oo na, aaminin ko na, may feelings pa rin ako sa kanya." It's the first step to moving on... or to getting into more trouble.
usage_notes: The root 'amin' in this context means 'to own up to'. It is different from the pronoun 'amin'. The actor-focus form is 'umamin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Aminin** mo na ang iyong pagkakamali.","translation":"**Admit** your mistake."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **aminin** sa sarili na nagkamali ka.","translation":"It's hard to **admit** to yourself that you were wrong."}]

translation: leading someone on (romantically); a flirt who feigns interest
meaning_filipino: (Kolokyal) Tumutukoy sa isang tao na nagpapakita ng mga kilos o sinyales ng romantikong interes nang walang tunay na intensyon, na nagiging sanhi upang mahulog ang loob ng iba sa kanila.
