etymology: Taglish compound from the Tagalog causative prefix 'pa-' + English 'fall' (as in 'fall in love').
original_explanation: That person who gives you mixed signals. They're sweet, they text you 'good morning', they remember your coffee order, but have 'no label' commitment issues. They make you fall for them, then hit you with a 'friends lang tayo.' It's an emotional trap, bes!
usage_notes: A very common term in modern Filipino dating culture. Can be used as an adjective to describe the person ('Ang pa-fall mo!') or a verb ('Huwag mo akong pa-fall-in').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Akala ko gusto niya ako, **pa-fall** lang pala siya.","translation":"I thought he liked me, but he was just **leading me on**."},{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na 'yang pagiging **pa-fall**, marami nang umasa sa'yo.","translation":"Stop being such **a flirt who leads people on**; too many have already gotten their hopes up because of you."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpunta sa isang lugar upang samahan o kunin ang isang tao.
original_explanation: This is what you ask your jowa or your parents to do when you're too tired to commute home after work. 'Sunduin mo naman ako.' So, 'manundo' is the general verb for doing that fetching. It’s the official verb of the 'hatid-sundo' culture, a classic Filipino love language.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to fetching people, not objects. For objects, 'kunin' is used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang laging **nanunundo** sa kanyang mga anak mula sa eskwelahan.","translation":"He is the one who always **fetches** his children from school."},{"sentence":"Pwede ka bang **manundo** mamaya sa airport?","translation":"Can you **pick me up** at the airport later?"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay, gawain, o kalagayan na mababa ang uri, walang dangal, at kahiya-hiya.
etymology: From dawal, meaning low or base. The prefix ma- makes it an adjective.
original_explanation: This is a deep cut. Marawal is that state of being na super low-quality, walang class, at nakakahiya. Think of a politician caught in a corruption scandal—that's a marawal na sitwasyon. It's not just poor, it's disgracefully so.
usage_notes: A formal and somewhat literary word. Not used in everyday casual conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinakwil niya ang **marawal** na pamumuhay upang magbagong-buhay.","translation":"He renounced the **ignoble** way of life to start anew."},{"sentence":"Isang **marawal** na krimen ang ginawa niya sa kanyang kapwa.","translation":"He committed a **base** crime against his fellow person."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang gawain o pangyayari na karaniwan, nakasanayan na, at bahagi ng isang rutina.
original_explanation: This describes an action that's so normal, it's almost boring. 'Yung pag-check ng attendance sa klase? Rutinaryo. 'Yung pag-reboot ng PC 'pag nag-hang? Rutinaryo. It's the "just another Tuesday" kind of activity. No surprises here.
usage_notes: The adjective form of "rutina".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **rutinaryo** na pagsusuri ang isinagawa ng mga doktor.","translation":"The doctors conducted a **routine** check-up."},{"sentence":"Para sa kanya, ang pagbiyahe sa EDSA ay isang **rutinaryo** na pagsubok.","translation":"For him, traveling on EDSA is a **routine** ordeal."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi karaniwan; naiiba sa nakasanayan o sa pangkalahatan.
etymology: From kaka- (a prefix indicating a special quality or degree) + iba (other, different).
original_explanation: This is your go-to word for anything that makes you go 'Huh?' or 'Wow!'. It's for that friend with a weird laugh, a new food combo like champorado with tuyo, or a plot twist in a teleserye you didn't see coming. It can be good-weird or bad-weird, but it's never boring.
usage_notes: Can have a neutral, positive (unique), or slightly negative (weird) connotation depending on the context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **kakaiba** siyang pakiramdam tungkol sa lugar na iyon.","translation":"She had a **strange** feeling about that place."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang istilo sa pagpipinta ay tunay na **kakaiba**.","translation":"His painting style is truly **unique**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng mga pagkakasala o maliliit na krimen, lalo na ng mga kabataan; pagpapabaya sa tungkulin.
original_explanation: The official term for your "pasaway" phase in high school. Skipping class, not doing homework, or just being a general pain to your parents and teachers. Think "juvenile delinquency".
usage_notes: A formal term often used in legal or sociological contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng gobyerno ang pagtaas ng kaso ng juvenile **dilingkuwensiya**.","translation":"The government is studying the rise in cases of juvenile **delinquency**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginagamit upang ipahiwatig na ang isang pahayag ay batay sa sabi-sabi o hindi pa kumpirmado; sinasabing.
etymology: Mula sa 'di' (isang marker) at 'umano' (isang pormal na salita para sa 'ayon sa sabi' o 'it is said').
original_explanation: The favorite phrase of news reporters and neighborhood chismosas. It's the ultimate disclaimer. It's like saying, 'Hey, this is what I heard, pero 'wag ako ang sisihin n'yo kung 'di totoo.' It's the verbal equivalent of an 'allegedly' tweet.
usage_notes: Karaniwan sa pormal na pag-uulat ng balita at sa mga legal na konteksto upang ipahiwatig ang impormasyong hindi pa beripikado.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang suspek **di umano** ay tumakas patungong probinsya.","translation":"The suspect **allegedly** fled to the province."},{"sentence":"Siya **di umano** ang nanalo sa lotto noong nakaraang linggo.","translation":"He **reportedly** won the lottery last week."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malakas na suntok o hampas; sa matalinghagang kahulugan, isang malaking kabiguan, problema, o pagsubok sa buhay.
original_explanation: Pwedeng literal na suntok, pero mas madalas, ito yung suntok ng buhay. Yung bagsak ka sa exam, iniwan ka ng jowa, at nawalan ka pa ng wallet—lahat sa isang araw. 'Yan ang **dagok**. It's life's ultimate uppercut. The 'plot twist' you never wanted.
usage_notes: Very common in its metaphorical sense for life's challenges.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malakas ang **dagok** na tumama sa kanyang panga.","translation":"The **blow** that hit his jaw was strong."},{"sentence":"Ang pagpanaw ng kanyang ama ay isang malaking **dagok** sa kanyang buhay.","translation":"The passing of his father was a major **setback** in his life."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang institusyon na nagbibigay ng kanlungan at pangangalaga sa mga ulila, matatanda, o mga taong may sakit na walang lunas.
original_explanation: Think of it as the old-school Spanish word for a place that takes care of people who can't be cared for at home—like an orphanage or a home for the aged. It sounds very "Maria Clara" era. You'd probably read this in a Noli Me Tángere chapter, not hear it at the mall. The more common Filipino spelling now is 'hospisyo'.
usage_notes: This is the Spanish spelling and is considered archaic or literary. The Filipinized spelling "hospisyo" is more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang matandang gusali sa dulo ng kalye ay dating isang **hospicio**.","translation":"The old building at the end of the street was once an **orphanage**."},{"sentence":"Nakatala sa mga aklat ng kasaysayan ang tungkol sa **Hospicio de San Jose**.","translation":"The history books record information about the **Hospicio de San Jose**."}]

translation: to think of, to consider, to imagine
meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng isip upang bumuo ng ideya, magmuni-muni, o magbigay-pansin sa isang bagay o konsepto.
original_explanation: "Isipin mo na lang, 5-minute walk lang ang office mo from your condo." This is the verb for daydreaming, overthinking, planning, and reminiscing. It's the command you give your brain when you need to solve a problem, or when your friend tells you a juicy story and says, "Isipin mo, girl..."
usage_notes: Often used in the imperative mood (as a command) or as an infinitive (the base form of the verb).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Isipin** mong mabuti ang magiging epekto ng iyong desisyon.","translation":"**Think** carefully about the effect of your decision."},{"sentence":"Ayokong **isipin** ang mga problema habang nagbabakasyon.","translation":"I don't want **to think about** problems while on vacation."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng tuldik na may anyong pahilis (´) na inilalagay sa ibabaw ng patinig. Ito ay nagpapahiwatig na ang diin ng salita ay nasa huling pantig (salitang mabilis) o nasa ibang pantig maliban sa penultima.
original_explanation: This is the 'forward slash' accent (´). It tells you to put the stress on that syllable with a bit more... oomph. Think of 'baká' (maybe) or 'tubó' (sugarcane). It's the little mark that screams “Stress dito, bes!”
usage_notes: Tinatawag ding 'mabilis'. Ipinapahiwatig nito ang diin sa huling pantig ng isang salita.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang salitang 'likó' ay may **tuldik na pahilis**.","translation":"The word 'likó' (turn) has an **acute accent**."},{"sentence":"Iba ang kahulugan ng 'pito' sa 'pitó' dahil sa **tuldik na pahilis**.","translation":"The meaning of 'pito' (whistle) is different from 'pitó' (seven) because of the **acute accent**."}]

meaning_filipino: Matinding pandidiri, pagkamuhi, o pagkasukol sa isang bagay o tao.
original_explanation: 'Suklam' is what you feel when you see your ex happily in a new relationship. Kidding! It's a deep, gut-wrenching feeling of disgust or hatred. It's stronger than 'inis' (annoyance) and deeper than 'galit' (anger). It's the feeling you get when you see a cockroach in your food or hear about a major corruption scandal. It's a "yuck" for the soul.
usage_notes: Often used in the form "nasusuklam" (feeling disgust) or "kinasusuklaman" (the object of disgust).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **suklam** ang kanyang puso para sa mga taong nang-api sa kanya.","translation":"Her heart was full of **loathing** for the people who oppressed her."},{"sentence":"Nasusuklam ako sa mga kasinungalingan mo!","translation":"I am **disgusted** by your lies!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng saging na malaki, magaspang ang balat, at hindi gaanong matamis ang lasa, karaniwang ginagamit sa pagluluto.
original_explanation: The 'pangit' cousin in the banana family. While 'saba' is the star for banana cue and 'lakatan' is the go-to for a quick snack, tibalbal is that big, awkward-looking one that's not very sweet. It's the banana you cook, not the one you eat raw, unless you enjoy a bit of a challenge. It's got character, but it's definitely not winning any beauty contests.
usage_notes: This word is not widely known and may be regional. It can also be used as an adjective to mean bulky or coarse.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagluto si Lola ng minatamis na **tibalbal**.","translation":"Grandma cooked sweetened **tibalbal** bananas."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso o bahagi ng kawayan, karaniwang may isang buko sa ilalim, na ginagamit bilang lalagyan ng tubig, tuba, o iba pang likido.
original_explanation: The OG Filipino tumbler. Before Hydro Flasks and Stanleys, there was the `balumbong`—a sturdy section of bamboo used to carry water or 'tuba' (coconut wine). It's eco-friendly, rustic, and has that 'probinsya life' aesthetic.
usage_notes: Associated with rural or provincial life. The term 'bumbong' is more commonly used today. It can also refer to the sound made by striking bamboo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-igib siya ng tubig gamit ang isang lumang **balumbong**.","translation":"He fetched water using an old **bamboo container**."},{"sentence":"Puno ng tuba ang mga **balumbong** na dala ng mangangarit.","translation":"The **bamboo containers** carried by the scythe worker were full of coconut wine."}]

translation: To cause to branch out extensively
meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng maraming maliliit at magkakaugnay na sanga mula sa isang pangunahin o ilang pangunahing sanga.
original_explanation: This is the next level of 'pagsangahin'. This isn't one chismis becoming five; this is one chismis spawning a whole cinematic universe of drama with subplots and character arcs. It's making something incredibly complex and multi-layered, like a project manager breaking down a huge task into a million tiny sub-tasks.
usage_notes: The repetition of 'sanga' emphasizes the multiplicity and complexity of the branching. It's an intensified version of 'pagsangahin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **pagsanga-sangahin** ang sistema ng irigasyon upang maabot ang lahat ng taniman.","translation":"The irrigation system needs **to be branched out extensively** to reach all the farmlands."},{"sentence":"Pilit niyang **pinagsanga-sanga** ang simpleng problema kaya lalong gumulo.","translation":"He deliberately **made** the simple problem **branch out into many smaller ones**, which is why it became more chaotic."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang patag na lalagyan, karaniwang gawa sa papel, na may tiklop na nagsisilbing takip, ginagamit sa paglalagay ng sulat o dokumento.
original_explanation: The OG paper container for your love letters, resignation letters, or yung 13th-month pay mo na cash. Bago pa nagkaroon ng email at Gcash, ang sobre ang aabangan mo, lalo na kung may lamang pera galing sa ninong at ninang tuwing Pasko. It's the physical form of "You've got mail!"
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit para sa mga sulat, pero sa Pilipinas, madalas itong gamitin bilang lalagyan ng pera (ampaw o regalo).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ilagay mo ang liham sa loob ng **sobre** bago ipadala sa post office.","translation":"Put the letter inside the **envelope** before sending it to the post office."},{"sentence":"Binigyan ako ni Tita ng pulang **sobre** na may lamang pera para sa aking kaarawan.","translation":"My aunt gave me a red **envelope** with money inside for my birthday."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan na may mga hibla o bristles na ginagamit sa paglilinis, pag-aayos, o paglalagay ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: The generic term for that thing with bristles. It could be for your teeth, your shoes, your floor, or even your back. It's the ultimate cleaning sidekick. Kapag sinabi ng nanay mo, 'Kunin mo ang sepilyo,' you better ask, 'Para saan po?' bago ka magkamali.
usage_notes: This is a general term. It's often clarified with another noun to specify its use (e.g., sepilyo sa ngipin, sepilyo sa buhok).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang **sepilyo** para alisin ang alikabok sa kanyang damit.","translation":"He used the **brush** to remove the dust from his clothes."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating bumili ng bagong **sepilyo** para sa sahig.","translation":"We need to buy a new **brush** for the floor."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lisensyadong propesyonal na nagbebenta at namamahala ng mga polisa ng seguro para sa isang kompanya.
original_explanation: That one friend from high school who suddenly became a 'Financial Advisor' on Facebook. They'll slide into your DMs with 'Hi, friend! Let's have coffee?' and you know it's not just to catch up. They sell peace of mind for the future, one VUL policy at a time.
usage_notes: A specific type of 'ahente'. Often used interchangeably with 'financial advisor'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aking **ahente sa seguro** ay napakamatulungin sa pagpapaliwanag ng mga benepisyo.","translation":"My **insurance agent** was very helpful in explaining the benefits."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong tawagan ang **ahente sa seguro** ko para i-update ang aking polisa.","translation":"I need to call my **insurance agent** to update my policy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang yunit ng bigat o masa sa sistemang metriko, katumbas ng isanlibong gramo.
original_explanation: The English-y way to say it. You use this when you're trying to sound a bit more formal or when you've just come from your science class. 'Isang kilogram ng manok, please.' sounds slightly different from 'Isang kilo...'. It's the same thing, just with a different vibe.
usage_notes: A direct loanword from English. Often shortened to 'kilo' in everyday conversation. 'Kilogramo' is the Spanish-derived equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang isang sako ng bigas ay may bigat na limampung **kilogram**.","translation":"A sack of rice weighs fifty **kilograms**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng dalawang **kilogram** na asukal para sa cake.","translation":"I need two **kilograms** of sugar for the cake."}]

meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng palawit o palamuting nakabitin ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: Ito yung command form. 'Uy, ang plain ng bag mo, palawitan mo kaya ng keychain?' It's the act of accessorizing something by making something dangle from it. Like when you tell your friend to add a tassel to their graduation cap para maging extra.
usage_notes: Isang pandiwang pautos o kilos na nag-uutos sa isang tao na magdagdag ng nakabiting palamuti.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Palawitan** mo ng mga perlas ang kurtina para magmukhang mamahalin.","translation":"**Add** pearl **tassels** to the curtain to make it look expensive."},{"sentence":"Pinapalawitan niya ang kanyang mga hikaw ng maliliit na diyamante.","translation":"She is having her earrings **adorned with** small dangling diamonds."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal at mapaglarong termino para sa isang "fan" o tagahanga.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Ingles na "fan" na nilagyan ng "-ey" suffix, isang karaniwang paraan ng pagbuo ng slang sa Pilipinas.
original_explanation: Ito yung mas cute at mas Pinoy pakinggan na version ng "fan". Kapag sinabi mong "**faney**" ka, parang sinasabi mo na enjoy ka lang sa pagiging tagahanga, less ng pressure, more ng fun. "Wag masyadong seryoso, **faney** lang!"
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa mga 'di-pormal na usapan at sa social media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halatang malaking **faney** siya ng KathNiel dahil kumpleto siya sa merchandise.","translation":"It's obvious she's a big **faney** of KathNiel because she has the complete merchandise."},{"sentence":"\"Gala tayo, mga **faney**! May cupsleeve event si bias!\"","translation":"\"Let's go out, fellow **fans**! Our bias has a cupsleeve event!\""}]

translation: is being permitted; is being allowed
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng pahintulot o permiso para gawin ang isang bagay; pagpayag.
etymology: From `pina-` + `hi` (reduplication of first syllable of root) + `hintulot` + `-an`. A complex verb form indicating a permitted action in progress.
original_explanation: This is the official 'G' from your parents or your boss. It's the green light, the go-signal, the 'ok, fine, you can go to the concert.' It’s that formal permission you need before you can proceed, unlike when you just 'ninja' your way through things. The opposite of 'bawal.'
usage_notes: A formal term often found in rules, regulations, and formal requests.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi **pinahihintulutan** ang pagpasok ng mga hindi miyembro.","translation":"The entry of non-members **is not permitted**."},{"sentence":"Tanging ang mga bakunado lamang ang **pinahihintulutan** na manood ng sine.","translation":"Only vaccinated individuals **are allowed** to watch the movie."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang manipis na balat sa loob ng tainga na tumatanggap at nagpapadala ng mga sound wave. Kilala rin bilang tímpano.
etymology: Hiram sa salitang Espanyol na 'oído', na nangangahulugang 'pandinig' o 'panloob na tainga'.
original_explanation: This is a very old-school, almost 'lola's baul' kind of word. Your doctor would probably say 'eardrum,' but your super makata (poetic) lolo might say, 'Nabasag ang uwido ko sa lakas ng sigaw mo!' (My eardrum shattered from your loud shout!). It’s the Tagalog word that sounds like it came from a Spanish biology textbook.
usage_notes: Bihirang-bihira gamitin sa modernong pag-uusap. Mas karaniwan ang paggamit ng 'eardrum'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingatan mo ang iyong **uwido** laban sa malalakas na tunog.","translation":"Protect your **eardrum** against loud sounds."},{"sentence":"Parang may pumitik sa **uwido** ko nang sumisid ako nang malalim.","translation":"It felt like something flicked my **eardrum** when I dove deep."}]

meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng pambalot ang isang bagay, gaya ng papel, plastik, o tela, upang takpan o protektahan ito.
original_explanation: The official verb of Christmas, birthdays, and packing your pabaon. It's what you ask the tita at the department store gift-wrapping section to do. Also what you do with leftover food from a fiesta. "Paki-balot naman po 'yung tirang lechon, ulam namin bukas."
usage_notes: Can be used for wrapping gifts, food ('take out'), or even covering something up figuratively.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magaling siyang mag-**ibalot** ng regalo.","translation":"She is good at **wrapping** gifts."},{"sentence":"**Ibalot** mo nang maigi ang pagkain para hindi langgamin.","translation":"**Wrap** the food well so the ants don't get to it."}]

translation: to attack; to assault; to charge at
meaning_filipino: Biglaang sugurin o salakayin nang may matinding puwersa o galit.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung mga bill collector sa 15th of the month. Bigla na lang susugod sa pinto mo. O kaya 'yung feeling mo kapag nakita mo 'yung ex mo na may kasamang iba, gusto mo siyang daluhungin... ng tanong na "Bakit?!".
usage_notes: Often implies a sudden, forceful, and aggressive action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binalaan ng kapitan ang mga pirata na **daluhungin** sila kung hindi sila aalis.","translation":"The captain warned the pirates that they would be **attacked** if they did not leave."},{"sentence":"Muntik na akong **daluhungin** ng asong kalye.","translation":"I was almost **charged at** by a street dog."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sining ng paggalaw ng katawan na karaniwang isinasagawa sa saliw ng musika, na nagpapahayag ng damdamin, ideya, o nagsasalaysay ng isang kuwento.
original_explanation: The OG stress-reliever bago pa nauso ang Netflix. It's what your tita does at parties after two glasses of wine, or what you do in your room when your favorite K-pop song comes on. From the graceful tinikling to the chaotic budots, it's our body's way of talking.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb root for "sumayaw" (to dance).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng kanyang **sayaw** sa entablado.","translation":"Her **dance** on the stage was beautiful."},{"sentence":"Niyaya niya akong isayaw, ngunit puno ng kaba ang aking **sayaw**.","translation":"He asked me to dance, but my **dance** was full of nervousness."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang Ingles na nangangahulugang "kasama" o "gamit ang," na karaniwang ginagamit sa mga pangungusap na Taglish.
original_explanation: The OG. The one and only. Before 'wit' and 'kasama' had to share the spotlight in your DMs. This is the English word we sprinkle into our Tagalog sentences to sound... well, to sound like we speak Taglish. 'Let's go to the party with them.' It's the glue that holds our code-switching together.
usage_notes: Extremely common in code-switching (Taglish). Standard English usage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kakain kami sa labas **with** my family later.","translation":"We will eat out **with** my family later."},{"sentence":"Can you please check **with** your manager?","translation":"Can you please check **with** your manager?"}]

translation: the act of shaking off dust or dirt; a stopover after a wake
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-alis ng alikabok, dumi, o anumang nakakapit sa isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng mabilis na pag-alog o pagyugyog. Sa modernong gamit, tumutukoy rin ito sa pamahiin ng pagdaan sa ibang lugar pagkatapos dumalaw sa burol.
etymology: From pag- (gerund prefix) + pa- (causative/intensifying prefix) + pagpag (to shake off).
original_explanation: Classic move after visiting a wake, where you go to Jollibee or a coffee shop before going home to 'shake off' any ghosts. It’s a Filipino superstition that became a modern-day excuse for a food trip. 'Tara, pagpag muna tayo!' The original meaning is literally just shaking a rug or blanket.
usage_notes: Has a very popular slang meaning: stopping somewhere after a wake or funeral to eat or hang out, based on the superstition that this 'shakes off' the spirit of the deceased so it doesn't follow you home. The primary meaning is literally shaking off dust.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng **pagpapagpag** ng mga lumang kumot na galing sa baul.","translation":"The old blankets from the chest need a good **shaking off** (of dust)."},{"sentence":"Daan muna tayo sa 7-Eleven para sa **pagpapagpag** bago umuwi galing sa burol.","translation":"Let's drop by 7-Eleven for a **'pagpag'** (ritual stopover) before going home from the wake."}]

translation: to force one's way through, to muscle through
meaning_filipino: Ang sapilitang pagdaan o pagsusuot sa isang masikip na lugar o sa gitna ng maraming tao.
original_explanation: The move you have to pull in Divisoria during the Christmas season. It's maneuvering through a crowd like you're playing a real-life video game, using your elbows and a lot of "excuse me po" (or not). It's the opposite of social distancing.
usage_notes: Usually used in its conjugated forms like 'pumuspas' (past tense), 'pumupuspas' (present tense), or as a root in commands.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pumuspas** siya sa gitna ng mga tao para makalapit sa entablado.","translation":"He **forced his way through** the crowd to get near the stage."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **magpuspas** sa MRT kapag rush hour.","translation":"It's hard **to muscle your way through** the MRT during rush hour."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa biglaan at mabilis na pagkilos o pagtalon, na parang may nagtulak o binitiwan mula sa pagkakapigil.
original_explanation: Parang yung puso mo nung bigla siyang nag-chat ng "hi". Biglang paigkas from zero to hero ang feelings. O kaya yung paggising mo na late ka na for work, paigkas ka sa kama.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a sudden, reflexive, or spring-loaded action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Paigkas** siyang bumangon nang marinig ang alarma.","translation":"He shot up **jerkily** from bed when he heard the alarm."},{"sentence":"Ang paggalaw ng manika ay **paigkas** na parang may de-susi.","translation":"The doll's movement is **jerky** as if it were key-wound."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahabang piraso ng kahoy o kawayan na ipinapatong sa balikat upang magbuhat ng dalawang mabigat na bagay na nakasabit sa magkabilang dulo.
original_explanation: The original Filipino dumbbell, a.k.a. the 'taho vendor stick'. It's the ultimate tool for work-life balance, literally. You put it on your shoulder to carry two heavy loads on each end. It’s a symbol of hard work and serious shoulder gains.
usage_notes: Commonly associated with street vendors (like taho or fish vendors) and rural farm life.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng **balagwit** upang madala ang dalawang timba ng tubig.","translation":"He used a **carrying pole** to carry the two buckets of water."},{"sentence":"Kinabit ng magtataho ang lalagyan sa kanyang **balagwit** bago umalis.","translation":"The taho vendor attached the containers to his **yoke** before leaving."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng mata upang makita o pagmasdan ang isang bagay, tao, o direksyon.
original_explanation: The OG "look." The most basic command your mom shouts before you cross the street: "Tumingin ka sa kaliwa't kanan!" It's the verb for everything from glancing at your crush to staring at your phone screen for hours. It’s the foundation of 'chismis'—you have to look first before you can talk.
usage_notes: A general-purpose verb for the act of looking. Can be made more specific with directional adverbs (sa kaliwa, sa itaas, etc.).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumingin** ka sa akin kapag kinakausap kita.","translation":"**Look** at me when I'm talking to you."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **tumingin** sa sagot ng katabi mo.","translation":"Don't **look** at your seatmate's answer."}]

translation: to attach; to install; to connect
meaning_filipino: Idikit, isabit, o iugnay ang isang bagay sa isa pa.
original_explanation: This is the official verb for when you ask your kuya to install the new WiFi router, or when you finally decide to hang that 'Live, Laugh, Love' poster on your wall. It's the opposite of 'tanggalin,' which is what happens when you get tired of that poster.
usage_notes: Commonly used for physical attachment, installation of appliances, or connecting devices.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**ikabit** mo naman ang bagong bumbilya sa kisame.","translation":"Please **attach** the new lightbulb to the ceiling."},{"sentence":"**Ikabit** mo ang extension cord para umabot ang saksakan.","translation":"**Connect** the extension cord so the plug can reach."}]

translation: pro-gun; inclined to use a gun
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao o pangkat na pabor sa pagmamay-ari o paggamit ng baril, o may tendensiyang gumamit nito.
original_explanation: Describes a person or policy that's all about the right to bear arms. Think of action movie heroes or someone who believes a gun is the answer to their problems. It's not a common term, but it directly means 'pro-gun.'
usage_notes: This is a descriptive word formed with the 'maka-' prefix, indicating an affinity or inclination towards guns. It is not frequently used in casual conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May mga grupong **makabaril** na nagsusulong ng mas maluwag na batas sa pag-aari ng armas.","translation":"There are **pro-gun** groups that advocate for more lenient laws on firearm ownership."},{"sentence":"Hindi siya ang tipong **makabaril**; mas naniniwala siya sa diplomasya.","translation":"He is not the **gun-inclined** type; he believes more in diplomacy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking bagay sa kalawakan na umiikot sa isang bituin, tulad ng Daigdig na umiikot sa Araw. Ito ay isang malalim o pampanitikang salita para sa planeta.
original_explanation: This is the poetic, 'makata' way of saying 'planeta'. You won't hear this in a science class, but you might read it in a classic poem or hear it in a Kundiman song. Using buntala instead of 'planeta' is like wearing a tuxedo to a casual dinner—it's technically correct but very, very extra.
usage_notes: Pampanitikan at hindi gaanong ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na usapan. Ang karaniwang salita ay 'planeta'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa malawak na kalawakan, maraming **buntala** ang hindi pa natutuklasan.","translation":"In the vastness of space, there are many **planets** yet to be discovered."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang linya na hindi tuwid at may paikot o baluktot na hugis; isang liko sa daan.
original_explanation: What motorcycle riders love on a mountain road and what you dread on your exam results (the "bell curve"). It can be a sharp turn on the highway ("Delikado 'yang **kurba** na 'yan!"), or a term used to describe a person's shapely figure. Versatile word, use with caution.
usage_notes: Can refer to a literal curve on a road, a shape in geometry, a statistical curve, or colloquially, the curves of a human body.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa pagmamaneho dahil matalim ang **kurba** sa kalsadang iyon.","translation":"Drive carefully because the **curve** on that road is sharp."},{"sentence":"Ipinapakita ng grap ang isang pataas na **kurba** sa ekonomiya.","translation":"The graph shows an upward **curve** in the economy."}]

meaning_filipino: Magdulot o maging sanhi ng kalungkutan o pighati.
original_explanation: 'Yung eksena sa K-drama na namatay 'yung aso. Or 'yung pag-check mo ng bank account mo after 12.12 sale. "Talagang makalulungkot isipin na mag-isa ka na lang sa Pasko." It's a verb for things that hit you right in the feels.
usage_notes: A causative verb. It describes something that *causes* sadness, rather than the state of *being* sad (malungkot).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Makalulungkot** ang balitang natanggap namin kanina.","translation":"The news we received earlier **is saddening** (causes sadness)."},{"sentence":"**Nakalungkot** sa akin ang kanyang pag-alis.","translation":"His departure **saddened** me."}]

translation: ant-infested; to be swarmed by ants
meaning_filipino: Inilalarawan ang isang bagay, lalo na pagkain, na pinupuntahan o dinudumog ng mga langgam.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you leave your half-eaten Jollibee spaghetti on the table overnight. Pag-gising mo, may sarili nang fiesta at parada ang mga langgam. It's the universe's way of telling you to clean up your mess. 'Bes, nilanggam 'yung cake na tinago mo!' is a tragedy in five words.
usage_notes: Can function as an adjective ('langgamin ang mesa' - the table is ant-infested) or a verb ('nilanggam ang tinapay' - the ants swarmed the bread).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itapon mo na 'yan, **nilanggam** na.","translation":"Throw that away, it's already **swarmed by ants**."},{"sentence":"Matamis kasi kaya madaling **langgamin**.","translation":"It's sweet, that's why it easily gets **ant-infested**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat, uri, o dibisyon ng mga tao o bagay na may magkakatulad na katangian.
original_explanation: Parang folders sa computer mo para hindi magulo ang files. Or yung mga label sa Shopee: 'Men's Wear', 'Gadgets', 'Home & Living'. It's how we sort things out para mas madaling intindihin, from a person's 'type' to the different genres of K-Drama.
usage_notes: The spelling "kategoriya" is also used but "kategorya" is more standard and preferred.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa anong **kategorya** nabibilang ang pelikulang ito?","translation":"In what **category** does this film belong?"},{"sentence":"Hinati niya ang mga gastos sa iba't ibang **kategorya**.","translation":"She divided the expenses into different **categories**."}]

meaning_filipino: Dalhin o ilagay sa harapan ng isang tao, bagay, o lugar, o direkta itong atubilihin.
original_explanation: It's what you do when your team lead tells you to 'present your deck to the client.' It's also what your mom tells you to do with your suitor: 'Iharap mo sa akin 'yan!' (Bring him before me!). It's about bringing something or someone to the forefront, whether it's a PowerPoint, a problem, or a potential partner.
usage_notes: Can be used literally (to place in front) or figuratively (to confront a problem).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Iharap** mo sa akin ang lahat ng ebidensya.","translation":"**Present** all the evidence to me."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **iharap** ang mga problema nang may tapang.","translation":"We need to **face** the problems with courage."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang panahon ng pamamahinga mula sa trabaho, pag-aaral, o karaniwang gawain, karaniwang ginugugol sa pagliliwaliw o paglalakbay.
original_explanation: The most magical word in the BPO industry. It's that glorious period when you don't have to deal with irate customers, endless emails, or your micro-managing boss. It's the time for beach trips, family gatherings, or just sleeping for 24 hours straight. The holy grail of every Filipino employee.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Saan ang punta ninyo sa darating na **bakasyon**?","translation":"Where are you going for the upcoming **vacation**?"},{"sentence":"Pagod na ako, kailangan ko na ng **bakasyon**.","translation":"I'm tired, I need a **vacation**."}]

translation: to use a spoon; to scoop with a spoon
meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng kutsara upang kumuha o kumain ng pagkain.
original_explanation: Ito yung ginagawa mo sa sabaw, sa kanin (kung di ka magkakamay), at sa ice cream. The verb form of existing with a spoon. "Mag-diet na sana ako, pero may ice cream sa ref, kaya ayun, kumutsara na naman ang lola mo."
usage_notes: Less common than the phrase "gumamit ng kutsara," but understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay **kumutsara** ng mainit na sabaw.","translation":"He **scooped** the hot soup **with a spoon**."},{"sentence":"Hindi ka pwedeng magkamay sa ulam na ito, kailangan mong **kumutsara**.","translation":"You can't eat this dish with your hands, you need to **use a spoon**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis at maingay na pag-nguya ng pagkain, na kadalasang ginagawa nang walang-ingat at bukas ang bibig.
original_explanation: This is how you eat chicharon when no one's watching. That loud, crunchy, satisfying (for you, maybe not for others) sound of pure snacking bliss. Think of a goat happily munching on anything. That's the spirit of 'ngasab'.
usage_notes: The root word itself is rarely used alone. More common are the inflected forms like 'ngumangasab' (chewing noisily) or 'ngasabin' (to chew something noisily). It implies a certain lack of table manners.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **ngumasab** ng pagkain, isara mo ang iyong bibig.","translation":"Don't **chew noisily**, close your mouth."},{"sentence":"Nginangasab niya ang isang buong bag ng chips habang nanonood ng pelikula.","translation":"He was **munching** on a whole bag of chips while watching a movie."}]

translation: to chip off; to slice off a piece
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-alis o pagbawas ng isang bahagi mula sa isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pagtaga o paghiwa sa gilid.
original_explanation: What happens when your budget suddenly gets cut. Or when your mom asks for a 'small slice' of your cake and ends up taking a huge chunk. 'Hoy, sino'ng tumapyas sa keso de bola?!' is a classic Noche Buena mystery.
usage_notes: Refers to removing a piece from the surface or edge of something, often with a sharp tool.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kusang **tumapyas** ang isang bahagi ng lumang pader.","translation":"A part of the old wall **chipped off** on its own."},{"sentence":"Nag-ingat ang karpintero na hindi **tumapyas** nang sobra sa kahoy.","translation":"The carpenter was careful not **to slice off** too much from the wood."}]

meaning_filipino: Pinong-pinong mga butil ng lupa o iba pang bagay na natitipon sa isang ibabaw o lumulutang sa hangin.
original_explanation: That stuff you write "wash me" on sa kotse ng kapitbahay mo. It's the physical manifestation of your procrastination to clean your room. Every time you sweep the floor, it's a battle against this airborne enemy.
usage_notes: Often used to describe something old, neglected, or unclean. The adjective form is 'maalikabok'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno na ng **alikabok** ang mga lumang libro sa bodega.","translation":"The old books in the storage room are full of **dust**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang punasan ang **alikabok** sa mga muwebles.","translation":"Don't forget to wipe the **dust** off the furniture."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagdaan o paggalaw ng daliri sa screen ng isang elektronikong aparato, karaniwan ay pakaliwa o pakanan.
original_explanation: Ano na 'to, Tinder? Swipe left, swipe right. 'Yan ang ginagawa mo sa phone mo habang naghihintay ng reply niya. O kaya 'yung pag-swipe ng credit card, tapos iiyak sa katapusan ng buwan pagdating ng bill. That's life.
usage_notes: This is a progressive tense verb (present/contemplated aspect). 'Nag-swipe' is past tense, 'mag-su-swipe' is future tense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagsaswipe** ako sa TikTok nang bigla kang tumawag.","translation":"I was **swiping** on TikTok when you suddenly called."},{"sentence":"Kanina pa siya **nagsaswipe** sa mga litrato sa gallery niya.","translation":"He's been **swiping** through the photos in his gallery for a while now."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagmula sa isang pamilya ng mga maharlika o may mataas na katayuan sa lipunan.
original_explanation: Basically, a "royal." Someone with blue blood, a socialite, or from an old-money "haciendero" family. In modern times, it's that classmate who arrives in a chauffeured car and has never experienced commuting via MRT during rush hour.
usage_notes: An idiomatic expression. The hyphen is important. 'Dugong-bughaw' is a more common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinasabing si Prinsesa Urduja ay may **dugong-marangal**.","translation":"It is said that Princess Urduja was of **noble blood**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga kilos niya ay tila nagpapatunay na siya ay **dugong-marangal**.","translation":"His actions seem to prove that he is **blue-blooded**."}]

translation: to wrap a tapis around the waist
meaning_filipino: Ibalot o ipulupot ang tapis, isang piraso ng tela, sa baywang na karaniwang isinusuot sa ibabaw ng saya o palda.
etymology: From i- (causative verb prefix) + tapis (a wrap-around cloth worn over a skirt).
original_explanation: Think of the traditional Filipiniana dress. That piece of cloth wrapped around the waist over the skirt? That's the `tapis`, and `itapi` is the action of putting it on. It's a classic fashion move, like cinching your waist with a belt, but make it historical and cultural.
usage_notes: Very specific to clothing, particularly the traditional Filipino `tapis` or the `malong`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **itapi** ito nang maayos para sa pagtatanghal.","translation":"Help me **wrap this tapis** properly for the performance."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **itapi** ang malong kung hindi ka sanay.","translation":"It's hard **to wrap a malong around your waist** if you're not used to it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng manipis at transparent na pansit na gawa sa gawgaw (starch), karaniwang mula sa monggo, na lumalambot kapag inilubog sa mainit na tubig.
etymology: From Hokkien Chinese 'soa' (mountain) + 'tang-hun' (winter powder/noodles), referring to noodles made in mountainous regions during winter.
original_explanation: This is the 'glass noodle' of the Philippines. It's what makes that birthday soup special, often with chicken and patola. It looks like a tangled mess of plastic wire before you cook it, but becomes soft and slippery, perfect for slurping. Best served when you're sick or on a rainy day.
usage_notes: The main ingredient for the popular Filipino dish 'Sotanghon Soup'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap ang **sotanghon** na niluto ni lola.","translation":"The **sotanghon** that grandma cooked is delicious."},{"sentence":"Magluto ka ng manok na may **sotanghon** para sa may sakit.","translation":"Cook chicken with **glass noodles** for the sick person."}]

meaning_filipino: Nakibahagi sa isang laro o gawaing panlibangan na tapos na.
etymology: The 'nag-' prefix marks the completed aspect (past tense) of the root 'laro'.
original_explanation: The reason you're sleepy at work. '**Naglaro** kasi ako ng video games magdamag.' This is the past action that leads to present consequences, like failing an exam or getting a scolding from your boss for being unproductive.
usage_notes: The completed aspect (past tense) of 'maglaro'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Naglaro** kami ng tagu-taguan hanggang gumabi.","translation":"We **played** hide-and-seek until it got dark."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **naglaro** sa computer ko at iniwang bukas?","translation":"Who **played** on my computer and left it on?"}]

meaning_filipino: Walang gaspang, lubak, kulubot, o anumang umbok sa ibabaw; walang depekto o kapintasan.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'ma-' at salitang ugat na 'kinis' (smoothness).
original_explanation: The ultimate compliment for skin, roads, or even a 'diskarte' move. 'Ang kinis ng legs mo!' is a classic. When a plan goes off without a hitch, that's a 'makinis' operation. It's the opposite of 'magaspang' (rough). It's the goal of every skincare routine and every government road project (in theory).
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin para sa literal na ibabaw (surfaces) o sa matalinghagang paraan para sa mga plano, pagganap, o daloy ng isang pangyayari.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang balat ng sanggol ay napaka-**makinis**.","translation":"A baby's skin is very **smooth**."},{"sentence":"Sana ay maging **makinis** ang takbo ng ating proyekto.","translation":"I hope our project's progress will be **smooth**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bakuran o espasyo kung saan pinipisan at inaalagaan ang mga tupa.
original_explanation: Kung saan natutulog ang mga tupa. Di kasing common sa Pinas kasi mas madalas kambing ang alaga, pero gets mo na. Ito 'yung lugar na pinapasok ng pastol ang mga tupa para safe sila sa gabi. More biblical vibes than palengke vibes.
usage_notes: Often heard in religious or pastoral contexts due to biblical references.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginabayan ng pastol ang mga tupa pabalik sa kanilang **kulungan**.","translation":"The shepherd guided the sheep back to their **sheepfold**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bilang na kardinal na kasunod ng siyam; katumbas ng 10.
etymology: Pinaniniwalaang pinaikling anyo ng 'isang pu', na nangangahulugang 'isang pangkat ng sampu'.
original_explanation: The number 10. The basis for our 'per dozen' being 'per ten' sometimes (e.g., sampung itlog). It's the number of fingers you have, the basis of the decimal system, and the number of years you feel you've aged after a week of OT.
usage_notes: Ginagamit bilang pang-uri ng bilang (numeral adjective). Madalas na nagiging 'sampu't' kapag sinusundan ng 'isa', 'dalawa', atbp. (hal. sampu't isa).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroon akong **sampu** na daliri sa aking mga kamay.","translation":"I have **ten** fingers on my hands."},{"sentence":"Bumili ka ng **sampu**ng pandesal sa panaderya.","translation":"Buy **ten** pieces of pandesal at the bakery."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng hayop na mabilis tumakbo, mas malaki kaysa sa kuneho, at may mas mahahabang tainga at paa sa likod.
original_explanation: The faster, leggier, and more athletic cousin of the rabbit (kuneho). You know, the one from "The Tortoise and the Hare." In the Philippines, you're more likely to see a liyebre in a storybook or a cartoon than in the wild. It's the "de-kampo" version of a kuneho.
usage_notes: A literary or formal word. Most Filipinos would just say 'kuneho' (rabbit) for any similar-looking animal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa kwentong-bayan, natalo ng pagong ang mabilis na **liyebre**.","translation":"In the fable, the tortoise defeated the fast **hare**."},{"sentence":"Ang **liyebre** ay kilala sa kanyang pambihirang bilis sa pagtakbo.","translation":"The **hare** is known for its extraordinary running speed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpukpok nang marahan sa isang bagay, lalo na sa pinto, upang makatawag-pansin o magpahiwatig ng pagdating.
original_explanation: What the delivery guy does when your doorbell is broken. It's less common than "kumatok," but it means the same thing. Think of it as the sound "tok tok tok" turned into a verb.
usage_notes: "Kumatok" is the more common verb for "to knock." "Tumuktok" is a valid but less frequent alternative.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumuktok** siya ng tatlong beses bago binuksan ang pinto.","translation":"He **knocked** three times before the door was opened."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **tumuktok** kagabi?","translation":"Who **knocked** last night?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpasok at pagnguya ng pagkain sa bibig para sa nutrisyon o kasiyahan.
original_explanation: The most important word in the Filipino vocabulary. It's a greeting ("Kain tayo!"), an invitation, a question ("Kumain ka na?"), and a command. It's the solution to heartbreak, stress, and celebration. Before you can do anything else, you must first "kain". It's the foundation of Filipino hospitality.
usage_notes: Ang salitang-ugat na 'kain' ay maaari ring gamitin bilang isang pautos: "Kain!" (Eat!). Ang anyong pangkasalukuyan ay 'kumakain', pangnagdaan ay 'kumain', at panghinaharap ay 'kakain'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **kumain** ng sinigang.","translation":"I want **to eat** sinigang."},{"sentence":"Tara, **kain** tayo!","translation":"Come on, let's **eat**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang yunit ng bilang na katumbas ng 144 na piraso, o labindalawang dosena.
original_explanation: The more Spanish-sounding, slightly more 'alta' version of 'gros'. It also means 144 pieces (12 dozens). If a supplier in Divisoria says 'gros', their competitor trying to sound more sophisticated might say 'gruesa'. Both mean you're about to buy a heck of a lot of something.
usage_notes: Synonymous with 'gros'. Used in wholesale and industrial contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **gruesa** ng bote ang inorder ng pabrika.","translation":"The factory ordered a **gross** of bottles."},{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng isang **gruesa** ng itlog para sa malaking order ng leche flan.","translation":"We need a **gross** of eggs for the large leche flan order."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang matalik na ugnayan o pag-iibigan ng dalawang tao, na maaaring tumukoy sa malalim na pag-uusap, paglalambingan, o ang akto ng pagtatalik.
etymology: From `pag-` (gerund prefix) + `ni-` (reduplication of first syllable of root) + `niig` (intimate contact).
original_explanation: This is the formal, almost poetic, 'lolo and lola's' term for... well, you know. It's the word you'd find in a classic Tagalog romance novel, not something you'd shout in a BPO pantry. It covers everything from a deep, soulful connection to the physical act itself. It’s 'Netflix and chill' but in Florante at Laura language. Very SFW (Safe for Writing) in literature, but might get you some weird looks if used in casual convo.
usage_notes: A formal and somewhat archaic term. Its meaning can range from intimate conversation to the physical act of love, depending on the context. Modern usage is rare and often literary.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tula ay tungkol sa sagradong **pagniniig** ng mag-asawa.","translation":"The poem is about the sacred **intimate communion** of a married couple."},{"sentence":"Sa kanilang **pagniniig** sa ilalim ng puno, ipinagtapat nila ang kanilang pag-ibig sa isa't isa.","translation":"In their **intimate communion** under the tree, they confessed their love for each other."}]

translation: if not for; were it not for
meaning_filipino: Isang pangatnig na nagpapahayag ng kondisyon o dahilan na siyang pumigil o naging hadlang; katumbas ng "kung hindi lamang dahil sa".
etymology: Likely from "kung" (if) and "daan" (way/reason) with the "-an" suffix, evolving over time.
original_explanation: Ito yung "sana" na may kasamang sisihan. "Sana mayaman na ako, kundangan sa gastos ko sa milk tea." It's the ultimate 'what if' word for explaining why you're not yet at your peak form. Basically, "if it weren't for..." this one thing that's holding me back.
usage_notes: Considered formal and somewhat archaic, but still used in literature and formal speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matagal na sana siyang nakatapos, **kundangan** ay nagkasakit siya.","translation":"He would have graduated long ago, **if not for** the fact that he got sick."},{"sentence":"Tagumpay sana ang plano, **kundangan** sa biglaang pag-ulan.","translation":"The plan would have been a success, **were it not for** the sudden rain."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na itinatago bilang paalala ng isang tao, lugar, o pangyayari; alaala.
original_explanation: Basically a souvenir or a keepsake. That 'I ❤️ Baguio' t-shirt, the tiny keychain from Palawan, or that concert ticket you can't throw away. It can also mean a memory, like a 'rekuwerdo ng kahapon' (a memory of yesterday). It's the physical or mental stuff you keep to remind you of the good (or cringey) times.
usage_notes: Mas makaluma kaysa sa 'souvenir' ngunit malawak pa ring naiintindihan. Maaaring mangahulugan ng pisikal na bagay o isang alaala sa isip.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinago niya ang luma nilang litrato bilang **rekuwerdo**.","translation":"She kept their old photograph as a **memento**."},{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng mga **rekuwerdo** mula sa Vigan para sa aking pamilya.","translation":"I bought **souvenirs** from Vigan for my family."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na madaling makaranas ng pagkahilo o pagsusuka kapag naglalakbay sa dagat o anumang anyong tubig.
original_explanation: Eto yung kaibigan mong 5 minutes pa lang sa ferry pa-Bohol, namumutla na at naghahanap ng plastic bag. Sila yung laging may dalang Katinko o White Flower sa byahe. Hindi sila pwede mag-apply sa Navy.
usage_notes: Primarily used for seasickness, but can be used loosely for motion sickness in general.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uminom ka ng gamot dahil baka **layagin** ka sa mahabang biyahe sa barko.","translation":"Take your medicine because you might get **seasick** on the long boat trip."},{"sentence":"\"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi ako **layagin**,\" sabi niya nang may pagmamayabang.","translation":"\"Don't worry, I'm not **prone to seasickness**,\" he said boastfully."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan na sumusukat at nagpapahiwatig ng oras.
original_explanation: Your constant reminder that you're late for your shift, that your lunch break is almost over, or that it's *finally* uwian na. The OG gadget before smartphones. It's either a status symbol (Rolex yarn?) or a practical tool from Casio.
usage_notes: Can refer to both a wristwatch ('relos sa kamay' or 'relo') and a clock ('relos sa pader'). The shorter form 'relo' is also very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Anong oras na sa **relos** mo?","translation":"What time is it on your **watch**?"},{"sentence":"Nawala ko ang paborito kong **relos**.","translation":"I lost my favorite **watch**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang huling hantungan o kahihinatnan ng isang bagay, pangyayari, o tao, na karaniwang may negatibong konotasyon.
original_explanation: This is the "This is your life!" moment, but usually the tragic version. It's the consequences of your actions finally catching up. 'Yung sinabihan ka na ng nanay mo na 'wag kang mag-motor nang walang helmet, tapos naaksidente ka. 'Yun ang kasapitan mo. It’s the final, often unfortunate, destination of a bad decision.
usage_notes: Often implies a negative or tragic end.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagiging sakim ang nagdala sa kanya sa malagim na **kasapitan**.","translation":"Greed led him to his tragic **fate**."},{"sentence":"Iniiwasan niyang matulad sa **kasapitan** ng kanyang ama.","translation":"He avoids ending up with the same **outcome** as his father."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang kilos ng di-sinasadyang pag-agos o pagkalat ng isang likido o butil; ang patuloy na pag-aaksaya ng isang bagay.
etymology: From 'na-' (progressive prefix) + reduplication of the first syllable of the root 'ta-' + 'tapon' (to throw away).
original_explanation: This is the 'spill' in real-time. It's the panic you feel when you see the softdrinks overflowing from the glass. It can also be used figuratively for wasting resources, like when your manager sees you on Facebook during work hours and says your time is 'natatapon' (being wasted).
usage_notes: This is the progressive/present tense form of 'matapon'. It can mean literally spilling or figuratively being wasted.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hawakan mo nang maigi, **natatapon** na ang bigas mula sa sako!","translation":"Hold it tightly, the rice **is spilling** from the sack!"},{"sentence":"Hala, **natatapon** yung tubig sa timba, may butas yata.","translation":"Oh no, the water **is spilling** from the bucket, I think there's a hole."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging walang kakayahan o kapangyarihang baguhin ang isang sitwasyon o tulungan ang sarili o ang iba.
original_explanation: This is the feeling of watching your favorite series character make a terrible decision and you can't do anything about it. It’s seeing your crush cry over someone else. It's when your internet connection dies in the middle of a crucial online meeting. You know what needs to be done, but you're completely unable to do it. The universe just says "no."
usage_notes: Describes a deep sense of inability to act or change a situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang matinding **pagkawalang-kaya** habang pinapanood ang nasusunog nilang bahay.","translation":"He felt extreme **helplessness** while watching their house burn down."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkawalang-kaya** sa harap ng sakuna ay isang napakasakit na damdamin.","translation":"The **powerlessness** in the face of disaster is a very painful feeling."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtaas at pagbaba ng tono o himig ng boses sa pagsasalita, na nakakaapekto sa kahulugan ng isang pahayag.
original_explanation: Ito yung sikreto sa Pinoy communication. 'Yung salitang "Talaga?" pwedeng mangahulugang "Wow, really?", "Are you serious?!", o "I don't believe you." Lahat 'yan depende sa intonasyon. It's not what you say, it's how you say it, with matching taas-kilay pa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa iyong **intonasyon** kapag kinakausap mo ang mga nakatatanda.","translation":"Be careful with your **intonation** when you speak to elders."},{"sentence":"Nagbago ang kahulugan ng sinabi niya dahil sa maling **intonasyon**.","translation":"The meaning of what he said changed because of the wrong **intonation**."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagsasayang o pag-aaksaya ng pera, yaman, o pagkakataon nang walang kabuluhan.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your 13th-month pay two weeks after you get it. You see something shiny on Lazada, you treat all your friends to a fancy dinner, and suddenly, you're back to eating instant noodles. You basically 'niwaldas' your bonus. It's the financial version of 'sana all' turning into 'sana 'di na lang.'
usage_notes: This is the completed action (past tense) of 'magwaldas'. It carries a strong negative connotation of irresponsible and reckless spending or wasting of resources.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Niwaldas** niya ang lahat ng kanyang mana sa loob lamang ng isang taon.","translation":"He **squandered** all his inheritance in just one year."},{"sentence":"Sayang, **niwaldas** mo lang ang tiwalang ibinigay ko sa'yo.","translation":"What a waste, you just **wasted** the trust I gave you."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghahati o pagbabahagi ng isang buo sa dalawa o higit pang parte.
original_explanation: That moment when you only have one piece of chicharon bulaklak left and your friend says "pahingi." So you have to humati. It's the ultimate test of friendship. Also applies to splitting the bill, or 'yung pag-aaway ng magkakapatid sa mana.
usage_notes: Can mean to physically cut something in half or to share something among people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Humati** siya sa amin ng kanyang baon na tinapay.","translation":"He **shared** his packed bread with us."},{"sentence":"Sila ang **humati** sa mga gawain para mas mabilis matapos.","translation":"They **divided** the tasks to finish faster."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ikalabing-walong titik sa alpabetong Griyego (Σ, σ, ς). Ginagamit din bilang simbolo sa matematika at agham.
original_explanation: This is that scary-looking 'E' thingy from your high school math class (Σ) that meant you had to add a bunch of numbers. It's a Greek letter that found a full-time job in scaring students during statistics and calculus exams.
usage_notes: Used almost exclusively in academic or technical contexts like mathematics, statistics, and engineering.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong gamitin ang simbolong **sigma** para makuha ang kabuuan ng serye.","translation":"You need to use the **sigma** symbol to get the sum of the series."},{"sentence":"Sa statistics, ang standard deviation ay madalas na kinakatawan ng maliit na letrang **sigma** (σ).","translation":"In statistics, the standard deviation is often represented by the lowercase **sigma** (σ)."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagkuha ng isang bagay mula sa iba na may kasunduang ito ay isasauli sa takdang panahon.
original_explanation: The national sport of Filipino neighbors looking for a cup of sugar, a chair for the fiesta, or your Netflix password. It's a transaction based on trust and the unspoken rule: "Ibabalik ko rin... promise." Often the root of "friendship over" when the item is never returned.
usage_notes: Used for borrowing objects. For borrowing money, "umutang" is more common, although "humiram ng pera" is also correct.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pwede ba akong **humiram** ng ballpen mo sandali?","translation":"Can I **borrow** your ballpen for a moment?"},{"sentence":"**Humiram** siya ng libro mula sa aklatan.","translation":"She **borrowed** a book from the library."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halaman (Curcuma longa) na ang ugat ay ginagamit bilang pampalasa at pangkulay sa pagkain, at mayroon ding mga katangiang gamot.
original_explanation: This is the OG pampakulay ng pagkain before food coloring was a thing. It's what makes your curry yellow and your t-shirt permanently stained if you're not careful. Your lola probably swears by it as a cure for everything from a sore throat to bad vibes. The English is turmeric.
usage_notes: Bagaman nauunawaan ang 'turmeric' sa mga usapang pagluluto, ang 'luyang dilaw' ang pamantayang termino sa Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagyan mo ng **luyang dilaw** ang adobo para magkakulay.","translation":"Add **turmeric** to the adobo to give it color."},{"sentence":"Ang **luyang dilaw** ay kilala sa mga benepisyong pangkalusugan.","translation":"**Turmeric** is known for its health benefits."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maikli at pigil na pag-iyak na may kasamang mabilis at pautal-utal na paghinga.
original_explanation: This is the sound you make when you're trying not to cry but failing miserably. It's the 'ugly cry' starter pack. That little gasp for air between sobs when you're watching a sad K-drama or when your 13th-month pay goes directly to bills.
usage_notes: Often heard in its verb form 'humikbi' (to sob).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang mahinang **hikbi** mula sa kabilang kwarto.","translation":"I heard a soft **sob** from the other room."},{"sentence":"Puno ng **hikbi** ang kanyang mga huling salita.","translation":"Her last words were full of **sobs**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng transaksyon kung saan ang pagbabayad at pagtanggap ng produkto o serbisyo ay nangyayari nang sabay.
etymology: From mag- + kaliwa + -an. Literally 'to do with the left hand,' possibly from the idea of giving with one hand (right) and receiving with the other (left) at the same time.
original_explanation: The official term for COD (Cash on Delivery). You get the Shopee/Lazada package, you hand over the cash. No trust issues, no "utang muna, bes." It's a straight-up, simultaneous exchange. I give you this, you give me that. Ganern.
usage_notes: Commonly used in commerce and informal transactions. The noun form is `kaliwaan`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas gusto ko ang **magkaliwaan** para sigurado.","translation":"I prefer to **pay and receive simultaneously** to be sure."},{"sentence":"**Nagkaliwaan** sila sa bayad at sa produkto.","translation":"They **exchanged payment and the product simultaneously**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan o makina na ginagamit sa pagdurog o paggiling ng mga bagay tulad ng butil, kape, o karne.
original_explanation: The magical machine that turns coffee beans into your morning sanity juice, or chunks of meat into lumpiang shanghai filling. Your lola's OG food processor is the 'gilingang-bato'. A true gilingan is a kitchen workhorse.
usage_notes: Often combined with other words, e.g., 'gilingan ng kape' (coffee grinder) or 'gilingan ng karne' (meat grinder).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakidala ng **gilingan** ng kape para makapagtimpla tayo.","translation":"Please bring the coffee **grinder** so we can brew some."},{"sentence":"Nabili ko ang **gilingan** sa palengke para sa gagawin kong longganisa.","translation":"I bought the **grinder** at the market for the sausage I will make."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, lugar, o teritoryo na katabi, karating, o may kaparehong hangganan. Maaari ring tumukoy sa isang katunggali o kalaban.
original_explanation: This is your neighbor who blasts karaoke at 2 AM, or the next barangay you have a basketball rivalry with. It's the person in the office competing with you for that promotion. It's both a literal neighbor and a figurative rival. Think of it as the person/place right next to you, whether you're sharing a fence or sharing a spot on the leaderboard.
usage_notes: The meaning of 'neighboring/bordering' is common for places (e.g., `kahanggang-bayan`). The meaning of 'rival' is common for people, especially in sports or competition. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Bulacan ay isa sa mga **kahangga** nating lalawigan sa hilaga.","translation":"Bulacan is one of our **bordering** provinces in the north."},{"sentence":"Siya ang itinuturing kong pinakamalakas na **kahangga** sa kompetisyon.","translation":"I consider him my strongest **rival** in the competition."}]

translation: to become peaceful; to pass away
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging tahimik at kalmado; isang pormal at magalang na paraan upang sabihing namatay o pumanaw na.
original_explanation: Has two main vibes. 1) The feeling after a stressful week when you can finally log off and just chill. 'Pumayapa na rin ang isip ko.' (My mind is finally at peace). 2) A gentle, respectful way to say someone has died. 'Pumayapa na si Lolo.' (Grandpa has passed away peacefully). It's the ultimate state of peace.
usage_notes: The meaning depends heavily on context. If referring to a situation or feeling, it means 'to become peaceful.' If referring to a person, it is a euphemism for 'to die.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawa'y **pumayapa** na ang kanyang kaluluwa.","translation":"May his soul now be **at peace**."},{"sentence":"**Pumayapa** ang paligid nang tumigil ang malakas na musika.","translation":"The surroundings **became peaceful** when the loud music stopped."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o kilos ng pagiging permanente o regular sa isang posisyon o trabaho, mula sa pagiging kontraktuwal o pansamantala.
original_explanation: The ultimate goal of every contractual employee in the Philippines. It's the 'sana all' moment when your boss finally gives you that piece of paper that says you're no longer 'endo' (end of contract). It means you can finally apply for that credit card.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in the context of employment and job regularization.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Anim na buwan na siyang nagtatrabaho at umaasa nang **mapermanente**.","translation":"He has been working for six months and is hoping **to be made permanent**."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang tsansang **mapermanente** ka kung maganda ang iyong ipapakita.","translation":"There's a big chance you'll **become permanent** if you show good performance."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagbabago ng isang solidong bagay sa anyong likido dahil sa init. Ginagamit din ito upang ilarawan ang proseso ng panunaw ng pagkain sa tiyan.
original_explanation: This has two main gigs. First, it’s what happens to your ice cream under the Philippine sun—it melts. 'Magtunaw ka ng butter sa pan.' Second, it's what your stomach does after you've eaten a feast. 'Kailangan kong maglakad-lakad para magtunaw ng kinain.' It's the body's way of dealing with that extra rice. Also, when you see your crush, your heart can also 'matunaw' (melt).
usage_notes: Can refer to literal melting (due to heat) or the biological process of digestion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magtunaw** ng keso para sa spaghetti.","translation":"You need to **melt** cheese for the spaghetti."},{"sentence":"Kumain siya ng papaya para **magtunaw** ng pagkain.","translation":"He ate papaya to **digest** the food."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pinakaunang sandali o simula ng isang bagay o pangyayari; sa simula't simula pa.
original_explanation: This is some deep, historical, lola-level Tagalog. It's not just 'from the start,' it's 'since time immemorial,' 'since the dawn of time.' You'd use this when talking about the origins of the universe or the start of your 'Sana All' feelings for your crush. It's very formal and poetic.
usage_notes: Highly formal and literary. Often found in older texts, poetry, or formal speeches. Preceded by 'sa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa **kamula-mulaan** pa lamang ay alam na niyang may mali.","translation":"**From the very beginning**, he already knew something was wrong."},{"sentence":"Ito na ang ating paniniwala sa **kamula-mulaan**.","translation":"This has been our belief **from the very beginning**."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang lugar na malinis, walang sagabal, at may kaaya-ayang amoy; presko at hindi kulob.
original_explanation: That feeling when you enter a room right after general cleaning. The air smells fresh, everything is in its proper place, and there's a sense of order. It's the opposite of a 'bodega' or your sibling's messy room. It's the scent of freshly washed laundry or a newly mopped floor.
usage_notes: A less common word, often replaced by 'malinis' or 'presko'. It specifically combines the idea of cleanliness with a fresh scent or clear atmosphere.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakasarap matulog sa kwartong **maalis-is** at bagong linis.","translation":"It feels so good to sleep in a **fresh and clean-smelling** room that has just been cleaned."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng ulan, naging **maalis-is** ang hangin sa bukid.","translation":"After the rain, the air in the field became **fresh and clear**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng malalim na di-pagkakasundo, alitan, o labanan sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang tao o pangkat.
etymology: From an old Tagalog root, likely related to separation or opposition.
original_explanation: This is the chismis that turns into a full-blown barangay-level drama. It's not just a simple away; it's a long-running feud. Think rival families in a teleserye, or two BPO teams competing for the same incentive. That's a hidwaan.
usage_notes: Implies a more serious and prolonged conflict than a simple 'away' (fight) or 'tampuhan' (petty quarrel).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **hidwaan** sa lupa ng dalawang pamilya ay umabot na sa korte.","translation":"The land **dispute** between the two families has reached the court."},{"sentence":"Sana'y matapos na ang **hidwaan** sa pagitan ng magkapatid.","translation":"Hopefully, the **feud** between the siblings will end soon."}]

translation: to be the reason for praise
meaning_filipino: Maging dahilan o sanhi ng pagbibigay ng papuri sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: Ito yung moment na dahil sa galing mo, napuri rin yung boss mo, o kaya yung buong pamilya mo. 'Good job, anak! Ipagkapuri mo ang ating lahi!' Parang ikaw yung trophy na pinapakita sa lahat.
usage_notes: Often used in a formal or slightly dramatic context, emphasizing that an action brings honor or praise to someone else.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang iyong tagumpay ay **ipagkapuri** ng iyong mga magulang.","translation":"Your success will **be a source of praise** for your parents."},{"sentence":"Sana ang bawat gawa ko ay **ipagkapuri** ng ating bansa.","translation":"I hope my every action **brings praise** to our country."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kabuuan ng lahat ng mga Kristiyano o ng mga bansang Kristiyano sa buong mundo.
original_explanation: Basically, 'squad goals' for all Christians worldwide. It's like saying "the whole fandom" but for Christianity. You'd use this when you want to sound grand and all-encompassing, like a priest during a very long sermon.
usage_notes: A formal and somewhat archaic term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagpapalaganap ng kapayapaan ay tungkulin ng buong **sangkakristiyanuhan**.","translation":"Spreading peace is the duty of all of **Christendom**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang anyong pangnagdaan ng pandiwang 'gawin'; tumutukoy sa isang aksyon na isinagawa o tinapos na.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'who done it?' word. 'Sino'ng ginawa 'to?' (Who did this?) is a question that brings fear to siblings everywhere. It's the past tense of 'to do' or 'to make'. Whatever the action was, it's already been done.
usage_notes: Past tense of the verb 'gawin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ginawa** niya ang lahat para manalo sa kompetisyon.","translation":"He **did** everything to win the competition."},{"sentence":"Ano ang **ginawa** mo kahapon?","translation":"What did you **do** yesterday?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mga tao na nag-subscribe sa isang partikular na account sa social media upang makita ang mga update at post nito.
original_explanation: Your digital congregation. Your online barangay. These are the people who see your food pics, your travel brags, and your 3 AM sad posts. The number of followers you have is the new currency of online relevance, often determining whether you get a brand deal for a whitening soap or just a 'seen' from your crush.
usage_notes: The plural form is almost always used. The number of followers is a key metric on social media platforms.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Wow, ang dami mo nang **followers** sa TikTok!","translation":"Wow, you have so many **followers** on TikTok already!"},{"sentence":"Hindi mahalaga ang bilang ng **followers**, ang importante ay ang engagement.","translation":"The number of **followers** isn't important, what's important is the engagement."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaki na may mga kilos, gawi, at pananalitang katulad ng sa isang babae. Ginagamit din ito upang tukuyin ang isang babaeng transgender.
original_explanation: Historically, this term was used (often negatively) to describe a man acting 'like a woman.' Today, it's a complex word. The community has reclaimed it to mean a trans woman or a proudly effeminate gay man. Think of your fabulous tita, the one who gives the best life advice and can slay a makeup look. It's about expressing femininity, regardless of the body you were born in.
usage_notes: Ang konotasyon ng salita ay maaaring maging deskriptibo o mapanlait, depende sa nagsasalita at sa konteksto. Ito ay lalong ginagamit sa loob ng komunidad ng LGBTQ+ bilang isang termino ng pagkakakilanlan sa sarili.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa kanilang komunidad bilang isang matagumpay na **binabae**.","translation":"She is known in their community as a successful **transgender woman**."},{"sentence":"May mga nagsasabing **binabae** raw ang kanyang mga kilos, ngunit hindi niya ito pinapansin.","translation":"Some say his actions are **effeminate**, but he doesn't pay it any mind."}]

translation: to run aground; to get stuck
meaning_filipino: Tumama at hindi na makausad mula sa mababaw na bahagi ng tubig, putik, o buhangin; bumagsak o napaupo nang biglaan sa lupa.
original_explanation: Like your career when you don't upskill, or your Grab car in EDSA traffic during a flash flood. It's when something hits the bottom and can't move. Pwede ring sa love life, 'yung relasyon ninyong sumadsad na sa 'seen-zone'.
usage_notes: Often used for vehicles, especially boats, that get stuck. Can also be used figuratively for a career, a project, or a relationship that has stalled or failed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumadsad** ang malaking barko sa dalampasigan dahil sa lakas ng bagyo.","translation":"The large ship **ran aground** on the shore because of the strong typhoon."},{"sentence":"Matapos ang ilang buwang walang benta, tila **sumadsad** na ang aming negosyo.","translation":"After months without sales, it seems our business has **hit rock bottom**."}]

meaning_filipino: Bawat isang bahagi o elemento na bumubuo sa isang kabuuan, lalo na sa pagluluto o paggawa ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: The individual members of your group project, or the different spices that make your adobo a certified banger. Without the right `sangkap`, your ulam is just... sad. It's the "what's inside" that counts, from sinigang mix to the elements of a good chismis.
usage_notes: Primarily used for cooking ingredients, but can be metaphorically used for components of anything, like "mga sangkap ng tagumpay" (ingredients of success).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano-ano ang mga **sangkap** ng paborito mong adobo?","translation":"What are the **ingredients** of your favorite adobo?"},{"sentence":"Ang tiwala ay mahalagang **sangkap** sa isang matatag na relasyon.","translation":"Trust is an important **component** in a strong relationship."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na nagdudulot ng tiyak na reaksyon o aktibidad sa isang organismo o sistema.
original_explanation: This is that thing that makes you *go*. Yung bonus from your BPO job is an estimulo to work harder. Yung amoy ng bagong saing na kanin is an estimulo to get up from bed. Basically, it's the official term for 'pampagana' or 'pampagalaw.'
usage_notes: Often used in formal, scientific, or economic contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ayuda ng gobyerno ay nagsilbing **estimulo** sa ekonomiya.","translation":"The government aid served as a **stimulus** for the economy."},{"sentence":"Ang liwanag ay isang **estimulo** para sa mga halaman upang lumago.","translation":"Light is a **stimulus** for plants to grow."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manunulat na lumilikha ng mga dula para sa teatro, radyo, telebisyon, o pelikula.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `man-` (tagagawa ng kilos) + pag-uulit ng unang pantig `du` + `dula` (dula).
original_explanation: Sila 'yung mga taong nagsusulat ng mga script na pinapaiyak, pinapatawa, at pinapakilig tayo sa teatro. Sila ang arkitekto ng mga eksena. Kung si Shakespeare ay buhay ngayon, baka Wattpad writer or head writer ng isang teleserye 'yan. Sila ang OG Marites, pero on-script.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa manunulat ng dula. Ang mga aktor ay tinatawag na "artista" o "aktor/aktris".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Severino Reyes ay isang tanyag na **mandudula**.","translation":"Severino Reyes is a famous **playwright**."},{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang maging isang matagumpay na **mandudula**.","translation":"Her dream is to become a successful **playwright**."}]

translation: to lie on one's back; to lie supine
meaning_filipino: Ang sinasadyang paghiga na nakatingala at ang likod ang nakasayad sa isang ibabaw.
original_explanation: This is your default position after a huge meal, when you just want to stare at the ceiling and contemplate your food baby. Also the official 'I give up on adulting today' pose.
usage_notes: The prefix 'magpa-' here acts reflexively, meaning to cause oneself to be in that position. It is the opposite of 'magpatirapa' (to lie face down).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagod na pagod si Ana kaya't **nagpatihaya** na lang siya sa kama.","translation":"Ana was so tired that she just **lay on her back** on the bed."},{"sentence":"Sabi ng doktor, mas mabuting **magpatihaya** para maibsan ang sakit sa likod.","translation":"The doctor said it's better to **lie on one's back** to alleviate back pain."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkabit ng plag (plug) ng isang de-koryenteng kasangkapan sa saksakan (outlet) upang ito ay gumana.
original_explanation: 'Bes, pa-charge!' The first step is to find an outlet and **magsaksak** the charger. This is the lifeblood of every Pinoy who can't live without their phone at 100%. The opposite of 'bunutin'.
usage_notes: This is the common, everyday meaning related to electricity. The object being plugged in is usually implied or stated separately.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **magsaksak** ng laptop bago maubos ang baterya.","translation":"I need to **plug in** the laptop before the battery runs out."}]

translation: to bequeath; to leave as an inheritance
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-iwan o pagbibigay ng ari-arian, katangian, o kaalaman sa mga susunod na henerasyon o sa isang tagapagmana.
