original_explanation: This is what your rich lola does in her last will and testament. It's not just about getting the house and lot; it can also be about inheriting her legendary adobo recipe or her 'maritess' skills. It's the ultimate 'pass down'.
usage_notes: 'Magpamana' is the act of giving the inheritance. 'Magmana' is the act of receiving it. The object-focus form 'ipamana' is very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang matanda na **magpamana** ng kanyang mga aklat sa pampublikong aklatan.","translation":"The old man decided to **bequeath** his books to the public library."},{"sentence":"Anong mahalagang aral ang nais mong **ipamana** sa iyong mga anak?","translation":"What important lesson do you want to **pass down as a legacy** to your children?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pansamantalang kalagayan ng damdamin o emosyon ng isang tao.
original_explanation: The ultimate excuse for everything. "Bakit di ka nag-reply?" "Wala ako sa mood." It's that specific vibe you're feeling, whether it's for Jollibee, for binge-watching, or for ghosting someone. It's the state of your soul after 3 hours of traffic in EDSA.
usage_notes: Ginagamit nang malawakan sa Taglish, lalo na ng mga nakababata, upang ipahayag ang kanilang kasalukuyang nararamdaman o pagnanais.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo muna akong kausapin, wala ako sa **mood**.","translation":"Don't talk to me first, I'm not in the **mood**."},{"sentence":"Ang **mood** ko ngayon ay matulog lang buong araw.","translation":"My **mood** right now is to just sleep all day."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng alak na may kulay pula na mula sa ubas; alak na pula.
etymology: From Spanish 'tinto' (red, as in 'vino tinto' or red wine).
original_explanation: This is what you order when you're feeling fancy at a restaurant. "Vino tinto" is red wine. It's the drink of choice for titas at brunch or for anyone trying to be 'sophisticated' on a date.
usage_notes: Almost always used in the context of wine ('vino tinto'). While it's an adjective in Spanish, in Filipino it's used as a noun to mean 'red wine'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umorder siya ng isang baso ng **tinto**.","translation":"She ordered a glass of **red wine**."},{"sentence":"Mas gusto ko ang alak na **tinto** kaysa sa puti.","translation":"I prefer **red** wine over white."}]

translation: to bridge; to put a bridge over
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay o pagtatayo ng tulay sa isang lugar upang magkaroon ng daanan.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of building a bridge. “Kailangang **tulayan** ang malaking ilog para mapabilis ang transportasyon.” In hugot terms, it's what you try to do to close the 'communication gap' in a relationship. “Sinubukan kong **tulayan** ang namamagitan sa amin, pero ayaw niya talagang mag-reply.”
usage_notes: Isang pandiwang nakapokus sa lokasyon/benepisyaryo. Ang kilos ay ang paglalagay ng tulay sa ibabaw ng isang bagay (ang obheto).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng gobyerno na **tulayan** ang dalawang pulo.","translation":"The government is studying how **to bridge** the two islands."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **tulayan** ang bangin ng hindi pagkakaunawaan.","translation":"It's difficult **to bridge** the chasm of misunderstanding."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pampalasa, ang monosodium glutamate (MSG), na ginagamit upang mapatingkad ang lasa ng pagkain.
etymology: Mula sa pangalan ng produktong 'Ve-Tsin', na naging genericized trademark o pangkaraniwang tawag para sa MSG sa Pilipinas.
original_explanation: The secret weapon of many lolas and carinderia cooks. It's that 'magic powder' that makes everything taste... more. Some people swear it gives them a headache ('Chinese Restaurant Syndrome'), while others can't live without it. It's the umami bomb, the OG flavor enhancer.
usage_notes: Isang genericized trademark, katulad ng 'Colgate' para sa toothpaste. Ang ibang baybay ay 'bitsin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagyan mo ng kaunting **vetsin** ang adobo para mas sumarap.","translation":"Add a little **MSG** to the adobo to make it more delicious."},{"sentence":"Sinasabing ang sobrang **vetsin** ay hindi maganda sa kalusugan.","translation":"It is said that too much **MSG** is not good for one's health."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit at patag na buto na nagmumula sa isang halaman sa tropiko, ginagamit bilang pampalasa sa pagkain o pinagkukunan ng langis.
original_explanation: That tiny seed that gets stuck in your teeth after eating buchí or kare-kare. It's the confetti of the Asian culinary world, adding that nutty crunch you didn't know you needed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nilagyan niya ng **linga** ang ibabaw ng tinapay.","translation":"She sprinkled **sesame seeds** on top of the bread."},{"sentence":"Ang butsi ay pinagulong sa maraming **linga**.","translation":"The buchí was rolled in a lot of **sesame seeds**."}]

meaning_filipino: Magdulot ng paglala o pagiging mas malubha ng isang sitwasyon, karamdaman, o problema.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung pag nag-self-medicate ka tapos mas lumala 'yung sakit mo. O 'yung sinubukan mong ayusin 'yung away ng mag-jowa, pero dahil sa'yo, mas lumaki 'yung gulo. "Huwag mo nang kausapin, baka makalubha lang 'yan sa sitwasyon."
usage_notes: Often used in the context of health, problems, or conflicts. The prefix 'maka-' here acts as a causative, meaning 'to cause to become'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paninigarilyo ay maaaring **makalubha** sa iyong ubo.","translation":"Smoking can **worsen** your cough."},{"sentence":"Ang pagwawalang-bahala sa maliliit na problema ay maaaring **makalubha** sa mga ito.","translation":"Ignoring small problems can **aggravate** them."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng alimango na karaniwang naninirahan sa lupa malapit sa mga dalampasigan o latian.
original_explanation: The land-based cousin of the alimango. You see these guys scuttling around beaches or mangroves, looking like they're late for a very important meeting. They're a bit shy and will bolt into their burrows if you get too close. Sometimes they end up in ginataan, which is a delicious but tragic end to their story.
usage_notes: Refers to a specific type of crab that lives on land, not to be confused with its fully aquatic relatives.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming butas ng **kagang** sa dalampasigan.","translation":"There are many **land crab** holes on the shore."},{"sentence":"Masarap daw lutuin sa gata ang **kagang**.","translation":"They say it's delicious to cook **land crab** in coconut milk."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang damdamin ng malalim na paghanga, pagkaakit, o pagmamahal sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: This is the old-school, Kundiman-level of being charmed. It's not just 'crush,' it's the feeling you get when your K-Pop bias smiles on screen. It’s a deep, almost poetic sense of delight. 'Puno ng gili ang puso' means your heart is just overflowing with uwu energy.
usage_notes: A more poetic and less common synonym for 'giliw'. Often found in literature and classic songs.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **gili** ang kanyang mga mata habang pinagmamasdan ang sanggol.","translation":"Her eyes were full of **affection** as she watched the baby."},{"sentence":"Ang **gili** na nadarama niya para sa bayan ay hindi matatawaran.","translation":"The **delight** he feels for his country is immeasurable."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang gawain ay mangalap o mangolekta ng mga abuloy o donasyon.
etymology: Actor-noun form derived from the verb 'mangilak'.
original_explanation: The person holding the "pasa lata" can or the clipboard for a signature campaign. They are the designated fundraiser. You see them in malls, on the street, or even in your office, armed with a hopeful smile and a mission to get you to open your heart (and your wallet).
usage_notes: The noun form of the person who performs the action 'mangilak'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **mangingilak** mula sa simbahan ay kumatok sa aming pinto.","translation":"The **solicitors** from the church knocked on our door."},{"sentence":"Naging boluntaryong **mangingilak** siya para sa kanilang proyekto.","translation":"He became a volunteer **collector** for their project."}]

translation: as big as; of the same size
meaning_filipino: May magkaparehong laki, sukat, o lawak.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'kasing-' (nagiging 'kasin-') at salitang-ugat na 'laki'.
original_explanation: You use this when you see a dog that's practically a small horse, or a piece of chicharon that's bigger than your face. 'Uy, 'yung aso niya **kasinlaki** ng maliit na baka!'
usage_notes: The 'g' in 'kasing-' assimilates to 'n' because the root word 'laki' starts with 'l'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May nakita akong gagamba na **kasinlaki** ng kamao ko.","translation":"I saw a spider that was **as big as** my fist."},{"sentence":"Ang bato na humarang sa daan ay **kasinlaki** ng tao.","translation":"The rock blocking the road was **as big as** a person."}]

translation: to venerate, to revere, to treat as a saint
meaning_filipino: Parangalan o igalang nang lubos na parang isang santo; ituring na may kabanalan.
original_explanation: To treat someone like they're a saint who can do no wrong. It's what you do to your crush before you get to know them, or how your mom wants you to treat your lola. "Huwag mo akong pagbubuhatan ng kamay, nanay mo ako! Santuhin mo ako!"
usage_notes: Can be used literally for religious veneration or figuratively for showing extreme respect or putting someone on a pedestal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat nating **santuhin** ang ating mga magulang.","translation":"We should **revere** our parents."},{"sentence":"Masyado mong **sinasanto** ang kasintahan mo, kaya ka inaabuso.","translation":"You **treat** your girlfriend too much **like a saint**, that's why you're being taken for granted."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalaan ng buong atensyon, isip, o pansin sa isang partikular na bagay, gawain, o layunin.
original_explanation: What you tell yourself you'll do at work, but then a new meme pops up. It's giving your all to something, whether it's your thesis, your workout, or binge-watching a K-drama until 3 AM. It’s the opposite of being 'sana all-ed' by distractions.
usage_notes: Often used with 'ng pansin' (pagtuon ng pansin) to mean 'focusing of attention'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng masusing **pagtuon** sa pag-aaral para sa pagsusulit.","translation":"Intense **concentration** on studying is needed for the exam."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagtuon** ng gobyerno sa kalusugan ay mahalaga.","translation":"The government's **focus** on health is important."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging payapa, tahimik, at walang-bahala o pangamba.
original_explanation: That feeling when your salary comes in, all bills are paid, and you still have money for milk tea. The opposite of 'petsa de peligro'. It's the Zen moment before you remember you have work tomorrow.
usage_notes: Often refers to an internal state of calmness, as opposed to 'kapayapaan' (peace) which can be external (e.g., world peace).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahanap niya ang **kapanatagan** ng loob sa pag-iisa sa probinsya.","translation":"She found inner **peace of mind** by being alone in the province."},{"sentence":"Walang katumbas na halaga ang **kapanatagan** na dulot ng isang malinis na konsensya.","translation":"The **tranquility** brought by a clear conscience is priceless."}]

meaning_filipino: Paglalapat ng puwersa upang paikutin, ibaluktot, o baliin ang isang bagay. Maaari ring tumukoy sa sadyang pagbabago sa kahulugan ng salita o katotohanan.
original_explanation: This is what you do to the facts when you're explaining to your parents why you came home late. You don't lie, you just... **ipilipit** the story a bit. 'Hindi po ako nag-bar, dumaan lang po sa birthday ng kaibigan ng pinsan ko.' It's the art of strategic twisting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ipilipit** ang aking mga salita para lang manalo sa usapan.","translation":"Do not **twist** my words just to win the argument."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **ipilipit** ang alambre para makabuo ng hugis-puso.","translation":"He tried to **twist** the wire to form a heart shape."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sariling sulat-kamay o pirma ng isang tao, lalo na ng isang sikat na personalidad, na kinukuha bilang isang alaala.
original_explanation: Before selfies, this was the ultimate proof that you met your idol. It's their signature, usually scribbled hastily on a piece of paper, a t-shirt, or even your forehead if you're that dedicated. Now, it's kinda like a physical version of a celebrity 'liking' your comment. You treasure it forever, or sell it on eBay.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb: 'magpa-autograp' (to ask for an autograph).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatago pa rin sa akin ang **autograp** ni Sharon Cuneta na nakuha ko noong bata ako.","translation":"I still have the **autograph** of Sharon Cuneta that I got when I was a child."},{"sentence":"Pumila siya nang mahaba para lang makakuha ng **autograp** mula sa kanyang paboritong manunulat.","translation":"He queued for a long time just to get an **autograph** from his favorite author."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng panghalip na ginagamit sa pagtukoy o pagturo sa mga tao, bagay, lugar, o pangyayari. Halimbawa: ito, iyan, iyon.
etymology: From "pan-" + "patlig" (an archaic root word meaning 'to point at'). The "n" in the prefix "pan-" assimilates to "m" before a root word starting with 'p'.
original_explanation: Grammar's version of pointing. When you're too lazy to say "yung laptop sa ibabaw ng lamesa," you just say "ito" (this). It's the "this," "that," and "that over yonder" (ito, iyan, iyon) of the Tagalog world. Essential for chismis: "Iyan ang suot niya kahapon!"
usage_notes: This is a grammatical term itself, not a word used in everyday conversation. However, the words it describes (e.g., ito, iyan, iyon) are used daily.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga salitang \"ito,\" \"iyan,\" at \"iyon\" ay halimbawa ng panghalip na **pamatlig**.","translation":"The words \"this,\" \"that,\" and \"that over there\" are examples of **demonstrative pronouns**."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan namin sa Filipino ang tungkol sa panghalip na **pamatlig**.","translation":"We are studying about **demonstrative pronouns** in our Filipino class."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso, sistema, o kalagayan ng paggawa sa isang tao na maging alipin; pag-agaw sa kalayaan at pagpapasailalim sa kapangyarihan ng iba.
etymology: Mula sa "pang-" (gawain ng) + pag-uulit ng unang pantig ng salitang-ugat na "alipin". Ang pag-uulit ay nagpapahiwatig ng isang sistematiko o tuluy-tuloy na aksyon.
original_explanation: This is some serious history class stuff. It's the ultimate 'power-tripping' – taking away someone's freedom completely. On a less serious note, it's what you jokingly call your relationship with your job during crunch time or hell week. "Ito'y pang-aalipin na, hindi na trabaho!"
usage_notes: Isang pormal at seryosong termino, madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng kasaysayan, politika, o lipunan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Labanan natin ang anumang uri ng **pang-aalipin** sa modernong panahon.","translation":"Let us fight any form of **enslavement** in the modern era."},{"sentence":"Ang kasaysayan ay puno ng mga kuwento ng paglaban sa **pang-aalipin**.","translation":"History is full of stories of struggle against **subjugation**."}]

translation: the act of composing or reciting poetry; versification
meaning_filipino: Ang sining o akto ng paglikha o pagbigkas ng isang tula.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `pag-` at sa salitang ugat na `tula` (isang anyo ng panitikan na may sukat at tugma).
original_explanation: That moment you feel extra 'makata' and start dropping hugot lines that rhyme. It's the act of writing poems, whether for a school project on Florante at Laura, a spoken word performance about your ex, or just a cheesy love poem for your SO. It's turning feelings into verses. #PoetNaSanaAll
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang hilig sa **pagtula** ay nagsimula noong siya'y bata pa.","translation":"Her passion for **writing poetry** started when she was still young."}]

translation: to cheat, to fool, to trick
meaning_filipino: Ang gumawa ng panloloko o pandaraya; ang hindi pagiging tapat sa isang kasunduan, relasyon, o pangako.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'sana all' betrayal verb. This is what you accuse someone of when they cheat in a relationship ('two-timer!'), cheat on a test, or sell you a fake iPhone. To 'manloko' is to break trust in a big way. It’s the action that fuels a thousand hugot posts and sad boi/girl playlists.
usage_notes: A very common word covering everything from relationship infidelity to general swindling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakasakit ang **manloko** ng taong nagtitiwala sa iyo.","translation":"It is very painful to **fool** a person who trusts you."},{"sentence":"Pinangako niya sa sarili na hindi na siya muling magpapaloko sa mga taong mahilig **manloko**.","translation":"She promised herself that she would never again be fooled by people who like to **cheat**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang isang tao o bagay na may kaparehong antas, halaga, o katangian; ang kapantay o katumbas.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na nahanap mo na ang katapat mo. Pwedeng sa pag-ibig (your soulmate), pwedeng sa chess (your rival), o pwedeng sa inuman (yung hindi ka uurungan). It's your match, your equal, the one who can finally put you in your place. The Pinoy version of "You've met your match!"
usage_notes: Can refer to a rival, a partner, or an equivalent force. It carries the connotation of being an equal challenge or complement.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa wakas, natagpuan na ni Berto ang kanyang **katapat** sa paglalaro ng Mobile Legends.","translation":"Finally, Berto has found his **match** in playing Mobile Legends."},{"sentence":"Akala niya kaya niya lahat, pero nahanap niya ang **katapat** niya sa bago niyang boss.","translation":"He thought he could handle everything, but he met his **match** in his new boss."}]

translation: to be able to improve; to be able to make better
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang gawing mas maayos, mas mainam, o mas mataas ang kalidad ng isang bagay o kalagayan.
original_explanation: The goal of every "New Year, New Me" resolution. It's the ability to level up something—your skills, your health, your relationship, or even just your internet connection. "Ang pag-eehersisyo araw-araw ay tiyak na makapagpapabuti ng iyong kalusugan."
usage_notes: A very versatile word for improvement in any context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagbabasa ng libro ay maaaring **makapagpabuti** ng iyong bokabularyo.","translation":"Reading books can **improve** your vocabulary."},{"sentence":"Nag-aaral siyang mabuti para **makapagpabuti** ng kanyang mga grado.","translation":"He is studying hard to **be able to improve** his grades."}]

meaning_filipino: Maging dahilan ng pagkabagabag, pag-aalala, o hindi pagkapalagay.
etymology: Mula sa panlaping pangkasanhi na "ika-" at sa salitang-ugat na "tigatig" (pagkabagabag, pagkabalisa).
original_explanation: This is what makes you feel restless and anxious, 'yung tipong 'di ka mapakali. It's the "seen-zone" from your crush. It's the vague "we need to talk" message from your boss. It's the sound of a dog barking nonstop at 3 AM. It’s the source of your inner turmoil.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang pormal o pampanitikang pandiwang sanhi na nagpapaliwanag sa dahilan ng pagkabalisa o hindi mapakaling pakiramdam.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kawalan ng balita mula sa kanya ang **ikatigatig** ng kanyang pamilya.","translation":"The lack of news from him is what **caused unease** for his family."},{"sentence":"Maraming bagay ang maaaring **ikatigatig** ng isang tao sa panahong ito.","translation":"Many things can **cause a person to be restless** in this day and age."}]

meaning_filipino: Isuplong o iulat sa mga may kapangyarihan ang isang tao o isang ilegal na gawain; hayagang tuligsain o kondenahin.
original_explanation: This is the elevated, more formal version of "isumbong." If you see your neighbor doing something illegal, like building a structure without a permit, you `idenunsiya` them to the barangay captain. It’s being a whistleblower or a concerned citizen with official paperwork. It’s "sumbong" with a college degree.
usage_notes: Stronger and more formal than 'isumbong'. It implies reporting a crime or a serious violation to an official body, or publicly condemning an act or person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May gantimpalang inaalok para sa sinumang **magdenunsiya** sa mga gumagawa ng pekeng gamot.","translation":"A reward is being offered for anyone who will **report** the makers of fake medicine."},{"sentence":"**Idinenunsiya** ng isang concerned citizen ang iligal na pagtotroso sa kanilang lugar.","translation":"A concerned citizen **denounced** the illegal logging in their area."}]

translation: fond of wandering, prone to travel
meaning_filipino: Isang taong mahilig maglakbay, maglibot, o mamasyal.
etymology: Mula sa "gala" at hulaping "-in," na nagpapahiwatig ng isang katangian o tendensiya.
original_explanation: This is the official title for the 'Travel Goals' friend in your barkada. The one whose IG feed is 90% scenery and 10% food. They have a passport full of stamps and a perpetually packed go-bag. If a long weekend is announced, they've already booked a flight before you've even finished reading the announcement. A certified 'galain' can't stay put.
usage_notes: Inilalarawan ang isang katangian ng pagkatao ng isang tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Talagang **galain** si Ana, halos linggo-linggo ay nasa ibang probinsya siya.","translation":"Ana is truly **fond of wandering**; she's in a different province almost every week."},{"sentence":"Dahil **galain** ako, pinili ko ang trabahong nangangailangan ng madalas na pagbiyahe.","translation":"Because I'm **prone to travel**, I chose a job that requires frequent trips."}]

translation: to go to the market; to shop at the market
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpunta sa pamilihan o palengke upang bumili ng mga pangangailangan, lalo na ng pagkain.
etymology: From `ma-` + `palengke`, which is from Spanish `palenque` (stockade, arena).
original_explanation: The ultimate weekend chore for many Pinoy households. It's the act of putting on your 'pambahay' clothes, grabbing your reusable bayong, and braving the wet floors and the lively calls of 'Bili na, suki!' to get the freshest produce and best deals. 'Ma, sasama ako **mamalengke** para makabili ng isaw.'
usage_notes: Specifically refers to shopping at a 'palengke' (wet market), not a supermarket or mall.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing Sabado ng umaga, ugali na ni Aling Nena ang **mamalengke**.","translation":"Every Saturday morning, it's Aling Nena's habit to **go to the market**."},{"sentence":"Sino ang naka-assign na **mamalengke** para sa handaan bukas?","translation":"Who is assigned to **shop at the market** for tomorrow's feast?"}]

meaning_filipino: Mga itlog ng isda, na maaaring nasa loob pa ng isda o inalis na upang kainin.
original_explanation: The caviar of the palengke. It's those tiny orange or yellow bubbles you find inside a fish. For some, it's the best part; for others, it's... an acquired taste. It's like finding a bonus prize inside your sinigang na isda.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to the mass of eggs (the sac), not individual eggs. Also known as 'bihod' in other dialects.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap ang isdang may **liya** kapag ipinirito.","translation":"Fish with **roe** is delicious when fried."},{"sentence":"Hinanap niya ang parte ng **liya** sa tiyan ng bangus.","translation":"He looked for the **fish eggs** in the milkfish's belly."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang lugar o pagkakataon kung saan mayroong pagdiriwang, salu-salo, o pangkalahatang saya.
original_explanation: The vibe at your tita's house kapag may birthday. You can smell the Pinoy spaghetti from a block away, hear the karaoke machine blasting Aegis songs, and see your cousins playing on the street. 'May-kasiyahan' means there's food, fun, and probably a lot of chismis.
usage_notes: Describes a state or location, e.g., 'May-kasiyahan sa kapitbahay' (The neighbor is having a party).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maingay sa kabilang bahay dahil **may-kasiyahan** sila.","translation":"It's noisy at the other house because they're **having a celebration**."},{"sentence":"Ang buong barangay ay **may-kasiyahan** para sa kanilang pista.","translation":"The whole barangay is **festive** for their fiesta."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng kaalaman o kasanayan sa isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pag-aaral, karanasan, o pagtuturo.
original_explanation: This is what you hope happens after hours of scrolling through TikTok tutorials or binge-watching YouTube videos. It's the 'Aha!' moment when the lesson finally clicks, whether it's a new recipe, a dance move, or why your ex was a bad idea. 'Sana all may matutuhan sa pagkakamali.'
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'malaman' (to know/find out), but 'matutuhan' emphasizes the process of learning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming bagay ang maaari mong **matutuhan** kung bubuksan mo lang ang iyong isipan.","translation":"There are many things you can **learn** if you just open your mind."},{"sentence":"Sana ay **matutuhan** mo na ang leksyon mula sa iyong mga pagkakamali.","translation":"I hope you finally **learn** the lesson from your mistakes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na nagiging hadlang, sagabal, o balakid sa pag-usad o pagsasakatuparan ng isang layunin.
original_explanation: Ito yung mga 'Marites' sa buhay mo na humahadlang sa iyong pag-move on. O kaya yung biglaang 'system down' sa bangko pag kukunin mo na sahod mo. Anything that gets in your way, from a slow internet connection during a crucial Zoom meeting to your tita asking when you're getting married.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa mas pormal o legal na konteksto. Ang karaniwang salita ay 'hadlang' o 'sagabal'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kakulangan sa pondo ang naging **impedimento** sa pagpapatuloy ng proyekto.","translation":"The lack of funds became an **impediment** to the project's continuation."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang maging **impedimento** ang takot sa iyong mga pangarap.","translation":"Don't let fear become an **impediment** to your dreams."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-aalok ng produkto o serbisyo kapalit ng pera na naisagawa na.
original_explanation: Past tense of selling. That satisfying 'Sold to the highest bidder!' moment. When you finally found a buyer for your old PS4, you **nagbenta**. It's the completed transaction, the 'cash on hand,' the end of a 'for sale' post.
usage_notes: Completed aspect (past tense) of 'magbenta'. From Spanish 'venta' (sale).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagbenta** siya ng kotse para makapag-aral ang anak.","translation":"He **sold** his car so his child could study."},{"sentence":"Mabilis siyang **nagbenta** ng lahat ng paninda.","translation":"She quickly **sold** all her merchandise."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaghalong semento, buhangin, at tubig na ginagamit sa pagtatayo upang pagdikitin ang mga bloke o ladrilyo. Maaari rin itong tumukoy sa isang uri ng kanyon na nagpapaputok ng mga bomba sa isang arko.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na "mortar", na galing sa Latin na "mortarium".
original_explanation: Ito yung pampasta sa hollow blocks para maging pader ang pangarap mong bahay. Parang pandikit, pero pang-construction. Sa military context naman, ito yung 'BOOM!' na galing sa itaas, hindi yung 'boom, panes!' na pang-meme.
usage_notes: Ang kahulugan ay nakadepende sa konteksto kung ito ba ay para sa konstruksyon o sa militar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating timplahin nang tama ang **mortar** para maging matibay ang pader.","translation":"We need to mix the **mortar** correctly so the wall will be strong."},{"sentence":"Isang **mortar** ang pinaputok ng mga sundalo sa kampo ng kaaway.","translation":"The soldiers fired a **mortar** at the enemy camp."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi ayon sa kalikasan; hindi karaniwan o gawa ng tao at hindi likas.
etymology: Mula sa "di-" (hindi) at "natural" (mula sa Espanyol na "natural").
original_explanation: Parang yung ngiti mo sa picture nung kasama mo yung ex ng best friend mo. Pilit. O kaya yung kulay ng buhok na sobrang shocking pink, or yung lasa ng powdered juice na sobrang tamis. That's di-natural. Anything that makes you say, "May mali dito."
usage_notes: Maaari ring mangahulugang 'supernatural' sa ilang konteksto, ngunit mas karaniwan ang 'artipisyal' o 'pilit'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **di-natural** na katahimikan sa loob ng bahay matapos ang kanilang pag-aaway.","translation":"There was an **unnatural** silence inside the house after their fight."},{"sentence":"Iwasan ang mga pagkaing may **di-natural** na sangkap at pampalasa.","translation":"Avoid foods with **artificial** ingredients and flavorings."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkilos na magpagawa o magpatayo ng isang tirahan o bahay para sa sarili o para sa iba.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "adulting" goal. After years of saving up, OFW remittances, and maybe a housing loan that feels like a lifetime commitment, you finally get to magpabahay. It's the act of commissioning a house to be built. Pwede ring government project, like "Pabahay program ni Mayor." It’s literally "to cause a house to exist."
usage_notes: Can mean having a house built for oneself, or sponsoring the construction of a house for others (e.g., a government program).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap ng mag-asawa na **magpabahay** sa kanilang lupang sinilangan.","translation":"It is the couple's dream **to have a house built** on their native land."},{"sentence":"Ang gobyerno ay may proyektong **magpabahay** para sa mga nasalanta ng bagyo.","translation":"The government has a project **to build houses** for the typhoon victims."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panginginig ng katawan dahil sa matinding lamig, takot, o iba pang malakas na damdamin.
etymology: From pa- + mam- (from ma- + ligpig) + ligpig. The root 'ligpig' is an archaic word for shuddering.
original_explanation: You know that feeling when the office AC is set to 'Antarctica' and you didn't bring a jacket? That's pamamaligpig. Or when you're watching a horror movie and the jump scare gets you good? That full-body shiver is pamamaligpig. It's your body's involuntary 'shake it off' moment due to cold or fear.
usage_notes: Often interchangeable with 'panginginig' but 'pamamaligpig' can imply a more intense, full-body shudder.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula ang kanyang **pamamaligpig** nang maramdaman ang malamig na hangin.","translation":"His **shuddering** began when he felt the cold wind."},{"sentence":"Dama ko ang **pamamaligpig** ng buong katawan niya sa takot.","translation":"I felt the **trembling** of his whole body in fear."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay o nagbibigay ng maraming biyaya o pagpapala.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `mapag-` (na nagsasaad ng pagkakaroon ng katangian) + `biyaya` (grasya, pagpapala).
original_explanation: This describes something that's overflowing with blessings. Parang 'yung puno ng mangga niyo na hitik na hitik sa bunga, or 'yung career mo na sunod-sunod ang promotion. It's the universe saying "Here, have some more!" It's the feeling of abundance, 'yung "sana all" ng blessings.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa isang espirituwal o mapagpasalamat na konteksto. Maaaring ilarawan ang isang tao, isang bagay (tulad ng ani), o isang panahon (tulad ng isang taon).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tunay na **mapagbiyaya** ang taon na ito para sa aming pamilya.","translation":"This year has been truly **bountiful** for our family."},{"sentence":"Salamat sa isang **mapagbiyaya** na ani.","translation":"Thank you for a **bountiful** harvest."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kondisyon kung saan ang isang tao ay may kahirapan o kawalan ng kakayahang makilala ang pagkakaiba ng ilang mga kulay.
etymology: Isang literal na salin ng pariralang Ingles na 'color blind'.
original_explanation: When you ask someone to pass the 'red' pen and they hand you the 'green' one, they might be this. It's a real medical condition, but also a good excuse when your outfit doesn't match. 'Sorry, medyo **bulag sa kulay** ako, kaya ganito suot ko.'
usage_notes: Ito ay isang nakapirming parirala. Ang terminong Ingles na 'color blind' ay karaniwan ding ginagamit sa Taglish.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nalaman niyang **bulag sa kulay** siya noong kumuha siya ng medical exam.","translation":"He found out he was **color blind** when he took a medical exam."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya makita ang numero sa larawan dahil **bulag sa kulay** siya.","translation":"He can't see the number in the picture because he is **color blind**."}]

meaning_filipino: Maliliit na bala o tingga na ginagamit sa baril, karaniwan para sa pangangaso ng mga ibon.
original_explanation: Think of it as the 'bagoong' of bullets—a bunch of tiny, powerful things packed together. It's what you use in a shotgun. Not the kind of 'shot' you take at a bar, but the kind that can ruin a bird's day (and yours if you're not careful).
usage_notes: Often used in rural or hunting contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **perdigones** ang katawan ng nahuling ibon.","translation":"The body of the caught bird was full of **pellets**."},{"sentence":"Nagkarga siya ng **perdigones** sa kanyang escopeta.","translation":"He loaded his shotgun with **birdshot**."}]

translation: mangled; crushed; smashed to a pulp
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging durog, wasak, o pipi na halos hindi na makilala ang orihinal na anyo.
original_explanation: The state of being completely wrecked. Think of a tomato after a truck runs over it, or your feelings after your favorite K-drama character gets killed off. It's beyond broken; it's 'di na ma-recognize'.
usage_notes: Describes a state of extreme physical damage. Can be used figuratively for emotions, but it's a very strong and graphic term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lasog** ang prutas na nahulog mula sa ikalimang palapag.","translation":"The fruit that fell from the fifth floor was **smashed to a pulp**."},{"sentence":"Naiwang **lasog** ang sasakyan matapos ang malakas na banggaan.","translation":"The car was left **mangled** after the strong collision."}]

meaning_filipino: May bahagyang alat, karaniwang tumutukoy sa tubig na pinaghalong tubig-tabang at tubig-alat.
original_explanation: The taste of water near the beach, but not quite the full-on ocean yet. It's the 'It's Complicated' relationship status of water—not quite fresh, not quite salty. Perfect for growing 'bangus' (milkfish) in fishponds.
usage_notes: Primarily used to describe water in estuaries, deltas, or fishponds where freshwater and saltwater mix.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nabubuhay ang mga alimango at sugpo sa **matabsing** na tubig.","translation":"Crabs and prawns live in **brackish** water."},{"sentence":"Hindi ito maiinom dahil **matabsing** ang tubig mula sa poso malapit sa dagat.","translation":"This cannot be drunk because the water from the pump near the sea is **slightly salty**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sinadya at malupit na pagpatay sa isang tao o maraming tao, lalo na kung ang biktima ay isang mahalagang tao o kung ang kilos ay isinagawa nang may kalupitan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'paslang' (to kill brutally) at unlaping 'pamama-'.
original_explanation: This is the darker, more intense version of 'pagpatay'. It's not just killing; it's brutal, intentional, and often makes headlines. Think 'Game of Thrones' Red Wedding or a political assassination. It’s killing with an exclamation point.
usage_notes: A strong word used for brutal or large-scale killings, often with political or criminal motives.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pamamaslang** sa mga mamamahayag ay isang atake sa kalayaan sa pamamahayag.","translation":"The **killing** of journalists is an attack on press freedom."},{"sentence":"Kinondena ng buong mundo ang naganap na **pamamaslang**.","translation":"The whole world condemned the **massacre** that occurred."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na mahilig maglaro, lalo na ng mga laro ng pagkakataon o sugal.
original_explanation: Your tito who spends his weekends at the *sabungan* (cockpit) or your officemate who's always organizing the online Mobile Legends tournament. It's the Spanish-sounding word for 'player' or 'gambler', giving it a slightly more classic, almost dramatic, flair.
usage_notes: Bagama't ang literal na kahulugan ay 'manlalaro,' madalas itong may negatibong konotasyon na tumutukoy sa isang sugarol.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa kanilang lugar bilang isang batikang **hugador** ng baraha.","translation":"He is known in their area as a veteran card **player**."},{"sentence":"Sinabihan siya ng kanyang asawa na itigil na ang pagiging **hugador**.","translation":"His wife told him to stop being a **gambler**."}]

translation: to report; to tell as news
meaning_filipino: Ipahayag o isalaysay ang isang pangyayari o impormasyon bilang isang balita.
etymology: From `i-` (causative prefix) + `balita` (news), which comes from Sanskrit vārttā (information, news).
original_explanation: This is the official term for what Marites does best. It's the act of sharing news, whether it's on TV Patrol, your group chat, or over the bakod with your kapitbahay. "Ano'ng latest? Ibalita mo naman!"
usage_notes: A very common word for disseminating information, from formal news reporting to casual gossip.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **ibalita** sa akin ang resulta ng exam.","translation":"Don't forget to **tell me the news** about the exam results."},{"sentence":"Agad na **ibinalita** ng reporter ang naganap na sunog.","translation":"The reporter immediately **reported** the fire that occurred."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng isang tanda, mantsa, o palatandaan.
original_explanation: Yung damit mong puti na natalsikan ng toyo, may-marka na 'yan forever. Parang puso mong minsan nang nasaktan, kahit mag-move on, may peklat pa rin. O 'yung exam paper mo na puro red pen ng teacher, 'yan ang tunay na may-marka.
usage_notes: Often used to describe something that is no longer pristine or has a distinguishing feature, sometimes negative (like a stain) or neutral (like a label).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong isuot ang damit na **may-marka** ng kape.","translation":"Don't wear the shirt that's **stained** with coffee."},{"sentence":"Lahat ng produkto ay dapat **may-marka** ng presyo.","translation":"All products must be **marked** with a price."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng gatas ng baka na inalisan ng tubig at dinagdagan ng asukal, na nagreresulta sa isang malapot at matamis na produkto.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'leche condensada' (gatas na pinalapot).
original_explanation: The lifeblood of Filipino desserts. From leche flan to fruit salad to yema, this is the secret ingredient. Pwede ring palaman sa pan de sal 'pag walang-wala na talaga. It's the sweet, sticky nectar of the Pinoy gods.
usage_notes: Isang napakakaraniwang sangkap sa kusinang Pilipino, lalo na sa mga panghimagas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng isang lata ng **condensada** para sa gagawin kong fruit salad.","translation":"I need one can of **condensed milk** for the fruit salad I'm going to make."},{"sentence":"Mas masarap ang kape kapag may halong **condensada**.","translation":"Coffee is more delicious when mixed with **condensed milk**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang idyoma na tumutukoy sa ugali ng pagiging masigasig lamang sa simula ng isang gawain ngunit nawawalan ng gana at hindi ito tinatapos. Ito ay hango sa mabilis na pag-aapoy at pagkawala ng apoy ng damong kugon.
etymology: From 'ningas' (flame) and 'kugon' (cogon grass, a type of tall grass that burns quickly).
original_explanation: The quintessential Filipino trait of starting something with 110% energy and then... meh. It's your New Year's resolution to go to the gym, which lasts until January 3rd. It's that online course you bought on sale but never opened. The fire of the 'kugon' grass burns brightly for a second and then dies. It's the ultimate "Started from the bottom, now we're... tired, let's just stop here" mood.
usage_notes: A very common Filipino idiom to describe a negative work ethic or fleeting interest, literally 'cogon grass flame'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iwasan natin ang ugaling **ningas-kugon** upang matapos ang ating mga proyekto.","translation":"Let's avoid the **[habit of] fleeting enthusiasm** so we can complete our projects."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula siyang mag-aral ng gitara pero **ningas-kugon** lang pala; pagkatapos ng isang linggo, ayaw na niya.","translation":"He started learning guitar, but it turned out to be just a **passing enthusiasm**; after one week, he didn't want to anymore."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng bag na isinasakbat o isinusuot sa likod, karaniwang may dalawang strap para sa mga balikat.
original_explanation: This is the official bag of every Filipino student from elementary to college. It's where you stuff your books, baon, PE uniform, and a whole lot of 'sana Biyernes na.' Also the essential gear for 'biyaheros' and 'biyaheras' exploring the 7,107 islands (and counting).
usage_notes: The word 'bag' is more common in casual conversation, but 'backpack' is universally understood and used, especially when specifying the type.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng libro ang kanyang **backpack**.","translation":"His **backpack** is full of books."},{"sentence":"Naiwan ko ang payong ko sa loob ng **backpack**.","translation":"I left my umbrella inside the **backpack**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasanayan ng pagpipigil sa sarili mula sa paggawa ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay may kinalaman sa pagkain, inumin, o gawaing sekswal.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa mo kapag Mahal na Araw at bawal kumain ng karne. O 'yung self-control challenge mo kapag sale sa Shopee at Lazada pero wala ka nang pera. From Spanish "abstinencia".
usage_notes: Often used in religious contexts, especially during Lent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bahagi ng Kuwaresma ang **abstinensya** sa pagkain ng karne tuwing Biyernes.","translation":"Part of Lent is the **abstinence** from eating meat on Fridays."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng matinding disiplina para sa **abstinensya**.","translation":"Strong discipline is needed for **abstinence**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paraan ng pagdadala ng isang bagay na mahigpit na nakasiksik o naiipit sa ilalim ng braso o sa kili-kili.
original_explanation: You know how you carry your laptop or a bunch of documents when you're rushing to a meeting, holding it tightly under your arm? That's 'kipit-kipit'. It’s the official way to carry your pan de sal in a brown paper bag on your way home from the bakery.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan sa paraan ng pagdadala ng isang bagay. Madalas na nagpapahiwatig ng pagmamadali o isang kaswal na paraan ng paghawak.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita ko siyang tumatakbo na **kipit-kipit** ang kanyang bag.","translation":"I saw him running with his bag **tucked under his arm**."},{"sentence":"Laging **kipit-kipit** ni lolo ang kanyang diyaryo tuwing umaga.","translation":"Grandpa always carries his newspaper **tucked under his arm** every morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Nauugnay sa industriya, mga pabrika, o malawakang produksyon ng mga kalakal.
original_explanation: Kung ang interior design ng coffee shop ay puro semento, bakal, at exposed pipes, 'yan ay industriyal ang theme. Ito rin ang tawag sa mga lugar na puro pabrika at bodega, kung saan mas amoy usok kaysa sariwang hangin. Think Valenzuela or parts of Pasig.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matatagpuan ang mga **industriyal** na parke sa labas ng kalakhang Maynila.","translation":"**Industrial** parks are located outside of metropolitan Manila."},{"sentence":"Umunlad ang bayan dahil sa pagdami ng mga pagawaang **industriyal**.","translation":"The town progressed because of the increase in **industrial** factories."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglakad o pagkilos nang hindi tuwid o balanse, karaniwan dahil sa pagkalasing, pagkahilo, o pinsala.
original_explanation: That walk of shame after three bottles of Red Horse and a round of tequila shots. It's how you move when you stand up too fast after binge-watching a series for 8 hours. The pagsuray is the universal sign for 'I'm either drunk, dizzy, or just saw my crush with someone else.'
usage_notes: Describes an unsteady movement, often due to dizziness, drunkenness, or physical weakness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kitang-kita sa kanyang **pagsuray** na siya ay lasing na.","translation":"It was obvious from his **staggering** that he was already drunk."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagsuray** ng bangka ay nagdulot ng takot sa mga pasahero.","translation":"The **wobbling** of the boat caused fear among the passengers."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa bawat sandali o iglap; sa paraang walang anumang sandali na lumilipas na hindi kasama o hindi nangyayari ang isang bagay.
etymology: Mula sa "sa", "bawat" (each), at "saglit" (moment). Ang "bawa't" ay lumang baybay ng "bawat".
original_explanation: This is the clingy version of "always". Ito 'yung level ng pagka-miss mo sa jowa mo na **sa bawa't saglit** gusto mo siyang ka-chat. Or 'yung anxiety bago ang exam na **sa bawa't saglit** feeling mo may nakalimutan kang i-review. It's about the micro-moments, the constant, unending stream of... whatever it is you're feeling or doing.
usage_notes: Mas matindi at mas madalas ang ipinapahiwatig nito kaysa sa "sa bawa't panahon". Ang modernong baybay nito ay "sa bawat saglit".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iniisip kita **sa bawa't saglit** ng aking buhay.","translation":"I think of you **every moment** of my life."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang opisyal na wikang ginagamit sa pagtuturo at pag-aaral sa loob ng mga paaralan at iba pang institusyong pang-edukasyon.
etymology: Tambalang salita ng "wika" at "panturo" (mula sa salitang-ugat na "turo").
original_explanation: Ito yung lenggwahe na ginagamit ni teacher sa classroom. Kaya minsan, nosebleed ka sa Math at Science kasi bukod sa mahirap na yung subject, English pa ang wikang panturo. Tapos sa Filipino class, biglang bawal mag-English. Nakakalito, 'di ba? Parang relasyon niyo, hindi mo alam kung anong "language" ang dapat gamitin.
usage_notes: Isang mahalagang konsepto sa sistema ng edukasyon sa Pilipinas, kung saan Filipino at Ingles ang mga pangunahing wikang panturo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Ingles ay isa sa mga opisyal na **wikang panturo** sa Pilipinas.","translation":"English is one of the official **mediums of instruction** in the Philippines."},{"sentence":"May mga debate tungkol sa kung ano ang dapat na maging pangunahing **wikang panturo** sa elementarya.","translation":"There are debates about what should be the primary **medium of instruction** in elementary school."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng ugali o katangiang tulad ng sa isang hayop; mabangis, walang awa, o hindi makatao.
original_explanation: This is how you describe someone who cuts in line at the MRT, or that officemate who eats your baon from the fridge. It's behavior that's so uncivilized, you just have to say, 'Grabe, malahayop ang ugali!' It's the opposite of 'maka-Diyos, maka-tao, makakalikasan.'
usage_notes: A strong, negative descriptor for behavior that is considered savage, cruel, or lacking in human decency.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **malahayop** na krimen ang naganap sa kanilang lugar.","translation":"An **inhumane** crime happened in their area."},{"sentence":"Ikinagalit ng lahat ang kanyang **malahayop** na pagtrato sa mga aso.","translation":"Everyone was angered by his **beastly** treatment of the dogs."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng tela o kasuotan gamit ang sinulid at isang espesyal na karayom na may kawit sa dulo, na tinatawag na gantsilyo.
original_explanation: This is what your lola does while watching her favorite noontime show. It's the OG DIY, turning a simple ball of yarn into coasters, beanies, or even a cute amigurumi character. It’s a hobby that requires patience, something most of us scrolling through TikTok don't have.
usage_notes: A specific type of needlework, different from 'manahi' (to sew) or 'magburda' (to embroider).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natuto siyang **maggantsilyo** para gumawa ng sarili niyang mga damit.","translation":"She learned to **crochet** to make her own clothes."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paghihiwalay ng mga sangkap sa isang likido sa pamamagitan ng piling pagsingaw (evaporation) at pagpapalamig (condensation).
original_explanation: This is the science-y way of making things pure. It's how lambanog is made from tuba, or how you get essential oils for your diffuser. Metaphorically, it's what you do to your thoughts after a chaotic day—you distill them down to the most important lesson. Or you just drink the distilled lambanog. Your choice.
usage_notes: A scientific or technical term, but also used in the context of traditional liquor making (e.g., lambanog).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marunong si Lolo na **magdistila** ng tuba para gawing lambanog.","translation":"Grandpa knows how **to distill** coconut wine to make lambanog."},{"sentence":"Sa laboratoryo, natutunan naming **magdistila** ng tubig.","translation":"In the laboratory, we learned **to distill** water."}]

translation: to hide; to keep; to conceal
meaning_filipino: Ilagay sa isang lugar na hindi makikita o malalaman ng iba; ilihim.
original_explanation: The universal command for when visitors suddenly arrive and the house is a mess. Also, what you do with your feelings for your crush ("Itago mo na lang 'yan, bes, 'di ka naman crush niyan"). It's the Filipino art of "out of sight, out of mind," whether it's clutter, a snack you don't want to share, or your marupok heart.
usage_notes: Very common word. Can refer to hiding physical objects, secrets, or emotions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Itago** mo ang iyong pitaka sa ligtas na lugar.","translation":"**Keep** your wallet in a safe place."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **itago** ang tunay niyang nararamdaman, ngunit halata pa rin sa kanyang mga mata.","translation":"She tried **to hide** her true feelings, but it was still obvious in her eyes."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-ingay o pagsasalita nang mabilis, tuluy-tuloy, at kadalasang walang katuturan, na maihahambing sa tunog ng manok.
etymology: Malamang na onomatopoeic o hango sa tunog na nililikha.
original_explanation: Imagine your tita sa chismisan, 'yung type na parang machine gun ang bibig. 'Yun ang taltak. It's the sound of nonstop, often pointless, chatter. Parang manok na putak nang putak. Can also describe the clucking sound of a chicken.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang isang taong sobrang madaldal o maingay magsalita. Maihahalintulad sa 'satsat' o 'daldal'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **taltak** nang **taltak** diyan, wala namang nakikinig sa iyo.","translation":"Don't just **chatter** on and on there, no one is listening to you."},{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **taltak** ng mga manok nang papalapit na ako sa kanilang kulungan.","translation":"I heard the **clucking** of the chickens as I approached their coop."}]

translation: full, whole, complete (of a time period)
meaning_filipino: Ganap o buo ang bilang o sukat, karaniwang ginagamit para sa panahon o edad.
original_explanation: The word you use when you want to add emphasis to a duration. "Isang taong **singkad**" isn't just one year, it's a *whole solid year*. It's like telling your boss you've rendered "8 hours **singkad**," meaning you didn't take a 3-hour lunch break. It's the opposite of "Filipino time."
usage_notes: Madalas itong kasunod ng isang yunit ng panahon, gaya ng 'taon', 'buwan', o 'araw'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang buwang **singkad** siyang hindi umuwi sa kanilang bahay.","translation":"For a **full** month, he did not go home to their house."},{"sentence":"Naghintay ako roon nang dalawang oras na **singkad**.","translation":"I waited there for two **whole** hours."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maselang tela na gawa sa sinulid o hibla sa isang bukas na padron na animo'y sapot, na karaniwang ginagamit bilang palamuti sa damit, kurtina, at iba pa.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na "puntas" (points, tips, lace).
original_explanation: That fancy, frilly, see-through fabric on your lola's bestida, your tita's curtains, or your... uh... 'special occasion' underwear. It's the go-to material to make anything look more delicate, vintage, or 'maarte'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang damit pangkasal ay may magandang disenyong **puntas**.","translation":"Her wedding dress has a beautiful **lace** design."},{"sentence":"Naglagay siya ng **puntas** sa laylayan ng kurtina para gumanda.","translation":"She put **lace** on the hem of the curtain to make it look nice."}]

translation: to rummage through; to dig up
meaning_filipino: Ang masinsinang paghalungkat o paghahanap sa isang lalagyan, bunton ng mga bagay, o lugar upang mahanap ang isang partikular na bagay.
etymology: From 'kalkal' (to dig, to scratch at), with the 'bu-' prefix intensifying the action, and the '-in' suffix making it an object-focused verb.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa mo sa drawer mo 'pag hinahanap mo 'yung charger na "hiniram" ng kapatid mo. Or 'yung ginagawa ng nanay mo sa bag mo 'pag may "hinahanap" siyang something. It's chaotic, messy searching. Also, what chismosas do to your past.
usage_notes: Implies a more intense and thorough rummaging than just 'kalkalin' or 'halungkatin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **bukalkalin** ang mga gamit ko!","translation":"Don't **rummage through** my things!"},{"sentence":"Kinailangan niyang **bukalkalin** ang lumang baul para mahanap ang litrato ng kanyang lola.","translation":"He had to **dig through** the old trunk to find his grandmother's picture."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tunog na nalilikha ng marahas na paglabas ng hangin sa ilong, na karaniwang nagpapahiwatig ng galit, pagkayamot, o pagsisikap, tulad ng sa hayop o makina.
etymology: Likely a reduplication or intensification of 'singa', emphasizing the sound.
original_explanation: This is the sound a bull makes before it charges, or what your boss does when you submit your report late. It's an angry, forceful exhale through the nose. It's the 'hmpf!' sound effect in real life. Think of a wild boar, a snake, or even an old, faulty steam pipe.
usage_notes: Can be a noun (the sound itself) or a verb ('sumingasing' - to make the sound). It implies more force and often anger or aggression compared to 'singa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **singasing** ng ahas sa damuhan kaya't napatakbo ako.","translation":"I heard the **hiss** of the snake in the grass so I ran."},{"sentence":"**Sumingasing** ang kalabaw sa galit nang guluhin ito.","translation":"The water buffalo **snorted** in anger when it was disturbed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng kawayan o tubo sa pagitan ng dalawang buko o "nodes".
original_explanation: You know how a bamboo stalk is made of sections? One of those sections, the smooth part between the bumpy rings (buko), is a `bias`. It's a fundamental unit of bamboo construction, literally.
usage_notes: Specific to plants with segmented stems like bamboo and sugarcane.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang isang **bias** ng kawayan para gawing lalagyan ng tubig.","translation":"He used a **segment** of bamboo as a water container."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bilang na katumbas ng tatlong sampu; tatlumpu (30).
original_explanation: The Spanish number for 30, often used when talking about money ("**Treinta** pesos") or age ("**Treinta** anyos na ako!"). It’s what you say when you want to sound a bit more formal or old-school than just saying "thirty". It’s also the age when your Titas start asking, "Kailan ka ikakasal?" with alarming frequency.
usage_notes: Commonly used for counting money, telling time, and stating age, often interchangeably with the native Tagalog 'tatlumpu'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bayad po sa kaniya ay **treinta** pesos.","translation":"The payment for him is **thirty** pesos."},{"sentence":"Ipagdiriwang niya ang kanyang **treinta** anyos na kaarawan sa susunod na buwan.","translation":"She will celebrate her **thirtieth** birthday next month."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng magaan at buhaghag na bato na nabuo mula sa bula ng lava na mabilis lumamig. Ito ay may mga butas at karaniwang ginagamit na pang-alis ng kalyo o libag.
etymology: Mula sa "bato" (stone) at "buga" (to spew, eject), na tumutukoy sa pinagmulan nitong bulkaniko.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'pang-hilod.' That lightweight, hole-y stone your lola uses to scrub the life (and kalyo) out of your feet. It's a volcanic rock that decided to have an identity crisis and become a beauty tool. Also known as 'batong pomes'.
usage_notes: Ang anyong walang gitling, `batong buga`, ay karaniwan din. Kasingkahulugan nito ang `batong pomes`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha si nanay ng **batong-buga** para ikuskos sa kanyang mga sakong.","translation":"Mother got a **pumice stone** to scrub her heels."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging walang kasama; ang pagiging bukod-tangi o kaisa-isa.
original_explanation: The default status of your single friend during Valentine's season. Or when you're the only one in the office who didn't get the memo to wear pink. 'Bakit ka nag-iisa?' is the ultimate tita question that's part concern, part chismis.
usage_notes: Can mean 'to be alone' or 'to be the one and only'. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay **nag-iisa** sa bahay nang dumating ang bagyo.","translation":"He was **alone** in the house when the storm arrived."},{"sentence":"**Nag-iisa** lang ang tulad niya sa buhay ko.","translation":"There is **only one** like her in my life."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na naglalaro ng volleyball, partikular na bilang isang miyembro ng isang koponan.
etymology: Blend of Tagalog "balibol" (from English "volleyball") and Spanish suffix "-ista".
original_explanation: Your friendly neighborhood volleyball player! Mula sa UAAP superstars hanggang sa mga tito at tita na naglalaro sa covered court ng barangay. Sila 'yung mga laging may 'pasa' (bruise) sa braso at malalakas pumalo. The term is a fun, Pinoy-fied way of saying 'volleyball player', mixing 'balibol' (volleyball) and the Spanish suffix '-ista'.
usage_notes: A common colloquial term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Alyssa Valdez ay isang sikat na **balibulista** sa Pilipinas.","translation":"Alyssa Valdez is a famous **volleyball player** in the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Puno ng mga **balibulista** ang sports complex tuwing Sabado.","translation":"The sports complex is full of **volleyball players** every Saturday."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang prinsipyo, batas, o katotohanan na siyang ginagawang batayan o pundasyon ng isang argumento, paniniwala, o sistema.
original_explanation: The 'resibo' of your argument. It's the 'because' part of your explanation, the solid ground you're standing on before you make your point. Kung sa thesis, ito 'yung RRL (Review of Related Literature) mo. It's not just any foundation, it's the foundation you are *currently* using to build your case, your project, or your life choices.
usage_notes: This is the progressive noun form, emphasizing an ongoing reliance on a basis. The root 'salig' means basis or foundation. 'Saligang Batas' is the Constitution.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tiwala sa isa't isa ang **pinagsasaligan** ng kanilang matibay na samahan.","translation":"Mutual trust is the **foundation** of their strong relationship."},{"sentence":"Ano ang **pinagsasaligan** mo sa iyong mga akusasyon?","translation":"What is the **basis** for your accusations?"}]

translation: to have something dried; to cause to dry
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng isang bagay sa ilalim ng araw o sa anumang paraan upang maalis ang taglay nitong tubig o pagkabasa.
original_explanation: This is the OG Filipino way of food preservation or doing laundry. Think of your lola leaving fish out in the sun to make daing, or your mom telling you to hang the clothes outside. "Nak, **magpatuyot** ka na ng mga sinampay bago umulan!" (Kid, go dry the laundry before it rains!). It's the solar-powered method for everything.
usage_notes: Commonly used for drying clothes, food (like fish or fruit), or anything wet.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagbilad sila ng isda sa tabing-dagat upang **magpatuyot**.","translation":"They laid fish on the seashore to **have them dried**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magpatuyot** ng sahig bago may madulas.","translation":"We need to **dry** the floor before someone slips."}]

meaning_filipino: Batay sa lohika, katwiran, at maayos na pag-iisip; hindi batay sa emosyon.
original_explanation: Yung kaibigan mong hindi nagpapadala sa "feelings" lang kapag nag-dedecide. Siya yung hindi bibili ng 11.11 sale item na hindi niya kailangan. "Be rasyonal naman," sabi niya sa'yo habang pa-check out ka na ng 20 items.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa pormal na usapan, lalo na sa akademya at pilosopiya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating gumawa ng isang **rasyonal** na desisyon para sa ikabubuti ng lahat.","translation":"We need to make a **rational** decision for the good of everyone."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang paliwanag ay hindi **rasyonal** at puno ng emosyon.","translation":"His explanation was not **rational** and was full of emotion."}]

translation: that is to say; in other words; namely
meaning_filipino: Isang pariralang ginagamit upang magbigay ng paglilinaw, paliwanag, o halimbawa sa naunang sinabi.
original_explanation: The ultimate "let me rephrase that for you" in formal Filipino. It’s the phrase your Lolo uses when he's about to drop some serious life wisdom. It's the equivalent of saying "to be specific..." or "what I mean is..." but with a PhD in Filipino literature.
usage_notes: Napakapormal, madalas matatagpuan sa mga legal na dokumento, lumang panitikan, at pormal na talumpati.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marami siyang katangian na hinahangaan ko, **alalaong baga'y** ang kanyang pagiging matapat at masipag.","translation":"He has many qualities I admire, **namely**, his honesty and diligence."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasalaysay ng isang kuwento o pangyayari sa isang tao o grupo.
etymology: From `mag-` (verb prefix) + `kuwento` (story), which is from Spanish `cuento`.
original_explanation: The verbal form of 'spilling the tea.' This is what your chismosa tita does best. From narrating the latest episode of a K-drama to giving a play-by-play of the neighbors' argument, 'magkkwento' is the foundation of all good (and bad) conversations.
usage_notes: This is a very common colloquial spelling and pronunciation. The formal, standard spelling is `magkuwento`. The double 'k' reflects the glottal stop that occurs between `mag-` and a root word starting with a vowel or 'k', as in /mag-ʔkuwento/.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umupo ka at **magkkwento** ako tungkol sa bakasyon ko sa Palawan.","translation":"Sit down and I **will tell a story** about my vacation in Palawan."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **magkkwento** ng mga katatakutan tuwing brownout.","translation":"He likes **to tell** scary **stories** during a power outage."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa teolohiyang Katoliko, isang kalagayan o proseso ng paglilinis kung saan ang mga kaluluwa ng mga namatay sa estado ng grasya ay sumasailalim sa paglilinis upang makamit ang kabanalan na kinakailangan upang makapasok sa langit.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're waiting for your 13th-month pay. You know it's coming, but the wait is agony. It's the ultimate 'waiting room'—not quite hell, but definitely not heaven yet. Also, the state of your love life when you're 'seeing each other' but have no label.
usage_notes: Primarily a religious term, but often used metaphorically to describe a state of suffering or waiting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayon sa turo, ang mga kaluluwa sa **purgatoryo** ay nangangailangan ng ating mga panalangin.","translation":"According to the teaching, the souls in **purgatory** need our prayers."},{"sentence":"Para sa akin, ang pag-commute sa EDSA araw-araw ay isang **purgatoryo**.","translation":"For me, commuting on EDSA every day is a **purgatory**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pang-ukol na tumutukoy sa paksa o bagay na pinag-uusapan o tinutukoy.
original_explanation: This is the formal way of saying 'about.' It's the word you use in your thesis paper, a legal document, or when you're trying to sound super serious in an email to your boss. 'Ang email na ito ay patungkol sa ating team building...' is the corporate way of saying 'Hey, about the team building...'
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'tungkol sa.' 'Patungkol' feels slightly more formal and is often followed by 'kay' (for people) or 'sa' (for things/places).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroon siyang tanong **patungkol** sa bagong patakaran.","translation":"He has a question **regarding** the new policy."},{"sentence":"Ang liham ay **patungkol** sa kanyang pagbibitiw sa tungkulin.","translation":"The letter is **about** his resignation from the position."}]

translation: to perform; to present; to stage
meaning_filipino: Magpakita ng isang palabas o presentasyon sa harap ng mga manonood, karaniwan sa isang entablado.
original_explanation: This is the verb for your 'artista' moment. When you sing on a stage, act in a play, or dance in a competition, you 'nagtatanghal'. It's about putting on a show. Even a formal work presentation can be described as 'pagtatanghal'. It's showtime!
usage_notes: Strongly associated with theater, music, arts, and public presentations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aming grupo ay **magtatanghal** ng isang sayaw para sa pagdiriwang.","translation":"Our group will **perform** a dance for the celebration."},{"sentence":"Sila ay **nagtanghal** ng isang dula-dulaan tungkol sa buhay ni Rizal.","translation":"They **staged** a short play about the life of Rizal."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagpapatawa sa pamamagitan ng pag-arte, pagkukuwento, o pagbibiro, lalo na bilang isang propesyon.
original_explanation: The person whose job is to make people laugh, like Michael V. or a stand-up comic in a bar. It's also your wittiest friend in the barkada, the one who always has a punchline ready for any situation. The designated "taga-sira ng seryosong usapan."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang tanyag na **komedyante** si Vice Ganda sa Pilipinas.","translation":"Vice Ganda is a famous **comedian** in the Philippines."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng pinaniniwalaang may masamang kapangyarihan o gumagamit ng itim na mahika; isang masamang-ugali o matandang babae.
original_explanation: Originally a witch from folklore, but now it's what you call the evil kontrabida in a teleserye, your terrifyingly strict manager, or the chismosa neighbor who seems to have a curse for every occasion. It can be a serious insult ("Ang sama ng ugali mo, para kang bruha!") or a playful jab among friends ("Hoy bruha, nasaan ka na?").
usage_notes: Can range from being a serious insult to a term of endearment among close female friends, depending on context and tone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa mga lumang kuwento, ang **bruha** ay lumilipad gamit ang walis tingting.","translation":"In old stories, the **witch** flies using a broomstick."},{"sentence":"Tara na, mga **bruha**, mag-kape tayo!","translation":"Let's go, you **witches** (girls), let's have coffee!"}]

meaning_filipino: Mga tuyong kahoy, sanga, o iba pang bagay na madaling magliyab na ginagamit bilang pampasimula ng apoy.
etymology: 'Saeng' is an old Tagalog word for kindling. 'Sasaeng' might be a variant or a derivative.
original_explanation: The OG fire starter, before lighters and gas stoves became a thing. This is what you gather in the province to cook rice over an open fire. It's the small, dry twigs and wood chips that get the party started for the bigger logs. The unsung hero of many lutong-bahay.
usage_notes: This is a very rare or archaic word. Most people would use 'panggatong' or 'kahoy na panggatong'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-ipon kami ng **sasaeng** para sa aming pagluluto sa bakuran.","translation":"We gathered **kindling** for our cooking in the yard."},{"sentence":"Dapat tuyo ang **sasaeng** para madaling sumiklab ang apoy.","translation":"The **firewood** must be dry so the fire starts easily."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyon na nagpapahayag ng matinding pagkagulat o hindi makapaniwalang reaksyon, na binibigyang-diin ng salitang "talaga".
original_explanation: This is the leveled-up version of "omg". The "talaga" adds a layer of genuine, no-holds-barred shock. Hindi ito yung "omg" na pang-chat lang. Ito yung "omg" na napapasigaw ka sa office pantry kasi nalaman mo na engaged na yung ex mo sa katrabaho niyo.
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang ipahayag ang mas matinding emosyon kaysa sa 'omg' lamang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**OMG talaga**, ang ganda ng performance niya kagabi!","translation":"**OMG really**, her performance last night was amazing!"}]

translation: to be able to look at; to be examined
meaning_filipino: Ang magkaroon ng pagkakataong makita, suriin, o pagmasdan ang isang bagay o tao.
original_explanation: This is what you say when your mom asks you to check if the sinigang is boiling yet ('Matingnan mo nga kung kumukulo na'). It's also what the doctor does to you ('Matingnan nga ang lalamunan mo'). It's the verb for 'let me see' or 'to be checked.'
usage_notes: A very common verb used in requests to check or look at something. It's the potential/ability form of 'tingnan' (to look at).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puwede bang **matingnan** ang iyong ginagawang proyekto?","translation":"Can I **take a look at** the project you are working on?"},{"sentence":"Dalhin mo sa mekaniko ang kotse para **matingnan** kung ano ang sira.","translation":"Bring the car to the mechanic so it can **be examined** to see what's broken."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na namatayan ng ama; walang ama.
original_explanation: This is a specific flavor of 'ulila'. While 'ulila' is the general term, 'ulila sa ama' specifies that the father is the one who passed away. It's often used to describe the specific challenges or emotional weight of growing up without a dad.
usage_notes: A common phrase used to be more specific than the general 'ulila'. The counterpart is 'ulila sa ina' (motherless).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lumaki siyang **ulila sa ama** mula pa noong limang taong gulang.","translation":"He grew up **fatherless** since he was five years old."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang akda, tulad ng libro, magasin, o dyaryo, na inilimbag at ipinamahagi sa publiko.
original_explanation: Anything that's printed and released, from your school's super serious literary folio ('Ang Folio') to the latest chismis magazine you pretend not to read at the salon. In the digital age, this now includes blogs and online news sites.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang tula ay napasama sa isang pambansang **publikasyon**.","translation":"Her poem was included in a national **publication**."}]

translation: to give a Christmas gift (aguinaldo) to someone
meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng aginaldo o regalo, karaniwang pera, tuwing Pasko.
original_explanation: 'Yung moment na pinakahihintay ng lahat ng bata (at isip-bata) tuwing Pasko. Ito 'yung action na ginagawa ng mga ninong at ninang—ang magbigay ng regalo o pera. 'Hoy, aginalduhan mo na 'yung inaanak mo!' ay isang battle cry sa Pinas. The verb form of receiving that crisp new bill from your tito.
usage_notes: A verb specifically used during the Christmas season. The command form is 'Aginalduhan mo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Aginalduhan** na ni Ninong ang lahat ng kanyang mga pamangkin.","translation":"Ninong already **gave Christmas gifts** to all his nieces and nephews."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **aginalduhan** ang mga bata.","translation":"Don't forget **to give gifts** to the children."}]

translation: Driver (especially of a public utility vehicle like a jeepney).
meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagmamaneho ng pampublikong sasakyan, partikular na ng dyipni.
etymology: A Filipino adaptation of the French 'chauffeur', likely via English, which has taken on a more specific, public transport context than 'tsoper'.
original_explanation: The undisputed 'hari ng kalsada' (king of the road). The one who navigates Manila's traffic jungle, collects your 'bayad po', and expertly passes the 'sukli' down a chain of passengers. Their skill is legendary, their patience... tested daily.
usage_notes: Strongly associated with jeepney drivers. While 'drayber' is a general term, 'tsuper' specifically evokes the image of a jeepney driver.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiabot po ng bayad sa **tsuper**.","translation":"Please pass the fare to the **driver**."},{"sentence":"Nagwelga ang mga **tsuper** ng dyipni.","translation":"The jeepney **drivers** went on strike."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging nakasalalay o nakabase sa isang partikular na prinsipyo, impormasyon, o pundasyon.
original_explanation: 'Yung decision mo na mag-resign, dapat mabatay sa facts, hindi lang sa chismis ng officemate mong Marites. It's like your life choices need a solid foundation, not just "sabi nila."
usage_notes: Often used in formal or academic contexts to mean "to be based on" or "to be founded upon."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang desisyon ng korte ay dapat **mabatay** sa matibay na ebidensya.","translation":"The court's decision must **be based on** solid evidence."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **mabatay** sa katotohanan ang lahat ng iyong sasabihin.","translation":"Everything you say needs to **be based on** the truth."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bahagi ng isang lungsod, lalawigan, o bansa na itinakda para sa isang partikular na layuning administratibo o politikal.
original_explanation: Ito yung area na sakop ng congressman mo. O kaya yung school district. Basically, a designated area. Sa Maynila, may mga distrito tulad ng Quiapo at Binondo, bawat isa may sariling vibe at specialty. Parang sa friend group, may assigned roles: ang 'distrito' ng mga komedyante, 'distrito' ng mga seryoso.
usage_notes: Commonly used in political and administrative contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nangangampanya ang kongresista sa lahat ng barangay sa kanyang **distrito**.","translation":"The congressman is campaigning in all the barangays in his **district**."},{"sentence":"Ang Binondo ay kilala bilang isa sa mga pinakamatandang Chinatown sa buong mundo at isang makasaysayang **distrito** ng Maynila.","translation":"Binondo is known as one of the oldest Chinatowns in the world and a historic **district** of Manila."}]

meaning_filipino: Paglalarawan sa isang bagay, karaniwan ay pagkain, na naluto nang husto hanggang sa maging malutong at bahagyang sunog o kulay-kape.
original_explanation: How you like your pandesal in the morning, or how your skin feels after a day trip to the beach without sunblock. 'Friend, tustado ka na!' It's that perfect crispy, almost-burnt state. Can also mean being drunk.
usage_notes: Often used for food like bread, garlic, or meat. Can also be used colloquially to describe being sunburnt or drunk.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko ng bawang na **tustado** sa sinangag.","translation":"I like **toasted** garlic in my fried rice."},{"sentence":"Naging **tustado** ang balat niya dahil sa pagbibilad sa araw.","translation":"His skin became **sunburnt** from staying under the sun."}]

translation: to plead; to ask for earnestly
meaning_filipino: Makiusap o humiling nang may buong pagpapakumbaba at pagsusumamo, lalo na para sa isang mahalagang bagay.
etymology: From Tagalog 'i-' (causative/instrumental prefix) + 'pamanhik' (a plea), from 'panhik' (to go up, as in going up the house to make a formal request).
original_explanation: This is more than just asking. This is 'luhod' level begging. It's the verb form of 'pamanhikan,' the traditional act of a man and his family formally asking for a woman's hand in marriage. In modern terms, it's what you do when you're trying to get your parents to let you go on a trip with friends. You don't just ask, you 'ipamanhik' your case, complete with a PowerPoint presentation on why you deserve it.
usage_notes: Carries a strong connotation of humility, formality, and deep sincerity. Most strongly associated with 'pamanhikan' or asking for a hand in marriage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tanging hiling na kanyang **ipinamamanhik** ay ang kapatawaran ng kanyang ama.","translation":"The only wish he is **earnestly pleading** for is his father's forgiveness."},{"sentence":"Sinama niya ang kanyang mga magulang upang **ipamanhik** ang kamay ng kanyang kasintahan.","translation":"He brought his parents with him **to formally ask for** his girlfriend's hand."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging sira, depekto, o pinsala; maaari ring tumukoy sa pagkawala ng dangal o puri.
etymology: From "sira" (broken, damaged) with the circumfix "ka-...-an" which creates a noun indicating a state, condition, or collective concept.
original_explanation: This is 'sira' in noun form. It's the damage after the storm, the defect in your Shopee order, or the 'dishonor on you, dishonor on your cow' moment. It's the consequence of something breaking, whether it's a thing, a plan, or your reputation.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical damage or abstract damage like reputation. The specific meaning is often clarified by context or a following phrase (e.g., 'kasiraan ng puri', 'kasiraan ng ulo').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-iwan ng matinding **kasiraan** sa mga pananim ang nagdaang bagyo.","translation":"The recent typhoon left severe **damage** on the crops."},{"sentence":"Ito ay isang malaking **kasiraan** sa kanyang magandang pangalan.","translation":"This is a huge **stain** on his good name."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panlabas na takip o bahagi ng katawan ng tao o hayop; ang panlabas na bahagi ng prutas o gulay.
original_explanation: The original 'casing' for your body. It's what gets dry when you don't use lotion, what gets dark under the summer sun, and what you spend a fortune on with all those skincare products from Korea. Also applies to the 'skin' of fruits, like balat ng saging (banana peel).
usage_notes: Very common word. The stress is on the first syllable. It can refer to human/animal skin, or the peel/rind of fruits and vegetables.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Makinis ang **balat** ng sanggol.","translation":"The baby's **skin** is smooth."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong itapon ang **balat** ng patatas; masarap itong iprito.","translation":"Don't throw away the potato **peel**; it's delicious when fried."}]

translation: to cause to win; to win for someone
meaning_filipino: Maging sanhi ng pagkapanalo; manalo para sa kapakanan o karangalan ng iba.
original_explanation: This is the verb for clutch moments. When you're the designated player to take the final shot in a basketball game, your team is counting on you to 'ipanalo' the game.
