It's also used when you're fighting for something, like arguing a case or trying to win a bid. 'Ipanalo mo 'to para sa bayan!' is the ultimate hype line.
usage_notes: Can mean to win something (causative) or to win *for* someone (benefactive).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sikaping **ipanalo** ang kaso para makamit ang hustisya.","translation":"Strive **to win** the case to achieve justice."},{"sentence":"Gagawin niya ang lahat para **ipanalo** ang puso ng dalaga.","translation":"He will do everything **to win** the young lady's heart."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lahat ng bagay, lugar, at kondisyon na nakapalibot sa isang tao o bagay.
etymology: Nagmula sa unlaping 'pa-' na nagpapahiwatig ng sirkumperensiya at salitang-ugat na 'ligid' (sa palibot).
original_explanation: Your immediate vicinity. Kung nasa office ka, 'yan 'yung cubicle mo, 'yung maingay mong katabi, at 'yung amoy ng kape. Kung nasa bahay ka, 'yan 'yung mga tambak na labahin at 'yung pusa mong natutulog sa laptop mo. Everything that makes up your current bubble.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin para sa pisikal na kapaligiran o sa makasagisag na paraan para sa sosyal na kapaligiran.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Panatilihing malinis ang ating **paligid**.","translation":"Let's keep our **surroundings** clean."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa mga tao sa iyong **paligid**.","translation":"Be careful with the people in your **environment**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang nagpapahayag ng damdamin ng pagkairita, pagkayamot, o pagkabuwisit sa isang tao, bagay, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: A classic Filipino expression for when you're mildly to moderately annoyed. It's the verbal equivalent of an eye-roll. Your sibling took the remote? "Kainis!" The internet is slow? "Kainis!" It's less intense than "Bwisit!" but gets the point across that your patience is wearing thin.
usage_notes: Often used as a standalone interjection. "Nakakainis" is the more formal adjectival form meaning "annoying".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kainis**! Naiwan ko na naman ang payong ko.","translation":"**How annoying**! I left my umbrella again."},{"sentence":"Talagang **kainis** ang mabagal na serbisyo.","translation":"Slow service is really **irritating**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng ibong-tubig na karaniwang inaalagaan para sa itlog at karne nito.
original_explanation: The OG source of 'balut'. Before it became a test of courage for tourists, it was just a regular pato waddling around the farm. Not to be confused with the Tagalog word for 'hit' or 'popular', which is 'patok'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paborito niyang alaga ay ang puting **pato** sa likod-bahay.","translation":"His favorite pet is the white **duck** in the backyard."},{"sentence":"Mas masarap daw ang itlog ng **pato** kaysa sa manok.","translation":"They say **duck** eggs are more delicious than chicken eggs."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, karaniwang pera, na ibinibigay bilang tulong o donasyon sa mga mahihirap o nangangailangan.
original_explanation: That barya you keep in your car's ash tray or coin purse, specifically for the kids at the stoplight. It’s your 'just-in-case' fund for good karma. 'Wala akong **panlimos** ngayon, ser, pasensya na.'
usage_notes: Can refer to the act of giving alms or the item (usually money) used for it.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtabi siya ng barya para may maibigay na **panlimos**.","translation":"She set aside coins to have **alms** to give."},{"sentence":"Ang pagbibigay ng **panlimos** ay isang paraan ng pagtulong sa kapwa.","translation":"Giving **alms** is one way to help others."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katawagan, na madalas may bahid ng panunuya, para sa isang taong hindi Koreano na labis ang pagkahumaling sa kultura ng Timog Korea, partikular sa K-pop at K-drama.
etymology: From English slang 'Koreaboo,' a portmanteau of 'Korea' and 'weeaboo' (a term for an obsessive fan of Japanese culture).
original_explanation: You know that friend who suddenly calls everyone 'oppa,' eats samgyupsal three times a week, and whose life goal is to marry Lee Min Ho? They're called a **Koreaboo**. It's more than just being a fan; it's a lifestyle obsession. Sometimes, they know more Korean words than deep Tagalog words.
usage_notes: A modern slang term, often used with a slightly negative or teasing connotation. It's a very specific cultural term related to the Hallyu wave.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Grabe, naging **Koreaboo** na talaga si Anna mula nang mapanood niya ang 'Crash Landing on You'.","translation":"Wow, Anna has really become a **Koreaboo** ever since she watched 'Crash Landing on You'."},{"sentence":"Hindi naman masamang maging fan, pero iba na kapag isa ka nang **Koreaboo** na kinakalimutan na ang pagka-Pilipino mo.","translation":"It's not bad to be a fan, but it's different when you're a **Koreaboo** who's already forgetting your Filipino identity."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ari-arian, pera, o regalo na ibinibigay ng pamilya ng babaing ikakasal sa pamilya ng lalaki bilang bahagi ng kasunduan sa kasal.
original_explanation: This is some old-school Maria Clara stuff. It's the property or money the bride's family gives to the groom's family. Today, the best 'dote' you can give is probably a stable job, good credit score, and no utang.
usage_notes: Isang makalumang termino na hindi na karaniwang ginagamit sa mga modernong pag-uusap ngunit lumalabas sa mga tekstong pangkasaysayan at panitikan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Noong unang panahon, malaking **dote** ang kailangan para maikasal sa isang prinsesa.","translation":"In the old days, a large **dowry** was needed to marry a princess."},{"sentence":"Sa nobela, ang **dote** ng pangunahing tauhan ay isang malawak na lupain.","translation":"In the novel, the protagonist's **dowry** was a vast piece of land."}]

translation: to be obliged, to be forced (by circumstance or duty)
meaning_filipino: Ang mapilitang gawin ang isang bagay dahil sa tungkulin, pangangailangan, o utang na loob.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're invited to a party you don't want to go to, but you have to show up because it's your boss's kid's birthday. 'Napilitan lang.' You're not exactly forced at gunpoint, but social pressure, utang na loob, or your job description makes you do it. You are 'ma-ubliga'.
usage_notes: A common Taglish/Filipino word derived from Spanish. It implies a sense of duty or social pressure rather than physical force.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi ka **mauubliga** na sumama kung ayaw mo.","translation":"Don't worry, you won't **be obliged** to come if you don't want to."},{"sentence":"**Nauubliga** akong tulungan siya dahil sa aming pinagsamahan.","translation":"I **am obliged** to help him because of our shared history."}]

translation: to be made up; to be fictional
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging bunga lamang ng isip, kathang-isip, o hindi totoo.
original_explanation: Ito yung status ng lovelife mo ayon sa mga kaibigan mong mapang-asar. "Uy, may ka-holding hands ka daw kahapon!" tapos sasabihin mo, "Sana all, pero magkata-kata lang 'yan." It's the polite way of saying "That's a lie," "It's just make-believe," or "You're just making that up."
usage_notes: Often used to dismiss rumors or deny something as mere fiction or gossip.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga kuwento tungkol sa aswang ay **magkata-kata** lamang.","translation":"The stories about the aswang are **just made up**."},{"sentence":"**Magkata-kata** lang ang sinabi niyang nanalo siya sa lotto.","translation":"What he said about winning the lottery was **just a fabrication**."}]

translation: to make something hit; to aim at
meaning_filipino: Asintahin o tiyaking tamaan ang isang target; hayaang tamaan ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the verb for when you're playing darts, basketball, or... throwing shade. "Patamain mo sa bullseye!" (Hit the bullseye!). But it's also used for "parinig" or subtle insults. When someone posts a vague "hugot" line on Facebook that's obviously for you, they're trying to `patamain` you. It's about making sure your shot, whether a ball or a word, hits its intended target.
usage_notes: Can be literal (physical impact) or figurative (verbal jab, indirect remark). The figurative sense is very common in social contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **patamain** ang bola sa ring mula sa malayo.","translation":"He tried to **make** the ball **hit** the ring from afar."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi ikaw ang pinapa**tamain** niya sa kanyang mga sinasabi.","translation":"Don't worry, you're not the one he's **aiming at** with his words."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginagamit bilang isang magiliw na pagbati sa isang panauhin o bagong dating, o bilang karaniwang tugon sa isang pasasalamat.
original_explanation: The first word you see on a doormat and the last word you say after someone says 'thank you'. In the Philippines, it's often interchanged with 'walang anuman', but saying 'welcome' is the default setting for most city folks. Also, the title of every company's most boring onboarding presentation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Salamat sa regalo! Sabi niya, '**Welcome**!'","translation":"Thank you for the gift! He said, '**You're welcome**!'"},{"sentence":"**Welcome** sa aming munting tahanan.","translation":"**Welcome** to our humble home."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangalawang bersyon o pag-imprenta ng isang aklat o anumang nailathalang akda, na maaaring may mga pagwawasto o karagdagan.
original_explanation: Parang "Version 2.0" ng isang libro. Minsan may "director's cut" na mga chapter, or inayos lang yung mga typo from the first round. Ito yung chance ng author na sabihing, "Oops, may mali sa una, ito na yung tamang version." Parang love life, hoping for a better "second edition."
usage_notes: Used in publishing and literature.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas maganda raw ang **ikalawang limbag** ng nobela dahil may dagdag na epilogo.","translation":"They say the **second edition** of the novel is better because it has an added epilogue."}]

translation: has a crack; has an explosion/gunshot sound
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na may lamat o basag; o sa isang sitwasyon kung saan may maririnig na tunog ng pagsabog o baril.
original_explanation: This is the literal meaning. Like when you hear fireworks on New Year's Eve, 'Hala, may putok na!' Or when you inspect a glass and tell your mom, 'Ma, 'wag mo nang gamitin 'to, may putok.' It's all about cracks and bangs.
usage_notes: The meaning is highly dependent on context, distinguishing between a sound and a physical flaw. This is the literal meaning, as opposed to the colloquial term for body odor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong bilhin ang banga na iyan dahil **may-putok** sa gilid.","translation":"Don't buy that jar because it **has a crack** on the side."},{"sentence":"Ang lugar na iyon ay magulo, palaging **may-putok** sa gabi.","translation":"That place is chaotic, there are always **gunshots** at night."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang natatangi at walang katulad; ang pinaka-espesyal o bukod-tangi sa lahat.
etymology: From the superlative prefix 'pinaka-' + 'tangi' (special, only one).
original_explanation: That one person you compare all your future prospects to. The 'the one that got away' or 'the one.' Your favorite ulam that you could eat every day. The holy grail of your collection.
usage_notes: Often used in a romantic or deeply appreciative context to denote uniqueness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para sa akin, ikaw ang **pinakatangi** sa lahat.","translation":"For me, you are the **most special** of all."},{"sentence":"Iyon ang **pinakatangi** niyang alaala mula sa kanyang pagkabata.","translation":"That was his **most unique** memory from his childhood."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan sa pagkain na may maliit at mababaw na mangkok sa dulo ng isang hawakan, ginagamit sa pagsubo ng pagkain, lalo na ng mga sabaw o malalambot na pagkain.
original_explanation: The better half of the Pinoy dining power couple: Kutsara & Tinidor. You can't have sinigang, adobo with extra sauce, or champorado without it. It's the ultimate tool for maximizing the 'sabaw' experience. Life without it is just... pointless (and fork-ward).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakikuha mo nga ang **kutsara** at tinidor.","translation":"Please get the **spoon** and fork."},{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng **kutsara** para sa sinigang.","translation":"He used a **spoon** for the sinigang."}]

meaning_filipino: Maging sanhi ng pagkakaroon ng takot, pangamba, o agam-agam.
etymology: Mula sa panlaping pangkasanhi na "ika-" at sa salitang-ugat na "takot" (damdamin ng pangamba).
original_explanation: The reason you're scared. The `ikatakot` of a BPO agent is a "sup call" (supervisor call). The `ikatakot` of a student is a surprise long quiz. The `ikatakot` of someone on a diet is a Jollibee delivery ad. It's the trigger for your "ay, kabahan ka na" moment.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang pandiwang sanhi na nagpapaliwanag kung bakit nakakaramdam ng takot ang isang tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang dilim sa eskinita ang **ikatakot** ng mga bata.","translation":"The darkness in the alley is what **causes fear** in the children."},{"sentence":"Ano ang **ikatakot** mo sa pagsasabi ng totoo?","translation":"What is **causing your fear** in telling the truth?"}]

translation: full of scratches, marred by scratches
meaning_filipino: Mayroong maraming gasgas o mababaw na hiwa sa ibabaw na bahagi.
original_explanation: The state of your phone screen after you put it in the same pocket as your keys. The condition of your car's bumper after navigating EDSA. The surface of a non-stick pan after your sibling used a metal fork on it. If something is **magalos**, it's seen better days and has the battle scars to prove it.
usage_notes: Used to describe surfaces of objects. For skin, `galos` or `kalmot` is more common for the scratch itself, but `magalos` can describe a surface with many old scratches.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **magalos** ang salamin ng kanyang relo dahil sa pagkakabagsak.","translation":"The crystal of his watch became **full of scratches** after it fell."},{"sentence":"Ayaw ko nang bilhin ang mesang iyan, **magalos** na ang ibabaw.","translation":"I don't want to buy that table anymore, the surface is already **marred by scratches**."}]

translation: to pat lightly; to tap gently
meaning_filipino: Ang marahang pagpindot o pagdampi sa isang bagay o tao gamit ang dulo ng daliri.
original_explanation: It's that gentle tap you give your friend to get their attention when you see your crush walking by. Parang "psst, bes, andyan na si ano." It can also have a more... adult connotation, like a gentle, suggestive tap. Let's just say it's context-dependent, okay?
usage_notes: Often used to describe a light, repetitive tapping motion. The '-in' suffix makes it a command or an action to be done to something/someone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pikpikin** mo ang balikat niya para magising.","translation":"**Tap** his shoulder to wake him up."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pikpikin** ang mikropono, baka masira.","translation":"Don't **tap** the microphone, it might break."}]

meaning_filipino: Pakiusap o utos na gabayan, samahan, o bigyan ng direksyon ang isang tao upang hindi maligaw o magkamali.
original_explanation: Basically, 'please guide this person.' What you ask a more senior colleague to do for the new intern. Or what you silently pray when you let your friend who's bad with directions lead the way. It's a more formal version of 'pakisama' or 'pakibantayan'.
usage_notes: Has a formal and caring connotation, often used in the context of mentorship or divine guidance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa mga magulang, mahalagang **ipatnubay** ang kanilang mga anak sa tamang landas.","translation":"For parents, it is important to **have** their children **guided** on the right path."}]

translation: a shake to settle contents; overflowing
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-alog sa isang lalagyan upang maisiksik ang laman nito; pagiging siksik at umaapaw.
original_explanation: This is that final jiggle the rice vendor gives the measuring cup to make sure it's packed. It's a key part of the ultimate blessing mantra: 'siksik, liglig, at umaapaw' (packed, shaken down, and overflowing). Think of your blessings (or your GrabFood order) being so abundant that you need to shake the container to fit it all in, and it's still spilling over.
usage_notes: Almost always appears in the idiomatic expression "siksik, liglig, at umaapaw" to mean 'abundant blessings'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga biyaya niya sa buhay ay tunay na siksik, **liglig**, at umaapaw.","translation":"His blessings in life are truly packed, **shaken down**, and overflowing."},{"sentence":"Isang **liglig** pa sa kahon at siguradong magkakasya na ang lahat ng donasyon.","translation":"One more **shake** of the box and all the donations will surely fit."}]

meaning_filipino: Ibigay o ipaubaya ang isang bagay, karapatan, o sarili sa iba dahil sa pagkatalo, pag-amin, o pagpapasakop.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you're cornered in a game of tag ('Suko na ako!'). It's also that dramatic moment in action movies when the hero tells the villain to surrender the hostage. In a #hugot sense, it's finally giving up on that person who keeps leaving you on 'seen'. Time to raise the white flag, bes.
usage_notes: Ang unlaping 'i-' ay nakapokus sa bagay na isinusuko. Ang anyong nakapokus sa gumagawa ng kilos ay 'sumuko'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napilitan ang mga magnanakaw na **isuko** ang kanilang mga sarili sa mga pulis.","translation":"The thieves were forced **to surrender** themselves to the police."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **isuko** ang pangarap mo nang dahil lang sa hirap.","translation":"Don't **give up** on your dream just because of hardship."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matining at malakas na sigaw, karaniwan dahil sa takot, tuwa, o sakit.
original_explanation: The sound you make when you see a cockroach fly. Or when your favorite K-pop idol looks at the camera. Or when you see the bill after a fancy dinner. It's that sharp, ear-piercing scream that communicates pure, unadulterated emotion.
usage_notes: Often used with verbs like 'tumili' (to shriek). The noun 'tilis' refers to the sound itself, which is sharper and higher-pitched than a 'sigaw' (shout).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malakas na **tilis** ang narinig mula sa loob ng horror house.","translation":"A loud **shriek** was heard from inside the horror house."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi bihasa o hindi nakasanayan sa isang gawain; walang sapat na karanasan.
original_explanation: Yung first day mo sa work at hindi mo alam paano gamitin 'yung coffee machine. O 'yung mayaman mong kaibigan na di-sanay mag-commute. It's the state of being a "newbie" or "noob" at something, from a job to life's little hardships.
usage_notes: Isang tambalang salita na gumagamit ng panangging 'di'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahihirapan sa una ang mga trabahador na **di-sanay** sa mabibigat na gawain.","translation":"Workers who are **unaccustomed** to heavy tasks will have a hard time at first."},{"sentence":"Halata sa kilos niya na siya ay **di-sanay** sa paggamit ng computer.","translation":"It's obvious from his actions that he is **inexperienced** in using a computer."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking empleyado sa isang restawran o kainan na ang trabaho ay kumuha ng order ng mga kostumer at maghatid ng pagkain at inumin.
original_explanation: Sila yung mga "Sir/Ma'am, ano po order nila?" experts. The unsung heroes of your date night or family lunch. Sila ang may hawak ng iyong kapalaran—kung gaano kabilis darating ang sisig mo. Master nila ang art of balancing a tray full of plates while navigating a crowded restaurant. Huwag kalimutang mag-thank you at mag-tip!
usage_notes: Malawakang ginagamit ang salitang Ingles. Ang katumbas sa Tagalog na "tagapagsilbi" ay mas pormal at hindi gaanong ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinawag ko ang **waiter** para humingi ng isa pang baso ng tubig.","translation":"I called the **waiter** to ask for another glass of water."},{"sentence":"Magalang ang mga **waiter** sa restawran na iyon.","translation":"The **waiters** at that restaurant are polite."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao o entidad na may umiiral na obligasyong pinansyal o utang sa iba.
original_explanation: The default status of every adult during "petsa de peligro." Ito 'yung estado mo 'pag may utang ka sa Bumbay, sa credit card, sa kaibigan, o sa ShopeePay Later. You're not just 'may utang', you are in a *state* of being indebted. May kasamang bigat sa dibdib.
usage_notes: This phrase emphasizes the state or condition of being in debt, rather than just the simple fact of having a debt.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sinumang **may-pagkakautang** ay dapat magsikap na bayaran ito.","translation":"Anyone who is **indebted** must strive to pay it off."},{"sentence":"Mahirap pagkatiwalaan ang taong laging **may-pagkakautang** at hindi nagbabayad.","translation":"It's hard to trust a person who is always **in debt** and doesn't pay."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging matatag, matigas, at hindi madaling masira o magupo. Tumutukoy ito sa pisikal na lakas o sa katatagan ng loob.
original_explanation: The secret ingredient in your lola's old Nokia phone, the 'Made in Marikina' shoes that last longer than your relationships, and the spirit of an OFW working three jobs. Tibay is that legendary Filipino resilience and durability. It’s when something—or someone—can take a beating (from typhoons, economic crises, or family drama) and still stand strong. 'Matibay!' is the highest compliment you can pay to a chair, a friendship, or a person's character.
usage_notes: A very common and versatile word. The adjective form is 'matibay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Subok na ang **tibay** ng mga produktong gawa sa Pilipinas.","translation":"The **durability** of products made in the Philippines has been tested."},{"sentence":"Kahanga-hanga ang **tibay** ng kanyang loob sa harap ng mga pagsubok.","translation":"The **strength** of his character in the face of challenges is admirable."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng nilalaman sa internet na ang pangunahing layunin ay akitin ang mga mambabasa na pindutin ang isang partikular na link, kadalasan sa pamamagitan ng mapanlinlang o sensasyonal na pamagat.
original_explanation: The YouTube title 'NAGHIWALAY NA KAMI! (GRABE ANG SAKIT!)' but when you watch it, they just separated seats on a bus. It's the ultimate 'akala mo, pero hindi pala' of the internet. The reason you have trust issues with online articles.
usage_notes: Used exactly as in English, with a universally negative connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala diyan, halatang **clickbait** lang ang pamagat.","translation":"Don't believe that, the title is obviously just **clickbait**."}]

translation: a type of sweet, sticky rice cake (nian gao)
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kakanin na yari sa malagkit na bigas, asukal, at mantika. Ito ay malagkit, matamis, at sikat lalo na tuwing Bagong Taon ng mga Tsino.
etymology: From Hokkien Chinese 甜粿 (tī-kóe), meaning 'sweet cake'.
original_explanation: The official sticky situation of Chinese New Year. This glutinous rice cake is a gift that symbolizes sticking together and achieving a 'higher' (sweeter) year. The struggle is real when you try to slice it, and even more real when you fry it and it sticks to the pan, your plate, your teeth... everything. But it's so good, you deal with it.
usage_notes: Primarily associated with Chinese New Year celebrations in the Philippines. It is often coated in egg and pan-fried before eating.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpadala ang aming kapitbahay na Tsino ng isang kahon ng **tikoy**.","translation":"Our Chinese neighbor sent over a box of **tikoy**."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang **tikoy** kapag pinirito sa itlog.","translation":"**Tikoy** is delicious when fried with egg."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahinang pagrereklamo o pagbulong na nagpapahiwatig ng pagkadismaya, pagtutol, o sama ng loob.
original_explanation: The sound you make under your breath when your boss gives you another task at 4:59 PM. It's a low-key, passive-aggressive grumble, not a full-blown 'reklamo'. A 'hmpf!' in word form. The official background noise of anyone who's 'pagod na pero bawal mag-resign.'
usage_notes: This meaning refers to a sound or expression of discontent. It is a homonym of 'yamutmot' (crumpled).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **yamutmot** niya nang utusan siyang maghugas ng plato.","translation":"I heard his **muttering** when he was told to wash the dishes."},{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na ang **yamutmot** at gawin mo na lang ang trabaho mo.","translation":"Stop the **grumbling** and just do your job."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bahagi o proporsyon na kaugnay sa kabuuang isang daan; ginagamitan ng simbolo na %.
etymology: Compound of 'bahagi' (part) and 'daan' (hundred), literally 'part of a hundred'.
original_explanation: This is the number that determines if you passed or failed an exam, or how much 'patong' (markup) your suki adds to the price. It's the '10% service charge' on your restaurant bill, the '50% off' sign that lures you into a sale, and the '1% battery remaining' that gives you anxiety.
usage_notes: The symbol % is often used. 'Porsiyento' (from Spanish 'por ciento') is a very common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakuha siya ng isandaang **bahagdan** sa pagsusulit.","translation":"She got one hundred **percent** on the exam."},{"sentence":"Maliit na **bahagdan** lang ng populasyon ang nabakunahan.","translation":"Only a small **percentage** of the population has been vaccinated."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpapalitan ng posisyon, tungkulin, o lugar sa isa't isa; ang sistema ng pagsasalitan.
original_explanation: This is the BPO agent's life: the constant 'paghahalili' of shifts. It's what you and your siblings do to take care of your parents. It's the 'tag-team' in wrestling, the 'sub' in basketball, or the political succession when one term ends and another begins. It’s the cycle of life, but for tasks and responsibilities.
usage_notes: Can refer to taking turns in a task, or to formal succession of power or role.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang maayos na **paghahalili** ng kapangyarihan sa isang demokrasya.","translation":"An orderly **succession** of power is important in a democracy."},{"sentence":"Nag-usap sila para sa **paghahalili** sa pagbabantay sa kanilang tindahan.","translation":"They talked about **taking turns** in watching their store."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang representasyon ng kapanganakan ni Hesukristo, na karaniwang nagpapakita kina Maria, Jose, ang sanggol na Hesus sa sabsaban, kasama ang mga pastol, ang tatlong hari, at mga hayop.
original_explanation: The OG Christmas decoration. It's the complete set of figurines—Mary, Joseph, Baby Jesus, some farm animals, and the three wise guys—that your mom carefully sets up every December. It's the centerpiece of the Pinoy Christmas home before the Christmas tree became the star. You know Christmas is near when the Belen is out.
usage_notes: Always capitalized. Refers specifically to the nativity scene, a staple of Philippine Christmas decorations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinayo na ng lola ang **Belen** sa ilalim ng aming Christmas tree.","translation":"Grandma has already set up the **Nativity scene** under our Christmas tree."},{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng mga ilaw sa **Belen** na nasa plasa.","translation":"The lights on the **Nativity scene** in the town plaza are beautiful."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglilitis o pag-aaway sa korte; usaping legal na dinidinig sa hukuman.
original_explanation: This is the fancy legal term for a full-blown court battle. It's not just a simple 'sumbong' to the barangay captain; this is when you lawyer up and get ready for a long, expensive, and dramatic process. It's the 'I'll see you in court!' threat, but make it formal.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa konteksto ng batas at mga usaping legal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa hindi pagkakasundo, umabot sa **litigasyon** ang kanilang alitan sa lupa.","translation":"Because of their disagreement, their land dispute ended up in **litigation**."},{"sentence":"Magastos at matagal ang proseso ng **litigasyon**.","translation":"The process of **litigation** is expensive and long."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng labis na pagmamalaki sa sariling mga nagawa, ari-arian, o kakayahan sa paraang nakakainis o mapagmataas.
original_explanation: The official sport of 'flexing' on social media. It's posting your new iPhone, your Starbucks cup, your plane ticket, and captioning it '#blessed'. It's that one 'tito' at the family reunion who won't shut up about how smart his kids are. It's the art of humble-bragging turned up to 11. The opposite of 'lowkey'.
usage_notes: Carries a strong negative connotation of arrogance and being annoying.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi maganda ang labis na **paghahambog** dahil nagdudulot ito ng inggit at sama ng loob.","translation":"Excessive **boasting** is not good because it causes envy and resentment."},{"sentence":"Sawa na ako sa **paghahambog** niya tungkol sa kanyang mga mamahaling gamit.","translation":"I'm tired of his **bragging** about his expensive things."}]

translation: hotdog, fried rice, and egg breakfast plate
meaning_filipino: Isang pagkaing pang-almusal na binubuo ng hotdog, sinangag (fried rice), at itlog.
etymology: Portmanteau of hotdog + sinangag (fried rice) + itlog (egg).
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino breakfast of champions (or college students cramming for an exam). It's a portmanteau: HOTdog + SInangag (fried rice) + itLOG (egg). It's the simplest, most reliable member of the -silog family, always there for you when you need a quick, greasy, and satisfying meal, any time of day.
usage_notes: Part of the "silog" family of breakfast dishes, which all feature fried rice and egg with a main protein.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang order ng **hotsilog** nga po, na may kasamang kape.","translation":"One order of **hotsilog**, please, with coffee."},{"sentence":"Ang **hotsilog** ang paborito niyang almusal bago pumasok sa eskwela.","translation":"**Hotsilog** is his favorite breakfast before going to school."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang makapal at mamantikang bahagi ng gatas na umaangat sa ibabaw, o anumang produktong may ganitong itsura at tekstura, tulad ng losyon o palaman.
original_explanation: Pwedeng yung pampasarap sa kape mo (coffee creamer), pwedeng yung pinapahid mo sa mukha para kuminis (face cream), o yung kulay na beige-ish na pang-pader. Basta't 'creamy', malamang **krema** ang katapat niyan.
usage_notes: Used for food, cosmetics, and even color.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglagay siya ng **krema** at asukal sa kanyang kape.","translation":"She put **cream** and sugar in her coffee."},{"sentence":"Ang paborito niyang kulay para sa dingding ay **krema**.","translation":"Her favorite color for the wall is **cream**."}]

translation: to arm someone or a group
meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng mga sandata ang isang tao o pangkat para sa depensa o pag-atake.
original_explanation: This is the full, formal verb for 'pasandata'. If 'pasandata' is the shout, '**pasandatahan**' is the detailed action plan. It's the process of equipping your troops. "Kailangang **pasandatahan** natin ang ating mga guwardiya," says the building admin. In the BPO world, it's when management gives you a new headset, a faster computer, and a script for irate callers—they're arming you for battle.
usage_notes: The complete verb form, more formal than the imperative 'pasandata'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang plano ay **pasandatahan** ang mga residente para maipagtanggol nila ang kanilang baryo.","translation":"The plan is **to arm** the residents so they can defend their village."},{"sentence":"Pinag-utos ng hari na **pasandatahan** ang kanyang buong hukbo.","translation":"The king ordered **to arm** his entire army."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang direksyong hilaga; ang rehiyon o pook na matatagpuan sa gawing hilaga ng isang lugar.
etymology: From `ka-`...`-an` (denoting a region or area) around `hilaga` (north).
original_explanation: Basically, 'The North.' For people in Manila, this is anywhere from QC to Baguio to Ilocos. 'Taga-**kahilagaan** ako' (I'm from the north). It's where the air (supposedly) gets cooler and the traffic... well, the traffic is still traffic. The opposite of 'katimugan' (the south).
usage_notes: Used to refer to the direction or a region in the north. 'Hilaga' is the direction, 'kahilagaan' is the northern region.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming magagandang dalampasigan sa **kahilagaan** ng Luzon.","translation":"There are many beautiful beaches in **the north** of Luzon."}]

meaning_filipino: May kakayahang umantig o magpaalab ng matinding emosyon o pakiramdam.
etymology: A compound word from "makapukaw" (to be able to stir) + "damdamin" (feelings, emotions).
original_explanation: This describes that Thai insurance commercial that made you cry, the 'hugot' movie that felt too real, or the song that reminds you of your ex. It hits you right in the feels. It's the adjective form of 'I'm not crying, you're crying!'
usage_notes: A compound adjective used to describe things like movies, songs, stories, speeches, or experiences.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napanood ko ang isang **makapukaw-damdamin** na pelikula kagabi.","translation":"I watched an **emotionally stirring** movie last night."},{"sentence":"Sumulat siya ng isang **makapukaw-damdamin** na tula para sa kanyang ina.","translation":"He wrote a **heart-rending** poem for his mother."}]

translation: to remove a part; to take out a portion
meaning_filipino: Alisin o tanggalin ang isang tiyak na bahagi mula sa isang kabuuan.
original_explanation: If 'awasan' is about reducing the whole (like the price), 'awasin' is about taking the specific part. Think of a cake. "Awasin mo 'yung parte na may cherry" means you're taking that specific slice. It's the action of removing the portion itself, like when HR tells you the exact tax amount na 'aawasin' sa sweldo mo.
usage_notes: "Awasin" is a verb in the object focus, referring to the specific part or amount being removed. For example, "Awasin mo ang dalawang tasa" (Take out the two cups). Compare with "Awasan mo ang lalagyan" (Take from the container).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **awasin** mo ang para sa akin bago ninyo ubusin 'yan.","translation":"Please, **take out my portion** before you finish that."},{"sentence":"Ang sampung porsyentong buwis ay **aawasin** mula sa iyong sahod.","translation":"The ten percent tax will be **deducted** from your salary."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang produkto na ginawa sa pamamagitan ng kamay at hindi ng makina.
original_explanation: The opposite of 'Made in China' mass production. This is your 'Made with love by nanay' stuff. The things you see on Etsy or at a local craft fair. It's more expensive because it comes with a piece of the creator's soul (and carpal tunnel).
usage_notes: Hyphenated compound adjective.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas pinahahalagahan ko ang mga regalong **yaring-kamay**.","translation":"I value **handmade** gifts more."}]

translation: carriage for hire, calash for rent
meaning_filipino: Isang sasakyang hila ng kabayo, tulad ng kalesa o karwahe, na maaaring arkilahin para sa transportasyon.
original_explanation: Basically, the Grab or Angkas of the Spanish colonial era. Before booking apps, you'd hail one of these to get around Intramuros. Ngayon, pang-tourist na lang 'yan, for the 'gram. "Manong, pa-picture po sa Vigan!"
usage_notes: This term is largely historical or used in specific tourist contexts (like Vigan or Intramuros).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dati, **paupahang karomata** ang pangunahing transportasyon sa Maynila.","translation":"Before, a **carriage for hire** was the main mode of transportation in Manila."},{"sentence":"Sumakay kami sa isang **paupahang karomata** para libutin ang mga makasaysayang lugar.","translation":"We rode a **calash for rent** to tour the historical sites."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pangkabit na metal, parang maikling pako na pinupukpok ang magkabilang dulo upang pagdikitin ang dalawang piraso ng materyales.
original_explanation: That little metal thingy that holds your maong jeans together. Or the things that keep bridges and old metal structures from falling apart. It's the unsung hero of construction and fashion, a permanent metal stitch. Not to be confused with 'remata', which is way more stressful.
usage_notes: Used in construction, metalwork, and even in clothing (e.g., jeans).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng matibay na **rematse** para sa proyektong ito.","translation":"A strong **rivet** is needed for this project."},{"sentence":"Natanggal ang **rematse** sa bulsa ng pantalon ko.","translation":"The **rivet** on my pants pocket came off."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao o kakayahan na makaramdam o makaalam ng mga bagay na hindi kayang ipaliwanag ng agham, tulad ng pagbasa ng isip o paghula sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: Yung tropa mong laging alam kung sino ang nag-text sa'yo bago mo pa tingnan ang phone mo. 'Bes, may powers ka ba? Ang lakas ng pagka-psikiko mo!' Also, the person you go to in Quiapo when modern medicine and prayers aren't working fast enough.
usage_notes: Maaari ring gamitin bilang pangngalan upang tumukoy sa isang tao na may ganitong kakayahan (e.g., 'isang psikiko').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naniniwala siya sa mga kakayahang **psikiko** tulad ng telepathy.","translation":"He believes in **psychic** abilities like telepathy."},{"sentence":"Nagpatingin sila sa isang **psikiko** upang hanapin ang nawawalang alaga.","translation":"They consulted a **psychic** (person) to find their missing pet."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglusong o pag-ilalim sa tubig nang buong katawan, na karaniwang una ang ulo.
original_explanation: What you do in the beautiful waters of Palawan or Batangas. You `sumisid` to see the corals and the fishies. It's also what you do to get the 1-peso coin your tito threw into the swimming pool during a family outing. 'Hala, nahulog ang cellphone ko sa baha! Sino matapang sumisid?'
usage_notes: Refers to diving into water. For diving from a high place (like a cliff or diving board), `tumalon` is also used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahusay siyang **sumisid** at kayang magtagal sa ilalim ng tubig.","translation":"He is good at **diving** and can stay underwater for a long time."},{"sentence":"**Sumisid** ang mga mangingisda upang manghuli ng perlas.","translation":"The fishermen **dove** to hunt for pearls."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging malamig at mamasa-masa, karaniwang tumutukoy sa simoy ng hangin o sa isang lugar.
original_explanation: This is a deep Tagalog word for that specific kind of cold you feel during a '-ber' month morning or when you're in Baguio. It's not just 'malamig' (cold); it has a hint of dampness, like the air after it rains. Imagine the feeling of a cool, slightly wet towel on your forehead. That's dimig. It's the OG aircon.
usage_notes: A more poetic or literary term for coldness, often implying moisture. Less common in everyday conversation than 'lamig'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang **dimig** ng hangin mula sa bundok.","translation":"She felt the **damp coolness** of the wind from the mountain."},{"sentence":"May kakaibang **dimig** ang gabi sa probinsya.","translation":"There is a unique **coolness** to the nights in the province."}]

translation: to have something tightened; to become stricter
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o pagpapagawa na gawing mas masikip, mas mahigpit, o mas istrikto ang isang bagay o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: Two meanings here. 1) When your favorite jeans don't fit anymore after the holidays, you go to a tailor to 'magpahigpit' (have it tightened). 2) When your parents find out your grades are slipping, they 'magpahigpit' on your curfew and social life. It's the act of increasing the tension, whether on your belt or on your freedom.
usage_notes: Can be literal (tightening an object) or figurative (imposing stricter rules).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagpahigpit** ako ng turnilyo sa upuan.","translation":"I **had the screw on the chair tightened**."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa pandemya, **nagpahigpit** ang gobyerno sa mga patakaran sa pagbyahe.","translation":"Because of the pandemic, the government **became stricter** with travel policies."}]

translation: to make someone stop; to put a stop to
meaning_filipino: Iutos o piliting ihinto ang isang gawain, kilos, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is the power move of every parent or teacher. When the kids are running wild, one loud 'TIGIL!' is an attempt to **magpatigil** the chaos. It's what the government tries to do with illegal activities, or what you try to do to your friend who's about to make a bad life decision after three bottles of beer. 'Bes, awat na.'
usage_notes: A verb of command or authority, used to halt an action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagpatigil** ng laro ang malakas na ulan.","translation":"The heavy rain **put a stop** to the game."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **magpatigil** sa pag-aaway ng kanyang mga kaibigan.","translation":"He tried to **make** his friends **stop** fighting."}]

translation: to hold a banquet for; to feast on
meaning_filipino: Ang pagdaraos ng isang piging o handaan para sa isang tao o okasyon. Maaari ring mangahulugang kainin nang may kasakiman o parang sa isang pista.
original_explanation: Two meanings: 1) To throw a fancy party for someone. "Bangketehin natin si lola sa 80th birthday niya!" 2) The more fun meaning: to absolutely demolish a spread of food. 'Yung inubos niyo ng friends mo 'yung buong bilao ng pancit, you didn't just eat it, you 'binangkete' it.
usage_notes: Can be used literally (to hold a banquet) or figuratively (to devour food). 'Bangketihin' is a common variant spelling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais ng alkalde na **bangketehin** ang mga atletang nanalo sa paligsahan.","translation":"The mayor wants **to hold a banquet for** the athletes who won the competition."},{"sentence":"Halika, **bangketehin** na natin ang mga natirang pagkain mula sa Pasko!","translation":"Come on, let's **feast on** the leftover food from Christmas!"}]

translation: smudge of dirt on the face
meaning_filipino: Maliit na dumi, uling, o mantsa na nakakapit sa mukha.
original_explanation: That little smudge of chocolate on a kid's cheek, the pen mark you accidentally got on your nose, or the charcoal on your face after a barbecue. It's the kind of dirt your mom would wet her thumb with her saliva to wipe off your face when you were a kid. It's not full-on 'dugyot' (filthy), just a cute or clumsy little spot of dirt. "May dusing ka sa pisngi."
usage_notes: Specifically refers to a small amount of dirt or a stain on the face.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinunasan niya ang **dusing** sa mukha ng kanyang anak.","translation":"She wiped the **smudge** off her child's face."},{"sentence":"Natawa ako kasi may **dusing** siya ng uling sa ilong.","translation":"I laughed because he had a **smudge** of charcoal on his nose."}]

meaning_filipino: Mailap at mahirap supilin; malikot at hindi mapakali, lalo na sa paraang maingay at magulo.
original_explanation: This is every kid on a sugar rush during a children's party. It's the vibe of a classroom when the teacher is late. It’s loud, chaotic energy. Parang 'yung aso mong 'di mapigilan sa pagtakbo at pagtalon kapag may bisita.
usage_notes: Often used to describe children or animals, but can apply to any group or individual exhibiting rowdy behavior.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masyadong **magaso** ang mga bata kaya pinagalitan sila ng kanilang nanay.","translation":"The children were too **rowdy** so their mother scolded them."},{"sentence":"Mahirap hulihin ang **magaso** na tuta.","translation":"It's hard to catch the **boisterous** puppy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging sigurado o walang duda.
original_explanation: That feeling when you've double-checked your alarm for your 6 AM flight. It's the assurance you get from a "Yes, confirmed!" text. It's the opposite of "Sana all." This is "Sure na all." It's the absence of "baka" (maybe) and "ewan" (I don't know). Pure, unadulterated confidence.
usage_notes: Refers to the state or quality of being certain. Interchangeable with 'katiyakan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng **pagkatiyak** na darating ka bago ako umalis.","translation":"I need **assurance** that you will arrive before I leave."},{"sentence":"Sa kabila ng mga pahiwatig, wala pa ring **pagkatiyak** sa resulta.","translation":"Despite the hints, there is still no **certainty** about the result."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pansamantalang pagtigil sa paggawa o anumang aktibidad upang makabawi ng lakas.
etymology: From `pa-` + `hinga` (breathe). The idea is to 'let oneself breathe'.
original_explanation: The most expensive thing in the BPO industry and the most desired thing by any student during finals week. Ito 'yung 15-minute break na nagiging 45 minutes. Pahinga is that sacred moment you close your eyes and pretend your deadlines don't exist. 'Pahinga, pero 'di susuko.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng **pahinga** pagkatapos ng mahabang araw ng trabaho.","translation":"I need a **rest** after a long day at work."},{"sentence":"Mag-**pahinga** ka muna bago mo ipagpatuloy 'yan.","translation":"Take a **break** first before you continue that."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasakatuparan o paggawa ng isang bagay na ipinangako, iniutos, o inaasahan.
original_explanation: This is the opposite of "drawing" or "paasa". When you say you'll do something and you actually do it, 'tumupad' ka. It's about keeping your promises, following the rules, or making a dream come true. A person of their word.
usage_notes: Often used with "sa pangako" (to a promise), "sa tungkulin" (to a duty), or "sa pangarap" (to a dream).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumupad** siya sa kanyang pangako na babalik siya.","translation":"He **fulfilled** his promise that he would return."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga para sa isang lider na **tumupad** sa kanyang tungkulin sa bayan.","translation":"It is important for a leader to **comply with** his duty to the country."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sawsawan na kulay itim at maalat, na gawa sa ibinurong balatong (soybeans), at karaniwang ginagamit sa pagluluto at bilang pampalasa sa mga pagkaing Asyano.
etymology: From Hokkien Chinese 豆油 (tāu-iû), meaning 'bean oil'.
original_explanation: The lifeblood of Filipino kitchens. That dark, salty liquid you put on literally everything: your adobo, your sinangag, your siomai. It's the partner-in-crime of calamansi and sili. A household isn't a home without a bottle of Silver Swan or Datu Puti.
usage_notes: A staple condiment in Filipino cuisine.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakilagyan mo ng **toyo** at calamansi ang isda.","translation":"Please put **soy sauce** and calamansi on the fish."},{"sentence":"Naubusan na tayo ng **toyo** para sa adobo.","translation":"We've run out of **soy sauce** for the adobo."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghahalo at pagpapakinis ng harina at iba pang sangkap gamit ang mga kamay upang makagawa ng masa para sa tinapay o iba pang lutuin.
original_explanation: The official workout for bakers and panaderos. It’s what you do to dough to make it ready for the oven, whether it’s for pandesal, pizza, or your quarantine-era sourdough starter. It's like giving the dough a deep-tissue massage.
usage_notes: This 'masa' refers to dough, not to be confused with 'masa' meaning 'the masses' or populace.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaga pa lang ay gising na ang panadero para **magmasa** ng pandesal.","translation":"The baker was already awake early to **knead** the pandesal dough."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magmasa** nang mabuti para lumambot ang dough ng pizza.","translation":"You need to **knead** well for the pizza dough to become soft."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang likhang-sining, pampanitikan, o pang-musika; isang mahalaga o natatanging gawa ng isang alagad ng sining, manunulat, o kompositor.
original_explanation: This isn't just any 'trabaho' or 'gawa.' Obra is a work with a capital W. It’s an artist's masterpiece, a writer's magnum opus, a director's film. It's the 'Obra Maestra' you studied in high school, like 'Noli Me Tángere.' When you call something an obra, you're giving it respect, acknowledging the skill and soul poured into it. It’s the difference between a drawing and a Spoliarium.
usage_notes: Often used with 'maestra' to form 'obra maestra' (masterpiece). Carries a connotation of high artistic value.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Spoliarium ni Juan Luna ay isang tanyag na **obra**.","translation":"Juan Luna's Spoliarium is a famous **work of art**."},{"sentence":"Lahat ng kanyang mga nobela ay itinuturing na mga **obra** ng panitikang Pilipino.","translation":"All of his novels are considered **masterpieces** of Philippine literature."}]

meaning_filipino: Makaranas ng panginginig ng katawan; manginig dahil sa ginaw, takot, o iba pang matinding dahilan.
original_explanation: The action version of 'kaligkig'. This is what you do when you step out of a hot shower into a cold room, or when your boss suddenly says "We need to talk." It’s the physical manifestation of "brrr" or "yikes!".
usage_notes: Often used in the form 'kinakaligkig' (is shivering).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maligo sa ulan at baka ka **kaligkigin**.","translation":"Don't bathe in the rain or you might **shiver** from the cold."},{"sentence":"**Kinakaligkig** ako sa takot tuwing nanonood ng horror movie.","translation":"I **shiver** in fear whenever I watch a horror movie."}]

meaning_filipino: Tulungan ang isang ina sa kanyang panganganak; gumanap bilang komadrona o hilot.
etymology: From `pa-` (causative prefix) + `anak` (child) + `-in` (object-focus suffix). Literally, 'to cause someone to have a child' in the sense of assisting the process.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate assist. Before hospitals were everywhere, the 'hilot' or 'komadrona' was the MVP of the barangay. They were the ones you called to **paanakin** the expectant mother. Today, it’s what OB-GYNs do, but with more machines that go 'bing'.
usage_notes: `Paanakin` refers to the person assisting the birth, not the one giving birth (`manganganak`).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lola niya na isang hilot ang **nagpaanak** sa kanyang ina.","translation":"Her grandmother, who was a traditional midwife, **assisted her mother in childbirth**."},{"sentence":"Isinugod siya sa ospital para **paanakin** ng doktor.","translation":"She was rushed to the hospital to be **delivered of her child** by the doctor."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbihag, paghuli, o pag-akit sa isang tao o sa puso nito, sa paraang literal man o matalinghaga.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "sana all" verb. It's what your crush does to your heart without even trying. It's the power of a charismatic leader, a stunning performance, or a really, really good story. To mamihag is to capture not just bodies (like a 'bihag' or captive), but attention, hearts, and minds. It's the verb for "I'm obsessed."
usage_notes: Can be used literally (to take captives) but is more often used figuratively (to captivate hearts).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang ganda at talino ay sapat na para **mamihag** ng kahit sinong puso.","translation":"Her beauty and intelligence are enough to **captivate** any heart."},{"sentence":"Noong unang panahon, ang mga mandirigma ay lumulusob sa ibang nayon upang **mamihag**.","translation":"In the old days, warriors would raid other villages to **take captives**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matayog na pagnanais, mithiin, o layunin na gustong makamit ng isang tao.
original_explanation: This is your "why" or your "big dream." It's not just a simple want, it's a deep-seated ambition. Think of it as the ultimate #goals. It's the reason you're grinding in your BPO job, taking extra classes, or starting a small business. It's the fuel for your hustle. Your adhika is what you'd put in your bio if you were a national hero.
usage_notes: A formal and literary word. Often used in patriotic songs, poems, and formal speeches.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **adhika** niya sa buhay ay ang makatulong sa mga mahihirap.","translation":"His **ambition** in life is to help the poor."},{"sentence":"Ipaglaban mo ang iyong mga **adhika**.","translation":"Fight for your **aspirations**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sinaunang instrumentong pangmusika na may mga kuwerdas, kahawig ng isang maliit na harpa.
original_explanation: That small harp-like thing you see in old Greek movies or statues. It's the OG acoustic guitar. The instrument of poets and angels in classical art. 'Parang anghel na tumutugtog ng lira.'
usage_notes: Mostly used in literary, historical, or mythological contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa mitolohiyang Griyego, si Apollo ay madalas ilarawan na may hawak na **lira**.","translation":"In Greek mythology, Apollo is often depicted holding a **lyre**."},{"sentence":"Ang tunog ng **lira** ay sinasabing nakapagpapakalma ng kaluluwa.","translation":"The sound of the **lyre** is said to be able to calm the soul."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang organisadong sistema o lugar kung saan isinasagawa ang pagbili at pagbenta ng mga sapi o 'shares' ng mga pampublikong kumpanya.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'sana all' and 'sana ol' place for money. It's where you buy a tiny piece of a big company (like Jollibee or SM) and hope it grows. It's like a high-stakes marites session where the chismis is about company performance and the economy. Pwedeng magpayaman, pwedeng magpaiyak. Invest at your own risk!
usage_notes: This is a direct, formal translation. The English term "stock market" is used more often in conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-aaral siyang mamuhunan sa **pamilihan ng sapi**.","translation":"He is studying how to invest in the **stock market**."},{"sentence":"Bumagsak ang halaga ng mga kumpanya sa **pamilihan ng sapi** dahil sa pandaigdigang krisis.","translation":"The value of companies in the **stock market** fell due to the global crisis."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita o pagdama ng pag-ibig o pagmamahal sa hinaharap. Ito ang aspektong kontemplatibo ng pandiwang 'magmahal'.
etymology: From the `ma-` verb affix combined with the reduplicated first syllable of the root `mahal` (love, expensive) to indicate future tense.
original_explanation: This is the future tense of loving someone. It's the 'I will love you' promise you make, the 'sana all' you whisper when you see a sweet couple, or the hope you have for a future relationship. 'Sino kaya ang **mamahal** sa akin nang tunay?' is the ultimate hugot question.
usage_notes: This is the future/contemplated aspect of 'magmahal'. The object-focused form 'mamahalin' is more frequently used in promises.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sabi niya, siya ay **mamahal** sa akin magpakailanman.","translation":"He said he **will love** me forever."},{"sentence":"Habangbuhay kitang **mamahal**in.","translation":"I **will love** you forever."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi kumplikado; madaling maunawaan, gawin, o gamitin; payak.
original_explanation: 'Gusto ko lang ng simpleng buhay.' - The battle cry of every burned-out BPO agent and traffic-weary commuter. It's the opposite of drama, of complicated Excel sheets, and of vague instructions from your boss. It's that Jollibee Chickenjoy meal—no frills, just pure, simple happiness. It can describe a person (low-maintenance), a task (madali lang), or a life goal (isang kahig, isang tuka... but with WiFi).
usage_notes: Used interchangeably with the Tagalog word "payak." However, "simple" is far more common in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Simple** lang ang pangarap ko, ang makasama ang pamilya ko.","translation":"My dream is **simple**, to be with my family."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang gawing kumplikado, **simple** lang ang solusyon diyan.","translation":"Don't complicate it, the solution for that is **simple**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mga kagamitan, pagkain, o anumang bagay na kinakailangan para sa isang tiyak na layunin o panahon; panustos.
original_explanation: This is your 'baon' for the long haul. Think of it as the supplies your mom packs for a week-long beach trip, or the company's budget for pantry snacks and coffee. When the 'abasto' runs out, it's either time to go home or time to file another PO request.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of business, shipping, or household supplies.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating tiyakin na sapat ang **abasto** ng bigas para sa buong buwan.","translation":"We need to ensure we have enough **supply** of rice for the whole month."},{"sentence":"Naubos na ang **abasto** ng kape sa opisina.","translation":"The **supply** of coffee in the office has run out."}]

translation: to become thin; to lose weight
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagbawas ng timbang o pagiging mas payat ng isang tao, na maaaring dahil sa sakit, diyeta, o pag-aalala.
original_explanation: The opposite of 'mangatawan'. This is what happens during your 'breakup diet', when you're swamped with deadlines, or when you're actually succeeding at your fitness goals. 'Hoy, nangangayayat ka! May problema ba?' is the standard concerned friend/tita opening line.
usage_notes: Often carries a connotation of losing weight due to stress, sickness, or hardship, but can also be neutral.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mula nang magkasakit siya, kitang-kita na siya ay **nangayayat**.","translation":"Ever since he got sick, it's very visible that he **has become thin**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa ng isang tungkulin, papel, o gawain; ang pagbibigay-buhay sa isang karakter sa dula o pelikula.
original_explanation: What actors do on screen, what you do during your job evaluation (performance review), or your 'acting' skills when your tita asks if you have a jowa. It's about playing a role or doing your part, whether on stage or in the office pantry.
usage_notes: Has a dual meaning of 'performance' (as in acting) and 'fulfillment' (as in of a duty). Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Humanga ang lahat sa kanyang mahusay na **pagganap** bilang kontrabida.","translation":"Everyone was amazed by her excellent **portrayal** as the villain."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang tapat na **pagganap** sa tungkulin ng isang lider.","translation":"Honest **fulfillment** of duty is important for a leader."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagtatrabaho para sa isang kumpanya, ahensya ng gobyerno, o indibidwal kapalit ng sahod.
etymology: Maaaring may kaugnayan sa `kawan` (flock, group), na nagpapahiwatig ng isang miyembro ng isang grupo ng mga manggagawa.
original_explanation: From the BPO agent grinding on the night shift to the government employee processing your papers (slowly, but surely), they are all kawani. It's the more formal term for 'empleyado.' If you have a boss and you receive a payslip, congratulations, you're a kawani.
usage_notes: Isang pormal na termino para sa isang empleyado, karaniwang ginagamit sa gobyerno at malalaking korporasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **kawani** ng gobyerno ay mayroong araw ng pahinga bukas.","translation":"The government **employees** have a day off tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Pinulong ng manager ang lahat ng **kawani** ng kumpanya.","translation":"The manager called a meeting with all the company **personnel**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mapanlait na salita para sa isang taong hangal, hindi nag-iisip, o gumagawa ng mga bagay na walang katuturan.
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino insult for someone who just did something incredibly dumb. It's what you mutter under your breath when a driver cuts you off, or when your friend makes the same bad love life decision for the nth time. 'Bes, use the kokote naman, please!' Literal translation is 'no brain', which is exactly how it feels.
usage_notes: A very strong and offensive insult. Use with caution.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **walang-utak**; pag-isipan mo muna ang iyong mga desisyon.","translation":"Don't be **brainless**; think about your decisions first."},{"sentence":"Tanging isang taong **walang-utak** ang maniniwala sa ganoong kalokohan.","translation":"Only a **stupid** person would believe such nonsense."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng kapangyarihan o lakas upang kontrolin, supilin, o mangibabaw sa iba.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'dominar' (to dominate), na inangkupan ng hulaping '-han'.
original_explanation: The action version of 'dominado'. It's what you do in Mobile Legends when you're on a winning streak. It's what that one super loud person does in a group meeting. Basically, to take control and be the one in charge, whether in a game, a relationship, or an argument.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang **dominahan** ang usapan sa pulong.","translation":"He is trying to **dominate** the conversation in the meeting."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **dominahan** ka ng iyong takot.","translation":"Don't let your fear **dominate** you."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang biglaan at marahas na pagsalakay o pag-atake.
original_explanation: That moment in a zombie movie when the horde breaks through the barricade. Or when you open a bag of chips and your friends suddenly appear out of nowhere. It's a sudden, overwhelming rush. Can also be the 'daluhong' of deadlines from your boss on a Friday afternoon.
usage_notes: The verb form is `dumaluhong`. It implies a swift, aggressive, and often unexpected charge.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghanda ang mga sundalo para sa posibleng **daluhong** ng mga kalaban.","translation":"The soldiers prepared for a possible **assault** from the enemies."},{"sentence":"Ang **daluhong** ng malalakas na alon ay sumira sa pader.","translation":"The **onslaught** of strong waves destroyed the wall."}]

translation: to telephone; to call (on the phone)
meaning_filipino: Ang pakikipag-usap sa isang tao gamit ang telepono.
original_explanation: The OG way to call someone before 'i-text' or 'i-message' became a thing. This is what your Tita from the province does. It implies using an actual phone for a voice call, maybe even a landline! Very vintage, very formal. "Itelepono mo si Mayor."
usage_notes: Sounds a bit formal or dated compared to 'tawagan'. More common with the older generation or in formal instructions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Itelepono** mo ang opisina para kumpirmahin ang iyong appointment.","translation":"**Telephone** the office to confirm your appointment."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan kong **itelepono** si lola pero laging busy ang linya.","translation":"I tried to **call** grandma but the line is always busy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagtantiya ng kita at gastusin sa loob ng isang tiyak na panahon; ang halagang inilaan para sa isang partikular na layunin.
original_explanation: 'Yung magic number na nagsasabi kung hanggang saan lang ang kaya mong gastusin. Para sa gobyerno, bilyon-bilyon 'yan. Para sa'tin, 'yan 'yung natitirang pera pagkatapos magbayad ng bills, na pinagkakasya para sa milk tea at pamasahe hanggang sa susunod na sahod.
usage_notes: Madalas na pinapalitan ng hiram na salitang Ingles na "budget" (badyet) sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kulang ang **presupuwesto** ng pamilya para sa mamahaling bakasyon.","translation":"The family's **budget** is not enough for an expensive vacation."},{"sentence":"Inaprubahan na ng Kongreso ang pambansang **presupuwesto**.","translation":"Congress has approved the national **budget**."}]

meaning_filipino: Bawat isa sa mga buhok na tumutubo sa gilid ng talukap ng mata.
etymology: From a combination of `pilik` (a fringe of hair, now obscure) and `mata` (eye).
original_explanation: The OG face accessory. It's the tiny curtain for your eyes that catches dust and falling mascara. When one falls, you put it on your finger, make a wish, and blow. It's the original 'manifesting'.
usage_notes: Often spelled as `pilik-mata`. Both forms are widely accepted.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang haba ng **pilikmata** mo, parang extension!","translation":"Your **eyelashes** are so long, they look like extensions!"},{"sentence":"May nahulog na **pilikmata**, mag-wish ka.","translation":"A fallen **eyelash**, make a wish."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, gawi, o kilos na naging bahagi na ng kultura o pang-araw-araw na pamumuhay dahil sa paulit-ulit na paggawa.
original_explanation: This is the 'kasi ganito na kami mula pa noon' (because this is how we've always been) logic. It's why we have fiestas for every saint, why we can't start a meeting on time (Filipino time!), and why we always bring home pasalubong. It's the habit that became culture.
usage_notes: Refers to long-standing traditions or personal habits.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagmamano sa mga nakatatanda ay isang **nakaugalian** na nating mga Pilipino.","translation":"The act of 'mano' to elders is a **customary** practice for us Filipinos."},{"sentence":"**Nakaugalian** na niyang magkape pagkagising sa umaga.","translation":"It has become his **habitual** practice to drink coffee upon waking up in the morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang hinto; walang patid; nagpapatuloy nang walang pagkaantala.
original_explanation: Describes the EDSA traffic on a payday Friday. The chismis from your kapitbahay. The unli-rice promo you can't resist. The K-drama series you binge-watch until 4 AM. It just keeps going and going and going...
usage_notes: Emphasizes the uninterrupted nature of an action or state. Can function as an adverb or an adjective.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tuluy-tuloy** ang buhos ng ulan magdamag.","translation":"The downpour of rain was **continuous** all night."},{"sentence":"Kahit pagod na, **tuluy-tuloy** pa rin siya sa pagtatrabaho.","translation":"Even though he was tired, he just kept on working **non-stop**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marahas na pagtama o pag-umpugan ng dalawang bagay, lalo na ng mga sasakyan.
original_explanation: The sound and action of two things meeting when they really, really shouldn't. This is what happens on EDSA during rush hour. It can be two cars, or you bumping into your ex at the mall. One is a traffic nightmare, the other is a social nightmare. Both are a type of "bangga".
usage_notes: Can be used for vehicles, people, or even abstract ideas colliding.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa pagmamaneho para hindi **makabangga**.","translation":"Drive carefully so you don't **get into a collision**."},{"sentence":"Sila ay **nagbangga** sa may kanto habang parehong nagmamadali.","translation":"They **collided** at the corner while both were in a hurry."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na may kakayahang humatak ng mga metal, partikular na ang bakal, dahil sa katangian nitong magnetismo.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung appeal ng crush mo, may mabatubalani effect. Kahit anong iwas mo, napapalapit ka pa rin. It's that invisible force that pulls things together, whether it's metal or your marupok heart.
usage_notes: This is the formal, scientific term for "magnet." The more common, everyday word is the Spanish-derived "magnet."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginagamit ang **mabatubalani** sa mga kompas upang ituro ang direksyong hilaga.","translation":"A **magnet** is used in compasses to point to the northern direction."},{"sentence":"Pinulot niya ang mga karayom gamit ang isang malakas na **mabatubalani**.","translation":"She picked up the needles using a strong **magnet**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isakay o ilagay ang isang bagay o kargamento sa isang sasakyan, lalagyan, o sistema.
original_explanation: What you tell the delivery guy to do with your massive Shopee/Lazada haul: '**Ikarga** niyo na po lahat sa motor!' Also what your brain does with all the stress from work and life. It's about putting something *onto* something else.
usage_notes: Commonly used in contexts of transport, shipping, and even uploading digital files ('ikarga ang file').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **ikarga** ang mga sako ng bigas sa trak.","translation":"Help me **load** the sacks of rice onto the truck."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ikarga** sa akin ang lahat ng problema.","translation":"Don't **load** all the problems onto me."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kalagayan ng pagiging lubog o payat, lalo na sa mga pisngi, dahil sa sakit, pagkapagod, o kakulangan sa nutrisyon.
original_explanation: That look when you've pulled three all-nighters for a final exam or a project deadline. Your cheeks have gone on vacation, leaving a hollow space. It's the 'puyat is real' or 'sobrang diet' look.
usage_notes: Halos eksklusibong ginagamit upang ilarawan ang mga pisnging lubog ('hipak ang pisngi').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **hipak** ang kaniyang mga pisngi dahil sa matagal na pagkakasakit.","translation":"His cheeks became **sunken** due to his long illness."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpagutom, baka maging **hipak** ka niyan.","translation":"Don't starve yourself, your cheeks might become **hollow**."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang bagay na may maliit na lapad o espasyo; masikip.
original_explanation: Tulad ng eskinita sa Quiapo na isang tao lang ang kasya. O yung skinny jeans mo na kailangan mong humiga para maisara. 'Pag sinabing makipot, ibig sabihin, siksikan, bes. Konting-konti lang ang space. Pwede ring 'makipot ang utak'—close-minded.
usage_notes: Can describe physical spaces (road, opening) or be used metaphorically, as in 'makipot ang pag-iisip' (narrow-minded).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumaan kami sa isang **makipot** na kalye.","translation":"We passed through a **narrow** street."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **makipot** ang pag-iisip; pakinggan mo ang iba.","translation":"Don't be narrow-minded; listen to others."},{"sentence":"Ang sinulid ay kailangang ipasok sa **makipot na butas** ng karayom.","translation":"The thread needs to be inserted into the **narrow hole** of the needle."}]

translation: to deform, to ruin the shape
meaning_filipino: Ang pagwasak o pagbabago sa orihinal na hubog o porma ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is basically the same as "sirain ang anyo," but with a slight emphasis on the geometric shape or silhouette. It’s what happens when you sit on your hat, or when your perfectly round pizza gets squished in the box. The integrity of its shape is compromised.
usage_notes: Madalas na ipinagpapalit sa "sirain ang anyo," ngunit ang "hugis" ay mas tumutukoy sa istruktura at balangkas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingatan mong huwag maupuan ang kahon para hindi **sirain ang hugis** ng mga bulaklak sa loob.","translation":"Be careful not to sit on the box so as not to **ruin the shape** of the flowers inside."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa init, nasira ang hugis ng kandila.","translation":"Because of the heat, the shape of the candle was ruined."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing malinaw, maliwanag, o madaling maunawaan ang isang bagay na malabo o mahirap intindihin.
original_explanation: What you tell your partner after a vague, one-word text reply. 'Ano'ng 'K'? Palinawin mo nga.' It's the act of demanding clarity, whether it's about a blurry photo, a confusing instruction from your boss, or the status of your 'M.U.' (mutual understanding).
usage_notes: Used for clarifying information, instructions, feelings, or even physical things like water or a picture.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaari mo bang **palinawin** ang iyong sinabi? Hindi ko masyadong naintindihan.","translation":"Can you **clarify** what you said? I didn't quite understand."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **palinawin** ang tubig sa balon bago ito inumin.","translation":"The water in the well needs **to be made clear** before it is drunk."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mga labi o pinagbagsakan ng isang estruktura, gusali, o bundok na gumuho o nasira.
original_explanation: This is what's left after a disaster. Think of the rubble after an earthquake, the ruins of an old building, or a Jenga tower that finally collapsed. Metaphorically, it's the state of your heart after your crush says 'friends lang tayo.' The wreckage, the debris, the emotional collapse.
usage_notes: Can be literal (physical collapse) or figurative (emotional/system collapse).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming bahay ang naging **guho** dahil sa malakas na lindol.","translation":"Many houses turned into **rubble** because of the strong earthquake."},{"sentence":"Sa gitna ng **guho** ng kanyang mga pangarap, pilit siyang bumangon.","translation":"In the midst of the **ruins** of his dreams, he tried hard to rise."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsusuot ng itinakdang kasuotan para sa isang partikular na pangkat, paaralan, o trabaho.
original_explanation: The daily struggle of every student and most office workers. It's that moment you transform from your pambahay-self to your professional/student-self. Bonus points if the uniform is uncomfortable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **mag-uniporme** bukas para sa flag ceremony.","translation":"You need to **wear a uniform** tomorrow for the flag ceremony."},{"sentence":"Ayaw na niyang **mag-uniporme** kaya nag-freelance na lang siya.","translation":"She didn't want to **wear a uniform** anymore, so she just went freelance."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapang ginagamit sa pagpihit o paghigpit ng mga tornilyo.
original_explanation: The official tool of every Filipino dad who says 'Ako na diyan.' Essential for assembling IKEA furniture you bought online and for threatening unruly cockroaches. From the Spanish 'destornillador'.
usage_notes: Often colloquially shortened to 'turnilyador'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiabot ng **destornilyador** para maikabit ko itong estante.","translation":"Please hand me the **screwdriver** so I can install this shelf."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mo ng Philips na **destornilyador** para sa tornilyong iyan.","translation":"You need a Philips **screwdriver** for that screw."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng silbato o ang pagsipol upang tawagin ang pansin ng isang tao, madalas sa paraang bastos o bilang babala.
original_explanation: The verb form of catcalling or getting someone's attention with a whistle. It can be the tanod `silbatuhan`-ing a snatcher, or, unfortunately, a creepy guy on the street `silbatuhan`-ing someone. Context is everything. One is for public safety, the other is for public nuisance.
usage_notes: Can have a neutral (e.g., referee whistling at a player) or negative/disrespectful connotation (e.g., catcalling).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sinilbatuhan** ng guwardiya ang magnanakaw para huminto.","translation":"The guard **whistled at** the thief to stop."},{"sentence":"Bastos ang **silbatuhan** ang mga babaeng dumadaan.","translation":"It's rude **to whistle at** women passing by."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mataas na opisyal sa Simbahang Katoliko na hinirang ng Papa; isang uri ng ibon na may matingkad na pulang balahibo; isang pangunahing numero (isa, dalawa, tatlo).
original_explanation: Ito yung boss level sa Simbahan, next kay Pope. O kaya yung kulay na parang dugo ng lipstick ng tita mong palaban. Pwede ring 'cardinal rule,' yung pinaka-basic na bawal, tulad ng "bawal umutang sa 5-6."
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa konteksto ng relihiyon, kulay, o bilang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Luis Antonio Tagle ay isang **kardinal** na Pilipino.","translation":"Luis Antonio Tagle is a Filipino **cardinal**."},{"sentence":"Ang kulay **kardinal** ay isang uri ng matingkad na pula.","translation":"The color **cardinal** is a type of bright red."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na baybay at bersyon ng 'nerbiyos'; isang estado ng pag-aalala, pagkabahala, o pagkatakot.
etymology: Colloquial shortening and respelling of Spanish 'nervios' ('nerves').
original_explanation: Same as 'nerbiyos', but this is the fast-food version. It's how people actually say it in a hurry. It's the spelling you'd use when texting your friend, "OMG teh, inaatake ako ng nerbyos, 'di ako prepared sa exam!" It's less formal, more conversational.
usage_notes: A common colloquial spelling and pronunciation of 'nerbiyos'. While widely used in informal communication, 'nerbiyos' (with an 'i') is preferred in formal writing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Grabe ang **nerbyos** ko kanina sa interview.","translation":"My **nerves** were really bad during the interview earlier."},{"sentence":"Tanggal **nerbyos** 'pag kasama ang barkada.","translation":"The **nervousness** goes away when I'm with friends."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang anyo ng pangangatwiran sa lohika na binubuo ng dalawang proposisyon (ang major premise at minor premise) na pinagbabatayan ng isang kongklusyon.
original_explanation: High-level logic na pang-philosophy class. Example: 'Lahat ng BPO agent puyat. Si Juan ay BPO agent. Samakatuwid, si Juan ay puyat.' It's basically connecting the dots using logic para ma-prove ang isang point. Parang pag-explain mo sa nanay mo kung bakit ka ginabi: 'Lahat ng may group project, umuuwi nang late. May group project kami. Kaya ako umuwi nang late.' See? Silohismo.
usage_notes: Isang termino na ginagamit sa lohika, pilosopiya, at pormal na debate.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ng abogado ang isang malinaw na **silohismo** upang patunayan ang kanyang punto sa harap ng hukom.","translation":"The lawyer used a clear **syllogism** to prove his point before the judge."}]

translation: to request; to wish for; to ask for
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapahayag ng isang kahilingan o pagnanais para sa isang bagay; makiusap.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you see a shooting star, blow a birthday candle, or slide into your crush's DMs. It's the polite version of 'gimme'. From asking your boss for a raise to asking the universe for a sign, you're 'humihiling'.
usage_notes: Can range from a simple request to a deep wish or prayer.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Humiling** ako sa Diyos na sana ay gumaling na ang aking ina.","translation":"I **prayed** to God that my mother would get well."},{"sentence":"**Humiling** ng dagdag na sahod ang mga manggagawa.","translation":"The workers **requested** for a salary increase."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pampublikong pagtatanghal ng mga likhang-sining, produkto, o iba pang mga bagay na may kahalagahan.
original_explanation: 'Yung art gallery show kung saan nakasabit 'yung mga painting ng friend mong artist. O 'yung sa World Trade Center na may mga booth para sa iba't ibang produkto. Ang eksibisyon ay parang "look what I/we can do" moment, pero for public viewing.
usage_notes: Madalas na ginagamit sa konteksto ng sining, kultura, at komersyo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumunta kami sa isang **eksibisyon** ng mga obra ni Juan Luna sa pambansang museo.","translation":"We went to an **exhibition** of Juan Luna's works at the national museum."},{"sentence":"May taunang **eksibisyon** ng mga bagong kotse sa mall.","translation":"There is an annual **exhibition** of new cars at the mall."}]

translation: to redeem; to pay off a pledge
