meaning_filipino: Ang pagbawi sa isang bagay na isinanla sa pamamagitan ng pagbabayad ng katumbas na halaga; o ang pagliligtas mula sa kasalanan o kaparusahan.
original_explanation: That feeling of victory when you finally go to the pawnshop (sanglaan) to get your jewelry back. "Yes, alahas, I have returned for you!" On a grander scale, it's what heroes and saviors do—they redeem people from a bad situation, whether it's from debt, danger, or a really bad hair day.
usage_notes: Has both a financial (pawning) and a spiritual/moral (redemption) context. This is the completed aspect (past tense).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais kong **tumubos** ng aking singsing sa sanglaan.","translation":"I want **to redeem** my ring from the pawnshop."},{"sentence":"Siya ang **tumubos** sa ating mga kasalanan.","translation":"He is the one who **redeemed** us from our sins."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng kawalan ng kaayusan dahil sa pagkawala o hindi pagkilala sa awtoridad o pamahalaan.
etymology: Isang varyant ng "anarkiya," na hiram sa Espanyol na "anarquía," mula sa Griyegong "anarkhia" (kawalan ng pinuno).
original_explanation: This is what happens when the teacher leaves the classroom, and the class president can't control anyone. Or when there's a piso fare sale and the website crashes. It's chaos, a free-for-all, every man for himself. Basically, EDSA on a Friday payday before a long weekend.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang hindi gaanong pormal o kolokyal na bersyon ng "anarkiya."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kung walang batas, magkakaroon ng **anarki** sa lipunan.","translation":"If there are no laws, there will be **anarchy** in society."},{"sentence":"Nagmistulang **anarki** ang pila nang biglang nagsiksikan ang mga tao.","translation":"The line turned into **anarchy** when the people suddenly started pushing."}]

translation: to oppose, to make an enemy of
meaning_filipino: Gawing kalaban; salungatin o tutulan ang isang tao o panig.
original_explanation: This is when you actively decide to go against someone. It's not just a disagreement; it's choosing to be on the opposite team. Like when you kalabanin your friend's toxic ex on their behalf, or when you decide to run against the incumbent barangay captain. Game on!
usage_notes: `kalabanin` is the act of making someone an enemy, while `labanan` is the act of fighting them.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **kalabanin** ang iyong mga magulang dahil gusto lang nila ang makabubuti sa iyo.","translation":"Do not **oppose** your parents because they only want what is best for you."},{"sentence":"Pinili niyang **kalabanin** ang korapsyon sa gobyerno.","translation":"He chose to **make an enemy of** corruption in the government."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi kaaya-aya sa paningin, pandinig, o asal; lumalabag sa pamantayan ng kagandahang-asal o kalinisan.
original_explanation: Yung tito mong nagjo-joke ng green sa family reunion, o yung kapitbahay mong lumalabas ng bahay na naka-briefs lang. Anything that makes you go "Huy, 'wag ganyan, may bata!" is probably indisente.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinuturing na **indisente** ang ganoong pananamit sa loob ng simbahan.","translation":"That kind of attire is considered **indecent** inside the church."},{"sentence":"Pinagsabihan siya dahil sa kanyang **indisente** na pag-uugali.","translation":"He was reprimanded for his **indecent** behavior."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong mahilig magtanong o mausisa.
original_explanation: Ito yung bata na laging may 'Bakit?'. Yung ka-team mo sa office na pagkatapos ng presentation ng boss, siya lang ang may 20 follow-up questions. Pwedeng sign of intelligence and curiosity, o pwedeng chismosa lang talaga. Sila yung human version ng Google search bar.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan sa pagiging mausisa ng isang tao. Maaaring ituring na positibo (curious) o bahagyang negatibo (nosy).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang batang **palatanong** ay madalas na matalino.","translation":"An **inquisitive** child is often intelligent."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa sinasabi mo sa kanya dahil **palatanong** iyan at baka malaman ang sikreto mo.","translation":"Be careful what you say to her because she's **fond of asking questions** and might find out your secret."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hanging may mataas na bilis at puwersa, karaniwang nararanasan tuwing may bagyo o masamang panahon.
original_explanation: This is PAGASA's favorite phrase. When you hear 'malakas na hangin' in the news, it's time to bring in the laundry, tie down the yero roof, and cancel your beach trip. It's the kind of wind that makes you walk diagonally and messes up your hair permanently. The official soundtrack of typhoon season.
usage_notes: A standard phrase used to describe windy conditions, especially during storms or typhoons.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa **malakas na hangin**, maraming puno ang natumba.","translation":"Because of the **strong wind**, many trees fell down."},{"sentence":"Nag-anunsyo ang PAGASA ng paparating na **malakas na hangin** at ulan.","translation":"PAGASA announced the coming of **strong winds** and rain."}]

translation: to doubt; to have reservations about
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng duda o kawalan ng katiyakan tungkol sa isang tao, bagay, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: That feeling when your friend says "5 minutes away na ako" but you know they just woke up. You're having doubts. It's the hesitation you feel when an online seller has zero reviews. "Huwag mo akong pag-alinlanganan," says the boyfriend who swears he was just "out with friends."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pag-alinlanganan** ang kanyang kakayahan dahil lamang siya ay bata pa.","translation":"Do not **doubt** his ability just because he is young."},{"sentence":"Mahirap hindi **pag-alinlanganan** ang isang alok na tila napakaganda para maging totoo.","translation":"It's hard not to **be suspicious of** an offer that seems too good to be true."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagbibigay ng kasiyahan o kaluguran sa mga pandama, isip, o damdamin; maganda sa paningin o pakiramdam.
original_explanation: This is the feeling you get when you see your salary credited to your bank account, or when your Grab ride arrives in 2 minutes. It's the opposite of traffic on EDSA. Anything that makes you go "Ah, nice" is kaaya-aya.
usage_notes: A very positive and versatile adjective used to describe people, places, experiences, and things.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakagandang pagmasdan ang **kaaya-aya** niyang mga ngiti.","translation":"It's so wonderful to watch her **pleasant** smiles."},{"sentence":"Humanap tayo ng lugar na **kaaya-aya** para sa ating bakasyon.","translation":"Let's look for a **pleasant** place for our vacation."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang matindi, nakasusulasok, at hindi kaaya-ayang amoy.
original_explanation: This is the smell that makes your nose wrinkle and your face go 'eww.' Think durian for first-timers, lumang bagoong, a blocked canal, or your gym clothes after a week. It's a smell that doesn't just enter your nose; it attacks it. Hindi lang siya mabaho, it's aggressively mabaho.
usage_notes: Exclusively used for strong, usually unpleasant smells.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **masangsang** na amoy na nanggagaling sa basurahan.","translation":"There is a **rank** smell coming from the trash can."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko makain ang durian dahil sa **masangsang** na amoy nito.","translation":"I can't eat durian because of its **pungent** smell."}]

translation: (slang) hope that for everyone; wish everyone had that
meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na pinaikling bersyon ng "sana all," na ginagamit upang ipahayag ang pagnanais na sana'y maranasan din ng lahat ang isang magandang bagay na nakita o narinig.
original_explanation: The official battle cry of the inggit-pikit crowd. When you see a friend's travel pics, a couple's sweet post, or someone's new iPhone, you just comment "naol." It's a shorter, punchier "sana all," a mix of envy and a genuine (or sarcastic) wish for universal good fortune.
usage_notes: Lubhang impormal at pangunahing ginagamit sa social media at kaswal na pag-uusap, lalo na sa mga kabataan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May bago siyang kotse? Wow, **naol**!","translation":"He has a new car? Wow, **wish everyone had that**!"},{"sentence":"In-love na raw siya. Ay, **naol**.","translation":"They say she's in love. Oh, **hope that for everyone**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabahagi o pagsasabi ng isang impormasyon, lalo na kung ito ay isang sikreto o tsismis.
etymology: From Swardspeak (Filipino gay lingo), possibly a playful onomatopoeic creation.
original_explanation: The Swardspeak (gay lingo) for "spill the tea!" When your marites friend says "I-spluk mo na, girl!", she's not asking you to vomit. She wants the full, unadulterated, chapter-and-verse details of the latest chika. To "spluk" is to unleash the information that everyone is dying to hear.
usage_notes: Primarily used in informal, conversational settings, especially among friends. The command form "I-spluk mo!" is very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang mahiya, i-**spluk** mo na ang totoong nangyari sa party.","translation":"Don't be shy, **spill** what really happened at the party."},{"sentence":"May isa-**spluk** ako sa'yo mamaya, 'wag kang mawawala.","translation":"I have something to **tell** you later, make sure you're there."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang idyoma na tumutukoy sa isang tao na taksil, espiya, o nagkakanulo sa kanyang mga kasamahan.
etymology: Idiomatic expression. The imagery suggests someone hiding their identity or betrayal under a long cloak, similar to spies or assassins in old stories.
original_explanation: Literally "long cape," but nobody's talking about superheroes here. This is classic Filipino `chismis` code for a traitor. The "long cape" hides their true intentions. Think of it as the person in your group chat who secretly screenshots your conversations and sends them to your boss or your ex. They're the `ahas` (snake) wearing a `mahabang kapa`.
usage_notes: This is a purely idiomatic expression. Using it literally to describe a long cape is possible but the idiomatic meaning is more prominent in certain contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa kanya, balita ko'y isa siyang **mahabang kapa** ng kalabang kumpanya.","translation":"Be careful with him, I heard he's a **spy** for the rival company."},{"sentence":"Ang **mahabang kapa** sa ating grupo ang nagkalat ng maling impormasyon.","translation":"The **traitor** in our group was the one who spread the wrong information."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng paggalang o pitagan sa kapwa. May mabuting asal at pag-uugali.
etymology: From Tagalog 'ma-' (prefix indicating having a quality) + 'galang' (respect).
original_explanation: This is the kid who always says 'po' and 'opo' and does the 'mano po' to their ninongs and ninangs. In the office, they're the one who doesn't steal your lunch from the fridge. Basically, the opposite of a 'Marites'.
usage_notes: A fundamental Filipino value. Describes a person's character and behavior towards others, especially elders.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magalang** na bata si Juan dahil lumaki siya sa kanyang mga lolo at lola.","translation":"Juan is a **respectful** child because he grew up with his grandparents."},{"sentence":"Kahit sa online meeting, dapat ay **magalang** pa rin ang pakikipag-usap.","translation":"Even in an online meeting, one should still communicate **politely**."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi pinahihintulutan; may pagbabawal o restriksiyon ayon sa batas, alituntunin, o kaugalian.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "no" in Filipino. You see it everywhere: "Bawal Umihi Dito" (Don't Pee Here), "Bawal Tumawid" (No Jaywalking). It's the word your parents used when you wanted to eat dessert before dinner. In a relationship, it's the "unspoken rules" you're not supposed to break. Basically, if something is bawal, just don't do it... unless you're feeling rebellious.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bawal** ang magtapon ng basura sa ilog.","translation":"It is **prohibited** to throw trash in the river."},{"sentence":"Talagang **bawal** sa kanya ang pagkain ng matatamis.","translation":"Sweets are strictly **forbidden** for him."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing paksa ng tsismis ang isang tao, bagay, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of making someone the 'main character' of your chika session. When you and your friends huddle in a corner and start whispering, 'Uy, alam mo ba si ano...', you're about to 'pagtsitsismisan' someone. It's the verb that fuels the Marites universe.
usage_notes: This is a verb focusing on the target of the gossip.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag nating **pagtsitsismisan** ang mga taong wala rito para ipagtanggol ang kanilang sarili.","translation":"Let's not **gossip about** people who aren't here to defend themselves."},{"sentence":"Ayaw kong **pagtsitsismisan** ang buhay ng may buhay.","translation":"I don't want **to gossip about** the lives of others."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pagkislap o pagningning ng isang bagay, karaniwan dahil sa repleksyon ng liwanag.
original_explanation: 'Yung mata ng crush mo 'pag nakikita ka niya, or 'yung diamond ring na sana all mayroon. It's that dazzling, shimmering effect that makes you go "Wow, shiny!" Parang glitters sa project noong elementary.
usage_notes: Ito ang kasalukuyang anyo (present progressive) ng pandiwang 'kumislap'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nangingislap** ang mga bituin sa madilim na kalangitan.","translation":"The stars are **sparkling** in the dark sky."},{"sentence":"**Nangingislap** sa tuwa ang kanyang mga mata nang matanggap niya ang regalo.","translation":"Her eyes were **glistening** with joy when she received the gift."}]

translation: to form, to constitute, to assemble
meaning_filipino: Pag-ugnay-ugnayin ang mga bahagi upang makabuo ng isang kabuuan; itatag o itayo ang isang grupo o organisasyon.
original_explanation: The act of putting something together, like assembling IKEA furniture without the manual, or trying to form a coherent group project with classmates who are always 'seen-zone.' 'Bubuin natin ang team' (Let's form the team) is the optimistic start before the scheduling nightmares begin. It's the verb form of 'buo' (whole).
usage_notes: A formal-sounding verb often used in organizational or constructive contexts. The future tense is 'bubuin', past is 'binuo', and present is 'binubuo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinusubukan nilang **bubuin** muli ang kanilang nasirang pamilya.","translation":"They are trying **to put** their broken family back **together** again."},{"sentence":"Ang komite ay **bubuin** ng mga kinatawan mula sa iba't ibang sektor.","translation":"The committee will **be composed** of representatives from different sectors."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang istraktura o lugar kung saan isinasagawa ang mga seremonya at pag-aalay sa isang diyos o espirituwal na nilalang.
etymology: From 'damba' (to rise up, to lunge) + '-han' (place indicator), suggesting a raised place.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'main character' spot in a church. It's where the priest does his thing, the place you stare at when you're praying for a sign about your crush, or wondering what to have for lunch. It's the sacred stage.
usage_notes: Primarily used in a religious or ceremonial context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-alay sila ng mga bulaklak sa **dambahan**.","translation":"They offered flowers at the **altar**."},{"sentence":"Ang **dambahan** ay napapalamutian ng ginto.","translation":"The **altar** is decorated with gold."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na matagal nang naitabi o hindi na bago, partikular sa mga butil tulad ng bigas o mais na nagiging mas maganda ang kalidad kapag naluto.
original_explanation: This is the OG, the classic, the 'vintage' before 'vintage' was cool. Think of bigas that's been chilling in the bodega for a while, making it fluffier when cooked. It's the opposite of that 'new relationship energy'; this one's stable, tested, and true.
usage_notes: Most commonly used to describe rice ('bigas na laon') which expands more and is less sticky when cooked compared to new rice ('bigas na bago').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas gusto ni Lola ang kaning mula sa bigas na **laon**.","translation":"Grandma prefers rice from **aged** rice grains."},{"sentence":"Maraming stock ng mais na **laon** sa kamalig.","translation":"There is a large stock of **old** corn in the granary."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang yugto sa buhay o karera ng isang tao o grupo kung saan sunud-sunod ang kanilang mga kabiguan, pagbaba ng kasikatan, o hindi magandang pagganap.
etymology: From English 'flop' + 'era', popularized in online fan culture.
original_explanation: That phase in your life when you can't seem to do anything right. Your projects fail, your crush ghosts you, and even your instant noodles get soggy. It's when the universe seems to be saying, 'Bes, 'di para sa 'yo 'to.' But don't worry, like all eras, it eventually ends... hopefully.
usage_notes: Used to describe a period of decline or multiple failures for celebrities, artists, or even for oneself in a humorous, self-deprecating way.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mukhang nasa **flop era** ngayon ang paborito kong banda dahil hindi na gaanong maganda ang mga bago nilang kanta.","translation":"It seems my favorite band is in their **flop era** because their new songs aren't that good anymore."},{"sentence":"Feeling ko nasa **flop era** ako, lahat ng ina-applyan kong trabaho, rejected ako.","translation":"I feel like I'm in my **flop era**, I get rejected by all the jobs I apply for."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang silid sa isang bahay o gusali na pangunahing ginagamit para sa pagtulog.
etymology: Compound word from "silid" (room) and "tulugan" (sleeping place, from root 'tulog').
original_explanation: The most accurate description of a bedroom. It's your fortress of solitude, where you can finally take off your 'outside' personality (and your pants). The place where '5 more minutes' turns into an hour and where your best ideas (and hugot moments) happen at 3 AM.
usage_notes: More descriptive but less common in casual conversation than 'kwarto'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May tatlong **silid-tulugan** ang bago nilang bahay.","translation":"Their new house has three **bedrooms**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maingay, may natutulog sa **silid-tulugan**.","translation":"Don't be noisy, someone is sleeping in the **bedroom**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang makaramdam ng matinding pag-ayaw o pagkasuklam sa isang tao, bagay, o sitwasyon dahil ito ay marumi, imoral, o hindi kaaya-aya.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `pan-` at salitang ugat na `diri` (disgust) at hulaping `-an`.
original_explanation: It's the feeling you get when you see a week-old Tupperware in the office fridge, or when someone double-dips their chip in the communal salsa. It's that 'eww factor' reaction. Your face literally contorts. 'Pinandidirihan kita' is the classier way of saying 'Yuck, you!'
usage_notes: Isang masidhing pandiwa na nagpapahayag ng pagkasuklam. Kadalasang ginagamit sa isang bagay o kilos na itinuturing na marumi o kasuklam-suklam.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Talaga namang **pandirihan** mo ang basurahang hindi kinokolekta nang isang linggo.","translation":"You would really **be disgusted with** the trash that hasn't been collected for a week."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang gumawa ng bagay na **pandirihan** ng mga tao.","translation":"Don't do things that people will **be disgusted with**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang modernong balbal na ekspresyon na pinaikli mula sa "aw, sakit," na nagpapahiwatig ng pagkadismaya, kalungkutan, o pagkaasiwa.
etymology: A modern contraction of "Aw, sakit" (Oh, painful).
original_explanation: Your one-word reaction when your crush posts a picture with their jowa. It's the Gen Z version of saying 'sakit naman' or 'sad life'. It's the sound of digital heartbreak and minor inconveniences. "Bumagsak ako sa exam? Awit."
usage_notes: Exclusively used as modern slang, especially online and among younger Filipinos. Often used as a standalone comment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Wala nang data? **Awit**.","translation":"No more data? **That sucks**."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko si crush may kasamang iba. **Awit**.","translation":"I saw my crush with someone else. **Ouch**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghiwa nang manipis gamit ang isang matalas na kasangkapan tulad ng kutsilyo.
original_explanation: That moment of truth when you're making sinigang and you need to slice the veggies. It's the action your nanay does with lightning speed at the palengke when you buy fish or meat. "Yung pag-slice mo ng sibuyas na parang nag-audition ka for a cooking show."
usage_notes: This is the completed aspect (past tense) of the verb. The infinitive is 'gumayat', present is 'gumagayat', and future is 'gagayat'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maingat siyang **gumayat** ng kamatis para sa ensalada.","translation":"He carefully **sliced** tomatoes for the salad."},{"sentence":"**Gumayat** ako ng karne para sa ating hapunan.","translation":"I **sliced** meat for our dinner."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa kalagayan na hindi makapagsalita, kadalasan dahil sa matinding gulat, takot, hiya, o pagkamangha.
etymology: Mula sa "di-" (not), "maka-" (ability prefix), at "imik" (utterance, a peep).
original_explanation: 'Yung moment na tinanong ka ng crush mo, "Crush mo rin ba ako?" Tapos para kang na-short circuit at hindi ka makasagot. 'Yan 'yung di-makaimik. Pwede rin 'pag nahuli ka ng nanay mo na hindi mo pa hinuhugasan 'yung mga plato. Speechless ka sa sermon na aabutin mo.
usage_notes: Very common expression for being at a loss for words.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Di-makaimik** siya sa gulat nang makita ang sorpresang inihanda para sa kanya.","translation":"She was **speechless** with surprise when she saw the surprise prepared for her."},{"sentence":"Naiwan siyang **di-makaimik** matapos marinig ang masamang balita.","translation":"He was left **unable to speak** after hearing the bad news."}]

translation: to command; to order; to instruct
meaning_filipino: Magbigay ng isang direktiba, kautusan, o tagubilin sa isang tao upang gawin ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is what your mom does on a Saturday morning ("Linisin mo 'to! Hugasan mo 'yan!"). It's what your team lead does when delegating tasks for a project. It’s the power move of telling someone what to do. Not to be confused with ordering food ('umorder'), this is about giving instructions. Being the one to `mag-utos` makes you the boss, at least for that moment.
usage_notes: The `mag-` prefix indicates the actor is the focus. The one giving the command is the subject of the sentence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang basta-basta **mag-utos** kung hindi mo naman alam ang buong sitwasyon.","translation":"Don't just **give commands** if you don't know the whole situation."},{"sentence":"Ang manager ang laging **nag-uutos** sa mga empleyado.","translation":"The manager is the one who always **instructs** the employees."}]

translation: will be made to sweat; will perspire
meaning_filipino: Ang maranasan ang paglabas ng pawis sa katawan, kadalasan dahil sa init, pagod, o kaba.
original_explanation: What happens when you commute via MRT at 5 PM, eat extra spicy Bicol Express, or get called for a surprise presentation by your boss. "Grabe ang init, siguradong papawisin ako mamaya sa gym."
usage_notes: Future tense. Can be used for oneself ("Papawisin ako") or to describe an action that will make someone sweat ("Papawisin ka ng ehersisyong ito").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magdala ka ng pamaypay dahil tiyak na **papawisin** ka sa prusisyon.","translation":"Bring a fan because you will surely **perspire** during the procession."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang kabahan sa interview, baka **papawisin** ka nang malamig.","translation":"Don't be nervous in the interview, you might get cold **sweats**."}]

meaning_filipino: Paulit-ulit na paggalaw ng ulo pakanan at pakaliwa bilang tanda ng pagtanggi, pagkadismaya, o hindi pagsang-ayon.
original_explanation: This is the universal sign for 'nope,' 'tsk-tsk,' or 'I can't even.' Your nanay does this when she sees your messy room. You do this when you see the price of onions. It's a silent, but very loud, commentary on a situation that is just... disappointing.
usage_notes: A reduplicated form of 'iling' (to shake the head), often used with 'pa-' to describe the manner of an action. It's almost always used with a verb of perception or being, e.g., 'Napailing-iling na lang ako.' (I just found myself shaking my head.)
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pailing-iling** na lamang ang matanda habang pinapanood ang magulong trapiko.","translation":"The old man was just **shaking his head** while watching the chaotic traffic."},{"sentence":"Sumagot siya nang **pailing-iling**, hudyat na hindi siya sang-ayon.","translation":"He answered by **shaking his head**, a sign that he did not agree."}]

meaning_filipino: Paggawa ng tunog na "click"; o sa makabagong gamit, ang pagkakaroon ng mabuting ugnayan o pagkakasundo sa isang tao o grupo.
etymology: From English 'click'. The 'nagki-' prefix is a modern, informal way to form the progressive aspect for loanwords, deviating from the standard 'nag- + (reduplicated first syllable of root)'.
original_explanation: This is the feeling when, on a first date, you just know, "This is it!" You both vibe perfectly, like a 100% match on a dating app. It's also the literal sound your mouse makes while you're online shopping at 3 AM. Figuratively: "Uy, nagkiclick na kami ng bago kong team lead!"
usage_notes: Often used in informal, conversational contexts, especially among younger generations or in office/urban settings. The double meaning (literal sound and figurative compatibility) is very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kanina pa **nagkiclick** nang paulit-ulit ang mouse niya pero ayaw gumana.","translation":"His mouse has been **clicking** repeatedly for a while now, but it won't work."},{"sentence":"Masaya ako dahil **nagkiclick** na ang mga personalidad ng mga bagong miyembro sa team.","translation":"I'm happy because the personalities of the new team members are finally **clicking** (getting along)."}]

translation: to wear a shawl or scarf
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsuot o pagpapatong ng alampay, isang uri ng tela na karaniwang inilalagay sa balikat.
original_explanation: This is the action of draping a shawl over your shoulders. It’s very 'dalagang Pilipina' or 'tita' vibes. You do this when the AC in the office is too cold, when you're going to church, or when you want to add a touch of elegance to your outfit. It’s the verb form of looking modest and chic at the same time.
usage_notes: 'Alampay' refers to a shawl, scarf, or any similar piece of cloth draped over the shoulders.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **mag-alampay** tuwing nanonood ng sine dahil sa lamig.","translation":"She likes to **wear a shawl** whenever she watches a movie because of the cold."},{"sentence":"**Nag-alampay** ang lola ng isang mamahaling seda para sa okasyon.","translation":"The grandmother **wore** a shawl made of expensive silk for the occasion."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o bagay na pumapalit o humahalili sa posisyon, tungkulin, o lugar ng iba.
original_explanation: Yung a-assume ng position mo pag nag-resign ka na sa trabaho. O kaya, yung rebound mo para lang may 'jowa' ka ulit. Siya yung pampalit, ang taga-take over.
usage_notes: Often used in formal contexts like politics (successor to a throne/office) or work (substitute). 'Panghalili' is a more common form for 'substitute'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **halili** sa trono ng hari?","translation":"Who is the **successor** to the king's throne?"},{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng **halili** para kay Ana habang siya ay naka-leave.","translation":"We need a **substitute** for Ana while she is on leave."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang panahon kung saan ang mga influencer sa social media ay may malaking epekto sa kultura, marketing, at opinyon ng publiko.
etymology: Mula sa pariralang Ingles na 'influencer era'.
original_explanation: This is the timeline we're currently living in. It's the age where a TikTok dance has more cultural impact than a presidential speech, and where 'content is king' is the 11th commandment. Welcome to the influencer era, where everyone has a ring light and a dream of unboxing PR packages.
usage_notes: Used to describe the current state of media and marketing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa gitna ng **influencer era**, mas naging mahalaga ang digital marketing.","translation":"In the middle of the **influencer era**, digital marketing became more important."},{"sentence":"Maraming nagsasabi na malapit nang matapos ang **influencer era**.","translation":"Many are saying that the **influencer era** is about to end."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang alternatibong baybay para sa 'bhe', na isang katawagan ng paglalambing.
etymology: Isang baryasyon sa pagbaybay ng 'bhe', na nagmula sa 'babe'.
original_explanation: This is 'bhe' but with more jeje flair. It's the same term of endearment, just spelled with a little extra... character. The 'h' and 'i' are there for emotional support. 'Hi bhie!' just hits different from 'Hi bhe!'.
usage_notes: Madalas na iniuugnay sa 'jejemon' o mga pacute na estilo ng pagsulat online noong huling bahagi ng 2000s at 2010s, ngunit malawak pa ring naiintindihan at ginagamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Good morning, **bhie**! Gising na.","translation":"Good morning, **bhie**! Wake up."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malagkit na sangkap na nagmumula sa mga halaman, lalo na sa mga puno ng pino, na tumitigas kapag nalantad sa hangin. Ginagamit ito sa paggawa ng barnis, gamot, at insenso.
original_explanation: That sticky stuff from trees that gets on your hands and won't come off. Nowadays, it's what your artsy tita or that Shopee seller uses to make those cute keychains with flowers trapped inside. The OG amber.
usage_notes: 'Resin' (the English spelling) is also commonly used, especially in the context of modern crafts and industrial applications.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **resina** mula sa puno ng pili ay ginagamit sa iba't ibang produkto.","translation":"The **resin** from the pili tree is used in various products."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang gumawa ng alahas gamit ang epoxy **resina**.","translation":"She loves making jewelry using epoxy **resin**."}]

translation: to enjoin; to instruct; to commend
meaning_filipino: Magbigay ng utos, payo, o paalala na dapat sundin o isakatuparan, lalo na kung aalis o bago mamatay.
original_explanation: This is the official "Last Will and Testament" verb. It’s what your Lola tells you before she goes to the palengke: "Huwag magpapasok ng kung sino-sino!" It's a command with weight, a final instruction, the OG "read the instructions carefully before proceeding." The ultimate habilin.
usage_notes: Formal and serious tone. Often associated with imparting wisdom, last wishes, or important responsibilities.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bago siya pumanaw, **itinagubilin** ng lolo ang pangangalaga sa kanilang lupain.","translation":"Before he passed away, grandfather **enjoined** the care of their land."},{"sentence":"**Itinagubilin** ng guro na pag-aralan namin ang susunod na kabanata.","translation":"The teacher **instructed** us to study the next chapter."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa matematika, isang bilang na nagsasaad kung ilang beses dapat i-multiply sa sarili ang isang batayang bilang (base).
original_explanation: That tiny number in your math class that has major trust issues and needs to be on top of everyone else. It's the reason why your calculator has an 'x^y' button you rarely use. It's what makes small numbers suddenly become huge, like your credit card debt after a 12.12 sale.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa konteksto ng matematika. Mas karaniwang ginagamit ang salitang Ingles na 'exponent' sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa 'dalawa na may **esponente** na tatlo' (2³), ang sagot ay walo.","translation":"In 'two with an **exponent** of three' (2³), the answer is eight."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpapakita ng kayabangan sa isang tao; o isang paligsahan o sitwasyon kung saan nagpapagalingan sa paghahambog ang dalawa o higit pang tao.
etymology: Mula sa salitang ugat na "yabang" at hulaping "-an".
original_explanation: Ito 'yung verb form. When you flex on someone. "Huwag mo akong yabangan, pareho lang tayong nagco-commute." It can also mean a showdown of flexing, like two hypebeasts comparing their limited-edition sneakers. A "who has more" contest.
usage_notes: Can mean "to direct arrogance at someone" or "a mutual exchange of arrogance." The context clarifies the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula na naman silang mag**yabangan** tungkol sa kanilang mga bagong cellphone.","translation":"They started to **boastfully compare** their new cellphones again."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niya akong **yabangan** pero hindi ko na lang pinansin.","translation":"He tried to **act boastfully towards** me but I just ignored him."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng mahinang tunog na may panginginig na karaniwang ginagawa ng isang pusa kapag ito ay masaya o kontento.
original_explanation: That vibrating sound your cat makes when you hit the perfect scratching spot. It's the ultimate sign of cat-isfaction. In human terms, it's the feeling you get when your GrabFood arrives earlier than expected or when your salary finally comes in. "Nag-pu-**purr** 'yung pusa sa kandungan ko."
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa Taglish, lalo na ng mga may-ari ng alagang hayop. Ang katutubong salita sa Tagalog ay "huning."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lakas mag-**purr** ng pusa ko kapag hinihimas ko siya.","translation":"My cat **purrs** loudly when I pet it."},{"sentence":"Narinig mo ba ang **purr** niya? Mukhang masaya siya.","translation":"Did you hear its **purr**? It seems happy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng manipis at malutong na pagkaing pangmeryenda, karaniwang gawa sa patatas, mais, o iba pang gulay na pinirito.
original_explanation: The official fuel for any movie marathon, inuman session, or late-night chismisan. Whether it's cheese, BBQ, or sour cream flavor, 'chips' is the universal term for that crunchy, salty snack that you can't stop eating once you open the bag. Best paired with a cold soft drink.
usage_notes: Universally understood in the Philippines to mean snack chips, not French fries (which are called 'fries').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili ka ng **chips** at softdrinks para sa party.","translation":"Buy some **chips** and softdrinks for the party."},{"sentence":"Naubos ko ang isang buong bag ng **chips** habang nanonood ng K-drama.","translation":"I finished a whole bag of **chips** while watching a K-drama."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-aaruga, pag-aalaga, at pagbibigay proteksyon, lalo na sa isang mas mahina o nangangailangan.
etymology: From the root 'kandili' (to care for, to protect), with the 'pagka-' prefix forming a noun that refers to the manner or quality of the action.
original_explanation: This is your lola's level of care. Not just 'take care,' but the full package: feeding you until you can't move, checking if you're cold, and giving you unsolicited but loving advice. It’s the ultimate TLC, Pinoy-style, often with a sense of protectiveness.
usage_notes: Carries a deeper, more protective connotation than 'pag-aalaga' (caring). It implies sheltering someone from harm.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa **pagkakandili** ng kanyang mga magulang, lumaki siyang may tiwala sa sarili.","translation":"Because of his parents' **nurturing**, he grew up with self-confidence."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkakandili** sa mga ulila ay isang marangal na gawain.","translation":"The **protection and care** for orphans is a noble deed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay sa isang tao, bagay, o sitwasyon sa kalagayang may panganib o kapahamakan.
original_explanation: That thing your mom warns you about 24/7. Crossing the street without looking? 'Huwag mong isapanganib ang buhay mo!' To **magsapanganib** is to deliberately or carelessly put something or someone in a 'delikado' situation, like investing all your savings in a sketchy crypto coin.
usage_notes: This is an object-focused verb. The actor causes something else to be in danger. It is more common to use 'isapanganib'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagtatapon ng basura sa ilog ay **magsasapanganib** sa kalusugan ng komunidad.","translation":"Throwing trash in the river will **endanger** the health of the community."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **magsapanganib** ang ating misyon dahil lang sa isang pagkakamali.","translation":"Don't **jeopardize** our mission just because of one mistake."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagyukod o pagluhod bilang tanda ng paggalang, lalo na sa kontekstong panrelihiyon.
original_explanation: This is that super-formal, old-school move of kneeling out of respect, usually in a church. It's not just 'luhod' (kneel); it has that extra 'oomph' of reverence, like you're about to meet the final boss of holiness. Think of your lola telling you to do it before you even see the altar.
usage_notes: A very formal and rare word, mostly found in religious or literary contexts. The common term is 'lumuhod'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lumikmo** ang mga deboto sa harap ng poon.","translation":"The devotees **knelt in reverence** before the sacred image."},{"sentence":"Sa lumang nobela, **lumikmo** ang binata sa paanan ng dalaga.","translation":"In the old novel, the young man **knelt** at the maiden's feet."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na may malalim na kaalaman sa kompyuter at network na ginagamit ang kakayahan upang makapasok sa isang sistema nang walang pahintulot.
original_explanation: Ito yung kaibigan mong techie na kayang i-recover yung deleted messages mo sa Messenger or alamin kung sino'ng nag-stalk sa'yo (pero 'di totoo yun, ha?). Sa totoong buhay, sila yung mga either nagpo-protect sa system ng bangko o yung sinusubukang pasukin ito. Pwedeng good guy (white hat) o bad guy (black hat).
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng teknolohiya at cyber security. Bagaman may negatibong konotasyon, maaari rin itong tumukoy sa isang dalubhasa sa kompyuter.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **hacker** diumano ang nag-leak ng mga pribadong impormasyon.","translation":"A **hacker** allegedly leaked the private information."},{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng isang 'ethical **hacker**' para subukan ang seguridad ng ating sistema.","translation":"We need an 'ethical **hacker**' to test our system's security."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbibigay ng mga kinakailangang bagay, tulad ng pagkain, pera, o suporta, para sa isang tao, pamilya, o gawain.
original_explanation: This is the adulting version of 'ambag'. It's how you fund your life, your family's needs, or a project. It's the 'supplying the budget' part, whether it's for the monthly bills, the family outing, or the group project's materials. The reason why everyone needs a 'sideline.'
usage_notes: Strongly associated with financial or material support and sustenance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagtutustos** sa pag-aaral ng mga anak ang kanyang pangunahing prayoridad.","translation":"The **financing** for the children's education is his main priority."},{"sentence":"Mahirap ang **pagtutustos** sa isang malaking pamilya.","translation":"**Providing** for a large family is difficult."}]

translation: to feign sickness; to pretend to be sick
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapanggap o pagkukunwaring may sakit upang makaiwas sa isang gawain o responsibilidad.
original_explanation: The classic move to get out of a Monday morning meeting, a surprise quiz, or a family gathering you don't want to go to. It's the 'acting' you do—a little cough here, a fake groan there—to secure a valid excuse. The national sport of students and some employees.
usage_notes: Ang anyong pandiwa ay 'mag-sakit-sakitan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mag-sakit-sakitan** para lang hindi makapasok sa eskwela.","translation":"Don't **pretend to be sick** just so you don't have to go to school."},{"sentence":"Nahuli ng nanay ang batang nag-**sasakit-sakitan** dahil bigla itong tumakbo para maglaro.","translation":"The mother caught the child who was **feigning sickness** because he suddenly ran off to play."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa kalangitan na may maraming ulap; hindi gaanong nasisikatan ng araw.
original_explanation: The sky's mood when it can't decide if it wants to be sunny or rainy. It’s perfect weather for an outdoor event until it suddenly pours. Also describes your vision without your glasses or the future of your love life. "Medyo **maulap** pa ang plano natin" means "Our plans are still a bit unclear."
usage_notes: Describes the sky's condition. Can be used figuratively to mean 'unclear' or 'hazy'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabuti at **maulap** ngayon, hindi masyadong mainit maglakad.","translation":"It's good that it's **cloudy** today, it's not too hot to walk."},{"sentence":"Naging **maulap** ang kanyang paningin dahil sa pagod.","translation":"His vision became **hazy** due to fatigue."}]

meaning_filipino: Inilalarawan ang isang tao o sitwasyon na walang suwerte o nakararanas ng kamalasan.
etymology: Mula sa "sama" (masama) + pang-angkop na "-ng" + "palad" (kapalaran). Literal na "masamang kapalaran".
original_explanation: This is the universe telling you, "Not today, bes." Ikaw yung nakapila sa lotto tapos yung nasa unahan mo ang nanalo. Ikaw yung nag-aral para sa exam, pero a-absent pala yung prof. You're the main character in a series of unfortunate events.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa mga dramatikong o pampanitikang konteksto. Maaari ring maging pangngalan ("ang samaing-palad" - ang taong walang suwerte).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **samaing-palad** na binata ay nawalan ng trabaho at kasintahan sa iisang araw.","translation":"The **unfortunate** young man lost his job and girlfriend on the same day."},{"sentence":"Maraming **samaing-palad** na pamilya ang nawalan ng tirahan dahil sa bagyo.","translation":"Many **unlucky** families lost their homes because of the typhoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na hindi nakasanayan o hindi karaniwang ginagawa ng isang tao.
original_explanation: When your friend who only drinks instant coffee suddenly orders a V60 drip single-origin whatever, that's **hindi gawi**. It's doing something out of character, like a night owl waking up at 5 AM to jog. It’s the feeling of awkwardness when you're forced to do something you don't normally do, like wearing formal clothes when you live in pambahay.
usage_notes: Describes an action or situation that is out of the ordinary for a person. Often used as 'hindi ko gawi' (it's not my habit).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hindi gawi** ni Ana ang manood ng horror movies kaya takot na takot siya.","translation":"It's **not a habit** for Ana to watch horror movies, that's why she was so scared."},{"sentence":"Ang paggising ng maaga ay **hindi ko gawi**, pero kailangan para sa trabaho.","translation":"Waking up early is **not my custom**, but it's necessary for work."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagtitipon o piging kung saan ang mga dumadalo ay nagsusuot ng mga maskara o balatkayo bilang bahagi ng kasuotan.
original_explanation: Basically a party where you can hide your face. It's like your online persona, but in real life. Perfect for when you want to gossip about your officemates without them knowing it's you, or when you want to feel like you're in a historical drama. It's the ultimate "it's complicated" relationship status, but for a party.
usage_notes: A specific, somewhat formal term. "Masquerade party" is more common in modern conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumalo kami sa isang marangyang **sayawan ng mga nakabalatkayo** sa isang lumang mansyon.","translation":"We attended a luxurious **masquerade ball** in an old mansion."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, kumpanya, o entidad na nagdadala ng mga produkto o kalakal mula sa ibang bansa papasok sa sariling bansa.
original_explanation: Sila 'yung mga big boss na nag-aangkat ng mga produkto from other countries. Kung ikaw 'yung taga-order ng sapatos galing US para ibenta sa mga kaibigan mo, in a way, isa kang micro-**importador**.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kumpanya nila ang pangunahing **importador** ng bigas sa bansa.","translation":"Their company is the main **importer** of rice in the country."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng lisensya upang maging isang lehitimong **importador**.","translation":"A license is needed to become a legitimate **importer**."}]

translation: A type of dried flour noodle
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pinatuyong pansit na yari sa harina, na karaniwang iniluluto bilang pancit canton.
etymology: Mula sa Hokkien Chinese na "kàn-thâu" na tumutukoy sa isang uri ng pagkain. Ipinangalan din sa rehiyon ng Canton (Guangdong) sa Tsina.
original_explanation: The official midnight snack of every Filipino student, BPO agent, and heartbroken soul. It's a five-minute solution to hunger that comes in 'Kalamansi', 'Chili-Mansi', and 'Original' flavors. Cooking canton is a national skill, and the debate on whether to put the seasoning first or last is a national issue.
usage_notes: Karaniwang tumutukoy sa instant pancit canton, bagaman maaari rin itong tumukoy sa tradisyonal na lutong ulam.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magluto ka nga ng **canton**, nagugutom ako.","translation":"Please cook some **canton** noodles, I'm hungry."},{"sentence":"Paborito kong almusal ang **canton** na may itlog.","translation":"My favorite breakfast is **canton** noodles with an egg."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na sadyang gumagawa ng mga bagay upang makuha ang atensyon ng iba; ang akto ng paghingi ng atensyon.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "pa-" (nagpapahiwatig ng paghiling) at "pansin".
original_explanation: The official Tagalog word for "KSP" (Kulang Sa Pansin). It’s that person in your group chat who posts cryptic "sad" statuses for replies, or the one who talks loudly in a quiet cafe. It's a low-key insult for someone doing the most for a little bit of validation. We all know one.
usage_notes: Madalas na may negatibong konotasyon. Maaaring gamitin bilang pang-uri ("Siya ay papansin") o pangngalan ("Isa siyang papansin").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigil-tigilan mo nga 'yang pagiging **papansin** mo sa social media.","translation":"Stop your **attention-seeking** behavior on social media."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo na siyang pansinin, **papansin** lang 'yan.","translation":"Don't mind him, he's just an **attention-seeker**."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa lahat ng oras o pagkakataon; madalas o palagian.
original_explanation: The default setting for your nanay's sermons, your pagiging 'marupok', and the traffic in EDSA. It's the opposite of 'minsan'. If your Jowa says, 'Ikaw **lagi** nasa isip ko,' a part of you is kilig, and a part of you is thinking, 'Weh, 'di nga?'
usage_notes: Ang 'palagi' ay isang karaniwang baryasyon nito at madalas na ipinagpapalit ang gamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lagi** siyang huli sa klase.","translation":"He is **always** late for class."},{"sentence":"Bakit ka **lagi** nakasimangot tuwing umaga?","translation":"Why are you **always** frowning every morning?"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao o bagay na nasa proseso ng pagpanaw o malapit nang masira o mawakasan.
original_explanation: This describes someone or something on their last leg. 'Yung cellphone mong 1% na lang ang battery, mamamatay na 'yan. O 'yung bida sa drama na umuubo ng dugo, he's in a dying state. It's the '-ing' form of the end.
usage_notes: Functions as an adjective or a noun referring to 'the one who is dying'. Can be used for living beings or inanimate objects (like batteries or engines).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inalagaan niya ang kanyang asong **mamamatay** hanggang sa huling sandali.","translation":"He took care of his **dying** dog until its last moment."},{"sentence":"Parang **mamamatay** na ang makina ng sasakyan dahil sa kakaibang tunog nito.","translation":"The car's engine sounds like it's **about to die** because of its strange noise."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy o may kaugnayan sa rektum, ang huling bahagi ng malaking bituka.
original_explanation: Let's be mature about this. It's a medical term for anything related to your... exit-only area. Like a rectal exam. It’s a word you hope you only hear from a doctor and not from a chismosa neighbor.
usage_notes: Halos eksklusibong ginagamit sa mga medikal o siyentipikong konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lagnat ng sanggol ay mas tumpak na nasusukat sa pamamagitan ng **rektal** na thermometer.","translation":"A baby's fever is more accurately measured using a **rectal** thermometer."},{"sentence":"May mga gamot na ibinibigay sa paraang **rektal**.","translation":"There are medicines that are administered in a **rectal** manner."}]

translation: to make something grow; to charge interest
meaning_filipino: Palakihin o paramihin ang isang bagay. Maaari rin itong mangahulugan ng pagpapatong ng interes sa isang utang o puhunan.
original_explanation: This word has two main vibes. Vibe 1: The wholesome farmer vibe. "To make something grow." You patubuin seeds into plants. Vibe 2: The "5-6" lender vibe. "To make money grow by adding interest." You lend 100 pesos, and you tell the person to pay you back 120. You just made your money "grow" by 20 pesos. That's the patubuin part. It’s all about making something multiply, whether it’s plants or cash.
usage_notes: Ang kahulugan ay nag-iiba nang malaki depende sa konteksto, mula sa agrikultura hanggang sa pananalapi.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **patubuin** ang mga buto ng kamatis sa kanilang bakuran.","translation":"She tried **to grow** tomato seeds in their yard."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo masyadong **patubuin** ang utang ko, baka hindi ko na mabayaran.","translation":"Don't **charge** too much **interest** on my debt, I might not be able to pay it back."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sining ng malinaw at mabisang pagsasalita sa publiko, na may diin sa tamang pagbigkas, tono, at kilos.
original_explanation: This is the 'how you say it' part of speaking. Yung paano ka magsalita na parang beauty queen sa Q&A portion, with confidence and a dazzling smile. Hindi lang basta 'what' you say, but 'how' you deliver the lines. Think of the intense training newscasters and hosts go through. That's elokusyon.
usage_notes: Isang teknikal at medyo pormal na termino na madalas marinig sa larangan ng teatro, brodkasting, at pampublikong pagsasalita.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-aral siya ng **elokusyon** upang mapabuti ang kanyang pagsasalita sa entablado.","translation":"She studied **elocution** to improve her speech on stage."}]

translation: to strike with the back of the hand; to backhand
meaning_filipino: Ang paghampas o pagpalo gamit ang likod ng palad.
etymology: From 'tabig' (a strike with the back of the hand) with the -um- infix.
original_explanation: The OG 'sampal' but with a different flavor. It's less of a dramatic confrontation and more of a "get that thing away from me" flick. Imagine seeing a huge ipis crawling on your desk; you don't caress it, you 'tumabig' it with your notebook. It’s a swat, a flick, a gesture of annoyance.
usage_notes: This action is usually quick and often a reaction of surprise or disgust.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa gulat, **tumabig** niya ang baso kaya ito nabasag.","translation":"Out of shock, he **struck** the glass with the back of his hand, causing it to break."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng kalyo o pagiging magaspang at makapal ng balat dahil sa patuloy na pagkiskis, presyon, o mabigat na gawain.
original_explanation: Yung kamay ng mga nagbubuhat ng bakal sa gym o 'yung paa na laging naka-tsinelas sa sementadong kalsada. It's the body's natural way of saying, 'Okay, I see we're doing this a lot, so let me just build some armor here.' The opposite of 'kutis-mayaman'.
usage_notes: Often used to describe hands or feet that have undergone hard labor. The verb form is 'nagkakangalot'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ngalot** na ang mga palad ng karpintero dahil sa araw-araw na paggamit ng martilyo.","translation":"The carpenter's palms are **calloused** from using a hammer every day."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya ikinahihiya ang kanyang mga paang **ngalot** dahil tanda ito ng kanyang pagsisikap.","translation":"She is not ashamed of her **calloused** feet because they are a sign of her hard work."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginagawa sa paraang pangkalahatan, sabay-sabay, o walang pagpili; para sa lahat.
original_explanation: This is the "no-filter, no-exceptions" mode. Pag sinabing "lahatan ang bayad," it means everyone pays the same, no student discounts, no senior citizen perks. It's the opposite of being selective. Parang group project na "lahatan ang bagsak" kasi isa lang ang gumawa. Ouch.
usage_notes: Describes the manner in which something is done (i.e., to everyone/everything).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagtaas ng presyo ay **lahatan** at ramdam ng bawat pamilya.","translation":"The price increase is **general** and felt by every family."},{"sentence":"**Lahatan** ang naging sisihan nang matalo ang koponan.","translation":"The blaming was **collective** when the team lost."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang taong labis na pumupuri o naglilingkod sa isang may kapangyarihan upang makuha ang pabor nito; sipsip.
etymology: Onomatopoeic, imitating the sound of sucking.
original_explanation: The office "Bida ang Saya" kid who laughs at the boss's unfunny jokes, brings them coffee every morning, and CC's them in emails that have nothing to do with them. They're not being nice, they're playing the game. Also the literal act of sucking, like with a straw, but nobody uses it that way in gossip.
usage_notes: Carries a strong negative connotation. Often used interchangeably with 'sipsip'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **supsop** sa boss para lang ma-promote.","translation":"Don't be a **suck-up** to the boss just to get promoted."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa opisina bilang pinakamatinding **supsop**.","translation":"He is known in the office as the biggest **sycophant**."}]

translation: to light, to ignite, a bonfire/blaze
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aapoy o pagliliyab ng isang bagay; isang malaking apoy, karaniwang mula sa mga sinunog na basura o damo.
original_explanation: This is the bonfire you make in your backyard to burn dry leaves (and maybe secretly, your ex's old letters). It's also the smell that fills the neighborhood in the late afternoon. It's the act of starting a fire, whether for a barbecue or just to get rid of the 'kalat'.
usage_notes: As a noun, it means 'blaze' or 'bonfire'. As a verb root, it is used in words like 'magsiga' (to make a bonfire), 'sumiga' (to flare up), and 'sinigaan' (a place where something was burned).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag**siga** sila sa dalampasigan kagabi.","translation":"They made a **bonfire** on the beach last night."},{"sentence":"Ang usok ay mula sa **siga** ng mga tuyong dahon.","translation":"The smoke is from the **blaze** of dry leaves."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang elektronikong aparato na naglalabas ng malakas na tunog bilang babala kapag nakadetekta ito ng usok, karaniwang senyales ng sunog.
original_explanation: Yung bagay sa kisame na tumutunog lang kapag nagsasaing ka na at nasunog yung kanin, hindi kapag may tunay na sunog. It's the ultimate 'Tita, may sunog!' alert for your failed cooking experiments.
usage_notes: The English term is used directly as there is no common Tagalog equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Biglang tumunog ang **smoke alarm** habang nagpiprito ako ng tuyo.","translation":"The **smoke alarm** suddenly went off while I was frying dried fish."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating palitan ang baterya ng **smoke alarm** taun-taon.","translation":"We need to change the battery of the **smoke alarm** every year."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi magkakabagay, magkakatulad, o magkakaayon; may pagkakaiba o salungatan.
etymology: From 'di-' (not) + 'magkakatugma' (will match each other) from the root 'tugma' (match, rhyme).
original_explanation: When your friend wears polka dots with stripes. Or when your team's project ideas are all going in different directions. It's like pineapple on pizza for some people—the flavors are just di-magkakatugma.
usage_notes: Can be used for physical objects, ideas, personalities, or rhymes in poetry.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kulay ng kanyang sapatos at bag ay **di-magkakatugma**.","translation":"The colors of her shoes and bag are **mismatched**."},{"sentence":"Madalas silang mag-away dahil **di-magkakatugma** ang kanilang mga ugali.","translation":"They often fight because their personalities are **incompatible**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang medikal na kondisyon kung saan may abnormal na paglaki ng thyroid gland na nagiging sanhi ng pamamaga sa leeg.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung sakit sa leeg na laging sinasabi ng mga matatanda na dahil daw sa kakulangan sa iodine. It's a medical term that has become common knowledge, often used in public health campaigns about using iodized salt.
usage_notes: A medical term used in general conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinayuhan ng doktor ang pasyente na magpatingin sa espesyalista para sa kanyang **bosyo**.","translation":"The doctor advised the patient to see a specialist for their **goiter**."},{"sentence":"Ang paggamit ng iodized salt ay nakakatulong upang maiwasan ang **bosyo**.","translation":"Using iodized salt helps to prevent **goiter**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabahagi ng isang bagay sa maraming maliliit na piraso o sa maraming tao.
etymology: From Tagalog `mag-` (verb prefix) + reduplicated `hati-hati` (divide into many parts).
original_explanation: This is what happens to the last pizza slice at a party. Everyone gets a tiny sliver. Or when you get your 13th month pay and you have to **maghati-hati** it for pamasko sa mga inaanak, bills, and a little something for yourself. The budget spreadsheet is real.
usage_notes: The reduplication of 'hati' implies dividing into more than two parts, often among multiple recipients.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Maghati-hati** tayo sa mga gawain para mas mabilis matapos.","translation":"Let's **divide** the tasks among ourselves to finish faster."},{"sentence":"Ang mga magnanakaw ay nag-away kung paano sila **maghahati-hati** sa kanilang ninakaw.","translation":"The thieves argued about how they would **divide** their loot among themselves."}]

meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng kapangyarihan o pahintulot ang isang tao o bagay.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "autorizar" at dinagdagan ng hulaping Tagalog na "-han".
original_explanation: Ito yung action na ginagawa mo para bigyan ng go-signal ang isang bagay. "Ina-**autorisahan** na kitang gamitin ang credit card ko, pero para sa pagkain lang ha!" It's like giving your friend the password to your Netflix account.
usage_notes: Isang pandiwa na tumutukoy sa akto ng pagbibigay ng permiso.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **autorisahan** ang transaksyon bago ito maproseso ng bangko.","translation":"You need to **authorize** the transaction before the bank can process it."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pag-aalala o pagkabalisa dahil sa isang problema, panganib, o hindi tiyak na sitwasyon.
etymology: From 'pagka-' (state of being) + 'bahala' (care/responsibility, often with a sense of worry).
original_explanation: That "overthinking at 3 AM" feeling. It’s what your mom feels when you're out late and not replying to her texts. It's the anxiety spike when your boss says, "Can we talk?" A universal feeling powered by "what ifs" and "paano na?"
usage_notes: A common word for feelings of worry or apprehension.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya maitago ang kanyang **pagkabahala** para sa kaligtasan ng anak.","translation":"She couldn't hide her **worry** for her child's safety."},{"sentence":"Nagdulot ng malaking **pagkabahala** sa komunidad ang pagtaas ng presyo ng bilihin.","translation":"The increase in the price of goods caused great **concern** in the community."}]

translation: to bundle up; to wrap up
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtatali o pagsasama-sama ng mga bagay upang maging isang bungkos.
original_explanation: The action verb for 'bungkos'. It's what the vendor does to your sitaw before handing it to you. 'Bungkusin mo na 'yan' means 'wrap it up' or 'bundle it up'. It can also be used figuratively, like when you're trying to gather all your scattered feelings for someone—"Sige, bungkusin mo muna yang feelings mo bago ka umamin."
usage_notes: This is the object-focus form of the verb. The actor-focus form is 'bumungkos'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinakiusapan niyang **bungkusin** nang maayos ang mga bulaklak.","translation":"He requested to **bundle** the flowers neatly."}]

meaning_filipino: Bilang pangngalan, tumutukoy sa tao na ang trabaho ay mangolekta ng bayad o utang. Bilang pandiwa, ito ay ang gagawing pagkolekta ng bayad sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: This is both the person and the action. As a noun, it's the dreaded 'collector'—the one from the credit card company or the 'Bombay' on a motorcycle. As a verb (future tense), it's the *promise* of collection. It’s your friend texting "maniningil ako sa'yo bukas ha," a threat more terrifying than any horror movie.
usage_notes: This word can be a noun (collector) or a verb (will collect). It is the future tense of 'maningil'. Context is key to determining its function in a sentence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumating na ang **maniningil** ng kuryente. (Pangalan)","translation":"The electricity **bill collector** has arrived. (Noun)"},{"sentence":"Bukas ako **maniningil** sa lahat ng may utang sa akin. (Pandiwa)","translation":"Tomorrow, I **will collect** from everyone who owes me money. (Verb)"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng dalawa o higit pang tao na sabay-sabay na pag-aalis ng kuto at lisa sa buhok ng isa't isa.
etymology: From kuto (louse). The affixes mag-, -hing- (a variant of mang- for searching/gathering), and -an (reciprocal action) combine to form this specific meaning.
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino bonding experience, usually done on a lazy afternoon under a mango tree. It's part grooming, part "chismisan" session. You find out all the neighborhood gossip while your friend meticulously searches for kuto (lice) on your scalp with a "suyod" (fine-toothed comb).
usage_notes: A very specific cultural activity. The singular form (delousing another person) is hingutuhan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing hapon, ugali ng magkakaibigan na **maghingutuhan** sa ilalim ng puno.","translation":"Every afternoon, it's the friends' habit to **delouse each other** under the tree."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko ang mag-ina na **naghihingutuhan** habang nagkukwentuhan.","translation":"I saw the mother and daughter **delousing each other** while chatting."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaikling salita para sa "milyon" o isang libong libo (1,000,000).
original_explanation: Slang for 'milyon'. Ito yung presyo ng pangarap mong bahay at lupa, o yung sweldo na gusto mong makuha pero sa panaginip lang nangyayari. Madalas marinig sa usapang negosyo, utang, o jackpot sa lotto. "Isang mil na lang, pre, kulang ko."
usage_notes: Primarily used in informal or business-related slang to quickly refer to millions, especially in the context of money (Philippine Pesos).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang halaga ng proyekto ay aabot sa limang **mil**.","translation":"The cost of the project will reach five **million**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paggalaw, paghawak, o pag-usisa sa isang bagay nang walang tiyak na layunin o sa paraang maaaring makasira.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you're bored and there's a remote control, a phone, or any gadget nearby. You press all the buttons, mess with the settings, and generally just 'explore' it until someone yells 'Huwag mong kalikutin 'yan, masisira mo!' It's the official hobby of curious titos trying to 'fix' the wifi.
usage_notes: Ang pandiwang anyo nito, 'kalikutin' (to tinker with something), ay mas karaniwang ginagamit. Ang salitang-ugat na 'kalikot' ay maaaring gamitin bilang isang utos: 'Huwag kang kalikot!' (Don't meddle!).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang mag-**kalikot** ng mga sirang gamit sa pag-asang maayos pa niya ito.","translation":"He loves to **tinker** with broken things in the hope that he can still fix them."},{"sentence":"Itigil mo ang pag-**kalikot** sa cellphone ko, baka may mabura ka.","translation":"Stop **fiddling** with my cellphone, you might delete something."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng bigat ng katawan sa isang paa sa ibabaw ng isang bagay o lugar.
original_explanation: The action you do when you see a cockroach and you're not a fan. Or what you accidentally do to your friend's new white shoes in a crowded MRT. It can also be used figuratively, like 'tinapakan ang pagkatao ko' (they stepped on my dignity), which is peak hugot drama.
usage_notes: The noun form is also 'tapak,' meaning a footstep or footprint. `Tumapak` (infinitive/past), `tumatapak` (present), `tatapak` (future).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka at baka may ma**tapak**an kang bubog.","translation":"Be careful or you might **step on** broken glass."}]

translation: to direct to, to make (someone) go to
meaning_filipino: Ibigay ang direksyon o atasan ang isang tao na pumunta sa isang tiyak na lugar.
original_explanation: This is what you do when someone asks for directions. You point and say, 'Doon po.' Or, it's what your boss does when they delegate a task: 'Patunguhin mo si client sa conference room.' You're basically the human Waze, setting someone on the right path.
usage_notes: A causative verb. It means to cause someone or something to go towards a certain direction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Patunguhin** mo ang mga bisita sa hardin.","translation":"**Direct** the guests **to** the garden."},{"sentence":"Saan ko ba dapat **patunguhin** ang sulat na ito?","translation":"Where should I **direct** this letter **to**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na may anemya, isang kondisyon kung saan kulang ang malusog na pulang selula ng dugo; maputla o mahina.
original_explanation: Medically, it's having low red blood cells. Culturally, it's what your lola calls you when you look pale, tired, and generally 'walang kabuhay-buhay' (lifeless). 'Hija, **anemika** ka ba? Kumain ka ng atay ng manok!' It's the go-to diagnosis for anyone who looks like they haven't seen the sun or eaten a proper meal in a week.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pang-uri (anemika siya) o pangngalan (isang anemika). Ang panlalaking anyo ay 'anemiko'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinayuhan ng doktor ang **anemika** na pasyente na kumain ng masustansyang pagkain.","translation":"The doctor advised the **anemic** patient to eat nutritious food."},{"sentence":"Lagi kang nahihilo kasi mukhang **anemika** ka.","translation":"You always feel dizzy because you seem **anemic**."}]

translation: to lock each other up; to be imprisoned together
meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay na pagkilos ng dalawa o higit pa na ikulong ang isa't isa, o ang sitwasyon kung saan sila ay magkakasamang nakakulong.
original_explanation: Parang toxic na relasyon, you're both trapping each other. Or when you and your siblings get grounded together in one room by your mom. "Sige, diyan kayo **magkulungan** hanggang magkabati kayo!"
usage_notes: Ito ay isang pandiwang palipat o panlipunan, na nagpapahiwatig na ang kilos ay ginagawa ng isang grupo sa isa't isa o nang magkasama.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang away ng magkapatid, sinabi ng ina, \"Sige, **magkulungan** kayo sa kwarto!\"","translation":"Because the siblings were fighting so much, the mother said, \"Fine, **lock each other up** in the room!\""},{"sentence":"Tila sila **nagkulungan** sa isang relasyon na wala nang pag-ibig.","translation":"It seems they have **imprisoned each other** in a loveless relationship."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit at masakit na sugat na karaniwang tumutubo sa loob ng bibig, partikular sa pisngi, dila, o labi.
original_explanation: Life's tiny, painful punishment for being stressed, sleep-deprived, or accidentally biting your cheek. This is the reason you can't enjoy your spicy ramen or green mangoes. It's a small problem that demands 100% of your attention.
usage_notes: A very common ailment. Despite having the same name as 'steam', the meaning is completely different and understood from context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ako makakain ng maanghang dahil may **singaw** ako.","translation":"I can't eat spicy food because I have a **canker sore**."}]

meaning_filipino: Naputol o napigtal dahil sa pagkahila o sobrang pagkabatak.
original_explanation: Ever pulled on a rubber band one too many times and it snaps? That's lumagot. It's the sound of your guitar string giving up mid-song, or your tsinelas strap breaking in the middle of the street. It can also be used for patience. 'Konting-konti na lang, lalagot na ang pasensya ko!' (Just a little more and my patience will snap!)
usage_notes: Specifically for things that are string-like, thin, or under tension, like ropes, strings, threads, or even patience.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Biglang **lumagot** ang tali ng saranggola.","translation":"The kite string suddenly **snapped**."},{"sentence":"Sa sobrang galit niya, parang **lalagot** ang mga ugat sa kanyang leeg.","translation":"He was so angry, it looked like the veins in his neck would **snap**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong tanyag at naging inspirasyon sa isang partikular na larangan; o isang bagay na nagbibigay ng liwanag, tulad ng araw o buwan.
original_explanation: Basically, a VIP of a certain field. The Jose Rizal, the Lea Salonga, the Hidilyn Diaz of their time. They're not just famous; they're the 'ilaw' (light) that guides others. Also, technically the sun and moon are 'luminaryos', but you're more likely to use this for a person you'd write a glowing tribute about on Facebook.
usage_notes: A loanword from Spanish. It's not very common in casual conversation but is understood in formal or academic contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Dr. Jose Rizal ay isang **luminaryo** sa kasaysayan ng Pilipinas.","translation":"Dr. Jose Rizal is a **luminary** in Philippine history."},{"sentence":"Kinilala ang mga **luminaryo** sa larangan ng agham sa ginanap na parangal.","translation":"The **luminaries** in the field of science were recognized at the awards ceremony."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan nag-aalaga o maraming itik; palaisdaan o pastulan ng mga itik.
original_explanation: It's the OG poultry business before everyone got obsessed with samgyupsal. Think of a field trip destination where the main event is watching ducks waddle and quack. It's where balut dreams are made.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumunta kami sa **itikan** para bumili ng sariwang itlog na maalat.","translation":"We went to the **duck farm** to buy fresh salted eggs."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pagkilos na marahan, dahan-dahan, at may pag-iingat.
original_explanation: Your lola's favorite word. It means "slow down, you're gonna break something/get hurt." Use it when carrying lechon, walking on a wet floor, or falling in love too fast. "**Hinay-hinay** lang sa pag-ibig, baka masaktan ka." It's the universe's "take it easy."
usage_notes: An instruction to be careful, slow down, or be gentle.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hinay-hinay** lang sa pagbaba ng hagdanan, madulas.","translation":"Go down the stairs **slowly**, it's slippery."},{"sentence":"Sabi ng doktor, **hinay-hinay** muna sa pagkain ng matataba.","translation":"The doctor said to go **easy** on fatty foods for now."}]

meaning_filipino: Nangangahulugang ayos lang, tama, o katanggap-tanggap.
original_explanation: The Swiss Army knife of Filipino responses. Can mean "yes," "I'm fine," "I agree," "it's acceptable," or "I'm secretly annoyed but don't want to argue." The tone is everything. "Okey lang ako" is the most famous lie in the Philippines, second only to "on the way na ako."
usage_notes: Extremely common. The spelling can vary (okay, ok). 'Okey lang' is a very versatile and common phrase.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Okey** lang ba sa iyo kung dito tayo kumain?","translation":"Is it **okay** with you if we eat here?"},{"sentence":"Mukhang pagod ka. **Okey** ka lang ba?","translation":"You look tired. Are you **alright**?"}]

translation: to be frank with; to confront; to match
meaning_filipino: Harapin o kausapin nang tuwiran at walang paligoy-ligoy; pantayan o tumbasan ang isang bagay o gawa.
original_explanation: The moment of truth. That scene in a teleserye where the protagonist finally confronts the kontrabida. "Mag-tapatan na nga tayo! Ikaw ang kumain ng leche flan sa ref, 'no?!" It can also mean to match someone's energy or skill.
usage_notes: Can mean 'to be honest with someone' (magsitapatan), 'to be frank with someone' (tapatan mo ako), or 'to face/match someone or something' (tapatan sa galing).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tapatan** mo ako, may problema ba tayo?","translation":"**Be frank with** me, do we have a problem?"},{"sentence":"Walang makaka**tapatan** sa galing niyang magluto.","translation":"No one can **match** her skill in cooking."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paggamit ng tuka, tulad ng ginagawa ng ibon o manok, upang kumuha ng pagkain o manakit.
original_explanation: When a chicken goes full-on keyboard warrior on a grain of rice. It's also what your chismosa kapitbahay does to your reputation, piece by piece. 'Wag mo akong tukain!' is the bird equivalent of 'Get off my back!'
usage_notes: Can be used literally for birds pecking or figuratively for someone nagging or attacking someone verbally.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong hahayaang **tukain** ng manok ang mga bagong tanim na palay.","translation":"Don't let the chicken **peck** at the newly planted rice seedlings."},{"sentence":"Para siyang manok na walang tigil sa **tukain** ang mga butil ng mais.","translation":"It's like a chicken that won't stop **pecking** the corn kernels."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang alternatibong tawag para sa isang tao na kabilang sa lahi o relihiyon ng Hudaismo.
original_explanation: Basically the same as 'Hudio', just a different spelling you might see in older texts. Think of it as the 'Filipino' vs 'Pilipino' debate, but for a different word.
usage_notes: Isang varyant ng salitang 'Hudio'. Maaaring ituring na medyo luma na ang baybay na ito kumpara sa 'Hudio'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa Lumang Tipan ang kasaysayan ng mga **Hudiyo**.","translation":"The history of the **Jews** is in the Old Testament."},{"sentence":"Ang Paskuwa ay isang mahalagang pista ng mga **Hudiyo**.","translation":"Passover is an important **Jewish** festival."}]

translation: The act of using up completely; draining
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-ubos ng isang bagay hanggang sa wala nang matira, lalo na sa likido o laman ng isang sisidlan.
original_explanation: This is that 'patayin-ang-baso' level of finishing something. It's scraping the last bit of Nutella from the jar, or squeezing the toothpaste tube until it's flatter than your wallet after a 12.12 sale. Metaphorically, it's when you feel completely drained—emotionally, physically, or financially. 'Said na said na ako' is the official cry of the overworked and underpaid.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa tagtuyot, naging problema ang **pagsaid** ng tubig sa mga dam.","translation":"Because of the drought, the **draining** of water in the dams became a problem."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagsaid** sa kanyang lakas ay dahil sa walang tigil na pagtatrabaho.","translation":"The **complete draining** of his energy was due to non-stop work."}]

meaning_filipino: Ipasok ang isang matulis na bagay sa isa pa, tulad ng pagtutuhog ng pagkain.
original_explanation: The official action for making street food. It's what you do to fishballs, kikiam, and squidballs before drowning them in sweet and spicy sauce. You take a bamboo stick and you 'magtusok' like your life depends on it. Also, what happens when you accidentally sit on a thumbtack.
usage_notes: Differentiated from 'magturok' which is almost always about injections. 'Magtusok' is for more general piercing or skewering, especially with food.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sige na, **magtusok** ka na ng fishball hangga't mainit pa.","translation":"Go ahead, **skewer** some fishballs while they're still hot."},{"sentence":"Nag-ingat siya na hindi **matusok** ang daliri sa karayom habang nananahi.","translation":"She was careful not to **pierce** her finger with the needle while sewing."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging nakausli o nakalabas mula sa karaniwang kinalalagyan, partikular na tumutukoy sa mga mata.
original_explanation: That look you have when you see the latest chismis, the price of your Meralco bill, or your crush walking by. Your eyes are practically popping out of your head. "OMG, luwa mata ko sa gulat!" It's the physical manifestation of being shookt.
usage_notes: Most commonly used in the phrase `luwa ang mata` (bulging eyes).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halos **luwa** na ang mga mata niya sa pagod at puyat.","translation":"His eyes were almost **bulging** from exhaustion and lack of sleep."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang post sa social media na walang saysay, mababa ang kalidad, o sadyang ginawa para maging nakakatawa, nakakainis, o panggulo lamang.
original_explanation: The art of posting absolute nonsense on the internet for laughs. Walang context, walang logic, basta funny (o cringey). Ito yung mga low-res memes, out-of-context screenshots, at mga tanong na 'Tulog na ba lahat?'. When you're bored at 2 AM, you don't post your feelings, you shitpost.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun (the post itself) or a verb (the act of posting, e.g. 'nag-shi-shitpost').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puro **shitpost** na lang ang nakikita ko sa feed ko ngayon.","translation":"I only see **shitposts** on my feed nowadays."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, nag-shi-**shitpost** lang siya.","translation":"Don't worry, he's just **shitposting**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sistema ng pag-aayos ng mga araw para sa mga layuning panlipunan, pangrelihiyon, pangkomersyo, o pang-administratibo. Ito rin ay tumutukoy sa pisikal na bagay na nagpapakita nito.
original_explanation: In the PH context, this is the freebie you get from a hardware store or a local politician, usually with their face on it. Digitally, it's your Google **Calendar** that's screaming at you with meeting invites. It's what you check to see how many days are left until the next long weekend.
usage_notes: Ang Tagalized na "kalendaryo" ay mas karaniwang ginagamit. Ang "calendar" ay mas madalas marinig sa konteksto ng opisina o teknolohiya.
