usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakitingnan sa **calendar** mo kung libre ka sa Biyernes.","translation":"Please check your **calendar** if you're free on Friday."},{"sentence":"Nag-release na ng **calendar** ng holidays ang Malacañang.","translation":"Malacañang has released the holiday **calendar**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pagkain na gawa sa harina, tubig, at lebadura na karaniwang iniluluto sa hurno.
original_explanation: The most basic of breakfast staples. The OG, the one and only, the reason you wake up in the morning for that hot pandesal with kape. From the 'monay' that Tita buys, to the 'tasty' bread for your baon sandwich, **pan** is life.
usage_notes: While 'tinapay' is the more generic and native-sounding term, 'pan' is extremely common, especially in compounds like 'pandesal' (pan de sal).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng **pan** sa panaderya.","translation":"I bought **bread** at the bakery."},{"sentence":"Gusto mo ba ng **pan** na may palamang keso?","translation":"Do you want **bread** with cheese filling?"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa dalawa o higit pang tao o bagay na magkatabi, magkasama, o sabay na kumikilos.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate #SanaAll relationship goal. Picture two people walking on the beach, holding hands, perfectly in sync. They are `magkaagapay`. It's also what you and your bestie are when you're facing life's problems together. It's teamwork, but with more feelings.
usage_notes: Can be used as an adjective to describe a state (`Sila'y magkaagapay`) or as a verb (`Upang magkaagapay...`). `Agapay` means alongside or abreast.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magkaagapay** na hinarap ng mag-asawa ang lahat ng pagsubok sa buhay.","translation":"The couple faced all of life's challenges **side-by-side**."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko silang naglalakad na **magkaagapay** sa parke.","translation":"I saw them walking **alongside each other** in the park."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagwawasto sa isang pagkakamali, pag-aayos sa isang bagay na baluktot, o paglilinaw sa isang maling impormasyon.
original_explanation: This is the 'let me correct you' or 'actually...' moment. It can be literal, like straightening a crooked picture frame. More often, it’s about correcting a mistake, whether it's a typo in a report, a wrong turn you took using Waze, or setting the record straight about some chismis. It's the act of making things right.
usage_notes: Can be used for both literal straightening (e.g., of a wire) and figurative correction (e.g., of a mistake or a person's behavior).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagtutuwid** sa maling balita ay responsibilidad ng mga mamamahayag.","translation":"The **correction** of false news is the responsibility of journalists."},{"sentence":"Isinagawa niya ang **pagtutuwid** ng mga baluktot na pako.","translation":"He performed the **straightening** of the bent nails."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga maliliit at walang gaanong halaga na bagay, detalye, o usapan. Ginagamit din bilang pamalit sa isang salitang hindi matandaan.
etymology: Likely from 'tsu-tsu' or related to Swardspeak. It can also be an onomatopoeia for idle chatter.
original_explanation: All the little things you have to deal with that aren't the main event. "Ay, dami pang chuchu bago matapos 'tong project." It's the admin work of life, the side quests you didn't sign up for, the miscellaneous folder on your desktop.
usage_notes: Often used in the plural form 'chuchu-chuchu' or with 'ka-' as 'ka-chuchuhan' to mean trivial matters or nonsense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na 'yang mga **chuchu** na 'yan at mag-focus tayo sa importante.","translation":"Stop with all those **trifles** and let's focus on what's important."},{"sentence":"Ang daming **chuchu** sa bag niya, puro hindi naman kailangan.","translation":"There are so many **knick-knacks** in her bag, mostly unnecessary things."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangunahing daanang pampubliko na nag-uugnay sa mga bayan, lungsod, o lalawigan; pambansang daan.
original_explanation: This is the 'SLEX' or 'NLEX' of the vocabulary. The official, government-maintained super-road. It’s not just any *kalye*; it’s a major artery connecting places. Think of it as the 'national highway' you see on Google Maps when you're trying to escape the city for a long weekend.
usage_notes: A more formal and specific term for a national or major public highway.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagbabawal ang paglalagay ng anumang harang sa **lansangan-bayan**.","translation":"Placing any obstruction on the **public highway** is prohibited."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa katangian ng pagiging mayabang, mapagmataas, o pagpapakita ng labis na tiwala sa sarili sa paraang nakakainis o kahanga-hanga.
original_explanation: This is that BDE (Big D*ck Energy) but make it Pinoy. It's the swagger of the guy who walks into a room like he owns the place, maybe with a toothpick in his mouth. It can be cool (like a basketball player hitting a buzzer-beater) or annoying (like the guy who cuts you off in traffic and then stares you down). It's a mix of confidence, arrogance, and a "what are you gonna do about it?" attitude. Mayabang na may dating.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pangngalan (kaangasan) o pang-uri (maangas).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa kanyang **angas** sa basketball court.","translation":"He is known for his **swagger** on the basketball court."},{"sentence":"Huwag masyadong ma-**angas**, baka mapahiya ka lang.","translation":"Don't be too **cocky**, you might just get embarrassed."}]

translation: to beg for; to implore for
meaning_filipino: Makiusap nang may matinding pagsusumamo para sa isang tao o bagay.
etymology: From i- + pag- + makaawa (to plead for mercy), from awa (mercy, pity).
original_explanation: This is your 'pity me' card. Yung tipong, 'Ma, please, payagan mo na ako!' while doing puppy eyes. It's what you do when you're begging your professor for a passing grade or begging your friend to lend you money before payday. It's not just asking, it's begging with full-on drama.
usage_notes: A very strong form of pleading. The focus is on begging *for* something on behalf of oneself or another.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinailangan niyang **ipagmakaawa** ang buhay ng kanyang anak sa mga kumidnap dito.","translation":"She had to **beg for** her child's life from the kidnappers."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang **ipagmakaawa** ang isang taong ayaw na sa'yo.","translation":"Don't **beg for** a person who doesn't want you anymore."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan o bagay na ginagamit upang hikayatin o pukawin ang interes at pagnanais ng isang tao na gawin ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: Ito yung 13th month pay, performance bonus, o yung 'seen' na may kasamang reply galing kay crush. Anything that makes you go, 'Okay, sige, game! Gagawin ko 'to!' It's the universe's (or your boss's) way of dangling a carrot in front of you.
usage_notes: Often used in formal contexts like business, education, or psychology.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mataas na sahod ay malaking **panggaganyak** para sa mga empleyado.","translation":"A high salary is a great **incentive** for employees."},{"sentence":"Gumagamit ang guro ng mga laro bilang **panggaganyak** sa pag-aaral.","translation":"The teacher uses games as a **motivation** for learning."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bilang na dalawa; ang pangalawa sa isang serye.
original_explanation: The Spanish version of 'dalawa'. You'll hear this when counting money, telling time (alas-dos), or when a vendor is giving you a price. It's the "uno, dos, tres" kind of counting that's deeply ingrained in Pinoy life, from palengke to boxing.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa pagbibilang ng pera, pagsasabi ng oras, at sa mga laro. Ang katutubong salita ay "dalawa".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Alas **dos** na ng hapon, kailangan ko nang umuwi.","translation":"It's already **two** in the afternoon, I need to go home."},{"sentence":"Pabili po ng **dos** kilong bigas.","translation":"I'd like to buy **two** kilos of rice."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kagamitan o lugar na ginagamit sa pag-iihaw, karaniwan ay yari sa metal at may parilya kung saan ipinapatong ang pagkain sa ibabaw ng uling.
original_explanation: The throne where the magic happens. This is the actual device, the metal grid over a bed of charcoal, where you cook your 'ihaw'. It can be a fancy stainless steel one from the department store, or a makeshift one from an old biscuit can. It's the altar of every Filipino barbecue party.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to the apparatus or the location of grilling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Linisin mo muna ang **ihawan** bago natin gamitin.","translation":"Clean the **grill** first before we use it."},{"sentence":"May bagong **ihawan** na de-kuryente si Tita.","translation":"Auntie has a new electric **grill**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglanghap o pag-amoy ng hangin o anumang bagay na may samyo.
original_explanation: That deep breath you take when you pass by a Pan de Manila or a sizzling sisig joint. It's the opposite of what you do when you pass by a smelly canal. It's the 'sarap sa ilong' moment.
usage_notes: The verb forms are 'sumanghap' (to inhale) and 'sanghapin' (to inhale something). Often used interchangeably with 'langhap'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kay sarap **sumanghap** ng sariwang hangin sa probinsya.","translation":"It's so wonderful to **inhale** the fresh air in the province."},{"sentence":"**Sanghapin** mo ang bango ng mga bulaklak.","translation":"**Smell** the fragrance of the flowers."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang patayo at matibay na istruktura, karaniwang gawa sa bato, laryo, o semento, na nagsisilbing harang, hangganan, o pananggalang.
original_explanation: The thing you talk to when no one else is listening. In hugot terms, it's the emotional barrier you build to avoid getting hurt again. "Ang taas ng pader na binuild mo around your heart!" Also, the thing your neighbor builds that's 1 inch into your property line, starting a 10-year family feud.
usage_notes: Refers to a solid, structural wall, usually made of concrete or brick, as opposed to 'dingding', which can be a lighter interior partition.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpagawa sila ng mataas na **pader** sa paligid ng kanilang bahay para sa seguridad.","translation":"They had a high **wall** built around their house for security."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang galaw, direksyon, o anyo na bumubuo ng bilog o umiikot sa isang sentro.
original_explanation: The default setting for your Grab driver who "can't find the entrance" to your condo. "Sir, paikot lang po ako." Also describes the logic of some people in arguments.
usage_notes: Can describe motion (as an adverb) or shape (as an adjective).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng **paikot** na argumento para lituhin ang kausap.","translation":"He used a **circular** argument to confuse the person he was talking to."},{"sentence":"Ang mga bata ay tumatakbo nang **paikot** sa plasa.","translation":"The children are running **in a circle** in the plaza."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng minatamis na gawa sa asukal na pinainit hanggang sa maging kulay kayumanggi at malapot.
original_explanation: 'Yung topping sa paborito mong frappuccino o 'yung matamis na sarsa sa leche flan. Minsan, parang love life, sobrang sweet sa una, pero pag tumagal, tumitigas at mahirap nang nguyain.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko ng ice cream na may maraming **karamelo** sa ibabaw.","translation":"I want ice cream with a lot of **caramel** on top."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa panlabintatlong posisyon o pagkakasunod-sunod sa isang serye.
original_explanation: Ah, the famous 13th month pay! The reason why December is the happiest (and most traffic-filled) month in the Philippines. It's the bonus that pays for Noche Buena, gifts, and the credit card bills from your 11.11 shopping spree.
usage_notes: Used to denote the 13th item in a sequence. Can be written as "ika-13". Famously associated with "13th month pay" in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inaasahan ng lahat ang kanilang **ikalabintatlong** buwang sahod bago mag-Pasko.","translation":"Everyone is expecting their **thirteenth** month pay before Christmas."},{"sentence":"Bakit laging wala ang **ikalabintatlong** palapag sa mga gusali?","translation":"Why is the **thirteenth** floor always missing in buildings?"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bilang o dami na malaki, marami, o higit pa sa inaasahan; ang kabaligtaran ng kaunti.
etymology: Kombinasyon ng 'di' (not) at 'kakaunti' (very few), na isang pag-uulit ng 'kaunti'. Ang dobleng negatibong anyo ay nagpapahiwatig ng malaking bilang.
original_explanation: This is the polite, low-key way of saying 'ang dami!' (so many!). Like when your tita asks how many exes you've had, and you say '**di kakaunti**' with a mysterious smile. It means you've collected them like Pokémon cards.
usage_notes: Isang uri ng litotes (understatement) kung saan ang negatibo ay ginagamit upang ipahayag ang isang malakas na positibo. Ipinapahiwatig nito ang 'medyo marami' o 'marami'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Di kakaunti** ang mga taong dumalo sa pagtitipon.","translation":"**Not a few** people (meaning, many people) attended the gathering."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mang-aawit, manunugtog, o mananayaw na nagtatanghal nang nag-iisa.
original_explanation: Yung bida sa a-cappella group na laging may sariling moment. Sila yung may pinakamalakas na boses sa videoke at hindi mo pwedeng agawan ng mic. Think Regine Velasquez or any 'birit' queen/king.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang napiling **solista** para sa konsiyerto ng koro.","translation":"She was chosen as the **soloist** for the choir's concert."},{"sentence":"Humanga ang lahat sa galing ng batang **solista** sa byolin.","translation":"Everyone was amazed by the skill of the young violin **soloist**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging malaya sa dumi, mantsa, o anumang bagay na nakarurumi; kalinisan.
original_explanation: The opposite of your bedroom floor after a week. The state your mom wants the house in before visitors arrive. The feeling after a good shower. It's not just about physical cleanliness, pwede ring 'malinis ang kunsensya' (clean conscience) or 'malinis ang record' (clean record).
usage_notes: Bilang pang-uri, ito ay 'malinis'. Bilang pangngalan, 'linis' o 'kalinisan'. Bilang salitang-ugat, ito ay isang utos: 'Linis!' (Clean up!).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **linis** ng kanyang kuwarto ay kahanga-hanga.","translation":"The **cleanliness** of his room is admirable."},{"sentence":"Siguraduhing ma**linis** ang mga gulay bago lutuin.","translation":"Make sure the vegetables are **clean** before cooking."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kahulugan, kabuluhan, o importansya ng isang salita, konsepto, o pangyayari.
etymology: From ka- + tuturan (from 'turan' - to state, to mention).
original_explanation: This is a level-up from 'kahulugan'. It's not just the definition, it's the *significance*. It's asking 'What's the point?' or 'What does it all mean?'. When you're having an existential crisis at 3 AM, you're looking for the katuturan of life. It’s the ‘why’ behind the ‘what’.
usage_notes: A deep, often philosophical word. More profound than 'kahulugan' (definition).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinahanap niya ang **katuturan** ng kanyang buhay.","translation":"He is searching for the **meaning** of his life."},{"sentence":"Nawalan ng **katuturan** ang lahat ng kanyang pinaghirapan.","translation":"Everything he worked hard for lost its **significance**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang likas na satelayt ng daigdig na umiikot dito at nagbibigay ng liwanag sa gabi sa pamamagitan ng pagsasalamin ng sinag ng araw.
original_explanation: The OG night light. The reason werewolves exist (in stories). The subject of a million haranas and 'I love you to the moon and back' declarations. It's that big, shiny thing in the sky that controls the tides and your friend's 'topak' during a full moon.
usage_notes: This is one of two primary meanings for 'buwan'. Context usually makes the meaning clear.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maliwanag ang sikat ng **buwan** kagabi.","translation":"The light of the **moon** was bright last night."},{"sentence":"Ang kabilugan ng **buwan** ay isang magandang tanawin.","translation":"The full **moon** is a beautiful sight."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pagkaing kalye na binubuo ng nilagang itlog ng pugo na binalutan sa harinang kulay kahel at ipinirito nang malutong.
etymology: Onomatopoeic, possibly from the sound of birds/ducks ('quack quack').
original_explanation: The iconic orange balls of goodness you find on the street. It's a hard-boiled quail egg deep-fried in a bright orange batter. Partner mo 'to with spicy vinegar and you're good to go. The smaller, cuter cousin of tokneneng.
usage_notes: Often confused with 'tokneneng', which uses chicken or duck eggs. Kwek-kwek is specifically for quail eggs.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili kami ng **kwek-kwek** sa tapat ng simbahan.","translation":"We bought **kwek-kwek** across from the church."},{"sentence":"Ang sarap isawsaw ng **kwek-kwek** sa matamis at maanghang na suka.","translation":"It's delicious to dip **kwek-kwek** in sweet and spicy vinegar."}]

meaning_filipino: Maunawaan o malaman nang lubusan ang isang bagay, ideya, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: That 'Aha!' moment when the chismis finally clicks and you understand the entire timeline of your friend's love life drama. It's when the lesson from a movie, a book, or a major life mistake finally sinks in. "At that moment, natalos ko... I've been the toxic one all along."
usage_notes: More formal and deeper than 'maintindihan'. Often used in literature or formal speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **natalos** ko ang tunay niyang intensyon.","translation":"At last, I **comprehended** his true intentions."},{"sentence":"Sana ay **matalos** ng lahat ang kahalagahan ng pagkakaisa.","translation":"I hope everyone will **realize** the importance of unity."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbaba mula sa isang mataas na lugar patungo sa isang mas mababang lugar.
etymology: From the root verb 'panaog' (to descend, to go down). The noun form `pananaog` is created by reduplicating the first syllable of the root's core 'naog'.
original_explanation: This is the opposite of your 'akyat-ligaw' efforts. It's literally just 'going down.' Think of getting off the MRT at your station, walking down the stairs from your condo, or that feeling when your grades 'go down' after prelims. It's the 'D' in 'D-scent.'
usage_notes: Less common in everyday conversation than 'pagbaba'. Often used in more formal, literary, or religious (e.g., Christ's descent) contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging marahan ang **pananaog** ng hari mula sa kanyang trono.","translation":"The king's **descent** from his throne was slow."},{"sentence":"Ang **Pananaog** ni Hesukristo sa mga yumao ay bahagi ng kredo.","translation":"The **Descent** of Jesus Christ to the dead is part of the creed."}]

meaning_filipino: Makaranas ng pagkabigo o kawalan ng pag-asa dahil hindi natupad ang inaasahan.
etymology: From Spanish `desmayar` (to faint, to be discouraged), adapted into Tagalog with the `ma-` verb affix.
original_explanation: The official feeling when your online order arrives and it looks nothing like the picture. 'Expectation vs. Reality' in verb form. It's the emotion you feel when your crush says you're 'like a brother' to them. That's the ultimate madismaya moment.
usage_notes: Can also be used as an adjective (e.g., `dismayado`).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **madismaya** kung hindi mo agad nakuha ang gusto mo.","translation":"Don't **be disappointed** if you don't get what you want right away."},{"sentence":"Marami ang **nadismaya** sa resulta ng eleksyon.","translation":"Many were **disappointed** with the election results."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapatama o pag-atake gamit ang kanyon o malalaking artilerya.
etymology: From `pang-` + `kanyon`. The word `kanyon` is from Spanish `cañón` (cannon).
original_explanation: Think of this as the original "unfriending" on a massive, historical scale. It's the act of firing cannons, a very loud way of saying "I don't like you." In modern terms, it's like getting hit with a barrage of angry comments in a Facebook thread.
usage_notes: A historical or military term. Not used in everyday conversation unless discussing history or warfare.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang walang tigil na **panganganyon** ay nagpabagsak sa mga pader ng kuta.","translation":"The relentless **bombardment** brought down the walls of the fort."},{"sentence":"Narinig sa buong bayan ang ingay ng **panganganyon**.","translation":"The sound of the **cannonade** was heard throughout the town."}]

translation: To blacken; to make something black
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng kulay itim sa isang bagay; gawing itim ang kulay nito.
original_explanation: What you do to your hair after a breakup for a dramatic change. Also, the verb for when you're shading in a drawing or filling out a lotto ticket with maximum hope. In a darker sense, it's what happens to your reputation when the chismis starts flying ('itiman ang pangalan').
usage_notes: Can be literal (to color something black) or figurative (to tarnish a reputation, 'itiman ang pangalan').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **itiman** ang mga bilog sa sagutang papel.","translation":"You need to **blacken** the circles on the answer sheet."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan nilang **itiman** ang kanyang pangalan, ngunit hindi sila nagtagumpay.","translation":"They tried to **tarnish** his name, but they did not succeed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging manipis, salat sa kapal, o madaling masira.
etymology: From `ka-` + `nipis` + `-an`, forming a noun describing the quality of being thin.
original_explanation: That feeling when you buy a shirt from an online store and the fabric is so sheer you can see your future through it. Or when your patience is wearing thin after your 5th Zoom meeting for the day. "Grabe ang kanipisan ng pader, rinig ko lahat ng chismis ng kapitbahay."
usage_notes: Describes the quality or state of being thin, whether physically (like paper) or metaphorically (like patience).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa **kanipisan** ng tela, madali itong napunit.","translation":"Because of the **thinness** of the fabric, it tore easily."},{"sentence":"Ramdam na ang **kanipisan** ng kaniyang pasensya.","translation":"The **thinness** of his patience can already be felt."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na bahagi o kasapi ng isang samahan, pangkat, o organisasyon.
etymology: From ka- (denoting partnership/membership) + anib (to join, to side with).
original_explanation: Someone who has paid the membership fee, literally or figuratively. You're a kaanib of your office team, your barkada's Viber group, or that K-Pop fandom. You have the ID, the t-shirt, or at least the inside jokes to prove it.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of formal organizations, clubs, or religious groups.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay isang aktibong **kaanib** ng aming kooperatiba.","translation":"He is an active **member** of our cooperative."},{"sentence":"Maraming **kaanib** ang dumalo sa pangkalahatang pagpupulong.","translation":"Many **affiliates** attended the general assembly."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na hiniram sa Ingles na "overpowered," na nangangahulugang sobrang lakas o napakahusay, lalo na sa konteksto ng mga video game.
etymology: Mula sa pagpapaikli ng salitang Ingles na "overpowered".
original_explanation: Short for "overpowered." This is what you scream when your opponent in Mobile Legends or Valorant is just too damn good. "Grabe, ang OP ng hero na 'to!" means that character needs to be nerfed, ASAP. Can also be used for anything ridiculously effective, like your lola's adobo recipe.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa komunidad ng mga manlalaro (gamers).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi na patas ang laro, sobrang **op** ng bagong character.","translation":"The game isn't fair anymore, the new character is too **OP**."},{"sentence":"Bakit ang **op** ng build mo? Patingin nga ng items.","translation":"Why is your build so **OP**? Let me see your items."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng puno (Nauclea orientalis) na katutubo sa Timog-silangang Asya at Australasia, na kilala sa mga bilog na kumpol ng bulaklak nito.
original_explanation: Ever seen those streets named 'Bangkal'? It's probably named after this tree. It's not as famous as a Narra or a Mango tree, but it's one of our own native trees. It's also the name of a famous district in Makati known for its antique and second-hand shops, where you go to 'mag-bangkal' (dig up) treasures. A bit of a wordplay there!
usage_notes: Refers to a specific tree species. Also a well-known place name in the Philippines (e.g., Bangkal, Makati City).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May malaking puno ng **bangkal** sa likod ng aming lumang bahay.","translation":"There is a large **bangkal** tree behind our old house."},{"sentence":"Ang mga bulaklak ng **bangkal** ay ginagamit sa tradisyonal na medisina.","translation":"The flowers of the **Nauclea orientalis** are used in traditional medicine."}]

translation: to hinder; to obstruct; to block
meaning_filipino: Pigilan o maglagay ng sagabal sa isang gawain, plano, o pag-usad ng isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: Eto yung ginagawa ng kontrabida sa teleserye para 'di magkatuluyan yung bida. O kaya yung ginagawa ng mabagal na internet sa online class mo. Basically, anything or anyone that gets in your way. 'Yung traffic sa EDSA? Ultimate example ng pag-hadlang sa mga pangarap mong makauwi nang maaga.
usage_notes: Isang pandiwa na nangangailangan ng tuwirang layon (direct object) na siyang hinahadlangan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **hadlangan** ang kanyang mga pangarap.","translation":"Do not **hinder** his/her dreams."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan nilang **hadlangan** ang pagpasa ng bagong batas.","translation":"They tried to **obstruct** the passing of the new law."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kataga na nagpapahiwatig ng kawalan ng katiyakan o pag-aalinlangan; hinuha o palagay.
original_explanation: The official word for when you're not sure, but you're gonna say it anyway. It's the verbal equivalent of a shrug emoji (🤷). "Darating siya ata." means "Maybe they'll come, maybe they won't, let's not get our hopes up but let's still prepare the chismis." It's your escape clause in any statement.
usage_notes: A very common conversational particle. Often used to soften a statement or express a personal guess.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uulan **ata** mamaya.","translation":"**I think** it will rain later."},{"sentence":"Wala na **ata** tayong bigas.","translation":"**Perhaps** we don't have any rice left."}]

translation: to turn upside down, to invert
meaning_filipino: Ilagay sa posisyong baligtad; gawing ang itaas ay nasa ibaba at ang ibaba ay nasa itaas.
original_explanation: Like when you check your wallet at the end of the month and nothing comes out. You itiwarik it, shake it, and all you get is dust and an old receipt. It's the physical manifestation of "wala na'ng natira."
usage_notes: Often used for containers or objects. Can also be used metaphorically for turning a situation or statement on its head.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Itiwarik** mo ang timba para matuyo ang loob nito.","translation":"**Turn** the bucket **upside down** so its inside can dry."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **itiwarik** ang mga katotohanan para lang pagtakpan ang iyong kasalanan.","translation":"Don't **invert** the facts just to cover up your mistake."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paglalarawan sa bilis na lubhang matulin at mapanganib, na tila maaaring makabali ng leeg.
etymology: Compound word from 'makabali' (to be able to break) and 'leeg' (neck).
original_explanation: That kamote rider on EDSA weaving through traffic like they're in a video game. Or how you run to the MRT station when you hear the train arriving. It's a speed so dangerously fast, it could metaphorically snap your neck.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used to describe dangerously high speed, often in the context of vehicles or running.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa **makabaling-leeg** na bilis, tinahak ng tsuper ang masikip na kalsada.","translation":"At **breakneck** speed, the driver navigated the narrow road."},{"sentence":"Tumatakbo siya nang **makabaling-leeg** para lang maabutan ang huling biyahe ng bus.","translation":"He was running at **breakneck** speed just to catch the last bus trip."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtawa nang mahina at pino, kadalasang pigil at may mataas na tono, na nagpapahiwatig ng hiya, kilig, o katuwaan.
original_explanation: 'Yung tawa mo 'pag dumaan si crush. 'Yung pilit mong tinatago pero naririnig pa rin ng best friend mo. It's the official laugh track of 'kilig' moments.
usage_notes: Different from 'humagakhak' (guffaw), 'humagikgik' is a suppressed, high-pitched laugh often associated with shyness or amusement.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Humagikgik** ang mga dalaga habang nag-uusap tungkol sa kanilang mga crush.","translation":"The young ladies **giggled** while talking about their crushes."},{"sentence":"Napansin niyang **humagikgik** ang bata sa likod niya.","translation":"She noticed the child **giggling** behind her."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na itinabi o inilaan para sa isang partikular na paggamit sa hinaharap; maaari ding tumukoy sa pagpapalista o pagpapareserba ng lugar o serbisyo.
original_explanation: Ito yung "Plan B" mo sa buhay. Yung extrang pera na tinago mo "just in case." Sa pagkain, ito yung huling piraso ng paborito mong ulam na ayaw mong ipagalaw sa iba. Sa love life, ito yung... ay, 'wag ganun. Bawal ang reserba! Also, ito yung booking mo sa restaurant o hotel.
usage_notes: Ginagamit din sa pangmaramihang anyo, 'mga reserba', upang tukuyin ang mga nakaimbak na suplay (hal. reserbang pagkain, reserbang sundalo).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroon akong **reserba** na pera para sa biglaang pangangailangan.","translation":"I have money **reserves** for emergencies."},{"sentence":"Tumawag ka na para magkaroon tayo ng **reserba** sa restoran.","translation":"Call now so we can have a **reservation** at the restaurant."},{"sentence":"Inihanda ng gobyerno ang mga **reserba** nilang pagkain para sa paparating na bagyo.","translation":"The government prepared their food **reserves** for the coming typhoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-iwan ng marka, tanda, o epekto sa isang bagay o sa isipan.
original_explanation: 'Yung hugot line na iniwan ng ex mo na hanggang ngayon, ramdam mo pa rin. "Bumakas sa puso ko ang mga sinabi niya." It's the mark left by a slipper on your leg (pinalo ni nanay), the footprint on a newly mopped floor, or the emotional scar from that K-drama finale. It's proof that something *was* there.
usage_notes: Ito ang pandiwang nasa anyong pangkasalukuyan o pangnagdaan (actor-focus) ng salitang-ugat na 'bakas'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumakas** ang mga yapak niya sa basang semento.","translation":"His footprints **left a mark** on the wet cement."},{"sentence":"Malinaw na **bumakas** sa kanyang mukha ang pagod.","translation":"The exhaustion was clearly **imprinted** on his face."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maikling pangungusap o parirala na nagpapahayag ng paniniwala o mithiin ng isang tao, pamilya, o institusyon.
original_explanation: That cheesy quote you put in your high school yearbook or slumbook, like 'Time is gold' or 'Honesty is the best policy.' Nowadays, it's probably something like 'Bahala na si Batman' or 'In this life, I am a potato.'
usage_notes: A direct loanword, used commonly in academic or formal settings, and nostalgically in informal ones.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **motto** mo sa buhay?","translation":"What is your **motto** in life?"},{"sentence":"Ang **motto** ng aming paaralan ay 'Para sa Diyos at sa Bayan'.","translation":"Our school's **motto** is 'For God and Country'."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kilos ng pagpapakita ng malalim na paggalang, karaniwan sa pamamagitan ng pagyuko o pagluhod.
original_explanation: Ito yung pag-bow na ginagawa mo sa harap ng altar o sa mga nakakatanda bilang tanda ng paggalang. Sa sayaw, ito yung final pose na parang "Thank you for watching!" Sa buhay, ito yung ginagawa mo sa harap ng boss mo pagkatapos niyang aprubahan ang leave mo.
usage_notes: Madalas makita sa mga kontekstong panrelihiyon at pormal na pagtatanghal tulad ng sayaw.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumawa siya ng isang malalim na **reberensiya** bago umalis sa entablado.","translation":"She made a deep **bow** before leaving the stage."},{"sentence":"Ang pagmamano ay isang uri ng **reberensiya** sa mga nakatatanda.","translation":"Pagmamano is a form of **reverence** towards elders."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang panghalip na tumutukoy sa pangalawang panauhan na maramihan, o sa magalang na paraan para sa isahan. Ipinapahiwatig nito ang pag-aari, direksyon, o benepisyo para sa kinakausap.
etymology: Mula sa pang-ukol na "sa" at panghalip na "inyo" (pangalawang panauhan, pangmaramihan/magalang).
original_explanation: The closing line of every Pinoy program host: "Salamat po sa inyo!" It can mean "to you," "for you," or even "at your house" (e.g., "Saan tayo kakain? Sa inyo na lang!"). It’s the polite way to address your elders or a whole barkada at once.
usage_notes: Ang "inyo" ay ang anyong "sa" ng "kayo". Maaari itong magpahiwatig ng direksyon (to you), pag-aari (yours), o lokasyon (at your place). Ang magalang na anyong pang-isahan ay "sa inyo", habang ang impormal ay "sa iyo".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ibibigay ko ito **sa inyo** bukas.","translation":"I will give this **to you** (pl./formal) tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Ang bahay na ito ay **sa inyo**.","translation":"This house is **yours** (pl./formal)."},{"sentence":"Maligayang Pasko po **sa inyo**!","translation":"Merry Christmas **to you** (pl./formal)!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpasok sa isang lugar nang walang pahintulot, o ang paglampas sa itinakdang hangganan o limitasyon.
original_explanation: This is when you cross the line. Literally, like trespassing on someone's property. Figuratively, like when your chismosa Tita asks why you're still single for the fifth time. It's about going where you're not supposed to, whether it's a physical space or someone's personal business.
usage_notes: A relatively rare word. "Paglampas sa hangganan" is a more common way to express the figurative meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paglalabos** sa pribadong ari-arian ay isang krimen.","translation":"The **act of trespassing** on private property is a crime."},{"sentence":"Itinuturing niyang **paglalabos** sa kaniyang personal na buhay ang mga tanong mo.","translation":"She considers your questions an **overstepping of boundaries** into her personal life."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing malungkot o pighatiin ang isang tao o damdamin.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you "seen-zone" someone's long, heartfelt message. You're actively choosing to **palungkutin** them. It's the emotional equivalent of canceling their online order right after they paid for it.
usage_notes: A causative verb, meaning to cause the state of sadness in someone else.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo naman akong **palungkutin** sa araw ng aking kaarawan.","translation":"Please don't **make me sad** on my birthday."},{"sentence":"Ang balitang natanggap niya ay sapat na upang siya ay **palungkutin**.","translation":"The news he received was enough to **make him sad**."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paraang isa-isa at hindi sabay-sabay; nagpapahiwatig ng paunti-unting pagdating o paggawa.
original_explanation: How your friends arrive at the meetup point. You said 7 PM, but they show up tigi-tigisa starting from 7:30 PM until 9 PM. It's the essence of Filipino time, but broken down into individual latecomers.
usage_notes: Emphasizes the individual and separate nature of the action, more so than "isa-isa".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tigi-tigisa**ng nagsidatingan ang mga bisita sa handaan.","translation":"The guests arrived **one by one** at the party."},{"sentence":"Inabutan niya ng tulong ang mga nasalanta, **tigi-tigisa** niyang kinamayan.","translation":"He gave aid to the victims, shaking their hands **individually**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang hanapbuhay ay ang pagbili at pagbenta ng mga produkto o kalakal para sa tubo.
etymology: From `mang-` + reduplication of the first syllable of the root `ka-` + `kalakal` (trade, goods). `mang-` + `ka` + `kalakal` -> `mangangalakal`.
original_explanation: Before 'entrepreneur' and 'CEO' became the buzzwords, we had mangangalakal. These are the OG business people—from the Chinese traders in pre-colonial times to your suki sa palengke. They're the ones who know how to buy low and sell high. If you've ever sold something on Carousell or Facebook Marketplace, congratulations, you've been a mangangalakal for a day.
usage_notes: A general term for someone engaged in commerce. Can range from a small-time vendor to a large-scale importer.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga unang dayuhang **mangangalakal** sa Pilipinas ay mga Tsino.","translation":"The first foreign **merchants** in the Philippines were Chinese."},{"sentence":"Isang tanyag na **mangangalakal** ang nagmamay-ari ng gusaling iyon.","translation":"A famous **businessman** owns that building."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggalaw sa tubig gamit ang mga braso at binti, na nangyayari sa kasalukuyan.
original_explanation: What you do sa beach for the 'gram. Also, a metaphor for being buried in work: 'Lumalangoy ako sa mga email.' Or drowning in debt: 'Lumalangoy sa utang.'
usage_notes: Present tense form of 'to swim'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masayang **lumalangoy** ang mga bata sa malinaw na tubig ng dagat.","translation":"The children are happily **swimming** in the clear water of the sea."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang opisyal ng pamahalaan na may kapangyarihang mamagitan, magpasya, at maglapat ng batas sa mga kasong idinudulog sa korte.
original_explanation: The person in the courtroom with the fancy robe and the little hammer (gavel). They're the ultimate decider, the "final answer" in a legal battle. In Pinoy culture, your lola can also be the huwes of the family, passing judgment on your life choices, your weight, and why you're still single. "Order in the court!"
usage_notes: The formal term is 'hukom,' but 'huwes' is very common in everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ibinaba na ng **huwes** ang kanyang desisyon sa kaso.","translation":"The **judge** has handed down his decision on the case."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating igalang ang hatol ng kagalang-galang na **huwes**.","translation":"We need to respect the verdict of the honorable **judge**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsubok na ibigay ang tamang sagot sa isang tanong o ang kalalabasan ng isang pangyayari nang walang sapat na kaalaman o katiyakan.
original_explanation: This is what you do when your friend asks "Saan tayo kakain?" and you just throw out random restaurant names. It's also the main strategy for multiple-choice exams when you didn't study. "Eenie, meenie, miny, moe" is a form of 'hulaan'.
usage_notes: Can be a command ("Hulaan mo!" - "Guess it!") or used in other verb forms (e.g., hinulaan, huhulaan).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hulaan** mo kung ano ang regalo ko para sa iyo.","translation":"**Guess** what my gift is for you."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **hulaan** ang mananalo sa eleksyon.","translation":"It's hard to **predict** who will win the election."}]

translation: to be able to act like a monster; to become monstrous
meaning_filipino: Kumilos o magpakita ng katangiang tulad ng isang halimaw, partikular sa bagsik, lakas, o kalupitan.
original_explanation: When someone goes "beast mode," but in a terrifying, not cool, way. It's when anger or greed turns a person into something unrecognizable and cruel. Parang 'yung boss na nag-power trip, or 'yung taong sinapian ng galit at nanakit na. The opposite of "makatao" (to be humane).
usage_notes: A strong word used to describe extreme negative behavior, often driven by rage, greed, or cruelty.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang labis na kapangyarihan ay maaaring **makahalimaw** sa isang tao.","translation":"Excessive power can **make a monster out of** a person."},{"sentence":"Nagulat ang lahat nang ang dati'y mabait na lalaki ay tila **nakahalimaw** dahil sa selos.","translation":"Everyone was shocked when the formerly kind man seemed to have **acted like a monster** due to jealousy."}]

translation: To conspire with; to collude with
meaning_filipino: Ang lihim na makipagkasundo o makipagtulungan sa iba para sa isang masamang layunin o panlilinlang.
etymology: Mula sa ugat na 'sabwat', na tumutukoy sa isang lihim na kasunduan o pagsasabwatan.
original_explanation: It's like forming a secret group chat with your workmates to plan how to get your toxic boss fired. It's plotting and scheming, pero with a group. Teamwork makes the dream work... or the evil plan work. Also used for planning surprise parties.
usage_notes: Madalas na may negatibong konotasyon ng panlilinlang. Ang 'sabuwatin' ay isang alternatibong baybay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinagplanuhan nilang **sabwatin** ang pangulo ng kanilang organisasyon.","translation":"They planned to **conspire against** the president of their organization."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **sabwatin** ang taong tapat sa kanyang mga prinsipyo.","translation":"It's hard to **get someone to conspire** who is true to their principles."}]

translation: to cause sorrow; to grieve for
meaning_filipino: Maging sanhi ng matinding kalungkutan o pighati para sa isang tao.
etymology: From i- (causative prefix) + pamighati (a variant form derived from pighati - sorrow).
original_explanation: This is the verb form of causing someone major hugot-levels of sadness, or when you're grieving for something or someone. It's the deep, heavy feeling you get when your favorite character in a series dies, or when you see your crush with someone else. #SakitBhe
usage_notes: This is a more literary or formal word, not commonly used in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang **ipamighati** ang kanyang pag-alis sa kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"He did not want his departure **to cause sorrow** for his parents."},{"sentence":"Ang pagkawala ng kanilang alagang aso ay labis niyang **ipinamighati**.","translation":"She deeply **grieved for** the loss of their pet dog."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang opisyal na pangalawa sa pinakamataas na ranggo sa isang pamahalaan, kumpanya, o organisasyon, na humahalili sa presidente kung kinakailangan.
original_explanation: The official "spare tire" of any organization, from the national government down to your high school student council. They're one heartbeat (or one resignation) away from the top job. Their main role is to wait, attend functions the president is too busy for, and sometimes, lead a major government department. In the office setting, it's the boss's boss that you only see during the Christmas party.
usage_notes: The "bise" prefix is from Spanish. Often abbreviated as "VP".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang nahalal na **bise presidente** ng Pilipinas.","translation":"She was elected **vice president** of the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Kausapin mo ang **bise presidente** para sa operasyon ng kumpanya.","translation":"Talk to the **vice president** for company operations."}]

translation: to fear, to worry, to be anxious
meaning_filipino: Ang makaramdam ng takot, pag-aalala, o kawalan ng kapanatagan tungkol sa isang posibleng masamang mangyayari.
etymology: From `mang-` + `amba` (threat, gesture of attack). The idea is reacting to a perceived threat.
original_explanation: It's that feeling you get when your phone is at 1% and the Grab driver is still 10 minutes away. It's the 'Sunday Scaries' when you think about work tomorrow. Mangamba is a more formal, deeper kind of worry than just 'kinakabahan.' It's the anxiety of the unknown, the fear of what *might* happen. 'Huwag kang mangamba,' is what your mom says, but you still do.
usage_notes: A more formal or literary word for 'matakot' or 'mag-alala'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula siyang **mangamba** nang hindi umuwi ang anak sa takdang oras.","translation":"She started **to worry** when her child did not come home at the appointed time."},{"sentence":"Walang dahilan para **mangamba** kung handa ka sa anumang pagsubok.","translation":"There's no reason **to fear** if you are prepared for any challenge."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sangkap na idinaragdag sa pagkain o inumin upang magbigay ng lasang matamis.
original_explanation: The stuff you add to your kape when life is already bitter enough. Can be sugar, honey, stevia, or even the sweet nothings your crush whispers to you (warning: the last one has side effects). It's the lifeblood of every milk tea shop and a frenemy to your diet.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong maglagay ng **pampatamis** sa kape ko.","translation":"Don't put too much **sweetener** in my coffee."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto o proseso ng pagkain; isang sesyon ng pagkain o salu-salo.
original_explanation: This refers to the event itself. "Anong oras ang kain natin?" (What time is our meal?). It’s less about the food and more about the event of eating. It's the 'eating' part of 'eating out'.
usage_notes: Ang paggamit nito bilang pangngalan ay hindi gaanong karaniwan kumpara sa anyong pandiwa ngunit naiintindihan sa konteksto, kadalasang tumutukoy sa oras ng pagkain.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matagal ang naging **kain** namin dahil sa masarap na kuwentuhan.","translation":"Our **meal** took a long time because of the good conversation."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng **kain**, maghugas ka ng plato.","translation":"After **eating**, wash the dishes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang gawain ay lagyan ng sabon ang isang bagay, o isang kasangkapan na naglalabas ng sabon.
original_explanation: Literally, the 'soap-applier'. In a car wash, it's the person who lathers up your car. In a fancy bathroom, it's the automatic dispenser you wave your hand under. In a more figurative sense, it could be that friend who 'soaps you up' with compliments before asking for a favor.
usage_notes: Isang salitang bihirang gamitin sa pang-araw-araw na usapan at mas literal ang pagkakabuo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinawag niya ang **tagapagsabon** para simulan na ang paglilinis ng sasakyan.","translation":"He called the **soaper** to start cleaning the car."},{"sentence":"Sino ang naka-assign na **tagapagsabon** sa car wash ngayon?","translation":"Who is assigned as the **soaper** at the car wash today?"}]

translation: act of scrambling or working hastily
meaning_filipino: Ang masigasig at mabilis na paggawa o pagkilos, kadalasan gamit ang mga kamay, upang makamit ang isang bagay sa gitna ng kahirapan o kakulangan sa oras.
etymology: From `pag-` + `-ku-` + `kamot`. The root `kamot` means "to scratch," implying a scratching/clawing effort.
original_explanation: This is you, 15 minutes before the deadline, frantically typing to finish your report. It's the mad dash to grab the last piece of crispy pata at a fiesta. It's the hustle of a vendor in Divisoria trying to make a sale. Pagkukumamot is the art of desperate, hands-on scrambling to get things done. It's pure, unadulterated "diskarte".
usage_notes: Implies a sense of urgency, difficulty, or even desperation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa kanyang **pagkukumamot**, naitaguyod niyang mag-isa ang kanyang mga anak.","translation":"Through her **laborious efforts**, she was able to support her children by herself."},{"sentence":"Kitang-kita ang **pagkukumamot** ng mga estudyante na matapos ang kanilang proyekto bago ang pasahan.","translation":"The students' **scrambling** to finish their project before the deadline was very visible."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang alagang hayop na may apat na paa, balahibo, at kilala sa kakayahang manghuli ng daga. Ito ay isang uri ng mamalyang karniboro sa pamilyang Felidae.
etymology: Mula sa Malay na "pusa," na maaaring nagmula sa isang wikang Nubian.
original_explanation: The furry, four-legged overlord of your household who demands food, scratches, and attention on their own terms. They are the living embodiment of "I do what I want." They're either sleeping in the most inconvenient spot or plotting world domination from the top of your fridge. Also known as "muning" or "miming".
usage_notes: Ang pangkalahatang termino para sa pusa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May alaga akong itim na **pusa**.","translation":"I have a pet black **cat**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong saktan ang **pusa**, masama iyan.","translation":"Don't hurt the **cat**, that's bad."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ikalawang oras pagkatapos ng tanghali o hatinggabi.
etymology: From Spanish 'a las dos' meaning 'at two'.
original_explanation: The time of day when you're either sleepy after lunch (siesta time!) or just getting your second wind at work. It's the 'kalahating araw pa lang, pagod na ako' hour.
usage_notes: Part of the Spanish-derived time-telling system in the Philippines. Can be written as 'alas-dos' or 'alas dos'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkita tayo mamayang **alas-dos** ng hapon.","translation":"Let's meet later at **two o'clock** in the afternoon."},{"sentence":"Nagising ako ng **alas-dos** ng madaling araw dahil sa ingay.","translation":"I woke up at **two o'clock** in the morning because of the noise."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpasok ng isang matulis na bagay, karaniwan ay karayom, upang maglagay ng gamot o likido sa katawan.
original_explanation: That moment at the clinic you either dread or don't mind. It’s what the nurse does with a syringe for your flu shot or vaccine. It's the 'tusok' part of a medical procedure. Not to be confused with the 'tusok-tusok' you enjoy with fishballs.
usage_notes: While 'turok' can mean pierce, 'pagtuturok' almost exclusively refers to medical injection.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagtuturok** ng bakuna ay mahalaga para sa kalusugan ng publiko.","translation":"The **injection** of vaccines is important for public health."},{"sentence":"Medyo kinakabahan ako sa **pagtuturok** ng gamot.","translation":"I'm a bit nervous about the **injection** of the medicine."}]

translation: to instruct; to give final instructions or will
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng mahalagang bilin, utos, o habilin sa isang tao, lalo na bago umalis o bago mamatay.
original_explanation: This is what your parents do before they leave for a trip: "Huwag magpapasok ng kung sino-sino! Mag-aral kang mabuti! Huwag puro cellphone!" It's that formal, serious list of instructions. It’s also used for a last will and testament, the ultimate "huling habilin". It's the more intense version of "bilin".
usage_notes: Mas pormal at seryoso kaysa sa `bilinan`. Madalas gamitin sa mga legal o napakahalagang konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tinagubilinan** ng ina ang kanyang anak na mag-ingat palagi.","translation":"The mother **instructed** her child to always be careful."},{"sentence":"Bago siya pumanaw, **tinagubilinan** niya ang lahat tungkol sa paghahati ng kanyang ari-arian.","translation":"Before he passed away, he **gave final instructions** to everyone regarding the division of his properties."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto o kalagayan ng pag-apaw ng tubig na nagdudulot ng paglubog ng lupa na karaniwang tuyo.
original_explanation: Ah, the unofficial fifth season in Metro Manila. 'Pagbaha' is that moment when the street outside your house suddenly looks like a Venice canal, but with more floating trash and less gondolas. It's the reason classes get suspended and your Grab fare suddenly costs more than your lunch.
usage_notes: Refers to the event or act of flooding, as opposed to 'baha' which is the flood itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang malakas na ulan ay nagdulot ng biglaang **pagbaha** sa maraming lugar.","translation":"The strong rain caused sudden **flooding** in many areas."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marahas o sakim na pagkuha ng isang bagay na hindi sa iyo, lalo na ang lupa o ari-arian.
original_explanation: This is what a corrupt official does with public funds. It's what you do to the last piece of lechon at a fiesta when no one is looking. It's the act of greedily taking something for yourself, often unfairly. The ultimate 'angkin' move.
usage_notes: Often has a negative connotation of greed and injustice, especially in the context of land grabbing ("pagkamkam ng lupa").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ikinagalit ng mga magsasaka ang **pagkamkam** sa kanilang mga lupain.","translation":"The farmers were angered by the **seizing** of their lands."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkamkam** ng yaman ng bayan ay isang malaking kasalanan.","translation":"The **unlawful acquisition** of the nation's wealth is a great sin."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga ari-ariang hindi maaaring ilipat ng lokasyon, tulad ng lupa, bahay, at mga gusali.
original_explanation: This is next-level 'abogado' talk. It's the specific term for property that you can't just pack up and move, like land or a building. It's the reason why family reunions sometimes turn into a scene from a teleserye.
usage_notes: A highly formal and legalistic term. The opposite is 'bienes muebles' (movable property).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-invest sa **bienes-imuwebles** ay isang magandang paraan para palaguin ang pera.","translation":"Investing in **real estate** is a good way to grow money."},{"sentence":"Nakasaad sa testamento ang hatian ng lahat ng **bienes-imuwebles** ng yumaong milyonaryo.","translation":"The will states the division of all the **immovable properties** of the deceased millionaire."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabago o proseso ng pagpapabuti sa kalagayan o kalidad ng isang bagay; pag-unlad.
original_explanation: The glow-up you promise yourself every New Year's resolution. It's that upgrade from 'pwede na' to 'wow, ang ganda!' Can refer to a renovated house, a fixed process, or your life after you finally block your toxic ex.
usage_notes: Often used in construction, legal, or formal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglaan sila ng pondo para sa **mehora** ng mga pampublikong paaralan.","translation":"They allocated funds for the **improvement** of public schools."},{"sentence":"May malaking **mehora** sa kaniyang kalusugan mula nang mag-ehersisyo siya.","translation":"There's a big **improvement** in his health since he started exercising."}]

translation: from the very beginning; since the start
meaning_filipino: Mula sa simula o umpisa; sa pinakaunang sandali.
original_explanation: **Sapulan** is the ultimate TBT (Throwback Thursday) word. It means 'since the very beginning'. "Sapulan, alam ko nang may gusto ka sa kanya." (From the very start, I knew you had a crush on them.) It's the 'I knew it all along' adverb.
usage_notes: Emphasizes the very starting point of a period or event. It is a more emphatic version of 'simula' or 'umpisa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sapulan** pa lang, ramdam ko nang may mali sa mga ikinikilos niya.","translation":"**From the very beginning**, I felt something was wrong with his actions."},{"sentence":"Magkaibigan na kami **sapulan** noong elementarya.","translation":"We have been friends **since** elementary school."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng tumatayong espirituwal na gabay at pangalawang magulang para sa isang bata sa seremonya ng binyag sa Kristiyanismo.
original_explanation: This is the OG godmother, the one from your baptism. She's the one who held a candle for you and promised the priest she'd help raise you Catholic. While you can have a 'ninang sa kasal' (wedding sponsor), the 'ninang sa binyag' is the one you've been awkwardly asking for money from since you were a kid. She's your lifetime aguinaldo source.
usage_notes: This term specifies the context of the godmother role, as opposed to a 'ninang sa kasal' (wedding sponsor) or 'ninang sa kumpil' (confirmation sponsor).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aking **ninang sa binyag** ay kapatid ng aking ina.","translation":"My **godmother (for baptism)** is my mother's sister."},{"sentence":"Maraming inaanak ang aking **ninang sa binyag** kaya't abala siya tuwing Pasko.","translation":"My **baptismal godmother** has many godchildren, so she is busy every Christmas."}]
related: ["ninong sa binyag","inaanak sa binyag","binyag","ninang sa kasal"]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghingi ng pahintulot bago umalis o gumawa ng isang bagay; o ang kilos ng pagsasabi ng paalam. Maaari rin itong mangahulugang pagbibigay-impormasyon.
etymology: From `pag-` + `pa-` + `alam` (know). The base `paalam` (goodbye) is also derived from this, signifying the 'act of making one's departure known'.
original_explanation: This word is a Swiss Army knife. It's what you do when you leave a party ('nagpaalam ka na ba?'). It's also what you do before you borrow your sibling's clothes to avoid a fight (`pagpapaalam` as asking permission). And in corporate-speak, it’s the formal 'act of informing' (`pagpapaalam sa management`). It's all about making your intentions known, whether you're leaving a party or a relationship.
usage_notes: The meaning depends heavily on context. 'Nagpaalam siya' could mean 'He said goodbye' or 'He asked for permission.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging emosyonal ang **pagpapaalam** ni Ana sa kanyang pamilya bago siya lumipad patungong Canada.","translation":"Ana's **saying goodbye** to her family before she flew to Canada was emotional."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapaalam** sa nakatatanda ay isang tanda ng paggalang.","translation":"The **act of asking permission** from one's elders is a sign of respect."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaki na itinuturing na pasibo, sunud-sunuran, at kulang sa mga katangiang karaniwang iniuugnay sa isang 'alpha male' tulad ng dominasyon at kumpiyansa.
etymology: Mula sa pariralang Ingles na 'beta male'.
original_explanation: The guy who holds the purse of the 'alpha female'. He's the supportive friend, the 'pambansang bestie', not the leading man. He's not the final boss, he's the NPC that gives you a side quest.
usage_notes: Isang termino mula sa internet slang, madalas gamitin sa mga talakayan tungkol sa social dynamics at pakikipag-date.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinasabi nila na isa siyang **beta male** dahil lagi siyang nagpaparaya sa kanyang kasintahan.","translation":"They say he is a **beta male** because he always gives way to his girlfriend."}]

translation: to invite; to fetch; to escort
meaning_filipino: Anyayahan o sunduin ang isang tao upang isama sa isang tiyak na lugar o pagtitipon.
original_explanation: The formal way of saying 'sunduin' or 'yayain.' It's what happens when you get a formal invitation card. It’s also what happens in old movies when the prince sends a carriage to fetch the maiden. You're not just being asked to come, you're being formally brought over.
usage_notes: More formal and literary than 'anyayahan' or 'sunduin'. The root 'dapit' implies bringing someone to a place, often as an escort.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinag-utos ng hari na **dapitin** ang lahat ng dalaga sa kaharian para sa pagpili ng kanyang mapapangasawa.","translation":"The king ordered to **invite/fetch** all the maidens in the kingdom for the selection of his future wife."},{"sentence":"Sino ang nais mong **dapitin** sa iyong kaarawan?","translation":"Who do you want to **invite** to your birthday?"}]

translation: the act of pulling or towing
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghila sa isang bagay nang may lakas, karaniwan ay upang ilipat ito mula sa isang lugar patungo sa iba.
original_explanation: This is what a tow truck does to your illegally parked car. It's what you do to your friend who doesn't want to leave the party. It can also be metaphorical, like the 'pull' of a strong personality or a good story ('paghatak ng manonood'). It's the act of forcefully drawing something towards you.
usage_notes: Implies a strong pull, often with some resistance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinailangan ang **paghatak** ng kalabaw para maialis ang kariton sa putik.","translation":"The **pulling** of the carabao was needed to get the cart out of the mud."},{"sentence":"Malakas ang **paghatak** ng pelikula sa mga manonood.","translation":"The movie has a strong **pull** on the audience."}]

translation: Cringe; something that causes secondhand embarrassment
meaning_filipino: Ang pakiramdam ng labis na hiya o pagkailang, lalo na para sa ginagawa ng ibang tao; isang bagay na nagdudulot ng ganitong pakiramdam.
original_explanation: That feeling you get when your tito tells a corny joke at the family reunion, or when you see your old Friendster posts. It's secondhand embarrassment personified. Yung gusto mo na lang lumubog sa kinauupuan mo dahil sa hiya para sa ibang tao. "Grabe, ang cringe ng pa-dance number nila!"
usage_notes: Used as both a feeling ("I feel cringe") and a descriptor ("That is so cringe"). Often used interchangeably with "cringey". The Filipino equivalent could be 'nakakahiya' or 'nakakakilabot sa hiya'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Na-**cringe** ako sa mga pinagsasabi niya sa live video niya.","translation":"I **cringed** at the things he was saying on his live video."},{"sentence":"Sobrang **cringe** ng pelikulang 'yon, hindi ko tinapos.","translation":"That movie was so **cringe**, I didn't finish it."}]

translation: to come to one's senses; to regain consciousness
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabalik ng kamalayan mula sa pagkahimatay o pagkawala ng ulirat. Sa matalinghagang paraan, ito ay ang paggising sa katotohanan mula sa pagkakamali o maling akala.
original_explanation: Two meanings: 1) Literally, when someone faints and you splash water on their face. 2) The more common, hugot meaning: The moment you realize your toxic ex was, in fact, toxic. It's the 'gising, girl!' moment, the realization that you deserve better, the epiphany that the 'marites' was right all along. It's waking up and smelling the kapeng barako of reality.
usage_notes: Can be literal (regain consciousness) or figurative (realize the truth/come to one's senses).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matagal bago siya **natauhan** matapos siyang mabagok.","translation":"It took a while for him **to regain consciousness** after hitting his head."},{"sentence":"Sana **matauhan** ka na at iwanan mo na ang masama mong bisyo.","translation":"I hope you **come to your senses** and leave your bad habits."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tiyak na oras o panahon na itinalaga para sa pagsisimula o pagtatapos ng isang gawain o pangyayari.
original_explanation: The final boss of any project, assignment, or work task. It’s that date on the calendar that gives you anxiety. The reason for your all-nighters fueled by coffee and panic. In BPO terms, it's the AHT (Average Handle Time) of your life.
usage_notes: Synonymous with the English loanword 'deadline', which is also very commonly used in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **takdang-oras** para sa pagpasa ng proyekto ay bukas na.","translation":"The **deadline** for submitting the project is tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Dumating siya sa **takdang-oras** ng aming pagkikita.","translation":"He arrived at the **appointed time** of our meeting."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang istrukturang pantalan o daungan ng mga barko. Tumutukoy rin ito sa isang piraso ng metal na paikot na nagsisilbing pansuporta o nagbibigay ng elastisidad, tulad ng sa kutson o sasakyan.
original_explanation: This word has two personalities, a real Gemini. Personality #1 is the romantic one: the pier where ships dock, like in old movies where someone's waving goodbye. Personality #2 is the practical one: the springs in your mattress that have given up on life. 'Sira na muwelye ng kama' is a cry for help. It's from the Spanish 'muelle' which conveniently also means both things.
usage_notes: Ang kahulugan ay nakadepende sa konteksto. Ang "Muelle" ay pangalan din ng isang lugar sa Maynila na kilala bilang daungan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumaong ang malaking barko sa **muwelye**.","translation":"The large ship docked at the **pier**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nang palitan ang **muwelye** ng lumang kama.","translation":"The **springs** of the old bed need to be replaced."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglunok ng anumang uri ng likido, tulad ng tubig, gamot, o alak. Ito ang gagawing pag-inom.
original_explanation: Future tense of 'inom'. The answer to "Tara?" on a Friday night. It's what you do with water to survive, coffee to function, and beer to... celebrate? "Pagkatapos ng exam, iinom talaga kami!"
usage_notes: Contemplated aspect (future tense) of 'uminom'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Iinom** ako ng maraming tubig dahil mainit ang panahon.","translation":"I **will drink** a lot of water because the weather is hot."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magmaneho kung **iinom** ka ng alak.","translation":"Don't drive if you **will drink** alcohol."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marahan ngunit matalas na pagtusok, karaniwan ng isang maliit na bagay tulad ng tinik. Sa matalinhagang paraan, ito ay ang pagbibigay ng isang masakit o mapanuyang komento.
etymology: Mula sa panlaping pandiwa na "mang-" at salitang-ugat na "turot" (isang uri ng pagtusok).
original_explanation: That passive-aggressive comment from a coworker that feels like a tiny needle prick. "Wow, ang aga mo ngayon ah!" (Wow, you're early today!) when you're only 5 minutes late. It's not a full-on attack, just a small, sharp 'turot' to your ego or feelings. It stings more than it should.
usage_notes: Mas karaniwang ginagamit sa patalinghagang paraan upang ilarawan ang isang masakit na komento. Ang salitang-ugat na 'turot' ay bihirang gamitin nang mag-isa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit pabiro, ramdam kong may layuning **manurot** ang kanyang sinabi.","translation":"Even if it was a joke, I felt his words had the intention to **sting**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagluluto ng pagkain sa mainit na mantika o langis.
original_explanation: The default cooking method for 80% of Filipino breakfasts. Tapa, tocino, longganisa, itlog, hotdog, dried fish—if you can 'magprito' it, it's probably on the breakfast menu. The sound and smell of someone frying is the Filipino's natural alarm clock.
usage_notes: 'Prito' is the adjective (fried), 'magprito' is the verb (to fry).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magprito** ka na ng itlog para sa almusal.","translation":"**Fry** some eggs for breakfast."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **nagprito** ng isda? Ang bango!","translation":"Who **fried** the fish? It smells great!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mangangalakal na nagbebenta ng mga produkto nang maramihan o bultuhan sa mga tingiang nagbebenta (retailers), at hindi direkta sa mga mamimili.
original_explanation: This is the 'tita' who buys things by the dozen from Divisoria. They're the supplier of your local sari-sari store. They don't sell you one piece, they sell you the whole box. The mangangalakal sa pakyawan is the middleman's middleman, the one who gets the goods in bulk ('pakyawan') and distributes them to the smaller players. They're the reason you can buy a single sachet of shampoo at the corner store.
usage_notes: This is a descriptive phrase that functions as a single noun concept. 'Pakyawan' is the key term, meaning 'wholesale' or 'by the lot'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas makakamura ka kung direkta kang bibili sa **mangangalakal sa pakyawan**.","translation":"You can get it cheaper if you buy directly from the **wholesaler**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga may-ari ng maliit na tindahan ay kumukuha ng kanilang paninda mula sa mga **mangangalakal sa pakyawan**.","translation":"The owners of small stores get their goods from **wholesalers**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na may masamang reputasyon o sira na ang pangalan sa paningin ng iba.
etymology: Isang idyomatikong ekspresyon. Ang metapora ay isang papel na nabasa, na sumisira sa nakasulat dito, na sumisimbolo sa isang sirang reputasyon.
original_explanation: Literally "wet paper." It means your reputation is ruined. Imagine writing your achievements on a piece of paper, and then someone spills coffee all over it. The ink bleeds, the paper tears—it's ruined and unreadable. That's what it means to be 'basa ang papel'. Your credibility is shot. Parang na-cancel ka na sa social media of life.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang nakapirming ekspresyon. Ang pang-uring `basa` dito ay nangangahulugang "wet," hindi "read."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Simula nang mahuli siyang nagsisinungaling, **basa na ang papel** niya sa aming lahat.","translation":"Ever since he was caught lying, he's **had a bad reputation** with all of us."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging karaniwan lamang, katamtaman ang kalidad, at walang anumang natatanging katangian; hindi mahusay at hindi rin masama.
etymology: From ka- + palamara + -an. The connection between the common root 'palamara' (treacherous, traitorous) and the derived meaning 'mediocrity' is obscure and not straightforward.
original_explanation: That feeling of being 'just okay.' Not great, not terrible. You're the 'pwede na' in a world of 'wow' and 'yikes.' It's the state of doing the bare minimum. You're not failing, but you're not exactly winning either. Parang grade na 75, pasang-awa.
usage_notes: This is an extremely rare, almost obscure word. Its meaning as 'mediocrity' is cited in some dictionaries but is not in common use. The more common definition for anything related to 'palamara' is 'treachery' or 'being traitorous'. Use with caution, as most native speakers would not recognize this word or would associate it with treachery.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais niyang takasan ang **kapalamarahan** ng kanyang buhay.","translation":"He wanted to escape the **mediocrity** of his life."},{"sentence":"Ang pagtanggap sa **kapalamarahan** ay ang kaaway ng pag-unlad.","translation":"Accepting **mediocrity** is the enemy of progress."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang inaakalang komunikasyon ng mga kaisipan o ideya sa pamamagitan ng paraan maliban sa mga kilalang pandama.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na alam mo na agad kung anong iniisip ng bestie mo kahit di pa siya nagsasalita. Parang may built-in Bluetooth connection ang utak niyo. "Bes, Jollibee?" tapos sabay kayong tatayo. Yan ang telepatia in action. Hindi ito 'yung naririnig mo 'yung chismis from three barangays away, iba 'yun.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa mga konteksto ng fiction, paranormal, o sikolohiya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naniniwala siya na mayroon siyang kakayahang **telepatia**.","translation":"She believes she has the ability of **telepathy**."},{"sentence":"Sa mga pelikula, madalas may mga karakter na gumagamit ng **telepatia** para mag-usap.","translation":"In movies, there are often characters who use **telepathy** to communicate."}]

translation: orator, one who will speak at a gathering
meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nakatakdang magbigay ng talumpati o pormal na pananalita sa harap ng publiko o sa isang pagpupulong.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'mang-' na nagiging 'mam-' at ang pag-uulit ng unang pantig ng salitang ugat na 'pulong' (meeting). Tumutukoy ito sa taong gagawa ng kilos, partikular ang magsasalita sa isang pulong.
original_explanation: This is the designated speaker, the one who will deliver the speech. Think of the class valedictorian, the politician during a campaign rally, or that one tito at the family reunion who grabs the mic and won't let go. They are the 'mamumulong.'
usage_notes: Ito ay pormang pangkasalukuyan/panghinaharap ng pandiwa na ginagamit bilang pangngalan. Ito ay tumutukoy sa 'taong magsasalita'. Ito ay mas pormal kaysa sa 'tagapagsalita'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **mamumulong** sa ating pambansang kumperensya bukas?","translation":"Who will be the **speaker** at our national conference tomorrow?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang pag-iwas o paglayo sa isang tao, bagay, o sitwasyon upang hindi ito makaharap o maranasan.
original_explanation: That thing you do when you see your tita who always asks "Kailan ka mag-aasawa?" at a party. Or when you see someone you owe money to at the mall. It's the art of becoming invisible. "Umiwas ka sa utang, pero mas lalo kang umiwas sa naniningil."
usage_notes: Can be physical avoidance or avoiding a topic/responsibility.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigla siyang **umiwas** ng tingin nang magtama ang mga mata namin.","translation":"He suddenly **avoided** my gaze when our eyes met."},{"sentence":"**Umiwas** ka sa masasamang bisyo para sa iyong kalusugan.","translation":"**Avoid** bad habits for your health."}]

meaning_filipino: Idulog sa mas mataas na hukuman o kapangyarihan ang isang kaso o desisyon upang muling isaalang-alang.
original_explanation: It's what you do when you get a bad grade you think you didn't deserve, or when your team loses in a competition and you question the referee's call. "I-apela mo, bes!" is the battle cry when you feel the result is unfair and you want a higher-up to review it.
usage_notes: Used in legal, academic, or formal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napagdesisyunan ng abogado na **iapela** ang hatol sa Korte Suprema.","translation":"The lawyer decided to **appeal** the verdict to the Supreme Court."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **iapela** ang iyong grado kung sa tingin mo ay mali ang pagkakabilang.","translation":"You need to **appeal** your grade if you think it was miscalculated."}]

meaning_filipino: Pag-isahin o iugnay ang dalawang dulo, bahagi, o bagay.
original_explanation: Like trying to connect your phone to a weak public WiFi signal. Or when you try to play matchmaker for your two single friends. "Bes, bagay kayo, pramis!"
usage_notes: Typically used for connecting two distinct items or points.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaari mo bang **pagdugtungin** ang dalawang alambre na ito?","translation":"Can you **connect** these two wires?"},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **pagdugtungin** ang simula at wakas ng kanyang kwento.","translation":"He tried **to join** the beginning and end of his story."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o estruktura kung saan maaaring tumayo o maglagay ng mga bagay nang patayo.
original_explanation: It's a stand, literally. The 'sampayan' is a 'tayuan' for clothes. The shoe rack is a 'tayuan' for shoes. In a crowded MRT, the whole train is your 'tayuan'. It’s the place where things (or people) stand.
usage_notes: The suffix '-an' denotes a place or location where the action of the root word occurs. Thus, 'tayuan' is a place for 'tayo' (standing).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ilagay mo ang mga baso sa **tayuan** para matuyo.","translation":"Put the glasses on the **rack** to dry."},{"sentence":"Naghintay kami sa **tayuan** ng bus.","translation":"We waited at the bus **stand**."}]

meaning_filipino: Maging sanhi ng pag-iyak ng isang tao; sadyang gawan ng bagay na ikaluluha ng iba.
original_explanation: The national sport of Filipino drama teleseryes. The goal is always to `paiyakin` the main character (and the audience). Also what happens when you cut onions, check your bank account after payday, or re-watch "Heneral Luna". "Huwag mo akong paiyakin" is a classic line that's basically a challenge.
usage_notes: A causative verb. The subject of the verb causes the object to cry.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **paiyakin** ang kapatid mo, isusumbong kita kay nanay!","translation":"Don't **make** your sibling **cry**, I'll tell mom on you!"},{"sentence":"Madaling **paiyakin** si Ana sa pamamagitan ng malulungkot na pelikula.","translation":"It's easy to **make** Ana **cry** with sad movies."}]

meaning_filipino: Aksidenteng pag-agos o pagkalat ng isang likido o maliliit na butil mula sa lalagyan nito.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `ma-` (pandiwa ng kakayahan/di-sinasadya) + `tapon` (magtapon, magbuhos).
original_explanation: That 'oh no' moment when your kape spills on your white uniform or your laptop. It's the universe telling you to slow down. Matapon is the accidental, often tragic, spilling of something important, like your last drop of milk tea or your carefully prepared sawsawan. The opposite of 'spill the tea'.
usage_notes: Ang unlaping `ma-` ay nagpapahiwatig ng isang aksidenteng pangyayari. Ang "itapon" ay ang anyong pautos o sinasadya (to throw away).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka, baka **matapon** ang sabaw.","translation":"Be careful, the soup might **spill**."},{"sentence":"Sayang, natapon ang bagong timplang kape ko.","translation":"What a waste, my freshly made coffee was **spilled**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng matinding kakapusan, kahirapan, o kawalan ng mga pangunahing pangangailangan sa buhay.
original_explanation: This isn't just 'petsa de peligro' before payday. This is 'petsa de peligro' every day. It's the level of broke where instant noodles are a luxury. It’s the ‘dramatic backstory’ of every successful person in their interviews. It’s a more formal, heavy-hitting word for being extremely poor.
usage_notes: A formal and strong word for poverty, often used in literature, news, and formal speeches.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa **pagkahikahos**, maraming pamilya ang napipilitang tumira sa ilalim ng tulay.","translation":"Because of **destitution**, many families are forced to live under bridges."},{"sentence":"Sinikap niyang ibangon ang kanyang pamilya mula sa **pagkahikahos**.","translation":"He strove to lift his family from **extreme poverty**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit at matulis na piraso ng kahoy, metal, o anumang materyal na tumusok at pumasok sa ilalim ng balat.
original_explanation: Parang 'toxic' na comment sa social media—maliit lang pero sobrang sakit at ang hirap tanggalin. Ito yung dahilan kung bakit bigla kang napapasigaw ng 'Aray!' habang naglalakad, at kailangan mo pa ng tiyani at karayom para lang maalis. A tiny thing that causes a disproportionate amount of drama.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **subyang** ang daliri ko kaya masakit isulat.","translation":"I have a **splinter** in my finger so it's painful to write."},{"sentence":"Tinanggal niya ang **subyang** sa aking talampakan gamit ang tiyani.","translation":"She removed the **splinter** from the sole of my foot using tweezers."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pakikipag-ugnayan, pagpupulong, o pag-aaral na nangyayari nang personal at hindi sa pamamagitan ng elektronikong midya. Akronim para sa "face-to-face".
etymology: Hiram na akronim mula sa Ingles na 'F2F' (Face-to-Face).
original_explanation: The post-pandemic glow-up we all waited for. No more 'patingin ng screen' or 'naka-mute ka'. F2F classes mean baon is back on the menu, boys! Ito 'yung pagbabalik sa totoong buhay, kung saan kailangan mo na talagang maligo para sa klase o meeting.
usage_notes: Naging lubhang popular noong at pagkatapos ng COVID-19 pandemic upang tukuyin ang pagbabalik sa mga personal na interaksyon.
