usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas gusto ng mga estudyante ang **F2F** na klase kaysa online.","translation":"Students prefer **face-to-face** classes over online."},{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **F2F** na ulit ang aming team building!","translation":"Finally, our team building is **face-to-face** again!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkilos ng pagkukumpuni o pag-aayos ng mga maliliit na bagay o detalye sa isang paraan na tila naglalaro, hindi seryoso, o walang tiyak na layunin.
original_explanation: This is the art of looking busy by fiddling with something, usually mechanical or electronic. It's what your dad does on a Sunday afternoon with an old radio. He's not really fixing it, he's just `butingting`-ing. It's tinkering without a professional license.
usage_notes: Verb forms: bumutingting (actor-focus), butingtingin (object-focus), binubutingting (is tinkering).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **butingtingin** ang cellphone ko at baka masira mo.","translation":"Don't **fiddle with** my cellphone, you might break it."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sangay ng sandatahang lakas ng isang bansa na responsable para sa mga operasyong militar sa kalupaan.
original_explanation: Same same but different from 'hukbong-kati'. It also means the army or land forces. Think of it like 'car' and 'automobile' - you can use either one. This is the official name for the Philippine Army ('Hukbong Katihan ng Pilipinas'). So when you see soldiers marching, you're looking at the 'hukbong-katihan'.
usage_notes: The more formal and common term for a nation's army, synonymous with 'hukbong-kati'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumapi siya sa **Hukbong Katihan** ng Pilipinas pagkatapos ng kolehiyo.","translation":"He joined the Philippine **Army** after college."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtrato sa isang tao nang walang galang, pagpapakita ng kawalang-hiyaan, o pagsasabi ng masasamang salita.
original_explanation: The verb form of being 'bastos'. It's what you do when you catcall someone, cut in line at the MRT, or talk back to your Lola. Basically, an action that will earn you a sermon or a flying tsinelas.
usage_notes: This is a transitive verb that requires an object—the person or thing being disrespected.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masama ang ugali ng taong mahilig **bastain** ang kapwa.","translation":"A person who likes to **disrespect** others has a bad character."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **bastain** ang mga nakatatanda sa iyo.","translation":"Do not **treat rudely** your elders."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagputol o paghiwalay sa isang bagay mula sa pinagkakabitan nito. Ito ay ang anyong pautos o layon ng pandiwang 'putol'.
original_explanation: The command form of 'to cut.' It's what your mom yells when you've been on the phone too long: 'Putulin mo na 'yang telepono!' (Cut that phone call!). It's also what you do to a rope, a string, or a toxic relationship. It's the action of making something 'putol.'
usage_notes: Ito ang pandiwa sa pokus sa layon. Ang katumbas nito sa pokus sa tagaganap ay 'pumutol'. Ang salitang 'putusin' ay isang di-karaniwang baryasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **putulin** ang lubid para maibaba ang kahon.","translation":"The rope needs **to be cut** to lower the box."},{"sentence":"**Putulin** mo na ang ugnayan ninyo kung hindi ka na masaya.","translation":"**Cut** your ties if you are no longer happy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar na may lilim o proteksyon laban sa sikat ng araw o ulan.
etymology: From "ma-" (prefix indicating 'having the quality of') + "silong" (shade, area underneath).
original_explanation: That perfect spot under a big mango tree to escape the scorching summer heat, or the covered court where you can still play basketball even when it's raining. It's the opposite of being 'bilad sa araw'. Your go-to tambayan spot when the sun is out for revenge.
usage_notes: Often refers to a physical space providing cover from the elements.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Humanap tayo ng **masilong** na lugar para doon magmerienda.","translation":"Let's find a **shady** place to have our snack."},{"sentence":"Ang ilalim ng malaking puno ng akasya ay **masilong** at presko.","translation":"The space under the big acacia tree is **shady** and cool."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mandirigma noong sinaunang Roma na nakikipaglaban sa ibang mandirigma, mababangis na hayop, o mga bilanggo para sa libangan ng mga manonood.
original_explanation: The original 'lodi' ng ancient world. They're like the MMA fighters of their time, but with more sand, less rules, and the constant threat of a thumbs-down from the emperor. Today, it's what you call your friend who braves the MRT during rush hour. A true warrior.
usage_notes: Primarily used in historical contexts or as a metaphor for a fierce fighter or someone facing a tough challenge.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tanyag ang Colosseum sa Roma bilang lugar ng mga labanan ng mga **gladyador**.","translation":"The Colosseum in Rome is famous as a venue for **gladiator** battles."},{"sentence":"Para siyang isang **gladyador** na lumalaban sa gitna ng matinding traffic sa EDSA.","translation":"He's like a **gladiator** fighting through the middle of heavy traffic on EDSA."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mapanlinlang na pagpapanggap; pagpapakita ng katangian, damdamin, o paniniwala na hindi tunay na taglay upang makalinlang.
original_explanation: This is pagkukunwa's evil twin. It's the "plastic" friend who smiles at you but talks behind your back. It's pretending to be busy on your phone to avoid an awkward conversation. It's the ultimate "fake it 'til you make it," but in a bad way. Pagkukunwari is all about deception, the mask you wear to hide what's really going on. It’s the core of being a "plastikan".
usage_notes: Carries a strong negative connotation of deceit or hypocrisy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagod na ako sa lahat ng **pagkukunwari** mo!","translation":"I'm tired of all your **pretense**!"},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang kabaitan ay isa lamang **pagkukunwari** upang makuha ang tiwala ng mga tao.","translation":"His kindness is just a **pretense** to get people's trust."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging maliit sa sukat, dami, o halaga.
original_explanation: This is the feeling when you see the serving size of a 'large' milk tea and it looks more like a medium. It's the pagkaliit of your sweldo after all the deductions. It's the state of being tiny, whether it's a condo unit or your patience for slow internet.
usage_notes: The 'pagka-' prefix emphasizes the quality or state of being small.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit sa **pagkaliit** ng kanyang sahod, natuto siyang mag-ipon.","translation":"Despite the **smallness** of his salary, he learned to save."},{"sentence":"Namangha siya sa **pagkaliit** ng mga letra sa lumang aklat.","translation":"He was amazed at the **smallness** of the letters in the old book."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging mahina; isang depekto, kapintasan, o kakulangan sa lakas, pisikal man o sa ibang aspeto.
original_explanation: Your kryptonite. For some, it's chismis. For others, it's a 50% off sale. It could be a person, a food (milktea!), or a situation (like being asked "Kumusta ka?" by a tita). We all have at least one **kahinaan**, and it's usually what drains our sahod.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical, emotional, or character weakness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **kahinaan** ay ang sobrang pagtitiwala sa mga tao.","translation":"Her **weakness** is trusting people too much."},{"sentence":"Inamin niya ang kanyang mga **kahinaan** sa harap ng komite.","translation":"He admitted his **weaknesses** in front of the committee."},{"sentence":"Tsokolate ang aking pinakamalaking **kahinaan**.","translation":"Chocolate is my biggest **weakness**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pang-uring pamilang na tumutukoy sa bilang na 100.
original_explanation: The OG of big numbers before 'thousands' and 'millions' became our salary goals. It's that crisp blue bill you're happy to get as pamasko but sad to break for a 20-peso purchase. In chismis, "siyento porsyento, totoo yan!" means it's 100% legit tea.
usage_notes: Madalas ginagamit sa pagbibilang ng pera o porsiyento. Ang "isang daan" ay mas karaniwan sa pangkalahatang pagbibilang, habang ang "siyento" ay mas madalas marinig kapag tumutukoy sa halaga ng pera at mga porsyento.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigyan mo ako ng **siyento** pesos, pakiusap.","translation":"Please give me **one hundred** pesos."},{"sentence":"**Siyento** porsyento akong sigurado na siya ang kumuha.","translation":"I am **one hundred** percent sure that they were the one who took it."}]

translation: return; the act of coming back
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpunta muli sa isang lugar na pinanggalingan o pag-uwi.
original_explanation: This is the 'hugot' word. The 'sana all' of actions. It's the promise of an OFW to their family, the hope you have for an ex who left ('sana all may pagbalik'), or just you telling the Grab driver where to go on your way home. 'Pagbalik' is the journey back, whether it's to a place, a person, or a memory.
usage_notes: Refers to the act of returning. 'Bumalik' is the verb form (to return).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matagal na naming hinihintay ang kanyang **pagbalik** mula sa abroad.","translation":"We have long been waiting for his **return** from abroad."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa iyong **pagbalik**.","translation":"Be careful on your **return**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit sa isang tao o bagay para sa sariling kapakinabangan sa paraang hindi makatarungan; samantalahin.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa ng company n'yo 'pag pinag-o-OT ka nang walang bayad. O 'yung ginagawa mo sa kabaitan ng kaibigan mo na laging nanlilibre. 'To eksplotahin' is to take advantage, BPO-style.
usage_notes: Carries a strong negative connotation of abuse, unfairness, or taking undue advantage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **eksplotahin** ang kabaitan ng iyong mga magulang.","translation":"Do not **exploit** the kindness of your parents."}]

translation: to be able to pronounce; to utter
meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang sabihin o ipahayag ang isang salita o pangungusap nang wasto at malinaw.
original_explanation: It's not just saying something, it's saying it *right*. Like finally learning how to pronounce "Worcestershire sauce" or your crush's complicated last name. Kapag hindi mo mabigkas, minsan tumatahimik ka na lang para iwas-sabit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko **mabigkas** nang tama ang mga salitang Pranses.","translation":"I can't **pronounce** French words correctly."},{"sentence":"Sa sobrang kaba, halos hindi niya **mabigkas** ang kanyang pangalan.","translation":"He was so nervous, he could barely **utter** his own name."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mapait at luntiang likido na nililikha ng atay at naiipon sa gallbladder, na tumutulong sa pagtunaw ng taba. Tumutukoy rin sa mismong organo.
original_explanation: That thing your doctor says you have stones in. It's also a metaphor for bitterness. "Puro ka na lang apdo," sabi sa'yo ng kaibigan mo kapag bitter ka pa rin sa ex mo. It's the physical manifestation of "ampalaya".
usage_notes: Sa pang-araw-araw na usapan, madalas itong metaporikal na tumutukoy sa kapaitan o sama ng loob. Sa medikal na konteksto, tumutukoy ito sa likido (bile) o sa organo (gallbladder).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinanggalan siya ng bato sa **apdo**.","translation":"They removed stones from his **gallbladder**."},{"sentence":"Ang pait ng sinabi niya ay parang **apdo**.","translation":"The bitterness of what he said was like **bile**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na ganap na napapaligiran, nakukulong, o napapaloob sa iba pang bagay.
original_explanation: Imagine you're the 'lumpia' filling and the wrapper is the 'talikop'. You are completely surrounded. It can be being surrounded by enemies in a video game, or being 'talikop' by chismosas in the palengke. It’s the feeling of being in the center with no easy way out.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang hindi gaanong karaniwan at mas pampanitikang salita. 'Napapaligiran' ang mas karaniwang termino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Talikop** ng mga kaaway ang maliit na grupo ng mga sundalo.","translation":"The small group of soldiers was **enveloped** by enemies."},{"sentence":"Ang buong bayan ay **talikop** ng makakapal na hamog tuwing umaga.","translation":"The whole town is **enclosed** by thick fog every morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Karaniwan; walang espesyal o kakaibang katangian; pangkaraniwan.
original_explanation: When something is just... meh. Not great, not terrible, just plain. 'Yung tipong "Kamusta araw mo?" at ang sagot mo ay "**ordinary** lang." Walang plot twist, walang major event. Parang unli-rice, it's expected and nothing to write home about. It's the default setting of life.
usage_notes: Mas karaniwang ginagamit sa Taglish kaysa sa pormal na katumbas nitong "karaniwan" o "pangkaraniwan".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi siya isang **ordinary** na manggagawa; siya ang may-ari ng kumpanya.","translation":"He's not an **ordinary** worker; he is the owner of the company."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa, o may kinalaman sa, parusa o sa pagpaparusa para sa mga krimen at paglabag sa batas.
original_explanation: Anything related to the consequences of breaking the law. Think 'Penal Code,' the big, scary rulebook of things you shouldn't do unless you want a free, long-term staycation courtesy of the government. It’s the formal, legalistic side of 'you're grounded.'
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in legal or formal contexts, such as in 'penal colony' or 'penal code'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang 'Revised **Penal** Code' ang pangunahing batas na nagtatakda ng mga krimen at parusa sa Pilipinas.","translation":"The 'Revised **Penal** Code' is the primary law that defines crimes and punishments in the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Ipinatapon siya sa isang **penal** colony.","translation":"He was exiled to a **penal** colony."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gagawing pagbibigay ng tugon o solusyon sa isang tanong, suliranin, o tawag sa hinaharap.
etymology: From `mag-` + reduplication of the first syllable of the root `sa-` + `sagot` (answer). This is the future tense of `magsagot`.
original_explanation: What you're supposed to do during a job interview or a recitation, but your brain goes into blue screen mode. Also what a sassy teenager does to their parents, turning a simple question into a full-blown debate. 'Huwag kang magsasagot nang pabalang!'
usage_notes: Future tense of `magsagot`. Can mean 'will answer' (a question) or 'will talk back' (disrespectfully).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **magsasagot** ng telepono?","translation":"Who **will answer** the phone?"},{"sentence":"Bukas na ako **magsasagot** ng mga email na iyan.","translation":"I **will answer** those emails tomorrow."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsunod sa isang partikular na plano ng pagkain, kadalasan upang magbawas ng timbang o para sa kalusugan.
original_explanation: The eternal cycle of Filipino life: Pista -> Kain -> 'OMG, ang taba ko na' -> Magdiyeta. It’s that solemn promise you make to yourself to eat only kamote and fish... which lasts until someone offers you a piece of crispy pata. Then the cycle repeats. Also known as 'starting a diet tomorrow, for the rest of your life.'
usage_notes: Commonly used. The struggle is real and universally understood in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **magdiyeta** para sa kanyang kalusugan.","translation":"She decided **to go on a diet** for her health."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **magdiyeta** kapag maraming masasarap na pagkain sa paligid.","translation":"It's hard **to diet** when there's a lot of delicious food around."}]

translation: to gather; to collect; to solicit
meaning_filipino: Magtipon o mag-ipon ng mga bagay, impormasyon, o pondo mula sa iba't ibang mapagkukunan.
etymology: From `mang-` (actor-focus verb prefix) + `kalap` (gather). The 'k' in 'kalap' assimilates into the 'ng' of the prefix.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you're raising funds for a cause, collecting signatures for a petition, or just trying to get all the chismis from different sources to form a complete story. It's the act of actively seeking and gathering things. The ultimate 'data gathering' verb.
usage_notes: The root 'kalap' is not commonly used on its own. The verb 'mangalap' is the most frequent form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **mangalap** ng pondo para sa mga nasalanta ng bagyo.","translation":"We need to **solicit** funds for the typhoon victims."},{"sentence":"Nagpunta siya sa library para **mangalap** ng datos para sa kanyang thesis.","translation":"She went to the library to **gather** data for her thesis."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang ibabaw o lugar na natakpan o ginawa gamit ang semento.
original_explanation: When the 'kalye' is no longer 'lubak-lubak' because the barangay captain finally used the budget. It's the difference between a dusty palengke and a clean-ish one. Smooth, hard, and ready for basketball.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malinis na ang daan dahil ito ay **simentado** na.","translation":"The road is now clean because it is already **cemented**."},{"sentence":"Naglalaro ng basketball ang mga bata sa **simentadong** kort.","translation":"The kids are playing basketball on the **cemented** court."}]

translation: to shout; to jeer; to yell
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalabas ng malakas na boses o sigaw, kadalasan upang ipahayag ang matinding damdamin, manlibak, o tumawag ng pansin.
original_explanation: What you do when your favorite team scores in a basketball game, when you see your idol at a concert, or when the jeepney driver just won't stop for you. It's releasing that inner energy, for better or for worse.
usage_notes: Can be a shout of joy, anger, or to get attention. 'Sumigaw' is a more general term for shouting, while 'manghiyaw' often implies a more public, collective, or intense yelling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **manghiyaw** ang mga tao nang lumabas sa entablado ang paborito nilang banda.","translation":"The people started to **shout** when their favorite band came out on stage."},{"sentence":"Pinagsabihan sila na huwag **manghiyaw** sa loob ng aklatan.","translation":"They were told not to **yell** inside the library."}]

translation: will go for a walk; will stroll; will go sightseeing
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalakad-lakad o pagpunta sa isang lugar para sa libangan o pagliliwaliw sa hinaharap.
etymology: Root word 'pasyal' is from Spanish 'pasear' (to walk, to stroll).
original_explanation: 'Yung sagot mo 'pag tinanong ka kung anong gagawin mo sa long weekend: 'Mamamasyal kami sa mall!' or 'Sa Baguio kami mamamasyal.' It's the future tense of 'gala,' the promise of leaving your house for fun and not for work.
usage_notes: This is the future tense of the verb 'mamasyal'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bukas, **mamamasyal** kami sa Luneta Park.","translation":"Tomorrow, we **will go for a walk** in Luneta Park."},{"sentence":"Saan kayo **mamamasyal** ngayong bakasyon?","translation":"Where **will** you **go sightseeing** this vacation?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggapi o pagwawagi laban sa isang kalaban sa isang kompetisyon, labanan, o argumento.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na na-1v5 mo 'yung kalaban sa Mobile Legends. You just had to **talunin** them all. Or 'yung ginagawa mo sa sarili mo 'pag nag-iisip ka ng counter-argument sa away niyo ng jowa mo three hours after the fact.
usage_notes: The object-focused form of the verb 'talo'. 'Talunin mo sila' means 'Defeat them'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **talunin** ang kabilang koponan para manalo sa kampeonato.","translation":"We need to **defeat** the other team to win the championship."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, kaya mong **talunin** ang lahat ng pagsubok na iyan.","translation":"Don't worry, you can **beat** all of those challenges."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi kung saan pinagdugtong o pinagkabit ang dalawa o higit pang bagay, tulad ng lubid, kawad, o kahoy.
original_explanation: Imagine two broken wires you need to connect to make the WiFi work again. That connection point is the sugpong. Or think of it like a 'collab' in the real world—two separate things joined to become one functional (or dysfunctional) unit. It's the OG version of copy-paste, but for physical objects.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb, 'isugpong' (to join/splice).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maluwag ang **sugpong** ng dalawang kable kaya nawawalan ng kuryente.","translation":"The **joint** of the two cables is loose, that's why the power goes out."},{"sentence":"Kailangang tibayan ang **sugpong** sa pagitan ng mga piraso ng kawayan.","translation":"The **connection** between the bamboo pieces needs to be strengthened."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa akto ng pagbili ng mga bagay na hindi naman talaga kailangan mula sa Lazada, na dala ng biglaang impulso o dahil sa mga alok at sale. Ito ay isang modernong paggamit ng salitang "budol".
etymology: Combination of the brand name "Lazada" and "budol" (a term for a swindling scheme, now adapted to mean an impulse buy).
original_explanation: The modern "budol-budol gang" is now just you, your phone, and a 12.12 sale. Lazada Budol is when you open the app to just "look" at a phone case, and you end up checking out a new air fryer, three pairs of socks, a "live-laugh-love" wall decal, and a 10-kilo sack of cat food. It's the stuff you bought that you didn't know you needed until you saw it on flash sale. #BudolFinds
usage_notes: A very popular slang term in the context of online shopping. Can also refer to being scammed, but more commonly refers to impulse buying.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hala, na-**Lazada Budol** na naman ako. Ang dami kong na-check out kagabi.","translation":"Oh no, I fell for a **Lazada impulse buy** again. I checked out so many items last night."},{"sentence":"I-share mo naman 'yang mga **Lazada Budol** finds mo!","translation":"Come on, share your **Lazada impulse buy** finds!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasapi ng hukbong sandatahan ng isang bansa na may tungkuling ipagtanggol ito laban sa mga banta.
original_explanation: Your real-life Captain America or Descendants of the Sun oppa. They're the brave folks in camo, protecting the country. In everyday life, 'sundalo' can also be a metaphor for someone who fights for something, like a 'sundalo ng pag-ibig' (soldier of love) who's fighting for a relationship.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tatay niya ay isang matapang na **sundalo**.","translation":"His father is a brave **soldier**."},{"sentence":"Nagbigay-pugay ang mga tao sa mga **sundalo** na lumaban para sa bayan.","translation":"The people paid tribute to the **soldiers** who fought for the country."}]

translation: to make someone eager; to excite
meaning_filipino: Pukawin ang matinding pagnanais o pananabik ng isang tao para sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is what teasers for the next Marvel movie or the '12.12 sale' notifications from Shopee do to you. They sabikin you. It's the act of making someone feel excited and impatient for something to happen. 'Huwag mo akong sabikin sa wala!' (Don't get my hopes up for nothing!) is a classic 'hugot' line.
usage_notes: It's a causative verb, meaning it's about causing the emotion of 'sabik' in someone else.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo siyang **sabikin** sa mga pangako na hindi mo tutuparin.","translation":"Don't **make him eager** with promises you won't fulfill."},{"sentence":"Sinabik ng anunsyo ang mga tagahanga para sa bagong album.","translation":"The announcement **excited** the fans for the new album."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang elektroniko na kumukuha ng tunog at ginagawang signal na elektrikal, karaniwang ginagamit sa pagpapalakas ng boses o pagre-record. Pinaikling anyo ng "microphone".
original_explanation: The magic wand of every karaoke king and queen. Ito yung sandata mo para marinig ng buong barangay ang version mo ng "My Way." Sa mga meeting, ito yung laging may "pa-check, pa-check, 1, 2, 3." Essential equipment for chismis amplification.
usage_notes: "Mike" is the common conversational term. "Mikropono" is the formal Filipino equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakitest nga kung gumagana ang **mike**.","translation":"Please test if the **microphone** is working."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang antas ng edukasyon sa pagitan ng elementarya at mataas na paaralan (high school), karaniwang sumasaklaw sa ika-7 hanggang ika-10 baitang sa ilalim ng sistemang K-12.
original_explanation: The awkward teenage years of your school life, personified. You're no longer a 'bata' but not yet a 'dalaga' or 'binata'. This is the era of JS Prom, first crushes that you only stare at from afar, and intense barkada drama. Welcome to the jungle, baby.
usage_notes: Corresponds to what is now commonly called "Junior High School" in the Philippine K-12 system.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aking anak ay papasok na sa **paaralang-panggitna** sa susunod na taon.","translation":"My child will enter **middle school** next year."},{"sentence":"Dito sa **paaralang-panggitna** unang nagkakilala ang magkakaibigan.","translation":"The friends first met here in **junior high school**."}]
related: ["elementarya","mataas na paaralan","junior high school","senior high school"]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng mahabang berdeng gulay na legumbre na karaniwang isinasahog sa mga lutuing Pilipino tulad ng sinigang at adobo.
original_explanation: The green, super long veggie that's a staple in every Pinoy kitchen. Kasama 'yan sa "Bahay Kubo" squad. Perfect sa sinigang, adobo, at pinakbet. Ito rin 'yung gulay na parang rubber band kung minsan, 'di mo makagat-kagat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghiwa si nanay ng **sitaw** para sa adobong lulutuin niya.","translation":"Mom sliced some **string beans** for the adobo she will cook."}]

translation: to make beautiful; to improve the appearance of
meaning_filipino: Gawing maganda, mas kaakit-akit, o mas maayos ang isang bagay; pagbutihin ang itsura.
original_explanation: That moment when your boss looks at your report and says, '**Gandahan** mo pa.' It means 'make it better/prettier.' It's what you do to your PowerPoint presentation before a big pitch, what you tell the makeup artist for your graduation, or what you do to your resume before a job hunt. It's the verb for leveling up the aesthetics.
usage_notes: Can be used literally (improving physical appearance) or figuratively (improving a work, plan, or story).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sige, **gandahan** mo pa ang drawing mo para mas mataas ang grado mo.","translation":"Go on, **make your drawing more beautiful** so you get a higher grade."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **gandahan** ang sulat-kamay mo para mabasa.","translation":"You need to **improve** your handwriting so it's readable."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang muling pagsusuri o pag-aaral sa isang bagay, tulad ng isang dokumento o aralin, upang ito ay iwasto o pagbutihin.
original_explanation: What you do to your thesis at 3 AM, fueled by coffee and desperation. Also, that moment you re-read your 'sent' message to your crush and realize you had a typo. That's a frantic, internal 'magrebisa' moment. In the BPO world, this is what you do before sending that crucial email to the client.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **magrebisa** para sa pagsusulit bukas.","translation":"I need to **review** for the exam tomorrow."},{"sentence":"**Magrebisa** ka muna ng iyong ulat bago mo ito ipasa.","translation":"You should **revise** your report first before you submit it."}]

meaning_filipino: Palamuti na isinusuot sa tainga, karaniwang nakasabit sa butas ng earlobe.
original_explanation: Your lola's term for 'hikaw' or earrings. It sounds more fancy and vintage, like something you'd find in her jewelry box along with other family heirlooms. If someone calls your earrings 'arilyos,' they're probably from an older generation or just feeling a bit formal.
usage_notes: 'Hikaw' is the more common, everyday term. 'Arilyos' is less common and sounds more classic or formal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng iyong gintong **arilyos**.","translation":"Your gold **earrings** are beautiful."},{"sentence":"Nawala ang isang piraso ng kanyang paboritong **arilyos**.","translation":"She lost one piece of her favorite **earrings**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o gusali kung saan kinakatay ang mga hayop upang ang karne ay maging pagkain.
original_explanation: The place your lechon, crispy pata, and sinigang na baboy had a very, very bad day. It's the pre-palengke stage of your favorite meat dishes. Not a great place to bring a date, unless you're both butchers.
usage_notes: The literal term for a slaughterhouse. The more common and specific term is 'katayan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala ang mga baboy sa **patayan ng hayop** para sa proseso ng pagkatay.","translation":"The pigs were brought to the **slaughterhouse** for the butchering process."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malapot na pormulasyon na ginagamit kasama ng sipilyo upang linisin at panatilihin ang kalusugan ng mga ngipin.
original_explanation: Yung kasama ng toothbrush mo sa umaga at gabi. Ang tawag ng lola mo sa Colgate o Close-Up. Kung wala kang **pasta**, bawal kang bumulong sa katabi mo. Essential para sa fresh breath, lalo na kung mahilig ka sa kape at yosi.
usage_notes: Bagama't ang "toothpaste" ay malawakang nauunawaan at ginagamit, ang "pasta" ay nananatiling isang karaniwan at medyo tradisyonal na termino, lalo na sa mga nakatatanda.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naubusan na tayo ng **pasta**; kailangan nating bumili.","translation":"We've run out of **toothpaste**; we need to buy some."},{"sentence":"Lagyan mo ng **pasta** ang sipilyo bago magsipilyo.","translation":"Put **toothpaste** on the toothbrush before brushing."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaayos ng mga pangyayari o petsa ayon sa kanilang pagkakasunod-sunod sa panahon.
original_explanation: The official timeline of events. Like when you're explaining a chismis to your friend and they say, 'Wait, from the top!' You have to give them the kronolohiya – who said what, when it happened, and in what order – so the tea is served correctly.
usage_notes: A formal term used in history, literature, and legal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inilahad ng historyador ang **kronolohiya** ng mga kaganapan bago ang rebolusyon.","translation":"The historian presented the **chronology** of events before the revolution."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kondisyong medikal kung saan ang isang bahagi ng organo o tisyu ay nakausli sa isang butas o mahinang bahagi ng kalamnan o tisyung pumapalibot dito.
original_explanation: This is the TMI (too much information) your tito shares after carrying a heavy sack of rice. It's when something inside you decides to pop out and say hello, usually in the groin area. Not a fun surprise. It's the body's version of a system breach.
usage_notes: Primarily a medical term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinayuhan ng doktor ang pasyente na mag-opera para sa kanyang **luslos**.","translation":"The doctor advised the patient to have surgery for his **hernia**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang teoryang pampulitika at pang-ekonomiya na naglalayon ng isang lipunang walang mga uri, kung saan ang mga kagamitan sa produksyon ay pag-aari ng lahat at pinamamahalaan ng komunidad.
original_explanation: That political idea where everything is supposedly shared, "from each according to his ability, to each according to his needs." In a barkada, it's the friend who says, "Share tayo lahat sa pagkain," but in reality, it’s a lot more... complicated. And often used as a bogeyman in political arguments.
usage_notes: A political and economic term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aralan namin ang kasaysayan ng **kumunismo** sa klase.","translation":"We studied the history of **communism** in class."},{"sentence":"Maraming debate ang umiikot sa mga ideolohiya ng **kumunismo** at kapitalismo.","translation":"Many debates revolve around the ideologies of **communism** and capitalism."}]

meaning_filipino: Katatapos pa lamang malampasan ang isang pagsubok, sakit, o mahirap na sitwasyon.
etymology: From the prefix ka- and the reduplication of the first syllable of the root word raos (ka-ra-raos), indicating a very recent past action.
original_explanation: That feeling of relief right after a hellish week of exams, a major client presentation, or surviving the flu. You're still a bit tired, but you're like, "Whew, tapos na!" It’s the "just survived" status update. "Kararaos lang sa 13th month pay, ubos na agad."
usage_notes: This is a verb in the recent perfective aspect. It emphasizes the very recent completion of overcoming a difficulty.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kararaos** lang ng pamilya sa matinding pagsubok.","translation":"The family **just got through** a severe trial."},{"sentence":"Mukha siyang pagod dahil **kararaos** lang niya sa sakit.","translation":"He looks tired because he **just recovered** from an illness."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbabalik sa isipan ng isang bagay, tao, o pangyayari na naganap sa nakaraan. Ito ay ang paggunita sa isang natapos na aksyon.
etymology: From na- (actor-focus verb prefix, past tense) + alala (memory, remember).
original_explanation: This is the past tense. The memory has been successfully retrieved from your brain's hard drive. It's when you suddenly go, "Ah! Naalala ko na kung saan ko nilagay 'yung susi!" It's that "eureka!" moment of remembering, or the bittersweet "I just remembered our anniversary" text.
usage_notes: This is the past tense form. 'Naaalala' is the present tense. 'Maaalala' is the future tense. Note the difference in stress and syllable count from the present tense 'naaalala'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigla kong **naalala** na may deadline pala ako ngayon.","translation":"I suddenly **remembered** that I have a deadline today."},{"sentence":"**Naalala** mo ba noong una tayong nagkita?","translation":"Do you **remember** when we first met?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang murang bahagi ng isang halaman na nagsisimula pa lamang tumubo; ang simula o pagsibol ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the 'new beginnings' aesthetic. It's the tiny green thing peeking out of the soil that makes a plantita's heart sing. Metaphorically, it's the start of a new love team (may umuusbong na pagtitinginan), a new trend, or a new business idea you had in the shower. The hope of what's to come.
usage_notes: Used both literally for plants and figuratively for new ideas, feelings, or movements.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May mga bagong **usbong** na ang aking tanim na kamatis.","translation":"My tomato plant has new **sprouts**."},{"sentence":"Sila ang mga bagong **usbong** na bituin sa industriya ng musika.","translation":"They are the newly **emerging** stars in the music industry."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagawaan kung saan inaayos ang mga butas o sira ng mga gulong ng sasakyan sa pamamagitan ng proseso ng bulkanisasyon.
etymology: Mula sa mga salitang Ingles na "vulcanizing" at "shop."
original_explanation: Ang superhero ng mga driver na na-flatan. Ito yung lugar na may sign na "FLAT TIRE? WE CAN FIX IT!" at laging may nakatambak na lumang gulong sa labas. Dito mo maririnig ang pamilyar na tunog ng "psssssst" ng hangin at ang amoy ng nasusunog na goma. Sila ang dahilan kung bakit hindi nauwi sa malagim na trahedya ang road trip mo dahil lang sa isang pako sa kalsada.
usage_notes: Ang katumbas sa Tagalog ay "pabulkanaysingan" o "pagawaan ng gulong," ngunit mas karaniwang ginagamit ang Ingles na termino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghanap kami ng bukas na **vulcanizing shop** noong nabutasan kami ng gulong sa SLEX.","translation":"We looked for an open **vulcanizing shop** when we got a flat tire on SLEX."},{"sentence":"Magkano ang bayad sa pagpapatapal ng gulong sa **vulcanizing shop**?","translation":"How much does it cost to patch a tire at the **vulcanizing shop**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging mapurol, maaaring tumukoy sa isang kagamitan na hindi matalim o sa isang tao na mabagal umunawa.
original_explanation: When the gunting in the kitchen can't even cut paper, that's kapulpulan. When your friend still doesn't get the joke after you've explained it three times, that's also kapulpulan. It’s the state of being hopelessly blunt or dense, whether it's a knife or a mind.
usage_notes: Can be considered offensive when used to describe a person's intelligence. More commonly used to describe the bluntness of objects.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa **kapulpulan** ng kutsilyo, nahirapan akong hiwain ang karne.","translation":"Because of the **dullness** of the knife, I had a hard time slicing the meat."},{"sentence":"Ikinainis niya ang **kapulpulan** ng sistema sa pagproseso ng mga dokumento.","translation":"He was annoyed by the **inefficiency** of the system for processing documents."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit at nabibitbit na kalan, karaniwang gumagamit ng gaas, denatured alcohol, o butane bilang panggatong.
original_explanation: The trusty sidekick for your kaldero during a brownout or a beach trip. It's the small, often single-burner stove that saves the day when you need to cook sinangag or heat up your coffee, but your main gasul ran out. The OG camping gear before those fancy induction cookers.
usage_notes: Often associated with camping, outdoor cooking, or as a backup cooking device.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit namin ang **kosinilya** para magluto ng sardinas noong nag-brownout.","translation":"We used the **portable stove** to cook sardines during the power outage."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyon na ginagamit sa dulo ng isang pahayag upang magbigay-diin na iyon na ang pinal na salita at hindi na mababago pa.
etymology: From African American Vernacular English (AAVE), popularized through internet and pop culture. A variation of 'period'.
original_explanation: The mic drop of conversations. You use this when you've stated a fact, an opinion, or a 'hugot' line so powerful that no further discussion is needed. Example: 'Mas masarap ang Jollibee Chickenjoy. Periodt.' It’s the final 't' that adds the sass and shuts down all arguments. No cap.
usage_notes: A very modern slang term. The final 't' is for emphasis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ako ang reyna dito. **Periodt**.","translation":"I am the queen here. **Period**."},{"sentence":"Hindi tayo bagay, tanggapin mo na. **Periodt**.","translation":"We're not meant for each other, just accept it. **And that's final**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang de-kuryente o pangkamay na ginagamit upang makagawa ng butas; o isang paulit-ulit na pagsasanay upang mahasa ang isang kasanayan.
original_explanation: May dalawang klase ng **drill**. Una, 'yung gamit ni Tatay pag may inaayos sa bahay at ang ingay-ingay. Pangalawa, 'yung pinapagawa sa'yo ng boss mo sa BPO, 'yung mga practice calls, o 'yung fire **drill** at earthquake **drill** na akala mo totoo na. Parehong nakaka-stress.
usage_notes: The word can refer to both the tool ('barena' in Spanish) and the repetitive exercise ('pagsasanay').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroon kaming earthquake **drill** sa opisina mamayang hapon.","translation":"We have an earthquake **drill** at the office this afternoon."},{"sentence":"Pahiram nga ng **drill**, bubutasan ko lang itong pader.","translation":"Can I borrow the **drill**? I just need to make a hole in this wall."}]

translation: to be able to eat; to accidentally eat
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang kumain; hindi sinasadyang mailagay sa bibig at malunok ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: The 'maka-' prefix here is a lifesaver. It's the difference between 'Kainin mo 'yan!' (Eat that!) and 'Sana makain ko 'yan.' (I hope I get to eat that.) It's also the verb for when you accidentally swallow a buto ng santol. 'Hala, nakain ko yung buto!'
usage_notes: Can express ability, opportunity, or accidental action. The context determines the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **makain** ko na ang paborito kong sinigang.","translation":"I hope I'll be **able to eat** my favorite sinigang."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka, baka **makain** ng bata ang maliliit na laruan.","translation":"Be careful, the child might **accidentally eat** the small toys."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang taong hindi maselan, madaling makibagay, at simple ang mga kagustuhan, lalo na sa pagkain.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na "cowboy," na inangkop sa bagong kahulugan sa Pilipinas.
original_explanation: 'Yung tropa mong kahit saang karinderya mo dalhin, go lang. Kahit anong pagkain ihain mo, kakainin (basta hindi panis). Hindi maarte, walang reklamo. "Tara, mag-kamay tayo!" 'Yan ang tunay na koboy. The opposite of your friend na, "Ew, I don't eat street food."
usage_notes: Ang kahulugang "hindi maselan" ay mas karaniwan sa Pilipinas kaysa sa literal na kahulugan nito (tagapag-alaga ng baka).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala sa akin, **koboy** ako, kahit ano kinakain ko.","translation":"Don't worry about me, I'm **not picky**, I eat anything."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malawak na anyong lupa na pantay at mababa; kapatagan.
etymology: Mula sa Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *pataR, na nangangahulugang 'patag, pantay'.
original_explanation: Not just a description, but the place itself. Think Central Luzon, the "Rice Granary of the Philippines." It's a huge expanse of flat land, perfect for farming. Basically, it's the adjective 'patag' made into a location.
usage_notes: Madalas gamiting kasingkahulugan ng "kapatagan."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malawak ang **patag** sa gitnang Luzon.","translation":"The **plain** in central Luzon is vast."},{"sentence":"Nagtanim sila ng palay sa **patag**.","translation":"They planted rice on the **flatland**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng pambalot sa isang bagay, tulad ng papel, plastik, o dahon, upang ito ay protektahan, itago, o ihanda para sa pagbibigay.
original_explanation: What you do to your Christmas gifts, your take-out ulam from the handaan ('pa-balot naman po!'), and your feelings when someone asks 'kamusta ka?'. You cover it up nicely so it's ready to go or ready to be hidden.
usage_notes: Very common verb. "Pabalot" is a staple phrase in Filipino eateries, meaning 'for takeout'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **magbalot** ng mga regalo para sa Pasko.","translation":"I need to **wrap** the gifts for Christmas."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **magbalot** ng tirang pagkain.","translation":"Don't forget to **pack** the leftover food."}]

translation: fishing with a hook and line; angling
meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng paghuli ng isda gamit ang isang bingwit, na binubuo ng pamansing, pisi, at pain.
etymology: From "bingwit" (fishing rod/hook and line). The "pan-" prefix becomes "pam-" and the first syllable of the root is reduplicated ("-bi-" becomes "-mi-").
original_explanation: The OG "waiting game." It's what your lolo does on a quiet Sunday morning by the river. It's the ultimate test of patience, where you spend hours staring at the water, hoping for a bite, only to end up buying fish from the palengke on your way home.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to angling, not other forms of fishing like using a net (lambat). This is the action, while 'pamingwit' is the tool.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pamimingwit** ay isang magandang paraan upang makapag-relax at malayo sa ingay ng siyudad.","translation":"**Angling** is a good way to relax and get away from the noise of the city."},{"sentence":"Nakatulong sa kanilang kabuhayan ang **pamimingwit** sa kalapit na lawa.","translation":"**Fishing with a hook and line** in the nearby lake helped with their livelihood."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagbawas o nag-alis ng isang bahagi mula sa isang kabuuan, karaniwan ay tumutukoy sa pera, puntos, o bilang.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung nangyayari sa sweldo mo tuwing payday. Bago mo pa mahawakan, andami nang SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, at tax na kumaltas. The original "sanaol" -- sanaol buo ang sahod.
usage_notes: Commonly used in financial or accounting contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumaltas** ng malaking buwis mula sa kanyang sahod ngayong buwan.","translation":"A large tax was **deducted** from his salary this month."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi ako **kumaltas** sa perang ipinadala mo.","translation":"Don't worry, I did not **deduct** from the money you sent."}]

translation: to have something carried or transported
meaning_filipino: Utos na ipabuhat o ipaalis ang isang bagay o mga bagay mula sa isang lugar patungo sa iba, karaniwan ay sa tulong ng ibang tao.
original_explanation: The official verb for 'lipat-bahay' (moving houses) or when you're delegating cleanup duty. "Pakisabi sa mga kargador na **ipahakot** na lahat ng gamit sa sala." It's the boss move of pointing at a pile of stuff and telling someone to get other people to move it.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagdesisyon siyang **ipahakot** na ang mga lumang kasangkapan sa bodega.","translation":"He decided to **have** the old furniture **transported** to the warehouse."},{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **ipahakot** mo na ang basura sa labas.","translation":"Please, **have** the trash **carried** outside."}]

translation: to inform someone, to let someone know
meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng balita o impormasyon ang isang tao.
original_explanation: The formal way of saying "i-update mo 'ko" or "keep me posted." 'Yung hiling ng nanay mo bago ka umalis ng bahay: "Pabalitaan mo ako kung nakarating ka na." It's the pre-chat era way of asking for a life update.
usage_notes: The person being informed is the object of the verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pabalitaan** mo na lang ako kung ano ang magiging desisyon nila.","translation":"Just **let me know** what their decision will be."},{"sentence":"Pinakiusapan niyang **pabalitaan** siya tungkol sa kalagayan ng kanyang lola.","translation":"He requested to be **informed** about his grandmother's condition."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang koleksiyon o kalipunan ng mga piling akdang pampanitikan, tulad ng mga tula, maikling kuwento, o sanaysay, na karaniwang may iisang tema o mula sa iisang panahon.
original_explanation: Parang playlist sa Spotify pero para sa mga libro. Imbes na mga kanta, mga tula o kwento ng iba't ibang author ang pinagsama-sama. Isipin mo, "Best of OPM Hugot Lines: The Anthology."
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa larangan ng panitikan at akademya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kasama ang kanyang tula sa isang **antolohiya** ng mga makabagong manunulat.","translation":"Her poem was included in an **anthology** of modern writers."},{"sentence":"Pinamagatang 'Mga Tinig Mula sa Laylayan' ang inilunsad na **antolohiya**.","translation":"The launched **anthology** was titled 'Voices from the Margins'."}]

translation: to make less flavorful; to dilute
meaning_filipino: Bawasan o alisin ang lasa o anghang ng isang bagay, karaniwan sa pamamagitan ng pagdaragdag ng tubig o iba pang sangkap.
original_explanation: When you add too much water to the sinigang and it loses its signature asim-kilig. 'Bes, tabangan mo ng konti yung kape, ang tapang eh.' It's the art of dilution, basically. Can also mean when a conversation or relationship loses its spark. Aray.
usage_notes: The root word 'tabang' means blandness or tastelessness. This verb means to cause something to become bland.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakilagyan ng tubig para **tabangan** ang sobrang alat na sabaw.","translation":"Please add water to **make** the very salty soup **less flavorful**."},{"sentence":"Nawalan ako ng gana nang **tabangan** niya ang usapan.","translation":"I lost interest when he **made** the conversation **bland**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging nabasa o natalsikan ng likido na naganap na.
original_explanation: The past tense of getting something wet. Like when you forgot your umbrella and the rain turned you into a walking wet look-supermodel, you **nagbasâ**. Or when you accidentally spilled your milk tea on your laptop. Panic!
usage_notes: Completed aspect of 'magbasâ'. The stress on the last syllable with a glottal stop /ba-SÂ/ distinguishes it from 'nagbasa' (read).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagbasâ** ng sahig ang tumulong bubong.","translation":"The leaking roof **wet** the floor."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang lumabas, **nagbasâ** ako ng sahig.","translation":"Don't go out, I just **wet** the floor."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagkukuwento o naglalahad ng mga pangyayari sa isang akda, pelikula, o pagtatanghal.
original_explanation: The official chismoso/chismosa of a story. This is the voice of Morgan Freeman in a movie, the lola telling scary stories on Halloween, or your friend recounting the entire plot of a K-drama they just binge-watched. They hold the thread of the story.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malinaw ang boses ng **tagapagsalaysay** sa dokumentaryo.","translation":"The narrator's voice in the documentary was clear."},{"sentence":"Sa kwentong-bayan, madalas ay may isang mahiwagang **tagapagsalaysay**.","translation":"In folklore, there is often a mysterious **narrator**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang halaga, bilang, o tantiya na malapit sa tunay na sukat o halaga ngunit hindi eksakto.
original_explanation: Your best guess. It's the "mga more or less" of mathematics and life. When you're telling your friend what time you'll arrive, and you say "mga 7 PM," that's an aproksimasyon. It's the official term for "hula-hula pero medyo may basis."
usage_notes: Primarily used in technical, mathematical, or formal contexts. In everyday conversation, 'tantiya' or 'mga' is more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ibinigay niyang sukat ay isang **aproksimasyon** lamang.","translation":"The measurement he gave was only an **approximation**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pautos na paraan ng pagsasabi na lumapit sa nagsasalita; pinaikling anyo ng "pumarito ka."
etymology: Pagsasama ng panlaping "pa-" (tungo sa) at "rito," na varyant ng "dito" (here) na ginagamit pagkatapos ng patinig.
original_explanation: The formal, almost biblical way of saying "Halika!" or "Come here!" Sounds like something your lola would shout from the probinsya when she wants you to get something for her. It has that classic, old-school authority vibe. Use it when "halika" is too casual and you want to sound like a character from a historical drama.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa pormal o pampanitikang konteksto. Ang mas karaniwang katumbas sa pang-araw-araw na usapan ay "Halika!" o "Punta ka dito!". Ang "Parito" ay ang anyong pautos ng pandiwang "pumarito" (to come here).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Parito** ka, anak, at may sasabihin ako sa iyo.","translation":"**Come here**, child, I have something to tell you."},{"sentence":"Sumigaw ang hari, '**Parito** kayong lahat sa aking harapan!'","translation":"The king shouted, '**Come here**, all of you, before me!'"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng langis na nakukuha mula sa pagpiga ng mga bunga ng puno ng oliba.
original_explanation: The *sosyal* cousin of regular cooking oil. This is the **langis** you use when you're feeling fancy and making pasta, or a salad dressing. It comes in different grades like "extra virgin," which sounds way more dramatic than it is. Basically, it's the Tito/Tita oil of Manila.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagyan mo ng kaunting **langis ng oliba** ang salad para sa dagdag na lasa.","translation":"Add a little **olive oil** to the salad for extra flavor."},{"sentence":"Mas healthy daw ang **langis ng oliba** kaysa sa ordinaryong mantika.","translation":"They say **olive oil** is healthier than regular cooking oil."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang natural na proseso ng paglalabas ng itlog mula sa katawan ng isang babaeng hayop, tulad ng manok, ibon, o reptilya.
original_explanation: The ultimate "push gift" in the animal kingdom. This is the main job of a hen in a poultry farm. It’s the reason you have eggs for breakfast. For sea turtles, it's that epic, tear-jerking journey back to the beach where they were born just to continue the circle of life.
usage_notes: Used for oviparous animals (those that lay eggs).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May takdang panahon para sa **pangingitlog** ng mga pawikan.","translation":"There is a specific season for the **egg-laying** of sea turtles."},{"sentence":"Humina ang **pangingitlog** ng aming mga manok.","translation":"Our chickens' **egg-laying** has weakened."}]

translation: To be pressed upon; to be squashed
meaning_filipino: Ang maranasan ang pagpindot, pagpisil, o pag-ipit nang may puwersa.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're in a jampacked MRT train at 7 AM and you can't breathe. You are being madiin-an by the sea of humanity. It's also what happens to your pandesal when you put it at the very bottom of your grocery bag.
usage_notes: The prefix 'ma-' indicates that the subject is receiving the action of being pressed. Often used in its inflected form 'madiinan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka baka **madiin** ng pinto ang kamay mo.","translation":"Be careful, your hand might **be pressed** by the door."},{"sentence":"**Nadiinan** ng mga libro ang kanyang salamin kaya ito nabasag.","translation":"His glasses **were squashed** by the books, that's why they broke."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangunahing hagdanan ng isang bahay o gusali, karaniwang malaki at marangya.
etymology: Mula sa `pa-` + `saog` (isang bihirang salitang-ugat para sa 'baba') + `-an`. Ang ideya ay 'daanan pababa'.
original_explanation: This isn't just any hagdan. This is the grand staircase you see in movies, 'yung bababa 'yung bida na naka-gown for the prom or debut. The kind of stairs you'd find in Malacañang Palace, not in your typical apartment. It's the stairway with drama. The OG "grand entrance" spot.
usage_notes: Isang pormal at medyo makalumang salita. Hindi karaniwang ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap; mas madalas marinig ang "pangunahing hagdanan".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marahan siyang bumaba sa malawak na **panaugan** ng mansyon.","translation":"She slowly descended the wide **main stairway** of the mansion."},{"sentence":"Ang disenyo ng **panaugan** ay hango sa arkitekturang Espanyol.","translation":"The design of the **grand staircase** is based on Spanish architecture."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mahabang bahagi sa likuran ng isang damit, bestida, o traje de boda na sumasayad o humahaba sa sahig.
original_explanation: The "buntot" of a wedding gown or any fancy dress. 'Yung kailangan pa ng abay (bridesmaid) para lang buhatin at ayusin para sa perfect wedding photo. The longer the kola, the more dramatic the entrance. Parang sa buhay, the more baggage you carry, the more dramatic your life is.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa pananahi, moda, at paglalarawan ng mga pormal na kasuotan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakaganda ng **kola** ng kanyang traje de boda.","translation":"The **train** of her wedding gown is so beautiful."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sidhi o tindi ng damdamin, pagnanasa, o pananampalataya.
etymology: From ka- + alab + -an. 'Alab' means 'blaze' or 'glow', so 'kaalaban' is the state of being ablaze with feeling.
original_explanation: This is the energy in the room when the Philippines is in a basketball final. It's the passion of a rallyist fighting for a cause. It's the intense 'hugot' you feel listening to a Moira song after a breakup. It’s not just a feeling; it’s a fire in your soul. Peak emotional intensity.
usage_notes: A poetic or literary term used to describe intense emotions, passion, or devotion. Not commonly used in casual conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Makikita sa kanyang mga mata ang **kaalaban** ng kanyang pag-ibig.","translation":"You can see in his eyes the **fervor** of his love."},{"sentence":"Ipinaglaban niya ang kanyang prinsipyo nang may **kaalaban**.","translation":"He fought for his principles with **ardor**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang nakasarang kompartimento o istruktura na iniinitan para sa pagluluto ng pagkain, pagpapatuyo ng materyales, o paglikha ng palayok.
original_explanation: The OG oven. Before La Germania, there was the pugon. It's the brick oven that makes the best-tasting pandesal and the crispiest lechon. It's hot, it's traditional, and it's where the magic happens. Think of your lola's house in the province.
usage_notes: Can refer to a traditional brick oven, a pottery kiln, or even an industrial furnace.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas masarap ang pandesal na niluto sa **pugon**.","translation":"The bread rolls baked in a **brick oven** are more delicious."},{"sentence":"Dinala ng magpapalayok ang kanyang mga gawa sa **pugon** upang patigasin.","translation":"The potter brought his creations to the **kiln** to harden them."}]

translation: to catch at the right time, to chance upon
meaning_filipino: Ang magkaroon ng pagkakataong makita, mahuli, o maisagawa ang isang bagay sa eksakto o tamang oras.
original_explanation: This is the universe conspiring in your favor. It's catching the last seat on the MRT, arriving just as the food is served, or messaging your crush right when they're online and feeling chatty. It's all about perfect timing. "Swerte! Na-tiyempuhan ko yung 12.12 sale!" The opposite is "minalas" or "di umabot."
usage_notes: Implies a stroke of luck or good timing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay **matiyempuhan** natin siyang nasa bahay.","translation":"I hope we **chance upon** him at home."},{"sentence":"Buti na lang at na-**tiyempuhan** ko ang pagdaan ng bus.","translation":"It's a good thing I **caught** the bus as it was passing by."}]

translation: to carry on the shoulder or back
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbubuhat ng isang mabigat na bagay sa pamamagitan ng paglalagay nito sa balikat o likod.
original_explanation: Literally, this is what a kargador at the palengke does with a sack of rice. Figuratively, it’s what every breadwinner, student with too many subjects, or person dealing with life's problems does. You carry the weight. It’s the physical and emotional act of shouldering a burden. 'Pasan ko ang daigdig' is the ultimate expression of this.
usage_notes: Often used figuratively to mean 'to shoulder a responsibility or burden.' The phrase 'magpasan sa likod' is slightly redundant as 'magpasan' already implies carrying on the back/shoulder, but it adds emphasis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumulong siyang **magpasan** ng isang sakong bigas.","translation":"He helped **carry** a sack of rice **on his shoulder**."},{"sentence":"Bilang panganay, siya ang **nagpasan sa likod** ng responsibilidad para sa kanyang mga kapatid.","translation":"As the eldest, he **shouldered the burden** of responsibility for his siblings."}]

translation: to put a veil on someone/something
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagpapatong ng belo sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: Same as 'belohan'. It's the action of putting a veil on something. This is a less common variant, kind of like saying 'tomayto' vs 'tomahto'. You're still putting that dramatic piece of cloth on someone.
usage_notes: A variant of 'belohan'. 'Belohan' is generally considered more standard.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sila ang naatasang **beluhan** ang lahat ng santo para sa prusisyon.","translation":"They were assigned to **put veils on** all the saints for the procession."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **beluhan** ang nobya.","translation":"Don't forget to **put the veil on** the bride."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang anyo ng pandiwa na nagsasaad ng kilos na pagtulak sa isang tiyak na bagay o tao.
original_explanation: “Bes, **itulak** mo nga ako sa swing!” vs. “Bes, ‘wag mo akong **itulak** sa maling tao.” This is the command form. It's what you tell someone to do. It's about applying force to a specific object or, you know, a friend towards their crush.
usage_notes: The general word for 'push'. Its antonym is 'hilahin' (to pull). It can also mean to push or peddle illegal drugs, a slang usage that is very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **itulak** ang iyong kapatid.","translation":"Do not **push** your sibling."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **itulak** nang malakas ang kariton para umandar.","translation":"You need **to push** the cart hard to make it move."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkulay sa tela o sinulid gamit ang katas mula sa halamang tayom (Indigofera tinctoria) upang magkaroon ito ng bughaw na kulay.
etymology: From 'tayom', the Tagalog name for the indigo plant.
original_explanation: Before there was "tina" from the department store, there was this. This is the OG, all-natural way to get that perfect blue for your pre-colonial OOTD. It's the process of using the 'tayom' or indigo plant to dye fabrics. Very artisanal, very traditional, and probably smells better than chemical dyes.
usage_notes: This is a very specific, traditional term related to weaving and fabric dyeing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga manghahabi sa Ilocos ay bihasa sa **pagtayom** ng kanilang mga tela.","translation":"The weavers in Ilocos are skilled in **dyeing** their fabrics **with indigo**."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan nila ngayon kung paano muling buhayin ang sining ng **pagtayom**.","translation":"They are now studying how to revive the art of **dyeing with indigo**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang inuming kape na inihahain nang malamig, karaniwan ay may kasamang yelo.
original_explanation: The fuel of the BPO industry, students pulling all-nighters, and basically every millennial and Gen Z in the Philippines. It's not just a drink; it's a personality trait. "Anong aayusin mo sa buhay mo?" "Yung pagiging dependent ko sa iced coffee."
usage_notes: Almost always used in its English form. "Kapeng may yelo" is a literal but less common translation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi kumpleto ang araw ko kapag walang **iced coffee**.","translation":"My day isn't complete without **iced coffee**."},{"sentence":"Magkano ang isang malaking baso ng **iced coffee** sa inyo?","translation":"How much is a large glass of **iced coffee** at your place?"}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi tama o wasto; isang pagkakamali o kamalian.
original_explanation: That feeling when you send a risky text and see "seen" but no reply. Or when you confidently answer the prof's question, only to be met with deafening silence. It's the universe's way of saying, "Try again, bes." Minsan, mali ang magmahal ng taong di ka naman mahal. Hugot!
usage_notes: Can be used as an adjective (mali ang sagot mo) or a noun (isang malaking mali).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Mali** ang ibinigay mong direksyon kaya kami naligaw.","translation":"The direction you gave was **wrong**, that's why we got lost."},{"sentence":"Inamin niya ang kanyang **mali** at humingi ng tawad.","translation":"He admitted his **mistake** and asked for forgiveness."}]

translation: to have someone represent; to embody
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-atas sa isang tao na maging kinatawan para sa isang grupo o indibidwal; ang pagsasakatawan sa isang ideya o konsepto.
etymology: `pa-` (causative prefix) + `katawan` (body) + `-in` (object-focus suffix). Literally, 'to make someone be the body (of something).'
original_explanation: When you're chosen for the group report because you're the only one who can speak straight English. You are being asked to 'pakatawanin' the group. It's being the designated champion, the tribute, the face of the brand (or the barkada). It's a lot of pressure, like being the only one who knows how to order for everyone at a restaurant.
usage_notes: This is the verb form related to 'kinatawan' (representative).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **ipapakatawan** natin sa darating na pagpupulong?","translation":"Who will we **have represent** us in the upcoming meeting?"},{"sentence":"Si Dr. Jose Rizal ay sinasabing **pinakatawan** ang diwa ng pagka-Pilipino.","translation":"Dr. Jose Rizal is said to have **embodied** the spirit of being Filipino."}]

translation: will crush; will flatten; will squeeze
meaning_filipino: Ang gagawing kilos ng pagdiin o pagpisat sa isang bagay upang ito ay mayupi, madurog, o mawalan ng orihinal na anyo.
etymology: Future tense of 'pisain', from the root 'pisa'. The first syllable of the root is reduplicated.
original_explanation: Future tense of 'pisain.' It's what you will do to a can before throwing it in the recycling bin. Or what you want to do to your alarm clock when it rings at 5 AM. 'Pag nahuli ko 'yang ipis, pipisilin ko talaga!'
usage_notes: Conveys a sense of crushing or flattening with pressure.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pipisilin** ko ang mga kamatis para gawing sarsa.","translation":"I **will crush** the tomatoes to make a sauce."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong upuan ang kahon, baka **pipisin** mo ang laman.","translation":"Don't sit on the box, you might **crush** the contents."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang anumang damit o saplot sa katawan; kita ang balat.
original_explanation: The state you're in before you panic-search for a towel after a shower. In a metaphorical sense, it's being emotionally vulnerable, 'yung tipong 'nag-open up ka na, sinaktan ka pa.' #HubadNaKatotohanan
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin sa literal na paraan (walang damit) o sa metaporikal na paraan (lantad, walang tinatago).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bawal pumasok nang **hubad** ang dibdib sa simbahan.","translation":"Entering the church **bare**-chested is not allowed."},{"sentence":"Inilahad niya ang **hubad** na katotohanan tungkol sa nangyari.","translation":"He revealed the **naked** truth about what happened."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hindi pagsunod sa utos, tuntunin, o batas.
original_explanation: When your parents say 'Matulog ka na,' and you whisper 'one more episode' to Netflix. It's logging into your personal social media at work despite the company policy. Basically, it's the 'Sorry, not sorry' of breaking the rules.
usage_notes: Often implies a conscious choice to go against authority or rules.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagsuway** sa batas trapiko ay may kaukulang parusa.","translation":"**Disobedience** of traffic laws has a corresponding penalty."},{"sentence":"Pinalo siya ng nanay niya dahil sa kanyang **pagsuway**.","translation":"His mother spanked him because of his **defiance**."}]

translation: to tell a story; to narrate (alternate spelling)
meaning_filipino: Isang alternatibong baybay para sa 'magkwento'. Ang pagsasalaysay ng isang kuwento o pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is the OG spelling before 'kw' became the cool kid on the block. It's like writing 'colour' instead of 'color'—a bit old-fashioned but gets the job done. You'll still see it, but 'magkwento' is what's hip now.
usage_notes: This is an alternative, older spelling of `magkwento`. The modern and preferred spelling follows the `kw` convention.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **magkuwento** sa iyo ng isang sikreto.","translation":"I want to **tell** you a story about a secret."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglutas ng isang sigalot o hindi pagkakasundo sa pamamagitan ng isang walang kinikilingang ikatlong partido (ang arbitro), na ang desisyon ay karaniwang may-bisa at legal na maipatutupad.
original_explanation: It's like court, but less formal and usually faster. Instead of a judge in a robe, you get an 'arbitro' to settle the score. Common in business contracts to avoid messy lawsuits. Think of it as the legal version of 'mag-usap tayo nang maayos, pero may magde-decide sa huli'.
usage_notes: A legal and business term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumaan sa **arbitrasyon** ang kaso upang mas mabilis itong malutas.","translation":"The case went through **arbitration** to be resolved more quickly."},{"sentence":"Nakasaad sa kontrata na **arbitrasyon** ang paraan ng pag-aayos ng anumang di-pagkakaunawaan.","translation":"The contract states that **arbitration** is the method for settling any disputes."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa proseso ng pagpunta o pagtungo sa isang partikular na lugar o direksyon.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'punta' (go) at panlaping 'pa-'.
original_explanation: The classic Filipino response when someone asks "Nasaan ka na?" (Where are you?) even if you're still in the shower. "Papunta na!" means "I'm on my way," but the actual ETA could be anywhere from 5 minutes to 5 business days. It's the verbal equivalent of a progress bar that's stuck at 99%.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin kasama ang 'na' ('papunta na'). Maaari ring ituring na anyong walang banghay ng pandiwa (non-finite verb form).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tawagan mo ako kapag **papunta** ka na sa opisina.","translation":"Call me when you're **on your way** to the office."},{"sentence":"Lagi siyang late, pero ang palusot niya palagi ay '**papunta** na raw siya.'","translation":"He's always late, but his excuse is always that 'he's **on his way**.'"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na nangangahulugang gutom.
etymology: Isang rhyming slang na hango sa pangalan ng mang-aawit na si Tom Jones, na ipinantutugma sa salitang "gutom".
original_explanation: When you're so hungry, you feel like singing "It's Not Unusual." This is classic Pinoy pun-based slang. Tom Jones (the singer) -> "Tom-guts" -> "Gutom". When someone says "Tomjones na ako," they're not asking you to play a record; they're telling you to feed them. ASAP.
usage_notes: Isang mapaglaro at medyo luma nang salitang balbal, ngunit malawak pa ring naiintindihan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tara, kain na tayo, **tomjones** na ako!","translation":"Let's go eat, I'm already **hungry**!"},{"sentence":"Narinig ko kumakalam sikmura mo, **tomjones** ka na 'no?","translation":"I heard your stomach rumbling, you're **hungry**, right?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbuga ng hangin mula sa ilong nang may puwersa at tunog, karaniwang dahil sa galit o pagkayamot. Maaari ring tumukoy sa tunog na nililikha ng ilang hayop o makina.
original_explanation: 'Yung tunog na ginagawa ng tita mong high-blood kapag narinig na naman niyang wala ka pa ring jowa. Pwede ring sound effect ng ahas sa teleserye, o 'yung lumang bus na paakyat ng Baguio.
usage_notes: Often associated with anger, annoyance, or the sound made by animals like bulls or snakes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumingasing** ang toro nang makita nito ang pulang kapa.","translation":"The bull **snorted** when it saw the red cape."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na bahagi ng isang pangkat o populasyon na naiiba sa karamihan dahil sa etnisidad, relihiyon, opinyon, o iba pang katangian.
original_explanation: The smaller group in any situation. In politics, they're the opposition. In a barkada, they're the only one who doesn't like milk tea. It's the feeling of being the only one raising your hand for a different movie choice.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa kontekstong politikal, sosyal, at kultural. Ang kasalungat nito ay 'mayorya' o karamihan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalagang pakinggan ang boses ng **minoria** sa senado.","translation":"It is important to listen to the voice of the **minority** in the senate."},{"sentence":"Kabilang sila sa isang **minoria** na etnikong pangkat sa rehiyon.","translation":"They belong to an ethnic **minority** group in the region."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkakaroon ng isang matigas na bagay, karaniwan ay pagkain, na nakabara sa lalamunan.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you're too 'sabik' eating that Jollibee chicken and a piece of bone gets stuck in your throat. It's not just any choking (like from water, which is 'nasamid'). This is specifically for solid objects, like a fishbone ('tinik'). It's the 'oh no, I need a piece of banana or a hard pat on the back, stat!' moment.
usage_notes: Differentiated from 'nasamid' (choked on liquid) and 'nabulunan' (a more general term for choking on food). 'Nakabikil' often implies a hard, solid object.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uminom siya agad ng tubig dahil may **nakabikil** na buto ng manok sa kanyang lalamunan.","translation":"He immediately drank water because a chicken bone was **choked** in his throat."},{"sentence":"Ingat sa pagkain ng isda, baka ka pa **makabikil** ng tinik.","translation":"Be careful when eating fish, you might get **choked** by a fishbone."}]

meaning_filipino: Nawalan ng malay-tao; hindi namamalayan ang nangyayari sa paligid.
original_explanation: The state you're in after a Tanduay-fueled karaoke night until 5 AM. You're physically there, but your consciousness has logged off. It's when someone is so out of it, they wouldn't notice if an elephant walked into the room.
usage_notes: Often used in medical emergencies, accidents, or describing someone who is extremely intoxicated or has fainted.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nadatnan siyang **walang-ulirat** sa sahig matapos madulas.","translation":"He was found **unconscious** on the floor after slipping."},{"sentence":"Dinala agad sa ospital ang biktima dahil **walang-ulirat** ito.","translation":"The victim was immediately brought to the hospital because they were **unconscious**."}]

translation: to get hit or bumped hard (usually on the head)
meaning_filipino: Matamaan o maumpog nang malakas, karaniwan sa ulo, na nagdudulot ng pagkayanig.
etymology: From `mag-` + `paka-` + `lantog`. `Lantog` refers to a hard bump or knock.
original_explanation: The sound effect-turned-verb for when your head meets a low-hanging cabinet door, a jeepney ceiling, or the floor. It’s that painful, jarring impact that makes you see stars. "Aray! Ingat sa pagtayo, baka ka magpakalantog sa pinto."
usage_notes: An informal and onomatopoeic-feeling word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigla siyang tumayo kaya **nagpakalantog** ang ulo niya sa ilalim ng mesa.","translation":"He suddenly stood up so his head **got bumped hard** under the table."},{"sentence":"Laging may pasa ang kapatid ko dahil palagi siyang **nagpapakalantog** kung saan-saan.","translation":"My sibling always has bruises because they're always **getting bumped** everywhere."}]

translation: to hold onto tightly; to harbor (feelings)
meaning_filipino: Ang paghawak nang mahigpit sa isang bagay; ang pag-iingat o pagtatago ng isang damdamin o lihim at hindi ito ipinapaalam.
original_explanation: The act of not letting go. It's when you refuse to share your last piece of chicharon, or more seriously, when you refuse to talk about what's bothering you. This is the official verb of the "strong, silent type" who's secretly full of hugot. "Huwag mo nang kimkimin ang galit mo, hindi 'yan healthy."
usage_notes: Can be used for both physical objects and abstract emotions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **kimkimin** ang iyong mga problema; mas mabuting ibahagi mo ito sa isang kaibigan.","translation":"Don't **harbor** your problems; it's better to share them with a friend."},{"sentence":"Nais niyang **kimkimin** ang liham upang walang ibang makabasa nito.","translation":"He wanted to **hold the letter tightly** so no one else could read it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, karaniwang lalaki, na may kumpirmadong pagkakakilanlan bilang bading o homoseksuwal, madalas batay sa kilos, pananalita, at itsura na hayagang nagpapakita nito.
original_explanation: This is when someone's gayness is so obvious, it's like they have a notarized document and a PRC license for it. They're not just 'suspected' or 'maybe,' they are 100%, no-doubt-about-it, Grade A bading. It's often said with a mix of admiration for their confidence and a touch of playful teasing.
usage_notes: Often used humorously or as a term of endearment within the LGBTQ+ community and its allies. It implies an open and unapologetic expression of one's gay identity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tingnan mo ang porma niya, mula ulo hanggang paa, **certified bading** talaga!","translation":"Look at his style, from head to toe, he's truly a **certified gay**!"},{"sentence":"Hindi na kailangang itanong, **certified bading** 'yan si accla.","translation":"No need to ask, that friend is **certified gay**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng lamat o siwang dahil sa puwersa, presyon, o pagkatuyo.
original_explanation: 'Yung nangyayari sa lupa 'pag tag-init, or sa semento 'pag may lindol. It's when a solid surface breaks and forms a line or gap. Pwede ring 'yung boses mo, 'yung biglang **bumitak** nung kumakanta ka ng high notes sa karaoke. Awkward.
usage_notes: Stative verb indicating a change of state. It means 'to crack' or 'to have cracked'. Present: bumibitak. Future: bibitak. Used for surfaces like land, walls, concrete, or even the voice.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumitak** ang lupa dahil sa matinding tagtuyot.","translation":"The land **cracked** due to the severe drought."},{"sentence":"**Bumitak** ang boses niya habang kumakanta.","translation":"His voice **cracked** while singing."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga bagay na may kaugnayan sa isang munisipalidad o bayan.
original_explanation: The official-sounding adjective for anything related to your town or "bayan." You'll see this on government buildings and documents: "Munisipal Hall," "Munisipal Ordinance," "Munisipal Health Officer." It's the bureaucratic way of saying "pang-bayan."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinatutupad ngayon ang bagong ordinansang **munisipal**.","translation":"The new **municipal** ordinance is now being implemented."},{"sentence":"Ang eleksyong **munisipal** ay gaganapin sa susunod na taon.","translation":"The **municipal** election will be held next year."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang estado ng pagiging panatag, walang alalahanin, at payapa ang isip at damdamin.
original_explanation: This is that feeling when your toxic boss finally resigns. 'Yung feeling after mo mag-submit ng thesis. 'Yung moment na nalaman mong negative ang result ng test na kinakatakutan mo. It's not just happiness, it's a deep exhale of relief. The weight is lifted. Your inner self can finally breathe. That's 'kaluwagan ng loob'.
usage_notes: An idiomatic expression. The literal translation "spaciousness of the inside" does not capture the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagdulot sa kanya ng **kaluwagan ng loob** ang paghingi ng tawad.","translation":"Asking for forgiveness gave him **peace of mind**."},{"sentence":"Nadama ko ang **kaluwagan ng loob** nang malaman kong ligtas sila.","translation":"I felt a sense of **relief** when I found out they were safe."}]

translation: to go back for; to return to
meaning_filipino: Puntahan muli ang isang lugar o isang tao; kunin muli ang isang bagay na naiwan o nakalimutan.
original_explanation: This is the official verb for when you leave your phone at the restaurant and have to do a walk of shame back to get it. It's also the verb your friends use when they warn you not to get back with your ex: "Huwag mo nang **balikin** 'yan, bes, move on na!" Two very different kinds of forgotten items, same verb.
usage_notes: Often used to mean returning to a place ('balikan ang probinsya'), retrieving a forgotten item ('balikan ang payong'), or revisiting a past relationship or memory ('balikan ang nakaraan').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **balikin** ang naiwan kong wallet sa opisina.","translation":"I need to **go back for** my wallet that I left at the office."},{"sentence":"Mahirap nang **balikin** ang tiwalang nasira.","translation":"It's hard to **get back** the trust that has been broken."}]
