translation: on the off chance, just in case
meaning_filipino: Ginagamit upang ipahayag ang paggawa ng isang bagay sa kabila ng maliit na posibilidad na magtagumpay, sa pag-asang maaaring mangyari ito.
original_explanation: This is the phrase of the hopeful romantic or the desperate job applicant. It's the 'what if' that fuels you to try something even when the odds are against you. You submit your resume to that dream company, 'baka sakali.' You text your crush, 'baka sakali.' It's the anthem of taking a long shot, because hey, you never know!
usage_notes: Expresses a more hopeful or wishful kind of 'maybe' than just 'baka'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumali ako sa raffle, **baka sakali** manalo ako ng kotse.","translation":"I joined the raffle, **on the off chance** I might win a car."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan ko siyang tawagan ulit, **baka sakali** sumagot na siya.","translation":"I tried calling her again, **just in case** she would finally answer."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng panunuyo o pagpapahayag ng pag-ibig ng isang tao sa kanyang nililiyag, karaniwan bago maging magkasintahan.
original_explanation: The OG 'getting to know you' stage. Dati, harana at pag-iigib ng tubig. Ngayon, G? (Game?) sa Messenger, 'hatid-sundo' sa office, at pag-send ng GrabFood. The goal is to get that sweet, sweet 'oo'.
usage_notes: Ang anyong pandiwa nito ay "manligaw".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tradisyonal na bahagi ng kulturang Pilipino ang **ligaw**.","translation":"**Courtship** is a traditional part of Filipino culture."},{"sentence":"Mahigit isang taon ang itinagal ng kanyang panunuyo at **ligaw**.","translation":"His wooing and **courtship** lasted for more than a year."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkulong o pagpaligid sa isang tao o hayop upang hindi na ito makatakas.
original_explanation: When you're playing an online game and the enemy team traps you with no escape route. That's it. You've been 'sinukol'. Also applies to when your boss and your HR manager are waiting for you in the conference room. You're cornered.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinikap ng mga pulis na **sumukol** sa magnanakaw sa isang eskinita.","translation":"The police tried **to corner** the thief in an alley."},{"sentence":"Nang **sumukol** na ang mga kalaban, wala na siyang nagawa kundi sumuko.","translation":"When the enemies **had cornered** him, he had no choice but to surrender."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay na ginagamit sa pagdundot o pagtusok. Sa modernong gamit, ito ay tumutukoy sa panghimagas o pagkaing kinakain pagkatapos ng pangunahing pagkain.
etymology: From `pan-` + `dundot` (to poke lightly). The 'dessert' meaning is a more modern, colloquial evolution.
original_explanation: Two meanings here! First, it's the stick you use to get the last piece of chicharon from the bottom of the bag. Second, and more common now, it's another word for dessert. After a heavy meal, you need something sweet "pang-panundot" to complete the experience, parang chaser.
usage_notes: The meaning "dessert" is more colloquial but very common. The original meaning is "something used for poking."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng patpat bilang **panundot** sa butas.","translation":"He used a stick as a **poker** for the hole."},{"sentence":"Ano ang **panundot** natin mamaya? Leche flan ba?","translation":"What's our **dessert** for later? Is it leche flan?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang parusa o hatol na ipinapataw sa isang tao dahil sa nagawang pagkakamali, paglabag sa batas, o kasalanan.
original_explanation: The 'lagot ka!' moment materialized. It's what your mom threatened you with when you didn't wash the dishes ('Walang internet!'). It's the consequence of 'seen-zoning' your boss's message. From getting grounded to facing legal charges, it's the universe's (or society's) way of saying 'you messed up.'
usage_notes: A formal and general term for any form of punishment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matinding **kaparusahan** ang naghihintay sa mga lumalabag sa batas.","translation":"A severe **punishment** awaits those who break the law."},{"sentence":"Ang paglilinis ng buong bahay ang naging **kaparusahan** ko sa pag-uwi nang gabi.","translation":"Cleaning the whole house became my **punishment** for coming home late."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paraang nakatiklop o tiniklop.
original_explanation: The state of your clothes before they go into the closet (if you're organized) or the state of your 100-peso bill that you've hidden in your phone case. It's doing origami, but with your laundry or your pamasahe. 'Ayusin mo 'yang damit, dapat **patupi**.'
usage_notes: Describes the manner of folding. The adjective form is 'nakatupi' (folded).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inilagay niya ang sulat sa sobre nang **patupi**.","translation":"He placed the letter in the envelope in a **folded** manner."},{"sentence":"Itinago niya ang pera nang **patupi** sa kanyang bulsa.","translation":"He hid the money, **folded**, in his pocket."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paunang bayad na ibinibigay bago pa man makumpleto ang isang serbisyo o matanggap ang isang produkto; paunang sahod.
original_explanation: 'Yung "vale" mo sa office 'pag petsa de peligro na. Basically, kinukuha mo na 'yung pera na 'di mo pa naman talaga pinagtrabahuhan. It's borrowing from your future self, who will probably hate you for it come actual payday. A necessary evil for survival.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng sahod o bayaran. Katumbas ng 'vale' sa kolokyal na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Humiram siya ng **antisipo** sa kanyang amo dahil may biglaang gastusin.","translation":"He asked for a **cash advance** from his boss because of a sudden expense."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong kumuha ng **antisipo** para sa matrikula ng anak ko.","translation":"I need to get a **cash advance** for my child's tuition fee."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging maputla o kawalan ng kulay sa mukha, karaniwang sanhi ng takot, sakit, o pagkabigla.
original_explanation: The look on your face when you check your bank account after a 12.12 sale. Or when your boss says 'we need to talk.' It's that sudden loss of color that screams 'Oh no!'
usage_notes: Ito ang anyong pangngalan. Ang anyong pang-uri ay 'maputla'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kitang-kita ang **putla** sa kanyang mukha nang malaman niya ang masamang balita.","translation":"The **paleness** on her face was very visible when she learned of the bad news."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang nilalaman; hungkag; mababaw at walang gaanong saysay (kung tumutukoy sa ideya o pahayag).
original_explanation: This describes that bag of chips that's 90% air. Or an essay that meets the word count but says absolutely nothing. It's the small talk you make with a distant tita at a family reunion. "Ang laki mo na, iho!" followed by... nothing. Purely walang-kalaman-laman. It’s all form, no substance.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin nang literal para sa mga lalagyan na walang laman o patalinghaga para sa mga ideya, talumpati, o usapan na mababaw.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kahon na ipinadala niya ay **walang-kalaman-laman**.","translation":"The box he sent was **empty**."},{"sentence":"Ayaw kong makinig sa mga talumpating **walang-kalaman-laman**.","translation":"I don't want to listen to speeches that are **without substance**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang masalimuot na istrukturang sapot na hinabi ng gagamba upang makahuli ng biktima o magsilbing tirahan.
original_explanation: The original dreamcatcher, but for flies. It's that sticky, intricate thing in the corner of your ceiling that you only notice when you have visitors. Also a great, free Halloween decoration, courtesy of your friendly neighborhood spider.
usage_notes: "Bahay-gagamba" often refers to an active web, while "agay-ay" can refer to old, dusty cobwebs.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **bahay-gagamba** ang lumang bodega.","translation":"The old warehouse is full of **cobwebs**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat o kalipunan ng mga bagay na magkakasama, magkakatugma, o magkapares.
original_explanation: Think of it as "terno." That huwego of earrings and a necklace your tita wears to every party. Or the huwego of plates and bowls you only use for Noche Buena. It's all about a matching set. It can also mean "game" (like from Spanish 'juego'), but 'laro' is more common for that.
usage_notes: Commonly used for sets of jewelry, furniture, or dinnerware.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binili niya ako ng isang **huwego** ng perlas na alahas.","translation":"She bought me a **set** of pearl jewelry."},{"sentence":"Maganda ang pagkakaterno ng **huwego** ng mga upuan at mesa sa sala.","translation":"The **set** of chairs and table in the living room matches beautifully."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking kutsara na may mahabang hawakan at malalim na mangkok, ginagamit sa pagsasalin o paghahain ng mga likido tulad ng sabaw, sarsa, o sinigang.
original_explanation: The Big Brother of the kutsara family. Siya ang bida tuwing may handaan at kailangang mag-serve ng sopas, sinigang, o punch. Kung ang kutsara ay for personal consumption, ang kutsaron ay for sharing. The designated server sa lahat ng sabaw ng buhay mo.
usage_notes: Also known as 'sandok' in many contexts, but 'kutsaron' specifically implies a ladle shape.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gamitin mo ang **kutsaron** para magsalin ng sabaw sa mangkok.","translation":"Use the **ladle** to transfer the soup into the bowl."},{"sentence":"Nawawala ang **kutsaron** para sa fruit punch.","translation":"The **ladle** for the fruit punch is missing."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tanyag na online marketplace at e-commerce platform sa Timog-silangang Asya.
etymology: A proper noun, the name of the e-commerce company.
original_explanation: Hindi lang isang app, kundi isang lifestyle. Ang black hole kung saan napupunta ang 13th month pay mo. Dito mo mahahanap ang lahat mula sa face mask hanggang sa washing machine, kadalasan may kasamang 'free shipping voucher' na may ₱500 minimum spend. Ang pambansang libangan tuwing sahod.
usage_notes: Often used as a verb with affixes, e.g., 'nag-Shopee', 'i-Shopee mo na'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tingnan ko muna sa **Shopee** kung may mas mura.","translation":"I'll check on **Shopee** first if there's a cheaper one."},{"sentence":"I-**Shopee** mo na lang 'yan para hindi ka na lumabas.","translation":"Just buy it on **Shopee** so you don't have to go out."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng kawalan ng ayos, kaayusan, o pagkakasundo. Maaaring tumukoy sa pisikal na gulo o sa hidwaan sa pagitan ng mga tao.
etymology: From 'di-' (not) + 'pagkaka-' (state of mutual action/relation) + 'ayos' (order, arrangement, settlement).
original_explanation: This is your room after a week of choosing outfits, and also your barkada's group chat when two people aren't speaking to each other. It's chaos, mess, and unresolved issues all rolled into one. The opposite of 'maayos'.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical mess ('gulo', 'kalat') or interpersonal conflict ('alitan', 'hindi pagkakasundo').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **di-pagkakaayos** ng mga aklat sa estante ay nakakairita.","translation":"The **disarrangement** of the books on the shelf is irritating."},{"sentence":"Naging sanhi ng kanilang **di-pagkakaayos** ang isang maliit na hindi pagkakaunawaan.","translation":"A small misunderstanding caused their **disagreement**."}]

meaning_filipino: Gagawin ang kilos ng pagtindig o pagbangon mula sa pagkakaupo o pagkakahiga. Ito ay nasa aspetong kontemplatibo o panghinaharap.
original_explanation: The future tense of 'tayo' (stand). It's what your mom tells you to do when a visitor arrives, or what you tell yourself you'll do to start working out... tomorrow. 'Sino ang **tatayo** para mag-present?' is the question that gives every student in the group project a mini heart attack.
usage_notes: This is the future tense of the verb 'tayo' (to stand). It should not be confused with the pronoun 'tayo' (we/us).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tatayo** ako para ibigay ang aking upuan sa matanda.","translation":"I **will stand** to give my seat to the elderly person."},{"sentence":"Saan ka **tatayo** mamaya sa concert para makita mo ang stage?","translation":"Where **will you stand** later at the concert so you can see the stage?"}]

meaning_filipino: May umbok o nakaalsang hugis; bilugan at malaman.
original_explanation: Describes anything that curves outwards. Think of a pregnant belly, a well-fed tummy after a fiesta, or those perfectly round pandesal. It's the opposite of flat-chested hopes and dreams. It's the 'plus' in plus-size, the 'extra' in extra rice.
usage_notes: Can be used for objects, body parts, or surfaces.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **matambok** na pisngi ng sanggol ay ang sarap kurutin.","translation":"The baby's **plump** cheeks are so cute to pinch."},{"sentence":"Pinalitan nila ang lumang TV ng may **matambok** na likod.","translation":"They replaced the old TV with a **bulging** back."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit sa isang tao, bagay, o sitwasyon para sa sariling kapakinabangan; ang pagsasagawa ng pananamantala.
original_explanation: The verb form. Ito yung ginagawa ng mga buwaya sa gobyerno. O yung ginagawa mo sa free wi-fi sa coffee shop—downloading a whole season of a series. 'Huwag mong pagsamantalahan ang kabaitan niya.' It's the command form of 'Don't be a user!'
usage_notes: The verb form of 'pagsamantala'. The object of the verb is the one being taken advantage of.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pagsamantalahan** ang kanyang tiwala.","translation":"Do not **take advantage of** his trust."},{"sentence":"Madaling **pagsamantalahan** ang mga taong desperado.","translation":"It is easy **to take advantage of** people who are desperate."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagtusok ng isang bagay sa isang panuhog o patpat.
original_explanation: This is the action verb for your barbecue prep. You `tuhugan` the stick with meat. It’s the act of impaling food with a stick for the greater good (of being delicious). For example, 'Bes, tuhugan mo na 'yang mga hotdog para maihaw na natin.'
usage_notes: Verb, locative/object focus. The focus is on the stick/skewer being filled. Contrast with `tuhugin`, where the focus is on the item being pierced.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tuhugan** mo ng maraming baboy ang bawat patpat.","translation":"**Skewer** a lot of pork onto each stick."},{"sentence":"Mas madaling ihawin kapag **tinuhugan** muna ang mga gulay.","translation":"It's easier to grill when you **skewer** the vegetables first."}]

translation: to throw a stone at, to stone
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpukol o paghagis ng bato sa isang tao, hayop, o bagay.
original_explanation: Literally, what you do to get mangoes from a high branch. Figuratively, what your crush does to your feelings when they leave you on 'seen'. 'Seen-zoned na naman, parang binato lang ang puso ko.'
usage_notes: Can be used both literally for throwing physical stones and metaphorically for hurling insults or harsh judgments.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bawal **mambato** ng mga hayop sa zoo.","translation":"It is forbidden **to throw stones** at the animals in the zoo."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mambato** ng akusasyon kung wala kang ebidensya.","translation":"Don't **throw** accusations if you don't have evidence."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng tunog sa pamamagitan ng paulit-ulit na paghampas ng dalawang palad. Ginagawa bilang tanda ng paghanga, pagsang-ayon, o katuwaan.
original_explanation: The OG 'like' button. Before hearts and thumbs-ups, this is how you showed appreciation. You do it when your friend finally sings on key, when the movie has a great ending, or sarcastically when your internet connection finally works after 3 hours.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for applause or figuratively for showing approval.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sabay-sabay na **pumalakpak** ang mga manonood pagkatapos ng palabas.","translation":"The audience **clapped** in unison after the show."},{"sentence":"Halos gusto kong **pumalakpak** nang ma-approve ang vacation leave ko.","translation":"I almost wanted to **applaud** when my vacation leave was approved."}]

translation: to be able to bite; to be bitten
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang kumagat; o maranasan ang makagat ng isang bagay o hayop.
original_explanation: Two scenarios: 1) You finally get to bite into that juicy Jollibee Chickenjoy you've been craving. "Gutom na 'ko, sana makagat ko na 'yung burger." 2) The more common use: getting bitten, usually by surprise. "Aray, may langgam! Baka makagat ako!"
usage_notes: Can be used in both active (to be able to bite) and passive (to be bitten) contexts, though the passive sense is more frequent in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa aso ng kapitbahay, baka ka **makagat**.","translation":"Be careful of the neighbor's dog, you might **be bitten**."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa pananakit ng ngipin, hindi siya **makagat** nang maayos.","translation":"Because of the toothache, he is not **able to bite** properly."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o antas ng pagiging marumi, madungis, o puno ng dumi at libag.
original_explanation: That feeling after a 3-day music festival with no showers. Yung itsura mo after mag-commute sa EDSA na open-window, tapos umulan, tapos umaraw. You're not just dirty, you're **panlilimahid**. It's a whole new level of 'lagkit' that requires industrial-grade soap to remove.
usage_notes: Describes an extreme or accumulated state of being dirty or grimy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halata ang **panlilimahid** sa kanyang damit matapos maglaro sa putikan.","translation":"The **griminess** on his clothes was obvious after playing in the mud."},{"sentence":"Hindi na makilala ang kulay ng sasakyan dahil sa **panlilimahid** nito.","translation":"The car's color was unrecognizable because of its **filthiness**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang pambutas na ginagamit upang pagdikitin ang mga papel sa pamamagitan ng isang maliit na piraso ng alambre (staple).
original_explanation: 'Yung bagay sa office na laging nawawala kapag kailangan mo. Tapos kapag nahanap mo, wala namang bala. The cause of trust issues among officemates. 'Sino kumuha ng stapler ko?!'
usage_notes: The default term used in offices and schools. The Tagalog 'pambutas' is less common for this specific item.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pahiram ng **stapler**, kailangan kong pagsamahin itong mga dokumento.","translation":"Can I borrow the **stapler**, I need to put these documents together."},{"sentence":"Laging walang laman ang **stapler** sa lamesa niya.","translation":"The **stapler** on his desk is always empty."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalipunan ng mga salita at ang kanilang mga kahulugan na alam at ginagamit ng isang tao, o matatagpuan sa isang wika.
etymology: From *tala-* (list, record) + *salita* (word) + *-an* (locus). Literally 'a list of words'.
original_explanation: Your personal database of words. The more you have, the better you are at expressing your hugot or winning arguments online. It's your ammo for Scrabble, or for sounding smart during a presentation. Expanding your **talasalitaan** is like upgrading your brain's software.
usage_notes: A formal term. In everyday conversation, people might just say 'mga salita' (words) or use the English word 'vocabulary'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Upang mapabuti ang pagsusulat, mahalagang palawakin ang iyong **talasalitaan**.","translation":"To improve your writing, it's important to expand your **vocabulary**."},{"sentence":"Mayaman ang **talasalitaan** ng mga akda ni Jose Rizal.","translation":"The **vocabulary** in Jose Rizal's works is rich."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang negosyo, puhunan, o transaksyon na nagbibigay ng malaking kita o tubo.
original_explanation: This is the goal of every 'raket' or side hustle. You want your investment to be 'matubo.' It's when you buy something for ₱100 and sell it for ₱500. It's the opposite of 'lugi' (loss). The dream of every online seller and stock market tita.
usage_notes: Used in business, finance, and informal discussions about making money.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Matubo** ang negosyong pagkain lalo na kung nasa magandang lokasyon.","translation":"A food business is **profitable** especially if it's in a good location."},{"sentence":"Naghahanap siya ng investment na **matubo** at maliit lang ang panganib.","translation":"He is looking for an investment that is **profitable** and has low risk."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang akto ng pagpapakita sa publiko ng isang dula, sayaw, awit, o anumang uri ng sining.
original_explanation: This is your moment to shine! 'Yung recital mo sa piano, 'yung presentation niyo sa office na pinagpuyatan, or even the grand production number sa ASAP. It's the act of showing something off to an audience. Think of it as the 'reveal' moment after all the 'sana all' practice.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of arts, theater, and formal presentations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakagaling ng **pagtatanghal** ng mga artista sa entablado.","translation":"The **performance** of the actors on stage was excellent."},{"sentence":"Pinaghahandaan namin ang aming **pagtatanghal** para sa Araw ng Wika.","translation":"We are preparing our **presentation** for Language Day."}]

meaning_filipino: Ngumuya o kumagat sa isang matigas na bagay na lumilikha ng maririnig na tunog ng pagkadurog.
original_explanation: This is the sound you make when you're attacking a bag of chicharon, crispy pata, or your favorite cornick. It's a very satisfying, ASMR-worthy crunch. It can also be the sound your dog makes with his bone, or the sound of your patience slowly being gnawed away during a long meeting.
usage_notes: Onomatopoeic. Describes the sound of chewing something hard and crispy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang aso na **lumangutngot** ng buto sa ilalim ng mesa.","translation":"I heard the dog **gnawing** on a bone under the table."},{"sentence":"Masarap pakinggan ang balat ng lechon kapag ito ay **lumangutngot** sa iyong bibig.","translation":"It's satisfying to hear the lechon skin when it **crunches** in your mouth."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang set ng mga kagamitan sa pagkain tulad ng mga pinggan, tasa, platito, at mangkok, karaniwang gawa sa porselana o seramika.
original_explanation: The fancy plates, bowls, and saucers your mom only brings out for Christmas, Noche Buena, or when very important visitors are coming over. The rest of the year, they're kept safe in the 'aparador.' You use the plastic or Corelle ones for everyday use, but the 'bahilya' is for flexing.
usage_notes: Itinuturing na isang mas pormal o klasikong termino. Ang 'pinggan' (plates) o 'kubyertos' (cutlery) ay mas karaniwan sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inilabas ni Lola ang mamahaling **bahilya** para sa pista.","translation":"Grandma took out the expensive **dinnerware** for the fiesta."},{"sentence":"Kasama sa regalo sa kasal ang isang kumpletong set ng **bahilya**.","translation":"The wedding gift included a complete set of **tableware**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking estruktura o gusali na itinayo upang alalahanin ang isang mahalagang tao, kaganapan, o kasaysayan.
original_explanation: That big statue in the middle of a rotunda you use as a landmark when giving directions. "Saan? Diyan lang sa may monumento ni Rizal." It's the ultimate selfie spot for field trips.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **monumento** ni Rizal sa Luneta ay isang tanyag na pasyalan.","translation":"The Rizal **monument** in Luneta is a famous tourist spot."},{"sentence":"Nagpulong sila malapit sa **monumento** ng People Power.","translation":"They met near the People Power **monument**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang natatanging paraan ng pagbigkas na partikular sa isang indibidwal, lokasyon, o bansa. Maaari rin itong tumukoy sa diin o bigat na inilalagay sa isang pantig ng salita.
original_explanation: Yan yung dahilan kung bakit alam mong taga-probinsya, conyo, o foreigner ang kausap mo. Halimbawa, yung 'Bisaya accent' o yung 'American accent.' Pwede ring yung stress sa word, like yung pagkakaiba ng BA:sa (read) at ba:SA' (wet). Parang sa relasyon, a little asento (stress) is needed para malaman kung ano ang importante.
usage_notes: May dalawang pangunahing kahulugan: (1) paraan ng pagsasalita (e.g. "may asento siyang Bisaya") at (2) diin sa pantig (e.g. "nasa huling pantig ang asento").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahahalata sa kanyang **asento** na siya ay lumaki sa Amerika.","translation":"You can tell from his **accent** that he grew up in America."},{"sentence":"Ang salitang \"tubo\" ay may dalawang kahulugan depende sa **asento** ng pagbigkas.","translation":"The word \"tubo\" has two meanings depending on the **stress** of the pronunciation."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging sinasakal o ang pagpigil sa paghinga sa pamamagitan ng diin sa leeg. Maaari ring tumukoy sa metaporikal na pakiramdam ng pagiging gipit o pigil.
original_explanation: Literally, it's what happens in action movies. But metaphorically? It's your mountain of debt. It's your micromanaging boss. It's a toxic relationship. It's that feeling of being suffocated by expectations or problems. When you say, 'Sinasakal na ako,' you're not talking about your airway, you're talking about your life. Pagkasakal is that feeling of having no breathing room.
usage_notes: Has both a literal, physical meaning and a very common metaphorical one related to pressure, debt, or emotional distress.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sanhi ng kanyang pagkamatay ay **pagkasakal**.","translation":"The cause of his death was **strangulation**."},{"sentence":"Ramdam niya ang **pagkasakal** sa dami ng utang na kailangang bayaran.","translation":"He felt the **suffocation** from the amount of debt that needed to be paid."}]

translation: to carry on the shoulder or across the body (with a strap)
meaning_filipino: Dalhin o pasanin ang isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng paglalagay nito sa balikat o pahilis sa katawan gamit ang isang panali o sakbat.
original_explanation: It's how you carry your messenger bag, your guitar case, or your tote bag when it's too heavy for your hand. You sling it across your body. That action is sakbatin. "Huwag mong bitbitin 'yan, mabigat. Sakbatin mo na lang."
usage_notes: Implies carrying something with a strap over the shoulder or across the chest, as opposed to 'pasanin' (to carry on the back) or 'bitbitin' (to carry by hand).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Madaling **sakbatin** ang bag na ito dahil mahaba ang strap.","translation":"It's easy **to carry this bag across the body** because the strap is long."},{"sentence":"Nais kong **sakbatin** ang aking gitara habang naglalakad.","translation":"I want **to carry** my guitar **slung over my shoulder** while walking."}]

translation: skewered one after another; a series of connected things
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kalagayan ng pagiging magkakasunod na nakatusok sa isang patpat o panusok; serye ng magkakaugnay na bagay o pangyayari.
original_explanation: Think of your favorite street food: isaw, betamax, kwek-kwek, all lined up on a stick. That's `tuhog-tuhog`. It can also describe a series of unfortunate events, like, 'Na-late ako, tapos naiwan ko wallet ko, tapos umulan pa, tuhog-tuhog ang kamalasan!' It's the physical or metaphorical version of things being connected in a line.
usage_notes: Can be used as an adjective to describe something as being skewered, or as a noun to refer to the skewered items themselves. The hyphenated form is common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili kami ng **tuhog-tuhog** na baboy sa bangketa.","translation":"We bought **skewered** pork on the sidewalk."},{"sentence":"Ang mga pangyayari ay **tuhog-tuhog**, mula umaga hanggang gabi.","translation":"The events were a **series**, from morning until night."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taludtod o hanay ng mga salita sa isang tula. Maaari rin itong tumukoy sa isang mahabang hilera o pila ng mga tao o bagay.
original_explanation: This word has two vibes. The artsy one: it's a line in a poem, the kind you'd use for a dramatic spoken-word piece or a 'hugot' post. "Sa bawat balaybay ng tula, ikaw ang paksa." The practical one: it's a long, orderly line, like the queue for a new milk tea shop or the line of cars on EDSA during rush hour.
usage_notes: Often used in literary contexts for poetry, but can also mean a physical line or row.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bawat **balaybay** ng kanyang tula ay puno ng damdamin.","translation":"Every **verse** of his poem is full of emotion."},{"sentence":"Isang mahabang **balaybay** ng mga sasakyan ang bumungad sa amin sa NLEX.","translation":"A long **line** of cars greeted us on NLEX."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpunta muli sa isang lugar o pag-uwi mula sa pinanggalingan sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: The most famous line of every Filipino who leaves to buy something from the store: 'Babalik ako.' Also the national anthem of exes who can't seem to move on. It's a promise, a threat, or just a statement of fact, depending on who's saying it and why they left in the first place.
usage_notes: This is the actor-focused future tense form of 'bumalik'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sabi niya **babalik** siya, kaya maghihintay ako.","translation":"He said he **will return**, so I will wait."}]

translation: to ask someone to hang (e.g., clothes)
meaning_filipino: Isang pakiusap o utos na isabit o ilagay ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay damit, sa sampayan upang matuyo.
etymology: From `pa-` (request/causative prefix) + `sampay` (to hang on a line).
original_explanation: The battle cry of every Filipino household on laundry day. When your mom finishes washing the clothes, this is the command she gives you. "**Pasampay** mo na 'tong mga damit!" (Go hang these clothes now!). It's a simple request that carries the weight of a thousand wet jeans.
usage_notes: A very common household command. The full verb form is 'ipasampay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pasampay** naman nitong tuwalya ko, please.","translation":"**Please hang** this towel of mine, please."},{"sentence":"Inutusan niya ang kanyang kapatid, '**Pasampay** na ng mga nilabhan!'","translation":"She ordered her sibling, '**Hang** the laundry now!'"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang yugto ng panahon na binubuo ng pitong magkakasunod na araw.
original_explanation: A more formal and slightly old-fashioned way of saying 'linggo' (week). You'll hear this more from your lola or in provinces. 'Isang simana na akong naghihintay ng 13th month pay!'
usage_notes: 'Linggo' is the more common term for 'week' in modern, everyday conversation. 'Simana' is still widely understood and used, especially in certain regions and in formal writing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **simana** kaming magbabakasyon sa probinsya.","translation":"We will be on vacation in the province for one **week**."},{"sentence":"Tuwing katapusan ng **simana**, umuuwi siya sa kanilang bayan.","translation":"Every end of the **week**, he goes home to his town."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manipis at mahabang piraso na bumubuo sa mga materyales tulad ng tela, papel, o kalamnan.
original_explanation: The single strand of hair you find that isn't yours. The tiny thread that, when pulled, unravels the whole sweater (or a big lie). It's the 'fiber' in your diet that keeps things moving, and metaphorically, the last 'hibla ng pag-asa' (strand of hope) you cling to when waiting for your 13th-month pay.
usage_notes: Can refer to literal fibers (plant, muscle, textile) or be used metaphorically for concepts like hope or a storyline.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang abaka ay kilala sa matibay nitong **hibla**.","translation":"Abaca is known for its strong **fiber**."},{"sentence":"May natitira pa bang kahit isang **hibla** ng pag-asa?","translation":"Is there even a single **strand** of hope left?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na mabilis, direkta, o walang hinto. Tumutukoy sa serbisyong mas mabilis kaysa sa karaniwan.
original_explanation: Your Lalamove or Grab delivery when you're willing to pay extra kasi gutom ka na or kailangan na talaga. It's that bus sa NLEX/SLEX na hindi humihinto sa bawat kanto. Basically, the 'no time for chika, go go go!' option.
usage_notes: Often used to describe transport or delivery services. Can also function as an adverb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumakay ako sa **ekspres** na bus para mas mabilis makarating sa probinsya.","translation":"I took the **express** bus to get to the province faster."},{"sentence":"May **ekspres** lane ba para sa mga may dalang sampung item lang?","translation":"Is there an **express** lane for those with only ten items?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyon na nagsasaad na tapos na, talo na, o wala nang pag-asa sa isang sitwasyon.
etymology: From English 'good game', often abbreviated as 'GG' in online gaming culture. Its meaning has evolved from sportsmanship to signifying an end or defeat.
original_explanation: What you say when your boss catches you scrolling through memes instead of finishing that report. It's the Pinoy gamer's way of saying 'I'm screwed.' From the online gaming world to real-life 'patay na' situations. 'GG na, bes.'
usage_notes: Slang term derived from gaming culture. Used to signify that a situation is over, usually in a negative or hopeless sense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakalimutan kong i-save ang file, **goodgame** na ang lahat ng ginawa ko.","translation":"I forgot to save the file, everything I did is **done for**."},{"sentence":"Nahuli siyang nangongopya sa exam, **goodgame** na talaga.","translation":"He was caught cheating on the exam, it's really **game over** for him."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mababang lugar sa pagitan ng mga burol o bundok, karaniwang may ilog o sapa na dumadaloy dito.
original_explanation: Think of it as nature's 'dip' or 'low point' between two high points (mountains). It's where the views are often stunning from above, and where communities or farms thrive because of the fertile soil. In hugot terms, it's the 'down' phase between the 'highs' of your life. 'Nasa lambak ako ng kalungkutan ngayon.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mataba ang lupa sa **lambak** kaya magandang pagtaniman.","translation":"The soil in the **valley** is fertile, so it's good for planting."},{"sentence":"Tanaw mula sa tuktok ng bundok ang luntiang **lambak**.","translation":"The green **valley** can be seen from the top of the mountain."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bilang na kasunod ng animnapu't siyam at bago ang pitumpu't isa; katumbas ng 70.
original_explanation: From the Spanish 'setenta'. Usually used for age or money. When your lola asks for her "setenta pesos," you better give it. Also, the age when you've officially seen everything and can say whatever you want.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'pitumpu'. 'Setenta' is more common when stating age or in financial contexts, especially among older generations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lolo ko ay **setenta** anyos na sa susunod na taon.","translation":"My grandfather will be **seventy** years old next year."},{"sentence":"“Magkano po?” “**Setenta** pesos po lahat.”","translation":"“How much is it?” “**Seventy** pesos for everything.”"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang siyentipikong pag-aaral ng isip at pag-uugali ng tao at hayop.
original_explanation: The subject you take in college that makes you overthink everyone's actions, including your own. It's the 'science' behind why your ex left you on read, why your boss is a micromanager, and why you keep adding to cart at 3 AM.
usage_notes: Ang 'sikolohia' ay isang mas lumang baybay. Ang 'sikolohiya' ang ginagamit sa kasalukuyang ortograpiyang Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-aaral siya ng **sikolohiya** upang mas maunawaan ang pag-iisip ng mga bata.","translation":"She is studying **psychology** to better understand the minds of children."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang naitutulong ng **sikolohiya** sa larangan ng pagnenegosyo.","translation":"**Psychology** is a great help in the field of business."}]

translation: to make something shine or glitter
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o paggawa ng isang bagay upang ito ay magkaroon ng kislap o liwanag na parang kumikinang.
original_explanation: This is the verb for adding that extra ✨sparkle✨. Whether you're a makeup guru adding highlighter, a carwash attendant applying wax, or a designer adding sequins to a dress, you're doing the work of magpakinang. It's the act of making something go from 'meh' to 'wow, shiny!'
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of beauty, cleaning, or decoration.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang polisher para **magpakinang** ng sahig na kahoy.","translation":"She used the polisher to **make** the wooden floor **shine**."},{"sentence":"Marunong siyang **magpakinang** ng anumang alahas na luma.","translation":"He knows how to **make** any old jewelry **glitter**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa o pagbuo ng isang bagay na dati ay wala pa, karaniwan ay mula sa imahinasyon o sariling kakayahan.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'from scratch' energy. When you're not just reheating last night's adobo but actually inventing a new ulam, you 'lumikha'. It's what artists, writers, and your friend who somehow made a working lamp out of a plastic bottle do. The OG 'manifesting'.
usage_notes: Actor-focus verb, completed aspect (past tense). 'Pumunta ang manlilikha upang lumikha.' (The creator went to create.)
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lumikha** siya ng isang obra maestra mula sa mga patapong materyales.","translation":"He/She **created** a masterpiece from discarded materials."},{"sentence":"Ang Diyos ang sinasabing **lumikha** ng langit at lupa.","translation":"God is said to have **created** heaven and earth."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang espasyo sa itaas ng lupa; ang himpapawid o kalawakan.
original_explanation: This is a more poetic, high-falutin' word for "sky." You don't just say, "Ang ganda ng alangaang." It's the word you use when you're feeling philosophical, staring at the vast expanse above, and thinking about the universe, your dreams, or why your data plan runs out so fast. It's the sky, but with a dash of drama and wonder.
usage_notes: A literary or formal term for the sky or atmosphere. It is rarely used in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumingala siya sa malawak na **alangaang**, pinagmamasdan ang mga bituin.","translation":"He looked up at the vast **sky**, watching the stars."},{"sentence":"Ang mga eroplano ay lumilipad nang mataas sa **alangaang**.","translation":"The airplanes fly high in the **atmosphere**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangyayari ng pagtama o pagbangga ng dalawa o higit pang bagay, lalo na kung may kasamang puwersa.
original_explanation: The literal car crash. Or that awkward moment when you bump into your ex at the mall and you both pretend you didn't see each other. It's the physical impact, the sudden jolt of an unexpected encounter.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin para sa malalaking bagay (sasakyan) o maliliit na bagay (tao, siko).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nabasag ang salamin dahil sa lakas ng **pagkabunggo**.","translation":"The glass shattered because of the force of the **impact**."},{"sentence":"Iniimbestigahan pa ng pulisya ang sanhi ng **pagkabunggo** ng dalawang bus.","translation":"The police are still investigating the cause of the **collision** of the two buses."}]

meaning_filipino: Ililipat ang datos o isang digital na file mula sa isang lokal na sistema patungo sa isang sentral na sistema o server sa internet.
original_explanation: The promise you make to your friends after a group picture. 'Guys, `mag-a-upload` ako mamaya!' which can mean anything from 10 minutes to 10 business days. It's the digital equivalent of 'I'll text you.'
usage_notes: This is the future tense form of 'mag-upload'. It is a Tagalized verb from English and is extremely common in modern, informal conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Mag-a-upload** ako ng mga litrato mula sa ating bakasyon sa Facebook mamaya.","translation":"I **will upload** the photos from our vacation to Facebook later."},{"sentence":"Kailan ka **mag-a-upload** ng bagong video sa YouTube channel mo?","translation":"When **will** you **upload** a new video to your YouTube channel?"}]

translation: to oil; to lubricate; to bribe
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng langis sa isang bagay upang ito ay dumulas, kuminis, o hindi kalawangin. Sa matalinghagang kahulugan, ito ay ang pagbibigay ng suhol.
original_explanation: Literally, it's what you do to a squeaky door hinge or a rusty bike chain. Figuratively, it’s a much more… *Filipino* concept. Need a permit approved faster? *Kailangang **langisan**.* Got caught by a traffic enforcer? *Baka kailangan mong **langisan**.* It's the "greasing" of palms, the unofficial system that runs on *padulas*.
usage_notes: This word has a very common figurative meaning related to bribery, which is often used in conversations about bureaucracy and corruption.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakitingnan kung kailangan nang **langisan** ang kadena ng bisikleta.","translation":"Please check if the bicycle chain needs to be **oiled**."},{"sentence":"Sabi nila, kailangan mo raw **langisan** ang mga tao diyan para mapabilis ang papeles mo.","translation":"They say you need to **bribe** (grease the palms of) the people there to speed up your papers."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging buhol-buhol, salit-salit, o magkakabit-kabit ng mga bagay tulad ng sinulid, alambre, o kahit mga pangyayari.
etymology: From "salabid" (tangle, snarl). The "pag- -an" affix with reduplication of the first syllable of the root ("sa") indicates the act or process of something becoming tangled.
original_explanation: That moment you pull your earphones out of your pocket and they're a chaotic mess. That's 'pagsasalabid'. It also applies to complicated situations, like when your love life is a web of "it's complicated" statuses, or when a political scandal involves so many people it's hard to track who's who. It's the physical and metaphorical "gulo" (mess).
usage_notes: Can be used literally for physical tangles or figuratively for complex, messy situations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang ayusin ang **pagsasalabid** ng mga kable sa likod ng computer.","translation":"He tried to fix the **entanglement** of the cables behind the computer."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagsasalabid** ng kanilang mga kuwento ang nagdulot ng malaking kalituhan.","translation":"The **intertwining** of their stories caused great confusion."}]

translation: hauling vehicle; something used for transport
meaning_filipino: Anumang sasakyan o kasangkapan na ginagamit sa paglilipat o pagdadala ng maraming bagay nang sabay-sabay.
etymology: From `pang-` (instrumental prefix) + `hakot` (to haul, transport in bulk).
original_explanation: Your **panghakot** could be the L300 van for your family's *lipat-bahay* (moving houses), the eco-bag you use to haul your groceries from the *palengke*, or even the group chat you use to gather all the *chismis*. It's anything you use to move a large quantity of stuff—physical or digital—from point A to point B.
usage_notes: Usually refers to a large vehicle or container.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit sila ng trak na **panghakot** para sa mga donasyon.","translation":"They used a **hauling** truck for the donations."},{"sentence":"Ang malaking bayong na ito ang aking **panghakot** tuwing namamalengke.","translation":"This large bayong is what I use **for carrying** things whenever I go to the market."}]

translation: to touch up, to alter, to revise (often cosmetically)
meaning_filipino: Isagawa ang pagreretoke; baguhin o ayusin ang isang bagay upang mapabuti ang itsura o kalagayan nito, karaniwan ay tumutukoy sa mga larawan, sasakyan, o maging sa itsura ng tao sa pamamagitan ng operasyon.
etymology: From Spanish 'retoque' (touch-up). Suffix '-hin' added to form the verb.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of "retoke." From fixing a pimple on your selfie using an app, to your tita getting a nose job, to pimping your ride. Basically, 'to enhance' or 'to alter' something para mas gumanda or ma-achieve ang #goals. "Pa-retoke naman ng eyebags ko sa picture na 'to!"
usage_notes: While it can mean simple touch-ups, it's now popularly associated with cosmetic surgery.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto niyang **retokihin** ang luma nilang kotse para magmukhang bago.","translation":"He wants to **touch up** their old car to make it look new."},{"sentence":"Nag-ipon siya ng pera para **retokihin** ang kanyang ilong.","translation":"She saved money to **have her nose altered**."}]

translation: to blow something (away); to be blown by the wind
meaning_filipino: Tangayin o ilipad sa pamamagitan ng hangin o pag-ihip.
original_explanation: The feeling when you're trying to keep your papers organized outdoors and the wind just decides to yeet them across the street. That's 'ihihip ng hangin'. It can also be what you do to birthday candles. 'Let's make a wish and ihihip the candles!'
usage_notes: Can be used in both an active sense (to blow something) and a passive sense (to be blown by something, like the wind).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Inihip** ng malakas na hangin ang mga sinampay.","translation":"The strong wind **blew** the laundry away."},{"sentence":"**Ihihip** mo ang alikabok sa lumang libro.","translation":"**Blow** the dust off the old book."}]

translation: to remind earnestly; to bear in mind
meaning_filipino: Taimtim at lubos na ipaalala sa sarili o sa iba ang isang mahalagang bagay; laging isaisip.
etymology: From `alala` (remember/care), with the complex circumfix `paka- -han` (becoming `paka- -in` in the object-focus form), and reduplication of the root.
original_explanation: This is what your mom tells you before you leave the house, with maximum intensity. "Pakaalalahanin mo, umuwi ka bago mag-alas-diyes!" It's not just 'remind', it's 'remind with the full weight of ancestral power'. It's "I'm telling you this for the nth time, so you better burn it into your brain" kind of reminder.
usage_notes: A very intensive form of "alalahanin" (to remember/remind). The prefix "paka-" adds a sense of earnestness, thoroughness, or intensity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pakaalalahanin** mo na ang edukasyon ang tanging yaman na hindi mananakaw sa iyo.","translation":"**Bear in mind** that education is the only wealth that cannot be stolen from you."},{"sentence":"Lagi mong **pakaalalahanin** ang mga bilin ng iyong mga magulang.","translation":"Always **remind** yourself **earnestly** of your parents' advice."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng binti sa pagitan ng tuhod at bukung-bukong, partikular na ang buto sa harap nito (tibia).
original_explanation: The part of your leg that you always seem to bang on the corner of the bed or the coffee table. It's the bony front part of your lower leg. In the palengke, it's the part of the cow's leg that makes the best, most gelatinous bulalo.
usage_notes: Primarily refers to the shinbone (tibia).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masakit ang **lulod** ko dahil natama sa silya.","translation":"My **shin** hurts because it hit the chair."},{"sentence":"Pakihiwa po ng **lulod** ng baka para sa bulalo.","translation":"Please chop the beef **shin** for the bulalo."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang partikular na subkultura o grupong sosyal (hal. music scene, art scene). Ginagamit din sa pariralang "gumawa ng eksena" na nangangahulugang lumikha ng iskandalo o atensyon sa publiko.
original_explanation: Can mean two things. First, 'yung "eksena" or making a scene, like when your tita starts arguing with the cashier over a 25-centavo change. Second, it's your social circle or subculture, like the "indie scene," "art scene," or "cafe-hopping scene." It's your tribe, your vibe. "Ano'ng scene mo?" means "What are you into?"
usage_notes: The meaning depends heavily on context, often used as "eksena".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw kong gumawa ng **eksena** sa party kaya tumahimik na lang ako.","translation":"I didn't want to make a **scene** at the party so I just kept quiet."},{"sentence":"Aktibo siya sa local music **scene**.","translation":"He is active in the local music **scene**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagpapaikli para sa pariralang Ingles na "sorry, late reply," na karaniwang ginagamit sa mga digital na mensahe upang humingi ng paumanhin sa naantalang pagtugon.
etymology: Acronym for the English phrase 'sorry, late reply'.
original_explanation: The official opening line ng mga taong sineen ka for 3 days. Automatic 'to pag gising mo tapos may 20 unread messages ka from yesterday. 'SLR' is the modern 'pasensya na, traffic sa EDSA.'
usage_notes: Exclusively used in text messages, chat, and social media comments.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**SLR**, ngayon ko lang nabasa message mo. Busy sa work.","translation":"**Sorry, late reply**, I only read your message now. Was busy with work."},{"sentence":"Uy, **slr**! Kakauwi ko lang galing probinsya.","translation":"Hey, **sorry, late reply**! I just got home from the province."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tunog ng pagputok-putok o pag-aalab ng apoy; maaari ring tumukoy sa matinding pintig o pulso ng sakit.
original_explanation: This is the sound effect for fire. It's that "crackle-crackle-pop" you hear when you're grilling isaw or having a bonfire. It can also be used to describe a throbbing pain, like a really bad headache that has its own soundtrack. "Naririnig mo ba 'yung dagabdab? Sunog 'yan o 'yung migraine ko lang?"
usage_notes: This word is less common than 'dabdab' (conflagration). It is onomatopoeic and describes the sound of fire, but can also be used for a throbbing sensation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig namin ang **dagabdab** ng apoy mula sa nasusunog na kugon.","translation":"We heard the **crackling** of the fire from the burning cogon grass."},{"sentence":"Ramdam ko ang **dagabdab** ng sakit sa aking sentido.","translation":"I can feel the **throbbing** pain in my temple."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao o hayop na walang tiyak na patutunguhan, palakad-lakad, o gumagala kung saan-saan.
original_explanation: This is the state of that one dog in your neighborhood that seems to belong to everyone and no one at the same time. It's you at the mall, window shopping with no money. 'Bakit ka pagala?' is what your mom asks when she sees you walking around the house instead of doing chores.
usage_notes: Often used to describe stray animals ('asong pagala') or people who seem to be loitering aimlessly. It is a less intense version of 'pagala-gala'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May isang asong **pagala** na laging natutulog sa tapat ng aming gate.","translation":"There is a **stray** dog that always sleeps in front of our gate."},{"sentence":"Pinagsabihan ng pulis ang mga kabataang **pagala** sa kalye nang hatinggabi.","translation":"The police reprimanded the youths **roaming** the streets late at night."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggamit o pagpapatakbo ng isang bisikleta bilang paraan ng transportasyon o libangan.
original_explanation: The verb form of becoming a 'padyak-warrior'. Whether you're doing it to save on gas, for exercise, or because you're part of a cycling club that takes over entire lanes on a Sunday morning, this is your word. #BikeLife
usage_notes: The verb 'mag-bike' is a more common, casual alternative.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Balak naming **magbisikleta** papuntang Tagaytay sa Sabado.","translation":"We plan **to ride a bicycle** to Tagaytay on Saturday."},{"sentence":"Natuto akong **magbisikleta** noong ako'y anim na taong gulang pa lamang.","translation":"I learned **to ride a bicycle** when I was only six years old."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng ipit na partikular na ginagamit upang isabit ang mga nilabhang damit sa sampayan.
original_explanation: The unsung hero of laundry day. This little 'sipit' is responsible for making sure your freshly washed clothes don't fly off to your neighbor's yard during a windy day. They also double as a cheap way to close a bag of chips.
usage_notes: This is a compound noun. While 'sipit' can be understood in context, 'sipit ng damit' is the full, unambiguous term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakikuha ng mga **sipit ng damit** sa sampayan.","translation":"Please get the **clothespins** from the clothesline."},{"sentence":"Nawawala ang isang **sipit ng damit** kaya nalaglag ang medyas.","translation":"One **clothespin** is missing, that's why the sock fell."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagbabago sa pisikal na kaanyuan, estruktura, o presentasyon ng isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'glow up.' It's what happens after a major haircut, a revenge body, or when a company rebrands its logo. It’s the ‘before and after’ reveal in makeover shows. From a messy bun and pambahay to a full-on glam look for a night out—that’s a bagong anyo.
usage_notes: Used to describe a significant change in appearance for people, places, or things.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinakita niya ang kanyang **bagong anyo** matapos ang ilang buwang pag-eehersisyo.","translation":"She showed off her **new look** after months of working out."},{"sentence":"Ang lumang gusali ay mayroon nang **bagong anyo** at ngayon ay isa nang modernong hotel.","translation":"The old building has a **new form** and is now a modern hotel."}]

meaning_filipino: (Pangngalan) Isang tao na mula sa mga bansa sa Kanluran (Europa at Amerika). (Pang-uri) Tumutukoy sa anumang bagay, kultura, o kaisipan na nagmula o may katangian ng Kanluran.
etymology: From `kanluran` + `-in`, a suffix indicating origin or characteristic.
original_explanation: This can be a person (a Westerner, a.k.a. the 'Kano' your tita wants you to marry) or a concept. "Kanluranin" culture is Hollywood movies, burgers, and individualism. "Pangarap na Kanluranin" is the Filipino immigrant dream. It's both an adjective for things and a noun for people from 'the West'.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun to refer to a person or as an adjective to describe something as 'Western'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **kanluranin** ang namamasyal sa Palawan.","translation":"Many **Westerners** are vacationing in Palawan."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang impluwensya ng **kanluraning** medya sa mga kabataan.","translation":"The influence of **western** media on the youth is significant."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng matigas na batong igneous na karaniwang ginagamit sa konstruksyon at mga monumento.
original_explanation: English version ng 'granito'. Parang 'color' vs 'colour'. Pareho lang granite, pero 'pag sinabing **granit**, parang mas tunog imported galing America. 'Pag 'granito', parang galing sa construction supply sa kanto na pagmamay-ari ng isang Don.
usage_notes: Isang variant ng 'granito'. Ang 'granito', na hiram sa Espanyol, ay mas karaniwang maririnig sa usapang lokal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto niya ng **granit** na countertop para sa kanyang bagong kusina.","translation":"She wants a **granite** countertop for her new kitchen."},{"sentence":"Ang monumento ay inukit mula sa isang malaking blokeng **granit**.","translation":"The monument was carved from a large block of **granite**."}]

translation: Boomer; an older person (often out of touch)
meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kabilang sa henerasyong 'Baby Boomer,' ngunit sa kolokyal na gamit, tumutukoy sa sinumang mas matanda na itinuturing na makaluma o hindi nakakasabay sa modernong pag-iisip.
original_explanation: Same as the West, but with a Filipino twist. A 'boomer' isn't just someone born between 1946 and 1964. It's your tito who forwards chain messages on Viber, your tita who says 'Nung panahon namin...', or any older person who thinks millennials/Gen Z are lazy just because they work from home. It's less about age and more about a mindset that clashes with the youth.
usage_notes: A direct loanword used as slang, often with a slightly derogatory or humorous connotation, similar to its international usage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinabihan ako ng tatay ko na mag-ipon para sa bahay, pero ang hirap na ngayon. Hay, mga **boomer**.","translation":"My dad told me to save up for a house, but it's so hard now. Ugh, **boomers**."},{"sentence":"“Okay, **boomer**,” ang sagot ng apo sa kanyang lolo na nagrereklamo tungkol sa TikTok.","translation":"“Okay, **boomer**,” the grandchild replied to his grandpa who was complaining about TikTok."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ugnayan ng sanhi at bunga; ang bagay na pinagmumulan o dahilan ng isang pangyayari o resulta.
etymology: From ka- + sanhi + -an. A less common formation, with 'sanhi' itself being the more standard term for 'cause'.
original_explanation: This is the deep, philosophical version of 'dahilan'. It's the 'why' behind the 'what'. If 'bunga' (effect) is your 'sawi' status, the kasanhian is 'seen-zoned ka niya'. It's the root cause you discuss with your therapist. A more formal, almost archaic word for 'sanhi' or 'dahilan'.
usage_notes: This word is quite rare and literary or archaic. 'Sanhi' or 'dahilan' are the everyday words for 'cause' or 'reason'. 'Kasanhian' might be encountered in old texts or very formal philosophical discussions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng mga pilosopo ang **kasanhian** ng pag-iral.","translation":"Philosophers study the **causality** of existence."},{"sentence":"Ang **kasanhian** ng kanyang pag-alis ay isang malaking misteryo.","translation":"The **reason** for his departure is a great mystery."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ayos ng buhok o anumang bagay na binubuo ng tatlo o higit pang hibla na pinag-isa-isa at pinagsasalit-salit.
original_explanation: Your go-to hairstyle nung elementary ka, usually ginagawa ng nanay mo habang nag-aagahan ka. Para kang si Elsa from Frozen pero a few decades earlier. Pwede rin sa lubid o sa bawang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang magsuot ng dalawang **tirintas** sa buhok.","translation":"She likes to wear two **braids** in her hair."},{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng isang **tirintas** ng bawang sa palengke.","translation":"Mom bought a **braid** of garlic from the market."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mananakop, lalo na ang isa sa mga Espanyol na mananakop ng Mexico at Peru noong ika-16 na siglo. Sa pangkalahatan, sinumang nagsasagawa ng pananakop.
original_explanation: The original bad boys of Philippine history class. These were the Spanish dudes in shiny armor who came for "God, Gold, and Glory" and ended up staying for 333 years. Think of them as the ultimate 'gatecrashers' of an entire archipelago.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa kontekstong pangkasaysayan na may kaugnayan sa kolonisasyon ng mga Espanyol.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinamunuan ng mga **konkistador** na Espanyol ang paggalugad at pananakop sa Pilipinas.","translation":"The Spanish **conquistadors** led the exploration and conquest of the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Si Hernán Cortés ay isang tanyag na **konkistador**.","translation":"Hernán Cortés was a famous **conquistador**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pang-abay na nagpapahiwatig ng katiyakan, kawalan ng pag-aalinlangan, o na ang isang bagay ay inaasahan at natural lamang.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'no-brainer' response. 'Libre mo ba?' '**Siyempre**!' 'Mahal mo pa ba ako?' '**Siyempre**... hindi.' It's the Filipino 'duh', 'obviously', and 'for sure' all rolled into one. Use it when the answer is as clear as your need for coffee on a Monday morning.
usage_notes: Extremely common in everyday conversation. Can be used to start a sentence or as a standalone answer. Often followed by 'naman' for emphasis ('Siyempre naman!').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tatanungin mo kung sasama ako? **Siyempre**!","translation":"You're asking if I'll come? **Of course**!"},{"sentence":"**Siyempre**, uunahin natin ang kalusugan bago ang lahat.","translation":"**Naturally**, we will prioritize health above all else."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang naaalis na artipisyal na kapalit para sa mga nawawalang ngipin at mga nakapalibot na tisyu; pustiso.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung "backup teeth" na madalas mong makikita sa baso sa tabi ng kama ni lolo o lola. Kilala rin bilang pustiso. Kapag tinanggal na nila ang kanilang dentyur, alam mong seryoso na ang usapan... o oras na para matulog.
usage_notes: "Pustiso" is a more common and native-sounding term. "Dentyur" is a direct Filipinized spelling of the English word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nililinis ni lola ang kanyang **dentyur** tuwing gabi.","translation":"Grandma cleans her **dentures** every night."},{"sentence":"Nahulog ang **dentyur** niya habang tumatawa nang malakas.","translation":"His **dentures** fell out while he was laughing hard."}]

translation: to become bruised; to get mushy
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging magulpi o malambot dahil sa pagkabagsak, pagkapukpok, o sobrang pagkahinog.
original_explanation: 'Yung itsura ng saging na naiwan mo sa bag for a week. Or 'yung pakiramdam mo after sumakay ng bus na siksikan from Cubao to Monumento. Pagbaba mo, lamog ka na. Your body after that ride? It has **lumamog**.
usage_notes: Refers to becoming soft, bruised, or crushed, applied to fruits, objects, or even a person's body after physical strain.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahulog ang mga kamatis kaya ito ay **lumamog**.","translation":"The tomatoes fell, that's why they **got mushy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paghahanda ng pagkain sa pamamagitan ng init; tumutukoy din sa isang partikular na putahe o uri ng pagkain.
original_explanation: 'Luto' is a word of power. It can mean the act of cooking ('Magaling siyang magluto'), the finished product ('Ano'ng luto mo?'), or a secret deal ('May luto sa laban!'). It's the reason we have adobo, sinigang, and kare-kare. But be careful, in sports or politics, 'may luto' means the game is rigged. So, it can be delicious or devious.
usage_notes: Can refer to the act of cooking, the cooked food itself, or figuratively, a pre-arranged or rigged outcome ('lutong makaw').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **luto** ni Nanay ang palaging pinakamasarap.","translation":"Mom's **cooking** is always the most delicious."},{"sentence":"May hinala silang may **luto** sa resulta ng kompetisyon.","translation":"They suspect the competition's result was **rigged**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pabango na karaniwang mas magaan ang konsentrasyon at amoy kaysa sa 'perfume'.
etymology: From Spanish 'colonia' (Agua de Colonia - Water of Cologne).
original_explanation: Ito 'yung amoy-baby na pabango na ginagamit mo after maligo para feeling fresh. That Nenuco or Johnson's Baby Cologne scent is the smell of Filipino childhood. Hindi kasing-tapang ng perfume, 'yung kolonya ay para sa 'pabebe' freshness lang.
usage_notes: Refers to a light fragrance, often associated with freshness and babies/children.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang maglagay ng **kolonya** pagkatapos maligo.","translation":"She loves to put on **cologne** after taking a bath."},{"sentence":"Pakibigay nga ng **kolonya** ng bata.","translation":"Please pass the baby's **cologne**."}]

meaning_filipino: Magdulot ng malawakang pinsala o pagkawasak sa mga ari-arian, kapaligiran, o sa buhay ng tao.
original_explanation: Ito yung ginagawa ng bagyo sa Pilipinas every year. Parang ex mo na dumaan lang sa buhay mo para sirain ang lahat at iwan kang wasak. Pwede ring action ng kontrabida sa pelikula, "Mamiminsala ako sa baryo ninyo!"
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng mga kalamidad, digmaan, o malawakang pagkasira.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang malakas na bagyo ay **naminsala** sa maraming bayan sa Bicol.","translation":"The strong typhoon **wreaked havoc** on many towns in Bicol."},{"sentence":"Ang layunin ng mga mananakop ay **maminsala** at maghasik ng takot.","translation":"The goal of the invaders is to **destroy** and spread fear."}]

translation: Way of the Cross, Stations of the Cross
meaning_filipino: Isang debosyon ng mga Katoliko na ginugunita ang mga huling oras ni Hesukristo, mula sa pagkakahatol hanggang sa kanyang paglilibing. Ito ay binubuo ng labing-apat na estasyon.
etymology: From Spanish "Via Crucis" (Way of the Cross).
original_explanation: That's the Tagalized "Via Crucis." It's the Catholic prayer marathon during Holy Week where you follow the 14 Stations of the Cross. For many, it's a solemn family tradition, often involving a long walk to a church or grotto.
usage_notes: Always capitalized. Primarily used in a religious context, especially during Lent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kasama ang buong pamilya sa pagdalo sa **Biakrusis** tuwing Biyernes Santo.","translation":"The whole family participates in the **Way of the Cross** every Good Friday."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang damdamin ng kasiyahan, galak, o libangan; isang bagay o tao na nagdudulot ng tuwa.
original_explanation: This is the raw element of joy. Think of it as the core ingredient. You don't usually say 'I feel katuwa,' you say 'Nakakatuwa!' (It's amusing!). Katuwa is the reason you smile when you see a cute puppy video or when your friend tells a corny but funny joke. It's the little spark of delight.
usage_notes: More commonly found in its affixed forms like 'nakakatuwa' (amusing), 'katuwaan' (merriment), or 'katuwa-tuwa' (very amusing). As a standalone word, it's somewhat poetic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga bata ang nagbibigay **katuwa** sa bahay.","translation":"The children are the source of **joy** in the house."},{"sentence":"Anong laking **katuwa** ang hatid ng balitang iyon!","translation":"What great **delight** that news brought!"}]

meaning_filipino: Sa anumang panahon o pagkakataon, sa nakaraan man o sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: The word for dramatic promises and declarations. With "hindi," it means "never ever." "Hindi kita iiwan kailanman" is the ultimate (and often broken) promise in Pinoy romance movies. Without "hindi," it means "ever," as in "ang pinakamagandang nakita ko kailanman" (the most beautiful I've ever seen). It adds a touch of forever to any statement.
usage_notes: Its meaning flips depending on whether it's in a positive or negative sentence. "kailanman" = ever; "hindi kailanman" = never.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko **kailanman** makakalimutan ang araw na iyon.","translation":"I will **never** forget that day."},{"sentence":"Ito na ang pinakamasayang Pasko ko **kailanman**.","translation":"This is the happiest Christmas I've **ever** had."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang mailupi o maitiklop ang isang bagay tulad ng papel o damit.
original_explanation: That feeling of accomplishment when you finally figure out how to fold a fitted sheet. "**Matupi** mo ba 'to nang maayos?" It's also what your mom tells you to do with your clean laundry that's been sitting on "the chair" for a week. The verb form of "tupi," the enemy of every tamad person.
usage_notes: A straightforward verb for the action of folding.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko **matupi** nang tama ang mapa dahil masyado itong malaki.","translation":"I can't **fold** the map correctly because it's too big."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos mamalantsa, kailangan mong **matupi** agad ang mga damit.","translation":"After ironing, you need to **be able to fold** the clothes immediately."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto o proseso ng pagbibigay ng serbisyo, paglilingkod, o pag-aalay ng sarili para sa isang tao, layunin, o institusyon.
etymology: From pag- (nominalizing prefix) + si- (reduplication of first syllable of root) + silbi (serve, use).
original_explanation: This is your 'render'-ing of service. Think of it as the loading time before your good deed is fully delivered. It's what you do for your country, for your family, or for your customer when they ask "pa-assist po?". It's the core of being a public servant, a waiter, or that one friend who's always the designated driver.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of public service, hospitality, or being useful in general.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagsisilbi** sa bayan ay hindi matatawaran.","translation":"His **service** to the country is invaluable."},{"sentence":"Bahagi ng **pagsisilbi** sa restawran ang pagiging magalang sa mga customer.","translation":"Part of **serving** in a restaurant is being polite to customers."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang propesyonal na dalubhasa sa pag-aangkop at pagbibigay ng mga salamin sa mata at contact lens ayon sa reseta. Maaari ring tumukoy sa isang taong gumagawa o nagbebenta ng mga instrumentong optikal.
original_explanation: Sila yung taga-salamin shop na nag-a-adjust ng eyeglasses mo para hindi mag-slide sa ilong mo habang nag-ma-marites. Sila ang bridge sa pagitan ng reseta ng doktor at ng actual mong salamin. Ito ang Hispanized na bersyon ng 'optisyan'.
usage_notes: Minsan ay napagpapalit sa 'optometra', ngunit ang 'optiko' ay mas nakatuon sa paggawa at pag-aayos ng salamin. Ang 'optisyan' na hiram sa Ingles ay mas karaniwang ginagamit ngayon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala ko ang aking sirang salamin sa **optiko** para ipaayos.","translation":"I brought my broken glasses to the **optician** to have them fixed."}]

meaning_filipino: Utusan ang isang tao na lagyan ng yelo ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay inumin.
etymology: From pa- (causative) + pag- (causative) + yelo (ice), which is from Spanish 'hielo'.
original_explanation: What you shout to your younger sibling from the sala when your Coke is getting warm. "Hoy, bunso! Papagyeluhin mo nga 'tong baso ko!"
usage_notes: A very specific causative verb. The 'pag-' makes it sound a bit more commanding or formal than just 'payeluhan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas masarap ang juice kapag malamig, kaya **papagyeluhin** mo si Maria.","translation":"The juice is better when it's cold, so **have** Maria **put ice** in it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking nagtatrabaho sa isang restawran o kainan na ang tungkulin ay kumuha ng order, maghatid ng pagkain at inumin, at asikasuhin ang mga pangangailangan ng mga kostumer.
original_explanation: The unsung hero of your date night. Sila yung may photographic memory para sa order ng isang buong pamilya at may superhuman strength para magbuhat ng tray na puno ng sizzling plates. Tip your serbidor well, sila ang tulay mo papuntang extra rice.
usage_notes: Partikular na tumutukoy sa lalaking serber. Ang katumbas para sa babae ay "serbidora".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinawag niya ang **serbidor** para humingi ng isa pang baso ng tubig.","translation":"He called the **waiter** to ask for another glass of water."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging maginhawa, walang hirap, o maluwag.
etymology: From ka- (denoting a state or quality) + alwan (ease, comfort) + -an (suffix indicating a state or place).
original_explanation: That feeling when your sahod finally drops, your internet is fast, and there's no traffic. It's the state of not being stressed, like a cat sleeping in a sunbeam. The opposite of 'Sana all,' it's the 'Sana now' that actually happened.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a life of comfort or a state of physical or financial ease.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghahanap siya ng **kaalwanan** sa gitna ng kanyang mga problema.","translation":"He is looking for **comfort** amidst his problems."},{"sentence":"Ang pagkakaroon ng sapat na ipon ay nagbibigay ng **kaalwanan** sa pag-iisip.","translation":"Having enough savings provides **ease** of mind."}]

translation: to decide; to resolve; to rule
meaning_filipino: Magbigay ng huling desisyon o hatol hinggil sa isang usapin o suliranin.
original_explanation: This is the more formal, almost judicial version of "magdesisyon." It's what a judge does in court, or what your parents do after a long family meeting about where to go for vacation. "Okay, katahimikan! **Ipinasiya** ng korte... este, ni Nanay, na sa Baguio tayo pupunta!" It carries weight and finality.
usage_notes: Often used in formal, legal, or serious contexts. 'Magpasya' is a more common synonym for 'to decide'. 'Ipasiya' focuses on the decision itself as the object of the verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ipasiya** na ng komite kung aling proyekto ang uunahin.","translation":"The committee will now **decide** which project to prioritize."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **ipasiya** ang isang bagay kapag kulang sa impormasyon.","translation":"It is difficult **to decide** on a matter when there is a lack of information."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-udyok o paghikayat sa isang tao na gumawa ng masama o mag-alsa laban sa isang awtoridad o kalagayan.
original_explanation: This is the 'Marites' friend who whispers, "Uy, awayin mo na, 'di ka papatalo 'di ba?" It's the act of poking the bear, but you're convincing someone *else* to do the poking. It's adding fuel to the fire, convincing your workmate to send that spicy email to HR, or telling your sibling to confront your parents about their curfew.
usage_notes: Carries a negative connotation of provoking trouble or conflict.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **manulsol** ng gulo sa pagitan ng magkakaibigan.","translation":"He tried to **instigate** a fight between the friends."},{"sentence":"Ang lider ng grupo ay inakusahang **manulsol** ng rebelyon.","translation":"The group's leader was accused of **inciting** a rebellion."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdaan o paglusot sa isang bagay mula sa isang panig patungo sa kabila.
original_explanation: 'Yung bala na **tumagos** sa pader. Or 'yung 'tagos sa buto' na lamig 'pag umuulan. Pwede ring 'yung mga salita ng nanay mo, **tumagos** sa puso mo. It's about piercing through something, whether physical or emotional.
usage_notes: This is the completed aspect (past tense). The infinitive is 'tumagos', the progressive is 'tumatagos', and the contemplative is 'tatagos'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis na **tumagos** ang bala sa manipis na dingding.","translation":"The bullet quickly **penetrated** the thin wall."},{"sentence":"**Tumagos** sa puso ko ang kanyang mga sinabi.","translation":"His words **pierced** through my heart."}]

translation: to scatter; to strew; to splash
meaning_filipino: Ikalat o ihagis ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay likido o maliliit na piraso, sa iba't ibang direksyon.
original_explanation: That dramatic movie scene where someone throws holy water at an *aswang*. Or when a kid playfully splashes water on you at the beach. It can also be scattering flower petals at a wedding. Basically, a controlled, wide-area throw.
usage_notes: Can refer to liquids (water, soup) or small solid particles (rice grains, confetti, petals).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maingat niyang **isinaboy** ang pagkain para sa mga isda sa lawa.","translation":"He carefully **scattered** the food for the fish in the lake."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng isang bagay na kasalukuyang bitbit o dinala ng isang tao.
original_explanation: This isn't the baggage itself, but the *state* of being carried. 'Dala mo ba ang payong?' (Did you bring the umbrella?). It's the past participle acting like an adjective. It's the 'brought' in 'Is this the pancit you brought?' The stress on the last syllable is key!
usage_notes: The stress on the last syllable /da-LA/ distinguishes it from the noun /DA-la/ (load). This form is frequently used in questions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ito ang mga prutas na **dala** ko mula sa probinsya.","translation":"These are the fruits I **brought** from the province."},{"sentence":"**Dala** mo ba ang susi ng kotse?","translation":"Did you **bring** the car key?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaki at matibay na kahon o sisidlan, karaniwang tumutukoy sa Arka ni Noe (Noah's Ark) o sa Kaban ng Tipan (Ark of the Covenant).
original_explanation: Parang yung baul ni lola na punung-puno ng mga lumang gamit at lihim, pero on a biblical scale. Ito yung original "bahay-bangka" ni Noah, at yung ultimate treasure chest ng mga Israelita.
usage_notes: Halos palaging ginagamit sa kontekstong biblikal o historikal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isinakay ni Noe ang mga hayop sa **arka** bago dumating ang malaking baha.","translation":"Noah brought the animals onto the **ark** before the great flood came."},{"sentence":"Itinago sa loob ng **arka** ang mga tapyas ng bato na kinasusulatan ng Sampung Utos.","translation":"The stone tablets on which the Ten Commandments were written were kept inside the **ark**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sarsa na gawa sa mga dinurog na kamatis, na pangunahing sangkap sa maraming lutuin tulad ng spaghetti at menudo.
etymology: Mula sa mga salitang Ingles na "tomato" at "sauce".
original_explanation: The lifeblood of Pinoy spaghetti, afritada, menudo, and caldereta. It's the reason our spaghetti is sweet and red. You can buy it in a can or a doypack. If your ulam is reddish, there's a 90% chance this guy is the culprit.
usage_notes: Madalas isulat bilang isang salita, "tomatosauce", sa impormal na pagsulat o tinutukoy na lang sa pangalan ng brand.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kulang pa ng **tomato sauce** ang spaghetti.","translation":"The spaghetti still needs more **tomato sauce**."},{"sentence":"Bumili ka ng isang lata ng **tomato sauce** para sa afritada.","translation":"Buy one can of **tomato sauce** for the afritada."}]

translation: the act of being saved; rescue
meaning_filipino: Ang akto o kalagayan ng pagkaligtas mula sa panganib, kapahamakan, o kamatayan.
original_explanation: This is the 'salamat, Lord!' moment. Whether it's being pulled from a flood, passing a subject you thought you'd fail, or your friend paying for your Grab ride when your card declines. That feeling of relief after a close call? That's the result of pagkasagip. The noun form of being rescued.
usage_notes: 'Pagkasagip' refers to the state or event of being saved, while 'pagsagip' refers to the act of saving someone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ikinuwento ng biktima ang kanyang himalang **pagkasagip** mula sa gumuhong gusali.","translation":"The victim narrated his miraculous **rescue** from the collapsed building."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkasagip** sa mga asong kalye ay adbokasiya ng grupo.","translation":"The **rescuing** of street dogs is the group's advocacy."}]

meaning_filipino: Magbigay ng serbisyo, tulong, o paglilingkod sa kapwa, sa bayan, o sa isang organisasyon.
original_explanation: The ultimate goal of every BPO agent ('to serve the customer'), politician ('to serve the people'... supposedly), and your nanay when she puts a mountain of rice on your plate ('para sa alaga ko'). It's about giving your time and effort for someone else, whether it's for a paycheck, for the country, or for love.
usage_notes: Can refer to service in many contexts: public service, customer service, religious service, or serving a meal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pangarap niya ay **maglingkod** sa bayan bilang isang tapat na pulis.","translation":"His dream is to **serve** the country as an honest police officer."},{"sentence":"Tayo na't **maglingkod** ng pagkain sa mga bisita.","translation":"Let's go and **serve** the food to the guests."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi makapal; may kaunting sukat sa pagitan ng dalawang magkabilang panig.
original_explanation: The opposite of your patience when the internet is slow. Also, how you describe your wallet before payday. "Bes, ang manipis ng tsismis mo, wala man lang resibo?"
