usage_notes: Can refer to physical objects (paper, cloth) or abstract concepts (patience, chance).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Manipis** lang ang pader kaya rinig ang usapan nila.","translation":"The wall is **thin** so their conversation can be heard."},{"sentence":"Bumili ka ng tela na hindi masyadong **manipis**.","translation":"Buy a fabric that isn't too **thin**."}]

translation: to slide down; to descend rapidly
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbaba o pagdausdos mula sa isang mataas na lugar, lalo na ng isang malaking bilang o dami.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your savings account when the 12.12 sale hits. Parang landslide ng gastos. It can also mean a lot of people coming down from the mountains, like in old stories.
usage_notes: Often used to describe things moving downwards in a large mass, like a landslide (paghugos ng lupa) or a crowd of people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **maghugos** ang mga bato mula sa tuktok ng bundok.","translation":"The rocks started to **slide down** from the top of the mountain."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng misa, **naghugos** ang mga tao palabas ng simbahan.","translation":"After the mass, the people **descended rapidly** out of the church."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay ng damit, sapatos, o anumang aksesorya sa katawan sa nakalipas na panahon.
original_explanation: Past tense. What you did this morning. Or what your friend did last night that made you say "Sana all!" Your OOTD's origin story. "Girl, ano'ng sinuot mo sa party?" is a classic question. It's the action that precedes the 'fit check'.
usage_notes: Past tense of "magsuot". The present/progressive is "nagsusuot".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagsuot** siya ng pulang bestida sa kasal.","translation":"She **wore** a red dress to the wedding."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **nagsuot** ng sapatos ko?","translation":"Who **wore** my shoes?"}]

translation: to hug each other; to embrace one another (reciprocal)
meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay na pagyayakapan ng dalawa o higit pang tao bilang pagpapahayag ng pagmamahal, pagkakaibigan, o kaginhawahan.
original_explanation: The ultimate group hug verb. It’s what happens at the airport during a balikbayan's arrival, at the end of a teleserye when the family finally reconciles, or when your team wins the championship. It's a mutual, often emotional, embrace. More than just a `yakap`, it's a shared moment of closeness.
usage_notes: A reciprocal verb. The action is mutual among the subjects.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagyapusan** ang mag-ina nang sila'y muling magkita pagkatapos ng sampung taon.","translation":"The mother and child **hugged each other** when they saw each other again after ten years."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng laro, **nagyapusan** ang magkabilang koponan bilang tanda ng sportsmanship.","translation":"After the game, the opposing teams **embraced one another** as a sign of sportsmanship."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar, establisyimento, o pook kung saan nagtitipon ang mga tao upang uminom, tulad ng isang bar o taberna.
original_explanation: Your friendly neighborhood bar, the videoke joint down the street, or even just Mang Berto's sari-sari store with a single plastic table outside. A **painuman** is any designated area where spirits are served and secrets (and salaries) are spilled.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to the location of drinking. Similar to `inuman` but `painuman` feels more like a formally established place.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagbukas ng bagong **painuman** sa kanto.","translation":"A new **drinking place** opened on the corner."},{"sentence":"Maraming tao sa **painuman** tuwing araw ng sahod.","translation":"The **bar** is full of people every payday."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagbabayad para sa mga biniling produkto o serbisyo, karaniwan sa isang tindahan, hotel, o online.
original_explanation: That moment of truth sa grocery, Shopee, or Lazada where you see the total damage. It's the final boss battle between your sahod and your 'add to cart' impulses. 'Mag-checkout ka na, baka maunahan ka pa!'
usage_notes: Used in the context of shopping (both online and in physical stores) and leaving a hotel. In spoken Taglish, it is often used as a verb ('i-checkout').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang haba ng pila sa **checkout** counter.","translation":"The line at the **checkout** counter is long."},{"sentence":"I-**checkout** mo na 'yang nasa cart mo bago mag-sold out.","translation":"**Checkout** what's in your cart before it gets sold out."}]

translation: can be directed; can be aimed
meaning_filipino: May kakayahang iharap o itutok ang isang bagay, tulad ng atensyon, direksyon, o paningin, sa isang partikular na lugar o layunin.
etymology: From `ma-` (potential prefix) + `itungo` (to direct/aim). The root is `tungo` (direction, towards).
original_explanation: This is your internal GPS. "Saan ko ba dapat maitungo ang career path ko?" (Where should I direct my career path?). It's about aiming your focus, your efforts, or even just your gaze. It’s what you do when you’re lost, literally or figuratively, and you’re trying to find your North Star.
usage_notes: Often used for abstract concepts like focus, attention, or one's life path. It has a slightly more formal or literary feel than 'maitutok'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana'y **maitungo** mo sa tama ang iyong mga desisyon sa buhay.","translation":"I hope you **can direct** your life decisions correctly."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya **maitungo** ang tingin sa akin matapos ang nangyari.","translation":"He couldn't **aim** his gaze at me after what happened."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagsasara o pagpapatiklop ng isang bagay na karaniwang bukas, tulad ng bibig, palad, o bulaklak.
original_explanation: The command you wish you could give your chismosa kapitbahay. It's the physical action of shutting something, often your mouth when you're about to say something you'll regret, or when your boss is explaining the new 'optional' OT policy.
usage_notes: Often used for mouths, hands (palms), and flowers, implying a gentle or natural closing rather than a forceful shutting (like 'isara').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Itikom** mo ang iyong bibig kung wala kang magandang sasabihin.","translation":"**Close** your mouth if you have nothing nice to say."},{"sentence":"Nang lumubog ang araw, nagsimulang **itikom** ng halaman ang mga talulot nito.","translation":"When the sun set, the plant began to **close** its petals."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubhang kaakit-akit, kahali-halina, o nakamamangha na may kakayahang umagaw ng buong atensyon at damdamin.
etymology: From ka- + bighani (reduplicated), a form of intensification meaning 'very enchanting'.
original_explanation: That feeling when you see your ultimate crush. Or when you watch a sunset at a perfect beach. It's the 'wow factor' turned up to 11. It's so beautiful or interesting that it makes you stop scrolling your phone. That's 'kabigha-bighani'.
usage_notes: A very expressive and somewhat poetic word. The reduplication of 'bighani' intensifies the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kabigha-bighani** ang tanawin mula sa tuktok ng bundok.","translation":"The view from the top of the mountain is **enchanting**."},{"sentence":"Mayroon siyang **kabigha-bighani** na ngiti.","translation":"She has a **captivating** smile."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagdadaiti at paggalaw ng dalawang bagay laban sa isa't isa, na kadalasang lumilikha ng priksyon, init, o tunog.
original_explanation: That awkward moment in a crowded MRT when you're pressed against a stranger – that's pagkikiskis. It's what happens when you start a fire with two sticks. It can also be that clingy officemate who's always 'rubbing elbows' with the boss. Friction, in all its literal and figurative glory.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical friction or social interaction (rubbing elbows).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkikiskis** ng dalawang bato ay maaaring lumikha ng apoy.","translation":"The **rubbing** of two stones against each other can create fire."},{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **pagkikiskis** ng mga sanga ng puno sa aming bintana dahil sa malakas na hangin.","translation":"I heard the **rubbing** of the tree branches against our window due to the strong wind."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na ginagamit bilang mura o ekspresyon ng matinding galit, pagkadismaya, o pagkagulat, na tumutukoy sa isang tao na may masamang pag-uugali.
etymology: From Spanish 'animal' or English 'animal'. Its use as a curse word is a local development.
original_explanation: Officially it means "animal" from English/Spanish, but in the Philippines? It's a classic mura (curse word). It's what you scream when someone cuts you off in traffic or when your internet dies mid-Zoom meeting. It's less about the literal creature and more about calling someone uncivilized. Usage: "Animal ka!"
usage_notes: Considered a mild to moderate curse word. Its intensity depends heavily on the tone of voice. Often used in the phrase 'Animal ka!'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napasigaw siya ng, '**Animal!**' nang matapunan ng kape.","translation":"He shouted, '**You animal!**' when coffee was spilled on him."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang basta-basta sumigaw ng '**animal**' sa kalye.","translation":"Don't just shout '**animal**' on the street."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang karaniwan at magiliw na katawagan para sa ama; ang magulang na lalaki.
etymology: Mula sa Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *tata na nangangahulugang 'ama, tiyo, o mas matandang kamag-anak na lalaki'.
original_explanation: The most common, all-around term for 'dad'. He's the designated driver, the taga-buhat ng mabibigat, the ATM, and the one who tells the corniest jokes that only he finds funny. Siya yung 'haligi ng tahanan' na minsan, siya rin yung nakahiga sa sofa at nanonood ng TV. The OG provider and protector.
usage_notes: Ang pinakamalawak na ginagamit na termino para sa 'ama' sa Pilipinas, anuman ang antas sa lipunan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahal na mahal ko ang aking **tatay**.","translation":"I love my **father** very much."},{"sentence":"\"Nasaan si **Tatay**?\" tanong ng bata.","translation":"\"Where is **Dad**?\" the child asked."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkuha sa isang bagay na ibinigay o inialok; ang pagkilala at pagpayag sa isang kalagayan, ideya, o tao.
original_explanation: When you get your 'sahod,' you **tumanggap** ng suweldo. When you finally move on from your ex, you **tumanggap** the fact that it's over. It's for everything from parcels from Lazada to harsh realities. The opposite of 'ghosting' a delivery rider.
usage_notes: A very versatile verb used in both literal (receiving an object) and figurative (accepting a situation) senses.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masaya siyang **tumanggap** ng regalo mula sa kanyang mga kaibigan.","translation":"He happily **received** a gift from his friends."},{"sentence":"Mahirap man, kailangan nating **tumanggap** ng katotohanan.","translation":"Even if it's difficult, we need **to accept** the truth."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sapin sa sahig na karaniwang yari sa hinabing dahon ng buri, pandan, o iba pang katulad na materyales, at ginagamit na higaan.
original_explanation: The OG portable bed. Before memory foam and king-sized mattresses, there was the **banig**. Perfect for sleepovers, picnics, or just chilling on the floor during a brownout. It has that distinct, earthy smell that reminds you of lola's house in the province. Roll it up when you're done, and it's like the sleepover never happened.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap matulog sa sahig na may **banig** kapag mainit ang panahon.","translation":"It feels good to sleep on the floor with a **sleeping mat** when the weather is hot."},{"sentence":"Naglatag si Lola ng makulay na **banig** para sa mga bisita.","translation":"Grandma laid out a colorful **sleeping mat** for the visitors."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pag-aalab o pagliliwanag na walang apoy, katulad ng sa umuusok na uling o baga; nagliliyab nang marahan at mainit.
original_explanation: That intense, fiery look in someone's eyes when they're super angry. "Tumingin siya sa akin at nagbabaga ang mga mata." It's not literally on fire, but it's the look that says "one more word and you're toast." Also used for charcoal when you're about to start the family BBQ.
usage_notes: Often used metaphorically to describe intense emotion, especially anger ("nagbabagang galit").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iniwan niyang **nagbabaga** ang mga uling bago ilagay ang isda sa ihawan.","translation":"He left the charcoal **glowing** before putting the fish on the grill."},{"sentence":"**Nagbabaga** sa galit ang kanyang mga mata habang nakatingin sa kaaway.","translation":"His eyes were **smoldering** with anger while looking at the enemy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sabay o palitang pagpikit ng isang mata ng dalawa o higit pang tao bilang senyas o pagbibiro sa isa't isa.
original_explanation: That silent communication you have with your workmate when the boss says something ridiculous. It's the 'I know, right?' expressed in a single, sneaky eye-twitch. Can also be a form of low-key landi (flirting) across a crowded jeepney.
usage_notes: `Magkindatan` is a reciprocal action, meaning two or more people are winking at each other. For a single person winking at someone, use `kumindat`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagulat ako nang **magkindatan** ang dalawang magkasintahan sa loob ng simbahan.","translation":"I was surprised when the couple **winked at each other** inside the church."},{"sentence":"Huwag kayong **magkindatan** diyan, baka isipin ng iba may sikreto kayo.","translation":"Don't you two **wink at each other** there, others might think you have a secret."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang panagot na nagpapahayag ng pagsang-ayon, pagkumpirma, o pagtanggap. Ito ang pamantayang paraan ng pagsasabi ng "yes."
original_explanation: The fundamental building block of agreement in Filipino. It's simple, direct, and gets the job done. But be careful with the tone! A quick 'Oo' is a simple yes. A long, drawn-out 'Oooooooh' might mean 'Oh, now I get it.' A hesitant 'O...o?' means you're probably agreeing to do the dishes and you regret it already.
usage_notes: 'Opo' is the polite form used when speaking to elders or superiors. 'Oo' is the informal/casual form for peers or those younger than you.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Oo**, sasama ako sa inyo mamaya.","translation":"**Yes**, I will go with you all later."},{"sentence":"Kumain ka na ba? **Oo**.","translation":"Have you eaten? **Yes**."}]

translation: to get wet; to become wet
meaning_filipino: Hayaan ang sarili na mabasa o malagyan ng likido tulad ng tubig, karaniwan ay dahil sa ulan.
original_explanation: What happens when you forget your umbrella during rainy season. Or when your 'friend' 'accidentally' pushes you into the pool. Your mom's classic warning: 'Huwag kang magbasa sa ulan, baka ka magkasakit!'
usage_notes: The stress is on the second syllable, distinguishing it from 'magbasá' (to read). Usually implies getting wet from rain.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayokong **magbasa** sa ulan dahil bagong ligo ako.","translation":"I don't want to **get wet** in the rain because I just took a shower."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng lasa na karaniwang matatagpuan sa mga prutas tulad ng sitrus, suka, at iba pang pagkain na nagdudulot ng pakiramdam ng pag-ngilo sa dila.
original_explanation: That face you make when you eat green mangoes with bagoong for the first time. It's the 'kilig' of your taste buds. Also used to describe someone's grumpy or sour mood ('asim ng mukha').
usage_notes: Can refer to the taste or a person's sour disposition.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Grabe ang **asim** ng sinigang na ito, tamang-tama sa panlasa ko!","translation":"The **sourness** of this sinigang is intense, just right for my taste!"},{"sentence":"Bakit ganyan ang mukha mo? Ang **asim**!","translation":"Why the long face? You look so **sour**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang epekto, pakiramdam, o opinyon na nabubuo sa isipan tungkol sa isang tao, bagay, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: Yung 'first impression', 'yan 'yung initial judgment mo sa isang tao. Parang sa job interview, kailangan good **impresyon** ang iwan mo. O kaya 'yung **impresyon** mo sa bagong episode ng paborito mong series, 'Medyo bitin, pero okay na rin.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maganda ang unang **impresyon** niya sa akin.","translation":"His/Her first **impression** of me was good."},{"sentence":"Ano ang **impresyon** mo sa bagong manager?","translation":"What's your **impression** of the new manager?"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na mayroong maraming buhok o balahibo sa katawan o mukha.
etymology: From 'balbas' (beard) + '-in' (a suffix indicating having the quality of the root word).
original_explanation: This is the word for your tito who looks like a friendly bear, or your crush who's rocking that full, glorious beard. Someone who is balbasin has a lot of hair where hair can grow - arms, legs, chest, face. It's the opposite of 'kinis'.
usage_notes: Can refer to hair on any part of the body, not just the face, although it's derived from 'beard'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang asawa niya ay **balbasin** kaya madalas itong mag-ahit.","translation":"Her husband is **hairy** so he often shaves."},{"sentence":"Hinahangaan niya ang mga lalaking **balbasin** ang dibdib.","translation":"She admires men with **hairy** chests."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga salita, letra, o simbolo na inukit, isinulat, o ipininta sa isang matigas na bagay tulad ng bato, metal, o kahoy bilang isang permanenteng tala.
original_explanation: 'Yung pangalan mo na naka-ukit sa tropeo, 'yung 'I love you' na sinulat niyo sa puno (na 'di dapat ginagawa!), o 'yung mga nakasulat sa mga lumang barya. 'Yan ang inskripsiyon. It's basically the ancient version of a tweet, but way more permanent and harder to delete.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng mga arkeologo ang **inskripsiyon** sa natagpuang banga.","translation":"The archaeologists are studying the **inscription** on the discovered jar."},{"sentence":"May **inskripsiyon** ng petsa sa likod ng lumang relos.","translation":"There is an **inscription** of the date on the back of the old watch."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang isang tao na may kaparehong mga magulang; anak ng iyong ama o ina.
etymology: From `ka-` + `patid`. The archaic root `patid` possibly refers to being 'cut' from the same umbilical cord.
original_explanation: Your built-in best friend and/or rival. The person you share parents, clothes (sometimes without permission), and blame with. They're the reason for 'Sumbong kita kay Mama!' and also the first person you call for backup. The term is so powerful it's also used for close friends ('kapatid sa ibang ina') and members of a brotherhood/fraternity.
usage_notes: A gender-neutral term for sibling. Can be specified with 'na lalaki' (brother) or 'na babae' (sister).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lima kaming magka**kapatid**.","translation":"There are five of us **siblings**."},{"sentence":"Itinuturing ko siyang higit pa sa kaibigan, para ko na siyang **kapatid**.","translation":"I consider him more than a friend, he's like a **sibling** to me."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pulbos na nalalabi matapos masunog nang lubusan ang isang bagay. Tumutukoy rin ito sa kulay na nasa pagitan ng itim at puti.
original_explanation: That dusty stuff left after a good inuman bonfire or what you get when your toast is forgotten. It's also the color of your soul during Monday meetings. 'Abo' is the aftermath, the residue, the official color of 'ay, sunog!'
usage_notes: Can refer to literal ash (from fire, volcanoes, cigarettes) or the color gray. The context usually makes the meaning clear.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **abo** mula sa bulkan ang mga bubong ng bahay.","translation":"The roofs of the houses were full of **ash** from the volcano."},{"sentence":"Gusto ko ng t-shirt na kulay **abo**.","translation":"I want a **gray** colored t-shirt."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos o pangyayari na paulit-ulit na nagaganap o bumabalik sa pinagmulan.
original_explanation: 'Yung ex mong pabalik-balik sa buhay mo. Akala mo okay na, biglang magpaparamdam ulit. Parang traffic sa EDSA, you keep going back and forth but never really moving forward. Also, the feeling you get when you forgot your wallet and you're already at the mall entrance.
usage_notes: Describes a repetitive action of coming and going.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pabalik-balik** siya sa kusina para tingnan kung luto na ang sinaing.","translation":"He kept going **back and forth** to the kitchen to check if the rice was cooked."},{"sentence":"Nakakahilo ang **pabalik-balik** na biyahe sa barko.","translation":"The **back and forth** boat trip is dizzying."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng pagiging buhol-buhol, magulo, o pagkakaroon ng maraming problema.
original_explanation: Your earphones after being in your pocket for 5 seconds. Your lovelife. The plot of a Filipino teleserye involving amnesia, long-lost twins, and a contested inheritance. Anything that's complicated, messy, and hard to untangle is a 'kagusutan'.
usage_notes: Can be used for both physical tangles (like threads) and abstract complications (like problems or conflicts).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinusubukang ayusin ng mga pulitiko ang **kagusutan** sa kanilang partido.","translation":"The politicians are trying to fix the **complication** in their party."},{"sentence":"Ang **kagusutan** ng sinulid ay nagpabagal sa kanyang pagtatahi.","translation":"The **tangle** of the thread slowed down her sewing."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging masaya at nasisiyahan sa kung anuman ang mayroon; walang hinahangad na iba o higit pa.
original_explanation: Ito yung state of mind mo kapag sahod day tapos nakabayad ka na ng lahat ng bills, may natira pa for milk tea. You're not aiming to be a billionaire, you just want peace of mind and a stable internet connection. Yung tipong, "Okay na ako dito."
usage_notes: Often used to describe a state of simple happiness and satisfaction with one's current situation. Sometimes spelled as 'kuntento'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kontento** na ako sa simpleng buhay basta't kasama ko ang aking pamilya.","translation":"I am **content** with a simple life as long as I am with my family."},{"sentence":"Mukhang **kontento** na ang pusa sa bago niyang higaan.","translation":"The cat seems **content** with its new bed."}]

translation: to invite; to ask someone out
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-anyaya o pag-imbita sa isang tao na sumama sa isang lugar, gawain, o kaganapan.
original_explanation: The ultimate "sana all" moment. Ito yung aabangan mong gawin ng crush mo. "Gusto mo bang kumain sa labas?" o "Tara, kape tayo?" It's the first step to either a beautiful relationship or a painful "friend zone" destination. To **ayain** someone is to take a leap of faith. Be brave, bes!
usage_notes: Ang salitang ugat na 'aya' para sa 'ayain' ay nangangahulugang 'imbita' at iba ito sa pangngalan na 'aya' na nangangahulugang 'yaya' o 'nanny'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Balak kong **ayain** si Maria na manood ng sine sa Sabado.","translation":"I plan to **ask** Maria **out** to watch a movie on Saturday."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **ayain** ang lahat ng ating mga kaibigan para sa salu-salo.","translation":"Don't forget to **invite** all our friends to the party."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpapakalma o pag-aalis ng galit, lungkot, o pag-aalala ng isang tao.
original_explanation: This is what you do when your friend is having a major 'hugot' moment. You buy them milk tea, listen to their rants, and say "Everything will be okay." It's emotional damage control. It's about making someone's 'loob' (inner self) 'lubag' (subside, calm down).
usage_notes: A compound verb. The noun form 'palubag-loob' can mean 'a consolation prize' or 'a conciliatory gesture'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagpapalubag-loob** ang ina sa kanyang umiiyak na anak.","translation":"The mother is **consoling** her crying child."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang magbigay ng regalo bilang paraan ng **pagpapalubag-loob** sa nagtatampong kasintahan.","translation":"He tried to give a gift as a way of **appeasing** his sulking girlfriend."}]

translation: to bake a cake; to have cake
meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagluluto ng keyk o ang pagkain nito bilang bahagi ng isang selebrasyon o meryenda.
etymology: From mag- (verb-forming prefix) + keyk (Tagalog spelling of English 'cake').
original_explanation: A very 21st-century Taglish verb. "Tara, mag-keyk tayo!" is the modern-day invitation for "Let's celebrate!" or "Let's have merienda!" It's what you do for birthdays, anniversaries, or just because you passed a stressful exam and deserve a slice of Red Ribbon or Goldilocks.
usage_notes: A clear example of code-switching becoming a standard colloquial word. Highly informal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sige na, **magkeyk** na lang tayo para sa birthday mo.","translation":"Come on, let's just **have cake** for your birthday."},{"sentence":"Marunong ka bang **magkeyk** ng sarili mong ube macapuno?","translation":"Do you know how **to bake** your own ube macapuno **cake**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng sakit na bulutong-tubig, isang nakahahawang karamdaman na nagdudulot ng mga makakating butlig sa balat.
original_explanation: Remember that itchy, can't-go-to-school, can't-play-outside part of your childhood? That's when you 'magkabulutong'. It's the official 'bawal maligo' and 'pahiran ng Caladryl' season of your life. A rite of passage for almost every Filipino kid.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to getting chickenpox ('bulutong-tubig').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Karamihan sa mga bata ay **nagkabulutong** na.","translation":"Most of the children have already **had chickenpox**."},{"sentence":"Pinayuhan siya ng doktor na magpahinga dahil siya ay **nagkabulutong**.","translation":"The doctor advised him to rest because he **got chickenpox**."}]

translation: to mock; to ridicule; to scorn
meaning_filipino: Insultuhin o laitin sa paraang mapanukso, mapang-uyam, o may halong paghamak.
original_explanation: This is what bashers do online. It's not just simple criticism ('puna'); it's making fun of someone with sarcasm and contempt. When you post a new profile pic and your 'friend' comments, 'Wow, filter pa more!' – that's them trying to tuyain you. It's teasing with a mean streak.
usage_notes: Implies a level of sarcasm and scorn, stronger than 'asarin' (to tease) and similar to 'uyamin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **tuyain** ang kanyang mga pangarap dahil lamang iba ito sa iyo.","translation":"Do not **mock** his dreams just because they are different from yours."},{"sentence":"Madalas siyang **tuyain** ng kanyang mga kaklase dahil sa kanyang kakaibang pananamit.","translation":"He is often **ridiculed** by his classmates because of his unique way of dressing."}]

translation: to fold over, to turn (a page)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbaligtad o pagtiklop ng isang patag na bagay, tulad ng pahina ng libro. Maaari ring mangahulugang pagtakip.
original_explanation: Imagine you're speed-reading a physical book (a rare activity these days) and you're just flipping through the pages—that's 'taklip'. Or when you quickly cover something to hide it from your chismosa Tita. It’s a quick, light covering or flipping action.
usage_notes: Isang hindi gaanong karaniwang salita. Mas madalas gamitin ang 'tiklop' para sa pag-fold o 'lipat' para sa paglipat ng pahina.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **taklipin** ang pahina, baka mapunit.","translation":"Don't **turn** the page so roughly, it might tear."}]

translation: act of taking out, releasing, or venting
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-aalis, paglalabas, o pagpapahayag ng isang bagay mula sa loob, tulad ng gamit, emosyon, o saloobin.
original_explanation: This is the general term for taking something out. But when you add 'ng sama ng loob' or 'ng galit,' it becomes the Filipino version of venting. It's that 3 AM chat with your best friend where you unload all your work stress and relationship drama. The modern English term 'trauma dumping' is an extreme form of this, where the **paglalabas** is unsolicited, unfiltered, and overwhelms the listener. Think of it as venting versus unloading a whole cargo ship of feels without warning.
usage_notes: Context is key. "Paglalabas ng resibo" means exposing someone. "Paglalabas ng pelikula" means a movie release.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paglalabas** ng saloobin ay mahalaga para sa kalusugang pangkaisipan.","translation":"The **venting** of feelings is important for mental health."},{"sentence":"Nakatulong sa kanya ang **paglalabas** ng lahat ng kanyang hinanakit sa kaibigan.","translation":"The **act of releasing** all her grievances to her friend helped her."}]

meaning_filipino: Ipasailalim ang isang bagay, lugar, o tao sa seremonya ng bendisyon o pagbabasbas, karaniwang isinasagawa ng isang pari o ministro.
original_explanation: That thing your tita does when she gets a new car, a new house, or even a new ref. 'Kailangan nating pabindisyunan 'to!' It's asking a priest to sprinkle holy water on something to ward off evil spirits, bad vibes, or maybe just to make sure the car doesn't get towed.
usage_notes: Strongly associated with Roman Catholic practices in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bukas natin **pabibindisyunan** sa pari ang bago nating bahay.","translation":"We will **have** our new house **blessed** by the priest tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Ipinayo niyang **pabindisyunan** ang mga bagong rosaryo.","translation":"He advised to **have** the new rosaries **blessed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng takip o panakip sa isang bagay, karaniwan sa isang lalagyan upang ito ay maisara.
original_explanation: What your mom tells you to do with the pot of adobo on the stove so the flies don't have a fiesta. "Hoy, takluban mo 'yang ulam!" It's the official verb for 'putting a lid on it', both literally with food and figuratively with office tsismis.
usage_notes: Ang pokus ng pandiwa ay nasa bagay na tinatakpan. "Takluban mo ang kaldero." (Cover the pot).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**takluban** ang palayok para mas mabilis kumulo ang tubig.","translation":"Please **cover** the pot so the water will boil faster."}]

translation: a place for crossing, a crosswalk
meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o daanan na itinalaga para sa pagtawid ng mga tao, lalo na sa kalsada.
etymology: From 'tawid' (to cross), with reduplication and suffix '-an' indicating a place.
original_explanation: This is your best friend when facing EDSA: the pedestrian lane. It's that magical zebra-striped patch on the road where cars are *supposed* to stop for you. It's the designated spot to play real-life Frogger. The word itself suggests a place where many people 'will cross'.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'tawiran'. 'Pagtatawiran' can sometimes imply the future or habitual act of crossing at a specific place.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gamitin ninyo ang **pagtatawiran** upang makaiwas sa disgrasya.","translation":"Use the **crosswalk** to avoid accidents."},{"sentence":"May bagong gawang **pagtatawiran** malapit sa paaralan.","translation":"There is a newly built **place for crossing** near the school."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pag-aalis, pagbura, o pagpapahupa sa isang bagay, tulad ng alaala, sakit, uhaw, o galit.
original_explanation: This is what you try to do with your ex's memory after a breakup—the `pagpawi` of feelings. Or what a cold glass of water does to your thirst (`pagpawi ng uhaw`) after walking under the Manila sun. It's the act of making something disappear, whether it's a bad memory, a physical sensation, or a chalk drawing on the sidewalk. The ultimate "delete" button for life's troubles.
usage_notes: Can be used for both physical and abstract things (thirst, hunger, sorrow, memory).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang malamig na inumin ay para sa **pagpawi** ng kanyang uhaw.","translation":"The cold drink is for **quenching** his thirst."},{"sentence":"Tila mahirap ang **pagpawi** sa masasakit na alaala ng nakaraan.","translation":"It seems the **erasure** of painful memories from the past is difficult."}]

translation: a sharp glance; a glare; an eye-roll
meaning_filipino: Isang matalim o masamang tingin na nagpapahiwatig ng galit, pagkasuklam, o hindi pagsang-ayon.
original_explanation: The ultimate non-verbal "wala akong pake" or "kainis ka." It's the look your mom gives you when you ask for money after she just saw your Shopee delivery. It's the signature move of the kontrabida in every teleserye. An irap can sometimes speak louder than a thousand angry words.
usage_notes: This is the root word and noun form. The verb forms are 'umirap' (to glare) or 'irapan' (to glare at someone).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang matalim na **irap** ang isinukli niya sa aking pagbati.","translation":"She returned my greeting with a sharp **glare**."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko napigilan ang **irap** ko nang marinig ko ang kanyang dahilan.","translation":"I couldn't stop my **eye-roll** when I heard his excuse."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng pagkakatugma o kaaya-ayang kombinasyon ng mga tunog, kulay, o elemento.
etymology: From Spanish 'armonía' (harmony). The prefix 'may-' indicates possession or having the quality of.
original_explanation: Like a choir that's perfectly in tune, or when your outfit's colors just *work*. It's the opposite of your family's videoke night where everyone is singing a different song. It's the vibe of a team that actually collaborates instead of backstabbing.
usage_notes: Often used to describe music, relationships, or arrangements.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**May-armonia** ang pagkakaawit ng koro.","translation":"The choir's singing is **harmonious**."},{"sentence":"Naghahangad sila ng isang pamilyang **may-armonia**.","translation":"They long for a **harmonious** family."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi maaaring palitan o baguhin; permanente o pinal.
etymology: From 'di-' (not) + 'ma-' (ability prefix) + future tense 'babago' from the root 'bago' (new, change).
original_explanation: This is your 'tita' who still thinks you need to get married, no matter how many times you tell her you're happy with your career. Her opinion is di-mababago. It's also that final, submitted report to your boss at 5 PM on a Friday. No turning back.
usage_notes: Can refer to decisions, facts, or inherent qualities.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang desisyon ng korte ay pinal at **di-mababago**.","translation":"The court's decision is final and **unchangeable**."},{"sentence":"May mga bagay sa nakaraan na, sa kasamaang-palad, ay **di-mababago**.","translation":"There are things in the past that, unfortunately, are **unchangeable**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang seksyon ng upuan sa isang lugar-palabasan tulad ng arena o teatro na matatagpuan sa mas mababang antas, karaniwang nasa pagitan ng seksyong patron at upper box.
original_explanation: 'Yung concert ticket na 'sakto lang.' Hindi kasing lapit ng VIP na amoy mo pabango ng idol mo, pero hindi rin kasing layo ng Gen Ad na mukhang langgam sila sa stage. Perfect spot para makita ang buong stage production nang hindi nababali ang leeg mo. Good view, but won't completely bankrupt you.
usage_notes: Specific to ticketing for events like concerts, sports games, etc. Often written as 'Lower Box'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Buti naka-secure ako ng **lowerbox** tickets para sa concert!","translation":"Good thing I was able to secure **lower box** tickets for the concert!"},{"sentence":"Mas maganda ang view sa **lowerbox** kaysa sa upperbox, siyempre.","translation":"The view in the **lower box** is better than the upper box, of course."}]

translation: mga artista, mga sikat na tao
meaning_filipino: Mga tanyag na tao, lalo na sa larangan ng pelikula, telebisyon, at musika.
original_explanation: Mga artista. 'Yung mga nakikita mo sa TV, pelikula, at sa mga billboard sa EDSA. Sila 'yung laging may chismis sa showbiz columns. 'Puno ng stars ang premiere night ng pelikula.'
usage_notes: Very common term in Philippine entertainment ('showbiz').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming malalaking **stars** ng ABS-CBN ang dumalo sa party.","translation":"Many big **stars** from ABS-CBN attended the party."},{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang maging isa sa mga sikat na **stars** balang araw.","translation":"She dreams of becoming one of the famous **stars** someday."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi nagtataglay ng karangalan, respeto sa sarili, o integridad.
original_explanation: Think of a politician caught stealing public funds who still runs for office. Or someone who cheats on their partner and blames the partner for it. Sila yung mga taong "kapal ng mukha" is an understatement. They have zero self-respect and will do anything, no matter how low, for personal gain.
usage_notes: A very strong and negative descriptor for a person's character.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang isang taong **walang-dangal** ay kayang ipagkanulo kahit ang sariling pamilya para sa pera.","translation":"A **dishonorable** person can betray even their own family for money."},{"sentence":"Isang gawaing **walang-dangal** ang pagnanakaw sa kaban ng bayan.","translation":"Stealing from the nation's treasury is a **shameless** act."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagliban sa klase o trabaho nang walang paalam o sapat na dahilan, karaniwan upang magliwaliw o gumala.
etymology: Mula sa kolokyal na Espanyol na 'la cuacha', na nangangahulugang 'pagbubulakbol' o 'to play hooky'.
original_explanation: The national pastime of students who are 'tinatamad' (feeling lazy). It’s cutting class to go to the mall, the computer shop, or your friend's house. The verb form, 'mag-lakwatsa', is the official term for 'gala na walang paalam'. It's the reason your mom used to say, 'Naku, puro ka **lakwatsa**, wala kang mararating!'
usage_notes: A very common, informal term. The verb is 'maglakwatsa'. A person who habitually plays truant is a 'lakwatsero' (male) or 'lakwatsera' (female).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itigil mo na 'yang **lakwatsa** at pumasok ka na sa klase.","translation":"Stop that **truancy** and go to class."},{"sentence":"Nahuli sila ng kanilang ina na nag-**lalakwatsa** sa halip na pumasok sa eskwela.","translation":"Their mother caught them **playing hooky** instead of going to school."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na kulisap na sumisipsip ng dugo at karaniwang matatagpuan sa mga higaan at siwang ng kasangkapan.
original_explanation: The tiny, invisible ninja that attacks you in your sleep and leaves you with itchy red spots that make you question your life choices and the cleanliness of your budget hotel. They're the reason you check the mattress before you even put your luggage down.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng kagat ng **surot** ang likod niya pagkatapos matulog sa lumang kutson.","translation":"His back was full of **bedbug** bites after sleeping on the old mattress."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating mag-pest control dahil may **surot** na sa bahay.","translation":"We need to call pest control because there are **bedbugs** in the house now."}]

meaning_filipino: Karagdagang oras ng pagtatrabaho na lampas sa regular na takdang oras; ang bayad para sa naturang karagdagang trabaho.
original_explanation: Also known as "OT." The reason why BPO agents have a weird body clock and why you can afford that extra milk tea. It's that love-hate relationship where you sacrifice your social life for "OT pay." A staple of Philippine work culture. "Boss, pa-approve ng overtime!"
usage_notes: Often abbreviated as "OT". Can be used as a verb with Filipino affixes, e.g., "nag-OT," "mag-o-OT."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong mag-**overtime** mamaya para matapos ang report.","translation":"I need to work **overtime** later to finish the report."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang nakuha niyang **overtime** pay noong nakaraang buwan.","translation":"He got a big **overtime** pay last month."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hindi sinasadyang pagbahin dahil sa isang panlabas na salik, tulad ng alikabok o matapang na amoy.
original_explanation: That moment when you're cleaning your room after a year and the alikabok (dust) attacks. Bigla ka na lang 'Hatchoo!' You've been mapabahin-ed. It's an involuntary action, a surprise party in your nose that you didn't ask for.
usage_notes: The 'mapa-' prefix indicates an involuntary or triggered action. One doesn't choose to sneeze; something makes them sneeze.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Napabahin** ako dahil sa pulbos na kumalat sa hangin.","translation":"I was **made to sneeze** by the powder that spread in the air."},{"sentence":"Kapag nakakaamoy ako ng paminta, palagi akong **napapabahin**.","translation":"When I smell pepper, I am always **made to sneeze**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang marahan at tuloy-tuloy na paghaplos o pagdampi, karaniwang gamit ang palad, upang magbigay-ginhawa, magpakita ng pagmamahal, o magpakinis ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: The feeling of Vicks VapoRub being gently spread on your back when you have a cold. It's the comforting stroke your lola gives your hair. It’s not a quick pat; it’s a long, soothing, 'aaah, sarap' kind of touch.
usage_notes: Often associated with comfort, care, or applying ointments. Can also refer to a stroke of a paintbrush or the caress of the wind.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **hagod** ng ina sa likod ng anak ay nakapagpakalma rito.","translation":"The mother's **gentle stroke** on her child's back calmed him down."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang malamig na **hagod** ng hangin sa kanyang balat.","translation":"She felt the cool **caress** of the wind on her skin."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang de-motor na nagpapaikot ng isang piraso ng materyal (tulad ng kahoy o metal) sa isang aksis upang mabigyan ito ng hugis sa pamamagitan ng pagputol, pagpapakinis, o pagbubutas.
original_explanation: This is the OG machine for your tito's DIY projects. The 'makinang-panturno' is what they use to shape wood or metal by spinning it super fast and carving it. Think of it as a potter's wheel, but for hard materials and way more dangerous. It's how they make those perfectly round table legs or custom metal parts.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa pagkakarpintero, paggawa ng metal, at inhinyeriya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng **makinang-panturno** upang gawin ang paa ng mesa.","translation":"He used a **lathe machine** to make the table leg."},{"sentence":"Ingatan ang kamay kapag nagpapatakbo ng **makinang-panturno**.","translation":"Be careful with your hands when operating a **lathe machine**."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang lugar na malawak, maaliwalas, at may sapat na espasyo at liwanag; maaari ring tumukoy sa isang pakiramdam na magaan at walang alalahanin.
original_explanation: Ito yung feeling pagkatapos mong mag-general cleaning. Yung bahay mo, biglang ang laki tingnan. Pwede rin sa isip, yung tipong walang deadlines, walang utang, walang kaaway. That "uncluttered" vibe, for your room or your mind. Ah, maliwalas!
usage_notes: Often used to describe physical spaces (rooms, sky) or a state of mind/feeling. It combines the sense of being spacious ('maluwag') and bright ('maliwanag').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sarap tumira sa bahay na **maliwalas** at mahangin.","translation":"It feels so good to live in a house that is **spacious** and airy."},{"sentence":"Naging **maliwalas** ang kanyang pakiramdam matapos magbakasyon.","translation":"His feeling became **serene** (light/untroubled) after going on vacation."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bilang na 500; katumbas ng limang daan, na ipinapahayag bilang isang salita.
original_explanation: A more poetic or formal way of saying 'limang-daan'. You might hear this in old songs or when someone's trying to sound fancy while counting money. It's the 'Shakespearean' version of 500.
usage_notes: Less common in everyday speech than 'limang-daan', but still understood. It's a single, contracted word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang halaga nito ay **limandaan** piso.","translation":"Its price is **five hundred** pesos."},{"sentence":"Mahigit **limandaan** taon na ang nakalipas.","translation":"More than **five hundred** years have passed."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng paputok na mabilis na tumataas sa himpapawid bago sumabog sa isang makulay na liwanag at tunog.
original_explanation: The main character of every New Year's Eve celebration. It goes up, makes a big bang, looks pretty for a few seconds, and then it's gone. A lot like your 13th-month pay. O 'yung mabilis na "spark" n'yo ng ka-talking stage mo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagliwanag ang kalangitan dahil sa mga makukulay na **kuwitis** noong Bagong Taon.","translation":"The sky lit up with colorful **fireworks** on New Year's."}]

translation: To shut one's mouth; to keep quiet
meaning_filipino: Isang idyomatikong pahayag na nangangahulugang manahimik, huwag magsalita, o ilihim ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'shhh' command. This is what you're told when you're about to spill the tea at the wrong time. It's the Filipino version of 'zip it,' often used to prevent secrets from turning into headlines on the barangay's chismis network.
usage_notes: A common command or piece of advice. Can be used sternly or jokingly.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas mabuting **itikom ang bibig** kaysa magsalita ng masama sa kapwa.","translation":"It's better to **keep quiet** than to speak ill of others."},{"sentence":"Sinabihan siya ng abogado na **itikom ang bibig** tungkol sa kaso.","translation":"The lawyer told him to **keep his mouth shut** about the case."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng masinsinang pagbanlaw upang maalis ang lahat ng dumi o sabon; maaari ring tumukoy sa paghalungkat o paghahanap sa loob ng isang lalagyan.
original_explanation: This has two flavors. 1) The 'OC sa laba' mode: It's that final, super-thorough rinse of your clothes to make sure every last bit of Surf is gone, usually involving a lot of squeezing. 2) The 'Hala, nasaan na yung susi?' mode: It's the frantic rummaging through your bag, turning it upside down, looking for that one thing you can't find. Both involve a desperate, thorough search.
usage_notes: The 'rummaging' sense is more common in some regions. The 'rinsing' sense is related to cleaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siguraduhin ang masinsinang **paghughog** sa mga damit para walang matirang sabon.","translation":"Ensure the thorough **rinsing** of clothes so that no soap is left."},{"sentence":"Sa kanyang **paghughog** sa lumang baul, nakakita siya ng mga litrato.","translation":"In her **rummaging** through the old chest, she found photographs."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tradisyonal na paraan ng panggagamot kung saan gumagamit ng mga baso o tasa na pinaiinit upang lumikha ng vacuum sa balat, na pinaniniwalaang nagpapabuti sa daloy ng dugo at nag-aalis ng 'lamig' sa katawan.
original_explanation: This is the Tita-approved solution for when you're feeling 'nalamigan' or just generally unwell. It involves turning your back into a relief map of circular purple marks using heated glasses. It looks painful, but for many, it's the ultimate 'ginhawa' feeling, like finally logging off after a toxic day at work.
usage_notes: Often done with a coin (kerik) or a massage. The dark marks are believed to indicate where 'lamig' (cold/wind) was extracted.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpa-**bentosa** ako kahapon kasi masama ang pakiramdam ko.","translation":"I had **cupping therapy** yesterday because I was feeling unwell."},{"sentence":"Ang likod niya ay puno ng mga bilog na marka dahil sa **bentosa**.","translation":"His back is full of circular marks because of the **cupping therapy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagtitipon para sa pagdarasal, karaniwang para sa isang yumaong miyembro ng pamilya o para sa isang espesyal na intensyon.
original_explanation: This is the traditional Filipino prayer session, usually for nine days (pasiyam) after someone passes away. It's a mix of solemn prayer, community gathering, and, let's be honest, lots of food (merienda). It’s where Tita Marites gets all the latest chismis while reciting the rosary.
usage_notes: The 'pa-' prefix here indicates "to cause" or "to have something done," so 'padasal' means to have prayers said. It can refer to the event itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-organisa ang pamilya ng isang **padasal** para sa ikasiyam na araw ng pagkamatay ng kanilang lola.","translation":"The family organized a **prayer gathering** for the ninth day after their grandmother's death."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagyapak o pag-apak ng maraming tao sa isa't isa o sa isang bagay, kadalasan sa paraang magulo at walang pag-iingat. Sa matalinhagang kahulugan, ito ay paninira sa kapwa upang umangat.
original_explanation: Literally, it's what happens in the MRT during rush hour when everyone's trying to get in or out. Figuratively, it's the 'crab mentality' in action. 'Yung sisiraan mo 'yung ka-team mo sa boss para ikaw ang ma-promote. It's the ruthless game of stepping on others to get ahead.
usage_notes: Can be literal (physical trampling) or figurative (social/career backstabbing). The suffix '-an' here implies a reciprocal or collective action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng **pagtatapakan** sa gitna ng gulat na mga manonood.","translation":"There was a **trampling** amidst the panicked audience."},{"sentence":"Sa mundo ng korporasyon, hindi maiiwasan ang **pagtatapakan** para sa promosyon.","translation":"In the corporate world, **stepping on each other** for a promotion is unavoidable."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng ritmikong paggalaw o pagpintig, tulad ng sa puso. Ito ay nasa panahunang pangnagdaan.
original_explanation: This is the action your heart did when you saw your crush walk by. It's the 'dug-dug-dug' sound translated into a verb. But it's not just for love! Your head can also 'tumibok' (throb) when you have a killer migraine after staring at your screen for 12 hours straight.
usage_notes: Past tense verb. The root 'tibok' is the noun for heartbeat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Biglang **tumibok** nang mabilis ang puso ko dahil sa kaba.","translation":"My heart suddenly **beat** fast because of nervousness."},{"sentence":"Nang makita kita, muling **tumibok** ang puso kong dati'y nanahimik.","translation":"When I saw you, my heart, which was once quiet, **beat** again."}]

meaning_filipino: Matinding hirap, pasakit, o kalungkutan na nararanasan ng isang tao sa katawan o damdamin.
etymology: From Proto-Malayo-Polynesian `*dusa` ("sin, transgression"), which evolved to mean the consequence of sin, i.e., suffering.
original_explanation: This isn't just a bad day. This is full-on teleserye-level suffering. The kind where you're crying in the rain because you lost your job, your love life is a mess, and you have to pay off a massive debt. It's the "pasan ko ang daigdig" feeling. `Hirap` is the daily struggle; `dusa` is the soul-crushing agony.
usage_notes: A strong, dramatic word often used in literary, religious, or formal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tila walang katapusan ang **dusa** na kanyang pinagdadaanan.","translation":"The **suffering** she is going through seems endless."},{"sentence":"Ang pagiging malayo sa pamilya ay isang malaking **dusa** para sa mga OFW.","translation":"Being far from family is a great **hardship** for OFWs."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-apaw at pagtapon ng likido mula sa isang lalagyan dahil sa paggalaw o pagkapuno nito.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your coffee when the jeepney driver suddenly hits the brakes. Yung sabaw ng sinigang na tumatapon sa gilid ng bowl kasi napuno mo masyado. It's the messy, sudden splash of liquid escaping its container. Parang luha mo nung napanood mo 'yung ending ng 'Rewind'.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa malaking dami ng likidong natapon dahil sa paggalaw o sobrang pagkapuno, mas dinamiko kaysa sa simpleng 'tapon'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lumigwak** ang tubig mula sa balde nang mabilis siyang tumakbo.","translation":"The water **spilled over** from the bucket when he ran quickly."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng sunod-sunod na tunog sa isang bagay, karaniwan sa pinto, upang makuha ang atensyon ng nasa loob.
etymology: From 'katok' (knock) + '-in' (verb suffix indicating an action to be done to an object).
original_explanation: What you do to a door when the doorbell is broken or when you're trying to be polite before barging in. Also what your officemate does to your cubicle wall to ask if you're free for lunch. 'Huwag mo na akong katukin sa puso, bukas na 'yan para sa'yo.' (Don't knock on my heart anymore, it's already open for you.) #Hugot
usage_notes: The object of the verb is the thing being knocked on (e.g., 'katukin ang pinto' - to knock on the door).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **katukin** mo ang pinto ni Lola at tanungin kung gising na siya.","translation":"Please, **knock** on Grandma's door and ask if she's awake."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mahiya, **katukin** mo lang ang bintana kung kailangan mo ng tulong.","translation":"Don't be shy, just **knock** on the window if you need help."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagnanakaw nang malakihan at may karahasan, karaniwang tumutukoy sa pagnanakaw sa yaman ng bayan o sa isang grupo ng tao.
original_explanation: This isn't just simple snatching. This is next-level, mega-scale pagnanakaw. Think pirates looting a ship or corrupt officials stealing public funds. 'Pag may **nandambong** sa kaban ng bayan, apektado ang budget para sa ayuda at infrastructure. It's the ultimate 'Sana all' in the worst possible way.
usage_notes: Strongly associated with large-scale theft, especially graft and corruption (plundering public funds). It's a word you'd see in news headlines about politics.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga opisyal na napatunayang **nandambong** sa kaban ng bayan ay dapat managot.","translation":"The officials proven to have **plundered** the nation's coffers must be held accountable."},{"sentence":"Kasaysayan ang maghuhusga sa mga **mandarambong**.","translation":"History will judge the **plunderers**."}]

translation: Act of putting into the mouth; taking on a challenge
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglalagay ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay pagkain, sa loob ng bibig. Sa matalinhagang paraan, ito ay tumutukoy sa pagharap sa isang mahirap o mapanganib na sitwasyon.
original_explanation: Literally, it's taking a bite of that extra rice. Figuratively, it's accepting that rush project your boss offered you on a Friday afternoon. 'Sure, I can do it!' you say, while your inner self is screaming. It's taking a risk, whether it's trying a new, exotic street food or accepting a job you're not 100% qualified for.
usage_notes: Has both a literal meaning (eating) and a common figurative meaning (taking a risk/challenge). The context determines the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **pagsubo** pa lang, alam na niyang masarap ang luto.","translation":"Just one **mouthful**, and he already knew the dish was delicious."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagsubo** niya sa bagong posisyon ay isang malaking hamon.","translation":"His **taking on** the new position is a big challenge."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi makapirmi o makapanatili sa isang lugar; malikot o laging gumagalaw.
etymology: From 'di-' (not) + 'mapirme' (to be able to stay still/firm), from Spanish 'firme' (firm).
original_explanation: A toddler who just drank a bottle of Coke. Or your friend who has had five jobs in the last two years. They just can't stay in one place, literally or figuratively. 'Saan na naman ang lakad mo? Di ka talaga mapirme!' It's the opposite of a house plant.
usage_notes: Can describe physical restlessness (fidgeting) or a tendency to move around a lot (from places, jobs, etc.).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang batang iyon ay **di-mapirme** sa kanyang upuan.","translation":"That child is **unable to stay still** in his seat."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa pagiging **di-mapirme**; laging lumilipat ng tirahan.","translation":"She's known for being **restless**; always moving residences."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na mahina ang ulo, mabagal umunawa, o may katigasan ng pag-iisip.
etymology: From Spanish "cabezote," augmentative of "cabeza" (head), meaning "big head" but used to imply stubbornness or dullness.
original_explanation: A throwback insult, parang ninuno ng "bobo" o "shunga." Ito ‘yung kaklase mong sampung beses mo nang in-explain ‘yung math problem pero ang sagot pa rin niya, "ha?". Sounds like a character from a Jose Rizal novel, probably because it is.
usage_notes: Considered an old-fashioned or literary term. It carries a strong negative connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinawag siyang **kabisote** ng kanyang guro dahil hindi niya makuha ang aralin.","translation":"His teacher called him a **blockhead** because he couldn't get the lesson."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **kabisote** at pakinggan mo ang payo ng mas nakatatanda.","translation":"Don't be a **dullard** and listen to the advice of elders."}]

translation: will act like a man; will become a man
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-aasal na parang lalaki; o ang pagbabago tungo sa pagiging isang ganap na lalaki o pagkakaroon ng mga katangiang panlalaki.
etymology: Future tense of `maglaki`. From `mag-` + `la` (repeated first syllable of root) + `laki` (big, great; often implying 'man').
original_explanation: This is often said to a young boy who's starting to show signs of maturity (or is expected to). "Hoy, binata ka na, **maglalaki** ka na dapat!" (Hey, you're a young man now, you should start acting like one!). It can also be used humorously for a girl who's acting tough or "unladylike", like a tomboy. It’s about embodying the stereotypical traits of being a ‘lalaki’ (man).
usage_notes: Can be used to mean 'to grow bigger' in some contexts, but more commonly 'to act like a man'. The context is key. `Lalaki` also means 'man' or 'male'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kapag tumuntong ka na sa tamang edad, inaasahang ikaw ay **maglalaki** na.","translation":"When you reach the right age, you are expected **to become a man**."},{"sentence":"\"Tigilan mo na ang pag-iyak, **maglalaki** ka dapat,\" sabi ng ama sa anak.","translation":"\"Stop crying, you should **act like a man**,\" the father told his son."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkakaroon ng mabigat na damdamin, pag-aalala, o hindi mapakali dahil sa isang suliranin o masamang pangitain.
etymology: From na- + reduplication of the first two syllables 'baba' + bagabag (anxiety, trouble).
original_explanation: This is next-level "worried." It's that 3 AM feeling when your brain won't shut up about your deadlines, your bills, and that awkward thing you said in 2012. You're not just thinking, you're nababagabag. It’s the official feeling of "Sunday Scaries" before a tough work week.
usage_notes: A deeper, more intense word for being worried or anxious. Can function as a verb (is feeling troubled) or an adjective (is troubled).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nababagabag** ang kanyang kalooban dahil hindi niya makontak ang kanyang anak.","translation":"He/She is **feeling troubled** because he/she cannot contact his/her child."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mabagabag**, malulutas din natin ang problemang ito.","translation":"Don't be **anxious**, we will solve this problem eventually."}]

translation: to have someone bring something up; to ask someone to carry something upwards
meaning_filipino: Isang pakiusap o utos na iakyat o dalhin ang isang bagay sa mas mataas na lugar. Karaniwang ginagamit sa anyong pautos.
original_explanation: This is what you shout to someone downstairs when you're on the second floor and too lazy to go down yourself. "Hoy, **pasampa** naman nitong kape ko!" (Hey, can you bring my coffee up here?). It's the official command of the tamad-bumaba-ng-hagdan club.
usage_notes: Often used as a command or request. The full verb form would be 'ipasampa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pasampa** nga ng mga pinamili ko sa taas.","translation":"Please **bring** my groceries **upstairs**."},{"sentence":"Narinig ko siyang sumigaw, '**Pasampa** ng meryenda!'","translation":"I heard him shout, '**Bring up** the snacks!'"}]

translation: to pound, to crush, to husk
meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng pandikdik o halo upang durugin, pulbusin, o tanggalan ng balat ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay butil tulad ng palay.
original_explanation: The original food processor. It's what you do with a giant mortar and pestle (lusong at halo) to turn palay into bigas, or garlic into a paste. It's a full-body workout that results in food. Think of it as manually grinding your coffee beans, but for rice.
usage_notes: Strongly associated with pounding rice or other grains in a large mortar (lusong).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sila ay maagang gumising para **bumayo** ng palay.","translation":"They woke up early to **pound** rice grains."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **bumayo** ng sili at bawang para sa sawsawan.","translation":"You need to **pound** chili and garlic for the dipping sauce."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang laro kung saan may isang 'taya' na humahabol sa ibang manlalaro upang 'mahuli' sila; isang pangkalahatang paghahabolan.
original_explanation: The official sport of your childhood, usually ending with a scraped knee or a friend crying 'ayoko na, dayà!'. As an adult, **habulan** is what you do with deadlines, bills, and the MRT train doors. 'Para kaming nagha-**habulan** ng pusa't daga sa office dahil sa dami ng trabaho.'
usage_notes: Can refer to the literal children's game 'tag' or any situation involving a mutual or chaotic chase.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglaro ng **habulan** ang mga bata sa parke hanggang hapon.","translation":"The children played the **game of tag** in the park until the afternoon."},{"sentence":"Naging parang **habulan** ng pusa't daga ang pag-aresto sa suspek.","translation":"The arrest of the suspect became like a cat-and-mouse **chase**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang solidong materyal kung saan ang mga atomo ay nakaayos sa isang maayos at paulit-ulit na padron, na kadalasang bumubuo ng mga anyong may patag na ibabaw at matutulis na anggulo. Tumutukoy din sa babasaging may mataas na kalidad.
original_explanation: Yung mamahaling baso sa bahay ng lola mo na bawal mong hawakan. Pwede ring 'yung mga healing stones na binibili mo online para sa 'good vibes'. Basta't makintab, malinaw, at mukhang mamahalin, malamang **kristal** 'yan. 'Crystal clear' ba kamo?
usage_notes: Can refer to high-quality glass, mineral formations, or metaphorical clarity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga chandelier sa mansyon ay gawa sa purong **kristal**.","translation":"The chandeliers in the mansion are made of pure **crystal**."},{"sentence":"Naniniwala siya sa kapangyarihan ng mga **kristal** para sa paggaling.","translation":"She believes in the healing power of **crystals**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong gumagamit ng labis na papuri o pambobola, karaniwan sa isang taong may kapangyarihan, upang makuha ang pabor nito.
etymology: From 'mapag-' (prefix indicating inclination) + 'langis' (oil). The metaphor is of 'oiling' or 'greasing' someone up with flattery to make things go smoothly for oneself.
original_explanation: The classic 'sipsip'. This is the office mate who laughs way too hard at the boss's bad jokes or the classmate who's always saying 'Ang galing niyo po, Ma'am/Sir!'. They use flattery like it's a weapon to climb the social or corporate ladder. Their tongue is practically brown from all the bootlicking.
usage_notes: A common and very descriptive term for a sycophant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi kinagigiliwan ng mga katrabaho ang empleyadong **mapaglangis** sa kanilang amo.","translation":"The co-workers do not like the employee who is **sycophantic** towards their boss."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **mapaglangis** na pag-uugali ay halata sa lahat.","translation":"His **ingratiating** behavior is obvious to everyone."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal para sa "ina" o "nanay," na nabuo sa pamamagitan ng pagbabaligtad ng mga pantig ng salitang "mater."
etymology: Mula sa salitang balbal na pagbabaligtad ng mga pantig ng 'mater', na hango sa Espanyol na 'madre' (ina).
original_explanation: Galing sa '80s slang na "syllable-switching" (baliktad). 'Mater' (mother) naging **ermat**. Ito ang cool na tawag mo sa nanay mo 'pag kasama ang tropa. "Tol, bawal ako lumabas, high-blood si **ermat**." Siya ang original na Google, ATM, at Waze ng buhay mo.
usage_notes: Salitang balbal o slang. Lubhang impormal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Humingi ka ng pera sa **ermat** mo.","translation":"Ask for money from your **mother**."},{"sentence":"Ang sarap ng luto ng **ermat** ko, pre.","translation":"My **mom's** cooking is delicious, bro."}]

translation: just kidding, not kidding; half-meant joke
meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyon na ginagamit pagkatapos ng isang pahayag upang linawin kung ito ay isang biro (char) o isang seryosong sinasabi (not char). Madalas, ito ay paraan upang sabihin ang isang bagay na totoo sa paraang pabiro.
etymology: Derived from the beki/swardspeak term 'charot' or 'char,' meaning 'just kidding.' The 'not char' is a direct, English-influenced negation.
original_explanation: The ultimate get-out-of-jail-free card for saying something brutally honest. You drop a truth bomb, then quickly add 'char!' to soften the blow. But then you add 'not char' to say, 'Yeah, I actually meant that.' It's the verbal equivalent of testing the waters. 'Ang taba mo na, char! ...not char.' It's peak Filipino passive-aggressiveness, but make it cute.
usage_notes: A very modern, conversational phrase used to navigate social situations where one wants to be honest without being confrontational.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"I think I'm in love with you, **char not char**.","translation":"I think I'm in love with you, **half-kidding, half-serious**."},{"sentence":"Gusto ko nang mag-resign. **Char not char**!","translation":"I want to resign already. **Kidding, not kidding**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang marka na binubuo ng dalawang linyang nagkurus (X). Ginagamit upang ipahiwatig ang kamalian, pagtanggal, o pagpili.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na "equis", ang pangalan ng titik na "x".
original_explanation: It's the letter 'X' used as a symbol. Yung marka sa test paper mo 'pag mali ang sagot. O yung "X" na nilalagay sa box sa balota. Sa modern slang, 'pag "ekis" ka na sa isang tao, it means you're out of their life, cancelled ka na. "Ekis na kami ng ex ko."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagyan mo ng **ekis** ang maling sagot.","translation":"Put an **X-mark** on the wrong answer."},{"sentence":"May malaking pulang **ekis** sa pinto, bawal pumasok.","translation":"There's a big red **cross mark** on the door, entry is forbidden."}]

meaning_filipino: Labis ang linamnam o kasiya-siyang lasa; sukdulan sa sarap.
etymology: From the intensifier prefix "napaka-" and the root word "sarap" (delicious, pleasant).
original_explanation: The feeling you get after the first bite of your lola's sinigang or a perfectly ripe mango. It's not just 'masarap', it's an experience that makes you close your eyes and say, "**Napakasarap**!" Food coma loading.
usage_notes: Primarily used for food, but can be used metaphorically to describe a very pleasant feeling or experience (e.g., "napakasarap matulog").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Napakasarap** ng luto mong adobo!","translation":"The adobo you cooked is **so delicious**!"},{"sentence":"**Napakasarap** sa pakiramdam na makapagtapos ng pag-aaral.","translation":"It's a **very wonderful** feeling to graduate."}]

translation: to do or handle two or more things at the same time
meaning_filipino: Pagsamahin o pagtugmain sa iisang panahon ang dalawa o higit pang gawain o bagay.
original_explanation: This is the multitasker's anthem. It's when you try to watch your K-drama while finishing your report for your BPO boss. 'Pinag-sabay ko' is the classic excuse. It's about timing things to occur simultaneously, often with chaotic results.
usage_notes: Focuses on the things/actions being done at the same time, whereas 'sabayan' focuses on the person being accompanied.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **sabayin** ang pag-aaral at pagtatrabaho.","translation":"He tried to **do** studying and working **at the same time**."},{"sentence":"Puwede bang **sabayin** na lang ang pagluto ng kanin at ulam para makatipid sa gas?","translation":"Can we just **cook** the rice and the viand **at the same time** to save on gas?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lahat ng bahagi na pinagsama-sama; ang kumpletong bilang o halaga; ang pangkalahatang diwa o buod.
original_explanation: This is the 'total' on your GrabFood receipt. It's what your team lead asks for in a meeting: 'Ano ang kabuuan ng report?' (What's the summary of the report?). It's the whole picture, not just one piece of the chismis. The opposite of 'isang piraso lang.'
usage_notes: Used to refer to the sum of parts, whether physical, numerical, or conceptual.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kabuuan** ng Pilipinas ay binubuo ng mahigit pitong libong isla.","translation":"The **entirety** of the Philippines is composed of over seven thousand islands."},{"sentence":"Sa **kabuuan**, naging matagumpay ang ating proyekto.","translation":"On the **whole**, our project was a success."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng libangan kung saan ang isang tao ay kumakanta kasabay ng isang music video na may nakasulat na liriko sa screen. Ito ay isang ebolusyon ng karaoke.
original_explanation: The national pastime of the Philippines. Ito yung dahilan kung bakit may 'My Way' killings at kung bakit alas-tres ng madaling araw ay may kumakanta pa rin ng 'Halik' sa kabilang kanto. Sa bawat handaan, hindi pwedeng mawala 'to. Kahit sintunado, basta galing sa puso, 100 points ka pa rin (sa score).
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'karaoke'. The defining feature is the presence of a music video, not just lyrics.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagrenta kami ng **videoke** para sa birthday party ni Lola.","translation":"We rented a **videoke** machine for Grandma's birthday party."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong agawin ang mikropono, turn ko nang kumanta sa **videoke**!","translation":"Don't grab the microphone, it's my turn to sing on the **videoke**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ilegal na nangangalakal o nagbebenta ng mga bagay, lalo na ng mga ipinagbabawal na gamot o ng mga tao (human trafficking).
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "diskarte" gone wrong. Not the friendly neighborhood tindera, but the villain in a primetime teleserye who deals with illegal stuff, from drugs to people. They're the reason your parents told you not to talk to strangers. The final boss of sketchy transactions.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng balita at batas, lalo na sa "human trafficker" o "drug trafficker".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahuli ng mga pulis ang kilabot na **trafficker** ng droga sa Maynila.","translation":"The police caught the notorious drug **trafficker** in Manila."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tangke sa ilalim ng lupa kung saan ang mga dumi mula sa bahay, tulad ng mula sa inidoro at lababo, ay tinitipon at unti-unting nabubulok sa pamamagitan ng pagkilos ng bakterya.
original_explanation: Eto yung underground VIP lounge para sa lahat ng ayaw mo nang makita ulit galing sa banyo mo. It's the final resting place of last night's bad decisions and sisig. Huwag mong apakan yung takip sa bakuran kung ayaw mong maging instant deep-sea diver ng... alam mo na.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa mga lugar na walang sentralisadong sistema ng alkantarilya o panmutsang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan na nating ipasipsip ang laman ng **septic tank** dahil puno na ito.","translation":"We need to have the contents of the **septic tank** pumped out because it's already full."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kariton o maliit na sasakyang de-gulong na ginagamit sa paghahanda at pagbebenta ng pagkain, karaniwan sa mga pampublikong lugar.
original_explanation: 'Yung modern version ng kariton ni Manong na nagbebenta ng fishball, kikiam, at kwek-kwek. Usually, mas "gourmet" ang tinda, like shawarma, sisig rice, o milk tea. Makikita mo 'to sa mga mall, BGC, o sa mga food park. It's the startup version of a restaurant.
usage_notes: A direct loanword from English, commonly used in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng siomai sa **foodcart** sa labas ng opisina.","translation":"I bought siomai from the **food cart** outside the office."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula lang siya sa isang maliit na **foodcart**, ngayon ay may restaurant na siya.","translation":"She just started with a small **food cart**, now she has her own restaurant."}]

translation: to move back; to slide back
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-urong o paggalaw nang paatras, kadalasan habang nakaupo o nasa isang partikular na posisyon.
original_explanation: That awkward little butt-scoot you do on a jeepney or a church pew to make space for someone else. 'Usod, 'pre.' It's a gesture of communal space-sharing, Filipino style.
usage_notes: Often used as a command in its root form ('usod' or 'pa-usod'). Synonymous with 'umurong' but often implies a smaller, sliding movement. The word 'usod' itself is rare, but the verb form 'umusod' and the command 'usod' are common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **umusod** ka nang kaunti para makaupo ako.","translation":"Please, **move back** a little so I can sit."},{"sentence":"Hindi **umusod** ang pila kahit isang pulgada.","translation":"The line didn't **move back** even an inch."}]

translation: to nail something onto; to fasten with a nail
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay o pagkakabit ng pako sa isang bagay o lugar.
etymology: Mula sa "pako" (nail) + hulaping "-an" (nagpapahiwatig ng lokasyon o obheto ng kilos).
original_explanation: The action version of 'pako'. It's what your dad does when he finally gets around to hanging that family picture on the wall. "Pakuan mo na 'yan!" is the command to stop procrastinating and just hammer the nail in already.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang pandiwa na tumutukoy sa kilos ng paggamit ng pako (nail).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **pakuan** itong poster sa pader.","translation":"Help me **nail** this poster onto the wall."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong laging sumasalungat o tumututol sa opinyon o mungkahi ng iba.
etymology: From Spanish 'contra' (against) with the Tagalog prefix 'pala-' (fond of doing).
original_explanation: That one friend in the group chat who replies 'No' to every suggestion. 'Tara, kain tayo sa Jollibee?' 'Ayoko, mas masarap sa McDo.' 'Okay, McDo?' 'Pass, diet ako.' They're the human embodiment of the 'Well, actually...' meme.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a personality trait. Can be slightly negative or teasing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang tanungin si Ana, **palakontra** 'yon palagi.","translation":"Don't bother asking Ana, she's always a **contrarian**."}]

translation: having a deformed or crippled hand/arm
meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang tao na may kapansanan o depekto sa kamay o braso, na nagiging sanhi ng pagiging hindi nito maigalaw nang maayos o pagkakaroon ng hindi karaniwang anyo.
original_explanation: Ito yung term na medyo luma na at 'di na masyadong politically correct ngayon. Pero dati, ito ang description sa isang taong may kapansanan sa kamay, parang kuluntoy o hindi buo ang daliri. Better use 'may kapansanan sa kamay' to be more respectful.
usage_notes: This term can be considered insensitive or archaic. It is better to use more descriptive and respectful language like 'may kapansanan sa kamay' (has a hand disability).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa isang aksidente noong bata pa, naging **komang** ang kanyang kaliwang kamay.","translation":"Due to an accident when he was young, his left hand became **crippled**."},{"sentence":"Pinagtawanan siya dahil **komang** daw siya, na labis niyang ikinalungkot.","translation":"He was laughed at for supposedly having a **maimed hand**, which made him very sad."}]

meaning_filipino: Isa pang pinaikling anyo ng salitang "baby," na katulad ng "bb" ay ginagamit sa mga di-pormal na pag-uusap, lalo na sa text at online chat.
original_explanation: A slightly more "effortful" version of 'bb' because it has one extra letter. It's the middle ground between the super-lazy 'bb' and the full 'baby'. It's the "I care enough to type 'y' but not 'a'" of terms of endearment.
usage_notes: Interchangeable with 'bb' but sometimes perceived as slightly more affectionate or "cuter".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Miss you na, **bby** ko.","translation":"I miss you already, my **bby** (baby)."},{"sentence":"Huwag magpagutom, **bby**.","translation":"Don't get hungry, **bby** (baby)."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng hayop na may malamig na dugo, karaniwang nangingitlog, at may balat na kaliskis o mga butong plato.
original_explanation: Mga kamag-anak ni Godzilla. Isipin mo 'yung mga buwaya, ahas, pagong, at butiki. Sila 'yung mga hayop na cold-blooded, parang 'yung ex mo. Kadalasan may kaliskis at nangangagat (minsan).
usage_notes: The English word "reptile" is also very common in casual conversation. "Reptil" is the Spanish-derived formal term used in academic or scientific contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang buwaya ay isang malaking **reptil** na matatagpuan sa mga ilog.","translation":"The crocodile is a large **reptile** found in rivers."},{"sentence":"Maraming takot sa mga **reptil** tulad ng ahas.","translation":"Many are afraid of **reptiles** like snakes."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging mas maayos, mas malusog, o pag-unlad mula sa isang naunang estado.
original_explanation: This is the 'glow-up' phase. It's when your internet connection finally stabilizes, your skin clears up after a breakout, or when you finally feel okay after a 'sana all' moment. It's the process of becoming 'mabuti'.
usage_notes: Commonly used to refer to health recovery or skill improvement.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ikinatuwa ng lahat ang mabilis na **pagbuti** ng kanyang kalusugan.","translation":"Everyone was happy about the quick **improvement** of his health."},{"sentence":"Makikita ang **pagbuti** sa iyong mga marka ngayong semestre.","translation":"An **improvement** in your grades can be seen this semester."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagtataglay ng mataas na karangalan, dangal, at integridad.
original_explanation: This is the 'walks the talk' energy. It's doing the right thing even when no one's watching, like returning a lost wallet with all the cash inside. It's the OFWs' quiet strength, the lolo's 'palabra de honor.' It’s having a clean conscience and a good name, which in the Philippines, is more valuable than gold.
usage_notes: Isang napakapositibo at iginagalang na katangian ng pagkatao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinakita niya ang kanyang **pagkamarangal** sa pamamagitan ng hindi pagtanggap sa suhol.","translation":"He showed his **integrity** by not accepting the bribe."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat o grupo ng labindalawang (12) piraso ng isang bagay.
