original_explanation: A group of twelve. The standard unit for buying eggs, donuts, or roses for your nililigawan. When you hear "isang dosena," you know you're getting 12 of something.
usage_notes: Ginagamit bilang isang yunit ng pagbibilang na katumbas ng labindalawa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng isang **dosena**ng itlog sa palengke.","translation":"I bought a **dozen** eggs at the market."},{"sentence":"Magkano ang isang **dosena**ng rosas ngayon?","translation":"How much is a **dozen** roses nowadays?"}]

translation: to be marked with spots; to be speckled
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagkakaroon ng mga batik o marka sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the 'action' version. It's what happens when you accidentally splash coffee on your white shirt. 'Ayan, na-batik-batikan na!' It can also mean to intentionally put spots on something. Basically, the 'how' or 'why' behind the 'batik-batik' state.
usage_notes: The '-an' suffix here indicates that the object is the recipient of the spots or marks.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **batik-batikan** ang pader na kakapinta lang.","translation":"Don't **put spots on** the newly painted wall."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang balat ay **batik-batikan** dahil sa araw.","translation":"Her skin **is speckled** because of the sun."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lihim na kasunduan o pagkakaisa ng dalawa o higit pang tao upang magsagawa ng isang ilegal, masama, o mapanlinlang na gawain.
etymology: From pag- (nominalizer) + sa- (reciprocal) + pakat (agreement, pact), with 'sapakatan' itself meaning conspiracy.
original_explanation: This is the plot of every political thriller and the reason for your trust issues. It's when your teammates secretly agree to make you the group leader so they can all chill. It’s what you suspect is happening when all the food stalls in the food court raise their prices at the same time. It's a secret group chat, but for evil.
usage_notes: A formal and serious term with strong negative and legal connotations. Synonymous with 'sabwatan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May hinala ang mga awtoridad na may naganap na **pagsasapakatan** upang manipulahin ang presyo ng bilihin.","translation":"The authorities suspect that there was a **collusion** to manipulate the price of goods."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagsasapakatan** laban sa gobyerno ay isang krimen na may mabigat na parusa.","translation":"**Conspiracy** against the government is a crime with a heavy penalty."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang biglaan at marahas na panginginig ng katawan, karaniwang sanhi ng matinding takot, pagkasuklam, o lagnat.
original_explanation: Ito yung mas intense na version ng panginginig. Hindi lang ito a-simple-shiver-from-the-cold. Ito yung parang na-electrocute ka sa gulat o dusa. Yung nakakita ka ng ipis na lumilipad papunta sa'yo? That's pangikig-worthy.
usage_notes: Implies a more intense or convulsive shudder than pangiki or panginginig.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **pangikig** ang dumaloy sa kanyang katawan nang makita ang multo sa dilim.","translation":"A **shudder** ran through his body when he saw the ghost in the dark."}]

translation: getting tired of; growing weary of
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkawala ng interes o sigla sa isang bagay, tao, o gawain dahil sa paulit-ulit na karanasan o pagkabigo.
etymology: From `pag-` (verbal noun prefix) + `sawa` (to be tired of, fed up).
original_explanation: That feeling when you've eaten the same adobo for three straight days. Or when you're finally over that crush who kept leaving you on 'seen.' It's the 'over it' stage of any relationship, food, or K-drama marathon. 'Sawa na ako.'
usage_notes: Describes a state of being fed up or bored with something or someone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **pagsasawa** sa paulit-ulit na trabaho, nagpasya siyang mag-resign.","translation":"Because of his **getting tired of** the repetitive job, he decided to resign."}]

translation: to put a layer/lining on something
meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng sapin o panakip sa ilalim upang maprotektahan ang ibabaw o gawing mas komportable.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you put a placemat on the table before your messy pamangkin eats. Or putting newspaper on the floor before painting. It's the "maglagay ka ng sapin" command from your mom to prevent a mess. In relationships, it's putting up a 'friend' layer first before admitting you have a crush.
usage_notes: Commonly used in household contexts for adding a protective or functional layer to a surface.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pasapinan** mo ng diyaryo ang sahig bago ka magpinta.","translation":"**Put a layer** of newspaper on the floor before you paint."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **pasapinan** ang kahon upang hindi mabasag ang laman.","translation":"The box needs **to be lined** so its contents won't break."}]

meaning_filipino: Lugar kung saan isinilang o lumaki ang isang tao; ang sariling bansa.
etymology: Kombinasyon ng 'tinubuan' (lugar kung saan tumubo o lumaki) at 'bayan' (bansa).
original_explanation: It's your OG hood, your birthplace, the place you rep no matter where you end up. It's the "probinsya" you miss when you're stuck in Manila traffic, or the Philippines itself when you're working abroad. The source of your ube cravings and your default karaoke accent.
usage_notes: Isang pormal at makabayang salita. Madalas gamitin sa mga tula, awit, at pormal na sanaysay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming Pilipino ang nangungulila sa kanilang **tinubuang-bayan**.","translation":"Many Filipinos long for their **homeland**."},{"sentence":"Isang karangalan ang paglingkuran ang **tinubuang-bayan**.","translation":"It is an honor to serve the **homeland**."}]

translation: to alternate; to cause to take turns
meaning_filipino: Ayusin o gawin sa paraang naghahalinhinan o salit-salitan ang dalawa o higit pang bagay o tao.
original_explanation: This is what you do with your kids to stop them from fighting over the iPad: 'Okay, 15 minutes ka, tapos 15 minutes siya. `Pagsalisihin` n'yo 'yan!' It's the official verb for 'mag-turnuhan kayo.' It can also mean to make things happen alternately, like work and rest days in a BPO agent's shifting schedule.
usage_notes: This usage of `salisi` is about alternation or taking turns, distinct from the more common 'acting in absence' meaning. Context determines the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **pagsalisihin** ang pag-inom ng gamot at pagkain.","translation":"It's necessary to **alternate** taking medicine and eating."},{"sentence":"Sinabi ng nanay na **pagsalisihin** na lang nila ang paggamit ng bisikleta.","translation":"The mother said that they should just **take turns** using the bicycle."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa halaga ng kredito na inilalagay sa isang prepaid mobile phone upang magamit sa pagtawag, pag-text, o paggamit ng data.
original_explanation: In the Philippines, load is life. It's not just data or call credits; it's the currency of communication, the lifeline for 'sana all' DMs, and the reason you're nice to your tita from the US. "Pa-load naman po" is a modern form of prayer. Running out of load during an important Mobile Legends match is a national tragedy.
usage_notes: Bagama't salitang Ingles, ito ay ganap nang bahagi ng pang-araw-araw na bokabularyong Filipino, partikular sa konteksto ng telekomunikasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ate, pabili pong **load**, regular 50.","translation":"Miss, I'd like to buy **prepaid mobile credit**, regular 50."},{"sentence":"Naubusan ako ng **load** kaya hindi ako nakapag-reply agad.","translation":"I ran out of **load**, that's why I couldn't reply right away."}]

meaning_filipino: Magsagawa ng pag-aalsa o paghihimagsik laban sa isang partikular na tao, pangkat, o sistema.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of rebellion. It's what happens when the BPO team has had enough of the unreasonable metrics. "Pag-alsahan na natin ang management!" might be whispered in the pantry. It's actively rising up against a specific target, be it a tyrannical boss or an unjust system.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang mga manggagawa na **pag-alsahan** ang mapang-aping pamunuan ng pabrika.","translation":"The workers decided to **revolt against** the oppressive factory management."},{"sentence":"Huwag ninyong **pag-alsahan** ang inyong mga magulang dahil lamang sa maliliit na hindi pagkakaunawaan.","translation":"Do not **rebel against** your parents just because of small misunderstandings."}]

translation: to be satisfied; to be met (a need)
meaning_filipino: Ang matugunan o mapunan ang isang pangangailangan, kagustuhan, o pamantayan.
original_explanation: This is the feeling when your sweldo finally comes and you can pay all your bills. Your needs have been 'masapatan'. It's when you're looking for a specific item on Shopee, and you finally find one that meets all your criteria (price, reviews, specs). That 'sakto lang' or 'this will do' feeling, but in verb form. It's about meeting a requirement or a need, not necessarily about being overjoyed, but about being sufficient.
usage_notes: Implies sufficiency or meeting a standard. 'Masapatan ang pangangailangan' (to meet the needs).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana'y **masapatan** ng tulong na ito ang kanilang mga pangangailangan.","translation":"I hope this help will be enough to **meet** their needs."},{"sentence":"Hindi **nasapatan** ng kanyang paliwanag ang mga tanong ng guro.","translation":"His explanation did not **satisfy** the teacher's questions."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagluto ng mga gulay sa pamamagitan ng pagpapakulo sa tubig na may kaunting pampalasa, karaniwan ay bagoong o isda.
original_explanation: It's a style of cooking that's basically "throw all the veggies in a pot with water and some bagoong and let it boil." It's the "bahala na si Batman" of veggie dishes. Healthy, but not exactly gourmet.
usage_notes: Refers to a specific type of Filipino vegetable stew, often with a fish or shrimp paste base.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naisipan ni nanay na **magbulanglang** ng mga natirang gulay sa pridyeder.","translation":"Mom decided to **cook** the leftover vegetables in the fridge **into a broth**."},{"sentence":"Masarap **magbulanglang** ng malunggay at kalabasa.","translation":"It's delicious to **cook** moringa and squash in a simple **broth**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malakas at malalim na iyak, daing, o ungal, karaniwan ng malalaking hayop tulad ng kalabaw o baka.
original_explanation: Yung iyak mo nung nalaman mong sold out na ang concert tickets ng paborito mong K-Pop group? 'Yan ang atungal. Hindi lang hikbi, kundi full-on, kapitbahay-rinig level na pag-iyak.
usage_notes: Often used hyperbolically for a person's loud, unrestrained crying.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig sa buong parang ang **atungal** ng kalabaw.","translation":"The **howl** of the water buffalo was heard across the entire field."},{"sentence":"Isang malakas na **atungal** ang pinakawalan niya nang malamang wala nang natirang ulam.","translation":"He let out a loud **bellow** when he found out there was no food left."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na bersyon ng salitang "probasyon," na tumutukoy sa isang panahon ng pagsubok sa trabaho o sa batas.
etymology: Pagbaybay sa Filipino ng salitang Ingles na "probation" o kolokyal na anyo ng "probasyon."
original_explanation: This is how your tita who loves to gossip pronounces "probation." It's the phonetic, palengke-friendly version. "Ano na, naka-probeyson pa rin ba 'yung pamangkin mo sa call center?" It's less formal, more chismis.
usage_notes: Considered a colloquial or non-standard spelling/pronunciation of 'probasyon'. More common in spoken language than in writing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagot, baka hindi ako pumasa sa **probeyson** ko, palagi akong late eh.","translation":"Oh no, I might not pass my **probation**, I'm always late."}]

translation: To surmise, to sense, to perceive
meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang maramdaman, maunawaan, o mahulaan ang isang bagay na hindi direktang sinasabi o ipinapakita.
original_explanation: Ito yung "spidey-sense" ng mga Pinoy. Yung feeling na alam mong may something fishy sa paligid kahit walang umaamin. When your friend says "Okay lang ako" but you can mahinagap the hugot and drama behind those three words. It's the ability to read between the lines of a cryptic FB post.
usage_notes: Often used in a more literary or formal context. It implies a subtle, intuitive understanding.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit hindi niya sabihin, **mahihinagap** mo sa kanyang mga mata ang lungkot na nararamdaman niya.","translation":"Even if she doesn't say it, you can **perceive** in her eyes the sadness she feels."},{"sentence":"Walang sinuman ang **nakahinagap** sa kanyang tunay na balak.","translation":"No one was able to **surmise** his true plan."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hindi kanais-nais na tunog o pakiramdam ng pagkaskas o pagkayod, lalo na sa mga ngipin.
etymology: From 'pang-' + 'ginggi', a probable onomatopoeic root for a grating sound, related to the sensation of teeth set on edge.
original_explanation: You know that feeling when someone scratches a fork on a plate? Or the sensation when you eat something super sour that makes your jaw feel weird? That's `pangginggi`. It's the cousin of `pangingilo` (that sensitive teeth feeling from cold stuff) but more for sounds and textures that make you cringe. It's the ASMR you *don't* want.
usage_notes: A very rare word, often replaced by 'pangingilo' or descriptive phrases. Its usage might be highly localized or archaic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman ko ang **pangginggi** sa aking mga ngipin nang marinig ko ang pagkayod ng bakal sa semento.","translation":"I felt a **grating sensation** in my teeth when I heard the scraping of metal on cement."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pag-aalis sa isang tao o bagay mula sa panganib, kapahamakan, o masamang kalagayan.
original_explanation: This is the Darna or Captain Barbell moment. It's the act of being a hero, whether it's a firefighter pulling someone from a burning building or you 'saving' your friend from a bad date by calling them with a fake emergency. The ultimate 'salamat, na-save mo ako!' situation.
usage_notes: Implies saving from danger, harm, or a negative situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagliligtas** sa mga hayop na na-trap sa baha ay isang bayaning gawain.","translation":"The **rescue** of the animals trapped in the flood is a heroic deed."},{"sentence":"Naging mabilis ang **pagliligtas** ng mga bumbero sa mga residente.","translation":"The firefighters' **act of saving** the residents was swift."}]

translation: to enrich; to cultivate; to make wealthy
meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagpapayaman, pagpapaunlad, o pagpapabuti sa isang bagay, tao, o kaalaman.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of "invest." It could mean literally making something richer (like adding more ingredients to a dish), but more often it's about developing or improving something. You `pagyamanin` your skills by upskilling, your vocabulary by reading, or your relationship by going on dates. It's the "grind" to level up yourself, your knowledge, or your bank account.
usage_notes: Used for both tangible wealth (money, resources) and intangible qualities (knowledge, culture, spirit).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat nating **pagyamanin** ang ating kaalaman sa sariling wika.","translation":"We should **enrich** our knowledge of our own language."},{"sentence":"**Pagyamanin** mo ang talentong ibinigay sa iyo ng Diyos.","translation":"**Cultivate** the talent that God gave you."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang umiikot na sisidlan, karaniwang yari sa metal na parang kulungan, na ginagamit sa pagbunot ng mga numero para sa raffle o lottery.
original_explanation: The official container of your hopes and dreams during the company Christmas party raffle. Dito umiikot ang kapalaran mo kung mananalo ka ng flat-screen TV o... another notepad. Ang heartbeat mo ay sumasabay sa pag-ikot ng tambyolo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lahat ay nakatingin sa **tampyolo** habang binubunot ang nanalong numero.","translation":"Everyone was looking at the **raffle drum** as the winning number was being drawn."}]

translation: to overpower, to conquer, to violate
meaning_filipino: Talunin o lupigin sa pamamagitan ng lakas o dahas; supilin. Maaari ring tumukoy sa sekswal na pananamantala.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "gahis" na nangangahulugang pagtagumpayan sa pamamagitan ng puwersa.
original_explanation: Think of it as the PG-13 version of 'gahasain' in some contexts, but it's much broader. 'Gahisin' is about overpowering someone or something, whether it's a rival company in a hostile takeover, an army conquering a city, or metaphorically, crushing someone's spirit. It has a strong connotation of unjust force.
usage_notes: Maaaring mangahulugang manakop, mang-api, o sa ilang konteksto, manggahasa. Ang kahulugan ay lubos na nakadepende sa konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng mananakop na **gahisin** ang mga katutubo.","translation":"The colonizer tried to **conquer** the natives."},{"sentence":"Hindi dapat hayaang **gahisin** ng takot ang ating mga pangarap.","translation":"Fear should not be allowed to **overpower** our dreams."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagsasaayos, pagkukumpuni, paglalagay sa tamang lugar, paglutas ng problema, o pagpapaganda sa sarili.
original_explanation: This word is a life-saver. It can mean fixing a broken appliance (pag-aayos ng aircon), cleaning your messy room (pag-aayos ng kwarto), settling a dispute (pag-aayos ng gulo), or getting ready for a date (pag-aayos ng sarili). It's the universal term for bringing something from a state of chaos to a state of 'ayos' (order).
usage_notes: A very versatile word with multiple related meanings depending on the context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahal ang singil para sa **pag-aayos** ng kotse.","translation":"The charge for the **fixing** of the car is expensive."},{"sentence":"Ang **pag-aayos** ng gusot sa pamilya ay hindi madali.","translation":"The **settlement** of the family's conflict is not easy."},{"sentence":"Maglaan ka ng oras para sa iyong sariling **pag-aayos**.","translation":"Set aside time for your personal **grooming**."}]

translation: To somersault; to turn over and over
meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit na pag-ikot o pagbaligtad ng katawan o isang bagay, tulad ng ginagawa sa himnastiko o kapag ang isang sasakyan ay naaksidente.
original_explanation: This is the action of a gymnast doing a floor routine, or a kid joyfully rolling down a grassy hill. 'Bumali-baligtad' is to turn over and over. On a darker note, it's also what a car does in a major highway accident. Figuratively, your stomach might 'bumali-baligtad' from extreme nervousness or 'kilig'.
usage_notes: The repetition in the word implies a repeated or continuous action of turning over.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwang-tuwa ang bata habang siya'y **bumabali-baligtad** sa kama.","translation":"The child was overjoyed while **somersaulting** on the bed."},{"sentence":"**Bumali-baligtad** ang sasakyan nang ilang beses bago ito tumigil.","translation":"The car **turned over and over** several times before it stopped."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-anyaya sa isang tao na dumalo sa isang pagtitipon, lugar, o kaganapan.
original_explanation: Yung sine-send mo sa group chat para yayain sila mag-Samgyup o mag-kape. "Guys, G?" 'Yan na 'yun. You're trying to imbitahin them. Kapag in-snob ka, seenzoned. Kapag sumama sila, success!
usage_notes: Ang pandiwang anyo ng 'imbita'. Madalas na ipinagpapalit sa 'anyayahan' o 'yayain'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Imbitahin** mo ang lahat ng kaibigan natin sa aking kaarawan.","translation":"**Invite** all our friends to my birthday."},{"sentence":"Sino ang dapat nating **imbitahin** sa kasal?","translation":"Who should we **invite** to the wedding?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging masama, baluktot ang moralidad, o tiwali. Ito ay tumutukoy sa sukdulang antas ng kasamaan ng isang tao o sistema.
etymology: From the prefix `ka-` (indicating an abstract quality) and `buktot` (crooked, perverse, evil).
original_explanation: This is the evil villain level of badness. Not just 'naughty,' but full-on scheming, corrupt politician, or 'kontrabida sa teleserye' kind of evil. It's the kind of bad that makes your lola shake her head and pray the rosary.
usage_notes: A formal and strong word used to denote deep moral corruption, often in literature, formal speeches, or religious contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat nating labanan ang **kabuktutan** sa lipunan.","translation":"We must fight the **wickedness** in society."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga **kabuktutan** ay nabunyag din sa huli.","translation":"His **perversities** were also exposed in the end."}]

meaning_filipino: Maging dahilan ng katahimikan, kawalan ng ingay, o kapayapaan ng isip.
etymology: Mula sa panlaping pangkasanhi na "ika-" at sa salitang-ugat na "tahimik" (walang ingay, payapa).
original_explanation: This is what will finally make things quiet. Your mom threatening to take the WiFi password is the `ikatahimik` of your noisy siblings. A good cup of coffee before your shift is the `ikatahimik` of your chaotic mind. It's the "shush" button for life's noise.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang pandiwang sanhi na tumutukoy sa dahilan ng pagtigil ng ingay o pagkamit ng kapayapaan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-amin sa kasalanan ang **ikatahimik** ng iyong budhi.","translation":"Admitting your fault is what will **bring peace** to your conscience."},{"sentence":"Bigyan mo na siya ng gatas at baka iyon ang **ikatahimik** ng sanggol.","translation":"Give him milk, that might be what **will quiet** the baby."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng sabaw na karaniwang may sahog na manok, macaroni, gulay, at gatas. Maaari ring tumukoy sa anumang uri ng sabaw sa pangkalahatan.
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino comfort food, especially on a rainy day or when you're feeling sick. It's that creamy macaroni soup with chicken, carrots, and evaporated milk that your nanay makes. It's not just soup; it's a warm hug in a bowl. Kapag sinabing "sopas," automatic ito 'yung iniisip, hindi 'yung clear broth na sinigang or tinola.
usage_notes: Bagama't maaaring mangahulugang "soup" sa pangkalahatan, ito ay madalas na tumutukoy sa partikular na uri ng Pilipinong creamy macaroni soup.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagluto si Nanay ng mainit na **sopas** dahil umuulan.","translation":"Mom cooked hot **sopas** because it was raining."},{"sentence":"Paborito kong kainin ang **sopas** tuwing may sakit ako.","translation":"It's my favorite thing to eat **sopas** whenever I'm sick."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o pangkat na biglaang sumasalakay o pumapasok sa isang teritoryo nang may masamang hangarin, tulad ng pananakop.
original_explanation: Think of it as the historical version of a 'gatecrasher' but for entire countries. Sila yung dahilan kung bakit may mga pader at kanyon ang mga lumang siyudad. The ultimate uninvited guest on a national scale.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa kontekstong historikal o militar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matapang na hinarap ng mga katutubo ang mga dayuhang **manlulusob**.","translation":"The natives bravely faced the foreign **invaders**."},{"sentence":"Naghahanda ang kaharian para sa posibleng pagdating ng mga **manlulusob**.","translation":"The kingdom is preparing for the possible arrival of the **attackers**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matalino o tusong pamamaraan o kagamitan na ginagamit upang linlangin o lokohin ang iba.
original_explanation: The fancy word for "gimmick" or "palusot." It's the clever trick you use to get what you want, like suddenly being extra helpful to your parents when you need to borrow money, or using creative camera angles for your "woke up like this" selfie. It's strategy, darling.
usage_notes: Carries a connotation of cleverness that can be either neutral or deceptive.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng iba't ibang **artipisyo** para makuha ang tiwala ng mga tao.","translation":"He used various **artifices** to gain the people's trust."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng manipis, matigas-tigas, at bahagyang transparent na tela na gawa sa koton, karaniwang ginagamit sa mga baro, kurtina, at pormal na kasuotan.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung tela na parang pang-manika or pang-debutante noong unang panahon. Manipis pero medyo matigas, kaya 'pag ginawang palda, may sariling "poof" factor. It's the fabric of choice for making those classic, elegant Filipiniana sleeves stand up straight. Not your everyday pambahay fabric, for sure.
usage_notes: Mas kilala sa mga mananahi at sa industriya ng fashion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang manggas ng kanyang Baro't Saya ay yari sa pinong **organdi**.","translation":"The sleeves of her Baro't Saya were made of fine **organdy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-ukit o paghubog sa isang matigas na materyal tulad ng kahoy, bato, o yelo upang makabuo ng isang anyo o disenyo.
original_explanation: This is what artists in Paete, Laguna do to wood, or what chefs do to ice and fruit for fancy buffets. It's the act of turning a boring block of something into a masterpiece. In hugot terms, it's like how pain and hardship "sculpt" you into a stronger person. Charot.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang matutong **maglilok** ng mga santo mula sa kahoy.","translation":"He dreams of learning to **sculpt** saints out of wood."},{"sentence":"Ang mga Ifugao ay kilala sa kanilang galing sa **paglilok**.","translation":"The Ifugao are known for their skill in **carving**."}]

translation: to bring to life; to portray
meaning_filipino: Magkaloob ng sigla, kulay, o katotohanan sa isang bagay, konsepto, o karakter.
original_explanation: What great actors do to a script. It's taking something flat—a drawing, a story, a character—and making it feel real and alive. Parang 'yung cosplayer na kuhang-kuha ang personality ng anime character, or 'yung chef na ginawang work of art ang simpleng adobo. To animate, to vitalize, to make it pop.
usage_notes: Often used in artistic, creative, or performance contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahusay niyang **binigyang-buhay** ang karakter ni Crisostomo Ibarra.","translation":"He skillfully **brought to life** the character of Crisostomo Ibarra."},{"sentence":"Ang mga dekorasyon ay **nagbigay-buhay** sa buong silid.","translation":"The decorations **gave life** to the entire room."}]

meaning_filipino: May banayad na pagkakahilig o pagbaba; hindi matarik.
original_explanation: Think of the hills in the Windows XP wallpaper, not the steep climb to Baguio. It's a gentle slope, perfect for a chill hike or a relaxing bike ride. It’s the opposite of that sudden, steep drop in your bank account after a 12.12 sale.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit upang ilarawan ang anyong lupa tulad ng mga burol, kalsada, o maging mga bubong.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas madaling akyatin ang bundok na iyon dahil **malanday** lamang ang daan.","translation":"That mountain is easier to climb because the path is only **gently sloping**."},{"sentence":"Ang disenyo ng bubong ay **malanday** upang maiwasan ang pag-ipon ng tubig.","translation":"The roof's design is **undulating** to prevent water from pooling."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lalaki o babae na legal na kabiyak o kinakasama ng isang tao sa matrimonyo ng kasal.
original_explanation: Your better half, your partner in crime, the person you share your Netflix password and life with. In the Philippines, your **asawa** is also the person your relatives will ask about incessantly until you get one. It's a gender-neutral term, so it can be your husband or your wife. Your 'forever'.
usage_notes: Gender-neutral. To specify gender, one can say 'asawang lalaki' (husband) or 'asawang babae' (wife), though context usually makes this clear. 'Maybahay' (for wife) and 'bana' (for husband, less common) are other terms.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **asawa** ko ang nagluto ng masarap na hapunan.","translation":"My **spouse** cooked our delicious dinner."},{"sentence":"Ipinakilala niya sa amin ang kanyang magiging **asawa**.","translation":"He/She introduced to us his/her future **spouse**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na tumatagal o nilayon na tumagal lamang sa limitadong panahon; hindi permanente.
original_explanation: Parang yung "kayo" na walang label. Parang "work from home" setup na anytime pwedeng bawiin. Ito yung status mo bilang "contractual" employee. Basically, lahat ng bagay na may expiration date. "Huwag kang masanay, temporario lang 'yan." Pwedeng tungkol sa pwesto sa palengke, sa trabaho, o sa pag-ibig. Aray.
usage_notes: Mas karaniwang ginagamit ang salitang "pansamantala".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang trabaho ay **temporario** lamang habang nag-aaral pa siya.","translation":"Her job is only **temporary** while she is still studying."},{"sentence":"Nagtayo sila ng isang **temporario** na tulay matapos ang bagyo.","translation":"They built a **temporary** bridge after the storm."}]

translation: to be able to match or suit
meaning_filipino: Magawang itugma o iakma ang isang bagay sa isa pa upang magkaroon ng harmoniya o pagiging angkop.
etymology: From 'bagay', meaning 'thing,' 'matter,' or 'suitable.' The 'ma-i-' prefix denotes ability.
original_explanation: This is your brain on 'OOTD' mode. You're trying to **maibagay** your shoes with your bag. It's also what you do when you're setting up two of your friends: 'Hmm, bagay kaya sila?' You're trying to see if you can match their personalities. It's the art of finding the perfect match, whether in fashion, love, or home decor.
usage_notes: Used for matching items, colors, people, or concepts. Implies creating a harmonious or suitable combination.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahihirapan siyang **maibagay** ang kulay ng kurtina sa kulay ng pader.","translation":"She's having a hard time **matching** the color of the curtain with the color of the wall."},{"sentence":"Sana ay **maibagay** ko ang aking presentasyon sa inaasahan ng mga kliyente.","translation":"I hope I can **suit** my presentation to the clients' expectations."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang likidong may kulay na ginagamit sa pagsulat, pag-imprenta, o pagguhit.
original_explanation: The lifeblood of your ballpen, printer, and tattoo artist. It's what you run out of during final exams or when you need to print a 100-page report due in an hour. Also, what your lolo used in his fountain pen back in the day.
usage_notes: Can refer to any kind of ink, from a pen to a printer to a tattoo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naubusan na ng **tinta** ang aking panulat.","translation":"My pen has run out of **ink**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating bumili ng bagong **tinta** para sa printer.","translation":"We need to buy new **ink** for the printer."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging naistorbo o nagulo; ang resulta ng isang biglaang ingay, gulo, o di-inaasahang pangyayari.
original_explanation: The feeling when you're in a deep sleep and someone turns on the vacuum cleaner. Or when you're concentrating on your work and the kapitbahay starts their videoke session at 10 AM on a Tuesday. That sudden jolt and annoyance? That's pagkabulabog.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa pandamdam (feeling disturbed) o sa mismong kaganapan (the disturbance itself).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Humingi siya ng paumanhin dahil sa **pagkabulabog** na idinulot niya kagabi.","translation":"He apologized for the **disturbance** he caused last night."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko matapos ang trabaho dahil sa **pagkabulabog** ng aking mga anak.","translation":"I can't finish my work because of the **state of being disturbed** by my children."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay na isinasama o idinaragdag sa isang umiiral na bilang o dami; karagdagan.
original_explanation: 'Dagdag' is the magic word for when one cup of rice isn't enough. It's the 'plus' in 'service charge plus VAT'. It's what you ask for from your boss ('dagdag sahod') and what you dread from your prof ('dagdag-bawas'). The opposite of 'bawas'.
usage_notes: Very common. Can be a noun ('Humingi ako ng dagdag') or an adjective ('May dagdag bayad ba ito?'). The verb form is 'magdagdag' or 'dagdagan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **dagdag** na bayad ba para sa extra cheese?","translation":"Is there an **additional** charge for the extra cheese?"},{"sentence":"Pahingi ng **dagdag** na kanin, pakiusap.","translation":"Can I have an **addition** of rice, please?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng marahan o mabilis na pagdiin ng daliri o anumang bagay sa isang rabaw, lalo na sa screen ng isang elektronikong gadyet.
etymology: Onomatopoeic, mula sa tunog ng pagdiin ng daliri.
original_explanation: This is what you do to your phone screen all day. Swipe, tap, *dutdot*. It's the sound your finger makes when you're stalking your ex's new partner on social media. It can be a gentle poke on the cheek, or a furious tap-tap-tap when your internet is slow and you're trying to refresh the page. 'Dutdot lang nang dutdot hanggang ma-lowbatt.'
usage_notes: Naging palasak ang paggamit ng salitang ito sa pagdating ng mga touchscreen na telepono at tableta. Ang pandiwa nito ay 'dutdutin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **dutdot** lang sa app at makaka-order ka na ng pagkain.","translation":"Just one **tap** on the app and you can order food."},{"sentence":"Naiirita ako sa walang tigil na **dutdot** niya sa balikat ko.","translation":"I'm getting irritated by his incessant **poking** on my shoulder."}]

translation: to turn one's back; to abandon
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-ikot ng katawan upang ang likod ang maiharap; sa matalinghagang kahulugan, ito ay ang pag-iwan o pagtataksil sa isang tao, paniniwala, o responsibilidad.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'ghosting' move, but in real life. It's when your friend sees you in the mall but pretends they didn't. Or worse, when someone you trusted leaves you hanging. The literal 'seen-zone' in physical form.
usage_notes: Carries a strong figurative meaning of betrayal or abandonment, aside from the literal physical action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nang kailanganin ko siya, bigla na lang siyang **tumalikod**.","translation":"When I needed him, he suddenly **turned his back** on me."}]

meaning_filipino: Itanggi o hindi aminin ang isang bagay, paratang, o katotohanan.
original_explanation: This is what you do when your mom asks who ate the last piece of leche flan. It's the classic "Hindi ako, promise!" even when you're caught red-handed. The official statement of someone in a scandal.
usage_notes: A more formal way of saying "itanggi". Often used in legal or serious contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **ikaila** ang katotohanang nakita ka sa lugar ng krimen.","translation":"It's hard **to deny** the fact that you were seen at the crime scene."},{"sentence":"Kahit anong gawin niya, hindi niya **maikakaila** ang nararamdaman para sa iyo.","translation":"No matter what they do, they cannot **deny** their feelings for you."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalatag ng banig sa isang partikular na lugar o para sa isang tao.
original_explanation: The ultimate act of Filipino hospitality. When guests are staying over and there aren't enough beds, you **banigan** mo sila sa sahig. It means "I'll lay down a mat for you." It's a gesture that says, "We don't have a guest room, but we have a floor and a heart big enough for you."
usage_notes: The root 'banig' (mat) + suffix '-an' (to do something on/at a location).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **banigan** mo ang sahig sa sala para sa mga bata.","translation":"Please, **lay a mat on** the living room floor for the kids."},{"sentence":"**Binanigan** ni Aling Nena ang kanyang mga panauhin dahil kulang ang kanilang mga silid.","translation":"Aling Nena **laid mats for** her guests because they didn't have enough rooms."}]

translation: to chastise, to reprimand, to punish
meaning_filipino: Magpataw ng parusa o magbigay ng matinding pagpuna o sermon bilang disiplina.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you get caught breaking curfew. Your parents kumastigo you with a lecture that's longer than EDSA traffic. It's not just a simple scolding; it's a full-on, 'I'm very disappointed in you' speech that hits harder than your mom's tsinelas. In politics, critics kumastigo the government for its shortcomings.
usage_notes: Carries a strong, formal tone, often used in contexts of discipline, law, or harsh criticism.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumastigo** ang guro sa mga estudyanteng nahuling nangongopya sa pagsusulit.","translation":"The teacher **chastised** the students who were caught cheating on the exam."},{"sentence":"Sa kanyang talumpati, **kumastigo** ang senador laban sa katiwalian sa gobyerno.","translation":"In his speech, the senator **railed against** corruption in the government."}]

translation: to make something float; to bring to the surface
meaning_filipino: Gawing lumutang o hindi lumubog sa isang likido; ilitaw o ipaangat sa ibabaw.
original_explanation: Literally, to make something float, like a salbabida in a pool. Figuratively, it’s what you do to an issue during a meeting that everyone's been avoiding. "I-**palutangin** mo 'yung issue ng budget para ma-settle na." It’s also what happens to your hidden talent when your friends push you to join a contest.
usage_notes: Can be used both literally for physical objects in liquid and figuratively for ideas, issues, or truths.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukang **palutangin** ng mga mangingisda ang lumubog na bangka.","translation":"The fishermen tried to **make the sunken boat float**."},{"sentence":"Sa pulong, sinikap niyang **palutangin** ang kanyang magandang ideya.","translation":"In the meeting, he tried to **bring his good idea to the surface**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang modernong sistema kung saan ang isang tao ay nakikiusap sa iba na bumili ng isang produkto para sa kanila, karaniwan ay may kaakibat na bayad para sa serbisyo.
etymology: Portmanteau of Tagalog `pasabay` (to go along with) and English `buy`.
original_explanation: The modern "bilin" for the online shopping era. It’s when you're too lazy (or busy) to go to the mall, so you pay someone who's already there to buy stuff for you. "Pabili" meets "sabay." It's the lifeblood of communities during lockdowns and the go-to for getting that specific brand of coffee you're craving without leaving your desk. The person doing the buying is your "pasabuy" hero.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun ("May pasabuy ako") or a verb ("I-pasabuy mo naman ako ng milk tea").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkano ang bayad sa serbisyo ng **pasabuy** mo?","translation":"How much is the service fee for your **personal shopping service**?"},{"sentence":"Puwede bang mag-**pasabuy** sa'yo ng pagkain galing diyan?","translation":"Can I **have you buy** me some food from there?"}]

translation: to return; to submit; to hand over
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabalik ng isang bagay sa pinanggalingan o may-ari nito; ang pagbibigay o pagpasa ng isang ulat o gawain.
original_explanation: That moment of reckoning when you have to return your tita's Tupperware, hopefully with some food still in it as a sign of goodwill. In an office setting, this is what you do with your report to the boss. It's the act of handing something over or back.
usage_notes: This meaning is often used in formal or official contexts, like submitting a report or returning an item. It is distinct from its homonym related to taking an exam.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magsulit** ng lahat ng resibo sa accounting department.","translation":"You need **to submit** all the receipts to the accounting department."},{"sentence":"Pinapapunta siya sa opisina ng prinsipal para **magsulit** tungkol sa nangyaring gulo.","translation":"He was asked to go to the principal's office **to report** on the trouble that happened."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang makinis at makintab na bagay na sumasalamin sa imahe ng anumang nasa harap nito. Maaari rin itong tumukoy sa babasaging materyal na ginagamit sa bintana, baso, at iba pa.
original_explanation: It's your number one hype man in the morning and your harshest critic at night. It shows you everything from your new outfit to that one pimple that decided to show up before a big date. Also refers to the glass on your window that your neighbor's kid might break with a basketball.
usage_notes: Can mean both a reflective mirror and the material 'glass'. Context is key to differentiate.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumingin siya sa **salamin** upang ayusin ang kanyang buhok.","translation":"She looked in the **mirror** to fix her hair."},{"sentence":"Nabasag ang **salamin** ng bintana dahil sa lakas ng hangin.","translation":"The window **glass** broke because of the strong wind."}]

meaning_filipino: Husto o tamang-tama sa laki, anyo, o pangangailangan; lapat.
original_explanation: That magical moment when the pants you bought online actually fit perfectly. 'Sukat na sukat!' It's when something is tailor-made for the situation, person, or place. It's the Goldilocks of Tagalog words: not too big, not too small, just right.
usage_notes: Often reduplicated as 'sukat na sukat' for emphasis, meaning 'a perfect fit'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang barong na ito ay **sukat** para sa iyo.","translation":"This barong is the right **fit** for you."},{"sentence":"**Sukat** na **sukat** ang dating niya para sa interview.","translation":"His arrival for the interview was perfectly **timed** (lit. exact)."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sandatang may sariling makina na ginagamit sa digmaan, na maaaring patamaan sa isang malayong target.
original_explanation: Basically, a rocket na may galit. Yung pinapadala mo sa video game para pasabugin ang base ng kalaban. Sa totoong buhay, ito yung dahilan kung bakit may mga world leader na kailangan ng chill pill. It's a high-tech, explosive 'I'm not happy with you' message.
usage_notes: A direct loanword used in news and formal contexts related to military and technology.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpakawala ng isang panubok na **misil** ang isang bansa.","translation":"A country launched a test **missile**."},{"sentence":"Ang barko ay nilagyan ng mga depensang kontra-**misil**.","translation":"The ship was equipped with anti-**missile** defenses."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng paggawa na may buong katapatan, sigasig, at walang pag-aalinlangan.
original_explanation: This is how you should love, according to hugot culture. No half-assing it. It's giving your all, whether it's in a relationship, a project, or singing your heart out in a karaoke session. It's the '100% effort, no regrets' mode.
usage_notes: Often used to describe acts of giving, accepting, or loving.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinanggap niya **nang buong-puso** ang responsibilidad.","translation":"He accepted the responsibility **wholeheartedly**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa panlima o ika-lima sa isang pagkakasunod-sunod.
original_explanation: The 'ka-' prefix here is a bit old-school for ordinal numbers. You're more likely to hear 'panlima' or 'ikalima'. Using 'kalima' is like saying 'thou' instead of 'you.' It's correct, but people might look at you funny. It's the 'lola's way' of counting.
usage_notes: Sinauna o pampanitikang anyo ng 'ikalima' o 'panlima'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **kalima** sa linya ng mga tagapagmana.","translation":"He is the **fifth** in the line of heirs."},{"sentence":"Ito na ang **kalima** mong babala.","translation":"This is now your **fifth** warning."}]

translation: to change the subject; by the way
meaning_filipino: Isang parirala na pinaikling 'maiba ako' na ginagamit upang magbago ng paksa sa isang usapan, katumbas ng "sa ibang paksa".
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "CTRL+ALT+DEL" of any awkward conversation. When your Tita asks about your love life, you hit them with a "Maiba'ko, ang sarap ng lechon!" It's the polite way to say "Let's not talk about that, okay?" A verbal smokescreen.
usage_notes: Often used to steer a conversation away from an uncomfortable or uninteresting topic. It's a very common conversational tool.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ganda ng sapatos mo! **Maiba'ko**, nakita mo na ba 'yung bagong series sa Netflix?","translation":"Nice shoes! **By the way**, have you seen the new series on Netflix?"},{"sentence":"Tungkol sa utang mo... **Maiba'ko**, uulan yata mamaya.","translation":"About your debt... **To change the subject**, I think it's going to rain later."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maliit at berdeng legumbre (Vigna radiata) na karaniwang ginagawang sangkap sa mga lutuin tulad ng ginisang munggo o ginataang munggo.
etymology: From Hokkien 'mung ko' (mung cake), referring to the bean used in the pastry.
original_explanation: The official dish of Fridays in the Philippines. Ginisang munggo with chicharon and ampalaya leaves is a staple. It's the budget-friendly, protein-packed ulam that signals the weekend is near. Also the star ingredient in hopia and butsi. It's the little green bean that could.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Biyernes ngayon, kaya **munggo** ang ulam namin.","translation":"It's Friday today, so we're having **mung beans** for our meal."},{"sentence":"Paborito kong palaman sa hopia ang **munggo**.","translation":"My favorite filling for hopia is **mung bean**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pamamaga o bukol, karaniwan sa ulo, na sanhi ng pagkahulog, pagkauntog, o malakas na tama.
etymology: From Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *baguk (sound of a dull blow).
original_explanation: That painful 'bukol' you get on your forehead after walking into a glass door you thought was open. It's the cartoonish lump that throbs and sometimes has birds flying around it. Your lola would immediately put a cold compress or a coin on it. 'Yan ang resulta ng katangahan, a.k.a. 'di pag-iingat.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to a bump or swelling from an impact, most commonly on the head.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon siya ng malaking **bagok** sa noo matapos mauntog sa pader.","translation":"He got a big **bump** on his forehead after hitting the wall."},{"sentence":"Nilagyan ng yelo ng nanay ang **bagok** ng bata.","translation":"The mother applied ice to the child's **bump**."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing pag-aari o pamamahala ng buong bansa o nasyon ang isang ari-arian, korporasyon, o industriya.
original_explanation: This is the government version of "it's complicated" turning into "it's ours now." Think of a private company, like a telco or an electric company, being taken over by the government. It's a major political and economic move, like when your parents decide your personal savings are now part of the "family fund."
usage_notes: Used in formal contexts, particularly in economics, politics, and history.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May panukala ang ilang mambabatas na **magsabansa** sa mga pangunahing kumpanya ng langis.","translation":"Some lawmakers have a proposal to **nationalize** the major oil companies."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng gobyerno kung dapat bang **magsabansa** ng mga serbisyong pangkuryente.","translation":"The government is studying whether it should **nationalize** electricity services."}]

translation: not even one; none at all
meaning_filipino: Isang pariralang nagbibigay-diin sa ganap na kawalan; ni isa ay walang natira o dumating.
etymology: Isang parirala na pinagsasama ang `wala` (none), `isa` (one), at `man` (even).
original_explanation: This is `wala` on steroids. It's when you throw a party and literally no one shows up. Not your best friend, not your tita, not even the caterer. It's the ultimate "seen-zoned" in real life. `Wala isa man` is the most dramatic way to say "zero, zilch, nada."
usage_notes: Ginagamit para sa matinding pagbibigay-diin sa kumpletong kawalan ng isang bagay na nabibilang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa lahat ng inimbita ko, **wala isa man** ang dumating.","translation":"Of all the people I invited, **not even one** came."},{"sentence":"Naghintay kami ng sagot, ngunit **wala isa man** kaming natanggap.","translation":"We waited for a reply, but we received **none at all**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na permanente, tiyak, at hindi na magbabago pa anuman ang mangyari.
etymology: Mula sa "di-" (not), "ma-", at pag-uulit ng "i-" mula sa salitang-ugat na "iba" (different/other).
original_explanation: Parang pagmamahal ng nanay mo, di-maiiba. O kaya 'yung fact na may traffic sa EDSA tuwing 5 PM. It's a constant. It's a given. Huwag ka nang umasa, ganun talaga.
usage_notes: Often used to express certainty or permanence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang desisyon ko ay pinal na at **di-maiiba**.","translation":"My decision is final and **unchangeable**."},{"sentence":"Kahit anong mangyari, ang pagtingin ko sa'yo ay **di-maiiba**.","translation":"Whatever happens, my feelings for you **will not be different**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o entidad na nagbibigay ng trabaho o gawain sa iba kapalit ng sahod o bayad.
etymology: From "may" (has) + "pa-" (causative prefix) + "trabaho" (work). Literally "one who causes work".
original_explanation: Your boss, the company, the one who signs the checks. Sila yung dahilan kung bakit ka nagigising ng maaga at kung bakit may pambili ka ng milk tea. Also known as 'The Source' of your stress and your sweldo.
usage_notes: Can be written as "may-patrabaho" or "may patrabaho", but "maypatrabaho" as a compound word is also common. It's the counterpart to "manggagawa" (worker).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpulong ang mga **maypatrabaho** at ang unyon ng mga manggagawa.","translation":"The **employers** and the workers' union had a meeting."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-alis o pag-iwas mula sa isang lugar o sitwasyon nang palihim o mabilisan upang makaiwas sa panganib o responsibilidad.
original_explanation: What you do when your tita asks "Kailan ka mag-aasawa?". It's the act of running away from an awkward situation. Verb forms: tumakas (escaped), tatakas (will escape), tumatakas (escaping).
usage_notes: The common actor-focus verb is "tumakas". The object-focus verb is "takasan" (to escape from something/someone).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumakas** ang bilanggo kagabi.","translation":"The prisoner **escaped** last night."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **takasan** ang kanyang mga problema.","translation":"He tried to **escape** his problems."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kumukuha ng pag-aari ng iba nang walang pahintulot at may layuning angkinin ito.
etymology: From `mag-` + `nanakaw` (reduplication of the first syllable of the root `nakaw`).
original_explanation: The OG "snatcher." Whether it's your wallet, your phone, or your heart (charot!), a magnanakaw takes what isn't theirs. In modern times, this can also be the person who "borrows" your Netflix password and changes the profile names, or the office mate who keeps stealing your favorite pen. The ultimate "bida-bida sa hindi niya property."
usage_notes: The noun form for a person who steals. The verb form is "magnakaw".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahuli ng CCTV ang **magnanakaw** na pumasok sa tindahan.","translation":"The CCTV caught the **thief** who entered the store."},{"sentence":"Sigaw! **Magnanakaw**! Habulin ninyo!","translation":"Shout! **Thief**! Go after him!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng isdang-alat na karaniwang kinakain, kilala sa siyentipikong pangalan na Carangoides sp.
original_explanation: 'Yung isda sa palengke na medyo sosyal ang dating at masarap i-ihaw o gawing sinigang. Hindi siya kasing sikat ng tilapia o bangus, pero 'pag nakahain, alam mong may budget.
usage_notes: A type of fish (trevally) popular in the Philippines for various dishes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap ang sinigang na **talakitok** na niluto ni Nanay.","translation":"The sinigang na **trevally** that Mom cooked is delicious."},{"sentence":"Magkano ang kilo ng sariwang **talakitok** sa palengke?","translation":"How much is a kilo of fresh **trevally** at the market?"}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng katapusan; hindi panghabambuhay o walang hanggan.
original_explanation: The opposite of your 'walang-hanggan' promise to your ex. Everything from your favorite K-drama series to your mobile data plan is may-wakas. It's a hugot-ready concept reminding you that nothing lasts forever, so you better make the most of it. #CarpeDiem
usage_notes: Often used in philosophical, romantic, or dramatic contexts to express the concept of impermanence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lahat ng bagay sa mundo ay **may-wakas**.","translation":"Everything in the world **has an end**."},{"sentence":"Kahit gaano kasaya, ang bakasyon ay **may-wakas** din.","translation":"No matter how fun, a vacation also **is finite**."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga gawi, asal, at paniniwala na nakasanayan na ng isang pangkat ng mga tao at naipapasa sa mga susunod na henerasyon.
etymology: From `ka-` + `ugali` (habit) + `-an`, signifying a collective set of habits or 'customs'.
original_explanation: This is why you have to 'mano po' to your elders, why there's always a mountain of food at fiestas, and why you can't go straight home after a wake (pagpag!). Kaugalian is the unwritten rulebook of Filipino culture, the 'it's just how we do things here' that baffles foreigners and comforts locals.
usage_notes: Refers to broader, community-level or cultural habits, as opposed to 'ugali' which is more individual.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paghahanda ng lechon tuwing pista ay isang **kaugalian** ng mga Pilipino.","translation":"Preparing lechon during fiestas is a Filipino **tradition**."},{"sentence":"Dapat igalang ang mga **kaugalian** sa lugar na iyong binibisita.","translation":"One must respect the **customs** of the place you are visiting."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit at bilugang masa, tulad ng isang patak ng likido.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung maliliit na taba na nakikita mo sa sabaw ng sinigang o 'yung mga bilog-bilog sa science experiment. Think small, round, and usually squishy.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa mga kontekstong siyentipiko o teknikal. Hindi karaniwan sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakita sila ng mga **globulo** ng langis sa ilalim ng mikroskopyo.","translation":"They saw **globules** of oil under the microscope."},{"sentence":"Ang pulang selula ng dugo ay isang uri ng **globulo**.","translation":"A red blood cell is a type of **globule**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang halamang gamot na may mabangong dahon, karaniwang ginagamit bilang pampalasa sa pagluluto at bilang tradisyonal na lunas sa ubo at sipon.
original_explanation: The ultimate Tita remedy for coughs. Bago ka pa dalhin sa doktor, for sure may lola o nanay na magsasabing, "Magpakulo ka ng dahon ng **oregano** at inumin mo." It's that plant in the backyard that doubles as a pizza topping and a DIY expectorant. A true multi-tasker.
usage_notes: Kilala pareho bilang sangkap sa lutuin (lalo na sa Italian-style dishes) at bilang halamang gamot.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinikdik niya ang dahon ng **oregano** para ipainom sa batang inuubo.","translation":"She crushed the **oregano** leaves to give to the coughing child."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang ituloy o ipagpatuloy ang isang nasimulang gawain, proyekto, o proseso.
original_explanation: This is the mantra of every student finishing their thesis, every BPO agent on a long shift, and everyone trying to finish a K-drama series in one weekend. "Kahit puyat na, kailangan kong **maipagpatuloy** 'to!" It's the power to 'push lang nang push' despite the odds.
usage_notes: Used when there's a possibility of stopping, but one wishes to or is able to proceed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa tulong pinansyal, **maipagpatuloy** niya ang kanyang pag-aaral.","translation":"Because of the financial aid, she was **able to continue** her studies."},{"sentence":"Sana **maipagpatuloy** natin ang magandang proyektong ito.","translation":"I hope we can **continue** this good project."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kasalungat sa isang debate, argumento, o diskusyon; katunggali sa pangangatwiran.
etymology: From 'ka-' (denoting a partner or companion) + 'talo' (to lose, defeat), implying someone you are in a contest of words with, aiming to defeat them in argument.
original_explanation: Your debate partner, but on the other team. The person you argue with on Facebook comments about politics. The one who always says 'Actually...' in a meeting. Not necessarily an enemy (kaaway), just someone on the other side of the issue.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to an opponent in a debate or argument, not necessarily in a physical fight ('kalaban') or a game ('katunggali').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Wala siyang takot na harapin ang kanyang **katalo** sa entablado.","translation":"He was not afraid to face his **opponent** on the debate stage."},{"sentence":"Naging mainit ang pagtatalo ng mag-**katalo**.","translation":"The argument between the two **adversaries** became heated."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na ginagamit upang ipahayag ang pagtatapos ng isang gawain nang may kahusayan, pagtama sa punto, o bilang isang tunog ng pagsampal o pagpalo.
etymology: Onomatopoeic, popularized and given new meaning by Filipino gay culture.
original_explanation: Originally the sound of a slap, but gay lingo turned it into the ultimate stamp of approval. Did you finish your report? Pak! Is your outfit on point? Pak! Did you deliver that killer presentation? Ganda ng lola mo, pak! It’s the verbal equivalent of a mic drop. Can also be combined: "Pak! Ganern!" for extra emphasis.
usage_notes: Highly informal and part of "swardspeak" or Filipino gay lingo that has entered mainstream consciousness. Can also be used as an onomatopoeia for a smack or a thud.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pak!** Ang ganda ng makeup mo ngayon, girl!","translation":"**On point!** Your makeup is beautiful today, girl!"},{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang malakas na **pak** ng pagbagsak ng libro.","translation":"I heard the loud **thud** of the book falling."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos niyang magsalita, **pak**, umalis na siya.","translation":"After he spoke, **bang**, he just left."}]

meaning_filipino: Mabilis na pagkalat ng impormasyon, video, o anumang content sa internet, na umaabot sa napakaraming tao sa maikling panahon, katulad ng pagkalat ng isang virus.
original_explanation: Ito ang pangarap ng bawat content creator at kinatatakutan ng bawat politiko na may itinatagong kalokohan. Kapag nag-viral ka, instant sikat ka. Pwedeng dahil sa cute na pusa, sa galing mong kumanta, o sa epic fail mong pag-park. One day you're a nobody, the next day, nasa news ka na. 'OMG, nag-viral yung post ko!'
usage_notes: Often used with the verb 'mag-' (mag-viral) to mean 'to go viral'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **viral** ang video ng asong marunong mag-matematika.","translation":"The video of the dog that knows math went **viral**."},{"sentence":"Sana mag-**viral** itong kanta ko para sumikat ako.","translation":"I hope this song of mine goes **viral** so I can become famous."}]

meaning_filipino: Kanin na isinangag sa mantika kasama ang iba't ibang sahog tulad ng bawang, itlog, at kung minsan ay karne o gulay.
original_explanation: The official national breakfast of the Philippines. The ultimate way to use up leftover rice (bahaw). Partner it with egg (itlog) and a protein (like tapa, tocino, longganisa) and you've got a -silog meal. A true lifesaver for students and BPO agents on a budget.
usage_notes: Often spelled as one word ('friedrice') in informal contexts, but 'fried rice' is the correct spelling. Directly refers to 'sinangag'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang almusal ko ay **fried rice** na may itlog at hotdog.","translation":"My breakfast is **fried rice** with egg and hotdog."},{"sentence":"Mas masarap ang kaning-lamig gawing **fried rice**.","translation":"Leftover cold rice is better for making **fried rice**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manggagawa na ang trabaho ay panatilihin ang kalinisan at kaayusan ng mga kalsada, kasama na ang pagwawalis ng mga basura at pag-aayos ng maliliit na sira.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'caminero', na nangangahulugang "manggagawa sa daan".
original_explanation: The unsung heroes of our city streets. Sila yung maaga pa lang, nagwawalis na ng mga kalat na iniwan natin. Kung walang kaminero, baka lumalangoy na tayo sa basura. They brave the sun, rain, and pollution para lang maging malinis ang daan mo papuntang work. Bigyan ng jacket 'yan!
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang tukuyin ang mga tagalinis ng kalsada na empleyado ng gobyerno (hal., MMDA).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Araw-araw, masipag na nililinis ng mga **kaminero** ang aming kalye.","translation":"Every day, the **road workers** diligently clean our street."},{"sentence":"Dapat nating igalang ang trabaho ng bawat **kaminero**.","translation":"We should respect the work of every **street sweeper**."}]

translation: main expense; what one is spending on
meaning_filipino: Ang bagay, serbisyo, o gawain kung saan patuloy na ginugugol o inilalaan ang pera.
original_explanation: Ito yung black hole ng wallet mo. Milktea, Shopee/Lazada checkout, online game skins, K-Pop merch... 'yan ang mga pinagkakagastahan mo kaya ka laging 'petsa de peligro'. It's your personal money pit, the reason for your 'ipon-challenge' fails.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa isang paulit-ulit o pangunahing gastusin. Ang pag-uulit na "ka-ka-" ay nagpapahiwatig ng isang tuloy-tuloy, nakagawian, o matinding pagkilos.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang edukasyon ng mga anak ang pangunahing **pinagkakagastahan** ng mag-asawa.","translation":"The children's education is the couple's main **expense**."},{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na 'yang **pinagkakagastahan** mong hindi naman importante.","translation":"Stop **what you are spending on** that isn't even important."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaghalong likido na karaniwang binubuo ng langis, suka, pampalasa, at yerba kung saan ibinababad ang karne, isda, o gulay bago lutuin upang lumambot at magkalasa.
etymology: From English 'marinade', from French 'marinade', from 'mariner' (to brine).
original_explanation: That magic sauce you soak your liempo or BBQ sticks in overnight. The longer it 'sleeps' in the marinade, the more 'woke' the flavor is when you grill it. It's the secret weapon behind every Tito's legendary inihaw.
usage_notes: A direct loanword from English, commonly used in Filipino kitchens. The native equivalent is 'babad' or 'timpla'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ihanda mo na ang **marinade** para sa baboy na iihawin bukas.","translation":"Please prepare the **marinade** for the pork we will be grilling tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Mas masarap ang manok kung matagal itong nakababad sa **marinade**.","translation":"The chicken is more delicious if it's soaked in the **marinade** for a long time."}]

translation: preacher; moralizer; one who will preach
meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagpapahayag ng mga aral, lalo na tungkol sa relihiyon, moralidad, o mabuting asal.
original_explanation: Could be a priest, pastor, or that one friend in your group chat who sends 'Good Morning' messages with Bible verses. Also applies to anyone who gives unsolicited advice like it's their full-time job. 'Wag kang mangaral!' is the classic comeback.
usage_notes: Can be used neutrally for a religious preacher, or slightly negatively for someone who is being preachy or moralizing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **mangangaral** ay nagbigay ng isang makapangyarihang sermon tungkol sa pagpapatawad.","translation":"The **preacher** gave a powerful sermon about forgiveness."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa pagiging **mangangaral** sa aming barkada, laging may payo sa lahat ng bagay.","translation":"He is known as the **moralizer** in our friend group, always having advice for everything."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng bahagyang pag-usog o paggalaw mula sa isang puwesto, karaniwan ay upang magbigay ng espasyo. Ito ang gagawing pag-isod.
original_explanation: Future tense of 'isod'. The magic word inside a jam-packed jeepney: "Paki-usog po." This is the future tense version. "Mamaya, iisod natin yung sofa para magkasya yung Christmas tree." It’s that small shuffle or scoot to make space for someone or something else.
usage_notes: Contemplated aspect (future tense) of 'i-isod' or 'umisod'. Often used with 'paki-' (paki-isod) as a polite request. Synonymous with 'usog'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Iisod** ko lang ang upuan ko para makadaan ka.","translation":"I **will just move** my chair a bit so you can pass."},{"sentence":"Pwede bang **iisod** mo nang kaunti ang mga gamit mo?","translation":"Can you **scoot** your things over a little?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang makina o kagamitan, maaaring de-kuryente o de-kamay, na ginagamit upang pinuhing mabuti ang karne.
original_explanation: Before you get your embutido or longganisa, the meat has to go through this. It's the kitchen equivalent of a horror movie device, but the results are delicious. The sound it makes is iconic in any palengke meat section.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy ito sa parehong manwal at de-kuryenteng kagamitan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang **pandurog ng karne** para gumawa ng giniling para sa spaghetti.","translation":"She used the **meat grinder** to make ground meat for the spaghetti."},{"sentence":"Maingay ang **pandurog ng karne** sa palengke tuwing umaga.","translation":"The **meat grinder** at the market is noisy every morning."}]

translation: to pose; to get into position
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aayos ng katawan sa isang partikular na posisyon, lalo na para sa isang larawan o sining. Ginagamit bilang salitang-ugat sa pag-uutos.
original_explanation: This is the command you give someone before taking their picture. 'Sige, porma!' means 'Okay, strike a pose!' It's the root word for action. It's less about the clothes (that's the noun) and more about the action of positioning your body to look good, cool, or just ready for the shot.
usage_notes: Used as a root word for verbs like 'pumorma' (to pose, to dress up, to make a move) and 'magporma'. Often used in its root form as an imperative command.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Porma** ka nang maayos, kukunan na kita ng litrato.","translation":"**Pose** properly, I'm going to take your picture now."},{"sentence":"Sinabihan ng direktor ang mga artista na **pumorma** para sa huling eksena.","translation":"The director told the actors to **get into position** for the final scene."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang institusyong pang-edukasyon na pinopondohan at pinamamahalaan ng gobyerno at bukas para sa lahat ng mamamayan.
original_explanation: The school where your classroom has 50+ students, the electric fan is a diva that only works sometimes, and the canteen sells the best 'palamig' and 'turon'. It's where you learn resourcefulness, resilience, and how to share one textbook with five other people. The real training ground for life in the Philippines.
usage_notes: The hyphenated form is formal. In common speech and writing, `paaralang bayan` (without a hyphen) is also widely used and accepted.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtapos siya sa isang pampublikong **paaralang-bayan** sa kanilang probinsya.","translation":"She graduated from a **public school** in their province."},{"sentence":"Ang edukasyon sa **paaralang-bayan** ay dapat libre at dekalidad.","translation":"Education in a **public school** should be free and of high quality."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging napupuno o natatakpan ng lumot.
etymology: From the complex formation `pagka-` + `lumot` + `-an`, indicating a state or condition of being covered in something.
original_explanation: This is the aesthetic of old churches in the province, or that rock in your garden that never sees the sun. It's when something gets that green, velvety coating because it's been left alone for a long, long time. Parang puso ng ilang tao, tinubuan na ng lumot sa tagal na walang nagmamahal. Hugot!
usage_notes: Describes a state or condition rather than an action. The pronunciation reflects the `pagka-` prefix.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa **pagkulumutan**, madulas ang mga bato sa tabi ng ilog.","translation":"Because of the **mossiness**, the rocks beside the river are slippery."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglubog o pagbabad ng isang bagay sa isang likido, tulad ng tubig o sarsa, sa loob ng isang takdang panahon.
original_explanation: The secret to most delicious Filipino dishes. Before it hits the pan, you gotta let it swim. 'Babarin mo muna sa toyo't suka,' is the start of many great adobo recipes. It's letting something sit and absorb all the good stuff, whether it's chicken in marinade or you in a bathtub after a hellish week.
usage_notes: Object-focused future tense of 'ibabad'. Used primarily in cooking contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **babarin** ang baboy sa barbecue marinade magdamag.","translation":"Don't forget to **marinate** the pork in barbecue marinade overnight."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang distansyang angular, na karaniwang sinusukat sa mga digri sa silangan o kanluran, mula sa prime meridian sa Greenwich, England.
original_explanation: That thing you tried to memorize in Heograpiya class along with 'latitud'. It's the vertical lines on a globe that look like the cage of a parrot. You probably haven't used this word since high school, unless you're a pilot, a sailor, or just really, really lost.
usage_notes: Isang terminong teknikal sa heograpiya at nabigasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinuro sa amin kung paano hanapin ang eksaktong **longhitud** at latitud ng isang lugar.","translation":"We were taught how to find the exact **longitude** and latitude of a place."},{"sentence":"Ang Pilipinas ay nasa pagitan ng 116° at 127° silangang **longhitud**.","translation":"The Philippines is located between 116° and 127° east **longitude**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng isang bagay na nakikita batay sa liwanag na sinasalamin nito; kulay.
original_explanation: A more formal or technical way of saying "kulay." You'd hear this from a painter, a photographer, or someone in printing. "Pare, ayusin mo 'yung kolor," sounds more serious than "Ayusin mo 'yung kulay." It’s the difference between your tita asking for the "color" and a graphic artist talking about "color grading."
usage_notes: 'Kulay' is the more common, everyday term. 'Kolor' is often used in more technical, artistic, or formal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magaling siyang mag-eksperimento sa iba't ibang **kolor** sa kanyang mga pinta.","translation":"He is good at experimenting with different **colors** in his paintings."},{"sentence":"Kailangang i-adjust ang **kolor** ng TV para mas maging matingkad.","translation":"The TV's **color** needs to be adjusted to be more vivid."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mga labi o guho ng isang gusali, istruktura, o lungsod na nasira dahil sa paglipas ng panahon, digmaan, o sakuna.
original_explanation: The dramatic aftermath. Picture the Cagsawa Church with only the bell tower standing, or the Parthenon in Greece. Pwede ring estado ng wallet mo after ng 12.12 sale. It's what's left when something grand has fallen apart. The beautiful, tragic mess.
usage_notes: Often used in historical or archaeological contexts. Can also be used figuratively to mean 'downfall' or 'destruction'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napuntahan nila ang mga **ruwina** ng isang sinaunang sibilisasyon.","translation":"They visited the **ruins** of an ancient civilization."},{"sentence":"Ang dating magandang bahay ay isa na lamang **ruwina**.","translation":"The once beautiful house is now just a **ruin**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang rolyo o lulon ng papel, tela, banig, o anumang bagay na maaaring ilulon.
original_explanation: Think of a diploma scroll, a rolled-up yoga mat, or even a giant lumpia before it's fried. It's anything that's been rolled into a tube shape. Before we had PDFs, ancient chismis was probably written on a `balumbon` of papyrus.
usage_notes: Often refers to documents, mats, or textiles. The verb form is 'balumbunin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inabot niya sa akin ang isang **balumbon** ng mga lumang mapa.","translation":"He handed me a **roll** of old maps."},{"sentence":"Itago mo ang **balumbon** ng banig sa ilalim ng kama.","translation":"Keep the **roll** of mat under the bed."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tradisyonal na sayaw ng panunuyo mula sa rehiyon ng Visayas, na nagpapakita ng paggalaw ng isang tandang at inahing manok.
etymology: From Spanish "curacha" (cockroach), though the dance movements are likened to fowls, not insects. The name's origin is debated.
original_explanation: The original "budots dance," but with more class and a barong. It's a folk dance, especially popular in Samar and Leyte, that mimics a rooster and hen during courtship. The best part is when people shower the dancers with money—it's like a live-action GoFundMe page set to festive music.
usage_notes: Primarily known in the Eastern Visayas region. It's a highlight of weddings, fiestas, and other celebrations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bagong kasal ang unang sumayaw ng **kuratsa** sa kanilang reception.","translation":"The newlyweds were the first to dance the **kuratsa** at their reception."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang nalikom na pera mula sa pagsasayaw ng **kuratsa** para sa proyekto ng barangay.","translation":"A large amount of money was collected from the **kuratsa** dance for the barangay's project."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tanyag na uri ng loterya sa Pilipinas na pinapatakbo ng Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office (PCSO) kung saan pumipili ng kombinasyon ng mga numero ang mananaya.
etymology: Shortened from Spanish 'lotería', popularized by the PCSO brand name 'Lotto'.
original_explanation: Ang pag-asa ng bayan every 9 PM. 'Yung kahit anong compute mo sa birthday, anniversary, at edad ng alaga mong aso, 'di pa rin tumatama. Pero sige pa rin taya, kasi... what if? 'Di ka mananalo kung 'di ka tataya. The national pastime of dreaming.
usage_notes: This is the everyday term for the national lottery game in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hala, ang laki na ng jackpot sa **loto**! Tataya ako mamaya.","translation":"Wow, the jackpot in the **lotto** is huge! I'll place a bet later."},{"sentence":"Laging mahaba ang pila sa mga outlet ng **loto** kapag malaki ang premyo.","translation":"The line at the **lotto** outlets is always long when the prize is big."}]

translation: to ripen fruit artificially; to let something mature
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagpapahinog ng prutas na pinitas na, karaniwan sa pamamagitan ng pagtatabi o pagbabalot nito sa isang madilim at saradong lugar.
etymology: From the prefix `mag-` (verb-forming prefix) and the root `in-in` (the act of artificially ripening fruit).
original_explanation: This is the OG life hack for unripe mangoes. You buy them green and hard from the palengke, wrap them in newspaper, and hide them in the rice dispenser (`bigasan`). A few days later, boom! Yellow, sweet mangoes. It's the process of forcing something to mature, like when your parents make you do chores to "build character."
usage_notes: Specifically used for ripening fruits after they have been picked. The most common method mentioned is placing them in a rice container.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **mag-in-in** ng mga saging para maging matamis.","translation":"We need **to ripen** the bananas to make them sweet."},{"sentence":"Inilagay niya ang mga mangga sa bigasan para **mag-in-in**.","translation":"She placed the mangoes in the rice container **to let them ripen**."}]

translation: to bring; to cause to arrive
meaning_filipino: Ang pagdating o pagpapadala ng isang bagay o tao sa isang tiyak na lugar o panahon.
original_explanation: This is what you tell your Grab driver to do with your food order. "Kuya, paki-idating na po sa lobby, gutom na ako." It's the verb form for making something arrive, like a package from Shopee or your friend who's always late.
usage_notes: The 'i-' prefix transforms the root 'dating' (arrival) into a causative verb, meaning 'to cause to arrive' or 'to bring something'. It's different from 'dumating' which means 'to arrive' (oneself).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **idating** mo ang mga dokumento bago mag-alas singko.","translation":"Please, **bring** the documents before five o'clock."},{"sentence":"Kailan kaya **idating** ng Lazada ang inorder kong sapatos?","translation":"I wonder when Lazada will **deliver** (cause to arrive) the shoes I ordered?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pook o lubluban, karaniwang putikan, kung saan naglulublob ang mga kalabaw o ibang malalaking hayop upang magpalamig.
etymology: Mula sa posibleng salitang-ugat na may kinalaman sa paglublob o paggulong sa putik.
original_explanation: Think of it as the local spa for our national animal, the carabao. It's their muddy jacuzzi, their personal cooling station after a long day of work under the hot Philippine sun. It's their 'me time' spot, pero sa putikan.
usage_notes: Isang salitang agrikultural at di-pangkaraniwan sa pang-araw-araw na usapan sa mga urban na lugar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masayang naglulublob ang mga kalabaw sa **ungulan** tuwing tanghali.","translation":"The carabaos are happily wallowing in the **mud pit** at noon."}]

translation: to bend; to warp; to become crooked
meaning_filipino: Ang pagyuko o pagbaluktot ng isang bagay na dati ay tuwid; ang pagiging hindi na deretso o pantay.
original_explanation: What happens to cheap utensils after one encounter with frozen ice cream. It's also what happens to your back after sitting in a monobloc chair for 8 hours straight. Or what happens to a politician's principles over time. Anything that was once straight, but isn't anymore.
usage_notes: Refers to the process of becoming bent or crooked. Can be used literally for objects or figuratively for abstract concepts like principles or one's path in life.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagbalikuko** ang alambre dahil sa bigat ng mga sampay.","translation":"The wire **bent** because of the weight of the laundry."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa init ng araw, **nagbalikuko** ang plastic na upuan.","translation":"Because of the sun's heat, the plastic chair **warped**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sanhi, dahilan, o paliwanag sa isang pangyayari, desisyon, o kilos.
original_explanation: The 'why' behind the 'what.' It's the excuse you give your boss for being late. It's the 'it's not you, it's me' speech. It's the deep, hugot-filled motive for your friend's sudden life changes. Everyone has a rason, whether it's valid, lame, or 'kasi, sinabi ng nanay ko.'
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'dahilan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **rason** kung bakit ka umalis?","translation":"What is the **reason** why you left?"},{"sentence":"Bigyan mo ako ng isang magandang **rason** para maniwala sa'yo.","translation":"Give me one good **reason** to believe you."}]

translation: condescending, disdainful, looking down on others
meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng pagmamaliit o mababang pagtingin sa kapwa, na para bang mas mataas ang sarili kaysa sa iba.
