etymology: From `ma-` + `pang-` + `mata` (eye). Literally "prone to using the eyes (to judge)".
original_explanation: This is the attitude of someone who looks at you from head to toe, tapos may kasamang irap. They judge your OOTD, your phone, your life choices. Sila 'yung mga taong ang standard ay kasing taas ng condo sa BGC, at lahat ng hindi umabot, "kawawa" sa paningin nila.
usage_notes: A very strong negative trait, synonymous with arrogance and looking down on people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala ang mayamang ginang sa pagiging **mapangmata** sa kanilang mga katulong.","translation":"The rich lady is known for being **condescending** to her helpers."},{"sentence":"Iwasan mo ang mga taong **mapangmata** dahil hindi sila makakabuti sa iyo.","translation":"Avoid **disdainful** people because they will not be good for you."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na namumuno, nangunguna, o may kapangyarihan sa isang grupo, organisasyon, o bansa.
etymology: From 'puno' (head/chief), possibly with a fossilized '-in-' infix, now functioning as a standalone noun.
original_explanation: The boss, the team lead, the barangay captain, the president. The person everyone looks at when things go wrong, and the person who takes the credit when things go right. Sila 'yung laging may 'final say.'
usage_notes: Distinct from 'puno' (tree) or 'puno' (full). The stress is on the second syllable: pi-NU-no.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pinuno** ng aming pangkat ang nagprisinta ng aming proyekto.","translation":"The **leader** of our group presented our project."},{"sentence":"Isang mabuting **pinuno** ang naglilingkod sa kanyang nasasakupan.","translation":"A good **leader** serves their constituents."}]

translation: dipper made of a tin can
meaning_filipino: Isang pansalok na gawa sa isang malaking lata, tulad ng lata ng gatas o mantika, na nilagyan ng hawakan.
original_explanation: The ultimate symbol of Filipino resourcefulness. This is what you get when you need a tabo but all you have is a big empty can of Nido or a can of cooking oil. It’s a DIY project born out of necessity. It might not be pretty, and you have to be careful with the sharp edges, but it gets the job done. Peak 'diskarte' culture.
usage_notes: A testament to Filipino ingenuity and the practice of upcycling before it was cool.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pansamantala, **tabong-lata** muna ang gamit namin habang wala pang pambili ng bagong tabo.","translation":"For now, we're using a **dipper made of a tin can** while we don't have money to buy a new one."},{"sentence":"Maingat niyang hinawakan ang **tabong-lata** upang hindi masugatan.","translation":"He carefully held the **tin can dipper** to avoid getting cut."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkilos ng pagkatawan o pagiging simbolo ng isang bagay o konsepto.
original_explanation: When your messy bun comes to 'sagisagin' your chaotic work week. Or when Jollibee starts to 'sagisagin' your longing for home when you're an OFW. It's when a simple thing takes on a much deeper, 'hugot'-filled meaning.
usage_notes: This is the object-focus form of the verb derived from 'sagisag'. The actor-focus form is 'sumagisag'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-aangat ng bandila ay **sinasagisag** ang ating kalayaan.","translation":"The raising of the flag **symbolizes** our freedom."},{"sentence":"Nais niyang **sagisagin** sa kanyang obra ang pag-asa ng mga kabataan.","translation":"He wants to **symbolize** the hope of the youth in his masterpiece."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ikaanim na buwan ng taon sa kalendaryong Gregorian, na mayroong 30 araw.
original_explanation: The month of weddings, Pride, and Philippine Independence Day. It's when school used to start, so it smells like new notebooks and floor wax for millennials. It's also the official start of the rainy season, so it's the month of 'may pasok ba?' announcements and epic floods.
usage_notes: Always capitalized as it is a proper noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Araw ng Kalayaan ng Pilipinas ay ipinagdiriwang tuwing ika-12 ng **Hunyo**.","translation":"Philippine Independence Day is celebrated every 12th of **June**."},{"sentence":"Maraming ikinakasal sa buwan ng **Hunyo**.","translation":"Many get married in the month of **June**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang seremonya o gawain ng pagkakaloob ng banal na pabor o basbas, karaniwang isinasagawa ng isang pari o taong may awtoridad sa relihiyon.
original_explanation: This is what the priest does to your new car so you don't get into accidents, or to a new house so the ghosts from the previous tenants move out. It's the formal version of your lola saying "God bless you" before you leave the house.
usage_notes: Primarily used in a religious or ceremonial context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging solemne ang **pagbebendisyon** sa bagong tayong kapilya.","translation":"The **blessing** of the newly built chapel was solemn."},{"sentence":"Isasabay ang **pagbebendisyon** ng mga alagang hayop sa pista ni San Roque.","translation":"The **blessing** of the pets will coincide with the feast of Saint Roch."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagmamadali; may kaunting oras lamang para gawin ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: The state of being when you have 5 minutes to get ready for a Zoom call you forgot about. It's the "dali-dali" mode, the "late na ako!" panic. When someone is apurado, they move like their life is on fast-forward, probably spilling coffee along the way.
usage_notes: Very common in everyday speech. Interchangeable with 'nagmamadali'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagi siyang **apurado** tuwing umaga papasok sa trabaho.","translation":"He is always **in a hurry** every morning on his way to work."},{"sentence":"Mukhang **apurado** ka, saan ang punta mo?","translation":"You look **rushed**, where are you off to?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na pinaikling anyo ng 'naroroon,' na nangangahulugang nasa malayong lugar na malayo sa nagsasalita at kausap.
original_explanation: This is the lazy, shortcut way of saying 'naroroon'. It's what you say when you're too tired to pronounce all the syllables. 'Asan si kuya?' '**Naron** sa kanto, bumibili ng yosi.' It’s fast, casual, and super common in everyday Pinoy street talk.
usage_notes: Strictly informal and conversational. You wouldn't write this in a formal paper, but you'd hear it constantly in the 'palengke' or while talking to a friend.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Saan mo nilagay yung payong? **Naron** sa may pinto.","translation":"Where did you put the umbrella? It's **over there** by the door."},{"sentence":"Hayaan mo na siya, **naron** na sa probinsya.","translation":"Just let him be, he's **over there** in the province now."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang bagay na pinutulan sa dulo, gaya ng buntot ng hayop, buhok, o kuko.
original_explanation: Think of a Doberman's tail, that's pungos. Or when your barber gets a little too scissor-happy with your bangs and they end up way too short. "Hala, pungos 'yung gupit sa'yo!" Can also apply to a pencil sharpened down to a tiny nub. It's something that's been shortened by cutting the tip.
usage_notes: Often used for animal tails, hair, or anything that has had its end cut off.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aso ng kapitan ay may **pungos** na buntot.","translation":"The captain's dog has a **docked** tail."},{"sentence":"Naging **pungos** ang lapis ko dahil sa kakatasa.","translation":"My pencil became **cut short** from too much sharpening."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang nagsasaad ng kasunod na pangyayari o kilos sa isang takdang panahon; sa dakong huli.
original_explanation: The most important word after "sweldo" (salary). It's the "what's next?" of the Filipino language. "Anong gagawin natin pagkatapos?" is the national question after every major event, from a movie to a final exam. It's the promise of a sequel, a dessert, or another round of chismis.
usage_notes: Extremely common. Can be followed by 'ng' (pagkatapos ng...) to mean 'after [noun]' or 'na' (pagkatapos na...) to mean 'after [verb clause]'. Often used interchangeably with 'matapos'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pagkatapos** ng klase, kumain tayo sa labas.","translation":"**After** class, let's eat out."},{"sentence":"Naligo siya, at **pagkatapos** ay natulog na.","translation":"He took a shower, and **afterwards**, he went to sleep."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghila o pag-unat sa isang bagay gamit ang lakas.
original_explanation: The struggle is real during a "tug-of-war" at a company team building. Also, that feeling in your muscles after your first day back at the gym. "Kailangan ng pagbatak sa sales para ma-hit ang quota!"
usage_notes: "Batak" or "pagbatak" can also be slang for using illegal drugs (shabu). This entry focuses on the literal meaning of pulling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sama-sama sila sa **pagbatak** ng malaking lambat.","translation":"They worked together in **pulling** the large net."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagbatak** sa lubid ang huling pagsubok sa paligsahan.","translation":"The **pulling** of the rope is the final challenge in the competition."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tubo na ginagamit sa paninigarilyo ng tabako; o isang mahabang tubo para sa daluyan ng tubig o ibang likido.
original_explanation: Can mean two things: 1) The old-school smoking device your lolo uses, making him look like a wise detective. 2) The tubes under your sink that burst at the worst possible time, forcing you to call a tubero. Context is key, my friend.
usage_notes: Can refer to a tobacco pipe or a conduit for liquids/gas (like a water pipe). The context usually makes the meaning clear.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May koleksyon ng mga lumang **pipa** ang aking lolo.","translation":"My grandfather has a collection of old **pipes**."},{"sentence":"Tumutulo ang **pipa** ng tubig sa ilalim ng lababo.","translation":"The water **pipe** under the sink is leaking."}]

translation: To tease playfully; to jest with
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbibiro o pagtukso sa isang tao sa paraang hindi nakakasakit o bilang isang anyo ng paglalambing.
original_explanation: The art of lovingly annoying someone. It's when your barkada keeps bringing up your crush's name when they're nearby, or when your lola pinches your cheeks saying 'tumaba ka,' but with a twinkle in her eye. It's 'tukso' with a hint of 'lambing'.
usage_notes: A form of teasing that is generally lighthearted and affectionate. Can be synonymous with 'kantiyawan' or 'biruan'. The root word 'gambol' is a homonym of the noun for 'tassel'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang **gambulin** ang kapatid mo, baka umiyak.","translation":"Don't **tease** your sibling anymore, they might cry."},{"sentence":"Mahilig **gambulin** ni Marco si Ana dahil may gusto siya rito.","translation":"Marco loves to **playfully tease** Ana because he has a crush on her."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang masusing paghahanap o pagsisiyasat sa isang lugar o bagay, kadalasan sa paraang nagdudulot ng kaunting gulo.
original_explanation: This is you frantically looking for your keys or wallet before leaving the house, turning your bag inside out. It's the police searching a crime scene for evidence. It's that 'Where's Waldo' level of searching.
usage_notes: Implies a very detailed and sometimes intrusive search.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hiniksik** ng mga pulis ang buong bahay para sa ebidensya.","translation":"The police **searched thoroughly** the entire house for evidence."},{"sentence":"**Hiniksik** niya ang kanyang bag ngunit hindi niya makita ang telepono.","translation":"She **rummaged through** her bag but couldn't find her phone."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang talim na mapurol at hindi na makahiwa nang maayos.
original_explanation: That tragic moment when your kitchen knife can't even slice a tomato and just squishes it. Yan ang ngidngid. It's the state of every pair of scissors in a Filipino household that has been used to cut everything from paper to wire to chicken bones.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to the dullness of a cutting edge.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ngidngid** na ang kutsilyo kaya kailangan nang hasain.","translation":"The knife is **blunt** so it needs to be sharpened."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong gamitin 'yan, **ngidngid** na ang gunting.","translation":"Don't use that, the scissors are **dull**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagbili at pagbebenta ng mga produkto o serbisyo; komersiyo.
original_explanation: This is the official business of the "marites" network—exchanging information. But for real, it’s what happens in Shopee, Lazada, and the palengke. The art of the deal, Pinoy style. "Buy and sell po tayo diyan."
usage_notes: A formal term for business or trade. 'Negosyo' is the more common, everyday term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pangangalakal** sa pagitan ng mga bansa ay mahalaga para sa ekonomiya.","translation":"**Trade** between countries is important for the economy."},{"sentence":"Bumagsak ang kanilang negosyo dahil sa mahinang **pangangalakal**.","translation":"Their enterprise failed due to weak **commerce**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang yunit ng bigat na katumbas ng labing-anim na onsa o humigit-kumulang 0.453592 kilogramo. Ginagamit din ito para sa pananalapi ng Britanya.
original_explanation: Before we went full metric, this was the OG way of weighing things at the palengke. "Ilang libra po ang manok?" Now, it's more known as the Zodiac sign for the titas who are into astrology, or the British Pound for your friend who just came back from London.
usage_notes: More commonly used in historical or specific contexts now, as 'kilo' is the standard. Also refers to the Zodiac sign.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng isang **libra**ng asukal sa tindahan.","translation":"Mother bought a **pound** of sugar at the store."},{"sentence":"Ang presyo ng baboy ay isandaang piso bawat **libra**.","translation":"The price of pork is one hundred pesos per **pound**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao, bagay, o gawain na kasuklam-suklam, hamak, at walang dangal.
original_explanation: Ito yung ugali ng kontrabida sa teleserye na handang manira ng buhay ng iba para sa sariling kapakanan. Yung tipong, "How dare you?!" ang reaction mo sa kanila. Level-up sa pagiging masama, ito yung taong walang moral compass.
usage_notes: Isang mabigat na salita na madalas gamitin sa pormal o pampanitikang konteksto upang ilarawan ang matinding kasamaang moral.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **imbi** niyang plano ay nabunyag sa lahat.","translation":"His **despicable** plan was revealed to everyone."},{"sentence":"Isang **imbi** na gawain ang pagtataksil sa bayan.","translation":"Betraying the country is a **vile** act."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bilog at itim na butas sa gitna ng iris ng mata, na nagpapahintulot sa liwanag na makapasok patungo sa retina.
etymology: From 'balin-' (a prefix denoting reflection or image) + 'tao' (person).
original_explanation: Literally 'image-person.' It's the pupil of the eye, named for the tiny reflection of a person you can see in it when you look closely. It's the window to the soul where you can literally see a tiny version of yourself. Ang poetic, 'di ba?
usage_notes: A very specific, anatomical, and somewhat literary term. 'Pupila' or 'itim ng mata' are more common in everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lumiliit ang ating **balintatao** kapag nasisilaw sa matinding liwanag.","translation":"Our **pupils** constrict when dazzled by intense light."},{"sentence":"Sa kanyang mga **balintatao**, nakita ko ang aking munting larawan.","translation":"In her **pupils**, I saw my own tiny reflection."}]

translation: to take care of; to manage; to look after
meaning_filipino: Magbigay ng kalinga, proteksyon, o superbisyon sa isang tao, bagay, o gawain.
original_explanation: This is the official verb of being a parent, a fur-parent, a plantito/plantita, or even the team lead who has to look after their 'pasaway' team members. It's the act of making sure something or someone doesn't just survive, but thrives.
usage_notes: The 'pang' prefix is often used instead in modern spoken language (e.g., 'pangalagaan'). 'Mangalaga' is slightly more formal or literary.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tungkulin nating **mangalaga** sa ating kalikasan.","translation":"It is our duty to **take care of** our environment."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **mangalaga** sa mga bata habang wala kami?","translation":"Who will **look after** the children while we are away?"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kalagayan ng pagiging paulit-ulit na tinusok o kinulimbat; butas-butas dahil sa pagdukit.
original_explanation: That annoying thing you do when you're bored, like poking holes in a styrofoam cup, or picking at the label of a beer bottle until it's gone. It's a motion of repeated, small, and sometimes destructive picking. Also what a chicken does to its food. 'Dukit-dukit na yung mansanas, ayoko na niyan.'
usage_notes: Can describe the state of an object ('dukit-dukit na') or the action itself ('pagdukit-dukit').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayoko nang kainin iyan, **dukit-dukit** na ng ibon.","translation":"I don't want to eat that anymore, it's been **repeatedly pecked at** by a bird."},{"sentence":"Ang pader ay **dukit-dukit** na dahil sa mga pako.","translation":"The wall is **full of small holes** from nails."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lumang salita para sa pagkuha o pagtanggap ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is a deep Tagalog word, the lolo of 'kumuha.' If you use 'kumaon' today, people might think you just came out of a time machine from the era of Jose Rizal. It means 'to take' or 'to get,' but with a very classic, literary flair. It's the vintage filter of verbs.
usage_notes: Archaic and poetic. 'Kumuha' is the modern and common equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumaon** siya ng isang bulaklak mula sa hardin.","translation":"He **took** a flower from the garden."},{"sentence":"Nais niyang **kumaon** ng tubig mula sa balon.","translation":"She wanted to **get** water from the well."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kasuotan o anumang gamit na isinusuot o dinadala sa pagpasok sa trabaho, paaralan, o opisina.
etymology: From 'pam-' (for) + 'pasok' (to enter, to go to school/work).
original_explanation: Your "outfit of the day" (#OOTD) for work or school. It's the uniform you hate, the corporate attire that makes you look "profesh," or the clothes you carefully picked out the night before only to realize it's laundry day. It's the armor you wear to battle traffic and deadlines.
usage_notes: Often refers to clothes, but can also refer to shoes or bags used for work/school.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Namamalantsa siya ng kanyang damit na **pampasok** para bukas.","translation":"She is ironing her **work clothes** for tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Bagong bili ang sapatos niyang **pampasok**.","translation":"His **school** shoes are newly bought."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang aklat o pormal na talaan kung saan itinatala ang mga transaksyong pampinansyal ng isang negosyo o indibidwal.
original_explanation: The notebook of a sari-sari store owner where all the "utang" is listed. Before Excel sheets, there was the mighty ledyer. It's the book of judgment that determines who gets to borrow money again and who's blacklisted. "Nakalista ka na sa ledyer ni Aling Nena."
usage_notes: Karaniwang iniuugnay sa pagtatala ng utang sa mga maliliit na tindahan o sa simpleng accounting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itala mo sa **ledyer** ang lahat ng pumasok na benta ngayon.","translation":"Record all of today's sales in the **ledger**."},{"sentence":"Puno na ang **ledyer** namin ng mga pangalan ng may utang.","translation":"Our **ledger** is already full of the names of debtors."}]

translation: to chop (wood); to fire/dismiss (from a job)
meaning_filipino: Hatiin o putulin ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay kahoy, sa pamamagitan ng malakas na pagtama ng palakol o katulad na kagamitan. Sa makabagong gamit, ito ay nangangahulugang tanggalin sa trabaho o tungkulin.
etymology: From 'sibak', meaning to split or cleave. The metaphorical extension to being fired is a 20th-century development.
original_explanation: Literally, it's what you do to firewood with an axe. 'Magsibak ng kahoy.' But in modern Pinoy slang, this is what happens when your boss tells you, 'You're fired!' It's the ultimate 'tanggal sa trabaho' move. 'Na-sibak si kuya sa BPO kasi laging late.' It's harsher than 'natanggal,' implying a forceful removal.
usage_notes: The meaning 'to fire from a job' is colloquial but very common. The literal meaning 'to chop wood' is more traditional.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **sibakin** ang mga kahoy na ito para may panggatong tayo.","translation":"You need to **chop** this wood so we have something for the fire."},{"sentence":"**Sinibak** sa trabaho ang empleyado dahil sa pagnanakaw.","translation":"The employee was **fired** from the job because of theft."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o resulta ng pagtutuos; ang maingat na pagtatantiya o pagpaplano.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa mo sa utak mo bago ka sumagot sa tanong na "Saan napunta sahod mo?". It's the mental math of figuring out how many vacation leaves you have left vs. how many long weekends there are. It's not just numbers, it's a strategy.
usage_notes: Refers to the act or result of calculating, while 'kalkula' is the verb root.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayon sa aking **kalkulasyon**, malulugi tayo sa proyektong ito.","translation":"According to my **calculation**, we will lose money on this project."},{"sentence":"Mali ang iyong **kalkulasyon** kaya sumobra ang binayad natin.","translation":"Your **calculation** was wrong, that's why we overpaid."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpapatalas sa isang bagay, karaniwan ay isang kasangkapang may talim tulad ng kutsilyo o gunting, sa pamamagitan ng pagkiskis nito sa isang hasaan.
original_explanation: Before you can slice the ingredients for your sinigang, you need to 'asa' the kutsilyo. It's that satisfying (or sometimes scary) sound of metal scraping against stone. It's also a metaphor for sharpening your skills. "Kailangan kong i-asa ang utak ko bago ang board exam."
usage_notes: Madalas ginagamit sa anyong 'ihasa' (to sharpen something) o 'mag-asa' (to sharpen).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan niya ang katulong na **mag-asa** ng mga kutsilyo.","translation":"He ordered the helper **to sharpen** the knives."},{"sentence":"I**hasa** mo muna ang itak bago mo gamitin.","translation":"**Sharpen** the bolo first before you use it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang aparato sa mga sasakyan o makina na nagpapababa ng temperatura ng makina sa pamamagitan ng pagpapalamig ng likidong dumadaloy dito.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung number one suspect mo 'pag umuusok na 'yung kotse mo sa gitna ng EDSA. Kung mainit ang ulo ng sasakyan mo, baka kailangan nang i-check ang radyetor. Think of it as the car's 'palamig' system.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumutulo ang tubig mula sa butas na **radyetor** ng lumang kotse.","translation":"Water is leaking from the hole in the old car's **radiator**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong mahilig magsabi ng mga papuri, na kadalasan ay hindi totoo, upang makuha ang loob o pabor ng iba.
original_explanation: That friend who's a master of 'sipsip' (sucking up) to the boss. Or that guy at the bar who has a script for every girl he talks to. That's a certified 'mambobola'. They can sell ice to an Eskimo with their sweet words. The verb is 'mambola', the person is the 'mambobola'.
usage_notes: Often has a negative connotation, implying insincerity and ulterior motives.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa opisina bilang isang tunay na **mambobola**.","translation":"He is known in the office as a real **flatterer**."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa kanya, isa siyang **mambobola** at baka may kailangan lang sa iyo.","translation":"Be careful with him, he's a **sweet-talker** and he probably just needs something from you."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapang pansara na nabubuksan sa pamamagitan ng susi o kombinasyon, ginagamit upang maikandado ang mga pinto, baul, o tarangkahan para sa seguridad.
original_explanation: The ultimate symbol of "bawal pumasok ang walang susi." It's what keeps your bike safe, your maleta secure, and your room private. Also, a metaphor for a closed-off heart. "May kandado na 'yang puso ko, 'wag mo nang pilitin." Hugot 101.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to a portable lock (padlock), but can be used for locks in general.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siguraduhing mailagay ang **kandado** sa pinto bago umalis ng bahay.","translation":"Make sure to put the **padlock** on the door before leaving the house."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang una o batayang uri sa isang serye o klasipikasyon.
original_explanation: Similar to 'pangunahing uri' but with a stronger sense of being 'number one' in a sequence. Think 'first-class' honors in school or the first model of a new phone. It's the prototype, the original, the first of its kind.
usage_notes: Ang "pangunang uri" ay nagbibigay-diin sa pagkakasunud-sunod ('unang uri'), samantalang ang "pangunahing uri" ay nagbibigay-diin sa kahalagahan ('pangunahing uri').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga dinosaur ang **pangunang uri** ng malalaking reptilya na namuhay sa mundo.","translation":"Dinosaurs were the **primary type** of large reptiles that lived on Earth."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malawak na lugar o dibisyon ng isang bansa o ng mundo, na may natatanging katangian ngunit hindi palaging may takdang hangganan.
original_explanation: This is what you learned in Sibika at Kultura. The Philippines is divided into different rehiyons, each with its own dialect, delicacies, and level of spiciness (shoutout to the Bicol Region!). It's like having different friend groups, each with its own inside jokes and 'flavor'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **Rehiyon** ng Ilocos ay kilala sa kanilang masasarap na pagkain.","translation":"The Ilocos **Region** is known for its delicious food."},{"sentence":"Nahahati ang Pilipinas sa labimpitong **rehiyon**.","translation":"The Philippines is divided into seventeen **regions**."}]

meaning_filipino: Talìan nang mahigpit ang mga kamay o paa ng isang tao o hayop upang hindi makagalaw.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na gusto mong gapusin 'yung sarili mo sa kama para hindi ka pumasok sa work on a Monday. Or more literally, what happens to the bad guy at the end of an action movie before the police arrive.
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of capture or physical restraint.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan ng kapitan ang kanyang mga tauhan na **gapusin** ang nahuling magnanakaw.","translation":"The captain ordered his men to **tie up** the captured thief."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagbibigay ng kalinga at tulong sa isang indibidwal na may sakit, matanda, o may kapansanan.
etymology: Nagmula sa unlaping "tagapag-" (tagagawa ng kilos) at salitang-ugat na "alaga" (kalinga).
original_explanation: The modern-day hero, often an OFW, who takes care of lolo or lola abroad. They're the ones with infinite patience, expert-level skills in making lugaw, and the ability to listen to the same story 100 times. A **tagapag-alaga** is basically a professional apo.
usage_notes: Ang salitang Ingles na 'caregiver' ay karaniwan ding ginagamit sa Pilipinas at madalas na ipinagpapalit sa 'tagapag-alaga'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha kami ng **tagapag-alaga** para sa aming lola na maysakit.","translation":"We hired a **caregiver** for our sick grandmother."}]

meaning_filipino: Iharap o ikompronta ang isang tao sa isang sitwasyon, problema, o ibang tao.
original_explanation: This is when it's time for a confrontation. It's the "let's settle this now" moment. Your boss wants to "paharapin" you to the client you messed up with. Or when your friend finally makes you and your other friend talk after a huge fight. It’s forcing a face-to-face, whether it’s with your responsibilities, your enemy, or the person who ate your leftover adobo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **paharapin** ang iyong mga takot upang malampasan ang mga ito.","translation":"You need to **make yourself face** your fears to overcome them."},{"sentence":"Pinag-usapan nila sa barangay at doon sila **pinaharap**.","translation":"They discussed it at the barangay and they were **made to face each other** there."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pagkakaroon ng magkatulad na katangian, anyo, halaga, o kalagayan.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'parejo' (even, level, alike).
original_explanation: The default answer when your mom asks who's her favorite child. Also the feeling when you and your bestie show up wearing the same Uniqlo shirt. 'Pareho tayo!' is the battle cry of accidental twinning and shared misery during a tough exam.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pareho** lang ang presyo ng bilihin dito at sa kabilang tindahan.","translation":"The price of goods here and in the other store are just the **same**."},{"sentence":"Mayroon kaming **pareho** na pangarap sa buhay.","translation":"We have the **same** dream in life."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang silid sa loob ng isang bahay o gusali, karaniwang ginagamit para sa pagtulog o pribadong gawain.
original_explanation: Your personal sanctuary. The place where you can be your true self, mag-mukmok, mag-binge watch ng K-drama, o mag-online class na naka-off ang camera. It's your bedroom, your personal space.
usage_notes: While it can mean any room, it most commonly refers to a bedroom.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumasok siya sa kanyang **kwarto** para magpahinga.","translation":"He entered his **room** to rest."},{"sentence":"Malinis at maayos ang **kwarto** ni Ana.","translation":"Ana's **bedroom** is clean and tidy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malapad na tabla, karaniwang kulay itim o berde, na sinusulatan gamit ang tisa o 'chalk'.
original_explanation: The OG PowerPoint. This is the blackboard your teacher used to write on with chalk (tisa) back in elementary. The sound of chalk screeching on the 'pisara' is a core memory for many Pinoys, along with the duty of being the 'blackboard eraser' for the day. Now mostly replaced by whiteboards, but the nostalgia is real.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to a chalkboard, though sometimes used colloquially for whiteboards too.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isinulat ng guro ang mga aralin sa **pisara**.","translation":"The teacher wrote the lessons on the **blackboard**."},{"sentence":"Pakibura ang mga nakasulat sa **pisara** pagkatapos ng klase.","translation":"Please erase the writings on the **chalkboard** after the class."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang punong guro o tagapamahala ng isang paaralan; ang pinakamataas na opisyal sa mga guro sa isang institusyon.
original_explanation: The final boss of the school. They're the one who approves your vacation leave, observes your class unexpectedly, and makes the god-tier 'Walang Pasok!' announcement. While 'ulong-guro' is the official DepEd term, most people just say 'prinsipal' to sound less like a textbook.
usage_notes: A formal term for a school principal. 'Prinsipal' is more common in colloquial speech, while 'punong-guro' is also a widely used formal alternative.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinatawag ng **ulong-guro** ang mga magulang ng mag-aaral.","translation":"The **head teacher** summoned the student's parents."},{"sentence":"Ang aming bagong **ulong-guro** ay dating isang guro sa agham.","translation":"Our new **principal** was formerly a science teacher."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto o kalagayan ng pagpapatuloy sa isang lugar, posisyon, o kondisyon; hindi pag-alis o pagbabago.
etymology: From the verb 'manatili' (to remain, to stay). The noun `pananatili` is formed from this verb, referring to the state or act of remaining. The ultimate root is the archaic 'tili' (stay, remain).
original_explanation: This is the art of 'staying put.' It's you, still working for the same company after 5 years despite the low pay because the coffee is free. It's your 'tita' who refuses to leave the family group chat despite the chaotic 'good morning' messages. It's the opposite of 'ghosting'—it's 'staying.'
usage_notes: Can refer to staying in a physical place, a job, a relationship, or maintaining a certain state or condition.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pananatili** sa bansa ay para sa kanyang pamilya.","translation":"His **staying** in the country is for his family."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **pananatili** ng kapayapaan sa rehiyon.","translation":"The **maintenance** (permanence) of peace in the region is important."}]

meaning_filipino: Puno o nababalutan ng alikabok; tumutukoy sa isang lugar o bagay na marumi dahil sa alikabok.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `ma-` (nagpapahiwatig ng katangian) at salitang-ugat na `alikabok` (dust).
original_explanation: The default state of a room after a long vacation. O 'yung kalsada sa probinsya na hindi sementado. Kung may "allergic rhinitis" ka, ito ang mortal enemy mo. It's the reason why you have to "punas-punas" your desk every morning.
usage_notes: Isang napakakaraniwang salita. Kasingkahulugan ng `maalabok`, ngunit ang `maalikabok` ay mas madalas gamitin sa modernong Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bodega ay **maalikabok** at madilim.","translation":"The storage room is **dusty** and dark."},{"sentence":"Linisin mo ang mesa, **maalikabok** na.","translation":"Clean the table, it's already **dusty**."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang daan, landas, o salaysay na may maraming sunod-sunod na kurbada o liko.
original_explanation: Describes the road to Baguio (Kennon Road), your thought process at 3 AM, or the plot of a Korean drama. It's the opposite of 'straight to the point.'
usage_notes: Reduplication of 'liko' to indicate multiplicity or intensity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahihilo ako sa **liku-likong** daan paakyat ng bundok.","translation":"I get dizzy on the **winding** road going up the mountain."},{"sentence":"Ang ilog ay may **liku-likong** landas patungo sa dagat.","translation":"The river has a **meandering** path towards the sea."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng gulay na mahaba, berde, at makipot na legumbre, karaniwang tinatawag na 'Baguio beans'.
original_explanation: The long, green veggie that's a staple in your sinigang or ginisang gulay. It's the less popular cousin of 'sitaw' (long beans) but shows up in more 'mestizo' dishes. Also known as Baguio beans because they thrive in the cold.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'Baguio beans' in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maghiwa ka ng **habitsuwelas** para sa ginisang baboy.","translation":"Slice some **green beans** for the sauteed pork."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng lagari na may mga ngiping idinisenyo para sa pagputol ng kahoy na kasabay o kahilera ng grano (wood grain).
etymology: From 'lagari' (saw) and 'panistis' (for ripping/splitting), from the root 'tistis' (to rip along the grain).
original_explanation: Not just any 'lagari' (saw). This is a specialist. If a regular saw is for cutting across the wood (like slicing bread), the lagaring panistis is for cutting *with* the grain (like splitting a string cheese). It's the right tool for a specific job, just like how you need a specific 'hugot' line for a specific kind of heartbreak.
usage_notes: This is a technical term used in carpentry.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit ang karpintero ng **lagaring panistis** para mahati ang mahabang tabla.","translation":"The carpenter used a **ripsaw** to split the long plank."},{"sentence":"Iba ang disenyo ng ngipin ng **lagaring panistis** kumpara sa lagaring pambalagtas.","translation":"The tooth design of a **ripsaw** is different from that of a crosscut saw."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng isdang-dagat na karaniwang kinakain sa Pilipinas, kilala bilang 'pagkain ng masa' dahil sa dati nitong mababang presyo.
original_explanation: The national fish of the Philippines, not by law, but by popular vote in every palengke and dining table. It's the fish you eat when it's 'petsa de peligro' but still tastes like a million bucks when fried to a crisp. The OG 'GG', its price is now an unofficial indicator of the country's economic health.
usage_notes: Often called 'GG' for short. Its market price is frequently cited in the news as an informal economic indicator for the common Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paksiw na **galunggong** ang ulam namin mamaya.","translation":"We're having sour fish stew with **mackerel scad** later."},{"sentence":"Tumaas na naman ang presyo ng **galunggong** sa palengke.","translation":"The price of **mackerel scad** at the market has gone up again."}]

translation: to hold in one's lap; to cradle
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-upo o paglalagay ng isang tao o bagay sa kandungan; ang pag-aruga o pag-alalay na parang isang sanggol.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'lambing' move. Ito yung action na ginagawa mo sa jowa mong pagod, sa aso mong clingy, o sa pamangkin mong antok na. Pag kinakalong mo ang isang bagay, you're basically saying, "Dito ka muna sa safe space mo, ako bahala sa'yo."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto niyang **kalungin** ang kanyang alagang pusa habang nanonood ng TV.","translation":"She wants to **hold** her pet cat **in her lap** while watching TV."},{"sentence":"**Kinalong** ng ina ang umiiyak na sanggol.","translation":"The mother **cradled** the crying baby."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na mamamayan o nagmula sa bansang India. Tumutukoy din sa mga bagay na may kaugnayan sa India.
original_explanation: Kilala sa pop culture bilang mga bida sa mga sumasayaw sa ulan na pelikula, o yung "Bumbay" na nagpapautang ng 5-6 (a stereotype, but a common cultural reference point). Also, source ng masasarap na curry at biryani. Note: "Bumbay" is often used but can be seen as derogatory; "Indiyan" is more neutral.
usage_notes: The term "Bumbay" is more common in colloquial speech but is sometimes considered offensive or a stereotype, especially when used in the context of money-lending. "Indiyan" is the more formal and neutral term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming pagkaing **Indiyan** ang mayaman sa pampalasa.","translation":"Many **Indian** foods are rich in spices."},{"sentence":"Ang kaibigan ko ay isang **Indiyan** na nagtatrabaho sa Makati.","translation":"My friend is an **Indian** who works in Makati."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na nilagyan ng maraming asin upang mapreserba o magkalasa.
etymology: Nagmula sa salitang-ugat na 'asin' na may unlaping 'in-' at hulaping '-an', na nangangahulugang 'nilagyan ng asin'.
original_explanation: This is what happens to food before there were refrigerators. Think of 'itlog na maalat' (salted egg), 'tuyo' (dried fish), or 'bagoong'. It's the original Filipino food preservation technique. In modern terms, it's what you feel like after a good cry session over a K-drama—all salty and dehydrated.
usage_notes: Ginagamit bilang pang-uri upang ilarawan ang isang pagkaing inimbak sa asin. Ang pandiwa nito ay 'in-asnan' (diniinan ang 'in') o 'inasinan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Inasnan** niya ang karne bago ito ibilad sa araw.","translation":"She **salted** the meat before drying it under the sun."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang manggang hilaw na may **inasnan** na alamang.","translation":"Green mango is delicious with **salted** shrimp paste."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalaman ng pinakamataas na dami na maaaring isilid; walang nang espasyo.
original_explanation: How you describe the MRT at 6 PM. How your stomach feels after an 'unli-rice' meal. How your heart feels when you're 'sana all'-ing. The stress is on the second syllable (pu-NÔ), which is super important to not mix it up with a tree.
usage_notes: The stress is on the last syllable (pu-NÔ). Often written with a circumflex accent (punô) in formal writing to differentiate it from the noun 'puno' (tree).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Puno** na ang bus, humanap na tayo ng ibang masasakyan.","translation":"The bus is already **full**, let's find another ride."},{"sentence":"Laging **puno** ang isipan niya ng mga alalahanin.","translation":"His mind is always **full** of worries."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsakay sa isang taxi bilang paraan ng transportasyon.
original_explanation: The verb form of "ayaw mag-jeep." This is what you do when you're running late, it's raining, or you just got your sahod and you feel like a baller for a day. Pre-Grab, this involved a lot of hand-waving and praying the driver uses the meter.
usage_notes: A common Taglish verb. In modern contexts, 'mag-Grab' is often used as a more specific alternative.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas mabuting **magtaxi** na lang tayo dahil umuulan nang malakas.","translation":"It's better if we just **take a taxi** because it's raining hard."},{"sentence":"Mahal **magtaxi** mula sa airport papuntang Makati.","translation":"It's expensive to **take a taxi** from the airport to Makati."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang umintindi, makaalam, o makatalos sa kahulugan, dahilan, o katangian ng isang bagay, sitwasyon, o tao.
original_explanation: Deeper than just 'intindi'. Unawa is comprehension with empathy. It's not just knowing your partner is mad; it's understanding *why*. It's what you ask for from your boss when you're late because of EDSA traffic: "Sana po may unawa kayo." It’s the highest form of 'gets'.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa mga anyong pandiwa tulad ng 'umunawa' (to understand), 'maunawaan' (to be able to understand), 'pag-unawa' (the act of understanding).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang susi sa isang matatag na relasyon ay ang malalim na **unawa** sa isa't isa.","translation":"The key to a strong relationship is a deep **understanding** of each other."},{"sentence":"Salamat sa iyong **unawa** sa aking sitwasyon.","translation":"Thank you for your **understanding** of my situation."}]

translation: act of blowing (a horn, trumpet); act of fanning flames
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-ihip ng hangin mula sa bibig, karaniwan upang patunugin ang isang instrumentong pang-ihip o upang palakasin ang apoy.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa ng referee sa basketball game, o 'yung tunog ng shofar sa mga historical movies. Pwede rin 'yung pag-ihip mo sa uling para sa inihaw na isda, 'yun ang pagbusa sa apoy. It's a forceful blow, not a gentle whisper.
usage_notes: More specific than 'pag-ihip'. 'Pagbusa' is for instruments or fanning flames, while 'pag-ihip' is more general (e.g., blowing a candle).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa **pagbusa** ng tambuli, nagsimula ang karera.","translation":"At the **blowing** of the horn, the race began."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang isang pamaypay para sa **pagbusa** ng apoy sa kalan.","translation":"He used a fan for the **fanning** of the fire in the stove."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang unang yugto ng pormal na edukasyon, karaniwang mula sa unang baitang hanggang ikaanim; mababang paaralan.
original_explanation: Ah, `primarya`. The good old days of 1-peso ice tubig, drawing mountains with a sun in between, and memorizing the Panatang Makabayan. This is where your academic trauma (or glory) began. Also known as 'elementarya.'
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'elementarya'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtapos ako ng **primarya** sa Mababang Paaralan ng San Roque.","translation":"I finished **elementary school** at San Roque Elementary School."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kilos ng kamay, ulo, o katawan na may partikular na kahulugan upang maghatid ng mensahe nang walang salita.
original_explanation: This is your non-verbal communication game. Yung pagturo ng nguso mo para ituro ang direksyon. Yung pagtaas mo ng kilay sa kaibigan mo para sabihing 'OMG, look!' That's a senyas. It's the secret language you use in a crowded room or when you're trying to cheat in a game.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to physical gestures, unlike "senyal" which can also be electronic or abstract. It's the basis for "sign language" (wikang pasenyas).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng **senyas** para ipahiwatig na kailangan na nilang umalis.","translation":"He used a **gesture** to indicate that they needed to leave."},{"sentence":"Ang simpleng pagtango ay isang **senyas** ng pagsang-ayon.","translation":"A simple nod is a **sign** of agreement."}]

translation: a bad job (shoddy work); an evil deed
meaning_filipino: Maaaring tumukoy sa (1) gawaing hindi pulido o mababa ang kalidad, o (2) isang gawain na labag sa batas o moralidad.
original_explanation: This has two flavors. 1) Shoddy work, like when the 'plumber' you hired just used duct tape to fix the leak. 2) A shady gig, the kind of 'trabaho' you see in action movies involving unmarked vans and briefcases. Think 'raket na delikado.'
usage_notes: The meaning depends on context. It can mean poorly done work ('gawang-palpak') or an illegal/immoral act ('masamang gawain').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-aayos ng pader ay **masamang trabaho**; hindi pantay ang pagkakapintura.","translation":"The wall repair is a **bad job**; the paint is uneven."},{"sentence":"Napilitan siyang pumasok sa **masamang trabaho** para may maipakain sa pamilya.","translation":"He was forced to take on an **evil deed** (illicit work) to feed his family."}]

translation: To be assigned; to be posted (to a place)
meaning_filipino: Ang maitalaga o mailagay sa isang partikular na lugar, trabaho, o posisyon, kadalasan ay bilang bahagi ng isang tungkulin.
original_explanation: This is a very BPO/corporate/military term. It's when your boss says, "Congratulations! You're being assigned to the night shift in our Alabang site," and you live in Quezon City. You've been madestino-d. It's like the Sorting Hat, but for your job assignment. From the Spanish word 'destino' (destination/destiny).
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of work, military, or official assignments.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga bagong pulis ay handang **madestino** kahit saang panig ng bansa.","translation":"The new police officers are ready **to be assigned** to any part of the country."},{"sentence":"Siya ay **nadestino** sa Mindanao noong kasagsagan ng gulo.","translation":"He **was posted** to Mindanao during the height of the conflict."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa ng isang bagay upang malaman ang resulta, kakayahan, o kalidad nito; ang pag-eeksperimento o pagtatangka.
original_explanation: This is your go-to word when your friend says 'Kaya mo ba?' (Can you do it?). It's the default response to any challenge, from eating a whole siling labuyo to confessing to your crush. 'Subukan lang natin, wala namang mawawala' is the official motto of the brave, the reckless, and those about to make a huge mistake.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin para sa pagsubok sa isang bagay, tao, o sitwasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Subukan** mong sagutin ang lahat ng tanong sa pagsusulit.","translation":"**Try** to answer all the questions in the exam."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **subukan**, alam mo ang kaya kong gawin.","translation":"Don't **test** me, you know what I can do."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging sensitibo sa damdamin ng iba o madaling makaramdam para sa kapwa.
etymology: Mula sa 'pagka-' + 'mapagdamdam' (sensitibo, may pakiramdam sa iba).
original_explanation: This is your friend who cries during the Meralco commercial. They feel everything, from the joy of a surprise party to the secondhand pain of a character in a teleserye. They're the opposite of 'manhid,' the designated 'i-comfort mo 'ko' person of the group.
usage_notes: Karaniwang may positibong konotasyon, na nagpapahiwatig ng pakikiramay at habag. Iba sa 'pagkamaramdamin' na tumutukoy sa pagiging madaling masaktan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinahangaan ko ang kanyang **pagkamapagdamdam** sa mga nangangailangan.","translation":"I admire her **empathy** for those in need."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapaliwanag o pagbibigay-kahulugan sa isang bagay, teksto, o pangyayari ayon sa sariling pagkaunawa.
original_explanation: Yung "K." na reply sa'yo ng jowa mo. Ang dami mong interpretasyon diyan! Galit ba siya? Tinatamad? O baka "Okay, noted with thanks" lang in corporate speak? Ikaw na bahala mag-decode.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bawat tao ay may kanya-kanyang **interpretasyon** sa isang likhang sining.","translation":"Every person has their own **interpretation** of a work of art."},{"sentence":"Maaaring magkaiba ang **interpretasyon** natin sa mga panuntunan.","translation":"We might have different **interpretations** of the rules."}]

translation: to recover, to make up for, to retaliate
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkuha muli ng isang bagay na nawala o naibigay; pagganti sa isang nagawang masama; o pagpunan sa isang pagkukulang.
original_explanation: The ultimate "comeback" move. It's when you lose the first round of Mobile Legends but dominate the next. It's posting a stunning travel pic after your ex posts their new partner. It's also what you promise to do for your friend after you forgot their birthday – "Babawi ako!"
usage_notes: A versatile word with a wide range of meanings from physical recovery to social redemption or even revenge.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Susubukan kong **bumawi** sa susunod na pagsusulit dahil mababa ang nakuha ko ngayon.","translation":"I will try to **make up for it** on the next exam because I got a low score today."},{"sentence":"Mabilis siyang **bumawi** ng lakas pagkatapos magkasakit.","translation":"He quickly **recovered** his strength after being sick."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, **bumawi** ka na lang sa Pasko.","translation":"Don't worry, just **make up for it** on Christmas."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang idyoma na tumutukoy sa isang taong matigas ang ulo, ayaw makinig sa payo o pangaral, o sadyang hindi sumusunod sa utos.
original_explanation: This is the classic Pinoy parent comeback when you just won't listen. It's like your ears are so full of *tutuli* (earwax) that their advice can't get in. Basically, you're being a 'pasaway'. "Anak, linisin mo kwarto mo!" "Mamaya na po." "Hay, may kulili ka talaga sa tainga!"
usage_notes: This is a figurative expression and doesn't literally mean the person has a lot of earwax, although it can be used humorously in that context too. It implies stubbornness or selective hearing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paulit-ulit ko nang sinasabi sa kanya na mag-aral nang mabuti, pero parang **may kulili ang tainga** niya.","translation":"I've repeatedly told him to study well, but it seems he's just **stubborn**."}]

meaning_filipino: Puno ng matinding damdamin; nagpapahayag ng malalim na emosyon.
etymology: Mula sa panlaping 'ma-' at salitang-ugat na 'damdamin' (feelings, emotion).
original_explanation: This is your friend who cries during the Meralco commercial. It's the vibe of every OPM ballad from the 90s. It's how you describe your ex's long, dramatic apology text that you know was copy-pasted. Full of feelings, sometimes too much.
usage_notes: Maaaring ilarawan ang isang tao, talumpati, kanta, pelikula, o anumang uri ng pagpapahayag.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumulat siya ng isang **madamdamin** na tula para sa kanyang minamahal.","translation":"He wrote a **passionate** poem for his beloved."},{"sentence":"Naging **madamdamin** ang kanyang talumpati kaya't napaiyak ang mga nakikinig.","translation":"Her speech became so **emotional** that the audience was moved to tears."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasuotang tela na isinasaklob sa unan upang maprotektahan ito at para sa kalinisan.
original_explanation: The only thing separating your face from that unan you've had since college. A good punda is life. A bad one is scratchy and makes you break out. Also, the designated bag for candies during Halloween trick-or-treating in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko nang palitan ang **punda** ng unan ko.","translation":"I need to change my pillow's **pillowcase** already."},{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng disenyo ng bagong bili mong **punda**.","translation":"The design of the **pillowcase** you just bought is beautiful."}]

translation: to send a text message (as a request)
meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na pakiusap o utos na magpadala ng mensahe sa pamamagitan ng text message sa cellphone.
etymology: Contraction of the Tagalog causative prefix `pa-` and the English word `text`. A common Taglish formation.
original_explanation: The official Batang 90s/early 2000s command. Before Messenger was king, this was how you asked for updates. "Patext ako 'pag nasa Jollibee na kayo." It's the ancestor of "PM is key". It's a blend of Tagalog 'pa-' (please do) and English 'text'.
usage_notes: Purely colloquial and very common in spoken language, especially from the early 2000s to mid-2010s. Not used in formal writing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Patext** naman kay Maria na male-late ako.","translation":"Please **send a text** to Maria that I'll be late."},{"sentence":"Wala na akong load, **patext** nga muna sa nanay ko.","translation":"I'm out of phone credits, can you **send a text** to my mom for me?"}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang lugar, bagay, o daanan na may maraming putik o basa at malagkit na lupa.
original_explanation: The state of most provincial roads and even some side streets in Manila after a 15-minute downpour. It's the reason you regret wearing your brand new white sneakers. 'Hala, ang maputik ng daan, paano tayo dadaan diyan?'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **maputik** ang buong bakuran pagkatapos ng malakas na ulan.","translation":"The entire yard became **muddy** after the heavy rain."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa daan dahil **maputik**.","translation":"Be careful on the road because it is **muddy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang propesyonal sa kalusugan na lisensyadong maghanda, mag-asikaso, at magbenta ng mga gamot ayon sa reseta ng doktor.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "farmacéutico." Ang baybay ay inangkop sa ponolohiyang Tagalog.
original_explanation: Sila 'yung mga bayani sa likod ng counter ng Mercury Drug o Watsons na nakakaintindi ng sulat-doktor mo. They're not just cashiers; they're the experts who make sure you're getting the right medicine and dosage. So next time, 'wag mo silang barahin 'pag tinanong kung para saan 'yung gamot. They're just doing their job to keep you safe!
usage_notes: Ang terminong Ingles na "pharmacist" ay karaniwan ding ginagamit. Ang kaugnay na salita ay "botikaryo," na isang mas lumang termino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinanong ko ang **parmaseutiko** kung may generic version ba ang gamot ko.","translation":"I asked the **pharmacist** if there was a generic version of my medicine."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong mag-aral nang mabuti upang maging isang **parmaseutiko**.","translation":"You need to study hard to become a **pharmacist**."}]

meaning_filipino: Madaling umiyak o mapaiyak; may tendensiyang maging emosyonal at lumuha.
original_explanation: This is your friend who cries during the Meralco commercial, the graduation scene in a movie, and when they see a cute puppy. They have a subscription to "iyak-later." If "hugot" was a person, they'd be **maluhain**. Their tear ducts are always on standby, ready for action at the slightest emotional trigger.
usage_notes: Describes a person's disposition or temporary emotional state. The suffix '-in' denotes a tendency or proneness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **maluhain** siya mula nang iwan siya ng kanyang kasintahan.","translation":"She became **prone to crying** ever since her boyfriend left her."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, **maluhain** lang talaga ako kapag nanonood ng drama.","translation":"Don't worry, I just get really **tearful** when I watch dramas."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sustansiya o lunas na kumokontra sa epekto ng lason.
original_explanation: Ang sagot sa "lason" mo. Kung ang lason ay ang ex mong toxic, ang antidoto ay ang masayang single life mo o 'yung bagong cutie na nameet mo. Basically, the cure for what's poisoning you, whether it's a snake bite or a bad memory.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghahanap sila ng **antidoto** para sa kamandag ng ahas.","translation":"They are looking for an **antidote** for the snake venom."},{"sentence":"Ang pagpapatawad ang **antidoto** sa galit.","translation":"Forgiveness is the **antidote** to anger."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalakbay o paglalayag sa kahabaan ng baybayin o pampang ng isang anyong tubig.
original_explanation: The scenic route! It's that picturesque drive or boat ride with the water on one side and land on the other. Think of a road trip through a coastal province, where every turn gives you a new view of the sea. Perfect for your travel vlog.
usage_notes: Often used in travel, geography, or historical narratives about voyages. The stress is on the last syllable (bu-may-BAY).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumaybay** ang aming sinasakyang bus sa magandang baybayin ng Ilocos.","translation":"The bus we were riding **traveled along the coast** of the beautiful shores of Ilocos."},{"sentence":"Ang mga sinaunang mangangalakal ay **bumaybay** sa mga isla ng Pilipinas.","translation":"The ancient traders **traveled along the coasts** of the Philippine islands."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malalim na pag-unawa o pag-alam sa isang bagay na mahirap intindihin, tulad ng isang konsepto, damdamin, o hiwaga.
original_explanation: This is more than just 'gets ko.' This is when you finally understand the ending of an indie film, the a-ha! moment when you get your parents' 'kasi nung panahon namin...' stories, or why your ex did what they did. It's deep-level, 3-AM-thoughts kind of understanding.
usage_notes: Often used in formal, literary, or philosophical contexts. It implies a deeper level of understanding than 'maintindihan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **matarok** ang lalim ng kanyang kalungkutan.","translation":"It is difficult to **fathom** the depth of his sadness."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan kong **matarok** ang tunay na kahulugan ng tula.","translation":"I am trying to **comprehend** the true meaning of the poem."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapahayag ng matinding pagpuna o pag-atake sa isang tao, ideya, o gawa, kadalasan sa paraang pormal o pampubliko.
original_explanation: Parang yung ginagawa ng mga Marites sa social media, pero mas professional at may resibo. Ito yung gigil mong i-call out ang isang mali o injustice, hindi lang basta chismis. Think of it as a formal "roast" or a fiery "call-out post" against a policy, a person, or an idea.
usage_notes: Often used in political commentary, formal debates, or academic critiques.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumuligsa** ang senador sa bagong panukalang batas.","translation":"The senator **criticized** the new proposed law."},{"sentence":"Maraming mamamahayag ang **tumuligsa** sa korapsyon sa gobyerno.","translation":"Many journalists **attacked** the corruption in the government."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan, karaniwang gawa sa magaspang na bato o metal, na ginagamit upang alisin ang mga kalyo at tuyong balat sa talampakan.
original_explanation: The OG beauty tool for your 'paa' goals. Before foot spas became a thing, your lola had this secret weapon to keep her feet smoother than your love life. It's the manual labor version of a pedicure, often a simple 'bato' from the river.
usage_notes: Can refer to a natural pumice stone ('bato') or a manufactured foot file.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko nang bumili ng bagong **kuskusan ng paa** dahil pudpod na ang luma.","translation":"I need to buy a new **foot file** because the old one is worn out."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos magbabad ng paa sa maligamgam na tubig, gumamit ka ng **kuskusan ng paa**.","translation":"After soaking your feet in warm water, use a **pumice stone**."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi kayang tiisin o batahin dahil sa matinding hirap, sakit, o sama ng kalagayan.
original_explanation: The summer heat in Manila without aircon? The sound of your neighbor's karaoke at 2 AM on a Tuesday? A toxic work environment? Lahat 'yan ay di-mapagtitiisan. It's that feeling of "I can't take this anymore!" when your patience and endurance have finally run out.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan ng isang sitwasyon, pakiramdam, o kondisyon na lumampas na sa hangganan ng kayang tiisin ng isang tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **di-mapagtitiisan** ang sakit ng kanyang ngipin kaya nagpatingin na siya sa dentista.","translation":"The pain in his tooth became **unbearable**, so he went to see a dentist."},{"sentence":"Ang init ng panahon ay **di-mapagtitiisan** kung walang bentilador.","translation":"The heat of the weather is **intolerable** without a fan."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong kulang sa pag-iisip, talino, o sentido komun; hangal.
original_explanation: A classic, almost Shakespearean-sounding insult your lola might use. It's more than just 'bobo'; it implies a special kind of reckless stupidity. It's the person who invests their life savings in a crypto coin a stranger on Facebook told them about. 'Huwag kang maging hunghang!'
usage_notes: A strong and somewhat old-fashioned insult.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tanging isang **hunghang** ang maniniwala sa kanyang mga kasinungalingan.","translation":"Only a **fool** would believe his lies."},{"sentence":"Ang **hunghang** na desisyon niya ay nagdulot ng malaking problema.","translation":"His **idiotic** decision caused a big problem."}]

translation: To haggle; to bargain down the price
meaning_filipino: Ang paghiling o pagsubok na makuha ang isang produkto o serbisyo sa mas mababang halaga kaysa sa orihinal na presyo nito sa pamamagitan ng pakikipagtawaran.
etymology: From 'barat', which means cheap or a cheapskate, possibly from Spanish 'barato' (cheap).
original_explanation: The national sport of the Filipino palengke. It's the art of charmingly, persistently, and sometimes dramatically, asking 'wala na bang tawad?' until the seller gives in. Mastering this can save you 20 pesos, which you can then use to buy extra chicharon. It's a win-win.
usage_notes: This is the verb form. The person who haggles is 'mamamaràt' and the quality of being a haggler is 'barat'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Subukan mong **baratahin** ang presyo ng isda sa palengke.","translation":"Try to **haggle** the price of the fish at the market."},{"sentence":"Kahit sa mall, sinusubukan niyang **baratahin** ang mga bilihin.","translation":"Even at the mall, she tries to **bargain down the price of** the goods."}]

translation: all at the same time; simultaneously
meaning_filipino: Nangyayari o isinasagawa nang magkakasama sa iisang tiyak na sandali o panahon.
original_explanation: The official adverb of Filipino family outings and group projects. 'Okay, picture na! Smile sabay-sabay!' It's the chaos of everyone trying to talk at once during a Zoom meeting. It means 'all together now!'
usage_notes: Emphasizes that multiple people or things are doing the same action simultaneously.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sabay-sabay** silang nagsigawan nang makita ang kanilang idolo.","translation":"They **all shouted at the same time** when they saw their idol."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating kumilos nang **sabay-sabay** para malutas ang problemang ito.","translation":"We need to act **simultaneously** to solve this problem."}]

meaning_filipino: Bukod sa; isang ekspresyon na nagbubukod sa isang bagay, tao, o sitwasyon mula sa isang pangkalahatang pahayag.
original_explanation: This is the "pero..." or "kaso..." of your sentence. It's how you make a general statement but then immediately add a disclaimer. "Lahat sila invited... maliban sa ex mo." It's the ultimate tool for strategic exclusion.
usage_notes: A prepositional phrase used to introduce an exception.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumakain ako ng lahat ng gulay **maliban sa** ampalaya.","translation":"I eat all vegetables **except for** bitter gourd."},{"sentence":"Tahimik ang buong klase **maliban sa** dalawang nag-iingay sa likod.","translation":"The whole class was quiet **aside from** the two making noise at the back."}]

translation: to lay a hand/arm on; to rest upon gently
meaning_filipino: Ang marahang pagpapatong ng kamay, braso, o anumang bahagi ng katawan sa ibabaw ng isang bagay o tao, karaniwang nagpapahiwatig ng pag-aalaga, pag-alo, o pagpapahinga.
original_explanation: This is that gentle, comforting touch. Parang 'yung pagpatong ng kamay ng kaibigan mo sa balikat mo when you're having a bad day, whispering 'kaya mo 'yan.' It's not a hard press, it's a light, reassuring gesture. Think of a cat gently resting its paw on you, or how your head 'dumantay' sa unan after a long day of adulting.
usage_notes: Carries a poetic and gentle connotation. Often used to describe acts of comfort, sympathy, or rest.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dumantay** ang kanyang kamay sa aking balikat bilang pakikiramay.","translation":"His hand **rested gently** on my shoulder in sympathy."},{"sentence":"Habang natutulog, **dumantay** ang ulo ng bata sa braso ng kanyang ina.","translation":"While sleeping, the child's head **rested upon** its mother's arm."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng sagabal o balakid upang pigilan ang isang gawain, plano, o pag-usad ng isang tao.
original_explanation: To be a 'kontrabida' to someone's success or plans. It's the overprotective parent who won't let their child follow their dreams, the slow car in the fast lane, or the sudden rain on your beach trip. Anything or anyone that gets in your way and makes you say, 'Bakit ba ang daming hadlang?!'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **maghadlang** sa mga pangarap ng iyong anak.","translation":"Do not **hinder** your child's dreams."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng kalaban na **maghadlang** sa aming tagumpay, ngunit nabigo sila.","translation":"The opponent tried to **obstruct** our victory, but they failed."}]

translation: to hide something from someone; to use as a hiding place
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggamit ng isang lugar bilang taguan, o ang sadyang pagkubli ng isang bagay o kaalaman mula sa isang tao.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of what you do when your friend asks "Saan mo tinago yung charger ko?" and you pretend you don't know. It's also what you do when you see your tita who always asks "Kailan ka mag-aasawa?" at the family reunion. You find a place to pagtaguan.
usage_notes: Often used to mean "to hide from someone" or "to hide something in a place". The focus is on the person being hidden from or the place used for hiding.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **pagtaguan** ng sekreto.","translation":"Don't **hide** secrets **from** me."},{"sentence":"Ang lumang bodega ang ginawa nilang **pagtaguan**.","translation":"They used the old warehouse as their **hiding place**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinuno o lider ng isang organisasyon o pangkat; isang impormal na tawag sa isang kaibigan o kakilala.
original_explanation: A casual way to call a male friend, a security guard, a police officer, or your actual boss. It's the friendlier, more Pinoy version of 'sir' or 'bro'. 'Chief, pa-assist naman dito!' is something you'd hear in an office or at a parking lot.
usage_notes: The pronunciation is often Filipinized to /tsip/. Can be a term of respect, a casual greeting, or a formal title (e.g., Police Chief).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hoy **chief**, kamusta na?","translation":"Hey **chief** (boss/bro), how are you?"},{"sentence":"Siya ang bagong **chief** ng pulisya.","translation":"He is the new **chief** of police."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kabiguan na isagawa o sundin ang isang tungkulin, pangako, kasunduan, o utos.
original_explanation: Ever promised your friend you'd pay them back by payday, but then a 12.12 sale happened? That's di-pagtupad. It's breaking a promise, whether it's a legal contract or just a "pinky swear." The reason why you get a "Failed" mark or a memo from HR.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa kontekstong legal, pang-negosyo, at pormal upang tumukoy sa paglabag sa kontrata o tungkulin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **di-pagtupad** sa kontrata ay may kaukulang parusa.","translation":"**Non-compliance** with the contract has corresponding penalties."},{"sentence":"Sinampahan siya ng kaso dahil sa **di-pagtupad** sa kanilang kasunduan.","translation":"A case was filed against him for his **failure to fulfill** their agreement."}]

meaning_filipino: Isinabit sa isang mataas na lugar; o di kaya'y hindi tinuloy o pinananabik sa isang sitwasyon.
original_explanation: This has two major vibes. 1) The literal: Binitin 'yung mga sinampay sa labas. (The laundry was hung outside). 2) The "sana all" is not available: 'Yung crush mo na pa-fall. He left you hanging. Binitin ka niya. It's the feeling of being on episode 7 of a K-drama and Netflix crashes. Nakakabitin!
usage_notes: Can be literal (to hang an object) or figurative (to leave someone in suspense or unsatisfied). The figurative sense is very common in modern conversations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Binitin** ang parol sa may bintana para sa Pasko.","translation":"The Christmas lantern **was hung** by the window."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **binitin** sa kuwento, ituloy mo na!","translation":"Don't **leave me hanging** with the story, continue it!"}]

translation: to have an occasion; to get a chance/opportunity
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng pagkakataon, sanhi, o angkop na panahon upang gawin o mangyari ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: That moment when you've been wanting to wear your new dress and someone finally invites you to a party. That's when you `magkaokasyon` to wear it. It's having the perfect excuse or opportunity to do something you've been wanting to do. 'Pag nagka-okasyon, treat kita!' is a classic line that may or may not happen.
usage_notes: Can refer to a formal event (occasion) or a simple opportunity (chance).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **magkaokasyon** tayong magkita muli.","translation":"I hope we **get a chance** to see each other again."},{"sentence":"Nang **magkaokasyon**, agad niyang sinabi ang kanyang saloobin.","translation":"When he **had the opportunity**, he immediately said what was on his mind."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halamang palumpong (Indigofera tinctoria) na pinagkukunan ng tina o pangkulay na asul.
etymology: From `tina` (dye) + `-an` suffix, with reduplication, meaning 'a plant that is like or a source of dye'.
original_explanation: Before synthetic dyes became the G.O.A.T., this plant was the OG source for that classic blue color in your *maong* (denim) pants. It's the natural, artisanal version of your blue food coloring, but for clothes.
usage_notes: Often used in botanical or historical contexts related to dyeing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **tina-tinaan** ay mahalaga sa industriya ng tela noong unang panahon.","translation":"The **indigo plant** was important in the textile industry in the olden days."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpuna o pagbibigay ng negatibong komento o hatol sa gawa, kilos, o ideya ng iba.
original_explanation: What you get from your tita at a family reunion: "Uy, tumaba ka!" It's also what happens in the comment section of any political post on Facebook.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatanggap ng matinding **pagbatikos** ang bagong panukalang batas.","translation":"The new proposed law received intense **criticism**."},{"sentence":"Handa siyang harapin ang anumang **pagbatikos** mula sa publiko.","translation":"He is ready to face any **censure** from the public."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pormal o malalim na salita para sa pag-alis sa isang lugar, na kadalasan ay may implikasyong permanente o may malaking kahalagahan.
original_explanation: This isn't just "umalis." This is leaving with ~*drama*~ and ~*significance*~. 'Yung OFW na paalis for a 2-year contract? Lumisan siya. 'Yung bida sa pelikula na nag-walk away into the sunset? Lumisan. Hindi ito 'yung pag-alis para bumili ng suka sa kanto. It has weight.
usage_notes: A more formal and poetic synonym for "umalis." Often used to describe leaving a home, country, or a significant place, or in the context of death ("lumisan sa mundo").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malungkot ang buong pamilya nang **lumisan** siya papuntang ibang bansa.","translation":"The whole family was sad when she **departed** for another country."},{"sentence":"Maraming bayani ang **lumisan** na, ngunit ang kanilang alaala ay mananatili.","translation":"Many heroes have **passed away**, but their memory will remain."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa Panahong Jurassic, isang yugto sa kasaysayan ng daigdig. Sa kolokyal na gamit, nangangahulugang napakatanda o luma na.
etymology: Loanword from English "Jurassic", referring to the geologic period.
original_explanation: Officially, it's about dinosaurs. Unofficially, it's what you call your friend's phone that still has a keypad, the office computer that runs on Windows 98, or your tito's jokes that were probably old when dinosaurs still roamed the earth. It's a step beyond "luma" or "antigo"—it's comically, anciently old.
usage_notes: Often used hyperbolically to describe something as extremely old or outdated.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Grabe, **Jurassic** pa yata ang computer na gamit mo!","translation":"Wow, the computer you're using seems to be from the **Jurassic** era!"},{"sentence":"Ang mga damit na iyan ay parang galing pa sa **Jurassic** period.","translation":"Those clothes look like they came from the **Jurassic** period."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na nakalutang sa tubig, ginagamit bilang pananda, babala, o tulong sa paglangoy.
original_explanation: This is your 'salbabida' or life preserver's more technical cousin. It's that floating thing in the sea that tells boats where to go or where the fishing nets are. In life, your 'timbulan' could be that one friend who keeps you afloat when you're drowning in problems (or in deadlines).
usage_notes: Ang 'salbabida' ay mas karaniwang ginagamit para sa life preserver. Ang 'timbulan' ay mas tumutukoy sa mga pananda sa tubig.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglagay ang mga mangingisda ng **timbulan** upang markahan ang kanilang mga lambat.","translation":"The fishermen placed a **buoy** to mark their nets."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sikat na pagkaing Koreano na binubuo ng inihaw na tiyan ng baboy. Sa Pilipinas, tumutukoy na rin ito sa karanasan ng pagkain sa mga Korean barbecue restaurant na may "unlimited" na handog.
etymology: From Korean "samgyeopsal" (삼겹살), meaning "three-layered flesh" referring to pork belly.
original_explanation: The Philippines' national sport. It's not just food (grilled pork belly), it's an event. It's the answer to "Saan tayo kakain?" and "Kamusta ka na?" A whole therapy session over a grill, unlimited side dishes, and the lingering smell on your clothes that says, "Yes, I made good life choices today." Let's go **samgyup**!
usage_notes: Shortened term for samgyeopsal. It can refer to the food itself or the entire dining experience.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tara, mag-**samgyup** tayo sa Sabado! Treat ko.","translation":"Let's go for **samgyup** on Saturday! My treat."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang agham na nag-aaral sa mga katangian, komposisyon, at istruktura ng mga sangkap at ang mga pagbabagong kanilang pinagdadaanan. Maaari din itong tumukoy sa emosyonal o sekswal na atraksyon sa pagitan ng dalawang tao.
original_explanation: The subject you probably struggled with in high school. But more importantly, it's that magical "spark" between two people. If you have great kemistri with someone, the conversation just flows, and you feel a connection. If not, it's like a first date that feels like a job interview. "Walang kemistri" is the official diagnosis for a failed love team.
usage_notes: Used both for the scientific field and the interpersonal connection. The spelling "kimika" is the formal, academic term for the science.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malakas talaga ang **kemistri** ng mga bida sa bagong teleserye.","translation":"The lead actors in the new TV series really have strong **chemistry**."},{"sentence":"Nahihirapan ako sa subject naming **kemistri** ngayong semestre.","translation":"I'm having a hard time with our **chemistry** subject this semester."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang operasyon sa aritmetika na katumbas ng paulit-ulit na pagdaragdag ng isang numero sa sarili nito; ang proseso ng pagpaparami.
original_explanation: Ito yung subject sa Math na una mong minemorize (multiplication table, anyone?). Sa totoong buhay, ito yung nangyayari sa utang mo 'pag may interest, or sa chismis na kumakalat sa office. It grows exponentially!
usage_notes: Ang pamantayan at pormal na termino para sa mathematical multiplication.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng mga bata ang **multiplikasyon** sa ikatlong baitang.","translation":"The children are studying **multiplication** in the third grade."},{"sentence":"Ang sagot sa 2 times 3 ay 6, isang simpleng halimbawa ng **multiplikasyon**.","translation":"The answer to 2 times 3 is 6, a simple example of **multiplication**."}]

translation: to cackle; to laugh loudly and coarsely
meaning_filipino: Tumawa nang malakas at magaspang, na parang tunog ng isang halimaw o mangkukulam.
etymology: From the onomatopoeic root `hakhak`, imitating a coarse laugh.
original_explanation: This isn't your cute little "haha" giggle. This is the full-on, kontrabida-in-a-teleserye laugh. Imagine the evil stepmother who just successfully stole the family inheritance—that's the "hakhak" sound. It's a laugh that's so over-the-top, it's almost villainous. "Hakhakin" is the verb form, to perform this kind of laugh.
usage_notes: Often used in literature or storytelling to describe a villain's or a very boisterous person's laugh.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig naming **hakhakin** ng mangkukulam ang kanyang tagumpay.","translation":"We heard the witch **cackle** at her success."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **hakhakin** diyan, nakakahiya sa mga kapitbahay!","translation":"Don't **laugh so coarsely** there, it's embarrassing to the neighbors!"}]

translation: to cause restlessness; to cause distress
meaning_filipino: Ang maging dahilan ng matinding pag-aalala, hindi mapakali, o pagkaligalig ng isang tao.
etymology: Mula sa panlaping 'ika-' (panlaping sanhi) at 'balisa' (restless, distressed).
original_explanation: Synonymous with ikabagabag, but with a bit more praning (paranoia) energy. It's what you feel when you've sent a risky text and you see the other person is typing... then stops... then is typing again. The uncertainty is what ikinabalisa mo.
usage_notes: Tulad ng 'ikabagabag', ito ay isang pandiwang sanhi. Ang 'balisa' ay madalas na nagpapahiwatig ng pisikal na manipestasyon ng pagkabalisa, tulad ng hindi mapakali o pagiging malikot.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang masamang balita ay **ikinabalisa** ng buong komunidad.","translation":"The bad news **caused distress** to the whole community."},{"sentence":"**Ikinabalisa** ko ang hindi niya pagsagot sa aking mga tawag.","translation":"His not answering my calls **made me restless**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng kulay o kolor sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung command na binibigay sa 'yo sa coloring book noong bata ka. "Okay class, koloran ninyo ang drawing ni Rizal." It’s the verb form of making something less boring and black-and-white. Parang paglalagay ng filter sa IG story mo, pero analog version.
