usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong **ice cream** ang may lasang mangga.","translation":"My favorite **ice cream** is mango-flavored."},{"sentence":"Tara, bili tayo ng **ice cream** sa kanto!","translation":"C'mon, let's buy **ice cream** at the corner!"}]

translation: to declare; to announce; to reveal
meaning_filipino: Isapubliko o ipaalam ang isang bagay na lihim o hindi pa nalalaman ng karamihan; magpahayag ng saloobin o impormasyon.
original_explanation: This is the 'grand reveal' verb. It's what a celebrity does with their new relationship in a tell-all interview. It's what you do when you finally post 'In a Relationship' on Facebook. From a president's SONA to a simple 'I love you,' if you're making it known, you're 'inihayag' it. The ultimate #SanaAll ng mga torpe.
usage_notes: Has a formal and often significant connotation. Used for important announcements, declarations of feelings, or revealing secrets.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Panahon na upang **ihayag** ang katotohanan.","translation":"It is time **to reveal** the truth."},{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **inihayag** na niya ang kanyang pag-ibig para sa dalaga.","translation":"Finally, he **declared** his love for the young woman."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mga kilos, gawi, o asal na paulit-ulit na ginagawa ng isang tao na nagiging bahagi na ng kanyang pagkatao. Maaari rin itong tumukoy sa tradisyon o kaugalian ng isang grupo o lipunan.
etymology: From Malay 'ugahari' meaning moderate, average, which evolved in meaning.
original_explanation: This is your default setting. 'Yung pagiging late mo palagi, that's an ugali. 'Yung pag-check mo ng phone pagkagising, ugali 'yan. It's your personality's OS, the code that runs in the background. Pwedeng "Filipino hospitality" or pwedeng "toxic Filipino traits." It's what makes you, you... for better or for worse.
usage_notes: A very common word used to describe both individual and collective behaviors.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap baguhin ang masamang **ugali**.","translation":"It's hard to change a bad **habit**."},{"sentence":"Naging **ugali** na ng mga Pilipino ang pagiging magiliw sa mga bisita.","translation":"It has become a **custom** for Filipinos to be hospitable to visitors."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kasuotan na isinusuot sa ulo, karaniwang may korona at labi, upang magbigay-proteksyon laban sa araw o ulan, o bilang palamuti.
original_explanation: Your lolo's favorite accessory, especially the straw ones used in the province. It's the OG bucket hat. Before there were caps and beanies, there was the mighty sambalilo. Perfect for farming or just looking dramatically mysterious while staring at the rice fields.
usage_notes: While "sumbrero" is more common, "sambalilo" is a classic, often more poetic or traditional term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Suot ng magsasaka ang kanyang **sambalilo** habang nag-aararo sa bukid.","translation":"The farmer wore his **hat** while plowing the field."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpilipit, pagpapalihis, o pag-iiba sa orihinal na anyo, kahulugan, o katotohanan ng isang bagay, salita, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is what happens when a story goes through five different Mariteses before it gets to you. The original "He has a cough" becomes "He has COVID, and he's going to the office!" It's the act of twisting the truth, like how politicians spin a bad report or how you try to explain your 'shopping' expenses to your parents.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagbabaluktot** sa katotohanan ay isang anyo ng pagsisinungaling.","translation":"The **distortion** of truth is a form of lying."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya namalayan ang unti-unting **pagbabaluktot** ng kanyang mga prinsipyo.","translation":"He did not notice the gradual **twisting** of his principles."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang bagay, gawain, o sitwasyon na nakakainip, walang sigla, at paulit-ulit.
original_explanation: Describes that 3-hour mandatory seminar on a Friday afternoon. Or that movie with no plot, just people staring into the distance. It's the traffic in EDSA that doesn't move. Anything that makes you say, "Jusko, tapusin na natin 'to," is kabagut-bagot.
usage_notes: The reduplication of 'bagot' intensifies the meaning of boredom.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para sa akin, **kabagut-bagot** ang pelikulang iyon.","translation":"For me, that movie was **boring**."},{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang pumasok sa isang **kabagut-bagot** na trabaho sa opisina.","translation":"He doesn't want to get into a **tedious** office job."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng masusing pagsisiyasat o paghahalughog sa isang tao, lugar, o bagay upang makahanap ng mga ipinagbabawal na kagamitan o upang tiyakin ang kaayusan.
original_explanation: That moment of mild panic at the mall entrance when the security guard does the 'pagrerekisa' and you suddenly can't remember if you left your 'baon' na Swiss army knife in your bag. It's the official 'welcome to the mall' gesture.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang **pagrerekisa** sa mga bag sa paliparan.","translation":"The **checking** of bags at the airport is strict."},{"sentence":"Nainis siya sa matagal na **pagrerekisa** ng guwardiya.","translation":"He got annoyed by the guard's lengthy **inspection**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagguhit ng isang linya o marka sa isang ibabaw.
original_explanation: This is like the OG 'friendzone' move. You literally draw a line, either on paper or metaphorically in a relationship. 'Hanggang dito na lang tayo.' It's an old-school word, like something your lolo would say when drawing property lines or when he wants his newspaper back in one piece.
usage_notes: A very rare and somewhat archaic term. 'Gumuhit' is the more common equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magraya** ka ng tuwid para paghiwalayin ang mga hanay.","translation":"**Draw a line** to separate the columns."},{"sentence":"Sinabihan ng guro ang mga bata na **magraya** sa kanilang kuwaderno.","translation":"The teacher told the children to **draw a line** in their notebooks."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manggagawa o kawani na nagtatrabaho sa isang kumpanya, opisina, o para sa isang indibidwal kapalit ng sahod.
original_explanation: He's the guy in the office polo or barong, trying to make a living. He could be your officemate who's always at the water cooler, the BPO agent on the night shift, or the government worker navigating bureaucracy. He's the one looking forward to 'sahod day' and dreading 'petsa de peligro'.
usage_notes: While strictly referring to a male, it is often used as a generic term for a group of employees of any gender. The gender-neutral terms 'manggagawa' or 'kawani' are more precise.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lahat ng **empleyado** ay kailangang dumalo sa seminar.","translation":"All **employees** need to attend the seminar."},{"sentence":"Isang tapat na **empleyado** si Mang Jose.","translation":"Mang Jose is a loyal **employee**."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi masukat o mabilang; napakalawak o napakarami.
etymology: Mula sa `walang` (without) + `kahulilip` (comprehension, measure). Ang 'hulilip' ay isang lumang salita para sa 'pag-unawa'.
original_explanation: This is a deep, poetic word. It’s for things so vast you can't wrap your head around them. The number of stars in the sky, the depth of the ocean, or the amount of 'chismis' in your neighborhood Viber group. It's so much, it's walang-kahulilip.
usage_notes: Mas karaniwan sa panitikan, tula, at pormal na talumpati kaysa sa kaswal na pag-uusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kalawakan ng uniberso ay **walang-kahulilip**.","translation":"The vastness of the universe is **unfathomable**."},{"sentence":"Nag-iwan siya ng pighating **walang-kahulilip** sa aming mga puso.","translation":"He left an **immeasurable** sorrow in our hearts."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nabibilang sa uring manggagawa; isang taong kumikita sa pamamagitan ng pisikal na paggawa.
etymology: Mula sa pagsasama ng mga salitang "anak" (child) at "pawis" (sweat), na tumutukoy sa "anak ng pagpapawis" o pagtatrabaho.
original_explanation: The direct opposite of anakmayaman. This is the backbone of the Philippine economy – the construction workers, the farmers, the factory employees. They're the ones who literally earn a living through their 'pawis' (sweat). In movies, they're the hardworking protagonist who eventually gets rich or wins the heart of the anakmayaman.
usage_notes: Isang marangal na termino para sa mga manggagawa, kadalasang ginagamit sa konteksto ng panlipunang aktibismo at pulitika.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga karapatan ng **anak-pawis** ang ipinaglalaban ng unyon.","translation":"The union is fighting for the rights of the **working class**."},{"sentence":"Isang tunay na **anak-pawis**, sinuong niya ang lahat ng hirap para sa kanyang pamilya.","translation":"A true **laborer**, he endured all hardships for his family."}]

translation: to stand around gaping, to be clueless
meaning_filipino: Manatiling nakatayo o nakaupo nang walang ginagawa, tila nag-iisip nang malalim o walang malay sa paligid, karaniwang may bahagyang bukas na bibig.
original_explanation: That moment when your brain just buffers. You're physically present but mentally AFK. Your prof asks a question, and you just **tumanga-tanga** because you weren't listening. Or when you get scammed online because you didn't read the fine print. You were being clueless.
usage_notes: A reduplication of 'tanga' (stupid), this verb describes the action of being spaced out or clueless in a specific moment. It's mildly self-deprecating or critical.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **tumanga-tanga** diyan, tulungan mo ako magbuhat nito!","translation":"Don't just **stand there gaping**, help me lift this!"},{"sentence":"Habang nagkakagulo ang lahat, siya ay **tumanga-tanga** lang sa isang sulok.","translation":"While everyone was in a panic, he just **stood cluelessly** in a corner."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang kilos o pagbabago na biglaan, matindi, at may malawak na epekto.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na 'drastic', na pinasimple ang baybay.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung spelling na ginagamit sa text o online. Parang 'drastiko' pero tinipid sa 'o'. 'Yung bigla kang nag-decide mag-resign kahit wala pang bagong work? **Drastik** move 'yan, bes. O 'yung nagpagupit ka from long hair to pixie cut after a breakup? Super **drastik**!
usage_notes: Impormal na baybay ng 'drastiko'. Karaniwan sa online at text messaging.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Medyo **drastik** ang naging desisyon niyang lumipat ng bansa.","translation":"Her decision to move to another country was a bit **drastic**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malawak na lugar na sagana at makapal ang mga puno at iba pang halaman.
etymology: From ka- + (reduplicated first syllable of root) kahoy + -an. The ka-...(an) with a reduplicated root often signifies a collection or abundance of the root word.
original_explanation: Basically, a place with a lot of 'kahoy' (wood/trees). It’s where duwendes, kapres, and other engkantos supposedly hang out. Think of it as nature's version of a crowded mall, but with trees instead of people and oxygen instead of sale signs.
usage_notes: Synonymous with 'gubat' but can sometimes imply a less wild, more managed or smaller wooded area.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglakad-lakad sila sa tahimik na **kakahuyan**.","translation":"They took a walk in the quiet **woods**."},{"sentence":"Maraming uri ng ibon ang matatagpuan sa **kakahuyan** na iyon.","translation":"Many species of birds can be found in that **woodland**."}]

translation: peck, a light and quick kiss
meaning_filipino: Isang mabilis at magaan na halik, karaniwang sa pisngi.
etymology: From Spanish 'beso' (kiss), with a change in spelling and a more specific, diminutive meaning.
original_explanation: This isn't a dramatic, movie-ending kiss. This is the quick 'beso-beso' your tita gives you, or the smack on the cheek from your lola. It's the G-rated, for-general-patronage version of a kiss. More of a 'hello/goodbye' than a 'hello, love of my life.'
usage_notes: Less common in modern conversation compared to 'beso' or 'halik'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **basio** sa pisngi ang paalam niya sa kanyang ina.","translation":"A **peck** on the cheek was his farewell to his mother."},{"sentence":"Binigyan niya ng **basio** ang sanggol na natutulog.","translation":"She gave a light **kiss** to the sleeping baby."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang yunit ng sukat ng haba na katumbas ng tatlong talampakan o humigit-kumulang 0.9144 metro.
original_explanation: Yung unit of measurement na ginagamit ng mananahi pag bumibili ka ng tela sa palengke. 'Ale, pabili pong tatlong yarda ng cotton.' It's not quite a meter, not quite a foot, but it's just right for making a dress or a school project.
usage_notes: Primarily used for measuring cloth or in contexts where the imperial system is referenced.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili siya ng limang **yarda** ng tela para sa kurtina.","translation":"She bought five **yards** of cloth for the curtain."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar, bagay, o tao na nasa ilalim ng kapangyarihan ng mahika, gayuma, o kababalaghan, karaniwang kagagawan ng isang engkanto o engkantada.
original_explanation: Like that one tito who suddenly becomes super charming and generous after winning the lottery – you suspect some magic is involved. An 'ingkantado' place is like Balete Drive, where you're half-expecting a white lady to ask for a ride. It's basically anything that has a magical, spooky, or "may something" vibe.
usage_notes: Commonly used in Filipino folklore and horror stories.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naniniwala ang mga matatanda na **ingkantado** ang malaking puno ng balete sa bukid.","translation":"The old folks believe that the large banyan tree in the field is **enchanted**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng wagas at matatag na katapatan, lalo na sa isang tao, simulain, o tungkulin.
original_explanation: The Hachiko of humans. The kind of loyalty you see in old married couples or someone who's been with the same company for 25 years. They're not just 'tapat,' their whole inner being ('loob') is committed.
usage_notes: A more profound and deeper form of 'tapat'. Often used in formal or literary contexts. Can also be written as 'tapat na loob'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga aso ay kilala bilang mga **tapat-loob** na kasama.","translation":"Dogs are known as **loyal** companions."},{"sentence":"Isang **tapat-loob** na lingkod-bayan ang kailangan ng bansa.","translation":"The country needs a **devoted** public servant."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagsasangla ng isang mahalagang bagay kapalit ng perang hiniram, o ang bagay mismo na isinangla.
original_explanation: The 'kapit sa patalim' move when petsa de peligro hits you hard and payday is a distant memory. You take your alahas or laptop to a pawnshop (the 'sanglaan') and get cash. The item itself is the **prenda**. You have to pay back the loan to get it back (tubusin), hopefully before it gets auctioned off (maremata).
usage_notes: The verb form is 'magprenda' (to pawn) or 'iprenda' (to pawn something). The noun refers to the act or the item itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa sanglaan pa ang singsing na ginawa niyang **prenda**.","translation":"The ring she used as **collateral** is still at the pawnshop."},{"sentence":"Kinailangan niyang i-**prenda** ang kanyang cellphone para may pambayad sa upa.","translation":"She had to **pawn** her cellphone to have money for rent."}]

translation: to date (to put a date on)
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagtatakda ng petsa sa isang dokumento, sulat, o anumang bagay.
original_explanation: This is what your boss tells you to do before you submit a report. It's the simple act of writing the date on something, which is surprisingly easy to forget. It's the opposite of "back-date," which is what you do when you *really* forgot to petsahan the document on time.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **petsahan** ang iyong tseke bago ibigay.","translation":"Don't forget to **date** your check before giving it."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **petsahan** ang bawat pahina ng kontrata.","translation":"You need to **date** every page of the contract."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa dalawa o higit pang bagay, tao, o sitwasyon na magkatulad at walang anumang katangiang nagpapaiba sa kanila.
original_explanation: It's like choosing between two unbranded shirts from the tiangge that look exactly the same. You hold them up, squint, and realize, 'Pareho lang pala.' There's **no difference**. Also what you say when your friend asks if you prefer the original or the milk tea version of a drink, but they both just taste like sugar.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin upang ilarawan ang mga pisikal na bagay, ideya, o kinalabasan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para sa kanya, **walang-pagkakaiba** ang mayaman at mahirap; lahat ay pantay-pantay.","translation":"For him, there is **no difference** between the rich and the poor; everyone is equal."},{"sentence":"Sa lasa, halos **walang-pagkakaiba** ang dalawang kape.","translation":"In terms of taste, there's almost **no difference** between the two coffees."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng langis na nakukuha mula sa mga buto ng linga, karaniwang ginagamit sa pagluluto at bilang pampalasa.
original_explanation: The holy grail of Asian cooking. One drop of this can make your pancit canton or fried rice taste 10x more legit. It's that distinct, nutty aroma that signals something delicious is being cooked in the kitchen. Also, the secret weapon for a killer siomai chili garlic sauce.
usage_notes: A compound noun. Often simply called 'sesame oil' even in Tagalog conversations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magpatak ka ng kaunting **langis ng linga** sa iyong noodles para sumarap.","translation":"Add a few drops of **sesame oil** to your noodles to make it more delicious."},{"sentence":"Amoy pa lang ng **langis ng linga** ay nakakagutom na.","translation":"Just the smell of **sesame oil** is already appetizing."}]

meaning_filipino: Nangangahulugang ang bawat isa sa isang pangkat (karaniwang dalawa) ay makakatanggap ng kalahati ng isang buo.
original_explanation: The ultimate "kapatid" deal. When there's only one piece of turon left, and your mom says "Tigkakalahati kayo." It’s a lesson in fairness, sharing, and how to cut something perfectly down the middle so your sibling doesn't complain they got the smaller piece.
usage_notes: Usually implies a division between two people or groups.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil iisa na lang ang natirang pizza, **tigkakalahati** na lang kami ng kaibigan ko.","translation":"Since there was only one pizza slice left, my friend and I just had **half for each**."},{"sentence":"Nagkasundo silang **tigkakalahati** sila sa kikitain ng kanilang negosyo.","translation":"They agreed to have **half for each** of the profits from their business."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagpapahayag ng buong-pusong pagtanggap, pagpapatawad, o paggawa ng isang bagay nang walang pag-aalinlangan o sama ng loob.
original_explanation: This is how you accept your friend's apology after they 'accidentally' ate your baon. It’s accepting a difficult task at work without complaining (at least, not out loud). It’s the feeling of letting go of a grudge—you’re not just okay, you’re genuinely at peace with it.
usage_notes: A common idiom expressing sincerity and lack of resentment. The opposite is 'mabigat sa loob' (with a heavy heart).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Maluwag sa loob** niyang tinanggap ang kanyang pagkatalo sa eleksyon.","translation":"He **wholeheartedly** accepted his defeat in the election."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging maasim; ang antas ng asim ng isang bagay, lalo na sa pagkain.
etymology: From `ka-` (denoting quality) + `asim` (sour) + `-an` (suffix indicating state or quality).
original_explanation: This is the 'sumakit-ang-panga' level of sourness you get from unripe mangoes or sinigang that's been blessed by the sampaloc gods. It's the face you make when your crush ignores your message. That's kaasiman.
usage_notes: Often used to describe the flavor profile of food, but can be used metaphorically for a sour disposition or attitude.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko kinaya ang **kaasiman** ng sinigang na niluto niya.","translation":"I couldn't handle the **sourness** of the sinigang she cooked."},{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na 'yang **kaasiman** ng mukha mo, hindi bagay sa'yo.","translation":"Stop that **sourness** on your face, it doesn't suit you."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang aparatong de-baterya na naglalabas ng ilaw, kadalasang may partikular na disenyo na kumakatawan sa isang K-pop group o artist, at ginagamit ng mga tagahanga sa mga konsiyerto.
original_explanation: This isn't just a flashlight, it's a status symbol. The holy grail for any K-Pop stan. Mas mahal pa minsan sa ticket ng concert. Waving this in a sea of fellow fans is a religious experience. If you don't have the official lightstick, baka i-judge ka ng fandom.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa konteksto ng K-Pop at mga fandom sa konsiyerto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinag-ipunan ko talaga ang pambili ng official **lightstick** ng BTS.","translation":"I really saved up to buy the official BTS **lightstick**."},{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng 'ocean' na nabuo ng mga **lightstick** sa concert.","translation":"The 'ocean' created by the **lightsticks** at the concert was beautiful."}]

translation: will deal in rice; will sell rice
meaning_filipino: Magkakaroon ng negosyo o gawain ng pagbebenta ng bigas sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: This is the future tense of a truly Filipino business venture. It's not just 'will sell,' it's specifically 'will sell rice.' It’s the dream of many OFWs to come home and open a 'bigasan' (rice store). It's a sign of stability, because in the Philippines, rice is life, and the one who sells it will always have customers.
usage_notes: A specific form of 'magbebenta' (will sell), focused on the commodity of rice. 'Magbibigas' is the future tense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagka-retire niya, plano niyang **magbibigas** sa kanilang probinsya.","translation":"When he retires, he plans to **deal in rice** in their province."},{"sentence":"Ang kooperatiba ay **magbibigas** sa mas murang halaga para sa mga miyembro nito.","translation":"The cooperative **will sell rice** at a cheaper price for its members."}]

translation: to catch (a signal, news); to scoop up
meaning_filipino: Makuha o masalo ang isang bagay na nasa hangin o daluyan, tulad ng signal ng radyo, balita, o tubig.
original_explanation: Before Netflix and Spotify, this was what you did with your antenna to get a clear TV channel. Today, it's what you do in the office pantry to get the latest chismis. You're trying to sumagap ng info.
usage_notes: Commonly used for intangible things like signals, broadcasts, news, or rumors.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **sumagap** ng signal para sa kanyang cellphone sa tuktok ng bundok.","translation":"He tried to **catch** a signal for his cellphone at the top of the mountain."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **sumagap** ng mga balita mula sa mga kapitbahay.","translation":"She likes to **gather** news from the neighbors."}]

translation: to ponder; to contemplate; to reflect on
meaning_filipino: Pag-isipang mabuti; suriing maigi sa isipan; pagnilay-nilayan.
original_explanation: To **limiin** something is the action version of "limi." It's what you do when your friend asks "Ano na'ng balak mo sa buhay mo?" and you're forced to actually think about it. You **limiin** your life choices, your career path, or whether you should have another cup of coffee. It’s the verb for overthinking with a purpose.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **limiin** ang mga posibleng kahihinatnan ng ating desisyon.","translation":"We need to **ponder** the possible consequences of our decision."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang babae na madaling makaramdam ng kaba, pag-aalala, o takot; o may katangiang madaling kabahan.
original_explanation: This is the adjective for a girl who's perpetually on edge. She's the one who jumps when a door slams, overthinks a "K" text message, and has probably rehearsed her coffee order in her head ten times. "Nerbiyosa ka na naman," is what her friends say when she's panicking about a deadline that's still a week away. It's the feminine form of 'nerbiyoso'.
usage_notes: This is the feminine form of the adjective. The masculine form is 'nerbiyoso'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging **nerbiyosa** si Ana tuwing mayroon siyang pagsusulit.","translation":"Ana is always **nervous** whenever she has an exam."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong **nerbiyosa**, matatapos din natin itong trabaho.","translation":"Don't be so **anxious**, we will finish this work."}]

translation: redpill; an awakening to a harsh truth
meaning_filipino: Sa kultura ng internet, ito ay tumutukoy sa proseso ng pagkamulat sa isang (kadalasan ay kontrobersyal o hindi popular) katotohanan na dating hindi nakikita o naiintindihan.
etymology: Mula sa pelikulang "The Matrix" (1999), kung saan ang pagpili sa pulang tableta (red pill) ay nangangahulugan ng pag-alis sa pekeng realidad.
original_explanation: Straight out of 'The Matrix', taking the 'redpill' means choosing to see the "truth" behind the illusion, no matter how ugly. In modern internet slang, it means you've been "awakened" to a particular worldview, often a cynical or controversial one. One person's 'redpill' moment is another's "nalunok mo na naman ang fake news." It’s the rabbit hole of online forums and YouTube conspiracy theories.
usage_notes: Malakas ang koneksyon nito sa iba't ibang online subculture, at maaaring magkaroon ng negatibo o kontrobersyal na konotasyon depende sa konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Simula nang mapanood niya ang mga dokumentaryong iyon, pakiramdam niya ay na-**redpill** siya tungkol sa sistema.","translation":"Ever since he watched those documentaries, he feels like he's been **redpilled** about the system."},{"sentence":"Ang pagkuha ng **redpill** ay nangangahulugang pagtanggap sa isang masalimuot na katotohanan.","translation":"Taking the **redpill** means accepting a complex truth."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng impormal na salita na karaniwang ginagamit sa mga kalye o sa pang-araw-araw na usapan, kadalasan ng mga kabataan o partikular na grupo.
etymology: Isang tambalang salita mula sa "salita" (word) at "kanto" (street corner).
original_explanation: This is the language of the streets, the "kanto boys" (and girls!). Think of words like 'erpat' (father), 'ermat' (mother), 'yosi' (cigarette), 'chibog' (eat). It's the secret code you use with your barkada so the adults don't understand. It's the OG Filipino slang before "stan" and "sksksk" became a thing.
usage_notes: Lubhang impormal. Ang mga salitang ginagamit ay mabilis magbago ayon sa uso. Kilala rin bilang "salitang-kalye".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko maintindihan ang mga **salitangkanto** ng mga kabataan ngayon, para silang may sariling wika.","translation":"I can't understand the **street slang** of the youth today, it's like they have their own language."},{"sentence":"Ang 'lespu' ay isang halimbawa ng **salitangkanto** para sa 'pulis'.","translation":"'Lespu' is an example of **street slang** for 'police'."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar, karaniwang nasa labas, na may mga kagamitan para sa paglalaro ng mga bata.
original_explanation: 'Yan 'yung lugar kung saan mo unang natutunan ang 'di matutumbasang sakit ng pagkahulog—physically man o sa first crush mo. Ngayon, ang 'playground' ng adults ay ang office pantry, Shopee cart, o Twitter.
usage_notes: Used directly in Tagalog, especially in urban areas or when referring to modern play structures. The native term is 'palaruan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala ni nanay ang mga bata sa **playground** para maglaro.","translation":"Mom brought the kids to the **playground** to play."},{"sentence":"Maraming bagong equipment sa **playground** ng aming subdivision.","translation":"There's a lot of new equipment in our subdivision's **playground**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan, kasangkapan, o kilos na ginagamit sa panlilinlang o panloloko.
etymology: From `pang-` + `daya` (trick, fraud). The `pang-` affix indicates a tool or means for an action.
original_explanation: Your kodigo during an exam? That's a 'pandaya'. That 'get rich quick' scheme your tito fell for? 'Pandaya'. The filter you use that changes your entire face? Ultimate 'pandaya'. It's any tool or tactic you use when you're not playing fair, from a simple card trick to a full-blown political scam.
usage_notes: While 'daya' is the act of cheating, 'pandaya' is the tool or method used for cheating.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng **pandaya** kaya nanalo siya sa laro.","translation":"He used a **cheat** that's why he won the game."},{"sentence":"Ang mga pekeng dokumento ay nagsilbing **pandaya** niya sa mga awtoridad.","translation":"The fake documents served as his **means of deception** against the authorities."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pagkain na nasira na, hindi na sariwa, at hindi na ligtas kainin, karaniwang may maasim na amoy o lasa.
original_explanation: That sad moment when you open the fridge, excited to eat last night's adobo, only to be greeted by a funky smell. In slang, it can also mean a joke that's old and no longer funny, or a performance that's so effortlessly good, it makes everyone else's efforts look "spoiled" in comparison. "Panis 'yang kalaban mo sa akin!"
usage_notes: Primarily for food. Can be used metaphorically for something that is old, outdated, or no longer effective (like a joke). The slang usage is a form of boasting, meaning 'nothing' or 'easy'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang kainin 'yan, **panis** na ang kanin.","translation":"Don't eat that anymore, the rice is already **spoiled**."},{"sentence":"**Panis** na 'yang biro mo, narinig ko na 'yan dati.","translation":"Your joke is **stale**, I've heard that before."},{"sentence":"Sa galing niyang sumayaw, **panis** ang lahat ng katunggali niya.","translation":"With his great dancing, all his competitors were **nothing** (lit. spoiled)."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na akto ng pag-alis sa isang posisyon, tungkulin, o pananagutan.
original_explanation: This is the "I quit!" moment. When you've had enough of your toxic boss, the endless OT, or the political drama, and you finally hand in that resignation letter. It’s the corporate version of 'pagbibitaw sa isang toxic na relasyon.' Freedom!
usage_notes: Specifically refers to quitting a job, post, or responsibility. Different from 'pagbibitaw' (physical letting go).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang biglaang **pagbibitiw** sa puwesto ay ikinagulat ng lahat.","translation":"His sudden **resignation** from the position surprised everyone."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang utos o kilos na maging dahilan upang ang isang tao ay lumakad nang walang sapin sa paa.
original_explanation: This is what your mom tells you to do before you step on the newly mopped floor. It's the act of forcing or telling someone to take off their shoes/slippers and walk barefoot. 'Huwag mo akong pagyapakin sa mainit na semento!' (Don't make me walk barefoot on the hot cement!).
usage_notes: This is a command/imperative form of the verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **pagyapakin** dito, ang dumi-dumi ng sahig!","translation":"Don't **make me go barefoot** here, the floor is so dirty!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng baboy na hindi alaga at malayang nabubuhay sa mga kagubatan o kabundukan.
etymology: Compound of "baboy" (pig) and "damo" (grass/weeds, but here implying "wild" or "of the wilderness").
original_explanation: The wild cousin of the domestic pig. This is the baboy that went off-the-grid, lives in the mountains, and probably has a man-bun. It's the original "free-range pork" before it was cool. Often the antagonist in folktales, messing up Ka Juan's kamote patch.
usage_notes: Literally "pig of the grass/wild".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malaking **baboy-damo** ang sumira sa mga pananim sa bukid.","translation":"A large **wild boar** destroyed the crops in the field."},{"sentence":"Mahirap hulihin ang mga **baboy-damo** dahil sa kanilang bilis at talino.","translation":"**Wild boars** are difficult to catch because of their speed and intelligence."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malakas na hangarin o pagnanasa para sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is more formal than 'gusto'. It's the 'I desire' to your 'I want'. You use this when you're writing a poem, a formal letter, or when you're being dramatic. 'Ang tanging nais ko ay kapayapaan... at unlimited data.'
usage_notes: More formal and poetic than 'gusto'. Often used in writing, songs, and formal speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang iyong **nais** para sa iyong kaarawan?","translation":"What is your **wish** for your birthday?"},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **nais** ay makapagtapos ng pag-aaral.","translation":"Her **desire** is to finish her studies."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng puno na karaniwang matatagpuan sa mga tropikal na lugar, na may malalaking dahon na tinatawag na palaspas.
original_explanation: The official tree of summer outings and Palawan desktop wallpapers. 'Pag nakakita ka nito, alam mong malapit na ang beach. Also, the source of 'palaspas' for Palm Sunday, na itatabi mo sa altar niyo sa bahay for a year para daw swerte.
usage_notes: Refers to the palm tree itself. The leaves are called 'palaspas'. This entry refers to the plant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matatayog ang mga puno ng **palma** sa dalampasigan.","translation":"The **palm** trees on the shore are tall."},{"sentence":"Gawa sa dahon ng **palma** ang mga palaspas na binasbasan sa simbahan.","translation":"The blessed fronds at church are made from the leaves of the **palm tree**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagpatay at paghihiwa-hiwalay sa katawan ng isang hayop para gawing pagkain.
original_explanation: What happens to the pig before it becomes lechon. In the modern world, it's also what you feel HR is doing during a company retrenchment ("mass katay"). It's a brutal, direct term for cutting up, whether it's for the dinner table or the unemployment line.
usage_notes: Primarily refers to butchering animals. Can be used figuratively for massive firings or project cancellations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula na ang **katay** ng baboy para sa pista.","translation":"The **slaughter** of the pig for the fiesta has begun."},{"sentence":"Maraming natanggal sa trabaho dahil sa **katay** sa kumpanya.","translation":"Many lost their jobs because of the **layoffs** (slaughter) in the company."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga indibidwal o grupo na magkatunggali sa isang laban, laro, o anumang uri ng kompetisyon.
etymology: From `mag-` + `ka-` (denoting a pair or group) + `laban` (fight, contest).
original_explanation: Sa Mobile Legends, sila 'yung nasa kabilang team. Sa basketball, sila 'yung kalaban ng Ginebra. Sa love life, sila 'yung kaagaw mo sa puso ng crush mo. Basically, anyone on the other side of the 'vs.'
usage_notes: Synonymous with `magkakontra` but often used more specifically in the context of games, sports, and direct competition. Can also be used as a noun 'opponents'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit **magkalaban** sa laro, magkaibigan pa rin sila sa totoong buhay.","translation":"Even if they are **opponents** in the game, they are still friends in real life."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **magkalaban** sa championship round?","translation":"Who are the **opponents** in the championship round?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kulisap na kilala sa tunog na nililikha nito sa gabi sa pamamagitan ng pagkiskis ng mga pakpak. Maaari din itong tumukoy sa isang uri ng isport.
original_explanation: Pwedeng 'yung maingay na kulisap sa probinsya na 'pag narinig mo, alam mong gabi na at oras nang matulog. Pwede ring 'yung sport na parang baseball pero British version na hindi masyadong sikat dito sa Pinas.
usage_notes: Can refer to the insect or the sport. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ingay ng mga **kriket** sa hardin tuwing gabi.","translation":"The **crickets** in the garden are noisy every night."},{"sentence":"Nanonood sila ng laro ng **kriket** sa telebisyon.","translation":"They are watching a **cricket** game on television."}]

translation: to eat all together; for a group to eat
meaning_filipino: Sabay-sabay na pagkain ng isang pangkat ng mga tao.
original_explanation: This is what your Lola shouts when the handaan is ready. It's the plural command form of "kain," basically telling everyone, "Alright, squad, let's feast!" It's the opposite of that sad desk lunch you have at work.
usage_notes: The '-si-' infix indicates that the action is performed by multiple subjects simultaneously or as a group.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magsikain** na tayo, bago pa lumamig ang pagkain!","translation":"Let's **all eat** now, before the food gets cold!"},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng pulong, inanyayahan silang lahat na **magsikain**.","translation":"After the meeting, they were all invited **to eat together**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katawan na ginamitan ng mga kemikal upang mapreserba at maiwasan ang mabilis na pagkabulok.
original_explanation: When someone has passed away and they get a 'makeover' to look presentable for their final viewing. It's the process that makes you say, 'mukha lang siyang natutulog.'
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa konteksto ng mga libing at agham pang-punerarya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maayos na na-**embalsamado** ang labi ng yumaong lider.","translation":"The remains of the deceased leader were properly **embalmed**."}]

translation: to allow oneself to be rescued
meaning_filipino: Hayaan ang sarili na mailigtas ng iba; humingi ng tulong upang maligtas.
original_explanation: This is that moment in a movie when the hero is dangling from a cliff and tells their friend, "Go on without me!" and the friend says "No! **Pasagip** ka na!" It means 'let yourself be saved!' It's also what you do when you're drowning in deadlines—you wave the white flag and ask your work bestie for help.
usage_notes: Can mean either allowing rescue or asking for rescue, depending on context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang **pasagip** dahil sa hiya, kahit nalulunod na siya sa utang.","translation":"He didn't want **to be rescued** out of shame, even though he was drowning in debt."},{"sentence":"Sumigaw siya ng 'Tulong!' upang **pasagip** sa mga bumbero.","translation":"He shouted 'Help!' **to ask to be rescued** by the firefighters."}]

translation: to be forgiven; to be able to forgive
meaning_filipino: Mabigyan ng kapatawaran sa isang nagawang pagkakamali o kasalanan.
original_explanation: The goal of every 'sorry na po' text and every peace offering (like buying them milk tea). It's what you hope for after a major 'lagot ka' moment. The opposite of being 'seen-zoned' by your galit na jowa or parent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umaasa siyang **mapapatawad** siya ng kanyang kaibigan.","translation":"He is hoping **to be forgiven** by his friend."},{"sentence":"Isang malaking biyaya ang **mapatawad** sa iyong mga kasalanan.","translation":"It is a great blessing **to be forgiven** for your sins."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang propesyon ay ang paggawa, pag-aayos, o pagtahi ng mga damit.
original_explanation: The unsung hero who saves you from an ill-fitting online shopping purchase. Your friendly neighborhood magdaramit (or "mananahi") can turn that "sana all" dress into a "sakin lang" masterpiece. They are the masters of the sewing machine and the tape measure.
usage_notes: "Mananahi" is a more common term for a tailor or seamstress. "Magdaramit" can sound slightly more formal or archaic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpagawa ako ng bestida sa sikat na **magdaramit** para sa aking kasal.","translation":"I had a dress made by a famous **couturier** for my wedding."},{"sentence":"Dinala ko ang aking pantalon sa **magdaramit** para paikliin.","translation":"I brought my pants to the **tailor** to have them shortened."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sining-bayan na gumagamit ng mga pinagdikit-dikit na piraso ng papel na hinulma, karaniwang pinipinturahan pagkatapos matuyo. Kilala ang Paete, Laguna sa paggawa nito.
etymology: Possibly from Spanish *tacar*, 'to tap, to press', referring to the process of pressing the paper strips into the mold.
original_explanation: Those colorful papier-mâché horses and other figures you see in souvenir shops, especially from Paete, Laguna. It's the OG Filipino upcycling craft before "upcycling" was even a cool word. Basically, turning old newspapers and gawgaw (starch) into art.
usage_notes: Strongly associated with the town of Paete, Laguna, which is famous for this craft.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili kami ng **taka** na kabayo bilang pasalubong.","translation":"We bought a papier-mâché horse as a souvenir."},{"sentence":"Ang paggawa ng **taka** ay isang mahalagang bahagi ng kultura ng Paete.","translation":"The art of making **taka** is an important part of Paete's culture."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamataas na hukuman sa sangay ng hudikatura ng isang bansa, na may pangwakas na kapangyarihan sa pagbibigay-kahulugan sa batas.
original_explanation: The final boss of Philippine law. When all else fails and you've gone through all the lower courts, this is where your case goes for the ultimate decision. Think of it as the council of elders in a fantasy movie, but with gavels, long robes, and decisions that can change the entire country. No take-backsies here.
usage_notes: Laging isinusulat na may malaking titik sa simula ng bawat salita dahil ito ay isang tiyak na ngalan ng institusyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Idinulog sa **Korte Suprema** ang usapin tungkol sa bagong batas.","translation":"The issue regarding the new law was brought before the **Supreme Court**."},{"sentence":"Ang desisyon ng **Korte Suprema** ay pinal at hindi na maaaring iapela.","translation":"The decision of the **Supreme Court** is final and executory."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpapadala ng isang bagay, tulad ng mensahe, email, o pakete, mula sa isang lugar patungo sa iba.
original_explanation: The Taglish verb that runs our lives. From "pa-magsend naman ng load" to "magsend ka ng Gcash" to "magsend ka ng nudes...charot!" It's the modern-day 'padala'.
usage_notes: Extremely common Taglish verb, replacing 'magpadala' in many digital and informal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **magsend** ng report mo sa akin bago mag-5 PM.","translation":"Don't forget **to send** your report to me before 5 PM."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **magsend** ng pera sa probinsya para sa pamilya ko.","translation":"I need **to send** money to the province for my family."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lumipad nang mataas sa himpapawid; ang umangat sa isang marangal o nakahihigit na kalagayan.
etymology: From '-um-' (actor-focus infix) + 'pailanglang' (upward flight). The root 'ilanglang' itself means to soar.
original_explanation: This isn't just 'lumipad' (to fly). This is flying with style and majesty. Think of an eagle gliding effortlessly in the sky, a kite catching the perfect wind, or your career taking off after a big promotion. Pumailanglang is the poetic, dramatic, slow-motion version of rising up. It's what you want your dreams to do.
usage_notes: A very descriptive and somewhat literary word. Used for both literal flying and metaphorical rising.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napanood namin ang agila na **pumailanglang** sa kalangitan.","translation":"We watched the eagle **soar** high in the sky."},{"sentence":"Mula sa pagiging simpleng empleyado, **pumailanglang** ang kanyang karera hanggang maging CEO.","translation":"From being a simple employee, his career **soared** until he became the CEO."}]

translation: homecoming; the act of going home
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbalik o pagpunta sa sariling tahanan o pinagmulan.
original_explanation: That magical moment at 5 PM when you can finally log off from your BPO shift. It's the 'uwian na, may nanalo na' moment of your day. For OFWs, it's the most awaited event, second only to the balikbayan box arriving. It's the journey back to where the wifi connects automatically and you don't have to wear pants.
usage_notes: A very common and emotionally charged word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inaabangan ko ang aking **pag-uwi** sa probinsya tuwing Pasko.","translation":"I look forward to my **homecoming** to the province every Christmas."},{"sentence":"Naging mahirap ang kanyang **pag-uwi** dahil sa matinding trapik.","translation":"His **journey home** became difficult because of the heavy traffic."}]

translation: to be able to receive Christmas gifts
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang makatanggap ng mga regalo o aginaldo sa panahon ng Pasko.
etymology: From "maka-" (ability prefix) + "pamasko" (for Christmas). "Pamasko" itself is from "pa-" + "Pasko" (Christmas, from Spanish *Pascua*).
original_explanation: This is the ultimate goal of every Filipino kid (and kid-at-heart) during the Christmas season. It's the verb form of hitting the jackpot from your ninongs and ninangs. 'Mano po, ninong!' is the magic spell to make this happen.
usage_notes: Often used by children or those asking for Christmas gifts (aguinaldo). It is distinct from 'makapasko' which means 'to be able to celebrate Christmas'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **makapamasko** ako ng bagong cellphone mula kay Ninang.","translation":"I hope I can **get a new cellphone as a Christmas gift** from my godmother."},{"sentence":"Nagpunta ang mga bata sa bahay-bahay para **makapamasko**.","translation":"The children went from house to house to **receive Christmas gifts**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pag-aalis ng bayag o pagputol sa kakayahang magparami ng isang lalaking hayop.
original_explanation: Before 'it's complicated' was a relationship status, this was a... more permanent solution. The kind of word you'd find in a dusty old book about farming, not in your DMs. Definitely NOT what you ask the vet for your pet cat in modern Tagalog (use 'kapon' for that).
usage_notes: This is a rare or obsolete term, primarily related to animal husbandry. The common modern term is 'kaponin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan ng may-ari ng asyenda ang kaniyang manggagawa na **magbuslog** ng mga bagong biik.","translation":"The hacienda owner ordered his worker to **castrate** the new piglets."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng kakayahang mag-isip, umunawa, o magpasya; may bait o talino.
original_explanation: This is your tita's compliment for a kid who isn't running around breaking things: 'Ay, may-isip na 'tong batang 'to!' It means someone has graduated from being a chaotic toddler to a person who can think logically. Also used for adults who make good decisions.
usage_notes: Can refer to being conscious (as opposed to unconscious), having intellect, or being mature enough to think for oneself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, **may-isip** na ang anak mo at alam na niya ang tama sa mali.","translation":"Don't worry, your child is **sensible** now and knows what is right from wrong."},{"sentence":"Kahit lasing, **may-isip** pa rin siya para umuwi.","translation":"Even though he was drunk, he was still **conscious** enough to go home."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kasuotan na isinusuot sa ibabang bahagi ng katawan, na may magkahiwalay na bahagi para sa bawat binti.
original_explanation: Your go-to leg-wear for when 'shorts' is too casual and 'skirt' is too inconvenient. From the 'maong' you wear everywhere to the slacks you have for your BPO job interview. Pro tip: always check the back pocket for money before washing your **pantalon**.
usage_notes: Refers to all kinds of pants, including jeans ('maong'), slacks, etc.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong magsuot ng itim na **pantalon** para sa uniporme sa trabaho.","translation":"I need to wear black **pants** for my work uniform."},{"sentence":"Butas na pala ang tuhod ng paborito kong **pantalon**.","translation":"The knee of my favorite **pants** has a hole in it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang teoryang pampulitika at pang-ekonomiya na nagtataguyod na ang mga paraan ng produksyon, distribusyon, at palitan ay dapat pag-aari o kontrolado ng buong komunidad.
original_explanation: A big word you hear in Araling Panlipunan class or from your very 'woke' friend. It's the idea that everyone should share the means to make stuff (like factories and land) so wealth is distributed more equally. Think less "what's mine is mine" and more "what's ours is ours." Not to be confused with 'sosyal,' which is about being fancy.
usage_notes: Isang terminong pampulitika at pang-ekonomiya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aralan namin sa klase ang mga prinsipyo ng **sosyalismo** at kapitalismo.","translation":"We studied the principles of **socialism** and capitalism in class."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbubuhos o pagwiwisik ng tubig sa mga halaman upang mabuhay at lumago ang mga ito.
original_explanation: Yung ginagawa ng mga plantito at plantita tuwing umaga. It's the ultimate act of love for your green babies. Parang pag-aalaga sa isang relationship, kailangan ng constant effort (at tubig) para hindi mamatay.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to watering plants.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Araw-araw ang kanyang **pagdidilig** sa mga rosas sa hardin.","translation":"Her **watering** of the roses in the garden is done daily."},{"sentence":"Nakalimutan kong gawin ang aking **pagdidilig** kaninang umaga kaya nalanta ang mga halaman.","translation":"I forgot to do my **watering** this morning, so the plants wilted."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o pagiging sanhi upang maramdaman ng isang tao ang isang bagay nang may matinding sidhi.
original_explanation: Yung effect ng last episode ng K-drama sa'yo. O 'yung ginawa ng ex mo na nag-post ng picture kasama 'yung bago niya. You were made to feel things, intensely. 'Yan ang tawag sa ginawa niya, ikaw ay kanyang pinapagdamdam.
usage_notes: This is a causative verb form, meaning 'to make someone do X'. Here, it's 'to make someone feel'. It's often used with an adverb like 'nang labis' (greatly) to emphasize the intensity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo naman siyang **papagdamdamin** nang labis dahil sa iyong mga salita.","translation":"Don't **cause him to feel so intensely** because of your words."},{"sentence":"Ang pelikula ay sadyang ginawa upang **papagdamdamin** ang mga manonood.","translation":"The movie was intentionally made to **evoke intense emotions** from the audience."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang estruktura o pader na itinatayo upang pigilan ang pag-apaw ng tubig, lalo na mula sa ilog, lawa, o dagat.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na `dique` o Olandes na `dijk`.
original_explanation: Ito yung pader na nagse-save sa'yo 'pag high tide o may bagyo. Parang 'yung best friend mo na pumipigil sa'yo na i-text 'yung ex mo at 3 AM. A dike is a barrier, a flood control system. Sa Pilipinas, lalo na sa mga tabing-ilog na lugar, life-saver 'to.
usage_notes: Isang hiram na salita na ganap nang naisama sa wikang Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpatayo ng mataas na **dike** ang gobyerno para maiwasan ang pagbaha.","translation":"The government built a high **dike** to prevent flooding."},{"sentence":"Nagsimulang umapaw ang tubig sa ibabaw ng **dike**.","translation":"The water started to overflow on top of the **levee**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging mas maliit o mas makitid ng isang espasyo, daanan, o siwang.
original_explanation: Picture EDSA during rush hour. The 5 lanes suddenly feel like 1. 'Yan 'yung pag-kipot ng daan. O 'yung paborito mong maong pants nung high school, 'di mo na maisuot kasi kumipot na (or you just got bigger, let's be real). It's the shrinking of a space or opening.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumipot** ang daan kaya nahirapan ang mga sasakyan na mag-overtake.","translation":"The road **became narrow**, so the vehicles had difficulty overtaking."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa pamamaga, **kumipot** ang kanyang lalamunan.","translation":"Because of the swelling, his throat **tightened**."}]

translation: to have something pulled out; to have something drawn (raffle)
meaning_filipino: Pahintulutan o maging dahilan upang alisin, hugutin, o bunutin ang isang bagay mula sa kinalalagyan nito, tulad ng ngipin, halaman, o pangalan sa isang palabunutan.
etymology: From 'mag-' (verb prefix) + 'pa-' (causative prefix) + 'bunot' (to pull out). Literally 'to cause to be pulled out'.
original_explanation: Two main scenarios: 1) The dreaded trip to the dentist. 'Kailangan ko nang magpabunot ng wisdom tooth, besh.' 2) The hopeful moment in a Christmas party raffle. 'Sana ako na ang susunod na mabunot!' In both cases, you're having something pulled for you.
usage_notes: Context is key to distinguish between extraction (tooth, weed) and a raffle draw.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pupunta ako sa dentista bukas para **magpabunot** ng ngipin.","translation":"I'm going to the dentist tomorrow to **have a tooth pulled**."},{"sentence":"Sino ang susunod na **magpapabunot** ng numero para sa raffle?","translation":"Who will be the next to **have a number drawn** for the raffle?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal para sa isang batang babae o dalaga.
original_explanation: This is a retro, almost 70s/80s way of saying 'chick' or 'babe', but in a less objectifying, more endearing way. Think of your tito calling a young lady 'tsikita'. It's like the Spanish 'chiquita'.
usage_notes: Often used by an older generation. Can sound a bit dated but is generally considered affectionate.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"\"Hoy, **tsikita**, kamusta ka na?\" tanong ng kanyang tito.","translation":"\"Hey, **young lady**, how are you?\" her uncle asked."},{"sentence":"Maraming **tsikita** ang nanonood ng concert.","translation":"Many **girls** were watching the concert."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bakasyon na isinasagawa ng mga bagong kasal pagkatapos ng kanilang kasal upang ipagdiwang ang kanilang pagsasama.
etymology: From Spanish "luna de miel" (moon of honey).
original_explanation: The official term for that post-wedding getaway where you can finally relax after months of stressful wedding planning. It's the trip where your social media is flooded with "just married" vibes, beach photos, and couple selfies. The modern Filipino version is often just a "staycation" because, you know, budget. Also known as "pulot-gata."
usage_notes: While understood, the native term 'pulot-gata' is more common in conversational Tagalog. 'Honeymoon' is also used directly.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagplano ang bagong kasal na sa Palawan ganapin ang kanilang **lunademiyel**.","translation":"The newlyweds planned to have their **honeymoon** in Palawan."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa pandemya, ipinagpaliban muna nila ang kanilang **lunademiyel** sa ibang bansa.","translation":"Because of the pandemic, they postponed their overseas **honeymoon**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan nagaganap ang pagtakas o daanan para sa pag-puga.
original_explanation: This is basically a synonym for 'pugahan' (the escape route one). If 'pugahan' is the fire exit, 'pugalan' is the entire fire escape plan. It's the place of the great escape. "Naging pugalan ng mga bilanggo ang isang butas sa pader."
usage_notes: Largely synonymous with 'pugahan' (place of escape). The choice between them can be a matter of regional preference or subtle nuance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit nilang **pugalan** ang estero sa likod ng gusali.","translation":"They used the canal behind the building as their **place of escape**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa tunog ng boses na magaspang, malat, at mababa, kadalasan dahil sa sakit, pagod, o labis na pagsasalita.
original_explanation: The voice you have the morning after a concert, a karaoke marathon, or shouting your lungs out at a basketball game. It's that sexy-but-actually-painful 'I-can't-talk' voice. Your BPO team lead knows this voice well after a long shift of taking calls.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'paos', but 'pagas' can imply a deeper, rougher quality.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **pagas** ang boses ng mang-aawit matapos ang kanyang konsiyerto.","translation":"The singer's voice became **hoarse** after his concert."}]

translation: to be honest with each other, to have a confrontation
meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay o mutual na pag-amin o pagsasabi ng katotohanan ng dalawa o higit pang tao sa isa't isa.
original_explanation: This is the multiplayer version of 'magtapat'. It's when the whole barkada or a couple sits down for a 'we need to talk' session. Expect drama, tears, and hopefully, resolution. Think of it as a reality show confrontation where everyone lays their cards on the table. 'Okay, let's magtapatan... sino'ng umubos ng Koko Krunch?'
usage_notes: Implies a reciprocal or group act of honesty or confrontation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Panahon na para **magtapatan** tayong lahat upang malutas ang problemang ito.","translation":"It's time for all of us **to be honest with each other** to solve this problem."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng maraming taon, nagkaroon ng pagkakataon ang magkapatid na **magtapatan** tungkol sa kanilang mga sama ng loob.","translation":"After many years, the siblings had the chance **to have a frank discussion** about their grievances."}]

translation: to hold a meeting about something
meaning_filipino: Pag-usapan ang isang paksa sa isang pormal na pagtitipon o pulong.
original_explanation: This is what your boss says when they want to "circle back" on an issue. Basically, you're all getting in a room (or a Zoom call) to talk about something until you're all aligned or until someone just gives up. "Guys, let's have a meeting about the meeting."
usage_notes: Often used in formal or organizational contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **pagpulungan** natin ang mga bagong patakaran sa opisina.","translation":"We need to **hold a meeting about** the new office policies."},{"sentence":"**Pagpulungan** natin kung paano gagastusin ang budget para sa Christmas party.","translation":"Let's **discuss in a meeting** how to spend the budget for the Christmas party."}]

meaning_filipino: (Balbal) Makakuha ng iskor na sero sa isang pagsusulit o paligsahan.
etymology: Slang term derived from 'itlog' (egg) due to its visual similarity to the number zero (0).
original_explanation: The most dreaded thing for a student during an exam. It means you got a big, fat zero—shaped like an egg ('itlog'). "Kamusta exam mo?" "Wag mo nang tanungin, mukhang mangingitlog ako." It's the academic equivalent of a strikeout.
usage_notes: This is purely slang and used in informal, often academic or competitive, contexts. It is used as a verb to mean "to get a zero".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kung hindi ka mag-aaral, baka **mangingitlog** ka sa quiz bukas.","translation":"If you don't study, you might **score zero** on the quiz tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Sa sobrang hirap ng tanong, halos lahat kami ay nangitlog.","translation":"Because the question was so hard, almost all of us **flunked**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang panghalip paari sa unang panauhan, isahan. Nagpapahiwatig ng pag-aari o ugnayan sa nagsasalita. Ginagamit din bilang palayon ng 'ako'.
original_explanation: The OG "mine." Bago pa magka-"jowa ko," "bebe ko," at "mahal ko," andiyan na ang "nanay ko," "bahay ko," at "pera ko." Ito ang simula ng lahat ng pag-aangkin sa mundo. Use it wisely, or else magiging "utang ko."
usage_notes: Bilang paari (my), laging sumusunod ito sa salitang inilalarawan (e.g., "libro ko," hindi "ko libro"). Bilang palayon (me), karaniwan itong kasunod ng pandiwa (e.g., "Bigyan mo ko.").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasaan na ang sapatos **ko**?","translation":"Where are **my** shoes?"},{"sentence":"Tulungan mo **ko** sa pagbuhat nito.","translation":"Help **me** carry this."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-unawa sa kahulugan ng mga nakasulat na salita o simbolo sa pamamagitan ng paningin.
original_explanation: What you do with your crush's old tweets, your boss's confusing email, or the latest 'Marites' blind item. It's the act of decoding text, whether it's for academic enlightenment or for gathering tea. In the digital age, it's a constant battle between reading long-form articles and just skimming the headlines.
usage_notes: A very common verb. This is a homograph; distinguish its pronunciation from /mag-ba-SÂ/ which means 'to get wet'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **magbasa** ng mga libro tungkol sa kasaysayan ng Pilipinas.","translation":"He/She loves to **read** books about Philippine history."},{"sentence":"**Magbasa** ka muna ng instructions bago mo buuin 'yan.","translation":"**Read** the instructions first before you assemble that."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang bagay, tao, o sitwasyon na nakakatawa, o kaya naman ay hindi kapani-paniwala at kahangalan.
etymology: Reduplication of `tawa` (laugh) with the `ka-` prefix, used as an adjective.
original_explanation: Can be two things: 1) Genuinely funny, like a good meme. 2) Ridiculous, like your ex's excuse for cheating. "Katawa-tawa ang dahilan niya!" It's the feeling when something is so absurd, you don't know whether to laugh or get angry. Often, you do both.
usage_notes: Can have a positive (funny) or negative (ridiculous, pathetic) connotation depending on the context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **katawa-tawa** ang sitwasyon nang madulas siya sa balat ng saging.","translation":"The situation became **funny** when he slipped on a banana peel."},{"sentence":"**Katawa-tawa** ang kanyang paliwanag; halatang nagsisinungaling siya.","translation":"His explanation is **laughable**; it's obvious he is lying."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbaon o pagtagos ng isang matulis na bagay sa isa pang bagay, o ang marka na resulta nito.
original_explanation: That feeling when your friend casually mentions your ex is now happily married. Ouch, 'tusok' sa puso! It's also what happens when you get a vaccine shot, or when you're making fishballs and you spear one with a stick.
usage_notes: Can refer to the act of piercing, the puncture itself, or the object used for piercing (like a barbecue stick).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingat sa **tusok** ng karayom.","translation":"Be careful of the **prick** of the needle."},{"sentence":"Bigyan mo ako ng dalawang **tusok** ng isaw.","translation":"Give me two **sticks** of intestine."}]

translation: to place someone or something on its back
meaning_filipino: Ilagay o ihiga ang isang tao o bagay sa posisyong nakaharap paitaas.
original_explanation: What you do to your friend who passed out drunk at the party. You turn them over para 'di malunod sa sariling suka. Or when a wrestler pins their opponent. "Patihayaín mo 'yan!"
usage_notes: This is the verb form that causes the state of 'patihaya'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pinatihaya** ng nars ang pasyente para sa eksaminasyon.","translation":"The nurse **placed the patient on his back** for the examination."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **patihayaín** ang sanggol pagkatapos dumede.","translation":"Don't **lay the baby on its back** after feeding."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagdugtungin o pag-ugnayin ang mga bagay sa paraang nagkakasalubong o nagkakapatong-patong na parang lala.
etymology: From `pag-` + `sala-sala` (interwoven, lattice) + `-hin` (verb suffix). The root `sala-sala` refers to a lattice or weave.
original_explanation: Imagine trying to explain your family tree at a reunion, and everyone is somehow related in three different ways. That's `pagsala-salahin`. It's also what you do with your fingers when you're praying your crush replies to your DM, or when you're weaving a banig. It's organized chaos.
usage_notes: This verb implies making something into a lattice-like or interwoven structure.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **pagsala-salahin** ang mga dahon ng niyog upang makagawa ng isang bubong.","translation":"You need to **intertwine** the coconut leaves to make a roof."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aralan niya kung paano **pagsala-salahin** ang mga hibla ng abaka.","translation":"He studied how to **crisscross** the abaca fibers."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng mineral na silicate na may kulay na mala-oliba at karaniwang matatagpuan sa mga batong igneous.
original_explanation: Ito yung batong pang-heolohiya, hindi yung pinsan ni Popeye na si Olive. Mukha siyang berdeng asukal na makikita mo sa mga bato galing sa bulkan. Para sa mga geology majors lang ang may pake dito, sa totoo lang.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa larangan ng heolohiya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakita ang mga heologo ng mga kristal ng **olibino** sa lava flow.","translation":"The geologists found crystals of **olivine** in the lava flow."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa maraming pagkakataon; karaniwan o madalas mangyari.
etymology: From ka- + dalas + -an, meaning the state or frequency of being 'often'.
original_explanation: Ito yung status ng traffic sa EDSA tuwing rush hour. Ito rin yung sagot mo kapag tinanong ka kung gaano ka kadalas mag-overthink. 'Usually, ganito ang nangyayari.'
usage_notes: Used to describe something that happens frequently or is the usual case.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kadalasan**, trapik sa EDSA tuwing Biyernes.","translation":"**Usually**, there's traffic on EDSA every Friday."},{"sentence":"**Kadalasan** siyang nag-o-overtime para matapos ang trabaho.","translation":"He **often** works overtime to finish his work."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matigas na bato, karaniwang hugis bilog at patag, na ginagamit sa pagpapatasa o paghahasa ng mga kagamitang may talim tulad ng kutsilyo at itak.
etymology: Mula sa "bato" (stone) at "kiskis" (to rub against), kung saan ang "kiskisan" ay ang gamit o lugar ng pagkiskis.
original_explanation: Before sharpening steels and fancy kitchen gadgets, there was this. The rock your lolo uses to sharpen his 'itak' or the 'manong magtataho' uses for his scraper. It’s that satisfying 'shing-shing' sound of metal against stone that means something is about to get very, very sharp.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa isang maliit na hasaan (`hasaang bato`) o sa isang malaking gilingan na karaniwang umiikot.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinatalas niya ang gulok sa **batong-kiskisan** bago pumunta sa bukid.","translation":"He sharpened the bolo on the **grindstone** before going to the field."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng isang lalaki na kaaya-aya, magiliw, at madaling pakisamahan.
original_explanation: He's the guy your Tita approves of. Not necessarily 'gwapo' in a matinee idol way, but he's got that charm that makes everyone from your lola to your baby cousin like him. He’s got good vibes, knows how to carry a conversation, and probably offers to help with the dishes after a family dinner. A solid, green flag dude.
usage_notes: Strictly used for males. The female counterpart is 'simpatika'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit hindi siya ang pinakagwapo, **simpatiko** naman si Marco kaya marami ang may gusto sa kanya.","translation":"Even if he's not the most handsome, Marco is **charming**, which is why many people like him."}]

translation: to raise; to increase; to elevate
meaning_filipino: Gawing mas mataas ang isang bagay, antas, o halaga.
etymology: Mula sa "pa-" (panlaping pangkasanhi) + "taas" + "-in" (panlaping pokus sa layon).
original_explanation: The magical word your boss says about your sahod (hopefully). O kaya yung request mo sa videoke operator para maabot mo yung high notes ng "My Way". It's the opposite of what you want to happen to gas prices and your blood pressure.
usage_notes: Isang napaka-karaniwang pandiwa na ginagamit para sa literal na taas, presyo, lakas ng tunog, katayuan, atbp.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyong **pataasin** ang bandila.","translation":"Please **raise** the flag."},{"sentence":"Huwag nating hayaang **pataasin** ng mga negosyante ang presyo ng bigas.","translation":"Let's not allow the businessmen to **increase** the price of rice."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang instrumento na ginagamit upang matukoy ang direksiyon, partikular na ang hilaga, sa pamamagitan ng isang malayang umiikot na karayom na magnetiko.
original_explanation: Before Waze and Google Maps, this was the OG navigation tool. It's that thing in your lolo's drawer from his Boy Scout days. For the lovelorn, it's what you wish your heart had to find 'The One' instead of just leading you to another maling tao. 'Sana may kompas din ang puso.'
usage_notes: 'Kompass' is an alternative but less common spelling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ng mga manlalakbay ang **kompas** upang hindi sila maligaw sa gubat.","translation":"The travelers used the **compass** so they wouldn't get lost in the forest."},{"sentence":"Luma na ang **kompas** na minana ko sa aking lolo.","translation":"The **compass** I inherited from my grandfather is old."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang walang-tigil at madalas ay walang-kabuluhang pag-uusap o tsismisan.
original_explanation: This is the official sport of the Marites community. It's the verbal equivalent of doomscrolling, but with your kapitbahay's love life. If your group chat is named "Daldalan," you know it's where the real tea is spilled.
usage_notes: Often has a slightly negative connotation, implying the conversation is frivolous or gossipy. The noun form is also "daldalan" (a chat session).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan n'yo na 'yang **daldalan** at magtrabaho na kayo.","translation":"Stop that **chatter** and get back to work."},{"sentence":"Nag-umpisa na naman ang **daldalan** ng mga tita sa reunion.","translation":"The aunties' **gossip session** has started again at the reunion."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalagyan, aparador, o silid kung saan itinatago ang mga damit.
etymology: From 'damit' (clothes) + '-an' (suffix indicating a place or container).
original_explanation: The Pinoy version of Narnia's entrance. It's your aparador, your closet, or that cabinet where you hide the clothes you bought but don't want your parents to see yet. It's the place where clothes go to either be neatly folded or become a chaotic mess.
usage_notes: Can refer to a piece of furniture (wardrobe) or a small room (closet). Less common than 'aparador' or 'closet' in modern colloquial speech but still understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno na ang kanyang **damitan** ng mga bagong bili na damit.","translation":"Her **wardrobe** is already full of newly bought clothes."},{"sentence":"Pakiayos ang mga damit sa loob ng **damitan**.","translation":"Please arrange the clothes inside the **closet**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal at legal na kasulatan ng kasunduan sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang panig.
original_explanation: The piece of paper that seals your fate for the next 6 months to a year. BPO agents, OFWs, and artists know this well. It's the 'read the fine print' document that dictates your sahod, your deliverables, and your non-compete clause. Breaking up with a jowa is hard, but breaking a 'kuntrata' can cost you money.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'kontrata', which is the more standard spelling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumirma siya ng dalawang taong **kuntrata** sa kumpanya.","translation":"He signed a two-year **contract** with the company."},{"sentence":"Basahing mabuti ang lahat ng nakasulat sa **kuntrata** bago pumirma.","translation":"Read everything written in the **contract** carefully before signing."}]

meaning_filipino: Mapagbigay, mapagpaumanhin, o ang pagkakaroon ng katangiang magparaya o magpaubaya sa iba.
etymology: Hindi tiyak ang pinagmulan, ngunit malalim ang ugat sa kulturang Pilipino na may kinalaman sa pagbibigay at pakikipagkapwa-tao.
original_explanation: This is the art of giving way, of letting go, of being the 'bigger person.' It's when you let your sibling have the last piece of chicken joy. It's when you let someone cut in line because they look more stressed than you. In love, 'pagpaparaya' is the ultimate hugot move: 'Mahal kita, pero mas sasaya ka sa kanya, kaya magpaparaya na ako.' (I love you, but you'll be happier with them, so I'll give way.) It's the theme song of every martyr in a Filipino movie.
usage_notes: Madalas ginagamit sa anyong pandiwa na 'magparaya' (to give way) at pangngalan na 'pagpaparaya' (the act of giving way). Nagpapahiwatig ito ng sakripisyo para sa ikabubuti ng iba.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong matutong **magparaya** para sa kapayapaan ng pamilya.","translation":"You need to learn to **give way** for the sake of family peace."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagpaparaya** ay tanda ng tunay na pagmamahal.","translation":"Her **act of giving way** is a sign of true love."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa estado ng sukdulang kahirapan; walang-wala ni isang kusing o anumang ari-arian.
original_explanation: That feeling a few days before sweldo. 'Yung 'isang kahig, isang tuka' level na. It's not just 'wala akong pera', it's 'wala TALAGA akong pera'. Your wallet is a desert, your G-Cash is crying, and your diet consists of instant noodles and hope.
usage_notes: The repetition of 'wala' emphasizes the complete lack of something, usually money.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula sila sa pagiging **walang-wala** pero dahil sa sipag at tiyaga, umasenso sila.","translation":"They started from being **completely broke**, but because of hard work and perseverance, they succeeded."},{"sentence":"Paano ako makakatulong kung ako mismo ay **walang-wala** ngayon?","translation":"How can I help when I myself am **destitute** right now?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay o pagpapatong ng isang bagay sa isang partikular na lugar o sisidlan sa hinaharap. Hinaharap na anyo ng "lagyan".
original_explanation: When your mom gives you a list of chores. "Lalagyan mo ng palaman 'yang tinapay." "Lalagyan mo ng tubig 'yung pitsel." It's the future tense of "to put," and it's your future for the next hour. The opposite of "aalisin."
usage_notes: This is the future tense, object-focus verb. It implies an action of placing something onto or into something else. Distinguish from the noun 'lalagyan' (container).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lalagyan** ko ng palamuti ang buong bahay para sa Pasko.","translation":"I **will put** decorations all over the house for Christmas."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **lalagyan** mo ng sisi sa nangyari?","translation":"Who **will you put** the blame on for what happened?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malambot na bahagi sa tuktok ng ulo ng isang sanggol; sa pangkalahatang gamit, ang pinakatuktok ng ulo.
original_explanation: That soft spot on a baby's head that gives everyone anxiety. It's the "loading... please wait" area of the skull. For adults, it's just the very top of your head, where a crown would sit if you were royalty, or where your kuya would give you a "kutos" (a light knock on the head).
usage_notes: Used both medically for the baby's soft spot (fontanelle) and generally for the crown of the head in adults.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa paghawak sa **bumbunan** ng sanggol dahil malambot pa ito.","translation":"Be careful in handling the baby's **fontanelle** because it is still soft."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman ko ang patak ng ulan sa aking **bumbunan**.","translation":"I felt the drop of rain on the **crown of my head**."}]

translation: to have someone wear something; to get something through
meaning_filipino: Ang paghiling o pag-uutos sa iba na isuot ang isang kasuotan; ang pagpilit na maipasok ang isang bagay sa masikip na espasyo.
original_explanation: This is what your mom says when she shoves a dress at you for a family gathering: "Ito, *pasuot* ko sa'yo." It's a command disguised as a suggestion. It can also mean to get something inserted into a tight space, like trying to get your oversized luggage into a small car trunk. "Paki-*pasuot* nga nitong maleta sa likod."
usage_notes: Can refer to clothing or fitting an object into a space. The context determines the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaari ko bang **pasuot** sa iyo itong ginawa kong damit?","translation":"May I **have you wear** this dress I made?"},{"sentence":"Mahirap **pasuot** ang sinulid sa butas ng karayom.","translation":"It's hard **to get** the thread **through** the eye of the needle."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglalapat o pagbibigay ng parusa, multa, o sentensya alinsunod sa batas o regulasyon.
original_explanation: This is the legal system's version of 'consequences.' It's the official act of handing down a punishment, like a judge sentencing a criminal, a traffic enforcer giving you a ticket, or your mom grounding you for a week. It's the formal application of a penalty. 'Due process, bes, bago ang pagpapatao ng parusa.'
usage_notes: Primarily used in legal, judicial, or formal administrative contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapatao** ng parusang kamatayan ay isang kontrobersyal na isyu.","translation":"The **imposition** of the death penalty is a controversial issue."},{"sentence":"Tinalakay sa pulong ang **pagpapatao** ng mas mataas na multa sa mga lumalabag sa batas-trapiko.","translation":"The meeting discussed the **imposition** of higher fines for traffic law violators."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, katibayan, o ebidensya na nagpapatunay sa katotohanan o kawastuhan ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the more common cousin of 'prueba'. When your friend says, "Nakita ko si ex mo may kasamang iba," you reply, "Pruweba? Picture or it didn't happen." It's the 'receipts' you show to win an argument. The ultimate tool against chismis.
usage_notes: Ito ang mas karaniwan at kolokyal na baybay at bigkas kumpara sa 'prueba'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Walang matibay na **pruweba** kaya ibinasura ang kaso.","translation":"There was no strong **proof**, so the case was dismissed."},{"sentence":"Ang resibo ang tanging **pruweba** mo na nagbayad ka.","translation":"The receipt is your only **proof** that you paid."}]

translation: to fish in the open sea
meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pangingisda sa malawak na karagatan o dagat.
original_explanation: This isn't just fishing in a small pond (that's more like 'mamingwit'). This is the real deal, the 'Deadliest Catch' version of fishing. It's what fishermen do, going out into the open sea, facing the waves, to bring back the fish for your sinigang. It implies a serious, often commercial, fishing expedition.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to fishing in the sea, as opposed to rivers or lakes. It implies a larger scale of fishing than 'mamingwit' (to fish with a hook and line).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maagang umaalis ang mga mangingisda upang **managat**.","translation":"The fishermen leave early to **fish in the open sea**."},{"sentence":"Ang **managat** ang pangunahing ikinabubuhay ng mga tao sa islang iyon.","translation":"**Fishing in the sea** is the main livelihood of the people on that island."}]

translation: to be skewered; to be strung together
meaning_filipino: Ang mailagay o maipasok sa isang patpat, alambre, o sinulid sa pamamagitan ng pagtusok.
