original_explanation: Ito 'yung ginagawa sa isaw, betamax, at hotdog bago iihaw. In a BPO context, ito 'yung sunod-sunod na irate calls na natatanggap mo; parang natuhog ka ng kamalasan. Pwede ring 'yung mga resibo na tinutusok mo sa isang lalagyan para 'di mawala.
usage_notes: Commonly associated with cooking, especially barbecue. Can be used metaphorically for a series of connected events or items.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **matuhog** nang maayos ang mga baboy para sa barbecue.","translation":"The pork pieces need **to be skewered** properly for the barbecue."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **matuhog** ang lahat ng butil ng kuwintas na kumalat.","translation":"She tried **to string together** all the beads of the necklace that scattered."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang palabas na karaniwang binubuo ng mga akrobata, payaso, at mga sinanay na hayop, na kadalasang ginaganap sa isang malaking tolda.
original_explanation: That one place with clowns, acrobats, and magic tricks. Also, a very accurate description of your group chat when a hot new chismis drops. Also, the Philippine Senate sometimes.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin nang literal para sa isang palabas o patalinghaga upang ilarawan ang isang magulo o nakakatawang sitwasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala kami ng aming mga magulang sa **sirko** noong Pasko.","translation":"Our parents brought us to the **circus** during Christmas."},{"sentence":"Para kayong **sirko** kung mag-away, ang gulo-gulo!","translation":"You guys are like a **circus** when you fight, so chaotic!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglusong o pag-lubog sa ilalim ng tubig.
original_explanation: What you do at the beach in Batangas to see the coral reefs, or what you do to your DMs when you see your crush is online. It's the act of going deep. Can also be used figuratively, like "sumisid sa problema" (to dive into a problem).
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pangngalan (ang sisid) o pandiwa (sumisid, sisirin).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahusay siyang **sumisid** para kumuha ng mga perlas.","translation":"He **dives** well to get pearls."},{"sentence":"Malalim ang kanyang **sisid** kaya nakaabot siya sa ilalim ng dagat.","translation":"His **dive** was deep, so he was able to reach the seabed."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng manok o ibon na walang buntot o may napakaikling buntot.
original_explanation: Imagine a chicken that looks like its rear end got cropped. That's 'tukol'. It's like your crush's text message—bitin, with no 'I love you too' at the end. It's the bob cut of the chicken world.
usage_notes: Primarily used to describe chickens or other birds.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kakaiba ang itsura ng manok na **tukol**.","translation":"The **tailless** chicken looks strange."},{"sentence":"Nahuli niya ang isang tandang na **tukol** sa bukid.","translation":"He caught a **tailless** rooster in the field."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pag-iisip o paglikha ng mga haka-haka habang gising at malay; paglalakbay ng diwa.
etymology: A phrase composed of `pangangarap` (dreaming) and `nang gising` (while awake).
original_explanation: This is you, staring at your computer screen at 3 PM, but in your head, you're on a beach in Palawan, accepting an Oscar, or finally telling your boss what you really think. It's the mind's escape-from-reality button, often pressed during boring meetings or long commutes.
usage_notes: A very common and expressive phrase.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na ang **pangangarap nang gising** at tapusin mo na ang iyong trabaho.","translation":"Stop **daydreaming** and finish your work."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang mag-isip tungkol sa kanyang hinaharap, isang uri ng **pangangarap nang gising**.","translation":"She loves to think about her future, a kind of **daydreaming**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manipis na aklat o babasahin na may takip na papel, naglalaman ng impormasyon o patalastas tungkol sa isang partikular na paksa.
original_explanation: Before pop-up ads, there were these. The thing that gets handed to you in the mall that you either politely accept and throw away later, or actually read if it's for a 50% off sale or a new condo you can't afford.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Namimigay sila ng **polyeto** tungkol sa tamang pag-iwas sa dengue.","translation":"They are giving out **pamphlets** about the proper prevention of dengue."},{"sentence":"Nakatanggap ako ng **polyeto** para sa isang bagong bukas na gym.","translation":"I received a **flyer** for a newly opened gym."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit at karaniwang maitim na marka sa balat ng tao na sanhi ng pagkakumpol ng mga selulang gumagawa ng kulay (melanocytes).
original_explanation: That beauty mark on your face? That's a 'taling'. It's a mole. Sometimes it's just a dot, sometimes it's the defining feature that makes someone memorable. People even get fake ones drawn on! It's one of those things that can be seen as a unique charm or something you want to have removed.
usage_notes: A very common word for a skin mole. 'Nunal' is a more formal synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **taling** siya malapit sa kanyang labi.","translation":"She has a **mole** near her lip."},{"sentence":"Ipinasuri niya sa doktor ang kakaibang itsura ng kanyang **taling**.","translation":"She had her unusually shaped **mole** checked by a doctor."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o bagay na nasa proseso ng pagdating o malapit nang dumating sa isang lugar.
original_explanation: This is the status of your Shopee or Lazada order. "Your package is padating na!" It's also what you tell your friends who are already at the resto: "On the way na ako, padating na!" (even if you just got out of the shower).
usage_notes: Formed from 'pa-' (going towards) + 'dating' (arrival). It functions like an adjective or a verb participle.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kayong maingay, **padating** na ang guro!","translation":"Don't be noisy, the teacher is **arriving**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng pagiging magulo, walang kaayusan, o hindi organisado sa mga bagay-bagay o sa pamumuhay.
original_explanation: Eto 'yung kwarto mo after a week of "saka na lang aayusin" or 'yung desk mo na parang dinaanan ng bagyo. It's when things are not in their proper place. Pwedeng tao (messy person) or lugar (messy place). Parang 'yung isip mo kapag sabay-sabay ang deadlines.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang isang lugar o ang pag-uugali ng isang tao. Ang pambabaeng anyo ay "disordenada."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayusin mo nga ang kwarto mo, napaka-**disordenado**!","translation":"Fix your room, it's so **messy**!"},{"sentence":"**Disordenado** ang kanyang mga plano kaya walang natapos nang maayos.","translation":"His plans were **disorganized**, that's why nothing was finished properly."}]

translation: to ride a truck; to use a truck
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsakay o paggamit ng isang trak para sa transportasyon o paghakot ng mga kargamento.
original_explanation: The Tagalized verb for when you need to move house and you call your one friend with a pickup, or when you see people in the province hitching a ride on the back of a large vehicle. It's not about driving the truck, but using it. 'Tara, mag-truck na lang tayo, 'di kasya sa kotse 'tong mga gamit.'
usage_notes: A colloquial, Taglish verb. Not formal. Often implies riding *on* a truck rather than driving it.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magtruck** para madala lahat ng donasyon sa evacuation center.","translation":"We need to **use a truck** to bring all the donations to the evacuation center."},{"sentence":"Noong bata kami, masayang **magtruck** papunta sa bukid.","translation":"When we were kids, it was fun to **ride a truck** going to the farm."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lubos na pagkaunawa o pag-alam sa isang bagay, ideya, o katotohanan na dati ay hindi malinaw.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `ma-` (pandiwa ng kakayahan/di-sinasadya) + `tanto` (pagkaunawa), na hango sa salitang Espanyol na 'tanto'.
original_explanation: ‘Yung "Aha!" moment mo kapag bigla mong naintindihan 'yung plot twist ng K-drama, o 'yung moment na na-realize mong ikaw pala 'yung "marupok" sa situationship. It's that sudden clarity, like when the Wi-Fi finally connects after 10 tries.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin para sa mga sandali ng biglaang pagkaunawa o realisasyon. Ito ay may bahagyang pormal o pampanitikang dating kaysa sa "malaman" o "maintindihan".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nang makita ko siyang may kasamang iba, doon ko lang **natanto** na tapos na talaga kami.","translation":"When I saw him with someone else, only then did I **realize** that we were really over."},{"sentence":"Kalaunan ay **matatanto** mo rin ang halaga ng iyong mga pinaghirapan.","translation":"Eventually you will also **comprehend** the value of your hard work."}]

translation: will be held accountable; will be made to answer for
meaning_filipino: Hihingan ng paliwanag o responsibilidad para sa isang kilos, pagkakamali, o kaganapan.
original_explanation: When you 'accidentally' use your mom's credit card for in-game purchases and she finds the bill. Nako, you **papanagutin**! It means you're going to be held responsible for your actions. It’s the corporate way of saying 'Someone's getting fired,' or the political way of saying 'We will form a committee.'
usage_notes: Commonly used in legal, political, and formal contexts to denote accountability.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga opisyal na sangkot sa katiwalian ay **papanagutin** sa batas.","translation":"The officials involved in corruption **will be held accountable** under the law."},{"sentence":"Sinuman ang may kasalanan sa nangyari ay dapat **papanagutin**.","translation":"Whoever is at fault for what happened must **be made to answer for it**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nangangahulugang napapalibutan o nasa paligid ng isang bagay o lugar.
original_explanation: Imagine you're the last piece of chicharon in the middle of the table, and everyone's staring at you. You are 'nililigiran'. You are surrounded. It's about being in the center of attention, or being completely enclosed. Pwedeng 'ligid ng kaaway' or 'ligid ng chismosa mong kapitbahay'.
usage_notes: Ang mga anyong pandiwa na 'lumigid' (to roam around), 'ligiran' (to surround), at pang-uri na 'paligid-ligid' (loitering) ay karaniwan ding ginagamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ligid** ng matataas na pader ang mansyon.","translation":"The mansion is **surrounded** by high walls."},{"sentence":"Pulis ang **ligid** sa buong lugar ng krimen.","translation":"Police **surrounded** the entire crime scene."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang muling pagpuno sa isang lalagyan; karagdagang serving ng inumin o pagkain.
original_explanation: The most beautiful nine-letter word in any Filipino restaurant, usually preceded by 'unli'. 'Kuya, pa-refill!' is the national anthem of Mang Inasal diners and anyone availing an 'unli-iced tea' promo. It's not just a word, it's a strategy.
usage_notes: Almost always used in the context of 'unlimited' or 'unli' rice, soup, or drinks.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Libre ang **refill** ng iced tea sa restoran na iyon.","translation":"The iced tea **refill** is free at that restaurant."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang baso o sisidlan na partikular na ginagamit para sa pag-inom ng alak, lalo na sa isang pangkatang inuman.
original_explanation: This is the sacred vessel, the Holy Grail of inuman sessions. It's the designated glass that gets passed around the circle. It could be a proper shot glass, a small plastic cup, or even the cap of the liquor bottle. Losing the tagayan is a minor crisis. "Nasaan na 'yung tagayan?" is a question that signals the party is getting serious.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to the cup/glass used for sharing a drink in a group setting. It can also refer to the drinking session itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiabot ng **tagayan**, ako na ang susunod na iinom.","translation":"Please pass the **drinking glass**, I'm next to drink."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula na ang **tagayan** sa kanto.","translation":"The drinking session has started at the corner."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal at pinaikling salita para sa 'pictures' o mga larawan.
etymology: Pinaikling anyo ng salitang Ingles na 'pictures'.
original_explanation: Ito ang sinisigaw mo sa kaibigan mong may magandang phone: "Send **pics** naman mamaya!" It's the currency of Instagram, the proof of "pics or it didn't happen," and the reason why your phone storage is always full. 'Yung 50 shots para sa isang disenteng profile picture.
usage_notes: Karaniwan sa impormal na digital at pasalitang komunikasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng kuha! Paki-send naman ng **pics** sa GC.","translation":"The shot is beautiful! Please send the **pics** to the group chat."}]

translation: to lose effect; to become invalid; to expire
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkawala ng kapangyarihan, epekto, o legalidad ng isang bagay, kasunduan, o batas.
original_explanation: Parang promo code na ginamit mo na, o 'yung powers ng kape pagkatapos ng pangatlong all-nighter sa BPO. It's when something just stops working. Your driver's license, your warranty, or even 'yung "I love you" na paulit-ulit na lang sinasabi pero wala nang dating. It has lost its magic, its power, its validity.
usage_notes: Commonly used in legal, medical, and formal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Mawawalan ng bisa** ang kontratang ito pagkatapos ng isang taon.","translation":"This contract will **become invalid** after one year."},{"sentence":"Unti-unting **nawalan ng bisa** ang gamot kaya bumalik ang lagnat niya.","translation":"The medicine gradually **lost its effect**, so his fever returned."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglalagay o pagkakabit ng isang kagamitan o sistema upang ito ay maging handa nang gamitin. Maaari rin itong tumukoy sa isang lugar o kampo ng militar.
original_explanation: 'Yung pagkabit ng bagong aircon, o 'yung pagse-set up ng bagong app sa phone mo na kailangan ng sandamakmak na "Allow" at "Agree". Pwede ring art exhibit na mukhang kalat para sa iba pero "deep" daw ang meaning.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa akto ng pag-install o sa lugar na na-install (hal. instalasyong militar, instalasyong pansining).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **instalasyon** ng bagong software ay aabutin ng isang oras.","translation":"The **installation** of the new software will take an hour."},{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang seguridad sa **instalasyon** ng militar.","translation":"The security at the military **installation** is tight."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong ang trabaho ay may kinalaman sa promosyon at pagbebenta ng mga produkto o serbisyo, kasama na ang market research at advertising.
original_explanation: The person in your office who's obsessed with 'engagement,' 'ROI,' and 'synergy.' They speak in acronyms and can sell you anything, from a new brand of coffee to a revolutionary can opener. They're the reason you suddenly want to buy that thing you saw on a Facebook ad at 3 AM.
usage_notes: A direct loanword used in business and corporate settings in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kapatid ko ay isang digital **marketer** sa isang malaking kumpanya.","translation":"My sibling is a digital **marketer** in a big company."},{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng isang mahusay na **marketer** para mapalakas ang benta.","translation":"We need a good **marketer** to boost sales."}]

translation: to be suitable for; to agree with (one's system)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging angkop o bagay ng isang bagay (gaya ng gamot, pagkain, o klima) sa isang tao, na nagdudulot ng mabuting epekto.
original_explanation: This is the magic word when a skincare product finally works on you. "OMG, bes, **humiyang** sa akin 'yung toner na 'to!" It's also what your lola says when the new 'katialis' works on her skin rash. It means your body and the 'thing' are in a happy, compatible relationship. #SanaAllHiyang
usage_notes: Commonly used in the context of health, medicine, food, skincare, and sometimes even climate or environment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa wakas, nakahanap ako ng shampoo na **humiyang** sa buhok ko.","translation":"Finally, I found a shampoo that is **suitable for** my hair."},{"sentence":"Hindi **humiyang** sa kanya ang gamot kaya pinalitan ito ng doktor.","translation":"The medicine did not **agree with** his system, so the doctor changed it."}]

translation: to be jealous, to feel envious
meaning_filipino: Ang pagdama ng matinding selos o inggit sa isang tao, kadalasan dahil sa atensyon, pag-aari, o tagumpay na natatanggap nito mula sa iba.
etymology: From the verb-forming prefix 'ma-' and the root 'bugho', which means jealousy or envy.
original_explanation: The feeling you get when you see your ex with someone new, and it feels like your heart is being pinched. Or when you see your friend's IG story from Japan while you're buried in work. That's it. You're 'manibugho'. It's the classier, more poetic version of 'selos'.
usage_notes: A more formal or literary term for 'magseselos'. The noun form is 'panibugho'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya maiwasang **manibugho** sa tagumpay ng kanyang kaibigan.","translation":"She couldn't help but **feel envious** of her friend's success."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa labis na pag-ibig, madali siyang **manibugho**.","translation":"Because of intense love, he easily **gets jealous**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga bagay, tao, o katangian na may kaugnayan sa isang isla o kapuluan. Maaari ring mangahulugan ng pagiging makitid ang pag-iisip o limitado ang pananaw.
original_explanation: Since the Philippines is an archipelago, technically tayong lahat ay 'insular'. But it can also mean someone who's close-minded, parang 'yung tita mo na ayaw sa lahat ng bago at iba sa nakasanayan niya. "Noong panahon namin..." ang laging simula.
usage_notes: Isang pormal at akademikong salita. Mayroon itong heograpikal na kahulugan (kaugnay sa isla) at metaporikal na kahulugan (makitid ang pag-iisip).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Pilipinas ay isang bansang **insular** na binubuo ng libo-libong mga pulo.","translation":"The Philippines is an **insular** nation made up of thousands of islands."},{"sentence":"Pinuna ang kanyang **insular** na pananaw sa mga isyung pandaigdigan.","translation":"His **insular** perspective on global issues was criticized."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang miyembro ng oligarkiya; isang napakayamang tao na may malaking impluwensya sa politika at lipunan.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na 'oligarch', na mula sa Griyegong 'oligarkhēs'.
original_explanation: Sila yung mga "ultra-rich" na aakalain mong may-ari ng Pilipinas. Yung yaman nila hindi na ma-compute ng calculator mo, at isang text lang nila sa politiko, baka magbago na ang batas. Sila ang mga totoong "big boss".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan sa klase sa kasaysayan ang papel ng mga **oligark** sa ekonomiya ng bansa.","translation":"The history class is studying the role of **oligarchs** in the country's economy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lugar na patutunguhan o layuning marating ng isang tao o bagay sa kanyang paglalakbay.
etymology: Nagmula sa salitang-ugat na 'doon' na may panlaping 'pa-...(an)' at pag-uulit ng pantig 'ro' (pa-ro-doon-an), na nangangahulugang 'lugar na pupuntahan doon'.
original_explanation: Kung saan ka bababa, sabi ng konduktor. Sa Grab, ito 'yung 'destination'. Sa buhay, ito 'yung goal mo. At higit sa lahat, ito yung tanong na mahirap sagutin: 'Saan ba ang **paroroonan** ng relasyong ito?' #Hugot
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi namin alam kung ano ang aming **paroroonan** pagkatapos ng kolehiyo.","translation":"We didn't know what our **destination** would be after college."},{"sentence":"Itanong mo sa tsuper kung dadaan ba siya sa iyong **paroroonan**.","translation":"Ask the driver if he will pass by your **destination**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sariling bansa o lupang sinilangan ng isang tao, na itinuturing na parang isang ina na nag-aaruga.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng 'ina' at 'bayan', na literal na nangangahulugang 'mother country'.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'para sa bayan' vibe. It's the reason why OFWs cry when they hear 'Lupang Hinirang' in another country. It's the ultimate addressee of every patriotic speech and every 'Pilipinas, Gising!' post on social media. It's the mother figure of the whole country.
usage_notes: Isang pormal at makatang pagtukoy sa sariling bansa. Madalas gamitin sa mga tula, awit, at talumpating makabayan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming bayani ang nag-alay ng buhay para sa **Inang-bayan**.","translation":"Many heroes offered their lives for the **Motherland**."},{"sentence":"Tungkulin nating mahalin at paglingkuran ang ating **Inang-bayan**.","translation":"It is our duty to love and serve our **Motherland**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat ng mga bagay na tinipon, inipon, o pinagsama-sama dahil sa isang partikular na katangian, interes, o layunin.
original_explanation: Ito yung formal, textbook spelling of 'koleksyon'. Parang 'yung mga Funko Pop mo na nakadisplay, 'yung mga stamps na tinatago ni lolo, o 'yung koleksiyon ng screenshots ng chat niyo ng ex mo. Anything you gather and keep is a koleksiyon.
usage_notes: This is the more formal, Hispanized spelling. 'Koleksyon' (Filipinized spelling) is more common in everyday use.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagmamalaki niya ang kanyang **koleksiyon** ng mga lumang barya.","translation":"He is proud of his **collection** of old coins."},{"sentence":"Ang museo ay may malawak na **koleksiyon** ng mga artifact.","translation":"The museum has an extensive **collection** of artifacts."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang elementong kemikal na metaliko, may kulay pilak-puti, magaan, matibay, at hindi kinakalawang. Ang atomic number nito ay 22 at may simbolong Ti.
etymology: From English "Titanium", adapted to Tagalog phonology.
original_explanation: That super strong, lightweight metal you hear about in sci-fi movies or high-end bike frames. It's the boujee cousin of steel and aluminum. If your phone case is made of **Titanyum**, you're either very clumsy or very extra.
usage_notes: Used in scientific and technical contexts. The English spelling "Titanium" is also widely accepted.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga artipisyal na buto ay madalas na gawa sa **Titanyum** dahil sa tibay nito.","translation":"Artificial bones are often made of **Titanium** because of its durability."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghatak o pagbatak sa isang bagay patungo sa direksyon ng gumagawa ng kilos.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're trying to pull open a door that clearly says 'Push'. Also, what your friend does to you when there's a 70% off sale at the mall. 'Tara na, bes!'
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'paghatak' but 'paghila' can be gentler.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paghila** sa lubid ang huling bahagi ng paligsahan.","translation":"The **pulling** of the rope is the final part of the competition."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang alternatibong baybay para sa 'momiya'; isang bangkay na pinreserba.
original_explanation: Same as 'momiya', just a different spelling. It's like 'Filipino' vs 'Pilipino' – you know what it means, but someone will always correct you. This is the version you'd probably text, while 'momiya' is what you'd see in a textbook.
usage_notes: Mas karaniwan sa pasalitang wika kaysa sa pormal na pagsulat. Ang "momiya" ang pamantayang baybay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakatakot ang itsura ng **momya** sa pelikula.","translation":"The appearance of the **mummy** in the movie was scary."}]

translation: to ring (a bell); to call (by phone)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapatunog ng kampana o doorbell; ang pagtawag sa telepono.
original_explanation: "Tumimbre ka 'pag nasa labas ka na." is the classic Pinoy "I'm here" text before Grab and Messenger made it automated. It's the sound that announces a visitor, a delivery, or your friend who's come to collect a debt. In modern terms, it can also mean to phone someone. "Tumimbre si boss, OT na naman daw."
usage_notes: Primarily used for doorbells or making a phone call. Can be used figuratively to mean "to get in touch" or "to make one's presence known."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumimbre** kaagad ang bata sa pinto pagdating niya mula sa eskwela.","translation":"The child immediately **rang** the doorbell upon arriving from school."},{"sentence":"Sino ba 'yung **tumimbre** sa telepono kaninang madaling araw?","translation":"Who was that who **called** on the phone in the early hours of the morning?"}]

meaning_filipino: Magbigay ng isang katanungan sa isang tao upang makakuha ng impormasyon o kasagutan.
original_explanation: The official verb of the chismosa. It's what you do when you see your friend with a new bag ('Tanungin mo kung magkano!'), or when your boss gives a vague instruction ('Tanungin mo kung para kailan 'to.'). It's the action of not being shy and just getting the info you need.
usage_notes: The object of this verb is the person being asked. To ask *about* something, you'd use 'itanong'. Ex: 'Tanungin mo si Maria.' (Ask Maria.) vs. 'Itanong mo ang presyo.' (Ask the price.)
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tanungin** mo nga si nanay kung ano ang ulam natin mamaya.","translation":"**Ask** mom what our viand is for later."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mahiyang **tanungin** ang guro kung may hindi ka naiintindihan.","translation":"Don't be shy to **ask** the teacher if there's something you don't understand."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing mataba ang isang tao, hayop, o bagay; lagyan ng pataba ang lupa.
etymology: Mula sa "pa-" (panlaping pangkasanhi) + "taba" + "-in" (panlaping pokus sa layon).
original_explanation: The action verb for 'pataba'. Ito yung ginagawa ng lola mo sa'yo tuwing bakasyon, "Kumain ka pa, apo, para kang tingting! Kailangan kang **patabain**!" It's also what farmers do to their land before planting season.
usage_notes: Ang layon ng pandiwa ang nagtatakda ng kahulugan. "Patabain ang baboy" (fatten the pig). "Patabain ang lupa" (fertilize the soil).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga baboy ay pinapakain nang marami upang **patabain** bago ibenta.","translation":"The pigs are fed a lot to be **fattened** before being sold."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **patabain** ang lupa bago ka magtanim ng gulay.","translation":"You need to **fertilize** the soil before you plant vegetables."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sapal o tuyong latak na naiiwan pagkatapos katasin ang isang prutas o halaman, lalo na ang tubo.
etymology: Hango sa wikang Espanyol na 'bagazo' (pulp, dregs).
original_explanation: The stuff that's left over after you squeeze all the juice out of sugarcane. It's the "sana all" of the sugarcane world—it's seen all the sweetness but is left dry. In a hugot sense, it's what you feel like after giving your all to a relationship that didn't work out: used and discarded.
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of sugarcane processing but can be applied to the pulp of other fruits.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginagamit ang **bagaso** ng tubo bilang panggatong sa mga pagawaan ng asukal.","translation":"The sugarcane **bagasse** is used as fuel in sugar mills."},{"sentence":"Itapon mo na lang ang **bagaso** ng pinya pagkatapos kunin ang katas.","translation":"Just throw away the pineapple **pulp** after extracting the juice."}]

translation: will become fast; will speed up
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagtaas ng tulin o pag-usad nang mas mabilis sa hinaharap. Ito ang anyong pangkasalukuyan ng pandiwang 'bilis'.
original_explanation: The future tense of "bilis". This is what you hope happens to the internet connection when you're lagging in Mobile Legends. Or what your Grab driver says about the traffic, but you both know it's a beautiful lie. "Bibilis din 'to, ma'am/sir."
usage_notes: Future tense of 'bilis'. Often used with 'ang' to refer to the thing that will speed up (e.g., *Bibilis ang takbo...*).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kapag inayos na ang kalsada, **bibilis** ang daloy ng trapiko.","translation":"When the road is fixed, the flow of traffic **will speed up**."},{"sentence":"**Bibilis** ang paggaling mo kung iinumin mo ang iyong gamot.","translation":"Your recovery **will be faster** if you drink your medicine."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking halamang may matigas at makahoy na katawan at mga sanga.
original_explanation: The big green thing in your backyard that gives you shade, mangoes, and a lot of leaves to sweep. It's where the kapre supposedly hangs out. Also, 'puno' can mean the trunk of the tree itself. Not to be confused with its alter-ego, 'punô'.
usage_notes: The stress is on the first syllable (PU-no). When used as a prefix, it often means 'chief' or 'head', like 'punong-guro' (head teacher).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakataas ng **puno** ng niyog na iyon.","translation":"That coconut **tree** is so tall."},{"sentence":"Umupo siya sa ilalim ng **puno** para magpahinga.","translation":"He sat under the **tree** to rest."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na kasuotang panlalaki sa Pilipinas, karaniwang gawa sa manipis na tela tulad ng pinya o jusi, may burda, at isinusuot na hindi nakasuksok sa loob ng pantalon. Maikling tawag para sa Barong Tagalog.
etymology: From 'baro ng Tagalog' meaning 'dress of the Tagalog'.
original_explanation: The official formal wear for Filipino men. It's what you wear to weddings, graduations, and SONA. It's classy, airy (perfect for the climate), and see-through, so you can't hide anything underneath—a philosophy that dates back to Spanish colonial times. Wearing a barong is an instant +100 pogi points.
usage_notes: This is the shortened, common name for 'Barong Tagalog'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magsuot ka ng **barong** sa kasal ni Kuya.","translation":"Wear a **barong** to your brother's wedding."},{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng burda ng **barong** na gawa sa Batangas.","translation":"The embroidery on the **barong** made in Batangas is beautiful."}]

meaning_filipino: Ilagay sa posisyong nakahiga ang isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: This is what you do to a baby when it's sleepy time, or what you do to yourself after a long day at work. It's the action of putting someone or something in a horizontal, lying-down position. 'Bes, pagod na 'ko, gusto ko na lang ihiga ang sarili ko sa kama.'
usage_notes: `Humiga` is the intransitive form (to lie down oneself), while `ihiga` is transitive (to lay something/someone else down).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahan-dahan niyang **inihiga** ang natutulog na sanggol sa kuna.","translation":"He gently **laid** the sleeping baby down in the crib."},{"sentence":"**Iihiga** ko lang itong mga libro sa mesa.","translation":"I'll just **lay** these books down on the table."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng alinlangan o kawalan ng tiwala sa isang bagay o tao na nangyari na.
original_explanation: That feeling you get when your friend says "On the way na ako" but you know they just woke up. You nagduda. It's the start of many marites investigations and "sabi ko na nga ba" moments.
usage_notes: Past tense of 'magduda'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagduda** ang detektib sa alibi ng suspek.","translation":"The detective **doubted** the suspect's alibi."},{"sentence":"Kahit minsan ba hindi ka **nagduda** sa mga sinabi niya?","translation":"Did you not even once **doubt** the things he said?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bilog at paarkong bubong o kisame, karaniwang matatagpuan sa ibabaw ng isang malaking gusali tulad ng simbahan o kapitolyo.
original_explanation: That big, round, majestic roof you see on top of old churches or government buildings. Parang half-ball na pinatong sa building. It's the architectural equivalent of a crown.
usage_notes: Primarily used in architectural or historical contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ginintuang **simboryo** ng moske ay kumikinang sa sikat ng araw.","translation":"The golden **dome** of the mosque glitters in the sunlight."},{"sentence":"Inakyat ng mga trabahador ang **simboryo** ng katedral para sa pagkukumpuni.","translation":"The workers climbed the **dome** of the cathedral for repairs."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbabahagi ng isang bagay sa hinaharap, lalo na ang impormasyon o isang post sa social media. Isa itong Taglish na anyo ng pandiwa.
etymology: Tagalog prefix 'mag-' + future tense infix '-se-' + English root 'share'.
original_explanation: The future tense of online generosity (or oversharing). 'Wait, this meme is hilarious, magseshare ako sa GC!' It's the promise to spread the word, whether it's a funny video, a juicy blind item, or a fake news article your tita found on Facebook.
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of social media and digital content. The formal Filipino equivalent is 'magbabahagi' or 'ibabahagi'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kapag nanalo ako sa lotto, **magseshare** ako ng balato sa inyo.","translation":"If I win the lottery, I **will share** a portion of the winnings with you."},{"sentence":"Sabi niya **magseshare** daw siya ng link para sa Zoom meeting.","translation":"He said he **will share** the link for the Zoom meeting."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay ng damit o kasuotan sa katawan. Ginagamit din ito para sa kilos ng pagpasok sa masikip na espasyo.
original_explanation: The act of getting dressed. It's also used for getting into tight spaces, like 'sumuot sa siksikan.' It's that feeling of trying to squeeze into your old high school jeans. 'Isinuot mo na ba yung facemask mo?' became the daily grind.
usage_notes: The root verb is 'suot'. Inflected forms include 'isinuot' (wore), 'sinusuot' (wearing), 'isusuot' (will wear). The alternate meaning is 'to squeeze through'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang mag-**suot** ng sapatos bago lumabas.","translation":"Don't forget to **wear** your shoes before going out."},{"sentence":"Nahirapan siyang **sumuot** sa maliit na butas sa pader.","translation":"He had a hard time **squeezing through** the small hole in the wall."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tradisyonal na paraan ng panggagamot sa pamamagitan ng masahe at pag-aayos ng mga buto o kalamnan. Tumutukoy din ito sa tradisyonal na komadrona na tumutulong sa panganganak.
original_explanation: This is the OG Pinoy chiropractor and massage therapist rolled into one. Feeling like your bones are misaligned from sitting in traffic for 5 hours? Or maybe you're 'lamig' from the office AC? You need a good hilot. It's that deep-tissue massage that feels like a full-body reset, often with coconut oil, and sometimes involves a bit of spiritual cleansing. Also, before modern hospitals were common, the hilot was the go-to person for delivering babies.
usage_notes: The term can refer to both the practice (the massage itself) and the practitioner (the person performing it).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng **hilot** dahil masakit ang likod ko.","translation":"I need a traditional **massage** because my back hurts."},{"sentence":"Ang **hilot** sa aming baryo ang tumulong sa lola ko na manganak.","translation":"The **traditional midwife** in our village helped my grandmother give birth."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpalo o paghampas nang malakas sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'hataw'. This is the action of delivering that powerful hit. It's what you do to a piñata at a birthday party. It's also what you want to do to your slow laptop to make it work faster (but please don't). In sales, 'hatawin ang quota' means to aggressively work to hit the sales target.
usage_notes: Object-focus infinitive/command form. Implies a strong, forceful action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binalaan siya na huwag **hatawin** ang aso.","translation":"He was warned not to **hit** the dog."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **hatawin** ang deadline para sa proyektong ito.","translation":"We need to **hit** (aggressively work towards) the deadline for this project."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malalim na damdamin o kaisipan na tila 'hinugot' o kinuha mula sa personal na karanasan, lalo na sa pag-ibig o kabiguan.
etymology: Metaphorical extension of 'hugot' (to pull out), as in 'pulling out' deep emotions.
original_explanation: That relatable, often heart-wrenching, line you blurt out that's 'drawn from' your painful past experiences. "Sana all" is a baby hugot. "Buti pa ang sahod, may increase. Ang feelings niya sa'yo, wala." is a full-blown, professional-grade hugot. It's the national sport of the brokenhearted.
usage_notes: A very popular cultural and slang term since the mid-2010s. Used to describe quotes, movies, songs, or any statement laden with emotional weight.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puro **hugot** ang mga pino-post niya sa Facebook; siguro brokenhearted.","translation":"Everything she posts on Facebook is full of **deep emotional sentiment**; she must be brokenhearted."},{"sentence":"Galing sa malalim na **hugot** ang isinulat niyang tula.","translation":"The poem he wrote came from a **deep emotional place**."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa balarila, ito ang bahagi ng pangungusap na nagbibigay ng impormasyon, kilos, o paglalarawan tungkol sa simuno o paksa.
etymology: Mula sa "pan-" (prefix for instrument/concept) + "uri" (kind, type, description).
original_explanation: Kung ang 'simuno' (subject) ay ang bida ng pangungusap, ang panaguri ang chismis tungkol sa kanya. Ito 'yung sumasagot sa tanong na "O, anong ganap sa bida?" Halimbawa: "Si crush [ay gwapo]." 'Yung 'ay gwapo' ang panaguri. Sa Tagalog, madalas nauuna 'tong chismis bago 'yung bida: "[Gwapo] si crush."
usage_notes: Isang pangunahing konsepto sa gramatikang Filipino. Sa karaniwang ayos ng pangungusap sa Filipino, nauuna ang panaguri sa simuno.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa pangungusap na \"Ang bata ay naglalaro,\" ang pariralang \"ay naglalaro\" ang **panaguri**.","translation":"In the sentence \"The child is playing,\" the phrase \"is playing\" is the **predicate**."}]

translation: what is being said; the point
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kasalukuyang ipinapahayag, mensahe, o punto ng isang tao.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "sabi" (to say), na may gitlaping "-in-".
original_explanation: This is the more neutral cousin of "ang pinagsasabi". It literally means "what is being said." If your boss is explaining a new project, you can turn to your confused colleague and ask, "Naiintindihan mo ba ang sinasabi niya?" (Do you understand what he's saying?). It's about the content, the message, the point being made.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin sa neutral na paraan upang tumukoy sa pahayag o argumento ng isang tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Makinig ka nang mabuti sa **kung ano ang sinasabi** ng guro.","translation":"Listen carefully to **what the teacher is saying**."},{"sentence":"**Ang sinasabi** ko lang, mas praktikal kung magbabaon tayo ng pagkain.","translation":"**What I'm saying** is, it's more practical if we pack our own food."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagkakamali, depekto, o pagkabigo sa paggana o pag-andar ng isang bagay, sistema, o plano.
original_explanation: Yan yung nangyayari sa internet connection mo 'pag may deadline ka. Biglang "palya". O kaya sa ATM machine 'pag petsa de peligro. It's the universe's way of saying "Not today, beshie." From the Spanish word 'fallar' (to fail), which is exactly how you feel when your plans go palya.
usage_notes: Commonly used for machines, systems, or plans that don't work as intended. The adjective form is 'palyado'. 'Palyadong linya' (faulty line) is a common phrase for bad phone or internet connections.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng **palya** ang makina kaya natigil ang produksyon.","translation":"The machine had a **malfunction**, so production stopped."},{"sentence":"Sorry, **palya** ang plano nating mag-beach, umuulan.","translation":"Sorry, our plan to go to the beach is a **failure**; it's raining."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi nabibilang o hindi angkop sa isang partikular na lugar, sitwasyon, o grupo.
etymology: Mula sa "wala" (none) + "-ng" (linker) + "lugal" (isang luma o patulang anyo ng "lugar").
original_explanation: This is that feeling when you're the only one in T-shirt and jeans at a formal wedding. Awkward. Or when you try to join a conversation about a TV series you've never watched. You feel walang-lugal, like an extra piece in a puzzle that's already been solved. It's the social anxiety of not belonging.
usage_notes: Ang "lugal" ay medyo luma o pampanitikang termino para sa "lugar." Ang pariralang "wala sa lugar" ay mas karaniwang ginagamit sa kasalukuyan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang birong bastos ay **walang-lugal** sa isang pormal na pagtitipon.","translation":"His rude joke was **out of place** at a formal gathering."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman niyang siya'y **walang-lugal** sa piling ng mayayamang kamag-aral.","translation":"She felt she was **out of place** among her rich classmates."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang harang na binubuo ng mga haligi at isang pang-itaas na gabay, na nagsisilbing proteksyon at suporta sa gilid ng hagdanan, balkonahe, o terasa.
original_explanation: The fancier cousin of 'barandal'. This is the term you'd use for the ornate railings in old churches in Vigan or the grand staircase of a rich tita's house. It's there to stop you from falling and to look good while doing it.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga lumang bahay sa Vigan ay may magagandang **barandilya** na yari sa kahoy.","translation":"The old houses in Vigan have beautiful **balustrades** made of wood."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa anumang uri ng pagkain na niluto sa pamamagitan ng paglulubog o paggisa sa mainit na mantika, at nasa anyong maramihan.
original_explanation: The plural form of your favorite sin. Whether it's fried chicken, fried tilapia, or fried isaw, if there's more than one, it's 'piniritos'. The official food group of every handaan and the reason your air fryer is getting a workout.
usage_notes: The singular form is "pinirito". "Piniritos" is used when referring to multiple fried items.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang daming **piniritos** na manok sa handaan!","translation":"There are so many **fried** chickens at the feast!"},{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng iba't ibang **piniritos** sa turo-turo.","translation":"I bought various **fried** items at the eatery."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagiging malupit, marahas, o walang-awa sa kapwa tao o hayop.
etymology: From pag- + the first syllable of mag- (ma-) + mag- + lupit (cruel).
original_explanation: This is the kontrabida's main job description in any Filipino teleserye. It's the act of being unnecessarily cruel, from a boss who shouts at employees for no reason to someone who harms stray animals. Pagmamalupit is cruelty in action, the opposite of compassion. It's the reason why characters like Valentina or Clara del Valle are so hated.
usage_notes: A strong word describing severe and intentional cruelty.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagmamalupit** sa mga hayop ay isang krimen.","translation":"**Cruelty** to animals is a crime."},{"sentence":"Hindi na niya matagalan ang **pagmamalupit** ng kanyang amo.","translation":"She could no longer endure the **maltreatment** from her boss."}]

translation: to offer, to dedicate, to sacrifice
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay o paghahandog ng isang bagay, serbisyo, o sarili para sa isang partikular na tao, layunin, o paniniwala.
original_explanation: Parang yung kanta ni Florante, "Handog." Or when you work overtime during Valentine's Day para sa pamilya mo, you're offering your time. "Iniaalay ko ang tagumpay na ito sa aking mga magulang." Classic valedictorian speech move.
usage_notes: Often used in formal, poetic, or religious contexts. It carries a deeper, more solemn meaning than 'ibigay' (to give).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais kong **ialay** ang awiting ito para sa iyo.","translation":"I want to **dedicate** this song to you."},{"sentence":"Handa siyang **ialay** ang kanyang buhay para sa bayan.","translation":"He is ready to **offer** his life for the country."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kasuotan para sa pang-itaas na bahagi ng katawan, karaniwang may mahabang manggas at siper o butones, na isinusuot sa ibabaw ng ibang damit.
original_explanation: The official uniform of BPO agents and anyone working in a freezing office. Also your best friend on a Baguio trip or inside a movie theater. In the Philippines, you wear a *dyaket* not just for the cold, but to protect yourself from the scorching sun. It's a multi-purpose tool.
usage_notes: Ang pagbaybay na 'jacket' ay malawakang ginagamit at tinatanggap din.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang magdala ng **dyaket** dahil malamig sa opisina.","translation":"Don't forget to bring a **jacket** because it's cold in the office."},{"sentence":"Bagay sa iyo ang suot mong maong na **dyaket**.","translation":"That denim **jacket** you're wearing suits you."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kalagayan ng pagiging magkakasalungat, magkakabuhol, o hindi maayos na pagkakalagay ng mga bagay. Pwede ring tumukoy sa sabay-sabay at magulong pagsasalita.
original_explanation: This is the state of your earphones inside your pocket. It's also the traffic in EDSA on a payday Friday. Or that one Zoom meeting where everyone is talking over each other. Pure, unadulterated chaos.
usage_notes: Can describe physical objects being tangled or conversations being disorderly. When used for speech, it implies interrupting one another.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sabat-sabat** ang mga kable ng kuryente sa poste.","translation":"The electrical wires on the post are **intertwined**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kayong magsalita nang **sabat-sabat** para magkaintindihan tayo.","translation":"Don't speak all at once, **interrupting** each other, so we can understand one another."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasama-sama o pag-iipon ng mga bagay sa isang bunton o salansan.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your laundry when you're too lazy to fold it. It’s also what you do with sand at the beach to build a sandcastle, or what a vendor does with mangoes at the 'palengke' to make them look appealing. 'Magtumpok ka ng mga tuyong dahon diyan sa sulok.' It’s organized chaos... or sometimes, just chaos.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magtumpok** ng mga bato sa gilid ng ilog.","translation":"You need to **pile up** the stones on the riverbank."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng party, nag-umpisa silang **magtumpok** ng mga basura.","translation":"After the party, they started to **pile up** the trash."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng mga palamuti o dekorasyon sa isang lugar o bagay upang ito ay gumanda.
original_explanation: The "let's make this place pretty" verb. Ito yung command na maririnig mo bago mag-Pasko, birthday, o anumang party. "Dekorasyunan mo na yung sala!" means "It's time to unleash your inner interior designer." Ito ang action word para sa pagkakabit ng banderitas, pag-aayos ng bulaklak, at pagsasabit ng parol.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais kong **dekorasyunan** ang aking kwarto ng mga poster ng paborito kong banda.","translation":"I want **to decorate** my room with posters of my favorite band."},{"sentence":"Sila ang naatasang **dekorasyunan** ang entablado para sa programa.","translation":"They were assigned **to decorate** the stage for the program."}]

translation: to reform; to make someone sensible
meaning_filipino: Pagsikapang ibalik sa tamang pag-iisip, landas, o asal ang isang tao.
etymology: From pa- (causative prefix) + tino (sensibleness, good judgment) + -in (object-focus suffix).
original_explanation: This is what your parents, a good friend, or a therapist tries to do when you're being 'pasaway' or making bad life choices. It's the verbal equivalent of a gentle (or not-so-gentle) slap to bring you back to your senses. "Hay nako, kailangan na talagang **patinuin** ang batang 'yan!"
usage_notes: Can refer to correcting behavior, illogical thinking, or morals. Carries a corrective, sometimes disciplinary, tone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng guro na **patinuin** ang magulong mag-aaral.","translation":"The teacher tried to **reform** the unruly student."}]

meaning_filipino: Eksklusibo o dinisenyo para sa mag-asawa.
original_explanation: This describes things specifically for two people who are 'kasal' (married). It could be a 'pangmag-asawa' bed (queen or king size), a 'pangmag-asawa' vacation package (hello, honeymoon!), or even 'pangmag-asawa' na away (a couple's quarrel) that you should definitely not get in the middle of. It's the level-up from 'pang-jowa'.
usage_notes: Used to describe items, plans, or situations intended for a married pair.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroon silang **pangmag-asawa** na life insurance plan.","translation":"They have a life insurance plan **for a married couple**."},{"sentence":"Ang seminar na ito ay **pangmag-asawa** lamang.","translation":"This seminar is only **for married couples**."}]

translation: to be presented; to be featured; to be proclaimed
meaning_filipino: Ang mailagay sa isang pampublikong pagtatanghal; maipakita o kilalanin sa harap ng madla.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'ma-' at salitang ugat na 'tanghal' (show, exhibit).
original_explanation: Your moment to shine! It's when you're chosen to be the 'bida' (star), whether it's being crowned Miss Universe, getting your work featured in a gallery, or finally being declared the winner of the barangay karaoke contest. It’s your main character energy moment.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng mga parangal, kompetisyon, at pagtatanghal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino kaya ang **matatanghal** na kampeon sa paligsahan?","translation":"Who will **be proclaimed** champion in the competition?"}]

translation: Is that a skin care thing?
meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na tanong o parirala na ginagamit upang kumpirmahin kung ang isang partikular na produkto, sangkap, o konsepto ay may kaugnayan sa pag-aalaga sa balat (skin care).
etymology: Isang pariralang nabuo sa social media, na pinagsasama ang Ingles na "skin care" at ang slang na "yarn" (isang baryasyon ng "iyan" na popular sa beki lingo).
original_explanation: The ultimate question of the Tita-in-training or anyone deep in the K-beauty rabbit hole. It's a phrase born from Filipino meme culture. You see a weird ingredient like 'snail mucin' or 'galactomyces'? You ask, "Skin care yarn?" to the group chat. It's a funny, slightly sarcastic way of saying, "Is this another one of those complicated things I need to put on my face to achieve 'glass skin'?" 'Yarn?' is the witty, beki-fied version of 'iyan ba?' (is that it?).
usage_notes: Lubhang impormal at ginagamit sa mga online na komunidad, lalo na sa mga usapang may kinalaman sa beauty at lifestyle. Ang "yarn" ay isang popular na slang na idinurugtong sa mga tanong.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sabi nila maganda daw ang rice water sa buhok. Ay, teka, pang-**skin care yarn**?","translation":"They say rice water is good for the hair. Oh, wait, is that a **skin care thing**?"},{"sentence":"Nakita ko may bagong serum na may 'propolis'. **Skin care yarn**?","translation":"I saw a new serum with 'propolis'. **Is that a skin care thing**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Nakasingit o nakalagay sa pagitan ng baywang at damit, karaniwan ay isang bagay na patulis o sandata.
original_explanation: Think of it as the old-school Filipino way of 'concealed carry'. It's when you tuck something, usually a weapon like a bolo or a gun, into your waistband. Today, it’s more likely your phone or wallet when you have no pockets. "Naka-sukbit sa baywang" is the classic image of a Filipino action hero or a local tanod.
usage_notes: Often used in its affixed form "nakasukbit" (is tucked in).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **sukbit** siyang itak sa kanyang baywang habang nagtatrabaho sa bukid.","translation":"He had a bolo **tucked into** his waistband while working in the field."},{"sentence":"Laging nakikita ang pulis na may baril na **sukbit** sa gilid.","translation":"The police officer was always seen with a gun **tucked in** at his side."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahaging nasa hulihan ng isang bagay, lugar, o tao.
original_explanation: The place where you find the 'good seats' in the cinema if you're tall. Also, the area of the classroom where all the magic (and sleeping) happens. 'Pakipasa po sa likuran.' - every student during an exam.
usage_notes: Often used to refer to a location, as in 'sa likuran' (at the back).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umupo ka sa **likuran** para mas malinaw mong makita ang entablado.","translation":"Sit at the **back** so you can see the stage more clearly."},{"sentence":"May pinto sa **likuran** ng gusali.","translation":"There is a door at the **rear** of the building."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang pagsasabi o paggawa ng isang bagay na nakakabastos o nakakababa ng dangal ng ibang tao.
original_explanation: What happens when "constructive criticism" loses the "constructive" part and just becomes plain rude. It's the verbal version of a slap. What keyboard warriors do for fun and what you should never do to your boss, at least not to their face.
usage_notes: "Mang-insulto" is also a very common and often preferred form of this verb, especially when indicating the actor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi magandang ugali ang **uminsulto** ng kapwa.","translation":"It is not a good habit to **insult** others."},{"sentence":"**Uminsulto** ba siya sa iyo kaya ka nagagalit?","translation":"Did he **insult** you, is that why you're angry?"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na nilikha o ginawa sa pamamagitan ng proseso ng paggagantsilyo, gamit ang isang sinulid at isang kawit.
original_explanation: That intricate, lacy stuff your lola makes. Coasters, doilies, tablecloths, even baby clothes. If it looks like it was made with one hook and a lot of patience, it's ginantsilyo. The ultimate 'handmade with love' aesthetic.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun (the crocheted item) or an adjective (describing something as crocheted).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mantel sa mesa ay **ginantsilyo** ng aking lola.","translation":"The tablecloth on the table was **crocheted** by my grandmother."},{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng isang pares ng **ginantsilyo** na hikaw.","translation":"I bought a pair of **crocheted** earrings."}]

translation: can be matched; can be equated
meaning_filipino: May kakayahang ipantay, ipareha, o ihalaga katulad ng iba.
etymology: From `ma-` (potential prefix) + `itumbas` (to match/equate). The root is `tumbas` (equivalent, match).
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'hugot' word. 'Walang halaga ang maitutumbas sa pagmamahal ng isang ina.' (There's no value that can be equated to a mother's love). It's trying to find an equal match or value for something, whether it's love, effort, or the price of a fancy coffee. It's the 'Is it worth it?' question, but for your soul.
usage_notes: Often used when comparing abstract concepts like love, sacrifice, or value, frequently in a negative construction (e.g., 'hindi maitumbasan' - cannot be matched).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Walang salapi ang **maitutumbas** sa mga sakripisyo ng ating mga magulang.","translation":"No amount of money **can be equated** to the sacrifices of our parents."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **maitumbas** ang kalidad ng produktong ito sa presyo nito.","translation":"It's difficult **to match** the quality of this product with its price."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pakikipag-usap upang mapababa ang presyo ng isang produkto o serbisyo.
original_explanation: The national sport of the Philippines, especially in palengkes and Greenhills. It's the art of asking 'May tawad pa ba?' (Is there a discount?) and trying to get the best price. A true master of pagtawad can walk away with a 50% discount and the seller's life story. It's a dance, a negotiation, a lifestyle.
usage_notes: The verb form is 'tumawad' (to haggle). The question is 'Pwedeng tumawad?' (Can I haggle?).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magaling sa **pagtawad** ang nanay ko kaya nakakamura kami sa palengke.","translation":"My mom is good at **bargaining**, that's why we get discounts at the market."},{"sentence":"Walang **pagtawad** sa mga department store.","translation":"There's no **haggling** in department stores."}]

translation: to tie hair into a bun
meaning_filipino: Ayusin ang buhok sa pamamagitan ng pag-ipon at pagtali nito sa isang bilog na buhol, karaniwan sa likod o tuktok ng ulo.
original_explanation: The default "get things done" mode for anyone with long hair. Mainit? Ipusod mo. Maglilinis ng bahay? Ipusod. Mag-aaral for finals? Ipusod. It's the official hairstyle of "ayoko munang ma-distract."
usage_notes: The object being put into a bun (the hair) is the focus of the verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **ipusod** mo ang buhok ko, ang init kasi.","translation":"Please, **tie my hair into a bun**, it's so hot."},{"sentence":"Maayos niyang **inipusod** ang kanyang mahabang buhok bago magsimula sa trabaho.","translation":"She neatly **tied her long hair into a bun** before starting work."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na nangangahulugang ayos lang, tama, o sang-ayon.
original_explanation: A very 90s/early 2000s slang for 'okay'. It's the cool, laid-back way of agreeing to something. If someone says 'tsoke lang,' it means everything's cool, no drama. It's the 'G!' of its time.
usage_notes: Considered dated slang but still understood by many.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tsoke** lang sa akin kung doon tayo magkita.","translation":"It's **alright** with me if we meet there."},{"sentence":"Basta may pagkain, **tsoke** na ako!","translation":"As long as there's food, I'm **okay**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taunang pagdiriwang tuwing ika-14 ng Pebrero upang ipagdiwang ang pag-ibig at pagmamahal sa pagitan ng mga magkasintahan, kaibigan, at pamilya.
etymology: From English 'Valentine's Day', named after Saint Valentine.
original_explanation: Araw ng mga Puso! Or as single people call it, "Single Awareness Day". Panahon kung saan biglang nagmamahalan ang presyo ng bulaklak at tsokolate. Kung may jowa ka, date night. Kung wala, either food trip with friends or movie marathon mag-isa with a gallon of ice cream. No judgment.
usage_notes: Commonly refers to Valentine's Day. Can also refer to the valentine card or gift itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Saan ang date ninyo sa darating na **Valentines**?","translation":"Where is your date this coming **Valentine's Day**?"},{"sentence":"Mahal ang mga bulaklak kapag malapit na ang **Valentines**.","translation":"Flowers are expensive when **Valentine's Day** is near."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan nagsasalubong o naghihiwalay ang dalawa o higit pang daan. Ginagamit din ito sa matalinghagang paraan upang ilarawan ang isang punto ng pagpapasya sa buhay.
etymology: From 'sanga' (branch) + 'daan' (road) + '-an' (location suffix). Literally 'a place where the road branches.'
original_explanation: The literal meaning is a street intersection, like EDSA corner Buendia. But the *hugot* meaning is where it gets real. A *sangandaan* is that point in your life where you have to make a big decision. Career or love life? Jollibee or McDo? Stay in the Philippines or move abroad? You're standing at a crossroads, and whichever path you take will change everything. It's the setting for every major life crisis and every teleserye turning point.
usage_notes: Very common in both literal and figurative senses.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkita tayo sa **sangandaan** malapit sa simbahan.","translation":"Let's meet at the **intersection** near the church."},{"sentence":"Nasa **sangandaan** ngayon ang kanyang buhay, hindi niya alam kung anong landas ang pipiliin.","translation":"His life is at a **crossroads** right now; he doesn't know which path to choose."}]

translation: to be able to dance with
meaning_filipino: Ang magkaroon ng pagkakataong maisayaw o sumayaw kasama ang isang tao.
original_explanation: The ultimate goal during a school dance, a JS prom, or a debut. It's that moment of truth when you ask your crush, 'Pwedeng makisayaw?' If they say yes, you get to 'makasayaw' them. It's a compound of 'maka-' (to be able to) and 'sayaw' (dance).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakasaya ko nang **makasayaw** ko ang aking hinahangaan sa party.","translation":"I was so happy when I was **able to dance with** my crush at the party."},{"sentence":"Sana **makasayaw** kita sa susunod nating pagkikita.","translation":"I hope I can **dance with** you the next time we meet."}]

translation: to take pity on, to feel sorry for
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita o pagdama ng awa o habag para sa isang tao.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of 'kawawa.' It's what you do when you see that pitiful sight. You see the basang sisiw sa ulan and you kawawaan them, so you take them in. It's the action of feeling pity. 'Kinawawaan ko siya' is like saying 'My heart went out to them.'
usage_notes: Isang pandiwa na nangangahulugang maging obheto ng awa ng isang tao. Madalas gamitin sa mga banghay nito tulad ng 'kinawawaan' (was pitied) o 'kinakawawaan' (is being pitied).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kinawawaan** ng lahat ang pamilyang nasunugan.","translation":"Everyone **took pity on** the family whose house burned down."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **kawawaan**; kaya ko ito.","translation":"Don't **feel sorry for** me; I can handle this."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapakita ng karangyaan, kayamanan, o anumang ipinagmamalaki sa isang magarbo at labis na paraan.
etymology: From pag- (gerund prefix) + pa- (causative prefix) + parangya (from pa- + dangya, 'luxury/ostentation'). Literally 'the act of causing ostentation'.
original_explanation: This is the 'flex culture' before it was even called 'flex culture.' It's posting your new iPhone, your Starbucks cup with your name misspelled, or your plane ticket to Boracay. It's the art of showing off what you have, sometimes to the point of being annoying. Think of it as the opposite of 'lowkey.' #SanaAll is the usual response.
usage_notes: Often has a slightly negative connotation of being boastful.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya hilig ang **pagpaparangya** ng kanyang mga mamahaling gamit.","translation":"She is not fond of **flaunting** her expensive things."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang social media ay puno ng **pagpaparangya** ng kanyang mga biyahe.","translation":"His social media is full of **ostentation** from his travels."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pampublikong sasakyan na tumatakbo sa riles na nakabaon sa kalsada.
original_explanation: The vintage version of the LRT/MRT. Imagine a jeepney that runs on tracks in the middle of the road. You might see this in old pictures of Manila, especially in Escolta. It's the lolo of our modern train systems, probably complaining about how much better traffic was "back in my day."
usage_notes: Halos hindi na ginagamit sa modernong Pilipinas, maliban sa mga kontekstong pangkasaysayan. Ang salitang "trambia" ay mas karaniwan sa mga lumang teksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Noong unang panahon, may mga **tram** na bumibiyahe sa mga pangunahing kalsada ng Maynila.","translation":"In the old days, there were **trams** that traveled on the main roads of Manila."}]

translation: act of moving to the side
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpunta o paggalaw patungo sa gilid; pagtabi.
original_explanation: The move you make in a crowded MRT train when you hear "Excuse me, paraan po, bababa na." It's the subtle art of making yourself smaller so others can pass. Or what you do when you see your chismosa tita approaching at a family reunion.
usage_notes: More commonly encountered as the verb 'pumagilid'. The noun form 'pagilid' is less frequent but understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagilid** ay hudyat na ayaw niyang masali sa usapan.","translation":"His **act of moving to the side** was a signal that he didn't want to be part of the conversation."}]

translation: to dance with someone; to join in dancing
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-anyaya o pagsama sa isang tao o grupo sa pagsasayaw.
original_explanation: The classic 'May I have this dance?' moment, but in verb form. Or when the DJ plays a banger and you pull your friend onto the dance floor, you're asking them to makisayaw. It's the social act of joining someone in the sacred ritual of awkward or amazing dancing at a party.
usage_notes: 'Makisayaw' is to join someone who is already dancing or to ask someone to dance with you. 'Sumayaw' is just to dance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahihiya akong **makisayaw** dahil hindi ako marunong.","translation":"I'm shy **to join in the dancing** because I don't know how."},{"sentence":"Puwede bang **makisayaw** sa iyo, Binibini?","translation":"May I **dance with** you, Miss?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangkalahatang publiko o ang mga mamamayan ng isang bansa o komunidad.
original_explanation: This is 'The People,' the ones politicians are always promising to serve. It’s everyone from the fishball vendor to the CEO. When you hear 'serbisyo sa taong-bayan,' it means service for all of us, the taxpayers, the voters, the Mariteses—the general population.
usage_notes: Often used in political, legal, and formal contexts. Carries a sense of collective identity and civic importance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga opisyal ng gobyerno ay dapat maglingkod sa **taong-bayan**.","translation":"Government officials should serve **the people**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-nguso o pagsimangot bilang tanda ng pagtatampo, pagkainis, o pagtutol.
original_explanation: The default face of a jowa who's 'tampororot'. It's the silent treatment in facial form. 'Ano na namang problema? Huwag mo akong mino-mule-han dyan!' It's less intense than a full-blown galit, but more annoying because you have to guess what you did wrong.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang tiyak na uri ng ekspresyon ng mukha na kinabibilangan ng pag-usli ng mga labi.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang mahabang **mule** ang isinagot niya nang hindi siya pinayagang lumabas.","translation":"A long **pout** was her reply when she wasn't allowed to go out."},{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na ang pag-**mule** at sabihin mo kung ano ang gusto mo.","translation":"Stop **pouting** and just say what you want."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mabilis, matalino, at karaniwang mapanuyang sagot sa isang kritisismo o pang-iinsulto.
etymology: From English 'clapback'. A modern term popularized by social media.
original_explanation: Not just a reply, it's a comeback with receipts. It's the art of responding to a hater or basher with so much wit and fire that they need to apply aloe vera on their soul. The national sport on Twitter and Facebook comment sections.
usage_notes: While an English word, it's used extensively in Taglish conversations, especially online, to refer to a witty retort. The verb form is 'mag-clapback' or 'i-clapback'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tindi ng **clapback** ni Marian sa basher niya!","translation":"Marian's **clapback** to her basher was intense!"},{"sentence":"Hintayin mo ang **clapback** ko, humanda ka.","translation":"Just wait for my **clapback**, you better be ready."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang napakahinang tunog o salita na halos hindi marinig; bulong.
original_explanation: That faint sound you hear at 3 AM that makes you pull your blanket over your head. Or the 'psst' from your seatmate during an exam asking for an answer. It's a sound meant to be secret or subtle, but often ends up being the source of ghost stories or chismis.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa panitikan. Maaari ring tumukoy sa isang napakahinang ingay, tulad ng "anas ng hangin."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May narinig siyang **anas** mula sa madilim na sulok ng kwarto.","translation":"He heard a **whisper** from the dark corner of the room."},{"sentence":"Ang tanging maririnig ay ang **anas** ng mga dahon.","translation":"The only thing that could be heard was the **murmur** of the leaves."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang anak ng ninong o ninang ng isang tao, itinuturing na parang kapatid dahil sa ugnayan sa binyag, kumpil, o kasal.
etymology: From 'kapatid' (sibling), with the 'kinaka-' affix, which implies a relationship by ritual or association, not by blood.
original_explanation: Your 'kapatid sa binyag.' They're not your blood sibling, but you're connected by the holy water of a baptismal font and the generosity of your parents' chosen friends (your godparents). It's that person you see during Christmas to get your aguinaldo from their parents, and you call them 'kuya/ate' out of respect.
usage_notes: This is a gender-neutral term. The gender is specified by adding 'na lalaki' (male) or 'na babae' (female). For example, 'kinakapatid na lalaki' (god-brother) and 'kinakapatid na babae' (god-sister).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Marco ang aking **kinakapatid na lalaki** dahil ninong ko ang tatay niya.","translation":"Marco is my **god-brother** because his father is my godfather."},{"sentence":"Inimbitahan ko ang aking mga **kinakapatid** sa aking kaarawan.","translation":"I invited my **god-siblings** to my birthday."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkatalo o pagkasakop sa isang labanan, kompetisyon, o alitan.
original_explanation: This is the feeling after a brutal final exam, or when your favorite team loses the championship. You've been conquered, defeated, totally owned. It's the 'GG, no re' moment of life.
usage_notes: Used to denote defeat, not just in war, but in any contest of power or will.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkalupig** ng kanilang hukbo ay naging hudyat ng bagong pamumuno.","translation":"The **defeat** of their army signaled the start of a new leadership."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang may negatibong konotasyon na tumutukoy sa isang babae na itinuturing na malandi, magaslaw kumilos, o imoral.
original_explanation: An old-school, very harsh word for a woman who is considered overly flirtatious or promiscuous. It's the kind of word a kontrabida in a teleserye would hiss at the bida. Not a nice word to use; it's basically the vintage version of "malandi" or "pokpok."
usage_notes: A derogatory and offensive term for a woman, often used as a noun as well. Its use is highly discouraged in polite conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinawag siyang **hitad** ng mga tsismosa sa kanilang baryo.","translation":"The gossips in their village called her a **flirt**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala sa mga paratang na siya ay isang babaeng **hitad**.","translation":"Don't believe the accusations that she is a **promiscuous** woman."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang pagwawakas o pagkitil sa sariling buhay.
etymology: Possibly from pati- (self-inflicted) + wakal (an archaic word meaning 'to untie' or 'to undo'), literally 'to undo oneself'.
original_explanation: This is a heavy one. It's the act of ending one's own life. It's a word we use with seriousness and sadness, often followed by discussions about mental health, depression, and the importance of reaching out. It's the 'final straw' hugot, but in the most tragic, irreversible way. If you hear this word in a real conversation, it's time to stop joking and start listening.
usage_notes: A very serious term. The verb form is 'magpatiwakal' (to commit suicide). Use with sensitivity. 'Pagpapakamatay' is a more common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-uusap tungkol sa **patiwakal** ay mahalaga upang mapataas ang kamalayan sa kalusugang pangkaisipan.","translation":"Discussing **suicide** is important to raise awareness about mental health."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagtatakda o paghihiwalay ng isang tiyak na halaga ng salapi para sa isang partikular na layunin o gastusin.
original_explanation: This is adulting level 99. Yung moment na sinusuweldo ka tapos kailangan mo nang hati-hatiin: pambayad sa Meralco, sa Wi-Fi, sa Netflix, sa Shopee, at kung may matira, pangkain. It's basically telling your money where to go instead of wondering where it went. Corporate-speak for 'pagba-budget.'
usage_notes: A formal term used in finance, government, and business. The everyday equivalent is "pagba-budget".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang debate sa Kongreso tungkol sa **paglalaan ng gugulin** para sa edukasyon.","translation":"The debate in Congress is intense regarding the **budget allocation** for education."},{"sentence":"Ang tamang **paglalaan ng gugulin** ay susi sa tagumpay ng isang proyekto.","translation":"Proper **appropriation** is key to a project's success."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamataas, pinakamatindi, o pinakamahalagang punto ng isang pangyayari, kuwento, o karanasan.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'eto na!' moment. In a teleserye, this is the part where the real mother is revealed, the villain gets their comeuppance, or the main characters finally kiss in the rain. Sa trabaho, ito yung peak season na halos 'di ka na umuuwi. Sa 'hugot', ito yung point na napuno ka na at sumabog ka na. The peak of it all.
usage_notes: A literary term often used in analyzing stories, but also applicable to any situation that reaches a peak intensity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-amin ng pangunahing tauhan ay ang **kasukdulan** ng kuwento.","translation":"The main character's confession is the **climax** of the story."},{"sentence":"Nasa **kasukdulan** na ang kanyang galit kaya't sumigaw na siya.","translation":"Her anger had reached its **peak**, which is why she shouted."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, kaganapan, o tao na hindi naging matagumpay; isang kabiguan.
original_explanation: Your 'great' idea that nobody liked. The concert that sold 10 tickets. The 'kilig' movie that made people cringe instead. Your love life. Basically, anything that epically failed to meet expectations. It's the sound your confidence makes when it hits the floor.
usage_notes: Used to describe anything from a movie, a project, a party, or even a person's attempt at something. Can function as a noun ('The movie was a flop') or an adjective ('The movie was flop').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **flop** ang concert dahil sa biglaang pag-ulan.","translation":"The concert became a **flop** because of the sudden rain."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala kung **flop** ang unang attempt mo, subok lang ulit.","translation":"Don't worry if your first attempt is a **failure**, just try again."}]

translation: to sue; to file a case; to accuse formally
meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na paghahain ng reklamo o kaso laban sa isang tao o entidad sa hukuman.
original_explanation: When the 'sumbungan' at the barangay hall doesn't cut it anymore and you decide to lawyer up. This is the legal version of 'I'm telling my mom!' but with courtrooms and a lot more paperwork.
usage_notes: A formal legal term. The actor is the one initiating the lawsuit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **magsakdal** laban sa kumpanya dahil sa hindi makatarungang pagtanggal sa trabaho.","translation":"He decided to **file a case** against the company for unjust termination."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang parusang habambuhay na pagkakakulong.
etymology: From Spanish 'perpetua' as in 'reclusión perpetua' (perpetual confinement).
original_explanation: The ultimate 'you messed up big time' consequence. This isn't just being grounded; it's being sent to the 'principal's office' of life, forever. It's the legal term you hear on the news for heinous crimes. Basically, it means your next address is Bilibid, and your new roommate is... well, let's not go there.
usage_notes: A formal, legal term. Often used in the phrase 'reclusion perpetua.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinatulan siya ng **perpetuwa** dahil sa malagim na krimen.","translation":"He was sentenced to **life imprisonment** for the heinous crime."},{"sentence":"Ang parusang reclusion **perpetua** ay ang pinakamabigat na sentensya sa bansa.","translation":"The penalty of reclusion **perpetua** is the heaviest sentence in the country."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sarkastikong ekspresyon na ginagamit upang tukuyin ang isang tao na gumagamit o nananamantala ng iba, madalas sa isang pabirong paraan.
etymology: Combination of English 'user' and Filipino gay lingo 'yarn' (from 'iyan').
original_explanation: The ultimate call-out for moochers and opportunists, delivered with Spongebob-meme energy. It's what you say when your friend only messages you when they need something ('Pautang naman, besh.' -> 'User yarn?'). It combines the English word 'user' (someone who uses others) with the gay lingo 'yarn' (a softener for 'iyan'). It's a playful but pointed accusation.
usage_notes: Purely conversational and part of modern Filipino internet/gay lingo. The 'yarn' adds a playful, non-confrontational but still shady tone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagi na lang siyang nagpapalibre, **user yarn**?","translation":"He always asks to be treated, is he a **user or what**?"},{"sentence":"Friend mo lang ako 'pag may kailangan ka? Ang **user yarn**!","translation":"I'm only your friend when you need something? Such a **user**!"}]

translation: to signal; to give a sign
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng isang senyas o palatandaan, sa pamamagitan ng kilos, tunog, o salita, upang magpahiwatig ng isang bagay o simulan ang isang gawain.
original_explanation: The 'go-na-friend' action. It's the subtle nod you give your bestie at a party when you want to leave. It's the bell that signals the start of your lunch break or, tragically, the end of it. In traffic, it's the jeepney driver's hand gesture that means 'sige, una ka na, pre.'
usage_notes: Can be used for any kind of signal, from a subtle gesture to a loud alarm.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Maghudyat** ka kapag handa ka nang umalis.","translation":"**Signal** me when you're ready to leave."},{"sentence":"Ang pagputok ng baril ang **naghudyat** sa simula ng karera.","translation":"The firing of the gun **signaled** the start of the race."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mag-anyaya o mag-imbita sa isang tao na dumalo sa isang pagtitipon, kaganapan, o okasyon.
original_explanation: The act of gathering your 'barkada' for a birthday party, inuman, or a simple 'kain tayo'. In Filipino culture, 'mangumbida' is often followed by the polite but usually rejected 'Huwag ka na mag-regalo, presence mo lang sapat na!' (Don't bring a gift, your presence is enough!).
usage_notes: Synonymous with 'mag-anyaya' or 'mag-imbita'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sila ang naatasang **mangumbida** ng mga panauhing pandangal para sa pagtatapos.","translation":"They were tasked to **invite** the guests of honor for the graduation."},{"sentence":"Balak kong **mangumbida** ng ilang kaibigan para sa isang salu-salo sa bahay.","translation":"I plan to **invite** a few friends for a get-together at home."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-aalay ng harana sa isang tao; ang pagbibigay ng harana sa isang tiyak na tao o lugar.
etymology: harana + -han (suffix indicating location or recipient of the action)
original_explanation: This is the verb form. It's what you *do*. 'Haranahan mo na, pare!' your friends would say, pushing you to finally sing for your crush. It's the action of putting the 'harana' plan into motion. The focus is on the person receiving the serenade.
usage_notes: This is a verb where the object is the person being serenaded. Example: 'Haranahan mo si Maria.' (Serenade Maria).
