usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagplano si Pedro na **haranahan** si Elena sa kanyang kaarawan.","translation":"Pedro planned **to serenade** Elena on her birthday."},{"sentence":"Sino ang masuwerteng babaeng **haranahan** mo ngayong gabi?","translation":"Who is the lucky girl you will **serenade** tonight?"}]

translation: to have an asthma attack; to have asthma
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon o pagdanas ng sakit na hika, na nagdudulot ng hirap sa paghinga.
original_explanation: This is literally "to have asthma." It’s the reason your tita tells you not to drink cold water when you're sweaty ("mahahapo ka, magkakahika ka!"). While medically debatable, it's a staple of Filipino household advice. The `magka-` prefix here means 'to acquire' or 'to suffer from' a condition.
usage_notes: Refers to the condition of having asthma or the event of having an asthma attack.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala siya sa ospital dahil **nagkahika** siya kagabi.","translation":"He was brought to the hospital because he **had an asthma attack** last night."},{"sentence":"Bawal sa kanya ang alikabok dahil madali siyang **magkahika**.","translation":"Dust is not allowed near him because he can easily **get an asthma attack**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matamis at malapot na likidong pagkain na gawa ng mga pukyutan (bees) mula sa nektar ng mga bulaklak.
original_explanation: The OG natural sweetener. This is what you get when bees do their magic on flower nectar. 'Pulot' means 'nectar' or 'syrup', and 'pukyutan' means 'honeybee'. So literally, "bee syrup". It's what Winnie the Pooh would risk it all for. Great for tea, pancakes, or soothing a sore throat.
usage_notes: 'Pulot' by itself can sometimes mean honey, but 'pulot-pukyutan' is the more specific and formal term to distinguish it from other syrups like 'pulot-tubo' (molasses).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas masarap ang tsaa kung lalagyan ng **pulot-pukyutan**.","translation":"Tea is more delicious if you add **honey**."},{"sentence":"Kilala ang Baguio sa kanilang masarap na **pulot-pukyutan**.","translation":"Baguio is known for their delicious **honey**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng tela o anumang katulad na produkto sa pamamagitan ng pagsasalikop ng mga pahalang at patayong sinulid.
original_explanation: This is the command form: 'Weave it!' It's what you tell someone to do with thread to make a masterpiece. Metaphorically, it's what your friend does when they need to **habihin** a believable excuse for being late to work... again.
usage_notes: This is the object-focus form of the verb 'to weave'. The actor-focus form is 'maghabi'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan siya ng mangangalakal na **habihin** ang pinakamagandang tela para sa reyna.","translation":"The merchant ordered her **to weave** the most beautiful cloth for the queen."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **habihin** ang mga kuwento ng kasinungalingan dahil madali itong masira.","translation":"It is difficult **to weave** tales of lies because they are easily broken."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sisidlan, karaniwang yari sa plastik o yantok, na ginagamit upang paglagyan ng maruruming damit o ng mga bagong laba.
original_explanation: The designated "floor" for your dirty clothes that makes you feel slightly more organized. It's a magical container that's always either completely empty or overflowing, there's no in-between. Also doubles as a makeshift basketball hoop for your socks.
usage_notes: Madalas na binabaybay bilang dalawang salita "laundry basket". Karaniwan din ang isahang salita sa impormal na pagsulat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno na ang **laundrybasket**, kailangan ko nang maglaba.","translation":"The **laundry basket** is full, I need to do the laundry."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi nagtataglay ng sapat na puwersa, kapangyarihan, o sigla, pisikal man o sa ibang aspeto.
original_explanation: This is you on a Monday morning before your first cup of coffee. You feel walang-lakas, like a phone on 1% battery. It can also describe that feeling when you see your crush with someone else—bigla kang nanlambot at nawalan ng ganang kumain. Emotionally and physically drained, bes.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa pisikal na kahinaan, kawalan ng awtoridad, o mahinang argumento o signal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiramdam niya ay **walang-lakas** siya matapos ang matinding sakit.","translation":"He felt **weak** after a severe illness."},{"sentence":"Isang lider na **walang-lakas** ay hindi kayang pamunuan ang kanyang mga nasasakupan.","translation":"A **powerless** leader cannot lead his constituents."}]

translation: to move along the edge; to scrape along the side
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagdaan o paggalaw nang halos dumikit o sumayad sa gilid ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: It's how you move through a crowded palengke or a packed MRT train—squeezing by, with your bag scraping the wall (or someone's back). It's the physical equivalent of 'excuse me po' when there's no space to actually move.
usage_notes: Often used in its conjugated forms like 'sumisidsid' (is moving along the edge) or 'sinidsid' (moved along the edge).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumisidsid** ang bangka sa gilid ng ilog upang maiwasan ang malakas na agos.","translation":"The boat is **moving along the edge** of the river to avoid the strong current."},{"sentence":"**Sinidsid** niya ang pader habang naglalakad sa makitid na eskinita.","translation":"He **scraped along** the wall while walking through the narrow alley."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang puti o walang kulay na malambot at solidong substansiya na gawa sa petrolyo, ginagamit sa paggawa ng kandila, wax paper, at pampadulas.
original_explanation: This is the stuff your floor polisher guy uses to make the floor so shiny you can see your reflection (and your pores). It's also the main ingredient of the candles you light during a brownout or when you're trying to be romantic. Basically, it's wax.
usage_notes: Commonly used in contexts related to cleaning (floor wax), candles, or industrial lubricants.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sahig ay kumikinang dahil sa bagong pahid na **parapina**.","translation":"The floor is shiny because of the freshly applied **paraffin wax**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga kandila ay gawa sa **parapina**.","translation":"The candles are made of **paraffin**."}]

translation: to be closed on; to be shut out
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng harang o takip sa isang daanan o bukasan para sa isang tao o bagay; ang hindi pagtanggap o pagbigyan.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "talk to the hand" move, but with a door. When someone 'pagsarhan ka ng pinto', they're literally or figuratively slamming the door in your face. It's being rejected, ghosted, or denied an opportunity. It's that feeling when you're late for the mall's closing time and the guard shuts the door right as you arrive. Ouch.
usage_notes: This is a verb in the object-focus, imperative/infinitive form. It implies an action being done *to* or *for* someone/something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **pagsarhan** ng pinto habang nagsasalita pa ako!","translation":"Don't **close** the door **on me** while I'm still talking!"},{"sentence":"Tila pinag**sarhan** na siya ng lahat ng pagkakataon.","translation":"It seems all opportunities have been **closed on** him."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bagay, halaga, o konsepto na kapareho o kapantay ng isa pa.
original_explanation: It's the 'what you see is what you get' but for value. Like when you trade your Funko Pop for your friend's, you hope for a fair katumbasan. Or, it's the salary you expect for the 'passion' and 'dedication' your job description demands.
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of value, exchange, or translation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **katumbasan** sa Ingles ng salitang 'kilig'?","translation":"What is the English **equivalent** for the word 'kilig'?"},{"sentence":"Ang halaga ng kaniyang sakripisyo ay walang **katumbasan**.","translation":"The value of his sacrifice has no **equivalent**."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa teolohiyang Katoliko, ang doktrina ng pagbabago ng buong sangkap ng tinapay at alak sa tunay na katawan at dugo ni Kristo sa Eukaristiya.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "transubstanciación", mula sa Latin na "transubstantiatio".
original_explanation: The ultimate glow-up story, Catholic edition. It's when the bread and wine at mass don't just *represent* Jesus, they *become* Jesus. This is that one word from Catechism class you tried to memorize for extra points but probably forgot right after. High-level, PhD-in-Religion stuff.
usage_notes: A highly specific theological term used almost exclusively within the context of Roman Catholicism.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang turo tungkol sa **transubstansyasyon** ay isang mahalagang bahagi ng pananampalatayang Katoliko.","translation":"The teaching on **transubstantiation** is an important part of the Catholic faith."},{"sentence":"Ipinaliwanag ng pari ang konsepto ng **transubstansyasyon** sa panahon ng misa.","translation":"The priest explained the concept of **transubstantiation** during the mass."}]

translation: to make the sign of the cross
meaning_filipino: Isagawa ang kilos ng pagkurus sa sarili bilang tanda ng pananampalatayang Kristiyano.
etymology: From Tagalog 'mag-' (verb prefix) + 'antanda', a variant of 'tanda' (sign), specifically referring to the sign of the cross.
original_explanation: This is the classic Filipino Catholic gesture. You do it when you pass by a church, when the bus you're on brakes suddenly, or when you're about to take a major exam. It's a quick prayer and a sign of faith rolled into one. 'Sa ngalan ng Ama, ng Anak, at ng Espiritu Santo. Amen.'
usage_notes: A specific religious term. 'Magkurus' is a more common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinuruan ng lola ang kanyang apo kung paano **mag-antanda**.","translation":"The grandmother taught her grandchild how **to make the sign of the cross**."},{"sentence":"Nag-**antanda** siya bago pumasok sa simbahan.","translation":"He **made the sign of the cross** before entering the church."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa katangiang pisikal o mental na may kakayahang magbuhat, tumagal, o magtiis; kapangyarihan, puwersa, o taas ng tunog.
original_explanation: This is your all-around "power" word. "Ang lakas ng ulan!" (The rain is strong). "Ang lakas niya!" (He/She is strong). It can also mean "loud": "Hinaan mo, ang lakas ng TV!" (Turn it down, the TV is loud). In slang, "Lakas maka-..." means something gives off a strong vibe, e.g., "Lakas maka-mayaman ng kape na 'to!" (This coffee gives off rich-person vibes!).
usage_notes: Isang napaka-versatile na salita na ginagamit para sa pisikal na lakas, volyum, intensidad, o impluwensya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mo ng **lakas** ng katawan para sa trabahong ito.","translation":"You need physical **strength** for this job."},{"sentence":"Ang **lakas** ng hangin kagabi.","translation":"The wind was **strong** last night."},{"sentence":"Ang **lakas** ng tugtog!","translation":"The music is so **loud**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na naghahanda o nagtitinda ng ikmo, na isang pinaghalong dahon ng ikmo, bunga, at apog na nginunguya.
etymology: From mang- (doer prefix) + reduplication of the first syllable of the root (i) + ikmo (betel leaf).
original_explanation: The person, usually a lola in the palengke, who prepares the traditional Filipino chew, the OG breath mint and social lubricant. They're like a local barista, but for *nganga* (betel chew).
usage_notes: Refers to a person involved in the preparation or sale of the components for betel nut chewing ('nganga' or 'mama'), a traditional practice more common in rural areas and among indigenous groups.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala ang **mang-iikmo** sa aming palengke sa kalidad ng kanyang tinda.","translation":"The **betel nut seller** in our market is known for the quality of her goods."},{"sentence":"Tuwing hapon, nagkakatipon ang mga matatanda sa tapat ng puwesto ng **mang-iikmo**.","translation":"Every afternoon, the elders gather in front of the **betel nut preparer's** stall."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maranasan na maipit o mabalam sa daloy ng mga sasakyan sa daan.
etymology: Taglish, from the Filipino verb-forming prefix 'ma-' and the English word 'traffic'.
original_explanation: The national pastime of every Filipino commuter. It's that moment when Waze says your ETA is 15 minutes, but your soul knows it's an hour. You've been 'na-traffic' if you've aged three years just trying to get across EDSA. This is a verb of suffering.
usage_notes: A very common Taglish verb used in everyday conversation. The past tense is 'na-traffic'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang dumaan sa C5 kung ayaw mong **matraffic**.","translation":"Don't take the C5 route if you don't want **to get stuck in traffic**."},{"sentence":"**Natraffic** ako nang dalawang oras kaninang umaga.","translation":"I **got stuck in traffic** for two hours this morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang silid sa isang bahay o gusali na mayroong inidoro at karaniwang may kasamang lababo at paliguan.
original_explanation: The throne room. The CR (Comfort Room). The place where you have your best ideas, practice your concert numbers in the shower, or scroll endlessly on your phone. It's the most sacred and sometimes most 'mabantot' room in the house.
usage_notes: Universally understood. 'CR' (Comfort Room) is a very common euphemism, especially in public places. 'Palikuran' is a more formal but less common term for 'toilet'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasaan ang **banyo**? Kailangan kong maghilamos.","translation":"Where is the **bathroom**? I need to wash my face."},{"sentence":"Laging malinis ang aming **banyo** dahil araw-araw itong nililinis ni Nanay.","translation":"Our **bathroom** is always clean because Mom cleans it every day."}]

translation: to have someone rub or stroke something
meaning_filipino: Utos na hayaan o ipagawa sa iba ang pagdampi o paghilot nang marahan sa isang bahagi ng katawan o ibabaw ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is what you tell someone when your back is killing you after a long day at the office. "Bes, ipahagod mo naman 'yung likod ko." It's the command form of getting a gentle massage or having something like Vicks or Omega Pain Killer rubbed on you.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ipahagod** mo lang ang langis sa likod niya para guminhawa ang pakiramdam.","translation":"Just **have someone rub** the oil on his back so he feels better."},{"sentence":"Maaari mo bang **ipahagod** ang pusa sa bata para tumahan na ito?","translation":"Can you **have** the child **stroke** the cat so it calms down?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang idyomatikong pahayag na nangangahulugang lubos na pagkahumaling o pag-ibig sa isang tao.
etymology: From the repetition of "lagot," which means 'snapped' or 'broken,' implying one's resolve or heart has been 'snapped' by love.
original_explanation: This is beyond "crush lang." Ito 'yung level na willing kang mag-abang ng jeep para sa kanya kahit may Grab ka, or 'yung ngiti niya lang, buo na ang araw mo. You're so whipped, you can't even think straight. Basically, you're doomed... in a good way (sana).
usage_notes: An idiomatic expression. The base word "lagot" by itself means "snapped" or "you're in trouble!" but when repeated this way, it means "in love". Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lagot na lagot** si Marco kay Jean.","translation":"Marco is **head over heels** for Jean."},{"sentence":"Halata sa mga mata niya na **lagot na lagot** siya sa'yo.","translation":"It's obvious in his eyes that he is **completely smitten** with you."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging duwag; kakulangan ng tapang sa pagharap sa panganib, hirap, o sakit.
original_explanation: This is that feeling when your friend asks you to confront the chismosa neighbor but you suddenly have an 'important call' to take. It's choosing to 'seen-zone' a difficult conversation. It’s the opposite of 'tapang' and is often the secret ingredient in many bad decisions.
usage_notes: A strong word denoting a lack of courage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi **karuwagan** ang pag-iwas sa gulo.","translation":"Avoiding trouble is not **cowardice**."},{"sentence":"Pinairal niya ang tapang at tinalikuran ang **karuwagan**.","translation":"He let bravery prevail and turned his back on **cowardice**."}]

translation: to be able to get along with; to be compatible with
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng kakayahang maging kaayon, magkaisa, o magkasundo sa isang tao; ang pagiging magkatugma.
etymology: From 'maka-' (ability prefix) + 'suwato' (compatible, in harmony), possibly from Chinese.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate #RelationshipGoals. It's when you and your partner, or even your work bestie, just *click*. You finish each other's sentences, you like the same weird memes, and you can communicate with just one look. You're in sync, like a perfect K-drama couple.
usage_notes: Used to describe compatibility between people, ideas, or things.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bihira kang makahanap ng isang taong talagang **makasuwato** mo sa lahat ng bagay.","translation":"It's rare to find a person you can truly **get along with** in everything."},{"sentence":"Sana **makasuwato** ko ang mga bago kong katrabaho.","translation":"I hope I can **be compatible with** my new officemates."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang labis na damdamin ng pagkahabag para sa sariling mga problema at kasawian.
original_explanation: This is your "hugot" moment soundtracked by a sad OPM playlist, while you're wrapped in a blanket like a human lumpia. It's scrolling through happy couple photos on IG after a breakup and thinking, "Sana all." It's a temporary, self-indulgent wallowing session before you get up and fight again (or just order more milk tea).
usage_notes: Generally seen as a negative or unproductive state of mind, but universally experienced.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na ang **pagkaawa sa sarili** at harapin mo ang iyong mga problema.","translation":"Stop your **self-pity** and face your problems."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkaawa sa sarili** ay hindi makakatulong sa iyong pagbangon.","translation":"**Self-pity** will not help you get back up."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay, balita, o pangyayari na nagdudulot ng kaguluhan, kontrobersiya, o usap-usapan sa publiko.
original_explanation: The kind of tea that's so hot it burns. This is the stuff of showbiz talk shows and viral Marites threads. If a story is 'maalingasngas', it's juicy, probably involves a celebrity or politician, and is guaranteed to be the topic of conversation at the office pantry for the next week.
usage_notes: Always carries a negative connotation of public controversy or scandal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **maalingasngas** ang balita tungkol sa paghihiwalay ng sikat na mag-asawa.","translation":"The news about the famous couple's separation became **scandalous**."},{"sentence":"Iwasan mo ang masangkot sa mga **maalingasngas** na isyu.","translation":"Avoid getting involved in **controversial** issues."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay o tao na lubos na kinikilala, tanyag, at itinuturing na kumakatawan sa isang partikular na panahon, ideya, o lugar.
original_explanation: A word overused by Gen Z but for good reason. It's for anything that's legendary, memorable, and has left a mark. Sharon Cuneta's 'copy-paste' line in 'Bituing Walang Ningning'? Iconic. The Jollibee mascot doing a dance-off? Iconic. Your lola's adobo recipe? Absolutely iconic.
usage_notes: A very popular loanword in modern Filipino conversations, especially among younger generations. The Tagalog equivalent "tanyag" or "makasaysayan" doesn't quite capture the modern, pop-culture sense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang disenyo ng jeepney ay tunay na **iconic** sa kulturang Pilipino.","translation":"The design of the jeepney is truly **iconic** in Filipino culture."},{"sentence":"Para sa marami, **iconic** ang papel ni Vilma Santos sa pelikulang \"Sister Stella L.\".","translation":"For many, Vilma Santos's role in the movie \"Sister Stella L.\" is **iconic**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang walang-humpay na pagpupunyagi, paggawa, o pag-aaral nang buong sigasig upang makamit ang isang layunin.
etymology: From `pag-` (nominalizer) + `sumikap` (the verb 'to strive', which is `sikap` + infix `-um-`).
original_explanation: This is the 'OFW working two jobs' kind of hustle. It's the student juggling studies and a part-time job at a coffee shop. It's the grind, the hustle, the blood, sweat, and tears you pour into something to make your dreams come true. Pagsusumikap is the core value that fuels every Filipino success story, from the palengke to the corner office. It's more than just working hard; it's working with heart.
usage_notes: A very positive word, often used to praise someone's work ethic and determination. A stronger form of 'pagsisikap'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tagumpay niya ay bunga ng kanyang matinding **pagsusumikap**.","translation":"Her success is the result of her great **diligence**."},{"sentence":"Ipinakita niya sa kanyang mga anak ang halaga ng **pagsusumikap**.","translation":"He showed his children the value of **striving** hard."}]

translation: to become round; to form into a ball
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagiging bilog o paghubog sa isang bagay upang magkaroon ng anyong bilog.
original_explanation: 'Pagkatapos ng Pasko at New Year, 'yung mukha mo, biglang 'mamilog'. It's the natural evolution of your face after consuming 10,000 calories worth of lechon and queso de bola. Also what you do to dough when making pandesal.
usage_notes: Often used to describe things gaining a round shape, like a face getting chubbier or dough being shaped.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Utos ng panadero na **mamilog** ng masa para sa pandesal.","translation":"The baker ordered to **form the dough into a ball** for the pandesal."},{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **mamilog** ang kanyang mga pisngi dahil sa katakawan.","translation":"Her cheeks started to **become round** due to her gluttony."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bahay o gusali na nag-aalok ng upahang kuwarto, karaniwan para sa mga estudyante o manggagawa na malayo sa kanilang sariling tahanan.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'pensión' (pensiyon, paupahang bahay).
original_explanation: Before there were Airbnbs, there was the 'pensyunan'. It's a no-frills boarding house, the OG of budget accommodations in the Philippines. Perfect for students on a tight allowance or provincial employees starting a new job in the city. Expect shared bathrooms, a strict landlady, and a curfew. It's where you learn independence, how to cook instant noodles in a thousand ways, and how to sneak in late without waking anyone up.
usage_notes: Bagama't kaugnay ng 'pensiyon' (pera), ang pangunahing kahulugan nito sa Pilipinas ay isang paupahang bahay o 'boarding house'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatira ako sa isang **pensyunan** malapit sa unibersidad noong kolehiyo.","translation":"I lived in a **boarding house** near the university during college."},{"sentence":"Magkano ang upa sa **pensyunan** na iyan?","translation":"How much is the rent at that **pension house**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng lutuan, karaniwang yari sa metal, na ginagamit sa pagluluto ng kanin, ulam, o pagpapakulo ng tubig.
original_explanation: The MVP of the Filipino kitchen. It's where the magic of sinigang and adobo happens. It's also the designated rice cooker for generations before rice cookers became a thing. You know it's a well-loved kaldero when the bottom is black with soot ('uling').
usage_notes: A general term for a cooking pot, especially one for cooking rice on a stove.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isalang mo na ang **kaldero** at magsaing ka na.","translation":"Put the **pot** on the stove and cook the rice now."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang **kaldero** na ginamit para sa handaan.","translation":"A large **pot** was used for the feast."}]

translation: to cause delay; to be the reason for the lengthiness
meaning_filipino: Maging sanhi ng pagluluwat, paghaba ng panahon, o pagkaantala.
etymology: Mula sa panlaping pangkasanhi na "ika-" at sa salitang-ugat na "tagal" (haba ng panahon).
original_explanation: This is the *reason* why something is taking forever. It's the "chismis" that's the `ikatagal` of your quick trip to the sari-sari store. It's the one unexpected bug that's the `ikatagal` of your project deployment. Basically, it's the culprit behind your "sandali lang" turning into two hours.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang pandiwang sanhi na nagpapaliwanag sa dahilan ng pagkaantala o paghaba ng isang gawain o pangyayari.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang trapiko sa EDSA ang **ikatagal** ng aming biyahe.","translation":"The traffic on EDSA is what will **cause our trip to be long**."},{"sentence":"Ang hindi pag-uusap ang **ikatagal** ng paglutas sa problema.","translation":"Not talking is what will **cause the delay** in solving the problem."}]

meaning_filipino: Paggamit ng panlilinlang o madayang pamamaraan sa usaping legal; panloloko sa pamamagitan ng batas.
etymology: From Spanish 'abogacía' (legal profession), which in archaic Tagalog took on a negative connotation of legal trickery.
original_explanation: The dark side of being an abogado. It's using legal loopholes not for justice, but for... well, for winning at all costs. Think of a courtroom drama villain's favorite tactic. It's the kind of move that makes people say 'I-Tulfo na 'yan!' This word is super old-school; you'd probably only hear it from your lolo who's a historian.
usage_notes: This is an obsolete or very rare term. The modern and more common word is 'abogasya', which means the legal profession itself. The negative meaning is now more associated with the actions of a person rather than this specific word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Biktima siya ng **abogasia** ng isang tusong manananggol.","translation":"He was a victim of the **chicanery** of a cunning lawyer."},{"sentence":"Sa mga lumang nobela, madalas ilarawan ang **abogasia** bilang isang kasangkapan ng mayayaman.","translation":"In old novels, **legal trickery** was often depicted as a tool of the rich."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang napakaliit na organismo, lalo na ang isang nagdudulot ng sakit; mikrobyo.
original_explanation: The invisible enemy. Ito yung dahilan kung bakit laging sumisigaw si Mama ng 'Maghugas ka ng kamay!' 'Yung mga tiny creatures na nagdudulot ng ubo, sipon, at LBM. Sa panahon ng pandemic, naging celebrity ang mga kagaw. Sila ang kontrabida sa bawat alcohol at hand sanitizer commercial.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'mikrobyo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maghugas ng kamay upang maiwasan ang mga sakit na dala ng **kagaw**.","translation":"Wash your hands to prevent diseases caused by **germs**."},{"sentence":"Ang alcohol ay mabisang pamatay ng **kagaw**.","translation":"Alcohol is effective in killing **germs**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pakiramdam ng matinding pagkainis, pagkabigo, o pagkayamot na dulot ng isang tao o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: The emotional baggage you get from being 'kinunsumi'. It's that high-blood feeling when the Grab driver cancels, the internet dies during a presentation, or your sibling wears your new shirt without asking. It’s a special blend of anger, frustration, and helplessness. 'Puro ka na lang kunsumisyon!'
usage_notes: A very common term to express frustration in daily life, often in a slightly dramatic way.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaking **kunsumisyon** ang dulot ng mabagal na trapiko.","translation":"The slow traffic causes great **frustration**."},{"sentence":"Iwasan mo na lang ang mga taong nagbibigay sa iyo ng **kunsumisyon**.","translation":"Just avoid people who give you **vexation**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng may kakulangan sa pag-iisip o pang-unawa; isang salitang ginagamit bilang pang-insulto o, sa ibang konteksto, bilang mapaglarong tawag sa kaibigan.
original_explanation: A term of endearment among close female friends, often used after one of them does something silly. "Ang gaga mo, bakit mo siya nireplyan?!" But be careful, used with the wrong tone to the wrong person, it's a declaration of war. Context is everything! The male equivalent is 'gago'.
usage_notes: Highly context-dependent. Can be an insult or a term of endearment. Refers specifically to a female.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halika rito, **gaga**! Namiss kita!","translation":"Come here, you **silly**! I missed you!"},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala diyan, **gaga** 'yan.","translation":"Don't believe her, she's **stupid**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kaalaman o kasanayang natamo mula sa paggawa, pagdanas, o pagmamasid sa isang bagay o pangyayari sa loob ng isang panahon.
original_explanation: Your life's collection of wins, losses, epic fails, and 'sana all' moments. Hindi ito 'yung '2 years experience required' sa Jobstreet lang. Ito 'yung mga pinagdaanan mo na humubog sa'yo. Sabi nga nila, "karanasan ang pinakamahusay na guro," at madalas, mataas maningil ng tuition fee. It's the reason you have 'trust issues' or why you know the best-kept secrets of Divisoria.
usage_notes: A very common and essential word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang malawak na **karanasan** sa pagluluto ang nagpanalo sa kanya sa kompetisyon.","translation":"Her extensive **experience** in cooking made her win the competition."},{"sentence":"Isang di malilimutang **karanasan** ang pag-akyat namin sa Bundok Pulag.","translation":"Our climb up Mount Pulag was an unforgettable **experience**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong labis na nagtitipid at ayaw gumastos ng pera; maramot.
original_explanation: Your friend who always 'forgets' their wallet during lunch out, insists on splitting the bill down to the last centavo, or walks 5 kilometers just to save on a 10-peso jeepney fare. They're not just 'matipid' (frugal), they're next-level 'di-makabasag-pinggan sa pagtitipid'.
usage_notes: While 'matipid' (frugal) is often seen as a positive trait, 'kuripot' carries a distinctly negative connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag ka namang maging **kuripot** sa sarili mo, bumili ka na ng bagong sapatos.","translation":"Don't be so **stingy** with yourself, buy new shoes already."},{"sentence":"Kilala siyang **kuripot** sa buong barangay.","translation":"He is known as a **miser** in the whole village."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking dram na may dalawang ulunan na pinapatunog sa pamamagitan ng pagpalo, karaniwang ginagamit sa mga banda o orkestra.
original_explanation: Ito yung malaking drum sa banda na laging nasa likod, parang yung kaibigan mong laging "seen" pero solid ang suporta. Kapag may parada para sa fiesta, siguradong maririnig mo ang boom-boom-boom ng tambulin.
usage_notes: Madalas na ipagkamali sa 'tamburin' (tambourine). Ang 'tambulin' ay ang malaking bass drum.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malakas ang tunog ng **tambulin** sa parada.","translation":"The sound of the **bass drum** in the parade is loud."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kataga na ginagamit sa pagbuo ng tanong, pagpapahayag ng pagtataka, o pagdidiin. Wala itong katumbas na direktang salita sa Ingles ngunit nagpapahiwatig ng tonong patanong.
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino question mark you can hear. It turns any statement into a question. "Kumain ka." (You ate.) vs "Kumain ka **ba**?" (Did you eat?). It's also the sound of your Tita being nosy: "May nobyo ka na **ba**?" (Do you have a boyfriend yet?). It can also express surprise or frustration, like "Ano **ba**?!" (What the heck?!).
usage_notes: Essential for forming yes/no questions in Tagalog. Its placement can slightly change the emphasis but usually comes after the first word (verb/adjective/noun) of the predicate.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Aalis ka na **ba**?","translation":"Are you leaving already?"},{"sentence":"Ganyan **ba** talaga 'yan?","translation":"Is it really like that?"},{"sentence":"Ano **ba** ang nangyayari dito?","translation":"What **in the world** is happening here?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hiram na salita para sa taong ang trabaho ay linisin at panatilihing maayos ang isang gusali, tulad ng paaralan, opisina, o ospital.
original_explanation: The unsung heroes of every building. They know all the building's secrets, from which CR has the best bidet to where the secret chismis spots are. They're the ones who magically make coffee spills and piso-sized ipis disappear. Always be nice to the janitor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisabi sa **janitor** na naubos na ang tissue sa banyo.","translation":"Please tell the **janitor** that the bathroom is out of tissue."},{"sentence":"Malinis ang aming opisina dahil masipag ang aming **janitor**.","translation":"Our office is clean because our **janitor** is hardworking."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang opisyal na gawain o seremonya ng pagdedeklara sa isang tao bilang santo, karaniwang isinasagawa ng Santo Papa sa Simbahang Katoliko.
original_explanation: The official ceremony. This is the big event in the Vatican, with all the pomp and circumstance, where a person is officially added to the list of saints. Think of it as the divine version of a Hall of Fame induction ceremony. The kanonisasyon is the culmination of a very, very long background check.
usage_notes: A formal, religious term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinaluhan ng maraming Pilipino ang **kanonisasyon** ni San Lorenzo Ruiz sa Roma.","translation":"Many Filipinos attended the **canonization** of Saint Lorenzo Ruiz in Rome."},{"sentence":"Ang **kanonisasyon** ay isang mahalagang kaganapan para sa mga mananampalataya.","translation":"A **canonization** is an important event for the faithful."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumpak o eksakto sa target; tumutukoy sa isang tao na may mahusay na kakayahan sa pagtama ng puntirya.
etymology: From Spanish 'asentado' (settled, placed), likely influenced by 'apuntar' (to aim).
original_explanation: Describes someone with a killer aim, whether in basketball, darts, or spilling the tea (chismis) with deadly accuracy. When your shot goes in, 'Asintado!'. When your friend's guess about your crush is spot-on, 'Asintado ka, bes!'.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a marksman or a successful shot.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siyang **asintado** sa paggamit ng pana at palaso.","translation":"He is known as a **sharp-shooter** with a bow and arrow."},{"sentence":"Ang galing! **Asintado** ang bawat tira mo sa basketball.","translation":"Amazing! Every shot you take in basketball is **well-aimed**."}]

translation: refuge, a person to run to
meaning_filipino: Isang tao, lugar, o institusyon na nilalapitan o pinupuntahan para sa tulong, kanlungan, o proteksyon sa oras ng pangangailangan.
original_explanation: Your go-to person when you need to rant, borrow money, or just cry about life. The human version of a 24/7 convenience store for your emotional needs. Your beshie, basically.
usage_notes: While it can literally mean 'a place for running' or 'a running event', the 'refuge' meaning is more common in colloquial speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang naging **takbuhan** ko noong mga panahong lugmok ako.","translation":"She became my **refuge** during the times I was down."},{"sentence":"Ang opisina ng HR ang **takbuhan** ng mga empleyadong may hinaing.","translation":"The HR office is the **place to go** for employees with grievances."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang makabagong parirala na nangangahulugang tapat o prangkang pagpapahayag, madalas na may halong katuwaan o tsismis.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Ingles na "candid" (tapat) at ang salitang "yarn", isang mapaglarong bersyon ng "iyan" o isang filler word na pinasikat sa online culture.
original_explanation: The Gen Z version of 'To be honest...' or 'Spill the tea.' You use 'candid yarn' right before you drop a truth bomb, a juicy piece of chismis, or a brutally honest opinion that nobody asked for but everyone wants to hear. It's like adding a glitter filter to your unfiltered thoughts.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa simula ng isang pangungusap bilang panimula sa isang tapat na komento.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Candid yarn**, hindi talaga bagay sa kanya 'yung damit na 'yun.","translation":"**Speaking frankly**, that outfit really doesn't suit her."}]
related: ["prangkahan","spill the tea","to be honest","sa totoo lang"]

translation: to hoe; to use a hoe
meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng asarol sa pagbubungkal ng lupa, pag-aalis ng damo, o pagtatabon ng tanim.
original_explanation: Another farming verb, but more for maintenance. If 'mag-araro' is for the big plow, 'mag-asarol' is for the detailed work: getting rid of weeds, loosening the soil around plants. It's the gardening equivalent of cleaning your room after you've already arranged the big furniture.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **mag-asarol** sa hardin para tanggalin ang mga damo.","translation":"I need **to hoe** the garden to remove the weeds."},{"sentence":"Tuwing hapon, makikita mo si Lolo na **nag-aasarol** sa kanyang mga tanim na gulay.","translation":"Every afternoon, you will see Grandpa **hoeing** his vegetable plants."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malalim at maputik na hukay o lubak, karaniwang puno ng maruming tubig; latian o putikan.
original_explanation: That treacherous mud puddle during typhoon season that looks shallow but is actually a portal to another dimension that swallows your entire slipper. It's the kind of unexpected, messy situation you find yourself in, both literally on the street and figuratively in life.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a very messy and difficult situation, a 'quagmire'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahulog ang gulong ng dyip sa isang **balaho** sa gilid ng kalsada.","translation":"The jeep's wheel fell into a **mud hole** on the side of the road."},{"sentence":"Ang pagkakabaon sa utang ay parang pagkalubog sa isang **balaho**.","translation":"Being deep in debt is like sinking into a **quagmire**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasuotan o damit na isinusuot sa katawan.
original_explanation: Your OOTD (Outfit of the Day). This is what you wear. From your ukay-ukay finds to your branded jacket na pang-aircon lang sa office. Yung pang-'awra' mo sa mall. 'Anong suot mo mamaya?' is the eternal question before any 'lakad'.
usage_notes: Can refer to a single piece of clothing or a whole outfit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng **suot** mo ngayon, saan mo nabili?","translation":"Your **outfit** today is beautiful, where did you buy it?"},{"sentence":"Pangkaraniwan lang ang kanyang **suot** ngunit malinis tingnan.","translation":"His **clothes** were simple but looked clean."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging walang kasama.
original_explanation: How you feel after a breakup, eating a whole tub of ice cream. It's your status when your friends make plans without you. It can be peaceful (me-time) or sad (lonely), depending on whether you chose it or it chose you.
usage_notes: Can be used as an adjective or an adverb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Mag-isa** niyang binuhat ang mabigat na kahon.","translation":"He lifted the heavy box **by himself**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpunta kasama ng isang tao; ang pagbibigay ng kompanya sa iba.
original_explanation: Ito yung pakiusap mo sa kaibigan mo, "Bes, samahan mo naman ako sa CR, ang dilim eh." o "Samahan mo akong mag-shopping, ha?" It’s the act of being someone's +1, their buddy, their chaperone.
usage_notes: Anyong pautos. Ang salitang-ugat na pandiwa ay 'sumama'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **samahan** mo ako sa palengke.","translation":"Please **accompany** me to the market."},{"sentence":"\"Sige, **sasamahan** kita,\" ang sagot niya.","translation":"\"Okay, I **will go with** you,\" he replied."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hindi pagsunod sa isang utos, batas, tuntunin, o payo ng isang tao o institusyon.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "suway" (pagsuway) at panlaping -um-.
original_explanation: That feeling when your parents tell you to wash the dishes but you binge-watch Netflix instead? That's you, *sumuway*. It's breaking the rules, whether it's your mom's curfew or your boss's 'no social media' policy. The classic 'pasaway' move.
usage_notes: Ito ay nasa anyong pangnagdaan. Ang pawatas ay "sumuway" at ang pangkasalukuyan ay "sumusuway".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumuway** siya sa utos ng kanyang mga magulang kaya siya napagalitan.","translation":"He **disobeyed** his parents' orders, so he was scolded."},{"sentence":"Binalaan ang mga empleyado na huwag **sumuway** sa bagong patakaran ng kumpanya.","translation":"The employees were warned not to **defy** the new company policy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbaba ng ulo o pagbaluktot ng katawan bilang tanda ng paggalang, pagsunod, o pagpapakumbaba.
original_explanation: This is the physical version of "sana all." You see someone important, you do the pagyukod. It's the OG way of showing respect, way before emojis and 'po' and 'opo' were texted. Think of it as the opposite of standing tall with pride; it's the "I know my place" gesture, whether you're meeting your jowa's parents for the first time or just dropped your phone.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of showing respect to elders, superiors, or in religious settings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagyukod** ay isang tanda ng paggalang sa kulturang Hapon.","translation":"**Bowing** is a sign of respect in Japanese culture."},{"sentence":"Nagpakita siya ng **pagyukod** sa harap ng dambana.","translation":"He showed a **bow** in front of the altar."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan o halaga ng pera na inilalagak bilang kapalit o alternatibo sa isang naunang napagkasunduan o kinakailangang deposito.
etymology: Combination of `kahalili` (substitute, alternate) from root `halili`, and `deposito` from Spanish 'depósito' (deposit).
original_explanation: This is a very specific term. It's like in online shopping, your first payment method gets declined, so you use your GCash instead. That GCash payment is the 'kahaliling deposito'. Or in renting a condo, maybe you can't pay the full 2-months security deposit upfront, so you negotiate an alternative payment scheme. It's the Plan B for your payments.
usage_notes: This is a technical term, mostly used in finance, banking, or legal contracts. It is not a common conversational term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-alok ang bangko ng opsyon para sa isang **kahaliling deposito** upang mabuksan ang account.","translation":"The bank offered an option for an **alternate deposit** to open the account."},{"sentence":"Bilang **kahaliling deposito**, tinanggap ng may-ari ang mga post-dated check.","translation":"As an **alternate deposit**, the owner accepted the post-dated checks."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malaking langaw, karaniwang may makintab na kulay berde o asul, na madalas makita sa mga nabubulok na bagay.
original_explanation: Not just your regular langaw (fly). This is the bigger, buzzier, often metallic-colored cousin that shows up uninvited to your picnic. It's the jumbo jet of flies, and you know it's been somewhere gross.
usage_notes: Ang 'bangaw' ay isang mas karaniwang singkahulugan. Ang 'bangyaw' ay maaaring mas madalas gamitin sa ilang rehiyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinapaalis niya ang mga **bangyaw** na dumadapo sa pagkain.","translation":"He was shooing away the **blowflies** landing on the food."}]

meaning_filipino: Nakalagay nang pahalang o pasalungat sa karaniwang direksyon; nakahalang.
original_explanation: The position of that motorcycle rider who cuts you off in traffic. Or when a tree falls across the road after a typhoon, it's 'nakabalagbag'. It’s the ultimate 'istorbo' or obstacle. It's anything that blocks the way by being sideways when it should be straight.
usage_notes: Often used in its verb form 'bumalagbag' (to lie across) or 'ibalagbag' (to place something across). Can also be a noun for a crossbeam or a short-cut.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May isang trak na **bumalagbag** sa gitna ng EDSA.","translation":"There is a truck **lying across** the middle of EDSA."},{"sentence":"**Ibalagbag** mo ang tabla sa pinto para hindi makapasok ang magnanakaw.","translation":"**Place** the plank **crosswise** on the door so the thief can't get in."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagbati o tanong na ginagamit upang alamin ang kalagayan o estado ng isang tao.
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino conversation starter. It’s our "hello," "what's up," and "how are you" all rolled into one. Can be a genuine question about your well-being or just a polite way to acknowledge someone's existence before you ask them for a favor. The expected answer is usually "Okay lang," even if your life is a mess.
usage_notes: The most common greeting in the Philippines. Can be spelled as 'kamusta' in informal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumusta** ka na? Matagal na tayong hindi nagkikita.","translation":"**How are you**? We haven't seen each other in a long time."},{"sentence":"Hi, **kumusta**! Pwede magtanong?","translation":"Hi, **hello**! Can I ask something?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na ginagamit bilang instrumento sa paggawa; o isang taong ginamit o naging kabahagi sa pagsasagawa ng isang bagay, lalo na sa masamang gawain.
original_explanation: This has two vibes. Vibe 1: The basic tool, like a single screwdriver. It's the 'lite' version of 'kasangkapan'. Vibe 2: The sidekick in a crime. If the mastermind is the 'utak ng krimen', the kasangkap is the one who drove the getaway car. The Robin to a villain's Batman.
usage_notes: Less common than 'kasangkapan' for 'tool'. The meaning 'accomplice' is more dramatic and often found in legal or news contexts. The context determines the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang martilyo bilang **kasangkap** sa pagpukpok ng pako.","translation":"He used the hammer as a **tool** to hit the nail."},{"sentence":"Itinuturing siyang **kasangkap** sa pagnanakaw kaya siya ay hinuli rin.","translation":"He was considered an **accomplice** in the robbery so he was also arrested."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubhang mababa ang taas o tangkad.
etymology: From 'napaka-' and the root word 'pandak' (short in height).
original_explanation: A term of endearment (or bullying, depends on the tone) for the vertically challenged friend in the barkada. The one who's always in front for group pictures. 'Huwag kang mag-alala, kahit napakapandak mo, abot mo pa rin ang pangarap mo.'
usage_notes: Generally refers to a person's height. Can be considered impolite if used to a stranger.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Palagi siyang inaasar na **napakapandak** noong bata pa siya, pero ngayon ay sikat na basketball player na.","translation":"He was always teased for being **very short** when he was a child, but now he's a famous basketball player."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagpapatala o pagrerehistro sa pagdating sa isang hotel, paliparan, o kaganapan.
etymology: Mula sa pariralang Ingles na "check in".
original_explanation: The first thing you do when you arrive at a hotel for your staycation, or at the airport for your much-awaited trip to Korea. Also, what you do on Facebook to let everyone know you're somewhere cool. From English 'check in'.
usage_notes: A direct borrowing from English, fully integrated into Filipino. Often used as an imperative: "Mag-tsekin na tayo."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating mag-**tsekin** sa hotel bago mag-alas dos ng hapon.","translation":"We need to **check in** at the hotel before 2 PM."},{"sentence":"Pumila na tayo para sa **tsekin** sa eroplano.","translation":"Let's line up for the flight **check-in**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matamis na pagkain na gawa sa inihaw at giniling na buto ng kakaw. Maaari itong inumin o kainin bilang kendi.
etymology: From Spanish 'chocolate', which is from Nahuatl 'xocolātl'.
original_explanation: More than just a sweet treat, it's a whole mood. 'Tsokolate, eh' refers to the dark, thick, traditional hot chocolate made from tablea, perfect with pandesal or ensaymada. 'Tsokolate, ah' is the watery, sad version. It's the hugot of hot beverages.
usage_notes: The phrase "Tsokolate, eh" (espeso - thick) and "Tsokolate, ah" (aguado - watery) originates from Jose Rizal's Noli Me Tángere, used to signify a guest's social standing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap inumin ang mainit na **tsokolate** kapag umuulan.","translation":"Hot **chocolate** is delicious to drink when it's raining."},{"sentence":"Gusto mo ba ng **tsokolate** na tablea mula sa Batangas?","translation":"Do you want some tablea **chocolate** from Batangas?"}]

translation: to hiss, to whistle (to get attention)
meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng isang matinis na tunog gamit ang bibig, karaniwang "psst" o "sst", upang makuha ang atensyon ng isang tao.
original_explanation: Ito yung universal, low-tech na paraan para tawagin ang isang kaibigan sa kabilang kalsada nang hindi isinisigaw ang pangalan niya. The classic "Psst!" It's the human equivalent of a notification ping. Pwede ring bastos, depende sa context at delivery.
usage_notes: This is the completed action (past tense) form. The present tense is 'sumusutsot'. It's an onomatopoeic word. In some contexts, it can be considered rude or a form of catcalling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **sumutsot** sa akin sa madilim na eskinita kaya binilisan ko ang paglakad.","translation":"Someone **hissed** at me in the dark alley so I walked faster."},{"sentence":"**Sumutsot** siya para tawagin ang nagtitinda ng ice cream.","translation":"He **whistled** to call the ice cream vendor."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-angat o paglipat ng isang bagay o sarili sa mas mataas na posisyon, lugar, o lebel.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `mag-` (gumanap ng kilos), `pa-` (patungo sa direksyon), at `itaas` (up, above).
original_explanation: This is what you do when the baha (flood) is rising—you `magpaitaas` all your appliances to the second floor. It's also a spiritual or motivational term, like 'magpaitaas ng antas ng kamalayan' (to raise one's level of consciousness). It’s about levelling up, literally or figuratively.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa pisikal na paggalaw o metaporikal na pag-angat ng estado o kalagayan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magpaitaas** ng mga gamit dahil sa paparating na baha.","translation":"We need to **move** the things **upwards** because of the coming flood."},{"sentence":"Layunin ng seminar na **magpaitaas** ng moral ng mga empleyado.","translation":"The seminar's goal is to **raise** the employees' morale."}]

translation: to put something into someone's pocket
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglalagay ng isang bagay sa bulsa ng ibang tao.
original_explanation: This is the less common, more literal version. Pwedeng ginagawa ng nanay mo na pasikretong naglalagay ng extra baon sa bulsa ng uniform mo. Or, in a more sinister way, planting evidence. "Hala, ba't may droga sa bulsa ko?" Baka may nag-imbulsahan sa'yo.
usage_notes: Hindi gaanong karaniwan kumpara sa 'imbulsa'. Maaaring magkaroon ng positibo (lihim na pagbibigay) o negatibong (paglalagay ng ebidensya) konotasyon depende sa konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pasikreto siyang **inimbulsahan** ng lola niya ng isang daang piso.","translation":"His grandmother secretly **put** one hundred pesos **into his pocket**."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka, baka may mag-**imbulsahan** sa iyo ng ipinagbabawal na gamot.","translation":"Be careful, someone might **plant** illegal drugs **in your pocket**."}]

translation: to take advantage of someone's absence, to act opportunistically
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa ng isang kilos o pagkuha ng pagkakataon habang ang isang tao ay pansamantalang wala o hindi nakatingin, na kadalasa'y may masamang layunin.
original_explanation: This is the classic move of a 'Salisi Gang' member in a coffee shop. You leave your laptop for 2 seconds to get sugar, and poof! Someone 'sumalisi'. On a lighter note, it's also what you do to the last piece of 'lechon' when everyone's distracted watching TV. You take your chance.
usage_notes: Often has a negative connotation, implying stealthy, opportunistic, and often illicit action. The term 'Salisi Gang' is a well-known criminal modus operandi in the Philippines involving theft by distraction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binalaan siya na mag-ingat sa mga magnanakaw na mahilig **sumalisi** sa mga restawran.","translation":"He was warned to be careful of thieves who like **to take advantage of one's absence** in restaurants."},{"sentence":"Habang abala ang lahat, may **sumalisi** at kinuha ang kanyang bag.","translation":"While everyone was busy, someone **took the opportunity** and took her bag."}]

translation: to shake off; to dust off
meaning_filipino: Alisin ang dumi, alikabok, o anumang nakakapit sa isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pag-uga o pagpalo nito.
original_explanation: The command form of "pagpag." It's what your mom yells when you're about to sit on the new sofa with your dusty pants: "Pagpagin mo muna 'yan!" It's the act of shaking off dirt, bad vibes, or even leftover food from a takeout bag (if you're a scavenger). It's the universal Filipino gesture for "get the dirt off."
usage_notes: A command form. "Pagpag" also famously refers to leftover food scavenged from garbage, cleaned, and resold, though "pagpagin" as a verb more commonly means "to dust off."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pagpagin** mo ang basahan bago mo ipunas sa mesa.","translation":"**Shake off** the rag before you wipe the table with it."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **pagpagin** ang lumang kumot na matagal nang nakatago.","translation":"The old blanket that has been stored for a long time needs **to be dusted off**."}]

meaning_filipino: Maging sanhi ng paglabas ng pawis sa katawan ng isang tao, karaniwan dahil sa pisikal na gawain, init, o kaba.
original_explanation: This is the goal of every Zumba instructor and every gym trainer. They want to **papagpawisin** you until you look like you just came out of a swimming pool. It's also what your crush does to you just by walking past, or what a surprise quiz from your prof does to your entire block.
usage_notes: Can refer to sweating from physical exertion, heat, or nervousness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mainit na sili ay siguradong **papagpawisin** ka.","translation":"The hot chili will surely **make you sweat**."},{"sentence":"Talagang **pinagpawisan** ako ng malamig sa PMP exam.","translation":"The PMP exam really **made me break out in a cold sweat**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-aangkop o pagtutugma ng mga bagay, tao, o ideya upang magkaroon ng harmoniya o kaayusan.
original_explanation: It's like playing dress-up and making sure your shoes match your bag ('terno'). Or in a group project, it's the art of adjusting your personality to get along with your difficult groupmates. It's about finding that perfect fit, whether in fashion or in relationships.
usage_notes: Can refer to fashion, social interaction, or general compatibility.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **pagbabagay** ng kulay sa disenyo ng bahay.","translation":"The **matching** of colors is important in house design."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagbabagay** sa ugali ng isa't isa ang susi sa matatag na relasyon.","translation":"The **adapting** to each other's personalities is the key to a strong relationship."}]

translation: to be able to store; to be stored
meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang maitago o maitabi ang isang bagay para sa paggamit sa hinaharap; maisalansan.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung mga screenshots mo ng convo niyo. Hindi mo na binabasa, pero nandoon lang, naka-save. O 'yung tone-toneladang pagkain na binili mo noong nag-panic buying ka dahil sa lockdown. Lahat 'yan ay naimbak sa bodega o sa phone gallery mo, taking up space, just like your unresolved feelings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siguraduhing tuyo ang bigas bago ito **maimbak** para hindi masira.","translation":"Make sure the rice is dry before it **is stored** so it won't spoil."},{"sentence":"Maraming lumang gamit ang **naimbak** sa aming bodega.","translation":"A lot of old things **were stored** in our storage room."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang hanapbuhay ay may kaugnayan sa dagat, tulad ng pangingisda o pagtatrabaho sa barko.
original_explanation: The original OFWs. These are the brave folks—fishermen, seafarers, mariners—whose office is the vast ocean. They know the sea better than you know your phone's settings. A magdaragat has more stories than your lola.
usage_notes: A general term for someone who works at sea. "Mangingisda" is more specific to a fisherman.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ama ni Jose ay isang **magdaragat** na naglalayag sa iba't ibang bansa.","translation":"Jose's father is a **seafarer** who sails to different countries."},{"sentence":"Bumalik ang mga **magdaragat** na may dalang maraming huli.","translation":"The **fishermen** returned with a large catch."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay, gawain, o titulo na nagbibigay-dangal, parangal, o pagkilala.
original_explanation: Think 'Guest of Honor' or 'Keynote Speaker.' It's the adjective you use for events or positions that are all about giving respect and prestige. A 'banggâ pandangal' is a testimonial match in sports. It's the formal way of saying 'this is for you, boss!'
usage_notes: Often used as a modifier, as in 'Susing Pandangal' (Key to the City), 'Panauhing Pandangal' (Guest of Honor), or 'Banggâ Pandangal' (Testimonial Match).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang alkalde ang magiging panauhing **pandangal** sa aming pagtatapos.","translation":"The mayor will be the **honorary** guest at our graduation."},{"sentence":"Nakatanggap siya ng isang plake bilang parangal na **pandangal**.","translation":"He received a plaque as an **honorary** award."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa sukdulang kalagayan ng kalungkutan, pagdurusa, o pagiging kaawa-awa.
original_explanation: This is when the situation is so bad, it's beyond 'sad boi' hours. It's full-blown telenovela drama level of suffering. Think of someone who lost their job, got ghosted, and their ulam for lunch fell on the floor all in one day. That's kahapis-hapis.
usage_notes: The reduplication of 'hapis' intensifies the meaning, signifying the highest degree of sorrow or misery.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kahapis-hapis** ang sinapit ng mga pamilyang nawalan ng tirahan dahil sa sunog.","translation":"The fate of the families who lost their homes in the fire was **most pitiful**."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagpapakita ng bahagyang galit o pagdaramdam dahil sa isang maliit na bagay o hindi pagkakaunawaan, karaniwang sa isang malapit na tao.
original_explanation: This is that classic Filipino passive-aggressive move. It's not full-on rage; it's the silent treatment, the subtle cold shoulder, the 'Bahala ka sa buhay mo' whispered under your breath. It's when your jowa forgets your monthsary and you're not mad, you're just... disappointed. That's tampo. 'Magtampo' is the action of initiating this state of emotional cold war.
usage_notes: Often used between close friends, family, and romantic partners. It implies a relationship where one expects a certain level of care or attention.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magtampo**, binili na kita ng paborito mong milk tea.","translation":"Don't **sulk** anymore, I already bought you your favorite milk tea."},{"sentence":"Mabilis **magtampo** ang kapatid ko kapag hindi siya pinapansin.","translation":"My sibling is quick to **feel slighted** when they are not given attention."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na nakabitin o nakalaylay dahil sa kabigatan, kahinaan, o kawalan ng suporta.
original_explanation: That feeling when sahod is still a week away and your wallet is empty. Or your shoulders after a 12-hour shift. Or your skin when you forget your skincare routine for a week. It's the physical manifestation of "pagod na me."
usage_notes: Can be used for physical objects, body parts, or even abstractly for spirit or morale.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **luyloy** ang mga dahon ng halaman dahil sa matinding init.","translation":"The leaves of the plant became **drooping** because of the intense heat."},{"sentence":"Kitang-kita sa kanyang mga balikat na **luyloy** ang pagod na kanyang nararamdaman.","translation":"You can clearly see from his **sagging** shoulders the exhaustion he feels."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon o pagtubo ng pakpak, karaniwang tumutukoy sa mga ibon, insekto, o mga mitolohikal na nilalang.
etymology: From 'magka-' (to have or to grow) + 'bagwis' (wing, especially a large flight feather).
original_explanation: This is what happens when you drink too much Red Bull. Kidding aside, it means "to grow wings." You'd use this for birds getting their flight feathers or in fantasy stories. It's the ultimate glow-up for a caterpillar or a 'diwata' leveling up.
usage_notes: Often used in a literary, poetic, or mythological context. 'Magkapakpak' is a more common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghintay ang inakay na **magkabagwis** upang makalipad.","translation":"The chick waited **to grow wings** so it could fly."},{"sentence":"Sa mga alamat, ang mga anghel ay mabilis na **nagkakabagwis**.","translation":"In legends, angels quickly **grow their wings**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit at de-gulong na kariton na tinutulak o hinihila ng kamay upang magbuhat ng mga kargamento.
original_explanation: The unsung hero of the palengke and construction sites. This is the small pushcart that carries everything from sacks of rice to blocks of ice. It's the low-tech, high-muscle-power solution for moving heavy stuff around.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'kariton' though 'kartilya' tends to be smaller and have two wheels.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang **kartilya** para buhatin ang mga sako ng semento.","translation":"He used the **handcart** to carry the sacks of cement."},{"sentence":"Nirentahan namin ang **kartilya** sa palengke para sa aming mga pinamili.","translation":"We rented the **handcart** at the market for our groceries."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkuha o pagsungkit sa isang bagay gamit ang isang kawit o anumang may katulad na hugis.
original_explanation: You know that arcade claw machine that's designed to make you fail? The act of trying to grab a stuffed toy with that claw is *kalawitin*. It's to hook something, whether it's a fish, a branch, or your friend's hoodie to get their attention.
usage_notes: Can also be used figuratively, e.g., to be hooked or snagged into a situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **kalawitin** ang mga susi na nahulog sa kanal.","translation":"He tried to **hook** the keys that fell into the drain."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang trabaho ay mamalantsa ng mga damit.
original_explanation: Ito yung professional na taga-alis ng gusot sa damit at sa buhay mo (at least yung part na related sa damit). Pwede ring term para sa kung sino man ang naka-assign sa bahay na magplantsa. Madalas, si Nanay o si Ate. Minsan, ikaw kapag may date ka.
usage_notes: Ang pambabaeng anyo ay "plantsadora".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghanap siya ng **plantsador** para sa kanyang mga uniporme.","translation":"She looked for an **ironer** for her uniforms."},{"sentence":"Ang aming kapitbahay na si Aling Nena ay isang mahusay na **plantsador**.","translation":"Our neighbor, Aling Nena, is an excellent **ironer**."}]

meaning_filipino: Mangyari o gawin sa iisang panahon o oras.
etymology: From magka- + alinsabay (a variant of sabay, meaning 'at the same time').
original_explanation: Parang 'yung work deadlines at bayarin sa credit card, laging **nagkakaalinsabay** dumating. It's when two (or more) things happen at the exact same moment, like when you and your bestie accidentally wear the same outfit. Twinning!
usage_notes: Often used to describe events or actions occurring concurrently. The root 'sabay' is more common in everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagkaalinsabay** ang pagdating ng ulan at ang pag-alis niya.","translation":"The arrival of the rain and his departure **happened at the same time**."},{"sentence":"Pinilit nilang **magkaalinsabay** ang kanilang mga iskedyul para makapagbakasyon.","translation":"They tried to make their schedules **coincide** so they could take a vacation."}]

translation: a small pinch; a tiny amount
meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na kurot o kaunting-kaunting dami ng isang bagay, tulad ng asin o asukal.
original_explanation: It's that 'pinch' of salt your lola tells you to add to the adobo, but you never know if it's a two-finger pinch or a three-finger pinch. It's the 'just a little bit' that can make or break a recipe. A 'kurit' of tsismis is also enough to start a fire.
usage_notes: Often used in cooking contexts for a very small, imprecise amount. Can be used figuratively for a small amount of anything.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magdagdag ka ng isang **kurit** ng paminta sa sinigang.","translation":"Add a **pinch** of pepper to the sinigang."},{"sentence":"Kahit isang **kurit** ng pag-asa ay sapat na.","translation":"Even just a **tiny amount** of hope is enough."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang panghalip na paari at palagyo (inclusive) na pinaikling anyo ng "sa atin," tumutukoy sa tagapagsalita at sa kausap.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'group project' pronoun. "Para sa'tin 'to!" is the battle cry before a group presentation or a drinking session. It's the opposite of 'samin' (our/ours, exclusive), which is what you use when you're talking about your squad and you don't want to include the person you're talking to. It's the pronoun of 'sana all'.
usage_notes: This is the inclusive 'our/ours', meaning it includes the speaker and the listener(s). It is a contraction of "sa atin".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tagumpay na ito ay para **sa'tin** lahat.","translation":"This success is for all of **us**."},{"sentence":"Hindi **sa'tin** ang bahay na 'yan.","translation":"That house is not **ours**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sama-samang pagtanggi na makipag-ugnayan, bumili, o gumamit ng produkto o serbisyo ng isang tao, kumpanya, o bansa bilang isang paraan ng protesta.
etymology: From English "boycott", named after Charles Boycott.
original_explanation: The act of "cancelling" a product or company before "cancel culture" was a thing. It's when a group of people gets mad and decides, "Ayoko na sa'yo, 'di na ako bibili ng produkto mo!" Parang ghosting, pero pang-ekonomiya at pang-masa.
usage_notes: The noun form. The verb form is "boykotin".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng panawagan para sa isang **boykot** laban sa dayuhang kumpanya.","translation":"There was a call for a **boycott** against the foreign company."},{"sentence":"Ang **boykot** ay isang mabisang paraan ng protesta.","translation":"A **boycott** is an effective form of protest."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang biglaan at hindi inaasahang pagkabigo o pagkasira ng isang mekanismo. Maaari ring tumukoy sa isang latigo o anumang bagay na biglang humaginit.
etymology: From 'paltik', which can mean a homemade, unreliable firearm, or the sound of a flick/snap.
original_explanation: That moment when your plan, joke, or even your lighter just doesn't work as intended. You tried to be witty, but the joke `pumaltik` and now it's awkward. Your DIY project suddenly broke. The lighter made a 'click' but no flame. It's the universe's way of saying, 'Nice try, but no.'
usage_notes: Often used for mechanical failures or plans that go wrong unexpectedly.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang paandarin ang kotse pero **pumaltik** lang ang makina.","translation":"He tried to start the car but the engine just **malfunctioned** (sputtered)."},{"sentence":"**Pumaltik** ang plano naming sorpresahin siya dahil nalaman niya ito nang maaga.","translation":"Our plan to surprise him **backfired** because he found out about it early."}]

translation: to be swindled; to be conned
meaning_filipino: Maging biktima ng panloloko o pandaraya, lalo na sa usaping pampinansyal.
original_explanation: Yung nagpa-budol ka online. You thought you were buying a legit iPhone 15 for 5k, but you got a bar of soap. You just got natekas. It's when someone scams you out of your hard-earned pera. The 'na-' form (natekas) is more common for past tense.
usage_notes: A colloquial term. The root 'tekas' means swindling. The more formal term is 'maloko' or 'madaya'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa mga investment scams para hindi ka **matekas**.","translation":"Be careful of investment scams so you won't **be swindled**."},{"sentence":"**Natekas** siya ng malaking halaga sa pekeng ahente.","translation":"She **was conned** out of a large sum of money by a fake agent."}]

meaning_filipino: Isulat o iguhit ang paunang bersyon o balangkas ng isang akda, plano, o disenyo.
original_explanation: Before you send that risky text or submit that major report, you iburador it first. It's the 'rough draft' stage of anything important. Think of it as storyboarding your life's next big move, or just making sure your resignation letter sounds professional and not like a diss track.
usage_notes: "Burador" as a noun means "draft". The verb form "iburador" is less common than saying "gumawa ng burador" (to make a draft).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko munang **iburador** ang aking talumpati bago ko ito isaulo.","translation":"I need to **draft** my speech first before I memorize it."},{"sentence":"**Iburador** mo muna ang plano para makita natin kung may kulang.","translation":"**Sketch out** the plan first so we can see if anything is missing."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mataas na lugar o moog na nagsisilbing kanlungan o tanggulan noong unang panahon, partikular na sa mga pamayanang Bisaya.
etymology: From Visayan 'ilihan', meaning a place of refuge. Possibly related to the root 'ilik' or 'ilag' (to evade).
original_explanation: Think of it as the pre-colonial version of a safe house or a mountain resort hideout. When rival barangays were about to throw down, people would run to the ilihan – a natural fortress, usually on a hill or cliff. It was the ultimate "BRB, hiding from my enemies" spot.
usage_notes: This is a historical and anthropological term, not used in everyday conversation. You'll likely encounter it in history books or museums.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natuklasan ng mga arkeologo ang mga labi ng isang sinaunang **ilihan** sa Bohol.","translation":"Archaeologists discovered the remains of an ancient **fortress** in Bohol."},{"sentence":"Ang **ilihan** ay nagsilbing proteksyon ng komunidad laban sa mga mananalakay.","translation":"The **refuge** served as the community's protection against invaders."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakadiwa, pinakaubod, o pinakamahalagang bahagi ng isang bagay, ideya, o pahayag.
etymology: From ka- + buod + -an, with a possible phonetic shift.
original_explanation: This is the 'TL;DR' (Too Long; Didn't Read) of a situation. It's the main point, the 'koko krunch' of the story. When someone tells a long, winding chismis, you ask, 'So, ano'ng kabuuran?' to get to the juicy part. It's the heart of the matter.
usage_notes: A more formal and literary word for 'buod' (summary) or 'diwa' (essence).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kabuuran** ng kanyang tula ay tungkol sa pag-ibig at pagkawala.","translation":"The **essence** of his poem is about love and loss."},{"sentence":"Sa kabila ng mahabang talumpati, ang **kabuuran** ng kanyang mensahe ay pagkakaisa.","translation":"Despite the long speech, the **gist** of his message was unity."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang opisyal na dokumento o ang akto ng pagtatalaga sa isang tao sa isang posisyon.
original_explanation: This is the actual appointment paper! The 'black and white' you receive from HR after being 'ninombrahan'. It's the physical or digital proof that you got the job or position. It sounds super formal, like something you'd hear from a government official announcing a new cabinet secretary. 'Pakipirmahan po ang inyong nombramyento.'
usage_notes: Refers specifically to the formal act or the document of appointment. More formal than the more common term 'pagtatalaga'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natanggap na niya ang kanyang **nombramyento** bilang bagong embahador.","translation":"He has already received his **appointment** as the new ambassador."},{"sentence":"Pinirmahan ng pangulo ang **nombramyento** ng mga bagong hukom.","translation":"The president signed the **appointment** of the new judges."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa sangay ng pisika na nag-aaral sa paggalaw ng mga likido, partikular na ang tubig, at ang mga puwersang nakakaapekto rito.
original_explanation: Ito yung science behind kung bakit smooth ang pag-swim ni Michael Phelps o kung paano gumagalaw ang bangka sa tubig. Isipin mo, parang physics pero sa tubig. Very science-y, 'di tulad ng pag-move on mo na walang scientific basis.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa mga teknikal o siyentipikong konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng mga inhinyero ang **haydrodaynamiko** na disenyo ng barko.","translation":"The engineers are studying the **hydrodynamic** design of the ship."}]

translation: to enjoy, to experience pleasure, to reap
meaning_filipino: Ang maranasan at damhin ang kaligayahan, kasaganaan, o anumang uri ng biyaya o mabuting bagay.
original_explanation: This is what you do after getting your 13th-month pay. You 'magtamasa' the fruits of your labor by going on a shopping spree, eating at a fancy restaurant, or finally booking that trip to La Union. It's the opposite of 'nagtitiis'.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of rights, freedom, or wealth. It carries a more profound sense of enjoyment than the English loanword 'mag-enjoy'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lahat ng mamamayan ay may karapatang **magtamasa** ng kalayaan sa pagpapahayag.","translation":"All citizens have the right to **enjoy** freedom of expression."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng maraming taon ng pagsisikap, oras na para siya naman ang **magtamasa** ng bunga ng kanyang pinaghirapan.","translation":"After many years of hard work, it's time for her to **reap** the fruits of her labor."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng gatas na de-lata kung saan tinanggal ang halos 60 porsyento ng tubig; pinaikling tawag para sa 'evaporated milk'.
etymology: Shortening of the English term 'evaporated milk'.
original_explanation: The lifeblood of Filipino desserts and coffee. It's not 'evaporated milk', it's 'evap'. The secret weapon in leche flan, fruit salad, and that perfect 'kremang-krema' coffee. When your mom sends you to the sari-sari store, she won't say the full name, just 'Bili ka ng isang lata ng evap, yung maliit lang.'
usage_notes: A very common colloquial abbreviation. Used in informal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakilagyan ng kaunting **evap** ang kape ko.","translation":"Please put a little **evaporated milk** in my coffee."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang fruit salad kapag maraming **evap** at condensed.","translation":"Fruit salad is delicious when it has a lot of **evap** and condensed milk."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkakaroon ng dalawa o higit pang bagay, ideya, o pahayag na hindi magkatugma o magkasalungat sa isa't isa.
etymology: From "pag-" (manner of) + "ka-" (abstract noun prefix) + "salungat" (contrary, opposite) + "-an" (noun-forming suffix).
original_explanation: 'Yung sinabi mong "on the way ka na" pero nasa bahay ka pa lang at kakaligo. That's a pagkakasalungatan between your words and reality. It's the conflict between your two exes showing up at the same party, or when your timesheet says you logged in at 8 AM but your face says you just woke up.
usage_notes: Can refer to conflicts in logic, stories, or between people/groups.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **pagkakasalungatan** sa testimonya ng dalawang saksi.","translation":"There is a **contradiction** in the testimonies of the two witnesses."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa **pagkakasalungatan** ng kanilang mga prinsipyo, naghiwalay sila ng landas.","translation":"Because of the **conflict** in their principles, they went their separate ways."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang butong bumubuo sa ibabang bahagi ng bungo na siyang humahawak sa mga ngipin at nagpapahintulot sa pagbubukas at pagsasara ng bibig.
original_explanation: The part of your face that gets a workout from eating crispy pata or chewing bubble gum. It's also what drops when you see your ex with a new partner ('nakakalaglag-panga'), or what hurts when you've been talking non-stop about the latest chismis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumasakit ang **panga** ko sa katatawa.","translation":"My **jaw** hurts from laughing so much."},{"sentence":"May matulis siyang **panga** na bagay sa kanyang mukha.","translation":"He has a sharp **jawline** that suits his face."}]

translation: to be able to put/place; to be placed
meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang maglagay o mailagay ang isang bagay sa isang partikular na lugar; ang pagiging nasa isang posisyon o lokasyon.
etymology: From the root word 'lagay' (to put, place) and the ability/potential verb prefix 'ma-'.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na after 30 minutes of Tetris with your groceries, 'di mo pa rin **malagay** yung isang galon ng tubig sa trunk. It's about being able to place something, or something being placed. It can also be used figuratively, 'di ko **malagay** sa isip ko' (I can't put it in my mind / I can't imagine it). It's the verb for finding a spot for something, literally or figuratively.
usage_notes: This is a potential verb form. 'Mailagay' is a more common synonym in object-focus sentences.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko **malagay** ang lahat ng libro sa maliit na estanteng ito.","translation":"I can't **put** all the books on this small shelf."},{"sentence":"Sana **malagay** na sa ayos ang lahat.","translation":"I hope everything will **be placed** in order."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malakas at hindi mapigilang pag-iyak na may kasamang panginginig ng katawan at malalalim na hikbi, karaniwang dulot ng matinding kalungkutan, sakit, o pighati.
original_explanation: This isn't your simple 'iyak-iyak lang.' This is the telenovela-level, ugly crying. The kind where your whole body shakes, you can't breathe, and snot is everywhere. It's the sound you make when your favorite K-drama character dies or when you see your ex with someone new. Maximum drama.
usage_notes: Represents the most intense form of crying, often involving sound and body tremors. The verb form is 'humagulgol'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig namin ang **hagulgol** niya mula sa kanyang silid.","translation":"We heard her **loud sobbing** from her room."},{"sentence":"Napuno ng **hagulgol** ang burol nang dumating ang kanyang ina.","translation":"The wake was filled with **wailing** when his mother arrived."}]

translation: to be able to be proud of; something one can be proud of
meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, tao, o pangyayari na karapat-dapat bigyan ng dangal at paghanga.
original_explanation: This is your "flex" moment. It's the thing you post on Facebook with the caption #Proud. It could be your kid graduating, your new promotion, or even just perfectly cooking adobo for the first time. "Yung anak mong nag-top sa klase? Ay, 'yan ang **maipagkakapuri**!"
