usage_notes: This is the future or contemplative tense. The more common form is 'maipagmamalaki'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tagumpay ng bawat Pilipino sa ibang bansa ay isang bagay na **maipagkakapuri** ng ating lahi.","translation":"The success of every Filipino abroad is something our race can **be proud of**."},{"sentence":"Wala siyang nagawang **maipagkakapuri** sa buong termino niya.","translation":"He did nothing **that he could be proud of** during his entire term."}]

meaning_filipino: May punit o sira; nasira sa pamamagitan ng paghila o pagkabatak.
original_explanation: The state of your jeans after trying to fit into them post-Christmas season. O kaya 'yung itsura ng puso mo after ng 'we need to talk.' It's not a clean cut, it's a tear. 'Hala, gisi 'yung damit ko!'
usage_notes: Synonymous with 'punit'. 'Gisi' often implies a more jagged or larger tear than 'punit'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **gisi-gisi** ang kanyang damit matapos siyang makipagbuno sa aso.","translation":"His clothes became **tattered** after he wrestled with the dog."},{"sentence":"Ayusin mo 'yang papel, **gisi** na ang isang tabi.","translation":"Fix that paper, one side is already **torn**."}]

translation: to have an adventure; to venture
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa ng isang paglalakbay o gawain na puno ng panganib, kaguluhan, at di-inaasahang mga pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is your travel vlogger life goal. It's what you tell your boss you're doing when you file for a long leave: "Gusto ko lang po **mag-abentura**." It can be as grand as climbing Mt. Apo or as simple as trying to navigate EDSA during rush hour on a payday Friday. Both are equally thrilling and dangerous.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang magkakaibigan na **mag-abentura** sa Palawan ngayong bakasyon.","translation":"The friends decided to **have an adventure** in Palawan this vacation."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malambot na telang hinabi, karaniwang gawa sa lana o koton, na kadalasang ginagamit para sa mga kumot, damit-pantulog, at kamiseta.
original_explanation: That cozy, soft fabric your lola's pajamas are made of. It's the material of choice for 'Ber' months fashion when you want to feel warm but it's not actually cold enough for a real jacket. Think of it as the official uniform for cuddle weather and Netflix marathons.
usage_notes: Not a very common word in everyday speech; people might just use the English word 'flannel' or the other loanword 'pranela'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili siya ng kumot na gawa sa **lanilya** para sa malamig na gabi.","translation":"She bought a blanket made of **flannel** for the cold nights."}]

meaning_filipino: Aawit ng mga awiting pag-ibig sa isang tao, karaniwan sa labas ng tahanan nito, bilang paraan ng panliligaw.
original_explanation: The future tense of the ultimate old-school romantic move. Before DMs and TikTok duets, this was the plan. Today, it’s the equivalent of planning to make a dedicated Spotify playlist for your crush. 'Balang araw, ako ang **manghaharana** sa'yo,' sabi ng bida sa pelikula. (One day, I **will be the one to serenade** you, said the hero in the movie.)
usage_notes: This is the future tense of 'mangharana'. It describes the act of serenading that will happen in the future. Now mostly seen in historical dramas or used romantically.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sabi ni Marco ay **manghaharana** raw siya sa kaarawan ni Clara.","translation":"Marco said he **will serenade** Clara on her birthday."},{"sentence":"Sino kaya ang susunod na **manghaharana** sa dalagang iyon?","translation":"I wonder who **will serenade** that young lady next?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kawalan ng paggalang, pitagan, o konsiderasyon sa damdamin o karapatan ng iba.
original_explanation: This is that one person who cuts in line at the MRT, the one who talks loudly in the cinema, or the one who replies to a serious work email with just "K." It's a blatant disregard for rules, both written and unwritten. It's the "bastos" behavior that makes you want to say, "Hindi ka ba tinuruan ng nanay mo ng magandang asal?"
usage_notes: A very formal and strong word for disrespectfulness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinagalitan siya dahil sa kanyang **pagkawalang-pakundangan** sa mga nakatatanda.","translation":"He was scolded for his **insolence** towards the elders."},{"sentence":"Hindi katanggap-tanggap ang **pagkawalang-pakundangan** sa anumang pook-sambahan.","translation":"**Lack of respect** is unacceptable in any place of worship."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit sa isang bagay, salita, o konsepto sa paraang hindi tama o hindi angkop sa orihinal na layunin nito.
original_explanation: Yung ginamit mo yung 'your' imbes na 'you're'. That's a classic maling gamit of words. Or worse, 'yung ginamit mo lang ako para makalimutan siya. That's maling gamit of a person, bes. #Hugot
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng gramatika, teknolohiya, o etika.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **maling gamit** ng kapangyarihan ay humahantong sa katiwalian.","translation":"The **misuse** of power leads to corruption."},{"sentence":"Itinuro ng guro ang tamang pagbigkas upang maiwasan ang **maling gamit** ng mga salita.","translation":"The teacher taught the correct pronunciation to avoid the **incorrect use** of words."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na itinakda bilang paunang kondisyon bago magawa o makuha ang isang bagay; mga pangunahing pangangailangan.
original_explanation: In college, this is the subject you *have* to pass before you can take the next one. In life, it's food, water, shelter, and WiFi. It's the non-negotiable, the must-have, the "di pwedeng wala". Before you ask for wants, you have to secure the unang kailangan.
usage_notes: A set phrase. Often used in academic, formal, or official contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Math 101 ay **unang kailangan** para sa Math 102.","translation":"Math 101 is a **prerequisite** for Math 102."},{"sentence":"Ang pagkain at tirahan ay mga **unang kailangan** ng bawat tao.","translation":"Food and shelter are **basic necessities** for every person."}]

translation: to arouse, to awaken, to inspire
meaning_filipino: Ang paggising o pag-udyok sa damdamin, isipan, o interes ng isang tao.
original_explanation: It's that feeling you get when a song, a movie, or a really good piece of chismis suddenly gets your full attention. 'Yung kanta na biglang nagpaalala sa ex mo? Yes, it 'pumukaw' your feelings. Or the smell of Jollibee that 'pumukaw' your hunger.
usage_notes: Used for emotions, interest, or literal awakening.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pumukaw** sa aking interes ang dokumentaryo tungkol sa mga pating.","translation":"The documentary about sharks **aroused** my interest."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang talumpati ay **pumukaw** sa damdaming makabayan ng mga nakikinig.","translation":"His speech **inspired** the patriotic feelings of the listeners."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang daglat para sa pariralang Ingles na "credit to the owner," na ginagamit upang kilalanin ang orihinal na pinagmulan ng isang ibinahaging nilalaman tulad ng larawan, video, o teksto.
etymology: English acronym for 'Credit To The Owner'.
original_explanation: The magic spell you cast on social media when you post a meme, a photo, or a quote that you totally didn't make yourself. It's the online equivalent of saying 'sabi lang po nila' to avoid getting called out for plagiarism. A must-have for every tita's inspirational morning posts on Facebook.
usage_notes: Halos eksklusibong ginagamit sa mga caption sa social media. Ito ay isang impormal na paraan ng pag-cite ng source.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng kuha! **CTTO** po.","translation":"What a beautiful shot! **Credit to the owner**."},{"sentence":"Shared this helpful infographic. **CTTO**.","translation":"Shared this helpful infographic. **CTTO**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-alis ng hawak o pagpapakawala sa isang bagay o tao sa hinaharap. Ito ang anyong pangkasalukuyan ng pandiwang 'bitaw'.
original_explanation: Future tense of "bitaw". The ultimate hugot word. This is what you tell yourself you'll do when the relationship gets too toxic. "Sa susunod na mag-away kami, bibitaw na talaga ako." But do you? Also used when you're literally holding on for dear life sa jeep or MRT and your grip is failing.
usage_notes: Future tense of 'bitaw'. Often carries a strong emotional connotation of letting go of a relationship or a burden.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **bibitaw** sa akin, baka mahulog ka.","translation":"Don't **let go** of me, you might fall."},{"sentence":"Alam kong mahirap, pero kailangan mo nang **bibitaw** sa sakit ng nakaraan.","translation":"I know it's hard, but you need **to let go** of the pain of the past."}]

translation: to pair up; to form a pair
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbuo ng isang tambalan o pares, karaniwan sa pagitan ng dalawang tao para sa isang gawain, sayaw, o kompetisyon.
etymology: From mag- (verb-forming prefix) + pareha (pair), which is from Spanish 'pareja'.
original_explanation: This is the teacher's command that gives you instant anxiety in PE class: 'Okay class, magpareha kayo for the folk dance!' It's the act of finding a partner, whether for a project, a dance, or in the game of love. It’s the verb form of creating a 'love team' or a 'tandem'.
usage_notes: 'Magpareha' is often used for functional pairs (dance partners, project partners), while 'magparis' can also mean this but more strongly implies a romantic couple or matched items.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ninyong **magpareha** para sa susunod na aktibidad.","translation":"You need to **pair up** for the next activity."},{"sentence":"Sino ang gusto mong **magpareha** sa sayaw?","translation":"Who do you want to **be partners with** in the dance?"}]

meaning_filipino: Pagsasagawa ng dalawa o higit pang gawain o pangyayari sa iisang panahon.
etymology: From i- (object focus prefix) + pag- + sabay (together, simultaneous).
original_explanation: The ultimate BPO agent or working student anthem. "Kaya kong ipagsabay ang trabaho at pag-aaral." It's the art of multitasking, like eating lunch while in a Zoom meeting, or juggling two "special someones" (wag tularan, bes).
usage_notes: The things being done at the same time are the object of the verb. Can be used as 'pagsabayin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang **ipagsabay** ang pag-aalaga sa anak at ang kanyang online business.","translation":"She is trying to **do** childcare and her online business **simultaneously**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ipagsabay** ang pagmamaneho at pagtetext.","translation":"Don't **do** driving and texting **at the same time**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong propesyonal na nangangabayo, lalo na sa karera ng kabayo.
original_explanation: The original Grab driver, but for horses. These are the small but mighty guys you see at the racetrack, expertly steering a creature ten times their size. The original high-stakes, high-speed delivery expert.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa konteksto ng karera ng kabayo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napanalunan ng paboritong **hinete** ang pinakamalaking karera ng taon.","translation":"The favorite **jockey** won the biggest race of the year."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng matinding pagsasanay upang maging isang magaling na **hinete**.","translation":"Intense training is needed to become a great **horseman**."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang laman sa loob; hungkag; tumutukoy sa isang bagay o tao na puro salita at walang katuturan o kabuluhan.
etymology: Mula sa katangian ng kakaning 'ampaw' na magaan at may hangin sa loob.
original_explanation: Describes that politician who makes grand promises but has zero follow-through. All talk, no action. Like the snack, they look substantial but are actually just full of air. 'Ang ganda ng speech, pero `ampaw` naman.'
usage_notes: Isang kolokyal na termino na ginagamit bilang metapora para sa isang bagay o taong walang sustansya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala sa mga pangako niya, puro **ampaw** lang 'yon.","translation":"Don't believe his promises, they are all just **full of hot air**."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang argumento ay napatunayang **ampaw** at walang batayan.","translation":"His argument was proven to be **hollow** and without basis."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging tapat, tunay, at walang pagkukunwari sa damdamin, salita, o gawa.
original_explanation: The holy grail of 'sorry.' It's not enough to say it, you have to *mean* it. 'Sinseridad' is what you're looking for when someone apologizes but their face looks like they'd do it again. It's the opposite of being 'plastic'. 'I can feel the sinseridad in his voice,' means you're actually buying what he's selling.
usage_notes: The native Tagalog equivalent is 'katapatan' or 'pagiging tapat'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinagdudahan niya ang **sinseridad** ng paghingi nito ng tawad.","translation":"She doubted the **sincerity** of his apology."},{"sentence":"Makikita sa kanyang mga mata ang **sinseridad** ng kanyang pag-ibig.","translation":"You can see the **sincerity** of his love in his eyes."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging may ulirat, kaalaman, o kamalayan sa mga nangyayari sa paligid, sa sarili, o sa isang partikular na bagay.
etymology: From `pagka-` (state or quality of being) + `malay` (consciousness, awareness).
original_explanation: This is that "Aha!" moment when you finally realize something, like when you wake up and remember you have a 10 AM meeting... at 9:55 AM. It's the state of being 'woke', not in the social media sense, but literally. The opposite of being tulog-mantika.
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of regaining consciousness or becoming aware of a situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nang magkaroon siya ng **pagkamalay**, agad niyang hinanap ang kanyang pamilya.","translation":"When he regained **consciousness**, he immediately looked for his family."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **pagkamalay** sa mga isyung panlipunan.","translation":"**Awareness** of social issues is important."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-iyak nang malakas at halos hindi makontrol, na may kasamang pagyanig ng katawan at hirap sa paghinga.
original_explanation: This is the ugly cry. Hindi ito yung pa-cute na iyak. Ito yung iyak na nanginginig buong katawan mo, a-alog-alog balikat mo, tapos may kasamang sipon at hikbi. Parang yung iyak mo nung nalaman mong may 'character development' yung paborito mong character sa series, aka namatay. Full-on telenovela breakdown.
usage_notes: Describes a more intense, convulsive, and sorrowful crying than 'umiyak'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Humibik** siya sa balikat ng kanyang ina matapos malaman ang masamang balita.","translation":"She **sobbed** on her mother's shoulder after hearing the bad news."},{"sentence":"Rinig sa buong kwarto ang kanyang pag-**humibik**.","translation":"Her **convulsive weeping** could be heard throughout the room."}]

translation: to place crosswise, to block, to grill
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng isang bagay nang pahalang o nakabalandra sa daan. Maaari ring tumukoy sa pag-iihaw ng pagkain sa ibabaw ng baga.
original_explanation: Two main meanings. 1) 'Yung ginagawa ng mga trike driver na biglang hihinto sa gitna ng daan to pick up a passenger. They ihalang their tricycle. It means to block the way by placing something across it. 2) 'Yung paglapag mo ng liempo o isda sa ibabaw ng uling. You ihalang it on the grill.
usage_notes: The context (road vs. food) is crucial to understanding the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ihalang** mo ang mga isda sa ihawan.","translation":"**Grill** the fish on the griller."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ihalang** ang sasakyan mo sa garahe.","translation":"Don't **block** the garage with your car."}]

translation: to convey; to cause to arrive
meaning_filipino: Dalhin o iparating ang isang bagay, mensahe, o balita sa isang tao o lugar.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung "seen" ng nanay mo sa chat tapos biglang may tatawag sa'yo na tita mo. Na-irating na niya ang chismis. It's about getting something—a message, a package, or even gossip—from point A to point B. "Pakisabi" is the verb form.
usage_notes: Often used for messages, news, or feelings. For physical objects, 'ihatid' is more common, but 'irating' can also be used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **irating** mo ang mensaheng ito sa iyong kapatid.","translation":"Please **convey** this message to your sibling."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan kong **irating** ang aking pagmamahal sa pamamagitan ng mga gawa.","translation":"I am trying to **convey** my love through actions."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagkuha o pagtanggap ng bayad, utang, o anumang nakatakdang halaga mula sa isang tao o entidad.
original_explanation: 'Yung trabaho ng Bumbay na naka-motor na sumisigaw ng "Palugi, Five-Six!" Ito rin 'yung ginagawa ng landlady mo tuwing katapusan. Sila ay nandito para **kumobra**.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in the context of collecting payments, debts, or fees. A more general Filipino term is `maningil`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing Sabado, dumarating ang ahente para **kumobra** ng bayad sa insurance.","translation":"Every Saturday, the agent comes **to collect** the insurance payment."},{"sentence":"Sino ang inatasan na **kumobra** ng mga donasyon para sa proyekto?","translation":"Who was assigned **to collect** the donations for the project?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang yunit ng sukat ng lupa na katumbas ng sampung libong metro kuwadrado (10,000 m²).
original_explanation: The unit of measurement for your Tito's "maliit na farm lang sa probinsya" which turns out to be a massive plantation. It's 10,000 square meters, or roughly the size of two football fields. A big piece of land, basically.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa agrikultura, real estate, at pagpaplano ng lupa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binili nila ang limang **ektarya** ng lupain para tamnan ng palay.","translation":"They bought five **hectares** of land to plant rice."},{"sentence":"Gaano kalaki ang isang **ektarya**?","translation":"How big is one **hectare**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging inaapi, pinagsasamantalahan, o hindi tinatrato nang makatarungan.
etymology: From ka- + api (oppressed) + -han (suffix denoting a state or condition).
original_explanation: That feeling when you're the only one in the group project who does all the work but everyone gets the same grade. It's the drama in a teleserye where the bida is poor and maltreated by the rich kontrabida. It's the state of being 'dehado' or on the losing end of a power dynamic.
usage_notes: A strong word used to describe injustice, exploitation, or maltreatment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinaglalaban nila ang mga karapatan ng mga biktima ng **kaapihan**.","translation":"They are fighting for the rights of victims of **oppression**."},{"sentence":"Hindi na siya makatiis sa **kaapihan** na dinaranas niya sa trabaho.","translation":"She can no longer endure the **state of being aggrieved** she experiences at work."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa kolokyal na gamit, ito ay isang masakit na salita na tumutukoy sa isang lalaking pinagtaksilan ng asawa, o bilang pangkalahatang mura. Ang literal na kahulugan nito ay lalaking kambing.
etymology: From Spanish 'cabrón' (large male goat; cuckold, bastard).
original_explanation: Literally, it's a male goat or billy goat. BUT! Be very careful. In the Philippines, this is a curse word, just like its Spanish origin 'cabrón'. It's used to call someone a bastard, an asshole, or a cuckold. You'd hear this shouted in traffic or during a heated argument. Don't use it unless you're looking for a fight.
usage_notes: Highly offensive slang. Its literal meaning (billy goat) is almost completely overshadowed by its vulgar meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumigaw siya ng, 'Hoy **kabron**!' sa tsuper na sumingit sa kanya.","translation":"He shouted, 'Hey **bastard**!' at the driver who cut him off."},{"sentence":"Ang **kabron** ang pinuno ng kawan ng mga kambing.","translation":"The **billy goat** is the leader of the herd of goats."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang nakasulat na komposisyon sa prosa na bahagi ng isang publikasyon; isang partikular na aytem o bagay; isang sugnay o seksyon sa isang pormal na dokumento.
original_explanation: That thing you were forced to write in your high school Filipino class. It can also be a section in the Constitution, like "Article III: Bill of Rights," which people love to quote online without actually reading. Or, it could just be any random "item," like the "artikulo" your tita sells in her sari-sari store.
usage_notes: Has multiple meanings: a written piece, a legal clause, or a commercial item. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsulat siya ng isang **artikulo** tungkol sa pagbabago ng klima para sa isang pahayagan.","translation":"She wrote an **article** about climate change for a newspaper."},{"sentence":"Ayon sa **Artikulo** III ng Saligang Batas, may karapatan tayong magsalita.","translation":"According to **Article** III of the Constitution, we have the right to speak."}]

translation: to lessen; to reduce in quantity
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabawas o pag-unti ng dami, bilang, o sukat ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is what you do to your rice serving when you're on a diet, pero nauuwi pa rin sa extra rice. "Magpaunti ka naman ng drama sa buhay," is also a valid, albeit savage, life advice.
usage_notes: Used to indicate causing something to become less or fewer.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinabihan ko siyang **magpaunti** ng kape para makatulog siya nang maaga.","translation":"I told him/her to **lessen** his/her coffee intake to be able to sleep early."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magpaunti** ng gastos ngayong buwan.","translation":"We need to **reduce** our expenses this month."}]

translation: to consume completely, to finish off
meaning_filipino: Ginamit o kinain ang lahat ng isang bagay hanggang sa wala nang natira.
original_explanation: The magic trick your dad performs on the leftover lechon. 'Umubos' is to make something disappear completely, whether it's food, your salary on 12.12, or your patience in traffic. It's the ultimate act of finishing something, leaving no survivors.
usage_notes: The verb is in the completed aspect (past tense). The infinitive is 'ubusin'. The actor-focus form is 'umubos'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **umubos** ng huling piraso ng pizza?","translation":"Who **finished off** the last slice of pizza?"},{"sentence":"**Umubos** siya ng isang galong ice cream dahil sa sama ng loob.","translation":"He/She **consumed** a whole gallon of ice cream out of heartbreak."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kilos ng pag-angat at pagbaba ng paa upang umusad; isang paraan o aksyon na isinasagawa upang makamit ang isang layunin.
original_explanation: Literally, a step you take with your feet. Figuratively, it's the 'next step' in your career, your relationship, or your plan to finally finish that Netflix series. 'Anong next hakbang?' is the question after every major life (or work) event. It's both a physical movement and a corporate buzzword.
usage_notes: Can be literal (a physical step) or figurative (a measure, an action plan).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **hakbang** na lang at matatapos na niya ang takbuhan.","translation":"Just one more **step** and he will finish the race."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating gumawa ng kagyat na **hakbang** upang masolusyunan ang problema.","translation":"We need to take immediate **action** to solve the problem."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lalaking miyembro ng species ng gansa.
original_explanation: The boyfriend goose. He's the one honking aggressively when you get too close to his goose girlfriend and their goslings. Basically, the overprotective 'jowa' of the bird world.
usage_notes: A straightforward descriptive phrase.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas malaki at mas agresibo ang **lalaking gansa** kaysa sa babae.","translation":"The **gander** is larger and more aggressive than the female."},{"sentence":"Hinabol ako ng **lalaking gansa** sa bukid.","translation":"I was chased by a **male goose** in the field."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang organikong kompuwesto na may katangiang malamig at amoy menta, karaniwang nakukuha mula sa langis ng menta at ginagamit sa mga produktong tulad ng sigarilyo, kendi, at gamot sa ubo.
original_explanation: Yung 'lamig-sarap' feeling ng Vicks VapoRub na pinapahid ni lola sa dibdib mo 'pag may ubo ka. Ito rin yung nagpapalamig sa yosi ng tito mo at sa candy na kinakain mo para gumaan ang baradong ilong. The official scent of every Pinoy's 'masama ang pakiramdam' kit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malakas ang amoy ng **mentol** sa efficascent oil.","translation":"The smell of **menthol** in the efficascent oil is strong."},{"sentence":"Nakatutulong ang **mentol** sa pagpapaginhawa ng paghinga.","translation":"**Menthol** helps in easing breathing."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mataas at patulis na istruktura na karaniwang matatagpuan sa tuktok ng isang simbahan o tore.
etymology: Isang pariralang Tagalog na binubuo ng "tore" (mula sa Espanyol na "torre") at "patulis" (mula sa salitang "tulis").
original_explanation: 'Yung matulis na part sa pinakatuktok ng simbahan na parang nakaturo sa langit. Parang 'yung sa Disney castle. Ito 'yung ginagawang palatandaan ng mga tao kapag naliligaw sila sa isang bayan. "Hanapin mo lang 'yung toreng patulis ng simbahan, malapit lang kami doon."
usage_notes: Ang "toreng patilos" ay isang baryasyon na may parehong kahulugan. Ang "patilos" ay nangangahulugan ding patulis o 'tapering'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Makikita mula sa malayo ang ginintuang **toreng patulis** ng moske.","translation":"The golden **spire** of the mosque can be seen from afar."},{"sentence":"Inaayos ng mga trabahador ang nasirang **toreng patulis** ng lumang simbahan.","translation":"The workers are repairing the damaged **steeple** of the old church."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang biglaan at masakit na pag-urong o paninigas ng kalamnan, lalo na sa binti o paa.
original_explanation: The ultimate betrayal from your own body. One minute you're sleeping peacefully, the next your calf muscle decides to audition for a role as a solid piece of concrete. That painful, involuntary muscle seizure is *kalambre*. The universal cure? Eating more bananas, apparently.
usage_notes: The most common term for muscle cramps in Tagalog. 'Pulikat' is a close synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inatake siya ng **kalambre** habang lumalangoy.","translation":"He was struck by a **cramp** while swimming."},{"sentence":"Kumain ka ng saging para maiwasan ang **kalambre**.","translation":"Eat a banana to prevent **muscle cramps**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghiwa nang malalim at mabilis gamit ang isang matalim na bagay, na karaniwang nag-iiwan ng mahabang sugat.
original_explanation: The sound your bag makes when a snatcher tries to open it with a cutter in Quiapo. Or, less dramatically, what you do to a box from Lazada when you're too excited to find the tape. Very graphic, very sharp.
usage_notes: Carries a strong sense of violence and urgency. Often associated with crime or self-harm.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May nakitang marka ng **paglaslas** sa kahon.","translation":"A mark from **slashing** was seen on the box."},{"sentence":"Ang **paglaslas** ng pulso ay isang seryosong senyales ng depresyon.","translation":"The **slashing** of wrists is a serious sign of depression."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ganap na pagwasak, pagpuksa, o pag-ubos sa isang pangkat, lahi, o bagay hanggang sa wala nang matira.
original_explanation: This is a very intense word. Think Thanos snap, but make it Tagalog. Ito 'yung ginagawa ng pest control sa mga ipis sa bahay mo, or 'yung goal mo sa ML kapag sinabing "Wipe out!" It's total destruction, no survivors.
usage_notes: A very strong and formal word, often used in historical, military, or epic contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanilang misyon ay **lumipol** ng lahat ng kalaban.","translation":"Their mission was to **annihilate** all enemies."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ikapito at huling araw ng sanlinggo, karaniwang itinuturing na araw ng pahinga at pagsamba.
original_explanation: The day of the week that feels like a 5-minute commercial break between your Saturday freedom and your Monday dread. It's for family lunches, hearing mass, catching up on sleep, and the slow, creeping realization that tomorrow is a work day. Aka "Sunday Scaries" day.
usage_notes: Always capitalized when referring to the day of the week. The uncapitalized 'linggo' means 'week'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magsisimba kami sa darating na **Linggo**.","translation":"We will go to church this coming **Sunday**."},{"sentence":"Ang **Linggo** ay araw ng pahinga para sa maraming manggagawa.","translation":"**Sunday** is a rest day for many workers."}]

meaning_filipino: Angkop o nauukol sa kasalukuyang panahon, pangyayari, o pangangailangan.
original_explanation: That meme you just shared? If everyone gets it, it's `napapanahon`. If it's from 2012, it's not. This word is the gold standard for news reports, chismis, and fashion. It means it's fresh, it's now, it's what's up. The opposite of being outdated or 'laos.'
usage_notes: Describes anything that is relevant to the current time or situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Napapanahon** ang talakayan tungkol sa mental health lalo na sa mga kabataan.","translation":"The discussion about mental health is very **timely**, especially for the youth."},{"sentence":"Hindi na **napapanahon** ang mga lumang patakaran sa opisina.","translation":"The old office policies are no longer **relevant**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang alternatibong tawag para sa kastanyetas, isang instrumentong pangmusika na pinatutunog gamit ang mga daliri.
etymology: Variant of Spanish 'castañetas'. The '-itas' suffix is a diminutive in Spanish.
original_explanation: Basically the same as 'kastanyetas', maybe just the 'kolehiyala' or conyo way of saying it. Sounds a bit cuter, like the 'mini' version. Think of it as the 'lite' version of its more formal cousin.
usage_notes: A common variant spelling and pronunciation of 'kastanyetas'. Sometimes perceived as a diminutive form, though they refer to the same instrument.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawawala ang isang piraso ng aking **kastanyitas**.","translation":"One piece of my **castanets** is missing."},{"sentence":"Gawa sa bao ng niyog ang ginamit nilang **kastanyitas**.","translation":"The **castanets** they used were made from coconut shells."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang serbisyo ng paghawak, paglilipat, at pag-iimbak ng mga kargamento sa isang pantalan o daungan.
original_explanation: The BPO of the pier. This is the company and the workers who handle all the heavy lifting when ships dock. They're the ones who move your balikbayan box from the container ship to the warehouse. Basically, they're the reason your stuff gets off the boat.
usage_notes: A technical term used in shipping and logistics. Refers to the service of moving cargo from the ship to the pier and vice versa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang serbisyo ng **arastre** sa pantalan ay mahalaga sa ekonomiya.","translation":"The **arrastre** service at the port is vital to the economy."},{"sentence":"Nagwelga ang mga manggagawa ng **arastre** dahil sa mababang sahod.","translation":"The **cargo handling** workers went on strike due to low wages."}]

meaning_filipino: Ipagdiwang ang isang tagumpay o masayang kaganapan sa pamamagitan ng pagsigaw, palakpakan, o iba pang paraan ng pagpapakita ng matinding kagalakan.
original_explanation: The feeling when your team wins the UAAP championship, when an extra long weekend is announced, or when your Shopee package finally arrives. Time to **magbunyi**! It's pure, unadulterated joy and public celebration.
usage_notes: Carries a more grandiose or public sense of celebration compared to the simpler 'magsaya' (to be happy).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **magbunyi** ang mga tao nang ianunsyo ang panalo ng kanilang kandidato.","translation":"The people began to **rejoice** when the victory of their candidate was announced."},{"sentence":"Halina't **magbunyi** para sa bagong taon!","translation":"Come, let's **celebrate** the new year!"}]

meaning_filipino: Sirain o wasakin nang lubusan ang isang bagay, estruktura, o damdamin.
original_explanation: This isn't just 'sira'. This is total demolition. Imagine a wrecking ball to a building, or what your heart feels like after a major 'sawi' moment. It's the 'wasak' level of destruction. Pwedeng literal na pader, pwedeng 'yung tiwala niya sa'yo.
usage_notes: Used in the imperative or infinitive form. Implies a forceful and complete destruction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **bagbagin** ang natitirang pag-asa sa kanyang puso.","translation":"Do not **shatter** the remaining hope in his/her heart."},{"sentence":"Inutusan silang **bagbagin** ang lumang gusali para tayuan ng bago.","translation":"They were ordered **to destroy** the old building to construct a new one."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang Espanyol na katawagan para sa sampalok.
original_explanation: The Spanish version of 'tamarind' or 'sampalok'. You might hear this from older relatives or see it in very old recipes. It's the lolo of 'tamarind' and the ninuno of 'sampalok' in the linguistic family tree.
usage_notes: Hindi gaanong karaniwan kaysa sa *sampalok* o *tamarind*. Kadalasang historikal o ginagamit sa mga tiyak na konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa lumang resipe ng lola, **tamarindo** ang nakasulat sa halip na sampalok.","translation":"In grandma's old recipe, **tamarindo** was written instead of sampalok."}]

meaning_filipino: Hahampasin o paluin ang isang tao o bagay, karaniwan bilang parusa. Ito ay nasa aspektong panghinaharap.
etymology: Future tense of the verb 'pumalo'. From root 'palo' (hit) with duplication of the first syllable ('pa-') to indicate future tense.
original_explanation: The classic Filipino parent threat, often involving a tsinelas, walis tambo, or hanger. "Sige, 'wag kang umuwi nang maaga, **papalo** ka sa akin!" It's the sound of impending doom for a pasaway kid.
usage_notes: Future tense, actor-focus verb. The person doing the hitting is the subject. A common variant is 'papaluin' (object-focus).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Papalo** raw ang nanay mo kapag nalamang bagsak ka sa exam.","translation":"They say your mom **will spank** you if she finds out you failed the exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtindig mula sa pagkahiga o pagkakaupo; o sa matalinghagang paraan, ang pag-ahon mula sa isang mahirap na sitwasyon sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: This is your inner monologue every Monday morning after hitting snooze for the 5th time: 'Babangon na ako... in 5 minutes.' It’s also the ultimate hugot battle cry after a major setback, heartbreak, or bankruptcy. 'Madapa man ako, babangon at babangon ako.' The theme song of every Pinoy teleserye protagonist.
usage_notes: Actor-focused future tense of 'bumangon'. Can be used literally for getting out of bed or figuratively for overcoming adversity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit anong pagsubok ang dumating, tayo ay muling **babangon**.","translation":"Whatever trials may come, we **will rise** again."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang puting pulbos na kemikal (calcium oxide) na nagmumula sa pag-init ng mga batong-apog (limestone), ginagamit sa konstruksyon, agrikultura, at tradisyonal na pagnganganga ng bunga.
original_explanation: Before there was cement, there was apog. It's the OG construction material your lolo's lolo used. It's also that white powder lola mixes with her betel nut (nga-nga) that turns her mouth red. It's basically the Swiss Army knife of old-school Filipino powders.
usage_notes: Often associated with the traditional practice of 'pagnganganga' (betel nut chewing).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ang **apog** at itlog bilang pampatibay sa pader ng lumang simbahan.","translation":"**Lime** and eggs were used to strengthen the walls of the old church."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging matigas, solido, o mahirap baluktutin o basagin. Maaari ring tumukoy sa pagiging matatag o sutil sa paninindigan.
original_explanation: This is the 'hardness' you feel when you knock on a narra table, or the 'stubbornness' of your friend who refuses to admit they're lost even with Waze on. It's the quality of being unyielding, whether it's a rock or a personality ('katigasan ng ulo').
usage_notes: Can be physical (hardness of an object) or metaphorical (stubbornness of a person, e.g., 'katigasan ng ulo').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubok ang **katigasan** ng diyamante.","translation":"The **hardness** of the diamond was tested."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko maintindihan ang **katigasan** ng ulo mo!","translation":"I can't understand your **stubbornness**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Paulit-ulit na gawin o sabihin ang isang bagay; magbigay-diin sa pamamagitan ng pag-uulit.
original_explanation: This is the 'unli-rice' version of 'ulitin'. It’s not just repeating, it’s repeating *repeatedly*. It's what you do when you're practicing a dance step, memorizing a script, or when your lola reminds you for the nth time to bring an umbrella. 'Huwag kalimutan ang payong, ha? Baka umulan. Dala ka ng payong.' That's 'ulit-ulitin' in action.
usage_notes: The reduplication of the root word adds intensity and indicates frequent, continuous, or habitual repetition.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **ulit-ulitin** ang pag-eensayo upang maging perpekto.","translation":"Practice must be **done over and over** to become perfect."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magsasawang **ulit-ulitin** sa kanya na mahal mo siya.","translation":"Don't get tired of **repeatedly telling** him/her that you love him/her."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang bagay na hiniwa sa napakarami at maninipis na piraso.
etymology: Reduplication of 'gayat' (slice) to denote multiplicity and fineness.
original_explanation: This is 'gayat' level 99. It's not just sliced, it's *aggressively* sliced. Think of the cabbage in your shawarma, the carrots in okoy, or the state of your heart after a really bad breakup. 'Durog na durog' is for feelings, 'gayat-gayat' is for when there are literal pieces.
usage_notes: Emphasizes the multiplicity and thinness of the slices. Can also be used figuratively for something torn to shreds.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Gayat-gayat** na ang papel nang makita niya ito.","translation":"The paper was **shredded** when he found it."},{"sentence":"Mas masarap ang sinigang kapag may **gayat-gayat** na labanos.","translation":"Sinigang is more delicious with **finely sliced** radish."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salita o bahagi ng pananalita na ginagamit bilang pamalit o panghalili sa isang pangngalan upang maiwasan ang pag-uulit nito.
etymology: From `pang-` (substitutive prefix) + `halip` (instead of, in place of).
original_explanation: The ultimate 'proxy' in grammar. A **panghalip** is that friend who subs for you in a meeting you want to skip. Instead of saying 'Maria loves the dog, the dog loves Maria, Maria feeds the dog,' you say 'Maria loves the dog, it loves *her*, *she* feeds *it*.' It's the grammar tool for people who are too lazy to repeat names. We love an efficient queen.
usage_notes: A fundamental concept in Filipino grammar, one of the primary parts of speech (Bahagi ng Pananalita).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang 'ako', 'ikaw', at 'siya' ay mga halimbawa ng **panghalip**.","translation":"'I', 'you', and 'he/she' are examples of **pronouns**."},{"sentence":"Gamitin ang tamang **panghalip** upang maging malinaw ang pangungusap.","translation":"Use the correct **pronoun** to make the sentence clear."}]

translation: to cause to stagger or sway
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging sanhi ng pagewang-gewang o di-matatag na paglakad o pagtayo ng isang tao o bagay.
etymology: magpa- (causative prefix) + suray-suray (reduplication of 'suray', meaning to sway or stagger)
original_explanation: This is what one too many bottles of Red Horse does to a person. The alcohol is the agent that makes them magpasuray-suray. It's the verb for causing that wobbly, unstable walk you see after a long inuman session or when someone gets really dizzy. The ground feels like it's moving, and you're just trying to stay upright.
usage_notes: The subject of this verb is the *cause* of the staggering, not the person staggering. The person who is staggering is 'sumusuray-suray'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sobrang pag-inom ng alak ay **nagpapasuray-suray** sa kanya.","translation":"Drinking too much alcohol is **causing him to stagger**."},{"sentence":"Ang malakas na lindol ay **nagpasuray-suray** sa mga tao sa loob ng gusali.","translation":"The strong earthquake **caused the people inside the building to sway**."}]

translation: disturbance; act of startling or scaring away
meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng paggulat, pag-istorbo, o paggulo sa kapayapaan o katahimikan ng isang tao, hayop, o lugar.
original_explanation: 'Yung biglang may kumatok sa pinto mo ng 3 AM, 'yun ang pagbulabog. O 'yung kapitbahay mong nag-videoke ng "My Way" nang wala sa tono. Also, 'yung biglang "ping!" ng work email sa phone mo on a Saturday night.
usage_notes: Often used to describe an abrupt and unwelcome interruption.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ingay mula sa construction site ay isang malaking **pagbulabog** sa aming pagtulog.","translation":"The noise from the construction site is a major **disturbance** to our sleep."},{"sentence":"Itigil niyo na ang **pagbulabog** sa mga natutulog na aso.","translation":"Stop the **act of disturbing** the sleeping dogs."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kumpol ng mga hinog na itlog mula sa mga isda at ilang hayop-dagat, na ginagamit bilang pagkain.
original_explanation: The "extra" you find when cleaning a fish, which some people consider the best part. It can be fried, cooked in a soup (sinigang), or salted. It's the Pinoy version of caviar, but way more accessible and often cooked until crispy. That popping texture is everything!
usage_notes: Can refer to roe from any fish, such as milkfish (bangus) or flying fish (bolinaw). The preparation varies by region.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinirito ni nanay ang **itlog ng isda** hanggang sa maging malutong.","translation":"Mom fried the **fish roe** until it became crispy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang walang-pakundangang pag-aaksaya o paggamit ng pera, yaman, o pondo na hindi sa tamang paraan, lalo na kung ito ay ipinagkatiwala lamang.
etymology: From 'lustay' (squandering, embezzlement). The '-um-' infix indicates a verb.
original_explanation: This is the official verb for when someone "borrows" the office funds for their personal "business trip" to Boracay. It's the act of treating the company's or the people's money like your own unlimited credit card. The classic "nawala na, naging bula pa" move on a grand, often criminal, scale.
usage_notes: Has a strong negative connotation, often implying illegal or unethical use of funds.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinasuhan ang tesorero matapos mapatunayang **lumustay** siya ng pondo ng bayan.","translation":"The treasurer was charged after it was proven that he **embezzled** public funds."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang may **lumustay** sa pinaghirapan mong ipon.","translation":"Don't let anyone **squander** the savings you worked hard for."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na daluyan ng tubig na mas maliit kaysa sa isang batis o sapa; isang artipisyal na kanal para sa patubig.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "ilog" na may pag-uulit (nagpapahiwatig ng maliit o imitasyon) at hulaping "-an".
original_explanation: The 'mini-me' version of a river. It's that small stream you see in fields or sometimes even on the side of the road after a heavy rain. It's not grand enough to be called an `ilog`, more like a baby `sapa`. In a farm, it's the irrigation canal that keeps the plants hydrated. Parang Wi-Fi signal na mahina, may connection pero hindi pang-heavy-duty streaming.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa mga rural o agrikultural na tagpuan upang tukuyin ang mga daluyan ng patubig.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumawa sila ng **ilug-ilugan** para madiligan ang mga pananim sa bukid.","translation":"They made a **rivulet** to water the crops in the field."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng preno upang pabagalin o patigilin ang takbo ng isang sasakyan o anumang gumagalaw.
original_explanation: What you scream at the jeepney driver when you want to get off: "Para!". To 'magpreno' is to hit the brakes. Also applies metaphorically when your friend is spending too much money at the mall and you have to tell them, "Uy, magpreno ka muna, wala pa tayong sahod."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigla siyang **nagpreno** nang may tumawid na pusa.","translation":"He suddenly **braked** when a cat crossed the road."},{"sentence":"Matuto kang **magpreno** sa tamang oras para iwas-disgrasya.","translation":"Learn **to brake** at the right time to avoid accidents."}]

translation: to extract the juice from; to distill
meaning_filipino: Kunin ang katas o diwa mula sa isang bagay, lalo na sa prutas o halaman. Maaari ding tumukoy sa pagkuha ng pinakamahalagang impormasyon o ideya.
original_explanation: Like when you're trying to get the tea (the chismis) from your friend's long story. You're not interested in the fluff, just the juicy parts. "Katasin mo na, besh, ano ba talaga nangyari?" It's also literally what you do to calamansi for your pancit canton.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for juicing fruits or figuratively for extracting information or essence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **katasin** ang mga kalamansi para sa sawsawan.","translation":"You need to **extract the juice from** the calamansi for the dipping sauce."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan kong **katasin** ang pinaka-importanteng aral mula sa libro.","translation":"I'm trying to **distill** the most important lesson from the book."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng romantikong relasyon kung saan ang dalawang magkasintahan ay naninirahan sa magkaibang lugar at may malaking distansyang heograpikal sa pagitan nila.
etymology: Acronym mula sa Ingles na "Long-Distance Relationship".
original_explanation: Yung relasyon na ang puhunan niyo ay unlimited data, puyat sa video call, at matinding tiwala. Mahal niyo isa't isa pero mas mahal ang plane ticket. Parang Wi-Fi, malakas ang connection pero may distance limit.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa mga text message, social media, at pang-araw-araw na usapan. Isa na itong bahagi ng modernong leksikon ng mga Pilipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap talaga ang **LDR**, pero kakayanin namin 'to para sa kinabukasan namin.","translation":"An **LDR** is really hard, but we will endure this for our future."},{"sentence":"Nag-break sila dahil hindi na nila kinaya ang pagiging **LDR**.","translation":"They broke up because they couldn't handle being in an **LDR** anymore."}]

translation: to cause something to be spilled; to make something flow
meaning_filipino: Hayaang dumaloy o tumapon ang isang likido, tulad ng dugo o tubig, nang maramihan.
original_explanation: This sounds dramatic, and it often is. Think action movies where the hero says, "Ayokong may madamay, ayokong may padanakin na dugo." (I don't want blood to be spilled). It's causing a liquid, usually something important like blood, to flow or spill.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of blood ("padanakin ang dugo"), making it sound very serious or violent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinag-utos ng heneral na huwag **padanakin** ang dugo ng mga sibilyan.","translation":"The general ordered not **to spill** the blood of the civilians."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tradisyonal na larong Pilipino, karaniwang isinasagawa tuwing pista, kung saan ang isang nakasakay sa kabayo ay sumusubok na sungkitin ang isang maliit na singsing gamit ang isang patpat.
etymology: From Spanish 'juego de anillo' (game of ring).
original_explanation: The OG Filipino fiesta game. Imagine a knight in shining barong on a horse, trying to spear a tiny ring with a stick while moving. It's like the provincial version of an extreme sport, requiring more skill than your average Mobile Legends match. A true test of precision and equestrian flair.
usage_notes: A traditional game often featured in town fiestas and cultural celebrations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napanood namin ang kapanapanabik na **huwego-de-anilyo** sa pista ng bayan.","translation":"We watched the exciting **game of rings** at the town fiesta."},{"sentence":"Ang nanalo sa **huwego-de-anilyo** ay itinuturing na hari ng pista.","translation":"The winner of the **game of rings** is considered the king of the fiesta."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang idyomatikong pahayag na tumutukoy sa isang taong mabagal umintindi, may kahinaan sa pag-iisip, o hindi matalino.
original_explanation: When your brain feels like a sweet potato – soft, mushy, and not processing information quickly. It's the Pinoy version of calling someone a blockhead or saying they're not the sharpest tool in the shed. "Bakit di mo ma-gets? **Kamote ang ulo** mo talaga!" It's a bit harsh, but often used jokingly among friends.
usage_notes: This is a common idiom. A milder version is just calling someone 'kamote'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paulit-ulit ko nang ipinaliwanag pero hindi niya pa rin maintindihan, parang **kamote ang ulo**.","translation":"I've explained it over and over but he still doesn't understand, it's like he's **slow-witted**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na nangangahulugang kawalan ng pakialam, interes, o pag-aalala sa isang bagay o sitwasyon.
etymology: Salitang balbal na maaaring nanggaling sa 'keri' (carry/can handle) o bilang isang mapaglarong pagpapaikli ng 'care'.
original_explanation: The ultimate millennial/Gen Z word for 'I don't care.' It's a verbal shrug. Got a hater? Kebs. Your ex has a new partner? Kebs. Failed a quiz you didn't study for? Kebs. It's the shortened, punchier version of 'I couldn't care less.' The official motto of someone who's unbothered, moisturized, happy, in their lane, focused, flourishing.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin kasama ang 'lang' (kebs lang). Purong impormal at ginagamit lamang sa kaswal na usapan at text.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Anong masasabi mo sa mga kritiko? **Kebs**.","translation":"What can you say to the critics? **Whatever**."},{"sentence":"Galit daw siya sa'yo. Sagot ko: **Kebs**.","translation":"They say she's mad at you. My reply: **I don't care**."}]

translation: to become senile; to become forgetful in old age
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng paghina ng isip at memorya na karaniwang nararanasan dahil sa katandaan.
etymology: From `mag-` (verb-forming prefix) + `ulianin` (senile). The root itself is from `uli` (again) with suffixes, implying a regression or return to a childlike state.
original_explanation: This is when Lolo forgets where he put his glasses... while they're on his head. It's becoming forgetful to the point of mixing up names or repeating stories you just told five minutes ago. The brain's version of a computer running out of RAM.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to senility or age-related memory loss.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsisimula na siyang **mag-ulianin** kaya kailangan ng mas mahabang pasensya.","translation":"He is starting **to become senile** so more patience is needed."},{"sentence":"Kinatatakutan ng marami ang **mag-ulianin** sa kanilang pagtanda.","translation":"Many fear **becoming senile** in their old age."}]

meaning_filipino: Ituring ang sarili bilang may kasalanan o responsibilidad sa isang hindi magandang pangyayari.
etymology: From "ma-" (verb prefix) + "sisi" (blame) + "ang sarili" (oneself). The 'ma-' prefix makes it a potential verb, but it's often used with other verb forms like 'sinisisi ang sarili'.
original_explanation: The default setting after you do something stupid. It's the "sana pala..." or "what if..." monologue in your head after a breakup or a failed project. It's when you keep replaying a scenario, thinking of all the ways you could have done better. The national sport of overthinkers.
usage_notes: Expresses guilt, regret, or taking responsibility for a negative outcome.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **sisihin ang sarili** mo sa nangyari; wala namang may gusto noon.","translation":"Don't **blame yourself** for what happened; nobody wanted that."},{"sentence":"Hanggang ngayon, **sinisisi niya ang kanyang sarili** sa pag-alis ng kanyang kaibigan.","translation":"Until now, he **blames himself** for his friend's departure."}]

meaning_filipino: May gilid o dulo na nakahihiwa o nakatutusok nang mabisa.
original_explanation: Can refer to a knife that's perfect for slicing mangoes, but more often used to describe your tita's tongue during family reunions. "Ang talim ng dila mo!" is a classic for a reason. It's that sharp wit, or just a really sharp comment, that cuts deep.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for objects (kutsilyo, gunting) or figuratively for words (salita, dila) or intellect (isip).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa paggamit ng **matalim** na kutsilyo.","translation":"Be careful when using a **sharp** knife."},{"sentence":"May **matalim** siyang dila pero mabuti naman ang kanyang puso.","translation":"She has a **sharp** tongue but her heart is good."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na sumasailalim sa pagsasanay sa ilalim ng isang dalubhasa upang matutunan ang isang partikular na kasanayan o propesyon.
etymology: Hango sa Espanyol na "aprendiz" o sa Ingles na "apprentice". Ang baybay na "aprentis" ay mas malapit sa bigkas-Ingles.
original_explanation: This is the 'Filipinized' version of 'apprentice'. It's what your tito who's a mechanic calls his young helper: 'Yung **aprentis** ko, utusan mo na lang.' It has a more 'blue-collar', hands-on vibe compared to 'intern', which sounds more corporate. You're an **aprentis** to a panday (blacksmith), not a law firm.
usage_notes: Ang baybay na "aprendis" (mula sa Espanyol) ay mas pormal ngunit mas bihirang gamitin kaysa "aprentis".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula siya bilang isang **aprentis** sa pagawaan ng sapatos.","translation":"He started as an **apprentice** in the shoe repair shop."},{"sentence":"Ang galing ng **aprentis** ni Mang Kardo, masipag at mabilis matuto.","translation":"Mang Kardo's **apprentice** is great, hardworking and a fast learner."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkuha o pagkopya ng datos na naganap na. Ito ay nasa pangnagdaang anyo.
original_explanation: Mission accomplished. After hours of waiting, you finally have the file. "Yes! Nag-download na rin sa wakas 'yung buong season!" It's the digital equivalent of a successful palengke trip.
usage_notes: A Tagalized verb in the past tense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagdownload** ako ng bagong app para sa pag-edit ng video.","translation":"I **downloaded** a new app for video editing."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **nagdownload** ng lahat ng pelikulang ito sa computer?","translation":"Who **downloaded** all these movies onto the computer?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar na ginagamit sa pagtatago; o isang uri ng larong pambata kung saan ang isang taya ay naghahanap sa mga nagtatagong kalaro.
original_explanation: The OG Filipino childhood game before ML and TikTok. "Tagu-taguan, maliwanag ang buwan..." It's also the general term for any hiding spot, like where you hide your snacks from your siblings, or where you hide your feelings for your crush. "Saan ba ang taguan ng Pringles dito?"
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa lugar (`taguan`) o sa laro (`larong taguan`).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglaro kami ng **taguan** sa bakuran hanggang magtakipsilim.","translation":"We played **hide-and-seek** in the yard until dusk."},{"sentence":"Nahanap niya ang lihim na **taguan** ng mga alahas.","translation":"He found the secret **hiding place** for the jewels."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapang pang-banyo na ginagamit sa paghuhugas ng pribadong bahagi ng katawan pagkatapos gumamit ng inidoro, karaniwang naglalabas ng tubig.
original_explanation: The real MVP of Philippine bathrooms. The reason why we look down on bathrooms that only have tissue paper. It's the 'tabo's' high-tech cousin. A true symbol of hygiene and civilization. If your condo doesn't have one, is it even a condo?
usage_notes: Pronunciation varies, with /bi-DEY/ being closer to the French origin and /BI-det/ being a common Anglicized version in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sira ang **bidet** sa banyo, kailangan nating tumawag ng tubero.","translation":"The **bidet** in the bathroom is broken, we need to call a plumber."},{"sentence":"Isa sa mga hinahanap ko sa hotel ay kung may **bidet** ba ang kanilang CR.","translation":"One of the things I look for in a hotel is if their restroom has a **bidet**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng utos o pakiusap na mag-antay para sa isang partikular na tao, bagay, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is a command, a plea, a promise. 'Hintayin mo ako' (Wait for me) can mean anything from 'I'm just getting my wallet' to 'Don't give up on us.' It's what you tell your friend who's about to start the Netflix episode without you. It's the verb form of our national pastime.
usage_notes: An object-focused verb. The action of waiting is directed towards a specific object or person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hintayin** mo ang sahod bago ka bumili ng bagong sapatos.","translation":"**Wait for** your salary before you buy new shoes."},{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **hintayin** mo ako sa labas ng sinehan.","translation":"Please, **wait for** me outside the movie theater."}]

translation: the act of basing on; grounding
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggamit sa isang bagay bilang pundasyon, batayan, o sanggunian para sa isang desisyon, ideya, o konklusyon.
original_explanation: This is your 'basis' for an argument. When you tell your friend "Uy, based on my experience...", that's pagbabatay. It's the "Source: Trust me, bro" of Filipino conversations, but hopefully with more credible foundations like actual facts or chismis from a reliable source.
usage_notes: Common in academic, legal, and formal discussions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang desisyon ay resulta ng maingat na **pagbabatay** sa mga ebidensya.","translation":"His decision was the result of carefully **basing** it on the evidence."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **pagbabatay** sa datos para sa isang epektibong pananaliksik.","translation":"The **act of grounding** on data is important for effective research."}]

translation: to be completely covered or smeared with
meaning_filipino: Ang ganap na pagkababalot o pagkalatag ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay likido o pulbos, sa isang ibabaw.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na nagluto ka ng ube halaya tapos from head to toe, pati pader ng kusina, may talsik ng purple. You are *makulapulan* in ube. Or 'yung bata na naglaro sa putikan, 'yun, *makulapulan* sa putik. Total coverage, besh. No spot left behind.
usage_notes: Often used for messy situations involving dirt, mud, blood, or paint. Implies a thick, often uneven coating.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binalaan niya ang anak na huwag maglaro sa labas upang hindi ito **makulapulan** ng putik.","translation":"She warned her child not to play outside so they wouldn't **be covered** in mud."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang uri ng kislap o kinang na katulad ng sa mga metal, na nagpapakita ng liwanag nang hindi ito hinahayaang tumagos.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng "kaningningan" (mula sa "ningning") at "metaliko" (mula sa Espanyol na "metálico").
original_explanation: This is a high school science class throwback. 'Yan 'yung itsura ng bagong-hugas na kaldero, 'yung bagong kotse ng kapitbahay, o 'yung eyeshadow na ginamit mo para sa 'New Year's Eve look' mo. That specific shine na nagsasabing 'I am metal.'
usage_notes: Isang teknikal na termino na ginagamit sa agham (heolohiya, kimika) at kung minsan sa sining o disenyo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isa sa mga katangian ng ginto ay ang **kaningningang metaliko** nito.","translation":"One of the properties of gold is its **metallic luster**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang kilos na ginawa nang biglaan, walang sapat na pag-iisip, o hindi pinagplanuhan.
original_explanation: The cause of 99% of bad decisions. It's the "add to cart" at 3 AM, the "I quit!" during a heated meeting, or the "yes" to a spontaneous trip you can't afford. It's when your 'id' takes over your 'superego'. "Huwag kang magdesisyon nang pabigla-bigla" is the advice you get *after* you've already made the impulsive choice.
usage_notes: Often repeated as "pabigla-bigla" to emphasize the rashness or abruptness of the action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pabigla**-bigla niyang pag-alis ay ikinagulat ng lahat.","translation":"His **sudden** departure surprised everyone."},{"sentence":"Pinagsisihan niya ang **pabigla** niyang pagsagot sa kanyang ina.","translation":"She regretted her **hasty** way of answering her mother."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, hayop, o bagay na pinaniniwalaang nagdudulot ng suwerte o sumisimbolo sa isang partikular na grupo, tulad ng isang koponan sa palakasan o isang kumpanya.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na 'mascot', na mula sa Pranses na 'mascotte'.
original_explanation: The most famous maskot in the Philippines is probably Jollibee. Siya 'yung character na sumasayaw sa birthday party at nagpapa-picture sa lahat. Or 'yung bunso sa pamilya na laging pinapasayaw sa harap ng mga bisita para sa P100.
usage_notes: Isang direktang hiram na salita.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Jollibee ang paboritong **maskot** ng mga bata.","translation":"Jollibee is the favorite **mascot** of children."},{"sentence":"Ang bawat koponan sa PBA ay may kani-kaniyang **maskot**.","translation":"Each team in the PBA has its own **mascot**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paraan ng pagpapahayag o pagtunog ng mga salita; ang akto ng pagsasalita o pagbasa nang malakas.
original_explanation: How you say things. It's the difference between 'three' and 'tree' that your call center trainer is always correcting. It's also what you do in front of the class for 'Tula' or 'Panatang Makabayan'. Clear diction, proper emotion—channel your inner theater actor.
usage_notes: Can refer to both the manner of speaking (pronunciation) and the act of reciting (recitation).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tamang **pagbigkas** ng mga salita ay mahalaga sa pag-aaral ng bagong wika.","translation":"The correct **pronunciation** of words is important when learning a new language."},{"sentence":"Humanga ang mga hurado sa madamdaming **pagbigkas** niya ng tula.","translation":"The judges were impressed by her emotional **recitation** of the poem."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong nagpapatakbo o namamahala sa isang makina, kagamitan, o sistema, tulad ng telepono, sasakyan, o negosyo.
original_explanation: Before everyone had a cellphone, the telephone operator was your gateway to calling long distance. "Hello, operator? Pa-connect sa Baguio." Now, it's the person driving the bus, the heavy equipment operator at a construction site, or the jeepney operator (the owner). It's the person behind the machine.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa iba't ibang konteksto, mula sa teknolohiya hanggang sa transportasyon at negosyo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tawagan mo ang **operator** para itanong kung may problema sa linya.","translation":"Call the **operator** to ask if there's a problem with the line."},{"sentence":"Ang tatay niya ay isang heavy equipment **operator** sa Saudi.","translation":"His father is a heavy equipment **operator** in Saudi."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang tao na may pananalig at paniniwala sa sariling kakayahan.
etymology: Mula sa pariralang `may` (has), `tiwala` (trust), at `sa sarili` (in oneself).
original_explanation: 'Yan 'yung friend mong lakas ng loob mag-present sa harap ng big boss, o 'yung nag-a-audition for a reality show. Sila 'yung mga taong may-tiwala sa sarili. They've got that main character energy. They believe in their own sauce.
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang parirala na naglalarawan ng isang katangian ng personalidad.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong maging **may-tiwala sa sarili** sa panahon ng job interview.","translation":"You need to be **self-confident** during the job interview."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang pagsasanay, siya ay naging isang batang **may-tiwala sa sarili**.","translation":"Because of his training, he became a **self-confident** child."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong may kilos o pag-iisip na taliwas sa karaniwan; madalas gamitin bilang isang impormal at kung minsan ay mapanuksong tawag.
etymology: Isang portmanteau ng "sira ang ulo" (broken is the head).
original_explanation: Your friend who decides to sing karaoke at 2 AM on a Tuesday? Siraulo. The guy in traffic who tries to weave through three lanes in two seconds? Siraulo. It literally means "broken head." It's the go-to Filipino word for someone acting wild, illogical, or just plain crazy in a casual, sometimes affectionate, sometimes insulting way.
usage_notes: Isang karaniwan, impormal, at kung minsan ay nakakainsultong termino. Maaaring gamitin bilang biro sa mga kaibigan o bilang isang tunay na insulto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Siraulo** ka talaga! Bakit ka tumalon diyan?","translation":"You're really **crazy**! Why did you jump from there?"},{"sentence":"Huwag mong pansinin 'yan, medyo **siraulo** 'yang taong 'yan.","translation":"Don't mind him, that person is a bit of a **lunatic**."}]

translation: a female friend; godmother of one's child
meaning_filipino: Isang katawagan para sa isang babaeng kaibigan, o sa ninang ng sariling anak (mula sa sistemang kumpare/kumare).
etymology: Shortened form of Spanish "comadre" via Filipino "kumare".
original_explanation: The ultimate tita-level term of endearment for a female friend. "Uy, mare, anong chika?" is the national anthem of chismis sessions everywhere. It originally comes from 'kumare' (co-mother, the godmother of your child), but now it's used for any close female friend, officemate, or kapitbahay you share life updates (and gossip) with.
usage_notes: Extremely common in informal, spoken Filipino. The male equivalent is 'pare' (from 'kumpare').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Mare**, nakita mo ba ang bagong teleserye kagabi?","translation":"**Friend**, did you see the new soap opera last night?"},{"sentence":"Pupunta kami sa bahay ni **Mare**ng Susan para sa kanyang kaarawan.","translation":"We're going to the house of **Mare** Susan for her birthday."}]

translation: to be peeled off; to flake off
meaning_filipino: Ang kusa o sapilitang pag-alis o pagbakbak ng panlabas na bahagi o balat ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: 'Yung pintura sa pader na parang feelings ng ex mo, kusa nang nagbabalat at nawawala. O 'yung sticker sa laptop mo na ayaw mo sanang tanggalin pero natuklap na sa gilid. Also, 'yung balat mo after mag-beach nang walang sunblock.
usage_notes: Often used for paint, skin, stickers, or any surface layer. 'Mabakbak' is a close synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula nang **matuklap** ang pintura sa aming gate dahil sa ulan at init.","translation":"The paint on our gate has started **to peel off** because of the rain and heat."},{"sentence":"Ingatan mong huwag **matuklap** ang wallpaper habang naglilinis ka.","translation":"Be careful not **to peel off** the wallpaper while you're cleaning."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging masaya; isang pagtitipon o gawain na puno ng saya at galak.
etymology: From `ka-` + `tuwa` (happiness) + `-an`, signifying a collective or abstract state of 'happiness'.
original_explanation: This is the vibe of a spontaneous get-together with friends where the only agenda is laughing 'til your stomach hurts. Think Friday night karaoke, family reunions without the drama, or that feeling when the whole barkada passes a tough exam. It's pure, unadulterated fun.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a fun event or a general atmosphere of joy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **katuwaan** ang kanilang Pasko.","translation":"Their Christmas was full of **merriment**."},{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng munting salu-salo para sa **katuwaan** ng lahat.","translation":"There was a small gathering for everyone's **fun**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang makakuha ng puntos sa isang laro, pagsusulit, o kompetisyon. Maaari ring tumukoy sa pagkakaroon ng tagumpay sa isang gawain.
original_explanation: What you hope to do on your exam, in a basketball game, or when you finally get the attention of your crush. It's getting that 'W'. Can also mean you found a great deal at the tiangge—"Naka-iskor ako ng murang sapatos!"
usage_notes: Widely used in sports, academics, and informally for achievements or acquisitions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **umiskor** ng panalong three-point shot para sa koponan.","translation":"He was the one who **scored** the winning three-point shot for the team."},{"sentence":"Sana **umiskor** ako nang mataas sa board exam.","translation":"I hope I **score** high on the board exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbuhat o paglipat ng isang bagay mula sa isang lugar patungo sa iba. Ito ay nasa pangkasalukuyang panahunan.
original_explanation: What you're doing with your team in a group project. "Ako na naman nagdadala dito." Or literally, what you do with your eco-bag at the palengke. It's the ongoing action of carrying something, whether it's groceries, a secret, or the emotional baggage from your last relationship.
usage_notes: Present progressive tense of "magdala". Can be used for physical objects or abstract concepts like problems or feelings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **nagdadala** ng aking bag?","translation":"Who **is carrying** my bag?"},{"sentence":"Siya ang laging **nagdadala** ng good vibes sa opisina.","translation":"She is the one who always **brings** good vibes to the office."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pag-aayos o pagbabalik sa maayos at gumaganang kondisyon ng isang bagay na nasira o may depekto.
etymology: From Spanish 'reparar' (to repair), with the Tagalog verbalizing suffix '-hin'.
original_explanation: The 'ayusin' for the 'conyo' crowd or when you're talking about something technical like a car or a gadget. It’s what your dad says he'll do to the broken washing machine, but it ends up sitting there for three months. "Kailangan nang **reparahin** 'yan."
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'ayusin' or 'kumpunihin'. 'Reparahin' can imply a more technical or mechanical repair, as opposed to a general fix.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **reparahin** ang bubong bago dumating ang tag-ulan.","translation":"We need **to repair** the roof before the rainy season arrives."},{"sentence":"Magkano pa-**reparahin** ang sirang cellphone?","translation":"How much does it cost **to get** a broken cellphone **repaired**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagsusuot ng bota, isang uri ng sapin sa paa na karaniwang mataas at matibay.
original_explanation: Literally, "to wear boots." This is what you do when it's raining cats and dogs in Manila and you need to wade through baha (floods), or when you're going for that "biker" or "E-girl/E-boy" aesthetic. It's the action you take before you can say, "These boots are made for walkin'... through this ridiculously flooded street."
usage_notes: A direct verb formation from the noun "bota".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magbota** kung pupunta ka sa putikan.","translation":"You need to **put on boots** if you're going to the muddy area."},{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang **magbota** dahil mainit daw sa paa.","translation":"He doesn't want to **wear boots** because he says they're hot on the feet."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng pagiging mahilig maglakbay, partikular na sa pamamagitan ng sasakyang-dagat, o ang pagiging malimit na naglalayag.
original_explanation: This is the original 'wanderlust' or 'travel goals' person, but make it nautical. Before travel bloggers, there were the mapaglayag. They're the type who'd rather be on a boat, exploring new islands, than stuck in traffic on EDSA. Think of ancient Austronesian ancestors or your modern-day friend who's always posting pics from a yacht party in Batangas.
usage_notes: A somewhat poetic and archaic term, now more often used figuratively for someone who loves to travel in general, not just by sea.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ating mga ninuno ay isang lahing **mapaglayag**.","translation":"Our ancestors were a people **fond of sailing**."},{"sentence":"Bilang isang taong **mapaglayag**, pangarap niyang libutin ang buong mundo.","translation":"As a person **fond of traveling**, it is her dream to go around the world."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sandali ng pagkawala ng pokus o atensyon na karaniwang nagreresulta sa pagkakamali o aksidente.
etymology: Root word 'lingat' means inattention or being distracted.
original_explanation: This is that split-second you look at your phone while walking and suddenly trip on a crack in the pavement. It's the moment your attention drifts in a Zoom meeting and your boss calls your name. Pagkalingat is the mortal enemy of anyone cooking fried fish—one moment of distraction and you've got charcoal. It's a small lapse with potentially big 'ay, patay!' consequences.
usage_notes: Refers to a brief, momentary lapse in attention.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **pagkalingat** lang ng drayber, at nangyari na ang aksidente.","translation":"Just one **moment of inattention** from the driver, and the accident happened."},{"sentence":"Sa isang **pagkalingat** ay nawala ang kanyang pitaka sa mataong palengke.","translation":"In a **moment of distraction**, his wallet was lost in the crowded market."}]

translation: to somersault; to turn upside down
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-ikot ng katawan kung saan ang mga paa ay pumapaitaas habang ang ulo ay pumapababa; pagbaligtad ng posisyon.
original_explanation: Like a gymnast doing a flip, or what your life feels like when you get your sweldo and then see all your bills. Biglang baliktad ang mundo. It can be literal (acrobatics) or figurative (your budget after a 12.12 sale).
usage_notes: Can be used both literally for physical action and figuratively for a situation being completely inverted.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng bata na **magbalintuwad** sa kama ngunit pinigilan siya ng kanyang ina.","translation":"The child tried to **somersault** on the bed but was stopped by his mother."},{"sentence":"Tila **nagbalintuwad** ang kanyang mundo nang malaman niya ang katotohanan.","translation":"It seemed his world **turned upside down** when he learned the truth."}]

translation: to uproot, to pull out completely
meaning_filipino: Ang pandiwa ng pagbunot sa isang bagay mula sa pagkakatanim o pagkakabaon nang buo at may kasamang lakas, kasama ang mga ugat nito.
original_explanation: This isn't just 'bunutin' (to pull out). This is pulling something out with force, roots and all. Imagine you're clearing out weeds ('damo') in the garden, and you grab one and yank it out with all your might—that's **bugnusin**. It's an aggressive, complete removal. Metaphorically, it's what you want to do with bad habits or toxic memories.
usage_notes: Implies force and completeness, often used for plants or things firmly embedded in the ground. It has a stronger and more violent connotation than 'bunutin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **bugnusin** ang mga damo hanggang sa mga ugat nito para hindi na tumubo muli.","translation":"The weeds need to be **uprooted** down to their roots so they won't grow back."},{"sentence":"Parang **binugnos** ang puso ko nang iwan niya ako.","translation":"It felt like my heart was **ripped out** when he/she left me."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang alternatibong hagdanan na karaniwang nasa labas ng isang gusali, na nagsisilbing daanan palabas kung sakaling may sunog o ibang emerhensiya.
etymology: Isang parirala na binubuo ng "hagdan" (stairs), "takasan" (escape route), at "sunog" (fire).
original_explanation: 'Yan 'yung metal na hagdan sa labas ng mga lumang building sa pelikula kung saan nagaganap ang mga madramang tagpo o 'yung romantic na usapan. Sa totoong buhay, 'yan ang escape plan mo 'pag may sunog. 'Wag gawing tambayan o sampayan, please.
usage_notes: Isang compound noun. Karaniwang tinutukoy bilang "fire escape" kahit sa mga usapang Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat laging malinis at walang harang ang **hagdang takasan sa sunog**.","translation":"The **fire escape** should always be clean and unobstructed."},{"sentence":"Sumigaw siya mula sa **hagdang takasan sa sunog**.","translation":"He/She shouted from the **fire escape**."}]

meaning_filipino: Maraming ganot o himaymay na matigas at hindi kanais-nais kainin, karaniwan sa mga prutas o gulay.
etymology: From Tagalog 'ma-' (adjective prefix) + 'ganot' (tough fiber in plants).
original_explanation: This is the evil twin of 'maganit', but for fruits and root crops. It's that mango that has so many stringy fibers you spend more time picking them from your teeth than eating. Or the kamote (sweet potato) that's more fiber than flesh. A 'maganot' fruit is a textural nightmare.
usage_notes: Used to describe the texture of plants, fruits, and vegetables like old mangoes, sweet potatoes, or ginger.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ay, **maganot** itong manggang nabili ko sa palengke.","translation":"Oh, this mango I bought from the market is **fibrous**."},{"sentence":"Piliin mo ang kamote na hindi **maganot** para masarap gawing kamote cue.","translation":"Choose the sweet potato that isn't **fibrous** so it will be delicious when made into kamote cue."}]

translation: to be able to predict; to foretell
meaning_filipino: Ang magkaroon ng kakayahang sabihin o alamin ang isang bagay bago pa ito mangyari.
original_explanation: It's when your tita correctly guesses you're getting fat and asks, "May jowa ka na?" It's also when you correctly predict the plot twist in a teleserye or a movie. You don't need a crystal ball; sometimes, all you need is Marites-level observation skills or a good understanding of patterns. "Sabi ko na nga ba!" is your catchphrase.
usage_notes: Implies an ability, whether innate or learned, to see the future or guess correctly.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Walang sinuman ang **makahuhula** kung ano ang eksaktong mangyayari bukas.","translation":"No one can **predict** exactly what will happen tomorrow."},{"sentence":"**Nakahula** siya na si Anna ang mananalo sa patimpalak.","translation":"She was **able to predict** that Anna would win the contest."}]

meaning_filipino: Nauukol o may kinalaman sa Eukaristiya.
original_explanation: Basically, the adjective form of 'Eucharist'. If something is 'Eucharistic', it's related to that whole holy communion scene. Think Eucharistic adoration, Eucharistic congress... it's the official, high-level term you'd see on a church banner.
usage_notes: A very formal, religious term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng isang malaking Kongresong **Eukaristiko** sa Cebu.","translation":"A large **Eucharistic** Congress was held in Cebu."}]

translation: to look at something from a window; to peer at from above
