usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang saya-saya maglaro ng **luksung-tinik** noong bata pa kami.","translation":"It was so much fun to play **luksung-tinik** when we were kids."},{"sentence":"Nasagi niya ang 'tinik' kaya taya na siya sa **luksung-tinik**.","translation":"He touched the 'thorn', so now it's his turn to be 'it' in **luksung-tinik**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng alimasag (Portunus pelagicus) na nabubuhay sa dagat, may batik-batik at mas mapusyaw na kulay, at ang mga hulihang paa ay lapad na parang sagwan para sa paglangoy.
original_explanation: The more common, budget-friendly cousin of the alimango. You'll see this one swimming in the sea, not chilling in the mud. It's the "sakto lang" crab—still delicious, but not quite the "special occasion" vibe of the alimango. Its back legs are like little paddles!
usage_notes: Distinguished from 'alimango' by its habitat (sea), spotted/lighter shell, and paddle-like hind legs. Generally cheaper.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming nahuling **alimasag** ang mga mangingisda kaninang umaga.","translation":"The fishermen caught a lot of **blue crabs** this morning."},{"sentence":"Paborito kong ulam ang nilagang **alimasag** na may maraming bawang.","translation":"My favorite dish is boiled **blue crab** with lots of garlic."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagpapahid ng barnis sa isang bagay, karaniwan ay yari sa kahoy, upang ito ay protektahan at pakintabin.
original_explanation: That thing your dad does to the old wooden dining table to make it look brand new again. It's the final step in any DIY woodworking project that fills the house with a distinct chemical smell for a few days. Basically, giving wood its 'glow-up'.
usage_notes: Used in the context of carpentry, home improvement, and arts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magbarnis** ng sahig para magmukha itong bago.","translation":"We need to **varnish** the floor to make it look new."},{"sentence":"Tinuruan ako ng lolo ko kung paano **magbarnis** ng silya.","translation":"My grandfather taught me how to **varnish** a chair."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng mga luha sa mata; pagiging nasa kalagayan ng pag-iyak.
original_explanation: That state when you've just watched 'Hachiko' or 'Miracle in Cell No. 7.' Or when you see your ex with their new partner. Your face is literally wet with tears. Luhaan is the adjective for 'may luha' (has tears). It's the look of someone deep in their feels.
usage_notes: Describes the state of having tears on one's face, not necessarily the act of crying itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Luhaan** siyang nagpaalam sa kanyang pamilya sa airport.","translation":"She was **in tears** as she said goodbye to her family at the airport."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko siyang **luhaan** habang nanonood ng pelikula.","translation":"I saw him **teary-eyed** while watching the movie."}]

translation: the act of rummaging or searching thoroughly
meaning_filipino: Ang masinsinang paghahanap o paghalungkat sa isang lugar o lalagyan, na kadalasan ay nagdudulot ng gulo.
original_explanation: This is what your room looks like after you search for that one specific shirt you want to wear. It's the act of rummaging through a bag, a closet, or a drawer, turning everything upside down. Think of a customs officer searching your luggage or your mom looking for her missing reading glasses. That chaotic searching is **halikwat**.
usage_notes: The verb form is "halikwatin". Often has a slightly negative connotation of being messy or invasive.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang gulo ng kwarto ay resulta ng kanyang **halikwat** para sa nawawalang susi.","translation":"The mess in the room was a result of his **rummaging** for the missing key."},{"sentence":"Pagod na siya sa **halikwat** sa mga lumang dokumento.","translation":"He is tired of **searching thoroughly** through the old documents."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang senyales ng babala na nagpapahiwatig ng posibleng panganib, problema, o isang hindi kanais-nais na katangian sa isang tao o sitwasyon.
etymology: Isang direktang hiram na parirala mula sa Ingles na "red flag".
original_explanation: In the dating world, this is a giant, flashing, neon sign that screams "U-turn! Abort mission!" Does he hate dogs? Red flag. Does she say "all my exes are crazy"? Red flag. It's that gut feeling, that "something's not right" vibe you get. Listen to it, bes. It might just save you from a world of 'sana pala nakinig ako' moments.
usage_notes: Popular na termino sa modernong diskurso tungkol sa mga relasyon, trabaho, at iba pang sitwasyon sa buhay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para sa akin, **red flag** kapag hindi marunong rumespeto sa service crew ang isang tao.","translation":"For me, it's a **red flag** when a person doesn't know how to respect service crew."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko agad ang mga **red flag** sa kanya, pero binalewala ko.","translation":"I saw the **red flags** in him right away, but I ignored them."}]

meaning_filipino: Isa sa tatlong pangunahing pangkat ng mga pulo sa Pilipinas, kasama ang Luzon at Mindanao. Binubuo ito ng maraming isla, kabilang ang Panay, Negros, Cebu, Bohol, Leyte, at Samar.
etymology: From Spanish 'Visayas', possibly from the name of the Srivijaya empire.
original_explanation: The heart of the Philippines! Home to the best beaches (Boracay, Palawan - yes, often grouped with them), the sweetest mangoes, and the Sinulog festival. Kung taga-Luzon ka, ito 'yung lugar na pinapangarap mong puntahan for that ultimate beach getaway. Kung taga-Visayas ka, you're living the dream (and probably have a very distinct, charming accent).
usage_notes: Always capitalized as it is a proper noun. Refers to the region and the people from it (Visayan or Bisaya).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming magagandang isla ang matatagpuan sa **Visayas**.","translation":"Many beautiful islands can be found in the **Visayas**."},{"sentence":"Pupunta kami sa Cebu, na bahagi ng **Visayas**, para sa Sinulog Festival.","translation":"We are going to Cebu, which is part of the **Visayas**, for the Sinulog Festival."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay o sistema na ginawa upang maibenta bilang isang kalakal. Ito ang resulta ng isang proseso ng paggawa o produksyon.
original_explanation: Ito yung tinitinda mo sa Shopee o Lazada. Yung binibili mo sa 12.12 sale kahit hindi mo kailangan. Ang produkto ay maaaring sabon, pagkain, o kahit yung "brilliant business idea" mo na hindi mo pa nasisimulan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming bagong **produkto** ang inilunsad ng kumpanya para sa Pasko.","translation":"The company launched many new **products** for Christmas."},{"sentence":"Ang gatas ng kalabaw ay isang pangunahing **produkto** ng aming probinsya.","translation":"Carabao's milk is a primary **product** of our province."}]

translation: To say or do in English
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasabi o pagpapahayag ng isang bagay gamit ang wikang Ingles; ang pagkilos o pagsasalita sa paraang Ingles.
original_explanation: "Uy, i-English-in mo para mas professional pakinggan." It's the act of switching to English to explain something complex, to sound more authoritative, or simply because you can't find the right Tagalog word. It's the code-switcher's ultimate power move.
usage_notes: A colloquial verb indicating the use of the English language.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **inglisin**, nasa Pilipinas tayo!","translation":"Don't **speak to me in English**, we're in the Philippines!"},{"sentence":"**Ininglis** niya ang kanyang ulat para maunawaan ng mga dayuhang bisita.","translation":"He **delivered his report in English** so the foreign visitors could understand."}]

translation: for rationing; intended as a ration
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa bagay, karaniwang pagkain, na inilaan upang ipamahagi nang may takdang dami o bilang.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `pan-` na nagiging `panr-` dahil sa asimilasyon sa salitang-ugat na `rasyon`, na hiram sa Espanyol na `ración`.
original_explanation: This is the adjective for the ayuda you get during a crisis. That can of sardines and pack of instant noodles? That's `pagkaing panrasyon`. It means it's meant to be distributed and portioned out, so 'wag mo ubusin lahat in one sitting!
usage_notes: Naglalarawan sa isang bagay na bahagi ng isang rasyon o pamamahagi.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga de-latang ito ay **panrasyon** para sa mga naapektuhan ng bagyo.","translation":"These canned goods are **for rationing** to those affected by the typhoon."},{"sentence":"Naghihintay ang mga tao para sa kanilang bigas na **panrasyon**.","translation":"The people are waiting for their rice **ration**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginagamit bilang pang-ugnay upang ipahiwatig ang pagkakasunod-sunod ng mga pangyayari; pagkatapos ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: The ultimate filler word when telling a story to your friends. It's the 'and then...' or 'like...' of chismis. 'Kumain kami, tapos nanood kami ng sine, tapos nag-away kami, tapos ayun, single na ulit ako.'
usage_notes: A very common conversational connector, often used to string clauses and events together in a narrative. Can also be a conjunction ('pangatnig').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-aral ka muna, **tapos** pwede ka nang maglaro.","translation":"Study first, **then** you can play."},{"sentence":"Nagkape ako, **tapos** naligo, **tapos** pumasok sa trabaho.","translation":"I had coffee, **then** I took a shower, **and then** I went to work."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang batang lalaking utusan o katulong.
original_explanation: This is some serious historical drama-level vocab. Think of the alalay of a rich haciendero in a period film. Today, you'd probably only hear this from your lola or when watching a Maria Clara at Ibarra-type series. It's the male version of 'mutsatsa'.
usage_notes: Medyo luma na ang termino at maaaring ituring na may mababang konotasyon sa modernong panahon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan ng don ang kanyang **mutsatso** na ihanda ang karwahe.","translation":"The don ordered his **male servant** to prepare the carriage."}]

meaning_filipino: Halaga ng salapi o bagay na hiniram na may kasunduang ibabalik sa takdang panahon, na maaaring may kasamang interes.
etymology: From the pa- prefix (to cause/allow) + utang (debt).
original_explanation: That thing your friend asks for when it's almost 'petsa de peligro', and you become their favorite person... until it's time to pay it back. It's the foundation of many a 'bes, friendship over na ba tayo?' conversation.
usage_notes: Can refer to both the act of lending and the loan itself. The person lending money provides a 'pautang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-apply siya ng **pautang** sa bangko para sa negosyo.","translation":"She applied for a **loan** at the bank for her business."},{"sentence":"May **pautang** ba kayong walang interes?","translation":"Do you offer a **loan** with no interest?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagpapaikli ng pariralang "bawat isa," na tumutukoy sa bawat indibidwal sa isang grupo. Ginagamit sa pormal o pampanitikang konteksto.
original_explanation: The formal, almost poetic way of saying "bawat isa." You'd use this when writing a formal speech or a love letter, not when telling your friends "kanya-kanyang bayad." It’s the "to whom it may concern" version of "everyone."
usage_notes: Often found in older texts, literature, or formal speeches. It is a direct contraction of 'bawat isa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang utos ay para sa **balang** mamamayan ng bayan.","translation":"The order is for **every** citizen of the town."},{"sentence":"**Balang** isa sa kanila ay may dalang regalo.","translation":"**Each** one of them brought a gift."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan matatagpuan ang maraming yaman o kayamanan; isang pinagkukunan ng kasaganaan.
original_explanation: If 'yaman' is the treasure, 'yamanan' is the treasure chest or the treasure map's 'X' spot. It's the place where the wealth is concentrated. Think of the Bangko Sentral's gold reserves, a hidden pirate chest, or your rich *ninang's* bank account that you hope to inherit. It's the source, the motherlode.
usage_notes: The suffix '-an' here denotes a place or a repository of the root word 'yaman'. It is less common than 'kayamanan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayon sa alamat, may nakatagong **yamanan** ng mga pirata sa islang iyon.","translation":"According to legend, there is a hidden pirate **treasure trove** on that island."},{"sentence":"Ang karagatan ay isang malaking **yamanan** na dapat nating pangalagaan.","translation":"The ocean is a great **source of wealth** that we must protect."}]

translation: to cause to fall; to topple; to push over
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging sanhi ng pagkahulog, pagguho, o pagbagsak ng isang bagay o tao.
original_explanation: Like what you did to the Jenga tower when it was your turn. Or when you playfully push a friend into the pool. It can also be used for more serious things, like 'to plunge into poverty' (magbulid sa kahirapan). It's the act of pushing something over the edge.
usage_notes: Can be used both literally (to push something physically) and figuratively (to cause someone's downfall or to plunge into a state).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang malakas na hangin ang **nagbulid** sa puno ng saging.","translation":"The strong wind **toppled** the banana tree."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga maling desisyon ang **nagbulid** sa kanya sa kapahamakan.","translation":"His wrong decisions **plunged** him into disaster."}]

translation: to motivate, to persuade, to entice
meaning_filipino: Hikayatin o himukin ang isang tao na gawin ang isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pagbibigay ng insentibo, panghihikayat, o pang-aakit.
original_explanation: This is the art of convincing someone to do something. It's what your friend does to make you go out on a Friday night when you'd rather be a potato ('Tara na, libre ko first round!'). It's what ads do to make you buy things you don't need. It's the 'sales talk' of life.
usage_notes: Implies using persuasion or offering an incentive.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **ganyakin** ang mga botante sa pamamagitan ng matatamis na pangako.","translation":"He tried to **entice** the voters with sweet promises."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **ganyakin** ang mga empleyado upang mas maging produktibo sila.","translation":"Employees need to be **motivated** to become more productive."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halamang-gamot na may makakapal at matutubig na dahon na karaniwang ginagamit para sa buhok at balat.
original_explanation: The OG plantita's best friend. Before all those fancy Korean skincare products, your lola was already using sabila straight from the garden to fix everything from sunburns to bad hair days. It's nature's slimy, green, all-in-one beauty solution.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of traditional medicine and home remedies.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magpahid ka ng **sabila** sa anit mo para kumapal ang buhok mo.","translation":"Apply **aloe vera** on your scalp to make your hair thicker."},{"sentence":"Ang katas ng **sabila** ay mabisang lunas sa paso.","translation":"The juice of **aloe vera** is an effective remedy for burns."}]

translation: fallen flat on one's face; face down
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging padapa o pagbagsak na una ang mukha.
original_explanation: Ever seen someone trip and land face-first on the pavement? That's **subasob**. It's the physical manifestation of "epic fail". Parang 'yung pag-amin mo sa crush mo tapos nalaman mong may jowa na pala siya. Ayan, **subasob** ang puso mo.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a clumsy or forceful fall.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang pagmamadali, nadapa siya at **subasob** sa putikan.","translation":"In his great hurry, he tripped and fell **flat on his face** into the mud."},{"sentence":"Natagpuang **subasob** ang lasing sa tapat ng tindahan.","translation":"The drunk man was found lying **face down** in front of the store."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kusang-loob na pag-iwas sa pagkain, inumin, o pareho, sa loob ng isang takdang panahon, kadalasan para sa layuning panrelihiyon, pangkalusugan, o bilang protesta.
etymology: From `pag-` (gerund prefix) + `a` (euphonic liaison) + `ayuno` (from Spanish 'ayuno' meaning fast).
original_explanation: Before "intermittent fasting" became a trendy diet, Filipinos have been doing this for centuries, especially during Lent (Kwaresma). It's the act of willingly skipping meals, usually for religious reasons. Now, it's also what your gym-bro friend does, calling it IF, while dreaming of the samgyupsal they'll eat during their 'eating window'.
usage_notes: Strongly associated with religious observances like Lent for Catholics or Ramadan for Muslims.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pag-aayuno** ay isang mahalagang bahagi ng Kwaresma para sa mga Katoliko.","translation":"**Fasting** is an important part of Lent for Catholics."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niya ang **pag-aayuno** para sa mga benepisyo nito sa kalusugan.","translation":"He tried **fasting** for its health benefits."}]

translation: to start a machine; to make something run
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsisimula ng operasyon o pag-andar ng isang makina, sasakyan, o anumang kagamitang mekanikal o elektroniko.
original_explanation: This is the first thing a Grab driver does in the morning. It's what you do to the generator during a brownout. It's the 'turn on' button for anything with an engine or motor. 'Hindi ko mapagana' is the cry for help, while 'magpaandar' is the action of the one who knows how to fix it.
usage_notes: Specifically for machines, engines, or systems. For simple electronics, 'buksan' (to open/turn on) is more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mo munang **magpaandar** ng makina bago umalis.","translation":"You need to **start the engine** first before leaving."},{"sentence":"Sino ang marunong **magpaandar** nitong lumang aircon?","translation":"Who knows how to **make this old aircon run**?"}]

translation: to form; to assemble; to create
meaning_filipino: Pagsama-samahin ang mga bahagi, ideya, o sangkap upang makalikha ng isang kabuuan.
original_explanation: Like assembling IKEA furniture without the manual, or trying to **magbuo** a coherent thought before your first cup of coffee. It's the act of putting pieces together to make a whole, whether it's a committee, a puzzle, or a sentence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya silang **magbuo** ng isang samahan para sa mga mahilig sa libro.","translation":"They decided to **form** an organization for book lovers."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **magbuo** ng tiwala na minsan nang nasira.","translation":"It is difficult to **build** trust that has once been broken."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkalahatang tawag sa mga mamalyang primado, na karaniwang may buntot at mahusay umakyat ng puno.
etymology: Mula sa Malay na *ungka*. Ito ay isang doublet ng 'unggo'.
original_explanation: The go-to Filipino word for 'monkey'. It's what you call that cute animal that steals your banana at the zoo. It's also what your mom calls you and your siblings when you're being hyper and jumping on the furniture. "Para kayong mga **unggoy**!"
usage_notes: Ang pangkalahatan at pinakakaraniwang termino para sa 'monkey'. Maaari ring gamitin nang kolokyal upang ilarawan ang isang malikot o magaslaw na tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masayang pinapanood ng mga turista ang mga **unggoy** na naglalaro.","translation":"The tourists happily watched the **monkeys** playing."},{"sentence":"Tumigil ka sa kakatalon, para kang **unggoy**!","translation":"Stop jumping, you're like a **monkey**!"}]

translation: to set aside; to put away; to move aside
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-alis ng isang bagay sa daan; ang paglalagay ng isang bagay sa isang ligtas na lugar; ang pag-iipon o paglalaan.
original_explanation: The ultimate multi-tasking verb. You can magtabi (move aside) to let someone pass ('Tabi po!'). You can magtabi (put away) your laptop after a long day of WFH. Or you can magtabi (save/set aside) some of your sahod for your #iponchallenge. It's the verb of being organized and considerate.
usage_notes: A versatile verb whose specific meaning ('move aside', 'put away', or 'save') is highly dependent on context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **magtabi** ka muna para makadaan kami.","translation":"Please, **move aside** for a moment so we can pass."},{"sentence":"Sinimulan niyang **magtabi** ng pera para sa kanyang kinabukasan.","translation":"She started to **set aside** money for her future."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos gamitin, dapat **magtabi** kaagad ng mga laruan.","translation":"After using them, you should **put away** the toys immediately."}]

translation: to split in half; to cleave
meaning_filipino: Ang paghati sa isang buong bagay sa dalawang bahagi, karaniwan sa pamamagitan ng pagpukpok o paggamit ng matulis na kasangkapan.
original_explanation: What you do to a coconut (niyog) with a bolo knife, or what you do to the last piece of Jollibee chicken so you can share it with your friend (kahit labag sa loob mo). It's an act of division, whether for sharing or destruction.
usage_notes: Often used for hard objects like wood, coconuts, or rocks. Can also be used metaphorically for things like splitting a group.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magbiyak** ng kahoy para sa ating sigâ.","translation":"We need **to split** wood for our bonfire."},{"sentence":"Pinanood namin ang magsasaka na **magbiyak** ng niyog gamit ang itak.","translation":"We watched the farmer **split** a coconut using a bolo."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tagapagbalita sa telebisyon o radyo, karaniwang pangunahing tagapag-ulat sa isang programa ng balita.
original_explanation: The face of the news. Sila yung mga tito at tita (looking at you, Kuya Kim and Ate Korina) na nagbabasa ng balita sa TV every 6 PM, telling you about the latest traffic, political drama, and showbiz chismis. Not to be confused with the thing that stops a boat ('angkla').
usage_notes: A direct loanword from English, very common in media contexts. The Tagalog word for a boat's anchor is 'angkla'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang maging isang sikat na **anchor** sa telebisyon.","translation":"Her dream is to become a famous TV **anchor**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga **anchor** ng 'TV Patrol' ay iginagalang sa industriya.","translation":"The **anchors** of 'TV Patrol' are respected in the industry."}]

translation: to narrate; to recount; to tell a story
meaning_filipino: Ikuwento o ilahad nang may pagkakasunod-sunod ang mga pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is the official term for spilling the tea, but in a formal way. It’s what a witness does in court, what your lolo does when he talks about "noong panahon namin," or what you do when your friend asks, "So, anong nangyari sa date niyo?" It’s storytelling with a purpose, laying out the facts (or your version of them) from start to finish.
usage_notes: More formal than 'magkwento'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hayaan ninyo akong **magsalaysay** ng tunay na nangyari.","translation":"Allow me to **narrate** what truly happened."},{"sentence":"Ang nasasakdal ay handa nang **magsalaysay** sa harap ng hukom.","translation":"The accused is ready to **recount** his story before the judge."}]

translation: to envy someone; to be envious of one another
meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay na pagkakaroon ng damdaming hili o inggit sa isa't isa. Maaari rin itong tumukoy sa pagiging tudlaan ng inggit ng isang tao.
original_explanation: This is the group chat drama version of envy. Kapag nag-post si A ng new phone, maiinggit si B. Kapag nag-post si B ng new bag, maiinggit si C. At kapag nag-post si C ng vacation, maiinggit si A. It's a toxic cycle of 'sana all' and quiet resentment.
usage_notes: Can be used in a reciprocal sense ('naghihilian sila') or a directional sense ('hilian mo siya').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkakaroon ng **hilian** sa opisina dahil sa mga bonus.","translation":"Envy is spreading in the office because of the bonuses."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang **hilian** ang kapatid mo, may kanya-kanya kayong galing.","translation":"Don't **envy** your sibling anymore, you each have your own strengths."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong dalubhasa o bihasa sa pagpapatakbo ng isang aparato, lalo na ng isang prodyektor sa sinehan.
etymology: From Spanish `aparato` (apparatus) + `-ista` (suffix for a person associated with something).
original_explanation: The unsung hero of your movie date night back in the day. They're the person in that little room with the window, making sure the film runs smoothly. In a modern context, it could be the tech guy who knows how to operate the complicated AV system for your company presentation. A very specific, almost vintage job title.
usage_notes: A somewhat dated term, more common when film projectors were standard. Can be used more broadly for any operator of a complex machine.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **aparatista** sa lumang sinehan ay bihasa na sa kanyang trabaho.","translation":"The **projectionist** in the old cinema was an expert at his job."},{"sentence":"Tinawag nila ang **aparatista** para ayusin ang sound system.","translation":"They called the **operator** to fix the sound system."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghulog o paglaglag ng isang bagay sa ibabaw ng isa pa o sa isang partikular na lugar.
original_explanation: That moment of panic when you're carrying too many groceries and you accidentally drop the eggs on the floor. Or when your friend 'bagsakan ka ng problema' (drops their problems on you) right before your exam. It's the act of letting something fall, intentionally or not, onto a target.
usage_notes: The stress on the first syllable /BAG-sa-kan/ distinguishes it from the noun /bag-sa-KAN/ (wholesale market).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **bagsakan** ng libro ang mesa, baka mabasag.","translation":"Don't **drop** a book **on** the table, it might break."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagtigil sa paggalaw, pagkilos, o pag-usad.
original_explanation: What the jeepney driver does when you yell 'Para!'. It's what your internet connection does in the middle of an important Zoom meeting. It's the sudden, abrupt pause in life's regularly scheduled programming. 'Walang hinto' (non-stop) is how you describe the chika from your Marites neighbor.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a command, "Hinto!" (Stop!).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Biglang nagkaroon ng **hinto** sa daloy ng trapiko.","translation":"There was a sudden **stop** in the flow of traffic."},{"sentence":"**Hinto**! May dadaan na sasakyan.","translation":"**Stop**! A car is passing."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halamang namumulaklak na may malalaki at makukulay na bulaklak, kilala bilang dahlia.
original_explanation: 'Yung bulaklak na parang 'yung gupit ng nanay mo noong '90s—puffy at maraming layers. Popular sa mga garden ng tita at lola, at pangalan din ng karakter sa mga lumang pelikula.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Namumukadkad na ang mga **dalya** sa hardin ni Lola.","translation":"The **dahlias** in Grandma's garden are now in full bloom."},{"sentence":"Binigyan niya ako ng isang pumpon ng mga pulang **dalya**.","translation":"He gave me a bouquet of red **dahlias**."}]

translation: to fluster, to rattle, to confuse
meaning_filipino: Gawing mataranta, maguluhan, o malito ang isang tao, lalo na sa ilalim ng pressure o sa isang biglaang sitwasyon.
etymology: Mula sa salitang "taranta" na hango sa Espanyol na "atarantar" (to daze or stun).
original_explanation: This is what happens when your boss asks for a report "ASAP," your crush suddenly messages you "we need to talk," and your internet dies all at the same time. You get flustered. 'Tarantahin' is the act of *causing* that panic. It's the favorite tactic of terror profs during oral exams. "Huwag mo akong tarantahin!" is the battle cry of someone trying to keep their cool.
usage_notes: Often used in the imperative form "Huwag mo akong tarantahin" (Don't fluster me).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan siyang **tarantahin** ng abogado sa pamamagitan ng sunod-sunod na tanong.","translation":"The lawyer tried to **fluster** her with a series of rapid-fire questions."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi kita **tatarantahin** sa iyong presentasyon.","translation":"Don't worry, I won't **rattle** you during your presentation."}]

translation: head; upper part; source (of a river)
meaning_filipino: Ang itaas na bahagi o pinagmulan ng isang bagay, tulad ng ilog; ang dulo na kabaligtaran ng wawa o bunganga.
original_explanation: The 'start here' point. Think of it as the upstream part of a river, the opposite of downstream where all the drama (and sometimes trash) collects. It can also mean the 'head' of a town, the part that's farther inland. It's the origin story before things get complicated.
usage_notes: Often contrasted with 'wawa' (river mouth).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagmula ang baha sa **hulo** ng ilog dahil sa malakas na ulan sa kabundukan.","translation":"The flood came from the **source of the river** because of heavy rain in the mountains."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aalok ng sariling serbisyo o tulong nang kusa at walang inaasahang kabayaran.
original_explanation: To offer your time, skills, or effort for free. Like when you join a coastal cleanup, help out at an animal shelter, or get "volun-told" by your manager to organize the Christmas party.
usage_notes: The root word 'boluntaryo' can be a noun (a volunteer) or an adjective (voluntary).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming kabataan ang **nagboluntaryo** para tumulong sa mga nasalanta ng bagyo.","translation":"Many young people **volunteered** to help the typhoon victims."},{"sentence":"Sino ang gustong **magboluntaryo** na maglinis ng silid-aralan?","translation":"Who wants **to volunteer** to clean the classroom?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kataga na nagpapahiwatig ng pagbibigay-diin, pag-aalinlangan, konsesyon, o pagiging pangkalahatan (hal. sino man, ano man).
original_explanation: This is the 'kahit ano na' or 'pwede na rin' particle of Tagalog. It's a tiny word that adds a universe of meaning. 'Sino?' (Who?) vs 'Sino man?' (Whoever?). It adds a layer of 'I'm open to possibilities,' 'even if,' or 'just in case.' It's the verbal equivalent of a shrug emoji sometimes. 'Okay man lang' - It's just okay, not great, not terrible. It's the ultimate hedge.
usage_notes: A versatile particle that often combines with question words (sino man, ano man, kailan man) or is used to soften a statement or express a concession.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit sino **man** ang dumating, handa kami.","translation":"Whoever **ever** comes, we are ready."},{"sentence":"Maganda **man** ang plano, mahirap pa ring isagawa.","translation":"**Although** the plan is good, it's still difficult to execute."},{"sentence":"Okay ka lang ba? Oo, okay lang **man**.","translation":"Are you okay? Yeah, I'm okay, I guess."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng mga guhit o tupi-tupi dahil sa pagkakapiga, pagkakayupi, o pagtanda.
original_explanation: This is the state of your uniform when you wake up 5 minutes before your alarm. Or your bedsheet after a long night of 'Netflix and chill.' Or your face after an all-nighter finishing a report. Anything that's not smooth and needs some serious 'plantsa' (ironing) is lukot.
usage_notes: Can refer to fabric, paper, or skin. Often used interchangeably with 'gusot'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang isuot ang damit dahil **lukot** ito.","translation":"He doesn't want to wear the shirt because it is **wrinkled**."},{"sentence":"Nakita ang pagod sa kanyang **lukot** na noo.","translation":"The exhaustion was visible on his **wrinkled** forehead."}]

meaning_filipino: Kabayaran para sa pinsala, danyos, o pagkakautang, na karaniwang iginagawad sa isang kontekstong legal, pampulitika, o pangkasaysayan.
original_explanation: This is the official term for 'sorry money.' It's not just an apology; it's an apology with a payment plan. Think of historical damages, legal settlements, or that time you broke your friend's limited-edition Funko Pop and had to pay for it. That's **reparasyon**.
usage_notes: Primarily used in formal, legal, or historical contexts. Less common in everyday conversation compared to 'bayad' or 'danyos'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga biktima ng digmaan ay humihingi ng **reparasyon** mula sa pamahalaan.","translation":"The war victims are demanding **reparation** from the government."},{"sentence":"Pinag-uusapan sa korte ang halaga ng **reparasyon** para sa nasirang ari-arian.","translation":"The amount of **compensation** for the damaged property is being discussed in court."}]

translation: to experience, to savor, to undergo
meaning_filipino: Ang maranasan nang malaliman ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay isang damdamin, kalagayan, o pangyayari.
etymology: From the root word 'lasap' (savor, experience) + the '-um-' infix.
original_explanation: This is more than just tasting; this is *experiencing* it with your whole being. It's when you finally get that promotion and you just sit there, savoring the moment. O 'yung pagod after a long week, 'di ba? You lumasap ng hirap. It’s to fully absorb an experience, good or bad.
usage_notes: Carries a deeper, more profound meaning than 'tikman' (to taste). It's about the full experience, often used for both hardship ('hirap') and pleasure ('sarap', 'tagumpay').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marami siyang **linasap** na hirap bago narating ang tagumpay.","translation":"He **experienced** a lot of hardship before achieving success."},{"sentence":"Hayaan mong **lumasap** ang bata ng kaunting kalayaan.","translation":"Let the child **savor** a little bit of freedom."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na paghahain ng reklamo o kaso laban sa isang tao o entidad sa hukuman.
original_explanation: Ito yung moment na hindi na kaya ng 'usap tayo' at kailangan nang dalhin sa korte. Parang yung chismis na naging legal battle. From barangay hall to the Supreme Court, ito na yung 'See you in court!' moment mo.
usage_notes: Maaari ring tumukoy sa lugar kung saan isinasampa ang kaso, tulad ng korte.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghain sila ng **sakdalan** laban sa kumpanya dahil sa hindi tamang pasahod.","translation":"They filed a **lawsuit** against the company for improper wages."},{"sentence":"Ang **sakdalan** ay umabot na sa korte suprema.","translation":"The **legal complaint** has already reached the supreme court."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na alpombra o piraso ng karpet na inilalatag sa sahig bilang palamuti o pampunas ng paa.
etymology: From Spanish "carpeta" (folder), with meaning influenced by English "carpet".
original_explanation: The mini-me of a 'karpet'. It's that small rug you put by the door or under a coffee table to add a bit of ~aesthetic~ or to trap dirt before it gets all over the house.
usage_notes: Often smaller than a 'karpet'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipagpag mo muna ang **karpeta** sa labas.","translation":"Shake the **rug** outside first."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang hayop na walang buntot o may putol na buntot. Maaari ring ilarawan ang isang bagay na mas maikli kaysa sa karaniwan.
original_explanation: That dog or cat with a stumpy, non-existent, or cut tail. It's the animal equivalent of being 'putol' but specifically for tails. Can also be used to describe someone who's short or stumpy, but that might be a bit rude, so use with caution unless you're talking about your corgi.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit para sa mga hayop. Ang paggamit nito para sa mga tao ay maaaring ituring na nakakainsulto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aso namin ay **putot**, mula pa noong ipinanganak ito.","translation":"Our dog is **tailless**, ever since it was born."},{"sentence":"May alagang manok na **putot** si Mang Teban.","translation":"Mang Teban has a **tailless** chicken."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagsubok o pagtatanghal na isinasagawa ng isang nagnanais maging artista, mang-aawit, o mananayaw upang ipakita ang kanyang talento at maging kwalipikado para sa isang papel o pagganap.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "audición" o Ingles na "audition".
original_explanation: The Pinoy Big Brother or Starstruck moment for aspiring talents. It's the ultimate 'show what you've got' challenge where you sing your heart out, act your 'hugot' scenes, or dance like nobody's watching... except for the three very judgmental-looking judges in front of you.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumila siya nang mahaba para sa **odisyon** ng bagong teleserye.","translation":"He lined up for a long time for the **audition** of the new TV series."},{"sentence":"Kinakabahan ako sa aking **odisyon** para sa aawiting papel sa dula.","translation":"I am nervous about my **audition** for the singing role in the play."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpapahayag ng isang malakas na damdamin, lalo na ang galit o pagkadismaya, sa isang hindi napipigilang paraan.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na 'vent', na nangangahulugang magbigay-daan sa paglabas ng hangin o emosyon.
original_explanation: This is what you do with your bestie over coffee (or a video call at 2 AM) when your boss is being unreasonable or when you're going through some major 'sana all' moments. It's basically an emotional data dump. 'Friend, I need to vent, puno na ako!'
usage_notes: Ginagamit bilang pandiwa, madalas sa anyong 'mag-vent'. Ito ay isang impormal na termino na popular sa mga nakababatang henerasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong mag-**vent** tungkol sa araw ko, grabe ang stress.","translation":"I need to **vent** about my day, the stress is unbelievable."},{"sentence":"Ligtas na lugar ang aming grupo para mag-**vent** nang walang panghuhusga.","translation":"Our group is a safe space to **vent** without judgment."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lugar na tinitirhan o tinatahanan ng mga tao, hayop, o anumang nilalang.
etymology: A complex verb form from the root 'tirahan' (residence), which itself comes from 'tira' (to live/stay), indicating the place where one resides.
original_explanation: The place you call home. Whether it's a condo in BGC, your lola's house in the province, or that specific spot on the couch that's yours and yours alone. It's the space where you exist, pay bills, and hoard Shopee deliveries.
usage_notes: A formal term for 'tinitirhan.' Often used in documentaries or formal writing about populations or ecology.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lumang bahay na iyon ay **pinaninirahanan** na raw ng mga multo.","translation":"That old house is said to be **inhabited** by ghosts now."},{"sentence":"Ang kagubatang ito ay **pinaninirahanan** ng maraming pambihirang uri ng ibon.","translation":"This forest **is inhabited by** many rare species of birds."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matinding puna o pagtuligsa sa isang tao, bagay, o gawain.
original_explanation: This isn't just feedback; this is the 'cancel culture' kind of criticism. The comments section of a political post? Puro batikos 'yan. It’s the heavy, often harsh, verbal smackdown you get for a mistake or an unpopular opinion.
usage_notes: Carries a strong, negative connotation. Often used in political or social commentary.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umani ng **batikos** ang bagong panukala mula sa mga mamamayan.","translation":"The new bill garnered **criticism** from the citizens."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya pinansin ang mga **batikos** at nagpatuloy sa kanyang ginagawa.","translation":"He ignored the **criticisms** and continued with what he was doing."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian na tumutukoy sa kakulangan ng linaw sa paningin, larawan, tubig, o pag-iisip.
etymology: Mula sa Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *labuʀ na nangangahulugang 'malabo, maulap'.
original_explanation: Yung picture niyo ng ex mo na gusto mo nang burahin pero di mo magawa. O yung sagot niya nung tinanong mo kung 'kayo na ba?' — 'it's complicated.' Ganyan ka-labo. Pwede ring tubig-baha sa EDSA pagkatapos ng malakas na ulan. The opposite of HD.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin para ilarawan ang paningin, tubig, mga larawan, o mga sitwasyon at relasyon na mahirap unawain.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Labo** ng kuha ng camera mo, 'tol.","translation":"The shot from your camera is **blurry**, bro."},{"sentence":"Ang **labo** naman ng usapan natin, hindi ko maintindihan.","translation":"Our conversation is so **vague**, I can't understand it."}]

meaning_filipino: Nauukol sa mga ngipin o sa dentistri.
original_explanation: Anything and everything about your teeth. Dental check-up, dental floss, dental clinic. Ito 'yung paalala na kailangan mong mag-toothbrush at mag-floss, kung hindi, magiging horror story ang susunod mong dental appointment.
usage_notes: Almost always used before a noun, as in "dental clinic" or "dental hygiene".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang regular na **dental** check-up para sa kalusugan.","translation":"Regular **dental** check-ups are important for health."},{"sentence":"Naghahanap ako ng magandang **dental** clinic na malapit dito.","translation":"I'm looking for a good **dental** clinic near here."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang pamalit o pantawag sa isang tao, bagay, lugar, o pangyayari na pansamantalang hindi maalala o ayaw tukuyin ang tiyak na pangalan.
etymology: Origin uncertain. It functions as a universal placeholder in colloquial speech.
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino filler word. It's our version of 'um,' 'uh,' 'like,' 'whatchamacallit,' and 'you-know-who' all rolled into one. Use it when your brain is buffering or when you're trying to talk about chismis without naming names. 'Si kuwan kasi... ayun, nakita ko kasama si kuwan!'
usage_notes: Extremely common in informal spoken Tagalog. Its meaning is entirely dependent on context and non-verbal cues. Sometimes spelled as 'kwan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakikuha mo nga 'yung **kuwan** sa ibabaw ng mesa.","translation":"Can you please get the **whatchamacallit** on the table?"},{"sentence":"Nagkita kami ni **kuwan** kahapon sa mall.","translation":"I saw **so-and-so** at the mall yesterday."},{"sentence":"Ang gagawin mo ay, **kuwan**, ihalo mo muna ang harina at asukal.","translation":"What you'll do is, **uhm**, mix the flour and sugar first."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang kapayapaan; magulo ang isip o damdamin; laging may alalahanin o kaguluhan.
original_explanation: Your mind at 3 AM thinking about all your life choices, that awkward thing you said in 2015, and whether you locked the door. It’s a state of mental gulo, like EDSA on a payday Friday. Your inner peace has left the chat.
usage_notes: Often refers to an internal state of mind or emotion, but can also describe a situation or place.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **di-mapayapa** ang kanyang pagtulog dahil sa masamang panaginip.","translation":"His sleep became **unpeaceful** because of a bad dream."},{"sentence":"Ang isip niya ay **di-mapayapa** sa kaiisip sa mga problema.","translation":"Her mind is **troubled** from thinking too much about problems."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng hindi pagiging maingat; kapabayaan o pagwawalang-bahala na nagreresulta sa pinsala o pagkakamali.
original_explanation: The reason why your phone screen is cracked. The 'bahala na' attitude applied to handling fragile items or sensitive information. It's forgetting to save your work before a brownout, or leaving your bag unzipped on the MRT. Basically, inviting disaster.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aksidente ay bunga ng **kawalang-ingat** ng drayber.","translation":"The accident was a result of the driver's **carelessness**."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **kawalang-ingat**, nawala ang mahahalagang dokumento.","translation":"Because of his **negligence**, the important documents were lost."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malamig na inumin na karaniwang gawa sa gatas, ice cream, o mga prutas na pinaghalo-halo sa pamamagitan ng blender.
original_explanation: The ultimate pampalamig on a hot Manila day. Whether it's the classic fruit shake from the palengke stall or the fancy ones from a cafe, it's the drink that makes you go "Ahhh." The perfect partner for fishball and kikiam after a long day of walking.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively refers to the beverage (fruit shake, milkshake). The verb 'to shake' is usually translated as 'alog' or 'yugyog'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pabili po ng isang large na mango **shake**.","translation":"Can I buy one large mango **shake**, please?"},{"sentence":"Masarap ang avocado **shake** nila dito, try mo.","translation":"Their avocado **shake** here is delicious, you should try it."}]

translation: to make a raft; to travel by raft
meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa o paggamit ng balsa, isang simpleng sasakyang pantubig na karaniwang gawa sa mga pinagdugtong-dugtong na kawayan o kahoy.
original_explanation: This is your OG provincial life hack for crossing a river when there's no bridge. Think Tom Hanks in 'Cast Away' but with bamboo. It's about building something simple to get you from point A to point B on water.
usage_notes: Associated with rural or provincial settings, or flood situations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya silang **magbalsa** upang makatawid sa ilog.","translation":"They decided to **travel by raft** to cross the river."},{"sentence":"Mabilis na **nagbalsa** ang mga residente gamit ang mga lumang drum at kawayan noong bumaha.","translation":"The residents quickly **made a raft** using old drums and bamboo when it flooded."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maliit at makintab na kabibi (seashell), na karaniwang ginagamit bilang palamuti o, noong unang panahon, bilang isang uri ng salapi.
original_explanation: Before GCash and credit cards, there was sagay. These were the OG coins of the sea, used for trade. Today, they're the shiny little things you see glued onto picture frames, keychains, and other beach-themed souvenirs from Boracay or Palawan. They're the puka shell's more sophisticated cousin.
usage_notes: Also the name of a city in Negros Occidental, famous for its marine reserves.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumawa siya ng kwintas mula sa mga kabibing **sagay**.","translation":"She made a necklace from **cowrie** shells."}]

translation: to be hindered; to be obstructed
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng hadlang, sagabal, o balakid na pumipigil sa pag-usad o pagpapatuloy ng isang gawain o layunin.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're about to leave work on a Friday, and your boss says "Uh, one more thing..." That's you getting 'mabalakid'. It's any obstacle—slow internet, EDSA traffic, a chismosa neighbor—that gets in the way of your goals.
usage_notes: More formal and literary than its common synonyms "mahadlangan" or "masagabal".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag nating hayaang **mabalakid** ng takot ang ating mga pangarap.","translation":"Let's not allow our dreams **to be hindered** by fear."},{"sentence":"**Nababalakid** ang proyekto dahil sa kakulangan ng pondo.","translation":"The project **is being obstructed** due to lack of funds."}]

translation: to have money; to become wealthy
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtataglay o pagkakaroon ng pera o yaman sa sapat o higit pang dami.
original_explanation: The ultimate goal after every 'sahod-ay-buhay' cycle. It's the state of having money. Not just 'may pera,' but really *having* money. The opposite of petsa de peligro. Sana lahat tayo **magkasalapi** para 'di na puro 'sana all'.
usage_notes: More formal or emphatic than 'magkapera'. 'Salapi' itself is a more formal word for 'pera' (money).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsusumikap siya para **magkasalapi** at matulungan ang kanyang pamilya.","translation":"He is working hard **to have money** and help his family."},{"sentence":"Sino ba ang ayaw **magkasalapi** sa panahong ito?","translation":"Who doesn't want **to be wealthy** in this day and age?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapanggap o pagpapakita ng isang bagay na hindi totoo; pag-arte o pagsasabuhay ng isang sitwasyon.
original_explanation: This is the more neutral, "let's pretend" version. Think kids playing bahay-bahayan. "Okay, pagkukunwa ko nanay ka tapos ako yung anak." It's role-playing, simulation, or acting something out for practice or play. It's less about deceiving someone (like its cousin, pagkukunwari) and more about creating a scenario. It's the "what if" game in noun form.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with `pagkukunwari`, but `pagkukunwa` can have a more neutral or even positive connotation (like in acting or simulation), while `pagkukunwari` almost always implies deceit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanilang laro ay isang **pagkukunwa** na sila ay mga doktor at pasyente.","translation":"Their game was a **simulation** where they were doctors and patients."},{"sentence":"Sa pamamagitan ng **pagkukunwa**, sinasanay ang mga piloto sa iba't ibang sitwasyon ng paglipad.","translation":"Through **simulation**, pilots are trained in various flight situations."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang balangkas o pagkakasunod-sunod ng mga posibleng mangyari sa isang sitwasyon, dula, o pelikula.
original_explanation: It's the 'what if' game we play in our heads. 'What if 'di siya nag-reply? May iba na ba siya?' That whole drama you just created in your mind? 'Yan ang senaryo. It's also the script for a movie, but let's be real, we use it more for our love life anxieties.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa pinakamasamang **senaryo**, maaaring mawalan tayo ng kuryente.","translation":"In the worst-case **scenario**, we might lose power."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng direktor ang bawat **senaryo** sa kanyang pelikula.","translation":"The director is studying every **scenario** in his film."}]

meaning_filipino: May kakayahang ibalik ang isang bagay sa dati nitong kinalalagyan, may-ari, o kalagayan.
etymology: From `ma-` (potential prefix) + `isauli` (to return something). The root is `uli` (again, return).
original_explanation: The feeling you get when you find the ₱1000 bill you thought you lost in your jeans. "Yes, maisauli ko na utang ko kay beshie!" It's the potential to return something, whether it's a borrowed book, a lost wallet, or your dignity after a karaoke fail.
usage_notes: Often used for returning borrowed or lost items. It implies the ability or possibility of returning something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **maisauli** mo ang hiniram mong libro bago ang takdang araw.","translation":"I hope you **can return** the book you borrowed before the due date."},{"sentence":"Hindi na **maisauli** sa dati ang nasirang tiwala.","translation":"Broken trust **cannot be returned** to its former state."}]

meaning_filipino: Putol o tabas na resulta ng isang mabilis at malakas na hiwa, karaniwang ginagamitan ng itak o katulad na kasangkapan.
original_explanation: Think of a provincial tito expertly cutting down a banana tree with one clean swing of his bolo knife. That's tigpas. It’s a swift, decisive cut. In a hugot context, it's how you wish you could sever ties with a toxic ex—isang tigpas lang, tapos na.
usage_notes: Implies a swift, clean cut, often with a bladed tool like a bolo or machete. Can also be a noun ('ang tigpas').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tigpas** ang ulo ng manok matapos itong tagain ng magsasaka.","translation":"The chicken's head was **severed** after the farmer chopped it."},{"sentence":"Isang maling galaw lang at baka ma**tigpas** ang daliri mo ng makinang iyan.","translation":"One wrong move and your finger might get **cut off** by that machine."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-usad sa pamamagitan ng paggapang; o ang sapilitang paghipo sa katawan ng iba nang walang pahintulot.
original_explanation: This word has two main vibes. The literal one: you're a baby learning to crawl, or you're in a horror movie, crawling away from the monster. The much darker, more common one: the act of a 'manyakis' on a crowded MRT. It's the unwanted, creepy touching that is a form of harassment. A word that instantly makes you want to shout 'Kadiri!'
usage_notes: The meaning of 'to grope' (sexual harassment) is more common in modern urban context than 'to crawl'. Context is crucial.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-iingat ang mga babae sa siksikang lugar upang hindi **manggapang**.","translation":"Women are careful in crowded places to avoid being **groped**."},{"sentence":"Kinailangan niyang **manggapang** sa dilim para hanapin ang switch ng ilaw.","translation":"He had **to feel his way by crawling** in the dark to find the light switch."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang yugto ng buhay sa pagitan ng pagkabata at pagiging ganap na may sapat na gulang, na kinabibilangan ng mga pagbabagong pisikal, emosyonal, at panlipunan.
original_explanation: The "awkward stage." That time in your life filled with pimples, first crushes, identity crises, and arguing with your parents that "it's not a phase, mom!" It's the era of high school drama, barkada hangouts, and figuring out who you are, one cringey moment at a time.
usage_notes: A formal or academic term. People are more likely to say "teenager" or "kabataan" in casual conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang gabay ng magulang sa yugto ng **adolesens**.","translation":"Parental guidance is important during the stage of **adolescence**."},{"sentence":"Ang pagrerebelde ay karaniwang bahagi ng **adolesens**.","translation":"Rebellion is a common part of **adolescence**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang seremonya o ritwal na hudyat ng pagtatapos ng panahon ng pagluluksa para sa isang yumaong mahal sa buhay, karaniwang ginagawa matapos ang ika-40 araw o unang anibersaryo ng pagkamatay.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng "baba" (ibig sabihin ay alisin o tapusin) at "luksa" (pagdadalamhati).
original_explanation: This is the Filipino tradition of formally ending the mourning period. It's when the family stops wearing black, holds a final prayer service, and celebrates the life of the person who passed. It's a bittersweet gathering—a mix of "we miss you" and "it's time to move forward."
usage_notes: A specific cultural term related to Filipino funeral and mourning customs.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkakaroon ng kainan sa bahay para sa **babaang-luksa** ni Lolo.","translation":"There will be a meal at the house for the **end of the mourning period** for Grandpa."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng **babaang-luksa**, maaari na silang magsuot ng makukulay na damit.","translation":"After the **end of the mourning period**, they can now wear colorful clothes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bulalas na nagpapahayag ng pagkagulat, pagkadismaya, o pagkainis.
etymology: Pinaniniwalaang isang eupemismo mula sa Espanyol na 'demonios' (demons) o 'dios' (God).
original_explanation: Expression ng lola mo kapag may narinig siyang chismis o kapag nabasag mo yung paborito niyang plato. It's the G-rated version of a curse word, full of vintage flair. The 'Hala!' or 'Naku!' of a bygone era.
usage_notes: Itinuturing na medyo luma na, ngunit ginagamit pa rin para sa komikong epekto o ng mga nakatatanda.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Diantres!** Nakalimutan ko ang aking pitaka!","translation":"**Darn!** I forgot my wallet!"},{"sentence":"**Diantres** ka, bata ka! Saan ka na naman nanggaling?","translation":"**Good heavens**, you child! Where have you been again?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang pansaka na hinihila ng kalabaw o traktora upang bungkalin ang lupa bilang paghahanda sa pagtatanim.
original_explanation: The OG farming tool. Think of the kalabaw's best friend (or worst enemy, depending on the day). It's the big, sharp thing that cuts through the soil, getting it ready for planting. It's the symbol of hard work and the agricultural backbone of the Philippines.
usage_notes: This is the noun for the tool. The verb is 'mag-araro' (to plow).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinihila ng kalabaw ang **araro** sa bukid.","translation":"The carabao pulls the **plow** in the field."},{"sentence":"Kinakalawang na ang lumang **araro** sa tabi ng kamalig.","translation":"The old **plow** beside the barn is already rusting."}]

meaning_filipino: Pahintulutan ang isang tao na maging bahagi ng isang grupo, gawain, o paligsahan.
original_explanation: When your barkada has a group chat and a new friend wants in, you tell the admin, "Pasalihan mo na si Mark." It's the act of officially adding someone to the circle of trust (or memes). This is for an activity or group.
usage_notes: Focuses on the activity or group being joined. Compare with 'pasalihin', which focuses on the person being made to join.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puwede bang **pasalihan** ang kaibigan ko sa laro ninyo?","translation":"Can my friend **be allowed to join** your game?"},{"sentence":"Sige, **pasalihan** na natin siya sa ating team.","translation":"Okay, let's **let him join** our team."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagdudulot ng pakiramdam ng pagduduwal o pagnanais na sumuka; lubhang kasuklam-suklam.
original_explanation: 'Yung amoy ng basurahan na 'di nakolekta for a week? Nakakasuka. 'Yung ugali ng officemate mong sipsip sa boss? Nakakasuka rin. It applies to both literal smells and figurative bad vibes.
usage_notes: "Nakakasuka" is stronger than "nakakahilo" (makes one dizzy). It can be used for physical disgust or moral revulsion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakakasuka** ang amoy mula sa kanal.","translation":"The smell from the canal is **nauseating**."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang pagtataksil ay isang **nakakasuka** na gawain.","translation":"His betrayal was a **sickening** act."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga maikling tala o sulatin na naglalaman ng impormasyon, paalala, o puna. Maaari ring tumukoy sa mga marka o grado sa paaralan sa mas lumang paggamit.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'notas', plural ng 'nota', na nangangahulugang 'tala' o 'marka'.
original_explanation: Before your iPhone had a Notes app, people used actual paper for 'notas'. It's a slightly more formal, almost vintage way of saying 'notes' or 'tala'. Parang 'yung lola mo, 'Pakita ng iyong mga notas sa klase, apo.' 'Di na masyadong maririnig sa mga Gen Z, na mas pamilyar sa 'notes' sa English or 'screenshot'.
usage_notes: Higit na karaniwan sa mga nakatatandang henerasyon o sa pormal na panitikan. Sa modernong Filipino, mas madalas gamitin ang 'tala' o ang hiniram na salitang Ingles na 'notes'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinuha ng kalihim ang mga **notas** ng pulong.","translation":"The secretary took the **notes** of the meeting."},{"sentence":"May ilang **notas** ang guro sa dulo ng aking sanaysay.","translation":"The teacher had a few **remarks** at the end of my essay."}]

meaning_filipino: Magkakaroon ng pagkakaintindihan o pagkakasang-ayon; magiging magkaibigan.
original_explanation: The rare, magical moment when everyone in the group chat agrees on where to eat. It's a miracle! Also, the hope of every parent when they introduce a new pet to the old one. 'Sana magkasundo sila.'
usage_notes: The root 'sundo' means 'to fetch', but in this conjugated form, it takes on the meaning of agreement or harmony.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa tingin mo ba, **magkakasundo** ang mga pusa at aso sa iisang bahay?","translation":"Do you think cats and dogs **will get along** in one house?"},{"sentence":"Kahit magkaiba kami ng gusto, umaasa akong **magkakasundo** kami sa huli.","translation":"Even if we want different things, I hope we **will agree** in the end."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang ginagamit sa pagtatanong ng dahilan o katwiran ng isang pangyayari, kilos, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: The official start of any 'Marites' session or a parent's interrogation. It's the one-word question that can either lead to a simple answer or a three-hour drama-filled explanation about your life choices. The prequel to 'kasi...'
usage_notes: Often shortened to 'ba't' in informal speech and text messages.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bakit** ka malungkot?","translation":"**Why** are you sad?"},{"sentence":"Hindi ko alam **bakit** ganito ang naramdaman ko.","translation":"I don't know **why** I feel this way."},{"sentence":"'**Ba't** ang traffic na naman?' tanong ng lahat ng nasa EDSA.","translation":"'**Why** is it traffic again?' asked everyone on EDSA."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang makabagong termino sa pakikipag-relasyon kung saan ang isang tao ay nagbibigay ng paunti-unting at hindi tuloy-tuloy na atensyon upang panatilihin ang pag-asa ng isa pa, nang walang tunay na intensyon na magkaroon ng seryosong ugnayan.
etymology: From English 'breadcrumbing', alluding to the fairy tale of Hansel and Gretel leaving a trail of breadcrumbs.
original_explanation: The dating equivalent of 'paasa'. This is when someone texts you 'good morning' one day, then ghosts you for a week, only to reappear by liking your IG story. They're dropping just enough 'crumbs' of attention to keep you interested, but never enough for a full meal (a real relationship). It's a low-effort way to keep their options open. Classic marupok-bait.
usage_notes: A modern dating slang term, often used in conversations about toxic relationship behaviors.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na 'yang kausap mo, halata namang **breadcrumbing** lang ang ginagawa sa'yo.","translation":"Stop talking to that person, it's obvious they're just **breadcrumbing** you."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging magkadikit o magkapatong ng mga palad, tulad ng sa pananalangin.
original_explanation: When you put your palms together like you're about to pray, do a 'mano po', or beg your boss for a vacation leave. It’s the universal sign of 'please,' 'thank you,' or 'I surrender.' Usually seen as 'magkadaop na palad'.
usage_notes: Often seen as 'magkadaop' (joined together) or 'nakadaop' (in a state of being joined). Primarily describes the joining of palms.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nanatiling **daop** ang kanyang mga palad habang taimtim na nagdarasal.","translation":"Her palms remained **clasped together** while praying solemnly."},{"sentence":"Lumuhod siya na **daop** ang mga palad bilang paghingi ng tawad.","translation":"He knelt with his palms **joined** as a plea for forgiveness."}]

translation: to lift from; to extract; to adapt
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkuha o pag-alis ng isang bagay mula sa kinalalagyan nito, lalo na mula sa likido, apoy, o isang mahirap na sitwasyon. Maaari ring tumukoy sa pagkuha ng ideya o akda mula sa isang orihinal na pinagmulan.
original_explanation: This is what you do to the fried chicken when it's golden brown—you 'hanguin' it from the hot oil. It's also what you do when you save a friend from a toxic relationship—you 'hanguin' them from their misery. In a literary sense, it's what happens when a movie is 'hango sa' a best-selling book. It’s the ultimate act of extraction, rescue, or adaptation.
usage_notes: Very versatile. Can be used in cooking, rescue situations, and for creative works. The preposition 'sa' is almost always used to indicate the source.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **hanguin** mo na ang sinaing.","translation":"Please **get** the cooked rice from the stove."},{"sentence":"Ang pelikula ay **hango** sa isang sikat na nobela.","translation":"The movie is **adapted** from a famous novel."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **hanguin** ang kaibigan sa pagkakalugmok.","translation":"He tried to **lift** his friend from despair."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ikawalong buwan ng taon sa kalendaryong Gregorian, na mayroong 31 araw.
original_explanation: The ghost month for some, Buwan ng Wika for all Filipino students. It's that time of the year you suddenly have to wear a baro't saya for a school program and speak deep Tagalog. It's also the month where the rains get serious, like 'may pasok ba?' serious.
usage_notes: Always capitalized as it is a proper noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagdiriwang ang Buwan ng Wika tuwing **Agosto**.","translation":"The National Language Month is celebrated every **August**."},{"sentence":"Ang kaarawan niya ay sa ika-dalawampu ng **Agosto**.","translation":"Her birthday is on the twentieth of **August**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdaraos ng isang salu-salo sa labas ng bahay, karaniwan sa isang parke o tabing-dagat, kung saan nagdadala ng sariling pagkain.
original_explanation: It's when you and your barkada decide to escape the city's traffic and pollution. You pack adobo, kanin, and Royal in a basket, find a nice spot under a tree (or sa beach!), and just chill. Bonus points if may dala kang banig at gitara. It's the OG 'healing' before the term 'healing' was a thing.
usage_notes: A loanword that has been fully integrated and conjugated as a Tagalog verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tara, **magpiknik** tayo sa Luneta sa Sabado!","translation":"Come on, let's **have a picnic** at Luneta on Saturday!"},{"sentence":"Mahilig silang **magpiknik** sa tabing-ilog tuwing Linggo.","translation":"They love to **have a picnic** by the river every Sunday."}]

translation: thorough consideration, deep thought, careful deliberation
meaning_filipino: Isang proseso ng malalim at maingat na pagmumuni-muni o pagsusuri sa isang bagay bago gumawa ng desisyon.
original_explanation: That moment when you're staring at the menu for 15 minutes, weighing the pros and cons of Chickenjoy vs. Jolly Spaghetti. It's what you *should* do before replying to a toxic comment online or before accepting a job offer. It's overthinking, but with a purpose.
usage_notes: Used as a noun phrase to refer to the act of careful thinking.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng **masusing pag-iisip**, nagpasya siyang mag-resign.","translation":"After **thorough consideration**, she decided to resign."},{"sentence":"Ang desisyon ay nangangailangan ng **masusing pag-iisip**.","translation":"The decision requires **deep thought**."}]

translation: to declare, to express, to announce
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalahad o pagsasabi ng isang kaisipan, damdamin, o impormasyon sa publiko o sa isang tao.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you finally post that 'It's Complicated' to 'In a Relationship' status update. It's the official announcement, the 'press release' of your life, whether it's about your feelings, a big decision, or just to let everyone know na may bago kang chika. Think of it as your State of the Nation Address (SONA) for your friends.
usage_notes: Often used in formal contexts like news reporting, official statements, or expressing deep emotions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **magpahayag** ng kanyang tunay na nararamdaman.","translation":"She decided to **express** her true feelings."},{"sentence":"Ang pangulo ay **magpapahayag** ng bagong batas bukas.","translation":"The president will **announce** a new law tomorrow."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay, gawain, o pagkain na laan o angkop para sa oras ng hapon.
original_explanation: This describes anything related to that magical post-lunch, pre-dinner window. It could be your `panghapon` na kape (afternoon coffee), `panghapon` na porma (your casual afternoon outfit), or the `panghapon` na chismis session with your neighbors.
usage_notes: Madalas ginagamit upang ilarawan ang damit, pagkain, o gawain. Maaari ring maging pangngalan na tumutukoy sa meryenda.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maghanda ka ng meryenda na **panghapon** natin.","translation":"Prepare a snack for our **afternoon** meal."},{"sentence":"Ito ang damit kong **panghapon** na isusuot ko sa parke.","translation":"This is my **afternoon** dress that I will wear to the park."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapahayag o pag-aanunsyo ng isang balita o kautusan sa publiko, karaniwan sa pamamagitan ng isang tagapagbalita o sa isang mataong lugar.
original_explanation: This is the OG "shoutout". Before social media posts, you had a town crier (bandilyo) walking around shouting the news. Think of it as a human megaphone or a live-action public service announcement. "Hoy, hoy, may bago tayong ordinance! Bawal na ang chismis sa kanto!"
usage_notes: Often associated with official announcements in a town or barangay, sometimes done with a megaphone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan ng kapitan ang tanod na **magbando** ng bagong curfew sa buong barangay.","translation":"The captain ordered the watchman to **announce** the new curfew throughout the barangay."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magbando** para malaman ng lahat ang tungkol sa paparating na pagpupulong.","translation":"We need to **make an announcement** so that everyone knows about the upcoming meeting."}]

translation: as difficult as; as poor as
meaning_filipino: May magkatulad na antas ng hirap o kahirapan, maging sa isang gawain o sa estado ng buhay.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'kasing-' at salitang-ugat na 'hirap'.
original_explanation: How you describe your final exams to your friend who's in a different course. 'Bes, **kasinghirap** din ng exam namin 'yung sa inyo!' It can also mean 'as poor as,' but most of the time you're using it to complain about how hard life, work, or moving on is.
usage_notes: The meaning, whether 'as difficult as' or 'as poor as', is determined by the context of the sentence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-move on sa kanya ay **kasinghirap** ng pag-solve ng Math problem na walang formula.","translation":"Moving on from him is **as difficult as** solving a Math problem without a formula."},{"sentence":"Hindi kami mayaman, pero hindi rin naman kami **kasinghirap** ng daga.","translation":"We are not rich, but we are not **as poor as** a mouse either."}]

translation: to reason; to justify; to argue
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng dahilan, paliwanag, o argumento upang ipagtanggol o suportahan ang isang panig, kilos, o paniniwala.
original_explanation: This is what you do when your manager asks why you were late and you start explaining the "unprecedented traffic on EDSA," the "sudden LRT breakdown," and the "cat that needed rescuing." You're giving your reasons, making your case. It's the verbal gymnastics of explaining yourself.
usage_notes: Often used in debates, arguments, or when providing an explanation for one's actions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **ikakatwiran** mo sa iyong mga pagkakamali?","translation":"How will you **justify** your mistakes?"},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **ikatwiran** na hindi niya sinasadya ang nangyari.","translation":"He tried to **argue** that what happened was not intentional."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na salita para sa pag-ibig o pagmamahal, pinaikling bersyon ng salitang Ingles na 'love'.
original_explanation: The text message version of 'love'. Short, sweet, and low-effort. 'I lab u' is the modern-day 'Iniibig kita' for people in a hurry. It's the 'GM' (good morning) of affection.
usage_notes: Highly informal, used primarily in text messages or casual online conversations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lab** kita, bes!","translation":"I **love** you, bestie!"},{"sentence":"Sabi niya 'I **lab** you' pero seen-zoned ako.","translation":"He said 'I **love** you' but he left me on seen."}]

translation: to cage, to put in a cage
meaning_filipino: Ilagay o ikulong sa loob ng isang tangkal o hawla.
etymology: From i- (causative verb prefix) + tangkal (cage, coop).
original_explanation: It's what you do to your pet bird or hamster. On a hugot level, it's what you feel your strict parents are doing to you when they don't let you go out on a Friday night. "Itinangkal ako sa bahay!"
usage_notes: Usually for animals, but can be used metaphorically for people being confined.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **itangkal** ang mga manok bago dumilim.","translation":"Don't forget to **put the chickens in the coop** before it gets dark."},{"sentence":"Parang **itinangkal** ako sa opisina dahil sa dami ng trabaho.","translation":"It feels like I was **caged** in the office because of so much work."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kamalayan sa tama at mali na gumagabay sa pag-uugali at pagpapasya ng isang tao.
original_explanation: 'Yung maliit na boses sa utak mo na nagsasabing, "Huy, 'wag mo nang i-check 'yung FB ng ex mo," o "'Wag mo nang kunin 'yung huling piraso ng pizza." It's your inner moral compass. Kapag may ginawa kang masama, 'yun 'yung "kinukunsensya" ka.
usage_notes: The verb form 'makonsyensya' (to feel guilty) is very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ako makatulog dahil sa aking **konsyensya**.","translation":"I can't sleep because of my **conscience**."},{"sentence":"Linisin mo ang iyong **konsyensya** sa pamamagitan ng pag-amin ng iyong pagkakamali.","translation":"Clear your **conscience** by admitting your mistake."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bilang na kasunod ng anim at bago ang walo; katumbas ng numerong 7.
original_explanation: The number of days in a week, the number of dwarfs for Snow White, and the number of times you promise yourself you'll start your diet "next week." "Bigyan mo ako ng pitong piraso, pakiusap." It's more than half a dozen, but not quite ten. The perfect number for when you want "a lot" but don't want to sound too greedy.
usage_notes: Note the stress on the second syllable, /pi-TO/, to distinguish from 'whistle'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroon siyang **pito**ng anak.","translation":"She has **seven** children."},{"sentence":"Nagkita kami noong ika-**pito** ng gabi.","translation":"We met at **seven** o'clock in the evening."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na isinasama o inihahalo sa iba; isang gawang ipinasok sa isang paligsahan.
original_explanation: Your official entry to the office talent show. Or that extra cheese you sprinkle on your instant noodles—that's your special 'lahok'. It's anything you add to the mix, whether it's a song, a poem, or a secret ingredient.
usage_notes: The person who participates is a 'kalahok'. The verb to enter something into a contest or mix is 'ilahok'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **lahok** niyang tula ay nanalo ng unang gantimpala.","translation":"Her poetry **entry** won first prize."},{"sentence":"Maraming **lahok** ang halo-halo kaya ito masarap.","translation":"Halo-halo has many **ingredients** which is why it's delicious."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng ibon na kilala sa maganda at malamyos nitong pag-awit, lalo na sa gabi.
original_explanation: Ito yung ibon na parang professional singer sa gabi, a la Regine Velasquez ng avian world. Perfect background music para sa mga nag-e-emote o nag-aaral ng Noli Me Tangere, kasi binanggit siya doon. Classic!
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa panitikan at mga tula upang maglarawan ng kagandahan, kalungkutan, o romantikong kapaligiran. Hindi ito karaniwang ibon sa Pilipinas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang huni ng **ruwisenyor** ay maririnig sa katahimikan ng gabi.","translation":"The song of the **nightingale** can be heard in the silence of the night."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang landas na hindi karaniwan o direkta; isang daan na mas maikli ngunit maaaring hindi opisyal; paglihis sa nakatakdang ruta.
original_explanation: The habal-habal driver's specialty. It's that sketchy-looking eskinita you take to avoid EDSA traffic. "Mag-tipas tayo" is the battle cry against rush hour. It's a gamble—it could save you 30 minutes, or you could end up in a dead-end street facing a curious gang of stray dogs. Use at your own risk.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng paglalakbay. Maaari ring gamitin bilang pandiwa: "tumipas" (to take a shortcut).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumaan kami sa **tipas** para makaiwas sa trapik.","translation":"We took a **shortcut** to avoid the traffic."},{"sentence":"May alam akong **tipas** papuntang palengke.","translation":"I know a way to **cut across** to the market."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa katangi-tanging amoy ng isda, dugo, o hindi sariwang lamang-dagat.
original_explanation: The smell of the fish section in the palengke. The scent that clings to your hands after preparing fish, even after washing with soap. It's the reason your mom insists on using calamansi or vinegar when cooking seafood. Not to be confused with the English "fishy" which means suspicious, although if your date smells malansa, that's probably suspicious too.
usage_notes: Halos eksklusibong ginagamit para sa partikular na amoy o lasa ng hilaw na isda, pagkaing-dagat, o dugo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hugasan mong mabuti ang mga kamay mo para mawala ang amoy na **malansa**.","translation":"Wash your hands well to get rid of the **fishy** smell."},{"sentence":"Nagiging **malansa** ang isda kapag hindi na ito sariwa.","translation":"Fish becomes **rank** when it's no longer fresh."}]

meaning_filipino: Makaranas ng pananakit ng mga kasu-kasuan o kalamnan na dulot ng rayuma.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na nararamdaman ng mga lolo at lola (at minsan, kahit ikaw na rin) kapag malamig ang panahon o umuulan. Biglang sasakit ang tuhod o balakang. "Hala, inaatake na naman ako ng rayuma!" is the prelude to being 'reumahin'.
usage_notes: This is an intransitive verb indicating the state of suffering from rheumatism.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Madalas **reumahin** si Lolo tuwing tag-lamig.","translation":"Grandpa often **suffers from rheumatism** during the cold season."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magbabad sa ulan at baka ka **reumahin**.","translation":"Don't stay too long in the rain or you might **get a rheumatic attack**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang partikular na layunin o balakin na pinagsisikapang isakatuparan, kadalasan para sa ikabubuti ng isang pangkat o ng lipunan.
etymology: From "adhika" + "-in" suffix, turning the abstract desire into a more concrete goal or objective.
original_explanation: If 'adhika' is the dream, 'adhikain' is the mission. It’s more specific and actionable. It’s the platform of a politician (the good ones, hopefully), the mission statement of an NGO, or the 'hugot' behind your passion project. It's the advocacy you'd post about on social media with a long, heartfelt caption.
usage_notes: Also a formal word, but slightly more common than 'adhika' as it refers to a specific, actionable goal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pangunahing **adhikain** ng kanilang organisasyon ay ang kalinisan ng kapaligiran.","translation":"The main **advocacy** of their organization is environmental cleanliness."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga na magkaroon ng malinaw na **adhikain** sa buhay.","translation":"It is important to have a clear **purpose** in life."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang anyo ng pandiwa na katumbas ng 'tikman', na tumutukoy sa pag-alam o pagsubok sa lasa ng isang bagay, kung minsan ay may diin sa masusing paglasa.
original_explanation: This is the slightly more formal or intense cousin of 'tikman'. If 'tikman' is 'have a taste,' 'tikmanin' is more like 'go on, evaluate the flavor profile.' It's what a chef might say. Or, in a dramatic teleserye: 'Hayaan mong siya ang tumikman ng sarili niyang lason!' (Let him be the one to taste his own poison!). It adds a bit of flair.
usage_notes: While often interchangeable with 'tikman', 'tikmanin' can sometimes feel more literary, formal, or emphatic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sarap **tikmanin** ng mga prutas na pinitas mula sa puno.","translation":"It's so good **to taste** the fruits picked from the tree."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang **tikmanin** 'yan, panis na.","translation":"Don't bother **tasting** that anymore, it's spoiled."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng magaspang o malagong na tunog mula sa ilong o lalamunan habang natutulog.
