original_explanation: It's the sound your tito makes after a family reunion, sounding like a chainsaw trying to start. It's the reason why you sometimes "accidentally" nudge the person sleeping next to you. The unofficial soundtrack of many Filipino bedrooms.
usage_notes: Maghilik is in the actor-focus, infinitive form. The completed aspect is naghilik, ongoing is naghihilik, and future is maghihilik.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **maghilik** nang malakas mamayang gabi, may bisita tayo.","translation":"Don't **snore** loudly tonight, we have a visitor."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula siyang **maghilik** pagkatapos niyang uminom ng alak.","translation":"He started to **snore** after he drank alcohol."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinagkukunan ng kita o paraan upang matustusan ang pang-araw-araw na pangangailangan at suportahan ang sarili o pamilya.
original_explanation: This is your 'hustle,' your 'grind,' your 9-to-5, your side-gig—whatever it is that pays the bills and funds your milk tea addiction. It's the reason you wake up on a Monday morning. When someone asks "Ano'ng ikinabubuhay mo?" they're asking how you're making a living.
usage_notes: Often used as a noun phrase ('ang ikinabubuhay') to mean 'livelihood'. It's more descriptive than just 'trabaho' (work), as it emphasizes that the activity sustains life.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagtitinda ng isda sa palengke ang **ikinabubuhay** ng kanilang pamilya.","translation":"Selling fish in the market is their family's **source of livelihood**."},{"sentence":"Marangal ang anumang **ikinabubuhay** basta't ito'y nasa tamang paraan.","translation":"Any **source of livelihood** is honorable as long as it is done the right way."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay ng guhit o drowing sa isang partikular na lugar o bagay.
original_explanation: The literal act of drawing *on* a surface. Like when your little pamangkin decides your newly painted white wall is the perfect canvas. "Hala, dinrawingan niya yung pader!"
usage_notes: A standard verb formation from the loanword "drowing".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **drowingan** ng mga bituin ang pabalat ng aking notebook.","translation":"I want **to draw** stars **on** the cover of my notebook."}]

translation: the act of opening one's eyes
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbubukas ng mga mata mula sa pagkakapikit.
original_explanation: That first, painful moment you open your eyes in the morning when the alarm rings, and you realize weekend's over. It's also that moment of realization, 'pag "namulat" ka na sa katotohanan. From literal na paggising to being "woke".
usage_notes: Can be used both literally and figuratively ('pagmulat ng isipan').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa kanyang **pagdilat**, ang unang nakita niya ay ang kisame ng kanyang kwarto.","translation":"Upon **opening his eyes**, the first thing he saw was the ceiling of his room."},{"sentence":"Isang malakas na ingay ang gumising sa kanya, at sa kanyang **pagdilat**, nakita niya ang usok.","translation":"A loud noise woke him up, and upon **opening his eyes**, he saw smoke."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa ng mga pisikal na gawain upang mapanatili o mapabuti ang kalusugan at lakas ng katawan.
original_explanation: That thing you promise yourself you'll do every New Year's Day but forget by January 3rd. Whether it's going to the gym, jogging, or just following a YouTube workout, it's all **maghersisyo**. It's the battle against the extra rice and the samgyupsal you had last night.
usage_notes: A very common, modern word borrowed from Spanish. The root word is the Filipinized spelling 'ehersisyo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinabi ng doktor na kailangan kong **maghersisyo** araw-araw.","translation":"The doctor said I need to **exercise** every day."},{"sentence":"Tara, **maghersisyo** tayo sa parke mamayang hapon.","translation":"Come on, let's **exercise** at the park this afternoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagtatanghal ng mga kahanga-hangang gawaing pampalakasan na nangangailangan ng husay, lakas, at liksi ng katawan.
original_explanation: That person in the circus or on 'Pilipinas Got Talent' who can bend their body in ways you didn't think were humanly possible. They're the reason you tried to do a cartwheel once and failed miserably. Also, what you feel like when you're trying to navigate a crowded MRT train during rush hour without falling over.
usage_notes: Refers to a performer known for gymnastic feats.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Namangha ang mga manonood sa galing ng **akrobata**.","translation":"The audience was amazed by the skill of the **acrobat**."},{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang maging isang sikat na **akrobata** sa sirko.","translation":"His dream is to become a famous **acrobat** in the circus."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kabayo na pinalaki at sinanay para sa bilis, partikular para sa mga paligsahan sa takbuhan.
etymology: Compound of 'kabayo' (horse) and 'pangarera' (for racing), from Spanish 'carrera' (race).
original_explanation: The F1 car of the animal kingdom. These are the elite athletes you see at the San Lazaro Hippodrome, the reason your tito loses his 'balato' money. A 'kabayong-pangarera' is bred for one thing: speed.
usage_notes: A specific term for a horse bred for racing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang pusta nila sa paborito nilang **kabayong-pangarera**.","translation":"They bet big on their favorite **racehorse**."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-aalaga ng **kabayong-pangarera** ay magastos.","translation":"Raising a **racehorse** is expensive."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tradisyonal na pagkaing Pilipino na kilala sa maasim nitong sabaw, na karaniwang ginagamitan ng sampalok, kamatis, at iba pang pampaasim, at may sahog na karne, isda, o gulay.
etymology: From the verb 'sigang', meaning to stew.
original_explanation: The official comfort food of the Philippines. It's the sour soup that makes you 'asim-kilig' and feels like a warm hug, especially on a rainy day. The ultimate test of a relationship: kung pareho kayo ng level ng asim na gusto. The cure for hangovers, heartbreaks, and the common cold.
usage_notes: Variations include Sinigang na Baboy (pork), Sinigang na Hipon (shrimp), and Sinigang sa Miso. The souring agent can vary from tamarind (sampalok) to guava (bayabas) or calamansi.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Walang tatalo sa mainit na **sinigang** sa isang maulang hapon.","translation":"Nothing beats hot **sinigang** on a rainy afternoon."},{"sentence":"Pakiabot ng patis, ilalagay ko sa **sinigang** ko.","translation":"Please pass the fish sauce, I'll put it in my **sinigang**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tawag o katawagan para sa pangalawang pinakamatandang kapatid na lalaki.
etymology: From Hokkien `二哥` (di-gō/jī-ko), meaning 'second elder brother'.
original_explanation: The original "middle child" before Sangko came along. If Kuya is the boss, Diko is often the cool, more approachable vice-president of the sibling hierarchy. A term of respect and endearment rooted in Chinese-Filipino family culture.
usage_notes: Part of the Chinese-Filipino honorific system for siblings, which also includes Kuya, Ditsi, Sangko, etc.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si **Diko** ang susunod kay Kuya sa aming magkakapatid.","translation":"**Diko** is next to Kuya among us siblings."},{"sentence":"Tinawag ni Inay si **Diko** para tulungan siya.","translation":"Mom called for the **second eldest brother** to help her."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi nagpapakita ng paggalang, lalo na sa mga nakatatanda, sagradong bagay, o may awtoridad.
original_explanation: 'Yung Gen Z na sinagot-sagot 'yung tita niyang boomer sa family reunion. O 'yung nag-TikTok sa loob ng simbahan. Basically, anyone who acts without the proper 'po' and 'opo' vibe in a situation that calls for it. The opposite of being a 'well-mannered' kid.
usage_notes: Isang mabigat na salita na nagpapahiwatig ng kawalan ng pangunahing paggalang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **walang-pitagan** na bata ang sumigaw sa matanda.","translation":"A **disrespectful** child shouted at the old man."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga salita ay **walang-pitagan** at nakasakit sa marami.","translation":"His words were **irreverent** and hurt many people."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkuha ng tubig mula sa isang balon, poso, o ilog, karaniwang gamit ang isang lalagyan tulad ng timba.
original_explanation: Before NAWASA and Maynilad blessed your condo with running water, your lolo and lola had to do this every day. It's the OG arm workout, fetching water from the *poso* (water pump) or a well. Think of it as a rural 'water run' before water delivery apps existed.
usage_notes: Typically refers to fetching water from a natural source or a manual pump, not just turning on a faucet.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **umigib** ng tubig sa balon para panligo.","translation":"I need to **fetch water** from the well to take a bath."},{"sentence":"**Umigib** si Maria ng tatlong timba para sa kanilang panlaba.","translation":"Maria **fetched** three pails of water for their laundry."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang pautos na ginagamit upang anyayahan o tawagin ang dalawa o higit pang tao na lumapit.
original_explanation: This is "Halika!" but for the whole barkada. When the food delivery arrives for the team, you don't just say "Halika!", you shout "**Halikayo**! Andito na ang pizza!" It's the plural, all-inclusive invitation.
usage_notes: The plural form of "Halika." "Kayo" refers to "you" (plural).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Halikayo**! Magsisimula na ang programa.","translation":"**Come here** (everyone)! The program is about to start."},{"sentence":"Mga bata, **halikayo** rito at kunin ang inyong meryenda.","translation":"Kids, **come** over here and get your snacks."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan, karaniwang gawa sa kahoy o bato, na ginagamit kasama ng pandikdik o halo upang durugin o pulbusin ang mga butil tulad ng palay. Ito rin ay tumutukoy sa lugar kung saan isinasagawa ang pagbabayo.
original_explanation: This is the OG food processor of our lolas. It's that big wooden bowl where they pound rice, garlic, or whatever needs a good smashing. Think of it as the analog version of a blender, powered by pure muscle and tita-level determination. The sound of pounding in the 'bayuhan' is the classic provincial morning alarm clock.
usage_notes: Often paired with 'halo' (pestle). The term can refer to both the object (mortar) and the place where pounding happens.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inilagay ni Lola ang palay sa **bayuhan** upang dikdikin.","translation":"Grandma placed the unhusked rice in the **mortar** to pound it."},{"sentence":"Naririnig ko pa rin ang tunog mula sa **bayuhan** sa aming probinsya.","translation":"I can still hear the sound from the **pounding place** in our province."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na pagpapahayag ng kaisipan, pananaw, o damdamin na binibigkas sa harap ng madla o mga tagapakinig.
etymology: Maaaring hango sa Sanskrit na *tala* (palad, kumpas) + *ampati* (panginoon), na posibleng tumutukoy sa pagsasalita na may kasamang maindayog na pagkumpas ng kamay.
original_explanation: This is your graduation speech, the SONA, or that thing your boss does in the town hall that could've been an email. It’s a formal, prepared talk delivered to an audience. Hindi ito 'yung chismis mo sa kapitbahay; ito 'yung may script, may stage, at (sana) may point.
usage_notes: Isang pangunahing salita sa larangan ng pampublikong pagsasalita, pulitika, at akademya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghanda siya ng isang makabagbag-damdaming **talumpati** para sa araw ng pagtatapos.","translation":"She prepared a heart-stirring **speech** for graduation day."},{"sentence":"Ang **talumpati** ng pangulo ay nakatuon sa pag-unlad ng ekonomiya.","translation":"The president's **oration** focused on economic development."}]

translation: to entrench; to surround with a trench
meaning_filipino: Ang paghuhukay ng mahabang kanal sa palibot ng isang lugar, karaniwan para sa layuning pandepensa sa digmaan.
original_explanation: Literally, digging a big ditch around something to protect it, like in old war movies. Figuratively, it's what you do when you refuse to change your opinion during a debate, no matter how much evidence is presented. You've dug your trench and you're not coming out.
usage_notes: A specific military or engineering term. It can also be used metaphorically for becoming deeply established in a position or belief.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-utos ang heneral na **magpaligid ng trinsera** sa kanilang base.","translation":"The general ordered to **entrench** their base."},{"sentence":"Mahirap nang mapasok ang kuta matapos silang **magpaligid ng trinsera**.","translation":"The fort became difficult to penetrate after they **surrounded it with a trench**."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawin o sabihin muli ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is what your teacher tells you to do when you fail an exam. It's the 'ctrl+c, ctrl+v' of actions. When your crush doesn't hear your 'hi' the first time, you gather all your courage to 'ulitin' it. Also, the core function of every call center agent's life: 'Ma'am/Sir, can you please **repeat** that?'
usage_notes: This is the object-focus verb form of 'ulit'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, huwag mo nang **ulitin** ang iyong pagkakamali.","translation":"Please, do not **repeat** your mistake."},{"sentence":"Maaari mo bang **ulitin** ang sinabi mo? Hindi ko narinig.","translation":"Can you **repeat** what you said? I didn't hear it."}]

translation: mobilization; act of causing movement or action
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-udyok, pag-engganyo, o pag-oorganisa sa mga tao upang kumilos o gumawa ng isang bagay nang sama-sama para sa isang layunin.
etymology: From pag- (gerund prefix) + papaki- (causative prefix) + los from kilos (action, movement). 'The act of causing action'.
original_explanation: This is what an activist group does for a rally, what a team lead does to meet a deadline, or what your mom does to get the whole family to do general cleaning on a Saturday. It’s about getting people off their butts and into action. It's the art of mobilization.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of social movements, politics, community organizing, or project management.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapakilos** sa mga mamamayan ay mahalaga para sa pagbabago.","translation":"The **mobilization** of citizens is important for change."},{"sentence":"Epektibo ang kanyang pamumuno sa **pagpapakilos** ng kanyang koponan.","translation":"His leadership is effective in the **act of causing his team to act**."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagkilos na tila o sadya na nahihirapang maglakad dahil sa kapansanan o sakit sa paa o binti; pag-ika-ika.
etymology: From the root word 'pilay' (lame, crippled), with the prefix 'pa-' indicating causation or pretense, and reduplication indicating a continuous or feigned action.
original_explanation: This describes how you walk after a leg day at the gym when you can't feel your thighs. Or when a basketball player fakes an injury to get a foul call. "Nag-iinarte lang 'yan, papilay-pilay para mapansin." It's walking with a dramatic limp, whether real or for show.
usage_notes: The reduplication implies a repetitive, sometimes exaggerated or feigned, limping motion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umuwi siyang **papilay-pilay** matapos matapilok sa hagdan.","translation":"He came home **limping** after stumbling on the stairs."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala diyan, **papilay-pilay** lang 'yan para makaiwas sa trabaho.","translation":"Don't believe him, he's just **pretending to limp** to avoid work."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsenyas o pagsabi sa isang tsuper ng pampublikong sasakyan na huminto upang makasakay o makababa.
original_explanation: The national sport of Filipino commuters. It's the art of waving your hand with just the right amount of desperation to make a jeepney or bus stop for you. 'Manong, para!' is a phrase every Pinoy has shouted at least once in their life.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used for hailing public transportation like jeepneys, buses, and tricycles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pumara** ako ng dyip sa tapat ng palengke.","translation":"I **hailed** a jeepney in front of the market."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **pumara** sa gitna ng kalsada; delikado iyan.","translation":"Don't **stop** (a vehicle) in the middle of the road; that's dangerous."}]

translation: to appoint; to name to a position
meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na paghirang o pagtalaga sa isang tao para sa isang posisyon, tungkulin, o katungkulan.
etymology: From Spanish 'nombrar' (to name, to appoint). Tagalog form is `mang-` + `nombra` + `-han`.
original_explanation: This is the more formal, Spanish-loanword version of 'to appoint.' It's what happens in government or big corporations. When the President picks a new cabinet secretary, he doesn't just 'choose' them, he 'nanunumbrahan' them. It has that official, stamped-and-sealed, 'may position ka na' vibe.
usage_notes: A formal term used in legal, political, or corporate contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pangulo ang may kapangyarihang **manumbrahan** ng mga miyembro ng kanyang gabinete.","translation":"The president has the power to **appoint** the members of his cabinet."},{"sentence":"Sino kaya ang susunod na **manunumbrahan** bilang bagong CEO?","translation":"Who do you think will be **appointed** next as the new CEO?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o pasilidad kung saan iniimbak at pinoproseso ang dugo at mga bahagi nito para sa transpusyon.
original_explanation: It's like a regular bank, but instead of money, they store the literal life juice of people. The ultimate 'pahingi ng life' station for emergencies. You go here to donate or to receive.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nangangailangan ng mga donor ang **bangko ng dugo** ng ospital.","translation":"The hospital's **blood bank** needs donors."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng hakbang upang alisin ang pag-aalinlangan at tiyakin ang isang bagay.
etymology: From 'siguro', which is from Spanish 'seguro' (sure, secure).
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa ng nanay mo bago umalis ng bahay: "Sinara mo ba pinto? Pinatay mo kalan? Sure ka?" That's the spirit of sumiguro. It’s double-checking, triple-checking, and maybe even screenshotting just to be safe. The motto of every "praning" and responsible adult.
usage_notes: While 'siguro' means 'maybe', 'sumiguro' (or 'siguraduhin') means 'to make sure'. This is a key distinction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumiguro** ka na nakasara ang lahat ng ilaw bago ka umalis.","translation":"**Make sure** that all the lights are turned off before you leave."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **sumiguro** na tama ang ating mga kalkulasyon.","translation":"We need to **ensure** that our calculations are correct."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na labis na mahilig at maalam sa isang partikular na larangan o aktibidad, lalo na sa teknolohiya, kompyuter, o mga paksang akademiko.
original_explanation: In the PH context, a **geek** is someone who's super passionate about something 'nerdy'—anime, K-Pop, gaming, coding, Star Wars, you name it. It's no longer an insult; it's a badge of honor. A **geek** is the person you run to when your laptop crashes, who can explain the entire Marvel timeline, or who has a spreadsheet for their K-Pop photocard collection. We love our geeks!
usage_notes: Used in the same way as in English, but often with a positive or affectionate connotation in modern Filipino slang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isa siyang computer **geek** kaya alam niya kung paano ayusin 'yan.","translation":"He's a computer **geek**, so he knows how to fix that."},{"sentence":"Nag-uusap ang mga **geek** tungkol sa bagong episode ng paborito nilang anime.","translation":"The **geeks** are talking about the new episode of their favorite anime."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ama o ina ng isang tao; ang tumatayong tagapag-alaga at gabay sa isang anak.
original_explanation: The OG source of your allowance and your 'sermons'. They are the reason you can't just up and leave, and also the reason you have a roof over your head. They oscillate between being your best friend and your strictest life coach. Plural form 'mga magulang' is very common.
usage_notes: Often used in the plural 'mga magulang' to refer to both parents. Pronunciation is key: /ma-gu-LANG/ for 'parent', /ma-GU-lang/ for 'cunning'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahal na mahal ko ang aking mga **magulang**.","translation":"I love my **parents** very much."},{"sentence":"Bilang isang **magulang**, responsibilidad mong gabayan ang iyong anak.","translation":"As a **parent**, it is your responsibility to guide your child."}]

translation: a dish cooked in coconut milk
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng lutuin na hinaluan ng gata; isang mas kolokyal na anyo ng salitang 'ginataan'.
original_explanation: Basically the same as 'ginataan', but this is how you'd say it when you're talking to your friends or the vendor at the carinderia. It's the slightly shortened, more casual version. 'Pabili po ng ginatan!'
usage_notes: A common colloquial variant of 'ginataan,' often referring specifically to the sweet dessert version.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para sa meryenda, nagluto si Aling Nena ng mainit na **ginatan**.","translation":"For snack time, Aling Nena cooked warm **ginatan** (sweet coconut milk dessert)."},{"sentence":"Gusto mo ba ng **ginatan** na mais?","translation":"Do you want some corn cooked in coconut milk (**ginatan** na mais)?"}]

translation: to jingle; to ring (like a small bell)
meaning_filipino: Tumunog nang paulit-ulit na parang kampanilya, batingaw, o mga barya.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung tunog ng bell sa bike mo nung bata ka, o 'yung bell sa pinto ng 7-Eleven pag may pumasok. 'Yung maliit at matinis na tunog. 'Pag narinig mo 'yan sa gabi, baka ice cream man 'yan... o baka hindi.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumililing** ang maliit na kampana sa tuktok ng simbahan.","translation":"The small bell at the top of the church **rang**."},{"sentence":"Naririnig mo bang **kumililing** ang mga susi sa bulsa niya?","translation":"Can you hear the keys **jingling** in his pocket?"}]

meaning_filipino: Daglat para sa "Role Play World," isang uri ng komunidad sa social media kung saan ang mga gumagamit ay gumaganap bilang ibang tao, karaniwan ay mga sikat na personalidad o kathang-isip na karakter.
original_explanation: This is the world of online alter-egos. In RPW, you're not Juan dela Cruz from Cebu; you're Jungkook from BTS, or maybe a fictional anime character you made up. It's a whole subculture on Facebook and Twitter where people create profiles to "role-play." It's like digital cosplay, complete with its own slang (op for operator, rs for relationship), drama, and communities. It's where you can live your best *artista* life, anonymously.
usage_notes: A very specific internet slang term, primarily known among younger social media users (Gen Z).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marami siyang kaibigan sa **RPW** pero hindi niya kilala sa totoong buhay.","translation":"She has many friends in **RPW** but doesn't know them in real life."},{"sentence":"Naging kumplikado ang buhay niya dahil sa drama sa **RPW**.","translation":"Her life got complicated because of drama in the **Role Play World**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pakiusap o pahayag ng pagnanais na sumama o lumahok sa isang gawain, laro, o grupo.
original_explanation: The official word of the FOMO generation. When you see your friends posting group pics, you slide into their DMs with "Pasali next time!" It's a polite but desperate plea to be included. The ultimate party-crasher's password.
usage_notes: Commonly used as a single-word question or request: "Pasali?"
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita kong naglalaro sila ng basketball kaya sumigaw ako, \"**Pasali**!\"","translation":"I saw them playing basketball so I shouted, \"**Let me join**!\""},{"sentence":"**Pasali** naman sa group chat ninyo.","translation":"**Please let me join** your group chat."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtatabi o pag-iimbak ng isang bagay, tulad ng pera o datos, para sa hinaharap.
etymology: Tagalog prefix 'mag-' (infinitive/contemplated) + English 'save'. A Taglish verb.
original_explanation: Future tense of 'magsave'. Ito yung pangako mo sa sarili mo tuwing sahod: "This time, magsasave na talaga ako!" Pero pagkatapos ng 11.11 sale, 'next time na lang' ulit. Also, what you do in a video game before a boss fight.
usage_notes: A common Taglish verb. The future tense form of 'magsave'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magsasave** ako ng pera para makabili ng bagong cellphone sa Pasko.","translation":"I **will save** money to buy a new cellphone for Christmas."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutan na **magsasave** ka ng kopya ng iyong file bago mo isara ang computer.","translation":"Don't forget that you **will save** a copy of your file before you close the computer."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggalaw pataas o pababa sa isang digital na screen, tulad ng sa telepono o kompyuter, upang tingnan ang nilalaman.
etymology: Taglish, from English "scroll" with Tagalog affix "nag-".
original_explanation: The modern-day zombie walk, but for your thumb. It's what you do when you're avoiding work, waiting for your Grab, or pretending to be busy in a social gathering. Also known as 'doomscrolling' when you're just looking at bad news at 2 AM.
usage_notes: Present progressive. Very informal and common in online chats and casual conversation. The double 's' is a common informal spelling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang oras na akong **nagsscroll** sa TikTok, wala pa rin akong nagagawang trabaho.","translation":"I've been **scrolling** on TikTok for an hour, I still haven't done any work."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maingay, **nagsscroll** lang ako ng memes.","translation":"Be quiet, I'm just **scrolling** through memes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng mag-aaral na naninirahan sa loob ng paaralan o isang dormitoryo na kaakibat nito.
original_explanation: Think of the classic Filipino movies set in exclusive all-girls schools. The interna is the student who lives in the school dormitory, subject to the strict rules of a head nun or dorm mother. She's the one who can't just 'go home' after class and probably has a secret plan to sneak out after curfew.
usage_notes: A somewhat dated term, strongly associated with Catholic boarding schools. The male equivalent is 'interno'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **interna** sa kolehiyo ay may mahigpit na curfew.","translation":"The female **boarders** in the college have a strict curfew."},{"sentence":"Noong araw, maraming pamilya ang nagpapaaral sa kanilang mga anak na babae bilang mga **interna**.","translation":"In the old days, many families sent their daughters to study as **live-in students**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng hindi maigalaw ang bahagi o kabuuan ng katawan dahil sa pinsala sa nerbiyos o sakit.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "parálisis". Ang unlaping "pagka-" ay nagpapahiwatig ng isang estado o kondisyon.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na na-seen ka lang niya. Emotionally, you experience **pagkaparalisa**. Or, more literally, 'yung nangyayari sa traffic sa EDSA tuwing Biyernes ng gabi – total system shutdown.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa kontekstong medikal, ngunit maaari ring gamitin nang metaporikal para sa pagiging-tigil o kawalan ng kakayahang kumilos.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkaparalisa** ng kanyang mga binti ay resulta ng isang malubhang aksidente.","translation":"The **paralysis** of his legs was the result of a serious accident."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa takot, naranasan niya ang pansamantalang **pagkaparalisa** at hindi nakasigaw.","translation":"Due to fear, she experienced a temporary **state of being paralyzed** and could not scream."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ulat o talaan ng mga kaganapan, gawain, o datos na inilalabas o sinusuri buwan-buwan.
original_explanation: Your boss's favorite word at the end of the month. It's the dreaded corporate document that summarizes all your team's wins and (mostly hidden) losses. Parang monthly subscription box ng stress.
usage_notes: Compound word. Primarily used in business, academic, or formal settings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nang ipasa ang **talabulanan** sa Biyernes.","translation":"The **monthly report** needs to be submitted on Friday."},{"sentence":"Naglalaman ang **talabulanan** ng aming benta at gastusin.","translation":"The **monthly report** contains our sales and expenses."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marubdob na paghiling o pagmamakaawa para sa isang bagay, kadalasan ay dahil sa matinding pangangailangan o desperasyon.
original_explanation: That "last na 'to, promise!" look you give your friend when you need to borrow money again. It's the energy of a teleserye character on their knees, crying in the rain, begging for forgiveness. The highest form of pakiusap.
usage_notes: Implies a sense of desperation or urgency, more intense than simply asking (paghiling).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **paggibik** ang kanyang mga liham para sa pangalawang pagkakataon.","translation":"His letters were full of **pleading** for a second chance."},{"sentence":"Sa kabila ng **paggibik** ng mga tao, itinuloy pa rin ang demolisyon.","translation":"Despite the people's **imploring**, the demolition still pushed through."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang akrobatikong kilos kung saan umiikot ang katawan sa ere, pauna o patalikod, bago lumapag muli sa paa.
original_explanation: The move you see gymnasts do, or what your hyperactive pamangkin tries to do on the bed. It's a flip, a tumble, a 'wow, flexible!' moment. Also, what your career might do if you suddenly quit your stable job to become a vlogger.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb (e.g., 'sumalto', 'mag-salto').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Humanga ang lahat sa perpektong **salto** ng gymnast.","translation":"Everyone was amazed by the gymnast's perfect **somersault**."},{"sentence":"Kaya niyang gumawa ng backflip **salto**.","translation":"He can do a backflip **somersault**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagtuklap o pag-alis ng kaliskis, lalo na sa balat ng tao na tuyo o sa isang isda.
original_explanation: This is your skin during ber-months pag 'di ka nag-lotion. Parang isdang tinanggalan ng kaliskis, or parang desert na nag-crack yung lupa. It's your body's way of saying, "Hoy, hydrate mo 'ko!"
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pandiwa (nangangaliskis ang balat niya) o pang-uri (nangangaliskis na balat).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nangangaliskis** ang kanyang mga binti dahil sa sobrang lamig.","translation":"His legs are **flaking** because of the extreme cold."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong magpahid ng lotion kapag **nangangaliskis** ang iyong balat.","translation":"You need to apply lotion when your skin is **scaling**."}]

meaning_filipino: Masakit o nakasasugat ng damdamin kung magsalita; matalas ang dila.
etymology: From "tabas," meaning "cut" or "style," metaphorically applied to speech.
original_explanation: Describes someone whose words can slice you up better than a samurai sword. The Marites ng bayan who delivers her chismis with surgical precision and a whole lot of shade. Their comebacks are legendary and leave you needing aloe vera for your burnt ego.
usage_notes: Almost always has a negative connotation, implying meanness or sarcasm in speech. A synonym is 'matalas ang dila'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa pagiging **matabas** ang dila kaya marami ang umiiwas sa kanya.","translation":"She is known for being **sharp-tongued**, which is why many avoid her."},{"sentence":"Isang **matabas** na komento ang binitiwan niya tungkol sa kinalabasan ng proyekto.","translation":"He let out a **caustic** comment about the project's outcome."}]

translation: to be able to touch; to feel; tangible
meaning_filipino: May kakayahang mahawakan, madamá, o maramdaman sa pamamagitan ng pandama, lalo na ang pagsalat.
original_explanation: The opposite of your feelings for your crush—this one can actually be felt. It's something physical, something real. Like the texture of crispy pata or the cold hard cash from your 13th-month pay. Something you can physically confirm exists, unlike 'work-life balance'.
usage_notes: Often used in its completed aspect 'nasalat' (was able to touch/feel). Can refer to both physical touch and the abstract concept of being perceivable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagmamahal ay hindi laging isang bagay na **masalat**, ngunit ito ay nararamdaman.","translation":"Love is not always something that is **tangible**, but it is felt."},{"sentence":"Gusto kong **masalat** ang buhangin sa dalampasigan.","translation":"I want to **feel** the sand on the shore."}]

translation: to be proven; to be strengthened
meaning_filipino: Mapagtibay o mapatunayan ang katotohanan o bisa ng isang bagay; gawing mas matatag.
original_explanation: When your 'Marites' friend's chismis turns out to be legit because it was reported on TV Patrol. Or when your friendship survives a major 'tampuhan,' proving it's built to last. It's the official 'Told you so!' seal of approval or the 'friendship goals' achievement unlocked.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aming pagkakaibigan ay lalong **napatibay** ng mga pagsubok.","translation":"Our friendship **was further strengthened** by challenges."},{"sentence":"Sa pamamagitan ng ebidensya, **napatibay** ang kanyang testimonya.","translation":"Through the evidence, his testimony **was proven**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bunga, resulta, o epekto ng isang pangyayari, kilos, o kalagayan. Maaari rin itong tumukoy sa isang bagay na inihahandog.
original_explanation: This is the 'what you get' from an action, for better or for worse. It's the 'consequence' in your mom's 'actions have consequences' lecture. Pwedeng magandang dulot (good effect) like the kilig from your crush's message, or masamang dulot (bad effect) like the hangover after a wild night out.
usage_notes: Often used to describe the effects, both positive and negative, of a situation or action. Can also mean 'offering', similar to 'handog'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagpupuyat ay may masamang **dulot** sa kalusugan.","translation":"Staying up late has a bad **effect** on one's health."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang **dulot** ng bagong teknolohiya sa ating pamumuhay.","translation":"The new technology has brought about a great **effect** in our way of life."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng puno (Ficus carica) o ang bunga nito, na karaniwang hugis-peras, malambot, at matamis kapag hinog.
original_explanation: That fancy fruit you see in expensive grazing boxes or as a jam flavor you can't really place. It's the fruit that makes you feel a bit more sophisticated when you eat it. Not your everyday saging or mangga, the igos is the 'special occasion' fruit.
usage_notes: Not native to the Philippines but known due to colonial influence and modern food trends. The plural form 'higos' in Spanish became the singular 'igos' in Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap na panghimagas ang **igos** na may kasamang keso.","translation":"**Figs** with cheese make for a delicious dessert."},{"sentence":"Bumili siya ng isang garapon ng 'fig jam' o preserbadong **igos**.","translation":"She bought a jar of fig jam or preserved **figs**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakapahid o pagkalagay ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay malagkit o makulay, sa isang ibabaw nang hindi pantay o walang ingat.
original_explanation: Imagine a kid with a chocolate cake. The mess on their face? That's kapol. It's not a neat application, it's a 'naglaro sa putik' or 'sumabog 'yung lipstick sa mukha' kind of smear.
usage_notes: Can be used as a root for verbs (e.g., 'kinapulan', 'ikapol') or as a noun/adjective describing the state of being smeared.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kapol** ng putik ang kanyang mukha pagkatapos maglaro sa ulan.","translation":"His face was **smeared** with mud after playing in the rain."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ikapol** ang pintura sa pader.","translation":"Don't **smear** the paint on the wall."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang nakaalsang bahagi sa isang patag na ibabaw; isang bagay na nakausli o bukol.
original_explanation: Yan yung 'bukol' sa pader na tinamaan mo, o yung umbok sa kalsada na parang mini-humps na 'di sinasadya. Pwede ring umbok ng abs mo kung nag-gym ka, o ng tiyan mo kung naparami ka ng kanin.
usage_notes: Can refer to a physical bump on a surface, a swelling on the body, or a raised part of the land.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **umbok** sa kalsada kaya dahan-dahan ang pagmamaneho niya.","translation":"There's a **bump** on the road so he is driving slowly."},{"sentence":"Pansin mo ba ang maliit na **umbok** sa pader na iyan?","translation":"Do you notice the small **bulge** on that wall?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang makapal at malapot na inumin na gawa sa pinaghalong hilaw na prutas o gulay, kasama ang iba pang sangkap tulad ng tubig, yelo, gatas, o yogurt.
original_explanation: Yung 'healthy' drink mo na mas marami pang asukal kesa sa softdrinks. Ito yung go-to breakfast ng mga BPO agent na nagmamadali o ng mga gym-goers na gustong mag-post ng #FitnessGoals sa IG. Basically, a glorified fruit shake.
usage_notes: While 'shake' is also used, 'smoothie' often implies a healthier, fruit/vegetable-based blend.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uminom ako ng strawberry banana **smoothie** kaninang umaga.","translation":"I drank a strawberry banana **smoothie** this morning."},{"sentence":"Maganda ba sa diet ang pag-inom ng **smoothie**?","translation":"Is drinking a **smoothie** good for one's diet?"}]

translation: to be exposed; to be revealed
meaning_filipino: Mailantad o maihayag sa publiko ang isang bagay na dating nakatago o lihim; mahantad sa isang elemento o kalagayan.
original_explanation: This is what happens when your 'private' DMs get screenshotted and posted. Or when a politician's corruption is finally revealed on the news. It's the 'tea' being spilled for everyone to see. The opposite of being low-key.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of secrets, scandals, or vulnerabilities being revealed. Can also mean physical exposure to elements like sun or chemicals.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natatakot ang korap na opisyal na **mabantad** ang kanyang mga katiwalian.","translation":"The corrupt official is afraid that his anomalies will **be exposed**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **mabantad** sa araw ang iyong balat nang matagal.","translation":"Don't let your skin **be exposed** to the sun for too long."}]

translation: to have a place cleared (of obstructions/weeds)
meaning_filipino: Utos na ipaalis ang mga sagabal, damo, o anumang bagay na nakaharang upang maging malinis at maluwag ang isang lugar.
original_explanation: Before you can build your dream house on that provincial lot, you need to **ipahawan** the area first. It means telling someone to clear the land of all the tall grass, weeds, and random debris. Think of it as the 'Ctrl+A, Delete' for a piece of land.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **ipahawan** ang bakuran bago magtanim ng mga gulay.","translation":"We need to **have** the yard **cleared** before planting vegetables."},{"sentence":"**Ipahawan** mo sa mga trabahador ang dadaanan ng sasakyan.","translation":"**Have** the workers **clear** the path for the vehicle."}]

translation: to catch up with; to find someone upon arrival
meaning_filipino: Marating ang isang tao o bagay na nauuna; madatnan sa isang lugar; magawang mag-abot ng isang bagay sa isang tao.
original_explanation: Yung tumakbo ka para habulin yung last trip ng jeep, pero naabutan mo lang yung usok niya. Saklap. O kaya, yung umuwi ka nang maaga para may maabutan ka pang ulam, pero naubos na ng kuya mo. Double saklap.
usage_notes: Has a dual meaning: 1) to catch up to someone/something moving ahead, and 2) to find someone at a particular place upon arriving.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **maabutan** natin silang gising pa.","translation":"I hope we **find** them still awake upon our arrival."},{"sentence":"Kahit anong bilis ng takbo ko, hindi ko na siya **naabutan**.","translation":"No matter how fast I ran, I wasn't able to **catch up** with him."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagkilos o pagsasalita na salungat o laban sa mungkahi, opinyon, o ginagawa ng karamihan.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "pa-" (nagpapakita ng paraan) + "kontra" (mula sa Espanyol na 'contra', nangangahulugang 'laban').
original_explanation: That one person in the group chat who, when everyone says "Let's eat at Jollibee!", will suddenly say "How about McDo?". They're not necessarily being mean, they just love playing the devil's advocate or have a natural instinct to go against the flow. The ultimate KJ (Kill Joy) or "kontrabida" of the barkada.
usage_notes: Maaaring ilarawan ang katangian ng isang tao (bilang pang-uri) o ang paraan ng isang kilos (bilang pang-abay).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagi na lang siyang **pakontra** sa lahat ng plano natin.","translation":"He's always **disagreeable** with all of our plans."},{"sentence":"Bakit ka ba laging **pakontra**?","translation":"Why are you always so **contrarian**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mga natitirang bahagi ng isang bagay na nasira, o ang katawan ng isang taong pumanaw na.
original_explanation: This is what's left behind. It can be the **labí** of a fallen building after an earthquake, the leftovers on your plate ('tira-tira'), or, more somberly, the physical body of someone who has passed away. "Nakita na ang **labí** ng nawawalang eroplano." It's a word that carries weight and a sense of finality.
usage_notes: Ang pagbigkas na /la-BI/ na may diin sa ikalawang pantig ay mahalaga. Madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng kamatayan, sakuna, o arkeolohiya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **labí** ng bayani ay inilagak sa Libingan ng mga Bayani.","translation":"The **remains** of the hero were interred at the Heroes' Cemetery."},{"sentence":"Hanggang ngayon, hinahanap pa rin ang mga **labí** ng sinaunang sibilisasyon.","translation":"To this day, they are still searching for the **ruins** of the ancient civilization."}]

translation: to farm, to till the land
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbungkal at pagtanim sa lupa, karaniwan sa isang bukirin, upang makapag-ani ng mga produkto tulad ng palay, gulay, at prutas.
original_explanation: The OG 'plantito/plantita' move. This isn't just about putting a succulent on your desk. This is the real deal: working the land, planting crops, and feeding the nation. It's the ultimate act of nurturing life from the soil.
usage_notes: The professional act or occupation of farming.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marangal na trabaho ang **magsaka**.","translation":"**To farm** is a noble job."},{"sentence":"Marami sa mga taga-probinsya ang natutong **magsaka** mula sa kanilang mga magulang.","translation":"Many from the provinces learned **to farm** from their parents."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng detalyadong paglalarawan sa katangian, anyo, o kalagayan ng isang tao, bagay, lugar, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is your friend asking you, "So, anong itsura niya?" after a first date. You have to `deskribihin` everything from their hair to their shoes to how they chew their food. It's painting a picture with words, usually for a chismosa friend.
usage_notes: A common verb used in everyday conversation and formal writing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **deskribihin** ang pakiramdam noong nanalo ako sa lotto.","translation":"It's hard **to describe** the feeling when I won the lottery."},{"sentence":"Maaari mo bang **deskribihin** ang hitsura ng suspek?","translation":"Can you **describe** the appearance of the suspect?"}]

meaning_filipino: Tunawin ang isang solidong bagay sa isang likido; haluan ng tubig o ibang likido upang mabawasan ang tapang o lapot.
original_explanation: Like making 3-in-1 coffee or powdered juice. You pour the powder, add water, and stir until it disappears. It's also what happens to your savings when 11.11 and 12.12 sales come. Biglang natunaw.
usage_notes: Synonymous with 'magtunaw' in many contexts, but 'magkanaw' is more specific to dissolving a solid into a liquid.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **magkanaw** muna ng gatas na pulbos sa maligamgam na tubig.","translation":"You need to **dissolve** the powdered milk in warm water first."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **magkanaw** ng asukal para sa kape ko.","translation":"Don't forget to **dissolve** sugar for my coffee."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang talasalitaan o bokabularyo ng isang tao, wika, o sangay ng kaalaman; isang diksyunaryo o aklat ng mga salita.
original_explanation: Your **leksikon** is your personal word bank. The collection of words you use, from 'charot' and 'awit' to 'moreover' and 'thus'. A BPO agent's **leksikon** includes 'escalate,' 'ticket,' and 'empathy statement.' A lawyer's **leksikon** has 'heretofore' and 'whereas.' It's the vocabulary specific to a person or group. Basically, what I'm building right now.
usage_notes: A formal, academic term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bawat propesyon ay may sarili nitong **leksikon**.","translation":"Every profession has its own **lexicon**."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng mga linggwista ang **leksikon** ng mga sinaunang wika.","translation":"Linguists study the **lexicon** of ancient languages."}]

translation: to go to a specific place (frequently or for a purpose)
meaning_filipino: Puntahan o sadyaing puntahan ang isang lugar, karaniwang nang may partikular na layunin o dalas.
original_explanation: This is the leveled-up version of 'adyo'. The '-an' suffix implies a destination. Think of it as the place you *purposefully* go to. "Adyusan natin ang bagong bukas na coffee shop." It's like saying "let's make that our destination." It's so rare though, if you use this in a conversation, your friends might ask if you just time-traveled from the 19th century.
usage_notes: Extremely rare and archaic. It functions similarly to 'puntahan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **adyusan** ang lugar na iyon sapagkat mapanganib.","translation":"Do not **go to** that place for it is dangerous."},{"sentence":"Balak naming **adyusan** ang tahanan ng yumaong bayani.","translation":"We plan to **go to** the home of the late hero."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pag-iisip at pag-aayos ng mga hakbang na gagawin upang makamit ang isang layunin.
original_explanation: 'Yung status niyo ng ka-talking stage mo: nagpaplano ng future, pero walang label. Or, that feeling when your barkada is nagpaplano for a beach trip in a GC that will never, ever happen. It's the act of making plans, whether they're solid or just wishful thinking.
usage_notes: Present progressive tense. Indicates the ongoing action of making a plan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagpaplano** kami ng isang sorpresa para sa kaarawan niya.","translation":"We **are planning** a surprise for her birthday."},{"sentence":"Ang gobyerno ay **nagpaplano** ng mga bagong proyekto para sa susunod na taon.","translation":"The government **is planning** new projects for next year."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa kalagayan ng matinding paghihirap, pagdurusa, o pagkabalisa ng isip at damdamin.
etymology: Likely an old Tagalog word of uncertain origin.
original_explanation: This isn't just 'sadboi' hours. This is full-on, teleserye-level torment. It's the feeling of your thesis being due tomorrow and you only have the title page done. It's the anguish of seeing your crush post their wedding photos. It's a word so deep and heavy, you'd probably only hear it from your lola or in a Florante at Laura stage play.
usage_notes: A very literary and dramatic word. Not used in casual conversation. Describes a state of profound mental or emotional suffering.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nanatili siyang **giyagis** sa pagkawala ng kanyang pinakamamahal.","translation":"She remained **tormented** by the loss of her beloved."},{"sentence":"Ang **giyagis** na kaluluwa ng sundalo ay hindi matahimik.","translation":"The **afflicted** soul of the soldier could not find peace."}]

translation: a tiny bit; a very small amount
meaning_filipino: Isang napakaliit na bahagi o piraso ng isang bagay; bahagya lamang.
etymology: Mula sa 'ka-' (na nagpapahiwatig ng maliit na bahagi) + 'titing'.
original_explanation: This is the "diet" version of everything. Yung kanin na kasing laki lang ng pison, yung sahod na parang dumaan lang sa palad mo, o yung pasensya mo sa traffic sa EDSA bandang 5 PM. It's that tiny, almost non-existent amount. "Just a pinch."
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ipahayag ang napakaliit na dami ng isang bagay, mahahawakan man o hindi.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pahingi naman ako ng **katiting** na asukal para sa kape ko.","translation":"Can I have a **tiny bit** of sugar for my coffee?"},{"sentence":"Wala na akong **katiting** na pasensya para sa iyo.","translation":"I don't have even a **tiny bit** of patience left for you."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng paputok na mabilis na umiikot at lumilikha ng matinis na tunog na parang sumisirit bago sumabog.
original_explanation: Ah, the sound of a Filipino New Year! It’s that small, unassuming paputok that you light up and then it just goes srrrrrrt! across the pavement, scaring your tita and the neighborhood cats. It's not as grand as a Kwitis or Fountain, but it's the chaotic, ground-level fun that makes the celebration real.
usage_notes: A specific type of firecracker known for its whizzing sound, popular during New Year's celebrations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-ingat ang mga bata sa paglalaro ng **pampasirit** tuwing Bagong Taon.","translation":"The children were careful when playing with **whizzing firecrackers** during New Year."},{"sentence":"Ang ingay ng **pampasirit** ay narinig sa buong kalye.","translation":"The noise of the **pampasirit** was heard all over the street."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang panahon o araw na may maraming pag-ulan.
original_explanation: The default weather setting in the Philippines from June to November. The reason your laundry has been hanging for three days, your Grab fare just tripled, and everyone suddenly craves champorado or ramen. A **maulan** na hapon is the perfect excuse for a nap.
usage_notes: Describes the weather condition.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Maulan** na naman, kaya siguradong matrapik pauwi.","translation":"It's **rainy** again, so it's surely traffic on the way home."},{"sentence":"Magdala ka ng payong dahil mukhang **maulan** mamaya.","translation":"Bring an umbrella because it looks **rainy** later."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagpapakintab sa isang bagay, lalo na sa sahig o metal, sa pamamagitan ng pagkuskos.
original_explanation: This is the action that gives you that "see-your-own-reflection" shine on the floor. It's the "floor polisher" dance your tatay does on a Saturday morning. Sa sapatos, ang buli ang nagbibigay ng 'pogi' points bago ka pumasok sa office o sa date. 'Yung kintab na parang salamin.
usage_notes: Refers to the act of polishing. The verb form is often 'bulihin' or 'magbuli'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng **buli** ang sahig para magmukhang bago.","translation":"The floor needs a **polishing** to look new."},{"sentence":"Inutusan niya ang katulong na **bulihin** ang lahat ng sapatos na pilak.","translation":"He instructed the helper to **polish** all the silverware."}]

translation: to detonate, to cause an explosion
meaning_filipino: Ang maging sanhi ng isang pagsabog, literal man o matalinghaga, sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng pampasabog o paglikha ng kaguluhan.
original_explanation: Literally, this is what happens with fireworks on New Year's Eve. Figuratively, it's what you do when you drop some major *chismis* in the group chat and watch the reactions explode. It can also mean to make a grand, explosive entrance or reveal, like a celebrity's 'pasabog' new look.
usage_notes: Has both a literal meaning (to detonate a bomb) and a very common figurative meaning (to reveal something shocking or spectacular, often called a 'pasabog').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bawal **magpasabog** ng paputok malapit sa ospital.","translation":"It is forbidden to **detonate** firecrackers near a hospital."},{"sentence":"**Nagpasabog** ng balita ang sikat na aktres tungkol sa kanyang pagbubuntis.","translation":"The famous actress **dropped a bombshell** (lit. caused news to explode) about her pregnancy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nakatalaga upang magbantay, magprotekta, o magbigay ng babala laban sa panganib; isang bantay o tanod.
original_explanation: The OG security guard. Before CCTV and biometrics, you had the 'taliba'—the reliable 'manong' at the village gate who knows all the chismis but will keep you safe. They're the vanguards, the frontliners, the ones who stay awake so you can sleep. Like your BPO friends on the night shift, but for physical security.
usage_notes: Madalas na may mas pormal o pampanitikang dating kaysa sa 'guwardiya' o 'bantay'. Ito rin ang pangalan ng isang kilalang pahayagang Tagalog noon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga sundalo ay nagsisilbing **taliba** ng bayan.","translation":"The soldiers serve as the **sentinels** of the nation."},{"sentence":"Naglagay sila ng **taliba** sa tore upang magmasid sa mga paparating na kaaway.","translation":"They placed a **watchman** in the tower to look out for approaching enemies."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang marahan at malamig na ihip ng hangin.
original_explanation: That perfect breeze that hits you on a hot day, making you say 'Ah, sarap!' It's the 'aircon ng mayaman' when you're just sitting on the porch. It's the wind that carries the smell of your neighbor's barbecue or the scent of the sea. The opposite of the hot, sticky air you feel in traffic.
usage_notes: Almost always refers to a pleasant or gentle wind. For a strong wind, 'hangin' or 'unos' is used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap ang **simoy** ng hangin sa tabing-dagat tuwing umaga.","translation":"The **breeze** by the seashore is pleasant every morning."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman ko ang malamig na **simoy** ng Disyembre.","translation":"I felt the cold **breeze** of December."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang magiliw na pagpapahayag ng pagmamahal o paglalambing, karaniwang sa pamamagitan ng malumanay na salita, haplos, o kilos.
original_explanation: This is the uniquely Filipino brand of affection. It's not just love; it's that sweet, almost clingy, tender way of showing it. It's the 'pabebe' voice you use with your partner, the gentle nuzzle, the 'please, please, please' with puppy dog eyes. It’s the secret weapon for getting what you want, from forgiveness to the last piece of lechon.
usage_notes: A very common and important cultural concept. The verb form is 'maglambing' (to show affection) or 'lambingin' (to be the recipient of affection).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Punô ng **lambing** ang yakap ng isang ina.","translation":"A mother's hug is full of **tenderness**."},{"sentence":"Idinadaan niya sa **lambing** ang lahat ng kanyang hiling.","translation":"She gets everything she wants by using **sweet affection**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang indibidwal na hayop, halaman, o bahagi nito na kinukuha bilang halimbawa ng uri nito para sa siyentipikong pag-aaral o pagpapakita.
original_explanation: 'Yung ihi mo sa maliit na container na binibigay mo sa clinic for a drug test or urinalysis. O 'yung pinatuyong paruparo na naka-frame sa science lab. It's a sample of something, usually for analysis, and often kinda gross.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa kontekstong medikal at siyentipiko.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha sila ng **ispesimen** ng dugo para sa pagsusuri sa laboratoryo.","translation":"They took a blood **specimen** for laboratory testing."}]

translation: To ponder; to reflect; to contemplate.
meaning_filipino: Mag-isip nang malalim at masusi tungkol sa isang bagay; magnilay-nilay.
original_explanation: This is what you do at 3 AM, staring at the ceiling, wondering where your life is going, kung bakit ka niya sineen, or if you should finally buy that thing in your Shopee cart. It's the intellectual version of 'mag-emote'.
usage_notes: A more formal and literary term for deep thinking.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang umupo sa tabi ng bintana upang **maglimi** sa mga nagdaang pangyayari.","translation":"He likes to sit by the window to **ponder** on past events."},{"sentence":"Bigyan mo ako ng panahon para **maglimi** sa iyong alok.","translation":"Give me time to **contemplate** your offer."}]

translation: to insert in between, to intersperse
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagsisingit ng isang bagay sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang bagay.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'singit' na may panlaping 'sa-…-an'.
original_explanation: Ito yung ginagawa mo 'pag siksikan sa LRT tapos may nakita kang konting space, sisingit ka. O kaya 'pag nag-uusap yung dalawang kaibigan mo tapos bigla kang may sasabihing 'speaking of...' at sisingit ka sa usapan. The art of wedging yourself—or something else—in.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang pautos o pakiusap na anyo ng pandiwa. Ang 'sumingit' (um-) ay ang mas karaniwang anyo para sa aktor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **salingitan** ng biro ang aming seryosong usapan.","translation":"Don't **insert** a joke into our serious conversation."},{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **salingitan** mo ng bulaklak ang bawat pahina ng libro.","translation":"Please, **intersperse** a flower between each page of the book."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pansamantalang pagkawala ng pakiramdam o paninigas ng isang bahagi ng katawan, na karaniwang tinatawag na "pamamanhid" o "pulikat".
original_explanation: That feeling when you sit on your foot for too long while scrolling through TikTok, and then pagtayo mo, it's like a thousand tiny ants are having a party on your skin. That's pangimay. Or when your hand goes numb from holding your phone up while lying down. The struggle is real.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with manhid (numbness) or pulikat (cramp).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman ko ang **pangimay** sa aking mga binti matapos ang mahabang pag-upo.","translation":"I felt the **numbness** in my legs after sitting for a long time."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapataw ng buwis sa isang tao, ari-arian, o serbisyo. Sa konteksto ng agrikultura, ito ay isang sistema kung saan ang isang magsasaka ay nagbabayad ng bahagi ng ani bilang upa sa may-ari ng lupa.
original_explanation: The verb form of that thing that makes your payslip sad. 'Buwisan' is what the BIR does to you. Also, it's a throwback to our history classes—the old-school system where a farmer gives a cut of his harvest to the landlord just to be able to farm the land. Basically, someone's always getting a cut.
usage_notes: Has two main meanings: the general act of taxing, and the specific agricultural tenancy system. Context determines the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat **buwisan** ang mga malalaking korporasyon nang naaayon sa kanilang kita.","translation":"Large corporations should be **taxed** according to their income."},{"sentence":"Ang sistema ng **buwisan** sa bukid ay matagal nang isyu sa mga magsasaka.","translation":"The land tenancy **system** in the fields has long been an issue for farmers."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang taong may masamang reputasyon dahil sa mga iskandalosong gawain; maaari ring mangahulugang magulo o walang ayos.
original_explanation: This is the Marites-certified adjective. 'Yung kapitbahay mong laging may issue? Aliwaswas 'yan. It's the human equivalent of a messy room or a chaotic Twitter thread. It screams "drama" and "walang kaayusan." If your life is a mess, baka aliwaswas ka.
usage_notes: Has a strong negative connotation, often implying moral looseness or a lack of propriety. Can also describe a physical state of messiness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging paksa ng tsismis ang kanyang **aliwaswas** na pamumuhay.","translation":"Her **scandalous** lifestyle became the topic of gossip."},{"sentence":"Ang **aliwaswas** na silid ay kailangang linisin agad.","translation":"The **untidy** room needs to be cleaned immediately."}]

translation: to indulge oneself lavishly; to revel in abundance
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakasawa o lubos na pagtatamasa sa isang bagay, karaniwan ay sa karangyaan, pagkain, o kapangyarihan.
original_explanation: This is "magpasarap" on steroids. It's not just treating yourself; it's feasting like a king, often with a slightly negative connotation of greed or overindulgence. Think of corrupt politicians who "nagpapasasa sa kaban ng bayan" (revel in the nation's treasury). On a lighter note, it's you at an unli-samgyupsal buffet, determined to eat more than what you paid for. You're not just eating; you're indulging to the max.
usage_notes: Often has a negative connotation of greed or excessive self-gratification, but can also be used neutrally for indulging in something plentiful. The root word `pasa` is not the common one meaning 'to pass'. This is a fossilized form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Habang naghihirap ang mga mamamayan, patuloy na **nagpapasasa** sa yaman ang mga tiwaling opisyal.","translation":"While the citizens are suffering, the corrupt officials continue to **lavishly indulge** in wealth."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng matinding pagod sa katawan o isipan dahil sa labis na paggawa, stress, o pagkilos.
etymology: From ka- + pagod + -an, forming a noun that denotes the state or quality of being tired.
original_explanation: That feeling after a 12-hour shift, followed by 3 hours of traffic on EDSA, only to get home and realize you still have to do the dishes. It's the official state of being for most working adults. Your body is basically sending a low-batt notification.
usage_notes: 'Kapaguran' is a slightly more formal or literary term for 'pagod' (tiredness). It emphasizes the state or condition of being tired.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ramdam na ramdam ko ang **kapaguran** matapos ang buong linggong pagtatrabaho.","translation":"I really feel the **fatigue** after a whole week of work."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya inalintana ang **kapaguran** upang matapos lamang ang proyekto.","translation":"She ignored her **exhaustion** just to finish the project."}]

translation: to cause to be separated (from each other)
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o pagiging sanhi upang magkahiwalay ang isang grupo ng mga tao o bagay.
original_explanation: When the team leader says, 'Okay, team, **papaghiwa-hiwalayin** ko kayo into smaller groups for the breakout session.' Also, what your parents threaten to do to you and your jowa if they find out you're failing your classes.
usage_notes: The reduplication `hiwa-hiwalay` implies separating a group into multiple parts or pairs, not just splitting one thing in two. This is the causative form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para sa laro, **papaghiwa-hiwalayin** natin ang mga kalahok sa dalawang pangkat.","translation":"For the game, let's **have the participants separated** into two teams."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **papaghiwa-hiwalayin** ang magkakabarkadang laging magkakasama.","translation":"It's hard to **cause a group of friends who are always together to be separated**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang anak ng ibon o manok na hindi pa marunong lumipad.
original_explanation: The cute, fluffy baby bird that's totally dependent on its parents. Figuratively, it's the new hire in the office who you have to guide, the 'newbie' or 'fresher' who still needs a lot of hand-holding. They're still in their 'soft-launch' phase of life.
usage_notes: Often used in the plural 'mga inakay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinapakain ng inahing manok ang kanyang mga **inakay**.","translation":"The mother hen is feeding her **chicks**."},{"sentence":"May nahulog na **inakay** mula sa pugad.","translation":"A **fledgling** fell from the nest."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang anyong lupa sa tabi ng dagat o karagatan na karaniwang binubuo ng buhangin, bato, o maliliit na kabibe.
original_explanation: The default answer to 'Saan tayo sa long weekend?' It's where Filipinos flock for vitamin sea, some much-needed tan lines, and an endless supply of buko juice and grilled everything. The official uniform is tsinelas and board shorts.
usage_notes: Interchangeable with the English word 'beach'. 'Dalampasigan' is the more formal, literary Tagalog term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magbabakasyon kami sa **playa** ng Boracay sa susunod na buwan.","translation":"We will vacation at the **beach** in Boracay next month."},{"sentence":"Masarap maglakad sa **playa** habang papalubog ang araw.","translation":"It's nice to walk on the **beach** while the sun is setting."}]

meaning_filipino: Nakatambak sa maraming tumpok o bunton; paglalarawan sa mga bagay na nakasalansan nang hindi maayos.
original_explanation: This is the state of your laundry chair. You know, the one with clothes that are not dirty enough for the hamper but not clean enough for the closet. Buntun-bunton is also how you'd describe the ukay-ukay pile you have to dig through to find a hidden gem, or the mountain of paperwork on your desk before a deadline.
usage_notes: Reduplication of 'bunton' emphasizes the multiplicity or largeness of the piles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Buntun-bunton** ang mga labahin na kailangan kong ayusin ngayong weekend.","translation":"The laundry that I need to sort this weekend is **in heaps**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na bumibili ng mga produkto o serbisyo sa isang tindahan, pamilihan, o mula sa isang nagtitinda.
original_explanation: Ikaw 'to. The person who says 'pa-tawad po' even if the price is already fixed. The one who asks 'last price?' The hero of the economy, the lifeblood of Shopee and Lazada. The one who always has the right to be right, because 'the customer is always right.'
usage_notes: This is the noun form, meaning 'shopper'. It is a homonym of the verb form. Note the stress on the last syllable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumagsa ang mga **mamimili** sa mall dahil sa malaking sale.","translation":"The **shoppers** flocked to the mall because of the big sale."},{"sentence":"Bilang isang **mamimili**, karapatan mong malaman ang kalidad ng produktong iyong binibili.","translation":"As a **customer**, it is your right to know the quality of the product you are buying."}]

translation: let me touch; may I touch
meaning_filipino: Isang pakiusap na mahawakan o madama ang isang bagay gamit ang kamay.
original_explanation: The classic Filipino mall-goer's request. You see a nice shirt, you don't just look, you ask the saleslady, "Pahipo nga po." It's our way of quality checking, feeling the texture ('tela'). It's a request, not a demand, to engage the sense of touch. Be careful with the context though, or you might get a slap instead of a shirt!
usage_notes: Used as a polite request, typically in the imperative form. The tone and context are extremely important to avoid misinterpretation. It's almost always followed by 'nga' or 'po' to soften it.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pahipo** nga po ng tela, titingnan ko lang kung maganda.","translation":"**May I touch** the fabric, please? I'll just see if it's good."},{"sentence":"Sabi ng bata sa kanyang ina, '**Pahipo** naman ng alaga mong pusa.'","translation":"The child said to their mother, 'Can I **touch** your pet cat?'"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng muling paghalal sa isang tao sa parehong posisyon o katungkulan na kanyang kasalukuyang hinahawakan.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "reelección", na kombinasyon ng "re-" (muli) at "elección" (halalan).
original_explanation: It's like asking your boss for a contract renewal, but the boss is the entire voting public. This is the sequel to a politician's first term. They spend years putting up tarps with their faces on them for every birthday and fiesta, hoping you'll check their name on the ballot again. It's the ultimate performance review, and the campaign trail is their "pa-bebe" moment to win you back.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng politika at halalan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghahanda na ang kasalukuyang mayor para sa kanyang kampanya sa **reeleksiyon**.","translation":"The current mayor is now preparing for his **reelection** campaign."},{"sentence":"Ipinagbabawal ng konstitusyon ang **reeleksiyon** para sa pangulo.","translation":"The constitution prohibits **reelection** for the president."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking mamalyang hayop na may isa o dalawang umbok (hump) sa likod, karaniwang matatagpuan sa mga disyerto ng Aprika at Asya, at kilala sa kakayahang mabuhay nang matagal nang walang tubig.
original_explanation: Yung hayop sa Bible stories na may built-in water tank sa likod. Sila yung original Grab service sa disyerto. Kilala mo sila dahil sa Three Kings o kaya sa mga pelikulang may sand dunes. Parang kabayong pang-matinding init at uhaw.
usage_notes: Pangunahing kilala mula sa mga kuwento, zoo, o mga kontekstong may kaugnayan sa Gitnang Silangan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakita kami ng mga **kamelyo** noong nagbakasyon kami sa Gitnang Silangan.","translation":"We saw **camels** when we vacationed in the Middle East."},{"sentence":"Ang tatlong hari ay sinasabing nakasakay sa mga **kamelyo**.","translation":"The three kings are said to have ridden on **camels**."}]

meaning_filipino: Mag-ukol ng panahon at atensyon sa pagtingin sa isang bagay na gumagalaw o nagaganap, tulad ng pelikula, palabas, o laro.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `ma-` + `nood` (panonood). Ang 'n' sa 'nood' ay nadodoble.
original_explanation: The national pastime. It's what you do when there's a new K-drama series on Netflix, when your favorite team is playing in the PBA, or when there's a developing chismis between your neighbors. The verb form of 'Netflix and chill' or 'YouTube marathon.'
usage_notes: Ang 'n' ay dinodoble mula sa salitang-ugat na 'nood', isang karaniwang pangyayaring ponetika sa Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto mo bang **manood** ng sine sa Sabado?","translation":"Do you want **to watch** a movie on Saturday?"},{"sentence":"Libo-libong tao ang pumunta sa plasa para **manood** ng libreng konsiyerto.","translation":"Thousands of people went to the plaza **to watch** the free concert."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi nakagapos o nakatali; malaya sa anumang nagtatali o humahawak.
original_explanation: Like that dog in your neighborhood that roams freely, scaring delivery riders. Or that one friend who is "single and ready to mingle" with absolutely zero attachments. No strings attached, literally or figuratively.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for objects or animals, or figuratively for people and commitments.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakawala ang aso dahil **walang-tali** ito.","translation":"The dog got loose because it was **untied**."},{"sentence":"Gusto niyang mamuhay nang **walang-tali** sa anumang responsibilidad.","translation":"He wants to live **without being tied** to any responsibility."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglipat o naglagay ng datos o isang file mula sa isang lokal na sistema patungo sa isang sentral na sistema o sa internet.
original_explanation: Yung pag-post mo ng 100 photos from your Boracay trip para makita ng lahat na 'you're living your best life.' From your phone to the cloud, to everyone's feed. Mission accomplished, Team Kahit Di Na Kumain Basta May Pang-Post.
usage_notes: Standard Taglish for internet and computer usage, denoting a past action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nag-upload** na ako ng mga bagong pictures sa Facebook.","translation":"I already **uploaded** the new pictures to Facebook."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **nag-upload** ng video na ito?","translation":"Who **uploaded** this video?"}]

translation: to collapse; to fall flat on the ground
meaning_filipino: Biglaang pagbagsak sa lupa nang nakahiga, kadalasan dahil sa matinding pagod, sakit, pagkalasing, o pagkahilo.
original_explanation: The state you're in after a 16-hour shift, a brutal leg day at the gym, or seeing your Meralco bill. You don't just sit down; you dramatically collapse onto the nearest horizontal surface, usually your bed. It's the physical manifestation of 'I'm so done.'
usage_notes: Indicates an involuntary and often dramatic fall to a prostrate position.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa tindi ng pagod, **napahandusay** siya sa sahig pag-uwi.","translation":"Due to extreme fatigue, he **collapsed** on the floor upon arriving home."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking nag-aaral sa seminaryo upang maging isang pari.
original_explanation: Yung friend mo na seryoso sa pag-aaral para maging pari. Sila yung may pinakamalinis na lecture notes at laging on-time sa Misa. Basically, a future 'Father' in training. The OG 'good boy'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pinsan ko ay isang **seminarista** sa San Carlos Seminary.","translation":"My cousin is a **seminarian** at San Carlos Seminary."},{"sentence":"Tumutulong sa mga gawain sa parokya ang mga **seminarista** tuwing bakasyon.","translation":"The **seminarians** help with parish activities during their vacation."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang biglaan at sabay-sabay na pagdating o pagdagsa ng maraming tao o bagay sa isang lugar.
original_explanation: Picture this: 11.11 sale on Shopee goes live at midnight. That mad scramble of people adding to cart and checking out? That's 'pagdagasa'. It's the human version of a flash flood, usually for a sale, a buffet, or getting on the MRT during rush hour.
usage_notes: Most commonly used in its verb forms like 'dumagasa' (to rush in) or 'dinagasa' (was rushed). The root word itself is rarely used alone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dumagasa** ang mga tao sa mall nang mag-anunsyo ng malaking sale.","translation":"People **rushed in** to the mall when they announced a big sale."},{"sentence":"Ang entablado ay **dinagasa** ng mga tagahanga pagkatapos ng konsiyerto.","translation":"The stage was **swarmed** by fans after the concert."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang pangunahing trabaho ay magpasok ng datos o impormasyon sa isang computer system.
original_explanation: The unsung hero of many offices, especially BPOs and government agencies. Sila 'yung nagta-type ng sandamakmak na data into spreadsheets or systems all day. Kung may trabahong nangangailangan ng mabilis na daliri, pasensya na kasing haba ng EDSA traffic, at mata na sanay sa computer screen—'yan ang trabaho ng isang encoder. Sila ang dahilan kung bakit digital na ang records mo.
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang katawagan sa trabaho sa Pilipinas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghahanap ang kumpanya ng sampung bagong **encoder**.","translation":"The company is looking for ten new **data entry clerks**."},{"sentence":"Mabilis mag-type ang **encoder** na iyon, halos hindi mo makita ang kanyang mga daliri.","translation":"That **encoder** types so fast, you can barely see their fingers."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maliit na kawit na gawa sa metal o plastik, ginagamit sa paggawa ng gantsilyo o crochet.
original_explanation: This is your lola's magic wand. With this tiny hook, she can turn a simple ball of yarn into a doily, a sweater, or even a cute amigurumi character. It's the OG 3D printer, but for textiles.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'gantsilyo' which refers to the craft itself, but 'gusanilyo' is specifically the tool.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawawala ang **gusanilyo** na bigay sa akin ni Lola.","translation":"The **crochet hook** that Grandma gave me is missing."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mo ng mas manipis na **gusanilyo** para sa sinulid na iyan.","translation":"You need a thinner **crochet hook** for that thread."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan, karaniwang isang bangkito na may nakausling metal na may matatalim na ngipin, na ginagamit sa pagkayod ng niyog.
original_explanation: The OG food processor for coconuts. It's that low stool in your lola's kitchen with a terrifyingly spiky metal tongue sticking out. You sit on it and grate a coconut half, praying you don't scrape your knuckles. It's a provincial kitchen staple.
usage_notes: While it can mean any grater, it almost exclusively refers to the traditional Filipino coconut grater stool.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa paggamit ng **kudkuran** para hindi ka masugatan.","translation":"Be careful when using the **coconut grater** so you don't get hurt."},{"sentence":"Kinalawang na ang lumang **kudkuran** ni Lola.","translation":"Grandma's old **coconut grater** has rusted."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang parisukat na piraso ng tela, karaniwang may disenyo, na isinusuot sa ulo, leeg, o braso bilang palamuti o proteksyon.
etymology: From Spanish 'bandana', from Hindi 'bāndhnū' (a method of tie-dyeing).
original_explanation: That square piece of cloth that has a thousand uses. It's a fashion statement for rockstars and '90s kids, a sweatband for your zumba-tita, a makeshift face mask during the pandemic, and the official uniform accessory of Axl Rose. It's the ultimate multi-tool of your wardrobe.
usage_notes: The spelling and pronunciation are very similar to the English word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatali ang pulang **bandana** sa kanyang ulo.","translation":"A red **bandana** was tied on his head."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang **bandana** para punasan ang kanyang pawis.","translation":"He used his **bandana** to wipe his sweat."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang samahan ng mga estado, organisasyon, o tao na nagkakaisa para sa isang karaniwang layunin habang pinapanatili ang kani-kanilang kalayaan o awtonomiya.
original_explanation: Imagine a group project where everyone is the leader of their own subgroup, and they only meet up to agree on the big stuff, like what to order for pizza. It's like an alliance of different student orgs for a university-wide event. They're together, but still have their own 'silos' and drama.
usage_notes: Primarily used in political, historical, or formal organizational contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kompederasyon** ng mga katutubong tribo ay nagpulong upang talakayin ang kanilang mga karapatan.","translation":"The **confederation** of indigenous tribes met to discuss their rights."},{"sentence":"Bumuo sila ng isang **kompederasyon** ng mga mangangalakal sa rehiyon.","translation":"They formed a **confederation** of merchants in the region."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang tao, bagay, o kalagayan na kaawa-awa, kahabag-habag, o kalunos-lunos.
etymology: Nagmula sa unlaping `ka-` at salitang ugat na `awa` (pity, mercy).
original_explanation: This is the feeling you get when you see a stray kitten in the rain, or your friend who got ghosted again. 'Kawawa naman.' It's a mix of pity and sympathy. It's the default Filipino reaction to someone in an unfortunate situation, from failing an exam to getting stuck in epic EDSA traffic.
usage_notes: Nagpapahayag ng simpatya o awa. Maaaring magkaroon ng bahagyang mapangmatang tono depende sa konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kawawa** naman ang batang umiiyak sa isang tabi.","translation":"How **pitiful** the child crying in the corner is."},{"sentence":"Naging **kawawa** ang kanyang itsura matapos ang mahabang paglalakbay.","translation":"His appearance became **miserable** after the long journey."}]
