meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na gumagawa ng isang bagay, kadalasan ay masama o ilegal, kapalit ng pera.
etymology: From "bayad" (payment). The stress shift to the last syllable gives it a negative connotation.
original_explanation: This has a totally different, more negative vibe. When used as an adjective, it means "for hire" or "paid," often with a shady connotation, like a "hired goon" or a biased media person ("**bayarang** media"). As a noun, it's a derogatory term for a prostitute. It's the difference between "bayáran" (to pay) and "bayarán" (someone who is paid to do dirty work). Pronunciation and stress are key!
usage_notes: The stress is on the last syllable (ba-ya-RAN) which distinguishes it from the verb 'bayáran' /ba-YA-ran/. This term is often derogatory.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binalaan siya na huwag magtiwala sa mga saksing **bayaran**.","translation":"He was warned not to trust the **paid** witnesses."},{"sentence":"Isang pulitikong **bayaran** ang nagpakalat ng maling impormasyon.","translation":"A **mercenary** politician spread the false information."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng lugaw na may manok, luya, at nilagyan ng pampalasa, karaniwang inihahain nang mainit.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "arroz caldoso," na nangangahulugang "brothy rice."
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino comfort food, especially when you're sick or it's raining. It's like lugaw that went to a private school and came back with chicken and a whole lot of ginger attitude. Best served with calamansi, patis, and a hard-boiled egg. It's the hug in a bowl you didn't know you needed.
usage_notes: Often garnished with toasted garlic, spring onions, and sometimes safflower (kasubha) for color.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpaluto si nanay ng **arrozcaldo** dahil nilalagnat ako.","translation":"Mom had **arrozcaldo** cooked because I have a fever."},{"sentence":"Masarap higupin ang mainit na sabaw ng **arrozcaldo** tuwing umuulan.","translation":"It's nice to sip the hot broth of **arrozcaldo** when it's raining."}]

meaning_filipino: Binubuo ng iba't ibang uri, klase, o piraso; halo-halo.
original_explanation: Like the biscuit can at your lola's house that might contain Fita, Marie, or a sewing kit—it's a gamble! Surtido is the official term for 'halo-halo' or 'assorted'. Think of a box of donuts with different flavors or the 'mixed seafood' platter at a restaurant.
usage_notes: Often used to describe food items, merchandise, or a collection of different things.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng isang kahong **surtido** na biskwit.","translation":"I bought a box of **assorted** biscuits."},{"sentence":"Nag-aalok sila ng **surtido** na mga kakanin tuwing Pasko.","translation":"They offer **assorted** rice cakes every Christmas."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi ayon sa katotohanan; walang batayan sa realidad; kasinungalingan.
original_explanation: The official status of "Okay lang ako" when you're clearly not okay. It's the polite term for fake news, chismis, or your friend's promise to be there in 5 minutes when they haven't even taken a shower yet. If it's not real, it's di-totoo.
usage_notes: A compound word formed by the negative prefix 'di-' and 'totoo'. It is synonymous with 'hindi totoo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kumakalat na balita tungkol sa kanya ay **di-totoo**.","translation":"The news spreading about him is **untrue**."},{"sentence":"Napatunayang **di-totoo** ang kanyang mga paratang.","translation":"Her accusations were proven to be **false**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang aparatong elektroniko na isinusuot sa loob o likod ng tainga upang mapalakas ang tunog para sa isang taong may kahinaan sa pandinig.
etymology: From `pang-` (instrument for) + `ulinig` (to hear faintly, to perceive a sound).
original_explanation: Basically, it's the tech support for your ears. When the world sounds like it's on mute or you keep saying 'Ha?' in every conversation about the latest 'chismis' (gossip), you might need a pang-ulinig. It's the device that turns the volume of life back up.
usage_notes: This is a more formal or technical term. The English term 'hearing aid' is more commonly used in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nirekomenda ng doktor na gumamit ng **pang-ulinig** ang aking lolo.","translation":"The doctor recommended that my grandfather use a **hearing aid**."},{"sentence":"Moderno na ang mga **pang-ulinig** ngayon at halos hindi na napapansin.","translation":"Modern **hearing aids** are now almost unnoticeable."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng kasalukuyang paglilinis gamit ang walis.
original_explanation: Eto yung eksenang aabutan mo tuwing Sabado ng umaga. May hawak na walis tingting sa labas o walis tambo sa loob. Usually may kasamang radio na nakatutok sa AM station or a 'pang-linis' playlist on Spotify. Ingat sa alikabok!
usage_notes: Ang unlaping 'nag-' at ang pag-uulit ng unang pantig ng salitang-ugat ('wa') ay nagpapahiwatig ng isang kasalukuyan, nagaganap, o nakagawiang kilos.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Araw-araw **nagwawalis** ang aming kapitbahay sa tapat ng kanilang bahay.","translation":"Our neighbor **sweeps** in front of their house every day."},{"sentence":"Teka lang, **nagwawalis** pa ako ng sahig.","translation":"Wait a moment, I'm still **sweeping** the floor."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na kasuotan na isinusuot ng babaeng ikakasal sa araw ng kanyang kasal.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "traje de boda", na nangangahulugang "kasuotan para sa kasal".
original_explanation: The most important OOTD (Outfit Of The Day) of a woman's life. It's the dress you've probably been pinning on Pinterest since high school. One day of wearing it costs more than your entire month's salary, and after that, it just sits in a box, full of memories and maybe a wine stain or two.
usage_notes: Isang partikular na uri ng damit pangkasal. Ang "trahe" ay pangkalahatang damit, ngunit ang "trahe-de-boda" ay para lamang sa kasal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Simple lang ngunit elegante ang kanyang **trahe-de-boda**.","translation":"Her **wedding gown** was simple yet elegant."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang buong baboy na niluto sa ibabaw ng nagbabagang uling habang dahan-dahang iniikot sa isang kawayan o bakal na tuhugan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na "lechón" (biik o batang baboy).
original_explanation: The ultimate party centerpiece. If you see a lechon at a party, you know it's a serious celebration. It's the crispy-skinned, juicy-meated star that makes everyone forget their diet. The best part? Fighting over the crispy balat (skin) with your titos and titas. Sawsawan is a must!
usage_notes: Bagaman ang orihinal na kahulugan ay 'biik', sa Pilipinas, ang 'lechon' ay tumutukoy sa anumang edad ng baboy na niluto nang buo sa ganitong paraan. Ang baybay na 'litson' ay ginagamit din.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi kumpleto ang pista kung walang **lechon**.","translation":"A fiesta isn't complete without a **roasted pig**."},{"sentence":"Pakikuha ako ng balat ng **lechon**, 'yung pinakamalutong.","translation":"Please get me some **lechon** skin, the crispiest one."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian, kalagayan, o diwa ng pagiging isang babae.
original_explanation: It's the essence of being a woman, your "divine feminine energy." It’s not just about biology; it's the whole package—the strength, the grace, the 'marupok' moments, the ability to find anything anyone has lost in the house, and the power to slay, whether in the boardroom or at the palengke.
usage_notes: Often used to discuss gender, identity, and the qualities associated with being a woman.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagdiriwang sa Buwan ng Kababaihan ang lakas at **pagkababae**.","translation":"Women's Month celebrates the strength and **womanhood**."},{"sentence":"Nahanap niya ang kanyang tunay na **pagkababae** nang maging ina siya.","translation":"She found her true **femininity** when she became a mother."}]

meaning_filipino: Salungat, laban, o hindi naaayon sa isang pamantayan, paniniwala, o inaasahan.
original_explanation: 'Yung sinabi mong "I'm okay" pero deep inside, hindi pala. **Taliwas** ang sinasabi mo sa nararamdaman mo. It's when your actions don't match your words, like saying you're on a diet while holding a box of pizza. Total opposite, bes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kaniyang mga kilos ay **taliwas** sa kaniyang mga ipinangako.","translation":"His actions are **contrary** to his promises."},{"sentence":"**Taliwas** sa inaakala ng marami, hindi siya ang may kasalanan.","translation":"**Contrary** to what many believe, he is not the one at fault."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng ngiti; isang ekspresyon ng kasiyahan, pagkatuwa, o pagbati sa pamamagitan ng pag-unat ng mga labi.
original_explanation: Yung itsura mo kapag pumasok na 'yung 13th-month pay. Or when your crush finally views your IG story. It's the universal "OK lang ako" mask, even when you're dying inside. A flight attendant's default setting.
usage_notes: The most common word for the state of smiling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Palagi siyang **nakangiti** tuwing umaga.","translation":"She is always **smiling** every morning."},{"sentence":"Sinalubong niya kami nang **nakangiti**.","translation":"He greeted us while **smiling**."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa literal na kahulugan, ito ay kidlat na tumatama sa lupa. Sa kolokyal na gamit, ito ay isang ekspresyon ng matinding galit, pagkadismaya, o isang pagmumura.
original_explanation: The OG Filipino curse word before "putangina" became mainstream. It literally means "lightning strike," as in "I hope you get struck by lightning." It's what your lola would mutter under her breath when you break her favorite vase. "Lintik ka!" is the classic, full-throated version, perfect for when someone cuts you off in traffic or steals your lunch from the office fridge.
usage_notes: "Lintik ka!" is a common curse phrase. It can also be used as an adjective for something difficult or annoying, e.g., "Lintik na traffic 'to!" (This damn traffic!).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lintik** ka! Bakit mo tinapon ang pagkain?","translation":"**Damn** you! Why did you throw away the food?"},{"sentence":"Nabalitaan kong tinamaan ng **lintik** ang puno ng niyog sa kanilang bukid.","translation":"I heard a **lightning strike** hit the coconut tree in their field."}]

translation: offering; effect; thing that is brought about
meaning_filipino: Ang sanhi o resulta ng isang pangyayari; paghahandog o pag-aalay.
original_explanation: This is a deep word. It's what something brings or causes, usually something significant like joy or suffering ('Ang dulot ng pag-ibig mo...'). It's the 'effect' in 'cause and effect'. It can also mean an offering, like what you give to ancient gods in a fantasy movie. It’s the consequence, the result, the ‘what it brings to the table’.
usage_notes: More commonly encountered as 'dulot'. 'Dulit' can feel more poetic or archaic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kaligayahang **dulit** mo sa akin ay walang kapantay.","translation":"The happiness you **bring** me is unparalleled."},{"sentence":"Naghanda sila ng **dulit** para sa mga anito.","translation":"They prepared an **offering** for the spirits."},{"sentence":"Ano ang **dulit** ng bagong batas na ito sa mamamayan?","translation":"What is the **effect** of this new law on the citizens?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang utusan o kasambahay, lalo na noong unang panahon.
etymology: From "bata" (child/young person) + "-an", possibly implying a young person in service.
original_explanation: An old-school word for a house helper or servant. You'd probably hear this more from your lola or in historical dramas. Today, we use 'kasambahay.' It's also the name of a province famous for the Death March, but the word itself has this separate, older meaning.
usage_notes: This term is now considered archaic and potentially classist. "Kasambahay" is the preferred modern term. It is also the name of a province in the Philippines, which is the more common usage today.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **bataan** ng mayamang pamilya ay tapat sa kanila.","translation":"The rich family's **servant** was loyal to them."},{"sentence":"Sa mga lumang nobela, madalas may karakter na **bataan**.","translation":"In old novels, there is often a **servant** character."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tanyag na lutuing Pilipino na karaniwang binubuo ng karne o gulay na ibinabad at niluto sa suka, toyo, bawang, paminta, at dahon ng laurel.
original_explanation: The unofficial national dish of the Philippines and the ultimate test of any Filipino household's cooking skills. Every family has their own secret recipe, leading to endless debates: "With soy sauce or without?" "Dry or saucy?" "With sugar or not?" It's the go-to baon, the star of any handaan, and the dish that tastes even better the next day.
usage_notes: Refers to the specific Filipino dish. The Spanish origin refers to a marinade, but in the Philippines, it refers to the entire cooking process and the resulting dish.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paborito kong ulam na luto ni nanay ay **adobo**.","translation":"My favorite dish cooked by my mom is **adobo**."},{"sentence":"Magdala ka ng kanin, may natirang **adobo** mula kagabi.","translation":"Bring some rice, there's leftover **adobo** from last night."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-apaw o pagtapon ng likido mula sa isang lalagyan dahil sa sobrang puno nito.
original_explanation: Yung nangyayari sa kanin kapag naparami ka ng sabaw. O yung luha mo na biglang um-**awas** nung nanonood ka ng K-drama. Pwede ring sa sweldo, "Wala pang 15/30, **awas** na agad ang pera ko sa dami ng bayarin."
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin para sa mga likido ngunit maaari ding gamitin sa metaporikal na paraan para sa damdamin o pera. Maaari ring maging pandiwa ('umawas').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagdulot ng baha ang **awas** ng tubig mula sa ilog.","translation":"The **overflow** of water from the river caused a flood."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya napigilan ang **awas** ng kanyang damdamin.","translation":"She could not stop the **overflow** of her emotions."}]

translation: to run away in different directions; to scatter by running
meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay na pagtakbo ng isang grupo ng tao o hayop sa iba't ibang direksyon, karaniwan dahil sa takot o gulat.
etymology: From mag- + pa- + takbuh- + -an. A complex verb form indicating a sudden, collective, and often chaotic action.
original_explanation: This is what happens when someone shouts 'May ipis!' in a room full of people, or 'Libre!' at a corporate event. It's chaotic, simultaneous running. It’s the physical manifestation of the 'panic' button being hit by a group. Everyone for themselves!
usage_notes: The '-an' suffix combined with 'magpa-' often denotes a simultaneous, reciprocal, or chaotic group action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagpanakbuhan** ang mga tao nang biglang umulan nang malakas.","translation":"The people **scattered by running** when it suddenly rained hard."},{"sentence":"Nang makarinig sila ng putok, **nagpanakbuhan** ang mga bata sa takot.","translation":"When they heard a gunshot, the children **ran away in different directions** in fear."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pampublikong sasakyan sa Pilipinas na karaniwang gawa mula sa mga segunda-manong military jeep ng Estados Unidos na pinahaba at pinalamutian nang husto.
original_explanation: The one and only "Hari ng Kalsada." Your mobile art gallery, sauna, and concert hall rolled into one. Ang sasakyan kung saan mo matututunan ang magic words na "bayad po" at "para po." It's more fun in the Philippines, and it's definitely more crowded in a dyip.
usage_notes: Isang pambansang simbolo ng Pilipinas. Ang mas tamang baybay ay "dyipni" (jeepney) ngunit karaniwang tinatawag na "dyip" sa kolokyal na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo naman po ng bayad sa **dyip**.","translation":"Please pass the fare on the **jeep**."},{"sentence":"Puno na ang **dyip**, sa bubong ka na lang sumakay!","translation":"The **jeep** is full, just ride on the roof!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tungkulin, posisyon, o kalagayan ng pagiging isang ministro, maging sa gobyerno o sa simbahan.
original_explanation: This is the job title that comes with a big office, a lot of meetings, and either a government seal or a holy book. It's the 'state of being a minister', whether you're handling foreign affairs or saving souls.
usage_notes: Can refer to a political cabinet minister or a religious minister/pastor. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa kanyang **pagkaministro** sa kalusugan, marami siyang naipasa na batas.","translation":"During his **tenure as minister** of health, he passed many laws."},{"sentence":"Itinalaga niya ang kanyang buhay sa **pagkaministro** sa mga mahihirap.","translation":"He dedicated his life to the **ministry** for the poor."}]

translation: to be crushed into powder; to crouch or huddle
meaning_filipino: Maging durog at pino na parang pulbos; o umupo o tumayo nang nakabaluktot at nakatago, karaniwan dahil sa takot o lamig.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `ma-` at salitang ugat na `yukmok` (powder/huddle).
original_explanation: Ever felt so small and defeated you just want to curl up in a corner? 'Yun ang mayukmok. Or, think of a biscuit that got totally annihilated at the bottom of your bag—nayukmok na, pure dust na lang. This word covers both being physically crushed to powder and emotionally/physically huddling to make yourself small.
usage_notes: Isang pambihirang salita na may dalawang magkaibang kahulugan. Ang kahulugang 'umupo nang nakabaluktot' ay mas karaniwan sa panitikan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nayukmok** ang biskwit sa loob ng kanyang bag.","translation":"The biscuit **was crushed into powder** inside her bag."},{"sentence":"Sa isang sulok, **nayukmok** ang bata dahil sa takot sa kulog.","translation":"In a corner, the child **crouched** in fear of the thunder."}]

meaning_filipino: Maruming tubig na hindi umaagos, karaniwang matatagpuan sa mga kanal, estero, o mabababang lugar pagkatapos ng ulan.
original_explanation: That nasty, smelly puddle of water that's been sitting there for days. It's the breeding ground for mosquitoes and smells like a science experiment gone wrong. You know, the kind of water you accidentally step in while wearing brand new white sneakers. The bane of every commuter's existence during rainy season.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa mabaho at hindi gumagalaw na tubig.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iwasang magtampisaw sa **pusali** para hindi magkasakit.","translation":"Avoid playing in the **stagnant water** to not get sick."},{"sentence":"Ang baho ng **pusali** sa gilid ng kalsada.","translation":"The **stagnant water** on the side of the road stinks."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang isang pangkat ng mga tao na naninirahan sa isang tiyak na lugar tulad ng isang bayan, lungsod, o bansa; ang kalipunan ng mga mamamayan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'bayan' (town, country, people).
original_explanation: It's the whole squad, the barangay, the nation. Basically, "the people". Kapag sinabing "para sa pamamayan", it means for everyone—from the Marites next door to the CEO in Makati. It's the collective 'us' in a specific place.
usage_notes: A more formal term for 'community' or 'the public'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagkakaisa ng **pamamayan** ang susi sa pag-unlad ng bansa.","translation":"The unity of the **citizenry** is the key to the nation's progress."},{"sentence":"Tungkulin ng pamahalaan na pagsilbihan ang **pamamayan**.","translation":"It is the government's duty to serve the **populace**."}]

translation: to preach; to give advice; to lecture
meaning_filipino: Magbigay ng payo, pangaral, o sermon, karaniwan tungkol sa moralidad, relihiyon, o tamang pag-uugali.
original_explanation: This is what a priest does on Sunday, what your parents do when you come home late, and what your friend does when they give you unsolicited 'love advice.' It's the act of giving a sermon or a lecture. It can be helpful (from a mentor) or annoying (when it's 'pangaral' you didn't ask for).
usage_notes: Can have a positive connotation (to teach, to guide) or a slightly negative one (to lecture, to nag). The noun form is 'pangaral' (sermon, moral lesson).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tungkulin ng mga magulang na **mangaral** sa kanilang mga anak.","translation":"It is the duty of parents to **give moral guidance** to their children."},{"sentence":"Ayoko nang makinig, puro **mangaral** na lang ang ginagawa niya.","translation":"I don't want to listen anymore, all he does is **lecture**."}]

translation: to move away; to distance something
meaning_filipino: Dalhin o ilagay ang isang bagay o tao sa isang lugar na malayo; ihiwalay.
original_explanation: Ginagawa mo 'to sa toxic ex mo. You block them, unfriend them, and generally ilayo mo ang sarili mo. Or, utos ng magulang, "Ilayo mo 'yan sa apoy, masusunog 'yan!" It's creating physical or emotional distance.
usage_notes: The focus is on the object being moved away. The actor is the one causing the distancing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **ilayo** mo ang mga bata sa matatalas na bagay.","translation":"Please, **move** the children **away** from sharp objects."},{"sentence":"**Inilayo** niya ang kanyang sarili mula sa gulo.","translation":"He **distanced** himself from the trouble."}]

translation: to send by mail, to mail
meaning_filipino: Ipahatid o ipadala ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay sulat o pakete, sa pamamagitan ng serbisyo ng koreo.
original_explanation: Before PMs, DMs, and emails, this was the OG way to send your love letter or your resumé. You go to the post office, buy a stamp, and pray to the high heavens it actually arrives. Today, it's what you do when you need to send a physical document for a government requirement and they don't accept LBC.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ikoreo** mo na ang mga imbitasyon para sa kasal natin.","translation":"Please **mail** the invitations for our wedding now."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **ikoreo** ang bayad sa kuryente.","translation":"Don't forget to **mail** the electricity payment."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng karbohidrat (carbohydrate) na matatagpuan sa mga pagkaing tulad ng kanin, patatas, at tinapay.
original_explanation: 'Yung dahilan kung bakit masarap ang kanin at French fries. 'Yung sinisisi mo kapag tumataba ka pero hindi mo pa rin maiwasang kumain ng extra rice. 'Less starch daw para pumayat, pero paano na ang unli-rice?'
usage_notes: The English word is often used in conversations about diet and nutrition, while 'gawgaw' or 'almirol' is used for cornstarch in cooking.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang bawasan ang pagkain ng mga pagkaing mataas sa **starch**.","translation":"She is trying to reduce her intake of foods high in **starch**."},{"sentence":"Ang kanin ay isang pangunahing pinagkukunan ng **starch** sa diyeta ng mga Pilipino.","translation":"Rice is a primary source of **starch** in the Filipino diet."}]

translation: the act of taking a path; traversing
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagdaan o paglakbay sa isang landas, daan, o kurso, lalo na kung ito ay mahirap o hindi pa gasgas.
etymology: From `pag-` (nominalizing prefix) + `tahak` (to traverse, forge a path).
original_explanation: Think of this as the 'choose your own adventure' verb. It’s not just walking, it's *traversing*. It’s what you do when you take the 'scenic route' home to avoid traffic, or when you decide to shift careers from accounting to being a vlogger. It’s the **pagtahak** of a new *landas*.
usage_notes: Has a slightly formal or literary feel. Often used metaphorically for life journeys or career paths.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagtahak** sa landas ng pagnenegosyo ay puno ng panganib.","translation":"The **act of taking** the path of entrepreneurship is full of risks."}]

meaning_filipino: Umiyak nang malakas at may kasamang hikbi at tunog na nagmumula sa lalamunan dahil sa matinding damdamin.
original_explanation: This isn't just 'iyak'. This is ugly crying. The kind you do after the season finale of your favorite K-drama, or when you see your credit card bill after a 12.12 sale. It's a full-body, can't-breathe, noisy sob fest. Peak teleserye moment.
usage_notes: Past tense. Describes a very intense and audible form of crying.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Humagulgol** ang bata nang hindi siya bilhan ng laruan.","translation":"The child **wailed** when they didn't buy him a toy."},{"sentence":"Nang malaman niya ang masamang balita, napaupo na lang siya at **humagulgol**.","translation":"When she heard the bad news, she just sat down and **sobbed loudly**."}]

translation: to journey with liquor (neologism); to travel (non-standard)
meaning_filipino: Isang salitang hindi karaniwan na maaaring mangahulugang paglalakbay habang may dalang alak o naiinom. Ito ay posibleng isang maling pagbaybay o pagbuo ng salitang 'maglakbay'.
etymology: Likely a modern portmanteau of 'alak' (liquor) and 'lakbay' (travel).
original_explanation: This word is a bit of a mystery, a rare Pokemon in the Tagalog world. It's likely a typo for **maglakbay** (to travel). But if we break it down, 'alak' (liquor) + 'lakbay' (journey), it could be a modern slang for 'to go on a trip with booze,' like a beach trip with the barkada. So, is it a typo or a cool new word for a drunken adventure? For academic purposes, use 'maglakbay'. For your next La Union trip, maybe 'mag-alakbay' fits better.
usage_notes: This is not a standard or recognized Filipino word. Its use is extremely rare and may be considered incorrect or a neologism. The standard word for 'to travel' is 'maglakbay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Baka ang ibig mong sabihin ay **maglakbay**? Hindi pamilyar ang salitang **mag-alakbay**.","translation":"Perhaps you mean **to travel**? The word **mag-alakbay** is not familiar."},{"sentence":"Plano ng barkada na **mag-alakbay** sa Zambales sa susunod na linggo, dala ang isang case ng beer.","translation":"The friends plan to **go on a boozy trip** to Zambales next week, bringing a case of beer."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay, gawain, o pangyayari na nakakaantala, nakakagambala, o nagdudulot ng sagabal.
etymology: Possibly from Malay 'bala' (army, troop), implying the commotion they cause.
original_explanation: That feeling when someone messages you 'urgent' but it's just for chismis. Or when you're about to leave the house and your tita asks you to do one more thing. 'Pasensya na sa abala' is the national anthem of anyone interrupting your day.
usage_notes: Often used in apologies like 'Pasensya na sa abala' (Sorry for the inconvenience). Pronunciation is key: stress on the first syllable /A-ba-la/ distinguishes it from the adjective 'abala' (busy).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pasensya na sa **abala**, pero maaari bang magtanong?","translation":"Sorry for the **disturbance**, but may I ask a question?"}]

meaning_filipino: Kasalukuyang nakikibahagi sa isang laro o anumang gawaing panlibangan.
etymology: The prefix 'nag-' and the reduplication of the first syllable 'la-' marks the progressive aspect (present, ongoing action).
original_explanation: This could mean kids playing patintero outside, or you, a full-grown adult, **playing** Mobile Legends until 4 AM. It's also what your crush is doing with your feelings. 'Huwag ka nang umasa, **naglalaro** lang 'yan sa feelings mo.' (Don't get your hopes up, he's just **playing** with your feelings.)
usage_notes: The progressive aspect (present tense) of 'maglaro'. Can be used literally for games or figuratively for toying with emotions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masayang **naglalaro** ng basketball ang mga kabataan sa court.","translation":"The youth are happily **playing** basketball on the court."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maingay, baka masira ang konsentrasyon ng kapatid mong **naglalaro** ng chess.","translation":"Don't be noisy, you might break your sibling's concentration who is **playing** chess."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang partikular na rehiyon o bahagi ng isang lugar, gusali, o espasyo; isang sakop na pook.
original_explanation: In the Philippines, 'area' is more than just a location. It's your territory, your turf. "Taga-saan ka?" is often followed by "Saang area?" It's how we map our social circles. Also used by security guards: "Sir, bawal po diyan. Restricted area." It's the space you're either supposed to be in or definitely not.
usage_notes: Widely used in everyday conversation, often interchangeably with "lugar" or "pook".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malakas ang ulan sa aming **area**.","translation":"The rain is heavy in our **area**."},{"sentence":"Nag-iikot ang mga tanod sa buong **area** ng subdivision.","translation":"The village watchmen are patrolling the whole **area** of the subdivision."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lugar kung saan isinasagawa ang paglalaba, maaaring isang bahagi ng bahay o isang pampublikong establisyimento.
original_explanation: This is the place where the magic (or the chore) happens. It can be the laundry area in your backyard, or the self-service laundromat where you meet your neighbors and exchange chismis while waiting for the spin cycle to finish. The modern-day community well.
usage_notes: Can refer to a private laundry area or a commercial laundry shop (laundromat).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May bagong bukas na **labadahan** sa kanto.","translation":"There's a newly opened **laundromat** at the corner."},{"sentence":"Ilagay mo ang washing machine sa **labadahan** sa likod-bahay.","translation":"Put the washing machine in the **laundry area** at the backyard."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng bakawan (mangrove) na may mapuputing bulaklak na hugis bituin. Sinasabing dito nagmula ang pangalan ng Maynila ('May-nilad' o mayroong nilad).
etymology: The name of Manila is a Hispanicized form of Tagalog 'may-nilad' (having nilad plants).
original_explanation: This is the OG plant that gave Manila its name, or so the story goes. Before skyscrapers and traffic, there was just a lot of this mangrove. Think of it as the city's botanical godparent. 'May-nilad' means 'there is nilad here.'
usage_notes: Primarily used in historical or botanical contexts, especially when discussing the etymology of 'Manila'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinasabing sagana sa halamang **nilad** ang pampang ng Ilog Pasig noong unang panahon.","translation":"It is said that the banks of the Pasig River were abundant with the **nilad** plant in ancient times."},{"sentence":"Ang pangalang Maynila ay hango sa 'may **nilad**', na tumutukoy sa pagkakaroon ng ganitong halaman sa lugar.","translation":"The name Manila is derived from 'may **nilad**', referring to the presence of this plant in the area."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang istruktura, kadalasang may mga maliliit na butas o kahon, na ginawa upang maging tirahan ng mga alagang kalapati.
original_explanation: A pigeon condo. It's that multi-level wooden box you see on rooftops where racing pigeons live, train, and probably gossip about the humans below. It's the avian equivalent of a high-rise apartment building.
usage_notes: Specific to housing domesticated pigeons, often for racing or as a hobby.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-aayos si Mang Tonyo ng kanyang **bahay-kalapati** tuwing umaga.","translation":"Mang Tonyo fixes his **dovecote** every morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aalay ng awit sa isang tao o para sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you're trying to win someone over (harana style) or when your baby cousin won't sleep. "Pre, kantahan mo para tumahan." It's also what happens when the whole barkada gets together for a KTV session.
usage_notes: The object of the verb is the person/thing being sung to.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais kong **kantahan** ka ng paborito mong awitin.","translation":"I want **to sing** your favorite song **for you**."},{"sentence":"**Kantahan** mo naman kami!","translation":"**Sing for** us!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtali o pagbigkis sa isang tao o bagay upang hindi makakilos o makawala.
original_explanation: Think of what villains do to the hero in action movies. But in real life, it's more like that feeling when you're stuck in a toxic relationship or a dead-end job. You feel 'gumapos'—tied down, unable to escape. It's the ultimate 'sana all makalaya' hugot.
usage_notes: Can be used both literally (tying with a rope) and figuratively (being bound by debt, love, or duty).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Gumapos** sa mga kamay ng bihag ang mga pirata.","translation":"The pirates **tied up** the hands of the captive."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam niya ay **gumapos** sa kanya ang malaking utang na loob.","translation":"He felt **bound** by a huge debt of gratitude."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pagkaing dumaan sa proseso ng pagluluto gamit ang init. Ito ay ang nakaraang anyo ng pandiwang 'lutuin'.
original_explanation: Past tense of 'to cook'. This is the adobo your mom made, the sinigang you miss from home, or the instant noodles you "cooked" at 2 AM. It can also be used figuratively for anything that's been "cooked up" or manipulated, like "nilutong eleksyon" (rigged election) or "nilutong laban" (a fixed match). The most important question at any Filipino gathering: "Sino'ng nagluto nito?"
usage_notes: Past tense, passive voice of 'luto' (cook). It can also mean 'fixed' or 'rigged' in a colloquial context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paborito kong adobo ay **niluto** ng aking lola.","translation":"My favorite adobo was **cooked** by my grandmother."},{"sentence":"May hinala silang **niluto** ang resulta ng kumpetisyon.","translation":"They suspect the results of the competition were **fixed** (cooked)."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bunga ng puno ng niyog, na may matigas na balat, puting laman, at sabaw. Isang pangunahing sangkap sa lutuing Pilipino.
original_explanation: The MVP of the Philippine fruit world. It gives us buko juice for the heat, gata for our laing and adobo sa gata, coconut oil for... everything, and the bao for our bunot floors. It's the tree of life, and **niyog** is its glorious gift.
usage_notes: Refers to the mature coconut fruit, as opposed to 'buko' which is the young coconut.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong kumayod ng **niyog** para sa gagawin kong biko.","translation":"I need to grate a **coconut** for the sticky rice cake I'm making."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang ginataang manok kung sariwa ang **niyog** na gagamitin.","translation":"Chicken cooked in coconut milk is delicious if the **coconut** used is fresh."}]

meaning_filipino: Magpasabog o magsindi ng mga paputok sa isang partikular na lugar o direksyon.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'putok' (explode) at panlaping 'pa- -an'.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of New Year's Eve chaos. It's when your tito decides to aim a 'kwitis' (skyrocket) at your neighbor's roof "by accident". "Paputukan mo diyan sa kalsada, 'wag dito sa loob ng bahay!" It can also be used figuratively, like to bombard someone with questions. "Pinaputukan nila ng tanong ang bagong-salta."
usage_notes: Karaniwang tumutukoy sa mga paputok. Ang diin ay sa lugar o target ng pagsabog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bawal **paputukan** ang bakuran ng kapitbahay tuwing Bagong Taon.","translation":"It's forbidden **to set off firecrackers at** the neighbor's yard during New Year."}]

translation: unrevealed, undisclosed, not brought to light
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang impormasyon, katotohanan, o bagay na nananatiling lihim at hindi pa naisasapubliko o naipapaalam.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng 'hindi' (not) at 'nahayag' (was revealed), mula sa salitang-ugat na 'hayag' (public, revealed).
original_explanation: This is the "secret episode" in your favorite K-drama, the "classified files" in a spy movie, or the real reason why your friend broke up with their jowa. It's the tea that hasn't been spilled yet. The "Marites network" is still investigating.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa pormal o pampanitikang konteksto, katulad ng salitang Ingles na "undisclosed."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming detalye ng kaso ang **hindi nahayag** sa publiko.","translation":"Many details of the case were **unrevealed** to the public."},{"sentence":"Ang tunay niyang nararamdaman ay nanatiling **hindi nahayag**.","translation":"His true feelings remained **undisclosed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isipin o gunigunihin ang isang bagay na posibleng mangyari sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of that gut feeling. It's what you do when you're daydreaming about your crush finally noticing you. It's to mentally picture a future scenario, good or bad. 'Ni sa panaginip ay hindi ko **hinagap** na mananalo ako sa lotto.'
usage_notes: A formal and literary verb. 'Isipin' or 'akalain' are more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **hinagapin** ang isang mundong walang teknolohiya.","translation":"It's hard **to imagine** a world without technology."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **hinagapin** kung ano ang pakiramdam ng maging isang bilyonaryo.","translation":"He tried **to imagine** what it would feel like to be a billionaire."}]

translation: a crack, a split, a fissure
meaning_filipino: Ang lamat o pagkakahiwalay ng isang bagay sa dalawa o higit pang bahagi.
original_explanation: It's the crack itself. If the road is `biak` (adjective), then the `biak` (noun) is the actual fissure you have to avoid. It's the physical evidence of the split.
usage_notes: While the adjective form is more common, the noun form is used to refer to the split itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May malaking **biak** sa pader ng bahay.","translation":"There is a large **crack** in the wall of the house."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging maramdamin, mapagmunimuni, o labis na emosyonal.
original_explanation: Parang switch 'to sa utak mo. 'Pag naka-on ang senti mode, bigla kang nagiging sensitive. Umuulan? Senti. Narinig 'yung theme song ng dati niyong love team? Senti. Nakakita ng matandang magka-holding hands? Super senti. It's a state of being where everything hits you right in the feels.
usage_notes: Katulad ng 'senti hours,' ito ay isang kolokyal na parirala.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo muna akong biruin, naka-**senti mode** ako ngayon.","translation":"Don't joke with me for now, I'm in a **sentimental mode** today."},{"sentence":"Na-activate ang **senti mode** ko dahil sa pinanood naming pelikula.","translation":"My **sentimental mode** was activated because of the movie we watched."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga bagay, ideya, o tao na walang anumang koneksyon o relasyon sa isa't isa.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "di-" (not), "magkaka-" (denoting relationship), at salitang-ugat na "ugnay" (connection).
original_explanation: Parang yung mga random topics sa group chat ninyo. Nagsimula sa work, napunta sa chismis, tapos biglang may nag-send ng meme ng pusa. Walang connect! Ganyan ang di-magkakaugnay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap intindihin ang sanaysay dahil **di-magkakaugnay** ang mga ideya.","translation":"It's hard to understand the essay because the ideas are **unrelated**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga pahayag niya ay tila isang koleksyon ng mga salitang **di-magkakaugnay**.","translation":"His statements seem to be a collection of **incoherent** words."}]

translation: to splash, to spurt, to spray
meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang paglabas o pagtalsik ng maliliit na patak ng likido.
original_explanation: What happens when you squeeze a calamansi too hard and it goes straight into your eye. Or when a car speeds through a puddle next to you on your way to a date. It's a sudden, tiny, and often annoying liquid attack.
usage_notes: Completed aspect (past tense). Present: `pumipisik`, Future: `pipisik`. Refers to small amounts of liquid, unlike 'bumuhos' which means to pour heavily.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pumisik** ang mantika mula sa kawali at napaso ako.","translation":"The oil **splashed** from the pan and I got burned."},{"sentence":"Biglang **pumisik** ang tubig mula sa sirang tubo.","translation":"Water suddenly **spurted** from the broken pipe."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malalim na hiwa o sugat na dulot ng isang matalim na bagay tulad ng itak o kutsilyo.
original_explanation: The result of chopping something, or someone. 'Yung sugat na makukuha mo 'pag nag-attempt kang mag-bukas ng niyog gamit ang itak for the first time. The action is 'pagtaga', the result is 'taga'.
usage_notes: Ito ay tumutukoy sa resulta ng pagtaga, na isang hiwa o sugat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon siya ng malaking **taga** sa braso mula sa paggamit ng itak.","translation":"He got a large **hack** wound on his arm from using the bolo knife."},{"sentence":"Makikita pa rin ang mga **taga** sa puno ng niyog.","translation":"The **chops** on the coconut tree can still be seen."}]

translation: to foam; to lather; to create bubbles
meaning_filipino: Gumawa o maglabas ng maraming bula.
original_explanation: That satisfying moment when your shampoo or dishwashing liquid starts creating a mountain of bubbles. It's the sign that the soap is working! Also, what happens to your mouth if you eat the wrong kind of wild plant, or in old movies, to show someone's been poisoned.
usage_notes: Can be used for soaps, beverages, or even natural phenomena.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Haluin mo ang sabon sa tubig para ito ay **magsabula**.","translation":"Mix the soap in the water so it will **foam**."},{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **magsabula** ang kanyang bibig matapos kumain ng hindi kilalang halaman.","translation":"His mouth started **to foam** after eating an unknown plant."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halamang-ugat (Dioscorea esculenta) na may maliliit at kumpol-kumpol na laman-ugat, na kahawig ng kamote ngunit mas maliit.
original_explanation: 'Tugi' is that underrated root crop, the smaller, cuter cousin of ube and kamote. You'll find it in the palengke, usually boiled and eaten with sugar or grated coconut. It's the kind of meryenda your lola would prepare. Simple, classic, and definitely not an avocado toast.
usage_notes: A specific type of yam, Dioscorea esculenta, known for its smaller tubers that grow in clusters.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpakulo si Lola ng **tugi** para sa aming meryenda.","translation":"Grandma boiled some **lesser yams** for our afternoon snack."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang nilagang **tugi** na may kasamang niyog at asukal.","translation":"Boiled **lesser yam** is delicious with coconut and sugar."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagpapalit ng balat o balahibo ng isang hayop, tulad ng ahas o ibon.
original_explanation: Like a snake shedding its old skin to grow, or you getting rid of your toxic ex to start a new life. It's the ultimate 'new year, new me' but for animals. "Sana kaya ko ring maghunos para iwan lahat ng problema ko." - a classic hugot line.
usage_notes: Primarily used in a biological context for animals. Can be used figuratively to mean a complete transformation or renewal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga ahas ay kailangang **maghunos** upang sila ay lumaki.","translation":"Snakes need to **molt** so they can grow."},{"sentence":"Tila **naghunos** ang kanyang pagkatao matapos ang mga pinagdaanan niya.","translation":"It seems his personality has **shed its old skin** (transformed) after everything he went through."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking ibon na kumakain ng bangkay ng mga hayop.
original_explanation: Literally, a vulture. Figuratively, that person who suddenly becomes your best friend on payday. Or the 'disaster tourist' who loves watching drama unfold. They circle around, waiting for something to die (a project, a relationship, your wallet) so they can swoop in and feast on the remains.
usage_notes: Often used metaphorically to describe opportunistic or predatory people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May mga **buwitre** na nag-aabang sa pagbagsak ng kumpanya.","translation":"There are **vultures** waiting for the company to fall."},{"sentence":"Nakakita kami ng mga **buwitre** na lumilipad sa ibabaw ng bundok.","translation":"We saw **vultures** flying over the mountain."}]

translation: the act of picking up; gathering
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkuha o pagdampot ng isang bagay, karaniwan mula sa sahig o isang mababang lugar.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you drop your phone for the nth time. It's the "5-second rule" in action. It's also used for gathering things, like pagpulot ng shells sa beach, or pagpulot ng chismis from your neighbors. Figuratively, it's also "picking up" a lesson or a moral from a story—"May aral kang mapupulot." (You can pick up a lesson).
usage_notes: Can be literal (picking up a physical object) or figurative (picking up a lesson, idea, or information). Not to be confused with `pulót` (honey).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagpulot** ng basura ay isang simpleng paraan upang mapanatiling malinis ang ating kapaligiran.","translation":"The **act of picking up** trash is a simple way to keep our environment clean."},{"sentence":"Maraming aral ang matututunan sa **pagpulot** ng mga kuwento mula sa mga nakatatanda.","translation":"Many lessons can be learned from **gathering** stories from the elders."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang dalubhasa sa batas, tulad ng isang hukom, abogado, o propesor ng batas.
original_explanation: The OG legal eagle. Not just any abogado, but someone whose opinion on the law is so respected, they're basically a walking, talking Constitution. Think of the wise old sage in a movie who knows all the ancient loopholes. Sila yung mga sinusulat sa textbook, hindi lang yung nagbabasa nito.
usage_notes: A very formal and somewhat rare term. 'Abogado' (lawyer) or 'hukom' (judge) are much more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinikilala si Justice Feliciano bilang isang mahusay na **hurista** sa internasyonal na batas.","translation":"Justice Feliciano is recognized as an excellent **jurist** in international law."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang asin ng asidong karboniko, na nailalarawan sa pagkakaroon ng ion na CO₃²⁻.
original_explanation: That fizzy magic in your soft drinks. It's the "soda" in baking soda (sodium bicarbonate). Basically, a science-y word for what makes things bubbly or what helps your cake rise.
usage_notes: Madalas marinig sa konteksto ng kimika o pagluluto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang calcium **karbonato** ay pangunahing sangkap ng apog at marmol.","translation":"Calcium **carbonate** is a primary component of limestone and marble."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang estruktura na may mga baitang na ginagamit para umakyat o bumaba sa pagitan ng magkaibang antas ng isang gusali o lugar.
original_explanation: Ang aakyatin mo para ma-reach ang second floor ng bahay niyo, o ang corporate ladder sa office. Puwedeng literal na step-by-step, o 'yung metaphorical na daan papunta sa tagumpay. Sabi nga nila, 'walang elevator to success, you have to take the stairs.' So, gamitin mo ang hagdan.
usage_notes: Pangkalahatang tawag para sa "stairs" (permanent) at "ladder" (movable), bagaman may hiwalay na salita para sa ladder (hagdanan).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahan-dahan siyang umakyat sa **hagdan**.","translation":"He/She slowly went up the **stairs**."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang **hagdan** para kunin ang pusa sa bubong.","translation":"He/She used the **ladder** to get the cat from the roof."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang dalubhasa sa antropolohiya, ang siyentipikong pag-aaral sa mga tao, kanilang pinagmulan, pag-unlad, lipunan, at kultura.
original_explanation: Sila yung mga professional na chismoso/chismosa ng buong sangkatauhan. Pinag-aaralan nila kung bakit tayo ganito, mula sa mga sinaunang buto hanggang sa kung bakit mahilig tayong mag-unfriend sa Facebook. Sila ang ultimate 'culture vulture' for science.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayon sa isang **antropologo**, mahalaga ang pag-unawa sa mga ritwal ng isang komunidad.","translation":"According to an **anthropologist**, understanding a community's rituals is important."},{"sentence":"Naglakbay siya sa iba't ibang bansa bilang isang **antropologo**.","translation":"She traveled to different countries as an **anthropologist**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kabilang sa pangkat etnolinggwistiko na pangunahing naninirahan sa rehiyon ng Kanlurang Visayas. Tumutukoy rin ito sa kanilang wika, na mas pormal na kilala bilang Hiligaynon.
etymology: Tumutukoy sa mga taga-Iloilo. Ang pangalang "Iloilo" ay sinasabing nagmula sa "Irong-Irong," ang lumang pangalan ng lungsod, na nangangahulugang "hugis-ilong" dahil sa isang maliit na pulo sa Ilog Iloilo.
original_explanation: Known for their sweet-sounding, 'malambing' accent that makes even an angry sentence sound like a love song. Ilonggos are from the Western Visayas region and are stereotypically seen as gentle and soft-spoken. Their language is Hiligaynon, and their food is legendary – think La Paz Batchoy and Chicken Inasal. Hearing an Ilonggo speak is like getting a verbal hug.
usage_notes: Ang 'Hiligaynon' ay ang mas teknikal na pangalan para sa wika, habang ang 'Ilonggo' ay karaniwang tumutukoy sa mga tao ngunit madalas ding ginagamit para sa wika sa kolokyal na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala ang mga **Ilonggo** sa kanilang masasarap na pagkain tulad ng batchoy.","translation":"**Ilonggos** are known for their delicious food like batchoy."}]

translation: to borrow from (a person or institution)
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghiram ng pera o bagay mula sa isang tao, lugar, o institusyon.
original_explanation: The verb form of finding your 'suki' for financial emergencies. Ito 'yung paglapit mo sa kaibigan mong mayaman-dahil-sa-13th-month-pay at sasabihing, 'Bes, pwedeng utangan muna kita?' It's the act of sourcing your funds, whether it's from a friend, a loan shark, or the company cooperative.
usage_notes: Focuses on the *source* of the loan. The object of the verb is the person or entity being borrowed from.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ba ang pwede kong **utangan** ng pambili ng gamot?","translation":"Who can I **borrow from** to buy medicine?"},{"sentence":"Ayaw ko sanang **utangan** ang mga kamag-anak natin para iwas-gulo.","translation":"I'd rather not **borrow from** our relatives to avoid trouble."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggalaw o pagpunta sa direksyong salungat sa agos ng tubig, ihip ng hangin, o takbo ng trapiko.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you're driving and you accidentally turn into a one-way street. Panic! It's literally going against the flow. Metaphorically, it's the struggle of commuting during rush hour, trying to 'sumalunga' against a sea of people all going the other way. It's the salmon's life story, but in the context of EDSA.
usage_notes: Used for going against a literal physical force or flow, like water current, wind, or traffic. Can also be used figuratively for going against a strong trend or opinion, but 'sumalunga' retains a stronger physical connotation than 'sumalansang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **sumalunga** sa malakas na agos ng ilog.","translation":"It's hard **to go against** the strong current of the river."},{"sentence":"Kahit pagod, pilit siyang **sumalunga** sa dagsaan ng mga tao palabas ng istasyon.","translation":"Even though tired, he forced himself **to go against the flow** of the crowd exiting the station."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking basket o buslo, karaniwang yari sa yantok o kawayan, na ginagamit sa paglalagay o pagbubuhat ng mga bagay.
original_explanation: Imagine the biggest, most heavy-duty 'bayong' you can find at the palengke. That's a kanastro. It's the lola's secret weapon for carrying a week's worth of groceries, from a whole jackfruit to a dozen cabbages. It's the OG 'eco-bag' before it was cool.
usage_notes: Often used for agricultural produce or large quantities of goods. Less common in urban settings now.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng mga mangga ang dala niyang **kanastro**.","translation":"The **large basket** he was carrying was full of mangoes."}]

translation: quarantining, the act of being in quarantine
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paghihiwalay o pagbubukod sa isang tao, hayop, o bagay na maaaring may sakit na nakahahawa upang maiwasan ang pagkalat nito.
etymology: From `pag-` (nominalizer) + `kuwarentenas`, a Filipinized form of the Spanish `cuarentena` (quarantine).
original_explanation: Ah, the word that defined 2020-2022. It's the act of being stuck at home, becoming a plantito/plantita, a master baker, or a binge-watching champion. The official term for 'bawal lumabas.'
usage_notes: Gained extremely high frequency during the COVID-19 pandemic. A modern loanword adaptation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit na ipinatupad ang **pagkukuwarentenas** sa buong lungsod noong panahon ng pandemya.","translation":"The act of **quarantining** was strictly implemented throughout the city during the pandemic."}]

translation: to be late; to be caught
meaning_filipino: Maabutan sa isang gawain, lalo na kung ito ay labag sa batas; hindi umabot sa takdang oras.
original_explanation: Two main flavors: 1) Yung feeling na 8:01 AM ka nag-clock in sa BPO tapos 8:00 AM ang start ng shift mo. You're late. **Mahuli** ka na. 2) Yung moment na nahuli ka ng jowa mo na may ka-chat kang iba. You're caught. Game over. Huli ka, balbon!
usage_notes: Can mean 'to be late' or 'to be caught,' depending on context. The stress on the syllable is important. maHÚli (to be caught) vs. MAhuli (last one). This entry focuses on maHÚli.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinikap niyang tumakbo ngunit **nahuli** pa rin siya ng mga pulis.","translation":"He tried to run but he was still **caught** by the police."},{"sentence":"Ayaw kong **mahuli** sa klase kaya maaga akong umalis.","translation":"I don't want to be **late** for class so I left early."}]

meaning_filipino: Ilalaan o gamitin ang panahon, salapi, o lakas sa isang partikular na gawain o layunin.
original_explanation: This is what you do with your sahod on 15/30—you spend it. Or what you do with your weekend—you allocate it for sleep, chores, or that long-overdue K-drama marathon. It's the 'budgeting' verb, whether for money, time, or energy. 'Paano mo gugugulin ang 13th month pay mo?'
usage_notes: Often used in the context of time, money, or effort.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **gugulin** ang lahat ng iyong oras sa paglalaro.","translation":"Don't **spend** all your time playing."},{"sentence":"Maingat niyang **gugugulin** ang perang natanggap para sa kinabukasan.","translation":"He will carefully **spend** the money he received for the future."}]

translation: sociable (with friends), someone who prioritizes their clique
meaning_filipino: Isang taong labis na nagpapahalaga at nag-uukol ng maraming oras sa kanyang mga kaibigan o barkada.
etymology: Mula sa `mapag-` (na nagsasaad ng hilig) + `barkada` (grupo ng mga kaibigan), na hango sa salitang Espanyol na *barcada* (boatload).
original_explanation: Ito 'yung tipo ng tao na ang sagot sa "Saan ka?" ay laging "Kasama barkada." Priority nila ang social life at ang "gala" with friends. Minsan, ito 'yung reklamo ng jowa: "Lagi mo na lang kasama 'yang barkada mo!" They live for the "squad goals" moments.
usage_notes: Maaaring neutral, ngunit kung minsan ay ginagamit na may negatibong tono kapag nagpapahiwatig ito ng pagpapabaya sa ibang mga responsibilidad (tulad ng pamilya o trabaho).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala si Marco bilang isang taong **mapagbarkada** mula pa noong high school.","translation":"Marco has been known as a **sociable** person (who prioritizes friends) since high school."},{"sentence":"Medyo nag-aalala ang kanyang mga magulang dahil masyado siyang **mapagbarkada** at napapabayaan na ang pag-aaral.","translation":"His parents are a bit worried because he **prioritizes his clique** too much and is neglecting his studies."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng mga pananim na sinisira o inaatake ng mga peste o kulisap.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung puso mo, inaatake ng mga insekyuridad at doubts. Sa agrikultura, 'pag ang palay mo ay binangyaw, parang kinain ng mga "marites" na peste ang pag-asa mong umani. It's a farmer's worst nightmare.
usage_notes: This is a specific agricultural term, not used in general conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nalugi ang magsasaka dahil **binangyaw** ang kanyang buong taniman ng mais.","translation":"The farmer went bankrupt because his entire cornfield was **infested by pests**."},{"sentence":"Kailangang mag-isprey ng pestisidyo upang hindi **bangyawin** ang mga gulay.","translation":"Pesticide must be sprayed so that the vegetables won't **be infested by pests**."}]

translation: to doubt something; to be apprehensive about
meaning_filipino: Ang pagdama ng pag-aalinlangan o pangamba; ang pag-isipan nang may kawalang-katiyakan.
etymology: From the noun "agam-agam" with the object-focus suffix "-in".
original_explanation: To "agam-agamin" is to actively entertain your doubts. It's when you're reviewing your sent messages, analyzing every emoji, and thinking, "Was that too much?" It's the verb form of being an overthinker, turning your worries into a full-blown mental project.
usage_notes: This is a literary or formal verb. More common ways to express this would be "pagdudahan" or "mag-alinlangan."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **agam-agamin** ang kanyang katapatan.","translation":"Do not **doubt** his loyalty."},{"sentence":"Madalas niyang **agam-agamin** ang sarili niyang kakayahan.","translation":"She often **feels apprehensive about** her own abilities."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pariralang pang-ukol na tumutukoy sa isang partikular na tao bilang pinagmulan o pinanggalingan.
etymology: Kombinasyon ng "mula" (from) at ang personal na pantukoy na "kay".
original_explanation: This is the 'from' you use when the source is a person, a.k.a. the source of the chismis. "Saan galing yang balita?" "Mula kay Marites!" It specifies that the origin isn't a place or a thing, but a person (singular). For plural, you use 'mula kina'.
usage_notes: Used specifically before a singular personal name. The plural form is "mula kina".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sulat na ito ay **mula kay** Lola Basyang.","translation":"This letter is **from** Grandma Basyang."},{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang balita **mula kay** John.","translation":"I heard the news **from** John."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng hadlang o pagtayo sa daan upang pigilan ang pagdaan o pagpapatuloy ng isang bagay o tao.
original_explanation: 'Yung kotse na biglang humarang sa harap ng jeep kaya na-traffic kayong lahat. Or 'yung chismosang kapitbahay na biglang humarang sa'yo para lang itanong kung kelan ka mag-aasawa. They are the human version of a "road closed" sign you didn't ask for.
usage_notes: Can be used for both physical and metaphorical obstruction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malaking trak ang **humaraǹg** sa kalsada kaya nagkaroon ng trapik.","translation":"A large truck **blocked** the road, causing traffic."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **haharaǹg** sa aking mga pangarap!","translation":"Don't **obstruct** my dreams!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay o pagpapadaloy ng tubig sa isang lugar, tulad ng bukid o halamanan.
original_explanation: The verb form. It means "to water something." You patubigan the rice paddies, you patubigan your lola's dusty garden. It's a more large-scale version of 'dilig' (to water plants). You 'dilig' a pot, you patubigan a field.
usage_notes: Ginagamit bilang pandiwa na nangangahulugang lagyan ng tubig. Huwag ipagkamali sa pangngalang "patubigan" (irrigation canal).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **patubigan** ang mga bagong tanim na palay.","translation":"The newly planted rice stalks need **to be watered**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal para sa isang babaeng may atraksyong romantiko o sekswal sa kapwa babae; isang tomboy.
original_explanation: A colloquial, sometimes dated, term for a lesbian. It can range from neutral to derogatory depending on the speaker and context, so read the room. It’s like the prequel to the more modern and widely accepted terms. Some older titas might still use this.
usage_notes: Can be considered offensive by some. More neutral or preferred terms include "tomboy" (in its local context), "lesbiyana," or simply part of the "LGBTQ+ community."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May mga maling akala pa rin ang iba tungkol sa pagiging **tibo**.","translation":"Some people still have misconceptions about being a **lesbian**."},{"sentence":"Ang karakter sa pelikula ay isang **tibo** na naghahanap ng pag-ibig.","translation":"The character in the movie is a **lesbian** looking for love."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kondisyong medikal kung saan ang mga mata ay hindi sabay o magkatuon sa iisang direksyon; ang kalagayan ng pagiging duling.
original_explanation: It's the formal/medical term for being 'duling' or cross-eyed. It's when your eyes have 'creative differences' and decide to look at two different things at once. One eye is checking out the menu, the other is already looking at the bill.
usage_notes: A more formal or medical way to refer to the condition of being cross-eyed. 'Duling' is the common, everyday term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroong operasyon upang itama ang **kadulingan**.","translation":"There is an operation to correct **strabismus**."},{"sentence":"Huwag pagtawanan ang isang tao dahil sa kanyang **kadulingan**.","translation":"Do not laugh at a person because of their **state of being cross-eyed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal o organisadong paraan ng pag-uusap o paglalahad ng isang paksa, karaniwang sumusunod sa mga tiyak na alituntunin o istruktura.
original_explanation: Basically, a 'serious talk.' Not your usual chismis session with friends, but more like a company meeting, a thesis defense, or when your parents say 'We need to talk.' It's a discussion with an agenda, structure, and probably some PowerPoint slides.
usage_notes: This is a compound noun phrase, common in academic, professional, and formal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang panel ay magkakaroon ng isang **maanyong pagtalakay** tungkol sa ekonomiya ng bansa.","translation":"The panel will have a **formal discussion** about the country's economy."},{"sentence":"Inaasahan ang lahat na maging magalang sa gaganaping **maanyong pagtalakay**.","translation":"Everyone is expected to be respectful during the upcoming **formal discussion**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na upuan na walang sandalan, karaniwang yari sa kahoy o plastik.
original_explanation: The unsung hero of Filipino households. It's a chair, a step-ladder to change a lightbulb, a makeshift table for your morning kape, and the official seat for washing clothes by hand. MVP ng kabahayan.
usage_notes: The diminutive form of 'bangko' (bench).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umupo siya sa **bangkito** habang naghihintay na maluto ang sinaing.","translation":"She sat on the **stool** while waiting for the rice to cook."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghila sa isang tao o bagay sa lupa o sa anumang ibabaw nang sapilitan o may kahirapan.
original_explanation: What you do to your friend who doesn't want to go out but you need a wingman. 'Tara na, 'wag ka nang umarte!' Also, how your mom drags you through Divisoria during Christmas season.
usage_notes: This is the object-focus verb form. The root 'kaladkad' itself is a noun meaning 'the act of dragging'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **kaladkarin**, ayokong sumama!","translation":"Don't **drag me** along, I don't want to go!"},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **kaladkarin** ang mabigat na sako ng bigas.","translation":"I have to **drag** the heavy sack of rice."}]

meaning_filipino: Labis na pagpapahalaga at pagbanggit sa sarili; sobrang pagmamataas o kayabangan.
original_explanation: If egoismo is the quiet "me-first" philosophy, 'egotismo' is the loud, obnoxious version. It's the constant "Ako, noong nasa States ako..." stories from your tito. It's the gym bro who posts more mirror selfies than workout reps. It’s the habit of talking about yourself all the time, as if you're the main character and everyone else is just an NPC.
usage_notes: Refers more to the outward expression of self-importance, as opposed to the internal motivation of egoism.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **egotismo** ang kanyang mga talumpati.","translation":"His speeches are full of **egotism**."},{"sentence":"Hindi na siya kinakausap ng mga dati niyang kaibigan dahil sa kanyang **egotismo**.","translation":"His former friends no longer talk to him because of his **egotism**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mapanuksong biro, panlilinlang, o gawain na naglalayong pagtawanan o maliitin ang isang tao.
etymology: From Spanish 'burlas' (plural of 'burla', meaning jest, mockery).
original_explanation: This is next-level 'asar'. It's not just a simple joke; it's a prank or mockery that has a bit of a sting. Think of it as the kind of 'joke' that's only funny to the person telling it, and borderline bullying to the person receiving it. The OG term for 'It's just a prank, bro!'
usage_notes: A slightly more formal or literary term for mockery. 'Pambuburlas' is the act of mockery.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi na iyon biro, isa na iyong **burlas** sa kanyang pagkatao.","translation":"That's not a joke anymore, that is a **mockery** of his character."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga salita ay puno ng **burlas** at panunuya.","translation":"His words were full of **jest** and sarcasm."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pakikiapid o pagtataksil ng isang taong may asawa sa kanyang kabiyak.
original_explanation: The plot of 90% of Filipino teleseryes. The ultimate "sana all" na hindi mo gugustuhin. When "me and my jowa" becomes "me, my jowa, and my ka-opisina." It's a legal and moral-Tita-level offense.
usage_notes: A formal and legal term. 'Pagtataksil' (betrayal) or 'pambababae/panlalalaki' (womanizing) are more colloquial.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaaring kasuhan ng **pangangalunya** ang isang taong may asawa na napatunayang nagtaksil.","translation":"A married person proven to have been unfaithful can be charged with **adultery**."},{"sentence":"Ang **pangangalunya** ay isa sa mga dahilan ng paghihiwalay ng mag-asawa.","translation":"**Infidelity** is one of the reasons for a couple's separation."}]

translation: to put a shape on (a surface)
meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng hugis o anyo ang isang bagay o ibabaw.
original_explanation: Parang pag-mold ng clay or play-doh. You're giving something a form. It's less about creating the entire shape from scratch (that's 'hugisin') and more about applying a shape onto a surface. Think: "Hugisan mo ng star yung cookie dough."
usage_notes: This verb focuses on the surface or object being given a shape. It is less common than 'hugisin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hugisan** natin ng mga bulaklak ang ibabaw ng keyk.","translation":"Let's **shape** flowers on the surface of the cake."},{"sentence":"Ang putik ay **hinugisan** ng mga daliri ng magpapalayok.","translation":"The clay was **shaped** by the potter's fingers."}]

meaning_filipino: Inuming iniaalok sa iba; isang pagtitipon para uminom, karaniwang tumutukoy sa mga inuming may alkohol.
original_explanation: The magic word after a long week at the office. 'Tara, **painom** naman diyan!' It can be a simple offer of a glass of water, or the prelude to an epic Friday night session with friends involving Red Horse and a lot of hugot stories.
usage_notes: Can mean a single drink offered, or a whole event centered on drinking. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghanda siya ng kaunting **painom** para sa kanyang mga bisita.","translation":"She prepared a small **drinking session** for her guests."},{"sentence":"Salamat sa **painom**, nauuhaw na talaga ako.","translation":"Thanks for the **drink**, I was really thirsty."}]

translation: to say mass, to hold a mass
meaning_filipino: Para sa pari, ito ay ang pangunguna sa seremonya ng Misa. Para sa karaniwang tao, ito ay maaaring tumukoy sa pagdalo sa Misa.
etymology: From Spanish 'misa' (mass), combined with the Tagalog verb prefix 'mag-'.
original_explanation: The ultimate Sunday obligation for your lola. For a priest, it's their main job. For everyone else, it's either "magsimba" (to go to church) or "dumalo sa misa" (to attend mass). But if you say, "Magpapamisa ako," it means you're requesting a mass, usually for a special intention like a birthday or for the soul of someone who passed away.
usage_notes: The subject of this verb is typically a priest. For laypeople, "magsimba" or "dumalo sa misa" is more common for "to attend mass". "Magpamisa" means "to have a mass said".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pari ay **magmimisa** para sa kapistahan ng bayan.","translation":"The priest will **say mass** for the town's fiesta."},{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang pamilya na **magpamisa** para sa anibersaryo ng pagkamatay ng kanilang lolo.","translation":"The family decided to **have a mass said** for the death anniversary of their grandfather."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtuon ng pansin at paningin sa isang bagay, kaganapan, o palabas. Ito ay isang pandiwang nakapokus sa layon.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `pa-` + salitang-ugat na `nood` + hulaping `-in`.
original_explanation: The command you give to your friend when a new series drops on Netflix: "Panoorin mo 'to!" (Watch this!). It's the verb form of our national pastime, whether it's the latest blockbuster, a viral TikTok video, or the chismis unfolding with your kapitbahay.
usage_notes: Isang pandiwang pokus sa layon. Ang pinapanood ang tuwirang layon ng pangungusap. Ang gumaganap ay nasa kaukulang paari (hal. Panoorin **mo** ang palabas).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **panoorin** ang bagong pelikula sa sinehan.","translation":"I want **to watch** the new movie in the cinema."},{"sentence":"**Panoorin** natin ang paglubog ng araw sa dalampasigan.","translation":"Let's **watch** the sunset on the beach."}]

translation: will be made to choose; will be made to shop
meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng pagkakataon o pilitin ang isang tao na pumili mula sa maraming pagpipilian o bagay; o utusang bumili ng mga pangangailangan.
original_explanation: This is what happens when your parents give you two "choices": "Mag-aral ka nang mabuti, o mag-aral ka nang mabuti." You're being *made to choose*, but the outcome is the same. It can also mean being sent to the palengke to do the shopping. "Anak, ikaw na ang **papamiliin** ko ng ulam para mamaya."
usage_notes: This is the contemplative (future) causative form, often implying that someone will be given the task or authority to choose or shop for others.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **papamiliin** ng komite para sa bagong disenyo ng uniporme.","translation":"She will be the one **made to choose** by the committee for the new uniform design."},{"sentence":"Dahil ikaw ang may alam sa mga presyo, ikaw na ang **papamiliin** ko sa palengke.","translation":"Since you know the prices, I will have you **do the shopping** at the market."}]

translation: will be allowed to ride; will be given a ride
meaning_filipino: Pahihintulutang sumakay o bibigyan ng serbisyong transportasyon. Ito ay nasa aspetong panghinaharap.
original_explanation: That moment of hope when you're late for work and your rich officemate pulls up in their SUV. You look at them with your best 'pa-cute' eyes, hoping na **pasasakyan** ka niya. It's the opposite of being 'seen-zoned' by a Grab driver.
usage_notes: Future tense of `pasakayin`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Libre lang daw, **pasasakyan** tayo sa van ng barangay.","translation":"They said it's free, we **will be given a ride** in the barangay van."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **pasasakyan** mo sa kotse mo bukas?","translation":"Who **will you allow to ride** in your car tomorrow?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pakikipag-usap sa isang nagbebenta upang pababain ang presyo ng isang produkto o serbisyo.
etymology: From makipag- + tawad + -an. The -an suffix emphasizes the reciprocal nature of the negotiation.
original_explanation: A sacred ritual in the palengke, tiangge, and Greenhills. It's the art of asking 'Miss, wala na po bang tawad?' with your most charming smile. This is a high-stakes negotiation where your success is measured by how many pesos you've saved. Not for the faint of heart, and definitely not for use in SM.
usage_notes: A key skill in Philippine market culture. The verb implies the interactive process of negotiating a price.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magaling **makipagtawaran** ang nanay ko kaya laging malaki ang natitipid namin sa palengke.","translation":"My mom is great at **haggling**, that's why we always save a lot at the wet market."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mahiyang **makipagtawaran** kapag namimili sa Divisoria.","translation":"Don't be shy to **bargain** when shopping in Divisoria."}]

meaning_filipino: Nakapagpapa-ulol; nagdudulot ng matinding galit, pagkabaliw, o pagkawala sa sarili dahil sa paulit-ulit na pang-aasar o panloloko.
original_explanation: Describes 'yung internet connection mong nagloloko 'pag nasa kalagitnaan ka ng online game. O 'yung kaibigan mong nang-aasar hanggang sa mapikon ka. It's anything that drives you up the wall and makes you want to scream "NAKAKABALIW!"
usage_notes: A very informal and strong word. "Ulol" itself can be a curse word, but in this adjectival form, it describes the effect of a situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Talagang **mapang-ulol** ang ginagawa niyang pang-aasar sa akin araw-araw.","translation":"The teasing he does to me every day is truly **maddening**."},{"sentence":"Ang ingay ng kapitbahay ay sadyang **mapang-ulol**.","translation":"The neighbor's noise is truly **infuriating**."}]

translation: to make something conform to; to follow strictly
meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagsunod o pag-ayon nang mahigpit sa isang pamantayan, tuntunin, o modelo.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of being a "sunud-sunuran." It's when you have to follow the template exactly as is, no questions asked. Like when your boss gives you a PowerPoint template and you have to alinsunurin your entire presentation to it, even if the font is Comic Sans.
usage_notes: This is a more formal and less common verb. The more common way to express this is 'sundin ang...'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **alinsunurin** ang bagong disenyo sa orihinal na plano.","translation":"The new design must be **made to conform** to the original plan."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bukas na espasyo o balkonahe na karaniwang matatagpuan sa itaas na bahagi ng isang bahay o gusali, kadalasan ay walang bubong.
original_explanation: That open-air terrace you see in old Filipino ancestral houses, usually connected to the kitchen. It's the OG 'chill spot' before condos had balconies. Perfect for drying laundry, growing plants in pots, or having a 'merienda' while catching up on the latest chismis with the neighbors.
usage_notes: Karaniwang nauugnay sa mga tradisyonal na bahay na bato at arkitekturang Espanyol sa Pilipinas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkakape ang mag-asawa sa **asotea** tuwing umaga.","translation":"The couple has coffee on the **terrace** every morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkuha ng kaalaman o kasanayan sa pamamagitan ng pag-aaral, pagbabasa, o pagtuturo. Ito ang anyong pangnakaraan ng pandiwang "mag-aral".
original_explanation: This is the past tense of "mag-aral". Ito 'yung ginawa mo a night before the exam, fueled by three cups of coffee and pure desperation. O 'yung sinasabi mong ginawa mo buong weekend, pero ang totoo, isang oras ka lang nag-aral tapos sampung oras ka nag-Netflix.
usage_notes: The completed aspect (past tense) of the verb "mag-aral".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nag-aral** si Jose nang mabuti para sa kanyang pagsusulit sa Math.","translation":"Jose **studied** hard for his Math exam."},{"sentence":"Saan ka **nag-aral** ng kolehiyo?","translation":"Where did you **study** for college?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kapatid na lalaki ng ama o ina; ang asawang lalaki ng tiya.
original_explanation: The male equivalent of a Tita. He's the one who asks "May boyfriend ka na?" at family reunions, gives you pamasko, and might be the designated driver or griller during outings.
usage_notes: Used as a direct address ('Tiyo, kamusta po?') or as a reference ('Kapatid siya ng tatay ko, tiyo ko siya.'). Often used with the person's name, e.g., 'Tiyo Ramon'. The more modern, colloquial term is 'Tito'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **tiyo** ko ay kapatid ng aking ina.","translation":"My **uncle** is my mother's brother."},{"sentence":"Bigyan mo ng baso ng tubig si **Tiyo**.","translation":"Give **Uncle** a glass of water."}]

meaning_filipino: Punong-puno at siksikan na halos umapaw sa dami ng laman; walang nang espasyo.
original_explanation: Imagine the MRT at 6 PM on a payday Friday. That's **asak**. Your balikbayan box when you're trying to fit one last bar of soap? **Asak** na **asak**. It’s the feeling of being so full there's no room to breathe, applicable to both people and things.
usage_notes: Often reduplicated as 'asak na asak' for emphasis. Synonymous with 'siksik'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Asak** na ang bus kaya sa susunod na lang kami sasakay.","translation":"The bus is already **crammed**, so we'll just take the next one."},{"sentence":"Naging **asak** ang maliit na silid nang dumating ang lahat ng bisita.","translation":"The small room became **packed full** when all the guests arrived."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang propesyon o pangunahing gawain ay ang pag-aaral o pagsasagawa ng agrikultura; isang magsasaka.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung a-upgrade na version ng magsasaka. Hindi lang sila nagtatanim, sila 'yung mga boss na nag-aaral ng science behind it para mas bongga ang ani. Sila ang dahilan kung bakit may bigas ka pa sa plato mo. #FarmToTable is real because of them.
usage_notes: Mas pormal na termino kaysa sa "magsasaka" at kadalasang tumutukoy sa isang taong may siyentipiko o propesyonal na pamamaraan sa pagsasaka.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang tanyag na **agrikultor** ang nagsalita sa aming seminar.","translation":"A famous **agriculturist** spoke at our seminar."},{"sentence":"Ang mga **agrikultor** ay mahalaga sa seguridad sa pagkain ng isang bansa.","translation":"**Agriculturists** are important for a country's food security."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging lubog sa isang likido sa loob ng mahabang panahon. Sa metaporikal na kahulugan, ito ay ang matagal na paggawa o pananatili sa isang gawain o lugar.
original_explanation: Literally, to soak something in water, like clothes before washing or meat in marinade for your adobo. Figuratively, it's what you do on weekends: "**babad** sa Netflix." Or when you're stuck in traffic: "**babad** sa EDSA." Or when you're working overtime: "**babad** sa opisina." It means you're totally immersed, for better or for worse.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun (pagbabad), adjective (babad na damit), or verb (ibinabad, magbabad).
