usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hayaan mong **babad** ang manok sa toyo at suka nang isang oras.","translation":"Let the chicken be **soaked** in soy sauce and vinegar for one hour."},{"sentence":"Maghapon siyang **babad** sa computer para tapusin ang kanyang trabaho.","translation":"He was **engrossed** in the computer all day to finish his work."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagmamaneho o sumasakay sa isang sasakyang de-motor, lalo na sa isang motorsiklo.
original_explanation: The general term for anyone driving a vehicle, but in the Philippines, it's usually the 'kamote' rider who just cut you off in traffic. They are the kings and queens of the road, weaving through EDSA like it's a video game.
usage_notes: While it can mean any motorist, it's very strongly associated with motorcycle riders in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahuli ng pulis ang **motorista** dahil sa walang helmet.","translation":"The police caught the **motorist** for not wearing a helmet."},{"sentence":"Dapat laging mag-ingat ang mga **motorista** sa daan.","translation":"**Motorists** should always be careful on the road."}]

meaning_filipino: Isipin o bumuo ng larawan sa isip; tantiyahin o kalkulahin ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the Tagalized version of 'figure out.' It's what you do when you're trying to calculate your budget for the next 11.11 sale. 'Pigurahan mo nga kung magkano lahat 'to.' It's also used for imagining something. 'Can you picture it out?' -> 'Mapipigurahan mo ba?' A very useful word for BPO agents and anyone trying to make sense of their finances before petsa de peligro.
usage_notes: A common Taglish/colloquial verb that has entered mainstream usage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pigurahan** mo kung paano natin gagawin ito nang hindi gumagastos nang malaki.","translation":"**Figure out** how we can do this without spending too much."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan kong **pigurahan** ang itsura niya batay sa iyong deskripsyon.","translation":"I'm trying **to picture** what he looks like based on your description."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng kasalukuyang pagiging sangkot o pagharap sa isang demanda o kasong legal sa korte.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na 'habla' (pagsasalita, diskurso), na naging 'legal na sakdal' sa kontekstong Filipino.
original_explanation: Nako, teh, may resibo! This is when your chismis becomes a legal battle. It's the 'I'll see you in court!' moment, but it's happening right now. Someone is formally accusing you of something, and the papers are being filed. This is more serious than a Twitter war.
usage_notes: Ang unlaping 'na-' at ang pag-uulit ng unang pantig ng salitang-ugat ('ha') ay nagpapahiwatig ng isang nagaganap at hindi kusang-loob na kalagayan o kilos.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nahahabla** ngayon ang sikat na artista dahil sa isyu ng tax evasion.","translation":"The famous celebrity is currently **being sued** over the issue of tax evasion."},{"sentence":"Maraming opisyal ng gobyerno ang **nahahabla** sa Ombudsman dahil sa katiwalian.","translation":"Many government officials are **getting sued** at the Ombudsman for corruption."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagkainis o pagkasawa sa isang paulit-ulit na ingay, sitwasyon, o gawain na nagdudulot ng pagkayamot.
original_explanation: That feeling when your neighbor has been doing karaoke since 10 AM and it's now 10 PM. You're not just annoyed, you're **rindi**. It's the next level of 'inis', where your patience has completely left the building and you're one "My Way" away from losing it. The official mood of anyone stuck in EDSA traffic.
usage_notes: Often used with the prefix "na-" (naririndi) to denote the state of being annoyed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naririndi na ako sa kahol nang kahol ng aso sa labas.","translation":"I'm getting **annoyed** by the dog's constant barking outside."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang ulit-ulitin 'yan, **rindi** na ang mga tao sa'yo.","translation":"Don't keep repeating that, people are already **fed up** with you."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maliit at bilog na prutas na may manipis na balat na kulay kayumanggi, malakatad na laman, at karaniwang matamis na lasa.
original_explanation: The official fruit of the "is there more?" season. You peel one, then suddenly you've finished a whole kilo and your fingers are sticky from the 'dagta' (sap). Best enjoyed while watching TV and pretending you're only having 'a few.'
usage_notes: The fruit is known for its sweet taste, but can sometimes be sour ('maasim'). The sap ('dagta') can be sticky and hard to remove from fingers.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong prutas ang **lanzones** tuwing Oktubre.","translation":"My favorite fruit is **lanzones** every October."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa dagta kapag nagbabalat ka ng **lanzones**.","translation":"Be careful of the sap when you're peeling **lanzones**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, lugar, o pangyayari na nakatatawag ng pansin at interes ng mga tao, lalo na ng mga turista.
original_explanation: This is the main event, the 'pasabog' of a place. Think of Mayon Volcano for Albay or the Chocolate Hills for Bohol. It's the reason you're willing to sit through a 12-hour bus ride or book a piso-fare flight. It's the place's profile picture on the tourism brochure.
usage_notes: Primarily used for tourist attractions or features in an event (e.g., 'Ang main attraction ng fiesta ay ang concert.').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Bulkang Mayon ay isang tanyag na **atraksiyon** sa Bicol.","translation":"Mayon Volcano is a famous **attraction** in Bicol."},{"sentence":"Maraming bagong **atraksiyon** ang itinayo sa amusement park.","translation":"Many new **attractions** were built at the amusement park."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malalim at putol-putol na pag-iyak na may kasamang panginginig ng katawan at hirap sa paghinga, dulot ng matinding kalungkutan o sakit.
original_explanation: This isn't just crying; this is the ugly-cry. It's the kind of crying you do after watching 'Hachiko' or when you realize your 'ayuda' is gone in one day. It's the sound of your soul leaving your body, one shaky breath at a time.
usage_notes: Describes a more intense and convulsive form of crying than 'iyak'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang kanyang mahinang **paghikbi** mula sa kabilang kwarto.","translation":"I heard her soft **sobbing** from the other room."},{"sentence":"Hindi napigilan ni Maria ang kanyang **paghikbi** nang malamang bagsak siya sa pagsusulit.","translation":"Maria couldn't stop her **sobbing** when she found out she failed the exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tirahan kasama ang mga kalapit na lugar nito, tulad ng bakuran, hardin, at kapitbahayan.
original_explanation: The whole package deal. Not just your house, but also the yard where the neighbor's cat does its business, the garden you swear you'll take care of 'bukas,' and the general vibe of the area. In real estate terms, this is the 'house and lot' plus the ambiance.
usage_notes: Commonly used in contexts of real estate, community planning, and general housekeeping that extends to the yard.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga na mapanatiling malinis ang ating **bahay at paligid**.","translation":"It is important to keep our **house and surroundings** clean."}]

translation: to look up at; to be able to look up
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-angat ng tingin o pagtingala sa isang bagay na nasa itaas.
original_explanation: What you do when you see a celebrity in the mall, or when you're checking if the Jollibee mascot is waving at you. It's that upward gaze of awe, surprise, or just trying to see the top of a super tall building without getting dizzy.
usage_notes: The root 'tingala' means to look up. 'Matingala' is the potential form, 'to be able to look up' or 'to happen to look up.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko **matingala** ang tuktok ng gusali dahil sa taas nito.","translation":"I can't **look up at** the top of the building because of its height."},{"sentence":"Napilitan siyang **matingala** sa mga bituin upang hanapin ang konstelasyon.","translation":"He was forced **to look up** at the stars to find the constellation."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang nagpapahayag ng pinagmulan, pinanggalingan, o pinagbuhatan ng isang bagay, tao, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is the 'tracking number' version of 'galing'. It's all about origin stories. 'Saan galing 'yan?' (Where did that come from?) is a question you ask about a new gadget, a piece of gossip (chismis), or that pasalubong from your balikbayan relative. It's used with 'sa' (for places/things) or 'kay' (for people).
usage_notes: Almost always used with 'sa' (for places/inanimate objects) or 'kay' (for people). For example: 'galing sa probinsya' (from the province), 'galing kay Maria' (from Maria). The verb form is 'nanggaling'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sulat na ito ay **galing** sa aking ina.","translation":"This letter is **from** my mother."},{"sentence":"**Galing** ako sa palengke kaya marami akong dala.","translation":"I **came from** the market, that's why I'm carrying a lot."},{"sentence":"Ang tsokolate na ito ay **galing** sa ibang bansa.","translation":"This chocolate is **from** another country."}]

translation: to be able to induce vomiting; to be able to make someone throw up
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang maging sanhi ng pagsuka o paglabas ng laman ng sikmura.
original_explanation: That feeling after riding the Viking at Star City ten times, eating expired food, or sometimes, hearing really cringey 'pick-up' lines. It's the ability to make someone vomit, either literally from being sick or figuratively from disgust. "Ang amoy ng panis na pagkain ay makapagpapasuka sa iyo."
usage_notes: Can be used literally for illness or disgust, and figuratively for extreme cringe or revulsion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uminom siya ng gamot na **makapagpapasuka** sa kanya upang mailabas ang lason.","translation":"He drank medicine that would **make him vomit** to expel the poison."},{"sentence":"**Nakapagpapasuka** ang sobrang kasweetan nila sa social media!","translation":"Their excessive sweetness on social media is **nauseating** (enough to make one vomit)!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang pagkilos ng pagluha dahil sa matinding damdamin tulad ng kalungkutan, sakit, o kagalakan.
original_explanation: What you're doing after watching *Hachiko* or a heart-wrenching Pinoy drama. It's the soundtrack to a breakup, a failed exam, or when you realize your sweldo is gone after two days. The progressive form, meaning the waterworks are currently on.
usage_notes: Progressive form of *umiyak*.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang bata na **umiiyak** sa kabilang kwarto.","translation":"I heard the child **crying** in the other room."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, **umiiyak** lang siya dahil sa tuwa.","translation":"Don't worry, she's just **crying** out of joy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hindi sinasadyang pagbabara ng lalamunan dahil sa pagkain, inumin, o laway na nagdudulot ng hirap sa paghinga.
original_explanation: That mini-panic moment when your saliva, a sip of water, or a tiny piece of chicharon goes down the wrong pipe. Suddenly you're coughing like you're in a dramatic telenovela scene, and everyone's shouting "Tubig! Tubig!"
usage_notes: Refers specifically to choking on something ingested, not being strangled. 'Pagkabulunan' is a close synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahan-dahan sa pagkain para maiwasan ang **pagkasamid**.","translation":"Eat slowly to avoid **choking**."},{"sentence":"Naging sanhi ng kanyang malakas na pag-ubo ang **pagkasamid** sa tubig.","translation":"His intense coughing was caused by **choking** on water."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging hukot o pagkakakuba dahil sa kahinaan, kalungkutan, o katandaan; ang kilos ng paglalakad nang nakayuko.
original_explanation: This is your posture after a 12-hour shift, or after your crush leaves you on 'seen'. It's that deep, soul-crushing slouch. Not just bad posture, but posture that tells a story of defeat, exhaustion, or simply being 'pagod na sa life'. Imagine a plant that hasn't been watered for a week—that drooping? That's pagyuyukayok.
usage_notes: Describes a state of being bent over due to sadness, sickness, or old age. More intense than just 'pagyuko'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kitang-kita sa kanyang **pagyuyukayok** ang bigat ng kanyang mga problema.","translation":"The weight of his problems was evident in his **slouching**."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa matinding karamdaman, halos gumapang na siya sa **pagyuyukayok**.","translation":"Due to severe illness, he was almost crawling from **stooping so low**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagsunod sa isang tuntunin, batas, o utos.
original_explanation: This is the reason you wear your company ID and follow the dress code. It's the "Terms & Conditions" that you scroll past and click "Agree" on. Basically, it's following the rules, whether it's the law of the land or the law of your office HR. "Pag-alinsunod sa bagong memo..." is how emails with bad news usually start.
usage_notes: Often used in formal or legal contexts, frequently preceded by 'bilang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pag-alinsunod** sa batas-trapiko ay para sa kaligtasan ng lahat.","translation":"**Adherence** to traffic laws is for everyone's safety."},{"sentence":"Ipinatupad ang bagong patakaran bilang **pag-alinsunod** sa direktiba ng gobyerno.","translation":"The new policy was implemented in **compliance** with the government's directive."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang idyoma na nangangahulugang biglaang pagtigil sa pagsasalita o pagpigil sa sasabihin. Mayroon ding literal na kahulugan na aksidenteng makagat ang sariling dila.
original_explanation: That awkward moment when you're about to say something you'll regret (like spilling some chismis or a spoiler) and you have to stop yourself. "Muntik ko nang masabi 'yung sikreto niya, buti na lang at napilitan akong makagat ang dila." It can also be literal, like when you're eating too fast.
usage_notes: A common Filipino idiom. The figurative meaning of stopping oneself from speaking is more prevalent than the literal meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais ko sanang sumagot, ngunit pinili kong **makagat ang dila** upang maiwasan ang pagtatalo.","translation":"I wanted to answer back, but I chose to **bite my tongue** to avoid an argument."},{"sentence":"Aray! Habang kumakain, hindi ko sinasadyang **makagat ang dila** ko.","translation":"Ouch! While eating, I accidentally **bit my tongue**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong may ugaling mag-utos o kumilos na parang isang reyna; dominante at mahilig magmando.
etymology: From Tagalog 'reyna' (queen), which is from Spanish 'reina'.
original_explanation: This is the groupmate who assigns all the work while they just 'supervise.' The 'Karen' of the Philippines. They act like they own the place, whether it's a coffee shop, an office, or a family reunion. They have a talent for making everyone their alila. 'Pakikuha mo nga ako ng tubig,' she says, despite being two feet from the dispenser.
usage_notes: Colloquial and highly negative. Describes someone who is imperious and bossy. The repetition of 'reyna' emphasizes the excessive and often ridiculous nature of the behavior.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw siyang makasama sa grupo dahil sa kanyang ugaling **mapagreyna-reynahan**.","translation":"Nobody wants to be in a group with her because of her **bossy** attitude."},{"sentence":"Mula nang ma-promote siya, naging **mapagreyna-reynahan** na ang pakikitungo niya sa amin.","translation":"Ever since she got promoted, she started being **imperious** towards us."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalipunan ng mga tuntunin, batas, o alituntunin na ipinatutupad ng isang awtoridad.
original_explanation: The official list of rules that everyone knows but some people pretend not to see. Like the 'Bawal Magtapon ng Basura Dito' sign right next to a pile of trash, or your condo's 'reglamento' about what time the karaoke must stop.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang **reglamento** ng paaralan pagdating sa tamang uniporme.","translation":"The school **regulations** are strict when it comes to the proper uniform."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang yunit ng timbang para sa mga mamahaling bato tulad ng diyamante, o isang sukat ng kadalisayan ng ginto.
original_explanation: This is the 'K' in 18K or 24K gold. It's the standard you use to check if your jowa's promise ring is the real deal or just something from a gumball machine. The higher the **kilatis**, the more you can flex on social media.
usage_notes: Habang ang salitang 'carat' ay naiintindihan, ang 'kilatis' ang wastong termino sa Filipino, lalo na kapag tinutukoy ang kadalisayan ng ginto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mataas ang **kilatis** ng gintong alahas na bigay ng lola niya.","translation":"The gold jewelry her grandmother gave her is of high **purity**."},{"sentence":"Ilang **kilatis** ba ang diyamante sa singsing na iyan?","translation":"How many **carats** is the diamond in that ring?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na aklat o manipis na babasahin, karaniwang naglalaman ng mga panalangin, tula, o maikling impormasyon.
original_explanation: Think of it as the analog version of a PDF. It's that small prayer book your lola gives you for protection, the mini-songbook for Christmas carols, or the manual for your new rice cooker. It's a book that's too small to be a book, but too important to be just a piece of paper.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May dala siyang **librito** ng mga panalangin sa simbahan.","translation":"She brought a **booklet** of prayers to church."},{"sentence":"Ang mga instruksyon ay nasa isang maliit na **librito** na kasama ng produkto.","translation":"The instructions are in a small **booklet** that comes with the product."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagkasira, pagkalusaw, o pagguho ng isang bagay dahil sa mga natural na elemento o kemikal na reaksyon.
original_explanation: It's what happens to the leftover adobo at the back of the ref after two months. It's what happens to an old iron gate left out in the rain. It's nature's way of recycling. In hugot terms, it's the slow, steady decay of feelings after a bad breakup.
usage_notes: Can be used for organic decay (synonymous with pagkabulok) or inorganic corrosion/erosion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng mga siyentipiko ang bilis ng **pagkaagnas** ng mga plastik.","translation":"Scientists are studying the speed of **decomposition** of plastics."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkaagnas** ng bakal ay tinatawag ding kalawang.","translation":"The **corrosion** of iron is also called rust."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagiging nasa unahan, paggabay, o pamumuno sa isang grupo o gawain.
etymology: From `pang-` + reduplication of the first syllable of the root `u-` + `una` (first).
original_explanation: This is your 'main character energy' moment. It's when you take charge, whether you're the team lead in a BPO, the one organizing the family reunion, or the first in line for the new milk tea shop. It's about being at the forefront.
usage_notes: Can refer to literal leadership, being physically in front, or being ranked first.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinamalas niya ang mahusay na **pangunguna** sa gitna ng krisis.","translation":"He showed great **leadership** in the middle of the crisis."},{"sentence":"Sa **pangunguna** ni Mayor, nalinis ang buong bayan.","translation":"With the Mayor's **leadership**, the whole town was cleaned."}]

meaning_filipino: Punuin nang husto ang isang sisidlan sa pamamagitan ng paglalagay ng mga bagay nang masinsinan.
original_explanation: The command form of 'siksik.' It's what your mom yells when you're packing for a trip and she thinks you're not maximizing the luggage space. 'Siksin mo pa! Kasya pa 'yang isang pares ng sapatos diyan!' It's the art of defying physics to fit 5 days' worth of OOTDs into a carry-on.
usage_notes: This is the object-focus imperative form. Other forms include 'sumiksik' (to squeeze oneself in) and 'isiksik' (to stuff something in).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Siksin** mo ng damit ang maleta para magkasya lahat.","translation":"**Stuff** the suitcase with clothes so everything will fit."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong masyadong **siksin** ang bag at baka masira ang siper.","translation":"Don't **pack** the bag too tightly or the zipper might break."}]

translation: to roam around aimlessly; to loiter
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalakad o paggala-gala sa isang lugar nang walang tiyak na patutunguhan o layunin.
etymology: From `magpa-` (prefix) + `ampang-ampang` (roaming, loitering). The root itself is rare.
original_explanation: This is what you do at the mall when you're waiting for your perpetually late friend. You're not really shopping, just drifting from Uniqlo to Muji and back, trying to look busy. It's the human equivalent of a screensaver, just bouncing around without a real destination.
usage_notes: Describes an aimless, wandering movement. Often has a slightly negative connotation of being idle or unproductive.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na ang **magpaampang-ampang** diyan at tulungan mo ako.","translation":"Stop **roaming around aimlessly** there and help me."},{"sentence":"Habang naghihintay, nagpasya siyang **magpaampang-ampang** sa parke.","translation":"While waiting, he decided to **wander aimlessly** in the park."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao, karaniwang lalaki, na may malakas, malusog, at magandang pangangatawan.
original_explanation: This is your gym bro, your "kuya na laging nasa Gold's," o yung bida sa action movie na kayang buhatin ang leading lady with one arm. Hindi lang basta malaki, kundi well-proportioned at mukhang healthy. Think Chris Hemsworth as Thor, but make it Pinoy. The opposite of "sakitin" or "payatot."
usage_notes: Often used to describe men with a physically impressive physique.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **matipuno** at matangkad na binata ang nagligtas sa kanya.","translation":"A **well-built** and tall young man saved her."},{"sentence":"Nagsasanay siya sa gym araw-araw upang magkaroon ng **matipunong** katawan.","translation":"He trains at the gym every day to have a **robust** body."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pag-aabang o pagbabantay sa isang tago at estratehikong lugar upang biglaang salakayin ang isang kaaway o hulihin ang isang tao o hayop.
original_explanation: The OG 'wait for it...' move. Parang yung pag-aabang mo sa chat na mag-'seen' siya, tapos bigla mo siyang sasalakayin ng 'Bakit gising ka pa?!' That's a digital tambang. It's also what snipers do in movies and what cats do to mice.
usage_notes: Often used in military, police, or hunting contexts. Can also be used metaphorically for any surprise trap or confrontation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahulog sa **tambang** ng mga pulis ang mga magnanakaw.","translation":"The thieves fell into the police's **ambush**."},{"sentence":"Naghanda ng **tambang** ang mga sundalo sa dadaanan ng mga rebelde.","translation":"The soldiers prepared an **ambush** on the rebels' path."}]

translation: to work in a sugarcane field
meaning_filipino: Magtrabaho o gumawa sa isang taniman ng tubo, karaniwan ay sa pag-aani nito.
etymology: From 'bagan', an old word for sugarcane plantation.
original_explanation: A very specific job description you won't find on LinkedIn unless you're in Tarlac or Negros. It's the back-breaking work of a 'sakada' under the scorching sun. The original 'grind'.
usage_notes: This is a highly specialized term related to agriculture, specifically the sugarcane industry.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming taga-probinsya ang umaasa sa **magbabagan** tuwing panahon ng anihan.","translation":"Many people from the province rely on **working in the sugarcane fields** during harvest season."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpapakita ng kagalakan o pagiging aliw na naganap na. Ito ay ang nakaraang anyo ng pandiwang "tawa".
original_explanation: The past tense of laughing. This is what you did when you finally got the joke, five minutes after everyone else. Or when you saw your friend trip over nothing. "Bigla na lang siyang tumawa." It's the "haha" react, but yesterday.
usage_notes: Past tense of "tawa" (to laugh).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumawa** ako nang malakas sa napanood kong komedya.","translation":"I **laughed** loudly at the comedy I watched."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya napigilang **tumawa** sa sinabi mo.","translation":"He/She couldn't help but **laugh** at what you said."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang musikero na tumutugtog ng bandurya, isang instrumentong de-kuwerdas na karaniwang bahagi ng isang rondalla.
original_explanation: The person in the rondalla ensemble who plays the bandurria, the instrument that looks like a tiny guitar and sounds like a musical mandolin. They're the ones carrying the main melody, making your lola feel all the feels with classic haranas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tatay ko ay isang magaling na **bandurista** sa kanilang rondalla noong kabataan niya.","translation":"My father was a skilled **bandurria player** in their rondalla during his youth."},{"sentence":"Naghahanap ang grupo ng isang bagong **bandurista**.","translation":"The group is looking for a new **bandurria player**."}]

meaning_filipino: (Balbal) Ang pananakit o pagbugbog sa isang tao nang matindi.
original_explanation: This is the 'peeling' you don't want to be on the receiving end of. It's the Tagalog street version of 'to thrash' or 'to beat someone to a pulp'. Think action movie fight scene, but in a local kanto. 'Uupakan kita!' is the PH equivalent of 'You're gonna get it!'
usage_notes: This is slang and is considered aggressive and informal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagbanta ang siga na **mag-upak** ng sinumang lalapit sa teritoryo niya.","translation":"The tough guy threatened to **beat up** anyone who came near his territory."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magsimula ng gulo kung ayaw mong **ma-upak**.","translation":"Don't start trouble if you don't want to get **thrashed**."}]

translation: to go ahead; to continue; to persist
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapatuloy sa isang gawain o direksyon nang walang pag-aalinlangan; pag-usad o pagsulong.
etymology: From 'sige', which is from Spanish 'sigue' (he/she/it continues/follows).
original_explanation: This is the verbal equivalent of "push lang nang push!" or "G!" When your friend asks, "Tuloy ba tayo?" and you reply, "Sumige tayo!" it means you're all in. It's the energy you channel when you're on your 5th coffee just to finish a report.
usage_notes: Often used as an encouragement. 'Sige' by itself is extremely common. 'Sumige' is the verb form, meaning 'to act on the "sige"'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit mahirap ang daan, **sumige** pa rin sila sa paglalakbay.","translation":"Even though the road was difficult, they still **persisted** on their journey."},{"sentence":"**Sumige** ka lang sa iyong mga pangarap.","translation":"Just **keep going** towards your dreams."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng perpektong pagtutugma o pagbabagay ng mga bahagi, elemento, o indibidwal sa isa't isa na nagreresulta sa kaayusan at ganda.
etymology: From "pag-" (manner of) + "ka-" (abstract noun prefix) + "suwato" (compatible, harmonious), likely from a Chinese dialect.
original_explanation: 'Yung OOTD mo na perfect ang color combination from head to toe. 'Yung choreography ng dance group na sabay-sabay at on point lahat. 'Yung relationship niyo na pareho kayo ng trip at nagkakaintindihan kahit sa tinginan lang. That's pagkakasuwato. It's the aesthetic and emotional equivalent of a perfectly tuned instrument. #SanaAll
usage_notes: Implies a deeper, more natural compatibility than "pagkakasundo." Often used in contexts of aesthetics, relationships, and music.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakikita sa kanilang pagsasama ang tunay na **pagkakasuwato**.","translation":"True **harmony** can be seen in their relationship."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkakasuwato** ng mga kulay sa obra maestra ay kahanga-hanga.","translation":"The **consonance** of colors in the masterpiece is admirable."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang engrande, magastos, at detalyadong pagtatanghal, pagdiriwang, o produksiyon.
original_explanation: This is not just a party, it's a PARTY. Yung debut na may pitong gown, fireworks, at celebrity host. Yung company Christmas party na parang awards night. It’s the 'OA sa ganda at gastos' level of event. More is more!
usage_notes: Used to describe lavish events.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malaking **ekstrabagansa** ang inihanda para sa ika-100 anibersaryo ng lungsod.","translation":"A huge **extravaganza** was prepared for the city's 100th anniversary."},{"sentence":"Ang taunang parada ay isang musical **ekstrabagansa**.","translation":"The annual parade is a musical **extravaganza**."}]

translation: a light poke or touch with the fingertip
meaning_filipino: Isang marahan at mabilis na pagdaiti o pag-abot gamit ang dulo ng daliri, karaniwan upang makuha ang atensyon ng isang tao.
original_explanation: The 'kulbit' is the OG Filipino notification system before smartphones. It's that gentle poke you give your friend to point out some chismis, or what your seatmate does to you in class to ask for the answer. It’s less aggressive than a tap ('kalabit') and more discreet. It’s the physical version of 'Psst!'
usage_notes: Often used with the verb form 'kulbitin' (to poke someone lightly). It is a gentler action than 'kalabit'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang marahang **kulbit** sa braso ang gumising sa kanya.","translation":"A **light poke** on the arm woke him up."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman ko ang **kulbit** ng bata sa aking likuran.","translation":"I felt the child's **light touch** on my back."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging ligtas mula sa panganib, kapahamakan, o kasalanan.
original_explanation: This is what you feel after surviving the EDSA traffic on a payday Friday. It's the feeling of passing a subject you thought you'd fail. On a more serious note, it's being rescued from a flood, surviving a major life crisis, or for the religious, achieving salvation. It's the ultimate 'Whew, buti na lang!' moment.
usage_notes: Used in various contexts from physical safety to spiritual salvation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagdiwang ng pamilya ang kanyang **pagkaligtas** mula sa malubhang sakit.","translation":"The family celebrated his **survival** from a serious illness."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkaligtas** ng mga minero ay isang himala.","translation":"The **rescue/survival** of the miners was a miracle."}]

translation: notch; step; rung of a ladder
meaning_filipino: Isang ukit, baitang, o lupi na nagsisilbing tukuran ng paa, kamay, o anumang bagay upang umakyat o magkaroon ng suporta.
etymology: From 'agpang', meaning to fit or to be suitable. An 'agpangan' is a place where something (like a foot) can fit.
original_explanation: Think of it as the original life hack for climbing. It’s the little cuts on a coconut tree so you can climb it, the steps on a ladder, or even the different levels in a corporate hierarchy you're trying to climb. Each agpangan is a foothold to get you to the next level, whether you're getting buko or a promotion.
usage_notes: Can refer to literal steps/notches or metaphorical levels.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumawa siya ng mga **agpangan** sa puno ng niyog para madali itong akyatin.","translation":"He made **notches** on the coconut tree to make it easier to climb."},{"sentence":"Bawat **agpangan** ng hagdan ay maingat niyang tinapakan.","translation":"He carefully stepped on each **rung** of the ladder."}]

translation: to bridge; to act as a go-between
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-ugnay sa dalawang magkahiwalay na bagay, lugar, o panig; ang pagiging daan o tagapamagitan.
original_explanation: This isn't just about building a physical bridge over a river. It's what your 'marites' tita does when she connects you with her friend's single son. It's also what a project manager does, trying to connect the client's crazy demands with the dev team's reality. 'Siya ang nagtulay para magkabati ang mag-asawa.'
usage_notes: Can be used literally for building a bridge or figuratively for connecting people, ideas, or resolving conflicts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang gobyerno ay nagplanong **magtulay** sa dalawang pulo.","translation":"The government planned to **build a bridge** between the two islands."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **magtulay** sa pagitan ng dalawang nag-aaway na magkaibigan.","translation":"He tried to **act as a go-between** for the two fighting friends."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na hinango sa Ingles na 'legitimate', nangangahulugang tunay, totoo, at hindi peke.
original_explanation: The ultimate stamp of approval for anything, from a 'buy 1 take 1' promo to your friend's new jowa. If it's not a scam, if it's the real deal, it's **legit**. Parang yung feeling na pumasok yung sahod mo on time. That's legit happiness.
usage_notes: Primarily used in informal, conversational, and online contexts. A direct borrowing that has been fully integrated into Filipino slang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Legit** ba 'yang online store na 'yan? Baka ma-scam tayo.","translation":"Is that online store **legit**? We might get scammed."},{"sentence":"Wow, ang ganda ng bag mo! **Legit** 'yan?","translation":"Wow, your bag is beautiful! Is that **legit**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang trabaho o gawaing pansamantala at hindi permanente, na karaniwang ginagawa upang kumita ng dagdag na pera sa labas ng pangunahing hanapbuhay.
etymology: From English 'racket', where the meaning shifted from an illegal scheme to any kind of sideline or gig.
original_explanation: This is the Filipino's survival mode activated. Your 'raket' is your side hustle. Selling baked goods online? That's a raket. Doing freelance design after your 9-to-5? Raket. Hosting events on weekends? Raket. It's the art of making extra cash because, let's be real, the main job sometimes isn't enough. #DiskarteLang
usage_notes: A very common term in modern Filipino culture to describe supplementary income-generating activities.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **raket** ako mamayang gabi, kailangan kong kumanta sa isang kasal.","translation":"I have a **gig** tonight, I need to sing at a wedding."},{"sentence":"Naghahanap ako ng pwedeng **raket** para may pambili ako ng bagong cellphone.","translation":"I'm looking for a **side hustle** so I can buy a new cellphone."}]

meaning_filipino: Dumi na namumuo sa balat, binubuo ng mga patay na selula ng balat, pawis, at alikabok.
original_explanation: The 'eraser dust' that appears on your skin when you scrub really hard after skipping a shower or two. It's the physical proof of your 'pagod' or 'katamaran.' Your lola would say it's why you need a 'hilod' (loofah). It's not just dirt; it's a collection of yesterday's adventures.
usage_notes: Isang napaka-karaniwang, pang-araw-araw na salita. Maaaring gamitin bilang biro upang tuksuhin ang isang tao tungkol sa kanilang kalinisan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maligo ka na nga, ang dami mo nang **libag**!","translation":"Go take a shower already, you have so much **grime**!"},{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng bimpo para matanggal ang **libag** sa likod ko.","translation":"I need a washcloth to remove the **dead skin** on my back."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng negatibong imahe o pagkakakilala sa lipunan dahil sa mga nakaraang gawa o asal.
original_explanation: This is when the chismis about you is not good. If people whisper 'ay, 'yan 'yung nang-utang at 'di nagbayad' when you walk by, you've got a 'masamang pangalan'. It's harder to clean than a stained white shirt.
usage_notes: Refers to a damaged reputation or public image.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa tsismis, nagkaroon siya ng **masamang pangalan** sa kanilang barangay.","translation":"Because of gossip, she got a **bad reputation** in their village."},{"sentence":"Iniingatan niyang hindi magkaroon ng **masamang pangalan** ang kanilang pamilya.","translation":"He is careful not to give their family a **bad reputation**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matigas na deposito na namumuo sa ngipin at nabubuo kapag ang plake ay tumigas sa ibabaw ng ngipin.
original_explanation: This is the stuff your dentist scrapes off your teeth with that scary metal hook. It's like the permanent resident version of the food you ate last week. If your teeth were a condo, tartar is the tenant who never pays rent and throws loud parties.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng kalusugang dental.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong magpatingin sa dentista para matanggal ang **tartaro** sa iyong ngipin.","translation":"You need to see a dentist to remove the **tartar** from your teeth."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang posisyon o ayos ng pagtayo o pag-upo kung saan ang mga hita at binti ay magkahiwalay o nakabukaka.
original_explanation: 'Yan 'yung pwesto mo 'pag sumasakay ng jeep na maikli ang shorts, trying to be modest pero alanganin. O 'yung pag-upo ng mga 'alpha male' sa MRT na akala mo kanila 'yung buong upuan. 'Man-spreading' ang katumbas nito sa modern terms.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang pag-upo o pagtayo nang may malawak na pagitan sa mga binti. Maaaring may bahagyang negatibong konotasyon ng kawalan ng pino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinagsabihan niya ang anak na huwag umupo nang **kangkang** habang naka-palda.","translation":"She told her child not to sit with her legs **spread apart** while wearing a skirt."}]

meaning_filipino: Ari-arian, karapatan, o tradisyon na ipinapasa mula sa isang henerasyon patungo sa susunod, lalo na pagkatapos ng kamatayan ng isang tao.
etymology: From `pa-` + `mana`. The prefix `pa-` often indicates something given or caused. `Mana` means inheritance.
original_explanation: This is what you get from your lolo or lola when they pass away—could be land in the province, their secret adobo recipe, or their chismosa tendencies. It's the ultimate "mana" from heaven (or from them, at least). It's not just about money; it can also be a legacy, like your family's good name or that one "puto" business that's been around since the Spanish era.
usage_notes: Can refer to both tangible assets (like property) and intangible things (like values, traditions, or even genetic traits).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lumang bahay na bato ang tanging **pamana** sa kanya ng kanyang mga ninuno.","translation":"The old stone house is the only **inheritance** left to him by his ancestors."},{"sentence":"Ipinagpatuloy niya ang **pamana** ng kanyang ama sa pagtulong sa mga mahihirap.","translation":"He continued his father's **legacy** of helping the poor."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghahalungkat o paghahanap ng isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pag-aalis o paggalaw sa mga nakaharang.
original_explanation: What your mom does to your room looking for 'that thing.' Also, what you do to the ukay-ukay pile to find that one branded jacket. It’s the frantic search in your bag for your keys when you're standing in front of your door at 2 AM.
usage_notes: Implies a somewhat messy or urgent search.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa kanyang **pagkalkal** sa lumang baul, nakita niya ang mga litrato ng kanyang lola.","translation":"In her **rummaging** through the old chest, she found her grandmother's photos."},{"sentence":"Napagalitan siya dahil sa **pagkalkal** ng basura ng aso.","translation":"He was scolded because of the dog's **digging through** the trash."}]

translation: to be summarized; to be compiled
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtipon at pagbuod ng mga impormasyon o ideya sa isang mas maikli at siksik na paraan.
original_explanation: When your prof says, 'Class, I need your thesis in 300 words,' ang kailangan mong gawin ay i-malagom ang lahat ng pinaghirapan mo for one year. It's the art of the TL;DR, but for academics. Like turning a whole teleserye into a one-minute TikTok summary.
usage_notes: Often used in academic or formal contexts for summarizing reports, research, or long texts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **malagom** ang lahat ng datos bago matapos ang araw.","translation":"All the data needs **to be summarized** before the end of the day."},{"sentence":"Sa isang talata, sinubukan niyang **malagom** ang kanyang mga natutunan.","translation":"In one paragraph, he tried **to summarize** what he had learned."}]

translation: to look younger; to become younger
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita ng anyong mas bata kaysa sa tunay na edad; ang magmukhang bata.
original_explanation: The effect of a good skincare routine, a new haircut, or simply being 'unbothered.' It's what your Tita says to another Tita as a compliment: 'Uy, parang bumata ka!' It's the opposite of 'stressedt.'
usage_notes: Used to describe a person's appearance, not a literal change in age.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Talaga namang **bumata** si Aling Nena mula nang mag-retire siya.","translation":"Aling Nena really started **to look younger** ever since she retired."},{"sentence":"\"Parang **bumata** ka ng sampung taon sa gupit mo!\" puri niya.","translation":"\"You seem **to have gotten younger** by ten years with your haircut!\" she complimented."}]

translation: to find fault in; to criticize
meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang paghahanap ng mali, depekto, o pagkakamali sa isang tao, bagay, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung ginagawa ng tita mo sa'yo tuwing family reunion. 'Tumaba ka ata, iho?' o 'Wala ka pa ring jowa?' They will mamaliyan everything about you. It's the act of actively looking for something to criticize.
usage_notes: This is a very rare word construction, not in common use. More common terms would be 'pulaan', 'pintasan', or 'hanapan ng mali'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **mamaliyan** ang gawa ng iba kung hindi ka naman tutulong.","translation":"Don't **find fault in** the work of others if you aren't going to help."},{"sentence":"Sa halip na **mamaliyan** ang bawat kilos niya, subukan mo siyang unawain.","translation":"Instead of **criticizing** her every move, try to understand her."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghalungkat o paghahanap sa isang lalagyan o tumpok ng mga bagay, karaniwang sa paraang hindi maayos.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you can't find your keys in your bag that's basically a black hole of receipts, old candy, and lipsticks. It's the frantic, sometimes desperate, act of digging through a mess. 'Yung pagbutbot mo sa ukay-ukay para makahanap ng vintage jacket.
usage_notes: Often implies a slightly messy or frantic search.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagbutbot** niya sa basurahan ay nagdulot ng ingay.","translation":"His **rummaging** through the trash can caused a noise."},{"sentence":"Itigil mo na ang **pagbutbot** sa mga lumang gamit ko.","translation":"Stop **rummaging** through my old things."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na porsyon ng pagkain na inihahain bago ang pangunahing putahe upang pampagana.
etymology: Origin is uncertain, but likely from 'pa-' + 'putat'. 'Putat' can mean to cut or pick, which fits the idea of small food portions.
original_explanation: The opening act before the main concert of your meal. Think of it as the 'pampagana'—the kropek, the cheese sticks, or the small bowl of peanuts you munch on while waiting for the sinigang. It's the food that tells your stomach, "Get ready, something bigger is coming!"
usage_notes: Often used for small side dishes or starters. Can sometimes be interchanged with 'pampagana'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghain siya ng inihaw na pusit bilang **pamutat**.","translation":"She served grilled squid as an **appetizer**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong ubusin ang **pamutat**; may darating pang main course.","translation":"Don't finish the **appetizer**; the main course is still coming."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang natamong abilidad o kagalingan sa isang partikular na gawain dahil sa madalas na pagsasagawa o pag-eensayo.
etymology: From ka- + sanay + -an. Denotes the quality or state of being 'sanay' (accustomed, practiced).
original_explanation: This is your 'special skill' sa resume, like 'marunong mag-Excel' or 'kayang ubusin ang isang galon ng ice cream in one sitting.' It's what you get from doing something over and over, like your kasanayan in navigating EDSA traffic or your kasanayan in finding the best ukay-ukay deals.
usage_notes: Can refer to both physical skills (like sports) and mental skills (like programming).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng matinding **kasanayan** upang maging isang magaling na chef.","translation":"You need great **skill** to become a good chef."},{"sentence":"Ang araw-araw na pagbabasa ay nagpapahusay sa kanyang **kasanayan** sa pagsusulat.","translation":"Daily reading improves his writing **practice**."}]

translation: to separate (from each other); to go separate ways
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtahak ng magkakaibang landas ng isang grupo ng mga tao o bagay; ang pagiging magkakalayo sa isa't isa.
original_explanation: The 'it's not you, it's me' of verbs. It's what barkadas do after college, what couples do when the 'cool off' becomes permanent, or what happens to your 13th-month pay the moment it enters your bank account. The official verb of 'Walang forever!'
usage_notes: The repetition 'hiwa-hiwalay' emphasizes that the action is done by or affects multiple subjects, each going their own way. It is a plural or distributive form of 'maghiwalay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng graduation, nagpasya ang magkakaibigan na **maghiwa-hiwalay** na ng landas.","translation":"After graduation, the friends decided to **go their separate ways**."},{"sentence":"Oras na para **maghiwa-hiwalay** tayo at hanapin ang ating mga pamilya sa mall.","translation":"It's time for us to **separate** and find our respective families in the mall."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging masining; ang mataas na antas ng kahusayan at pagkamalikhain sa sining o anumang gawain.
etymology: Mula sa kabilaang panlaping 'ka-...-an' at salitang-ugat na 'sining' (art).
original_explanation: This is a deep, slightly formal word. It's not just 'art,' it's the *artistry* itself. It's the vibe you get from a well-directed indie film, a perfectly plated sisig, or a beautifully crafted parol. It’s the 'wow' factor in creation, the opposite of 'pwede na 'yan'.
usage_notes: More formal and less common in everyday conversation than 'sining' (art). It refers to the quality or state of being artistic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Makikita sa kanyang mga obra ang pambihirang **kasiningan**.","translation":"Extraordinary **artistry** can be seen in his masterpieces."},{"sentence":"Hinahangaan ko ang **kasiningan** sa pagkakagawa ng pelikula.","translation":"I admire the **artistry** in the making of the film."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sapilitang kontribusyon sa kita ng estado, na ipinapataw ng pamahalaan sa mga manggagawa, negosyo, at idinadagdag sa halaga ng mga bilihin at serbisyo.
original_explanation: The reason your payslip has a 'deductions' column that makes you cry a little inside. It's the government's subscription fee that you can't cancel, supposedly for roads, bridges, and... well, you know. That thing you have to file every April 15th while questioning all your life choices.
usage_notes: Can also be used figuratively as a tribute or offering, as in 'buwis-buhay' (life-threatening, lit. 'life tax').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang pagbabayad ng tamang **buwis** para sa ikauunlad ng bansa.","translation":"Paying the correct **tax** is important for the country's progress."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang kaltas sa sahod ko dahil sa **buwis**.","translation":"The deduction from my salary is big because of the **tax**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang opisyal na pahintulot o kapangyarihang ibinigay para sa isang gawain.
original_explanation: Ito yung papel o dokumento (or even a text message) na pruweba na pinayagan ka. "Nasaan ang **autorisasyon** mo para kainin ang huling piraso ng pizza?" Ito ang 'written consent' para hindi ka mapagalitan.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa permiso o permit mismo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Humingi siya ng **autorisasyon** mula sa kanyang manager bago umalis.","translation":"He asked for **authorization** from his manager before leaving."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagtatantiya o kalkulasyon sa bilang, halaga, o sukat ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung "hula-hula with a little bit of math". 'Yung tinatanong ka, "Mga ilan kaya ang tao sa party?" tapos sasabihin mo, "Taya ko mga 50." It's your educated guess. Parang pag-estimate mo kung aabot pa ba 'yung sahod mo hanggang sa susunod na kinsenas. Puro taya lang.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin kasama ang salitang "mga" (around/about). Maaari ring maging pandiwa: "tayain" (to estimate).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **taya** mo sa magagastos natin sa biyahe?","translation":"What is your **estimate** of our expenses for the trip?"},{"sentence":"Sa **taya** ng mga eksperto, aabutin pa ng ilang taon bago matapos ang proyekto.","translation":"According to the experts' **calculation**, it will take several more years before the project is finished."}]

translation: to attend to; to take care of
meaning_filipino: Pagbibigay ng atensyon, pag-aalaga, o pag-aasikaso sa isang tao, bagay, o gawain.
original_explanation: What your mom does for the entire family, 24/7, with no pay and no days off. It's being the project manager of the household, the event planner for the fiesta, and the nurse for a sick relative, all rolled into one. The ultimate act of service.
usage_notes: A very common verb that encompasses a wide range of actions related to managing, caring for, and attending to needs.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **umasikaso** sa lahat ng bisita sa kasal.","translation":"She was the one who **attended to** all the guests at the wedding."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **umasikaso** ng mga papeles sa munisipyo.","translation":"I need to **take care of** some documents at the municipal hall."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyon na nagpapahiwatig ng pagkamangha, paghanga, o kung minsan ay pagkadismaya o pagkainis.
etymology: From English slang 'sheesh', popularized by internet culture and Gen Z.
original_explanation: Originally from AAVE, this became a Gen Z sound effect for anything impressive or shocking. Narinig mo sa TikTok at sa mga ML players. 'Sheesh! Ganda ng sapatos mo!' o 'Sheesh! Ang mahal ng bilihin!'. Parang 'wow' na may kasamang hype.
usage_notes: Primarily used by younger generations and online. The intonation is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sheesh!** Ang galing ng ginawa mong play sa laro kanina!","translation":"**Sheesh!** Your play in the game earlier was amazing!"},{"sentence":"Nakita mo ba yung presyo ng sibuyas? **Sheesh!**","translation":"Did you see the price of onions? **Sheesh!**"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang labis na pagkahilig o pagkalulong sa isang bagay o gawain, kadalasan ay may negatibong konotasyon; o ang paglubog sa isang kalagayan tulad ng putik o kalungkutan.
original_explanation: It's more than just a habit. It's being stuck. You can be 'gumumon sa droga' (addicted to drugs), but you can also be 'gumumon sa kalungkutan' (wallowing in sadness) after a breakup. It’s that feeling of being neck-deep in something you can't easily get out of, like being stuck in EDSA traffic but for your soul.
usage_notes: Has a strong negative connotation, implying a destructive dependency or a state of being helplessly stuck.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming kabataan ang **gumugumon** sa online games.","translation":"Many youths are **becoming addicted** to online games."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **gumumon** sa kalungkutan; kailangan mong bumangon.","translation":"Don't **wallow** in sadness; you need to get back up."}]

meaning_filipino: Malapit nang mangyari ngunit hindi natuloy; halos.
original_explanation: The official phrase for all life's close calls. Kamuntik na akong mahulog sa kanal (I almost fell into the canal). Kamuntik na akong ma-late (I was almost late). Kamuntik na kaming maging kami (We almost got together). It's the story of things that didn't happen, but were *this close*. The 'na' is almost always attached.
usage_notes: Almost always used as the two-word phrase 'kamuntik na'. The verb that follows is often in the completed aspect (e.g., 'kamuntik na nahulog' not 'kamuntik na mahuhulog').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kamuntik na** akong manalo sa lotto.","translation":"I **almost** won the lottery."},{"sentence":"Dahan-dahan, **kamuntik na** siyang madapa!","translation":"Careful, he **nearly** stumbled!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghukay o pag-alis ng lupa, bato, o iba pang materyal upang lumikha ng butas, guwang, o uka.
original_explanation: Think of it as digging, but with more force. Like when a backhoe takes a huge bite out of the earth for a new condo construction, or when you aggressively scoop out the last bit of ice cream from the tub. That's the spirit of 'ukab'.
usage_notes: Often used for large-scale digging or creating a significant cavity. Can also be a noun 'uka' meaning cavity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Inukab** ng malakas na agos ng tubig ang pampang ng ilog.","translation":"The strong water current **excavated** the riverbank."},{"sentence":"Nag-**ukab** sila ng malaking butas sa likod-bahay para gawing swimming pool.","translation":"They **dug out** a large hole in the backyard to make a swimming pool."}]

translation: to obtain, to achieve, to attain
meaning_filipino: Makuha o matamo ang isang bagay na ninanais o pinagsikapan sa pamamagitan ng pagsisikap.
original_explanation: This is the goal of every student finishing their thesis, every employee chasing a promotion, and every person swiping right hoping for a match. It's about finally getting what you worked for, whether it's a diploma, a higher salary, or true love. 'Sana all makamtan ang true love.'
usage_notes: Often used in the context of goals, dreams, justice, or success. It implies effort was exerted.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsisikap siyang mag-aral upang **makamtan** ang kanyang mga pangarap.","translation":"He is studying hard to **achieve** his dreams."},{"sentence":"Sana ay **makamtan** na natin ang hustisya para sa mga biktima.","translation":"Hopefully, we can **obtain** justice for the victims."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kabuuang ayos, tindig, o paraan ng paglakad ng isang tao na nagpapakita ng kanyang katangian o damdamin.
original_explanation: "Kiyas" is your overall vibe in motion. It’s your swag, your tindig, your "aura" when you walk into a room. May "kiyas-militar" (military bearing), "kiyas-mayaman" (looks rich), or "kiyas-pagod" (looks tired from a 12-hour shift). It’s how you carry yourself. Your lola might say, "Ayusin mo ang kiyas mo!" which means "Stop slouching and walk like you have a purpose!"
usage_notes: Often used to describe a person's physical presence and how it reflects their personality or status.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit simple lang ang damit niya, may **kiyas** siyang pang-artista.","translation":"Even with simple clothes, she has the **bearing** of a celebrity."},{"sentence":"Makikita sa kanyang **kiyas** ang pagiging isang sundalo.","translation":"You can see from his **posture** that he is a soldier."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malalim na sisidlan na karaniwang bilog, ginagamit para sa mga pagkaing may sabaw tulad ng sopas, sinigang, o lugaw.
etymology: Likely from Hokkien 碗 (buan, 'bowl') + 鈷 (koo, 'cup'), evolving into 'mangkok'.
original_explanation: The official vessel for anything with sabaw. It's the throne for sinigang, the kingdom of lugaw, and the holy grail for your late-night instant noodles. A plate is for presentation, but a **mangkok** is for serious, get-down-to-business eating. It's a hug in ceramic form.
usage_notes: A fundamental piece of kitchenware in any Filipino household.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakikuha mo ako ng isang **mangkok** para sa sopas.","translation":"Please get me a **bowl** for the soup."},{"sentence":"Paborito niyang gamitin ang asul na **mangkok** tuwing kumakain ng ramen.","translation":"He loves using the blue **bowl** whenever he eats ramen."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sining ng pagbuburda o paglalagay ng disenyo sa tela gamit ang karayom at sinulid.
original_explanation: Your lola's favorite hobby. It's the art of making flowers and names appear on handkerchiefs and pillowcases using a needle and thread. Today, it’s making a comeback as "aesthetic" patches on denim jackets. **Sulam** is basically drawing with thread.
usage_notes: The verb form is "magsulam" (to embroider) or "sulsihan" (to embroider on something). Not to be confused with "ulam" (viand).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng **sulam** sa Barong Tagalog na suot niya.","translation":"The **embroidery** on the Barong Tagalog he's wearing is beautiful."},{"sentence":"Natuto siyang gumawa ng **sulam** mula sa kanyang lola.","translation":"She learned how to do **embroidery** from her grandmother."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kondisyong medikal kung saan namamaga ang daluyan ng hangin patungo sa baga (bronchial tubes), na nagdudulot ng matinding pag-uubo.
etymology: From Spanish 'bronquitis' or a Filipinized spelling of English 'bronchitis'.
original_explanation: That nasty cough that won't go away, making you sound like a walwal-era car engine trying to start on a cold morning. It's more than just a simple 'ubo'; it's the kind that makes your lola tell you to stop drinking cold water and sleeping with wet hair.
usage_notes: A medical term used in formal and informal health discussions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinayuhan ng doktor ang pasyente na may **brongkitisin** na itigil ang paninigarilyo.","translation":"The doctor advised the patient with **bronchitis** to stop smoking."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng sadyang pakikipagtalo o pakikipag-away sa isang tao hinggil sa isang usapin.
original_explanation: When you're ready to throw down, not with fists, but with words. It's that "Tara, usap tayo sa labas" energy, but you're just going to argue. The verbal equivalent of squaring up, often used to dare someone into a debate they can't win.
usage_notes: This is the object-focused future tense form. 'Babagan mo siya' means 'You will confront him/her'. More common synonyms are 'awayin' or 'kainisan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang **babagan** ang guro, tanggapin mo na lang ang iyong grado.","translation":"Don't **confront** the teacher anymore, just accept your grade."}]

translation: to strike against; to hold a strike at
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa ng welga o sama-samang pagtigil sa pagtatrabaho laban sa isang kumpanya, institusyon, o pamahalaan bilang isang anyo ng protesta.
original_explanation: When the BPO team has had enough of the toxic management and low pay, and they all decide to log off at the same time. This is the verb form of "Tama na! Sobra na!" It's the ultimate group project where the goal is to stop working to demand better conditions. The target of this action is the one being `pinagwewelgahan`.
usage_notes: A verb used to denote the target of a labor strike or protest.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagbanta ang mga manggagawa na **pagwelgahan** ang pabrika kung hindi itataas ang kanilang sahod.","translation":"The workers threatened **to strike against** the factory if their wages are not increased."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng unyon kung dapat bang **pagwelgahan** ang buong industriya.","translation":"The union is studying whether they should **hold a strike against** the entire industry."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang balbal na parirala na pinagsasama ang "woke" at "yarn" (isang pagpapaikli ng "iyan"). Karaniwan itong ginagamit nang may panunuya upang tukuyin ang isang pahayag na nagkukunwaring may malalim na kamalayang panlipunan.
etymology: Combination of English loanword 'woke' and Filipino gay lingo/slang 'yarn' (a stylized form of 'iyan' or 'that').
original_explanation: The sarcastic younger sibling of 'woke'. It's what you say when someone states the most obvious 'socially aware' take and expects a medal for it. Friend: 'Guys, I think poverty is bad.' You: 'Woke yarn?' It's the Filipino way of saying 'Wow, what a groundbreaking revelation' with a digital eye-roll. It's peak Swardspeak-meets-Gen-Z-internet-culture.
usage_notes: Almost always used sarcastically or ironically. A very contemporary slang phrase popular on social media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sabi niya, 'Dapat maging mabait tayo sa isa't isa.' **Woke yarn**?","translation":"He said, 'We should be kind to each other.' **So woke of him, right**?"},{"sentence":"Nag-post siya tungkol sa climate change habang nasa eroplano. **Woke yarn**.","translation":"He posted about climate change while on a plane. **(That's so) woke (of him)**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng katawan ng tao sa magkabilang gilid ng leeg kung saan nakakabit ang mga braso.
original_explanation: The original 'sandalan'. Dito ka umiiyak kapag sawi, dito sumasandal pag pagod sa commute. It's the part of your body that carries the weight of your backpack and the 'bigat ng mundo'. Tandaan: 'Aanhin mo ang malapad na balikat kung hindi naman para sa'yo sasandal?' Hugot!
usage_notes: Ginagamit nang literal para sa bahagi ng katawan. Sa matalinghagang paraan, ito ay kumakatawan sa responsibilidad o pasanin, tulad ng sa 'pasan sa balikat'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masakit ang aking kaliwang **balikat**.","translation":"My left **shoulder** hurts."},{"sentence":"Nasa iyong mga **balikat** ang kinabukasan ng iyong pamilya.","translation":"The future of your family rests on your **shoulders**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mapanganib at nakahahawang sakit na dulot ng Variola virus, na nagdudulot ng mga butlig na may nana sa buong katawan.
original_explanation: The OG pandemic disease bago pa nauso ang COVID. 'Pag sinabing bulutong, ang image agad ay 'yung mga butlig-butlig na nag-iiwan ng peklat. The more common and less severe version today is chickenpox, or *bulutong-tubig*.
usage_notes: In modern casual conversation, it is often confused with 'bulutong-tubig' (chickenpox). However, medically and formally, 'bulutong' refers to the much more severe and now-eradicated disease, smallpox.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa bakuna, halos nalipol na ang sakit na **bulutong** sa buong mundo.","translation":"Because of the vaccine, the disease **smallpox** has been almost eradicated worldwide."},{"sentence":"Nagkaroon siya ng peklat dahil sa **bulutong** noong bata pa siya.","translation":"He has a scar because of **smallpox** when he was a child."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang dalubhasa sa paglalagay ng pampaganda o kolorete sa mukha at katawan, karaniwan para sa mga layuning pansining, pantelebisyon, pampelikula, o pang-entablado.
etymology: Mula sa wikang Ingles na 'makeup' (pampaganda) at 'artist' (artista, alagad ng sining).
original_explanation: The person you hire for your wedding, debut, or graduation so you don't look like a stressed-out puyat zombie in your photos. They're magicians who can hide your eyebags from last night's K-drama marathon and give you that 'effortless' glow that actually took two hours and a lot of setting spray.
usage_notes: Isang salitang hiram mula sa Ingles na malawakang ginagamit sa Pilipinas, lalo na sa industriya ng pagpapaganda at aliwan. Madalas isinusulat bilang dalawang salita.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong mag-book ng **makeup artist** para sa kasal ko.","translation":"I need to book a **makeup artist** for my wedding."},{"sentence":"Sikat na **makeup artist** sa mga celebrity si Juan.","translation":"Juan is a famous **makeup artist** for celebrities."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng bitag o patibong na partikular na idinisenyo para sa paghuli ng mga daga.
original_explanation: The ultimate frenemy of Jerry (from Tom and Jerry). It's that contraption you set up in the dark corners of your house, baited with cheese or a piece of dried fish, hoping to end the pitter-patter of tiny feet at 3 AM. A classic panghuli ng daga is a testament to human ingenuity against household pests.
usage_notes: This is a specific compound noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si Tatay ng bagong **panghuli ng daga** sa palengke.","translation":"Dad bought a new **mousetrap** at the market."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka at baka maipit ka sa **panghuli ng daga**.","translation":"Be careful or you might get caught in the **mousetrap**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng maraming laman; may sustansya o kabuluhan.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung part ng manok na gusto mo, puro karne walang buto. O kaya 'yung chismis na juicy at may resibo. Hindi 'yung puro hangin lang. It's about having substance, whether it's in your adobo or the latest tea.
usage_notes: Often used to describe food (meaty, fleshy) or content (substantial, meaningful).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas gusto ko ang **malaman** na parte ng isda.","translation":"I prefer the **fleshy** part of the fish."},{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng isang **malaman** na talakayan tungkol sa isyung ito.","translation":"We need a **substantial** discussion about this issue."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangunahing lungsod ng isang bansa o rehiyon, na nagsisilbing sentro ng pamahalaan at komersiyo.
etymology: A compound word from 'ulo' (head) and 'bayan' (nation, town).
original_explanation: Another deep Tagalog word you'll find in textbooks but rarely hear at the 'palengke'. It literally means 'head of the nation' ('ulo' + 'bayan') and refers to the capital city, like Manila. If you use 'ulumbayan' in a sentence, people might think you're a history professor or a contestant in a 'Buwan ng Wika' contest. 'Kabisera' or just 'capital' is what we say.
usage_notes: A very formal and somewhat archaic term for a capital city. 'Kabisera' (from Spanish 'cabecera') or 'punong lungsod' are more common formal alternatives.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Lungsod ng Maynila ang kasalukuyang **ulumbayan** ng Pilipinas.","translation":"Manila City is the current **capital city** of the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Maraming pangarap ang nabubuo at nasisira sa **ulumbayan**.","translation":"Many dreams are made and broken in the **metropolis**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mabilis at paikot na paggalaw ng hangin, tubig, o kahit ng alikabok.
original_explanation: Imagine a mini-ipo-ipo (tornado) made of dust and leaves in the street. That's an alimpuyo. It can also describe the swirl of water going down the drain, or more dramatically, a whirlpool in the sea. Metaphorically, it's the chaotic swirl of emotions you feel during a major life crisis or when 5 deadlines are due on the same day.
usage_notes: Can refer to wind (whirlwind), water (whirlpool), or even dust (dust devil). Often used in literature to describe turmoil.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **alimpuyo** ng alikabok ang namuo sa gitna ng kalsada.","translation":"A **whirlwind** of dust formed in the middle of the road."},{"sentence":"Nahigop ng malakas na **alimpuyo** sa dagat ang maliit na bangka.","translation":"The small boat was sucked in by a strong **whirlpool** in the sea."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang isipan ay nasa gitna ng isang **alimpuyo** ng mga problema.","translation":"His mind was in the middle of a **vortex** of problems."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng pagsasalita, pagsulat, o pagkilos na may bigat, diin, o puwersa.
original_explanation: This is how your mom says "Umuwi ka nang maaga!" It's not a suggestion; it's a command backed by the threat of a flying tsinelas. A madiin na "no" is the kind that ends all arguments. It has weight, it has power, it has finality.
usage_notes: Can describe a way of speaking, writing, or even a physical press.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Madiin** ang kanyang pagtanggi sa alok.","translation":"His refusal of the offer was **emphatic**."},{"sentence":"Binigkas niya ang bawat salita sa **madiin** na paraan.","translation":"He uttered every word in a **forceful** manner."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggalaw pataas o pababa sa nilalaman ng isang screen ng kompyuter o telepono.
original_explanation: 3 AM na, nagscroll ka pa rin sa Facebook feed mo. You're not looking for anything, you're just avoiding your responsibilities. It's called 'doomscrolling,' bes.
usage_notes: Past tense. The present tense is 'nag-i-scroll' or 'nag-scro-scroll'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagscroll** ako sa newsfeed hanggang makita ko ang luma naming litrato.","translation":"I **scrolled** through the newsfeed until I saw our old photo."},{"sentence":"Walang magawa kaya **nagscroll** na lang siya sa Instagram.","translation":"Having nothing to do, he just **scrolled** on Instagram."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang elementong kemikal na may simbolong Mg at atomikong bilang na 12. Ito ay isang mamuting-pilak na metal na mahalaga sa maraming prosesong biyolohikal.
original_explanation: 'Yung mineral na iniinom mo para 'di ka pulikatin after mag-Zumba, o para makatulog ka nang mahimbing after mag-overthink buong gabi. It's the chill pill of minerals.
usage_notes: Isang terminong siyentipiko na ginagamit sa kimika, medisina, at nutrisyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang saging at mga mani ay mayaman sa **Magnisyum**.","translation":"Bananas and nuts are rich in **Magnesium**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang impormal at magiliw na tawag sa isang kaibigang lalaki o kasama.
etymology: Mula sa salitang balbal na 'paps' o 'papi', na may impluwensyang Espanyol ('-ito' diminutive suffix).
original_explanation: A cuter, more 'conyo' version of 'paps' or 'papi'. It's what you call your bro when you're feeling extra friendly, maybe when you're about to ask for a favor. "Paprito, pa-libre naman ng kape!" It has that "tropa but make it charming" vibe.
usage_notes: Isang salitang balbal na karaniwang ginagamit ng mga kabataan at sa mga impormal na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uy, **paprito**, kamusta ang lakad mo kahapon?","translation":"Hey, **buddy**, how was your trip yesterday?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa ng pananahi ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay damit, para sa ibang tao.
original_explanation: The ultimate pakiusap to your lola or a fashion student friend. 'Bes, pwede mo ba akong **ipagtahi** ng costume para sa Christmas party?' It's not just 'to sew' (manahi), but 'to sew FOR someone.' It’s a verb powered by favors and deadlines.
usage_notes: A common benefactive verb. The person for whom the sewing is done is the beneficiary.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpapasalamat ako dahil **ipinagtahi** ako ni nanay ng bagong uniporme.","translation":"I am thankful because my mom **sewed** a new uniform **for me**."},{"sentence":"Maaari mo ba akong **ipagtahi** ng butas sa aking medyas?","translation":"Could you **sew** the hole in my sock **for me**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ilipat o isalin ang isang likido mula sa isang lalagyan patungo sa iba; magbigay nang walang pag-iimbot o pagtitira.
original_explanation: Like pouring your heart out in a hugot post at 3 AM. Or when your team lead asks you to ibuhos all your effort into a project with a crazy deadline. Also, what you do with the gravy at Jollibee. UNLI GRAVY!
usage_notes: Can be used literally for liquids or figuratively for emotions, effort, or support.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ibuhos** mo na ang lahat ng tubig sa balde.","translation":"**Pour** all the water into the bucket."},{"sentence":"Hayaan mong **ibuhos** ko ang lahat ng sama ng loob ko.","translation":"Let me **pour out** all my frustrations."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking plantang pang-industriya kung saan ang mga hilaw na materyales, tulad ng langis, ay dinadalisay o pinoproseso upang maging mga produktong magagamit.
original_explanation: Ito yung lugar na parang giant kusina para sa krudo (crude oil). Dito niluluto at hinihiwa-hiwalay ang langis para maging gasolina, diesel, at iba pang petrolyo products. Basically, the source of the magic liquid that makes your Grab car run and your Meralco bill... well, exist.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May malaking **repineriya** ng langis sa Bataan.","translation":"There is a large oil **refinery** in Bataan."},{"sentence":"Ang pagsasara ng **repineriya** ay maaaring makaapekto sa presyo ng gasolina.","translation":"The closure of the **refinery** could affect the price of gasoline."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking tropikal na prutas na may matulis at matinik na balat at malakas na amoy, na kilala sa lasa nitong parang custard.
original_explanation: The king of fruits that requires a hazmat suit to eat. It smells like a gas leak in a gym locker but tastes like heaven to those who dare. You either love it or want to ban it from all public transportation. There is no in-between.
usage_notes: The spelling 'duryan' is also common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala ang Davao sa masasarap na **durian**.","translation":"Davao is known for its delicious **durian**."},{"sentence":"Bawal magpasok ng **durian** sa hotel dahil sa matapang na amoy nito.","translation":"Bringing **durian** into the hotel is prohibited because of its strong odor."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tahimik at matiyagang pagtitiis sa sakit, hirap, o sama ng loob nang hindi nagrereklamo o nagpapakita ng damdamin.
original_explanation: "Atim" (or more commonly, its verb forms like 'atimin' or 'inatim') is that classic Filipino trait of enduring hardship without making a fuss. It's your mom working two jobs without complaining, or you silently dealing with your slow office internet. It’s the emotional equivalent of biting your tongue. It’s suffering in silence, but with dignity.
usage_notes: Often used in its conjugated forms like 'inatim' (endured) or 'aatiimin' (will endure). It implies silent suffering or stoic endurance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"In**atim** niya ang lahat ng panunukso ng kanyang mga kaklase.","translation":"He silently **endured** all the teasing from his classmates."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **atimin** ang hirap para sa kinabukasan ng pamilya.","translation":"One must **bear** the hardship for the family's future."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat ng mga bagay na tinipon o inipon dahil sa isang partikular na interes.
original_explanation: This is your stash. Your hoard. Your treasure trove. Pwedeng koleksyon ng sapatos, ng action figures, o ng sama ng loob. It's the set of things you gather, whether they spark joy or trauma.
usage_notes: This is the more common spelling compared to 'koleksiyon' for a set of items.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng **koleksyon** mo ng mga halaman!","translation":"Your **collection** of plants is beautiful!"},{"sentence":"May bago akong idadagdag sa **koleksyon** ko ng Funko Pop.","translation":"I have a new one to add to my Funko Pop **collection**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamataas na uri ng boses ng isang lalaking mang-aawit, o isang mang-aawit na may ganitong boses.
original_explanation: In the choir, this is the guy with the highest male voice, often getting the romantic lead or the soaring high notes. Think of him as the male counterpart to the soprano, the Birit King of the group.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa konteksto ng musika, partikular sa pag-awit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya bilang isang mahusay na **tenor** sa buong Asya.","translation":"He is known as a great **tenor** throughout Asia."},{"sentence":"Ang piyesa ay nangangailangan ng isang **tenor** na kayang abutin ang mataas na C.","translation":"The piece requires a **tenor** who can reach a high C."}]

translation: to jog; to run lightly or intermittently
meaning_filipino: Paggalaw na parang tumatakbo ngunit sa mas mabagal na tulin o may kasamang paghinto; pagtakbo nang hindi seryoso o sa maikling distansya lamang.
original_explanation: This is the 'I want to be healthy but I also love my bed' kind of run. It's not a full-on sprint; it's more like a casual jog around the village or what you do when you're late for the MRT but not *that* late. A little bit of running, a little bit of walking, a lot of 'kaya pa ba?'
usage_notes: The repetition of the root's first two syllables (`takbu`) indicates a diminutive, less intense, or intermittent action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **tumakbu-takbo** sa parke tuwing umaga para mag-ehersisyo.","translation":"He likes to **jog** in the park every morning to exercise."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na tawag o pantukoy sa isang lalaki, karaniwang kaibigan o kasamahan.
original_explanation: It's the Pinoy version of "bro" or "dude". It's what you call your barkada when you're about to play basketball, go for a drink, or just hang out. "Tara, boi!" is the unofficial start of many great (and sometimes questionable) adventures.
usage_notes: A very informal and friendly term of address between males.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uy, **boi**, kamusta na? Tagal nating hindi nagkita.","translation":"Hey, **bro**, how are you? It's been a while since we last saw each other."},{"sentence":"Salamat sa tulong mo, **boi**!","translation":"Thanks for your help, **dude**!"}]

translation: act of braving, wading through, facing (a challenge)
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagharap o pagdaan sa isang panganib, hirap, o balakid nang may tapang.
original_explanation: This is you braving the EDSA traffic on a payday Friday. It's walking through a flooded street in España just to get to class. Pagsuong is the national sport of every Filipino commuter and anyone trying to finish their thesis. It's facing a challenge head-on, whether it's a storm or your mother-in-law's critical gaze.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of facing difficulties, dangers, or physical obstacles like floods or storms.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinahangaan ko ang kanyang **pagsuong** sa malakas na ulan para lamang makarating.","translation":"I admire his **act of braving** the strong rain just to arrive."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagsuong** sa mga hamon ng buhay ay nagpapatatag sa atin.","translation":"**Facing** life's challenges makes us stronger."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pampublikong sasakyan na maaaring arkilahin para sa isang partikular na biyahe, na may metro para sukatin ang bayad batay sa distansya at oras.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na "taxi", pinaikling anyo ng "taxicab".
original_explanation: Before Grab and Angkas, there was the OG ride-hailing service, the taxi. Sila 'yung "boss, metro plus" o "boss, dagdag bente" gang. Sila rin 'yung sasabihan mong "sa tabi lang po, manong" pero ihahatid ka sa gitna ng kalsada. A true test of patience and negotiation skills.
usage_notes: Isang napakakaraniwang salitang hiram.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumakay kami ng **taxi** papuntang airport dahil marami kaming dala.","translation":"We took a **taxi** to the airport because we had a lot of luggage."},{"sentence":"Manong, magkano po hanggang SM Megamall kung de-kontrata at hindi de-metro ang **taxi**?","translation":"Sir, how much to SM Megamall if the **taxi** is on a contract basis and not metered?"}]

meaning_filipino: Puno o batbat ng isang bagay; nag-uumapaw.
original_explanation: Imagine your phone's gallery after a vacation - 'timak' sa pictures. Or your lola's house during Christmas - 'timak' sa palamuti. It means something is absolutely jam-packed or overflowing. It's the state of your bag when you try to fit all your 'just in case' items.
