usage_notes: A bit more poetic or literary than 'puno'. Often used with 'ng' or 'sa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang hardin ay **timak** sa makukulay na bulaklak.","translation":"The garden is **full of** colorful flowers."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang puso ay **timak** ng galit matapos siyang lokohin.","translation":"His heart was **replete with** anger after being deceived."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi nagpapakita o nakakaramdam ng emosyon; manhid o walang pakialam sa nararamdaman ng iba.
original_explanation: This is your ex who broke up with you via text. Or that boss who lays off people with a smile. Parang robot, walang empathy. Sila yung tipo na iiyak ka sa harap nila pero ang tanong, "Tapos ka na?" Cold as ice.
usage_notes: A strong term describing a lack of empathy or emotional response. Can be seen as an insult.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paano mo nagawang saktan siya nang ganoon? Isa kang **walang-damdamin** na tao!","translation":"How could you hurt her like that? You are a **heartless** person!"},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang tugon ay maikli at **walang-damdamin**.","translation":"His response was short and **emotionless**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang baybayin o pampang ng dagat; ang lugar kung saan nagtatagpo ang lupa at dagat.
original_explanation: This is where the land says 'Hi!' to the sea. It's the ultimate chill spot – your go-to for beach trips, sunset viewing, and contemplating life choices while getting sand in your shoes. Also known as the default location for pre-nup shoots.
usage_notes: More poetic or formal than 'beach' or 'baybayin' in some contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatira sila sa isang maliit na bahay sa **tabindagat**.","translation":"They live in a small house on the **seashore**."},{"sentence":"Naglakad-lakad kami sa **tabindagat** habang papalubog ang araw.","translation":"We walked along the **coast** as the sun was setting."}]

translation: to have someone go first; to prioritize; to give an advance (payment)
meaning_filipino: Pahintulutan o iutos na mauna ang isang tao o bagay; bigyang-priyoridad. Maaari ring tumukoy sa pagbibigay ng paunang bayad.
original_explanation: When you're in a long queue at the bank and you see an elderly person, you tell the guard, "Ipauna na po natin si lola." It's the Pinoy courtesy move. It can also mean to give a down payment, like "ipauna ang bayad."
usage_notes: Has a dual meaning: letting someone/something be first, or giving a portion of a payment in advance (down payment).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil may emergency siya, minabuti kong **ipauna** siya sa pila.","translation":"Because she had an emergency, I decided to **let her go first** in the line."},{"sentence":"Puwede bang **ipauna** muna ang kalahati ng bayad?","translation":"Can I **give half of the payment as an advance**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang makatanaw o mapagmasdan gamit ang mga mata. Ang pagiging hayag o lantad.
original_explanation: The root word for all things 'seeing'. It's the 'seen-zone' in messenger. It's the 'makita' in 'Sana makita mo ang halaga ko.' It's the 'nakita' in 'Nakita ko resibo mo sa 11.11 sale!'. It's the fundamental action of perception, whether you wanted to see it or not.
usage_notes: As a root word, it's rarely used alone. It's the base for verbs like 'makita' (to be able to see), 'nakita' (saw), 'ipakita' (to show). The pronunciation is the same as the noun 'kita' (income).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakita** mo ba ang aking mga susi?","translation":"Did you **see** my keys?"},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka para hindi **makita** ng boss na natutulog ka.","translation":"Be careful so the boss won't **see** that you are sleeping."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang luma at pampanitikang katawagan para sa kuryente o daloy ng elektrisidad.
original_explanation: Before Meralco and "kuryente" became the norm, this was the high-tech word. Think of it as the 'steam-punk' version of electricity. You won't use this to complain about a brownout, but you might see it in a Rizal-era novel or a modern "makata's" poem. It's the OG 'spark'.
usage_notes: Highly literary and archaic. 'Kuryente' is the everyday word. 'Dagitab' is more common than 'dagitabin' and refers to a spark or electricity in a more general, poetic sense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kapangyarihan ng **dagitabin** ay isa sa mga pinakadakilang tuklas ng sangkatauhan.","translation":"The power of **electricity** is one of mankind's greatest discoveries."},{"sentence":"Sa mga lumang aklat, tinatawag na **dagitabin** ang kuryente.","translation":"In old books, electricity is called **dagitabin**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagsasampa ng apela sa isang mas mataas na hukuman. Maaari din itong tumukoy sa isang pangalan, titulo, o katawagan.
original_explanation: The formal term for "apela." It’s what lawyers say to sound smart. It also has a lesser-known meaning: a fancy name or title, like how "The Queen City of the South" is an apelasyon for Cebu.
usage_notes: Mas pormal at teknikal kaysa sa salitang 'apela'. Ang pangalawang kahulugan (appellation) ay bihirang gamitin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang karapatan sa **apelasyon** ay mahalaga sa sistema ng hustisya.","translation":"The right to **appeal** is important in the justice system."},{"sentence":"\"Maharlika\" ang dating **apelasyon** na gustong ipangalan sa Pilipinas.","translation":"\"Maharlika\" was the former **appellation** that was proposed as a name for the Philippines."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa hayop, halaman, o bagay na hindi alaga, hindi inaalagaan, o wala sa tamang lugar; naliligaw.
original_explanation: Yung pusa na bigla na lang sumulpot sa gate niyo at humihingi ng pagkain? That's a 'pusang ligaw'. Yung bala na tumama sa hindi dapat tamaan? 'Ligaw na bala'. Yung thoughts mo kapag 3 AM na at di ka pa makatulog? 'Ligaw na diwa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May isang pusang **ligaw** na laging natutulog sa aming garahe.","translation":"There is a **stray** cat that always sleeps in our garage."},{"sentence":"Maraming halamang **ligaw** ang tumutubo sa bakanteng lote.","translation":"Many **wild** plants grow in the vacant lot."}]

meaning_filipino: Itiklop ang isang bagay tulad ng damit, papel, o kumot upang maging mas maliit o mas maayos tingnan.
original_explanation: The ultimate chore your nanay pesters you about. It's the art of turning a mountain of freshly-washed laundry into neat, stackable squares. Fail to do this, and your room will look like a ukay-ukay bin. Also applies to folding paper for your resignation letter.
usage_notes: A very common household term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **magtupi** ng mga damit.","translation":"Help me **fold** the clothes."},{"sentence":"Marunong ka bang **magtupi** ng paper crane?","translation":"Do you know how to **fold** a paper crane?"}]

translation: to be able to distribute; to be able to share
meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang maibahagi, maikalat, o maipamigay ang isang bagay sa maraming tao.
etymology: ma- (ability) + ipamahagi (to distribute, from 'pamahagi' which is 'pa-' + 'bahagi')
original_explanation: The spirit of 'ayuda' and community pantries in one word. It's about sharing what you have, whether it's relief goods, 'pasalubong' from your province, or even just 'chismis'. "Sana **maipamahagi** nang tama ang mga donasyon." It's the opposite of being 'madamot'.
usage_notes: Implies distribution to a group rather than just giving to one person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Layunin ng programa na **maipamahagi** ang mga aklat sa mga pampublikong paaralan.","translation":"The program's goal is **to be able to distribute** the books to public schools."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **maipamahagi** ang pagkain bago ito masira.","translation":"We need **to be able to share** the food before it spoils."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan o aparato na sumusukat at nagpapakita ng oras; orasan.
original_explanation: The old-school term for 'orasan.' Ito 'yung malaking wall clock sa bahay ng lola mo na kailangan pang susian para umandar, o 'yung grandfather clock sa mga horror movies na biglang tumutunog ng hatinggabi. It's the OG time-teller before smartwatches and phone screens.
usage_notes: 'Orasan' is much more common today. 'Urasan' has a more classic, sometimes regional, feel.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumingin siya sa lumang **urasan** na nakasabit sa pader.","translation":"He looked at the old **clock** hanging on the wall."},{"sentence":"Hatinggabi na ayon sa aming **urasan**.","translation":"It's already midnight according to our **timepiece**."}]

meaning_filipino: Bumagsak nang paunti-unti o tig-isa-isa, tulad ng likido, butil, o luha.
original_explanation: This is the 'plip-plop' verb. It's the sound of a leaky faucet that keeps you up at night, the first few drops of rain that make you rush to get the laundry inside, or when your tears start to fall during a sad movie. It's the start of something, whether it's a downpour or a 'hugot' moment.
usage_notes: The base verb for rain, leaks, or any falling liquid. The phrase 'pumatak nang malakas' means 'to pour' or 'to rain heavily.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **pumatak** ang ulan kaya sinara ko agad ang mga bintana.","translation":"The rain started **to fall**, so I immediately closed the windows."},{"sentence":"**Pumatak** ang luha sa kanyang mga mata nang marinig ang balita.","translation":"A tear **fell** from her eyes when she heard the news."}]

meaning_filipino: Dalawang bagay, tao, o salita na pinagsama upang bumuo ng isang yunit. Sa gramatika, ito ay salitang nabuo sa pagsasama ng dalawang magkaibang salita.
original_explanation: The official term for a 'love team' or 'ship' (KathNiel, JaDine). It's any two things that work as a pair, like kape at pandesal, or a BPO agent and their headset. In grammar, it's a compound word like 'bahaghari' (bahag + hari).
usage_notes: May kahulugang pang-gramatika (tambalang salita) at pangkalahatang kahulugan (pares/tandem).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **tambalan** nina Kathryn at Daniel ay sikat na sikat sa Pilipinas.","translation":"The **tandem** of Kathryn and Daniel is very famous in the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Ang 'bahay-kubo' ay isang halimbawa ng salitang **tambalan**.","translation":"'Bahay-kubo' is an example of a **compound** word."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang patungan o mesang may hilig na ibabaw, karaniwang ginagamit upang pagpatungan ng libro, tala, o musika habang nagbabasa, nagsasalita, o tumutugtog.
original_explanation: That tilted stand where the priest puts his big book during mass, or where the CEO puts his notes during the town hall meeting. It’s also what musicians use to hold their sheet music so they don't look like they're scrambling for papers. It's the official furniture of 'I have something important to say/play.'
usage_notes: Often seen in churches, schools, and concert halls.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inilagay ng pari ang bibliya sa **atril**.","translation":"The priest placed the bible on the **lectern**."},{"sentence":"Nakalimutan ng musikero ang kanyang **atril** para sa piyesa.","translation":"The musician forgot his **music stand** for the piece."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga kondisyon na nakakaapekto sa kalusugan, lalo na sa kalinisan at pag-iwas sa sakit; malinis.
original_explanation: Your mom's standard for everything. Is that spoon sanitary? Did you wash your hands? Is the CR sanitary? It's the opposite of 'dugyot.' The goal of every food stall trying to get a permit and every person using a public toilet.
usage_notes: A formal, somewhat technical term. 'Malinis' is more common in everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat laging **sanitaryo** ang paghahanda ng pagkain upang maiwasan ang sakit.","translation":"Food preparation must always be **sanitary** to prevent illness."},{"sentence":"Siniguro ng health inspector na **sanitaryo** ang mga kagamitan sa karinderya.","translation":"The health inspector ensured that the equipment in the eatery was **sanitary**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tuwid na linya na dumaraan sa gitna ng isang bilog o esfera, na nag-uugnay sa dalawang punto sa gilid nito.
original_explanation: Naalala mo yung math class nung high school? Ito 'yun. Yung linya na humahati sa pizza mo nang sakto sa gitna. Kung 'yung ex mo ay radius (halfway there), ang 'the one' ay ang diametro (completes the circle). Hugot math!
usage_notes: Isang terminong teknikal na ginagamit sa matematika, inhinyeriya, at iba pang agham.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sukatin mo ang **diametro** ng bilog gamit ang ruler.","translation":"Measure the **diameter** of the circle using a ruler."},{"sentence":"Ang **diametro** ng gulong ay dalawampung pulgada.","translation":"The **diameter** of the wheel is twenty inches."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kilos o galaw na bastos, walang pinong pag-iingat, at hindi kaaya-aya sa paningin.
etymology: ma- (prefix indicating quality) + gaslaw (crudeness of movement)
original_explanation: Describes someone who moves like a bull in a china shop. 'Yung kaibigan mong kumakain na parang wala nang bukas, o sumasayaw na parang sinasapian. It's not about being bad, just... lacking finesse. Think less ballerina, more 'siga' sa kanto.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to physical actions and movements, not necessarily speech (though it can be related). Differentiated from 'magaspang' which is more about texture or general coarseness of character.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinuturing na **magaslaw** ang pagtawa nang malakas habang nakabukaka.","translation":"Laughing loudly while sitting with legs wide apart is considered **crude**."},{"sentence":"Pinagsabihan siya dahil sa kanyang **magaslaw** na pagkilos sa hapag-kainan.","translation":"He was reprimanded for his **unrefined** actions at the dinner table."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng pagnanais o paghahangad para sa isang bagay, tao, o gawain.
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino decision-maker. "Gusto ko 'to," is the start of every impulsive Shopee checkout and extra rice order. It's the opposite of "bahala na." When you know what you want, you say "gusto ko." When you're still figuring out your feelings for someone, you might just be at the "gusto kita" stage before leveling up to "mahal kita."
usage_notes: Acts as a pseudo-verb. Often used with pronouns like "ko/mo/niya" to indicate the person wanting something (e.g., "Gusto ko ng kape"). The phrase 'gusto pa' means 'to want more' or 'to still want'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Gusto** kong matutong magluto ng adobo.","translation":"I **want** to learn how to cook adobo."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko **gusto** ang maingay na lugar.","translation":"I don't **like** noisy places."},{"sentence":"Pagod na ako, pero **gusto ko pa** mag-aral.","translation":"I'm tired, but I **still want** to study."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa isang mabilis, masigla, at masayang paraan, partikular na ginagamit bilang direksyon sa musika.
original_explanation: The musical term for when the tempo is 'go-go-go!' It's the speed of your heartbeat when you see your crush, or the energy of a fiesta parade. If your life had a soundtrack, the 'alegro' parts would be the fun, upbeat montages.
usage_notes: Mostly used in a musical context to indicate tempo. Can be used metaphorically to describe a lively mood or pace.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ikalawang bahagi ng piyesa ay dapat tugtugin nang **alegro**.","translation":"The second part of the piece should be played **allegro** (in a lively manner)."},{"sentence":"Isang **alegro** na himig ang kanilang sinayawan sa plasa.","translation":"They danced to a **lively** tune in the plaza."}]

translation: to meditate; to reflect; to ponder
meaning_filipino: Ang malalim na pag-iisip o pagninilay-nilay tungkol sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you're staring at the ceiling at 3 AM, thinking about your life choices, your ex, or why onions are so expensive. It's the more poetic version of "overthinking."
usage_notes: Often used in a spiritual, philosophical, or deeply personal context. Synonymous with "magbulay-bulay".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumunta siya sa tabing-dagat upang **magbulay**.","translation":"He went to the seaside to **meditate**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magbulay** sa mga nagawa nating pagkakamali.","translation":"We need to **reflect** on the mistakes we've made."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang propesyonal na sinanay sa pagbibigay ng terapiya o panggagamot, lalo na para sa mga isyung pangkalusugang pangkaisipan o pisikal.
original_explanation: The professional you pay to listen to your drama, unlike your friends who listen for free (but also judge you). A therapist helps you unpack your baggage—not the one from your vacation, but the emotional one you've been carrying since childhood. #MentalHealthMatters
usage_notes: Ang salitang "therapist" mula sa Ingles ay mas karaniwang ginagamit sa mga usapang kolokyal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpatingin siya sa isang **terapeuta** upang matulungan siya sa kanyang anxiety.","translation":"She saw a **therapist** to help her with her anxiety."},{"sentence":"Ang physical **terapeuta** ay tumutulong sa mga pasyenteng makabawi mula sa pinsala.","translation":"The physical **therapist** helps patients recover from injury."}]

translation: to gain an advantage; to lead
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng kalamangan o pag-una sa isang kumpetisyon, bilang, o kalagayan.
original_explanation: That feeling in a group project when you do 90% of the work, tapos 'yung ka-grupo mo 'yung nag-present. Sila 'yung gustong lumamang. Or in basketball, when your team finally gets a 2-point lead.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of competition, sports, business, or any situation involving comparison.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa huling minuto ng laro, sinikap ng koponan na **lumamang**.","translation":"In the final minute of the game, the team tried **to gain a lead**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng manggagawa o kawani na nagtatrabaho sa isang kumpanya, opisina, o para sa isang indibidwal kapalit ng sahod.
original_explanation: The female counterpart of 'empleyado'. She's the one you see rushing to beat the morning bundy clock, juggling deadlines in the BPO industry, or managing the sales floor at the mall. She's a working girl, a professional, the one who pays the bills.
usage_notes: Strictly refers to a female. The gender-neutral term is 'manggagawa' or 'kawani'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **empleada** sa pabrika ang nag-welga.","translation":"Many **female employees** in the factory went on strike."},{"sentence":"Siya ay isang masipag na **empleada** ng gobyerno.","translation":"She is a hardworking government **employee**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangunahin at pinakasolemneng Misa na idinaraos sa isang parokya sa mga araw ng Linggo o mahahalagang kapistahan, kadalasang pinamumunuan ng kura paroko.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'misa mayor' ('pangunahing misa').
original_explanation: This is the "main event" Mass on a Sunday or a fiesta. It's the primetime slot, usually around 9 or 10 AM, with the best choir, the longest sermon, and the biggest crowd. If the Masses were a concert, this is the one with the headline act.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa pangunahing Misa ng araw sa isang partikular na simbahan, lalo na sa mga malalaking okasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ang simbahan tuwing **Misa Mayor** sa araw ng Linggo.","translation":"The church is full during the **High Mass** on Sundays."},{"sentence":"Ang obispo ang magdiriwang ng **Misa Mayor** para sa anibersaryo ng diyosesis.","translation":"The bishop will celebrate the **High Mass** for the diocese's anniversary."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mataas na entablado o plataporma kung saan nakatayo ang isang tagapagsalita, hukom, o mga opisyal upang manood o magtalumpati sa harap ng madla.
original_explanation: Ito yung VIP section bago pa nauso ang "VIP section". Sa mga fiesta sa probinsya, dito nakaupo si mayor, si congressman, at si parish priest habang pinapanood ang parade. Sa school, ito yung stage kung saan ka nanginginig habang nagre-report sa harap ng klase. Basically, a place to be seen and heard, whether you like it or not.
usage_notes: Madalas marinig sa mga pormal na kaganapan, politika, at sa mga mas lumang gusali o istruktura.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga opisyal ng gobyerno ay nasa **tribuna** habang nanonood ng parada.","translation":"The government officials were in the **grandstand** while watching the parade."},{"sentence":"Mula sa **tribuna**, nagbigay ng makapangyarihang talumpati ang pangulo.","translation":"From the **rostrum**, the president delivered a powerful speech."}]

translation: to set aside; to allocate; to designate
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalaan o pagbubukod ng isang bagay para sa isang partikular na tao, layunin, o gamit.
original_explanation: This is what you do with your sweldo. You 'itaan' a portion for bills, for ipon (savings), for your parents, and of course, for your milk tea addiction. It's the adulting verb for budgeting. 'Itaan mo na 'yang huling piraso ng pizza para kay bunso.' It's an act of reserving something, whether it's money, food, or time. It's the opposite of 'bahala na si Batman.'
usage_notes: Similar to 'ilaan'. 'Itaan' often feels more concrete, like setting aside a physical object or a specific amount.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **itaan** ang sapat na pondo para sa iyong pagreretiro.","translation":"You need to **allocate** enough funds for your retirement."},{"sentence":"**Itaan** mo ang upuang iyan para sa ating bisita.","translation":"**Set aside** that seat for our guest."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pansit na may makapal na sarsang kulay-kahel na gawa sa hipon, at nilalagyan ng iba't ibang sahog tulad ng tinapa, chicharon, itlog, at bawang.
etymology: Possibly from a Chinese Hokkien dialect, related to adding flavor or garnish.
original_explanation: The noodle dish that looks like a party on a plate. It's got that bright orange sauce, topped with everything but the kitchen sink: crushed chicharon, shrimp, hard-boiled egg, smoked fish flakes... It's the "extra" cousin in the pansit family. Not to be confused with its simpler relative, Pansit Luglog.
usage_notes: A popular dish for celebrations like birthdays and fiestas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-order ako ng isang bilao ng **palabok** para sa handaan.","translation":"I ordered a large tray of **palabok** for the party."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sangay ng medisina na tumutukoy sa pag-aaral, diyagnosis, at paggamot sa mga sakit at karamdaman ng mata.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "oftalmología", na hango sa Griyegong "ophthalmos" (mata) + "logia" (pag-aaral).
original_explanation: Ito yung specialization ng doktor na tinitingnan ang 'windows to your soul.' Sila ang bahala sa lahat ng problema sa mata, mula sa paglabo dahil sa kaka-scroll sa TikTok hanggang sa mga seryosong kondisyon. Basically, ang science ng pag-aalaga sa ating mga chismis-detectors.
usage_notes: Isang teknikal at akademikong termino. Ang karaniwang tao ay mas malamang na gumamit ng "doktor sa mata".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-aaral siya ng **optalmolohia** upang maging isang espesyalista sa mata.","translation":"She is studying **ophthalmology** to become an eye specialist."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paghahanda o pagsasanay para sa isang pagtatanghal, presentasyon, o anumang gawain na nangangailangan ng pag-eensayo.
etymology: From Spanish 'ensayo'. The 'i' spelling is a phonetic adaptation in Tagalog.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung ginagawa niyo bago ang mismong performance. 'Yung kahit sa insayo pa lang, todo bigay ka na, pang-grand finals na ang energy, pero pagdating ng actual, biglang kinabahan. Relate? It's the 'practice makes perfect' stage, pero minsan 'practice makes nervous' din.
usage_notes: The spelling 'ensayo' is more common and formal. 'Insayo' is a widely used colloquial or phonetic spelling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumunta ka sa **insayo** ng banda mamayang hapon.","translation":"Go to the band **rehearsal** later this afternoon."},{"sentence":"Kailangan pa ng maraming **insayo** para maging perpekto ang aming sayaw.","translation":"We still need a lot of **practice** to perfect our dance."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, karaniwang gawa sa bakal o asero, na may kakayahang humila ng ibang mga bagay na metal dahil sa puwersa ng magnetismo.
original_explanation: That thing on your ref holding up your Meralco bill, a takeout menu, and a photo from your Boracay trip in 2012. Also used to describe someone with an irresistible personality, a "chick/dude magnet." It's the physical embodiment of "attraction," whether it's for paper clips or potential baes.
usage_notes: A direct loanword from English.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginagamit niya ang **magnet** para pulutin ang mga nahulog na karayom.","translation":"She uses the **magnet** to pick up the fallen needles."},{"sentence":"Puno na ng ref **magnet** mula sa iba't ibang bansa ang palamigan nila.","translation":"Their refrigerator is full of ref **magnets** from different countries."}]

translation: to stir with a finger; to meddle
meaning_filipino: Halukayin o paglaruan ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay likido o pagkain, gamit ang daliri. Sa matalinhagang paraan, ito ay nangangahulugang manghimasok o makialam.
original_explanation: Literally, it's stirring your coffee with your finger because you're too lazy to get a spoon. Figuratively, it's what your 'marites' na kapitbahay does: sticking their nose into your business, stirring up trouble where there was none. So, don't 'kalikawin' the sleeping dog, or your friend's relationship drama.
usage_notes: Has both a literal (stirring with a finger) and a very common figurative (meddling) meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **kalikawin** ang asukal sa kape, gamitin mo ang kutsarita.","translation":"Don't **stir** the sugar in the coffee with your finger, use the teaspoon."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **kalikawin** ang mga bagay na hindi niya dapat pinakikialaman.","translation":"He likes to **meddle** in things that are not his business."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang instrumentong perkusyon na gawa sa metal, karaniwang patag at pabilog, na pinapatunog sa pamamagitan ng pagpalo ng isang malyete.
original_explanation: That big, shiny, circular thing you see in old kung fu movies and traditional Filipino dances. You hit it, it makes a loud 'GONGGGG' sound. In modern times, it's what you wish you could hit to end a boring meeting.
usage_notes: A common musical instrument in many Southeast Asian cultures, including indigenous Filipino music.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinatunog nang malakas ang **gong** upang simulan ang seremonya.","translation":"The **gong** was struck loudly to begin the ceremony."},{"sentence":"Ang tunog ng **gong** ay bahagi ng katutubong musika ng Cordillera.","translation":"The sound of the **gong** is part of the indigenous music of the Cordillera."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kilos sa hinaharap na tumutukoy sa pagtungo o paglipat sa isang partikular na lugar o destinasyon.
original_explanation: The official word for "G na!" (Game na!). This is your status when your barkada texts "Asan na u?" and you're still in the shower. It's the promise of arrival, the hopeful beginning of any lakad.
usage_notes: Future tense of 'punta'. The most common way to express the future action of going somewhere.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pupunta** kami sa mall mamayang hapon.","translation":"We **will go** to the mall this afternoon."},{"sentence":"Saan ka **pupunta** pagkatapos nito?","translation":"Where **are you going** after this?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang anyong tubig na napapaligiran ng lupa; lawa.
etymology: From Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *danaw, meaning 'lake'. It is a cognate in many Philippine and Austronesian languages (e.g., Ilocano 'danaw', Maranao 'ranaw').
original_explanation: It's a body of water, bigger than a puddle, smaller than the ocean. Think Taal Lake, Laguna de Bay, or that small pond in your lola's province. It's a slightly more poetic or archaic term for 'lawa' (lake). "Ang ganda ng tanawin sa tabi ng **danaw** sa pagsikat ng araw." Sounds like a great place for some deep thoughts or a pre-nup photoshoot.
usage_notes: 'Lawa' is more common in everyday Tagalog speech. 'Danaw' is still widely understood and used, often in more formal, literary, or geographical contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming isda ang nahuhuli sa **danaw** na iyon.","translation":"A lot of fish are caught in that **lake**."},{"sentence":"Payapa ang paligid ng maliit na **danaw** sa gitna ng gubat.","translation":"The surroundings of the small **pond** in the middle of the forest are peaceful."}]

translation: to charm, to fascinate, to enchant
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-akit o paghalina sa isang tao sa pamamagitan ng angking ganda, talino, o pambihirang katangian.
original_explanation: Think of your K-Pop bias. They don't just sing and dance; they 'mambighani'. They have this magical ability to make you spend all your 'ipon' on merch and concert tickets. It's a level up from just being 'attractive'; it's enchanting.
usage_notes: A more poetic and intense word than 'umakit' (to attract). It implies a deeper, almost magical level of captivation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Layunin ng mananayaw na **mambighani** sa kanyang pag-indak.","translation":"The dancer's goal is **to enchant** with her movements."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang kanyang talino upang **mambighani** sa mga hurado.","translation":"She used her intelligence **to fascinate** the judges."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mataas na opisyal ng Simbahang Katoliko, pangalawa lamang sa Santo Papa, na bumubuo sa Kolehiyo ng mga Kardinal.
original_explanation: In the Catholic Church's org chart, they're the C-suite executives reporting directly to the CEO (the Pope). They wear red, which signifies they're willing to die for their faith. They're also the ones who huddle up and vote for the next Pope, like a holy version of "Pinoy Big Brother: Vatican Edition".
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa isang ranggo sa herarkiya ng Simbahang Katoliko.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinirang ng Santo Papa ang bagong **kardenal** mula sa Pilipinas.","translation":"The Pope appointed a new **cardinal** from the Philippines."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang kilos ng pagbibigay-pugay o pagpapahayag ng magandang hangarin sa isang tao.
original_explanation: What you do when you see a neighbor and you give them the ol' eyebrow-raise-and-nod combo. Or when a TV host reads birthday messages on air. It's the act of greeting someone. 'Bumabati po ako sa lahat ng mga nanonood sa Tondo!'
usage_notes: The root 'bati' can mean 'to greet' or 'to mix/beat' (like eggs). Context makes the meaning clear. The other form would be 'binabati' (is being greeted).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Palaging **bumabati** ang bata sa mga nakatatanda sa kanya.","translation":"The child always **greets** his elders."},{"sentence":"**Bumabati** ako ng 'Maligayang Kaarawan' sa aking ina.","translation":"I **am greeting** my mother a 'Happy Birthday'."}]

meaning_filipino: Sistematikong pag-aaral ng estruktura at kilos ng pisikal at natural na mundo sa pamamagitan ng obserbasyon at eksperimento.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung subject sa school na nagpapasakit ng ulo mo dahil sa experiments, formulas, at memorization ng mga parte ng katawan ng palaka. Pero ito rin 'yung dahilan kung bakit may WiFi ka, bakit gumagana ang cellphone mo, at bakit may gamot sa sakit mo. Science is life, bes!
usage_notes: A broad term covering all scientific disciplines. 'Siyensiya', from Spanish 'ciencia', is a common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **agham** sa pag-unlad ng isang bansa.","translation":"**Science** is important for a country's progress."},{"sentence":"Paborito niyang asignatura ang **agham**.","translation":"His favorite subject is **science**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na may masamang pag-uugali, malupit, o mapaglaro sa masamang paraan.
original_explanation: This is what your Tita calls you when you take the last piece of leche flan. It can range from playfully naughty ("Salbahe ka, inubos mo 'yung ulam!") to genuinely mean or cruel. It's the go-to word for villains in teleseryes and kids who won't behave.
usage_notes: The severity depends heavily on context and tone of voice.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **salbahe** sa iyong mga kalaro.","translation":"Don't be **naughty** to your playmates."},{"sentence":"Ang **salbahe** ng kontrabida sa pelikula, lahat na lang sinaktan!","translation":"The villain in the movie is so **cruel**, he hurt everyone!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagtatatag ng isang kordon sa isang lugar upang ito ay mapalibutan at maihiwalay.
original_explanation: This is the action verb for 'kordon'. When authorities **kordunan** an area, they're basically saying, 'Okay, stop right there! No gossips allowed.' This is done to secure a place, for example, if there's an accident or a VIP is passing through.
usage_notes: This is the verb form indicating the action of creating a cordon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan ang mga sundalo na **kordunan** ang buong kampo.","translation":"The soldiers were ordered to **cordon off** the entire camp."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **kordunan** ang lugar kung saan natagpuan ang ebidensya.","translation":"We need to **cordon off** the area where the evidence was found."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong nakatamo ng pormal na edukasyon o nagpapakita ng mabuting asal na inaasahan sa isang naturuan.
original_explanation: This isn't just about having a diploma. It's about acting like it. When your tita says, 'Mag-behave ka, para kang walang pinag-aralan,' she's not questioning your grades, she's questioning your 'home training.' It means you know how to use 'po' and 'opo' and don't put your feet up on the monobloc chair at the reunion.
usage_notes: Carries a dual meaning of both academic education and good breeding/manners. The context determines the primary meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kitang-kita sa kanyang kilos na siya ay isang taong **may-pinag-aralan**.","translation":"It's very evident in his actions that he is an **educated/well-mannered** person."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang prosesong kemikal kung saan ang isang sangkap ay nagsasama sa oxygen, na karaniwang nagreresulta sa pagbabago tulad ng pagkakalawang ng bakal o pangingitim ng prutas.
original_explanation: What happens when you leave a half-eaten apple on your desk and it turns brown. It's also the reason why your yero roof gets rusty (kalawang) after a few rainy seasons. Basically, it's chemistry's way of saying "use it or lose it." For beauty gurus, it's why your foundation turns orange after a few hours of wear.
usage_notes: A technical, scientific term. 'Pagkakalawang' is the common term for the oxidation of metals. 'Pangingitim' is used for fruits.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagkakalawang ng bakal ay isang halimbawa ng **oksidasiyon**.","translation":"The rusting of iron is an example of **oxidation**."},{"sentence":"Upang maiwasan ang **oksidasiyon**, pahiran ng lemon juice ang hiniwang mansanas.","translation":"To prevent **oxidation**, rub lemon juice on the sliced apple."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng mga katangian, kilos, o anyo na itinuturing na tipikal o ideyal para sa isang lalaki; napaka-macho.
etymology: Reduplication of 'lalaki' (man) to intensify the meaning.
original_explanation: Describes a guy who's the epitome of "macho." He probably drinks kapeng barako, can fix anything with duct tape, and has a voice deeper than the MRT tunnel. It's the "alpha male" energy, the "tunay na lalaki" vibe you see in old action movies.
usage_notes: Used to describe appearance, behavior, or overall aura. Can sometimes carry connotations of traditional or even toxic masculinity, depending on context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lalaking-lalaki** ang dating ni Fernando Poe Jr. sa kanyang mga pelikula.","translation":"Fernando Poe Jr. had a **very masculine** appeal in his movies."},{"sentence":"May boses siyang **lalaking-lalaki**.","translation":"He has a **very masculine** voice."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang estado ng matinding kalituhan sa pag-iisip, kadalasang sanhi ng mataas na lagnat, sakit, o pagkalason, na may kasamang guni-guni o maling pananaw sa realidad.
etymology: Likely a blend of Tagalog 'dili-dili' (imagination) and Spanish 'delirio' (delirium).
original_explanation: This is when your brain goes full-on abstract art mode, usually because you have a fever of 40°C. You start seeing things that aren't there, talking to the electric fan, or thinking the lizards on the ceiling are plotting against you. It's the brain's version of a system crash and rebooting with weird, corrupted files.
usage_notes: A very specific and somewhat archaic term for a medical or psychological state.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa taas ng lagnat, nagsimula na siyang magkaroon ng **dili-diliryuhan**.","translation":"Because of the high fever, he started to experience **delirium**."},{"sentence":"Sa kanyang **dili-diliryuhan**, nakikita niyang lumilipad ang mga upuan.","translation":"In his **hallucination**, he saw the chairs flying."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang halaga ng salapi na ibinabalik kapag ang ibinayad ay mas malaki kaysa sa presyo ng biniling produkto o serbisyo.
original_explanation: That moment of suspense at the *tindahan* when you give a ₱1000 bill for a piece of candy. The *tindera's* "may barya ka?" is the national anthem of small businesses. The **sukli** is your trophy for surviving the awkward wait. "Keep the change" is a foreign concept; we wait for that last peso.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ate, paki-bilang po ng **sukli** kung tama.","translation":"Miss, please count the **change** to see if it's correct."},{"sentence":"Wala akong baon bukas dahil kinuha mo ang buong **sukli**.","translation":"I don't have any allowance for tomorrow because you took all the **change**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabago ng lasa tungo sa pagiging mapait; o sa metaporikal na kahulugan, ang pagdama ng matinding sama ng loob o hinanakit.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `mag-` (nagiging) at salitang-ugat na `pait` (bitterness).
original_explanation: This is what happens to your ampalaya when you overcook it. It's also what happens to your heart when you see your ex happily in a new relationship. You `magpait`—you become bitter. It's the feeling behind the hugot line, 'Sana naging kape na lang ako, para kahit bitter, may nagkakagusto pa rin.'
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin nang literal para sa panlasa o patalinghaga para sa damdamin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **magpait** ang iyong puso dahil sa mga kabiguan.","translation":"Don't let your heart **become bitter** because of failures."},{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **magpait** ang niluluto niyang gulay nang masunog ito.","translation":"The vegetable dish he was cooking started to **become bitter** when it got burnt."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar sa disyerto na may tubig at mga halaman; isang kaaya-ayang lugar o panahon sa gitna ng isang mahirap o nakakabagot na sitwasyon.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'oasis', mula sa Latin na 'oasis', mula sa Sinaunang Griyego na 'ὄασις' (óasis). Isang direktang hiram na salita.
original_explanation: Literally, that place with water in a desert. Figuratively, it's that one air-conditioned coffee shop you find after walking under the Manila sun for 30 minutes. It's your sweldo day in the middle of a petsa de peligro week. It's that 15-minute break in your 12-hour shift. Your oasis is your personal sanctuary from the chaos.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa parehong literal at metaporikal na kahulugan. Ang bigkas at kahulugan ay kapareho ng sa Ingles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aklatan ay nagsisilbing **oasis** ng kaalaman para sa mga mag-aaral.","translation":"The library serves as an **oasis** of knowledge for the students."},{"sentence":"Nakatagpo sila ng isang **oasis** sa gitna ng malawak na disyerto.","translation":"They found an **oasis** in the middle of the vast desert."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng pagtitiis, kasipagan, at hindi pagsuko sa harap ng paghihirap o pagkabagot upang makamit ang isang layunin.
original_explanation: This is the student na nagpupuyat para sa thesis, the BPO agent na tinitiis ang irate customer with a smile, the parent na pumipila ng pagkahaba-haba para sa ayuda. It's the opposite of "give up na me." To be matiyaga is to have the grit to see things through, kahit gaano pa kahirap o katagal. It's a core Filipino value, right next to "bahala na."
usage_notes: A highly positive trait, often praised in Filipino culture.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil siya ay **matiyaga**, natapos niya ang kanyang pag-aaral.","translation":"Because she was **persevering**, she finished her studies."},{"sentence":"Kailangang maging **matiyaga** sa pag-aalaga ng halaman.","translation":"One needs to be **patient** in taking care of plants."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat o grupo ng mga taludtod sa isang tula; maaari ring tumukoy sa sining o sistema ng pagbuo ng tula, kasama ang sukat at tugma.
etymology: Nagmula sa salitang 'taludtod' na may hulaping '-an', na nagpapahiwatig ng isang koleksyon o sistema.
original_explanation: Kung ang taludtod ay isang linya, ang taludturan ay ang 'paragraph' ng tula. It's a group of lines, also known as a stanza. Pwede ring tumukoy ito sa mismong 'rules of the game' ng paggawa ng tula—'yung sukat at tugma. So it's both the product (stanza) and the process (versification).
usage_notes: Isang terminong teknikal sa panitikan na may dalawang magkaugnay na kahulugan: ang saknong mismo at ang sistema ng pagbuo nito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang unang **taludturan** ng tula ay naglalarawan sa kagandahan ng umaga.","translation":"The first **stanza** of the poem describes the beauty of the morning."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan nila ang tradisyonal na **taludturan** ng mga makatang Pilipino.","translation":"They are studying the traditional **versification** of Filipino poets."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mekanismo na ginagamit upang pabagalin o pahintuin ang paggalaw ng isang sasakyan o makina.
original_explanation: That thing you stomp on when a jeepney suddenly cuts you off in EDSA. Also, a metaphor for telling someone to slow down or calm down. 'Hoy, **preno** ka muna sa gastos!' (Hey, hit the brakes on your spending!). Essential for surviving Manila traffic and impulsive online shopping.
usage_notes: Can be used as a verb metaphorically, 'magpreno' (to brake, to slow down).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Biglang kumapit ang **preno** ng bus kaya nagulat ang mga pasahero.","translation":"The bus's **brakes** suddenly engaged, surprising the passengers."},{"sentence":"Mag-**preno** ka sa pagsasalita, baka may masabi kang hindi maganda.","translation":"Put a **brake** on your talking, you might say something you'll regret."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang damdamin o kilos ng mababang pagtingin, pag-alipusta, o kawalan ng respeto sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: This is the look your mom gives you when you say you're tired after just waking up. It's the feeling behind a 'seen-zone' message. It’s looking down on someone, the ultimate 'you're nothing to me' vibe. It's the opposite of respect, often delivered with a side of epic side-eye.
usage_notes: A strong word indicating deep disrespect or a feeling of superiority over another.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya matanggap ang **paghamak** na ipinakita sa kanya.","translation":"He could not accept the **contempt** shown to him."},{"sentence":"Ang **paghamak** sa mahihirap ay isang masamang ugali.","translation":"Having **scorn** for the poor is a bad trait."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, tao, o sitwasyon na nagdudulot ng inis, pagkainis, o pagkayamot.
original_explanation: That feeling you get when the internet connection drops during a crucial Zoom meeting. O yung paulit-ulit na tanong ng tita mo kung kailan ka mag-aasawa. Anything that makes you go "Ugh, kainis!" is a pangyamot. It's a major source of stress.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa pinagmulan o sanhi ng pagkayamot.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaking **pangyamot** sa biyahe ang matinding trapik.","translation":"The heavy traffic is a major **annoyance** during the commute."},{"sentence":"Ang ingay ng kapitbahay ay isang **pangyamot** tuwing gabi.","translation":"The neighbor's noise is an **irritant** every night."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalapat ng masahe sa isang tao o bahagi ng katawan; ang pagiging tuon ng serbisyong masahe.
original_explanation: This is you when you're the chosen one. 'Sino ang masahihin?' (Who's getting the massage?). It's the object-focus verb. You are the 'masahihin' when your SO finally agrees to give you that back rub you've been asking for all night. You are the target, the recipient of the glorious hilot.
usage_notes: Object-focus verb. The person or body part being massaged is the grammatical subject. Not to be confused with 'masahin' (to knead).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang likod ng pasyente ang **masahihin** ng terapista.","translation":"The patient's back is the one **to be massaged** by the therapist."},{"sentence":"**Masahihin** mo nga ang balikat ko, pagod na pagod ako.","translation":"Please **massage** my shoulders, I'm so tired."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na matangkad at payat nang hindi karaniwan; patpatin.
etymology: Unknown, possibly a regional or colloquial term.
original_explanation: Your friend who's all arms and legs, the one who looks like a human selfie stick. They're not just 'matangkad', they're 'tilandog'—so tall and thin they might get tangled up in a strong wind. Often said with a mix of awe and lighthearted teasing.
usage_notes: A very informal and somewhat rare word to describe a person's lanky build. Can be considered comical or slightly teasing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **tilandog** na basketbolistang iyon ay madaling maka-shoot.","translation":"That **lanky** basketball player can shoot easily."}]

meaning_filipino: Magsusuot ng sapatos na may mataas na takong.
original_explanation: The ultimate act of 'tiis-ganda' (suffering for beauty). You **magtakong** for the OOTD and the glam, even if it feels like your feet are auditioning for a horror movie by the end of the night. It's a choice you make for fashion, and a choice you regret after three hours of standing.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to wearing high-heeled shoes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinili niyang huwag na lang **magtakong** dahil alam niyang marami silang lalakarin.","translation":"She chose not to **wear high heels** because she knew they would be walking a lot."}]

translation: to go on a date; to have an appointment/rendezvous
meaning_filipino: Ang pakikipagkita sa isang tao sa isang takdang oras at lugar, na kadalasan ay may romantikong konotasyon.
etymology: From makipag- (social verb prefix) + tipan (agreement, covenant, date).
original_explanation: The old-school, more formal way of saying 'to go on a date.' It sounds more romantic and less casual than just 'mag-date.' It evokes images of harana and writing love letters. It can also mean a secret meeting or rendezvous, like what spies or lovers in a telenovela do.
usage_notes: Has a more formal, sometimes romantic, and slightly archaic feel compared to the modern loanword 'mag-date.' Can also be used for a secret or important meeting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Noong unang panahon, sa plasa madalas **makipagtipan** ang mga magkasintahan.","translation":"In the old days, lovers would often **go on a date** at the town plaza."},{"sentence":"May usapan silang **makipagtipan** sa ilalim ng puno ng mangga.","translation":"They had an agreement to **have a rendezvous** under the mango tree."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng matinding kalungkutan, pagdadalamhati, o paghihinagpis, na kadalasang may kasamang pag-iisa o pagmumukmok.
etymology: From `pang-` + `kulughoy` (a very rare root meaning deep sadness).
original_explanation: This is next-level lungkot. Not just 'sad girl autumn' vibes, but full-on telenovela protagonist level of grief where you're staring at the rain, probably with a dramatic slow-motion scene. It's the feeling of being so utterly heartbroken that you just want to curl up and disappear.
usage_notes: This is a deep, literary word. You won't hear this at the palengke. Use it to sound poetic or to describe a profound, almost paralyzing sadness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pangungulughoy** ng biyuda ay ramdam sa bawat sulok ng bahay.","translation":"The widow's **extreme grief** was felt in every corner of the house."},{"sentence":"Itigil mo na ang iyong **pangungulughoy** at harapin ang bukas.","translation":"Stop your **wallowing in sorrow** and face tomorrow."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maikling pagsubok na pagganap ng isang aktor, mang-aawit, o mananayaw upang matukoy ang kanilang kaangkupan para sa isang papel o palabas.
original_explanation: From Pinoy Big Brother to The Voice, this is the first step to stardom (or a viral meme). It's that nerve-wracking moment you perform in front of judges, hoping they don't say "Thank you, next!" It's a job interview, but with more drama and sometimes, forced crying for a backstory.
usage_notes: A loanword that has been fully integrated into Filipino and is the standard term used in the entertainment industry.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumila siya nang maaga para sa **awdisyon** ng bagong teleserye.","translation":"She lined up early for the **audition** of the new TV series."},{"sentence":"Kahit kinakabahan, ibinigay niya ang lahat sa kanyang **awdisyon** sa pagkanta.","translation":"Even though she was nervous, she gave her all in her singing **audition**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tinanggal o inalis sa trabaho o tungkulin, lalo na dahil sa pagbabawas ng empleyado o pagkalugi ng kumpanya.
etymology: From Spanish 'cesante' (one who is dismissed from a job).
original_explanation: The formal, almost old-school term for 'na-endo' or 'tinanggal sa work.' It's what happens when the company is 'rightsizing' (a fancy word for firing people). It’s the dreaded status update no one wants to post. The opposite of getting promoted.
usage_notes: More formal and less common in everyday conversation than 'tinanggal' or 'natanggal'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming manggagawa ang naging **sesante** nang magsara ang pabrika.","translation":"Many workers were **laid off** when the factory closed."},{"sentence":"Nag-aalala siyang baka mapabilang sa mga magiging **sesante** sa susunod na buwan.","translation":"He is worried he might be among those who will be **dismissed** next month."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salita o parirala na may kapareho o halos kaparehong kahulugan sa isa pang salita o parirala sa isang wika.
original_explanation: This is the official Filipino term for 'synonym.' It's what your Filipino teacher drilled into your head in elementary school. It's literally 'of the same meaning.' Its mortal enemy in every quiz is 'kasalungat' (antonym).
usage_notes: A very common term in academic, linguistic, and educational contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kasingkahulugan** ng 'maganda' ay 'marikit'.","translation":"The **synonym** of 'beautiful' is 'gorgeous'."},{"sentence":"Magbigay ng limang **kasingkahulugan** ng salitang 'masaya'.","translation":"Give five **synonyms** for the word 'happy'."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-usad pasulong o pagpunta sa unahan. Ito ay nasa nakaraang anyo.
original_explanation: This is what you did in the MRT queue when the person in front finally tapped their Beep card. 'Sa wakas, umabante rin!' It means to have moved forward, physically or metaphorically. It's the opposite of 'umatras' (moved back). It's a small victory in the daily commute.
usage_notes: Anyong pangnakaraan ng pandiwang 'umabante'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umabante** ang pila nang bumukas ang isa pang counter.","translation":"The line **advanced** when another counter opened."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng sundalo na binabayaran upang lumaban para sa isang dayuhang hukbo o grupo. Sa malawak na kahulugan, isang taong gumagawa ng isang bagay para lamang sa pera.
original_explanation: The female version of a 'mersenaryo'. She's in it for the money, not the loyalty. Think of a character in a video game or action movie who's the highest bidder's best friend. In a 'hugot' context, it's that friend who only shows up when there's free food or a 'libre'.
usage_notes: The distinction between 'mersenaryo' (male) and 'mersenarya' (female) is maintained from its Spanish origin. The masculine form is often used as a general term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang kilalang **mersenarya** ang kontrabida sa pelikula.","translation":"The villain in the movie is a known female **mercenary**."},{"sentence":"Tinawag siyang **mersenarya** dahil pera lang ang habol niya.","translation":"She was called a **mercenary** because she's only after money."}]

translation: to conceive; to have pregnancy cravings
meaning_filipino: Ang maranasan ang mga unang senyales ng pagbubuntis, kabilang ang mga di-pangkaraniwang paghahangad sa pagkain (cravings) o pag-ayaw sa ilang bagay.
original_explanation: That magical, mysterious, and sometimes weird phase of early pregnancy. It's the reason your wife suddenly wants green mangoes with bagoong at 2 AM, or why she suddenly hates the smell of your pabango. When someone is "naglilihi", you just say "yes" to their cravings. No questions asked. "Hatinggabi na, pero kailangan kong humanap ng santol kasi naglilihi ang asawa ko."
usage_notes: Specifically refers to the conception period and the associated cravings and aversions. There is a folk belief that the baby will resemble the object of the mother's craving.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Noong **naglihi** si nanay sa akin, paborito niya raw kumain ng maasim na mangga.","translation":"When my mom **was conceiving** me, she said her favorite thing to eat was sour mangoes."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong pagtawanan ang mga pinaglilihian niya; sundin mo na lang.","translation":"Don't laugh at her pregnancy cravings; just go with it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isagawa o gawin ang isang partikular na proyekto, gawain, o tungkulin; pag-ukulan ng panahon at pagsisikap.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'procrastination fuel'. 'Sige, trabahuhin ko na 'yan,' you say, before opening TikTok for 'a quick break'. Also what you do to a relationship to 'make it work'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **trabahuhin** ang report na ito para bukas.","translation":"I need **to work on** this report for tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, **trinatrabaho** na namin ang iyong request.","translation":"Don't worry, we are already **working on** your request."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao mula sa nakaraang relasyon, partikular ang isang dating kasintahan, asawa, o katrabaho. Hango sa unlaping Ingles na "ex-".
etymology: From the English prefix 'ex-', meaning 'out of' or 'former', used as a standalone noun.
original_explanation: Ah, the 'ex'. The ghost of relationships past. In the Philippines, this one word carries a whole teleserye's worth of drama, hugot, and 'sana all' flashbacks. It could be an ex-jowa, ex-M.U., ex-boss, or even an ex-friend. The mere mention of 'yung ex ko' can either start a 3-hour kwentuhan or a 3-hour crying session.
usage_notes: Used as a standalone noun in colloquial Filipino, almost always referring to a former romantic partner.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita ko ang **ex** ko sa mall kahapon, may kasama nang iba.","translation":"I saw my **ex** at the mall yesterday, they were already with someone else."},{"sentence":"Move on na, 'wag mo nang isipin ang **ex** mo.","translation":"Move on already, don't think about your **ex** anymore."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang aklat-sanggunian na naglalaman ng mga salita ng isang wika na nakaayos nang paalpabeto, na may kasamang kahulugan, pagbigkas, at iba pang impormasyon.
etymology: From 'pala-' (indicating a system or study) + 'wika' (language) + '-an' (place or collection). It can also refer to linguistics or a collection of proverbs ('palasawikain').
original_explanation: The OG Google search. The book you used to have to lug around in Filipino class to find the meaning of 'malikmata' or 'balintataw'. Now it's an app on your phone, but the purpose is the same: to define words and settle arguments about what they mean.
usage_notes: A formal and somewhat dated term for 'dictionary'. 'Talahuluganan' and the Spanish loanword 'diksiyonaryo' are more common today.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ng guro ang isang makapal na **palawikaan** upang mahanap ang kahulugan ng salita.","translation":"The teacher used a thick **dictionary** to find the meaning of the word."},{"sentence":"Ang pagbuo ng isang komprehensibong **palawikaan** ay isang napakalaking gawain.","translation":"Creating a comprehensive **dictionary** is a monumental task."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian kung saan ang mga binti ay baluktot palabas, na nag-iiwan ng espasyo sa pagitan ng mga tuhod kapag magkadikit ang mga paa.
original_explanation: An old-school word for being bow-legged, or 'sakang'. It's that cowboy-like stance where your knees refuse to meet. You don't hear this word much anymore; people usually just say `sakang`. If you use `pilipot` in a conversation today, your friends might ask if you time-traveled from the Spanish era.
usage_notes: This is a rare and somewhat archaic term. The more common and neutral word is 'sakang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayon sa matatanda, ang batang laging kinakarga ay maaaring maging **pilipot**.","translation":"According to the elders, a child who is always carried might become **bow-legged**."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa pagiging **pilipot**, hirap siyang tumakbo nang mabilis.","translation":"Because of being **bow-legged**, he has difficulty running fast."}]

meaning_filipino: Hayaan o ipahintulot na tratuhin ang isang tao nang may labis na pagmamahal at pagbibigay sa lahat ng gusto, na maaaring magresulta sa pagiging suwail.
original_explanation: This is when a lola sees her apo and declares, 'Hayaan niyo ako!' It's the act of letting someone else (usually a grandparent or tita) spoil the kid rotten. 'Gusto mo ng Jollibee? Gusto mo ng bagong laruan? Sige!' It's basically outsourcing the spoiling.
usage_notes: This is a causative verb. It's different from `layawin` (to spoil someone directly). `Ipalayaw` means to allow or cause someone to be spoiled, often by a third party.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong masyadong **ipalayaw** sa lola niya ang bata, baka lumaking walang disiplina.","translation":"Don't **let his grandmother spoil** the child too much, he might grow up without discipline."},{"sentence":"Dahil nag-i-isang anak, halos **ipinalayaw** na siya sa lahat ng kamag-anak.","translation":"Because he's the only child, he was basically **allowed to be spoiled** by all the relatives."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na gumagawa ng krimen ng pagnanakaw sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng puwersa o pananakot, karaniwan sa pampublikong lugar.
etymology: From English "hold-upper". A pseudo-English word common in Philippine English.
original_explanation: The reason your mom texts you 'Ingat ka, anak' every five minutes. The classic villain in Pinoy action movies, usually shouting 'Akin na ang bag mo!' on a jeepney. Not to be confused with someone who just holds up a sign.
usage_notes: A very common term in Philippine news and daily conversation regarding crime.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahuli ng pulis ang **holdaper** sa bus.","translation":"The police caught the **robber** on the bus."},{"sentence":"'Huwag kang papalag kung ayaw mong masaktan!' sabi ng **holdaper**.","translation":"'Don't resist if you don't want to get hurt!' said the **hold-upper**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang araw bago ang kahapon.
etymology: A contraction of 'ika-makalawa' or related to 'ikalawang araw' (second day) in the past.
original_explanation: The official term for that day you can barely remember what you had for lunch. It's not yesterday (kahapon), not today (ngayon), but the one before that. It's the "ay teka, ano nga bang nangyari nun?" of the calendar.
usage_notes: The corresponding word for 'the day after tomorrow' is 'samakalawa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kamakalawa** pa siya umalis papuntang probinsya.","translation":"He left for the province **the day before yesterday**."},{"sentence":"Natanggap ko ang sulat noong **kamakalawa**.","translation":"I received the letter **the day before yesterday**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang anyong pampanitikan o lumang Tagalog para sa "kayong lahat".
etymology: Likely from older Tagalog or related Philippine languages where 'tanan' means 'all'.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'sana all'. It's a poetic, almost Shakespearean way of saying 'all of you.' You'd probably hear this in a *balagtasan* or a historical drama, not when your friend is asking 'Sino sasama sa Jollibee?' The answer isn't 'Tananan!' unless you want to sound like you just time-traveled from the 1800s.
usage_notes: Primarily used in literature, formal speeches, and historical contexts. It is very rare in modern conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Makinig kayo, **tananan**, sa aking sasabihin.","translation":"Listen, **all of you**, to what I have to say."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-ibig ko'y alay sa inyong **tananan**.","translation":"My love is offered to **all of you**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na nasubukan na, napatunayan ang bisa, o dumaan sa pagsusuri.
original_explanation: Parang yung friendship ninyo na "tested and prubado" na. Dumaan na sa maraming chismis at utangan pero matatag pa rin. O yung paborito mong brand ng suka, kasi prubado na ang asim!
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin kasama ang "na" (hal. prubado na).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Prubado** na ang galing ng sabon na ito sa pagtanggal ng mantsa.","translation":"The effectiveness of this soap in removing stains is already **proven**."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang katapatan ay **prubado** na ng panahon.","translation":"His loyalty has been **tested** by time."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang nakausli o lubog; pantay ang ibabaw.
etymology: Mula sa Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *pataR, na nangangahulugang 'patag, pantay'.
original_explanation: The opposite of your life's problems (which are bumpy and complicated). 'Patag' is that perfectly smooth road you dream of driving on. Or that feeling when your crush's reply is so dry and unenthusiastic, you'd call their personality 'patag'. "Ang patag kausap" = boring.
usage_notes: Maaaring ilarawan ang mga ibabaw (hal., lupa, daan) o gamitin sa matalinghagang paraan para sa isang walang kabuhay-buhay o walang emosyong tono o sitwasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas madaling magbisikleta sa **patag** na daan.","translation":"It's easier to bike on a **flat** road."},{"sentence":"Naghahanap kami ng **patag** na lugar para pagtayuan ng aming tolda.","translation":"We are looking for a **level** spot to pitch our tent."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa katangian ng isang tao na hirap o hindi makagawa ng isang pinal na desisyon; pabago-bago ng isip.
original_explanation: This is your friend who takes 30 minutes to choose a Netflix show, only to fall asleep after 5 minutes. O yung ka-talking stage mo for 6 months na hindi masabi kung gusto ka ba talaga o hindi. It's the state of being a human "loading..." screen when a decision needs to be made. "Ano, aalis ba tayo o hindi?" "Ewan." That's the vibe.
usage_notes: Isang deskriptibong parirala para sa katangian ng isang tao na maging urong-sulong sa pagpapasya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap siyang asahan dahil siya ay taong **walang matibay na pasiya**.","translation":"It's hard to rely on him because he is an **indecisive** person."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang pagiging **walang matibay na pasiya**, nawala ang magandang oportunidad.","translation":"Because of his **irresolute** nature, the great opportunity was lost."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na sapilitan o kailangang-kailangan gawin o sundin ayon sa batas, patakaran, o kaugalian.
original_explanation: This is the 'no-choice' version of 'ubligado'. Think company-mandated team building, wearing the office uniform, or that 'ubligatoryo' selfie with the balikbayan relative you barely know. It's the stuff you have to do, whether you like it or not. The "required" field in the form of life.
usage_notes: Stronger than 'ubligado'. Implies a rule or law is in place.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ubligatoryo** ang pagsuot ng ID sa loob ng paaralan.","translation":"Wearing an ID inside the school is **obligatory**."},{"sentence":"Naging **ubligatoryo** ang pagbabakuna upang makapaglakbay.","translation":"Vaccination became **obligatory** in order to travel."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng mga hayop na kumain ng damo o halaman sa isang pastulan o bukirin.
etymology: A complex nominalization from `pang-` + `-in-` + `kain` (eat), referring to the act of foraging for food.
original_explanation: This is what cows, carabaos, and goats do all day. It's their version of an "unli-salad bar" out in the fields. Imagine a chill animal buffet where the main course is grass. It's the OG farm-to-table dining experience.
usage_notes: Used almost exclusively for herbivorous animals eating in a pasture.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malawak ang lugar para sa **panginginain** ng mga baka.","translation":"The area for the cows' **grazing** is wide."},{"sentence":"Maagang dinadala ng pastol ang mga tupa para sa **panginginain**.","translation":"The shepherd brings the sheep early for **pasturing**."}]

translation: to expose to heat; to roast
meaning_filipino: Ilantad sa init ng apoy, baga, o sikat ng araw upang matuyo, maluto, o uminit.
original_explanation: This is the low-and-slow method of heating things up. Think of sun-drying fish ('darangin sa araw') or slowly roasting a pig over embers. It's also used figuratively for when you're being 'roasted' or put on the spot by your friends. 'Bakit ako ang laging dinadarang niyo?!' (Why are you always putting me on the hot seat?!).
usage_notes: Can refer to heat from fire (direct or embers) or the sun. It implies a direct exposure to the heat source.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **darangin** ang isda sa araw para maging daing.","translation":"You need to **expose** the fish to the sun to make dried fish."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong masyadong **darangin** ang kamay mo sa apoy.","translation":"Don't **expose** your hand too much to the fire."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na itinapon na, inalis, o hindi na pinakikinabangan.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'deshecho' (undone, destroyed, waste).
original_explanation: Parang 'yung mga gamit mo na "for decluttering" na napunta sa ukay-ukay o sa basurahan. Or 'yung ex mong "di-netso" mo na sa contacts list mo. Out of sight, out of mind. It's the Marie Kondo "does not spark joy" pile.
usage_notes: Kadalasang ginagamit sa konteksto ng pagtatapon ng basura o mga bagay na hindi na kailangan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lahat ng lumang damit ay **disetso** na para magkaroon ng espasyo sa aparador.","translation":"All the old clothes were **disposed of** to make space in the closet."},{"sentence":"Itinuring niyang **disetso** ang mga sirang kasangkapan.","translation":"He considered the broken furniture as **discarded**."}]

translation: To block; to clog; to obstruct
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpigil o pagharang sa daloy sa isang daanan, gaya ng tubo, kalsada, o ugat. Ang pang-uring anyo ay "barado".
original_explanation: The reason why your sink overflows or why EDSA is a parking lot. 'Bumara' is the verb, 'barado' is the state of being. It can be physical, like hair in the drain, or metaphorical, like a creative block. 'Barado ilong ko' is the national anthem during flu season.
usage_notes: Ang anyong pandiwa ay "bumara" (pokus sa aktor) o "barahan" (pokus sa layon). Ang anyong pang-uri na "barado" ay napakakaraniwan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang magtapon ng basura diyan para hindi **bumara** ang kanal.","translation":"Don't throw trash there so the canal won't **get clogged**."},{"sentence":"May **bumara** sa lababo kaya hindi umaagos ang tubig.","translation":"Something **is blocking** the sink that's why the water isn't draining."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maingat na pag-aaral o pagsusuri sa mga pagpipilian, sitwasyon, o kahihinatnan bago gumawa ng desisyon.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you're stuck between two choices, like 'Mag-resign na ba ako or tiisin ko muna for the 13th-month pay?' It's the mental gymnastics of weighing the pros and cons, trying to find balance. It's adulting in verb form.
usage_notes: The verb is often used to describe a state of careful consideration, not just physical balancing. The noun form is 'paninimbang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **manimbang** nang mabuti bago ka gumawa ng isang malaking desisyon sa buhay.","translation":"You need to **weigh your options** carefully before you make a big life decision."},{"sentence":"Siya ay nasa estado ng paninimbang kung tatanggapin ba ang alok sa ibang bansa. (using the noun form)","translation":"He is in a state of **deliberation** on whether to accept the job offer abroad."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na nangangahulugang kahanga-hanga, nakagugulat sa ganda o galing, o lubos na nakabibighani.
original_explanation: A Tagalized 'knockout.' When someone or something is so impressive, it figuratively knocks you out. 'Yung performance ni Sarah G, grabe, nak-aut!' or 'Nakita mo ba yung bagong jowa ni ano? Nak-aut sa ganda!' It's the highest form of praise from a tita or a friend watching a talent show.
usage_notes: Purely slang. Used in informal, conversational settings. The hyphen is often included in writing to mimic the pronunciation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Grabe ang ganda ng damit mo, pang-party talaga, **nak-aut**!","translation":"Wow, your dress is so beautiful, really for a party, it's **stunning**!"},{"sentence":"**Nak-aut** ang presentation ng kabilang grupo, kailangan nating galingan.","translation":"The other group's presentation was **impressive**, we need to do better."}]

meaning_filipino: Matinding pagnanasang sekswal o sensuwal; pagiging malandi o mapagbigay-motibo sa romantikong paraan.
original_explanation: The old-school word for 'landi'. It's that spark, that flirtatious energy. While 'landi' is more everyday and can be playful, 'biga' sounds more intense, more deliberate, and a bit more scandalous. It’s the vibe your lola warns you about.
usage_notes: Carries a stronger, more serious, and often negative connotation than the modern term 'landi'. Pronounced with stress on the last syllable, distinguishing it from the plant 'biga' (/BI-ga/).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **biga** ang mga tingin niya sa dalaga.","translation":"His glances towards the young woman were full of **lust**."},{"sentence":"Pinagsabihan siya ng kanyang ina na itigil na ang kanyang **biga** at mag-aral nang mabuti.","translation":"Her mother told her to stop her **flirtatiousness** and study well."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng lutuing Pilipino na gawa sa hiniwang baboy at atay, na may sahog na patatas, karot, at pasas, at niluto sa sarsang kamatis.
etymology: From Spanish 'menudo', meaning 'small' or 'tripe stew'. The Filipino version adapted to use pork.
original_explanation: The ultimate handaan-staple. It's the ulam that has everything: baboy, atay, patatas, karot, and the controversial pasas (raisins). It's the reason why may 'Menudo cut' sa palengke. Its presence signals a celebration, or just a really good Tuesday lunch.
usage_notes: While the Spanish origin refers to tripe, Filipino menudo primarily uses pork meat and liver.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong ulam ang **menudo** na luto ni nanay.","translation":"My favorite dish is the **menudo** that my mom cooks."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang lagyan ng pasas ang **menudo**.","translation":"Don't forget to put raisins in the **menudo**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng sasakyan na mas malaki kaysa sa karaniwang kotse, karaniwang ginagamit para sa paghahatid ng mga tao o kargamento.
original_explanation: The official vehicle of family outings, barkada road trips, and the "UV Express" service. It's that magical vehicle that can somehow fit 18 people, 5 maletas, a cooler, and a guitar. Siksikan man, at least sama-sama. The AC better be working though, or else it's a rolling sauna.
usage_notes: Widely used to refer to passenger vans, school buses, and UV Express vehicles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumakay kami ng **van** papuntang Baguio.","translation":"We rode a **van** going to Baguio."},{"sentence":"Puno na ang **van**, sa susunod na biyahe ka na sumakay.","translation":"The **van** is full, you'll have to take the next trip."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa isang tuwid na direksyon o landas nang walang pagliko o paghinto; tuwiran.
original_explanation: When you ask a jeepney driver for directions and he says 'diretso lang,' this is the action. Going straight ahead, no detours, no side trips. Kinda like how you should go home after getting your salary, but we all know that's not what happens.
usage_notes: Commonly used when giving directions or describing a direct course of action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mula rito, **padiretso** ka lang at makikita mo na ang simbahan.","translation":"From here, just go **straight ahead** and you will see the church."},{"sentence":"**Padiretso** siya sa opisina ng boss para magreklamo.","translation":"He went **directly** to the boss's office to complain."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan na may maliliit na butas sa dulo ng tubo nito, ginagamit sa pagdidilig ng mga halaman.
original_explanation: The OG hydration tool for your plantita/plantito journey. Before there were fancy misters, there was the trusty rigadera, looking like a metal elephant trunk that gives your plants a much-needed shower. It's the low-tech, high-satisfaction gadget of every lola's garden.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ni Nanay ang **rigadera** para diligan ang mga rosas sa hardin.","translation":"Mom used the **watering can** to water the roses in the garden."},{"sentence":"Pakiabot nga ng **rigadera**, puno na ito ng tubig.","translation":"Please hand me the **watering can**, it's already full of water."}]

meaning_filipino: Ayon sa, batay sa, o bilang pagsunod sa isang batas, patakaran, utos, o tao.
original_explanation: The formal way of saying "Sabi ni..." or "According to the chismis...". You use this in office memos, legal documents, or when you want to sound smart while telling your friend, "Alinsunod sa S.O.P., bawal mag-Vape dito." Use `sa` for things/rules and `kay` for people.
usage_notes: `Alinsunod sa` is used for non-human antecedents (e.g., laws, rules, announcements). `Alinsunod kay` is used for people's names.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lahat ng desisyon ay ginawa **alinsunod sa** patakaran ng kumpanya.","translation":"All decisions were made **in accordance with** company policy."},{"sentence":"**Alinsunod kay** Dr. Rizal, ang kabataan ang pag-asa ng bayan.","translation":"**According to** Dr. Rizal, the youth is the hope of the nation."}]

translation: to consider, to take into account
meaning_filipino: Ang masusing pag-iisip o pagbibigay-pansin sa isang bagay, ideya, o damdamin ng iba bago gumawa ng desisyon o aksyon.
etymology: From 'isa' (to make one with/put into) and 'alang-alang' (sake, consideration).
original_explanation: This is the corporate email equivalent of 'Think before you click.' It's what your boss tells you when you're about to make a risky move. 'Please **isaalang-alang** the budget.' It’s also what you whisper to yourself when you're about to buy something on Shopee but you remember you have bills to pay. 'Kailangan kong **isaalang-alang** ang aking future.'
usage_notes: A formal and important verb in decision-making contexts. Often translated as 'to consider' but carries a heavier weight of 'for the sake of'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat nating **isaalang-alang** ang kapakanan ng lahat bago magpasya.","translation":"We must **consider** the welfare of everyone before deciding."},{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **isaalang-alang** mo ang aking mungkahi.","translation":"Please, **take into account** my suggestion."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng mataas at magaspang na damo, katulad ng kugon, na ginagamit sa paggawa ng bubong.
original_explanation: Imagine the OG version of a G.I. sheet roof. Before yero, Pinoys used dried grass like **gisok** to make their bahay kubo waterproof. It's the ultimate eco-friendly roofing material, but probably a nightmare during typhoon season.
usage_notes: Madalas na ipinagkakamali o ipinagpapalit sa 'kugon'. Tumutukoy ito sa isang partikular na uri ng damo na ginagamit sa pagbububong.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bubong ng lumang dampa ay yari sa **gisok**.","translation":"The roof of the old hut is made of **thatch grass**."}]

translation: to make do with; to endure something patiently
meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit o pagtanggap sa isang bagay na hindi perpekto o sapat dahil sa kawalan ng mas magandang pagpipilian, na ginagawa nang may pasensya at tiyaga.
original_explanation: The art of "making it work" when you have less than ideal options. It's using a slow, laggy phone because you can't afford a new one yet. It's eating the same 'baon' for a week to save money. It's dealing with a difficult client with a smile. It's the verb form of 'pagtitiyaga', where you actively apply that patience to a specific, often frustrating, person or thing.
usage_notes: This verb implies that the object being endured is less than ideal, but one persists out of necessity or patience.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **pagtiyagaan** ang luma mong laptop habang nag-iipon para sa bago.","translation":"You have **to make do with** your old laptop while saving up for a new one."},{"sentence":"**Pinagtiyagaan** niyang turuan ang makulit na bata.","translation":"She **patiently endured** teaching the unruly child."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng matinding pag-aalala, hindi mapakali, o pagkabalisa na may kasamang takot o pangamba.
original_explanation: It's that feeling when you're waiting for your exam results, or when your boss says "we need to talk." It's the physical manifestation of anxiety—the racing heart, the fidgeting, the constant checking of your phone. That 'di mapakali' feeling, but elevated to a more poetic, high-stress level.
usage_notes: Isang malalim at pampanitikang salita para sa pagkabalisa. Hindi karaniwang ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa kalagayan ng **talibatab** ang ina habang hinihintay ang balita tungkol sa kanyang anak.","translation":"The mother was in a **state of apprehension** while waiting for news about her child."},{"sentence":"Ang **talibatab** sa kanyang dibdib ay hindi nawala hangga't hindi siya nakauwi nang ligtas.","translation":"The **anxiety** in her chest did not disappear until he returned home safely."}]

translation: to exalt oneself, to make oneself seem great
