meaning_filipino: Gawin ang sarili na maging dakila, marangal, o tanyag sa paningin ng iba, na kung minsan ay may pahiwatig ng pagyayabang o pagmamataas.
etymology: From 'mag-' (verb prefix) + 'pa-' (causative prefix) + 'dakila' (great, noble). 'To cause oneself to be great.'
original_explanation: This is when someone tries to make themselves look great, often in a showy way. Think of a politician during election season highlighting all their 'accomplishments.' It can be positive (striving for greatness) but often has a slightly negative flavor, like you're trying too hard to be praised. The opposite of being humble.
usage_notes: Carries a connotation that can range from ambition to arrogance, depending on the context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tunay na pinuno ay hindi kailangang **magpadakila** sa sarili; ang gawa niya ang nagsasalita.","translation":"A true leader doesn't need to **exalt** himself; his actions speak for him."},{"sentence":"Sa halip na **magpadakila**, mas pinili niyang maglingkod nang tahimik.","translation":"Instead of **making himself seem great**, he chose to serve quietly."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bulalas na nagpapahayag ng pagkainis, pagkadismaya, o magkahalong pagkabigla at pagkayamot. Ito ay isang pinaikling anyo ng 'malay ko at'.
etymology: Believed to be a contraction of "(ma)lay ko at", literally "I don't know and".
original_explanation: This is your tito's go-to curse word when he hits his thumb with a hammer or when his favorite team misses a crucial free throw. '**Lekat!**' is a milder, more classic version of 'P*tangina!'. It’s got that old-school, 'I'm annoyed but I'm still a gentleman' vibe. It's the 'Hay, nako!' of mild frustration.
usage_notes: Considered slightly old-fashioned but still understood. A mild expletive.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lekat** naman, naiwan ko ang wallet ko sa bahay!","translation":"**Damn it**, I left my wallet at home!"},{"sentence":"**Lekat!** Bakit ngayon pa nawalan ng internet?","translation":"**Heck!** Why did the internet have to go out now?"}]

translation: to become weak, to become listless
meaning_filipino: Ang unti-unting panghihina ng katawan, pagkawala ng sigla, o pagiging matamlay.
original_explanation: That feeling you get on a Monday morning. Or after eating too much at a buffet. It's when your energy level is on 'low batt' and you just want to lie down and do nothing. Your phone's battery at 1%? That's 'nananamlay'.
usage_notes: Commonly used to describe a person's physical state (being sick or tired) or even an economic state (a languishing market).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **manamlay** ang bata mula nang magkasakit ito.","translation":"The child started to **become weak** ever since he got sick."},{"sentence":"**Nanananmlay** ang bentahan sa tindahan tuwing tag-ulan.","translation":"Sales at the store **languish** during the rainy season."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagbuo ng tuyo at matigas na balat sa ibabaw ng isang sugat habang ito ay gumagaling.
original_explanation: It's your body's natural Band-Aid. After you get a 'galos' (scrape) from falling off a bike, your skin works its magic and creates this protective crust. The golden rule your nanay taught you: "Huwag tuklapin, kusa 'yang matatanggal!" (Don't pick it, it will fall off on its own!).
usage_notes: A biological process of healing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hayaan mo lang ang sugat mo, **magkakalangib** din 'yan.","translation":"Just leave your wound alone, it will **form a scab** eventually."},{"sentence":"Mabilis **nagkalangib** ang gasgas niya sa tuhod.","translation":"The scrape on his knee quickly **formed a scab**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malaking alimasag (Scylla serrata) na karaniwang matatagpuan sa mga putikan o bakawan, may makinis at maitim na talukab, at mas malalaking sipit kumpara sa alimasag.
original_explanation: The heavyweight champion of the crab world. This is the one you save up for, the star of the handaan. It has bigger, meatier claws (sipit) than its cousin, the alimasag. Getting the meat out is a workout, but the reward is so worth it.
usage_notes: Often confused with 'alimasag'. Alimango lives in muddy/mangrove areas, is darker, and generally larger with bigger claws. Alimasag lives in the sea, is lighter/spotted, and has flatter back legs for swimming.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap ang ginataang **alimango** na niluto ni Lola.","translation":"The **mud crab** in coconut milk that Grandma cooked is delicious."},{"sentence":"Ang mahal ng isang kilong **alimango** sa palengke ngayon.","translation":"A kilo of **mud crab** is so expensive at the market today."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kaugnayang pamilang sa pagitan ng dalawang halaga, na nagpapakita kung gaano karaming beses ang isang halaga ay nilalaman ng isa pa.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na "ratio" o Espanyol na "ratio".
original_explanation: Yung tamang timpla ng kape mo: 2 is to 1 ang ratio ng kape sa asukal. O kaya sa work, 100 tasks to 1 employee ang ratio pag malapit na ang deadline. It's all about the perfect (or sometimes, crazy) balance.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa matematika, agham, at pagluluto. Ang bigkas na /REY-syo/ ay mula sa Ingles, habang ang /RA-syo/ ay mas malapit sa Espanyol.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tamang **ratio** ng tubig sa bigas ay mahalaga para sa masarap na kanin.","translation":"The correct **ratio** of water to rice is important for delicious rice."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan nila ang **ratio** ng lalaki sa babae sa kanilang kumpanya.","translation":"They are studying the male-to-female **ratio** in their company."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan o bagay na ginagamit sa pagkayod, pag-alis ng dumi, o pagpapakinis ng isang ibabaw sa pamamagitan ng pagkuskos.
original_explanation: Your lola's secret weapon against a dirty 'kawali'. It could be the 'bunot' (coconut husk) for the floor, the steel wool for the pot, or even a 'bato' (pumice stone) for your 'kalyo'. If it's used to scrub something aggressively, it's a panguskos.
usage_notes: Can refer to a wide variety of scraping or scrubbing tools.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang **panguskos** na yari sa bunot upang pakintabin ang sahig.","translation":"She used a **scrubber** made of coconut husk to shine the floor."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng bagong **panguskos** para sa mga makakapal na kalawang sa kawali.","translation":"I need a new **scraper** for the thick rust on the frying pan."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagbabawas ng konsentrasyon o tapang ng isang likido sa pamamagitan ng pagdaragdag ng isa pang likido, karaniwan ay tubig. Tumutukoy rin ito sa mismong idinadagdag na panunaw.
etymology: Possibly related to Malay 'bantu' (help, assist), in the sense of 'assisting' a liquid to become less concentrated.
original_explanation: This is what you do to your Zesto or Tang when it's too sweet—you add water. 'Banto' is the act of diluting, or the water you use to do it. It’s the ultimate life hack for making your coffee less strong, your juice last longer, or your mom's sinigang less maasim.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of drinks or liquid flavorings. The verb form is 'bantuhan' (to dilute something).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masyadong matapang ang kape, lagyan mo ng kaunting **banto**.","translation":"The coffee is too strong, add a little water to **dilute** it."},{"sentence":"Ang paglalagay ng **banto** sa alak ay paraan upang hindi agad malasing.","translation":"Adding a **diluent** to the alcohol is a way to not get drunk quickly."}]

translation: to beg for mercy; to plead pitifully
meaning_filipino: Manikluhod o makiusap nang buong pagpapakumbaba at pagpapakita ng kaawa-awang kalagayan upang makamit ang awa o pabor.
original_explanation: This is a level up from `magmakaamo`. It's more desperate and intense. This is what the kontrabida does in the final scene of a teleserye when they're cornered and about to be arrested. It's begging for your life, your job, or for forgiveness when you've messed up big time. There's a sense of desperation and pity involved.
usage_notes: More intense and desperate than 'magmakaamo'. It emphasizes the pitiful state of the one pleading.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagmamakaawa** ang bilanggo na patawarin na siya sa kanyang mga kasalanan.","translation":"The prisoner is **begging for mercy** to be forgiven for his sins."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magmakaawa** sa akin; dapat inisip mo 'yan bago mo ginawa.","translation":"Don't **plead pitifully** to me; you should have thought of that before you did it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng libangan kung saan ang mga amateur na mang-aawit ay kumakanta kasabay ng isang paunang-record na musika (minus one) gamit ang mikropono at isang monitor na nagpapakita ng liriko.
etymology: Borrowed from Japanese カラオケ (karaoke), from 空 (kara, "empty") + オーケストラ (ōkesutora, "orchestra").
original_explanation: The national sport of the Philippines. It's the main event at every birthday party, reunion, and random Tuesday night. It's where your shy tita transforms into a rockstar, your tito sings "My Way" against everyone's advice, and you finally get a score of 98 on a song you've been practicing. Videoke, anyone?
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with "videoke" in the Philippines, which specifically refers to systems with video displays.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-arkila kami ng **karaoke** para sa Pasko.","translation":"We rented a **karaoke** machine for Christmas."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kantahin ang 'My Way' sa **karaoke**, baka magkagulo.","translation":"Don't sing 'My Way' at the **karaoke**, it might cause trouble."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng kapintasan, sira, o hindi paggana nang tama.
etymology: From 'may' (has/have) + Spanish 'diferencia' (difference, but adopted to mean defect/problem).
original_explanation: When your phone suddenly dies, your internet connection is slower than a snail, or the remote control only works if you hit it three times. It's the universal diagnosis for anything that's not working properly, from your laptop to your brain on a Monday morning. 'Sorry, late ako, may-diperensiya ata yung alarm clock ko.' (Sorry I'm late, I think my alarm clock is faulty.)
usage_notes: Can apply to machines, objects, systems, or even people (often humorously or offensively, e.g., 'may diperensiya sa pag-iisip').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ibalik mo 'yang binili mo, **may-diperensiya** sa makina.","translation":"Return that thing you bought, it **has a defect** in the engine."},{"sentence":"Tila **may-diperensiya** ang ating koneksyon sa internet ngayon.","translation":"It seems our internet connection **is faulty** today."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paraang mabilis o nagmamadali; walang pag-aaksaya ng panahon.
original_explanation: That 'dali-dali' energy when your boss emails you 'for immediate action' at 4:59 PM on a Friday. Or when you hear the 'sana all' chismis and need to share it with your group chat ASAP. It's action done with the speed of a GrabFood driver during a lunch rush.
usage_notes: Implies haste, often with a sense of urgency or even recklessness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinapos niya nang **sabilisan** ang report dahil malapit na ang deadline.","translation":"She finished the report **hurriedly** because the deadline was near."},{"sentence":"Nag-empake sila nang **sabilisan** nang malaman nilang may paparating na bagyo.","translation":"They packed **in a rush** when they learned a typhoon was coming."}]

meaning_filipino: Madaling ibagay, iakma, o ilapat sa isang partikular na sitwasyon, layunin, o kapaligiran.
etymology: From madali (easy) + -ng (linker) + iagpang (to adapt, to fit).
original_explanation: This is the ultimate BPO agent skill. Can work dayshift, nightshift, graveyard shift. Can handle irate callers and sweet-talkers. It's also that one black dress that you can wear to the office, to a party, or even sa binyag. Versatile!
usage_notes: Often used to describe objects, systems, or people that are flexible. Synonymous with 'madaling ibagay' but sounds slightly more formal or technical.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang disenyo ng muwebles ay **madaling iagpang** sa kahit anong espasyo.","translation":"The furniture's design is **easy to adapt** to any space."},{"sentence":"Ang isang mahusay na lider ay kayang **iagpang** ang kanyang istilo sa kanyang mga tauhan.","translation":"A good leader is able to **adapt** his style to his people."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng soberanya na namumuno sa isang monarkiya, o ang asawa ng isang hari. Ginagamit din bilang titulo ng karangalan para sa isang babaeng nangingibabaw sa isang larangan.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'Sana All' goals. Siya 'yung nanalo sa beauty pageant, 'yung bida sa Flores de Mayo, o 'yung nanay mong naghahari-harian sa bahay (with love, of course). In short, the boss lady. "Ikaw ang aking reyna," sabi ng jowa mong nanghihiram ng pang-load.
usage_notes: Malawak ang paggamit, mula sa literal na monarkiya hanggang sa mga beauty pageant (Reyna Elena) at bilang termino ng paghanga.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinoronahan si Pia Wurtzbach bilang Miss Universe, ang **reyna** ng kagandahan sa buong mundo.","translation":"Pia Wurtzbach was crowned as Miss Universe, the **queen** of beauty in the whole world."},{"sentence":"Ang **reyna** ng tahanan ay ang aking ina.","translation":"The **queen** of the house is my mother."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking yunit ng mga sundalo, lalo na sa hukbong Romano noong unang panahon; isang napakaraming pangkat ng mga tao o bagay.
original_explanation: Think of a **lehiyon** as a huge group of anything. Originally, it was for Roman soldiers, but now you can have a **lehiyon** of fans at a K-Pop concert, a **lehiyon** of mosquitos during rainy season, or a **lehiyon** of tasks from your boss before a long weekend. It's basically the word for 'sobrang dami na hindi mo na mabilang.'
usage_notes: Often used hyperbolically to mean a very large number.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **lehiyon** ng mga deboto ang dumalo sa prusisyon.","translation":"A **legion** of devotees attended the procession."},{"sentence":"Tinalo ng Romanong **lehiyon** ang mga kalaban nito.","translation":"The Roman **legion** defeated its enemies."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbuo o pagsali sa isang hanay ng mga tao o bagay na naghihintay ng kanilang pagkakataon.
original_explanation: The national sport of the Philippines, whether it's for the MRT, a new milk tea shop, or getting your NBI clearance. It's the ultimate test of patience where you stand behind someone and someone stands behind you, creating a human centipede of waiting.
usage_notes: Verb is in the completed aspect (past tense). Present tense is `pumipila`, future is `pipila`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pumila** ako nang tatlong oras para lang sa concert tickets.","translation":"I **lined up** for three hours just for concert tickets."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **pumila** para makakuha ng ayuda.","translation":"You need to **get in line** to receive aid."}]

meaning_filipino: Gumawa ng matining na tunog sa pamamagitan ng pagbuga ng hangin mula sa mga labing nakaawang nang bahagya.
original_explanation: The classic move of the 'tambay sa kanto' when a pretty girl walks by. It's what the security guard does to get your attention, or what you do when you're trying to call your dog. It can be a catcall, a signal, or just you trying to remember a song's melody.
usage_notes: Often associated with catcalling ('paninipol'), but its neutral meaning is simply to whistle. 'Sumipol' is a more common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pumasuwit** ang guwardiya upang pahintuin ang sasakyan.","translation":"The guard **whistled** to stop the vehicle."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **pumasuwit** sa mga babaeng dumadaan, bastos iyan.","translation":"Don't **whistle** at the women passing by, that's rude."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang instrumento o aparato na ginagamit upang sukatin, panatilihin, at ipahiwatig ang oras.
etymology: Mula sa salitang 'oras' na may hulaping '-an', na nagpapahiwatig ng isang lugar o bagay na nauugnay sa salitang-ugat.
original_explanation: The thing on the wall (or your wrist) that you stare at, begging it to move faster on a Friday afternoon. Also the source of your mini-heart attack when the alarm goes off. Before smartphones, this was the OG status symbol. "Nice orasan!"
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa isang 'clock' (orasan sa pader) o isang 'wristwatch' (relo, orasan sa kamay).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sira yata ang **orasan** sa pader, laging alas-tres.","translation":"I think the **clock** on the wall is broken, it's always three o'clock."},{"sentence":"Regalo sa akin ng lolo ko itong gintong **orasan**.","translation":"My grandfather gifted me this gold **watch**."}]

translation: to get muddy; to be splattered with mud
meaning_filipino: Ang marumihan o matalsikan ng putik.
etymology: From ma- (ability/accidental verb prefix) + putik (mud) + -an (locative/object-focus suffix).
original_explanation: The inevitable consequence of walking on a 'maputik' road. This is what happens when a speeding jeepney passes by a puddle right next to you. 'Naman o! Bago pa 'tong pantalon ko, naputikan agad!' It's the action of becoming muddy.
usage_notes: Often used in the completed aspect 'naputikan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang maglaro sa labas dahil baka **maputikan** ang kanyang bagong sapatos.","translation":"He doesn't want to play outside because his new shoes might **get muddy**."},{"sentence":"**Naputikan** ako ng dumaang sasakyan.","translation":"I **was splattered with mud** by a passing car."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng mabilis na pag-iwas sa isang bagay, tao, o sitwasyon upang hindi matamaan o masangkot. Ito ang gagawing pag-ilag.
original_explanation: Future tense of 'ilag'. What you'll do when your mom throws a tsinelas at you. Or when you see your ex at the mall. Or when someone asks "kelan ka mag-aasawa?" during a family reunion. "Pag nakita ko si boss, iilag ako, 'di ko pa tapos yung report."
usage_notes: Contemplated aspect (future tense) of 'umilag'. It implies a quick, reflexive action to avoid something immediate.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis siyang **iilag** para hindi matamaan ng bola.","translation":"He **will dodge** quickly to avoid getting hit by the ball."},{"sentence":"Sa tuwing tatanungin siya tungkol sa utang niya, bigla siyang **iilag** sa usapan.","translation":"Whenever he's asked about his debt, he **will** suddenly **evade** the topic."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang grupo ng mga tao na nagkakaisa para sa isang partikular na layunin o interes; isang samahan o kapisanan.
original_explanation: Think your homeowners' association (HOA) that keeps reminding you about monthly dues. Or the 'alumni association' that only seems to exist to ask for donations. It's basically any official group or 'samahan' where you have meetings, officers, and probably a Viber or FB group chat that's always buzzing.
usage_notes: Madalas na ginagamit sa pormal na konteksto tulad ng negosyo, gobyerno, o mga organisasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumali siya sa **asosasyiyon** ng mga manunulat upang mapabuti ang kanyang kasanayan.","translation":"He joined the writers' **association** to improve his skills."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangyayari na naganap nang hindi sinasadya, hindi binalak, o nagkataon lamang.
original_explanation: Ito yung 'di ko sinasadya' moment mo. Yung natapunan mo ng kape yung boss mo, o na-send mo sa group chat yung message na para sa jowa mo. It wasn't planned, it just... happened. Oops.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **aksidental** na pagkikita ang naganap sa pagitan ng magka-dating kasintahan.","translation":"An **accidental** meeting happened between the former lovers."},{"sentence":"Humingi siya ng paumanhin para sa **aksidental** na pagkasira ng plorera.","translation":"He apologized for the **accidental** breaking of the vase."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kilos kung saan ang dalawa o higit pang tao ay sabay-sabay o palitang nagtutulak sa isa't isa; maaari ring tumukoy sa pandiwa na magtulak nang sabayan.
original_explanation: Picture this: Black Friday sale sa mall. ‘Yan ang **tulakan**. O ‘di kaya ‘yung pila sa community pantry na nauwi sa gulo. It's the physical version of arguing in a group chat.
usage_notes: Nagpapahiwatig ng isang resiprokal o magulong pagkilos ng pagtutulak na kinasasangkutan ng maraming tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng **tulakan** sa harap ng entablado nang lumabas ang banda.","translation":"A **pushing match** occurred in front of the stage when the band came out."},{"sentence":"Huwag kayong mag-**tulakan** sa pila, lahat naman ay mabibigyan.","translation":"Don't **push each other** in the line, everyone will be served."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasuotan o damit na isinusuot sa katawan.
original_explanation: Your OOTD (Outfit Of The Day). The armor you choose for your daily battles, whether it's a corporate uniform for a client presentation or pambahay shorts for a Netflix marathon. "Ganda ng bihis natin ah!" is the ultimate Pinoy compliment.
usage_notes: Can refer to a specific set of clothes for an occasion. It is a homonym of "bihis" (adjective), meaning "dressed", which has a different pronunciation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghanda siya ng magandang **bihis** para sa party.","translation":"She prepared a nice **outfit** for the party."},{"sentence":"Ang pormal na **bihis** ay kailangan sa pagdalo sa seminar.","translation":"Formal **attire** is required to attend the seminar."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain o laro ng boling, kung saan nagpapagulong ng bola upang tamaan at pabagsakin ang mga pin sa dulo ng isang lane.
etymology: Hiram sa salitang Ingles na 'bowling'. Ang paglalagay ng unlaping 'pag-' at pag-uulit ng unang pantig ('bo') ay karaniwang paraan ng pagbuo ng pangngalan ng kilos mula sa mga hiram na salita.
original_explanation: A very straightforward word. This is what you do on a Friday night with your BPO team for a 'team building' activity. It's the act of throwing a heavy ball down a slippery lane, hoping for a strike but usually ending up with a gutter ball. The 'pag-' prefix and reduplication just turns the English word 'bowling' into a Filipino-style noun for the activity.
usage_notes: A direct loanword adaptation common in Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Niyaya niya ang kanyang mga kaibigan para sa isang sesyon ng **pagboboling**.","translation":"He invited his friends for a session of **bowling**."},{"sentence":"Kasama sa team building namin ang **pagboboling** at pagkain sa labas.","translation":"Our team building includes **bowling** and eating out."}]

translation: to drive away; to banish; to shoo
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapaalis o pagbugaw sa isang tao, hayop, o bagay mula sa isang lugar, kadalasan sa paraang hindi maganda.
original_explanation: This is what you do to a stray dog sniffing your garbage, a persistent suitor you're not interested in, or that negative thought trying to ruin your day. It's the act of saying 'Shoo! Alis! Layas!' It has a stronger, more forceful connotation than just asking someone to leave; it implies rejection. 'Itaboy' is the command form.
usage_notes: Used for both literal shooing of animals/people and figurative banishing of feelings or thoughts. The root word itself, 'taboy', can act as a noun for the act of shooing away.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **itaboy** ang mga pusang kalye, bigyan mo na lang ng pagkain.","translation":"Don't **shoo away** the street cats, just give them some food."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang **itaboy** ang masasamang alaala ng nakaraan.","translation":"She is trying to **banish** the bad memories of the past."}]

meaning_filipino: Maramihan ng arko; tumutukoy sa dalawa o higit pang kurbadong istruktura.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "arcos", ang anyong maramihan ng "arco".
original_explanation: Kapag hindi lang isa, kundi marami ang welcome arch sa bayan niyo, 'yan na ang arkos. Parang yung hallway sa isang lumang simbahan na sunod-sunod ang arko. More arches, more fun!
usage_notes: Ito ay ang anyong maramihan (plural) ng 'arko'. Sa Tagalog, madalas inuulit na lang ang 'mga arko' ngunit tinanggap na rin ang 'arkos' dahil sa impluwensya ng Espanyol.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakaganda ng hilera ng mga **arkos** sa loob ng lumang monasteryo.","translation":"The row of **arches** inside the old monastery is very beautiful."},{"sentence":"Ang disenyo ng tulay ay gumagamit ng maraming **arkos** para sa katatagan.","translation":"The bridge's design uses multiple **arches** for stability."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang pagputol ng lahat ng komunikasyon sa isang tao nang walang anumang paliwanag, lalo na sa konteksto ng isang relasyon o pakikipag-date.
etymology: Isang Tagalized na pandiwa mula sa salitang Ingles na "ghost", gamit ang panlaping pandiwang pokus sa tagaganap na "nang-".
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "seen-zone" level up. One day you're talking, the next day, *poof*! They vanished like a bubble. Bigla na lang naging multo. You're left wondering if their phone died, they died, or your personality was just that bad. #SanaAllMayClosure
usage_notes: Isang napakamodernong salitang balbal na malawak na nauunawaan ng mga nakababatang henerasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Akala ko okay kami, tapos bigla na lang siyang **nangghost**.","translation":"I thought we were okay, then he suddenly **ghosted** (me)."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang paasa, masama ang **mangghost** ng tao.","translation":"Don't lead someone on, it's bad **to ghost** people."}]

meaning_filipino: Lapnosin o sunugin ang balat o anumang bagay sa pamamagitan ng init, apoy, o kemikal.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you touch the sizzling plate without the wooden tray, or when you confidently drink coffee that's fresh off the kettle. It's also a metaphor for getting hurt in a relationship—'mapaso sa pag-ibig'—that feeling of being burned by someone you trusted. Ouch, both literally and figuratively.
usage_notes: This is the object-focused verb form. 'Magpaso' is the actor-focused form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka at baka **pasuin** mo ang iyong kamay sa mainit na kawali.","translation":"Be careful or you might **burn** your hand on the hot pan."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **pasuin** ng araw ang iyong balat.","translation":"Don't let the sun **burn** your skin."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang pangunahing gawain ay ang paglilinis ng mga ginamit na plato, kubyertos, at iba pang kagamitan sa kusina.
etymology: Isang parirala na binubuo ng "tagapaghugas" (washer) at "ng pinggan" (of plates).
original_explanation: The unsung hero of every handaan or fiesta. While everyone else is posting their food on Instagram, this person is in the trenches, battling a mountain of oily plates and 'sebo.' This is the designated 'bunso's' first job training.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy ito sa tao, hindi sa makina (na tinatawag ding 'dishwasher' sa Ingles).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng handaan, ako ang laging naatasan bilang **tagapaghugas ng pinggan**.","translation":"After the feast, I am always assigned as the **dishwasher**."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagkabitin o pagdugtungin ang mga bagay gamit ang isang pisi, lubid, o anumang panali.
original_explanation: What you do to the plastic bag of your take-out 'sinigang' so the 'sabaw' doesn't spill on your commute. Also, what you do to your shoelaces, or what you wish you could do to your friend's mouth when they're about to spoil a series.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **magtali** ng mga kahon na ito para sa paglipat.","translation":"Help me **tie** these boxes for the move."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magtali** ng aso bago ito pakawalan sa bakuran.","translation":"You need to **tie** the dog before letting it loose in the yard."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang muling isipin o balikan sa alaala ang isang nakaraang pangyayari, impormasyon, o karanasan.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping pandiwa na `ma-` at inuulit na unang pantig ng salitang-ugat na `alaala` (memorya).
original_explanation: 'Yung bigla mong naisip 'yung utang sa'yo ng kaibigan mo nung nakita mo siya sa mall. Or when a song plays on the radio and suddenly, you're back in your high school prom, feeling all the feels. It's the brain's "On This Day" feature. Ito ang pormal na bersyon na madalas makita sa mga libro.
usage_notes: Ito ang anyong potensyal o may kakayahan, na nangangahulugang "to be able to remember" o "to happen to remember". Ito ang mas pormal na baybay; ang `maalala` ay ang karaniwang pinaikling anyo sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay **maalaala** mo pa rin ang ating mga pinagsamahan.","translation":"I hope you can still **remember** what we've been through together."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko **maalaala** kung saan ko inilagay ang aking mga susi.","translation":"I can't **recall** where I put my keys."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng pagkalito, pagkabahala, o pag-aalala na dulot ng biglaang pangyayari o pagmamadali, na nagreresulta sa hindi maayos na pagkilos.
original_explanation: That feeling when your boss calls you for a "quick chat" on a Friday afternoon, or when you realize you left your phone in the Grab car. It's a state of panicked confusion where you can't think straight. Praning level 100.
usage_notes: Often used in the verb form "mataranta" (to be panicked) or "nataranta" (was panicked).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpadala sa **taranta**; huminga ka muna nang malalim.","translation":"Don't give in to **panic**; take a deep breath first."},{"sentence":"Sa sobrang **taranta** niya, naiwan niya ang kanyang wallet.","translation":"In his extreme **fluster**, he left his wallet behind."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, kumpanya, o entidad na nagbibigay o nagsu-suplay ng mga produkto, materyales, o serbisyo sa iba.
original_explanation: The person your sari-sari store owner gets their stocks from. The BPO agent's lifeline for good coffee beans. The one you call when your business is running out of inventory. They're the source, the plug, the "taga-kuha ng paninda." Without a good supplier, your online selling business is doomed.
usage_notes: A direct loanword from English, commonly used in business and commerce contexts. Often used interchangeably with the Tagalized spelling "suplayer".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating maghanap ng bagong **supplier** ng tela.","translation":"We need to find a new **supplier** of fabric."},{"sentence":"Huli na naman ang dating ng deliver mula sa aming **supplier**.","translation":"The delivery from our **supplier** is late again."}]

translation: to twitch; to throb; to pulsate
meaning_filipino: Mabilis at bahagyang paggalaw o pagpitik ng isang bahagi ng katawan, karaniwang hindi sinasadya.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na biglang gumalaw 'yung talukap ng mata mo na parang may sariling buhay? O 'yung labi mo after mong makakita ng ahas? 'Yan ang pag-kimbot. It’s that involuntary little muscle spasm or twitch. Minsan may kasamang pamahiin pa 'yan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Biglang **kumimbot** ang kaliwang talukap ng kanyang mata.","translation":"His left eyelid suddenly **twitched**."},{"sentence":"Nararamdaman kong **kumikimbot** ang sugat sa aking binti.","translation":"I can feel the wound on my leg **throbbing**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bilang na kasunod ng pito at sinusundan ng siyam; ang simbolo nito ay 8.
original_explanation: The number that looks like an infinity sign doing a sit-up. It's the number of hours you're supposed to sleep (but don't), the number of glasses of water you're supposed to drink (but won't), and the number of members in a classic barkada outing that will somehow fit in one tricycle.
usage_notes: Can function as both a noun (e.g., "ang walo") and an adjective (e.g., "walong tao").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroon akong **walong** kapatid.","translation":"I have **eight** siblings."},{"sentence":"Alas **walo** na ng gabi, kailangan ko nang umuwi.","translation":"It's already **eight** o'clock at night, I need to go home."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang damdamin ng pag-asam at pagnanais na mangyari ang isang bagay; pagtitiwala sa magandang kahihinatnan.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na tinitingnan mo 'yung sweldo mo sa payslip at umaasa kang aabot pa 'yan hanggang sa susunod na sahod. Ito 'yung nag-iisang bagay na natitira kapag na-seen-zone ka na, 'yung "baka sakali" sa lotto, at 'yung paniniwalang magkaka-character development din 'yung paborito mong kontrabida sa teleserye.
usage_notes: Mas karaniwang ginagamit ang "pag-asa" sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mawalan ng **esperansa**.","translation":"Don't lose **hope**."},{"sentence":"Siya ang tanging **esperansa** ng kanilang pamilya.","translation":"He/She is the only **hope** of their family."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagpapakita ng kawalan ng interes, malasakit, o pagkabahala sa isang bagay, tao, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: Ito yung jowa mong sine-seen ka lang. Yung ka-group mo sa project na walang ambag. Yung pusa mong titingnan ka lang habang umiiyak ka. Basically, "I don't care" with a Spanish accent. The "K." reply in human form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bakit ka ba **indiperente** sa mga problema ng ating bayan?","translation":"Why are you so **indifferent** to our country's problems?"},{"sentence":"Naging **indiperente** siya matapos siyang masaktan nang paulit-ulit.","translation":"She became **apathetic** after being hurt repeatedly."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng karaniwang malawakang ipinamamahaging metamorphic na bato na may mga guhit-guhit na nabuo sa ilalim ng mataas na temperatura at presyon.
original_explanation: Isang klase ng bato na mukhang may layers o stripes. Parang 'yung mga mamahaling bato na ginagawang countertop sa kusina or sahig sa mayayamang bahay. It's a fancy rock, basically. Pronounced like "nice".
usage_notes: Isang napaka-espesipikong termino na ginagamit sa heolohiya. Karamihan sa mga Pilipino ay tatawagin lang itong 'bato'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **gneis** ay isang halimbawa ng metamorphic rock.","translation":"**Gneiss** is an example of a metamorphic rock."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng mga heologo ang pormasyon ng **gneis** sa bundok.","translation":"The geologists are studying the **gneiss** formation in the mountain."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglalakbay sa tubig gamit ang isang sasakyang-dagat, lalo na ang may layag.
etymology: From pa- + mam- (from ma- + layag) + layag. The root 'layag' means 'sail'.
original_explanation: Before Grab, Angkas, or even airplanes, this was the ultimate long-distance travel. It's the act of sailing, going on a voyage. Think Magellan's crew, the ancient Austronesians exploring the Pacific, or even just a rich person on their yacht in Subic. It's the OG way to 'travel a-sea'.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for sailing or metaphorically for a journey or venture.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matagal at mapanganib ang **pamamalayag** noong unang panahon.","translation":"**Sailing** in ancient times was long and dangerous."},{"sentence":"Ang buhay ay isang **pamamalayag** sa malawak na karagatan ng panahon.","translation":"Life is a **voyage** on the vast ocean of time."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o bagay na palaging nasa tabi o kasama sa lahat ng oras at pagkakataon.
etymology: From the reduplication of "kasama" (companion), which intensifies the meaning to 'constant companion'.
original_explanation: Your 'beshie for life.' Your phone. Your anxiety. That one friend na laging present sa lahat ng lakad, from 7-Eleven runs to out-of-town trips. Sila 'yung "plus one" mo by default. Sabi nga nila, "Sana all may kasa-kasama."
usage_notes: The repetition of "kasa-" emphasizes the constancy and closeness of the companionship.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aso niya ang kanyang **kasa-kasama** sa bahay.","translation":"His dog is his **constant companion** at home."},{"sentence":"Simula pagkabata, si Maria na ang aking **kasa-kasama**.","translation":"Since childhood, Maria has been my **constant companion**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang butas sa damit, karaniwang may tahi sa gilid, kung saan isinusuot o ikinakabit ang butones.
original_explanation: The forever-partner of the butones (button). It's that slit in your shirt that's either too tight for the button or has gotten so loose that your shirt keeps opening at the worst possible moment. "Manang, pasikipan mo naman 'tong ohales ng polo ko, laging bukas eh!"
usage_notes: More common among older generations or in the context of sewing and tailoring. 'Butas ng butones' is a more descriptive alternative.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sira na ang **ohales** ng luma kong pantalon.","translation":"The **buttonhole** on my old pants is broken."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong tahiin nang maigi ang paligid ng **ohales** para hindi ito masira.","translation":"You need to sew the edge of the **buttonhole** carefully so it doesn't fray."}]

translation: to stage a show; to present a performance
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-organisa at pagtatanghal ng isang palabas, dula, o anumang uri ng pagtatanghal para sa mga manonood.
original_explanation: The official verb for every school program committee, theater group, and concert producer. It's the act of putting on a show, from a simple classroom presentation of 'Ang Pasko Ay Sumapit' to a massive concert at the Araneta Coliseum. You're getting something up on a stage for all to see.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aming klase ay **magpapatanghal** ng isang dula para sa Linggo ng Wika.","translation":"Our class will **stage** a play for the National Language Week."},{"sentence":"Nagpasya silang **magpatanghal** ng isang benefit concert para sa mga nasalanta ng bagyo.","translation":"They decided to **present** a benefit concert for the typhoon victims."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang kilos o pangyayari na nagaganap sa bawat gabi nang paulit-ulit.
original_explanation: Your daily routine, but make it nocturnal. It's what you do **every night**, like clockwork. Watching your favorite teleserye, scrolling through TikTok until your eyes hurt, or having that existential crisis right before you sleep. It's the adverb for consistent nightly habits.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Gabi-gabi** siyang tumatawag sa kanyang kasintahan sa ibang bansa.","translation":"He calls his girlfriend abroad **every night**."},{"sentence":"Mayroong ingay na naririnig mula sa kapitbahay **gabi-gabi**.","translation":"There's a noise heard from the neighbor **nightly**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marka o impresyon na iniiwan ng paa sa isang ibabaw, tulad ng lupa o buhangin.
original_explanation: Literally 'trace of the foot'. This is what you leave behind on the beach for your IG story, or what the chismosa neighbor looks for in the mud outside your window. It's evidence that someone was there.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May nakita kaming **bakas ng paa** ng isang malaking aso sa hardin.","translation":"We saw the **footprints** of a large dog in the garden."},{"sentence":"Ang mga **bakas ng paa** sa buhangin ay binura ng alon.","translation":"The **footprints** on the sand were erased by the waves."}]

translation: to outline; to make a framework of
meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa o pagbuo ng isang balangkas; pag-ayos ng mga pangunahing ideya o bahagi ng isang plano, sulatin, o proyekto sa isang sistematikong paraan.
original_explanation: The verb form of "drawing." No, not the art kind, the planning kind. It's what your boss tells you to do for the new project, what your teacher required for your thesis. "Balangkasin mo muna" is the corporate way of saying "Gawa ka muna ng draft para may A-approve-an ako." It’s about creating the skeleton before adding the meat (or the chismis).
usage_notes: A command form (imperative) or infinitive. Used in contexts of planning, writing, and project management.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **balangkasin** muna natin ang buong ulat bago ito isulat.","translation":"We need to **outline** the entire report first before writing it."},{"sentence":"**Balangkasin** mo ang mga hakbang para sa proyekto.","translation":"**Outline** the steps for the project."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang langis, pamahid, o gamit na ginagamit sa pagmamasahe o sa tradisyonal na paggamot ng pilay o sakit sa katawan.
etymology: From pang- (instrumental prefix) + hilot (massage, traditional Filipino healing massage).
original_explanation: This refers to the oil, liniment, or even a special leaf used by a 'manghihilot' (traditional masseuse/healer). It's the stuff that makes the massage happen—think Efficascent Oil, Omega Pain Killer, or that secret herbal concoction your lola swears by. It's the fuel for the 'hilot' engine.
usage_notes: Refers to the substance or tool for the massage, not the person ('manghihilot') or the act ('paghilot').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Amoy luya at menthol ang **panghilot** na ginagamit ng matanda.","translation":"The **liniment** used by the old man smells like ginger and menthol."},{"sentence":"Nagpabili si Lolo ng langis ng niyog para gawing **panghilot**.","translation":"Grandpa asked someone to buy coconut oil to be used as a **massage liniment**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paggaling at pagsasara ng isang sugat sa balat. Tumutukoy din ito sa peklat o marka na naiiwan pagkatapos gumaling ng sugat.
original_explanation: This is for physical wounds, but the 'hugot' is real. It's the process of your 'sugat' (wound) closing up. Parang pag-move on sa ex mo—may 'peklat' (scar) na maiiwan, a reminder of the pain, pero at least 'di na 'fresh'. The wound has healed. 'Naghihilom na ang puso ko.' Charot.
usage_notes: Can refer to the process of healing or the resulting scar. 'Humilom' or 'maghilom' is the verb form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis na nag-**hilom** ang sugat sa kanyang tuhod.","translation":"The wound on his knee **healed** quickly."},{"sentence":"May naiwang marka ng **hilom** sa kanyang braso.","translation":"A **scar** was left on his arm."}]

translation: the process of melting or dissolving
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagbabago ng isang solidong bagay upang maging likido, karaniwan dahil sa init, o ang paghahalo nang lubusan ng isang sangkap sa isang likido.
original_explanation: 'Yung ice cream mo under the Philippine sun. Or your heart when your crush finally smiles at you. That glorious, sometimes tragic, process of turning into a puddle is pagkatunaw. Also applies to your sahod after 2 days.
usage_notes: Can be literal (ice, metal) or figurative (a heart melting, money disappearing).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binantayan niya ang **pagkatunaw** ng yelo sa baso.","translation":"He watched the **melting** of the ice in the glass."},{"sentence":"Mabilis ang **pagkatunaw** ng kanyang ipon dahil sa hindi inaasahang gastos.","translation":"The **dissolving** of his savings was fast due to unexpected expenses."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglilipat ng dugo mula sa isang tao, o mula sa isang nakaimbak na suplay, patungo sa daluyan ng dugo ng ibang tao.
original_explanation: That thing doctors do when your blood count is lower than your chances with your crush. It's literally getting someone else's life force pumped into you, like a medical vampire situation but for your own good.
usage_notes: A medical term. The 'pa-' prefix signifies a request or the act of having something done. The full phrase is 'magpasalin ng dugo' (to have a blood transfusion).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **pasalinan ng dugo** ang pasyente sa lalong madaling panahon.","translation":"The patient needs a **blood transfusion** as soon as possible."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging madaling magalit, mainis, o mawalan ng pasensya.
original_explanation: This is your mood on a Monday morning before your first cup of coffee, when the internet is slow, and your boss emails you "for urgent assistance". It's the quality of being easily triggered, the 'sungit' mode activated.
usage_notes: Describes the personality trait or temporary state of being easily annoyed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko maintindihan ang kanyang **pagkamayamutin** ngayong araw.","translation":"I can't understand his **irritability** today."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa kanyang **pagkamayamutin**, kaya iniiwasan siyang biruin ng mga kasamahan niya.","translation":"He is known for his **irascibility**, so his colleagues avoid joking with him."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng paghithit ng sigarilyo o tabako.
original_explanation: The more formal, almost vintage-sounding way of saying 'to smoke.' You'd imagine your lolo in a rocking chair would magtatabako, not your Gen Z cousin vaping. It’s the verb form of what the sign 'Bawal Manigarilyo Dito' is trying to prevent.
usage_notes: Synonymous with "manigarilyo" (to smoke a cigarette), but "magtatabako" can also specifically refer to smoking a cigar or pipe. "Manigarilyo" is more common in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinayuhan siya ng doktor na itigil na ang **pagtatabako**.","translation":"The doctor advised him to stop **smoking tobacco**."},{"sentence":"Nakasanayan na ng matanda na **magtatabako** pagkatapos kumain.","translation":"The old man has made it a habit to **smoke tobacco** after eating."}]

translation: The act of showing off; boasting.
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagmamayabang o pagpapakita ng mga ari-arian, nagawa, o katangian sa iba, lalo na sa social media.
original_explanation: This is the -ing form of the national sport. It's the whole process of taking 50 photos of your Starbucks cup, choosing the perfect filter, and crafting a caption that says 'blessed' but really means 'look at me.' Yung 'weird flex, but okay' moment mo sa buhay.
usage_notes: Refers to the action or process of showing off itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi na nakakatuwa ang **flexing** niya ng mga mamahaling gamit araw-araw.","translation":"His daily **boasting** of expensive things is no longer amusing."},{"sentence":"Minsan, ang **flexing** ay paraan lang para makakuha ng validation mula sa iba.","translation":"Sometimes, **showing off** is just a way to get validation from others."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng isang ibon o manok na paggamit ng tuka upang kumuha ng pagkain o umatake.
original_explanation: What a chicken does to the grains you throw on the ground. Also, what your friend does to the fries on your plate when they said they weren't hungry—they tumuka one piece at a time until it's all gone.
usage_notes: Primarily used for birds. Can be used humorously for people who eat small bites from a shared plate.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumuka** ang manok sa mga butil ng mais.","translation":"The chicken **pecked** at the corn kernels."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang matakot, hindi **tutuka** ang ahas.","translation":"Don't be afraid, the snake won't **strike**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nakabuka o nakabukaka nang husto ang mga hita o binti.
original_explanation: The default sleeping position of every Tito after a few beers and a heavy meal. Legs and arms spread out, occupying maximum bed/sofa space. Also describes how you sit on a jeepney when you're feeling entitled. "Huy, umayos ka ng upo, 'wag kang bikangkang!"
usage_notes: Often used with a slightly negative or comical connotation, implying a lack of decorum. It has a related verb form, "bumikangkang".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita niyang natutulog nang **bikangkang** ang aso sa sahig.","translation":"He saw the dog sleeping **spread-eagled** on the floor."},{"sentence":"\"Huwag kang umupong **bikangkang**,\" paalala ng kanyang lola.","translation":"\"Don't sit with your **legs wide apart**,\" his grandmother reminded him."}]

meaning_filipino: 1. May ibabaw na hindi pino o makinis. 2. Tumutukoy sa ugali o pananalita na bastos, walang galang, at hindi kaaya-aya.
original_explanation: Two main flavors: 1) Physical - like 'yung sementong hindi pa napapalitadahan, or 'yung kamay ng nagbubuhat ng bakal. 2) Personality - 'yung tao na diretsahan at walang preno kung magsalita, medyo bastos ang dating. It's the opposite of "smooth" in every sense.
usage_notes: A very versatile word describing both physical texture and coarse behavior/speech. It's one of the most common words for 'rough'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magaspang** ang tela ng lumang tuwalya.","translation":"The fabric of the old towel is **rough**."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko gusto ang kaibigan mo, **magaspang** siyang magsalita.","translation":"I don't like your friend, he speaks **coarsely**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-abot o pagbangga sa isang target; o ang pagkuha ng tamang sagot o solusyon.
original_explanation: Two meanings! 1) Yung feeling na sapul ka sa "random" hugot post ng friend mo. That's a direct hit. 2) Yung moment na nanalo ka sa lotto, o kahit sa hula-hula lang sa exam. You hit the jackpot, bes!
usage_notes: Can be literal (physical impact) or figurative (getting an answer correct, being affected by something).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malakas ang **pagtama** ng bola sa kanyang mukha.","translation":"The **hitting** of the ball on his face was strong."},{"sentence":"Ipinagdiwang niya ang **pagtama** niya sa anim na numero sa lotto.","translation":"He celebrated his **getting right** the six numbers in the lotto."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang karagdagang bubong o silungan na nakakabit sa isang pangunahing gusali, karaniwang mas mababa at yari sa mas magaan na materyales.
etymology: From Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *səbi, meaning eaves or extension of a roof.
original_explanation: That extra roof you see attached to the side of a house, usually over the 'bangerahan' (dish-drying rack) or where the 'labahan' (laundry area) is. It's the original house extension before people started building whole new rooms. It protects you from the sun and rain while you're gossiping with the neighbor. In the city, it's the makeshift roof of a sari-sari store.
usage_notes: A common architectural term in the Philippines, especially for traditional and rural houses.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpatayo sila ng **sibi** sa gilid ng bahay para may paglagyan ng mga paso.","translation":"They built a **lean-to** on the side of the house to have a place for the plant pots."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paraang parang tumutusok, tumatarak, o direktang tumatama, lalo na sa pananalita.
etymology: From the prefix "pa-" indicating manner, and "tusok" meaning 'pierce' or 'prick'.
original_explanation: Like how your Tita gives you 'the look' when you get the last piece of leche flan. It's sharp, direct, and you feel it deep in your soul. It can describe a sharp comment ('patusok na salita') or the way a BBQ stick goes through a hotdog.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a Pang-uri (Adjective) to mean 'pointed' or 'sharp', as in 'patusok na pananalita' (pointed words).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Patusok** siyang sumagot sa kanyang ina.","translation":"She answered her mother in a **piercing** manner."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa mga salitang **patusok** na binitiwan niya.","translation":"Be careful of the **pointed** words she uttered."}]

translation: to bet; to wager; to estimate
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng pusta sa isang laro o kaganapan na may hindi tiyak na resulta; maaari ding mangahulugang pagbibigay ng pansamantalang kalkulasyon o hula.
original_explanation: Two main flavors: 1) The Lotto/sabong/basketball version where you bet your last 20 pesos hoping to become a millionaire. 2) The "hugot" version where you bet your heart on someone who just leaves you on 'seen'. In both cases, you're taking a risk. It can also mean to estimate, like when you "magtaya" how many minutes you can be late for work before the boss notices.
usage_notes: Context is key. 'Magtaya sa lotto' is 'to bet on the lotto', while 'Magtaya ka kung ilan' is 'Make an estimate of how many'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto niyang **magtaya** sa lotto dahil sa laki ng jackpot prize.","translation":"He wants to **bet** on the lotto because of the huge jackpot prize."},{"sentence":"**Magtaya** ka, mga ilang tao kaya ang darating sa party?","translation":"**Estimate**, about how many people do you think will come to the party?"},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magtaya** ng puso sa taong hindi sigurado sa'yo.","translation":"Don't **wager** your heart on someone who isn't sure about you."}]

translation: to be overcome; to be surpassed
meaning_filipino: Malampasan o mahigitan sa isang labanan, kumpetisyon, o anumang sitwasyon; matalo.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na na-seen zone ka kasi may mas pogi/maganda. 'Yung kalaban mo sa Mobile Legends, na-Gusion ka tapos na-wipe out kayo. You were outplayed. You got beaten. You were 'nadaig'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi dapat tayo **madaig** ng takot.","translation":"We should not be **overcome** by fear."},{"sentence":"Kahit maliit, hindi siya **madadaig** sa pagtatalo.","translation":"Even if he's small, he won't be **surpassed** in an argument."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tungkulin o akto ng pamumuno bilang tagapangulo sa isang pagpupulong, komite, o bansa.
etymology: From a formal derivation related to "pagka-" (state of) + "pangulo" (president/head).
original_explanation: This is the official term for being the "big boss" of a meeting. You're the one who says "Order in the court!" or, more likely in a corporate setting, "Okay guys, let's circle back to the main agenda." It's the act of being the *pangulo* or chairperson.
usage_notes: A very formal and somewhat rare term. "Pagkapangulo" (presidency) or "pamumuno" (leadership) are much more common. This word is often found in formal minutes of meetings or historical texts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mahusay na **pagkanuluhan** sa pulong ay nagbunga ng mabilis na desisyon.","translation":"The excellent **chairmanship** of the meeting resulted in a quick decision."},{"sentence":"Ipinagkatiwala sa kanya ang **pagkanuluhan** ng mahalagang komite.","translation":"He was entrusted with **presiding** over the important committee."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng husay sa pagpaplano at pagpapatupad ng mga pamamaraan o taktika upang makamit ang isang layunin.
etymology: From `ma-` (adjective-forming prefix) + `taktika` (tactic), which is from Spanish 'táctica'.
original_explanation: Describes someone who knows how to play the game. The friend who perfectly plans the 'barkada' trip down to the last peso. The BPO agent who knows exactly what to say to de-escalate an angry caller. The person at the palengke who can get the best 'tawad' from a 'suki'. They're not just smart, they're 'mataktika'.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a person's cleverness in handling situations or people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa pagiging **mataktika** ng heneral, nanalo sila sa laban.","translation":"Because the general was **tactical**, they won the battle."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong maging **mataktika** sa pagnenegosyo.","translation":"You need to be **strategic** in business."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bayan o komunidad ng mga tao; ang mga mamamayan ng isang lugar.
original_explanation: Think of the 'poblacion' or town center. That's the puweblo. It's where the church, the munisipyo, and the plaza are. It's the heart of the town, straight out of a Spanish colonial textbook. Today, it might feel a bit old-school, but it's the OG hub before malls took over.
usage_notes: Often refers to the town proper or central district, synonymous with 'poblacion'. Can also mean 'the people' or 'populace' in a more literary sense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sentro ng aming **puweblo** ay may malaking plasa.","translation":"The center of our **town** has a large plaza."},{"sentence":"Nagtipon ang buong **puweblo** para sa pista.","translation":"The entire **populace** gathered for the fiesta."}]

translation: afam hunter; someone who actively seeks a foreign partner
meaning_filipino: Isang mapanglarawang termino, kadalasang may bahid ng panghuhusga, para sa isang taong partikular na naghahanap ng dayuhang karelasyon, karaniwan ay para sa pinansyal na seguridad o pag-asang makapag-abroad.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng slang na 'afam' at Ingles na 'hunter'.
original_explanation: A term, sometimes used jokingly, sometimes... not, for someone whose dating preference is exclusively afam. Their Tinder location is set to 'Global,' and their natural habitat is a tourist spot or an expat bar. It’s a controversial label, but it’s definitely part of the modern Pinoy vocabulary.
usage_notes: Maaaring ituring na mapanlait o mapanghusga ang terminong ito depende sa konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binansagan siyang **afam hunter** ng kanyang mga kaibigan dahil lahat ng naging nobyo niya ay dayuhan.","translation":"Her friends labeled her an **afam hunter** because all her past boyfriends were foreigners."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian o kalagayan ng pagiging pula; ang tindi ng kulay pula.
etymology: From 'ka-' + 'pula' + '-han'. The 'ka-X-han' affix often denotes the quality or essence of 'X'.
original_explanation: That shade your face turns when your crush walks by. Or the color of your eyes after a 3-day K-drama binge-watching session. It's the essence of being 'red'—from the flush of embarrassment to the fiery glow of a sunset.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napansin ko ang **kapulahan** ng kanyang mga mata, mukhang galing siya sa iyak.","translation":"I noticed the **redness** of her eyes, it seems she had been crying."},{"sentence":"Ang **kapulahan** ng kalangitan ay hudyat na papalubog na ang araw.","translation":"The **redness** of the sky is a sign that the sun is about to set."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng laman sa isang bagay hanggang sa ito ay umabot sa sukdulan o sapat na dami.
original_explanation: This is what you do to your GrabFood cart before checkout. Or what happens to the MRT at 7 AM. "Bes, magpuno ka na ng gas, baka ma-stuck tayo sa EDSA." It's also that feeling when you've had enough of the drama: "Napuno na ako sa'yo!"
usage_notes: Can refer to filling a physical container or reaching an emotional limit ('mapuno').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magpuno** ka ng tubig sa balde para may magamit tayo mamaya.","translation":"**Fill** the bucket with water so we have some to use later."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magpuno** ng sama ng loob sa iyong dibdib.","translation":"Don't **fill** your heart with resentment."}]

meaning_filipino: Nauukol sa mga makina o mekaniks; ginagawa o pinapatakbo sa pamamagitan ng makinarya.
original_explanation: Describes anything that works with gears, levers, and moving parts, like a mechanical keyboard that annoys your officemates or an old-school watch. Also describes your dance moves if you look like a robot.
usage_notes: Used to describe processes, objects, or properties related to machines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May problemang **mekanikal** ang sasakyan kaya hindi ito umaandar.","translation":"The car has a **mechanical** problem, that's why it won't start."},{"sentence":"Mas gusto niya ang pakiramdam ng **mekanikal** na keyboard kaysa sa karaniwan.","translation":"He prefers the feel of a **mechanical** keyboard over a regular one."}]

translation: to be last; to be left behind
meaning_filipino: Maiwan sa hulihan; maging huli sa isang pangkat o karera.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na group project tapos ikaw lang 'di sinama sa group chat. Ikaw yung na-matauli. Or when the LRT door closes right in front of you. Saklap.
usage_notes: A very rare word, more common in older literature or specific dialects. 'Mahuli' is the everyday equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsikap siyang tumakbo ngunit **natauli** pa rin siya sa dulo.","translation":"He tried his best to run but was still **left behind** at the end."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpaiwan para hindi ka **matauli**.","translation":"Don't get left behind so you won't **be last**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagmula sa parehong lalawigan o probinsiya ng isa pa.
etymology: From 'ka-' (denoting company or shared quality) + 'probinsiya' (from Spanish 'provincia').
original_explanation: The instant connection you feel when you find out your new officemate is also from Batangas, Pampanga, or Cebu. Suddenly, you have an ally, a potential source for local delicacies, and someone who gets your specific regional accent. "Uy, kaprobinsiya pala kita!" is the start of a beautiful friendship (and maybe a pasalubong exchange).
usage_notes: The prefix 'ka-' is very productive in Tagalog to mean 'fellow X' or 'co-X'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nalaman kong **kaprobinsiya** ko pala ang katrabaho ko nang mag-usap kami tungkol sa aming mga bayan.","translation":"I found out my coworker was my **provincemate** when we talked about our hometowns."},{"sentence":"Nag-ambagan ang mga **kaprobinsiya** para tulungan ang pamilyang naapektuhan ng bagyo.","translation":"The **provincemates** chipped in to help the family affected by the typhoon."}]

translation: to stand with hands on hips
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng mga kamay sa magkabilang baywang, karaniwang isang kilos na nagpapahiwatig ng pag-aantay, pagkadismaya, o paghahamon.
etymology: From `maN-` (verb prefix) + `bewang` (waist). The prefix and root combine in a specific phonological process.
original_explanation: The official pose of every Pinoy mom about to ask 'Saan ka galing?' or a Marites waiting for the latest chismis. It's a non-verbal cue that can mean anything from 'I'm tired of waiting for this jeep' to 'You're grounded for life.' Power pose level: Tita.
usage_notes: Describes a very specific and culturally understood posture. The completed form is `namaywang`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napansin kong **nakamaywang** ang guro habang pinagmamasdan ang magulong klase.","translation":"I noticed the teacher was **standing with her hands on her hips** while watching the chaotic class."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mamaywang** diyan, tulungan mo ako magbuhat!","translation":"Don't just **stand there with your hands on your hips**, help me carry this!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang komposisyong musikal na may mga salita o liriko, na nilikha upang kantahin ng boses ng tao.
original_explanation: The classic meaning: What you sing in the shower, at the karaoke, or dedicate to your crush. It's the soundtrack of your life, from OPM rock to hugot ballads.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb form 'umawit' (to sing). Distinct from its modern slang usage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong pakinggan ang mga lumang **awit** ng OPM.","translation":"I love listening to old OPM **songs**."},{"sentence":"Sumulat siya ng isang **awit** para sa kanyang minamahal.","translation":"He wrote a **song** for his beloved."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggalaw o direksyon na laban sa agos ng tubig, daloy ng trapiko, o nakagawian. Ginagamit bilang pang-abay.
original_explanation: This is you driving your car against a one-way street. Or a salmon swimming upstream to spawn. It's going against the flow, whether it's traffic, water, or popular opinion. It's the 'kontrabida' move, the act of being 'pasaway.'
usage_notes: Often used with verbs of motion like `lumangoy` (to swim) or `maglakbay` (to travel). `Pasalunga` is a common adverbial form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap lumangoy nang **pasalunga** sa malakas na agos.","translation":"It's difficult to swim **against** the strong **current**."},{"sentence":"Sumasagwan siya nang **salunga** kaya mas mabagal ang kanyang bangka.","translation":"He was paddling **upstream**, which is why his boat was slower."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagpapadaan ng pagkain, inumin, o anumang bagay mula sa bibig patungo sa lalamunan at sikmura.
etymology: From `pag-` + reduplication of the first syllable of the root `lunok` (`lu-`) + `-lon` (a variation of the root). `Paglunok` is the more standard form.
original_explanation: Yung hirap na hirap mong gawin kapag may masakit kang pride. "Swallowing your pride" is a thing, 'di ba? Also, what you do when the chismis is so hot, you just have to take it all in. Literally, it's how you get your meds or that last piece of lechon down.
usage_notes: `Paglunok` is the more common term for swallowing. `Paglulon` might be encountered in older texts or poetry.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahirapan siya sa **paglulon** ng malaking tableta.","translation":"He had difficulty **swallowing** the large tablet."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang artipisyal na daluyan ng tubig o ibang likido, karaniwan sa gilid ng daan, para sa irigasyon, paglalakbay, o pag-aalis ng dumi.
original_explanation: The OG meaning is the ditch on the side of the road, the final destination of rainwater and your dreams if you're not careful. It's a fundamental part of Philippine infrastructure, sometimes functioning as a drainage system, sometimes as a surprise swimming pool after 10 minutes of rain.
usage_notes: This entry refers to the literal meaning. The modern slang meaning, referring to a low-brow aesthetic, is treated as a separate entry under the adjective form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahulog ang barya ko sa **kanal**.","translation":"My coin fell into the **gutter**."},{"sentence":"Nililinis ng mga residente ang baradong **kanal**.","translation":"The residents are cleaning the clogged **canal**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang itaas na bahagi ng loob ng bibig, na nasa likod ng mga ngipin.
etymology: From 'langit' (sky) + '-an' with reduplication, meaning 'false sky' or 'imitation sky'.
original_explanation: This is that part of your mouth you burn with scorching hot pizza or a fresh-from-the-pan lumpia. It's literally your "little sky" inside your mouth. You don't notice it until you've scalded it, and then it's all you can think about for three days.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napaso ang **langit-langitan** ko dahil sa mainit na sabaw.","translation":"I burned my **palate** because of the hot soup."},{"sentence":"May dumikit na pagkain sa kanyang **langit-langitan**.","translation":"Some food got stuck on his **palate**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gagawing pagbabago, pagwawasto, o pagsasaayos sa isang akda, larawan, video, o anumang materyal sa hinaharap.
etymology: Anyong panghinaharap (future tense) ng 'mag-edit', kung saan inuulit ang unang pantig ng salitang-ugat na nagsisimula sa patinig ('e').
original_explanation: The future tense of mag-edit. This is the promise you make to your team lead: "Yes po, **mag-eedit** ako ng deck mamaya after coffee break." It's the "I'll get to it" verb for writers, video editors, and anyone trying to make their IG feed look perfect.
usage_notes: Ito ang anyong panghinaharap (future tense) ng pandiwang 'mag-edit'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Mag-eedit** ako ng mga litrato natin mula sa bakasyon.","translation":"I **will edit** our photos from the vacation."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **mag-eedit** ng final report?","translation":"Who **will edit** the final report?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katagang ginagamit upang magbigay-diin, magpatotoo, o sumang-ayon sa isang naunang pahayag. Katumbas ng 'nga' sa maraming konteksto.
original_explanation: This is the Bisaya/regional cousin of the Tagalog 'nga'. It's the verbal seasoning you add to a sentence to say 'I told you so,' 'See?', or just to add a bit of friendly insistence. 'Sabi ko sa'yo masarap dito eh. Masarap ngani!'
usage_notes: Primarily used in Visayan languages, but its usage has seeped into casual Manila Tagalog, often for a humorous or specific regional flavor. It functions very similarly to 'nga'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tama ka **ngani**, mas mabilis nga ang daan na ito.","translation":"You are **indeed** correct, this road is faster."},{"sentence":"\"Ganda ba?\" \"Oo, maganda **ngani**!\"","translation":"\"Is it beautiful?\" \"Yes, it is **indeed** beautiful!\""}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bansa sa Europa na bahagi ng United Kingdom, na kilala sa kasaysayan, kultura, at bilang pinagmulan ng wikang Ingles.
original_explanation: The land of tea, the Queen, Harry Potter, and people who apologize even when it's your fault. It's where your tita wants to have her picture taken with a red telephone booth. Basically, the place whose language we're trying to speak with a "conyo" accent.
usage_notes: The standard Filipino name for the country.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang makarating sa **Inglatera** upang makita ang Buckingham Palace.","translation":"It's her dream to go to **England** to see Buckingham Palace."}]

translation: to be able to bet; to place a bet
meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang maglagak ng pera o anumang halaga sa isang laro o kaganapan na may hindi tiyak na resulta.
original_explanation: When your tito asks for your birthday to mataya on the lotto. It's the act of placing that bet, hoping your suwerte will pull through. 'Taya' is the bet, mataya is the action of placing it.
usage_notes: Can also be used in a figurative sense, meaning 'to risk' or 'to estimate'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit maliit lang ang pera ko, susubukan kong **mataya** sa huling karera.","translation":"Even if I only have a little money, I will try **to bet** on the last race."},{"sentence":"Magkano ang kaya mong **mataya** para sa pangarap mo?","translation":"How much are you willing **to risk** for your dream?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang seremonya ng kasal o ang pagdiriwang nito.
original_explanation: The formal, slightly more 'alta' way of saying 'kasal'. You'd see this on a fancy wedding invitation. It's less 'let's get married' and more 'witness our grand union'. It's the difference between a city hall wedding and a Balesin wedding.
usage_notes: More formal than 'kasal'. Often used in written invitations and formal announcements.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inaanyayahan kayo sa aming **boda** sa darating na Sabado.","translation":"You are invited to our **wedding** this coming Saturday."},{"sentence":"Napakagarbo ng kanilang **boda** sa simbahan.","translation":"Their **wedding** at the church was so grand."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang kilos ng paglalapat ng takip, pinto, o pagtatapos ng operasyon ng isang negosyo. Ito ay nasa aspektong imperpektibo.
original_explanation: That panic you feel when you're running to the bank at 2:55 PM and you see the guard **nagsasara** na ng pinto. "Kuya, sandali lang, magdedeposit lang po!"
usage_notes: Present progressive tense (imperpektibo) of 'magsara'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming negosyo ang **nagsasara** dahil sa hirap ng buhay.","translation":"Many businesses **are closing** because of the difficult life."},{"sentence":"Bakit laging **nagsasara** ang isip mo sa mga bagong ideya?","translation":"Why **are** you always **closing** your mind to new ideas?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng parusa sa isang tao, karaniwan sa isang bata o tinedyer, sa pamamagitan ng pagbabawal na lumabas ng bahay o gumamit ng mga gadyet.
original_explanation: The ultimate horror story for a Gen Z kid. This is what happens when your mom finds out you failed a subject or stayed out too late. 'No gadgets for a week! Bawal lumabas! You're grounded!' It's the verbal form of having your wings (and your Wi-Fi) clipped.
usage_notes: This is a colloquial, Taglish term. The formal Filipino equivalent would be something like 'parusahan sa bahay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang pasaway kung ayaw mong **mag-graun** ka sa bahay buong linggo.","translation":"Don't be naughty if you don't want to **be grounded** at home for the whole week."},{"sentence":"**Nag-graun** ako kaya hindi ako makakasama sa party.","translation":"I **got grounded** so I can't come to the party."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng mamalyang pandagat na kilala sa kanyang katalinuhan at palakaibigang kalikasan.
original_explanation: Eto yung Flipper ng dagat! Yung parang isda pero mas matalino pa sa ex mong di marunong mag-reply. Sila yung mga acrobatic swimmers na laging masaya, a stark contrast sa'yo tuwing Monday morning.
usage_notes: Madalas na ipinagkakamali sa 'dugong' (dugong) o 'balyena' (whale). Ang 'lumbalumba' ay partikular na tumutukoy sa mga dolphin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakita kami ng mga **lumbalumba** na tumatalon sa dagat habang kami'y nasa bangka.","translation":"We saw **dolphins** jumping in the sea while we were on the boat."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ikaapat na daliri ng kamay, na karaniwang pinagsusuutan ng singsing, lalo na ang singsing sa kasal o pakikipagtipan.
etymology: Mula sa `pala-` (unlaping nagpapahiwatig ng lugar o gamit) + `singsing` + `-an` (hulaping nagpapahiwatig ng lokasyon).
original_explanation: The designated finger for the bling! Ito yung daliri na laging under pressure, lalo na kapag nasa 'marrying age' ka na. Pag may singsing diyan, aakalain engaged ka na o kasal. Pag wala, tatanungin ka, 'Kailan pa?' The original 'status symbol' finger.
usage_notes: Literal na nangangahulugang 'lugar para sa singsing.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isinuot niya ang engagement ring sa **palasingsingan** ng kanyang nobya.","translation":"He put the engagement ring on his fiancée's **ring finger**."},{"sentence":"Masakit ang aking **palasingsingan** kaya't tinanggal ko muna ang aking singsing.","translation":"My **ring finger** hurts, so I took off my ring for a while."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos na pagpindot sa 'like' button sa hinaharap. Aspektong panghinaharap ng pandiwang 'maglike'.
etymology: Future tense of "maglike". Root: "like", Prefix: "mag-", Repetition of first syllable of root: "li-".
original_explanation: This is the future tense of digital validation. It's the promise you make to your friend, "Oo, sige, i-post mo lang, magli-like ako." It's the hope you have when you upload a new photo, thinking, "Sana maraming magli-like."
usage_notes: This is the future tense form of the slang verb 'maglike'. Often written as 'magli-like'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sigurado akong **magli-like** si crush sa bago kong profile picture.","translation":"I'm sure my crush **will like** my new profile picture."},{"sentence":"Sino kaya ang unang **magli-like** sa status update ko?","translation":"I wonder who **will like** my status update first?"}]

translation: to be able to add; to contribute to
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang magbigay ng karagdagan; maging sanhi ng pagdami o pagtaas ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: Yung chismis na narinig mo, 'wag mo nang ipasa. Baka **makadagdag** ka lang sa gulo. Pero kung may handaan at magdadala ka ng pagkain, go lang, para **makadagdag** sa saya (at sa ulam)!
usage_notes: The 'maka-' prefix indicates the ability to perform the action of 'dagdag' (to add). It can be used for both tangible (money, food) and intangible (problems, joy) things.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang iyong donasyon ay **makadagdag** nang malaki sa aming pondo para sa mga nasalanta.","translation":"Your donation **will be able to add** greatly to our funds for the victims."},{"sentence":"Iwasan ang mga salitang **makadagdag** lang sa kanyang kalungkutan.","translation":"Avoid words that will only **contribute to** his sadness."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis na pagpikit at pagdilat ng isang mata bilang isang senyas o pagpapahiwatig.
original_explanation: That subtle (or not-so-subtle) eye-flick you give your friend when you see your crush walk by, or when your tita says something wild at the family reunion. It's the non-verbal "gets mo?" or "OMG, look!". The ultimate silent communication tool.
usage_notes: Often used with the verb 'kumindat' (to wink).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **kindat** lang mula sa kanya, napangiti na ako.","translation":"Just one **wink** from him/her, and I was already smiling."},{"sentence":"**Kumindat** siya sa akin bago umalis.","translation":"He/she **winked** at me before leaving."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi tama, isang pagkakamali, o ang pagkabigo na matamaan ang isang target. Ginagamit din bilang pangalan na tumutukoy sa kasalanan.
original_explanation: That feeling when you send a risky text to the wrong GC. Or when you try to shoot your shot (basketball or love life) and you miss. 'Walang sala' (not guilty) is what you plead, even when you ate the last piece of lechon from the fridge.
usage_notes: The stress is on the second syllable /sa-LA/. As a noun, it means 'sin' or 'fault' (kasalanan). As an adjective, it means 'wrong' (mali).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inamin niya ang kanyang **sala** at humingi ng tawad.","translation":"He admitted his **fault** and asked for forgiveness."},{"sentence":"**Sala** ang ibinigay mong numero ng telepono.","translation":"The phone number you gave is **wrong**."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa matalinhagang paraan, tumutukoy sa dalawa o higit pang tao na matalik na magkaibigan o magkasundo. Ang literal na kahulugan ay ang pagkakaroon ng iisang uri ng ngiping bagang.
etymology: From 'magka-' (denoting a shared quality) + 'bagang' (molar tooth). The figurative sense likely comes from the idea of being 'of the same kind' or makeup.
original_explanation: Originally about having matching molars, which is weirdly specific. Now, it means you and your bestie are so close, it's like you share the same DNA, or at least the same taste in memes and milk tea. You're practically joined at the hip, or in this case, the molar. "BFF goals!"
usage_notes: The figurative meaning of being close friends is much more common in modern usage than its literal meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sila ay **magkabagang** mula pa noong elementarya kaya alam na nila ang lahat tungkol sa isa't isa.","translation":"They have been **close friends** since elementary school, so they know everything about each other."},{"sentence":"Imposibleng mag-away ang dalawang iyan, **magkabagang** kaya sila.","translation":"It's impossible for those two to fight, they're **inseparable**."}]

meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng katapusan o hangganan ang isang bagay, pangyayari, o ugnayan.
original_explanation: Ito yung moment na sinabi mong, "Tama na, itigil na natin 'to." Pwedeng sa isang toxic na relasyon, sa isang project na walang katapusan, o sa subscription mo sa gym na hindi mo naman pinupuntahan. It's the act of putting a definitive full stop, not just a comma.
usage_notes: Ito ay nasa anyong pautos o pawatas. Ipinahihiwatig nito ang isang sinadyang pagkilos upang tapusin ang isang bagay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Panahon na upang **wakasan** ang lahat ng ating hindi pagkakaunawaan.","translation":"It is time to **end** all our misunderstandings."},{"sentence":"Nais niyang **wakasan** ang kontrata dahil sa mga paglabag.","translation":"He wants to **terminate** the contract due to violations."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang pagkilos ng pagkakaroon ng alinlangan, pag-aalinlangan, o kawalan ng tiwala.
original_explanation: When your partner is suddenly extra sweet and you're thinking, "Anong kasalanan nito?" That's you, nagdududa. It's the official state of mind when you see a "PISO SALE" that seems too good to be true.
usage_notes: Present progressive tense of 'magduda'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Palagi siyang **nagdududa** sa katapatan ng kanyang mga kaibigan.","translation":"He is always **doubting** the loyalty of his friends."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi ako **nagdududa** sa kakayahan mo.","translation":"Don't worry, I am not **doubting** your abilities."}]
