original_explanation: Can describe sugar that's perfect for baking (vs. rough sugar for your kape), or the 'kolehiyala' accent of your conyo friend. It's the opposite of 'magaspang' (rough). 'Napakapino ng buhangin sa Boracay.' / 'Napakapino niyang kumilos, parang hindi marunong magkamay.'
usage_notes: Can refer to physical texture (e.g., sand, sugar) or to a person's manners and demeanor (refined, genteel).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gamitin mo ang asukal na **napakapino** para sa icing ng cake.","translation":"Use the **very fine** sugar for the cake's icing."},{"sentence":"Lahat ay humanga sa **napakapino** niyang pagkilos at pananalita.","translation":"Everyone was impressed by her **very refined** demeanor and speech."}]

translation: to turn one's back on; to abandon; to forsake
meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang pag-iwan, pagtalikod, o paglimot sa isang tao, responsibilidad, o paniniwala.
etymology: Mula sa 'talikod' (to turn one's back), na nagmula sa 'likod' (back). Ang hulaping '-an' ay ginagawa itong pandiwang nakatuon sa layon.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'seen-zone' in real life. It's when you ghost someone, abandon a promise, or renounce your duties. It's more than just leaving; it's a deliberate act of turning away. 'Huwag mong talikdan ang iyong mga pangarap' is what your motivational speaker friend tells you. 'Tinalikdan niya ako' is the ultimate hugot line.
usage_notes: Isang malakas, pormal, at madalas na may mabigat na emosyon na salita.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malaking kasalanan ang **talikdan** ang sariling pamilya.","translation":"It is a great sin to **abandon** one's own family."},{"sentence":"Pinili niyang **talikdan** ang marangyang buhay upang maglingkod sa mahihirap.","translation":"He chose to **turn his back on** a luxurious life to serve the poor."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa ng pagbabago, pagwawasto, o pagsasaayos sa isang akda, larawan, video, o anumang materyal.
etymology: Hiram sa salitang Ingles na 'edit' at nilapian ng unlaping `mag-`.
original_explanation: What you do to your selfie 17 times before posting it on Instagram. It's also what your boss tells you to do to your report for the 5th time, 10 minutes before the deadline. This is the infinitive form, as in: "Sige na, **mag-edit** ka na ng video para ma-upload na natin."
usage_notes: Ito ang anyong pawatas (infinitive) ng pandiwa. Ginagamit sa mga utos o bilang batayang pandiwa. Ang kilos na natapos na ay 'nag-edit'. Ang kilos na gagawin pa lang ay 'mag-eedit'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **mag-edit** ng resume ko bago mag-apply.","translation":"I need to **edit** my resume before applying."},{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **mag-edit** ka ng mga mali sa dokumento.","translation":"Please, **edit** the mistakes in the document."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagnanasang sekswal o ang lakas ng enerhiyang sekswal ng isang tao.
original_explanation: This is the Spanish/English loanword that explains why you suddenly find your officemate attractive after they started working out. It's the 'gana' or 'urge' that fuels hugot lines about 'marupok' (fragile/easily falls in love) moments. When your **libido** is high, even the BGC-Taft MRT ride feels like a romantic journey.
usage_notes: A direct loanword, used in psychological and medical contexts, but also understood in casual conversation about relationships and attraction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang stress sa trabaho ay maaaring magpababa ng **libido**.","translation":"Stress at work can lower one's **libido**."},{"sentence":"May mga pagkain daw na nakapagpapataas ng **libido**.","translation":"They say there are foods that can increase **libido**."}]

translation: to allow someone to ask; to field questions
meaning_filipino: Pahintulutan ang isang tao na magbigay ng katanungan; tumanggap at sumagot ng mga tanong, karaniwan sa isang pormal na pagtitipon.
original_explanation: This is what you do in a press conference or after a presentation when you're ready for the Q&A. 'Okay guys, magpatanong na kayo.' It's your way of saying, 'Bring on the chismis, I'm ready to answer... or deflect.'
usage_notes: The 'magpa-' prefix here indicates allowing or causing an action. It's often used by someone in a position of authority or a speaker addressing an audience.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magpapatanong** ang guro pagkatapos ng kanyang leksyon.","translation":"The teacher will **field questions** after her lecture."},{"sentence":"Matapang siyang **nagpatanong** sa mga mamamahayag tungkol sa kontrobersiya.","translation":"He bravely **allowed the reporters to ask him questions** about the controversy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na sisidlan, karaniwang gawa sa katad o tela, na ginagamit upang paglagyan ng pera, kard, at iba pang mahahalagang dokumento.
original_explanation: The command center of your financial life. Madalas masaya sa a-kinse at a-trenta, tapos nagiging onion na sa mga sumunod na araw—mapapaiyak ka sa tuwing bubuksan mo. It's also the graveyard of expired receipts and forgotten calling cards.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naiwan ko ang **pitaka** ko sa bahay kaya wala akong pambayad.","translation":"I left my **wallet** at home so I have no money to pay."}]

translation: to tie something; to tie onto something
meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng tali ang isang bagay; igapos o ibigkis ang isang bagay sa isa pa gamit ang tali.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'tali'. It's the action you do when you secure the 'lechon manok' box so the sauce doesn't spill, or when you tie a ribbon on a gift. In hugot terms, 'Huwag mo akong talian kung bibitawan mo lang din naman.' (Don't tie me to you if you're just going to let go.)
usage_notes: Ito ang anyong pandiwa na nakatuon sa layon. Ang anyong pautos ay 'Talian mo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Talian** mo nga ang aso para hindi makawala.","translation":"**Tie** up the dog so it doesn't get loose."},{"sentence":"Dapat nating **talian** ang mga kahon sa bubong ng sasakyan.","translation":"We need to **tie** the boxes to the roof of the car."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtama o pag-impis sa isang bagay o tao gamit ang malakas na sipa ng paa.
original_explanation: The action you want to do to your laptop when the internet dies during a crucial Zoom meeting. It's the foot's version of a punch. From a baby's cute kicks in the womb to a powerful martial arts move, 'tumadyak' is all about that forceful foot action.
usage_notes: Refers to a strong, forceful kick. A lighter or more playful kick might be 'sumipa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa galit, **tumadyak** siya sa pader.","translation":"In anger, he **kicked** the wall."}]

meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng surpresa ang isang tao; gulatin o biglain sa isang hindi inaasahang paraan.
etymology: From Spanish 'sorpresa' (surprise), with the Tagalog verb suffix '-hin'.
original_explanation: The act of hiding behind a door with a cake and balloons, ready to scream "SURPRISE!" at an unsuspecting victim... I mean, birthday celebrant. Also what your Meralco bill does to you every month.
usage_notes: Commonly used for both pleasant and unpleasant surprises.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Plano naming **surpresahin** si Ana sa kanyang kaarawan.","translation":"We plan to **surprise** Ana on her birthday."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **surpresahin** nang ganyan, atakihin ako sa puso!","translation":"Don't **surprise** me like that, I might have a heart attack!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging handa, mabilis kumilos, at mapagmatyag sa anumang maaaring mangyari.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung kaibigan mong chismosa na laging updated. One mention of a name and their ears perk up. Alisto! It's also the required state of mind when crossing EDSA, or when your boss is walking towards your cubicle. Be alisto or get left behind (or get more work).
usage_notes: Commonly used to describe someone who is sharp, quick-witted, and ready for action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat laging **alisto** ang mga guwardiya sa kanilang tungkulin.","translation":"The guards must always be **alert** in their duties."},{"sentence":"**Alisto** siyang sumagot sa tanong ng guro.","translation":"He was **quick** to answer the teacher's question."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng pinili ng mga magulang upang maging pangalawang ina at gabay sa espirituwal na buhay ng isang bata, karaniwan sa konteksto ng binyag, kumpil, o kasal.
etymology: A familiar term derived from the role of godparents, likely influenced by the Spanish 'madrina'. The 'na' part signifies the feminine.
original_explanation: Your Tita-but-make-it-official. She's supposed to be your spiritual guide, but for most Filipino kids, she's the VIP who gives you the best gifts (or at least a crisp bill) on Christmas and your birthday. You see her at family parties and say "Mano po, Ninang," and hope she remembers your name. She's a key player in the Filipino social fabric.
usage_notes: The female counterpart to 'ninong' (godfather). The term can refer to a godmother from a baptism, confirmation, or even a wedding sponsor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hihingi ako ng aguinaldo sa aking **ninang** sa Pasko.","translation":"I will ask for a Christmas gift from my **godmother**."},{"sentence":"Si Tita May ang napili kong maging **ninang** ng aking anak.","translation":"I chose Tita May to be my child's **godmother**."}]

meaning_filipino: Maramdaman ang hapdi o matinding kirot sa isang bahagi ng katawan.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of that ouchie feeling. When the alcohol hits the wound, you don't just say it *is* stinging, you say you *feel* the sting. 'Nung nilinis ang sugat ko, nahapdian talaga ako.' It's the active experience of that specific 'yikes!' pain.
usage_notes: Focuses on the person or body part experiencing the stinging sensation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong hawakan, baka lalo akong **mahapdian**.","translation":"Don't touch it, I might **feel more stinging pain**."},{"sentence":"**Nahapdian** ang mga mata niya dahil sa sabon.","translation":"His eyes **were stung** by the soap."}]

translation: to be stunned, to be stupefied
meaning_filipino: Ang mawalan ng kakayahang mag-isip o kumilos nang maayos dahil sa pagkabigla, pagkalito, o malakas na ingay; matuliro.
original_explanation: 'Yung reaction mo nung nalaman mong sold out na 'yung concert tickets in 5 minutes. You just sat there, tumulig. It's that feeling of being stunned into silence, either by shock, confusion, or a really loud noise. Parang nag-hang 'yung utak mo.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a state of being mentally overwhelmed or stunned. Less common than 'natulala' or 'natuliro'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumulig** siya sa lakas ng pagsabog.","translation":"He **was stunned** by the force of the explosion."},{"sentence":"Nang marinig niya ang balita, siya'y sandaling **tumulig** at hindi makapagsalita.","translation":"When he heard the news, he was momentarily **stupefied** and could not speak."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na bahagi ng isang organisasyon, kumpanya, o pangkat; o isang katauhan sa isang akdang pampanitikan o dula.
original_explanation: This word has two main vibes. 1) The 'corporate slave' vibe: your employees, staff, or personnel. 'Kumusta mga **tauhan** ko?' (How's my staff?) asks the boss. 2) The 'Netflix series' vibe: the characters in a story. 'Sino ang paborito mong **tauhan** sa 'Maria Clara at Ibarra'?' (Who's your favorite **character** in 'Maria Clara at Ibarra'?). It's all about the people in the system, whether that system is a company or a story.
usage_notes: The context determines whether it means 'personnel' or 'character'. The phrase 'tauhan ng dula' explicitly means 'character in a play'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lahat ng **tauhan** ng kumpanya ay inimbitahan sa Christmas party.","translation":"All company **personnel** were invited to the Christmas party."},{"sentence":"Ang pangunahing **tauhan** sa nobela ay si Crisostomo Ibarra.","translation":"The main **character** in the novel is Crisostomo Ibarra."}]

translation: to defeat; to subdue; to overpower
meaning_filipino: Talunin o supilin ang isang kalaban o hadlang sa pamamagitan ng lakas o kapangyarihan.
original_explanation: This is what you do to your enemies in Mobile Legends. Or what you want to do to your deadlines on a Friday afternoon. 'Gapiin ang mga gawain!' para weekend na! It's about total domination, no mercy.
usage_notes: Implies a decisive and complete victory.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Layunin ng bayani na **gapiin** ang masamang hari at palayain ang kaharian.","translation":"The hero's goal is to **defeat** the evil king and free the kingdom."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tagasunod at mag-aaral ng isang guro, pinuno, o pilosopiya.
original_explanation: Sa original context, ito yung mga 'apostles' ni Jesus. Sa modern world, ito yung mga die-hard fans ng isang K-Pop group, o yung mga loyal followers ng isang vlogger na lahat ng sinabi at ginawa, sinusunod. 'Mga **disipulo** ni Ivana Alawi, assemble!'
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa kontekstong panrelihiyon, ngunit maaari ring gamitin sa mas malawak na kahulugan ng pagiging tagasunod.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang labindalawang **disipulo** ni Hesus ay nangaral ng kanyang mga turo.","translation":"The twelve **disciples** of Jesus preached his teachings."},{"sentence":"Itinuturing niya ang kanyang sarili na isang **disipulo** ng yumaong pintor.","translation":"He considers himself a **disciple** of the late painter."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pook o istruktura na sadyang ginawa upang paglagyan at limitahan ang kilos ng isang tao, hayop, o bagay.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung literal na pinaglalagyan ng mga hayop or... mga tao (hello, Bilibid!). Parang 'yung friend mong ayaw kang payagang umalis sa toxic relationship niya, ginawa kang emosyonal na preso sa kulungan ng feelings niya. #NoToJailTimeSaPagIbig
usage_notes: A general term for any enclosure intended to confine. Can be a literal cage, a prison, or used metaphorically.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatakas ang ibon mula sa **kulungan** nito.","translation":"The bird escaped from its **cage**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga bilanggo ay dinala sa pambansang **kulungan**.","translation":"The prisoners were brought to the national **jail**."}]

translation: to get wet; to wet something
meaning_filipino: Ang pagdudulot na mabasa o malagyan ng tubig o anumang likido ang sarili o isang bagay.
original_explanation: What happens when you forget your payong during the rainy season and the jeepney you're in has a leaky roof. It’s also what you do to your plants so they don't die, or to your hair before putting on gel. Basically, introducing H2O where it wasn't before.
usage_notes: The stress and glottal stop on the last syllable is crucial to differentiate it from 'magbasa' (to read). In formal writing, this is sometimes spelled 'magbasâ'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maglaro sa ulan para hindi ka **magbasâ**.","translation":"Don't play in the rain so you don't **get wet**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **magbasâ** ng basahan para punasan ang mesa.","translation":"I need to **wet** a rag to wipe the table."}]

translation: to be repulsed by; to find ugly or obscene
meaning_filipino: Makaramdam ng pandidiri o pagkadismaya sa isang bagay, tao, o sitwasyon dahil sa kapangitan o kalaswaan nito.
original_explanation: That feeling when you see your crush's new partner and you're just... not impressed. 'Nako, na-masagwaan ako sa ugali niya.' It's the active verb form of feeling the 'eww'. It's when something crosses the line from 'okay lang' to 'nope, can't unsee'.
usage_notes: This is a verb expressing a subjective reaction. The '-an' suffix indicates that the subject of the sentence is the one experiencing the feeling of repulsion. The completed aspect is 'nasagwaan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nasagwaan** ang mga manonood sa malalaswang eksena sa pelikula.","translation":"The audience **found** the lewd scenes in the movie **obscene**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi ako **masasagwaan** sa hitsura mo kahit bagong gising.","translation":"Don't worry, I won't **be repulsed** by how you look even if you've just woken up."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi mahirap dalhin o ilagay mula sa isang lugar patungo sa iba; magaan o may disenyo para sa madaling paglipat.
etymology: From madali (easy) + -ng (linker) + ilipat (to move, to transfer).
original_explanation: Think of your laptop vs. a desktop computer, or a condo vs. a house and lot. It's the convenience of being able to pack up and go. For feelings, it's that 'move on' ability some people have. 'Grabe, parang ang feelings niya, madaling ilipat from one person to another.'
usage_notes: Used for physical objects (portable) or abstract concepts like files, data, or even feelings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas praktikal ang lamesang ito dahil **madaling ilipat** kung saan mo kailangan.","translation":"This table is more practical because it's **easy to move** wherever you need it."},{"sentence":"Siguraduhin na ang mga file ay nasa format na **madaling ilipat** sa ibang computer.","translation":"Make sure the files are in a format that is **easy to transfer** to another computer."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mas matindi, paulit-ulit, o mas mahabang proseso ng malalim na pag-iisip kumpara sa pagninilay.
etymology: From 'pag-' + reduplication of 'nilay'. The repetition implies a more intense or prolonged action.
original_explanation: This is 'pagninilay' on steroids. It's not just one coffee session; it's the whole weekend, maybe even a silent retreat. You're overthinking, but in a productive, soul-searching way. Like when you're trying to figure out why your ex's new partner looks exactly like you.
usage_notes: The reduplication of 'nilay' emphasizes the intensity, duration, or repetitive nature of the contemplation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng mahabang **pagninilay-nilay**, nagpasya siyang mag-resign.","translation":"After a long period of **deep reflection**, he decided to resign."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga tula ay bunga ng kanyang **pagninilay-nilay** sa buhay.","translation":"His poems are the fruit of his **musings** on life."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pandiwa sa aspektong panghinaharap na nagsasaad ng pagbabago ng estado o pag-iral sa isang partikular na katangian o pagkakakilanlan.
etymology: Aspektong panghinaharap/kontemplatibo ng pandiwang 'maging' (to be, to become).
original_explanation: The ultimate 'manifesting' verb. 'Yong sinasabi mo sa sarili mo habang nagpupuyat sa pag-aaral: "**Magiging** CPA din ako!" Ito rin ang sagot mo 'pag tinanong kung anong mangyayari 'pag nanalo ka sa lotto: "**Magiging** milyonaryo!"
usage_notes: Ito ang anyong panghinaharap ng 'maging', na naglalarawan ng isang kalagayan na iiral o mabubuo sa hinaharap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kung magpapatuloy ka sa iyong kasipagan, **magiging** matagumpay ka balang araw.","translation":"If you continue with your diligence, you **will be** successful someday."},{"sentence":"Sabi ng PAGASA, **magiging** maulan ang buong linggo.","translation":"PAGASA said that the whole week **will be** rainy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabahagi ng isang buo sa dalawa o higit pang bahagi.
original_explanation: Like when you have one piece of chicharon left and your friend gives you 'the look'. You have to **maghati**, even if it hurts your soul. It's the ultimate test of friendship. Or when you and your ex decide to split the bills after the breakup. Awts.
usage_notes: Typically means dividing something into two equal or unequal parts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Maghati** tayo sa bayad sa kuryente.","translation":"Let's **split** the electricity bill."},{"sentence":"Nagpasya silang **maghati** ng kita.","translation":"They decided to **divide** the profits."}]

translation: to be traced; to be noticeable (of a trace or mark)
meaning_filipino: Maaninag, matagpuan, o makita ang isang tanda, bakas, o palatandaan, lalo na kung ito ay sinusubukang ikubli.
original_explanation: When you're trying to hide the fact you ate the last piece of cake, but your mom can still see the chocolate smudge on your face. 'Yan, 'mabakas' pa rin ang ebidensya. It's about seeing the receipts or the trail, literally or figuratively.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit anong tago mo ng lungkot, **nababakas** pa rin sa iyong mga mata.","translation":"No matter how you hide your sadness, it can still **be traced** in your eyes."},{"sentence":"Mahirap nang **mabakas** ang pinagdaanan ng mga sinaunang tao.","translation":"It is now difficult to **trace** the path of ancient people."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang anak ng kapatid ng isang tao.
etymology: Possibly from `pa-` + `mang-` + `angkin`, related to the idea of a claimed or related child. The exact origin is debated but linked to kinship terms.
original_explanation: Your built-in sidekick and the reason you have to buy extra pasalubong. They're the kids you can spoil rotten and then give back to their parents when they start crying. The gender-neutral term for your brother's or sister's child. In the Philippines, you're basically a second parent to them.
usage_notes: This is a gender-neutral term. To specify gender, one can add "lalaki" (male) or "babae" (female).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Darating ang mga **pamangkin** ko mula sa probinsya para magbakasyon.","translation":"My **nephews and nieces** are coming from the province for a vacation."},{"sentence":"Paborito kong **pamangkin** si Ana dahil siya ay napakabait.","translation":"Ana is my favorite **niece** because she is very kind."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang napakasamang amoy, karaniwang mula sa nabubulok na bagay o hindi malinis na lugar.
original_explanation: Yung amoy na parang pinagsamang basura, medyas na 'di nalabhan for a week, at estero. It's the kind of smell that makes you question your life choices, like walking past a pile of garbage on a hot summer day. "Amoy alisangsang" is an insult to your nostrils.
usage_notes: Often used to describe very strong, unpleasant odors, like that of stagnant water, decay, or unhygienic places.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **alisangsang** na amoy mula sa basurahan sa likod-bahay.","translation":"There's a **foul-smelling** odor coming from the trash can in the backyard."},{"sentence":"Nang buksan niya ang lumang baul, sumingaw ang **alisangsang**.","translation":"When he opened the old chest, a **rank** smell emanated."}]

meaning_filipino: Sadyain o maging sanhi ng pagkaantala ng isang tao, gawain, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: To actively cause a delay. This is what you do to your friend who's always early by 'forgetting' your wallet so you have to go back. Or what a slow government process does to your application. 'Atrasuhin' is the verb form of creating an 'atraso' for someone else. It's the 'wait lang, may kukunin lang ako' that turns into 30 minutes.
usage_notes: A transitive verb that requires an object to be delayed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo sanang **atrasuhin** ang biyahe natin bukas.","translation":"I hope you don't **delay** our trip tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Inatraso ng masamang panahon ang pagdating ng eroplano.","translation":"The bad weather **delayed** the airplane's arrival."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbibigay ng pera sa isang tao na may kasunduang ito ay ibabalik, kadalasan ay may kasamang interes.
etymology: From pag- (nominalizer) + pa- (causative) + pa- (progressive aspect) + utang (debt). Lit. 'the act of causing someone to have debt'.
original_explanation: The original 'pautang-ina' system. Ito 'yung business model ng ka-officemate mong laging may dalang notebook at ballpen tuwing kinsenas at katapusan. Minsan, ito rin ang simula ng pagkasira ng pagkakaibigan.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to lending, usually money. The opposite of 'pangungutang' (borrowing).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iligal ang **pagpapautang** na may sobrang taas na interes o '5-6'.","translation":"The **act of lending** with excessively high interest or '5-6' is illegal."},{"sentence":"Naging hanapbuhay na niya ang **pagpapautang** sa kanyang mga kapitbahay.","translation":"**Lending** to his neighbors has become his livelihood."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng sigla, interes, o pagnanais na kumain o gawin ang isang bagay.
etymology: From Spanish 'ganado' (won/gained), but its meaning in Filipino is directly influenced by 'gana' (appetite, desire), also from Spanish.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're super pumped to do something, whether it's to work, to work out, or to attack a buffet. 'Walang preno, ganado!' Kapag may bonus, biglang ganado mag-trabaho. Kapag may bagong chismis, ganado makinig.
usage_notes: Can refer to an appetite for food or an enthusiasm for an activity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ganado** siyang mag-aral ngayong gabi dahil malapit na ang pagsusulit.","translation":"He is **motivated** to study tonight because the exam is near."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa masarap na ulam, **ganado** kumain ang mga bata.","translation":"Because of the delicious viand, the children are **eager to eat** (have a good appetite)."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang tao na madaling magalit, mainitin ang ulo, o hindi palangiti. Ginagamit din ito upang ilarawan ang masamang panahon.
original_explanation: Two main flavors: 1) Your boss before their morning coffee. That tita who always asks when you're getting married. Moody, irritable, and generally unapproachable. 2) The weather when it can't decide if it wants to be sunny or a super typhoon. Basically, 'bad trip' in person or weather form.
usage_notes: A very common word used for both people's moods and the weather.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kausapin si Ma'am, **masungit** siya ngayon.","translation":"Don't talk to Ma'am, she's **grumpy** today."},{"sentence":"**Masungit** ang panahon kaya't ipinagpaliban ang biyahe.","translation":"The weather is **inclement**, so the trip was postponed."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng katangian ng pagiging isang mabuting kaibigan; palakaibigan, madaling lapitan, at mabait sa kapwa.
original_explanation: Ito yung kaklase mo nung first day of school na unang bumati sa'yo. Sila yung kapitbahay na laging may "Good morning!" at ngiti. Basically, the human equivalent of a Golden Retriever—approachable, warm, and makes you feel welcome.
usage_notes: A very positive trait, synonymous with `palakaibigan`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala ang mga Pilipino sa pagiging **mapagkaibigan** sa mga dayuhan.","translation":"Filipinos are known for being **friendly** to foreigners."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **mapagkaibigan** na ugali, marami siyang naging kliyente.","translation":"Because of his **friendly** attitude, he gained many clients."}]

translation: a superstitious belief against siblings marrying in the same year
meaning_filipino: Isang pamahiin na nagbabawal sa magkapatid na magpakasal sa loob ng iisang taon dahil diumano'y magdudulot ito ng kamalasan sa isa sa kanila.
original_explanation: A classic Filipino superstition that causes major family drama and logistical nightmares for wedding planners. Two siblings can't get married in the same calendar year, or else one of them will have bad luck. It’s the ultimate "pili ka, ate o ako?" showdown, courtesy of your *lola's* beliefs. "Hindi kayo pwedeng ikasal this year, **sukob** kayo ng kapatid mo!"
usage_notes: Often used in the phrase "sukob sa taon". The word itself refers to the taboo or the state of being under this taboo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayon sa matatanda, masama raw ang **sukob** sa kasal.","translation":"According to the elders, the **taboo of siblings marrying in the same year** is bad."},{"sentence":"Ipinagpaliban nila ang kasal para maiwasan ang **sukob**.","translation":"They postponed the wedding to avoid the **curse/taboo**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang daglat para sa pariralang Ingles na "on the way," na nangangahulugang papunta na o nasa daan na.
original_explanation: The most common, most beautiful lie in the Philippines. When your friend says they're "OTW," it could mean anything from "I just woke up" to "I'm looking for parking" to "I'm actually on the way." Use with a grain of salt. Standard text/chat lingo.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in text messages and online chats. The pronunciation is either spelling out the letters "O-T-W" or phonetically as /o-te-we/.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Wait lang, **OTW** na ako!","translation":"Just wait, I'm **on the way**!"},{"sentence":"Nag-text siya, **OTW** na raw pero 30 minutes na ang nakalipas.","translation":"She texted, said she was **OTW**, but it's already been 30 minutes."}]

translation: scalded; steamed (cooked in its own juice)
meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pagluto kung saan ang isang sangkap, karaniwan ay hipon o alimango, ay pinakukuluan sa kaunting tubig-alat o sa sarili nitong katas hanggang sa maluto at maging kulay kahel.
original_explanation: The simplest, purest way to cook shrimp: "Halabos na Hipon." It's basically steaming the shrimp in a bit of salted water (or even just Sprite/7-Up!) until they turn bright orange. No fancy sauces, no complicated steps. It's the "I'm too lazy to cook but I want something delicious" method for seafood. It lets the natural sweetness of the shrimp shine.
usage_notes: Primarily used to describe a cooking method for crustaceans like shrimp and crabs. As a noun (`ang halabos`), it refers to the dish itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-uwi si tatay ng sariwang hipon at ginawa naming **halabos**.","translation":"Dad brought home fresh shrimp and we cooked it **steamed-style** (halabos)."},{"sentence":"Paborito kong pulutan ang **halabos** na hipon.","translation":"My favorite bar chow is **steamed** shrimp."}]

translation: to pant; to gasp for breath
meaning_filipino: Ang paghinga nang mabilis at malalim, karaniwan dahil sa pagod, takot, o matinding emosyon.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na hinabol mo 'yung huling byahe ng jeep tapos nakaalis na. You're left standing there, humahangos, defeated. Or 'yung late ka na sa morning shift mo sa BPO, tapos 'di pa gumagana 'yung elevator. Akyat-hagdan gaming, besh.
usage_notes: Often used to describe someone who has just finished running or is in a state of panic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Humangos** ang bata pagdating sa bahay matapos habulin ng aso.","translation":"The child was **gasping for breath** upon arriving home after being chased by a dog."},{"sentence":"Bakit ka **humahangos**?","translation":"Why are you **panting**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang direksyon o panig na katapat ng kaliwa; ang gawing kanan.
original_explanation: This is the formal, almost GPS-like way of saying 'sa kanan' (to the right). You'd use this if you were giving directions to a king or writing an old-timey novel. In modern traffic, you just shout, 'Kanan, Manong!' but 'pakakanan' is the version for your Lolo's Lolo.
usage_notes: Rarely used in modern conversation. 'Kanan' is the standard word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lumiko ang karwahe sa **pakakanan** na daan.","translation":"The carriage turned to the **right-hand** road."},{"sentence":"Ang dambana ay matatagpuan sa **pakakanan** ng ilog.","translation":"The shrine is located on the **right side** of the river."}]

translation: to add as an ingredient; to mix in
meaning_filipino: Idagdag o ihalo ang isang sangkap sa nilulutong pagkain.
original_explanation: This is what your nanay tells you to do with the carrots and potatoes when you're making menudo. It's the art of adding something to the mix, whether it's a vegetable in a soup or a new task to your already full workload. 'Bes, 'wag mo na ako i-sahog sa drama niyo, please.'
usage_notes: Used in a cooking context, but can also be used metaphorically to mean adding someone or something into a situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Isahog** mo na ang repolyo kapag kumukulo na ang sabaw.","translation":"**Add** the cabbage when the soup is boiling."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **isahog** ang personal na problema sa trabaho.","translation":"Don't **mix in** your personal problems with work."}]

meaning_filipino: Butil ng murang palay na sinangag at pagkatapos ay binayo o dinikdik upang maging pipi. Ginagamit sa paggawa ng mga kakanin.
original_explanation: The OG rice crispies, but make it Filipino. It's what happens when young, green rice gets roasted and then beaten up (literally, pounded). The result is this crunchy, fragrant, green flake that's amazing on top of ice cream, in hot chocolate, or in kakanin like espasol. It's the glow-up of `palay`.
usage_notes: Also commonly spelled as `pinipig`. Both refer to the same ingredient, a popular topping and component in Filipino desserts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap lagyan ng **pilipig** ang mainit na tsokolate.","translation":"It's delicious to add **pounded young rice** to hot chocolate."},{"sentence":"Ang halo-halo ay may sahog na ube, leche flan, at **pilipig**.","translation":"The halo-halo has ingredients like purple yam, custard flan, and **pounded young rice**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng pagiging maselan o mapili sa isang bagay; hindi basta-basta tumatanggap o kumukuha ng anuman.
etymology: Nagmula sa salitang-ugat na 'pili' at hulaping '-an'.
original_explanation: Yung kaibigan mong ayaw kumain sa karinderya. O yung tao na may checklist bago pumasok sa isang relasyon. High standards kumbaga, pero minsan, arte lang. 'Di naman masama maging pilian, basta 'wag lang aabot sa pagiging 'entitled'.
usage_notes: Maaari ring maging pandiwa na nangangahulugang 'pagpipilian' o 'lugar kung saan namimili'. Hal: "Ito ang pilian ng mga prutas."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masyado siyang **pilian** sa pagkain kaya laging gutom.","translation":"He is too **picky** with food, that's why he's always hungry."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang panghalip na paari na tumutukoy sa pangalawang panauhan (second person possessive). Ginagamit din bilang katumbas ng "ka" sa ilang konstruksyon ng pangungusap.
original_explanation: The shortest way to make something about someone else. "Crush mo ba ako?" is the ultimate test of friendship. Also, the other half of the iconic Filipino phrase "Ikaw at ako," which becomes "Tayo" but often ends up as "Wala na pala 'yung 'tayo' mo." It's possessive, literally.
usage_notes: It's a clitic pronoun, meaning it usually follows the word it modifies. It can mean "your" (as in "bahay mo" - your house) or act as the agent in certain verb forms ("kinain mo" - you ate).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasaan na ang libro **mo**?","translation":"Where is **your** book?"},{"sentence":"Nakita **mo** ba ang susi ko?","translation":"Did **you** see my key?"},{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng ngiti **mo**.","translation":"**Your** smile is beautiful."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng mamahaling bato o 'gemstone' na karaniwang may kulay na dilaw, ngunit maaari ring maging asul, rosas, o walang kulay.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "topacio" o Ingles na "topaz".
original_explanation: 'Yung birthstone ng mga taga-November. Akala mo dyamante pero hindi. It's that gemstone you see in jewelry stores that gives off a rich, warm, honey-like color. Parang kulay ng sunset sa Manila Bay, pero mas mahal.
usage_notes: Hinihiram nang direkta mula sa Ingles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang singsing niya ay may batong **topaz**.","translation":"Her ring has a **topaz** stone."},{"sentence":"Ang **topaz** ang 'birthstone' para sa buwan ng Nobyembre.","translation":"**Topaz** is the birthstone for the month of November."}]

translation: to be buried; to get stuck; to be in deep debt
meaning_filipino: Mailibing o matabunan ng lupa o iba pang bagay; malubog sa isang mahirap na kalagayan tulad ng utang.
original_explanation: This word has layers. Literally, it's getting your car stuck in mud ('mabaon sa putik'). Figuratively, it's what happens to your finances after buying everything on a 12.12 sale—'mabaon sa utang' (to be buried in debt). It's the feeling of being stuck deep in something you can't easily get out of.
usage_notes: Has both literal (buried/stuck) and figurative (debt/trouble) meanings. The root word 'baon' also means 'packed lunch/provisions', which is unrelated to this verb form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingat sa pagmamaneho, baka **mabaon** ang gulong mo sa putik.","translation":"Drive carefully, your tires might **get stuck** in the mud."},{"sentence":"Maraming Pilipino ang **nababaon** sa utang dahil sa taas ng bilihin.","translation":"Many Filipinos are **getting buried** in debt due to the high cost of goods."}]

translation: to rise (the sun); to become famous
meaning_filipino: Ang paglitaw ng araw sa silangan; ang pagiging kilala o tanyag ng isang tao.
original_explanation: The OG "glow up." Literally, it's what the sun does every morning. Figuratively, it's what happens to an artist, a vlogger, or even a meme that goes viral. One day they're unknown, the next day, "Wow, sumikat na si accla!" From sunrise to stardom.
usage_notes: A very common word with two primary, distinct meanings. The context usually makes it clear which one is intended.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumikat** na ang araw, kaya't kailangan na nating bumangon.","translation":"The sun has **risen**, so we need to get up now."},{"sentence":"Mula nang **sumikat** siya, marami na siyang naging proyekto.","translation":"Ever since she **became famous**, she has had many projects."}]

translation: A person from Pangasinan; the Pangasinan language
meaning_filipino: Isang taong katutubo o naninirahan sa lalawigan ng Pangasinan. Tumutukoy rin ito sa wikang sinasalita sa rehiyong iyon, na mas pormal na tinatawag na Pangasinense.
etymology: An exonym for the people and language of Pangasinan. The preferred endonym (term used by the people themselves) is `Pangasinense`.
original_explanation: This refers to both the awesome people from Pangasinan (home of the best bangus!) and their language. Fun fact: calling them "Pangalatok" can sometimes be seen as slightly informal or even pejorative by some; the more preferred term is "Pangasinense." It's like calling a British person a "Brit" – context matters.
usage_notes: The term `Pangasinense` is generally preferred as it is the official and more respectful term. `Pangalatok` is more colloquial and can be considered offensive by some individuals.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marunong siyang magsalita ng **Pangalatok** dahil doon siya lumaki.","translation":"He knows how to speak **Pangasinan** because he grew up there."},{"sentence":"Ang mga **Pangalatok** ay kilala sa kanilang masasarap na pagkain tulad ng bangus.","translation":"The **people of Pangasinan** are known for their delicious food like milkfish."}]

translation: to be blocked, to be intercepted
meaning_filipino: Mapigilan ang pagdaan o pagpapatuloy ng isang bagay o tao dahil sa isang hadlang.
original_explanation: What happens when you try to leave the office at exactly 5 PM and your boss suddenly says 'Upo ka muna, may urgent task.' You've been maharang. Also, what happens to your Grab delivery when it gets stuck in a checkpoint or EDSA traffic.
usage_notes: Can be used for physical blocking (a road) or for interception (a person, a message).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Baka **maharang** tayo sa checkpoint kung wala tayong dalang ID.","translation":"We might **be blocked** at the checkpoint if we don't bring an ID."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang tumakas pero **naharang** siya ng mga guwardiya sa gate.","translation":"He tried to escape but was **intercepted** by the guards at the gate."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging malinis, maayos, at nasa tamang lugar ng mga gamit. Ginagamit din sa pagliligpit ng mga pinagkainan sa mesa.
original_explanation: This is your mom's superpower. The ability to transform a chaotic room into a neat one. 'Pag sinabing "Mag-imis ka nga!", it means fix your life, starting with your messy bed or the plates you left on the dining table. The opposite of 'kalat'.
usage_notes: Ang anyong pandiwa na 'mag-imis' o 'imisin' (to tidy up) ay mas karaniwang ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na usapan kaysa sa pangngalan mismo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahanga-hanga ang **imis** ng kanyang kwarto.","translation":"The **tidiness** of her room is admirable."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos kumain, tulungan mo ako sa pag-**imis** ng mesa.","translation":"After eating, help me with clearing the table."}]

translation: is self-supporting; is providing for oneself
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging malaya sa pananalapi at pagtustos sa sariling mga pangangailangan nang hindi umaasa sa iba.
original_explanation: The adulting dream. You're paying your own bills, buying your own groceries, and funding your own milk tea addiction. You've graduated from 'palamunin' to 'breadwinner' (even if it's just for yourself). This is the 'Sana all' of every fresh grad stuck in a BPO night shift.
usage_notes: A common phrase to describe financial independence. 'Nagsusustento' is the present progressive form of 'magsustento'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit mahirap, masaya siyang **nagsusustento sa sarili**.","translation":"Even though it's difficult, she is happy **providing for herself**."},{"sentence":"Simula noong nagtrabaho siya, **nagsusustento na siya sa sarili** niya.","translation":"Ever since he started working, he has been **self-supporting**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng pagiging mapili o may partikular na pamantayan sa mga bagay-bagay.
original_explanation: This describes your friend who takes 30 minutes to decide what to order from GrabFood because "nothing looks good." They have a 100-point checklist for their "the one" and won't settle for less. It's having high standards, sometimes to a fault. In short, `magustuhin` is the official adjective for the "arte" or "pihikan" club.
usage_notes: Describes a person who is hard to please. It can have a slightly negative connotation, implying someone is overly selective.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masyado kang **magustuhin** sa pagkain, kaya ka nahihirapang pumili.","translation":"You are too **picky** with food, that's why you have a hard time choosing."},{"sentence":"Hindi naman sa **magustuhin** ako, pero may hinahanap lang akong partikular na katangian.","translation":"It's not that I'm **choosy**, but I'm just looking for a particular quality."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa paraan ng pagsasalita kung saan ang hangin ay lumalabas sa ilong, na nagreresulta sa isang tunog na parang 'ngongo'.
original_explanation: That voice you get when you have a bad cold (sipon). Also the default voice of every kontrabida tita in soap operas. 'I-kaw ay hi-ndi tu-nay na A-nak!' It's a voice that sounds like it's permanently stuck in traffic on EDSA.
usage_notes: This is a root word and an adjective describing a quality of voice. It's not a verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **humal** ang boses niya dahil sa matinding sipon.","translation":"His voice became **nasal** because of a bad cold."}]

translation: to persuade, to urge, to convince
meaning_filipino: Hikayatin o udyukan ang isang tao na gawin ang isang bagay sa paraang malumanay at mapang-akit.
original_explanation: This is the action of trying to get your friend to join your MLM scheme, or convincing your parents to let you go on a trip with your barkada. It's the art of the gentle push. 'Bes, sama ka na!' is the most common form of himukin.
usage_notes: A more gentle term than 'pilitin' (to force). It implies using reason or charm.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan kong **himukin** si Ana na sumali sa paligsahan.","translation":"I tried to **persuade** Ana to join the contest."},{"sentence":"**Himukin** mo ang iyong mga kapatid na mag-aral nang mabuti.","translation":"**Urge** your siblings to study well."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa balarila, isang anyo ng pandiwa na nagpapahayag ng pag-aalinlangan, posibilidad, kagustuhan, o isang sitwasyon na salungat sa katotohanan.
etymology: From 'panagano' (mood, from 'gano' related to 'paano') + 'pasakali' (conditional, from 'sakali'). A grammatical term.
original_explanation: This is the grammar mood for all your 'what ifs' and 'sana all' moments. It's the language of daydreaming, wishing, and hypothetical situations. 'Kung naging tayo lang...' – that's the subjunctive mood working its magic, or its heartache. It's the official mood of 'hugot'.
usage_notes: This is a technical term in Filipino grammar (Balarila). Not used in everyday conversation, but essential for linguistic studies.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan namin sa klase ang gamit ng **panaganong pasakali**.","translation":"We are studying the use of the **subjunctive mood** in class."},{"sentence":"Ang mga salitang 'sana', 'kung', at 'kapag' ay madalas gamitin sa **panaganong pasakali**.","translation":"The words 'sana' (I wish), 'kung' (if), and 'kapag' (when) are often used in the **subjunctive mood**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang daglat para sa pariralang Ingles na "out of character," na ginagamit sa mga laro (role-playing games) o sa social media upang ipahiwatig na ang isang pahayag ay mula sa tunay na tao at hindi sa karakter na ginagampanan.
etymology: From the English acronym 'OOC' (Out Of Character).
original_explanation: A term from the geeky depths of roleplaying and fanfiction that has gone mainstream. When your favorite 'alter' account on X (Twitter) suddenly tweets about their thesis, they'll add '(ooc)' to let you know they're breaking character. It's the digital equivalent of an actor taking off their wig and saying, 'Okay guys, real talk for a sec.'
usage_notes: Primarily used in online role-playing communities, fan fiction, and 'alter' or parody accounts on social media. Often enclosed in parentheses.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"(**ooc**: Guys, anong magandang kainan sa Baguio?)","translation":"(**ooc**: Guys, what's a good place to eat in Baguio?)"},{"sentence":"Sorry kung medyo seryoso ang tweet, **ooc** moment lang.","translation":"Sorry if the tweet is a bit serious, just an **out of character** moment."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sitwasyon kung saan ang isang tao ay may romantikong pagtingin sa kanyang kaibigan, ngunit ang kaibigan na ito ay nais lamang manatili sa antas ng pagkakaibigan.
original_explanation: The Bermuda Triangle of relationships. It's a place where romantic feelings go to die. You enter with hope, but you're stuck in a platonic purgatory where you're 'like a brother/sister to me.' The national capital of 'sana all' and 'hanggang tingin na lang.'
usage_notes: A very popular term in modern Filipino dating culture and hugot lines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mukhang napunta na naman ako sa **friendzone**.","translation":"It looks like I've landed in the **friend zone** again."},{"sentence":"Paano ba makakaalis sa **friendzone**?","translation":"How does one get out of the **friend zone**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malawak na lupain na tinutubuan ng matataas na damong talahib (Saccharum spontaneum).
etymology: From 'talahib' (cogon grass) + '-an' (locative suffix indicating a place).
original_explanation: The default setting for any Filipino horror movie scene or a dramatic music video. It's that itchy, scratchy field you had to run through as a kid. Also, a prime spot for secret lovers' trysts in old movies, or a place where snakes are probably judging your life choices.
usage_notes: Talahib (Saccharum spontaneum) is a specific type of tall, perennial grass.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtago ang mga bata sa gitna ng **talahiban**.","translation":"The children hid in the middle of the **cogon grass field**."},{"sentence":"Madalas masunog ang mga **talahiban** tuwing tag-init.","translation":"**Grasslands** often catch fire during the dry season."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tanyag na social media platform para sa pagbabahagi ng maiikling video.
etymology: From the brand name of the social media application.
original_explanation: The black hole of short-form videos where you go to 'just watch one' and suddenly it's 3 AM and you've learned a new dance, a pasta recipe, and three conspiracy theories. It's the modern 'tambayan' and the ultimate source of 'budol finds'.
usage_notes: Refers to the social media application. Usually capitalized. The stress is on the first syllable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-scroll lang ako sa **Tiktok** buong hapon kaya wala akong natapos.","translation":"I just scrolled on **TikTok** all afternoon, that's why I didn't finish anything."}]

translation: to cause to wobble; to make unstable
meaning_filipino: Gawing hindi matatag o hindi balanse ang isang bagay; paganahin o galawin nang paroo't parito.
original_explanation: What you do to the Jenga tower to mess with the next player. It's also what a toxic person does to your emotional stability. To 'pagiwangin' something is to shake its foundation, to make it wobble and threaten to fall, whether it's a table with a short leg or your will to finish your tasks on a Friday afternoon.
usage_notes: The object being made to wobble is the grammatical subject in this verb form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pagiwangin** ang mesa, matatapon ang kape.","translation":"Don't **make the table wobble**, the coffee will spill."},{"sentence":"**Pinagiwang** ng malakas na hangin ang tulay na kawayan.","translation":"The strong wind **caused the bamboo bridge to sway**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng posas o pangaw na karaniwang inilalagay sa paa o binti ng isang bilanggo upang hadlangan ang paggalaw.
original_explanation: Think old-school bilanggo vibes from a historical movie. This is the heavy metal cuff you put on someone's ankle, not the fluffy ones. It's a symbol of being physically trapped or held back, like how your student loans feel.
usage_notes: This is the less common meaning today compared to the gambling game. Often seen in historical contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga bilanggo ay may **sakla** sa kanilang mga paa.","translation":"The prisoners had **shackles** on their feet."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglikha ng musika gamit ang tinig na magaganap pa lamang sa malapit na hinaharap.
etymology: From the contemplative aspect verb form, reduplicating the first syllable of the root word: ka- + kanta.
original_explanation: The future tense of 'kanta' (sing). This is the warning your tita gives you at a family reunion before handing you the karaoke microphone. It’s the promise of every aspiring 'Tawag ng Tanghalan' contestant. 'Sa susunod na kabanata, kakanta na po ako.'
usage_notes: This is the contemplative (future) aspect of the verb 'kanta'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kakanta** ako ng paborito mong awit sa iyong kaarawan.","translation":"I **will sing** your favorite song on your birthday."},{"sentence":"Sino ang sunod na **kakanta** sa videoke?","translation":"Who **will sing** next on the videoke?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isinasailalim sa isang kasunduan kung saan ang isang ari-arian ay ipinagagamit sa iba kapalit ng regular na bayad o upa.
etymology: From 'upa' (rent), with the complex affix pa- + -in- + progressive reduplication.
original_explanation: That sign you see on an apartment gate or a condo unit that screams "This could be your new home... for a monthly fee." It's the landlord's favorite word and the tenant's constant reality. The state of 'for rent'.
usage_notes: Refers to the ongoing action of having something rented out by its owner. The object being rented out is the focus of the sentence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pinauupahan** ng pamilya ko ang lumang bahay sa probinsya.","translation":"My family **is renting out** the old house in the province."},{"sentence":"Magkano raw ang apartment na **pinauupahan** sa kanto?","translation":"How much is the apartment **being rented out** on the corner?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hindi sinasadyang pagbukas ng bibig kasabay ng malalim na paghinga, karaniwan ay senyales ng pagkaantok o pagkabagot.
original_explanation: The universal sign na 'low-batt' ka na, or 'boring ang kwento mo, bes.' It's your body's ninja move to get more oxygen to your brain, or a not-so-subtle hint to the meeting facilitator that it's time to wrap things up. Contagious af.
usage_notes: 'Humikab' is a more common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya napigilang **humigab** sa kalagitnaan ng klase.","translation":"He couldn't stop himself from **yawning** in the middle of the class."},{"sentence":"Takpan mo ang iyong bibig kapag **humihigab** ka.","translation":"Cover your mouth when you **yawn**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking gulong na umiikot nang patayo at may mga upuan para sa mga pasahero, karaniwang matatagpuan sa mga perya o amusement park.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "tíovivo" (merry-go-round, carousel), ngunit nagbago ng kahulugan sa Filipino upang tumukoy sa Ferris wheel.
original_explanation: The classic perya ride. It's romantic when you're at the top with your date, and terrifying when it stops and you're stuck swaying in the wind. The OG giant lantern of Pampanga before the giant lanterns.
usage_notes: In Spanish, "tíovivo" means carousel, but in the Philippines, 'tiyubibo' exclusively means Ferris wheel. The word for carousel is 'kabayuhan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Takot akong sumakay sa **tiyubibo** dahil mataas ito.","translation":"I'm afraid to ride the **Ferris wheel** because it's high."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit at naisusuot na orasan, karaniwang inilalagay sa pulso, na ginagamit upang malaman ang oras.
original_explanation: Ito yung pangarap mong bilhin pagka-sweldo, pero laging nauuwi sa "add to cart" lang. Accessory na nagsasabing "on time ako dapat" pero sa totoo lang, "Filipino time" pa rin ang nasusunod. Ang pormal na tawag ay 'relo'.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa impormal na pakikipag-usap o Taglish. Ang pormal na salita ay 'relo' o 'orasan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng bago mong **watch**! Saan mo nabili?","translation":"Your new **watch** is beautiful! Where did you buy it?"},{"sentence":"Nawala ko ang paborito kong **watch** kahapon.","translation":"I lost my favorite **watch** yesterday."}]

meaning_filipino: Maramihan ng munisyon; mga bala, bomba, at iba pang kagamitang pumuputok na ginagamit sa mga baril at artilerya.
original_explanation: The plural, more formal, and slightly more intimidating version of "munisyon." It sounds like you're talking about a whole arsenal, not just a few bullets. This is what the general in a movie would ask for a report on. "Ilang munisyones pa ang natitira?"
usage_notes: Plural of 'munisyon'. In modern usage, 'munisyon' is often used as both singular and plural, making 'munisyones' less common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang trak na puno ng mga **munisyones** ang naharang ng militar.","translation":"A truck full of **ammunitions** was intercepted by the military."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-iimbak ng mga **munisyones** ay mahigpit na ipinagbabawal.","translation":"The stockpiling of **ammunitions** is strictly prohibited."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang deklarasyon, pasalita man o pasulat, na hindi totoo o hindi wasto.
original_explanation: Yung sinabi mong 'on the way' ka na pero nasa banyo ka pa lang, that's a maling pahayag. Pwedeng kasuhan ng 'violation of friendship trust' yan. Also, fake news is the ultimate maling pahayag.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa mga pormal, legal, o peryodistikong konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinabulaanan ng opisyal ang **maling pahayag** na ibinabato laban sa kanya.","translation":"The official refuted the **false statement** being thrown against him."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa pagbibitiw ng **maling pahayag** dahil maaari itong magdulot ng gulo.","translation":"Be careful in making a **misstatement** as it can cause trouble."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglalagay o paglikha ng mga ukit o gatla na paikot (thread) sa isang tornilyo, tubo, o butas upang ito ay magkaroon ng kakayahang ikabit sa pamamagitan ng pagpihit.
original_explanation: This is what a plumber or a mekaniko does to a pipe or bolt. Imagine trying to screw something in, but it's smooth. *Roskasan* is the act of carving those spiral grooves onto it so it can actually connect. It's like giving a smooth-talker some actual points to make a connection. Without the *roskas*, it's just a smooth, useless piece of metal.
usage_notes: Used in mechanical, construction, or plumbing contexts. The root 'roskas' refers to the screw thread itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **roskasan** muna ang dulo ng tubo bago ito ikabit.","translation":"The end of the pipe needs **to be threaded** first before it can be attached."},{"sentence":"Sira na ang roskas, kaya hindi na maipasok. Kailangan itong **roskasan** ulit.","translation":"The thread is damaged, so it can't be inserted. It needs **to be re-threaded**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pagkahulog o pagkatanggal ng mga bagay na karaniwang nakakabit, tulad ng buhok, dahon, o talulot ng bulaklak.
original_explanation: Ito yung nangyayari sa buhok mo tuwing stress ka sa work o sa lovelife. O kaya sa mga puno sa UP Diliman pag 'autumn' na (kahit walang autumn sa Pinas). Yung feeling na isa-isang nawawala, parang pag-asa.
usage_notes: Often used for hair, leaves, petals, or feathers.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nalagas** ang mga dahon ng puno dahil sa malakas na hangin.","translation":"The tree's leaves **fell off** because of the strong wind."},{"sentence":"Sobrang stress ko na, halos **nalagas** na lahat ng buhok ko!","translation":"I'm so stressed, almost all my hair has **fallen off**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglalabas ng ihi mula sa katawan.
original_explanation: Let's be real, it means to pee, to take a leak, to answer the call of nature. The polite way to say "CR lang ako." The less polite, kid version is "jingle". When you've had too much milk tea, you'll need to do this a lot.
usage_notes: The standard and generally polite term for urination. More formal than 'jingle' but less clinical than 'pag-ihi'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sandali, **iihi** lang ako.","translation":"Wait, I just need to **urinate**."},{"sentence":"Bawal **umihi** dito.","translation":"It is forbidden to **urinate** here."}]

translation: in a rush; in a sudden, heavy flow
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa biglaan at sabay-sabay na pagdating o paggalaw ng maraming tao o bagay sa isang lugar.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'dagsa' (influx, surge) at ang unlaping 'pa-'.
original_explanation: Imagine a 12.12 sale on Shopee and everyone's orders arriving at the delivery hub at the same time. That's 'padagsa.' Or when it's rush hour and people pour out of the MRT station like a human waterfall. It implies a sudden, overwhelming, and slightly chaotic influx. Not a trickle, but a flood.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang mga pulutong ng tao, mga order, o mga pagdating.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Padagsa** ang dating ng mga turista tuwing Pasko.","translation":"The arrival of tourists is **a sudden rush** during Christmas."}]

translation: to become arrogant; to act proud
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita ng labis na pagmamataas o pag-iisip na nakahihigit sa iba.
etymology: From 'magpa-' (reflexive/stative prefix) + 'lalo' (more). The sense is 'to make oneself more (than others).'
original_explanation: This is that character arc when someone gets a little bit of success—a promotion, a viral TikTok video, a new iPhone—and suddenly they're too good for everyone. They start acting 'big time.' It's the transformation into a mayabang. 'Lumaki ang ulo' is the state, 'magpalalo' is the act of getting there.
usage_notes: Carries a strong negative connotation, implying an unattractive display of pride.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nang siya ay yumaman, nagsimula siyang **magpalalo** sa kanyang mga dating kaibigan.","translation":"When he got rich, he started to **act arrogant** towards his old friends."}]

translation: to sprawl or lie down lazily and repeatedly
meaning_filipino: Paulit-ulit at walang-ingat na paghiga o paghilata sa kung saan-saan.
etymology: From 'hilata' (to sprawl) with the -um- infix and reduplication of the first two syllables of the root.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na pagod ka from doing nothing, so you just plop down anywhere, get up, then plop down somewhere else. Parang pusa na laging naghahanap ng bagong spot na hihigaan sa bahay. This is peak "tamad" energy.
usage_notes: Describes a repeated or habitual action of sprawling lazily. It has a slightly more negative or lazy connotation than just 'humilata'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng Pasko, puro **humila-hilata** na lang siya sa sofa sa sobrang kabusugan.","translation":"After Christmas, he just kept **sprawling lazily** on the sofa from being so full."},{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na 'yang pag-**humila-hilata** mo diyan at tulungan mo ako maglinis.","translation":"Stop your **repeatedly lying around** there and help me clean."}]

translation: the act of swooping down; a sudden attack
meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis at biglaang pagsugod o paglusob, karaniwan ay mula sa itaas, na may layuning manakit o kumuha ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is what a hawk does to a poor, unsuspecting sisiw. It's also what you do to the last piece of lechon at a fiesta. A sudden, swift, and decisive attack. In the office, it's that coworker who swoops in to take credit for your idea.
usage_notes: A very descriptive and somewhat archaic word. Often used in literary or formal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagulat ang mga sisiw sa biglaang **paghandulong** ng lawin.","translation":"The chicks were startled by the sudden **swoop** of the hawk."},{"sentence":"Ang **paghandulong** ng mga mandirigma ay ikinagapi ng mga kalaban.","translation":"The **sudden attack** of the warriors caused the enemies to fall."}]

translation: to lift, to raise, to uplift
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtaas o pag-angat ng isang bagay mula sa kinalalagyan nito; pagpapabuti sa estado o kalagayan ng isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: It's like 'iakiat' but more versatile. You can 'iangat' a box, but you can also 'iangat' someone's spirit (uplift). It's also what you do to your crush's 'galing'—"I-angat ang bangko" means to praise someone excessively. "Tulungan nating **iangat** ang antas ng pamumuhay sa ating komunidad."
usage_notes: Has both literal (physical lifting) and figurative (improving a condition, uplifting morale) meanings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **iangat** ang iyong paa para makita ang sugat.","translation":"You need to **lift** your foot so we can see the wound."},{"sentence":"Layunin ng programa na **iangat** ang mga pamilyang naghihirap.","translation":"The program's goal is to **uplift** impoverished families."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng bahay na karaniwang may iisang palapag lamang at malawak na beranda.
etymology: From English "bungalow", which in turn is from Gujarati બંગલો (baṅglo), from Hindi बंगला (baṅglā, “Bengali-style house”).
original_explanation: The Tita's dream house. It's a one-story house, so no more 'sakit sa tuhod' moments climbing stairs. Perfect for retirement or for people who just hate cardio. It's the horizontal living goals.
usage_notes: A direct loanword from English, referring to a single-story house.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang magkaroon ng isang maliit na **bunggalo** sa tabi ng dagat.","translation":"She dreams of having a small **bungalow** by the sea."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi nagbabago; matatag; palagian.
original_explanation: This is like your "permanent" status sa work after regularization, or that friend na laging andyan, hindi seasonal. It's the opposite of "pa-fall" – consistent and stable. "Pirmi na ba 'yan?" is asking if it's the final decision, no take-backs.
usage_notes: Often used to describe something that is stable, unchanging, or a permanent fixture. Can function as an adjective or an adverb (palagi).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pirmi** ang kaniyang desisyon na manirahan sa probinsya.","translation":"His decision to live in the province is **permanent**."},{"sentence":"Siya ay **pirmi** na sa kaniyang trabaho bilang guro.","translation":"She is **fixed** in her job as a teacher."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malaking hipon na nabubuhay sa tubig-tabang.
original_explanation: The bigger, more 'sosyal' cousin of the hipon (shrimp) that you find in rivers and lakes, not the sea. It's the star of dishes like 'sinigang na ulang.' Think of it as the freshwater lobster for when you're feeling a bit fancy but still want that local flavor.
usage_notes: Often confused with 'hipon' (shrimp) or 'sugpo' (prawn/tiger prawn). 'Ulang' specifically refers to freshwater varieties.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap gawing sinigang ang **ulang**.","translation":"It's delicious to make sinigang with **crayfish**."},{"sentence":"Nakahuli sila ng malalaking **ulang** sa ilog.","translation":"They caught big **freshwater prawns** in the river."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marahas na pagpigil, pagkontrol, o pag-abuso sa kapangyarihan laban sa mga karapatan, kalayaan, o pag-aalsa ng isang tao o grupo.
original_explanation: This is when 'the man' keeps you down. Think of a super strict condo admin who won't let you have pets, visitors after 10 PM, or breathe too loudly. On a serious note, it’s about the abuse of power to silence dissent, like a villain in a historical movie trying to crush a rebellion.
usage_notes: A very strong and formal word, often used in political or historical contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinuligsa ng mga aktibista ang **panunupil** sa kalayaan sa pamamahayag.","translation":"The activists condemned the **suppression** of the freedom of the press."},{"sentence":"Ang kasaysayan ay puno ng mga kwento ng **panunupil** at pag-aalsa.","translation":"History is full of stories of **oppression** and rebellion."}]

translation: to become evil; to be intentionally bad
meaning_filipino: Sadyain ang pagiging masama o paggawa ng kasamaan; talikuran ang landas ng kabutihan.
etymology: From the prefix `magpaka-` (to deliberately cause oneself to be) and the root `sama` (bad, evil).
original_explanation: When the 'mabait' friend finally snaps. This is the villain origin story. After being taken for granted one too many times, you declare, "Sige, gusto niyo pala ng masama, edi magpapakasama na ako!" It’s the decision to finally stop being a doormat and start being the whole damn door.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa lahat ng panloloko sa kanya, nagbanta siyang **magpapakasama** na.","translation":"Because of all the deception he experienced, he threatened **to become evil**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **magpakasama** ka dahil lang sa galit.","translation":"Don't let yourself **become intentionally bad** just because of anger."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang unang bahagi o punto ng isang bagay, pangyayari, o panahon; pinagmulan.
original_explanation: This is the 'Chapter 1' of everything. The first day of class, the first episode of a K-drama, the 'Hi/Hello' that starts a new 'Marupok' cycle. It's the opposite of 'wakas' (the end). Every 'sana all' starts with a simula. It's the moment before everything gets complicated, messy, and beautiful.
usage_notes: Very common word. Can be used with 'umpisa' interchangeably. `Sa simula` means 'In the beginning'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap ang lahat ng bagay sa **simula**.","translation":"Everything is difficult in the **beginning**."},{"sentence":"Ito na ang **simula** ng ating bagong buhay.","translation":"This is the **start** of our new life."}]

translation: act of pressing or squeezing between two things; being cornered
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagiging naiipit o nasisiksik sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang bagay; ang kalagayan ng pagiging nasa mahirap na sitwasyon.
original_explanation: This is you during rush hour on the MRT, becoming one with the crowd. It's also that feeling when two of your friends are fighting and you're stuck in the middle. Financially, it's the "petsa de peligro" squeeze between your last peso and payday. Basically, being in a tight spot, literally or figuratively.
usage_notes: Can be used literally (physical squeezing) or figuratively (in a dilemma).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang **pag-ipit** ng kanyang kamay sa pinto.","translation":"He felt the **squeezing** of his hand in the door."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa **pag-ipit** ng sitwasyon, napilitan siyang mamili sa pagitan ng pamilya at trabaho.","translation":"Because of being **cornered** by the situation, he was forced to choose between family and work."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pampalamuting disenyo o panakip na karaniwang inilalagay sa itaas na bahagi ng bintana, kurtina, o sa gilid ng bubong.
original_explanation: That frilly, fancy border thingy you see on your lola's curtains, old-school jeepneys, or the eaves of a bahay na bato. It's the architectural equivalent of putting a cherry on top. It serves no real function but to say, 'I'm extra.'
usage_notes: Often associated with traditional Filipino architecture and interior design.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **senepa** ng kanilang lumang bahay ay yari sa matibay na kahoy.","translation":"The **valance** of their old house is made of sturdy wood."},{"sentence":"Nagkabit si nanay ng bagong **senepa** sa kurtina ng sala.","translation":"Mom installed a new **valance** on the living room curtain."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kulisap na may makintab at metalikong kulay, karaniwang berde o ginto, at madalas makita tuwing tag-ulan.
etymology: A compound word from an unknown first element 'sala-' and 'ginto' (gold), referring to its golden sheen.
original_explanation: The shiny, metallic green bug that kids in the province used to catch and tie a string to. It's the OG fidget spinner. Seeing one meant the rainy season was here, and you'd hear them buzzing around light bulbs at night.
usage_notes: A specific name for an insect, often associated with nostalgia for a rural childhood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakahuli ang mga bata ng maraming **salaginto** sa bukid.","translation":"The children caught many **June beetles** in the field."},{"sentence":"Kumikinang na parang **salaginto** ang kanyang damit na sequins.","translation":"Her sequined dress shines like a **June beetle**."}]

translation: obvious; obviously; done in a way that is noticeable
meaning_filipino: Isang kilos o paraan na hindi ikinukubli at sadyang ipinapakita o ipinapansin.
original_explanation: When you're trying to be subtle but failing spectacularly. That's pahalata. Like when you have a crush and you "accidentally" walk by their desk 17 times. Or when you're 'tampo' and you slam the door just a little too loudly. It's the art of making something known without saying it directly, but everyone gets the message anyway. "Uy, 'wag kang pahalata na may gusto ka sa kanya!"
usage_notes: Can function as an adjective describing a person/action, or an adverb modifying a verb. Often used as a command or observation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masyado kang **pahalata**, alam na ng lahat na ikaw ang kumuha ng cake.","translation":"You're too **obvious**, everyone already knows you're the one who took the cake."},{"sentence":"Nag-iwan siya ng mga pahiwatig na **pahalata** na aalis na siya sa kumpanya.","translation":"He left **obvious** hints that he was leaving the company."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagpapalitan ng mga produkto, serbisyo, o kalakal sa pagitan ng mga tao, kumpanya, o bansa.
etymology: From pakiki- (reciprocal action) + pag- (action noun) + kalakal (trade, goods).
original_explanation: The OG "add to cart" and "check out" before Shopee and Lazada existed. This is basically business—buying, selling, importing, exporting. Think of the Galleon Trade, but make it modern: China-made goods in Divisoria, a BPO company servicing US clients, or you selling your pre-loved items on Carousell.
usage_notes: A formal term used in business, economics, and history.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinalakas ng bagong kasunduan ang **pakikipagkalakalan** sa pagitan ng dalawang bansa.","translation":"The new treaty strengthened the **trade** between the two countries."},{"sentence":"Ang malayang **pakikipagkalakalan** ay may mabuti at masamang epekto sa lokal na industriya.","translation":"Free **commerce** has good and bad effects on the local industry."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto o proseso ng pagpigil, paglupig, o pagpuksa sa isang bagay na lumalaganap o nagdudulot ng pinsala, tulad ng sakit, krimen, o rebelyon.
original_explanation: This is the government's favorite word during a crisis. 'Pagsugpo sa droga,' 'pagsugpo sa kahirapan,' 'pagsugpo sa fake news.' It's the official term for 'let's try to fix this mess,' whether it's a disease outbreak or your tita's endless chismis.
usage_notes: Often used in formal contexts like news reports, government announcements, and public health campaigns.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang kooperasyon ng lahat para sa **pagsugpo** sa pagkalat ng sakit.","translation":"Everyone's cooperation is important for the **suppression** of the disease's spread."},{"sentence":"Ang programa ay naglalayong tulungan ang **pagsugpo** sa kriminalidad sa lungsod.","translation":"The program aims to help in the **control** of crime in the city."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit at mabilis na pagpikit at pagdilat ng mga mata; o ang pag-andar at pagpatay ng ilaw nang sunod-sunod.
etymology: From mag- (verb-forming prefix) + -ki- (reduplication of the first syllable, indicating repeated action) + kisap (blink/flicker).
original_explanation: This is what your eyes do when something gets in them, or what a faulty fluorescent light does before it finally gives up. It's that annoying, rapid on-and-off state, whether it's your eyelids or the bumbilya in your office.
usage_notes: The 'magki-' prefix here implies a repetitive or continuous action, not future tense. It differs from 'kumurap' (a single blink) or 'kikindat' (will wink).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **magkikisap** ang ilaw sa kisame bago tuluyang namatay.","translation":"The light on the ceiling started **to flicker** before it completely went out."},{"sentence":"Napuwing yata siya kaya **nagkikisap** ang kanyang mga mata.","translation":"Something might have gotten into his eye, that's why his eyes are **blinking repeatedly**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-arte o pagpapakita ng isang bagay na hindi totoo o hindi tunay na nararamdaman.
etymology: From `pag-` + `pa-` + `kunwari` (pretense, as if). The double `pa-` indicates the act of causing or making someone pretend.
original_explanation: That thing you do when your Tita asks if you're okay and you say "yes po" but deep inside you're one breakdown away from a major life crisis. It's the "I'm fine" of the Filipino emotional dictionary. The art of putting on a brave face, or pretending you actually like your officemate's adobo.
usage_notes: Often used to describe feigning emotions or situations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na ang iyong **pagpapakunwari**, alam kong nasasaktan ka.","translation":"Stop your **pretense**, I know you are hurting."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapakunwari** niya na masaya ay hindi nakumbinsi ang kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"Her **act of pretending** to be happy did not convince her parents."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng isang bagay na labag sa batas, moralidad, o kautusang panrelihiyon.
original_explanation: The feeling you get when you eat that extra cup of rice while on a diet. Or when you tell your mom you're on your way but you're just getting out of the shower. It's the act of doing something you know is wrong, from minor 'white lies' to major 'huli ka, balbon!' moments.
usage_notes: Has strong moral and religious connotations, but can also be used for secular faults or errors.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Aminado siyang siya ay **nagkakasala** sa kanyang kapwa.","translation":"He admits that he is **sinning** against his fellow men."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang matakot na umamin kung sa tingin mo ay **nagkakasala** ka.","translation":"Don't be afraid to admit it if you think you are **committing a fault**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong may matinding paghanga o pagsuporta sa isang partikular na tao, pangkat, o bagay, lalo na sa larangan ng sining, isports, o aliwan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Ingles na "fan," na pinaikling anyo ng "fanatic."
original_explanation: Ito yung taong handang magpuyat para sa livestream, mag-ipon ng merch, at makipag-bardagulan online para sa idol nila. Sila yung nagbibigay ng 'power' sa mga artista, K-pop group, o kahit sa paborito nilang basketball team. From 'fanatic'.
usage_notes: Ginagamit nang malawakan sa Pilipinas, lalo na sa konteksto ng showbiz at K-Pop.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bilang isang **fan**, lahat ng album ng paborito niyang banda ay binili niya.","translation":"As a **fan**, she bought all the albums of her favorite band."},{"sentence":"Grabe ang suporta ng mga **fan** sa concert kagabi.","translation":"The support from the **fans** at the concert last night was incredible."}]

translation: to get dressed; to wear clothes
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsusuot ng kasuotan sa katawan upang takpan ito.
original_explanation: The daily struggle of choosing your OOTD (Outfit Of The Day). Before you can post that 'fit check' video, you first have to magdamit. It's the first step to adulting every morning.
usage_notes: "Magbihis" is a more common synonym for "to get dressed" or "to change clothes". "Magdamit" can sometimes imply the general act of wearing clothes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinuruan ng ina ang kanyang anak kung paano **magdamit** nang mag-isa.","translation":"The mother taught her child how to **get dressed** by herself."},{"sentence":"Kahit nasa bahay lang, dapat pa ring **magdamit** nang maayos.","translation":"Even if you're just at home, you should still **dress** properly."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal para sa "takot".
etymology: From 'takot' (scared), with syllables reversed ('kot-ta') and playfully altered to 'shokot', a common pattern in Filipino gay lingo (Swardspeak).
original_explanation: Gay lingo for 'takot'. It's 'takot' but make it fabulous. You say this when you're scared but you still want to sound chic. 'Shokot ako sa multo, mars!' (I'm scared of ghosts, girl!). It's the fear you feel when your boss messages you 'Can we talk?'
usage_notes: Primarily used in informal conversations and gay lingo (Swardspeak).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mars, **shokot** na akong buksan ang electric bill ko.","translation":"Girl, I'm **scared** to open my electric bill."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang ma-**shokot**, hindi naman nangangagat 'yan.","translation":"Don't be **scared**, it doesn't bite."}]

translation: to take a life; to kill
meaning_filipino: Ang sinasadyang pagwawakas sa buhay ng isang tao o nilalang.
original_explanation: This is the formal, almost biblical way of saying "to kill." You'd hear this in a very serious news report or a historical drama. It's not what you'd say when you see a dead cockroach. "Pinatay" is the everyday version; "kitlan ng buhay" is for when you need to sound like you're writing a legal document or a telenovela script.
usage_notes: A very formal and somewhat literary phrase for "to kill". Often used in legal contexts, news reports about crimes, or historical narratives.
