meaning_filipino: Isang tao na lumilikha, nagho-host, o naglalabas ng mga audio file na tinatawag na podcast, na karaniwang pinakikinggan sa internet.
original_explanation: The modern 'chismoso/chismosa' but with a microphone, a Spotify account, and a sponsor. They're the ones filling your commute with everything from 'hugot' stories and true crime to financial advice you'll probably forget by the time you get to the office.
usage_notes: A direct loanword that has been fully adopted into modern Filipino vocabulary, especially among millennials and Gen Z.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang maging isang sikat na **podcaster** sa Pilipinas.","translation":"Her dream is to become a famous **podcaster** in the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Maraming sikat na komedyante ngayon ay mga **podcaster** na rin.","translation":"Many famous comedians nowadays are also **podcasters**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sining o gawain ng pag-aalaga at pagpapalago ng mga halaman, tulad ng mga bulaklak, gulay, o palamuti.
etymology: From 'halaman' (plant). The 'pag-ha-' prefix denotes the act or practice of something.
original_explanation: The official hobby of every 'plantita' and 'plantito' during the pandemic lockdown. It's the therapeutic act of talking to your succulents, giving your monstera a prime spot by the window, and panicking when a leaf turns yellow. Your wallet might cry from all the pots and soil, but your heart (and your IG feed) is happy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging libangan ng marami ang **paghahalaman** noong panahon ng pandemya.","translation":"**Gardening** became a hobby for many during the pandemic."},{"sentence":"May benepisyong pangkalusugan ang **paghahalaman**, tulad ng pagbabawas ng stress.","translation":"**Gardening** has health benefits, like reducing stress."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa alanganing sitwasyon kung saan maaaring masira ang reputasyon o integridad; may pananagutan o pangako sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: This word has two vibes. 1) Your data is komprometido kapag na-hack ang account mo. Your principles are komprometido if you do something shady for money. 2) On the flip side, it can mean you're taken. 'Sorry, komprometido na ako,' means 'I'm already committed,' a classy way to say you're in a relationship.
usage_notes: Has a dual meaning: negative (compromised, at risk) and neutral/positive (committed, engaged). Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **komprometido** ang seguridad ng gusali matapos ang pagnanakaw.","translation":"The building's security was **compromised** after the theft."},{"sentence":"Bilang isang lalaking may asawa, **komprometido** na siya.","translation":"As a married man, he is already **committed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang natural na proseso ng paghuhunos o pagpapalit ng balat ng ilang hayop, tulad ng ahas at alimango.
original_explanation: The animal kingdom's version of 'new year, new me'. It's when a snake decides its current outfit is so last season and sheds it for a fresh new look. It's a glow-up, but for reptiles and crustaceans.
usage_notes: Primarily used in a biological context for animals like snakes and crabs.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pag-upas** ng ahas ay isang palatandaan ng paglaki nito.","translation":"The **molting** of a snake is a sign of its growth."},{"sentence":"Nakatagpo kami ng lumang balat ng ahas, resulta ng **pag-upas** nito.","translation":"We found an old snake skin, a result of its **shedding**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagsira o paghadlang sa panliligaw ng isang tao, kadalasan ay ginagawa ng isang kaibigan o karibal.
etymology: A playful extension of 'torpe'. The idea is that you are 'torpedoing' or sinking their romantic chances.
original_explanation: In Pinoy slang, this is when you try to help a 'torpe' friend court someone, but you mess it up so badly you ruin their chances. Or worse, when you intentionally sabotage their efforts. It's like being a wingman who crashes the plane.
usage_notes: This is a slang or colloquial term derived from 'torpe'. The verb can be conjugated ('Tinorpedo niya ako!'). The noun form for the person doing the action is also 'torpedo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong i-**torpedo** kay crush, pare!","translation":"Don't **sabotage my chances** with my crush, bro!"},{"sentence":"Siya ang **torpedo** sa grupo, laging sinisira ang diskarte ng iba.","translation":"He's the **saboteur** in the group, always ruining the others' moves."}]

meaning_filipino: Mayroong maraming layag; mahangin at angkop sa paglalayag.
original_explanation: Picture a classic pirate movie scene in the Philippines. The sea is perfect, the wind is just right, and all the vintas have their colorful sails up. That scene is malayag. It's the ideal condition for sailing, or for flying a kite at the Luneta park.
usage_notes: Primarily used in contexts related to sailing, the sea, or wind. Can be used literally (many sails) or descriptively (windy for sailing).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **malayag** na barko ang dumaong sa pantalan.","translation":"A ship **with many sails** docked at the port."},{"sentence":"**Malayag** ang karagatan ngayon kaya maganda ang takbo ng aming bangka.","translation":"The sea is **windy** today so our boat is running well."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na may kaugnayan sa dugo o kamag-anak; kadugo.
original_explanation: This is the 'flesh and blood' connection. Your 'karugo' are the people you're related to by blood, not just by choice or Wi-Fi password sharing. It's the ultimate 'kadugo' or 'kapamilya' label, the one you can't unfriend on Facebook.
usage_notes: 'Kadugo' is a more common variant. Can be used as an adjective ('karugo niya') or a noun ('isang karugo').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit sila nag-aaway, magpinsan sila at **karugo**.","translation":"Even if they fight, they are cousins and **blood relatives**."},{"sentence":"Hinanap niya ang kanyang mga **karugo** sa probinsya.","translation":"He searched for his **blood relatives** in the province."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang makalangit na katawan na binubuo ng yelo, alikabok, at bato na umiikot sa araw, at nagkakaroon ng mahabang buntot kapag malapit dito.
original_explanation: The drama queen of the solar system. It shows up, makes a big, flashy scene with its tail, and then disappears for years, leaving everyone wondering when it'll be back. Basically the celestial equivalent of a celebrity who only appears for major events.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang bihirang pagkakataon na makakita ng **kometa** sa kalangitan.","translation":"It's a rare opportunity to see a **comet** in the sky."},{"sentence":"Pinangalanan ang **kometa** sa astronomong nakatuklas nito.","translation":"The **comet** was named after the astronomer who discovered it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang impormal at pinaikling katawagan para sa "sister," na ginagamit bilang pantawag sa isang babae, kaibigan man o hindi kilala, bilang tanda ng pakikipagkapwa.
etymology: Pinaikling anyo ng salitang Ingles na "sister".
original_explanation: The go-to term of address for every girl, ate, tita, or even the saleslady at the department store. It's the shorter, cooler, and more text-friendly version of "sister" or "ate". "Siz, magkano 'to?" is the national anthem of every shopper. It's friendly, casual, and universally understood in the modern Pinoy landscape.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa social media, text messages, at sa mga impormal na usapan. Bahagi ng "beki lingo" o gay lingo ngunit naging mainstream na.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hi **siz**, anong balita sa'yo?","translation":"Hi **sis**, what's new with you?"},{"sentence":"**Siz**, pa-DM naman ng price.","translation":"**Sis**, please DM me the price."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal para sa multo o espiritu ng isang yumaong tao.
etymology: Isang pambata o pinalambot na pagbigkas ng salitang "multo".
original_explanation: Your friendly neighborhood ghost. It's the cuter, less terrifying way to say 'multo'. Parang Casper the Friendly Ghost, hindi yung white lady sa Balete Drive. Kids use this a lot. 'May mumo sa ilalim ng kama ko!'
usage_notes: Itinuturing na salitang balbal o pambata.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natatakot ang bata dahil may **mumo** raw sa kanyang kuwarto.","translation":"The child is scared because they say there's a **ghost** in their room."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala diyan, walang **mumo** dito.","translation":"Don't believe that, there are no **ghosts** here."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lugar o istraktura sa isang expressway kung saan isinasagawa ang pagbabayad at pagkolekta ng toll fee.
original_explanation: The finish line of one traffic jam and the starting line of the next. Dito mo malalaman kung valid pa ba ang RFID load mo or if you're about to be *that person* holding up the entire line. Pro-tip: Smile at the attendant, their job is tough.
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang termino para sa sinumang naglalakbay sa mga expressway.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahaba ang pila sa **tollgate** tuwing long weekend.","translation":"The line at the **tollgate** is long during long weekends."},{"sentence":"Nalaglag ko ang resibo ko sa **tollgate**.","translation":"I dropped my receipt at the **tollgate**."}]

translation: to rescue; to succor; to aid
meaning_filipino: Magbigay ng tulong o saklolo sa isang taong nasa panganib o kagipitan.
original_explanation: Ito yung ginagawa ng best friend mo kapag na-ghost ka ng ka-date mo at kailangan mo ng karamay with matching ice cream. O kaya yung pagdating ng GrabFood rider sa gitna ng gutom na gutom ka na. 'Isaklolo mo ako sa deadline na 'to, Lord!'
usage_notes: Often used in dramatic or urgent situations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **isaklolo** ang mga residenteng naipit sa baha.","translation":"The residents trapped in the flood need **to be rescued**."},{"sentence":"**Isinaklolo** niya ang kaibigang nalulunod sa utang.","translation":"He **rescued** his friend who was drowning in debt."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi pagtama sa target o layunin; isang pagkabigo.
etymology: Pinaniniwalaang nagmula sa salitang Espanyol na 'mentís' (nagsisinungaling ka), ngunit nagbago ang kahulugan sa Pilipinas bilang 'pagkabigo' o 'hindi pagtama'.
original_explanation: The feeling when you shoot your shot, but it doesn't even hit the backboard. It's when your joke doesn't land, your plan fails, or you miss the last piece of chicken joy. It's the universe saying, 'Try again, beshie.'
usage_notes: Maaari ring gamitin bilang pangngalan (isang mintis) o pang-uri (naging mintis).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sayang, **mintis** ang huling tira niya sa basketball.","translation":"Too bad, his last shot in basketball was a **miss**."},{"sentence":"Naging **mintis** ang lahat ng aming pagtatangka na kausapin siya.","translation":"All our attempts to talk to him were **unsuccessful**."}]

translation: to have someone say no; to forbid on someone's behalf
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-utos o pagsabi sa isang tao na tanggihan o huwag sumang-ayon sa isang bagay, lalo na kung ito ay para sa kapakanan ng iba.
original_explanation: This is a very specific, almost manipulative verb. It's when you tell someone to refuse something for you. "Kung tatawag si ex, **ipahindi** mo ako, sabihin mo tulog." You're basically outsourcing your "no." It's the ultimate 'paki-ghost' move.
usage_notes: This verb is often used in situations where a person uses another person (like a parent or a secretary) as the reason for refusal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinuruan niya ang bata na **ipahindi** ang alok ng mga hindi kilalang tao.","translation":"She taught the child to **refuse** offers from strangers (literally: to have a 'no' said)."},{"sentence":"Kung may mag-alok sa'yo ng alak, **ipahindi** mo sa akin; sabihin mong bawal ako uminom.","translation":"If someone offers you alcohol, **use me to refuse**; tell them I'm not allowed to drink."}]

translation: to man (a post), to attend to, to staff
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbantay, pag-asikaso, o pamamahala sa isang lugar, tulad ng tindahan o tanggapan; ang pagiging naroroon upang asikasuhin ang mga gawain o kliyente.
original_explanation: When your mom leaves for the market and says, 'Nak, ikaw muna ang **tumao** sa tindahan.' It means you're in charge, you're the person-in-charge for a while. It's your shift. Whether it's a sari-sari store or a booth at a convention, someone has to be there to run it.
usage_notes: Derived from 'tao' (person), it literally means 'to be the person' at a certain post or duty.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **tumao** sa opisina habang nasa pulong ang lahat?","translation":"Who **manned** the office while everyone was in a meeting?"},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong umuwi nang maaga kaya pinakiusapan ko si Ana na **tumao** muna sa puwesto ko.","translation":"I needed to go home early so I asked Ana to **attend to** my post for a while."}]

translation: to work, to function, to be effective
meaning_filipino: Maging epektibo o kumilos ayon sa inaasahan, tulad ng isang makina, plano, o gamot.
etymology: From the root 'gana' (function, appetite) with the infix '-um-'.
original_explanation: When something actually works. 'Gumana yung Wi-Fi!' is a cry of victory. 'Hindi gumana yung pick-up line ko' is a tragedy. It's the verb for when your brain finally starts working after your first cup of coffee or when a plan succeeds.
usage_notes: While 'gana' can also mean appetite, 'gumana' almost exclusively means 'to function' or 'to work'. To say 'to have an appetite', you'd say 'ganahan' or 'magkaroon ng gana'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **gumana** na ulit ang aircon!","translation":"Finally, the aircon is **working** again!"},{"sentence":"Hindi **gumana** ang plano namin kaya kailangan naming mag-isip ng iba.","translation":"Our plan didn't **work**, so we need to think of something else."}]

translation: to scatter; to sow; to spread
meaning_filipino: Ikalat o ihagis ang mga butil, pulbos, o anumang maliliit na bagay sa isang malawak na lugar.
original_explanation: Like a tita at a wedding throwing rice or flower petals. Or that friend who "scatters" good vibes (or gossip) everywhere they go. Can also be used for farmers sowing seeds, or for you accidentally dropping your bag and scattering its entire contents on the MRT floor during rush hour.
usage_notes: Can refer to literal scattering of objects or figurative spreading of information/influence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang magsasaka ay maagang gumising upang **magsabog** ng binhi sa bukid.","translation":"The farmer woke up early **to sow** seeds in the field."},{"sentence":"Pumunta siya sa entablado upang **magsabog** ng pera sa mga manonood.","translation":"He went on stage **to scatter** money to the audience."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi na tuloy; ipinawalang-bisa; itinigil o winakasan.
original_explanation: The most heartbreaking word for someone waiting for a flight, a concert, or a date. "Flight 5J 815 is... kanselado." In the age of social media, it's also what happens to a celebrity after a problematic tweet from 2010 is unearthed. "You're cancelled!" is the modern equivalent of being disowned by the internet.
usage_notes: Widely used for events, appointments, and now, people (in the context of 'cancel culture').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kanselado** ang klase bukas dahil sa bagyo.","translation":"Classes are **cancelled** tomorrow because of the typhoon."},{"sentence":"Ay, **kanselado** na pala ang lakad natin?","translation":"Oh, so our trip is **cancelled**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggaya o pagkuha ng isang bagay, ideya, o gawa mula sa orihinal na pinagmulan nito nang walang pahintulot o pagkilala.
original_explanation: The national pastime of students during exams. 'Copy-paste' lang sa homework ng classmate, or sa office, 'yung pag-imitate sa signature ng boss mo para sa delivery receipt. It's the art of being 'inspired by' without giving credit.
usage_notes: Can refer to copying text, ideas, actions, or even physical objects. The root word 'kopya' means 'a copy'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"\"Huwag kang **kumopya** sa katabi mo,\" babala ng guro.","translation":"\"Don't **copy** from your seatmate,\" the teacher warned."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **kumopya** ng istilo ng pananamit ng kanyang idolo.","translation":"He tried to **copy** the fashion style of his idol."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang propesyon o trabaho ay ang pagtahi o paggawa ng mga damit.
etymology: From 'maN-' + 'tahi' (sew), where the 'N' assimilates and the first syllable of the root is repeated.
original_explanation: The OG life-saver when your pants are too long, your uniform needs fixing, or you need a custom-made gown for JS prom. They are the wizards who can turn a piece of cloth into a work of art with just a sewing machine and a thread. Before Zara and H&M, there was the neighborhood mananahi.
usage_notes: A gender-neutral term, but 'modista' is often used for a female fashion designer/dressmaker and 'sastre' for a male tailor, especially for suits.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpagawa ako ng bagong bestida sa **mananahi**.","translation":"I had a new dress made by the **seamstress**."},{"sentence":"Magaling ang **mananahi** sa kanto, kaya laging puno ang kanyang patahian.","translation":"The **tailor** on the corner is good, that's why his shop is always full."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaloob ng kapangyarihan o awtoridad upang maging balido, epektibo, o maipatupad ang isang batas, kasunduan, o patakaran.
etymology: Compound verb from `magbigay` (to give) + `bisa` (effect, validity, power).
original_explanation: This is the official 'go' signal. It's when a rule, law, or contract becomes legit and starts working. When a law is signed, it's given power. When your manager approves your vacation leave, your request is validated. It's the action that turns a piece of paper or a digital request into a real, enforceable thing. It's the verb for 'It's official!'
usage_notes: Primarily used in legal, bureaucratic, or formal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lagda ng pangulo ang **magbibigay-bisa** sa bagong batas.","translation":"The president's signature **will give effect** to the new law."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng selyo ng notaryo upang **magbigay-bisa** sa kontrata.","translation":"A notary's seal is needed **to validate** the contract."}]

translation: to complete, to finish entirely, to make the most of
meaning_filipino: Gawing lubos o ganap; ubusin o tapusin ang isang bagay nang walang itinitira.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of going all-in. "Lulubusin ko na ang pagkain sa handaan" means you're going to finish off all the food at the party. "Lubusin mo na ang pag-aaral" is what your parents say when they want you to finish your degree with no interruptions. It's about seeing something through to the absolute end.
usage_notes: Often used in the imperative mood, telling someone to finish or complete something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lubusin** mo na ang iyong bakasyon at mag-relax ka nang husto.","translation":"**Make the most** of your vacation and relax completely."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong sayangin ang pagkakataon, **lubusin** mo na!","translation":"Don't waste the opportunity, **see it through to the end**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang trabaho ay gumapas o mag-ani ng mga pananim, lalo na ng palay, gamit ang isang karit o gapas.
original_explanation: The person who does the back-breaking work of harvesting rice stalks in the fields. They're the original OGs of 'grind,' working under the scorching sun to make sure we have unli-rice. Respect the manggagapas.
usage_notes: A specific term for a harvester who uses a scythe ('gapas'). Often associated with rice harvesting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maagang nagsimula sa bukid ang mga **manggagapas** upang matapos bago tumirik ang araw.","translation":"The **harvesters** started early in the field to finish before the sun got too high."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang pinsala sa katawan na nagiging sanhi ng pagkasira o pagkabukas ng balat o ibang bahagi ng katawan.
original_explanation: Pwedeng pisikal, like yung hiwa sa daliri mo nung nag-attempt kang magluto. Pwede ring emotional, like yung iniwan ng 'the one that got away.' Parehong masakit, parehong nag-iiwan ng peklat. Yung isa, kailangan ng Betadine. Yung isa, kailangan ng Tanduay at videoke.
usage_notes: Can refer to both physical and emotional wounds.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Linisin mo agad ang **sugat** mo para hindi maimpeksyon.","translation":"Clean your **wound** immediately so it doesn't get infected."},{"sentence":"Mahirap hilumin ang **sugat** na dulot ng pagtataksil.","translation":"It's hard to heal the **wound** caused by betrayal."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamataas o pinakamakapangyarihang hari sa lahat; ang pinuno ng mga hari.
original_explanation: The ultimate boss, the final boss, the CEO of all kings. Think Mufasa, not Scar. This isn't just any hari, this is the top dog, the one everyone else reports to. In modern terms, it's the title you'd give to the undisputed champion of something, like the 'Pinakahari ng Videoke.'
usage_notes: Often used in a figurative or grandiose sense, as well as in religious or historical contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinikilala siya bilang ang **pinakahari** ng mga manunulat sa kanyang panahon.","translation":"He is recognized as the **supreme king** of writers of his time."},{"sentence":"Ang leon ay tinaguriang **pinakahari** ng gubat.","translation":"The lion is called the **king of kings** of the jungle."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsunod sa kung ano ang popular o napapanahon sa isang partikular na sandali, lalo na sa moda, teknolohiya, o kultura.
etymology: From "maki-" (social verb prefix) + "uso" (in trend, fashionable, from Spanish 'uso' meaning 'use').
original_explanation: When you see everyone doing the latest TikTok dance, wearing the same style of pants, or using a new slang word, and you decide to join in, that's "makiuso". It's the fear of missing out (FOMO) in verb form. "Uy, milk tea na naman? Makiuso lang, besh?"
usage_notes: Can be used neutrally, but sometimes carries a slightly negative connotation of being unoriginal or just a follower.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang basta-basta **makiuso** kung hindi mo naman talaga gusto.","translation":"Don't just **follow the trend** if you don't really like it."},{"sentence":"Lahat ng kaibigan ko ay naglalaro ng bagong video game, kaya **makiuso** na rin ako.","translation":"All my friends are playing the new video game, so I decided to **join the trend** as well."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghaharang o pagsikip sa isang daluyan na nagiging sanhi ng pagtigil ng agos.
original_explanation: What happens to your kitchen sink after your roommate 'washes' the oily pans. What happens to EDSA at 5 PM. What happens to your brain during an exam when you can't think of the answer. Anything that gets stuck and stops the flow? Yan, 'bumara' na.
usage_notes: Used for physical blockages (pipes, roads) and can be used metaphorically for mental blocks.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumara** ang lababo dahil sa mga natirang pagkain.","translation":"The sink **got clogged** because of leftover food."},{"sentence":"Isang aksidente ang **bumara** sa daloy ng trapiko sa NLEX.","translation":"An accident **blocked** the flow of traffic on NLEX."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-aalis o pagbura ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay datos o impormasyon sa isang elektronikong kagamitan. Ito ay nasa pangkasalukuyang anyo.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa mo sa picture niyo ng ex mo. Isa-isa, walang tinitira. Also, the state of your phone memory when you realize you've downloaded too many K-dramas. "Nagdedelete na ako ng files para magkasya 'yung bagong episode."
usage_notes: A Tagalized verb in the present progressive tense, formed with the mag- prefix and reduplication of the first syllable of the root word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagdedelete** ako ng mga lumang mensahe para lumuwag ang espasyo sa aking telepono.","translation":"I am **deleting** old messages to free up space on my phone."},{"sentence":"Bakit ka **nagdedelete** ng comment? May tinatago ka ba?","translation":"Why are you **deleting** the comment? Are you hiding something?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng prutas na sitrus, karaniwang kulay dilaw, maasim ang lasa, at ginagamit sa pagluluto at paggawa ng inumin.
original_explanation: The OG sourpuss of fruits. Before calamansi became the national sawsawan king, limon was there. It's what you use when you want to feel a bit fancy, like adding it to your water or gin and tonic. It's the "conyo" cousin of calamansi.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with the local 'dalanghita' or 'dayap' in some contexts, but 'limon' specifically refers to the yellow lemon (Citrus limon).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maghiwa ka ng **limon** para sa iced tea.","translation":"Slice a **lemon** for the iced tea."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang manok kung pinigaan ng **limon** bago iluto.","translation":"The chicken is delicious if you squeeze **lemon** on it before cooking."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng likidong preparasyon na may sangkap na pampahid sa balat upang ito ay lumambot, pumuti, o maprotektahan laban sa araw.
original_explanation: Ang best friend mo 'pag feeling mo dry na ang skin mo na parang disyerto. May pampaputi, may pampakinis, at may pang-alis ng 'ashiness' sa siko at tuhod. Essential 'to lalo na 'pag aircon ang office at feeling mo nagiging chicharon na ang balat mo.
usage_notes: The English word 'lotion' is also very commonly used, often interchangeably.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maglagay ka ng **losyon** pagkatapos maligo para hindi manuyo ang iyong balat.","translation":"Apply **lotion** after taking a bath so your skin doesn't get dry."},{"sentence":"Amoy pa lang ng **losyon** niya, alam mo nang bagong ligo.","translation":"Just from the scent of his/her **lotion**, you know he/she just took a bath."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-inom ng gamot upang alisin ang mga bulate o parasito sa katawan. Maaari ring tumukoy sa pag-alis ng mga hindi kanais-nais na elemento sa isang grupo o sistema.
original_explanation: Medically, it's what you do to your pets (or kids, back in the day) to get rid of worms. "Time to magpurga the askals!" Metaphorically, it's what a company does during a layoff, or what you do to your friends list after a major drama. "Need to magpurga my social media, daming toxic."
usage_notes: Can be used in a medical or a metaphorical/political context (e.g., a political purge).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinayuhan ng doktor ang mga bata na **magpurga** dalawang beses sa isang taon.","translation":"The doctor advised the children to **deworm** twice a year."},{"sentence":"Nais ng bagong lider na **magpurga** ng mga tiwaling opisyal sa gobyerno.","translation":"The new leader wants to **purge** corrupt officials from the government."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lugar o destinasyon na balak tunguhin o puntahan. Ginagamit din bilang pandiwa na tumutukoy sa aksyon ng pagtungo sa isang bagay o lugar.
original_explanation: This is the "where" in "where are we going?". It's the pin on your Grab app, the beach in your travel plans, the name of the resto you've been craving. It's the destination of your 'pupunta' action.
usage_notes: Object-focus verb, future tense. The object is the place being gone to. It can also function as a noun meaning 'destination'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Boracay ang **pupuntahan** namin sa bakasyon.","translation":"Boracay is the place we **will go to** for vacation."},{"sentence":"**Pupuntahan** kita sa bahay ninyo bukas.","translation":"I **will go to** you at your house tomorrow."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa sinaunang lipunang Tagalog, tumutukoy ito sa uri ng mga malayang tao (freemen) na may-ari ng lupa at may karapatang hindi magbayad ng buwis sa datu, ngunit may tungkuling sumama sa digmaan. Sa modernong gamit, ito ay nangangahulugang marangal, aristokrata, o kabilang sa mataas na lipunan.
etymology: From Sanskrit 'maharddhika', meaning 'man of wealth, wisdom, and power'.
original_explanation: Historically, they were the warrior-freeman class, not exactly royalty, but definitely not 'alipin'. Fast forward, it's been co-opted to mean 'noble' or 'royal,' like the 'Maharlika Highway.' It's that word you use when you want to sound deep and nationalistic. It has that 'old-school cool' vibe, but its actual historical meaning is more complex than just 'royalty.'
usage_notes: A historically significant word whose modern meaning has shifted towards a more general sense of 'nobility' or 'aristocracy.' Used in both historical contexts and modern branding/naming.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **maharlika** ay isang mahalagang bahagi ng sinaunang lipunan sa Pilipinas.","translation":"The **maharlika** were an important class in ancient Philippine society."},{"sentence":"Ipinangalan sa kanya ang kalsada bilang pagkilala sa kanyang **maharlika** na pagkatao.","translation":"The road was named after him in recognition of his **noble** character."}]

translation: that's the one; that very one
meaning_filipino: Ginagamit upang bigyang-diin o tukuyin nang may kasiguruhan ang isang bagay na malapit sa kausap.
original_explanation: The 'Bingo!' or 'That's it!' of pointing things out. When your friend is describing a person across the room and you finally spot them, you say, 'Iyang-iyan ang sinasabi ko!' It's the upgraded, high-definition, 4K version of 'iyan' (that). Used with 100% certainty, no refunds.
usage_notes: Emphatic form of 'iyan' (that, near the listener). It stresses that the object/person is precisely the one being referred to.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Iyang-iyan** ang damit na nakita ko sa mall kahapon!","translation":"**That's the very** dress I saw at the mall yesterday!"},{"sentence":"A: \"Alin dito ang gusto mo?\" B: \"**Iyang-iyan**! Ang kulay asul.\"","translation":"A: \"Which one here do you like?\" B: \"**That's the one**! The blue one.\""}]

meaning_filipino: Pagkilos nang agaran at madalian, na madalas ay hindi isinasaalang-alang ang iba; pag-uunahan.
original_explanation: This is the "no-respect-for-the-line" move. Picture a buffet and someone just goes for it, piling their plate high before others get a chance. That's una-una. It's the kiasu attitude in the wild. "Hoy, 'wag kang una-una, may pila!"
usage_notes: Nagdadala ng bahagyang negatibong konotasyon ng pagiging makasarili o pagmamadali nang walang kaayusan. Madalas gamitin kasama ng pandiwa, hal., 'nag-uuna-una'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-**una-una** ang mga tao sa pagkuha ng libreng pagkain.","translation":"The people **scrambled** to get the free food."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-**una-una** sa pagsagot, pakinggan mo muna ang buong tanong.","translation":"Don't **rush ahead** in answering, listen to the whole question first."}]

translation: bandaging; the act of applying a bandage
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o kilos ng paglalagay ng benda o panapal sa isang sugat upang maprotektahan ito at mapabilis ang paggaling.
original_explanation: That thing your tita who's a nurse is a pro at. It's the act of wrapping up a wound, whether it's a small "gasgas" from falling or your "sugat" from a broken heart (though the latter might need more than just gauze). It's first aid 101.
usage_notes: The `pag-` + `reduplicated first syllable` form indicates a continuous or habitual action, but here it simply functions as the noun for the action itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maingat ang **pagbebendahe** ng nars sa sugat ng pasyente.","translation":"The nurse's **bandaging** of the patient's wound was careful."},{"sentence":"Itinuro sa amin sa Red Cross ang tamang **pagbebendahe**.","translation":"They taught us the correct way of **bandaging** at the Red Cross."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nasisiyahan o kuntento sa isang ugnayang walang pormal na titulo o pangmatagalang pangako.
original_explanation: The person who says "I'm not ready for a commitment but I want the perks." They thrive in ambiguity. They want the late-night talks, the dates, the kilig, but not the "official" status on Facebook. They're the masters of "no strings attached," living their best life one "what are we?" non-conversation at a time.
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang ilarawan ang isang personalidad o isang yugto sa modernong pakikipag-date.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dati akong **situationship enjoyer**, pero ngayon, gusto ko na ng seryosohan.","translation":"I used to be a **situationship enjoyer**, but now, I want something serious."}]

meaning_filipino: Labis ang pagkakaroon ng taba sa katawan; sobra sa timbang.
etymology: From the intensifier prefix "napaka-" and the root word "taba" (fat).
original_explanation: How you feel after the Noche Buena feast and a week of eating Christmas leftovers. It's that "I need to go on a diet starting tomorrow" feeling. Can also be used to describe a juicy, thick-cut steak. Context is key, but be careful using it for people—it's not always a compliment!
usage_notes: Can be considered rude when used to describe a person, similar to English. Often used more neutrally for animals or objects.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang alaga niyang pusa ay **napakataba** dahil laging kumakain.","translation":"Her pet cat is **very fat** because it's always eating."},{"sentence":"**Napakataba** ng hiwa ng liempo na binili ko sa palengke.","translation":"The slice of pork belly I bought at the market is **very fatty**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaikling katawagan para sa bakuna (vaccine) o sa akto ng pagbabakuna (to vaccinate).
original_explanation: Short for vaccine/vaccination. The 'it' word of the 2020s. "Are you vaxxed?" became the new "What's your sign?". Getting your vax shot was a whole event, complete with the mandatory "just got vaxxed!" social media post and the subsequent "sakit ng braso" complaint.
usage_notes: Slang term that became mainstream during the COVID-19 pandemic. Can be a noun (vaccine) or a verb (to vaccinate, e.g., 'na-vax').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumpleto na ba ang **vax** mo laban sa COVID-19?","translation":"Is your **vax** against COVID-19 complete?"},{"sentence":"Na-**vax** na ang karamihan sa aming opisina.","translation":"Most of our office have been **vaxxed**."}]

translation: to get an injection; to have something injected
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapahintulot o pag-uutos na tusukan ng karayom ang sarili o ang iba para maglagay ng gamot o likido sa katawan.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you finally decide to get that flu shot, COVID vaccine, or a gluta drip. It's the ultimate "tiis-ganda" or "tiis-kalusugan" move. You're telling the nurse, "Sige na po, magpapaturok na ako, kahit takot ako sa karayom!" (Okay, I'll get the shot, even if I'm scared of needles!).
usage_notes: Often used in medical contexts, like getting a vaccine or treatment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **magpaturok** ng anti-tetanus dahil natapakan ko ang pako.","translation":"I need to **get an injection** for anti-tetanus because I stepped on a nail."},{"sentence":"Nagdesisyon siyang **magpaturok** ng bakuna para sa proteksyon ng kanyang pamilya.","translation":"He decided to **get injected** with the vaccine for his family's protection."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging hindi magkasama o magkadikit; may pagitan o distansya sa isa't isa.
etymology: Possibly from 'hiwa' (cut) + '-lay' (a suffix indicating separation or distance).
original_explanation: The official relationship status after a "Cool off muna tayo." It means 'separate.' Can apply to your laundry (whites and colors), your living situation with your parents, or your relationship status that all your chismosa titas will ask about.
usage_notes: Can be used as an adjective ("hiwalay na gamit" - separate things) or an adverb ("tumira nang hiwalay" - to live separately).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkaibigan pa rin kami kahit **hiwalay** na kami.","translation":"We are still friends even though we have **broken up**."},{"sentence":"Ilagay mo sa **hiwalay** na lalagyan ang mga puti.","translation":"Put the whites in a **separate** container."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpunta sa isang lugar o tao upang makipagkita, manatili nang panandalian, o magbigay-galang.
original_explanation: What your relatives from the province do when they're in Manila, and you have to clean the whole house. Or what you do when your friend is sick, and you bring them food. It's the act of showing up, for whatever reason. **Bumisita** ka naman sa bahay 'pag may time ka.
usage_notes: Actor-focus verb in the completed aspect. Present: bumibisita. Future: bibisita. The object-focus form 'bisitahin' is also very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumisita** kami sa aming lola noong nakaraang Linggo.","translation":"We **visited** our grandmother last Sunday."},{"sentence":"Maraming turista ang **bumisita** sa Palawan ngayong taon.","translation":"Many tourists **visited** Palawan this year."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang hanapbuhay ay ang pag-aalaga ng mga hayop na pinagkukunan ng gatas, o ang pagbebenta at paghahatid nito.
original_explanation: The OG food delivery guy. Before there was GrabFood, there was the 'maggagatas' who delivered fresh milk to your doorstep. Today, the term can also refer to anyone in the dairy business, from the farmer milking the carabao to the person selling kesong puti at the palengke.
usage_notes: The prefix 'mag-' plus a noun root often creates a noun for a person whose occupation is related to that noun (e.g., magtataho, magbabalut).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumaan na ba ang **maggagatas** ngayong umaga?","translation":"Has the **milkman** passed by this morning?"},{"sentence":"Ang pamilya nila ay kilalang **maggagatas** sa kanilang bayan sa probinsya.","translation":"Their family is a well-known **dairy farmer** family in their province."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang magaan at mabilis na pagdampi o pagkalabit gamit ang dulo ng daliri.
original_explanation: Yung ginagawa ng friend mong makulit na pitik nang pitik sa tenga mo. O kaya yung super light na tap sa screen ng phone mo para hindi mag-sleep. It's a flick, but a very gentle one.
usage_notes: Very rare word. 'Kalabit' or 'dampi' are much more common. Might be dialectal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **dagipik** lang sa pisngi ang ginawa niya para gisingin ako.","translation":"Just a **light flick** on the cheek was what she did to wake me up."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman ko ang **dagipik** ng isang insekto sa aking braso.","translation":"I felt the **light touch** of an insect on my arm."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang opisyal na utos, batas, o proklamasyon na may bisa ng batas, karaniwang ipinapatupad ng isang pinuno o pamahalaan.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "because I said so" power move. Isang utos galing sa taas (presidente, hari, o nanay mo) na hindi pwedeng kwestyunin. Parang 'pag sinabi ng nanay mo na, "Bawal lumabas hangga't hindi malinis ang bahay,"—'yan ang dekreto ng tahanan. It's a non-negotiable command.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng batas, gobyerno, at kasaysayan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglabas ng **dekreto** ang pangulo na nagsususpinde sa klase dahil sa bagyo.","translation":"The president issued a **decree** suspending classes due to the typhoon."},{"sentence":"Sa ilalim ng Batas Militar, maraming **dekreto** ang ipinatupad ng diktador.","translation":"Under Martial Law, many **decrees** were implemented by the dictator."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpulupot ng mga braso sa isang tao o bagay bilang pagpapahayag ng pagmamahal, pag-aliw, o pagbati.
etymology: Mula sa salitang ugat na 'yakap' (hug) at panlaping '-um-'.
original_explanation: The universal Filipino cure for everything—from a broken heart (hugot moment) to celebrating a PBA win. It's that warm, tight squeeze from your nanay that makes you feel safe, or that awkward side-hug from a tita you haven't seen in 10 years. This is the past tense; the action has been done.
usage_notes: Ito ay ang anyong naganap (completed aspect) ng pandiwa. Ang pawatas ay 'yumakap', pangkasalukuyan ay 'yumayakap', at panghinaharap ay 'yayaka'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigla siyang **yumakap** sa akin nang umiiyak.","translation":"She suddenly **hugged** me while crying."},{"sentence":"**Yumakap** siya sa unan dahil sa lamig.","translation":"He **hugged** the pillow because of the cold."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ugali ng pagmamaliit o mababang pagtingin sa mga taong mahihirap o may mas mababang antas sa lipunan.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na `matar` (pumatay) + `pobre` (mahirap), literal na "pumapatay ng mahirap," ngunit ginagamit upang tukuyin ang isang taong humahamak sa mahihirap.
original_explanation: The classic kontrabida in every Pinoy teleserye. 'Yung titignan ka from head to toe tapos iirapan ka kasi hindi branded 'yung suot mo. They say things like "Yuck, kadiri!" or "Don't you know who I am?". It's the attitude of looking down on others based on their financial status. The mortal enemy of "jologs" and "promdi".
usage_notes: Isang karaniwan at matinding panlalait sa kulturang Pilipino. Inilalarawan nito ang isang partikular na uri ng snobbery na may kaugnayan sa katayuan sa lipunan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw ko sa kanya dahil sobrang **matapobre** siya at mapanghusga sa kapwa.","translation":"I don't like her because she's so **snobbish towards the poor** and judgmental of others."},{"sentence":"Pinalaki siya ng kanyang mga magulang na huwag maging **matapobre**.","translation":"He was raised by his parents not to be an **elitist**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mga solidong piraso o materyal na namumuo at naiiwan sa ilalim ng isang likido, tulad ng kape, alak, o langis.
original_explanation: The stuff at the bottom of your cup of barako coffee that you try to avoid drinking. Figuratively, it refers to the dregs of society, the 'scum', or the leftover, unwanted bits of something. It's the gritty reality check at the bottom of your glass.
usage_notes: Used both for literal sediments and as a powerful metaphor for social outcasts or undesirable elements.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itapon mo na ang **latak** ng kape bago ka maghugas ng tasa.","translation":"Throw away the coffee **dregs** before you wash the cup."},{"sentence":"Itinuturing silang **latak** ng lipunan.","translation":"They are considered the **dregs** of society."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paghahanap o pagsunod sa bakas o pinagmulan ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you're trying to find the source of the latest office chismis. It's basically being a detective, whether you're tracking a package from Shopee, or stalking your crush's social media history from 2012.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagtunton** sa mga ninuno ay isang mahabang proseso.","translation":"The **tracing** of ancestors is a long process."},{"sentence":"Nagtagumpay ang mga pulis sa **pagtunton** sa kinaroroonan ng suspek.","translation":"The police succeeded in **tracking** the suspect's whereabouts."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-amin o paglalantad sa publiko, karaniwan sa social media, kung sino ang taong lihim na hinahangaan o 'crush'.
etymology: A compound phrase from English "crush" and "reveal", popularized by social media challenges and trends.
original_explanation: The moment of truth sa barkada group chat o sa "Truth or Dare." Ito yung high-stakes na pag-amin kung sino ba talaga yung tinitibok ng puso mo. Minsan, ginagawa itong content ng mga vlogger for views ("50K LIKES FOR A CRUSH REVEAL!"). The modern-day version of writing your crush's name on your notebook.
usage_notes: Primarily used by younger generations (Gen Z, Millennials) and in the context of social media or peer groups.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-dare sila sa akin na gumawa ng **crush reveal** sa Twitter.","translation":"They dared me to do a **crush reveal** on Twitter."},{"sentence":"Abangan niyo ang **crush reveal** ko sa susunod na vlog!","translation":"Wait for my **crush reveal** on my next vlog!"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na may kakayahang paranormal, tulad ng pagbasa ng isip o paghula sa hinaharap; may kaugnayan sa isip o kaluluwa.
original_explanation: Your tita who "just knew" you were pregnant before you announced it? That's some sikiko energy. It's the person who can predict the ending of a teleserye or knows who ate the last piece of leche flan without any evidence. Basically, a human chismis-detector with supernatural powers.
usage_notes: Can function as both a noun (a psychic) and an adjective (psychic abilities).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naniniwala ka ba sa mga **sikiko**?","translation":"Do you believe in **psychics**?"},{"sentence":"May mga kakayahang **sikiko** raw ang matanda.","translation":"They say the old man has **psychic** abilities."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maliit, tuyo, at malutong na tinapay.
etymology: A simplified or colloquial form of "biskuwit", from English "biscuit".
original_explanation: The everyday Pinoy cracker. This is your SkyFlakes, Fita, Rebisco, or Marie. The go-to 'pantawid-gutom' (hunger-stopper) when you're stuck in traffic, in a boring meeting, or when your sahod is still a week away. Perfect partner for coffee, instant noodles, or even as a base for mango float. It's the ultimate survival food.
usage_notes: The more common, colloquial term compared to "biskuwit."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isawsaw mo ang **biskwit** sa kape.","translation":"Dip the **biscuit** in the coffee."},{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng isang pakete ng **biskwit** sa tindahan.","translation":"I bought a pack of **crackers** at the store."}]

translation: a sweeping motion to gather things; appropriation
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-ipon o pagkolekta ng mga bagay, lalo na ang pera o yaman, sa paraang mabilis at malakihan, na tila winawalis patungo sa sarili.
original_explanation: Picture a corrupt politician seeing a pile of public funds. That sweeping motion they make to pull it all towards themselves? That's 'hamig.' It's also what you do with all the coins on the table after winning a game of 'tong-its.' It's a greedy, all-for-me gathering gesture.
usage_notes: Often has a negative connotation of greed or corruption, especially in the context of money or power. The verb form is 'hamigin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **hamig** lang, naubos na niya ang lahat ng pagkain sa mesa.","translation":"In just one **sweep**, he finished all the food on the table."},{"sentence":"Inaakusahan ang opisyal ng malawakang **hamig** ng kaban ng bayan.","translation":"The official is being accused of a massive **appropriation** of public funds."}]

meaning_filipino: Bulag ang isang mata.
original_explanation: This is when you have one eye that's not working, either blind or missing. Parang pirate lang ang peg. It's a very specific descriptor, not to be confused with 'duling' (cross-eyed) or 'bulag' (completely blind).
usage_notes: A specific term for being blind in one eye.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **pisak** ang aso matapos ang isang aksidente.","translation":"The dog became **blind in one eye** after an accident."},{"sentence":"May isang pusang **pisak** na laging nasa aming bakuran.","translation":"There's a **one-eyed** cat that's always in our yard."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa matindi o mariing lasa o amoy, karaniwan sa alak, kape, o suka.
original_explanation: When your barako coffee is so strong it could wake up your ancestors. Or when the vinegar for your chicharon is so potent it makes your eyes water. 'Grabe, ang tapang ng suka!'
usage_notes: This adjectival sense is often expressed through the form 'matapang' but using 'tapang' in a phrase like 'ang tapang ng...' is very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **tapang** ng kapeng barako na ito!","translation":"This barako coffee is so **strong**!"},{"sentence":"Hindi ko kaya ang **tapang** ng alak na ininom niya.","translation":"I can't handle the **potency** of the liquor he drank."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang alagang hayop na may apat na paa (Canis lupus familiaris), kilala sa pagiging matapat na kasama ng tao at tinaguriang 'man's best friend'.
etymology: Katutubong salita sa maraming wika sa Pilipinas.
original_explanation: The official stress reliever, security guard, and food-scrap vacuum of the Filipino household. From the 'askal' (asong kalye) that's everyone's community pet to the fluffy 'fur baby' who has more outfits than you do. An 'aso' isn't just a pet, it's family. A 'bantay' (guard) that alerts you to the arrival of the Shopee delivery guy.
usage_notes: A very common word. The term "askal" (asong kalye) is a popular portmanteau for street dogs, now often rebranded as "Aspin" (Asong Pinoy).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumahol nang malakas ang **aso** nang may dumaang tao.","translation":"The **dog** barked loudly when someone passed by."},{"sentence":"Ang paborito kong **aso** ay isang Aspin na napulot namin sa daan.","translation":"My favorite **dog** is an Aspin we found on the street."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang masusing pagsiyasat o paghahanap sa isang lugar o sa mga gamit sa pamamagitan ng pag-aalis o paggalaw sa mga ito.
original_explanation: That frantic moment when you can't find your phone or wallet and you turn your entire room upside down. It's more intense than 'maghanap'. This is the 'raid' level of searching, like when your mom looks for contraband in your room or when police search a suspect's house in a teleserye.
usage_notes: Often implies a messy, frantic, or forceful search.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinailangan niyang **maghalughog** sa lumang baul para mahanap ang mga litrato ng kanyang lola.","translation":"She had to **rummage** through the old chest to find her grandmother's photos."},{"sentence":"Nag-umpisang **maghalughog** ang mga pulis sa bahay ng suspek.","translation":"The police started to **search thoroughly** the suspect's house."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong may kaparehong diwa, isipan, o layunin. Sa modernong konteksto, ito rin ay tumutukoy sa isang programa ng pamahalaan na naglalayong magbenta ng mga pangunahing bilihin sa mas mababang halaga.
etymology: Mula sa `ka-` (nagsasaad ng pagsama o pagkakatulad) + `diwa` (espiritu, esensya, isipan).
original_explanation: Originally meant 'kindred spirit' or someone who just *gets* you, your ka-vibes. Now, it's more famous as that government-run rolling store where you can buy cheaper veggies and rice. So, it's either your soulmate or your suki for sibuyas.
usage_notes: The meaning has shifted in popular consciousness due to the Kadiwa program started during the Marcos Sr. era and revived in modern times. Context is key to distinguish between the person and the market.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natagpuan ko sa kanya ang isang tunay na **kadiwa**.","translation":"I found in her a true **kindred spirit**."},{"sentence":"Pumila kami sa **Kadiwa** para makabili ng murang bigas at gulay.","translation":"We lined up at the **Kadiwa** (market) to buy cheap rice and vegetables."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang opisyal na tungkulin ay isagawa ang parusang kamatayan, partikular na ang pagbigti.
original_explanation: The historical equivalent of the person who clicks 'End Meeting for All' on a Zoom call. A grim job from the past, now mostly seen in history books and period dramas. In hugot culture, 'tagabitay ng pag-asa' is that person who kills your vibe.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinatatakutan ng lahat ang **tagabitay** noong unang panahon.","translation":"Everyone feared the **executioner** in the old days."},{"sentence":"Walang may gustong gumanap na **tagabitay** sa dula-dulaan.","translation":"No one wanted to play the role of the **executioner** in the play."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng artropod na may mahabang katawan na binubuo ng maraming bahagi, at bawat bahagi ay may isang pares ng paa.
original_explanation: The stuff of nightmares. That creepy crawly with a million legs (okay, not a million, but it feels like it) that makes you jump on a chair and scream. Seeing a *guyaman* in your bathroom is a universal Filipino experience that triggers a frantic search for the nearest *tsinelas* or bug spray. Also known as *alupihan*.
usage_notes: Synonymous with 'alupihan', which is more common in many regions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatapak siya ng malaking **guyaman** sa hardin.","translation":"He stepped on a big **centipede** in the garden."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka, may makamandag na **guyaman** dito.","translation":"Be careful, there are venomous **centipedes** here."}]

translation: the act of having something delivered or someone escorted
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-aatas o pag-aayos na may magdala sa isang tao o bagay patungo sa isang destinasyon.
etymology: From pag- (gerund prefix) + pa- (causative prefix) + -pa- (reduplication of first syllable of the root) + hatid (to deliver, to escort).
original_explanation: Before Grab or Lalamove, this was you asking your kuya to drop you off at the mall. Now, it's the magical process where you click a button and food/parcels/groceries appear at your doorstep. It's also the classic Pinoy courtship move: 'Magpapahatid ka ba?' (Will you let me escort you home?). It's about ensuring something—or someone—gets to their destination safely.
usage_notes: Can refer to delivery of goods or escorting a person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-asikaso ang **pagpapahatid** ng mga dokumentong ito sa kliyente.","translation":"Please take care of **having these documents delivered** to the client."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapahatid** niya sa akin pauwi gabi-gabi ay isang matamis na kilos.","translation":"His **escorting** me home every night is a sweet gesture."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mararamdamang pagnanais o ang mismong akto ng pagsusuka sa hinaharap; ang paglabas ng laman ng sikmura.
original_explanation: This is your body's future reaction after five rounds of sisig, three bottles of beer, and a questionable street food adventure at 2 AM. It's also the feeling you get when you see your ex being sweet with their new partner. That 'parang may aakyat' feeling.
usage_notes: Future tense of "magduwal" or "dumuwal". Can refer to the feeling of nausea or the act of vomiting itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang kumain niyan, baka ka **magduduwal**.","translation":"Don't eat that, you might **feel nauseous**."},{"sentence":"Sa sobrang pagod at puyat, pakiramdam ko ay **magduduwal** ako anumang oras.","translation":"From extreme fatigue and lack of sleep, I feel like I **will vomit** any moment."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsilo o pagkulong sa isang tao sa isang sitwasyon na mahirap takasan, lalo na sa konteksto ng sapilitang pagpapakasal o relasyon.
original_explanation: Classic teleserye plot device! This is when someone traps another person into a relationship or marriage, often through manipulation, blackmail, or a fake pregnancy. 'Pinikot niya ang mayaman na CEO.' It's about cornering someone so they have no choice but to be with you. It's the ultimate 'sana all' gone wrong.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in the context of forcing someone into a relationship or marriage. Carries a strong negative and manipulative connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayaman ang lalaki kaya sinubukan siyang **pumikot** ng babae.","translation":"The man was rich, so the woman tried to **entrap** him (into marriage)."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpapaloko sa mga taong gustong **pumikot** sa'yo.","translation":"Don't be fooled by people who want to **trap** you."}]

translation: to be dented, to be deformed by pressure
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng lupi o pagkasira sa anyo dahil sa pagkakadiin o pagkakapukpok.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `ma-` at salitang ugat na `yupi` (dent, fold).
original_explanation: 'Yung kotse mong nasagi sa parking lot? Nayupi 'yung pinto. 'Yung lata ng sardinas na nahulog mo? Nayupi rin. It's when something gets dented or loses its original shape because of impact or pressure. Pwedeng literal, pwedeng 'yung pride mo ang nayupi after mapahiya.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit para sa mga bagay na metal tulad ng sasakyan at lata, ngunit maaaring gamitin para sa anumang bagay na maaaring masira ang anyo dahil sa diin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong upuan ang karton, baka **mayupi** ang laman.","translation":"Don't sit on the cardboard box, the contents might **get crushed**."},{"sentence":"**Nayupi** ang bumper ng sasakyan matapos itong bumangga.","translation":"The car's bumper **got dented** after it crashed."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay, paraan, o puwersa na ginagamit upang pigilan, hadlangan, o kontrolin ang isang kilos, paggalaw, o pangyayari.
etymology: From `pan-` (instrument prefix) + `pigil` (to stop, to restrain). The `n` in `pan-` assimilates to `m` before `p`.
original_explanation: Your self-control when you see a 12.12 sale but it's not yet payday. It's the leash on a dog, the brakes on a car, or your friend stopping you from texting your ex. Anything that holds you back, for better or for worse. Minsan kailangan, minsan gusto mong kumawala.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng gobyerno ng epektibong **pamigil** sa pagtaas ng presyo ng bilihin.","translation":"The government needs an effective **control** for the rising prices of goods."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang konsensya ang nagsilbing **pamigil** sa kanyang masamang balak.","translation":"His conscience served as the **restraint** against his evil plan."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbuo ng isang larawan, ideya, o pakiramdam sa isipan na hindi nakikita o nararanasan sa kasalukuyan.
original_explanation: This is your brain on 'what if' mode. Yung tipong iniisip mo na lahat ng posibleng mangyari sa isang scenario, from winning the lottery to tripping on a flat surface. It's the power to create your own mental teleserye.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **maguniguni** ang kinabukasan kung hindi ka kikilos ngayon.","translation":"It's hard to **imagine** the future if you don't act now."},{"sentence":"Na-**maguniguni** ko na yata ang lahat ng paraan para manalo sa raffle.","translation":"I think I've **imagined** all the ways to win the raffle."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tugon, paliwanag, o solusyon sa isang tanong o suliranin. Tumutukoy din ito sa pananagutan o responsibilidad sa isang bagay o tao.
original_explanation: This is the 'final answer' you give on a game show, or the text you've been waiting for all day. But it's also the 'Ako bahala' or 'I got this' you tell your friend. 'Sagot kita' means 'I've got your back,' making it the ultimate word for both solutions and support.
usage_notes: This word has two primary meanings: 1) a reply or solution, and 2) a charge, responsibility, or something one sponsors/pays for ('my treat'). The context determines the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Alam mo ba ang **sagot** sa tanong number five?","translation":"Do you know the **answer** to question number five?"},{"sentence":"**Sagot** ko ang meryenda ninyo mamaya.","translation":"The snacks later are my **treat** (I'll be responsible for them)."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng isang instrumento o pamantayan upang alamin ang dimensyon, kantidad, o lawak ng isang bagay.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "sukat" (pagsukat) at panlaping -um-.
original_explanation: What the mananahi does before making your prom gown, or what you do to see if you can fit that new sofa through the door. It's the act of checking if something "fits"—be it clothes, furniture, or your expectations vs. reality. Minsan, kailangan mong `sumukat` para malaman kung hanggang saan ka lang. Ouch.
usage_notes: Anyong pangnagdaan. Maaaring gamitin para sa pisikal na pagsukat o sa matalinhagang pagtantya sa isang tao o sitwasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumukat** ang karpintero ng haba ng kahoy.","translation":"The carpenter **measured** the length of the wood."},{"sentence":"**Sumukat** siya ng damit sa department store.","translation":"She **measured** (tried on) clothes at the department store."}]

translation: act of cursing at each other; exchange of curses
meaning_filipino: Ang palitan ng mga mura o masasamang salita sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang tao.
etymology: From the root "mura" (curse word), with the prefix "pag-", reduplication of the first syllable "mu-", and the suffix "-han" which indicates a reciprocal or collective action.
original_explanation: This is what you hear during intense traffic altercations, a heated online comments section, or when your favorite basketball team is losing badly. It's a verbal showdown where everyone's vocabulary suddenly consists of words your lola told you never to say. Not a good look, but definitely a common sound.
usage_notes: The "-han" suffix is key here, implying that the cursing is mutual or happening between multiple people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natigil lang ang kanilang **pagmumurahan** nang dumating ang pulis.","translation":"Their **exchange of curses** only stopped when the police arrived."},{"sentence":"Iwasan ang **pagmumurahan** sa social media para hindi ma-ban.","translation":"Avoid the **act of cursing at each other** on social media to not get banned."}]

meaning_filipino: Maglakad nang walang tiyak na patutunguhan o para lamang magpalipas ng oras.
etymology: Reduplication of `lakad` (walk) with the infix `-um-` on the first part.
original_explanation: This is what you do in the mall when you have no money. You're not really shopping, you're just 'walking around.' It's the official pastime of people waiting for their friend who is always late. Not a power walk, not a commute, just a chill, aimless stroll to see what's up. The perfect activity for a lazy Sunday afternoon.
usage_notes: The repetition of `lakad` indicates a casual, non-purposeful, or repetitive action, similar to `kain-kain` (eating a little) or `tulog-tulog` (sleeping lightly/intermittently).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **lumakad-lakad** sa parke tuwing hapon.","translation":"He likes to **stroll** in the park every afternoon."},{"sentence":"Habang naghihintay, **lumakad-lakad** muna kami sa loob ng mall.","translation":"While waiting, we **walked around** inside the mall for a while."}]

meaning_filipino: Paghiwa-hiwalayin ang mga bagay o tao at ayusin sa iba't ibang grupo batay sa kanilang katangian.
etymology: From pag- (verb prefix) + bukod-bukod (reduplication of the root, implying multiple/distributive action) + -in (object-focus suffix).
original_explanation: This is 'pagbukod' on steroids. It's not just separating one thing, but sorting *everything* into its proper category. Think of a librarian organizing books by genre, a BPO agent tagging customer concerns, or you sorting your online shopping haul into 'keep,' 'return,' and 'hide from mom.' It's organized separation.
usage_notes: Implies sorting a collection of items into multiple distinct groups.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **pagbukud-bukurin** ang mga donasyon ayon sa uri.","translation":"We need **to sort out** the donations according to type."},{"sentence":"Inutusan siyang **pagbukud-bukurin** ang mga prutas na sariwa at ang mga nabubulok na.","translation":"He/She was instructed **to segregate** the fresh fruits from the rotten ones."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aararo o pagbubungkal ng lupa, karaniwan bilang paghahanda sa pagtatanim.
original_explanation: This is a term straight from the *probinsya* playbook. To **singkalin** the land is the original "hustle"—the back-breaking work of preparing the soil for planting. It’s the farmer's workout routine, powered by carabao and sheer grit, long before gyms and "leg day" were a thing.
usage_notes: Ito ang anyong pautos o pawatas ng pandiwa. Ang 'singkal' ay ang mismong araro o pang-araro.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maagang gumising ang magsasaka upang **singkalin** ang kanyang bukid.","translation":"The farmer woke up early to **plow** his field."},{"sentence":"Dapat nang **singkalin** ang lupa bago pa dumating ang tag-ulan.","translation":"The land must be **tilled** before the rainy season arrives."}]

translation: to curse, to berate, to scold
meaning_filipino: Pagsasabihan ng masasamang salita; pagmumulan ng galit sa pamamagitan ng bibig.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you cut someone off in traffic on EDSA, or when your nanay finds out you haven't washed the dishes. It's a verbal smackdown, a tirade of expletives. The goal is to make the other person feel as small as your sahod on the 29th of the month.
usage_notes: This is derived from the root word 'mura' meaning 'curse'. It is a homonym of 'mumurahin' (cheap), which comes from a different root 'mura'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **mumurahin** ang iyong kapwa dahil lang sa maliit na pagkakamali.","translation":"Don't **curse** your fellow person just because of a small mistake."},{"sentence":"Pinagalitan siya at **mumurahin** ng kanyang amo sa harap ng maraming tao.","translation":"He was scolded and **berated** by his boss in front of many people."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapang yari sa kahoy o metal na may ukit-ukit na rabaw para sa pagkukuskos ng damit; maaari ring tumukoy sa pook na pinaglalabhan.
original_explanation: The OG washing machine. Ito yung parang abs na kahoy o yero na ginagamit ng lola mo para kuskusin ang mga damit hanggang pumuti. Before the era of spin cycles, there was the 'kuskos' on the labahan. It can also mean the 'laundry area' itself, just like 'labadahan'. Context is key, bes.
usage_notes: This word has two common meanings: 1) the washboard tool, and 2) the laundry area (synonymous with 'labadahan'). The washboard meaning is becoming rarer with modern appliances, while the laundry area meaning is still common, especially in rural areas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit si lola ng **labahan** para tanggalin ang mantsa sa puting damit.","translation":"Grandma used a **washboard** to remove the stain from the white shirt."},{"sentence":"Doon tayo magkita sa **labahan** sa tabi ng ilog.","translation":"Let's meet at the **laundry area** beside the river."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghampas o pagtama sa isang bagay o tao gamit ang kamay o anumang instrumento.
original_explanation: Can be literal, like what your mom threatened you with the walis tambo (broom), or figurative, like when a song 'hits' you right in the feels. It can also mean to 'spike' in volleyball, or to hit a target number, like when your sales 'pumalo sa quota.' A special use is 'pumalo para sa iba,' which means to take the hit for someone else, like a true martyr friend.
usage_notes: Has a wide range of meanings from physical striking to achieving a target. 'Pumalo para sa iba' is an idiomatic phrase meaning to take the blame or punishment for another, or to substitute for someone (like a pinch-hitter in baseball).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malakas na **pumalo** ang presyo ng sibuyas noong nakaraang buwan.","translation":"The price of onions **hit** a high last month."},{"sentence":"Siya ang laging **pumapalo para sa iba** para lang maprotektahan ang kanyang mga kaibigan.","translation":"He always **takes the hit for others** just to protect his friends."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang tao o bagay na may pambihirang ganda, pang-akit, o katangian na nakakabighani at mahirap iwasan o kalimutan.
original_explanation: This is that crush who makes you forget your own name. It's the vibe of a perfect beach sunset or the plot of a K-drama that keeps you up until 3 AM. It’s the opposite of 'seen-zoned'—it demands your full attention. If something is kahali-halina, it's not just pretty; it has that magnetic pull that makes you go 'Sana all.'
usage_notes: A very poetic and positive word, often used in literature, songs, and to give a heartfelt compliment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroon siyang **kahali-halina** na ngiti na kayang magpagaan ng anumang problema.","translation":"She has a **captivating** smile that can lighten any problem."},{"sentence":"Ang tanawin mula sa tuktok ng bundok ay tunay na **kahali-halina**.","translation":"The view from the mountain top is truly **enchanting**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang titulo ng paggalang para sa isang babaeng kabilang sa maharlikang angkan, partikular sa mga kultura sa Mindanao.
etymology: Mula sa iba't ibang wika sa Timog Pilipinas (hal., Maranao, Maguindanao).
original_explanation: This is a term for a princess or a noble lady, especially in the southern Philippines. Think of it as the Mindanao equivalent of 'prinsesa' or 'lady.' It carries a sense of royalty and respect. Not to be confused with the Visayan 'bai,' which is like 'bro' or 'pare.'
usage_notes: Ito ay isang tiyak na titulong pangkultura.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tawag sa kanya ay **Bai** Ayesha dahil nagmula siya sa pamilya ng mga datu.","translation":"She is called **Princess** Ayesha because she comes from a family of datus."},{"sentence":"Iginagalang ng lahat si **Bai** sa kanilang komunidad.","translation":"Everyone in their community respects the **noble lady**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglilinis gamit ang tubig, at karaniwan ay may kasamang sabon. Ito ang nakaraang anyo ng pandiwang "maghugas".
original_explanation: The ultimate "bunso" task. After a big family dinner, someone has to do the dishes. "Sino'ng **naghugas**?" usually means "Who was the unlucky one assigned to wash the mountain of plates?" Can also apply to hands, feet, or your car.
usage_notes: Past tense of 'maghugas'. Often refers to washing dishes ('naghugas ng pinggan') or hands ('naghugas ng kamay').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Naghugas** ako ng mga plato pagkatapos ng hapunan.","translation":"I **washed** the plates after dinner."},{"sentence":"Tinanong ng nanay kung sino ang **naghugas** ng kotse.","translation":"The mother asked who **washed** the car."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang opisyal na dokumento na nagpapatunay ng isang katotohanan, tulad ng pagtatapos ng kurso, pagmamay-ari, o paglahok sa isang kaganapan.
original_explanation: The piece of paper you get after finishing a seminar, a course, or winning a barangay-level singing contest. It's the proof that you didn't just waste your time. You post it on LinkedIn to flex, or hang it on the wall for your parents to proudly show visitors.
usage_notes: Can refer to a wide range of documents, from a certificate of attendance to a stock certificate.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinakita niya ang kanyang **sertipiko** ng pagtatapos sa kolehiyo.","translation":"He showed his college diploma **certificate**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mo ng **sertipiko** ng kapanganakan para kumuha ng pasaporte.","translation":"You need a birth **certificate** to get a passport."}]

meaning_filipino: Sukatin ang dami ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay butil o likido, sa pamamagitan ng isang takalan o panukat.
original_explanation: What you do every single day before cooking rice. "Ilang tasa?" is the question, and "itakal mo" is the action. It's the sacred ritual of measuring out grains, sugar, or flour using a specific container, ensuring perfect proportions for your sinangag or pandesal.
usage_notes: Specifically for measuring by volume (e.g., with a cup), not by weight. Usually for dry goods like rice, flour, sugar, or liquids.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Itakal** mo ang tatlong tasang bigas para sa ating pananghalian.","translation":"**Measure out** three cups of rice for our lunch."},{"sentence":"Bago timplahin ang kape, **itinatakal** muna niya ang asukal.","translation":"Before mixing the coffee, he first **measures out** the sugar."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagputol sa buhay; ang pagpigil sa pag-unlad o pagpapatuloy ng isang bagay sa simula pa lamang.
original_explanation: A heavy word. It's what happens when a good idea gets shot down in a meeting before it even has a chance ('kinitil ang suggestion'). More seriously, it's used for ending a life, often prematurely. Think of it as hitting the 'end process' button on something that was just starting to load.
usage_notes: Often used in its conjugated form 'kitilin' (to end a life) or 'kinitil' (ended a life). It has a strong, often violent, connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming pangarap ang **kinitil** ng digmaan.","translation":"Many dreams were **cut short** by the war."},{"sentence":"**Kitilin** mo na ang masamang ugali habang maaga pa.","translation":"**Nip** that bad habit **in the bud** while it's still early."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang biglaan at hindi inaasahang sitwasyon na nangangailangan ng agarang aksyon o tulong.
original_explanation: That moment when things go from 0 to 100 real quick. Like when you accidentally send a message to the wrong person, or when you realize you forgot your wallet after eating at a karinderya. "Tawagan mo ang ambulansya, emerhensiya ito!" is the serious version. "Bes, emerhensiya, pa-load naman!" is the more common, friend-in-need version.
usage_notes: Used in both formal contexts (medical, disasters) and informal ones (personal "emergencies").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dalhin agad sa ospital ang pasyente, ito ay isang **emerhensiya**.","translation":"Bring the patient to the hospital immediately, this is an **emergency**."},{"sentence":"Mayroon kaming 'emergency fund' para sa mga hindi inaasahang **emerhensiya**.","translation":"We have an 'emergency fund' for unexpected **emergencies**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nangangasiwa, gumagawa, o nagwawasto ng mga pagsusulit o iksamen.
original_explanation: The person you try to make eye contact with during an exam, hoping for a sign of divine intervention or at least a clue. Also known as the proctor, the final boss before you can finally submit your test paper and leave the room.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang aming **iksaminador** kaya walang nakapangopya.","translation":"Our **examiner** was strict so no one was able to cheat."},{"sentence":"Ang **iksaminador** sa LTO ay kilalang istrikto.","translation":"The **examiner** at the LTO is known to be strict."}]

translation: turning point, bend (in a road), intersection
meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan maaaring lumiko o magbago ng direksyon, tulad ng kanto o kurbada sa daan.
original_explanation: That specific spot on Waze or Google Maps where you're supposed to turn, but you miss it and have to 'recalculate.' It's a more formal-sounding 'kanto' or 'liko.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa susunod na **likuan**, kumanan ka.","translation":"At the next **turning point**, turn right."},{"sentence":"Mapanganib ang **likuan** na iyon dahil walang ilaw.","translation":"That **bend** is dangerous because there are no lights."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-aakusa o pagpaparatang ng kasalanan sa isang tao.
etymology: Tambalang salita mula sa "bigay" (give) at "sala" (sin, fault).
original_explanation: This is the art of pointing fingers. It’s when you pin the blame on someone, whether they're guilty or not. 'Huwag kang mag-bigay-sala kung wala kang ebidensya!' is the standard defense. It's the classic 'It wasn't me!' scenario, where everyone is trying to find a scapegoat. Sa group project, ito yung ginagawa sa member na 'di nag-contribute, pero minsan, kahit sa nag-contribute, ginagawa rin.
usage_notes: Madalas na may negatibong konotasyon ng di-makatarungang pag-aakusa. Karaniwang ginagamit sa anyong pandiwa ('magbigay-sala').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **bigay-sala** ay walang sapat na batayan.","translation":"His **imputation** of guilt has no sufficient basis."},{"sentence":"Mabilis siyang mag-**bigay-sala** sa iba para pagtakpan ang sarili niyang pagkakamali.","translation":"He is quick to **blame** others to cover up his own mistakes."}]

translation: to comb through; to search thoroughly; to scour
meaning_filipino: Ang masusing paghahanap, pagsisiyasat, o paggalugad sa isang lugar.
etymology: Mula sa 'suyod' (isang uri ng suklay na pang-agrikultura), na may kinalaman sa masusing pagdaan sa isang lugar.
original_explanation: Yung ginagawa ng mga pulis sa crime scene, o yung ginagawa mo sa Shopee at Lazada for the best deals. It's about searching every nook and cranny. 'Bes, **suyurin** natin yung buong Divisoria para mahanap yung a-match sa OOTD natin.'
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng operasyong pulis o militar, o anumang masinsinang paghahanap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan ng heneral ang mga sundalo na **suyurin** ang buong kagubatan.","translation":"The general ordered the soldiers to **scour** the entire forest."},{"sentence":"**Suyurin** natin ang buong kabahayan para mahanap ang nawawalang singsing.","translation":"Let's **comb through** the entire house to find the missing ring."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglikha o pag-organisa ng mga bahagi upang makagawa ng isang kabuuan.
original_explanation: This is the verb for putting things together. Like when you and your barkada are bumubuo ng plano for the weekend, which will probably get cancelled anyway (drawing na naman!). Or when a love team's chemistry is so strong, you can say sila ang bumubuo ng araw mo.
usage_notes: Present tense of 'bumuo'. Used for both tangible things (building a house) and intangible concepts (forming a plan, making up a story).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga mag-aaral ang **bumubuo** sa pinakamalaking sektor ng populasyon ng unibersidad.","translation":"The students **constitute** the largest sector of the university's population."},{"sentence":"Sila ay **bumubuo** ng isang bagong samahan para sa mga kabataan.","translation":"They are **forming** a new organization for the youth."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong may malaking impluwensya, kapangyarihan, o kahalagahan sa isang larangan o sa lipunan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "bigat" (weight) at hulaping "-in".
original_explanation: This is your VIP, your 'heavyweight.' Not necessarily in physical size, but in influence, power, or wealth. The type of person who can make one phone call and solve a problem. In office politics, sila yung mga 'bossing.' In showbiz, sila yung mga A-lister. Sila yung reason kung bakit may traffic kasi may special convoy sila.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa di-pormal na konteksto upang ilarawan ang katayuan ng isang tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mga **bigatin** sa pulitika ang dumalo sa kanyang kaarawan.","translation":"The **heavyweights** in politics attended his birthday."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya bilang isang **bigatin** na abogado sa bansa.","translation":"He is known as an **influential** lawyer in the country."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kulisap, karaniwang gamu-gamo o paruparo, na naaakit sa liwanag o apoy.
original_explanation: The original 'marupok'. 'Yung friend mong paulit-ulit na bumabalik sa ex niyang toxic, parang **aliparo** na lapit nang lapit sa apoy, kahit alam niyang masusunog siya. They're drawn to the flame, no matter how many times they get burned.
usage_notes: Maaari ring tumukoy sa ilang uri ng tutubi o alitaptap sa ibang mga rehiyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **aliparo** ang pumasok at paikot-ikot sa bumbilya.","translation":"A **moth** came in and was circling the light bulb."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkakaroon ng kaalaman, kamalayan, o pag-unawa sa mga bagay-bagay sa paligid.
