original_explanation: This is your 'pake' level with the world. When you were a baby, wala ka pang muwang. When you finally understood why your parents were always tired, nagkaroon ka na ng muwang. It's that moment the lightbulb turns on and you realize, 'Ah, ganun pala 'yun.' It's the opposite of being blissfully ignorant.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa pariralang "wala pang muwang" (innocent, naive) o "magkaroon ng muwang" (to become aware).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Noong bata ako, wala pa akong **muwang** sa mga problema ng matatanda.","translation":"When I was a child, I had no **awareness** of adult problems."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula siyang magkaroon ng **muwang** sa politika noong kolehiyo.","translation":"He started to gain political **consciousness** in college."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal o di-pormal na paanyaya sa isang tao upang dumalo sa isang pagtitipon, okasyon, o kaganapan.
original_explanation: This is the official 'save the date' or 'G ka ba?' message you get for a birthday, wedding, or even just a simple inuman session. It's the reason you have to either buy a new outfit or think of a good excuse not to go. From the Spanish word 'convidar'.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin nang palitan sa salitang 'imbita' o 'anyaya'. Ang 'kumbite' ay isang mas pormal na bersyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatanggap ako ng **kumbida** para sa kasal ni Ana.","translation":"I received an **invitation** to Ana's wedding."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpunta sa loob ng isang lugar o espasyo. Ginagamit din bilang utos na pumasok.
original_explanation: The triumphant feeling of clocking in at 8:59 AM. What you say to a guest at your door: 'Tuloy po kayo, **pasok**!' It's also that satisfying moment when the key finally fits the lock.
usage_notes: As a command, it's a direct and common way to invite someone inside. 'Pumasok' is the infinitive/actor-focus form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pasok**! Huwag kang mahiya.","translation":"**Come in**! Don't be shy."},{"sentence":"May **pasok** ka ba bukas?","translation":"Do you have **work/school** (to go in to) tomorrow?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng karampatang importansya, respeto, o pagkilala sa halaga ng isang tao, bagay, o pangyayari.
etymology: From pag- (gerund prefix) + pa- (causative prefix) + -pa- (reduplication of first syllable of the root) + halaga (value).
original_explanation: This is what you hope your boss shows you during performance reviews (with a bonus, please). It's what your S.O. wants when they say 'You don't appreciate me!' It's the opposite of being 'seen-zoned.' Pagpapahalaga is knowing someone's worth and acting on it, whether it's for a person, a vintage item, or your mental health.
usage_notes: A core Filipino value.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapahalaga** sa pamilya ay isang mahalagang katangiang Pilipino.","translation":"**Giving importance** to family is an important Filipino trait."},{"sentence":"Ipakita mo ang iyong **pagpapahalaga** sa pamamagitan ng gawa, hindi lang salita.","translation":"Show your **appreciation** through actions, not just words."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang kilos ng pagtigil sa paggawa o paggalaw upang maibalik ang lakas.
original_explanation: This is you, right now, scrolling through your phone instead of working. You're 'taking a break.' It's the BPO agent on their 15-minute coffee break, or your dad napping on the sofa on a Sunday afternoon. The act of chilling, in progress.
usage_notes: This is the progressive aspect (present tense) of the verb 'magpahinga'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag ninyo siyang istorbohin dahil **nagpapahinga** siya.","translation":"Don't disturb him because he is **resting**."},{"sentence":"**Nagpapahinga** lang ang utak ko, hindi ako tulog.","translation":"My brain is just **taking a break**, I'm not asleep."}]

translation: to run amok; to fight wildly
meaning_filipino: Ang marahas at walang-patumanggang pag-atake o pakikipag-away, kadalasan ay dulot ng matinding galit o pagkawala sa sarili.
etymology: From Malay 'amuk', meaning "uncontrollable rage". This is the origin of the English word "amok".
original_explanation: Ever seen someone lose it completely in traffic and just start a fight with everyone? That's it. It's going berserk. The kind of chaos you see in movies when one hero decides to take on a hundred enemies at once. Not your typical 'away-kalye', this is a full-on, uncontrolled rampage.
usage_notes: A very strong word, implying a loss of control and violent rage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nang mabalitaan niya ang trahedya, nagbanta siyang **maghamok** sa kalsada.","translation":"When he heard of the tragedy, he threatened to **run amok** in the streets."},{"sentence":"Ang sundalong sugatan ay nagpasyang **maghamok** sa kampo ng kaaway hanggang sa huling hininga.","translation":"The wounded soldier decided to **fight wildly** in the enemy's camp until his last breath."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang batayan o pundasyon; hindi nakabase sa katotohanan o sapat na ebidensya.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung chismis na narinig mo sa kapitbahay na kesyo may ahas daw sa ilalim ng mall. **Walang-saligan**, 'teh! It's an accusation or a story with no receipts, no proof, no basis in reality. Just pure 'sabi-sabi'.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang mga tsismis, akusasyon, o argumento na kulang sa ebidensya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga paratang laban sa kanya ay **walang-saligan**.","translation":"The accusations against him are **baseless**."},{"sentence":"Isang teoryang **walang-saligan** ang madaling pabulaanan.","translation":"An **unfounded** theory is easy to disprove."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pagluluto o lasa na pinagsasama ang tamis at asim.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na "agridulce" (agrio 'sour' + dulce 'sweet').
original_explanation: Yung feeling mo sa ex mong 'di mo malaman kung love mo pa o hate mo na. Parang 'yung sauce sa lumpiang shanghai na both sweet and sour, 'yan ang agridulse. Perfect for when your feelings are complicated.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa mga kontekstong panluto upang ilarawan ang isang partikular na lasa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong ulam ang isdang may **agridulse** na sarsa.","translation":"My favorite dish is fish with **sweet and sour** sauce."},{"sentence":"Pakilagyan mo ng maraming **agridulse** ang aking order na pork.","translation":"Please put a lot of **sweet and sour** sauce on my pork order."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paraan ng paglalagay ng tagpi o piraso ng materyal upang takpan ang butas o sira. Tumutukoy din sa isang bagay na binubuo ng iba't ibang piraso na pinagsama-sama.
original_explanation: Describes something that's literally "patched up." Think of your lolo's favorite shorts with a different colored square on the knee, or how your team's project looks when everyone just pastes their part together without editing. A bit of this, a bit of that. Pwede na 'yan!
usage_notes: Can be used as an adverb describing how something is done, or as an adjective describing the state of an object.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inayos niya ang butas sa pantalon sa paraang **patagpi**.","translation":"He fixed the hole in the pants in a **patched manner**."},{"sentence":"Mukhang **patagpi** ang bubong dahil sa iba't ibang kulay ng yero.","translation":"The roof looks like **patchwork** because of the different colors of galvanized iron sheets."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na dalubhasa o nagtatrabaho sa sining ng litograpiya, isang paraan ng pag-imprenta gamit ang bato.
original_explanation: The OG graphic artist. Bago pa magkaroon ng Photoshop at Canva, sila ang gumagawa ng mga print ads at posters gamit ang bato at tinta. Medyo hipster ang dating, 'di ba?
usage_notes: Isang di-pangkaraniwang salita sa kasalukuyang panahon dahil sa pagbabago ng teknolohiya sa pag-imprenta.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagmamalaki ng museo ang mga obra ng isang tanyag na **litograpo** noong ika-19 na siglo.","translation":"The museum is proud of the works of a famous **lithographer** from the 19th century."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng paghinto o pagtigil mula sa isang kilos, galaw, o proseso.
etymology: Mula sa ugat na "tigil" (hinto). Ang unlaping "pagka-" dito ay nangangahulugan ng akto o estado ng paghinto, madalas ay biglaan.
original_explanation: 'Yung biglang nag-buffer 'yung Netflix sa gitna ng climax. 'Yan ang **pagkapatigil** na nakakainis. O 'yung biglang tumigil 'yung usapan nung dumating ka. Awkward silence.
usage_notes: Madalas na nagpapahiwatig ng biglaan o hindi inaasahang paghinto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang biglaang **pagkapatigil** ng makina ay nagdulot ng panic sa mga pasahero.","translation":"The sudden **stopping** of the engine caused panic among the passengers."},{"sentence":"Napansin niya ang **pagkapatigil** ng bata sa pag-iyak nang bigyan ito ng laruan.","translation":"She noticed the **cessation** of the child's crying when it was given a toy."}]

translation: to be able to help; to be helped
meaning_filipino: Ang makapagbigay ng saklolo o suporta sa isang taong nangangailangan; o ang kalagayan ng pagtanggap ng tulong.
original_explanation: The magic phrase you say to the sales associate at SM: "Hi, Miss, baka pwedeng **matulungan**?" Also the thing you wish your friends would do when you're moving apartments instead of just saying "Kaya mo 'yan!"
usage_notes: 'Matulungan' can mean both 'to be helped' (object-focus) and 'to be able to help' (potential mood). The context clarifies the meaning. Ex: 'Sana matulungan kita' (I hope I can help you). Ex: 'Sana matulungan ako' (I hope I can be helped).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paano kita **matutulungan** sa iyong problema?","translation":"How can I **help** you with your problem?"},{"sentence":"Salamat at **natulungan** mo akong mahanap ang nawawala kong aso.","translation":"Thank you for being **able to help** me find my missing dog."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahan na magsalita o magsulat ng isang wika nang mahusay, malinaw, at walang kahirap-hirap.
original_explanation: This is your level of skill in speaking a language. 'Yung friend mong BPO na ang galing mag-English, may tatas siya sa pagsasalita. It's not just about knowing the words, but using them smoothly, like a pro. Parang pag-explain mo sa magulang mo kung bakit kailangan mo ng bagong phone—dapat may tatas para convincing.
usage_notes: Madalas ginagamit sa pariralang "tatas sa pagsasalita" (fluency in speaking).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Humanga ang lahat sa **tatas** ng kanyang pananagalog.","translation":"Everyone was impressed by the **fluency** of his Tagalog."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng **tatas** sa Ingles para sa trabahong iyon.","translation":"**Eloquence** in English is needed for that job."}]

translation: was induced; was persuaded (negatively); was incited
meaning_filipino: Ang mapilit o mahikayat na gumawa ng isang bagay, kadalasan ay isang masamang gawain, dahil sa udyok o impluwensya ng iba.
original_explanation: This isn't just simple persuasion. This is when you're talked into doing something you know you probably shouldn't, like skipping work or buying a ridiculously expensive gadget. It has a slightly negative flavor, like being peer-pressured. "Hindi ko naman talaga gustong sumama, pero nabuyo ako ng mga kaibigan ko." It's the "the devil on my shoulder made me do it" excuse.
usage_notes: Carries a connotation of being persuaded into a negative or impulsive action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nabuyo** siyang sumali sa gulo dahil sa mga sinabi ng kanyang barkada.","translation":"He **was incited** to join the trouble because of what his friends said."},{"sentence":"Dala ng matinding pangangailangan, **nabuyo** siyang magnakaw.","translation":"Driven by extreme need, he **was induced** to steal."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa anumang bagay na nagmula o may kaugnayan sa bansang Rusya at sa kultura nito. Maaari ring tumukoy sa mamamayan ng Rusya.
original_explanation: The people from the land of vodka, matrioshka dolls, and really, really cold winters. If you're talking about the language, the people, or that one friend who loves Dostoevsky, you'd call them Ruso.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun (a Russian person) or an adjective (Russian culture).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kaibigan kong si Ivan ay isang **Ruso**.","translation":"My friend Ivan is a **Russian**."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan niya ang panitikang **Ruso**.","translation":"She is studying **Russian** literature."}]

translation: to be able to please; to be able to give pleasure
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang magdulot ng saya, galak, o kasiyahan sa iba.
original_explanation: This is the goal of every 'pasalubong' you bring home, every joke you tell to make your friends laugh, or every 'good job' you give to a teammate. It's the ability to spark joy, Marie Kondo style, but for people's feelings.
usage_notes: A compound verb indicating the ability to cause delight or please someone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang karangalan ang **makapagbigay-lugod** sa ating mga magulang.","translation":"It is an honor **to be able to please** our parents."},{"sentence":"Sana'y **makapagbigay-lugod** ang munti kong handog sa iyo.","translation":"I hope my small gift **can give you pleasure**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-iiwan ng isang bagay na may halaga bilang garantiya o kolateral para sa isang utang.
original_explanation: The national sport during 'petsa de peligro.' It's when you temporarily break up with your alahas (jewelry) or gadgets at a pawnshop just to get through the week. You promise to come back for them, but sometimes... life happens. 'See you again... maybe.'
usage_notes: The verb is often inflected as 'isangla' (to pawn something) or 'magsangla' (to perform the act of pawning).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napilitan siyang **isangla** ang singsing na pamana ng kanyang lola.","translation":"She was forced **to pawn** the ring inherited from her grandmother."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **isangla** ang kinabukasan mo para sa panandaliang ligaya.","translation":"Don't **mortgage** your future for temporary happiness."}]

translation: to send help to; to aid someone
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapadala o pagbibigay ng tulong o saklolo sa isang tao o lugar na nangangailangan.
original_explanation: Ito ang response sa "pasaklolo". Kung may sumigaw ng "Tulong!", ang paglapit mo para tumulong ay ang akto ng pasaklolohan. Ito yung ginagawa ng mga rescue team sa mga biktima ng baha, o yung ginagawa ng best friend mo kapag tumawag kang umiiyak dahil sa breakup. You are answering the call for help.
usage_notes: Focuses on the act of providing aid to the person/place in need. Command form: "Pasaklolohan ninyo sila!" (Send help to them!)
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **pasaklolohan** kaagad ang mga na-trap sa gumuhong gusali.","translation":"Help must **be sent immediately** to those trapped in the collapsed building."},{"sentence":"Pinuntahan ng mga kapitbahay upang **pasaklolohan** ang nasunugang pamilya.","translation":"The neighbors went to **aid** the family whose house burned down."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggalaw pataas o pababa sa nilalaman ng isang digital na screen.
original_explanation: Ang pambansang libangan ng Pilipinas habang nasa banyo, nakapila, o naghihintay ng ka-date. Ito yung ginagawa mo ng 2 AM, promising yourself "isang post na lang," pero inabot ka na ng umaga kaka-magscroll sa TikTok.
usage_notes: A very common Taglish verb, essential for modern digital life.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hilig kong **magscroll** sa Instagram bago matulog.","translation":"I like **to scroll** through Instagram before sleeping."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang puro **magscroll**, may trabaho ka pang dapat tapusin.","translation":"Don't just keep **scrolling**, you still have work to finish."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na partikular na idinisenyo, angkop, o nakalaan para sa mga lalaki.
original_explanation: The sign on the department store floor that leads you to shirts, pants, and... that three-in-one shampoo/body wash/conditioner. It's the opposite of "pambabae." "Gupit **panlalaki** po," you tell the barber. It can refer to clothes, scents, accessories, or even attitudes that are stereotypically for dudes.
usage_notes: Often used to specify gender-appropriateness for items or styles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa ikalawang palapag ang seksyon ng mga damit na **panlalaki**.","translation":"The section for **men's** clothing is on the second floor."},{"sentence":"Mayroon siyang koleksyon ng mga pabangong **panlalaki**.","translation":"He has a collection of **masculine** perfumes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na kahilingan, karaniwan ay nakasulat, para sa isang bagay tulad ng trabaho, pagpasok sa isang institusyon, o pag-apruba sa isang pautang. Maaari rin itong tumukoy sa isang computer program o software.
original_explanation: That dreaded form you have to fill out for a job, a visa, or a loan, where you suddenly question all your life choices. Also, the reason your phone storage is always full (shoutout to all the mobile games and social media apps). 'I-download mo lang yung aplikasyon.'
usage_notes: Has a dual meaning: a formal request (like a job application) and a software application (app). Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasa ako ng **aplikasyon** para sa bagong trabaho.","translation":"I submitted an **application** for a new job."},{"sentence":"Aling **aplikasyon** sa phone mo ang paborito mo?","translation":"Which **application** on your phone is your favorite?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagbibigay ng tulong, suporta, o pagtugon sa pangangailangan ng iba; ang pagganap sa isang tungkulin o trabaho para sa isang tao, organisasyon, o sa bayan.
original_explanation: This is the core concept of every BPO agent, government employee, and your favorite 'tindera' at the 'sari-sari' store. It's 'Serbisyo, hindi negosyo.' From 'paglilingkod-bayan' (public service) to serving customers with a smile (even when you don't feel like it), it's all about putting others' needs first. It's the reason you say 'po' and 'opo' to your boss.
usage_notes: Commonly used in contexts of public service, customer service, and religious service.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tapat na **paglilingkod** sa bayan ay isang malaking karangalan.","translation":"Honest **service** to the country is a great honor."},{"sentence":"Salamat sa iyong maraming taon ng **paglilingkod** sa aming kumpanya.","translation":"Thank you for your many years of **service** to our company."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang estado ng pagiging malakas, masigla, at puno ng buhay; enerhiya at lakas.
original_explanation: The energy you wish you had on a Monday morning. Ito yung 'ganado' level 999. Yung lolo na nag-zuzumba pa rin at 80 years old? Puno ng bitalidad 'yan. It's the life force that makes you want to do things, not just "sanaol".
usage_notes: A more formal or literary word for energy and vigor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang regular na ehersisyo ay nagpapanatili ng **bitalidad** ng katawan.","translation":"Regular exercise maintains the body's **vitality**."},{"sentence":"Kahit siya'y may edad na, hindi pa rin nababawasan ang kanyang **bitalidad**.","translation":"Even though he is old, his **vitality** has not diminished."}]

translation: to strike with force; to perform exceptionally well
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpalo o paghampas nang may buong lakas. Sa makabagong gamit, tumutukoy din ito sa paggawa ng isang bagay nang may pambihirang galing o sigla.
original_explanation: 'Yung dance group na humataw sa stage na parang wala nang bukas. Or 'yung top agent sa BPO na humataw sa sales at na-hit ang quota for the whole team. It's going all out, 110%, no-holds-barred performance. Hataw kung hataw!
usage_notes: Has a literal meaning of 'to strike' and a more common, modern meaning of 'to perform with great energy and skill'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Humataw** sa pagsayaw ang mga kalahok sa kumpetisyon.","translation":"The contestants **performed energetically** in the dance competition."},{"sentence":"**Humataw** siya ng martilyo sa pako.","translation":"He **struck** the nail hard with a hammer."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang batang halaman na itinatanim, karaniwang mula sa buto, na ililipat sa permanenteng lugar kapag lumaki na.
original_explanation: The baby plant you grow in a small pot or tray before moving it to the main garden. It's the 'probie' stage of a plant's life. Figuratively, it's used for ideas or children—the 'seedlings' of the future. "Ang mga kabataan ang punla ng ating bayan."
usage_notes: Common in agriculture and gardening. Also used metaphorically.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inilipat na ng magsasaka ang mga **punla** ng palay sa bukid.","translation":"The farmer has already transferred the rice **seedlings** to the field."},{"sentence":"Ang bawat mabuting gawa ay parang **punla** na balang araw ay mamumunga.","translation":"Every good deed is like a **seedling** that will one day bear fruit."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking katulong o lingkod na karaniwang gumagawa ng mas mabibigat na gawain sa isang tahanan.
original_explanation: The male version of the 'utusang babae'. He's the one tasked with fixing the leaky faucet, carrying the heavy sacks of rice, or washing the car. Like its female counterpart, this term is also a bit outdated. Think of him as the all-around handyman or 'boy' of the house in older contexts.
usage_notes: Less common than 'utusang babae'. 'Katulong na lalaki' or specific roles like 'hardinero' (gardener) or 'driver' are more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha sila ng **utusang lalaki** para tumulong sa pag-aalaga ng kanilang hardin.","translation":"They hired a **male helper** to help maintain their garden."},{"sentence":"Bihira nang marinig ang tawag na **utusang lalaki** sa panahon ngayon.","translation":"The term **male servant** is rarely heard nowadays."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pampalasa na mula sa dinurog na buto ng puno ng Myristica fragrans, na karaniwang ginagamit sa pagluluto at pagbe-bake.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na 'nuez moscada'.
original_explanation: That fancy spice your mom or lola only brings out for Christmas baking or for making a special 'sopas'. It's that warm, slightly sweet, and aromatic powder that screams 'holiday season'. You don't use it every day, but when you do, you know something delicious is coming.
usage_notes: Partikular na tumutukoy sa pampalasang nutmeg.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagyan mo ng kaunting **nuwes muskada** ang iyong bechamel sauce.","translation":"Add a little **nutmeg** to your bechamel sauce."},{"sentence":"Ang amoy ng **nuwes muskada** ay nagpapaalala sa akin ng Pasko.","translation":"The smell of **nutmeg** reminds me of Christmas."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o pagpapagawa ng isang bagay na naaayon sa partikular na sukat, disenyo, o kagustuhan ng isang tao.
original_explanation: This is the opposite of 'add to cart.' It's when you go to a tailor to get a Barong Tagalog that fits you perfectly, or commission an artist for a portrait. It's the 'bespoke' life, for when off-the-rack just won't do. More effort, more expensive, but totally worth it.
usage_notes: Implies commissioning a specialist (a tailor, carpenter, artist, etc.) to create something unique. The resulting object is called 'pasadya'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagpasadya** ako ng damit para sa kasal ng kapatid ko.","translation":"I **had a dress custom-made** for my sister's wedding."},{"sentence":"Saan ka **nagpasadya** ng iyong barong?","translation":"Where did you **have your barong custom-made**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malangis at madulas na substansiya, karaniwang ginagamit bilang pampadulas sa mga makinarya o sa pagluluto.
original_explanation: 'Yung itim at malagkit na pampadulas sa kadena ng bisikleta o sa mga pyesa ng sasakyan. Minsan, ito rin 'yung sebo o mantika mula sa nilutong pagkain. Pag nadumihan ka nito, ang hirap tanggalin sa damit!
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napuno ng **grasa** ang kamay ng mekaniko.","translation":"The mechanic's hands were covered in **grease**."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka at baka matalsikan ka ng **grasa** mula sa kawali.","translation":"Be careful or you might get splattered by **grease** from the pan."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga kilos, gawi, o asal na karaniwang ipinapakita ng isang tagahanga, na maaaring positibo (gaya ng pag-organisa ng mga charity event) o negatibo (gaya ng labis na pagiging mapaghanap o pakikipag-away sa ibang fans).
etymology: Direktang hiram mula sa Ingles na "fan behavior."
original_explanation: Ito yung sinasabi mo kapag may ginawang kakaiba ang isang tao para sa idol niya. "Uy, nag-abang sa airport ng 12 hours? **Fan behavior** yarn?" Puwedeng compliment, puwede ring slight na pang-asar. It's the set of actions that screams "I am a certified stan!"
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin bilang isang mapaglarong puna o deskripsyon sa mga social media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-print ng sarili mong photocard ng idol mo ay sukdulan na **fan behavior**.","translation":"Printing your own photocard of your idol is the ultimate **fan behavior**."},{"sentence":"\"Pinanood mo lahat ng V-live niya in one sitting? Grabe, **fan behavior** na 'yan!\"","translation":"\"You watched all of his V-lives in one sitting? Wow, that's some serious **fan behavior**!\""}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangkat ng mga tao na nangangasiwa o namumuno sa isang organisasyon, samahan, o pamahalaan.
original_explanation: The group of people in charge, AKA 'management'. They're the ones who approve your vacation leave, set the company KPIs, and organize the (sometimes awkward) Christmas party. When you hear 'kakausapin tayo ng **pamunuan**,' it's either you're getting a bonus or you're in trouble.
usage_notes: The stress shifts from the verb form. Verb: /pa-mu-nu-AN/. Noun: /pa-mu-NU-an/.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglabas ng bagong memo ang **pamunuan** ng kumpanya.","translation":"The company **management** released a new memo."},{"sentence":"Ang buong **pamunuan** ay dumalo sa mahalagang pagpupulong.","translation":"The entire **leadership** attended the important meeting."}]

meaning_filipino: Mamuno o manguna sa isang grupo, organisasyon, o pagpupulong.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of being the 'bida-bida' in a good way. When you mangulo, you're the boss, the chairman, the president, the team lead. You're the one who calls the shots, facilitates the meeting, and gets blamed when the group project fails. From the barangay captain to the CEO, they all mangulo.
usage_notes: From 'ulo' (head), literally 'to be the head'. 'Pangulo' (President) is a noun derived from this. Not to be confused with 'mang-ulo' (to hit on the head).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang napiling **mangulo** sa aming bagong tatag na kooperatiba.","translation":"He was chosen **to lead** our newly established cooperative."},{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng isang taong may sapat na karanasan upang **mangulo** sa pulong.","translation":"We need someone with enough experience **to preside** over the meeting."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kilos na tapos na kung saan tinakpan o isinilid ang isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pambalot tulad ng papel, plastik, o tela.
original_explanation: The past tense of wrapping something up. Like when you **nagbalot** ng tirang pagkain from the party kasi #probiyaNoMore, or when you finally wrapped that gift you bought two months ago. It's the 'I did it' version of putting something in a container or cover.
usage_notes: This is the completed aspect (past tense) of the verb 'magbalot'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay **nagbalot** ng mga damit para sa kanyang biyahe.","translation":"She **wrapped** clothes for her trip."},{"sentence":"**Nagbalot** ako ng regalo para sa kaarawan mo.","translation":"I **wrapped** a gift for your birthday."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malalim na pag-iisip o pagninilay-nilay sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is what you do at 3 AM, staring at the ceiling, wondering about your life choices. It's your "sana all" moment while scrolling through travel pics, or that deep thought you have while stuck in traffic, questioning the universe and your career path. It's overthinking, but with a more poetic, dramatic flair.
usage_notes: A very literary and deep word, not used in everyday conversation. "Pag-iisip" or "pagninilay" are more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng mahabang **pag-ino** bago gumawa ng malaking desisyon.","translation":"Long **contemplation** is needed before making a big decision."},{"sentence":"Sa kanyang **pag-ino**, natuklasan niya ang tunay na kahulugan ng kaligayahan.","translation":"In his **reflection**, he discovered the true meaning of happiness."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malinaw at walang lasa na sangkap sa pagkain, na nagmula sa collagen ng hayop, ginagamit bilang pampabuo o pampakunat sa mga pagkain tulad ng gulaman, jelly, at dessert.
original_explanation: That jiggly, wiggly stuff you find in Filipino desserts! It's the key ingredient for making 'gulaman' for your sago't gulaman, the colorful cubes in your fruit salad, or that fancy coffee jelly. In the palengke, you'd ask for the powdered **gelatin** or the pre-made bars. It's the foundation of many pampalamig and panghimagas that make the Pinoy heat bearable.
usage_notes: While 'gelatin' is understood, the word 'gulaman' is more commonly used to refer to the jelly-like substance itself, especially the one made from seaweed (agar-agar).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating tunawin ang **gelatin** powder sa mainit na tubig.","translation":"We need to dissolve the **gelatin** powder in hot water."},{"sentence":"Paborito kong sahog sa fruit salad ang pulang **gelatin**.","translation":"My favorite ingredient in fruit salad is the red **jelly**."}]

meaning_filipino: Sadyain na magdulot ng takot sa isang tao o hayop sa pamamagitan ng salita, gawa, o pananakot.
etymology: From 'takot' (fear) + '-in' (suffix indicating action upon an object).
original_explanation: What your older sibling did to you as a kid with stories about the 'aswang'. Or what you do to your friend who's afraid of cockroaches. Also, what your boss does when they say, "We need to talk." 'Wag mo akong takutin, hindi ako aatras!'
usage_notes: 'Takutin' is the act of scaring someone, while 'matakot' is the state of being scared.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **takutin** ang bata, iiyak iyan.","translation":"Don't **scare** the child, he will cry."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan siyang **takutin** ng mga bully, pero hindi siya natinag.","translation":"The bullies tried to **frighten** him, but he was not intimidated."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpapahinga sa hinaharap kung saan ang katawan at isipan ay nasa estado ng kawalang-malay.
original_explanation: The most beautiful promise you can make to yourself after a long day of adulting. "After this one last email, **tutulog** na ako." It's the future tense of escape, the ultimate goal at the end of a toxic workday or a marathon of chores. It's the 'sana all' for insomniacs.
usage_notes: This is the actor-focus, future tense form of the verb 'tulog' (to sleep).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaga akong **tutulog** mamaya dahil may pasok ako bukas.","translation":"I **will sleep** early tonight because I have work tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Saan ka **tutulog** pagkatapos ng party?","translation":"Where **will you sleep** after the party?"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa panahon, sandali, o pangyayaring nagdaan na; lumipas na.
original_explanation: This is the official word for your past. The 'mga nakalilipas na araw' is your throwback Thursday content. It's the ex you see on your Facebook memories, the 'what could have been.' It's everything that's already happened, the good, the bad, and the cringey.
usage_notes: Almost always used to refer to time (e.g., araw, taon, sandali). The form 'lumipas' is more common as a standalone verb. 'Nakalilipas' often acts as an adjective modifying a time noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag na nating balikan ang mga masasakit na alaala ng **nakalilipas**.","translation":"Let's not revisit the painful memories of the **past**."},{"sentence":"Sa bawat **nakalilipas** na sandali, lalo siyang nangungulila.","translation":"With every **bygone** moment, she misses him even more."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahan ng isip na matuto, umunawa, mangatwiran, magplano, lumutas ng problema, at mag-isip nang abstrakto.
original_explanation: Ito yung skill na kailangan mo para masagutan ang logic exam sa job application, maintindihan ang plot twist ng K-drama, at para malaman kung totoo o "scam" yung investment offer ng tita mo. Hindi lang 'to book smarts, kasama na rin dito ang street smarts at emotional quotient (EQ). Basically, your brain's processing power.
usage_notes: Maaari ring tumukoy sa impormasyong nakalap, lalo na sa kontekstong militar o espiya (e.g., "intelligence report").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinahangaan siya dahil sa kanyang angking **intelihensya** at kabaitan.","translation":"She is admired for her natural **intelligence** and kindness."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng masusing **intelihensya** para malutas ang kumplikadong kasong ito.","translation":"Careful **intelligence** (gathering) is needed to solve this complicated case."}]

meaning_filipino: Patungo sa katapusan; panghuli o pampinid.
original_explanation: The 'last na talaga, pramis' part of anything. The 'pawakas' na kanta at a concert before the encore, the 'pawakas' na slide in a presentation before the Q&A, or the 'pawakas' na hugot line before you finally decide to move on.
usage_notes: Can also function as an adjective ('pawakas na salita' - concluding words).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pawakas** na talumpati ay nagbigay ng pag-asa sa lahat.","translation":"His **concluding** speech gave hope to everyone."},{"sentence":"**Pawakas** na ang palabas nang dumating kami.","translation":"The show was already **nearing its end** when we arrived."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang unang buwan ng taon sa kalendaryong Gregorian, na mayroong tatlumpu't isang araw.
original_explanation: The month of new beginnings, new gym memberships that will be forgotten by February, and the "New Year, New Me" posts. It's also when you're at your poorest because you spent all your money during Christmas. Panahon ng pagbabayad ng utang from all the 12.12 sales.
usage_notes: Palaging nagsisimula sa malaking titik bilang isang pangngalang pantangi.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa **Enero** ang kaarawan ng aking ina.","translation":"My mother's birthday is in **January**."},{"sentence":"Maraming pista sa Pilipinas tuwing buwan ng **Enero**.","translation":"There are many festivals in the Philippines during the month of **January**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkuha ng bulaklak, bunga, o dahon mula sa tangkay o sanga nito sa pamamagitan ng mga daliri.
original_explanation: This is what you do in your Lola's garden when she's not looking. You see a perfect rose or a ripe mango and you just have to have it. That's 'pumitas'. It's also what you do to get sampaguita to make a lei. A very specific, delicate kind of 'getting'.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to picking by hand, usually from a plant or tree.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais kong **pumitas** ng isang rosas para sa iyo.","translation":"I want to **pick** a rose for you."},{"sentence":"**Pumitas** kami ng hinog na mangga mula sa puno.","translation":"We **picked** ripe mangoes from the tree."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal para sa isang kabataan o tinedyer.
etymology: Slang, portmanteau of "bago" (new) and "tao" (person), popularized by the 1984 film "Bagets".
original_explanation: The OG Pinoy slang for 'teenager', coming from 'bagong tao' (new person). Before there were 'Gen Z' or 'millennials', there were 'bagets'. It's what your tito calls you when you're still in high school or college, probably while reminiscing about the 80s movie of the same name.
usage_notes: Considered somewhat dated slang by younger generations but is still widely understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Noong kami ay mga **bagets** pa, simple lang ang aming kasiyahan.","translation":"When we were still **teenagers**, our joys were simple."},{"sentence":"Puno ng mga **bagets** ang mall tuwing Sabado.","translation":"The mall is full of **youths** every Saturday."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging walang kabuluhan, kahalagahan, o naiwang marka sa paglipas ng panahon.
original_explanation: This is the fear of every artist, writer, or influencer—to be forgotten. It's the feeling of being a 'saling-pusa' (tag-along cat) in the grand scheme of things. It's the opposite of being a 'Marites' whose stories live on forever. It's being historically irrelevant.
usage_notes: A deep, philosophical term. The root 'kasaysayan' means 'history' but also 'significance' or 'meaning'. So 'kawalang-kasaysayan' can mean both being without a history and being without significance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kawalang-kasaysayan** ng kanyang buhay ay nagdulot sa kanya ng matinding kalungkutan.","translation":"The **insignificance** of his life brought him deep sadness."},{"sentence":"Labanan natin ang **kawalang-kasaysayan** sa pamamagitan ng pag-alala sa ating mga bayani.","translation":"Let's fight against **historical irrelevance** by remembering our heroes."}]

translation: to have a drinking session; to drink together
meaning_filipino: Ang sama-samang pag-inom ng alak o anumang inuming nakalalasing, karaniwan bilang isang paraan ng sosyalisasyon.
original_explanation: The Filipino's answer to group therapy. It's where secrets are spilled, hugot lines are born, and someone inevitably starts singing "My Way" on the karaoke machine. It starts with "Tara, isang bote lang" and ends with the sun rising.
usage_notes: Implies a social gathering focused on drinking alcoholic beverages.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkayayaan ang magkakaibigan na **mag-inuman** pagkatapos ng trabaho sa Biyernes.","translation":"The friends decided to **have a drinking session** after work on Friday."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumatakbo o kumikilos sa isang tuwid na linya o direksyon nang walang pagliko; pagtungo nang direkta sa isang partikular na lugar.
original_explanation: This is the "no side trips" verb. After work, instead of going for milk tea, you *dumidiretso* home. When the jeepney driver doesn't make any unnecessary stops, *dumidiretso* siya. It's the opposite of "ligaw," both in navigation and in love.
usage_notes: Progressive form of 'dumiretso'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dumidiretso** ako sa opisina pagkatapos ihatid ang mga bata sa eskwela.","translation":"I **go straight** to the office after dropping the kids off at school."},{"sentence":"Bakit hindi ka **dumidiretso** ng uwi galing sa trabaho?","translation":"Why don't you **head directly** home from work?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan, karaniwang yari sa plastik o metal na may hawakan, na ginagamit kasama ng walis upang kolektahin ang dumi o basura mula sa sahig.
original_explanation: The trusty sidekick of the 'walis tingting' or 'walis tambo'. It’s the unsung hero of 'general cleaning' day. It's always a struggle to get that last frustrating line of dirt into it without leaving a trail.
usage_notes: Formed from 'pan-' (instrument) and 'dampot' (to pick up with fingers).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakikuha ng walis at **pandampot** para malinis ang mga kalat.","translation":"Please get the broom and **dustpan** to clean up the mess."},{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng bagong **pandampot** dahil sira na ang luma.","translation":"Mom bought a new **dustpan** because the old one was broken."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagtutuon ng pansin, kasanayan, o pag-aaral sa isang partikular na larangan o paksa.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you decide to focus on one thing, like that one friend who only knows how to cook adobo, but it's the best adobo you've ever tasted. It's the verb form of becoming an 'expert' or 'specialist'. Your Tita who only sells one specific kind of kakanin? She's mastered the art of pag-espesyalistahan.
usage_notes: Often used in academic, professional, or technical contexts. The hyphen is common due to the foreign root word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Plano kong **pag-espesyalistahan** ang cyber security sa aking pag-aaral.","translation":"I plan to **specialize in** cyber security in my studies."},{"sentence":"Dapat nating **pag-espesyalistahan** ang paggawa ng produktong ito para tayo ang maging numero uno.","translation":"We should **specialize in** making this product so we can be number one."}]

translation: grouping together; forming a coalition or alliance
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o akto ng pagbubuklod-buklod o pag-iisa ng iba't ibang pangkat o indibidwal para sa isang partikular na layunin.
etymology: From `pag-` (verbal noun prefix) + reduplication of `sapi` (to join, to affiliate).
original_explanation: This is what happens when different barkadas decide to team up for a bigger project, like winning the intramurals or organizing a huge birthday surprise. It's like forming an Avengers-level team, but for school activities or office politics. It's the 'United we stand, divided we fall' but make it Pinoy.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of politics, organizations, or social groups. The reduplication implies a more complex or multi-party joining.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagsasapi-sapi** ng mga partido ng oposisyon ay isang malaking hamon sa kasalukuyang administrasyon.","translation":"The **grouping together** of the opposition parties is a huge challenge for the current administration."}]

meaning_filipino: Magkabuhol-buhol o magkasanit-sanit sa isang paraang magulo o masalimuot.
etymology: From the root 'sala' (to filter, to miss) but reduplicated to mean intertwining, like a sieve's mesh.
original_explanation: Imagine the wires behind your TV, the Christmas lights you just took out of the box, or the traffic in EDSA during rush hour. That's magsâla-salâ. It's when things get tangled up in a complex, crisscrossing mess. It can also describe how rumors or 'chismis' spread and get complicated.
usage_notes: The stress pattern is important: magsâla-salâ. It implies a complex, often messy, network or pattern.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-**magsâla-salâ** ang mga kable ng kuryente pagkatapos ng bagyo.","translation":"The electric cables **became intertwined** after the storm."},{"sentence":"Sa kanyang isipan, nag-**magsâla-salâ** ang mga alaala ng nakaraan.","translation":"In his mind, memories of the past **crisscrossed**."}]

translation: to be at the entrance; to be what one first sees
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging nasa unahan o bukana ng isang lugar; ang unang makita o maranasan pagdating.
original_explanation: The moment you open the door and something 'bumungad' (appears right in front of you). It could be a surprise party, your dog, or a mountain of laundry. It's the first thing that greets your senses upon entering a space. 'Pagbukas ko ng FB, mukha agad ng ex ko ang bumungad sa akin.' (When I opened FB, my ex's face was the first thing I saw.)
usage_notes: The actor-focus form 'bumungad' is more commonly used in active sentences (e.g., 'Bumungad sa akin ang...').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malaking tarpaulin ang **bumungad** sa mga bisita.","translation":"A large tarpaulin was the **first thing seen** by the visitors at the entrance."},{"sentence":"Pagpasok sa kwarto, kalat ang **bumungad** sa kanya.","translation":"Upon entering the room, a mess was the **first thing she saw**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan o kagamitan na ginagamit sa paghiwa o pagputol ng mga bagay, karaniwan ay pagkain.
original_explanation: Your trusty kutsilyo in the kitchen. The bread knife, the butcher knife, even the tiny knife for your calamansi. Anything that helps you slice and dice, that's your panghiwa. It's the weapon of choice for every kusinero and kusinera preparing for the Noche Buena feast.
usage_notes: A general term for any slicing tool.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakikuha nga ng **panghiwa** ng sibuyas.","translation":"Please get the slicer for the onions."},{"sentence":"Matalas ang bagong **panghiwa** na binili ni nanay.","translation":"The new **slicer** mom bought is sharp."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkontrol o pagpapakita ng kapangyarihan sa isang tao, bagay, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung ginagawa ng team mo sa Mobile Legends kapag lamang na lamang na kayo, or 'yung ginagawa ng mic hog sa karaoke. It's when you assert so much control, the other party has no choice but to submit. "Dominahin mo ang stage!"
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of power, competition, and relationships.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **dominahin** ka ng iyong takot.","translation":"Don't let your fear **dominate** you."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **dominahin** natin ang laro mula sa simula.","translation":"We need **to dominate** the game from the start."}]

meaning_filipino: Mayroon o naglalabas ng masamang amoy; hindi kaaya-aya sa pang-amoy.
original_explanation: The smell of your gym clothes after a week, the mysterious odor from the back of the fridge, or the estero you pass by on your commute. That's mabaho. It’s the kind of smell that makes you scrunch up your face and ask, "Ano 'yun?!"
usage_notes: A basic and direct word for describing bad smells.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itapon mo na 'yan, **mabaho** na ang amoy.","translation":"Throw that away, it already smells **stinky**."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko matiis ang **mabaho** na basura sa labas.","translation":"I can't stand the **foul-smelling** trash outside."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-uudyok o pagsusulsol sa isang tao upang magalit, makipag-away, o gumawa ng masama.
original_explanation: Ito yung ginagawa ng officemate mong "Marites" na binubulungan ka ng, "Uy, narinig mo ba sabi ni ano tungkol sa'yo? Kung ako sa'yo, 'di ko papalampasin 'yun." Basically, adding fuel to the fire para magkagulo. The art of starting drama.
usage_notes: Madalas na may negatibong konotasyon, na nagpapahiwatig ng masamang hangarin na magdulot ng hidwaan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pang-uupat** niya ang naging sanhi ng kanilang pag-aaway.","translation":"His **instigation** was the cause of their fight."},{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na ang **pang-uupat** sa mga bata.","translation":"Stop **inciting** the children."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi nagkasala o nakagawa ng mali; malinis sa anumang paratang.
original_explanation: This is the face you make when your mom asks who ate the last piece of leche flan. It's the 'hindi ako, promise!' defense. It can be a legal term (not guilty) or a description of someone pure of heart, like a newborn baby or a puppy that just chewed your new slippers. They just don't know any better!
usage_notes: Can be used in legal, moral, or casual contexts to mean guiltless.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinatunayan ng korte na siya ay **walang-kasalanan**.","translation":"The court proved that he was **not guilty**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga bata ay isinilang na **walang-kasalanan**.","translation":"Children are born **innocent**."}]

meaning_filipino: Alisin o itakwil bilang kasapi ng isang samahan, lalo na sa simbahan, dahil sa isang malubhang kasalanan.
original_explanation: The ultimate "you can't sit with us." This is when the church officially kicks you out. It's like being blocked and unfriended by God's fan club on a cosmic scale. Seryosong-seryosong "cancel culture" ito, a-la medieval times.
usage_notes: Isang pormal na terminong panrelihiyon. Madalas matagpuan sa mga tekstong pangkasaysayan o panrelihiyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagbanta ang pari na **eskomulgahin** ang sinumang susuway sa utos ng simbahan.","translation":"The priest threatened to **excommunicate** anyone who would defy the church's command."},{"sentence":"Maaari kang **eskomulgahin** kung mapatunayang ikaw ay isang erehe.","translation":"You can be **excommunicated** if you are proven to be a heretic."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalipunan o pangkat ng mga kliyente o parokyano ng isang negosyo, propesyonal, o establisyimento.
original_explanation: Ito ang 'squad' o 'fanbase' ng isang negosyo. Kung ang 'kliente' ay isa lang, ang 'klientela' ay ang buong tropa ng mga suki mo. Ito yung mga taong laging bumabalik sa'yo, kaya alagaan mo sila. Isipin mo ang loyal followers ng isang influencer—ganun ang klientela sa isang business.
usage_notes: Isang alternatibong baybay para sa 'kliyentela', na siyang mas karaniwang ginagamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malakas ang **klientela** ng bagong bukas na kapihan.","translation":"The newly opened coffee shop has a strong **clientele**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsuot ng kapote, isang kasuotang hindi tinatablan ng tubig, bilang proteksyon sa ulan.
etymology: From 'mag-' (to wear/use) + 'kapote' (raincoat), which is from Spanish 'capote'.
original_explanation: Your go-to move when it's raining cats and dogs and your payong (umbrella) just won't cut it. Essential gear for motorcycle riders, delivery guys, and anyone who refuses to let the typhoon win. "Bes, magkapote ka, lakas ng ulan!"
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit umuulan, tuloy ang trabaho basta't **magkapote** lang.","translation":"Even if it's raining, work continues as long as one **wears a raincoat**."},{"sentence":"Pinayuhan ng ina ang anak na **magkapote** bago pumasok sa eskwela.","translation":"The mother advised her child to **wear a raincoat** before going to school."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang larong pampalakasan na nilalaro ng dalawang koponan na may siyam na manlalaro bawat isa, gamit ang bat, bola, at guwantes.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na 'baseball', na isinulat ayon sa ponetikong Tagalog.
original_explanation: The sport your balikbayan cousin from the US tries to explain to you, but you're just thinking about basketball. It's that game with the bat, the ball, and the running around in a diamond. We spell it how we say it: beysbol.
usage_notes: Ang 'baseball' ay karaniwan ding ginagamit. Ang 'beysbol' ay ang naka-Filipinong baybay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nanonood kami ng laro ng **beysbol** sa telebisyon.","translation":"We are watching a **baseball** game on television."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang partikular na kombinasyon at proporsyon ng iba't ibang sangkap upang makabuo ng isang nais na lasa, amoy, o kulay.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na 'templar' (to temper, to mix).
original_explanation: The magic that makes your mom's adobo different from your tita's. It's the specific ratio of coffee, creamer, and sugar in your morning cup. When someone says, 'Kulang sa timpla,' it's a polite way of saying, 'This tastes bland AF.'
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa pagluluto at paghahanda ng inumin. Maaari ring gamitin sa metaporikal na paraan para sa emosyon (hal. 'masamang timpla' - bad mood).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Perpekto ang **timpla** ng kanyang sinigang.","translation":"The **flavor profile** of her sinigang is perfect."},{"sentence":"Ikaw na ang bahala sa **timpla** ng juice.","translation":"You be in charge of the **mixture** for the juice."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking pangkat ng mga tao na namumuhay nang magkakasama sa isang organisadong komunidad na may iisang kultura, batas, at mga institusyon.
original_explanation: This is the "We live in a society" meme, but in Tagalog. It's the whole system—the government, the economy, the chismis from your kapitbahay, the traffic in EDSA. It's the collective 'us'. The more formal, textbook word is 'lipunan', but 'sosyedad' is what you use when you're being dramatic.
usage_notes: Madalas gamiting kapalit ng 'lipunan'. Ang 'sosyedad' ay maaari ring magkaroon ng konotasyon ng "high society" o ang mga mayayaman at sikat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga isyung ito ay salamin ng mga malalim na problema sa ating **sosyedad**.","translation":"These issues are a reflection of the deep-seated problems in our **society**."}]

meaning_filipino: Labis na pagkabalisa, pag-aalala, o pagkainis dahil sa isang problema.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung feeling na 'di ka mapakali. Para kang na-seen-zone ng boss mo sa isang importanteng tanong, o 'yung kapitbahay mong alas-singko ng umaga nagvi-videoke. You're not just annoyed, you're mentally drained and stewing in it. You are konsumido.
usage_notes: Describes a state of being mentally and emotionally drained by a persistent problem or annoyance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Konsumido** ang ale dahil hindi pa umuuwi ang kanyang anak.","translation":"The lady is **vexed** because her child has not yet come home."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong maging **konsumido** sa maliliit na bagay.","translation":"Don't get too **consumed by worry** over small things."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginagamit sa pagtukoy o pagturo sa isang tao, bagay, o lugar na nasa malayo ngunit abot pa rin ng tanaw.
original_explanation: 'Yan yung isasagot mo pag tinanong ka, "Nasaan na 'yung pangarap mo?" sabay turo sa malayo. "Hayun, o! Ang layo pa." It's for pointing at something far away, like your sweldo on the 14th of the month. So close, yet so far.
usage_notes: Iba ito sa "ayan" (near the speaker), "iyan" (near the person being spoken to), at "doon" (there, far, often out of sight). Ang "hayun" ay para sa malayo ngunit nakikita.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hayun** na ang bus na hinihintay natin!","translation":"**There** is the bus we've been waiting for!"},{"sentence":"Tingnan mo, **hayun** ang bulkang Mayon sa di-kalayuan.","translation":"Look, **there** is Mayon volcano in the distance."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pamantayan, huwaran, o modelo na ginagamit bilang batayan ng paghahambing o pagsusuri.
etymology: The connection to 'sungkad' (to probe) is semantic, possibly from 'probing/measuring against a standard'.
original_explanation: This is your 'gold standard,' your 'benchmark,' your 'peg.' It's the person, thing, or KPI (Key Performance Indicator) that you measure everything else against. 'Siya ang sungkaran ng kagandahan.' (She's the standard of beauty). In a BPO setting, it's the top agent's stats that everyone else is compared to.
usage_notes: This is a very formal and somewhat archaic word. 'Pamantayan' or 'huwaran' are much more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga gawa ang naging **sungkaran** para sa mga susunod na henerasyon ng mga artista.","translation":"His works became the **standard** for the next generations of artists."},{"sentence":"Itinuturing nilang **sungkaran** ng katapatan ang kanilang yumaong lider.","translation":"They consider their deceased leader as the **model** of honesty."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pakiusap na pahintulutang subukan ang isang bagay; isang bagay na inaalok para lamang sa pagsubok o eksperimento.
etymology: The `pa-` prefix indicates a request or command + `subok` (try).
original_explanation: The official mantra of every Filipino who sees you eating something interesting. 'Uy, pasubok nga!' It's our national sport, a low-commitment way to sample everything from your friend's new vape flavor to their Jollibee Chickenjoy. It’s a request, a demand, and a term of endearment all rolled into one.
usage_notes: Used as a command or request. Can also function as an adjective meaning 'for trial'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pasubok** naman ng niluluto mong adobo, mukhang masarap!","translation":"**Let me try** that adobo you're cooking, it looks delicious!"},{"sentence":"Itong unang batch ay **pasubok** lang, para malaman kung magugustuhan ng mga customer.","translation":"This first batch is just **for trial**, to see if the customers will like it."}]

translation: to be closed (unintentionally); to cause to be closed
meaning_filipino: Hindi sinasadyang maisara o maisarado. Maaari ring tumukoy sa pagkilos na maging sanhi ng pagsasara ng isang bagay.
etymology: ma- (unintentional action prefix) + pa- (causative prefix) + sara (close)
original_explanation: This is what happens to your favorite milk tea shop when the landlord raises the rent. It's also that "oops" moment when you accidentally slam the car door on someone's hand, causing it to close. "Sorry na, besh! Hindi ko sinasadyang mapasara yung pinto sa daliri mo!" It's the accidental, "ay, hala!" version of closing something.
usage_notes: The 'mapa-' prefix often indicates an unintentional or involuntary action. In this case, it can mean either 'to be unintentionally closed' or 'to unintentionally cause something to close.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa malakas na hangin, biglang **napasara** ang bintana.","translation":"Because of the strong wind, the window was suddenly **closed**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **mapasara** ang isipan mo sa mga bagong ideya.","translation":"Don't let your mind **be closed** to new ideas."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong masugid na nanliligaw o nagpapakita ng labis na pagsuyo at pag-ibig. Tumutukoy din ito sa mismong akto ng masugid na panunuyo.
etymology: From 'tali-' (bound) + 'suyo' (to woo, to please). Literally 'bound by courtship'.
original_explanation: This is the 'extra rice' version of a suitor. A 'talisuyo' is not just any manliligaw; they are the persistent, always-present, will-do-anything-for-you type. They're the ones who bring you food when you're on your shift, serenade you (maybe), and basically make their world revolve around you during the courtship phase. It's intense, borderline 'sana all' levels of panliligaw.
usage_notes: A literary and romantic term, often used to describe a very devoted suitor or the act of being one.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Don Juan ay isang **talisuyo** na handang gawin ang lahat para kay Prinsesa Leonora.","translation":"Don Juan is an **ardent suitor** willing to do everything for Princess Leonora."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang pagiging **talisuyo** ay nagbunga rin sa huli.","translation":"His act of **ardent courtship** finally paid off in the end."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghampas o pagbigay ng isang malakas na tama gamit ang nakakuyom na kamao.
original_explanation: The action of making a fist and hitting something or someone. It can be a literal punch like Manny Pacquiao in the ring, or a figurative one, as in the idiom 'sumuntok sa buwan' (punch the moon), which means trying to do the impossible. It’s a direct, forceful action.
usage_notes: The object that is punched is marked with 'ng' or 'sa'. 'Sumuntok siya ng pader' (He punched a wall).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang galit, **sumuntok** siya sa pader.","translation":"In his extreme anger, he **punched** the wall."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **susuntok** kung hindi ka naman lalabanan.","translation":"Don't **punch** if they're not going to fight back."}]

translation: to give birth to; to be born
meaning_filipino: Iluwal ang isang sanggol mula sa sinapupunan; ang simula ng buhay ng isang tao sa mundo.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'push' notification. It's the grand debut, the world premiere of a new human being. It's when a mother's 'labor' of love finally pays off.
usage_notes: Often used in the past tense 'isinilang' (was born).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dito sa aming bayan **isinilang** ang isang pambansang bayani.","translation":"A national hero **was born** here in our town."},{"sentence":"Nais niyang **isilang** ang kanyang anak sa Pilipinas.","translation":"She wants **to give birth to** her child in the Philippines."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagdaragdag ng tamis sa isang bagay, tulad ng pagkain, inumin, o isang alok.
original_explanation: The command you give when your kape is too strong or your life is too bitter. "Patamisin mo, please!" It's the act of adding sugar, honey, or even sweet words to make something more palatable. Like when you're trying to win someone over, you `patamisin` the deal.
usage_notes: This is the imperative or object-focus form of the verb. It requires an object to be sweetened.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyong **patamisin** ang aking tsaa.","translation":"Please **sweeten** my tea."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **patamisin** ang alok para tanggapin niya.","translation":"The offer needs to **be sweetened** for them to accept it."}]

translation: to have something raised; to increase
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-utos o pagiging sanhi na tumaas ang isang bagay, presyo, o antas.
original_explanation: This is what Meralco and the gas stations do that makes everyone sigh. It's also what you ask your boss for: 'Boss, baka naman pwedeng magpataas ng sahod.' It's the act of making something go up, whether it's a flag, your grade, or your blood pressure.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical height, price, salary, rank, or level.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang kumpanya na **magpataas** ng presyo ng kanilang mga produkto.","translation":"The company decided to **increase** the price of their products."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magpataas** ng iyong kamay kung may tanong ka.","translation":"You need to **raise** your hand if you have a question."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang aklat na naglalaman ng mga dasal o panalangin; isang lugar o silid na itinalaga para sa pagdarasal.
original_explanation: This is your spiritual toolkit. It can be the actual prayer book (like a novena booklet) you carry to church, or it can be the quiet corner in your house where you talk to God. It's your personal Bat-cave for prayer, your direct line to the divine. The place you go to when you need to pray for a sign... or for your Grab to arrive faster.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa aklat ng mga dasal o sa lugar ng pagdarasal. Ang konteksto ang magdidikta ng kahulugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binuklat niya ang kanyang lumang **dalanginan** at nagsimulang magdasal.","translation":"She opened her old **prayer book** and began to pray."},{"sentence":"May maliit na **dalanginan** sa loob ng kanilang bahay para sa pamilya.","translation":"There is a small **oratory** inside their house for the family."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gagawing pagsasabit ng mga nilabhang damit o anumang tela sa sampayan upang matuyo.
etymology: From `mag-` + reduplication of the first syllable of the root `sa-` + `sampay` (to hang clothes). Future tense of `magsampay`.
original_explanation: The daily Filipino weather forecast gamble. You do this hoping it doesn't rain, and when it does, it turns into an Olympic sprint to save the laundry. The person who magsasampay is the designated laundry-person of the house for the day.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to hanging wet items, usually clothes, to dry. This is the future tense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos kong maglaba, ako ay **magsasampay** sa labas.","translation":"After I do the laundry, I **will hang the clothes** outside."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **magsasampay** ng mga basang tuwalya?","translation":"Who **will hang** the wet towels **to dry**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na salita na nangangahulugang "totoo" o "tunay," kadalasang ginagamit bilang pagpapatibay o pagsang-ayon sa isang pahayag.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Ingles na "true" na dinagdagan ng hulaping "-lalu", isang karaniwang pormasyon sa Swardspeak o gay lingo.
original_explanation: The ultimate confirmation from your beshie. It's "true" with extra steps and glitter. Kapag sinabing "trulalu," 100% certified totoo, walang halong chismis. Example: "Maganda ba 'ko?" "Trulalu, mars!" It's the verbal equivalent of a check mark emoji.
usage_notes: Itinuturing na gay lingo o bekimon, ngunit malawakang ginagamit na rin sa pangkalahatang kolokyal na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Trulalu** bang nag-resign na siya sa trabaho?","translation":"Is it **for real** that she already resigned from her job?"},{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng concert, **trulalu**!","translation":"The concert was so good, **really**!"}]

translation: escort; delivery; something brought or delivered
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagdadala o pagsama sa isang tao o bagay patungo sa isang destinasyon. Maaari ring tumukoy ito sa mismong bagay na dinala.
original_explanation: The Filipino version of 'I'll see you out.' Whether it's your Grab driver dropping you off, your jowa walking you to the LRT station, or your mom packing your baon and saying 'hatid ko na 'to sa'yo'—it's an act of service and care. It's the opposite of 'sundo' (to fetch). Hatid is to drop off/escort.
usage_notes: Commonly used in verb forms: `maghatid` (to deliver/escort) and `ihatid` (to be delivered/escorted).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang nag-**hatid** sa akin pauwi kagabi.","translation":"He **escorted** me home last night."},{"sentence":"May **hatid** na pasalubong si Tatay mula sa abroad.","translation":"Dad **brought** souvenirs from abroad."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagsusulat ng mga computer program; isang dalubhasa sa computer programming.
original_explanation: Sila yung mga taong kayang kausapin ang computer sa lenggwaheng hindi mo maintindihan. Madalas puyat, laging may kape sa tabi, at ang sagot sa tanong na "Kamusta?" ay "It's compiling." Kung may problema ka sa computer, i-off at i-on mo lang. Kung ayaw pa rin, tawagin mo ang programmer.
usage_notes: Madalas ginagamit sa industriya ng teknolohiya at impormasyon (IT).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang mahusay na **programmer** ang kailangan ng aming kumpanya.","translation":"Our company needs a skilled **programmer**."},{"sentence":"Nag-aaral siya para maging isang computer **programmer**.","translation":"He is studying to become a computer **programmer**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang hanapbuhay ay ang pag-aalaga o pagbebenta ng mga manok.
original_explanation: Your friendly neighborhood 'tindero' or 'tindera' at the palengke who can chop up a whole chicken in 30 seconds flat. They know the difference between 'pang-tinola' and 'pang-prito' cuts. Also refers to someone who raises chickens, from the cute little chicks to the ones that end up in your adobo.
usage_notes: The prefix 'mag-' + duplicated first syllable of the root + root word often denotes a profession or a person who sells/works with the root word (e.g., magtataho, magbabalut).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng isang kilong manok sa **magmamanok** sa palengke.","translation":"I bought a kilo of chicken from the **chicken vendor** at the market."},{"sentence":"Isang kilalang **magmamanok** ang ama niya sa kanilang probinsya.","translation":"His father is a well-known **poultry raiser** in their province."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi sa gilid ng isang bagay; ang hangganan o dulo ng isang lugar o espasyo.
original_explanation: It's your personal space bubble's boundary. When someone says 'Sa tabi mo,' they mean right next to you, close enough to smell their pabango. It's the edge of the bed you cling to when you're sharing it with a blanket hog.
usage_notes: Very common word. Can be used in many contexts (side of the road, side of a person, etc.).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umupo ka sa **tabi** ko.","translation":"Sit by my **side**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong lumapit sa **tabi** ng bangin.","translation":"Don't get too close to the **edge** of the cliff."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pinulbos na berdeng tsaa mula sa Hapon na ginagamit sa seremonya ng tsaa at bilang sangkap sa mga inumin at pagkain.
original_explanation: The official flavor of titas and broke millennials who want to feel fancy. That green powder you pay ₱180 for in a latte. Some say it tastes like damo (grass), others can't live without it. It's the aesthetic drink of choice.
usage_notes: A direct loanword. Used widely in cafes and restaurants in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko ng **matcha** latte, please.","translation":"I want a **matcha** latte, please."},{"sentence":"Masarap ba talaga ang **matcha** ice cream?","translation":"Is **matcha** ice cream really that good?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpunta sa isang lugar para maglibang, maglakad-lakad, o magmasid sa kapaligiran.
etymology: From 'ma-' + 'pasyal' (a walk, a trip). Likely influenced by Spanish 'pasear' (to walk).
original_explanation: The cure for 'na-bored ako sa bahay.' It's your tita inviting you to 'mamasyal sa mall' (which really means shopping), your friends planning a beach trip, or just you taking a walk in the park to get some fresh air and maybe buy some dirty ice cream. It's the general term for going out for fun.
usage_notes: A very common verb for leisure activities, including strolling, sightseeing, or simply going out for pleasure.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tara, **mamasyal** tayo sa Luneta Park ngayong Linggo.","translation":"Come on, let's **go for a stroll** at Luneta Park this Sunday."},{"sentence":"Gusto nilang **mamasyal** sa Tagaytay para makita ang Bulkang Taal.","translation":"They want to **go sightseeing** in Tagaytay to see Taal Volcano."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpapatilapon o pagwiwisik ng likido papunta sa isang tao, lugar, o bagay, sinasadya man o hindi.
original_explanation: This is the action version of `talsik`. When a speeding car passes through a puddle and gives you a free, muddy shower? Ayun, na-**talsikan** ka. It's the verb form of that "ay, bwisit!" moment when you're the target of the splash.
usage_notes: The object receiving the splash is the focus. 'Tinalsikan niya ako' (He splashed me).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **talsikan** ng tubig ang laptop ko!","translation":"Don't **splash** water on my laptop!"},{"sentence":"Nainis siya nang **talsikan** ng putik ng dumaang traysikel.","translation":"He got annoyed when he was **splashed** with mud by a passing tricycle."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang unang kainan sa umaga, karaniwang binubuo ng sinangag, itlog, at iba pang ulam tulad ng tapa, longganisa, o tuyo.
etymology: Mula sa pandiwang Espanyol na 'almorzar' (kumain ng tanghalian), na nagbago ng kahulugan sa Filipino upang tumukoy sa pagkain sa umaga.
original_explanation: The most important meal of the day, Pinoy style. It's the reason you wake up in the morning. We're talking sinangag (garlic fried rice), itlog (egg), and a choice of your fighter: Tapa (Tapsilog), Longganisa (Longsilog), or Tocino (Tosilog). It's the power-up you need before facing Manila traffic. A verb form is 'mag-almusal' (to eat breakfast).
usage_notes: Maaari ring gamitin bilang pandiwa na may mga panlapi: 'mag-almusal' (kumain ng almusal), 'almusalin' (kainin bilang almusal).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **almusal** natin ngayon?","translation":"What's our **breakfast** today?"},{"sentence":"Huwag kang aalis nang hindi ka pa nag-a-**almusal**.","translation":"Don't leave without having **breakfast** yet."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang nakaangat na plataporma, karaniwang nasa loob ng isang teatro o bulwagan, kung saan nagtatanghal ang mga artista o nagsasalita ang mga panauhin.
original_explanation: The stage. Not just the physical platform in a theater, but also the metaphorical one. 'Yung pangarap mong maging singer? Ang gusto mo ay umakyat sa estrada. It's the place where you perform, give a speech, or get your diploma during graduation. It's your moment in the spotlight. Also, a very famous presidential surname.
usage_notes: More formal than 'entablado' or 'tanghalan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umakyat sa **estrada** ang nagwagi upang tanggapin ang kanyang tropeo.","translation":"The winner went up on the **stage** to receive his trophy."},{"sentence":"Lahat ng mata ay nakatuon sa **estrada** habang nagsasalita ang pangulo.","translation":"All eyes were on the **dais** while the president was speaking."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging taksil o lilo; ang gawain ng pagtataksil sa isang tao, simulain, o sa bayan.
original_explanation: This is some next-level, teleserye villain stuff. It's not just a simple lie; it's the ultimate betrayal. Think of a best friend who steals your jowa, a business partner who runs away with the money, or a politician who breaks every single campaign promise. It's the kind of backstabbing that deserves its own dramatic slow-motion scene with thunder and lightning.
usage_notes: Isang napakapormal at pampanitikang salita. Hindi ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kaliluhan** ni Hudas ay isa sa mga pinakakilalang kuwento ng pagtataksil.","translation":"The **treachery** of Judas is one of the most well-known stories of betrayal."},{"sentence":"Pinarusahan siya dahil sa kanyang **kaliluhan** sa kaharian.","translation":"He was punished for his **perfidy** against the kingdom."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng daanan ng pagkain na nag-uugnay sa lalamunan (pharynx) at sa sikmura.
original_explanation: Ito yung 'expressway' ng kinakain mo mula bibig papuntang tiyan. It's the tube that connects your throat to your stomach. Kapag nakalunok ka ng malaking piraso ng pagkain at parang may na-stuck, 'yan, sa **esopago** mo 'yan nararamdaman.
usage_notes: Isang terminong medikal o siyentipiko. Ang katumbas nito sa karaniwang usapan ay "lalaugan".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagkain ay dumadaan sa **esopago** bago marating ang sikmura.","translation":"Food passes through the **esophagus** before reaching the stomach."},{"sentence":"Inaatake ng acid reflux ang lining ng kanyang **esopago**.","translation":"Acid reflux attacks the lining of his **esophagus**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bahagi ng tradisyonal na bahay na karaniwang yari sa kawayan at walang bubong, na ginagamit bilang hugasan o paliguan.
etymology: Possibly from Spanish 'batalán' or a native term. Its usage is now mostly historical.
original_explanation: Before condos had service areas or laundry rooms, the old-school bahay kubo had a batalan. It's the open-air back porch, usually made of bamboo slats, where you'd wash dishes, do laundry, or even take a quick bath (using a tabo, of course). It's the original "wet kitchen."
usage_notes: This term is archaic and mostly found in historical texts or descriptions of traditional Filipino houses.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghuhugas ng mga pinggan si Lola sa **batalan**.","translation":"Grandma is washing the dishes on the **back porch**."},{"sentence":"Ang sahig ng **batalan** ay gawa sa magkakahiwalay na patpat ng kawayan.","translation":"The floor of the **washing area** is made of separate bamboo slats."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kondisyon o karamdaman na nagdudulot ng hirap sa pagtulog o pananatiling tulog sa gabi.
original_explanation: 'Yung alas-tres na ng madaling araw pero gising na gising pa rin diwa mo, nag-o-overthink sa mga nangyari noong 2015 at nag-sc-scroll sa TikTok. Kapag ang kape ay naging tubig mo at ang gabi ay naging umaga. That's insomnia, the official sponsor of late-night thoughts and eyebags.
usage_notes: A medical and psychological term that has become a common word for sleeplessness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inatake na naman ako ng **insomnia** kagabi kaya puyat ako ngayon.","translation":"I had an attack of **insomnia** again last night that's why I lack sleep today."},{"sentence":"Ang sobrang pag-aalala ay maaaring magdulot ng **insomnia**.","translation":"Excessive worrying can cause **insomnia**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkaputol o pagkalamat ng isang matigas na bagay, karaniwan ay buto, dahil sa puwersa o presyon.
original_explanation: That "oh no" moment when you hear a snap after falling down. This is why you need health insurance. It's the reason for the cast on your friend's arm and their newfound expertise on calcium supplements. It's a literal "break," not the "let's take a break" kind (that's a different kind of pain).
usage_notes: Primarily used in a medical context for bones, but can also be used for other rigid objects that snap or break.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkabali** ng kanyang braso ay dahil sa pagkahulog niya sa bisikleta.","translation":"The **fracture** of his arm was due to falling off his bike."},{"sentence":"Iniinda niya ang sakit mula sa **pagkabali** ng kanyang buto sa paa.","translation":"He is suffering from the pain of the **fracture** of his foot bone."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang inumin na gawa sa katas ng limon, tubig, at asukal.
original_explanation: The ultimate summer drink. It's what you make when life gives you lemons, literally. Perfect for when you're feeling the heat, whether from the sun or from your TL's urgent emails. It's the classier, less intense version of just drinking calamansi juice.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to the sweet and sour drink made from lemons.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumawa si nanay ng malamig na **limunada** para sa meryenda.","translation":"Mom made cold **lemonade** for our snack."},{"sentence":"Magkano ang isang basong **limunada** sa tindahan?","translation":"How much is one glass of **lemonade** at the store?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar na pansamantalang tinitigilan o pinagpapahingahan sa isang paglalakbay; himpilan o istasyon.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung 7-Eleven sa NLEX or SLEX. The official pit stop for bathroom breaks, 'pasalubong' buying, and stretching your legs. Sa BPO world, ito 'yung pantry kung saan ka nagkakape bago bumalik sa battle station mo.
usage_notes: Not as common in modern everyday speech; 'istasyon', 'terminal', or 'stopover' are more frequent. Often found in older texts or specific regional contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aming baryo ang naging **hapitan** ng mga manlalakbay noon.","translation":"Our village used to be the **stopover point** for travelers back then."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tao na pansamantalang humahalili sa gawain ng iba; ang paghalili sa tungkulin.
original_explanation: In the BPO world, this is your guardian angel who takes over your shift so you can finally go on break or log off. "Brad, pa-relyebe muna, CR break lang!" is a sacred prayer. It's the human version of a "save point" in a video game.
usage_notes: Primarily used in a work or duty context, like for guards, nurses, call center agents, etc.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **relyebe** mo mamayang gabi?","translation":"Who is your **reliever** tonight?"},{"sentence":"Hinihintay ko na lang ang **relyebe** ko bago umuwi.","translation":"I'm just waiting for my **relief** before I go home."}]

translation: blurring; the act or process of becoming blurry/unclear
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o kalagayan ng pagiging malabo o pagkawala ng linaw ng isang bagay, tulad ng paningin o isang imahe.
etymology: From `panl-` + reduplication of the first syllable `la-` + `labo` ("blurry, unclear"). This formation indicates a continuous or developing state.
original_explanation: That feeling when you've been staring at your screen for 12 hours straight and everything starts to look hazy. "Grabe ang **panlalabo** ng mata ko." It's also a great metaphor for a relationship na hindi mo na alam kung saan papunta. The lines are blurred, the future is unclear. "May **panlalabo** sa usapan namin, 'di ko na gets kung kami pa ba."
usage_notes: Describes the process or state of becoming blurry. Often refers to eyesight. `Paglabo` is a more common synonym.
