usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **panlalabo** ng kanyang paningin ay senyales na kailangan na niyang magpatingin sa doktor.","translation":"The **blurring** of his vision is a sign that he needs to see a doctor."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa hamog, nagkaroon ng **panlalabo** ang tanawin mula sa bintana.","translation":"Because of the fog, the view from the window experienced **blurring**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kinalabasang halo o ang mismong produkto ng pagtitimpla.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na 'templada' (tempered, mixed).
original_explanation: The finished product. If 'timpla' is the concept, 'timplada' is the concrete result. It's the actual drink you're holding, the final sauce in the pan. 'Okay ba ang timplada ko?' is asking for validation on your bartending or cooking skills.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa natapos at nahalong produkto. Halos kapareho ng 'timpla' ngunit nagbibigay-diin sa resulta.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tikman mo itong **timplada** kong kape.","translation":"Taste this coffee **blend** I made."},{"sentence":"Iba ang **timplada** ng adobo sa bawat rehiyon.","translation":"The **mixture** of adobo is different in every region."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapalaganap ng impormasyon, balita, o programa sa malawak na madla sa pamamagitan ng radyo, telebisyon, o internet.
original_explanation: This is what news anchors, radio DJs, and your favorite vlogger do. It's the act of sending out info, music, or chismis to a massive audience. In the age of social media, everyone can suddenly "magbrodkast" their lunch, their workout, or their unsolicited opinions via Facebook Live or TikTok. You don't need a TV station anymore, just a phone with a data plan.
usage_notes: A Tagalized version of the English word. "Mag-ere" is a less common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang estasyon ng radyo ay **magbo-brodkast** ng special coverage ng eleksyon.","translation":"The radio station will **broadcast** special coverage of the election."},{"sentence":"Gusto niyang **magbrodkast** ng kanyang mga laro sa Twitch.","translation":"He wants to **broadcast** his games on Twitch."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng higit pa sa sapat na dami ng isang bagay; masagana o mayaman.
original_explanation: The opposite of "petsa de peligro." It's that glorious feeling when the buffet table is overflowing, your data allowance is unlimited, or the chismis from your friend is non-stop. It's the fiesta life—bountiful, overflowing, and more than enough for everyone.
usage_notes: Often used with 'sa' to specify what is abundant (e.g., sagana sa prutas). The form 'masagana' is more common in everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sagana** sa isda ang karagatan ng Pilipinas.","translation":"The Philippine seas are **abundant** with fish."},{"sentence":"Nawa'y maging **sagana** ang ating ani ngayong taon.","translation":"May our harvest be **plentiful** this year."}]

translation: to adapt, to derive from, to extract
meaning_filipino: Kumuha ng ideya, paksa, o istilo mula sa isang umiiral na gawa upang gamitin sa paglikha ng bago.
original_explanation: This is what filmmakers do when they turn a Wattpad story into a movie. They **halawin** the plot. It's also what you do when you get 'inspiration' from your classmate's code but change the variable names.
usage_notes: Distinct from 'halawan', 'halawin' refers to adapting concepts or ideas, not physical quantities. It implies transformation or reinterpretation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pelikulang ito ay **halawin** sa isang sikat na nobela.","translation":"This movie will be **adapted** from a famous novel."},{"sentence":"Maraming aral ang maaaring **halawin** sa kanyang talumpati.","translation":"Many lessons can be **extracted** from his speech."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na desisyon o pasya ng isang hukuman, hukom, o anumang may awtoridad sa isang kaso o usapin.
original_explanation: The final boss of decisions. This is the judge's verdict in a court case, the final score in a competition, or your mom's final 'hatol' on whether you can go out or not. It's a decision with weight and consequences. 'Hinatulan na siya ng korte,' or more relatably, 'Ang hatol ng barkada, KKB tayo mamaya.'
usage_notes: Often used in legal contexts. The verb form is `hatulan` (to sentence) or `humatol` (to judge).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinihintay ng lahat ang **hatol** ng mga hurado.","translation":"Everyone is waiting for the jury's **verdict**."},{"sentence":"Mabigat ang **hatol** na ipinataw sa akusado.","translation":"A heavy **sentence** was imposed on the accused."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na sumusuporta sa isang republikanong anyo ng pamahalaan, o isang miyembro ng partidong Republikano.
original_explanation: Ito yung tito mo na laging may opinyon sa pulitika tuwing family reunion, at kadalasan, pabor siya sa isang partikular na partido politikal. Pwede ring tumukoy sa pamahalaan na hindi monarkiya.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pangngalan (isang republikano) o pang-uri (pamahalaang republikano).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay isang tapat na **republikano** at laging bumoboto tuwing eleksyon.","translation":"He is a loyal **republican** and always votes during elections."},{"sentence":"Ang sistemang **republikano** ang umiiral sa ating bansa.","translation":"The **republican** system is what prevails in our country."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang trabaho o sining ay ang pagpipinta, maaaring sa pader ng gusali o sa kanbas bilang isang alagad ng sining.
original_explanation: Can refer to two things: 1) The artist who creates masterpieces, like Juan Luna. 2) The kuya who's an expert at mixing Boysen paint for your fence every 3 years. Both are artists in their own right.
usage_notes: Can refer to both a house painter ('magpipinta') and a fine artist. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpatawag kami ng **pintor** para ayusin ang mga nabakbak na pader.","translation":"We called a **painter** to fix the peeling walls."},{"sentence":"Si Fernando Amorsolo ay isang tanyag na **pintor** na Pilipino.","translation":"Fernando Amorsolo is a famous Filipino **painter** (artist)."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng daan na naka-angat at nakalaan para sa mga taong naglalakad.
original_explanation: In the Philippines, this is a multi-purpose area. It’s a parking lot for motorcycles, a sari-sari store extension, a dining area for the local carinderia, an obstacle course of broken tiles and random poles, and occasionally, a place for people to walk. The Tagalog word is 'bangketa', but everyone knows 'sidewalk'.
usage_notes: The English word is commonly used. The official Filipino term is 'bangketa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bawal magtinda sa **sidewalk** ayon sa utos ng mayor.","translation":"Selling on the **sidewalk** is prohibited according to the mayor's order."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa paglalakad, maraming butas ang **sidewalk**.","translation":"Be careful walking, the **sidewalk** has many holes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na kasunduan o seremonya ng pag-iisang-dibdib; ang pagdiriwang ng pagkasundong magpakasal ng isang magkasintahan.
original_explanation: The pre-game to the wedding championship. It's the formal announcement where both families meet, size each other up, and pretend they love the choice their child made. Think of it as the 'pamamanhikan' but with a fancier, Spanish-derived name.
usage_notes: Isang makalumang termino, madalas na matatagpuan sa mga akdang pampanitikan o pangkasaysayan. Mas karaniwan na ngayon ang 'engagement party' o 'pamamanhikan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatakda ang kanilang **esponsales** sa susunod na buwan.","translation":"Their **betrothal ceremony** is set for next month."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang madre o babaeng kasapi sa orden ng mga Pransiskano, isang samahang panrelihiyon sa Simbahang Katolika.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "Franciscana", ang pambabaeng anyo ng "Franciscano".
original_explanation: Think of it as the female counterpart of a Franciscan friar, like St. Clare of Assisi's squad. They live a life of prayer, simplicity, and service. You probably won't see them on TikTok, but their 'collab' with St. Francis has been a hit for centuries.
usage_notes: Isang tiyak na terminong panrelihiyon na hindi karaniwang ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang madreng **Pransiskana** ay kilala sa kanyang pagiging mapagkumbaba at pagtulong sa mga mahihirap.","translation":"The **Franciscan nun** is known for her humility and helping the poor."}]

translation: to happen to meet; to encounter
meaning_filipino: Di-sinasadyang makatagpo ng isang tao na naglalakad mula sa salungat na direksyon.
original_explanation: 'Yung awkward moment na naglalakad ka sa mall tapos bigla mong nakasalubong 'yung ex mo with their new jowa. Freeze! Do you say hi? Do you pretend you didn't see them? It's that chance encounter with someone walking towards you. It can be a good thing (your crush!) or a bad thing (your landlord on the 29th of the month).
usage_notes: "Maka-" here implies a chance or accidental encounter. It specifically refers to meeting someone face-to-face while moving in opposite directions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing umaga, **nakakasalubong** ko ang aking guro sa daan papuntang eskwelahan.","translation":"Every morning, I **happen to meet** my teacher on the way to school."},{"sentence":"Ayokong **makasalubong** si Ana dahil may utang pa ako sa kanya.","translation":"I don't want to **encounter** Ana because I still owe her money."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o bagay na may pananagutan sa isang pagkakamali, krimen, o hindi kanais-nais na pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is the feeling you get when you ate the last piece of Lechon Kawali and everyone's looking for it. You're not just 'busog', you're also 'may-kasalanan'. It's the 'it wasn't me' stage of a crime, whether it's a broken vase or a broken heart.
usage_notes: Used to describe a person who committed a sin, a mistake, or a crime.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napatunayang **may-kasalanan** ang akusado sa pagnanakaw.","translation":"The accused was proven **guilty** of theft."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, alam kong hindi ikaw ang **may-kasalanan** kung bakit nasira ang printer.","translation":"Don't worry, I know you're not the one **at fault** for why the printer broke."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang manipis na balat na nagsisilbing takip at proteksyon ng mata.
original_explanation: Literally the 'cover of the eye.' This is what gets heavy when you're sleepy during a meeting, or what you put eyeshadow on. Ito 'yung bumibigat kapag 3 AM na pero scroll ka pa rin nang scroll sa phone mo. The OG eye-protector.
usage_notes: Ito ang pinakakaraniwan at tiyak na gamit ng salitang 'talukap' sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumibigat na ang aking mga **talukap ng mata** dahil sa antok.","translation":"My **eyelids** are getting heavy due to sleepiness."},{"sentence":"Naglagay siya ng makintab na pangkulay sa kanyang **talukap ng mata**.","translation":"She applied a shimmery color on her **eyelid**."}]

translation: to prop up, to support with a post
meaning_filipino: Suportahan ang isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng paglalagay ng tukod o anumang patayong suporta upang hindi ito bumagsak o gumuho.
original_explanation: This is the verb for when something is about to collapse and needs a hero. You 'itukod' a piece of wood to hold up a sagging shelf. Emotionally, your friends 'itukod' you when you're feeling down—they become your support system. It's the act of providing a temporary, or sometimes permanent, pillar of support.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for physical support or metaphorically for emotional or financial support.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **itukod** ang sanga ng puno para hindi ito mabali.","translation":"We need to **prop up** the tree branch so it doesn't break."},{"sentence":"**Itinukod** niya ang kanyang mga siko sa mesa habang malalim na nag-iisip.","translation":"He **propped** his elbows on the table while thinking deeply."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng paliwanag sa isang tao o grupo upang maunawaan nila ang isang paksa, isyu, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is the action version of 'paliwanag'. It’s what a manager does during a town hall, what a professor does during a lecture, or what you do when you have to paliwanagan your parents why you need money again. It's the act of shedding light on a topic for a specific audience.
usage_notes: The '-an' suffix makes the verb focus on the person or thing receiving the explanation. "Paliwanagan mo *siya*." (Explain it *to him/her*.)
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **paliwanagan** ang mga bata kung bakit mahalaga ang pag-aaral.","translation":"You need **to explain to** the children why studying is important."},{"sentence":"Pinapunta siya sa opisina ng prinsipal para **paliwanagan** ang kanyang ginawa.","translation":"He was sent to the principal's office to **explain** what he did."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng ulam na nilaga na karaniwang may karne ng baka o manok, saging na saba, kamote, repolyo, at sarsa ng kamatis. Ito ay hango sa 'cocido' ng Espanya.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'puchero', na nangangahulugang 'palayok para sa nilaga' o isang uri ng nilaga.
original_explanation: The Filipino version of the Spanish `cocido`. It's a hearty, tomato-based stew that's like a party in a pot. You've got beef or chicken, chunks of saba bananas (yes, bananas in a stew!), sweet potatoes, cabbage, and sometimes chickpeas. It's that Sunday lunch ulam that makes you want to take a long nap afterwards.
usage_notes: Ang baybay na 'puchero' ay malawakang ginagamit din. Ang kombinasyon ng tamis (mula sa saging at kamote) at alat (mula sa karne at sarsa ng kamatis) ang katangian ng lasa nito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghanda si Lola ng masarap na **putsero** para sa aming pananghalian.","translation":"Grandma prepared a delicious **pochero** for our lunch."},{"sentence":"Ang paborito kong sahog sa **putsero** ay ang saging na saba.","translation":"My favorite ingredient in **pochero** is the saba banana."}]

meaning_filipino: Biglaang at malakas na hilahin ang isang bagay o tao.
etymology: Possibly from Spanish 'jalar' (to pull) + Tagalog affixation.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na bigla kang kinalabit ng kaibigan mo para ipakita ang chismis sa phone niya. O yung pag-agaw sa huling piraso ng lechon sa handaan. It’s not a gentle pull; it’s a 'GIMME THAT' kind of pull. A sudden, forceful, no-questions-asked tug.
usage_notes: This is the object-focus form of the verb. The actor-focus form is 'humaltak'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **haltakin** ang damit ko, masisira!","translation":"Don't **yank** my clothes, they'll get ruined!"},{"sentence":"**Hinaltak** ng pulis ang magnanakaw palabas ng kotse.","translation":"The policeman **pulled** the thief out of the car."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mag-aaral na may pinakamataas na akademikong ranggo sa isang nagtatapos na klase, na karaniwang nagbibigay ng talumpati sa pagtatapos.
etymology: From English 'valedictorian', from Latin 'valedicere' (to say farewell).
original_explanation: Ito yung anak ng kapitbahay niyo na laging bukambibig ng nanay mo. "Tingnan mo si ano, valedictorian! Ikaw, puro ka laro!" Sila yung nagbibigay ng speech sa graduation na nagpapaiyak sa lahat, lalo na sa mga magulang na gumastos ng malaki sa tuition.
usage_notes: Used in the context of graduation and academic achievements.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pangarap ng bawat magulang ay maging **valedictorian** ang kanilang anak.","translation":"The dream of every parent is for their child to be the **valedictorian**."},{"sentence":"Siya ang nahirang na **valedictorian** ng aming batch.","translation":"She was chosen as the **valedictorian** of our batch."}]

translation: to be able to receive one's salary
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng pagkakataon o kakayahang matanggap ang bayad o sweldo para sa ginawang trabaho.
original_explanation: The best feeling ever, especially on the 15th and 30th of the month! 'Yung "Salamat Lord, sa wakas, makakasahod na!" moment. It's the ability to finally get that hard-earned money you've been waiting for. The opposite is 'yung delayed ang sahod at 'di ka pa makasahod. Apir sa mga BPO agents at office workers!
usage_notes: "Maka-" indicates the ability or opportunity to do something. "Sumahod" is the act of receiving salary, while "makasahod" emphasizes the ability or chance to do so.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maghintay lang tayo ng ilang oras at **makakasahod** na rin tayo.","translation":"Let's just wait a few more hours and we'll finally be **able to receive our salary**."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa problema sa payroll, hindi pa kami **makasahod** hanggang ngayon.","translation":"Because of a payroll problem, we haven't been **able to receive our salary** until now."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasabi, pagpapahayag, o paglalantad ng isang kaisipan, damdamin, o impormasyon sa publiko o sa isang tao.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'sana masabi ko' verb. It's what you do when you finally confess your feelings ('**ipahayag** ang pag-ibig'), when a company releases a public statement, or when the pageant host announces the winner. It's making something known, officially. No more secrets, no more marites-level whispers.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Panahon na upang **ipahayag** mo ang iyong tunay na nararamdaman.","translation":"It is time for you to **express** your true feelings."},{"sentence":"Ang pangulo ay nakatakdang **ipahayag** ang bagong patakaran bukas.","translation":"The president is set to **announce** the new policy tomorrow."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapahayag o pagpapalaganap ng impormasyon sa publiko, karaniwan sa pamamagitan ng midya, upang isulong ang isang produkto, serbisyo, o kaganapan.
original_explanation: The OG way of saying 'to run an ad.' Before Facebook Ads and TikTok promotions, companies would `magpatalastas` on TV during primetime. It’s making sure everyone and their tita knows about your new laundry detergent or upcoming teleserye.
usage_notes: Often used in formal or broadcast media contexts. 'Mag-advertise' is a common modern substitute.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang kumpanya na **magpatalastas** sa radyo upang maabot ang mas maraming customer.","translation":"The company decided to **advertise** on the radio to reach more customers."},{"sentence":"Ang gobyerno ay **nagpatalastas** tungkol sa bagong patakaran sa kalusugan.","translation":"The government **made an announcement** about the new health policy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan na nag-iimbak ng enerhiya upang paganahin ang mga de-kuryenteng aparato. Isa itong alternatibong pagbaybay para sa 'baterya'.
etymology: From English 'battery', as a direct phonetic adaptation. A variant of the Spanish-derived 'baterya'.
original_explanation: This is a less common, slightly more English-sounding spelling for 'baterya'. It's like ordering 'iced tea' instead of 'ice tea'—people get what you mean, but one way is just more common. You'll see this sometimes, but 'baterya' is the final answer.
usage_notes: A spelling variation of 'baterya', influenced by English pronunciation. 'Baterya' is the standard and more widely accepted spelling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng bagong **bateri** para sa relo ko.","translation":"I need a new **battery** for my watch."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng alahas na yari sa huwad na ginto o iba pang materyales na ginagaya ang tunay na hiyas.
original_explanation: This is the bling-bling on a budget. The kind of accessory you buy in Divisoria that looks good from afar, but far from good. It's the 'gold' necklace that turns your neck green after a day at the beach. It's the physical manifestation of 'fake it 'til you make it.'
usage_notes: Often used with a slightly derogatory or humorous tone to point out something fake or of low quality.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puro **urupel** lang ang alahas niya, pero kung makaporma, akala mo milyonarya.","translation":"Her jewelry is all just **imitation**, but the way she carries herself, you'd think she's a millionaire."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magtiwala diyan, baka **urupel** na ginto ang ibenta sa'yo.","translation":"Don't trust that person, they might sell you **fake** gold."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahan na maabot ang kahulugan ng isang bagay, ideya, o sitwasyon; ang proseso ng pag-intindi.
original_explanation: That moment when you finally get why your ex did what they did, but you're still not taking them back. It's the 'gets ko na' moment after a long meeting that could have been an email. The opposite of what you have when your parents explain why you can't go out.
usage_notes: Often used with 'sa' to denote understanding *of* something (e.g., pag-unawa sa sitwasyon).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng mas malalim na **pag-unawa** sa isa't isa.","translation":"We need a deeper **understanding** of each other."},{"sentence":"Ang **pag-unawa** sa aralin ay susi sa pagpasa sa pagsusulit.","translation":"**Understanding** the lesson is key to passing the exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang dalubhasang manggagawa na nag-aayos at nagmamantini ng mga makina, lalo na ng mga sasakyan.
original_explanation: The wizard who speaks the secret language of 'tiktiktik' and 'kalampag' sounds from your car. You give them your money, they perform some magic under the hood, and suddenly your car doesn't sound like it's dying anymore. The real superhero when you're stranded on the side of the road.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala ko ang kotse sa **mekaniko** para ipaayos ang preno.","translation":"I brought the car to the **mechanic** to have the brakes fixed."},{"sentence":"Magaling ang **mekaniko** namin, alam niya agad kung ano ang sira.","translation":"Our **mechanic** is good, he immediately knows what's broken."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang parirala na nagpapahayag ng pagpansin o kung minsan ay pagkainis na ang isang tao ay muling aktibo o gumagamit ng internet o social media.
etymology: Combination of English 'online' and Filipino phrase 'ka nanaman' (you again).
original_explanation: The official greeting from your *marites* tita or your concerned parent when they see your green 'active' dot on Messenger at 3 AM. It’s a loaded phrase that can mean 'Why are you still awake?', 'Are you just procrastinating?', or 'Sino ka-chat mo?!' It's the digital version of being caught with your hand in the cookie jar.
usage_notes: Often used humorously in memes or as a gentle (or not-so-gentle) ribbing among friends and family.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita ko ang post mo ng madaling araw, **online ka nanaman**!","translation":"I saw your post in the early morning, **you're online again**!"},{"sentence":"Sabi mo matutulog ka na, pero **online ka nanaman**.","translation":"You said you were going to sleep, but **you're online again**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sistema ng pagsukat o pagmamarka; isang hanay ng mga antas o halaga mula sa pinakamababa hanggang sa pinakamataas; o isang kagamitan sa pagtimbang.
original_explanation: This is the 'on a scale of 1 to 10' word. From the Richter scale for earthquakes (lindol) to the weighing scale (timbangan) at the palengke, to the pay scale sa BPO company mo. It's all about measurement, range, and knowing where things stand, whether it's your weight, your salary, or the intensity of a chismis.
usage_notes: Can refer to a measuring device (like a weighing scale, which is more specifically 'timbangan') or an abstract range/system of measurement.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa **iskala** mula isa hanggang sampu, gaano ka kasaya ngayon?","translation":"On a **scale** from one to ten, how happy are you right now?"},{"sentence":"Mataas ang nakuha niyang marka sa **iskala** ng pagsusulit.","translation":"He got a high mark on the test **scale**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tubig na walang anumang halo, dumi, o kemikal; malinis at dalisay na tubig na ligtas inumin.
etymology: Isang pariralang binubuo ng Tagalog na "puro" (dalisay) na hiram sa Espanyol, at "tubig" (water).
original_explanation: What you hope you're drinking when you buy those blue gallons from the water station. It's the opposite of that murky tap water that looks like it has a whole ecosystem living in it. It's the "all-natural, no-preservatives" of H2O.
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang parirala na ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na buhay, lalo na kapag tumutukoy sa inuming tubig.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siguraduhing **purong tubig** ang iinumin ng sanggol.","translation":"Make sure the baby drinks **pure water**."},{"sentence":"Mas gusto ko ang lasa ng **purong tubig** kaysa sa mga may pampalasa.","translation":"I prefer the taste of **pure water** over flavored ones."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng pag-aalinlangan; hindi makapagpasya kung tutuloy o aatras.
original_explanation: 'Yung nasa harap ka na ng Jollibee at McDo, hindi mo alam kung Chickenjoy o McSpicy. O 'yung pag-chat mo sa crush mo, type... delete... type... delete. That's urung-sulong. The official state of the perpetually 'marupok' and 'overthinker.'
usage_notes: Describes a state of indecision or hesitation, often manifested by physically or metaphorically moving back and forth.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa takot, siya ay **urung-sulong** sa pagpasok sa madilim na silid.","translation":"Because of fear, he was **hesitant** to enter the dark room."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **urung-sulong** sa iyong desisyon kung sigurado ka na.","translation":"Don't be **indecisive** about your decision if you are already sure."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang indibidwal na kabilang sa lahi ng mga tao (Homo sapiens), na may kakayahang mag-isip, magsalita, at kumilos.
original_explanation: The most basic unit of chismis and social life. It can be your friend, your enemy, that stranger on the MRT, or the subject of the latest viral video. 'Ang daming **tao** sa mall, sale siguro.'
usage_notes: Can also mean 'people' in a general sense. When referring to one's subordinates or people under their care, it can be used as 'mga tao ko' (my people).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang mabuting **tao** si G. Reyes.","translation":"Mr. Reyes is a good **person**."},{"sentence":"Lahat ng **tao** ay may karapatang maging masaya.","translation":"All **people** have the right to be happy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pakikipag-ugnayan, pakikipag-usap, o pakikihalubilo sa ibang tao sa isang pagtitipon o sa lipunan.
original_explanation: This is your tita asking 'Bakit di ka nakikipag-salamuha?' at the family reunion. 'Pagsalamuha' is the act of socializing, mingling, making small talk. It’s what you do at parties, team-building events, and conferences. It’s moving through a crowd and interacting with different people. An introvert's nightmare, an extrovert's playground.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in the context of social interaction with groups of people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **pagsalamuha** sa iba't ibang tao upang mapalawak ang iyong kaalaman.","translation":"**Socializing** with different people is important to broaden your knowledge."},{"sentence":"Iniiwasan niya ang **pagsalamuha** sa mga party dahil siya ay mahiyain.","translation":"He avoids **mingling** at parties because he is shy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapahayag ng kagalakan o kasiyahan dahil sa isang espesyal na okasyon, tagumpay, o mabuting balita, kadalasan sa pamamagitan ng isang pagtitipon o salu-salo.
original_explanation: This is the official verb for 'party!' It's what Pinoys do when Manny Pacquiao wins, when someone passes the board exams, or when it's a random Tuesday that feels like a fiesta. It’s more than just celebrating; it's celebrating with *feeling*. With lechon, karaoke, and probably a Tita asking when you're getting married. 'Pumasa siya sa board! Tara, magdiwang tayo!'
usage_notes: The root 'diwang' is related to 'diwa' (spirit, essence). 'Magdiwang' is literally 'to bring out the spirit'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat tayong **magdiwang** dahil sa mga biyayang ating natanggap.","translation":"We should **celebrate** because of the blessings we have received."},{"sentence":"Ang buong pamilya ay nagtipon upang **magdiwang** ng Pasko.","translation":"The whole family gathered **to celebrate** Christmas."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malapad na tangkay ng dahon ng mga palmang tulad ng niyog, saging, o buri.
original_explanation: The OG Pinoy walis tingting starter pack. Bago maging walis, palapa muna siya. It's the stem part of a coconut leaf that, when dried, becomes the backbone of provincial-level home cleaning and sometimes, pamalo sa pasaway na bata.
usage_notes: Karaniwang tumutukoy sa mga dahon ng puno ng niyog o nipa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang natuyong **palapa** ng niyog bilang panggatong.","translation":"He used the dried coconut **frond** as firewood."},{"sentence":"Maingat niyang inalis ang mga **palapa** mula sa puno.","translation":"He carefully removed the **fronds** from the tree."}]

meaning_filipino: Gagawaan ng paraan upang maging hindi kaaya-aya sa paningin ang isang tao, bagay, o lugar.
original_explanation: When your sibling gets ahold of your graduation picture and draws a mustache on it. That's it. Your photo **papangitin** nila. It can also be used for things like a bad paint job on a house or a terrible haircut. "Huwag mong hayaang **papangitin** ng mga problema ang iyong pananaw sa buhay."
usage_notes: This is the causative form, meaning to cause something or someone to become ugly.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bakit mo naman **papangitin** ang iyong sulat-kamay?","translation":"Why would you **make** your handwriting **ugly**?"},{"sentence":"Ang magandang pader ay **pinangit** ng bandalismo.","translation":"The beautiful wall was **made ugly** by vandalism."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng labis na pagpapahalaga sa sarili at madalas na ipinagmamalaki ang mga katangian o ari-arian, kadalasan sa paraang nakakainsulto sa iba.
original_explanation: That one friend who posts their new iPhone, Starbucks cup, and branded shoes in one selfie with a caption like '#blessed #hustle.' That's hambog. It's being so full of yourself that there's no room for anyone else. It's the opposite of 'humble,' with a side of 'look at me, I'm better than you.'
usage_notes: Can also be used as a noun to refer to an arrogant person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw siyang kausapin ng mga tao dahil siya ay **hambog** at mayabang.","translation":"People don't want to talk to him because he is **arrogant** and boastful."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **hambog** kapag umasenso ka sa buhay.","translation":"Don't be **conceited** when you succeed in life."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangunahing sangkap o bahagi ng isang mas malaking kabuuan; sa kimika, isang sangkap na hindi maaaring hatiin sa mas simpleng anyo sa pamamagitan ng kemikal na paraan.
original_explanation: Parang 'The Last Airbender' lang: hangin, tubig, lupa, apoy. O kaya sa chemistry, yung mga nasa periodic table. Pwede ring 'elemento' ng isang magandang kuwento: tauhan, tagpuan, banghay. It's the basic building block of anything, even chismis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tubig ay binubuo ng mga **elemento** ng hydrogen at oxygen.","translation":"Water is composed of the **elements** of hydrogen and oxygen."},{"sentence":"Isa sa mga **elemento** ng isang matagumpay na relasyon ay tiwala.","translation":"One of the **elements** of a successful relationship is trust."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagsikapang makamit o isakatuparan ang isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pagtitiyaga at determinasyon.
original_explanation: Ito yung verb form ng hustle. 'Pag may goal ka—promotion sa work, 1-day-old na Jollibee chickenjoy, o 'yung pag-accept sa'yo ng crush mo—kailangan mo itong punyagiin. Hindi ito basta hinihintay, ito ay pinagtatrabahuhan, pinagpupuyatan, at ipinagdarasal.
usage_notes: A formal verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat nating **punyagiin** ang pag-unlad ng ating bansa.","translation":"We must **strive for** the progress of our country."},{"sentence":"Anuman ang pangarap mo, **punyagiin** mo itong makamit.","translation":"Whatever your dream is, **persevere** to achieve it."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang lalaki na malambing, mapagmahal, at mahilig magpakita ng karinyo.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung lalaking hindi torpe magpakita ng affection. Siya 'yung mag-aakbay sa'yo in public, hahawakan kamay mo, at sasabihing "ingat ka." He's the opposite of the "macho" stereotype who thinks showing feelings is a weakness. The term is for males.
usage_notes: This is the masculine form. For females, use "karinyosa".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **karinyoso**ng ama si Mang Ben sa kanyang mga anak.","translation":"Mang Ben is an **affectionate** father to his children."},{"sentence":"Sana makahanap ako ng kasintahang **karinyoso**.","translation":"I hope to find an **affectionate** boyfriend."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matindi at masidhing damdamin ng kaligayahan o kasiyahan.
etymology: From `ka-` + `igaya` + `-han`. `Igaya` means to please or delight someone.
original_explanation: This is not just your everyday "happy." This is "nanalo sa lotto" happy. "Nakita mo 'yung K-Pop idol mo sa mall" happy. It's an elevated, almost ecstatic joy. Think of "kaligayahan" (happiness) but turn the volume up to 11. It's the feeling of pure, unadulterated bliss.
usage_notes: More poetic and formal than the common "kaligayahan" or "kasiyahan."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Labis na **kaigayahan** ang nadama niya nang makapiling ang pamilya.","translation":"She felt immense **delight** when she was with her family."},{"sentence":"Ang pagtanggap ng parangal ay nagdulot ng **kaigayahan** sa buong komunidad.","translation":"Receiving the award brought **great joy** to the whole community."}]

translation: to claim; to appropriate; to own
meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagkuha o pagsasabi na sa iyo ang isang bagay, karapatan, o titulo, na maaaring mayroon o walang legal na basehan.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of what a 'mangangamkam' does. It's when you see a cute stray cat and decide, 'You're mine now.' Or when your sibling leaves their fries unattended and you *mang-angkin* them. It can be wholesome or a total jerk move, depending on the context.
usage_notes: Can be neutral (to claim what is rightfully yours) or negative (to appropriate something that isn't). Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mang-angkin** ng gawa na hindi sa iyo.","translation":"Do not **claim** work that is not yours."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **mang-angkin** ng lupaing hindi naman sakop ng kanyang titulo.","translation":"He tried **to claim** land that was not covered by his title."}]

translation: to feel numb, to have pins and needles
meaning_filipino: Mawalan ng pakiramdam sa isang bahagi ng katawan, karaniwang dahil sa pagkaipit ng daloy ng dugo, na nagreresulta sa pakiramdam na parang tinutusok ng karayom.
original_explanation: That "TV static" feeling in your arm after sleeping on it wrong, or in your legs after sitting on the floor for too long during a meeting. Your limb is technically still there, but it has entered the void and is now sending you angry, tingly signals. You try to shake it back to life, looking like you're doing a weird dance.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'manhid', but 'ngimay' specifically refers to the tingling, "pins and needles" sensation (paresthesia) as feeling returns, while 'manhid' can be pure numbness or emotional numbness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **mangimay** ang mga binti ko sa tagal ng pagkakaupo sa sahig.","translation":"My legs started to **feel numb** from sitting on the floor for so long."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong ipatong ang ulo mo sa braso ko, baka **mangimay**.","translation":"Don't rest your head on my arm, it might **get pins and needles**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na hindi matatag, umuuga, o hindi pantay ang galaw.
original_explanation: 'Yung sinasakyan mong jeep na parang masahista sa likod sa sobrang alog. O 'yung lamesa sa karinderya na kailangan mong lagyan ng tissue sa ilalim ng paa para hindi gumalaw. "Pre, makalog 'yung daan papunta sa resort, kapit ka."
usage_notes: Used for physical objects, roads, or vehicles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Makalog** ang biyahe dahil sa baku-bakong kalsada.","translation":"The trip is **bumpy** because of the uneven road."},{"sentence":"Ayusin mo 'yang silya, **makalog** na.","translation":"Fix that chair, it's already **wobbly**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginagamit o inilalaan para sa ikapitumpung bilang sa isang serye o pagkakasunod-sunod.
original_explanation: This is for the 70th item on your Shopee checkout, the 70th person in the queue for the MRT, or the 70th attempt at perfecting your TikTok dance. It's the 'para sa ika-70' in the group chat.
usage_notes: Isang pang-uring pamilang na nagpapahiwatig ng layunin para sa ika-70 posisyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang medalyang ito ay **pampitumpu** sa listahan ng mga pararangalan.","translation":"This medal is **for the seventieth** on the list of awardees."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na bahay o silid, karaniwang yari sa kahoy at matatagpuan sa tabing-dagat o sa kabundukan.
original_explanation: Your dream staycation spot in Tagaytay or Batangas. It’s that small, cozy house, often wooden, that you rent for a weekend getaway. It's the setting for countless 'unplug and unwind' Instagram posts. Think of it as a bahay-kubo with WiFi and maybe a dipping pool.
usage_notes: Often associated with resorts and vacation spots.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagrenta kami ng isang **kabanya** sa tabi ng dagat para sa aming bakasyon.","translation":"We rented a **cabana** by the sea for our vacation."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan na pinagkukunan ng kuryente para sa mga elektronikong bagay. Isa itong karaniwang alternatibong pagbaybay.
etymology: A phonetic spelling of the Spanish 'batería', leading to the modern standard 'baterya'.
original_explanation: This is the phonetic spelling for people who write like they talk. It's a totally valid way to spell it, just a bit more literal. Think of it as the difference between 'theater' and 'theatre'. 'Bateriya' and 'baterya' are basically twins, but 'baterya' gets invited to more parties.
usage_notes: A common phonetic spelling variation of 'baterya'. While understood by everyone, 'baterya' is the more standard form in writing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakibili mo ako ng dalawang AA na **bateriya**.","translation":"Please buy me two AA **batteries**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging bahagyang bukas, tulad ng pinto, bintana, o bibig.
original_explanation: This is the state of the door when your mom wants to check on you without fully committing to entering your room. It's how your mouth hangs when you see something shocking (nga-nga). Not fully open, not fully closed. Just enough for chismis (or a draft) to get through.
usage_notes: Describes a state, not an action. It's the result of the action 'umawang' or 'inawang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iniwan niyang **nakaawang** ang bintana upang makapasok ang sariwang hangin.","translation":"He left the window **ajar** to let the fresh air in."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang direksyong timog.
original_explanation: The "Tita from Spain" version of 'Timog'. You'll almost never hear this unless you're reading a very old map or talking to someone who wants to sound extra fancy. Everyone else just says 'Timog'. It's like calling a car a "horseless carriage."
usage_notes: Extremely rare in modern spoken Tagalog. 'Timog' is the standard and universally understood term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Ilocos **Sur** ay isang probinsya sa Pilipinas.","translation":"Ilocos **Sur** (South) is a province in the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Ayon sa lumang mapa, ang kayamanan ay nasa gawing **sur**.","translation":"According to the old map, the treasure is in the **south** direction."}]

meaning_filipino: Pinigil, hindi pinakawalan, o naantala sa isang lugar.
original_explanation: This is a classic word you'd hear from your lola. It’s what happens when you get stuck somewhere. Na-retinido ka sa traffic sa EDSA. Na-retinido ka sa office kasi may urgent report. It’s like being held hostage by circumstances. Yung feeling na gusto mo nang umuwi pero hindi ka makaalis.
usage_notes: Considered a bit old-fashioned or formal, but still understood. Often used in legal or official contexts, or by older speakers.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Na-**retinido** ang mga turista sa isla dahil sa biglaang paglakas ng bagyo.","translation":"The tourists were **detained** on the island due to the sudden strengthening of the typhoon."},{"sentence":"Pansamantalang **retinido** sa presinto ang suspek para sa interogasyon.","translation":"The suspect is temporarily **held** at the precinct for interrogation."}]

translation: to go on an excursion; to go on a field trip
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa ng isang maikling paglalakbay o pamamasyal, karaniwan ay isinasagawa ng isang grupo para sa libangan, pag-aaral, o paglilibang.
etymology: Hiram sa salitang Espanyol na 'excursión' at nilapian ng unlaping `mag-`.
original_explanation: The more formal term for "mag-field trip." This is what your teacher announces, and the whole class erupts in cheers. It means a day away from the classroom, a long bus ride with friends, packed baon, and a mandatory visit to a museum or historical site you'll mostly ignore while taking selfies.
usage_notes: Madalas na iniuugnay sa mga school field trip o mga organisadong group tour.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Balak ng aming klase na **mag-ekskursiyon** sa National Museum.","translation":"Our class plans to **go on a field trip** to the National Museum."},{"sentence":"Noong bata ako, paborito kong **mag-ekskursiyon** kasama ang aking pamilya.","translation":"When I was a child, I loved to **go on excursions** with my family."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong mapang-api, mayabang, at gumagamit ng lakas o pananakot upang makuha ang gusto sa kapwa.
original_explanation: The classic neighborhood tough guy who probably peaked in high school. He walks with a swagger, talks loudly, and thinks a sleeveless shirt is formal wear. Every barangay has one, usually found near the basketball court or the local sari-sari store, trying to look intimidating. The main character in a 'sumbong mo ko sa tatay ko' scenario.
usage_notes: Carries a very negative connotation, implying someone who preys on the weak.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinumbong ng bata ang **maton** na laging nang-aagaw ng baon niya.","translation":"The child reported the **bully** who always snatches his lunch money."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya bilang **maton** sa kanilang lugar.","translation":"He is known as the **bully** in their area."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay o pagmumungkahi ng isang bagay, serbisyo, o ideya upang tanggapin o pag-isipan ng iba.
original_explanation: 'Yung friend mo na laging may "business proposal" na networking pala. O 'yung tindera sa palengke na sinisigaw, "Suki, bili na!" They're offering you something. "Sinubukan niyang **ialok** ang luma niyang telepono sa akin."
usage_notes: Different from 'ialay'. 'Ialok' is for transactions, suggestions, and general offerings, while 'ialay' is for dedication and sacrifice.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ialok** mo sa kanila ang kape at biskwit.","translation":"**Offer** them coffee and biscuits."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-atubiling **ialok** ang iyong mga mungkahi sa pulong.","translation":"Don't hesitate to **offer** your suggestions at the meeting."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kulay abong pulbos na nalalabi matapos masunog nang lubusan ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: What's left after something gets completely burned. Think of the gray stuff from a yosi, the remains in a crematorium, or what's left of your heart after your crush says 'friends lang tayo.' Charot. Also, the cross on your forehead on Ash Wednesday.
usage_notes: Often used in religious (Miyerkules ng Senisa / Ash Wednesday) or funereal contexts. The more common word is 'abo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **senisa** ng sumabog na bulkan ay umabot sa mga kalapit na bayan.","translation":"The **ashes** from the erupted volcano reached the nearby towns."},{"sentence":"Nagpapahid ng **senisa** sa noo ang mga deboto tuwing Miyerkules de Senisa.","translation":"Devotees have **ashes** put on their foreheads during Ash Wednesday."}]

translation: stupefied; idiotic (in a state of being)
meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng katangahan o kawalan ng mabilis na pag-iisip; nasa estado ng pagiging tanga.
original_explanation: This is when you're just standing there, mouth open, looking completely clueless. You know that moment when someone tells a joke and you're the last one to get it? 'Yan 'yun. Or when you trip over your own feet in front of your crush. It's not just *being* tanga (stupid), it's the specific look or state of being caught in a moment of pure, unadulterated "clownery."
usage_notes: This is the past tense form of the verb "matanga" (to be stupefied), but often used as an adjective to describe someone's state or appearance. It's a stronger, more descriptive word than just "tanga."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatayo lang siyang **tinanga** matapos siyang iwanan ng bus.","translation":"He just stood there looking **stupefied** after the bus left him."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang tumunganga diyan na parang **tinanga**, tulungan mo ako!","translation":"Don't just gape there like an **idiot**, help me!"}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang kalagayang labis na kalungkutan, paghihirap, o kawalan ng pag-asa.
original_explanation: Yung feeling mo nung nalaman mong 100 pesos na lang ang natira sa ATM mo, tapos petsa de peligro pa. O kaya yung itsura mo nung na-ghost ka for the nth time. That's being miserable. It's the official mood of a Monday morning commute sa EDSA.
usage_notes: A direct loanword used commonly in colloquial Tagalog to express extreme sadness or wretchedness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Miserable** ang buhay niya mula nang iwan siya ng kanyang pamilya.","translation":"His life has been **miserable** since his family left him."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magmukhang **miserable** diyan, may pag-asa pa.","translation":"Don't look so **miserable** there, there's still hope."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit na pagtingin sa paligid, partikular sa likuran, na parang may hinahanap o tinitiyak.
etymology: From `magpa-` and the reduplicated root `lingon` (to look back).
original_explanation: That thing you do when you're walking alone at night in a dark alley and you hear a random noise. Or when you're waiting for your Grab but you're not sure which direction it's coming from. It's the 'paranoid look', the 'lost tourist look', or the 'looking for a chismosa neighbor look' all rolled into one.
usage_notes: The repetition in `lingun-lingon` implies a continuous, repeated, or anxious action of looking around, especially behind.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magpalingun-lingon** para hindi halatang may tinataguan ka.","translation":"Don't **keep looking around** so it's not obvious you're hiding from someone."},{"sentence":"Siya ay **nagpalingun-lingon** sa paghahanap ng pamilyar na mukha sa gitna ng maraming tao.","translation":"She **looked around repeatedly**, searching for a familiar face in the middle of the crowd."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtama o pagbigay ng suntok sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: The verb form. It's the action of delivering the punch. "Gusto kitang **suntukin**!" is what you mentally scream at your slow office computer. It's the "to punch" in the equation. While "suntok" is the noun, **suntukin** is the to-do list.
usage_notes: This is the object-focus form of the verb. The actor-focus form is "sumuntok".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binalaan niya ang magnanakaw na **susuntukin** niya ito kapag hindi umalis.","translation":"He warned the thief that he would **punch** him if he didn't leave."},{"sentence":"Sa sobrang inis, gusto niyang **suntukin** ang pader.","translation":"Out of extreme annoyance, he wanted to **punch** the wall."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malawak na tuyong lupain na may kakaunting halaman at tubig, at karaniwang may matinding temperatura.
original_explanation: The ultimate "dry" place. Walang tubig, walang halaman, puro buhangin. Parang chatbox mo sa Messenger, isang malaking disyerto. O kaya parang wallet mo bago mag-sweldo.
usage_notes: The pronunciation follows the Spanish origin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming kamelyo ang ginagamit bilang transportasyon sa **disyerto**.","translation":"Many camels are used as transportation in the **desert**."},{"sentence":"Ang buhay sa **disyerto** ay napakahirap dahil sa kakulangan ng tubig.","translation":"Life in the **desert** is very difficult due to the lack of water."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng inuming may alkohol na gawa mula sa pinakasim na butil tulad ng mais, sebada, o rye, na karaniwang pinatatanda sa mga bariles na gawa sa kahoy.
original_explanation: Ito yung inumin ng mga tito na biglang nagiging deep ang usapan tungkol sa buhay at pulitika pagkatapos ng ilang tagay. Perfect partner ng yelo, o 'on the rocks' kung gusto mo mag-feeling sosyal. Minsan, ito rin ang sagot sa tanong na, "Anong gusto mong pain reliever?"
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit ang salitang Ingles sa Pilipinas. Bihira ang Tagalog na baybay nito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-order siya ng isang baso ng **whisky** para i-celebrate ang kanyang promotion.","translation":"He ordered a glass of **whisky** to celebrate his promotion."},{"sentence":"Mahal ang mga bote ng Japanese **whisky** na binebenta nila.","translation":"The bottles of Japanese **whisky** they sell are expensive."}]

translation: to become tasteless; to become bland
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkawala o pagbawas ng lasa ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay pagkain o inumin.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your relationship when the 'kilig' fades. Parang sinigang na kulang sa asim o kape na kulang sa tamis. It's that moment when you taste something and your reaction is just 'meh'. The culinary equivalent of getting left on 'seen'.
usage_notes: This is the completed aspect (past tense). The present tense is 'tumatabang' and the future tense is 'tatabang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumabang** ang sabaw dahil naparami ang tubig na idinagdag ko.","translation":"The soup **became bland** because I added too much water."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpuna o pagsita sa isang tao nang hayagan dahil sa isang pagkakamali o maling gawi.
etymology: Mula sa phrasal verb sa Ingles na "call out".
original_explanation: This is what happens when your boss publicly points out your mistake during a team meeting. 'Na-**call out** ako ni Ma'am.' It's the corporate version of being shamed. On social media, it's when you expose someone's problematic behavior, armed with resibo (receipts/proof).
usage_notes: Madalas ginagamit sa anyong pandiwa, lalo na sa anyong nagdaan na "na-call out" (was called out).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong i-**call out** sa harap ng lahat, nakakahiya.","translation":"Don't **call me out** in front of everyone, it's embarrassing."},{"sentence":"Na-**call out** siya dahil sa kanyang hindi propesyonal na pag-uugali.","translation":"He was **called out** for his unprofessional behavior."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang hiram mula sa mga wikang Bisaya na tumutukoy sa lupa, lupain, o teritoryo.
original_explanation: This is the Visayan version of 'lupa.' You'll hear this a lot from people from Cebu, Davao, etc. It's the ground you walk on, the *lupang hinirangan* you own (or dream of owning, #realestategoals), or your hometown province. Think of it as the solid ground beneath your feet when your love life feels like quicksand.
usage_notes: Primarily used in Visayan languages but is understood in many parts of the Philippines, especially in communities with a large Visayan-speaking population. It's often used interchangeably with the Tagalog 'lupa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malawak ang **yuta** ng aming pamilya sa probinsya.","translation":"Our family's **land** in the province is vast."},{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang bilhin ang sarili niyang **yuta** balang araw.","translation":"It's her dream to buy her own piece of **land** someday."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang damdamin ng pagkainis, pagkabugnot, o pagkasuklam na sanhi ng isang bagay o sitwasyong hindi kaaya-aya.
original_explanation: That feeling you get when the internet connection is slower than a turtle in traffic. Or when someone keeps chewing loudly beside you. It's the low-level anger before it becomes full-blown `galit`. `Pagyamot` is the "gigil" you feel when you're trying to be patient, but the universe (or your sibling) keeps testing you. It's the death by a thousand papercuts of annoyance.
usage_notes: Describes a state of being annoyed or irritated. Less intense than 'galit' (anger).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya maitago ang kanyang **pagyamot** sa ingay ng mga kapitbahay.","translation":"He couldn't hide his **annoyance** at the neighbors' noise."},{"sentence":"Ang paulit-ulit na tanong ay nagdulot ng **pagyamot** sa kanya.","translation":"The repetitive question caused him **irritation**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panahon sa umaga kung kailan nagsisimula nang sumikat ang araw at magliwanag ang kalangitan.
original_explanation: That magical time when you're either just finishing your shift at the BPO, just starting your morning jog, or just heading home from a party. It's the universe's soft-launch for the new day. The sky turns from black to that pretty gradient of colors before the sun officially clocks in.
usage_notes: A very poetic and common term for dawn.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula na silang maglakad bago pa man sumapit ang **bukang-liwayway**.","translation":"They started walking even before **dawn** arrived."},{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng tanawin sa tabing-dagat tuwing **bukang-liwayway**.","translation":"The view at the seaside is beautiful every **daybreak**."}]

meaning_filipino: Pananakit na nararamdaman sa anumang bahagi ng ulo. Sa matalinhagang kahulugan, ito ay isang problema o abala.
original_explanation: Literally a headache, but also the term for your pasaway sibling, your toxic boss, or that one government agency with the slowest processing time. It's any person, thing, or situation that makes you want to massage your temples and sigh heavily.
usage_notes: Can be literal (a physical headache) or figurative (a nuisance, a problem). See also 'sakit-ulo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigyan mo ako ng gamot, may **sakit ng ulo** ako.","translation":"Give me some medicine, I have a **headache**."},{"sentence":"Talaga namang **sakit ng ulo** ang mabagal na internet connection.","translation":"A slow internet connection is really a **headache** (a nuisance)."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghawak nang mahigpit; ang pananatiling nakakabit o nakadikit sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: "Kapit lang, bes!" This is the mantra for surviving deadlines, traffic, and life in general. It means to hang in there, to hold on tight. It's what you do when your salary is about to run out before the next payday. Figuratively, it’s about perseverance; literally, it's what you scream at your friend on a roller coaster.
usage_notes: Ang pandiwang-ugat ay madalas gamitin sa anyong pautos ('Kapit!') o bilang bahagi ng mas mahabang pandiwa (kumapit, kumakapit, kakapit). Ang diin ay nasa huling pantig, na iba sa pangngalan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumapit** ka nang mahigpit,\" sabi ng drayber ng habal-habal.","translation":"**Hold on** tight,\" said the habal-habal driver."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **kumapit** sa pag-asa sa gitna ng mga pagsubok.","translation":"We need **to cling** to hope amidst the trials."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagkaranas ng matinding pagod sa katawan at isipan, karaniwang resulta ng mabigat na gawain o mahabang paglalakbay.
original_explanation: This isn't just 'pagod.' This is next-level pagod. This is 'commute from Cavite to QC during a storm' level tired. This is 'after rendering 16 hours of OT' tired. When you're mahapo, you don't just want to sleep, you want to enter a coma for three days.
usage_notes: Implies a deeper, more bone-weary exhaustion than the more common 'pagod'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pag-uwi mula sa bukid, ang mga magsasaka ay laging **mahapo**.","translation":"Coming home from the farm, the farmers are always **exhausted**."},{"sentence":"Ramdam ko ang pagiging **mahapo** pagkatapos ng buong linggong trabaho.","translation":"I feel so **weary** after a whole week of work."}]

meaning_filipino: Indibidwal na nag-aalay ng serbisyo ng paghahatid ng tao, bagay, o mensahe sa isang tiyak na destinasyon.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "taga-" (tagagawa ng kilos) at salitang-ugat na "hatid" (dalhin o ihatid).
original_explanation: Your personal Grab driver, FoodPanda rider, or your dad when you were in high school and needed a ride to a party. 'Ihahatid kita' is a Filipino love language that means 'I'll make sure you get there safely.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-aabang ako sa **tagahatid** ng pagkain na inorder ko online.","translation":"I am waiting for the **deliverer** of the food I ordered online."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang baryasyon ng salitang 'charot,' na nangangahulugang 'biro lang.' Ito ay isang paraan upang ipahiwatig na ang sinabi ay hindi dapat seryosohin.
etymology: A variant of 'charot,' which is the quintessential swardspeak (beki lingo) word for 'joke.' The '-eng' suffix is a common stylistic addition in beki lingo to make words sound more playful or feminine.
original_explanation: A cuter, slightly more affectionate version of 'charot' or 'char'. It's like 'charot' went to finishing school. You use it to soften a joke or a slightly risky statement. 'Ang ganda mo ngayon... chareng!' It has a playful, sing-song quality that makes it less of a blunt instrument and more of a friendly poke.
usage_notes: Interchangeable with 'charot' but can feel slightly softer or more playful.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Libre kita mamaya... **chareng**!","translation":"My treat later... **just kidding**!"},{"sentence":"Ikaw na ang pinakamatalino sa klase, **chareng**!","translation":"You're the smartest in class, **joke**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamataas na antas, punto, o hangganan ng isang bagay; kasukdulan.
original_explanation: This is the "extra" in "extra rice". It's the highest point, the very peak, the 'final boss' level of something. When you've reached the 'sukdol' of your pagod, you're not just tired, you're 'ayoko-na-besh' tired. It's the limit, the very end of the line.
usage_notes: Less common in everyday speech than its derivative "sukdulan". Often used in a literary or formal context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakarating siya sa **sukdol** na hirap ng buhay.","translation":"He reached the **utmost** hardship in life."},{"sentence":"Ito na ang **sukdol** ng kanyang pasensya.","translation":"This is the **limit** of his patience."}]

translation: to crowd together; to cram into a space
meaning_filipino: Ang sama-samang pagpunta o pananatili sa isang masikip na lugar, na halos walang espasyo sa pagitan ng isa't isa.
original_explanation: Picture this: a jeepney during rush hour. The driver shouts "Kasya pa lima diyan!" but you're already sharing your personal space with three other people. That's **magsiksikan**. It's the national sport of Filipino commuters.
usage_notes: Implies a collective action of people squeezing into a tight space.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag na kayong **magsiksikan** sa loob ng elevator, maghintay na lang ng susunod.","translation":"Don't **crowd together** inside the elevator, just wait for the next one."},{"sentence":"Nag-unahan ang mga tao na **magsiksikan** sa may pinto ng concert venue.","translation":"The people rushed to **cram** themselves at the door of the concert venue."}]

translation: the act of picking flowers or fruits
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpitas ng mga bulaklak o bunga mula sa tangkay o sanga nito.
original_explanation: The romantic gesture you see in movies where someone gracefully picks a flower for their loved one. In reality, it's also what your tita does to your mom's prize-winning roses when she thinks no one is looking. It's the gentle harvest.
usage_notes: A more poetic or gentle term than "pitas".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagpupol** ng sampaguita ay isang karaniwang hanapbuhay.","translation":"The **picking of sampaguita flowers** is a common livelihood."},{"sentence":"Naalala ko ang aming masayang **pagpupol** ng mga bayabas sa bukid noong bata pa kami.","translation":"I remember our happy **act of picking** guavas in the field when we were young."}]

translation: To soar, to cause to fly high
meaning_filipino: Paliparin nang mataas sa himpapawid.
original_explanation: This is what your dreams do when you finally get your 13th-month pay. It's also what a kite does on a windy day at Luneta Park. Parang career mo, sana all, laging pa-**ilanglang**!
usage_notes: A poetic or literary word. Not commonly used in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais niyang **ilanglang** ang saranggola hanggang sa maabot nito ang mga ulap.","translation":"He wants to **make** the kite **soar** until it reaches the clouds."},{"sentence":"Ang agila ay malayang nag-**ilanglang** sa kalawakan.","translation":"The eagle freely **soared** in the sky."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang buong baboy na inihaw sa ibabaw ng nagbabagang uling, karaniwang inihahanda para sa mga espesyal na okasyon.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'lechón' na nangangahulugang 'suckling pig'.
original_explanation: The undisputed superstar of every Pinoy handaan. Kapag may litson, alam mong legit ang party. The crispy skin (balat) is the most coveted part, and getting the first piece is like winning the lottery. 'Pag walang litson, baka potluck lang 'yan, hindi fiesta.
usage_notes: Bagama't ang orihinal na kahulugan ay 'suckling pig', sa Pilipinas, tumutukoy ito sa inihaw na baboy ng anumang edad. Mayroon ding litson manok (roasted chicken) at litson baka (roasted cow).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-ambagan ang buong opisina para makabili ng isang buong **litson** para sa Christmas party.","translation":"The whole office chipped in to buy a whole **roasted pig** for the Christmas party."},{"sentence":"Pakikuha mo ako ng balat ng **litson**!","translation":"Please get me some skin from the **roasted pig**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang di-pangkaraniwang larawan o imahe na nakikita sa isipan o panaginip, na madalas ay pinaniniwalaang may kahulugan o babala tungkol sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: It's like your brain's version of a movie trailer for the future, but it's usually blurry, cryptic, and gives you a weird feeling. Your lola might have a 'pangitain' about who wins the lottery or that you shouldn't go out tonight. It's a psychic text message you can't reply to.
usage_notes: Often has a supernatural or mystical connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon siya ng isang masamang **pangitain** bago mangyari ang aksidente.","translation":"She had a bad **premonition** before the accident happened."},{"sentence":"Ang paglitaw ng kometa ay itinuturing na **pangitain** noong unang panahon.","translation":"The appearance of a comet was considered an **omen** in ancient times."}]

translation: to let something rot, to cause to decay
meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang pag-iwan o pagpapabaya sa isang bagay hanggang sa ito ay masira o mabulok.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung act of letting something go bad. 'Yung saging na binili mo last week na ngayon itim na? Pinabulok mo. 'Yung potential niyo ng 'the one that got away' na hindi mo pinursue? Pinabulok mo rin. Ouch.
usage_notes: This is the causative verb form of 'bulok' (rotten).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **bulukin** ang mga prutas sa ref; gawin mo na lang juice.","translation":"Don't **let** the fruits **rot** in the fridge; just make juice out of them."},{"sentence":"**Binuluk** niya ang isda sa labas ng bahay kaya bumaho.","translation":"He **let the fish rot** outside the house, so it stank."}]

meaning_filipino: Maliliit na piraso o durog ng pagkain, lalo na ng tinapay o kanin, na naiiwan pagkatapos kumain.
original_explanation: 'Yung mga maliliit na tira-tira ng Skyflakes or biscuit sa kama mo after a midnight snack. Or 'yung kanin na natira sa plato mo na ayaw mo nang ubusin. It's the tiny leftovers that you either brush away or get scolded for leaving behind.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin para ilarawan ang durog ng tinapay, kanin, o biskwit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiwalis naman ang mga **mumo** sa sahig.","translation":"Please sweep the **crumbs** on the floor."},{"sentence":"Kinain ng langgam ang mga **mumo** ng tinapay na nahulog sa mesa.","translation":"The ants ate the bread **crumbs** that fell on the table."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagkuha o pagkopya ng datos mula sa isang sentral na sistema (tulad ng internet) patungo sa isang lokal na sistema (tulad ng kompyuter o telepono).
original_explanation: Yung pagkuha mo ng movie, kanta, o app mula sa internet papunta sa phone o computer mo. Minsan, ito rin 'yung pag-absorb mo ng lahat ng chismis galing sa Marites mong kaibigan. 'I-download mo na lahat ng tea!'
usage_notes: Madalas ginagamitan ng mga panlaping Tagalog tulad ng 'i-download' (to download something) o 'nag-download' (downloaded). Ang entri na ito ay para sa salitang-ugat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-**download** ng kung ano-anong file, baka may virus.","translation":"Don't **download** just any file, it might have a virus."},{"sentence":"I-**download** mo na ang bagong season ng paborito nating serye.","translation":"**Download** the new season of our favorite series now."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpunta sa panlabas na bahagi mula sa loob; pagpapakita o pagiging hayag.
original_explanation: Two meanings: 1) The act of finally leaving the house for a night out. 2) The tea. 'Yung totoong kulay or a secret that's finally revealed. 'After all the drama, lumalabas na siya pala ang may kasalanan.'
usage_notes: Can be used literally for 'going outside' or figuratively for 'it turns out that...' or 'it appears that...'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Madalas siyang **lumalabas** kasama ang kanyang mga kaibigan tuwing Sabado.","translation":"She often **goes out** with her friends every Saturday."}]

translation: to be drowsy, to be half-asleep
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging antukin pa o hindi pa lubusang gising, karaniwang pagkatapos magising mula sa pagtulog.
original_explanation: That feeling when your alarm goes off for your 6 AM shift but your soul is still in bed. You're physically up, but your brain is still buffering. You're walking around, eyes half-closed, bumping into things. That's you, 'pumungas-pungas'.
usage_notes: It's a state of being, describing the groggy, disoriented moments after waking up. The repetition of 'pungas' emphasizes the lingering sleepiness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit naligo na siya, **pumungas-pungas** pa rin siyang pumasok sa trabaho.","translation":"Even after taking a shower, he was still **drowsy** when he went to work."},{"sentence":"**Pumungas-pungas** na sumagot ng telepono ang bata dahil nagising sa kalagitnaan ng kanyang pagtulog.","translation":"The child answered the phone **half-asleep** because he was awakened in the middle of his sleep."}]

translation: to search for something frantically; to grope for
meaning_filipino: Ang masinsinan at mabilisang paghahanap sa isang bagay, tao, o lugar, na madalas ay ginagamitan ng kamay o paningin sa paraang tila bulag.
original_explanation: This is you looking for your phone in your bag while the Grab driver is waiting. It's that 'pabulag-bulag' searching motion, full of panic and desperation, patting every surface hoping to find what you're looking for, especially in the dark.
usage_notes: The -in suffix makes it an object-focus verb, meaning the action is done *to* something. It implies a more desperate or less systematic search than 'hanapin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **hagilapin** ang kanyang salamin sa dilim.","translation":"He tried to **grope for** his glasses in the dark."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **hagilapin** ang nawawalang dokumento bago magalit ang boss.","translation":"We need to **frantically search for** the missing document before the boss gets angry."}]

translation: to be together; to be side-by-side
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging magkasama o magkatabi ng dalawa o higit pang tao.
etymology: From 'magka-' (denoting a reciprocal or shared state) + 'piling' (side, presence).
original_explanation: The ultimate #SanaAll goal. 'Yung LDR couple na finally nagkita. 'Yung mag-jowa na magkayakap habang nanonood ng Netflix. It's being physically close to someone you care about. Ang opposite nito ay 'yung social distancing.
usage_notes: Often carries a romantic or intimate connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nananabik na ang OFW na muling **magkapiling** ang kanyang pamilya.","translation":"The OFW is excited to **be together** with his family again."},{"sentence":"Ang tanging hiling ko sa Pasko ay **magkapiling** tayong lahat.","translation":"My only wish for Christmas is for all of us to **be together**."}]

translation: to do with sincerity, to do from the heart
meaning_filipino: Gawin o ipahayag nang may buong katapatan at mula sa kaibuturan ng puso.
etymology: From i- (causative verb prefix) + taos (sincere, heartfelt).
original_explanation: This is the opposite of "plastic" or "napipilitan lang." When you apologize and you really, really mean it, you say "itaos-puso kong hinihingi ang iyong tawad." It’s doing something with your whole chest, whether it’s a prayer, a promise, or a thank you. No half-assing allowed.
usage_notes: Almost always paired with "puso" (heart) as in "itaos-puso" to mean "heartfelt" or "sincere."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais kong **itaos** sa aking puso ang pasasalamat sa lahat ng tumulong.","translation":"I want to express my **heartfelt** thanks to everyone who helped."},{"sentence":"**Itinaos** niya ang kanyang panalangin para sa kaligtasan ng pamilya.","translation":"She offered her prayer for her family's safety **with sincerity**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nakaramdam ng biglaang pagkayamot o iritasyon bunga ng isang pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is the past tense of 'naiinis'. It's what happened *after* the Wi-Fi finally disconnected or your officemate wouldn't stop clicking their pen. The annoyance has peaked and is now a completed event. 'Kanina, nainis talaga ako sa traffic.'
usage_notes: Past tense. Describes a completed action of becoming annoyed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nainis** siya nang malaman niyang hindi siya kasama sa listahan.","translation":"He **got annoyed** when he found out he wasn't on the list."},{"sentence":"Bigla akong **nainis** sa sinabi niya.","translation":"I suddenly **became irritated** by what he said."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pang-abay na pampanukat na ginagamit upang magbigay-diin sa tindi ng isang pang-uri, karaniwang sa mga pahayag na padamdam.
original_explanation: This is the OG way to be dramatic and extra. Before 'sobrang' or 'super' became a thing, there was 'kay'. "Kay ganda ng umaga!" (What a beautiful morning!). It's the word you use when you're feeling poetic or want to sound like a character from a classic Filipino movie. It adds a touch of class and exaggeration to your compliments or complaints. "Kay bagal ng internet!"
usage_notes: Placed before an adjective to intensify its meaning, often in exclamatory sentences. It is more formal or literary.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kay** ganda ng tanawin mula sa tuktok ng bundok!","translation":"**How** beautiful the view is from the mountaintop!"},{"sentence":"Naku, **kay** hirap pala ng pagsusulit na ito!","translation":"Oh, this exam is **so** difficult!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalabas ng malakas na boses na nakatuon sa isang tao o bagay, karaniwan dahil sa galit o upang makuha ang atensyon.
original_explanation: This is what happens when your mom finds out you haven't done the dishes yet. 'Sigawan' is to shout *at* someone. It’s a one-way communication where the volume is high and the patience is low. Also what happens in Congress, on a teleserye, or in a heated Valorant match.
usage_notes: This is a verb. The object being shouted at is the focus.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **sigawan** ang bata, kausapin mo nang mahinahon.","translation":"Don't **shout at** the child, talk to him calmly."},{"sentence":"**Sinigawan** niya ang kapatid niya dahil kinuha ang charger niya.","translation":"She **shouted at** her sibling for taking her charger."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o bagay na pansamantalang ginagamit bilang kapalit o panghalili upang punan ang isang kakulangan o pangangailangan.
etymology: A compound of `pamasak` (plug) and `butas` (hole). Literally "plug for a hole."
original_explanation: The ultimate "hugot" word. This is the person you date right after a breakup just so you're not alone. You're not the main character, you're the stand-in. The B-team player sent in because the star is injured. It’s the "pwede na 'to for now" choice. Harsh, but real. Applies to things too, like a temp job while you look for your dream career.
usage_notes: Carries a strong negative connotation of being a second choice or a mere temporary solution, especially in relationships.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayokong maging **pamasak-butas** lang habang hinihintay mo siyang bumalik.","translation":"I don't want to just be a **rebound** while you wait for her to come back."},{"sentence":"Ang pagtanggap niya sa trabahong iyon ay **pamasak-butas** lamang habang naghahanap siya ng mas maganda.","translation":"His acceptance of that job is just a **stopgap** while he looks for something better."}]

translation: to assume; to think; to suppose
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng isang palagay o paniniwala tungkol sa isang bagay na hindi pa napapatunayan o walang sapat na batayan; ang pag-iisip na totoo ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the official verb for 'assuming'. It's what you do when you see your crush talking to someone else and you immediately think they're dating. 'Akala ko...' is the national anthem of the heartbroken and the mistaken. It's the prelude to drama, the foundation of 'marites' chismis, and the reason we have the saying, 'Huwag kang mag-assume, para hindi ka masaktan.'
usage_notes: Often used in the past tense 'nag-akala' or with 'akala ko' (I thought) to express a mistaken belief.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mag-akala** na alam mo na ang lahat.","translation":"Don't **assume** that you know everything."},{"sentence":"**Nag-akala** akong Biyernes na ngayon, kaya pala walang gaanong tao sa opisina.","translation":"I **thought** it was Friday already, that's why there aren't many people in the office."}]

meaning_filipino: Nauukol o may kaugnayan sa mga daanan ng hangin sa baga na tinatawag na 'bronchi'.
original_explanation: This is what your tita who chain-smokes is probably complaining about. "Hay, inaatake na naman ako ng brongkyal asthma ko." It's that medical term you hear in commercials for cough syrup or from your doctor when you've been coughing up a lung.
usage_notes: Primarily used in medical or health-related contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **brongkyal** asthma ang bata kaya madali siyang hingalin.","translation":"The child has **bronchial** asthma, so he gets out of breath easily."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasuotang isinusuot sa ibabaw ng damit upang protektahan ito mula sa dumi, lalo na sa pagluluto o pagtatrabaho.
original_explanation: This is your mom's or lola's battle armor in the kitchen. Bago sila mag-gisa or magprito, isusuot muna ang delantal para hindi tumalsik ang mantika sa kanilang pambahay na daster. It's the original splash guard.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng pagluluto, paglilinis, o pagtatrabaho sa mga gawaing maaaring makadumi sa damit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang isuot ang iyong **delantal** bago ka maghiwa ng mga sangkap.","translation":"Don't forget to wear your **apron** before you chop the ingredients."},{"sentence":"Puno ng mantsa ng harina ang **delantal** ng panadero.","translation":"The baker's **apron** was full of flour stains."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng mahilig makialam o sumali sa usapan o gawain ng iba na hindi naman siya kasali. Ang panlalaking katumbas ay 'sawsawero'.
etymology: From 'sawsaw' (to meddle) + '-era' (Spanish suffix indicating a female doer of an action).
original_explanation: The female form of the species that can't resist butting in. She's the officemate who listens to your phone call, the tita who asks when you're getting married, the friend who gives unsolicited advice on your relationship. She lives for the drama, as long as it's not hers. The 'sawsawero' is her male counterpart.
usage_notes: A colloquial and often derogatory term. The male equivalent is 'sawsawero'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw ko siyang kausap dahil isa siyang **sawsawera**.","translation":"I don't like talking to her because she's a **meddler**."},{"sentence":"Nagalit si Ana nang tawagin siyang **sawsawera** ng kanyang kaibigan.","translation":"Ana got angry when her friend called her a **busybody**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na nakalagay nang pahalang o nakaharang sa daan. Sa matalinhagang kahulugan, ito ay tumutukoy sa kawalan ng awa o pagiging malupit.
original_explanation: That motorcycle parked right in the middle of a one-way street. Also used to describe a person with no conscience, like someone who cuts in line at the milk tea shop. 'Halang ang kaluluwa' is the ultimate insult for someone who's just pure evil, no remorse.
usage_notes: Commonly used in the idiom 'halang ang kaluluwa' which translates to 'a soul laid across,' meaning cruel, ruthless, or remorseless.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroong **halang** na troso sa gitna ng kalsada kaya hindi kami makadaan.","translation":"There is a wooden log as an **obstruction** in the middle of the road so we cannot pass."},{"sentence":"Sinasabing **halang** ang kaluluwa ng mga taong pumapatay nang walang dahilan.","translation":"It is said that people who kill without reason have a **ruthless** soul."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagwawakas o pagtatapos ng isang gawain, pangyayari, o proseso.
original_explanation: What you tell yourself you'll do with your Netflix series, but you end up starting a new one instead. Also, that glorious feeling when you finally submit your thesis. To tumapos is to conquer the mountain of 'saka na' (later).
usage_notes: A very common verb for completing any kind of task.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang unang **tumapos** ng takdang-aralin?","translation":"Who was the first to **finish** the assignment?"},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **tumapos** ng proyekto bago ang Biyernes.","translation":"We need **to complete** the project before Friday."}]
