meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging mabangis, matapang, o malakas ang epekto.
original_explanation: The 'extra spicy' level of everything. It's the potency of a strong liquor ('alak'), the venom of a snake ('kamandag'), or the fury of your mom when you come home past curfew. It's not just strong, it's dangerously strong. The phrase 'bagsik pumatay' just emphasizes its lethal quality.
usage_notes: Often used to describe poison (lason), storms (bagyo), diseases (sakit), or anger (galit).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakatakot ang **bagsik** ng kamandag ng ahas.","translation":"The **potency** of the snake's venom is frightening."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan maaaring magtago, magkanlong, o sumilong upang hindi makita o mapahamak.
original_explanation: Your "safe space." It could be a literal treehouse, a cozy corner in a coffee shop, or just your bed under a mountain of blankets where you can hide from adult responsibilities. A "makublihan" is any spot that gives you shelter from the storm, whether the storm is a literal typhoon or a series of stressful emails.
usage_notes: A poetic and evocative word for a hiding place or shelter.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lumang bahay sa gubat ang nagsilbing **makublihan** ng mga gerilya.","translation":"The old house in the forest served as a **refuge** for the guerillas."},{"sentence":"Naghahanap siya ng **makublihan** mula sa ingay ng siyudad.","translation":"She is looking for a **shelter** from the noise of the city."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kilos sa hinaharap kung saan kukunin o kokopyahin ang isang digital na file mula sa isang server patungo sa isang lokal na aparato.
original_explanation: This is the future tense of 'patience-testing.' It's what you say when your internet is slow as a turtle on EDSA during rush hour. 'Mamaya na, magdodownload pa ako ng bagong season ng K-drama.' It's the promise of future entertainment, pending your internet provider's approval.
usage_notes: A Taglish verb conjugation (mag- + duplicated first syllable of root + root). This is the future tense form of 'magdownload'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magdodownload** ako ng mga pelikula para sa biyahe bukas.","translation":"I **will download** movies for the trip tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Sabi niya, **magdodownload** siya ng mga bagong kanta.","translation":"He said he **will download** new songs."}]

meaning_filipino: Espesyal na kasuotan na isinusuot para sa pagganap ng mga gawain sa isang trabaho o propesyon.
original_explanation: Your 'corporate attire' or your BPO-approved outfit. It's the uniform you have to wear, or the set of clothes you've designated as 'okay to get coffee stains on during a stressful Monday'. The opposite of your pambahay.
usage_notes: Refers to any clothing specifically for work, whether a formal uniform or just adherence to a dress code.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong labhan ang aking mga **damit na pantrabaho** para bukas.","translation":"I need to wash my **work clothes** for tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang patakaran sa opisina tungkol sa **damit na pantrabaho**.","translation":"The office policy regarding **work clothes** is strict."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbabalik ng isang bagay sa pinanggalingan o may-ari nito.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of 'give it back.' Think of your friend who borrowed your charger and 'forgot' to return it. You'd tell them, 'Saulian mo naman ako!' It's the act of returning, whether it's a borrowed book, the change from your pamalengke, or the Tupperware your Tita sent with food. The '-an' suffix focuses on the person receiving the returned item.
usage_notes: Madalas ginagamit sa anyong pautos. Ang 'mag-saulian' ay nangangahulugang pagbabalik ng mga bagay sa isa't isa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **saulian** mo na lang ako ng libro bukas.","translation":"Please, just **return** the book to me tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Nangako siyang **saulian** ako sa lahat ng hiniram niya.","translation":"He promised to **return** to me everything he borrowed."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng mantika na nakukuha mula sa pagpiga ng bunga ng oliba.
original_explanation: Yung mamahaling mantika na ginagamit ng mga tita for their "healthy" lifestyle. Extra virgin daw, pero ang tanong, ikaw ba virgin pa? Perfect pang-gisa sa pasta o pang-drizzle sa salad para magpanggap na fit and healthy ka.
usage_notes: Madalas hindi isinasalin at ginagamit bilang 'olive oil' sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas gusto niyang gamitin ang **olive oil** sa pagluluto ng isda.","translation":"She prefers to use **olive oil** when cooking fish."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maikling pantalon na ang laylayan ay nagtatapos sa itaas ng tuhod.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'corto' na nangangahulugang 'maikli' (short).
original_explanation: The official 'pambahay' uniform of every Filipino. Whether you're buying suka from the sari-sari store, playing basketball in the street, or just chilling at home watching Netflix, the korto is your best friend. Also known as 'shorts', but 'korto' just sounds more comfortable and ready for a quick nap.
usage_notes: Habang ang ugat na Espanyol ay nangangahulugang 'maikli' (pang-uri), sa Filipino ito ay ginagamit bilang pangngalan para sa 'shorts'. Ang pang-uring katumbas ay 'maikli'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magsuot ka ng pantalon, bawal ang **korto** sa loob ng simbahan.","translation":"Wear pants, **shorts** are not allowed inside the church."},{"sentence":"Ang komportable lang magsuot ng **korto** at t-shirt sa bahay.","translation":"It's so comfortable just wearing **shorts** and a t-shirt at home."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pampublikong debate o hindi pagkakasundo tungkol sa isang bagay na nagdudulot ng magkakaibang opinyon at matinding damdamin.
original_explanation: The lifeblood of showbiz talk shows and social media. Ito yung 'tea' or 'chismis' na level-up. Kapag may artistang nag-break, may politikong may bagong issue, o may bagong policy na ayaw ng lahat—yan ang **kontrobersiya**. Perfect pampainit ng usapan sa inuman o sa family reunion.
usage_notes: Often spelled colloquially as 'kontrobersya'. The '-iya' ending is more formal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang isyu ay nagdulot ng malaking **kontrobersiya** sa social media.","translation":"The issue caused a huge **controversy** on social media."},{"sentence":"Nasangkot sa isang **kontrobersiya** ang sikat na politiko.","translation":"The famous politician was involved in a **controversy**."}]

translation: to get mixed in with; to happen to join
meaning_filipino: Hindi sinasadyang maging bahagi ng isang grupo, samahan, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: When you, an introvert, accidentally get dragged into your extrovert friend's huge circle at a party. Or when you're just walking peacefully and suddenly you're in the middle of a flash mob. It’s about unintentionally becoming part of the mix, for better or for worse.
usage_notes: The phrase 'mapahalo sa' implies an accidental or unplanned joining of a group or situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglalakad lang ako sa EDSA nang bigla akong **mapahalo sa** isang rally.","translation":"I was just walking along EDSA when I suddenly **got mixed in with** a rally."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng pagiging laging may pag-aalinlangan o kawalan ng tiwala sa isang tao, bagay, o sitwasyon.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `mapag-` (na nagsasaad ng tendensiya) at `duda`, na hango sa Espanyol na 'duda' (doubt).
original_explanation: Eto yung jowa na chine-check ang phone mo, o yung kaibigan na 'pag sinabi mong "OT ako," ang sagot, "Saan at sino kasama mo?" They have trust issues level 99. Kahit ang pusa niyo, pinaghihinalaan nilang may hidden agenda. 'Pag may nag-chat sa'yo ng "Hi," para sa kanila, simula na 'yan ng a-fer.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **mapagduda** siya mula nang lokohin siya ng dati niyang kasintahan.","translation":"She became **suspicious** ever since her former partner cheated on her."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong **mapagduda** sa lahat ng tao.","translation":"Don't be too **doubtful** of everyone."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng bendisyon o paggawad ng kabanalan sa isang tao, bagay, o lugar, karaniwan sa pamamagitan ng isang ritwal.
original_explanation: What a priest does to your new car so you don't get into an accident, or to holy water to make it holy. It's the ultimate 'good vibes only' action, officially sanctioned by a higher power. Your lola asks for this for everything from a new house to your graduation photo.
usage_notes: Strongly associated with religious or spiritual contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pari ang **bumasbas** sa bagong kasal.","translation":"The priest **blessed** the newlyweds."},{"sentence":"Sana'y **bumasbas** ang langit ng ulan para sa ating mga pananim.","translation":"May the heavens **bless** (us) with rain for our crops."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa larangan ng accounting, ito ay isang entrada na nagpapakita ng pagbabawas sa isang account o pagtaas ng assets. Ginagamit din bilang pandiwa para sa pagtatala nito.
original_explanation: The reason your bank account balance goes down. It's the opposite of 'credit'. Every time you tap your card for coffee, food delivery, or that 12.12 sale item, a 'debit' happens. It's the silent and swift ninja that takes money out of your account. Your payroll is 'credit', everything else you buy is 'debit'. The story of our lives.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa konteksto ng pagbabangko, pananalapi, at accounting. Maaari ring gamitin bilang pandiwa: 'i-debit'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lahat ng binili ko ay lumabas bilang **debit** sa aking bank statement.","translation":"All my purchases appeared as a **debit** on my bank statement."},{"sentence":"Paki-**debit** na lang sa account ko ang bayad.","translation":"Please just **debit** the payment from my account."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghahanda, pagluluto, o pagkain ng ulam na gawa sa gulay.
original_explanation: Your mom's favorite command when you keep ordering fast food. 'Mag-gulay ka naman!' It's the act of either cooking a veggie dish (like pinakbet or chopsuey) or simply incorporating greens into your meal. The culinary equivalent of an adulting checkpoint.
usage_notes: Can mean 'to sell vegetables' in a market context, but the primary meaning is related to cooking/eating.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Balak kong **maggulay** ng ampalaya para sa tanghalian.","translation":"I plan to **cook** ampalaya (bitter melon) for lunch."},{"sentence":"Sinabihan ako ng doktor na kailangan kong **maggulay** araw-araw.","translation":"The doctor told me I need to **eat vegetables** every day."}]

translation: to do something for a moment; to do briefly
meaning_filipino: Gawin ang isang bagay sa maikling panahon o sandali lamang.
original_explanation: When you're in a Zoom meeting but need to quickly get a package from the delivery guy. You say, "Saglit lang," and you **isaglit** mo lang yung pagkuha. It's the verb for doing something in a flash, "sandali lang" mode.
usage_notes: Often used to indicate a quick, temporary action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Isinaglit** ko lang ang bata sa kapitbahay habang may binibili ako sa tindahan.","translation":"I **briefly** left the child with the neighbor while I bought something from the store."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos na naganap na kung saan ang isang gawain, pangyayari, o proseso ay umpisahan.
original_explanation: Dito nagsimula ang lahat. Sa isang 'hi' sa chat. Tapos naging 'haha', tapos naging 'I love you', tapos ngayon, 'who you?' na lang. The cycle of 'marupok'.
usage_notes: Past tense. The present tense is 'nagsisimula' and the future tense is 'magsisimula'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagsimula** ang programa nang eksaktong alas-nuwebe ng umaga.","translation":"The program **started** at exactly nine in the morning."},{"sentence":"**Nagsimula** siyang magtrabaho sa BPO noong isang taon.","translation":"He **started** working at a BPO last year."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng isang taong malapit nang mamatay, na may kasamang hirap sa paghinga.
original_explanation: This is the most dramatic and final stage of 'pagod na ako.' It's the scene in every telenovela where the dying matriarch gathers the family to reveal one last secret. It's the ultimate 'low batt' notification for life itself. Dark, but true.
usage_notes: Isang seryosong salita na naglalarawan sa mga sandali bago ang kamatayan. Ang pandiwa nito ay 'naghihingalo' (dying).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naabutan nilang nasa estado na ng **hingalo** ang matanda.","translation":"They arrived to find the old man already in his **death throes**."},{"sentence":"Ang nag-aagaw-buhay na pasyente ay nagpapakita ng mga senyales ng **hingalo**.","translation":"The dying patient is showing signs of the **agony of dying**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maliit na tubo sa gilid ng mata kung saan dumadaloy ang luha.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung pipeline ng lahat ng feels mo. Kapag puno na ang "emotional baggage" mo, dito 'yan nag-o-overflow. Kung may nagtanong, "Bakit ka umiiyak?", sabihin mo lang, "May bara sa daluyang-luha ko, teh."
usage_notes: A compound, descriptive noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng impeksyon ang kanyang **daluyang-luha** kaya namaga ang kanyang mata.","translation":"His **tear duct** got infected, which is why his eye swelled."},{"sentence":"Ang sobrang pag-iyak ay maaaring maging sanhi ng pagbabara ng **daluyang-luha**.","translation":"Excessive crying can cause a blockage of the **tear duct**."}]

translation: to spurt; to give up (in a game)
meaning_filipino: Ang biglaan at mabilis na paglabas o pagbuga ng likido. Sa konteksto ng laro, ito ay pagsuko at paghingi ng sagot.
etymology: Maaaring onomatopoeic o tunog na naglalarawan sa aksyon.
original_explanation: That's the sound and action when you squeeze a calamansi and the juice shoots right into your eye. Or when a water gun gets you. It's a small, sudden, high-pressure burst of liquid. "Sirit" is also what kids say in a game when they give up and want to know the answer, like "I give up, squirt out the answer!"
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pandiwa (sumirit) o bilang isang hudyat ng pagsuko sa isang laro o bugtungan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Biglang **sumirit** ang tubig mula sa nabutas na tubo.","translation":"Water suddenly **squirted** from the punctured pipe."},{"sentence":"Ayoko na manghula, **sirit** na! Ano ang sagot?","translation":"I don't want to guess anymore, **I give up**! What's the answer?"}]

translation: a bitter dish (specifically an Ilocano soup)
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng ulam na Pilipino, partikular sa lutuing Ilokano, na kilala sa mapait na lasa nito na karaniwang nagmumula sa apdo ng hayop.
original_explanation: This is the Ilocano 'hugot' soup. It's bitter, just like your feelings for your ex, but somehow, it's also comforting and makes you feel alive. Made with goat innards and bile, it's the dish that separates the brave from the 'maarte'. If you can handle paitan, you can handle anything life throws at you.
usage_notes: A famous dish from the Ilocos region in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap humigop ng mainit na **paitan** lalo na kung malamig ang panahon.","translation":"It's delicious to sip hot **paitan** especially when the weather is cold."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong sosobrahan ang apdo sa **paitan** para hindi maging sobrang pait.","translation":"Don't put too much bile in the **paitan** so it doesn't become overly bitter."}]

translation: to entertain; to amuse; to divert one's attention
meaning_filipino: Aliwin o libangin ang isang tao upang makuha ang kanyang atensyon o interes at malimutan ang pagkabagot o kalungkutan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "wili", na nangangahulugang pagkakaroon ng interes o pagkagusto.
original_explanation: Ito yung ginagawa mo sa jowa mong nagtatampo. Dinadaan mo sa K-drama, milk tea, o "kain tayo sa labas" para ma-distract siya sa galit niya. Para ka ring "winiwili" ng TikTok algorithm—akala mo 15 minutes ka lang manonood, pero 3 hours na pala ang lumipas. It's the art of distraction.
usage_notes: Madalas ginagamit sa konteksto ng pag-aliw sa isang bata, isang malungkot na tao, o paglilibang sa sarili.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Subukan mong **wilihin** ang bata ng mga laruan para tumigil siya sa pag-iyak.","translation":"Try to **amuse** the child with toys so he will stop crying."},{"sentence":"Para **wilihin** ang sarili, nagbasa na lang siya ng libro habang naghihintay.","translation":"To **entertain** herself, she just read a book while waiting."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa teolohiyang Katoliko, isa sa pitong sakramento kung saan ang isang binyagan ay tumatanggap ng kabuuan ng Banal na Espiritu, na nagpapatibay sa pananampalataya.
original_explanation: This is the Catholic church's version of a software update for your faith. You got the basic install at baptism, and pagkukumpil is the patch that gives you the "adult" features of the Holy Spirit. It's a big deal, usually involves a bishop, a light slap on the cheek (traditionally), and a party with lots of pancit and cake afterwards. Your ninong/ninang from the kumpil is your spiritual "backer".
usage_notes: Strictly a religious term within Catholicism.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming kabataan ang nakilahok sa sakramento ng **pagkukumpil** ngayong taon.","translation":"Many youths participated in the sacrament of **Confirmation** this year."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkukumpil** ay nagpapatibay sa ating ugnayan sa Simbahan.","translation":"**Confirmation** strengthens our connection to the Church."}]

meaning_filipino: Itinapon na o itatapon pa lamang dahil wala nang halaga o pakinabang.
etymology: From `pa-` (denoting direction or manner) + `tapon` (to throw away).
original_explanation: This is the vibe of that one t-shirt you own with more holes than fabric but you can't let go of. It's also what you call someone who seems to be wasting their life away, like a "black sheep" or someone who's always getting into trouble. "Sayang, ang talino pa naman niya, pero naging patapon."
usage_notes: Can be used for objects or, colloquially and often pejoratively, for people whose lives are perceived as wasted.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong itabi ang mga **patapon** na gamit sa bodega.","translation":"Don't keep the **discarded** things in the storage room."},{"sentence":"Kinupkop niya ang mga pusang **patapon** sa kalye.","translation":"She adopted the **stray** cats on the street."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong ang trabaho ay magbenta ng mga produkto o serbisyo.
original_explanation: Ito yung kuya na makulit sa mall na may hawak na credit card application form o kaya yung nag-aalok ng condo sa'yo habang naglalakad ka. Sila ang frontliners ng kapitalismo, laging may sales quota na kailangang habulin.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa Taglish at sa mga di-pormal na usapan. Ang mas pormal na katumbas ay 'ahente ng bentahan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinausap ako ng isang **salesman** para bilhin ang bagong sabon.","translation":"A **salesman** talked to me to buy the new soap."},{"sentence":"Magaling magsalita ang **salesman** na iyon kaya napabili ako.","translation":"That **salesman** was a smooth talker, that's why I was convinced to buy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagbuo ng konklusyon o palagay batay sa mga umiiral na ebidensya, pahiwatig, o pangangatwiran.
original_explanation: This is your inner Marites or Sherlock Holmes at work. You see your crush post 'Finally happy!' and you immediately conclude they're in a new relationship. It's reading between the lines, connecting the dots, and arriving at a conclusion that may or may not be 100% correct. It's the basis of all chismis.
usage_notes: A formal word often used in academic, legal, or analytical contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang galing ng detektib sa **paghihinuha** kung sino ang salarin.","translation":"The detective is skilled in the **deduction** of who the culprit is."},{"sentence":"Batay sa mga datos, ang kanyang **paghihinuha** ay tila tama.","translation":"Based on the data, his **inference** seems to be correct."}]

translation: please wash (this); to ask someone to wash
meaning_filipino: Isang pakiusap na linisin ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay mga plato o kamay, gamit ang tubig.
original_explanation: The magic word used by the eldest child (the 'panganay') to the younger sibling ('bunso') after dinner. 'Bunso, pahugas naman ng plato.' It’s a request that carries the weight of a command, a cornerstone of Filipino sibling dynamics.
usage_notes: A very common household request. Often used with 'naman' to soften the request (pahugas naman).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ate, **pahugas** naman nitong mga baso.","translation":"Big sister, can you **please wash** these glasses?"},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos kumain, sinabihan niya ang kapatid, '**Pahugas** ka na ng kamay.'","translation":"After eating, she told her sibling, '**Go wash** your hands now.'"}]

meaning_filipino: Pagsalungatan o pagtalunan ang isang paksa sa isang pormal o impormal na paraan upang malaman ang iba't ibang panig o opinyon.
etymology: From `pag-` + `debate` + `-han` (object focus suffix). 'Debate' is from Spanish 'debate'.
original_explanation: What happens when you bring up politics, religion, or pineapple on pizza at a family gathering. It's the 'let's agree to disagree' but in a more structured (or sometimes, chaotic) way. The main event in Congress and on Twitter threads.
usage_notes: This is an object-focus verb. The thing being debated is the object of the sentence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw kong **pagdebatihan** pa ang isyung iyan.","translation":"I don't want **to debate about** that issue anymore."},{"sentence":"Mainit na **pinagdebatihan** sa senado ang bagong batas.","translation":"The new law was heatedly **debated** in the senate."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang kilos ng pag-aabot, pagkakaloob, o paghahandog ng isang bagay sa iba.
etymology: nag- + bi- (repetition of first syllable for present tense) + bigay (give)
original_explanation: The '-ing' form of giving. It's the act in progress. Like your boss who's **nagbibigay** ng bonus (sana all!), or your lola who's always **nagbibigay** ng advice (and sometimes, cash). It's the continuous flow of generosity, blessings, or unsolicited opinions.
usage_notes: Incomplete/Progressive aspect (present tense) of 'magbigay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay laging **nagbibigay** ng tulong sa mga nangangailangan.","translation":"He is always **giving** help to those in need."},{"sentence":"Ang araw ay **nagbibigay** ng liwanag at init.","translation":"The sun **is giving** light and heat."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng prutas na tumutubo nang kumpol-kumpol sa isang baging, karaniwang ginagawang alak o kinakain nang sariwa.
original_explanation: The official fruit of New Year's Eve media noche parties. Filipinos believe eating 12 of these at the stroke of midnight brings good luck for each month of the coming year. It's the OG 'pampaswerte' before online sellers started selling lucky charms. Also, the reason your cheap wine exists.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng isang kilong **ubas** para sa Bagong Taon.","translation":"Mom bought a kilo of **grapes** for New Year's."},{"sentence":"Ang alak ay gawa sa piniga at pinatagal na katas ng **ubas**.","translation":"Wine is made from pressed and aged **grape** juice."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapahiwatig ng mataas na posibilidad na maganap o mangyari ang isang bagay; marahil.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung sagot mo 'pag tinanong ka kung mag-o-overtime ka na naman. 'Malamang.' Or when your friend asks if you're going to order milk tea again. It's the Pinoy's diplomatic way of saying 'almost certainly' or 'duh, of course.'
usage_notes: Used to express a high degree of probability. Often used colloquially.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kung hindi ka mag-aaral, **malamang** ay babagsak ka sa pagsusulit.","translation":"If you don't study, you will **most likely** fail the exam."},{"sentence":"Umuulan na naman, **malamang** na ma-traffic tayo.","translation":"It's raining again, we'll **probably** get stuck in traffic."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kusang-loob na pagpapakasakit o pagdidisiplina sa sarili bilang tanda ng pagsisisi sa mga kasalanan.
original_explanation: The act of making up for your sins, Filipino-style. This can range from the extreme, like self-flagellation during Holy Week, to the more mundane, like your tita making you wash all the dishes after you said something sassy. It’s the 'sorry na po, eto na po ginagawa ko' action.
usage_notes: Strongly associated with religious practices, especially during Lent (Mahal na Araw) in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang anyo ng **penitensiya** ang paglalakad nang paluhod patungo sa altar.","translation":"Kneeling while walking towards the altar is a form of **penance**."},{"sentence":"Maraming deboto ang nagsasagawa ng **penitensiya** tuwing Mahal na Araw.","translation":"Many devotees perform **penitence** every Holy Week."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kemikal na panlinis, karaniwang nasa anyong pulbos o likido, na ginagamit sa paglalaba ng damit o paghuhugas ng mga gamit.
original_explanation: The magic powder or liquid that makes your 'pambahay' smell like 'Fresh Breeze' or 'Kalayaan Fields'. Sold in tingi-tingi packs at the sari-sari store for your daily laba needs. Often just called by brand names like 'Tide' or 'Surf'.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'sabon' (soap), although 'sabon' can also refer to bar soap. 'Sabong panlaba' is a more traditional term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili ka ng **detergent** sa tindahan, naubusan na tayo.","translation":"Buy some **detergent** at the store, we've run out."},{"sentence":"Mas mabango ang damit kapag maganda ang klase ng **detergent** na ginamit mo.","translation":"The clothes smell better when you use a good quality **detergent**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagmamasid, pagbabantay, o pagsusuri sa isang bagay o proseso sa loob ng isang takdang panahon.
original_explanation: This is what your boss does to your work, what a 'marites' does to her neighbors, and what you do to your crush's social media profile. It's observing something closely, whether it's for quality control, security, or just for the sake of gossip. In Tagalog, we often say 'i-monitor'.
usage_notes: Often used with Filipino affixes, like "i-monitor," "minomonitor," "momonitorin."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **i-monitor** ng doktor ang kalagayan ng pasyente.","translation":"The doctor needs **to monitor** the patient's condition."},{"sentence":"**Minomonitor** ng guro ang progreso ng kanyang mga estudyante.","translation":"The teacher is **monitoring** the progress of her students."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga bagay na nabubuhay, lumalaki, o nagaganap sa tubig.
original_explanation: Anything na may kinalaman sa tubig. Halamang-dagat? Akwatiko. Mga isda at pawikan? Akwatiko. Swimming competition? Akwatiko sports. Basically, kung nababasa at nasa tubig, malamang akwatiko 'yan. Parang si Aquaman, akwatiko ang lifestyle.
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang ilarawan ang mga halaman, hayop, o gawain na may kaugnayan sa tubig.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming uri ng halamang **akwatiko** ang makikita sa lawa.","translation":"Many types of **aquatic** plants can be found in the lake."},{"sentence":"Ang paglangoy ay isang tanyag na isport na **akwatiko**.","translation":"Swimming is a popular **aquatic** sport."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan na may malapad na bunganga at makitid na dulo, ginagamit sa pagsasalin ng likido o pulbos sa isang lalagyan na may maliit na butas upang maiwasan ang pagkatapon.
original_explanation: The plastic thingy from your mom's kitchen that you use to transfer cooking oil from a big container to a small bottle. Also, a metaphor for traffic in EDSA where 5 lanes suddenly become 2. That bottleneck? That's an **embudo** effect.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin nang literal para sa kagamitan sa kusina o sa matalinhagang paraan para sa isang 'bottleneck' na sitwasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit ka ng **embudo** para hindi matapon ang langis.","translation":"Use a **funnel** so the oil won't spill."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bilang ng pag-uulit o pagganap ng isang pangyayari sa loob ng isang tiyak na yugto ng panahon.
original_explanation: This is your 'how often' meter. 'Yung **dalas** ng pag-check mo sa phone mo 'pag may hinihintay kang message galing kay crush. Or the frequency of your 'sana all' moments while scrolling through IG. High frequency = madalas. Low frequency = bihira.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit kasama ng 'ng' upang tukuyin ang dalas 'ng' isang bagay (hal. 'dalas ng ulan'). Ang pang-abay na anyo nito ay 'madalas' (often).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakabahala ang **dalas** ng paglindol sa ating bansa.","translation":"The **frequency** of earthquakes in our country is alarming."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa **dalas** ng kaniyang pagliban, bumagsak siya sa klase.","translation":"Because of the **frequency** of his absences, he failed the class."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kabayarang natatanggap ng isang manggagawa o empleyado para sa kanyang serbisyo o trabaho, karaniwang ibinibigay nang regular.
original_explanation: The most beautiful word in the Filipino language, spoken with reverence every 15th and 30th of the month. It's the reason you tolerate your boss, the traffic, and endless Zoom meetings. It's that magical text message from your bank that temporarily solves 99% of your problems. "Wala pa bang sahod?" is the BPO worker's daily prayer.
usage_notes: Not to be confused with the verb 'sahod' (/sa-HOD/), which means to catch falling liquid.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malapit na ang a-kinse, malapit na ang **sahod**!","translation":"The 15th is near, **salary** is near!"},{"sentence":"Kulang pa rin ang **sahod** ko para sa lahat ng bayarin.","translation":"My **wage** is still not enough for all the bills."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon o pagdanas ng lagnat o mataas na temperatura ng katawan.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na bigla ka na lang nag-iinit, pero hindi dahil sa kilig. Ito 'yung legit na kailangan mo na ng Biogesic at kumot. Usually, dahilan 'to para mag-absent sa school o work, or 'pag naulanan ka after makipag-break. "Inuubo, sinisipon, nilalagnat..."
usage_notes: Often used in its future tense "lalagnatin" (will get a fever) or past tense "nilagnat" (had a fever).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpapaulan at baka ka **lagnatin**.","translation":"Don't play in the rain or you might **get a fever**."},{"sentence":"**Nilagnat** ako matapos ang mahabang biyahe.","translation":"I **got a fever** after the long trip."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang propesyonal na nagpaplano, nagdidisenyo, at nangangasiwa sa pagtatayo ng mga gusali at iba pang istruktura.
original_explanation: Sila yung mga artist na math genius din. Sila yung nagde-drawing ng bahay mo sa papel bago pa man maghalo ng semento si kuya. They're the masterminds behind condos, malls, and that dream house you have pinned on your Pinterest board.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinontrata namin ang isang sikat na **arkitekto** para idisenyo ang aming bagong bahay.","translation":"We hired a famous **architect** to design our new house."},{"sentence":"Ang isang magaling na **arkitekto** ay isinasaalang-alang ang kapaligiran sa kanyang mga disenyo.","translation":"A good **architect** considers the environment in his designs."}]

translation: to reflect, to ponder, to contemplate
meaning_filipino: Ang malalim na pag-iisip o pagmumuni-muni tungkol sa isang bagay; pagninilay-nilay.
original_explanation: This is deep-level thinking. 'Yung tipong nakatitig ka sa kawalan habang umiinom ng kape at tinatanong ang sarili, 'Ano na ba ang purpose ko sa buhay?' or 'Mag-reresign na ba ako?' It's the intellectual cousin of 'mag-emote'.
usage_notes: A more formal or literary term for deep thinking.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang umupo sa tabi ng bintana at **magdilidili**.","translation":"She likes to sit by the window and **reflect**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magdilidili** sa mga naging pagkakamali natin.","translation":"We need to **contemplate** on the mistakes we made."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tatak ng liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) na naging pangkalahatang tawag para sa anumang tangke ng gas na ginagamit sa pagluluto.
etymology: Mula sa pangalan ng tatak na 'Gasul' (isang brand ng LPG sa Pilipinas).
original_explanation: That heavy, usually blue or red, metal tank that's the source of your mom's power in the kitchen. When you hear the "click-click-click" of the stove but no fire, you know it's your turn to do the 'buhat' challenge and replace the Gasul. It's a brand name that became the generic term, like 'Colgate' for toothpaste.
usage_notes: Isang klasikong halimbawa ng isang brand name na naging generic trademark o pangkalahatang tawag sa isang produkto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naubusan kami ng **gasul** habang nagsasaing.","translation":"We ran out of **cooking gas** while cooking rice."},{"sentence":"Pakibili mo naman ako ng isang tangke ng **Gasul** sa kanto.","translation":"Please buy me a tank of **Gasul** from the corner store."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkilala at pagpapanatili ng sariling dignidad, karangalan, at halaga bilang isang indibidwal.
original_explanation: Your internal 'Know Your Worth' alarm. It's what stops you from texting your ex at 2 AM, accepting a lowball salary offer, or letting someone treat you like an option. It's the ultimate 'self-care' that doesn't involve a face mask.
usage_notes: A compound noun phrase treated as a single concept, derived from 'paggalang' (respect) and 'sarili' (self).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagkakaroon ng **paggalang sa sarili** ay mahalaga upang hindi ka abusuhin ng iba.","translation":"Having **self-respect** is important so that others won't abuse you."},{"sentence":"Umalis siya sa trabahong iyon bilang pagpapakita ng **paggalang sa sarili**.","translation":"She left that job as a show of **self-respect**."}]

translation: to talk to; to speak with
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pakikipag-ugnayan sa isang tao sa pamamagitan ng salita upang magpahayag ng ideya, damdamin, o impormasyon.
original_explanation: This is what you need to do to your crush instead of just staring. Also, what your boss does to you before giving you a new task on a Friday afternoon. "Bes, kausapin mo naman ako, 'di yung seen zone lang."
usage_notes: The `-in` suffix makes it an object-focused verb, meaning the person being talked to is the focus of the sentence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kausapin** mo siya para malaman mo ang buong katotohanan.","translation":"**Talk to** him so you will know the whole truth."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **kausapin** ang mga taong sarado ang isip.","translation":"It's difficult **to talk to** people who are close-minded."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos o proseso ng pagdurog ng pagkain sa bibig.
original_explanation: The noun form of that ASMR-inducing sound. "Ang lakas ng nguya mo!" is what you tell someone who sounds like they're munching on gravel. It's the rhythm of a good meal.
usage_notes: Refers to the action itself, as a concept or noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang tamang **nguya** ng pagkain para sa maayos na panunaw.","translation":"Proper **chewing** of food is important for good digestion."},{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **nguya** niya mula sa kabilang kwarto.","translation":"I heard his **chewing** from the other room."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sitwasyon kung saan ang dalawa o higit pang tao ay nagpapalitan ng mga panunukso, pang-iinis, o mapanlibak na mga salita.
original_explanation: This is the group chat roasting session in one word. It's the 'asaran' between best friends that's all in good fun (usually). When you and your barkada make fun of each other's old pictures or relationship fails. It's a love language for some, a declaration of war for others.
usage_notes: The `-an` suffix is key, as it implies a reciprocal or mutual action between two or more people. It's often lighthearted.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natigil ang kanilang masayang **pagtutuyaan** nang dumating ang kanilang guro.","translation":"Their happy **mutual teasing** stopped when their teacher arrived."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagtutuyaan** ay normal sa magkakaibigan, basta't walang napipikon.","translation":"**Mutual mockery** is normal among friends, as long as no one gets offended."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng puno na may malalaki at mababangong bulaklak, na karaniwang puti, dilaw, o rosas ang kulay.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung official, Filipinized spelling ng bulaklak na ka-pangalan ng paborito mong ice cream. Kung sa text, 'magnolia' 'yung casual, ito 'yung pormal na email sa boss mo.
usage_notes: Ito ang tamang baybay sa wikang Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakabango ng mga bulaklak ng **magnolya** tuwing umaga.","translation":"The flowers of the **magnolia** are very fragrant every morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Bilang pang-uri, tumutukoy sa isang bagay na may mataas na kalidad, tradisyonal, at nananatiling mahalaga sa paglipas ng panahon. Bilang pangalan, tumutukoy ito sa mga akda o sining na itinuturing na pamantayan ng kahusayan.
original_explanation: Anything that's so good, it never goes out of style. The original "OG." Think Beethoven, Shakespeare, LV bags, or even a simple white t-shirt. In Pinoy context, it's the movie "Himala," a Sharon Cuneta song, or your lola's adobo recipe. If it's still awesome decades later, it's "klasika". The opposite of a one-hit wonder.
usage_notes: Can be used as both an adjective ("musikang klasika" - classical music) and a noun ("isang klasika" - a classic). The masculine form "klasiko" is also used, often for male artists or when referring to a work in the masculine gender in Spanish (e.g., el libro clasico).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang makinig sa musikang **klasika** habang nag-aaral.","translation":"He likes listening to **classical** music while studying."},{"sentence":"Ang nobelang \"Noli Me Tángere\" ay isang **klasika** ng panitikang Pilipino.","translation":"The novel \"Noli Me Tángere\" is a **classic** of Philippine literature."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang kilos ng pagtama sa isang bagay o tao gamit ang kamao.
original_explanation: What Manny Pacquiao does for a living. What you feel like doing to your slow laptop. Metaphorically, "sumusuntok sa buwan" means trying to do the impossible, like trying to get your Grab on a Friday rush hour during a storm.
usage_notes: Present tense of 'sumuntok'. The idiom 'sumusuntok sa buwan' means 'to attempt the impossible'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang boksingero ay malakas **sumuntok**.","translation":"The boxer **punches** hard."},{"sentence":"Para siyang **sumusuntok** sa buwan sa pangarap niyang iyon.","translation":"It's like he's **punching** the moon with that dream of his (trying to achieve the impossible)."}]

translation: to ask for a gift; to have someone give a gift
meaning_filipino: Ang paghiling o pag-udyok sa isang tao na magbigay ng regalo.
etymology: From magpa- (causative prefix) + regalo (gift), which is from Spanish 'regalo'.
original_explanation: This is the art of hinting (or outright asking) for a gift. It's that 'Uy, birthday ko na sa Friday!' text you send to your friends. Or when you tag your jowa in a post of that new phone with the caption 'Sana all.' It's basically causing a gift-giving situation to happen, with you as the happy recipient.
usage_notes: The 'magpa-' prefix makes it a causative verb, meaning 'to cause someone to give a gift'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mahiya, **magparegalo** ka sa ninong mo ng bagong sapatos.","translation":"Don't be shy, **ask for a gift** of new shoes from your godfather."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **magparegalo** tuwing Pasko sa kanyang mga kapatid.","translation":"She likes to **have her siblings give her gifts** every Christmas."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng isang solido na naging likido dahil sa init, o isang bagay na natunaw at humalo sa isang likido.
original_explanation: Your ice cream on a hot day? *Lusaw*. The 3-in-1 coffee powder in hot water? *Lusaw*. Your brain after a 3-hour company meeting that could have been an email? *Lusaw na lusaw*. It's the state of losing your solid form, literally or mentally.
usage_notes: Can apply to things melted by heat (like ice or butter) or dissolved in a liquid (like sugar or salt). `Tunaw` is a common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **lusaw** na ang ice cream bago mo kainin.","translation":"Don't let the ice cream get **melted** before you eat it."},{"sentence":"Siguraduhin mong **lusaw** na ang asukal sa iyong kape.","translation":"Make sure the sugar is **dissolved** in your coffee."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangalan ng isang sikat na pahayagang tabloid sa Pilipinas na kilala sa mga balitang pang-aliw at sensasyonal na pamamaraan.
etymology: From the Spanish 'avante' (forward), used as a brand name for a newspaper founded in 1987.
original_explanation: Not just 'move forward,' but the name of a famous Filipino tabloid. It's the newspaper you see at the newsstand with headlines that are pure clickbait, often featuring showbiz chismis or a scantily clad starlet. 'Teka, tignan ko headline sa Abante!' is a classic line for someone looking for the day's hot gossip.
usage_notes: The capitalization and context distinguish it from the common word 'abante'. Often used as a metonym for tabloid culture itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nabasa mo ba ang balita tungkol sa artista sa **Abante**?","translation":"Did you read the news about the celebrity in **Abante**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing matigas, solido, o matatag ang isang bagay na malambot o likido.
original_explanation: This is what you do to cement to build a house, or to your "paninindigan" (principles) when you're trying to prove a point. It's also what you do to your heart ("patigasin ang puso") when you've had enough of the drama and decide to go full-on stone-hearted. "Bes, 'wag mo nang replyan. **Patigasin** mo 'yang puso mo!"
usage_notes: Can be used literally for physical objects (e.g., cement, jelly) or figuratively for emotions, resolve, etc.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **patigasin** ang semento bago ito tuluyang patungan.","translation":"The cement needs **to be hardened** before anything is placed on top of it."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **patigasin** ang kanyang puso upang hindi na masaktan.","translation":"She tried **to harden** her heart so she wouldn't get hurt anymore."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong ang propesyon ay ang pag-aayos at pagpapaganda ng mga kuko sa kamay.
original_explanation: Your nail technician, therapist, and chismis-buddy all rolled into one. They're the artists who can turn your boring nails into a masterpiece and the keepers of the juiciest neighborhood secrets. A good manikyurista is worth their weight in gold (or at least in expensive nail polish).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahusay gumuhit ng nail art ang aking paboritong **manikyurista**.","translation":"My favorite **manicurist** is excellent at drawing nail art."},{"sentence":"Naghahanap ang salon ng bagong **manikyurista**.","translation":"The salon is looking for a new **manicurist**."}]

translation: to pull towards oneself; to collect (winnings)
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghila o pag-ipon ng isang bagay palapit sa sarili, tulad ng pag-ani ng panalo sa sugal. Ito ang salitang-ugat ng mga pandiwang 'kumabig' at 'kinabig'.
original_explanation: This is what you do with your winnings at the poker table or with the last piece of lechon on the plate. *Kabig!* It's that satisfying motion of pulling something towards you. The opposite of 'tulak' or 'bigay'.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of gambling, games, or gathering items. As a root word, it forms verbs like 'kumabig' (to pull in) and 'kinabig' (pulled in). The noun form 'ang kabig' refers to the act itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **kabig** lang, naubos ang mga taya sa mesa.","translation":"With just one **pull/sweep**, all the bets on the table were gone."},{"sentence":"**Kinabig** niya ang lahat ng panalo sa tong-its.","translation":"He **collected** all the winnings in tong-its."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bulalas na nagpapahayag ng pagkagulat, pag-aalala, pagkabahala, o pag-uudyok.
original_explanation: The Swiss Army knife of Pinoy expressions. It can mean "Oh no, you're in trouble!" when your mom catches you sneaking in past curfew ("Hala ka!"). It can be a gentle "Go on, shoo!" to a stray cat ("Hala, umalis ka diyan"). It can also be a mild "Wow!" or "Really?" when you hear some juicy chismis. The meaning is all in the tone.
usage_notes: The meaning heavily depends on intonation. A sharp, high-pitched "Hala!" expresses alarm, while a drawn-out, low-pitched "Halaaa..." expresses mild surprise or concern.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hala!** Nahulog ang baso!","translation":"**Oh no!** The glass fell!"},{"sentence":"**Hala**, sige, subukan mo kung kaya mo.","translation":"**Go on**, try it if you can."},{"sentence":"**Hala** ka sa nanay mo, hindi ka nagpaalam.","translation":"**You're in for it** with your mom, you didn't ask for permission."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng luwad, semento, o ibang materyales na inihurno at karaniwang ginagamit bilang pantakip sa bubong o sahig.
original_explanation: This is the red, clay tile on your lola's ancestral house roof. The kind that looks like it's seen every typhoon since the Spanish era. When one breaks, it's a whole family project to replace it.
usage_notes: Primarily refers to clay roofing tiles, but can sometimes be used for floor tiles as well, though 'tiles' (the English word) is more common for the latter.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nabasag ang ilang piraso ng **tisa** sa bubong dahil sa malakas na hangin.","translation":"A few pieces of **tile** on the roof broke because of the strong wind."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bansa na katabi o may hangganan sa sariling bansa.
etymology: From 'kapit' (to hold on, to be next to) + 'bansa' (country).
original_explanation: The geopolitical version of a 'kapitbahay'. It's the country you can fly to in an hour or two, the one you have territorial disputes with, or where your Tita gets her imported beauty products. Think Malaysia, Vietnam, or Taiwan for the Philippines.
usage_notes: Used in discussions about geography, politics, and international relations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Malaysia ay isang **kapitbansa** ng Pilipinas.","translation":"Malaysia is a **neighboring country** of the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang magandang relasyon sa mga **kapitbansa**.","translation":"Good relations with **neighboring countries** are important."}]

translation: to sag; to bend; to deform
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbaluktot, pagyuko, o pagbabago ng anyo dahil sa bigat, presyon, o puwersa.
original_explanation: Like your back after carrying the team in a group project, or your will to live after seeing your ex with someone new. It's that feeling of giving in to pressure, literally or figuratively. 'Humutok ang balikat ko sa dami ng trabaho.' It’s the physical or metaphorical act of bending under a heavy load.
usage_notes: Often used to describe something physical bending under weight, like a branch or a shelf. Can also be used metaphorically for a person bending under pressure or hardship.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Humutok** ang sanga ng puno dahil sa dami ng bunga.","translation":"The branch of the tree **sagged** due to the abundance of fruit."},{"sentence":"Parang **humuhutok** ang likod ko sa pagbubuhat ng sako-sakong bigas.","translation":"It feels like my back is **bending** from carrying sacks of rice."}]

translation: chin rest; act of resting the chin on the hand
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpapatong ng baba sa kamay o sa anumang patungan, karaniwang nagpapahiwatig ng malalim na pag-iisip, pagkabagot, o pagmamasid.
original_explanation: This is the official pose of someone who's "overthinking," bored in a Zoom meeting, or watching a sad K-drama. It's the universal sign for "Marites, ano na ang latest?" while waiting for the chismis to drop.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napansin ko ang kanyang malalim na **salungbaba** habang nakatingin sa malayo.","translation":"I noticed his deep **chin rest** as he stared into the distance."},{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na ang **salungbaba**, hindi ka niyan matutulungan sa problema mo.","translation":"Stop **resting your chin on your hand**, that won't help you with your problem."}]

translation: to reflect; to ponder; to contemplate
meaning_filipino: Ang malalim na pag-iisip o pagbubulay-bulay tungkol sa isang paksa, karanasan, o ideya.
original_explanation: 'Yung moment na nakatitig ka lang sa kawalan habang umiinom ng kape, iniisip kung saan ka nagkamali sa life choices mo. O 'yung ginagawa mo kapag Holy Week at bawal mag-ingay, so napipilitan kang kausapin ang sarili mo. The OG "me time".
usage_notes: Kadalasang ginagamit sa pormal o pampanitikang konteksto, at may kaugnayan sa espiritwalidad o malalim na pag-iisip.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga na **magnilay** tayo sa ating mga nagawang pagkakamali upang matuto mula sa mga ito.","translation":"It is important that we **reflect** on the mistakes we've made to learn from them."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdami at pagpatong-patong ng mga bagay sa isang lugar hanggang sa makabuo ng isang bunton o tumpok.
original_explanation: This is your laundry chair on a Saturday morning. Or the unread messages from your GC. Or the work from your boss that piled up right before a long weekend. It's the physical embodiment of 'mamaya na.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumambak** na naman ang mga labahin sa aming bahay.","translation":"The laundry has **piled up** again in our house."}]

translation: to train; to practice; to accustom
meaning_filipino: Turuan o bigyan ng paulit-ulit na gawain ang isang tao o hayop upang maging bihasa o masanay sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: The act of turning a 'noob' into a 'pro'. This is what your manager does during onboarding, what a coach does to an athlete, or what you do to your new puppy to get it to stop peeing on the rug. It's the process of leveling up someone's skills, often through repetition and a lot of patience.
usage_notes: This is a transitive verb, meaning it requires an object (the one being trained). Object-focus verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **sanayin** nang mabuti ang mga bagong empleyado.","translation":"The new employees need **to be trained** well."},{"sentence":"**Sanayin** mo ang iyong sarili na gumising nang maaga.","translation":"**Accustom** yourself to waking up early."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng muwebles na ginagamit upang higaan o tulugan, karaniwang binubuo ng isang kutson at balangkas.
original_explanation: Your ultimate happy place after a long day of adulting. It's where you binge-watch Netflix, have imaginary arguments, and promise yourself you'll wake up early tomorrow (you won't). The final boss of "sana higa na lang ako buong araw."
usage_notes: Madalas itong tumutukoy sa mas tradisyonal o simpleng kama, kumpara sa mga modernong kama.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagod na pagod ako at gusto ko na lang humiga sa aking **katre**.","translation":"I'm so tired and I just want to lie down on my **bed**."},{"sentence":"Isang lumang **katre** na gawa sa yantok ang nasa silid.","translation":"An old **cot** made of rattan was in the room."}]

meaning_filipino: Ialok o ibigay ang isang ari-arian, tulad ng bahay o sasakyan, upang gamitin ng iba sa loob ng takdang panahon kapalit ng bayad o upa.
etymology: Panlaping 'ipa-' + salitang-ugat na 'alkila' (mula sa Espanyol na 'alquilar').
original_explanation: The official verb for becoming a landlord. Eto yung plano mo sa extra room sa bahay para maging "passive income." From condo units to event gowns, kung may gamit kang hindi ginagamit, pwede mong ipaalkila para kumita. It's the "make your assets work for you" action word.
usage_notes: Ang 'alkila' ay hiram na salita mula sa Espanyol. Ang katutubong katumbas ay 'upa', kaya karaniwan din ang 'paupahan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Plano niyang **ipaalkila** ang kanyang lumang apartment.","translation":"He plans to **rent out** his old apartment."},{"sentence":"Magkano daw **ipaalkila** ang sound system para sa party?","translation":"How much is it to **have the sound system rented** for the party?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging maga o malaki ng mga mata, karaniwang sanhi ng pag-iyak, kakulangan sa tulog, o alerdyi.
original_explanation: The official look of someone who just finished a K-drama marathon, had a major 'iyak' session with their bestie, or just pulled an all-nighter for a deadline. The evidence of your emotional or physical exhaustion, printed right on your face.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used to describe swollen eyes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya maitago ang **pamumugto** ng kanyang mga mata matapos umiyak buong gabi.","translation":"She couldn't hide the **swelling** of her eyes after crying all night."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa puyat, halata ang **pamumugto** sa ilalim ng mata niya.","translation":"Because of lack of sleep, the **swelling** under his eyes was obvious."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang taong hangal, tanga, o walang sapat na pag-iisip.
original_explanation: This is what your nanay calls you when you do something incredibly stupid, like leaving the house without an umbrella during typhoon season. It's the Spanish-sounding cousin of "tanga" and "gago." Medyo old-school na pakinggan, parang kontrabida sa lumang pelikula.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pang-uri (adjective) o pangalan (noun, 'a fool'). Itinuturing na medyo luma na at mas karaniwan sa mga nakatatanda.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **tonto**, isipin mo muna ang iyong gagawin.","translation":"Don't be a **fool**, think about what you're going to do first."},{"sentence":"Ang **tonto**ng desisyon niya ay nagdulot ng malaking problema.","translation":"His **foolish** decision caused a big problem."}]

translation: carriage for a saint's statue; processional carriage
meaning_filipino: Isang pormal at pinalamutiang sasakyan o plataporma, kadalasang para sa mga imahen ng santo, na ginagamit sa mga prusisyon.
etymology: From Spanish "carroza" (carriage, float), possibly a shortened or variant form.
original_explanation: The holy roller. It's the pimped-out ride for saints during fiestas and Holy Week. It's got more lights and flowers than a debutante's cotillion, and it moves at 0.5 kph, powered by pure devotion (and a lot of pushing).
usage_notes: Often synonymous with 'karosa'. 'Karos' might be a more specific or regional term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinapasan ng mga deboto ang **karos** ni San Isidro Labrador.","translation":"The devotees are carrying the **processional carriage** of Saint Isidore the Laborer."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangalan, titulo, o bansag na ibinibigay sa isang tao, bagay, o lugar bilang pagkilala sa isang natatanging katangian.
original_explanation: Your screen name, your barkada's panga-asar name for you, or that special title you give to your crush ('Mr. Chinito from Accounting'). It's the label you're known by, whether it's 'Pambansang Kamao' for Pacquiao or 'Babe' for your jowa.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa pormal o pampanitikang konteksto para tukuyin ang isang titulo o epithet.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **taguri** kay Jose Rizal ay Pambansang Bayani ng Pilipinas.","translation":"The **title** for Jose Rizal is National Hero of the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa **taguri** na 'Ang Henerasyon ng Lagim' sa mundo ng wrestling.","translation":"He is known by the **appellation** 'The Generation of Terror' in the world of wrestling."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matindi at malalim na damdamin ng galit, pagkasuklam, o pag-ayaw sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: This is a level up from 'inis' or 'galit'. This is the 'I block you on all social media platforms' kind of feeling. It's the intense emotion reserved for villains in teleseryes, your ex's new partner (jk!), or pineapple on pizza for some people. It's pure, unadulterated hatred.
usage_notes: "Pagkamuhi" is a stronger and deeper emotion than "galit" (anger) or "inis" (annoyance).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkamuhi** ay isang mabigat na dalahin sa puso.","translation":"**Hatred** is a heavy burden to carry in one's heart."},{"sentence":"Puno ng **pagkamuhi** ang kanyang mga mata habang tinitingnan niya ang kanyang kaaway.","translation":"His eyes were full of **animosity** as he looked at his enemy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng panloloko o pandaraya, o sa modernong gamit, ang pagkilos dahil sa biglaang sulsol na bumili ng isang bagay na hindi planado.
etymology: From the 'Budol-budol Gang,' a criminal syndicate known for swindling. The term has been reappropriated for consumer culture.
original_explanation: Originally a serious scam ('Budol-budol gang'). Now, it's what you call the act of being influenced by friends (or yourself) to buy something you don't need. 'Tara, kape lang,' ends with a P5,000 shopping spree. 'Yun ang budol.
usage_notes: Has two main meanings: the original criminal scam and the modern, more lighthearted meaning related to impulse buying.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nabiktima ng **budol** ang matanda at nakuha ang kanyang pensyon.","translation":"The old woman was a victim of a **scam** and her pension was taken."},{"sentence":"Ang 12.12 sale ay isang malaking **budol** para sa mga mahilig mag-shopping online.","translation":"The 12.12 sale is a big **impulse-buy temptation** for those who love to shop online."}]

translation: Bicolano; a person from the Bicol region
meaning_filipino: Isang taong katutubo o naninirahan sa Rehiyon ng Bicol sa Pilipinas. Tumutukoy rin sa wika o pangkat etniko ng rehiyong ito.
original_explanation: A person from the Bicol region, the land of spicy food and the majestic Mayon Volcano. If someone can handle extra sili in their laing or Bicol Express without breaking a sweat, they might be a Bicolano. They're known for being "uragon" (brave/feisty) and for their delicious, gata-heavy cuisine.
usage_notes: Capitalized as it is a proper noun referring to a specific group of people or language. The feminine form is 'Bicolana'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **Bicolano** ang nagluto ng masarap na laing na ito.","translation":"A **Bicolano** cooked this delicious laing."},{"sentence":"Marunong siyang magsalita ng **Bicolano** dahil doon siya lumaki.","translation":"He knows how to speak **Bicolano** because he grew up there."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paraang hindi sinasadya, hindi namamalayan, o labag sa kalooban.
original_explanation: This is your "Oops, I did it again" moment, but make it literary. 'Yung **sa di-kawasa** ay napindot mo 'yung "send" sa maling tao. O 'yung **sa di-kawasa** ay napaluha ka habang nanonood ng K-drama. It's that action or feeling that just... happens, without you consciously deciding on it. Your body or emotions betraying your brain.
usage_notes: Isang pampanitikang salita na bihira nang gamitin sa pang-araw-araw na usapan. Madalas itong matatagpuan sa mga nobela at klasikong akda.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sa di-kawasa**, napangiti siya nang maalala ang kanilang nakaraan.","translation":"**Unknowingly**, he smiled as he remembered their past."}]

translation: to make an entrance; to start a job
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpasok sa isang lugar, partikular sa isang paraan na nakakatawag-pansin; maaari ring tumukoy sa pagsisimula sa isang bagong trabaho o tungkulin.
etymology: Hiram sa salitang Espanyol na 'entrar' (to enter) at nilapian ng unlaping `mag-`.
original_explanation: This isn't just "pumasok" (to enter). This is entering with style! Yung pagpasok mo sa party na slow-motion at may background music sa isip mo. It can also mean starting a new job, like, "Kelan ka **mag-eentra** sa bago mong work?" It's about making a significant entry, whether onto a stage or into a new office.
usage_notes: May bahagyang mas dramatiko o pormal na konotasyon kaysa sa 'pumasok'. Karaniwan ding ginagamit sa konteksto ng pagsisimula sa trabaho.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Aabangan ko kung paano siya **mag-eentra** sa entablado mamaya.","translation":"I will watch for how she **makes an entrance** on stage later."},{"sentence":"Sa Lunes na ako **mag-eentra** sa bago kong kumpanya.","translation":"I **will start** at my new company on Monday."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang unahang bahagi ng isang bagay, lalo na ng sasakyan; ang posisyon sa unahan o pangunguna.
original_explanation: In a jeepney, this is the prime real estate seat right beside the driver. May extra bayad 'yan for the privilege of being the unofficial DJ and taga-abot ng bayad. In sports, it means being the striker or forward. Basically, "nasa unahan ka, bes."
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng sasakyan (lalo na sa jeepney) o sa palakasan (sports).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto niyang umupo sa **delantera** para maluwag.","translation":"He wants to sit in the **front** because it's spacious."},{"sentence":"Magaling ang **delantera** ng kanilang koponan sa basketball.","translation":"The **forward player** of their basketball team is excellent."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng mga bantas, tulad ng tuldok, kuwit, o tandang pananong, sa isang sulatin upang maging malinaw ang kahulugan nito.
original_explanation: This is what your Filipino teacher kept telling you to do in your essays. To `magbantas` is to use periods, commas, and question marks correctly. In the age of texting, this is a dying art. A message without punctuation can mean anything. 'Tara kain' vs 'Tara, kain!' — one is a suggestion, the other is an urgent, hungry command. Punctuation saves lives... and relationships.
usage_notes: Used in the context of writing and grammar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natutunan namin sa klase kung paano **magbantas** nang tama sa aming mga sanaysay.","translation":"We learned in class how to **punctuate** our essays correctly."},{"sentence":"Mahalagang **magbantas** ka ng iyong mga pangungusap upang maunawaan ka ng mambabasa.","translation":"It's important to **punctuate** your sentences so the reader can understand you."}]

translation: formation; act of creating or assembling
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglikha, pag-aayos, o pagtatag ng isang bagay mula sa mga bahagi nito upang maging isang kumpletong yunit.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung pag-assemble ng bagong bili na IKEA furniture na may kasamang manual na parang hieroglyphics. O 'yung pagbuo ng isang K-Pop group na dumaan sa matinding training. It's the process of making something whole, from a sentence to a team, to a new 'ikaw' after a heartbreak. #Pagbangon
usage_notes: Can be used for physical assembly, forming groups, creating concepts, or personal development.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang teamwork sa **pagbuo** ng isang matagumpay na proyekto.","translation":"Teamwork is important in the **creation** of a successful project."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagbuo** ng pamilya ay isang malaking responsibilidad.","translation":"The **formation** of a family is a big responsibility."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng labanan sa pagitan ng dalawang tandang na may tari o talim sa mga paa, kadalasang may kasamang pustahan.
original_explanation: It's the national pastime for many 'titos' and 'tatays'. More than just a sport, it's a culture of breeding, betting ('pusta'), and a whole lot of shouting ('hiyawan'). You'll hear terms like 'meron' and 'wala', and see intense action that's faster than your internet connection. It's the original e-sports, but with real chickens.
usage_notes: While a popular pastime, it is often associated with gambling. 'E-sabong' refers to the online version.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming tao sa pintakasi para manood ng **sabong**.","translation":"There are many people at the fiesta to watch the **cockfight**."},{"sentence":"Natalo ng malaki ang kanyang pera sa **sabong**.","translation":"He lost a lot of his money in **cockfighting**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang patag na ibabaw sa loob ng isang gusali o silid na tinatapakan o nilalakaran.
original_explanation: The most underrated part of your house until you drop your phone face down on it. It's where you sleep when it's too hot for the bed, where you spill your coffee, and where your mom will make you scrub until it shines like the top of the Crianza. "Paki-punas ng sahig, may natapon!" is a national anthem.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Madulas ang bagong wax na **sahig**.","translation":"The newly waxed **floor** is slippery."},{"sentence":"Natutulog sa **sahig** ang mga bata dahil sa sobrang init.","translation":"The children are sleeping on the **floor** because it's too hot."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapahayag ng katotohanan, pagiging-awtentiko, o kawalan ng pagkukunwari.
original_explanation: The opposite of "fake news." This is the real deal, the OG, the 100% authentic article. "Tunay na kaibigan" is a friend who'll tell you if you have food stuck in your teeth, not just someone who likes your posts. "Tunay na pag-ibig" is the stuff of teleseryes and OPM songs. When you say something is "Tunay!", it's like saying "For real!" or "Legit!"
usage_notes: Can be used as an adjective (tunay na kaibigan) or an adverb (tunay na masaya).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang aking **tunay** na kaibigan.","translation":"She is my **true** friend."},{"sentence":"**Tunay** ngang napakaganda ng Pilipinas.","translation":"The Philippines is **truly** very beautiful."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng isang matinis at paulit-ulit na tunog, karaniwan mula sa isang maliit na kampana o batingaw. Ito ang anyong pangkaganapan ng 'kuliling'.
original_explanation: This is the sound a small bell makes. Think of the ice cream man's bell on a hot afternoon, the bell on a cat's collar, or the little bell at a hotel front desk. It's a light, happy, tinkling sound. The past tense of making that sound is "kumuliling."
usage_notes: Past tense/completed aspect. Used for the sound of small bells.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumuliling** ang kampanilya, hudyat na naririyan na ang sorbetero.","translation":"The small bell **tinkled**, a sign that the ice cream vendor was there."},{"sentence":"Biglang **kumuliling** ang bisikleta ng bata.","translation":"The child's bicycle bell suddenly **rang**."}]

meaning_filipino: Inilalarawan ang isang bagay na may kulay, kintab, o anyo na katulad ng sa pilak.
original_explanation: How you describe your lola's beautiful hair, or the reflection of the moon on the water. It’s that shimmering, metallic-white look. 'Wow, ganda ng buhok niya, **parang pilak**.'
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang ilarawan ang kulay o kintab na katulad ng pilak.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang buhok ng matanda ay kumikinang na **parang pilak** sa sikat ng araw.","translation":"The old person's hair was shining **like silver** in the sunlight."},{"sentence":"Ang tubig sa lawa ay **parang pilak** sa ilalim ng kabilugan ng buwan.","translation":"The water in the lake was **silvery** under the full moon."}]

translation: usurper; grabber; one who seizes property
meaning_filipino: Isang tao na sapilitang kumukuha o umaangkin ng pag-aari, kapangyarihan, o karapatan ng iba.
original_explanation: The OG land-grabber. That tita in the family who mysteriously ends up with all the ancestral properties after lola passes. In the office, they're the one who takes credit for your work. Basically, a human black hole for things that aren't theirs.
usage_notes: Carries a strong negative connotation of greed and unjust acquisition.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinawag siyang **mangangamkam** ng lupa ng mga apektadong magsasaka.","translation":"He was called a **usurper** of land by the affected farmers."},{"sentence":"Isinumpa ng matanda ang pamilya ng **mangangamkam** na umagaw sa kanilang tirahan.","translation":"The old woman cursed the family of the **grabber** who took their home."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-alis ng panlabas na bahagi ng isang bagay mula sa isang ibabaw sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng isang matalim o magaspang na kasangkapan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'kayod' (scrape) at hulaping pandiwa na '-in'.
original_explanation: The action you do to get the last bit of 'sahog' from the pan, or to get coconut meat for 'buko' salad. It's also what you do to a scratch card, hoping to win the jackpot. In a 'hugot' sense, it's like trying to scrape away memories of your ex. 'Bes, kayurin mo na 'yang feelings mo para sa kanya.'
usage_notes: Ang 'kayurin' ay nasa anyong pawatas o pautos. Ang ibang anyo ay kinabibilangan ng 'kinayod' (naganap), 'kinakayod' (nagaganap), at 'kakayurin' (magaganap).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **kayurin** mo ang niyog para sa gagawing bibingka.","translation":"Please, **grate** the coconut for the rice cake we will make."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **kayurin** ang lumang pintura bago magpinta ulit.","translation":"You need to **scrape** off the old paint before painting again."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng sepilyo na ginagamit sa paglilinis o pagpapakintab ng sapatos.
original_explanation: The unsung hero of your 'OOTD.' This is the tool that turns your dusty, sad-looking leather shoes into something respectable for a job interview or a date. It works hand-in-hand with shoe polish (kiwi!). Using a sepilyo sa sapatos is a sign of true adulting.
usage_notes: Used for both cleaning off dirt and for buffing shoes after applying polish.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinuha ni tatay ang **sepilyo sa sapatos** para pakintabin ang kanyang sapatos na panlakad.","translation":"Dad got the **shoe brush** to shine his dress shoes."},{"sentence":"Marumi ang **sepilyo sa sapatos** kaya kailangan itong linisin muna.","translation":"The **shoe brush** is dirty so it needs to be cleaned first."}]

translation: to have someone scoop or fetch (with a container)
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o paghiling sa isang tao na kumuha ng isang bagay, karaniwang likido o butil, gamit ang isang panalok o sisidlan.
original_explanation: When you're too lazy to get water from the 'banga' (clay jar) yourself, so you yell at your younger sibling, "Hoy, pasalok nga ng tubig!" It's the act of delegating the scooping.
usage_notes: The 'pa-' prefix here indicates a request or command. 'Salok' is the act of scooping, often water or grains.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pasalok** ka naman ng bigas sa sako, pakiusap.","translation":"Please **have someone scoop** some rice from the sack for me."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o gusali kung saan isinasagawa ang mga gawaing pang-negosyo, administratibo, o propesyonal.
original_explanation: Your second home, where the coffee is free but so is the stress. The place you commute for 2 hours to reach, just to send emails to the person sitting across from you. Also known as "the office".
usage_notes: The more common, anglicized spelling 'opisina' is also widely used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumalik na sa **upisina** ang karamihan sa mga empleyado pagkatapos ng pandemya.","translation":"Most of the employees have returned to the **office** after the pandemic."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang estado ng pagpapahinga, pagrerelaks, o paglilibang nang walang partikular na ginagawa.
original_explanation: This is the national pastime of the Filipino tito. It's when you're just... there. Maybe on a monobloc chair, with a beer, staring into the middle distance. It's not doing 'nothing', it's actively 'chilling'. It's a low-energy state of contentment, the opposite of 'grind culture'.
usage_notes: Used in informal Taglish. Often used in a verb-like phrase 'nag-chi-chilling'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano'ng ginagawa mo diyan? Wala, **chilling** lang.","translation":"What are you doing there? Nothing, just **chilling**."},{"sentence":"Tara, **chilling** tayo sa bahay mamaya.","translation":"Let's go, let's **hang out** at my place later."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na humihiram ng pera o anumang bagay mula sa iba na may kasunduang ito ay isasauli o babayaran sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: The person who slides into your DMs with 'Friend, baka naman...' and promises to pay you back on the 15th or 30th (sweldo day). They exist in every family, BPO team, and barkada. Sometimes they pay, sometimes they become the subject of 'hugot' posts about 'utang na loob' vs. 'utang na pera'.
usage_notes: The doer/actor form of 'umutang' (to borrow money). Refers to the person who borrows.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging tinataguan ng **mangungutang** ang kanyang pinagkakautangan.","translation":"The **debtor** always hides from his creditor."},{"sentence":"Mahirap magpautang sa isang **mangungutang** na hindi marunong magbayad.","translation":"It's hard to lend money to a **borrower** who doesn't know how to pay back."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sitwasyon kung saan ang isang tao, lalo na ang isang lalaki, ay itinuturing lamang na 'kapatid' o 'bro' ng taong gusto niya, na pumipigil sa pagkakaroon ng romantikong relasyon.
etymology: A blend of "bro" and "friend zone". A modern English neologism adopted into Taglish.
original_explanation: The male equivalent of the friendzone. It's when she sees you as just a 'kuya' or a 'tropa'. You're so busy being a "protective" bro that she never even considered you as a romantic option. Saklap. You just entered the brozone.
usage_notes: A very modern, slang term used by younger generations. Often used interchangeably with 'friendzone'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagi mo kasi siyang tinatawag na 'tol, ayan tuloy, napunta ka sa **brozone**.","translation":"You always called her 'bro', so now you've ended up in the **bro zone**."}]

meaning_filipino: May lasang katulad ng asin; nagtataglay ng mataas na antas ng asin.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `ma-` (nagpapahiwatig ng katangian) at salitang-ugat na `alat` (pagka-maalat).
original_explanation: That feeling when you lose in a game and you're super bitter about it? That's also "maalat." But literally, it's your adobo when you accidentally spill the whole bottle of toyo. It's the taste of the ocean, or the taste of tears (iykyk).
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit para sa pagkain. Isa rin itong karaniwang salitang balbal na nangangahulugang "salty" sa Ingles, o pagiging pikon, masama ang loob, lalo na pagkatapos matalo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Medyo **maalat** ang luto mong sinigang ngayon.","translation":"The sinigang you cooked is a bit **salty** today."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **maalat** diyan, laro lang naman 'yan.","translation":"Don't be **salty** over there, it's just a game."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagkukunwari o pagpapakita ng kabutihan, moralidad, o paniniwala na hindi naman tunay na taglay; pagkukunwaring banal.
etymology: From pa- + pa- + imbabaw (a variant of ibabaw, meaning 'surface'), literally "the act of putting on a surface" or "being superficial."
original_explanation: This is that "Marites" in your neighborhood who gossips about everyone else's sins but goes to church every Sunday. It's posting "#Blessed" on Instagram while being mean to the waiter. It's the art of "Do as I say, not as I do." It's being "plastik."
usage_notes: A strong word used to call out hypocrisy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapaimbabaw** ay ang pagpapakita ng ugaling hindi naman talaga taglay.","translation":"**Hypocrisy** is showing a character that one does not truly possess."},{"sentence":"Galit ang mga tao sa **pagpapaimbabaw** ng politiko.","translation":"The people are angry at the politician's **sanctimoniousness**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na pinagkatiwalaang mangalaga, mag-ingat, o mamahala sa isang ari-arian, negosyo, o kapakanan ng iba.
etymology: Nagmula sa unlaping "ka-" (kaisa) at salitang-ugat na "tiwala".
original_explanation: The designated "bantay." Sila yung iniiwanan ng susi ng bahay 'pag aalis ka, yung friend na pinagkakatiwalaan mo sa chismis, o yung taga-alaga ng aso mo 'pag nag-bakasyon ka. They are the person you trust not to burn the house down or spill the tea.
usage_notes: Bagama't maaari itong mangahulugang 'caregiver', ang 'katiwala' ay mas tumutukoy sa pangangasiwa ng ari-arian, habang ang 'tagapag-alaga' ay para sa pag-aalaga ng tao o hayop.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Mang Jose ang **katiwala** ng aming bukid sa probinsya.","translation":"Mang Jose is the **caretaker** of our farm in the province."},{"sentence":"Bilang **katiwala** ng kumpanya, responsibilidad niyang pangalagaan ang pondo.","translation":"As the company's **trustee**, it is his responsibility to manage the funds."}]

translation: something that will be heard from; source of something heard
meaning_filipino: Ang pinagmumulan o lugar kung saan may maririnig na tunog o balita. Isang anyong pampanitikan na tumutukoy sa isang bagay na magiging paksa ng pandinig.
etymology: From "ka-" + "-ri-" (reduplication of the first syllable of the root) + "dinig" (hear) + "-an".
original_explanation: This is a deep Tagalog word, very poetic. It's like saying "from whence the sound shall come." Imagine you're waiting for gossip (chismis) and you ask, "Saan kaya ang kariringgan natin ng bagong update?" It's the source of the audio, the origin of the tea you're about to hear. Very dramatic.
usage_notes: Primarily used in literary or formal contexts. It's a future passive form of the verb "dinggin" (to hear) but often functions as a noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang silid na iyon ang **kariringgan** ng magandang musika mamaya.","translation":"That room will be the **source of the beautiful music** to be heard later."},{"sentence":"Wala kang **kariringgan** ng anumang reklamo mula sa akin.","translation":"You will **hear** no complaints from me."}]

meaning_filipino: Mahirap unawain dahil sa pagiging masalimuot, magulo, o may maraming magkakaugnay na bahagi.
original_explanation: Parang love life mo, salimuot. O yung traffic sa EDSA. O yung pag-assemble ng gamit galing IKEA na nawawala yung manual. Ito yung level-up ng 'mahirap', ito yung may kasamang pag-ikot ng utak at sakit ng ulo.
usage_notes: Isang mas malalim at pampanitikang salita kaysa sa 'kumplikado' o 'magulo'. Ang pangngalan nito ay 'kasalimuutan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **salimuot** na problema ay nangangailangan ng masusing pag-aaral.","translation":"The **complex** problem requires careful study."},{"sentence":"Naging **salimuot** ang takbo ng istorya ng nobela.","translation":"The plot of the novel's story became **intricate**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na iniluklok sa posisyon sa pamahalaan sa pamamagitan ng boto ng mamamayan.
etymology: From Arabic حَلَال‎ (ḥalāl, “lawful, permitted”), but in the Philippine political context, it has shifted to mean 'elected', likely through Malay influence. This is distinct from the Islamic dietary term 'halal'.
