original_explanation: The person who had the most tarpaulins in your neighborhood last May. They are the "chosen one" by the people—not by a magic wand, but by a ballot and an indelible ink-stained finger. The result of a nationwide "The Voice" competition where the prize is a government seat.
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of politics and elections in the Philippines. As an adjective ('nahalal', 'inihalal'), it means 'elected'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga bagong **halal** na opisyal ay manunumpa sa kanilang tungkulin sa Lunes.","translation":"The newly **elected** officials will take their oath of office on Monday."},{"sentence":"Sino-sino ang mga **halal** para sa senado ngayong taon?","translation":"Who are the **elected officials** for the senate this year?"}]

translation: will be for the better; will do good
meaning_filipino: Magdudulot ng kabutihan, kapakinabangan, o magandang resulta sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: Yung payo ng nanay mo na 'mag-aral ka muna, 'wag muna mag-jowa.' Hindi mo pa gets ngayon, pero **makabubuti** 'yan sa'yo in the long run. It's for your own good, 'ika nga.
usage_notes: A future/potential form using the 'makabu-' prefix. It implies a future positive outcome and is frequently used when giving advice or making predictions about benefits.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-eehersisyo araw-araw ay **makabubuti** sa iyong kalusugan.","translation":"Exercising daily **will be for the better** for your health."},{"sentence":"Sa tingin mo ba ay **makabubuti** kung sasabihin ko ang totoo?","translation":"Do you think it **will do good** if I tell the truth?"}]

meaning_filipino: Magaspang o hindi makinis ang ibabaw o pagkakahabi.
original_explanation: The texture of your lola's 'walis tingting' or unfinished wooden furniture. It's the opposite of 'makinis'. It can also describe a person's speech or manners—harsh and unrefined. Parang kalyo sa kamay ng isang masipag na manggagawa.
usage_notes: Usually refers to physical texture, but can be used metaphorically for behavior.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Maligasgas** ang ibabaw ng lumang mesa na ito.","translation":"The surface of this old table is **rough**."},{"sentence":"Nasanay na ang kanyang mga kamay sa **maligasgas** na trabaho.","translation":"His hands have gotten used to **coarse** work."}]

meaning_filipino: Maaaring tumukoy sa (1) isang lalaking kasabwat sa krimen, o (2) isang karagdagang kagamitan, pyesa, o palamuti para sa isang mas malaking bagay.
original_explanation: Dual-purpose 'to, besh. Pwedeng yung tropa mong sidekick sa kalokohan (yung lalaking version ng aksesoriya), o yung mga gamit na dinadagdag mo sa kotse o cellphone mo para gumanda. Think phone case, car spoiler, or that friend who drives the getaway car.
usage_notes: May dalawang pangunahing kahulugan: isa sa batas (panlalaking anyo ng 'aksesoriya') at isa sa pangkalahatang gamit para sa mga bagay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tsuper ang itinuturong **aksesoryo** sa krimen.","translation":"The driver is being pointed to as an **accessory** to the crime."},{"sentence":"Marami siyang biniling **aksesoryo** para sa bago niyang motorsiklo.","translation":"He bought many **accessories** for his new motorcycle."}]

translation: act of toasting or stir-frying rice
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagluto sa pamamagitan ng paghalo-halo sa isang kawali nang walang o may kaunting mantika, partikular na ang paggawa ng sinangag o pritong kanin.
original_explanation: The sacred morning ritual of turning leftover rice (bahaw) into the glorious breakfast staple, sinangag. It's the sound and smell that wakes up the whole house. The 'pagsasangag' is the key to a perfect 'silog' meal. Level up: add lots of garlic.
usage_notes: Primarily refers to making fried rice (sinangag), but can also refer to toasting other things like coffee beans or nuts in a pan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahusay siya sa **pagsasangag**; malasa at buhaghag ang kanyang sinangag.","translation":"She is excellent at **making fried rice**; her fried rice is flavorful and fluffy."},{"sentence":"Ang sikreto sa masarap na kare-kare ay ang **pagsasangag** ng bigas bago ito durugin.","translation":"The secret to delicious kare-kare is the **toasting** of the rice grains before grinding them."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kumitil o pumatay ng buhay ng kanyang kapwa.
etymology: From 'mamamatay' (future tense of 'pumatay', to kill) and 'tao' (person).
original_explanation: This is the ultimate kontrabida in any teleserye, the one who does the unspeakable. It's not just someone who kills your vibe; this is the real deal, criminal-level stuff. The term literally means 'will kill person.'
usage_notes: A compound noun often used in news reports and legal contexts. It specifically refers to a person who kills another person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahuli na ng mga awtoridad ang **mamamatay-tao** na matagal nang nagtatago.","translation":"The authorities have finally caught the **murderer** who has been hiding for a long time."},{"sentence":"Itinuturing siyang isang malupit na **mamamatay-tao** sa kasaysayan ng kanilang bayan.","translation":"He is considered a cruel **murderer** in the history of their town."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manipis na materyal na karaniwang ginagamit sa pagsulat, pag-imprenta, o pambalot. Tumutukoy din ito sa tungkulin o bahaging ginagampanan ng isang tao.
original_explanation: Literally, the stuff you write your resume on. Figuratively, your 'role' in life or in a situation. "Ano ba ang papel ko sa buhay mo?" is a classic hugot line. It's the ultimate question of whether you're the main character or just an extra.
usage_notes: Has two distinct meanings: the literal object (paper) and the metaphorical role (role). The context of the sentence makes the meaning clear.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng isang malinis na **papel** para sa sulat.","translation":"I need a clean sheet of **paper** for the letter."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **papel** ng mga magulang sa paghubog ng pagkatao ng kanilang anak.","translation":"The **role** of parents is important in shaping their child's character."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panlabas na bahagi o ibabaw ng isang bagay, lalo na ng isang gusali.
original_explanation: Basically, the outside of your house. It's the part you paint, where the plants are, and what your kapitbahay sees when they're being chismosa. Anything 'pang-labas' can be called the eksteryor. Opposite of 'interyor'.
usage_notes: Commonly used in architecture, design, and general descriptions of buildings or vehicles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinapinturahan nila ang **eksteryor** ng kanilang bahay.","translation":"They are having the **exterior** of their house painted."},{"sentence":"Maganda ang disenyong **eksteryor** ng bagong mall.","translation":"The **exterior** design of the new mall is beautiful."}]

meaning_filipino: May hugis na papaloob o parang mangkok; baluktot papasok ang gitnang bahagi.
original_explanation: Think of a satellite dish, a soup bowl, or that dent on your car door after a close encounter with a parking post. It's a surface that curves inward. If you pour water on it, the water will pool in the middle. It's the opposite of a "beer belly" (which is convex, or `umbok`).
usage_notes: A descriptive term for shape and form, often used in geometry, art, or describing physical objects.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang plato ay dapat medyo **malukong** para hindi tumapon ang sabaw.","translation":"The plate should be slightly **concave** so the soup doesn't spill."},{"sentence":"Naging **malukong** ang yero dahil sa bigat ng taong umakyat dito.","translation":"The galvanized iron sheet became **dented/concave** because of the weight of the person who climbed on it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na may pambihirang kakayahang intelektuwal, malikhain, o orihinalidad, na higit pa sa karaniwan.
original_explanation: The person in your group project who does all the work and actually enjoys it. Yung kaklase mong hindi nagre-review pero perfect sa exam. In short, the opposite of someone who asks 'Is the deadline the deadline or the dead-deadline?'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinuturing si Jose Rizal bilang isang **henyo** ng lahing Pilipino.","translation":"Jose Rizal is considered a **genius** of the Filipino race."},{"sentence":"Ang diskarte mo sa paglutas ng problema ay parang **henyo**!","translation":"Your strategy for solving the problem is like that of a **genius**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa ayos na nasa isang tuwid o kurbadong guhit; nakaayos sa isang hanay.
original_explanation: Like when you're at the bank, NFA rice queue, or waiting for the MRT, you're **nakalinya**. It's the state of being in a perfectly straight (or not-so-straight) line, waiting for your turn. Also used for things that are aligned, like projects for the year or even potential romantic partners. "Sino ba ang mga nakalinya sa puso mo ngayon?"
usage_notes: Can refer to people, objects, or even abstract concepts like plans or tasks.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakalinya** na ang mga estudyante para sa \"flag ceremony\".","translation":"The students are already **lined up** for the flag ceremony."},{"sentence":"Marami pa siyang trabahong **nakalinya** para sa buong linggo.","translation":"He has many tasks **lined up** for the whole week."}]

translation: to endure; to bear with patience
meaning_filipino: Harapin at tanggapin ang isang mahirap na sitwasyon, sakit, o pagdurusa nang may pagpapasensya at katatagan.
original_explanation: The unofficial motto of every commuter in Metro Manila. Stuck in traffic for 3 hours? **Magtiis** ka. Siksikan sa MRT? **Magtiis** ka. Mahina ang internet? **Magtiis** ka. It's the art of enduring hardship with a sigh and a silent prayer for patience. A truly Filipino trait.
usage_notes: A very common word expressing the concept of enduring hardship, often with a sense of resignation but also resilience.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magtiis** sa init habang sira pa ang aircon.","translation":"We have **to endure** the heat while the aircon is still broken."},{"sentence":"Para sa pamilya, handa siyang **magtiis** ng kahit anong hirap.","translation":"For his family, he is ready **to endure** any hardship."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng salapi o katumbas na halaga bilang kabayaran para sa isang produkto, serbisyo, o utang.
original_explanation: The most painful part of "add to cart." It's that moment of truth when the GrabFood arrives, the Meralco bill is due, or the waiter puts the bill on your table. The opposite of "libre."
usage_notes: A fundamental verb in commerce and daily life. The actor-focus form of 'magbayad'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **bumayad** para sa ating hapunan kagabi?","translation":"Who **paid** for our dinner last night?"},{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **bumayad** ng pamasahe sa jeep.","translation":"Don't forget to **pay** the fare on the jeep."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay, tao, o pamamaraan na ginagamit bilang proteksiyon, kalasag, o depensa laban sa panganib, atake, o pinsala.
etymology: From pan- + sangga ('to block, parry'). An instrument or means for blocking.
original_explanation: Your ultimate defense mechanism. It can be your lawyer ('abogadong pananggol'), your witty comeback to a basher, or even just your payong against the scorching sun. It's what you use to block the negativity, whether it's a literal punch or just your tita asking 'Kailan ka mag-aasawa?'
usage_notes: Can be literal (a shield) or figurative (a legal defense, a protective argument). 'Abogadong pananggol' is a common term for a defense attorney.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang pananampalataya ang kanyang **pananggol** sa lahat ng pagsubok.","translation":"Her faith is her **shield** against all trials."},{"sentence":"Kumuha sila ng mahusay na abogadong **pananggol** para sa kaso.","translation":"They hired a good **defense** lawyer for the case."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sangay ng medisina na tumutukoy sa pag-aaral at pangangalaga sa pagbubuntis, panganganak, at sa panahon pagkatapos nito.
original_explanation: This is the 'subject' or 'specialization' of the OB-Gyne. It's the entire field of study about pregnancy and childbirth. So if your 'obstetrician' is the player, 'obstetrics' is the game they mastered.
usage_notes: A technical medical term used in academic and clinical settings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-aaral siya ng medisina na may espesyalisasyon sa **obstetrics** and gynecology.","translation":"She is studying medicine with a specialization in **obstetrics** and gynecology."},{"sentence":"Ang **obstetrics** ay isang mahalagang sangay ng pangangalagang pangkalusugan para sa mga ina.","translation":"**Obstetrics** is an important branch of healthcare for mothers."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pang-ugnay na ginagamit upang paghambingin o pag-ugnayin ang dalawang magkasabay na pangyayari o magkasalungat na ideya.
original_explanation: This is the word you use to throw shade politely, or just state a contrast. "Siya, chill lang **samantalang** ako, nagpa-panic na!" or "Mahilig siyang gumala, **samantalang** ako ay mas gusto sa bahay lang." It’s the ultimate "compare and contrast" word for daily life.
usage_notes: Nagsisilbing pangatnig upang pag-ugnayin ang dalawang sugnay. Ipinapakita nito ang pagiging sabay o ang pagkakaiba ng dalawang ideya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umuunlad ang ibang bansa, **samantalang** tayo ay naiiwan.","translation":"Other countries are progressing, **whereas** we are being left behind."},{"sentence":"Nagtatrabaho siya nang husto **samantalang** ang iba ay nagpapahinga.","translation":"He is working hard **while** the others are resting."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na hindi kayang sukatin, isipin, o arukin ng pang-unawa dahil sa kalakhan, kalaliman, o pagiging pambihira nito.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na hindi mo ma-explain. 'Yung pagmamahal ng nanay mo, di-sukat mahaka. 'Yung data usage mo sa kaka-TikTok, di-sukat mahaka. 'Yung lalim ng hugot mo after ng breakup, di-sukat mahaka. It's something so vast, you can't even begin to guess or measure it.
usage_notes: A very literary and deep Filipino phrase.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagmamahal ng isang ina ay **di-sukat mahaka**.","translation":"A mother's love is **immeasurable**."},{"sentence":"Ang lawak ng kalawakan ay **di-sukat mahaka** ng isipan ng tao.","translation":"The vastness of the universe is **beyond human comprehension**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang opisyal na kapangyarihan o karapatan na gumawa ng legal na desisyon at paghatol; ang sakop na teritoryo o lawak kung saan maaaring gamitin ang kapangyarihang ito.
original_explanation: "Sorry, wala sa hurisdiksyon ko 'yan." - The official line of every government employee when you're being passed around from one window to another. It's the invisible line that decides if the Pasig City police or the Mandaluyong City police will respond to a crime on the Guadalupe bridge. It's the ultimate "That's not my job" card.
usage_notes: A formal, legal term used in government and law.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kasong ito ay nasa ilalim ng **hurisdiksyon** ng Korte Suprema.","translation":"This case is under the **jurisdiction** of the Supreme Court."},{"sentence":"Hindi na sakop ng aming **hurisdiksyon** ang kabilang barangay.","translation":"The next barangay is no longer under our **jurisdiction**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking tumpok, tambak, o salansan ng mga bagay na magkakasama sa isang lugar.
etymology: From `ka-` + `bunton` (pile, heap) + `-an`, forming a noun that means 'a place of heaps' or simply 'a large heap'.
original_explanation: Think of the 'laundry chair' in your bedroom that has a mountain of clothes. That's a 'kabuntunan ng damit'. Or the pile of paperwork on your desk that you've been avoiding since last month. It’s an overwhelming pile of stuff.
usage_notes: This is the more standard form than the potential typo 'kabuntuhan'. It emphasizes a large, often messy, pile.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May isang **kabuntunan** ng mga lumang diyaryo sa bodega.","translation":"There is a **heap** of old newspapers in the storage room."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong iwanan na parang **kabuntunan** ang mga laruan mo.","translation":"Don't leave your toys in a messy **pile**."}]

translation: To tease; to jest with; to mock lightly
meaning_filipino: Ang magbiro o mang-asar sa isang tao sa paraang mapaglaro at karaniwang hindi malisyoso.
etymology: Nagmula sa unlaping 'man-' at salitang-ugat na 'tudyo'.
original_explanation: This is the national sport of Filipino families. When your tita asks, 'O, kailan ka ikakasal?' she's not just asking, she's practicing the art of **manudyo**. It's that playful teasing that can sometimes hit a little too close to home. It's supposed to be fun, pero minsan napipikon din tayo.
usage_notes: Karaniwang tumutukoy sa magaan at mapaglarong panunukso, ngunit maaaring ituring na nakakainis depende sa konteksto at relasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **manudyo** sa kanyang mga nakababatang kapatid.","translation":"He likes to **tease** his younger siblings."},{"sentence":"Tumigil ka na sa **panunudyo** sa akin, hindi na nakakatuwa.","translation":"Stop **teasing** me, it's not funny anymore."}]

meaning_filipino: Pormal na pinag-isa sa isang kasalan sa pamamagitan ng isang seremonya, karaniwang pinangungunahan ng isang pari, pastor, o hukom.
original_explanation: The past tense of "I do." It's what happens after the pamamanhikan, the prenup shoot, and spending a fortune on a reception. The result of finding your "the one" (or so you hope). After this, your FB relationship status officially changes to "Married".
usage_notes: 'Ikinasal' implies an agent (like a priest or judge) performed the marriage ceremony for the couple. 'Nagpakasal' focuses on the couple's decision to get married. 'Kinasal' is a more direct past tense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ikinasal** sila ng kanilang ninong na si Mayor.","translation":"They **were married** by their godfather, the Mayor."},{"sentence":"Noong isang taon pa sila **ikinasal** sa huwes.","translation":"They **got wed** by a judge last year."}]

translation: to extort; to squeeze money from
meaning_filipino: Ang kolokyal na termino para sa kilos ng sapilitang paghingi ng pera o anumang bagay na may halaga mula sa isang tao, kadalasan sa pamamagitan ng pananakot o panlilinlang.
etymology: Metaporikal na paggamit ng 'kilkil' (to file), na parang unti-unting kinukuha o 'kinikikil' ang pera ng iba.
original_explanation: This is the more famous, modern meaning. It's what a corrupt traffic enforcer does when they catch you on a 'coding' day, asking for 'pang-kape lang.' It's a subtle (or not-so-subtle) way of squeezing money out of someone. The root 'kilkil' (to file) is used metaphorically, as if you're slowly 'filing away' someone's money.
usage_notes: Ito ay may negatibong konotasyon at itinuturing na slang o kolokyal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahuli ang pulis na **kumikil** sa mga tsuper ng dyip.","translation":"The policeman was caught **extorting** money from jeepney drivers."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal o Taglish na nangangahulugang kasalukuyang tumatanggap ng isang bagay. Ito ay nasa aspektong imperpektibo.
original_explanation: That awkward moment when you're on a video call and someone asks "Naririnig niyo ba ako?" and you reply, "Yes, **nagrereceive** kami ng audio, loud and clear!" Also the state of your cart when you're adding items during a 12.12 sale.
usage_notes: The present progressive form of the Taglish verb "mag-receive". Common in tech, BPO, and casual chats.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagrereceive** na ng mga donasyon ang aming grupo para sa mga biktima ng bagyo.","translation":"Our group is now **receiving** donations for the typhoon victims."},{"sentence":"Hindi ako **nagrereceive** ng text messages ngayon, baka sira ang signal.","translation":"I'm not **receiving** text messages right now, maybe the signal is bad."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging baluktot, hindi tuwid, o pagiging pahilis.
original_explanation: Ever tried drawing a straight line without a ruler and it came out... not so straight? That's kilwa. It's the subtle crookedness in things, or even in a person's intentions. Parang 'yung ngiting peke, may kilwa.
usage_notes: Hindi gaanong karaniwan sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **kilwa** ang pagkakagawa ng mesa kaya umuuga ito.","translation":"There is a **crookedness** in how the table was made, which is why it wobbles."},{"sentence":"Napansin niya ang **kilwa** sa mga linya ng guhit.","translation":"She noticed the **obliqueness** in the drawn lines."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging magkatugma o pareho ng opinyon, damdamin, o desisyon sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang tao.
original_explanation: When the whole barkada finally agrees on where to eat after 30 minutes of "Kahit saan." That magical moment of unity is pagkakasang-ayon. It's the "samedt" moment in the group chat, the collective nod during a meeting, or when your parents finally approve of your life choices (a rare form of consensus).
usage_notes: Stronger than just agreeing; it implies a shared understanding or consensus.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakamit ang desisyon sa pamamagitan ng **pagkakasang-ayon** ng lahat ng miyembro.","translation":"The decision was reached through the **agreement** of all members."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **pagkakasang-ayon** sa loob ng isang pamilya.","translation":"Consensus is important within a family."}]

translation: to erupt; to explode; to fire (a gun)
meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang pagsabog na may kasamang malakas na tunog, gaya ng bulkan, baril, o paputok.
original_explanation: What a volcano does (e.g., Mayon). What you hope fireworks do on New Year's Eve. What you hope your temper *doesn't* do during a stressful meeting, "Kalma lang, bes, baka magputok ka na diyan." It can also refer to the 'BOOM' sound itself.
usage_notes: Can refer to a volcano, a gun, fireworks, or metaphorically, to a person's anger.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagbabala ang PHIVOLCS na maaaring **magputok** ang Bulkang Taal anumang oras.","translation":"PHIVOLCS warned that Taal Volcano could **erupt** at any time."},{"sentence":"Narinig naming **magputok** ang baril sa di kalayuan.","translation":"We heard a gun **fire** in the distance."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang sisigaw, baka **magputok** ang ugat ko sa noo.","translation":"Don't shout, a vein on my forehead might **burst**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang karaniwang pagpapaikli at baybay ng salitang 'katuwiran'; tumutukoy sa batayan, dahilan, o paliwanag.
etymology: A syncopated form of `katuwiran`. The 'u' is elided in common speech.
original_explanation: This is the fast-food version of 'katuwiran'. It's how people actually say it in everyday chika. When you're arguing with your sibling or explaining to a Grab driver why your pin is wrong, you use 'katwiran'. It's quicker, punchier, and gets the job done.
usage_notes: While 'katuwiran' is the formal and grammatically correct form, 'katwiran' is extremely common in spoken language and informal writing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Wala kang **katwiran** para magalit.","translation":"You have no **reason** to be angry."},{"sentence":"Bawat isa ay may kanya-kanyang **katwiran**.","translation":"Each person has their own **justification**."}]

meaning_filipino: Pinaikling tawag para sa sinangag; kaning pinrito sa bawang.
original_explanation: The street-smart, shortened term for *sinangag*. When you're ordering at a *carinderia* and you're in a hurry, you don't say 'Isang tapsilog na may sinangag.' You say, 'Isang tapsilog, extra **sangag**!' It's efficient, just like the dish itself, which efficiently uses up last night's leftover rice.
usage_notes: Used interchangeably with 'sinangag' in informal contexts, especially when referring to garlic fried rice.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pares at mainit na **sangag** ang paborito niyang almusal.","translation":"Beef pares and hot **garlic fried rice** are his favorite breakfast."},{"sentence":"Magluto ka ng **sangag** para sa tapsilog.","translation":"Cook some **garlic fried rice** for the tapsilog."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal at Taglish na termino para sa pagtanggap ng isang bagay, lalo na sa konteksto ng teknolohiya, komunikasyon, o transaksyon.
original_explanation: The Taglish verb for when your G-Cash finally comes through. 'Friend, na-receive mo na ba 'yung pinadala ko?' It's the official language of online sellers, call center agents, and anyone waiting for a package from Shopee. The proper Filipino word is 'tumanggap', but who has time for that when you're tracking a delivery?
usage_notes: This is a Taglish (Tagalog-English code-switching) word and is considered informal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutan **mag-receive** ng OTP sa iyong telepono.","translation":"Don't forget to **receive** the OTP on your phone."},{"sentence":"Paki-check kung **nag-receive** ka na ng email mula sa HR.","translation":"Please check if you have **received** an email from HR."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking gusali na may mga silid-tulugan para sa maraming tao, karaniwan ay para sa mga mag-aaral sa isang kolehiyo o unibersidad.
original_explanation: The place where you learn independence, budgeting, and how to cook anything with a water heater. It's a mix of a library, a party house, and a laundry shop. Also known as "the dorm." Your second home, where your roomies become your second family.
usage_notes: Kadalasang ginagamit sa konteksto ng mga paaralan at unibersidad. Ang "boarding house" ay isang kaugnay na konsepto ngunit karaniwang mas maliit at pribadong pinapatakbo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatira siya sa isang **dormitoryo** na malapit sa unibersidad.","translation":"He/She lives in a **dormitory** near the university."},{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang mga patakaran sa aming **dormitoryo**, lalo na ang curfew.","translation":"The rules in our **dormitory** are strict, especially the curfew."}]

translation: to be smashed to smithereens; to be crushed into tiny pieces
meaning_filipino: Ang tuluyang pagkasira ng isang bagay hanggang sa ito ay maging maliliit na piraso o pulbos.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your heart after a major heartbreak. Charot! It's also what happens to a SkyFlakes cracker inside your bag, or to an ice cube when you're making halo-halo. Total annihilation into tiny bits.
usage_notes: Implies a complete and often violent destruction into small fragments.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Babala: Maaaring **magkadurug-durog** ang babasaging gamit sa loob ng kahon kung hindi ito iingatan.","translation":"Warning: The fragile items inside the box might **be smashed to smithereens** if not handled with care."},{"sentence":"**Nagkadurug-durog** ang biskwit sa ilalim ng kanyang bag.","translation":"The biscuit **was crushed into tiny pieces** at the bottom of her bag."}]

translation: (A command to perform the gesture of 'mano')
meaning_filipino: Isang utos o paanyaya na isagawa ang "pagmamano," isang tradisyonal na paraan ng paggalang kung saan idinidikit ang noo sa kamay ng isang nakatatanda.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na "mano" na nangangahulugang "kamay".
original_explanation: Not a question, but a command that unlocks a core Filipino tradition. It’s the verbal cue for 'bless,' where you take an elder's hand and press it to your forehead. The ultimate sign of respect that also sometimes gets you pamasko (Christmas money).
usage_notes: Kadalasan sinasabi ng nakatatanda (lolo, lola, tito, tita) sa isang nakababata bilang hudyat na gawin ang paggalang na pagmamano. Ang bata naman ay sasagot ng "Mano po."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Mano!** sabi ni Lola sa kanyang apo pagdating nito.","translation":"**(Perform the mano gesture)!** said Grandma to her grandchild upon their arrival."},{"sentence":"“O, mga apo, dating na kayo. **Mano**!”","translation":"“Oh, grandchildren, you've arrived. **(Give me your hand for a) bless**!”"}]

translation: to motivate; to stimulate one's appetite
meaning_filipino: Pukawin ang gana o interes ng isang tao na gawin ang isang bagay o kumain.
original_explanation: This is what your crush does to you without even trying. Bigla ka na lang may energy mag-reply kahit 2 AM na. It's also what happens when you smell sizzling sisig—bigla kang nagutom. 'To be motivated' or 'to have your appetite whetted.'
usage_notes: Often used for food cravings or the motivation to do something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Amoy pa lang ng kape ay **ganahin** ka nang magtrabaho.","translation":"Just the smell of coffee is enough to **motivate** you to work."},{"sentence":"Sana **ganahin** akong mag-aral mamaya.","translation":"I hope I **get the motivation** to study later."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong kabilang sa lahing Semitiko na katutubo sa Gitnang Silangan at Hilagang Aprika.
original_explanation: A person from the Middle East or North Africa. In the Philippines, this often brings to mind images of OFWs in Dubai, shawarma stands, or rich-looking foreigners. It's a broad term for a diverse group of people, so use it respectfully!
usage_notes: Refers to the ethnicity or nationality. The adjective form is also 'Arab'. The form 'Arabo' is also common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming manggagawang Pilipino sa mga bansang **Arab**.","translation":"There are many Filipino workers in **Arab** countries."},{"sentence":"Isang **Arab** ang may-ari ng tindahan ng shawarma.","translation":"An **Arab** owns the shawarma shop."}]

meaning_filipino: Bagay, tama, o akma para sa isang partikular na layunin, sitwasyon, o tao.
original_explanation: That feeling when your outfit perfectly matches the event's dress code. Or when you find the perfect GIF to reply in a group chat. It's the 'sakto' or 'swak na swak' of situations. The opposite of 'out of place.'
usage_notes: A formal and widely used term in academic, professional, and formal settings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang humanap ng **maangkop** na solusyon sa problema ng trapiko.","translation":"We need to find a **suitable** solution to the traffic problem."},{"sentence":"Hindi **maangkop** ang kanyang kasuotan para sa isang pormal na pagtitipon.","translation":"Her attire is not **appropriate** for a formal gathering."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahina at pigil na tunog ng pag-iyak o pagtawa; isang tunog na parang sa kuting o maliit na hayop.
original_explanation: The sound you make when you're trying not to laugh out loud in a serious meeting. It's that squeaky, suppressed giggle that escapes when your friend messages you a meme during a lecture. Also the sound of a spoiled kid demanding a toy in the mall.
usage_notes: Can refer to both suppressed laughter and a weak, whimpering cry. Context determines the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **ngikngik** niya sa ilalim ng kumot habang nanonood ng nakakatawang palabas.","translation":"I heard her **giggle** under the blanket while watching a funny show."},{"sentence":"Ang **ngikngik** ng tuta ay nakakaawa.","translation":"The **whimper** of the puppy is pitiful."}]

translation: to capsize, to overturn, to invert
meaning_filipino: Pagbaligtad ng isang bagay, tulad ng bangka o lalagyan, na nagiging sanhi ng pagkatapon ng laman nito.
original_explanation: Think of that clumsy moment when you accidentally flip your cup of coffee all over your laptop. That's magtaob. It's the universe telling you to slow down. Also, what happens to a small boat in a big wave, or your patience when the internet goes down during a final exam.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for objects capsizing or figuratively for a situation being completely overturned.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-ingat ang mangingisda upang hindi **magtaob** ang kanyang maliit na bangka.","translation":"The fisherman was careful not to **capsize** his small boat."},{"sentence":"Sa isang iglap, maaaring **magtaob** ang sitwasyon at matalo ang nangungunang koponan.","translation":"In an instant, the situation can **overturn** and the leading team might lose."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, koponan, o hayop na nagwagi at nanguna sa isang kumpetisyon o paligsahan.
original_explanation: The person or team na may karapatang mag-post ng 'Thank you, Lord!' with a trophy emoji. From Manny Pacquiao to the barangay basketball league winner, sila ang bida. Sila yung pinag-uusapan sa inuman at may libreng lechon pag-uwi.
usage_notes: A direct loanword, used in sports, contests, and any competitive event.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Idineklara si Hidilyn Diaz bilang **kampiyon** sa Olympics.","translation":"Hidilyn Diaz was declared the **champion** at the Olympics."},{"sentence":"Ang aming koponan ang naging **kampiyon** sa nakaraang palaro.","translation":"Our team became the **champion** in the last games."}]

translation: to strive for; to persevere for something
meaning_filipino: Pagsikapan nang may tiyaga at determinasyon na makamit ang isang layunin o mithiin.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "tiis ganda" or "tiis-pogi" verb. It’s the grind, the hustle, the blood, sweat, and tears you pour into something. Like finishing your thesis, getting that promotion, or perfecting your lola's adobo recipe. It's not just working hard; it's working hard with *passion* and *sakit sa likod*.
usage_notes: Carries a strong connotation of diligence, perseverance, and overcoming hardship.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat nating **pagpunyagian** ang ating mga pangarap.","translation":"We must **strive for** our dreams."},{"sentence":"Kahit mahirap, kailangan mong **pagpunyagian** ang iyong pag-aaral.","translation":"Even if it's difficult, you have to **persevere for** your studies."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar na may maraming bato o kung saan maraming bato ang matatagpuan.
etymology: From 'bato' (stone, rock) with the circumfix 'ka- -an', denoting a place abundant in something.
original_explanation: Literally, a place that rocks. It's not a party, but a place full of stones. Think of a riverbed, a quarry, or that empty lot where you and your friends used to play when you were kids. It can also describe a bumpy, unpaved road that makes you feel like you're in a cheap massage chair.
usage_notes: Used to describe a location. Can be a natural formation or a man-made one like a quarry.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghanap kami ng magagandang ilog sa **kabatuhan** ng Rizal.","translation":"We looked for beautiful rivers in the **rocky area** of Rizal."},{"sentence":"Mahirap maglakad sa **kabatuhan** nang nakayapak.","translation":"It's difficult to walk barefoot in a **stony place**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng sapat na kaalaman, kasanayan, o kakayahan upang maisagawa nang maayos ang isang gawain o tungkulin.
original_explanation: That one groupmate who actually does their part and does it well. The opposite of the government official you see on the news who clearly has no idea what they're talking about. A kompetente person is someone you can trust to 'get the job done' without you having to micromanage them. A rare gem.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng isang **kompetente** na lider para sa ating bansa.","translation":"We need a **competent** leader for our country."},{"sentence":"Napatunayan niyang siya ay **kompetente** sa kanyang trabaho.","translation":"He proved that he is **competent** in his job."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa anumang karamdaman na partikular sa sistemang reproduktibo ng babae, o sakit na nakukuha sa pakikipagtalik.
original_explanation: A somewhat old-fashioned and vague term that titas and lolas use to refer to anything from a simple UTI to more serious 'women's problems.' It's a discreet, almost euphemistic way of talking about health issues below the belt.
usage_notes: The term can be ambiguous, sometimes referring to STDs and other times to general reproductive health issues. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinayuhan siya ng doktor na magpatingin sa espesyalista para sa kanyang **sakit sa babae**.","translation":"The doctor advised her to see a specialist for her **gynecological disorder**."},{"sentence":"Noong unang panahon, malaking kahihiyan ang pagkakaroon ng **sakit sa babae**.","translation":"In the old days, having a **venereal disease** was a great source of shame."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-alis o pagputol sa ulo ng isang tao o hayop.
original_explanation: The most brutal 'delete head' command ever. It's what villains in historical epics do to their enemies. In modern terms, it's what you feel like doing to your laptop when it crashes during a deadline, but, you know, not literally. 'Pugutan ng ulo' is the full, dramatic phrase.
usage_notes: Often used in the form 'pugutan ng ulo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinamumuhian ang malupit na hari na nag-utos na **pugutan** ang mga bilanggo.","translation":"The cruel king who ordered to **behead** the prisoners was hated."},{"sentence":"Isang malagim na krimen ang **pugutan** ng ulo ang isang tao.","translation":"To **behead** a person is a gruesome crime."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasapi o miyembro ng isang lupon o konseho, karaniwan sa antas ng barangay (barangay kagawad) o munisipalidad.
original_explanation: The local politician you see every day. Sila 'yung nag-aapruba ng barangay clearance, nag-oorganisa ng basketball league, at 'yung pangalan laging nakasulat sa mga tarpaulin tuwing fiesta o Pasko. The barangay kagawad is your go-to person for small-time community issues, from a busted streetlight to a neighborhood dispute.
usage_notes: Most commonly refers to a 'barangay kagawad', a member of the village council.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si G. Reyes ay isang masipag na **kagawad** sa aming barangay.","translation":"Mr. Reyes is a hardworking **councilor** in our village."},{"sentence":"Lumapit kami sa **kagawad** upang ireklamo ang maingay na kapitbahay.","translation":"We approached the **councilor** to complain about the noisy neighbor."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbabalik sa isipan ng isang bagay o pangyayari; ang pag-iisip nang may pagkabahala.
original_explanation: That thing your brain does when you suddenly remember you have a 9 AM meeting and it's 8:55. Or when you're trying to sleep and your brain decides to play a highlight reel of all your embarrassing moments. It's also what your mom tells you to do with your keys, and what you feel about your bills: "Ang dami kong alalahanin!" (I have so many worries!).
usage_notes: Maaaring mangahulugang "tandaan" (hal. alalahanin mo ang sinabi ko) o "mag-alala tungkol sa" (hal. huwag mong alalahanin iyan). Ang anyong pangngalan nito ay may ibang diin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Alalahanin** mo sana ang mga pangaral ng iyong mga magulang.","translation":"I hope you **remember** the advice of your parents."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong masyadong **alalahanin** ang problema; malulutas din 'yan.","translation":"Don't **worry about** the problem too much; it will be solved."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bihirang gamiting salita para sa akto ng pagsasama o pag-angkin sa isang teritoryo, na katulad ng pananakop.
etymology: From the root 'salakop' (to annex, to include). The noun is formed via `pan-` + reduplication of the first syllable of the root, resulting in `pananalakop`.
original_explanation: This is the less popular cousin of 'pananakop'. It's like the off-brand version you might hear once in a blue moon, maybe from a lolo who's really into deep Tagalog. For all intents and purposes, you'll probably use 'pananakop' 99.9% of the time.
usage_notes: This word is very rare in modern Filipino. 'Pananakop' is the standard and far more common term for conquest or colonization.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pananalakop** sa mga kalapit na barangay ay matagal nang plano ng datu.","translation":"The **annexation** of the neighboring villages has long been the chieftain's plan."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng isang bagay tulad ng oras, pera, o pagkain sa paraang walang kabuluhan, labis, o hindi produktibo.
etymology: From Sanskrit 'akṣaya' (inexhaustible, undecaying), used ironically in Tagalog to mean the opposite (to cause something to be exhausted).
original_explanation: This is what your mom accuses you of when you spend more than 5 minutes in the shower or leave rice on your plate ('pagkain ng demonyo daw'). It's wasting resources—time, money, effort, food. Spending your whole sahod on 11.11 sale? Nag-aksaya ka. Binge-watching a series instead of working? Nag-aksaya ka. Pursuing someone who doesn't like you back? That's the ultimate 'hugot' version of mag-aksaya ng feelings.
usage_notes: Commonly used with objects like 'pera' (money), 'oras' (time), 'pagkain' (food), or 'lakas' (energy).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mag-aksaya** ng pera sa mga bagay na hindi mo kailangan.","translation":"Don't **waste** money on things you don't need."},{"sentence":"Ayokong **mag-aksaya** ng laway sa pakikipagtalo sa kanya.","translation":"I don't want to **waste** my breath arguing with him."}]

meaning_filipino: Nangangailangan ng ibayong pag-iingat sa paghawak o pagtalakay dahil sa pagiging sensitibo, marupok, o kritikal.
original_explanation: 'Maselang' is the adulting version of 'handle with care.' It's for topics you don't bring up at the family dinner table (like politics or who's paying for the bill). It's also for that stage in a project when one wrong move means you're working overtime all weekend. It’s the verbal equivalent of walking on eggshells.
usage_notes: Used for topics, situations, health conditions, or even body parts. 'Maselang bahagi' is a common euphemism for private parts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iyan ay isang **maselang** usapin kaya't mag-ingat sa iyong sasabihin.","translation":"That is a **sensitive** topic so be careful with what you say."},{"sentence":"Nasa **maselang** kondisyon ang pasyente pagkatapos ng operasyon.","translation":"The patient is in a **critical** condition after the operation."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi nagtataglay ng katangian ng isang nilalang na nabubuhay; patay o walang sigla.
original_explanation: This is that feeling on a Monday morning before coffee. Parang zombie ka lang sa office, nakatingin sa screen pero wala namang pumapasok. It can also describe a boring party or a presentation that could've been an email. "Yung performance nila, parang rehearsal lang, walang-buhay."
usage_notes: Can be used literally for inanimate objects or figuratively for something lacking energy, excitement, or spirit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **walang-buhay** na katawan ay natagpuan sa tabi ng ilog.","translation":"The **lifeless** body was found by the river."},{"sentence":"Naging **walang-buhay** ang pagdiriwang nang umalis ang banda.","translation":"The celebration became **lifeless** when the band left."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malambot at puting keso na nagmula sa Italya, na kadalasang ginagamit sa pizza at iba pang lutuin.
original_explanation: The cheese that gives you that IG-worthy 'cheese pull' shot. It's the reason your pizza is so stretchy and satisfying. Basically, the 'bae' of the cheese world for many Pinoys who love Korean-style cheesy dishes.
usage_notes: Purely a food term. The spelling can be inconsistent in local menus.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **mozzarella** ang pizza na inorder niya.","translation":"The pizza he ordered was full of **mozzarella**."},{"sentence":"Mas masarap ang corndog kung may **mozzarella** sa loob.","translation":"The corndog is better if it has **mozzarella** inside."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng panganganak o paglalabas ng sanggol mula sa sinapupunan ng ina.
etymology: From pag- (nominalizing prefix) + luwal (to issue forth, to come out).
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'delivery' – not from Lazada, but from the womb. It's the final boss level of pregnancy, the culmination of nine months of waiting, cravings, and 'manas' (edema). It's the most intense, painful, and miraculous act of bringing new life (and a new source of 'puyat') into the world.
usage_notes: A more formal or medical term than the common 'panganganak'. It is often followed by 'ng sanggol' (of a baby) to be specific.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ligtas na **pagluluwal** ng sanggol ang pangunahing layunin ng mga doktor.","translation":"The safe **childbirth** is the primary goal of the doctors."},{"sentence":"Isang himala ang bawat **pagluluwal**.","translation":"Every **act of giving birth** is a miracle."}]

meaning_filipino: Naaayon sa katarungan; walang kinikilingan; patas at wasto.
original_explanation: What you hope your boss is during performance reviews. What you wish the referee was during that controversial basketball game. It's about fairness, giving what is due, and not playing favorites. "Sana all makatarungan para walang away."
usage_notes: Often used in legal, ethical, and social contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Humingi sila ng **makatarungan** na sahod para sa kanilang trabaho.","translation":"They asked for a **fair** wage for their work."},{"sentence":"Ang isang **makatarungan** na lider ay pinakikinggan ang lahat ng panig.","translation":"A **just** leader listens to all sides."}]

translation: to oppress; to scorn; to look down upon
meaning_filipino: Hamakin, alipustain, o tratuhin nang walang paggalang at may pagmamaliit.
etymology: Possibly from Sanskrit `duṣṭa` (दुष्ट), meaning 'corrupt, wicked, bad.' The verb form `dustain` is more common than the root `dusta` in modern Tagalog.
original_explanation: This is the verb for treating someone like they're worthless. It’s what the kontrabida does to the bida in every Filipino soap opera. It's looking down on someone, insulting them, and making them feel small. It’s a mix of verbal abuse and social oppression. "Huwag mong dustain ang mga mahihirap." It's a heavy word, full of injustice.
usage_notes: A formal and strong word. 'Maliitin' or 'insultuhin' are more common synonyms.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masakit para sa kanya na **dustain** ng sarili niyang mga kamag-anak.","translation":"It's painful for him to be **scorned** by his own relatives."},{"sentence":"Ipinaglaban niya ang karapatan ng mga **dinudusta** sa lipunan.","translation":"He fought for the rights of the **oppressed** in society."}]

meaning_filipino: Magpalitan ng masasamang salita o pagmumura ang dalawa o higit pang tao.
original_explanation: What happens in a heated online comments section, a road rage incident, or between two rival neighborhood tsismosas. It's a verbal boxing match where the only punches thrown are P.I.s and other colorful insults.
usage_notes: A reciprocal action, meaning it's done by multiple parties to each other. The suffix '-han' indicates this reciprocal nature.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula sa simpleng banggaan, pero nauwi sa **pagmumurahan** ang dalawang driver.","translation":"It started with a simple collision, but the two drivers ended up **cursing at each other**."},{"sentence":"Itigil n'yo na 'yang **pagmumurahan** n'yo, nakakahiya sa mga kapitbahay!","translation":"Stop **cursing at each other**, it's embarrassing to the neighbors!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-alis ng takip, harang, o pagbubukas ng isang bagay na nakasara na naganap na. Ito ay nasa pangnagdaang panahunan.
original_explanation: The "past tense" of opening something. Like when your friend finally tells you their secret, "Sa wakas, nagbukas na siya ng saloobin niya." Or when Jollibee finally launched that new chicken sandwich, "Nagbukas na sila ng bagong item!"
usage_notes: This is the past tense of the verb "bukas" (to open).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **nagbukas** ng lata ng biskwit?","translation":"Who **opened** the can of biscuits?"},{"sentence":"**Nagbukas** ang isang malaking mall malapit sa aming bahay.","translation":"A big mall **opened** near our house."}]

translation: to achieve; to attain; to acquire
meaning_filipino: Maabot, makuha, o makamit ang isang bagay na ninanais o pinagsisikapan.
original_explanation: This is the feeling of finally getting what you worked hard for. Your diploma after years of puyat. Your promotion after endless OTs. That 10-step Korean skincare glow. It's the goal at the end of the "sana" and "dasal lang" journey. It's the ultimate "na-achieve!"
usage_notes: A more formal term for 'makuha' (to get). Often used for abstract goals like peace, success, or knowledge.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinagsisikapan niyang **matamo** ang tagumpay sa kanyang karera.","translation":"He is striving **to achieve** success in his career."},{"sentence":"Ang tunay na kaligayahan ay mahirap **matamo**.","translation":"True happiness is difficult **to attain**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang idyomatikong pagpapahayag para sa isang taong walang hiya, hindi marunong mahiya, o hindi tinatablan ng puna.
original_explanation: Describes someone with a face as flat and unfeeling as a piece of wood ('tabla'). They can take criticism, be caught in a lie, or be called out and just... nothing. The human equivalent of a frozen loading screen. The more common variant is 'makapal ang mukha'.
usage_notes: This is a strong idiom used to express disapproval of someone's lack of shame.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matapos mahuling nandaraya, **tabla ang mukha** niyang humarap sa lahat.","translation":"After being caught cheating, he faced everyone, completely **shameless**."},{"sentence":"Inutangan niya ako pero siya pa ang galit? Talagang **tabla ang mukha**!","translation":"He borrowed money from me but he's the one who's mad? So **thick-faced**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tumanggap o magkamit ng ari-arian, katangian, o responsibilidad mula sa isang yumaong kamag-anak o sa mga naunang salinlahi.
original_explanation: When you get your lola's land, your dad's old watch, or your mom's 'pagiging high-blood.' It's not just about a 'pamana' of wealth; sometimes, what you 'manahin' is the family's 'utang na loob' or even their talent for singing out of tune at karaoke.
usage_notes: This is an object-focus verb ('-in' suffix). The thing being inherited is the subject of the sentence in Filipino. The actor-focus form is 'magmana' or 'mamana'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay **manahin** ng mga anak niya ang kanyang kabutihang-loob.","translation":"I hope her children **inherit** her kindness."}]

meaning_filipino: Butil ng mais na pinaputok o iniluto sa init nang walang mantika; isang uri ng miryenda.
original_explanation: This is the Filipino term for popcorn! Yung sine-snack mo habang nanonood ng Netflix or movie. Before the days of microwave popcorn, si lola would just throw some dried corn kernels into a hot pot, cover it, and wait for the magic popping sound. Classic, simple, at masarap.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to popcorn, the snack made from heated corn kernels.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig kumain ng **binusang mais** ang mga bata habang nanonood ng pelikula.","translation":"The children love to eat **popcorn** while watching a movie."},{"sentence":"Amoy **binusang mais** ang buong bahay.","translation":"The whole house smells like **popcorn**."}]

meaning_filipino: Paghihiwalay o pagtatangi ng isang bagay mula sa karamihan o sa pinagsamahan nito.
original_explanation: This is what you do with your laundry (whites from colors), your trash (biodegradable from non-), and sometimes, your feelings from your decision-making. Also, what your mom does to the good food when guests are coming over. "Okay team, let's **ihiwalay** the urgent tasks from the 'pwede-na-next-week' tasks."
usage_notes: Object-focus verb. The emphasis is on the thing being separated.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **ihiwalay** ang puting damit sa mga de-kolor bago maglaba.","translation":"You need to **separate** the white clothes from the colored ones before doing laundry."},{"sentence":"**Inihiwalay** niya ang para sa bigas at para sa ulam.","translation":"He/She **separated** the money for rice and for the main dish."}]

translation: to have something delivered to someone
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o paghiling na magpadala o maghatid ng isang bagay sa isang partikular na tao o lugar.
original_explanation: Before Grab and Lalamove, this was the original "pabili" culture verb. It's telling someone, "Hey, can you get this delivered to my crush?" "Pahatdan mo naman ako ng pagkain" is the ultimate love language for someone who's too lazy to cook. It's the verb of delegation for deliveries.
usage_notes: This verb focuses on the recipient of the delivery. Compare with 'ipahatid', which focuses on the object being delivered.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pahatdan** mo ng bulaklak si Maria para sa kanyang kaarawan.","translation":"**Have flowers delivered** to Maria for her birthday."},{"sentence":"Gusto ko sanang **pahatdan** ng sulat ang aking mga magulang sa probinsya.","translation":"I would like to **have a letter sent** to my parents in the province."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagbabago ng isang solidong bagay sa anyong likido dahil sa init; ang proseso ng paglusaw ng pagkain sa tiyan.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your heart kapag nginitian ka ni crush. It's also what happens to your ice cream sa ilalim ng araw, and your salary five minutes after payday. The ultimate state of 'nalusaw ako, bes.'
usage_notes: Can refer to literal melting (like ice), digestion of food, or figuratively, the 'melting' of one's heart.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bilis ng **pagtunaw** ng yelo sa baso niya.","translation":"The **melting** of the ice in his glass was fast."},{"sentence":"Maghintay ka ng ilang minuto para sa tamang **pagtunaw** ng pagkain sa iyong tiyan.","translation":"Wait for a few minutes for the proper **digestion** of food in your stomach."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamataas o pinakatampok na bahagi ng isang pangyayari, kuwento, o damdamin.
original_explanation: The 'teleserye' moment. It’s the highest point of drama, the peak of excitement, or the ultimate level of anything. It's the confrontation scene where the 'kabit' is revealed, the final round of the game show, or the moment your data plan runs out during a crucial Zoom call. It's the peak, the climax, the "OMG" moment.
usage_notes: More common than 'sukdol'. Can be used as a noun (climax) or an adverb (extremely). "Kasukdulan" is a common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa **sukdulan** na ng galit ang ama dahil sa ginawa ng anak.","translation":"The father was at the **peak** of his anger because of what his child did."},{"sentence":"Ang **sukdulan** ng pelikula ay ang paghaharap ng magkapatid.","translation":"The **climax** of the movie is the confrontation between the siblings."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan na may paikutan o karete na ginagamit upang iikid at bitawan ang isang linya, tulad ng pamingwit o lubid.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na "molinillo" (maliit na gilingan, pambati).
original_explanation: Ito yung pinapaikot mo sa fishing rod para hilahin yung isda, o yung jowa mong pa-fall. Paikot-ikot lang, hihilahin ka papalapit tapos biglang bibitawan. It's the thing that winds the line, basically.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa konteksto ng pangingisda o mga mekanikal na winches.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inikot niya ang **mulinilyo** para makuha ang malaking isda.","translation":"He turned the **reel** to catch the big fish."},{"sentence":"Sira ang **mulinilyo** ng kanyang pamingwit kaya hindi siya makahuli.","translation":"The **reel** of his fishing rod was broken so he couldn't catch anything."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang eksaktong sentro o pinakapuso ng isang bagay, lugar, o panahon.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'ka-' (nagsasaad ng kasidhian) at 'gitna' (sentro).
original_explanation: 'Yung sweet spot. The bullseye. Sa sinehan, 'yan 'yung upuan na hindi masyadong malapit, hindi masyadong malayo. Sa gabi, 'yan 'yung hatinggabi. Sa barkada, 'yan 'yung tropa mong laging nasa gitna ng chismis. It's the dead center of anything.
usage_notes: Ang unlaping "ka-" ay nagbibigay-diin na ito ang eksakto o pinaka-gitnang bahagi.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa **kagitna** ng gabi, bigla siyang nagising.","translation":"In the **very middle** of the night, he suddenly woke up."},{"sentence":"Itinayo nila ang monumento sa **kagitna** ng plaza.","translation":"They built the monument in the **exact center** of the plaza."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagmula o kasalukuyang naninirahan sa kaparehong nayon, bayan, o lalawigan.
etymology: From 'ka-' (denoting company or being part of a group) + 'nayon' (village, town).
original_explanation: Your "kababayan" but on a more local, small-town level. It's that instant connection you feel when you're in the big city (or abroad!) and meet someone from your tiny hometown. Suddenly, you're best friends, sharing stories about the local chismosa and the best kakanin vendor.
usage_notes: The prefix 'ka-' here signifies a shared origin or community.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagulat si Maria nang malamang **kanayon** pala niya ang bago niyang katrabaho.","translation":"Maria was surprised to find out that her new coworker was her **townmate**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain o hanapbuhay na may kinalaman sa pagtatanim, pag-aalaga ng mga halaman, at pag-ani sa bukid.
original_explanation: Before 'work from home,' there was 'work from bukid.' This is the OG grind, the original source of your sinangag and your mom's pinakbet ingredients. It's the tiring but noble profession that city dwellers romanticize when they get tired of their office jobs and dream of a 'simple life' in the province.
usage_notes: Refers to the act and profession of farming.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagbubukid** ang pangunahing ikinabubuhay ng mga tao sa aming probinsya.","translation":"**Farming** is the main livelihood of the people in our province."},{"sentence":"Maraming kaalaman ang kailangan sa modernong **pagbubukid**.","translation":"A lot of knowledge is needed in modern **agriculture**."}]

translation: to prove; to verify; to confirm
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng katibayan o ebidensya upang mapatunayan ang katotohanan ng isang bagay o pahayag.
original_explanation: This is the formal way of saying 'show me the receipts.' When your friend tells a story that sounds too good to be true, you ask them to patotohanan it. In the corporate world, it's 'kindly provide documentation.' In a court of law, it's presenting evidence. It's the ultimate 'pics or it didn't happen.'
usage_notes: A very formal word. Often found in legal documents, academic papers, and religious texts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **patotohanan** ang iyong mga paratang sa korte.","translation":"You need **to prove** your accusations in court."},{"sentence":"Pinapunta ang saksi upang **patotohanan** ang kanyang naunang salaysay.","translation":"The witness was called **to verify** his previous statement."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sunod-sunod na diskusyon o usapan sa social media, karaniwang nagsisimula sa isang kontrobersyal na post, na naglalantad ng isang problema o 'issue'.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na "issue" (problema) at "thread" (serye ng mensahe).
original_explanation: When a simple tweet or Facebook post explodes into a full-blown investigation by the internet. It starts with 'Spilling the tea...' and ends with screenshots, receipts, and a hundred replies saying 'pa-tag ako 'pag may update.' It's the digital version of a public exposé, where everyone with a data plan is part of the jury.
usage_notes: Isang napakamodernong slang na termino na partikular sa internet. Madalas na ginagamit nang palitan sa 'issue yarn'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita mo na ba 'yung bagong **issue thread** tungkol sa influencer na 'yun?","translation":"Have you seen the new **issue thread** about that influencer?"},{"sentence":"Nag-umpisa lang sa isang comment, naging **issue thread** na agad.","translation":"It just started with one comment, it immediately became an **issue thread**."}]

translation: to root; to dig up with the snout
meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng nguso o ilong upang halungkatin o hukayin ang lupa, karaniwang ginagawa ng mga hayop tulad ng baboy, sa paghahanap ng pagkain.
original_explanation: Think of a pig going wild at a buffet, but the buffet is the ground. It's that messy, determined digging for something good, whether it's truffles or chismis. Figuratively, it's what you do when you "dig up dirt" on someone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **magsungkal** ng lupa ang alagang baboy sa bakuran.","translation":"The pet pig started to **root around** in the yard's soil."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magsungkal** ng mga lumang isyu para iwasan ang gulo.","translation":"Don't **dig up** old issues to avoid trouble."}]

translation: to build; to erect; to stand up
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbuo o pagtindig ng isang estruktura; ang pagtulong sa isang tao na makatayo mula sa pagkakaupo o pagkahiga.
original_explanation: You 'itayo' a building, a business (like 'itatag'), or a friend who just fell down (literally or emotionally). It's the act of making something stand upright. From building a condo to helping your drunk friend get up, the principle is the same: from horizontal to vertical.
usage_notes: Can mean to physically build something, or to help someone stand.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais nilang **itayo** ang isang bagong paaralan sa kanilang komunidad.","translation":"They want to **build** a new school in their community."},{"sentence":"**Itayo** mo ang nahulog na silya.","translation":"**Stand** the fallen chair **up**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbibigay-alam ng pangalan at pagkatao sa iba; nagsasaad o nagpapahiwatig ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: "Hi, I'm [your name], and you are?" That's nagpapakilala. It's the first day of class, a new job orientation, or that awkward moment at a party where you have to introduce yourself. It can also mean 'reveals' or 'shows', like when your actions reveal your true character: `Ang mga gawa mo ay nagpapakilala kung sino ka talaga.`
usage_notes: Can refer to introducing oneself, introducing someone else, or something that reveals or signifies a quality.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bagong empleyado ay **nagpapakilala** sa kanyang mga kasama sa opisina.","translation":"The new employee is **introducing** himself to his officemates."},{"sentence":"Ang usok na iyon ay **nagpapakilala** na may sunog sa di-kalayuan.","translation":"That smoke **indicates** that there is a fire nearby."}]

translation: a dish cooked in coconut milk
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa anumang lutuin, maaaring matamis o maalat, na ang pangunahing sangkap sa sarsa o sabaw ay gata o gatas ng niyog.
original_explanation: The secret to making almost any Filipino dish 10x better. It’s that creamy, rich, slightly sweet flavor you get from coconut milk. From Bicol Express to bilo-bilo, if it's swimming in that white gold, it's ginataan.
usage_notes: 'Ginatan' is a common colloquial or regional variant. 'Ginataan' can refer to the dish itself (as a noun) or describe how it was cooked (as an adjective).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paborito kong meryenda ay **ginataan** bilo-bilo.","translation":"My favorite snack is **ginataan** (sweet coconut milk stew with rice balls)."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang **ginataan** na manok na luto ni nanay.","translation":"The chicken **cooked in coconut milk** that mom makes is delicious."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging hindi malinaw, mahirap maunawaan, o hindi tiyak.
original_explanation: The status of your relationship when they say 'I like you' but still entertain others. 'Ano ba talaga tayo?' The ultimate state of 'hugot'. It's also your eyesight without your glasses on.
usage_notes: Can refer to literal blurriness (vision, photo) or figurative vagueness (idea, relationship).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **kalabuan** ang aming usapan kaya kailangan naming mag-usap muli.","translation":"There was some **vagueness** in our discussion, so we need to talk again."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa **kalabuan** ng kanyang paningin, kailangan niya ng salamin.","translation":"Because of the **blurriness** of his vision, he needs glasses."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang kasangkapan o kagamitan na ginagamit sa pagwiwilig o pagbabasa nang bahagya sa pamamagitan ng pagpapatalsik ng maliliit na patak ng likido.
original_explanation: This could be the spray bottle you use for your plants, the sprinkler in your garden, or even the bottle your barber uses to wet your hair. Basically, anything that turns a liquid into a fine mist or spray.
usage_notes: Karaniwang tumutukoy sa isang kasangkapan, tulad ng spray bottle o sprinkler sa hardin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasira ang **pangwilig** ko ng halaman.","translation":"My plant **sprinkler** broke."},{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng bote na may butas sa takip bilang **pangwilig**.","translation":"She used a bottle with holes in its cap as something **for sprinkling**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mabasa o mapatakan ng ambon, na isang uri ng mahinang pag-ulan.
original_explanation: That feeling when you thought it was just a light drizzle, pero pagdating mo sa office, you look like you took a shower. "Ay, naambunan ako, basang-basa tuloy 'yung buhok ko!" It's the universe's way of saying, "You should've brought an umbrella."
usage_notes: This is the passive form of the verb, focusing on the person or object being drizzled on. The active form is 'umambon' (to drizzle).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maglaro sa labas at baka ka **ambunin**.","translation":"Don't play outside, you might **get caught in the drizzle**."},{"sentence":"**Inambunan** ang mga sinampay kaya basa na naman.","translation":"The laundry **was drizzled on**, so it's wet again."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kulisap na lumilipad at kumakain ng mga halaman, karaniwang itinuturing na peste sa agrikultura.
original_explanation: The OG plague. Before traffic sa EDSA, these guys were the ultimate cause of delays... for farmers. They travel in swarms, like a group of titas descending on a sale at SM.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a plague of locusts, distinguishing it from a solitary grasshopper (tipaklong).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang salot ng **balang** ang sumira sa mga palayan.","translation":"A plague of **locusts** destroyed the rice fields."},{"sentence":"Hinuli ng mga bata ang **balang** sa damuhan.","translation":"The children caught a **grasshopper** in the grass."}]

translation: to be able to make happy; to be able to please
meaning_filipino: Ang magdulot ng kagalakan, kasiyahan, o ligaya sa isang tao.
original_explanation: The goal of every 'manliligaw' or someone trying to impress their partner's parents. It's about bringing joy. When your small gift makes someone's day, you were able to 'makasaya'. 'Sana ang simpleng regalo ko ay makasaya sa iyo.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit simpleng pagbati lang ay sapat na para **makasaya** ng isang kaibigan.","translation":"Even a simple greeting is enough **to make** a friend **happy**."},{"sentence":"Ginagawa niya ang lahat para **makasaya** sa kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"He does everything **to be able to please** his parents."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maikling kuwento na naglalarawan ng isang aral o prinsipyong moral o espirituwal.
original_explanation: This is just the Tagalized spelling of "parable". Think of the stories Jesus told in the Bible, like 'The Good Samaritan'. It's a story with a 'hugot' or a deep life lesson. We call it 'parabola' more often, but 'parabol' is also used.
usage_notes: Mas karaniwang ginagamit ang salitang 'parabola' o 'talinghaga'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **parabol** ng Mabuting Samaritano ay nagtuturo tungkol sa pagtulong sa kapwa.","translation":"The **parable** of the Good Samaritan teaches about helping others."},{"sentence":"Maraming **parabol** sa Bibliya na puno ng aral.","translation":"There are many **parables** in the Bible that are full of lessons."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na laging tumutupad sa kanyang mga pangako, salita, o tungkulin; mapagkakatiwalaan.
original_explanation: This describes a person who's not "paasa." They're the friend who says "On the way na ako" and is actually just 5 minutes away, not still in the shower. A **matuparin** person has a high credit score in the bank of friendship. They keep their word. A rare gem in a world of "seenzone."
usage_notes: Describes a person's character trait of being reliable and true to their word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala si Mayor bilang isang lider na **matuparin** sa kanyang mga binitawang salita.","translation":"The Mayor is known as a leader who is **faithful in fulfilling** his words."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong maging **matuparin** sa iyong tungkulin bilang ama.","translation":"You need to be **dependable** in your duties as a father."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang isang tao o bagay na nasa tapat o harapan; ang taong kinakausap o kasama sa isang sitwasyon.
original_explanation: The person you're literally facing. Can be your boss during a one-on-one, your date across the table, or your mortal enemy in a staring contest. 'Sino ba 'yang **kaharap** mo sa video call?' It’s all about who's in your direct line of sight or interaction.
usage_notes: Often used to refer to the person one is interacting with. Can also be used as an adjective meaning 'facing'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maging magalang ka sa iyong **kaharap**.","translation":"Be polite to the **person you are facing**."},{"sentence":"Ang bahay namin ay **kaharap** ng plasa.","translation":"Our house is **facing** the plaza."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabago o pag-aayos sa isang sistema, institusyon, o indibidwal upang mapabuti at maiwasto ang mga pagkakamali nito.
etymology: From Spanish 'reformar' (to reform), with Filipino verb affixes.
original_explanation: Ito yung "new year, new me" pero para sa mga bagay na mas malaki pa sa'yo, like the government or an entire system. It's the act of trying to fix something that's broken, a process often filled with meetings, paperwork, and people saying "dati pa namang ganyan."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **repormahin** ang sistema ng edukasyon sa bansa.","translation":"The country's education system needs **to be reformed**."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan nilang **repormahin** ang mga patakaran ng kumpanya.","translation":"They tried **to reform** the company's policies."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging maluwag, wala sa higpit, o pagkawala ng orihinal na tensyon o pagkakabinat, karaniwan sa mga tali, lastiko, o balat.
original_explanation: That feeling of your favorite garterized shorts after a year of use—wala nang kapit. It’s like a relationship that's lost its spark, medyo 'maluwag' na. It's the opposite of 'banat' (taut).
usage_notes: Often used to describe things that have lost their elasticity or tension, like ropes, garters, or skin. Do not confuse with the verb root 'hagpos' which means 'to whip' (e.g., hagpusin).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hagpos** na ang garter ng luma kong shorts.","translation":"The garter of my old shorts is already **loose**."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa katandaan, naging **hagpos** ang kanyang balat.","translation":"Due to old age, her skin became **slack**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang impormal na pagdiriwang na ginaganap buwan-buwan upang gunitain ang isang anibersaryo, karaniwan ng isang relasyon.
etymology: Isang portmanteau o pinagsamang salita mula sa Ingles na "month" at "anniversary".
original_explanation: A very Pinoy invention to celebrate love every single month because waiting a whole year for an anniversary is just too long. It's the reason for surprise deliveries, cheesy social media posts ('Happy 17th, babe!'), and the monthly pressure to think of a gift. If your relationship survives past the third 'monthsary', you might be in it for the long haul.
usage_notes: A modern, informal, and very common slang term, especially among young couples.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Saan tayo kakain para sa ating **monthsary**?","translation":"Where are we eating for our **monthsary**?"},{"sentence":"Nakalimutan niyang batiin ako ng \"Happy **Monthsary**!\" kaya may tampo ako.","translation":"He forgot to greet me \"Happy **Monthsary**!\" so I'm a bit upset."}]

translation: bully; to act tough; to hog
meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na termino para sa isang taong mapang-api o siga; maaari ring tumukoy sa kilos ng pagiging mayabang o hindi pagbabahagi ng isang bagay (pagdamot).
etymology: From the name of American actor Humphrey Bogart, known for his 'tough guy' roles. The meaning 'to hog' likely comes from 1960s US slang 'to Bogart a joint'.
original_explanation: Named after the tough-guy actor Humphrey Bogart. In the Philippines, it means to act like a tough guy, a bully. 'Huwag mo akong i-bogart!' means 'Don't you try to bully me!'. It can also mean to hog something, like when your friend won't pass the last piece of chicharon. Classic Pinoy appropriation of a foreign name.
usage_notes: Slang term. Can be used as an adjective ('He's so bogart') or a verb ('Binogart niya yung pagkain').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa lugar nila bilang isang **bogart**.","translation":"He is known in their area as a **bully**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **i-bogart** ang lahat ng lumpia, magtira ka para sa iba!","translation":"Don't **hog** all the spring rolls, leave some for the others!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ihinto ang isang gawain, kilos, o pananalita; huwag nang ituloy. Ito ay karaniwang nasa anyong pautos.
original_explanation: What your mom yells when you've been annoying your sibling for 30 minutes straight. "Tigilan mo na 'yan!" is the Filipino equivalent of "Knock it off!" or "For the love of God, stop!" Also applicable to your feelings for someone who's already taken: "Bes, tigilan mo na."
usage_notes: Usually used in the imperative mood (as a command).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tigilan** mo na ang kakaiyak, walang maitutulong 'yan.","translation":"**Stop** crying, that won't help anything."},{"sentence":"Sana'y **tigilan** na nila ang pag-aaway.","translation":"I hope they **stop** fighting."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggamit ng mga mata upang pagmasdan, suriin, o bigyang-pansin ang isang bagay, tao, o pangyayari. Ito ay nasa pangkasalukuyang aspekto.
original_explanation: That thing you do when your crush walks by, trying to be subtle but failing miserably. Or when you're "working from home" but you're actually just looking at memes all day. The '-um-' infix plus the reduplicated first syllable of the root 'tingin' means it's happening *right now*.
usage_notes: Present tense of 'tumingin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bakit ka **tumitingin** sa akin nang ganyan?","translation":"Why are you **looking at** me like that?"},{"sentence":"**Tumitingin** lang po, miss. Wala pa pong pambili.","translation":"Just **looking**, miss. I don't have money to buy yet."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghahati-hati o paglilimita sa pamamahagi ng mga bagay, lalo na ng pagkain o suplay, sa panahon ng kakulangan.
original_explanation: What you have to do with your 13th-month pay so it lasts until the next sweldo. Or when the family shares one small pack of Chicharon and everyone gets exactly three pieces. 'Uy, **magrasyon** tayo sa kape, paubos na.' It’s the art of making 'petsa de peligro' a lifestyle.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa krisis, kinailangang **magrasyon** ng bigas ang pamahalaan.","translation":"Because of the crisis, the government had to **ration** rice."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magrasyon** ng tubig habang may water interruption.","translation":"We need to **ration** water during the water interruption."}]

translation: to involve; to implicate; to drag into
meaning_filipino: Isama o isangkot ang isang tao sa isang sitwasyon, karaniwan ay isang gulo o problema, kahit hindi ito direktang kasali.
original_explanation: The classic group project nightmare. One person messes up, but the whole group gets dragged down. 'Huwag mo akong **idamay** sa kalokohan mo!' is the national anthem of anyone trying to stay out of trouble their friends are actively seeking.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bakit mo ako **idinamay** sa problema mo sa pera?","translation":"Why did you **involve** me in your money problems?"},{"sentence":"Galit siya dahil **nadamay** ang pangalan niya sa iskandalo.","translation":"He is angry because his name **was dragged** into the scandal."}]

meaning_filipino: Magtanong o humingi ng impormasyon, kasagutan, o paliwanag tungkol sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: Your go-to move sa palengke when you see something you like: "Magkano po?" `Itanong` is the verb for that action. "Itanong mo kay Google" is the modern-day solution to everything. "Itanong mo sa puso mo" is the classic hugot line when you're confused about your feelings.
usage_notes: The object of `itanong` is the question itself or the topic being asked about. Often used in phrases like 'itanong ang daan' (ask for directions) or 'itanong ang presyo' (ask the price).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **itanong** kung anong oras magsisimula ang programa.","translation":"I want to **ask** what time the program will start."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mahiyang **itanong ang presyo** bago ka bumili.","translation":"Don't be shy to **ask the price** before you buy."}]

translation: stool; small chair without a backrest
meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na upuan na walang sandalan at karaniwang may tatlo o apat na paa.
original_explanation: The humble stool. It's the extra seat you pull out when unexpected visitors arrive for merienda. It's the low chair your lola sits on while hand-washing clothes. It's what you stand on to change a lightbulb. It’s not as comfy as a sofa, not as formal as a dining chair, but it's always there when you need a quick place to sit or a little boost in height.
usage_notes: Can also be spelled 'taborete'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umupo siya sa **taburete** habang naghihintay.","translation":"He sat on the **stool** while waiting."},{"sentence":"Kumuha ka ng **taburete** para maabot mo ang bumbilya.","translation":"Get a **stool** so you can reach the lightbulb."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahaging nasa ilalim o pinakamababang posisyon ng isang bagay o lugar.
original_explanation: This is where you find the stuff you forgot you owned. It's the "ground floor" of a building, the "downstairs" of a house, or the bottom of your bag where coins and old receipts go to die. "Nasa ibaba lang ako" is what you text your Grab driver when you're actually still in the shower.
usage_notes: Often contrasted with 'itaas' (top/upstairs).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakikuha ng walis sa **ibaba** ng hagdan.","translation":"Please get the broom at the **bottom** of the stairs."},{"sentence":"Naghintay ako sa **ibaba** ng halos isang oras.","translation":"I waited **downstairs** for almost an hour."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ranggo ng opisyal sa militar, pulisya, o pamahalaang lokal, na mas mababa sa kapitan.
original_explanation: The Tagalized version of 'teniente' or 'lieutenant'. You'll hear this in historical movies about the Katipunan or in rural areas referring to a barangay official.
