It sounds more formal and old-school than the English word. 'Tawagin mo si Tininte!' has a different, more classic ring to it than 'Call the lieutenant!'
usage_notes: More common in historical contexts or formal military/police address. The modern equivalent is often just the English word 'lieutenant'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si **Tininte** Garcio ang namumuno sa aming platun.","translation":"**Lieutenant** Garcio is the one leading our platoon."},{"sentence":"Noong panahon ng Kastila, ang **tininte** del baryo ay isang mahalagang posisyon.","translation":"During the Spanish era, the village **lieutenant** was an important position."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapaligsahan ng dalawa o higit pang tao sa pamamagitan ng pagbaybay o pag-ispeling ng mga salita.
original_explanation: The ultimate showdown between the class nerds. The "-an" suffix turns this into a group activity, like a "bardagulan" but with words. "Tara, mag-ispelingan tayo, ang matalo, taya sa milk tea."
usage_notes: The suffix "-an" denotes a reciprocal or group action, so it implies a contest or a game between people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang magkakaibigan na **mag-ispelingan** habang naghihintay sa kanilang order.","translation":"The friends decided to **have a spelling contest** while waiting for their order."},{"sentence":"Tuwing Buwan ng Wika, mahilig kaming **mag-ispelingan** sa aming klase.","translation":"During National Language Month, we love to **have spelling contests** in our class."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-aalis ng lahat ng saplot sa katawan hanggang sa maging ganap na hubad.
etymology: Isang pinagsamang salita mula sa 'hubo' at 'hubad', na pinagdugtong ng pinaikling 'at' (na naging 't), upang magbigay-diin sa lubos na kahubaran.
original_explanation: This is the nuclear option of undressing. It's not just taking off your work clothes; it's taking off *everything*. This is what you do when you lock the bathroom door for a long, hot shower after the worst week ever. It's the verb form of 'walang-wala na,' both literally and sometimes, figuratively.
usage_notes: This is an intensive form, emphasizing complete nakedness. It's more descriptive and emphatic than just 'maghubad'. The adjective form 'hubu't hubad' is more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dali-dali siyang **naghubu't-hubad** at lumusong sa ilog.","translation":"He quickly **stripped completely naked** and jumped into the river."},{"sentence":"Sa isang eksena sa pelikula, kinailangan ng aktor na **maghubu't-hubad**.","translation":"In one scene in the movie, the actor needed to **strip completely naked**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang partikular na sisidlan o lalagyan na eksklusibong para sa ulam o putahe, karaniwang hiwalay sa lalagyan ng kanin.
original_explanation: The specialized BPO agent of lunch boxes—it only handles one thing: the ulam. This is crucial for preventing your sinigang from making your rice soggy. It's the key to a well-structured, non-chaotic packed lunch. A symbol of culinary organization.
usage_notes: A descriptive phrase rather than a single word, though often functions as a compound noun. It specifies the container is for the main dish, separate from the rice container.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May hiwalay akong **baunan-ng-ulam** para hindi maghalo ang lasa.","translation":"I have a separate **viand container** so the flavors don't mix."},{"sentence":"Naiwan ko yata ang takip ng **baunan-ng-ulam** ko.","translation":"I think I left the lid of my **dish container**."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubhang bago, malinis, o hindi pa nalalaos; may kasiglahan at kalusugan.
etymology: From English 'fresh' + Tagalog linker 'na'. The repetition is for emphasis, a common feature in Philippine languages.
original_explanation: When your tita from the province brings you produce that was literally picked that morning, that's 'fresh na fresh'. Also you, after a 10-hour sleep, ready to face another day of adulting. Or that chismis you just heard, straight from the source.
usage_notes: A common Taglish phrase used to emphasize the freshness of something, from food to looks to gossip.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Wow, **fresh na fresh** ka ngayon ah! Bagong gupit?","translation":"Wow, you look **very fresh** today! New haircut?"},{"sentence":"Galing pa sa Baguio ang mga gulay kaya **fresh na fresh**.","translation":"The vegetables are from Baguio so they are **very fresh**."}]

translation: to break, to snap, to fracture
meaning_filipino: Isang alternatibong anyo ng 'balihin'; putulin o sirain sa pamamagitan ng pagpiko.
etymology: Mula sa salitang 'bali' (broken, fractured) + hulaping pandiwa na '-in'. Ito ay isang karaniwang baryasyon ng 'balihin'.
original_explanation: Same lang 'to sa 'balihin'. Parang 'ikaw' at 'ka', or 'doon' at 'duon'. Either way, may nasisira—patpat man 'yan o tiwala. It's just a variation of the same heartbreaking (or stick-breaking) action.
usage_notes: Ang 'baliin' at 'balihin' ay madalas na ipinagpapalit. Ang pagpili sa pagitan ng dalawa ay maaaring depende sa diyalekto ng rehiyon o personal na kagustuhan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **baliin** ang sanga ng puno.","translation":"Don't **break** the branch of the tree."},{"sentence":"Madaling **baliin** ang puso ng taong nagmamahal nang totoo.","translation":"It's easy to **break** the heart of someone who truly loves."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi tuwid ang pagkakatayo o pagkakalagay; may pagkiling o pabor sa isang panig.
original_explanation: Literally, the Leaning Tower of Pisa is nakakiling. Figuratively, 'yung referee na laging pabor sa isang team, nakakiling ang desisyon niya. Or your friend who always sides with their jowa in an argument, even when they're wrong. Biased, besh.
usage_notes: Can be used both literally for physical tilting and figuratively for bias or partiality.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang poste ng ilaw ay **nakakiling** na matapos ang malakas na bagyo.","translation":"The light post is now **leaning** after the strong typhoon."},{"sentence":"Sinasabing ang desisyon ng hurado ay **nakakiling** sa mas sikat na kalahok.","translation":"They say the judge's decision was **biased** towards the more famous contestant."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng alon na binubuo ng magkaugnay na pitak ng kuryente at balani na naglalakbay sa kalawakan.
etymology: A neologism or coined word from "dagitab" (electricity), "balani" (magnetism), and "liboy" (wave).
original_explanation: Okay, deep breath. This is what happens when Filipino scientists create a word for 'electromagnetic wave'. 'Dagibalni' = dagitab (electricity) + balani (magnetism). 'Liboy' = wave. It's the high-tech, super-formal, textbook-only term for the thing that makes your WiFi, radio, and microwave work. You will never, ever hear this at the palengke. Say this to a friend and they'll think you're casting a spell.
usage_notes: This is a technical, academic term created by the Lupon sa Agham (Committee on Science) to Filipinize scientific vocabulary. It is not used in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ilaw ay isang halimbawa ng **dagibalniing liboy**.","translation":"Light is an example of an **electromagnetic wave**."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan sa pisika ang katangian ng mga **dagibalniing liboy**.","translation":"The properties of **electromagnetic waves** are studied in physics."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maliit at kuwadradong keyk na gawa sa tsokolate, karaniwang malaman at medyo basâ sa loob.
original_explanation: The ultimate "I deserve this" treat. That fudgy, chocolatey square of happiness you buy from a cafe, a bake sale, or that one office mate who's a master baker. Comes in many forms: with nuts, with fudge, with a scoop of ice cream, or even the "special" kind you hear about from your cool Tito in Baguio.
usage_notes: A direct loanword. The meaning is identical to English.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong dessert ang **brownie** na may kasamang vanilla ice cream.","translation":"My favorite dessert is a **brownie** with vanilla ice cream."}]

translation: shield; block; something used for parrying
meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na ginagamit upang harangin o salagin ang isang suntok, atake, o anumang puwersa.
etymology: From 'sangga' (to block, to parry) and the prefix 'pan-' (instrument for).
original_explanation: Your ultimate defense mechanism. Pwedeng literal na shield sa Mobile Legends, o pwedeng yung kaibigan mo na taga-salo ng 'utang' mo muna sa tindahan. It's your go-to excuse when you're late for work ('Grabe po traffic!'), or the 'seen zone' you use to block someone's messages. It's your personal firewall against life's projectiles.
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of fighting, sports, or defense. Can be used metaphorically.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang kanyang braso bilang **pansangga** sa paparating na bola.","translation":"He used his arm as a **block** against the incoming ball."},{"sentence":"Ang pananampalataya niya ang nagsilbing **pansangga** sa mga pagsubok.","translation":"Her faith served as a **shield** against trials."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lantsa na espesyal na idinisenyo o ginagamit para sa paghakot ng mga kalakal o kargamento.
original_explanation: This is a more general term for a cargo boat. While a 'lantsa-de-deskarge' specializes in unloading, a **lantsa-de-kargada** is any motorboat whose main gig is to haul stuff. It's the L300 or pickup truck of the sea, moving everything from chickens and vegetables to construction materials between islands.
usage_notes: 'Kargada' comes from Spanish 'cargada' (loaded). Similar to 'lantsa-de-deskarge' but can be used more broadly.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng mga gulay at prutas ang **lantsa-de-kargada** na patungong palengke.","translation":"The **cargo boat** going to the market is full of vegetables and fruits."},{"sentence":"Ang kanilang negosyo ay ang pagpapaupa ng mga **lantsa-de-kargada**.","translation":"Their business is renting out **cargo boats**."}]

meaning_filipino: Bawasan o pagaanin ang bigat, sakit, hirap, o anumang pasanin.
original_explanation: What you hope Biogesic does for your headache, or what a good hugot playlist does for your broken heart. It's the act of making a burden—physical or emotional—a little bit lighter. 'Friend, anong gamot para ibsan ang sakit ng katotohanang 'di na siya babalik?'
usage_notes: Often used in a more formal or literary context. It is a root word that functions as a verb, typically in the command form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uminom siya ng gamot upang **ibsan** ang sakit ng ulo.","translation":"He took medicine to **alleviate** his headache."},{"sentence":"Walang anumang salita ang maaaring **ibsan** ang kanyang kalungkutan.","translation":"No words could **ease** her sorrow."}]

translation: to burn with anger, to flare up in anger
meaning_filipino: Ang maramdaman ang matinding galit na parang nagliliyab o nag-aapoy sa kalooban.
original_explanation: This is next-level anger. Hindi lang ito 'inis' or 'bad trip.' This is full-on 'Hulk smash!' mode. 'Yung tipong gusto mo nang manira ng gamit o isigaw lahat ng sama ng loob mo. Parang apoy na biglang sumiklab. 'Nang malaman niyang niloko siya, **nagdingas sa galit** ang kanyang puso.'
usage_notes: This is a phrasal verb or idiomatic expression. 'Magdingas' by itself means to flare up or to blaze.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo na siyang asarin pa at baka **magdingas sa galit** 'yan.","translation":"Don't tease him anymore or he might **flare up in anger**."},{"sentence":"**Nagdingas sa galit** ang amo nang matuklasan ang pandaraya ng kanyang empleyado.","translation":"The boss **burned with anger** when he discovered his employee's fraud."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang lalaki na nagpapakita ng kalakasan, katapangan, at pagiging dominante, na karaniwang itinuturing na katangian ng isang tunay na lalaki.
etymology: From Spanish 'barraco' or 'verraco', meaning a boar or an uncastrated pig, implying virility.
original_explanation: The Pinoy equivalent of a 'man's man' or 'alpha male.' He's the tito who drinks his beer straight from the bottle, can fix anything with duct tape, and whose chest hair has its own zip code. Think Lito Lapid in his prime action movie days.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a certain type of masculine ideal, which can be seen as both positive (strong, provider) or negative (toxic masculinity).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala si Mang Tonyo sa kanilang lugar bilang isang tunay na **barako**.","translation":"Mang Tonyo is known in their area as a real **macho man**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong **barako**, matuto ka ring umiyak paminsan-minsan.","translation":"Don't be too **macho**, learn to cry sometimes too."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sining, gawain, o propesyon ng pananahi; maaari ring tumukoy sa tahi mismo o sa taong nananahi (mananahi o modista).
original_explanation: The magic that turns a piece of Divisoria fabric into a prom dress. It's the skill your lola uses to fix the hole in your favorite jeans or alter your pants because you 'gained a little weight.' The OG life skill before online shopping made everything disposable.
usage_notes: Can refer to the act of sewing, the profession, or the seam itself. 'Mananahi' or 'modista' is more common for the person, but 'kustura' can also be used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magaling sa **kustura** ang aking lola; siya ang gumawa ng bestida ko.","translation":"My grandmother is great at **dressmaking**; she made my dress."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong dalhin itong pantalon sa **kustura** para ipaayos.","translation":"I need to bring these pants to the **seamstress** to have them fixed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis na pagbagsak o pagdaloy ng malaking bahagi ng lupa, bato, at mga labi mula sa isang dalisdis o bundok.
original_explanation: This is what happens when a mountain has a bad day, usually after too much rain. It's a literal 'everything is falling apart' moment, but for a slope. A serious and scary event often seen in the news during typhoon season. It’s nature’s way of reminding us who’s boss.
usage_notes: A compound noun. 'Pagguho' means collapse or ruin, and 'lupa' means land/earth. Often used in news reports about natural disasters.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-ingat ang mga residente dahil sa banta ng **pagguho ng lupa**.","translation":"The residents were cautious due to the threat of a **landslide**."},{"sentence":"Maraming bahay ang nasira ng biglaang **pagguho ng lupa**.","translation":"Many houses were destroyed by the sudden **landslide**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gusali o lugar na may mga espesyal na kagamitan, tulad ng teleskopyo, para sa pag-aaral at pagmamasid sa mga bituin, planeta, at iba pang bagay sa kalawakan.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'stargazing' spot, but make it scientific. It's where astronomers go to spy on the universe, like a cosmic 'chismis' session with planets and galaxies. Think PAGASA but for space, not typhoons.
usage_notes: The user provided 'obserbatory', which has been corrected to the standard spelling 'obserbatoryo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais kong bisitahin ang **obserbatoryo** sa Baguio upang makita ang mga bituin gamit ang malaking teleskopyo.","translation":"I want to visit the **observatory** in Baguio to see the stars using the large telescope."},{"sentence":"Ang PAGASA ay may sariling **obserbatoryo** para sa pag-aaral ng panahon at astronomiya.","translation":"PAGASA has its own **observatory** for studying weather and astronomy."}]

meaning_filipino: May mataas na temperatura; hindi malamig.
original_explanation: The default weather setting in the Philippines for 11 months of the year. It's why we have malls, halo-halo, and a national obsession with air conditioning. "Ang init!" is our version of "Hello."
usage_notes: Can describe weather, objects, food, and even situations (e.g., `mainit na usapan` - heated discussion).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sobrang **mainit** ang panahon ngayon, kailangan nating uminom ng maraming tubig.","translation":"The weather is very **hot** today, we need to drink a lot of water."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka, **mainit** pa ang kape.","translation":"Be careful, the coffee is still **hot**."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi angkop, hindi tama, o hindi karapat-dapat para sa isang partikular na sitwasyon, tao, o layunin.
original_explanation: Yung joke na sinabi mo sa isang formal meeting. Yung suot mong shorts sa kasal. Yung pag-text sa ex mo ng "u up?" at 3 AM. Lahat 'yan ay mga bagay na di-nararapat. It's the "read the room" concept. Kung hindi ka sure, malamang di-nararapat 'yan.
usage_notes: A strong word for something that is not fitting, proper, or deserved.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga salita ay **di-nararapat** sa isang pagpupulong.","translation":"His words were **inappropriate** for a meeting."},{"sentence":"Naniniwala siyang **di-nararapat** ang parusang iginawad sa kanya.","translation":"He believes the punishment given to him is **undeserving**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghila o pag-unat sa isang bagay nang may puwersa.
original_explanation: This is what you do when your friend is too lazy to get up, so you literally just pull them off the bed. "Bes, batakin mo na 'yang sarili mo palabas ng kwarto, may life outside!" Also, this is the feeling in your muscles after a hardcore gym session or after carrying all the groceries from the palengke in one trip. "Sakit ng braso ko, parang binatak."
usage_notes: Often used to mean "to pull someone along" or "to stretch something out." The command form is 'batakin mo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Batakín** mo ang lubid para tumibay ang pagkatali.","translation":"**Pull** the rope to tighten the knot."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **batakin** ang mga binti bago tumakbo para hindi mapulikat.","translation":"You need to **stretch** your legs before running to avoid cramps."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan kung saan mayroong labis na bilang ng mga kailangan o kondisyon na dapat tuparin.
etymology: A phrase combining 'napakarami' (very many) and 'rekisitos' (from Spanish 'requisitos').
original_explanation: The official motto of any Philippine government agency, school admission office, or HR department. It's that moment you're handed a list and realize you need your NSO birth certificate, NBI clearance, and a photo of your great-grandmother's pet dog just to apply for a library card. 'Mag-a-apply lang sana ng loan, pero napakaraming rekisitos!'
usage_notes: A common complaint in bureaucratic or formal processes. 'Rekisitos' is a Filipino-ized version of 'requirements'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawalan ako ng ganang mag-apply para sa scholarship dahil sa **napakaraming rekisitos**.","translation":"I lost the motivation to apply for the scholarship because of the **too many requirements**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay-alam sa pagkakakilanlan ng isang tao o bagay sa iba.
original_explanation: The moment of truth when you bring your "special friend" to a family gathering. "Ma, Pa, **ipakilala** ko po sa inyo si..." It's the formal start of either a beautiful relationship or a series of awkward questions from your titas.
usage_notes: Can be used for people, ideas, products, etc.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ipakilala** mo naman ako sa kaibigan mong maganda.","translation":"**Introduce** me to your beautiful friend."},{"sentence":"Oras na para **ipakilala** ang bagong produkto sa merkado.","translation":"It's time to **introduce** the new product to the market."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi kayang tunawin, alinman sa pamamagitan ng init o sa proseso ng panunaw sa tiyan.
original_explanation: Para siyang tingin sa'yo ng ex mo—malamig at di-matunaw. Or 'yung chismis na narinig mo, kahit anong pilit mong intindihin, di-matunaw sa utak mo. It's that thing that just won't break down, whether it's an ice cube that refuses to melt or a heavy meal that feels like a rock in your stomach.
usage_notes: Can refer to literal melting (ice, metal) or digestion (food). Metaphorically, it can mean something difficult to accept or understand.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kinain niyang steak ay parang **di-matunaw** sa kaniyang tiyan.","translation":"The steak he ate felt **indigestible** in his stomach."},{"sentence":"Parang yelo sa puso mo, **di-matunaw** ang galit niya.","translation":"Like ice in your heart, his anger is **unmeltable**."}]

meaning_filipino: Madaling magbago ng isip, desisyon, o damdamin; pabago-bago.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `mapag-` (na nagsasaad ng hilig) + `bago` (pagbabago).
original_explanation: 'Yung jowa mo na sabi "I love you" ngayon, tapos bukas "I need space." O 'yung kaibigan mo na "Tara, beach!" ngayon, tapos mamaya, "Ay, tinatamad ako." Sila 'yung mahirap basahin kasi parang weather, laging nagbabago ang mood at plano. This is the human version of "It's complicated."
usage_notes: Madalas na may bahagyang negatibong konotasyon, na nagpapahiwatig ng kawalan ng paninindigan o pagiging hindi maaasahan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap pagkatiwalaan ang taong **mapagbago** ang isip.","translation":"It's hard to trust a person who is **fickle**-minded."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **mapagbago** sa iyong mga pangako.","translation":"Don't be **capricious** with your promises."}]

translation: to stand around; to stand up intermittently
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paulit-ulit o palipat-lipat na pagtayo, o pananatiling nakatayo nang walang partikular na ginagawa.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you're waiting for your friend who's "on the way" but is probably still in the shower. You stand up, sit down, check your phone, stand up again... just pacing and standing around awkwardly. "Huwag kang tumayu-tayo diyan, umupo ka muna." It's the official verb for people waiting in line at the bank or for a bus.
usage_notes: A repetitive or frequentative form of "tumayo," indicating repeated or aimless standing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bakit ka **tumayu-tayo** lang diyan? Tulungan mo ako dito.","translation":"Why are you just **standing around** there? Help me here."},{"sentence":"Naiinip na siya kaya **tumayu-tayo** na lang siya sa labas ng sinehan.","translation":"He was getting impatient so he just **stood around intermittently** outside the movie theater."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang espasyo sa itaas ng lupa; ang kalangitan; tumutukoy din sa midyum na dinadaanan ng signal ng radyo at telebisyon.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'cloud.' Before iCloud, there was just himpapawid. It's where airplanes fly, where birds chill, and where radio DJs used to say 'Nasa himpapawid po tayo!' It's the sky, but with a more poetic, 'Lupang Hinirang' vibe.
usage_notes: Sounds formal and poetic. 'Langit' is more common for 'sky'. 'Airwaves' is a common modern meaning, especially in broadcasting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga eroplano ay lumilipad sa **himpapawid**.","translation":"The airplanes fly in the **sky**."},{"sentence":"Maririnig ang aming programa sa **himpapawid** sa buong kapuluan.","translation":"Our program can be heard on the **airwaves** throughout the archipelago."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapatuloy o muling pagsisimula ng isang gawain, proseso, o kalagayan na pansamantalang natigil.
etymology: From pag- (nominalizer) + pa- (causative) + tuloy (to continue, to proceed).
original_explanation: This is the "To be continued..." of life. After the commercial break, it's the pagpapatuloy of your favorite teleserye. After a long weekend, it's the pagpapatuloy of work. It’s what you tell your chismosa friend when you get interrupted: "Wait, ituloy mo!" It's moving forward, picking up where you left off.
usage_notes: Extremely common word, used in all contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapatuloy** ng pag-aaral ay isang mahalagang puhunan para sa kinabukasan.","translation":"The **continuation** of one's studies is an important investment for the future."},{"sentence":"Inanunsyo ng PAGASA ang **pagpapatuloy** ng pag-ulan hanggang bukas.","translation":"PAGASA announced the **continuation** of the rain until tomorrow."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kilos, tunog, o tanda na nagbibigay ng impormasyon, babala, o utos.
original_explanation: Yung biglang pag-green ng chat bubble niya after 12 hours of silence? That's a senyal. Or when your internet connection drops during a crucial online meeting, that's 'nawalan ng senyal.' It's any sign, from a traffic light to a subtle hint from your crush.
usage_notes: Often used for electronic signals (Wi-Fi, phone) but also for physical signs or warnings. "Senyales" is a common alternative.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagbigay ng **senyal** ang guro na oras na para magpasa ng papel.","translation":"The teacher gave a **signal** that it was time to pass the papers."},{"sentence":"Mahina ang **senyal** ng Wi-Fi sa kuwartong ito.","translation":"The Wi-Fi **signal** is weak in this room."}]

translation: Act of drawing water from a well
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagkuha ng tubig mula sa isang balon o malalim na sisidlan, karaniwang gumagamit ng timba at lubid.
original_explanation: Before NAWASA and Maynilad, this was the original workout. It's the OG way of getting water—dropping a bucket down a well and pulling it up. Think of it as the ultimate arm day, provincial style. The verb is 'kumadlo'.
usage_notes: Primarily used in rural or historical contexts. The noun form refers to the act itself (`pagkadlo`), while the verb is `kumadlo` (to draw water).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkadlo** ng tubig sa balon ang kanyang unang gawain sa umaga.","translation":"The **act of drawing water** from the well is his first chore in the morning."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang mahabang lubid para sa **pagkadlo**.","translation":"He used the long rope for the **act of drawing water**."}]

meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang tumugon o magbigay ng kasagutan sa isang tanong, suliranin, o tawag.
original_explanation: When you're in a job interview and you nail the question 'Where do you see yourself in 5 years?', you were able to `masagot` it. It’s also what you wish you could do to your ex's late-night 'kamusta ka na?' text, but you know you shouldn't. It's about having the ability, the knowledge, or the courage to respond.
usage_notes: Implies ability or potential. 'Hindi ko masagot' means 'I can't answer,' not just 'I won't answer.' It can refer to answering questions, calls, or even prayers.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay **masagot** ko nang tama ang lahat ng tanong sa pagsusulit.","translation":"I hope I can **answer** all the questions on the exam correctly."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko **masagot** ang tawag niya dahil nasa meeting ako.","translation":"I couldn't **answer** his call because I was in a meeting."}]

translation: to become like steel; to harden (emotionally)
meaning_filipino: Isang matalinhagang pagpapahayag para sa pagtigas o pagiging manhid ng damdamin, na maihahalintulad sa katigasan ng asero.
original_explanation: This is a very old-school, dramatic way to say someone's heart has turned to stone. After a series of heartbreaks, 'Nangangasera na ang puso niya.' It's not just being cold; it's becoming impenetrably hard. Very telenovela vibes.
usage_notes: Primarily used in a figurative or literary sense. Rarely heard in modern casual conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa paulit-ulit na panloloko, tila **nangasera** na ang kanyang puso sa pag-ibig.","translation":"Because of repeated deceit, her heart seemed **to have turned to steel** when it comes to love."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang bagay na akmang-akma ang pagkakabit o pagkakalagay, walang anumang puwang, siwang, o nakausli.
original_explanation: That satisfying feeling when the Tupperware lid actually fits the container on the first try. Or when your custom-made Barong fits you like a glove. It's the OCD dream, the 'sakto' moment, the 'chef's kiss' of fitting things together.
usage_notes: The repetition of 'lapat' serves as an intensifier, meaning 'very well-fitted'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lapat na lapat** ang takip ng garapon kaya hindi natatapon ang laman.","translation":"The jar's lid is a **perfect fit**, so the contents do not spill."},{"sentence":"Gusto ko **lapat na lapat** ang pagkakalagay ng mga tiles sa sahig.","translation":"I want the floor tiles to be laid **perfectly flush**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang masamang espiritu o diyablo; isang taong labis ang kasamaan, kalupitan, o tuso.
original_explanation: The ultimate kontrabida in your lola's stories. Also what your mom calls you when you forget to do the dishes. 'Anak ng dimonyo!' is a classic expression of frustration. It can be a literal evil spirit, or just that one officemate who steals your lunch from the pantry fridge.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun or an expletive. The spelling 'demonyo' is also very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpadala sa tukso ng **dimonyo**.","translation":"Do not give in to the temptation of the **devil**."},{"sentence":"Tinawag niyang **dimonyo** ang amo niyang malupit.","translation":"She called her cruel boss a **demon**."}]

translation: sound of voracious eating; gobbling sound
meaning_filipino: Ang tunog na nalilikha ng mabilis at malakas na pagkain, na tila walang pag-iingat o pagsasaalang-alang sa iba.
original_explanation: 'Yan 'yung tunog ng officemate mong gutom na gutom pagdating ng lunch break, parang may vacuum cleaner sa pantry. Tunog ng pagkain na parang wala nang bukas. 'Di siya 'yung "nom nom" na cute, ito 'yung "HOG HOG HOG" na level.
usage_notes: Isang salitang onomatopeic na naglalarawan ng tunog. Maaari ring gamitin bilang pandiwa (humagabhab).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Rinig na rinig ang **hagabhab** ng mga bata habang kumakain ng kanilang meryenda.","translation":"The **gobbling sound** of the children eating their snacks could be clearly heard."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang humagabhab, para kang hindi nakakain ng isang linggo!","translation":"Don't eat so noisily, it's like you haven't eaten in a week!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng saging na maliit, mataba, at may mga buto.
original_explanation: Not your everyday 'saba' or 'lakatan'. The 'sangi' is a more exotic cousin in the banana family reunion, the one with seeds that makes you go, "Uy, may buto pala 'to?"
usage_notes: Also a known surname in some parts of the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap gawing minatamis ang saging na **sangi**.","translation":"The **Sangi** banana is delicious when made into a sweet preserve."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay o paghahandog ng isang alay sa isang tao, lugar, o entidad.
original_explanation: The action part of 'alay'. It's when you actually *give* the offering. 'Alayan mo ng flowers si crush.' Or when your lola tells you to 'alayan mo ng dasal ang mga pumanaw,' which means to offer a prayer for the departed. It's about directing your sacrifice or gift towards a specific recipient.
usage_notes: This is a verb focusing on the recipient of the offering. 'Alayan mo siya' means 'Offer it to him/her'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat nating **alayan** ng respeto ang ating mga nakatatanda.","translation":"We should **offer** respect to our elders."},{"sentence":"**Alayan** mo ng pagkain ang mga bisita.","translation":"**Offer** food to the guests."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpulupot ng mga braso sa isang tao o bagay bilang pagpapahayag ng pagmamahal, pag-aliw, o pagbati.
original_explanation: The universal cure-all for a bad day, a breakup, or just seeing your lola after a long time. A yakap can be a quick, friendly one ('beso-beso' level) or a tight, 'I-missed-you-so-much' one that lasts for 10 seconds too long. It's the physical form of 'Kaya mo 'yan.'
usage_notes: This is the noun form. The verb form is 'yumakap' or 'yakapin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigyan mo ako ng isang mahigpit na **yakap**.","translation":"Give me a tight **hug**."},{"sentence":"Walang hihigit sa init ng **yakap** ng isang ina.","translation":"Nothing beats the warmth of a mother's **embrace**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang magtiis, maghintay, o magtimpi nang hindi nagagalit; ginagamit din bilang paghingi ng paumanhin.
original_explanation: The national currency of Metro Manila traffic and slow internet. It's what you tell your friend when you're 30 minutes late ('Pasensya na, bes, traffic!'). It's both 'patience' and 'sorry,' which is efficient, really. We've combined the virtue and the apology into one word because we need both constantly.
usage_notes: Commonly used in the phrase 'Pasensya na' to mean 'I'm sorry' or 'My apologies'. 'Humingi ng pasensya' means 'to ask for forgiveness/patience'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Habaan mo ang iyong **pasensya** sa kanya.","translation":"Lengthen your **patience** with him."},{"sentence":"**Pasensya** ka na sa nagawa kong gulo.","translation":"**Sorry** for the mess I made."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang natitirang bahagi ng braso o binti matapos itong maputol; punggos.
original_explanation: This is a deep cut, a word you'd probably hear from your lolo from the province. It's the part of a limb that's left after amputation. It's a heavy word, not something you'd use when talking about your brunch plans. Think of it as the anatomical equivalent of a tree stump.
usage_notes: Very rare in modern conversation. More common in literary or older texts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit may **ukod** na ang isang paa, patuloy siyang lumaban sa buhay.","translation":"Even with a **stump** for a foot, he continued to fight in life."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na ibinibigay o ginagawa nang paunti-unti, may takdang sukat, o limitado dahil sa kakulangan.
original_explanation: Yung internet data mo bago dumating ang sweldo—rasyun-rasyon ang paggamit. Bawal mag-stream ng Netflix, hanggang FB lite ka lang muna. It's the lifestyle of living on a budget, where everything is measured, from your coffee to your patience.
usage_notes: Nagpapahiwatig ng pagtitipid o limitadong suplay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa krisis, **rasyun-rasyon** ang pagdating ng ayuda sa aming barangay.","translation":"Because of the crisis, the aid arrived in our barangay **in a rationed manner**."},{"sentence":"Naging **rasyun-rasyon** ang pagkain nila sa loob ng isang linggo.","translation":"Their food was **rationed** for a week."}]

translation: was charmed; was attracted; was enticed
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging nabighani o naakit sa isang tao, bagay, o ideya.
original_explanation: Na-budol ka, but in a romantic or magical way. It's when you see someone from across the room and suddenly the world goes into slow-motion with a cheesy background song. Or when the 12.12 sale starts and you're just 'charmed' into adding everything to your cart. You were drawn in, and you couldn't resist.
usage_notes: Ang unlaping 'na-' ay nagpapahiwatig ng isang natapos na, at madalas ay hindi kusang-loob, na kilos o kalagayan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nahalina** ang prinsipe sa kagandahan ni Cinderella.","translation":"The prince **was charmed** by Cinderella's beauty."},{"sentence":"Marami ang **nahalina** sa pangakong mabilis na pagyaman.","translation":"Many **were enticed** by the promise of getting rich quick."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdanas ng matindi at masidhing kalungkutan o pighati, karaniwang dahil sa isang malaking kawalan tulad ng pagkamatay ng isang mahal sa buhay.
original_explanation: This isn't just "sad." This is "main character in a dramatic teleserye crying in the rain after a major tragedy" level of sadness. It's grief, anguish, and deep sorrow all rolled into one. You don't use this for failing an exam; you use this for deep, life-altering loss.
usage_notes: Isang napakatindi, pormal, at pampanitikang salita para sa pagpapahayag ng dalamhati. Higit na masidhi kaysa sa 'nalulungkot'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang buong pamilya ay **namimighati** sa pagpanaw ng kanilang lolo.","translation":"The whole family is **grieving** over the passing of their grandfather."},{"sentence":"**Namimighati** ang kanyang puso dahil sa pagkakanulo ng kaibigan.","translation":"His heart is **in anguish** because of his friend's betrayal."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kabayaran o sahod na tinatanggap ng isang manggagawa para sa kaniyang serbisyo, karaniwan sa isang takdang panahon.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'sueldo' na nangangahulugang 'sahod'.
original_explanation: That thing you wait for every 15th and 30th, but disappears faster than your data plan. 'Magkano suwelo mo dyan?' is the slightly archaic but still understood way of asking about someone's salary. It's the 'tito' version of 'sweldo'.
usage_notes: Ang 'sweldo' ay mas karaniwang ginagamit sa modernong Filipino. Ang 'suwelo' para sa sahod ay maaaring ituring na medyo luma o pampanitikan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi sapat ang kanyang **suwelo** para sa gastusin ng buong pamilya.","translation":"His **salary** is not enough for the whole family's expenses."},{"sentence":"Humihingi ng mas mataas na **suwelo** ang mga manggagawa.","translation":"The workers are asking for a higher **salary**."}]

translation: to put something on top of
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay ng isang bagay sa ibabaw ng isa pang bagay.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "patong" (layer, something placed on top). Ang hulaping "-an" ay nagiging sanhi upang ang pandiwa ay maging pokus sa ganapan (locative focus).
original_explanation: Ito yung sinasabi ng nanay mo, "**Patungan** mo ng takip 'yang ulam baka langawin." Or when you're making a burger, you **patungan** the patty with cheese, lettuce, and tomatoes. Sa work, baka **patungan** ka pa ng additional tasks ng boss mo. It's all about adding layers.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang pandiwang nakapokus sa ganapan (locative-focused). Ang pinapatungan ang siyang tuon ng pandiwa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **patungan** ng mabibigat na libro ang salamin na mesa.","translation":"Don't **put** heavy books **on top of** the glass table."},{"sentence":"**Pinatungan** niya ng keso ang kanyang spaghetti.","translation":"She **put** cheese **on top of** her spaghetti."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng sabaw na may sahog na noodles, karne, at gulay.
etymology: Hiram na parirala mula sa Ingles.
original_explanation: The cure for the common cold, heartbreak, and rainy days. Whether it's a quick instant mami or a fancy ramen, a hot bowl of noodle soup is like a warm hug from your lola.
usage_notes: Madalas itong tumutukoy sa mga pagkaing tulad ng 'mami', 'lomi', o 'ramen'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap humigop ng mainit na **noodle soup** kapag malamig ang panahon.","translation":"It's nice to sip hot **noodle soup** when the weather is cold."},{"sentence":"Nag-order siya ng beef **noodle soup** sa paborito niyang restaurant.","translation":"He ordered beef **noodle soup** from his favorite restaurant."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lugar kung saan nilalaro ang beisbol; isang palaruan na may apat na base. Maaari ring tumukoy sa kaganapan o aktibidad ng paglalaro ng beisbol.
etymology: Mula sa salitang 'beisbol' + hulaping '-an', na nagpapahiwatig ng lugar o gawain.
original_explanation: This is the "court" for baseball. While we have "basketball court," we have **beisbolan** for baseball—the diamond-shaped field where you run like you're stealing second base from your crush's heart. It can also mean the game itself, like, "Tara, **beisbolan** tayo!" (Let's go play baseball!). It’s like the word ‘basketbolan’ for basketball.
usage_notes: Ang hulaping '-an' ay maaaring mangahulugang lugar (lugar ng beisbol) o isang kaganapan/gawain (paglalaro ng beisbol).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkita-kita tayo sa **beisbolan** mamayang hapon para mag-ensayo.","translation":"Let's meet at the **baseball field** this afternoon to practice."}]

translation: for, so that, in order to
meaning_filipino: Ginagamit upang ipahiwatig ang layunin, benepisyaryo, o direksyon ng isang kilos o bagay.
original_explanation: "Para" is the Swiss Army knife of Pinoy prepositions. It means "for" (Para sa'yo - For you), "so that" (Mag-aral ka para pumasa - Study so that you'll pass), and it's also the magic word you yell in a jeepney to stop. It's the reason for your 'why', the recipient of your 'what'. "Para kanino ka bumabangon?" is the ultimate Filipino existential question.
usage_notes: Ginagamit kasama ng 'sa' para sa mga bagay o lugar (para sa), 'kay' para sa isang tao (para kay), at 'kina' para sa maraming tao (para kina).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga bulaklak na ito ay **para** kay Maria.","translation":"These flowers are **for** Maria."},{"sentence":"Nag-iipon ako **para** sa kinabukasan ko.","translation":"I am saving **for** my future."},{"sentence":"Uminom ka ng gamot **para** gumaling ka.","translation":"Take your medicine **so that** you'll get better."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa ng isang pormal at masusing pagsisiyasat upang matuklasan at masuri ang mga katotohanan ng isang insidente, paratang, o krimen.
original_explanation: When you hear this word, you know someone's in trouble. It's what the police do after a crime, what your boss does when money goes missing, or what your mom does when the ulam for dinner mysteriously disappears. It's the formal version of "usisa-in" or "alamin kung sino ang may sala." It's the official start of the chismis becoming a full-blown case. "Kailangan nating **imbestigahan** kung sino ang kumain ng huling piraso ng leche flan!"
usage_notes: The suffix '-han' indicates the object or person to be investigated.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan ng hepe ang kanyang mga tauhan na **imbestigahan** ang nangyaring pagnanakaw.","translation":"The chief ordered his men to **investigate** the robbery that occurred."},{"sentence":"Dapat **imbestigahan** ang mga alegasyon ng korapsyon laban sa kanya.","translation":"The allegations of corruption against him must be **investigated**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na namamahala, nangangasiwa, o may katungkulan sa isang organisasyon, negosyo, o grupo.
etymology: From English 'manager,' adapted into Tagalog spelling.
original_explanation: Your boss. The one who approves your vacation leave, asks 'updates?' on Viber at 10 PM, and organizes the team building that nobody asked for. Can be a source of inspiration or the reason you update your JobStreet profile. From the BPO floor supervisor to the fast-food branch head, they are the 'manedyer.'
usage_notes: 'Manager' (English spelling) is also very commonly used in written and spoken Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinausap ko ang **manedyer** para magreklamo tungkol sa serbisyo.","translation":"I spoke to the **manager** to complain about the service."},{"sentence":"Ang aming **manedyer** ay magaling mag-handle ng team.","translation":"Our **manager** is good at handling the team."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na proseso kung saan ang isang bansa ay naghahatid ng isang taong pinaghihinalaan o napatunayang nagkasala sa isa pang bansa para sa paglilitis o pagpaparusa.
original_explanation: This is a legal term you hear in the news when a high-profile criminal tries to hide in another country. It's the government's way of saying, 'You can run, but you can't hide.' It’s the official process of shipping a fugitive back to where they committed the crime. Think international legal drama.
usage_notes: Strictly a legal and political term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May kasunduan sa **estradisyon** sa pagitan ng Pilipinas at Estados Unidos.","translation":"There is an **extradition** treaty between the Philippines and the United States."},{"sentence":"Humarap sa proseso ng **estradisyon** ang pugante pabalik sa kanyang bansa.","translation":"The fugitive faced the **extradition** process back to his country."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pag-upo kung saan ang bigat ng katawan ay nakasalalay sa mga sakong, habang ang mga tuhod ay nakatukod.
original_explanation: The classic Filipino 'tambay' pose. You see it everywhere: outside the sari-sari store, at the basketball court sidelines, while waiting for the jeep. It's the low-power mode for your body, a sign you're just chilling and observing the world go by. It's the original Asian squat.
usage_notes: The verb form is `tumungkayad` (to squat) or the descriptive state `nakatingkayad` (is squatting).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakatingkayad** ang mga bata habang naglalaro ng teks sa kalsada.","translation":"The children were **squatting** while playing cards on the street."},{"sentence":"**Tumingkayad** siya para kausapin ang maliit na pusa.","translation":"He **squatted** to talk to the small cat."}]

meaning_filipino: Buto ng halaman na maaaring itanim; punla. Sa biyolohiya, tumutukoy din ito sa likidong naglalaman ng isperma na nagmumula sa lalaki para sa reproduksiyon.
original_explanation: The "start-up" capital of life. Whether you're a farmer planting for the next harvest or... well, you get the other meaning. It's all about potential and new beginnings. In agriculture, it's the promise of food. In biology, it's the reason you exist. No pressure.
usage_notes: Ang salita ay may dalawang pangunahing gamit: agrikultural (plant seed) at biyolohikal (semen/sperm). Ang konteksto ang magdidikta ng kahulugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghanap ang magsasaka ng pinakamagandang klase ng **semilya** ng palay.","translation":"The farmer looked for the best kind of rice **seed**."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang pagsusuri ng **semilya** sa mga klinika para sa pag-aaral ng fertility.","translation":"The analysis of **semen** in clinics is important for fertility studies."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na may labis na gana sa pagkain; matakaw.
original_explanation: We all have that one friend who turns into a different person at a buffet. That's 'masiba'. It's beyond 'gutom' (hungry); it's a state of being where you inhale food like a vacuum cleaner. It's seeing the lechon and planning your attack, strategy, and how to get a second plate without anyone noticing. It's the spirit animal of anyone who's ever said, 'unli-rice, please.'
usage_notes: Often used with a slightly negative or humorous connotation, similar to 'matakaw'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong **masiba**, magtira ka para sa iba.","translation":"Don't be so **gluttonous**, leave some for the others."},{"sentence":"Kilala ang alaga kong aso sa pagiging **masiba**; kaya niyang ubusin ang isang buong mangkok ng pagkain sa isang minuto.","translation":"My pet dog is known for being **voracious**; he can finish a whole bowl of food in one minute."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpunta sa mas mataas na lugar, tulad ng pag-akyat sa hagdan, bundok, o puno. Maaari rin itong tumukoy sa pagtaas ng posisyon, estado sa buhay, o halaga.
original_explanation: Literally, it's what you do to get a good signal in the province or to reach the top of Mt. Pulag for that sea-of-clouds selfie. Figuratively, it’s your promotion from junior developer to senior. It's also 'pag-akyat ng ligaw,' where a suitor visits his crush's house to formally court her and win over the family.
usage_notes: Can be literal (climbing a mountain), figurative (social climbing, promotion), or quantitative (increase in price).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinaghandaan ng mga mountaineer ang kanilang **pag-akyat** sa Bundok Apo.","translation":"The mountaineers prepared for their **ascent** of Mount Apo."},{"sentence":"Ang **pag-akyat** ng presyo ng bilihin ay isang malaking problema.","translation":"The **increase** in the price of goods is a big problem."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kaaya-ayang pagkakabaluktot o arko, lalo na sa mga pilikmata, kilay, o baywang.
original_explanation: This is that perfect, gentle curve that makes you go "wow." The curve of long eyelashes that don't need mascara, the arch of a well-shaped kilay (on fleek!), or the graceful sway of a dancer's hips. It's the "S" curve of beauty, a subtle flex that speaks volumes.
usage_notes: Most commonly used to describe eyelashes ('pilikmata'). When used as a noun, it refers to the curve itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming humahanga sa **lantik** ng kanyang mga pilikmata.","translation":"Many admire the **curve** of her eyelashes."},{"sentence":"Ang **lantik** ng kanyang baywang ay kapansin-pansin habang siya'y sumasayaw.","translation":"The **shapely arch** of her waist is noticeable while she dances."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggawa ng kopya o pagkuha ng isang bahagi mula sa isang orihinal na akda o dokumento.
original_explanation: The action of making a 'sipi'. This is what students do a minute before the deadline, what you do when the HR department asks for 3 copies of everything, and what your friend does to your homework. "Patingin, sisipiin ko lang 'yung number 5."
usage_notes: Object-focused verb. The actor-focused form is 'sumipi'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **sipiin** nang basta-basta ang gawa ng iba.","translation":"Do not just **copy** the work of others."},{"sentence":"Maaari mo bang **sipiin** ang pangalawang talata para sa akin?","translation":"Can you **copy** the second paragraph for me?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pakiramdam ng kawalan ng interes, pagkainip, o pagkasawa dahil sa paulit-ulit o walang saysay na gawain.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're stuck in traffic, in a boring meeting that could've been an email, or when the WiFi is down. It's the official state of being of someone endlessly scrolling through their phone, looking for something—anything—to cure the "umay" of the moment.
usage_notes: Describes a state of mental weariness from lack of stimulation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para maiwasan ang **pagkabagot**, naghanap siya ng bagong libangan.","translation":"To avoid **boredom**, she looked for a new hobby."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkabagot** sa trabaho ay maaaring magdulot ng mababang produktibidad.","translation":"**Tedium** at work can lead to low productivity."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pariralang Ingles na tumutukoy sa isang batang legal na inampon. Ito ay madalas na ginagamit sa mga usapang Taglish.
original_explanation: This is literally just the English term dropped into a Tagalog sentence, usually because it's easier to say or sounds more... teleserye? The proper Filipino word is 'ampon,' but saying "adopted child" is common in casual, code-switching conversations. It's the direct, no-frills way to state the fact.
usage_notes: This is an English phrase used in code-switching (Taglish). The native Filipino equivalent is "ampon" or "anak na ampon". Its usage indicates a casual, often urban, conversational context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Alam mo ba na **adopted child** pala si Sarah sa kwento?","translation":"Did you know that Sarah is actually an **adopted child** in the story?"},{"sentence":"Ipinagmamalaki niya na isa siyang **adopted child** at mahal na mahal niya ang kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"She is proud to be an **adopted child** and she loves her parents very much."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbuka o pagbukaka ng mga hita o binti.
original_explanation: The action version of the adjective. When you're trying to find a comfortable position on a hot night and you just bumikangkang on the bed. Or when a gymnast does a split. It's the verb for achieving that maximum-space-occupying pose.
usage_notes: The root word itself can function as a verb in imperative or descriptive contexts, but is more commonly conjugated as "bumikangkang" (past/infinitive), "bumibikangkang" (present), "bibikangkang" (future).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumikangkang** siya sa kama dahil sa sobrang pagod.","translation":"He **spread his legs apart** on the bed due to extreme exhaustion."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **bumikangkang** nang ganyan sa upuan, maluwag pa naman.","translation":"Don't **spread your legs** like that on the seat, there's still a lot of space."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na ibinibigay o ginagawa upang mapakalma o mabawasan ang galit, lungkot, o pagkadismaya ng isang tao.
original_explanation: This is the peace offering. The milk tea you give your angry partner? That's the **palubag-loob**. The bonus you get after a stressful project? That's a **palubag-loob** from the company. It's the 'sorry gift,' the consolation prize, the thing that makes a bad situation a little bit better. It's the noun form of the verb 'palubagin ang loob'.
usage_notes: Often used with 'bilang' (as a). Example: 'Bilang palubag-loob...' (As a consolation...).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagbigay siya ng tsokolate bilang **palubag-loob** sa umiiyak na bata.","translation":"She gave chocolate as a **consolation** to the crying child."},{"sentence":"Ang kaniyang paghingi ng tawad ay hindi sapat na **palubag-loob** para sa akin.","translation":"His apology was not a sufficient **consolation** for me."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pagtitiwala na ipinagkakaloob ng isang nagpapautang sa isang umuutang, na nagpapahintulot sa huli na makakuha ng produkto o serbisyo kapalit ng pangakong magbabayad sa hinaharap. Maaari din itong tumukoy sa pagkilala sa isang nagawa.
original_explanation: Yung magic na nagpapahintulot sa'yong bilhin yung bagong phone kahit wala ka pang sahod, basta may credit card ka. Pwede ring 'yung pasasalamat sa dulo ng movie o project, 'Uy, bigyan mo naman ako ng **kredit** diyan, ako nag-edit niyan!'
usage_notes: Can refer to financial credit or giving credit/recognition to someone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mababa ang **kredit** score niya kaya nahirapan siyang kumuha ng pautang.","translation":"His **credit** score is low, that's why he had a hard time getting a loan."},{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang ilagay ang mga **kredit** sa lahat ng tumulong sa proyektong ito.","translation":"Don't forget to put the **credits** for everyone who helped in this project."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagbibigay ng dahilan upang maghinala o magduda; may mga palatandaan ng pagiging hindi tapat, hindi totoo, o may masamang hangarin.
original_explanation: That feeling you get when someone messages you "Hi/Hello" out of the blue. Or when a job offer sounds too good to be true ("Earn 100k a week, no experience needed!"). It's your inner Maritess alarm ringing, telling you something's fishy.
usage_notes: The `ka-` prefix and reduplication intensify the meaning, making it mean "very suspicion-inducing".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga kilos ng lalaki ay **kahina-hinala** kaya tinawag nila ang pulis.","translation":"The man's actions were **suspicious**, so they called the police."},{"sentence":"Nakatanggap siya ng isang **kahina-hinalang** email na humihingi ng kanyang personal na impormasyon.","translation":"She received a **suspicious** email asking for her personal information."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagbuti ng kalagayan mula sa sakit, pinsala, o anumang masamang karanasan.
original_explanation: The feeling when you can finally taste food again after having a cold. It's the 'New Me' phase after a heartbreak or the 'Salamat, doc!' moment after an illness. Basically, the glow-up after a major downer.
usage_notes: Often used in the phrase 'mabilis na paggaling' (speedy recovery). Do not confuse with 'galing' (excellence) or 'galing' (from).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagdarasal ko ang iyong mabilis na **paggaling**.","translation":"I am praying for your speedy **recovery**."},{"sentence":"Ang tamang pahinga ay susi sa mabilis na **paggaling**.","translation":"Proper rest is key to a fast **recovery**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pang-abay na nagpapahiwatig ng pagpapatuloy ng isang kilos o kalagayan, o pagdaragdag sa isang umiiral na dami o antas.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "wait, there's more!" particle in Tagalog. It's the reason why your mom says "isa pa" (one more) and suddenly you've eaten five more spoonfuls of rice. It's the "still" in "Mahal pa kita" (I still love you) that either gives you hope or makes you want to change your number. It's the 'more' in your 'more assignments, please' nightmares.
usage_notes: 'Pa' is a versatile particle placed before verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs to indicate continuation, addition, or a state that has not yet concluded.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulog **pa** si Maria.","translation":"Maria is **still** asleep."},{"sentence":"Gusto ko **pa** ng kanin.","translation":"I want **more** rice."},{"sentence":"Hindi **pa** ako tapos.","translation":"I'm not done **yet**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang balangkas na gawa sa kawayan o kahoy na ikinakabit sa magkabilang gilid ng isang bangka upang magbigay ng katatagan at maiwasan ang pagtaob nito.
original_explanation: The "floats" on the side of a bangka (a small boat). They're like the training wheels for the boat, keeping it from flipping over when the waves get choppy or when your one tito who can't swim starts panicking. It's the reason you can ride a tiny boat across the sea to get to that hidden beach.
usage_notes: A fundamental part of traditional Filipino bancas (boats).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matibay ang pagkakagawa sa **katig** ng kanilang bangka.","translation":"The **outrigger** of their boat is sturdily made."},{"sentence":"Sumabit ang lambat sa **katig**.","translation":"The net got caught on the **outrigger**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkaramdam ng pagod o sakit sa mga mata, karaniwang sanhi ng matagal na paggamit nito sa pagbabasa, paggamit ng kompyuter, o pagtutok sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: That feeling when you've been doomscrolling on TikTok for 5 hours straight, or when your Team Lead asks you to render OT for the 3rd time this week. Your eyes are screaming "tama na, besh!" It's the official mascot of BPO agents, online students, and anyone binge-watching a K-drama until 4 AM.
usage_notes: Madalas na ipinagpapalit sa "sakit sa mata" ngunit partikular na tumutukoy sa pagkapagod sa halip na impeksyon o iba pang karamdaman.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iwasan ang **pagkapagod ng mata** sa pamamagitan ng pagpapahinga kada dalawampung minuto.","translation":"Avoid **eye strain** by taking a break every twenty minutes."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa walang tigil na trabaho sa laptop, nararanasan ko ang matinding **pagkapagod ng mata**.","translation":"Because of non-stop work on the laptop, I am experiencing severe **eye strain**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang istilo ng musika na nagtatampok ng ritmikong pagsasalita o pagbigkas ng mga salita na may tugma, karaniwang sinasabayan ng isang tiyak na kumpas o 'beat'.
original_explanation: It's poetry for the streets. It's Gloc-9's social commentary, Abra's wordplay, and the entire FlipTop battle scene. To rap is to talk fast with rhymes, either to tell a story, drop some truth bombs, or just to prove you're the best. It's the modern balagtasan.
usage_notes: Can refer to the genre or the act of performing it ('mag-rap').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang makinig sa Pinoy **rap**.","translation":"He likes listening to Pinoy **rap**."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang mag-**rap** sa harap ng klase.","translation":"He tried to **rap** in front of the class."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-alis o pagbura ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay datos o impormasyon mula sa isang elektronikong aparato.
original_explanation: The modern way of saying "kalimutan mo na siya." When you **delete** their number, their photos, and unfriend them on all social media, you're trying to erase them from your life. Also, what you do to your browser history after searching for embarrassing things.
usage_notes: Isang direktang hiram na salita mula sa Ingles na karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng teknolohiya. Ang katumbas nitong Tagalog ay "burahin".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**delete** ang mga hindi na kailangang file sa computer.","translation":"Please **delete** the unnecessary files on the computer."},{"sentence":"Nag-desisyon siyang i-**delete** na ang lahat ng mensahe mula sa kanyang ex.","translation":"She decided to **delete** all the messages from her ex."}]

meaning_filipino: Daglat para sa "mililitro," isang yunit ng sukat para sa likido na katumbas ng isang libong bahagi ng isang litro.
original_explanation: 'Yung sukat ng softdrinks mo na "sakto" lang, o 'yung onting-onting pabango na natira sa bote. Sa mga reseta ng gamot, ito 'yung nagdidikta kung gaano karaming syrup ang ipapainom sa'yo ni nanay.
usage_notes: Always capitalized. Used in scientific, medical, and culinary contexts. Often written as 'mL'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mo ng 100 **ML** na tubig para sa resipe.","translation":"You need 100 **mL** of water for the recipe."},{"sentence":"Ang bote ay naglalaman ng 500 **ML** ng juice.","translation":"The bottle contains 500 **mL** of juice."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na tumutulad o kumokopya sa gawa, kilos, o paraan ng ibang tao.
original_explanation: The human version of 'Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V'. This is your classmate who copies your homework, the local brand that releases a 'dupe' of a famous sneaker, or the content creator whose skits look suspiciously familiar. Pwedeng 'impersonator' sa comedy bar, o pwedeng 'plagiarist' sa thesis. The context is everything.
usage_notes: Can be neutral (like an impersonator) or negative (like a plagiarist).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya bilang isang mahusay na **manggagaya** ng mga sikat na mang-aawit.","translation":"He is known as a great **imitator** of famous singers."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **manggagaya**; maging orihinal ka.","translation":"Don't be a **copycat**; be original."}]

translation: peal of bells; ringing of bells
meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay at masayang pagpapatunog ng mga kampana, karaniwang ginagawa tuwing may pista o mahalagang okasyon sa simbahan.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate church bell concert. Hindi lang isang "ding-dong," kundi isang buong production number ng mga kampana. Naririnig mo ito kapag may fiesta, kasal, o Misa de Gallo, at sign 'yun na may malaking ganap. It's the church's way of saying, "It's party time!"
usage_notes: Primarily used in a religious or historical context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula ang prusisyon kasabay ng malakas na **repike** ng mga kampana.","translation":"The procession began with the loud **peal of bells**."},{"sentence":"Ang **repike** ay hudyat na magsisimula na ang misa para sa pista.","translation":"The **ringing of bells** is the signal that the mass for the fiesta is about to start."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katawagang balbal na tumutukoy sa isang tao o bagay na itinakwil o hindi na tinatangkilik ng publiko, kadalasan dahil sa isang kontrobersyal na pahayag o kilos.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Ingles na "canceled" at ang patok na suffix na "-edt" sa social media.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na parang na-block ka sa group chat ng buong Pilipinas. One wrong move, canceledt ka na. It's when the internet mob decides you're no longer 'it' and collectively unfollows, un-stans, and uno-reverses your career. Good luck applying for a new one.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa konteksto ng "cancel culture" sa social media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging trending topic ang vlogger matapos ang kanyang lumang tweet, at ngayon ay **canceledt** na siya ng marami.","translation":"The vlogger became a trending topic after his old tweet resurfaced, and now he's **canceled** by many."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang imahen, rebulto, o anumang bagay na sinasamba bilang isang diyos.
original_explanation: Ito yung original, old-school na 'idol'. Hindi 'yung K-pop star, kundi 'yung golden calf sa Bible. Ito 'yung mga rebulto na sinasamba noong unang panahon, madalas gawa sa ginto o bato. Think Indiana Jones and the ancient artifacts.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa isang pisikal na bagay na sinasamba. Iba ito sa modernong 'idol' na tumutukoy sa isang hinahangaang tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagbabawal sa kanilang relihiyon ang paglikha at pagsamba sa mga **idolo**.","translation":"The creation and worship of **idols** (graven images) are forbidden in their religion."},{"sentence":"Nakahanap ang mga arkeologo ng isang sinaunang **idolo** sa kweba.","translation":"The archaeologists found an ancient **idol** in the cave."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pag-aari o pagkakakilanlan ng isang bagay o katangian sa grupo ng mga nagsasalita, hindi kasama ang kausap.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "this is ours, not yours" vibe. It's what you say when you and your friends have an inside joke and someone else tries to join in. "Sorry, **sarili namin** 'tong trip, wala kang ambag dito." It's exclusive, like a private party you weren't invited to.
usage_notes: 'Namin' is the exclusive 'our', meaning the person being spoken to is not included. Use 'atin' for the inclusive 'our' (e.g., 'sarili natin').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ito ang **sarili namin**g bahay.","translation":"This is **our own** house."},{"sentence":"Kailangan naming lutasin ang **sarili namin**g problema.","translation":"We need to solve **our own** problems."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tunog na nalilikha ng pagtama-tama ng mga maliliit at matitigas na bagay, tulad ng barya, susi, o metal.
etymology: Onomatopoeic, imitating the sound of small metal objects hitting each other.
original_explanation: The sound of hope when you shake your piggy bank. The sound of anxiety when the bus conductor is shaking his coin-filled hand, reminding you to pay up. The sound of your freedom when you jiggle your house keys after a long day at the office. It's the official soundtrack of 'sweldo day' and 'bayad po'.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to the light, sharp sound of small metal or glass objects hitting each other.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **kalansing** ng mga barya sa kanyang bulsa.","translation":"I heard the **jingle** of coins in his pocket."},{"sentence":"Ang tanging maririnig sa gabi ay ang **kalansing** ng mga susi ng guwardiya.","translation":"The only thing you could hear at night was the **clinking** of the guard's keys."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paghiwa o pagbukas sa katawan ng isang hayop o tao, karaniwan para sa layuning medikal o siyentipiko.
original_explanation: Remember your high school biology class with the frog? That's it. That's `busbusin`. It's the act of cutting something open to see what's inside. Pwede ring gamitin metaphorically, like when you 'dissect' a chismis to get to the truth. "Busbusin natin 'yang issue na 'yan para malaman kung sino talaga ang may sala."
usage_notes: Primarily used in a medical or scientific context (autopsy, surgery, dissection). Can be used figuratively for detailed analysis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **busbusin** ang katawan upang malaman ang sanhi ng pagkamatay.","translation":"The body needs to be **cut open** (autopsied) to determine the cause of death."},{"sentence":"Sa klase sa biology, natutunan naming **busbusin** ang isang palaka.","translation":"In biology class, we learned to **dissect** a frog."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging malinaw, maliwanag, at madaling maunawaan.
original_explanation: This is what you're begging for from your professor during a confusing lecture, from your boss when they give vague instructions, and from your partner after a fight ('Gusto ko lang ng kalinawan! Ano ba talaga tayo?'). It's the opposite of 'malabo.' It’s that 'Aha!' moment when everything finally makes sense.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa kalinawan ng isip, paliwanag, tubig, o kahit larawan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Humingi siya ng **kalinawan** tungkol sa mga bagong patakaran sa opisina.","translation":"He asked for **clarity** regarding the new office policies."},{"sentence":"Nawa'y magkaroon ng **kalinawan** ang isip mo sa paggawa ng desisyon.","translation":"May your mind have **clarity** in making a decision."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manggagawang pansakahan, karaniwang mula sa ibang lugar, na kinukuha upang magtrabaho sa mga taniman, lalo na ng tubo, sa panahon ng anihan.
etymology: From Spanish "sacada", meaning "a taking out" or "exportation", referring to the transport of laborers.
original_explanation: Before there were BPO agents flying to Manila for work, there were 'sakadas'—seasonal farmhands, often from the Visayas, who traveled to work in the vast sugarcane haciendas of Negros. They are the unsung heroes of our sugar supply, enduring tough conditions for meager pay. A word loaded with social and historical meaning.
usage_notes: Strongly associated with the sugar industry in the Philippines, particularly in Negros Occidental.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marami sa mga **sakada** ay inaabuso ng kanilang mga kontratista.","translation":"Many of the **migrant farmworkers** are abused by their contractors."},{"sentence":"Ang dokumentaryo ay tungkol sa buhay ng mga **sakada** sa Hacienda Luisita.","translation":"The documentary is about the lives of the **seasonal laborers** in Hacienda Luisita."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa tao, bagay, o kaisipan na nagmula o may kaugnayan sa kontinente ng Asya.
original_explanation: The catch-all term for anyone from the largest continent on Earth. From K-pop stans in Manila to your friendly neighborhood tindero of Japanese surplus, we're all part of the same continental crew. Also, the reason your lola thinks all chinito-looking actors are the same.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun ('Isang Asyano') or an adjective ('kulturang Asyano'). The feminine form is 'Asyana'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagmamalaki niya ang kanyang pagiging **Asyano**.","translation":"He is proud of his **Asian** heritage."},{"sentence":"Maraming turista ang bumibisita sa mga bansang **Asyano**.","translation":"Many tourists visit **Asian** countries."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang opisyal na paunawa o utos na humihiling sa isang tao na humarap sa korte; maaari ring tumukoy sa pagbanggit o pagkilala sa isang sanggunian sa isang akdang akademiko.
original_explanation: Two main flavors. First, the scary one: 'yung traffic enforcer, "Lisensya mo, sir." Tapos bibigyan ka ng ticket. That's a citation. Second, the academic one: 'yung kailangan mong ilagay sa dulo ng thesis mo para patunayang hindi mo chinika-chika lang 'yung sinulat mo. "According to..." 'yan, sitasyon 'yan.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa kontekstong legal (summons, ticket) at akademiko (reference).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatanggap siya ng **sitasyon** mula sa korte dahil sa hindi pagbabayad ng utang.","translation":"He received a **summons** from the court for not paying his debt."},{"sentence":"Siguraduhing tama ang pormat ng iyong mga **sitasyon** sa bibliograpiya.","translation":"Make sure the format of your **citations** in the bibliography is correct."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang damdamin ng matinding pagkamangha o pagtataka dahil sa isang bagay na hindi pangkaraniwan o hindi inaasahan.
original_explanation: That 'pog-face' you make when you see the 'pasabog' finale of a fireworks display. It's your reaction when your friend who never studies suddenly tops the exam. It’s a mix of 'wow' and 'paano nangyari yun?!'.
usage_notes: A more formal and poetic term for surprise. 'Pagkamangha' is a more common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kitang-kita sa kanyang mukha ang **pagkagilalas** sa natuklasan.","translation":"The **astonishment** at the discovery was clearly visible on his face."},{"sentence":"Napuno ng **pagkagilalas** ang mga manonood sa galing ng salamangkero.","translation":"The audience was filled with **amazement** at the magician's skill."}]

translation: to deliver a speech, to give an oration
meaning_filipino: Magbigay ng isang pormal na pahayag o pananalita sa harap ng maraming tao.
original_explanation: That moment in 'Buwan ng Wika' when one student has to stand in front of everyone and speak in deep, dramatic Filipino. Also what your dad does at the dinner table when he starts with 'Noong panahon namin...' and you're stuck listening for 30 minutes. It's a monologue, but with an audience.
usage_notes: A formal act, usually performed on a stage or in front of an audience for a specific occasion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magtatalumpati** ang valedictorian sa araw ng kanilang pagtatapos.","translation":"The valedictorian will **deliver a speech** on their graduation day."},{"sentence":"Handa na ba ang senador na **magtalumpati** tungkol sa bagong batas?","translation":"Is the senator ready **to give an oration** about the new law?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malalim na pakiramdam ng pagkabalisa, pag-aalala, o paghihinagpis, lalo na tungkol sa mga personal na problema o sa kalagayan ng mundo.
original_explanation: That deep, dramatic feeling you had as a teenager when you felt nobody in the world understood you. It's the fuel for writing bad poetry, listening to sad indie music on repeat, and thinking 'wala na, finish na!' over minor inconveniences. It's high-level 'hugot' mixed with existential dread.
usage_notes: Used in Taglish to describe a specific type of moody, existential anxiety.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Daanin mo na lang sa tulog 'yang **angst** mo.","translation":"Just sleep off that **angst** of yours."},{"sentence":"Grabe ang **angst** ng mga tula niya noong high school.","translation":"The **angst** in his high school poems was intense."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangkalahatang pakiramdam, kapaligiran, o emosyonal na kalidad na nagmumula sa isang tao, lugar, o bagay.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na 'vibes', pinaikling anyo ng 'vibrations'.
original_explanation: The overall energy or feeling you get from a person, place, or situation. It’s the non-verbal communication that tells you everything. 'Good vibes lang tayo dito,' means let's keep it positive. 'Ang weird ng vibes sa office ngayon,' means something feels off at work. It's the aura, the mood, the 'pakiramdam' 2.0.
usage_notes: Laging ginagamit sa anyong plural. Napaka-impormal at laganap sa usapang Gen Z at Millennial.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko ang **vibes** ng coffee shop na ito, ang kalmado.","translation":"I like the **vibes** of this coffee shop, it's so calm."},{"sentence":"Iwasan mo 'yan, nega ang **vibes** ng taong 'yan.","translation":"Avoid him, that person has negative **vibes**."}]

translation: to have something reserved; to set aside for someone
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalaan o pagtatabi ng isang bagay para sa isang partikular na tao o layunin.
original_explanation: Like when you tell your suki at the palengke, 'Ate, magpataan ka ng isang kilong manok para sa akin ha, babalikan ko mamaya.' It's the verbal version of putting a 'Reserved' sign on something, whether it's the last piece of liempo or your heart (charot!).
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of buying, selling, or allocating resources.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puwede po bang **magpataan** ng isang mesa para sa dalawang tao mamayang gabi?","translation":"Can I **have a table reserved** for two people tonight?"},{"sentence":"Nagbilin si Inay na **magpataan** ako ng ulam para kay Kuya.","translation":"Mom instructed me to **set aside** a dish for my older brother."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng isang lipunan na may mataas na antas ng kultura, agham, industriya, at pamahalaan.
etymology: From `ka-` + `bihasa` + `-nan`, meaning 'state of being skilled or civilized.'
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'squad goals' of a society. It's when people level up from just surviving to actually building cool stuff like pyramids, writing epic poems, and creating a government that (ideally) works. Think of it as the difference between a group chat and a well-organized corporation with its own culture and bylaws.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kabihasnan** ng mga Ehipsiyo ay kilala sa kanilang mga piramide.","translation":"The **civilization** of the Egyptians is known for their pyramids."},{"sentence":"Mahalagang pag-aralan ang mga sinaunang **kabihasnan** upang maunawaan ang kasalukuyan.","translation":"It is important to study ancient **civilizations** to understand the present."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapakita ng paggalang, paghanga, at pagmamahal sa isang diyos o sa anumang itinuturing na sagrado.
etymology: From Malay 'sembah', meaning to worship or pay homage.
original_explanation: That thing you do every Sunday (or Saturday for some) when you put on your best clothes and listen to a sermon. Also, how you look at your crush when they're not looking. It's the ultimate act of devotion, whether for a deity or for that limited-edition sneaker drop.
usage_notes: Often used in a religious context, but can be used hyperbolically to mean intense admiration or devotion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagsamba** ay isang mahalagang bahagi ng kanilang relihiyon.","translation":"**Worship** is an important part of their religion."},{"sentence":"Linggo-linggo, dumadalo sila sa **pagsamba** sa kanilang simbahan.","translation":"Every Sunday, they attend the **worship** service at their church."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging baligtad, kung saan ang panloob na bahagi ay nasa labas.
original_explanation: Like when you're so tired from work, you take off your shirt and it ends up inside out. 'Yan, nakatalikwas 'yung damit mo. Or when someone's argument is so twisted, their logic is basically nakatalikwas.
usage_notes: Often used for clothing or objects that have been flipped inside out.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong isuot 'yan, **nakatalikwas** ang pagkakabit ng manggas.","translation":"Don't wear that, the sleeve is attached **inside out**."},{"sentence":"Nakita niya ang pitaka na **nakatalikwas** sa sahig.","translation":"He saw the wallet **inverted** on the floor."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking inordenahan sa ministeryo ng simbahan, lalo na sa Simbahang Katoliko, na may kapangyarihang magsagawa ng mga sagradong ritwal tulad ng pagmimisa at pagbibigay ng mga sakramento.
original_explanation: The guy in the white robe at church. You call him 'Father'. He's the OG 'pare' since the word 'pare' (friend) is short for 'kumpare', a spiritual co-fatherhood role officiated by a priest during baptism. Full circle!
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pari** ang namuno sa misa kaninang umaga.","translation":"The **priest** led the mass this morning."},{"sentence":"Nagpakumpisal ako sa **pari** noong isang linggo.","translation":"I went to confession with the **priest** last week."}]

translation: to mark; to leave a mark
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng tanda o bakas sa isang bagay; ang pag-iwan ng isang di-malilimutang impresyon.
original_explanation: This is what your ex did to your heart. Charot! But seriously, magmarka can be literal, like a teacher using a red pen, or figurative, like an experience that leaves a lasting impression. It's about making an impact, for better or for worse. "Nagmarka sa isip ko ang sinabi niya."
usage_notes: Can be both literal (to put a physical mark) and figurative (to leave an impression).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **magmarka** ng titser sa daan-daang test paper.","translation":"The teacher needs **to mark** hundreds of test papers."},{"sentence":"Ang kabaitan niya ay tunay na **nagmarka** sa aking puso.","translation":"His/Her kindness truly **left a mark** on my heart."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglilipat ng dugo mula sa isang tao patungo sa isa pa bilang isang medikal na pamamaraan.
