meaning_filipino: Ganap; lubusan; sa huli at walang pagbabago.
etymology: From 'tuloy' (continue, proceed) + '-an', signifying an action proceeding to its final state.
original_explanation: When something goes from "pwede pa" to "wala na, finish na." It's the point of no return. You tried to save your dying plant, but it **tuluyan** nang nalanta. You tried to fix a relationship, but it **tuluyan** nang nasira. It's the adverb of finality and hugot.
usage_notes: Often used with 'na' (e.g. 'tuluyan na') to emphasize finality. It implies an irreversible state or outcome.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng matagal na pagtitiis, **tuluyan** na siyang umalis.","translation":"After a long period of suffering, she **finally** left."},{"sentence":"Sana hindi **tuluyang** masira ang ating pagkakaibigan.","translation":"I hope our friendship doesn't get **completely** ruined."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay at malawakang pag-atake o paglusob sa isang lugar, kuta, o pangkat ng mga tao.
original_explanation: This is raid mode. Think of cops raiding a hideout in an action movie, or your squad deciding to 'salakayan' the enemy base in Mobile Legends. On a lighter note, it's what you and your barkada do to the buffet table at a party.
usage_notes: The '-an' suffix here indicates the target/location of the attack. It implies a group action against a place or a group.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binalak ng mga pirata na **salakayan** ang baryo sa tabing-dagat.","translation":"The pirates planned to **raid** the seaside village."},{"sentence":"Nagkasundo ang magkakaibigan na **salakayan** ang pinakabagong samgyupsal restaurant.","translation":"The friends agreed to **raid** the newest samgyupsal restaurant."}]

translation: To pass by; to drop by; to go through
meaning_filipino: Ang paggalaw sa isang lugar upang makarating sa iba; pagbisita nang mabilisan; paglagpas.
original_explanation: The act of making a quick stop. "Daan ka muna sa bahay," your mom says, which is code for "Come over and I'll give you food to take home." It's also what you do to your crush's desk, hoping they'll notice you.
usage_notes: This is the root word for the verb. Common conjugations include: dumadaan (passing by), dumaan (passed by), dadaan (will pass by).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dumaan** ka ba sa palengke kanina?","translation":"**Did you pass by** the market earlier?"},{"sentence":"**Dadaan** ako sa opisina mo mamaya para kunin ang mga dokumento.","translation":"I'll **drop by** your office later to get the documents."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paraan o proseso ng paglutas sa isang problema o mahirap na sitwasyon; ang sagot sa isang tanong o suliranin.
original_explanation: Yung hinahanap mo sa math problems at sa mga problema niyo ng jowa mo. Minsan, ang solusyon ay "sorry na," pero madalas, kailangan mo talagang pag-isipan. Parang sa work, hindi pwedeng "bahala na si Batman," kailangan may concrete action plan.
usage_notes: Madalas na ipinagpapalit sa "lunas" (para sa mga problema o sakit) o "sagot" (para sa mga tanong).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **solusiyon** sa matinding trapiko sa EDSA?","translation":"What is the **solution** to the heavy traffic on EDSA?"},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating maghanap ng agarang **solusiyon** sa problemang ito.","translation":"We need to find an immediate **solution** to this problem."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bangkay ng tao o hayop na pinreserba ang balat at laman sa pamamagitan ng sinasadya o di-sinasadyang paglantad sa kemikal, matinding lamig, napakababang halumigmig, o kawalan ng hangin.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung mga nakabalot sa toilet paper sa mga horror movies, pero 'yung totoong version galing sa Egypt. In short, 'yung patay na hindi na-decompose at naging historical artifact. Minsan, ito rin 'yung itsura mo after ng isang linggong OT sa work, parang tuyot na tuyot.
usage_notes: Ang "momya" ay isang alternatibong baybay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May nakitang **momiya** sa isang sinaunang libingan sa Ehipto.","translation":"They found a **mummy** in an ancient tomb in Egypt."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang masusing pagsusuri, pagkukumpuni, o pagbabago sa isang makina, sistema, o organisasyon upang mapabuti ang kalagayan nito.
original_explanation: That thing your car needs when it's making sounds you've never heard before. It's not just a tune-up; it's a full-on, take-it-apart-and-put-it-back-together-again kind of fix. In BPO terms, it's what happens to a process that's failing its metrics—time for a complete oberhol. Can also be used as a verb: 'I-oberhol mo na 'yang luma mong laptop.'
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pangngalan ('Kailangan ng oberhol') o bilang salitang-ugat ng pandiwa ('i-oberhol', 'ino-oberhol').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng malawakang **oberhol** sa sistema ng transportasyon sa siyudad.","translation":"The city's transportation system needs a massive **overhaul**."},{"sentence":"Ipinasok niya sa talyer ang kotse para sa **oberhol** ng makina.","translation":"He brought the car to the workshop for an engine **overhaul**."}]

meaning_filipino: Magbigay ng tulong o donasyon, karaniwan ay pera o materyal na bagay, para sa isang layunin, tao, o institusyon.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "i-" at salitang-ugat na "abuloy" (tulong na ibinibigay sa namatayan o nangangailangan).
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa mo 'pag may nakitang lata ng "Piso para sa Puso" sa cashier, o 'pag nag-G-Cash ka sa donation drive para sa mga nasalanta ng bagyo. It's giving what you can, kahit pa barya lang 'yan, for a cause.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng pagbibigay sa simbahan, charity, o sa mga nangangailangan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais niyang **iabuloy** ang kalahati ng kanyang sahod sa bahay-ampunan.","translation":"He wants to **donate** half of his salary to the orphanage."},{"sentence":"Maaari ninyong **iabuloy** ang inyong mga lumang damit na maayos pa.","translation":"You can **donate** your old clothes that are still in good condition."}]

translation: to banter with each other; to tease one another playfully
meaning_filipino: Magbiruan o magkantiyawan nang may halong pagbibiro at pagpapatawa sa isa't isa, karaniwan sa isang pangkat.
original_explanation: ‘Yung asaran ng barkada na walang pikunan. Parang sa office, ‘pag may bagong haircut ‘yung isa, ‘yun na ang topic of the day hanggang meryenda. It's the group chat roast session but in real life.
usage_notes: Often done in a group setting, this implies a light-hearted, reciprocal teasing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig **magbatyawan** ang magkakaibigan tungkol sa kanilang mga lovelife.","translation":"The friends love to **banter with each other** about their lovelives."},{"sentence":"Nag-umpisa na silang **magbatyawan** nang dumating ang kanilang huling kasama.","translation":"They started to **tease one another playfully** when their last companion arrived."}]

translation: to be able to calculate; to be able to reckon
meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang makalkula, mabilang, o masuma ang isang halaga o kabuuan.
original_explanation: This is your brain's ability to process numbers, usually when splitting the bill with friends. "Wait lang, 'di ko **matuos** kung magkano ambag ng bawat isa." It's also used for figuring out something complex, like your feelings or the total damage of your Shopee cart. It's the mental math you do before realizing you should've just used a calculator.
usage_notes: Often used in the negative form "hindi matuos" to mean incalculable or immeasurable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko **matuos** kung gaano kalaki ang utang na loob ko sa iyo.","translation":"I cannot **calculate** how much I owe you in gratitude."},{"sentence":"Subukan mong **matuos** ang lahat ng nagastos natin sa biyahe.","translation":"Try to **calculate** everything we spent on the trip."}]

translation: a well; water source for fetching
meaning_filipino: Isang balon o poso kung saan kumukuha o sumasalok ng tubig.
original_explanation: Before Nawasa and Maynilad, there was the igiban. This is the OG water station of the barrio, the local well or pump where everyone got their daily supply. It was also the prime spot for neighborhood chismis. 'Saan mo nakuha 'yang balita?' 'Diyan lang sa igiban.' Today, your water cooler at the office is the modern igiban.
usage_notes: Refers to the place of fetching water, not the act itself (which is 'pag-igib').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumila ang mga tao sa **igiban** dahil sa kawalan ng tubig sa gripo.","translation":"The people lined up at the **well** because of the lack of water from the faucet."},{"sentence":"Malinis ang tubig mula sa aming **igiban** sa probinsya.","translation":"The water from our **water source** in the province is clean."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi malinaw, tiyak, o maliwanag; tila may pagka-ulap o pagkalabo sa anyo o kahulugan.
etymology: From 'laboy,' which can mean to wander or to be turbid/muddy. The prefix 'ma-' turns it into an adjective describing this state.
original_explanation: Yung sagot ng ex mo nung tinanong mo kung 'what are we?'. 'Di malinaw, 'di sigurado. Parang picture na kuha sa low-end na Android phone nung 2010—pixelated at blurry. Ganyan ang **malaboy**. It's that feeling of uncertainty, when things are as clear as mud.
usage_notes: Often used to describe ideas, explanations, or visual things that lack clarity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Malaboy** ang kanyang paliwanag kaya walang naniwala sa kanya.","translation":"His explanation was **vague**, so no one believed him."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kapal ng hamog, **malaboy** ang tanawin sa daan.","translation":"Because of the thick fog, the view on the road was **blurry**."}]

meaning_filipino: Utusan o hilingin sa isang tao na ahitin ang balbas, buhok, o balahibo ng iba.
original_explanation: This is the verb for when you're not doing the shaving yourself. For example, "Ipapahaircut ko na, tapos **paahitan** ko na rin 'yung balbas" (I'll get a haircut, and have my beard shaved too). It's what you do when you take your pet poodle to the groomer. You're not shaving the poodle, the groomer is. You just 'paahitan' it.
usage_notes: The focus is on the person being shaved. `Paahitan mo si Juan` (Have Juan be shaved). Contrast with `Magpaahit ka` (You go and get a shave).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Paahitan** mo na ang iyong balbas para magmukha kang malinis.","translation":"**Have your beard shaved** so you'll look clean."},{"sentence":"Dinala niya ang aso sa beterinaryo para **paahitan**.","translation":"He brought the dog to the vet to **be shaved**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng mamamayan o nagmula sa bansang Kanada.
etymology: From 'Kanada' (Canada) + '-ana' suffix, a Hispanized feminized demonym.
original_explanation: A woman from the land of maple syrup, poutine, and saying 'sorry' a lot. The female counterpart to a 'Kanadyano'. Just like you have 'Amerikano' and 'Amerikana'.
usage_notes: The male form is 'Kanadyano'. The neutral/plural form is 'mga taga-Kanada' or 'mga Kanadyano'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bagong guro namin sa Ingles ay isang **Kanadyana**.","translation":"Our new English teacher is a **Canadian (female)**."},{"sentence":"Maraming Pilipino ang naninirahan sa Canada, kaya may mga anak silang **Kanadyana** na.","translation":"Many Filipinos live in Canada, so they have children who are now **Canadian (female)**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paraan ng pagkakasalikop ng mga sinulid upang makabuo ng tela; ang resulta o produkto ng paghahabi.
original_explanation: This is the OG Filipino art form before vlogging was a thing. It's the intricate pattern you see on a banig, a piña barong, or those beautiful Inabel blankets from Ilocos. It’s about connecting threads to make something beautiful and strong. Parang relationship lang, 'di ba? The habi must be tight, or else it all falls apart.
usage_notes: Maaari ring tumukoy sa mismong kilos ng paghahabi (verb form: humabi, maghabi).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pino ng **habi** ng telang ito.","translation":"The **weave** of this fabric is so fine."},{"sentence":"Ang paghahabi ay isang mahalagang bahagi ng kanilang kultura, at makikita ito sa magandang **habi** ng kanilang mga kasuotan.","translation":"Weaving is an important part of their culture, and it can be seen in the beautiful **texture** of their garments."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong mamamayan o katutubo ng bansang Sweden (Suwesya).
original_explanation: The people who gave us IKEA, ABBA, and Spotify. 'Pag sinabing Suweko, 'yun 'yung mga taong kailangan mo ng manual para i-assemble ang friendship niyo, pero 'pag nabuo na, matibay at minimalist ang design.
usage_notes: Palaging isinusulat na may malaking titik sa unahan (capitalized) kapag tumutukoy sa tao o lahi.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **Suweko** ang mahilig magbakasyon sa mga tropikal na bansa.","translation":"Many **Swedes** love to vacation in tropical countries."}]

translation: to exceed; to surpass; to be better than
meaning_filipino: Ang lumampas o mangibabaw sa bilang, sukat, kalidad, o katayuan ng iba.
original_explanation: This is the goal of every overachieving pamangkin (nephew/niece) during family reunions. It's when your unli-rice serving beats your friend's, or when your meme gets more shares. It's the constant desire to one-up someone, whether it's in grades, salary, or the number of Jollibee chickenjoys you can eat. Level up!
usage_notes: Can be used in both literal (quantity) and figurative (quality, status) senses.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Walang **makahihigit** sa pagmamahal ng isang ina.","translation":"Nothing can **surpass** a mother's love."},{"sentence":"Sinikap niyang **makahigit** sa mga nagawa ng kanyang mga kapatid.","translation":"He tried **to be better than** what his siblings had achieved."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit na paggawa ng isang bagay upang mapabuti ang kasanayan, kaalaman, o kakayahan.
original_explanation: What you do before a job interview, a client presentation, or your K-pop dance cover. It's the 'practice makes perfect' mantra in action. From call center agents practicing their spiels to athletes training for a game, `magsanay` is the hustle before the win.
usage_notes: Can be used for physical training, practicing a skill (like playing an instrument), or rehearsing a performance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magsanay** araw-araw kung gusto mong gumaling sa pagtugtog ng gitara.","translation":"You need to **practice** every day if you want to get better at playing the guitar."},{"sentence":"Siya ay nagpunta sa gym upang **magsanay** para sa marathon.","translation":"He went to the gym to **train** for the marathon."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng isang tao na madalas magpakita ng pagkadismaya o pagtutol sa pamamagitan ng pag-ungot, pagbulong, o pagdadabog.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `mapag-` (nagpapahiwatig ng pagkahilig) at salitang-ugat na `maktol` (pag-ungot o pagrereklamo).
original_explanation: Eto yung kaibigan mong laging may reklamo. Inaya mo sa Jollibee, ayaw kasi mas gusto sa McDo. Dinala mo sa McDo, aangal kasi mas mura daw sa Jollibee. Parang laging may PMS (Palaging May Sinasabi) at laging naka-pout. The official "KJ" (killjoy) of the barkada.
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang ilarawan ang ugali o pagkahilig ng isang tao sa halip na isang pansamantalang damdamin. Ipinahihiwatig nito ang nakagawiang katangian ng pagrereklamo o pagpapakita ng hindi kasiyahan sa paraang may kasamang pagtatampo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mapagmaktol** kung hindi mo nakuha ang gusto mo; matuto kang magpasalamat.","translation":"Don't be **petulant** if you didn't get what you want; learn to be grateful."},{"sentence":"Kilala si Aling Nena sa pagiging **mapagmaktol** tuwing may pag-uusap sa barangay.","translation":"Aling Nena is known for being **grumbling** during barangay meetings."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagiging mas malubha, mas masama, o mas matindi ng isang kalagayan, karamdaman, o suliranin.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung moment na akala mo okay na, pero 'di pa pala. From 'it's complicated' to 'blocked ka na sa lahat ng social media.' Yung simpleng ubo na naging pneumonia, o yung maliit na away na nauwi sa hiwalayan. The situation is escalating, and not in a good way.
usage_notes: Often used in medical contexts (paglala ng sakit) or for problems (paglala ng krisis).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang hindi pag-inom ng gamot ay nagdulot ng **paglala** ng kaniyang sakit.","translation":"Not taking the medicine caused the **worsening** of his illness."},{"sentence":"Pinipigilan ng gobyerno ang **paglala** ng krisis sa ekonomiya.","translation":"The government is preventing the **aggravation** of the economic crisis."}]

translation: to strike with a rope; to whip
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpalo o paghampas sa isang tao, hayop, o bagay gamit ang isang lubid.
original_explanation: This is what your lola threatens to do when you're being extra pasaway. It’s the verb form of 'you're gonna get it!' using a rope or something similar, like a belt. The action is so intense, it's rarely used today except in historical dramas or very, very angry parental threats.
usage_notes: An object-focus verb. The root is 'lubid' (rope).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa lumang pelikula, madalas **lubigan** ng mga kontrabida ang kanilang mga bihag.","translation":"In old movies, villains often **whip** their captives."},{"sentence":"Binalaan siya na **lulubigan** siya kapag hindi siya umayos.","translation":"He was warned that he would be **struck with a rope** if he didn't behave."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinuno ng gobyerno sa isang sistemang parlyamentaryo, na karaniwang lider din ng partidong may mayorya sa lehislatura.
etymology: Loan translation from English "prime minister," using `kataas-taasan` (highest) and `ministro` (minister).
original_explanation: The "President" of countries that have a king or queen, but the royal is mostly for show (like the UK or Japan). They're the head honcho of the government, the main character in the political drama, while the monarch is the executive producer. The Philippines doesn't have one, so we just call our leader "Pangulo."
usage_notes: This is a direct translation and less common than the English loanword "Prime Minister" or the Tagalog "Punong Ministro."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kataas-taasang ministro** ng Japan ay bumisita sa Pilipinas.","translation":"The **prime minister** of Japan visited the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Nagtalumpati ang **kataas-taasang ministro** sa harap ng parlyamento.","translation":"The **prime minister** delivered a speech before the parliament."}]

translation: to meet someone at a designated place
meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang pagsalubong o pakikipagkita sa isang tao sa isang tiyak na lugar at oras.
original_explanation: The verb form of "tagpuan" (meeting place). It's what you tell your friend to do when you set a meeting spot. "Tagpuin mo ako sa may entrance ng SM, yung malapit sa Jollibee." It’s the active version of planning a meetup, often to avoid getting lost or ghosted.
usage_notes: Nangangahulugan ito ng isang napagkasunduang pagkikita. Iba ito sa `salubungin` na maaaring mas biglaan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tagpuin** mo ako sa istasyon ng tren mamayang alas-sais.","translation":"**Meet me** at the train station later at six o'clock."},{"sentence":"Sinabihan niya akong **tagpuin** siya sa paborito naming kapihan.","translation":"He told me to **meet him** at our favorite coffee shop."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manggagawa o alagad ng sining na dalubhasa sa paghubog at paggawa ng mga kagamitan o alahas mula sa pilak o plata.
original_explanation: The OG artisan who could turn a boring lump of silver into your grad ring or your mom's earrings. Before mass-produced jewelry, you went to the local platero to get something custom-made. Think of them as the jewelry ninjas of the pre-mall era.
usage_notes: A somewhat archaic term, as 'jeweler' or 'alahero' are more common now, but still understood, especially in historical or literary contexts like in Rizal's novels.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala niya sa **platero** ang sirang kuwintas ng kanyang lola.","translation":"She brought her grandmother's broken necklace to the **silversmith**."},{"sentence":"Kilala ang aming bayan sa mga mahuhusay na **platero**.","translation":"Our town is known for its skilled **silversmiths**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtatakda na ang isang bagay ay hindi pinahihintulutan o ipinagbabawal ng batas, alituntunin, o awtoridad.
original_explanation: "Bawal tumawid, may namatay na dito." "Bawal umihi dito." This is the Philippines' national pastime. Pagbabawal is the act behind all those signs. It's your parents telling you not to date yet, or your office memo about not using Facebook during work hours. It's the rule you're most tempted to break.
usage_notes: A very common concept in daily Filipino life, from public signs to household rules.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagbabawal** sa paninigarilyo sa mga pampublikong lugar ay isang magandang hakbang.","translation":"The **prohibition** of smoking in public places is a good step."},{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang **pagbabawal** ng mga magulang niya sa pag-uwi nang gabi.","translation":"Her parents' **act of forbidding** her from coming home late is strict."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na proseso ng pag-aaral o pag-uusisa sa isang bagay o pangyayari upang matukoy ang mga katotohanan.
original_explanation: This is what happens when your mom finds a receipt that isn't yours in your jeans. It's the NBI, the police, and your chismosa tita all rolled into one intense session of questioning. 'Saan ka galing? Sino kasama mo? Bakit may bawas na 500 ang G-Cash mo?'
usage_notes: Often used in formal contexts like police work, journalism, or academic research.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagsisiyasat** sa kaso ay nagpapatuloy pa rin.","translation":"The **investigation** into the case is still ongoing."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula na ang **pagsisiyasat** ng komite sa anomalya.","translation":"The committee has begun its **investigation** into the anomaly."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay na pagkolekta o pagsasama-sama ng maraming hiwa-hiwalay na tao o bagay sa isang lugar.
etymology: From `pag-` (verbal noun prefix) + `tipun-tipon` (reduplication of `tipon`, meaning 'gather') + `-in` (object focus suffix).
original_explanation: This is what you do with all your K-Pop photocards for a group photo. It's also your Tita's command during a family reunion: '**Pagtipun-tipunin** ang lahat ng pinsan para sa picture!' The repetition of 'tipon' implies gathering many small or scattered items/people.
usage_notes: The reduplication 'tipun-tipon' emphasizes that many disparate items or individuals are being gathered.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinabi ng guro na **pagtipun-tipunin** ang lahat ng aklat sa mesa.","translation":"The teacher said to **gather together** all the books on the table."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **pagtipun-tipunin** ang buong angkan para sa Pasko.","translation":"It's difficult to **gather together** the whole clan for Christmas."}]

meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng gatas ang isang sanggol, mula man sa suso ng ina o sa pamamagitan ng bote.
etymology: The root 'dede' is baby talk for breast or milk bottle.
original_explanation: A classic command for new parents, lolos, and lolas. "Umiiyak na yung bata, padedehin mo na!" It's the universal solution for a crying baby. It literally means 'to make [the baby] suckle from a breast/bottle'.
usage_notes: A very common, colloquial term used in households. The formal term would be 'pasusuhin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko nang **padedehin** ang sanggol dahil oras na ng kanyang gatas.","translation":"I need **to feed** the baby now because it's time for his milk."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking mamalyang karniboro o omniboro na kabilang sa pamilyang Ursidae, na may makapal na balahibo at malalaking kuko.
original_explanation: The original teddy bear. You know, the big, furry animal you see in cartoons and movies, but in real life, you should probably run from it. Not to be confused with your ex who you called 'oso' because he was cuddly but also kinda grumpy.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa mga konteksto tulad ng zoo, mga kuwentong pambata, o biyolohiya. Hindi ito isang katutubong hayop sa Pilipinas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakita kami ng malaking **oso** sa zoo.","translation":"We saw a big **bear** at the zoo."},{"sentence":"Paborito ng bata ang kanyang laruang **oso**.","translation":"The child's favorite toy is his teddy **bear**."}]

translation: to attach; to connect; to install
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay, pagkakabit, o pagdudugtong ng isang bagay sa isa pa. Ito ay isang salitang-ugat.
original_explanation: The action you do when the internet is down. "Pakitingnan kung may ilaw ‘yung modem, baka natanggal sa kabit." Also, what you do with Christmas lights, or how you assemble your Shopee/Lazada finds that came with a manual in a language you don't understand.
usage_notes: This is the root word for actions like "ikabit" (to attach something), "magkabit" (to attach/install), "nakakabit" (attached). The pronunciation is different from the noun form, with stress on the first syllable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sila ang mag-ka-**kabit** ng internet sa aming bahay.","translation":"They are the ones who will **install** the internet in our house."},{"sentence":"Sino ang nag-**kabit** ng aircon natin?","translation":"Who **installed** our aircon?"}]

translation: to award; to grant; to confer
meaning_filipino: Ibigay o ipagkaloob ang isang karangalan, gantimpala, o kapangyarihan sa isang tao, karaniwan sa isang pormal na seremonya.
original_explanation: This is the verb for graduation day, awards night, or when the pageant host finally announces the winner. 'At ang korona ay igagawad kay...'. It's not just 'giving,' it's 'bestowing.' It's got that formal, ceremonial vibe, like when your boss igawads you the 'Employee of the Month' certificate. It's giving with gravitas.
usage_notes: Used for formal bestowing of honors, prizes, or authority. More formal than 'ibigay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang medalya ng karangalan ay **igagawad** sa pinakamahusay na mag-aaral.","translation":"The medal of honor will be **awarded** to the best student."},{"sentence":"**Iginawad** sa kanya ang titulong Pambansang Alagad ng Sining.","translation":"The title of National Artist was **conferred** upon him."}]

translation: will be amused by; will find joy in
meaning_filipino: Ang pandiwa sa hinaharap na tumutukoy sa pagkakaroon ng saya, ligaya, o aliw mula sa isang tao, bagay, o pangyayari.
etymology: From ka- + tuwa + -an. Future tense, object-focused.
original_explanation: 'Yung reaction mo sa mga lumang Friendster photos mo. You cringe, but you also laugh. Iyon ang pagkatuwaan mo. It's the act of finding amusement in something, often something silly, nostalgic, or even slightly embarrassing.
usage_notes: The object of the verb is the source of amusement. `Kakatuwaan ng tao ang bagay.` (The person will be amused by the thing.)
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siguradong **kakatuwaan** ng mga bata ang bagong alagang tuta.","translation":"The children will surely **be amused by** the new pet puppy."},{"sentence":"Maraming tao ang **kakatuwaan** ang mga bloopers sa palabas.","translation":"Many people **will find joy in** the show's bloopers."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang tao na madalas o laging inaantok at mahilig matulog.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung friend mo na 5 minutes pa lang kayo sa sinehan, humihilik na. Or ikaw, after lunch break, na nagdadasal na lang na 'di ka mahalata ng boss mo. The human version of Snorlax.
usage_notes: A descriptive word for a person's characteristic. 'Antukin' is a very close synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Talaga namang **matulugin** ang bunso naming kapatid.","translation":"Our youngest sibling is truly a **sleepyhead**."},{"sentence":"Nagiging **matulugin** ako kapag malamig ang panahon.","translation":"I become **prone to sleeping** when the weather is cold."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubog sa tubig, lalo na dahil sa pag-apaw o baha.
original_explanation: The state of your street after 30 minutes of strong rain. It's when your house becomes a temporary island and you have to decide if it's 'baha' (flood) or just 'taog' (submerged). Basically, it means 'lubog sa tubig.'
usage_notes: Less common than 'baha' or 'lubog'. Often used to describe fields, roads, or low-lying areas after a heavy downpour or a high tide.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Taog** ang buong palayan matapos ang malakas na bagyo.","translation":"The entire rice field was **submerged** after the strong typhoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkaubos ng lakas o enerhiya ng pag-iisip, karaniwang dulot ng matagal na konsentrasyon, stress, o emosyonal na pasanin.
original_explanation: This is what you feel after a whole day of Zoom meetings that could have been emails. It's the brain fog after studying for finals, or the exhaustion from overthinking a simple text message. Your body might be fine, but your brain has clocked out and is ready for a nap.
usage_notes: A descriptive phrase that is widely understood. It is the direct equivalent of "mental fatigue."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkapagod ng isip** ay mas mahirap i-recover kaysa sa pisikal na pagod.","translation":"**Mental fatigue** is harder to recover from than physical tiredness."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang matinding **pagkapagod ng isip** pagkatapos ng board exam.","translation":"She felt intense **mental exhaustion** after the board exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng katatagan, kasipagan, at hindi pagsuko sa pag-abot ng isang layunin sa kabila ng mga hadlang.
original_explanation: This is the 'walang sukuan' attitude. The spirit of every student finishing their thesis, every BPO agent hitting their quota, and every person trying to get a visa. It’s the opposite of 'bahala na'. It's 'bahala na, basta gagawin ko lahat ng paraan'. Grind culture in one word.
usage_notes: A formal and admirable trait. Often used in motivational contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang pagiging **mapunyagi**, natapos niya ang kanyang pag-aaral.","translation":"Because of being **persevering**, he/she was able to finish his/her studies."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis na pagkalat ng isang nakahahawang sakit sa isang malaking bilang ng mga tao sa loob ng isang komunidad sa maikling panahon.
original_explanation: Ito yung mas lumang spelling, parang "Tito" version ng "epidemiko." Bago pa mag-pandemic, nagkaroon muna ng mga epidemik (e.g., dengue, cholera). Isipin mo na lang, ito yung level bago maging global issue. Parang chismis na kumalat sa buong barangay, pero hindi pa umabot sa kabilang bayan.
usage_notes: Isang baryasyon ng salitang "epidemiko." Mas karaniwan na ngayon ang paggamit ng "epidemiko" na hiram sa Espanyol.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagdeklara ng state of calamity dahil sa **epidemik** ng dengue.","translation":"A state of calamity was declared due to the dengue **epidemic**."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng mga doktor kung paano masusugpo ang **epidemik**.","translation":"Doctors are studying how to stop the **epidemic**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o patungan kung saan isinasagawa ang pagluluto gamit ang apoy, karaniwang gawa sa luwad o bato; kalan.
etymology: Pinaniniwalaang nagmula sa salitang 'dingal' na may kaugnayan sa apoy o init, ngunit iba sa 'dingal' na nangangahulugang maringal.
original_explanation: This is the OG kalan. Before gas stoves and induction cookers, there was the dingalan. It's the traditional clay stove where your lola would cook the most amazing adobo using charcoal or wood. It's the heart of the ancestral kitchen.
usage_notes: Isang lumang salita, na halos napalitan na ng 'kalan'. Maaaring marinig sa mga lalawigan o sa mga usapang pangkasaysayan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagluto si Lola ng sinigang sa lumang **dingalan**.","translation":"Grandma cooked sinigang on the old **hearth**."},{"sentence":"Ang uling sa **dingalan** ay kailangan nang dagdagan.","translation":"The charcoal in the **stove-top** needs to be replenished."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang babaeng magulang ng isang tao; ina.
etymology: Posibleng mula sa Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *ina, na may impluwensya mula sa iba't ibang wika sa rehiyon.
original_explanation: The OG, the queen, the source of unconditional love and unlimited 'kain ka na?' messages. She's your first teacher, first critic, and forever your number one fan. Also the final boss when you don't clean your room.
usage_notes: The most common and general term for 'mother' in Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahal na mahal ko ang aking **nanay**.","translation":"I love my **mother** very much."},{"sentence":"Tumawag ka ba sa **nanay** mo ngayong Mother's Day?","translation":"Did you call your **mother** this Mother's Day?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng paligsahan sa pagtakbo kung saan kailangang lampasan o talunin ng mga manlalaro ang mga nakahanay na hadlang.
original_explanation: Ito yung literal na representation ng adulting. Tatakbo ka, tapos may biglang lilitaw na problema (hadlang) na kailangan mong lampasan. Parang pag-commute mo araw-araw, isang malaking karerang may hadlang.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa isports at bilang metapora sa mga pagsubok sa buhay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumali siya sa **karerang may hadlang** sa palarong pambansa.","translation":"He joined the **hurdles** event in the national games."},{"sentence":"Ang buhay ay parang isang **karerang may hadlang**; puno ng mga pagsubok na kailangang malampasan.","translation":"Life is like an **obstacle race**; full of challenges that need to be overcome."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay-halaga o pagpansin. Karaniwang ginagamit sa mga pariralang negatibo upang ipahiwatig ang kawalan ng pag-aalala.
original_explanation: As a noun, it's the 'f*ck' in "I don't give a f*ck." It's the thing you don't have or don't give when you're ignoring haters, bad weather, or your responsibilities for a while. "Walang alintana sa mundo" is the vibe when you're on vacation mode.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in negative phrases like 'hindi alintana' (unheeded), 'walang alintana' (without a care).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya **alintana** ang panganib.","translation":"The danger was of no **regard** to him."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan kung saan ang isang daanan o bukasan ay nakasara, nakatakip, o hindi maaaring gamitin o pasukin.
original_explanation: The saddest word you'll see on your favorite milk tea shop at 10 PM. Sarado na! It means 'closed,' 'game over,' 'try again tomorrow.' Also applies to minds that won't accept new ideas. 'Ay, sarado isip niyan.'
usage_notes: Describes the state of being closed, as opposed to 'sara' which is the action of closing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sarado** na ang lahat ng tindahan nang dumating kami sa palengke.","translation":"All the stores were already **closed** when we arrived at the market."},{"sentence":"Laging **sarado** ang puso niya para sa pag-ibig.","translation":"Her heart is always **closed** to love."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pakikipag-ugnayan o pakikisama sa isang grupo ng mga tao, lalo na sa isang pagtitipon.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'halubilo' (pakikisama) at ang gitlaping '-um-'.
original_explanation: That awkward moment sa party na kailangan mong **humalubilo** sa mga kamag-anak ng jowa mo. It's about breaking out of your shell and socializing with the crowd, kahit introvert ka pa. The ultimate 'makipag-plastikan' skill for corporate events.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng mga social gathering tulad ng mga party, seminar, o pagtitipon ng komunidad.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahiyain si Ana kaya nahihirapan siyang **humalubilo** sa mga bagong kaklase.","translation":"Ana is shy, so she finds it difficult to **mingle** with new classmates."},{"sentence":"Inutusan ng boss ang mga bagong empleyado na **humalubilo** sa Christmas party ng kumpanya.","translation":"The boss instructed the new employees to **socialize** at the company's Christmas party."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang muling pagbabalik sa isang dating posisyon ng katanyagan o tagumpay; isang matalinong tugon o sagot.
original_explanation: Two meanings! 1) Sa K-Pop, ito 'yung pinakahihintay na pagbabalik ng paborito mong grupo na may bagong album at music video. 2) Sa bardagulan, ito 'yung matalino at mabilis mong sagot sa nang-asar sa'yo. 'Wala kang comeback?'
usage_notes: Malawak ang gamit, mula sa K-Pop at sports hanggang sa pang-araw-araw na argumento.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Grabe ang **comeback** ng Ginebra sa huling quarter!","translation":"Ginebra's **comeback** in the final quarter was amazing!"},{"sentence":"Inaabangan ko na ang **comeback** ng BLACKPINK.","translation":"I'm already waiting for BLACKPINK's **comeback**."},{"sentence":"Na-speechless siya, walang masabing **comeback**.","translation":"He was speechless, couldn't think of a **comeback**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkiskis ng dalawang bagay, lalo na ng bato, upang lumikha ng apoy o kislap. Sa makabagong gamit, tumutukoy din ito sa alitan o tensyon sa pagitan ng dalawang tao o grupo.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na `pingki` (kiskis, pag-umpog) at hulaping `-an`. Naging tanyag bilang sagisag-panulat ni Emilio Jacinto.
original_explanation: Literally, it's how you make fire with two stones, caveman-style. Figuratively, it's that 'friction' or 'tension' between two people who just don't get along. That co-worker you always argue with? May `pingkian` kayo. It was also the pen name of Emilio Jacinto, a Katipunero, because his ideas were meant to spark a revolution. Angas!
usage_notes: Can be literal (striking stones) or figurative (conflict, tension).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa pamamagitan ng **pingkian** ng dalawang bato, nakagawa sila ng apoy.","translation":"Through the **striking** of two stones, they were able to make a fire."},{"sentence":"May matinding **pingkian** sa pagitan ng management at ng unyon ng mga manggagawa.","translation":"There is intense **friction** between the management and the workers' union."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtulad o paggaya sa kilos, pananalita, o anyo ng isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: It's what your younger sibling does to annoy you, copying everything you say and do. It's also the core skill of every stand-up comedian doing impressions. Think of it as the OG 'copy-paste' but for human behavior. 'Gaya-gaya, puto maya!' is the national anthem against paggagad.
usage_notes: The form 'panggagagad' is also commonly used and is often interchangeable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paggagad** niya sa boses ng presidente ay talagang nakakatawa.","translation":"His **imitation** of the president's voice is really funny."},{"sentence":"Itigil mo na ang **paggagad** sa lahat ng ginagawa ko!","translation":"Stop **mimicking** everything I do!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging payapa, tahimik, maayos, at walang anumang kaguluhan o panganib.
original_explanation: This is the feeling you get when your internet is fast, your Grab arrives on time, and your salary has just been deposited. It's the opposite of "Sana all." It's the "All is well" moment. The ultimate state of zen amidst the chaos of Manila life.
usage_notes: Isang mas pormal at malalim na termino para sa kapayapaan, madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng kaayusang panlipunan o panloob na kapayapaan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang layunin ng pamahalaan ay mapanatili ang **katiwasayan** ng buong bansa.","translation":"The government's goal is to maintain the **peace and order** of the entire country."},{"sentence":"Nahanap niya ang **katiwasayan** ng isip matapos ang mahabang pagninilay-nilay.","translation":"He found mental **tranquility** after a long period of reflection."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing kulay itim ang isang bagay; padilimin ang kulay.
original_explanation: This is what you do to your profile picture when you're mourning or just feeling the emo phase. You 'itimin' the background. It also applies to overcooking your adobo until the sauce is super dark and rich. It's the act of turning something black.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of coloring, dyeing, or cooking.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto niyang **itimin** ang kanyang buhok para sa bagong itsura.","translation":"She wants to **dye** her hair **black** for a new look."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong masyadong **itimin** ang sabaw ng adobo.","translation":"Don't make the adobo sauce too **dark**."}]

meaning_filipino: Biglaan at hindi makontrol na paggalaw ng katawan, karaniwang sanhi ng sakit o matinding kirot. Pagkislot o pagpilipit ng katawan.
original_explanation: That moment when you get a leg cramp in the middle of the night and you start doing some weird, involuntary breakdance moves. Or when your internet connection dies during a crucial online game or a Zoom presentation, and you just internally have a 'kisay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang magkaroon ng **kisay** ang pasyente dahil sa mataas na lagnat.","translation":"The patient started to have **convulsions** due to a high fever."}]

meaning_filipino: Pumanig o kumampi sa isang tao, grupo, o pananaw sa isang alitan o sitwasyon.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'panig' (side) at hulaping '-an', na nagpapahiwatig ng kilos na isinasagawa sa isang direksyon o panig.
original_explanation: 'Yung moment na may away ang dalawa mong kaibigan tapos kailangan mong pumili kung kanino ka kakampi. 'Wag mo siyang panigan dahil lang mas close kayo; alamin mo muna kung sino ang tama. It's choosing a side, like in a group project or a family drama. Choose wisely, or you'll be the next topic in the group chat.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa mga konteksto ng hindi pagkakasundo, debate, o anumang sitwasyon na nangangailangan ng pagpili ng kakampihan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **panigan** ang mali kahit na kaibigan mo pa siya.","translation":"Do not **side with** the wrong one even if they are your friend."},{"sentence":"Sa huli, pinanigan ng korte ang karapatan ng mga manggagawa.","translation":"In the end, the court **sided with** the rights of the workers."}]

translation: to insert; to tuck in; to stick into
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpasok o pagsingit ng isang bagay sa isang masikip na espasyo, siwang, o sa pagitan ng ibang mga bagay.
original_explanation: It's that move you do when you're trying to hide your phone in your bag discreetly, or when you're stuffing one last piece of chicharon into an already full container of pasalubong. It's a more forceful, sometimes hidden, version of 'insert'. 'Isaluksok mo na lang diyan sa gilid.' (Just stick it in there on the side.)
usage_notes: Often implies inserting something into a tight or hidden space. The most common verb form is `isaluksok`. `Saluksok` as a noun can mean 'something inserted'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang i**saluksok** ang kanyang wallet sa masikip na bulsa.","translation":"He tried to **tuck** his wallet into the tight pocket."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong i**saluksok** ang basura sa siwang ng upuan.","translation":"Don't **stick** the trash into the crevice of the seat."}]

meaning_filipino: Isailalim sa proseso ng embalsamo ang isang bangkay upang mapreserba ito at hindi kaagad maagnas.
original_explanation: The less cheerful meaning. This is what funeral homes do. It's the process of preserving a body for a wake, so everyone has time to pay their last respects (and play some card games). The word itself is a loan from Spanish 'embalsamar'.
usage_notes: The common term for embalming in the Philippines. This is a homonym of 'ibalsa' (to raft).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala ang labi sa punerarya upang **ibalsa**.","translation":"The remains were brought to the funeral parlor to be **embalmed**."},{"sentence":"Sila ay espesyalista sa pag-**ibalsa** ng mga yumaong may matagal na burol.","translation":"They are specialists in **embalming** the deceased who will have a long wake."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng maraming sanga; ginagamit din upang ilarawan ang isang bagay na masalimuot o may maraming magkakaugnay na bahagi.
original_explanation: Describes something with more branches than your family tree during a reunion. Also, the plot of your favorite K-drama or the tsismis chain in your office. 'Ang gulo ng kwento, sanga-sanga na!'
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin nang literal para sa mga puno o sa makabagay na paraan para sa mga kumplikadong sitwasyon, kwento, o sistema.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **sanga-sanga** na ugat ng puno ay humaharang sa daan.","translation":"The **branching** roots of the tree are blocking the path."},{"sentence":"Naging **sanga-sanga** ang usapin dahil sa dami ng isyung lumabas.","translation":"The discussion became **complex** because of the many issues that came up."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ideya, likha, o konsepto na nagmula sa imahinasyon o pag-iisip ng isang tao; isang katha.
etymology: Literally 'fruit of the mind' (bunga + ng + isip).
original_explanation: The official term for your "what if" scenarios that keep you up at 3 AM. It’s the story you wrote, the business idea you pitched, or the elaborate excuse you came up with for being late. Basically, anything that came out of your brain, whether it's genius or just plain *kalokohan*.
usage_notes: A compound word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang nobelang iyan ay **bungang-isip** lamang ng may-akda.","translation":"That novel is purely the **imagination** of the author."},{"sentence":"Ang bagong app na ito ay **bungang-isip** ng isang batang programmer.","translation":"This new app is the **brainchild** of a young programmer."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mensahe, balita, o bagay na ipinadala o ipinaabot sa isang tao.
original_explanation: This is the thing being delivered, not the act of delivering. It could be a text message, a GrabFood order, or a cryptic 'hugot' quote on Facebook meant for a specific person. "May pahatid ako sa'yo" can either be exciting (a gift!) or terrifying (a summons!). It's the package, the memo, the "pasabog" you're sending out into the world.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **pahatid** daw para sa iyo galing sa probinsya.","translation":"They said there's **something sent** for you from the province."},{"sentence":"Ano ang **pahatid** ng kanyang huling liham?","translation":"What is the **message** of his last letter?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na paglalarawan sa isang tao na may hindi kanais-nais na amoy sa kili-kili.
etymology: From "may" (has) + "putok" (explosion). The metaphor is that the smell 'explodes' from the underarm.
original_explanation: Ah, the dreaded 'B.O.' The reason why deodorants are a multi-million peso industry in the Philippines. This is the 'putok' you *don't* want to hear about. It's the invisible force field that makes people subtly move away from you in a crowded MRT. The ultimate social distancing tool, even before it was cool.
usage_notes: This is a colloquial and somewhat impolite term. Use with caution. Often used in jokes or gossip.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"\"Bes, pa-check nga, parang **may-putok** ata ako.\"","translation":"\"Friend, can you check, I think I **have body odor**.\""}]

meaning_filipino: Pilitin ang isang tao na gawin ang isang bagay labag sa kanyang kalooban; gumamit ng lakas o kapangyarihan.
original_explanation: When your mom makes you sing for the relatives at a family reunion, 'pinuwersa' ka niya. It's being made to do something you don't want to do, from finishing your veggies to working overtime on a Friday. It's the opposite of 'kusa' (voluntary).
usage_notes: Often stronger than 'pilitin', implying the use of authority, physical strength, or coercion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **puwersahin** ang sarili mo kung pagod ka na.","translation":"Don't **force** yourself if you're already tired."},{"sentence":"**Pinuwersa** siyang pumirma sa kasunduan.","translation":"He was **forced** to sign the agreement."}]

translation: to make oneself sweat; to work out
meaning_filipino: Ang sadya o sinasadyang pagkilos upang pagpawisan, karaniwan sa pamamagitan ng ehersisyo o mabigat na gawain.
original_explanation: Your Tita's favorite advice for everything from a common cold to a broken heart: "Magpapawis ka!" It's the Filipino catch-all term for any form of exercise—jogging, Zumba, basketball, or even just intense house cleaning. The goal? To sweat out the toxins, the fats, or the bad vibes.
usage_notes: Often used as a command ('Magpawis ka!') or to state an intention ('Magpapawis ako.'). It is a very common and colloquial term for exercising.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing umaga, lumalabas siya para **magpapawis** sa parke.","translation":"Every morning, he goes out to **work out** at the park."},{"sentence":"Pinayuhan ako ng doktor na **magpapawis** kahit tatlong beses sa isang linggo.","translation":"The doctor advised me to **make myself sweat** at least three times a week."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malapot at malinamnam na sarsa na gawa sa katas ng talaba, toyo, at iba pang pampalasa, na karaniwang ginagamit sa lutuing Asyano.
etymology: English 'oyster sauce', a calque of Chinese (Cantonese) 'hòuh yàuh' (蚝油).
original_explanation: The secret weapon for making any vegetable dish (like kangkong or broccoli) instantly delicious. It's that thick, savory, brownish sauce that adds a magical umami punch. If you want to level up your ginisang gulay, just add a splash of oyster sauce. Instant chef!
usage_notes: Direct loan phrase. A staple ingredient in many Filipino-Chinese dishes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong ulam ang Ginisang Kangkong na may **oyster sauce**.","translation":"My favorite dish is Sautéed Water Spinach with **oyster sauce**."},{"sentence":"Pakiabot ng bote ng **oyster sauce** diyan sa tabi mo.","translation":"Please pass the bottle of **oyster sauce** beside you."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang taong walang kakayahang pinansyal o kapangyarihang baguhin ang isang sitwasyon.
original_explanation: Two meanings here. First, it's that feeling when your internet is down during a crucial online meeting—**walang-kaya** ka, you're helpless. Second, it's the more serious meaning: someone who is financially struggling, 'isang kahig, isang tuka'. Both describe a state of powerlessness, whether it's against a bad Wi-Fi signal or poverty.
usage_notes: Can refer to financial status (poor) or a state of being unable to act (helpless). Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiramdam niya ay **walang-kaya** siya habang pinapanood ang pagguho ng kanyang bahay.","translation":"He felt **helpless** as he watched his house collapse."},{"sentence":"Ang programa ay naglalayong tulungan ang mga pamilyang **walang-kaya**.","translation":"The program aims to help **poor** families."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat ng mga tao na may ugnayan ng pagtitiwala, pagmamahal, at pagsuporta sa isa't isa.
original_explanation: 'Yung barkada mo na kasama mo sa kalokohan, sa iyakan, at sa food trip. Kayo 'yun, ang magkakaibigan. The squad, the gang, the people you send ugly selfies to at 3 AM. The ones who know your Wi-Fi password by heart.
usage_notes: Refers to the group of people who are friends with each other. The singular form is "kaibigan".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matagal nang **magkakaibigan** sina Ana, Bea, at Carla.","translation":"Ana, Bea, and Carla have been **friends** for a long time."},{"sentence":"Nagplano ang **magkakaibigan** na magbakasyon sa Palawan.","translation":"The **group of friends** planned a vacation to Palawan."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bidyo na inilalathala sa social media kung saan ang isang tao, karaniwan ay isang influencer o public figure, ay humihingi ng paumanhin para sa isang kontrobersyal na kilos o pahayag.
original_explanation: The modern-day public execution for influencers who messed up. Usually features a bare face, a sad-looking background, a lot of deep sighs, and the classic line, 'I'm still learning and growing.' The comments section is the real entertainment.
usage_notes: A very recent term that entered the Filipino lexicon through social media culture. The spelling and pronunciation are directly from English.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-upload na naman ng **apology video** yung vlogger na na-cancel.","translation":"The vlogger who got canceled uploaded an **apology video** again."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, bagay, o sitwasyon na natagpuan o naabutan sa isang lugar sa oras ng pagdating.
etymology: Mula sa "ka-" (nagpapahiwatig ng kasama o kaugnayan) + "datnan" (found upon arrival).
original_explanation: It's like when you arrive at a party and there's that one person already passed out on the couch. Sila 'yung karatnan mo. You found them there. It's a super rare word, though, so don't use it unless you want to sound like you swallowed a 19th-century dictionary.
usage_notes: Isang napakabihirang salita na halos hindi na ginagamit sa modernong pag-uusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tanging **karatnan** niya sa bahay ay isang pusang natutulog.","translation":"The only **one he found** at home upon arrival was a sleeping cat."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng tulay na gawa sa kawayan, karaniwang pansamantala at yari sa iilang piraso lamang na pinag-ugpong.
original_explanation: Imagine crossing a creek in the province. That rickety, slightly scary bamboo bridge that sways with every step? That's a 'tayuntong'. It's the ultimate test of your balancing skills, the OG "trust the process" infrastructure before it was cool.
usage_notes: Often used in rural or provincial contexts. It implies a simple, non-permanent structure, sometimes consisting of just one or two bamboo poles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maingat siyang tumawid sa **tayuntong** para makarating sa kabilang pampang.","translation":"He carefully crossed the **bamboo bridge** to get to the other side."},{"sentence":"Gumuho ang **tayuntong** dahil sa malakas na agos ng ilog.","translation":"The **makeshift bamboo bridge** collapsed due to the strong river current."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa anumang bagay na may kaugnayan sa mga salita, pasalita man o pasulat.
original_explanation: It's all talk. When your 'bardagulan' with a frenemy on social media escalates from passive-aggressive memes to actual, written threats, that's a **berbal** war. It's the opposite of physical; it’s when words are your weapons of choice, from a formal debate to a shouting match with the kapitbahay over the karaoke volume.
usage_notes: Can refer to spoken or written words, but in common parlance, it often emphasizes the spoken aspect, as in 'berbal na kasunduan' (verbal agreement).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon sila ng mainit na **berbal** na pagtatalo.","translation":"They had a heated **verbal** argument."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng **berbal** na pahintulot mula sa tagapamahala.","translation":"A **verbal** permission is needed from the manager."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ikalimang araw ng linggo (o ikaapat na araw ng trabaho), pagkatapos ng Miyerkules at bago ang Biyernes.
etymology: From Spanish 'jueves' (Thursday), named after the Roman god Jupiter.
original_explanation: Ah, Huwebes. The official "konting kembot na lang, Biyernes na!" day. It's the Throwback Thursday (#TBT) of the week, where you feel the weekend getting closer. For many, it's also the last day to cram everything before the Friday chill mode activates.
usage_notes: Always capitalized when referring to the day of the week.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May meeting tayo tuwing **Huwebes** ng umaga.","translation":"We have a meeting every **Thursday** morning."},{"sentence":"Sa **Huwebes** na ang deadline ng ating proyekto.","translation":"The deadline for our project is on **Thursday**."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi nabibilang; walang itinakdang bilang o numero.
original_explanation: This can mean two things. Literally, 'unnumbered,' like a house on a rural road na walang house number. Figuratively, it means 'countless' or 'innumerable,' like the 'walang-numerong' beses na nag-overthink ka today.
usage_notes: Ang konteksto ang nagtatakda kung ito ay nangangahulugang 'walang marka ng numero' o 'sobrang dami para bilangin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang bahay ay **walang-numero** kaya mahirap hanapin.","translation":"His house is **unnumbered** so it's hard to find."},{"sentence":"**Walang-numero** ang mga bituin sa kalangitan.","translation":"The stars in the sky are **countless**."}]

translation: act of taking care of; fostering; sheltering
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-aalaga, pagkalinga, at pagbibigay-proteksyon sa isang tao na nangangailangan, partikular na sa isang bata o maysakit.
etymology: From pag- (gerund prefix) + papaka- (intensive/causative prefix) + kandili (care, protection).
original_explanation: This is that deep, nurturing care you see from a lola looking after her apo, or an OFW parent sending everything back home. It’s more than just 'taking care'; it’s about sheltering someone, providing for them, and making them your responsibility. It’s the ultimate act of 'alaga'.
usage_notes: A deep and somewhat poetic word implying great care and responsibility. More intense than 'pag-aalaga'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagpatuloy niya ang **pagpapakandili** sa kanyang mga nakababatang kapatid nang sila'y maulila.","translation":"She continued the **act of taking care of** her younger siblings when they were orphaned."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapakandili** sa mga ulila ay isang marangal na gawain.","translation":"The **fostering** of orphans is a noble deed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang isa sa dalawang bahagi ng isang pares; ang kapareha o katambal.
etymology: From `ka-` (denoting a partner or part of a whole) + `baak` (to split, cleave).
original_explanation: Your other half, your partner in crime, the Jollibee to your McDo. It's often used for spouses, but can also mean the other half of a coconut you just split. It's the "sana all" part of a relationship.
usage_notes: While it can mean a literal half, it is more poetically and commonly used to refer to a spouse or life partner.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinakilala niya sa amin ang kanyang **kabaak** sa buhay.","translation":"He introduced to us his **partner** in life."},{"sentence":"Nawawala ang **kabaak** ng tsinelas ko.","translation":"The **other half** of my slipper is missing."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o grupo na sumusuporta, nagtatanggol, o nagsusulong ng isang layunin, simulain, o adhikain.
etymology: From taga- (doer of an action) + taguyod (to support, to promote).
original_explanation: The ultimate hype-man for a cause. Sila yung nag-o-organize ng fund-raising, nag-she-share ng petitions sa social media, o yung kaibigan mong laging nag-po-promote ng small business ng isa pang kaibigan. They don't just 'like' your post, they 'share' it with a long caption.
usage_notes: A formal and powerful word, often used in social, political, and non-profit contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay isang kilalang **tagataguyod** ng karapatan ng mga kababaihan.","translation":"She is a known **advocate** for women's rights."},{"sentence":"Ang aming kumpanya ay isa sa mga **tagataguyod** ng proyektong ito.","translation":"Our company is one of the **sponsors** of this project."}]

translation: to fall flat on one's back
meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang pagbagsak o pagkahiga nang patihaya o nakatingala.
original_explanation: This isn't just falling down. This is the dramatic, telenovela-style fall where you land flat on your back, eyes wide with shock. Imagine slipping on a wet floor in the mall and landing with a loud THUD, lahat ng tao nakatingin. That's 'timbuwang'. It's a fall with 100% commitment and zero grace.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa isang partikular na uri ng pagbagsak. Ang pandiwa nito ay 'tumimbuwang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Timbuwang** ang boksingero matapos tamaan ng isang malakas na suntok.","translation":"The boxer **fell flat on his back** after being hit by a strong punch."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-inom o pagkuha ng likido sa bibig sa pamamagitan ng pagsipsip, karaniwang nagdudulot ng tunog.
original_explanation: That satisfying sound you make when the bulalo soup is just *perfect*. It's the official sound of enjoying a hot bowl of mami, a cup of coffee, or the last drops of your milk tea through a straw. Paghigop is an auditory confirmation that what you're drinking is delicious.
usage_notes: Often associated with hot liquids like soup or coffee and implies an audible sound.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Rinig na rinig ang kanyang malakas na **paghigop** ng mainit na sabaw.","translation":"His loud **slurping** of the hot soup could be clearly heard."},{"sentence":"Wala nang tatalo sa sarap ng **paghigop** ng kape sa umaga.","translation":"Nothing beats the pleasure of **sipping** coffee in the morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o grupo ng mga tao na inupahan upang protektahan ang isang indibidwal mula sa panganib o pag-atake.
original_explanation: The guy in the barong or suit with the earpiece who always looks serious. They're the human version of a firewall, making sure no one gets too close to the VIP. Or, in a more relatable context, your overprotective kuya who screens all your 'manliligaw'. He's your personal, unpaid bodyguard.
usage_notes: The English word is used directly in Tagalog. There is no common Tagalog equivalent, though 'bantay' or 'guwardiya' can be used in some contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May kasamang dalawang **bodyguard** ang politiko saan man siya magpunta.","translation":"The politician has two **bodyguards** with him wherever he goes."},{"sentence":"Kumuha siya ng **bodyguard** matapos makatanggap ng mga banta.","translation":"He hired a **bodyguard** after receiving threats."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginagamit upang ipahayag ang isang posibilidad o kawalan ng katiyakan.
etymology: Unknown origin, possibly related to Sanskrit 'vakra' (crooked, indirect).
original_explanation: This is the official word for Filipino uncertainty. It's the 'maybe' you use when you don't want to commit. 'Pupunta ka?' 'Ewan, baka.' It's the sound of a non-committal shrug. Often followed by a verb in the contemplative aspect (e.g., 'baka umulan' - it might rain).
usage_notes: Often used to express a possibility or a slight warning. It is distinct from 'siguro' (I guess/probably) as 'baka' often implies a consequence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magdala ka ng payong, **baka** umulan mamaya.","translation":"Bring an umbrella, it **might** rain later."},{"sentence":"**Baka** hindi na ako makahabol sa huling biyahe ng bus.","translation":"**Maybe** I won't be able to catch the last bus trip."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang taong nagpapatakbo o nagmamaneho ng kalesa; kutsero.
original_explanation: The original Uber driver, but with a horse. He's your tour guide, historian, and photographer all in one, navigating the cobblestone streets of old Manila. He's got more stories than your lolo and knows all the best angles for your IG post.
usage_notes: The driver of a 'kalesa'. Synonymous with 'kutsero'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magaling magkuwento ang **kalesero** tungkol sa kasaysayan ng mga lumang gusali.","translation":"The **carriage driver** was good at telling stories about the history of the old buildings."},{"sentence":"Binigyan namin ng tip ang **kalesero** dahil sa kanyang magandang serbisyo.","translation":"We gave the **carriage driver** a tip for his good service."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpapakita ng kagalakan o pagiging aliw sa pamamagitan ng mga tunog at ekspresyon ng mukha. Ito ay ang kasalukuyang anyo ng pandiwang "tawa".
original_explanation: That's the sound you make when you see a funny meme, hear your tita's corny joke, or remember something embarrassing you did five years ago. It's the "haha" react in real life. "Bakit ka tumatawa diyan mag-isa?" is the question your mom asks when you're just staring at your phone, smiling.
usage_notes: Present progressive tense of "tawa" (to laugh).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumatawa** ang buong klase sa kwento ng guro.","translation":"The whole class **is laughing** at the teacher's story."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko alam kung bakit siya **tumatawa** habang nanonood ng horror movie.","translation":"I don't know why he/she **is laughing** while watching a horror movie."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang muling pagkabuhay mula sa mga patay; ang pagpapanumbalik sa dating kalagayan, gamit, o kasikatan.
original_explanation: Same as 'resureksiyon', but this is the spelling you're more likely to see and hear in everyday convo. It's the ultimate comeback. Think of a 'laos' na celebrity suddenly getting a blockbuster movie, or your WiFi connection coming back to life after a 3-hour outage. That, my friend, is a resureksyon.
usage_notes: This is a more common and simplified spelling of 'resureksiyon'. Both are acceptable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagdiriwang tuwing Linggo ng Pagkabuhay ang **resureksyon** ni Kristo.","translation":"The **resurrection** of Christ is celebrated every Easter Sunday."},{"sentence":"Ang muling pagbubukas ng lumang sinehan ay parang **resureksyon** para sa buong bayan.","translation":"The reopening of the old cinema is like a **resurrection** for the whole town."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi pantay o balanse; nakahilig o nakatabingi sa isang panig.
etymology: Possibly from a root word "gibang" meaning 'to tilt' or 'to be off-balance'.
original_explanation: Your picture frame is tagibang. The Leaning Tower of Pisa is tagibang. Your stack of papers on your desk is tagibang. Your life after a breakup might feel tagibang. It's that feeling of imbalance, when things are just... off-center.
usage_notes: Often used to describe physical objects that are not level or upright. Can be used metaphorically for unbalanced situations. A common synonym is "tabingi".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayusin mo ang salamin, **tagibang** ang pagkakasabit.","translation":"Fix the mirror, it's hanging **lopsided**."},{"sentence":"Naging **tagibang** ang tingin niya sa mundo matapos ang trahedya.","translation":"His view of the world became **askew** after the tragedy."}]

translation: to be able to stay; to push through; to happen (often negatively)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakapagpatuloy o pagkakapaglagi sa isang lugar; ang tuluyang pagkaganap ng isang bagay, lalo na ang isang masamang pangyayari.
etymology: ma- (potential prefix) + tuloy (to continue, to stay)
original_explanation: This is what happens when a guest overstays their welcome and you can't kick them out, so you just let them stay. "Sige, dito ka na matuluyan." It can also mean when something you were dreading actually happens, like a project getting cancelled. "Naku, natuluyan na ang project cancellation." It's the "it's really happening" verb, often with a sigh of resignation.
usage_notes: Often implies that an action or event has reached its final, often irreversible, stage. Can be used for lodging or for an event coming to fruition.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay may **matuluyan** kaming otel ngayong gabi.","translation":"I hope we can **find a place to stay** in a hotel tonight."},{"sentence":"Kung hindi ka mag-iingat, baka **matuluyan** ang iyong sakit.","translation":"If you are not careful, your illness might **become serious**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mapanlait na salita para sa isang taong hangal o tanga, na binaligtad mula sa salitang 'bobo'.
original_explanation: The reversed, edgier version of 'bobo.' It's what you type in all caps in a heated online game when your teammate messes up. Obob is a slang insult, a bit more aggressive and 'internet-y' than just calling someone stupid. It's the kind of word you'd hear in a computer shop or see in the comments section of a viral video.
usage_notes: This is considered a rude and offensive slang term. It can also be used as a noun ('moron'). Use with caution.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinabihan siyang **obob** ng kalaro niya sa online game.","translation":"His playmate in the online game called him a **moron**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang gumawa ng mga desisyong **obob**; pag-isipan mo muna.","translation":"Don't make **stupid** decisions; think it over first."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang pagkuha o pag-agaw sa isang bagay at mabilis na pag-alis habang dala ito.
original_explanation: The classic modus operandi. A snatcher on a motorcycle who grabs your phone? **Tumangay** ng cellphone. A huge wave that pulls your tsinelas into the sea? **Tumangay** din 'yun. Basically, anything that quickly and forcefully takes something away from you.
usage_notes: Often implies speed and a degree of force or theft, but can also be used for natural forces like wind or water.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis na **tumangay** ng bag ang magnanakaw bago ito nakatakas.","translation":"The thief quickly **snatched** the bag before escaping."},{"sentence":"Malakas ang agos ng ilog kaya **tumangay** ito ng ilang mga damit na nakasampay.","translation":"The river's current was strong so it **carried away** some of the clothes on the line."}]

translation: to get dressed up; to adorn
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aayos sa sarili sa pamamagitan ng pagsusuot ng maganda, pormal, o natatanging kasuotan at mga palamuti.
original_explanation: What you do when the dress code isn't 'pambahay chic.' It's the process of transforming from your 'ghosting sa work' look to your 'ready for the party' look. To `magayak` is to put on your best clothes, do your makeup, and prepare to slay. 'Bihis na, 'di pa `magayak`?'
usage_notes: Implies more than just getting dressed ('magbihis'). 'Magayak' suggests dressing for a special occasion with care and adornments.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magayak** nang pormal para sa kasal.","translation":"We need to **get dressed up** formally for the wedding."},{"sentence":"Ang mga kalahok sa parada ay nagsimulang **magayak** kahit madaling araw pa.","translation":"The parade participants began to **adorn** themselves even though it was still dawn."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal at pinaikling paraan ng pagsasabi ng 'iyan' o 'ayan,' kadalasang ginagamit sa social media at usapang bakla (swardspeak).
etymology: Filipino slang, a corruption/shortening of 'iyan.' Popularized on social media.
original_explanation: Not the one for knitting! This is pure Gen Z/Twitter slang. It's a cuter, faster way to say 'iyan' (that) or 'ayan' (there). Used to point something out, either literally or figuratively. 'Ganda ng outfit mo, yarn!' or 'Ay, nahulog. Awkward, yarn?' It's the verbal equivalent of a finger-pointing emoji.
usage_notes: Highly informal and trendy. Using it might make you sound cool or trying-too-hard, depending on your age and audience.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Wow, new phone! Sana all, **yarn**?","translation":"Wow, new phone! Wish everyone had one, **is that it**?"},{"sentence":"Okay, tapos na ang work. Uwi na, **yarn**!","translation":"Okay, work is done. Time to go home, **there we go**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng pagkain ang isang tao, hayop, o anumang may buhay.
original_explanation: The universal Filipino love language. It’s what your lola does the moment you walk in the door, even if you just ate. "Kumain ka na?" is just a formality; the real action is the 'pakain'. It can be an act of love ("Pakainin mo ang bisita!"), a chore ("Pakainin mo na yung aso!"), or a business ("May pakain si mayor!").
usage_notes: The causative form of the verb 'kain' (to eat).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **pakainin** ang mga alagang hayop.","translation":"Don't forget to **feed** the pets."},{"sentence":"Naghanda siya ng pagkain upang **pakainin** ang mga bata sa kalye.","translation":"She prepared food to **feed** the street children."}]

translation: to be shaken, to be jolted
meaning_filipino: Ang maranasan ang malakas o mabilis na pag-uga o pagyanig, kadalasan dahil sa pagdaan sa magaspang na daan o dahil sa isang malakas na pwersa.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your internal organs when the bus driver thinks he's in an F1 race on a bumpy provincial road. 'Yung feeling na nag-vibrate 'yung buong kaluluwa mo dahil sa lubak. Also, 'yung epekto sa 'yo ng malakas na bass sa concert.
usage_notes: Often used to describe the experience of riding in a vehicle on a rough road.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Natigtig** kami nang husto sa biyahe papuntang Baguio dahil sa liku-likong daan.","translation":"We **were shaken** a lot on the trip to Baguio because of the winding roads."},{"sentence":"Ingatan mo ang cake para hindi **matigtig** at masira ang itsura.","translation":"Be careful with the cake so it won't **be jolted** and its appearance gets ruined."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pandiwa ng paggawa ng isang bagay na maging balumbon; ilulon o irolyo.
original_explanation: The action of making a `balumbon`. It's what you do to your banig after a picnic, your diploma after graduation, or that poster you bought at a convention. "Okay guys, pack up na, **balumbunin** na natin 'yung tent!"
usage_notes: This is the verb form of 'balumbon'. 'Ilulon' or 'irolyo' are more common synonyms.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Balumbunin** mo nang maayos ang banig para magkasya sa sasakyan.","translation":"**Roll up** the mat properly so it will fit in the car."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos basahin, maingat niyang **binalumbon** ang lumang sulat.","translation":"After reading, he carefully **rolled up** the old letter."}]

translation: to cook or eat pansit (Filipino noodles)
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagluluto o pagkain ng pansit.
etymology: From Hokkien Chinese 扁食 (pián-si̍t), meaning "something conveniently cooked".
original_explanation: This is the go-to verb for birthday preparations. "Long life" daw, kaya sige, magpansit tayo! It's either the act of cooking that giant *bilao* of noodles or the act of consuming it with gusto. The MVP of Filipino party food verbs.
usage_notes: Can mean either "to cook pansit" or "to eat pansit," depending on context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **magpapansit** para sa kaarawan ni Lola?","translation":"Who will **cook pansit** for Grandma's birthday?"},{"sentence":"Tara, **magpansit** tayo sa kanto, gutom na ako.","translation":"Let's go, let's **eat pansit** at the corner, I'm hungry."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng isang balangkas o paunang plano para sa isang sulatin, proyekto, o gawain.
etymology: From Visayan 'banhay' meaning outline or sketch.
original_explanation: This is what your Filipino teacher told you to do before writing an essay, but you probably just skipped to the main part. It's like creating the skeleton of your thesis before adding the 'flesh' (aka the 200 pages of pure agony). In project management, it's making the gantt chart before the actual work.
usage_notes: A more formal or academic term for 'magbalangkas'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan muna nating **bumanhay** ng mga hakbang bago simulan ang proyekto.","translation":"We first need to **outline** the steps before starting the project."},{"sentence":"Pinapagawa kami ng guro na **bumanhay** ng aming sanaysay.","translation":"The teacher is asking us to **draft** an outline of our essay."}]

translation: a type of Filipino sweet bread
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng mamon o tinapay na malambot at matamis, karaniwang may mantikilya, asukal, at keso sa ibabaw.
original_explanation: That fluffy, buttery, cheesy, sugary bread that screams 'Pasko na!' or 'May balikbayan sa bahay!' It's the ultimate merienda treat, the kind you get from a fancy bakeshop or from your tita who makes the best ones. The final boss of Filipino pastries.
usage_notes: A very popular pastry in the Philippines, especially during the Christmas season. The spelling 'ensemada' is a common variant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong kainin ang **ensaymada** na may mainit na tsokolate.","translation":"My favorite thing to eat is **ensaymada** with hot chocolate."},{"sentence":"Nag-uwi si nanay ng masarap na **ensaymada** mula sa panaderya.","translation":"Mom brought home delicious **ensaymada** from the bakery."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbuga ng hangin mula sa bibig o ang pagdaan ng mahinang hangin.
original_explanation: The gentle cousin of 'buga' (exhale forcefully). 'Hihip' is the soft puff of air you use to blow out a candle, cool down your hot coffee, or make a dandelion's seeds fly. It's a delicate, controlled gust. It's also what you wish for on a hot summer day: 'sana may hihip ng hangin.'
usage_notes: 'Hihip' implies a gentler or more controlled release of air compared to 'ihip' or 'buga'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **hihip** lang niya ay namatay na ang kandila.","translation":"With just one **blow** from him, the candle went out."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman ko ang malamig na **hihip** ng hangin.","translation":"I felt the cold **blow** of the wind."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging nasa panganib, kapinsalaan, o kasawian.
etymology: Mula sa `pagka-` (estado ng pagiging) + `pahamak` (magdulot ng pinsala/kasiraan).
original_explanation: This is when things go south, big time. It's when you thought you could get away with a little white lie, but it snowballs into a full-blown Marites-level chismis that ruins your reputation. It's the "This is fine" dog meme, but everything is actually on fire. Ito yung resulta kapag ang "bahala na si Batman" ay hindi gumana.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa resultang estado ng pagkasira o pagiging nasa panganib, madalas bilang bunga ng sarili o gawa ng iba.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang masamang bisyo ang nagdulot ng kanyang **pagkapahamak**.","translation":"His bad habits led to his **misfortune**."},{"sentence":"Upang maiwasan ang **pagkapahamak**, sumunod sa mga babala ng awtoridad.","translation":"To avoid **peril**, follow the authorities' warnings."}]

meaning_filipino: Marupok at mabilis maputol o mapatid, tulad ng sinulid o lubid; tumutukoy din sa pasensya na madaling maubos.
original_explanation: This is that cheap sinulid you bought from Divisoria that snaps when you just look at it. It's also your patience when you're stuck in EDSA traffic for 3 hours. 'Konting-konti na lang, madaling malagot na ang pisi ko!'
usage_notes: Used for thin, long objects that can snap (like threads or strings), and metaphorically for patience ('pisi ng pasensya').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit ka ng mas matibay na sinulid; iyang hawak mo ay **madaling malagot**.","translation":"Use a stronger thread; the one you're holding is **easy to snap**."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa pagiging **madaling malagot** ang pasensya.","translation":"He is known for having a patience that is **easy to snap** (i.e. he gets angry easily)."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-alis mula sa isang lugar o espasyo; ang paglitaw o pagiging hayag.
original_explanation: This is the grand reveal. The paglabas of your sweldo into your bank account. The paglabas of a new Marvel movie trailer. The paglabas mo ng bahay on a Friday night, ready to forget the stress of the work week. It's the moment something or someone emerges from the inside.
