usage_notes: Can refer to the physical act of exiting, the release of a product (like a movie or album), or coming out (as in revealing one's sexual orientation or gender identity).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inaabangan ng lahat ang **paglabas** ng bagong album ng paborito nilang banda.","translation":"Everyone is waiting for the **release** of their favorite band's new album."},{"sentence":"Sa kanyang **paglabas** sa entablado, nagsigawan ang mga manonood.","translation":"Upon his **exit** onto the stage, the audience screamed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagsisilang o pagluluwal ng isang sanggol mula sa sinapupunan ng ina.
original_explanation: The ultimate "push" notification. The final boss battle after 9 months of grinding. It's when a woman transforms into a superhero whose only weakness is unsolicited parenting advice from relatives.
usage_notes: The general term for the entire process of giving birth.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala siya sa ospital para sa kanyang **panganganak**.","translation":"She was brought to the hospital for her **childbirth**."},{"sentence":"Naging ligtas at mabilis ang kanyang **panganganak**.","translation":"Her **delivery** was safe and fast."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapakita ng mukha sa unang pagkakataon sa publiko o online, lalo na ng isang taong dati nang kilala sa pamamagitan lamang ng boses, avatar, o nakatakip na mukha.
original_explanation: This is the moment of truth for anonymous YouTubers, VTubers, and your online jowa na 'camera shy' daw. After months or years of just seeing a logo or a cat picture, they finally show their face. It's either a 'Sana all!' moment or a 'Sana 'di na lang' moment. The ultimate 'plot twist' of the digital age.
usage_notes: A common term in gaming, streaming, and online communities.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailan kaya magkakaroon ng **face reveal** ang paborito kong streamer?","translation":"I wonder when my favorite streamer will have a **face reveal**?"},{"sentence":"Nag-trending ang **face reveal** niya dahil hindi 'yun ang inasahan ng mga fans.","translation":"His **face reveal** trended because it wasn't what the fans expected."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pusang-kalye o pusang-ligaw na walang permanenteng tirahan o nag-aalaga; pinaikling anyo ng pusakal.
etymology: Maaaring pinaikling anyo ng "pusang kalye" o "pusakal."
original_explanation: The street-smart version of a house cat. These are the 'pusa sa kalye' or 'pusakal' who've seen things. They're the ones you see hanging out near the carinderia, hoping for scraps. They're tougher, scrappier, and probably have a more interesting life story than your pampered Siamese.
usage_notes: Madalas na ginagamit bilang kapalit ng "pusakal." Tumutukoy sa mga pusang-gala o ligaw.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **pusak** ang nag-aabang ng pagkain sa labas ng palengke.","translation":"Many **stray cats** are waiting for food outside the market."},{"sentence":"Pinakain niya ang gutom na **pusak**.","translation":"He fed the hungry **stray cat**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nangangasiwa at namumuno sa isang subasta o pampublikong bentahan.
etymology: From Spanish 'subasta'. The affix 'mang-' + duplicated first syllable 'su-' indicates a professional role.
original_explanation: Sila yung mabilis magsalita sa mga palabas na may 'Going once, going twice... SOLD!' Sila yung nagdidikta ng presyo sa auction, parang live na live na Shopee bidding. Ang mangsusubasta ang hari ng 'add to cart' bago pa nauso ang online shopping.
usage_notes: This is a specialized term. A more common way to say this might be 'tagapagsubasta'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis at malinaw magsalita ang **mangsusubasta** kaya maraming naengganyong tumawad.","translation":"The **auctioneer** spoke quickly and clearly, which encouraged many to bid."},{"sentence":"Ang dating **mangsusubasta** ay isa na ngayong kolektor ng mga antigong gamit.","translation":"The former **auctioneer** is now a collector of antiques."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang impormal na katawagan para sa Starbucks, isang kilalang internasyonal na coffee shop.
original_explanation: Short for Starbucks. Kasi 'pag full name, parang ang formal masyado. "Tara, SBUX tayo" sounds more casual than "Let's go to Starbucks." It's the go-to place for students pretending to study, BPO agents on their break, and anyone who needs a dose of overpriced but reliable caffeine and Wi-Fi.
usage_notes: Primarily used by millennials and Gen Z in urban areas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkita tayo sa **SBUX** mamaya para sa group project.","translation":"Let's meet at **SBUX** later for the group project."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng Venti Iced Caramel Macchiato from **SBUX** para magising ang diwa ko.","translation":"I need a Venti Iced Caramel Macchiato from **SBUX** to awaken my soul."}]

meaning_filipino: Plural na anyo ng 'magaling'. Tumutukoy sa katangian ng higit sa isang tao o bagay na may pambihirang kakayahan, husay, o kahusayan sa isang partikular na larangan.
original_explanation: This is the squad goals version of 'magaling'. It's what you say when your whole team passes the exam, your favorite basketball team is on fire, or when you're describing the lineup of singers at a concert. 'Magagaling sila' is the ultimate compliment for a group. It's the opposite of a group project where you're the only one doing the work.
usage_notes: The plural form of 'magaling'. It's formed by repeating the first syllable of the root word ('ga-ling' -> 'ga-galing') and adding the prefix 'ma-'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magagaling** ang mga doktor sa ospital na iyon.","translation":"The doctors in that hospital are **excellent**."},{"sentence":"Pinili niya ang mga pinaka-**magagaling** na manlalaro para sa kanyang koponan.","translation":"She chose the most **skilled** players for her team."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagkahulog o pagkalagas ng mga dahon mula sa puno o ng buhok mula sa anit.
original_explanation: Parang buhok mo 'pag sobrang stressed ka na sa work o sa acads, kusa na lang nalalagas. O kaya parang mga puno sa autumn, letting go of what's no longer needed. #Hugot. It's the natural process of shedding.
usage_notes: Madalas na ipinagpapalit sa 'nalalagas'. Ito ang kasalukuyang anyo ng pandiwa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nangungulag** na ang mga dahon ng puno dahil taglagas na.","translation":"The tree's leaves are now **shedding** because it's autumn."},{"sentence":"Sobrang stress niya kaya **nangungulag** ang kanyang buhok.","translation":"She is so stressed that her hair is **falling out**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpindot sa 'like' button sa isang social media platform upang ipahiwatig ang pagsang-ayon, paghanga, o pagkilala sa isang post.
etymology: From English "like", with the Tagalog verbalizing prefix "mag-".
original_explanation: The most important verb of the 21st century. This is what you do to your friend's new profile picture, your crush's cryptic status, or a funny meme. To "maglike" is to give digital validation. The opposite is to "mag-seen," which is a digital crime.
usage_notes: A clear example of code-switching becoming a standard verb in modern Filipino. Often written as 'mag-like'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **mag-like** at mag-share ng aming video!","translation":"Don't forget to **like** and share our video!"},{"sentence":"Bakit hindi siya **nag-like** sa post ko? May problema kaya kami?","translation":"Why didn't he/she **like** my post? Do we have a problem?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o akto ng pag-aangkop ng isang kuwento, pangyayari, o ideya sa anyong pandulaan para sa pagtatanghal sa entablado, radyo, telebisyon, o pelikula.
original_explanation: Eto 'yung ginagawa sa 'Magpakailanman' at 'MMK'. Kinukuha nila ang isang totoong kwento ng buhay tapos nilalagyan ng slow-motion effects, madamdaming background music, at mga artistang umiiyak. 'Yun ang **dramatisasyon**—ang pag-level up ng chismis into art.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napanood mo ba ang **dramatisasyon** ng buhay niya sa TV kagabi?","translation":"Did you watch the **dramatization** of her life on TV last night?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o proseso ng pagiging payat o pagbawas ng timbang at laman ng katawan.
etymology: From pa- + N (nasal assimilation of p) + payat, with reduplication of the first syllable of the root form (pa-mayat -> panayat -> pananayat). Describes the process or state of becoming thin.
original_explanation: This is that awkward phase when your tita sees you and goes, "Hala, anong nangyari sa'yo, 'nak? Anyare sa cheeks mo?" It's the physical manifestation of either a successful diet, a stressful breakup, or forgetting to eat because of too much work. The opposite of "tumaba."
usage_notes: Often used to describe a noticeable and sometimes concerning weight loss.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napansin ng doktor ang biglaang **pananayat** ng kanyang pasyente.","translation":"The doctor noticed the sudden **emaciation** of his patient."},{"sentence":"Ang **pananayat** niya ay dahil sa labis na pag-eehersisyo at pagdidiyeta.","translation":"His **becoming thin** is due to excessive exercise and dieting."}]

meaning_filipino: Bilang pangngalan, tumutukoy sa isang tao na may kapansanan sa paningin o walang kakayahang makakita. Bilang pang-uri, ito ay naglalarawan sa kawalan ng paningin.
original_explanation: Literally, someone who cannot see. Figuratively, it's what you become when you're 'in love' and ignore all the red flags. 'Pag-ibig na **bulag**' is the theme song of your friend who keeps going back to their toxic ex. Also used when you can't see the obvious, like where you put your keys.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pangngalan ('isang bulag') o pang-uri ('lalaking bulag'). Ang pariralang 'may kapansanan sa paningin' ay ang mas pormal at sensitibong termino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinutulungan niya ang isang **bulag** na tumawid sa kalsada.","translation":"He is helping a **blind** person cross the street."},{"sentence":"Naging **bulag** siya sa katotohanan dahil sa sobrang pagmamahal.","translation":"She became **blind** to the truth because of too much love."}]

meaning_filipino: Mapagmasid, mabilis makapansin ng mga detalye, o may matalim na paningin.
etymology: A Filipino idiom. Literally translates to 'sharp the eye', from 'matalas' (sharp) and 'mata' (eye).
original_explanation: This is your 'tita' at a family gathering who will notice your 1-kilo weight gain, your new pimple, and the fact that you're wearing the same shirt from last Christmas. It's also the security guard who can spot a shoplifter in a crowd, or your friend who can find the last available parking spot in a full mall lot. They miss nothing.
usage_notes: Used to describe someone's keen sense of observation, not necessarily their literal eyesight quality.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Matalas ang mata** ng aking lola; nakita niya agad ang nawawala kong hikaw.","translation":"My grandmother is **sharp-eyed**; she immediately saw my missing earring."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong maging **matalas ang mata** kung ikaw ay isang imbestigador.","translation":"You need to be **observant** if you are an investigator."}]

translation: to criticize, to find fault with
meaning_filipino: Paghahanap o pagbanggit ng mali, kapintasan, o depekto sa isang tao, bagay, o gawa.
original_explanation: The national sport of Marites and judgmental titas. It's when you look at someone's work, OOTD, or life choice and your first instinct is to say, "Okay, but..." or "Maganda sana, kaya lang..." It's fault-finding, but make it a hobby.
usage_notes: This is the action of pointing out flaws ('pintas'). The object being criticized is often marked with 'ang' or 'ng'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pintasan** ang gawa ng iba kung hindi ka naman tutulong.","translation":"Don't **criticize** the work of others if you're not going to help."},{"sentence":"Lagi na lang niya pinipintasan ang aking pananamit.","translation":"She always **finds fault** with my clothes."}]

translation: to photograph; to take a picture of (object-focused)
meaning_filipino: Kunan ng larawan ang isang partikular na tao o bagay. Ang diin ay nasa mismong paksa ng larawan.
original_explanation: Similar to 'ritratuhan', but with more focus on the subject. Think of it as the 'object-focused' version. "Sino ang gusto mong **ritratuhin** ko? Yung aso o yung pusa?" It's about singling out the subject to be photographed.
usage_notes: The suffix '-in' focuses the action on a specific object. So, 'ritratuhin' means to make something the direct subject of the picture-taking.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **ritratuhin** ang paglubog ng araw sa Manila Bay.","translation":"I want **to take a picture of** the sunset at Manila Bay."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **ritratuhin**, hindi pa ako nagsusuklay!","translation":"Don't **take a picture of** me, I haven't combed my hair yet!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng latigo na ang pangunahing sangkap ay yari sa pinatuyong balat ng hayop o katad.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng "latigo" (mula sa Espanyol na "látigo") at "balat".
original_explanation: The premium version of the `latigo`. It's not just any whip; it's the kind made of leather, for that extra *sting* and classic aesthetic. Think Indiana Jones, but make it Divisoria.
usage_notes: Isang tiyak na uri ng latigo na binibigyang-diin ang materyal na gawa sa katad.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang antigong **latigong balat** ay nakasabit sa pader ng museo.","translation":"The antique **leather whip** was hung on the museum wall."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtanggap ng responsibilidad o pagkakaroon ng pananagutan para sa isang kilos, desisyon, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you're the team lead and the project fails. It's you, in front of the boss, explaining why the deadline was missed. Basically, 'ikaw ang haharap.' It's the adulting version of your mom asking 'Sino'ng gumawa nito?!' and you can't blame your sibling anymore.
usage_notes: This implies a formal or serious responsibility. The root 'sagot' means 'answer'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga may-sala ay dapat **managot** sa batas.","translation":"The guilty ones must **be held accountable** before the law."},{"sentence":"Bilang lider, handa siyang **managot** sa anumang pagkukulang ng kanyang grupo.","translation":"As a leader, he is ready **to be accountable** for any shortcomings of his group."}]

translation: act of showing affection; caress; fondness
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita ng pagmamahal, paggiliw, o pagkagusto sa isang tao o hayop sa pamamagitan ng malumanay na salita, haplos, o kilos.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "pa-cute" move. It's when you talk in a slightly higher pitch to your jowa to ask for a favor, or when you snuggle up to your mom after messing up. It's the weapon of choice for getting what you want, powered by sweetness. Your cat is a master of this right before feeding time.
usage_notes: A very common cultural concept in the Philippines, denoting a specific way of showing affection that is often gentle, sweet, and sometimes mildly persuasive.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napangiti siya sa **paglalambing** ng kanyang kasintahan.","translation":"He/She smiled at his/her partner's **show of affection**."},{"sentence":"Kahit gaano ako katanda, hindi nawawala ang **paglalambing** ko sa aking mga magulang.","translation":"No matter how old I get, my **act of showing fondness** to my parents never fades."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kasama sa trabaho sa loob ng iisang opisina o kumpanya.
original_explanation: Your 'work wife/husband/sibling'. The person you share coffee breaks, project deadlines, and office chismis with. They're the reason you either love or dread going to work on a Monday. The 'ka-' prefix means 'fellow' or 'co-', so it's your 'co-office' person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Anna ang paborito kong **kaopisina** dahil lagi siyang may dalang pagkain.","translation":"Anna is my favorite **officemate** because she always brings food."},{"sentence":"Nag-ambagan ang mga **kaopisina** para sa kanyang despedida party.","translation":"The **colleagues** chipped in for his/her farewell party."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salita na hiniram o kinuha mula sa ibang wika at inangkop sa wikang Filipino.
etymology: Isang tambalang salita mula sa "salita" (word) at "hiram" (borrow).
original_explanation: These are the "imported goods" of the Filipino language. Words we borrowed from Spanish (like 'silya', 'mesa'), English ('kompyuter', 'basketbol'), Chinese ('siopao', 'pansit'), and more. We loved them so much, we decided to keep them and give them a Filipino citizenship. It's like your friend who borrows your charger and it becomes theirs over time.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa mga talakayang pangwika at akademiko. Maraming salitang-hiram ang naging pangkaraniwan na sa puntong hindi na itinuturing na banyaga.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang salitang 'tsismis' ay isang **salitang-hiram** mula sa wikang Espanyol na 'chismes'.","translation":"The word 'tsismis' is a **loanword** from the Spanish word 'chismes'."},{"sentence":"Marami tayong **salitang-hiram** sa Ingles, lalo na sa larangan ng teknolohiya.","translation":"We have many **loanwords** from English, especially in the field of technology."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan kumakain ang mga tao, tulad ng restawran o karinderya. Maaari ring tumukoy sa mga gamit sa pagkain tulad ng plato, kutsara, at tinidor.
etymology: From `pag-` + `kain` + `-an` (denoting a place or object used for the action).
original_explanation: This can be two things. 1) The place where you eat, from the fancy resto in BGC to the turo-turo stall in the palengke. 2) The actual plates, spoons, and forks you use. So when your mom says 'Ilabas mo ang pagkainan,' she could mean 'Set the table' or 'Let's go to the eatery,' depending on her tone and if she's holding her purse.
usage_notes: Context is crucial to distinguish between 'eatery' and 'dining set'. `Pagkainan sa labas` specifically refers to eating out or an outdoor eatery.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming masarap na **pagkainan** sa Maginhawa Street.","translation":"There are many delicious **eateries** on Maginhawa Street."},{"sentence":"Itago mo na ang mga **pagkainan** pagkatapos mong hugasan.","translation":"Put away the **dining set** after you wash them."},{"sentence":"Niyaya niya akong kumain sa isang **pagkainan** sa labas.","translation":"He invited me to eat at an **eatery** outside."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapatala ng sariling pangalan o ng iba sa isang opisyal na listahan para sa isang tiyak na layunin.
original_explanation: This is what you do for everything in the Philippines. To get 'ayuda'? Magpalista sa barangay. To join a Zumba class? Magpalista. To get a discount at the grocery? Magpalista for the loyalty card. It's the act of getting your name on "the list," which is the first step to almost any bureaucratic or social process here.
usage_notes: A causative verb where the subject causes their own name (or someone else's) to be added to a list.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumila siya nang maaga para **magpalista** sa libreng bakuna.","translation":"She lined up early **to register** for the free vaccine."},{"sentence":"Gusto kong **magpalista** sa fun run sa susunod na buwan.","translation":"I want **to sign up** for the fun run next month."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi tumutugma sa tamang tono o nota sa musika o pag-awit; wala sa tamang sintunado.
original_explanation: Para kang kaibigan mong confident kumanta sa videoke pero lahat ng nota, sinasabayan niya ng sarili niyang version. Sintunado, wala sa tono. Ito yung dahilan kung bakit may 'mute' button sa remote ng TV. 'Friend, **disintonado** ka, next time paki-minus one na lang yung boses mo.'
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng musika at pag-awit. Ang katumbas nitong salita ay 'sintunado'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Medyo **disintonado** ang kanta niya kaya mababa ang nakuha niyang puntos.","translation":"His singing was a bit **out of tune** so he got a low score."},{"sentence":"Paki-tono nga 'yang gitara, **disintonado** na.","translation":"Please tune that guitar, it's already **out of tune**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagdaramit ng kasuotan sa katawan.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you're getting ready for a date, work, or just lounging at home. It's the action of putting on clothes, shoes, or even your 'game face.' 'Bes, anong isusuot ko sa party mamaya?' is the eternal question. It's not just about covering your body, it's about making a statement, or sometimes, just finding the least crumpled shirt in your closet.
usage_notes: The prefix 'i-' indicates that the object being worn is the focus of the sentence. Contrast with 'magsuot' where the actor is the focus. 'Isuot mo ang sapatos' (Wear the shoes) vs. 'Magsuot ka ng sapatos' (You wear shoes).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Isuot** mo ang paborito mong damit para sa iyong kaarawan.","translation":"**Wear** your favorite dress for your birthday."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **isuot** ang iyong salamin bago magbasa.","translation":"Don't forget to **wear** your glasses before reading."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang anumang dumi, mantsa, o kalat. Sa matalinhagang kahulugan, ito ay nangangahulugang dalisay o walang bahid ng kasamaan.
original_explanation: Yung kwarto mo after general cleaning, malinis for about 5 minutes. Also, malinis ang konsensya ng taong hindi nang-seen-zone. The rest of us? Messy.
usage_notes: Isang napakakaraniwang pang-uri na may parehong literal (malinis) at matalinghagang (dalisay, malinis na rekord) kahulugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Panatilihing **malinis** ang kapaligiran upang makaiwas sa sakit.","translation":"Keep the surroundings **clean** to avoid sickness."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa pagkakaroon ng **malinis** na pangalan sa politika.","translation":"He is known for having a **clean** name in politics."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng hindi pag-aasikaso, hindi pag-aalaga, o pagwawalang-bahala sa isang tungkulin, tao, o bagay.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you 'bahala na' your responsibilities. It's leaving your group project mates on 'seen', ignoring your plants until they're crispy, or forgetting to pay your bills. The ultimate 'I'll do it later' that turns into 'Oops, I never did it.'
usage_notes: Carries a strong negative connotation of irresponsibility.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapabaya** sa pag-aaral ay nagdulot ng mababang marka.","translation":"**Negligence** in studies resulted in low grades."},{"sentence":"Sinampahan siya ng kaso dahil sa **pagpapabaya** sa kanyang mga anak.","translation":"A case was filed against him for **neglecting** his children."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtalo, pagsupil, o pagpapasuko sa isang kaaway o hadlang sa pamamagitan ng lakas.
etymology: From pag- (nominalizing prefix) + lupig (to conquer, to vanquish).
original_explanation: Think of it as the ultimate 'sana all' in a competition. It's not just winning; it's total domination. It's what Lapu-Lapu did to Magellan, what your mom does to your arguments, or what your team does in Mobile Legends when it's a 20-0 wipeout. It's the act of making someone 'umiyak sa pighati.'
usage_notes: A strong, often historical or literary term used to denote complete victory or subjugation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paglupig** sa mga mananakop ay isang mahalagang kabanata sa ating kasaysayan.","translation":"The **conquest** of the colonizers is an important chapter in our history."},{"sentence":"Ang **paglupig** sa sariling kahinaan ang tunay na tagumpay.","translation":"The **subjugation** of one's own weakness is the true victory."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paraan ng pagsalakay sa isang pader o kuta sa pamamagitan ng pag-akyat gamit ang mga hagdan.
original_explanation: This is some serious 'Game of Thrones' or 'Lord of the Rings' level stuff. Imagine trying to climb a castle wall with a ladder while people are throwing stuff at you. That's eskilada. It's the ultimate 'akyat-bahay' but for castles.
usage_notes: Isang napaka-espesipikong terminong militar na karaniwang matatagpuan sa mga aklat pangkasaysayan o piksyon. Hindi ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nabigo ang planong **eskilada** ng mga mananakop dahil sa matibay na depensa ng kuta.","translation":"The invaders' plan for a **siege by scaling** failed due to the fort's strong defense."}]

translation: is dying; is at the point of death
meaning_filipino: Nasa bingit ng kamatayan; malapit nang malagutan ng hininga.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'malapit na mag-log out sa Earth.' It's that dramatic scene in a teleserye where the dying patriarch is trying to say who gets the mana. Figuratively, it's your WiFi connection during a storm, your phone at 1% battery, or your will to work on a Friday afternoon. It's on its last breath.
usage_notes: A very evocative and serious word. The 'hi-' reduplication indicates the present progressive tense. Often used for living beings, but can be used figuratively for inanimate objects or concepts that are failing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nadatnan nilang **naghihingalo** na ang matandang maysakit.","translation":"They arrived to find the sick old man already **dying**."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam ko ay **naghihingalo** na ang laptop ko sa sobrang dami ng tabs.","translation":"I feel like my laptop is **dying** because of too many tabs."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapanatili ng katatagan o timbang upang hindi matumba; ang pagtutugma o pagpapantay ng dalawang magkaibang bagay.
original_explanation: The struggle of every BPO agent trying to juggle work, life, and 3 hours of sleep. It's trying to walk on a wet floor without slipping, or trying to make your 13th-month pay last until January 1st. The ultimate adulting skill.
usage_notes: Used for both literal physical balance and figurative balance, like in finances ('balance the budget') or life ('work-life balance').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **magbalanse** sa isang paa habang nakapikit.","translation":"It's difficult to **balance** on one foot while your eyes are closed."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magbalanse** ng iyong oras sa pag-aaral at paglalaro.","translation":"You need to **balance** your time between studying and playing."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bansa sa hilagang-silangang Aprika na kilala sa mga sinaunang sibilisasyon nito, kabilang ang mga piramide at ang Ilog Nilo.
original_explanation: The country. Pyramids, mummies, pharaohs, the Nile river. That's Ehipto. It's on everyone's bucket list for travel.
usage_notes: Laging nagsisimula sa malaking titik dahil ito ay isang pangngalang pantangi (proper noun).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais kong makarating sa **Ehipto** upang makita ang mga piramide.","translation":"I want to go to **Egypt** to see the pyramids."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbebenta o ang kabuuang halaga ng mga produkto o serbisyong naibenta sa isang tiyak na panahon.
original_explanation: The hustle. The grind. The number one topic sa GC ng mga online seller. "Kumusta benta natin today, sis?" Whether you're selling lumpia, pre-loved clothes, or insurance, the goal is always to have good benta. Pag mataas ang benta, may pang-Starbucks. Pag mababa, tubeg is life.
usage_notes: Maaari ring gamitin bilang pandiwa ('ibenta', 'magbenta').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malakas ang **benta** ng mga palamig ngayong tag-init.","translation":"The **sales** of cold drinks are high this summer."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating maabot ang ating quota sa **benta** para sa buwang ito.","translation":"We need to reach our **sales** quota for this month."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mamamayan ng sinaunang kaharian ng Israel; isang inapo ni Jacob.
original_explanation: The OG people from the Bible stories you learned in Sunday school. Think Moses, David, and the folks who crossed the Red Sea. They're the ancestors of the Jewish people, the main characters of the Old Testament. Not to be confused with modern-day Israelis, although there's an overlap.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa mga kontekstong pangkasaysayan o panrelihiyon. Ang modernong termino para sa isang mamamayan ng Israel ay 'Israeli'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinangunahan ni Moises ang mga **Israelita** palabas ng Ehipto.","translation":"Moses led the **Israelites** out of Egypt."},{"sentence":"Ang Sampung Utos ay ibinigay sa mga **Israelita** sa Bundok Sinai.","translation":"The Ten Commandments were given to the **Israelites** at Mount Sinai."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang magbigay ng testimonya o pahayag bilang saksi sa isang pangyayari, lalo na sa isang paglilitis o pormal na imbestigasyon.
original_explanation: This is what the 'Marites' of the neighborhood does, but in a formal setting like a courtroom or a barangay hearing. You're not just 'nakakita' (saw), you're officially 'nanaksi' (testifying). It's leveling up from chismis to a legal statement.
usage_notes: Has a strong legal or formal connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumayag siyang **manaksi** sa korte laban sa akusado.","translation":"He agreed **to testify** in court against the accused."}]

translation: had a snack; ate as a snack
meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na salita para sa kilos ng pagkain ng meryenda na naganap sa nakalipas na panahon.
etymology: A colloquial/slang past-tense form derived from the Spanish loanword 'merienda' (snack). The standard Tagalog form is 'nagmerienda' or 'mineryenda'.
original_explanation: This is the past tense of 'nag-meryenda,' but with a creative twist. It's like you didn't just have a snack, you *conquered* it. You didn't just eat the turon, you `minandal` it. Sounds more action-packed, like something a tito would say to sound cool. 'Anong minandal niyo?' 'Pancit canton, tito.'
usage_notes: Highly informal and colloquial. Not used in formal writing. It's a creative verb form of 'meryenda'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Aba, naubos n'yo na pala! Ano'ng **minandal** ninyo?","translation":"Wow, you finished it already! What snack **did you eat**?"},{"sentence":"**Minandal** lang namin yung natirang spaghetti kagabi.","translation":"We just **ate** the leftover spaghetti from last night **as a snack**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa mabuting kalagayan ng pag-iisip o damdamin; hindi galit o iritado; kalmado.
etymology: Literally 'the head is good.' An idiomatic expression.
original_explanation: When your boss is like this, it's the perfect time to ask for a raise or file for that vacation leave. When your mom is like this, pwedeng humingi ng extra baon. It means the coast is clear, no 'sungay' (horns) are showing, and the emotional weather forecast is sunny.
usage_notes: The opposite is 'masama ang ulo' (in a bad mood) or 'mainit ang ulo' (angry, literally 'hot-headed').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mukhang **mabuti ang ulo** ng boss natin ngayon, aprubado lahat ng request.","translation":"It looks like our boss is **in a good mood** today, all requests were approved."},{"sentence":"Kausapin mo siya kapag **mabuti ang ulo** para hindi kayo mag-away.","translation":"Talk to him when he is **clear-headed** so you won't fight."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagkakalat ng binhi sa lupa upang tumubo. Sa matalinhagang paraan, ito ay ang pagpapalaganap ng isang ideya, balita, o damdamin.
etymology: From 'hasik' (sow). 'Pag-ha-hasik' is the act of sowing or spreading.
original_explanation: Literally, it's what farmers do with seeds. Figuratively, it’s what Marites does with chismis. It's spreading anything from good vibes to fake news. 'Paghahasik ng lagim' (sowing terror) is a classic teleserye villain move.
usage_notes: Often used metaphorically, sometimes with negative connotations (e.g., spreading fear, lies, discord).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paghahasik** ng palay ay dapat gawin sa tamang panahon.","translation":"The **sowing** of rice seeds must be done at the right time."},{"sentence":"Itigil na ninyo ang **paghahasik** ng maling impormasyon sa social media.","translation":"Stop the **spreading** of false information on social media."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing kumislap o magningning na parang bituin ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the more fabulous cousin of 'pakintabin'. While 'pakintabin' is for floors and shoes, 'pakislapin' is for jewelry, Christmas lights, and a beauty queen's eyes. It's adding that extra ✨bling✨ and ✨sparkle✨. Think of it as the verb form of a KiraKira filter.
usage_notes: Implies a more intense, glittering shine compared to 'pakintabin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto niyang **pakislapin** ang kanyang mga alahas bago ang party.","translation":"She wants to **make** her jewelry **sparkle** before the party."},{"sentence":"Ang mga palamuti ay sapat na upang **pakislapin** ang buong silid.","translation":"The decorations are enough to **make** the whole room **glitter**."}]

translation: to be able to get loose; to be able to escape
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang makalaya mula sa pagkakagapos, pagkakakulong, o isang mahirap na sitwasyon.
etymology: From `makaka-` (future ability prefix) + `wala` (in the context of `kawala` or being loose/free).
original_explanation: This is for your aso who keeps getting off its leash, or for you trying to escape a boring family reunion. It’s the verb for freedom, whether it's from a literal cage, a 'toxic' relationship, or a mountain of debt. 'Kailan kaya ako makakawala sa mga utang ko?'
usage_notes: This is the future tense. `Nakawala` is past tense, `nakakawala` is present tense. It implies breaking free from a restraint.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itali mong mabuti ang aso para hindi **makakawala**.","translation":"Tie the dog securely so it won't be **able to get loose**."},{"sentence":"Umaasa siyang **makakawala** siya sa mahirap na buhay.","translation":"He hopes he **will be able to escape** from his difficult life."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na sadyang hindi papasok sa isipan na gawin o mangyari; hindi kailanman gagawin o aalalahanin.
original_explanation: This is your brain's "seen-zone" for bad ideas. It's that "hard pass" you give to drama, extra work on a Friday, or replying to an ex's 2 AM message. "Mag-cheat sa exam? Hindi iisipin."
usage_notes: Often used to express a strong refusal or a moral boundary. It implies something is so out of the question, it's not even worth considering.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hindi iisipin** ng isang tunay na kaibigan na traydurin ka.","translation":"A true friend **would not think of** betraying you."},{"sentence":"Ang saktan ang kanyang mga anak ay isang bagay na **hindi iisipin** ng isang ina.","translation":"Hurting her children is something a mother **would never think of**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang may pinakamataas na antas ng lakas na pisikal, impluwensya, o puwersa.
original_explanation: This is the person who wins the arm-wrestling match every time, the typhoon that requires you to stock up on canned goods, or the coffee that keeps you awake for 24 hours straight. It's the ultimate measure of force or impact. Ang **pinakamalakas** na kape ang kailangan ko ngayon.
usage_notes: Refers to strength, force, intensity, or influence. Homonymous with 'pinakamalakas' (loudest).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **pinakamalakas** na boksingero sa kanyang henerasyon.","translation":"He is the **strongest** boxer of his generation."},{"sentence":"Ang Bagyong Yolanda ay isa sa **pinakamalakas** na bagyong tumama sa Pilipinas.","translation":"Typhoon Yolanda is one of the **strongest** typhoons to hit the Philippines."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang likidong nagmumula sa mga glandula sa bibig na tumutulong sa pagtunaw ng pagkain at pagpapanatiling basa ng bibig.
original_explanation: The stuff that comes out of your mouth when you see your crush or a picture of crispy pata. Also, what you secretly wipe off your pillow in the morning. "Naglalaway ako sa lechon!"
usage_notes: 'Takam' is the feeling of craving that causes one to salivate. 'Drool' is often translated as 'tulo-laway'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumutulo ang **laway** ng aso habang hinihintay ang pagkain niya.","translation":"The dog's **saliva** is dripping while it waits for its food."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa posisyong nakaharap o nakatuon ang mukha sa isang ibabaw, karaniwan ay sa lupa o sa mesa.
etymology: From `subsob` (the act of plunging face first). `Naka-` indicates the resulting state.
original_explanation: Picture this: Lunes, 8 AM, nasa office ka na pero 'di pa nag-kick in yung kape. Yung ulo mo, dahan-dahang bumabagsak sa keyboard. 'Yan, **nakasubsob** ka na. O kaya yung pagod na pagod ka na sa buhay, gusto mo na lang dumapa sa kama at i-face plant sa unan.
usage_notes: Describes a state or position. Can imply exhaustion, sleep, drunkenness, or even death.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natagpuan siyang **nakasubsob** sa kanyang mesa, marahil ay nakatulog dahil sa pagod.","translation":"He was found **face down** on his desk, probably having fallen asleep from exhaustion."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng party, may mga lasing na **nakasubsob** na sa sahig.","translation":"After the party, there were drunk people lying **prone** on the floor."}]

translation: to send a telegram; to wire a message
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapadala ng mensahe sa pamamagitan ng telegrapo, gamit ang mga kable o kawad.
original_explanation: Okay, boomer alert! Ito 'yung original version ng pag-send ng DM or PM. Before fiber internet, mayroong literal na 'kawad' (wire). You'd go to a telegraph office to **magpahatid-kawad** of a short message, usually for emergencies. It's the ancestor of your chat apps.
usage_notes: This term is now largely historical and obsolete, referring to the technology of the telegraph.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Noong unang panahon, kailangan mong **magpahatid-kawad** para sa mabilisang komunikasyon.","translation":"In the old days, you needed to **send a telegram** for urgent communication."},{"sentence":"**Nagpahatid-kawad** siya sa kanyang pamilya sa probinsya upang ipaalam ang kanyang pagdating.","translation":"He **wired a message** to his family in the province to inform them of his arrival."}]

translation: to have news announced or spread
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos na ipaalam o ikalat ang isang impormasyon o pangyayari sa maraming tao, kadalasan sa pamamagitan ng midya o usap-usapan.
etymology: From the causative prefix "ipa-" and "balita" (news), which is derived from Sanskrit "vārttā".
original_explanation: The analog version of 'make this go viral.' Before social media, you'd ask the town crier or the local Marites to **ipabalita** something. Now, it's more like asking a media outlet to cover a story, or just telling your friend with a big mouth. '**Ipabalita** mo na engaged na kami!'
usage_notes: Can be for formal announcements (e.g., on TV Patrol) or for informal gossip (chismis).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan ng hari ang kanyang mga kawal na **ipabalita** sa buong kaharian ang kanyang pagbabalik.","translation":"The king ordered his soldiers **to have the news of his return announced** throughout the kingdom."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo munang **ipabalita** ang nangyari hangga't hindi pa kumpirmado.","translation":"Don't **have what happened spread as news** yet until it's confirmed."}]

translation: to match, to equal, to compensate
meaning_filipino: Magbigay ng katumbas o kapantay na halaga, gantimpala, o parusa para sa isang bagay o gawa.
original_explanation: It's like finding the perfect pair or equivalent. When you give 100% effort sa work, you expect your sahod to 'tumbasan' that effort. Or when your friend treats you to lunch, 'tutumbasan' mo by treating them to coffee. It's all about balance and reciprocity, parang 'what you give is what you get.'
usage_notes: The '-an' suffix makes it an object-focused verb, meaning 'to apply the root action to something'. The actor-focus form is 'tumumbas'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paano mo **tutumbasan** ang pagmamahal na ibinigay ng iyong mga magulang?","translation":"How will you **match** the love given by your parents?"},{"sentence":"Kailangang **tumbasan** ng kumpanya ang pinsalang idinulot nito sa kalikasan.","translation":"The company needs to **compensate** for the damage it caused to the environment."}]

translation: to sell bottles; to gather and sell used bottles
meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pangongolekta at pagbebenta ng mga gamit nang bote, karaniwan para sa maliit na kita o bilang paraan ng pagreresiklo.
original_explanation: This is the OG side hustle. Before online selling, there was "magbote." It's the act of collecting empty bottles (usually beer or soft drink bottles) and selling them to the junk shop or the roving "dyaryo, bote, bakal" guy for some extra cash. It’s sustainability and entrepreneurship rolled into one noisy, clanking kariton.
usage_notes: Often associated with junk shops ("dyaryo-bote-bakal") and recycling for a small income.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para may pambili ng bigas, **nagbote** muna si Mang Kanor.","translation":"To have money to buy rice, Mang Kanor first **gathered and sold bottles**."},{"sentence":"Ipunin mo 'yang mga bote, baka pwedeng i-**magbote** para may extra kang pera.","translation":"Collect those bottles, you might be able to **sell them** for extra money."}]

translation: to shelter; to protect; to give refuge
meaning_filipino: Magbigay ng proteksyon o silungan laban sa panganib, ulan, o init; kupkupin o itago ang isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: `Magkanlong` is what you do when you see a stray cat during a storm and you let it stay on your porch. It's offering a safe space, a temporary shield. It’s what a big payong does for a group of friends, or what a good friend does for you when you need to hide from your responsibilities for a while.
usage_notes: Implies providing cover or concealment, either literally from the elements or figuratively from danger or trouble.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang malaking puno ng akasya ang nagsilbing lugar kung saan sila **nagkanlong** mula sa init ng araw.","translation":"The large acacia tree served as the place where they **took shelter** from the heat of the sun."},{"sentence":"Ipinagbabawal na **magkanlong** ng mga kriminal sa ilalim ng batas.","translation":"It is forbidden by law **to harbor** criminals."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paraan ng pagkain na mabilis, magulo, at parang hayop na sumusubsob sa pagkain.
original_explanation: This is how you eat when you're 'gutom na gutom' and the food finally arrives. It's eating with zero chill, like a pig at a trough. No more 'pa-demure'. Your face is practically in the bowl. Think 'unli-rice' challenges or that one cousin at the fiesta who piles their plate to the sky. That's 'sumasabsab'.
usage_notes: Almost always used in a derogatory or informal way to describe messy or voracious eating. The verb form is 'sumabsab' or 'sabsabin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **sumabsab** ng pagkain, para kang hindi kumain ng isang linggo.","translation":"Don't **gobble** your food, you look like you haven't eaten in a week."},{"sentence":"Pinanood niya ang mga baboy na **sumasabsab** sa kanilang labangan.","translation":"He watched the pigs **eating greedily** from their trough."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan na partikular na ginagamit sa paghahanda o pagpapakulo ng kape.
original_explanation: The most important appliance for any BPO agent, student pulling an all-nighter, or anyone who believes "adulting is hard." Whether it's a fancy espresso machine or a simple coffee press, this is the holy grail that turns grumpy zombies into semi-functional human beings every morning.
usage_notes: A specific phrase for a coffee-making appliance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sira ang aming **lutuan ng kape**, kaya instant muna tayo.","translation":"Our **coffee maker** is broken, so we'll have instant for now."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na tawag sa isang malapit na kaibigang lalaki; katumbas ng 'pare' o 'tropa'.
etymology: Likely a playful alteration of 'batchoy' (the noodle soup), used as a term of endearment, combined with the prefix 'ka-' (partner/companion).
original_explanation: Your 'bro', your 'dude', your 'pare'. The person you can send the ugliest selfies to without judgment. Sila yung kasama mong kumain ng batchoy (the food) or just chill. It's a term of endearment that sounds like a delicious noodle soup, because maybe true friendship is just as comforting.
usage_notes: An informal, slang term for a close male friend. Similar to 'tropa' or 'barkada'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uy, **kabatsoy**, kamusta na? Tagal nating hindi nagkita!","translation":"Hey, **buddy**, how are you? We haven't seen each other in a while!"},{"sentence":"Inuman tayo mamaya kasama ang mga **kabatsoy**.","translation":"Let's go for a drink later with the **pals**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagbibigay ng tulong, lalo na sa anyong pinansyal, sa isang tao o institusyon.
original_explanation: Your sugar daddy/mommy, but for a good cause. The rich tita/tito who funds your education, sponsors an orphanage, or donates to the church. They're the silent heroes in teleseryes who suddenly appear to save the protagonist from poverty. The OG "sponsor."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang hindi nagpakilalang **benepaktor** ang nag-abot ng malaking donasyon.","translation":"An anonymous **benefactor** gave a large donation."},{"sentence":"Siya ang naging **benepaktor** ng maraming mahihirap na mag-aaral.","translation":"He became the **benefactor** of many poor students."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pakiramdam ng pag-aatubili, pag-aalangan, o pagkailang na sanhi ng kamalayan sa kung ano ang iisipin ng iba; pagpapakumbaba o kawalan ng kompiyansa.
original_explanation: The core Filipino social emotion. It's that feeling that stops you from getting the last piece of lumpia, singing karaoke first, or telling your crush you like them. It's a complex mix of shyness, shame, and saving face. "Wala ka bang hiya?" is a top-tier parental insult.
usage_notes: A very important cultural concept in the Philippines, governing social interactions and preserving one's 'face'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa **hiya**, hindi niya inamin ang kanyang pagkakamali.","translation":"Because of **shame**, he did not admit his mistake."},{"sentence":"Nawala ang aking **hiya** nang kailangan kong magsalita sa harap ng maraming tao.","translation":"My **shyness** disappeared when I had to speak in front of many people."}]

translation: to have one's honor stained; to be defiled
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkasira o pagkawala ng dangal, karangalan, o malinis na pangalan ng isang tao, lalo na sa dating konteksto ng sekswal na integridad ng isang babae.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'na-scam' feeling in old Filipino movies. It's when a person's reputation, especially a woman's 'chastity,' is ruined. This phrase is straight out of a classic teleserye drama where the bida cries in the rain after being wronged.
usage_notes: A very dramatic and somewhat dated phrase, often found in literature and film. It carries a heavy, serious connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa mga lumang nobela, ang pinakamalaking takot ng isang dalaga ay ang **marungisan ang puri**.","translation":"In old novels, a maiden's greatest fear is **to have her honor stained**."}]

translation: to drive; to manage, to handle
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapatakbo o pagkontrol sa isang sasakyan; ang pangangasiwa o pag-aasikaso sa isang sitwasyon, gawain, o tao.
original_explanation: The action version of 'maneho.' It means to take the wheel, literally or figuratively. You can 'manehohin' a jeepney through EDSA traffic, or you can 'manehohin' a difficult client at work. It's about being in control and directing the outcome. 'Kaya mo bang manehohin ang tatlong projects nang sabay-sabay?' (Can you handle three projects at once?)
usage_notes: A versatile verb used for both driving a vehicle and managing a situation or task.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **manehohin** nang maingat ang kotse dahil madulas ang daan.","translation":"You need to **drive** the car carefully because the road is slippery."},{"sentence":"Siya ang naatasang **manehohin** ang buong kumpanya habang wala ang CEO.","translation":"He was tasked to **manage** the entire company while the CEO was away."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi malinis; may dumi, alikabok, o anumang bagay na nagdudulot ng karumihan.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'ma-' (mayroon) at salitang-ugat na 'dumi'.
original_explanation: The state of your bedroom floor when you haven't cleaned it in a month. It's the opposite of 'malinis.' Can be literal (a dirty shirt) or figurative, like 'maruming pulitika' (dirty politics) or 'maruming isip' (dirty mind). It's the reason your mom is always telling you to wash your hands.
usage_notes: 'Madumi' is a very common colloquial variation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Labhan mo na 'yang damit mo dahil **marumi** na.","translation":"Wash your clothes now because they are already **dirty**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-isip ng **marumi** sa kapwa mo.","translation":"Don't have **dirty** thoughts about your fellow person."}]

translation: to hurry up; to speed up
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapabilis sa isang kilos, gawain, o proseso; gawing mas mabilis.
original_explanation: The official command of anyone who is "Filipino time" intolerant. Your mom yells "Bilisan mo!" when you're getting ready for school. Your friend texts "Bilisan n'yo, nandito na 'ko!" when they arrive first. It's the verb form of panic and impatience. It means "Hurry up!" or "Step on it!".
usage_notes: A command or a request to increase speed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bilisan** mo ang paglalakad, male-late na tayo!","translation":"**Hurry up** your walking, we're going to be late!"},{"sentence":"Kailangang **bilisan** ang proyekto para maabot ang deadline.","translation":"The project needs to be **sped up** to meet the deadline."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang taong maramdamin, madaling masaktan o magtampo sa mga biro o puna.
etymology: From 'balat' (skin) and 'sibuyas' (onion). Refers to the thinness of an onion's skin.
original_explanation: You know that friend who cries over everything? 'Yung konting asar lang, "I hate you na!" agad? Sila 'yun. They have feelings as thin as an onion skin. One wrong comment and the waterworks start, just like when you're chopping onions. Handle with care, or you'll get the tears.
usage_notes: A very common idiom to describe an overly sensitive person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo siyang biruin nang ganyan, **balat-sibuyas** 'yan.","translation":"Don't joke with her like that, she's very **sensitive**."},{"sentence":"Naging **balat-sibuyas** siya mula nang magkaroon ng problema.","translation":"He became **touchy** ever since he had problems."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkilos o pag-usad nang may matinding bilis, tulad ng isang mabilis na sasakyan o hangin.
original_explanation: 'Yung motor na dumaan sa tabi mo na parang may hinahabol na multo. O 'yung sweldo mo, dumaan lang, **humagibis** paalis ng wallet mo. Gone in 60 seconds. Ayan, tapos na, wala na.
usage_notes: Often used in literature or for dramatic effect to emphasize extreme speed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Humagibis** ang sports car sa kahabaan ng highway.","translation":"The sports car **sped** along the highway."},{"sentence":"Parang **humagibis** ang oras, uwian na pala.","translation":"It seems like time **whizzed** by, it's already time to go home."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salansan o tumpok ng mga bagay na magkakapatong, karaniwan ay nakaayos nang maayos.
original_explanation: That's what your laundry looks like before you finally decide to fold it—a 'kamada' of clothes. Or the stack of papers on your desk that you keep telling yourself you'll organize "tomorrow." It's organized chaos in noun form.
usage_notes: Often used for things like wood, bricks, sacks of rice, or papers.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **kamada** ng kahoy ang nakatambak sa likod-bahay.","translation":"A **pile** of wood is stacked in the backyard."},{"sentence":"Pakiayos ang **kamada** ng mga libro sa estante.","translation":"Please arrange the **stack** of books on the shelf."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalaman o may angking katangian, kakayahan, o bagay.
original_explanation: This is a more formal, almost poetic way of saying 'may' or 'has'. You don't just 'have' beauty, you are 'maytaglay ng ganda' (endowed with beauty). It’s not that the anting-anting 'has' power, it is 'maytaglay ng kapangyarihan' (possessing of power). It elevates the simple act of having something to a state of being. It's the résumé word for 'has'.
usage_notes: Often written as two words: "may taglay". The single word form "maytaglay" is more literary or formal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay isang babaeng **maytaglay** ng pambihirang talino.","translation":"She is a woman **possessing** extraordinary intelligence."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang institusyon para sa pagtuturo sa mga mag-aaral sa ilalim ng direksyon ng mga guro. Kasingkahulugan ng paaralan.
original_explanation: This is the old-school, Spanish-era term for 'school'. Think of what your lola would call your 'paaralan'. It has that vintage, historical vibe, like something you'd hear in a period drama. Not to be confused with 'eskuwela' which is more common.
usage_notes: A less common, more formal or historical synonym for 'paaralan' or 'eskuwelahan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga bata ay masayang nagtungo sa **espuwela**.","translation":"The children happily went to **school**."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang dumi, mantsa, o anumang bahid; malinis.
original_explanation: The state of your condo 5 minutes before your parents or a hot date arrives. It's that 'bagong-linis' smell, the shiny floor, the absence of 'kalat.' It's not just clean, it's *limpyo*—so clean you could probably eat off the floor, but please don't. From the Spanish 'limpio,' it's the conyo cousin of 'malinis.'
usage_notes: A common synonym for 'malinis'. Sometimes implies a more thorough or polished kind of cleanliness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siguraduhing **limpyo** ang kusina bago ka umalis.","translation":"Make sure the kitchen is **clean** before you leave."},{"sentence":"Gusto ko ang pakiramdam ng **limpyo** at bagong paligo.","translation":"I like the feeling of being **clean** and newly bathed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang babaeng testigo sa isang binyag, kumpil, o kasal na may tungkuling gabayan sa pananampalataya ang inaanak; ninang.
original_explanation: The more formal, Spanish-sounding version of 'Ninang'. She's the one who's supposed to be your spiritual guide but is more popularly known as the source of aguinaldo (cash gifts) during Christmas. She's a VIP at your baptism, confirmation, and wedding.
usage_notes: `Ninang` is far more common in everyday conversation. `Madrina` is used in more formal contexts or documents.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pangalan ng kanyang **madrina** ay nakasulat sa sertipiko ng binyag.","translation":"Her **godmother's** name is written on the baptismal certificate."},{"sentence":"Siya ang napili kong maging **madrina** sa aking kasal.","translation":"I chose her to be the **godmother** (matron of honor) at my wedding."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng marka, palatandaan, o ebidensya ng isang bagay na nangyari o dumaan.
original_explanation: This is the "CSI: Manila" phrase. You see it when you're trying to figure out who ate the last piece of leche flan. "May bakas ng daliri mo dito!" It can also be emotional, like when your friend is trying to act okay after a breakup but their smile "may bakas ng lungkot."
usage_notes: A common descriptive phrase.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**May bakas** ng putik ang sapatos niya kaya alam kong galing siya sa labas.","translation":"His shoes **had traces** of mud so I knew he came from outside."},{"sentence":"Kahit nakangiti siya, **may bakas** pa rin ng kalungkutan sa kanyang mga mata.","translation":"Even if she was smiling, her eyes still **showed signs** of sadness."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bayad para sa transportasyon o pag-upa ng sasakyan.
original_explanation: 'Yung perang inihahanda mo bago ka pa sumakay ng jeep, pero nagkukunwari kang naghahanap sa wallet kapag siningil na ni manong driver. "Bayad po!" is the magic phrase, and "sukli po sa bente" is the follow-up spell.
usage_notes: Primarily used for public transportation fare. 'Pamasahe' is the more common, native-sounding synonym. 'Plete' can also mean the fee for chartering or renting a whole vehicle.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkano na ngayon ang **plete** sa jeep?","translation":"How much is the jeepney **fare** now?"},{"sentence":"Siningil kami ng limang libo para sa **plete** ng van papuntang Baguio.","translation":"We were charged five thousand for the **rent** of the van to Baguio."}]

translation: to make (someone) tell the truth; to make (two things) face each other
meaning_filipino: Pilitin o himukin ang isang tao na sabihin ang katotohanan; pagharapin ang dalawang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'The truth will set you free... but first, I'll make you tell it' move. It’s what happens in a police interrogation room, or when your mom catches you and your sibling and says, 'Mag-usap kayo! Pagtapatin ko kaya kayo!' It's forcing a confrontation to get to the bottom of the 'chismis'.
usage_notes: This is a command or objective verb form. It has two main meanings: 1) To make someone be honest. 2) To align or make two things face each other directly.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng imbestigador na **pagtapatin** ang suspek tungkol sa kanyang nalalaman.","translation":"The investigator tried **to make the suspect tell the truth** about what he knew."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **pagtapatin** ang dalawang dulo ng kahoy para maging tuwid ang pagkakadikit.","translation":"You need **to make the two ends of the wood face each other** so they stick together straight."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkaramdam ng pighati, kawalan ng saya, o pagiging malungkot.
original_explanation: This is your everyday, standard-issue sadness. 'Yung na-seen ka lang, 'yung umorder ka ng chicken joy pero leg part ang dumating imbes na thigh, 'yung kinansela 'yung paborito mong series. It's the most common word for "sad."
usage_notes: Ang pinaka-pangkaraniwan at pangkalahatang termino para sa kalungkutan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nalulungkot** ako dahil hindi ako nakapasa sa pagsusulit.","translation":"I'm **sad** because I didn't pass the exam."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **malungkot**, nandito lang ako para sa'yo.","translation":"Don't be **sad**, I'm just here for you."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang huling resulta o kinalabasan ng isang serye ng mga pangyayari, gawain, o proseso.
etymology: From `ka-` + `hinatnan` (past form related to `hantong` 'to end up' or `datnan` 'to find upon arrival'). Often considered a nominal form of `kinahinatnan`.
original_explanation: The "so, what happened?" part of the story. It's the final score of the basketball game, the grade you get after a semester of puyat, or the ending of that K-drama you've been bingeing. It's the universe's way of showing you the receipt for your actions.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with `kinalabasan` or `resulta`. `Kinahinatnan` is also a common form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang naging **kahinatnan** ng kanilang pag-uusap?","translation":"What was the **outcome** of their conversation?"},{"sentence":"Ang pagbagsak niya sa pagsusulit ay ang **kahinatnan** ng kanyang katamaran.","translation":"Failing the exam was the **consequence** of his laziness."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagsasaliksik at paglalathala ng pribado at pagkakakilanlang impormasyon tungkol sa isang partikular na indibidwal sa internet, karaniwang may malisyosong layunin.
original_explanation: The act of being a super-Marites with evil intentions. Ito 'yung paghahanap at pag-post ng personal info ng iba online para ipahiya, takutin, o sirain sila. It's a form of cyberbullying and it's a crime, bes. Huwag tularan.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa mismong gawain. Ginagamit sa mga talakayan tungkol sa kaligtasan sa internet at online harassment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ilegal ang **doxxing** at maituturing na isang anyo ng cyberbullying.","translation":"**Doxxing** is illegal and can be considered a form of cyberbullying."},{"sentence":"Ang pagbabanta ng **doxxing** ay seryosong bagay na dapat i-report.","translation":"The threat of **doxxing** is a serious matter that should be reported."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na labis-labis kung kumain; maaari ring tumukoy sa isang tao na sakim o sobrang ganid sa yaman o kapangyarihan.
original_explanation: Two types: 1) The Foodie Glutton: The friend who says 'I'm full' but still gets a second plate at the buffet. They see 'unli-rice' as a personal challenge, not an option. 2) The Power Glutton: The politician or boss who wants everything for themselves, leaving nothing for others. Whether it's food or fortune, their mantra is 'Akin lang!' (Mine only!).
usage_notes: May dalawang kahulugan: matakaw sa pagkain, o sakim sa yaman/kapangyarihan. Ang konteksto ang naglilinaw ng kahulugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya bilang isang **taong masiba** dahil kaya niyang ubusin ang pagkain na para sa tatlong tao.","translation":"He is known as a **gluttonous person** because he can finish food meant for three people."},{"sentence":"Ang mga politikong korap ay mga **taong masiba** sa kapangyarihan at pera.","translation":"Corrupt politicians are **people greedy** for power and money."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na nasa murang edad o hindi pa matanda.
original_explanation: The adjective form of 'child'. It means young. "Mas bata siya sa akin" means "He/She is younger than me." It's the opposite of 'matanda' (old). Not to be confused with 'bata' (child), though they're obviously related. The difference is the stress: /BA-ta/ is the noun, /ba-TA/ is the adjective.
usage_notes: The stress is on the last syllable /ba-TA/, differentiating it from the noun 'bata' /BA-ta/ (child).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mukha siyang mas **bata** kaysa sa kanyang edad.","translation":"She looks **younger** than her age."},{"sentence":"Noong **bata** pa ako, pangarap kong maging piloto.","translation":"When I was still **young**, I dreamed of being a pilot."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pook o establisyimento kung saan nagbebenta at naghahain ng mga inuming may alkohol.
original_explanation: A place where you pay P200 for a beer that costs P50 at 7-Eleven. It's the official venue for TGIF celebrations, drowning your sorrows, or pretending to watch a basketball game while waiting for your friend. Also where you find a 'videoke' machine for your inner Regine Velasquez to shine.
usage_notes: Isang hiram na salita na unibersal na naiintindihan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkita tayo sa **bar** mamayang gabi para mag-inuman.","translation":"Let's meet at the **bar** tonight for some drinks."}]

translation: an act of whispering (among a group)
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng sabay-sabay o palitan ng pabulong na usapan sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang tao.
original_explanation: This is the noun for the *event* of whispering. 'Yung moment na nag-uusap kayo ng mga ka-team mo sa pantry tapos biglang dumaan 'yung boss niyo. The 'huddle' of whispers. "Ano 'yang bulungan niyo diyan?" tanong ni Mama pag nakita kayong magkakapatid na nagbubulungan.
usage_notes: Refers to the collective act or the atmosphere of whispering, distinct from 'bulung-bulungan' which is the rumor itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natigil ang kanilang **bulungan** nang pumasok ang guro.","translation":"Their **whispering** stopped when the teacher entered."},{"sentence":"Rinig sa buong silid ang kanilang malakas na **bulungan**.","translation":"Their loud **whispering** could be heard throughout the room."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng muling pagyakap sa pananampalataya, pagsisisi sa mga kasalanan, at pagpapanumbalik ng relasyon sa Diyos.
original_explanation: This is the spiritual equivalent of "new year, new me" but for your soul. It's when you've been living the 'Marites' lifestyle or been too focused on the grind, and you suddenly feel the need to go to church, pray the rosary, and basically tell God, "Kabs, I'm back. Pasensya na sa lahat." It’s a spiritual reboot.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagbabalik-loob sa Diyos** ay nagdulot ng malaking pagbabago sa kanyang buhay.","translation":"His **returning to God** brought a great change in his life."},{"sentence":"Marami ang nakahanap ng kapayapaan sa **pagbabalik-loob sa Diyos**.","translation":"Many have found peace in **religious conversion**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maliliit na titik sa alpabeto, taliwas sa malalaking titik o mayuskula.
original_explanation: The 'small letters' you use when you're texting your friends or trying to be aesthetic on social media. The opposite of the 'ALL CAPS' your tita uses on Facebook. It's the default setting of chill.
usage_notes: Ang kasalungat nito ay 'mayuskula' (uppercase).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isulat mo ang iyong pangalan sa **minuskula**.","translation":"Write your name in **lowercase**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga password ay karaniwang sensitibo sa paggamit ng mayuskula at **minuskula**.","translation":"Passwords are usually sensitive to the use of uppercase and **lowercase**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng pagiging sakang o may mga binti na pakurba palabas.
original_explanation: This is the old-school term for 'sakang' or bow-legged. Imagine a cowboy who's been on a horse for too long. It's a physical descriptor, but often used playfully or teasingly among friends.
usage_notes: Considered a bit dated or regional by some. The word 'sakang' is more commonly used in modern conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa pagiging **bake** noong bata pa siya.","translation":"He was known for being **bow-legged** when he was young."},{"sentence":"Medyo **bake** ang lakad niya dahil sa pagod.","translation":"His walk is a bit **bow-legged** from exhaustion."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian o estado ng pagiging malamig; mababang temperatura.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'lamig' (cold) at panlaping 'ka- -an'.
original_explanation: Ito yung feeling na kailangan mo na ng jacket sa Baguio o sa sinehan, o 'yung dahilan kung bakit ka nagkukumot kahit summer kasi naka-full blast ang aircon. Pwede ring estado ng relasyon niyo pagkatapos ng away. 'The cold never bothered me anyway,' sabi ni Elsa, pero sa Pinas, reklamo 'yan.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa pisikal na temperatura. Maaari ring gamitin sa metaporikal na paraan, ngunit may mas tiyak na parirala para doon (kalamigan ng loob).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko kinaya ang **kalamigan** sa Tagaytay kaya bumili ako ng kape.","translation":"I couldn't handle the **coldness** in Tagaytay so I bought coffee."},{"sentence":"Ang **kalamigan** ng umaga ay masarap para sa pagtulog.","translation":"The **coolness** of the morning is nice for sleeping."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na wala sa tamang pag-iisip, may pagka-sira ang ulo, o gumagawa ng mga bagay na katawa-tawa at walang katuturan.
original_explanation: This is what your tita calls you when you do something silly, like quitting your stable job to become a vlogger. It's a mix of 'crazy,' 'foolish,' and 'endearingly dumb.' It's less clinical than 'baliw' and more of a shake-of-the-head, 'hay nako' kind of crazy. Can be an insult or a term of endearment, depending on who's saying it.
usage_notes: Also spelled 'loko-loko'. The intensity can range from playful to insulting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala diyan, **luku-luko** 'yan.","translation":"Don't believe him, he's **crazy**."},{"sentence":"Ang **luku-luko** mong kaibigan, isinama ako sa kalokohan niya.","translation":"Your **silly** friend got me involved in his foolishness."}]

meaning_filipino: Kakulangan ng sigla, interes, o pagnanasa, lalo na sa pagkain.
original_explanation: This is your mood on a Monday morning before coffee. It's also you looking at your ex's new profile pic—zero interest, zero appetite. When you feel completely unmotivated and everything seems 'meh', you're feeling walang-kagana-gana.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa kawalan ng gana sa pagkain o sa kawalan ng sigla para sa isang gawain.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mula nang magkasakit siya, naging **walang-kagana-gana** siyang kumain.","translation":"Ever since he got sick, he has been **without appetite** to eat."},{"sentence":"Bakit parang **walang-kagana-gana** kang pumasok sa trabaho ngayon?","translation":"Why do you seem so **unenthusiastic** to go to work today?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na bago pa lamang sa isang larangan, gawain, o propesyon; kulang pa sa karanasan.
etymology: Possibly from Spanish "vaguido" (dizziness), but its modern meaning is heavily influenced by the Tagalog "bago" (new). Some also link it to "bagong tao" (new person).
original_explanation: The new guy in the office who still calls the boss 'Sir/Ma'am' every sentence. The fresh grad on their first day, looking lost. In online games, this is the 'noob.' You were once a bagito, I was once a bagito, we were all bagitos at some point. It's a rite of passage.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun ('He is a newbie') or an adjective ('He is new to this'). Often used in a teasing but not necessarily malicious way.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, lahat tayo ay dumaan sa pagiging **bagito**.","translation":"Don't worry, we all went through being a **newbie**."},{"sentence":"**Bagito** pa siya sa trabaho kaya kailangan ng gabay.","translation":"He is still a **rookie** at the job so he needs guidance."}]

translation: retoucher, someone who alters or enhances
meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang trabaho o hilig ay ang mag-retoke o baguhin ang isang bagay upang mapabuti ang anyo nito.
original_explanation: This could be your friend who's a Photoshop wizard, turning your ID picture into a profile pic-worthy glam shot. Or, in showbiz parlance, the surgeon who gives you "a gift from God, through my doctor." Sila ang bahala sa enhancements.
usage_notes: Often used humorously in the context of photo editing or cosmetic surgery.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang galing ng **tagaretoke** ng mga litrato, nawala lahat ng pimples ko.","translation":"The photo **retoucher** is so good, all my pimples disappeared."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa buong opisina bilang **tagaretoke** ng mga presentasyon para maging mas maganda.","translation":"He's known in the whole office as the one who **retouches** presentations to make them look better."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mas masidhing paglalarawan ng isang bagay na lubhang punit-punit, watak-watak, o durog na durog.
original_explanation: The "Extra Joss" version of 'gutay'. This is for when something isn't just torn, it's OBLITERATED. Think of your payslip after all the deductions. Or your dignity after tripping in public. "My heart is not just broken, it's gutay-gutay." It's the final form of being destroyed.
usage_notes: The common, emphatic form of 'gutay'. Describes extreme disrepair or destruction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natagpuan ang lumang libro na **gutay-gutay** na ang mga pahina.","translation":"The old book was found with its pages **torn to shreds**."},{"sentence":"Naging **gutay-gutay** ang mga pananim dahil sa pananalasa ng mga balang.","translation":"The crops became **tattered** due to the plague of locusts."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o kalagayan ng pagbawas ng timbang o pagiging payat.
original_explanation: Ito yung journey mo after the holiday season. Yung resulta ng "diet starts on Monday," intermittent fasting, at pag-iwas sa kanin (kahit isang linggo lang). It can be a healthy glow-up or a sign of stress—depende sa context kung bakit ka nag-lose ng weight.
usage_notes: Can have a neutral, positive (intentional weight loss), or negative (due to illness or stress) connotation depending on the context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napansin ng lahat ang kanyang biglaang **pamamayat**.","translation":"Everyone noticed his sudden **weight loss**."},{"sentence":"Ang ehersisyo at tamang pagkain ang sikreto sa kanyang matagumpay na **pamamayat**.","translation":"Exercise and proper diet are the secret to her successful **process of becoming thin**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang may pinakamataas na antas ng pagiging kumplikado o nangangailangan ng pinakamalaking pagsisikap upang maisagawa o maunawaan.
original_explanation: This is that final boss in a video game, that one exam question you stared at for 20 minutes, or trying to assemble IKEA furniture without instructions. It's the ultimate challenge that tests your patience, skill, and sanity. Ang **pinakamahirap** na parte ng pagiging adult ay ang magbayad ng bills.
usage_notes: Refers to difficulty or complexity. It is a homonym with 'pinakamahirap' (poorest).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para sa marami, ang Matematika ang **pinakamahirap** na asignatura.","translation":"For many, Mathematics is the **most difficult** subject."},{"sentence":"Ito na yata ang **pinakamahirap** na desisyong ginawa ko sa buong buhay ko.","translation":"This might be the **hardest** decision I've made in my entire life."}]

meaning_filipino: Oringal o likas sa isang lugar; hindi dayuhan. Tumutukoy din sa isang katangian na likas o taal sa isang tao.
etymology: From ka- + tubo (to grow, to sprout).
original_explanation: As an adjective, it means something is 'native' to a place. The sampaguita is a katutubo flower. It can also mean 'innate' or 'inborn'. Like, your talent for singing might be a katutubo talent—it's just naturally there, no tutorials needed.
usage_notes: Can describe plants, animals, languages, or even inherent traits.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang waling-waling ay isang **katutubo** na orkidyas sa Pilipinas.","translation":"The waling-waling is an **indigenous** orchid in the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Sa kanya ay **katutubo** ang pagiging matulungin.","translation":"Being helpful is **innate** in him."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paghahanda at pagbuburo ng mga gulay o prutas, karaniwan sa suka, asukal, at asin, upang mapreserba.
original_explanation: The OG Pinoy side dish hustle. Before people were making dalgona coffee, lolas were busy deciding to `mag-atsara` with all the extra green papayas. Perfect partner for anything fried and oily, para kunwari healthy pa rin.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to the act of making 'atsara' (Filipino pickles), most commonly from green papaya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinuruan ako ng lola ko kung paano **mag-atsara** ng papaya.","translation":"My grandmother taught me how to **make papaya pickles**."},{"sentence":"Para sa Pasko, plano naming **mag-atsara** para ipamigay sa mga kapitbahay.","translation":"For Christmas, we plan to **make pickles** to give to our neighbors."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pariralang panlarawan na ginagamit kapag hindi matukoy o maalala ang eksaktong salita para sa isang katangian, na nagpapahiwatig ng isang mataas na antas nito.
etymology: Kombinasyon ng Ingles na 'very' at Tagalog na 'ano'.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'placeholder' adjective. When your brain lags and you can't find the exact word, you just say 'very ano.' It's like, 'Yung pelikula, it's very... ano... basta, maganda!' It's the verbal equivalent of a loading icon.
usage_notes: Isang impormal na pananalita na karaniwang maririnig sa pang-araw-araw na usapan. Gumagana bilang isang pansamantalang pang-uri kapag ang nagsasalita ay nag-iisip pa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang performance niya kagabi ay **very ano**... powerful!","translation":"Her performance last night was **very, you know**... powerful!"},{"sentence":"Hindi ko ma-explain, basta ang feeling ko ay **very ano**, alam mo 'yun?","translation":"I can't explain it, I just feel **very... something**, you know?"}]

translation: to be able to advise; can advise
meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang magbigay ng payo, suhestiyon, o rekomendasyon.
etymology: ma- (ability) + i- (object focus) + pa- (future tense/contemplative) + payo (advice)
original_explanation: That moment when your friend is having a 'sana all' crisis and you're the designated 'Tita' who has to give life advice. "Ano'ng **maipapayo** mo sa 'kin? Mag-resign na ba ako?" It's the unsolicited (or solicited) advice you give, hoping it actually helps.
usage_notes: The verb form for giving advice.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bilang kaibigan, ano ang **maipapayo** mo sa kanya?","translation":"As a friend, what **can you advise** him?"},{"sentence":"Ang tanging **maipapayo** ko ay maging matatag ka.","translation":"The only thing I **can advise** is for you to be strong."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging lubos na nawalan ng pag-asa, tapang, o kumpiyansa sa sarili dahil sa matinding kabiguan o pagsubok.
etymology: Mula sa "sira" (broken, inuulit para sa diin) at "loob" (inside, spirit).
original_explanation: This is the feeling after you've been rejected for the 10th job, ghosted by your "the one," and your data plan just ran out. It's rock bottom. 'Loob' is your inner self, your spirit, and when it's 'sirang-sira' (completely broken), you're emotionally shattered and have zero will to fight back. All you want to do is listen to sad songs and eat ice cream from the tub.
usage_notes: Isang napaka-makahulugang parirala para sa malalim na emosyonal na pagkabalisa at pagkawala ng moral.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matapos malaman ang resulta, **sirang-sira ang loob** ng buong koponan.","translation":"After finding out the results, the whole team was **completely demoralized**."},{"sentence":"Naiwan siyang **sirang-sira ang loob** nang iwan siya ng kanyang kasintahan.","translation":"She was left **utterly discouraged** when her boyfriend left her."}]
related: ["nawalan ng pag-asa","bagsak ang loob","durog ang puso","nanlulumo"]

translation: the state of being gathered; assembly
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging magkakasama sa isang lugar; ang paraan ng pagtitipon.
original_explanation: This is what happens when the whole barkada finally has the same day off. It's the family reunion during Christmas, the general assembly for your condo association, or even just a group of people huddled around the latest chismis. It's the state of being together in one place.
usage_notes: Refers to the result or state of a gathering, whereas 'pagtitipon' refers more to the event or act of gathering itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging maayos ang **pagkakatipon** ng mga donasyon para sa mga nasalanta ng bagyo.","translation":"The **gathering** of donations for the typhoon victims was orderly."},{"sentence":"Sa kanilang **pagkakatipon**, napag-usapan nila ang mga plano para sa susunod na taon.","translation":"In their **assembly**, they discussed the plans for the next year."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paraan ng pagbilang na tig-i-labindalawa; sa napakaraming bilang o dami.
