original_explanation: This is how your tita buys things from Divisoria. Not just one or two, but by the dozen. It implies abundance, wholesale, and a "go big or go home" attitude. "Bumili si Mama ng itlog, dose-dosena!" means you're having eggs for breakfast, lunch, and dinner for the next week.
usage_notes: Isang paraan ng pagpapahayag ng maramihan sa pamamagitan ng pag-uulit ng salitang-ugat. Nagpapahiwatig ng malaking halaga o dami.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kung bibili ka ng rosas, mas makakamura ka kung **dose-dosena**.","translation":"If you're buying roses, it's cheaper if you buy them **by the dozen**."},{"sentence":"**Dose-dosena** ang dumating na bisita sa kanyang kaarawan.","translation":"Guests arrived **by the dozens** for his/her birthday."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng materyal, karaniwang pa-tatsulok ang hugis, na isinisingit sa siwang upang patigilin, i-level, o suportahan ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: That folded piece of cardboard you stuff under a wobbly table at the karinderya? That's a kalso. The rock you kick under a car tire parked on a hill? Kalso. It's the unsung hero of stability, the ultimate low-tech solution for life's uneven moments. The "pampatigil sa umuugang relasyon" of furniture.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb `kalsuhan` (to put a wedge under something).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha ka ng **kalso** para hindi gumalaw ang mesa.","translation":"Get a **wedge** so the table won't move."},{"sentence":"Nilagyan niya ng **kalso** ang gulong ng trak.","translation":"He placed a **chock** under the truck's wheel."}]

translation: a meal of longganisa, fried rice, and egg
meaning_filipino: Isang pagkaing pang-almusal na binubuo ng **long**ganisa (batutay), **si**nangag (pritong kanin), at it**log** (pritong itlog).
etymology: Isang portmanteau o pinagsamang salita mula sa **long**ganisa, **si**nangag, at it**log**.
original_explanation: The holy trinity of Filipino breakfast. It's a portmanteau and a lifestyle. When you can't decide what to eat, 'longsilog' is the answer. It's the ultimate comfort food, available 24/7 in 'silog' places. Best served with a side of suka (vinegar) with chili and a hot cup of kapeng barako.
usage_notes: Bahagi ng serye ng mga "silog" na pagkain (hal. tapsilog, tosilog).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umorder ako ng **longsilog** sa karinderya.","translation":"I ordered **longsilog** at the eatery."},{"sentence":"Para sa akin, ang pinakamasarap na almusal ay **longsilog**.","translation":"For me, the best breakfast is **longsilog**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kabayaran, sahod, o gantimpala para sa isang serbisyo o trabahong isinagawa.
original_explanation: The fancy, high-falutin' Spanish way of saying 'sweldo' or 'sahod.' Ito yung word na makikita mo sa job contract mo na kailangan mo pa i-Google. Basically, the reason you wake up for your 8 AM meeting. It's the 'bayad sa pagod.'
usage_notes: A very formal term, usually found in legal or business documents.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakalagay sa kontrata ang halaga ng **remunerasyon** para sa proyektong ito.","translation":"The contract states the amount of **remuneration** for this project."},{"sentence":"Ang tamang **remunerasyon** ay mahalaga upang mapanatili ang motibasyon ng mga empleyado.","translation":"Proper **remuneration** is important to maintain employee motivation."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matinding pagnanais, hangarin, o mithiin para sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na gusto mo talagang makuha 'yung isang bagay, parang 'yung last piece ng lechon sa handaan, o 'yung 13th-month pay mo. It's the 'sana all' in your heart turned into a deep, personal goal. 'Yung ultimate 'go-getter' fuel mo.
usage_notes: Isang mas matulain o pormal na salita para sa 'nais' o 'gusto'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pita** ng kanyang puso ay ang makapaglingkod sa bayan.","translation":"The **intense desire** of his heart is to serve the country."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagwasak o pagsira sa isang bagay, karaniwan ay marupok o babasagin, na nagiging sanhi ng pagkapira-piraso nito.
original_explanation: The sound your mom hears from the kitchen that makes her yell your full name. It’s what you do to a piggy bank, a plate, or someone's heart. Also what a good joke does to the silence in a room—'bumasag sa katahimikan'.
usage_notes: Often used for fragile items like glass, pottery, or figuratively for silence, trust, or hearts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-ingat siya nang husto para hindi **bumasag** ng kahit anong plato.","translation":"He was very careful not **to break** any plates."},{"sentence":"Isang malakas na tawa ang **bumasag** sa katahimikan ng silid.","translation":"A loud laugh **broke** the silence of the room."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang tao na may ugaling magpakita ng pagwawalang-halaga, pag-insulto, o mababang pagtingin sa kapwa.
original_explanation: Parang 'mapang-api' pero more on the emotional and verbal side. Ito yung titingin sa'yo from head to toe, tapos tataas ang kilay. The master of the side-eye. They use words and looks to make you feel worthless. Social media trolls are the digital version of this.
usage_notes: Describes an attitude or behavior of looking down on others. Stronger and more active than just being arrogant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroon siyang **mapanghamak** na tingin sa mga mahihirap.","translation":"He has a **scornful** way of looking at the poor."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **mapanghamak** na pananalita ay nakasakit sa damdamin ng marami.","translation":"His **contemptuous** speech hurt the feelings of many."}]

translation: to widen; to make more spacious; to loosen
meaning_filipino: Gawing mas maluwang ang isang espasyo, daanan, o bagay. Dagdagan ang sukat o lawak nito.
original_explanation: That feeling when your favorite jeans don't fit anymore after the holidays. You wish you could just tell your body, "Paluwangin mo, please!" Also, what you tell the driver of a crowded jeepney when you're trying to squeeze in: "Boss, pa-usog, paluwangin niyo po." It's the opposite of "Sana all slim."
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of construction (widening a road), clothing (loosening a waistband), or giving more space figuratively (e.g., paluwangin ang isip - to open one's mind).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **paluwangin** ang kalsada upang mabawasan ang trapiko.","translation":"The road needs to be **widened** to reduce traffic."},{"sentence":"Paki-**paluwangin** mo naman ang sinturon ko, medyo masikip.","translation":"Please **loosen** my belt, it's a bit tight."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking kasapi ng isang relihiyosong komunidad, na karaniwang naninirahan sa isang monasteryo at sumusunod sa mga panata ng pag-iisa, pagdarasal, at paglilingkod.
original_explanation: The guy version of a 'mongha'. They live simple lives, often in silence and prayer. If your life feels too chaotic with traffic, deadlines, and toxic relatives, you might have jokingly said you want to become a 'monghe' and just live in a mountain somewhere.
usage_notes: Ginagamit para sa mga lalaking relihiyoso sa iba't ibang pananampalataya, tulad ng Budismo at Kristiyanismo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglakbay siya sa Tibet upang makasalamuha ang mga **monghe**.","translation":"He traveled to Tibet to interact with the **monks**."},{"sentence":"Ang buhay ng isang **monghe** ay puno ng disiplina at panalangin.","translation":"The life of a **monk** is full of discipline and prayer."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bahagi ng makina na gumagalaw nang pabalik-balik sa loob ng isang silindro, karaniwang ginagamit sa mga motor ng sasakyan.
original_explanation: Yung parte ng makina ng motor mo na parang puso, nagpa-pump para umandar. Kung 'di 'to gumana, 'tulak' ang next word na maririnig mo. Parang sa trabaho, kung may isang 'piston' sa team na ayaw gumalaw, apektado lahat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang palitan ang **piston** ng makina para bumalik sa dati ang lakas nito.","translation":"The engine's **piston** needs to be replaced to restore its power."}]

meaning_filipino: Pumasok sa kumbento upang italaga ang sarili sa serbisyo ng Diyos bilang isang madre.
original_explanation: The classic "mag-aartista ako o magmamadre!" line from a dramatic teleserye character. It's the ultimate career path pivot for a devout Catholic woman, choosing a life of religious service. It's the female equivalent of `magpari` (to become a priest).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matagal na niyang pangarap na **magmadre** pagkatapos ng kolehiyo.","translation":"It has long been her dream to **become a nun** after college."},{"sentence":"Nagulat ang lahat nang ipahayag ni Elena na siya ay **magmamadre**.","translation":"Everyone was surprised when Elena announced that she would **become a nun**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng dayuhan na hindi mamamayan ng bansang kanyang kinaroroonan.
original_explanation: She's the female tourist everyone wants a selfie with, or the expat in your office who's still figuring out why everyone eats rice three times a day. Basically, a woman from another country.
usage_notes: Ito ang pambabaeng anyo ng "ekstranghero".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **ekstranghera** ang nahuhumaling sa ganda ng mga isla sa Pilipinas.","translation":"Many female **foreigners** are captivated by the beauty of the islands in the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Ang nobya ng pinsan ko ay isang **ekstranghera** mula sa Espanya.","translation":"My cousin's girlfriend is a female **foreigner** from Spain."}]

translation: to inhale; to savor a scent
meaning_filipino: Ang malalim na paglanghap ng isang kaaya-ayang amoy; namnamin ang bango.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "samyô" (bango, halimuyak) at idinugtong ang hulaping "-hin".
original_explanation: That feeling when you walk past a bakery and take a deep breath. That's 'samyuhin'. It's not just smelling, it's *savoring* the scent. Like when your food delivery finally arrives and you open the box to inhale the glorious aroma before digging in.
usage_notes: Mayroon itong makata o pampanitikang dating. Ang "amuyin" ay ang mas karaniwan at neutral na termino para sa "to smell". Ang "samyuhin" ay nagpapahiwatig ng kasiyahan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **samyuhin** ang sariwang hangin sa probinsya.","translation":"I want to **inhale** the fresh air in the province."},{"sentence":"**Sinamyo** niya ang bango ng mga bulaklak sa hardin.","translation":"She **savored the scent** of the flowers in the garden."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang babae na may angking kilos na kaaya-aya, maganda, at elegante.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung tita mong mahinhin kumilos, o 'yung kaklase mong parang laging may invisible crown. Hindi pabebe, kundi natural ang pagiging elegante. 'Yung kahit madapa, parang part pa rin ng sayaw. The opposite of 'lampa'.
usage_notes: Ang katumbas para sa lalaki ay "grasyoso". Karaniwang ginagamit upang ilarawan ang kilos o galaw.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **grasyosa** na mananayaw ang nagtanghal sa entablado.","translation":"A **graceful** dancer performed on stage."},{"sentence":"Kahit sa simpleng paglalakad, makikita ang pagiging **grasyosa** ni Ana.","translation":"Even in simple walking, you can see Ana's **gracefulness**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagbabago ng pagkain sa loob ng katawan upang maging sustansya na magagamit ng mga selula.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung magic na nangyayari sa tiyan mo after mong kumain ng isang buong lechon. Kung mabilis ang 'yong panunaw, swerte ka. Kung mabagal, good luck sa feeling bloated na parang 'di ka pa rin nakaka-move on sa ex mo.
usage_notes: Can refer to the physiological process or to a substance that aids digestion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang papaya ay mabuti para sa **panunaw**.","translation":"Papaya is good for **digestion**."},{"sentence":"Mabagal ang kanyang **panunaw** kaya madalas siyang magkaroon ng heartburn.","translation":"His **digestion** is slow, so he often gets heartburn."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng salamin na may kulay, na ginagamit upang bawasan ang tindi ng liwanag o para sa palamuti. Karaniwang tumutukoy sa salamin sa mata na pananggalang sa araw.
etymology: From Tagalog 'salamin' and Spanish 'de color' (of color).
original_explanation: Literally 'colored glass.' This is what you wear to look cool, mysterious, or to hide the fact that you only got three hours of sleep. The OG term for sunglasses before 'shades' became a thing. Also refers to the colored glass panes in old churches or your lola's house.
usage_notes: While it can mean any colored glass, it most commonly refers to sunglasses.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang magsuot ng **salaming de-kolor** kapag matindi ang sikat ng araw.","translation":"Don't forget to wear **sunglasses** when the sun is intense."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na pagiging kasapi o miyembro ng isang samahan, partido, o organisasyon.
original_explanation: The official verb for signing up. When you finally join that gym, org, or online group you've been stalking for months. It's making your membership official, like getting your ID card and being added to the group chat.
usage_notes: More formal than 'sumali'. Implies becoming a member or an affiliate of a group with a structure or ideology.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumapi** siya sa isang organisasyon na tumutulong sa mga batang lansangan.","translation":"She **joined** an organization that helps street children."},{"sentence":"Maraming rebelde ang **sumapi** sa kilusan noong panahon ng diktadurya.","translation":"Many rebels **joined** the movement during the dictatorship era."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapang pambahay na pinananatiling malamig ang mga pagkain at inumin upang hindi ito masira.
original_explanation: Universally known as the 'ref'. It's the sacred box where last night's adobo, a half-eaten cake, and a questionable Tupperware from three weeks ago live in harmony. The main source of all midnight snacks and the place you stare into when you're bored but not really hungry.
usage_notes: Commonly shortened to 'ref' in casual conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakilagay na lang ng tirang ulam sa loob ng **refrigerator**.","translation":"Please just put the leftover food inside the **refrigerator**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na naibenta na sa pamamagitan ng remata o subasta.
original_explanation: The status of your property after it's been through a 'remata'. "Ay, rematado na pala 'yung lupa sa kanto." It's the past tense of a financial tragedy, meaning the bank has won and the item has been sold off to the highest bidder.
usage_notes: Used to describe a property or item that has undergone foreclosure or auction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binili niya ang **rematado** na kotse sa isang malaking bangko.","translation":"He bought the **foreclosed** car from a big bank."},{"sentence":"Maraming **rematado** na condominium units ang binebenta online.","translation":"Many **foreclosed** condominium units are being sold online."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paunang bersyon ng isang ililimbag na akda, tulad ng libro o pahayagan, na ginagamit para sa pagwawasto ng mga kamalian bago ang pinal na pag-imprenta.
original_explanation: Before "Ctrl+P," there was the galerada. This is the draft version of a newspaper or book page that the editor massacres with a red pen. It's the "proofread this or else" copy. In the digital age, it's the PDF with a million comments and tracked changes from your boss. A very specific, old-school publishing term.
usage_notes: A technical term in printing and publishing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuri ang **galerada** para sa anumang typo bago natin ito isalang sa imprenta.","translation":"Please check the **galley proof** for any typos before we send it to the press."}]

translation: Ahem; a clearing of the throat; a slight cough
meaning_filipino: Isang bahagya at sinadyang pag-ubo upang linisin ang lalamunan o kuhanin ang atensyon ng iba.
original_explanation: That little "ehem" you do when someone you know walks by with their new jowa, and you want them to see you. It's the universal signal for "Notice me!" or "May sinasabi ako pero di ko masabi nang diretsahan."
usage_notes: Often used to get someone's attention subtly. Can be repeated for emphasis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **tighim** lang ang narinig mula sa kanya nang tanungin tungkol sa dating kasintahan.","translation":"Only a slight **cough** was heard from him when asked about his ex-girlfriend."},{"sentence":"Nagbigay ng **tighim** ang guro para makuha ang atensyon ng mga maiingay na estudyante.","translation":"The teacher gave an **ahem** to get the attention of the noisy students."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sitwasyon ng hindi pagkakasundo, pag-aaway, o pagkakaroon ng magkasalungat na mga ideya, interes, o prinsipyo.
etymology: From `salungat` meaning 'opposite' or 'contrary', with the suffix `-an` creating a noun that signifies a place or situation characterized by the root word.
original_explanation: That moment in a teleserye when the protagonist finds out her boyfriend is also her long-lost brother. That's a major 'salungatan'. It's any kind of conflict, from a simple 'conflict of interest' in the office to the deep philosophical contradictions you think about at 3 AM. It's the drama, the plot twist, the 'resbak' waiting to happen.
usage_notes: A formal term for conflict, dispute, or contradiction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **salungatan** sa pagitan ng dalawang bansa ay kailangang matugunan sa mapayapang paraan.","translation":"The **conflict** between the two countries needs to be addressed peacefully."},{"sentence":"Mayroong **salungatan** sa kanyang mga pahayag kahapon at ngayon.","translation":"There is a **contradiction** in his statements yesterday and today."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kulay na kumupas o nawalan ng tingkad dahil sa pagkaluma, pagkababad sa araw, o madalas na paglalaba.
original_explanation: 'Yung favorite mong black shirt na ngayon ay parang kulay abo na lang dahil sa sobrang laba. Or 'yung feelings niya para sa'yo, dati intense, ngayon **pusaw** na. It's the aesthetic of things that have lost their saturation, both literally and figuratively. #Hugot
usage_notes: Naglalarawan ng pagkawala ng tingkad o sigla ng isang kulay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **pusaw** na ang kulay ng kanyang lumang maong.","translation":"The color of his old jeans has become **faded**."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa araw, **pusaw** na ang pintura ng pader.","translation":"Because of the sun, the paint on the wall is now **faded**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangunahing delegado o taong kumakatawan sa isang grupo, organisasyon, o bansa.
original_explanation: The main character of a delegation. If your barangay sends a team to a competition, the punong-kinatawan is the team captain. In a company, they're the lead person sent to negotiate a deal. They're the one who gets to speak for everyone else, so dapat magaling.
usage_notes: Used in formal settings like politics, business, or official delegations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang embahador ang nagsisilbing **punong-kinatawan** ng Pilipinas sa ibang bansa.","translation":"The ambassador serves as the **chief representative** of the Philippines in another country."},{"sentence":"Siya ang napiling **punong-kinatawan** para sa pandaigdigang kumperensya.","translation":"She was chosen as the **head delegate** for the international conference."}]

meaning_filipino: Isagawa ang isang bagay sa tamang oras o pagkakataon; abangan ang eksaktong sandali para sa isang kilos.
etymology: Mula sa salitang "tiyempo" (mula sa Espanyol na "tiempo" na nangangahulugang 'oras' o 'panahon') at hulaping "-han".
original_explanation: The art of perfect timing. Like when you arrive at a party just as the food is served, or when you message your crush right when you see they're 'Active Now'. It's a skill, a strategy, a way of life.
usage_notes: Can be used in both positive (e.g., catching an opportunity) and negative (e.g., catching someone doing something wrong) contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tiyempuhan** mo ang pag-alis ng boss bago ka mag-break.","translation":"**Time** it for when the boss leaves before you take a break."},{"sentence":"Natiyempuhan ko siyang may kausap na iba sa telepono.","translation":"I **caught** him at the exact moment he was talking to someone else on the phone."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gagawing pagpunta sa iba't ibang lugar, malapit man o malayo. Ito ay nasa panahunang panghinaharap.
etymology: Future tense of `maglakbay`. Formed from `mag-` + `la` (repeated first syllable of root) + `lakbay` (journey).
original_explanation: This is the future tense of your #TravelGoals. When you're finally cashing in your leave credits and booking that flight, you can say, "**Maglalakbay** ako sa Palawan!" It's the promise of adventure, of seeing new places, and of course, taking lots of photos for the 'gram.
usage_notes: This is the future tense of the verb `maglakbay` (to travel).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa susunod na buwan, **maglalakbay** ang aming pamilya sa Cebu.","translation":"Next month, our family **will travel** to Cebu."},{"sentence":"Saan ka **maglalakbay** para sa iyong kaarawan?","translation":"Where **will you travel** for your birthday?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang harapan o unahang bahagi ng isang bagay, lugar, o pangyayari; ang simula.
original_explanation: The "welcome" mat of a house or a situation. It's the first thing you see, like the grand entrance of a mall or the *bungad* of your salary (which quickly disappears). Your "opening spiel" when you're about to ask a favor from your parents. "Ma, Pa, ang ganda ng araw 'no?"—that's the *bungad*.
usage_notes: The verb form "bumungad" means "to appear suddenly in front" or "to be greeted by".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa **bungad** pa lang ng pelikula, alam mo nang maganda ito.","translation":"Right from the **beginning** of the movie, you already know it's good."},{"sentence":"Malinis ang **bungad** ng kanilang bahay.","translation":"The **front** of their house is clean."}]

translation: manner of lying down; posture while lying down
meaning_filipino: Ang paraan o posisyon ng paghiga ng isang tao o bagay.
etymology: From `pagkaka-` + `higa` (to lie down). Describes the manner or position of lying down.
original_explanation: This is your 'Netflix and chill' posture. It's the way you're lying down. Are you curled up in a fetal position after a rough day? Or sprawled out like a starfish on a Sunday morning? 'Ayusin mo ang pagkakahiga mo, baka manakit ang likod mo.' (Fix the way you're lying down, your back might hurt.) It's the art of being horizontal.
usage_notes: Refers to the specific posture or way someone is lying.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita ko sa **pagkakahiga** niya na hindi siya komportable.","translation":"I saw from the **way he was lying down** that he was not comfortable."},{"sentence":"Ang pusa ay mahimbing na natutulog at mukhang kuntento sa **pagkakahiga** nito.","translation":"The cat is sleeping soundly and looks content with its **lying posture**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagkakaroon ng mababang temperatura; ang pakiramdam na dulot ng kawalan ng init.
original_explanation: That feeling you get from your jowa after a fight. Or that sudden chill when the aircon in the BPO office is set to 'Antarctica mode'. Pwede ring excuse para mangyakap: 'Ang lamig naman, pa-hug!'
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun (ang lamig - the coldness) or as a root for an adjective (malamig - cold). This entry focuses on the noun form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nararamdaman ko na ang **lamig** ng Disyembre.","translation":"I can already feel the **coldness** of December."},{"sentence":"Grabe ang **lamig** sa Baguio!","translation":"The **cold** in Baguio is intense!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang institusyong pampinansyal na tumatanggap ng mga deposito, nagpapautang, at nagbibigay ng iba pang serbisyong pananalapi.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'banco' (bangko, institusyong pampinansyal).
original_explanation: Yung lugar kung saan ka pumipila para mag-withdraw ng sahod mo, para lang ma-realize na ubos na pala pambayad sa bills at Shopee. Dito rin nakatira ang utang mo sa credit card.
usage_notes: Ito ay tumutukoy sa isang institusyong pampinansyal. Mayroon itong katunog na salita na nangangahulugang 'upuan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong pumunta sa **bangko** para magdeposito ng pera.","translation":"I need to go to the **bank** to deposit money."},{"sentence":"Inaprubahan ng **bangko** ang aking loan application.","translation":"The **bank** approved my loan application."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang alternatibong baybay para sa 'apatiya'; ang kawalan ng damdamin o interes.
etymology: Isang kolokyal na pagbaybay ng 'apatiya', mula sa Ingles na 'apathy'.
original_explanation: This is 'apatiya' but with a more "jologs" or text-message-friendly spelling. It's the "skenks" to 'salamat', the "lodi" to 'idol'. Same meaning, different vibe. You type this when you're too apathetic to even type the extra 'i'.
usage_notes: Hindi ito ang pamantayang baybay at mas itinuturing na kolokyal o impormal. Mas mainam gamitin ang 'apatiya' sa pormal na pagsulat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi dapat manaig ang **apatya** sa ating lipunan.","translation":"**Apathy** should not prevail in our society."},{"sentence":"Ikinababahala niya ang **apatya** ng kanyang mga kaklase sa mga isyung panlipunan.","translation":"He is worried about the **apathy** of his classmates towards social issues."}]

translation: to steam; to evaporate; to leak (gas)
meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang paglabas ng singaw (gaseous na anyo ng tubig), amoy, o gas mula sa isang bagay.
etymology: Possibly related to Malay `singah` (to pant, breathe hard).
original_explanation: That thing your rice cooker does when the rice is almost cooked. It's also what happens to your patience when you're stuck in EDSA traffic. 'Amoy gasul, parang may sumisingaw!' It can also mean a secret or a hidden feeling is starting to come out. 'Sumisingaw na ang baho ng mga kalokohan niya.' (The stink of his misdeeds is starting to leak out.)
usage_notes: This is the present tense of `sumingaw`. It is versatile and can be used for steam, vapor, gas leaks, or even bad odors.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumisingaw** na ang sinaing, malapit nang maluto.","translation":"The rice is **steaming**, it's almost cooked."},{"sentence":"May **sumisingaw** na hangin mula sa gulong ng kotse.","translation":"There's air **leaking** from the car's tire."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagbabago-bago o pagkakaroon ng iba't ibang anyo, katangian, o halaga.
etymology: From `pag-` + `iba-iba` (reduplication of `iba`, meaning 'different'). The reduplication implies variety or continuous change.
original_explanation: It's the Philippines' weather in a nutshell. It's your crush's mood. It's the price of onions at the palengke. It's that constant state of flux that keeps you on your toes. One minute it's sunny, the next it's a typhoon. That's pag-iba-iba.
usage_notes: Refers to a state of being varied or changing over time.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Normal lang ang **pag-iba-iba** ng mood ng isang tinedyer.","translation":"The **fluctuation** of a teenager's mood is just normal."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa **pag-iba-iba** ng presyo, mahirap magbadyet.","translation":"Because of the **variation** in prices, it's hard to budget."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang social media account na nakatuon sa pag-post ng mga nakakahiyang sandali, kabiguan, o kontrobersyal na gawi ng mga sikat na personalidad o iba pang account.
etymology: From English 'flop' + 'account', popularized on Stan Twitter.
original_explanation: The chismosa tita of the internet. These are the social media accounts that exist to call out celebrities, influencers, or even brands when they do something cringey or problematic. They are the keepers of receipts, the masters of screenshots, and the reason why public figures should think before they tweet.
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of online fan communities and social media platforms like X (formerly Twitter).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging viral ang video niya matapos itong i-post ng isang **flop account**.","translation":"Her video went viral after a **flop account** posted it."},{"sentence":"Maraming natatakot na mapunta sa **flop account** kaya maingat sila sa kanilang mga sinasabi online.","translation":"Many are afraid to end up on a **flop account**, so they are careful with what they say online."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng salaan na may malalaking butas, karaniwang ginagamit sa paghihiwalay ng magaspang na butil mula sa pino, tulad ng sa bigas o buhangin.
etymology: From the root "ag-ag" which means 'to sift'. The suffix "-an" denotes a tool or place for the action.
original_explanation: Think of an "ag-agan" as the salaan for the big stuff. It's the tool your lola uses to separate the good rice grains from the 'ipa' (chaff) or small pebbles. In life, your friend group is your "ag-agan" – they help you sift out the fake friends from the real ones.
usage_notes: This is a more traditional or provincial term. "SALAAN" is the more common, general term for a sieve or strainer.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang **ag-agan** upang linisin ang mga butil ng mais.","translation":"He used the **coarse sieve** to clean the corn kernels."},{"sentence":"Humanap ka ng **ag-agan** sa bodega para sa buhangin.","translation":"Look for a **sieve** in the storage room for the sand."}]

translation: to be removed; to be detached; can be removed
meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang maalis, maalis sa pagkakakabit, o mapawalang-bisa.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'ma-' at salitang ugat na 'tanggal' (remove).
original_explanation: The feeling when you finally get to unhook your bra after a long day. Or when you successfully peel off a price tag without leaving that sticky residue. It can also be used for more serious things, like getting fired ('matanggal sa trabaho') which is the ultimate 'unfriended' status in the corporate world.
usage_notes: Isang pandiwang nasa anyong potensyal. Ipinapahiwatig nito ang posibilidad o kakayahang mangyari ang pag-alis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay **matanggal** na ang mantsa sa damit ko.","translation":"I hope the stain on my clothes **can be removed**."},{"sentence":"Nanganganib siyang **matanggal** sa trabaho dahil lagi siyang huli.","translation":"He is in danger of **being removed** from his job because he is always late."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pahayag ng matinding kalungkutan, pagkadismaya, o pagkabigla dahil sa isang masamang pangyayari.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung OG "Hala, bes!" o "OMG, patay!" ng mga lolo't lola natin. Ginagamit kapag nalaman mong tumaas ang presyo ng sibuyas, na-seen ka lang ng crush mo, o kapag napagtanto mong malapit na ang deadline pero nags-scroll ka pa rin. It's the classic Pinoy expression for when things go south.
usage_notes: Isang lumang ekspresyon na madalas marinig sa mga dula, lumang pelikula, o sa mga nakatatanda. Medyo dramatiko ang dating nito sa modernong panahon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sa aba ko!** Naiwan ko ang aking pitaka sa bahay.","translation":"**Woe is me!** I left my wallet at home."},{"sentence":"Nang makita niya ang sirang tanim, napabulalas siya, '**Sa aba ko!**'","translation":"When she saw the ruined plants, she exclaimed, '**Oh my!**'"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na tumatakas o nagtatago mula sa batas, sa isang responsibilidad, o sa isang mapanganib na sitwasyon.
original_explanation: Someone on the run, not for a fun run, but from the law, from their 'utang' to the money lender, or from their responsibilities as an adult. The main character of an action movie, or just you avoiding your landlord.
usage_notes: This noun form has the same spelling and pronunciation as the verb form, but a different meaning. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **takbuhin** ay nagtatago sa liblib na gubat.","translation":"The **fugitives** are hiding in the remote forest."}]

meaning_filipino: Maglagay ng isang bagay sa ibabaw o harapan ng iba pa upang ito ay maitago, maprotektahan, o hindi makita.
original_explanation: What you do when the chismis gets too hot and you cover your mouth in shock. Or when you use your hand to cover your friend's ATM pin from prying eyes. It's the ultimate act of concealment, whether it's covering a pot of adobo or covering up for your sibling's kalokohan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumakip** siya ng unan sa kanyang mukha para hindi marinig ang ingay.","translation":"She **covered** her face with a pillow so she wouldn't hear the noise."}]

meaning_filipino: Posisyon ng paghiga kung saan ang likod ay nasa ibaba at ang harapan ng katawan, lalo na ang tiyan at mukha, ay nakaharap sa itaas.
original_explanation: The default position for binge-watching Netflix, scrolling through TikTok, or contemplating your life choices at 3 AM. Yung pagod na pagod ka na sa adulting, hihiga ka na lang nang tihaya at tititig sa kisame. It's the official posture of weekend relaxation and existential dread.
usage_notes: The opposite of "taob" (lying on one's stomach).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap matulog nang **tihaya** kapag bagong palit ang bedsheet.","translation":"It feels good to sleep **on one's back** when the bedsheets are newly changed."},{"sentence":"Nakita niyang **tihaya** ang sanggol sa kuna, mahimbing na natutulog.","translation":"He saw the baby lying **supine** in the crib, sleeping soundly."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging itim; ang kalagayan ng matinding kadiliman o kawalan ng liwanag.
etymology: From ka- + itim + -an, denoting the abstract quality of being 'black'.
original_explanation: This is the 'emo' level of black. Not just 'itim', but the very essence of it. It's the color of your soul after a rough week, the darkness in a horror movie just before the jump scare, or the color of the strongest, unsweetened kape barako.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for color or figuratively for concepts like gloom, evil, or despair.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakasisilaw ang **kaitiman** ng kanyang buhok.","translation":"The **blackness** of her hair was stunning."},{"sentence":"Bumalot sa buong silid ang **kaitiman** dahil sa pagkawala ng kuryente.","translation":"A deep **darkness** enveloped the whole room due to the power outage."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang halaga o kalagayan na kasya o sapat ngunit walang labis; katamtaman lamang.
original_explanation: This is the official budgetarian motto. When your sweldo comes and you've paid all your bills, what's left is `sapat lamang` to survive until the next payday. It's not a lot, it's not a little, it's just... enough. "Yung pagmamahal na binibigay niya? Sapat lamang. Hindi kulang, pero hindi rin umaapaw."
usage_notes: Nagpapahiwatig ng kakulangan sa sobra o luho.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kinikita niya ay **sapat lamang** para sa kanilang pang-araw-araw na gastusin.","translation":"His income is **just enough** for their daily expenses."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang idyomatikong paglalarawan sa isang tao na sobrang payat o mahina ang pangangatawan, na inihahalintulad sa maninipis na binti ng nasabing ibon.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng "parang" (like/as if) at "kikiyo" (isang uri ng maliit na ibon na kilala sa maninipis na binti).
original_explanation: Your friend who eats a lot but never gains weight. 'Saan mo nilalagay lahat ng kinakain mo, teh? Katawan mo **parang kikiyo**!' It refers to being stick-thin, sometimes with a hint of concern about their health.
usage_notes: Isang idyomatikong ekspresyon para sa pagiging sobrang payat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magpataba ka naman, ang mga binti mo ay **parang kikiyo** na.","translation":"You should gain some weight, your legs are **like a kikiyo's** (very thin)."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos niyang magkasakit, naging **parang kikiyo** ang katawan niya.","translation":"After he got sick, his body became **very frail**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang opisyal na pagsusuri sa mga libro, pelikula, balita, atbp., upang supilin ang mga bahaging itinuturing na hindi katanggap-tanggap, imoral, o isang banta sa seguridad.
original_explanation: Ito yung trabaho ng MTRCB. Sila 'yung naglalagay ng 'SPG' sa TV o nagpuputol ng mga 'love scene' na OA para sa 'General Patronage'. Parang magulang na nagbabantay sa pinapanood mo.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa usapin ng media, sining, at pamahalaan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang **sensura** sa mga palabas sa telebisyon noong panahon ng Martial Law.","translation":"There was strict **censorship** of television shows during the Martial Law era."},{"sentence":"Ikinagalit ng mga direktor ang pagpapataw ng **sensura** sa kanilang mga pelikula.","translation":"The directors were angered by the imposition of **censorship** on their films."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marahan at bahagyang pag-ulan o pag-ambon.
original_explanation: That annoying kind of rain that's too light for an umbrella but will definitely ruin your freshly straightened hair. Parang "mUloK" - 'muka lang ulan'. Hindi full-blown ulan, parang 'almost' relationship niyo lang, hindi nag-commit.
usage_notes: Describes a very fine, misty rain. Often used interchangeably with 'umambon'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula nang **manisnis** kaya binilisan namin ang paglalakad.","translation":"It started to **drizzle lightly** so we quickened our pace."},{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang magpayong, naninisnis lang naman.","translation":"Don't bother with an umbrella, it's just drizzling."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking dalubhasa sa takigrapiya o ang sining ng mabilis na pagsulat gamit ang mga simbolo at pagpapaikli.
original_explanation: The male counterpart of the takigrapa. This guy's shorthand skills were legendary. He could probably write down your entire 'Marites' chika session before you even finished the intro. The original fast hands of the office.
usage_notes: Like 'takigrapa', this term is now considered rare or archaic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **takigrapo** ng korte ay mabilis na nagtala sa kanyang kwaderno.","translation":"The court's **stenographer** quickly took notes in his notebook."},{"sentence":"Bihira na makahanap ng trabaho bilang **takigrapo** sa panahon ngayon.","translation":"It's rare to find a job as a **stenographer** nowadays."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pampublikong pahayag ng mga layunin, intensyon, o pananaw ng isang indibidwal, grupo, partidong pampulitika, o pamahalaan.
original_explanation: Basically a super formal, public "hugot" or declaration. It's what you write when you want the whole world (or just your Facebook friends) to know your platform, your principles, or why you're unfriending toxic people. Think of it as a political party's official list of promises or an artist's detailed explanation of their new, weird art style.
usage_notes: A loanword used in formal, political, or academic contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inilabas ng grupo ang kanilang **manipesto** na nananawagan para sa pagbabago sa sistema.","translation":"The group released their **manifesto** calling for a change in the system."},{"sentence":"Ang **manipesto** ng partido ay naglalaman ng kanilang mga plataporma para sa darating na eleksyon.","translation":"The party's **manifesto** contains their platforms for the upcoming election."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghiwalay ng mga bahagi mula sa isang saradong posisyon, tulad ng bibig, bulaklak, o lupa.
original_explanation: What happens to your mouth when you hear the latest chismis. Also what a flower does in the morning. It’s the gentle unfolding or parting of things, unlike 'bumukas' which is for doors and windows. Think 'open sesame' but for your lips or a blooming rose.
usage_notes: Specific to things that open by parting or unfolding, like mouths, flowers, wounds, or the ground.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumuka** ang bibig niya sa gulat.","translation":"His mouth **opened** in surprise."},{"sentence":"**Bumuka** ang mga bulaklak ng rosas sa hardin.","translation":"The rose buds **opened** in the garden."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kalagayan ng panahon na madilim o malabo dahil sa makakapal na ulap na tumatakip sa araw.
original_explanation: That 'I-cancel-na-ba-natin-ang-outing' weather. It's not raining yet, but the sky is a moody gray, like your friend's face when you eat the last piece of pizza. Perfect weather for a dramatic movie marathon or mag-emote sa bintana.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun (Ang kulimlim ng panahon) or an adjective (Makulimlim ang panahon). It describes the dimness caused by thick clouds.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kulimlim** ang langit kaya nagdala ako ng payong.","translation":"The sky was **overcast**, so I brought an umbrella."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa **kulimlim** na hapon, masarap matulog.","translation":"Because of the **gloomy** afternoon, it's nice to sleep."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bulalas na nagpapahiwatig ng kilig, panunukso, o tuwa, karaniwang ginagamit kapag may nagaganap na romantikong sandali o biruan.
etymology: Onomatopoeic, imitating a squeal of delight or teasing. Variations include 'yiiie', 'yii', and 'ayieee'.
original_explanation: The official sound of third-wheeling. It's what your friends scream when your crush so much as looks in your direction. The more 'e's at the end (e.g., yieee, yieeeee), the higher the level of kilig. It’s the verbal equivalent of the 😏 or 😉 emoji in a romantic context.
usage_notes: The spelling is highly variable (yii, yiiiie, ayieee) but the meaning is the same. It's almost always used in a social, informal setting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Yiee**, binigyan siya ng bulaklak ni crush!","translation":"**Yiee**, her crush gave her flowers!"},{"sentence":"Nakita ko kayong magkasama kahapon, **yiee**!","translation":"I saw you two together yesterday, **yiee**!"}]

translation: to act cute; to try to be cute
meaning_filipino: Ang sinasadyang pagkilos sa paraang kaakit-akit o kaibig-ibig, kadalasan upang makuha ang atensyon o pabor ng iba.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Ingles na 'cute' at ang unlaping 'pa-' na nangangahulugang 'to make oneself' o 'to act as if.'
original_explanation: You know that friend who suddenly changes their voice to a higher pitch and makes puppy eyes when asking for a favor? That's 'pa-cute.' It's the act of weaponizing your cuteness, whether you actually have it or not. It can be endearing or cringe, depending on execution and the target's mood. Think of it as the human equivalent of a cat rubbing against your leg before you feed it.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa negatibong konotasyon, na nagpapahiwatig ng pagiging hindi natural o pilit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang **pa-cute** diyan, hindi kita ililibre ng milk tea.","translation":"Stop **acting cute**, I'm not going to treat you to milk tea."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang palihim na pagkuha ng maliit na halaga o bahagi ng isang bagay na hindi sa iyo; maliit na pagnanakaw.
original_explanation: That thing your office mate does to the communal coffee supply, taking a little bit every day for their house. It's not a full-blown heist, just a sneaky "five-finger discount." Classic "kupit" culture.
usage_notes: Refers to small, often repeated acts of theft, not large-scale robbery. It implies stealth and pettiness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahuli sa CCTV ang pag-**kupit** ng empleyado sa kaban ng bayan.","translation":"The employee's **pilfering** from the cash register was caught on CCTV."},{"sentence":"Ang simpleng **kupit** ay maaaring mauwi sa malaking pagnanakaw.","translation":"Simple **petty theft** can lead to major robbery."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang paningit na katumbas ng 'parang' o 'kasi', karaniwang ginagamit sa impormal na usapan o sa konteksto ng beki lingo.
etymology: Derived from gay lingo (bekimon), possibly a variant of 'kasi' or a standalone creation for phonetic effect.
original_explanation: The ultimate beki (gay slang) filler word. It's the glitter on your sentence. You use it when you're thinking, when you're explaining something with ~flair~, or just to sound more fabulous. 'Ang init, kash! Parang nasa impyerno.' It's the new 'ano' or 'kasi' for the modern marites.
usage_notes: Highly informal. Use only with friends or in very casual settings. Its meaning is heavily dependent on context and intonation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ay, hindi ako makakapunta, **kash** may trabaho pa ako.","translation":"Oh, I can't go, **like**, I still have work."},{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng outfit niya, **kash**, parang pang-red carpet!","translation":"Her outfit is so beautiful, **as in**, it's like for the red carpet!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagmulat mula sa pagkakatulog o ang pagkamulat sa isang katotohanan.
original_explanation: What happens at 5 AM because of your alarm, or at 3 AM because of a random 'what if' thought. Can also be figurative, like when you finally realized your ex was toxic. 'Buti na lang at nagising ako sa katotohanan.'
usage_notes: This is the completed action (past tense). It can be used literally for waking from sleep or figuratively for coming to a realization.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagising** ako dahil sa malakas na tahol ng aso.","translation":"I **woke up** because of the dog's loud barking."},{"sentence":"Parang **nagising** siya sa isang masamang panaginip nang malaman niya ang totoo.","translation":"It was as if she **woke up** from a nightmare when she learned the truth."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita o may katangian ng pagkainggit o pagnanasa sa tagumpay, ari-arian, o kalagayan ng iba.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung tropa mong 'di makatiis 'pag may bago kang gadget. Imbes na "congrats," ang maririnig mo "sana all." 'Yung tingin niya sa'yo, parang gusto niyang agawin 'yung bago mong sapatos. A **mapanaghili** person is a professional hater disguised as a friend.
usage_notes: Describes a person's character or disposition. Stronger and more active than "mainggitin."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang isang **mapanaghiling** tao ay hindi kailanman magiging tunay na masaya.","translation":"An **envious** person will never be truly happy."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **mapanaghili** sa tagumpay ng iyong kapwa.","translation":"Do not be **jealous** of your neighbor's success."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manipis at malinaw na plastik na karaniwang ginagamit bilang pambalot ng pagkain o iba pang produkto.
original_explanation: This is the *actual* plastic wrap, 'yung pambalot ng yema, pastillas, o kaya 'yung sa bulaklak na binibigay mo sa jowa mo. It's the more formal, less common cousin of 'selopeyn,' which most people now use to mean 'tape.' Think of it as the clear, crinkly stuff, not the sticky one.
usage_notes: While 'selopin' is the more accurate term for cellophane wrap, 'selopeyn' (tape) is more commonly used in daily conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga kendi ay nakabalot sa makukulay na **selopin**.","translation":"The candies are wrapped in colorful **cellophane**."},{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng **selopin** upang hindi malanta agad ang mga bulaklak.","translation":"She used **cellophane** so the flowers wouldn't wilt quickly."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi maaaring kunin, kilalanin, o pahintulutan; labag sa pamantayan o kalooban.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `di-` (hindi) at `matatanggap` (aspektong panghinaharap ng 'matanggap'), na galing sa salitang ugat na `tanggap`.
original_explanation: This is the official status of your friend request from your crush for the past 3 years. It's also the company's response to your leave request during peak season. Basically, it's a hard "NOPE." Something so out of line, it can't be allowed.
usage_notes: Mas matindi kaysa sa 'hindi tinanggap'. Ipinahihiwatig nito na ang isang bagay ay likas na hindi katanggap-tanggap dahil labag ito sa mga alituntunin, ngayon at sa hinaharap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganitong uri ng pag-uugali ay **di-matatanggap** sa aming paaralan.","translation":"This kind of behavior is **unacceptable** in our school."},{"sentence":"Para sa akin, **di-matatanggap** ang anumang dahilan para sa panloloko.","translation":"For me, any reason for cheating is **unacceptable**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sikat na online multiplayer 'battle royale' game kung saan ang mga manlalaro ay naglalaban-laban hanggang sa may isang natitirang manalo.
etymology: Acronym for the game title PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds.
original_explanation: Acronym for 'PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds,' but in the Philippines, it's a valid excuse for not answering texts ('Sorry, nag-pubg'), a source of domestic arguments ('Pubg na naman?!'), and a new skill to add to your dating profile ('marunong magluto at mag-clutch sa pubg').
usage_notes: Often used as a verb, e.g., 'Nag-pubg ako' (I played PUBG).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tara, isang laro lang ng **pubg**.","translation":"Come on, just one game of **pubg**."},{"sentence":"Naubos ang data niya kaka-**pubg**.","translation":"His data ran out from playing too much **pubg**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng papel, karton, kahoy, o metal na may nakasulat o nakaguhit na anunsyo, babala, o impormasyon na ipinapakita sa publiko.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "cartel" o "carátula" (title page, mask).
original_explanation: That thing you see everywhere from "Bawal Umihi Dito" to "For Sale: House and Lot with 50 years of family drama". It's the original social media post, posted on a wall instead of a timeline.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nabasag ang **karatula** ng tindahan dahil sa malakas na hangin.","translation":"The store's **signboard** broke because of the strong wind."},{"sentence":"May hawak silang **karatula** na nagsasabing 'Itigil ang Korapsyon!'","translation":"They were holding a **placard** that said 'Stop Corruption!'"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na nangyayari o ginagawa paminsan-minsan lamang; hindi palagian.
original_explanation: Describes something you do, but not often enough to be a habit. Like that gym membership you use once a month, or that 'healthy' salad you eat in between servings of crispy pata. "Hindi ako laging umiinom ng kape, okasyonal lang." (Says the person on their third cup of the day).
usage_notes: Used to describe the frequency of an event or action. Synonymous with 'paminsan-minsan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-ulan ng yelo sa Pilipinas ay isang **okasyonal** na pangyayari.","translation":"Hail in the Philippines is an **occasional** event."},{"sentence":"**Okasyonal** lang kaming lumalabas para kumain sa mamahaling restaurant.","translation":"We only **occasionally** go out to eat at expensive restaurants."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na ginawa upang maging eksaktong katulad ng isa pa; isang reproduksyon o duplikasyon.
original_explanation: What you ask from your classmate when you were absent yesterday: 'Pahingi ng kopya ng notes!' Also, the result of a Xerox machine, or right-clicking a file and choosing 'Copy'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng dalawang **kopya** ng aking birth certificate.","translation":"I need two **copies** of my birth certificate."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang sining ay isang **kopya** lamang ng gawa ng isang sikat na pintor.","translation":"His art is just a **copy** of a famous painter's work."}]

translation: to be able to shock; to horrify; to cause terror
meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang magdulot ng matinding takot, pagkasindak, o pagkabigla sa isang tao.
original_explanation: This is that feeling you get when you see your phone bill after a month of 'unli-data' that wasn't actually unlimited. It's the shock and awe, horror movie style, but for your wallet. Parang multo sa dilim, pero sa totoong buhay.
usage_notes: Often used to describe something overwhelmingly frightening or shocking, like a horrific event or a powerful performance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang balitang iyon ay talagang **makasindak** sa buong bansa.","translation":"That news was truly able **to shock** the entire nation."},{"sentence":"May kakayahan siyang **makasindak** ng mga manonood sa kanyang pag-arte.","translation":"She has the ability **to horrify** the audience with her acting."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na namumuhay nang may kabanalan, malapit sa Diyos, at itinuturing na may pambihirang kabutihan at debosyon.
original_explanation: This is your lola who goes to church every single day, or that one officemate who never says a bad word about anyone and seems to radiate kindness. Sometimes used sarcastically for someone who acts 'holier-than-thou.' 'Wow, di umiinom? **Taong banal** ka ba?'
usage_notes: Can be used sincerely to describe a pious person or sarcastically for someone who is self-righteous.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Mother Teresa ay kinikilala bilang isang **taong banal** dahil sa kanyang paglilingkod sa mga mahihirap.","translation":"Mother Teresa is recognized as a **holy person** for her service to the poor."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang de-kuryenteng sasakyan na tumatakbo sa ibabaw ng riles sa kalsada, ginamit bilang pampublikong transportasyon noong unang panahon sa Maynila.
original_explanation: The same as a "tram," but with a more Spanish-Filipino flavor. This was the original "beep card" ride of our great-grandparents. It's the OG of Manila's public transport, a historical icon that makes you feel nostalgic for a time you never even lived in.
usage_notes: Isang salitang pangkasaysayan. Mas kilala ito kaysa sa "tram" sa Pilipinas para tukuyin ang dating sistema ng transportasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Makikita sa mga lumang larawan ang mga **trambia** na puno ng pasahero sa Avenida Rizal.","translation":"You can see in old pictures the **streetcars** full of passengers on Avenida Rizal."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangungusap, parirala, o salita na humihingi ng impormasyon o kasagutan.
original_explanation: The thing you have a million of during a meeting that could've been an email. It's the classic "Saan tayo kakain?" that never gets a straight answer. It's the "Mahal mo pa ba ako?" that you're afraid to ask. A **tanong** is the start of all 'chismis', all knowledge, and all complicated relationships.
usage_notes: The verb form is 'magtanong' (to ask). The more formal noun is 'katanungan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **tanong** ako tungkol sa ating aralin.","translation":"I have a **question** about our lesson."},{"sentence":"Mahirap sagutin ang kanyang mga **tanong**.","translation":"His **questions** are hard to answer."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang tao na may malalim na kakayahang mangarap o palaging nag-iisip ng mga mithiin; isang taong nangangarap.
etymology: From "ma-" (adjective prefix) + "pangarap" (dream) + "-in" (suffix indicating a characteristic or tendency).
original_explanation: Slightly different from 'mapangarap.' This is the person themselves, the 'dreamer.' Sila yung tipo na kahit nasa jeep na siksikan, ang isip lumilipad na sa Paris. They are the artists, the writers, the innovators. It's a title, a state of being. You don't just have dreams, you *are* a dreamer.
usage_notes: While 'mapangarap' describes the quality of having dreams, 'mapangarapin' often refers to the person who is a dreamer. It can function as both an adjective and a noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Likas siyang **mapangarapin**, kaya sumali siya sa teatro.","translation":"She is a natural **dreamer**, so she joined the theater."},{"sentence":"Ang mga **mapangarapin** ang nagdadala ng pagbabago sa mundo.","translation":"The **dreamers** are the ones who bring change to the world."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malapad na piraso ng kahoy o metal sa likuran ng isang bangka o barko na ginagamit upang imaneho o gabayan ang direksyon nito.
original_explanation: Before there was a steering wheel, there was the dimon. It's the thing at the back of a boat that decides if you're going straight to your destination or ending up in a completely different barangay. Metaphorically, it's your moral compass or the principles that steer your life. 'Nawalan ng dimon' means you've lost control.
usage_notes: Primarily used in a nautical context. Sometimes used metaphorically to mean 'guidance' or 'control'. The original Spanish spelling 'timon' is also used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinira ng malakas na alon ang **dimon** ng kanilang bangka.","translation":"The strong waves broke their boat's **rudder**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga magulang ang nagsisilbing **dimon** sa buhay ng kanilang mga anak.","translation":"Parents serve as the **rudder** in their children's lives."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang portable na teleponong de-baterya na gumagamit ng cellular network para sa komunikasyon.
original_explanation: Ang extension ng kamay ng bawat Pilipino. Mas mahalaga pa sa wallet minsan. Dito nakasalalay ang Gcash mo, ang landi mo sa chat, at ang pag-stalk mo kay crush. Kapag naiwan mo 'to sa bahay, parang katapusan na ng mundo.
usage_notes: Bagama't ang "cellphone" ay karaniwan pa rin, ang "phone" o "cp" (para sa numero) ay mas madalas gamitin sa kaswal na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawala ang **cellphone** ko sa bus.","translation":"I lost my **cellphone** on the bus."},{"sentence":"Paki-charge naman ng **cellphone** ko, lowbatt na.","translation":"Please charge my **cellphone**, the battery is low."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang propesyonal na tumutulong sa mga indibidwal, pamilya, at komunidad upang mapabuti ang kanilang kapakanan at malampasan ang mga suliraning panlipunan.
original_explanation: The real-life Darna. They're the ones who swoop into crisis situations—family problems, abuse cases, community disasters—armed with paperwork, empathy, and an unbelievable amount of patience. They work for the DSWD or NGOs, often underpaid but over-dedicated.
usage_notes: This is a specific professional title.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinausap ng **manggagawang panlipunan** ang mga batang lansangan.","translation":"The **social worker** talked to the street children."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng mas maraming **manggagawang panlipunan** sa mga nasalanta ng bagyo.","translation":"More **social workers** are needed in the areas affected by the typhoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sukat ng isang bagay mula sa isang gilid patungo sa kabilang gilid; ang kaluwangan o distansyang pahalang.
original_explanation: The 'how thicc?' measurement. It's what you check when buying furniture to see if it'll fit through the door, or when you're judging if you can squeeze through a tight space in the MRT.
usage_notes: Used in measurements, along with 'haba' (length) and 'taas' (height).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sukatin mo ang **lapad** ng mesa bago natin bilhin.","translation":"Measure the **width** of the table before we buy it."},{"sentence":"Ano ang **lapad** at haba ng lote ninyo?","translation":"What are the **width** and length of your lot?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang titulo ng paggalang na inilalagay bago ang pangalan ng isang taong mas matanda o may mataas na katayuan, karaniwan sa mga lalawigan. Ito ay pinaikling anyo ng 'kapatid'.
etymology: Shortened form of "kapatid" (sibling), used to denote camaraderie and respect.
original_explanation: This is the OG term of respect, often used in provinces, that comes before a name. Think of it as the rural equivalent of "Manong" or "Manang." When you hear "Ka Roger," you know you're talking to a respected elder in the community, not just some random dude named Roger. It has a vibe of community, respect, and a bit of revolutionary history.
usage_notes: Carries a strong sense of respect and is often associated with historical figures, community leaders, or elders in rural areas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si **Ka** Ambo ang pinuno ng aming barangay.","translation":"**Ka** Ambo is the leader of our village."},{"sentence":"Magandang umaga po, **Ka** Tasyo.","translation":"Good morning, **Ka** Tasyo."}]

translation: to cause to sag; to make something bend downwards
meaning_filipino: Pasanhiin o maging dahilan ng paglundo o pagyuko ng isang bagay dahil sa bigat o kawalan ng suporta.
etymology: From pa- prefix + lundo (sag, dip) + -in suffix, a causative verb form.
original_explanation: When you overload the 'sampayan' with wet jeans and it starts to droop—that's 'palunduin'. It's what happens to your shoulders after a 12-hour shift, or to a bridge with too many cars. It’s the action of defeating gravity's opponent.
usage_notes: This is a less common word. 'Lundo' or 'lumulundo' (is sagging) are more frequently heard.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong punuin masyado ang sako at baka **palunduin** mo ang sanga ng puno.","translation":"Don't fill the sack too much, you might **cause** the tree branch **to sag**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang trabaho ay magkatay ng hayop para sa karne, o maghiwa at magbenta nito.
etymology: Hiram na salita mula sa Ingles na 'butcher'.
original_explanation: Not just the English word, but a Pinoy job title. Sila 'yung suki mo sa palengke na hihingian mo ng 'pang-adobo cut' or 'pang-sinigang cut'. They know their way around a slab of meat better than you know your way around your feelings. Also used for someone who messes up a language badly, e.g., 'Don't butcher the Tagalog.'
usage_notes: A common loanword used in markets and daily conversations. It can also be used as a verb in Taglish ('na-butcher') to mean something was ruined or done poorly.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala ang **butcher** sa amin sa pagiging tapat sa timbangan.","translation":"The **butcher** in our area is known for being honest with the weighing scale."},{"sentence":"Nagpahiwa ako sa **butcher** ng karneng baboy para sa menudo.","translation":"I had the **butcher** slice the pork for the menudo."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng molusko na may dalawang kabibe, karaniwang kulay berde o itim, na naninirahan sa tubig-alat at kinakain bilang pagkain.
original_explanation: The go-to pulutan when you're on a budget but still want to feel fancy. Best cooked with ginger and lemongrass (tinola-style) or baked with cheese and garlic. Warning: a bad batch can lead to a *very* bad time, a phenomenon known as "nalason sa tahong."
usage_notes: "Tahong" almost exclusively refers to the green mussel (*Perna viridis*).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap ang nilutong **tahong** ni nanay.","translation":"Mom's cooked **mussels** are delicious."},{"sentence":"Bumili kami ng isang kilong **tahong** sa palengke.","translation":"We bought a kilo of **mussels** at the market."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong tumutulong o sumusuporta sa iba sa kanilang gawain, partikular sa isang propesyonal na kapasidad.
original_explanation: The person who knows more about the boss's schedule than the boss themself. In the PH context, they're the one you befriend to get an appointment. The real power behind the throne.
usage_notes: Commonly used in professional and business settings in the Philippines, often preferred over the Tagalog "katulong" or "katuwang" in these contexts to avoid connotations of being a domestic helper.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tawagan mo ang **assistant** ko para i-set ang meeting.","translation":"Call my **assistant** to set the meeting."},{"sentence":"Siya ang bagong executive **assistant** ng CEO.","translation":"She is the new executive **assistant** to the CEO."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga produkto na ipinapahid sa mukha o katawan upang mapabuti o baguhin ang itsura, tulad ng lipstick, pulbos, at mascara.
original_explanation: The modern-day 'gayuma' you buy from Watsons or Sephora. It's your war paint for the daily battle, whether it's for a client presentation, a first date, or just to feel 'ganda' while buying suka at the sari-sari store. From 'no-makeup makeup look' to full-on drag queen glam, ito ang sandata mo.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun (mga kosmetiko) or an adjective (gamit na kosmetiko).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang bumili ng iba't ibang **kosmetiko** online.","translation":"She loves buying various **cosmetics** online."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng puwersa upang mapaalis o mapagalaw ang isang bagay; pag-alis o pagbyahe; pagbebenta ng maliliit na bagay.
original_explanation: This word has layers, like a good adobo. 1) Literally pushing something, like a broken-down car or a grocery cart (kariton). 2) When a jeep or bus is about to leave the terminal, "Tumutulak na!" 3) The street-level meaning: pushing or selling goods, sometimes illicitly. So, context is everything. Are you pushing a cart, a bus, or... something else?
usage_notes: Present/Progressive aspect of the verb 'tumulak'. Has multiple meanings depending on context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumutulak** siya ng kariton para mabuhay.","translation":"He is **pushing** a cart to make a living."},{"sentence":"Alas-singko ng umaga kung **tumulak** ang unang biyahe ng bus.","translation":"The first bus trip **departs** at five in the morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Sunugin ang isang bagay hanggang sa ito ay maging abo o maubos nang tuluyan.
etymology: From the root 'supok', meaning to be consumed by fire or smoke.
original_explanation: What you want to do with all the evidence of your cringe teenage photos. To supukin is to burn something so thoroughly there's nothing left but dust and regret. Think of it as the final stage after 'sunugin'. It's total annihilation by fire.
usage_notes: Implies a more intense and complete burning than the more common 'sunugin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinabihan siyang **supukin** ang lahat ng tuyong dahon sa bakuran.","translation":"He was told to **incinerate** all the dry leaves in the yard."},{"sentence":"Gusto kong **supukin** ang lahat ng masasamang alaala.","translation":"I want to **burn completely** all the bad memories."}]

meaning_filipino: Igalaw nang paurong-sulong o pataas-pababa ang isang bagay, karaniwang mga braso, kamay, o anumang hawak.
original_explanation: 'Yung pag-cheer mo sa paborito mong basketball team, todo ikampay ka ng banner. Or 'yung feeling na nanalo ka sa raffle, you wave your arms in the air like you just don't care. It's the motion of victory, a desperate "para, para!" to the jeepney driver, or just shooing away a giant ipis.
usage_notes: Often refers to arms, flags, or wings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ikinampay** niya ang kanyang mga braso bilang pagbati.","translation":"He **waved** his arms as a greeting."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ikampay** ang basang payong sa loob ng bahay!","translation":"Don't **swing** the wet umbrella inside the house!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagkaing karaniwang binubuo ng pinaghalong mga sangkap, tulad ng prutas, gulay, o pasta, na kadalasang may kasamang dressing o sarsa.
original_explanation: In the Philippines, this isn't just lettuce and tomatoes. This is Buko Salad, Macaroni Salad, or Fruit Salad—creamy, sweet, and swimming in condensed milk. It's the star of every Noche Buena and fiesta, the 'healthy' dessert you eat after three cups of rice and lechon.
usage_notes: A direct loanword, but with a distinctly Filipino application focusing on sweet, creamy dessert salads rather than savory vegetable ones.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gagawa si nanay ng fruit **salad** para sa Pasko.","translation":"Mom will make fruit **salad** for Christmas."},{"sentence":"Paborito kong handa sa birthday ang macaroni **salad**.","translation":"Macaroni **salad** is my favorite dish served at birthdays."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na nahati o nabiyak sa dalawang bahagi, lalo na ang mga bagay na matitigas tulad ng kahoy o kawayan.
original_explanation: Imagine you're trying to chop firewood like a pro, but you only manage to split it halfway. That's **baak**. It's that satisfying *CRACK* sound made visible. Also, the state of your heart after seeing your crush with someone else. Ouch, baak.
usage_notes: Often used for wood, bamboo, or sometimes even bone. Implies a large, longitudinal split, different from 'basag' (shattered) or 'putol' (snapped).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **baak** ang kawayan dahil sa lakas ng hangin.","translation":"The bamboo became **split** because of the strong wind."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong gamitin 'yan, **baak** na ang hawakan.","translation":"Don't use that, the handle is already **cracked**."}]

translation: to give aid to; to assist
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng tulong o suporta sa isang tao, grupo, o lugar.
original_explanation: The verb form of "ayuda." This is what the government *tries* to do, or what you do when your friend is broke before payday. "Ayudahan mo naman ako" is a slightly more formal way of saying "Pautang!" or "Libre mo 'ko!"
usage_notes: Focus is on the recipient of the aid.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **ayudahan** ang mga pamilyang nawalan ng tirahan dahil sa baha.","translation":"The families who lost their homes due to the flood need **to be given aid**."},{"sentence":"Sino ang dapat **ayudahan** ng gobyerno sa panahong ito?","translation":"Who should the government **assist** at this time?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahalaga at maningning na metal na may kulay dilaw, ginagamit sa paggawa ng alahas, barya, at iba pang palamuti.
original_explanation: The OG bling. Before credit cards and Gcash, this was the ultimate status symbol. In the Philippines, it's also part of a superstitious counting game for stairs: "**oro**, plata, mata" (gold, silver, death). You always want to end on **oro** or plata, never mata. So next time you build a house, count the steps!
usage_notes: 'Ginto' is the more common, native Tagalog term. 'Oro' is often used in specific contexts like the "oro, plata, mata" superstition or in jewelry shop names.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa pag-akyat ng hagdan, ang bilang ay dapat magtapos sa **oro** o plata.","translation":"When going up the stairs, the count should end on **gold** or silver."},{"sentence":"Ang singsing ay yari sa purong **oro**.","translation":"The ring is made of pure **gold**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lupang sinilangan o ang lugar kung saan isinilang at lumaki ang isang tao; ang inang-bayan.
etymology: Compound word from "bayan" (country) and "tinubuan" (place where something grew), from the root "tubo" (to grow).
original_explanation: This is the poetic, "Lupang Hinirang" version of where you're from. It's not just your hometown; it's the land where your roots grew, your *motherland*. It has that deep, nostalgic, OFW-missing-home kind of vibe. You don't just say "I'm going to my **bayang-tinubuan**"; you say it with a hand over your heart, probably while looking at a sunset.
usage_notes: A more formal and literary term for 'homeland' or 'motherland'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matagal na niyang hindi nabibisita ang kanyang **bayang-tinubuan**.","translation":"He has not visited his **homeland** for a long time."},{"sentence":"Palaging nasa puso ng mga OFW ang kanilang **bayang-tinubuan**.","translation":"The **motherland** is always in the hearts of OFWs."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal para sa paa ng manok na karaniwang inihahaw at itinitinda bilang pagkaing kalye.
etymology: Named after the "Adidas" brand, as the three claws of the chicken foot resemble the brand's three-stripe logo.
original_explanation: No, not the shoes. In the Philippines, 'adidas' is the street food name for grilled or fried chicken feet. Why? Because the three main claws look like the three stripes of the Adidas logo. It's a classic 'tusok-tusok' staple, best enjoyed with a spicy vinegar dip. It's proof that Pinoys are so resourceful, even the feet don't go to waste.
usage_notes: A very common slang term for a specific street food.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pabili po ng limang pirasong **adidas** at isang isaw.","translation":"I'd like to buy five pieces of **chicken feet** and one 'isaw' (chicken intestine)."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang timpla ng **adidas** sa ihawan na iyon.","translation":"The marinade for the **chicken feet** at that grill stand is delicious."}]

translation: the act or state of having tripped or stumbled
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o akto ng pagkadapa o pagka-tisod dahil sa isang bagay na sumabit sa paa.
original_explanation: Ever walked in Divisoria and suddenly you're eating pavement because you tripped on a random box or a rogue extension cord? That moment of sudden, ungraceful, gravity-assisted faceplant is pagkabayakid. It's the physical version of 'sana all' when you see someone else succeed while you're stumbling.
usage_notes: Less common than 'pagkadapa' or 'pagkatisod'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagdulot ng malaking hiya ang kanyang **pagkabayakid** sa gitna ng entablado.","translation":"His **stumble** in the middle of the stage caused great embarrassment."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kalagayan ng prutas o gulay na labis na sa pagkahinog, malambot na, at malapit nang mabulok.
original_explanation: That banana you forgot in your bag for three days. It's not just 'hinog', it's 'hinog na hinog to the point of no return'. Perfect for banana bread, but sad for eating as is.
usage_notes: Primarily used for fruits and vegetables. Connotes a mushy, overly soft texture.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang kainin 'yan, **kalabsakan** na ang mangga.","translation":"Don't eat that anymore, the mango is already **overripe**."},{"sentence":"Naging **kalabsakan** ang mga kamatis dahil sa sobrang init.","translation":"The tomatoes became **mushy** because of the extreme heat."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso, seksyon, o parte na bumubuo sa isang kabuuan.
original_explanation: Your share of the bill after a group lunch. Or that part of your heart you gave to your ex that you can never get back. #hugot. It's the 'parte' in 'parte-parte tayo'.
usage_notes: This is a root word. It can be used to form verbs like 'ibahagi' (to share something) and 'magbahagi' (to share/distribute).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kunin mo na ang **bahagi** mo sa cake.","translation":"Take your **share** of the cake."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-aaral ay mahalagang **bahagi** ng buhay.","translation":"Studying is an important **part** of life."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na termino para sa matalik na kaibigan, direktang hiniram mula sa Ingles.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Ingles na "bestie," pinaikling "best friend."
original_explanation: Ito 'yung original English slang na na-adopt na rin sa Pinas. Medyo mas conyo or Gen Z ang dating kumpara sa 'bes'. Ito 'yung tawag mo sa kaibigan mong kasama mo sa lahat ng TikTok dance challenges.
usage_notes: Malawakang ginagamit sa social media at sa mga nakababatang henerasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"OMG, **bestie**, nakita mo ba 'yung bagong post niya?","translation":"OMG, **bestie**, did you see his new post?"},{"sentence":"Ikaw lang ang nakakaintindi sa akin, **bestie**.","translation":"You're the only one who understands me, **bestie**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong ang trabaho ay itala ang mga transaksyong pampinansyal ng isang negosyo o kumpanya; isang tagatuos.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "tenedor de libro" na nangangahulugang "tagahawak ng aklat".
original_explanation: The OG accountant. Before Excel sheets and accounting software, there was the tenedor-de-libro, meticulously writing down every peso and centavo in a giant ledger. Think of your tita who lists down every single utang in her notebook, but make it a formal profession.
usage_notes: Isang salitang luma na at bihirang gamitin sa kasalukuyan. Ang mga salitang "accountant" o "tagatuos" ay mas karaniwan na.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang dating trabaho ng lolo ko sa isang pabrika ay bilang **tenedor-de-libro**.","translation":"My grandfather's old job at a factory was as a **bookkeeper**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng kumpanya ng isang mahusay na **tenedor-de-libro** upang ayusin ang kanilang mga talaan.","translation":"The company needs a skilled **accountant** to fix their records."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggalaw sa isang likido o pinaghalong mga sangkap gamit ang isang kagamitan upang maging pantay ang pagkakahalo nito.
original_explanation: That thing you do to your morning coffee, or to your feelings when you see your crush with someone else. You stir things up, literally and figuratively. It's the process of blending everything together, whether it's 3-in-1 coffee or complicated emotions.
usage_notes: Used for mixing liquids or ingredients in cooking. Can also be used metaphorically to mean 'to confuse' or 'to jumble'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Haluin** mong mabuti ang sarsa para hindi mamuo.","translation":"**Stir** the sauce well so it doesn't form lumps."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang **haluin** pa ang isipan ko, please lang.","translation":"Please don't **confuse** my thoughts anymore."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kataga o ekspresyon na nagpapahiwatig ng pagkagulat, pagtataka, o kawalan ng paniniwala, katumbas ng 'pala' o 'naman pala'.
original_explanation: That short, sharp sound you make when you realize something you didn't know before. It's the Pinoy version of 'Oh, really?', 'Is that so?', or 'Huh!'. Example: 'Akala ko single pa siya.' 'May asawa na 'yan.' 'La!' It's a filler word that packs a punch of surprise.
usage_notes: Primarily used in spoken, informal conversation. Its meaning is heavily dependent on tone and is often used to express mild surprise or sudden realization.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**La**! Ikaw pala 'yan! Akala ko kung sino.","translation":"**Oh**! So it was you! I thought it was someone else."},{"sentence":"A: 'Umuwi na si Mark.' B: '**La**! Ang aga naman.'","translation":"A: 'Mark already went home.' B: '**Oh**! That's so early.'"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng muling pagsasaayos ng estruktura, sistema, o mga bahagi ng isang bagay, tulad ng isang kumpanya o organisasyon.
original_explanation: That corporate memo you get that makes everyone nervous. It means 'to reorganize.' It's when your boss decides to shuffle teams, change job descriptions, or move your desk to the other side of the office. It's the corporate version of 'Nililinis ko lang kwarto ko,' but for a whole department, and someone might lose their chair.
usage_notes: A formal verb used in business, government, and organizational contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **reorganisahin** ang buong departamento upang maging mas mahusay.","translation":"The whole department needs **to be reorganized** to become more efficient."},{"sentence":"Plano ng bagong CEO na **reorganisahin** ang pamunuan ng kumpanya.","translation":"The new CEO plans **to reorganize** the company's leadership."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng ayon sa isang utos, tuntunin, o halimbawa; ang pagpunta o paggalaw sa likuran o sa direksyon ng isang nauuna.
original_explanation: The word has two main flavors: 1) Obeying: what your parents demand when they say, "Sumunod ka sa akin!" (Obey me!). 2) Following: what you do when you're stalking your crush's IG stories, or literally tailing a car in traffic. It's about aligning your actions or path with someone or something that came before.
usage_notes: Can mean both literal following (as in a chase) and figurative following (as in obeying rules). Context is key.
