usage_notes: A very important concept in Filipino psychology. As a pronoun, it means "fellow being." As an adjective, it means "both" or "fellow."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat nating mahalin ang ating **kapwa**.","translation":"We should love our **fellow** human beings."},{"sentence":"**Kapwa** sila nag-aral nang mabuti para sa pagsusulit.","translation":"**Both** of them studied well for the exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salaysay ng mga pangyayaring hindi lubos na makatotohanan na nagpapaliwanag sa pinagmulan ng isang bagay, pook, o pangyayari.
etymology: From Arabic "علامة" (ʿalāma), meaning sign, mark, or token, via Malay.
original_explanation: Before Wikipedia, we had 'alamat'. These are the OG "How It's Made" episodes of the Philippines, explaining why pineapples have a hundred eyes (Pinya), or how a mountain got its shape (Maria Makiling). It's a story your lola tells you that's part history, part fantasy, and 100% a lesson about not being lazy or disrespectful.
usage_notes: A staple of Philippine literature, often taught in elementary and high school Filipino classes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong basahin ang **alamat** ng pinya noong ako'y bata pa.","translation":"My favorite to read was the **legend** of the pineapple when I was a child."},{"sentence":"Ang bawat bayan ay may kani-kaniyang **alamat** na ipinapasa sa bawat henerasyon.","translation":"Every town has its own **folklore** passed down through each generation."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sistema o paraan ng paglilipat ng mga tao, hayop, o kalakal mula sa isang lugar patungo sa iba.
original_explanation: The formal, textbook term for your daily commute struggle. It's what you blame when you're late for work, even if you just woke up 30 minutes ago. "Sorry, boss, ang hirap ng transportasyon!" is the national motto.
usage_notes: This is the standard and formal term for 'transportation'. 'Trapiko' (traffic) is a related but distinct concept often affecting it.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagpapaunlad ng pampublikong **transportasyon** ay prayoridad ng bagong administrasyon.","translation":"The development of public **transportation** is a priority of the new administration."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang maayos na **transportasyon** para sa paglago ng ekonomiya.","translation":"A proper **transportation** system is important for economic growth."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malapot at matamis na likido, na maaaring gamitin bilang gamot, sa pagkain tulad ng pancake, o bilang pampatamis sa inumin.
original_explanation: Either the stuff you get from the doctor that tastes like fake cherries but you have to drink it anyway, OR the glorious liquid you drown your pancakes in. Also, the magical ingredient in your favorite milk tea.
usage_notes: Ginagamit para sa parehong medikal at pangkusina na mga syrup. Ang 'arnibal' ay isang katutubong katumbas para sa caramelized sugar syrup.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang inumin ang **syrup** para sa ubo mo, anak.","translation":"Don't forget to drink your cough **syrup**, child."},{"sentence":"Pakiabot ng **syrup** para sa pancake.","translation":"Please pass the **syrup** for the pancake."}]

translation: a type of two-masted native sailboat
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng tradisyonal na sasakyang-pandagat sa Pilipinas na may dalawang layag, na ginagamit para sa pangingisda o paghakot ng kalakal.
original_explanation: Before container ships and RORO ferries, the batel was one of the workhorses of the Philippine seas. It's a classic wooden sailboat, bigger than a bangka, used for transporting goods between islands. Think of it as the historical equivalent of a Lalamove cargo truck, but for the ocean, powered by wind and sheer grit.
usage_notes: An archaic term, mostly used in historical or literary contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng mga kopra ang **batel** na dumaong sa pantalan.","translation":"The **sailboat** that docked at the pier was full of copra."},{"sentence":"Sa mga lumang kwento, ang mga bayani ay naglalakbay sakay ng isang matatag na **batel**.","translation":"In old stories, heroes would travel aboard a sturdy **batel**."}]

translation: act of looking back; turning one's head
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbaling ng ulo o mukha upang tumingin sa likuran o sa isang partikular na direksyon.
original_explanation: That quick turn of the head when you hear someone call your name, or when you hear the "psst!" of a chismosa. It's the classic move in horror movies right before the jump scare. Also, the metaphorical act of looking back at your past, your "hugot" moments, or your ex. "Bawal lumingon," they say, but sometimes, a little paglingos is needed.
usage_notes: Refers to the physical action of turning the head to look. Can be used metaphorically for looking back at the past.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang mabilis na **paglingos** lang ang ginawa niya bago tuluyang umalis.","translation":"He just gave a quick **look back** before finally leaving."},{"sentence":"Sa kanyang **paglingos**, nakita niya ang matagal nang nawawalang kaibigan.","translation":"Upon **turning his head**, he saw his long-lost friend."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang masidhing pagmamahal, paggalang, at pagiging tapat sa sariling bansa.
original_explanation: It's that feeling you get when Manny Pacquiao has a fight, when a Filipino wins an international competition, or when you hear 'Lupang Hinirang' played abroad. It's more than just wearing a flag-themed shirt during Independence Day. It's about supporting local products, paying your taxes (ouch), and maybe not throwing your trash just anywhere. It’s loving your country, warts and all.
usage_notes: The more common, nativized term is 'pagkamakabayan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagtangkilik sa sariling produkto ay isang uri ng **patriotismo**.","translation":"Patronizing our own products is a form of **patriotism**."},{"sentence":"Ipinamalas ng mga bayani ang kanilang **patriotismo** sa pamamagitan ng pagsasakripisyo ng buhay.","translation":"The heroes showed their **patriotism** by sacrificing their lives."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbuo at paglabas ng nana mula sa isang sugat o impeksiyon.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you don't clean a wound properly, or when you keep poking at a pimple. It's the body's gross but effective way of saying, "Hey, there's a party of bacteria in here and I'm kicking them out." Think of it as your skin's version of a messy breakup—there's a lot of drama and unpleasant stuff coming out.
usage_notes: Often used in a medical or descriptive context for infected wounds.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong pilitin na putukin ang pigsa dahil baka **magnana** lang iyan lalo.","translation":"Don't force bursting the boil because it might just **fester** even more."},{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **magnana** ang sugat niya dahil hindi nalinis nang maayos.","translation":"His wound started to **suppurate** because it wasn't cleaned properly."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagsagawa ng sekswal na pag-atake o panggagahasa sa isang tao laban sa kanyang kalooban.
original_explanation: A very serious and heavy word. This is the past tense, actor-focus verb for the crime of rape. There is no witty way to put this; it refers to a heinous act of sexual violence and should be used with gravity.
usage_notes: A word with a very strong and negative connotation, used in legal and serious contexts. The object-focus form 'ginahasa' (was raped) is more commonly used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang salarin na **gumahasa** sa biktima ay nahuli na ng mga pulis.","translation":"The culprit who **raped** the victim has been caught by the police."},{"sentence":"Kinasuhan ng panggagahasa ang lalaking **gumahasa** sa kanya.","translation":"The man who **raped** her was charged with rape."}]

meaning_filipino: Magsalita sa napakahinang tinig, karaniwang malapit sa tainga ng kausap, upang hindi marinig ng iba.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'bulong' at gitlaping '-um-'.
original_explanation: Eto ‘yung ginagawa niyo ng bestie mo ‘pag may chismis kayong on-the-spot. ‘Yung tipong kailangan idaan sa hangin para ‘di mahuli ni Marites na nasa kabilang table. That subtle, low-volume info drop.
usage_notes: Ang kilos ng pagsasalita nang napakahina.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **bumulong** sa akin ng sikreto habang kami ay nasa pila.","translation":"Someone **whispered** a secret to me while we were in line."},{"sentence":"**Bumulong** ang bata sa kanyang ina na gusto na niyang umuwi.","translation":"The child **whispered** to his mother that he wanted to go home."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malagkit at pinong hibla na nililikha ng gagamba; agiw.
original_explanation: A **sapot** is a spider's condo, a.k.a. a cobweb. It’s that thing you walk into in the morning that makes you do an instant panic-karate-chop dance. Also, metaphorically, it's the 'web of lies' your ex told you.
usage_notes: Synonymous with 'agiw'. 'Sapot' can also be used figuratively for any entangling network or scheme.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **sapot** ang lumang bodega dahil matagal na itong hindi nalilinisan.","translation":"The old warehouse is full of **cobwebs** because it hasn't been cleaned for a long time."},{"sentence":"Inalis ng nanay ang **sapot** sa kisame gamit ang walis.","translation":"Mother removed the **spiderweb** from the ceiling using a broom."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagkakaroon ng kaalaman, kamulatan, o pag-unawa sa isang bagay o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: 'Yung moment na after three cups of coffee, bigla kang nakakamalay sa lahat ng maling desisyon mo sa buhay. It's that "woke" moment, pero hindi 'yung sa social media. Ito 'yung totoong "Oh, shoot!" moment.
usage_notes: Describes the dawning of realization or consciousness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Habang tumatagal, **nakakamalay** siya sa tunay na intensyon ng kaibigan niya.","translation":"As time went on, she **is becoming aware** of her friend's true intentions."},{"sentence":"Ngayon lang ako **nakakamalay** na mali pala ang aking desisyon.","translation":"Only now do I **realize** that my decision was wrong."}]

meaning_filipino: Paggalaw sa iba't ibang direksyon na nagtatagpo o nagsasalubong na parang mga linyang bumubuo ng krus.
etymology: Reduplication of 'kurus' (from Spanish 'cruz') with the 'pa-' prefix indicating manner.
original_explanation: Describes the way jeepneys navigate EDSA during rush hour, or how you walk around the mall when you can't decide which store to enter first. It's organized chaos in motion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pakurus-kurus** ang mga sasakyan sa rotonda kaya dapat mag-ingat sa pagmamaneho.","translation":"The vehicles were **criss-crossing** at the roundabout, so one must drive carefully."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko ang mga langgam na **pakurus-kurus** na naglalakad sa sahig.","translation":"I saw the ants walking in a **criss-cross pattern** on the floor."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng lathalain na naglalaman ng mga balita, impormasyon, at anunsyo, na karaniwang inililimbag araw-araw o lingguhan.
etymology: From `pahayag` (statement) + `-an` (locative/collective suffix). Literally, 'a place/collection of statements'.
original_explanation: Before your Facebook feed and Twitter timeline, there was the *pahayagan*. It's your lolo's morning coffee partner, the thing fish vendors use to wrap *tuyo*, and where you checked movie schedules and job openings. It's the physical, ink-on-your-fingers version of the news.
usage_notes: Synonymous with 'dyaryo' and 'peryodiko'. 'Pahayagan' is the more formal Filipino term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nabasa mo ba ang balita sa **pahayagan** kaninang umaga?","translation":"Did you read the news in the **newspaper** this morning?"},{"sentence":"Naghahanap siya ng trabaho sa classified ads ng **pahayagan**.","translation":"He is looking for a job in the classified ads of the **newspaper**."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi angkop, wasto, o nababagay sa isang partikular na sitwasyon, lugar, o layunin.
original_explanation: 'Yung suot mong beach attire sa isang formal meeting. O 'yung pag-send mo ng meme sa group chat ng pamilya na para lang sa barkada. That's alingaling. It's when something is just... off, misplaced, and totally cringe. Awkward!
usage_notes: This is a very rare word and might not be understood by most contemporary speakers.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinuring na **alingaling** ang kanyang kasuotan para sa okasyon.","translation":"His attire was considered **inappropriate** for the occasion."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang pangkusina na de-kuryente na ginagamit upang paghaluin, durugin, o gawing katas ang mga pagkain tulad ng prutas at gulay.
original_explanation: The kitchen appliance that turns your healthy-living ambitions into reality... for about a week. You buy a blender to make fruit shakes and green smoothies, but it often ends up being used to make mango graham shakes, crush ice for halo-halo, or just gathering dust on the counter. It’s the sound of summer and broken New Year's resolutions.
usage_notes: A direct loanword for the kitchen appliance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gamitin mo ang **blender** para gumawa ng mango shake.","translation":"Use the **blender** to make a mango shake."},{"sentence":"Nasira ang **blender** kaya hindi ako makapag-smoothie.","translation":"The **blender** is broken so I can't make a smoothie."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paggawa ng isang bagay, karaniwang upang makamit ang isang layunin; isang kilos o galaw.
original_explanation: "Action speaks louder than words," 'ika nga. Ito yung 'gawin mo, 'wag mong i-kwento.' Hindi puro plano, hindi puro salita. From 'drawing' to 'done.' Also, a movie genre na paborito ni tatay, kung saan laging may sumasabog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating gumawa ng mabilis na **aksiyon** bago lumala ang sitwasyon.","translation":"We need to take swift **action** before the situation worsens."},{"sentence":"Paborito niyang manood ng mga pelikulang **aksiyon** ni Fernando Poe Jr.","translation":"He loves watching Fernando Poe Jr.'s **action** movies."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong nagsasagawa ng pagsusuri o analisis, lalo na sa isang partikular na larangan tulad ng pananalapi, datos, o negosyo.
original_explanation: The person in your BPO office who lives in Excel sheets and whose favorite phrase is 'Let me pull up the data.' They can turn a mountain of numbers into a one-page report that decides the fate of a project. They're the modern-day mangkukulam, but with pivot tables instead of potions.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa mga propesyonal na setting, lalo na sa BPO, IT, at finance. Ang Tagalog na katumbas ay "analista" o "tagasuri."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bilang isang data **analyst**, trabaho niyang suriin ang mga trend sa merkado.","translation":"As a data **analyst**, it's her job to examine market trends."},{"sentence":"Kinausap ng CEO ang mga financial **analyst** para sa kanilang prediksyon.","translation":"The CEO spoke with the financial **analysts** for their predictions."}]

meaning_filipino: Magbigay ng isang ideya o plano para isaalang-alang ng iba; magpayo o magpanukala.
original_explanation: The polite way of saying "Eto na lang gawin niyo kasi mas maganda idea ko." Often starts with "Suggestion lang ha..." before dropping a truth bomb that changes the whole plan for the barkada outing.
usage_notes: More formal than 'magsabi' or 'mag-suggest'. It implies a well-thought-out proposal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang gustong **magmungkahi** ng lugar para sa ating Christmas party?","translation":"Who wants to **suggest** a place for our Christmas party?"},{"sentence":"Nais kong **magmungkahi** na bigyan natin ng bonus ang mga empleyado.","translation":"I would like to **propose** that we give the employees a bonus."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mapanlinlang na tao na nagpapanggap na doktor o may kaalaman sa panggagamot ngunit walang pormal na pagsasanay o lisensya.
etymology: Literally 'saliva doctor', from 'mediko' (Spanish for doctor) and 'laway' (Tagalog for saliva), implying their 'medicine' is as worthless as spit.
original_explanation: The OG "fake news" of medicine. This is the person who claims they can cure anything with just saliva, herbs, or a magic chant. They're the ones your tita heard about from her kumare who knows someone whose cousin was supposedly cured. Basically, a walking WebMD page with no credentials and lots of confidence. Avoid at all costs.
usage_notes: A highly derogatory and colloquial term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniniwala diyan, baka **medikong-laway** lang 'yan.","translation":"Don't believe that person, they might just be a **quack doctor**."},{"sentence":"Maraming nabiktima ang **medikong-laway** na nangakong kayang magpagaling ng kanser.","translation":"Many fell victim to the **charlatan** who promised to cure cancer."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kumpletong landas o daanan na inuulit-ulit, partikular na para sa kuryente o sa isang karera.
original_explanation: The more "tito" version of 'sirkit'. It's what your dad calls the wiring in the house. It can also be the race track where cars go round and round, much like you scrolling through your feed for hours.
usage_notes: Mas karaniwan sa pangkalahatang pag-uusap kaysa sa 'sirkit', na mas teknikal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng short **sirkito** kaya nag-brownout sa buong bahay.","translation":"There was a short **circuit** which caused a blackout in the whole house."},{"sentence":"Ang mga motorista ay umikot sa **sirkito** nang sampung beses.","translation":"The racers went around the **circuit** ten times."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na pag-ayaw o pagtanggi sa isang tao (lalo na sa isang miyembro ng pamilya) o sa isang paniniwala.
original_explanation: This is the "You are no longer my child!" scene in every Filipino family drama. It's when you're officially removed from the family group chat and the will. It's the act of hitting 'unfriend' and 'block' on a family member, but in real life and with much more drama.
usage_notes: Stronger than a simple disagreement; implies a complete and often permanent severing of ties.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagtatakwil** sa sariling anak ay isang masakit na desisyon para sa isang magulang.","translation":"The **disownment** of one's own child is a painful decision for a parent."},{"sentence":"Ito ay isang **pagtatakwil** sa kanyang mga dating prinsipyo.","translation":"This is a **renunciation** of his former principles."}]

translation: not a secret; open; public knowledge
meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na hindi itinago, lantad, o alam na ng karamihan; hayag at hindi sekreto.
original_explanation: This is the opposite of "TOP SECRET." It's the chismis that everyone in the office already knows, the "surprise" party that the celebrant already found out about, or your friend's new relationship that's already "Facebook official." It's an open secret, the kind of info that's technically out there for everyone to see.
usage_notes: Often used in the phrase 'di-lihim sa lahat' (not a secret to anyone).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Di-lihim** sa lahat ang kanilang pag-iibigan.","translation":"Their romance is **not a secret** to anyone."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga plano ay **di-lihim** sa kanyang mga katrabaho.","translation":"His plans are **open knowledge** to his coworkers."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagkakalas o pagkatanggal ng tahi sa damit o anumang bagay na pinagdugtong sa pamamagitan ng sinulid.
original_explanation: That moment of horror when you bend over and hear a faint *rrrrip* sound. That's `bigtas`. It's when the seam of your pants gives up on life, usually at the most inconvenient time, like during a presentation or while squeezing into a crowded MRT. It's a wardrobe malfunction waiting to happen.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang mga tahi sa damit, bag, o upholstery na kumalas. Maaaring gamitin bilang pangngalan (ang bigtas) o pang-uri (bigtas ang laylayan).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naku, **bigtas** ang tahi ng palda ko!","translation":"Oh no, the seam of my skirt is **unstitched**!"},{"sentence":"Ipapaayos ko ang pantalon ko dahil **bigtas** na ang bulsa.","translation":"I will have my pants repaired because the pocket is already **ripped**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gusali kung saan isinasagawa ang mga paglilitis at iba pang opisyal na gawain ng korte o sistema ng hustisya.
etymology: From "bahay" (house) + "hukuman" (court of law), from the root "hukom" (judge).
original_explanation: The ultimate 'resbak' arena. It's where disputes go from heated Facebook comments to formal legal proceedings. The place is full of people in barongs, serious faces, and stacks of paper that could kill a forest. Basically, the final level of 'Sumbong kita sa tatay ko!'
usage_notes: Synonymous with "bahay-husgado" and "korte".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Idinaos ang pagdinig sa kaso sa **bahay-hukuman** ng lungsod.","translation":"The case hearing was held at the city's **courthouse**."}]

translation: to praise; to glorify; to celebrate
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng papuri, parangal, o pagdakila sa isang tao, bagay, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: It's the verb form of giving a major shoutout. Think of it as hyping up a national hero, your favorite OPM band, or that one friend who finally passed the board exams. It's about celebrating someone or something and making their greatness known.
usage_notes: Often used in formal or literary contexts, such as in songs, poems, or speeches.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat nating **bunyiin** ang mga bayaning nag-alay ng buhay para sa kalayaan.","translation":"We must **praise** the heroes who offered their lives for freedom."},{"sentence":"Sa awit na ito, nais nilang **bunyiin** ang kagandahan ng kanilang bayan.","translation":"In this song, they want to **celebrate** the beauty of their town."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagpapahid ng barnis (varnish) sa isang bagay, karaniwan sa kahoy, upang ito ay maging makintab at maprotektahan.
original_explanation: That thing your dad does to the old wooden chair to make it look brand new and shiny again. It's the final step in any DIY woodworking project that you see on YouTube. Barnisan mo para 'di magasgasan agad at para 'di pasukan ng anay. It's basically giving wood a top coat.
usage_notes: The root word 'barnis' (varnish) is a noun. 'Barnisan' is the verb form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **barnisan** ang mesa para kumintab.","translation":"You need **to varnish** the table to make it shiny."},{"sentence":"**Barnisan** mo na ang sahig na kahoy pagkatapos mong lihain.","translation":"**Varnish** the wooden floor after you sand it."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o pagpapagawa ng kopya ng isang teksto, imahe, o dokumento sa pamamagitan ng imprenta o printer.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you need 50 copies of your resume because you're about to "explore other opportunities" after a stressful client call. It's also for wedding invitations, tarps for your tito's political campaign, or that thesis you finished at 4 AM. You go to a print shop and tell them, "Paki-print po," which is the same as wanting to 'magpalimbag'.
usage_notes: A causative verb. The subject of the verb is the one causing the printing to happen, not the one doing the actual printing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **magpalimbag** ng isang daang kopya ng kanyang unang nobela.","translation":"She decided **to have** one hundred copies of her first novel **printed**."},{"sentence":"Saan ba maganda at murang **magpalimbag** ng mga T-shirt?","translation":"Where is a good and cheap place **to have** T-shirts **printed**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkaubos na wala ni katiting na natira; pag-ubos sa lahat hanggang sa kahuli-hulihang piraso o patak.
original_explanation: What happens to your sahod two days after payday. It's the state of the ulam after your kuya gets to it first. 'Wala nang natira.' It's that clean plate your mom is proud of, or the empty bank account that makes you cry. Total annihilation of resources.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun (e.g., 'ang pagkasimot') or an adjective ('simot na'). The verb form is 'simutin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Simot** na ang kanin sa kaldero pagkagaling niya sa kusina.","translation":"The rice in the pot was **wiped out** after he came from the kitchen."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa bagyo, **simot** ang lahat ng paninda sa palengke.","translation":"Because of the typhoon, all the goods in the market were **used up**."}]

meaning_filipino: Inasnang karne mula sa likod o tagiliran ng baboy, na karaniwang hinihiwa nang manipis at ipiniprito.
original_explanation: The ultimate breakfast upgrade. That crispy, salty strip of happiness that makes any 'silog' meal a hundred times better ('bacsilog'!). It's the reason why some people say 'I could never be a vegetarian.' It's a luxury breakfast item, the kind you order when you get your sahod.
usage_notes: A universally understood food item. Often associated with American-style breakfast.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko ng kanin, itlog, at malutong na **bacon** sa umaga.","translation":"I want rice, egg, and crispy **bacon** in the morning."},{"sentence":"Ang mahal na ng **bacon** sa grocery ngayon.","translation":"The price of **bacon** at the grocery is so expensive now."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tawag sa lupang sakahan na nakatakdang araruhin, o ang panahon ng pag-aararo.
etymology: From 'araro' (plow) + '-an' suffix, denoting place or time.
original_explanation: It's the 'plowing grounds' or the 'plowing season.' When a farmer looks at a field and says, 'Ayan na, araruhan na,' it's like a developer looking at an empty lot and seeing a future condo. It's the time and place where the hard work of plowing begins.
usage_notes: Can refer to either the place for plowing or the time/season for plowing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malawak ang **araruhan** ngayong taon.","translation":"The **plowing field** is wide this year."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula na ang **araruhan** bilang paghahanda sa tag-ulan.","translation":"The **plowing season** has begun in preparation for the rainy season."}]

translation: to make someone sing; to have someone sing
meaning_filipino: Utos o pakiusap na kumanta ang isang tao o grupo.
original_explanation: The go-to command during birthday parties when you want to force your shy tita to use the Magic Sing. 'Pakanta ka naman!' is the official anthem of family gatherings. In a darker context, like in crime movies, it means to make a witness 'sing' or confess.
usage_notes: The `pa-` prefix here indicates a request or command for someone else to perform the action of the root word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pakantahin** mo nga si Ana ng 'Bakit Ngayon Ka Lang?'","translation":"Please **have Ana sing** 'Bakit Ngayon Ka Lang?'"},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **pakantahin**, baka umulan.","translation":"Don't **make me sing**, it might rain."}]

translation: to end; to put a stop to
meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng tuldok bilang tanda ng pagtatapos ng isang pangungusap. Sa metaporikal na kahulugan, ito ay ang pagbibigay-wakas sa isang usapin, relasyon, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: Ito yung action na ginagawa mo kapag pagod ka na. 'Let's put a period on this.' Pag-ayaw mo nang i-seen zone, i-ghost, o paasahin, kailangan mo nang tuldukan. Tapusin na ang kwento, isara na ang libro. Move on na, bes!
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa matalinhagang paraan upang tukuyin ang pagbibigay ng tiyak na katapusan sa isang bagay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Panahon na para **tuldukan** ang walang katapusang pag-aaway nila.","translation":"It's time **to end** their endless fighting."},{"sentence":"Matapos ang mahabang pag-uusap, napagdesisyunan nilang **tuldukan** na ang kanilang relasyon.","translation":"After a long conversation, they decided **to put a stop to** their relationship."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang unti-unting pagkawala ng liwanag at pagiging madilim ng isang lugar o kapaligiran.
original_explanation: When the lights go out, literally or figuratively. Ito 'yung nangyayari 'pag papalubog na ang araw, o kapag biglang nag-brownout. Pwede ring 'nagdilim ang paningin,' which means you suddenly got extremely angry. 'Nang makita niya ang resibo ng credit card, biglang **nagdilim** ang kanyang paningin.'
usage_notes: Can be used literally for the absence of light or figuratively for a sudden burst of anger ('magdilim ang paningin').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magsiuwi na tayo bago **magdilim**.","translation":"Let's all go home before it **gets dark**."},{"sentence":"Biglang **nagdilim** ang kalangitan at bumuhos ang malakas na ulan.","translation":"The sky suddenly **darkened** and a heavy rain poured."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking uri ng palaka o karag na may magaspang na balat at malakas na boses, karaniwang tumutukoy sa bullfrog.
original_explanation: This is the 'final boss' version of the regular palaka. It’s the big, bumpy, and sometimes scary-looking toad that you find near ponds. Its voice isn't just 'kokak,' it's bass-boosted. It's the type that when it jumps, the ground seems to shake.
usage_notes: 'Kabkab' can mean 'to palpitate' or 'throb', possibly referring to its loud, throbbing croak. It is often used to refer to a bullfrog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahuli nila ang isang dambuhalang **palakang-kabkab** sa may sapa.","translation":"They caught a giant **bullfrog** near the creek."},{"sentence":"Nakakagulat ang malakas na ungal ng **palakang-kabkab** sa gabi.","translation":"The loud croak of the **bullfrog** at night is startling."}]

translation: the state or manner of being choked/strangled
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o paraan ng pagiging sinakal o nahihirapang huminga dahil sa paghigpit sa leeg.
original_explanation: This can be literal, like in an action movie scene. But more often, it’s a metaphor for how you feel when the deadlines are piling up, your boss is watching your every move, and you have bills to pay. That "hindi makahinga" feeling. "Parang sinasakal ako sa trabaho" is a common BPO/corporate hugot.
usage_notes: Can be literal (physical strangulation) or figurative (feeling suffocated by pressure).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang biktima ay namatay dahil sa **pagkakasakal**.","translation":"The victim died due to **being strangled**."},{"sentence":"Ramdam ko ang **pagkakasakal** sa dami ng utang na kailangang bayaran.","translation":"I feel the **suffocation** from the amount of debt that needs to be paid."}]

translation: to be hit by an explosion
meaning_filipino: Tamaan o maapektuhan ng isang pagsabog.
etymology: From `ma-` (involuntary action) + `sabog` (explode) + `-an` (locative suffix, indicating the place/person affected).
original_explanation: Literally, to be caught in an explosion. Figuratively, it's what happens to your DMs when you post a viral selfie, or your brain after a 12-hour shift and your boss asks for 'one more thing.' You get `masabugan` with notifications or information overload.
usage_notes: Refers to being the target or location of an explosion. The figurative sense of being overwhelmed is very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawasak ang mga bintana nang **masabugan** ng bomba ang kalapit na gusali.","translation":"The windows shattered when the nearby building was **hit by a bomb explosion**."},{"sentence":"Para akong **masasabugan** ng ulo sa dami ng trabaho.","translation":"I feel like my head is **going to explode** from so much work."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang masigla at ritmikong paggalaw ng katawan, lalo na ang balakang at paa, kasabay ng tugtog o musika.
original_explanation: That feeling when a good beat drops at the fiesta or on TikTok. You can't help it, your body just moves. It's more than just dancing; it's feeling the rhythm in your soul. From the 'budots' dance to the latest K-Pop craze, it all starts with 'pag-indak'.
usage_notes: Implies a more energetic and rhythmic movement than 'pag-imbay'. It's strongly associated with music and beat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi mapigilan ang **pag-indak** ng mga tao nang tumugtog ang paborito nilang banda.","translation":"The people couldn't stop their **rhythmic dancing** when their favorite band played."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hula, haka-haka, o palagay na batay sa limitadong ebidensya o kutob; isang teorya na hindi pa napapatunayan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "sapantaha" na maaaring nagmula sa Sanskrit na "saṃtarka" (pagsasaalang-alang, pag-iisip).
original_explanation: This is your 'feeling ko...' or 'I have a hunch...' elevated to a more formal, almost scientific level. It's the official term for a well-thought-out guess. When you suspect your officemate is the one stealing your pens, that's your `sapantaha`. It's not yet proven, but the evidence (your missing G-Techs) points to it.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa akademikong pagsulat, pormal na diskusyon, o sa mga legal na konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayon sa **sapantahaan** ng mga pulis, may kasabwat ang suspek.","translation":"According to the **hunch** of the police, the suspect had an accomplice."}]

translation: to spy on, to observe secretly, to surveil
meaning_filipino: Lihim na obserbahan o bantayan ang kilos ng isang tao o isang lugar.
etymology: Mula sa `manman` (pagmamasid) + hulaping `-an` (na nagsasaad ng kilos sa isang bagay).
original_explanation: This is what your chismosa kapitbahay does from her window. It's also what you do to your crush's social media profile at 2 AM. The act of being a low-key, unofficial CCTV camera.
usage_notes: Nangangahulugan ng isang patago o lihim na pagmamasid.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan ng heneral ang kanyang mga espiya na **manmanan** ang bawat kilos ng kalaban.","translation":"The general ordered his spies to **spy on** the enemy's every move."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **manmanan** ang lugar bago tayo pumasok.","translation":"We need to **observe** the place before we enter."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging naaayon sa batas o legal.
etymology: From Spanish 'legal'. The 'pagka-' prefix here denotes the state or quality of being something.
original_explanation: This is the state of something being legit, not colorum. When your side hustle finally gets its DTI and BIR registration, that's its pagkalegal. It's the opposite of 'under the table' transactions.
usage_notes: Often used in formal contexts related to law, business, and government.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng mga abogado ang **pagkalegal** ng kontrata.","translation":"The lawyers are studying the **legality** of the contract."},{"sentence":"Tiniyak nila ang **pagkalegal** ng kanilang operasyon bago magsimula.","translation":"They ensured the **legality** of their operation before starting."}]

meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang umunawa o maabutan ng isip ang isang konsepto, sitwasyon, o wika.
original_explanation: The goal of every student listening to a difficult lecture, every person in a new relationship, and every Pinoy trying to assemble IKEA furniture without instructions. 'Sana makaintindi na sila' is the silent prayer for clarity in a world of confusion.
usage_notes: The ability to comprehend. Often used in the present tense `nakakaintindi`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong maging matiyaga para **makaintindi** sa aralin.","translation":"You need to be patient to be **able to understand** the lesson."},{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **nakaintindi** rin siya sa sitwasyon ko.","translation":"Finally, he was also **able to understand** my situation."}]

translation: to be interrogated; to be pried into
meaning_filipino: Maging paksa ng masinsinang pagtatanong o pagsisiyasat, kadalasan sa paraang nakakakulit o nakakainis.
etymology: From 'urira' or 'urirat', meaning to pry or investigate closely. 'Maurira' is the passive form, 'to be pried into'. Related to 'usisa'.
original_explanation: What happens when you come home late and your parents are waiting for you in the living room. Or when your Tita asks, "Kailan ka mag-aasawa?" for the fifth time at a family gathering. It's being put on the hot seat, feeling like a suspect in a crime you didn't commit (or maybe you did). It's the receiving end of a 'chismosa's' line of questioning.
usage_notes: This word is less common than 'mausisa' (to be curious) or 'usigin' (to be prosecuted/questioned). It specifically implies being subjected to annoying or persistent questioning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw kong sumama sa kanila dahil siguradong **maurira** lang ako tungkol sa buhay ko.","translation":"I don't want to go with them because I'm sure I'll just **be interrogated** about my life."},{"sentence":"Nang dumating ang pulis, lahat ng nasa silid ay **naurira**.","translation":"When the police arrived, everyone in the room **was interrogated**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng hindi pagtanggap, hindi pagsang-ayon, o pag-ayaw sa isang bagay, alok, o akusasyon.
original_explanation: This is the 'No!' in noun form. It's what happens when you apply for a visa and get a rejection letter. It's your friend's reaction when you ask to borrow money for the fifth time this month. In hugot terms, it's the painful act of someone saying 'friends lang tayo' when you confess your feelings.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'pagtanggi'. 'Pagkatanggi' can sometimes emphasize the manner or quality of the denial itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mabilis na **pagkatanggi** sa akusasyon ay kahina-hinala.","translation":"His quick **denial** of the accusation was suspicious."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **pagkatanggi** na tumulong, kami na lang ang gumawa.","translation":"Because of his **refusal** to help, we just did it ourselves."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging maganda, kaakit-akit, o kahali-halina sa paningin, pandinig, o isipan. Maaari ring tumukoy sa mismong kagandahan bilang isang pangngalan.
original_explanation: The ultimate compliment. It's what you say when you see your friend's new profile pic, a perfect sunset in La Union, or a beautifully plated adobo. It can be a noun ('Ang **ganda** ng Pilipinas') or an adjective ('**Ganda** mo, teh!'). It's a word powered by pure appreciation and sometimes, a little bit of friendly envy.
usage_notes: One of the most common and versatile words. Can be used as a noun (kagandahan/ganda) or an adjective. Often used in exclamations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **ganda** ng mga tanawin sa Batanes.","translation":"The sceneries in Batanes are **beautiful**."},{"sentence":"**Ganda** ng boses mo, puwede kang sumali sa contest.","translation":"Your voice is **beautiful**, you could join a contest."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na katutubo, likas, o hindi nagmula sa ibang lugar; dalisay o puro.
original_explanation: The OG. The original gangster. The pureblood. When you say someone is a 'taal na Batangueño,' you mean they are Batangueño through and through—from their accent to their love for kapeng barako. It's about being authentic and deeply rooted in a place or culture.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang malalim na koneksyon ng isang tao sa kanyang lugar na pinagmulan (hal., taal na taga-Maynila) o ang kadalisayan ng isang wika (hal., taal na Tagalog).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay isang **taal** na taga-Laguna kaya't alam niya ang lahat ng pasikot-sikot doon.","translation":"She is a **native** of Laguna, which is why she knows all the ins and outs there."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tunog na nalilikha sa pagkatok sa isang bagay na hungkag o walang laman sa loob, tulad ng sa isang tuyong kawayan o hinog na pakwan.
original_explanation: It's that satisfying 'thump-thump' sound when you tap a perfectly ripe pakwan at the palengke. If a politician's promise had a sound, it would be *kalubkob*—hollow on the inside.
usage_notes: Can also be used as an adjective (pang-uri) to mean hollow or concave.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig niya ang **kalubkob** ng kawayan nang hampasin ito ng hangin.","translation":"He heard the **hollow sound** of the bamboo as the wind struck it."},{"sentence":"Sinuri ng magsasaka ang **kalubkob** ng pakwan upang malaman kung ito ay hinog na.","translation":"The farmer checked the **hollow sound** of the watermelon to see if it was ripe."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagganap bilang isang tagasubaybay o tagabantay, karaniwan sa isang pagtitipon o sa pagitan ng dalawang taong may relasyon, upang tiyakin ang wastong pag-uugali.
original_explanation: The act of being the designated 'bantay.' You're the third (or fifth) wheel, not for romance, but for surveillance. This is what your Kuya does when a suitor visits, or what a teacher does at a school dance. Your mission: to make sure nothing *too* exciting happens. You're the human CCTV.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of dating, family gatherings, or school events.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinakiusapan ako ni Tita na **magtsaperon** sa date ng pinsan ko.","translation":"My aunt asked me to **act as a chaperone** on my cousin's date."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **magtsatsaperon** sa mga bata sa field trip?","translation":"Who will **chaperone** the kids on the field trip?"}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang nakasulat, nakalimbag, o elektronikong talaan na naglalaman ng impormasyon, ebidensya, o patunay.
original_explanation: That pile of papers you need for any government transaction (PSA, NBI, SSS). You need a photocopy, a certified true copy, and the original copy, but they will still find something wrong with it. The physical form of adulting's burdens.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakipasa ang lahat ng kinakailangang **dokumento** bago ang deadline.","translation":"Please submit all the required **documents** before the deadline."},{"sentence":"Nawala ko ang mga importanteng **dokumento** para sa aking visa.","translation":"I lost the important **documents** for my visa."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang tigil; patuloy at walang paghupa, lalo na sa isang gawain o pangyayari na matindi o nakapapagod.
original_explanation: This is a more intense 'walang-patlang'. Isipin mo 'yung pag-iyak ng baby sa madaling araw na parang walang katapusan. O 'yung pag-aaral mo for board exams, **walang-puknat**. It has a feeling of relentless effort or an unending, intense event.
usage_notes: Mas makata at matindi kaysa sa 'walang-hinto' o 'tuloy-tuloy'. Madalas itong nagpapahiwatig ng kawalan ng pahinga.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Walang-puknat** ang kanyang pag-iyak buong gabi.","translation":"Her crying was **incessant** all night."},{"sentence":"Nagtrabaho sila nang **walang-puknat** upang matapos ang proyekto.","translation":"They worked **relentlessly** to finish the project."}]

translation: to make charcoal; to sell charcoal
meaning_filipino: Gumawa ng uling mula sa kahoy sa pamamagitan ng proseso ng mabagal na pagsunog; maaari ring mangahulugang magbenta ng uling.
original_explanation: Before gas stoves and induction cookers, this was a legit hustle. It's the OG way to prep for a barbecue party. You're either the one burning wood to create the charcoal (the producer) or the one selling it by the plastic bag in the palengke (the dealer).
usage_notes: The meaning (to make vs. to sell) is usually clear from the context. "Mag-uling ka na para sa ihawan" means "Make charcoal for the grill". "Nag-uuling siya sa probinsya" could mean his livelihood is making/selling charcoal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pamilya nila ay **nag-uuling** para may pambili ng bigas.","translation":"Their family **makes charcoal** to have money to buy rice."},{"sentence":"Sino ang naka-tokang **mag-uling** para sa ating barbecue mamaya?","translation":"Who is assigned **to make the charcoal** for our barbecue later?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong ang trabaho ay basahin ang metro ng gas upang matukoy ang konsumo at singilin ng isang kostumer.
original_explanation: The person who shows up at your gate and you're not sure if they're from Meralco, Manila Water, or selling something. They're the real-life counter-checker for your LPG or piped gas usage. Their visit is a premonition of the bill to come.
usage_notes: A compound word borrowed from English. Less common now with digital meters and online billing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Papasukin mo 'yung **gasmiter** para mabasa na niya 'yung metro.","translation":"Let the **gas meter reader** in so he can read the meter."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan o paraan na ginagamit para sa proteksyon laban sa panganib, pinsala, o sakit.
etymology: From 'sanggalang' (to protect) and the prefix 'pan-' (instrument for).
original_explanation: This is the upgraded version of 'pansangga'. It's not just for blocking one hit, it's for overall protection. Think face masks and face shields during the pandemic. Think of your antivirus software. Think of your ninang who always defends you from your mom's sermon. It's your complete protective gear for life's hazards.
usage_notes: A more formal and comprehensive term than 'pansangga'. 'Pansangga' is for parrying, 'pansanggalang' is for overall protection.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bakuna ay isang mabisang **pansanggalang** laban sa sakit.","translation":"The vaccine is an effective **protection** against disease."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating magsuot ng helmet bilang **pansanggalang** sa ulo.","translation":"We need to wear a helmet as **protection** for the head."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagpigil sa sarili o pagkontrol sa matinding damdamin, pagnanasa, o galit.
original_explanation: That moment when the internet is lagging during your online game, your boss is asking for a revision for the 10th time, or your tita asks why you're still single, and you just take a deep breath instead of screaming. That's you trying to 'magtimpi.'
usage_notes: Used for controlling emotions like anger, desire, or impatience.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pilit siyang nag**timpi** upang hindi masigawan ang kausap.","translation":"He tried hard to **restrain** himself from shouting at the person he was talking to."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magtimpi** sa pagkain ng matatamis kung ikaw ay may diabetes.","translation":"You need to **control yourself** from eating sweets if you have diabetes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinal na kahingian o kondisyon, na ang pagtanggi ay magreresulta sa pagputol ng relasyon o paggamit ng puwersa.
etymology: From Latin 'ultimatum' (the last thing), likely borrowed via Spanish or English.
original_explanation: When your jowa says, 'It's me or your DOTA team.' That's an ultimatum. It's a non-negotiable, take-it-or-leave-it demand. It’s what your mom gives you: 'Mag-aral ka o kukunin ko ang cellphone mo.' There's no 'let's meet halfway' option here.
usage_notes: Used in the same context as its English counterpart, for serious, final demands where consequences are implied.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binigyan ng **ultimatum** ng unyon ang management: itaas ang sahod o magwewelga sila.","translation":"The union gave the management an **ultimatum**: raise their wages or they will go on strike."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang pananahimik ay isang uri ng **ultimatum**.","translation":"His silence was a type of **ultimatum**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang gawain o proseso na isinasagawa sa pamamagitan ng mga kamay o lakas-tao, sa halip na awtomatiko o sa tulong ng makina.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "manual" (ginagawa gamit ang kamay).
original_explanation: This is anything that requires your own pawis and effort. Think 'manual' transmission sa kotse (the reason your left leg is more muscular), 'manual' na paglalaba (before washing machines saved us all), or any 'manual labor' that makes you appreciate air conditioning.
usage_notes: Isang direktang hiram na salita na ginagamit katulad ng sa Ingles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas gusto niya ang kotseng **manwal** ang kambyo.","translation":"He prefers a car with a **manual** transmission."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay na inilalagay o ipinapasok upang mapuno at maging masinsin ang isang sisidlan.
original_explanation: The extra crumpled newspaper you shove into a Balikbayan box to make sure the pasalubong doesn't break. It's the 'palaman' that's not for eating, but for making things sturdy and un-shakeable, like your determination to finish that K-drama series in one weekend.
usage_notes: Can also refer to the act of stuffing itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng lumang diyaryo bilang **siksik** sa mga babasaging plato.","translation":"He used old newspaper as **stuffing** for the fragile plates."},{"sentence":"Kailangan pa ng **siksik** para hindi gumalaw ang mga prutas sa basket.","translation":"More **packing material** is needed so the fruits in the basket won't move."}]

meaning_filipino: Isagawa ang akto ng pag-unawa sa mga nakasulat na simbolo, letra, o salita upang makuha ang kahulugan.
original_explanation: What you're doing right now. Also, what your boss thinks you're doing with that important report, but you're actually just scrolling through memes. The classic line: 'Magbabasa na nga ako ng libro.' (continues to watch TikTok).
usage_notes: This is the verb for 'to read'. The stress is on the last syllable. Distinct from 'magbasa' (to get wet).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **magbasa** ng mga nobela tuwing Sabado.","translation":"She loves to **read** novels every Saturday."}]

translation: to unfold, to unroll, to reveal
meaning_filipino: Buksan o i-unat ang isang bagay na nakatupi o nakalulon; ibunyag o isiwalat ang isang lihim o katotohanan.
original_explanation: Imagine opening an old treasure map or a love letter you've kept for years. That's `maglatlat`. It's also what a chismosa does when they finally spill the tea. "Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi ko ilalatlat ang sikreto mo." (Sure...)
usage_notes: Often used for things that are rolled or folded, like paper, scrolls, or leaves. Can also be used figuratively for revealing secrets.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinimulan niyang **maglatlat** ng lumang mapa na nahanap niya sa baul.","translation":"He started to **unfold** the old map he found in the chest."},{"sentence":"Sa wakas, nagpasya siyang **maglatlat** ng lahat ng katotohanan sa kanyang pamilya.","translation":"Finally, she decided to **reveal** the whole truth to her family."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maingat at malalimang pag-aaral o pagsisiyasat sa isang bagay, konsepto, o sitwasyon upang maunawaan ang mga bahagi at katangian nito.
original_explanation: This is what you do to your crush's social media profile, your monthly budget, or the latest K-drama episode. It's the act of deep-diving, dissecting, and overthinking. In a BPO, it's 'QA'. In school, it's your book report. In a relationship, it's the 'we need to talk' moment.
usage_notes: A very common word in academic, professional, and medical contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng masusing **pagsusuri** ang mga datos bago maglabas ng konklusyon.","translation":"The data needs careful **analysis** before releasing a conclusion."},{"sentence":"Sumailalim siya sa medikal na **pagsusuri**.","translation":"He underwent a medical **examination**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tahakin, lakbayin, o daanan ang isang lugar, landas, o espasyo.
original_explanation: This is the poetic way of saying 'to cross a path'. It's not just walking; it's embarking on a journey, like the hero in an epic. Think of it as the original 'long walk' before it became a meme, where every step is full of meaning. It's Waze, but for your soul's journey.
usage_notes: This usage is less common and more literary compared to 'tawirin' or 'bagtasin'. It carries a more profound or epic connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais ng manlalakbay na **balagtasin** ang buong kapuluan sa loob ng isang taon.","translation":"The traveler wants **to traverse** the entire archipelago within a year."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **balagtasin** ang masukal na gubat nang walang gabay.","translation":"It is difficult **to traverse** the dense forest without a guide."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi totoo, walang batayan sa katotohanan, o kathang-isip lamang.
etymology: Mula sa "walang" (without) at "katotohanan" (truth), na mula sa ugat na "totoo" (true).
original_explanation: Ito 'yung chismis na kumalat tungkol sa'yo na kesyo mayaman ka raw, pero sa totoo lang, petsa de peligro na at instant noodles na naman ang ulam mo. 'Yung mga fake news na sine-share ni Tita sa Facebook? 'Yun, **walang-katotohanan** 'yun. Pure Marites-level fiction.
usage_notes: A strong way to deny an accusation or label information as false.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga paratang laban sa kanya ay napatunayang **walang-katotohanan**.","translation":"The accusations against him were proven to be **untrue**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala sa sabi-sabi, **walang-katotohanan** ang mga iyan.","translation":"Don't believe in hearsay, those are **baseless**."}]

translation: a type of bamboo musical instrument
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng instrumentong pangmusika na yari sa kawayan na pinatutunog sa pamamagitan ng pagpalo; ang tunog na nalilikha nito.
etymology: Malamang na onomatopoeic, na ginagaya ang tunog na nalilikha nito.
original_explanation: Imagine a bamboo xylophone's deep-voiced cousin from the province. It's an indigenous instrument that gives you that authentic, rhythmic *tktktktk-TONG* sound. It's the OG beat machine before Spotify playlists existed.
usage_notes: Nauugnay sa katutubong musika, lalo na mula sa Mindanao (hal., ng mga Sama-Bajau).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Rinig sa buong nayon ang kalansing ng **tagungtong** tuwing may pagdiriwang.","translation":"The sound of the **tagungtong** could be heard throughout the village during celebrations."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng masinsinang panghihikayat, pag-aamo, o pagsusumamo sa isang tao upang pumayag sa isang nais.
original_explanation: This is the art of 'lambing' and 'pambobola' rolled into one. It's how you convince your mom to let you go out, or how you get your friend to treat you to milk tea. It requires skill, charm, and sometimes a bit of drama. The ultimate 'please, please, please' move.
usage_notes: Implies a persistent and often gentle or pleading form of persuasion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa pamamagitan ng matiyagang **paghihimuko**, napapayag din niya ang kanyang ama.","translation":"Through patient **persuading**, she was finally able to get her father's consent."},{"sentence":"Hindi na kailangan ang **paghihimuko** dahil bukal sa loob niya ang pagtulong.","translation":"There is no need for **coaxing** because helping is from his heart."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan o kagamitan na ginagamit sa pagtutupi o paglilipit ng mga bagay tulad ng damit o papel.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `pan-` (nagiging `panl-` dahil sa asimilasyon) + salitang-ugat na `lupi` (tupi o fold).
original_explanation: That plastic thingy you see on shopping channels that helps you fold your t-shirts perfectly every single time? That's a `panlupi`. Or the bone folder crafters use to get that crisp fold on paper. It's any tool that makes your `pagtupi` game level up.
usage_notes: Isang hindi gaanong karaniwang salita, ngunit ang kahulugan nito ay diretsong nagmumula sa salitang-ugat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng **panlupi** para maging pantay-pantay ang tupi ng mga damit.","translation":"She used a **folding tool** to make the folds of the clothes even."},{"sentence":"Ang butong **panlupi** ay mahalaga sa paggawa ng mga kard.","translation":"A bone **folder** is important in card making."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tao o panig na pormal na kinasuhan ng isang krimen o paglabag sa batas sa isang hukuman.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "sakdal" (charge, accuse) na may panlaping "nasa-".
original_explanation: Sa mga palabas sa TV, ito yung taong nakaupo sa tabi ng abogado niya, mukhang kinakabahan, habang sinisigawan ng prosecutor. Siya yung "the defendant" na laging tinatanong ng judge, "Guilty or not guilty?". Basically, a person in deep, legal trouble.
usage_notes: Madalas ginagamit sa konteksto ng batas at korte. Ang paggamit ng pantukoy na "ang" bago ang salita (ang nasasakdal) ay nagiging katumbas ng "the accused".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iniharap sa korte ang **nasasakdal** upang dinggin ang kanyang kaso.","translation":"**The accused** was brought before the court to hear his case."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga malalim na pag-iisip, alalahanin, o realisasyon na karaniwang dumarating sa hatinggabi o madaling araw kung kailan tahimik ang paligid at walang ibang gumagambala.
etymology: Hiram na parirala mula sa Ingles, na sumikat sa kultura ng internet.
original_explanation: 'Yung moment na dapat tulog ka na pero biglang nag-pop up sa isip mo lahat ng what ifs, regrets, at existential questions mo sa buhay. Minsan, kasama pa diyan 'yung mga utang mo at 'yung chat na 'di nireplyan. Your brain suddenly decides it's time for a major life audit.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa social media upang ilarawan ang estado ng pagkabalisa, malalim na pag-iisip, o 'hugot' sa gitna ng gabi.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inaatake na naman ako ng **3am thoughts** ko tungkol sa career path ko.","translation":"My **3am thoughts** about my career path are attacking me again."},{"sentence":"Isinulat ko lahat sa journal ang mga **3am thoughts** ko para gumaan ang pakiramdam ko.","translation":"I wrote all my **3am thoughts** in a journal to feel better."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na unan o sisidlan na ginagamit upang paglagyan o pagbaunan ng mga aspili at karayom.
etymology: A phrase combining 'tusukan' (place to pierce) and 'aspili' (pin).
original_explanation: That little tomato-looking thingy in your lola's sewing kit. It's a dedicated place for stabbing pins so you don't lose them or step on them. The OG stress ball for sewers.
usage_notes: A compound noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawawala ang aking **tusukan ng aspili**, nakita mo ba?","translation":"My **pincushion** is missing, have you seen it?"},{"sentence":"Puno na ng karayom ang **tusukan ng aspili**.","translation":"The **pincushion** is already full of needles."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang halaga ng pera na inilalagay o ipinagkakatiwala sa isang tao, bangko, o institusyon bilang paunang bayad, garantiya, o piyansa.
original_explanation: It's that money you put down to show you're serious. Like the security deposit for your condo, the down payment for that new phone you're getting on installment, or the money you give to get your tito out of jail (piyansa). It’s a promise in the form of cash.
usage_notes: While it can mean bail ('piyansa'), it is more commonly used for commercial or rental deposits.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong maghanda ng pera para sa **lagak** sa uupahang apartment.","translation":"I need to prepare money for the **deposit** on the apartment for rent."},{"sentence":"Magkano ang paunang **lagak** para sa bagong kotse?","translation":"How much is the initial **down payment** for the new car?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng halal na opisyal ng pamahalaan na kasapi ng Senado.
original_explanation: The female counterpart of a 'senador'. She's the Tita of the nation who can either be your fierce defender or the one who gives you a death stare during a hearing. Often seen in stylish Filipiniana during the SONA.
usage_notes: Specifically used for a female senator.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala ang **senadora** sa kanyang pagtatanggol sa karapatan ng mga kababaihan.","translation":"The **senator** (female) is known for her defense of women's rights."}]

translation: A mythical creature with the head and feet of a horse and the body of a human
meaning_filipino: Isang nilalang sa mitolohiyang Pilipino na may katawan ng tao ngunit may ulo at mga paa ng kabayo. Sinasabing naninirahan sa mga puno ng balete at may kakayahang magligaw ng mga manlalakbay.
original_explanation: The original Filipino prankster god. This half-horse, half-human creature from folklore loves to get travelers lost in the woods. If you're walking in circles in a forest, you might be a victim of a **tikbalang**. The pro-tip from lola is to wear your shirt inside out to break the spell. Think of it as the ultimate GPS jammer of Philippine mythology.
usage_notes: Often depicted smoking a large cigar. A 'tabi-tabi po' is often said to avoid offending them when passing through their territory.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayon sa alamat, naglalaro ang mga **tikbalang** sa ilalim ng puno ng balete tuwing kabilugan ng buwan.","translation":"According to legend, **tikbalangs** play under the balete tree during a full moon."},{"sentence":"Naligaw daw sila sa gubat dahil pinaglaruan sila ng **tikbalang**.","translation":"They said they got lost in the forest because a **tikbalang** played tricks on them."}]

translation: to run out of something (for someone)
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan kung saan ang isang tao o lugar ay nawalan ng isang bagay dahil naubos na ito.
original_explanation: The horror! 'Ubusan' is that tragic moment you get to the bakery and they're out of pandesal, or when you're the last one in line for the buffet and all the lechon skin is gone. It's the verb form of 'FOMO' (Fear of Missing Out). The "-an" suffix implies the location or person affected by the 'ubos' (running out).
usage_notes: A locative-focus verb. The action focuses on the person or place that experiences the lack of the item.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **ubusan** ng paborito kong kape.","translation":"Don't leave me with no more of my favorite coffee. (Lit: Don't cause me to **run out of** my favorite coffee)."},{"sentence":"Lagi kaming **inuubusan** ng yelo sa tindahan ni Aling Puring.","translation":"Aling Puring's store always **runs out of** ice on us."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtatakda o paglalagay ng halaga o bayad para sa isang produkto o serbisyo.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'presyo'. This is what sellers in the palengke, Divisoria, or Carousell do. "Magkano po?" is the question, and how they 'magpresyo' is the answer. Sometimes, you feel they 'magpresyo' based on your outfit. "Mukha kang mayaman, plus 20% 'yan."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **magpresyo** ng mga produktong gawang-kamay.","translation":"It's difficult **to price** handmade products."},{"sentence":"**Nagpresyo** siya ng limang daang piso para sa lumang sapatos.","translation":"He **set a price** of five hundred pesos for the old shoes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan o paraan na mainam, mahusay, o wasto; walang kapintasan o pagkukulang.
original_explanation: "Maigi" is "mabuti" with a college degree. It's not just good, it's *thoroughly* good. When your mom tells you to clean your room "nang maigi," she means she better not find a single alikabok. It implies care, attention to detail, and a higher standard. "Okay ka lang?" "Maigi naman." means you're genuinely fine, not just pretending.
usage_notes: Can be used as an adjective (maiging tao - a good person) or an adverb (mag-aral nang maigi - study well). Often interchangeable with 'mabuti' but can imply a greater degree of quality or thoroughness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pag-isipan mong **maigi** ang iyong desisyon.","translation":"Think about your decision **well**."},{"sentence":"**Maigi** ang kanyang kalagayan pagkatapos ng operasyon.","translation":"His condition is **fine** after the operation."},{"sentence":"Linisin mo **nang maigi** ang mga bintana.","translation":"Clean the windows **thoroughly**."}]

translation: to click; to get along well
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng agaran at natural na pagkakasundo o pagkakaintindihan sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang tao.
original_explanation: The magic that happens when you meet a new teammate and you both hate the same things. It's when the conversation flows easier than EDSA traffic on a payday Friday. 'Di niyo kailangan ng icebreaker, kasi nag-click na kayo agad.
usage_notes: Primarily used in informal, conversational Taglish to describe personal chemistry.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa unang pagkikita pa lang, alam kong **mag-click** kami dahil pareho kaming mahilig sa kape.","translation":"From our very first meeting, I knew we would **click** because we both love coffee."},{"sentence":"Sana **mag-click** kami ng bago kong boss.","translation":"I hope I **get along well** with my new boss."}]

meaning_filipino: Medyo malaki o may sapat na kalakihan; hindi gaanong maliit ngunit hindi rin sukdulan ang laki.
etymology: Derived from `malaki` through partial reduplication (`laki` -> `laki-laki`) to indicate a moderate or considerable degree.
original_explanation: It's not *malaki* malaki, just *malaki-laki*. It's 'sizable.' Like the discount you get sa 11.11 sale – it's something, but not enough to zero out your cart. It's the 'pwede na' size of your bonus.
usage_notes: Used to express a size that is significant but not extreme. It sits between 'katamtaman' (medium) and 'malaki' (big).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Malaki-laki** rin ang natipid ko dahil sa promo code.","translation":"I also saved a **sizable** amount because of the promo code."},{"sentence":"May **malaki-laking** problema siyang kinakaharap sa trabaho.","translation":"He is facing a **rather big** problem at work."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagya at mabilis na paggalaw o pagpintig ng isang bahagi ng katawan, lalo na ng kalamnan.
original_explanation: ‘Yung biglang pag-vibrate ng talukap ng mata mo na parang may sariling buhay. Sabi ng matatanda, may darating daw na pera, o baka naman kulang ka lang sa tulog at sobra sa kape. It's your body's low-battery warning.
usage_notes: Often used to describe involuntary muscle spasms, especially in the eyelids.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kanina pa may **kibot** sa kaliwang mata ko.","translation":"There's been a **twitch** in my left eye for a while now."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang **kibot** sa kanyang puso nang makita niya ito.","translation":"She felt a **throb** in her heart when she saw him."}]

meaning_filipino: Laganap, pangkaraniwan, o kalat sa isang lugar o pangkat ng mga tao; hindi pambihira.
original_explanation: When something is so common it's almost basic. Like milk tea shops in Manila, hugot lines on Facebook, or people complaining about traffic. It's the opposite of 'unique' or 'limited edition.'
usage_notes: Can be used to describe practices, ideas, or things that are very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Balasak** na ang paggamit ng cellphone sa panahon ngayon.","translation":"The use of cellphones is **widespread** nowadays."},{"sentence":"Isang **balasak** na paniniwala na mas masarap ang luto ng nanay.","translation":"It's a **common** belief that a mother's cooking is more delicious."}]

translation: yoyo competition; a place for playing yoyo
meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o isang kaganapan kung saan naglalaro o nagpapaligsahan sa paggamit ng yoyo.
etymology: Mula sa salitang 'yoyo' (na sinasabing may pinagmulang Filipino) at ang hulaping '-an' na tumutukoy sa lugar o gawain.
original_explanation: Sounds like a place where all the cool 90s kids would hang out. It's either a competition ("May yoyoan sa plaza!") or the actual toy itself, but a more formal, old-school version. Not to be confused with "yoyo" which can also be slang for a watch.
usage_notes: Medyo hindi na karaniwan ang paggamit ngayon, ngunit nauunawaan pa rin sa konteksto ng laro.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumali siya sa **yoyoan** na ginanap sa kapistahan ng bayan.","translation":"He joined the **yoyo competition** held during the town fiesta."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang bagay, lugar, o konsepto na may pambihirang taas o antas.
original_explanation: That new condo in BGC? Matayog. Your life goals? Sana matayog. Your standards for your next jowa after the last one was a walking red flag? Dapat matayog. It's not just physically high, it's also about having high ideals or aspirations.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for physical height (e.g., buildings, mountains) and figuratively for abstract concepts (e.g., dreams, ideals).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **matayog** na pangarap niya ay maging isang astronaut.","translation":"Her **lofty** dream is to be an astronaut."},{"sentence":"Mula sa tuktok, kitang-kita ang mga **matayog** na gusali sa siyudad.","translation":"From the summit, the **towering** buildings in the city are clearly visible."}]

translation: like that, in that manner, so
meaning_filipino: Sa paraan o itsurang iyon; katulad ng ipinahiwatig o sinabi na.
original_explanation: It's the formal way of saying 'ganun' or 'ganyan'. Think of it as the 'thus' or 'in such a way' you use when you're trying to sound smart in an essay. 'Bakit ka malungkot?' 'Sapagkat gayon ang takbo ng buhay.' Boom, instant philosopher.
usage_notes: Often used in formal writing, speeches, and literature. The more common spoken forms are 'ganoon' and 'ganyan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Gayon** ang nais niyang iparating sa kanyang liham.","translation":"**Like that** is what he wanted to convey in his letter."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko inasahan na magiging **gayon** kadali ang pagsusulit.","translation":"I did not expect the exam to be **so** easy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maranasang pagkahilo o pag-ikot ng paningin, na maaaring sanhi ng paggalaw, sakit, o pagkapagod.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you ride the Vikings at Star City ten times in a row. Or when you try to read your crush's mixed signals. "Teh, 'di ko na alam, nakaka-liyo siya kausap!" It's that feeling when the world starts spinning, literally or figuratively.
usage_notes: The verb form of 'liyo' (dizziness). A close synonym is 'mahilo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang umikot nang mabilis, baka ka **maliyo**.","translation":"Don't spin so fast, you might **get dizzy**."},{"sentence":"Madalas akong **maliyo** kapag nakatingin sa baba mula sa matataas na lugar.","translation":"I often **get dizzy** when looking down from high places."}]

meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng kasiyahan, kaluguran, o katuparan sa isang pangangailangan o kagustuhan ang isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: This is the action you take to make someone happy or meet their standards, like when you're trying to please your future mother-in-law by washing the dishes without being told. It's the verb form of hitting someone's satisfaction quota. 'Paano ko ba siya masisiyahan?' is the ultimate 'sana all' question.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of pleasing someone or meeting their requirements. Distinct from 'pasayahin' (to make happy), as 'siyahan' implies meeting a specific need or standard.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **siyahan** ang isang taong hindi alam ang gusto.","translation":"It's hard to **please** a person who doesn't know what they want."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **siyahan** ang lahat ng kahilingan ng kanyang nobya.","translation":"He tried to **satisfy** all the requests of his girlfriend."}]

meaning_filipino: Magdulot ng pagkasira, pagkawala ng integridad, o pagkasira ng anyo ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: The action you want to do to your laptop when it freezes during a crucial presentation. It can be physical destruction or, more commonly, ruining someone's reputation. "Huwag kang manira ng gamit na hindi sa'yo."
usage_notes: A broad term. Can mean to physically break something, or to ruin a plan, a day, or a reputation (though 'manirang-puri' is more specific for the last one).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bakit ka ba mahilig **manira** ng gamit?","translation":"Why are you fond of **destroying** things?"},{"sentence":"Huwag mong sirain ang araw ko.","translation":"Don't ruin my day."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng ilong upang matukoy o malanghap ang isang halimuyak o alingasaw.
original_explanation: The verb for when your inner 'Marites' kicks in via your nose. You walk past a bakery and you 'umamoy' fresh pandesal. Your dog 'umaamoy' your grocery bags for treats. It's the action of smelling, whether it's the neighbor's adobo or the suspicious smell from the back of the fridge.
usage_notes: 'Umamoy' is the actor-focus verb (the one doing the smelling). 'Naamoy' is the object-focus verb (something was smelled).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umamoy** ako ng bulaklak para malaman kung mabango ito.","translation":"I **smelled** the flower to know if it was fragrant."},{"sentence":"Biglang **umamoy** ng sunog na sinaing ang kusinera.","translation":"The cook suddenly **smelled** burnt rice."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pakiramdam o kutob na may hindi magandang mangyayari.
original_explanation: This is your internal 'Marites' alarm going off. It’s that gut feeling you get before you check your partner's phone, or when your boss says 'Can we talk?'. It’s the universe giving you a heads-up that drama is about to unfold.
usage_notes: Often synonymous with 'kutob.' It's an intuition or a gut feeling about something negative.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroon akong **masamang palagay** tungkol sa alok niyang negosyo.","translation":"I have a **bad feeling** about his business offer."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula ang kanyang **masamang palagay** nang hindi umuwi ang anak sa takdang oras.","translation":"Her **bad feeling** started when her child did not come home at the expected time."}]

translation: to say goodbye; to bid farewell
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng paalam o pagpapaalam bago umalis o maghiwalay.
etymology: From `ma-` + `paalam`. `Paalam` itself is from `pala` + `alam`, conveying the idea of 'making known' one's departure.
original_explanation: This is the official "I'm out" move. It's what you do before you ghost a party, or when you finally decide to resign from your toxic job. It's the polite, slightly more dramatic version of "Bye, Felicia!"
usage_notes: Often used in formal or dramatic contexts. The more common, casual term is 'magpaalam'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bago siya umalis papuntang ibang bansa, **mamaalam** muna siya sa kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"Before he left for another country, he first had to **say goodbye** to his parents."},{"sentence":"\"**Mamaalam** na ako sa buhay binata,\" sabi ng ikakasal.","translation":"\"I am **bidding farewell** to my bachelor life,\" said the groom-to-be."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang halaga ng pera na ginugol o kinakailangang gugulin para sa isang bagay; ang mga gastusin.
original_explanation: This is the collective noun for all your Shopee checkouts, GrabFood orders, and milk tea cravings. It's what your parents ask about when they see you have a new gadget. 'Magkano pagastos mo diyan?' The reason why 'sahod' feels more like a suggestion than a reality.
usage_notes: Often used to refer to the cost or funds allocated for a specific project or purpose. Can be synonymous with 'gastos' or 'gastusin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang naging **pagastos** para sa pagpapatayo ng bagong tulay.","translation":"The **expenditure** for building the new bridge was large."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating magbawas ng **pagastos** upang makatipid.","translation":"We need to reduce **expenses** in order to save."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na ginagamit bilang pamalit sa anumang salita na hindi masabi o maalala, o bilang isang ekspresyon na nangangahulugang "biro lang" o "anuman."
etymology: Believed to have originated from gay lingo, possibly as a playful alteration of "ano" or other words. Its exact origin is debated but its function as a placeholder is key.
original_explanation: The ultimate filler word. When your brain buffers, just say "eme". It can mean anything and everything. "Kunin mo yung eme sa lamesa." (Get the thingamajig on the table). It's also the "just kidding" escape hatch after saying something too real. "Mahal kita... eme!" (I love you... just kidding!). The Swiss Army knife of Pinoy slang.
usage_notes: Highly versatile. Can be a noun, verb, or just a random utterance. Its meaning is heavily dependent on context and tone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano na naman yang **eme** mo sa buhay?","translation":"What's your latest **shenanigan** in life?"},{"sentence":"Gusto ko lang mag-**eme** buong araw.","translation":"I just want to do **whatever** all day."}]

translation: is being bribed, can be bribed
meaning_filipino: Tumatanggap o maaaring tumanggap ng suhol o lagay kapalit ng isang pabor.
original_explanation: This is the 'under the table' transaction in verb form. It's when someone's principles are as flexible as a contortionist because of 'padulas' (grease money). You know someone **nasusuhulan** when they suddenly approve your request after you give them a 'token of appreciation'. The official verb of 'fixing' things, Philippine-style.
usage_notes: Can be used in the progressive aspect ('is being bribed') or to describe a characteristic ('is bribable').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap magtiwala sa isang opisyal na kilalang **nasusuhulan**.","translation":"It's hard to trust an official who is known to **be bribable**."},{"sentence":"Ayon sa balita, **nasusuhulan** daw ang ilang empleyado sa ahensyang iyon.","translation":"According to the news, some employees in that agency **are reportedly being bribed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng sira o puwang sa gilid ng isang bagay, tulad ng baso, plato, o talim, na sanhi ng pagkatama o pagkabagsak.
original_explanation: You know that favorite mug you have? The one you accidentally hit against the faucet while washing it, and now it has a tiny piece missing from the rim? That mug is now `bingal`. It's still usable, but it's imperfect. It's the physical representation of "medyo damaged but still fighting."
usage_notes: Describes a chip or notch on the edge of a hard object, especially ceramics or blades. Not to be confused with 'bingaw' which is for teeth.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong gamitin ang basong **bingal** at baka masugatan ka.","translation":"Don't use the **chipped** glass, you might get cut."},{"sentence":"Naging **bingal** ang kutsilyo matapos gamiting pangbukas ng lata.","translation":"The knife became **chipped** after being used to open a can."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pag-upo ng inahing manok o ibon sa mga itlog upang mapisa ang mga ito sa pamamagitan ng init ng katawan.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'work from home' for chickens. It's the act of a mother hen sitting patiently on her eggs, keeping them warm until they hatch. Metaphorically, it's like you, brooding over a new project idea or a 'hugot' moment, letting it develop in your mind before it's ready to 'hatch'.
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of poultry and birds. Can be used metaphorically for nurturing an idea.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tamang **paghalimhim** ay mahalaga para mapisa ang lahat ng itlog.","translation":"Proper **incubation** is important for all the eggs to hatch."},{"sentence":"Tila nasa **paghalimhim** siya ng isang bagong plano.","translation":"It seems he is **brooding** over a new plan."}]

translation: to be able to cite as an example
meaning_filipino: Ang magamit o maisama bilang isang halimbawa upang magbigay-linaw, magpatunay, o maglarawan ng isang punto o konsepto.
original_explanation: This is a deep cut. It's the verb form of "example." It means you can use something *as* an example.
