It's what your teacher does when they point to the top-notcher and say, "Tularan ninyo si Maria." Maria is now the `mahalimbawa` for academic excellence. It's a very formal word, you'd probably hear it in a thesis defense, not in the palengke.
usage_notes: Napakapormal at bihirang gamitin sa pang-araw-araw na usapan. Mas karaniwan sa mga akademikong sulatin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang tagumpay ay **mahalimbawa** sa lahat ng nagsisikap.","translation":"His success can **be cited as an example** for everyone who strives."},{"sentence":"Maraming bayani ang **mahalimbawa** pagdating sa pagmamahal sa bayan.","translation":"Many heroes can **be cited as an example** when it comes to love for the country."}]

translation: something used for pulling; lure; attraction
meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan, kagamitan, o paraan na ginagamit upang humila o umakit ng isang bagay o tao.
original_explanation: Can be literal or figurative. Literally, it's the tow truck for your car or the rope you use for tug-of-war. Figuratively, it's your "panghatak" sa customers—your special promo, your good looks, or the free candy at the counter. It's your main draw, your "it" factor.
usage_notes: Ang kahulugan ay nag-iiba mula sa pisikal na kagamitan patungo sa metaporikal na pang-akit depende sa konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit nila ang kalabaw bilang **panghatak** ng araro.","translation":"They used the carabao as a **pulling** force for the plow."},{"sentence":"Ang magandang boses ng mang-aawit ang nagsilbing **panghatak** sa mga manonood.","translation":"The singer's beautiful voice served as the **attraction** for the audience."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagtutol o hindi pagsang-ayon sa isang pahayag, ideya, o kilos ng iba.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na kahit anong sabihin ng ka-meeting mo, kailangan mong i-challenge kasi alam mong mali ang data niya. Ikaw ang resident "devil's advocate" ng team. To "salungatin" is to be the ultimate 'kontrabida' in a debate, but for a good reason... hopefully.
usage_notes: Often used in formal debates, arguments, or when expressing a dissenting opinion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **salungatin** ang utos ng iyong mga magulang.","translation":"Do not **oppose** the orders of your parents."},{"sentence":"Sinadya niyang **salungatin** ang opinyon ng lahat para mag-umpisa ng diskusyon.","translation":"He deliberately **contradicted** everyone's opinion to start a discussion."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis at marahas na paglapit o pag-atake sa isang tao, bagay, o lugar.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "sugod" (pagsugod) at panlaping -um-.
original_explanation: The energy you have when there's a 12.12 sale on Shopee and the item you want is running out of stock. You `sumugod` to the checkout page. Also, what an angry mob does, or what you do when you see the last piece of lechon. It's moving with urgent, aggressive purpose.
usage_notes: Anyong pangnagdaan. Nagpapahiwatig ng bilis at agresyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumugod** ang mga sundalo sa kuta ng kalaban.","translation":"The soldiers **charged** the enemy's fortress."},{"sentence":"Nang buksan ang mall, **sumugod** ang mga tao para sa sale.","translation":"When the mall opened, the people **rushed** in for the sale."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang sanggol na ipinanganak na wala nang buhay.
original_explanation: A deeply serious and sad term. This phrase is used in medical and personal contexts to describe the tragedy of a baby being born without life. It's a direct, literal phrase with no sugarcoating.
usage_notes: This is a formal and somber term used in medical and legal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malungkot na balita na ang sanggol ay **patay nang ipanganak**.","translation":"It was sad news that the baby was **stillborn**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangi-tanging amoy o lasa ng sariwang isda, dugo, o hindi pa gaanong lutong karne.
original_explanation: That smell that hits you when you walk into the wet market. It's the distinct smell of raw fish or seafood that isn't super fresh. To get rid of the *lansa* when cooking, you use calamansi, vinegar, or ginger. In conversation, a story can be *malansa*—meaning it's a bit scandalous or 'fishy.'
usage_notes: The adjective form is 'malansa'. It's a very specific type of unpleasant smell, different from 'baho' (stinky) or 'anghit' (body odor).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang hugasan nang mabuti ang isda para maalis ang **lansa**.","translation":"The fish needs to be washed well to remove the **fishy smell**."},{"sentence":"Ayaw niya sa lasa ng isda dahil sa **lansa** nito.","translation":"He dislikes the taste of fish because of its **rankness**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lakas o kapasidad na gumawa ng trabaho o magdulot ng pagbabago. Ito ay maaaring pisikal, mental, o espirituwal.
original_explanation: Yung kailangan mo para bumangon sa umaga after mong magpuyat kaka-scroll sa TikTok. It's the 'Sana all' feeling you get when you see your friend who just finished a marathon while you're still on your first cup of coffee. Parang battery level mo, 'pag low-batt, kailangan mag-charge (aka matulog o kumain ng sisig).
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa parehong siyentipiko at pang-araw-araw na konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kulang ako sa **enerhiya** ngayon kaya hihiga na lang ako.","translation":"I'm lacking **energy** today so I'll just lie down."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating magtipid ng kuryente para makabawas sa paggamit ng **enerhiya**.","translation":"We need to save electricity to reduce our use of **energy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang idyoma na tumutukoy sa pambihirang liksi at galing sa paggamit ng mga kamay, karaniwan sa mahika o panlilinlang.
original_explanation: The secret behind every magician's trick and every *mandurukot* (pickpocket) in Quiapo. It’s that "now you see it, now you don't" skill. When someone tries to trick you in a shell game, they're using **bilis ng kamay**. It's also what you jokingly accuse your friend of when they somehow win every round of cards.
usage_notes: Used to describe magic tricks, deception, or simply impressive manual dexterity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa **bilis ng kamay** ng salamangkero, nawala ang barya sa kanyang palad.","translation":"Because of the magician's **sleight of hand**, the coin disappeared from his palm."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malalim at di-materyal na pagkakautang dahil sa isang kabutihang-loob na tinanggap mula sa iba, na nangangailangan ng pagtanaw at pagbabayad sa pamamagitan din ng kabutihan.
original_explanation: The social contract that's more binding than any written document in the Philippines. It's that feeling you have when someone helps you get your first job, so now you feel obligated to help their nephew get an internship 10 years later. It's a non-transferable, non-refundable, and sometimes, a lifetime subscription to obligation. It can be beautiful, but it can also be used for emotional blackmail. 'Tandaan mo, may utang-na-loob ka sa akin!'
usage_notes: A core Filipino value. It's a complex concept that governs many social and political relationships. It's not just about saying 'thank you' but about a deep, often lifelong, sense of obligation to reciprocate a significant favor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Habambuhay kong tatanawin bilang **utang-na-loob** ang pagtulong mo sa aking pamilya.","translation":"I will forever see the help you gave my family as a **debt of gratitude**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong gamitin ang **utang-na-loob** para manipulahin ang desisyon niya.","translation":"Don't use the **debt of gratitude** to manipulate his decision."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagtitipon ng mga tao para sa isang partikular na layunin, tulad ng pagtalakay sa mga isyu o paggawa ng desisyon.
original_explanation: That thing that could have been an email. The reason you're late for lunch, stuck in a cold conference room, pretending to listen while actually planning what to eat for dinner. "May miting kami" is the corporate version of "I can't, I'm busy."
usage_notes: A very common loanword used in both formal (business) and informal (barangay meeting) contexts. Often used interchangeably with "pulong".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang malelate sa **miting** natin mamayang alas-tres.","translation":"Don't be late for our **meeting** later at three o'clock."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagpapahid ng isang bagay sa isang ibabaw gamit ang isang roler o panggulong.
original_explanation: This is a bit different. It's about applying something *with* a roller. Think painting a wall: 'Rolyuhan mo ng pintura ang pader' (Roll paint onto the wall). Or applying deodorant: 'Rolyuhan mo 'yang kili-kili mo' (Roll it on your armpit). It's the action of using a roller-type object.
usage_notes: Madalas ginagamit sa konteksto ng pagpipinta o paglalagay ng mga produktong nasa roll-on na lalagyan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **rolyuhan** ng puting pintura ang buong dingding.","translation":"We need to **roll** white paint **onto** the entire wall."},{"sentence":"Mas mabilis **rolyuhan** ang malaking pader kaysa gumamit ng brush.","translation":"It's faster to **roll** the large wall than to use a brush."}]

translation: a flock, a herd, a swarm
meaning_filipino: Isang malaking grupo ng mga hayop, lalo na ng mga ibon, isda, o insekto, na magkakasamang kumikilos.
original_explanation: The animal kingdom's version of a barkada. It's a `sangkawan` of birds flying south, a `sangkawan` of fish you see while snorkeling, or a `sangkawan` of mosquitos plotting to ruin your evening al fresco. Basically, any group of animals moving with a single purpose.
usage_notes: Used specifically for groups of animals. Can be used metaphorically for a large group of people, but it's less common and might carry a slightly negative or dehumanizing connotation depending on context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **sangkawan** ng mga ibon ang lumilipad sa himpapawid.","translation":"A **flock** of birds is flying in the sky."},{"sentence":"Nabulabog ang **sangkawan** ng mga isda nang may lumapit na maninisid.","translation":"The **school** of fish was disturbed when a diver approached."}]

translation: likewise, also, in the same way
meaning_filipino: Sa kaparehong paraan; bilang karagdagan o katulad ng naunang nabanggit.
original_explanation: This is the formal 'same here' or 'also'. It's what you say when you want to agree with someone but make it sound like you're signing a treaty. 'Mahal ko ang Pilipinas.' 'Ako **gayon din**.' Very presidential.
usage_notes: Used to express agreement or similarity in a formal context. The common spoken equivalent is 'ganun din' or 'ako rin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magaling siyang mananayaw, at **gayon din** ang kanyang kapatid.","translation":"She is a good dancer, and **likewise** is her sibling."},{"sentence":"Pinuri ng guro ang kanyang proyekto, at **gayon din** ang ginawa ng mga hurado.","translation":"The teacher praised his project, and the judges did **the same**."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi maaaring bawiin, kanselahin, o alisin ang pagiging epektibo o legalidad; permanente at pinal.
original_explanation: Like a marriage contract after the first year (kidding!), or more seriously, a legally binding document you signed without reading the fine print. It's the 'no take-backsies' of the legal and adulting world. Once it's done, it's DONE.
usage_notes: Primarily used in legal, formal, and official contexts to describe contracts, decisions, or declarations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang desisyon ng korte suprema ay pinal at **di-mapawawalang-bisa**.","translation":"The decision of the supreme court is final and **irrevocable**."},{"sentence":"Pumirma siya sa isang kasunduang **di-mapawawalang-bisa**.","translation":"He signed an agreement that **cannot be nullified**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aani ng mga pananim, lalo na ng palay, gamit ang isang karit o lilik.
original_explanation: This is the OG way of harvesting before tractors and fancy machines. Think grim reaper, but for rice. It's hard work, parang pag-move on sa ex mong ayaw paawat.
usage_notes: Often associated with rice harvesting using a scythe.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Panahon na ng **gapas** kaya abala ang mga magsasaka sa bukid.","translation":"It's time for the **harvest**, so the farmers are busy in the field."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang siyentista na nag-aaral ng mga buhay na organismo at ang kanilang ugnayan sa kapaligiran.
original_explanation: The person who actually knows why your plant is dying. They study everything from the germs on your phone to the whales in the ocean. They're the experts on life itself. Basically, a scientist for living things.
usage_notes: A formal term for a scientist specializing in biology. The feminine form is 'biologa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang sikat na **biologo** ang magbibigay ng panayam tungkol sa marine life.","translation":"A famous **biologist** will give a lecture about marine life."},{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang maging isang **biologo** upang pag-aralan ang mga hayop sa gubat.","translation":"He dreams of becoming a **biologist** to study forest animals."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kulisap na may kakayahang gumawa ng sarili nitong liwanag (bioluminescence), karaniwang nakikita sa gabi.
original_explanation: The original, OG Christmas lights of the province. They're nature's fairies, the little sparks that make a probinsya night magical. It's what you wish your love life was like—sporadically bright and magical, instead of just... dark. Also, a classic song by The Cueshé.
usage_notes: A common and well-known word, especially in literature and songs.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **alitaptap** ang nagliwanag sa madilim na gubat.","translation":"Many **fireflies** lit up the dark forest."},{"sentence":"Ang mga bata ay masayang hinuhuli ang mga **alitaptap**.","translation":"The children were happily catching **fireflies**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sangay o departamento ng isang unibersidad o kolehiyo na nakatuon sa isang partikular na larangan ng pag-aaral. Karaniwang pagbaybay: 'fakultad'.
original_explanation: This is the old-school or conyo way of saying 'college' or 'department' inside a university, from the Spanish 'facultad'. 'Saan ka nag-aaral?' 'Sa pakultad ng Sining at Panitikan.' Sounds more 'alta' than just saying 'sa CAS'.
usage_notes: 'Fakultad' is the more common and academically accepted spelling, borrowed from Spanish. 'Pakultad' is a phonetic, less common variant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang dekano ng **pakultad** ng medisina ang nagbigay ng talumpati.","translation":"The dean of the **faculty** of medicine gave the speech."},{"sentence":"Nais niyang pumasok sa **pakultad** ng inhinyeriya.","translation":"He wants to enter the **faculty** of engineering."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang listahan ng mga bagay na dapat gawin, mga pangyayari, o impormasyon na nakaayos sa isang partikular na pagkakasunod-sunod, tulad ng programa sa isang pagtitipon o listahan ng mga numero ng telepono.
etymology: From *tala-* (list, record) + *tuntunin* (rule, guideline), from the root *tunton* (to trace, follow).
original_explanation: The game plan, the itinerary, the 'what's next' list. For a wedding, it's the sequence of events from the ceremony to the 'kainan na!' For a TV guide, it's the list of shows. Yung **talatuntunan** ng buhay mo, ikaw ang gumagawa... or sometimes, your boss.
usage_notes: A formal term. 'Programa' or 'iskedyul' (schedule) are much more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa **talatuntunan** ang pagkakasunod-sunod ng mga magsasalita sa kumperensya.","translation":"The sequence of speakers for the conference is in the **program**."},{"sentence":"Sinusunod namin ang **talatuntunan** ng aming paglalakbay upang hindi kami maligaw.","translation":"We are following our trip's **schedule** so we don't get lost."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking baka na hindi pa kinakapon, karaniwang mas malaki at mas agresibo kaysa sa karaniwang baka.
original_explanation: The OG 'beast mode' farm animal. In the Philippines, it's less about bullfighting and more about the zodiac sign (Taurus) or a really strong, stubborn dude.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **toro** sa bukid ay mukhang galit.","translation":"The **bull** in the field looks angry."},{"sentence":"Siya ay ipinanganak sa ilalim ng sign na **Toro**.","translation":"He was born under the sign of the **Bull** (Taurus)."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o gawain ng pagpasok ng mga kalakal, produkto, o serbisyo mula sa ibang bansa patungo sa sariling bansa.
original_explanation: This is the reason why your Shopee or Lazada package from China takes weeks to arrive. It's the 'import' button for the whole country. When we buy rice, gadgets, or even K-pop merch from abroad, that's **pag-angkat**. The opposite is pagluwas (export).
usage_notes: A key term in economics and trade discussions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pag-angkat** ng bigas ay isang sensitibong isyu sa agrikultura.","translation":"The **importation** of rice is a sensitive issue in agriculture."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa **pag-angkat**, mas maraming pagpipiliang produkto sa merkado.","translation":"Because of **importation**, there are more product choices in the market."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang anak ng pinsang-buo ng iyong magulang, o ang apo ng kapatid ng iyong lolo o lola. Kayo ay may parehong lolo at lola sa tuhod.
etymology: From "pinsan" (cousin) and "makalawa" (a variant related to "ikalawa" or "twice removed").
original_explanation: This is where the family tree gets complicated. This is the cousin you meet at a massive reunion and you both need a flowchart to figure out how you're related. Your parents are first cousins. You share great-grandparents. Basically, they're 'kamag-anak pa rin' (still a relative).
usage_notes: This term is understood but less commonly used in casual conversation than the more general "pinsan". People might just say "malayong pinsan" (distant cousin).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nalaman ko na lang na **pinsang-makalawa** ko pala ang bago naming kapitbahay.","translation":"I just found out that our new neighbor is actually my **second cousin**."},{"sentence":"Mahirap nang i-trace ang aming ugnayan dahil **pinsang-makalawa** na kami.","translation":"It's hard to trace our connection because we are already **second cousins**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang damdamin ng malaking paggalang, pagtataka, o pagmamahal para sa isang tao o bagay dahil sa mga katangian nito.
original_explanation: That feeling when you see your crush's new profile pic. Or when your officemate presents a killer PowerPoint and you're just like, "Sana all!" It's the silent "wow" or the loud "Idol!" you give someone who's just incredibly amazing.
usage_notes: Often used with the verb 'humanga' (to admire) or the adjective 'kahanga-hanga' (admirable).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko maitago ang aking **hanga** sa kanyang talento.","translation":"I cannot hide my **admiration** for his/her talent."},{"sentence":"Puno ng **hanga** ang kanyang mga mata habang pinapanood ang pagtatanghal.","translation":"His/Her eyes were full of **awe** while watching the performance."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mekanismo sa sasakyan, karaniwang pinapatakbo ng paa, na ginagamit upang paghiwalayin o pagdugtungin ang makina at ang transmisyon para makapagpalit ng kambyo.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung pangatlong pedal sa manual na kotse na dahilan kung bakit namamatayan ka ng makina sa gitna ng EDSA nung nag-aaral ka pa lang mag-drive. 'Yung kailangan mong i-master ang timing para hindi umurong sa paahon. The thing that separates the 'marunong mag-drive' from the 'marunong lang magpaandar ng kotse.'
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa konteksto ng mga sasakyan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahan-dahan mong bitawan ang **klats** habang inaapakan ang silinyador.","translation":"Slowly release the **clutch** while stepping on the accelerator."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng biglaan at hindi makontrol na pag-urong ng dayapram na nagreresulta sa isang tunog na 'hic'.
original_explanation: 'Yung moment na bigla ka na lang nag-"hic!" sa gitna ng Zoom meeting tapos hindi mo mapigilan. Sabi ng matatanda, may nakaalala daw sa'yo. Sabi ng science, uminom ka lang ng tubig pabaliktad. Ang sinukin ay ang patunay na minsan, kahit katawan mo, hindi mo kontrolado.
usage_notes: The verb form is 'sinukin' (to get the hiccups) or 'suminok' (to hiccup). 'Sinisinok' is the progressive form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang tumawa habang kumakain, baka ka **sinukin**.","translation":"Don't laugh while eating, you might **get the hiccups**."},{"sentence":"Kanina pa ako **sinisinok**, may nakaalala siguro sa akin.","translation":"I've **been having hiccups** for a while now, someone must be thinking of me."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagpunta mula sa isang lugar patungo sa iba, lalo na kung ito ay malayo o tumatagal.
original_explanation: The 'sana all' post on your feed. It's more than just a trip; it's a journey. It could be your backpacking trip through Southeast Asia, your daily commute from Cavite to Makati (a different kind of adventure), or your 'journey' of self-discovery after a breakup. It's about the destination and the chismis you gather along the way.
usage_notes: Has a more profound, meaningful connotation than "biyahe" (trip), which is more logistical.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paglalakbay** ay nagpapalawak ng ating pananaw sa mundo.","translation":"**Travel** broadens our perspective of the world."},{"sentence":"Ang buhay ay isang mahabang **paglalakbay**.","translation":"Life is a long **journey**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang halaman na pinagmumulan ng bigas, o ang butil nito bago alisin ang balat.
original_explanation: Ito yung 'before' picture ng kanin. Yung halaman na nakatanim sa bukid. Pag inani, **palay** pa rin. Pag giniling at natanggal ang balat, nagiging bigas. Pag niluto, kanin na. So, **palay** is rice in its most natural, unprocessed state, straight from the farm.
usage_notes: Naiiba sa 'bigas' (husked, uncooked rice) at 'kanin' (cooked rice).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginintuan ang kulay ng mga **palay** na malapit nang anihin.","translation":"The **rice plants** ready for harvest are golden in color."},{"sentence":"Nagbibilad sila ng **palay** sa kalsada pagkatapos ng anihan.","translation":"They are drying **unhusked rice** on the road after the harvest."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging puno o kumpleto. Maaari din itong tumukoy sa isang pangkat ng mga puno o kakahuyan.
original_explanation: This has two common meanings. First is that feeling when you've eaten too much samgyupsal and you're at peak "kapunuan." The second is literally a bunch of trees, like the last remaining green space in the city that's about to become a condo.
usage_notes: The context determines whether it means "fullness" or "grove/forest." "Ang kapunuan ng mangkok" (the fullness of the bowl) vs. "Ang kapunuan sa gubat" (the grove in the forest).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang **kapunuan** ng kaligayahan sa araw ng kaniyang pagtatapos.","translation":"She felt the **fullness** of happiness on her graduation day."},{"sentence":"Isang malawak na **kapunuan** ng mga niyog ang aming nadaanan.","translation":"We passed by a wide **grove** of coconut trees."}]

meaning_filipino: Itinaas o inilipat ang isang bagay mula sa isang mababang lugar patungo sa mas mataas na posisyon gamit ang lakas.
original_explanation: The past tense of 'magbuhat.' This is what you did to your team during a group project, or what you do to the 5-gallon water container because it's your turn. It's the physical act of carrying a burden, whether it's a dumbbell at the gym or the emotional baggage from your ex.
usage_notes: Often used for lifting heavy objects.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumuhat** si Juan ng isang sakong bigas.","translation":"Juan **lifted** a sack of rice."},{"sentence":"Siya ang **bumuhat** sa buong pamilya nang magkasakit ang kanilang ama.","translation":"She **carried** the whole family when their father got sick."}]

translation: to part, to clear a path
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-alis o paghihiwalay ng mga bagay o tao upang makagawa ng daan.
original_explanation: Parang yung eksena sa pelikula na dadaan ang bida, automatic na naghihiwalay ang mga tao sa paligid. 'Excuse me, coming through!' version ng katawan. Or yung ginagawa mo sa sangkaterbang damit sa ukay-ukay para makita mo yung aytem na bet mo.
usage_notes: Often used to describe parting a crowd, curtains, or tall grass.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Humawi** ang mga tao nang dumating ang presidente.","translation":"The people **parted** when the president arrived."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **humawi** sa makakapal na kugon.","translation":"He tried to **clear a path** through the thick cogon grass."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang babaeng mamamayan ng Pransiya (France).
original_explanation: The female counterpart to Pranses. She's the one you imagine walking chicly along the Seine, probably wearing a beret (because stereotypes). In the Philippines, calling someone 'parang Pransesa' is a compliment on their style and elegance.
usage_notes: Tiyak na tumutukoy sa isang babaeng taga-Pransiya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang guro namin sa French class ay isang **Pransesa**.","translation":"Our teacher in French class is a **Frenchwoman**."},{"sentence":"Napagkamalan siyang **Pransesa** dahil sa kanyang pananamit.","translation":"She was mistaken for a **Frenchwoman** because of how she dressed."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang makitid na piraso ng lupa na nagdurugtong sa dalawang mas malaking masa ng lupa at napapaligiran ng tubig sa magkabilang panig.
etymology: Maaaring mula sa "dalay" (dalhin) + "-an" (hulaping panlunan), na tumutukoy sa isang lugar kung saan may dinadala o tinatawid.
original_explanation: Imagine two big islands that want to hold hands but are too shy. The dalahikan is that skinny strip of land connecting them. It's the land bridge in your geography class, the thing that keeps two places from being totally separate. Parang 'bridge' sa dalawang nag-aaway na magkaibigan, pero lupa.
usage_notes: Isang terminong pang-heograpiya. Hindi karaniwang ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na usapan ngunit lumalabas sa mga tekstong pang-akademiko.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Bataan ay isang **dalahikan** na nakausli sa Look ng Maynila.","translation":"Bataan is a **peninsula** that juts out into Manila Bay."},{"sentence":"Naglakad sila sa kahabaan ng **dalahikan** upang makatawid sa kabilang pulo.","translation":"They walked along the **isthmus** to cross to the other island."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbibigay-buhay o pag-abot sa isang pangarap, plano, o pangako; ang pagiging totoo ng isang bagay na inaasahan.
etymology: From "tupad" (to fulfill), which becomes "katuparan" (fulfillment). The "pagsa-" prefix indicates the process of making something happen.
original_explanation: This is the "dream come true" moment. The grand finale. After all the 'pagsasagawa' (execution), this is the result. It's graduating after years of puyat, getting that promotion you worked hard for, or finally launching the business you only doodled in a notebook. It's turning your "sana all" into "sa wakas!".
usage_notes: A very formal and somewhat dramatic word for achieving a goal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagtatayo ng bagong ospital ay ang **pagsasakatuparan** ng matagal nang pangarap ng komunidad.","translation":"The construction of the new hospital is the **fulfillment** of the community's long-held dream."},{"sentence":"Nangangailangan ng pagkakaisa para sa **pagsasakatuparan** ng ating mga layunin bilang isang bansa.","translation":"Unity is needed for the **realization** of our goals as a nation."}]

translation: prone to being wasteful; having spendthrift tendencies
meaning_filipino: Mayroong ugali o tendensiyang maging magastos o maluho.
original_explanation: This is the adjective form for the 'buhalhal' lifestyle. If your mom says you're 'buhalhalin', it means she's noticed your growing collection of online shopping packages and your tendency to treat every day like payday. It's a gentle (or not-so-gentle) warning that you're leaning into your inner 'gastador'.
usage_notes: Describes the characteristic or tendency, whereas "buhalhal" describes the person or the state. It's the "-ish" in "spendthrift-ish".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Medyo **buhalhalin** ang anak niya kaya tinuturuan niya itong mag-ipon.","translation":"Her child is **prone to being wasteful**, so she is teaching him/her to save money."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nasa edad na labintatlo (13) hanggang labinsiyam (19); isang kabataan.
original_explanation: That phase in life when you think you know everything, your parents know nothing, and your biggest problem is your crush not viewing your IG story. A Filipino 'teenager' is often called 'binata' (male) or 'dalaga' (female), and is an expert in TikTok dances, mobile games, and saying 'gets ko na 'yan, Ma' while not getting it at all.
usage_notes: Commonly used loanword. 'Binata' (for males) and 'dalaga' (for females) are the more traditional Tagalog equivalents, but 'teenager' is universally understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap kausapin ang mga **teenager** ngayon dahil may sarili na silang mundo.","translation":"It's hard to talk to **teenagers** nowadays because they have their own world."},{"sentence":"Bilang isang **teenager**, marami siyang pinagdadaanang pagbabago.","translation":"As a **teenager**, she is going through many changes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng nagmula o naninirahan sa lungsod ng Maynila.
etymology: From Spanish 'manileña', the feminine form for a person from Manila.
original_explanation: She's a girl from Manila. Can be a stereotype for someone who's city-smart, maybe a bit conyo, and knows how to navigate the LRT, traffic, and the latest food trends. But really, a Manilenya is any woman who calls the chaotic, beautiful mess of Manila her home.
usage_notes: The masculine form is 'Manilenyo'. 'Taga-Maynila' is a more neutral, genderless alternative.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang tunay na **Manilenya** si Ana, dahil kabisado niya ang lahat ng pasikot-sikot sa Quiapo.","translation":"Ana is a true **Manila girl**, because she knows all the ins and outs of Quiapo."},{"sentence":"Maraming sikat na artista ang ipinanganak bilang **Manilenya**.","translation":"Many famous actresses were born as **women from Manila**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging isang diyos o diyosa; pagka-diyos. Tumutukoy din sa isang banal na nilalang.
original_explanation: This is the highest level of 'awra'. It's that god-like quality. Think of how Pinoys describe their idols: "Ang ganda niya, parang diwata!" That's a taste of **dibinidad**. It's the ultimate glow-up, beyond human, straight to the heavens. It's the quality that makes you say, "Sana all, divine."
usage_notes: A formal and literary term, often used in religious or philosophical discussions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan sa teolohiya ang kalikasan at **dibinidad** ni Kristo.","translation":"Theology studies the nature and **divinity** of Christ."},{"sentence":"Ang mga sinaunang Griyego ay naniniwala sa maraming diyos na may iba't ibang antas ng **dibinidad**.","translation":"The ancient Greeks believed in many gods with varying degrees of **divinity**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang espiritwal na nilalang na pinaniniwalaang itinalaga upang magbantay, gumabay, at magprotekta sa isang partikular na tao, pangkat, o bansa.
original_explanation: Your "anghel na tagatanod" is your spiritual bodyguard, the invisible BFF who keeps you from tripping on flat surfaces or making even worse life decisions. When you narrowly avoid a jeepney, you thank them. When you pass an exam you didn't study for, you suspect they had a divine cheat sheet.
usage_notes: A common religious and cultural concept in the predominantly Catholic Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagi kong nararamdaman na ginagabayan ako ng aking **anghel na tagatanod**.","translation":"I always feel that I am being guided by my **guardian angel**."},{"sentence":"Salamat sa pagligtas mo sa akin, para kang **anghel na tagatanod** ko!","translation":"Thanks for saving me, you're like my **guardian angel**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pahayag na ginawa nang walang patunay o bago pa mapatunayan, karaniwang nagsasaad na may nagawang mali o ilegal ang isang tao.
original_explanation: The official term for 'chismis' when it gets serious and lawyers get involved. It's what you see in news headlines: "Aktor, nahaharap sa mga alegasyon ng..." It's basically saying "someone said you did it," but it hasn't been proven in court yet. The fuel of all Marites-level investigations.
usage_notes: Primarily used in legal, political, and journalistic contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mariing itinanggi ng politiko ang mga **alegasyon** ng korapsyon laban sa kanya.","translation":"The politician strongly denied the **allegations** of corruption against him."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng matibay na ebidensya upang mapatunayan ang isang **alegasyon**.","translation":"Strong evidence is needed to prove an **allegation**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang babaeng nakararanas ng matinding kawalan ng pag-asa o nangangailangan nang lubos.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'desesperada', ang anyong pambabae ng 'desesperado' (desperate).
original_explanation: The 'ate girl' version of being desperate. 'Yung tipong nag-message ka na sa ex mo ng 'I miss you' at 3 AM kasi wala nang iba. Or 'yung handa ka nang gawin lahat para lang sa promo code ng Grab. Classic 'kapit sa patalim' but make it feminine.
usage_notes: Eksklusibong ginagamit para sa babae. Ang katumbas nito para sa lalaki ay 'desesperado'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Desesperada** na si Ana na makahanap ng trabaho kaya tinanggap na niya ang alok kahit mababa ang sahod.","translation":"Ana was so **desperate** to find a job that she accepted the offer even with a low salary."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng tela o plastik na isinusuot sa dibdib, lalo na ng mga sanggol, upang maprotektahan ang damit mula sa pagkain o laway.
original_explanation: The OG baby fashion accessory. It's the shield that protects a baby's cute onesie from a barrage of Cerelac and spit-up. For adults, it's that napkin you tuck into your shirt collar when facing a glorious bowl of ramen or a crab feast.
usage_notes: Not a very common word in daily conversation anymore, as many just say "bib."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Suotan mo ng **babero** ang bata para hindi madumihan ang damit niya.","translation":"Put a **bib** on the child so his clothes don't get dirty."},{"sentence":"Nawawala ang paboritong **babero** ng sanggol.","translation":"The baby's favorite **bib** is missing."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagdulas o pagpapadulas sa isang makinis na ibabaw.
etymology: Likely onomatopoeic or descriptive of the sliding sound/motion.
original_explanation: The feeling of your tsinelas on a newly-mopped SM floor. That's **dausdos**. It's the sound and motion of something sliding smoothly (or dangerously) downwards. It's the 'whee' of going down a slide, or the 'oops' of slipping on a banana peel.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a smooth, downward sliding movement. Can be a noun or the root for a verb (e.g., dumausdos).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **dausdos** ng mga bato mula sa bundok.","translation":"I heard the **sliding** of rocks from the mountain."},{"sentence":"Ang **dausdos** niya sa slide ay napakabilis.","translation":"His **slide** down the slide was very fast."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggalaw ng katawan nang mabilis at hindi makontrol, karaniwang sanhi ng lamig, takot, o matinding emosyon.
etymology: From the prefix 'mang-' and the root 'kinig', meaning 'tremble' or 'shudder'.
original_explanation: That 'woke up like this' moment when 'this' is in a freezer. It's your body's natural reaction to seeing your ex with a new bae, the AC in the BPO office set to 'Antarctica', or a horror movie jump scare. It's the physical manifestation of 'OMG'.
usage_notes: Often used for shivering from cold (ginaw), trembling from fear (takot), shaking from anger (galit), or even trembling with excitement or romantic thrill (kilig).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **manginig** ang kanyang mga tuhod bago ang kanyang job interview.","translation":"His knees started to **tremble** before his job interview."},{"sentence":"**Nanginginig** ako sa lamig dahil sa malakas na ulan.","translation":"I'm **shivering** from the cold because of the heavy rain."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tao o partido na may pananagutang pinansyal o obligasyon na dapat bayaran sa iba.
original_explanation: This is the person who's always "seenzoning" you on payday. They're the one who borrowed money for "pamasahe" and suddenly developed amnesia. In short, the debtor. The opposite of the "nagpapautang" who is now questioning their life choices.
usage_notes: Literal na nangangahulugang "ang taong may pagkakautang".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging nagtatago **ang may-utang** kapag naniningil na ako.","translation":"**The debtor** always hides when I come to collect."},{"sentence":"Bilang **may-utang**, responsibilidad mong magbayad sa takdang oras.","translation":"As **the debtor**, it is your responsibility to pay on time."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang sasakyan na nakahinto at nakalagay sa isang lugar para sa paradahan.
etymology: From Tagalog naka- (stative prefix) + Spanish parada (a stop, halt).
original_explanation: The state of your Grab car that's 2 minutes away... for the last 10 minutes. Or that car blocking your driveway. "Nakahinto at hindi umaalis" — can also apply to your feelings for your crush.
usage_notes: Used to describe the state of a vehicle that is parked. It's the result of the action 'pumarada' (to park).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May kotse na **nakaparada** sa tapat ng gate natin.","translation":"There's a car **parked** in front of our gate."},{"sentence":"Matagal nang **nakaparada** ang jeep na iyan diyan.","translation":"That jeep has been **parked** there for a long time."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng inumin na karaniwang inihahaing malamig upang magbigay-ginhawa, lalo na sa mainit na panahon.
etymology: Isang parirala na binubuo ng "inumin" (drink) at "pampalamig" (chiller/cooler, mula sa ugat na "lamig").
original_explanation: The official savior during Philippine summer. This is your halo-halo, sago't gulaman, ice-cold Coke, or any juice that stops you from melting into a puddle on the sidewalk. It's the reason why 7-Eleven's Slurpee machine is a national treasure.
usage_notes: Karaniwang tumutukoy sa mga hindi nakalalasing na inumin tulad ng juice, iced tea, at soft drinks.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili tayo ng **inuming pampalamig** dahil sobrang init ng panahon.","translation":"Let's buy a **cold beverage** because the weather is so hot."},{"sentence":"Paborito ko ang sago't gulaman bilang **inuming pampalamig**.","translation":"Sago't gulaman is my favorite **refreshment**."}]

translation: Rustling sound; sound of a swift current
meaning_filipino: Ang tunog na nililikha ng mabilis na pagdaloy ng tubig o ng paggalaw ng mga tuyong dahon, damo, o papel.
original_explanation: This is the sound of nature's drama. Pwedeng 'yung mabilis na agos ng tubig sa ilog after a storm, or 'yung tunog ng paglalakad mo sa isang gubat na puno ng tuyong dahon. It's the sound that tells you something is moving—either water or a potential 'aswang' in the bushes.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa tunog ng tubig (tulad ng 'lagasaw') o sa kaluskos ng mga tuyong bagay. Ang 'lagaslas' ang ugat na salita.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakatakot ang **lagaslasan** ng mga dahon sa madilim na eskinita.","translation":"The **rustling** of the leaves in the dark alley is scary."},{"sentence":"Mula sa malayo, dinig na ang **lagaslasan** ng ilog.","translation":"From afar, the **sound of the river's current** could already be heard."}]

translation: person in a picture with another; look-alike
meaning_filipino: Ang isang tao na kasama sa isang litrato; o isang tao na kamukha o kawangis ng iba.
etymology: From 'larawan' (picture, image) with the prefix 'ka-', denoting a companion or a shared quality.
original_explanation: Your photo-buddy! The person you're with in that IG post, the one who completes your groufie. 'Sino 'yang kalarawan mo?' is the classic question from a nosy tita. It can also mean your doppelgänger. 'Uy, may kalarawan ka sa kabilang department!' It's your twin from another mother, captured in a photo or just by someone's observation.
usage_notes: The meaning depends on context. It can mean 'person in the photo with' or 'person who looks like'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kaibigan ko ang aking **kalarawan** sa litratong ito.","translation":"My friend is the one **in the picture with me** in this photo."},{"sentence":"Marami ang nagsasabi na **kalarawan** niya ang isang sikat na artista.","translation":"Many say that she is a **look-alike** of a famous actress."}]

translation: to have someone look for; to point out
meaning_filipino: Ipatukoy o ipahanap sa iba ang isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng paningin.
original_explanation: This is a subtle, low-key power move. Instead of pointing with your finger (which your lola said was rude), you ask someone to find something for you. 'Hindi ko makita yung remote.' 'Ipamata mo nga kay bunso, malakas ang mata n'un.' (I can't find the remote. 'Have the youngest look for it, that kid has sharp eyes.). It's delegating the act of seeing.
usage_notes: Not as common as 'ipahanap' (to have someone search), but it specifically emphasizes the use of sight.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ipamata** mo sa kanya kung nasaan ang mga susi.","translation":"**Have him spot** where the keys are."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **ipamata** ang isang maliit na bituin sa maulap na kalangitan.","translation":"It's hard **to have someone find** a small star in a cloudy sky."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglisan o pag-alis mula sa isang lugar, sitwasyon, o piling ng isang tao sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: The most dreaded word in a "paalam" scene. Also, the most common threat of a parent to a kid who takes too long getting ready: "Bilisan mo, aalis na tayo!"
usage_notes: The most common future tense form of 'alis'. It is used widely in daily conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Anong oras ka **aalis** bukas para sa flight mo?","translation":"What time **will** you **leave** tomorrow for your flight?"},{"sentence":"Kung hindi ka pa mag-aayos, **aalis** ako nang wala ka.","translation":"If you don't get ready now, I **will leave** without you."}]

meaning_filipino: Atasan, payagan, o maging sanhi na ang isang tao ay maturuan ng iba.
original_explanation: This is what your parents do when they hire a tutor for you because your math grades are... let's just say, 'developing.' 'Pinaturuan nila ako ng piano.' It’s not you asking to be taught (that's 'paturo'), but someone else arranging for you to receive instruction. It’s the outsourcing of teaching.
usage_notes: A causative verb. It means to cause someone to be taught by another person. The object of the verb is the person being taught.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais niyang **paturuan** ng Ingles ang kanyang anak sa isang dayuhan.","translation":"She wants to **have her child be taught** English by a foreigner."},{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **paturuan** ang kapatid niya sa pagmamaneho.","translation":"He decided to **have his sibling taught** how to drive."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-ilalim sa tubig o anumang likido; ang pagbaba ng isang bagay mula sa paningin, tulad ng araw sa kanluran.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your DMs when you get ghosted—they sink to the bottom. It’s also what the sun does every afternoon, giving you that perfect golden hour selfie opportunity. Metaphorically, it's when your career, your grades, or your ship (the romantic kind) goes down. 'Lumubog na ang career niya.'
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa literal na paglubog (isang bangka), ang pagtatakda ng mga bagay sa kalangitan (araw, buwan), o metaporikal na pagkabigo/paghina.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **lumubog** ang barko matapos itong mabangga sa isang malaking bato.","translation":"The ship began to **sink** after hitting a large rock."},{"sentence":"Napakagandang pagmasdan ang pag-**lumubog** ng araw sa Manila Bay.","translation":"It's beautiful to watch the sun **set** over Manila Bay."},{"sentence":"**Lumubog** siya sa utang dahil sa pagsusugal.","translation":"He **sank** into debt because of gambling."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbuo ng mga tanong upang makakuha ng impormasyon, linawin ang isang bagay, o magpahayag ng pagdududa.
original_explanation: The official sport of every chismosa, journalist, and curious cat. It's what you do when you see your ex with someone new ('Sino 'yan?!'), when you're lost in Quiapo ('Saan po papunta dito?'), or during a job interview ('What is your greatest weakness?'). It's the engine of all knowledge and gossip.
usage_notes: A fundamental act of communication.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Walang masama sa **pagtatanong** kung ikaw ay nalilito.","translation":"There's nothing wrong with **asking** if you are confused."},{"sentence":"Sinimulan niya ang imbestigasyon sa pamamagitan ng **pagtatanong** sa mga saksi.","translation":"He began the investigation by **questioning** the witnesses."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagkitil o pag-alis ng buhay ng isang tao, hayop, o anumang may buhay.
original_explanation: This is the grim, final act in a crime show or the reason you call pest control for that giant ipis. The darker side of the word, used for everything from tragic news reports to squashing a mosquito.
usage_notes: The general term for ending a life, less formal or specific than 'pagpaslang'. Context distinguishes it from 'turning off'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ikinulong siya dahil sa **pagpatay** sa isang negosyante.","translation":"He was jailed for the **killing** of a businessman."}]

translation: to change one's ways; to reform one's behavior
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabago ng ugali, asal, o gawi, karaniwan tungo sa mas mabuting kalagayan.
original_explanation: This is a level up from 'magbago.' It's not just a promise, it's a full character development arc. It’s what parents hope their pasaway na anak will do. When a notorious playboy suddenly becomes a one-woman man, that's **pagbabagong-kilos**. It’s about actions, not just words.
usage_notes: Refers to a change in behavior, conduct, or habits, usually for the better.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Simula nang magkaroon siya ng anak, napilitan siyang **magbagong-kilos** para sa kinabukasan nito.","translation":"Since having a child, he was forced **to change his ways** for its future."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang damdamin ng pagmamahal, paghanga, o pagkalugod sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: The feeling you get when you see a super cute puppy or a baby. It's the 'awww' emotion. It's the warm, fuzzy feeling that makes you want to pinch someone's cheeks (gently!). It's the opposite of 'pagkainis'.
usage_notes: Often associated with affection for something cute, charming, or endearing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya mapigilan ang kanyang **pagkagiliw** sa cute na tuta.","translation":"She couldn't contain her **delight** for the cute puppy."},{"sentence":"May espesyal na **pagkagiliw** ang lola sa kanyang bunsong apo.","translation":"The grandmother has a special **fondness** for her youngest grandchild."}]

meaning_filipino: Proseso ng pagkasira o pagkabulok ng isang organikong bagay dahil sa pagkilos ng mga mikroorganismo.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'bulok' at gitlaping '-um-'.
original_explanation: ‘Yung prutas na binili mo last week na nakalimutan mo sa ref, tapos pagkakita mo, ayun, may sarili nang ecosystem. Or ‘yung sistema na corrupt, `bumulok` na. It's when something good goes bad, literally or figuratively.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin nang literal para sa mga organikong bagay o sa matalinghagang paraan para sa mga sistema, moralidad, atbp.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumulok** ang isda dahil hindi agad nailagay sa yelo.","translation":"The fish **rotted** because it wasn't immediately put on ice."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa korapsyon, tila **bumulok** na ang tiwala ng tao sa gobyerno.","translation":"Because of corruption, it seems the people's trust in the government has **decayed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang unang bahagi ng Bibliyang Kristiyano, na binubuo ng mga aklat na isinulat bago ang kapanganakan ni Hesukristo.
original_explanation: The first half of the Bible, basically the 'OG' series before the main character's big reveal. It's got all the classic stories your lola told you about, like Noah's Ark, Moses parting the sea, and David vs. Goliath. Think of it as Season 1 of a massive epic.
usage_notes: Isang partikular na pangalan para sa isang relihiyosong teksto. Laging malaki ang mga unang titik.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming kuwento ng propesiya ang mababasa sa **Matandang Tipan**.","translation":"Many stories of prophecy can be read in the **Old Testament**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong mahilig magpasikat o laging gustong maging sentro ng atensyon, madalas sa paraang nakakainis.
original_explanation: That one officemate who answers the question you asked your boss. The 'know-it-all' in the group chat. The person who tries too hard to be the main character, but ends up being the annoying side character everyone wants to mute. It's giving 'pick me' energy.
usage_notes: Often used with a negative connotation. The spelling 'bidabida' (without the hyphen) is also common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag ka ngang **bida-bida**, hindi naman ikaw ang tinatanong.","translation":"Don't be a **show-off**, you weren't the one being asked."},{"sentence":"Nakakainis talaga 'yung mga taong **bida-bida** sa meeting.","translation":"Those **attention-seeking** people in the meeting are really annoying."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang pagkilos ng pakikilahok sa isang alitan, argumento, o pisikal na labanan sa ibang tao o pangkat.
original_explanation: When you're in the middle of a "bardagulan" online or a heated debate with your S.O. about where to eat. It's the present tense of conflict. "Huwag mo akong kausapin, nakikipag-away ako sa customer service sa chat."
usage_notes: This is a reciprocal verb, meaning the action is done with someone else. It is the progressive tense form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Palagi na lang silang **nakikipag-away** dahil sa pera.","translation":"They are always **fighting** because of money."},{"sentence":"Naririnig ko ang mga pusa na **nakikipag-away** sa bubong.","translation":"I can hear the cats **fighting** on the roof."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paunang proseso ng pagluto ng karne o gulay sa sarili nitong katas at kaunting mantika, bawang, at sibuyas bago tuluyang lutuin sa isang partikular na putahe.
original_explanation: This is the 'trust the process' stage in Filipino cooking. It's the step your lola does that you always want to skip, but she insists is the secret to a flavorful adobo or menudo. It's like pre-gaming for your ulam; you're not cooking it all the way, just getting it ready for the main event to lock in all that flavor.
usage_notes: A specific culinary term. It's different from 'paggigisa' (sautéing) as 'pagsasangkutsa' often involves letting the meat cook in its own juices for a bit longer.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tamang **pagsasangkutsa** ng baboy ay nagpapasarap sa adobo.","translation":"The proper **preliminary cooking** of the pork makes the adobo more delicious."},{"sentence":"Sinimulan niya ang pagluluto sa **pagsasangkutsa** ng manok sa bawang at sibuyas.","translation":"She started cooking by **searing** the chicken in garlic and onions."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagtataksil sa tiwala ng iba, lalo na sa isang kaibigan, pangkat, o sa sariling bayan.
original_explanation: That friend who eats the last piece of pizza you were saving. Or the one who tells your crush you like them without your permission. In teleseryes, the **traydor** is usually the 'best friend' of the bida who is secretly plotting their downfall. Basically, anyone who commits an act of ultimate backstabbing. Judas Iscariot is the poster boy for this.
usage_notes: Can also be used as an adjective (e.g., 'siya ay traydor'). The native Tagalog equivalent is 'taksil'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinuring ko siyang matalik na kaibigan, ngunit isa pala siyang **traydor**.","translation":"I considered him a close friend, but he turned out to be a **traitor**."},{"sentence":"Ang pagbenta ng sikreto ng kumpanya ay gawain ng isang **traydor**.","translation":"Selling company secrets is the act of a **traitor**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging naitanim o naibaon sa lupa; maaari ring tumukoy sa isang bagay na malalim na nakaugat sa isipan o damdamin.
original_explanation: Literally, 'yung halaman na tinanim mo sa paso. But figuratively, it's that 'hugot' or grudge you have against your ex that's been there for years. "Nakatamin pa rin sa puso ko ang sakit." It's deeply rooted, like a good 'chismis' in a group chat.
usage_notes: Can be used both literally for plants and figuratively for ideas, feelings, or memories.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming puno ng mangga ang **nakatanim** sa kanilang bakuran.","translation":"Many mango trees are **planted** in their yard."},{"sentence":"Hanggang ngayon, **nakatanim** pa rin sa isip niya ang sinabi mo.","translation":"Until now, what you said is still **embedded** in his mind."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pagkain na binubuo ng dalawa o higit pang piraso ng tinapay na may palaman sa gitna, tulad ng keso, hamon, o iba pang karne at gulay.
original_explanation: In the Philippines, a *sandwich* isn't just two slices of bread. It's the pambaon your mom makes, usually with cheese pimiento or egg salad in simple white bread. It's the star of birthday party meriendas, often with the crusts cut off. The pronunciation itself is a cultural marker - are you a /SAND-wits/ person or a more Pinoy /san-WITS/ person?
usage_notes: A common loanword fully integrated into Tagalog. Can also be used as a verb 'i-sandwich' (to be squeezed between two things).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko ng tuna **sandwich** para sa meryenda.","translation":"I want a tuna **sandwich** for a snack."},{"sentence":"Na-**sandwich** ako sa loob ng MRT sa sobrang dami ng tao.","translation":"I was **sandwiched** inside the MRT because it was so crowded."}]

meaning_filipino: Itulak o dalhin sa unahan; paunlarin o itaguyod ang isang bagay, ideya, o tao.
original_explanation: Think of it as hitting the 'fast forward' button on a project, a career, or a person's development. It's when your boss decides to 'pasulungin' your promotion, or when the government tries to 'pasulungin' a new infrastructure project. It's the act of giving something a push to get it going or to move it to the next level. Let's go!
usage_notes: This is the object-focused verb. The actor-focused counterpart is 'magsulong'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat nating **pasulungin** ang adbokasiya para sa malinis na kapaligiran.","translation":"We should **advance** the advocacy for a clean environment."},{"sentence":"Sila ang mga taong dapat nating **pasulungin** sa ating kumpanya.","translation":"They are the people we should **promote** in our company."}]

meaning_filipino: Isangkot o isama ang pangalan ng isang tao sa isang usapin, karaniwan ay sa isang kontrobersiya, krimen, o masamang gawain.
original_explanation: The ultimate "Huy, 'wag mo 'kong isama diyan" word. When your friend gets caught cheating on a test and tells the teacher you were their accomplice, you've just been `idinawit`. It's getting dragged into drama you (maybe) didn't start. Classic chismis-level stuff.
usage_notes: Carries a negative connotation, implying being unwillingly or unjustly involved in something problematic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pilit siyang **idinadawit** sa kaso ng pagnanakaw kahit wala siyang kinalaman.","translation":"They are trying to **implicate** him in the theft case even though he has no involvement."},{"sentence":"Ayokong **madawit** sa gulo ng mag-asawa.","translation":"I don't want to **get involved** in the couple's conflict."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng pag-ayaw, pagmamaliit, o mababang pagtingin sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: 'Yung tingin sa'yo ng guard sa isang high-end store. Or the look your dog gives you when you serve him the cheap dog food. It’s a look of judgment, a silent "eww," a mix of disgust and superiority. The physical manifestation of "you can't sit with us."
usage_notes: Often describes a look, glance ('tinging-iri'), or a general attitude. The verb form is 'irihan' (to look at each other with scorn) or adjective form 'ma-iri'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **iri** na tingin ang ipinukol niya sa akin.","translation":"She threw a **scornful** look at me."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko gusto ang kanyang pagiging **ma-iri** sa mga mahihirap.","translation":"I don't like his **disdainful** attitude towards the poor."}]

translation: to go to a neighboring town
meaning_filipino: Pumunta o maglakbay sa kalapit o katabing bayan, lalo na para sa isang partikular na layunin tulad ng pamimili o pagdalo sa pista.
original_explanation: This is what you do when the palengke in your town is 'meh', so you go to the next town over for better deals. Or when your town's fiesta is over, and you move on to the next town's celebration to get more free food. It's a low-key, local version of traveling.
usage_notes: This verb implies a short trip to an adjacent locality, not a long-distance journey. It's the town-level equivalent of 'mangapitbahay' (to visit a neighbor).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **mangapit-bayan** tuwing Sabado para mamili ng sariwang gulay.","translation":"She likes to **go to the neighboring town** every Saturday to buy fresh vegetables."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing malamig o ibaba ang temperatura ng isang bagay na mainit.
original_explanation: The command you give to your freshly cooked rice or coffee before you dive in and burn your tongue. It's also what you need to do to your phone when it's overheating from playing games all day. Basically, taking the 'init' out of something.
usage_notes: Primarily used for objects, food, and drinks. For emotions, see the idiom "palamigin ang galit" or "palamigin ang ulo".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hayaan mo munang **palamigin** ang sopas bago kainin.","translation":"Let the soup **cool down** first before eating."},{"sentence":"Gusto kong **palamigin** ang tubig sa refrigerator.","translation":"I want to **chill** the water in the refrigerator."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salita, ideya, o bagay na may diwa o katangiang kabaligtaran ng isa pa.
original_explanation: Ito yung 'It's not you, it's me' mo sa ex mo. Yung exact opposite ng sinasabi mo sa nararamdaman mo. Sa grammar, ito ang antonym. Sa buhay, ito yung best friend mong laging kontra sa'yo pero mahal mo pa rin.
usage_notes: Commonly used in academic settings (language, logic) and also in general conversation to mean a contrary or opposite concept.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kasalungat** ng 'mainit' ay 'malamig'.","translation":"The **opposite** of 'hot' is 'cold'."},{"sentence":"Lagi siyang **kasalungat** ng opinyon ng karamihan.","translation":"He is always on the **opposite** side of the majority's opinion."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang napakakolokyal na termino para sa isang grupo ng magkakaibigan o barkada.
etymology: Hindi malinaw ang pinagmulan, posibleng baryasyon ng "tropa" o hango sa isang pangalan. Naging popular sa social media noong mga 2010s.
original_explanation: Parang "tropa" pero medyo conyo or trying hard, depende sa gumagamit. Baka galing sa "Tyrone," isang generic name, na naging pangalan ng grupo. "Sama ka sa 'tryon' namin mamaya?" sounds like an invite to a very exclusive, possibly awkward, barkada hangout.
usage_notes: Isang napakakolokyal at hindi gaanong laganap na slang. Mas karaniwan ang "tropa" o "barkada".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kasama ko ang **tryon** ko kagabi, nanood kami ng sine.","translation":"I was with my **squad** last night, we watched a movie."},{"sentence":"Ang ingay ng **tryon** nina Mark sa kabilang table.","translation":"Mark's **group of friends** at the other table is so noisy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang istrukturang harang sa daluyan ng tubig, tulad ng ilog, upang kontrolin ang agos, patubig, o para manghuli ng isda.
original_explanation: It's like the original flood control project of the barangay. Before DPWH had mega-dams, our ancestors built a **saplad** to manage water flow and get a steady supply of fish. Think of it as a natural, low-tech dam made of bamboo and rocks.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglagay ang mga mangingisda ng **saplad** sa ilog upang makahuli ng maraming isda.","translation":"The fishermen placed a **weir** in the river to catch a lot of fish."},{"sentence":"Nasira ang **saplad** dahil sa malakas na agos ng tubig mula sa bundok.","translation":"The **dam** was destroyed by the strong water current from the mountain."}]

meaning_filipino: Mawalan ng kulay o maging maputla ang balat, karaniwan dahil sa takot, sakit, o gulat.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your face when your boss catches you scrolling through TikTok at work, or when you see the bill after treating all your friends. It's the physical manifestation of 'patay kang bata ka.' Your blood literally drains from your face.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for paleness due to illness or figuratively for paleness due to strong emotion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula siyang **mamutla** nang makita niya ang multo.","translation":"He started to **turn pale** when he saw the ghost."},{"sentence":"Kung lagi kang puyat, hindi katakatakang **mamumutla** ka.","translation":"If you're always sleep-deprived, it's not surprising that you will **become pale**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng isang kagamitan o bagay na idinisenyo upang hawakan o kapitan.
original_explanation: Yung parte ng mug, pinto, o kaldero na pwede mong kapitan para hindi ka mapaso o mahirapan. The 'user interface' for your hands on any object. Kung sa relationship, ito yung 'label'. Para alam mo kung saan ka kakapit.
usage_notes: Ang diin ay nasa huling pantig (ha-wa-KAN), na nagpapaiba rito sa pandiwa na 'hawákan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasira ang **hawakan** ng pinto kaya hindi kami makalabas.","translation":"The door **handle** broke so we couldn't get out."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mensaheng isinulat sa papel; ang paraan o estilo ng pagsusulat ng isang tao; anumang nakasulat na bagay.
original_explanation: Before DMs, Messenger, and email, there was **sulat**. This involved paper, a pen, and a trip to the post office. It's also used to refer to your handwriting, which your teacher would either praise or call "sulat-manok" (chicken scratch).
usage_notes: A very versatile root word. "Sumulat" (to write), "isulat" (to write something down), "sulatan" (to write to someone/on something).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatanggap ako ng **sulat** mula sa aking kaibigan sa probinsya.","translation":"I received a **letter** from my friend in the province."},{"sentence":"Ang hirap basahin ng **sulat** mo, parang kinahig ng manok.","translation":"Your **handwriting** is so hard to read, it looks like chicken scratch."}]

translation: act of taking a detour; meandering
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-iwas sa tuwid o karaniwang daan; pagpili sa isang paliku-likong landas.
etymology: From `pag-` (gerund prefix) + reduplication of the first syllable of the root `li-` + `likaw` (coil, wind).
original_explanation: It's what Waze does when there's an accident on EDSA—the 'paglilikaw' to a side street that looks promising but is actually a portal to another dimension of traffic. It's also your friend's storytelling style, taking a million detours before getting to the point.
usage_notes: Can refer to a physical detour or a metaphorical one, like in a conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa saradong kalsada, kinailangan naming gawin ang **paglilikaw** sa mga eskinita.","translation":"Because of the closed road, we had to do a **detour** through the side streets."},{"sentence":"Ang **paglilikaw** ng usapan ay paraan niya upang iwasan ang tunay na isyu.","translation":"The **meandering** of the conversation is his way of avoiding the real issue."}]

meaning_filipino: Halaga ng pera na ibinibigay bilang kapalit ng isang produkto, serbisyo, o utang.
original_explanation: The one word that can either bring you joy (sahod!) or cause you immense stress (bills!). From the "Bayad po!" you shout in the jeepney, to the due date on your Meralco bill, this word runs the Filipino economy. It's the reason you work OT and the reason you can afford that milk tea.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb root (e.g., magbayad, bayaran).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakalimutan kong iabot ang **bayad** ko sa jeep.","translation":"I forgot to hand over my **fare** in the jeep."},{"sentence":"Tumaas na naman ang **bayad** sa kuryente.","translation":"The **payment** for electricity has increased again."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsara o pagtiklop, karaniwang tumutukoy sa bibig, labi, o mga bagay na may dalawang bahagi tulad ng kabibe o aklat.
original_explanation: When your friend is about to spill a secret in the wrong company and you give them "the look." Their mouth immediately does this. It's the physical manifestation of "shut up." Also what you do when your Tita asks, "Kailan ka ikakasal?" You just smile and **tumikom** ang bibig.
usage_notes: Most often used as 'tumikom ang bibig' (to shut one's mouth), implying silence or refusal to speak.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nang tanungin tungkol sa sikreto, siya ay ngumiti lamang at **tumikom**.","translation":"When asked about the secret, he just smiled and **kept his mouth shut**."},{"sentence":"Mabilis na **tumikom** ang mga kabibe nang maramdaman ang panganib.","translation":"The clams quickly **closed** shut when they sensed danger."}]

translation: to fall flat on one's back
meaning_filipino: Isang baryasyon ng 'timbuwang'; ang biglaang pagbagsak na nakatihaya.
original_explanation: This is the slightly less common but equally dramatic twin of 'timbuwang'. Same energy: you slip, you fall, you see the ceiling. It’s just a different flavor of saying you had a very ungraceful, gravity-won-today moment.
usage_notes: Isang baryasyon ng 'timbuwang', na mas madalas gamitin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang pagod, halos **timbwang** na siya sa kama pag-uwi.","translation":"From extreme exhaustion, he practically **fell flat on his back** onto the bed upon arriving home."}]

translation: a type of Filipino bread roll
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng sikat na tinapay sa Pilipinas na malambot, medyo matamis, at may katangian na hiwa sa gitna.
etymology: Pinaniniwalaang nagmula sa "pan de monja" (tinapay ng madre).
original_explanation: The OG of Pinoy breads. It’s that dense, slightly sweet bread roll with a distinctive butt-like shape or a split down the middle. Perfect for dipping in coffee or pairing with kesong puti. It's the comfort food your lola would buy from the panaderia every morning.
usage_notes: This entry refers to the bread. The word has a well-known vulgar slang meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pabili po ng sampung pisong **monay**.","translation":"I'd like to buy ten pesos' worth of **monay**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gusali na ginagamit bilang sentro ng mga gawain at pagpupulong ng isang partikular na samahan, organisasyon, o klub.
original_explanation: This is your subdivision's clubhouse where they hold the homeowners' association meetings, Zumba classes, and the annual Christmas party. It’s the HQ for all the chismis and official business of your community.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gaganapin ang pagpupulong ng mga miyembro sa **bahay-samahan**.","translation":"The members' meeting will be held at the **clubhouse**."},{"sentence":"Ipinaparenta ang **bahay-samahan** para sa mga pribadong okasyon.","translation":"The **association building** is for rent for private occasions."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpapanatili ng pagkakapantay-pantay sa timbang, distribusyon, o posisyon upang hindi gumuho o mahulog.
original_explanation: The verb form of your life goal. It's what you do when you're carrying 5 grocery bags, a laptop, and your dignity, all while trying not to trip. It's also what your accountant does with your finances, or what you try to do with your feelings after seeing your ex's wedding photos.
usage_notes: Often used in both literal (physical balance) and figurative (balancing accounts, emotions, schedules) contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **balansihin** ang mga libro ng kumpanya bago matapos ang buwan.","translation":"You need **to balance** the company's books before the end of the month."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang **balansihin** ang kanyang mga paa habang naglalakad sa makitid na tulay.","translation":"He is trying **to balance** his feet while walking on the narrow bridge."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng katangiang nakakaakit o nakakabighani sa iba, maaaring sa pisikal na anyo, ugali, o paraan ng pananalita.
original_explanation: Yung friend mo na kahit anong suot, kahit bagong gising, ang lakas pa rin ng dating. Parang magnet sa tao, hindi mo maiwasang mapatingin. Sila yung tipo na kahit 'pabili po' lang ang sinasabi, parang nang-haharana na. Charisma level: 9000.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a person's physical appearance, personality, or even a place or an offer.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **mapang-akit** na ngiti ang dalaga kaya marami ang nabibighani sa kanya.","translation":"The young woman has an **attractive** smile, which is why many are charmed by her."},{"sentence":"Ang alok na trabaho sa ibang bansa ay **mapang-akit** ngunit kailangan itong pag-isipang mabuti.","translation":"The job offer abroad is **alluring**, but it needs to be carefully considered."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng bahagi o ambag sa isang grupo para sa isang partikular na layunin.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of "ambag". When your team is ordering pizza and the boss says "KKB" (kanya-kanyang bayad), you need to "iamot" your share. It's the spirit of bayanihan but for potlucks and group projects.
usage_notes: While 'ambag' is the more common noun/root, 'iamot' is the specific verb for contributing one's share. It's closely related to 'mag-ambag'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **iamot** ang P100 para sa ating Christmas party.","translation":"Don't forget to **contribute** P100 for our Christmas party."},{"sentence":"Ang bawat miyembro ay inaasahang **iamot** ang kanilang kaalaman sa proyekto.","translation":"Each member is expected to **contribute** their knowledge to the project."}]

translation: to consume; to use up; to exasperate
meaning_filipino: Ubusin o gamitin ang isang bagay. Sa ibang pakahulugan, magdulot ng matinding inis o pagkabagot.
original_explanation: Has two flavors. 1) The literal one: what you do to a whole tub of ice cream after a breakup ('kinunsumo ko lahat'). 2) The emotional one: what your slow internet connection does to your patience. It's that feeling of being drained, either of resources or of your will to live. 'Nakukunsumi ako sa'yo!' is the Pinoy version of 'You're testing me.'
usage_notes: The meaning shifts based on context, from literal consumption of goods to the emotional 'consumption' of one's patience.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **kunsumihin** lahat ng pagkain; magtira ka para sa iba.","translation":"Don't **consume** all the food; leave some for others."},{"sentence":"Talagang kinunsumi niya ang pasensya ko sa kahihintay.","translation":"He really **used up** (exasperated) my patience while I was waiting."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na tawag sa ninong ng anak ng isang tao o sa kapwa lalaking abay sa kasal. Ito ang orihinal na anyo ng salitang 'kumpare'.
original_explanation: This is the 'Tito' or 'old school' version of 'kumpare.' It sounds more formal, like something your Lolo would say. You use 'kumpadre' when you're feeling a bit classy or talking about the actual sacramental relationship. It has a slightly more serious, 'we are officially bonded by the church' vibe than the beer-buddy 'kumpare.'
usage_notes: The more formal and older variant of 'kumpare'. Often used by older generations or in more formal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"\"Isang malaking karangalan na maging **kumpadre** ninyo,\" wika ni Don Alberto.","translation":"\"It is a great honor to be your **kumpadre**,\" said Don Alberto."},{"sentence":"Ipinakilala niya sa amin ang kanyang **kumpadre** na galing pa sa Espanya.","translation":"He introduced us to his **kumpadre** who came all the way from Spain."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging maginhawa, walang hirap, o madali.
original_explanation: The feeling of "Sana all." Ito 'yung buhay na chill lang, walang stress sa bills, walang toxic na boss. 'Yung tipong naka-pajama ka lang buong araw, nanonood ng Netflix, with matching unlimited food delivery. The opposite of "sa hirap at ginhawa" -- ito 'yung pure ginhawa part.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa anyong 'kaalwanan' na nangangahulugang kaginhawahan o kasaganaan. Isang mas pampanitikan na salita. Mas karaniwan ang 'ginhawa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghahanap siya ng **alwan** sa buhay.","translation":"He is searching for **ease** in life."},{"sentence":"Sana'y magdulot ng **alwan** sa iyong kalooban ang balitang ito.","translation":"I hope this news brings **comfort** to your spirit."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tanong na tumutukoy sa bilang o dami na nakalaan para sa bawat isa sa isang pangkat.
original_explanation: The question you ask your friend who just came back from a trip with pasalubong. "So, tig-iilan ang keychains na dala mo? Para alam ko kung aasa pa ba ako." It's the official question for fair distribution.
usage_notes: The "Tig-" prefix denotes distribution among a group. Can also be written as 'Tig-ilan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tig-iilan** ang dapat nating ibigay na candy sa bawat bata?","translation":"**How many for each** of us should we give candies to each child?"},{"sentence":"Hindi ko alam kung **tig-iilan** tayo sa bayad, kaya hatiin na lang natin nang pantay-pantay.","translation":"I don't know **how many each** of us should pay, so let's just split it equally."}]

meaning_filipino: Salitang balbal para sa isang alternatibo o pangalawang account sa social media, karaniwang anonimo at ginagamit para sa mga pribado, prangka, o sekswal na nilalaman.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na 'alternate', pinaikli at binigyan ng bagong kahulugan sa konteksto ng social media sa Pilipinas.
original_explanation: This is your secret identity on Twitter or other social media. It's the account where you can be your 'truest' self, free from the judgment of family and workmates. For many, 'Alter World' is a space for thirst traps, hugot, political rants, or finding community. It's the digital version of wearing a mask at a party—what happens on 'alter,' stays on 'alter.'
usage_notes: Isang napakapopular na salitang balbal sa 'Filipino Twitter' at iba pang online spaces, lalo na sa mga komunidad ng LGBTQ+. Ang kahulugan nito ay iba sa karaniwang pandiwang Ingles na 'alter' (to change).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong i-follow ang **alter** ko, para sa mga kaibigan ko lang 'yun.","translation":"Don't follow my **alter** account, that's just for my friends."},{"sentence":"Maraming naglalabas ng kanilang tunay na saloobin sa kani-kanilang mga **alter** account.","translation":"Many express their true feelings on their respective **alter** accounts."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging sanhi ng paulit-ulit at madalas na paglundag ng isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: This is what you do to a baby on your lap to make them giggle, or what a bumpy jeepney ride does to its passengers on a rough road. It's causing continuous, often playful, jumping. Think of a kid on a trampoline because you paid for their 30-minute session.
usage_notes: The reduplication 'talun-talon' implies a repeated, often less controlled, jumping motion compared to a single 'patalonin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **magpatalun-talon** ng sanggol sa kanyang mga tuhod.","translation":"He likes to **make the baby jump repeatedly** on his knees."},{"sentence":"Ang magaspang na kalsada ang **nagpapatalun-talon** sa mga sakay ng bus.","translation":"The rough road is **causing the bus passengers to jump repeatedly**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng paligsahan kung saan ang mga kalahok ay bumibili ng tiket para sa pagkakataong manalo ng malalaking premyo, na kadalasang pinangangasiwaan ng pamahalaan o isang malaking korporasyon.
original_explanation: Yung pag-asa mong manalo sa lotto o sa raffle sa Christmas party ng office. Biglang yaman ang pangarap, pero madalas, drawing lang. Ito 'yung official na 'sana all' moment kapag may nanalo ng grand prize.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng mga loterya, raffle, at mga promosyonal na paligsahan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumali si Aling Nena sa **sweepstakes** sa pag-asa na manalo ng bahay at lupa.","translation":"Aling Nena joined the **sweepstakes** hoping to win a house and lot."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hanay ng mga tagubilin, alituntunin, o gabay na dapat sundin upang maisagawa nang wasto ang isang gawain o proseso.
original_explanation: The thing you're supposed to read before assembling your Shopee/IKEA purchase but never do. It's the 'Basahin nang mabuti' on your exam paper that you ignore at your own peril. From cooking instant noodles to answering a test, the panuto is your guide to not messing things up.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sundin ang **panuto** sa kahon para sa tamang pagluto.","translation":"Follow the **instructions** on the box for proper cooking."},{"sentence":"Hindi malinaw ang **panuto** ng guro kaya marami ang nagkamali sa pagsusulit.","translation":"The teacher's **directions** were not clear, so many made mistakes on the test."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ideya, parirala, o elemento sa sining na gasgas na o masyado nang nagamit kaya nawalan na ng orihinalidad at epekto.
etymology: Mula sa Pranses na 'cliché', sa pamamagitan ng Espanyol.
original_explanation: Ito yung mga linyang 'It's not you, it's me' sa breakup, o 'yung eksena sa pelikula na biglang uulan 'pag may dramatic moment. Mga bagay na sobrang paulit-ulit na ginamit, alam mo na ang kasunod. Parang 'yung 'All roads lead to Rome'—sa Pinoy teleserye, 'All plots lead to amnesia.' 'Yan ang klitse.
usage_notes: Ginagamit din bilang pang-uri (hal. 'klitseng linya').
