usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating mag-**usap** nang masinsinan tungkol dito.","translation":"We need to **talk** seriously about this."},{"sentence":"Ano ba ang pinag-uusapan ninyo at mukhang seryoso?","translation":"What are you talking about that seems so serious?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng panandaliang pag-idlip o pagtulog nang hindi sinasadya, lalo na kapag nakaupo.
original_explanation: That head-bobbing motion you do in a boring meeting or during a long bus ride in traffic. It's the 'tulog-manok' state where you're not fully asleep but definitely not awake. The body's way of saying 'I give up, kahit 5 minutes lang'.
usage_notes: A more literary or formal term for dozing off. 'Pag-idlip' is the more common term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya namalayan ang kanyang **pagkagupiling** dahil sa sobrang pagod.","translation":"He didn't notice himself **dozing off** due to extreme fatigue."},{"sentence":"Madalas ang kanyang **pagkagupiling** sa klase tuwing hapon.","translation":"His **dozing off** in class in the afternoon is frequent."}]

meaning_filipino: Mapagmasid o mapag-obserba sa mga pangyayari, tao, o bagay sa paligid.
original_explanation: Ito yung kaibigan mong parang CCTV, lahat napapansin. Mula sa bagong T-shirt mo hanggang sa pag-iba ng mood mo dahil di ka ni-replyan ni crush. Sila yung mga professional 'spot the difference' player sa totoong buhay.
usage_notes: Mas karaniwang ginagamit ang anyong 'mapagmasid' sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap upang ilarawan ang isang tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **masid** na bata si Jose, lahat ng detalye ay kanyang napupuna.","translation":"Jose is a very **observant** child; he notices every detail."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katawagan para kay Hesukristo, na tumutukoy sa kanyang pinagmulan sa Nazaret. Ginagamit din ito upang ilarawan ang imahen ng Itim na Nazareno sa Quiapo.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "Nazareno", na nangangahulugang "mula sa Nazaret".
original_explanation: Ito yung dahilan kung bakit super traffic sa Maynila tuwing January. Ang Poong Nasareno (o Black Nazarene) ay dinudumog ng milyun-milyong deboto sa Quiapo na umaasang sa isang himala. Ang prusisyon ay isang extreme sport ng pananampalataya.
usage_notes: Kadalasang tumutukoy sa Itim na Nazareno ng Quiapo sa kontekstong Pilipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming deboto ang dumalo sa pista ng Itim na **Nasareno** sa Quiapo.","translation":"Many devotees attended the feast of the Black **Nazarene** in Quiapo."}]

translation: to become clear, to perceive clearly
meaning_filipino: Maging malinaw at lantad sa paningin o pang-unawa; makita o maunawaan nang malinaw ang isang bagay na dati'y malabo.
original_explanation: That 'Aha!' moment when the chismis finally makes sense. Dati, blurry 'yung details, parang 240p na YouTube video. Ngayon, nag-HD na, at finally, 'umaninaw' na sa'yo kung sino talaga ang ahas sa group chat.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for vision (e.g., something seen through water) or figuratively for understanding.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **umaninaw** din sa kaniya ang tunay na motibo ng kaibigan niya.","translation":"Finally, the true motive of his friend **became clear** to him."},{"sentence":"Nang tumahimik ang tubig, **umaninaw** ang mga isda sa ilalim ng ilog.","translation":"When the water became still, the fish at the bottom of the river **became visible**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtakas o pag-alis mula sa isang lugar, sitwasyon, o obligasyon nang walang pahintulot.
original_explanation: That feeling when you successfully leave the family reunion without having to sing karaoke. Or when you manage to log off exactly at 5 PM before your boss can give you more work. It's the art of the ninja exit.
usage_notes: A Tagalized version of the English word, commonly used in informal speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng bilanggo na **umiskape** ngunit nahuli rin siya.","translation":"The prisoner tried to **escape** but was eventually caught."},{"sentence":"Gusto ko sanang **umiskape** sa lahat ng problema ko kahit isang araw lang.","translation":"I wish I could **escape** from all my problems for just one day."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging nakahandusay o nakalagay nang pahalang sa isang daanan, na nagsisilbing hadlang o sagabal.
original_explanation: Imagine a motorcycle parked horizontally, taking up three parking slots. Or your dog sleeping right in the middle of the hallway at night. That's 'hambalang'. It's something lying in the way, being a total nuisance, blocking the flow. 'May punong **hambalang** sa kalsada kaya traffic.'
usage_notes: Almost always used with the prefix 'naka-' (nakahambalang) to mean 'is lying across'. Describes a state of obstruction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malaking troso ang **hambalang** sa gitna ng daan pagkatapos ng bagyo.","translation":"A large log was **lying across** the middle of the road after the storm."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang matulog nang **hambalang** sa kama, wala na akong mahihigaan.","translation":"Don't sleep **sprawled across** the bed, there's no space left for me to lie down."}]

translation: to put beside; to place next to
meaning_filipino: Ilagay o ilipat ang isang tao o bagay sa tabi ng iba pa, kadalasan sa paraang maingat o magiliw.
original_explanation: That romantic movie scene where the hero lays the unconscious heroine on a bed. Or more practically, when your mom tells you to put the fragile vase beside the wall so no one knocks it over. "Ipiling mo ang bata sa kanyang ina."
usage_notes: This word is a bit more literary or formal compared to the more common 'ilagay sa tabi'. It often carries a gentle or careful connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marahan niyang **inipiling** ang sanggol sa kuna.","translation":"She gently **placed** the baby **beside** (her) in the crib."},{"sentence":"**Ipiling** mo ang plorera sa gitna ng mesa.","translation":"**Place** the vase **next to** the center of the table."}]

meaning_filipino: Inilalarawan ang isang tao na mayroon pang muta sa mata.
original_explanation: The adjective form of 'muta'. If 'muta' is the 'what', 'mutain' is the 'who'. 'Huwag kang mag-selfie, mutain ka pa!' It's a state of being, specifically the 'I just woke up and haven't looked in a mirror' state.
usage_notes: While it can technically be a verb ('to get rheum on something'), it is overwhelmingly used as a descriptive adjective.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bakit **mutain** ka pa? Hindi ka pa ba naghihilamos?","translation":"Why do you still **have sleep in your eyes**? Haven't you washed your face yet?"},{"sentence":"Nagmamadaling pumasok sa klase ang **mutain** na estudyante.","translation":"The student, still **with sleep in his eyes**, rushed to enter the class."}]

translation: to shelter; to adopt; to take someone in
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng kanlungan, proteksyon, at pag-aaruga sa isang tao o hayop na nangangailangan.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you see a stray kitten in the rain and decide to take it home. It's the act of providing a safe space, whether you're an NGO helping street children or just a friend letting another friend crash on their couch after a bad breakup. It’s pure, kind-hearted sheltering.
usage_notes: Carries a strong connotation of care and protection.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pamilya nila ang **kumupkop** sa mga batang naulila dahil sa bagyo.","translation":"Their family **sheltered** the children who were orphaned by the typhoon."},{"sentence":"**Kumupkop** siya ng isang pusang kalye.","translation":"He **adopted** a stray cat."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdagdag sa kapal, lapot, o pagiging mas siksik ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: This describes something getting thicker. It could be the sauce you're cooking that's finally reducing ('lumabnaw' is the opposite). It could be the crowd at the mall during a sale. Or, in classic Pinoy slang, it could be someone's face: "Kumapal na ang mukha mo!" means "You've become shameless!" It's a versatile word for density, literal or figurative.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for substances (sauce, paint) or figuratively for things like crowds or a person's shamelessness ('kapal ng mukha').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinalo niya ang sarsa hanggang sa ito ay **kumapal**.","translation":"She stirred the sauce until it **thickened**."},{"sentence":"**Kumapal** ang usok mula sa nasusunog na gusali.","translation":"The smoke from the burning building **grew thicker**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, **kumapal** na ang kalyo ko sa mga ganyang salita.","translation":"Don't worry, my skin has **grown thick** to words like that (figurative)."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang biglaan at hindi mapigilang pagbuga ng hangin mula sa ilong at bibig, karaniwang sanhi ng iritasyon sa ilong. Ang salita ay maaari ring gamitin bilang pangngalan na tumutukoy sa mismong akto.
original_explanation: That explosive 'Achoo!' that happens when dust, pepper, or your allergies decide to attack. It’s always followed by someone saying 'Bless you!'. The verb form is 'bumahin' (to sneeze). The noun for the sneeze itself is also 'bahin'.
usage_notes: Ang salitang 'bahin' ay parehong pangngalan (sneeze) at pandiwang-ugat (to sneeze). Ang pandiwang pokus sa aktor ay 'bumahin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malakas na **bahin** ang pinakawalan niya.","translation":"He let out a loud **sneeze**."},{"sentence":"**Bumahin** siya nang maamoy ang alikabok.","translation":"He **sneezed** when he smelled the dust."}]

translation: to shake out; to dust off by shaking
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng malakas na pag-alog o pagpagpag sa isang bagay upang maalis ang laman, alikabok, o anumang nakakapit dito.
original_explanation: The move you do with a bag of chips to get the last crumbs out. Or what you do to your doormat before bringing it inside. Also a metaphor for getting rid of bad vibes or a clingy ex. "Itaktak mo na 'yang lungkot, girl. Friday na!"
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun ('pagtaktak') or a verb ('itaktak', 'taktakin'). Often implies a downward shaking motion to empty a container or remove dust.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Taktak** mo muna ang basahan bago mo ipasok sa bahay.","translation":"**Shake out** the rag first before you bring it inside the house."},{"sentence":"Itinaktak niya ang laman ng kanyang pitaka sa mesa.","translation":"He **shook out** the contents of his wallet onto the table."}]

translation: to be able to make someone smile
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang maging sanhi ng pagngiti ng isang tao.
original_explanation: The effect of a cute dog video, a surprise 'kamusta' from a friend, or seeing your salary finally hit your bank account. It's the ability to cause a smile. "Kahit simpleng text lang, makapagpapangiti na sa kanya."
usage_notes: Purely about causing a smile, often indicating happiness or amusement.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang alaala ng aming pagkabata ay laging **nakapagpapangiti** sa akin.","translation":"The memory of our childhood always **makes me smile**."},{"sentence":"Sana ang dala kong pasalubong ay **makapagpangiti** sa mga bata.","translation":"I hope the souvenir I brought can **make the children smile**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na hindi pa umabot sa legal na gulang para sa isang partikular na gawain, tulad ng pagboto, pag-aasawa, o pag-inom ng alak.
original_explanation: The classic line used by bouncers or your parents when you want to do something "adult." "Bakit hindi ako pwede pumasok sa club?" "Wala ka pa sa edad." "Bakit bawal pa magka-jowa?" "Wala ka pa sa edad." It's the official term for being a minor with major adulting ambitions.
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang termino sa batas at lipunan. Ang partikular na "edad" ay depende sa konteksto (hal., 18 para sa pagboto).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi siya maaaring bumoto dahil **wala pa siya sa edad**.","translation":"She cannot vote because she is **underage**."},{"sentence":"Bawal magbenta ng alak sa mga customer na **wala pa sa edad**.","translation":"It's forbidden to sell alcohol to customers who are **not of legal age**."}]
related: ["menor de edad","bata pa","nasa hustong gulang","may sapat na gulang"]

meaning_filipino: Isang solusyon ng tubig na may mataas na konsentrasyon ng asin, ginagamit sa pag-iimbak o pagluluto ng pagkain.
original_explanation: That salty water you soak your chicken in before frying to make it extra juicy. It's the secret weapon of many home cooks and fast-food chains for achieving next-level 'sarap'. Basically, tubig na may asin, but make it sound fancy.
usage_notes: Primarily used in culinary contexts. Not a common word in everyday conversation, but understood by those familiar with cooking techniques.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ibinabad niya ang manok sa **brine** nang magdamag para lumambot.","translation":"She soaked the chicken in **brine** overnight to make it tender."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o pagkuha ng serbisyo ng iba upang maglagay ng halaman o buto sa lupa upang ito ay tumubo.
original_explanation: The official verb of the 'plantito/plantita' who has more money than time. You don't plant the Monstera yourself; you hire a gardener to do it. Or, it's what the DENR does during tree-planting drives—they cause people to plant trees. You're the director of the planting operation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagpatanim** si Mayor ng maraming puno sa gilid ng kalsada.","translation":"The Mayor **had many trees planted** on the side of the road."},{"sentence":"Gusto kong **magpatanim** ng mga gulay sa aming bakuran.","translation":"I want to **have vegetables planted** in our yard."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-ipon o pagpagsalubong ng mga kilay na nagpapahiwatig ng pagkalito, pag-aalala, o galit.
original_explanation: The default facial expression when your internet suddenly dies during a final presentation, or when you see your sibling wearing your favorite shirt without permission. It's the "RBF" (Resting Baffled Face) of the Filipino psyche. The opposite of a "sana all" moment.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used with "noo" (forehead) or "kilay" (eyebrows). "Ikunot ang noo."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ikunot** ang iyong noo, malulutas din natin ang problemang ito.","translation":"Don't **furrow** your brow, we will solve this problem eventually."},{"sentence":"Napangiwi siya at biglang **ikinunot** ang kilay nang marinig ang balita.","translation":"He winced and suddenly **furrowed** his eyebrows when he heard the news."}]

translation: to be able to be like; to be able to imitate
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang gumaya, maging kapareho, o maging kawangis ng isang tao, bagay, o ideya.
original_explanation: When your mom says, "Sana makatulad ka ng kuya mo!" (I hope you can be like your older brother!), that's 'makatulad'. It's the ability to be similar to or to successfully imitate someone or something, for better or for worse. It's the core of every impersonator's career.
usage_notes: Often used in comparisons, aspirations, or warnings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Walang sinuman ang **makakatulad** sa galing ni Jose Rizal.","translation":"No one will **be able to be like** the greatness of Jose Rizal."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang **makatulad** sa istilo ng pananamit ng kanyang idolo.","translation":"She is trying **to be able to imitate** the fashion style of her idol."}]

meaning_filipino: Ipakita o iparamdam ang kasiyahan at paghanga para sa isang tao, bagay, o nagawa. Madama ang karangalan dahil sa isang bagay.
etymology: From i- + pag- + malaki (big). The sense is 'to make something big' in the eyes of others, to hold in high esteem.
original_explanation: This is the feeling when your sibling graduates with honors, when Hidilyn Diaz wins a gold medal, or when your ube cheese pandesal business finally takes off. It's the positive version of showing off. You're not just bragging; you're genuinely happy and honored. It's the 'That's my boy!' or 'Pinoy Pride!' moment. You want to **be proud of** it and tell the whole world.
usage_notes: Can be used positively to express genuine pride. It's different from `ipagmagaling` or `ipagyabang`, which are almost always negative (boasting/bragging).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat nating **ipagmalaki** ang ating kultura at wika.","translation":"We should **be proud of** our culture and language."},{"sentence":"Talagang **ipinagmalaki** niya ang kanyang anak na nakapasa sa board exam.","translation":"She was really **proud of** her child who passed the board exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pampublikong pagmamartsa o prusisyon, karaniwang isinasagawa bilang bahagi ng isang pagdiriwang, na may kasamang mga banda, float, at mga kalahok na naka-kostyum.
original_explanation: Fiesta mode: ON! A 'parada' is a parade, the highlight of any town fiesta. Expect marching bands playing off-key, dazzling floats sponsored by the local pawnshop, beauty queens waving awkwardly, and politicians taking the opportunity to shake hands. It's loud, colorful, and a guaranteed cause of traffic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nanonood kami ng **parada** tuwing pista sa aming bayan.","translation":"We watch the **parade** every town fiesta."},{"sentence":"Sumali ang mga mag-aaral sa **parada** para sa Araw ng Kalayaan.","translation":"The students joined the **parade** for Independence Day."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng damit na walang manggas, karaniwang isinusuot sa mainit na panahon o bilang panloob na damit.
etymology: Likely from a genericized brand name or a colloquial evolution from Spanish clothing terms.
original_explanation: The official uniform of the Pinoy *tambay* and the go-to outfit for a quick trip to the sari-sari store. Also the required attire for playing basketball in the *kanto* or doing household chores on a sweltering Saturday. It's the Philippines' answer to summer fashion, prioritizing ventilation above all else.
usage_notes: Often worn by men, but the term can apply to women's tank tops as well.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pawis na pawis siya kaya nagsuot na lang siya ng **sando**.","translation":"He was so sweaty so he just wore a **tank top**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang lalabas nang naka-**sando** lang, baka sipunin ka.","translation":"Don't go out wearing just a **tank top**, you might catch a cold."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paraan ng pagtulak; paggamit ng puwersa upang maialis sa isang lugar o maipasa sa iba.
original_explanation: How you get through a crowded MRT station during rush hour. Or how you pass the blame to your workmate when the boss asks who made the mistake. "Sagot niya 'yan," you say while gesturing patulak towards your colleague. It’s an action done by pushing, whether physically or metaphorically.
usage_notes: Can describe a physical motion or a figurative passing of responsibility.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isinara niya ang pinto nang **patulak** dahil sa galit.","translation":"He closed the door **in a pushing manner** out of anger."},{"sentence":"Ibinigay niya sa akin ang responsibilidad nang **patulak**.","translation":"She passed the responsibility to me **as if pushing it away**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pagsusugal kung saan ang mga manlalaro ay bumibili ng mga tiket na may numero, at ang mga nanalong numero ay binubunot upang magkamit ng premyo, kadalasan ay pera.
original_explanation: Ang pambansang 'sana all.' Dito umaasa ang marami para sa biglaang yaman. 'Yung tipong isang taya mo lang, baka makabili ka na ng sarili mong isla. Pero mas madalas, 'yung taya mo, pambayad lang sa taya ng iba. The ultimate 'bahala na si Batman' investment.
usage_notes: While understood, the term 'loto' is far more common in everyday speech in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nanalo raw sa **loteria** ang kapitbahay namin sa Amerika.","translation":"They say our neighbor in America won the **lottery**."},{"sentence":"Ang buwis mula sa **loteria** ay napupunta sa mga proyektong pangkawanggawa.","translation":"The tax from the **lottery** goes to charitable projects."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang panghalip na ginagamit sa pagtatanong upang tukuyin ang pagkakakilanlan ng isang tao.
original_explanation: The ultimate chismis starter pack. 'Sino kasama niya kagabi?' 'Sino 'yung bago mong ka-work?' It's the Filipino equivalent of sliding into the DMs, but for gathering intel. The first word you learn when you want to know everyone's business. Plural form 'sinu-sino' is for when the tea involves a whole group.
usage_notes: Can be combined with markers like 'si' (Sino si...?), 'ang' (Sino ang...?), or 'kay' (Para kanino?). 'Sinu-sino' is the plural form used when expecting multiple people in the answer.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sino** ang kumain ng huling piraso ng cake?","translation":"**Who** ate the last piece of cake?"},{"sentence":"Hindi ko alam kung **sino** ang dapat kong kausapin tungkol dito.","translation":"I don't know **who** I should talk to about this."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian, kakayahan, o posisyon ng pagiging isang lider; ang pamumuno.
original_explanation: This isn't the person, but the *quality* of being a leader. It's the "how" of leading. "May liderato ba siya?" means "Does he have what it takes to lead?" It's the abstract concept you talk about during elections, corporate trainings, or when you're complaining about your boss's lack of it.
usage_notes: Refers to the quality or act of leadership, distinct from 'lider' which is the person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinamalas niya ang kanyang galing sa **liderato** sa panahon ng krisis.","translation":"He demonstrated his skill in **leadership** during the crisis."},{"sentence":"Ang pagpili ng tamang **liderato** ay mahalaga para sa kinabukasan ng bansa.","translation":"Choosing the right **leadership** is important for the country's future."}]

meaning_filipino: Kasalukuyang nagpapakita ng pagpabor o pagkagusto sa isang bagay, lalo na sa social media, sa pamamagitan ng pagpindot sa 'like' button.
etymology: From English "like" + Tagalog prefix "nag-" and infix "-li-".
original_explanation: The present progressive tense of 'liking' something online. It's what you're doing while scrolling through your feed at 2 AM. 'Uy, naglilike siya sa mga old posts ko, may meaning ba 'to?' - a question that has launched a thousand 'what if' scenarios.
usage_notes: A modern, Taglish verb used primarily in the context of social media. The infix "-li-" marks the progressive aspect.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bakit ka **naglilike** ng mga post mula pa noong 2015?","translation":"Why are you **liking** posts from way back in 2015?"},{"sentence":"Nakita ko siyang **naglilike** ng mga comment na laban sa akin.","translation":"I saw him **liking** the comments against me."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng isang babae na may dinadalang sanggol sa kanyang sinapupunan.
etymology: From 'dala' (to carry) and 'tao' (person), literally "to carry a person".
original_explanation: This is the more formal and somewhat poetic way to say someone is pregnant. It literally means "to carry a person." It's what your lola would say instead of the more direct "buntis." It adds a certain gravitas and humanity to the state of being pregnant, reminding everyone that a whole new person is on the way.
usage_notes: A more formal or refined synonym for 'mabuntis'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ibinahagi ng mag-asawa ang masayang balita na **magdalang-tao** na si Ana.","translation":"The couple shared the happy news that Ana **is pregnant**."},{"sentence":"Mahirap ang **magdalang-tao** lalo na kung maselan ang iyong pagbubuntis.","translation":"It is difficult **to be pregnant**, especially if your pregnancy is delicate."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi nagbibigay ng sapat na pansin, pag-aalaga, o pag-aasikaso sa isang tao, bagay, o tungkulin.
original_explanation: Describes that one groupmate who only shows up on the day of the presentation to ask "Ano'ng part ko?" It's the vibe you get from a customer service rep who's clearly just waiting for their shift to end. Basically, their care level is at zero, and they've left you on "seen."
usage_notes: Nangangahulugan ng kakulangan sa pag-aalaga o responsibilidad sa isang bagay o tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naiinis ako sa mga serbisyong **walang-asikaso** sa kanilang mga customer.","translation":"I get annoyed with services that are **inattentive** to their customers."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa pagiging **walang-asikaso** ng drayber, nabangga ang sasakyan.","translation":"Because the driver was **neglectful**, the car crashed."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malaking isda sa dagat na kilala sa Ingles bilang yellowfin tuna (Thunnus albacares), na karaniwang ginagawang sashimi, sinigang, o iniihaw.
original_explanation: The VIP of the tuna world, often seen flexing its yellow fins. This is the fish that becomes your fancy sashimi or that delicious grilled panga. It's the cousin of the canned tuna, but way more sosyal.
usage_notes: Isang sikat na isda sa Pilipinas para sa iba't ibang lutuin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-uwi si Tatay ng sariwang **tambakol** mula sa palengke.","translation":"Father brought home fresh **yellowfin tuna** from the market."},{"sentence":"Masarap gawing sinigang ang ulo ng **tambakol**.","translation":"The head of the **yellowfin tuna** is delicious for sinigang."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pagiging nag-iisa; ginagawa o nangyayari nang walang kasama.
original_explanation: The official status of your friend who travels alone (solo traveler), eats alone (solo dining), or goes to the movies alone. It's not necessarily sad; it's a power move. 'Me time' in one word.
usage_notes: Can function as an adjective (e.g., 'solo flight') or an adverb (e.g., 'pumunta siyang solo').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-**solo** flight siya papuntang Japan.","translation":"He took a **solo** flight to Japan."},{"sentence":"Mas gusto niyang magtrabaho nang **solo**.","translation":"He prefers to work **solo** (alone)."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking pulutong o kumpol ng mga tao, hayop, o bagay na magkakasama.
original_explanation: Imagine mo yung Divisoria on a payday Friday before Christmas. 'Yan ang kalibumbon. Or yung mga langgam na biglang nag-party sa natapon mong softdrinks. It's a chaotic but united group, like a flash mob ng mga insekto or shoppers.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a dense, somewhat chaotic gathering of living things, like insects or people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **kalibumbon** ng mga bubuyog ang lumabas mula sa kanilang pugad.","translation":"A **swarm** of bees emerged from their hive."},{"sentence":"Nagkagulo ang mga tao sa **kalibumbon** sa palengke nang biglang umulan.","translation":"The people in the **crowd** at the market panicked when it suddenly rained."}]

translation: to be able to ride; to be able to get on (a vehicle)
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng pagkakataong sumakay o makapasok sa isang sasakyan.
original_explanation: Commuter life 101. 'Yung rush hour sa EDSA at siksikan sa MRT. Your victory is when you finally manage to squeeze yourself in. "Yes! Nakasakay din!" It's that small win of getting a ride, whether it's a jeep, bus, or tricycle, especially when you've been waiting for ages.
usage_notes: The "maka-" prefix highlights the ability or success in getting a ride, often against some difficulty (like a full vehicle or long queue).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **makakasakay** na rin ako pagkatapos ng isang oras na paghihintay sa terminal.","translation":"Finally, I'll be **able to get a ride** after waiting for an hour at the terminal."},{"sentence":"Ang daming tao, hindi ako sigurado kung **makakasakay** pa tayo sa huling biyahe ng bus.","translation":"There are so many people, I'm not sure if we'll still be **able to get on** the last bus trip."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabago ng direksyon sa paglalakad o pagpapatakbo ng sasakyan.
original_explanation: Your Grab driver's favorite (or least favorite) action. It's the 'kumanan dito, ser' moment. Also applies to your life choices when you suddenly decide to shift careers from accounting to becoming a TikTok dancer. You just 'lumiko'.
usage_notes: Actor-focus verb, completed aspect (past tense).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lumiko** pakanan ang sasakyan sa susunod na kanto.","translation":"The vehicle **turned** right at the next corner."},{"sentence":"Bakit ka biglang **lumiko** ng landas sa buhay?","translation":"Why did you suddenly **turn** to a different path in life?"}]

translation: to be the cause of surprise
meaning_filipino: Maging dahilan o sanhi ng pagkabigla o pagkagulat.
original_explanation: This is the 'tea' that makes you spit out your coffee. The reason why your jaw dropped when you saw your ex's wedding photos on Facebook. It's the 'why' behind the 'OMG'.
usage_notes: Used to specify the reason or cause for someone's surprise. Often appears in questions like "Ano ang ikinagulat mo?" (What was the cause of your surprise?).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ikinagulat** ng lahat ang biglaang pag-anunsyo ng pangulo.","translation":"The president's sudden announcement **was the cause of everyone's surprise**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ikagulat** kung manalo ako sa lotto.","translation":"Don't be surprised if I win the lottery. (Literally: Don't let my winning the lottery be the cause of your surprise.)"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga bagay, gawain, o tao na may kaugnayan sa isang misyon, partikular na sa gawaing panrelihiyon o pagkakawanggawa.
original_explanation: This describes anything related to being 'on a mission'. Usually, it has religious or NGO vibes, like a 'pangmisyon' trip to a remote community to give out relief goods. But in a modern sense, it can also describe your 'pangmisyon' OOTD when you're about to do something important, like presenting a major project to your boss. It's for when you're in 'get it done' mode.
usage_notes: Often associated with religious or charitable work.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumama siya sa isang biyaheng **pangmisyon** sa Africa.","translation":"He joined a **missionary** trip to Africa."},{"sentence":"Ang kanilang buhay ay inilaan sa gawaing **pangmisyon**.","translation":"Their lives were dedicated to **missionary** work."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang krimen ng sapilitang pakikipagtalik o anumang uri ng sekswal na pananalakay na isinagawa laban sa kalooban ng isang tao.
etymology: From `pag-` (prefix indicating action) + `gahasa` (to do with force, to rape).
original_explanation: This is a serious, non-joking term for a heinous crime. It refers to the act of forcing sexual intimacy upon someone against their will. It's a word used in news reports, legal cases, and serious discussions about violence and consent. There is no witty or lighthearted way to explain this; it is a grave violation of a person's body and rights.
usage_notes: This is a very serious and formal term. In conversation, people might use the verb form 'ginahasa' (was raped) or 'manggahasa' (to rape). 'Panggagahasa' is a common variant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paggahasa** ay isang karumal-dumal na krimen na walang puwang sa ating lipunan.","translation":"**Rape** is a heinous crime that has no place in our society."},{"sentence":"Nagsampa siya ng kaso ng **paggahasa** laban sa suspek.","translation":"She filed a case of **rape** against the suspect."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pagiging bukod-tangi ng isang tao o bagay; siya o iyon lamang at wala nang iba.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'sana all' phrase in love songs. 'Ikaw lang, sapat na.' When you say someone is 'walang-iba', it means they're 'The One'. It's that feeling when you find the perfect milk tea flavor and you know, deep in your soul, that there is **nothing else** for you.
usage_notes: Used to emphasize exclusivity. Often followed by 'kundi' or 'kung hindi' (except, if not).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para sa akin, **walang-iba** kundi ikaw.","translation":"For me, there is **no one else** but you."},{"sentence":"**Walang-iba** ang may kasalanan sa nangyari kundi siya.","translation":"**No one else** is to blame for what happened but him."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng kakulangan sa enerhiya, sigla, o sigasig; pananamlay o kawalan ng gana.
original_explanation: That feeling on a Monday morning when your body is at work but your soul is still in bed. Parang low-batt na phone, may power pa pero pang-text na lang, hindi na pang-ML. Ang official state of being pagkatapos ng isang long weekend.
usage_notes: Maaaring ilarawan ang pisikal na kalagayan ng isang tao, emosyonal na kalagayan, o maging ang kapaligiran ng isang lugar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dama ko ang **tamlay** ng katawan niya dahil sa sakit.","translation":"I could feel the **lethargy** in his body due to his illness."},{"sentence":"Nawala ang **tamlay** ng opisina nang dumating ang libreng pizza.","translation":"The **listlessness** of the office disappeared when the free pizza arrived."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggalaw nang pabalik-balik sa pagitan ng dalawang lugar o punto.
original_explanation: 'Yung lakad ng guard sa mall, or 'yung kaibigan mong 'di makapag-decide kung saan kakain. It's the physical manifestation of indecisiveness or a routine patrol. It's pacing. Like when you're waiting for an important text and you just keep walking from the sala to the kusina.
usage_notes: Describes movement between two points. Not to be confused with `paulit-ulit` which is about repeating an action or sound.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay **pauli-uli** sa paglalakad sa pasilyo habang naghihintay ng balita.","translation":"He was walking **back and forth** in the hallway while waiting for news."},{"sentence":"Bakit ka **pauli-uli** diyan? Mahihilo ako sa'yo.","translation":"Why are you pacing **back and forth** there? You're making me dizzy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salaysay ng mga pangyayari, totoo man o likhang-isip, na inilalahad sa paraang pasalita o pasulat.
original_explanation: The Pinoy's favorite pastime. Pwedeng chismis, pwedeng recap ng teleserye, pwedeng life story mo sa Grab driver. 'Ano'ng kwento?' is our version of 'What's up?' or 'What's the tea?'.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb 'magkwento' (to tell a story).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig si Lola magbasa ng mga **kwento** bago matulog.","translation":"Grandma loves to read **stories** before sleeping."},{"sentence":"May bago akong **kwento** sa iyo tungkol sa nangyari sa opisina.","translation":"I have a new **story** for you about what happened at the office."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang kilos ng pagtanggap, pagturing, o pagbigay-halaga sa isang tao, bagay, o konsepto.
etymology: From 'kilala' (known, acquainted). This is the present progressive form of 'kilalanin' (to recognize).
original_explanation: This is the present tense of "to recognize." It's what happens when your boss finally notices your hard work (and gives you a raise, sana all). It's also acknowledging someone's existence or authority, like when you nod at your building's security guard, or when a government kinikilala a new law. It's the opposite of being "seen-zoned."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kinikilala** na ngayon sa buong mundo ang galing ng mga atletang Pilipino.","translation":"The skill of Filipino athletes **is now being recognized** worldwide."},{"sentence":"**Kinikilala** ko ang iyong karapatan na magpahayag ng saloobin.","translation":"I **acknowledge** your right to express your feelings."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o resulta ng muling pagsasaayos ng isang sistema o estruktura.
original_explanation: The noun form of that scary corporate memo. When you hear 'magkakaroon ng **reorganisasyon**,' it's code for 'things are about to get shaken up.' It could mean new bosses, new teams, or a new seating plan. It's the corporate world's 'New Year, New Me' but for the org chart.
usage_notes: Formal noun, often paired with its verb form 'reorganisahin.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagdulot ng kaba sa mga empleyado ang balita tungkol sa **reorganisasyon**.","translation":"The news about the **reorganization** caused anxiety among the employees."},{"sentence":"Ang **reorganisasyon** ng gobyerno ay naglalayong pabilisin ang serbisyo publiko.","translation":"The **reorganization** of the government aims to speed up public service."}]

translation: to be coiled around; to be entangled by
meaning_filipino: Mapalibutan o makabitan ng isang bagay na pumupulupot, tulad ng baging o ahas.
original_explanation: Like when your earphones get impossibly tangled in your bag, or when you get stuck in a web of lies ('sana all may web'), or literally when a snake decides you'd make a great tree. It's being wrapped up, usually against your will.
usage_notes: The '-an' suffix indicates that the subject is the one being wrapped around.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-ingat ang lalaki na baka siya ay **mapuluputan** ng sawa sa gubat.","translation":"The man was careful not to **be coiled around** by a python in the forest."},{"sentence":"Ang poste ay halos **mapuluputan** na ng mga baging.","translation":"The post was almost completely **entangled** by vines."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapang pangkusina na ginagamit sa paggiling o pagdurog ng mga butil ng kape upang maging pulbos.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na "molinillo" na nangangahulugang maliit na gilingan.
original_explanation: Yung old-school na paraan para gawing powder yung coffee beans bago pa nauso yung mga automatic grinders sa Starbucks. Usually umiikot 'to na parang de-susi, at amoy na amoy mo yung fresh na kape habang ginagawa. Parang pag-ibig, kailangan ng effort para makuha yung pinakatamis na resulta.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ni Lola ang luma niyang **molinilyo ng kape** para ihanda ang aming almusal.","translation":"Lola used her old **coffee grinder** to prepare our breakfast."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagmamasid o pagbabantay sa isang bagay o tao para sa kapakanan ng iba.
original_explanation: This is what you ask your *chismosa* neighbor to do to your house while you're on vacation. "Pakitingnan mo naman kung may aakyat ng bakod, ha?" It's also what your paranoid mom asks your older sibling to do to you at a party: "Ipagbantay mo 'yang kapatid mo, baka kung ano'ng mangyari." It's entrusting the act of guarding to someone else.
usage_notes: The prefix 'ipag-' indicates that the action is done for someone's benefit or on their behalf.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ipagbantay** mo muna ang mga bata habang may kausap ako sa telepono.","translation":"Please **watch over** the kids for me while I'm on the phone."},{"sentence":"Maaari mo bang **ipagbantay** ang aking bag sandali?","translation":"Can you **watch** my bag for a moment for me?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit at mababang mesa o dulang na karaniwang ginagamit sa sahig para sa pagkain, lalo na sa mga kulturang Asyano.
original_explanation: The OG "floor gang" dining setup. Before aesthetic low tables from IKEA became a thing for condo living, Pinoys in the province were already mastering the art of eating on a `latok`. It's a communal, humble, and oddly comfortable way to eat, usually on a banig.
usage_notes: Nauugnay sa tradisyonal, probinsyal, o istilong Hapon na kainan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inihain ang pagkain sa **latok** habang kami ay nakaupo sa banig.","translation":"The food was served on a **low dining table** while we sat on a mat."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang hanapbuhay ay ang pagbili at pagbebenta ng mga produkto, sapi (stocks), o pananalapi (currencies) upang kumita.
original_explanation: The person in your barkada who suddenly talks about 'candlesticks', 'support levels', and 'going to the moon!' after watching a 5-minute crypto video on YouTube. They either treat you to dinner or ask you for 500 pesos, no in-between.
usage_notes: Isang direktang hiram na salita mula sa Ingles na ginagamit sa negosyo, pananalapi, at sa kaswal na usapan dahil sa kasikatan ng stock at crypto trading.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang batikang **trader** sa stock market ang aking tiyuhin.","translation":"My uncle is a veteran **trader** in the stock market."},{"sentence":"Maraming baguhang **trader** ang sumubok sa crypto.","translation":"Many new **traders** tried their hand at crypto."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na paltos o bula sa balat na naglalaman ng likido, kadalasang sanhi ng pagkagasgas, pagkapaso, o impeksyon.
original_explanation: What you get on your feet after walking around all day in new, unforgiving shoes. It's your skin's way of saying, 'I told you that was a bad idea.' That painful little bubble of 'I should've worn socks.'
usage_notes: Habang 'paltos' o 'lintos' ay mas karaniwan, ang 'ampolyas' ay naiintindihan din sa kontekstong ito, lalo na sa mga mas matatanda o sa mga lugar na may malakas na impluwensyang Espanyol.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ako ng **ampolyas** sa paa dahil sa bago kong sapatos.","translation":"I got a **blister** on my foot because of my new shoes."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong putukin ang **ampolyas** para maiwasan ang impeksyon.","translation":"Don't pop the **blister** to avoid infection."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng kalinga, pag-aalaga, at pagmamahal, lalo na sa mga bata, maysakit, o sinumang nangangailangan.
original_explanation: This is more than just 'to take care of.' It's the verb that defines Filipino family values. It's what a mother does for her child, what an 'panganay' does for their younger siblings, and what an OFW does for their family back home, but in a hands-on, nurturing way. It’s love in action, often involving feeding, comforting, and protecting.
usage_notes: Has a stronger emotional and nurturing connotation than 'mag-alaga'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tungkulin ng magulang na **mag-aruga** sa kanilang mga anak.","translation":"It is the duty of parents **to care for** their children."},{"sentence":"Siya ang nag-iisang **nag-aruga** sa kanyang lola na may sakit.","translation":"He was the only one who **nurtured** his sick grandmother."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na baryasyon ng salitang "erupsiyon," na tumutukoy sa biglaang pagbuga ng materyales mula sa isang bulkan.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "erupción", pinaikling baybay ng "erupsiyon".
original_explanation: The simplified, text-friendly version of 'erupsiyon.' It's the same volcanic explosion, just spelled with less effort. "Bes, may erupsyon daw sa balat mo." "Hindi, pimple lang 'to."
usage_notes: Mas karaniwan sa pang-araw-araw na usapan kaysa sa "erupsiyon".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakatakot ang balita tungkol sa **erupsyon** ng bulkan.","translation":"The news about the volcano's **eruption** is scary."},{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng skin **erupsyon** ang bata dahil sa allergy.","translation":"The child had a skin **eruption** due to an allergy."}]

translation: to contribute to a collection; to chip in
meaning_filipino: Ang sama-samang pagbibigay ng tulong pinansyal o materyal para sa isang partikular na layunin, karaniwan para sa isang nangangailangan o para sa isang proyektong pangkomunidad.
original_explanation: This is the bayanihan spirit in financial form. It's when a collection bag is passed around for a cause—be it for a sick neighbor, a community project, or during a church service. To **mag-abuluyan** is to chip in what you can. It's the grown-up version of "ambagan" for the group project merienda, but with more heart and less complaining.
usage_notes: Often implies a collective, voluntary contribution for a common cause, distinct from a simple donation ('donasyon') as it highlights the group effort.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang buong barangay na **mag-abuluyan** upang matulungan ang mga nasunugan.","translation":"The whole village decided to **contribute** to help the fire victims."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o bayad sa pagpapadala ng mga produkto o kalakal mula sa isang lugar patungo sa iba, lalo na sa konteksto ng e-commerce.
original_explanation: Ito yung dahilan kung bakit mas mahal ang binabayaran mo sa Shopee o Lazada kaysa sa nakalistang presyo. The 'shipping fee' is the silent killer of your 12.12 budget. Ito rin yung proseso ng pag-aabang sa delivery rider na parang nag-aabang ka sa pag-ibig—minsan mabilis, minsan paasa.
usage_notes: Often used as 'shipping fee'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Libre ang **shipping** kapag umabot ka sa ₱500.","translation":"**Shipping** is free when you reach ₱500."},{"sentence":"Magkano ang **shipping** papuntang Cebu?","translation":"How much is the **shipping** to Cebu?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasama o kabahagi sa isang salu-salo, pagdiriwang, o handaan.
etymology: A Tagalized blend of `ka-` (denoting a companion) and the English word 'party'.
original_explanation: Slang for your buddy at a party. Your 'ka-inuman', your 'ka-videoke', or the person you conspire with to attack the lechon first. Not to be confused with 'kaparte' (your share), though your 'kaparti' might try to get a 'kaparte' of your food.
usage_notes: This is an informal and conversational term, considered modern slang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang dami kong nakilalang **kaparti** kagabi sa birthday ni Ana.","translation":"I met a lot of **fellow party-goers** last night at Ana's birthday."},{"sentence":"Tara, yayain natin ang buong tropa para marami tayong **kaparti**.","translation":"Come on, let's invite the whole gang so we have lots of **party-mates**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang anyong tubig kung saan kusang bumubukal ang tubig mula sa ilalim ng lupa; pinagmumulan o bukal.
original_explanation: This is the Earth's natural water dispenser. It's where a river or stream starts, with fresh water bubbling up from the ground. Think of those hidden springs you find when hiking, where the water is so clean you're tempted to drink it (but maybe don't). It's the ultimate source, the 'pinanggagalingan' of clean water.
usage_notes: A more poetic or specific term for a spring than the common word 'bukal'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malinis ang tubig na nagmumula sa **sibulan** sa paanan ng bundok.","translation":"The water coming from the **spring** at the foot of the mountain is clean."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagiging yupi o pipi dahil sa pagkakadagan o pagkakaipit ng isang mabigat na bagay.
original_explanation: Imagine a cockroach meets your tsinelas. The aftermath? **Lapisak**. It's that feeling when you're in a full MRT train during rush hour—ikaw yung ipis, the crowd is the tsinelas.
usage_notes: Usually describes something that was once 3D but is now sadly 2D due to extreme pressure.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lapisak** ang kamatis na nadaganan ng mga pinamiling de lata.","translation":"The tomato that was crushed by the canned goods is **squashed**."},{"sentence":"Nakita siyang **lapisak** sa ilalim ng gulong ng trak.","translation":"He was found **flattened** under the truck's wheel."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na pagsubok sa kaalaman o kasanayan ng isang tao, karaniwan sa paraang pasulat o pasalita, lalo na sa paaralan.
original_explanation: The number one cause of stress, puyat, and excessive coffee consumption for students. It's that piece of paper that makes you question all your life choices. "Bes, may kodigo ka sa iksamen mamaya?"
usage_notes: Often spelled 'eksamen'. 'Pagsusulit' is the more formal, native equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong mag-aral para sa **iksamen** bukas.","translation":"I need to study for the **exam** tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Bumagsak siya sa huling **iksamen** sa Math.","translation":"She failed the last Math **test**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang daglat sa internet na nangangahulugang "Want to Sell" o "Nais Ibenta," na ginagamit sa mga online na platform upang ianunsyo ang isang aytem na ipinagbibili.
etymology: Daglat mula sa pariralang Ingles na "Want To Sell".
original_explanation: Ang acronym ng mga 'pre-loved' sellers at mga nagde-declutter. "WTS my old laptop, RFS: need funds for a new one." Ito ang signal na may bagong listing sa Carousell o sa FB Marketplace.
usage_notes: Madalas na sinusundan ng deskripsyon ng produkto, presyo, at "RFS" (Reason For Selling).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**WTS**: Almost new na sapatos, size 9, ginamit lang isang beses sa kasal. PM for price.","translation":"**Want to sell**: Almost new shoes, size 9, used only once at a wedding. PM for price."},{"sentence":"Nag-post siya sa group, \"**WTS** gaming account, max level na, quit na 'ko.\"","translation":"He posted in the group, \"**Want to sell** gaming account, already max level, I'm quitting.\""}]

translation: requiring a lot of care; high-maintenance
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao o bagay na nangangailangan ng masusing pag-aalaga at atensyon, kadalasan dahil sa pagiging sakitin o maselan.
original_explanation: Describes that friend who is always sick, or that plant you bought that dies if you look at it the wrong way. Also, your jowa when they have a slight cold and act like it's the end of the world. 'Ay, alagain pala 'tong Fiddle Leaf Fig na 'to.'
usage_notes: Can be used for people, pets, or even objects. Can sometimes have a slightly negative or burdensome connotation, implying weakness or being a hassle.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mula pagkabata ay sakitin at **alagain** na si Ana.","translation":"Since childhood, Ana has been sickly and **requires a lot of care**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang bumili ng ganyang lahi ng aso kung wala kang pasensya dahil **alagain** sila.","translation":"Don't buy that breed of dog if you don't have patience because they are **high-maintenance**."}]

translation: act of descending upon; act of bestowing (from above)
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbaba o pagdating mula sa isang mataas na lugar; o sa metaporikal na paraan, ang pagkakaloob ng isang bagay tulad ng hatol, biyaya, o inspirasyon mula sa isang nakatataas na pinagmulan.
original_explanation: This sounds like something straight out of a history book or the Bible, and it is. It's the act of something "coming down from on high." Think of the Holy Spirit descending, or a king issuing a decree from his throne. It's very dramatic, very top-down. If your boss emails a new company policy, that's just an announcement. If a divine entity gives you a sudden, brilliant idea for a startup, 'yan ang **pagpanaugan** ng inspirasyon.
usage_notes: This is a very formal, literary, and somewhat archaic word. It's rarely used in modern conversation. Primarily found in literature, religious texts, or historical accounts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagpanaugan** ng hatol ng korte ay hinihintay ng lahat.","translation":"Everyone is waiting for the **bestowing** of the court's verdict."},{"sentence":"Pinaniniwalaan nila ang **pagpanaugan** ng mga diyos sa kanilang sagradong bundok.","translation":"They believe in the **descending** of the gods upon their sacred mountain."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang Republika ng Pilipinas, isang kapuluang bansa sa Timog-silangang Asya.
etymology: Named `Las Islas Filipinas` in 1543 by Spanish explorer Ruy López de Villalobos, in honor of Philip II of Spain.
original_explanation: The land of 7,000+ islands, epic traffic, Jollibee on every corner, and the world's most hospitable people. It's where you'll find the most beautiful beaches and the most challenging government processes. We complain about it 24/7, but we'll fight anyone who says anything bad about it. The modern, official name is 'Filipinas'.
usage_notes: The official name of the country in Filipino. The English 'Philippines' is used in international contexts. The modern Filipino spelling is 'Filipinas', but 'Pilipinas' remains extremely common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahal ko ang aking bayang **Pilipinas**.","translation":"I love my country, the **Philippines**."},{"sentence":"Maraming magagandang tanawin sa buong **Pilipinas**.","translation":"There are many beautiful sights throughout the **Philippines**."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing pira-piraso o pulbos ang isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pagpiga, pagpukpok, o paggiling.
original_explanation: This is what you do to garlic with the side of a knife, to ice for your halo-halo, or to your enemies in Mobile Legends. Figuratively, it's also what happens to your heart when you see your crush with someone else. "Durugin mo 'yung OREO para sa graham cake." or "Dinurog mo ang puso ko!" The ultimate 'sira' mode.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for physical objects or figuratively for emotions, hopes, or opponents.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **durugin** nang pino ang mga mani para sa kare-kare.","translation":"The peanuts need to be **crushed** finely for the kare-kare."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **durugin** ng kabiguan ang iyong mga pangarap.","translation":"Don't let failure **shatter** your dreams."}]

translation: to take to heart; to take seriously
meaning_filipino: Isapuso o bigyan ng matinding pansin at damdamin ang isang bagay; seryosohin.
original_explanation: This is what you do with hugot lines, your crush's "seen" message, or your mom's passive-aggressive comments. You're not just listening; you're letting it marinate in your feels. "Huwag mo masyadong pakadibdibin" is the classic advice from friends when you're overthinking, but you do it anyway. It's internalizing to the max.
usage_notes: Often used in the negative form ("huwag pakadibdibin") as advice not to worry or overthink.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pakadibdibin** ang mga sinabi niya; biro lang iyon.","translation":"Don't **take to heart** what he said; it was just a joke."},{"sentence":"**Pinakadibdib** niya ang payo ng kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"She **took seriously** the advice of her parents."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pamantayang hanay ng mga titik o grapema na kumakatawan sa mga ponema o tunog ng isang wika.
original_explanation: This is your A-B-K-D-E... wait, that's the old 'abakada'. The modern Filipino 'alpabeto' has 28 letters, including the cool kids from the English alphabet like C, F, J, Ñ, Q, V, X, and Z. It's the building blocks of all the 'chismis' you read online and the 'hugot' lines you post.
usage_notes: Ang lumang alpabetong Tagalog ay tinatawag na 'Abakada'. Ang kasalukuyang opisyal na alpabeto ay ang 'Makabagong Alpabetong Filipino'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinuro sa amin ang bagong **alpabeto**ng Filipino sa paaralan.","translation":"We were taught the new Filipino **alphabet** in school."},{"sentence":"Ilang letra mayroon ang modernong **alpabeto**?","translation":"How many letters does the modern **alphabet** have?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit na paglikha ng tunog ng kalansing; ang ingay mula rito.
etymology: From 'kalansing' + '-an' suffix, indicating a place or a collective/repeated action.
original_explanation: This is 'kalansing' in overdrive. It's not just one clink, it's a whole symphony of it. Imagine the konduktor on a mission, shaking his coins non-stop. Or that one officemate who can't sit still and keeps playing with their keys. 'Pakiusap, itigil mo na ang kalansingan ng mga barya mo, hindi ako makapag-focus!'
usage_notes: Implies a continuous or repeated action, often more intense than a single 'kalansing'. Can also be a verb: 'nagkakalansingan' (are jingling).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakairita ang **kalansingan** ng kanyang mga alahas.","translation":"The continuous **jingling** of her jewelry is irritating."},{"sentence":"Mula sa kusina, narinig niya ang **kalansingan** ng mga kutsara't tinidor.","translation":"From the kitchen, she heard the **clatter** of spoons and forks."}]

translation: to give the silent treatment (to someone); to sulk about (something)
meaning_filipino: Ang pandiwa para sa pagpapakita ng tampo o sama ng loob sa isang tao o dahil sa isang bagay, karaniwang sa pagitan ng mga malapit sa isa't isa.
original_explanation: Ito yung ginagawa mo sa jowa mo pag 'di ka niya nireplyan agad. Hindi ka galit, pero hindi mo rin siya kinakausap. You're not breaking up, you're just... marinating in your feelings. It's the cold shoulder, Pinoy-style, usually solved with food or lambing.
usage_notes: A very culturally specific verb. 'Tampo' has no direct English equivalent. It's a non-confrontational way of expressing hurt feelings to a loved one.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo naman akong **pagtampuhan** dahil lang nakalimutan ko ang ating anibersaryo.","translation":"Please don't **give me the silent treatment** just because I forgot our anniversary."},{"sentence":"Ano ba ang **pinagtatampuhan** ninyong magkapatid?","translation":"What is it that you siblings are **sulking about** with each other?"}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng bahagyang kakulangan sa talino o pag-unawa; may katangahan.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung kaibigan mong nag-reply sa "Hi/Hello" ng scammer. Hindi naman siya bobo all the time, pero may moments of pure, unadulterated "shunga" moments. Parang 'yung nagtulak ng pinto na may "HILA" sign. 'Yung "pagka-" prefix ay parang slight disclaimer: "konti lang naman."
usage_notes: A slightly less harsh way of calling someone "tanga". The "pagka-" implies it's a trait or a temporary state, not their entire identity. Can be used self-deprecatingly.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Aminado siyang **may-pagkatanga** siya pagdating sa direksyon.","translation":"She admits she's a **bit foolish** when it comes to directions."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo siyang seryosohin, **may-pagkatanga** lang talaga 'yan minsan.","translation":"Don't take him seriously, he's just **a bit stupid** sometimes."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng matinding emosyonal o sikolohikal na reaksyon dahil sa isang bagay na nagpapaalala ng isang masamang karanasan o trauma. Sa modernong gamit, tumutukoy din ito sa pagiging labis na sensitibo o madaling magalit.
original_explanation: The official feeling of every netizen who sees a political post they don't agree with. Ito yung bigla kang nag-init ang ulo dahil may nag-sabi na "mas masarap ang Jollibee kaysa McDo" (o vice versa). Dati, for serious trauma lang 'to, ngayon, kahit sa maling spelling ng pangalan mo sa Starbucks cup, triggered ka na. It's the "na-offend ako" of the new generation.
usage_notes: Isang napakapopular na slang sa social media. May dalawang antas ng kahulugan: ang seryosong sikolohikal na termino, at ang pang-araw-araw na ekspresyon ng pagkainis o pagka-asar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo siyang biruin tungkol diyan, **triggered** siya sa ganyang topic.","translation":"Don't joke with him about that, he gets **triggered** by that topic."},{"sentence":"Uy, **triggered** ka na naman sa comment niya,\" biro ng kaibigan ko.","translation":"Hey, you're **triggered** by his comment again,\" my friend joked."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sistema ng pag-uuri o pagpapangkat ng mga bagay; ang resulta ng pagklasipika.
original_explanation: Ang 'klasipikasyon' ay 'yung listahan ng categories na nabuo mo. Sa call center, ito 'yung 'Case Type' na pipiliin mo. Sa palengke, 'yung paghiwalay ng isdang pang-prito, pang-sarsa, at pang-sinigang. It's the final system of organization, the finished categories.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin kasama ng "klasipikahin".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang tamang **klasipikasyon** ng mga halaman at hayop sa biyolohiya.","translation":"The correct **classification** of plants and animals is important in biology."}]

translation: to get in touch; to inform; to coordinate
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkilos ng pagbibigay o pagkuha ng impormasyon mula sa isang tao; ang pakikipag-ugnayan upang ipaalam ang isang bagay.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'makipag-' at salitang ugat na 'alam' (know). Ang unlaping 'makipag-' ay nagpapahiwatig ng isang kilos na panlipunan o may kasamang ibang tao.
original_explanation: This is the corporate way of saying 'mag-update ka naman' or 'let's sync.' 'Makipag-alam' is what your boss tells you to do with another department. It's about communicating, coordinating, and making sure everyone is on the same page. It’s more formal than just 'sabihan mo sila'.
usage_notes: Nagpapahiwatig ng isang pormal o opisyal na komunikasyon o koordinasyon sa pagitan ng mga partido.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **makipag-alam** sa HR department tungkol sa iyong leave.","translation":"You need **to get in touch** with the HR department about your leave."},{"sentence":"**Makipag-alam** ka sa akin kung may pagbabago sa plano.","translation":"**Inform me** if there are any changes to the plan."}]

translation: to massage; to act as a traditional healer/midwife
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa ng hilot, isang tradisyonal na paraan ng pagmamasahe upang lunasan ang pilay, o ang pagpapaanak sa isang buntis.
original_explanation: When your muscles are screaming "help me!" after a workout or a week of OT, you need someone to 'humilot'. It's not just any massage; it's the traditional Pinoy kind that feels like it's rearranging your soul (and your bones) back into place. Also, the OG term for what a traditional midwife does.
usage_notes: Can mean to perform the act of 'hilot' (massage) or to work as a 'hilot' (practitioner).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magaling **humilot** ang matanda sa kabilang baryo.","translation":"The old person in the next village is good at **giving traditional massages**."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **humilot** sa iyo noong ipinanganak ka?","translation":"Who **acted as the midwife** for you when you were born?"}]

meaning_filipino: Labis o sukdulan ang pagiging duguan o pagkakaroon ng dugo.
original_explanation: When the action movie is so intense it's not just 'madugo,' it's 'madugung-madugo.' Think less John Wick, more... well, more John Wick but with extra ketchup packets. It's the highest level of gore, the kind that makes you say 'OA na, direk!'
usage_notes: The `-ng` is a linker connecting the repeated adjective. Used for intense emphasis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napanood mo ba yung bagong pelikula? **Madugung-madugo** ang mga eksena!","translation":"Did you see the new movie? The scenes are **extremely gory**!"},{"sentence":"Ang eleksyon sa aming bayan ay naging **madugung-madugo** dahil sa matinding hidwaan.","translation":"The election in our town became **very bloody** due to intense conflict."}]

translation: to sermonize, to lecture, to preach
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng isang pangaral o mahabang payo, karaniwan sa paraang pormal, may awtoridad, o may pagkadismaya.
original_explanation: This is what your nanay does when you come home at 3 AM. It's not just a scolding; it's a full-blown TED talk on responsibility, life choices, and the price of rice. Often starts with 'Noong panahon namin...' and ends with you staring at the floor.
usage_notes: Can be used in a religious context (a priest giving a sermon) or a domestic one (a parent lecturing a child). The tone is often one of lengthiness and being told what to do.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang **magsermon**, Inay. Alam ko na po ang gagawin ko.","translation":"Please don't **lecture** me anymore, Mom. I already know what to do."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula nang **magsermon** ang pari tungkol sa pagkakaisa.","translation":"The priest began to **preach** about unity."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging tuyo, walang halumigmig, o kakulangan sa tubig.
etymology: From `ka-` + `tuyo` (dry) + `-an`, signifying the state or quality of 'dryness'.
original_explanation: That feeling when your throat is a desert after a long presentation, or when your skin feels like chicharon in the summer heat. It's also the vibe of a conversation that has died, or a bank account before payday. 'Grabe ang katuyuan ng lalamunan ko, pa-abot ng tubig.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa matagal na tag-init, ramdam ang **katuyuan** ng lupa.","translation":"Because of the long drought, the **dryness** of the land is felt."},{"sentence":"Hindi maganda sa balat ang labis na **katuyuan**.","translation":"Excessive **dryness** is not good for the skin."}]

translation: to close; to shut; to adjourn
meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na pagsasara ng isang bagay, tulad ng pinto, bintana, aklat, o isang pagpupulong o sesyon.
original_explanation: This is a more formal, almost dramatic way of saying "to close". It's not just closing the door; it's *sealing* it. It’s what the session head says in a conference: "The session is now adjourned." Or when you finally close the book on a toxic ex, you can say, "**Nagpinid** na ang kabanata namin." It has a sense of finality.
usage_notes: More formal and literary than the common "magsara". Often used for meetings, sessions, or in a figurative sense for closing a chapter in life.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang hukom ay **nagpinid** ng sesyon ng korte para sa araw na iyon.","translation":"The judge **adjourned** the court session for that day."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nang **magpinid** ng mga pinto bago dumilim.","translation":"The doors must be **closed** before it gets dark."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang labis na pagtingin sa sarili na may kasamang pagmamaliit sa iba; kayabangan o kahambugan.
etymology: From ka- + palalo + -an. 'Palalo' (arrogant) is derived from 'lalo' (more), implying a sense of being 'more' than others.
original_explanation: This is the evil twin of 'self-confidence.' It's not just being proud of your achievements; it's using them to make others feel small. Ito yung kontrabida sa teleserye who always says, 'Hindi mo alam kung sino ang kinakalaban mo!' It's the opposite of kapakumbabaan.
usage_notes: A formal and literary word for arrogance. 'Kayabangan' or 'pagiging mayabang' are more common in daily speech. It is one of the seven deadly sins (Pito na Nakamatay na Kasalanan).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **kapalaluan** ang naging sanhi ng kanyang pagbagsak.","translation":"His **arrogance** was the cause of his downfall."},{"sentence":"Ibagsak ang **kapalaluan** at matutong magpakumbaba.","translation":"Shed your **pride** and learn to be humble."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng domestikadong ibon (Gallus gallus domesticus) na inaalagaan para sa karne at mga itlog nito.
original_explanation: The Philippines' national MVP (Most Valuable Poultry). It's the star of Jollibee's Chickenjoy, your lola's tinola, and the roadside inasal stand. Also, a slang term for your bet in any competition, from sabong (cockfighting) to Miss Universe. 'Siya ang manok ko!'
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa buhay na hayop, sa karne nito, o sa kolokyal na termino para sa paboritong kandidato o pusta sa isang kompetisyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagluto si nanay ng adobong **manok** para sa pananghalian.","translation":"Mom cooked chicken adobo for lunch."},{"sentence":"Si Catriona Gray ang naging **manok** ng marami sa Miss Universe 2018.","translation":"Catriona Gray was the **bet** of many in Miss Universe 2018."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagkakaroon ng matibay na paniniwala at tiwala, lalo na sa isang bagay na hindi nakikita o sa isang kapangyarihang higit sa tao.
etymology: From the phrase 'sumasampalataya ako' (I believe). The root 'sampalataya' itself is a lexicalized phrase.
original_explanation: It's believing your Grab driver will find your obscure 'pin' location without calling you five times. On a serious note, it's the foundation of religion and belief systems. It's your trust in God, in the universe, or even just in yourself, that things will work out. It's the 'tiwala lang' philosophy, but make it formal.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in a spiritual or religious context. A deeper, more active form of 'paniniwala' (belief).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagsampalataya** sa Diyos ang nagbibigay sa kanya ng lakas.","translation":"The **act of having faith** in God is what gives him strength."},{"sentence":"Sinubok ang kanyang **pagsampalataya** nang magkasakit ang kanyang anak.","translation":"Her **faith** was tested when her child got sick."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglalagay sa isang saradong espasyo upang malimitahan ang paggalaw, mapausukan, o mapanatili ang isang partikular na kondisyon tulad ng temperatura.
etymology: From `pag-` + reduplication of the first syllable of `kulob`.
original_explanation: This is what happens when your mom tells you to stay in your room to "think about what you've done." It's also the secret to a perfect Lechon Manok - trapping all that heat and smoke to make the chicken juicy. In agriculture, it’s fumigating a space to get rid of pests. Basically, it's trapping something in a space for a specific purpose, whether it's for punishment, flavor, or pest control.
usage_notes: Can refer to heat, smoke, or simply being enclosed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkukulob** ng usok sa silid ay epektibo laban sa mga lamok.","translation":"The **fumigation** (enclosing of smoke) in the room is effective against mosquitoes."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang tamang **pagkukulob** sa pagpapapisa ng mga itlog ng manok.","translation":"Proper **incubation** is important for hatching chicken eggs."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang silid o gusali na nilagyan ng mga kagamitan para sa mga pang-agham na eksperimento, pananaliksik, o pagtuturo.
original_explanation: That place in school where you either felt like a genius mixing chemicals or prayed you didn't cause an explosion. It's the natural habitat of scientists, med-techs, and students dissecting frogs. Madalas din itong setting ng mga zombie apocalypse movie.
usage_notes: Ang karaniwang salitang Filipino para sa 'laboratory'. Madalas pinaikli bilang 'lab'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating gawin ang eksperimento sa **laboratoryo** ng kemistri.","translation":"We need to do the experiment in the chemistry **laboratory**."},{"sentence":"Bawal kumain sa loob ng **laboratoryo**.","translation":"Eating is not allowed inside the **laboratory**."}]

translation: someone who reads a message but doesn't reply
meaning_filipino: Isang katawagan sa isang tao na nakita o nabasa na ang isang mensahe sa social media o messaging app ngunit hindi tumugon o nagbigay ng sagot.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na "seen" + "-er". Isang neologism sa Filipino slang.
original_explanation: Eto yung kaibigan mong nag-iwan sa'yo ng "seen" sa 2:00 AM. Nag-type ka ng nobela, pinag-isipan mo bawat salita, tapos ang isinukli sa'yo ay ang resibo ng pagkabasa. Aray. Ang isang seener ay master ng passive-aggressive communication. Sila ang dahilan kung bakit may anxiety ka 'pag may lumabas na "Seen" sa chat.
usage_notes: Isang salitang balbal (slang) na nagmula sa tampok na "seen" o "read receipt" sa mga messaging app.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi ka niya gusto. **Seener** talaga 'yun sa lahat.","translation":"Don't worry, it's not that they don't like you. They're a **seener** to everyone."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sistema ng pagtatala, pagbubuod, at pagsusuri ng mga transaksyong pampinansyal; ang proseso ng pagkwenta o pagbilang.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'adulting' word. It's what your accountant does with your taxes, what you do with your budget before the 15th and 30th, and what your friend does when they split the bill down to the last centavo. 'Mag-tuusan tayo' is the polite way of saying 'Let's see who owes whom.'
usage_notes: Often used in the context of finance, business, or any situation requiring a final calculation or settlement.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating gawin ang **tuusan** ng mga gastos para sa proyektong ito.","translation":"We need to do the **accounting** of expenses for this project."},{"sentence":"Sa huli, magkakaroon din ng **tuusan** ng lahat ng ating mga ginawa.","translation":"In the end, there will also be a **reckoning** for all of our actions."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang panghalip na pananong na ginagamit upang magtanong tungkol sa bagay, pangyayari, o pagkakakilanlan.
original_explanation: The Swiss Army knife of Filipino questions. It means 'what?', but it can also mean 'huh?', 'what did you say?', 'what's that thing called again?', or the passive-aggressive 'so... what now?'. It's the start of every chismis ('Ano'ng nangyari?') and every confused moment ('Ano daw?').
usage_notes: One of the most fundamental words in Tagalog. Can be combined with markers like "ang" (ano'ng), "ito" (ano'ng 'to), etc. Its meaning can change dramatically based on intonation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ano** ang pangalan mo?","translation":"**What** is your name?"},{"sentence":"Hindi ko maintindihan, **ano** ba ang sinasabi mo?","translation":"I don't understand, **what** are you saying?"},{"sentence":"Na-traffic ako.","translation":"I got stuck in traffic."},{"sentence":"**Ano**!","translation":"**What**!"}]

translation: Invisibility; state of not being seen
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging hindi nakikita o natatanaw ng mata.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'ghosting' power. It’s the state of being invisible, whether literally (like an 'engkanto') or figuratively (like your salary on the 16th of the month). It's that feeling when you're in a group but no one acknowledges you, or when you're looking for your keys and they're right there, but their 'pagka-di-makita' is just too strong.
usage_notes: A compound noun phrase. The hyphenation is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ng espiya ang dilim para sa kanyang **pagka-di-makita**.","translation":"The spy used the darkness for his **invisibility**."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagka-di-makita** ng problema ay hindi nangangahulugang wala ito.","translation":"The **invisibility** of the problem does not mean it doesn't exist."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-alis o pagtanggal ng buhok o balbas sa katawan gamit ang isang matalas na kasangkapan tulad ng labaha.
original_explanation: The verb form of your dad's weekend ritual or what you do before a big date para 'fresh'. It's the action of getting rid of unwanted hair, whether it's on your face (balbas), legs (paa), or armpits (kilikili). Think of it as a manual 'delete' button for body hair.
usage_notes: The prefix 'mag-' indicates an action done by the subject. 'Inahitan' would be the object-focused form, meaning someone was shaved.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **mag-ahit** ng balbas bago pumasok sa trabaho.","translation":"I need to **shave** my beard before going to work."},{"sentence":"**Nag-ahit** siya ng kilay para sa bago niyang anyo.","translation":"She **shaved** her eyebrows for her new look."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang biglaan at marahas na pagkilos laban sa isang tao o lugar; isang biglaang pagsisimula ng isang sakit o karamdaman.
original_explanation: Can be a literal 'sugod!' moment, like in Mobile Legends. Or it can be what your tita experiences after eating too much lechon ("Inatake sa puso!"). It's a versatile word for any sudden, aggressive onset, from a verbal takedown to a medical emergency.
usage_notes: Used for both physical/military attacks and medical episodes (e.g., 'atake sa puso' - heart attack, 'atake sa utak' - stroke).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nailagan niya ang **atake** ng kalaban.","translation":"He dodged the enemy's **attack**."},{"sentence":"Isinugod siya sa ospital dahil sa **atake** sa puso.","translation":"He was rushed to the hospital due to a heart **attack**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagsubok sa lasa ng isang maliit na bahagi ng pagkain o inumin.
original_explanation: The national sport of the Philippines, especially in kitchens and fiestas. It's that 'free taste' you do before committing to a full plate. 'Patikim nga!' is the magic phrase that unlocks a spoonful of adobo, a sip of sinigang, or a piece of chicharon. It's a gesture of sharing, a quality control check, and sometimes, a full meal in itself if you're shameless enough.
usage_notes: The verb form is 'tikman' (to taste).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **tikim** pa lang, alam mo nang masarap ang luto niya.","translation":"With just one **taste**, you already know her cooking is delicious."},{"sentence":"Puro ka **tikim**, kailan ka ba kukuha ng buong plato?","translation":"You just keep getting **samples**, when are you going to get a full plate?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng puno (genus Cupressus) na karaniwang may hugis na balisungsong at nananatiling luntian sa buong taon.
original_explanation: The emo kid of trees. It's that tall, pointy, dark green tree you see in old paintings, cemeteries, or fancy subdivisions in Ayala Alabang. It has a very 'mahangin sa Baguio' vibe.
usage_notes: A direct loanword. Not a native tree, but the word is understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatayo ang matatayog na **sipres** sa gilid ng lumang simbahan.","translation":"Tall **cypress trees** stand beside the old church."},{"sentence":"Ang amoy ng **sipres** ay nakakarelaks.","translation":"The scent of **cypress** is relaxing."}]

translation: To fool; to dupe; to make a fool of
meaning_filipino: Ang sinasadyang panloloko o paglilinlang sa isang tao upang magmukha siyang hangal o para sa sariling kapakinabangan.
original_explanation: This is the next level of 'panloloko'. It's when someone intentionally tries to make you look like a total idiot. Think fake news forwards from your tita, or that 'friend' who tells you the party theme is formal when it's actually a pool party. It's not just teasing; it's designed to make you 'gago' or 'tanga'.
usage_notes: Stronger and more malicious than 'mang-ulok' or 'manloko'. 'Ulol' itself means 'crazy' or 'foolish'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Galit na galit siya dahil sinubukan siyang **mang-ulol** ng pekeng ahente.","translation":"He was furious because a fake agent tried to **dupe** him."},{"sentence":"Hindi mo ako kayang **mang-ulol**; alam ko ang mga karapatan ko.","translation":"You can't **make a fool of** me; I know my rights."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpasok at pagnguya ng pagkain sa bibig; ang pagkonsumo ng isang bagay.
etymology: From 'kain' (eat). Past tense, object focus form.
original_explanation: The most basic human function, but in Pinoy context, it's a love language. 'Kumain ka na ba?' is our 'I care about you.' 'Kinain' is the past tense. It's also used figuratively, like when 'kinain ka na ng sistema' (the system has consumed you) or when your pride gets eaten ('kinain ang pride').
usage_notes: A fundamental verb. Can be used literally for food or figuratively for being consumed by a system, emotion, or situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kinain** ko ang lahat ng sinigang.","translation":"I **ate** all of the sinigang."},{"sentence":"Parang **kinain** siya ng lupa at bigla na lang nawala.","translation":"It's like the earth **swallowed** him and he suddenly disappeared."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, **kinain** ko na ang pride ko at hihingi ako ng tawad.","translation":"Don't worry, I've **swallowed** my pride and I will ask for forgiveness."}]

translation: going home; the act of returning home
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbalik sa tahanan o sa lugar na pinanggalingan.
etymology: Nagmula sa Proto-Philippine *uliq* na nangangahulugang 'bumalik' o 'umuwi'.
original_explanation: The magic word every employee waits to hear at 5 PM. It's the opposite of 'OT pa more'. 'Tara, uwi na tayo!' is the sweetest sound after a long day of adulting. It can also be a noun, like 'Anong oras ang uwi mo?' (What time are you going home?).
usage_notes: Kadalasang ginagamit bilang salitang-ugat para sa mga pandiwang tulad ng 'umuwi' (to go home) o bilang utos na 'Uwi!' (Go home!).
