usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaga ang **uwi** ko ngayon dahil walang traffic.","translation":"My **return home** is early today because there's no traffic."},{"sentence":"Ang pasalubong ay bahagi ng kultura ng pag-**uwi** ng mga Pilipino.","translation":"Bringing home gifts is part of the Filipino culture of **going home**."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi kayang pasukin, tawirin, o daanan dahil sa pagiging makapal, matibay, o siksik.
original_explanation: Like the EDSA traffic on a Friday payday. It's a wall of cars. Di-malalagusan. Or the walls of Intramuros, built to be exactly that. Also describes your friend's logic when they're defending a toxic ex—no amount of reason can get through.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin para sa mga pisikal na harang tulad ng pader, gubat, o trapiko, ngunit maaari ring gamitin sa matalinhagang paraan para sa mga argumento o depensa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtayo sila ng pader na **di-malalagusan** ng sinuman.","translation":"They built a wall that is **impenetrable** by anyone."},{"sentence":"Ang makapal na gubat ay tila **di-malalagusan** kahit ng pinakamatapang na manlalakbay.","translation":"The thick forest seemed **impassable** even by the bravest explorer."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan naninirahan at gumagawa ng pulot-pukyutan ang mga pukyutan; bahay ng pukyutan.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'pa-' na tumutukoy sa lugar at ang lumang salitang 'nilan' na nangangahulugang pukyutan o pulot.
original_explanation: This is the condo building for bees. A panilan is a beehive, the place where all the magic (and honey) happens. Think of it as a super busy office with a queen bee as the CEO, and all the worker bees are hustling 24/7. It's the source of your honey, and also the source of "OMG, bees!" if you get too close.
usage_notes: Isang teknikal o pampanitikang termino. Ang mas karaniwang salita ay 'bahay ng pukyutan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May malaking **panilan** sa likod ng kanilang bahay kaya marami silang ani na pulot.","translation":"There is a large **beehive** behind their house so they have a large honey harvest."},{"sentence":"Ingat sa paglapit sa **panilan** dahil maaaring magalit ang mga pukyutan.","translation":"Be careful when approaching the **apiary** because the bees might get angry."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na pilapil o dike na gawa sa lupa, karaniwang ginagamit sa mga palayan o bukirin upang kontrolin ang daloy ng tubig.
etymology: Hindi tiyak ang pinagmulan, posibleng isang rehiyonal o teknikal na termino sa agrikultura.
original_explanation: Isipin mo yung pilapil sa gitna ng rice fields, pero a smaller version. Parang mini-hump lang siya na gawa sa lupa para hindi umapaw agad yung tubig sa isang plot. It's the low-budget, DIY flood control ng mga magsasaka.
usage_notes: Isang napaka-espesipikong termino sa agrikultura, hindi karaniwan sa pangkalahatang pag-uusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-ayos ng **moton** ang mga magsasaka upang hindi masira ng tubig ang kanilang tanim.","translation":"The farmers fixed the **small earthen dike** so that the water would not destroy their crops."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bukas na espasyo sa labas ng isang gusali, karaniwang sementado o naka-baldosa, at kadalasang tumutukoy sa malawak na bakuran sa harap ng simbahan.
original_explanation: The original hangout spot before malls. It's the open area in front of a church where you'd see kids playing, vendors selling dirty ice cream after mass, and where your lola would meet her 'amigas'. In modern houses, it's that fancy space for your outdoor furniture that you only use when guests come over.
usage_notes: Strongly associated with churches in the Philippines ('patyo ng simbahan'), but can also mean a residential patio or any open courtyard.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglaro ang mga bata sa **patyo** ng simbahan pagkatapos ng misa.","translation":"The children played in the church **courtyard** after the mass."},{"sentence":"Magkakape kami sa aming **patyo** mamayang hapon.","translation":"We will have coffee at our **patio** later this afternoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Pipilitin o uutusang ibalik ang isang bagay sa may-ari o sa dati nitong kinalalagyan.
original_explanation: This is the feeling when you borrow a friend's Netflix password and they change it. They're making you return to your non-Netflix-having state. More literally, if you borrow a book and forget, your friend might say, "**Papanauliin** ko sa'yo 'yun!" (I will make you return that!). It's a bit formal; "ipapasoli" is the everyday term.
usage_notes: A formal term for causing an object to be returned. The colloquial and more common equivalent is 'ipapasoli'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lahat ng aklat na hiniram sa aklatan ay **papanauliin** bago matapos ang semestre.","translation":"All books borrowed from the library **will be made to be returned** before the semester ends."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay, karaniwan ay damit, na maluwag, nakalaylay, o hindi ayos ang pagkakasabit.
original_explanation: Describes your favorite daster or 'pambahay' shorts that have lost all their shape and garter. It's the official uniform for 'tamad days' at home. Also, how you feel after a long day at work—just completely sagging. "Ang **lawlawin** na ng shorts mo, baka malaglag 'yan!"
usage_notes: Often used to describe old, worn-out clothes. Can also describe a person's posture or mood (droopy, listless).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Palitan mo na 'yang t-shirt mo, **lawlawin** na ang kuwelyo.","translation":"Change your t-shirt, the collar is already **droopy**."}]

translation: to crumple; to be crushed or wrinkled
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging lukot, gusot, o pagkasiksik dahil sa pagkakadiin o pagkakapisa.
original_explanation: Ito yung nangyayari sa puso mo 'pag na-seen ka lang. O sa resibo sa bulsa mo na kailangan mo pa pala. O sa mukha mo paggising mo sa umaga na nakasubsob ka sa unan. That state of being crumpled, literally and emotionally.
usage_notes: Can be used for physical objects or abstractly for feelings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumuyumos** ang papel sa kanyang kamao dahil sa galit.","translation":"The paper **crumpled** in his fist due to anger."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam ko ay **kumuyumos** ang puso ko nang iwan niya ako.","translation":"I felt like my heart was **crushed** when he left me."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sandata na may matulis na dulo, katawan, at mga balahibo sa kabilang dulo, na pinakakawalan mula sa isang pana.
original_explanation: Ito yung bala ni Kupido. One shot lang, tinamaan ka na, in love ka na. Sa modern times, ito yung text message ng crush mo na biglang nag-reply. Straight to the heart! Pwede ring bala ni Katniss Everdeen o ni Hawkeye.
usage_notes: Ginagamit nang literal para sa sandata at matalinghaga para sa isang bagay na mabilis at matalas tumama, tulad ng pag-ibig.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinudla ni Kupido ang kanyang puso ng isang **palaso**.","translation":"Cupid struck his heart with an **arrow**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga katutubo ay gumagamit ng pana at **palaso** sa pangangaso.","translation":"The indigenous people use a bow and **arrow** for hunting."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagsisiksikan o pagtutulakan sa isang masikip na lugar o sitwasyon upang makakuha ng espasyo o posisyon.
etymology: From pakiki- (reciprocal action) + pag- (action noun) + gitgit (to press against, to crowd).
original_explanation: That feeling sa MRT pag rush hour. Yung kailangan mong makipag-siksikan at makipag-balyahan para lang makapasok o makalabas. It's the physical version of competing for a limited-slot promo fare. Everyone's just trying to get ahead, literally.
usage_notes: Often used to describe crowded public transport, busy markets, or any situation involving a physical struggle for space.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi maiiwasan ang **pakikipaggitgitan** sa Divisoria kapag malapit na ang Pasko.","translation":"You can't avoid the **jostling** in Divisoria when Christmas is near."},{"sentence":"Pagod na ako sa araw-araw na **pakikipaggitgitan** sa pila ng bus.","translation":"I'm tired of the daily **crowding** in the bus queue."}]

meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng direksyon o patnubay ang isang tao, bagay, o gawain.
original_explanation: This is what you do when your friend is driving for the first time, and you're the designated "Waze" in the passenger seat. "Dito, dito! Sa kaliwa! Ay, lagpas!" You're not the driver, but you're giving the directions. It's also what your TL (Team Leader) does during your first few calls sa BPO.
usage_notes: Often used in the imperative form "giyahan mo" (guide him/her/it). The root word 'giya' can also mean the gear stick of a car.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Giyahan** mo ang iyong nakababatang kapatid sa paggawa ng kanyang takdang-aralin.","translation":"**Guide** your younger sibling in doing their homework."},{"sentence":"Sana ay **giyahan** tayo ng Panginoon sa ating mga desisyon.","translation":"May the Lord **guide** us in our decisions."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o kalagayan ng pagkakaroon ng kamalayan, kaalaman, o pag-unawa sa isang bagay na dati ay hindi alam o napapansin.
etymology: From 'pa-' (instrumental prefix) + 'mulat' (to open eyes, to be aware). Literally, 'the means or place of becoming aware.'
original_explanation: That 'Aha!' moment. 'Yung bigla mong naintindihan kung bakit ka single, kung bakit laging traffic sa EDSA, o kung bakit 'di ka pa rin promoted. It's your personal enlightenment, your 'woke' era kicking in.
usage_notes: Often used in a philosophical, political, or spiritual context to denote a significant shift in consciousness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang edukasyon ang nagsilbing **pamulatan** ng kanyang kaisipan tungkol sa mga isyung panlipunan.","translation":"Education served as the **awakening** of his mind regarding social issues."},{"sentence":"Naganap ang kanyang espirituwal na **pamulatan** matapos ang mahabang pagninilay-nilay.","translation":"His spiritual **enlightenment** occurred after a long period of reflection."}]

translation: to be amazed, to be astounded
meaning_filipino: Ang makaranas ng matinding pagkamangha o pagtataka sa isang bagay na hindi pangkaraniwan.
original_explanation: This is your reaction when your friend who's always late actually arrives on time. Or when your data allowance lasts until the end of the month. It's the 'shookt' of our grandparents. A level of surprise that makes you go, "Weh, 'di nga?"
usage_notes: A more formal or literary word for being surprised.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Talagang ikaw ay **manggilalas** sa ganda ng tanawin sa Batanes.","translation":"You will truly **be amazed** by the beauty of the scenery in Batanes."},{"sentence":"**Nanggilalas** ang lahat sa ipinakita niyang talento.","translation":"Everyone **was astounded** by the talent he showed."}]

translation: last; tail-end; bringing up the rear
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa nasa huli sa isang hilera, pila, o listahan; nasa pinakadulong posisyon.
original_explanation: This is the person who's always last in line, the caboose of the friend group, the student who submits their project right at the deadline. Also, the car that gets stuck at the tail-end of EDSA traffic. If there's a 'kulelat,' this is it.
usage_notes: Can function as an adjective ('pambuntot na kotse' - the last car) or a noun to refer to the one in the last position ('Siya ang pambuntot' - He is the last one).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagi na lang ako ang **pambuntot** sa pila.","translation":"I'm always the **one at the end** of the line."},{"sentence":"Ang **pambuntot** na kalahok ay nakahabol pa rin.","translation":"The **last** participant was still able to catch up."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pag-aalis ng balat sa dulo ng ari ng lalaki, na isang kaugalian o ritwal sa maraming kultura.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `pag-` at sa salitang ugat na `tuli` (walang balat sa dulo ng ari).
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino summer rite of passage for boys. It's that one vacation where you "graduate" to being a "binata." Usually involves a trip to the local health center (or sometimes, a traditional "pukpok" method, yikes!), a week of wearing a skirt-like garment or loose shorts, and lots of teasing from your friends and family. A core memory, for better or for worse.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isinasagawa ang libreng **pagtuli** sa aming barangay tuwing bakasyon.","translation":"Free **circumcision** is performed in our village every vacation."}]

translation: to dig up, to rummage through
meaning_filipino: Ang paghahanap ng isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng paghuhukay o pagkakalkal sa isang tumpok ng mga gamit, lupa, o alaala.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you can't find your keys and you turn your bag upside down. Or when your nanay is looking for that one specific resibo from 2018. It's a desperate, chaotic search. It's also what your 'marites' friend does to find old, incriminating social media posts. 'Halukayin mo 'yung baul, baka nandoon 'yung lumang photo album.'
usage_notes: Implies a more forceful or less organized search than 'hanapin' (to look for). Often used metaphorically for digging up the past.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **halukayin** ang lumang aparador para mahanap ang mga dokumento.","translation":"We need to **rummage through** the old cabinet to find the documents."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang **halukayin** pa ang nakaraan.","translation":"Don't **dig up** the past anymore."}]

translation: toward, to, in the direction of
meaning_filipino: Isang salitang nagpapahiwatig ng direksyon o patutunguhan ng isang kilos, paggalaw, o layunin.
original_explanation: This is Waze or Google Maps in one word. "Saan ang tungo mo?" is the classic "Where are you headed?" It's about direction, purpose, and destination. Whether you're going to the office or 'tungo sa pag-move on', this word points the way.
usage_notes: Often interchangeable with 'papunta'. Requires a 'sa' phrase to indicate the destination (e.g., 'tungo sa simbahan').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglalakad sila **tungo** sa plasa.","translation":"They are walking **toward** the plaza."},{"sentence":"Ito ang unang hakbang **tungo** sa tagumpay.","translation":"This is the first step **to** success."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kalagayan ng pagiging lubos na pagod, nanghihina, at halos hindi na makagalaw dahil sa matinding gawain o sakit.
original_explanation: This is the feeling after a 12-hour shift, followed by 3 hours of traffic. It's being so tired you just collapse on the bed, still in your work clothes, and can't even reach for the remote. It's 'pagod' level 99. The physical state of 'ayoko na, suko na ako.'
usage_notes: Describes a state of extreme physical exhaustion, often to the point of being unable to move.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natagpuan siyang **gulapay** sa sahig dahil sa mataas na lagnat.","translation":"He was found **exhausted** on the floor due to a high fever."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng marathon, **gulapay** ang lahat ng mga mananakbo.","translation":"After the marathon, all the runners were completely **worn out**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkain sa umaga; ang gawain ng pag-aalmusal.
etymology: From `ma-` + `pamahaw` (breakfast). The word `pamahaw` is more common in Visayan languages but is understood and used in Tagalog, especially in southern regions.
original_explanation: Literally, 'to breakfast.' This is the act of eating your sinangag, itlog, and longganisa (or pandesal with kape). It's the most important meal of the day, fueling you for your commute or morning meeting. 'Tara, **mamahaw** muna tayo bago pumasok sa trabaho.'
usage_notes: 'Mag-almusal' is the more common Tagalog equivalent. 'Mamahaw' is often heard in Southern Tagalog regions or from speakers with Visayan influence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gisingin mo ako nang maaga para makapag-ayos at **mamahaw** bago umalis.","translation":"Wake me up early so I can get ready and **eat breakfast** before leaving."},{"sentence":"Hindi ako sanay na hindi **mamahaw** sa umaga.","translation":"I'm not used to not **eating breakfast** in the morning."}]

translation: to treat, to heal, to practice medicine
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalapat ng lunas o kasanayang medikal upang pagalingin ang sakit o karamdaman ng isang tao o hayop.
original_explanation: The act of playing doctor, whether you're a licensed M.D. or just your family's designated 'taga-abot ng Bioflu'. It's the core action of doctors, nurses, and even albularyos. When your friend is heartbroken, you also 'manggamot' their feelings with comforting words and a bucket of ice cream.
usage_notes: Can refer to formal medical practice or traditional/folk healing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pangarap niya ay maging doktor upang **manggamot** sa kanilang probinsya.","translation":"Her dream is to become a doctor to **treat** people in her province."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **manggamot** ng sarili gamit ang mga halamang-gamot.","translation":"He tried **to heal** himself using medicinal plants."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hindi inaasahang biyaya, tulong, o magandang pangyayari na dumating sa tamang-tamang pagkakataon.
original_explanation: That unexpected 13th-month pay when you're down to your last 100 pesos. The Grab driver who doesn't cancel. The friend who treats you to milk tea. It's any unexpected good thing that feels like a gift from the universe, saving you from your 'kamalasan'.
usage_notes: An idiomatic expression for a timely blessing or a person who brings great fortune or help.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para sa akin, ikaw ay isang **hulog ng langit**.","translation":"For me, you are **heaven-sent**."},{"sentence":"Ang tulong na dumating ay parang **hulog ng langit** sa mga nasalanta ng bagyo.","translation":"The aid that arrived was like a **blessing from heaven** for the typhoon victims."}]

translation: state of being overturned; state of being face down
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging nakabaligtad o nakasubsob.
original_explanation: This is that "I give up" pose when life gives you too many lemons. Imagine your bangka flipping over during a storm, or you, face-down on your bed after a brutal work week. That's the energy of pagkataob. Total surrender, but not always in a bad way. Sometimes, it's just accepting you need a nap.
usage_notes: Can refer to literal overturning (like a boat or a cup) or a figurative defeat or overwhelming situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang biglaang **pagkataob** ng bangka ay ikinagulat ng lahat.","translation":"The sudden **overturning** of the boat surprised everyone."},{"sentence":"Ramdam niya ang **pagkataob** ng kanyang diwa matapos mabalitaan ang masamang nangyari.","translation":"He felt the **overwhelming defeat** of his spirit after hearing the bad news."}]

meaning_filipino: Isasagawa ang paghahanda ng pagkain sa pamamagitan ng init. Ito ay nasa panahunang panghinaharap.
original_explanation: The classic Filipino response to "Anong ulam?" (What's for dinner?). It's a statement of future action that holds the promise of adobo, sinigang, or maybe just fried hotdogs. "Huwag ka nang bumili ng pagkain sa labas, magluluto ako ng paborito mo."
usage_notes: Future tense of 'magluto'. One of the most common verbs used in a Filipino household.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **magluluto** para sa Pasko?","translation":"Who **will cook** for Christmas?"},{"sentence":"Mamayang gabi, **magluluto** ako ng sinigang na baboy.","translation":"Tonight, I **will cook** pork sinigang."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang palagay o hinala na may nagawang mali o kasalanan ang isang tao, o mayroong isang bagay na hindi tama, kahit walang tiyak na katibayan.
original_explanation: That feeling you get when your partner suddenly becomes extra sweet after a night out with friends. Or when the "ulam" is suspiciously delicious and you wonder what your mom wants you to do. It’s your inner Marites tingling, sensing that something is up.
usage_notes: Often used with "may" (e.g., "may suspetsa ako") or as the root for verbs like "magsuspetsa" or "paghinalaan".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **suspetsa** ang mga pulis kung sino ang nasa likod ng krimen.","translation":"The police have a **suspicion** about who is behind the crime."},{"sentence":"Nawala ang tiwala niya dahil sa laging may **suspetsa** sa bawat kilos ko.","translation":"He lost his trust because he always had **suspicion** about my every move."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malubhang impeksyon na sanhi ng bakteryang Clostridium tetani, na karaniwang pumapasok sa katawan sa pamamagitan ng sugat at nagdudulot ng paninigas ng mga kalamnan, lalo na sa panga.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na 'tetanus', na galing sa Latin na 'tetanus', mula sa Griyegong 'tetanos'.
original_explanation: The reason your mom freaks out when you step on a rusty nail ('kalawang na pako'). It's that scary infection that can give you lockjaw, which is not a cool wrestling move but a serious medical condition. This is why you get your anti-tetanus shot, so you can continue your 'kalye' adventures without worry.
usage_notes: Isang terminong medikal na ginagamit sa buong mundo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala siya sa ospital para sa anti-**tetanus** shot matapos matapakan ang isang pako.","translation":"He was brought to the hospital for an anti-**tetanus** shot after stepping on a nail."},{"sentence":"Ang bakuna laban sa **tetanus** ay mahalaga para maiwasan ang malubhang komplikasyon.","translation":"The vaccine against **tetanus** is important to prevent serious complications."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkilos ng pag-imbita o pag-aanyaya sa isang tao na dumalo, sumama, o makibahagi sa isang okasyon, gawain, o lugar.
original_explanation: This is what your tita does for every birthday, binyag, and Pasko. To mag-anyaya is to formally (or informally via chat) ask someone to come over. "Halika, kain tayo!" is the most basic form of Pinoy invitation. It's the prelude to every good handaan.
usage_notes: Can be used for formal or informal invitations. Synonymous with `mag-imbita`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino-sino ang plano mong **mag-anyaya** sa iyong kaarawan?","translation":"Who are you planning **to invite** to your birthday?"},{"sentence":"Nag-**anyaya** si Mayor para sa isang pagtitipon sa plasa.","translation":"The Mayor **invited** everyone to a gathering at the plaza."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na nangyayari o ginagawa nang mabilis at walang paghahanda; biglaan.
original_explanation: Ito yung adjective version. Parang instant noodles, pero para sa mga pangyayari. Isang **daglian** na desisyon? Yung bigla ka na lang nag-book ng flight pa-beach. Isang **daglian** na meeting? Yung biglang tawag ng boss mo, "Zoom tayo, now na!".
usage_notes: Adjective form of 'dagli'. Describes a noun as being instant or sudden.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **daglian** na pag-alis ay ikinagulat ng lahat.","translation":"His **sudden** departure surprised everyone."},{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng **daglian** na solusyon sa problemang ito.","translation":"We need an **immediate** solution to this problem."}]

translation: to let go of; to release
meaning_filipino: Pakawalan ang isang bagay na hawak, pinanghahawakan, o pinipigilan.
original_explanation: The slightly more dramatic, more 'malamig-ang-boses' cousin of 'bitawan'. If 'bitawan' is a friend's casual advice, 'bitiwan' is the line in a teleserye where the protagonist finally decides to move on, often with tears and rain. 'Panahon na para **bitiwan** ang nakaraan.' Same meaning, different emotional weight.
usage_notes: A common variant of 'bitawan', often perceived as slightly more formal or emphatic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **bitiwan** ang mga alaala, ngunit kailangan para makapagpatuloy.","translation":"It's hard **to let go of** the memories, but it's necessary in order to move on."},{"sentence":"Pinakiusapan niya itong **bitiwan** ang baril.","translation":"He pleaded with him **to let go of** the gun."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong bago o walang karanasan sa isang partikular na gawain, lalo na sa mga online game o komunidad.
original_explanation: Ito yung tawag sa'yo sa DOTA o Mobile Legends kapag bago ka pa lang at laging namamatay. Basically, you're the team's liability. "Weak," ika nga. Pero lahat naman tayo nag-umpisa bilang noob, 'di ba?
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng online gaming, teknolohiya, o anumang hobby kung saan may mga antas ng kasanayan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala kung magkamali ka, lahat naman tayo ay naging **noob** noong una.","translation":"Don't worry if you make a mistake, we were all a **noob** at first."},{"sentence":"Tinuruan ng beteranong manlalaro ang mga **noob** sa team.","translation":"The veteran player taught the **newbies** on the team."}]

translation: to do somersaults; to tumble head over heels
meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng kilos kung saan ang katawan ay umiikot nang pasulong o paurong, na ang mga paa ay dumadaan sa ibabaw ng ulo.
original_explanation: This is the more acrobatic cousin of `magpabali-baligtad`. It's not just rolling, it's a full-on somersault or cartwheel. Ito yung ginagawa ng mga gymnast, o nung pinsan mong hyperactive sa family reunion na gustong mag-show off. It's the act of causing oneself to tumble head over heels, usually with some flair.
usage_notes: Specific to acrobatic or playful tumbling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig **magpabali-balintong** ang mga bata sa damuhan.","translation":"The kids love **to do somersaults** on the grass."},{"sentence":"Nais niyang matutong **magpabali-balintong** tulad ng isang gymnast.","translation":"He wants to learn **to do somersaults** like a gymnast."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o daungan kung saan maaaring sumilong, mag-angkla, o humimpil ang mga barko at iba pang sasakyang-pandagat upang maging ligtas mula sa masamang panahon.
etymology: A phrase. `Panganlungan` is from `pang-` + `lungan` (refuge, shade). `Bapor` is from Spanish `vapor` (steamship).
original_explanation: Basically, a parking lot for boats. It's a safe space where ships can chill, protected from storms and big waves. It's the "refuge" or "safe harbor" in a very literal sense. Think of it as the ships' 'tambayan' where they can rest before their next long journey.
usage_notes: A descriptive and somewhat formal phrase. "Daungan" or "pier" are more common in everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Subic Bay ay isang tanyag na **panganlungan ng mga bapor**.","translation":"Subic Bay is a famous **harbor for ships**."},{"sentence":"Naghahanap ang kapitan ng isang ligtas na **panganlungan ng mga bapor** bago dumating ang bagyo.","translation":"The captain was looking for a safe **port for ships** before the typhoon arrived."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-alis ng lukot sa damit o tela gamit ang isang plantsa.
original_explanation: The act of making your gusot-mayaman na damit look presentable. It's a chore that requires patience, a good playlist, and the skill to not burn the collar of your favorite polo. Ito rin ang ginagawa mo sa mga problema minsan, 'pinaplantsa' o inaayos ang gusot.
usage_notes: Ito ang pandiwang nakapokus sa layon. Ang "magplantsa" ay nakapokus sa tagaganap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **plantsahin** ang aking uniporme para bukas.","translation":"I need **to iron** my uniform for tomorrow."},{"sentence":"**Plantsahin** mo nang maayos ang mga damit para hindi mukhang lukot.","translation":"**Iron** the clothes properly so they don't look wrinkled."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng kasama o ang pagsabay sa isang tao o grupo sa isang gawain o lugar.
original_explanation: This is your +1. The person you bring to a party, the friend you go to the movies with. 'Sino'ng makakasama mo?' is the classic question from your parents before letting you go out. This is the 'good' version of the word, all about companionship.
usage_notes: This form, with the stress on the third syllable (SA-ma), specifically means 'to accompany' or 'to be with'. It is distinct from the other 'makasama' which means 'to do harm'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kitang **makasama** sa paglalakbay ko.","translation":"I want you **to be with** me on my journey."},{"sentence":"Sana'y **makasama** ko ang buong pamilya sa Pasko.","translation":"I hope I can **be with** my whole family for Christmas."}]

translation: to award; to grant; to bestow
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng isang parangal, premyo, o karapatan sa isang tao o grupo bilang pagkilala sa kanilang nagawa.
original_explanation: This is what happens at graduation ceremonies or awards nights. The school will **maggawad** ng diploma to the students. A company will **maggawad** ng 'Employee of the Year' award. It’s a very formal way of saying 'to give an award.' You don't 'maggawad' a piece of candy; you 'maggawad' a medal of honor.
usage_notes: A formal term used in the context of ceremonies, official recognitions, and bestowing honors.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pangulo ay **maggagawad** ng parangal sa mga natatanging atleta.","translation":"The president will **bestow** an honor upon the outstanding athletes."}]

meaning_filipino: Alisin sa isipan, serbisyo, o tungkulin; ipawalang-bisa o ituring na hindi mahalaga.
original_explanation: What you do to your alarm clock on a weekend. What a judge does to a weak case. What you should do to your ex's 'kumusta ka?' message at 2 AM. It's the ultimate 'You are cancelledt' move.
usage_notes: A verb in the object-focus form (-in). Used in legal, professional, and casual contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang korte na **dismisin** ang kaso dahil sa kakulangan ng ebidensya.","translation":"The court decided **to dismiss** the case due to lack of evidence."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo basta-basta **dismisin** ang kanyang mga mungkahi.","translation":"Don't just **dismiss** his suggestions."}]

meaning_filipino: Bigkasin ang isang tula o piyesa nang may angkop na damdamin, kilos, at diin, karaniwan sa harap ng mga manonood.
original_explanation: Throwback to your Buwan ng Wika days in elementary school. This is what you did with "Ang Puso ng Saging" or "Ako'y Isang Pinoy" while wearing a baro't saya, complete with dramatic hand gestures. It's not just reading—it's performing with ~*feelings*~.
usage_notes: Used for formal, often dramatic, recitation of literary pieces. The focus is on performance and emotion, not just speaking the words.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahusay niyang **idineklama** ang tulang isinulat ni Jose Rizal.","translation":"She skillfully **declaimed** the poem written by Jose Rizal."},{"sentence":"Ang nanalo sa patimpalak ay ang batang buong pusong **nagdeklama** ng piyesa.","translation":"The winner of the contest was the child who **recited** the piece with full heart."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na may labis na pag-iingat sa detalye, partikular sa kilos, pananamit, o kagustuhan; pihikan o maselan.
original_explanation: The OG 'main character syndrome.' Yung kaibigan mong ayaw kumain sa karinderya kasi 'it's not aesthetic.' Can also mean someone who is overly dramatic about small things. The line between being classy and being maarte is thinner than your patience during rush hour traffic.
usage_notes: Often has a negative connotation, implying someone is difficult to please or overly dramatic. However, it can sometimes be used playfully.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang **maarte**, kanin mo na lang 'yang gulay.","translation":"Stop being so **picky**, just eat the vegetables."},{"sentence":"Gusto niya laging branded ang damit, medyo **maarte** talaga siya.","translation":"She always wants branded clothes, she's really quite **high-maintenance**."}]

translation: to ration; to give a share/ration
meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng takdang bahagi o rasyon ang isang tao o grupo, lalo na sa panahon ng kakulangan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang "rasyon" (ration), na galing sa Espanyol na "ración".
original_explanation: Ito yung ginagawa ng nanay mo sa ulam para umabot hanggang sa susunod na sahod. O kaya yung ginagawa ng gobyerno sa ayuda, kailangan mong hintayin ang turn mo bago ka rasyunan. It's the art of making things last, whether it's food, budget, or pasensya.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng pagbabahagi ng pagkain, tulong, o suplay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **rasyunan** ang natitirang tubig dahil hindi natin alam kung kailan darating ang tulong.","translation":"We need **to ration** the remaining water because we don't know when help will arrive."},{"sentence":"**Rasyunan** mo na ang mga bata ng kanilang meryenda.","translation":"**Give** the children their snack **rations**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang de-kuryente na may kulay na mga ilaw (pula, dilaw, berde) na ginagamit upang kontrolin ang daloy ng trapiko sa mga kalsada.
etymology: A compound word from Tagalog 'ilaw' (light) and Spanish 'tráfico' (traffic).
original_explanation: The ultimate "Wait ka lang" and "Go na!" sign sa EDSA. Red means 'stop', green means 'go', and yellow means 'go faster' para sa mga Pinoy driver. Ito rin yung nagiging dahilan ng "close ba tayo?" moment niyo ng katabing driver.
usage_notes: More commonly called 'traffic light' even in Tagalog conversations. 'Stoplight' is also a common term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumigil ang mga sasakyan nang mag-pula ang **ilaw-trapiko**.","translation":"The cars stopped when the **traffic light** turned red."},{"sentence":"Laging may nagtitinda ng sampaguita malapit sa **ilaw-trapiko** na iyon.","translation":"There are always sampaguita vendors near that **traffic light**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pagkakaroon ng pagkakatulad o pagiging kawangis ng isang bagay, tao, o pangyayari sa iba.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'same vibes.' Before we had 'relate,' we had 'Gaya mo ako!' (You're just like me!). It's the word you use when you see someone wearing the same Uniqlo shirt as you, or when your friend's love life is as much of a mess as yours.
usage_notes: Often used with 'ng' or 'ni' to introduce the object of comparison (e.g., gaya ng, gaya ni). Can also function as an adverb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang boses niya ay **gaya** ng sa isang anghel.","translation":"Her voice is **like** that of an angel."},{"sentence":"**Gaya** ng inaasahan, nahuli na naman siya sa klase.","translation":"**As** expected, he was late for class again."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagkuha ng pagmamay-ari sa isang bagay o serbisyo kapalit ng pera.
original_explanation: The "add to cart" verb. This is what you do when you see something on Shopee or Lazada and your self-control has left the chat. "Bilhin mo na 'yan!" is the official mantra of your enabler friend. Unlike 'bilhan' (buy *for* someone), 'bilhin' focuses on the object of your desire. It's the verb that powers online shopping and impulsive "treat yourself" moments.
usage_notes: The focus of the action is on the object being bought.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **bilhin** ang bagong sapatos na nakita ko.","translation":"I want to **buy** the new shoes I saw."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **bilhin** lahat, magtira ka para sa iba.","translation":"Don't **buy** everything, leave some for others."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagdakip o pagsilo sa isang tao, hayop, o bagay; ang bagay na nadakip o nasilo.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you get caught doing something you shouldn't, from getting "huli" by your mom for eating chocolate before dinner, to getting "huli" by the MMDA for swerving. It's the "Gotcha!" moment.
usage_notes: The stress on the first syllable /HU-li/ is crucial to differentiate it from /hu-LI/ (last, late).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang **huli** ng mga mangingisda ngayong araw.","translation":"The fishermen's **catch** is big today."},{"sentence":"Naging maugong sa balita ang **huli** sa isang kilabot na kriminal.","translation":"The **arrest** of a notorious criminal was all over the news."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tuluyang pagkawala ng tubig o halumigmig sa isang bagay, na nagreresulta sa pagkatuyo, pagkasira, o pagkamatay nito.
etymology: From ma- (involuntary/process prefix) + tuyot (dried up, arid).
original_explanation: What happens to your plants when you forget to water them for a week. Also, what happens to your bank account before payday, or the conversation when you bring up an awkward topic. It's the state of being completely drained and moisture-free.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for plants, rivers, etc., or figuratively for resources, inspiration, or emotions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa matinding tag-init, nagsimulang **matuyot** ang mga ilog.","translation":"Because of the intense heat, the rivers began to **dry up**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **matuyot** ang iyong mga pangarap.","translation":"Don't let your dreams **wither**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kasuotan na isinusuot sa mga kamay para sa proteksiyon, init, o bilang palamuti.
original_explanation: Your hands' personal protective equipment (PPE). Whether you're a doctor, a boxer, a gardener, or just someone who's *maarte* about touching things, you need a pair of *guwantes*. It's the thing that stands between your skin and whatever the world throws at it.
usage_notes: The word is already plural in Spanish, but in Tagalog, it is treated as singular ('isang guwantes') or made plural with 'mga' ('mga guwantes').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong magsuot ng **guwantes** kapag maglilinis ng banyo.","translation":"You need to wear **gloves** when cleaning the bathroom."},{"sentence":"Binigyan siya ng isang pares ng **guwantes** na pang-boksing.","translation":"He was given a pair of boxing **gloves**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ito ay ang kilos ng paggawa o pagbuo ng isang bagay mula sa wala o mula sa mga umiiral na materyales. Tumutukoy sa nakaraang aksyon ng paglikha.
original_explanation: This is the past tense of 'to create'. It's what God did in Genesis, what your favorite artist does with their music, or what you do when you perfectly assemble a meme that goes viral. It's the 'done' version of making something awesome. "Nilikha kita, sa'yo lang ang puso ko" - sounds like a cheesy song lyric, but it's peak creation myth vibes.
usage_notes: Past tense of 'lumikha' (to create) or 'likhain' (to be created).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang magandang tula ay **nilikha** ng isang tanyag na makata.","translation":"The beautiful poem was **created** by a famous poet."},{"sentence":"Ayon sa alamat, ang mundo ay **nilikha** sa loob ng pitong araw.","translation":"According to legend, the world was **created** in seven days."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang bagay, tao, o pangyayari na lubhang kasuklam-suklam, nakapandidiri, at nagdudulot ng matinding pagkamuhi o pagtanggi.
original_explanation: That feeling you get when you see a two-week-old tupperware of adobo forgotten in your bag. It's next-level 'kadiri'. It's the kind of disgusting that makes you want to un-see something.
usage_notes: A strong word used for things that are morally or physically repulsive.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **masuklam** na krimen ang naganap sa kanilang lugar.","translation":"An **abominable** crime occurred in their area."},{"sentence":"Ang amoy mula sa basurahan ay talagang **masuklam**.","translation":"The smell from the garbage can was truly **disgusting**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-alis ng putik, buhangin, at iba pang materyales mula sa ilalim ng anyong tubig tulad ng ilog, lawa, o daungan upang ito ay palalimin o palawakin.
original_explanation: Eto 'yung ginagawa sa mga baradong estero para hindi bumaha. Isipin mo, parang paglilinis ng kanal pero industrial-sized. Yung mga backhoe na kumukuha ng lahat ng basura at putik sa ilog? 'Yan, dina-**dragahin** nila para mas maluwag ang daanan ng tubig.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **dragahin** ang Ilog Pasig upang maiwasan ang matinding pagbaha sa Kamaynilaan.","translation":"The Pasig River needs to be **dredged** to prevent severe flooding in Metro Manila."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang karangalan, reputasyon, o magandang tingin ng ibang tao sa isang indibidwal o pamilya.
original_explanation: This is a big deal in Pinoy culture. It's the invisible asset your family has been building for generations. One scandal, one viral 'Marites' video, and that mabuting pangalan can be tarnished. It's more valuable than your credit score and harder to repair. 'Ingatan mo ang apelyido natin' is the classic parent line.
usage_notes: Emphasizes the importance of honor and reputation in Filipino society.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap sirain ang isang **mabuting pangalan** na iningatan sa loob ng maraming taon.","translation":"It is difficult to destroy a **good reputation** that has been protected for many years."},{"sentence":"Ang tanging yaman na maipapamana ko sa inyo ay ang ating **mabuting pangalan**.","translation":"The only wealth I can leave to you is our **good name**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hanay ng mga positibo at malusog na katangian o kilos na nagpapahiwatig na ang isang tao ay isang mabuting kapareha, kaibigan, o kasama.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung mga senyales na "GO!" ka sa isang tao. 'Yung aalukin ka ng "text me 'pag nakauwi ka na," o 'yung marunong mag-sorry at aminin 'pag mali sila. Basically, the opposite of toxic. 'Pag may green flag behavior 'yung ka-date mo, baka 'yan na 'yan, bes!
usage_notes: Isang modernong slang na karaniwang ginagamit sa social media at sa mga usapan tungkol sa relasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagiging magalang sa mga waiter ay isang malinaw na **green flag behavior**.","translation":"Being polite to waiters is a clear **green flag behavior**."},{"sentence":"Tinitingnan niya ngayon ang mga **green flag behavior** sa halip na balewalain ang mga red flag.","translation":"She now looks for **green flag behaviors** instead of ignoring the red flags."}]

translation: To be considered a bandit / To act like a bandit
meaning_filipino: Ituring na isang tulisan; kumilos o mag-isip na parang isang bandido o taong labas sa batas.
original_explanation: When your friend 'borrows' your charger and never returns it, that's not just borrowing, that's 'tulisanin' behavior. It's the verb form for acting like an outlaw, whether it's stealing treasure on the high seas or 'stealing' the last piece of pizza without asking.
usage_notes: A less common word, often found in literature. It can mean to be branded as a bandit or to have the characteristics of one.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang mga ginawa, **tulisanin** na ang turing sa kanya ng mga tao sa bayan.","translation":"Because of his actions, he is now **considered a bandit** by the townspeople."},{"sentence":"Pinangaralan siya ng kanyang ama na huwag magkaroon ng isipang **tulisanin**.","translation":"His father advised him not to have the mindset **of a bandit**."}]

translation: to act like a precocious child
meaning_filipino: Kumilos o magsalita na parang matanda kahit bata pa, madalas sa paraang nakakainis o hindi angkop sa edad.
original_explanation: Describes a kid who talks and acts like a tiny, know-it-all adult. They use big words, give unsolicited advice, and join grown-up conversations. It's like seeing a 7-year-old talk about politics or the economy. Cute, but also kinda... "Easy ka lang, 'nak." The term literally means 'to be a green tomato'—not yet ripe.
usage_notes: This is an idiomatic expression. It's often used with a slightly negative or teasing connotation. The root 'mura' here means unripe/young, not cheap or curse.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magmurang-kamatis** diyan, tapusin mo muna ang homework mo.","translation":"Don't **act all grown-up** there, finish your homework first."},{"sentence":"Mahilig **magmurang-kamatis** ang pamangkin ko, alam na ang lahat ng chismis sa pamilya.","translation":"My nephew loves to **act like a precocious child**; he knows all the family gossip."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtawa nang mahina, pigil, at may mataas na tono, karaniwan ay dahil sa kilig, katuwaan, o pag-kahiya.
etymology: Onomatopoeic, imitating the sound of a giggle.
original_explanation: It's the sound a group of high school girls makes when their crush walks by. It's that suppressed, high-pitched laugh you let out when you're trying not to be too loud in a quiet place like a library or a church. It's the sound of 'kilig' or sharing a secret joke. Basically, a laugh that's trying to stay on a leash but failing adorably.
usage_notes: Often used to describe the laughter of women or children.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi mapigilan ng mga dalaga na **maghagikgik** nang dumaan ang kanilang hinahangaang aktor.","translation":"The young ladies couldn't stop **giggling** when their favorite actor passed by."},{"sentence":"Narinig ko silang **naghahagikgikan** sa kabilang kwarto habang nag-uusap.","translation":"I heard them **tittering** in the other room while they were talking."}]

translation: to get into the habit of; to make a habit
meaning_filipino: Gawing isang regular na kasanayan o gawi ang isang kilos o gawain.
etymology: From `maka-` + `ugali` (habit) + `-an`. A complex verbal affix formation indicating the creation of a habit.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you start doing something so often it becomes automatic, like checking your phone the moment you wake up or ordering the same milk tea flavor every single time. It's turning a 'one-time thing' into a 'lifestyle.' 'Sana makaugalian mong mag-ipon, hindi 'yung puro add to cart.'
usage_notes: Implies a conscious or unconscious process of forming a habit. Often used in a prescriptive or advisory tone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sikapin mong **makaugalian** ang pagbabasa ng libro araw-araw.","translation":"Try to **get into the habit of** reading a book every day."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **makaugalian** ang pagiging huli sa mga pulong.","translation":"Don't **make a habit** of being late to meetings."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kaganapan, insidente, o anumang naganap.
original_explanation: The formal way to say 'the tea' or 'the chismis'. When someone asks 'Ano ang pagyayari?', they're asking for the full story, the sequence of events, the 'what went down'. It's the more dramatic cousin of 'pangyayari'.
usage_notes: 'Pangyayari' is the more common term for 'event'. 'Pagyayari' in this sense is slightly more literary or formal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isinalaysay niya ang buong **pagyayari** sa mga pulis.","translation":"He narrated the entire **occurrence** to the police."}]

translation: to darken; to make something dark
meaning_filipino: Gawing madilim ang isang lugar o bagay sa pamamagitan ng pag-alis o pagbawas ng liwanag.
original_explanation: The command you give when you want to set the mood for a horror movie marathon. Or what happens to your future kapag 'di ka nag-review para sa exam. 'Make it dark!'
usage_notes: A verb form to command or request making something darker.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaari mo bang **padilimin** ang kwarto para makatulog na ako?","translation":"Can you **darken** the room so I can sleep?"},{"sentence":"Sinadyang **padilimin** ang entablado bago lumabas ang bida.","translation":"The stage was intentionally **darkened** before the main star came out."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halamang-gamot (herba) na may mabango at nagpapalamig na lasa, karaniwang ginagamit sa pagkain, inumin, at kendi.
original_explanation: That cool, fresh flavor in your toothpaste, chewing gum, or fancy mojito. It's the tita's go-to for 'herbal' tea. The flavor that makes you feel like your breath is ready for a job interview.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang hiram na salita. Ang katutubong termino ay 'yerba buena' (mula sa Espanyol), ngunit ang 'mint' ay malawakang ginagamit, lalo na sa pagluluto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko ng ice cream na may lasang **mint** chocolate chip.","translation":"I want ice cream with **mint** chocolate chip flavor."},{"sentence":"Nagtanim si lola ng **mint** sa kanyang hardin para sa tsaa.","translation":"Grandma planted **mint** in her garden for tea."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga prinsipyo ng kagandahan at sining; ang pagpapahalaga sa kung ano ang kaaya-aya sa paningin o ang pangkalahatang istilong biswal ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: Your IG feed's color palette. The vibe of a coffee shop with minimalist furniture and lots of plants. That carefully curated 'messy' look. Basically, it's the overall 'porma' or 'dating' of something, from your outfit to your life choices. If it looks good for the 'gram, it's aesthetic.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa Taglish, lalo na sa konteksto ng social media, disenyo, at fashion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinipili niya ang mga gamit sa bahay na babagay sa kanyang minimalist **aesthetic**.","translation":"She chooses house items that will fit her minimalist **aesthetic**."},{"sentence":"Para sa kanya, hindi lang sa lasa, mahalaga rin ang **aesthetic** ng pagkain.","translation":"For her, it's not just about the taste, the **aesthetic** of the food is also important."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng paa upang tamaan ang isang bagay o tao nang may puwersa.
original_explanation: The primary move in football, street fights, and your baby cousin's tantrum. Also, what you feel like doing to your laptop when it freezes for the 10th time. Can also describe a strong drink that "kicks" you. "Wow, ang lakas ng sipa ng alak na 'to!"
usage_notes: Can be literal (kicking a ball) or figurative (a strong drink "kicking").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigla na lang **sumipa** ang kabayo kaya nahulog ang sakay nito.","translation":"The horse suddenly **kicked**, causing its rider to fall."}]

meaning_filipino: Magsasalita sa napakahinang tinig na halos hangin lamang ang maririnig. Ito ay nasa aspetong panghinaharap ng pandiwang 'bulong'.
etymology: From 'bulong' (whisper) with the future tense verb affix 'bu-'.
original_explanation: Future tense of 'bulong' (whisper). This is what you do when you're about to share some juicy chismis in the office and the boss is nearby. 'Mamaya, may ibubulong ako sa'yo.' (Later, I'll whisper something to you.) It's the official verb of secret-telling, prayer, and sweet nothings.
usage_notes: Standard future tense conjugation of the root word 'bulong'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bubulong** na lang ako sa'yo para walang ibang makarinig.","translation":"I **will just whisper** to you so no one else can hear."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **bubulong** ng mga sagot sa kanya bukas?","translation":"Who **will whisper** the answers to him tomorrow?"}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi batay sa katwiran, lohika, o matinong pag-iisip; salungat sa rason.
original_explanation: Yung ex mong bigla na lang nag-chat ng "miss na kita" after 5 years of no contact. The audacity! Ganyan ka-irasyonal. Walang logic, puro feelings (na mali pa). Parang pagbili ng mamahaling kape araw-araw kahit minimum wage ka.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang desisyon niyang umalis sa trabaho nang walang ipon ay **irasyonal**.","translation":"His decision to quit his job without any savings was **irrational**."},{"sentence":"Minsan, ang pag-ibig ay nagiging **irasyonal**.","translation":"Sometimes, love becomes **irrational**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na mahilig gumawa ng mga biro o kalokohan sa iba para sa katuwaan.
original_explanation: Your office-mate who puts tape under your mouse, the vlogger who does "social experiments," or your tito who tells the same corny joke every family reunion. A prankster is either the life of the party or the reason you have trust issues. There is no in-between.
usage_notes: Isang direktang hiram na salita na malawak na nauunawaan at ginagamit sa mga pag-uusap na Taglish.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siyang **prankster** sa buong opisina.","translation":"He's known as the **prankster** in the whole office."},{"sentence":"Ang mga **prankster** sa YouTube ay kumikita ng malaki.","translation":"The **pranksters** on YouTube earn a lot."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paraang katulad niyan; isang kilos o gawi na tumutulad sa ipinapakita o tinutukoy.
original_explanation: When you're trying to copy someone's signature move, that little flick of the wrist or that specific 'sana all' tone. 'Gawin mo, paganyan.' It's the non-verbal version of 'just like this,' often said with a demo.
usage_notes: Often used in demonstrations or when giving instructions. It's a more active/demonstrative form than just saying 'ganyan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hawakan mo ang manibela nang **paganyan** para mas madali.","translation":"Hold the steering wheel **in this manner** so it's easier."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang idyomatikong pahayag na nangangahulugang duwag, madaling sumuko, o walang lakas ng loob na harapin ang isang pagsubok.
etymology: Literally "weak in the knee," a common expression for fear or lack of resolve.
original_explanation: This isn't about literally having bad knees from aging. Ito yung taong aatras sa challenge. Yung ka-team mo sa group project na unang-unang magsasabing "Hindi ko kaya 'yan" bago pa man subukan. Or yung torpe na friend mo na ilang taon nang may gusto kay crush pero hanggang tingin lang. In short, 'di palaban.
usage_notes: An idiomatic expression used to describe a person's character, not a physical ailment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **mahina ang tuhod**; harapin mo ang iyong mga problema.","translation":"Don't be **weak-kneed**; face your problems."},{"sentence":"Akala ko matapang siya, pero **mahina pala ang tuhod** nang kausapin na siya ng aming boss.","translation":"I thought he was brave, but he turned out to be **cowardly** when our boss talked to him."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking sisidlan para sa likido o gas. Maaari ring tumukoy sa isang sasakyang pandigma na may baluti at kanyon.
original_explanation: Can mean two things: 1) The big blue or white container on your roof that holds your water supply, which always runs out when you're in the middle of a shower. 2) The heavily armored vehicle you see in movies and news reports. For Pinoys, the first one is a much more common daily struggle. "Walang tubig! Ubos na laman ng tangke!"
usage_notes: The meaning depends entirely on context, whether it's about household utilities or military hardware.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang linisin ang **tangke** ng tubig minsan sa isang taon.","translation":"The water **tank** needs to be cleaned once a year."},{"sentence":"Nagpadala ng mga **tangke** ang militar sa lugar ng labanan.","translation":"The military sent **tanks** to the battle zone."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malakas at biglaang tunog na nililikha ng pagbagsak ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay mabigat.
original_explanation: That sound your upstairs neighbor makes at 3 AM. Or when you drop your Hydro Flask for the nth time. It's the official sound effect of 'patay, nahulog ko yung baso ni mama'.
usage_notes: Often used to describe something heavy falling. A stronger version is 'lagabog'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig mo ba ang **kalabog** sa kusina?","translation":"Did you hear that **thud** in the kitchen?"},{"sentence":"Isang malakas na **kalabog** ang gumising sa buong kapitbahayan.","translation":"A loud **thud** woke up the entire neighborhood."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mahaba at malungkot na tahol o ungal ng aso, lobo, o katulad na hayop, lalo na sa gabi.
etymology: Onomatopoeic. Ang tunog ay kahalintulad ng salita mismo.
original_explanation: 'Yung sound effect sa horror movie tuwing full moon. Ito 'yung sigaw ng mga aspin (asong Pinoy) sa kapitbahay niyo at 3 AM na parang may nakikita silang hindi mo nakikita. Nakikipag-chismisan lang siguro sa multo.
usage_notes: Madalas na iniuugnay sa mga aso, lobo, at mga nakakatakot o misteryosong sitwasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakakilabot ang **alulong** ng mga aso sa hatinggabi.","translation":"The **howl** of the dogs at midnight is creepy."},{"sentence":"Narinig namin ang **alulong** mula sa malayong kabundukan.","translation":"We heard a **howl** from the distant mountains."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagkakabuhol-buhol o pagkakabit-kabit ng mga bagay tulad ng sinulid, alambre, o lubid sa paraang mahirap kalasin.
original_explanation: Ever tried to untangle your earphones after pulling them from your pocket? That mess is the result of 'pagsalabid'. It's things getting twisted and tangled together, whether it's Christmas lights, your hair, or even people's lives and problems. 'Nagkasalabid-labid ang kwento nila' means their stories got complicated and intertwined. It's the physical or metaphorical state of being a hot mess.
usage_notes: Often implies a complex, messy, and difficult-to-untangle situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagsalabid** ng mga kable ng kuryente ay maaaring magdulot ng sunog.","translation":"The **entanglement** of electric cables can cause a fire."},{"sentence":"Naging kumplikado ang kaso dahil sa **pagsalabid** ng mga testimonya.","translation":"The case became complicated because of the **intertwining** of testimonies."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng mataas na halaga, materyal man o sentimental; itinuturing na mahalaga at hindi dapat sayangin.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung last piece ng paborito mong chocolate, o 'yung 8 hours of sleep na bihira mo nang makuha. Ito 'yung mga bagay na ayaw mong mawala, mapa-alahas man 'yan o 'yung oras na kasama mo si crush. Smeagol to the One Ring levels of 'My preciousss.'
usage_notes: Ang pambabaeng anyo ay "presyosa" (preciosa).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang oras ay isang **presyoso** na yaman na hindi maibabalik.","translation":"Time is a **precious** resource that cannot be returned."},{"sentence":"Itinuturing niyang **presyoso** ang mga alaala nila ng kanyang lola.","translation":"She considers her memories with her grandmother **precious**."}]

translation: passing of sentence; rendering of judgment
meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na proseso sa isang hukuman kung saan ipinapahayag ng hukom ang kaparusahan o desisyon sa isang kaso.
etymology: From `paggagawad` (act of awarding/granting, from root `gawad`) and `hatol` (judgment/sentence).
original_explanation: The most dramatic part of any legal TV show. It's when the judge, after all the 'objection, your honor!' and 'I rest my case,' finally drops the hammer. Everyone in the courtroom holds their breath. This is the moment of truth, the final verdict. 'Guilty or not guilty?'
usage_notes: A formal legal term. 'Paggawad ng hatol' is also used and is more common. The reduplicated 'paggagawad' might imply a series of judgments or a very formal, ceremonial process.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paggagawad ng hatol** sa akusado ay itinakda sa susunod na linggo.","translation":"The **passing of sentence** for the accused is scheduled for next week."},{"sentence":"Kinabahan ang lahat habang nagaganap ang **paggagawad ng hatol**.","translation":"Everyone was nervous while the **rendering of judgment** was happening."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o pagsasagawa ng hakbang upang maikulong o maparusahan sa bilangguan ang isang tao.
etymology: From the causative prefix `ipa-` and the noun `bilanggo` (prisoner), which is derived from Spanish.
original_explanation: The ultimate teleserye threat. This isn't just 'ipakulong' (to jail); this has the gravitas of a final-act courtroom drama. The rich matriarch, pointing a trembling finger at the villain, screams, "Mananagot ka! **Ipabibilanggo** kita hanggang sa mabulok ka sa kulungan!" It's the legal system's version of 'cancel culture'.
usage_notes: Carries a strong, serious tone, often related to legal justice or a desire for severe punishment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang layunin ng piskal ay **ipabilanggo** ang lahat ng sangkot sa krimen.","translation":"The fiscal's goal is to **have** all those involved in the crime **imprisoned**."},{"sentence":"Ipinangako niya sa sarili na **ipabibilanggo** niya ang pumatay sa kanyang ama.","translation":"He promised himself that he would **have** his father's killer **imprisoned**."}]

translation: string; cord; something used for tying
meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay, tulad ng lubid, sinulid, o alambre, na ginagamit sa pagtatali o pagbubuhol.
original_explanation: Your go-to for keeping things together, literally. It's the straw string for your takeout plastic bag, the rubber band for your hair, the shoelace for your sneakers. In a metaphorical, #hugot sense, `panali` is what keeps you attached to someone, whether it's a good relationship or a toxic one. "Ano bang panali mo sa kanya at 'di mo maiwan?"
usage_notes: A very general and common term for any tying material.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha ka ng **panali** para sa mga kahon.","translation":"Get something to **tie** the boxes with."},{"sentence":"Wala akong makitang **panali** sa buhok ko.","translation":"I can't find a **hair tie**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang akronim para sa 'Personal Computer,' isang uri ng kompyuter na idinisenyo para sa indibidwal na paggamit.
original_explanation: Short for 'Personal Computer.' The holy grail for any gamer, work-from-home professional, or student whose laptop is crying from all the open Chrome tabs. In the Philippines, building your own 'PC' is a rite of passage for the tech-savvy, often discussed in online forums and Gilmore.
usage_notes: Pronounced as the English letters 'P-C'. Widely used and understood in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-iipon ako para makabili ng bagong **PC** para sa gaming.","translation":"I'm saving up to buy a new **PC** for gaming."},{"sentence":"Mas mabilis magtrabaho kung sa **PC** ka gagawa kaysa sa phone.","translation":"It's faster to work if you do it on a **PC** than on a phone."}]

meaning_filipino: Pakinggan nang may-pag-unawa; bigyan ng pansin o sundin ang isang pakiusap, payo, o utos.
original_explanation: This isn't just "to hear" (marinig), this is "to listen and actually consider it." Ito yung hiling mo sa management na sana dinggin ang request mo for a salary increase. O yung dasal mo kay Lord na sana dinggin niya. It's more than just sound waves hitting your ear; it involves the heart and mind.
usage_notes: Isang mas pormal at malalim na bersyon ng 'pakinggan'. Ang 'dinggin' ay nagpapahiwatig ng pagsunod o pagbibigay, habang ang 'pakinggan' ay maaaring mangahulugan lamang ng pakikinig.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawa'y **dinggin** ng langit ang ating mga panalangin.","translation":"May heaven **heed** our prayers."},{"sentence":"**Dinggin** mo ang payo ng iyong mga magulang,\" sabi ng lola.","translation":"**Listen to** the advice of your parents,\" said the grandmother."}]

translation: to raise; to increase the height of
meaning_filipino: Pagpapataas o pagdaragdag sa elebasyon, antas, o halaga ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: Yung ginagawa mo sa standards mo after a failed talking stage. O kaya, yung hiling mo sa boss mo para sa sahod mo. 'Boss, baka pwedeng taasan naman.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **taasan** ang pader para hindi mapasok ng baha.","translation":"We need to **raise** the wall so the flood can't get in."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong masyadong **taasan** ang iyong boses.","translation":"Don't **raise** your voice too much."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay o paraan na ginagamit upang magdulot ng paghinto sa isang kilos, galaw, o proseso.
original_explanation: This can be a literal brake on a car, a doorstop, or the 'seen' message that ends a promising chat conversation. It's the red light, the 'end of contract' notice, or your credit card getting declined. Anything that brings momentum to a screeching halt.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maglagay ka ng **pampatigil** sa pinto para hindi sumarado.","translation":"Put a **stopper** on the door so it doesn't close."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal para sa isang lalaking homoseksuwal.
etymology: A playful alteration of "bakla," a common feature of "swardspeak" or gay lingo in the Philippines. The transformation often involves changing consonants or adding syllables.
original_explanation: Your friendly neighborhood gay best friend. "Accla" is the quintessential gayspeak term for "bakla." It's what you call your friend who gives the best life advice, can roast you into oblivion, and has a PhD in spotting red flags from a mile away. It's a term of endearment within the community.
usage_notes: Primarily used within and by the LGBTQ+ community and those familiar with gay lingo. Can be used affectionately.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Accla**, tulungan mo naman ako sa outfit ko para sa party mamaya.","translation":"**Girlfriend** (gay friend), help me with my outfit for the party later."},{"sentence":"Ang daming chika ng mga **accla** sa kanto.","translation":"The **gays** on the corner have so much gossip."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpakamatay sa pamamagitan ng pagsasabit ng sarili sa leeg gamit ang isang tali o lubid.
original_explanation: This is a serious and sensitive word referring specifically to the act of suicide by hanging. It’s a word you hear in grim news reports or see in very serious literature, a stark reminder of deep despair. Not a word to be used lightly or colloquially.
usage_notes: A very sensitive and specific term. It should be used with utmost caution and respect due to its subject matter. It is not a general term for suicide.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natagpuan sa ulat ng pulisya na ang biktima ay **bumigti**.","translation":"It was found in the police report that the victim **committed suicide by hanging**."},{"sentence":"Ang tema ng pelikula ay napakabigat, ipinakita nito kung bakit **bumigti** ang pangunahing tauhan.","translation":"The film's theme was very heavy, it showed why the main character **committed suicide by hanging**."}]

meaning_filipino: Mag-utos o magpahintulot na salakayin o lusubin ang isang lugar, grupo, o bagay.
original_explanation: Like when you and your officemates decide to raid the newly opened samgyupsal place. "Tara, pasalakayin na natin 'yang unli-pork!" It's a full-on foodie assault. Can also be used in a literal, military sense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-utos ang heneral na **pasalakayin** ang kuta ng mga kalaban.","translation":"The general ordered to **have the** enemy's fort **attacked**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pasalakayin** sa mga langgam ang pagkain; takpan mo iyan.","translation":"Don't **let the** food **be attacked** by ants; cover it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na namamahala sa pagbibigay at pagbabantay ng isang pagsusulit o eksaminasyon.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "taga-" (tagapamahala) at salitang-ugat na "iksamen", na hiram sa Ingles na "examine".
original_explanation: The proctor during your board exams whose only job seems to be making you nervous by walking around. The person who says 'pencils up!' and holds your future in their hands for three hours. Their stare is more powerful than any CCTV.
usage_notes: More commonly used in formal academic or testing contexts. 'Proctor' is also widely used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang **tagaiksamen** kaya walang nangahas na mandaya.","translation":"The **examiner** was strict so no one dared to cheat."}]

translation: to go around; to tour; to deceive
meaning_filipino: Ang paglibot sa isang lugar; ang paggalaw nang paikot sa isang bagay; maaari ring mangahulugan ng panlilinlang o hindi pagiging direkta sa pagsasalita.
original_explanation: Can mean literally going around the block to find parking, or showing your balikbayan relatives around Manila. But in 'hugot' terms, it's what your ex did to your feelings. "Huwag mo akong ikut-ikutin!" is the classic line when someone's giving you the runaround, whether it's a customer service rep or a jowa who won't give a straight answer.
usage_notes: Has both a literal meaning (to physically go around) and a figurative one (to deceive or be evasive). Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Plano naming **ikutin** ang buong isla ng Palawan sa aming bakasyon.","translation":"We plan to **tour** the entire island of Palawan on our vacation."},{"sentence":"Diretsuhin mo ako, huwag mo akong **ikutin**!","translation":"Be straight with me, don't give me the **runaround**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang daan, ilog, o landas na maraming liko, kurbada, o paikot-ikot.
original_explanation: Like the roads going up to Baguio or Tagaytay. A "maliklik" na daan will test your driving skills and your passenger's stomach. It can also describe a story with too many side-plots (like a Pinoy teleserye) or a convoluted explanation from your friend who's trying to hide something. "Diretsuhin mo na, 'wag nang maliklik pa!"
usage_notes: Primarily used to describe paths, roads, and rivers. Can be used figuratively for speech or writing that is not direct.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Maliklik** ang daan paakyat ng bundok kaya mag-ingat sa pagmamaneho.","translation":"The road up the mountain is **winding**, so drive carefully."},{"sentence":"Ayoko ng mga sagot na **maliklik**; sabihin mo ang totoo.","translation":"I don't like **circuitous** answers; tell me the truth."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng matinding galit o poot, kadalasan ay sa pamamagitan ng pagkagat o paggiling ng mga ngipin.
original_explanation: This is your face when the internet goes out during a crucial Zoom meeting or in the middle of a Netflix finale. It's that silent, teeth-grinding fury. Parang kontrabida sa teleserye na nagpaplanong maghiganti. Pure, unadulterated rage.
usage_notes: Often associated with the phrase 'nagngangalit ang mga ngipin' (gnashing the teeth).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halos marinig mo ang kanyang mga ngipin na **nagngangalit** sa galit.","translation":"You could almost hear his teeth **gnashing** in anger."},{"sentence":"**Nagngangalit** sa galit ang amo nang malamang ninakawan siya.","translation":"The boss was **raging** in anger when he found out he was robbed."}]

translation: to hurry up; to do something quickly
meaning_filipino: Ang pagmamadali o paggawa ng isang bagay sa mas mabilis na paraan.
original_explanation: This is your team lead's favorite word during crunch time before a deadline. "Guys, dalian n'yo, client is waiting!" It's the verb form of panic, fueled by coffee and the fear of your manager's follow-up email.
usage_notes: Object-focus verb. The actor-focus equivalent is "magmadali."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dalian** mo ang paglalakad, baka mahuli tayo.","translation":"**Hurry up** your walking, we might be late."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **dalian** ang proyektong ito.","translation":"We need **to rush** this project."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging luma o matagal na; ang paglipas ng mahabang panahon.
etymology: From `laon` (old, of long duration) with `ka-` and `-an` affixes, forming an abstract noun.
original_explanation: This is that deep, historical 'oldness.' Not just your lola's old sewing machine, but the vibe of Intramuros, the ancient Banaue Rice Terraces, or a story passed down through generations. It's the weight of time itself. It’s what makes vintage cool and history important.
usage_notes: A formal and somewhat literary word. 'Katagalan' is a more common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa **kalaanan** ng panahon, ang mga lumang gusali ay unti-unting gumuho.","translation":"With the **passage of time**, the old buildings gradually collapsed."},{"sentence":"Ang mga alamat ay nagbabago rin sa **kalaanan**.","translation":"Myths also change with **antiquity**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng pagiging madaling mapapayag, mapaniwalain, o mahikayat na sumang-ayon sa isang kasunduan, na kung minsan ay sa ikapapahamak o ikalulugi ng sarili.
etymology: From 'mapag-' + 'ka-' + 'yari' (to finish, to make) + '-an'. The construction suggests being the object or place where an agreement is 'finished' or made.
original_explanation: This is the friend who always ends up paying for everyone's coffee because they're too nice to say no. They're the 'yes man' of the group, easily convinced to agree to a deal, even if it's a bad one. Basically, 'sige na nga' is their life motto, and they often get the short end of the stick for it.
usage_notes: Carries a slightly negative connotation, implying a lack of assertiveness that leads to being taken advantage of.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging masyadong **mapagkayarian** sa negosyo, baka malugi ka.","translation":"Don't be too **agreeable to a fault** in business, you might lose money."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang pagiging **mapagkayarian**, siya ay laging napagkakasunduan na gumawa ng mga gawaing hindi naman sa kanya.","translation":"Because of his **easily swayed** nature, he always ends up agreeing to do tasks that aren't his."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tunog na nililikha ng manok, lalo na pagkatapos mangitlog; putak.
etymology: Onomatopoeic. The word itself imitates the sound.
original_explanation: This is the sound a chicken makes after laying an egg. It's the ultimate 'I did it!' announcement in the chicken world. Think of it as the poultry version of posting your achievement on social media. 'Guys, may itlog na! #blessed #NewEgg'.
usage_notes: 'Putak' is a more common synonym. Can also be used as a verb (mag-kakak).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **kakak** ng manok mula sa likod-bahay.","translation":"I heard the **cackle** of the chicken from the backyard."},{"sentence":"Nag-umpisang mag-**kakak** ang inahing manok.","translation":"The mother hen started to **cackle**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang balangkas ng mga bakal na bara na karaniwang ginagamit bilang harang sa bintana, pinto, o kulungan.
original_explanation: Ito yung literal na harang sa buhay mo. Pwedeng rehas ng bintana para di ka manakawan, o rehas ng kulungan para di ka makatakas. Sa 'hugot' terms, ito yung "walls" na binuo mo around your heart para 'di na masaktan ulit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May mga bakal na **rehas** ang lahat ng bintana sa bahay.","translation":"All the windows in the house have iron **bars**."},{"sentence":"Ikinulong siya sa likod ng mga **rehas**.","translation":"He was imprisoned behind **bars**."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubos na masigla, puno ng enerhiya, at aktibo.
original_explanation: This is 'buhay' on steroids. It's not just alive, it's *thriving*. Like the Quiapo market on a Wednesday, the comments section of a celebrity scandal, or your tita after her third cup of coffee. It's the energy you wish you had on a Monday morning.
usage_notes: An intensifier for the adjective 'buhay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Buhay na buhay** ang diwa ng Pasko sa kanilang tahanan.","translation":"The Christmas spirit is **very much alive** in their home."},{"sentence":"Naging **buhay na buhay** ang usapan nang dumating ang bagong chismis.","translation":"The conversation became very **lively** when the new gossip arrived."}]

translation: to grow fond of; to endear oneself to
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng pagtingin, pag-aalaga, o pagmamahal para sa isang tao, hayop, o bagay sa paglipas ng panahon.
original_explanation: Akala mo 'for fun' lang, 'friends lang' kayo, pero sa araw-araw na ka-chat at ka-late night call, ayun na, nahulog ka na. **Napamahal** ka na sa kanya. Pwede rin sa aspin (Asong Pinoy) na pinapakain mo lang sa labas ng gate, pero ngayon, sa loob na ng bahay niyo natutulog. You didn't expect to catch feelings, but you did.
usage_notes: This verb is about the process of developing affection, not the state of being in love. Not to be confused with 'mapamahal' as in 'to become expensive'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit aso lang siya, **napamahal** na siya sa buong pamilya.","translation":"Even if he is just a dog, the whole family has **grown fond of** him."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko sinasadyang **mapamahal** sa'yo.","translation":"I didn't mean **to grow fond of** you."}]

translation: to let out; to make something come out; to release
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapahintulot o pagpwersa sa isang bagay, tao, o konsepto na lumabas mula sa isang espasyo.
original_explanation: The command you give when you need to "release the kraken"—or just some air from a tire. It's what you do to a secret ("palabasin ang totoo"), a character in a show ("palabasin mo na si character X!"), or literally, to vent your feelings. "Palabasin ang hangin" is what you do to a flat tire, or what your tita tells you to do after eating too many beans (burp!).
usage_notes: This is the verb form. It often appears in commands. For the specific phrase 'palabasin ang hangin', it means 'to let the air out' or 'to deflate'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **palabasin ang hangin** sa gulong bago ito ayusin.","translation":"You need **to let the air out** of the tire before fixing it."},{"sentence":"**Palabasin** mo na ang katotohanan.","translation":"**Let out** the truth now."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng paglalaro o kompetisyon na sumusunod sa mga alituntunin at nagpapakita ng respeto sa kalaban, na walang ginagawang anumang uri ng pandaraya.
original_explanation: This is the spirit of sportsmanship. It's shaking hands after a game, whether you win or lose. It's *not* tripping your opponent in a basketball game or using cheat codes in an online match. It's about playing with honor, even if it means losing. Basically, the opposite of how some people play Tong-its with their family.
usage_notes: A common phrase in sports, games, and competitions to emphasize the importance of sportsmanship and adherence to rules.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinapaalala ng coach sa kanyang mga manlalaro ang kahalagahan ng **walang-dayang paglalaro**.","translation":"The coach reminds his players about the importance of **fair play**."},{"sentence":"Ang paligsahan ay naging matagumpay dahil sa **walang-dayang paglalaro** ng lahat ng kalahok.","translation":"The competition was a success because of the **fair play** of all participants."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na kulisap na panlipunan, nabubuhay sa mga kolonya, at kilala sa pagiging masipag at malakas.
original_explanation: The ultimate team player. Sila 'yung original na 'sana all' sa group projects. Kahit gaano kabigat ang isang butil ng kanin o mumo ng biskwit, kakayanin 'yan basta't magkakasama. They're also the tiny ninjas that will find that one drop of spilled Coke on your desk from three rooms away.
usage_notes: A general term for any species of ant. Larger, biting ants are often called 'hantik'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May mga **langgam** sa asukal.","translation":"There are **ants** in the sugar."},{"sentence":"Kinagat ako ng pulang **langgam**.","translation":"I was bitten by a red **ant**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng hayop-dagat na may matigas na pares ng talukab na nagsisilbing proteksyon; tumutukoy din sa mismong talukab na ito.
original_explanation: Your beach trip souvenir haul. These are the pretty shells you pick up by the seashore, hoping to 'hear the ocean'. Also, a key ingredient in dishes like 'tinolang kabibe'. It's nature's jewelry box.
usage_notes: Can refer to the live animal or just the empty shell.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Namulot kami ng mga **kabibe** sa dalampasigan.","translation":"We picked up **seashells** on the shore."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang sabaw ng nilutong **kabibe**.","translation":"The broth of the cooked **clams** is delicious."}]
