meaning_filipino: Inilagay sa isang maayos at ligtas na lugar; nakaayos o hindi nakakalat.
original_explanation: The state of your room for the 5 minutes after you clean it and before you mess it up again. It's what your mom wants to see when she says 'magligpit ka ng gamit mo.' Also refers to evidence that has been 'put away' permanently. 'Nakaligpit na ang lahat ng ebidensya' has a very different, more sinister vibe.
usage_notes: Can mean simply 'tidied up' or, in a more colloquial/sinister context, 'disposed of' or 'eliminated'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos maglaro, sinigurado niyang **nakaligpit** ang lahat ng kanyang mga laruan.","translation":"After playing, he made sure all his toys were **put away**."},{"sentence":"Maayos na **nakaligpit** sa aparador ang mga damit na bagong laba.","translation":"The newly washed clothes are neatly **kept** in the cabinet."}]

translation: to suppress; to put out (a fire); to quell
meaning_filipino: Patigilin o sugpuin ang paglaganap ng isang bagay, tulad ng apoy, kaguluhan, o damdamin.
original_explanation: The act of stopping something from getting out of control. It's what firefighters do to a fire, what a bouncer does to a bar fight, or what you do to your feelings for your "friend" because "friends lang daw kayo". It's the ultimate "pigilan mo 'ko!" action.
usage_notes: Can be used for literal fires, figurative fires (like rebellion), or emotions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinikap ng mga bumbero na **apulain** ang malaking sunog.","translation":"The firefighters tried to **put out** the huge fire."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **apulain** ang galit na nararamdaman niya.","translation":"It's hard to **suppress** the anger that he feels."}]

meaning_filipino: Itutok at pakawalan ang isang bagay, tulad ng palaso o bala, patungo sa isang tiyak na puntirya.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'shoot your shot.' Before DMs, there was Cupid's arrow. 'Itudla' is to aim something precisely, whether it's a Nerf gun bullet at your unsuspecting sibling or your feelings towards your crush. You line up the target, take a deep breath, and hope for a bullseye.
usage_notes: Often used poetically or in the context of archery, hunting, or older forms of weaponry. Metaphorically, it can mean to direct something (like a comment or accusation) at someone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Itudla** mo ang pana sa gitna ng target.","translation":"**Aim** the arrow at the center of the target."},{"sentence":"Tila sa akin **itinudla** ang lahat ng sisi para sa pagkabigo ng proyekto.","translation":"It seems all the blame for the project's failure was **aimed** at me."}]

meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang magpadaan ng isang bagay mula sa bibig patungo sa lalamunan at sikmura.
original_explanation: 'Yung struggle mo sa pag-inom ng gamot na tableta na kasing laki ng Vios. "Hindi ko makalulon 'tong kapsula, besh! Pwede 'yung syrup na lang?" Also used figuratively for hard truths: "Isang mapait na katotohanan na mahirap makalulon."
usage_notes: Can be literal (swallowing food/pills) or figurative (swallowing one's pride, accepting a difficult situation).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahihirapan siyang **makalulon** ng pagkain dahil masakit ang kanyang lalamunan.","translation":"He is having a hard time **being able to swallow** food because his throat hurts."},{"sentence":"May mga desisyon sa buhay na kailangan mong tanggapin kahit mahirap **makalulon**.","translation":"There are decisions in life you have to accept even if they are hard to **swallow**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na tumatalon mula sa isang sasakyang panghimpapawid gamit ang parasyut, para sa libangan, kompetisyon, o bilang bahagi ng operasyong militar.
original_explanation: Literally, someone who jumps out of a plane with a parachute. But in Philippine politics, a 'parasyutist' is a political candidate who suddenly appears in a new district to run for office, even though they have no real roots or connection there. They're 'parachuted in' by a political party. It's like suddenly claiming you're 'taga-dito' a month before the election.
usage_notes: Ginagamit din sa kontekstong politikal upang ilarawan ang isang kandidato na biglaang tumatakbo sa isang lugar na hindi niya taal na kinabibilangan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga bihasang **parasyutist** ay kayang gumawa ng mga pormasyon sa himpapawid.","translation":"Experienced **parachutists** can create formations in the air."},{"sentence":"Inakusahan siyang isang **parasyutist** ng kanyang mga kalaban sa politika dahil hindi naman talaga siya taga-roon.","translation":"He was accused of being a **parachutist** by his political opponents because he isn't really from there."}]

meaning_filipino: Umupo sa kandungan ng ibang tao bilang paglalambing o dahil sa kakulangan ng espasyo.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa ng bata sa nanay niya sa jeep para makatipid sa pamasahe. Or 'yung ultimate clingy move ng jowa mo habang nanonood kayo ng Netflix. "Sana all may kakalungan."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Agad na **kumalong** sa kanyang ama ang batang matagal na hindi ito nakita.","translation":"The child who hadn't seen their father in a long time immediately **sat on his lap**."},{"sentence":"Pwede ba akong **kumalong** muna? Puno na kasi ang upuan.","translation":"Can I **sit on your lap** for a while? The seats are already full."}]

translation: a trip; a snap; a cut
meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang pagkaputol ng isang bagay na may tensyon tulad ng tali; o ang sinadyang pagharang sa paa ng iba upang ito ay matisod o matumba.
original_explanation: When your internet connection suddenly dies in the middle of a winning Mobile Legends match, that's "patid". When a kite string snaps, that's "patid". And when a "frenemy" subtly sticks their foot out to make you fall, that's also "patid". It’s a sudden, frustrating disconnection or interruption.
usage_notes: As a root word, it conveys the idea of a sudden break, interruption, or the act of tripping someone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawalan kami ng kuryente dahil sa **patid** na kawad ng kuryente.","translation":"We lost power because of a **snapped** electrical wire."},{"sentence":"Ingat sa **patid** ng mga mandurukot sa Divisoria.","translation":"Beware of the **tripping** tactics of pickpockets in Divisoria."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang modernong ekspresyon na nagpapahiwatig ng pagkakaroon ng 'kilig', na may kasamang bahagyang panunukso o modernong tono. Ang 'yarn' ay isang salitang balbal na hango sa 'iyan'.
original_explanation: This is "kilig" for the Gen Z/Twitter/TikTok generation. The 'yarn' (a playful evolution of 'iyan') adds a layer of sass, irony, or modern flair. You say it when your friend tells you about their crush's minimal effort: "Binigyan niya ako ng tissue. Omg, kilig yarn!" It can be genuine, but it often has a playful, slightly teasing tone. It's the 2026 version of "Ayieee!"
usage_notes: A very informal, modern slang expression popular in social media and among younger speakers.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-reply siya sa story ko? **Kilig yarn**!","translation":"He replied to my story? **Oh, the kilig**!"},{"sentence":"Friend 1: 'He held the door open for me.' Friend 2: '**Kilig yarn**! Baka naman sanay lang siyang maging gentleman.'","translation":"Friend 1: 'He held the door open for me.' Friend 2: '**So romantic!** Or maybe he's just used to being a gentleman.'"}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay na ginagamit bilang palamuti o pampaganda upang mapabuti ang anyo ng isang lugar, bagay, o tao.
original_explanation: The formal version of "dekor." Ito yung salitang ginagamit sa mga event planning proposal o sa school project. Habang ang "dekor" ay para sa chismisan, ang "dekorasyon" ay para sa presentation. Pareho lang silang palamuti, pero ito, mas may class pakinggan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili kami ng mga bagong **dekorasyon** para sa aming Christmas tree.","translation":"We bought new **decorations** for our Christmas tree."},{"sentence":"Ang engrandeng **dekorasyon** sa plasa ay para sa darating na pista.","translation":"The grand **decoration** in the plaza is for the upcoming fiesta."}]

meaning_filipino: Magtakda o mag-utos, karaniwan ay isang doktor, ng isang gamot o paraan ng paggamot para sa isang pasyente.
original_explanation: The verb form of what you hope the doctor does para ma-approve ang sick leave mo. It's the official act of a doctor writing down your meds on a piece of paper that's almost impossible to read. "Doc, ano po ang pwede kong inumin?" "Sige, ireseta ko sa'yo ito."
usage_notes: Primarily used in a medical context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang doktor lang ang may karapatang **ireseta** ang gamot na ito.","translation":"Only a doctor has the right to **prescribe** this medicine."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang iinom ng kahit ano na hindi **inireseta** sa iyo.","translation":"Don't take anything that wasn't **prescribed** to you."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na may kaparehong dugong nananalaytay; kamag-anak sa dugo.
original_explanation: This is your 'bloodline.' Your fam, your clan, the people you're stuck with during family reunions whether you like it or not. They're the ones who can donate a kidney to you (biologically speaking) or ask 'May asawa ka na?' (annoyingly speaking).
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun (a blood relative) or an adjective (related by blood).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit hindi kami **kadugo**, tinuring niya akong parang tunay na kapatid.","translation":"Even if we are not **blood relatives**, she treated me like a real sibling."},{"sentence":"Lahat ng naririto sa reunion ay mga **kadugo** ko.","translation":"Everyone here at the reunion are my **blood relatives**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng puno o ang bilog na bunga nito na may makapal na balat at maraming maliliit na buto na nababalutan ng mamula-mulang laman.
original_explanation: Isang prutas na parang high-maintenance. Ang hirap balatan, pero 'pag nakain mo na, worth it naman. Parang jowa mo lang. Ang daming buto sa loob, parang ang dami niyang issues, pero masarap at healthy naman. Also, sosyal pakinggan. 'Kumakain ako ng **granada**.'
usage_notes: Dahil sa homonimo, madalas kailangan ng konteksto para malaman kung prutas o pampasabog ang tinutukoy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap at masustansya ang katas ng **granada**.","translation":"The juice of the **pomegranate** is delicious and nutritious."},{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng **granada** sa fruit stand.","translation":"Mom bought a **pomegranate** at the fruit stand."}]

meaning_filipino: At iba pa; at ang mga katulad. Ginagamit sa dulo ng isang listahan upang ipahiwatig na marami pang ibang halimbawa na hindi na binanggit.
original_explanation: Ang life-saver ng mga estudyante kapag kailangan magbigay ng maraming examples pero tatlo lang ang alam. 'Magdala ng papel, ballpen, libro, etsetera.' Ito rin ang sinasabi mo sa isip mo kapag nagra-rant ang kaibigan mo tungkol sa 1,001 problema niya sa buhay. 'Walang pera, pagod sa work, toxic ang boss, etsetera.'
usage_notes: Commonly abbreviated as 'etc.' in writing. The Tagalog equivalent is 'at iba pa' (atbp.).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang kumain ng prutas tulad ng mangga, saging, pinya, **etsetera**.","translation":"He likes to eat fruits like mango, banana, pineapple, **etcetera**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglipat ng mga tao mula sa isang lugar patungo sa iba upang doon manirahan, pansamantala man o permanente.
etymology: From `pang-` + `dayo` (foreigner, visitor) + `-han`. The root `dayo` refers to coming from another place.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'lipat-bahay' on a global scale. It's what your Tita did to get to Canada, or what your ancestors did when they moved from the province to Manila. It's the story of every OFW—leaving one home to build another, fueled by dreams, remittances, and a giant balikbayan box.
usage_notes: Often used in formal, academic, or news contexts to discuss population movements. 'Migrasyon' is a common Spanish-derived synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pandarayuhan** ay isang malaking salik sa pagbabago ng kultura ng isang bansa.","translation":"**Migration** is a major factor in the cultural change of a country."},{"sentence":"Maraming Pilipino ang nagnanais na mangibang-bayan, isang anyo ng **pandarayuhan**.","translation":"Many Filipinos wish to go to other countries, a form of **immigration**."}]

translation: mock priest; someone pretending to be a priest
meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagpapanggap o gumagaya sa isang pari, o isang laro kung saan ang isang bata ay gumaganap bilang pari.
etymology: Pag-uulit ng salitang "pari" na may hulaping "-an", na nagpapahiwatig ng laro, lugar, o panggagaya.
original_explanation: This is what kids play during Flores de Mayo season, using a blanket as a cassock and a biscuit as the host. It can also refer to someone acting all high and mighty and preachy, but isn't the real deal. "Ay, 'wag kang mag **pari-parian** diyan, hindi ka naman banal."
usage_notes: Ang hulaping "-an" dito ay nangangahulugang laro o imitasyon, katulad ng "bahay-bahayan" (playing house).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig maglaro ng **pari-parian** ang mga bata tuwing Mayo.","translation":"The children love to play **mock priest** every May."},{"sentence":"Itigil mo 'yang **pari-parian** mo, hindi ka nakakatuwa.","translation":"Stop your **pretending-to-be-a-priest** act, you're not funny."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng isang ibabaw na walang gaspang, guhit, o anumang umbok; pagiging makinis.
original_explanation: The ultimate #skincaregoals. That flawless, poreless, "parang kutis-porselana" smoothness. It's what beauty products promise and what you hope for after a facial. Can also be used for smooth surfaces like a newly polished floor or a perfectly sanded piece of wood. "Ang kinis!" is the highest compliment for someone's skin.
usage_notes: Often used as a root for the adjective 'makinis' (smooth). The noun 'kinis' itself emphasizes the quality of smoothness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hangang-hanga ako sa **kinis** ng kanyang kutis.","translation":"I am so amazed by the **smoothness** of her skin."},{"sentence":"Upang makuha ang tamang **kinis**, kailangan mong lihain nang maigi ang kahoy.","translation":"To get the right **smoothness**, you need to sand the wood thoroughly."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paraang magkakaiba o magkakasalungat ang direksyon; halinhinan at magkasalubong.
original_explanation: Like how jeepneys weave through EDSA traffic, or how your lies get tangled when you're trying to explain where you were last night. It's messy, crisscrossing, and definitely not a straight line. Think of it as organized chaos.
usage_notes: Implies a pattern of alternating or opposing movements or arrangements. The repetition of 'sali' emphasizes the interwoven nature.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga hibla ng niyog ay inayos nang **pasali-saliwa** upang makabuo ng isang matibay na banig.","translation":"The coconut fibers were arranged **crisscrossing** each other to form a sturdy mat."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babae na gumaganap sa tungkulin ng isang ina ngunit hindi siyang tunay na ina; maaaring tiyahin, madrasta, o tagapag-alaga.
etymology: Reduplication of 'ina' (mother) with the suffix '-an', indicating a role or imitation.
original_explanation: This is the role you play in 'bahay-bahayan' when you were a kid. As an adult, it's the tita who acts like your second mom, the stepmom in your life, or even the senior manager at work who is surprisingly motherly. It's motherhood by action, not just by blood.
usage_notes: Can refer to a stepmother ('madrasta'), a foster mother, or simply someone who takes on a motherly role.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang tumayong **ina-inahan** namin mula nang pumanaw si Nanay.","translation":"She acted as our **mother figure** since Mom passed away."},{"sentence":"Sa larong bahay-bahayan, ako palagi ang **ina-inahan**.","translation":"In the game of playing house, I am always the **one acting as the mother**."}]

meaning_filipino: Daglat para sa "General Community Quarantine"; isang antas ng kuwarantina na ipinatupad sa Pilipinas noong pandemya ng COVID-19 na may mas maluwag na restriksyon kaysa sa ECQ.
original_explanation: Ah, the pandemic era throwback. **GCQ** was that weird in-between stage. You could go out, but you felt guilty about it. You could work, but only some of you. It was the 'pwede na pero ingat' phase of our lives. We all became experts in the alphabet soup of quarantines: ECQ, MECQ, GCQ, MGCQ. A true 2020-2021 mood.
usage_notes: This term is historically significant and tied specifically to the COVID-19 pandemic response in the Philippines. Its usage has become rare after the pandemic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Noong panahon ng **GCQ**, limitado pa rin ang paglabas ng bahay.","translation":"During the **GCQ** period, going out of the house was still limited."},{"sentence":"Maraming negosyo ang nagsimulang magbukas muli nang isinailalim ang lugar sa **GCQ**.","translation":"Many businesses started to reopen when the area was placed under **GCQ**."}]

translation: to license; to grant a permit to
meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng pormal na pahintulot o lisensya ang isang tao, negosyo, o gawain upang legal na makapag-operate o maisagawa ito.
original_explanation: This is what the LTO does to you after you've survived their obstacle course and written exams. It's the government's way of saying, "Okay, sige, you're legit. For now." To be 'lisensiyahan' is to get the official go-signal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **lisensiyahan** ng gobyerno ang lahat ng bagong negosyo.","translation":"The government needs **to license** all new businesses."},{"sentence":"Hindi pa **nililisensiyahan** ang paggamit ng sasakyang iyon sa pampublikong daan.","translation":"The use of that vehicle on public roads has not yet **been licensed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang obal na bagay na may matigas na balat, na inilalabas ng mga babaeng ibon at ilang reptilya, na naglalaman ng embryo at sustansya para sa pag-unlad nito. Karaniwang tumutukoy sa itlog ng manok na ginagamit bilang pagkain.
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino breakfast staple. Sunny-side up, scrambled, or hard-boiled, it's the partner of sinangag in "silog" meals. Also, a classic "pasalubong" from the province, carefully transported so it doesn't become "basag." Metaphorically, it can also mean "zero" or "nothing," like the score you get on a test you didn't study for.
usage_notes: Can refer to any egg (chicken, duck, quail), but defaults to chicken egg unless specified. Also used as slang for "testicles."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko ng dalawang pritong **itlog** para sa almusal.","translation":"I want two fried **eggs** for breakfast."},{"sentence":"**Itlog** ang nakuha niyang iskor sa pagsusulit.","translation":"He got a **zero** (egg) score on the exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang numerong sero (0); ang halaga ng kawalan o pagiging wala.
original_explanation: Ah, "sero." The grade you get when you copy-paste from Wikipedia without changing anything. Also, the amount of money in your wallet the day before payday. It's the starting point of everything, and sometimes, the ending point of your sweldo.
usage_notes: "Wala" is more common in everyday speech for "nothing", while "sero" is used for the number 0, especially in academic, technical, or formal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakuha siya ng **sero** sa pagsusulit dahil sa pandaraya.","translation":"He got a **zero** on the exam for cheating."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa mitolohiya, ito ay isang uri ng diwata o espiritu ng kalikasan, karaniwang isinasakatawan bilang isang magandang dalaga na naninirahan sa mga ilog, puno, o bundok.
etymology: From Spanish 'ninfa', from Latin 'nympha', from Ancient Greek 'νύμφη' (númphē).
original_explanation: Think of them as the original nature influencers from mythology. They're the beautiful, ethereal ladies hanging out by rivers (naiads), trees (dryads), or mountains (oreads). In modern terms, it's that girl with the perfect "cottagecore" aesthetic who looks like she talks to birds and lives in an enchanted forest.
usage_notes: A word borrowed from Greek mythology, used in literature and fantasy contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayon sa alamat, isang **nimpa** ang nagbabantay sa ilog na iyon.","translation":"According to legend, a **nymph** guards that river."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang kagandahan ay maihahalintulad sa isang **nimpa** sa gubat.","translation":"Her beauty is comparable to a **nymph** in the forest."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang dalubhasa o siyentista na nag-aaral sa larangan ng haynayan o biyolohiya.
etymology: Mula sa salitang "haynayan" na may hulaping "-on" na nagpapahiwatig ng isang tao na dalubhasa sa isang larangan.
original_explanation: The person who studies 'haynayan'. Sila yung mga nag-aaral ng lahat ng may buhay, from the smallest bacteria to the biggest blue whale. Sila yung legit na 'plantito' at 'plantita' at 'animal lover' with a science degree. The more common term is 'biologist'.
usage_notes: Tulad ng "haynayan", ito ay isang neolohismo at hindi karaniwang ginagamit. "Biyolohista" o "biologist" ang mas madalas marinig.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang kilalang **haynayanon** ang nagbigay ng panayam tungkol sa mga bagong tuklas na specie.","translation":"A famous **biologist** gave a lecture about newly discovered species."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaki at mataas na anyong lupa na karaniwang mas mataas kaysa sa isang burol.
original_explanation: The ultimate destination for your "soul searching" trip after a breakup. It's where you go to hike, shout "walang forever!", and take selfies with the sea of clouds, hoping your ex sees them on Instagram. Also, where your lola warns you not to point at things, or else you'll get cursed by an *engkanto*.
usage_notes: Often used metaphorically to mean a large pile or a huge amount of something, e.g., "bundok ng labahin" (mountain of laundry).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umakyat kami sa **bundok** para makita ang pagsikat ng araw.","translation":"We climbed the **mountain** to see the sunrise."},{"sentence":"Parang **bundok** ang mga problema ko ngayon.","translation":"My problems feel like a **mountain** right now."}]

translation: to lift, to raise, to revolt
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-angat ng isang bagay. Sa malalim na kahulugan, ito ay tumutukoy sa pag-aaklas o paghihimagsik.
original_explanation: From the Spanish 'alzar'. It's literally lifting something heavy, like a sack of rice. But it's more famous for its historical meaning: "Ialsa ang bandera ng pag-aaklas!" It’s the OG “fight the power” verb.
usage_notes: Has both a literal meaning (to lift) and a figurative one (to revolt). The context determines the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ialsa** mo ang kabilang dulo ng mesa.","translation":"**Lift** the other end of the table."},{"sentence":"Panahon na upang **ialsa** ang ating mga boses laban sa katiwalian.","translation":"It is time to **raise** our voices against corruption."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sistema kung saan ang pag-unlad o pagkuha ng pabor ay nakabatay sa impluwensya, koneksyon, o personal na ugnayan sa halip na sa merito o kakayahan.
original_explanation: This is the infamous 'backer system.' When someone gets a promotion not because they're competent, but because the boss is their buddy. It's the art of pulling strings and using connections. 'It doesn't matter if you're not qualified, as long as you have **palakasan**.' It's a national sport, unfortunately.
usage_notes: Carries a strong negative connotation related to corruption and unfairness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laganap ang **palakasan** sa maraming ahensya ng gobyerno.","translation":"**Cronyism** is rampant in many government agencies."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa **palakasan**, hindi nakuha ng mas kwalipikadong aplikante ang trabaho.","translation":"Because of the **patronage system**, the more qualified applicant did not get the job."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan kung saan ang isang bagay ay malapit nang maubos o maglaho nang tuluyan.
original_explanation: 'Yung sahod mo two days after payday. Or 'yung pasensya mo sa ka-team mong ayaw mag-mute sa Zoom call. It's that feeling of "OMG, malapit na!" It's the anxiety of seeing the last piece of chicharon in the bowl.
usage_notes: Often used to describe supplies, patience, or time.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Paubos** na ang bigas kaya kailangan na nating bumili.","translation":"The rice is **running out**, so we need to buy more."},{"sentence":"**Paubos** na ang pasensya ko sa'yo!","translation":"My patience with you is **running out**!"}]

translation: layer; something placed on top; surcharge
meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na inilagay o idinagdag sa ibabaw ng isa pa; sapin. Maaari ring tumukoy sa dagdag na bayarin.
original_explanation: Think of your lasagna, your sans rival, or your 7-layer dip. Each level is a patong. It's also what your mom tells you to do with clothes in cold weather ('Mag-patong ka ng jacket!'). In a more 'adulting' context, it can refer to the extra 'under-the-table' fee or bribe added on top of a legitimate price. The dark side of layering.
usage_notes: The verb form 'magpatong' means 'to place on top of'. The meaning of 'surcharge' or 'bribe' is very common in colloquial speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagyan mo ng isa pang **patong** ng keso ang spaghetti.","translation":"Add another **layer** of cheese to the spaghetti."},{"sentence":"May **patong** daw sa presyo kaya naging mas mahal.","translation":"They said there was a **surcharge** on the price, that's why it became more expensive."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsusuot ng damit, sapatos, o anumang kasuotan upang alamin kung ito ay kasya, bagay, o komportable.
original_explanation: The verb you use in the department store fitting room. 'Wait lang, magsusukat lang ako nito.' It's the process of figuring out if the clothes you saw on the mannequin look as good on you (spoiler: sometimes they don't). It's a crucial step before the ultimate 'add to cart' moment.
usage_notes: Specifically used for trying on apparel or accessories. Often interchangeable with 'isukat'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumunta siya sa fitting room para **magsukat** ng pantalon.","translation":"She went to the fitting room to **try on** a pair of pants."},{"sentence":"Pwede po bang **magsukat** nitong sapatos?","translation":"May I **try on** these shoes?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpapalit o pagsusuot ng damit na naisagawa na.
original_explanation: Past tense of getting dressed. You already did it. You've transformed from your 'pambahay' self to your 'pang-alis' persona. 'Bakit ang tagal mo?' 'Sorry, **nagbihis** lang ako from my work-from-home uniform to my going-out uniform.'
usage_notes: Completed aspect (past tense) of 'magbihis'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos maligo, agad siyang **nagbihis**.","translation":"After showering, he immediately **got dressed**."},{"sentence":"**Nagbihis** ako ng pormal para sa interview.","translation":"I **dressed** formally for the interview."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging walang-bisa, hindi epektibo, o walang legal na kapangyarihan ng isang kasunduan, batas, o gamot.
original_explanation: When your free coupon has expired. When your alibi doesn't work on your mom. When your password reset link is only good for 10 minutes and you clicked it on the 11th. It's basically "Sorry, too late" or "Nice try, but no."
usage_notes: Commonly used in legal, medical, and formal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinahayag ng korte ang **kawalan ng bisa** ng kanilang kasal.","translation":"The court declared the **invalidity** of their marriage."},{"sentence":"Ang **kawalan ng bisa** ng gamot ay dahil sa maling pag-iimbak nito.","translation":"The **ineffectiveness** of the medicine was due to its improper storage."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mataas na ranggong opisyal sa militar, karaniwang mas mataas sa tenyente koronel at mas mababa sa brigadyer heneral.
original_explanation: That high-ranking military uncle or tito in every family reunion who everyone is slightly scared of but also respects. He's the guy who tells stories about discipline while you're trying to get a third serving of lechon. Also, the face of a famous chicken brand.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aming kapitbahay ay isang retiradong **koronel**.","translation":"Our neighbor is a retired **colonel**."},{"sentence":"Inatasan ng **koronel** ang kanyang mga tauhan na maghanda para sa misyon.","translation":"The **colonel** ordered his men to prepare for the mission."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbibigay ng banal na pabor o biyaya, karaniwang isinasagawa ng isang pari o lider ng relihiyon, o paghingi ng pahintulot at gabay mula sa mga nakatatanda.
original_explanation: What you ask from your lola before you leave the house by pressing her hand to your forehead (mano po). Also, the priest sprinkling holy water on your new car, hoping it protects you from crazy bus drivers.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hiningi ng magkasintahan ang **pagbasbas** ng kanilang mga magulang.","translation":"The couple asked for the **blessing** of their parents."},{"sentence":"Naging solemne ang misa dahil sa **pagbasbas** ng obispo.","translation":"The mass became solemn because of the bishop's **benediction**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay o pagbibitay ng mga nilabhang damit sa sampayan upang matuyo. Ito ay nasa aspektong perpektibo.
original_explanation: The ultimate race against the rain clouds. You just finished hanging a week's worth of laundry, and then you feel a drop. That's the panic of someone who just **nagsampay**.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to hanging clothes on a line or rack to dry. Completed aspect of 'magsampay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaga siyang gumising para maglaba at **nagsampay** bago pumasok sa trabaho.","translation":"She woke up early to do laundry and **hung the clothes to dry** before going to work."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **nagsampay** ng basang tuwalya sa upuan?","translation":"Who **hung** the wet towel on the chair?"}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang materyal, tulad ng kahoy o uling, na ginagamit upang makalikha o mapanatili ang apoy. Sa matalinhagang salita, ito ay isang bagay na nagpapasidhi sa isang sitwasyon o damdamin.
original_explanation: Literally, ito yung kahoy at uling para sa inihaw na liempo. Figuratively, ito yung chismis na binubulong mo sa kaibigan mong galit na sa jowa niya. Ikaw ang naglalagay ng 'panggatong' sa apoy ng kanilang away. You're adding fuel to the fire!
usage_notes: Has both a literal (for fire) and a common figurative meaning (to worsen a conflict or situation).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nangunguha sila ng **panggatong** sa bundok para sa kanilang pagluluto.","translation":"They are gathering **firewood** from the mountain for their cooking."},{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang magdagdag ng **panggatong** sa galit niya.","translation":"Don't add any more **fuel** to his anger."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamataas na bahagi o tuktok ng isang bundok, burol, o anumang mataas na bagay.
etymology: Possibly a combination of 'tayog' (height) and 'tugtog' (summit, an older meaning not related to music).
original_explanation: The very top. The 'Sana all' of locations. It's not just 'taas', it's the *pinakamataas*. Think the summit of Mt. Apo, the top floor of the tallest condo in BGC, or the highest rank you can get in Mobile Legends. That's the tayugtog.
usage_notes: This is a very rare or archaic word. 'Tuktok' or 'taluktok' are the common modern equivalents.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iilan lamang ang nakaabot sa **tayugtog** ng bundok.","translation":"Only a few reached the **peak** of the mountain."},{"sentence":"Mula sa **tayugtog**, tanaw ang buong lambak.","translation":"From the **summit**, the entire valley can be seen."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglahok, pakikisali, o panghihimasok sa isang usapan o gawain ng iba.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "maki-" (paglahok) at salitang ugat na "alam" (kaalaman).
original_explanation: What your tita tells you not to do in family business, but also what you MUST do when you see injustice. It's the 'sawsaw' culture. Can be negative (chismosa) or positive (active citizen). The line is thinner than your patience during rush hour traffic on EDSA.
usage_notes: Maaaring magkaroon ng positibo o negatibong konotasyon depende sa konteksto. Ang positibo ay pagiging mulat at pakikisangkot sa isyung panlipunan, habang ang negatibo ay panghihimasok sa pribadong buhay ng iba.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **makialam** sa usapan ng matatanda.","translation":"Don't **meddle** in the adults' conversation."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga para sa mga kabataan na **makialam** sa mga isyu ng bayan.","translation":"It's important for the youth to **get involved** in national issues."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkuha ng isang pagsusulit o eksaminasyon upang sukatin ang kaalaman o kasanayan.
original_explanation: That moment of truth during finals week. 'Sumulit' is what every student does, armed with a ballpen and a prayer. It's the verb form for 'pagsusulit' (exam). Not to be confused with the adjective 'sulit' which means 'worth it'. Taking an exam is rarely 'sulit'.
usage_notes: This verb specifically means to take a test/exam. It is derived from 'pagsusulit' (examination) and is distinct from the adjective 'sulit' (worth it).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong mag-aral nang mabuti dahil **susulit** kami bukas sa Math.","translation":"I need to study well because we will **take a test** in Math tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Lahat ng estudyante sa ika-apat na baitang ay **sumulit** kaninang umaga.","translation":"All fourth-grade students **took a test** this morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang kaganapan o bagay na naganap o nangyari sa isang partikular na oras at lugar.
etymology: Mula sa "pang-" (unlaping pangngalan) + "yayari" (isang anyo ng "yari", na nangangahulugang maganap).
original_explanation: The "what's the chika?" or "what's the tea?". It's the plot point of your life's teleserye. From a simple birthday party to a major historical event, it's the stuff that happens. The "ganap".
usage_notes: Isang napaka-pangkalahatan at karaniwang salita para sa anumang uri ng kaganapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang EDSA Revolution ay isang makasaysayang **pangyayari** sa Pilipinas.","translation":"The EDSA Revolution is a historical **event** in the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Ikuwento mo naman ang mga **pangyayari** sa party kagabi.","translation":"Tell me about the **happenings** at the party last night."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay na itinuturing na walang halaga, sira, o hindi na kailangan at nararapat nang itanggal o iligpit.
original_explanation: The physical representation of your bad decisions from last night's party. Also, what your mom calls the things you 'collect' (read: hoard) in your room. 'Anak, itapon mo na 'yang mga tapon mo!'
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'basura'. The pronunciation stress is on the first syllable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong ihalo ang nabubulok sa di-nabubulok na **tapon**.","translation":"Don't mix the biodegradable with the non-biodegradable **trash**."},{"sentence":"Ang daming **tapon** pagkatapos ng pista.","translation":"There was so much **garbage** after the festival."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pandiwa na tumutukoy sa gawain ng pagtahi o pagdurugtong ng mga bagay gamit ang sinulid at karayom.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "tahi" at hulaping pampandiwa na "-in".
original_explanation: The verb form. Ito yung utos o action na gagawin mo. 'Uy, tahiin mo nga 'tong butas sa medyas ko!' Parang sa work, pag sinabi ng boss mo, 'Tahiin mo na yang mga loose ends sa project,' meaning tapusin at ayusin mo na.
usage_notes: Isang pandiwang nakapokus sa layon (object-focus). Ang bagay na tinatahi ang siyang sentro ng pangungusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **tahiin** ang butas sa aking uniporme.","translation":"I need **to sew** the hole in my uniform."},{"sentence":"Sino ang magaling **tahiin** ang mga gown para sa pageant?","translation":"Who is good at **sewing** the gowns for the pageant?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyon na nagpapahiwatig ng pagtatanong, pagkalito, o hindi paniniwala sa narinig o nakita. Katumbas ng 'Ano?'.
etymology: Likely a shortened, emphatic form of 'Ano?'.
original_explanation: The shorter, more aggressive cousin of 'Ano?'. It's what you say when someone says something so unbelievable or confusing you need them to repeat it with more clarity. 'May utang ka pa sa akin.' 'Han!?' It's a single syllable that carries the weight of 'Are you serious right now?' and 'I dare you to say that again.' It's the Tagalog version of a record scratch.
usage_notes: Purely conversational and informal. The exclamation point is almost mandatory to convey the right tone. Can also be spelled 'Anu!'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Han**! Totoo ba 'yang sinasabi mo?","translation":"**What**?! Is what you're saying true?"},{"sentence":"A: 'Wala na tayong ulam.' B: '**Han**!? Kakabili ko lang kahapon!'","translation":"A: 'We don't have any more food.' B: '**Huh**!? I just bought some yesterday!'"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maikling pagtigil o pahinga sa pagitan ng mga bahagi ng isang dula, konsiyerto, o anumang pagtatanghal.
original_explanation: Ito yung commercial break ng mga live shows. Yung chance mo para mag-CR, bumili ng popcorn, o i-check kung nag-reply na ba si crush. Yung sandaling paghinga bago ka ulit paiyakin ng bida sa second act.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa konteksto ng teatro, pelikula, at iba pang pagtatanghal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-inat-inat muna ako noong **entreakto** ng dula.","translation":"I stretched a bit during the play's **intermission**."},{"sentence":"May sampung minutong **entreakto** bago ang ikalawang bahagi ng konsiyerto.","translation":"There is a ten-minute **intermission** before the second part of the concert."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang taong handang tumanggap ng mga bagong ideya, opinyon, o pananaw na iba sa kanya.
original_explanation: This is your tita who doesn't judge your life choices, your friend who listens to your weirdest theories, or you when you finally try that weird food combo. To be malawak ang isipan is to have a mind that's not a one-way street, but more like EDSA on a good day – open to all possibilities (kahit traffic minsan).
usage_notes: A descriptive phrase used to characterize a person's way of thinking.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating maging **malawak ang isipan** upang maunawaan ang iba't ibang kultura.","translation":"We need to be **open-minded** to understand different cultures."},{"sentence":"Buti pa si Lola, **malawak ang isipan** at hindi mapanghusga.","translation":"It's a good thing Grandma is **open-minded** and not judgmental."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagpapatupad o pagpapatibay sa isang batas, kasunduan, o dokumento upang magkaroon ito ng legal na kapangyarihan o epekto.
etymology: Compound of `pagbibigay` (act of giving) and `bisa` (effect, power, validity).
original_explanation: This is what happens when a law is finally signed and becomes real. It's the "go live" button for rules and regulations. Think of it as activating a power-up: before pagbibigay-bisa, a contract is just a piece of paper; after, it's a legally binding document that can cause you serious headaches if you ignore it.
usage_notes: Often used in legal, bureaucratic, or formal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagbibigay-bisa** sa bagong batas ay magsisimula sa susunod na buwan.","translation":"The **enforcement** of the new law will begin next month."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan pa ng komite ang **pagbibigay-bisa** sa kasunduan.","translation":"The committee is still studying the **validation** of the agreement."}]

translation: to cause to droop or wilt; to cause exhaustion
meaning_filipino: Ang maging sanhi ng pagkalaylay o panghihina ng isang bagay, tulad ng halaman, o ng isang tao dahil sa pagod o sakit.
original_explanation: This is what the summer heat does to plants and people. It's that feeling after a long commute on EDSA, or after a whole day of meetings that could have been an email. You feel drained, weak, and just want to lie down. That's being 'pinalupaypay'. The verb is to cause that state.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for plants and figuratively for people's energy or spirit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang matinding sikat ng araw ay **nagpapalupaypay** sa mga halaman.","translation":"The intense heat of the sun **causes the plants to wilt**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong magtrabaho, baka **magpalupaypay** iyan sa iyo.","translation":"Don't work too much, that might **cause you to become exhausted**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng unti-unting pagbabago at pag-unlad ng mga anyo ng buhay sa paglipas ng mahabang panahon, mula sa mas simpleng anyo patungo sa mas kumplikadong anyo.
original_explanation: Parang career path mo. Nagsimula ka as a fresh grad na takot sa lahat, tapos after several years, naging senior ka na na may sariling 'theory of survival' sa office politics. It's the slow, painful, but ultimately amazing process of change. Darwin would be proud of your glow-up.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa konteksto ng agham, teknolohiya, at panlipunang pag-unlad.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan sa biyolohiya ang teorya ng **ebolusyon** ni Charles Darwin.","translation":"In biology, Charles Darwin's theory of **evolution** is studied."},{"sentence":"Ang **ebolusyon** ng teknolohiya ay napakabilis sa modernong panahon.","translation":"The **evolution** of technology is very fast in the modern era."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ahensya ng pamahalaan na responsable sa pangongolekta ng mga buwis (taripa) sa mga inaangkat at iniluluwas na kalakal, at sa pagkontrol ng mga produkto na pumapasok at lumalabas sa bansa.
original_explanation: The place your Shopee/Amazon package from overseas goes to die... or at least gets stuck for a few weeks. It's the government office (Bureau of Customs) you have to deal with and pay taxes to before you can get your imported goods. The final boss level for online shoppers.
usage_notes: Refers to the Bureau of Customs (BOC) or the concept of customs itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naiipit pa sa **adwana** ang inorder kong libro mula sa ibang bansa.","translation":"The book I ordered from abroad is still stuck at **customs**."},{"sentence":"Kailangang magbayad ng malaking buwis sa **adwana** para sa mga imported na sasakyan.","translation":"You need to pay a large tax at **customs** for imported cars."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong may matinding pagkahumaling sa anime, manga, at kulturang popular ng Hapon.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Hapon na 'otaku' (おたく), isang pormal na termino para sa 'iyong bahay', na naging tawag para sa mga panatikong tagahanga.
original_explanation: Someone whose diet consists of instant ramen, pocky, and the tears of their favorite anime characters. They can probably name more Japanese voice actors than Filipino politicians. Their natural habitat is a comic convention or a room filled with anime figures and wall scrolls.
usage_notes: Isang pandaigdigang termino na ganap na tinanggap sa kultura ng kabataang Pilipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isa siyang certified **otaku** at kumpleto ang kanyang koleksyon ng manga.","translation":"He is a certified **otaku** and his manga collection is complete."},{"sentence":"Pumunta ang mga **otaku** sa convention para makita ang kanilang mga paboritong cosplayer.","translation":"The **otaku** went to the convention to see their favorite cosplayers."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang serye ng mga hakbang o tuntunin na sinusunod upang malutas ang isang problema o makumpleto ang isang gawain, lalo na sa larangan ng kompyuter.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung dahilan kung bakit puro pusa, K-drama, o food vlogs ang laman ng feed mo. The algorithm knows you better than your jowa. It's the secret recipe of social media apps para ma-hook ka.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa mga kontekstong teknikal at akademiko. Ang baybay na 'algoritmo' ay umiiral din ngunit mas karaniwan ang paggamit ng salitang Ingles sa mga usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng mga inhinyero ang bagong **algorithm** para sa search engine.","translation":"The engineers are studying the new **algorithm** for the search engine."},{"sentence":"Nagbago na naman ang **algorithm** ng Facebook, kaya bumaba ang reach ng posts ko.","translation":"The Facebook **algorithm** changed again, that's why the reach of my posts decreased."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o pook na may aplaya; isang baybaying-dagat na pamayanan.
original_explanation: This is the '-an' suffix in action, turning 'aplaya' (beach) into a place *of* beaches. Think of it as the whole district or barangay name, like 'Brgy. Aplayan.' It's not just the sand, it's the whole coastal 'hood.
usage_notes: More commonly used as a proper noun for a place name than as a generic noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming mangingisda ang nakatira sa **Aplayan**.","translation":"Many fishermen live in the **coastal area**."}]

translation: to scratch or dig with paws/claws; to rummage
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggamit ng mga kuko o paa upang maghukay o maghalungkat sa lupa, buhangin, o anumang bunton ng bagay.
original_explanation: This is what your dog does to your garden bed when it's trying to bury a bone, or what a chicken does in the yard looking for worms. It can also mean you, rummaging through your messy closet (nagkaykay ng damit) looking for that one specific t-shirt.
usage_notes: Can be used for animals digging with their paws or humans rummaging messily through a pile of things.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig **magkaykay** ng lupa ang aso namin sa likod-bahay.","translation":"Our dog loves **to dig** the soil in our backyard."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magkaykay** diyan sa bunton ng mga lumang gamit.","translation":"Don't **rummage** through that pile of old things."}]

translation: to be able to feel; to sense
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang maranasan o mapansin ang isang pisikal o emosyonal na sensasyon.
original_explanation: 'Yung moment na bigla kang kinabahan kahit wala namang dahilan? Naka-makaramdam ka ng "bad vibes". O kaya 'yung finally, after a long day sa office, nakaupo ka na at doon mo lang naramdaman lahat ng pagod. It's that ability to feel something, whether it's kilig from a crush's message or the pain of stepping on a Lego brick.
usage_notes: The prefix "maka-" here indicates ability or potential. "Nakaramdam" is the past tense (felt), "nakakaramdam" is the present tense (feeling).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **makaramdam** ka man lang ng kaunting hiya sa ginawa mo.","translation":"I hope you could **feel** even a little bit of shame for what you did."},{"sentence":"Hindi ako **makaramdam** ng lamig dahil sa makapal kong dyaket.","translation":"I can't **feel** the cold because of my thick jacket."}]

translation: to excuse; to make allowances for; to pardon
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng kapatawaran, pag-unawa, o pagpapahintulot sa pagkukulang, pagkakamali, o kamalian ng isang tao.
etymology: From `pag-` + `paumanhin` + `-an`. `Paumanhin` itself is a formal word for 'pardon' or 'apology'.
original_explanation: This is the super formal, almost poetic way of saying "pasensya na" or "patawarin mo ako." You use this when you've committed a major blunder, like accidentally deleting your boss's presentation. It’s the verbal equivalent of a deep bow. "Pagpaumanhinan ninyo ang aking kapangahasan" sounds way more dramatic than "Sorry, ang kulit ko."
usage_notes: Very formal and literary. Rarely used in casual conversation. It's the kind of word you'd find in a formal letter of apology or in historical fiction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pagpaumanhinan** ninyo ang aking biglaang pag-alis.","translation":"**Please excuse** my sudden departure."},{"sentence":"Sana ay **pagpaumanhinan** mo ang aking mga pagkukulang.","translation":"I hope you can **make allowances for** my shortcomings."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi tuwid o pantay; nakahilig o nakakiling sa isang panig.
original_explanation: It’s that picture frame on the wall that's just a little bit off, triggering your OCD. It’s how your glasses sit after you fall asleep with them on. It's the state of your sanity after a long week of deadlines. Basically, anything that isn't straight.
usage_notes: Describes physical orientation. Can be used metaphorically for something unfair (see 'tabingan'), but its primary meaning is physical.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tabingi** ang pagkakalagay ng salamin sa pader.","translation":"The mirror on the wall is placed **crookedly**."},{"sentence":"Natawa ako dahil **tabingi** ang suot niyang sombrero.","translation":"I laughed because the hat he was wearing was **tilted**."}]

translation: to be able to measure by handspan
meaning_filipino: Masukat sa pamamagitan ng dangkal (ang sukat mula sa dulo ng hinlalaki hanggang sa dulo ng hintuturo o kalingkingan kapag nakaunat).
original_explanation: The OG Filipino measurement system before tape measures were a thing. This is how your lola checks if the fish is big enough at the palengke, or how you estimate if the new TV will fit on the console. 'Kaya mo bang madangkal 'yan?' (Can you measure that with your handspan?)
usage_notes: Isang pandiwang pangkakayahan na nagpapahiwatig ng kakayahang sumukat gamit ang dangkal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko **madangkal** ang lapad ng mesa dahil masyadong malaki.","translation":"I can't **measure the width of the table by handspan** because it's too big."},{"sentence":"Subukan mong **madangkal** kung ilang dangkal ang haba ng aklat na iyan.","translation":"Try **to measure by handspan** how many handspans long that book is."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kulisap na kumakain ng kahoy at may kakayahang sumira sa mga istrukturang gawa sa materyales na ito.
original_explanation: That silent little destroyer that eats your house from the inside out. Also a perfect metaphor for that 'friend' who slowly ruins your reputation with backstabbing comments. 'Uy, parang may anay sa relationship niyo, unti-unting nasisira.'
usage_notes: Can be used metaphorically to refer to a traitor or something that causes slow, internal destruction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinain ng **anay** ang mga haligi ng lumang bahay.","translation":"The **termites** ate the posts of the old house."},{"sentence":"Siya ang **anay** sa aming grupo na nagkalat ng mga sikreto.","translation":"He was the **traitor (termite)** in our group who spread secrets."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lubusang paglipol, pagwasak, o pagpatay sa isang grupo ng mga bagay, hayop, o tao.
original_explanation: This is what you want to do to the ipis population in your kitchen. It's not just killing one; it's wiping out the entire clan. Mamuksa is total annihilation, the final boss level of "pumatay". Think Thanos snap, but for pests, enemies, or corruption.
usage_notes: A very strong word implying total destruction or eradication.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **mamuksa** ng mga peste sa ating mga pananim.","translation":"We need to **exterminate** the pests in our crops."},{"sentence":"Ang layunin ng bagong programa ay **mamuksa** sa katiwalian sa gobyerno.","translation":"The new program's goal is to **annihilate** corruption in the government."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng manipis at may maliliit na butas na tela na isinasabit sa ibabaw ng higaan upang magsilbing proteksyon laban sa kagat ng lamok at iba pang insekto habang natutulog.
original_explanation: The original, low-tech anti-dengue device. Before Off! lotion and plug-in katol, there was the kulambuan. It's that net canopy you sleep under that makes you feel like royalty but also sometimes traps the one mosquito you were trying to avoid inside with you. Classic probinsya life.
usage_notes: 'Kulambo' is the more common term, but 'kulambuan' is also widely used and understood, sometimes implying a grander or more permanent setup.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkabit ka ng **kulambuan** para hindi ka makagat ng lamok.","translation":"Put up the **mosquito net** so you won't get bitten by mosquitoes."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang bagay na may malaking sukat mula sa isang gilid patungo sa kabila.
original_explanation: Describes your new widescreen monitor, the smile on your face on payday, or your 'noo' (forehead) according to your teasing friends. 'Ang **lapad** ng ngiti mo, ah!'
usage_notes: Often intensified as 'malapad'. The opposite is 'makitid' or 'makipot' (narrow).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **lapad** ng kalsada kaya mabilis ang daloy ng trapiko.","translation":"The road is **wide** so the flow of traffic is fast."},{"sentence":"Mayroon siyang **lapad** na noo.","translation":"He/She has a **broad** forehead."}]

translation: to charm, to fascinate, to enchant
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-akit o paghalina sa isang tao upang makuha ang atensyon o paghanga nito.
original_explanation: The active verb form. This is you, on your A-game, trying to capture someone's attention. It's the effort you put in—the witty banter, the perfect OOTD, the strategic IG story reply—all to make someone go, "Wow, sino 'to?" You're not just existing; you're actively casting the spell.
usage_notes: A transitive verb. "Bighaniin mo siya" (Charm him/her).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang **bighaniin** ang madla sa kanyang talumpati.","translation":"He is trying to **captivate** the audience with his speech."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpapaloko sa mga taong susubukang **bighaniin** ka para sa kanilang pansariling interes.","translation":"Don't be fooled by people who will try to **charm** you for their own self-interest."}]

translation: to side with; to ally with
meaning_filipino: Pumanig o sumama sa isang grupo o indibidwal; maging kaalyado.
original_explanation: This is what you do when there's "tea" or "chismis" and you have to pick a side. Are you Team A or Team B? In a group project, you makikampi with the person who actually does the work. In office politics, choosing who to makikampi with can make or break your career.
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of conflict, debate, or choosing allegiances.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa halip na **makikampi** sa isa, sinubukan niyang maging tagapamagitan.","translation":"Instead of **siding with** one, he tried to be the mediator."},{"sentence":"Pinili niyang **makikampi** sa mga naapi.","translation":"He chose to **ally with** the oppressed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbigkas ng mga salita ng isang awit sa isang partikular na tono at ritmo; ang pag-awit ng isang partikular na komposisyon.
original_explanation: The verb form of your go-to videoke move. When someone asks you, "Ano'ng kantahin mo?" they're asking for your signature song. It's the action of turning your hugot into a performance.
usage_notes: The object of the verb is the song being sung. Contrast with 'kumanta' (to sing, general) and 'kantahan' (to sing for someone).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **kantahin** mo ang \"Bakit Ngayon Ka Lang?\".","translation":"Please, **sing** \"Bakit Ngayon Ka Lang?\"."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **kantahin** ang mga matataas na nota sa awiting iyon.","translation":"It's difficult **to sing** the high notes in that song."}]

translation: the state of being that way; circumstance
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o sitwasyon ng pagiging ganoon o sa ganoong paraan.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'it is what it is.' It's a slightly formal way of saying 'the way things are' or 'because it's like that.' When your tita asks why you're still single, and you just shrug and say, 'Sa pagkakagayon ng buhay...' (With the way life is...), you're using this word perfectly. It's a philosophical mic drop.
usage_notes: Often used in more formal or literary contexts to refer to a state of affairs or a particular circumstance. It's related to 'ganoon' but in a noun form describing the state of being 'like that'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa **pagkakagayon**, wala na tayong magagawa kundi maghintay.","translation":"Because of **the way things are**, we can do nothing but wait."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkakagayon** ng mga pangyayari ay hindi inaasahan ng lahat.","translation":"The **circumstance** of the events was not expected by everyone."}]

translation: to be snagged; to get caught on; to be implicated
meaning_filipino: Hindi sinasadyang maikabit o makabit sa isang bagay; madawit o masangkot sa isang usapin o gulo.
etymology: From `ma-` (involuntary action prefix) + `sabit` (to hang, to get caught).
original_explanation: That feeling when your earphones get caught on a doorknob and get yanked out of your ears? That's `masabit`. It's also what happens to your friend who gets dragged into your mess just by being there. 'Huwag kang didikit sa akin, baka **masabit** ka sa utang ko.' (Don't stick with me, you might get **implicated** in my debts.)
usage_notes: Can be physical (snagging clothes) or figurative (being implicated in a problem).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingat ka, baka **masabit** ang damit mo sa nakausling pako.","translation":"Be careful, your clothes might get **snagged** on the protruding nail."},{"sentence":"Ayaw kong **masabit** sa gulo ng mag-asawa.","translation":"I don't want to get **involved/implicated** in the couple's fight."}]

translation: to treat (someone in a certain way)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita ng isang partikular na pag-uugali o pakikitungo sa isang tao, hayop, o bagay.
original_explanation: How you deal with people. Whether you magtrato your officemate to lunch (to treat them to a meal) or you magtrato someone badly (pakikitungo). It's all about the vibe you give. Remember the Golden Rule: 'Wag mong gawin sa iba ang ayaw mong gawin sa'yo. So, 'wag kang magtrato ng iba na parang basahan.
usage_notes: Can mean 'to treat' in the sense of behavior (e.g., treat someone well) or 'to treat' in the sense of paying for something for someone (e.g., I'll treat you to coffee). Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat mong **magtrato** nang may respeto sa mga nakakatanda.","translation":"You should **treat** elders with respect."},{"sentence":"Sige na, ako na ang **magtratrato** sa iyo ng sine.","translation":"Alright, I'll be the one to **treat** you to the movies."}]

translation: to be able to squeeze in; to be jostled
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng pagkakataong makasingit o makisiksik sa isang masikip na lugar; o maranasan ang magitgit ng iba.
original_explanation: The daily struggle of a commuter in the MRT during rush hour. Yung kailangan mong maging ninja para lang makagitgit papasok ng pinto bago ito magsara. It can also mean being jostled or pushed aside in a crowd.
usage_notes: Can be used actively (to be able to squeeze in) or passively (to be squeezed/jostled). The passive sense is common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **makagitgit** sa unahan para makita ang parada.","translation":"He tried to **squeeze in** to the front to see the parade."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa Divisoria at baka ka **makagitgit** ng mga tao.","translation":"Be careful in Divisoria as you might **be jostled** by the people."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging matulungin, mapagbigay, at may mabuting kalooban sa kapwa nang walang hinihintay na kapalit.
etymology: From `kagandahan` (beauty) + `loob` (inner self), literally 'beauty of the inner self'.
original_explanation: This is the 'libre-pancit-canton-sa-opisina' kind of kindness. It's helping someone without expecting anything in return, like when a stranger helps you pick up the coins you dropped or when your friend treats you to coffee just because. It’s the core of 'pakikipagkapwa-tao,' the pure, no-strings-attached goodness from the heart.
usage_notes: Differentiated from 'utang na loob', which involves a debt of gratitude. Kagandahang-loob is a pure act of giving.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko malilimutan ang **kagandahang-loob** na ipinakita mo sa aming pamilya.","translation":"I will never forget the **kindness** you showed our family."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **kagandahang-loob**, marami ang nagmamahal sa kanya.","translation":"Because of her **benevolence**, many people love her."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang bagay na may galaw o anyong parang alon; umaalon-alon o paikid-ikid.
original_explanation: Yung buhok mo after mag-beach, "beach waves" kung tawagin. O 'yung itsura ng bubong na yero pagkatapos ng malakas na bagyo. Pwede ring 'yung takbo ng buhay, minsan nasa taas, minsan nasa baba.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan ng hugis o galaw na kahawig ng mga alon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto niya ang **alun-alon** na buhok.","translation":"She likes **wavy** hair."},{"sentence":"Ang daan paakyat ng bundok ay **alun-alon**.","translation":"The road going up the mountain is **undulating**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan inililibing ang mga yumao; sementeryo o libingan.
etymology: From Spanish `pavimento` (pavement) or `monumento` (monument), which evolved into a local term for a tomb, then `pamentuhan` as a place of tombs.
original_explanation: The final resting place. The OG subdivision for those who have passed on. It's where you visit your ancestors during Undas, light some candles, and maybe have a mini-reunion with relatives you only see once a year. Medyo creepy sa gabi, pero during the day, it's surprisingly peaceful.
usage_notes: A more formal or slightly dated term for "sementeryo."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dadalaw kami sa **pamentuhan** sa Araw ng mga Patay.","translation":"We will visit the **cemetery** on the Day of the Dead."},{"sentence":"Malinis at maayos ang bagong **pamentuhan** sa aming bayan.","translation":"The new **cemetery** in our town is clean and orderly."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng dagat kung saan ang tubig ay nasa pinakamababang antas nito; ang kabaligtaran ng taog o high tide.
original_explanation: The opposite of high tide. This is when the sea pulls back and you can walk farther out on the beach, discovering starfish, sea shells, and sometimes, someone's lost tsinelas. Perfect time for "pangangapa" or looking for shellfish.
usage_notes: Pronunciation is key to distinguish this from "kati" (itch). Here, the stress is on the first syllable: /KA-ti/. The opposite is "taog" or "lakas-tubig".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maganda mamasyal sa dalampasigan kapag **kati** ang dagat.","translation":"It's nice to stroll on the shore during **low tide**."},{"sentence":"Hihintayin natin na maging **kati** bago tayo manghuli ng alimango.","translation":"We will wait for the **low tide** before we catch crabs."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng salamin o ibang transparent na materyal na may kurbadong gilid, na ginagamit upang palakihin o paliitin ang mga imahe, tulad ng sa salamin sa mata, kamera, o teleskopyo.
original_explanation: Yung salamin sa eyeglasses mo na lumalabo kapag kumakain ka ng mainit na sabaw. O yung mahal na part ng DSLR mo na pinag-iipunan mo para sa mas 'aesthetic' na shots. Sa chismis, ito yung 'pananaw' o 'perspective' ng isang tao. 'Sa lente ng mga Marites...'
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa lente ng kamera, salamin sa mata, mikroskopyo, at iba pa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko nang magpalit ng **lente** ng aking salamin dahil lumabo na ang mata ko.","translation":"I need to change the **lens** of my glasses because my vision has worsened."},{"sentence":"Magkano ang telephoto na **lente** para sa kamerang ito?","translation":"How much is the telephoto **lens** for this camera?"}]

meaning_filipino: Nagdudulot ng kabutihan, kapakinabangan, o positibong epekto.
original_explanation: This is your mom's favorite word. 'Anak, kumain ka ng gulay, nakabubuti 'yan sa katawan.' 'Mag-aral ka, nakabubuti 'yan sa future mo.' It's anything that results in a good outcome. It's the opposite of anything that's 'nakakasama'. Think of it as the +1 to your life's stats.
usage_notes: Often used in giving advice or stating a beneficial fact. Can function as a verb-like adjective.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang regular na ehersisyo ay **nakabubuti** sa kalusugan.","translation":"Regular exercise **is good for** one's health."},{"sentence":"Naniniwala siyang **nakabubuti** ang pagpapatawad para sa kapayapaan ng isip.","translation":"She believes that forgiveness **is beneficial** for peace of mind."}]

meaning_filipino: Panghalip panao na tumutukoy sa isang taong kinakausap. Ito ay ginagamit bilang simuno ng pangungusap.
original_explanation: The most important word in any "hugot" line, right after "ako." As in, "Ikaw na lang ang kulang." Or when your mom is looking for a culprit, points a finger around the room, and it lands on... YOU.
usage_notes: 'Ikaw' is the nominative or ang-case pronoun for 'you' (singular). It's used as the subject of the sentence. Its counterpart in the genitive/ergative (ng-case) is 'mo' and in the oblique (sa-case) is 'iyo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ikaw** ang nagwagi sa patimpalak.","translation":"**You** are the winner of the contest."},{"sentence":"Bakit **ikaw** ang laging napagbibintangan?","translation":"Why are **you** always the one being accused?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkaramdam ng panghihina o kakulangan ng lakas dahil sa pisikal o mental na gawain.
original_explanation: The national feeling of the Filipino workforce, especially on a Friday after a week of OT. It's that feeling when you just want to lie down and not move until the next billing cycle. Can be physical (from exercise), mental (from adulting), or emotional (from a toxic relationship).
usage_notes: Can function as an adjective ('Pagod ako') or a noun ('ang pagod ko') referring to the state of fatigue.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nararamdaman ko ang **pagod** pagkatapos ng mahabang araw sa opisina.","translation":"I feel the **fatigue** after a long day at the office."},{"sentence":"**Pagod** na **pagod** na ako sa traffic sa EDSA.","translation":"I'm so very **tired** of the traffic on EDSA."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang anyong panghinaharap ng pandiwang 'magsuot'. Tumutukoy sa kilos ng paglalagay ng kasuotan sa katawan na isasagawa pa lamang.
original_explanation: This is the "planning phase" verb for your OOTD. When your friend asks, "Anong isusuot mo?" they're asking what you magsusuot. It’s all about future fashion choices, from a simple t-shirt to a full-on Filipiniana gown.
usage_notes: This is the future tense of the verb 'magsuot'. The infinitive form, 'magsuot', is the main dictionary entry.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magsusuot** ako ng barong sa kasal mo.","translation":"I **will wear** a barong to your wedding."},{"sentence":"Ano ang **magsusuot** mo para sa Pasko?","translation":"What **will you wear** for Christmas?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pandiwa na nangangahulugang tiyakin, siguruhin, o alamin nang may katiyakan ang isang bagay.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "siyerto" (mula sa Espanyol na "cierto" na nangangahulugang 'tiyak' o 'sigurado') at hulaping "-hin".
original_explanation: This is your mom's favorite verb before you leave the house: "Siyertuhin mong nakasara ang pinto!" It's the official word for "double-checking" or "making sure" your crush is single before you make a move. In the BPO world, it's what you do before escalating a ticket: "Siyertuhin mo muna ang details, bes."
usage_notes: Ginagamit bilang utos o pakiusap upang tiyakin ang isang bagay. Ang mga kasingkahulugan nitong "siguruhin" at "tiyakin" ay mas karaniwan sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Siyertuhin** mo na dala mo ang lahat ng kailangan mo bago umalis.","translation":"**Make sure** you have everything you need before leaving."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **siyertuhin** ang petsa ng ating pagpupulong.","translation":"We need to **ascertain** the date of our meeting."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtira o pag-okupa sa isang lugar bilang tahanan; maaari ring tumukoy sa mismong lugar kung saan naninirahan.
etymology: From pan- + tirahan, with reduplication of the first syllable of the root word.
original_explanation: Your "address" when you're filling up a government form. It's where you live, sleep, and probably hoard things you bought online. It's your home base, your sanctuary, the place you tell the Grab driver to drop you off.
usage_notes: More formal than 'bahay' (house) or 'tahanan' (home). Often used in legal or official contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang permanenteng **paninirahan** ay nasa probinsya ng Cebu.","translation":"His permanent **residence** is in the province of Cebu."},{"sentence":"Ang gastos sa **paninirahan** sa siyudad ay napakamahal.","translation":"The cost of **dwelling** in the city is very expensive."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na naninirahan o nagmula sa isang urbanong lugar o siyudad.
original_explanation: The opposite of a 'probinsyano/probinsyana'. They're used to the 24/7 hustle, the traffic, the pollution, and having a convenience store on every corner. They probably can't survive without a good data plan and know all the shortcuts on Waze.
usage_notes: Often used to create a contrast with 'taganayon' or 'tagaprobinsya'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bilang isang **tagalunsod**, sanay na ako sa ingay at mabilis na takbo ng buhay.","translation":"As a **city dweller**, I'm used to the noise and the fast pace of life."},{"sentence":"Makikita mo ang pagkakaiba ng pamumuhay ng **tagalunsod** at taganayon.","translation":"You can see the difference in the lifestyle of a **city dweller** and a villager."}]

translation: to form a group; to group together
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbuo ng isang lupon o grupo ng mga tao na may iisang layunin o gawain.
original_explanation: This is what your teacher tells you to do for a group project, which is code for "one person does all the work, and the rest just pay for the printing." It's the "Avengers, assemble!" moment for school reports or team building activities.
usage_notes: Used in contexts like school, work, or community organizing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magpangkat** upang mas mapadali ang gawain.","translation":"We need to **form a group** to make the task easier."},{"sentence":"**Nagpangkat** ang mga estudyante ayon sa kanilang napiling paksa.","translation":"The students **grouped together** according to their chosen topic."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maging katulad o kapareho ng isang tao, bagay, o sitwasyon; ang gumaya sa gawi o katangian ng iba.
original_explanation: Sabi ng nanay mo, "Huwag kang sasama diyan, baka **matulad** ka sa kanila!" It's the classic parental warning against bad influence. You don't want to copy-paste someone else's bad life choices. It's the fear of becoming a 'bad copy'.
usage_notes: Often used in a cautionary or comparative sense. The person or thing being imitated is usually introduced by 'sa' (e.g., 'matulad sa kanya').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw kong **matulad** sa mga taong sumusuko agad sa kanilang pangarap.","translation":"I don't want **to become like** the people who give up easily on their dreams."},{"sentence":"Pinagsabihan niya ang anak na huwag **matulad** sa mga batang kalye.","translation":"She advised her child not **to imitate** the street children."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglilinis ng isang bagay, lalo na sa pamamagitan ng kemikal, upang sirain ang mga bakterya at iba pang mikroorganismo na maaaring magdulot ng sakit.
original_explanation: The official term for what everyone became an expert in during the pandemic. It's the act of spraying everything with alcohol or Lysol—your hands, your groceries, your online shopping deliveries. It's the "new normal" ritual of waging war against germs. The verb form is "disimpektahin".
usage_notes: Isang teknikal na termino na naging pang-araw-araw na salita dahil sa mga isyung pangkalusugan tulad ng pandemya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang regular na **disimpeksyon** ng mga pampublikong lugar upang maiwasan ang pagkalat ng sakit.","translation":"Regular **disinfection** of public places is important to prevent the spread of disease."},{"sentence":"Nag-iskedyul ang opisina ng lingguhang **disimpeksyon**.","translation":"The office scheduled a weekly **disinfection**."}]

translation: to object; to oppose; to protest
meaning_filipino: Ipahayag ang hindi pagsang-ayon o pagtutol sa isang mungkahi, desisyon, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is your 'Objection, Your Honor!' moment. It's what you do when your friends want to eat at Jollibee but you're craving McDo. Or on a more serious note, what activists do when they disagree with a government policy. To 'itutol' is to make your disagreement known.
usage_notes: Often used in formal, legal, or political contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May karapatan kang **itutol** ang anumang desisyon na sa tingin mo ay hindi makatarungan.","translation":"You have the right to **object** to any decision that you think is unjust."},{"sentence":"**Itinutol** ng mga residente ang planong pagpapatayo ng pabrika sa kanilang lugar.","translation":"The residents **protested** the plan to build a factory in their area."}]

meaning_filipino: Paulit-ulit na pagtayo nang walang malinaw na dahilan o patutunguhan; pag-aaksaya ng oras sa pagtayo-tayo lamang.
etymology: From reduplication of tindig with the pa- prefix, indicating a casual or repeated action.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa ng guard sa mall, o 'yung tambay sa kanto. You're just standing there, maybe shifting your weight, looking around, not really doing anything productive. "Bakit ka **patindig-tindig** lang diyan? Tulungan mo ako dito!" is what your mom yells when she sees you being useless.
usage_notes: Carries a slightly negative connotation of aimlessness or wasting time.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Imbes na magtrabaho, **patindig-tindig** lang siya sa labas buong araw.","translation":"Instead of working, he was just **loitering** outside all day."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko siyang **patindig-tindig** sa may kanto, tila may hinihintay.","translation":"I saw him **standing intermittently** at the corner, seemingly waiting for someone."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang utos o pakiusap na siyasatin o pag-aralan nang husto at maigi ang isang bagay, ideya, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: This is what your boss tells you when they want you to check a report for the 10th time. 'Pakasuriin mo 'yan,' means 'I want you to go full Sherlock Holmes on this spreadsheet, find every mistake, and don't talk to me until it's perfect.' It's analysis on beast mode.
usage_notes: The `paka-` prefix intensifies the action of the root word, implying a very deep and thorough examination.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **pakasuriin** ang bawat detalye ng kontrata bago pumirma.","translation":"Every detail of the contract needs **to be examined thoroughly** before signing."},{"sentence":"**Pakasuriin** mo ang kanyang mga sinabi; baka may iba siyang ibig sabihin.","translation":"**Analyze** what he said **very carefully**; he might have a different meaning."}]

meaning_filipino: May kakayahang magbalik ng alaala o magpaalala sa isang tao tungkol sa isang bagay, pangyayari, o karanasan.
original_explanation: Like how the smell of floor wax is nakapagpapagunita of your elementary school days. Or how a certain song on Spotify suddenly reminds you of a past 'sana all' moment or a 'what if'. It's a trigger for a "Throwback Thursday" moment in your brain.
usage_notes: Describes something that causes one to remember or reminisce.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lumang litratong ito ay **nakapagpapagunita** ng ating kabataan.","translation":"This old photograph **serves as a reminder** of our youth."},{"sentence":"Ang kantang iyan ay **nakapagpapagunita** sa akin ng aking lola.","translation":"That song is **reminiscent** for me of my grandmother."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na anyo ng salitang "hintay"; ang kilos ng pananatili sa isang lugar o pag-antala ng gawain hanggang sa dumating ang isang tao o mangyari ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: The shorter, more impatient version of "hintay." This is what you text your friend who's always "on the way" but is probably still in the shower. "'Tol, intay lang, 5 minutes!" (Narrator: It was not 5 minutes). It's the official word for Filipino time-induced anxiety.
usage_notes: Lubos na kolokyal at karaniwang ginagamit sa pasalitang pakikipag-usap o impormal na pagsulat. Ang pormal na anyo ay "hintay".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Intay** ka lang diyan, parating na ako.","translation":"Just **wait** there, I'm on my way."},{"sentence":"Mag-**intay** tayo ng jeep sa kanto.","translation":"Let's **wait** for a jeepney at the corner."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang posisyon ng paghiga na ang tiyan at mukha ay nakaharap sa ibaba.
original_explanation: The official sleeping position after a long, tiring day at work or a heavy meal. It’s also the position you're in when you trip and fall flat on your face in public. The opposite is 'nakatihaya' (lying face up). When you're too tired to even move, you're just nakadapa on your bed, scrolling through your phone.
usage_notes: Describes a specific body position.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natagpuan siyang **nakadapa** sa sahig, mahimbing na natutulog.","translation":"He was found **lying face down** on the floor, fast asleep."},{"sentence":"Mas komportable akong matulog nang **nakadapa**.","translation":"I am more comfortable sleeping while **lying face down**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na sumasailalim sa pagsasanay para sa isang partikular na trabaho o kasanayan.
original_explanation: The BPO industry's "Padawan." You're fresh, hopeful, and probably still figuring out the coffee machine. You spend your days in training rooms, drowning in modules and mock calls, fueled by the dream of finally getting out of "nesting" and onto the production floor. Basically, you're an "intern" with a headset.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng trabaho, lalo na sa mga opisina at call center.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bilang isang **trainee**, kailangan niyang matutunan ang lahat ng proseso ng kumpanya.","translation":"As a **trainee**, he/she needs to learn all the company's processes."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paniningil o pagkuha ng bayad, utang, o anumang kontribusyon.
original_explanation: The opposite of fun. Ito yung pagdating ng bill collector, yung 'ambagan para sa handaan,' o yung paghahabol sa kaibigan mong may utang. Pag narinig mo'to sa opisina, it's either for the coffee fund or the paluwagan.
usage_notes: Very common in financial, business, and informal group contribution contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing Biyernes ang **koleksyon** para sa upa.","translation":"The rent **collection** is every Friday."},{"sentence":"Mahina ang **koleksyon** ng tindahan ngayong araw.","translation":"The store's **collection** (of earnings) is low today."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pakikipagtunggali, pakikipaglaban, o pagharap sa isang hamon sa hinaharap.
