original_explanation: This is the future tense of 'laban' (fight) and the battle cry of every Filipino in a competition, from a basketball game to a beauty pageant ('PILIPINAS, **LALABAN** TAYO!'). It's the promise you make to yourself when you see the long queue at the MRT: '**Lalaban** ako.' (I will fight/endure). It’s a vow of resilience, grit, and hope.
usage_notes: The future tense of the verb 'lumaban'. It signifies an intention or certainty to engage in a struggle or competition.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit anong mangyari, **lalaban** ako para sa aking mga pangarap.","translation":"Whatever happens, I **will fight** for my dreams."},{"sentence":"Sinabi ng koponan na sila ay **lalaban** hanggang sa huling segundo ng laro.","translation":"The team said they **will fight** until the last second of the game."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga bagay na kinuha o sinamsam nang sapilitan, karaniwan sa panahon ng digmaan, kaguluhan, o operasyon ng awtoridad.
original_explanation: This is the stuff you get when you seize things, legally or illegally. Think of a police raid where they haul off evidence—that's 'samsam'. Or, on a lighter note, the office supplies you 'confiscate' from the supply room for your 'home office'. Shhh.
usage_notes: Ang pandiwang "samsamin" (to confiscate) ay mas karaniwang ginagamit kaysa sa pangngalan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ibinenta sa palengke ang mga **samsam** mula sa operasyon.","translation":"The **confiscated goods** from the operation were sold in the market."},{"sentence":"Itinago ng mga pirata ang kanilang **samsam** sa isang kuweba.","translation":"The pirates hid their **loot** in a cave."}]

translation: about to get up, on the way up
meaning_filipino: Nasa akto ng pagtindig mula sa pagkakaupo o pagkakahiga; nasa proseso ng pag-angat o pag-unlad.
original_explanation: That moment when you're still in bed, scrolling through your phone, pabangon pa lang. You're not fully up, but you're not fully lying down either. It can also be used for a business or a career: "Pabangon pa lang ang negosyo ko after the pandemic." It's the state of "getting there."
usage_notes: Describes a state of rising, either literally from a seat/bed or figuratively in life/career. Can also function as an adjective.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naabutan ko siyang **pabangon** mula sa kanyang pagkakahiga.","translation":"I caught him as he was **getting up** from lying down."},{"sentence":"**Pabangon** pa lang ang ekonomiya mula sa matinding krisis.","translation":"The economy is just **on its way up** from a severe crisis."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbibigay ng buong pansin, diin, o pokus sa isang partikular na bagay, gawain, o layunin.
original_explanation: This is your 'game face' in noun form. It’s what you need when you're trying to finish a work deadline while your kapitbahay is having a karaoke party. It's the laser-like focus required to find the best ukay-ukay deal or to perfectly balance the flavors in your adobo.
usage_notes: Often used with 'ng pansin' (pagtutuon ng pansin) to mean 'focusing of attention.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagtutuon** sa pag-aaral ay susi sa tagumpay.","translation":"**Focusing** on studies is the key to success."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng matinding **pagtutuon** para matapos ang proyektong ito.","translation":"Intense **concentration** is needed to finish this project."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paggamit ng kuko upang makasugat o mag-iwan ng marka, karaniwang ginagawa ng mga hayop tulad ng pusa.
original_explanation: A love bite from your cat that isn't really a love bite. It's the souvenir you get for trying to give your 'mingming' a belly rub when it didn't ask for one. The resulting red lines are proof of your poor life choices.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to scratching with claws, most often by a cat. For human scratching, 'pagkakamot' is more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May marka sa braso niya dahil sa **pagkalmot** ng alagang pusa.","translation":"He has a mark on his arm from the **scratching** of his pet cat."},{"sentence":"Umiyak ang bata dahil sa sakit ng **pagkalmot**.","translation":"The child cried because of the pain from the **scratch**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng buhangin na may napakaliliit at makikinis na butil, karaniwang matatagpuan sa mga dalampasigan.
original_explanation: The official texture of Philippine vacation goals. It's that Boracay, Palawan, Siargao sand that feels like powder under your feet. If your beach trip doesn't have **pinong-buhangin**, did you even really go on a proper beach trip? #TravelGoals
usage_notes: Often used as a compound noun or adjective to describe a quality of a beach.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakasarap maglakad sa **pinong-buhangin** ng El Nido.","translation":"It feels so good to walk on the **fine sand** of El Nido."},{"sentence":"Pangarap kong tumira sa isang islang may **pinong-buhangin**.","translation":"I dream of living on an island with **fine sand**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tiyak, malinaw na natukoy, o partikular.
original_explanation: Kapag tinanong ka kung anong gusto mong kainin at hindi "kahit ano" ang sagot mo. "Gusto ko ng tapsilog, with extra garlic rice and suka with sili." Yan, espesipiko ka. Hindi 'yung "ikaw bahala," na source ng 99% ng away ng mag-jowa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroon siyang **espesipiko** na dahilan kung bakit siya umalis.","translation":"He has a **specific** reason why he left."},{"sentence":"Humingi siya ng **espesipiko** na disenyo para sa kanyang damit.","translation":"She asked for a **specific** design for her dress."}]

translation: to give meaning; to define; to interpret
meaning_filipino: Ang paglilinaw o pagpapaliwanag sa ibig sabihin ng isang salita, simbolo, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you try to explain a meme to your parents. You're giving context, you're defining the punchline. It's also that deep, philosophical thing you do when you're trying to find your 'purpose' in life, trying to magbigay-kahulugan to your very existence, usually after a long night out or a major life crisis.
usage_notes: Used both in academic/formal contexts (defining a term) and in personal/philosophical contexts (finding meaning).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **magbigay-kahulugan** sa kanyang panaginip.","translation":"He tried to **interpret** his dream."},{"sentence":"Ang pagtulong sa kapwa ang **nagbibigay-kahulugan** sa aking buhay.","translation":"Helping others is what **gives meaning** to my life."}]

translation: to disturb, to harass, to cause trouble
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-abala, paggulo, o pagbibigay ng ligalig sa kapayapaan o kaayusan ng isang tao, bagay, o lugar.
original_explanation: This is what your noisy neighbors are doing at 2 AM when they decide it's videoke time. It's the act of being a public nuisance, whether it's a 'Marites' spreading gossip or a troll online trying to get a rise out of you. To 'manligalig' is to actively mess with someone's peace.
usage_notes: Often implies a persistent and annoying form of disturbance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **manligalig** sa mga natutulog.","translation":"Don't **disturb** those who are sleeping."},{"sentence":"May mga taong gustong **manligalig** sa social media para lang makakuha ng atensyon.","translation":"There are people who like to **cause trouble** on social media just to get attention."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na binigyan ng kapangyarihan o awtoridad na kumilos o magsalita para sa isang tao, pangkat, o institusyon.
etymology: Derived from `katawan`, meaning 'body'. The idea is that the representative 'embodies' the group they are representing. The verb form is `kumatawan` (to represent).
original_explanation: Your designated "human shield" or spokesperson. In school, they are your student council rep. In Congress, they are the people who (supposedly) speak for you. In a group project, they are the one you push forward to do the presentation. "Sino'ng kinatawan ng Pinas sa Miss Universe ngayon?" It's the person embodying the whole group's hopes, dreams, and potential for failure.
usage_notes: While it can be a past tense verb ('kinatawan niya ang grupo' - he represented the group), it is far more commonly used as a noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Kongresista ang **kinatawan** ng aming distrito.","translation":"The Congressman is the **representative** of our district."},{"sentence":"Ipinadala siya bilang **kinatawan** ng kumpanya sa kumperensya.","translation":"She was sent as the company's **representative** to the conference."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghiling o paggawa ng paraan upang ang isang bagay ay maging mas maikli sa haba o tagal.
etymology: From mag- (actor-focus verb prefix) + pa- (causative prefix) + ikli (shortness).
original_explanation: What you tell the tailor: "Manong, pa-ikli po ng pantalon." It's the verb for shortening anything—pants, a speech, a meeting, or even your hair. If a meeting is dragging on, you're secretly wishing the speaker would magpaikli of their presentation.
usage_notes: `Magpaikli` is to have something shortened. `Paikliin` is the command form to shorten something. `Umikli` means something became short on its own.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagpaikli** ako ng buhok para mas presko sa pakiramdam.","translation":"I **had** my hair **shortened** to feel fresher."},{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **magpaikli** ka ng iyong talumpati dahil limitado lang ang oras.","translation":"Please, **shorten** your speech because time is limited."}]

meaning_filipino: Kulay na kahalintulad ng sa hinog na kahel, isang kombinasyon ng pula at dilaw.
original_explanation: The color of your Meralco bill envelope, the sunset over Manila Bay, and your favorite brand of cheese-flavored chips. It's a more traditional, slightly more formal way to say 'orange' compared to just borrowing the English word.
usage_notes: Less common in casual conversation than the loanword 'orange', but standard in formal writing and descriptions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsuot siya ng blusang kulay **narangha**.","translation":"She wore an **orange**-colored blouse."},{"sentence":"Pininturahan nila ang pader ng matingkad na **narangha**.","translation":"They painted the wall a bright **orange**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na lubos na hinahangaan at tinitingala, karaniwan ay isang sikat na personalidad o isang taong may pambihirang galing.
original_explanation: Lodi! Petmalu! Your fave K-Pop star, basketball player, or even that kuya sa kanto na ang galing mag-gitara. It's who you look up to and say, 'Sana all.' Pagbati na rin 'to sa tropa: 'Uy, idol! Musta?'
usage_notes: Ito ang modernong paggamit para sa isang hinahangaang tao. Maaari ring gamitin bilang isang kolokyal na tawag o pagbati sa isang kaibigan o kakilala.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Kathryn Bernardo ang **idol** ng maraming kabataan ngayon.","translation":"Kathryn Bernardo is the **idol** of many youths today."},{"sentence":"Uy, **idol**, pa-autograph naman sa jersey mo!","translation":"Hey, **idol**, can I get an autograph on your jersey!"}]

translation: to perform (a duty); to fulfill (a role)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasakatuparan o pagtupad sa isang tungkulin, obligasyon, o papel na inaasahan sa isang tao.
original_explanation: This is what your boss expects you to do with your job description, what your parents expect you to do as a 'mabuting anak,' and what your partner wishes you'd do in the relationship. It’s about playing your part and doing it well. Level up from just 'doing'; this is 'fulfilling'.
usage_notes: Carries a sense of responsibility and duty. It's more formal than 'gawin' (to do).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga na **gampanan** ng bawat isa ang kanilang tungkulin sa komunidad.","translation":"It is important for everyone to **fulfill** their duties in the community."},{"sentence":"Mahusay niyang ginampanan ang papel bilang kontrabida sa pelikula.","translation":"She excellently **performed** the role of the antagonist in the movie."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malapit na kaibigan, kasama, o karelasyon na laging kausap at kasalamuha sa matalik na paraan.
etymology: Nagmula sa unlaping 'ka-' at salitang-ugat na 'ulayaw', na nangangahulugang matalik na pakikipag-usap o pagsasama.
original_explanation: This isn't just your 'beshie' or 'BFF'. This is the person you share your Netflix password, your deepest 'hugot,' and maybe even your GrabFood order with. The one you can be your ugliest, most 'sabaw' self with, no judgment. Your ultimate confidant. Your ride-or-die.
usage_notes: A deep and somewhat poetic word. Not typically used in casual conversation but is common in literature, songs, and formal speeches to denote a very close bond.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang aking naging **kaulayaw** sa lungkot at ligaya.","translation":"She became my **intimate companion** in sadness and joy."},{"sentence":"Ang mga libro ang nagsilbing **kaulayaw** niya sa gabi.","translation":"Books served as his **intimate companions** at night."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na gumagana nang kusa o sa sarili nito, nang hindi nangangailangan ng direktang interbensyon ng tao.
original_explanation: Parang yung pag-iyak mo kapag narinig mo yung theme song ng ex mo. Hindi mo na kailangang isipin, **automatiko** na lang na tumutulo ang luha. O kaya yung ATM, 'Automatic Teller Machine', hindi 'At The Moment'.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin para sa mga makina, proseso, o maging sa mga reaksyon ng tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **automatiko** ang pagbukas ng pinto nang lumapit ako.","translation":"The door's opening became **automatic** when I approached."},{"sentence":"**Automatiko** na ang pag-reply niya ng \"k\" sa mga mensahe ko.","translation":"His reply of \"k\" to my messages is now **automatic**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang damdamin ng bahagyang galit o pagkayamot dahil sa isang bagay na nakagagambala o hindi kaaya-aya.
original_explanation: It's that low-level anger you feel when someone chews loudly, or when the internet buffers in the middle of a crucial scene. It's not full-blown rage, just... ugh. That "ugh" feeling is 'inis'. "Nakaka-inis 'yung traffic sa EDSA!" is the national mood.
usage_notes: A very common emotion word. Can be a noun (`ang inis`) or the root for adjectives (`nakakainis`, `naiinis`) and verbs (`inisin`).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ramdam ko ang **inis** niya nang hindi siya sinagot sa text.","translation":"I felt his **annoyance** when he didn't get a reply to his text."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong ipahalata ang iyong **inis** sa harap ng kliyente.","translation":"Don't show your **irritation** in front of the client."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paniniwala o doktrina na ang tunay na kaalaman at ang pagkakaisa sa Diyos o sa isang absolutong katotohanan ay maaaring makamit sa pamamagitan ng malalim na pagninilay-nilay at espiritwal na karanasan.
original_explanation: This is the 'ism' or the practice behind the 'mistiko'. It's the whole belief system. Think tarot cards, crystals, astral projection, communing with nature spirits, and deep meditation all rolled into one philosophical package. It's the deep dive into the 'hiwaga' of the universe.
usage_notes: A formal, academic, or religious term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan niya ang **mistisismo** ng mga katutubong Pilipino.","translation":"He is studying the **mysticism** of the indigenous Filipino people."},{"sentence":"Ang **mistisismo** ay isang mahalagang bahagi ng maraming relihiyon sa Silangan.","translation":"**Mysticism** is an important part of many Eastern religions."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang tao na mahilig mag-isip nang malalim, suriin ang mga bagay-bagay, at pagnilayan ang mga karanasan o ideya.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `mapag-` (pagkahilig) at `muni-muni` (reflection, contemplation), na pag-uulit ng salitang `muni` (to reflect, ponder).
original_explanation: Eto yung kaibigan mong bigla na lang tatahimik at tititig sa malayo, tapos pag tinanong mo, ang sasabihin, "Iniisip ko lang ang kalagayan ng ekonomiya ng Pilipinas." They're the ones who enjoy long walks, staring at the rain, and having deep talks at 3 AM. The "philosopher" of the group.
usage_notes: Karaniwang isang neutral o positibong katangian, na nauugnay sa pagiging maalalahanin at pagsisiyasat sa sarili.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang umupo sa tabi ng bintana at maging **mapagmuni-muni**.","translation":"She likes to sit by the window and be **reflective**."},{"sentence":"Ang isang taong **mapagmuni-muni** ay madalas na may malawak na pang-unawa.","translation":"A **contemplative** person often has a broad understanding."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng panandaliang pagtulog o paghimbing.
original_explanation: That power nap you take on the MRT, in the office pantry during lunch break, or on the sofa while "watching" a movie. It's the body's low-batt warning response, a mini-recharge before the next wave of adulting hits you.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to a short, light sleep, not a full night's rest.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang mabilis na **pag-idlip** lang ang kailangan ko para bumalik ang aking lakas.","translation":"I just need a quick **nap** to get my energy back."},{"sentence":"Nahuli niya ang kanyang lolo na nasa kalagitnaan ng **pag-idlip** sa tumba-tumba.","translation":"She caught her grandfather in the middle of **dozing off** on the rocking chair."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagkalooban ng biyaya, grasya, o mabuting kapalaran.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na "Sana all." Ito 'yung pagtanggap ng blessings, mapa-bonus man sa trabaho, makapasa sa exam, o 'yung simpleng may nag-abot sa'yo ng upuan sa MRT. If someone is `biniyayaan`, they got the good stuff.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pautos ('Biyayaan nawa kayo') o upang ilarawan ang isang kalagayan ('Siya ay biniyayaan').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana'y **biyayaan** ka ng magandang kalusugan.","translation":"May you **be blessed** with good health."},{"sentence":"**Biniyayaan** siya ng tatlong anak.","translation":"She **was blessed** with three children."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalagyan o kahon, karaniwang gawa sa plastik o metal, na ginagamit sa paglalagay at pagdadala ng baon na pagkain, lalo na para sa pananghalian.
original_explanation: The OG Filipino Tupperware. The source of all baon, from adobo to hotdog with rice. In the BPO world, this is the sacred vessel that holds your '15-minute lunch break' meal. Seeing your crush's lunchbox gives you a clue if they're a 'baon-is-life' person or a 'kain-sa-labas' socialite.
usage_notes: A direct loanword, very common in daily conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naiwan ko yata ang **lunchbox** ko sa bus.","translation":"I think I left my **lunchbox** on the bus."},{"sentence":"Ano ang baon mo sa **lunchbox** mo ngayon?","translation":"What did you bring in your **lunchbox** today?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamahalaga at pangunahing kahulugan, katangian, o kalikasan ng isang bagay; ang sentro o buod ng isang ideya.
original_explanation: This is the 'What's the point?' or 'the main thing.' The very soul of the matter. It's the core message of a hugot line, the essential ingredient in your lola's adobo, the real reason behind the 'team building.' It's the truth without the fluff.
usage_notes: A slightly formal or literary term used to get to the heart of a matter.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagmamahal sa kapwa ang **pinakadiwa** ng Pasko.","translation":"Loving one's neighbor is the **essence** of Christmas."},{"sentence":"Ano ba ang **pinakadiwa** ng iyong argumento?","translation":"What is the **gist** of your argument?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang itinalagang lugar kung saan maaaring pansamantalang huminto ang mga sasakyan upang magbaba ng mga pasahero o kargamento.
etymology: Mula sa pariralang Ingles na "unloading zone".
original_explanation: That magical, often ignored, strip of road where you're *supposed* to get off the jeepney or bus. In reality, for many Pinoys, the entire street is an unloading zone. It's also a metaphor for a toxic friendship where you just dump all your problems on someone. "Friend, unloading zone lang ako sa 'yo?" #hugot
usage_notes: Ginagamit bilang isang buong yunit sa mga karatula at sa usapan, lalo na sa konteksto ng transportasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bawal pumarada dito, **unloading zone** lang ito.","translation":"No parking here, this is just an **unloading zone**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mahikayat o mapaniwala sa isang ideya, argumento, o pananaw matapos ang pagpapaliwanag o pangungumbinsi ng iba.
original_explanation: That "aha!" moment when your friend finally convinces you to try that sketchy-looking street food and it turns out to be amazing. Or when a salesperson's pitch is so good, you walk out with a new gadget you didn't even know you needed. When you finally agree, you've been "makombensi".
usage_notes: Often used to express a change of mind or heart. The root 'kombensi' is from the verb 'kumbinsihin' (to convince).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **nakombensi** rin niya akong sumali sa kanilang proyekto.","translation":"Finally, he **convinced** me to join their project."},{"sentence":"Mahirap siyang **makombensi** dahil matatag ang kanyang paninindigan.","translation":"It's hard for him **to be convinced** because his principles are firm."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang maunawaan o malaman ang isang bagay nang hindi nangangailangan ng mulat na pangangatwiran o lohikal na pag-iisip; kutob o pakiramdam.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "intuición". Ang baybay na 'intwisyon' ay karaniwan din.
original_explanation: That 'gut feeling' you get when your friend says '5 minutes na lang' but you know it's really an hour. It's your inner Marites telling you something's up. It’s what makes your mom text 'Umuwi ka na' exactly 2 minutes after you did something you weren't supposed to do.
usage_notes: Ang "kutob" ay ang mas pang-araw-araw at katutubong katumbas nito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malakas ang **intuwisyon** ko na may mangyayaring maganda ngayon.","translation":"I have a strong **intuition** that something good will happen today."},{"sentence":"Sundin mo ang iyong **intuwisyon**; madalas ay tama ito.","translation":"Follow your **intuition**; it's often right."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hindi pagiging direkta sa pagsasalita o pagkilos; ang paggawa ng maraming hindi kinakailangang pagliko o paghinto.
etymology: Mula sa 'ligoy' (paliko-liko) na may pag-uulit ng salitang-ugat at '-um-' gitlapi.
original_explanation: Eto yung sagot ng kaibigan mo pag tinanong mo kung may utang pa siya sa'yo. Instead of a 'yes' or 'no', you get a whole life story. It's also that Grab driver who seems to be touring you around the city para lumaki ang metro. To be indirect, evasive, and take the scenic route when a straight path exists.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa pananalita (pagiging hindi direkta) o sa pisikal na pagkilos (pagiging paliko-liko). Ang pag-uulit na 'liguy-ligoy' ay nagbibigay-diin sa kahulugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang **lumiguy-ligoy** pa, sabihin mo na ang totoo.","translation":"Stop **beating around the bush** and just tell the truth."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagsapit o pag-abot sa isang tiyak na lugar o destinasyon.
original_explanation: The opposite of 'paalis'. It's when your Shopee/Lazada package finally shows up, when your balikbayan relative arrives at NAIA with pasalubong, or when you finally clock in at work after braving the MRT. The moment of 'sa wakas!'
usage_notes: Can also be used adverbially, meaning 'upon arrival' or 'when'. For example, 'Pagdating ko sa bahay...' (When I arrived home...).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inaabangan namin ang **pagdating** ng mga bisita.","translation":"We are waiting for the **arrival** of the guests."},{"sentence":"**Pagdating** ko sa bahay, natulog ako agad.","translation":"**Upon arriving** home, I immediately went to sleep."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalipunan o pangkat ng mga kliyente o parokyano ng isang negosyo, propesyonal, o establisyimento.
original_explanation: Kung ang 'kliyente' ay solo flight, ang 'kliyentela' ay ang buong barkada. Ito ang collection of loyal customers mo. 'Yung mga tita na laging nagpapaluto sa'yo ng pagkain para sa party nila, o 'yung mga kabarkada na laging tumatambay sa coffee shop mo—sila ang bumubuo ng iyong kliyentela. Treasure them more than your first-edition Pokémon cards.
usage_notes: Ito ang mas karaniwan at tinatanggap na baybay kaysa 'klientela'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala na ng may-ari ng karinderya ang kanyang regular na **kliyentela**.","translation":"The owner of the eatery already knows her regular **clientele**."},{"sentence":"Unti-unting nabubuo ang **kliyentela** ng kanyang online business.","translation":"The **clientele** of her online business is gradually being built."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagkontrol o pagbabawas ng kinakain upang makamit ang isang partikular na timbang o para sa kalusugan.
original_explanation: The eternal struggle between you and that extra rice. Ito yung "starting Monday" na laging nauurong. Yung titingin ka lang sa masarap na pagkain pero hanggang tingin na lang talaga kasi "on a diet" ka. The ultimate test of self-control.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap ang **pagdidiyeta** lalo na kung maraming handaan.","translation":"The **act of dieting** is hard, especially when there are many feasts."},{"sentence":"Sinamahan niya ng ehersisyo ang kanyang **pagdidiyeta**.","translation":"She accompanied her **dieting** with exercise."}]

translation: a place to live in; to be able to live in
meaning_filipino: Bilang pangngalan, isang lugar na maaaring maging tahanan o tirahan. Bilang pandiwa, ang pagkakaroon ng kakayahan o posibilidad na manirahan sa isang lugar.
etymology: From *ma- -an* (potential/locative affix) + *tira* (to reside). Note: This 'tira' is a homonym of 'tira' (leftover).
original_explanation: As a noun: It's your future condo, your dream house, or even just a decent apartment for rent. The place you can finally call home. As a verb: It's the "pwede na 'to!" moment when you're house-hunting and find a place that's actually livable. "Bes, malinis at may tubig, matitirahan na 'to!"
usage_notes: Can function as a noun (a place to live) or a potential verb (can be lived in). Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghahanap sila ng disenteng **matitirahan** sa Maynila.","translation":"They are looking for a decent **place to live in** in Manila."},{"sentence":"Kahit maliit ang espasyo, basta malinis ay **matitirahan** naman.","translation":"Even if the space is small, as long as it's clean, it **can be lived in**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nauugnay sa puso o mga sakit nito.
original_explanation: 'Yung term na maririnig mo sa ospital kapag may inatake sa puso. "Nag-cardiac arrest!" or "May cardiac condition siya." Basically, anything related sa heart mo, mapa-physical or emotional, pero sa medical field, physical lang 'to. Huwag mong sabihing "May cardiac issue ako sa ex ko," baka dalhin ka sa ER.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa medikal na konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala siya sa ospital dahil sa atake sa **kardyak**.","translation":"He was brought to the hospital due to a **cardiac** arrest."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gagawing pag-ipit sa balat ng isang tao gamit ang hinlalaki at hintuturo, na karaniwang nagdudulot ng bahagyang sakit o ginagamit bilang paraan ng paglalambing.
original_explanation: This is what your tita does to your cheeks when she finds you cute (or chubby). 'Ang cute-cute mo, kukurot ako sa pisngi mo!' It's also that sharp, sudden feeling of 'aray' or 'kilig' in your heart. Parang hugot na biglang kumurot sa puso mo.
usage_notes: The future tense of 'kurot'. It can be an act of affection, annoyance, or a metaphor for a sharp emotional feeling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang malikot, **kukurot** ako sa singit mo.","translation":"Don't be naughty, I **will pinch** your side."},{"sentence":"Ang mga alaala ninyo ay bigla na lang **kukurot** sa puso mo.","translation":"Your memories together **will** suddenly **pinch** at your heart."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagdaragdag ng mga detalye, paliwanag, o impormasyon upang gawing mas malinaw, mas kumpleto, o mas masalimuot ang isang ideya o pahayag.
original_explanation: This is what your teacher asks for when your answer is too short. It's the "Can you explain further?" moment. Sa chismis, ito yung pag-spill ng tea with all the juicy details, walang labis, walang kulang. From a simple "Nag-away sila" to a full-blown "Eto kasi 'yung nangyari..."
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa pormal na diskurso, pagsulat, at talakayan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng mas malalim na **elaborasyon** ang iyong sanaysay.","translation":"Your essay needs more thorough **elaboration**."},{"sentence":"Humingi ang mga tagapakinig ng **elaborasyon** tungkol sa kanyang teorya.","translation":"The audience asked for an **elaboration** on his theory."}]

meaning_filipino: May sukat, lawak, o dami na higit sa karaniwan.
etymology: From the prefix `ma-` (having the quality of) and the root `laki` (size, bigness).
original_explanation: The OG size description. Before 'plus-size' or 'grande,' there was just 'malaki.' It's the size of your Jollibee chickenjoy bucket, your utang sa BDO, and the chance na ma-ghost ka niya.
usage_notes: This is the most fundamental and widely used adjective in Tagalog for describing something as 'big' or 'large' in any context, from physical size to abstract concepts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Malaki** ang bahay nila sa probinsya.","translation":"Their house in the province is **big**."},{"sentence":"May **malaki** kang problema kung hindi mo pa sinisimulan ang proyekto.","translation":"You have a **big** problem if you haven't started the project yet."}]

meaning_filipino: Mahahabang piraso ng papel o plastik na may iba't ibang kulay na isinasabit bilang palamuti, lalo na sa mga pagdiriwang.
original_explanation: Not the person playing Mobile Legends online. This is the OG streamer—the colorful, crinkly paper or plastic strips you hang for birthdays, fiestas, and Christmas parties. It's the official sign that 'May handa!' (There's a party/food!).
usage_notes: The English word is used directly. This entry refers to the decoration, not the person who streams online content (which is also called a 'streamer').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkabit tayo ng mga **streamer** at lobo para sa birthday ni Lola.","translation":"Let's hang some **streamers** and balloons for Grandma's birthday."},{"sentence":"Puno ng makukulay na **streamer** ang buong kalye para sa pista.","translation":"The whole street is full of colorful **streamers** for the fiesta."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang hiram na nangangahulugang "kabanal-banalan," karaniwang ginagamit sa mga bagay o lalaking banal sa kontekstong relihiyoso.
etymology: From Spanish 'santísimo' (most holy, masculine superlative of 'santo').
original_explanation: The masculine version of 'santisima'. It's the highest level of holiness, often used to refer to the 'Santisimo Sakramento' (Most Holy Sacrament). It's the kind of word you only hear during Holy Week or when someone is *really* exasperated.
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of the Catholic Church, especially referring to the Eucharist ('Santisimo Sakramento').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inilagak ang **Santisimo** Sakramento sa monstrance para sa adorasyon.","translation":"The **Most Holy** Sacrament was placed in the monstrance for adoration."},{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng prusisyon para sa **Santisimo**.","translation":"There was a procession for the **Most Holy** (Sacrament)."}]

meaning_filipino: Ganap na walang kasuotan; lubos na kahubaran.
etymology: Reduplication ng 'hubad'. Ang 'hubo' ay isang varyant na pinaikli at ang 't ay pinaikling 'at', na nagreresulta sa 'hubo at hubad'.
original_explanation: This is the next level of 'hubad'. This is not just 'no shirt', this is 'no anything at all'. The state of a newborn baby, or how you feel when your most embarrassing secret gets exposed in the group chat. It's 'hubad' squared.
usage_notes: Isang mas masidhing paraan ng pagsasabing 'hubad'. Nagpapahiwatig ng ganap o total na kawalan ng saplot.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natagpuan ang bata na naglalaro sa ulan nang **hubu't-hubad**.","translation":"The child was found playing in the rain **completely naked**."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam niya'y **hubu't-hubad** ang kanyang kaluluwa nang aminin niya ang lahat.","translation":"He felt his soul was **stark naked** when he confessed everything."}]

translation: to be disregarded; to become worthless
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkawala ng importansya, kabuluhan, o pagpapahalaga sa isang tao, bagay, o pagsisikap.
original_explanation: The ultimate "hugot" verb. 'Yung feeling na binigay mo na ang lahat pero binalewala ka lang. You feel unseen, unappreciated. Parang group project na ikaw lahat gumawa pero 'yung credit napunta sa iba. Lahat ng effort mo, **nawalang-halaga**. It's the pain of being taken for granted.
usage_notes: A compound verb from 'mawala' (to be lost) and 'halaga' (value). Often used in emotional or dramatic contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayokong **mawalang-halaga** lang ang lahat ng sakripisyo ng aking mga magulang.","translation":"I don't want all the sacrifices of my parents to just **be disregarded**."},{"sentence":"Sa isang iglap, tila **nawalang-halaga** ang lahat ng pinagsamahan nila.","translation":"In an instant, it seemed that everything they had built together **became worthless**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggamit ng isang matalim na kagamitan, tulad ng kutsilyo, upang hatiin o putulin ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: The fundamental skill you need to survive in the kitchen, unless your life goal is to live on GrabFood forever. It's what you do to the onions that make you cry, reminding you of your ex. Also, what your Tita does to the lechon with expert precision at every family gathering.
usage_notes: 'Maghiwa' generally implies slicing, as opposed to 'magputol' which can mean to chop or cut more broadly, or 'tadtarin' which means to mince.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **maghiwa** ka ng sibuyas para sa ating adobo.","translation":"Please, **slice** some onions for our adobo."},{"sentence":"Nag-iingat siyang **maghiwa** ng karne upang hindi masugatan.","translation":"She is carefully **slicing** the meat so she won't get hurt."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na pagpapasya o hatol ng isang korte; ang pagbuo ng opinyon o konklusyon tungkol sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: The final verdict, the "Guilty or Not Guilty." But in everyday life, it's what you get from your titas at a family reunion: "Uy, tumaba ka!" That's a husga. It's the side-eye you get when you order extra rice for the third time. Everyone's a judge, and every action is on trial in the court of public opinion. Don't be so quick to husga!
usage_notes: Can be formal (legal verdict) or informal (personal judgment/prejudice).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang magbigay ng **husga** kung hindi mo alam ang buong kwento.","translation":"Don't pass **judgment** if you don't know the whole story."},{"sentence":"Hinihintay ng lahat ang **husga** ng korte sa kaso.","translation":"Everyone is waiting for the court's **verdict** in the case."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na anyong tubig, karaniwang matatagpuan sa mga urbanong lugar, na nagsisilbing daluyan ng tubig-ulan o sobrang tubig patungo sa mas malaking ilog o dagat.
original_explanation: The unsung hero (and sometimes smelly victim) of Manila's drainage system. It's the city's natural canal that's supposed to prevent floods, but often ends up as a community swimming pool for discarded plastics and other 'floaters.' When it rains hard, the estero is the first one to tell you, 'Bes, baha na.'
usage_notes: Often associated with urban pollution and flooding issues in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nililinis ng pamahalaan ang mga **estero** sa Maynila upang maiwasan ang pagbaha.","translation":"The government is cleaning the **creeks** in Manila to prevent flooding."},{"sentence":"Maraming informal settlers ang nakatira sa tabi ng **estero**.","translation":"Many informal settlers live beside the **estuary**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang pandamdam na ginagamit bilang ekspresyon ng pang-aasar o pagmamaliit, na kadalasang sinasabayan ng paglalabas ng dila.
etymology: Onomatopeya o salitang naglalarawan ng tunog o kilos ng pagdila bilang pang-aasar.
original_explanation: The ultimate childhood comeback. It's the sound you make when you stick your tongue out at someone to tease them. "Di mo ko maabot, **belat**!" (You can't catch me, bleah!). It's the verbal equivalent of the :P emoji. Even as adults, there are moments you just wanna go "**Belat**!" to your problems.
usage_notes: Halos palaging sinasabayan ng kilos ng paglalabas ng dila. Itinuturing na pambata ngunit ginagamit din ng mga matatanda sa pabirong paraan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naunahan kitang matapos! **Belat**!","translation":"I finished before you! **Bleah**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga bagay, panahon, o kaugalian na napakatagal na o mula sa malayong nakaraan.
original_explanation: Anything from "before your time." For millennials, this could be a floppy disk. For Gen Z, it's a phone with buttons. It's the vibe of your lola's house, full of wooden furniture and stories from "noong panahon ng Hapon." Also describes your friend's dating advice if it sounds like it came from a Maria Clara novel.
usage_notes: Refers to things that are very old, from a past era.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marami tayong matututunan sa mga **sinauna** nating ninuno.","translation":"We can learn a lot from our **ancient** ancestors."},{"sentence":"Ang paraan ng kanyang panliligaw ay parang **sinauna**.","translation":"His way of courting is very **old-fashioned**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga bagay, gawain, o usapin na may kaugnayan sa liturhiya o pampublikong pagsamba ng isang relihiyon.
original_explanation: This is the church version of 'corporate attire' or 'official business.' Anything labeled 'liturhika' is part of the formal program of a religious service, like the songs, the readings, the vestments of the priest. It's the 'by the book' stuff in worship.
usage_notes: Kadalasang ginagamit sa konteksto ng relihiyong Kristiyano, lalo na sa Simbahang Katoliko.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang koro ay nagsanay ng mga awiting **liturhika** para sa Misa de Gallo.","translation":"The choir practiced **liturgical** songs for the Dawn Mass."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdiriwang ng ikalimampung anibersaryo ng kasal.
etymology: From Spanish 'boda de oro' (wedding of gold).
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'sana all' for married couples. 50 years together! That's longer than most people's BPO careers, phone plans, and even their 'forever.' It's the level of commitment that deserves a grand celebration, complete with grandchildren running around and a slideshow of old, grainy photos. #RelationshipGoals for real.
usage_notes: Specific term for a 50th wedding anniversary. 'Boda de plata' is for the 25th anniversary.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagdiwang ng kanilang **boda-de-oro** ang aking lolo at lola.","translation":"My grandfather and grandmother celebrated their **golden wedding anniversary**."},{"sentence":"Isang malaking handaan ang inihanda para sa **boda-de-oro** nina Mang Tony at Aling Nena.","translation":"A big feast was prepared for the **golden wedding anniversary** of Mang Tony and Aling Nena."}]

meaning_filipino: Magsagawa ng kampanya para sa isang partikular na kandidato, produkto, o layunin.
original_explanation: This is the action version of 'kampanya'. It's what you do when you're actively promoting someone or something. Example: "Bes, **kampanyahin** mo naman 'yung bago kong small business sa mga friends mo!" It means to put in the work—distribute flyers, post on social media, convince people—to support a cause or person.
usage_notes: An object-focus verb. The subject of the sentence is the one being campaigned for.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Balak nilang **kampanyahin** ang kasalukuyang mayor para sa muling pagtakbo.","translation":"They plan **to campaign for** the current mayor for his re-election bid."},{"sentence":"Dapat nating **kampanyahin** ang paggamit ng eco-bags sa halip na plastic.","translation":"We should **campaign for** the use of eco-bags instead of plastic."}]

translation: in every season; at all times
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa lahat ng pagkakataon, yugto, o kapanahunan, na walang pinipiling oras o sitwasyon.
etymology: Mula sa "sa", "bawat" (each), at "panahon" (time/season). Ang "bawa't" ay lumang baybay ng "bawat".
original_explanation: Ito yung parang 24/7 convenience store, laging andyan. 'Yung kaibigan na masasandalan mo "in every season" of your life, mapa-tag-araw (masaya) o tag-ulan (may pinagdadaanan). It implies consistency, whether you're talking about love, a reliable product, or God's grace.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa mga pormal na sulatin, kanta, at tula. Ang modernong baybay nito ay "sa bawat panahon".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-ibig ng ina ay tapat **sa bawa't panahon**.","translation":"A mother's love is faithful **at all times**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paunawa o pahiwatig na nagbibigay ng kaalaman tungkol sa isang posibleng panganib, tuntunin, o mahalagang impormasyon.
etymology: Possibly from Malay 'bahala' which relates to divine power or fate, implying a forewarning.
original_explanation: That sign that says 'Bawal Umihi Dito' which people still pee next to. It's the text from your mom saying 'Umuwi ka nang maaga,' the Meralco notice about a power interruption, or the 'Wet Floor' sign you only see after you've slipped. A heads-up you sometimes choose to ignore at your own peril.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **babala** ang PAGASA tungkol sa paparating na malakas na bagyo.","translation":"PAGASA has a **warning** about the approaching strong typhoon."},{"sentence":"Ang usok ay isang **babala** na may sunog.","translation":"Smoke is a **sign** that there is a fire."}]

translation: to apply by wiping or smearing
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng isang bagay (karaniwan ay likido o malapot) sa isang ibabaw sa pamamagitan ng pagdampi at pagkalat nito.
original_explanation: Whether you're putting on sunscreen, spreading palaman on pandesal, or applying ointment on a wound, you **ipahid** it. It's the act of smearing something onto a surface. The classic lola command: "**Ipahid** mo itong Vicks sa dibdib mo!"
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ipahid** mo ang gamot sa sugat pagkatapos itong linisin.","translation":"**Apply** the medicine on the wound after cleaning it."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **ipahid** ang sunblock bago lumabas ng bahay.","translation":"Don't forget to **apply** the sunblock before leaving the house."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalakbay o paglalakad nang walang tiyak na patutunguhan sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: Your game plan for the weekend when you have no actual plans but don't want to stay home. "Saan punta mo sa Sabado?" "Ewan, gagala lang siguro sa mall." It's the future tense of being a 'laagan' or 'layas'.
usage_notes: Future tense of the verb 'gala'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Gagala** kami sa Baguio sa susunod na buwan.","translation":"We **will roam** around Baguio next month."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng exam, **gagala** muna ako para mag-relax.","translation":"After the exam, I **will wander** for a bit to relax."}]

translation: to long for; to greatly desire
meaning_filipino: Ang matinding pagnanais o pananabik para sa isang bagay, tao, o pangyayari na matagal nang hinihintay.
etymology: Reduplication of 'asam' (desire, hope) with the infix '-in-'.
original_explanation: This is next-level "sana all." It's that feeling when you're staring at the Lazada/Shopee tracking page for the 10th time today, waiting for your 12.12 haul. It's the "manifesting" you do for a promotion, a long vacation, or for your crush to finally notice you. It's a desire so intense, you repeat the word.
usage_notes: The repetition of 'asam' intensifies the meaning of longing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-uwi sa probinsya ang tanging **inaasam-asam** niya.","translation":"Going home to the province is the one thing he **longs for**."},{"sentence":"Matagal ko nang **inaasam-asam** ang pagkakataong ito.","translation":"I have been **greatly desiring** this opportunity for a long time."}]

translation: To make sure; to ascertain; to specify
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pag-alam o paggawa ng isang bagay upang maging sigurado; tukuyin o linawin ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the action you take when your friend says "mga 8pm" and you reply, "Tiyakan mo, anong oras talaga? Filipino time o sakto?" It's the verb form of making things 'tiyak'. It's confirming the G-meet link, double-checking the price on Shopee, or asking "Ano ba talaga tayo?" to clarify the relationship status.
usage_notes: 'Tiyakin' is a more common synonym. 'Tiyakan mo' means 'Make it sure/specific'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tiyakan** mo muna kung may pasok bukas bago ka matulog.","translation":"**Make sure** first if there are classes tomorrow before you sleep."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **tiyakan** ang mga detalye ng kontrata.","translation":"The details of the contract need **to be specified**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapang pangkarpintero na may talim at dalawang hawakan, ginagamit sa paghuhugis o pagpapakinis ng kahoy sa pamamagitan ng paghila nito.
original_explanation: This is a classic tool from your Lolo's toolbox. The **limbas** is used by carpenters to shape wood, kinda like peeling a giant potato. It's for detailed work, shaving off wood to get the perfect curve. It's the analog version of 3D modeling for wood.
usage_notes: Isang espesyal na kasangkapan sa karpinterya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ng karpintero ang **limbas** upang hubugin ang paa ng silya.","translation":"The carpenter used the **drawknife** to shape the leg of the chair."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang unang nota sa iskalang musikal na sol-fa (do-re-mi-fa-sol-la-ti-do).
original_explanation: Yung unang nota sa kantang "Do-Re-Mi" from The Sound of Music. Ito yung simula ng lahat, parang "Hi" sa chat bago maging "kayo na." Kung sa videoke, ito yung unang nota na kailangan mong tamaan para hindi ka pagtawanan.
usage_notes: Ginagamit lamang sa konteksto ng musika.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magsimula tayo sa notang **do**.","translation":"Let's start with the note **do**."},{"sentence":"Ang 'do-re-mi' ay batayang pagsasanay sa pag-awit.","translation":"The 'do-re-mi' is a basic exercise in singing."}]

translation: as big as, as large as
meaning_filipino: May sukat o laki na katulad ng sa iba; ginagamit sa paghahambing ng dalawang bagay na magkapareho ang laki.
etymology: From the prefix `sin-` (denoting sameness or equality) + `laki` (size, bigness).
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'sana all' for size comparison. When something is 'sinlaki ng' something else, it means they're the same size. It's the prefix 'sin-' (meaning 'same') plus 'laki' (big). Like when you compare your workload to your sahod and realize it's definitely not 'sinlaki'. The phrase 'sinlaki nang tao' specifically means 'as big as a person'.
usage_notes: Often followed by 'ng' or 'ni' to specify the object of comparison. For example, 'sinlaki ng bahay' (as big as a house) or 'sinlaki ni Juan' (as big as Juan). 'Kasinglaki' and 'kasinlaki' are common variants.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang alaga niyang aso ay **sinlaki** na ng isang guya.","translation":"His pet dog is now **as big as** a calf."},{"sentence":"Wow, **sinlaki** ng kamao mo ang prutas!","translation":"Wow, the fruit is **as big as** your fist!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking prutas na may berdeng balat at puting laman, karaniwang ginagamit sa pagluluto ng sabaw o ginagawang minatamis.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung gulay na nagpapanggap na prutas. Bida sa hopia at sa palamig na sago't gulaman. Mukha siyang higanteng pipino na may puting pulbos. Don't judge a book by its cover, masarap 'to, lalo na 'pag ginawang candy!
usage_notes: A common ingredient in Filipino and Chinese-Filipino cuisine.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-init si Nanay ng sabaw ng manok na may **kondol**.","translation":"Mom heated up some chicken soup with **winter melon**."},{"sentence":"Paborito kong palamig ang sago at gulaman na may minatamis na **kondol**.","translation":"My favorite cooler is sago and gulaman with sweetened **winter melon**."}]

meaning_filipino: Inabot at hinawakan ang kamay ng ibang tao bilang tanda ng pagbati, pagkakasundo, o paggalang.
original_explanation: The universal sign for "deal," "nice to meet you," or "congrats!" Pre-pandemic, this was standard. Post-pandemic, it's a mix of this, fist bumps, and awkward waves. 'Yung kumamay ka sa boss mo after mo ma-promote? Power move.
usage_notes: The action is synonymous with 'nakipagkamay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matapos ang mahabang pag-uusap, **kumamay** sila bilang tanda ng kanilang pagkakasundo.","translation":"After a long discussion, they **shook hands** as a sign of their agreement."},{"sentence":"**Kumamay** ang Pangulo sa bawat atletang nag-uwi ng medalya.","translation":"The President **shook the hands** of every athlete who brought home a medal."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na mabilis maglaho o sa isang tao na madaling magalit.
etymology: Mula sa 'madali' (easy) at 'sumingaw' (to evaporate, to let off steam).
original_explanation: This is your friend who goes from zero to Hulk-mode in 2.5 seconds when their internet lags during a game. Also applies to alcohol left uncapped, or your 13th-month pay. It's there one moment, gone the next. Literally 'easy to evaporate' or figuratively 'easy to let off steam'.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin nang literal para sa mga likido o patalinghaga para sa mga emosyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong iwanang bukas ang bote ng pabango dahil **madaling sumingaw** ang amoy nito.","translation":"Don't leave the perfume bottle open because its scent is **volatile**."},{"sentence":"Pasensya na, pero **madaling sumingaw** ang ulo ng boss natin tuwing Lunes.","translation":"I'm sorry, but our boss is **short-tempered** every Monday."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tunog na nalilikha ng bituka, lalo na kapag nagugutom o hindi maganda ang tiyan.
original_explanation: You know that sound your tummy makes after you ate that sketchy street food from a vendor you've never seen before? The one that sounds like a science experiment gone wrong and signals you need a toilet, STAT. That's hagutak. It's the official soundtrack of LBM.
usage_notes: A very specific and somewhat informal word, but universally understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ako nakatulog dahil sa **hagutak** ng tiyan ko.","translation":"I couldn't sleep because of the **gurgling** of my stomach."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula sa **hagutak** bago siya tuluyang nagtae.","translation":"It started with a **stomach gurgle** before he got full-blown diarrhea."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng laro na ginagamitan ng tako upang itulak ang mga bola sa isang mesang may mga butas sa gilid.
original_explanation: Yung laro sa kanto na madalas pag-pustahan ng bote ng beer. Tambayan ng mga 'cool' na tito at mga BPO agent na nagpapa-release ng stress after a long shift. Requires skills, geometry, and a steady hand (kahit may tama na).
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa laro ng 'billiards' o 'pool'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagyaya si kuya na maglaro ng **bilyar** pagkatapos ng trabaho.","translation":"My older brother invited us to play **billiards** after work."},{"sentence":"Magaling siyang tumira sa **bilyar**.","translation":"He is a skilled shot in **billiards**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malalim na paghinga na karaniwang nagpapahiwatig ng pagod, kalungkutan, o ginhawa.
etymology: Combination of "bunton" (pile, heap) and "hininga" (breath). A "heap of breath."
original_explanation: This is the universal Filipino response to everything. Traffic? *Sigh*. Puno ang MRT? *Sigh*. Boss gives you more work at 4:59 PM? *Sigh*. Finally get to sit down after a long day? *Sigh of relief*. It's the sound of your soul logging off for a second. It's a whole mood compressed into one breathy sound. Hay nako.
usage_notes: A very expressive word that captures a specific emotional action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malalim na **pagbubuntunghininga** ang pinakawalan niya nang matapos ang mahirap na pagsusulit.","translation":"She let out a deep **sigh** after finishing the difficult exam."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang madalas na **pagbubuntunghininga** ay senyales ng malalim na problema.","translation":"His frequent **act of sighing** is a sign of a deep problem."}]

translation: to be the cause of tiredness
meaning_filipino: Ang maging dahilan o sanhi ng pagod o pagkapagal.
original_explanation: Traffic sa EDSA. Back-to-back meetings na pwedeng email lang sana. 'Yung jowang seloso/selosa na walang tiwala. 'Yung pag-explain ng paulit-ulit sa isang bagay. Lahat 'yan, pwedeng ikapagod mo, physically or emotionally. It's the reason why you say "Pagod na 'ko" even if you just woke up.
usage_notes: Often used to express the reason for one's fatigue. The past tense 'ikinapagod' is very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang maghapong paglalaba ang **ikinapagod** ni Aling Nena.","translation":"The whole day of doing laundry was the **cause of Aling Nena's tiredness**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ikapagod** ang isip mo sa mga bagay na hindi mahalaga.","translation":"Don't **let your mind be tired by** (lit: don't let it be the cause of your tiredness) things that are not important."}]

translation: fan palm; the leaf of a fan palm
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng palma (Livistona rotundifolia) na may malalapad at pabilog na dahon na kahugis ng pamaypay; ito rin ang pambansang dahon ng Pilipinas.
original_explanation: The OG Filipino fan. Before aircon and electric fans, there was the anahaw leaf. You'd see it used as a pamaypay during hot summer days in the province, or as roofing for a bahay kubo. It's the national leaf, basically the leafy equivalent of a barong tagalog—classic, functional, and very Pinoy.
usage_notes: Refers to both the tree (Livistona rotundifolia) and its iconic, fan-shaped leaf. It is the national leaf of the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng dahon ng **anahaw** bilang pamaypay dahil sa matinding init.","translation":"She used an **anahaw** leaf as a fan because of the intense heat."},{"sentence":"Ang bubong ng kanilang kubo ay gawa sa pinatuyong **anahaw**.","translation":"The roof of their hut is made of dried **fan palm** leaves."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng arina (starch) na mula sa kamoteng-kahoy (cassava). Karaniwan itong ginagawang maliliit at bilog na sangkap (pearls) sa mga palamig at panghimagas.
original_explanation: The chewy, bouncy balls of happiness in your milk tea. The OG 'sago'. Before the boba craze took over the world, there was good old tapioca in taho and ginumis.
usage_notes: In the Philippines, it's often used interchangeably with 'sago', although they are technically from different plant sources (sago from palm, tapioca from cassava).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong sahog sa milk tea ang **tapioca** pearls.","translation":"**Tapioca** pearls are my favorite topping in milk tea."},{"sentence":"Ang taho ay may arnibal, malambot na tokwa, at **tapioca**.","translation":"Taho has syrup, soft tofu, and **tapioca**."}]

translation: to let someone ride behind/with you (on a vehicle)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapahintulot sa isang tao na sumakay sa likuran o kasama sa isang sasakyan, karaniwan ay bisikleta o motorsiklo.
etymology: From `magpa-` (causative prefix) + `angkas` (to ride as a passenger, especially at the back).
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'sana all' moment for commuters stuck in traffic. It's when a motorcycle rider lets someone ride pillion. It's the signature move of Angkas and Joyride drivers. You're the one in control, the driver, and you're letting someone else hitch a ride. 'Bes, magpaangkas ka naman hanggang sa kanto!'
usage_notes: The subject is the driver who allows a passenger to ride. The passenger 'umaangkas' or 'nakikiangkas'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabait ang tsuper, pumayag siyang **magpaangkas** sa akin kahit puno na.","translation":"The driver was kind, he agreed to **let me ride with him** even if it was already full."},{"sentence":"Bawal **magpaangkas** ng bata sa motorsiklo nang walang helmet.","translation":"It's forbidden to **let a child ride on the back** of a motorcycle without a helmet."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng pagiging mapagtago o hindi naglalabas ng impormasyon; mapaglihim.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung kaibigan mong laging may "secret", pero 'di naman masabi-sabi. Parang 'yung feelings mo para sa kanya, tinatago mo na lang kasi alam mong 'seen' lang aabutin mo. Sila rin 'yung mahirap basahin, parang terms and conditions ng app.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masyadong **mailihim** si Ana tungkol sa kanyang personal na buhay.","translation":"Ana is too **secretive** about her personal life."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong maging **mailihim** sa plano nating sorpresa.","translation":"You need to be **discreet** about our surprise plan."}]

meaning_filipino: Nakaayos nang mabuti; nakasalansan nang maayos at mahigpit.
original_explanation: This is your mom's standard for your closet. Not just folded, but **limpit**. Everything is stacked perfectly, no wasted space, ready for inspection. Think of how you pack for a trip when you're trying to avoid paying for extra baggage—every square inch counts. That's the art of paglilimpit. It's Marie Kondo before Marie Kondo.
usage_notes: Often used as a verb 'limpitin' (to pack neatly) or as an adjective 'nakalimpit' (is neatly packed).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakalagay sa isang kahon ang mga gamit na **limpit** na **limpit**.","translation":"The things that were **packed very neatly** were placed in a box."},{"sentence":"Inutusan niya akong **limpitin** ang mga aklat sa estante.","translation":"He ordered me to **stack** the books neatly on the shelf."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos o damdamin ng pagtingin nang mababa sa isang tao; pag-aalipusta o paghamak.
etymology: From `pang-` + a variation of `mata` (eye), implying the use of one's eyes to look down on others.
original_explanation: This is that 'judging you' look. The ultimate side-eye. It's when someone looks at you like you're something they scraped off their shoe. That feeling you get when a sosyal officemate sees you eating instant pancit canton for lunch. It’s more than just looking, it’s a whole statement of superiority packed into one dismissive glance.
usage_notes: A strong word describing a condescending attitude shown through looks or actions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko makakalimutan ang **pangmamata** sa akin ng dati kong amo.","translation":"I will never forget the **condescension** my former boss showed me."},{"sentence":"Ramdam ko ang **pangmamata** sa kanyang bawat salita.","translation":"I could feel the **contempt** in his every word."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi maaaring daanan o malakbay, karaniwan dahil sa sagabal, kasikipan, panganib, o pagiging pribado.
original_explanation: EDSA during a flash flood. Or the hallway outside your room when your mom is mopping the floor. It's a literal 'you shall not pass' situation, enforced by nature or a determined parent.
usage_notes: Typically used for roads, paths, or areas that are physically blocked or obstructed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **di-maraanan** ang kalsada dahil sa bumagsak na puno.","translation":"The road became **impassable** because of a fallen tree."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa baha, maraming lugar sa Metro Manila ang **di-maraanan**.","translation":"Because of the flood, many places in Metro Manila are **inaccessible**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pamahalaan kung saan ang kapangyarihan ay nasa kamay ng isang maliit at piling pangkat ng mga mamamayan na itinuturing na nakatataas dahil sa kanilang yaman, angkan, o katayuan sa lipunan.
original_explanation: Basically, the original 'old money' squad. Think of the powerful, land-owning families in historical teleseryes who look down on everyone else. They're the ones with names like de la Cruz y de la Torre, who rule society not by votes, but by birthright and fabulous wealth. The OG 'conyo'.
usage_notes: A concept from political science and history.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Pransiya ay dating pinamumunuan ng isang **aristokrasya** bago ang rebolusyon.","translation":"France was formerly ruled by an **aristocracy** before the revolution."},{"sentence":"Maraming bansa ang tumalikod na sa sistema ng **aristokrasya**.","translation":"Many countries have already abandoned the system of **aristocracy**."}]

translation: to be able to utter or say
meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang mabigkas, masabi, o maipahayag ang isang salita o kaisipan.
etymology: ma- (potential prefix) + turan (to say, to mention)
original_explanation: When you're so shocked, angry, or kilig that you're literally speechless. "Hindi ko **maturan** ang nararamdaman ko!" It's the verb for when words fail you. It's a bit more formal and poetic than just saying "hindi ko masabi." It’s what happens when you see your crush and your brain just blue-screens.
usage_notes: A more formal or literary synonym for "masabi." Often used in the negative to express being speechless.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang gulat, wala siyang **maturan** ni isang salita.","translation":"Due to extreme shock, he couldn't **utter** a single word."},{"sentence":"Subukan mong **maturan** ang iyong tunay na saloobin.","translation":"Try to **be able to say** your true feelings."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kakanin mula sa Pilipinas na gawa sa galapong (harinang bigas) at gata ng niyog, na niluluto sa isang terracotta na hurno na may uling sa ibabaw at ilalim. Karaniwang inihahain tuwing Kapaskuhan.
etymology: Possibly from a Malay cognate, related to the Goan dessert 'bebinca'.
original_explanation: The official Christmas season food! You smell this being cooked outside the church after Simbang Gabi. It's that fluffy, slightly sweet rice cake topped with salted egg, cheese, and niyog. Best paired with hot tsokolate and a cool December breeze. It’s not just a kakanin; it's a core memory.
usage_notes: A type of 'kakanin' (rice-based delicacy). Strongly associated with Christmas in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng Simbang Gabi, kumain kami ng mainit na **bibingka** at puto bumbong.","translation":"After the Dawn Mass, we ate hot **bibingka** and puto bumbong."},{"sentence":"Nag-uwi si nanay ng **bibingka** na may itlog na maalat.","translation":"Mom brought home **bibingka** with salted egg."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang introduksiyon o pambungad na pananalita sa isang aklat, dula, o anumang akda, na karaniwang isinulat ng may-akda o ibang tao.
original_explanation: This is the part of the book you probably skip to get to the good stuff, 'yung Chapter 1 agad. It's like the author's "A little something about me and this book before we begin..." speech. Parang disclaimer sa unahan ng YouTube video.
usage_notes: Used almost exclusively in literary or academic contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakalagay sa **paunang-sabi** ng libro ang pasasalamat ng manunulat.","translation":"The author's acknowledgments are written in the book's **foreword**."},{"sentence":"Ang **paunang-sabi** ay nagbigay ng konteksto sa mga pangyayari sa nobela.","translation":"The **prologue** gave context to the events in the novel."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng biglaang hinala, sapantaha, o masamang pangitain, na maaaring sabay na naramdaman ng dalawa o higit pang tao.
original_explanation: Yung sabay kayo ng nanay mo na nakaramdam na may mali. 'Parang may hindi tama,' sabay pa kayo. It's that shared spidey-sense, that gut feeling that something's up, usually something bad. The universe sending the same bad vibes text to multiple recipients.
usage_notes: The `magka-` prefix implies a sudden onset of the feeling. It can be used for a single person experiencing a sudden hunch, or multiple people sharing one.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigla akong **nagkakutob** na baka may nangyaring masama.","translation":"I suddenly **had a hunch** that something bad might have happened."},{"sentence":"**Nagkakutob** ang mag-ina nang hindi pa umuuwi ang kanilang padre de pamilya.","translation":"The mother and child **had a shared premonition** when the head of the family had not yet come home."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangkalahatang saloobin, opinyon, o pakiramdam ng mga mamamayan ng isang bansa o komunidad hinggil sa isang partikular na isyu.
original_explanation: This is the 'vibe' of the nation. It's what's trending on Twitter, the main topic in the barbershop, and what your taxi driver is ranting about. When everyone's fired up about a political scandal or celebrating a win by a Filipino athlete, that's damdaming-bayan. It's the collective 'feels' of the Filipino people.
usage_notes: Often used in political commentary, news reports, and social analysis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinusubukan ng mga politiko na makuha ang **damdaming-bayan** bago ang eleksyon.","translation":"Politicians try to capture the **public sentiment** before the election."},{"sentence":"Ang pagtaas ng presyo ng bilihin ay salungat sa **damdaming-bayan**.","translation":"The increase in the price of goods goes against **public sentiment**."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi naiiba sa karamihan; walang espesyal na katangian; normal.
original_explanation: This is your basic, no-frills, vanilla ice cream kind of situation. It's not special, not extra, just the everyday stuff. Think of it as the 'general admission' ticket of life, not the VIP pass. It's the default setting.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang mga bagay, sitwasyon, o tao na hindi katangi-tangi o pambihira.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pangkaraniwan** lang ang suot niyang damit pero bagay sa kanya.","translation":"The clothes she was wearing were just **ordinary**, but they suited her."},{"sentence":"Isang **pangkaraniwan** na araw lang ito sa opisina, maraming trabaho at kaunting tsismis.","translation":"It's just another **usual** day at the office, with lots of work and a little gossip."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubhang kagalang-galang; karapat-dapat sa mataas na pagtingin at pagpipitagan.
original_explanation: This is next-level 'lodi'. It's not just 'respeto', it's the kind of respect you give to a National Artist, a highly esteemed elder, or a religious figure. It’s the vibe you get when someone walks into a room and everyone just knows they're in the presence of greatness. The opposite of 'cancel culture'.
usage_notes: A very formal and poetic word. Used to describe people, institutions, or traditions held in very high esteem.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **kapita-pitagan** na hukom ang hahawak sa kaso.","translation":"A **venerable** judge will handle the case."},{"sentence":"Ang Santo Papa ay isang **kapita-pitagan** na pinuno ng Simbahan.","translation":"The Pope is a **revered** leader of the Church."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagluluto o paggawa ng bukayo, isang uri ng matamis na minatamis na gawa sa kinayod na niyog at asukal.
etymology: From `mag-` (verb-forming prefix) + `bukayo` (a type of coconut candy).
original_explanation: This is the verb for creating that super sweet, chewy, coconut-y goodness that is bukayo. It's a labor of love that involves a lot of stirring (and potential arm muscle gain). When someone says they're going to `magbukayo`, you know you're in for a diabetic-but-worth-it treat. It's the ultimate pasalubong from a trip to the province.
usage_notes: A very specific verb related to cooking a particular Filipino delicacy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing pista, laging **nagbubukayo** si Lola para sa mga apo niya.","translation":"During the fiesta, Grandma always **makes bukayo** for her grandchildren."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang taong nagmamay-ari at karaniwang namamahala sa isang tindahan.
original_explanation: The 'Aling Nena' or 'Mang Berto' of the neighborhood. This is the person who knows all the local chismis, decides whether to give you 'utang,' and is the master of the 'Tingî' system (selling items in small portions). The may-ari ng tindahan is a pillar of the community, your go-to for a single egg, a sachet of shampoo, or the latest news on the block.
usage_notes: A specific and very common noun phrase, often referring to the owner of a small, local shop like a sari-sari store.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabait ang **may-ari ng tindahan** sa kanto, pinapautang niya kami.","translation":"The **store owner** on the corner is kind, they let us buy on credit."},{"sentence":"Nakausap mo na ba ang bagong **may-ari ng tindahan**?","translation":"Have you spoken to the new **store owner**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Sabay-sabay at malakas na pagsigaw ng maraming tao, karaniwang nagpapahayag ng matinding damdamin tulad ng tuwa, galit, o pagsuporta.
etymology: From "hiyaw" (shout) + "-an" (suffix indicating a place or collective action).
original_explanation: That moment in a concert when the artist finally comes out and everyone just loses it. Or when your team scores the winning basket in the final second. It's the collective 'Wooooo!' of the Filipino crowd, a sound that can be either pure joy or pure rage.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of crowds, concerts, sporting events, or even protests.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig sa buong barangay ang **hiyawan** nang manalo si Catriona Gray.","translation":"The **cheering** was heard throughout the whole neighborhood when Catriona Gray won."},{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng malakas na **hiyawan** at palakpakan pagkatapos ng kanyang talumpati.","translation":"There was loud **shouting** and applause after his speech."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang yunit ng tunog sa pagsasalita na binubuo ng isang patinig o kombinasyon ng patinig at katinig, na binibigkas sa isang bugso ng hininga.
original_explanation: The building blocks of words you had to clap out in Grade 1. 'Ma-gan-da.' Three claps, three syllables! It's how you break down long and complicated words... like your ex's convoluted explanation for why they cheated.
usage_notes: A fundamental concept in Filipino linguistics and phonology.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang salitang 'pag-ibig' ay may tatlong **pantig**.","translation":"The word 'pag-ibig' has three **syllables**."},{"sentence":"Pinapalakpak ng mga bata ang bawat **pantig** ng kanilang pangalan.","translation":"The children clap each **syllable** of their names."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghuhugas ng mga ginamit na plato, baso, kubyertos, at iba pang kagamitan sa pagkain.
original_explanation: The final boss battle after every Filipino fiesta. This is the chore that decides who *really* loves the family. It's the reason paper plates were invented. Often used as a threat: 'Sige, ikaw ang mag-uurong mamaya!'
usage_notes: This is the most common meaning of 'mag-urong' in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang nakatoka na **mag-urong** ng mga plato ngayong gabi?","translation":"Whose turn is it to **wash the dishes** tonight?"},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos kumain, ugaliin nating **mag-urong** kaagad.","translation":"After eating, let's make it a habit to **wash the dishes** immediately."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking piraso o dahon ng papel, lalo na kapag ito ay nakatupi. Ginagamit din upang tukuyin ang isang pormal na dokumento o hanay ng mga kondisyon.
original_explanation: Before we had PDFs, we had the 'pliego'. This is that big sheet of paper, like Manila paper or cartolina, that you had to fold perfectly for a school project. In a more formal sense, it's a document with a list of conditions, like the 'pliego de cargos'—a list of charges na parang 'yung listahan ng mga kasalanan mo sa jowa mo.
usage_notes: Now considered somewhat formal or technical. More common in legal or historical contexts. The term 'pliego ng papel' is sometimes used to emphasize 'sheet of paper'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili ka ng isang **pliego** ng kartolina para sa ating report.","translation":"Buy one **sheet** of cartolina for our report."},{"sentence":"Nakatala sa **pliego** de kondisyones ang lahat ng alituntunin ng kontrata.","translation":"All the rules of the contract are listed in the **document** of conditions."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalapat ng takip, pinto, o anumang maaaring isara upang hindi na ito bukas. Maaari ring tumukoy sa pagtatapos ng operasyon ng isang negosyo. Ito ay nasa aspektong perpektibo.
original_explanation: What your favorite milk tea shop did right when you were craving it most. Also, what your heart did after that last painful "break na tayo." #NagsaraAngPuso
usage_notes: Can mean physically closed (a door) or conceptually closed (a business). Completed aspect of 'magsara'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagsara** ang tindahan nang maaga dahil umuulan.","translation":"The store **closed** early because it was raining."},{"sentence":"Pakitingnan kung sino ang hindi **nagsara** ng pinto ng refrigerator.","translation":"Please check who didn't **close** the refrigerator door."}]

meaning_filipino: Palaging nagtatagumpay o nananalo sa mga laban, paligsahan, o anumang uri ng kumpetisyon.
original_explanation: That friend who always wins at board games, raffle draws, and in life. The Hidilyn Diaz or Manny Pacquiao of your barkada. They just have that winner's aura. The opposite of 'laging talo' or 'sana all.' Sila 'yung 'ako all.'
usage_notes: Describes a person or a team that has a consistent history of winning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinilala ang kanilang koponan bilang **mapagwagi** sa larangan ng basketball.","translation":"Their team was recognized as **victorious** in the field of basketball."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglalagay ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay pera, sa sariling bulsa; madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng pagnanakaw o pagkuha ng hindi sa iyo.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na 'embolsar' (to put in a bag/pocket).
original_explanation: The classic move of a corrupt official. Yung budget para sa kalsada, biglang napunta sa 'bulsa' niya. It's not just putting something in your pocket; it's taking what's not yours and hiding it for yourself. The verb form of 'kurakot.'
usage_notes: May matinding negatibong konotasyon, na nagpapahiwatig ng pagnanakaw o katiwalian.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May hinala silang **inimbulsa** ng kahero ang bahagi ng benta.","translation":"They suspect the cashier **pocketed** a portion of the sales."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **imbulsa** ang perang hindi sa iyo.","translation":"Do not **pocket** the money that is not yours."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng nilalaman sa social media na sadyang idinisenyo upang hikayatin ang mga tao na mag-iwan ng reaksyon, komento, o ibahagi ito, kadalasan sa pamamagitan ng mga mapanlinlang o mababaw na paraan upang mapataas ang 'engagement'.
original_explanation: Yung mga post na, "LIKE kung naniniwala ka kay Lord, SCROLL kung kampi ka kay Satanas." or "Anong kulay ng brief mo? Comment below!" Ginagawa 'to ng mga pages para lang dumami ang likes at shares nila para masabi ng algorithm na 'relevant' sila. It's the social media equivalent of a 'papansin' friend.
usage_notes: Isang modernong katawagan sa digital marketing at social media. Madalas itong ituring na negatibong taktika.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puro **engagement bait** na lang ang nakikita ko sa Facebook feed ko, tulad ng 'Type AMEN'.","translation":"All I see on my Facebook feed is **engagement bait**, like 'Type AMEN'."},{"sentence":"Binawasan ng algorithm ang reach ng mga post na gumagamit ng **engagement bait**.","translation":"The algorithm reduced the reach of posts that use **engagement bait**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-iiwan o pagtitiwala ng isang habilin sa isang tao.
original_explanation: 'Hey, can I leave this with you?' This is the act of making someone your 'habilinan' (the noun). 'Bes, **habilinan** ko muna sa'yo 'tong laptop ko, ha? CR lang ako.' It's the official term for 'pakibantay muna nito.'
usage_notes: This is a verb, specifying the action of entrusting something to a specific person or place.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puwede bang **habilinan** muna kita ng mga gamit ko?","translation":"Can I **entrust** my things to you for a while?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbato o pagtapon ng isang bagay patungo sa isang partikular na tao, bagay, o lugar.
original_explanation: This is what happens in a 'bardagulan' (brawl/argument) when words aren't enough and someone starts throwing shoes. Or more nicely, when you're in a pool and your friend wants you to throw the beach ball *at* them. The focus is on the target receiving the throw.
usage_notes: The -an suffix makes it a locative-focus verb, where the action is directed *towards* a location, person, or object. The object being thrown is usually implied or stated separately.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **hagisan** ng pagkain ang mga aso sa kulungan.","translation":"Don't **throw** food **at** the dogs in the cage."},{"sentence":"**Hagisan** mo ako ng unan, please.","translation":"**Throw** a pillow **at** me, please."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos o proseso ng pagpigil, paghadlang, o pagpapatigil sa pag-unlad o paglaganap ng isang bagay, tulad ng krimen, sakit, o rebelyon.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'stop it right there' move, whether you're talking about crushing a rebellion, ending a pandemic, or just trying to stop the spread of chismis in the office. It's the act of putting a hard, decisive stop to something that's getting out of hand.
usage_notes: Often used in formal contexts related to law enforcement, public health, or politics.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkasugpo** sa epidemya ay naging pangunahing layunin ng pamahalaan.","translation":"The **suppression** of the epidemic became the primary goal of the government."},{"sentence":"Epektibo ang mga bagong batas para sa **pagkasugpo** ng katiwalian.","translation":"The new laws are effective for the **suppression** of corruption."}]

translation: being bedridden; confinement to bed due to illness
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging nakahiga na lamang sa higaan o banig dahil sa malubhang karamdaman o kapansanan.
etymology: From 'pagka-' + 'ratay' (to be bedridden) + 'sa banig' (on the mat).
original_explanation: The ultimate 'sick leave' but not the fun kind. This isn't just a simple flu. This is when you're so sick, you're literally one with your bed (or banig, for that classic provincial feel). It’s a serious state, often used to describe a long and severe illness. Ang pagkaratay sa banig ang dahilan kung bakit may pa-lugaw ang kapitbahay.
usage_notes: A common Filipino idiom to express severe illness.
