usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagdating mo sa pangalawang kanto, **kumaliwa** ka.","translation":"When you get to the second corner, **turn left**."},{"sentence":"Nabalitaan naming **kumaliwa** raw ang mister ni Aling Nena.","translation":"We heard that Aling Nena's husband **cheated on her**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sukdulang antas ng kahihiyan; lubos na nahihiya.
etymology: From the reduplication of 'hiya' (shame) with a '-ng' linker, used for intensification.
original_explanation: This is `hiya` level 99. It's when you're so embarrassed you wish the ground would swallow you whole. Like when your mom shows your baby pictures to your crush, or when you trip in front of a crowd. You're not just shy, you're mortified.
usage_notes: The repetition intensifies the meaning of 'hiya' to its extreme.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hiyang-hiya** ako sa ginawa ko kanina.","translation":"I am **so ashamed** of what I did earlier."},{"sentence":"Nagtago siya sa ilalim ng mesa dahil **hiyang-hiya** siya.","translation":"She hid under the table because she was **mortified**."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing pula o lagyan ng kulay pula ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: When you need to paint the town red, literally. Or when your crush walks by and your cheeks `pulakin` themselves without your permission. Also what happens to your report card when you don't study.
usage_notes: This is the infinitive/command form. Other forms include `pinula` (past), `pinupula` (present), and `pupulakin` (future).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pulakin** ang damit ko ng iyong lipstick.","translation":"Don't **redden** my clothes with your lipstick."},{"sentence":"Nais niyang **pulakin** ang kanyang buhok para sa pista.","translation":"She wants to **dye her hair red** for the festival."}]

translation: to go through a tight space; to wear
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpasok o pagdaan sa isang makipot o masikip na espasyo; maaari ring tumukoy sa akto ng pagbibihis o paglalagay ng damit sa katawan.
original_explanation: This is the verb for squeezing into things. Think of navigating through the packed MRT during rush hour, or a jeepney driver taking a narrow shortcut ('sumuot sa eskinita') to beat traffic. While its root 'suot' also means 'to wear', the verb form 'sumuot' more often emphasizes the 'going into/through' meaning. 'Sinuot' is more commonly used for 'wore'.
usage_notes: 'Sumuot' is often for entering tight spaces. For wearing clothes, 'nagsuot' or 'sinuot' are more common. Ex: 'Nagsuot ako ng jacket.' (I wore a jacket). 'Sumuot ako sa butas.' (I went through the hole).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumuot** ang pusa sa maliit na butas sa bakod.","translation":"The cat **went through** the small hole in the fence."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **sumuot** sa masikip na eskinita para makarating doon.","translation":"You have **to go through** a narrow alley to get there."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pinasingawang tinapay na may palamang karne (karaniwang asado o bola-bola) na nagmula sa lutuing Tsino.
original_explanation: The fluffy, white, steamed bun that's like a warm hug for your stomach. You have to choose your destiny: Asado (sweet pork) or Bola-bola (pork meatball, sometimes with egg). Eating one is a gamble – will you get a mouthful of delicious filling or just a whole lot of bread? It's the perfect on-the-go snack for a busy commuter.
usage_notes: A staple in Filipino-Chinese cuisine and widely popular as a snack. 'Asado' (sweet-style filling) and 'Bola-bola' (meatball filling) are the two most common variants.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si tatay ng **siopao** na asado para meryenda namin.","translation":"Dad bought asado **siopao** for our snack."},{"sentence":"Mas gusto ko ang **siopao** na may itlog na pula sa loob.","translation":"I prefer the **siopao** that has a salted egg inside."}]

translation: to be paired with; to act as a partner
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkilos bilang kapareha ng isang tao sa isang gawain, pagtatanghal, o relasyon sa entablado o pelikula.
original_explanation: This is when your favorite actors finally get paired in a new teleserye, forming a new 'love team.' From KathNiel to DonBelle, 'tumambal' sila to make us all kilig. It's being the other half of a duo, whether on screen or in a group project.
usage_notes: Commonly used in the context of showbiz and entertainment for on-screen pairings (love teams).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Unang beses **tumambal** ang dalawang sikat na artista sa bagong pelikula.","translation":"The two famous actors **were paired** for the first time in the new movie."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng bakal na hugis 'U' na ikinakabit sa kuko ng kabayo upang protektahan ito.
original_explanation: Literally 'iron of a horse.' It's a horseshoe. You see this in provinces where 'kalesas' are still a thing, or in movies with cowboys. It's also considered a lucky charm by some, who hang it over their doors.
usage_notes: This is the literal term for horseshoe.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglagay ang kutsero ng bagong **bakal ng kabayo**.","translation":"The coachman put on a new **horseshoe**."},{"sentence":"May nakasabit na **bakal ng kabayo** sa pinto nila para sa suwerte.","translation":"There's a **horseshoe** hanging on their door for good luck."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang impeksiyon sa bituka na nagdudulot ng matinding pagtatae na may kasamang dugo o mucus.
original_explanation: Ito yung sakit na resulta ng pag-inom ng maruming tubig o pagkain ng kontaminadong pagkain. Basically, your stomach declares war on you. Hindi ito yung simpleng LBM lang, ito yung level-up na version na may 'special effects'.
usage_notes: Medikal na termino na karaniwang ginagamit sa mga konteksto ng kalusugan at bihirang marinig sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon siya ng **disinteria** matapos uminom ng tubig mula sa poso.","translation":"He got **dysentery** after drinking water from the well."},{"sentence":"Ang malinis na tubig ay mahalaga upang maiwasan ang sakit na **disinteria**.","translation":"Clean water is important to prevent **dysentery**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-aalis ng dumi o likido mula sa isang ibabaw gamit ang isang tela o anumang pamunas. Ito ay nasa aspektong pangkasalukuyan.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're the designated taga-punas ng mesa after a family feast. You're not just cleaning, you're erasing the evidence of that extra serving of lechon. "Ma, **nagpupunas** na po ako, pwede na ba mag-cellphone?"
usage_notes: This is the present progressive tense (imperpektibo) of the verb 'magpunas'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay **nagpupunas** ng mga bintana para maging malinaw ang tanawin.","translation":"He/She is **wiping** the windows to make the view clear."},{"sentence":"Laging **nagpupunas** ng pawis ang manlalaro sa gitna ng laban.","translation":"The player is always **woping** his sweat in the middle of the game."}]

translation: a gulp; a swig (of a drink)
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng mabilis at malakas na pag-inom ng likido, karaniwang sa isang lagukan lamang.
original_explanation: That sound you make when you chug your drink. It's the 'glug-glug' of Friday night inuman sessions. 'Isang **tungga** lang, ubos agad ang isang bote ng beer.' It’s the action, the sound, and the result all in one.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in the context of drinking, often alcoholic beverages. Also used as a verb root.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa isang **tungga** ay inubos niya ang laman ng baso.","translation":"In one **gulp**, he finished the contents of the glass."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang teorya sa sikolohiya na naglalarawan sa kalikasan ng emosyonal na ugnayan sa pagitan ng mga tao, karaniwang nabubuo sa pagkabata.
original_explanation: Bes, kaya ka siguro 'anxious' o 'avoidant' sa relationships mo, baka 'yan ang attachment style mo. Ito 'yung pattern kung paano ka kumapit (o umiwas) sa mga taong mahal mo, na nagsimula pa noong baby ka at kung paano ka inalagaan ng nanay mo. #SanaAllSecure
usage_notes: Isang modernong konseptong sikolohikal na madalas gamitin sa mga talakayan tungkol sa relasyon. Hindi ito isang tradisyonal na salitang Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan niya ang kanyang **attachment style** para maintindihan ang kanyang mga reaksyon sa pag-ibig.","translation":"She is studying her **attachment style** to understand her reactions in love."}]

meaning_filipino: Itinuturing na kapangyarihang nagtatakda ng mga pangyayari sa hinaharap na hindi kayang baguhin o iwasan ng tao.
original_explanation: Yung script na sinulat ni Lord para sa'yo. Kahit anong re-route mo sa Waze ng buhay, doon ka pa rin babagsak. Minsan happy ending, minsan may plot twist na 'di mo in-expect. The ultimate 'bahala na' justification.
usage_notes: Isang salitang may malalim na konotasyong pangkultura at kadalasang ginagamit sa mga usapang romantiko o pilosopikal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naniniwala siyang **tadhana** ang naglapit sa kanila.","translation":"She believes that **destiny** brought them together."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong isisi sa **tadhana** ang iyong mga maling desisyon.","translation":"Don't blame **destiny** for your wrong decisions."}]

translation: to give a reason; to cause
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalahad ng paliwanag o katwiran para sa isang kilos o pangyayari; ang pagiging sanhi ng isang resulta.
original_explanation: To give a reason, an excuse, or a justification. It's what you do when your mom asks why you came home late. It can also mean 'to cause' something. Your ex's 'panloloko' might 'magbigay-dahilan' for your trust issues. It's the verb that bridges action and consequence, or action and explanation. The national sport of 'palusot' is an art form of this.
usage_notes: Can be neutral (to explain) or negative (to make excuses). Context is everything.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magbigay-dahilan** kung bakit ka nahuli sa klase.","translation":"You need **to give a reason** why you were late for class."},{"sentence":"Ang kanilang pag-aaway ay **nagbigay-dahilan** upang maghiwalay ang banda.","translation":"Their fighting **caused** the band to break up."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sangay ng heolohiya na gumagamit ng mga prinsipyo ng heolohiya upang muling buuin at maunawaan ang kasaysayan ng Daigdig, kabilang ang pag-aaral sa mga fossil at stratigraphy.
original_explanation: This is basically 'CSI: Earth.' Instead of solving a crime from last night, these geologists are solving mysteries from 200 million years ago. They look at layers of rock like pages in a history book to figure out what the planet was like back when dinosaurs were the ones complaining about traffic.
usage_notes: Isang akademikong larangan sa loob ng heolohiya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa pamamagitan ng **heolohiyang pangkasaysayan**, nalaman natin ang tungkol sa mga sinaunang anyo ng buhay sa mundo.","translation":"Through **historical geology**, we learned about the ancient life forms on earth."}]

meaning_filipino: Isdang pinatuyo sa araw o sa ibang paraan upang mapreserba, karaniwang kinakain bilang ulam.
etymology: Mula sa pang-uring 'tuyo' (dry), na tumutukoy sa paraan ng paghahanda nito.
original_explanation: The ultimate Pinoy breakfast staple, best paired with sinangag (garlic fried rice) and itlog (egg) - the legendary 'TuySiLog'. It's that salty, crispy, and aromatic (some would say smelly, but we call it aromatic) ulam that will make you ask for extra rice. Don't forget the suka (vinegar) with sili!
usage_notes: Refers specifically to dried fish, often herring or sardines. A sub-category of 'daing'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagprito si nanay ng **tuyo** para sa almusal.","translation":"Mom fried some **dried fish** for breakfast."},{"sentence":"Amoy **tuyo** ang buong bahay tuwing umaga.","translation":"The whole house smells like **dried fish** every morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na lumilipat mula sa isang lugar patungo sa iba, lalo na kung sa ibang bansa, upang manirahan doon nang permanente o pansamantala.
original_explanation: Sila yung mga Pinoy na nag-e-excel abroad at nagiging OFW, pero in a more general sense. Ito yung kamag-anak mong nasa Canada na laging nagpo-post ng snow, o yung kaibigan mong nasa US na biglang may accent na. They're chasing a different kind of dream, often fueled by a desire to help their family back home.
usage_notes: "Mandarayuhan" is the formal term. In everyday speech, people often use more specific terms like "OFW" (Overseas Filipino Worker), "immigrant", or simply say "nasa abroad". The English word "migrant" is also understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming Pilipinong **mandarayuhan** ang nagsisikap sa ibang bansa para sa kanilang pamilya.","translation":"Many Filipino **migrants** work hard in other countries for their families."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bahagya o di-gaanong mataas na lagnat; pakiramdam ng banayad na init o pamamanhid sa katawan.
original_explanation: It's that "Am I getting sick?" feeling. Not a full-blown lagnat, but a low-grade fever or a warm, prickly sensation that makes you want to curl up with a blanket and a cup of salabat. It's the body's pre-game show for a potential flu.
usage_notes: Often used to describe the initial stages of a fever or a tingling feeling from poor circulation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **galamgam** ako kaya hindi muna ako papasok sa trabaho.","translation":"I have a **slight fever**, so I won't go to work first."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang **galamgam** sa kanyang mga daliri matapos itong maipit.","translation":"She felt a **tingling sensation** in her fingers after they got pinched."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mga pagsubok, hirap, o karanasang kakaharapin o pinagdadaanan ng isang tao.
original_explanation: This is the official word for 'the struggle.' When your lola says, 'Marami ka pang *pagdaraanan* sa buhay,' she's not talking about traffic on EDSA (though that counts). She's talking about all the heartbreaks, challenges, and adulting problems you have yet to face. It’s your character development arc.
usage_notes: Refers to future or ongoing trials and challenges. It is the future/contemplated form of the verb 'pagdaanan' (to go through) used as a noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lahat tayo ay may kanya-kanyang **pagdaraanan** sa buhay.","translation":"We all have our own **ordeals** to go through in life."},{"sentence":"Tiwala lang, malalampasan mo rin ang lahat ng iyong **pagdaraanan**.","translation":"Just have faith, you will also overcome all your **trials**."}]

meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng dingding ang isang lugar o istruktura.
original_explanation: When your personal space is being invaded, you dingdingan it. Literally, it's what carpenters do. Figuratively, it's what you do when you put up emotional walls after a bad breakup. "Ayoko na, dinidingdingan ko na ang puso ko."
usage_notes: Anyong pandiwa ng 'dingding'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **dingdingan** ang likod-bahay para maging pribado.","translation":"We need **to put a wall around** the backyard for privacy."},{"sentence":"**Dinidingan** na ng karpintero ang bagong kwarto.","translation":"The carpenter is now **putting up the walls** for the new room."}]

translation: to throw away, to dispose of, to waste
meaning_filipino: Ihagis o ilagay sa basurahan ang isang bagay na hindi na kailangan o gamit; maaari ring mangahulugang aksayahin.
etymology: From i- (causative verb prefix) + tapon (throw, waste).
original_explanation: The classic "Tapos na, pwede nang itapon." This applies to trash, leftovers, and sadly, for some, relationships (charot!). It's the final act of decluttering your room and your life. "Itapon mo na 'yan" is the advice you give your friend who's still keeping their ex's old shirt. It can also mean to waste an opportunity: "Huwag mong itapon ang pagkakataon."
usage_notes: Can mean literal disposal of garbage or metaphorical wasting of things like time, money, or opportunities.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **itapon** ang basura kung saan-saan.","translation":"Don't **throw** your trash just anywhere."},{"sentence":"Sayang ang tiwala niya, para mo na ring **itinapon**.","translation":"His trust is wasted, it's as if you just **threw it away**."}]

translation: to let hang loosely; to dangle
meaning_filipino: Hayaang nakabitin o nakalaylay nang maluwag ang isang bagay, tulad ng damit o buhok.
original_explanation: 'Yung suot mong damit na sobrang laki sa'yo, parang hiniram mo sa kuya mo? That's 'nakalawlaw'. Or when you're too tired to even fix your hair and you just let it hang. Pwede ring "Huwag mong ilawlaw 'yang paa mo sa bintana ng bus!"
usage_notes: The verb form 'ilawlaw' means to cause something to hang loosely. The adjective form is 'lawlaw' or 'nakalawlaw'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Inilawlaw** niya ang kanyang basang tuwalya sa sampayan.","translation":"She **let** her wet towel **hang loosely** on the clothesline."},{"sentence":"Bakit mo naman **inilalawlaw** 'yang dila mo?","translation":"Why are you **dangling** your tongue out?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pag-aayos ng pagkain sa hapag-kainan upang pagsaluhan.
original_explanation: This is the official verb for 'put the food on the table, it's time to eat!' It's more formal than just dumping the Tupperware on the table; it implies presentation, setting the table for others to eat. It's what your mom tells you to do when guests are over. 'Tulungan mo akong **manghain** ng hapunan.' (Help me serve dinner.)
usage_notes: Often used in the context of meals for a family or guests. The command form is 'Maghain ka.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagod man galing sa trabaho, nagawa pa rin niyang **manghain** ng masarap na pagkain para sa kanyang pamilya.","translation":"Even though she was tired from work, she still managed **to serve** delicious food for her family."},{"sentence":"Tayo na at **manghain** dahil darating na ang mga bisita.","translation":"Let's go and **serve the food** because the visitors are about to arrive."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging hindi angkop, hindi wasto, o hindi nararapat para sa isang partikular na sitwasyon, layunin, o tao.
original_explanation: It's that awkward feeling when you wear a gown to a beach party, or when you crack a "That's what she said" joke during a company-wide town hall with the CEO. It's the mismatch between a thing and its context. The cringey feeling of something being out of place.
usage_notes: A formal term. In casual conversation, people might say 'hindi bagay', 'hindi angkop', or 'wala sa lugar'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita ng komite ang **di-pagkaangkop** ng kanyang kasuotan para sa okasyon.","translation":"The committee noted the **inappropriateness** of his attire for the occasion."},{"sentence":"Ang **di-pagkaangkop** ng mga materyales ang naging sanhi ng pagguho ng istruktura.","translation":"The **unsuitability** of the materials caused the structure to collapse."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hanay ng mga pindutan o tiklado (key) sa isang instrumento tulad ng piyano, organ, o makinilya na pinipindot upang makalikha ng tunog o letra.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'tipa' (pagpindot sa tiklado) at hulaping '-an' (lugar o kagamitan).
original_explanation: Your mechanical keyboard that costs more than your monthly rent. Or the keys on your lola's old-school piano. It's the physical interface for your fingers to do their magic, whether you're coding, writing your thesis, or playing "Für Elise." Before QWERTY, there was the 'tipaan'.
usage_notes: Maaari ring tumukoy sa paraan ng pagtipa. Medyo pormal o luma na ang termino at mas karaniwan nang ginagamit ang salitang hiram na "keyboard".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malambot ang **tipaan** ng bagong piyano.","translation":"The **keyboard** of the new piano is soft to the touch."},{"sentence":"Nasira ang ilang letra sa **tipaan** ng lumang makinilya.","translation":"Some letters on the **keyboard** of the old typewriter were broken."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang muling pagbabalik sa buhay mula sa kamatayan; ang panunumbalik ng sigla o muling pag-iral.
original_explanation: The OG comeback story. Think Jesus during Easter, or your favorite K-drama character who 'died' in Episode 10 but is back for Season 2. Also applies to your career after a major failure, or your love life after a 'ghosting' incident. #PagkabuhayNgFeelings.
usage_notes: Madalas na may kontekstong relihiyoso (Pagkabuhay na Mag-uli), ngunit maaari ring gamitin sa metaporikal na paraan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Pasko ng **Pagkabuhay** ay isang mahalagang selebrasyon para sa mga Kristiyano.","translation":"Easter **Resurrection** is an important celebration for Christians."},{"sentence":"Ang muling pagbubukas ng negosyo ay tila isang **pagkabuhay** para sa mga empleyado.","translation":"The reopening of the business was like a **revival** for the employees."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mabigat at bilog na bola na ginagamit sa laro ng boling (bowling).
original_explanation: That heavy thing you try to roll straight down the lane but always ends up in the gutter. Choosing a bola ng boling is a serious commitment—too light and it's weak, too heavy and you might dislocate your shoulder. It's the key to getting a strike or just looking silly in those rented shoes.
usage_notes: A straightforward compound noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masyadong mabigat ang **bola ng boling** na napili ko.","translation":"The **bowling ball** I chose is too heavy."},{"sentence":"Bumili siya ng sarili niyang **bola ng boling**.","translation":"He bought his own **bowling ball**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga bagay na may kaugnayan sa isang parokya ng simbahan. Sa mas malawak na kahulugan, ito ay naglalarawan sa pagkakaroon ng isang makitid o limitadong pananaw.
original_explanation: 'Pag ang isip mo ay kasing kitid lang ng eskinita sa inyo. 'Yung aalalahanin mo lang ay 'yung mga bagay sa loob ng barangay o opisina ninyo at wala ka nang pakialam sa labas. Like someone who only listens to their local radio station and thinks it's the best in the world. "Basta taga-atin, magaling."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang eskwelahang pinasukan niya ay isang **parokyal** na paaralan.","translation":"The school he attended is a **parochial** school."},{"sentence":"Sinabihan siyang masyadong **parokyal** ang kanyang pananaw sa mundo.","translation":"He was told that his worldview is too **parochial**."}]

meaning_filipino: Panatilihin sa isang kalagayan, lugar, o posisyon nang matagalan o permanente.
original_explanation: This is what you tell your jowa when the relationship is going great: "Sana ganito na lang tayo palagi." It's the act of trying to make something last forever, like your high score in a game, your savings account balance before the 11.11 sale, or that perfect IG-worthy photo. It's the opposite of "seasonal" or "for a limited time only."
usage_notes: The verb is in the object-focus, imperative/infinitive form. It's a command or a goal to make something stay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pamalagiin** natin ang kapayapaan sa ating komunidad.","translation":"Let us **maintain** peace in our community."},{"sentence":"Ang hamon sa kanila ay **pamalagiin** ang kalinisan ng ilog.","translation":"The challenge for them is to **keep** the river clean permanently."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggalaw o pag-usad sa isang daanan na hindi tuwid at may maraming kurbada o pagliko.
etymology: From `magpa-` (causative prefix) and the reduplicated root `liko` (turn, curve).
original_explanation: This is that Waze route that looks like a snake having a seizure. You know, the "shortcut" your friend insists on that takes you through every back alley and subdivision in Quezon City just to avoid 2 minutes of traffic on EDSA. The road itself is 'paliku-liko', and the driver who takes it 'nagpa-paliku-liko'.
usage_notes: Describes a non-linear path or movement, either literally for a road or figuratively for a convoluted explanation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **magpaliku-liko** ng bus sa matarik na daan paakyat ng Baguio.","translation":"The bus had to **meander** on the steep road going up to Baguio."},{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang **magpaliku-liko** pa sa iyong paliwanag, diretsuhin mo na ako.","translation":"Don't **beat around the bush** with your explanation, just tell me straight."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang masamang pangyayari, sitwasyon, o kalagayan na nagdudulot ng pinsala, panganib, o sakuna sa isang tao.
etymology: From ka- + pahamak + -an. 'Pahamak' itself comes from the root 'hamak' (lowly, debased), meaning something that causes debasement or harm.
original_explanation: This is what your nanay warns you about when you go out late at night. 'Huwag kang gagawa ng ikapapahamak mo!' It's the universe's way of saying 'plot twist!' but the bad kind. It's the consequence of 'bahala na' when 'bahala na' doesn't work out.
usage_notes: A common word used in warnings and describing negative outcomes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagiging pabaya ay maaaring magdulot ng **kapahamakan**.","translation":"Being negligent can lead to **harm**."},{"sentence":"Iniligtas niya ang bata mula sa tiyak na **kapahamakan**.","translation":"He saved the child from certain **peril**."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa pananampalatayang Kristiyano, siya ang Anak ng Diyos at ang sentral na pigura, kinikilala bilang Mesiyas o Tagapagligtas ng sangkatauhan.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "Jesucristo," na mula sa Latin na "Iesus Christus," mula sa Griyegong "Iesous Christos."
original_explanation: The ultimate "Sana All." He turned water into wine, had 12 ride-or-die 'barkada' (though one was a 'marites'), and his comeback story is literally the greatest ever told. In the Philippines, his name is everywhere—on jeepneys, in names, and exclaimed when you stub your toe ("Ay, Jesukristo!"). He's both the holiest figure and the go-to expression for shock.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa mga solemne na kontekstong panrelihiyon at bilang isang karaniwang bulalas ng pagkagulat, pagkadismaya, o sakit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naniniwala ang mga Kristiyano na si **Jesukristo** ay namatay para sa kasalanan ng sanlibutan.","translation":"Christians believe that **Jesus Christ** died for the sins of the world."},{"sentence":"**Jesukristo**, ang mahal na ng sibuyas!","translation":"**Jesus Christ**, onions are so expensive now!"}]

meaning_filipino: Iutos o ipagawa sa iba ang pagkakabit ng isang bagay gamit ang pako.
original_explanation: The 'boss mode' version of `ipako`. This is when you don't want to get your hands dirty or you're just terrible with a hammer. You tell someone else, 'Uy, pakigawa naman.' So instead of doing it yourself, you `ipalako` mo sa kanila. It's the art of delegation, BPO-style.
usage_notes: This is a causative verb, indicating that the subject of the sentence is causing someone else to perform the action of nailing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ipalako** mo na lang sa karpintero ang bago nating bookshelf.","translation":"Just **have the carpenter nail** our new bookshelf."},{"sentence":"Ayokong masaktan ang daliri ko, kaya **ipalalako** ko na lang ito kay Kuya.","translation":"I don't want to hurt my finger, so I'll just **have my older brother nail** this."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang direksiyon o panig na kasalungat ng kanan; tumutukoy sa banda na karaniwang kinaroroonan ng puso ng isang tao.
original_explanation: The opposite of 'kanan'. Kung sa Waze, ito yung "Turn left." Sa politika, ito yung mga aktibista. Sa pagsusulat, ito yung kamay na laging namantsahan ng ink noong elementary. In short, 'yung hindi tama (right). Charot!
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun (the left side) or an adjective (left-handed, left side). Also has political connotations (leftist).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa **kaliwa** ang exit, huwag kang liliko sa kanan.","translation":"The exit is on the **left**, don't turn right."},{"sentence":"Siya ay nagsusulat gamit ang kanyang **kaliwa**ng kamay.","translation":"She writes using her **left** hand."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang teoretikal na pinakamababang posibleng temperatura, kung saan ang lahat ng paggalaw ng mga molekula ay humihinto. Ito ay katumbas ng 0 Kelvin.
original_explanation: "Sero absoluto" is that feeling you get when your crush leaves you on "seen." It's colder than your ex's heart, the theoretical point where all hope and molecular motion just stops. It's the emotional temperature of the friend zone.
usage_notes: A technical term used in physics and chemistry.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa agham, ang **sero absoluto** ang pinakamalamig na temperatura na teoretikal na posible.","translation":"In science, **absolute zero** is the coldest theoretically possible temperature."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagsunod, pagpapasakop, o pag-ayon sa isang utos, kahilingan, o kapangyarihan nang walang pagtutol.
original_explanation: That moment you finally give in to your friend's 'budol' plan even if you know you shouldn't. It's what you do when your mom gives you 'the look'. It's giving up the fight over the TV remote. Pagsuko na 'to, bes.
usage_notes: This is a less common word, with 'pagtalima' or 'pagsunod' being more frequently used. 'Tupa' is a verb root meaning to obey or submit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagtupa** sa utos ng hari ay nagligtas sa kanyang buhay.","translation":"His **submission** to the king's command saved his life."},{"sentence":"Hindi laging kahinaan ang **pagtupa** sa kagustuhan ng nakararami.","translation":"**Yielding** to the will of the majority is not always a weakness."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paraan ng pagluluto sa pamamagitan ng direktang paglalantad ng pagkain sa init mula sa nagbabagang uling, kahoy, o iba pang katulad nito.
original_explanation: The official scent of every Filipino family outing. It's the art of cooking anything from isaw to liempo over hot coals, usually involving a pamaypay made of cardboard and a secret marinade passed down through generations. This is what you do when you want that smoky, delicious, 'kain-na-tayo!' flavor.
usage_notes: A very common term, especially in culinary and social contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Amoy pa lang ng **pag-ihaw** niya ng baboy ay nakakagutom na.","translation":"Just the smell of his **grilling** of the pork is already making me hungry."},{"sentence":"Ang **pag-ihaw** ng isda ay isang masustansyang paraan ng pagluluto.","translation":"**Grilling** fish is a healthy way to cook."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tungkulin o obligasyon na panagutan ang isang gawain, desisyon, o ang resulta nito; pananagutan.
original_explanation: This is "adulting" in one word. It's that heavy feeling when you realize you're the one who has to pay the bills, kill the ipis, and be accountable for your choices. When you mess up at work, you can't just say "my bad"; you have to face your 'kapanagutan'. It's the opposite of "bahala na."
usage_notes: A formal term often used in legal, corporate, or moral contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bawat karapatan ay may kaakibat na **kapanagutan**.","translation":"Every right comes with a corresponding **responsibility**."},{"sentence":"Dapat may **kapanagutan** ang mga opisyal sa kanilang mga aksyon.","translation":"Officials must have **accountability** for their actions."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi maaaring igalaw, pakialaman, o baguhin ang posisyon o katayuan.
etymology: From 'di-' (not) + 'ma-' (ability prefix) + future tense 'gagalaw' from the root 'galaw' (move).
original_explanation: This is your Lola's collection of porcelain figurines on the center table—look but don't touch, or else. It's also the 'final' version of the file on the shared drive that everyone is scared to edit. That file is di-magagalaw.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical objects, abstract concepts like decisions, or people with a lot of power ('untouchable').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa laro ng 'statue dance,' dapat kang manatiling **di-magagalaw** kapag huminto ang musika.","translation":"In the game of 'statue dance,' you must remain **immovable** when the music stops."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang paninindigan sa isyu ay matatag at **di-magagalaw**.","translation":"Her stance on the issue is firm and **immovable**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang gawain ay mag-imbentaryo, magbilang, o mag-ayos ng mga kuwenta at talaan ng pananalapi.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'taga-' (tagagawa), 'pag-' (nagpapangalan), at salitang-ugat na 'tuos' (calculate, account).
original_explanation: The numbers person. Sila yung taga-compute ng gastos, kita, at kung may budget pa ba hanggang sa susunod na sahod. The human calculator of the group, making sure everything adds up, from company finances to the 'ambagan' for the team lunch.
usage_notes: Mahigpit na nauugnay sa pananalapi, accounting, at auditing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinuha ng kumpanya ang serbisyo ng isang mahusay na **tagapagtuos**.","translation":"The company hired the services of an excellent **accountant**."},{"sentence":"Ang **tagapagtuos** ang mag-a-audit ng mga resibo.","translation":"The **auditor** will audit the receipts."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagbibigay ng talumpati o nagsasalita sa harap ng madla. Tumutukoy din sa kagamitang elektroniko na naglalabas ng tunog.
original_explanation: Two types: 1) The person on stage at a seminar trying to keep you awake after a free lunch. 2) The loud, bass-boosted box your neighbor uses for their 7 AM budots practice. Either way, it's all about making noise and getting a message across, whether it's 'synergy' or 'para sa Tiktoke'.
usage_notes: Ang konteksto ng pangungusap ang karaniwang naglilinaw kung ito ay tumutukoy sa isang tao o sa isang elektronikong kagamitan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang panauhing **ispiker** ay isang kilalang negosyante.","translation":"The guest **speaker** is a well-known entrepreneur."},{"sentence":"Pakihinaan mo naman ang **ispiker**, masyadong malakas.","translation":"Please turn down the **speaker**, it's too loud."}]

translation: will cause to drip; will make drip
meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng kilos upang ang isang likido ay tumulo nang paunti-unti o paisa-isa.
original_explanation: Like when you're trying to get the last drop of ketchup from the bottle, or when your officemate asks for a sample of your perfume and you just give them one tiny drop. "Papatakin ko lang 'tong eyedrops."
usage_notes: This is the future tense, causative form of 'patak' (drip). It describes the action of making something drip.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Papatakin** ko na lang ang gamot sa mata ng aso dahil ayaw niyang uminom.","translation":"I will just **make the medicine drip** into the dog's eye because it doesn't want to drink it."},{"sentence":"Isang kutsara lang ang kailangan, kaya **papatakin** mo lang ang toyo.","translation":"Only one tablespoon is needed, so just **let the soy sauce drip**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghahatid ng impormasyon, balita, o kaalaman sa isang tao o pangkat.
original_explanation: Basically, 'to give a heads-up.' This is the formal way of saying 'to let someone know.' Your boss will 'magbigay-alam' about a new company policy via email. It's more formal than just saying 'sabihan mo sila.' Think of it as the official memo in verb form. 'Pa-FYI' but make it corporate.
usage_notes: Often used in formal, official, or written communication.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magbigay-alam** sa opisina kung hindi ka makakapasok.","translation":"You need **to inform** the office if you cannot come to work."},{"sentence":"Sila ang naatasang **magbigay-alam** sa lahat ng miyembro.","translation":"They were tasked **to notify** all the members."}]

meaning_filipino: Dumi ng mga paniki o ibong-dagat na ginagamit bilang pataba sa lupa.
etymology: From Spanish `guano`, which is from Quechua `wanu`.
original_explanation: Basically, high-class poop. It's the dried droppings of bats or seabirds, and it's a fantastic fertilizer. Before you turn your nose up, remember this stuff is organic gold for farmers. Think of it as nature's premium plant food.
usage_notes: Primarily used in agricultural or scientific contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **guwano** mula sa mga kuweba ay mahalagang pataba.","translation":"**Guano** from the caves is a valuable fertilizer."},{"sentence":"Nangongolekta sila ng **guwano** para ibenta sa mga magsasaka.","translation":"They collect **guano** to sell to farmers."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging handa, gising ang diwa, at mabilis tumugon sa anumang mangyayari.
etymology: From `pagka-` (state of being) + `alisto` (alert), from Spanish `listo` (ready, clever).
original_explanation: Your pagkaalisto is what kicks in when you hear a noise at 2 AM and you grab the nearest walis tambo for defense. It's the mindset of a BPO agent during a surprise call audit, or a "marites" when she senses fresh chismis nearby. Stay woke, kumbaga.
usage_notes: Connotes a state of being mentally and physically prepared for action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **pagkaalisto**, naiwasan niya ang aksidente sa daan.","translation":"Because of his **alertness**, he avoided the accident on the road."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ang **pagkaalisto** ng mga guwardiya sa gabi.","translation":"The **vigilance** of the guards at night is necessary."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga ari-arian na hindi maaaring ilipat ng lugar, tulad ng lupa at mga gusali.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "bienes inmuebles" (mga hindi natitinag na pag-aari).
original_explanation: This is some high-level, "I'm signing legal documents" kind of talk. It's the Spanish term for things you can't just pick up and move, like land, a house, or a condo unit. The opposite of your gadgets and furniture (which are 'bienes muebles'). Basically, if you own `biyenes inmuwebles`, you're probably doing okay in life.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa mga legal at pormal na usaping pangnegosyo. Hindi pang-araw-araw na salita.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lupa at bahay ay itinuturing na **biyenes inmuwebles**.","translation":"Land and a house are considered **real estate**."},{"sentence":"Nakasaad sa testamento ang paghahati-hati ng kanyang mga **biyenes inmuwebles**.","translation":"The will states the division of his **immovable properties**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamataas na kapulungan ng mga mambabatas sa isang bansa na may sistemang parlamentaryo.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "parlamento," na galing sa Italyano na "parlamento," mula sa "parlare" (magsalita).
original_explanation: Ito 'yung version ng Congress sa ibang bansa tulad ng UK. Dito nagde-debate at gumagawa ng batas 'yung mga "parlamentaryo". Isipin mo na lang 'yung Batasang Pambansa or Senate, pero iba 'yung tawag at sistema. It's the building and the institution itself.
usage_notes: Katumbas ng "Kongreso" sa konteksto ng Pilipinas, ngunit partikular na tumutukoy sa sangay na tagapagbatas sa isang parlamentaryong sistema ng pamahalaan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng mainitang debate sa **parlamento** tungkol sa bagong buwis.","translation":"There was a heated debate in the **parliament** about the new tax."},{"sentence":"Ang Punong Ministro ay kailangang sumagot sa mga tanong ng **parlamento**.","translation":"The Prime Minister must answer questions from the **parliament**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng pagtataya o pagkalkula sa isang halaga, sukat, o dami nang hindi gumagamit ng eksaktong pagsukat.
original_explanation: This is your go-to skill at the palengke. 'Manong, magkano po lahat?' and before he answers, you've already made a mental calculation. That's you, **tumantiya**. Also applies to project managers estimating timelines or you trying to guess if your salary will last until the next payday.
usage_notes: Used in contexts of budgeting, planning, cooking, or any situation requiring an educated guess about quantity or amount.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **tumantiya** kung ilang tao ang kasya sa loob ng bulwagan.","translation":"He tried **to estimate** how many people would fit inside the hall."},{"sentence":"Magaling **tumantiya** ng sangkap ang lola ko kahit walang panukat.","translation":"My grandmother is good at **estimating** ingredients even without measuring tools."}]

meaning_filipino: Samahan ang isang tao sa pagpunta sa isang lugar o sa paggawa ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: To be someone's +1. Whether it's going to the mall, a concert, or just to the sari-sari store because they're scared of the dark. It's the verb form of 'Sama ka?' (Wanna come?). Can be for moral support, for safety, or just because misery (or fun) loves company.
usage_notes: The root 'akompanya' is rarely used on its own. The verb 'akompanyahan' is common, but the native Tagalog equivalent 'samahan' is more frequently used in casual speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puwede mo ba akong **akompanyahan** sa pagpunta sa doktor?","translation":"Can you **accompany** me to the doctor?"},{"sentence":"Inutusan siyang **akompanyahan** ang bisita pabalik sa hotel.","translation":"He was instructed to **accompany** the guest back to the hotel."}]

meaning_filipino: Puno ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay mga butas, hiwa, o marka; tinadtad o pinira-piraso nang pino.
original_explanation: Parang katawan mo after ng first day sa gym, tadtad ng sakit. O 'yung project mo, tadtad ng revisions galing sa boss mo. Puwede ring 'yung balita, tadtad ng fake news.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin sa literal na paraan (tadtad ng bala) o sa matalinhagang paraan (tadtad ng problema).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang katawan ng sasakyan ay **tadtad** ng butas ng bala.","translation":"The car's body was **riddled** with bullet holes."},{"sentence":"Ang kuwaderno niya ay **tadtad** ng mga drowing.","translation":"His notebook is **full of** drawings."}]

meaning_filipino: Matinding kalungkutan o pighati, lalo na dahil sa isang kawalan o kabiguan.
original_explanation: This is the 'sana all' feeling but in reverse. 'Yung level ng lungkot na pang-MMK (Maalaala Mo Kaya) episode. Hindi lang 'sad', ito 'yung deep, soul-crushing sadness na parang nawalan ka ng 10-year relationship o nakita mong sold out na 'yung concert tickets ng paborito mong K-Pop group.
usage_notes: Often used in literary or formal contexts to describe deep sorrow. Can be used as a noun (grief) or an adjective (grieved).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi maipinta ang **hapis** sa mukha ng biyuda.","translation":"The **grief** on the widow's face was indescribable."},{"sentence":"Isang pusong **hapis** ang naiwan sa kanyang pag-alis.","translation":"A **grieved** heart was left behind upon his departure."}]

translation: To appease; to console; to placate
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakalma o pagpapatahan sa isang tao na galit, nag-aalala, o malungkot sa pamamagitan ng mabubuting salita o gawa.
original_explanation: This is the art of 'making suyò' or damage control. When your partner is mad, you buy them milk tea to **palubagin ang loob** nila. When your boss is stressed, you finish your report ahead of schedule to do the same. It's the act of soothing a ruffled ego, calming a worried mind, or pacifying an angry heart. The ultimate 'pampakalma' move.
usage_notes: A common idiomatic expression. The object being appeased is usually placed after 'ang loob ng [tao]'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang **palubagin ang loob** ng kaniyang kasintahan sa pamamagitan ng pagbibigay ng bulaklak.","translation":"He is trying to **appease** his girlfriend by giving her flowers."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **palubagin ang loob** ng isang taong nasaktan nang husto.","translation":"It's hard to **console** a person who has been deeply hurt."}]

translation: a forcible tear or rip; detachment
meaning_filipino: Ang biglaan at sapilitang pagkapunit, pagkatanggal, o pagkabakbak ng isang bagay mula sa pagkakadikit nito.
original_explanation: Yung tunog ng balat ng manok na tinatanggal mo sa buto. O 'yung pagtanggal ng band-aid sa mabalahibong braso. It's a violent, satisfying (or painful) rip. Parang pag-alis ng ex mo sa buhay mo—biglaan at may bakas na naiwan. Hugot!
usage_notes: Implies force and suddenness. Can refer to skin, bark, labels, etc. Often used to describe something being peeled or stripped away forcefully.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-iwan ng peklat ang **labnit** ng balat sa kanyang braso.","translation":"The **forcible tear** of skin on his arm left a scar."},{"sentence":"Isang malakas na **labnit** lang ang kailangan para matanggal ang takip.","translation":"Just one strong **rip** is needed to remove the cover."}]

translation: to sentence; to pass judgment on
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapataw ng parusa o pagbibigay ng pormal na desisyon sa isang tao o kaso.
original_explanation: This is the action version of 'hatol.' It's what the judge does. 'Hinatulan siya ng habambuhay na pagkabilanggo.' (He was sentenced to life imprisonment). In a less serious context, it's what your friends do when you make a questionable fashion choice. 'Hinatulan ka na nila, baduy daw 'yang suot mo.' It's the act of passing the final verdict.
usage_notes: This is an object-focused verb. The actor-focused form is `humatol` (to judge).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hinirang** ng hukom ang nasasakdal na may sala.","translation":"The judge **sentenced** the defendant as guilty."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong agad **hatulan** ang isang tao batay lamang sa sabi-sabi.","translation":"Don't immediately **pass judgment** on a person based only on rumors."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang plano o guhit na nilikha upang ipakita ang itsura at paggana o pagkakaayos ng isang gusali, damit, o iba pang bagay bago ito gawin.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung dahilan kung bakit ang ganda ng mga cafe sa Instagram. 'Yung layout ng condo mo, 'yung print sa damit mo, 'yung itsura ng phone app mo—lahat 'yan may disenyo. Parang sa buhay, kailangan mo rin ng disenyo o plano, hindi 'yung 'bahala na si Batman.'
usage_notes: A very common word used in art, architecture, fashion, and everyday planning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagustuhan ko ang **disenyo** ng bagong gusali.","translation":"I liked the **design** of the new building."},{"sentence":"Siya ang gumawa ng **disenyo** para sa aming wedding invitation.","translation":"She created the **design** for our wedding invitation."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pahayag sa matematika na nagsasaad ng pagkakapantay-pantay ng dalawang ekspresyon, na karaniwang pinagdurugtong ng simbolong 'equals' (=).
original_explanation: The reason for your high school math trauma. It's that thing with x's and y's that you had to solve. But outside the classroom, it's also used to describe any complex situation. Example: Commute + Rain + Rush Hour = The Ultimate Ekuwasyon for Stress.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang alternatibong baybay ng "ekwasyon", bagaman hindi gaanong karaniwan. Mas pormal na tingnan dahil sa pagkakaroon ng 'u'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko masagutan ang huling **ekuwasyon** sa pagsusulit.","translation":"I couldn't solve the last **equation** on the test."},{"sentence":"Sa buhay, maraming bagay ang hindi masusukat ng simpleng **ekuwasyon**.","translation":"In life, many things cannot be measured by a simple **equation**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hindi inaasahang masamang pangyayari na nagdudulot ng pinsala, kapahamakan, o kahihiyan.
original_explanation: The universe's way of saying 'plot twist!' but in the worst way possible. It's when you trip in public, when your adobo gets burnt, or on a more serious note, a vehicular accident. It's the catch-all term for when things go south. Madalas sinasabi ng mga lola: 'Mag-ingat ka, baka ma-desgrasya ka!'
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang salita na sumasaklaw sa maliliit na aberya hanggang sa malalaking trahedya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nabalitaan naming may nangyaring **desgrasya** sa kanto kaninang umaga.","translation":"We heard an **accident** happened at the corner this morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kilos, galaw, o anumang uri ng reaksyon, pasalita man o hindi. Madalas itong ginagamit sa anyong negatibo ('walang-kibo') na nangangahulugang hindi kumikilos o hindi nagsasalita.
original_explanation: 'Kibo' is like your 'status' or 'activity.' When someone is 'walang kibo,' they're completely still and silent. It’s that friend who suddenly goes quiet in the group chat after a controversial topic is brought up. Or you, pretending to be asleep when your mom comes into the room to ask you to do chores. No movement, no sound, no 'kibo'. It's the art of being unresponsive.
usage_notes: Most frequently used in the negative form 'walang-kibo' or 'di-kumikibo' to mean motionless, silent, or unresponsive.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatayo lang siya roon, **walang-kibo**.","translation":"He just stood there, **motionless**."},{"sentence":"Nang tanungin siya tungkol sa isyu, ni **walang kibo** siyang sinabi.","translation":"When asked about the issue, he didn't even make a **remark**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kagat ng isang ahas o anumang makamandag na hayop, na karaniwang naglalabas ng lason.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'ouchie' from a snake. It's not just a bite; it's a bite with a deadly receipt (venom). When someone says 'natuklaw', you know it's a medical emergency, not just a 'kagat ng langgam'.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to a bite from a venomous creature, most commonly a snake.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Namatay ang kalabaw dahil sa **tuklaw** ng ahas.","translation":"The water buffalo died due to a snake's **venomous bite**."},{"sentence":"Dinala agad siya sa ospital matapos makaranas ng **tuklaw**.","translation":"He was immediately brought to the hospital after suffering a **snakebite**."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga puntos o pabor na nakukuha, lalo na mula sa isang tao, sa pamamagitan ng pagpapakita ng kabaitan, pagiging maginoo, o anumang kaaya-ayang kilos.
etymology: From Tagalog "pogi" (handsome) and English "points". A Taglish compound noun.
original_explanation: This is the currency of a guy trying to win a girl's heart. It's like collecting reward points, but instead of a free coffee, you get a 'seen' message replied to. You get +10 pogi points for opening a door for her, +20 for remembering her favorite milk tea order, and -100 for forgetting your anniversary. It's a high-stakes game.
usage_notes: A colloquial, modern term used in informal conversations, especially among younger generations, to denote earning favor through charming or helpful acts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-volunteer akong magbuhat ng gamit niya para magkaroon ng **pogi points**.","translation":"I volunteered to carry her things to earn some **brownie points**."},{"sentence":"Ay, minus 10 ka na sa **pogi points** ko, kinalimutan mo birthday ko!","translation":"Oh, you're minus 10 on my **pogi points**, you forgot my birthday!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikas o pag-alis mula sa isang lugar na may panganib patungo sa isang mas ligtas na lokasyon.
etymology: Hiram sa salitang Ingles na 'evacuate' at nilapian ng unlaping `mag-`.
original_explanation: The official activity during typhoon season in the Philippines. When PAGASA raises the signal, and your barangay captain starts knocking, it's time to pack your go-bag and **mag-ebakwet** to the nearest covered basketball court or elementary school.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng mga sakuna tulad ng bagyo, baha, o pagputok ng bulkan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **mag-ebakwet** bago pa tumaas ang baha.","translation":"We need to **evacuate** before the floodwaters rise."},{"sentence":"Nag-anunsyo ang LGU na lahat ng residente malapit sa ilog ay dapat nang **mag-ebakwet**.","translation":"The LGU announced that all residents near the river must **evacuate** now."}]

translation: to shoo away, to drive away
meaning_filipino: Pagtataboy o pagpapaalis sa mga hayop, insekto, o kung minsan ay tao, sa pamamagitan ng tunog o kilos.
original_explanation: This is what you do to the fly that won't leave your lumpia alone. Or to the neighborhood cat trying to steal your sinampay. It’s the universal hand-waving, "shoo-shoo" action turned into a verb. In a more serious context, it's also what bouncers do.
usage_notes: While the root word 'bugaw' can also mean 'pimp', the verb 'bumugaw' almost exclusively means 'to shoo away'. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumugaw** siya ng mga ibon na kumakain ng palay.","translation":"He **shooed away** the birds that were eating the rice grains."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **bumugaw** ng mga lamok gamit ang pamaypay.","translation":"She tried to **drive away** the mosquitoes using a fan."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagsasara ng pinto o bintana sa pamamagitan ng aldaba o trangka upang hindi ito mabuksan.
etymology: From Spanish 'aldaba' (door knocker, latch) + Tagalog 'mag-' (verb prefix).
original_explanation: The OG Filipino security system before smart locks. It's that metal hook or wooden bar you slide across the door to make sure no one gets in. It's the verb form of 'i-lock mo, dali!'
usage_notes: Refers specifically to using a latch or bolt, a more physical and often older method than using a key lock.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **mag-aldaba** ng pinto bago matulog.","translation":"Don't forget **to latch** the door before sleeping."},{"sentence":"**Nag-aldaba** siya nang mariin dahil sa takot.","translation":"She **bolted** the door firmly out of fear."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglilipat ng datos o digital file mula sa isang lokal na kompyuter patungo sa isang sentral na server o sa internet.
original_explanation: The modern-day ritual of sharing your life online. From your latest travel pics to that 100-page report your boss needs ASAP. It's the opposite of 'binge-watching' on Netflix; you're the one providing the content for others to consume. 'Pa-wifi, may i-a-upload lang!'
usage_notes: A very common loanword used in digital contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **mag-upload** ng mga litrato mula sa ating bakasyon.","translation":"Don't forget to **upload** the photos from our vacation."},{"sentence":"Ang bagal ng internet, hindi ako makapag-**upload** ng video.","translation":"The internet is so slow, I can't **upload** my video."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi sinasadyang pagkalaglag o pagkawala ng sanggol sa sinapupunan bago pa ito mabuo nang husto.
etymology: From `ma-` (potential prefix) + `agas` (flow, ooze, specifically referring to miscarriage) + `-an` (locative/experiencer suffix).
original_explanation: This is a serious and sensitive topic. Maagasan is when an expectant mother loses her baby unintentionally. It's a heartbreaking experience, a loss that needs to be handled with care and empathy, not with 'hugot' or jokes. It's the body's tragic 'system error' during pregnancy.
usage_notes: This is a specific medical and biological term. It is used in serious contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Labis ang kanyang kalungkutan nang siya ay **maagasan**.","translation":"Her sadness was immense when she **had a miscarriage**."},{"sentence":"Pinayuhan ng doktor ang buntis na mag-ingat nang husto upang hindi **maagasan**.","translation":"The doctor advised the pregnant woman to be very careful so she would not **have a miscarriage**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagkuha o pag-agaw ng mga bagay mula sa isang tao o lugar, kadalasan ay isinasagawa ng may kapangyarihan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "samsam" at idinugtong ang hulaping "-an", na tumutukoy sa lugar o tatanggap ng kilos.
original_explanation: The verb form of the raid. 'Samsaman mo na 'yang charger niya, lagi niyang kinukuha sa'yo.' (Go confiscate his charger, he always takes yours anyway.) It's the act of taking stuff, usually from a specific person or place. Think of a customs officer going through your luggage for undeclared items.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sinamsaman** ng mga pulis ang bahay ng suspek.","translation":"The police **raided** the suspect's house."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **samsaman** ng pagkain ang kapatid mo.","translation":"Don't **confiscate** food from your sibling."}]

translation: to do to the maximum; to push to the limit
meaning_filipino: Itulak o gawin ang isang bagay hanggang sa pinakadulo, sukdulan, o hangganan nito.
original_explanation: Like when you're parking and you reverse until the car almost touches the wall—that's "isinagad mo." Or when you use your data plan until the very last megabyte. It's the "all-in, no holding back" move. "Isagad mo na ang effort sa project na 'to!"
usage_notes: Connotes reaching the absolute limit, edge, or end of something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Isinagad** niya ang upuan sa pader para magkaroon ng mas malaking espasyo.","translation":"He **pushed** the chair **all the way** to the wall to create more space."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang hanapbuhay ay ang pagkatay ng baboy upang gawing karne.
original_explanation: The unsung hero of every lechon, sinigang, and adobo. This is the person you call when it's fiesta time and a pig needs to become... well, food. They have the skills, the tools, and the stomach for a job that's definitely not for the faint of heart.
usage_notes: A compound noun formed from 'magpapatay' (one who slaughters) and 'baboy' (pig). It is a specific job title.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating kumuha ng **magpapatay-baboy** para sa handaan sa pista.","translation":"We need to hire a **pig slaughterer** for the feast at the fiesta."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang kita ng **magpapatay-baboy** tuwing Disyembre.","translation":"A **butcher of pigs** earns a lot during December."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsulat ng sariling pangalan o marka sa isang dokumento bilang tanda ng pagpapatunay, pagsang-ayon, o pag-ako ng responsibilidad.
original_explanation: The final boss of "adulting." You do this to get a job, a loan, a condo, or a marriage certificate. It's the simple act of scribbling your name that can either seal your fate for a 30-year housing loan or get you a free planner from a coffee shop.
usage_notes: Completed aspect (past tense). Present: `pumipirma`, Future: `pipirma`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pumirma** na siya sa kontrata para sa bagong trabaho.","translation":"She already **signed** the contract for the new job."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **pumirma** sa anumang dokumento na hindi mo naiintindihan.","translation":"Don't **sign** any document that you don't understand."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang una o paunang modelo ng isang bagay, tulad ng isang makina o sasakyan, kung saan kinokopya o binubuo ang mga susunod na anyo.
original_explanation: Ito yung 'sample' o 'version 1.0' ng isang imbensyon. Parang yung unang version ng app na puro bugs pa, o yung unang luto mo ng adobo na medyo sablay pa ang timpla. Dito tinitingnan kung ano ang mali at ano ang dapat i-improve bago i-mass produce.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinakita ng mga inhinyero ang **prototipo** ng bagong kotse.","translation":"The engineers presented the **prototype** of the new car."},{"sentence":"Bago ilunsad ang produkto, dumaan muna ito sa maraming pagsubok bilang isang **prototipo**.","translation":"Before the product was launched, it first went through many tests as a **prototype**."}]

meaning_filipino: Masaktan o magkaroon ng pinsala sa balat dahil sa pagkadikit sa isang bagay na napakainit.
original_explanation: That "ouch!" moment when you touch the hot pan without a pot holder. Or when you take a sip of your coffee too soon. It’s the physical version of getting burned. The emotional version is when you find out your crush is "just friends" with you. Parehong masakit. "Ingat sa plantsa, baka mapaso ka."
usage_notes: Refers specifically to burns from heat, not from fire (which would be 'masunog'). This word has a homonym, 'mapaso' (/ma-pa-SO/), which means 'to expire'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-ingat siyang huwag **mapaso** sa mainit na sabaw.","translation":"He was careful not to **get burned** by the hot soup."},{"sentence":"**Napaso** ang kamay ko sa kakalabas na oven toaster.","translation":"My hand **got burned** on the oven toaster that was just used."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pigurang heometriko na may apat na magkakasinghabang gilid at apat na anggulong pare-parehong 90 digri.
etymology: Mula sa salitang "sukat" (measure) na may panlaping "pa-" at gitlaping "-ri-" na nagpapahiwatig ng regular o pare-parehong anyo.
original_explanation: 'Yung shape na parang box, o 'yung tile sa sahig. Perfect for when you need to describe something na "pantay ang lahat ng gilid," unlike your ex's stories. It's the geometric equivalent of a fair and balanced deal.
usage_notes: Maaari ring gamitin bilang pang-uri upang ilarawan ang isang bagay na hugis-kwadrado.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumuhit siya ng isang perpektong **parisukat** sa papel.","translation":"He drew a perfect **square** on the paper."},{"sentence":"Ang mesa ay may disenyong **parisukat**.","translation":"The table has a **square** design."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang tao o sitwasyon na palaging nakararanas ng kamalasan o hindi pinapaboran ng magandang kapalaran.
original_explanation: The feeling when you missed the last seat on the MRT, your Grab got cancelled, and it started raining the moment you decided to walk. Basically, the universe is playing a prank on you. You're "malas."
usage_notes: Interchangeable with "malas". "Suwerte" itself is a very common loanword.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiramdam ko ay **walang-suwerte** ako sa raffle draw.","translation":"I feel like I'm **unlucky** in raffle draws."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong isiping **walang-suwerte** ka, baka hindi pa lang ito ang tamang panahon.","translation":"Don't think you're **unlucky**, maybe it's just not the right time yet."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng paggamit ng kalaykay upang ipunin o linisin ang mga tuyong dahon, basura, o iba pang kalat sa lupa.
original_explanation: The OG way of cleaning the yard before leaf blowers became a thing. It's that chore your parents make you do on a Saturday morning, gathering all the dried leaves and twigs. Good for the arms, but not so much for your weekend plans.
usage_notes: This is a verb of action. The prefix `mag-` indicates the actor is performing the action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magkalaykay** ng mga tuyong dahon sa bakuran.","translation":"We need to **rake** the dry leaves in the yard."},{"sentence":"Tuwing umaga, si Lolo ay nagpupunta sa hardin para **magkalaykay**.","translation":"Every morning, Grandpa goes to the garden to **rake**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal at malalim na salita para sa pangalan o pirma ng isang tao; pagkakakilanlan.
original_explanation: This is the fancy, old-school word for your name or signature. It's not just "Juan dela Cruz," it's his lagyo. Think of it as your official government name versus your nickname "Totoy." When you sign a very important document, you're not just writing your name, you're affixing your lagyo. Ang bigat!
usage_notes: A very formal or literary term. Not used in everyday conversation. 'Pangalan' or 'pirma' are the common equivalents.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **lagyo** ng bayani ay nakaukit sa bantayog.","translation":"The hero's **name** is engraved on the monument."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi kayang pakinggan o hindi abot ng pandinig dahil sa sobrang hina, layo, o ingay.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `di-` (hindi) at `marinig` (kayang pakinggan), na galing sa salitang ugat na `dinig`.
original_explanation: This is you on a Zoom call with bad internet, shouting "Sorry, **di-marinig**!" It's also what you pretend happens when your mom asks you to wash the dishes from the other room. "Ano po? 'Di ko marinig!" Classic.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan ng isang tunog na napakahina, malayo, o natatabunan ng ingay para marinig. Maaaring gamitin nang literal o patalinghaga.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bulong lang siya nang bulong kaya **di-marinig** ang sinasabi niya.","translation":"He just kept whispering so what he was saying was **inaudible**."},{"sentence":"Sa sobrang ingay ng konsiyerto, **di-marinig** ang tawag mo sa telepono.","translation":"Because of the concert's noise, your phone call **could not be heard**."}]

translation: act of opening or browsing a book
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbubukas o paglilipat ng mga pahina ng isang aklat, kuwaderno, o anumang babasahin.
original_explanation: That moment when you're speed-reading for an exam, flipping pages like there's no tomorrow. 'Yung state ng libro mo after mo mag-pull ng all-nighter. It’s the physical action before you can say 'buklatin' or 'basahin'.
usage_notes: Often used as a root word for verbs. As a noun, it refers to the action itself. It can also be used as an adjective meaning 'opened flat' (e.g., 'buklat na ang aklat').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang mabilis na **buklat** lang sa menu at alam na niya ang oorderin.","translation":"Just one quick **browse** of the menu and he already knew what to order."},{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **buklat** ng mga pahina mula sa kabilang kwarto.","translation":"I heard the **flipping** of pages from the other room."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang aksyon ng paghinto, paghadlang, o hindi pagpapahintulot sa isang bagay na magpatuloy, mangyari, o maipahayag.
original_explanation: This is your self-control when you see a 50% off sale but it's still 'petsa de peligro' (danger days before payday). It's the `pagpigil` sa sarili. It’s also what you do when you want to laugh at a serious meeting, or what you feel when you're trying not to cry while watching a sad movie—the `pagpigil` ng iyak. It's the human "pause" or "cancel" button.
usage_notes: A very versatile word. Can be used for actions (`pagpigil sa pag-alis`), emotions (`pagpigil ng tawa`), and abstract concepts (`pagpigil sa pag-unlad`).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **pagpigil** sa pagkalat ng pekeng balita.","translation":"The **prevention** of the spread of fake news is important."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya nakayanan ang **pagpigil** sa kanyang mga luha.","translation":"She couldn't manage the **suppression** of her tears."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagpigil** sa sarili ay isang birtud.","translation":"**Self-restraint** is a virtue."}]

meaning_filipino: Kasalukuyang kumikilos nang mas mabilis kaysa karaniwan dahil sa kakulangan sa oras.
etymology: From "dali" (haste, speed) with the "nag-ma-" prefix and reduplication of the first syllable of the root.
original_explanation: This is the state of being late. You're weaving through crowds in the mall, speed-walking to your next class, or typing furiously to meet a deadline. When someone asks 'Bakit ka nagmamadali?' it's because your frantic energy is palpable. You are currently in the rush.
usage_notes: Refers to the ongoing act of rushing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagi siyang **nagmamadali** tuwing umaga papasok sa trabaho.","translation":"He is always **hurrying** every morning on his way to work."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **nagmamadali** sa pag-ibig, darating din 'yan.","translation":"Don't be **rushing** into love, it will come."}]

translation: To serve (food, customers); to hit the ball (sports)
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghahain ng pagkain o inumin; ang pagbibigay serbisyo sa isang kustomer; ang pagpalo ng bola upang simulan ang laro sa palakasan.
original_explanation: A very versatile word. It's what the waiter does with your adobo. It's what Alyssa Valdez does with a volleyball. It's also what you do when you show up to a party with a killer outfit – you "serve" looks. "Ano'ng i-se-serve natin sa bisita?" (What will we serve the guests?) is a question that haunts every Pinoy host.
usage_notes: A direct loanword from English, commonly used in food service, sports, and increasingly in slang ("serving looks"). Tagalog equivalents are "maghain" (food), "magsilbi" (service), and "pumalo" (sports).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magaling siyang mag-**serve** ng bola sa volleyball.","translation":"She's good at **serving** the ball in volleyball."},{"sentence":"I-**serve** mo na ang pagkain habang mainit pa.","translation":"**Serve** the food while it's still hot."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mapaglarong parirala sa social media na karaniwang ginagamit bilang tugon sa isang tweet, na pinagsasama ang "fancam" at ang slang na "yarn?" (mula sa "iyan?"). Ito ay maaaring paraan ng pag-promote ng idolo, pag-iiba ng usapan, o bilang isang uri ng meme.
etymology: Pinagsamang "fancam" at ang Pinoy slang na "yarn" (isang paglalaro sa "iyan" o "ayan").
original_explanation: The ultimate "anyway..." or "so what?" of Stan Twitter. It's a way to dismiss a topic or a hater by replying with a fancam. Example: "Your idol can't sing!" Reply: "**Fancam yarn**? [inserts a fancam of their idol hitting a high note]". It's a power move, a meme, and a promotion tactic all in one.
usage_notes: Isang internet slang na popular sa mga Pilipinong K-Pop fan sa Twitter. Ang paggamit nito ay nagpapahiwatig ng pagiging pamilyar sa kultura ng Stan Twitter.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinagot niya lang ng \"**fancam yarn**?\" ang basher sa Twitter.","translation":"She just replied \"**fancam yarn**?\" to the basher on Twitter."},{"sentence":"Person A: \"Ang boring ng araw ko.\" Person B: \"**Fancam yarn**? Heto, para sumaya ka.\"","translation":"Person A: \"My day is boring.\" Person B: \"**Fancam yarn**? Here, to make you happy.\""}]

translation: a chase (involving multiple parties); a race
meaning_filipino: Isang sitwasyon ng sabay-sabay na paghabol o pag-uunahan ng dalawa o higit pang panig.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "hagad" na nangangahulugang habol.
original_explanation: Ito yung laro niyo nung bata, yung "habulan". Pero sa adulting world, hagaran ang tawag sa pag-aagawan sa huling piraso ng lechon sa handaan, o sa pag-uunahan makasakay sa MRT 'pag rush hour. It's a competitive chase.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa isang kaganapan o laro ng paghahabulan. Iba sa "hagad" na tumutukoy sa akto mismo ng paghabol.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglaro ng **hagaran** ang mga bata sa parke.","translation":"The children played **chase** in the park."},{"sentence":"Naging **hagaran** ang pagkuha ng promosyon sa opisina.","translation":"Getting the promotion at the office became a **race**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagtuturo o nagbibigay ng kaalaman, kasanayan, o gabay sa mga mag-aaral.
etymology: From Sanskrit 'guru' (गुरु), meaning teacher, master, or spiritual guide.
original_explanation: Your 'ma'am' or 'sir' in school. The unsung hero who had to deal with your kulit days, check your impossible-to-read handwriting, and probably needed a lot of coffee to get through the day. Shoutout to our teachers, the original influencers!
usage_notes: The standard, formal term for a teacher. 'Titser' is a common colloquial alternative.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aking ina ay isang **guro** sa pampublikong paaralan.","translation":"My mother is a **teacher** in a public school."},{"sentence":"Marami akong natutunan sa aking **guro** sa Filipino.","translation":"I learned a lot from my Filipino **teacher**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sukat ng kaluwangan, kalaparan, o saklaw ng isang espasyo, bagay, o konsepto.
etymology: Mula sa Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *lawaq ("kalawakan, bukas na espasyo").
original_explanation: The measurement of your patience when you're in EDSA traffic. It can refer to physical space ('ang lawak ng kwarto!') or the scope of your understanding ('ang lawak ng isip niya'). It's that feeling of "wow, ang laki" or "wow, ang lalim" applied to anything from a rice field to a friend's chismis knowledge.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin para sa pisikal na sukat (area) at abstraktong saklaw (scope). Ang pang-uri nito ay "malawak".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko masukat ang **lawak** ng kanyang pagmamahal sa akin.","translation":"I cannot measure the **breadth** of his/her love for me."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating alamin ang **lawak** ng lupang ito.","translation":"We need to determine the **area** of this land."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gusali o kumplikadong residensyal kung saan ang mga yunit o apartment ay pagmamay-ari ng mga indibidwal, habang ang mga karaniwang lugar ay pagmamay-ari ng lahat.
original_explanation: Ang bahay na 'sky-high' na pangarap ng maraming BPO agent at young professional. Mas kilala bilang 'condo'. May kasamang swimming pool na pang-IG story at gym na 'di mo naman ginagamit. The monthly association dues are the 'hugot' part of living here.
usage_notes: Madalas na pinaikli sa 'condo' sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming bagong **condominium** ang itinatayo sa mga sentro ng kalakalan tulad ng BGC at Makati.","translation":"Many new **condominiums** are being built in business centers like BGC and Makati."},{"sentence":"Nangungupahan siya ng maliit na yunit sa isang **condominium** malapit sa kanyang opisina.","translation":"He is renting a small unit in a **condominium** near his office."}]

meaning_filipino: Nauukol sa demokrasya; batay sa mga prinsipyo ng pagkakapantay-pantay ng mga mamamayan sa karapatan at pagkakataon.
original_explanation: Parang sa group project, 'yung lahat may say, hindi lang 'yung leader na bida-bida. Sa isang demokratikong bansa, in theory, boses ng taumbayan ang masusunod, hindi lang ng iilang nasa kapangyarihan. Parang eleksyon, 'di ba? Bumoto ka, may karapatan kang magreklamo.
usage_notes: Often used in political, social, and academic contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Pilipinas ay isang **demokratiko**ng bansa.","translation":"The Philippines is a **democratic** country."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating magkaroon ng isang **demokratiko**ng proseso sa pagpili ng ating mga lider.","translation":"We need to have a **democratic** process in choosing our leaders."}]

meaning_filipino: Pasanhiin o maging dahilan ng pag-iyak ng isang tao.
etymology: From pa- prefix + luha (tear) + -in suffix, a causative verb form.
original_explanation: The national sport of teleserye antagonists. It's what you do to your friend when you spoil the ending of their favorite K-drama, or what your ex did to you. The ultimate goal: to activate the tear ducts.
usage_notes: Often used in dramatic or emotional contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **paluhain** sa harap ng maraming tao.","translation":"Don't **make me cry** in front of many people."}]

meaning_filipino: Putulin ang isang halaman, partikular ang saging o tubo, sa pamamagitan ng isang matalas na kasangkapan.
original_explanation: The OG way of harvesting. Before you get your Dole bananas neatly packed in plastic, someone had to cut down (tibain) the whole plant stalk with a giant bolo knife. It's a swift, decisive chop at the base. It’s what you do to a banana plant to get its fruit, or to sugarcane to make sugar. Think of it as a very specific, agricultural 'Timber!'
usage_notes: Primarily used in an agricultural context for plants like banana trees and sugarcane.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nang **tibain** ang mga saging dahil hinog na ang bunga.","translation":"The banana plants need **to be cut down** because the fruit is already ripe."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagsanhian na magkaroon ng alon; dalhin o tangayin ng alon.
original_explanation: This is what a speeding motorboat does to the calm water, creating a wake. It can also mean to let something be carried by the waves. Parang 'go with the flow' pero literally. "Hayaan mo lang **paalunin** ang bangkang papel."
usage_notes: This is a less common verb. It's more common to say "gumawa ng alon" (to make waves) or "tinangay ng alon" (carried by the waves).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang malakas na hangin ang **nagpaalon** sa dating payapang lawa.","translation":"The strong wind **caused waves to form** on the previously calm lake."},{"sentence":"Nag-ingat ang mga mangingisda na huwag **paalunin** ang kanilang maliit na bangka.","translation":"The fishermen were careful not to let their small boat **be hit by the waves**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng pambihirang ganda o pang-akit na mahirap alisin sa isipan.
original_explanation: This is the feeling you get when you see your ultimate crush walk by in slow motion. It's that 'shet, ang ganda/gwapo' moment. It's not just pretty; it's enchanting, mesmerizing, makes you forget your own name. Think of a sunset in El Nido or the smile of the person you're about to give your 'sahod' to. That's nakabibighani.
usage_notes: A more poetic and intense word than 'maganda' (beautiful).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakabibighani** ang tanawin mula sa tuktok ng bundok.","translation":"The view from the top of the mountain is **captivating**."},{"sentence":"May **nakabibighani** siyang ngiti na kinahuhumalingan ng lahat.","translation":"She has an **enchanting** smile that everyone adores."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging dakila, marangal, tanyag, o solemne. Tumutukoy ito sa mataas na karangalan o sa isang maringal na katayuan.
etymology: From `ka-` + `bunyi` (fame, honor) + `-an`, creating an abstract noun for the state of being renowned or honored.
original_explanation: This is a very formal, almost poetic word. It's the vibe of a national hero's monument, a very formal state event, or receiving a lifetime achievement award. It's the opposite of being 'jologs' or 'baduy'. Think 'grandeur' but for reputation or atmosphere.
usage_notes: Primarily used in formal, literary, or historical contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinarangalan ang kanyang **kabunyian** bilang isang pambansang alagad ng sining.","translation":"His **greatness** as a national artist was honored."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman namin ang **kabunyian** ng seremonya nang tumugtog ang pambansang awit.","translation":"We felt the **solemnity** of the ceremony when the national anthem played."}]

meaning_filipino: Matutuklasan o magkakaroon ng kaalaman tungkol sa isang bagay sa hinaharap.
etymology: From the root `alam` (know), with the affix `ma- -an` and future tense reduplication of the first syllable of the root (`a` -> `ala`), forming `ma-ala-alam-an` which simplifies to `malalaman`.
original_explanation: The ultimate threat of every Filipino parent and chismosa tita: 'Malalaman ko rin 'yan!' (I'll find out eventually!). It's the future tense of knowing, often used when you're trying to hide your new tattoo, your failing grade, or the fact that you spent your entire sweldo in one day. The truth will out!
usage_notes: This is the future tense, object-focus form of the verb 'to know' or 'to find out'. The subject of the sentence is the thing being known, and the actor is indicated by 'ng' or a pronoun like 'mo', 'niya', etc.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bukas mo pa **malalaman** ang resulta ng pagsusulit.","translation":"You **will find out** the result of the exam tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Sa huli, **malalaman** din ng lahat ang katotohanan.","translation":"In the end, everyone **will know** the truth."}]

translation: act of catching something falling; supporting
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagsalo o pagsuporta sa isang bagay na bumabagsak o nangangailangan ng alalay upang hindi bumagsak.
etymology: From `pag-` (gerund prefix) + `sapo` (to catch or support from underneath).
original_explanation: Think of this as the ultimate 'salo' move. It's not just catching a ball. It's when you dive to catch your phone before it hits the pavement, or when you put your hands under a leaking ceiling.
