It's also used figuratively, like when a friend 'catches' you during a tough time. It's the act of being the support system, the human safety net.
usage_notes: Can be both literal (catching a physical object) and figurative (providing support).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis ang kanyang **pagsapo** sa nahulog na plorera.","translation":"His **act of catching** the falling vase was quick."},{"sentence":"Nagpapasalamat ako sa kanyang **pagsapo** sa akin noong panahong bagsak ako.","translation":"I am thankful for his **supporting** me when I was down."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang likas na pagkagusto, pagkahalina, o pagkakaugnay-ugnay sa isang tao, bagay, o ideya.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na 'di mo ma-explain pero 'click' kayo ng isang tao? May **apinidad** kayo. It's the 'same wavelength' energy you have with your best friend, or your strange attraction to collecting Funko Pops. It's a natural pull.
usage_notes: Isang pormal at di-karaniwang salita; mas madalas gamitin ang 'hilig' o 'pagkagusto'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroon siyang malakas na **apinidad** sa sining at musika.","translation":"He has a strong **affinity** for arts and music."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lihim na pagkuha ng maliit na halaga ng pera o bagay na hindi sa iyo; maliit na pagnanakaw.
original_explanation: This is the low-key, "discreet" version of stealing. 'Yung pagkuha mo ng barya sa wallet ni Mama para pambili ng yosi, or 'yung "paghiram" mo ng office supplies na hindi na naibabalik. The act of mangupit is a gateway drug to full-blown corruption, charot!
usage_notes: Refers to stealing small amounts, often in a sneaky, repeated manner.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahuli siyang **nangungupit** ng barya mula sa kaha.","translation":"He was caught **pilfering** coins from the cash register."},{"sentence":"Binalaan ng nanay ang kanyang anak na huwag na huwag **mangungupit** ng pera.","translation":"The mother warned her child never to **filch** money."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o akto ng pagtanggap ng ari-arian, katangian, o titulo mula sa isang yumaong tao o mula sa mga ninuno.
original_explanation: This is what starts family drama after Lola passes away. It’s not just about getting money or the old house; it can also be about inheriting your dad's nose, your mom's singing voice (or lack thereof), or the family's secret adobo recipe. It's the "mana sa akin" moment of every proud parent.
usage_notes: Can refer to inheriting tangible assets, genetic traits, or abstract qualities. `Pagmamana` is a more common synonym focusing on the act itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aawayan ng magkakapatid ang **pagkamana** sa mga lupain ng kanilang ama.","translation":"The siblings are fighting over the **inheritance** of their father's lands."},{"sentence":"Kitang-kita sa kanya ang **pagkamana** niya sa talento ng kanyang ina sa pagpipinta.","translation":"Her **inheritance** of her mother's talent in painting is very evident in her."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi kabilang o bahagi ng isang grupo, listahan, o gawain.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "sali" na may unlaping "ka-" at "di-".
original_explanation: The feeling of being the only one in the friend group who wasn't invited to the beach trip. The fine print in a promo that says "VAT di-kasali." It’s when you're picked last in PE, or worse, not picked at all. The official word for FOMO (Fear Of Missing Out).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lahat ay imbitado sa party, **di-kasali** ang mga bata.","translation":"Everyone is invited to the party, children are **not included**."},{"sentence":"Bakit ako laging **di-kasali** sa mga plano ninyo?","translation":"Why am I always **excluded** from your plans?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang dulo o matulis na bahagi ng isang bagay, tulad ng sa daliri, lapis, o tuka ng ibon.
original_explanation: The very end point of something. The **tungki** of your ilong (nose). The **tungki** of the tsismis (the very juicy tip!). When your shoes are so pointy they can be considered weapons, that's a sharp **tungki**. 'Aray! Natapakan mo ang **tungki** ng sapatos ko!'
usage_notes: Can refer to the tip of an object, a body part, or the beak of a bird.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matulis ang **tungki** ng bagong tasa na lapis.","translation":"The **tip** of the newly sharpened pencil is sharp."},{"sentence":"May maliit na ibon na dumapo sa sanga, ang **tungki** nito'y kulay dilaw.","translation":"A small bird landed on the branch, its **beak** was colored yellow."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na sumusuporta, tumutulong, o kumakampi sa isang tao, grupo, ideya, o kilusan.
original_explanation: The person who likes and shares all your posts. The one who buys your friend's homemade pastries. The "tiga-cheer" during your barangay basketball league game. In politics or showbiz, they are the loyal fans or followers who will defend their idol to the death in the comments section. They are your "kakampi."
usage_notes: A direct loanword from English, widely used in various contexts like politics, sports, and entertainment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isa siya sa mga pinakamatapat na **supporter** ng mayor.","translation":"He is one of the most loyal **supporters** of the mayor."},{"sentence":"Bilang isang **supporter**, bumili ako ng lahat ng album ng banda nila.","translation":"As a **supporter**, I bought all of their band's albums."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking sakuna o kapahamakan na nagdudulot ng malawakang pinsala, pagkasira, o pagdurusa.
original_explanation: Your internet connection dying in the middle of a ranked game or a client presentation. The ultimate "Lord, bakit?" moment. It's when everything that could go wrong, does go wrong, spectacularly. Basically, Monday morning.
usage_notes: A formal, loanword for a major disaster. Often used in news reports.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagputok ng bulkan ay nagdulot ng isang malaking **katastrope** sa buong rehiyon.","translation":"The eruption of the volcano caused a major **catastrophe** in the entire region."}]

translation: to fill a lack or deficiency; to compensate for
meaning_filipino: Punan o kumpletuhin ang isang bagay na may kakulangan o pagkukulang.
original_explanation: This is what you try to do when your friend who promised to bring the ice for the party flakes. You have to "pagpunuan" their absence by running to the nearest 7-Eleven. It’s about filling a gap, whether it’s a missing ingredient in your sinigang or a missing person in your team project.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of compensating for a shortcoming or absence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang **pagpunuan** ang pagkukulang ng kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"He is trying to **compensate for** the shortcomings of his parents."},{"sentence":"Tayo na ang **pagpunuan** sa mga gawaing hindi natapos ni Ana.","translation":"Let's be the ones to **fill in** for the tasks that Ana didn't finish."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang unang yugto sa siklo ng buhay ng isang kulisap matapos mapisa mula sa itlog at bago maging isang ganap na kulisap.
original_explanation: The baby picture of a butterfly or mosquito that you definitely don't want to see on your feed. It's their awkward glow-up phase, parang itsura mo sa high school yearbook. Sa science project lang 'to nagiging bida.
usage_notes: Isang terminong pang-agham na ginagamit sa biyolohiya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **larba** ng lamok ay nabubuhay sa mga tubig na hindi umaagos.","translation":"The **larva** of a mosquito lives in stagnant water."},{"sentence":"Nagiging uod o **larba** muna ang itlog bago ito maging paruparo.","translation":"The egg first becomes a caterpillar or **larva** before it becomes a butterfly."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagbubungkal o pagtatanim sa lupa, lalo na sa isang bukirin.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'plantito/plantita' move. While you're busy with your succulents, someone doing 'saka' is actually cultivating a whole field to produce food. It's the back-breaking, sun-scorching work that puts rice on our tables.
usage_notes: This is a root word. Common verb forms are 'magsaka' (to farm), 'sinasaka' (is being farmed), 'sakahan' (farmland).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pamilya niya ay matagal nang nag-**sasaka** ng palay sa Nueva Ecija.","translation":"His family has been **farming** rice in Nueva Ecija for a long time."},{"sentence":"Mahirap ang buhay ng pag-**saka**.","translation":"The life of **farming** is hard."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pandiwa sa kasalukuyang aspekto na nangangahulugang sinusundan ang isang tao o isang account sa social media. Ito ay hango sa salitang Ingles na 'follow'.
original_explanation: The present tense of 'following' someone on Instagram, TikTok, or X. It's what you do when you find a new chismis source or a content creator whose aesthetic matches your feed. 'Uy, nagfofollow ka pala sa ex ng ex mo?'
usage_notes: A very common Taglish verb, especially in the context of social media. The 'fo-' is a reduplication of the first syllable of the English root word, which mimics a standard Tagalog verbal conjugation pattern.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagfofollow** ako sa kanya sa TikTok kasi ang galing niya sumayaw.","translation":"I'm **following** them on TikTok because they are a great dancer."},{"sentence":"Sino-sino ang mga **nagfofollow** sa bagong celebrity love team?","translation":"Who are the ones **following** the new celebrity love team?"}]

meaning_filipino: Pag-ugnayin o pag-isahin sa pamamagitan ng pagtatali. Maaari ring tumukoy sa makasagisag na pagkakaisa.
original_explanation: Literally, to tie something up, like a bundle of firewood or your long hair. Figuratively, it’s about unity—like when your team lead says "Kailangan nating mag-`bigkis` para ma-hit ang quota!" It's the "group hug" verb, the call to action for teamwork, or the feeling of being tied down in a relationship you can't escape. #SanaAllUnited vs. #ItsComplicated.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for tying physical objects or figuratively for uniting people or ideas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **bigkisin** nang mahigpit ang mga panggatong.","translation":"The firewood needs to be **bound** tightly."},{"sentence":"Dapat nating **bigkisin** ang ating mga puso bilang isang bansa.","translation":"We must **bind** our hearts as one nation."}]

translation: coastal dweller, someone from the seaside
meaning_filipino: Isang taong naninirahan o nagmula sa isang lugar na malapit sa baybayin o dagat.
etymology: From taga- (from a place) + tabing-dagat (seaside, coast).
original_explanation: The ultimate beach-lover, but they don't just visit—they live there. Sila yung laging may tan, alam kung kailan high tide o low tide by instinct, at ang almusal ay mas sariwa pa sa isda na binili mo sa palengke. Their backyard is your summer destination.
usage_notes: This is a descriptive term, not an official title. It emphasizes a person's origin or place of residence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bilang isang **tagatabing-dagat**, sanay na si Mang Jun sa amoy ng alat.","translation":"As a **coastal dweller**, Mang Jun is used to the salty smell of the sea."},{"sentence":"Ang mga **tagatabing-dagat** ang unang nakakita sa papalapit na bagyo.","translation":"The **people from the seaside** were the first to see the approaching storm."}]

translation: to adapt; to get along with; to conform
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aangkop ng sariling kilos, gawi, o pananalita upang maging kaaya-aya at katanggap-tanggap sa isang grupo o kapaligiran.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "maki-" (paglahok) at salitang ugat na "bagay" (angkop, tama).
original_explanation: This is the survival skill you learn on your first day at a new job or when meeting your partner's family for the first time. It's about reading the room, laughing at the tito jokes (even if they're corny), and not bringing up politics at the dinner table. It's the opposite of being 'bida-bida.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong matutong **makibagay** sa iyong mga bagong katrabaho.","translation":"You need to learn to **get along with** your new coworkers."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **makibagay** sa isang lugar kung iba ang iyong mga kaugalian.","translation":"It's hard to **adapt** to a place if you have different customs."}]

translation: to come to one's senses; to act with good judgment
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkilos nang may tamang pag-iisip, matinong pagpapasya, at bait.
original_explanation: It's what your mom tells you to do when you're about to make a bad decision. "Maghuwisyo ka nga!" means "Get a grip!" or "Use your brain!" It's the opposite of being 'pasaway' or 'matigas ang ulo'. It's the moment of clarity after doing something stupid.
usage_notes: Often used as a command or an admonition to someone who is acting irrationally or immaturely.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana naman ay **maghuwisyo** ka na at tigilan mo na ang iyong mga bisyo.","translation":"I hope you **come to your senses** now and stop your vices."},{"sentence":"Sinabihan siya ng kanyang ina, '**Maghuwisyo** ka sa iyong paggasta!'","translation":"His mother told him, '**Act with good judgment** in your spending!'"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa paglala o pagtindi ng isang bagay, tulad ng apoy, sakit, o damdamin.
etymology: From pa- + sindi (to light, to ignite).
original_explanation: 'Yung lagnat na akala mo okay na, tapos biglang tumaas ulit. 'Yung away niyo na nagsimula sa "Saan ka galing?" at nauwi sa "Maghiwalay na tayo!" 'Yung apoy sa niluluto mong adobo na biglang lumakas. It's when things escalate or intensify, usually for the worse.
usage_notes: Often used to describe the intensification of negative things like illness, fire, or arguments. `Pasindi nang pasindi` means getting progressively worse.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pasindi** ang lagnat ng bata tuwing gabi.","translation":"The child's fever **flares up** every night."},{"sentence":"Sa halip na humupa, **pasindi** nang **pasindi** ang kanilang pagtatalo.","translation":"Instead of subsiding, their argument just got **worse and worse**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang matalim at matinding pagtitig na karaniwang nagpapahiwatig ng galit, pagbabanta, o masidhing damdamin.
original_explanation: This is the look your mom gives you when you're being pasaway in front of visitors. No words needed, just the **panlilisik** of her eyes and you know you're grounded until 2030. It's the human equivalent of a laser-guided death stare.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to the intense, angry glare of the eyes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **panlilisik** ng mata ang isinukli niya sa mga nang-aasar sa kanya.","translation":"She returned a **fierce glare** to those who were teasing her."},{"sentence":"Natahimik ang lahat nang makita ang **panlilisik** sa mga mata ng kanilang hepe.","translation":"Everyone fell silent when they saw the **intense stare** in their boss's eyes."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang pagtalsik o pagkalat ng maliliit na patak ng likido dahil sa isang malakas na pagtama o paggalaw.
original_explanation: That annoying little spray of water that hits your pants when a car speeds through a puddle. Or the splatter of hot oil when you're frying tilapia. It's a small, sudden, and often unwanted explosion of liquid. Unlike a gentle 'tilamsik', a 'tabsik' implies more force and a slightly larger volume.
usage_notes: Often used to describe the spray from puddles, waves, or when cooking. 'Tumabsik' is the verb form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nainis siya dahil puno ng **tabsik** ng putik ang bago niyang sapatos.","translation":"She was annoyed because her new shoes were full of mud **splatters**."},{"sentence":"Ang lakas ng **tabsik** ng alon sa may batuhan.","translation":"The **splash** of the waves on the rocks was strong."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kilos, gawi, o asal na marangal, maharlika, at tila isang hari.
original_explanation: The complete opposite of kilos-bata. This is that person who walks into a room with quiet confidence, speaks with authority, and commands respect without even trying. Think of a CEO with great posture, or your lolo who has that dignified air about him. It's the 'main character energy' of a king.
usage_notes: Used to describe a dignified, noble, and commanding demeanor. Can be used as an adjective or a noun referring to the behavior itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mula sa kanyang pananalita hanggang sa pananamit, siya ay **kilos-hari**.","translation":"From the way he speaks to the way he dresses, he is **regal**."},{"sentence":"Ang pagiging kalmado niya sa gitna ng krisis ay nagpakita ng kanyang **kilos-hari**.","translation":"His calmness in the middle of the crisis showed his **kingly demeanor**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng paggaya o paggawa ng pekeng kopya ng isang bagay, tulad ng dokumento, pera, o pirma, na may layuning manlinlang.
etymology: From `pang-` + reduplication of the first syllable of the root `huwad`.
original_explanation: This is the art of making "Class A" or "OEM" versions of everything, from luxury bags to your parents' signature on your report card. It's the OG "fake news" but for physical items. Yung kaibigan mong nagbebenta ng "authentic" na sapatos sa presyong divisoria? That's panghuhuwad in action.
usage_notes: Refers to the act or process of falsification.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **panghuhuwad** ng pirma ay isang seryosong krimen.","translation":"The **forgery** of a signature is a serious crime."},{"sentence":"Nahuli ang sindikato dahil sa **panghuhuwad** ng pera.","translation":"The syndicate was caught because of money **counterfeiting**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paggalaw sa tubig gamit ang mga braso at binti upang hindi lumubog at makarating sa ibang lugar.
original_explanation: The official activity of every Filipino beach trip. It's 10% actual swimming and 90% "babad sa tubig" while taking selfies. It's also a metaphor for surviving a sea of deadlines or "swimming" in debt. "Kapit lang, bes, malapit na sa sahod!"
usage_notes: A straightforward term for the action of swimming.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paglalangoy** ay isang magandang ehersisyo para sa buong katawan.","translation":"**Swimming** is a good full-body exercise."},{"sentence":"Nagsanay siya sa **paglalangoy** para sa darating na kompetisyon.","translation":"He/She practiced **swimming** for the upcoming competition."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pananakop, pagpapayuko, o pagtalo sa isang kalaban o hadlang sa pamamagitan ng higit na lakas o kapangyarihan.
etymology: From `pag-` (prefix indicating action) + `gahis` (to conquer, to overpower).
original_explanation: This is an old-school, epic-movie kind of word. It's not just winning; it's completely dominating and conquering your opponent. Think Lapu-Lapu vs. Magellan, or a corporate takeover where one company completely absorbs the other. It's the act of making someone or something 'luhod, tala!' (kneel, star!). It has a strong sense of force and power.
usage_notes: Often used in historical, literary, or formal contexts to describe conquest. In some older or regional contexts, it can be a synonym for sexual assault ('paggahasa'), but this usage is less common in modern standard Filipino to avoid ambiguity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paggahis** sa isang bansa ay nangangahulugan ng pagkawala ng kalayaan nito.","translation":"The **subjugation** of a country means the loss of its freedom."},{"sentence":"Hindi nila inasahan ang mabilis na **paggahis** ng kanilang koponan.","translation":"They did not expect the swift **vanquishing** of their team."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging nakabuka o nakanganga ng bibig, karaniwan dahil sa pagkamangha, pagkatulala, o pagkapagod.
original_explanation: 'Yung itsura mo kapag nakita mo 'yung presyo ng bilihin sa grocery at parang gusto mo na lang mag-photosynthesis. O 'yung reaction mo sa plot twist ng K-drama na hindi mo ine-expect. Your jaw is on the floor, literally.
usage_notes: A very rare word, almost literary or obsolete. 'Nakanga-nga' is the common term. This noun form is almost never used in modern speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa tindi ng pagod, halos nasa estado na siya ng **pangangahin** habang nakaupo.","translation":"Due to extreme fatigue, he was almost in a state of **gaping** while sitting."}]

meaning_filipino: Isda na biniyak, inasnan, at ibinilad sa araw upang mapreserba.
original_explanation: The official breakfast of champions, especially when paired with sinangag (garlic fried rice) and itlog (egg). Amoy pa lang, alam na ng buong barangay kung ano'ng ulam n'yo. It's the Pinoy version of an aromatic candle, but for the kitchen. Your kapitbahay will either love you or hate you for it.
usage_notes: The pronunciation is different from the verb. Here the stress is on the first syllable /DA-ing/.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sarap ng almusal namin, pritong **daing** na bangus at sinangag.","translation":"Our breakfast was delicious, fried **dried** milkfish and garlic rice."},{"sentence":"Nag-uwi siya ng isang kilong **daing** mula sa Bantayan.","translation":"He brought home a kilo of **dried fish** from Bantayan."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay, tao, o pangyayari na nagiging hadlang o balakid sa pag-abot ng isang layunin o sa pagpapatuloy ng isang gawain.
original_explanation: Your toxic ex who won't let you move on? A *sagwil*. The EDSA traffic when you have a 9 AM meeting? A major *sagwil*. That one subject you need to pass to graduate? The ultimate *sagwil*. It's anything that makes you say, "Hay, nako, eto na naman."
usage_notes: Often used in a more formal or literary context than "hadlang" or "balakid".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kahirapan ay hindi dapat maging **sagwil** sa pag-abot ng iyong mga pangarap.","translation":"Poverty should not be an **obstacle** to reaching your dreams."},{"sentence":"Tinanggal nila ang mga **sagwil** sa daan upang makadaan ang ambulansya.","translation":"They removed the **hindrances** on the road so the ambulance could pass."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbigkas ng masasakit o mapanirang-puring salita laban sa isang tao; pag-alipusta gamit ang salita.
original_explanation: This is the action verb for when your mom finds out you failed a subject, or when a taxi driver gets cut off in traffic. 'Minura' is the past tense, the verbal lashing you receive. 'Murahing mabuti' is the full-on, no-holds-barred, HD version of this scolding, complete with hand gestures and a litany of your past mistakes. It's a national sport.
usage_notes: Can range from a simple scolding to intense cursing. The object-focused form is 'murahin' (e.g., 'Huwag mo akong murahin,' Don't curse at me). This is a homonym to 'mura' (adjective), which means 'cheap'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang magsalita ng masama, baka ka **murahin** ng nanay mo.","translation":"Don't say bad things, your mom might **scold** you."},{"sentence":"**Minura** niya ang driver na biglang lumiko sa harap niya.","translation":"He **cursed** at the driver who suddenly turned in front of him."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manggagawa, lalo na mula sa Silangan o Timog-Silangang Asya noong panahon ng kolonyalismo, na inuupahan para sa mabigat na trabahong pangkamay. Ito ay isang salitang luma at maaaring ituring na hindi kaaya-aya sa kasalukuyan.
etymology: From Hindi 'qūlī' (hired laborer), which entered Tagalog likely via English 'coolie'.
original_explanation: This is a term straight out of your Araling Panlipunan textbook. 'Kuli' refers to the laborers, often of Chinese or Indian descent, during the colonial era who did the heavy lifting for very low wages. Today, the word is pretty much obsolete and can even be considered offensive. It's a historical term that reminds us of a tough past.
usage_notes: This term is archaic and potentially offensive in modern contexts. It's primarily used in historical discussions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Noong panahon ng mga Kastila, maraming **kuli** ang nagtrabaho sa pagtatayo ng mga riles ng tren.","translation":"During the Spanish era, many **coolies** worked on the construction of the railroads."},{"sentence":"Ang buhay ng isang **kuli** sa mga plantasyon ay napakahirap.","translation":"The life of a **laborer** on the plantations was very difficult."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, grupo, o kumpanya na naglalagak ng puhunan o salapi sa isang negosyo o proyekto sa pag-asang ito ay kikita o tutubo.
original_explanation: Ito yung tita mo na nag-invest sa'yo ng pang-review center, tapos ang inaasahang ROI (Return on Investment) niya ay makapasa ka sa board exam. Sila yung mga taong nagbibigay ng pera hindi para gumastos, kundi para lumago. Sila ang "sana all may pera" ng business world.
usage_notes: Isang pormal na termino sa mundo ng pagnenegosyo at pananalapi.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghahanap ang startup company ng mga **mamumuhunan** para mapalago ang kanilang operasyon.","translation":"The startup company is looking for **investors** to grow their operations."},{"sentence":"Ang bawat magulang ay isang **mamumuhunan** sa kinabukasan ng kanilang mga anak.","translation":"Every parent is an **investor** in their children's future."}]

translation: will be made to feel weak; will be discouraged
meaning_filipino: Gagawaan ng paraan upang humina ang lakas, katawan, o loob ng isang tao.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your spirit after your 10th job rejection. Or what your crush does to you by leaving you on "seen." They are causing you to become weak (emotionally). "**Papanghinain** ng kalaban ang kanilang loob bago sumalakay." (The enemy will demoralize them before attacking.)
usage_notes: Can refer to both physical weakness and emotional/mental weakness (demoralization).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **papanghinain** ng mga pagsubok ang iyong loob.","translation":"Don't let trials **weaken** your spirit."},{"sentence":"Ang kakulangan sa tulog ay tiyak na **papanghinain** ang iyong katawan.","translation":"Lack of sleep will surely **weaken** your body."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang partikular na uri o klase; sa kolokyal na gamit, ang taong nagugustuhan o hinahanap sa isang romantikong kapareha batay sa mga katangian.
etymology: Hiram na salita mula sa Ingles na 'type'.
original_explanation: This is your 'checklist' for a potential bae. 'Ano type mo?' 'Moreno, matangkad, mabait...' It's not about blood type, but your *heart's* type. When you see someone attractive, you'd whisper to your friend, 'Type ko siya, bes!' It’s the Taglish shortcut for 'He/She is my type of person.'
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in colloquial and informal conversations, particularly about romantic interests. It is used as a noun, not a verb ('to type' on a keyboard is 'mag-type').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko siya **type**, masyado siyang mayabang.","translation":"He's not my **type**, he's too arrogant."},{"sentence":"Si Chris Evans ang **type** kong lalaki.","translation":"Chris Evans is my **type** of guy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang masining na pagtatalo sa paraang patula, karaniwang isinasagawa ng dalawang mambabalagtas na may isang tagapamagitan o lakandiwa. Pinangalanan ito bilang parangal kay Francisco Balagtas.
etymology: From the surname of Francisco Balagtas, the 'Prince of Tagalog Poets'.
original_explanation: This is the OG rap battle of the Philippines, but make it literature. Instead of sick burns about yo' mama, you get eloquent verses about love, society, and patriotism. Think of it as Fliptop for your Lolo and Lola, complete with a referee (the Lakandiwa) to keep things classy.
usage_notes: A formal and artistic event, often held during town fiestas or literary gatherings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napanood mo ba ang **kabalagtasan** tungkol sa teknolohiya at tradisyon?","translation":"Did you watch the **poetic joust** about technology and tradition?"},{"sentence":"Ang lolo ko ay isang sikat na mambabalagtas noong kanyang kabataan at laging nananalo sa mga **kabalagtasan**.","translation":"My grandfather was a famous poet in his youth and always won in **poetic jousts**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kilos na ginawa nang may buong kaalaman, sadya, at hindi nagkataon lamang.
original_explanation: This is the adverb for when you do something shady and you know it. It's the 'seen-zone' sa Messenger, 'yung pag-iwas mo sa inaanak mo 'pag Pasko, o 'yung pagbili mo ng milk tea kahit nagtitipid ka. You did it **deliberately**. It's the opposite of 'Sorry, hindi ko sinasadya.' Here, you meant it, and you'll probably do it again.
usage_notes: Often implies a negative or malicious intent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tikis** niyang hindi pinansin ang tawag ko.","translation":"She **deliberately** ignored my call."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong isipin na **tikis** kitang sinaktan; isang aksidente lang iyon.","translation":"Don't think that I hurt you **on purpose**; it was just an accident."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang opisyal na namumuno sa isang yunit ng militar, pulisya, o anumang organisadong pangkat.
original_explanation: Siya yung boss sa military, yung nagbibigay ng utos na 'Sugod, mga kapatid!' o 'Retreat!'. Sa office setting, siya yung team lead mo na nagde-delegate ng tasks. Sa bahay, si nanay ang supreme commander, at ang utos niya ay batas.
usage_notes: Primarily used in military, police, or similar hierarchical contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumaludo ang mga sundalo sa kanilang **komander**.","translation":"The soldiers saluted their **commander**."},{"sentence":"Ang **komander** ang nagplano ng buong operasyon.","translation":"The **commander** planned the entire operation."}]

translation: to cluck (like a chicken); to grumble (stomach)
meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng tunog na katulad ng sa isang inahing manok; o ang tunog na nililikha ng tiyan kapag nagugutom.
original_explanation: This word has two vibes. First, it’s the sound a happy, broody chicken makes. Second, and more relatable, it's the sound your stomach makes in a quiet room during a meeting when you skipped breakfast. That embarrassing, low rumble that announces to everyone, "Gutom na ako!"
usage_notes: Context is key to distinguish between the chicken and the stomach meaning. The stomach meaning is more common in everyday urban conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig kong **kumurok** ang mga sisiw na sumusunod sa inahin.","translation":"I heard the chicks **clucking** as they followed the mother hen."},{"sentence":"Biglang **kumurok** ang tiyan ko sa gitna ng klase.","translation":"My stomach suddenly **grumbled** in the middle of the class."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kasamang nag-aaral o nag-aral sa iisang paaralan; kaklase o kaeskuwela.
original_explanation: Anyone who went to the same school as you, from the person you shared a table with in the canteen to that guy from a different batch you only know by face. Reconnecting with a schoolmate years later often starts with, "Uy, taga-[School Name] ka rin pala! Kilala mo si...?"
usage_notes: The Tagalog 'kaeskuwela' is also common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakasalubong ko ang dati kong **schoolmate** sa mall.","translation":"I bumped into my old **schoolmate** at the mall."},{"sentence":"Pareho kaming grumaduate sa UP, pero hindi kami **schoolmate** sa parehong department.","translation":"We both graduated from UP, but we weren't **schoolmates** in the same department."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o bagay na nagsisilbing perpektong halimbawa o pamantayan na dapat tularan.
etymology: From `huwad` (to pattern after) + `-an` (place/object suffix), evolving to mean the pattern/model itself.
original_explanation: This is your "model student," your "employee of the month," or that one tita everyone in the family compares you to. A huwaran is someone so good, they're basically a living, breathing template for success. #SanaAll. They're the 'gold standard' you're measured against.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun (a role model) or an adjective (exemplary), as in 'huwarang paglilingkod'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Dr. Jose Rizal ay isang **huwaran** para sa mga kabataang Pilipino.","translation":"Dr. Jose Rizal is a **role model** for the Filipino youth."},{"sentence":"Ipinakita niya ang **huwaran** na paglilingkod sa bayan.","translation":"He showed **exemplary** service to the country."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sisidlan o imbakan ng bigas.
original_explanation: Literally, your rice dispenser. In Filipino culture, it's a symbol of prosperity and stability. If your palabigasan is full, you're doing okay. If it's empty, it's "petsa de peligro" time. It's the most important appliance next to the rice cooker.
usage_notes: Can also be used metaphorically to mean 'source of income' or 'bread and butter', but this is less common. The primary meaning is the physical container.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan na nating punuin ang **palabigasan** dahil paubos na ang bigas.","translation":"We need to fill the **rice container** because the rice is almost gone."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng baging na may bunga na karaniwang pinatutuyo at ginagamit bilang lalagyan ng tubig o sisidlan. Kilala rin bilang upo.
etymology: Pinaniniwalaang mula sa isang katutubong wika sa Pilipinas.
original_explanation: The OG water bottle. Before Hydro Flasks and Klean Kanteens, our ancestors used this dried-out gourd to carry their liquids. It's the plant that looks like a giant green dumbbell. You probably know its more famous cousin, `upo`.
usage_notes: Hindi gaanong ginagamit sa modernong Tagalog; ang salitang "upo" ang mas karaniwan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumawa sila ng mga palamuti mula sa pinatuyong **purunggo**.","translation":"They made decorations from dried **bottle gourds**."},{"sentence":"Noong unang panahon, **purunggo** ang ginagamit na baunan ng tubig.","translation":"In the old days, a **bottle gourd** was used as a water container."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng palitan ng salita, ideya, o damdamin sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang tao.
original_explanation: The OG way to get chismis. Before DMs, Messenger, or group chats, there was 'pag-uusap'. It's that thing your parents want to have with you when your grades drop ('We need to talk'), or what you do with your barkada over coffee for hours. The official term for 'Marites-ing' in person.
usage_notes: The most common word for conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang maayos na **pag-uusap** upang malutas ang hindi pagkakaunawaan.","translation":"A proper **conversation** is important to resolve misunderstandings."},{"sentence":"Napunta sa pulitika ang kanilang masayang **pag-uusap**.","translation":"Their happy **discussion** turned to politics."}]

translation: when you are free; when you have free time
meaning_filipino: Isang idyomatikong pahayag na nangangahulugang 'kapag mayroon kang libreng oras o hindi abala.'
etymology: Literally 'if when you are loose/spacious,' combining 'kung kailan' (when) and 'maluwag' (loose, spacious, not tight/busy).
original_explanation: The classic, non-committal way to make plans in the Philippines. It sounds polite, but it's the professional way of saying 'Let's schedule a meeting that might never happen.' The corporate version of 'See you when I see you.'
usage_notes: A polite and indirect way to ask about someone's availability, often used to defer scheduling to a later, unspecified time.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tawagan mo na lang ako **kung kailan ka maluwag**.","translation":"Just call me **when you are free**."},{"sentence":"Mag-usap tayo tungkol sa proyekto **kung kailan ka maluwag**.","translation":"Let's talk about the project **when you have free time**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bulalas na nagpapahayag ng matinding pagkadismaya, galit, o inis. Itinuturing na isang mura o di-magandang salita.
etymology: From Spanish 'leche' (milk), a common euphemistic curse in Spain.
original_explanation: The SFW-ish curse word you can probably get away with in front of your tita (but not your lola). From the Spanish word for 'milk' (leche), it's the perfect expression for when you stub your toe, your internet goes out during a crucial Zoom meeting, or you realize you left your wallet at home. 'Letse!' is the sigh of a frustrated Filipino soul.
usage_notes: A very common expression of frustration. While milder than other Filipino curses, it is still considered vulgar and inappropriate in formal settings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Letse!** Naiwan ko na naman ang payong ko, at ang lakas ng ulan!","translation":"**Damn it!** I left my umbrella again, and it's raining so hard!"}]

translation: circling around; going around in circles
meaning_filipino: Paulit-ulit na pag-ikot sa isang lugar o paksa nang walang malinaw na patutunguhan o solusyon.
original_explanation: Describes your thought process at 3 AM wondering if you should text your ex. Or when you're looking for parking at SM on a payday weekend. You're just going paikit-ikit, hoping for a miracle.
usage_notes: The repetition of "ikit" emphasizes the continuous, often frustrating, nature of the circling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kanina pa tayo **paikit-ikit** dito, hindi mo ba alam ang daan?","translation":"We've been **going around in circles** here for a while, don't you know the way?"},{"sentence":"Huwag na tayong mag-usap nang **paikit-ikit**, sabihin mo na ang punto mo.","translation":"Let's not talk **in circles**, just get to your point."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sinasadyang pagdudulot ng hirap o sakit sa sariling katawan o damdamin, kadalasan para sa isang layunin, paniniwala, o para sa kapakanan ng iba.
etymology: From pagpapakasakit (act of enduring hardship) + sa sarili (to oneself). Pagpapakasakit comes from pag- + papaka- + sakit (pain, illness).
original_explanation: On one hand, it's the ultimate 'martyr' move—the OFWs working abroad, the parent giving up their last piece of chicken joy for their kid. On the other, it's what you do when you keep re-reading old convos with your ex. It's the act of intentionally enduring hardship, whether for a noble cause or just because 'mahilig kang masaktan'.
usage_notes: Can refer to altruistic self-sacrifice or the psychological tendency of self-harm or deriving pleasure from pain (masochism). Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapakasakit sa sarili** ng mga bayani ay hindi dapat kalimutan.","translation":"The **self-sacrifice** of the heroes should not be forgotten."},{"sentence":"Itigil mo na 'yang **pagpapakasakit sa sarili** mo sa pag-iisip sa kanya.","translation":"Stop that **masochism** of yours by thinking about him."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng tunog na "meow" na katangian ng pusa, o ang pag-iyak nang malakas na parang pusa.
original_explanation: Primarily the sound a cat makes when it's 5 AM and its food bowl is empty. By extension, it's also what a person does when they cry in a whiny, attention-seeking way. "Stop meowing and tell me what's wrong!" is a valid parental response.
usage_notes: While it can mean 'to wail' for humans, its primary and more common meaning is 'to meow' for cats.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gabi-gabi, naririnig kong **ngumawa** ang pusa sa bubungan.","translation":"Every night, I hear the cat **meow** on the roof."},{"sentence":"**Ngumawa** na naman ang bata dahil sa taas ng bill ng kuryente.","translation":"The child **wailed** again because of the high electricity bill."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao o bagay na simple, natural, at hindi maarte o nagpapanggap.
etymology: Mula sa "wala" (none) at Espanyol na "arte" (art), na sa kontekstong ito ay nangangahulugang pagkukunwari o pagka-pihikan.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate compliment for a "kalog" friend. The one who'll eat at a karinderya in their pambahay, laugh with their mouth open, and won't throw a fit if their iced coffee is 90% ice. They're the "what you see is what you get" type. The opposite of a ✨main character✨ who needs everything to be aesthetic.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang pagiging simple at totoong tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko siyang kaibigan dahil **walang-arte** siyang tao.","translation":"I like her as a friend because she is an **unpretentious** person."},{"sentence":"Masarap kumain kasama ang mga taong **walang-arte**.","translation":"It's fun to eat with people who have **no-frills**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking pangkat ng mga tao na namumuhay sa isang tiyak na teritoryo, may magkakatulad na kultura, at pinamamahalaan ng iisang Gobyerno.
original_explanation: Basically, all of us. It's the giant 'group chat' of a country. Includes the government, the marites, the BPO workers, the students, the jeepney drivers... everyone. It's the system and the people living in it. 'Isang salamin ng ating lipunan ang mga isyung nakikita natin online.'
usage_notes: A fundamental word in social studies (Araling Panlipunan) and formal discussions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang papel ng kabataan sa paghubog ng ating **lipunan**.","translation":"The youth play a big role in shaping our **society**."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan nila ang iba't ibang uri ng **lipunan** sa buong mundo.","translation":"They are studying the different kinds of **societies** around the world."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang taong may labis na pagtingin sa sarili, mapagmataas, at may ugaling hamakin ang iba.
original_explanation: This is the vibe of that one officemate who looks down on you for eating 'baon' while they have their Starbucks. It's the energy of someone who thinks their poop doesn't stink. Peak 'feelingero/feelingera' mode.
usage_notes: A somewhat strong and old-fashioned word. 'Mayabang' or 'hambog' are more common synonyms.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naiinis ang lahat sa kanyang **tukaki** na pag-uugali.","translation":"Everyone is annoyed by his **haughty** attitude."},{"sentence":"Simula nang yumaman siya, naging **tukaki** na ang pakikitungo niya sa mga dati niyang kaibigan.","translation":"Ever since he got rich, his treatment of his old friends became **snobbish**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kainan o restawran na ang pangunahing inihahain ay iba't ibang uri ng pancit.
etymology: Combination of Tagalog `pancit` (from Hokkien) and Spanish suffix `-ería` (place of).
original_explanation: The mothership. The HQ of all things pancit. Your go-to place when mom or tita is too busy to cook for the potluck. Usually has that distinct, comforting smell of soy sauce, broth, and history. Often an old-school Chinese-Filipino establishment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumaan muna kami sa paborito naming **panciteria** bago umuwi.","translation":"We dropped by our favorite **noodle house** before going home."},{"sentence":"Maraming lumang **panciteria** sa Binondo na masarap pa ring kainan.","translation":"There are many old **noodle houses** in Binondo that are still great places to eat."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkakaroon ng kakulangan o kakapusan sa isang bagay na kailangan, tulad ng pagkain, tubig, o pera.
etymology: From "ka-" + "salat" (lacking, scarce) + "-an", meaning 'the state of scarcity'.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling pag "petsa de peligro" na at puro instant noodles na lang ang laman ng pantry mo. That's kasalatan sa budget. Or when there's a water interruption and you have to ration every drop. It's the opposite of abundance, the state of "wala na."
usage_notes: Often used to describe a lack of basic necessities. More formal than "kakulangan".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naranasan ng bansa ang matinding **kasalatan** sa bigas noong nakaraang taon.","translation":"The country experienced a severe **shortage** of rice last year."},{"sentence":"Ang **kasalatan** sa pagmamahal ay maaaring magdulot ng kalungkutan.","translation":"A **lack** of love can cause sadness."}]

translation: to let go completely; to release with force
meaning_filipino: Pakawalan nang buong-buo o biglaan; hayaang umagos o gumalaw nang walang pagpigil.
original_explanation: Imagine holding a rope that's pulling a heavy load, and then you just let go. That's ibulos. It's also what you do with your anger after bottling it up for weeks, or when you finally give your all in the last 100 meters of a fun run. Total, unrestrained release.
usage_notes: Implies a sudden and complete release of something held back, whether it's a physical object, a force, or an emotion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nang bumigay ang dam, **ibinulos** nito ang napakaraming tubig sa buong bayan.","translation":"When the dam broke, it **unleashed** a massive amount of water upon the whole town."},{"sentence":"**Ibinulos** niya ang lahat ng kanyang lakas sa huling suntok.","translation":"He **released** all his strength into the final punch."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mahigpit na pagtikom o paghawak sa isang bagay, karaniwan gamit ang kamay upang bumuo ng isang kamao.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na sobrang gigil mo sa isang tao o sitwasyon, gusto mo na lang kuyumin 'yung kamao mo. Parang 'pag nakita mo 'yung ex mo na may bago na, tapos kailangan mong magpigil. That's the clench.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for clenching a fist or metaphorically for suppressing strong emotions like anger or frustration.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **kuyumin** ang kanyang kamao upang pigilan ang galit.","translation":"He tried to **clench** his fist to hold back his anger."},{"sentence":"**Kuyumin** mo ang pera sa iyong palad para hindi mawala.","translation":"**Grasp** the money tightly in your palm so it won't get lost."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng isang maikli at mataas na tunog, karaniwang dahil sa tuwa, takot, o kiliti.
original_explanation: The sound your friend makes when they see their K-Pop bias on screen. The sound a piglet makes. The sound you make when someone tickles you unexpectedly. It's that high-pitched burst of sound that's half-laugh, half-scream.
usage_notes: Onomatopoeic. Can be used for humans (giggling) or animals (squealing).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang maririnig na **pag-igik** ng mga bata ay hudyat na sila'y nagkakatuwaan.","translation":"The audible **giggling** of the children is a sign that they are having fun."},{"sentence":"Isang malakas na **pag-igik** ang pinakawalan niya nang makita ang daga.","translation":"She let out a loud **squeal** when she saw the mouse."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang atasan o pilitin ang isang tao na gawin ang isang bagay bilang isang tungkulin o pananagutan, kadalasan ay dahil sa isang kasunduan, batas, o moral na dahilan.
etymology: From 'mang-' and 'obliga', which is derived from the Spanish 'obligar' (to obligate).
original_explanation: The special skill of titas and bosses. It's when someone 'asks' you to do something in a way that you can't say no. 'Di kita **inoobliga**, pero...' is the classic opening line before you're guilt-tripped into doing something. It's the power of 'utang na loob' and social pressure rolled into one verb.
usage_notes: Carries a sense of compulsion, whether legal, social, or moral. The prefix 'mang-' suggests the act of imposing this obligation on others.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang batas ay **nang-oobliga** sa mga mamamayan na magbayad ng buwis.","translation":"The law **obligates** citizens to pay taxes."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mang-obliga** ng tao kung ayaw niyang tumulong.","translation":"Don't **compel** someone if they don't want to help."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sinag o guhit ng liwanag, karaniwan mula sa araw, na tumatagos sa siwang o kadiliman.
original_explanation: Literally, it’s that ray of sunshine that peeks through your window in the morning, telling you it's time to face the world (or your deadlines). Figuratively, and more known in modern slang, it was a term for a bisexual man. It's a play on 'sinag' (ray) and how it can 'hit' both ways. It's a bit dated as a slang term, but still understood.
usage_notes: The word has a literal meaning (ray of light) and a colloquial, somewhat dated slang meaning for a bisexual male. The slang usage can be considered pejorative by some, and newer, more affirming terms are preferred within the LGBTQ+ community.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng **silahis** ng araw na tumatama sa mga bulaklak.","translation":"The **sunbeam** hitting the flowers is beautiful."},{"sentence":"Pumasok ang isang **silahis** ng pag-asa sa kanyang puso.","translation":"A **ray** of hope entered his heart."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang taong kasama o katulong sa pagsasalin ng isang wika, teksto, o kahit na ng isang likido mula sa isang sisidlan patungo sa iba.
original_explanation: Your work partner sa pag-translate ng K-drama subtitles for fun. O 'yung kachikahan mo habang nagsasalin kayo ng tsismis from one group chat to another. The 'co-' in your 'salin' activities.
usage_notes: Isang di-karaniwang salita. Mas madalas sabihing 'kasama sa pagsasalin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Dr. Jose ang aking **kasalin** sa proyektong ito.","translation":"Dr. Jose is my **co-translator** for this project."}]

translation: to expose; to catch someone; to call someone out
meaning_filipino: Sadyang ilantad o ihayag ang lihim o pagkakamali ng isang tao.
original_explanation: The act of doing the 'bisto'. It's when you actively expose someone. Parang sa meeting, "I'd like to bistuhin the person who keeps eating the shared office snacks." It's the verb form of dropping the tea, a confrontation in the making.
usage_notes: An action directed at a specific person or group.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **bistuhin** sa harap ng maraming tao.","translation":"Don't **expose** me in front of many people."},{"sentence":"Plano nilang **bistuhin** ang katiwalian sa kanilang kumpanya.","translation":"They plan to **expose** the corruption in their company."}]

translation: somehow, in any way, at least
meaning_filipino: Isang pariralang pang-abay na nagpapahiwatig ng pagkakaroon ng resulta o paraan sa kabila ng mga paghihirap o kawalan ng katiyakan.
etymology: A fixed phrase composed of 'kahit' (even if) and 'paano' (how).
original_explanation: The mantra of everyone just trying to make it through the day. It's the 'bahala na, but with a little more hope' vibe. 'Di ko alam paano ko natapos 'yung report, pero natapos ko **kahit paano**.' It means you winged it, and it worked. It can also mean 'at least.' 'Sira ang phone ko, pero **kahit paano** gumagana pa 'yung text.'
usage_notes: A very common fixed expression. It conveys a sense of managing to do something against the odds, or finding a silver lining in a negative situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawalan ako ng wallet, pero **kahit paano** ay naitabi ko ang aking ID.","translation":"I lost my wallet, but **at least** I was able to save my ID."},{"sentence":"Mahirap ang pagsusulit, ngunit nakapasa ako **kahit paano**.","translation":"The exam was difficult, but I passed **somehow**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbalik sa sariling tahanan o tirahan.
original_explanation: The magic word every BPO agent, student, and office worker wants to hear at the end of the day. "Tara, umuwi na tayo!" is the battle cry of the tired and weary. It's not just going to a house, it's going *home*. For OFWs, this word carries a universe of meaning and longing. This is the past/imperative tense.
usage_notes: This is the completed (past) tense or imperative (command) form of the verb. "Umuuwi" is the present tense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagod na ako, gusto ko nang **umuwi**.","translation":"I'm tired, I want **to go home** now."},{"sentence":"**Umuwi** siya nang maaga dahil masama ang kanyang pakiramdam.","translation":"He **went home** early because he was not feeling well."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggisi o paghiwa-hiwalay sa isang manipis na materyal tulad ng papel o tela sa pamamagitan ng paghila.
original_explanation: The action you do to your ex's photos after a bad breakup. Or what happens to your 100-peso bill when you try to pull it out of your tight jeans pocket. It's the act of ripping paper, fabric, or your hopes and dreams.
usage_notes: Used for thin, flat materials like paper, cloth, or plastic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagalit ang guro nang may **pumunit** sa pahina ng aklat.","translation":"The teacher got angry when someone **tore** a page from the book."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **pumunit** ng pera, labag iyan sa batas.","translation":"Don't **rip** money, that's against the law."}]

translation: to equip, to furnish, to add ingredients to
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagdaragdag ng mga sangkap sa isang bagay upang ito ay makumpleto o maging handa.
original_explanation: This is the action of "putting it all together." It's what you do when your mom tells you, "Sige, sangkapan mo na 'yang kaldereta." It’s the verb form of getting things ready, like equipping your team before a presentation or adding all the toppings to your halo-halo.
usage_notes: The object receiving the ingredients/equipment is the focus of the verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sangkapan** mo ng maraming bawang at sibuyas ang ating lulutuin.","translation":"**Add** plenty of garlic and onions **to** what we're cooking."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **sangkapan** ang mga sundalo ng modernong kagamitan.","translation":"The soldiers need **to be equipped** with modern gear."}]

translation: consultation; the act of having something checked
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagdulog o paglapit sa isang tao, karaniwan ay isang propesyonal, upang suriin o siyasatin ang isang bagay o kalagayan.
original_explanation: This is the classic "Pa-check-up mo na 'yan" moment. Whether it's your persistent cough (pagpapatingin sa doktor), your busted laptop (pagpapatingin sa technician), or your essay (pagpapatingin sa prof), it's the act of seeking an expert's eyes. It's admitting, "I can't figure this out, please look at it."
usage_notes: Most commonly used for medical check-ups but applicable to any situation requiring expert examination.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang regular na **pagpapatingin** sa dentista para sa kalusugan ng ngipin.","translation":"Regular **consultation** with a dentist is important for dental health."},{"sentence":"Isinagawa niya ang **pagpapatingin** ng kanyang sasakyan bago ang mahabang biyahe.","translation":"He did the **act of having his car checked** before the long trip."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, grupo, o institusyon na binibigyan ng buong pananampalataya at kumpiyansa, at inaasahang hindi gagawa ng panloloko o pagkakanulo.
original_explanation: Your human vault. Sila 'yung huling taong aalisan mo ng chat history, pero sila rin 'yung unang makakaalam ng latest chika. This is your 'no questions asked' person, the one you trust with your secrets, your money, or worse, your Netflix password.
usage_notes: Can refer to a person (confidant), a place (a trusted bank), or an abstract concept. It is the object being trusted.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang aking **pinagkakatiwalaan** pagdating sa mga sensitibong usapin sa opisina.","translation":"He is my **confidant** when it comes to sensitive matters at the office."},{"sentence":"Maraming bangko ang nawalan ng **pinagkakatiwalaan** ng publiko matapos ang krisis.","translation":"Many banks lost the public's **trust** after the crisis."}]

translation: to throw a stone; to throw something hard
meaning_filipino: Ang paghagis o pagpukol ng isang bato o anumang matigas na bagay.
original_explanation: The action of yeeting a rock. Can be used for skipping stones on water, for protesting ('mambabato'), or what you metaphorically do when you 'throw shade' or a harsh comment at someone. 'Sinong unang walang kasalanan, siyang unang bumato.'
usage_notes: Implies throwing something hard and solid, as opposed to 'maghagis' which is more general.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **bumato** sa bintana namin kagabi kaya nabasag ito.","translation":"Someone **threw a stone** at our window last night, which is why it broke."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **bumato** ng salita na hindi mo kayang panindigan.","translation":"Don't **throw** words that you can't stand by."}]

translation: to register; to enroll; to have recorded
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagpapalista o paglalagay ng pangalan o impormasyon sa isang opisyal na talaan, gaya ng sa paaralan, ahensya ng gobyerno, o para sa isang kaganapan.
original_explanation: The official verb of adulting. It's what you do during enrollment season, when getting a National ID, or when you finally decide to register your small 'ukay-ukay' business with the DTI. It's the act of getting your name on 'The List' to make it official.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumila siya nang maaga para **magpatala** para sa bagong semester.","translation":"He lined up early to **enroll** for the new semester."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magpatala** sa SSS para magkaroon ng benepisyo.","translation":"You need to **register** with the SSS to have benefits."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pag-uusap o pagkakalat ng mga kuwento tungkol sa ibang tao, na kadalasan ay hindi kumpirmado o pribado.
original_explanation: The national sport of the Philippines, charot! This is the act of being a 'Marites' (Mare, ano ang latest?). It's the sacred art of sharing 'chika' over coffee, in the office pantry, or in the family group chat. It's not just talking; it's a performance, a social ritual.
usage_notes: Refers to the action of gossiping itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itigil na ninyo ang **pagtsitsismis** at magtrabaho na kayo.","translation":"Stop the **act of gossiping** and get back to work."},{"sentence":"Walang mabuting naidudulot ang **pagtsitsismis**.","translation":"Nothing good comes from the **act of gossiping**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal at pinaikling tawag sa 'jeepney,' ang tanyag na pampublikong sasakyan sa Pilipinas.
original_explanation: The shorter, more common way to say 'jeepney'. It's what you shout when you're trying to hail one down. 'Para, sa tabi lang!' is its universal stop signal. Riding a jeep is a full sensory experience: the diesel fumes, the cramped seating, the blaring radio, and the bayad being passed from person to person.
usage_notes: 'Jeep' is used interchangeably with 'Jeepney' in almost all colloquial contexts. 'Jeepney' might be slightly more formal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"'Bayad po,' sabi ng pasaherong sumakay sa **jeep**.","translation":"'My fare, please,' said the passenger who boarded the **jeep**."},{"sentence":"Dalawang sakay ng **jeep** ang kailangan para makarating sa amin.","translation":"You need to take two **jeep** rides to get to our place."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay, gawain, o karanasan na ang halaga, hirap, o pagod na inilaan ay katumbas o higit pa sa benepisyong natamo.
original_explanation: That feeling when you brave the 12.12 sale traffic, wait in a long line for milk tea, or work overtime, and the result is just... *chef's kiss*. It's the ultimate "value for money" or "value for effort" rating. "Puyat is real, but the bonus is coming? Sulit!" It's the opposite of "na-scam."
usage_notes: A very common word in everyday conversation, especially related to shopping, food, and experiences.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sulit** ang pagod sa akyat ng bundok dahil sa ganda ng tanawin.","translation":"The exhaustion from climbing the mountain was **worthwhile** because of the beautiful view."},{"sentence":"Sa halagang isang daan, **sulit** na itong unli-rice.","translation":"For one hundred pesos, this unli-rice is totally **worth it**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sinasadyang pagwasak, pagpinsala, o paghadlang sa isang bagay, gawain, o sistema, karaniwang ginagawa nang palihim.
etymology: Hiram sa salitang Kastila na 'sabotaje' at Ingles na 'sabotage', na mula sa Pranses na 'sabotage'.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung tropa mong sinadyang i-delete 'yung file ng presentation niyo kasi galit siya sa'yo. Or when you deliberately 'forget' to tell your office rival about the deadline change. It's the art of the sneaky takedown.
usage_notes: Isang modernong hiram na salita na mas karaniwang ginagamit kaysa sa mga katutubong katumbas tulad ng 'manabotahe' sa mga pormal o teknikal na konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May hinala siyang may nagtangkang **sabutahihin** ang kanyang negosyo.","translation":"He suspects someone tried to **sabotage** his business."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **sabutahihin** ang sarili mong tagumpay dahil sa takot.","translation":"Don't **sabotage** your own success out of fear."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahabang patpat o piraso ng kahoy na ginagamit bilang suporta sa paglalakad, lalo na ng mga matatanda o may kapansanan, o bilang simbolo ng kapangyarihan.
original_explanation: This is what your lolo or lola uses to walk, and sometimes, to threaten you with a 'palo' when you're being a pasaway na apo. It's the OG mobility aid before walkers and wheelchairs became common. Also, think Gandalf or Moses – they had epic staffs (tungkod).
usage_notes: Can refer to a simple walking aid or a more ornate staff of authority (scepter).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ng matanda ang kanyang **tungkod** upang makatayo.","translation":"The old man used his **cane** to stand up."},{"sentence":"Ang **tungkod** ng hari ay simbolo ng kanyang kapangyarihan.","translation":"The king's **staff** is a symbol of his power."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nakapagtapos ng isang kurso sa kolehiyo o unibersidad at pinagkalooban ng antas ng Batsilyer.
original_explanation: The official title you get after four (or more) years of puyat, stress, and instant noodles. It's the piece of paper your parents can finally hang on the wall. Not to be confused with a 'bachelor' who is just single—though you might be that, too, after all the studying.
usage_notes: Refers to a person who has earned a bachelor's degree. Often followed by the specific field, e.g., 'Batsilyer sa Sining'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay isang **batsilyer** sa larangan ng Inhenyeriya.","translation":"He is a **bachelor** in the field of Engineering."},{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang makapagtapos at maging isang **batsilyer**.","translation":"Her dream is to graduate and earn a **bachelor's** degree."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng pagsisikap at pagpupunyagi sa anumang gawain.
original_explanation: Basically, the slightly more formal cousin of 'masipag'. Ito yung ginagamit sa mga recommendation letter at performance review. "Si Juan ay masikap na empleyado." Hindi lang siya masipag, may effort, may initiative. Hindi lang naghihintay ng utos, gumagawa ng paraan.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'masipag', but 'masikap' can carry a stronger connotation of striving and exerting effort, not just being busy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil siya ay **masikap**, mabilis siyang umangat sa kanyang trabaho.","translation":"Because he is **diligent**, he was quickly promoted in his job."}]

translation: to traverse; to take a path
meaning_filipino: Ang paglakbay, pagdaan, o pagpunta sa isang partikular na landas, lugar, o direksyon.
original_explanation: To go through something, whether it's the traffic on EDSA, the long path to your career goals, or the 'friend zone' (which you hope to traverse, but often get stuck in). It’s about taking on a journey, no matter how difficult. 'Kahit mahirap, kailangan nating tahakin ang landas na ito.'
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin sa literal (pisikal na landas) at metaporikal (landas sa buhay, karera, atbp.) na paraan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming bundok ang kailangan mong **tahakin** bago marating ang tuktok.","translation":"You need **to traverse** many mountains before reaching the summit."},{"sentence":"Pinili niyang **tahakin** ang landas ng pagiging isang doktor.","translation":"She chose **to take the path** of becoming a doctor."}]

translation: to hiss; to make a 'psst' sound
meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng isang matinis na tunog gamit ang bibig, tulad ng 'psst' o 'ssss,' upang makuha ang atensyon ng isang tao.
original_explanation: Ah, the classic Filipino way of calling someone's attention without knowing their name. 'Psst! Psst!' That's `sumitsit`. It's what you do in a quiet library to get your friend's attention, or what that creepy guy on the street corner does. Context is everything. It can be a friendly 'hey!' or a rude catcall.
usage_notes: `Sumitsit` is the completed past tense. The present tense is `sumisitsit`. Often considered informal and can be rude depending on the tone and context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumitsit** siya para tawagin ang aso.","translation":"He **made a 'psst' sound** to call the dog."},{"sentence":"May bastos na lalaking **sumitsit** sa akin sa kalye kanina.","translation":"A rude man **hissed/catcalled** at me on the street earlier."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng tunog na "ungot" o ang pag-ungol na karaniwang ginagawa ng isang baboy.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "ungot," na isang onomatopeya para sa tunog ng baboy.
original_explanation: It's the sound a pig makes. Parang 'yung tunog mo kapag tinatamad kang sumagot sa umaga, 'yung "hnggg" lang. Or 'yung sound effect kapag nabusog ka sa unli-samgyup.
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang ilarawan ang partikular na tunog ng baboy. Maaari ring gamitin nang patalinghaga para sa isang taong gumagawa ng katulad na tunog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ungutan** ang pagkain; magpasalamat ka.","translation":"Don't **grunt** at the food; be thankful."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar, kulungan, o gusali kung saan inaalagaan at pinalalaki ang mga baboy.
original_explanation: The pig's condo unit. It's where the magic happens before the lechon. Metaphorically, it's what your mom calls your bedroom when you haven't cleaned it for a week. "Ano ba 'to, kwarto o babuyan?!"
usage_notes: Can also be used metaphorically to describe a very dirty or messy place.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May amoy na nagmumula sa **babuyan** sa dulo ng kalsada.","translation":"There's a smell coming from the **piggery** at the end of the road."},{"sentence":"Linisin mo nga ang kwarto mo, mukha nang **babuyan**!","translation":"Clean your room, it looks like a **pigsty**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkilos na tila maraming alam o pagpapakita ng higit na karunungan kaysa sa tunay na taglay, madalas sa paraang nakakainis.
original_explanation: We all have that one tito or officemate in a meeting. They use big words they can't explain and have an opinion on everything. Sila 'yung nagdudunung-dunungan. The human version of a Wikipedia article that has a "[citation needed]" tag on every sentence.
usage_notes: A pejorative term. The repetition of the root word 'dunong' (knowledge) with affixes implies pretense or acting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw ko siyang kausap kasi palagi siyang **nagdudunung-dunungan** tungkol sa pulitika.","translation":"I don't like talking to him because he's always **acting like a know-it-all** about politics."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magdunung-dunungan** kung hindi mo naman talaga alam ang sagot.","translation":"Don't **pretend to be smart** if you don't really know the answer."}]

meaning_filipino: Binubuo ng maraming magkakaugnay na bahagi o detalye na mahirap unawain, suriin, o lutasin.
original_explanation: Your relationship status on Facebook. The plot of a Christopher Nolan movie. Trying to explain to your parents what your BPO job actually is. Anything that makes you say, "Teka, pa-ulit? Ang gulo." It's the adult version of untangling your earphones.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang isyu ng trapiko sa EDSA ay isang **masalimuot** na problema.","translation":"The traffic issue on EDSA is a **complicated** problem."},{"sentence":"Mayroon silang **masalimuot** na kasaysayan bilang pamilya.","translation":"They have a **complex** history as a family."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang istruktura o bahagi ng pader o bakod na nagsisilbing pasukan at labasan, na karaniwang mayroong pinto o harang na maaaring isara at buksan gamit ang isang trangka.
etymology: Mula sa "trangka" (bar, bolt), na galing sa Espanyol na "tranca". Ang hulaping "-han" ay nagpapahiwatig ng isang lugar.
original_explanation: This is the OG gate. Before fancy electronic gates or even doorknobs, there was the 'trangka'—a simple wooden or metal bar. The 'trangkahan' is the whole gate assembly. It's what keeps the dogs (and the chismosa neighbor) out.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisara nang maigi ang **trangkahan** para hindi makalabas ang mga manok.","translation":"Please close the **gateway** properly so the chickens can't get out."},{"sentence":"May malaking parol na nakasabit sa aming **trangkahan** tuwing Pasko.","translation":"There's a big lantern hanging on our **gateway** every Christmas."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao o bagay na madaling maapektuhan o masaktan, pisikal man o emosyonal.
etymology: Mula sa 'madali' (easy) at 'talaban' (to be penetrated, to be affected).
original_explanation: Describes someone who easily catches feelings (or a cold). You give them one compliment and they're already planning the wedding. You give one critique and they're writing a sad poem. Like a phone with no screen protector, it's easily scratched.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang pagiging sensitibo sa kritisismo, sakit, o kahit sa mga supernatural na puwersa (tulad ng kulam).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Madaling talaban** ng tukso ang mga taong mahina ang pananampalataya.","translation":"People with weak faith are **susceptible** to temptation."},{"sentence":"Magsuot ka ng jacket, **madaling talaban** ng sakit ang katawan mo ngayon.","translation":"Wear a jacket, your body is **susceptible** to sickness right now."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagligo gamit ang isang 'shower' o 'dutsa'; paliligo.
original_explanation: That magical 15 minutes where you either have a full concert, practice your debate arguments, or have a life-changing epiphany. In the Philippines, this is often done with a 'tabo' and a 'balde', but we still call it a 'shower'. It's our national pastime, especially when it's 35 degrees Celsius outside.
usage_notes: Used interchangeably with 'ligo'. 'Mag-shower' (to shower) is a very common verb form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-**shower** ka na, amoy-araw ka na.","translation":"Go take a **shower**, you smell like you've been under the sun."},{"sentence":"Ang sarap mag-**shower** pagkatapos mag-ehersisyo.","translation":"It feels so good to **shower** after exercising."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng panunuyo o pagpapakita ng romantikong interes ng isang tao sa iba, na may layuning maging magkasintahan.
original_explanation: The classic Pinoy 'panunuyo'. Before DMs, there was 'harana' (serenade). Today, it’s about sending Grab Food to their office, making 'sundo' after work, and dropping hints via IG stories. It's the 'getting to know you' stage, but with extra effort and gastos. The original 'Sana All' phase.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to romantic courtship. For 'getting lost', the word is 'pagkaligaw'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagligaw** noon ay madalas may kasamang harana at pag-iigib ng tubig.","translation":"**Courtship** back then often included serenading and fetching water."},{"sentence":"Tila epektibo ang kanyang mga diskarte sa **pagligaw** dahil sinagot na siya ni Maria.","translation":"It seems his **wooing** strategies were effective because Maria has already said yes to him."}]

meaning_filipino: Nakabatay o nakasuhay sa isang bagay; pagtitiwala o pananalig.
original_explanation: Ito yung 'based on a true story' ng mga salita. 'Pag sinabing 'salig sa batas,' ibig sabihin, ayon sa batas at hindi pwedeng basta-basta. Parang sa relationship, dapat 'salig sa trust' para 'di mag-away. It's the foundation, the 'because' part of a statement.
usage_notes: Madalas makita sa mga pormal at legal na dokumento, tulad ng 'Saligang Batas' (Constitution). Maaari ring mangahulugang tiwala.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang desisyon ay **salig** sa mga ebidensyang nakalap.","translation":"His decision is **based on** the collected evidence."},{"sentence":"Ang Saligang Batas ang pinakamataas na batas na **salig** sa kapangyarihan ng mamamayan.","translation":"The Constitution is the highest law **founded on** the power of the people."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang aparato na ginagamit sa pagkuha ng mga litrato o gumagalaw na larawan (video).
original_explanation: Before your iPhone had three lenses, this was the OG gadget for capturing memories. It's the Spanish-derived term for a camera. You'd hear your lola say "Kunin mo ang kamara!" during family reunions. Now, it sounds a bit vintage, like using "telepono" instead of "cellphone".
usage_notes: The English word "camera" (or "kamera") is now far more common in everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang luma niyang **kamara** para kunan ng litrato ang paglubog ng araw.","translation":"He used his old **camera** to take a picture of the sunset."},{"sentence":"May dala ka bang **kamara** para sa ating biyahe?","translation":"Did you bring a **camera** for our trip?"}]

translation: to be set apart; to be isolated
meaning_filipino: Maihiwalay o mapatangi mula sa karamihan o sa isang pangkat.
original_explanation: What happens to the 'Team SANA ALL' friend when everyone else in the barkada gets a jowa. Or when you're the only one in the office who didn't get the memo about wearing blue today. Can be good (being recognized for an award) or bad (social distancing before it was cool).
usage_notes: Can have a neutral, positive (to be distinguished), or negative (to be ostracized) connotation depending on the context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang **mabukod** sa kanyang mga kaibigan kaya sumama siya sa lakad.","translation":"He didn't want **to be isolated** from his friends, so he joined the outing."},{"sentence":"Ang Pilipinas ay **nabukod** sa ibang bansa dahil sa natatangi nitong kultura.","translation":"The Philippines **is set apart** from other countries because of its unique culture."}]

translation: to put a drop on; to drip on
meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng isa o higit pang patak ng likido.
original_explanation: The act of applying liquid drop by drop. Like when you're using eye drops (`**patakan** mo ng Vyzine`), adding soy sauce to your calamansi (`**patakan** mo ng toyo`), or when a leaky roof starts dripping on your homework. It's all about controlled, small amounts.
usage_notes: The '-an' suffix indicates that the object of the verb is the thing being dripped upon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Patakan** mo ng gamot ang kanyang mata.","translation":"**Put drops** of medicine on his eye."},{"sentence":"Ingat, baka **patakan** ng kandila ang mantel.","translation":"Be careful, the tablecloth might get **dripped on** by the candle."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging mailap; ang hirap sa paghuli o paglapit, tulad ng isang ligaw na hayop, o ang pag-iwas sa pakikisalamuha.
original_explanation: This is the energy of that crush who's always 'seen' but never replies. It's the vibe of a stray cat that won't let you get close, or a good idea that vanishes the moment you try to write it down. It's hard to catch, hard to tame, and always seems to be just out of reach.
usage_notes: Can refer to animals, people (who are unsociable or hard to get close to), or abstract concepts like success or peace.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagka-mailap** ng pusa ang dahilan kung bakit hindi pa ito nahuhuli.","translation":"The cat's **elusiveness** is the reason why it hasn't been caught yet."},{"sentence":"Nawala ang kanyang **pagka-mailap** nang makahanap siya ng mga tunay na kaibigan.","translation":"Her **standoffishness** disappeared when she found true friends."}]

meaning_filipino: Aalisin at hahalinhan ng iba; magkakaroon ng kapalit. Ito ay nasa aspektong panghinaharap.
etymology: From pa- (causative prefix) + palit (change/replace) + -an (locative/object suffix). The duplication of the first syllable 'pa' indicates future tense.
original_explanation: The promise your ex gave you right before they found someone new. Also, what happens to your 13th-month pay ('papalitan ng mga bayarin'). In tech, it’s what happens to your phone model after 6 months.
usage_notes: Future tense, object-focus verb. The thing being replaced is the subject of the sentence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Papalitan** na raw ang lumang aircon sa opisina.","translation":"They say the old aircon in the office **will be replaced**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapabatid o pagbibigay ng impormasyon sa isang tao o pangkat.
original_explanation: This is the formal way of saying "pasabi" or "paki-chismis." It's what you do when you need to disseminate info. The HR department will "ipagbigay-alam" a new memo. You ask your friend, "Ipagbigay-alam mo naman sa kanila na male-late ako." It’s basically being the messenger, the town crier, or the admin of the group chat.
usage_notes: A compound verb phrase often treated as a single unit. The focus is on the information being shared. The root is from the compound 'bigay-alam'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **ipagbigay-alam** sa lahat ang tungkol sa pagbabago ng petsa ng pagpupulong.","translation":"We need to **inform** everyone about the change in the meeting date."},{"sentence":"**Ipinagbigay-alam** ng PAGASA ang pagdating ng malakas na bagyo.","translation":"PAGASA **notified** (the public) of the arrival of a strong typhoon."}]

translation: to be able to hug; to be embraced
meaning_filipino: Magawang yakapin o mapaloob sa isang yakap.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of your 'sana all' hugot. 'Sana all mayapos.' It’s that feeling of longing to embrace someone, or the sweet relief when you finally get to. It's the goal after a long day of adulting, or when you see your dog after being away. It's the verb for a much-needed hug.
usage_notes: `Mayapos` implies being able to hug, while `mayakap` (from root `yakap`) is a more common synonym. `Yapos` can sometimes imply a more intimate or tighter embrace.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naiyak siya nang sa wakas ay **mayapos** niya ang kanyang ina.","translation":"She cried when she was finally **able to hug** her mother."},{"sentence":"Ang sarap sa pakiramdam na **mayapos** ang isang mahal sa buhay.","translation":"It feels so good **to be able to embrace** a loved one."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit o pag-ubos ng pera sa pamamagitan ng pagbili o pagbabayad.
etymology: Mula sa salitang 'gastos' na hango sa Espanyol na 'gastos'.
original_explanation: What you tell yourself you won't do on 12.12, but end up doing anyway. "Sige na, gastusin mo na 'yang 13th month pay mo, deserve mo 'yan!" - The little devil on your shoulder, probably.
usage_notes: Ito ang anyong pandiwa na tumutukoy sa aksyon ng paggamit ng pera.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Madali lang **gastusin** ang pera na hindi pinaghirapan.","translation":"It's easy **to spend** money that wasn't hard-earned."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **gastusin** lahat ng ipon mo sa isang bagay lang.","translation":"Don't **spend** all your savings on just one thing."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagmula, ipinanganak, o naninirahan sa probinsya. Bilang pang-uri, ito ay tumutukoy sa mga katangian, gawi, o bagay na nauugnay sa probinsya.
original_explanation: Used to be a term for someone from outside the big city, sometimes with a hint of "hampaslupa" condescension.
