But thanks to Cardo Dalisay, being a probinsiyano now means you're basically an unkillable, morally upright action hero. Also, someone who gets genuinely excited by the MRT and thinks Manila traffic is a form of punishment from the gods.
usage_notes: The feminine form is 'probinsiyana'. The term can be neutral, a point of pride, or sometimes used pejoratively by city dwellers.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang orgullosong **probinsiyano** si Mang Tony na mula pa sa Ilocos.","translation":"Mang Tony is a proud **man from the province** who hails from Ilocos."},{"sentence":"May punto de-amerikano siya pero **probinsiyano** ang kanyang pananamit.","translation":"He has an American accent but his style of dress is **provincial**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging maningning; matinding liwanag, kislap, o kinang.
etymology: Nagmula sa panlaping ka- at -an na idinugtong sa salitang ugat na 'ningning'.
original_explanation: Ito yung glow-up na hindi lang pang-physical. It's the 'main character energy' radiating from you. Pwedeng kaningningan ng bituin, ng brilyante, o ng performance mo sa work na napansin ni boss. The opposite of 'dull'. It's your time to shine, literally and figuratively.
usage_notes: Isang mas pampanitikan o pormal na salita para sa 'liwanag' o 'kislap'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit sa dilim, hindi maikukubli ang **kaningningan** ng kanyang kabutihan.","translation":"Even in darkness, the **radiance** of his kindness cannot be hidden."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkilos o pagsasalita na tila isang bakla; ang pag-amin o pagpapakita ng pagiging homoseksuwal na lalaki.
original_explanation: A very loaded and often derogatory term. It's used when a straight guy suddenly shows stereotypically "gay" mannerisms, usually as a joke among friends. "Uy, bumakla ka na, pre?" It can also be used to describe the "coming out" process, but in a very informal, sometimes insensitive way. It's a word that lives in the complicated space of Filipino humor and LGBTQ+ identity. Handle with care.
usage_notes: Ang salitang ito ay kolokyal at maaaring ituring na mapanlait o nakakasakit depende sa konteksto at intensyon. Madalas itong ginagamit bilang biruan sa magkakaibigan ngunit maaaring maging insulto kapag ginamit ng iba.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtaka ang barkada nang bigla siyang **bumakla** sa pagsayaw.","translation":"The friends were surprised when he suddenly **acted effeminately** while dancing."},{"sentence":"Sa harap ng pamilya niya siya **bumakla** at umamin sa tunay niyang pagkatao.","translation":"He **came out as gay** in front of his family and admitted his true self."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging bugnot; pagkainis, pagkayamot, o pagkasuya dahil sa isang bagay na paulit-ulit o nakakabalam.
original_explanation: This is that feeling of extreme annoyance when the internet connection drops for the 10th time during your online game, or when someone keeps asking you 'Are we there yet?' on a long road trip. It's the 'Ugh, I've had it!' emotion. The final stage of 'inis' before you either explode or just give up.
usage_notes: A strong word for annoyance. Less common than 'inis' or 'yamot' but more descriptive.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya maitago ang kanyang **kabugnutan** sa paulit-ulit na tanong.","translation":"She couldn't hide her **exasperation** at the repetitive questions."},{"sentence":"Ang trapik sa EDSA ay nagdudulot ng matinding **kabugnutan** sa mga motorista.","translation":"The traffic on EDSA causes intense **annoyance** for motorists."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng gulay na may kulay ube o lila, pahaba ang hugis, at karaniwang ginagamit sa mga lutuing Filipino tulad ng torta, pinakbet, at adobo.
original_explanation: The purple vegetable that's the star of tortang **talong**. It's the reason why your lola tells you to eat your veggies. It's healthy, versatile, and has an emoji that's... often misinterpreted. 🍆 The OG budget ulam partner.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong almusal ang tortang **talong** na may kasamang sinangag at kamatis.","translation":"My favorite breakfast is **eggplant** omelette with fried rice and tomatoes."},{"sentence":"Mag-ihaw tayo ng **talong** para isawsaw sa toyo na may sibuyas.","translation":"Let's grill some **eggplant** to dip in soy sauce with onions."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o gawain ng pagiging barbaro; kalupitan, kawalan ng sibilisasyon, o matinding kalaswaan.
etymology: From Spanish 'bárbaro' (barbarian) with the Tagalog circumfix 'ka- -han' indicating a quality or state.
original_explanation: This is when someone acts like they have no Wi-Fi connection to civilization. Think of someone cutting in a long queue, or a driver who treats traffic rules as mere suggestions. It's the opposite of "GMRC" (Good Manners and Right Conduct). The ultimate "walang modo" behavior.
usage_notes: A strong, formal word used to condemn uncivilized or extremely cruel acts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **kabarbaruhan** na ginawa noong panahon ng digmaan ay hindi dapat malimutan.","translation":"The **atrocities** committed during the war should not be forgotten."},{"sentence":"Itinuturing na **kabarbaruhan** ang pananakit sa mga walang kalaban-laban.","translation":"Harming the defenseless is considered an act of **savagery**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahaba at manipis na hibla ng materyal tulad ng bulak, seda, o nylon, na ginagamit sa pananahi o paghahabi.
etymology: Nagmula sa salitang-ugat na "sulid" na may gitlaping "-in-".
original_explanation: The OG 'thread'. Before Twitter threads, this was the stuff your lola used to fix your ripped uniform pants the night before school. It’s the lifeline of every "mananahi sa kanto" and the eternal enemy of anyone trying to thread a needle. One wrong move and you've got a tangled mess, much like a chaotic Twitter argument.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng itim na **sinulid** para tahiin ang butas sa aking pantalon.","translation":"I need black **thread** to sew the hole in my pants."},{"sentence":"Naputol ang **sinulid** ng saranggola kaya ito ay lumipad palayo.","translation":"The kite's **thread** broke so it flew away."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos o epekto ng paggalaw o panginginig nang may puwersa, tulad ng sa isang lindol.
etymology: Mula sa 'pagka-' (paraan o akto ng) + 'yanig' (shake, quake).
original_explanation: Literally, this is what you feel during an earthquake. Figuratively, it’s the feeling when your boss says "We need to talk." It's the internal shake-up when you find out a major chismis about someone you know. It’s that jolt, that disturbance to your calm, whether it's the ground beneath you or the foundations of your beliefs.
usage_notes: Most commonly associated with earthquakes, but can be used figuratively for emotional or social upheavals.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman sa buong gusali ang malakas na **pagkayanig**.","translation":"The strong **tremor** was felt throughout the building."},{"sentence":"Ang balita ay nagdulot ng **pagkayanig** sa buong industriya.","translation":"The news caused a **shaking** throughout the entire industry."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbibigay ng sagot, reaksyon, o solusyon sa isang tanong, pangangailangan, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: This is the BPO agent's life motto. "Thank you for calling, how may I help you?" - that's `tumutugon`. It's also what you're doing when you finally reply to that "seen-zoned" chat from three days ago. It means you're addressing the need, whether it's a customer's complaint or a friend's hugot.
usage_notes: Present/Progressive aspect of the verb 'tumugon'. Often followed by 'sa' to indicate what is being responded to (e.g., 'tumutugon sa tawag').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumutugon** ang gobyerno sa mga pangangailangan ng mga nasalanta ng bagyo.","translation":"The government is **responding** to the needs of the typhoon victims."},{"sentence":"Hindi siya **tumutugon** sa mga text ko.","translation":"He is not **answering** my texts."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang trabaho ay pamahalaan ang publisidad o imahe ng isang kilalang tao, kumpanya, o produkto sa madla.
original_explanation: The person who cleans up the mess. Sila yung nag-iisip ng damage control, nagsusulat ng public apology, at tinitiyak na laging 'on-brand' ang artista o politiko, kahit sa likod ng camera ay jollibee-spaghetti-level ang pagiging messy. The ultimate spin doctor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha ng bagong **publisista** ang sikat na aktres.","translation":"The famous actress hired a new **publicist**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hanay ng buhok sa itaas ng mga mata ng tao.
original_explanation: Ah, the Filipino woman's (and sometimes man's) secret weapon. It's not just hair above your eyes; it's a statement. "Kilay is life" isn't a joke, it's a mantra. It can convey more emotions than a Shakespearean actor—surprise, anger, doubt, or "taray" mode—all with a single arch. Having your eyebrows 'on fleek' is more important than being on time for some.
usage_notes: "Taas-kilay" (raised eyebrow) is a common expression for showing doubt, surprise, or being unimpressed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magaling siyang mag-drawing ng **kilay** gamit ang eyebrow pencil.","translation":"She's good at drawing her **eyebrows** using an eyebrow pencil."},{"sentence":"Isang taas ng **kilay** lang niya, alam ko nang may mali.","translation":"Just one raise of her **eyebrow** and I already knew something was wrong."}]

translation: to take a bath; to bathe
meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng paglilinis ng katawan gamit ang tubig at sabon.
original_explanation: The national pastime, second only to eating. This is the Pinoy solution to everything: feeling hot? Maligo ka. Stressed? Maligo ka. May sakit? 'Wag kang maliligo. It's the ultimate reset button, unless you have a fever, then it's a no-go according to lola.
usage_notes: A fundamental daily activity in the Philippines. The concept of "ligo" can range from a quick "buhos" (dousing with a bucket/tabo) to a full shower.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **maligo** bago umalis ng bahay.","translation":"I need **to take a bath** before leaving the house."},{"sentence":"Ang sarap **maligo** sa ilog!","translation":"It feels so good **to bathe** in the river!"}]

meaning_filipino: Paggalaw nang mabilis gamit ang mga paa, kung saan sa isang punto ay parehong nakaangat ang mga paa sa lupa.
original_explanation: The OG Filipino cardio. You do this to catch the jeep, to escape your responsibilities (charot!), or to run for public office. From a fun run in BGC to running away from a 'Marites,' `tumakbo` is the answer.
usage_notes: Can also mean "to run for office" (e.g., tumakbo para presidente) or "to function/operate" for a machine (though `umandar` is more common).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis na **tumakbo** ang bata papalayo sa aso.","translation":"The child quickly **ran** away from the dog."},{"sentence":"Balak niyang **tumakbo** bilang kapitan sa susunod na halalan.","translation":"He plans to **run** for captain in the next election."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matinding antas ng pagkatakot; labis na pangamba.
etymology: Pag-uulit ng salitang-ugat na 'takot' para sa pagbibigay-diin.
original_explanation: This isn't just regular "I saw a spider" takot. This is "The deadline is tomorrow and you haven't started" takot. It's "Your mom used your full name" takot. This is the final boss of fear. The reduplication plus 'na' is the Filipino way of hitting the panic button.
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang paraan upang paigtingin ang isang pang-uri sa Filipino ay ang ulitin ito na may 'na' sa gitna.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Takot na takot** ang bata matapos makakita ng multo sa pelikula.","translation":"The child was **terrified** after seeing a ghost in the movie."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kilos na isasagawa sa hinaharap na tumutukoy sa pag-alis ng takip, pagbukana, o pagsisimula ng operasyon ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the future tense of "open". It's the promise of a new mall branch ("Magbubukas ang bagong SM!"), the start of a new chapter in your life ("Magbubukas ako ng bagong business"), or what you tell your friend who's emotionally closed off ("Sana'y magbukas ka na ng iyong puso."). It's full of hope and potential, whether it's for a sale or for a second chance.
usage_notes: Future tense of "magbukas".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magbubukas** ang tindahan mamayang alas-otso ng umaga.","translation":"The store **will open** later at eight in the morning."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **magbubukas** ng pinto para sa mga bisita?","translation":"Who **will open** the door for the guests?"}]

translation: leaning; tilted; related to Mount Makiling
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na nakahilig o tagilid. Ginagamit din bilang pangalan ng tanyag na bundok sa Laguna na pinaniniwalaang hugis ng isang nakahigang babae.
etymology: From `kiling` (tilt, inclination). The mountain is named for its shape.
original_explanation: First, it's the name of the famous mountain, home of the diwata Maria Makiling. Legend says the mountain's shape is her sleeping form. Second, it literally means 'tilted' or 'leaning'. Like that one friend's selfie angle, or the Leaning Tower of Pisa, but make it Pinoy. "Bakit Makiling 'yang pagkakabit ng frame?"
usage_notes: When capitalized, it almost always refers to Mount Makiling. When lowercase, it's an adjective meaning tilted.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Bundok **Makiling** ay isang tanyag na pasyalan sa Laguna.","translation":"Mount **Makiling** is a famous destination in Laguna."},{"sentence":"Naging **makiling** ang poste pagkatapos ng malakas na bagyo.","translation":"The post became **tilted** after the strong typhoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagbibigay ng buhay, sigla, o lakas; may kakayahang magpanumbalik ng sigla o magdulot ng kalakasan.
original_explanation: Yung unang higop mo ng kape sa umaga, 'yun ang **makabubuhay** ng kaluluwa mo. O 'yung sahod na papasok na sa Biyernes, sobrang **makabubuhay** ng pag-asa!
usage_notes: The 'makabu-' prefix is a reduplication of the first syllable of the root word 'buhay' combined with 'maka-', indicating a future or potential state. It functions as an adjective meaning 'life-giving' or 'revitalizing'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang malamig na inumin ay tunay na **makabubuhay** sa isang taong nauuhaw.","translation":"A cold drink is truly **life-giving** to a thirsty person."},{"sentence":"Ang ngiti niya ay parang sikat ng araw na **makabubuhay** ng anumang nalantang damdamin.","translation":"Her smile is like a sunbeam that is **invigorating** to any withered feeling."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang puwersa ng pulisya na may kapangyarihang militar, partikular na tumutukoy sa Philippine Constabulary (PC) na dating sangay ng sandatahang lakas ng Pilipinas.
original_explanation: This is a major throwback term. Before there was the PNP (Philippine National Police), there was the PC or the Philippine Constabulary. Ask your lolo, he'll probably have stories about the "Konstabularyo." They were the police force with a more military-style structure. Today, it's mostly a historical term, like a landline or a floppy disk.
usage_notes: Primarily a historical term referring to the now-defunct Philippine Constabulary (1901-1991), which was a gendarmerie-type force.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lolo ko ay dating miyembro ng **Konstabularyo** ng Pilipinas.","translation":"My grandfather was a former member of the Philippine **Constabulary**."},{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang disiplina sa ilalim ng **konstabularyo** noong araw.","translation":"Discipline was strict under the **constabulary** back in the day."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pang-abay na nagsasaad ng agarang pagsunod ng isang pangyayari o kilos; pinaikling anyo ng 'pagdaka at'.
original_explanation: This is the classic 'and then suddenly' from a dramatic storyteller. Like when you're telling your friend about your crush, 'He looked at me, *pagdaka'y* ngumiti!' It’s the literary, old-school version of “tapos bigla.” You'll find this more in books than in a TikTok comment section.
usage_notes: Primarily used in literary or formal writing. It connects two clauses, with the second one happening immediately after the first.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig niya ang putok, **pagdaka'y** nagtago sa ilalim ng mesa.","translation":"He heard the shot, **and then immediately** hid under the table."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng sibat na may tatlo o higit pang matutulis na dulo, na ginagamit sa pangingisda o pangangaso sa tubig.
original_explanation: Think Aquaman's weapon, but the Pinoy version. It's a spear with multiple pointy ends, perfect for spearfishing. It’s what you use when you want to catch fish with more drama and skill than just a simple net or line. The ultimate 'I will personally stab that fish' tool.
usage_notes: A traditional tool for fishing and hunting aquatic animals, typically having three or more prongs.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit ang mangingisda ng **salapang** upang makahuli ng malaking talakitok.","translation":"The fisherman used a **harpoon** to catch a large trevally."}]

translation: to ask someone to tell a story
meaning_filipino: Isang pakiusap na magsalaysay o magbahagi ng isang kuwento o pangyayari.
etymology: From Spanish 'cuento' (story), with the Tagalog request prefix 'pa-'.
original_explanation: The magic word you use to get the latest 'chismis' (gossip) from your favorite tita or office mate. It's the verbal cue that means 'spill the tea!' The full, unedited version, please.
usage_notes: Often used in an informal, conversational context as a request, like 'pakwento naman'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uy, **pakwento** naman tungkol sa bakasyon ninyo sa Boracay!","translation":"Hey, **tell me a story** about your vacation in Boracay!"},{"sentence":"Lumapit ang mga bata sa kanilang lolo at nagsabing, \"Lolo, **pakwento** po!\"","translation":"The children approached their grandfather and said, \"Grandpa, **please tell us a story**!\""}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bahagi ng sistemang reproduktibo ng babae, na kilala rin bilang bahay-bata, kung saan lumalaki ang sanggol bago isilang.
etymology: From Spanish 'útero', which comes from Latin 'uterus'.
original_explanation: A Spanish loanword that sounds more clinical than 'bahay-bata'. You'd probably hear this from a doctor or in a biology class. It's the original 'first home' or 'maternal condo unit' for every person.
usage_notes: A medical or scientific term. 'Bahay-bata' is the more common, native term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan sa klase ng biology ang mga bahagi ng **utero**.","translation":"The parts of the **uterus** are being studied in biology class."},{"sentence":"Ang myoma ay isang uri ng bukol na tumutubo sa **utero**.","translation":"A myoma is a type of tumor that grows in the **uterus**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng sayaw na panlipunan na nagmula sa Argentina at Uruguay, na may masidhing damdamin at dramatikong mga galaw.
original_explanation: It's that dance you see in movies where the couple looks like they're about to either kiss or kill each other. Full of passion, drama, and sharp turns. Parang 'yung relationship niyo ng ex mo—a dramatic **tanggo** of 'I love you' and 'I hate you.' It takes two to tango, and sometimes in life, it takes two to mess things up beautifully.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa sayaw. Ang pariralang Ingles na "It takes two to tango" ay paminsan-minsang ginagamit sa Pilipinas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-aral silang sumayaw ng **tanggo** para sa kanilang kasal.","translation":"They studied how to dance the **tango** for their wedding."},{"sentence":"Ang **tanggo** ay isang sayaw na puno ng pagnanasa at damdamin.","translation":"The **tango** is a dance full of passion and emotion."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglunok ng anumang uri ng likido, tulad ng tubig, gatas, gamot, o alak.
original_explanation: The universal solution to thirst and, for some, to problems. Can refer to drinking water, juice, or your daily dose of meds. But when used on a Friday night ("Tara, uminom tayo!"), it almost always means alcohol. It's the verb that powers hydration and inuman sessions.
usage_notes: A very common verb. The context determines what is being drunk. 'Uminom ng tubig' (drink water), 'uminom ng gamot' (drink medicine), 'uminom' by itself in a social context often implies alcoholic beverages.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **uminom** ng walong basong tubig araw-araw.","translation":"Don't forget to **drink** eight glasses of water every day."},{"sentence":"Kailangan niyang **uminom** ng gamot tatlong beses sa isang araw.","translation":"He needs to **drink** his medicine three times a day."},{"sentence":"Niyaya niya akong **uminom** pagkatapos ng trabaho.","translation":"He invited me to **drink** (alcohol) after work."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na tumutukoy sa isang tao na may mataas at matinis na boses, o kumikilos sa paraang nakakainis, pabebe, o isip-bata.
etymology: Onomatopoeic, possibly mimicking a high-pitched, grating sound or laugh.
original_explanation: You know that one friend whose laugh sounds like a rusty hinge? Or someone who acts overly cute and silly to the point of being annoying? That's kengkeng. It's the sound of nails on a chalkboard but in human form. Often used to describe a "pabebe" or trying-hard-to-be-cute attitude.
usage_notes: This is a very informal, colloquial term. Can be considered mildly insulting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakairita 'yung boses niyang **kengkeng**.","translation":"Her annoyingly **high-pitched** voice is irritating."},{"sentence":"Tigilan mo nga 'yang pagiging **kengkeng** mo, hindi na nakakatuwa.","translation":"Stop your **silly/ditzy** behavior, it's not funny anymore."}]

translation: to spread the news; to announce
meaning_filipino: Ikalat o ipaalam sa marami ang isang balita o impormasyon.
etymology: From Tagalog 'i-' (causative/instrumental prefix) + 'pamalita' (act of spreading news), from 'balita' (news).
original_explanation: The official verb for our 'Marites' culture. When you have some juicy chismis, your duty is to 'ipamalita' it to the group chat. It's taking a piece of news and making sure everyone knows about it. 'Uy, engaged na si crush! Ipamalita mo na sa buong barkada!' (Hey, our crush is engaged! Spread the news to the whole squad!).
usage_notes: Can be used for both formal announcements and informal gossip.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo munang **ipamalita** ang sorpresa hangga't hindi pa handa ang lahat.","translation":"Don't **spread the news** about the surprise until everything is ready."},{"sentence":"Agad niyang **ipinamalita** sa kanilang pamilya ang magandang balita.","translation":"She immediately **announced** the good news to her family."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang kumpanya o organisasyon na legal na nakarehistro bilang isang korporasyon.
original_explanation: The fancy term you see after a company name, like "Ayala Corporation, Inkorporada." It's the legal way of saying "we're a legit business, not just some random tiangge stall." It has its own legal personality, separate from its owners. It's the "-Inc." in the Philippines.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in formal business and legal contexts. Refers to entities treated as feminine in Spanish (e.g., la corporación).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aming kumpanya ay opisyal nang **inkorporada** at nakarehistro sa SEC.","translation":"Our company is now officially **incorporated** and registered with the SEC."},{"sentence":"Makikita sa dulo ng pangalan ng negosyo kung ito ay **inkorporada**.","translation":"You can see at the end of the business name if it is **incorporated**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal at pinaikling anyo ng pariralang 'tingnan mo', na ginagamit bilang isang utos na pagmasdan ang isang bagay.
etymology: Contraction of 'tingnan mo' (look at it/you look).
original_explanation: This is the faster, more casual, and sometimes more urgent version of 'Tingnan mo'. It's the 'Yo, look!' of Tagalog. You use it when you don't have time for the extra syllable because that jeepney is about to leave or the chismis is happening *right now*.
usage_notes: Highly colloquial and common in spoken language. It is considered slang or informal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tingni**, ang ganda ng damit niya!","translation":"**Look**, her dress is so beautiful!"},{"sentence":"**Tingni**! Ayan na ang bus na hinihintay natin.","translation":"**Look**! There's the bus we've been waiting for."}]

translation: to contribute; to donate (especially for a wake or cause)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng tulong na pinansyal o materyal, karaniwan para sa isang namatayan, may sakit, o para sa isang kawanggawa.
etymology: From the root word 'abuloy' (contribution) with the infix '-um-'.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you see a GCash QR code for a friend's sick relative or when you drop a few coins in the donation box at a wake. It's the Filipino 'bayanihan' spirit in financial form. It's not just giving money, it's showing you're there for them, kahit sa konting halaga lang. More formal than 'nag-ambag'.
usage_notes: Strongly associated with giving financial or material aid for funerals, medical expenses, or community projects.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming kaibigan ang **umabuloy** para sa operasyon ng kanyang ina.","translation":"Many friends **donated** for his mother's operation."},{"sentence":"Pumunta kami sa burol upang **umabuloy** at makiramay.","translation":"We went to the wake to **contribute** and offer our condolences."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang indibidwal na hayop, halaman, bahagi ng isang bagay, o substansiya na kinukuha bilang halimbawa ng uri nito para sa siyentipikong pag-aaral o pagsusuri.
original_explanation: Yung sample na hinihingi sa'yo sa clinic para sa laboratory test. Pwedeng ihi, dugo, o kung ano pa man. Or 'yung tuyong dahon na pinadikit sa'yo sa science project mo noong elementary. Basically, a sample for scientific chismis.
usage_notes: Kadalasang ginagamit sa kontekstong medikal o siyentipiko.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha sila ng **espesimen** ng bato mula sa buwan.","translation":"They took a rock **specimen** from the moon."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong magdala ng **espesimen** ng iyong ihi para sa urinalysis.","translation":"You need to bring a urine **specimen** for the urinalysis."}]

translation: goods for sale; merchandise on consignment
meaning_filipino: Mga produkto, kalakal, o anumang bagay na inilalaan upang ipagbili, karaniwang para sa ibang tao.
etymology: From pa- prefix indicating purpose/causation + tinda (sell/goods).
original_explanation: Ito yung mga paninda na hindi mo direktang pag-aari, pero ikaw ang nagbebenta. Parang consignment. Yung kaibigan mong nag-iwan ng ube cheese pandesal sa'yo para ibenta, 'yan ang **patinda** niya. Or when you help your mom sell her Avon products.
usage_notes: Refers to goods being sold by someone on behalf of the owner.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinuha ni Aling Nena ang mga **patinda** niyang kakanin mula sa kapitbahay.","translation":"Aling Nena got her rice cakes, which were **goods for her to sell**, from her neighbor."},{"sentence":"Marami siyang **patinda** sa kanyang maliit na sari-sari store.","translation":"She has a lot of **merchandise for sale** in her small variety store."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagkahulog o pagkalagas ng buhok, balahibo, o balat, karaniwan sa mga hayop bilang bahagi ng kanilang siklo ng buhay.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `pan-` (na nagiging `panl-` dahil sa asimilasyon) + pag-uulit ng unang pantig ng salitang-ugat (`lu`) + `lugon` (pagkalagas o pagkahulog ng buhok/balahibo).
original_explanation: This is what happens to your dog or cat when suddenly, your black shirt looks like a furry sweater. It's the natural "ghosting" ng fur nila before a new batch grows. Parang buhok mo rin after a stressful week sa work, naglalagas din.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng mga hayop na nagpapalit ng balahibo (ibon), balat (ahas), o buhok (aso). Bihirang gamitin para sa paglalagas ng buhok ng tao, maliban sa pampanitikang paraan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa panahon ng **panlulugon** ang alaga kong ahas kaya't ayaw nitong kumain.","translation":"My pet snake is in its **molting** period, which is why it doesn't want to eat."},{"sentence":"Kitang-kita ang **panlulugon** ng manok dahil nagkalat ang balahibo sa kulungan.","translation":"The chicken's **shedding** is very evident because feathers are scattered in the coop."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o akto ng pagiging mas maikli o pagbawas sa haba, tagal, o lawak ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: That feeling when your sahod goes through a 'pag-igsi' because of all the bills. Or when your long weekend suddenly feels too short. It's the process of something becoming shorter, whether it's your patience in traffic or the hemline of a skirt.
usage_notes: Used to describe the reduction in length, duration, or extent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napansin ko ang **pag-igsi** ng kanyang buhok.","translation":"I noticed the **shortening** of her hair."},{"sentence":"Ang **pag-igsi** ng araw ay tanda ng papalapit na taglamig sa ibang bansa.","translation":"The **shortening** of the day is a sign of approaching winter in other countries."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal para sa "ama" o "tatay".
etymology: From Spanish 'padre' (father), modified into a slang form.
original_explanation: This is the '90s cool kid way of saying "dad". It's the male counterpart of "mudra" (mother). "Uwi na ako, baka hanapin na ako ng pudra ko." It's got that retro, jeprox vibe.
usage_notes: Often used with 'mudra' (mother). Considered informal and somewhat dated, but still widely understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpaalam ka na ba sa **pudra** mo na gagabihin ka?","translation":"Did you ask permission from your **dad** that you'll be home late?"},{"sentence":"Ang **pudra** ko ang nagturo sa akin kung paano mag-bike.","translation":"My **father** was the one who taught me how to ride a bike."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang pamatlig na ginagamit sa pagtukoy o pag-abot sa isang bagay na malapit sa nagsasalita.
etymology: A variant of 'ito', possibly influenced by 'narito'.
original_explanation: The shorter, more urgent version of 'Ito o.' It's what you say when you finally find your keys, when you're handing over the bayad in a jeepney, or when you present your finished report to your boss like a trophy. 'Heto na, boss! Pwede na mag-leave?'
usage_notes: Often used as an interjection ('Heto!'). It implies presentation or handing something over. 'Ito' just points, 'Heto' presents.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Heto** na ang sukli mo.","translation":"**Here's** your change."},{"sentence":"Kanina ko pa hinahanap ang salamin ko, **heto** lang pala sa ibabaw ng ulo ko!","translation":"I've been looking for my glasses, and **here they are**, right on top of my head!"}]

translation: a mutual exchange of affection; a place for affectionate moments
meaning_filipino: Ang tagpuan o pagkakataon kung saan nagaganap ang pagpapalitan ng lambing o pagmamahal ng dalawa o higit pang tao.
original_explanation: This is the 'session' or 'venue' for 'lambing'. It's the mutual act of being sweet and tender to each other. 'Mag-lambingan tayo' is an invitation to cuddle and be sweet. It can also be a place, like a specific park bench or a corner of the house known for sweet nothings. It's the G-rated part of 'Netflix and chill.'
usage_notes: The suffix '-an' denotes a place, a reciprocal action, or a time for something. Here, it signifies the reciprocal action between two or more people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ilalim ng puno ng mangga ang kanilang paboritong lugar ng **lambingan**.","translation":"Under the mango tree is their favorite place for **sweet, affectionate moments**."},{"sentence":"Natigil ang kanilang **lambingan** nang biglang dumating ang nanay niya.","translation":"Their **mutual exchange of affection** was interrupted when her mother suddenly arrived."}]

translation: to command someone; to order someone to do something
meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng isang partikular na gawain o direktiba ang isang tao na kailangan niyang sundin.
original_explanation: The official verb of parents and bosses everywhere. 'Pag-utusan mo na lang yung bunso' (Just order the youngest to do it) is a phrase heard in every Filipino household. It's the power to delegate, whether it's buying suka at the sari-sari store or finishing a report by EOD.
usage_notes: The focus of the verb is on the person being commanded.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **pag-utusan** na parang hindi mo ako kaibigan.","translation":"Don't **command me** as if I'm not your friend."},{"sentence":"Madalas siyang **pinag-uutusan** ng kanyang ina na bumili sa palengke.","translation":"He is often **ordered** by his mother to buy from the market."}]

translation: conflict of opinions; clash of ideas
meaning_filipino: Ang sitwasyon kung saan mayroong matinding hindi pagkakasundo o salungatan sa pagitan ng iba't ibang pananaw, opinyon, o ideya.
etymology: From pagkaka- + laban-laban (fighting each other) + ng mga (of the) + kuru-kuro (opinions).
original_explanation: This is what happens in every family group chat during election season, or in a meeting when everyone thinks their idea is the best. It's the intellectual version of a "bardagulan," a chaotic but sometimes productive clash of minds.
usage_notes: A complex phrase used to describe ideological or intellectual conflict.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging mainit ang talakayan dahil sa **pagkakalaban-laban ng mga kuru-kuro**.","translation":"The discussion became heated due to the **clash of opinions**."},{"sentence":"Makikita sa social media ang malinaw na **pagkakalaban-laban ng mga kuru-kuro** tungkol sa bagong patakaran.","translation":"A clear **conflict of ideas** regarding the new policy can be seen on social media."}]

translation: He himself / She herself; The very one
meaning_filipino: Isang parirala na nagbibigay-diin sa pagkakakilanlan ng isang tao; tumutukoy sa eksaktong taong pinag-uusapan at hindi sa iba.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng panghalip na "siya" (he/she) at ang pang-abay na "mismo" (self, exactly).
original_explanation: The ultimate "It's him/her!" phrase. You use this when you want to confirm with 100% certainty that you're talking about THE person. "Sino ang may utang sa'yo?" "Siya mismo!" (Points dramatically). It's the verbal equivalent of pointing a finger, adding an exclamation point, and maybe a spotlight for good measure. No room for doubt, it's that specific person.
usage_notes: Isang pariralang nagbibigay-diin. Ang "mismo" ay nagsisilbing pampatindi o intensifier.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Akala ko assistant lang niya, pero **siya mismo** ang sumagot ng telepono.","translation":"I thought it was just his assistant, but it was **he himself** who answered the phone."},{"sentence":"Ang sikat na aktres? **Siya mismo** ang nakita kong bumibili ng tuyo sa palengke!","translation":"The famous actress? It was **the very one** I saw buying dried fish at the market!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahaba at makitid na hukay sa lupa, karaniwang ginagamit para sa irigasyon o bilang depensa.
etymology: From Malay 'khandak', from Arabic 'خَنْدَق' (ḵandaq), from Middle Persian 'kndk' (kandag, “that which has been dug”).
original_explanation: Think of it as the 'kanal' your lolo dug to keep the carabaos out, or the trenches you see in old war movies. It's a man-made line in the sand, but with more mud and probably some frogs.
usage_notes: This is a more formal or literary term. "Kanal" is the more common word for a ditch or canal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumawa sila ng malalim na **handak** sa paligid ng kuta.","translation":"They made a deep **trench** around the fort."},{"sentence":"Nahulog ang kalabaw sa **handak** na puno ng tubig.","translation":"The carabao fell into the water-filled **ditch**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtanggap o pagsalin ng ari-arian, katangian, o tradisyon mula sa isang ninuno o naunang henerasyon sa kasalukuyang panahon.
etymology: From 'mana' (inheritance). The object-focus present tense form.
original_explanation: This is what's happening when your lola is still alive but has already promised you the 'good' plates. It's the live-action, slow-burn process of getting stuff passed down to you. It can be property, a family recipe, or 'yung ilong ng tatay mo.
usage_notes: This is the object-focus verb form for the present tense of inheriting something. The action is currently in progress.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Minamana** niya ang negosyo ng kanilang pamilya.","translation":"He/She **is inheriting** their family business."},{"sentence":"Ang galing niya sa pagluluto ay **minamana** niya sa kanyang lola.","translation":"Her skill in cooking **is being inherited** from her grandmother."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-upo o pagtayo na may malawak na pagitan ang mga binti o hita.
original_explanation: That pose you strike when you're super tired and just want to occupy as much space as possible on the couch. It's the opposite of sitting prim and proper. In jeepneys, this is the ultimate 'siksikan na, pero feeling solo' move.
usage_notes: Can be considered impolite or overly casual depending on the context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagod na pagod, **bumukaka** siya sa silya.","translation":"Exhausted, he **sat with his legs spread apart** on the chair."},{"sentence":"\"Huwag kang **bumukaka** diyan, para kang hari,\" saway ng nanay.","translation":"\"Don't **sit with your legs spread apart** there, you look like a king,\" his mother scolded."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalakbay o paglalakad nang walang tiyak na patutunguhan; pagala-gala.
original_explanation: This is the official term for being a 'lakwatsero/lakwatsera'. It's not just walking; it's aimless, adventurous walking. When you and your barkada decide to just 'see where your feet take you' in a new city or even just a giant mall, you're about to maglagalag.
usage_notes: Often implies a sense of freedom or sometimes, being lost or aimless.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **maglagalag** sa mga bundok tuwing Sabado.","translation":"He loves to **wander** in the mountains every Saturday."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng exam, gusto kong **maglagalag** sa Baguio.","translation":"After the exams, I want to **roam** around Baguio."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang awitin na kaaya-aya ang ritmo upang sayawin, o sa isang tao na mahilig sumayaw.
original_explanation: That feeling when a song drops and you can't help but move. If it's a certified bop that makes you want to hit the dance floor, it's 'masayaw'. Also describes your tita who's the first one to boogie during the family reunion, even if it's just to an 'Otso-Otso' remix.
usage_notes: Can refer to both a person's quality (fond of dancing) and a song's quality (danceable). Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Masayaw** talaga ang bagong kanta ng SB19!","translation":"The new song by SB19 is really **danceable**!"},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa pagiging **masayaw** na tao, laging nasa gitna ng salu-salo.","translation":"She is known for being a person who is **fond of dancing**, always in the middle of the party."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kathang-isip na linyang humahati sa globo sa Hilaga at Timog Hemispero, na may latitud na sero digri.
original_explanation: That imaginary belt around the Earth's waistline. Countries near it, like the Philippines, are blessed with two seasons: hot and hotter. It's the reason why your "summer body" is a year-round project.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa heograpiya at agham.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Pilipinas ay malapit sa **ekuwador**, kaya't tropikal ang klima dito.","translation":"The Philippines is near the **equator**, which is why it has a tropical climate."},{"sentence":"Tinawid ng barko ang linya ng **ekuwador**.","translation":"The ship crossed the **equator** line."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bahagi, kaputol, o yunit ng isang mas malaking kabuuan.
original_explanation: The default unit of measurement sa Pinoy birthday parties. "Ilang pirasong manok nakuha mo?" "Isang pirasong cake pa nga!" Also used for documents, "Isang pirasong xerox copy, please."
usage_notes: Used as a counter for items, especially parts of a whole.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigyan mo ako ng isang **piraso** ng papel.","translation":"Give me one **piece** of paper."},{"sentence":"Limang **piraso** ng fried chicken ang inorder niya.","translation":"He ordered five **pieces** of fried chicken."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na proseso ng pagdeklara ng Simbahang Katoliko na ang isang yumaong tao ay isang santo.
original_explanation: This is what happens when someone was so good in life that the Vatican decides to make them an official Saint, complete with a feast day. It's the ultimate 'level up' in the Catholic world. If your lola says you're a saint for helping her with her phone, she doesn't mean `magkanonisa`, she just means you're very patient.
usage_notes: A specific religious term used almost exclusively within the context of the Catholic Church.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang mahabang proseso ang kailangang pagdaanan bago **magkanonisa** ang isang tao.","translation":"A long process must be undergone before a person can be **canonized**."},{"sentence":"Umaasa ang marami na balang araw ay **magkanonisa** si Beato Carlo Acutis.","translation":"Many hope that Blessed Carlo Acutis will be **canonized** someday."}]

translation: to allocate for, to set aside for, to dedicate to
meaning_filipino: Mag-ukol o magtabi ng isang bagay (tulad ng oras, pera, o espasyo) para sa isang partikular na tao, layunin, o gamit.
original_explanation: This is you setting aside a portion of your salary for your 'ipon para sa concert' fund. It's dedicating your weekend to binge-watch a new series, or saving the last piece of chicken for your favorite sibling. It's the act of reserving something for a special purpose.
usage_notes: A verb that requires an object (what is being allocated) and a beneficiary or purpose (who or what it's for).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat nating **paglaanan** ng sapat na pondo ang sektor ng edukasyon.","translation":"We must **allocate** sufficient funds for the education sector."},{"sentence":"**Paglaanan** mo naman ako ng kaunting oras mo.","translation":"**Set aside** a little of your time for me."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aalis ng sabon, dumi, o anumang kemikal mula sa isang bagay gamit ang malinis na tubig.
original_explanation: It's that final step in doing the laundry or washing dishes. After all the scrubbing and soaping, you `magbanlaw` to get rid of the suds. If you don't do this properly, your plate will taste like Joy dishwashing liquid, and your shirt will feel stiff. It's the 'final rinse' cycle of your life's washing machine.
usage_notes: Often used for laundry, dishes, or even rinsing hair after shampooing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **magbanlaw** ka na ng mga plato pagkatapos mong magsabon.","translation":"Please, **rinse** the plates after you've soaped them."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **magbanlaw** nang mabuti ng mga damit para hindi mangati ang balat mo.","translation":"Don't forget to **rinse** the clothes well so your skin won't get itchy."}]

meaning_filipino: Kasalukuyang nagbabayad o kumukuha ng isang bagay kapalit ng pera.
original_explanation: What you're doing at 3 AM during a Shopee/Lazada 11.11 sale. You're not just 'buying', you're bumibili ng 'essentials' na hindi mo naman talaga kailangan, pero 'naka-sale, eh.' It's the official sport of the 'sahod' weekend.
usage_notes: Present progressive tense of 'bili' (to buy). The actor-focus form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming tao ang **bumibili** ng palamuti para sa Pasko.","translation":"Many people **are buying** decorations for Christmas."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko siyang **bumibili** ng bulaklak sa palengke kanina.","translation":"I saw her **buying** flowers at the market earlier."}]

translation: a tiny fraction; a minuscule amount
meaning_filipino: Isang napakaliit na bahagi, mas maliit pa sa karaniwan.
etymology: From ka- (reduplication) + titing (a very small bit).
original_explanation: This is the data allowance you have left on the 29th of the month. Or the patience you have left for your noisy kapitbahay's karaoke session at 2 AM. It's the "I can't even" level of smallness. Kakarampot's even smaller cousin.
usage_notes: Similar to "kakarampot", but can imply an even smaller, almost insignificant amount.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kakatiting** na asukal na lang ang natitira sa garapon.","translation":"There's only **a minuscule amount** of sugar left in the jar."},{"sentence":"May **kakatiting** na pag-asa pa siyang makapasa sa pagsusulit.","translation":"He still has **a tiny fraction** of hope to pass the exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang halaga ng salapi na ibinayad nang higit sa kinakailangang bayaran o utang.
original_explanation: That magical moment when you pay your Meralco bill and realize you paid extra. Yung sukli na hindi mo na binalikan sa tindahan, or yung bonus na binigay ng client mo kasi "keep the change" daw. It's the opposite of "kulang ang bayad mo." A rare but beautiful financial phenomenon.
usage_notes: Hindi ito gaanong karaniwan sa pang-araw-araw na usapan ngunit ginagamit sa mga pormal na transaksyon sa pananalapi o negosyo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **sobrepaga** ka na limampung piso sa iyong bill ng tubig.","translation":"You have an **overpayment** of fifty pesos on your water bill."},{"sentence":"I-apply na lang sa susunod na buwan ang nagawang **sobrepaga**.","translation":"Just apply the **overpayment** made to next month's bill."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-alis mula sa isang lugar na mapanganib patungo sa isang mas ligtas na lokasyon, karaniwan ay dahil sa isang kalamidad o kaguluhan.
original_explanation: Eto yung ginagawa ng buong barangay kapag may paparating na super typhoon at baha na hanggang leeg. It's the organized (or sometimes chaotic) act of getting the heck out of dodge because of danger. Hindi ito 'yung pag-alis mo sa party kasi na-awkwardan ka; this is for serious threats like floods, volcanic eruptions, or maybe when your tita starts asking about your love life at a family reunion.
usage_notes: Ang 'lumikas' ay partikular para sa pag-alis dahil sa panganib. Iba ito sa 'umalis' (to leave) o 'lumipat' (to move/transfer).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinailangang **lumikas** ng mga residente nang tumaas ang tubig-baha.","translation":"The residents had to **evacuate** when the floodwaters rose."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang 'social media account' na nilikha gamit ang isang huwad na pagkakakilanlan, karaniwang ginagamit upang manatiling anonimo, mag-obserba sa ibang tao nang hindi nalalaman, o para sa iba pang kaduda-dudang gawain.
etymology: From English "dummy" (a stand-in or imitation) and "account".
original_explanation: Your digital ninja suit. This is your spy account, used to check up on your ex, see what your crush is up to, or to join fan groups without revealing your real identity. Unlike a 'dump account' for your friends, a 'dummy' is for your... 'research'.
usage_notes: Often has a negative or mischievous connotation, associated with stalking ('marites' behavior) or online trolling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumawa siya ng **dummy account** para lang i-stalk ang Facebook ng dati niyang kasintahan.","translation":"She created a **dummy account** just to stalk her ex-boyfriend's Facebook."},{"sentence":"Nahuli siyang gumagamit ng **dummy account** para mag-comment sa sarili niyang post.","translation":"He was caught using a **dummy account** to comment on his own post."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sentro ng atensyon, interes, o aktibidad; ang kalinawan ng isang imahe na nakikita sa pamamagitan ng lente ng kamera o mata.
original_explanation: That thing your boss keeps telling you to have during meetings but is impossible to maintain when your phone is buzzing with Shopee notifications. It's your brain's 'Do Not Disturb' mode. When you're trying to study for an exam but your crush posts a new IG story, your 'pokus' is officially out the window. 'Focus lang, beshie, matatapos din 'yan!'
usage_notes: Used in both literal (camera focus) and figurative (concentration) senses.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawala ang **pokus** ko sa pag-aaral nang biglang nag-brownout.","translation":"I lost my **focus** on studying when the power suddenly went out."},{"sentence":"Ang **pokus** ng pelikula ay ang buhay ng mga OFW.","translation":"The **focus** of the movie is the life of OFWs."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang halagang ibinabayad para sa serbisyo ng pagpapadala ng sulat o pakete sa pamamagitan ng post office.
original_explanation: Ah, postage. A word that feels almost as vintage as the post office itself. This is the 'shipping fee' of our parents' generation. Before LBC and J&T Express tracking numbers, there was the humble selyo (stamp) you bought with your **bayad sa koreo**. It's the cost of making sure your love letter (or your bill statement) gets to its destination.
usage_notes: Now often replaced by "shipping fee" in modern contexts, but still the correct term for official postal services.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang isama ang tamang **bayad sa koreo** sa iyong sobre.","translation":"Don't forget to include the correct **postage** on your envelope."},{"sentence":"Magkano na ba ngayon ang **bayad sa koreo** para sa isang ordinaryong sulat?","translation":"How much is the **postage** for a regular letter nowadays?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal at pinaikling anyo ng salitang "dekorasyon"; tumutukoy sa mga palamuti o pampaganda sa isang lugar.
etymology: Pinaikling anyo ng salitang Espanyol na "decoración".
original_explanation: This is the Tita-speak for "aesthetic." Yung tanong na, "Ano'ng dekor natin sa Pasko?" ay isang seryosong isyu sa bawat pamilyang Pilipino. It's all about the palamuti—Christmas lights, parol, fiesta banderitas. Basically, anything that makes a place look more festive or IG-worthy.
usage_notes: Isang salitang kolokyal at madalas gamitin sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng **dekor** sa kasal nila, napaka-elegante.","translation":"The **decor** at their wedding is beautiful, very elegant."},{"sentence":"Tulungan mo ako sa **dekor** ng bahay para sa Pasko.","translation":"Help me with the house **decor** for Christmas."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang puno at ang bilog na bunga nito na may makapal at mamalahibong balat, at matamis-asim na laman na nakapalibot sa mga buto.
original_explanation: The fruit that's a workout to eat. You peel the thick skin, then suck on the fluffy, sweet-sour pulp around the seeds until your jaw gets tired. Also famous for being the main ingredient in Sinigang na Santol. Don't ever swallow the seed, or you'll be the subject of a medical drama episode.
usage_notes: The scientific name is *Sandoricum koetjape*. Swallowing the large seed is dangerous and can cause intestinal obstruction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap isawsaw sa asin ang maasim na **santol**.","translation":"It's delicious to dip sour **santol** in salt."},{"sentence":"Nagluto si nanay ng sinigang na baboy na may **santol**.","translation":"Mom cooked pork sinigang with **cotton fruit**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ipasok o isuksok ang isang bagay sa isang patusok na bagay tulad ng panuhog o sinulid.
original_explanation: The official verb of your friendly neighborhood BBQ stand. 'Ituhog' is to impale pieces of marinated pork onto a bamboo stick to create the glorious barbecue we all love. It's also what you do to beads to make a necklace, or metaphorically, how you connect a series of unfortunate events. 'Parang itinuhog ang kamalasan ko ngayon.'
usage_notes: Used for the action of piercing through one or multiple items with a long, thin object like a skewer, needle, or stick.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **ituhog** ang mga karne para sa ating ihawan.","translation":"Help me **skewer** the meat for our barbecue."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **ituhog** ang sinulid sa napakaliit na karayom.","translation":"It's hard to **thread** the string through a very small needle."}]

translation: to cause to separate; to break up (a couple, a fight)
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagiging sanhi ng paghihiwalay ng dalawa o higit pang tao o bagay na magkasama.
original_explanation: This is what a "kontrabida" does in a teleserye—they try to pahiwalayin the main couple. It's also what you do to two friends who are about to get into a fistfight, or when you sort your white clothes from your colored ones for laundry. Basically, it's the act of creating space between things that were once together.
usage_notes: The focus is on the people or things being separated.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan silang **pahiwalayin** ng kanilang mga magulang ngunit mas lalong tumibay ang kanilang pagmamahalan.","translation":"Their parents tried to **break them up**, but their love only grew stronger."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **pahiwalayin** ang mga basurang nabubulok at hindi nabubulok.","translation":"The biodegradable and non-biodegradable trash need to **be separated**."}]

translation: to make someone angry; to infuriate
meaning_filipino: Magdulot ng matinding galit o inis sa isang tao; galitin o yamutin nang husto.
etymology: Literal translation: 'to heat the head'. An idiomatic expression for causing anger.
original_explanation: What happens when your internet connection dies mid-Netflix binge, or when a client has 'just one more revision' for the 10th time. It's not a literal headache; it's that special kind of rage that makes you want to flip a table. Someone is **painitin-ing ang ulo** mo.
usage_notes: The verb `painitin` is conjugated. For example, `Pinainit mo ang ulo ko` (You made me angry).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **painitin ang ulo** ko sa umagang ito!","translation":"Don't **make me angry** this morning!"},{"sentence":"Talagang **pinaiinit** niya **ang ulo** ng lahat sa kanyang mga komento.","translation":"He is really **infuriating** everyone with his comments."}]

translation: act of washing hands or feet
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglilinis ng mga kamay o paa gamit ang tubig, na maaaring may kasamang sabon.
original_explanation: The OG anti-COVID measure. It's what your lola tells you to do the moment you step inside the house, even before you can say 'Mano po.' It's the simple act of washing away the grime of the outside world, or the germs from holding the LRT handrail.
usage_notes: Less common than 'paghuhugas ng kamay'. Often found in more formal or literary contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paghihinaw** bago kumain ay isang mabuting gawi.","translation":"The **act of washing hands** before eating is a good habit."},{"sentence":"Naghanda siya ng palanggana para sa **paghihinaw** ng mga bisita.","translation":"He prepared a basin for the guests' **washing of hands/feet**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang krimen ng sapilitang pagkuha ng pera o anumang mahalagang bagay mula sa isang tao sa pamamagitan ng pananakot o pagbabanta.
original_explanation: This is the classic 'bigyan mo ako ng pera kundi...' move. It's when someone forces you to pay up, not because you owe them, but because they're threatening you. Think of those 'kotong cops' in movies or someone blackmailing you with your old Friendster photos. It's a serious crime, not just 'panghihingi'.
usage_notes: A legal and criminal term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinampahan siya ng kasong **ekstorsiyon** matapos mangikil ng pera.","translation":"He was charged with **extortion** after demanding money."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang matakot isumbong ang anumang uri ng **ekstorsiyon**.","translation":"Don't be afraid to report any form of **extortion**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtama nang direkta at may katiyakan sa isang target o layunin.
original_explanation: That "bullseye!" moment. When your comeback in an argument is so good it leaves them speechless, that's *sumapol*. When a basketball player hits a perfect swish, *sumapol*. It's a direct, undeniable, no-questions-asked hit. Can be literal (a punch) or figurative (a perfect comment).
usage_notes: Implies a direct and accurate hit. Often used in contexts of fighting, sports, or arguments. 'Sapol' as a standalone word is an exclamation for a direct hit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumapol** sa kanyang mukha ang malakas na suntok ng boksingero.","translation":"The boxer's strong punch **hit** his face **squarely**."},{"sentence":"**Sumapol** sa puso ko ang sinabi niya tungkol sa pag-ibig.","translation":"What she said about love really **hit the mark** in my heart."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hindi pag-alala o pagkawala sa isipan ng isang bagay, tao, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: The more dramatic, poetic cousin of 'nakalimot'. You don't just 'lumimot' your keys. You 'lumimot' a promise, a past love, or your responsibilities. It has a weight to it, like you actively (or passively-aggressively) let the memory go. Perfect for hugot posts. 'Sana gano'n kadali lumimot.'
usage_notes: An alternative form of 'nakalimot'. It is less common in colloquial speech but often used in literature, songs, and formal writing for a more profound or dramatic effect. It's an actor-focus verb in the completed aspect.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paano ka nakayanang **lumimot** sa lahat ng ating pinagsamahan?","translation":"How could you manage **to forget** everything we've been through?"},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **lumimot** sa iyong mga pinagmulan.","translation":"Do not **forget** where you came from."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong labas sa batas, karaniwang miyembro ng isang armadong grupo na nagnanakaw o gumagawa ng krimen sa mga liblib na lugar.
original_explanation: The classic villain in old Filipino action movies, usually hiding out in the mountains. Today, the term can be jokingly used for someone who "steals" the last piece of chicken joy, for a cat who steals food from the table, or for a politician with questionable wealth.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinahabol ng mga alagad ng batas ang mga **bandido** sa kabundukan.","translation":"The law enforcers are chasing the **bandits** in the mountains."},{"sentence":"Tinagurian siyang **bandido** ng kanyang mga kaibigan dahil palagi niyang inuubos ang pulutan.","translation":"He was jokingly called a **bandit** by his friends because he always finishes the appetizer."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang baryasyon ng 'kaartehan'; tumutukoy sa pagiging maselan, pabebe, o labis na pag-arte sa kilos o pananalita na hindi natural.
etymology: From ka- + arte (from Spanish 'arte') + -han. A common phonetic variation of 'kaartehan'.
original_explanation: Basically 'kaartehan's' slightly less common twin. Same meaning, different spelling, same level of extra-ness. If 'kaartehan' is the main character, 'kaartihan' is the stunt double. You can use them interchangeably when calling out your friend's dramatic antics.
usage_notes: A common variant of 'kaartehan' with the exact same meaning. The choice between the two is often a matter of personal or regional preference.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puro **kaartihan** lang ang alam ng batang iyan.","translation":"That child knows nothing but **affectation**."},{"sentence":"Wala akong panahon para sa **kaartihan** mo.","translation":"I don't have time for your **fussiness**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng orkidya (Dendrobium anosmum) na kilala sa mabango at kumpol-kumpol nitong mga bulaklak na karaniwang kulay lila o rosas.
original_explanation: The OG air freshener of your lola's garden. This orchid doesn't just look pretty; it smells amazing. It's the kind of flower that makes you want to take a deep breath and forget your problems, even for just a second.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa isang partikular na uri ng orkidya na kilala sa bango nito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Namumulaklak na ang mga **sanggumay** sa aming hardin.","translation":"The **sanggumay** orchids in our garden are now blooming."},{"sentence":"Mabango ang amoy ng bulaklak ng **sanggumay**.","translation":"The flower of the **sanggumay** smells fragrant."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtitiklop ng isang bagay, tulad ng damit o papel, upang maging mas maliit o mas maayos.
original_explanation: This is the verb your mom yells when she sees your clothes ("mga damit") scattered everywhere. It's the act of folding, the mortal enemy of the "sampay-bakod" and "chair-drobe" system. "Hoy, ilupi mo yang mga damit mo!"
usage_notes: Primarily used for folding clothes, paper, or other flat, pliable objects.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **ilupi** ang mga bagong labang damit.","translation":"I need **to fold** the newly washed clothes."},{"sentence":"**Inilupi** niya ang sulat at inilagay sa sobre.","translation":"She **folded** the letter and put it in an envelope."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aaral at paggamit ng mga idyoma o sawikain sa isang wika.
original_explanation: This is the study of why 'balat-sibuyas' means sensitive and not 'onion-skinned', and why 'nagbibilang ng poste' means unemployed and not literally counting posts. Idyomatika is the Level Up course in Filipino, where you learn the secret codes and inside jokes of the language.
usage_notes: A technical term used in linguistics and language studies.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **idyomatika** ay isang mahalagang bahagi ng pag-aaral ng anumang wika.","translation":"**Idiomatics** is an important part of studying any language."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kaparusahan na pinaniniwalaang nagmula sa isang mas mataas na kapangyarihan o sa Diyos bilang ganti sa isang kasalanan.
original_explanation: This is what your lola warns will happen if you don't finish the food on your plate or if you talk back. It's karma on a cosmic, biblical scale. Think floods, lightning strikes, or maybe just really bad traffic on payday Friday—that could be a parusa ng langit for some.
usage_notes: A dramatic and often religious phrase to describe a calamity or misfortune perceived as punishment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinuring nilang **parusa ng langit** ang biglaang pagbaha sa kanilang lugar.","translation":"They considered the sudden flood in their area as **divine punishment**."},{"sentence":"Sabi ng matanda, ang sakit na dumapo sa kanya ay **parusa ng langit**.","translation":"The old man said the illness that befell him was a **punishment from heaven**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtanggap o pagsalin ng ari-arian, katangian, o tradisyon na naganap na sa nakaraan mula sa isang ninuno.
etymology: From 'mana' (inheritance). The object-focus past tense form.
original_explanation: Past tense na 'to. The deed is done. You got the house, the money, the antique furniture, or your dad's receding hairline. It's the 'sana all' moment when your friend gets a condo from their parents, and you just got... well, character development.
usage_notes: This is the object-focus verb form for the past tense of inheriting something. The action is completed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Minana** ko ang lumang relos na ito mula sa aking lolo.","translation":"I **inherited** this old watch from my grandfather."},{"sentence":"Sayang, hindi niya **minana** ang talento ng kanyang ina sa pagkanta.","translation":"Too bad, he/she did not **inherit** his/her mother's talent in singing."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan o sitwasyon na hindi tiyak, hindi sigurado, o may pag-aalinlangan.
etymology: Mula sa "walang" (without) at "katiyakan" (certainty), na mula sa ugat na "tiyak" (certain).
original_explanation: Yung status ng relationship niyo. Hindi mo alam kung kayo ba, M.U. lang, o friends with benefits. Puro "ano tayo?" pero walang sagot. Ganyan, **walang-katiyakan**. It's the "we need to talk" that never happens, leaving you in a permanent state of confusion.
usage_notes: Often used to describe abstract situations like the future, a relationship status, or the outcome of an event.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nababalot ng **walang-katiyakan** ang hinaharap ng ekonomiya.","translation":"The future of the economy is shrouded in **uncertainty**."},{"sentence":"Ayaw ko na sa sitwasyong **walang-katiyakan**; kailangan ko ng malinaw na sagot.","translation":"I don't want this **uncertain** situation anymore; I need a clear answer."}]

translation: to carry across; to help cross
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtulong sa isang tao o pagdala sa isang bagay upang makarating sa kabilang panig ng isang hadlang, tulad ng ilog, kalsada, o hirap.
original_explanation: Literally, helping someone cross the street. Figuratively, it's what you do for your friend who's broke before payday—you 'itawid' them with a loan. It's getting someone or something over a hump, whether it's a river or the last five days of the month.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for crossing physical barriers or metaphorically for overcoming difficulties.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **itawid** mo ang matanda sa kalsada.","translation":"Please, **help** the old person **cross** the road."},{"sentence":"Sa tulong ng scholarship, **naitawid** niya ang kanyang pag-aaral sa kolehiyo.","translation":"With the help of a scholarship, he was able to **get through** his college studies."}]

meaning_filipino: Agad-agad; sa sandaling iyon din; walang pagkaantala.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'send' button. The moment you think it, it happens. Parang PM is the key, pero with actions. It's the opposite of 'mamaya na,' the official slogan of procrastination.
usage_notes: This is a formal and somewhat archaic word. You'll find it more in literature or formal speeches than in everyday conversation. 'Agad-agad' is the more common equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kapagkaraka** siyang tumayo nang marinig ang tawag.","translation":"He stood up **immediately** upon hearing the call."},{"sentence":"Nang dumating ang balita, **kapagkaraka** silang umalis.","translation":"When the news arrived, they left **at once**."}]

translation: illegitimate child, child born out of wedlock
meaning_filipino: Isang anak na isinilang ng mga magulang na hindi kasal sa isa't isa.
etymology: Isang pariralang Tagalog na literal na nangangahulugang "child outside," na tumutukoy sa pagiging "sa labas ng kasal."
original_explanation: The classic teleserye plot twist! It's the secret child who appears years later to claim their inheritance or confront a parent. While the term sounds harsh ('child outside'), modern society is thankfully becoming more accepting. Still, the drama associated with this term is *chef's kiss*.
usage_notes: Bagama't karaniwan, ito ay maaaring ituring na hindi sensitibo o masakit na termino. Mas pormal at neutral ang "anak na ipinanganak sa labas ng kasal."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nalaman niyang mayroon pala siyang kapatid na isang **anak sa labas**.","translation":"He found out that he had a sibling who was an **illegitimate child**."},{"sentence":"Ang pagiging **anak sa labas** ay hindi hadlang upang maging matagumpay sa buhay.","translation":"Being a **child born out of wedlock** is not a hindrance to being successful in life."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang estado o kalagayan kung saan ang isang gawain, proyekto, o pangyayari ay umabot na sa kanyang katapusan o wakas.
original_explanation: The best feeling in the world after a long exam, a hell week at school, or a toxic project. It's the 'mic drop' moment of any task. 'Project? Tapos na. Report? Tapos na. Pasensya ko? Tapos na rin.'
usage_notes: Can be used to describe tasks, events, or even relationships.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tapos** na ang klase, pwede na tayong umuwi.","translation":"Class is **finished**, we can go home now."},{"sentence":"Hindi pa ako **tapos** sa trabaho ko.","translation":"I'm not yet **done** with my work."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng pagkakahawig o pagiging pareho sa katangian, anyo, o kalagayan.
original_explanation: When you and your bestie show up wearing the same color without planning it. 'Uy, magkatulad tayo!' It's the low-key twin moment. Not exactly identical, but close enough for a side-by-side IG story.
usage_notes: The form 'magkatulad na magkatulad' is an intensifier, meaning 'exactly alike' or 'identical'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magkatulad** ang kanilang mga pananaw sa buhay.","translation":"Their views on life are **similar**."},{"sentence":"Sila ay **magkatulad na magkatulad**; para silang kambal.","translation":"They are **exactly alike**; they are like twins."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gagawing pag-aalis ng dumi, kalat, o anumang bagay na hindi kaaya-aya sa isang lugar o bagay. Aspektong panghinaharap ng pandiwang 'maglinis'.
original_explanation: The weekend promise you make to your mom that sometimes never happens. "Ma, maglilinis ako ng kwarto mamaya." It's the battle cry before general cleaning, fueled by coffee and the fear of your mother's sermon (or walis).
usage_notes: Future tense of the verb 'maglinis'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Maglilinis** ako ng buong bahay bukas para sa Pasko.","translation":"I **will clean** the entire house tomorrow for Christmas."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **maglilinis** ng pinagkainan natin?","translation":"Who **will clean** up after our meal?"}]

meaning_filipino: Tuwiran; walang namamagitan o walang paligoy-ligoy.
original_explanation: Yung prangka mong kaibigan na walang filter. "Uy, tumaba ka," imbes na "You're glowing!" Ganyan ang direkta magsalita. Walang preno, walang detour, diretso sa puso (o sa ego). Effective sa work, minsan masakit sa personal na buhay.
usage_notes: Maaari ring gamitin bilang pang-abay, at madalas na ipinagpapalit sa 'diretso'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas gusto ko ang **direkta** na sagot kaysa sa mga pahiwatig.","translation":"I prefer a **direct** answer over hints."},{"sentence":"May **direkta** siyang koneksiyon sa manager kaya madali siyang natanggap.","translation":"She has a **direct** connection to the manager which is why she was hired easily."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-abot o pagpunta sa pinakamataas na bahagi o rurok, lalo na ng isang bundok o anumang mataas na lugar.
original_explanation: What mountaineers do after a long, tiring hike. "Sa wakas, tumuktok na kami!" It's reaching the summit, the highest point. Can also be used figuratively for your career: "After 10 years in the company, finally, tumuktok na rin siya as CEO."
usage_notes: Refers to reaching the physical top of something, like a mountain, or figuratively, the pinnacle of a career or achievement.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nanghina sila bago pa man **tumuktok** ng Bundok Apo.","translation":"They grew weak even before they could **reach the summit** of Mount Apo."},{"sentence":"Layunin ng bawat empleyado na **tumuktok** sa hagdan ng korporasyon.","translation":"It is the goal of every employee to **reach the peak** of the corporate ladder."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pamahalaan kung saan ang kataas-taasang kapangyarihan ay nasa kamay ng isang monarka.
original_explanation: The OG political system. It's a government run by a king or queen. Think of it as a family business, but the business is an entire country, and the CEO position is passed down to their kids. It's all about bloodlines and 'divine right'—basically, "My dad was king, so now I'm king. Deal with it."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang United Kingdom ay isang halimbawa ng konstitusyonal na **monarkiya**.","translation":"The United Kingdom is an example of a constitutional **monarchy**."}]

translation: to fuel; to add fuel to
meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng panggatong ang apoy upang lumaki o magpatuloy sa pag-aapoy. Sa matalinhagang kahulugan, ito ay ang pag-udyok o pagsulsol sa isang tao na magpatuloy sa isang kilos o damdamin, lalo na sa galit o alitan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang `gatong` (fuel) at hulaping `-an` (locative/directional suffix).
original_explanation: Ito yung ginagawa ng 'marites' mong kaibigan. Imbes na awatin ka sa away niyo ng jowa mo, lalo ka pa niyang binibigyan ng rason para magalit. 'Oo nga, girl, tama ka, 'wag kang papatalo!' Parang pagbubuhos ng gasolina sa apoy, pero sa chismis at drama. To add fuel to the fire, literally and figuratively.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin nang literal para sa apoy, o patalinghaga para sa mga damdamin tulad ng galit, pagtatalo, o pananabik.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Gatungan** mo pa ang apoy para hindi mamatay habang nagluluto tayo.","translation":"**Add more fuel** to the fire so it doesn't die out while we're cooking."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang **gatungan** ang galit niya; hayaan mo na lang siyang kumalma.","translation":"Don't **fuel** his anger anymore; just let him calm down."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng paligsahan o palaro kung saan may mga kalahok na naglalaban-laban upang magkamit ng gantimpala o karangalan.
etymology: From 'ka-' prefix + 'paligsahan' (a variant of ligsahan). 'ligsahan' itself is from 'ligsa' + '-han'.
original_explanation: This is the official term for any "patimpalak" you see in a fiesta, a noontime show, or even the office Christmas party. It's where your hidden talent for belting out Whitney Houston songs or your team's questionable dance moves finally get their moment in the spotlight. Winner gets a cash prize, the losers get "exposure".
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'paligsahan' or 'kompetisyon'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumali siya sa isang **kapaligsahan** sa pag-awit.","translation":"He/She joined a singing **competition**."},{"sentence":"Ang premyo para sa mananalo sa **kapaligsahan** ay malaki.","translation":"The prize for the winner of the **contest** is big."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking nangingibabaw, agresibo, at may kumpiyansa sa sarili na itinuturing na pinuno ng isang grupo.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na 'alpha male', isang terminong ginagamit sa ethology (pag-aaral sa asal ng hayop).
original_explanation: The guy who acts like the main character in a teleserye. He's confident, maybe a little too much, and everyone seems to listen to him. Think of the stereotypical gym buff who gives unsolicited advice or the boss who commands a room. Sa Pinas, it's the 'hari ng barkada' or the 'pogi problems' guy who thinks he's God's gift to the world.
usage_notes: Isang loan phrase na madalas gamitin sa pop culture, social media, at impormal na usapan para ilarawan ang isang partikular na tipo ng pagkalalaki.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming kababaihan daw ang naaakit sa isang **alpha male**.","translation":"They say many women are attracted to an **alpha male**."},{"sentence":"Nag-aagawan ang dalawang **alpha male** sa opisina para sa promosyon.","translation":"The two **alpha males** in the office are competing for the promotion."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay, ideya, pahayag, o kilos na sadyang ginawa upang magdulot ng kalituhan o pagkaligaw ng isip.
original_explanation: In an exam, it's the multiple-choice option that's *almost* correct. In an argument with your jowa, it's when they bring up something you did in 2018. It's a distraction, a mental smoke bomb. A classic **panlito**.
usage_notes: Often implies an intentional act to confuse someone, like a red herring.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglagay ang guro ng mga **panlito** sa pagsusulit upang subukin ang mga mag-aaral.","translation":"The teacher placed **confusers** (distractors) in the test to challenge the students."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpadala sa kanyang mga **panlito**; ituon mo ang pansin sa totoong isyu.","translation":"Don't be swayed by his **red herrings**; focus on the real issue."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging mabilis mag-isip, alisto, at handa sa anumang sitwasyon.
original_explanation: This is your brain on its third cup of coffee during a client presentation. It's that moment you perfectly answer a surprise question from the boss, or when you manage to dodge a flying slipper from your mom. It's the opposite of 'loading...'
usage_notes: Often used to describe a person's mental quickness or readiness. The prefix 'pagka-' turns the adjective 'listo' into a noun describing the state or quality of being 'listo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Humanga ako sa **pagkalisto** ng bata sa pagsagot sa mga tanong.","translation":"I was amazed by the child's **quick-wittedness** in answering the questions."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **pagkalisto**, naiwasan niya ang aksidente.","translation":"Because of his **alertness**, he avoided the accident."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging wasak, depektibo, o hindi na gumagana nang maayos, maaaring tumukoy sa bagay, reputasyon, o kaisipan.
etymology: From `pagka-` (the act or state of) + `sira` (broken, damaged).
original_explanation: This is what happens to your diet during the holidays, your phone after it falls face down, or your trust after someone "seen-zones" your very important message. It's the state of being broken, busted, or malfunctioning—physically or emotionally.
usage_notes: A very versatile word that can mean physical damage, food spoilage, mental instability ('sira ang ulo'), or a broken promise ('sira ang usapan').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang naging **pagkasira** ng mga pananim dahil sa bagyo.","translation":"The **damage** to the crops due to the typhoon was extensive."},{"sentence":"Ang biglaang **pagkasira** ng ref ang problema namin ngayon.","translation":"The sudden **breakdown** of the refrigerator is our problem now."}]

translation: to keep oneself busy; to be very busy
meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang pag-uukol ng sarili sa maraming gawain upang maging okupado o maiwasan ang pag-iisip sa ibang bagay.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `mag-` (gumanap ng kilos), `paka-` (pagpapaigting), at salitang-ugat na `abala` (busy, disturbance).
original_explanation: The post-breakup survival tactic. Instead of wallowing in sadness, you `magpakaabala`—you hit the gym, take on a new hobby, accept all the OT (overtime) at work. It's the art of distracting yourself with a to-do list as long as EDSA traffic. 'Friend, move on ka na.' 'Paano?' 'Magpakaabala ka!'
usage_notes: Madalas na nagpapahiwatig ng isang sinadyang pagsisikap na maging abala, kung minsan bilang isang paraan ng paglihis ng atensyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **magpakaabala** sa trabaho upang makalimot sa kanyang mga problema.","translation":"She tried to **keep herself busy** with work to forget her problems."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong **magpakaabala** at baka magkasakit ka.","translation":"Don't **be too busy** or you might get sick."}]

meaning_filipino: Pormal na ipahayag, ipaalam, o iproklama ang isang bagay sa publiko o sa isang awtoridad.
original_explanation: This is what you do at customs when you have something to, well, declare: you `ideklara` it. It's also what a President does to announce a state of calamity, or what you do when you finally, officially tell your crush, "Gusto kita!" You're making it official and public. No take-backs!
usage_notes: Used in formal, legal, political, or personal contexts to mean making a formal statement or proclamation.
