usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **ideklara** ang lahat ng iyong binili sa Bureau of Customs.","translation":"You need to **declare** all your purchases at the Bureau of Customs."},{"sentence":"**Idineklara** ng pangulo ang araw na iyon bilang isang special non-working holiday.","translation":"The president **declared** that day as a special non-working holiday."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagbibigay-diin sa agarang pagiging magkalapit o magkadikit ng dalawang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: This isn't just 'next to', this is 'breathing-the-same-air' next to. This is when you're in a packed jeepney and your face is practically in someone's armpit. It's the level of closeness when you can read the messages on your seatmate's phone without even trying. It's "katabi" with zero personal space.
usage_notes: An intensified form of 'katabi'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umupo siya sa silyang **katabing-katabi** ng pinto para madaling makalabas.","translation":"He sat on the chair **right next to** the door so he could get out easily."},{"sentence":"Ang tindahan ng prutas ay **katabing-katabi** lang ng palengke.","translation":"The fruit stand is **immediately adjacent** to the market."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit na paghinto habang nasa daan o gumagawa ng isang bagay; ang pagpapaliban-liban o pagbabagal-bagal.
original_explanation: This is you on the way to the office when you really don't want to go to work. Stop for coffee, stop to look at a cat, stop to tie your already-tied shoelaces. It's the act of delaying the inevitable by making frequent, unnecessary stops. "Huwag kang **tumigil-tigil** diyan, baka ma-late ka!"
usage_notes: Implies a sense of dawdling, laziness, or hesitation. The repetition of 'tigil' emphasizes the intermittent nature of the stopping.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bakit ka ba **tumigil-tigil** sa paglalakad? May hinahabol pa tayo.","translation":"Why do you **keep stopping** while walking? We still have something to catch."},{"sentence":"Pinagalitan siya ng nanay niya dahil **tumigil-tigil** siya sa kanto kasama ang mga barkada.","translation":"His mother scolded him because he was **loitering** at the corner with his friends."}]

translation: elegance; splendor; quality of being grand
meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging marangya, maganda, o kahanga-hanga sa itsura o ayos.
original_explanation: Yung OOTD mo na pang-SONA, pang-red carpet, or pang-debut. 'Yung tipong mapapa-'Sana all!' ang mga Marites sa garaan ng suot mo. It's the physical manifestation of 'extra'.
usage_notes: The `-an` suffix turns the root adjective `gara` (grand, elegant) into a noun describing the quality itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi maikakaila ang **garaan** ng kanyang kasuotan sa gabing iyon.","translation":"The **elegance** of her attire that night was undeniable."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay na inilalagay sa pagitan ng dalawang piraso ng tinapay o sa loob ng ibang pagkain.
original_explanation: The best part of the sandwich! It's the cheese, ham, egg, or tuna spread that makes boring tinapay exciting. In life, it's the 'extra' stuff that makes things interesting. 'Ano'ng palaman mo sa buhay?' can be a hugot question for 'What gives your life substance?'
usage_notes: Can also refer to stuffing for toys or pillows, but the food context is most common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paborito kong **palaman** sa pandesal ay keso.","translation":"My favorite **filling** for pandesal is cheese."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagdaragdag ng yaman, kaalaman, o karanasan.
etymology: From pag- (nominalizer) + pa- (causative) + pa- (progressive aspect) + yaman (wealth). Lit. 'the act of causing to become wealthy'.
original_explanation: The process of going from 'isang kahig, isang tuka' to 'unli-samgyup anytime'. It's not just about money; pwede ring 'pagpapayaman ng kaalaman' (reading books) or 'pagpapayaman ng kultura' (watching K-dramas). It's leveling up your life, one way or another.
usage_notes: Can refer to material wealth (kayamanan), knowledge (kaalaman), or experience (karanasan).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapayaman** ng bokabularyo ay mahalaga sa pag-aaral ng wika.","translation":"The **enrichment** of vocabulary is important in language learning."},{"sentence":"Inakusahan siya ng ilegal na **pagpapayaman** habang nasa pwesto.","translation":"He was accused of illegal **enrichment** while in office."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi patag o hindi makinis ang daanan na nagdudulot ng malakas na pag-alog o pag-uga sa isang sasakyan.
original_explanation: Describes 90% of provincial roads and even some parts of EDSA. It's a free, unwanted massage you get while riding a jeepney or a bus. If your journey feels like it's inside a washing machine on spin cycle, the road is **matagtag**.
usage_notes: Specifically describes the quality of a journey or a surface that causes violent shaking or jarring.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakasarap sanang matulog sa bus kung hindi lang **matagtag** ang daan.","translation":"It would have been great to sleep on the bus if only the road wasn't **bumpy**."},{"sentence":"Humawak kang mabuti, **matagtag** ang biyahe paakyat ng bundok.","translation":"Hold on tight, the ride up the mountain is **rough**."}]

translation: to name after; to give a name
meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng pangalan ang isang tao, bagay, o lugar; isunod ang pangalan sa isang tao o bagay bilang parangal.
original_explanation: This is what your parents did when they decided to call you 'John Lloyd' or 'Bea' because they were huge fans. It's the act of bestowing a name, often in honor of someone or something. 'Sino kaya ang ipapangalan nila sa bago nilang aso?' (I wonder what they'll name their new dog?).
usage_notes: Often used in the context of naming a child, a pet, a place, or a project. The structure is typically 'ipangalan ang [new thing] sa [person/thing being honored]'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ipangalan** mo raw sa lolo mo ang iyong panganay na anak.","translation":"They say you should **name** your firstborn child **after** your grandfather."},{"sentence":"Ang bagong tulay ay **ipinangalan** sa isang pambansang bayani.","translation":"The new bridge was **named after** a national hero."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa tunog na hindi malayang lumalabas, tila pigil o nagmumula sa lalamunan.
original_explanation: That sound you make when you're trying not to laugh in a serious meeting. That little squeak or choked sob when you're trying to hide that you're crying. It's a sound that's held back, full of unexpressed emotion. A 'paimpit na tawa' (stifled laugh) or a 'paimpit na iyak' (suppressed sob). It's the audio equivalent of biting your tongue.
usage_notes: Often describes a sound, like a laugh, cry, or scream. The glottal stop at the end is characteristic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang kanyang **paimpit** na hikbi mula sa kwarto.","translation":"I heard her **stifled** sob from the room."},{"sentence":"Isang **paimpit** na sigaw ang kumawala sa kanya nang makita ang multo.","translation":"A **suppressed** scream escaped from her when she saw the ghost."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi kasama sa sakop, abot, o nasasakupan ng isang bagay, batas, o kasunduan.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na nag-file ka ng insurance claim tapos ang sagot, "Sorry po, di-saklaw ng policy niyo 'yan." Or sa project management, 'yung gusto ni client na feature pero di-saklaw ng original na napag-usapan. The official term for "wala 'yan sa usapan."
usage_notes: Isang tambalang salita na gumagamit ng panangging 'di' (pinaikling 'hindi').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga pinsalang dulot ng baha ay **di-saklaw** ng kanilang insurance.","translation":"The damages caused by the flood are **not covered** by their insurance."},{"sentence":"Ang paksang iyan ay **di-saklaw** ng ating talakayan ngayon.","translation":"That topic is **out of scope** for our discussion today."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng maingay at magaspang na tunog mula sa lalamunan habang natutulog.
original_explanation: 'Yung tunog ng tatay mo 'pag mahimbing ang tulog, parang may nagse-chainsaw sa kwarto. 'Yung sound na dahilan kung bakit kailangan mo ng earphones para makatulog. The national anthem of deep sleep.
usage_notes: 'Humagok' is often considered a stronger or louder version of 'humilik'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lakas **humagok** ng kasama ko sa kwarto kaya hindi ako makatulog.","translation":"My roommate **snored** loudly so I couldn't sleep."},{"sentence":"Alam mong mahimbing ang tulog niya kapag nagsimula na siyang **humagok**.","translation":"You know he's fast asleep when he starts to **snore**."}]

translation: to feel resentful; to harbor a grudge
meaning_filipino: Ang pagdaramdam ng sama ng loob o galit sa isang tao dahil sa isang nagawang kasalanan o hindi magandang karanasan.
etymology: From sakit (pain, illness). The affix -hin- and reduplication of 'na' imply a deep, internalized feeling, forming 'hinanakit' (resentment).
original_explanation: This is the silent treatment level 99. It's when you say "Okay lang ako" but your face says "You're dead to me." It’s the emotional baggage you carry after a friend betrays you or when you were the only one who didn't get invited to the group lunch. The root of all "tampo".
usage_notes: Describes an internal feeling of resentment. Hinanakit is the noun form. The verb describes the act of feeling or harboring this resentment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Madali siyang **maghinanakit** kahit sa maliliit na bagay lamang.","translation":"He easily **feels resentful** even over small things."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang hindi **maghinanakit** sa kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"She tried not to **harbor a grudge** against her parents."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit na pagbaling ng ulo upang tumingin sa likuran.
original_explanation: That dramatic "movie scene" moment when you're leaving someone and you keep looking back, hoping they'd run after you. It's the classic "don't look back in anger," but you do it anyway. Also, when you're walking home late at night and you think someone's following you.
usage_notes: Similar to 'palinga-linga' but specifically for looking *back*. Often implies nostalgia, regret, longing, or fear.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umalis siyang **palingun-lingon**, umaasang tatawagin mo siya.","translation":"She left, **repeatedly looking back**, hoping you would call her."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **palingun-lingon** sa nakaraan; harapin mo ang bukas.","translation":"Don't keep **looking back** at the past; face the future."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian, gawa, o diwa ng pagiging isang bayani; pagpapakita ng pambihirang katapangan at pagmamahal sa bayan.
etymology: From ka- + bayani + -han, meaning the essence or act of being a 'bayani' (hero).
original_explanation: This is what OFWs are often called—mga bagong bayani—for their sacrifices. Kabayanihan isn't just for history books; it's the Grab driver working 16 hours for his family, the nurse on a double shift, or anyone who puts others before themselves. It's the ultimate 'sana all' moment for character.
usage_notes: A highly formal and respected term, often used in nationalistic or historical contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginugunita natin ang **kabayanihan** ni Dr. Jose Rizal tuwing Disyembre.","translation":"We commemorate the **heroism** of Dr. Jose Rizal every December."},{"sentence":"Ang pagtulong sa kapwa sa gitna ng sakuna ay isang tunay na gawa ng **kabayanihan**.","translation":"Helping others in the midst of a disaster is a true act of **heroism**."}]

meaning_filipino: Mahati o mapaghiwalay sa dalawang bahagi, karaniwang tumutukoy sa mga bagay na matitigas tulad ng kahoy, bato, o bao ng niyog.
etymology: From the prefix 'ma-' (denoting ability or potential) + 'baak' (a split or cleavage).
original_explanation: What happens to a coconut when the manong with the bolo hits it just right. Also, what happens to your heart ('pusong nabaak') when you see your crush with someone else. It's a clean, decisive split, not just a crack. Hugot: 'Sana kung 'di tayo para sa isa't isa, mabaak na lang agad, 'wag nang patagalin pa.'
usage_notes: Often used for hard, brittle objects. The active verb form is 'baakin' (to split something). 'Mabiyak' is a close synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit anong pilit, hindi niya **mabaak** ang buko gamit lang ang kanyang mga kamay.","translation":"No matter how he tried, he couldn't **split** the young coconut using only his hands."},{"sentence":"Sa lakas ng kidlat, tila **nabaak** ang malaking puno ng akasya.","translation":"From the force of the lightning, the large acacia tree seemed to have been **cleaved**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging puno o pagkakaroon ng mga uod, karaniwan sa pagkain o organikong bagay na nabubulok.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'uod' (worm) at hulaping '-in', na nagsasaad ng isang kalagayan o aksyon na gagawin sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is what happens to that fruit you forgot at the back of the ref. Or metaphorically, 'yung chismis na kumakalat sa office, parang uurin na sa sobrang luma pero pinag-uusapan pa rin. It describes something being eaten from the inside out, literally or figuratively.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin para sa mga pagkaing nasisira na, ngunit maaari ring gamiting patalinghaga para sa isang bagay na bulok o sira mula sa loob.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kainin 'yan, baka **uurin** na ang mangga.","translation":"Don't eat that, the mango might be **infested with worms** already."},{"sentence":"Ang sistema ng gobyerno ay tila **uurin** na sa korapsyon.","translation":"The system of government seems to be **infested** with corruption."}]

translation: to move over; to slide over
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-usog o paggalaw nang bahagya upang magbigay ng puwang.
original_explanation: The magic word inside a crowded jeepney. "Para! Bayad po. Mag-ipod po ng konti." It's the polite way of saying "Your bag is taking up a whole person's space, please move."
usage_notes: A less common synonym for "umusog". Primarily used when asking someone to make space while seated.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **mag-ipod** ka naman para makaupo ako.","translation":"Please, **move over** so I can sit."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang parirala o ekspresyon na ang kahulugan ay hindi literal at hindi mahihinuha mula sa kahulugan ng mga indibidwal na salita nito.
original_explanation: An idyum is a password to sounding like a local. It's when you say someone has a 'butas ang bulsa' (hole in the pocket) to mean they're broke, not that their pants need sewing. It's the OG hugot line of language, where words mean something deeper than what they literally say.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'sawikain'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang \"kumukulo ang dugo\" ay isang **idyum** na nangangahulugang galit na galit.","translation":"\"Blood is boiling\" is an **idiom** that means very angry."},{"sentence":"Mayaman sa mga **idyum** ang wikang Filipino.","translation":"The Filipino language is rich in **idioms**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay, karaniwan ay bulaklak, na ganap na bukas o namumukadkad nang husto. Maaari ring gamitin sa isang bagay na punong-puno o umaapaw.
original_explanation: Imagine a flower that's not just blooming, it's *extra*. It's serving full-on, glorious, 'wala nang bukas' levels of bloom. It's the floral equivalent of getting your 13th-month pay and everything feels abundant. Pwedeng gamitin sa bulaklak o sa pusong nag-uumapaw sa saya.
usage_notes: Often used to describe flowers, but can be used metaphorically for anything that is bursting or overflowing with abundance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Busaksak** na ang mga rosas sa hardin ni Lola.","translation":"The roses in Grandma's garden are in **full bloom**."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng bonus, **busaksak** sa pagkain ang aming handaan.","translation":"After the bonus, our feast was **bursting** with food."}]

translation: a heavy blow; a powerful strike
meaning_filipino: Isang malakas at mabilis na hampas o suntok, karaniwang ginagamitan ng kamay o isang bagay.
original_explanation: This isn't just a tap; it's a full-on, "umilag ka kung ayaw mong ma-ospital" kind of hit. Think Manny Pacquiao's punch, or your mom's "palo" with a walis tambo when you've been a pasaway. It's a strike with intent and power.
usage_notes: Often implies a sudden and forceful action. Can be used literally for a physical strike or figuratively for a major setback.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malutong na **bigwas** ang pinakawalan ng boksingero sa kanyang kalaban.","translation":"The boxer unleashed a solid **heavy blow** on his opponent."},{"sentence":"Ang biglaang pagtaas ng presyo ng bilihin ay isang **bigwas** sa mga mamimili.","translation":"The sudden price hike of goods is a **heavy blow** to consumers."}]

translation: to cause to halt or be thwarted
meaning_filipino: Magdulot ng paghinto o pagkabigo sa isang nasimulang gawain o plano.
original_explanation: Ever planned a beach trip but then a typhoon suddenly enters the PAR? That's it. Your plans were "mapa-udlot". It's the universe telling you "Not today, satan!" A classic example of "drawing ka pa."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang biglaang pag-ulan ang siyang **mapaudlot** sa aming lakad.","translation":"The sudden rain was what **caused our trip to be halted**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **mapaudlot** ang iyong mga pangarap dahil lang sa isang pagkabigo.","translation":"Don't let your dreams **be thwarted** just because of one failure."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang sangkap o rekado na idinadagdag sa pagkain upang mapainam o mapatingkad ang lasa nito.
original_explanation: This is the secret weapon in every nanay's kitchen. It could be Magic Sarap, MSG, a cube of bouillon, or even just a squeeze of calamansi. It's that extra 'something' that turns a boring dish into a "Wow, ano'ng sahog nito?" moment. The culinary equivalent of a magic wand.
usage_notes: Refers to ingredients that make food taste better.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagdagdag siya ng kaunting patis bilang **pampasarap** sa nilaga.","translation":"She added a little fish sauce as a **flavor enhancer** for the stew."},{"sentence":"Ang paborito niyang **pampasarap** ay ang bagoong.","translation":"His favorite **flavoring** is shrimp paste."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matamis na pampahid o pangkober para sa mga keyk, cupcake, o biskwit, karaniwang gawa sa asukal, mantikilya, at gatas.
original_explanation: The best part of any birthday cake, let's be real. It's that sugary, creamy goodness you scrape off with a fork when no one's looking. For kids (and kids-at-heart), the cake is just a vessel for the **frosting**.
usage_notes: Used interchangeably with 'icing'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paborito kong parte ng cupcake ay ang **frosting**.","translation":"My favorite part of the cupcake is the **frosting**."},{"sentence":"Sobrang tamis ng **frosting** ng keyk.","translation":"The **frosting** of the cake is too sweet."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking homoseksuwal o may atraksyon sa kapwa lalaki. Maaari ring gamitin bilang pang-uri upang ilarawan ang katangiang ito.
etymology: Origin is uncertain, but has been in use since at least the mid-20th century.
original_explanation: The most common, neutral-to-slangy term for a gay man in the Philippines. It's less formal than 'homoseksuwal' but more direct than 'beki'. Like many labels, its sting (or lack thereof) depends entirely on who's saying it and how. Among friends, it's just a fact. From a bully, it's an insult.
usage_notes: Can be considered derogatory by some, especially when used by non-LGBTQ+ individuals with malicious intent. However, it is also widely used for self-identification. 'Bakla' is a more widely accepted neutral term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marami akong kaibigang **bading**.","translation":"I have many **gay** friends."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong gamitin ang salitang '**bading**' bilang panlait.","translation":"Don't use the word '**gay**' as an insult."}]

meaning_filipino: Paghiwa-hiwalayin ang mga bahagi ng isang bagay na binuo; buwagin o itigil ang operasyon ng isang grupo o organisasyon.
original_explanation: What happens to your carefully built Lego masterpiece when your younger sibling gets to it. On a more serious note, it's what happens to a company, a government agency, or a K-Pop group when they decide to disband. It's the end of an era. Pack it up, folks, the show's over.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical objects (dismantle) or abstract entities like groups (dissolve, disband).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang pamunuan na **maglansag** ng buong departamento dahil sa pagkalugi.","translation":"The management decided **to dissolve** the entire department due to financial losses."},{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **maglansag** ng lumang aparador na ito.","translation":"Help me **dismantle** this old cabinet."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na bersyon ng salitang Ingles na 'deserve', na nangangahulugang karapat-dapat o nararapat. Ginagamit bilang pandiwa o pang-uri.
etymology: From English 'deserve', a phonetic and stylized spelling popular in Filipino social media and gay lingo.
original_explanation: The ultimate validation from Pinoy internet culture. When you achieve something, you didn't just 'deserve' it, you 'dasurv' it! It's sprinkled with a little bit of sass and a whole lot of affirmation. Got that promotion? Dasurv! Treated yourself to milk tea? Dasurv! It's the short, punchy way of saying 'You earned it, gurl!'
usage_notes: Highly informal and used primarily in online conversations and among younger speakers. Can function as a verb ('I dasurv this') or an adjective ('This is so dasurv').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Congratulations sa new phone! **Dasurv** mo 'yan!","translation":"Congratulations on the new phone! You **deserve** it!"},{"sentence":"Pagod sa work, kaya **dasurv** ko ang isang oras na massage.","translation":"Tired from work, so I **deserve** a one-hour massage."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa asawang babae sa isang kasal; ang babaeng kabiyak ng isang lalaki.
etymology: Mula sa "may" at "bahay", na literal na nangangahulugang "may-ari ng bahay" o "nasa bahay".
original_explanation: Siya ang reyna ng tahanan, ang C.E.O. of Household Affairs, at ang Finance Manager ng budget. Minsan tinatawag ding "misis" o "kumander". Siya yung taong alam kung nasaan ang lahat ng nawawala mong gamit at kung kailan ka huling naligo. Ang paghingi ng permiso sa kanya ay mas mahirap pa kaysa sa visa application.
usage_notes: Medyo tradisyonal ang tunog ng "maybahay". Mas karaniwan na ngayon ang "misis" o "asawa".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinakilala niya sa amin ang kanyang magandang **maybahay**.","translation":"He introduced his beautiful **wife** to us."},{"sentence":"Ang aking **maybahay** ang nag-aasikaso ng lahat sa aming tahanan.","translation":"My **wife** takes care of everything in our home."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghinto sa isang kilos, galaw, o gawain.
original_explanation: What your mom screams from the kitchen when you and your siblings are about to break a vase. It's the ultimate 'cut it out' command. Also, what your heart wishes your feelings would do for that person who left you on 'seen'. "Puso, **tumigil** ka na, please."
usage_notes: A very common command. The root 'tigil' is often used on its own as an imperative.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumigil** ang ulan kaya nakauwi na kami.","translation":"The rain **stopped**, so we were able to go home."},{"sentence":"Sabi ng doktor, kailangan ko nang **tumigil** sa paninigarilyo.","translation":"The doctor said I need to **stop** smoking."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang indibidwal na nagpapakita ng kawalan ng hiya, galang, o konsiderasyon sa damdamin o karapatan ng iba.
original_explanation: Literally, a 'person with no shame.' This isn't just someone who made a mistake; this is their whole personality. They are the living embodiment of `walang-hiya`. Think of the tita who comments on your weight gain at every family reunion. Yes, that's a `walang-hiyang tao`.
usage_notes: A very common and strong pejorative phrase. The linker '-ng' is attached to 'walang-hiya' to modify the noun 'tao'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **walang-hiyang tao** lamang ang magnanakaw mula sa mahihirap.","translation":"Only a **shameless person** would steal from the poor."},{"sentence":"Tinawag siyang **walang-hiyang tao** matapos niyang magkalat ng tsismis.","translation":"She was called a **shameless person** after she spread gossip."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na pinaikli mula sa salitang Ingles na 'relatable', na nangangahulugang nakauugnay o may pagkakatulad sa isang sitwasyon, damdamin, o karanasan.
etymology: Mula sa pinaikling salitang Ingles na "relatable".
original_explanation: The official battle cry of the chronically online. When a meme, a hugot line, or a post about being broke before sweldo hits too close to home, you just comment "rel". It's the digital equivalent of nodding knowingly while saying "same, beshie, same." Short, sweet, and perfectly captures the shared struggle.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa social media at impormal na pag-uusap. Itinuturing na isang salitang hiram na naging bahagi ng Taglish.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Yung post niya about sa pagod pero kailangan pa rin mag-work, sobrang **rel**.","translation":"Her post about being tired but still needing to work is so **relatable**."},{"sentence":"Sabi sa meme, \"Nag-ipon ako, tapos nagutom.\" **Rel**.","translation":"The meme said, \"I saved money, then I got hungry.\" **Relatable**."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi nagbabago; nananatili sa isang kalagayan, antas, o halaga.
original_explanation: 'Yung pagmamahal niya sa'yo, parang bill ng Meralco—konstante ang pagtaas. O kaya naman 'yung feelings mo for your crush na 'di ka pinapansin, konstante pa rin kahit masakit na. It's something that doesn't change, for better or for worse.
usage_notes: Can also be used as an adverb (pang-abay) meaning 'constantly'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Konstante** ang pag-ulan sa buong linggo kaya bumaha.","translation":"The rain was **constant** all week, which caused a flood."},{"sentence":"Dapat **konstante** ang iyong pagsisikap upang makamit ang iyong mga pangarap.","translation":"Your effort must be **constant** to achieve your dreams."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matinding damdamin ng pag-ayaw o pagkasuklam sa isang tao o bagay. Baryant ng 'antipatiya'.
original_explanation: Same as 'antipatiya'. That gut feeling that makes you want to avoid someone. 'Yung 'di mo lang sila bet. Period. No further explanation needed. The vibes are just off.
usage_notes: Karaniwang baybay at bigkas sa modernong Tagalog, kasama ng 'antipatiya'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya maitago ang kanyang **antipatya** sa bagong manager.","translation":"She couldn't hide her **antipathy** towards the new manager."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginagamit upang ipahayag ang isang posibleng mangyari o bilang pag-iingat sa isang bagay na hindi tiyak.
original_explanation: This is the official word for your "what if" scenarios with your crush. It's also your mom's favorite phrase when she makes you bring an umbrella on a sunny day. "Magdala ka ng extra face mask, saka-sakali." It's the ultimate 'just in case' contingency planning.
usage_notes: Often used at the beginning of a clause to introduce a hypothetical situation. Interchangeable with 'sakali'. The 'saka-' adds a slight emphasis on 'and then, if...'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ipon ka ng pera, **saka-sakali** magkaroon ng emergency.","translation":"Save money, **just in case** an emergency happens."},{"sentence":"Dalhin mo ang resibo, **saka-sakali** kailanganing palitan ang binili mo.","translation":"Bring the receipt, **if ever** you need to exchange what you bought."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang serye ng mga paliwanag, opinyon, o tala na naglalarawan o nagsusuri sa isang kaganapan, teksto, o isyu.
original_explanation: This is the actual "sabi" or opinion that the komentarista gives. It's the unsolicited advice from your tita about your life choices, but written down or broadcasted for everyone to hear. It's the long-winded caption on a Facebook post dissecting a social issue.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglabas ng **komentaryo** ang pahayagan tungkol sa bagong batas.","translation":"The newspaper released a **commentary** about the new law."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **komentaryo** sa pelikula ay naging viral online.","translation":"His **commentary** on the movie went viral online."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging huli o pagkaantala sa isang gawain, lakad, o plano dahil sa isang hindi inaasahang pangyayari.
etymology: From Tagalog na- (verb prefix) + Spanish 'atraso' (delay, backwardness).
original_explanation: This is what happens when you plan to leave at 7 AM but EDSA has other plans for you. You get stuck in traffic for 3 hours and arrive at your meeting late. "Sorry, boss, naastraso ako sa traffic." It's the official anthem of every Manila commuter. Derived from the Spanish 'atraso' (delay).
usage_notes: A very common word in the context of traffic, appointments, and project deadlines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Naastraso** ang byahe namin dahil sa biglaang pagbaha.","translation":"Our trip **was delayed** because of sudden flooding."},{"sentence":"Ayokong **maastraso** ang sweldo ng mga empleyado.","translation":"I don't want the employees' salaries **to be delayed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Kumilos sa tubig sa pamamagitan ng paggalaw ng mga braso at binti upang umusad o manatiling nakalutang.
original_explanation: The official national sport during summer vacation. It's what you do to escape the heat, whether in a fancy resort, a provincial river, or a crowded wave pool. Also, a metaphor for being overwhelmed is 'nalulunod' (drowning), but this is the fun version where you're actually moving forward.
usage_notes: This is the general verb for the act of swimming.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **maglangoy** sa dagat bukas.","translation":"I want **to swim** in the sea tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Natuto siyang **maglangoy** noong siya ay limang taong gulang pa lamang.","translation":"She learned **to swim** when she was only five years old."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tao, lugar, o entidad na tatanggap o kung saan dapat ihatid ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the answer to the Shopee/Lazada rider's question, 'Sino po'ng pag-entregahan nito?' (Who is the recipient of this?). It's the target, the destination, the person whose day will be made (or whose wallet will be saddened) by the arrival of a package. You are the pag-entregahan of your online shopping addiction.
usage_notes: This word specifies the recipient or destination of a delivery. It's different from 'pag-entrega,' which is the act of delivery itself. It often functions as the object of a verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ikaw ba ang **pag-entregahan** ng paketeng ito?","translation":"Are you the **recipient** of this package?"},{"sentence":"Pakisulat nang malinaw ang pangalan ng **pag-entregahan** at ang address.","translation":"Please write the name of the **recipient** and the address clearly."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng puna, opinyon, o hatol sa isang bagay, gawa, o tao, na maaaring positibo o negatibo. Isang anyo ng pagsusuri.
etymology: From `puna` (comment, remark, criticism). The `paN-` prefix (manifesting as `pam-`) and reduplication creates a noun for the act of criticizing or commenting.
original_explanation: The national sport of titas at a family gathering. It can be constructive, like what your prof gives you on your thesis, or... not. It's the "Uy, tumaba ka" comment that's disguised as an observation. It’s what happens in the comments section of any social media post.
usage_notes: Can be neutral (critique), positive (praise), or negative (fault-finding). The context determines its nature.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bukás siya sa anumang **pamumuna** upang mapabuti ang kanyang trabaho.","translation":"He is open to any **critique** to improve his work."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pamumuna** ay hindi nakatulong, bagkus ay nakasakit pa ng damdamin.","translation":"His **criticism** wasn't helpful, instead it was hurtful."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking basket na karaniwang yari sa yantok o kawayan, ginagamit sa paglalagay o paglilipat ng mga ani tulad ng prutas at gulay.
original_explanation: Imagine the OG eco-bag. It's that huge, sturdy basket you see at the palengke, overflowing with mangoes or kamote. It's what your lola uses to bring home enough produce to feed a small barangay. Not for your little grocery run, this is for serious hauling.
usage_notes: Often associated with agriculture, harvests, and provincial life. It is larger than a 'bayong' or 'buslo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng mangga ang **tiklis** na dala ni Mang Jose mula sa bukid.","translation":"The **large basket** Mang Jose carried from the farm was full of mangoes."},{"sentence":"Ilang **tiklis** ng kamatis ang kanilang inani ngayong araw?","translation":"How many **large baskets** of tomatoes did they harvest today?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggalaw ng isang bagay tulad ng pinto, bintana, o libro mula sa pagiging sarado tungo sa pagiging hindi sarado.
original_explanation: The past tense of 'magbukas.' This is what the door did when you forgot to lock it. It’s what your Lazada package did when you finally got your hands on it. Unlike 'bumuka' (for mouths/flowers), 'bumukas' is for things with hinges, covers, or latches. It's the grand reveal!
usage_notes: Used for objects like doors, windows, books, boxes, etc. Not to be confused with 'bukas' (tomorrow).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Biglang **bumukas** ang pinto dahil sa malakas na hangin.","translation":"The door suddenly **opened** because of the strong wind."},{"sentence":"**Bumukas** ang isipan niya sa mga bagong ideya.","translation":"His mind **opened** to new ideas."}]

meaning_filipino: Isinasagawa o nangyayari nang paunti-unti, sa mga magkakahiwalay na bahagi o yugto, at hindi nang sabayan.
etymology: Pag-uulit ng salitang-ugat na 'yugto' (stage, act, phase).
original_explanation: The perfect description for your never-ending thesis or that project from your boss that keeps getting new requirements. It means doing something "in phases" or "in episodes." Also describes how you pay for your Shopee/Lazada "SpayLater" purchases: yugtu-yugto.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit upang ilarawan ang isang proseso, pagbabayad, o serye ng mga kaganapan. Maaari ring maging pang-uri.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagbabayad para sa bahay at lupa ay maaaring gawin nang **yugtu-yugto**.","translation":"The payment for the house and lot can be done **in stages**."},{"sentence":"Ang teleserye ay may **yugtu-yugtong** paglalabas ng mga sikreto ng pamilya.","translation":"The soap opera has an **episodic** revelation of the family's secrets."}]

translation: to flicker; to blink repeatedly; to twinkle
meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit at mabilis na pagbukas at pagsara ng mga mata, o ang paiba-ibang liwanag na parang aandap-andap.
original_explanation: Eto 'yung ilaw ng Christmas lights na sira-sira na, 'yung "on-again, off-again" ang relationship. Pwede ring 'yung mata mo 'pag napuwing ka or 'pag inaantok ka na sa meeting pero pilit mong pinipigilan. It's the blinking, twinkling, flickering effect of lights or eyes.
usage_notes: The repetition of the root 'kisap' emphasizes the continuous or repetitive nature of the action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga bituin ay **kumikisap-kisap** sa madilim na kalangitan.","translation":"The stars are **twinkling** in the dark sky."},{"sentence":"**Kumikisap-kisap** ang ilaw sa poste, mukhang malapit nang mapundi.","translation":"The light on the post is **flickering**, it looks like it's about to burn out."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa pagod, **kumikisap-kisap** na ang kanyang mga mata.","translation":"Because of fatigue, his eyes are **blinking repeatedly**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ilagay ang sarili o isang bagay sa isang lugar kung saan hindi ito makikita o matatagpuan; ilihim.
original_explanation: The national sport of people with 'utang'. Also, what you do when your toxic kamag-anak visits. It's the main verb in the game 'taguan'. "Sige, magtago ka na, bibilang ako hanggang sampu!" Can be about hiding yourself, an object, or feelings (yung tinatago mong feelings para sa kanya).
usage_notes: Can refer to hiding oneself, an object, or concealing information/emotions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **magtago** sa ilalim ng kama.","translation":"He decided to **hide** under the bed."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **magtago** ng sikreto sa isang maliit na bayan.","translation":"It's hard to **hide** a secret in a small town."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang ulam o pagkain na iniluto sa paraan ng paggisa.
original_explanation: This is the 'finished product' version of gisa. 'Yung ampalaya na ayaw mo, pero naging 'Ampalaya con Carne' na. Basically, any food that went through the 'bawang-sibuyas-kamatis' ritual. The '-ado' suffix is your clue that it's 'been done'.
usage_notes: Often used as a descriptor in dish names, like 'Munggo Gisado'. Can also function as a noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito ko ang munggong **gisado** tuwing Biyernes.","translation":"Sautéed mung beans are my favorite every Friday."},{"sentence":"Mas masarap ang repolyo kung **gisado** sa hipon.","translation":"Cabbage is more delicious if **sautéed** with shrimp."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkawala o paglisan nang biglaan at walang bakas; pagtatakip ng isang bagay sa kalawakan sa isa pa, tulad ng sa buwan o araw.
etymology: From Sanskrit 'rāhu', a mythological demon believed to swallow the sun or moon, causing eclipses.
original_explanation: Like your salary on the 16th of the month—it just disappears. One minute it's there, the next, 'naglaho na.' It's also what happens when your 'ka-talking stage' suddenly ghosts you. The original term, however, refers to an eclipse.
usage_notes: The verb form 'maglaho' (to vanish) is more common in everyday speech. As a noun, 'laho' often specifically refers to an eclipse.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinanood namin ang **laho** ng buwan kagabi.","translation":"We watched the lunar **eclipse** last night."},{"sentence":"Ang mabilis na pag-**laho** ng kanyang alaala ay nakakabahala.","translation":"The rapid **disappearance** of his memory is concerning."}]

translation: to be startled; to be shocked and disturbed
meaning_filipino: Biglaang pagkagulat o pagkabahala na nagdudulot ng pagkaantala sa ginagawa o pag-iisip; malalim na pagkaistorbo.
etymology: From ma- (accidental verb prefix) + a possible root bulwag (commotion, disturbance). Often associated with bulwagan (main hall) as a place of gathering and potential commotion.
original_explanation: Level up ito ng "mabulahaw." Hindi lang ingay. Ito 'yung gulat na may kasamang panic. Tipong nanonood ka ng horror movie, tahimik, tapos biglang may sumigaw sa likod mo. O 'yung nakita mo 'yung bill ng credit card mo pagkatapos ng 12.12 sale. Ayun, na-mabulwagan ka sa katotohanan.
usage_notes: Stronger than `magulat` or `maistorbo`. Implies a deeper sense of shock or alarm that disrupts one's composure.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay na-**mabulwagan** nang malaman niyang nasusunog ang kalapit na bahay.","translation":"He was **shocked and disturbed** when he found out the neighboring house was on fire."},{"sentence":"Huwag kayong mag-ingay, baka **mabulwagan** ang sanggol na natutulog.","translation":"Don't make noise, you might **startle** the sleeping baby."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang butas o siwang kung saan hindi sinasadyang nakakalabas ang likido o gas; ang pagkalat o paglabas ng kumpidensyal na impormasyon.
original_explanation: 'Yung butas sa bubong na tuwing umuulan lang naaalala. O 'yung chismis na sinabi mo sa "best friend" mo na may "promise, sa'tin lang 'to," pero kinabukasan alam na ng buong barangay. Information leak is the new marites.
usage_notes: Ginagamit para sa parehong pisikal na butas (sa tubo, bubong) at sa paglabas ng impormasyon o sikreto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **leak** sa tubo ng tubig kaya malaki ang bill namin.","translation":"There's a **leak** in the water pipe, that's why our bill is high."},{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng data **leak** ang sikat na social media app at nalantad ang impormasyon ng mga user.","translation":"The popular social media app had a data **leak** and the users' information was exposed."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing laganap o sabog ang isang bagay sa isang lugar. Ipamahagi sa maraming tao.
original_explanation: Ito yung ginagawa ng kapitbahay mong chismosa sa mga sikreto mo. Or yung ginagawa mo sa peanut butter sa pandesal. Or worse, yung pag-share ng fake news sa social media. "Spread the love, not the virus... or the chismis."
usage_notes: Often used for spreading news, gossip, items, or making a mess.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ikalat** mo na ang balita na walang pasok bukas.","translation":"**Spread** the news that there are no classes tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ikalat** ang mga laruan mo sa sahig.","translation":"Don't **scatter** your toys on the floor."}]

translation: act of doing something in someone's absence
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paggawa ng isang bagay habang wala ang taong karaniwang gumagawa nito, ang may-ari, o ang bantay.
original_explanation: This is the classic telenovela plot. The husband is away on a business trip, and the 'other woman' shows up at the house. That's `pagsalisi`. It's also when you wait for your boss to go on lunch break before you start watching Netflix at your desk. It's all about timing and absence. Sneaky, sneaky.
usage_notes: Often has a negative or clandestine connotation, as in taking advantage of someone's absence. The term 'Salisi Gang' refers to thieves who operate this way in restaurants and public places.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Biktima sila ng **pagsalisi** ng mga magnanakaw habang sila'y nasa bakasyon.","translation":"They were victims of **thieves acting in their absence** while they were on vacation."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagsalisi** sa pwesto ng hepe ay pinagplanuhan nang maigi.","translation":"The **act of taking over** the chief's position (while he was vulnerable or away) was well-planned."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manipis at pahilis na hiwa, karaniwan sa isda o karne.
original_explanation: Ito yung hiwa na parang 'slash' (/). Hindi basta-basta hiwa, may angle. Think of how they slice the fish for sinigang or paksiw—that's hilis. It's the kind of cut that shows you know your way around a palengke kitchen. It's a cut with technique.
usage_notes: Primarily used in a culinary context, especially for fish.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng isang **hilis** ng tanigue para sa hapunan.","translation":"I bought a **slice** of Spanish mackerel for dinner."},{"sentence":"Mas maganda ang pagkaluto kapag pahilis ang **hilis** ng isda.","translation":"The cooking is better when the **slice** of the fish is slanted."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na nilagyan o minarkahan ng isang maliit na bandera o pananda.
etymology: From Spanish 'bandera' + '-ado' suffix, meaning 'adorned with flags' or 'flagged'.
original_explanation: This is what your project manager does to your task on Jira or Asana—they put a little red flag on it, meaning "URGENT! GAWIN MO NA 'TO!" In old taxis, it's when the meter is down ('flagged down'). In construction, it's that post with a red cloth tied to it to warn you, "Huwag kang dumaan dito, may butas." Basically, it means something is marked for attention.
usage_notes: Often used in contexts like racing, project management (as a borrowed concept), or marking locations. Can also refer to a taxi whose meter is running.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Banderado** na ang taxi kaya alam naming may sakay na.","translation":"The taxi was already **flagged** (i.e., the meter was running), so we knew it was already occupied."},{"sentence":"Lahat ng mga item na may depekto ay **banderado** ng pulang sticker.","translation":"All defective items are **marked** with a red sticker."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kulisap na kamag-anak ng paruparo, karaniwang aktibo sa gabi at naaakit sa liwanag. Ang mga uod nito ay minsan sumisira sa mga damit na gawa sa lana.
original_explanation: The goth cousin of the butterfly. While butterflies are out during the day being all pretty and colorful, the polilya is the creature of the night, frantically headbanging against your lightbulb for no apparent reason. They're harmless but annoying, and seeing one in your closet is a bad sign—it means your favorite sweater might soon have more holes than a slice of Swiss cheese.
usage_notes: Refers to the insect.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May isang malaking **polilya** na pumasok sa bintana at paikot-ikot sa ilaw.","translation":"A big **moth** entered through the window and is circling the light."},{"sentence":"Sinira ng **polilya** ang mga lumang damit sa aparador.","translation":"The **moths** destroyed the old clothes in the closet."}]

translation: to put into a box; to box up
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay o pagsisilid ng mga bagay sa loob ng isang kahon.
original_explanation: It's that "lipat-bahay" or "spring cleaning" energy. You're trying to fit your whole life into cardboard boxes, playing a real-life game of Tetris with your stuff. "Paano ko ba ito ima-magkahon?" you ask, staring at a giant teddy bear and a tiny box.
usage_notes: A straightforward verb for the action of boxing items for storage or transport.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **magkahon** ng mga lumang damit para sa donasyon.","translation":"Help me **box up** the old clothes for donation."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magkahon** ng lahat ng gamit bago dumating ang movers.","translation":"We need to **put everything in boxes** before the movers arrive."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan o aparato na awtomatikong naglalabas ng tiyak na dami ng isang bagay tulad ng tubig, sabon, o tiket.
original_explanation: That office water cooler where all the chismis happens. Or the alcohol dispenser at the mall entrance that everyone has to use. It's any machine that gives you something when you push a button or wave your hand, saving you from the effort of... pouring.
usage_notes: A direct loanword from English, pronounced in a Filipino way.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha ka ng malamig na tubig sa **dispenser**.","translation":"Get some cold water from the **dispenser**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang-utos na pinaikling anyo ng "halika," na nangangahulugang "lumapit dito."
etymology: Shortened from 'halika', which is from 'hali ka rito' (come here).
original_explanation: The one-word command your lola uses when she wants to give you money (or a pinch on the side). It's the shorter, more urgent, and more familiar version of 'halika.' '**Hali** ka, may ibibigay ako sa'yo.'
usage_notes: This is colloquial and used in informal speech, often in an imperative or commanding tone. It is almost always followed by 'ka'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hali** ka, anak, at may sasabihin si Inay.","translation":"**Come here**, child, Mom has something to say."},{"sentence":"'**Hali**!' sigaw niya mula sa kabilang kwarto.","translation":"'**Come here**!' he shouted from the other room."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng panalangin sa simbahan na binubuo ng mga serye ng kahilingan na binibigkas ng pari o lider, at tinutugon naman ng mga tao.
original_explanation: In church, it's a prayer. In real life, it's the long, repetitive list of complaints your Tita makes at every family gathering. "Ang mahal ng bilihin, ang traffic, ang init ng panahon, ang sakit ng likod ko..." That's a modern-day 'litania'. It's a list so long and repetitive, it feels like a prayer for patience.
usage_notes: Primarily used in a religious context, but can be used hyperbolically for any long, tedious list of items or complaints.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bahagi ng prusisyon ang pagdarasal ng **litania**.","translation":"Praying the **litany** is part of the procession."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula na naman siya sa kanyang **litania** ng mga reklamo.","translation":"He started with his **litany** of complaints again."}]

meaning_filipino: Inilalarawan ang isang tao, bagay, o tanawin na napakaganda, na tila isang perpektong kuha sa isang litrato o isang obra maestra.
original_explanation: This is how you describe your crush when they're just staring into space, looking effortlessly perfect. 'OMG, look at him, **parang larawan**!' Also used for IG-worthy spots in Batanes or El Nido. So beautiful it looks fake.
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang papuri para sa kagandahan ng isang tao o sa isang magandang tanawin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda niya sa suot niyang iyon, **parang larawan**.","translation":"She is so beautiful in that outfit, **like a picture**."},{"sentence":"Ang tanawin mula sa tuktok ng bundok ay **parang larawan**.","translation":"The view from the top of the mountain is **picturesque**."}]

meaning_filipino: Mapasò o masaktan dahil sa pagkakabuhos o pagkakadampi ng mainit na likido, tulad ng tubig o mantika.
original_explanation: That 'Aray!' moment when the hot ramen broth splashes on your hand. Or when you're making instant coffee and the hot water decides to attack you. It's the minor but very real pain from hot liquids.
usage_notes: This is a passive verb form. The actor-focus form is 'magbanli' (to scald something). The object that gets scalded is the subject of the sentence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa kumukulong sopas para hindi ka **mabanlian**.","translation":"Be careful with the boiling soup so you don't **get scalded**."},{"sentence":"Siya ay **nabanlian** ng mantika habang nagpiprito ng isda.","translation":"She **was scalded** by oil while frying fish."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing alipin ang isang tao; agawan ng kalayaan at piliting maglingkod sa ilalim ng kontrol ng iba.
original_explanation: This is what your toxic boss does to you with 'urgent' tasks at 5:01 PM on a Friday. They **alipinin** you with the promise of 'exposure' and a pizza party.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binalak ng mga mananakop na **alipinin** ang mga katutubo.","translation":"The colonizers planned to **enslave** the natives."}]

translation: to defile; to desecrate; to make filthy
meaning_filipino: Dungisan o lapastanganin ang isang bagay, lugar, o konsepto na itinuturing na dalisay, banal, o malinis.
original_explanation: This is a heavy word. It's not just about making something dirty, like spilling coffee on a white shirt. It's about violating something sacred. Think of someone vandalizing a church, spreading fake news to ruin a person's reputation, or turning a beautiful park into a dumpsite. It’s the act of taking something pure and making it profane.
usage_notes: Carries a strong moral or spiritual connotation of impurity and violation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **magsalaula** sa pangalan ng pamilya ay isang malaking kasalanan.","translation":"To **defile** the family name is a great sin."},{"sentence":"Layunin ng mga mananakop na **magsalaula** sa aming kultura.","translation":"The invaders' goal was to **desecrate** our culture."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kabuuan ng daigdig, kasama ang lahat ng nilalang at bagay dito; ang sansinukob.
original_explanation: When you're feeling dramatic and say "My whole world is falling apart!"—that's your 'sangkalibutan'. It's more poetic than 'buong mundo'. It's the universe, the cosmos, everything under the sun and moon. The term beauty queens use when they talk about world peace.
usage_notes: Often used in literary, poetic, or formal contexts. Can also mean 'the whole of humanity'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawa'y maghari ang kapayapaan sa buong **sangkalibutan**.","translation":"May peace reign over the **whole world**."}]

meaning_filipino: Inilalarawan ang isang bagay na may sapat na suporta, patunay, o batayan.
original_explanation: Your argument in a debate when you actually have facts and not just "feelings." It's when your claim is backed up by receipts, screenshots, and a 10-page Google Docs file. Hindi 'to basta chismis, ito ay sustentado!
usage_notes: Can refer to an argument being factually supported or, less commonly, a person being financially supported.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kaniyang mga paratang ay hindi **sustentado** ng matibay na ebidensya.","translation":"His accusations are not **substantiated** by strong evidence."},{"sentence":"Dapat **sustentado** ang iyong opinyon para pakinggan ka ng mga tao.","translation":"Your opinion must be **supported** (by facts) for people to listen to you."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang makarinig o ang estado ng pagiging naririnig ng isang tunog.
original_explanation: Yung state na kahit pabulong lang sinabi ng katabi mo yung chismis, clear as day pa rin sa'yo. Your Marites senses are tingling and your hearing is at 100%. "Rinig ko" is the more active form, "dinig ko" is more about the state of being heard.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'rinig'. The d/r rule often applies depending on the preceding word. 'Rinig' is common in active constructions ("Narinig ko"), while 'dinig' is common in passive or descriptive ones ("Dinig na dinig ang sigaw niya").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dinig** mo ba ang sinabi niya?","translation":"Did you **hear** what he said?"},{"sentence":"Mula sa malayo, **dinig** ko ang kulog.","translation":"From afar, I could **hear** the thunder."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagbibigay ng serbisyo o paglilingkod; ang akto ng pagbibigay ng serbisyo.
original_explanation: This is the formal term for 'service.' You'll see it everywhere: 'Lingkod Bayan' for public servants, 'Paglilingkod' on government office signs. It's like being a Customer Service Rep, but for the country, your boss, or your God. High-level 'utusan'.
usage_notes: Ang 'lingkod' bilang pangngalan ay nangangahulugang 'servant' o 'one who serves'. Ang pandiwang 'maglingkod' ay nangangahulugang 'to serve'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang tapat na **lingkod** ng bayan ang yumaong senador.","translation":"The late senator was a faithful **servant** of the people."},{"sentence":"Ang aming tanggapan ay laging bukas para mag**lingkod** sa inyo.","translation":"Our office is always open to **serve** you."}]

translation: to be divided, to be split
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkilos ng paghihiwalay sa dalawa o higit pang bahagi.
original_explanation: When the pizza arrives and you have to split it with your siblings. 'Yung sahod mo na pagdating pa lang, hati-hati na sa mga bayarin. That's `mahati`.
usage_notes: Can be used for physical objects, abstract concepts (like time), or groups of people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang cake ay **mahati** sa walong piraso.","translation":"The cake will **be divided** into eight pieces."},{"sentence":"Ayaw kong **mahati** ang atensyon mo sa iba.","translation":"I don't want your attention to **be divided** among others."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang itinakdang plano, nais, o desisyon ng Maykapal para sa sangkatauhan o sa isang indibidwal.
etymology: From `ka-` + `loob` + `-an`, meaning "inner-ness" or "will," combined with `ng Diyos` (of God).
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "Bahala na si Batman" but with more reverence. When you've done everything you can—submitted the reports, prayed to all the saints, and even lit a candle—and things still don't go your way, you sigh and say, "kalooban ng Diyos." It's the universe's way of saying, "Plot twist!"
usage_notes: A common phrase used to express acceptance of a situation believed to be part of a divine plan, often in times of hardship, uncertainty, or unexpected outcomes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tanggapin na lang natin ang nangyari, marahil ito ay **kalooban ng Diyos**.","translation":"Let's just accept what happened, perhaps this is **God's will**."},{"sentence":"Mahirap man, kailangan nating magtiwala sa **kalooban ng Diyos**.","translation":"Even if it's difficult, we need to trust in **God's will**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapahayag ng pagtanggi, hindi pagkagusto, o hindi pagsang-ayon sa isang bagay sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: That moment when your friend offers to set you up on a blind date and your gut feeling screams no. "Tingin ko aayaw ako diyan." Also, a kid's default reaction to vegetables.
usage_notes: Future tense of 'ayaw'. It's a definitive statement of future refusal. Often used in sentences expressing a choice or condition.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sigurado akong **aayaw** siya sa plano mo.","translation":"I'm sure he/she **will refuse** your plan."},{"sentence":"Kahit anong pilit mo, **aayaw** at **aayaw** pa rin ako.","translation":"No matter how much you insist, I **will** still **refuse**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagdiin o pagpisil sa isang bagay upang maalis ang likido o katas nito, o upang mabago ang anyo nito.
original_explanation: 'Yan 'yung ginagawa mo sa calamansi para sa toyo, or sa damit na basâ bago isampay. But in the hugot world, **piga** is what your heart feels like after a rough week, what your brain feels like after a major exam, or what your wallet feels like after the 15th of the month. "Pigang-piga na ako, bes!"
usage_notes: Ito ay isang salitang-ugat. Madalas gamitin sa anyong pandiwa (pigain, pumiga, piniga). Ang anyong pangngalan ay tumutukoy sa mismong kilos.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **piga** lang sa damit ay tumulo na agad ang maraming tubig.","translation":"Just one **wring** of the clothes and a lot of water immediately dripped out."},{"sentence":"Ang lakas ng **piga** niya sa kamay ko.","translation":"His **squeeze** on my hand was so strong."}]

meaning_filipino: Banlawan o hugasan nang bahagya sa tubig upang alisin ang sabon, dumi, o iba pang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the final boss of doing the dishes or laundry. After scrubbing with soap (magsabon), you have to 'mag-anglaw' to get all the suds out. If you don't do it properly, your plate tastes like Joy dishwashing liquid, or your shirt feels stiff. It's the step everyone rushes but is super important.
usage_notes: Synonymous with 'magbanlaw'. 'Magbanlaw' is far more common in modern spoken Tagalog. 'Mag-anglaw' might be considered slightly more formal or regional.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos sabunin ang mga plato, kailangan mo itong **mag-anglaw** nang mabuti.","translation":"After soaping the plates, you need **to rinse** them well."},{"sentence":"Nag-**anglaw** na ako ng mga damit bago isampay.","translation":"I already **rinsed** the clothes before hanging them to dry."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bilog na sitrus na prutas na may makapal, kulay kahel na balat at maasim-asim na matamis na laman.
original_explanation: Ito yung prutas na laging kasama sa fruit salad tuwing Pasko at New Year. Yung kamag-anak ng dalandan at ponkan. Masarap na source ng Vitamin C para 'di ka sipunin after magpa-ulan for dramatic effect.
usage_notes: Ang katumbas sa Tagalog ay "dalandan" o "kahel", bagaman malawakang tinatanggap at ginagamit ang "orange".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong kumain ng **orange** pagkatapos ng tanghalian.","translation":"I want to eat an **orange** after lunch."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghinto sa pag-iyak o pagtangis.
original_explanation: This is what your mom tells you after a good cry over a breakup or a failed exam. 'Tahan na.' When you finally stop sobbing and catch your breath, you have **tumahan**. It's the calm after the emotional storm.
usage_notes: This is the completed aspect (past tense). Infinitive: tumahan, Progressive: tumatahan, Contemplative: tatahan. Often used in the command form 'Tahan na.' which means 'Stop crying now.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumahan** din ang bata matapos bigyan ng kendi.","translation":"The child finally **stopped crying** after being given candy."},{"sentence":"Nang makita niya ang kanyang ina, agad siyang **tumahan**.","translation":"When she saw her mother, she immediately **stopped crying**."}]

translation: to be able to join; to become a member
meaning_filipino: Ang maging bahagi o miyembro ng isang grupo, organisasyon, o samahan.
original_explanation: This is your official entry into the club. Whether it's joining the school dance troupe, getting accepted into a 'Home Buddies' Facebook group, or signing up for a new gym membership. 'Paano ba makasapi sa inyong kooperatiba?'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming kabataan ang nagnanais **makasapi** sa sikat na banda.","translation":"Many youths want **to be able to join** the popular band."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong punan ang pormularyo para **makasapi** sa aming organisasyon.","translation":"You need to fill out the form to **become a member** of our organization."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kasamang naninirahan sa iisang bahay.
original_explanation: Your roommate who either steals your food from the ref or becomes your lifelong best friend. They're the one you split the Meralco bill with. Whether it's a condo-sharing situation in BGC or a boarding house near your university, your kabahay knows your "pambahay" look and your late-night instant noodle habits.
usage_notes: Not to be confused with 'kasambahay' (household help).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May bago akong **kabahay** na mula pa sa Cebu.","translation":"I have a new **housemate** who is from Cebu."},{"sentence":"Mahirap maghanap ng **kabahay** na malinis sa gamit.","translation":"It's hard to find a **housemate** who is tidy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang utos o pakiusap na lagyan ng hinang ang isang partikular na bagay o lugar.
original_explanation: Yung command form. Kapag inutusan ka ng tatay mo na ayusin na yung sirang gate. "Hoy, **hinangan** mo na 'yan!" Parang sa office, "Paki-finalize na 'yan!"
usage_notes: This is an imperative or infinitive form telling someone *where* or *on what* to weld. It is a locative-focus verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyong **hinangan** ang nasirang bahagi ng rehas.","translation":"Please **weld** the broken part of the railing."},{"sentence":"Sabi ng mekaniko, kailangang **hinangan** ang chassis.","translation":"The mechanic said the chassis needs to **be welded**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gawain, bagay, o larangan na partikular na gusto o pinagtutuunan ng pansin bilang isang libangan.
etymology: From 'hilig' (inclination, fondness, hobby). The 'kina-hi-' + '-an' form denotes the object of the inclination.
original_explanation: This is your hobby, your passion project, your 'thing.' It's what you binge-watch on Netflix, the video game you play until 3 AM, or your sudden urge to become a plantito/plantita. It's that specific interest that makes your friends go, 'Ah, oo, mahilig ka nga pala diyan.'
usage_notes: Similar to 'kinagigiliwan' but often points more towards a hobby or active interest rather than just passive delight. Can also function as a verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagbabasa ng mga nobela ang kanyang **kinahihiligan**.","translation":"Reading novels is her **hobby**."},{"sentence":"Ano ba ang **kinahihiligan** mong gawin sa iyong libreng oras?","translation":"What **are you interested in** doing during your free time?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng tela na isinasabit sa balikat o ipinapatong sa ulo bilang palamuti o proteksyon.
original_explanation: The original 'it-girl' accessory, way before influencers. This is the shawl your lola wears to church, or what Maria Clara gracefully drapes over her shoulder. Today, it's what you grab when the office AC is on arctic blast mode or when you want to add a touch of class to your outfit. The alampay is both a fashion statement and a practical solution for a sudden chill.
usage_notes: Often associated with traditional Filipino attire like the baro't saya, where it is also called a 'pañuelo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **alampay** ay bahagi ng tradisyonal na kasuotang pambabae sa Pilipinas.","translation":"The **shawl** is part of the traditional women's attire in the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Nagsuot siya ng magandang **alampay** upang takpan ang kanyang mga balikat sa simbahan.","translation":"She wore a beautiful **shawl** to cover her shoulders at church."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbibiro, pag-asar, o pag-aglahi sa isang tao sa paraang mapanukso o mapang-inis.
original_explanation: This is the act of teasing someone, but with a bit more bite than "panunukso." It's the kind of teasing your "frenemy" does. 'Yung birong "uy, tumataba ka," pero may kasamang ngiting aso. It's the official sport in family reunions, usually targeting your love life or career choices.
usage_notes: Implies a slightly more malicious or mocking tone than "tukso".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itigil mo na ang iyong **panunudyo** sa kanya.","translation":"Stop your **teasing** of him."},{"sentence":"Hindi na siya natutuwa sa palagiang **panunudyo** ng kanyang mga kaibigan.","translation":"He is no longer amused by the constant **mockery** from his friends."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang siyentipikong pag-aaral ng pag-iisip, damdamin, at pag-uugali ng tao at hayop.
original_explanation: Ito yung course sa college na kinukuha ng mga gustong intindihin kung bakit sila ganun, tapos malalaman nilang mas kailangan pala nilang intindihin kung bakit ganun yung ibang tao. The science of 'why are you like that?'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang naitulong ng **psikolohia** sa pag-unawa sa kalusugang pangkaisipan.","translation":"**Psychology** has greatly helped in understanding mental health."}]

translation: to separate; to cause to be distant
meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang paghiwalayin o pag-ibahin ng landas ang dalawa o higit pang tao o bagay upang magkaroon ng distansya sa pagitan nila.
original_explanation: The kontrabida's favorite verb in every teleserye. It's the act of actively trying to break a couple up. 'Gagawin ko ang lahat, paglayuin lang sila!' Also, what you do with your pets when they start fighting over food.
usage_notes: This is a causative verb. The subject of the verb is the one causing the separation, not the ones being separated.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan silang **paglayuin** ng kanilang mga magulang ngunit mas lalo lang tumibay ang kanilang pagmamahalan.","translation":"Their parents tried **to separate** them, but their love only grew stronger."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **paglayuin** ang mga kemikal na ito upang maiwasan ang pagsabog.","translation":"We need **to separate** these chemicals to avoid an explosion."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o kalagayan ng pagkahulog o pagkatanggal ng mga bagay tulad ng dahon, buhok, o talulot ng bulaklak, kadalasan ay maramihan.
etymology: From pagka- (state/process of) + lagas (to fall off).
original_explanation: The reason why your bathroom drain is always clogged. It's what happens to trees in autumn (if we had one). It can also describe your G-Cash balance after a 12.12 sale—ubos, 'nalagas lahat'. It's a gradual but definite falling away, a sign that something is ending or changing.
usage_notes: Commonly used for hair loss and leaves falling from a tree. Can be used metaphorically for numbers or members of a group dwindling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nababahala siya sa sobrang **pagkalagas** ng kanyang buhok.","translation":"She is worried about the excessive **falling** of her hair."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkalagas** ng mga dahon ay hudyat ng pagbabago ng panahon.","translation":"The **falling** of leaves is a sign of the changing season."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nakikinig, lalo na sa isang programa sa radyo, podcast, o talumpati.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'taga-' (tagagawa) at pandiwang 'pakinig' (to listen intently).
original_explanation: The person on the other end of the speakers. Sila yung audience ng paborito mong DJ sa radyo, ng podcast na pinapakinggan mo habang nagco-commute, or simply your friend who's all ears sa mga hugot at rants mo sa buhay. Sila ang dahilan kung bakit may 'Hello sa lahat ng mga tagapakinig!'
usage_notes: Pinakakaraniwang ginagamit para sa mga tagasubaybay ng audio-based media tulad ng radyo at podcast.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang maligayang bati sa lahat ng ating mga **tagapakinig**!","translation":"A happy greeting to all of our **listeners**!"},{"sentence":"Maraming sulat ang natanggap ng istasyon mula sa kanilang tapat na **tagapakinig**.","translation":"The station received many letters from their loyal **listeners**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bahagi ng makina na gumagalaw pabalik-balik sa loob ng isang silindro dahil sa presyon ng likido o gas.
original_explanation: Not a gun! This is the 'puso' of an engine. It's the part that goes up and down, up and down, turning fuel into 'galaw' (motion). If your car is 'umubo' (sputtering), baka may problema sa pistol. It's the hardworking BPO agent of your car's engine, doing the same repetitive task over and over to make everything work.
usage_notes: Madalas mapagkamalang "pistola" (gun). Ang bigkas ay may diin sa ikalawang pantig (pis-TOL), hindi tulad ng Ingles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang palitan ang **pistol** ng makina ng motor.","translation":"The **piston** of the motorcycle's engine needs to be replaced."}]

translation: to be swallowed, to be engulfed
meaning_filipino: Mailunok o mapunta sa loob ng lalamunan; masakop o matabunan nang buo ng isang malaking bagay, tulad ng alon o problema.
original_explanation: Literally, this is what you do with food or medicine. But figuratively, it's what happens when you're drowning in debt, swamped with work, or overwhelmed by your feelings for your "situationship". "Nalululon ako sa trabaho" is the BPO agent's mantra during peak season. You're being engulfed by something much bigger than you.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for swallowing or figuratively for being overwhelmed by a situation, system, or emotion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka at baka **malulon** mo ang buto ng isda.","translation":"Be careful or you might **swallow** the fish bone."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang padala sa problema, baka **malulon** ka ng sistema.","translation":"Don't give in to the problem, you might get **engulfed** by the system."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtitiwala o pag-asa sa isang bagay bilang batayan, pundasyon, o suporta.
etymology: From `pag-` (verbal noun prefix) + `salig` (based on, founded on).
original_explanation: This is your relationship with your morning coffee. Your entire day's success is based on it. It’s the act of putting your trust in something as your foundation. Like how your entire argument in a debate is based on one Wikipedia article you skimmed five minutes before. It's the 'I'm basing this on...' moment.
usage_notes: Often used in formal or legal contexts, e.g., 'pagsalig sa batas' (basing on the law).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang desisyon ay nagpapakita ng **pagsalig** sa mga prinsipyo ng katarungan.","translation":"His decision shows **reliance** on the principles of justice."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **pagsalig** sa datos sa paggawa ng isang matibay na pananaliksik.","translation":"The **act of basing on** data is important in creating a strong research."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagpapangkat-pangkat ng mga bagay, tao, o ideya batay sa kanilang mga katangian o uri.
original_explanation: Basically what your brain does when you see a group of people and think, 'Ah, ito yung mga Titos and Titas of Manila, ito naman mga K-Pop fans.' It's sorting things into folders, but for real life. Also, what you do to your laundry: whites, colors, delicates.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tungkulin ng librarian na **mag-uri** ng mga bagong dating na aklat.","translation":"It is the librarian's duty to **classify** the newly arrived books."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **mag-uri** ng tao batay lamang sa panlabas na anyo.","translation":"It's difficult to **categorize** people based only on their external appearance."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong katutubo o mamamayan ng Italya; tumutukoy sa wika, kultura, o anumang bagay na nagmula sa Italya.
original_explanation: Pizza, pasta, Ferrari, Gucci, and that charming accent. When you say something is 'Italyano,' you're talking about the country known for its amazing food, fashion, and history. The feminine form is 'Italyana.'
usage_notes: Can be a noun for a person ('Ang Italyano') or an adjective for a thing ('pagkaing Italyano').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bago naming kapitbahay ay isang **Italyano** na mahusay magluto ng spaghetti.","translation":"Our new neighbor is an **Italian** who cooks spaghetti well."},{"sentence":"Bumili siya ng sapatos na gawang-**Italyano**.","translation":"He bought **Italian**-made shoes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan na may utong na artipisyal, na ibinibigay sa sanggol upang sipsipin para sa pagpapakalma.
etymology: From Spanish 'chupón' (pacifier, something to suck on), from the verb 'chupar' (to suck).
original_explanation: The baby's 'mute button'. It's that magical object parents pray the baby will accept, providing a few precious moments of peace and quiet. Also known as the thing that always falls on the floor at the worst possible moment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iyak nang iyak ang sanggol dahil nawawala ang kanyang **tsupon**.","translation":"The baby was crying because his **pacifier** was missing."},{"sentence":"Pakuluan mo muna ang **tsupon** bago ibigay sa bata.","translation":"Boil the **pacifier** first before giving it to the child."}]

meaning_filipino: Tulusan o tarakan ng isang matulis na bagay, tulad ng kutsilyo.
original_explanation: This is a very direct and violent word. It's what villains do in action movies. But in a less dramatic, everyday context, it's what you do to your straw when you sumaksak it into your milk tea cup's seal. Or when you're trying to plug something into a crowded extension cord. It's the act of forcefully piercing something.
usage_notes: A violent action, but can be used hyperbolically or for mundane actions like plugging in a device. This is the completed action (past tense) form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May nagtangkang **sumaksak** sa kanya ngunit nakailag siya.","translation":"Someone tried to **stab** him but he was able to dodge."},{"sentence":"**Sumaksak** siya ng tinidor sa karne para tingnan kung luto na.","translation":"He **pierced** the meat with a fork to see if it was cooked."}]

meaning_filipino: Magsagawa ng pagsusuri o pagsubok sa isang tao o bagay upang alamin ang kaalaman, kalagayan, o katangian nito.
original_explanation: What a doctor does to you during a check-up. Also, what your potential mother-in-law does to you the first time you meet, but with more piercing questions and less medical equipment. "Para akong in-iksamin ng nanay niya from head to toe!"
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Iksaminin** natin ang pasyente upang malaman ang kanyang sakit.","translation":"Let's **examine** the patient to find out his illness."},{"sentence":"Plano ng guro na **iksaminin** ang mga mag-aaral sa pamamagitan ng isang oral recitation.","translation":"The teacher plans to **test** the students through an oral recitation."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyon na nangangahulugang 'walang biro,' 'totoo,' o 'seryoso,' na ginagamit upang bigyang-diin ang katotohanan ng isang pahayag.
etymology: From African-American Vernacular English (AAVE) slang 'no cap'.
original_explanation: Straight from Gen Z's dictionary, this is the 2020s version of 'pramis,' 'swear,' or 'seryoso.' You drop this when you want to make sure your friends know you're not joking about the latest chismis or that the 2-pc chicken you ordered is, in fact, life-changing. 'This unli-rice is the best, nocap.'
usage_notes: Primarily used by younger generations and online. It's a direct import from global internet culture used to add emphasis and assert truthfulness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng concert kagabi, **nocap**.","translation":"Last night's concert was amazing, **for real**."},{"sentence":"Siya na yata ang pinakamagaling na player sa team, **nocap**.","translation":"He might be the best player on the team, **no cap**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang anak o inakay ng manok o iba pang ibon.
original_explanation: A baby chicken. Also, an expression for something super easy. 'Sisiw lang 'yan!' is the Pinoy equivalent of 'That's a piece of cake!' It's what you say before an exam you didn't study for, only to regret it later.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for a chick or figuratively in the phrase 'sisiw lang' to mean something is very easy or trivial.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang cute ng mga bagong pisang **sisiw** sa bukid.","translation":"The newly hatched **chicks** on the farm are cute."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala sa exam, **sisiw** lang 'yan!","translation":"Don't worry about the exam, it's a **piece of cake**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi namamatay; walang hanggan ang buhay.
original_explanation: What you wish your phone's battery was. Also, that one tito who seems to survive every family drinking session without a hangover. In showbiz, it's what they call artists whose legacy lives on, like FPJ or Dolphy.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for mythical beings or figuratively for someone/something whose fame or influence lasts forever.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naniniwala sila na ang mga diyos at diyosa sa mitolohiya ay **imortal**.","translation":"They believe that the gods and goddesses in mythology are **immortal**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga akda ni Jose Rizal ay nagpapatunay na ang kanyang diwa ay **imortal**.","translation":"The works of Jose Rizal prove that his spirit is **immortal**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng lutuin, karaniwan ay isda, na pinirito at ibinuhos sa sarsang matamis at maasim na gawa sa suka, asukal, at mga gulay.
etymology: From Spanish 'escabeche', a method of marinating food in an acidic mixture.
original_explanation: This is the Filipino's answer to sweet and sour fish, but with more flair. It’s that brightly colored fish dish at the fiesta that looks super festive. The fish is fried to a crisp, then drowned (in a good way) in a tangy, sweet sauce with colorful veggies. It’s the perfect ‘pang-alis ng umay’ dish.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to the Filipino sweet and sour fish dish, typically using fish like tilapia or lapu-lapu.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito ng lolo ko ang **iskabetse** na luto ni lola.","translation":"My grandpa's favorite is the **escabeche** that my grandma cooks."},{"sentence":"Magluto tayo ng **iskabetse** para sa pananghalian.","translation":"Let's cook **escabeche** for lunch."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagtiyak o pagbibigay ng katiyakan na ang isang bagay ay magaganap, tama, o protektado.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "asegurar", na nangangahulugang "to secure" o "to insure".
original_explanation: Parang yung ginagawa mo sa kaibigan mong nag-o-overthink. You have to 'asegurahin' them na hindi sila pabigat at valid ang feelings nila. It's giving 'I got you, fam.' Also, yung pag-double check mo kung naka-lock ba ang pinto bago umalis.
usage_notes: Madalas ginagamit sa pormal na usapan o sulatin. Ang "siguraduhin" ay ang mas karaniwang katumbas nito sa pang-araw-araw na salita.
