usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **asegurahin** na sapat ang pondo para sa proyekto.","translation":"We need to **ensure** that the funds for the project are sufficient."},{"sentence":"**Asegurahin** mo na nakasara ang lahat ng bintana bago tayo umalis.","translation":"**Make sure** all the windows are closed before we leave."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang opisyal na dokumento na nagpapatunay ng legal na pagmamay-ari sa isang piraso ng lupa.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'proof of ownership.' This is the piece of paper that ends all 'sino ba talaga may-ari nito?' arguments. It's the holy grail for Filipino families, the subject of many teleserye plot twists, and the reason you have to deal with so much bureaucracy. Having the **titulo ng lupa** means it's officially, legally yours.
usage_notes: A specific legal term. Often shortened to just 'titulo' if the context is about property.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinago niya sa bangko ang orihinal na **titulo ng lupa**.","translation":"He kept the original **land title** in the bank."},{"sentence":"Mahirap ayusin ang gusot kapag nawala ang **titulo ng lupa**.","translation":"It's hard to fix the mess when the **land title** is lost."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang nakalalason at nakakaadik na alkaloid na matatagpuan sa tabako, na siyang pangunahing aktibong sangkap sa sigarilyo at vapes.
original_explanation: The main villain (or for some, the main character) in your cigarette or vape juice. It's the stuff that gives you the 'hit' and also the reason why it's so hard to quit. It's the 'Sana all' of addiction – present in almost all tobacco products. Your doctor warns you about it, your vape-loving friend can't live without it.
usage_notes: A scientific and health-related term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mataas ang lebel ng **nikotina** sa mga sigarilyo.","translation":"The level of **nicotine** in cigarettes is high."},{"sentence":"Ang **nikotina** ang dahilan kung bakit mahirap itigil ang paninigarilyo.","translation":"**Nicotine** is the reason why it is difficult to stop smoking."}]

translation: to lessen, to decrease, to subtract
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-alis ng isang bahagi mula sa kabuuan upang ito ay kumonti; magbawas o magtanggal.
original_explanation: What happens to your salary after taxes, SSS, PhilHealth, and Pag-IBIG. Also what you wish you could do to your body weight after the Noche Buena feast. It's the act of something becoming less, whether it's your money, your worries, or the pancit in the bilao.
usage_notes: Can be used for tangible things (money, food) and intangible things (pain, workload).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay **bumawas** na ang bigat ng trapiko sa EDSA.","translation":"I hope the heavy traffic on EDSA **lessens**."},{"sentence":"**Bumawas** ang laman ng wallet ko pagkatapos ng 12.12 sale.","translation":"The contents of my wallet **decreased** after the 12.12 sale."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong madaling makatulog o palaging inaantok.
original_explanation: Describes that one friend (or you) who can fall asleep anywhere: in the jeepney, during a meeting, while the movie is just starting. The human version of a sloth. Your spirit animal on a Monday morning.
usage_notes: A descriptive adjective for a person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong istorbohin si Lolo, **tulugin** talaga 'yan pagkatapos mananghalian.","translation":"Don't disturb Grandpa, he's really **prone to sleeping** after lunch."},{"sentence":"Kilala siyang **tulugin** sa klase kaya lagi siyang napapagalitan.","translation":"He's known for being a **sleepyhead** in class, that's why he always gets scolded."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging magkatabi, magkadikit, o magkasiping.
original_explanation: When you're sitting next to your crush in the jeepney and your shoulders touch. It's being physically close to someone or something. "Sana all siping."
usage_notes: Often used in the context of people sleeping or sitting next to each other. 'Magsiping' is the verb form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natulog silang **siping** sa iisang banig.","translation":"They slept **side-by-side** on a single mat."},{"sentence":"Ang bahay namin ay **siping** sa isang maliit na ilog.","translation":"Our house is **adjacent** to a small river."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang akronim para sa 'Fear of Missing Out'; ang pakiramdam ng pagkabalisa na maaaring mayroong isang masayang kaganapan o karanasan na nangyayari sa ibang lugar, na madalas na pinalalala ng nakikita sa social media.
etymology: Acronym for the English phrase 'Fear of Missing Out'.
original_explanation: The reason why you say 'yes' to that 10 PM gimmick even though you have a 7 AM shift. It's the anxiety you feel when you're at home in your pajamas, scrolling through your friends' IG stories of a party you were invited to but were too tamad to attend. FOMO is the tiny, nagging voice that whispers, 'Sila nagkakasiyahan, ikaw nakahiga lang.'
usage_notes: Used as a noun to describe the feeling. People can 'have FOMO' or 'feel FOMO'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Grabe ang **FOMO** ko kagabi, lahat sila nasa concert.","translation":"My **FOMO** was intense last night, everyone was at the concert."},{"sentence":"Pumunta ako sa party dahil sa **FOMO**, pero gusto ko na talagang umuwi.","translation":"I went to the party because of **FOMO**, but I really want to go home already."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pakiramdam ng biglaang sakit o di-komportableng kuryente sa ngipin, karaniwang sanhi ng malamig, mainit, o matamis na pagkain.
original_explanation: That "zing!" or "ouch!" you feel in your teeth when you bite into ice cream or drink something super cold. It's your teeth's way of saying, "Chill ka lang, bes!" It's the reason why sensitive toothpaste commercials are so relatable. The ultimate enemy of ice candy lovers.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to the sharp, temporary pain in teeth, often described as 'setting teeth on edge'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko maubos ang sorbetes dahil sa **pangingilo** ng ngipin ko.","translation":"I can't finish the ice cream because of my **tooth sensitivity**."},{"sentence":"May gamot ka ba para sa **pangingilo**?","translation":"Do you have any medicine for **sensitive teeth**?"}]

translation: to flatter, to sweet-talk, to cajole
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasabi ng mga papuri, kadalasa'y labis o hindi totoo, upang makuha ang gusto mula sa isang tao.
etymology: From Spanish 'bola' (ball), with the meaning evolving from 'playing with someone' to 'deceiving with flattery'.
original_explanation: The OG LinkedIn networking skill. It's when you compliment your boss's new haircut right before asking for a day off. Or when a suitor says, 'You're the most beautiful person I've ever seen.' Be careful, baka gusto ka lang 'mambola'. The person who does this is the 'mambobola'.
usage_notes: Implies using flattery to manipulate or deceive someone for personal gain.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong subukang **mambola**, alam ko na ang iyong mga taktika.","translation":"Don't try **to flatter** me, I already know your tactics."},{"sentence":"Magaling siyang **mambola** ng mga customer para makabenta.","translation":"He is good at **cajoling** customers in order to make a sale."}]

translation: to play truant; to skip class/work
meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang hindi pagpasok sa klase o trabaho nang walang paalam o sapat na dahilan.
original_explanation: The national sport of students who'd rather be at a computer shop playing Dota than listening to a lecture. In the corporate world, it's taking an "unauthorized leave" to go to the mall. It's when you say you're "on the way" but you're still in bed.
usage_notes: Almost always has a negative connotation of irresponsibility.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magbulakbol** kung ayaw mong bumagsak sa pagsusulit.","translation":"Don't **play truant** if you don't want to fail the exam."},{"sentence":"Nahuli siyang **nagbubulakbol** sa trabaho kaya siya natanggal.","translation":"He was caught **skipping** work, which is why he was fired."}]

meaning_filipino: Kasalukuyang nagbabago ng direksyon; nasa akto ng pagliko.
original_explanation: This is the 'in the act' version of turning. It's the Waze voice saying 'In 200 meters...' and now you're actually, physically doing it. Also describes your friend who's currently in the middle of a major life crisis/change, 'Uy, parang lumiliko na ng landas si beshy.'
usage_notes: Actor-focus verb, progressive aspect (present tense).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tingnan mo, **lumiliko** na ang jeep papunta sa ating kalye.","translation":"Look, the jeep is already **turning** onto our street."},{"sentence":"Habang **lumiliko** ang usapan, naramdaman kong may mali.","translation":"As the conversation **was turning** (changing topic), I felt something was wrong."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panloob na bahagi ng isang bagay, tulad ng isang gusali, sasakyan, o lugar. Tumutukoy din sa mga pook na malayo sa baybayin o sentro ng kabihasnan.
original_explanation: Yan 'yung pinapaganda mo sa bahay mo (interior design) para "aesthetic" sa IG story. O 'yung mga lugar sa probinsya na kailangan mo pang mag-habal-habal para marating. Kung hindi coast, 'yan ang intiryor.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pangngalan (ang intiryor) o pang-uri (intiryor na bahagi).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maganda ang **intiryor** ng bagong coffee shop.","translation":"The **interior** of the new coffee shop is beautiful."},{"sentence":"Naglakbay sila sa **intiryor** na bahagi ng Mindanao.","translation":"They traveled to the **interior** parts of Mindanao."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa konteksto ng panitikan o media, tumutukoy ito sa materyal na magaan, masaya, at walang malalim na tunggalian o drama, na naglalayong magbigay ng aliw at magandang pakiramdam.
etymology: From English 'fluff', meaning something light and soft, extended to mean light, non-serious content.
original_explanation: The opposite of angst. This is your mental comfort food. In fanfiction, it's the story where your favorite characters just go on a coffee date, hold hands, and are generally cute with no drama. It's the literary equivalent of a warm hug, a sweet boba drink, or a video of a sleeping puppy. Pure, unadulterated kilig.
usage_notes: Heavily used in fanfiction and online communities to categorize stories that are purely lighthearted and conflict-free.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagod na ako sa drama, gusto ko lang magbasa ng **fluff** ngayon.","translation":"I'm tired of drama, I just want to read some **fluff** right now."},{"sentence":"Ang galing niyang magsulat ng **fluff**, lahat ng eksena ay nakakakilig.","translation":"She's great at writing **fluff**, all the scenes make you feel giddy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pinaghalong kemikal na mabilis masunog o sumabog, ginagamit bilang pampasabog sa mga bala ng baril at paputok.
original_explanation: The spicy dust that makes things go boom. Essential for fireworks on New Year's Eve (the illegal kind, usually) and for historical movies about the Philippine Revolution. It's the 'putok' in 'paputok'.
usage_notes: Also refers to the explosive powder in fireworks (`paputok`).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maingat na hinahawakan ng mga sundalo ang mga bala na puno ng **pulbura**.","translation":"The soldiers carefully handle the bullets filled with **gunpowder**."},{"sentence":"Ang amoy ng **pulbura** ay naiiwan sa hangin tuwing Bagong Taon.","translation":"The smell of **gunpowder** lingers in the air every New Year."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglikha, pagbuo, o pagganap sa isang gawain o produkto. Tumutukoy rin ito sa trabaho o hanapbuhay.
original_explanation: Your daily grind. Whether it's building a PowerPoint presentation for your boss, cooking adobo, or literally constructing a building. It's the effort you put in before you can say, "TGIF!" Also, the reason why we have Labor Day.
usage_notes: Can refer to the physical act of making something or the broader concept of labor/work.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paggawa** ng parol ay isang tradisyon tuwing Pasko.","translation":"The **act of making** lanterns is a Christmas tradition."},{"sentence":"Iginagalang natin ang mga karapatan ng mga manggagawa sa sektor ng **paggawa**.","translation":"We respect the rights of workers in the **labor** sector."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-alis sa isang tao, bagay, o lugar; ang hindi pagsama o pagdala sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: The national sport of the Philippines, second only to basketball. This is what happens when someone ghosts you, or when you forget your baon in the ref. 'Wag mo 'kong iwanan' is the official tagline of every Pinoy drama teleserye.
usage_notes: Often used in the imperative form. `Iwanan mo ako` (Leave me) vs `Iniwanan niya ako` (He/she left me).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **iwanan** dito,\" pakiusap niya.","translation":"Don't **leave** me here,\" he pleaded."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **iwanan** ang masamang bisyo para sa iyong kalusugan.","translation":"You need to **leave** your bad habits for your health."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing maliliit na piraso sa pamamagitan ng paulit-ulit na paghiwa o pagtaga; punuin ng butas o tama.
original_explanation: Ginagawa sa bawang at sibuyas para sa gisa. Ginagawa rin ng chismosa sa'yo 'pag nakatalikod ka—tinatadtad ka ng paninira.
usage_notes: Ang '-in' ay nagpapahiwatig na ito ay isang utos o aksyon na gagawin sa isang bagay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tadtarin** mo nang pino ang bawang para sa gisa.","translation":"**Chop** the garlic finely for the sauté."},{"sentence":"Binalak nilang **tadtarin** ng saksak ang biktima, ngunit ito'y nakatakas.","translation":"They planned to **riddle** the victim with stab wounds, but he escaped."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang produktong gawa sa gatas na mayaman sa taba; ang pinakamataas na bahagi ng gatas na umaangat sa ibabaw. Ginagamit din ito para sa mga pampahid sa balat.
original_explanation: That white stuff you put in your coffee to make it less 'kapeng barako' and more 'Starbucks-level'. It's also what you slap on your face hoping to look like a K-drama star, or the filling in your favorite cheap bakery bread. The "best part" of something, like the *cream* of the crop.
usage_notes: Widely used in cooking, beauty, and metaphorically. The Filipino pronunciation is a single syllable /krim/.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiabot ng **cream** para sa kape ko.","translation":"Please pass the **cream** for my coffee."},{"sentence":"Gumagamit siya ng face **cream** tuwing gabi para kuminis ang mukha.","translation":"She uses face **cream** every night to make her face smoother."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapang pangkamay na may dalawang hawakan at mga panga, ginagamit sa paghawak, pagpihit, pagputol, o pagbaluktot ng mga bagay tulad ng alambre.
etymology: From English `pliers`, with Filipinized spelling and pronunciation.
original_explanation: Tatay's best friend. That tool you can never find when you need it, but is always in the way when you don't. It's the go-to solution for everything from fixing a leaky faucet to pulling out a stubborn milk tooth (don't do this). Also known as 'alyas'.
usage_notes: 'Alyas' (from Spanish `alicates`) is another common term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiabot mo nga ng **plais**, aayusin ko lang itong alambre.","translation":"Please hand me the **pliers**, I'll just fix this wire."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang **plais** para bunutin ang pako.","translation":"He used the **pliers** to pull out the nail."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang awayan o labanan kung saan ang mga sangkot ay nagpapalitan ng mga suntok.
original_explanation: This is what happens when a heated argument in a basketball game or a drinking session escalates. **Suntukan** is the chaotic, often clumsy, exchange of punches between two or more people. It's the "hold my beer" moment before things get messy. "Tara, labas!" is its official invitation.
usage_notes: The suffix "-an" denotes a reciprocal or social action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nauwi sa **suntukan** ang mainit na pagtatalo ng dalawang lalaki.","translation":"The heated argument between the two men ended in a **fistfight**."},{"sentence":"Inawat ng mga tanod ang nagaganap na **suntukan** sa kanto.","translation":"The village watchmen broke up the ongoing **brawl** at the corner."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pang-abay na nagpapahayag ng pagkakatulad, paghahambing, o pag-aakala; katumbas ng "wari," "tila," o "parang."
etymology: From Spanish 'ánimo' (spirit, mind, intention), but its meaning in Tagalog shifted to 'it seems'.
original_explanation: This is the formal, literary version of "parang." You use it to say something seems like something else. "Animo isang anghel" (Like an angel). It's the word you use in a poem or a formal speech to sound deep and dramatic. It’s the "as if" you use when you want to be more Shakespeare and less "Clueless."
usage_notes: Often used in literature, poetry, and formal speech. 'Parang' or 'tila' are more common in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga mata ay **animo** mga bituin sa dilim.","translation":"Her eyes were **like** stars in the dark."},{"sentence":"Tahimik ang buong paligid, **animo**'y walang taong nakatira.","translation":"The entire surrounding was quiet, **as if** no one lived there."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang alternatibo at kolokyal na anyo ng "karneng-baka"; ang karne o laman na nagmumula sa baka.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "carne" (karne) at Tagalog na "baka" (cow), na may di-pamantayang paggamit ng pang-ugnay na "-ng".
original_explanation: Same beef, different spelling. This is like when someone types "u" instead of "you" in a text. We all know what it means. It's the less formal, perhaps faster way to say 'karneng-baka'. Still ends up as your delicious bulalo.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang kolokyal o di-pormal na baryasyon ng "karneng-baka". Ang wastong paggamit ng pang-ugnay para sa salitang nagtatapos sa patinig tulad ng "karne" ay "-ng", kaya "karneng-baka" ang pamantayang anyo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakibili mo ako ng **karning-baka** para sa nilaga.","translation":"Please buy me some **beef** for the nilaga."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang **karning-baka** nila dito.","translation":"Their **beef** here is delicious."}]

translation: to correspond with each other; to respond to one another
meaning_filipino: Ang palitan ng sagot o tugon sa isa't isa, maaaring sa paraang pasulat o pasalita.
original_explanation: Before DMs and Messenger, people used to 'magtugunan' through love letters. Today, it's that rapid-fire exchange of emails with your boss or thesis adviser. It’s the formal term for a back-and-forth communication, where each party is responding to the other.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of formal communication, like letters or official queries.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matagal nang **nagtutugunan** sa pamamagitan ng email ang dalawang opisyal.","translation":"The two officials have been **corresponding with each other** via email for a long time."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga na **magtugunan** ang mga ahensya ng gobyerno para sa mabilis na serbisyo.","translation":"It's important for government agencies to **respond to one another** for fast service."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong maramdamin, madaling masaktan o magtampo sa mga biro o puna.
etymology: From 'pabalat' (cover/skin) + 'sibuyas' (onion). Refers to the thin, delicate skin of an onion.
original_explanation: Literally 'onion-skinned.' 'Yung kaibigan mong konting biro mo lang, iiyak na o magtatampo for a week. Parang sibuyas, konting hiwa lang, luha agad. 'Wag kang ganyan, pabalat-sibuyas ka talaga!'
usage_notes: A common idiomatic expression.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong **pabalat-sibuyas**; biro lang iyon.","translation":"Don't be so **overly sensitive**; it was just a joke."},{"sentence":"Kilala siyang **pabalat-sibuyas** kaya't maingat ang mga tao sa pakikipag-usap sa kanya.","translation":"He/She is known to be **thin-skinned**, so people are careful when talking to him/her."}]

translation: to have something registered or listed
meaning_filipino: Utos o pakiusap na isulat o i-rehistro ang isang pangalan, numero, o impormasyon sa isang opisyal na talaan.
original_explanation: What you do when you sign up for a new class, register your SIM card, or when a chismosa neighbor mentally lists down everyone who visited your house. 'Ipatala mo na pangalan ko sa listahan ng mga a-attend sa party.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **ipatala** ang iyong pangalan sa attendance sheet.","translation":"Don't forget to **have** your name **listed** on the attendance sheet."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ugnayan o pagkakabit ng dalawa o higit pang mga bagay, tao, o ideya; ang estado ng pagiging magkaugnay.
original_explanation: That thing you lose during an important Zoom meeting or when you're about to win in Mobile Legends. Also, what you need to get a job, a government permit, or a discount from your suki. It's not what you know, it's *who* you know, and if their Wi-Fi is strong.
usage_notes: Karaniwang binabaybay din bilang 'koneksyon'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawala ang **koneksiyon** ko sa internet.","translation":"I lost my internet **connection**."},{"sentence":"Malakas ang **koneksiyon** niya sa gobyerno kaya madali siyang nakakuha ng pwesto.","translation":"He has strong **connections** in the government, that's why he easily got a position."}]

translation: to wait for the right time; to make seasonal
meaning_filipino: Gawin o hintayin ang angkop na panahon o pagkakataon para sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: It's like waiting for your crush to be single before you make a move. "Panahunin mo muna," sabi ng tropa mo. It's about perfect timing, whether for confessing your feelings or for planting rice. You don't rush it; you let the universe (or the weather) give you the go-signal.
usage_notes: Can mean to let time pass for something or to do something at the right season. It implies a strategic delay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Panahunin** muna natin ang pag-aani ng mangga para mas matamis ang mga ito.","translation":"Let's **wait for the right season** to harvest the mangoes so they will be sweeter."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magmadali, **panahunin** mo ang iyong desisyon.","translation":"Don't rush, **wait for the right time** for your decision."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bahagi ng panloob na organo ng mga ibon, lalo na ng manok, na matigas at makunat na ginagamit sa pagdurog ng pagkain.
etymology: Likely a reduplication of an older root word related to internal organs.
original_explanation: The gizzard. That chewy, sometimes rubbery, but oh-so-good part of the chicken you find in your adobo, or grilled on a stick as an isaw-adjacent street food. It's the chicken's personal food processor. For the uninitiated, it might look sus, but for Pinoys, it's a delicacy.
usage_notes: A common ingredient in Filipino cuisine, especially in dishes like "adobong balumbalunan" or as "pulutan" (bar chow). Often sold alongside chicken liver (atay).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong pulutan ang inihaw na **balumbalunan**.","translation":"Grilled **gizzard** is my favorite bar chow."},{"sentence":"Pakilinis nang mabuti ang mga **balumbalunan** bago ito igisa.","translation":"Please clean the **gizzards** well before sautéing them."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahalagang pista sa Kristiyanismo na ginugunita ang pagbaba ng Espiritu Santo sa mga Apostol, limampung araw pagkatapos ng Linggo ng Pagkabuhay.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'Pentecostés,' mula sa Griyegong 'Pentēkostē' (hēmera), na nangangahulugang 'ikadalawampu'.
original_explanation: This is the 'birthday' of the Christian Church. It's the day the Holy Spirit basically downloaded a language pack and a courage upgrade to the apostles, turning them from a scared, hiding group into a worldwide movement. In the Philippines, it's a significant feast day, but doesn't have the same commercial hype as Christmas or Easter. It's more of a 'for your spiritual knowledge' kind of holiday.
usage_notes: Palaging isinusulat na may malaking titik dahil ito ay isang pangngalang pantangi na tumutukoy sa isang partikular na kapistahang panrelihiyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagdiriwang ng mga Kristiyano ang **Pentekostes** tuwing ikalimampung araw pagkatapos ng Pasko ng Pagkabuhay.","translation":"Christians celebrate **Pentecost** on the fiftieth day after Easter."},{"sentence":"Ang pagbaba ng Espiritu Santo ay ang sentro ng selebrasyon ng **Pentekostes**.","translation":"The descent of the Holy Spirit is the center of the **Pentecost** celebration."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagkakaroon ng posisyon kung saan ang mukha at baba ay nakatuon paitaas, karaniwang nagpapahiwatig ng pagmamataas o pagiging arogante.
original_explanation: Yung pose mo kapag feeling mo ang ganda-ganda mo at 'di ka pwedeng basta-basta kausapin. Head tilted back, chin up, parang ready ka sa profile picture. 'Yung tingin na "Who you?" sa mga peasants.
usage_notes: Often carries a negative connotation of arrogance or haughtiness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging **tingadngad** ang ulo niya kaya madalas siyang nasusubsob.","translation":"His head is always **tilted upward**, that's why he often stumbles."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi permanente; pabago-bago ng estado, lokasyon, o desisyon.
original_explanation: This is the official status of your 'situationship.' It's the Wi-Fi signal in a coffee shop, the price of gasoline, or your friend who changes their career plans every week. There's no stability, no fixed state. 'Walang label,' but for jobs, locations, and decisions.
usage_notes: Describes a state of flux or lack of permanence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa kontrata, **walang-kapirmihan** ang kanyang trabaho.","translation":"Because of the contract, his job is **not permanent**."},{"sentence":"Ang buhay ay **walang-kapirmihan** kaya dapat maging handa sa pagbabago.","translation":"Life is **inconstant**, so one must be ready for change."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa ng isang medikal na pamamaraan kung saan binubuksan o minamanipula ang katawan ng isang pasyente upang gamutin ang isang sakit o pinsala.
original_explanation: This is what doctors do in medical dramas when they say 'Scalpel!' It's the ultimate 'trust fall'—you're literally putting your life in someone's hands. It's also what your tita thinks will happen if you keep eating instant noodles: 'Naku, baka kailanganin mong magpa-opera sa bato!'
usage_notes: Primarily used in a medical context. The causative form is 'magpa-opera', meaning to undergo surgery.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga doktor ay handa nang **mag-opera** sa pasyenteng may appendicitis.","translation":"The doctors are ready to **operate** on the patient with appendicitis."},{"sentence":"Mahirap at maselan ang **mag-opera** sa puso.","translation":"It is difficult and delicate to **perform surgery** on the heart."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na inilalagay sa loob ng isa pa bilang panloob na patong, proteksyon, o para sa kalinisan. Karaniwang tumutukoy sa "eye liner" o "panty liner".
original_explanation: This is a catch-all term for anything that 'lines' something else. Pwedeng eye liner para sa 'on fleek' cat-eye mo, pwedeng panty liner for 'that time of the month' feels, or even the plastic liner of your trash can. It's the sidekick, the support act, the thing that protects the main event.
usage_notes: The specific meaning is highly dependent on context. Most common usages are for cosmetics and hygiene products.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahihirapan akong maglagay ng eye **layner** nang pantay.","translation":"I have a hard time applying eye **liner** evenly."},{"sentence":"Pakilagyan ng bagong **layner** ang basurahan.","translation":"Please put a new **liner** in the trash can."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na walang talim o hindi matulis, tulad ng lapis o kutsilyo.
original_explanation: This is your lapis nung elementary days after a long-ass exam, totally flat. Or the kutsilyo in the office pantry that couldn't even slice a birthday cake properly. Basically, something that has lost its edge and is now functionally useless for its main cutting/piercing purpose.
usage_notes: Primarily used for objects that are supposed to have a sharp point or edge.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paano ako magsusulat kung **walang-tasa** ang lapis ko?","translation":"How will I write if my pencil is **unsharpened**?"},{"sentence":"Mahirap maghiwa ng sibuyas gamit ang kutsilyong **walang-tasa**.","translation":"It's hard to slice onions with a **dull** knife."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking miyembro ng banda na namumuno sa parada, karaniwang may hawak na isang malaking baston o 'mace'.
original_explanation: The male counterpart of the bastonera. He's the guy at the front of the marching band, looking sharp in his uniform, leading the charge with a big shiny mace. He sets the tempo not just for the music, but for the whole fiesta vibe.
usage_notes: The masculine form of 'bastonera'. While less common in everyday conversation, it is the correct term for a male drum major leading a marching band.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **bastunero** ang nagbibigay ng hudyat sa buong banda.","translation":"The **drum major** gives the signal to the entire band."},{"sentence":"Magara ang uniporme ng **bastunero** ngayong taon.","translation":"The **drum major's** uniform is fancy this year."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang anumang pagkakahawig o pagkakatulad sa iba; bukod-tangi.
etymology: From 'wala' (none) + 'ka-' + 'mukha' (face/resemblance), with the root reduplicated for emphasis.
original_explanation: When you can't even say 'parang kamukha ni...' because there's just no one like them. It's the level of uniqueness that makes you stand out, for better or for worse. It’s that one dish your lola makes that no restaurant can copy, or your friend's laugh that you can identify from a kilometer away. Truly one of a kind.
usage_notes: The reduplication 'mukta-mukta' is a more emphatic and slightly more poetic form of 'walang-kamukha'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng tanawin sa Batanes ay **walang-kamukta-mukta**.","translation":"The beauty of the scenery in Batanes is **incomparable**."},{"sentence":"Talaga namang **walang-kamukta-mukta** ang kanyang talento sa pag-awit.","translation":"Her talent in singing is truly **without any resemblance** to others."}]

meaning_filipino: Inilaan, itinabi, o itinalaga para sa isang partikular na tao, bagay, o layunin.
original_explanation: Parang yung feelings mo na para lang sa kanya, 'laan' na. Or yung sweldo mo na pagdating pa lang, may pangalan na ng Meralco, Maynilad, at Shopee. It's earmarked, baby.
usage_notes: Often used with 'para sa' (for). The verb form is 'maglaan' (to allot/reserve).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tulong na ito ay **laan** para sa mga nasalanta ng bagyo.","translation":"This aid is **intended for** the victims of the typhoon."},{"sentence":"Naglaan ako ng pera na **laan** sa aking pagreretiro.","translation":"I set aside money that is **allotted** for my retirement."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa posisyong nakahiga o nakahandusay; hindi nakatayo o nakaupo.
etymology: From `pa-` (prefix indicating manner or position) + `higa` (to lie down).
original_explanation: This is your default state on a Sunday morning or after a long shift. Not sitting, not standing, just... horizontal. Whether you're binge-watching a series or just 'resting your eyes,' if your back is on a flat surface, you're in a *pahiga* state. It's the opposite of the 'hustle' culture.
usage_notes: Describes the state or manner of being. Often used with verbs like 'matulog', 'magbasa', or 'manood'. Can also function as an adjective.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap magbasa ng libro nang **pahiga** sa kama.","translation":"It's nice to read a book while **lying down** in bed."},{"sentence":"Natagpuan siyang **pahiga** sa sahig at walang malay.","translation":"He was found **lying** on the floor, unconscious."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos na ginawa sa nakaraan kung saan ang isang bagay ay ibinalik sa dati nitong posisyon o kinalalagyan; pagbawi sa isang sinabi o ipinangako.
etymology: From "i-" (object-focus verb prefix) + "urong" (recede, move back), with past tense infix "-in-".
original_explanation: Like when you're about to send that risky text, but then you get cold feet and delete it. That's "iniurong mo." Or when your boss announces a salary deduction, but due to massive backlash, they take it back. "Iniurong" is the past tense for pulling something back, whether it's a chair, a decision, or a lawsuit.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical movement or the cancellation of a plan, statement, or action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Iniurong** niya ang upuan para makadaan ako.","translation":"He **moved back** the chair so I could pass."},{"sentence":"**Iniurong** ng kumpanya ang kaso laban sa mga empleyado.","translation":"The company **withdrew** the case against the employees."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hindi pagbibigay ng importansya, pagwawalang-bahala, o pagmamaliit sa isang tao, bagay, o damdamin.
original_explanation: The ultimate hugot verb. This is what you accuse your ex of doing to your feelings. "Huwag kang magpawalang-halaga sa sakripisyo ng mga magulang mo." It’s the act of treating something or someone like they’re just an optional side dish, not the main course.
usage_notes: Carries a strong emotional or moral weight.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masakit para sa kanya na **magpawalang-halaga** sa kanyang mga opinyon ang sarili niyang pamilya.","translation":"It's painful for her that her own family **disregards** her opinions."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **magpawalang-halaga** sa'yo ang sino man.","translation":"Don't let anyone **devalue** you."}]

translation: the act of being halted or stopped abruptly
meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang paghinto o pagkatigil ng isang kilos, balak, o proseso na nasimulan na.
original_explanation: When you're about to send that risky 'Hi' to your crush, but then you see they're 'In a Relationship.' Or when the Wi-Fi dies in the middle of a crucial download. That sudden, frustrating stop is pagkaudlot. It's the universe saying 'not today.'
usage_notes: Often implies that an action was started but was prevented from being completed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkaudlot** ng kanilang bakasyon ay dahil sa biglaang anunsyo ng lockdown.","translation":"The **abrupt halting** of their vacation was due to the sudden announcement of a lockdown."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang inis dahil sa **pagkaudlot** ng kanyang magandang panaginip.","translation":"He felt annoyed because of the **abrupt end** of his nice dream."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na isinama, idinugtong, o idinagdag sa isang mas malaking kabuuan.
etymology: From 'langkap' meaning 'to incorporate or include'. The prefix 'ka-' often denotes a state of being or a co-member of something.
original_explanation: Think of it as a "DLC" (downloadable content) for a document or a building. It's the extra part that's officially attached, like when your barangay suddenly gets a new zone added to it, or that extra PDF page in your employment contract. It's an official 'kasama' or 'karugtong'.
usage_notes: Often used in formal, legal, or architectural contexts to mean 'annexed' or 'included as a part of'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bagong gusali ay **kalangkap** ng lumang munisipyo.","translation":"The new building is an **annex** to the old municipal hall."},{"sentence":"Nasa **kalangkap** na dokumento ang mga detalye ng proyekto.","translation":"The project details are in the **attached** document."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng isang lugar o bagay kung saan nagtatagpo ang dalawa o higit pang gilid o linya.
original_explanation: Your personal space when you're "nag-e-emote" or need to "think-box." Also the best place to find spiders, dust bunnies, and forgotten chargers. Sa coffee shop, ito yung spot na may saksakan. Sa kwarto, ito yung "The Chair" kung saan nakatambak lahat ng damit na "pwede pa isuot uli."
usage_notes: Can refer to a physical corner or a remote, secluded place ('sa bawat sulok ng mundo' - in every corner of the world).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinago niya ang kahon sa madilim na **sulok** ng bodega.","translation":"He hid the box in a dark **corner** of the storage room."},{"sentence":"May maliit na kapihan sa **sulok** ng kalye.","translation":"There's a small coffee shop on the street **corner**."}]

meaning_filipino: Pabilisin ang isang gawain, proseso, o paggalaw; dagdagan ang tulin.
original_explanation: Utos sa'yo ng boss mo 5 minutes before end-of-day: 'Tulinan mo 'yang report!' Utos mo sa sarili mo kapag may chismis: 'Tulinan ang paglalakad papunta sa kung saan man sila nag-uusap.' Basically, 'step on it!' or 'make it faster!'
usage_notes: Isang pautos o naglalarawang pandiwa para sa pagpapabilis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tulinan** mo ang pagmamaneho, baka mahuli tayo sa ating flight.","translation":"**Speed up** your driving, we might be late for our flight."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **tulinan** ang produksyon upang matugunan ang demand.","translation":"Production needs **to be hastened** to meet the demand."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tunog na nalilikha ng isang tao sa pamamagitan ng bibig at lalamunan kapag nagsasalita, kumakanta, o gumagawa ng ingay.
original_explanation: This is your vocal superpower! Pwedeng pang-videoke night with the titas, pang-sermon sa kapatid, or pang-bulong ng 'psst' sa katabi mo sa jeep. Your 'boses' is your signature sound. It's what makes people turn when you call their name, or what makes your dog come running.
usage_notes: A fundamental and widely used word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng **boses** mo, pwede kang sumali sa singing contest.","translation":"You have a beautiful **voice**; you could join a singing contest."},{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **boses** ni nanay mula sa kusina.","translation":"I heard mom's **voice** from the kitchen."}]

translation: had an accident; met with misfortune
meaning_filipino: Sumapit sa isang di-inaasahang kapahamakan o masamang pangyayari.
etymology: From Spanish "desgracia" (misfortune, accident) with the Tagalog prefix "na-".
original_explanation: Eto 'yung moment na "Ay, sh*t!" From spilling coffee on your white shirt, to a minor fender-bender sa EDSA, to something more serious. Kapag sinabing "nadisgrasya," may nangyaring hindi maganda. It's the universe saying "Oops!" on your behalf.
usage_notes: Can range from minor mishaps to serious accidents.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nadisgrasya** ang sinasakyan nilang bus kagabi.","translation":"The bus they were riding **had an accident** last night."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi ako **nadisgrasya**, nadulas lang ako.","translation":"Don't worry, I **didn't have a serious accident**, I just slipped."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang pangkusina na may butas-butas na ginagamit sa paghihiwalay ng likido sa solido, o sa pagsasala ng mga pagkain.
original_explanation: Your best friend when you're making pancit canton and you don't want to burn your hands draining the hot water. It's the thing that separates the essentials (noodles) from the non-essentials (the water you just boiled them in). Parang sa life, you need a salaan to filter out the fake friends.
usage_notes: The root word is 'sala' in the sense of 'to filter', combined with the suffix -an to denote a tool or place.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gamitin mo ang **salaan** para alisin ang mga buto sa calamansi juice.","translation":"Use the **strainer** to remove the seeds from the calamansi juice."},{"sentence":"Naiwan ang pansit sa **salaan** habang tinatapon ang mainit na tubig.","translation":"The noodles were left in the **colander** while the hot water was being thrown out."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan opisyal na naninirahan ang isang tao; isang tirahan, lalo na ang isang malaki at marangyang bahay.
original_explanation: Sounds fancier than 'bahay' or 'tahanan'. This is what you call the Malacañang Palace or the house of a CEO in a posh village. When you say 'residensiya,' you're not talking about a condo unit in Cubao; you're picturing a mansion with a driveway and maybe a fountain. It's a house with an upgrade.
usage_notes: Often used to refer to official or large, impressive homes. 'Residensya' is a common alternative spelling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang opisyal na **residensiya** ng Pangulo ng Pilipinas ay ang Palasyo ng Malakanyang.","translation":"The official **residence** of the President of the Philippines is Malacañang Palace."},{"sentence":"Nakatira sila sa isang malaking **residensiya** sa Forbes Park.","translation":"They live in a large **residence** in Forbes Park."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa dalawa o higit pang bagay na may parehong porma o anyo.
etymology: From `magka-` + `hugis`, where `magka-` indicates having a shared quality.
original_explanation: It's like when you and your bestie accidentally buy the same cookie cutter or phone case. "Uy, magkahugis yung phone natin!" It means they're twinsies, but for shapes.
usage_notes: Used as a predicate adjective. To use it to describe a noun, you would say "mga bagay na magkahugis".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magkahugis** ang mga ulap na tila mga kumpol ng bulak.","translation":"The clouds **have the same shape**, like clumps of cotton."},{"sentence":"Bumili siya ng mga hikaw na **magkahugis** sa kanyang kuwintas.","translation":"She bought earrings that **have the same shape** as her necklace."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghiling na manirahan o tumuloy nang pansamantala sa tahanan ng ibang tao.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "maki-" (paghiling ng pakikisali) at salitang ugat na "bahay" (tahanan).
original_explanation: The act of asking a relative or friend, 'Pwede bang diyan muna ako for a few weeks/months/years?' It happens when you're starting a new job in the city, waiting for your own place, or after a major 'tampo' with your parents. Key to survival: be helpful, buy your own toiletries, and don't overstay your welcome.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa pansamantalang paninirahan at hindi sa permanenteng paglipat. May kasamang paghingi ng pahintulot.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Habang naghahanap ng apartment, sa tiyahin muna niya siya **makikibahay**.","translation":"While looking for an apartment, she will **live with** her aunt for the time being."}]

meaning_filipino: Mag-isip o mag-ilusyon tungkol sa mga bagay na ninanais habang gising at hindi natutulog; paglalakbay ng diwa.
etymology: A literal phrase meaning 'to dream while awake'.
original_explanation: This is what you do during a boring Zoom meeting. Your eyes are open, but your mind is in Siargao, on a date with your crush, or imagining your life after winning the lottery. It's building castles in the air while wide awake. It can be a pleasant escape or a sign you're totally checked out.
usage_notes: A common idiomatic expression. It carries a slightly negative connotation, implying inaction or unrealistic fantasy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag ka lang puro **mangarap nang gising**, kumilos ka para matupad 'yan.","translation":"Don't just **daydream**, you have to act to make it happen."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang likas na kaganapang elektrostatiko na naglalabas ng kuryente na makikita bilang isang maliwanag na guhit sa kalangitan, karaniwang kasama ng kulog.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung flash ng camera ni Lord bago ka Niya sermonan via kulog. Perfect for dramatic entrances, exits, and realizing you forgot to save your work before the brownout. Sing with me: "Kasama kang tumanda... *sabay flash ng **kidlat***".
usage_notes: Often paired with 'kulog' (thunder). 'Kumidlat' is the verb form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang tumayo sa ilalim ng puno kapag may **kidlat** at kulog.","translation":"Don't stand under a tree when there is **lightning** and thunder."},{"sentence":"Parang **kidlat** sa bilis ang pagdating ng rider na may dalang pagkain.","translation":"The rider with the food arrived as fast as **lightning**."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa musika, ito ay ang pagbibigay-diin sa mahinang kumpas ng sukat. Sa linggwistika, ito ay ang pagkakaltas ng isang tunog o pantig sa gitna ng isang salita.
original_explanation: In music, **singkopa** (syncopation) is the funky, off-beat rhythm that gives OPM its flavor. In language, it's our natural tendency to be efficient (or lazy). It's why "tayo na" becomes "tena," and "nasaan" becomes "asan." It's the linguistic shortcut that makes Tagalog flow so smoothly in conversation.
usage_notes: A technical term used in both music theory and linguistics.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ritmo ng kantang iyon ay puno ng **singkopa** kaya masarap sayawin.","translation":"The rhythm of that song is full of **syncopation**, which is why it's great to dance to."},{"sentence":"Ang salitang 'kanin' ay halimbawa ng **singkopa** mula sa salitang 'kainin'.","translation":"The word 'kanin' (rice) is an example of **syncope** from the word 'kainin' (to be eaten)."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng kakayahang gayahin, sipiin, o kopyahin ang isang bagay, tulad ng sulat, ideya, o gawa.
original_explanation: The ultimate student skill during a surprise quiz. "Pst! Patingin! Para may makopya lang!" It's also what happens when your files get transferred from a USB or when your brilliant idea gets "borrowed" by a coworker. It can be a lifesaver or a source of workplace drama.
usage_notes: Can mean either "to be able to copy" (as the subject) or "to be copied" (as the object). Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **makopya** ko ang lahat ng files bago mag-shutdown ang computer.","translation":"I hope I can **copy** all the files before the computer shuts down."},{"sentence":"Ingatan mo ang iyong sagot para hindi **makopya** ng katabi mo.","translation":"Guard your answers so they won't **be copied** by the person next to you."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang walang-pigil na pagtatamasa o pagpapakasawa sa isang bagay, karaniwan ay sa pagkain o anumang kaligayahan, na para bang isang piging.
original_explanation: This is how you attack a 'samgyup' buffet when you haven't eaten all day. It's the feeling of getting your 13th-month pay and thinking of all the things you'll buy. It's indulging to the max, no holds barred. 'Pista!' mode.
usage_notes: The root 'pasa' here is different from 'pasa' (pass) or 'pasa' (bruise). It's an archaic root related to feasting or abundance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga bisita ay nasiyahan sa **pagpasasaan** sa masasarap na handa.","translation":"The guests enjoyed **feasting upon** the delicious food prepared."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang taong madaling maniwala, mabilis malinlang, o medyo mahina ang pag-iisip.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung friend mo na laging naniniwala sa 'PM for details' at 'Send this to 10 people or else...' 'Yung tipo na madaling mabudol. Literally 'soft head,' it means someone is either too trusting or not the sharpest tool in the shed.
usage_notes: Can be slightly derogatory, implying either gullibility or a lack of intelligence. Contrast with 'matigas ang ulo' (hard-headed, stubborn).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **malambot ang ulo** at maniwala agad sa mga pekeng balita.","translation":"Don't be **gullible** and immediately believe fake news."},{"sentence":"Madali siyang maloko dahil **malambot ang ulo** niya.","translation":"He is easily fooled because he is **easily persuaded**."}]

translation: to mark with a 'kudlit'; to make a small mark on
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng kudlit sa isang titik; ang paggawa ng isang maliit na marka o guhit sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: The act of adding that tiny game-changing mark in Baybayin. Verb form of 'kudlit'. It's like proofreading your ancient script homework. 'Bes, 'wag kalimutan kudlitan 'yan, baka iba mabasa nila.'
usage_notes: Used in the context of writing or making small, precise marks, especially in historical scripts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kudlitan** mo ang simbolong 'ba' para maging 'bi'.","translation":"**Put a diacritical mark** on the 'ba' symbol to make it 'bi'."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **kudlitan** ang mesa, baka magasgasan.","translation":"Don't **make a mark on** the table, it might get scratched."}]

translation: to pull or stretch something out (variant of banatin)
meaning_filipino: Hilaing mabuti upang umunat o humaba. Ito ay isang di-karaniwang varyant ng salitang "banatin".
etymology: From root 'banat' (stretch) + '-in' suffix. A less common conjugation compared to 'banatin'.
original_explanation: This is like the less popular sibling of the word "banatin." They both mean to stretch something, like when you try to make your sweldo last until the 30th. It's pulling and hoping for the best. While most people say "banatin," using "banasin" is like ordering a "Coke float" instead of a "Coke McFloat"—people might understand you, but they'll know you're a little different.
usage_notes: 'Banatin' is the more standard and widely used term. 'Banasin' may be encountered in some dialects or older texts but is generally considered non-standard.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong masyadong **banasin** ang lastiko at baka maputol.","translation":"Don't **stretch** the rubber band too much or it might break."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang pag-agos o paglabas nang marami ng likido mula sa isang sisidlan o pinagmulan.
original_explanation: Imagine you accidentally stab your milk tea with a straw too hard and the whole thing explodes out the top. That's 'bugwak'. It's the dramatic exit of any liquid, like water from a broken pipe, juice from a dropped tetra-pak, or even tears when you finally let it all out. It’s a sudden, messy 'whoosh'.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun for the gush itself, or as a verb root (bumugwak, nagbugwak) for the action of gushing out.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng **bugwak** ng tubig mula sa sirang tubo sa kalsada.","translation":"There was a **gush** of water from the broken pipe on the street."},{"sentence":"Bumugwak ang dugo mula sa kanyang sugat.","translation":"Blood **spurted** from his wound."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalagyan na idinisenyo upang mapanatili ang temperatura ng likido sa loob nito, mainit man o malamig, sa loob ng mahabang panahon.
etymology: Mula sa tatak na Ingles na "Thermos", na naging pangkaraniwang tawag sa produkto.
original_explanation: Ang best friend ng mga mahilig sa kape sa office at ng mga nanay na nagbabaon ng mainit na sabaw para sa anak. It's the OG 'insulated tumbler' bago pa nauso yung mga mamahaling brand. Yung silver na may pulang takip? Classic!
usage_notes: A genericized trademark. Used to refer to any vacuum flask, regardless of brand.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtimpla si nanay ng mainit na kape sa **termos** para sa almusal.","translation":"Mom prepared hot coffee in the **thermos** for breakfast."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang dalhin ang **termos** na may lamang malamig na tubig.","translation":"Don't forget to bring the **thermos** with cold water."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sistema, patakaran, o pamamaraan ng pamamahala sa isang organisasyon, tanggapan, o gawain.
original_explanation: This is the 'rules and regulations' or 'how things are done around here.' The 'No tardiness,' 'Clean as you go,' and 'Ask permission before borrowing money' — all of that is part of the **palakad** of the office, the house, or the country. It’s the unwritten (or written) rules of the game.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ako sang-ayon sa bagong **palakad** ng management.","translation":"I do not agree with the new **policy** of the management."},{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang **palakad** sa loob ng kampo militar.","translation":"The **system** inside the military camp is strict."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa estadistika, ito ang gitnang halaga sa isang set ng mga numero na nakaayos ayon sa pagkakasunud-sunod ng laki.
etymology: From English 'median', derived from Latin 'mediānus' (of the middle).
original_explanation: The middle child of statistics. It's not the 'average' (mean) that gets all the attention, nor the 'mode' that's the most popular. The medyan is just the one chilling in the exact middle once you've lined everyone up. It's the most "sakto lang" (just right) number in the group, unbothered by outliers.
usage_notes: A technical term used in mathematics and statistics.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para makuha ang **medyan**, kailangan mo munang ayusin ang mga numero mula sa pinakamababa hanggang sa pinakamataas.","translation":"To get the **median**, you first need to arrange the numbers from lowest to highest."},{"sentence":"Sa aming klase, ang **medyan** na edad ay labing-siyam.","translation":"In our class, the **median** age is nineteen."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lapis na gawa sa may-kulay na pagkit (wax), ginagamit sa pagsulat o pagguhit.
etymology: From the brand name 'Crayola', which itself is from French 'craie' (chalk) + 'ola' (from 'oléagineux', meaning oily). The brand has become a genericized trademark in the Philippines.
original_explanation: The smell of your childhood. This is the ultimate art material for every Filipino kid, used to draw the classic 'bahay-bundok-araw' scene. The 8-piece set was for beginners, the 64-piece set with a built-in sharpener meant your parents really loved you. Also, the first thing you tried to eat that wasn't food.
usage_notes: Used universally to mean any wax crayon, regardless of brand.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawala ang paborito niyang kulay ng **krayola**.","translation":"He lost his favorite color of **crayon**."}]

translation: to make someone an accomplice; to conspire with
meaning_filipino: Isama o hikayatin ang isang tao na maging kabahagi sa isang lihim o masamang plano.
original_explanation: The action of recruiting your partner in crime. "Gusto niya akong kasabwatin sa plano niyang pagtakas sa trabaho." (He wants to make me his accomplice in his plan to escape work early). It's the verb for when the main kontrabida convinces a formerly good character to join the dark side.
usage_notes: This is the verb form of 'kasabuwat'. It means to recruit or involve someone in a conspiracy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang papayag na **kasabwatin** ka sa kanilang masamang balak.","translation":"Don't allow them **to make you an accomplice** in their evil plan."},{"sentence":"Tinangka ng suspek na **kasabwatin** ang guwardiya ngunit nabigo siya.","translation":"The suspect tried **to conspire with** the guard but he failed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging isang panatiko; labis at bulag na paghanga o pananampalataya sa isang tao, ideya, o bagay, partikular na tumutukoy sa isang babae.
etymology: Mula sa `pagka-` (estado ng pagiging) + `panatika` (babaeng panatiko, mula sa Espanyol na 'fanática').
original_explanation: This is the female version of a die-hard fan. Think of a Tita who defends her favorite political candidate on Facebook 24/7, or a fangirl who would sell a kidney for a concert ticket to see her K-pop bias. It's intense, unwavering loyalty that sometimes borders on scary. The "walang makakapigil sa amin" energy is strong with this one.
usage_notes: Isang terminong pangkasarian, partikular para sa isang babaeng panatiko. Ang pangkalahatan at mas karaniwang termino ay "pagkapanatiko".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halata sa kanyang mga post sa social media ang kanyang **pagkapanatika** sa artistang iyon.","translation":"Her **fanaticism** for that artist is obvious in her social media posts."},{"sentence":"Nag-aalala ang pamilya sa **pagkapanatika** niya sa isang kulto.","translation":"The family is worried about her **fanaticism** towards a cult."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging kalmado o tiwasay ng damdamin matapos ang isang panahon ng pag-aalala, takot, o kaguluhan.
original_explanation: That feeling when you finally get the 'nakauwi na ako' text. It's the 'aaahhh' moment of relief after a period of intense anxiety, like when you thought you lost your phone but it was in your bag all along. Your heart rate slows down, your breathing stabilizes, and you can finally chill.
usage_notes: Refers to an emotional or mental state of becoming calm. Often used with 'loob' (pumanatag ang loob).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pumanatag** ang kanyang loob nang malaman niyang ligtas ang kanyang pamilya.","translation":"He **was reassured** (his inside became calm) when he found out his family was safe."},{"sentence":"Hindi ako **papanatag** hangga't hindi natin nalulutas ang problemang ito.","translation":"I will not **be at ease** until we solve this problem."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na kailangan o hinihingi bilang kondisyon bago magawa o matamo ang isang bagay; isang paunang pangangailangan.
original_explanation: Yung listahan ng mga bagay na kailangan mong ipasa sa prof mo para lang makagraduate, or yung listahan ng qualities na hinahanap mo sa jowa. 'Must be 5'8", must have a car, must love dogs.' Lahat 'yan, rekisito.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa mga kontekstong akademiko, legal, at burukratiko.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong kumpletuhin ang lahat ng **rekisito** bago ka payagang kumuha ng pagsusulit.","translation":"You need to complete all the **requirements** before you are allowed to take the exam."},{"sentence":"Isa sa mga **rekisito** sa pag-apply ng trabaho ay ang NBI clearance.","translation":"One of the **requirements** for a job application is the NBI clearance."}]

translation: a load carried on the shoulder
meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na pasan o buhat sa balikat; ang akto ng pagbubuhat sa balikat.
etymology: A root word, likely from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *pasaŋ.
original_explanation: This is the OG way of carrying things before backpacks became cool. Think of a farmer with a sack of rice on his shoulder, or Jesus carrying the cross—that's **pasang**. In modern life, it's the invisible weight of your responsibilities, your "kruses sa buhay." When you say, "Ang bigat ng **pasang** ko ngayon," you're not talking about a sack of rice, you're talking about deadlines, bills, and adulting in general.
usage_notes: Often used with 'krus' as in 'pasang na krus' (carrying a cross) to mean a life's burden.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang magsasaka ay may **pasang** na isang sakong bigas.","translation":"The farmer is **carrying** a sack of rice **on his shoulder**."},{"sentence":"Ang bawat isa ay may kanya-kanyang **pasang** na krus sa buhay.","translation":"Everyone has their own cross **to bear** (lit. carry on their shoulder) in life."}]

translation: detrimental; ruinous; a person who causes trouble
meaning_filipino: Isang tao, bagay, o pangyayari na nagdudulot ng kapahamakan, perwisyo, o kasiraan.
original_explanation: This is that one friend who always gets you into trouble. The "tara, isang bote lang" (come on, just one bottle) friend. That's a pahamak. It can also be a situation. Forgetting your wallet on a date? Pahamak. Replying-all to a company-wide email with a meme? Super pahamak. It's anything or anyone that leads to your downfall, big or small.
usage_notes: As a noun, it refers to the troublemaker. As an adjective, it describes something as being the cause of trouble.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang sasama sa mga **pahamak** na kaibigan na iyan.","translation":"Don't go with those **troublemaker** friends."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang pagsusugal ang naging **pahamak** sa kanilang pamilya.","translation":"His gambling became the **ruin** of their family."}]

meaning_filipino: May kulay na katulad ng abo; kulay-abo.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "abo" (ash) at hulaping "-in".
original_explanation: 'Yung kulay ng langit bago umulan, o 'yung kulay ng buhok ng lolo mo. Sa fashion, ito 'yung "safe" color kapag ayaw mong mag-itim o mag-puti. Minsan, ito rin ang kulay ng future mo pag petsa de peligro na.
usage_notes: Can describe color or a state of being pale (ashen-faced). The formal term is 'kulay-abo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko ng damit na may kulay na **abuhin**.","translation":"I want a dress that is **grayish** in color."},{"sentence":"Naging **abuhin** ang kanyang mukha dahil sa takot.","translation":"His face became **ashen** due to fear."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga bagay, katangian, o pangyayari na may kaugnayan sa isang bulkan.
original_explanation: Anything and everything related to a volcano. Volcanic rock? Batong bulkanika. Volcanic eruption? Pagsabog na bulkaniko. It's the adjective you use when you want to sound smart while talking about volcanoes. Parang "volcanic" pero with a Spanish flair.
usage_notes: Isang mas pormal o teknikal na termino. Ang "bulkaniko" (panlalaki) ay mas karaniwan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga batong **bulkanika** ay resulta ng lumamig na lava.","translation":"**Volcanic** rocks are the result of cooled lava."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan nila ang aktibidad na **bulkanika** sa rehiyon.","translation":"They are studying the **volcanic** activity in the region."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal mula sa internet, partikular sa platapormang Twitch, na ginagamit upang ipahayag ang kalungkutan o pagkabigo, kadalasan sa paraang nagbibiro o may kababaang-loob.
etymology: Mula sa isang 'emote' sa Twitch na nagpapakita ng malungkot na bersyon ng 'Pepe the Frog', na naging popular noong 2020.
original_explanation: The official emote and sound of disappointment in the internet age. When your internet cuts out during a crucial game moment? Sadge. When your GrabFood order gets cancelled? Sadge. It's the resigned sigh of the chronically online.
usage_notes: Halos eksklusibong ginagamit sa online chat at mga komunidad ng gaming. Bihira itong bigkasin nang malakas sa labas ng konteksto ng pagbibiro tungkol sa kultura ng internet.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ako nakakuha ng tiket sa concert. **Sadge**.","translation":"I didn't get a ticket to the concert. **Sadge**."},{"sentence":"Player 1: Natalo tayo. Player 2: **Sadge**.","translation":"Player 1: We lost. Player 2: **Sadge**."}]

meaning_filipino: Putulin o anihin ang mga pananim gamit ang karit.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'gapas'. Ito 'yung act of actually doing the reaping. 'Yung kailangan mong i-exert 'yung effort, hindi 'yung naghihintay ka lang ng resulta. Parang sa trabaho, kailangan mong gapasin ang mga task para may sahod sa kinsenas.
usage_notes: The `-in` suffix indicates the object to be acted upon (i.e., the crops to be harvested).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nang **gapasin** ang mga palay bago pa dumating ang bagyo.","translation":"The rice stalks need to **be harvested** before the typhoon arrives."}]

translation: to splash water with the hands
meaning_filipino: Ang paghampas o pagwisik ng tubig gamit ang kamay o palad.
original_explanation: Yung ginagawa mo sa beach o sa swimming pool para asarin ang mga kasama mo. Hindi ito yung seryosong langoy, ito yung playful na pagwiwisik ng tubig. Ang 'tampol' ay ang first stage ng isang nagbabadyang basaan.
usage_notes: Ang salitang-ugat mismo ay madalas gamitin bilang utos, "Tampol!". Ang mga anyo ng pandiwa ay 'tumampol', 'tinatampol', 'tatampulin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **tampulin** ng tubig, mababasa ang cellphone ko!","translation":"Don't **splash** me with water, my cellphone will get wet!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasalita nang marami at madalas, na kung minsan ay walang gaanong kabuluhan o saysay.
original_explanation: We all have that one friend (or we are that friend). The one who can talk about anything and everything, from the latest chismis to their detailed analysis of a new K-drama episode, without taking a breath. To "magdaldal" is to unleash a torrent of words. It's not necessarily a bad thing, unless you're trying to watch a movie in silence.
usage_notes: Often has a slightly negative or teasing connotation, implying that the talking is excessive or trivial.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumigil ka na sa **pagdaldal** at tulungan mo ako dito.","translation":"Stop **chattering** and help me here."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **magdaldal** sa telepono nang maraming oras.","translation":"She loves to **talk excessively** on the phone for many hours."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi kayang tumbasan ng anumang halaga; hindi masukat ang kahalagahan.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `di-` (hindi) at `matataya` (aspektong panghinaharap ng 'mataya'), na galing sa salitang ugat na `taya` (tantiya, pusta).
original_explanation: Like a Mastercard commercial, but make it Filipino. Your lola's love, your barkada's loyalty, a good night's sleep after a stressful week—these are things that are **di-matataya**. You can't put a price tag on them. It's priceless, bes!
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na ang halaga ay hindi kayang sukatin, lalo na sa pera. Binibigyang-diin nito ang napakalaking halaga na kadalasa'y sentimental o abstrakto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang halaga ng edukasyon ay isang yaman na **di-matataya**.","translation":"The value of education is a **priceless** treasure."},{"sentence":"Ang mga alaala namin ay may kahalagahang **di-matataya**.","translation":"Our memories have an **incalculable** worth."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pag-agaw o mabilis na pagkuha sa isang bagay. Ito ang anyong pautos o pokus sa layon ng pandiwang 'dagit'.
original_explanation: Ito yung command form or object-focused version ng 'dagit'. Kapag sinabi ng nanay mo sa pusa, "Huwag mong **dagitin** yung isda!", 'yan yun. O kaya kapag kinukwento mo, "Muntik nang **dagitin** yung bag ko sa Divisoria." It's the action of snatching directed *at* an object.
usage_notes: Object-focus verb. From 'dagit' + '-in'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **dagitin** ng pusa ang ulam.","translation":"Don't let the cat **snatch** the viand."},{"sentence":"Ang sisiw ay **dinagit** ng isang malaking ibon.","translation":"The chick **was snatched** by a large bird."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang ibabaw na hindi makinis, magaspang, o hindi pino ang tekstura.
original_explanation: Describes the texture of un-sanded wood, cheap toilet paper, or your skin after a beach trip without lotion. Also, can sometimes describe a person's voice that sounds like they smoke 40 cigarettes a day.
usage_notes: Primarily used for physical textures but can be used metaphorically for a rough or grating voice or manner.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magalasgas** ang papel de liha na ginamit ng karpintero.","translation":"The sandpaper used by the carpenter is **coarse**."},{"sentence":"Naging **magalasgas** ang kanyang mga kamay dahil sa mabigat na trabaho.","translation":"His hands became **rough** because of hard work."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kulay na nasa pagitan ng dilaw at asul sa spectrum ng liwanag; ang kulay ng mga dahon at damo.
original_explanation: The color of money (dollars, specifically), nature, and 'go' signals. It's the color of your 'plantita' friend's condo jungle. In classic Filipino humor, it can also mean 'dirty-minded' ('berde ang isip' or 'green-minded'). So depending on context, it could be about ecology or that joke your tito just told.
usage_notes: The native Tagalog term is 'lunti' or 'luntian,' but 'berde' is far more common in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paborito niyang kulay ay **berde**.","translation":"Her favorite color is **green**."},{"sentence":"Naging **berde** na ang ilaw-trapiko kaya umandar na kami.","translation":"The traffic light turned **green** so we started moving."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bilang na kasunod ng lima at sinusundan ng pito; katumbas ng tambilang na 6.
original_explanation: The number 6. It's half a dozen eggs from the palengke, the number of months in your 'probationary' relationship stage, or the number of unread messages from your boss at 7 AM.
usage_notes: A basic Filipino numeral.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroon akong **anim** na kapatid.","translation":"I have **six** siblings."},{"sentence":"Bumili ka ng **anim** na mansanas sa tindahan.","translation":"Buy **six** apples from the store."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang madala at manatili sa isang ospital para sa panggagamot o pag-aalaga dahil sa sakit o pinsala.
original_explanation: Ito yung ayaw na ayaw mong marinig sa nanay mo pagkatapos mong umubo ng isang beses. 'Naku, baka kailangan mo nang maospital!' It's the ultimate 'health is wealth' reminder, kasi ang mahal maospital, beshie.
usage_notes: The prefix 'ma-' here indicates an involuntary or non-volitional event.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay hindi na **maospital** si Lolo dahil sa kanyang pneumonia.","translation":"I hope Grandpa doesn't have to be **hospitalized** for his pneumonia."},{"sentence":"**Naospital** siya nang isang linggo dahil sa dengue.","translation":"She was **hospitalized** for a week due to dengue."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na ipinapasak o inilalagay sa isang butas o bibig upang takpan o pigilan ang pagdaloy ng anuman.
original_explanation: That thing you stuff into a hole to stop a leak, or more dramatically, what villains use to keep the hero from shouting for help. Parang 'yung feelings mo for your ex na pilit mong binaon sa limot pero biglang sumulpot ulit. You need a bigger 'sumpal' for that.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin para sa mga pisikal na bagay (tulad ng tapon sa bote) o sa matalinhagang paraan para sa pagpapatahimik sa isang tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng basahan bilang **sumpal** sa tumatagas na tubo.","translation":"He used a rag as a **plug** for the leaking pipe."},{"sentence":"Tinanggal niya ang **sumpal** sa bibig ng bihag.","translation":"He removed the **gag** from the hostage's mouth."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian o kalagayan ng pagiging masungit, mapagmataas, at hindi palakaibigan ng isang lalaki.
etymology: From `pagka-` (state of being) + `suplado` (snobbish male), likely influenced by Spanish `soberbio` (proud, arrogant).
original_explanation: This is the male version of the suplada. He's the guy who gives one-word answers, never initiates a conversation, and looks like he's mentally calculating your net worth. He's the 'seen-zoner' king on Messenger. Often mistaken for being 'cool and mysterious,' but most of the time, he's just... suplado.
usage_notes: Specifically used to describe the quality or state of a male being a snob.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itago mo na lang ang **pagkasuplado** mo kapag kaharap ang mga kliyente.","translation":"Just hide your **snobbishness** when you're in front of clients."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkasuplado** niya ang dahilan kung bakit kaunti lang ang kaibigan niya.","translation":"His **snobbishness** is the reason why he has few friends."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagtatatag ng relasyon ng pagkakaibigan sa isang tao.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of making a 'kaibigan' (friend). It's the act of turning a stranger or an acquaintance into your 'beshie' or 'barkada'. It's less common now than 'makipagkaibigan,' but it has a more direct, almost intentional feel. Like you're on a mission to win someone's friendship. 'Pinilit niyang mangaibigan ang buong klase.' (He tried to befriend the entire class.)
usage_notes: The verb 'makipagkaibigan' (to try to make friends with) is more commonly used in modern conversation. 'Mangaibigan' can sound a bit more formal or literary.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **mangaibigan** ng taong hindi mapagkakatiwalaan.","translation":"It is difficult to **befriend** a person who is not trustworthy."},{"sentence":"Ang dayuhan ay natutong **mangaibigan** sa pamamagitan ng pagiging bukas-palad.","translation":"The foreigner learned to **befriend** people by being generous."}]

translation: to squat with one leg extended
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-upo sa posisyong nakabaluktot ang isang binti habang ang isa naman ay tuwid na nakaunat. Ito ay isang uri ng pag-upo na malapit sa lupa.
original_explanation: This is that specific, almost-acrobatic squat you do when you're trying to check something low on a grocery shelf but don't want your pants to touch the floor. It's the "tindera sa palengke" power pose while sorting vegetables. A very Filipino way of resting without actually sitting down.
usage_notes: A very specific posture, often associated with rural or market settings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita ko si Lolo na **maningkayad** habang inaayos ang kanyang mga pananim.","translation":"I saw Grandpa **squatting with one leg extended** while fixing his plants."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **maningkayad** kung masikip ang iyong pantalon.","translation":"It's hard to **squat with one leg out** if your pants are tight."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalaro o paggalaw gamit ang sapatos na may gulong (roller skates/blades) o talim (ice skates).
original_explanation: What you did in the 90s at SM Megamall's skating rink, trying to look cool while secretly holding onto the rails for dear life. Now it's an "aesthetic" TikTok trend.
usage_notes: Can refer to roller skating, inline skating, or ice skating. Context usually clarifies which one.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **mag-isketing** sa parke tuwing Sabado ng hapon.","translation":"She loves to **go skating** at the park every Saturday afternoon."},{"sentence":"Tara, **mag-isketing** tayo sa bagong rink sa mall!","translation":"Let's go, let's **go skating** at the new rink in the mall!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasunduan kung saan ang bawat tao sa isang grupo ay magbabayad ng kani-kanilang bahagi sa isang gastusin, karaniwan sa pagkain sa isang restawran.
original_explanation: The ultimate friendship test. "KKB" (kanya-kanyang bayad) is the traditional way, but to "split" the bill equally is the modern barkada move. It's faster than using a calculator to figure out who owes what for the extra rice. Often declared with "Split tayo, ha?" to avoid one person getting stuck with the whole bill, aka the "taya" for the day.
usage_notes: Commonly used in the context of dining out. Often used with 'tayo' as in "Mag-split tayo" (Let's split the bill).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang laki ng bill natin, **split** na lang tayo para mas madali.","translation":"Our bill is huge, let's just **split** it to make it easier."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, ako na ang taya. Hindi na natin kailangang mag-**split**.","translation":"Don't worry, it's my treat. We don't need to **split** the bill."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang matinding damdamin ng pananabik o pagnanais para sa isang bagay o pangyayari na inaasahan.
original_explanation: That feeling when you see 'item out for delivery' on your Shopee/Lazada tracker. Or when it's 4:59 PM on a Friday. Or when you're waiting for your crush to reply. That mix of anticipation and pure joy is pagkasabik. It's the opposite of 'seen-zoned'.
usage_notes: Pagkasabik is the noun form of the feeling. 'Nasasabik' is the verb form ('I am excited').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya maitago ang kanyang **pagkasabik** na makita ang kanyang pamilya.","translation":"He couldn't hide his **eagerness** to see his family."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkasabik** sa pag-uwi ng OFW ay ramdam sa buong bahay.","translation":"The **excitement** for the OFW's homecoming was felt throughout the house."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang matinding pagnanasa sa mga bagay na pag-aari ng iba; kasakiman.
etymology: From `pag-` (nominalizer) + `imbot` (covet). The repetition in `pag-iimbot` emphasizes the intensity or the act itself.
original_explanation: This is that feeling when you see your officemate's 13th-month pay bonus and you suddenly wish it was yours, or when your kapitbahay buys a new car and you start plotting how to 'accidentally' scratch it. It's the 'sana all' that has turned to the dark side. It's not just wanting what they have; it's wanting it *so bad* it consumes you.
usage_notes: Carries a strong negative and moral connotation, often related to the concept of envy and one of the seven deadly sins.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pag-iimbot** sa yaman ng iba ay nagdudulot lamang ng kapighatian.","translation":"**Covetousness** towards the wealth of others only brings misery."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagtukoy at pagkuha ng isa o higit pa mula sa isang grupo ng mga opsyon o pagpipilian.
original_explanation: This is you in a milk tea shop, staring at the menu for 10 minutes, causing a long line behind you. "Wintermelon ba o Okinawa? 50% sugar o 25%? With pearls or nata de coco?" The struggle is real. It's the adult version of 'eenie meenie miney moe' but with more consequences, like choosing a career or a life partner.
usage_notes: A very common verb used in daily decision-making.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magpili** ng kursong kukunin mo sa kolehiyo.","translation":"You need to **choose** the course you will take in college."},{"sentence":"**Nagpili** siya ng pinakamagandang damit para sa party.","translation":"She **selected** the most beautiful dress for the party."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kawalan ng kahit isang tao; ni isa mang tao.
original_explanation: The ultimate "seen-zone" status. When you throw a party and literally no one shows up. It's the headcount when your crush asks who likes them back... and you're too shy to admit it. "Sino'ng sasama sa 'kin?" "..." That silence? That's 'walang sinuman'.
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang idiin ang ganap na kawalan ng mga tao sa isang sitwasyon o lugar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Walang sinuman** ang nakakaalam ng kanyang tunay na nararamdaman.","translation":"**No one** knows what he truly feels."},{"sentence":"Sa lahat ng aking tinanong, **walang sinuman** ang nakasaksi sa pangyayari.","translation":"Of all the people I asked, **nobody** witnessed the event."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matalinhagang pananalita para sa isang taong may malubhang sakit at hindi na makabangon sa higaan.
etymology: Idiomatic expression. 'Ratay' means confined to bed due to sickness. 'Banig' is a handwoven mat.
original_explanation: A classic, dramatic Filipino expression. It's not just "sick in bed," it's SICK in bed. It evokes images of old teleseryes where someone is gravely ill, lying on a traditional woven mat (banig). You don't use this for a simple cold; you use it when the chismis is that someone is really, really unwell. "Narinig mo ba? Si Mang Kanor, nakaratay sa banig."
usage_notes: This is a very specific and somewhat old-fashioned idiom. It implies a serious, long-term illness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matagal nang **nakaratay sa banig** ang matandang maysakit.","translation":"The old sick man has been **bedridden due to illness** for a long time."},{"sentence":"Ipinagdasal nila ang agarang paggaling ng kanilang amang **nakaratay sa banig**.","translation":"They prayed for the quick recovery of their father who was **bedridden due to illness**."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga bagay, gawain, o pagnanasa na may kinalaman sa buhay sa lupa at materyal na mundo, salungat sa espirituwal.
etymology: From Spanish 'mundo' (world) + 'ka-...-an' affix, signifying a collective concept or quality.
