original_explanation: Basically, everything your lola tells you to avoid during Holy Week. It's the 'worldly stuff'—partying, chasing money, living for the 'gram, the opposite of being spiritual. 'Layuan mo ang kamunduhan, iho/iha.' (Stay away from worldly things, son/daughter.)
usage_notes: Often carries a negative or cautionary connotation, especially in religious or moral contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinalikuran niya ang **kamunduhan** upang maging isang monghe.","translation":"He turned his back on **worldly matters** to become a monk."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang padadala sa tukso ng **kamunduhan**.","translation":"Don't be swayed by the temptations of **worldliness**."}]

translation: to flail, to wriggle, to wag
meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit at mabilis na paggalaw o pagkampay ng bahagi ng katawan, tulad ng kamay, paa, o buntot.
original_explanation: This is the motion your dog's tail makes when you get home. It's also what your legs do when you're trying not to drown (wag naman sana). It’s that frantic, uncontrolled wriggling or flailing motion. Imagine a fish out of water or a baby excitedly waving its arms and legs. That's kumawag-kawag.
usage_notes: The repetition in 'kawag-kawag' implies a continuous or frantic motion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumawag-kawag** ang buntot ng aso nang makita nito ang kanyang amo.","translation":"The dog's tail **wagged** excitedly when it saw its owner."},{"sentence":"Nang mahulog sa tubig, **kumawag-kawag** ang kanyang mga kamay at paa.","translation":"When he fell into the water, his arms and legs **flailed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa dalawa o higit pang bagay na may parehong bilang, dami, o sukat.
original_explanation: That moment when you and your friend order the same number of chicken wings. "Parehas lang tayo." Or when you check your bank accounts and realize you're both equally "petsa de peligro." It's the perfect equality in numbers, for better or for worse.
usage_notes: Part of the "magkasing-" family of comparative adjectives.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magkasindami** kami ng librong nabasa ngayong taon.","translation":"We read the **same number** of books this year."},{"sentence":"Siguraduhing **magkasindami** ang ibibigay mong pagkain sa mga bata.","translation":"Make sure you give the children the **same amount** of food."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kakanin na yari sa malagkit na bigas, karaniwang niluto sa gata ng niyog, at binabalot sa dahon ng saging o niyog.
original_explanation: The OG Pinoy energy bar. It's the sweet, sticky rice cake you bring home as *pasalubong* that's tightly wrapped like your family secrets. Perfect with hot chocolate, a sprinkle of sugar, or even fresh mangoes.
usage_notes: Often associated with holidays, fiestas, and as a pasalubong (homecoming gift). Different regions have their own versions, such as Suman sa Lihiya or Suman sa Ibos.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito ni lola ang **suman** na may latik tuwing umaga.","translation":"Grandma's favorite is the **rice cake** with coconut caramel every morning."},{"sentence":"Nag-uwi si Tatay ng isang tali ng **suman** mula sa Antipolo.","translation":"Dad brought home a bundle of **rice cakes** from Antipolo."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pahayagan na may mas maliit na sukat kaysa sa karaniwang broadsheet, at kadalasang naglalaman ng mga balitang sensasyonal at mga larawan na nakakaagaw-pansin.
original_explanation: The OG source of chismis before social media took over. You'd see these being sold by vendors weaving through traffic. Known for their screaming headlines about celebrities, crime, and the occasional supernatural tale. Think of it as the physical version of a clickbait article, complete with scantily-clad women on the back page.
usage_notes: Often associated with sensationalism and lower journalistic standards compared to broadsheets.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nabasa ko sa **tabloid** ang tungkol sa pinakabagong iskandalo ng artista.","translation":"I read about the artist's latest scandal in the **tabloid**."},{"sentence":"Murang-mura lang ang mga **tabloid** kaya sikat ito sa masa.","translation":"**Tabloids** are very cheap, which is why they are popular with the masses."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng kawalan ng kaayusan, katahimikan, o kapayapaan; kaguluhan.
original_explanation: Your room before your mom threatens to disown you. The group chat when a chismis drops. The traffic on EDSA during a payday Friday. Basically, any situation that makes you say, "Ayoko na."
usage_notes: Can refer to a physical mess ('ang gulo ng kwarto') or a chaotic situation ('huwag kang gumawa ng gulo').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula ang **gulo** nang magtalo ang dalawang panig.","translation":"The **trouble** started when the two sides began to argue."},{"sentence":"Ayusin mo ang **gulo** sa iyong silid-tulugan.","translation":"Fix the **mess** in your bedroom."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng lalagyan ng pagkain na karaniwang may maraming patong o suson para sa iba't ibang uri ng ulam at kanin.
original_explanation: The OG lunch box, the multi-tiered, stainless steel baunan of your lolo or your dad. It’s the Pinoy version of a bento box. Each layer is a surprise: one for rice, one for adobo, and maybe one for a paksiw. It’s a symbol of a lovingly packed meal from home, way before Tupperware became a thing.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to the stacked, often cylindrical metal food containers.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dala ni Tatay ang kanyang lumang **piyambrera** papunta sa bukid.","translation":"Father brought his old **tiered lunch box** to the farm."},{"sentence":"Inayos ni Nanay ang ulam at kanin sa loob ng **piyambrera**.","translation":"Mother arranged the viand and rice inside the **tiered food container**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalagyan o kabinet, karaniwang nasa kusina, na pinaglalagyan ng mga pinggan, baso, at iba pang kagamitan sa pagkain.
etymology: From "pinggan" (plate). The "pan-" prefix becomes "pam-" and the "-an" suffix denotes a place. So, "pam-pinggan-an" -> "pamingganan".
original_explanation: The final resting place for plates and utensils after their epic battle in the kitchen sink. It's that sacred corner of the kitchen where the 'good plates' (the ones you only use for guests) are kept, separate from the everyday, battle-scarred ones. Also known as a 'platera'.
usage_notes: Can refer to a dish rack for drying or a cupboard for storage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiayos ng mga plato sa **pamingganan** pagkatapos mong hugasan.","translation":"Please arrange the plates on the **dish rack** after you wash them."},{"sentence":"Itinago ni nanay ang mga mamahaling baso sa itaas na bahagi ng **pamingganan**.","translation":"Mother kept the expensive glasses in the upper part of the **cupboard**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa isang kalagayan na hindi gaanong paborable; may mas maliit na tsansang manalo o magtagumpay.
etymology: From Spanish 'dejado' (left behind, abandoned). Its meaning shifted in Filipino to 'disadvantaged'.
original_explanation: Being the underdog. It's when you're in a basketball game and the other team has a player who's 7 feet tall. It's applying for a job where another applicant is the boss's nephew. You're starting with a handicap. But hey, Pinoys love a good 'dihado' story who wins in the end!
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'dehado', which is closer to the Spanish original. 'Dihado' reflects a more nativized spelling and pronunciation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit **dihado** sa laban, hindi sumuko ang boksingero.","translation":"Even if he was at a **disadvantage** in the fight, the boxer did not give up."},{"sentence":"Laging **dihado** ang mga maliliit na magsasaka pagdating sa presyo ng kanilang ani.","translation":"Small farmers are always **disadvantaged** when it comes to the price of their harvest."}]

translation: to become robust, to become healthy/sturdy
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-unlad tungo sa pagiging malusog, matatag, at masigla ang katawan.
etymology: From the root word 'lusog' (healthiness, robustness) + the '-um-' infix.
original_explanation: 'Yung alaga mong tuta na dati'y sakitin, tapos ngayon ang taba-taba na. Lumasog! Or your friend who started hitting the gym, dati payatot, ngayon pang-Marvel na ang katawan. It's the glow-up of health.
usage_notes: Often used for children, animals, or plants that are growing well and becoming healthy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tingnan mo ang mga tanim, **lumasog** mula nang umulan.","translation":"Look at the plants, they've **become robust** since it rained."},{"sentence":"Mula nang alagaan siya ng kanyang lola, **lumasog** ang bata.","translation":"Ever since his grandmother took care of him, the child **became healthy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang biyolohikal na proseso ng paglanghap ng hangin (oxygen) at pagbuga nito (carbon dioxide) na mahalaga sa buhay.
original_explanation: What you forget to do when your crush walks by. Also, what your boss tells you to do ('Hinga lang, guys!') before dropping a mountain of work on a Friday afternoon. The most basic, yet most forgotten, survival skill.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging mabilis ang kanyang **paghinga** matapos tumakbo.","translation":"His **breathing** became fast after running."}]

meaning_filipino: Mabilis at paulit-ulit na pagtibok o pagpintig, karaniwan ay tumutukoy sa puso.
original_explanation: This is your heart when you see your crush, or when you get your credit card bill. It's that extra, frantic beat that says, 'OMG, this is it!' It’s the BPO agent’s heart after three cups of coffee on a night shift.
usage_notes: The repetition in `tahip-tahip` emphasizes the rapid, continuous, and often frantic nature of the beating.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumahip-tahip** ang dibdib niya habang hinihintay ang resulta ng exam.","translation":"Her chest **throbbed rapidly** while waiting for the exam results."}]

translation: A Filipino fish dish with fermented black beans
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng lutuing Pilipino na karaniwang isda (tulad ng bangus o tilapia) na ginigisa sa bawang, sibuyas, kamatis, at tausi (fermented black beans).
etymology: From Hokkien Chinese 豆豉 (tāu-sī), meaning 'fermented black beans', the key ingredient.
original_explanation: It's that fish dish your lola makes that smells... interesting... but tastes amazing. The secret ingredient is tausi (fermented black beans), which gives it that unique savory, slightly funky flavor. Think of it as the umami bomb of Filipino fish stews.
usage_notes: Often spelled as 'totcho'. The dish is characterized by its savory and slightly salty sauce from the black beans.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-request si Tatay ng **totso**ng bangus para sa pananghalian.","translation":"Dad requested milkfish in black bean sauce (**totso**) for lunch."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang **totso** kapag maraming kamatis at sibuyas.","translation":"**Totso** is delicious when it has a lot of tomatoes and onions."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong nakatapos o dumalo sa Cursillo, isang kilusang apostoliko ng Simbahang Katoliko.
original_explanation: That tito or tita in your family who, after a weekend retreat, suddenly greets everyone with 'De Colores!' and is super active in church. They've been through the 'Kursilyo' and are now part of a lifelong spiritual barkada.
usage_notes: Specific to a person who has completed the Cursillo, a movement within the Catholic Church.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Aktibo sa parokya ang mga **kursilyista**.","translation":"The **cursillistas** are active in the parish."},{"sentence":"Ang tatay ko ay isang **kursilyista** mula pa noong dekada '80.","translation":"My father has been a **cursillista** since the 80s."}]

meaning_filipino: Ilagay sa isang dambana; ituring na sagrado, sambahin, o parangalan nang lubos.
original_explanation: This is what hardcore fans do to their K-pop idols. They treat them like gods. You **idambana** someone when you put them on a pedestal so high they can't even see the ground anymore. It can be literal, like placing a statue on an altar, or figurative, like how you view your ultimate celebrity crush.
usage_notes: Often used in a figurative or literary sense to mean 'to glorify' or 'to hold in very high regard'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa kanyang mga tula, tila **idinadambana** niya ang kagandahan ng kalikasan.","translation":"In his poems, it seems he **enshrines** the beauty of nature."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mapanirang-puri o mapangutyang pananalita laban sa isang tao; paghamak o pag-alipusta.
original_explanation: The OG 'bashing'. Before cyberbullying became a thing, there was 'lait'. It's what your tita does at the family reunion when she says, 'Uy, tumaba ka!' with matching judgmental eyes. That's pure, unadulterated lait.
usage_notes: The verb form is 'laitin' (to insult someone). It implies a level of scorn and looking down on the person being insulted.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi maganda ang panay na **lait** sa kapwa.","translation":"Constant **mockery** of others is not good."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **laitin** ang kanyang hitsura.","translation":"Don't **insult** his appearance."}]

meaning_filipino: Laganap o karaniwan; madalas na ginagamit o naririnig kaya't nawawalan na ng pagiging natatangi.
original_explanation: Ito yung mga bagay, salita, o idea na sobrang gamit na gamit na, parang 'sana all' o 'awit'. Sa sobrang common, nagiging basic na. Parang yung plot ng Pinoy teleserye na may amnesia o nagkapalit na anak. Alam mo na, gasgas na.
usage_notes: Maaaring magkaroon ng bahagyang negatibong konotasyon, na nagpapahiwatig na ang isang bagay ay sobra nang gamit o hindi na orihinal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang salitang 'hugot' ay naging **palasak** na sa social media.","translation":"The word 'hugot' has become **widespread/trite** on social media."},{"sentence":"Isang **palasak** na dahilan ang pagsasabing 'traffic' kapag nahuhuli sa usapan.","translation":"Saying 'traffic' is a **common** excuse when late for an appointment."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-awit ng isang partikular na kanta o mga kanta bilang harana sa isang tao.
etymology: harana + -in (suffix indicating the object or thing acted upon)
original_explanation: Similar to 'haranahan', but the focus shifts slightly to the song or the act of singing itself as the means of serenading. Think of it as 'to use a song to serenade.' While they are often interchangeable, 'haranahin' can put more emphasis on the song being performed.
usage_notes: Verb. While it can also refer to the person being serenaded, it is often used when the song is the object. 'Anong kanta ang haharanahin mo?' (What song will you use to serenade?).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Anong kanta ang gusto mong **haranahin** sa kanya?","translation":"What song do you want **to use to serenade** her?"},{"sentence":"Balak kong **haranahin** ang aking kasintahan sa aming anibersaryo.","translation":"I plan **to serenade** my girlfriend on our anniversary."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga tagasunod o kampon ng isang makapangyarihang tao, karaniwang may negatibong konotasyon na tumutukoy sa mga kasabwat sa masamang gawain.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'alguaciles y porras' (constables and clubs).
original_explanation: The 'sipsip' squad of a corrupt politician or a kontrabida in a teleserye. They're the ones who do the dirty work, laugh at the boss's bad jokes, and are always lurking in the background. Think of them as the backup dancers to a crime.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng pulitika o krimen. Halos palaging may dalang negatibong kahulugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging nakabuntot sa alkalde ang kanyang mga **alipores**.","translation":"The mayor's **minions** are always tailing him."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang masinsinan at walang-ingat na paghahanap o paghalungkat sa loob ng isang lalagyan, bunton ng mga bagay, o espasyo.
original_explanation: This is what you do to your closet when you can't find that one specific shirt. It's the frantic searching in your bag for your keys or wallet. It's organized chaos, but mostly chaos. The end result is a bigger mess than when you started.
usage_notes: Often used in its affixed form 'balutbutin' (verb). The root itself is less common in speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **balutbutin** ang mga gamit ko!","translation":"Don't **rummage** through my things!"},{"sentence":"Binabalutbot niya ang buong aparador para hanapin ang nawawalang medyas.","translation":"He is **rummaging** through the entire closet to find the missing sock."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang yugto o panahon sa buhay ng isang tao kung saan binibigyan niya ng matinding pokus ang pagpapaganda ng kanyang kapaligiran, itsura, o pangkalahatang istilo.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng 'aesthetic' at 'era' mula sa Ingles.
original_explanation: When you suddenly decide everything in your life needs to look good. You start buying beige clothes, drinking iced coffee from glass straws, and journaling with fancy pens. It's your 'main character' phase, but specifically focused on visuals. 'Sorry, 'di ako pwede gumala, nasa aesthetic era ako, nag-aayos ng kwarto.'
usage_notes: Isang modernong slang na popular sa mga kabataan at sa social media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa **aesthetic era** daw si Lisa kaya lahat ng gamit niya, dapat matchy-matchy.","translation":"Lisa is supposedly in her **aesthetic era**, that's why all her things have to be matchy-matchy."}]

translation: to pile up neatly; to stack
meaning_filipino: Ayusin ang mga bagay sa paraang magkakapatong-patong nang maayos at organisado.
original_explanation: This is the art of arranging your 1,000-page reading for your finals, or stacking the plates after washing them so they don't crash. It's the opposite of how your clothes look on 'the chair.' 'Bes, isalansan mo naman yang feelings mo, ang gulo na.'
usage_notes: Implies order and neatness, not just random piling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**isalansan** ang mga libro sa estante.","translation":"Please **stack** the books neatly on the shelf."},{"sentence":"**Isinalansan** niya ang mga damit sa aparador.","translation":"She **piled up** the clothes neatly in the closet."}]

meaning_filipino: Matinding takot o pangingilabot na nararamdaman dahil sa isang nakasisindak na pangyayari, bagay, o isipin.
original_explanation: That feeling you get when you're watching a horror movie alone at 3 AM and you hear a strange noise from the kitchen. Or when you check your bank account after a 12.12 sale. Pure hilakbot. It's not just 'takot' (fear); it's fear with goosebumps and a racing heart.
usage_notes: Often used with the verb 'makaramdam' (to feel) or as a verb with the prefix 'mang-,' becoming 'manghilakbot' (to be terrified).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napuno ng **hilakbot** ang mga manonood sa huling eksena ng pelikula.","translation":"The audience was filled with **terror** during the movie's final scene."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang **hilakbot** nang biglang mamatay ang lahat ng ilaw.","translation":"She felt **horror** when all the lights suddenly went out."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na inihuhulog, tulad ng bayad para sa isang utang o bilihin (installment), o isang kagamitan para maghulog ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: The money you set aside for your monthly Shopee SPayLater or Home Credit payments. It's the "hulog" that makes owning that new iPhone possible, one payment at a time. It can also be a physical thing, like the coin you drop into an arcade machine. Basta may inihuhulog, panghulog 'yan.
usage_notes: Commonly refers to installment payments.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinabi ko na ang pera para sa **panghulog** sa motorsiklo.","translation":"I've set aside the money for the motorcycle **payment**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mo ng barya bilang **panghulog** sa vending machine.","translation":"You need a coin as **something to drop** into the vending machine."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang apelyido o pangalan ng pamilya sa Pilipinas.
etymology: Pinaniniwalaang hango sa Espanyol, posibleng may kaugnayan sa salitang 'apellido' (apelyido) o ibang rehiyonal na salita.
original_explanation: It's a surname. Like Santos or Cruz, but less common. You probably know someone, or know someone who knows someone, with this last name. It's not something you'd use in a regular sentence unless you're calling Mang **Apido**.
usage_notes: Ginagamit bilang isang pantanging ngalan ng tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pamilya **Apido** ay matagal nang naninirahan sa bayang ito.","translation":"The **Apido** family has long been living in this town."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang opisyal na desisyon o sentensiya na iginagawad ng isang hukuman, hukom, o anumang awtoridad.
original_explanation: The moment of truth in a courtroom drama. It's the 'Guilty or Not Guilty?' reveal. In everyday life, it's the 'verdict' your parents give you after you try to explain why you broke curfew. The final, non-negotiable decision.
usage_notes: Primarily used in legal or formal contexts, but can be used metaphorically for any final judgment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinihintay ng buong bansa ang **kahatulan** sa kaso.","translation":"The entire nation is waiting for the **verdict** on the case."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maling paggamit, pagmamalabis, o masamang pagtrato sa isang tao, bagay, o kapangyarihan.
original_explanation: This is the 'what'—the action itself. It's working unpaid overtime, getting gaslighted, or seeing someone use their position for personal gain. It's the reason why HR exists and why we have 'hugot' lines about being taken for granted.
usage_notes: A very common word in legal, social, and personal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **abuso** sa kapangyarihan ay isang malubhang krimen.","translation":"The **abuse** of power is a serious crime."},{"sentence":"Dumanas siya ng maraming **abuso** sa kamay ng kanyang mga kaaway.","translation":"He experienced a lot of **abuse** at the hands of his enemies."}]

translation: to extend a greeting; to greet on behalf of
meaning_filipino: Magpaabot o magbigay ng pagbati sa isang tao, kadalasan para sa ibang tao o sa isang okasyon.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'Hi, po!' or 'Good morning, ma'am/sir!' It's what you do when you see a familiar face, or when a radio DJ gives a shoutout. 'Gusto ko lang ibati ang lahat ng nakikinig!' It's the verbal equivalent of a friendly wave or a nod, often done as a proxy: 'Pakibati ako sa kanya' means 'Say hi to him/her for me'.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa anyong pautos (ibati mo) upang magpasabi ng pagbati sa pamamagitan ng ibang tao. Ang 'batiin' ay mas direktang pagbati sa isang tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **ibati** mo ako sa iyong mga magulang pag-uwi mo.","translation":"Please **greet** your parents for me when you get home."},{"sentence":"Gusto kong **ibati** ng 'Maligayang Kaarawan' ang aking kaibigan sa radyo.","translation":"I want to **extend a greeting** of 'Happy Birthday' to my friend on the radio."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang magsagawa ng biglaan at marahas na pagsalakay o pag-atake sa isang lugar o grupo ng mga tao.
original_explanation: This is more than just a simple 'atake'. Think of pirates raiding a village, or your immune system fighting off a virus. In a modern sense, it's what happens when a rival company launches a massive, aggressive marketing campaign to steal your customers. It's an all-out assault.
usage_notes: Implies a sudden, forceful, and often collective attack. It has a historical or military feel.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghanda ang mga mandirigma upang **manalakay** sa kampo ng kaaway.","translation":"The warriors prepared **to attack** the enemy's camp."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng hindi pagiging abala o kawalan ng anumang kasalukuyang aktibidad.
etymology: Mula sa "wala" (none) at "ginagawa" (doing), ang kasalukuyang anyo ng pandiwang "gawin".
original_explanation: The default status of a *tambay*. It's you, right now, scrolling on your phone instead of working. It's that moment at work between tasks where you just stare into space. It's not necessarily boredom, it's just a state of... existing. Your boss might call it "unproductive," you call it "conserving energy."
usage_notes: Very similar to 'walang-gagawin', but this emphasizes the current state ('doing nothing') while 'walang-gagawin' can refer to a future state ('nothing to do').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita ko siyang nakaupo lang at **walang-ginagawa**.","translation":"I saw him just sitting and **doing nothing**."},{"sentence":"Masarap matulog kapag malamig ang panahon at **walang-ginagawa**.","translation":"It's nice to sleep when the weather is cold and you're **doing nothing**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na nasubukan na at napatunayang epektibo, totoo, o may kalidad.
original_explanation: This is the 'Subok na Matibay' seal of approval. When someone says a product, a method, or even a person is probado, it means they've been through the wringer and came out on top. It's your lola's secret adobo recipe, the 'pamatay-kuto' shampoo from the 90s, or that friend who's always reliable. Probado means it works, period.
usage_notes: Often used in advertising ('Probadong matibay!') and to describe something with a good track record.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tatak na ito ay **probado** na at matibay.","translation":"This brand is **proven** and durable."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang katapatan ay **probado** na sa maraming pagkakataon.","translation":"His loyalty has been **proven** on many occasions."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa isang laro o sugal, ito ang taong namamahala sa pusta o salapi ng lahat ng manlalaro; ang bangka.
original_explanation: In the context of Filipino games, the **banker** isn't the guy in a suit at BDO. He's the one holding all the cash in a game of "tong-its" or "pusoy dos." The **banker** is the house, the dealer, the one you need to beat to take home the pot. Losing to the banker feels like getting a low credit score.
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of gambling and card games, not professional banking. The term 'bangka' is a more common local equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang laging taya bilang **banker** sa aming laro ng baraha.","translation":"He always takes the role of the **banker** in our card game."},{"sentence":"Natalo ang lahat ng manlalaro sa **banker** kagabi.","translation":"All the players lost to the **banker** last night."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao, lalo na sa isang lalaki, na kumikilos o nag-iisip nang mas maaga sa inaasahan; maaari ring tumukoy sa bayad na ibinigay nang pauna.
original_explanation: The male version of 'adelantada'. He's the guy who plans the one-year anniversary trip on the first date. He's also the one who gets a cash advance from the office ATM five minutes after the payroll is credited. Basically, living in the future, for better or for worse.
usage_notes: Masculine counterpart to 'adelantada'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **adelantado** sa mga plano mo, baka hindi matuloy.","translation":"Don't be too **advanced/forward** with your plans, they might not push through."},{"sentence":"Laging **adelantado** ang suweldo niya kaya laging kapos.","translation":"His salary is always taken in **advance**, that's why he's always short on cash."}]

translation: to disturb; to trouble; to cause anxiety
meaning_filipino: Ang pagdudulot ng pagkabalisa, pag-aalala, o kawalan ng kapayapaan sa isip o damdamin ng isang tao.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'bagabag', na nangangahulugang ligalig o balisa.
original_explanation: That feeling you get at 3 AM when you remember an embarrassing thing you did in high school. It's when your conscience, or a "seen" message with no reply, starts to haunt you. "Binabagabag ng konsensya" is the classic Pinoy drama trope.
usage_notes: Often used to describe being troubled by one's conscience ("binabagabag ng konsensya").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi kita **babagabagin** sa iyong pagpapahinga.","translation":"Don't worry, I will not **disturb** you during your rest."},{"sentence":"Tila **binabagabag** siya ng kanyang mga problema sa trabaho.","translation":"It seems he is **being troubled** by his problems at work."}]

meaning_filipino: Pag-isipan nang mabuti o bigyan ng pansin ang isang bagay bago gumawa ng desisyon.
original_explanation: What you tell your friend to do before they text their ex at 2 AM. "Girl, konsiderahin mo muna!" It means to think it over, weigh the options, and maybe check your bank account before adding to cart. It's the brain's "pause" button.
usage_notes: A command or suggestion to think about something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **konsiderahin** mo ang aking alok.","translation":"Please, **consider** my offer."},{"sentence":"Dapat nating **konsiderahin** ang lahat ng anggulo bago tayo magpasya.","translation":"We should **consider** all angles before we decide."}]

translation: to use a container to catch something
meaning_filipino: Gamitin ang isang sisidlan o lalagyan upang saluhin ang isang bagay na bumabagsak o umaagos, karaniwan ay likido.
original_explanation: When there's a leak in the ceiling and you put a "balde" (pail) under it, you are "isinahod mo ang balde." It's the act of positioning a container to catch something, like catching rainwater or your own tears after watching a sad K-drama.
usage_notes: The root "sahod" also means salary, but this verb form is completely unrelated and refers to catching/collecting. The context makes the meaning clear.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha siya ng timba upang **isahod** sa tumutulong tubig mula sa bubong.","translation":"He got a pail to **use to catch** the dripping water from the roof."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsuutin ng salawal ang isang tao, karaniwang tumutukoy sa pagbibihis sa isang bata o sa taong nangangailangan ng tulong.
original_explanation: This is the action of putting pants or underwear on someone else. It’s what parents do for their toddlers every morning. "Bebe, wait lang, salawalan ka muna ni Mommy." It's a very specific verb for a very specific (and often chaotic) parenting moment.
usage_notes: Primarily used when dressing another person, not oneself. The verb for dressing oneself is 'magsalawal'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan mong **salawalan** ang iyong nakababatang kapatid.","translation":"Help **put pants on** your younger sibling."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ko munang **salawalan** ang bata bago kami umalis.","translation":"I need to **put pants on** the child first before we leave."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng malalim na pagkalito, pagkaligalig, o kawalan ng katiyakan sa isip.
original_explanation: This is the feeling you get when you're trying to assemble IKEA furniture without the manual, or when your crush gives you mixed signals. It's not just simple confusion; it's a deep, 'my brain has stopped working' level of bewilderment. Yung para kang nag-blue screen.
usage_notes: A deeper and more profound state of confusion than the more common 'kalituhan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bakas sa kanyang mukha ang **kagulumihanan** habang pinakikinggan ang kumplikadong paliwanag.","translation":"**Perplexity** was visible on his face while listening to the complicated explanation."},{"sentence":"Ang misteryo ay nag-iwan ng **kagulumihanan** sa mga imbestigador.","translation":"The mystery left the investigators in a state of **bewilderment**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang hiram mula sa Ingles na tumutukoy sa bilang na "isa" o ginagamit bilang pantukoy para sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: The ultimate Taglish filler word. 'Can you give me *one* piece of chicken?' when 'isa' is just too much effort. Also used in a very *colegiala* accent, like, 'It's so hard to find *one* good coffee shop, *diba*?'
usage_notes: Primarily used in Taglish contexts, often interchangeably with 'isa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pahingi naman ng **one** paper, please.","translation":"Can I have **one** (piece of) paper, please."},{"sentence":"Bigyan mo ako ng **one** more chance.","translation":"Give me **one** more chance."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na kopya o modelo ng isang mas malaking bagay; anumang bagay na napakaliit sa sukat.
original_explanation: A tiny version of something big. Like those little jeepney souvenirs, Gundam models, or the travel-size bottle of your favorite shampoo. It’s for things that are so cute because they're smol. 'Ang cute, parang minyatura ng totoong bahay!'
usage_notes: Maaari ring gamitin bilang pang-uri (hal., 'isang minyaturang hardin').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May koleksyon siya ng mga **minyatura** ng iba't ibang sikat na gusali.","translation":"He has a collection of **miniatures** of different famous buildings."},{"sentence":"Gumawa siya ng **minyatura** ng kanilang bahay-kubo para sa proyekto.","translation":"She made a **miniature** of their nipa hut for a project."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng hindi pag-ako sa mga tungkulin, obligasyon, o sa resulta ng sariling kilos.
etymology: Mula sa `ka-` + `wala` + `-an` (kawalan, "lack of"), `ng` ("of"), at `pananagutan` (responsibility), na mula sa ugat na `sagot` (answer).
original_explanation: This is that classic "It's not my fault" energy. 'Yung nag-group project kayo pero isa lang gumawa, tapos 'yung iba, "Sorry, busy eh." That's kawalan ng pananagutan. It's ghosting your responsibilities, whether it's in the office, at home, or sa G-chat. The adult version of "the dog ate my homework."
usage_notes: Isang pormal na parirala na madalas gamitin sa legal, etikal, o propesyonal na konteksto upang tukuyin ang pag-iwas sa obligasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kawalan ng pananagutan** ng ilang opisyal ang nagpalala sa krisis.","translation":"The **irresponsibility** of some officials worsened the crisis."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya matanggap ang paratang na nagpapakita siya ng **kawalan ng pananagutan** sa kanyang pamilya.","translation":"He could not accept the accusation that he was showing a **lack of accountability** to his family."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang empleyado ng bangko na direktang nakikipag-ugnayan sa mga kliyente para sa mga transaksyon tulad ng pagdeposito at pag-withdraw ng pera.
original_explanation: Sila yung mga ate at kuya sa bangko na laging nakangiti (kahit pagod na) at nagbibilang ng sandamukal na pera. Sila ang hahanapin mo para mag-deposit ng sweldo o mag-withdraw ng pambayad ng bills. Pro tip: Maging mabait sa kanila, baka may free ballpen.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng pagbabangko.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahaba ang pila sa **teller** tuwing araw ng sahod.","translation":"The line at the **teller** is long during payday."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong mag-withdraw ng pera, kaya pupunta ako sa **teller**.","translation":"I need to withdraw money, so I'll go to the **teller**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos o kalagayan ng sabay na pagtatampo ng dalawa o higit pang tao sa isa't isa.
original_explanation: This is 'tampo' in multiplayer mode. 'Pag ikaw at ang jowa mo ay parehong may tampo at naghihintayan kung sino ang unang susuyo. Isang cold war ng silent treatment at pag-iwas. Ang bahay ay nagiging demilitarized zone. Usually ends when one person gets hungry and asks, "Kakain na ba tayo?"
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa kilos o estado ng 'tampo' na ginagawa ng magkabilang panig.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Normal lang sa magkaibigan ang magkaroon ng kaunting **tampuhan**.","translation":"It's normal for friends to have a bit of **mutual sulking**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang trabaho ay ang mag-ulat ng mga pangyayari at impormasyon sa publiko, karaniwan sa telebisyon, radyo, o pahayagan.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "tagapag-" (doer/agent of action) at sa salitang ugat na "balita" (news).
original_explanation: The person on TV or radio who tells you why there's traffic, who won the basketball game, or what the latest political chismis is. Before social media influencers, they were the OGs.
usage_notes: Madalas na tumutukoy sa mga propesyonal sa midya. Ginagamit din ang "mamamahayag" (journalist) o "reporter."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala ang **tagapagbalita** sa kaniyang matapang na pag-uulat tungkol sa gobyerno.","translation":"The **newscaster** is known for his brave reporting on the government."},{"sentence":"Nais niyang maging isang **tagapagbalita** paglaki niya.","translation":"She wants to become a **news reporter** when she grows up."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na likas na mahilig magtanong, mag-usisa, o magsiyasat tungkol sa mga bagay-bagay.
etymology: From the affix 'pala-' (indicating fondness or habit) + 'tanong' (question).
original_explanation: That one officemate in a meeting who keeps asking questions, making the whole thing 30 minutes longer. Also, your 5-year-old pamangkin who won't stop asking 'Bakit?' about everything from the sky to your love life. The human question mark.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a curious person, sometimes with a slightly negative connotation if the questions are seen as excessive or nosy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala si Jose sa klase bilang isang batang **palatanungan** at laging nagtataas ng kamay.","translation":"Jose is known in class as an **inquisitive** child who always raises his hand."},{"sentence":"Magingat sa pagsagot dahil **palatanungan** ang reporter na iinterbyu sa iyo.","translation":"Be careful with your answers because the reporter who will interview you is **inquisitive**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalaro gamit ang mga baraha, tulad ng sa mga larong pusoy, tong-its, o poker.
original_explanation: What Filipinos do during a wake (`lamay`), a family reunion, or just to kill time on a lazy afternoon. To `magbaraha` is to break out a deck of cards. It could be a friendly game of 'tong-its' with your titos, 'pusoy dos' with your barkada, or 'solitaire' when you're bored at home. Just be ready for the 'daya' accusations and the flying tsinelas if the stakes get too high.
usage_notes: A general term for playing any game that involves a deck of playing cards.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing hapon, nagkikita-kita ang magkakaibigan para **magbaraha** sa tindahan ni Aling Nena.","translation":"Every afternoon, the friends meet up to **play cards** at Aling Nena's store."},{"sentence":"Magdamag silang **nagbaraha** sa burol ng kanilang yumaong kaibigan.","translation":"They **played cards** all night at the wake of their deceased friend."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marahan at magiliw na paghaplos o pagdampi, karaniwang gamit ang palad, bilang pagpapakita ng pagmamahal o pag-aalaga.
original_explanation: This is that gentle, comforting stroke you give your pet cat or dog. It's the "good boy" pat. It's what you do to a baby's back to lull them to sleep. It's softer than a 'haplos' and definitely not a 'hilot'. Think less therapeutic, more affectionate. It's the physical version of saying "there, there."
usage_notes: Connotes gentleness and affection.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **himas** ng ina sa kanyang anak ay nakapagpatahan dito.","translation":"The mother's **caress** of her child calmed him down."},{"sentence":"Gustong-gusto ng aso ko ang **himas** sa kanyang ulo.","translation":"My dog really loves a **pet** on its head."}]

translation: to sprout, to emerge, to spring up
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtubo o paglitaw ng isang bagay, tulad ng halaman mula sa lupa, o ang pagsisimula ng isang ideya, damdamin, o kilusan.
original_explanation: This is what happens to new milk tea shops every week. Bigla na lang umusbong sa bawat kanto. It's also what happened to your feelings for your workmate after that one team-building event. Oops.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umusbong** ang mga bagong dahon pagkatapos ng ulan.","translation":"New leaves **sprouted** after the rain."},{"sentence":"Isang bagong pag-asa ang **umusbong** sa kanyang puso.","translation":"A new hope **emerged** in his/her heart."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahabang guhit o uka sa lupa na likha ng araro. Sa peryodismo, ito ay isang espasyo sa pahayagan o magasin para sa isang regular na manunulat o paksa.
original_explanation: A 'tudling' is a line. If you're a farmer, it's the furrow your carabao just plowed. If you're a writer, it's your newspaper column where you spill all the 'chismis' (or 'political commentary'). It's your dedicated space to make your mark, whether in soil or in print.
usage_notes: Has two primary, distinct meanings: one in agriculture (furrow) and one in journalism (column). The context usually makes the meaning clear.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga magsasaka ay gumagawa ng **tudling** sa bukid para pagtamnan ng mais.","translation":"The farmers are making **furrows** in the field to plant corn."},{"sentence":"Binabasa ko palagi ang kanyang **tudling** sa diyaryo tuwing Linggo.","translation":"I always read his **column** in the newspaper every Sunday."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi ang pinakamataas na uri o kalidad; pangalawa sa ranggo o kategorya.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung feeling na hindi ka priority. Parang option ka lang, hindi ka 'yung choice. Sa bus, ito 'yung non-aircon. Sa produkto, ito 'yung may konting depekto pero pwede pa. Sa feelings, ito 'yung "mahal ka niya, pero mas mahal niya 'yung isa." Aray. Never settle for being treated like segunda klase.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin upang ilarawan ang mga produkto, serbisyo, o kahit ang pagtrato sa isang tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayokong maramdaman na parang **segunda klase** lang akong mamamayan sa sarili kong bansa.","translation":"I don't want to feel like a **second-class** citizen in my own country."}]

meaning_filipino: Nag-aastang parang hari; mapagmalupit o mayabang sa paggamit ng kapangyarihan, lalo na kung limitado ito.
etymology: From 'hari' (king) + '-an' suffix, with reduplication, indicating imitation or pretense.
original_explanation: That one security guard at the mall entrance who acts like he owns the place. Or your team lead who goes on a power trip. It's someone who's not the real 'hari' but acts like it, often in an annoying or oppressive way. It’s the classic 'big fish in a small pond' syndrome.
usage_notes: Carries a negative connotation of being a petty, arrogant, or domineering person in a limited scope of authority. Can also function as a noun ('isang hari-harian').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw ng mga empleyado sa manager nila dahil sa ugali niyang **hari-harian**.","translation":"The employees dislike their manager because of his **tyrannical** attitude."},{"sentence":"Nag-aasal **hari-harian** na naman ang kapitan ng barangay.","translation":"The barangay captain is **acting like a king** again."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong laging sumusunod sa pinakabagong uso o istilo sa pananamit at iba pang bagay.
etymology: Mula sa `pala-` (unlaping nagsasaad ng hilig) + `sunod` + `sa` + `moda` (mula sa Espanyol na 'moda').
original_explanation: Ito yung friend mo na laging 'in'. Kung ano ang latest sa TikTok, sa K-Drama, o sa runway, suot niya na agad. Sila yung unang nag-crop top, unang nag-mom jeans ulit, at unang naka-discover ng 'quiet luxury'. Basically, a walking fashion magazine.
usage_notes: Isang tambalang pariralang naglalarawan. Ang unlaping 'pala-' dito ay nagpapahiwatig ng hilig o ugali.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala si Anne bilang isang taong **palasunod sa moda**.","translation":"Anne is known as someone who is very **fashionable**."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko kayang maging **palasunod sa moda** dahil magastos ito.","translation":"I can't afford to be **trendy** because it's expensive."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang kilos na nagpapacute, parang sanggol, o nag-iinarte sa isang paraan na maaaring ituring na kaakit-akit o nakakainis.
etymology: From `pa-` (to act like) + `bebe` (from English 'baby'). A modern coinage popularized by social media.
original_explanation: The OG "pick me girl" energy before it was a thing. It's that high-pitched, trying-to-be-cute voice that makes you either go "Awww" or "Ugh, stop." Think of the "pabebe wave" that went viral. It's an art form of calculated cuteness, often seen in social media posts with lots of filters. "Wag kang pabebe" is the Filipino equivalent of "stop being so extra."
usage_notes: Can be used affectionately or as a mild insult, depending on the tone and context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan mo nga 'yang boses mong **pabebe**.","translation":"Stop it with your **cutesy** voice."},{"sentence":"Sumikat ang **pabebe** girls dahil sa kanilang viral video.","translation":"The **pabebe** girls became famous because of their viral video."}]

translation: to touch lightly; to feel with the hands
meaning_filipino: Ang marahang pagdampi o paghawak sa isang bagay o tao, karaniwan gamit ang kamay, upang ito ay maramdaman.
original_explanation: This is what you do at the ukay-ukay to check the fabric quality ("Prada ba to?"). It's also that gentle, "paramdam" touch that gives you kilig, or a creepy touch that makes you say "Don't me." Context is everything. It's a touch with intention.
usage_notes: Can have a gentle, curious connotation or a negative, inappropriate one depending on the context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bawal **humipo** sa mga artipakto sa loob ng museo.","translation":"It is forbidden to **touch** the artifacts inside the museum."},{"sentence":"Marahan siyang **humipo** sa tela upang alamin kung ito ay malambot.","translation":"She lightly **touched** the fabric to see if it was soft."}]

translation: to be from the same town/country
meaning_filipino: Parehong nagmula sa iisang bayan, lalawigan, o bansa.
original_explanation: That magical moment when you're abroad, you hear someone speaking Tagalog, and you instantly become best friends. "Uy, Pinoy ka?" That's the power of being **magkababayan**. You share a common origin, a secret language (in a foreign land), and an unspoken understanding about the superiority of Jollibee.
usage_notes: Often used to describe people from the same locality or country meeting each other. The noun form is 'kababayan' (compatriot).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nalaman kong **magkababayan** pala kami nang marinig ko siyang magsalita ng Ilokano.","translation":"I found out we were **from the same province** when I heard him speak Ilocano."},{"sentence":"Nagulat si Manny Pacquiao at ang kanyang kalaban na sila pala ay **magkababayan** sa General Santos.","translation":"Manny Pacquiao and his opponent were surprised to find out they were **from the same town** of General Santos."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pundamental na batas o saligang batas ng isang bansa o organisasyon na nagtatakda ng mga prinsipyo, kapangyarihan, at tungkulin ng pamahalaan.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung pinaka-ultimate rulebook ng buong Pilipinas. Parang "Terms and Conditions" ng bansa na hindi mo pwedeng i-skip at i-click na lang ang "Agree". Dito nakasulat lahat ng karapatan mo, pati na rin ang limits ng gobyerno.
usage_notes: Often referred to as 'Saligang Batas'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang karapatan sa malayang pamamahayag ay ginagarantiyahan ng ating **konstitusyon**.","translation":"The right to free speech is guaranteed by our **constitution**."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan sa klase sa Araling Panlipunan ang **Konstitusyon** ng 1987.","translation":"The 1987 **Constitution** is being studied in Social Studies class."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahabang upuan, karaniwang yari sa kahoy o metal, na maaaring upuan ng dalawa o higit pang tao.
original_explanation: That thing you sit on sa plaza while waiting for your jowa na laging late, or where titas gather to start the daily chismis marathon. Pwede ring sa loob ng jeep, 'yung mahabang upuan.
usage_notes: Ito ay tumutukoy sa isang upuan. Mayroon itong katunog na salita na nangangahulugang 'institusyong pampinansyal'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umupo kami sa **bangko** sa ilalim ng puno ng mangga.","translation":"We sat on the **bench** under the mango tree."},{"sentence":"Puno na ang mga **bangko** sa parke.","translation":"The **benches** in the park are already full."}]

translation: Exposed; laid bare; lying on one's back
meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng pagiging lantad, walang takip, o nakahiga na ang likod ang nasa ibaba.
original_explanation: Yung position mo sa kama kapag pagod na pagod ka from work, staring at the ceiling and contemplating your life choices. It's being completely exposed, like leaving your Facebook profile public or when your friend reveals your secret crush to everyone. Vulnerable, bes.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa pisikal na posisyon (nakahiga nang patihaya) o sa matalinhagang pagiging lantad.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatulog siyang **hayang** sa sahig dahil sa pagod.","translation":"He fell asleep **lying on his back** on the floor due to exhaustion."},{"sentence":"**Hayang** na ang kanyang mga lihim sa lahat.","translation":"His secrets are now **exposed** to everyone."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na lalagyan para sa tinta, karaniwang ginagamit kasama ng panulat na isinasawsaw.
original_explanation: The old-school version of a printer cartridge. It's that small pot of ink you see in historical movies where people dip their feather quills. Think Jose Rizal writing his novels. Today, it's more of a vintage desk accessory or something a calligrapher would use.
usage_notes: An old-fashioned term, but still understood, especially in historical or literary contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroon pa siyang lumang **tintero** na pamana mula sa kanyang lolo.","translation":"He still has an old **inkwell** inherited from his grandfather."},{"sentence":"Isinawsaw niya ang pluma sa **tintero** bago nagsimulang sumulat.","translation":"He dipped the quill in the **inkwell** before starting to write."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kusang-loob na pagkilos o paggawa ng isang bagay nang hindi inuutusan o hinihilingan.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung "proactive" sa corporate world. 'Yung ikaw na mismo ang naghugas ng pinagkainan kahit hindi mo turn, o 'yung nag-volunteer ka sa isang project na walang dagdag-sahod. It's doing something out of your own free will, hopefully for a good reason and not just to be a 'pabida'.
usage_notes: A highly valued trait in Filipino culture, often associated with helpfulness ('pagtulong') and responsibility.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinuri ng guro ang **pagkukusa** ng mag-aaral na linisin ang silid-aralan.","translation":"The teacher praised the student's **initiative** to clean the classroom."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang alternatibong baybay o katawagan para sa balumbalunan, ang panloob na organo ng mga ibon na pandurog ng pagkain.
original_explanation: This is just another way to say `balumbalunan` (gizzard). It's like the difference between "soda" and "pop," or "elevator" and "lift." Same chewy, delicious chicken part, different spelling. Your lola from a different province might call it this.
usage_notes: Less common than `balumbalunan` but understood in the same context. The 'm' sound is often replaced with 'n' in some regional dialects or by assimilation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap isahog sa pansit ang hiniwang **balun-balunan**.","translation":"It's delicious to add sliced **gizzard** to noodles."},{"sentence":"Magkano ang isang kilo ng **balun-balunan** sa palengke?","translation":"How much is one kilo of **gizzards** at the market?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang umbok o pamamaga sa ibabaw ng balat o sa isang bagay, na karaniwang sanhi ng pagkabagok, sakit, o depekto.
original_explanation: That thing that magically appears on your forehead after walking into a glass door or when you accidentally hit your head on the jeepney's ceiling. Also, 'yung 'bukol' sa wallet mo 'pag bagong sahod, na dahan-dahang nawawala bago mag-petsa de peligro.
usage_notes: Can refer to a bump on the body, a lump in a surface, or metaphorically to something that sticks out or is bulging.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon siya ng malaking **bukol** sa noo nang mauntog siya.","translation":"He got a big **bump** on his forehead when he hit his head."},{"sentence":"May **bukol** sa kalsada kaya mag-ingat sa pagmamaneho.","translation":"There's a **lump** on the road, so be careful when driving."}]

translation: to use as motivation; to use to entice
meaning_filipino: Gamitin bilang pampasigla, pang-akit, o pampukaw ng interes upang kumilos ang isang tao.
original_explanation: This is your 'why'. The bonus you're working towards, the beach trip you're saving up for, or the 'para sa pamilya' mantra that gets you through a tough day at your BPO shift. It's the reason, the carrot on the stick, the thing you use to motivate yourself or someone else. 'Ang pangarap kong magkaroon ng sariling bahay ang ipinanggaganyak ko sa aking sarili.'
usage_notes: Refers to the specific thing (an idea, a reward, a person) used as the source of motivation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ng guro ang mga premyo para **ipangganyak** sa mga mag-aaral na mag-aral nang mabuti.","translation":"The teacher used prizes **to motivate** the students to study well."},{"sentence":"Ang kinabukasan ng kanyang mga anak ang kanyang **ipinanggaganyak** sa pagtatrabaho sa abroad.","translation":"His children's future is what he **uses as motivation** for working abroad."}]

translation: to have something moved back; to cause to retreat
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-utos o pagsasanhi na igalaw paatras ang isang bagay o tao; ang pag-udyok sa isang tao na umurong o bawiin ang isang desisyon.
original_explanation: When you're directing a car backing into a tight parking spot, you shout "Urong! Urong pa!". The driver is the one who 'umuurong', but you are the one who tells them to 'magpaurong'. It can also be used for plans: "Huwag kang magpaurong sa pangarap mo dahil lang sa sinabi niya." (Don't let them make you back down from your dream).
usage_notes: Can be literal (moving an object) or figurative (changing a decision).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **magpaurong** ka ng kaunti sa sasakyan mo para makadaan ako.","translation":"Please, **have your car moved back** a little so I can pass."},{"sentence":"Hindi siya nagtagumpay na **magpaurong** sa akin sa laban.","translation":"He did not succeed in **making me withdraw** from the fight."}]

meaning_filipino: Kinikilala, may-bisa, o katanggap-tanggap ayon sa batas, patakaran, o lohika.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung status ng ID mo na hindi pa expired. O 'yung rason mo sa pag-absent sa work na tinanggap ng boss mo. O 'yung feelings mo na "gets" ng kaibigan mo ("Your feelings are valid!"). In short, it's legit, it counts, it's acceptable. Kung hindi balido, it's either fake, expired, or just plain 'di uubra.
usage_notes: Interchangeable with the English word "valid" in Taglish conversations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi na **balido** ang iyong lisensya dahil paso na ito.","translation":"Your license is no longer **valid** because it is expired."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mo ng **balido** na dahilan para payagan kang umalis.","translation":"You need a **valid** reason to be allowed to leave."}]

meaning_filipino: Ipagtanggol o protektahan ang isang tao, karapatan, o prinsipyo laban sa anumang panganib, atake, o pinsala.
etymology: From i- (object focus prefix) + pag- + sanggalang (shield, protection).
original_explanation: This is your "I will fight for you" moment. It's what lawyers do for their clients, what activists do for a cause, and what you do when someone talks trash about your favorite K-pop group. "Handa kong ipagsanggalang ang karapatan nating mag-ingay!"
usage_notes: A formal and strong word for "defend". It carries a sense of righteousness and is often used for abstract concepts like rights and freedom, not just physical defense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tungkulin ng bawat mamamayan na **ipagsanggalang** ang kalayaan ng bansa.","translation":"It is the duty of every citizen to **defend** the nation's freedom."},{"sentence":"Palagi niyang **ipagsasanggalang** ang kanyang mga kaibigan kahit anong mangyari.","translation":"He will always **protect** his friends no matter what happens."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bukas na bahagi sa dingding ng isang gusali o sasakyan na karaniwang may salamin, upang makapasok ang liwanag at hangin, at upang tanawin ang labas.
etymology: From `dungaw` (to look out/down from a height) + `-an` suffix, forming a noun for a place.
original_explanation: This is the old-school, poetic, Maria Clara-era word for "bintana" (window). You don't just look out of a `durungawan`, you gaze wistfully from it, waiting for your haranista. It's the window in Noli Me Tángere, not the sliding window in your condo. Think capiz shells and wooden frames. It comes from `dungaw` (to look out).
usage_notes: Considered archaic or literary. 'Bintana' is the common word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumisilip ang dalaga sa **durungawan** habang naghihintay sa kanyang manliligaw.","translation":"The young lady peeks through the **window** while waiting for her suitor."},{"sentence":"Ang disenyo ng lumang bahay ay may malalaking **durungawan**.","translation":"The design of the old house has large **windows**."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paraang nagkukunwari o umaakma lamang na kumikilos; hindi tunay na pagkilos.
etymology: From pa- (denoting manner or pretense) + kilos (movement).
original_explanation: It's that move you do when your boss walks by your desk—you suddenly look super busy, clicking and typing furiously at nothing. It's the "I'm doing something, promise!" performance. Also used to describe a fake-out in basketball or when a cat pretends to pounce. It’s motion without real intention.
usage_notes: Often implies pretense or a half-hearted motion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pakilos** siyang tumayo na para bang aalis na, ngunit umupo rin kaagad.","translation":"He stood up **as if to leave**, but immediately sat down again."},{"sentence":"Nagulat ang pusa sa **pakilos** kong pag-abot sa kanya.","translation":"The cat was startled by my **feigned motion** of reaching for it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halaman na may matigas at makahoy na katawan, mga sanga, at dahon; isang kasingkahulugan ng 'puno'.
original_explanation: A more formal or specific way to say 'tree'. 'Puno' can mean tree, trunk, or chief, but 'punong-kahoy' *always* means tree. It's what you'd write in a school essay about the environment to sound more knowledgeable. Literally "tree of wood".
usage_notes: A more descriptive synonym for 'puno' (tree). Although it seems redundant, it's commonly used to specifically refer to a tree.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming ibon ang namumugad sa matandang **punong-kahoy** na iyon.","translation":"Many birds are nesting in that old **tree**."},{"sentence":"Bawal pumutol ng **punong-kahoy** nang walang pahintulot.","translation":"It is forbidden to cut down a **tree** without a permit."}]

meaning_filipino: Takpan o ipinid ang isang bukana, siwang, o daanan.
original_explanation: The OG command to prevent lamok from entering the house or to stop your sibling from eavesdropping. 'Isara mo ang pinto!' It also applies to closing a shop for the day, closing your mouth ('pag may nasabi kang mali), or closing a bank account ('pag wala nang laman). The opposite of 'open.' Duh.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **isara** ang bintana bago umalis.","translation":"Don't forget to **close** the window before you leave."},{"sentence":"**Isinara** na ang tindahan para sa araw na ito.","translation":"The store has been **closed** for the day."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagtataksil o pagiging hindi tapat sa isang tao, pangkat, o sa sariling bayan.
etymology: From 'taksil' (traitor) + '-an' suffix, denoting an act or quality.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'saksak sa likod' moment. It's when your best friend dates your ex, or your groupmate submits the project without your name on it. It’s the plot of every teleserye ever. The highest level of 'walang-hiya'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya mapapatawad ang **kataksilan** ng kanyang kaibigan.","translation":"She cannot forgive her friend's **betrayal**."},{"sentence":"Ang paniniktik para sa kaaway ay isang malaking **kataksilan** sa bayan.","translation":"Spying for the enemy is a great act of **treason** against the country."}]

meaning_filipino: Sira, gupo, o nasira nang lubusan; walang kaayusan.
original_explanation: Can refer to a thing (like a phone after you drop it) or a feeling (like your heart after watching a sad K-drama). "Wasak na ang phone ko!" (My phone is wrecked!). "Wasak ang puso ko." (My heart is broken). It's also used to describe being extremely tired or drunk. "Pagod na pagod ako, wasak na katawan ko." (I'm so tired, my body is destroyed).
usage_notes: A very versatile word describing physical, emotional, or even mental destruction or exhaustion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Wasak** ang bahay pagkatapos ng malakas na lindol.","translation":"The house was **destroyed** after the strong earthquake."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam ko **wasak** ang pagkatao ko pagkatapos ng breakup.","translation":"I feel like my whole being is **wrecked** after the breakup."}]

translation: to make someone believe; to convert someone's faith
meaning_filipino: Hikayatin, pilitin, o himukin ang isang tao na magkaroon ng pananampalataya o maniwala sa isang partikular na doktrina, relihiyon, o ideolohiya.
etymology: From `pa-` (causative prefix) + `sampalataya` (faith) + `-hin` (object-focus verbal suffix). `Sampalataya` is from Sanskrit *sampratyaya* (trust, confidence).
original_explanation: This is the more intense version of "pasambahin." It's not just about making someone pray; it's about making them a full-blown believer. Think of missionaries trying to convert a whole tribe, or that one friend who's super into crypto and is trying to get you to "believe" in the power of Dogecoin. It's about changing someone's core beliefs.
usage_notes: A formal and somewhat profound word, often used in religious or philosophical contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **pasampalatayahin** ang isang taong sarado na ang isip.","translation":"It's difficult to **make** a close-minded person **believe**."},{"sentence":"Layunin ng misyonero na **pasampalatayahin** ang buong komunidad sa kanilang aral.","translation":"The missionary's goal is to **convert** the entire community to their teachings."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng lupi, yupi, o pagkasira paloob, lalo na sa mga bagay na yari sa metal o anumang manipis na materyales, dahil sa pagkabangga o pagkapukpok.
original_explanation: What happens to your car door when a motorcycle sideswipes you in EDSA traffic. Or that sad little dent in your water bottle after you drop it for the nth time. It's the opposite of 'umbok' (bulge). 'Yupi' is the more common term, though.
usage_notes: 'Yupi' is a more frequently used synonym for 'iyok'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Iyok** ang lata ng sardinas kaya hindi ko na binili.","translation":"The sardine can was **dented**, so I didn't buy it anymore."},{"sentence":"Nag-iwan ng **iyok** sa pinto ng kotse ang tumamang bato.","translation":"The rock that hit it left a **dent** on the car door."}]

meaning_filipino: Binubuo ng maraming magkakaugnay na bahagi o aspekto na mahirap unawain, lutasin, o ipaliwanag.
original_explanation: Your relationship status on Facebook. Yung pag-commute sa EDSA rush hour. Yung instructions para i-assemble ang bagong bili mong furniture. In short, 'It's komplikado.'
usage_notes: Often used to describe situations, relationships, or problems.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **komplikado** ang sitwasyon dahil sa biglaang pag-ulan.","translation":"The situation became **complicated** because of the sudden rain."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang gawing **komplikado** ang simpleng problema.","translation":"Don't make a simple problem **complicated**."}]

translation: to have one's head lice removed
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapahintulot sa ibang tao na alisin ang mga kuto sa iyong buhok.
etymology: From `magpa-` (causative prefix) + `hinguto` (to delouse). The root `hinguto` itself is likely a portmanteau of `hanap` (to look for) and `kuto` (louse).
original_explanation: A classic Filipino bonding activity, right up there with sharing chismis over merienda. This is when you ask your nanay, lola, or tita to hunt for lice in your hair, usually while watching a noontime show. It's an intimate, slightly itchy, but oddly satisfying ritual from many Filipino childhoods. 'Nay, pwede po **magpahinguto**?'
usage_notes: A very specific cultural practice. The verb 'hinguto' means to delouse someone, while 'magpahinguto' means to be the one having their lice removed by another person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing hapon, **nagpapahinguto** si Ana sa kanyang ina sa ilalim ng puno ng mangga.","translation":"Every afternoon, Ana **has her head lice removed** by her mother under the mango tree."},{"sentence":"Nakakahiya man, kailangan kong **magpahinguto** dahil makati na talaga ang ulo ko.","translation":"Even if it's embarrassing, I need to **have my lice removed** because my head is really itchy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan o sitwasyon kung saan ang kamatayan ay hindi maiiwasan at siguradong mangyayari.
original_explanation: This is what you feel when your mom uses your full name, or when you accidentally send a risky text to the wrong person. It's the feeling of seeing your phone's battery at 1% with no charger in sight. Basically, it's any "It was at this moment he knew... he messed up" scenario. A one-way ticket to disaster.
usage_notes: A dramatic phrase used to describe a situation with no escape or a guaranteed negative, often fatal, outcome.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagtalon mula sa eroplano nang walang parachute ay **tiyak na pagkamatay**.","translation":"Jumping from a plane without a parachute is **certain death**."},{"sentence":"Para sa munting daga, ang makaharap ang gutom na pusa ay **tiyak na pagkamatay**.","translation":"For the little mouse, facing the hungry cat was **certain death**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang permanenteng pagtigil ng lahat ng mahahalagang tungkulin ng buhay sa isang organismo; pumanaw.
original_explanation: The ultimate "log out" from life. Pwede rin sa bagay, like 'yung phone mong namatay kasi low-batt, or 'yung apoy na namatay dahil sa ulan. It's the final state of being "wala na." More direct than "sumakabilang-buhay."
usage_notes: Pangnagdaang anyo. Maaaring tumukoy sa mga tao, hayop, halaman, o kahit na mga bagay na tumigil sa paggana (hal. apoy, makina). Ang 'pumanaw' o 'sumakabilang-buhay' ay mas pormal at magalang na kasingkahulugan para sa mga tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Namatay** ang kanyang alagang aso noong isang linggo.","translation":"His pet dog **died** last week."},{"sentence":"Biglang **namatay** ang ilaw dahil sa brownout.","translation":"The light suddenly **went out** because of the brownout."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng bulaklak na may maputi at mabangong talulot, kilala rin bilang sampagita, na siyang pambansang bulaklak ng Pilipinas.
original_explanation: The flower of the Philippines! It's that fragrant white flower they string together and sell outside churches or hang on the rearview mirror of jeepneys. It's the scent of piety, welcome garlands, and car fresheners, all rolled into one. It is botanically the same as sampaguita.
usage_notes: A synonym for 'sampagita,' though 'sampagita' is more commonly used. 'Kampupot' is often used in more literary or poetic contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bango ng kwintas ng **kampupot** na nakasabit sa altar.","translation":"The necklace of **Arabian jasmine** hanging on the altar smells so fragrant."},{"sentence":"Pumitas siya ng **kampupot** sa kanilang hardin.","translation":"She picked some **Arabian jasmine** from their garden."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng isang ari-arian na ipinagkatiwala bilang kolateral o garantiya para sa isang utang.
original_explanation: This is the official status of your laptop during "petsa de peligro." You bring your valuable item to a pawnshop ("sanlaan") for some quick cash. The item is now **nakasangla**. It's basically telling your PS5, "See you next sweldo, buddy." A classic Filipino financial hugot move.
usage_notes: The 'naka-' prefix describes the state of the object that has been pawned or mortgaged. The object is temporarily owned by the creditor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakasangla** pa rin ang alahas na minana niya sa kanyang lola.","translation":"The jewelry she inherited from her grandmother is still **pawned**."},{"sentence":"Maraming bahay at lupa ang **nakasangla** sa bangko dahil sa krisis.","translation":"Many houses and lots are **mortgaged** to the bank because of the crisis."}]

meaning_filipino: Sundan ang bakas o linya ng isang bagay; alamin ang pinagmulan o kinaroroonan sa pamamagitan ng pagsunod sa mga palatandaan.
original_explanation: This is what a chismosa does to find the source of the latest gossip. They 'itunton' the story from one person to another until they find Patient Zero. It's also what you do when your WiFi is slow and you try to trace the cable to see if someone unplugged it.
usage_notes: Can be used for physical tracking (like footprints) or abstract tracking (like the source of a problem or information).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng mga pulis na **itunton** ang pinanggalingan ng tawag.","translation":"The police tried to **trace** the origin of the call."},{"sentence":"**Itunton** mo lang ang linya sa mapa upang mahanap ang lokasyon.","translation":"Just **trace** the line on the map to find the location."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapalabas ng hangin mula sa bituka sa pamamagitan ng butas ng puwit.
original_explanation: The sound effect you try to hide in a crowded elevator or during a quiet meeting. When someone umut-ot, it's a classic "suminga ka ba?" moment. It's the silent-but-deadly or the loud-and-proud release of bodily gases. The universal language of awkwardness.
usage_notes: A common, informal word. The more "polite" or clinical term is 'dighay' for burping or just 'naglabas ng hangin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **umut-ot** sa loob ng jeep at lahat ay nagtakip ng ilong.","translation":"Someone **farted** inside the jeep and everyone covered their noses."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang pipigil kung gusto mong **umut-ot**; masama iyan sa katawan.","translation":"Don't hold it in if you want to **fart**; that's bad for the body."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagdudulot ng pakiramdam ng panghihinayang o pagsisisi dahil sa isang nawala o nasayang na pagkakataon, bagay, o pagsisikap.
etymology: From naka- (causative prefix) + panghihinayang (regret), from root sayang (waste, pity).
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na na-miss mo 'yung 12.12 sale para sa item na matagal mo nang tinitingnan. O 'yung ex mong nag-glow up after niyo mag-break. That's a "Sayang!" moment. It's the official emotion of seeing leftover lechon go bad.
usage_notes: Used to describe a situation, action, or object that makes one feel it's a "pity" or a "waste."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakapanghihinayang** ang mga nasirang pagkain dahil sa baha.","translation":"The food that was spoiled because of the flood is **such a waste**."},{"sentence":"**Nakapanghihinayang** isipin na hindi niya tinanggap ang alok na trabaho.","translation":"It's **regrettable** to think that he did not accept the job offer."}]

meaning_filipino: Nakakaramdam o nagpapahayag ng galak, ligaya, at kasiyahan.
original_explanation: The default answer to 'Kamusta ka?' even when you're dying inside. It's the feeling of payday, a surprise Jollibee delivery, long weekends, and seeing your online order finally marked 'Out for Delivery.'
usage_notes: Distinct from 'masayang' (to be wasted), which has a different root ('sayang') and pronunciation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Masaya** ako na makita kang muli.","translation":"I am **happy** to see you again."},{"sentence":"Isang **masaya** at mapagpalang Pasko sa inyong lahat!","translation":"A **happy** and blessed Christmas to you all!"}]

translation: to make someone believe; to convince; to fool
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkumbinsi o paghikayat sa isang tao na tanggapin ang isang bagay bilang totoo, na maaaring may kasamang panlilinlang.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of "gaslighting" or "budol". It's when you try to convince someone of something, whether it's true or not. "Paniwalain mo siya na good investment 'yan," says the friend who's into crypto. It can be used for harmless persuasion or for full-on scamming. The goal is to make them think, "Oo nga 'no!"
usage_notes: `Paniwalain` is a causative verb. It means to *cause* someone to believe. The focus is on the person being made to believe.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpadala sa mga taong susubukang **paniwalain** ka sa mga kasinungalingan.","translation":"Don't be swayed by people who will try to **make you believe** lies."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **paniwalain** ang kanyang ina na nag-aral siya buong gabi, pero nakita ang status niya sa online game.","translation":"He tried to **convince** his mother that he studied all night, but his status on the online game was seen."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapatawad o paglimot sa kasalanan o pagkukulang ng isang tao.
etymology: From "tawad" (discount/pardon) + "-in" suffix, object-focused verb. The concept of "pardon" is extended to forgiveness.
original_explanation: This is the deep, hugot version of the word. When someone messes up badly and they ask you to forgive them, they're asking you to "tawarin" them. It's about letting go of a grudge or a fault. "Mahirap tawarin ang isang kasinungalingan." (It's hard to forgive a lie.)
usage_notes: Synonymous with 'patawarin'. 'Tawarin' can sometimes sound a bit more archaic or poetic in this context, with 'patawarin' being more common for "forgive".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana'y **tawarin** mo ang aking mga pagkakamali.","translation":"I hope you **forgive** my mistakes."},{"sentence":"Ang kasalanang hindi kayang **tawarin** ay yaong inuulit-ulit.","translation":"A sin that cannot be **forgiven** is one that is repeated."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pagkilos na may kasamang paulit-ulit at masiglang paglundag. Ginagamit din bilang paglalarawan sa isang taong pabago-bago ng desisyon o trabaho.
etymology: From pa- prefix + duplicated root lundag. The repetition indicates a continuous, repeated, or non-serious action.
original_explanation: This is you after getting your 13th-month pay. Literally, it's a happy kid on a sugar rush. Figuratively, it's your 'career path' if you've had 5 jobs in 2 years. The movement of a person who can't stay in one place, literally or metaphorically.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for movement or figuratively for someone who frequently changes jobs, ideas, or loyalties ('job-hopper').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Palundag-lundag** sa tuwa ang bata nang matanggap ang regalo.","translation":"The child was **jumping around** in joy upon receiving the gift."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya bilang isang empleyadong **palundag-lundag** ng kumpanya.","translation":"He is known as an employee who is always **hopping from one** company **to another**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pakikipagtalik sa isang tao na hindi mo asawa, lalo na kung ang isa o parehong sangkot ay kasal na sa iba.
etymology: From pakiki- (social participation prefix) + apid (a less common root related to being a concubine or illicit partner).
original_explanation: The formal, almost biblical term for cheating. You won't hear this in a casual chismis session; you'll see it in a legal document or hear it in a fiery sermon. It's the "thou shalt not commit adultery" kind of word. In modern terms, it's the official name for what happens in viral Raffy Tulfo episodes involving a third party.
usage_notes: A very formal and serious term. The common term is 'panloloko' (cheating) or 'pambababae/panlalalaki'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pakikiapid** ay isang malubhang kasalanan sa mata ng simbahan at batas.","translation":"**Adultery** is a grave sin in the eyes of the church and the law."},{"sentence":"Maaari siyang kasuhan ng **pakikiapid** ng kanyang asawa.","translation":"He can be charged with **adultery** by his spouse."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paglalarawan sa isang bagay o nilalang na tumatanggap ng sukdulan at maingat na pag-aalaga; nasa pinakamainam na kondisyon dahil sa kalinga.
original_explanation: How you describe your face after a 10-step Korean skincare routine. Also how your lola describes her antique santos and her prized orchids. It's the opposite of 'pinabayaan'. 'Alagang-alaga ko 'tong kotse, kaya 'wag mong babanggain.'
usage_notes: The reduplication of the root word 'alaga' emphasizes the intensity and consistency of the care given.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit luma na ang sasakyan, **alagang-alaga** pa rin ito ng may-ari.","translation":"Even though the car is old, it is **very well taken care of** by the owner."},{"sentence":"Makikita sa makintab niyang buhok na **alagang-alaga** ito.","translation":"You can see from her shiny hair that it is **very well taken care of**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng fungus na ginagamit sa pagpapatubo o pagpapaalsa ng masa para sa tinapay at sa pag-ferment ng mga inumin tulad ng serbesa.
original_explanation: The magic stuff that makes your pandesal fluffy and your beer... well, beer. It's the silent worker behind your favorite carbs, kind of like that one groupmate who does all the work but doesn't get the credit.
usage_notes: While 'pampaalsa' is the general term, 'yeast' is specifically used by bakers and in modern recipes. 'Lebadura' is the Spanish-derived term, now less common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mo ng **yeast** para umalsa nang maayos ang dough ng pizza.","translation":"You need **yeast** for the pizza dough to rise properly."},{"sentence":"Nakalimutan kong bumili ng **yeast** sa grocery.","translation":"I forgot to buy **yeast** at the grocery."}]

meaning_filipino: Ito ang kasalukuyang proseso ng pagdinig at pagpapasya sa isang kaso sa hukuman. Tumutukoy sa isang taong sumasailalim sa paglilitis.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you're in the hot seat, courtroom drama style. Think "Ipaglaban Mo" or "Case Unclosed". It's the legal version of your mom asking "Saan ka galing at anong oras na?" with matching evidence from your FB posts. You're being questioned, examined, and judged.
usage_notes: Present tense, passive voice of 'litis' (trial).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang akusado ay kasalukuyang **nililitis** para sa kasong pagnanakaw.","translation":"The accused is currently **being tried** for the crime of theft."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam ko'y **nililitis** ako sa tuwing tinatanong ako ng aking biyenan.","translation":"I feel like I'm **being cross-examined** every time my mother-in-law asks me questions."}]

meaning_filipino: Manloko o mangdaya, lalo na sa usaping pera, upang makakuha ng hindi nararapat na pakinabang.
etymology: From the root word 'duit,' an old term for money, possibly of Hokkien origin. The prefix 'man-' indicates performing an action.
