meaning_filipino: Puntahan ang isang lugar sa pamamagitan ng paglipad; paglalakbay sa himpapawid patungo sa isang destinasyon.
original_explanation: Your travel goals! Yung pangarap mong 'liparin ang buong mundo.' It's the act of flying *to* a specific destination, not just flying in general. Think booking a flight to Siargao or Korea.
usage_notes: This is the object-focus form of the verb 'lumipad' (to fly). You use 'liparin' when the destination is the focus.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang **liparin** ang Paris balang araw.","translation":"It's her dream to **fly to** Paris someday."},{"sentence":"Kaya bang **liparin** ng drone ang buong lawa para makuhaan ng video?","translation":"Can the drone **fly over** the entire lake to get a video?"}]

translation: to put in order; to improve
meaning_filipino: Ayusin, pagbutihin, o ilagay sa kaayusan ang isang bagay; gawing mas mahusay.
original_explanation: It's the verb form of 'husay' (skill, excellence). When your manager tells you to '**ihusay** mo 'yang report mo,' they mean 'make that report better/more presentable.' It's about taking something and making it better, neater, or more skillful. The opposite of 'bahala na si Batman'.
usage_notes: Often used as a command or suggestion to improve the quality of one's work or an arrangement.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **ihusay** ang pagkakalagay ng mga gamit sa aparador.","translation":"You need to **arrange properly** the things in the closet."},{"sentence":"**Ihusay** mo ang iyong trabaho para ma-promote ka.","translation":"**Improve** your work so you can get promoted."}]

translation: to put at the end; to make last
meaning_filipino: Ilagay sa pinakadulo o gawing pangwakas ang isang bagay sa isang pagkakasunod-sunod.
original_explanation: When you're eating and you save the best bite for last. That's 'ihuli'. Or when you're arranging a presentation and you decide which slide goes at the very end. It's the 'save the best/worst for last' verb. "Huwag mo akong **ihuli** sa pila, male-late na ako!"
usage_notes: Not to be confused with 'huli' (to catch). The stress on the second syllable /i-HU-li/ is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Palagi kong **inihuhuli** ang paborito kong ulam sa aking plato.","translation":"I always **make** my favorite dish the **last** one to eat on my plate."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ihuli** ang paggawa ng iyong takdang-aralin.","translation":"Don't **put off** doing your homework for **last**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang anyo ng pandiwa na gumaganap bilang isang pangalan sa loob ng pangungusap, karaniwang nabubuo sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng mga panlaping 'pag-' at 'pagka-'.
etymology: Isang portmanteau o pinagsamang salita ng `pandiwa` (verb) at `wari` (as if, like) at `pangalan` (noun), na nangangahulugang 'parang-pandiwa na pangalan'.
original_explanation: This is when a verb decides to cosplay as a noun. Take the verb 'takbo' (run). When you say 'Ang pagtakbo ay nakakapagod' (Running is tiring), 'pagtakbo' is the subject of the sentence, which is a noun's job. It's the action itself, treated as a thing. Basically, the '-ing' form in English when used as a noun.
usage_notes: Isang teknikal na termino sa balarilang Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang 'pag-ibig' ay isang halimbawa ng **pandiwaring pangalan**.","translation":"'Pag-ibig' (loving/love) is an example of a **gerund**."},{"sentence":"Sa pangungusap na 'Mahalaga ang pag-aaral,' ang 'pag-aaral' ay gumaganap bilang **pandiwaring pangalan**.","translation":"In the sentence 'Studying is important,' 'pag-aaral' functions as a **gerund**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang balangkas o listahan ng mga pangunahing punto o paksa ng isang sulatin, talumpati, o plano.
original_explanation: The skeleton of your report before you put the meat on it. It's the 'I, II, A, B, 1, 2' format you learned in high school that you now use in PowerPoint presentations to look organized, even if your thoughts are pure chaos.
usage_notes: A compound word, less common in daily speech than its English counterpart 'outline'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumawa muna tayo ng **talaguhitan** bago simulan ang pagsusulat.","translation":"Let's make an **outline** first before starting to write."},{"sentence":"Nasa **talaguhitan** ang mga pangunahing paksang tatalakayin natin.","translation":"The main topics we will discuss are in the **outline**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang gawain o sigasig na masigasig lamang sa simula ngunit hindi nagtatagal at agad na nawawala, katulad ng mabilis na pag-apoy at pagkaabo ng tuyong damong kugon. Ito ay baryasyon ng 'ningas-kugon'.
etymology: From 'lingas' (flame) and 'kugon' (cogon grass). A variant of the more common 'ningas-kugon'.
original_explanation: The official term for your New Year's resolution to go to the gym, which lasts for exactly one week. It’s that fiery start to a new hobby, project, or diet, that fizzles out faster than a free data promo. All flame, no follow-through.
usage_notes: The term 'ningas-kugon' is more commonly used and recognized.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana hindi **lingas-kugon** ang pag-aaral mo ng bagong wika.","translation":"I hope your study of a new language isn't just a case of **initial enthusiasm that fades**."},{"sentence":"Maraming proyekto ang hindi natatapos dahil sa ugaling **lingas-kugon**.","translation":"Many projects are left unfinished because of the **ningas-kugon** attitude."}]

translation: to be inclined; to be biased; to lean towards
meaning_filipino: Pagkakaroon ng inklinasyon, pagkiling, o pagpanig sa isang partikular na panig, tao, o ideya.
original_explanation: When a referee seems to favor one basketball team, the crowd yells, "Makiling ang ref!" (The ref is biased!). It's about leaning towards one side. It can be about your preference for adobo over sinigang, or a judge's questionable bias in a legal case.
usage_notes: Often carries a negative connotation of unfair bias, but can also be neutral (e.g., inclined towards a certain opinion).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi dapat **makiling** ang isang hukom sa alinmang panig.","translation":"A judge should not **be biased** towards any side."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang karanasan, siya ay **makiling** sa mas praktikal na solusyon.","translation":"Because of his experience, he **is inclined** towards the more practical solution."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagbagsak, pagkasira, o pagkawask ng isang istruktura o bagay.
original_explanation: What happens to your Jenga tower when someone breathes too hard. It's the dramatic result of a strong typhoon on an old house, or the state of your life plans during a quarter-life crisis. The total 'bagsak'.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for structures or figuratively for plans, hopes, or systems.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagdulot ng malawakang **pagkagiba** ng mga bahay ang malakas na lindol.","translation":"The strong earthquake caused the widespread **collapse** of houses."},{"sentence":"Nasaksihan niya ang unti-unting **pagkagiba** ng kanilang negosyo.","translation":"He witnessed the slow **destruction** of their business."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpasok sa isang lugar, estado, o kalagayan sa ikalawang pagkakataon o higit pa.
original_explanation: That awkward moment when you leave a room and immediately have to come back because you forgot your keys. Or for OFWs, it's the process of coming back to a foreign country to work again. It can also be that feeling of trying to get back into a friend group after a long absence.
usage_notes: Isang pariralang pangngalan. Madalas gamitin sa mga pormal na konteksto tulad ng imigrasyon o paglalakbay sa kalawakan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang mga patakaran para sa **muling pagpasok** ng mga dayuhan sa bansa.","translation":"The rules for the **re-entry** of foreigners into the country are strict."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng mga siyentipiko ang ligtas na **muling pagpasok** ng spacecraft sa atmospera.","translation":"Scientists are studying the safe **re-entry** of the spacecraft into the atmosphere."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maliit na isdang-alat (Sardinella fimbriata) na kahawig ng sardinas, karaniwang pinapatuyo o kinakain nang sariwa.
etymology: Possibly from a local Philippine language, specific to this type of fish.
original_explanation: The unsung hero of the palengke and the breakfast table. This is the fish that gets fried to a crisp and paired with sinangag and suka. It's the more affordable cousin of tawilis and the fresh version of what goes into that 555 or Ligo can. Your lola's favorite 'pritong isda'.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to the Fimbriated Sardinella. Often sold dried (tuyo) or fresh in markets.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng isang kilong sariwang **tunsoy** sa palengke.","translation":"Mom bought a kilo of fresh **fimbriated sardinella** at the market."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang pritong **tunsoy** na isasawsaw sa sukang may bawang.","translation":"Fried **tunsoy** is delicious when dipped in vinegar with garlic."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakalat o paghahatid ng impormasyon, balita, o programa sa pamamagitan ng radyo, telebisyon, o internet.
etymology: From English 'broadcast', with Filipino phonetic spelling.
original_explanation: Before Netflix and TikTok, this was how we got our entertainment and news. It's what radio DJs and TV news anchors do. Today, it can also mean that "group message" your Tita sent to 50 people on Viber announcing the next family reunion.
usage_notes: Often used in media and communication fields. The verb form is often 'i-brodkast'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **brodkast** ng balita ay magsisimula mamayang alas-sais ng gabi.","translation":"The news **broadcast** will start at six in the evening."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang aparato na ginagamit upang durugin ang malalaking piraso ng yelo upang maging maliliit na bahagi, karaniwan para sa mga palamig o panghimagas.
original_explanation: The sound of summer in the Philippines! This is the machine that powers every halo-halo and mais con yelo stand. Whether it's the manual hand-cranked one or the noisy electric one, it's the hero we need during a heatwave.
usage_notes: Kilala rin bilang 'pangkayod ng yelo', lalo na para sa halo-halo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng bagong **pandurog ng yelo** para sa aming tindahan ng halo-halo.","translation":"Mom bought a new **ice crusher** for our halo-halo store."},{"sentence":"Pakilagay na lang sa **pandurog ng yelo** ang isang buong bloke.","translation":"Please just put the whole block in the **ice crusher**."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagkain na karaniwang matamis at kinakain sa huli o pagkatapos ng pangunahing pagkain.
etymology: From pang- (nominalizing prefix) + himagas (an old word for after-taste or the final course of a meal).
original_explanation: The best part of any meal. The reason you save a little bit of space in your stomach after devouring a plate of adobo. Whether it's leche flan, halo-halo, a slice of cake, or just a piece of fruit, this is the grand finale, the sweet reward for finishing your vegetables. Life is short, eat the panghimagas first.
usage_notes: A staple word in Filipino dining culture.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **panghimagas** natin mamaya?","translation":"What's our **dessert** for later?"},{"sentence":"Ang paborito kong **panghimagas** ay leche flan.","translation":"My favorite **dessert** is leche flan."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o akto ng paglikha, pag-imbento, o pagbuo ng isang bagay mula sa wala o mula sa mga umiiral na materyales.
original_explanation: The OG "new project." This is God-tier level of making something. It's not just cooking adobo; it's inventing the entire concept of adobo. It's what artists, writers, and programmers do when they stare into the void and pull out a masterpiece. The ultimate "from scratch."
usage_notes: Often used in a formal, literary, or religious context to mean "creation." More profound than the everyday 'paggawa' (making).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan sa klase ng Pilosopiya ang kuwento ng **paglalang** sa sanlibutan.","translation":"The story of the **creation** of the universe is studied in Philosophy class."},{"sentence":"Ang **paglalang** ng isang obra maestra ay nangangailangan ng panahon at dedikasyon.","translation":"The **creation** of a masterpiece requires time and dedication."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang simbolo o karakter na kumakatawan sa isang tunog sa pagsulat, na bahagi ng alpabeto. Maaari ring tumukoy sa sulat-kamay.
original_explanation: It's a letter, like A, B, C. It can also mean your handwriting. 'Ang ganda ng letra mo!' is the ultimate compliment when you've spent hours practicing your calligraphy for a crush's card. It’s the building block of all the 'chismis' you type and the 'hugot' you post.
usage_notes: 'Titik' is the more indigenous Tagalog term for a letter of the alphabet, while 'letra' is a common Spanish-derived synonym. 'Letra' is also more frequently used to refer to handwriting style.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap basahin ang **letra** ng doktor sa reseta.","translation":"It's hard to read the doctor's **handwriting** on the prescription."},{"sentence":"Ang salitang 'pag-ibig' ay may anim na **letra**.","translation":"The word 'pag-ibig' has six **letters**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isama, ihalo, o idahok ang isang tao o bagay sa isang grupo, gawain, o usapan.
etymology: 'pa-' + 'lahok' + '-in'. Causative verb from 'lahok' (to participate, join, an entry). 'To cause to be an entry/participant'.
original_explanation: When you're in a meeting and your boss says, 'Palahukin natin si Marites sa project na 'to.' It means 'Let's include Marites in this project.' It's about adding someone or something to the mix, whether it's an ingredient in a recipe or a person in a team... or chismis.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of including someone in an activity or group.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo siyang **palahukin** sa usapan ng matatanda.","translation":"Don't **include** him in the adults' conversation."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **palahukin** ang lahat ng departamento sa pagpaplano.","translation":"We need to **involve** all departments in the planning."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng ugaling wari'y ayaw ngunit sa kalooban ay may gusto; pagiging mailap o mahirap suyuin.
etymology: From pa- (prefix indicating pretense or causing) + kipot (narrow). The idea is to make the path to winning one's affection 'narrow' or difficult.
original_explanation: The classic 'pabebe' move in dating. You say 'no' but your kilay says 'yes.' It's the human equivalent of a cat that wants to be petted but walks away when you get close. In the land of ligaw (courtship), this is a national sport.
usage_notes: Can be used to describe a person or their actions. Often has a slightly negative or teasing connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang maging **pakipot**, alam ko namang gusto mo rin.","translation":"Stop **playing hard to get**, I know you like it too."},{"sentence":"Ang dami niyang dahilan, ang **pakipot** talaga.","translation":"She has so many excuses, she's really being **coy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng malakas at paulit-ulit na pag-uga o pag-alog sa isang bagay.
etymology: From 'liglig' (to shake vigorously) with the infix '-in-'.
original_explanation: This is what you do to a bottle of salad dressing, a can of paint, or your sibling when they won't wake up. It's a more intense, more aggressive version of 'inuga' (shaken). If an earthquake was a verb, it would be 'niliglig' the whole country.
usage_notes: 'Niliglig' implies a more forceful, often vertical or back-and-forth shaking, compared to 'inuga' which can be a gentler sway.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Niliglig** niya ang bote ng gamot bago inumin.","translation":"He **shook the medicine bottle vigorously** before drinking."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam ko ay **niliglig** ang buong pagkatao ko sa narinig kong balita.","translation":"I feel like my whole being was **shaken** by the news I heard."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lugar, panahon, o dahilan kung saan nag-umpisa o nagmula ang isang bagay, pangyayari, o konsepto.
etymology: From `pinag-` + `simula` + `-an`. Indicates the place or reason where something began.
original_explanation: This is the 'Saan nagsimula ang lahat?' moment. The origin story of your away with your jowa, the chismis about your kapitbahay, or the reason why you have trust issues. It's the ground zero, the patient zero, the 'back when...'
usage_notes: Often used to refer to the cause or starting point of a conflict, story, or project.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ba ang **pinagsimulan** ng away ninyo?","translation":"What was the **origin** of your fight?"},{"sentence":"Dito sa lumang bahay na ito ang **pinagsimulan** ng aming pamilya.","translation":"This old house is the **beginning** of our family."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggalaw o paglipat ng lugar sa pamamagitan ng paghakbang gamit ang mga paa.
original_explanation: The original 'Libre lang mangarap.' The cheapest form of transportation and therapy. It's what you do to get from Point A to Point B when your Grab budget says 'no.' It's also what you do around the mall for 'exercise' or to clear your head after a stressful day. Minsan, ito rin ang pag-aasikaso ng papeles (processing papers).
usage_notes: "Maglakad-lakad" implies a more leisurely, aimless walk (strolling). "Paglalakad" can also refer to the act of processing something, like documents ("paglakad ng papeles").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maganda sa kalusugan ang regular na **paglalakad** tuwing umaga.","translation":"Regular **walking** in the morning is good for one's health."},{"sentence":"Matagal ang proseso ng **paglalakad** ng mga dokumento sa gobyerno.","translation":"The process of **walking** (processing) documents in the government is long."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan ng sukdulang kasamaan, kalupitan, o pag-uugaling maihahalintulad sa isang demonyo.
etymology: From `napaka-` (superlative prefix) + `demonyo` (demon), which is from Spanish 'demonio'.
original_explanation: When 'masama' or 'salbahe' is not enough. This is reserved for your evil boss who gives you work at 5:59 PM on a Friday, or that ex who broke your heart into a million pieces. It's evil on another level.
usage_notes: A very strong, often hyperbolic, term to describe extreme cruelty or malevolence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga krimeng ginawa niya ay **napakademonyo** at hindi katanggap-tanggap sa lipunan.","translation":"The crimes he committed were **very demonic** and unacceptable in society."},{"sentence":"Para siyang **napakademonyo** kung magalit.","translation":"He seems **extremely evil** when he gets angry."}]

translation: to pass by; to let pass
meaning_filipino: Ang paghiling ng pahintulot na dumaan sa isang lugar o daanan; ang pagbibigay ng espasyo para sa iba na makadaan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'daan' (way, path) at ang unlaping 'pa-' na nagpapahiwatig ng paghiling o pagpapahintulot.
original_explanation: This is the magic word you say when you're trying to squeeze through a crowded MRT train or a packed palengke aisle. It's the polite way of saying 'Excuse me, coming through!' without sounding like a bulldozer. You say 'Padaan po!' with a slight bow and people will (usually) part like the Red Sea for you. It's a fundamental skill for surviving Manila's crowds.
usage_notes: Kadalasan ay may kasamang 'po' o 'ho' para sa paggalang. Maaaring isang pakiusap ('Padaan po') o isang utos ('Padaanin mo sila').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Padaan** po, mainit po ang dala ko!","translation":"**Excuse me, please let me pass**, I'm carrying something hot!"},{"sentence":"Pwede bang **padaan** muna ako saglit sa opisina mo bago umuwi?","translation":"Can I **pass by** your office for a moment before going home?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mabigat na kasangkapan, karaniwang yari sa kahoy, bato, o metal, na ginagamit na pandikdik o pambayo ng mga sangkap sa isang lusong.
original_explanation: The partner of the 'lusong' (mortar). It's your lola's original food processor for making garlic and pepper extra potent. In the gym, it's what your arms feel like they're being hit with after arm day.
usage_notes: Almost always used in conjunction with 'lusong' (mortar). The pair is 'lusong at pambayo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gamitin mo ang **pambayo** para durugin ang bawang.","translation":"Use the **pestle** to crush the garlic."},{"sentence":"Mabigat ang lumang **pambayo** na gawa sa bato.","translation":"The old **pounder** made of stone is heavy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang pananong na ginagamit upang alamin ang lokasyon o kinaroroonan ng isang tao, bagay, o lugar.
original_explanation: The ultimate question ng mga nanay na naghahanap ng gamit sa bahay: "Nasaan na yung gunting?!" or "Nasaan ka na?" kapag 10 PM na at wala ka pa. It's the Filipino version of "Where art thou?". Also the title of a lot of hugot songs.
usage_notes: Ginagamit para sa mga pangngalan (tao, bagay). Ang "Saan" ay ginagamit para sa mga pandiwa (e.g., "Saan ka pupunta?").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nasaan** ang mga susi ng kotse?","translation":"**Where are** the car keys?"},{"sentence":"**Nasaan** si Maria? Kanina ko pa siya hinahanap.","translation":"**Where is** Maria? I've been looking for her."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang artipisyal na piraso ng buhok na isinusuot upang takpan ang pagkapanot.
original_explanation: That little patch of 'instant pogi' for titos who are a bit... aerodynamically challenged on top. It's the analog version of a hair transplant. You hope it's secured properly, especially on a windy day at the beach.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nalaglag ang **tupe** ng pulitiko habang nagtatalumpati.","translation":"The politician's **toupee** fell off while he was giving a speech."},{"sentence":"Bumili siya ng bagong **tupe** para sa kasal ng anak niya.","translation":"He bought a new **hairpiece** for his child's wedding."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi batid o walang kaalaman sa isang bagay; walang kamalayan o ulirat.
original_explanation: Two main vibes here. First is the 'clueless' kind of innocent, like a fresh grad on their first day sa BPO, hindi pa alam ang horrors ng night shift. The second is literally 'unconscious,' like after too much Red Horse, bagsak ka na at walang-malay sa mundo.
usage_notes: Maaaring mangahulugang 'inosente/walang alam' o 'walang ulirat/hinimatay'. Ang konteksto ang magdidikta ng tamang kahulugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Walang-malay** ang bata sa panganib na nag-aabang.","translation":"The child was **innocent** of the danger that awaited."},{"sentence":"Natagpuan siyang **walang-malay** sa tabi ng kalsada.","translation":"He was found **unconscious** on the side of the road."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan na may dalawang bahagi na nagsasara upang humawak, kumurot, o mag-ipit ng isang bagay. Tumutukoy din sa bahagi ng katawan ng alimango o alimasag.
original_explanation: Anything that pinches. From the crab's 'sipit' that you're scared of at the palengke, to the 'sipit' (tongs) you use for the barbecue, to the 'sipit' (hair clip) holding your life together on a stressful day. It's the OG multi-tool.
usage_notes: A general term. Specific types are often named, e.g., 'sipit ng damit' (clothespin), 'sipit sa buhok' (hair clip).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa **sipit** ng alimango.","translation":"Be careful of the crab's **pincers**."},{"sentence":"Gamitin mo ang **sipit** para kunin ang mainit na uling.","translation":"Use the **tongs** to get the hot charcoal."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong lumilikha ng nilalaman o content, lalo na para sa mga digital na platform tulad ng YouTube, TikTok, o Instagram.
etymology: From English "creator", specifically referring to "content creator".
original_explanation: The modern-day 'artista'. Sila yung mga vlogger, TikToker, at streamer na nag-a-upload ng "Hi, guys! For today's video..." Sila ang dahilan kung bakit may 'budol' finds ka sa Shopee at kung bakit alam mo ang latest dance challenge. Aspiring lahat maging creator.
usage_notes: In modern Filipino parlance, this refers almost exclusively to online content creators, distinct from 'manlilikha' (artist/artisan) or 'Tagapaglikha' (The Creator/God).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang sikat na **creator** sa TikTok ang nagpasimuno ng sayaw na iyon.","translation":"A famous **creator** on TikTok started that dance."},{"sentence":"Gusto niyang maging isang gaming **creator** paglaki niya.","translation":"He wants to be a gaming **creator** when he grows up."}]

translation: prefixation; a word with a prefix
meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pagbuo ng salita sa pamamagitan ng pagdaragdag ng panlapi sa unahan nito (unlapi). Tumutukoy rin ito sa salitang nabuo sa pamamaraang ito.
original_explanation: This is a grammar nerd term. It's when you stick something at the beginning of a word to change its meaning, like adding 'ma-' to 'ganda' to get 'maganda'. It's the original "remix" of Filipino words. Think of prefixes as the filters you add to a photo—they change the vibe of the original.
usage_notes: Isang terminong pang-gramatika na ginagamit sa pag-aaral ng wikang Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang salitang 'umalis' ay isang halimbawa ng **unlapian** dahil mayroon itong unlaping 'um-'.","translation":"The word 'umalis' is an example of a **prefixed word** because it has the prefix 'um-'."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging malaya sa hirap, sakit, o anumang pasanin; pagkakaroon ng magaan at payapang pamumuhay.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'ka-', ugat na 'ginhawa' (gaan ng pakiramdam), at hulaping '-han'.
original_explanation: The feeling after a long day of work when you finally get to lie down on your bed with the AC on full blast. It's the "Salamat Lord, payday na!" feeling. The opposite of stress, traffic, and adulting problems. The ultimate goal of every 13th-month pay.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang isang estado ng pisikal, mental, o pinansyal na kaginhawahan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang hangad lang ng bawat magulang ay ang **kaginhawahan** ng kanilang mga anak.","translation":"The only wish of every parent is the **well-being** of their children."},{"sentence":"Nakadama siya ng malaking **kaginhawahan** nang matapos na ang kanyang mga problema.","translation":"He felt great **relief** when his problems were finally over."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtusok at pag-iisa-isa ng mga bagay sa isang patpat o anumang matulis na bagay. Ito ay ang anyong naganap ng pandiwang "tuhugin".
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'tuhog' na nangangahulugang pagtusok sa patpat.
original_explanation: Think BBQ night. It's what you did to the pork, hotdogs, and bell peppers to make the perfect stick. It can also be used figuratively, like when you "skewered" multiple tasks in one go, or when a chismosa connected different unrelated stories to create one juicy narrative. "Tinuhog niya lahat ng meeting in one morning."
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa pagluluto. Ang anyong pangkasalukuyan ay "tinutuhog" at panghinaharap ay "tutuhugin".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tinuhog** niya ang mga piraso ng manok para sa ihawan.","translation":"He **skewered** the pieces of chicken for the grill."},{"sentence":"Parang **tinuhog** ang puso ko sa sakit nang iwan niya ako.","translation":"It felt like my heart was **pierced through** with pain when they left me."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na may kakayahang impluwensiyahan ang mga desisyon sa pagbili ng iba dahil sa kanyang awtoridad, kaalaman, posisyon, o relasyon sa kanyang mga tagasubaybay. Karaniwang ginagamit para sa mga personalidad sa social media.
original_explanation: The modern-day 'artista.' They're the reason you suddenly want to buy that random Shopee/Lazada product from a 12.12 sale. They have a 'following' and can make or break a product with a single 'honest review' (wink, wink). Their job is to influence... and to post aesthetically pleasing coffee photos.
usage_notes: A direct loanword that has been fully integrated into Taglish and even formal Filipino media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang sikat na **influencer** ang kinuha para i-promote ang bagong produkto.","translation":"A famous **influencer** was hired to promote the new product."},{"sentence":"Gusto niyang maging isang travel **influencer** paglaki niya.","translation":"She wants to be a travel **influencer** when she grows up."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng katawan ng tao mula sa balikat hanggang sa kamay.
original_explanation: Your body's built-in selfie stick. Also, the part of you that gets sore after carrying all the groceries from the palengke in one trip because you refuse to make a second one. "Ang lalaki ng braso mo, ah! Nag-gym ka ba?"
usage_notes: A common anatomical term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masakit ang **braso** ko sa kakabuhat ng mga libro.","translation":"My **arm** hurts from carrying so many books."},{"sentence":"Kumapit ka lang sa **braso** ko.","translation":"Just hold on to my **arm**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang lalaki na pabago-bago ang isip o kagustuhan; mahirap hulaan ang kilos o desisyon.
original_explanation: The guy version of kapritsosa. He's the one who says "Kahit ano" when you ask where to eat, but rejects all your suggestions. His moods change like the EDSA traffic situation—unpredictable and often frustrating.
usage_notes: Used specifically for males. The female counterpart is 'kapritsosa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **kapritsoso** si boss ngayon, lahat ng trabaho ay pinapaulit niya.","translation":"The boss became **capricious** today, he's making everyone redo their work."},{"sentence":"Mahirap basahin ang isip ng isang taong **kapritsoso**.","translation":"It's hard to read the mind of a **fickle** person."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang estado ng pagiging kalmado, hindi nababahala, o hindi natitinag sa kabila ng mga kaguluhan o pagsubok.
etymology: Mula sa "di-" (hindi) at "natitigatig" (nababagabag), mula sa ugat na "tigatig" (pagkabagabag, pagkabalisa).
original_explanation: Ito yung estado mo kapag may limang deadline ka pero nag-scroll ka pa rin sa TikTok. Yung kahit anong gulo sa paligid, kahit nag-aaway na ang mga kapitbahay o may bagyo, ikaw ay chill lang. Di-natitigatig. The ultimate "This is fine" dog meme mood.
usage_notes: Isang pormal at pampanitikang termino. Ang "hindi nababahala" ay mas karaniwang katumbas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nanatili siyang **di-natitigatig** sa gitna ng kaguluhan sa pulong.","translation":"He remained **unperturbed** amidst the chaos in the meeting."},{"sentence":"Sa kabila ng masamang balita, ang kanyang pananampalataya ay **di-natitigatig**.","translation":"Despite the bad news, her faith remains **unfazed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkuha, pagtipon, o pagsama-samahin ang mga bagay, lalo na ang mga bayarin, datos, o mga piraso ng isang koleksyon.
original_explanation: The command form. Ito 'yung sinasabi sa'yo ng nanay mo: 'Kolektahin mo na 'yang mga laruan mo!' O 'yung utos ng boss mo: 'Kolektahin mo lahat ng resibo.' It means to gather or collect specific things. Get it done.
usage_notes: A common verb form used to direct someone to collect something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **kolektahin** ang lahat ng basura bago umalis.","translation":"We need **to collect** all the trash before leaving."},{"sentence":"Inutusan siyang **kolektahin** ang mga bayad mula sa mga miyembro.","translation":"He was instructed **to collect** the payments from the members."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matinding damdamin ng takot, pagkasindak, o pangingilabot dahil sa isang nakakagulat o masamang pangyayari.
original_explanation: That feeling when you check your bank account after a 12.12 sale. Or when you accidentally send a screenshot of the conversation *back to the person you're talking about*. Pure gimbal. It's that stomach-dropping, 'oh no' moment.
usage_notes: Often used to describe the aftermath of a tragedy or a shocking event.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-iwan ng **gimbal** sa buong komunidad ang biglaang pagputok ng bulkan.","translation":"The sudden eruption of the volcano left the entire community in **terror**."},{"sentence":"Makikita sa kanyang mga mata ang **gimbal** ng nasaksihan niyang krimen.","translation":"You could see in his eyes the **shock** of the crime he witnessed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamataas na antas ng saya o galak na walang halong lungkot o pag-aalala.
original_explanation: The feeling you get when your 13th-month pay comes in. Or when your Lazada package arrives earlier than expected. It's not just 'happy,' it's 'cancel-all-my-plans-and-just-bask-in-this-moment' kind of happy. The ultimate #SanaAll feeling.
usage_notes: Used to describe a state of supreme, unadulterated joy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang makasama ang kanyang mga anak ay nagbibigay sa kanya ng **lubos na kaligayahan**.","translation":"Being with her children gives her **absolute happiness**."},{"sentence":"Para sa akin, ang **lubos na kaligayahan** ay isang tasang kape sa umaga na walang kausap.","translation":"For me, **pure joy** is a cup of coffee in the morning with no one to talk to."}]

translation: to do one's best, to excel at something
meaning_filipino: Pagbutihin o gawing napakahusay ang isang gawain o pagganap. Ito ay isang utos o pakiusap na ibigay ang lahat ng makakaya.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'pep talk' word. It's what your mom tells you before an exam ('Galingan mo, anak!'), what your friends say before a job interview, and what you tell yourself before a presentation. It means 'do your best,' 'slay,' 'bring your A-game.' It's a command to be awesome.
usage_notes: Often used in the imperative form to encourage someone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Galingan** mo sa laro mamaya para manalo tayo!","translation":"**Do your best** in the game later so we can win!"},{"sentence":"Sinabihan ako ng aking guro na **galingan** ko ang aking proyekto.","translation":"My teacher told me to **excel at** my project."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panandalian at mabilis na pagliwanag o pagningning ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: It's the glint in your crush's eye when they see you. It's the sparkle of your phone screen when you get a 'G?' message from your barkada on a Friday night. It's that ✨main character energy✨ radiating from a newly-bought sequined dress.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May kakaibang **kislap** ang mga bituin ngayong gabi.","translation":"The stars have a special **twinkle** tonight."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko ang **kislap** sa kanyang mga mata nang matanggap niya ang regalo.","translation":"I saw the **sparkle** in her eyes when she received the gift."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gagawing paghiga sa isang partikular na lugar o bagay.
original_explanation: This is the future tense of finding a spot to crash. While 'hihiga' is just the act of lying down, 'hihigan' is about *what* you will lie down on. 'Hihigan ko ang sahig kung walang kama.' (I will lie on the floor if there's no bed). It's about claiming your temporary horizontal territory.
usage_notes: This is the object-focus (locative) future tense of 'higa', indicating the place or object that will be lain upon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malinis ba ang papag na **hihigan** natin?","translation":"Is the cot we **will lie on** clean?"},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **hihigan** ang mga damit na bagong lantsa.","translation":"Don't **lie on** the newly ironed clothes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang opisyal na pagsusuri at pag-inspeksyon sa mga talaang pampinansyal ng isang organisasyon o indibidwal upang matiyak ang katumpakan nito.
original_explanation: Yung moment na biglang darating ang taga-COA sa office niyo. That's an audit. Or 'yung ginagawa ng jowa mo sa phone mo, tinitingnan lahat ng messages at call logs, that's a relationship audit. Basically, a formal check-up to see if everything is legit and walang tinatago.
usage_notes: Ginamit sa konteksto ng negosyo, pananalapi, at pamamahala.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng taunang **audit** sa aming kumpanya.","translation":"There was an annual **audit** in our company."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng lagari upang putulin ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay kahoy.
original_explanation: The sound of your neighbor doing home repairs on a Sunday morning. It’s the act of using a saw, whether you’re a pro-carpenter building a cabinet or just someone trying to cut down that branch blocking your WiFi signal. The verb for making sawdust.
usage_notes: Can be used for both manual saws and power saws.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **maglagari** ng kahoy para panggatong.","translation":"We need to **saw** some wood for fuel."},{"sentence":"Nag-ingay ang karpintero habang siya ay naglalagari.","translation":"The carpenter made a lot of noise while he was **sawing**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghampas o pagpalo gamit ang isang batuta, karaniwan bilang paraan ng pagkontrol o pagpapatupad ng awtoridad.
original_explanation: When the riot police get tired of your protest signs and decide to give you a 'gentle' tap with their favorite stick. It's the physical version of "talk to the hand," but with a police baton.
usage_notes: Often associated with police or authority figures dispersing a crowd or subduing a suspect.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumatuta** ang mga pulis sa mga nagwawalang ralyista.","translation":"The police **struck** the rowdy rallyists **with batons**."},{"sentence":"Nagbanta siyang **bumatuta** sa sinumang magnanakaw na papasok sa kanyang bakuran.","translation":"He threatened to **strike with a stick** any thief who would enter his yard."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng tunog na katangian ng isang pusa.
etymology: From the root "ngaw" (an onomatopoeia for a cat's cry) + infix "-um-".
original_explanation: The sound a cat makes when it wants food, attention, or to be let inside at 4 AM. It's the universal cat-call, literally. Also what you might do jokingly to get a cat's attention. The more common term is 'ngumiyaw'.
usage_notes: Specifically for the sound a cat makes. "Ngumiyaw" is a more common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Biglang **umingaw** ang pusa sa ilalim ng mesa.","translation":"The cat under the table suddenly **meowed**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maingay, baka marinig kang **umingaw** ng mga aso.","translation":"Don't be noisy, the dogs might hear you **meow**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pangngalan na tumutukoy sa isang pangkat o kalipunan ng mga tao, hayop, o bagay na iisa ang uri.
original_explanation: It's the 'squad goals' of nouns. Instead of saying 'isang sundalo, isa pang sundalo...', you just say 'hukbo' (army). It's one word for a whole group. Think 'pamilya' (family), 'klase' (class), or 'barkada' (group of friends). It's the ultimate group chat name.
usage_notes: Isang tiyak na termino sa balarila para sa isang uri ng pangngalan. Bihira itong gamitin sa labas ng mga aralin sa wika.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang salitang 'kawan' na tumutukoy sa grupo ng mga ibon ay isang **pangngalang palansak**.","translation":"The word 'kawan' which refers to a flock of birds is a **collective noun**."},{"sentence":"Ang 'tumpok' ng basura ay isa ring halimbawa ng **pangngalang palansak**.","translation":"A 'tumpok' (pile) of trash is also an example of a **collective noun**."}]

translation: to move away from each other, to become distant
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-alis o paglipat ng mga tao o bagay upang magkaroon ng distansya sa pagitan nila; ang panlalamig o pagbabago ng isang relasyon.
original_explanation: Remember your super close high school bestie? Then college happened, you got different jobs, and now you just see each other's lives on Instagram. That's `naglayo`. It's the slow, silent drift. The opposite of "sana all" and the beginning of "kamusta na kaya siya?". It can also be literal, like following social distancing protocols. "Okay lang maglayo ang landas, basta huwag lang magkalimutan."
usage_notes: Can refer to physical distance ("maglayo-layo tayo") or emotional/relational distance ("naglayo ang loob nila").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **maglayo** ang kanilang landas pagkatapos ng kolehiyo.","translation":"Their paths started to **move away from each other** after college."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa pandemya, natuto tayong **maglayo** sa isa't isa para sa kaligtasan.","translation":"Because of the pandemic, we learned to **keep a distance** from one another for safety."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi kaaya-aya sa paningin, pandinig, o asal; malaswa o bastos.
original_explanation: Yung itsura ng ex mong iniwan ka para sa iba. Or yung joke ng tito mo na medyo off-color na. It's that feeling of 'yuck' or 'eww' that makes you cringe. It's not just physically ugly, but can also be about behavior or language that's just plain gross.
usage_notes: Often used to describe something visually unappealing, but can also refer to behavior, jokes, or language that is vulgar or inappropriate.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Masagwa** tingnan ang basurang nagkalat sa kalsada.","translation":"The trash scattered on the street is **ugly** to look at."},{"sentence":"Itigil mo 'yang **masagwa** mong biro.","translation":"Stop your **lewd** joke."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangunahing bahagi ng isang eruplano na naglalaman ng mga pasahero, kargamento, at ang sabungan ng piloto.
original_explanation: The main body of the plane. It's where you're stuck for hours on a flight to Cebu, trying to decide if you should get the beef or chicken from the flight attendant. It's the "jeep" part of the "air jeepney".
usage_notes: A descriptive phrase used when the specific technical term 'fuselage' is not known or needed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Makikita ang logo ng airline sa **katawan ng eruplano**.","translation":"The airline's logo can be seen on the **fuselage**."}]

meaning_filipino: May katangian, anyo, o komposisyon ng metal; tumutukoy sa isang bagay na gawa sa metal o parang metal.
original_explanation: Yung finish ng sasakyan na kumikinang sa araw. Yung eyeshadow na ginagamit mo para sa party look. O yung lasa sa bibig mo kapag aksidenteng nakagat mo yung tinidor. 'Eww, may lasang metaliko!'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **metaliko** na tunog ang narinig ko mula sa makina.","translation":"I heard a **metallic** sound from the engine."},{"sentence":"Pininturahan niya ang kanyang kuko ng kulay **metaliko** na pilak.","translation":"She painted her nails a **metallic** silver color."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na kahugis ng tao, karaniwang ginagamit bilang laruan o sa isang palabas; maaari ring tumukoy sa isang taong walang sariling kapangyarihan at sunud-sunuran lamang sa iba.
etymology: From "tao" (person) with reduplication and the suffix "-an", suggesting a diminutive or artificial version of a person.
original_explanation: It's either a literal doll/action figure, or the more juicy meaning: someone who looks like they're in charge but is actually just a puppet for the real boss. Think of that manager who can't approve your leave without asking their own boss first. Sila yung tau-tauhan lang.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for a manikin or puppet, or figuratively for a person with no real authority.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginagamit ng guro ang isang **tau-tauhan** upang ituro ang mga bahagi ng katawan.","translation":"The teacher uses a **manikin** to teach the parts of the body."},{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang maging **tau-tauhan** lamang ng mga mas makapangyarihang politiko.","translation":"He doesn't want to be a mere **puppet** for more powerful politicians."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang masidhi, patuloy, o paulit-ulit na paghabol sa isang tao, bagay, o layunin.
etymology: From "pag-" + reduplication of the first syllable of the root "ha-" + "habol". Indicates an intense or prolonged action.
original_explanation: This is 'paghabol' on steroids. It’s not just chasing the jeep; it's the entire action sequence in a movie. It's the BPO agent's "paghahabol sa quota." It's the relentless pursuit of justice, a promotion, or that person who left you on "read." The hustle is continuous and intense.
usage_notes: More common than "paghabol" for describing a sustained effort or a dramatic chase.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napanood namin sa balita ang **paghahabol** ng mga pulis sa mga kriminal.","translation":"We watched the police's **chasing** of the criminals on the news."},{"sentence":"Ang **paghahabol** niya sa kanyang mga grado ay nagbunga nang maging cum laude siya.","translation":"Her intense **pursuit** of her grades paid off when she became a cum laude."}]

translation: to be comparable; to be similar
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng pagkakatulad o pagiging halos magkapareho sa katangian, anyo, o kalidad.
original_explanation: When you can put two things side-by-side and they're basically the same, they are "magkahambing." Think of two K-drama male leads with the same haircut, or two milk tea shops with identical menus. It's the basis for the classic Filipino parent move: "Bakit si [pinsan's name], mataas ang grades? Hindi ba kayo magkahambing?" (Spoiler: you're not).
usage_notes: Often used with "halos" (almost) to mean "almost identical." The prefix `magka-` implies a reciprocal or shared quality.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halos **magkahambing** ang aming mga ideya para sa proyekto.","translation":"Our ideas for the project are **almost similar**."},{"sentence":"Hindi **magkahambing** ang sitwasyon noon at ngayon.","translation":"The situation then and now are not **comparable**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang patayong istruktura, karaniwang yari sa kahoy, semento, o ibang materyales, na nagsisilbing harang, hangganan, o panakip sa isang espasyo o gusali.
original_explanation: Your personal art gallery, your Zoom background, and the thing you talk to when you're lonely. Ang dingding ang silent witness sa lahat ng drama mo sa kwarto. Dito mo isinasabit ang graduation picture mo at dito rin tumatama ang unan na binato mo sa galit. Also known as 'pader', pero mas common ang 'dingding' for internal walls.
usage_notes: Ang 'dingding' ay karaniwang tumutukoy sa panloob na pader ng isang bahay, habang ang 'pader' (mula sa Espanyol na 'pared') ay mas madalas gamitin para sa mga pader na gawa sa semento o bato, lalo na sa labas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isinabit niya ang kanilang litrato sa **dingding** ng sala.","translation":"She hung their picture on the living room **wall**."},{"sentence":"Gawa sa lawanit ang **dingding** ng kanilang bahay.","translation":"The **wall** of their house is made of fiberboard."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pandiwa para sa pagtataas o pag-iikli ng laylayan ng damit, tulad ng manggas ng damit o binti ng pantalon, sa pamamagitan ng pagtutupi nito nang paulit-ulit.
etymology: From 'alilis' (to roll up sleeves/pants) with the infix '-in-'.
original_explanation: This is the universal sign for "Okay, let's get to work" or "It's about to get messy." Whether you're washing dishes, getting into a heated debate, or preparing to wade through a flooded street in Manila, this is the first step. It's the physical act of 'getting ready for business'.
usage_notes: Past tense of 'alilisin'. Commonly refers to sleeves or pant legs.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Inalilis** niya ang manggas ng kanyang baro bago maghugas ng pinggan.","translation":"He **rolled up** his shirt sleeves before washing the dishes."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa baha, **inalilis** ng mga tao ang kanilang mga pantalon.","translation":"Because of the flood, the people **rolled up** their pants."}]

translation: is commanding; is ordering (someone to do something)
meaning_filipino: Kasalukuyang nagbibigay ng isang direktiba, kautusan, o atas sa isang tao upang isagawa ang isang partikular na gawain.
original_explanation: The default mode of your nanay when she sees you sitting down for 2 seconds. Also, your boss on a Friday afternoon. It's the 'paki-kuha,' 'paki-gawa,' 'paki-bilis' power trip. 'Heto na naman si Ma'am, **nag-uutos** na parang walang bukas.'
usage_notes: Present progressive tense of 'mag-utos'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagi na lang siyang **nag-uutos** sa mga nakababatang kapatid niya.","translation":"He is always **ordering** his younger siblings around."},{"sentence":"Sino ba 'yang **nag-uutos** sa iyo na gawin 'yan?","translation":"Who **is commanding** you to do that?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdaragdag ng isa o higit pang sangkap sa isang lutuin o timpla upang mapabuti ang lasa o dami nito.
original_explanation: The secret to any good Filipino dish! It's all about the 'sahog'. In pancit, it's the meat and veggies. In life, it's the extra drama or 'spice' you add to a story to make it more interesting. 'Wag puro kwento, magsahog ka ng details!'
usage_notes: Commonly used in cooking contexts. Can be used metaphorically to mean 'add details' or 'spice things up'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **magsahog** ng gulay sa sinigang.","translation":"Don't forget to **add** vegetables to the sinigang."},{"sentence":"Mas masarap ang lugaw kung **magsasahog** ka ng itlog at tinapa.","translation":"The porridge is more delicious if you **add** egg and smoked fish as ingredients."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang gawain o paligsahan na may mga alituntunin, isinasagawa para sa libangan, ehersisyo, o kompetisyon.
original_explanation: What you say you're doing on your phone when you're actually scrolling through memes at work. From piko to Mobile Legends, basta may fun (at minsan, pusta), **laro** 'yan. It's the reason for your puyat and the source of your 'squad goals'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito ng mga bata ang **laro** ng tagu-taguan.","translation":"Hide-and-seek is a favorite **game** of children."},{"sentence":"Seryoso siya pagdating sa anumang **laro** ng basketball.","translation":"He is serious when it comes to any basketball **game**."}]

translation: to rise, to lift, to revolt
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-angat o pagtaas ng isang bagay mula sa kinalalagyan nito; pagtutol o paghihimagsik laban sa isang kapangyarihan.
original_explanation: To 'alsa' is to make something go up. Your pandesal dough? It needs to 'umalsa'. Your kilay when you hear chismis? Nag-aalsa 'yan. Your blood pressure from traffic? Umaalsa. And on a more serious note, it's what heroes do against colonizers—they 'nag-alsa'. It's the ultimate 'get up, stand up' move.
usage_notes: Ang pandiwang ito ay maaaring maging 'umalsa' (actor focus) o 'i-alsa' (object focus). Mayroon din itong anyong 'mag-alsa' na tumutukoy sa paghihimagsik.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hayaan mong **umalsa** ang masa ng tinapay bago ito iluto.","translation":"Let the bread dough **rise** before baking it."},{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang mga katipunero na **mag-alsa** laban sa mga mananakop.","translation":"The katipuneros decided to **revolt** against the colonizers."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbibigay ng isang ideya, payo, o plano para isaalang-alang ng iba.
etymology: From the root "mungkahi" (suggestion), with the prefix "pag-" and reduplication of the first syllable of the root ("mu-") to form a verbal noun.
original_explanation: This is when your friend asks for advice on their love life, and you drop some serious wisdom (or what you think is wisdom). It's the "What if..." or "Maybe you should..." part of the conversation. In a corporate setting, it's that idea you nervously share during a brainstorming session, hoping your boss likes it.
usage_notes: Denotes the ongoing or general act of suggesting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bukas ang aming opisina sa anumang **pagmumungkahi** para mapabuti ang serbisyo.","translation":"Our office is open to any **suggestion** to improve the service."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagmumungkahi** na mag-outing ay sinang-ayunan ng lahat.","translation":"His **act of suggesting** an outing was approved by everyone."}]

translation: chipped, having a part sliced off
meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang bagay na may bahaging natanggal, nabawas, o nahiwa nang pahilis.
etymology: Mula sa salitang `may` (has/with) at `tapyas` (a slice, a chip).
original_explanation: 'Yung paborito mong baso na nahulog mo, ngayon may-tapyas na sa gilid. O 'yung puso mong nabawasan ng pag-asa, parang may-tapyas na rin. It means something is chipped or has a piece sliced off.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa isang pisikal na bagay na nabungi o isang bahagi na nahiwa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa pag-inom, baka masugatan ka dahil **may-tapyas** ang baso.","translation":"Be careful drinking, you might get cut because the glass is **chipped**."},{"sentence":"Ang mesa ay **may-tapyas** sa isang kanto.","translation":"The table has a **chip** on one corner."}]

translation: on the tip of one's tongue
meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyon na nangangahulugang malapit nang maalala o masabi ang isang bagay ngunit pansamantalang hindi matandaan.
etymology: Isang idyomatikong pagsasalin ng pariralang Ingles na "on the tip of the tongue".
original_explanation: That super frustrating feeling when you know the answer, but your brain is buffering. Parang nag-lag ang memory mo. You know it, you can almost taste it, pero ayaw lumabas. "Ano nga ulit pangalan nun... ay, nasa dulo ng dila ko lang!"
usage_notes: Ginagamit kapag ang isang tao ay nahihirapang alalahanin ang isang salita, pangalan, o impormasyon na alam naman niya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Teka, sino nga ulit yung artista na yun? Naku, **nasa dulo ng dila** ko lang!","translation":"Wait, who was that actor again? Oh, it's **on the tip of my tongue**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Daglat para sa pariralang Ingles na 'looking for buyer,' na nangangahulugang 'naghahanap ng mamimili.'
etymology: Daglat ng pariralang Ingles na 'looking for buyer.'
original_explanation: The hopeful prayer of every online seller, declutterer, and 'need-lang-ng-cash' person on the internet. You see this caption on a photo of pre-loved clothes or an old gadget. It's the digital equivalent of putting a 'For Sale' sign on your stuff.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa mga online selling platform at social media group para sa komersyo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**LFB**: Pre-loved na libro, good as new. PM for price.","translation":"**Looking for buyer**: Pre-loved book, good as new. PM for price."},{"sentence":"Mine na 'yan! 'Wag mo nang i-post na **LFB**.","translation":"That's mined! Don't post it as **LFB** anymore."}]

translation: Move!; Get out of the way!
meaning_filipino: Isang utos na nagsasabing umalis o lumayo sa daan.
etymology: From 'tabi' (side), as in 'move to the side'.
original_explanation: The OG Filipino way of saying 'get out of my way' before 'excuse me, po' became mainstream. It's what you shout when you're carrying something heavy and someone's blocking the path. It's abrupt, a bit rude, but very effective. Use with caution in the office.
usage_notes: Can be considered rude depending on tone and context. A more polite version is 'Padaan po' or 'Makikiraan po.' The phrase 'Tabi-tabi po' is a respectful variant used to ask unseen spirits to move aside.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tabi!** Mainit ang dala ko!","translation":"**Move!** I'm carrying something hot!"},{"sentence":"Sumigaw siya ng '**Tabi!**' para makadaan ang ambulansya.","translation":"He shouted '**Get out of the way!**' so the ambulance could pass."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng sukdulang pag-uugaling asal-hayop, malupit, o walang-awa.
original_explanation: This is what you scream at the kontrabida in a movie. It means someone is acting without humanity, conscience, or mercy. It's for the person who parks in two slots, cuts in line, and steals your lunch from the office fridge.
usage_notes: A strong insult implying someone has descended to the level of a beast in their actions. The negative and more traditional meaning of the word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang taong gumawa ng ganoong krimen ay **napakahayop**.","translation":"The person who committed such a crime is **truly beastly**."},{"sentence":"**Napakahayop** mo! Paano mo nagawa iyon sa sarili mong pamilya?","translation":"You are **so inhumane**! How could you do that to your own family?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan, makina, o lugar kung saan isinasagawa ang paghahabi ng tela, banig, o iba pang hinabing produkto.
original_explanation: This is the OG 3D printer for clothes. Before fast fashion and Shopee hauls, there was the 'habihan,' where patient hands turned thread into beautiful textiles. Think of it as your lola's secret workshop for making those intricate blankets that last forever.
usage_notes: Often refers to both the weaving device (loom) and the place of weaving (weaving mill/workshop).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming pamilya sa Ilocos ang may sariling **habihan** sa kanilang mga tahanan.","translation":"Many families in Ilocos have their own **loom** in their homes."},{"sentence":"Dinalaw namin ang isang **habihan** sa Iloilo upang makita kung paano ginagawa ang Hablon.","translation":"We visited a **weaving place** in Iloilo to see how Hablon is made."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malalim na paghinga at pagbuga ng hangin, karaniwang nagpapahiwatig ng pagod, kalungkutan, o ginhawa.
etymology: Tambalang salita mula sa 'bunton' (pile, heap) at 'hininga' (breath).
original_explanation: The universal Filipino expression for 'ay, nako.' It's the sound you make when you see your Meralco bill, when your crush walks by, when you finally sit down after a long day, or when you're stuck in EDSA traffic. A buntunghininga can mean a thousand things: frustration, relief, longing, or just plain being tired of it all. It's a 'hugot' in sound form.
usage_notes: The verb is 'bumuntunghininga'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malalim na **buntunghininga** ang pinakawalan niya nang matapos ang mahirap na pagsusulit.","translation":"He let out a deep **sigh** after finishing the difficult exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking kumpanya o grupo ng mga kumpanya na pinahihintulutan ng batas na kumilos bilang isang entidad para sa mga layuning pangnegosyo.
original_explanation: The reason why you have to wake up at 4 AM, brave the EDSA traffic, and sit in a cubicle for 8-10 hours. A korporasyon is that giant entity that gives you your sahod, your HMO, and your yearly 13th-month pay (which is already spent before you even get it). Welcome to the corporate world!
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtatrabaho siya sa isang malaking **korporasyon** sa Makati.","translation":"He works at a large **corporation** in Makati."},{"sentence":"Ang pagtatayo ng isang **korporasyon** ay nangangailangan ng malaking puhunan.","translation":"Building a **corporation** requires a huge investment."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan kung saan ang ulo ay nakatingala o nakataas, madalas dahil sa pagkamangha, pagmamataas, o paghahanap sa itaas.
original_explanation: That pose you make when you're looking at a tall building, a fireworks display, or when you're trying to stop a nosebleed. It's also the 'feeling mayaman' pose, walking with your chin up, looking down on no one but seeing everything from a higher perspective.
usage_notes: A specific posture of the head. Not a very common word in daily conversation but understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Namangha ang mga bata, lahat sila ay **nakalingay** habang pinapanood ang mga paputok.","translation":"The children were amazed, all of them had their **heads tilted back** while watching the fireworks."},{"sentence":"Naglakad siyang **nakalingay**, tila ba may hinahanap sa kalangitan.","translation":"He walked **with his head tilted up**, as if searching for something in the sky."}]

translation: to be able to weaken; to be able to debilitate
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang magdulot ng pagbawas sa lakas, sigla, o bisa ng isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: This is what a 12-hour shift does to you, or what happens to your Wi-Fi signal when it rains. It's the ability to drain the battery, literally or figuratively. "Ang sobrang pag-aalala ay maaaring makapagpahina ng iyong katawan."
usage_notes: Can refer to physical, emotional, or metaphorical weakening.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kakulangan sa tulog ay **makapagpapahina** ng resistensya.","translation":"Lack of sleep can **weaken** one's resistance."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **makapagpahina** sa iyo ang mga pagsubok.","translation":"Don't let challenges **be able to weaken** you."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mag-aaral na nasa ikalawang taon sa mataas na paaralan o kolehiyo.
original_explanation: You're no longer a clueless "freshie," but you're not yet a "junior" with one foot out the door. This is the year you think you know everything, but you really don't. Sa college, ito 'yung "sophomore slump" era, kung saan medyo nawawala na 'yung excitement ng first year at nagsisimula na ang tunay na hirap ng major subjects.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa konteksto ng sistema ng edukasyon na nakabase sa Amerika (high school at kolehiyo). Hindi na gaanong karaniwan ngayon sa sistema ng K-12, kung saan mas tiyak ang "Grade 8" o "Grade 12". Malawakang ginagamit pa rin para sa mga antas sa kolehiyo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isa na siyang **sopomor** sa kursong engineering.","translation":"He is now a **sophomore** in the engineering program."},{"sentence":"Mas mahirap daw ang mga asignatura kapag **sopomor** ka na.","translation":"They say the subjects are harder when you're a **sophomore**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglalaan ng salapi, oras, o lakas sa isang bagay (tulad ng negosyo o pag-aaral) na may layuning magkaroon ng kita o pakinabang sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: The adult version of 'plant a seed and watch it grow.' It's putting your money in stocks, crypto, or a small business, hoping it doesn't ghost you like your last situationship. It can also be emotional—'yung pag-invest mo ng feelings sa maling tao. A risky business, indeed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang edukasyon ay isang mahusay na **pamumuhunan** para sa kinabukasan.","translation":"Education is an excellent **investment** for the future."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan niya ang tungkol sa stock market para sa kanyang unang **pamumuhunan**.","translation":"She is studying about the stock market for her first **investment**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagmamasa ng harina o galapong upang maging isang malambot at buong masa, karaniwan sa paggawa ng tinapay o kakanin.
etymology: Possibly related to 'bilog' (round), as kneading often involves forming round shapes.
original_explanation: That satisfying (or tiring) process of making pandesal dough. It's like giving the dough a deep-tissue massage until it's smooth and elastic. If you see a panadero hard at work, malamang **bumilo** siya ng dough for hours.
usage_notes: Actor-focus verb in the completed aspect. Present: bumibilo. Future: bibilo. The object-focus form 'biluhin' is also common. The root 'bilo' is rarely used on its own.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maagang gumising ang panadero para **bumilo** ng masa para sa pandesal.","translation":"The baker woke up early to **knead** the dough for the pandesal."},{"sentence":"Siya ang **bumilo** ng galapong para sa aming bilo-bilo.","translation":"She was the one who **kneaded** the glutinous rice flour for our bilo-bilo."}]

translation: to develop a watery condition; to be filled with water
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng tubig o pagiging matubig ng isang bagay o lugar na dati ay wala o kaunti lang.
original_explanation: Yung sugat mo na ayaw gumaling at parang laging basa. 'Hala, nag-start nang magkatubig!' Also, the goal for your rice fields during planting season, or the unfortunate state of your basement during a typhoon.
usage_notes: Can refer to medical conditions (e.g., a wound exuding fluid) or agricultural/environmental situations (e.g., a field becoming irrigated or flooded).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kamutin ang pantal para hindi **magkatubig**.","translation":"Don't scratch the rash so it won't **develop a watery condition**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nang **magkatubig** ang bukid bago magtanim ng palay.","translation":"The field needs **to be filled with water** before planting rice."}]

translation: to become entangled or implicated with each other
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging sangkot o kasama sa isang masalimuot na sitwasyon o problema, kung saan ang bawat isa ay may kaugnayan sa iba.
original_explanation: This is when a simple issue becomes a group project of problems. Parang chismis na nagsimula sa isa, tapos biglang damay na 'yung buong barkada, 'yung kapitbahay, at 'yung pusa nila. It's a messy web of involvement where everyone gets dragged in. "Nadamay lang po ako!"
usage_notes: Often has a negative connotation, implying being dragged into trouble or a complex situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa isang malaking kaso ng korapsyon, hindi maiiwasang **magkadawit-dawit** ang maraming pangalan.","translation":"In a large corruption case, it's unavoidable for many names to **become implicated with each other**."},{"sentence":"Ayaw kong **magkadawit-dawit** pa tayo sa gulo nila.","translation":"I don't want us to **get entangled** any further in their mess."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marahan at magaan na pagdampi o paggalaw ng kamay sa ibabaw ng isang bagay o balat, karaniwang nagpapahiwatig ng pagmamahal, pag-aalaga, o pag-alo.
original_explanation: It's that gentle touch that says "Okay lang 'yan" without words. 'Yung paghaplos ng nanay mo sa buhok mo when you're feeling down, or 'yung pag-comfort ng jowa mo sa likod mo. It's the physical equivalent of a warm hug for the soul.
usage_notes: Connotes tenderness, care, and affection.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Humaplos** ang ina sa pisngi ng kanyang natutulog na anak.","translation":"The mother **caressed** the cheek of her sleeping child."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang pag-asa nang **humaplos** ang hangin sa kanyang mukha.","translation":"She felt hope when the wind **gently stroked** her face."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng popular na tinapay sa Pilipinas na bilog, malambot, at karaniwang binubudburan ng bread crumbs sa ibabaw.
etymology: From Spanish `pan de sal`, literally 'bread of salt'.
original_explanation: The undisputed king of Filipino breakfast. This isn't just bread; it's a cultural icon. It's the hot, fluffy reward for waking up early. You dip it in coffee, slice it for palaman (Reno Liver Spread, anyone?), or just eat it plain. Buying 'pandesal' from the corner bakery at 6 AM is a core Filipino experience. Its name means 'salt bread,' which is ironic because the modern version is actually slightly sweet.
usage_notes: A staple food in the Philippines, especially for breakfast. The name is often retained in English.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong almusal ang mainit na **pandesal** na isinasawsaw sa kape.","translation":"My favorite breakfast is hot **pandesal** dipped in coffee."},{"sentence":"Pabili po ng sampung pisong **pandesal**.","translation":"Can I buy ten pesos worth of **pandesal**, please."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging matamis sa panlasa, o ang kalidad ng pagiging kaaya-aya at kaibig-ibig sa kilos o salita.
etymology: From 'tamis' (sweet) + 'ka- -an' affix group, denoting the quality or essence of being sweet.
original_explanation: This is the flavor of your favorite milk tea at 100% sugar, or the feeling you get during the 'kilig' stage of a relationship. It's the 'sweet-pabebe' voice you use when asking for a favor. It can be literal (lasa) or figurative (ugali, alaala).
usage_notes: Can be used literally for taste or figuratively for pleasant memories, actions, or words.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko malilimutan ang **katamisan** ng iyong mga ngiti.","translation":"I will never forget the **sweetness** of your smiles."},{"sentence":"Hinahanap-hanap niya ang **katamisan** ng mangga mula sa kanilang probinsya.","translation":"He longs for the **sweetness** of the mangoes from their province."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat ng malalapit na magkakaibigan o kasama.
etymology: Syllabic reversal of "barkada," which is from Spanish "barcada" (boatload).
original_explanation: Your ultimate squad, your ride-or-die crew. The term was popularized by the long-running noontime show "Eat Bulaga!" It's a playful reversal of the syllables of "barkada." If you have 'dabarkads', you're never truly alone, whether it's for an impromptu beach trip or just sharing a single order of large fries.
usage_notes: Primarily informal and colloquial. Widely understood due to its media exposure.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging magkakasama ang aming **dabarkads** tuwing Sabado.","translation":"Our **squad** is always together every Saturday."},{"sentence":"Ipinakilala niya ang kanyang nobya sa buong **dabarkads**.","translation":"He introduced his girlfriend to the whole **group of friends**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon o pagtubo ng balahibo sa katawan, tulad ng sa mga hayop o sa ilang bahagi ng katawan ng tao.
etymology: From 'magka-' (to have or to grow) + 'balahibo' (body hair, fur, feather).
original_explanation: Means "to grow hair" or fur. This is what happens to your legs when you've been in quarantine too long and forgot where the razor is. Also describes your pet dog transforming into a fluffy cloud during the colder months.
usage_notes: Can refer to body hair on humans or fur/feathers on animals. For head hair, 'magkabuhok' or 'tubuan ng buhok' is used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **magkabalahibo** ang mga braso ng binatilyo.","translation":"The teenager's arms started **to grow hair**."},{"sentence":"Kapag malamig, **nagkakabalahibo** nang mas makapal ang mga aso.","translation":"When it's cold, dogs **grow** thicker **fur**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kasamang nag-aaral o nag-aral sa iisang paaralan.
original_explanation: A more formal-sounding but still common way to say "kaklase" (classmate) or "schoolmate." It's from the Spanish 'escuela'. You'd use this when talking about someone from the same school but not necessarily the same class or batch. "Uy, kaiskuwela ko 'yan sa UST dati!" (Hey, that person was my schoolmate at UST before!).
usage_notes: While often used interchangeably with 'kaklase' (classmate), 'kaiskuwela' specifically means 'schoolmate' and can refer to anyone from the same institution, regardless of batch or class.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakasalubong ko ang dati kong **kaiskuwela** sa mall kahapon.","translation":"I ran into my former **schoolmate** at the mall yesterday."},{"sentence":"Marami akong naging kaibigan na **kaiskuwela** noong high school.","translation":"I made many friends who were my **schoolmates** during high school."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng kalinga, atensyon, at suporta sa isang tao, hayop, o bagay upang mapanatili ang kalusugan, kaligtasan, at kaayusan nito.
original_explanation: The verb that powers OFWs, nurses, moms, and fur-parents everywhere. It's more than just 'to care'; it's the whole package—feeding, cleaning, protecting, worrying. It's what you do for a baby, a sick relative, a pet, or even your precious plantita collection. The '-an' suffix implies a more dedicated, ongoing action. It's the active form of love.
usage_notes: 'Mag-alaga' is the simpler form, often for a single subject. 'Mag-alagaan' can imply reciprocity or a more dedicated, ongoing process, but they are often used interchangeably.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang magkakapatid ay dapat **mag-alagaan** sa isa't isa.","translation":"Siblings should **take care of** each other."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **mag-alagaan** ng sanggol lalo na kung ikaw ay bagong magulang.","translation":"It's difficult to **take care of** a baby, especially if you are a new parent."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang estado ng pagkalito o kawalan ng malinaw na pag-iisip; litó at hindi malaman ang gagawin.
original_explanation: That feeling when you have 10 tabs open in your brain, 5 urgent emails, 2 missed calls from your mom, and someone asks you 'Kumain ka na?' You're not just busy, you're tuliro. It's the mental equivalent of a loading screen that's stuck at 99%.
usage_notes: Can also mean dizzy or disoriented.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naiwan siyang **tuliro** matapos ang biglaang anunsyo.","translation":"He was left **bewildered** after the sudden announcement."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong kausapin ngayon, **tuliro** pa ako sa dami ng trabaho.","translation":"Don't talk to me right now, I'm still **dazed** from the amount of work."}]

translation: snare; trap for birds or small animals
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng patibong o silo, karaniwang gawa sa lubid o alambre, para sa paghuli ng mga ibon o maliliit na hayop.
original_explanation: The OG way of catching things before Shopee sold nets. It's a snare or a trap, usually a loop that tightens when triggered. Think of it like a low-tech security system for catching your lunch in the province. Also, a good metaphor for feeling trapped in a dead-end job or a bad relationship: 'Parang nasa bitlingan ako.'
usage_notes: Primarily used in rural, agricultural, or hunting contexts. Less common in urban settings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglagay siya ng **bitlingan** sa gilid ng bukid para makahuli ng ibon.","translation":"He set a **snare** at the edge of the field to catch a bird."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malaking pawikan (Eretmochelys imbricata) na may matulis na nguso at magagandang kaliskis na ginagamit sa paggawa ng mga palamuti.
original_explanation: This isn't just any 'pagong' (turtle). Kala specifically refers to the hawksbill sea turtle, the one with the cool, patterned shell that sadly gets poached for accessories. Think of it as the high-fashion, endangered model of the turtle world.
usage_notes: Often confused with the more general term 'pawikan' (sea turtle) or 'pagong' (turtle/tortoise).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kala** ay isang nanganganib na uri ng pawikan dahil sa pangongolekta ng mga itlog at shell nito.","translation":"The **hawksbill sea turtle** is an endangered species because of the collection of its eggs and shell."}]

translation: to ride a car; to use a car
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsakay o paggamit ng kotse bilang sasakyan patungo sa isang lugar.
original_explanation: 'Yung desisyon mo araw-araw kung magko-commute ka ba at makikipagsiksikan, o mag-Grab/angkas, o kung mayaman ka, magkotse ka na lang. Basically, the act of choosing four wheels over your own two feet or public transpo.
usage_notes: Implies using a private car, as opposed to commuting via public transportation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas pinili niyang **magkotse** papuntang Baguio kaysa mag-bus.","translation":"He chose to **use a car** going to Baguio instead of taking a bus."},{"sentence":"Kung hindi umuulan, mas gugustuhin kong maglakad kaysa **magkotse**.","translation":"If it's not raining, I'd rather walk than **ride a car**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang elementong kemikal na may simbolong S at atomikong bilang na 16. Ito ay isang dilaw na solido sa karaniwang temperatura at kilala sa amoy nito kapag nasa anyong tambalan.
original_explanation: That yellow, stinky stuff they warned you about in chemistry class. It's the 'amoy-bulok-na-itlog' element found near volcanoes. In old Filipino horror, it's basically the official scent of hell and demons. So if you smell it, it's either a science experiment or a demon is nearby. Good luck.
usage_notes: Usually spelled with a capital 'A' when referring to the element, but can be lowercase. Often associated with volcanoes and the underworld in a folkloric context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayaman sa **asupre** ang mga lupaing malapit sa Bulkang Taal.","translation":"The lands near Taal Volcano are rich in **sulfur**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pook-kainan kung saan ang mga customer ay nagsisilbi sa kanilang sarili mula sa isang counter na may nakahandang pagkain.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Ingles na "cafeteria", na hango naman sa Espanyol na "cafetería".
original_explanation: This is your school or office lunch spot. It's where you find the cheapest ulam, the reliable pancit canton, and where all the chismis happens during lunch break. The cafeteria is the neutral ground for all departments, from accounting to HR.
usage_notes: Madalas na ipinagpapalit sa salitang "kanteen" (canteen).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng fish fillet sa **cafeteria** kanina.","translation":"I bought fish fillet at the **cafeteria** earlier."},{"sentence":"Puno ang **cafeteria** tuwing tanghalian.","translation":"The **cafeteria** is full during lunchtime."}]

translation: anyway, after all, in any case
meaning_filipino: Isang pang-ugnay na nagpapahiwatig ng pagbibigay-katuwiran, pagtanggap sa isang sitwasyon, o pagbubuod; sa kabila ng lahat.
original_explanation: The official word for when you're trying to justify an impulse buy. 'Sige na, bilhin ko na 'to. Tutal, sweldo naman bukas.' (Okay, I'll buy this. After all, it's payday tomorrow.) It's the verbal shrug that says 'might as well.'
usage_notes: Used to connect clauses, often to provide a reason or justification for a preceding or subsequent statement.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumain ka na, **tutal** nandito na rin lang ang pagkain.","translation":"Go ahead and eat, **anyway** the food is already here."},{"sentence":"Sasama na ako sa inyo, **tutal** wala naman akong gagawin sa bahay.","translation":"I'll go with you guys, **after all**, I have nothing to do at home."}]

translation: to go out, to exit, to appear
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpunta sa labas mula sa isang espasyong nakasara; maaari ring mangahulugang paglitaw o pagiging hayag.
etymology: From the root 'labas' (outside) with the infix '-um-'.
original_explanation: When your friend who's been ghosting everyone suddenly posts a story, "Uy, lumabas na siya ng kweba!" It means to go out of your house, to exit a room, or for a result/truth to come out. "Kailan lalabas ang resulta ng exam?" is the question that gives every student anxiety.
usage_notes: This is the actor-focus past tense form (naganap). It can also mean 'came out' for results, movies, or secrets. The phrase 'lumabas ka naman' is a common friendly invitation, meaning 'you should go out sometime'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lumabas** kami kagabi para maghapunan.","translation":"We **went out** last night for dinner."},{"sentence":"**Lumabas** na ang totoong kulay niya nang magkapera siya.","translation":"His true colors **appeared** when he got money."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpakita ng pagpabor o pagkagusto sa isang bagay, lalo na sa social media, sa pamamagitan ng pagpindot sa 'like' button. Ito ay isang salitang hiram na inangkupan ng panlaping Tagalog.
original_explanation: The past tense of 'liking' something on social media. You saw your crush's new profile pic, so you naglike. It's the digital equivalent of a secret admirer's nod. You've already done the deed; now you wait and see if they notice.
usage_notes: A modern, Taglish verb used primarily in the context of social media platforms like Facebook, Instagram, etc.
