usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Naglike** ako sa lahat ng litrato niya para mapansin niya ako.","translation":"I **liked** all of her photos so she would notice me."},{"sentence":"Sino ba ang **naglike** ng post mo na iyon?","translation":"Who **liked** that post of yours?"}]

meaning_filipino: Nakabitin o nakabagsak nang malambot at walang suporta.
original_explanation: Imagine a sad dog's ears, a plant that needs water, or even the 'panga' (jaw) of your friend after seeing their Meralco bill. That's **nakaluyloy**. It's hanging down, looking tired and defeated. "Nakaluyloy ang balikat" is the ultimate sign of pagod or disappointment.
usage_notes: Often used to describe body parts, plants, or fabric that are hanging limply. It carries a connotation of weakness, sadness, or lack of energy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakaluyloy** ang mga dahon ng halaman dahil sa init.","translation":"The leaves of the plant are **drooping** because of the heat."},{"sentence":"Umuwi siyang **nakaluyloy** ang mga balikat matapos matalo sa laro.","translation":"He went home with his shoulders **sagging** after losing the game."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na pansamantalang naninirahan o nangungupahan sa isang bahay o silid.
etymology: Nagmula sa "man-" + pag-uulit ng unang pantig ng ugat ("tu-") + "tuloy" (pumasok/manatili). Ang "manunuluyan" ay ang taong nananatili o nakikitira.
original_explanation: The person renting a room in your tita's house. They could be a student from the province, a BPO agent on the night shift, or just someone trying to save on rent. They're the reason why there's always a "Bawal maingay, may natutulog na boarder" sign.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng mga boarding house o pag-upa ng silid sa loob ng isang tahanan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May bagong **manunuluyan** sa kabilang kwarto.","translation":"There's a new **lodger** in the other room."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng matigas at maitim na kahoy na karaniwang ginagamit sa paggawa ng muwebles at mga instrumentong pangmusika. Tumutukoy din ito sa kulay na itim na itim.
original_explanation: Yung kulay ng pinakamahal na mesa sa bahay ng lola mo, o kaya yung kulay ng piano na pinapangarap mong tugtugin. It's that deep, rich, 'I have expensive taste' kind of black.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga piyesa ng chess ay gawa sa **eboni** at garing.","translation":"The chess pieces are made of **ebony** and ivory."},{"sentence":"Pininturahan niya ang pader ng kulay **eboni** para magmukhang elegante.","translation":"He painted the wall an **ebony** color to make it look elegant."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sangay ng serbisyong militar o ahensya ng gobyerno na responsable sa pagpapatupad ng batas sa katubigan at pagbabantay sa baybayin ng isang bansa.
original_explanation: The guardians of the archipelago's galaxy... este, coastlines. They're the ones who make sure our waters are safe, conduct search and rescue missions when a ferry gets into trouble, and generally keep an eye on everything happening along our 7,000+ islands. Think of them as the sea police.
usage_notes: Often refers to the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Philippine **Guwardakosta** ay nagsasagawa ng rescue operations sa lugar na tinamaan ng bagyo.","translation":"The Philippine **Coast Guard** is conducting rescue operations in the area hit by the typhoon."},{"sentence":"Sumali ang kapatid niya sa **guwardakosta** pagkatapos ng kolehiyo.","translation":"His brother joined the **coast guard** after college."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang talaan ng mga pang-araw-araw na pangyayari, transaksyon, o obserbasyon; maaari ring tumukoy sa isang pahayagan.
original_explanation: Before blogs, vlogs, and TikTok, there was the hurnalan. It's the ancestor of your 'daily dump' on Instagram stories. It could be your secret diary where you write your crushes, or the official logbook a security guard uses to track who comes in and out. Basically, the analog version of "What's on your mind?".
usage_notes: The word is now quite rare. 'Diyaryo' or 'pahayagan' is used for newspaper, and 'talaarawan' or 'diary' for a personal journal. It might be found in older literature.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinatala niya sa isang **hurnalan** ang lahat ng kanyang mga gastos.","translation":"He records all his expenses in a **journal**."}]

translation: to do something exceptionally well; to look amazing
meaning_filipino: Sa modernong paggamit, ito ay nangangahulugang pagtagumpayan o paggawâ ng isang bagay sa napakahusay na paraan. Maaari rin itong tumukoy sa pagiging kaakit-akit o sunod sa moda.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Ingles na "slay," na orihinal na nangangahulugang "pumatay." Ang modernong kahulugan nito ay nagmula sa kulturang drag at gay lingo sa Amerika.
original_explanation: Borrowed from African-American Vernacular English (AAVE) and popularized by gay lingo, 'slay' is the ultimate compliment. It's what you scream when your friend's OOTD is on point, when their presentation at work was flawless, or when they deliver the perfect comeback to a toxic tita. It means "You killed it!" or "Arrasou!" It's the verbal equivalent of a standing ovation.
usage_notes: Often used as an exclamation. Can be intensified with "malala" (e.g., "slay malala") or drawn out for emphasis (e.g., "slayyyy").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Girl, nag-**slay** ka sa performance mo kanina!","translation":"Girl, you **slayed** your performance earlier!"},{"sentence":"Tingnan mo yung outfit niya, ang ganda! **Slay**!","translation":"Look at her outfit, it's so beautiful! **Slay**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglilinis ng ngipin gamit ang sipilyo at toothpaste na naganap na.
original_explanation: Bes, nagsipilyo ka ba? Amoy Vicks 'yung hininga mo eh. Charot! Pero seryoso, good hygiene is a must, lalo na kung may ka-date ka. Don't forget to brush your tongue!
usage_notes: Past tense. The present tense is 'nagsisipilyo' and the future tense is 'magsisipilyo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagsipilyo** ako ng ngipin bago umalis ng bahay.","translation":"I **brushed my teeth** before leaving the house."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos kumain, **nagsipilyo** agad ang bata.","translation":"After eating, the child immediately **brushed his teeth**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa tela o anumang materyal na gagamitin o nilalaan para sa paggawa ng salawal o pantalon.
original_explanation: This is the stuff you buy at the fabric store to make pants. It's the 'pantalunin' but for 'salawal'. You go to Divisoria and tell the tindera, "Ate, pabili ng salawalin," and she'll show you rolls of denim, cotton, or linen. It's the 'potential pants' fabric.
usage_notes: Not a common word. 'Tela para sa pantalon' is more frequently used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng telang maong na gagawing **salawalin**.","translation":"Mom bought denim fabric to be used as **material for pants**."},{"sentence":"Maganda ang kalidad ng **salawalin** na ito.","translation":"The quality of this **pants material** is good."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng pisikal na lakas, kapangyarihan, impluwensya, o matinding antas ng tunog o epekto.
original_explanation: The most versatile Pinoy adjective. It can be your buff gym bro (malakas ang katawan), your tita with connections to every government office (malakas sa gobyerno), the videoke next door at 2 AM (malakas ang soundtrip), or your coffee preference (barako, malakas ang tama). It's all about intensity.
usage_notes: A very common and versatile word. Its specific meaning (strong, loud, influential) is determined by context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Malakas** ang katawan ng boksingerong iyon.","translation":"That boxer's body is **strong**."},{"sentence":"Pakihinaan mo ang radyo, masyadong **malakas**.","translation":"Please turn down the radio, it's too **loud**."},{"sentence":"Kilala siyang **malakas** sa city hall kaya nakukuha niya ang gusto niya.","translation":"He is known to be **influential** at city hall, that's why he gets what he wants."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbaon o pagpasok nang malalim at biglaan ng isang matulis na bagay.
original_explanation: Like when a hugot line *really* hits you. 'Bes, tumarak sa puso ko 'yung sinabi niya.' It's also what happens when you step on a nail or when Cupid's arrow (or your crush's smile) finds its mark. It's sharp, sudden, and you definitely feel it.
usage_notes: Often used for sharp, pointed objects. Figuratively, it's used for words or feelings that have a deep, sharp impact.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumarak** ang pako sa gulong ng kanyang bisikleta.","translation":"The nail **pierced** the tire of his bicycle."},{"sentence":"Ang mga salita niya ay tila kutsilyong **tumarak** sa aking damdamin.","translation":"His words were like a knife that **stuck into** my feelings."}]

translation: to get someone's consent; to make someone say yes
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkuha ng pagsang-ayon o "oo" mula sa isang tao; ang pagkumbinsi sa isang tao na sumang-ayon.
original_explanation: This is the art of "panliligaw" or sales pitching. You're trying to get that coveted "oo" from your crush, your boss, or your parents when you ask for more allowance. It's the final boss level of persuasion.
usage_notes: Not a very common word in modern conversation, more formal or literary. "Kumbinsihin" or "pasang-ayunin" are more frequently used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **magpaoo** sa kanyang mga magulang tungkol sa kanyang planong mag-abroad.","translation":"He tried to **get his parents to say yes** to his plan of going abroad."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **magpaoo** sa isang taong sarado na ang isip.","translation":"It's difficult to **get someone's consent** when their mind is already closed."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangatnig na nag-uugnay ng dalawang sugnay, na nagpapahayag ng kondisyon o panahon. Ito ay ang pinaikling anyo ng salitang 'kapag'.
original_explanation: The shorter, more chill version of 'kapag'. It's the 'if' in your 'what ifs' and the 'when' in your 'see you when I see you.' You use it a million times a day without thinking. 'Pag may time,' 'Pag-uwi mo,' 'Pag galit ka'... it's the glue of everyday Filipino sentences.
usage_notes: 'Pag' is used ubiquitously in informal and spoken Tagalog. 'Kapag' is generally preferred in formal writing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uuwi ako nang maaga **pag** natapos ko ang trabaho.","translation":"I will go home early **when** I finish my work."},{"sentence":"**Pag** may tiyaga, may nilaga.","translation":"**If** there is perseverance, there is success (lit. stew)."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang kulay na nawalan ng tingkad o sigla; maputla.
original_explanation: Parang kulay ng luma mong t-shirt na paborito mong isuot noong high school, ngayon makapusyaw na at halos di na makilala ang print. O kaya parang kulay ng balat mo after a week ng matinding trabaho at kulang sa tulog—medyo pale and washed out.
usage_notes: Often used to describe colors of fabric, paint, or even skin tone when someone is sick or anemic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Makapusyaw** na ang kulay ng dati'y matingkad na pader.","translation":"The color of the once vibrant wall is now **pale**."},{"sentence":"Naging **makapusyaw** ang kaniyang mga labi dahil sa sakit.","translation":"Her lips turned **pale** because of her illness."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian o kalidad ng pagiging masining; pagkakaroon ng galing o hilig sa sining.
original_explanation: This is the quality that makes your friend's Instagram feed look like a magazine, or how your tita arranges the fruit platter like it's a museum piece. It's the flair, the aesthetic, the 'extra' touch that turns something ordinary into something beautiful. It's not just creativity ('pagkamapanlikha'), it's the *style* in which it's executed.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa kalidad ng pagiging masining, na maaaring ilapat sa isang tao, bagay, o kilos.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Makikita ang **pagkamasining** ng mga Pilipino sa kanilang mga makukulay na piyesta.","translation":"The **artistry** of Filipinos can be seen in their colorful fiestas."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piyesa ng musika na nilikha para sa dalawang mang-aawit o manunugtog; o ang mismong pagtatanghal ng dalawang tao.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na 'dueto' o Italyano na 'duetto'.
original_explanation: Your go-to videoke move with your bestie, probably singing a Regine Velasquez and Ogie Alcasid song. It's the musical equivalent of a 'sana all' moment when a couple sings it perfectly.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa mismong komposisyon ng musika o sa pagtatanghal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging sikat ang kanilang **duweto** ng kantang 'Bakit Ngayon Ka Lang?'","translation":"Their **duet** of the song 'Bakit Ngayon Ka Lang?' became famous."},{"sentence":"Nagpapraktis sila para sa isang **duweto** sa darating na paligsahan.","translation":"They are practicing for a **duet** in the upcoming competition."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghamak, pag-aglahi, o pagtawa sa isang tao o bagay sa paraang mapanukso at mapang-insulto.
etymology: From 'pan-' (prefix indicating action) + reduplication of the first syllable of 'libak' (scorn, mockery).
original_explanation: This is what happens in a group chat when someone posts an old, embarrassing photo of you. It's the high-level, more venomous version of 'asar.' It's not just teasing; it's teasing with the intent to belittle. The fuel of bashers and trolls online.
usage_notes: A strong word indicating intense and often malicious ridicule.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya pinansin ang **panlilibak** ng kanyang mga kaaway.","translation":"He ignored the **mockery** of his enemies."},{"sentence":"Puno ng **panlilibak** ang mga komentong natanggap niya sa social media.","translation":"The comments he received on social media were full of **ridicule**."}]

translation: To dress formally, to act formally
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aayos ng sarili sa pormal na paraan, sa pananamit man o sa kilos, para sa isang partikular na okasyon.
etymology: From the Tagalog word 'pormal', which is derived from the Spanish 'formal'.
original_explanation: When your crush's parents invite you to dinner and you have to trade your usual pambahay shorts and t-shirt for something decent. You iron your shirt, comb your hair, and try not to say 'lods' or 'sana all'. That's 'pumormal'. It's leveling up your porma for a special occasion.
usage_notes: A colloquial or slang term formed by treating the adjective 'pormal' (formal) as a verb root. Common in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uy, **pumormal** ka yata ngayon, saan ang lakad mo?","translation":"Hey, you seem to have **dressed up formally** today, where are you going?"},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **pumormal** para sa kasal bukas.","translation":"We need **to dress formally** for the wedding tomorrow."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang espasyo o bahagi sa loob ng isang gusali o bahay na may pader, sahig, at kisame.
original_explanation: Your personal kingdom, sanctuary, or 'bodega' for all the stuff you bought online. It's where you take your Zoom calls (business on top, pambahay on the bottom) and where you practice your TikTok dances. The one place your mom will always tell you to clean.
usage_notes: Often used as a prefix for specific types of rooms, like 'silid-aralan' (classroom).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakilinis ang iyong **silid** bago ka umalis.","translation":"Please clean your **room** before you leave."},{"sentence":"Maliit lang ang **silid** na inuupahan ko sa Maynila.","translation":"The **room** I'm renting in Manila is just small."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng bagay na madaling magliyab o masunog.
original_explanation: Ito yung warning label sa mga lata ng spray paint at bote ng alcohol. In hugot terms, ito yung kaibigan mong "masilab" ang ulo—madaling mag-init o magalit. Konting asar lang, nagliliyab na sa galit. Handle with care!
usage_notes: Can be used literally for materials or figuratively for a person's temper ('masilabin ang ulo' means hot-headed).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa paggamit ng gas dahil ito ay isang **masilab** na materyal.","translation":"Be careful when using gas as it is a **flammable** material."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang muling isipin o balikan sa gunita ang isang nakaraang pangyayari, impormasyon, o karanasan.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping pandiwa na `ma-` at salitang-ugat na `alaala`. Ito ay isang karaniwang pagpapaikli ng `maalaala`.
original_explanation: The shorter, more chill version of 'maalaala'. This is what you say when you suddenly remember you have a 11:59 PM deadline. "Uy, teka, may naalala ako!" It's the brain's pop-up notification. Ito ang ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_notes: Habang ang `maalaala` ang pormal na anyo, ang `maalala` ang mas nangingibabaw sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap. Pareho silang anyong potensyal ng pandiwa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigla kong **naalala** na may usapan pala kami ngayon.","translation":"I suddenly **remembered** that we had an appointment today."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko **maalala** ang pangalan niya, pero pamilyar ang mukha niya.","translation":"I can't **recall** his name, but his face is familiar."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi nagtataglay ng sapat na abilidad, lakas, o kapangyarihan upang maisagawa ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: Feeling you're walang-kakayahan is that 'impostor syndrome' hitting hard. It's when you're asked to do a V-lookup in Excel and you just stare at the screen. It can describe a person who is genuinely incompetent, or it can be a feeling of helplessness in a difficult situation, like trying to fix the wifi when the whole neighborhood is down.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin upang ilarawan ang pangkalahatang kawalan ng kakayahan ng isang tao o ang partikular na kawalan ng kakayahang gawin ang isang gawain.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiramdam niya ay **walang-kakayahan** siyang tulungan ang kanyang pamilya.","translation":"He feels **incapable** of helping his family."},{"sentence":"Ang komite ay napatunayang **walang-kakayahan** na lutasin ang problema.","translation":"The committee was proven **incompetent** to solve the problem."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginawa o ipinagawa ang isang bagay nang labag sa kalooban o sa pamamagitan ng pamimilit.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na `pilit` (puwersa, paggiit) at gitlaping `-in-` na nagsasaad ng nagdaang kilos sa pokus ng layon.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're super full but your Tita insists you eat another serving of her spaghetti ("Sige na, tikman mo lang!"). That's being `pinilit`. It's doing something you don't want to do because of external pressure. From finishing your vegetables to smiling for a picture when you're not in the mood, `pinilit` is the verb for reluctant actions. "Pinilit lang po, promise."
usage_notes: Past tense, object-focus form of the verb `pilitin` (to force). The actor-focus counterpart is `pumilit` (to insist) or `nagpilit` (insisted).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pinilit** niya akong sumama kahit ayoko.","translation":"He/She **forced** me to come even though I didn't want to."},{"sentence":"**Pinilit** niyang ngumiti para sa litrato.","translation":"She **forced** a smile for the picture."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bilang na katumbas ng sampung sampu; ang numerong 100.
original_explanation: The blue bill with Manuel Roxas on it (pre-polymer). The price of your fancy milk tea (before add-ons). The grade you're trying to get in your exam. It's the OG 'isang daan'.
usage_notes: Can function as an adjective (sandaang piso) or a noun (bigyan mo ako ng sandaan).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroon akong **sandaan** na piso sa aking pitaka.","translation":"I have **one hundred** pesos in my wallet."},{"sentence":"Mahigit **sandaan** katao ang dumalo sa pagtitipon.","translation":"More than **one hundred** people attended the gathering."}]

meaning_filipino: Matuklasan o mahanap ang isang bagay, lugar, o kaalaman na hindi pa dati nalalaman.
etymology: From Spanish `descubrir` (to discover), adapted into Tagalog with the `ma-` verb affix.
original_explanation: That 'Aha!' moment when you find a new hole-in-the-wall resto with epic sisig, or when you finally figure out your partner's Netflix password. It's the feeling of uncovering something new, whether it's a new planet or a new 'budol' find on Shopee.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marami pa tayong kailangang **madiskubre** tungkol sa ating kasaysayan.","translation":"We still have much **to discover** about our history."},{"sentence":"Ang galing niya, **nadiskubre** niya ang lunas sa sakit.","translation":"He's amazing, he **discovered** the cure for the illness."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal para sa "ama" o "tatay," na nabuo sa pamamagitan ng pagbabaligtad ng mga pantig ng salitang "pater" (Latin para sa ama) o "father".
etymology: Mula sa balbal na pagbabaligtad ng mga pantig ng salitang Ingles na "father" o Latin na "pater".
original_explanation: The OG "lods." This is 90s slang for 'father,' created by flipping the syllables of 'pater' (from Latin) or 'father.' It's the cooler, more retro way of saying 'dad' before 'fadir' became a thing. Your tito probably still uses this.
usage_notes: Isang salitang balbal na karaniwang ginagamit sa di-pormal na pakikipag-usap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-text ang **erpat** ko, umuwi na raw ako.","translation":"My **dad** texted, he said I should go home now."},{"sentence":"Galing sa **erpat** ko itong luma kong relo.","translation":"This old watch of mine is from my **father**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tiyak na oras o panahon na itinalaga para sa isang gawain o pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is the Visayan cousin of "deadline" that sometimes visits Manila. It’s that specific moment you promised your client you'd send the report, or the time you agreed to meet for milk tea. It has more weight than just 'oras'; it feels more... destined. "Ito na ang takna."
usage_notes: Pangunahing salita sa Cebuano, ngunit ginagamit sa pampanitikang Tagalog o ng mga nagsasalita na may lahing Bisaya. Katumbas ng "takdang oras."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumating siya sa itinakdang **takna** ng kanilang pagkikita.","translation":"He arrived at the **appointed time** of their meeting."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggamit ng makinilya upang makapagsulat o makapaglimbag ng teksto sa papel.
original_explanation: 'Makinilyahin' is the OG 'to type.' It's the verb form for using a 'makinilya'. When your boss in the 80s told you, 'Makinilyahin mo itong report,' it meant you were in for a long day of hammering keys, dealing with ink ribbons, and praying you don't make a typo that requires starting the whole page over.
usage_notes: Kadalasan, ginagamit na lamang sa mga kontekstong pangkasaysayan o kapag tumutukoy mismo sa paggamit ng makinilya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **makinilyahin** ang tatlong kopya ng liham na ito.","translation":"I need **to type** three copies of this letter (on a typewriter)."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aralan niyang **makinilyahin** nang mabilis ang mga dokumento.","translation":"She studied how **to type** documents quickly."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang hanapbuhay ay ang pagluluto at pagbebenta ng busa o binusang mais.
etymology: From `mag-` (prefix indicating actor/doer) + `bu-` (repetition of the first syllable of the root for actor) + `busa` (to pop corn).
original_explanation: The original OG of movie night snacks. Before your microwave popcorn existed, the `magbubusa` was the one making that irresistible smell of toasted corn waft through the plaza or outside the movie theater. They're the masters of the giant wok, shaking it like they're mixing a potion for ultimate happiness.
usage_notes: This term is specific and not as common now with commercial popcorn brands, but people will know it, especially in provincial settings or during fiestas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili tayo ng popcorn sa **magbubusa** bago magsimula ang parada.","translation":"Let's buy popcorn from the **popcorn vendor** before the parade starts."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng prutas na tropikal (pang-agham na pangalan: Mangifera indica) na may dilaw at matamis na laman kapag hinog, at berde at maasim naman kapag hilaw.
original_explanation: The undisputed National Fruit and the GOAT of all fruits. Whether it's hilaw na mangga with bagoong, a perfectly ripe carabao mango that's sweet as a promise, or a mango graham shake from the mall, mangga is life. It's the flavor of Philippine summer.
usage_notes: Refers to both the fruit and the tree.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong panghimagas ang hinog na **mangga**.","translation":"My favorite dessert is ripe **mango**."}]

translation: act of moving over; sliding or shifting position
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-usog o paglipat ng kaunti mula sa isang posisyon, karaniwang habang nakaupo.
original_explanation: The classic jeepney scenario: "Ipod-ipod lang po, para makaupo lahat." It's the subtle art of scooting over on a bench to make space for someone else, or inching away from someone who's invading your personal space. It's the polite shuffle we do in crowded places.
usage_notes: Often used with "kaunti" (a little). Synonymous with "pag-usog."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang marahang **pag-ipod** ay nagbigay ng puwang para sa bagong dating.","translation":"His gentle **act of moving over** gave space for the newcomer."},{"sentence":"Isang senyas lang ay sapat na para sa kanilang **pag-ipod** palayo.","translation":"One signal was enough for them to **shift** away."}]

translation: a large, ancient type of boat
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malaki at sinaunang sasakyang pandagat na ginagamit para sa paglalakbay at kalakalan, karaniwang mas malaki kaysa sa isang bangka.
etymology: From Malay 'birai' (decorated edge of a boat).
original_explanation: This is the OG ship of the pre-colonial Philippines. Think of it as the galleon's ancestor, a large boat used by our ancestors for long-distance travel and trade. It's not your typical bangka; it's a vessel with history.
usage_notes: An archaic or historical term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga ninuno natin ay naglakbay gamit ang malalaking **biray**.","translation":"Our ancestors traveled using large **biray** (boats)."},{"sentence":"Nakalarawan sa lumang mapa ang isang **biray** na puno ng mga mangangalakal.","translation":"A **biray** full of traders is depicted on the old map."}]

meaning_filipino: Sistema ng pagsulat ng sinaunang Ehipto na gumagamit ng mga larawan at simbolo.
original_explanation: The original emojis. Also, what your doctor's handwriting looks like. Or your crush's mixed signals. 'Ano ba talaga ibig sabihin nito?!' You need a Rosetta Stone just to figure it out.
usage_notes: Can be used metaphorically to describe any writing that is hard to read or understand.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng mga arkeologo ang mga **heroglipiko** sa pader ng piramide.","translation":"The archaeologists are studying the **hieroglyphics** on the pyramid wall."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko mabasa ang sulat-kamay mo, parang **heroglipiko**!","translation":"I can't read your handwriting, it's like **hieroglyphics**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Pahalagahan, bigyan ng paggalang, o tantiyahin ang halaga o sukat ng isang bagay o tao.
original_explanation: A two-in-one word. It's either you're trying to guess the price of an item sa Shopee ('Estimahin mo nga.') or you're giving someone the respect they deserve, like how you should value your elders or even your ex's new partner para walang gulo. To value someone or something.
usage_notes: The meaning can shift heavily based on context, from a purely mathematical estimation to a deep emotional valuation of respect.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **estimahin** nang mabuti ang gastos para sa proyekto.","translation":"The project costs need to be **estimated** carefully."},{"sentence":"Dapat mong **estimahin** ang mga taong tumutulong sa iyo.","translation":"You should **value** the people who help you."}]

translation: to act snobbish towards someone; to snub
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita ng ugaling mapagmataas o hindi pagpansin sa isang tao sa intensyonal na paraan.
original_explanation: This is the action of being a suplada/suplado. It's when you deliberately ignore someone's "hi," roll your eyes when they speak, or give them the cold shoulder. "Huwag mo akong suplahan!" is what you say when your friend is giving you the silent treatment after you ate the last piece of pizza.
usage_notes: A verb of action. Often used in commands or descriptions of interactions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sinusuplahan** niya ang lahat ng nanliligaw sa kanya.","translation":"She **snubs** everyone who is courting her."},{"sentence":"Bakit mo ako **sinuplahan** kanina sa mall?","translation":"Why did you **act snobbish** towards me at the mall earlier?"}]

meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng gabay, payo, o direksyon ang isang tao o pangkat.
original_explanation: This is the action of being a human Waze. It’s what a mentor does for a newbie, what a thesis adviser does for a student, or what you pray for God to do when you're facing a tough choice. "Lord, please **patnubayan** mo po ako." It's actively showing someone the way.
usage_notes: Often used in prayers or formal requests for guidance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawa'y **patnubayan** ka ng Panginoon sa iyong mga paglalakbay.","translation":"May the Lord **guide** you in your travels."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kabuuang halaga na nalikom mula sa pangangalap ng pondo o donasyon.
etymology: From the root 'ilak' (to solicit), with affixes 'pinang-' and '-an'. It refers to the result or collection from the act of soliciting.
original_explanation: It's the contents of that donation box passed around during a cause-oriented event, or the GCash transfers you get for a friend's hospital bills. The 'pinangilakan' is the fruit of everyone's bayanihan spirit.
usage_notes: Primarily used as a noun to refer to the collected amount from fundraising. Can also be a verb in other forms (e.g., pinangilakan ng donasyon ang mga tao - solicited donations from the people).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gagamitin ang **pinangilakan** para sa pagpapatayo ng bagong kapilya.","translation":"The **proceeds** will be used to build the new chapel."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang naging **pinangilakan** sa isinagawang fund-raising concert.","translation":"The **proceeds** from the fund-raising concert were large."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagpapalipad ng sasakyang panghimpapawid; isang bagay o nilalang na may kakayahang lumipad.
original_explanation: Before we called them 'piloto,' this was the cool term. A 'manlilipad' is literally a 'flier.' It has a slightly old-school, adventurous vibe, like someone from a black-and-white movie with goggles and a scarf. Today, you might use it more poetically to describe a bird, a kite, or even your dreams taking flight (charot!).
usage_notes: 'Piloto' is now the common term for an aircraft pilot. 'Manlilipad' is less common and can sound poetic or archaic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang maging isang **manlilipad** at ikutin ang buong mundo.","translation":"He dreams of becoming an **aviator** and traveling the whole world."},{"sentence":"Ang agila ay isang magaling na **manlilipad**.","translation":"The eagle is an excellent **flier**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hanay ng mga tao o bagay na nakaayos sa isang tuwid na linya.
original_explanation: In the office, this is what you deal with in Excel sheets (row 1, row 2, etc.). In the cinema, it's where you find your seat (Row C, Seat 5). It's the horizontal version of a 'column'. Basically, a straight line of things. The Tagalog equivalent is 'hanay', but in tech and specific seating contexts, 'row' is king.
usage_notes: Primarily used in technical contexts (like spreadsheets) or for seating arrangements (cinemas, airplanes). The native word 'hanay' is more general.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisama lahat ng data mula sa **row** 5 hanggang **row** 20.","translation":"Please sum up all the data from **row** 5 to **row** 20."},{"sentence":"Nasa anong **row** ang upuan natin sa sinehan?","translation":"What **row** are our seats in at the cinema?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagliligtas sa isang tao, bagay, o hayop mula sa kapahamakan, panganib, o kamatayan.
original_explanation: That feeling when your friend saves you a seat during a crowded MRT ride, or when GrabFood arrives just as you're about to faint from hunger. That's 'sagip' in action. It's the dramatic rescue, whether from a flood or from being 'seen-zoned'.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of natural disasters (bagyo, baha, lindol) or life-threatening situations. The verb forms are 'sumagip' (actor-focus) and 'sagipin' (object-focus).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinikap ng mga bumbero na **sagipin** ang pusang naipit sa puno.","translation":"The firefighters tried to **rescue** the cat stuck in the tree."},{"sentence":"Ang mabilis na pag-iisip niya ang **sumagip** sa buong team mula sa kapalpakan.","translation":"His quick thinking **saved** the whole team from failure."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kabuuan ng mga ninuno o lahi na pinagmulan ng isang tao o pamilya.
etymology: Mula sa "pinag-" + "apo" + "-han". Tumutukoy sa linya ng mga inapo mula sa isang ninuno.
original_explanation: Your family tree, but make it deep Tagalog. Ito yung source ng "mana-mana lang 'yan" comments sa family reunion kapag may naging successful (o naging pasaway) sa pamilya. It's your bloodline, your 'pinanggalingan.'
usage_notes: Isang pormal at medyo bihirang salita para sa lahi o angkan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagmamalaki niya ang kanilang marangal na **pinag-apuhan**.","translation":"He is proud of their noble **ancestry**."},{"sentence":"Mababakas sa kanyang mga kilos ang maharlikang **pinag-apuhan**.","translation":"His noble **lineage** can be traced in his actions."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong katutubo o naninirahan sa rehiyon ng Kabisayaan sa Pilipinas, o ang pangkat ng mga wikang sinasalita sa rehiyong iyon.
etymology: From Old Malay viṣaya ("region, territory, province"), from Sanskrit विषय (viṣaya, "sphere of influence, country, kingdom").
original_explanation: A person from the beautiful central islands of the Philippines (the Visayas!). They're known for being brave, hardworking, and having a distinct, often musical accent that Manila folks sometimes unfairly imitate. They're the source of amazing food (lechon!), beautiful beaches, and a whole family of languages (like Cebuano, Hiligaynon, Waray) that are NOT just "dialects" of Tagalog. Don't make that mistake.
usage_notes: Refers to both the people and the group of languages. When referring to the language, it's more precise to specify (e.g., Cebuano, Ilonggo/Hiligaynon), but "Bisaya" is often used as a general term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **Bisaya** ang nagtatrabaho dito sa Maynila.","translation":"Many **Visayans** work here in Manila."},{"sentence":"Nakakaintindi ka ba ng **Bisaya**?","translation":"Do you understand **Visayan (language)**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang serye ng mga panalangin sa Katolisismo, o ang kuwintas ng mga butil na ginagamit bilang gabay sa pagdarasal nito.
original_explanation: The ultimate Catholic accessory. It's both a powerful prayer tool and something you see hanging from the rearview mirror of jeepneys and buses for divine protection against traffic and accidents. Your lola probably has one in every bag and will give you one to keep you safe on your flight abroad.
usage_notes: Refers to both the set of prayers (e.g., 'magdasal ng rosaryo') and the beaded necklace used for it (e.g., 'isang kuwintas na rosaryo').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gabi-gabi kaming nagdarasal ng **rosaryo** bilang isang pamilya.","translation":"We pray the **rosary** as a family every night."},{"sentence":"Isinabit niya ang **rosaryo** sa leeg ng imahen ni Mama Mary.","translation":"She hung the **rosary** on the neck of the statue of Mama Mary."}]

translation: to do something early or in advance; to be proactive
meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng isang bagay nang mas maaga sa takdang oras upang makaiwas sa pagmamadali o problema.
etymology: From the root word 'agap' (promptness, being early) with the infix '-um-'.
original_explanation: This is the student who finishes their thesis a month before the deadline. This is you leaving for the airport 5 hours before your flight 'para sure'. It's the opposite of being a 'crammer'. Umagap is the life motto of every Tita who brings baon and a first-aid kit to a picnic. Be prepared, be early.
usage_notes: Conveys a sense of being proactive and prepared.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **umagap** sa pag-apply para hindi ka maunahan sa slot.","translation":"You need to **apply early** so you don't lose the slot to someone else."},{"sentence":"Lagi siyang **umaagap** sa pagbabayad ng bills.","translation":"He always **pays** his bills **in advance**."}]

translation: to act as a midwife; to deliver a baby
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtulong sa isang ina sa proseso ng panganganak; ang pagsasagawa ng pagpapaanak.
etymology: From `magpa-` (causative prefix) + `anak` (child). Literally, 'to cause to child' or 'to cause to be born'.
original_explanation: This is the OG frontliner role. Before hospitals became the norm, there was the 'hilot' or 'kumadrona' in the barrio who would `magpaanak`. It's the high-stakes, high-pressure job of welcoming a new human into the world, usually with just hot water, towels, and a whole lot of skill and prayer.
usage_notes: Refers to the person assisting the birth (midwife, doctor), not the mother giving birth. The mother 'nanganak' or 'nanganganak'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lola niya ay isang kilalang hilot na **nagpapaanak** sa kanilang baryo.","translation":"Her grandmother was a well-known traditional midwife who **delivers babies** in their village."},{"sentence":"Pumunta sila sa ospital para **magpaanak** sa isang doktor.","translation":"They went to the hospital to **have a doctor deliver the baby**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpapahinga ng katawan at isipan sa isang kalagayan ng kawalang-malay; ang nakaraang anyo ng pandiwang 'matulog'.
original_explanation: What you did last night for 8 hours (sana all!) or what you did for 20 minutes during your lunch break. It's the past tense of sleeping. 'Yung ginawa mo sa sinehan nung boring 'yung movie.
usage_notes: Ito ang perpektibo o pangnagdaang anyo ng pandiwang 'matulog'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaga siyang **natulog** kagabi dahil sa pagod.","translation":"He **slept** early last night because of fatigue."},{"sentence":"**Natulog** ako nang mahimbing pagkatapos ng mahabang araw.","translation":"I **slept** soundly after a long day."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng makatas na halaman na gumagapang, may maliliit at makakapal na dahon, at karaniwang itinuturing na damo ngunit nakakain at masustansya.
original_explanation: This is the 'survivor' plant you see growing in the cracks of the sidewalk. You probably thought it was just a weed, but your lola knows it's a secret superfood. It's kinda sour, kinda salty, and perfect for ensalada or sinigang when you're on a budget. The ultimate 'don't judge a book by its cover' vegetable.
usage_notes: Also known as 'ngalog' or 'olasiman' in other Philippine languages. It is known for its high Omega-3 fatty acid content.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap gawing ensalada ang sariwang dahon ng **kulasiman**.","translation":"The fresh leaves of **purslane** are delicious when made into a salad."},{"sentence":"Tumutubo ang **kulasiman** kahit saan, kaya madali itong hanapin.","translation":"**Purslane** grows anywhere, so it's easy to find."}]

translation: to toast; to pan-fry without oil
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagluto ng isang bagay sa isang mainit na kawali nang walang mantika o anumang likido, tulad ng pag-gisa ng butil, mani, o niyog.
original_explanation: Before you get your glorious *sinangag* (garlic fried rice), you must first understand *sangag* the verb. It's the act of toasting something dry in a hot pan. Think toasting garlic until it's fragrant, roasting peanuts, or making desiccated coconut. It's the 'dry' part of the cooking process, the opposite of *gisa* which uses oil. It's the first step to unlocking a deeper flavor.
usage_notes: This is a root word. It needs affixes to become a verb, e.g., 'sangagin' (to toast something), 'isangag' (to toast something).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **isangag** muna ang bigas para sa champorado.","translation":"The rice needs to be **toasted** first for the champorado."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-**sangag** ng bawang ay nagpapalabas ng aroma nito.","translation":"Toasting the garlic brings out its aroma."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pang-ugnay na ginagamit sa paghahambing ng dalawang tao, bagay, o ideya na hindi magkapantay o magkatulad ang katangian, na nagpapakilala sa bagay na may mas mababang antas.
original_explanation: The ultimate comparison tool in Tagalog. 'Mas bet ko 'to kaysa dyan.' It's the word you use when you have to choose between two Jollibee chicken parts (thigh vs. drumstick) or two potential 'ships. It establishes a hierarchy of preference, putting one thing over another.
usage_notes: Ginagamit kasunod ng isang pang-uring pahambing tulad ng 'mas' o 'higit pa'. Madalas itong sinusundan ng 'sa' (para sa mga bagay) o 'kay' (para sa mga tao).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas gusto kong maglakad **kaysa** sumakay ng dyip.","translation":"I prefer to walk **than** ride a jeep."},{"sentence":"Para sa kanya, mas mahalaga ang karanasan **kaysa** pera.","translation":"For him, experience is more important **than** money."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang simbolo o salita na kumakatawan sa isang bilang o kantidad; numero.
etymology: Possibly a blend of 'tala-' (list, record) and 'bilang' (count, number).
original_explanation: The very formal, almost-lola's-baul-level word for 'number.' You use 'numero' in everyday life. You use 'tambilang' when you want to sound like you're writing a math textbook for the Department of Education or reciting an old poem. It's the 'whom' to 'numero's' 'who.'
usage_notes: A formal and somewhat archaic term. 'Numero' is far more common in daily conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isulat ang mga **tambilang** mula isa hanggang sampu.","translation":"Write the **numerals** from one to ten."},{"sentence":"Ang **tambilang** na Romano para sa 50 ay L.","translation":"The Roman **numeral** for 50 is L."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-alinsunod sa isang utos, batas, o panuntunan; pagtalima.
original_explanation: It's what your parents demand, your boss expects, and what Waze requires you to do. 'Turn left,' it says. You turn right. Chaos ensues. That's the opposite of pagsunod. It's the art of not questioning the ulam for today and just being grateful there is ulam.
usage_notes: Can refer to following rules, instructions, or physically following someone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagsunod** sa batas trapiko ay mahalaga para sa kaligtasan ng lahat.","translation":"**Obedience** to traffic laws is important for everyone's safety."},{"sentence":"Ipinakita niya ang kanyang **pagsunod** sa pamamagitan ng agarang pagtayo.","translation":"He showed his **compliance** by immediately standing up."}]

translation: to make things worse; to worsen
meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng isang bagay na nagdudulot ng paglala o paglubha sa isang negatibong sitwasyon.
original_explanation: This is the "don't add fuel to the fire" warning. When you're already in a bad situation, and your next action could make it a total disaster. Example: Your friend is angry. You try to calm them down by saying "Kalma ka lang," which only makes them angrier. Your action just made the situation lalong magpasama. It's the verbal equivalent of tripping while already falling down the stairs.
usage_notes: A verbal phrase indicating the worsening of a situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagsisinungaling mo ay **lalong magpapasama** sa sitwasyon.","translation":"Your lying will only **make the situation worse**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo na siyang sigawan, baka **lalong magpasama** lang ang lahat.","translation":"Don't shout at him anymore, it might just **worsen** everything."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pagpapahayag na malinaw, tiyak, at walang anumang paligoy-ligoy o pag-aalinlangan.
original_explanation: This is "no filter" mode. Yung sinabi mo, 'yun na talaga. Walang hidden meaning, walang sugarcoating. Parang 'yung prangka mong kaibigan na sasabihing, "Sis, 'di bagay sa'yo 'yan," instead of "Hmm, interesting choice." It's direct to the point, zero BS.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang isang pahayag, pagtanggi, o utos na walang bahid ng pagdududa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tandisan** niyang itinanggi ang mga paratang laban sa kanya.","translation":"He **explicitly** denied the accusations against him."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng **tandisan** na sagot, oo o hindi lang.","translation":"I need a **direct** answer, just yes or no."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bilang na katumbas ng limampung libo (50,000).
original_explanation: This is old-school counting, like something your lola would say when estimating how many ants are marching to your dropped candy. Before we just said "fifty-kay," there was **limanlaksa**. It sounds more epic, like you're counting an army for a fantasy movie.
usage_notes: Bihirang gamitin sa pang-araw-araw na usapan; mas karaniwan sa panitikan o pormal na konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang halaga ng nawawalang alahas ay tinatayang aabot sa **limanlaksa**ng piso.","translation":"The value of the missing jewelry is estimated to reach **fifty thousand** pesos."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o pangkat na nakikipagpaligsahan sa iba para sa parehong layunin o para sa pangingibabaw sa isang larangan.
original_explanation: Ito yung kaagaw mo sa lahat ng bagay. Kaagaw sa promotion sa office, sa huling piraso ng lechon, at siyempre, sa puso ng crush mo. Parang sa teleserye, siya yung kontrabida sa love story niyo. Minsan, mas magaling pa siyang mag-effort sayo. Ouch.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang aking **karibal** sa pag-ibig ni Maria.","translation":"He is my **rival** for Maria's love."},{"sentence":"Magkaibigan sila noon, ngunit ngayon ay mag-**karibal** na sa negosyo.","translation":"They were friends before, but now they are business **rivals**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na gumagawa, naglalagay, o nagpapasabog ng bomba.
etymology: From Spanish 'bomba' (bomb) + '-ista' (a suffix denoting a person associated with something).
original_explanation: This isn't your friendly neighborhood pyrotechnician. A 'bombista' is someone involved with explosives, usually for illegal or destructive purposes. Think action movie villain, not the person lighting the *lusis* at New Year's.
usage_notes: Often used in news reports about terrorism or criminal activities.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahuli ng mga pulis ang pinaghihinalaang **bombista**.","translation":"The police captured the suspected **bomber**."},{"sentence":"Ang pagsasanay ng mga **bombista** ay isinagawa sa isang liblib na lugar.","translation":"The training of the **bomb makers** was conducted in a remote area."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maliit na butiki o bayawak na karaniwang makikita sa mga damuhan at hardin, na may makinis at makintab na balat.
original_explanation: Not a butiki, not a tuko, but the shiny, slithery cousin you see in the garden. They're the fast little lizards that look like they've been polished. You'd see one dart into the grass and think, 'Was that a tiny snake or a very smooth lizard?' That's a 'bubuli'.
usage_notes: A specific term for a type of lizard (skink), less common in everyday conversation than 'butiki' (house lizard) or 'bayawak' (monitor lizard).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May mabilis na **bubuli** na dumaan sa damuhan.","translation":"A fast **skink** passed through the grass."},{"sentence":"Makintab ang balat ng **bubuli** kapag tinatamaan ng araw.","translation":"The **skink's** skin is shiny when hit by the sun."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pook o pamilihan kung saan nagtitipon ang mga nagtitinda ng iba't ibang uri ng produkto, karaniwang sa mas mababang halaga.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "tianguis", na hango sa salitang Nahuatl na "tiānquiztli" (pamilihan).
original_explanation: Your go-to place for bargain hunting, from ukay-ukay clothes to cellphone cases. It's like Shopee but in real life, with more haggling and the summer heat as your checkout fee. The Divisoria or Greenhills of your local neighborhood.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'bazaar' or 'palengke', but 'tiyangge' implies a more temporary or specialized market setup, often for non-food items.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumunta kami sa **tiyangge** sa Greenhills para bumili ng murang damit.","translation":"We went to the **bazaar** in Greenhills to buy cheap clothes."},{"sentence":"Tuwing Pasko, dagsaan ang mga tao sa **tiyangge**.","translation":"During Christmas, people flock to the **bazaar**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal at magalang na paraan ng pagsasabi na ang isang tao ay namatay o sumakabilang-buhay.
original_explanation: The formal, respectful, and less harsh way to say someone died. It’s the word you use in official obituaries and news reports. Instead of the blunt 'namatay,' you say `pumanaw` to soften the blow and show respect for the deceased. It’s the verbal equivalent of putting on a barong to a funeral.
usage_notes: A euphemism for 'namatay' (died). Used in formal and respectful contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Noong isang linggo pa **pumanaw** ang dating pangulo.","translation":"The former president **passed away** last week."},{"sentence":"Malungkot ang lahat sa pagpanaw ng kanilang minamahal na lola.","translation":"Everyone is sad about the passing of their beloved grandmother."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malalim at maingat na pag-iisip o pagsusuri sa isang bagay, ideya, o sitwasyon bago gumawa ng desisyon o konklusyon.
original_explanation: This is that 3 AM overthinking session, but make it sound intellectual. It's the process of weighing your options, like choosing between ordering milk tea or saving the money. It's the deep thought you give before sending a risky text or accepting a job offer. A moment of intense `pagwawari-wari` can save you from a lifetime of `pagsisisi`.
usage_notes: Implies a deeper, more prolonged, and careful thinking process than just 'pag-iisip'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matapos ang mahabang **pagwawari-wari**, nagpasya siyang tanggapin ang alok.","translation":"After a long **deliberation**, he decided to accept the offer."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng masusing **pagwawari-wari** bago ka pumasok sa isang seryosong relasyon.","translation":"Careful **contemplation** is needed before you enter a serious relationship."}]

translation: to be bad for; to harm
meaning_filipino: Ang magdulot ng pinsala, kapahamakan, o negatibong epekto sa isang tao, bagay, o kalagayan.
original_explanation: This is the 'sama' that's not your friend; it's the 'sama' in 'masamang ugali'. It’s what happens when you eat too much chicharon, or how that toxic ex was for your mental state. 'Huwag kang kumain niyan, baka makasama pa sa tiyan mo.'
usage_notes: This form, with the stress on the last syllable (sa-MA), specifically means 'to be bad for' or 'to cause harm'. It is the antonym of 'makabuti' (to be good for).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sobrang asukal ay maaaring **makasama** sa iyong kalusugan.","translation":"Too much sugar can **be bad for** your health."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko sinasadyang **makasama** ng loob mo.","translation":"I didn't mean **to hurt** your feelings."}]

meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng mga tanda ng krus ang isang bagay o lugar.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you need to mark multiple spots on a map with an 'X' or when you're trying to bless a very large, possibly haunted, area. It's basically 'X marks the spot' but in plural, command form.
usage_notes: This is a very rare word and is more likely to be understood through its construction (pa- + kurus + -an) than from common usage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan ng heneral na **pakurusan** ang mapa upang tandaan ang mga lokasyon ng kaaway.","translation":"The general ordered to **have crosses placed on** the map to mark the enemy locations."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na mamamayan ng Pransiya (France), ang wikang pambansa ng Pransiya, o anumang bagay na nagmula o may kaugnayan sa bansang ito.
original_explanation: When you say something is Pranses, you're thinking of baguettes, the Eiffel Tower, and maybe that "oui oui" you learned in a movie. As a person, it could be a male or non-gender-specific French national. It's the adjective for things that feel a little more 'sosyal' or 'classy', like French fries... which aren't even French, but you get the idea.
usage_notes: Ginagamit para sa lalaki o grupo ng tao, sa wika, o bilang pang-uri. Ang bansa ay "Pransiya".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-aaral ako ng wikang **Pranses**.","translation":"I am studying the **French** language."},{"sentence":"Ang turista ay isang **Pranses**.","translation":"The tourist is a **French** man."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang **Pranses** na tinapay na binili ko.","translation":"The **French** bread I bought is delicious."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging nasa tamang pag-iisip, pagkakaroon ng mabuting asal, at kakayahang magpasya nang wasto.
original_explanation: This is your 'good sense' or 'sanity'. When your mom asks "Nasaan ang tino mo?!", she's asking where your common sense went, probably after you did something incredibly stupid. It's the opposite of being 'wala sa sarili' or 'baliw'. A 'matinong tao' is a decent, upright person.
usage_notes: Often used in the negative form 'walang katino-tino' (completely nonsensical/absurd) or to describe a person's character 'matinong tao' (a decent/sensible person).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana naman ay magkaroon ka na ng **tino** sa pag-iisip.","translation":"I hope you finally gain some **sense**."},{"sentence":"Walang **tino** ang mga plano niya.","translation":"His plans have no **sense**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang alternatibong bersyon ng isang awitin, na nilikha sa pamamagitan ng pagbabago o pagdaragdag sa orihinal na audio.
original_explanation: 'Yung kanta na alam mo na, pero this time, may kasamang "dug-dug" beats na pang-TikTok dance challenge. It's taking something old and making it trendy again, parang pag-recycle ng ex—pero this one actually sounds good.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb ('i-remix').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumikat ang **remix** ng lumang kanta sa TikTok.","translation":"The **remix** of the old song became famous on TikTok."},{"sentence":"Gawa tayo ng DJ **remix** ng paborito nating OPM.","translation":"Let's make a DJ **remix** of our favorite OPM."}]

meaning_filipino: (Kolokyal/Pabalbal) Kumain.
etymology: Slang, derived from a playful alteration of 'kain'.
original_explanation: This is the slang, cooler way of saying "kumain." It's from the word "kain," just rearranged a bit. "Tara, kumana na tayo, gutom na ako!" is the 2026 version of "Let's eat!"
usage_notes: Strictly informal and considered slang. Not appropriate for formal writing or speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tara, **kumana** na tayo sa bagong bukas na karinderya.","translation":"C'mon, let's **eat** at the newly opened eatery."},{"sentence":"Busog na ako, **kumana** na kami kanina.","translation":"I'm already full, we already **ate** earlier."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay, gawain, o panahon na may itinalagang hangganan o limitasyon.
etymology: Mula sa salitang `may` (has/with) at `takda` (limit, allotment, deadline).
original_explanation: Para kang project sa work na may-takda ang deadline. O kaya 'yung free trial mo sa streaming service, may-takda rin 'yan. It means there's a set limit, a boundary, a deadline. Nothing lasts forever, besh.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit para sa oras, mga patakaran, o dami.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ating pagsusulit ay **may-takda** na isang oras lamang.","translation":"Our exam is **limited** to only one hour."},{"sentence":"Lahat ng bagay sa mundo ay **may-takda**.","translation":"Everything in the world has a **limit**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay na pagdadala o paglilipat ng maraming bagay o tao mula sa isang lugar patungo sa iba, karaniwang ginagamitan ng sasakyan.
etymology: From `hakot` (to carry, to haul) + `-an` (suffix indicating a place or collective action).
original_explanation: Think "Lipat Bahay" vibes. It's the organized chaos of moving stuff. "Hakutan" is the event itself, the great migration of your gamit from the old place to the new. It can also refer to transporting people, like when a company provides a shuttle service ("hakutan ng empleyado") or when politicians "hakot" people to a rally.
usage_notes: The verb is `maghakot`. `Hakutan` refers to the reciprocal or collective act of hauling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bukas na ang **hakutan** ng mga gamit namin papunta sa bagong bahay.","translation":"The **hauling** of our things to the new house is tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng **hakutan** ng mga residente bago dumating ang bagyo.","translation":"There was a mass **transport** of residents before the typhoon arrived."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na pinalamig nang husto o may yelo. Maaari ring tumukoy sa sorbetes sa lumang gamit.
original_explanation: This is a word your lola might use. "Cafe elado" is basically iced coffee before it was cool and called "iced coffee." It means iced or frozen. While it can also mean ice cream ("helado" in Spanish), we're more likely to say "sorbetes" or just "ice cream" now. Think of it as the vintage, hispanized version of "chilled."
usage_notes: Medyo luma na ang paggamit nito, lalo na bilang pangalan para sa sorbetes. Mas karaniwan itong maririnig sa mga pangalan ng pagkain na may impluwensiyang Espanyol tulad ng 'kape elado'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa init ng panahon, masarap uminom ng sago't gulaman na **elado**.","translation":"In this hot weather, it's delicious to drink an **iced** sago't gulaman."},{"sentence":"Naghahanap siya ng karinderyang nagbebenta ng kape **elado**.","translation":"He is looking for a diner that sells **iced** coffee."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang silid na laan para sa pagpapahinga, paglilibang, o pagtanggap ng bisita.
etymology: Compound word from "silid" (room) and "pahingahan" (resting place, from root 'pahinga').
original_explanation: The room with the comfiest sofa, the biggest TV, and the family's collection of 'display-only' figurines. It's where you binge-watch K-dramas, where your dad falls asleep watching the news, and where visitors are entertained. Often used interchangeably with 'sala' (living room).
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'sala'. 'Silid-pahingahan' might sound slightly more formal or imply a specific room for rest, like a lounge in an office.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkape muna tayo sa **silid-pahingahan**.","translation":"Let's have coffee first in the **lounge**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga bisita ay naghihintay sa **silid-pahingahan**.","translation":"The guests are waiting in the **lounge**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang tungkulin ay magbantay, magprotekta, o magmasid sa isang lugar upang mapanatili ang kaayusan at kaligtasan.
original_explanation: The official neighborhood watch. They're the ones roaming the streets at night, usually with a 'batuta' (nightstick) and a flashlight, making sure everything's peaceful. They're your first line of defense against local 'chismis' turning into a full-blown street fight. Sila ang rason kung bakit kailangan mo nang umuwi bago mag-curfew.
usage_notes: Commonly refers to a 'barangay tanod', a civilian volunteer who helps maintain peace and order in a local community (barangay).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpapatrolya ang mga **tanod** tuwing gabi sa aming barangay.","translation":"The **watchmen** patrol our village every night."},{"sentence":"Tawagin mo ang **tanod** kung may kahina-hinalang tao.","translation":"Call the **guard** if there is a suspicious person."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagiging masaya o pagkakaroon ng kagalakan.
etymology: From sum- (actor-focus infix) + saya (happy), with reduplication of the first syllable (sa-) to indicate progressive aspect.
original_explanation: That feeling when sahod day finally comes. Or when your Shopee package arrives. It's the "loading... happiness" state. You're not fully happy yet, but you're getting there. It’s the journey, not the destination. "Sumasaya ang araw ko kapag nakikita ko ang mga aso sa kalye."
usage_notes: This is the progressive or present tense, describing the process of becoming happy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumasaya** ako tuwing napapakinggan ko ang paborito kong kanta.","translation":"I **become happy** whenever I listen to my favorite song."},{"sentence":"Unti-unting **sumasaya** ang paligid dahil sa mga palamuting pamasko.","translation":"The surroundings are gradually **getting cheerful** because of the Christmas decorations."}]

translation: to blaze; to flare up; to burn intensely
meaning_filipino: Ang marahas na paglaki ng apoy o siga. Sa metaporikal na gamit, ito ay tumutukoy sa matinding pag-init o pag-igting ng damdamin tulad ng galit, pag-ibig, o pagnanasa.
original_explanation: Literally, for a fire to go from zero to a hundred real quick. But we mostly use it for feelings. When your 'puso' (heart) is 'nag-aalab', you're intensely in love. When your 'galit' (anger) is 'nag-aalab', someone better run. It's passion, rage, desire—all the big, fiery emotions. It's the feeling behind a protest chant or a love confession.
usage_notes: Often used poetically or to describe strong emotions. 'Nag-aalab na puso' (a heart ablaze) is a common trope.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis na **nag-alab** ang apoy dahil sa malakas na hangin.","translation":"The fire quickly **flared up** because of the strong wind."},{"sentence":"Dapat laging **mag-alab** ang ating pagmamahal sa bayan.","translation":"Our love for the country should always **burn intensely**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang direktang pagboto ng buong elektoral sa isang partikular na panukalang-batas o isyung pampulitika na inihain para sa kanilang pagpapasya.
etymology: From Latin 'referendum', via Spanish 'referéndum' or English 'referendum'.
original_explanation: When the politicians can't decide (or don't want to), they pass the decision to the people. It's like a national group project where everyone has to vote 'Yes' or 'No'. "Should we change the constitution? Let's have a **reperendum**!" It's democracy, but with extra steps and lots of campaign ads.
usage_notes: Used in the context of politics, law, and governance. Often used interchangeably with 'plebisito' (plebiscite), though they have technical differences in law.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpatawag ng isang **reperendum** upang pagbotohan ang bagong saligang batas.","translation":"A **referendum** was called to vote on the new constitution."},{"sentence":"Ang resulta ng **reperendum** ay magiging basehan ng susunod na hakbang ng gobyerno.","translation":"The result of the **referendum** will be the basis for the government's next step."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na tawagan sa isang kaibigan, karaniwang lalaki, na nagmula sa mga wikang Bisaya at ginagamit na rin sa ilang lugar na nagsasalita ng Tagalog.
etymology: Mula sa Cebuano na 'bai', isang pinaikling anyo ng 'abay' (kaibigan, kasama).
original_explanation: This is the Visayan version of 'pare' or 'bro'. You'll hear this a lot in Cebu, Davao, and other parts of the Visayas and Mindanao. 'Bai, musta na?' ('Bro, how are you?'). It has become popular slang in Manila too, a cool way to call your friends.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa impormal at pasalitang wika. Ito ay isang termino ng paglalambing at pagiging pamilyar sa pagitan ng magkakaibigan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"\"Tara, kain tayo, **bai**,\" sabi ni Paolo sa kanyang kaibigan.","translation":"\"Let's go eat, **bro**,\" Paolo said to his friend."},{"sentence":"Hoy **bai**, ang galing ng laro mo kanina!","translation":"Hey **dude**, your game earlier was great!"}]

translation: to show consideration, to have regard for
meaning_filipino: Pagbibigay ng konsiderasyon o pag-iisip sa kapakanan, damdamin, o kalagayan ng iba bago gumawa ng isang desisyon o kilos.
etymology: From 'mag-' (verb prefix) + 'alang-alang' (for the sake of, in consideration of).
original_explanation: This is what you do when you want to blast your K-Pop playlist at 2 AM but remember your housemates have a 6 AM shift. It's the 'pakisama' spirit in action. You consider others, you don't just 'go lang nang go'.
usage_notes: Often used with 'sa' (for). 'Mag-alang-alang sa...' means 'to be considerate of...'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay **mag-alang-alang** ka naman sa mga natutulog.","translation":"I hope you would **be considerate** of those who are sleeping."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **mag-alang-alang** sa kinabukasan ng susunod na henerasyon.","translation":"We need to **have regard for** the future of the next generation."}]

translation: to be itchy; to feel an itch
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkaranas ng pakiramdam sa balat na nag-uudyok sa isang tao na ito'y kamutin.
original_explanation: The literal feeling after a mosquito decides you're a buffet. It's also used in famous idioms: 'nangangati ang kamay' means you're itching to hit someone, and 'nangangati ang paa' means you have an uncontrollable urge to travel or go out.
usage_notes: Can be literal (skin irritation) or figurative (a strong urge to do something).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **mangati** ang braso ko matapos makagat ng lamok.","translation":"My arm started **to be itchy** after being bitten by a mosquito."}]

translation: will revolt; will go on strike
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa ng isang pag-aalsa o pagtutol, karaniwan ng isang grupo, laban sa isang awtoridad o sistema.
etymology: From Tagalog `mag-` (future tense verb prefix) + `aklas` (strike, revolt).
original_explanation: 'Yung gagawin ng mga empleyado kapag hindi na nila kaya ang management. O 'yung gagawin ng mga estudyante kapag biglang nag-announce ng major exam kinabukasan. Ito 'yung "Team Bahay" version ng protesta.
usage_notes: Refers to the future tense of the verb 'to strike' or 'to revolt'. It implies a collective action against authority.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Mag-aaklas** ang mga manggagawa kung hindi ibibigay ang kanilang benepisyo.","translation":"The workers **will go on strike** if their benefits are not given."},{"sentence":"Tila **mag-aaklas** ang mga bata kung hindi sila papayagang maglaro.","translation":"It seems the children **will revolt** if they are not allowed to play."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sisidlan na ginagamit bilang pansamantalang palikuran, karaniwang inilalagay sa ilalim ng kama, lalo na noong unang panahon.
original_explanation: Before the era of en-suite bathrooms and 24/7 access to a CR, there was the humble **orinola**. It's the OG portable toilet, usually for midnight emergencies. 'Yung lola mo, baka may kwento tungkol dito. It's the low-tech solution when you're too lazy or too scared to go to the outhouse in the middle of the night.
usage_notes: The 'a' at the end is a common Tagalog adaptation. The word is now considered old-fashioned.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa mga lumang bahay sa probinsya, makakakita ka pa rin ng **orinola**.","translation":"In old houses in the province, you can still see a **chamber pot**."},{"sentence":"Ginamit ng maysakit ang **orinola** dahil hindi siya makatayo.","translation":"The sick person used the **bedpan** because they couldn't stand up."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubhang malupit, marahas, o walang awa. Sa modernong kolokyal na paggamit, maaari ring tumukoy sa isang bagay na kahanga-hanga o pambihira sa galing.
etymology: From the superlative prefix 'napaka-' and the root word 'lupit' (cruelty, fierceness).
original_explanation: This word is two-faced. It can mean your boss is a tyrant ('Napakalupit ng boss ko, ayaw mag-approve ng leave!'), or your friend just did something epic ('Napakalupit mo, pre! Galing!'). It's the 'savage' or 'badass' of Tagalog slang, used for both extreme cruelty and extreme coolness.
usage_notes: The meaning is highly dependent on context and tone. It can be negative (very cruel) or positive (awesome/amazing) in modern slang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinuring siyang isang **napakalupit** na pinuno dahil sa kanyang mga marahas na patakaran.","translation":"He was considered a **very cruel** leader because of his harsh policies."},{"sentence":"**Napakalupit** ng ginawa mong artwork, para kang pro!","translation":"Your artwork is so **awesome**, you're like a pro!"}]

translation: to form into herds/flocks; to group together
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbuo ng malalaking grupo o pulutong, karaniwan ay tumutukoy sa mga hayop, ngunit maaari ring gamitin para sa mga tao.
original_explanation: Picture the scene at the MRT station at 5 PM. That's people who magkawan-kawan. It means to gather in a large group, flock, or herd. It's what your friends do when there's a chismis, or how shoppers swarm a 12.12 sale. It's organized chaos in motion.
usage_notes: The reduplication 'kawan-kawan' emphasizes the formation of multiple or large groups.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **magkawan-kawan** ang mga ibon bago lumubog ang araw.","translation":"The birds began to **flock together** before the sun set."},{"sentence":"Ang mga estudyante ay **nagkawan-kawan** sa labas ng gate pagkatapos ng klase.","translation":"The students **grouped together** outside the gate after class."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang makina o lugar kung saan tinatanggalan ng ipa ang palay upang maging bigas.
etymology: From 'kiskis' (to rub) + '-an' (place suffix). Literally 'a place for rubbing/milling'.
original_explanation: The OG factory for our unli-rice dreams. It's the place where palay (unhusked rice) gets its glow-up and becomes bigas (husked rice). Think of it as a spa for rice grains, where they get a good scrubbing to reveal their true, white, fluffy potential.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala ng magsasaka ang kanyang ani sa **kiskisan**.","translation":"The farmer brought his harvest to the **rice mill**."}]

meaning_filipino: Paggawa ng isang aksyon nang padalos-dalos, walang pag-iingat, o hindi muna pinag-isipan ang kahihinatnan.
original_explanation: This is the official motto of 'add to cart' during a midnight sale. It's that moment you blurt something out in a meeting and immediately regret it. Basically, your impulse winning over your brain. The opposite of 'think before you click.'
usage_notes: Carries a negative connotation of recklessness or lack of forethought.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumagot siya **nang hindi iniisip** kaya napagalitan siya.","translation":"She answered **without thinking**, which is why she was scolded."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang marahas na pag-aalsa o paghihimagsik ng isang pangkat ng mga tao laban sa isang pamahalaan o may kapangyarihan.
original_explanation: This is not your typical "Ayaw ko na, magre-resign na 'ko" drama. This is the ultimate "fed up" mode, level 999. Think Katipunan tearing up their cedulas. It's a full-blown, organized rebellion, not just a passive-aggressive tweet against the government.
usage_notes: Ang "insureksyon" ay isang karaniwang baryasyon sa pagbaybay na mas madalas gamitin sa pasalitang wika.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **insureksiyon** ng mga Pilipino laban sa mga Kastila ay isang mahalagang bahagi ng ating kasaysayan.","translation":"The **insurrection** of the Filipinos against the Spanish is an important part of our history."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan nila ang mga sanhi ng bigong **insureksiyon**.","translation":"They are studying the causes of the failed **insurrection**."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagbibigay ng tulong o suporta sa isang tao o sa isang gawain.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "asistir," na nangangahulugang "to attend" o "to assist."
original_explanation: Parang 'yung kaibigan mong laging andyan 'pag may group project, pero 'pag sa love life mo, 'seen' lang. To assist is to help out, like being the official 'taga-abot ng gamit' during a DIY project or being the moral support for your friend's disastrous karaoke performance.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of providing direct help or support in a specific activity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Asistihan** mo muna ang lola sa pag-akyat sa hagdan.","translation":"Please **assist** grandma in climbing the stairs."},{"sentence":"Sino ang mag-a**asistihan** sa chef sa kusina mamaya?","translation":"Who will **assist** the chef in the kitchen later?"}]

translation: to carry out; to implement; to execute
meaning_filipino: Tuparin, isakatuparan, o gawin ang isang plano, utos, o tungkulin.
original_explanation: This is the corporate and formal way of saying "gawin mo na" (just do it). Your boss doesn't say "Gawin mo yung project," they say, "Isagawa natin ang bagong marketing plan." It’s the "let's put this into action" verb.
usage_notes: More formal than "gawin." Often used in official contexts, news reports, and business.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Plano ng pamahalaan na **isagawa** ang isang malawakang paglilinis sa buong bansa.","translation":"The government plans to **carry out** a nationwide clean-up drive."}]

translation: to go to the middle; to mediate
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpunta o pagpwesto sa gitna; tumayong tagapamagitan sa dalawang nag-aaway na panig.
original_explanation: That awkward moment you have to sit between two bickering friends in the jeepney. Or when you're the designated 'ate' or 'kuya' of the group who has to play referee when drama erupts. "Huwag ka nang gumitna sa away nila, baka ikaw pa masisi."
usage_notes: Can be used literally (to be physically in the middle) or figuratively (to mediate a conflict).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **gumitna** sa dalawang nagtatalong magkapatid.","translation":"He **mediated** between the two arguing siblings."},{"sentence":"**Gumitna** ka sa pila para hindi ka maunahan.","translation":"**Go to the middle** of the line so you won't be overtaken."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong kabilang sa subkulturang 'punk' na may katangiang rebelyoso sa pananamit at musika; o isang uri ng musikang rock na mabilis at may agresibong liriko.
original_explanation: Think leather jackets, spiked hair, Doc Martens, and listening to The Ramones or local bands like The Wuds. It's that "against the system" vibe your Tito had in the 80s. Today, it's more of an aesthetic, but the rebellious spirit is still there. Not to be confused with 'pangkó', which is carrying someone on your back.
usage_notes: Used in the context of music and subculture. The pronunciation is often Filipinized to /pangk/.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang makinig sa musikang **punk** noong kabataan niya.","translation":"He loved listening to **punk** music during his youth."},{"sentence":"Ang ayos niya ay parang **punk** rocker.","translation":"His style is like a **punk** rocker."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na may mas matinding diin kaysa 'chaka'; tumutukoy sa isang tao o bagay na sukdulan sa kapangitan o hindi talaga kaaya-aya.
etymology: A swardspeak (beki lingo) term, likely an emphatic or superlative form of 'chaka.' The '-rat' suffix adds a layer of harshness or intensity.
original_explanation: If 'chaka' is just ugly, 'chararat' is the final boss of ugly. It's 'chaka' level 99. This is the word you use when something is so spectacularly, jaw-droppingly un-aesthetic that 'chaka' just doesn't cut it. It has a more playful, almost cartoonish exaggeration to it. 'Hindi lang siya chaka, friend. Chararat na siya.'
usage_notes: A more intense and informal version of 'chaka.' Use with caution, as it can be more offensive.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Yung gown na sinuot niya sa party, sobrang **chararat**!","translation":"The gown she wore to the party was so **hideously ugly**!"},{"sentence":"Naging **chararat** ang resulta ng make-up tutorial na sinunod ko.","translation":"The result of the make-up tutorial I followed turned out **very ugly**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagdudulot ng kasiyahan, kagalakan, o kaaya-ayang pakiramdam.
original_explanation: That feeling you get when your online order arrives earlier than expected, or when the traffic on EDSA is magically light. It's something that makes you happy or satisfied. It's the "sana all" feeling but for positive events. "Nakalulugod isipin na may bonus na darating."
usage_notes: A formal and somewhat poetic word. "Masaya" is the everyday equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakalulugod** pagmasdan ang paglubog ng araw sa Manila Bay.","translation":"It is **pleasing** to watch the sunset at Manila Bay."},{"sentence":"**Nakalulugod** ang balitang natanggap niya mula sa kanyang pamilya.","translation":"The news he received from his family was **delightful**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkalahatang pagtutol o paghihimagsik, karaniwang may sandata, laban sa isang umiiral na awtoridad, pamahalaan, o sistema.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na "alzar" (itinaas, iangat).
original_explanation: This is the historical 'I've had enough!' moment, like what Andres Bonifacio and the Katipunan did. It's the people rising up against oppression, the ultimate form of 'reklamo'. It's the plot of many historical films and the reason we have holidays for heroes.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa isang politikal o panlipunang paghihimagsik, madalas ay armadong labanan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pag-aalsa** ng Katipunan ay isang mahalagang bahagi ng kasaysayan ng Pilipinas.","translation":"The **uprising** of the Katipunan is an important part of Philippine history."},{"sentence":"Nagbunsod ng **pag-aalsa** ang hindi makatarungang mga patakaran.","translation":"The unjust policies led to a **rebellion**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marahan at magaan na pagdampi o paghimas sa ibabaw ng isang bagay, karaniwan gamit ang kamay, bilang pagpapakita ng pagmamahal o pag-aalaga.
original_explanation: This is the gentle way your lola touches your face. It's how you pet a cat to make it purr. It’s that soft, comforting stroke that says "I care about you" or "It's going to be okay" without using words. The opposite of 'hampas'.
usage_notes: A very gentle and often affectionate action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang magaan na **paghaplot** ng kamay ng kanyang ina sa kanyang buhok.","translation":"She felt the light **caress** of her mother's hand on her hair."},{"sentence":"Isang **paghaplot** lang sa likod ay sapat na para pakalmahin ang bata.","translation":"Just one **gentle stroke** on the back is enough to calm the child."}]

translation: Hastiness; state of being in a hurry
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagmamadali o paggawa ng isang bagay nang mabilis at walang sapat na pag-iingat o pag-iisip.
