original_explanation: This is you trying to leave the office at exactly 5:01 PM. It's the 'dali-dali, baka ma-traffic' mindset that often leads to forgetting your keys, your wallet, or your baon. It's rushing, which as the saying goes, often leads to waste.
usage_notes: Refers to the state of being rushed or acting hastily, often with negative consequences. Homonym of 'pagkamadali' (easiness).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **pagkamadali**, naiwan niya ang kanyang telepono sa bahay.","translation":"Because of his **hastiness**, he left his phone at home."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa buhok na magulo, hindi maayos ang pagkakasuklay, o nakatayo dahil sa pagkakagising sa umaga.
original_explanation: This is the official term for your 'just woke up' hair, or 'sabog' hair after a long day of commuting. It's when your buhok has a life of its own and refuses to cooperate with any 'suklay' or 'pomada'. The kind of hair that screams 'I need coffee' or '5 more minutes please'.
usage_notes: Partikular na ginagamit upang ilarawan ang buhok.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Talibadbad** ang buhok ng bata pagkatapos maglaro sa labas.","translation":"The child's hair was **disheveled** after playing outside."},{"sentence":"Sinuklay niya ang kanyang **talibadbad** na buhok bago humarap sa camera.","translation":"She combed her **unkempt** hair before facing the camera."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng mabilis at biglaang pagdakma o pag-agaw sa isang bagay o pagkakataon.
etymology: From 'sunggab' (grab) + '-an' (suffix indicating action on an object).
original_explanation: This is the command/infinitive form. 'Grab it!' It’s what your inner voice screams during a 12.12 sale when the last item is in your cart but you haven't checked out yet. *Sunggaban mo na 'yang opportunity!* It’s about seizing the moment, whether it's a career opportunity or the last slice of pizza.
usage_notes: Used to mean grabbing a physical object or seizing an opportunity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **sunggaban** ng iba ang pangarap na para sa iyo.","translation":"Don't let others **snatch** away the dream that is meant for you."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **sunggaban** ang nahuhulog na plorera.","translation":"He tried to **grab at** the falling vase."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong may kakulangan sa talino o pang-unawa; hangal. Ginagamit bilang isang mapanirang-puri na salita.
original_explanation: The OG Filipino insult you learned before 'putangina'. It's what your mom calls you when you forget the 'suka' she asked you to buy. It's a classic, a staple, the adobo of Filipino insults. Use with caution, as it can escalate a simple argument into a full-blown family drama.
usage_notes: A very common but offensive term. Can be used for any gender, but 'boba' is specific to females.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiramdam ko ang **bobo** ko dahil bumagsak ako sa exam.","translation":"I feel so **stupid** because I failed the exam."},{"sentence":"Tinawag siyang **bobo** ng kanyang kaaway.","translation":"His enemy called him an **idiot**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kawalan ng pag-iingat, pagtitimpi, o pagpipigil sa kilos, salita, o paggasta.
original_explanation: This is your "YOLO" friend who spends their entire sweldo on 11.11 sale without thinking about the bills. "Walang habas sa pag-gastos!" It's that "bahala na si Batman" attitude applied to anything—eating at a buffet, talking trash, or driving. It's the opposite of "sana all" may self-control.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa pariralang "walang habas" upang ilarawan ang isang kilos na walang pagpipigil.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang walang **habas** na pagsasalita ay nagdulot ng gulo.","translation":"His **reckless** speech caused trouble."},{"sentence":"Walang **habas** kung gumastos ng pera ang lalaking iyon.","translation":"That man spends money with no **restraint**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang alinman sa dalawang patag at tatsulok na buto sa likod ng balikat; maaari ring tumukoy sa palikpik ng isda.
original_explanation: Yung buto sa likod mo na parang pakpak ng anghel pag sobrang payat ka. It's your shoulder blade. Also, it's the fin of a fish, yung ginagamit niya for steering and balance. So whether you're a human trying to get a back massage or a fish trying to swim away from becoming sinigang, you use your **palaypay**.
usage_notes: May dalawang karaniwang kahulugan: ang buto sa balikat at ang palikpik ng isda. Ang konteksto ang susi sa pag-unawa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masakit ang aking **palaypay** pagkatapos magbuhat ng mabigat.","translation":"My **shoulder blade** hurts after lifting something heavy."},{"sentence":"Tingnan mo ang matatalas na **palaypay** ng isdang iyon.","translation":"Look at the sharp **fins** of that fish."}]

meaning_filipino: Hayaang bumagsak ang isang bagay mula sa itaas; maglagak ng pera sa bangko o sulat sa post office.
original_explanation: Can mean literally dropping your phone (please don't!), dropping a letter in the mailbox, or depositing money in the bank ("**ihulog** sa bangko"). It's also what happens to your standards when you're desperate. Also used for paying for something in installments ('hulugan').
usage_notes: A very versatile word. Can mean a literal, accidental drop ('nahulog') or a deliberate, purposeful drop/deposit ('ihulog').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **ihulog** mo naman itong sulat sa post office.","translation":"Please, could you **drop** this letter at the post office."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka at baka **mahulog** mo ang mga itlog.","translation":"Be careful or you might **drop** the eggs."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ko nang **ihulog** ang buwanang bayad para sa bahay.","translation":"I need to **deposit** the monthly payment for the house."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pakikipagsapalaran sa pamamagitan ng pagpusta ng pera o mahahalagang bagay sa isang laro o kaganapan na may hindi tiyak na resulta.
etymology: Nagmula sa unlaping 'man-' at salitang-ugat na 'sugal'.
original_explanation: To **manugal** is to play a game of chance, whether it's Tong-its with the neighbors, a high-stakes poker game, or betting on the next UAAP champion. It's that 'bahala na' attitude applied to your finances. Minsan panalo, madalas talo, pero laging exciting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinagbawalan siya ng kanyang asawa na **manugal**.","translation":"His wife forbade him to **gamble**."},{"sentence":"Maraming pera ang nawala sa kanya dahil sa hilig niyang **manugal**.","translation":"He lost a lot of money because of his fondness for **gambling**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagkilos o pangyayari na hindi sinasadya, hindi binalak, o hindi ginusto.
etymology: From `di-` (not) + `kinukusa` (present progressive form of kusa, 'to do voluntarily').
original_explanation: It's the "oops, sorry, 'di ko sinasadya" moment. Like when you accidentally like your ex's photo from 3 years ago while stalking their profile. It wasn't on purpose, but the damage is done.
usage_notes: Often used to explain accidents, mistakes, or involuntary physical reactions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagbagsak ng plorera ay **di-kinukusa**.","translation":"The falling of the vase was **accidental**."},{"sentence":"Isang **di-kinukusang** ngiti ang lumabas sa kanyang mga labi.","translation":"An **involuntary** smile appeared on his lips."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapakita ng pakikiramay, pakikiisa sa kalungkutan, o pagtulong sa isang taong nasa mahirap na kalagayan.
original_explanation: This is the core of the Filipino 'bayanihan' spirit. When someone's going through a tough time, *pagdamay* is bringing them food, sitting with them, or just sending a 'thinking of you' GCash. It's the 'we're in this together' vibe, especially during wakes and calamities. More than just saying 'condolences,' it's about showing up.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'pakikiramay', but 'pagdamay' can also imply more active help beyond just expressing condolences.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Taos-puso ang kanyang **pagdamay** sa mga biktima ng sunog.","translation":"Her **act of showing sympathy** for the fire victims was sincere."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagdamay** sa kapwa ay tanda ng mabuting pagkatao.","translation":"Showing **sympathy** for others is a sign of good character."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tradisyong Pilipino kung kailan ginugunita at binibigyang-galang ang mga yumaong kamag-anak sa pamamagitan ng pagdalaw sa sementeryo, pag-aalay ng bulaklak at kandila, at pagdarasal. Ito ay karaniwang tumutukoy sa Araw ng mga Santo (Nobyembre 1) at Araw ng mga Kaluluwa (Nobyembre 2).
etymology: Posibleng mula sa salitang Espanyol na "honras" (honors) na tumutukoy sa mga parangal sa libing.
original_explanation: The one time of the year when cemeteries turn into giant family reunion spots. It's about remembering loved ones who've passed, but it's also about the traffic, the food trip (people bring entire feasts), playing cards on top of a tomb, and melting candles forming colorful, waxy rivers. It's a uniquely Filipino blend of solemn remembrance and festive gathering.
usage_notes: Laging nakasulat sa malaking titik. Tumutukoy sa kaganapan o panahon sa paligid ng Nobyembre 1 at 2.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uuwi kami sa probinsya para sa darating na **Undas**.","translation":"We are going home to the province for the upcoming **All Saints' Day**."},{"sentence":"Naging parang pista ang sementeryo noong **Undas**.","translation":"The cemetery became like a festival during **All Souls' Day**."}]
related: ["Araw ng mga Patay","Araw ng mga Santo","sementeryo","kaluluwa","kandila"]

meaning_filipino: Tumungo o kumilos sa isang tuwid na direksyon nang walang pag-abala; ang pagpunta nang direkta sa isang tiyak na destinasyon.
original_explanation: Past tense of *dumidiretso*. This is what you did yesterday when you were so tired you skipped dinner with friends and *dumiretso* ka na lang sa bahay to crash on your bed. It’s the completed action of having no side quests.
usage_notes: Past tense form. The progressive is "dumidiretso."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagbaba niya ng bus, **dumiretso** siya sa pinakamalapit na karinderya.","translation":"After getting off the bus, he **went straight** to the nearest eatery."},{"sentence":"Hindi na siya nagpaalam, **dumiretso** na lang siyang lumabas ng pinto.","translation":"He didn't say goodbye anymore, he just **headed directly** out the door."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na termino para sa daloy at paggalaw ng mga sasakyan, barko, o eroplano sa isang ruta.
original_explanation: This is 'trapik' wearing a barong. It's the word you hear on DZBB radio reports ("Bumigat na ang daloy ng trapiko sa SLEX!") or read in official MMDA announcements. While your Uber driver says "Grabe ang trapik," the news anchor says "Malubha ang sitwasyon ng trapiko." Same problem, different levels of formality.
usage_notes: The formal word for traffic, used in news, government documents, and formal writing. 'Trapik' is its more common, colloquial counterpart.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng MMDA ang mga bagong solusyon sa problema ng **trapiko**.","translation":"The MMDA is studying new solutions to the **traffic** problem."},{"sentence":"Ang daloy ng **trapiko** ay inaasahang bubuti sa pagbubukas ng bagong skyway.","translation":"The flow of **traffic** is expected to improve with the opening of the new skyway."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang usbong ng munggo (mung bean), karaniwang ginagamit bilang sangkap sa mga lutuing Asyano tulad ng lumpiang sariwa.
etymology: From Hokkien 豆芽 (tāu-gê), meaning "bean sprout".
original_explanation: That crunchy white stuff you find in lumpia, pad thai, and pancit. Some people love it, some people pick it out. It's basically baby munggo (mung beans). In the palengke, you buy tawge by the plastic bag full for just a few pesos.
usage_notes: A common ingredient in Filipino and other Asian cuisines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong sahog sa lumpiang sariwa ang **tawge**.","translation":"**Bean sprouts** are my favorite ingredient in fresh spring rolls."},{"sentence":"Mag-gisa ka ng manok na may **tawge** para sa ating pananghalian.","translation":"Sauté some chicken with **bean sprouts** for our lunch."}]

translation: to decant; to pour out carefully
meaning_filipino: Maingat na ibuhos o isalin ang likido mula sa isang sisidlan patungo sa iba, karaniwang iniiwasan ang latak o mga solidong bahagi.
original_explanation: This is the art of pouring lambanog or wine without getting the dregs. It's a slow, careful pour, like how you dispense your last few drops of perfume or how you try to get the last bit of ketchup out of the bottle without that watery stuff. Precision pouring!
usage_notes: Not a common word. More likely to be heard in rural areas or in specific contexts like making traditional wine or vinegar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahan-dahang **itagis** ang alak sa pitsel upang hindi sumama ang latak.","translation":"Slowly **decant** the wine into the pitcher so the sediment is not included."},{"sentence":"**Itinagis** niya ang natirang kape sa kanyang tasa.","translation":"He carefully **poured out** the remaining coffee into his cup."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay na inilalagay upang makahadlang sa daan, o maging sagabal sa pagpapatuloy ng isang gawain o layunin.
original_explanation: This is anything that gets in your way. The 'closed' sign on your favorite milk tea shop, the security guard asking for your ID, the slow internet connection during an online game. It can be a physical barrier like a road block ('harang sa kalsada') or a metaphorical one, like your tita asking when you're getting married.
usage_notes: Can be physical (a fence, a roadblock) or metaphorical (fear, doubt).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **harang** sa kalsada dahil sa ginagawang konstruksyon.","translation":"There is a **block** on the road due to ongoing construction."},{"sentence":"Ang takot ay isang malaking **harang** sa pag-abot ng ating mga pangarap.","translation":"Fear is a big **obstacle** to reaching our dreams."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-ikot o paggalaw sa isang ibabaw sa pamamagitan ng pagpapaikot-ikot, o ang paghiga at pagpapaikot-ikot ng katawan. Ito ay isang salitang-ugat.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa mo sa kama kapag tinatamad kang bumangon. O 'yung ginagawa ng aso mo sa damuhan dahil masaya siya. Verb forms: gumulong (rolled), gumugulong (rolling), gugulong (will roll). Also, what you do with lumpia wrappers.
usage_notes: As a verb root, it requires affixes. Common forms are 'gumulong', 'igulong', 'magpagulong-gulong'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Gumulong** ang bola pababa ng burol.","translation":"The ball **rolled** down the hill."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **magpagulong-gulong** sa kama tuwing umaga.","translation":"He likes **to roll** around in bed every morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha o pagbigkas ng mga salita na may magkakatugmang tunog sa huli, lalo na sa tula o awit.
etymology: Mula sa salitang 'rima' (mula sa Espanyol 'rima') + panlaping '-um-'.
original_explanation: From the Spanish 'rima' (rhyme). This is what rappers, poets, and your Tito who loves making cheesy birthday poems do. It's the act of making words rhyme. In FlipTop battles, the ability to rumima on the spot is crucial. For the rest of us, it's trying to find a word that rhymes with 'mahal' that isn't 'hangal' or 'tanga.'
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa konteksto ng panitikan, musika, at tula.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahusay siyang **rumima** kaya nanalo siya sa patimpalak sa pagtula.","translation":"He is good at **rhyming**, which is why he won the poetry contest."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan ng bata na **rumima** habang kumakanta.","translation":"The child is trying to **rhyme** while singing."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng regular na pag-iikot sa isang lugar upang mapanatili ang kaayusan, seguridad, at para magbantay laban sa anumang panganib.
original_explanation: This is what the barangay tanod does at 2 AM, armed with a flashlight and a cup of kape. It's the act of making your rounds, whether you're a security guard checking the building, a BPO team lead checking on your agents, or a mom checking if her kids are *actually* sleeping. The verb form is "magpatrolya".
usage_notes: Madalas na tumutukoy sa opisyal na pag-iikot ng mga pulis, sundalo, o guwardiya. Ang 'patrulya' ay isang karaniwang alternatibong baybay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kabilang sa kanilang tungkulin ang gabi-gabing **patrolya** sa buong subdibisyon.","translation":"Their duty includes a nightly **patrol** of the entire subdivision."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na dalubhasa sa pagkakabit, pag-aayos, at pagpapanatili ng mga sistemang de-kuryente. Ito ay isang alternatibong baybay ng 'eletrisyan'.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "electricista" sa pamamagitan ng Ingles na "electrician".
original_explanation: Your tito's best friend who fixes the faulty wiring that caused your WiFi to die. A hero, basically. This spelling is the more 'Tagalized' phonetic version, but 'eletrisyan' is more common in formal writing.
usage_notes: Isang alternatibong baybay para sa 'eletrisyan', na mas karaniwang ginagamit at itinuturing na pamantayan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumawag ka ng **elektrisyan** para ayusin ang ilaw sa kusina.","translation":"Call an **electrician** to fix the light in the kitchen."}]

translation: to have a tantrum, to become hysterical
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng biglaan at matinding pagsiklab ng damdamin, karaniwang galit o pagkabigo, na mahirap kontrolin.
etymology: From 'sapot' (cobweb, film, covering) + '-in' suffix. The idea is being 'covered' or overwhelmed by an emotion.
original_explanation: 'Yung moment na nag-crash ang laptop mo sa gitna ng deadline, tapos nawala pa ang internet. The only logical response is to saputihin. It's the adult version of a toddler's tantrum, often triggered by slow WiFi, a plot twist sa K-drama, or when your food delivery is late.
usage_notes: Often used to describe an emotional outburst that seems disproportionate to the situation. The root verb form is 'sinapot'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo siyang sigawan, baka **saputihin** 'yan.","translation":"Don't shout at her, she might **have a tantrum**."},{"sentence":"Nang malaman niyang bagsak siya sa exam, bigla siyang **sinapot** sa loob ng kwarto.","translation":"When she found out she failed the exam, she suddenly **had a hysterical fit** inside the room."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang nakasanayang pagkakasunod-sunod ng mga gawain o kilos na regular na isinasagawa.
original_explanation: This is a less common spelling, the more common one is 'rutina'. It's that thing you do every single day without thinking. Gising, kape, ligo, bihis, pasok sa work. That's your morning rutin. It’s the human equivalent of being on autopilot.
usage_notes: A direct borrowing from English. The Spanish-derived "rutina" is more common and considered more standard in formal Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bahagi ng kanyang pang-araw-araw na **rutin** ang pag-eehersisyo.","translation":"Exercise is part of his daily **routine**."},{"sentence":"Nakakasawa na ang paulit-ulit na **rutin** sa opisina.","translation":"The repetitive **routine** at the office is getting boring."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na nangangahulugang malaki.
etymology: Slang, possibly a playful inversion of 'sakdal' (extreme) or a simple neologism.
original_explanation: A modern slang term, a playful reversal of 'sakdal' (as in 'sakdal laki'), meaning 'big'. It's the kind of word you'd whisper to your friend when you see a ridiculously large serving of halo-halo. 'Uy, ang daks ng order mo!' While it has a notorious origin related to size, it's now more broadly used for anything impressively large.
usage_notes: Primarily used in informal, colloquial conversations. Can be considered vulgar depending on the context and what is being described.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Wow, ang **daks** naman ng muscle mo!","translation":"Wow, your muscles are so **huge**!"},{"sentence":"Bumili siya ng TV na sobrang **daks** para sa maliit niyang sala.","translation":"He bought a TV that was way too **big** for his small living room."}]

meaning_filipino: Harina na gawa sa dinikdik o giniling na bigas, karaniwang ginagamit sa paggawa ng mga kakanin.
original_explanation: The secret ingredient to your lola's famous bibingka, puto, and palitaw. It's basically powdered rice, the foundation of many Filipino desserts and snacks (kakanin). If you see a white powder in a Pinoy kitchen that isn't sugar or salt, there's a good chance it's galpong.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to flour made from regular rice (bigas), while 'malagkit na galpong' refers to flour from glutinous rice.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng **galpong** para makagawa ng palitaw.","translation":"We need **rice flour** to make palitaw."},{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng isang kilong **galpong** sa palengke.","translation":"Mom bought a kilo of **rice flour** at the market."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagsusumikap o nag-aasam na maging isang sikat na influencer, ngunit hindi pa gaanong matagumpay o kinikilala.
etymology: Mula sa pariralang Ingles na 'influencer wannabe'.
original_explanation: That friend who posts their Starbucks cup with their name misspelled, tags 20 unrelated brands in their OOTD, and asks 'What's your favorite coffee shop?' for engagement. They have the gear—the ring light, the mic—but their follower count is still in the double digits (mostly relatives). Bless their hearts, they're trying.
usage_notes: Often used with a slightly derogatory or teasing tone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ang feed ko ng mga **influencer wannabe** na nagpo-post ng kanilang a-aesthetic na kape.","translation":"My feed is full of **influencer wannabes** posting their 'aesthetic' coffee."},{"sentence":"Dati siyang **influencer wannabe**, pero sikat na vlogger na siya ngayon.","translation":"She used to be an **influencer wannabe**, but now she's a famous vlogger."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang kakayahang magsalita, pansamantala man o permanente.
original_explanation: Yung moment na tinawag ka ng prof mo for recitation tapos bigla kang nag-freeze. O kapag nakita mo si crush, bigla kang naging di-nakapagsasalita. Minsan dahil sa gulat, minsan dahil sa takot, madalas dahil sa kilig.
usage_notes: Can describe a temporary state of speechlessness or a permanent condition like being mute.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang gulat, naiwan siyang **di-nakapagsasalita**.","translation":"Due to extreme shock, she was left **unable to speak**."},{"sentence":"May mga taong **di-nakapagsasalita** ngunit gumagamit ng sign language upang makipag-usap.","translation":"There are people who are **mute** but use sign language to communicate."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang propesyon ay ang paggupit ng buhok.
etymology: From `mang-` + `gugupit` (future tense of `gupit`, 'to cut'). Literally, "one who will cut."
original_explanation: Your friendly neighborhood therapist who also happens to cut your hair. They know all the local chismis and can give you a fresh new look while you vent about your life problems. Whether it's a '2x3' or a 'Korean oppa' hairstyle, they're the artist.
usage_notes: `Barbero` is also a common term, specifically for a men's barber. `Manggugupit` is more general and can be used for any gender.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magaling ang **manggugupit** sa bagong bukas na salon.","translation":"The **hairdresser** at the newly opened salon is good."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ko nang magpunta sa **manggugupit** dahil mahaba na ang buhok ko.","translation":"I need to go to the **barber** because my hair is already long."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang biglaan at hindi inaasahang pag-atake mula sa isang nakatagong posisyon.
original_explanation: Parang yung biglaang "may meeting" na sinabi ng boss mo 5 minutes before uwian on a Friday. You've been ambushed. Or when your tita suddenly asks, "Kailan ka mag-aasawa?" at a family gathering. That's a classic emotional ambush.
usage_notes: Often used in military, police, or crime contexts. Can also be used metaphorically for any surprise attack or confrontation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nailagan ng mga sundalo ang **ambus** ng mga rebelde.","translation":"The soldiers evaded the rebels' **ambush**."},{"sentence":"Para itong isang **ambus** nang tanungin niya ako tungkol sa ex ko.","translation":"It felt like an **ambush** when she asked me about my ex."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal at pampalumanay na tawag para sa pusa, lalo na sa kuting.
original_explanation: The cutesy, almost baby-talk word for a cat. It's what you call the neighborhood stray you've been feeding, or your own fluffy overlord. If "pusa" is the formal term, "muning" is the affectionate nickname. Often accompanied by a "swswswsws" sound to call them.
usage_notes: Often used by children or when talking to cats in an affectionate manner.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang cute naman ng **muning** na iyan!","translation":"That **kitten** is so cute!"},{"sentence":"Hoy, **muning**, halika rito!","translation":"Hey, **kitty**, come here!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-angkin, pagtanggap, o pagdala ng isang bagay o tao mula sa isang lugar. Ito ay ang anyong pangkaganapan (completed aspect) ng pandiwang 'kuha'.
original_explanation: This is the past tense of 'to get.' Like when your mom asks, "Kumuha ka na ba ng NBI clearance?" or when you finally kumuha ng courage to chat your crush, only to be left on "seen." It's the action of taking something, whether it's a physical object, a course in college, or a chance on someone.
usage_notes: Past tense/completed aspect of the verb 'to get/take'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumuha** siya ng isang pirasong mangga mula sa basket.","translation":"He/She **took** a piece of mango from the basket."},{"sentence":"**Kumuha** ako ng kursong engineering sa kolehiyo.","translation":"I **took** an engineering course in college."}]

translation: to be torn; to get ripped
meaning_filipino: Ang di-sinasadyang mapunit o masira dahil sa pagbanat o paghila.
original_explanation: That tragic moment when your favorite shirt or your last 100-peso bill gets a tear. It's the sound your tight jeans make when you squat. "Hala, nagisi!" is the national expression of fabric-related despair.
usage_notes: Refers to the tearing of thin materials like paper, cloth, or plastic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingatan mo ang lumang litrato at baka **magisi**.","translation":"Be careful with the old photograph, it might **get torn**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isinampa ng kaso o pormal na inakusahan sa hukuman.
original_explanation: When the chismis escalates to a legal battle. This is what happens when someone files a case against you. 'Nako, **hinakdal** daw si mayor dahil sa isyu ng korapsyon!' It's the past tense of 'See you in court!'
usage_notes: Specifically used in a legal context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay **hinakdal** ng kanyang kapitbahay dahil sa hindi pagbabayad ng utang.","translation":"He **was sued** by his neighbor for not paying his debt."},{"sentence":"**Hinakdal** ang kumpanya dahil sa paglabag sa karapatan ng mga empleyado.","translation":"The company **was accused in court** for violating employee rights."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalagyan na partikular na idinisenyo para sa pagtatapon ng basura at iba pang mga hindi na kailanganing bagay.
original_explanation: The designated black hole in every Filipino home where empty chichirya wrappers, balat ng saging, and broken dreams go. You have the main **basurahan** sa kusina, and then the mini one sa CR. Pro-tip: Always line it with a recycled grocery plastic bag. The English word "trashcan" is also very common in code-switching.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong ikalat ang balat ng kendi, itapon mo sa **basurahan**.","translation":"Don't scatter the candy wrapper, throw it in the **trash can**."},{"sentence":"Araw ng Lunes ang koleksyon ng basura kaya ilabas mo na ang **basurahan**.","translation":"Monday is garbage collection day so take the **garbage bin** out now."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghintay na matapos o mawala ang isang bagay, tulad ng panahon, galit, o pagkakataon, bago gumawa ng aksyon.
original_explanation: "Let it go, let it gooo..." but in Tagalog. Your friend's advice when you're super angry: "Palipasin mo muna ang galit mo." It's what you do with a bad day, a missed opportunity, or a storm—you just wait it out. It's the art of letting time do its thing.
usage_notes: Commonly used for time, emotions (especially anger), and opportunities.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hayaan mong **palipasin** ko muna ang sama ng loob ko bago tayo mag-usap.","translation":"Let me **let** my anger **pass** first before we talk."},{"sentence":"Sayang, pinalipas niya ang magandang pagkakataon.","translation":"What a waste, he **let** the good opportunity **pass**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **palipasin** ang gabi sa hotel dahil sa bagyo.","translation":"We need **to let** the night **pass** at the hotel because of the storm."}]

translation: please step on; let someone step on
meaning_filipino: Isang pakiusap o utos na tapakan o yurakan ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: The weird request you make to someone with clean shoes when there's a cockroach. "Paki-patapak nga nitong ipis!" It's the causative command form of 'to step on'. Can also be used figuratively, like asking someone to 'crush' your enemies, but usually, it's about a bug.
usage_notes: Usually used with 'paki-' for politeness (`pakipatapak`). It's asking someone else to do the stepping.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Patapak** mo nga itong lata para lumiit.","translation":"**Please step on** this can to flatten it."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **patapak** ng halaman sa hardin.","translation":"Don't **let anyone step on** the plants in the garden."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagkakaroon ng pare-parehong katayuan, karapatan, sukat, o oportunidad para sa lahat ng kasangkot, nang walang sinumang nakalalamang o naiiwan.
etymology: Reduplication of the root word 'pantay' (equal, level) to indicate 'all are equal'.
original_explanation: The ideal state of a relationship, but sometimes one person is more 'marupok' than the other. It's what you want when dividing the last slice of pizza among the barkada. Also, that feeling when everyone in the group project gets the same failing grade. #SanaAll
usage_notes: The reduplication emphasizes that the equality applies to every member of a group.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat **pantay-pantay** ang pagtingin ng batas sa mayaman at mahirap.","translation":"The law's treatment of the rich and poor should be **equal**."},{"sentence":"Hinati niya ang cake upang maging **pantay-pantay** ang lahat.","translation":"She divided the cake so that everyone would have an **equal** share."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking kahon na karaniwang gawa sa kahoy o metal, may takip na may bisagra, ginagamit sa pag-iimbak ng mga damit, kayamanan, o mahahalagang bagay.
original_explanation: Lola's version of cloud storage. It's where she keeps old photos, love letters from lolo, your baby clothes, and mysterious, ancient-smelling blankets. Unlocking a 'baul' feels like discovering a time capsule or a pirate's treasure.
usage_notes: Often implies an old, traditional wooden chest. Figuratively, 'baul ng alaala' means a repository of memories.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatago sa loob ng **baul** ang mga lumang litrato ng aming pamilya.","translation":"The old family photos are kept inside the **chest**."},{"sentence":"Mayaman daw ang matanda dahil mayroon siyang **baul** na puno ng ginto.","translation":"They say the old woman is rich because she has a **trunk** full of gold."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan na ginagamit sa pagsukat ng bigat o timbang ng isang bagay; estado ng pagiging pantay o patas ng distribusyon.
original_explanation: That thing in the palengke that the vendor uses to weigh your kilo ng bigas or isda. Also, what you need in your life when you're juggling work, love life, and your K-drama addiction. It's the 'work-life balance' everyone's chasing but few actually find.
usage_notes: Can refer to a physical weighing scale or the abstract concept of balance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gamitin mo ang **balansa** para malaman kung sapat ang timbang ng harina.","translation":"Use the **weighing scale** to know if the weight of the flour is enough."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **balansa** sa pagitan ng trabaho at personal na buhay.","translation":"**Balance** between work and personal life is important."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sumusunod sa pagkakasunod-sunod, espasyo, o panahon; ang susunod na bagay, tao, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: The next person in line at the Jollibee counter. The next episode of your favorite K-drama that you're dying to watch. 'Yung chismis na kasunod ng 'OMG, may sasabihin ako sa'yo!' It's simply 'what comes after.'
usage_notes: Can function as a noun ('Sino ang kasunod?'), an adverb ('Kasunod siyang dumating.'), or part of a prepositional phrase ('kasunod ng bahay').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **kasunod** sa pila para magbayad.","translation":"He is **next** in line to pay."},{"sentence":"**Kasunod** ng malakas na lindol ay ang pagbaha.","translation":"**Following** the strong earthquake was the flood."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kilos ng paghihimagsik laban sa isang awtoridad; ang proseso ng pag-umbok o pag-angat, tulad ng sa masa ng tinapay.
original_explanation: Can mean two things: 1) The Katipunan vs. Spain—a full-on rebellion. Think historical drama. 2) What your pandesal dough does before baking. It's the act of rising up, whether against a colonial power or because of yeast. So next time you see a perfect monay, you can say "Ganda ng pag-alsa!"
usage_notes: This word has a dual meaning, one historical/political and one culinary. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pag-alsa** ni Bonifacio ay isang mahalagang bahagi ng kasaysayan ng Pilipinas.","translation":"Bonifacio's **uprising** is an important part of Philippine history."},{"sentence":"Hintayin natin ang **pag-alsa** ng masa bago ito ilagay sa oven.","translation":"Let's wait for the dough's **rising** before putting it in the oven."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging gutay-gutay, punit-punit, o sira-sira, lalo na sa papel o tela.
original_explanation: Describes the aftermath of 'gumutay'. If your homework was 'ginutay' by the dog, it is now 'gunot'. It's that old 'basahan' (rag) that's more holes than fabric. It’s a state of being utterly shredded and worn out.
usage_notes: Often intensified by repetition: 'gunot-gunot'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **gunot** ang damit niya matapos sumabit sa pako.","translation":"His clothes became **tattered** after getting snagged on a nail."},{"sentence":"Itapon mo na 'yang **gunot** na papel.","translation":"Throw away that **shredded** paper."}]

meaning_filipino: (Kolokyal) Loko, wala sa tamang pag-iisip, o may sira sa ulo.
original_explanation: When someone's "may sapak," it means they're a bit off their rocker. It's like their brain got a *sapak* (the noun) and now it's not working right. "May sapak ka ba? Bakit mo binenta 'yung PS5 mo para sa Funko Pop?" It's the Pinoy equivalent of calling someone 'cray-cray'.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang salitang balbal o kolokyal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong pansinin 'yan, may **sapak** 'yan sa ulo.","translation":"Don't mind him, he's a bit **crazy** in the head."}]

translation: afam-core; style associated with foreigners in the Philippines
meaning_filipino: Isang istilo ng pananamit o pamumuhay na karaniwang iniuugnay sa mga dayuhang naninirahan sa Pilipinas, tulad ng pagsusuot ng shorts, tsinelas, at sando anuman ang okasyon.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng slang na 'afam' at hulaping '-core' mula sa Ingles, na tumutukoy sa isang aesthetic.
original_explanation: The official uniform of an expat in the Philippines: khaki shorts, a slightly faded shirt (maybe from a fun run or a local beer brand), flip-flops, and a backpack. It's a style that screams 'I'm comfortable with the heat and I'm probably heading to the beach or a bar.' If your Tito from abroad dresses like this, he's rocking the afamcore look.
usage_notes: Isang napaka-modernong slang na ginagamit upang ilarawan ang isang partikular na istilo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naka-shorts, sando, at tsinelas lang siya sa mall, talagang **afamcore** ang porma.","translation":"He was just wearing shorts, a tank top, and flip-flops at the mall, his style is really **afamcore**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sistema ng pagsukat, o isang pamantayan na ginagamit sa pagtatasa o paghahambing ng isang bagay, lalo na sa datos o pagganap.
original_explanation: Sa BPO, ito 'yung mga numerong nagpapasakit sa ulo mo: AHT, CSAT, QA score. 'Yan ang mga metrik na tinitingnan ng TL mo para malaman kung 'na-meet' mo ba ang 'expectations' o kailangan mo na ng coaching. Sa marketing, ito 'yung likes, shares, at engagement rate. Basically, a way to measure if you're winning or failing.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng negosyo, teknolohiya, at agham.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang mga **metrik** na gagamitin natin para sukatin ang tagumpay ng kampanya?","translation":"What are the **metrics** we will use to measure the success of the campaign?"},{"sentence":"Bumaba ang kanyang **metrik** sa customer satisfaction ngayong buwan.","translation":"His customer satisfaction **metrics** went down this month."}]

translation: to gang up on someone; to single out (collectively)
meaning_filipino: Ang sama-samang pagtuunan ng pansin, kritisismo, o kilos ang isang tao o bagay, kadalasan sa negatibong paraan.
original_explanation: This is what happens in a group chat when everyone suddenly agrees to make fun of one person's new haircut. It's the "pinagtulungan" or "pinagtripan" verb. In a work setting, it's when the whole team blames you for the failed project. Not a good feeling.
usage_notes: Has a strong negative connotation of ganging up or unfairly targeting an individual.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag ninyong **pagkaisahan** ang bago nating kaklase.","translation":"Don't **gang up on** our new classmate."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman niyang **pinagkaisahan** siya ng kanyang mga katrabaho.","translation":"She felt that her coworkers had **ganged up on** her."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang sasakyang-dagat, tulad ng barko o bangka, na nakatigil at nakatali sa daungan o piyer.
original_explanation: Like a Grab car that has ended the trip and is now parked at the destination. When a ship isn't sailing the high seas but is chilling at the port, taking on cargo, or letting passengers off, it's 'nakaduong'. It's in a state of being parked, but for boats.
usage_notes: Specifically used for water vessels.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming barko ang **nakaduong** sa pantalan ng Maynila.","translation":"Many ships are **docked** at the port of Manila."},{"sentence":"Mananatiling **nakaduong** ang lantsa hanggang gumanda ang panahon.","translation":"The ferry will remain **anchored** until the weather improves."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mensahe, pagbati, o awit na ipinadala at ipinarinig sa pamamagitan ng isang programa sa radyo.
original_explanation: The OG way to send a message before PMs and DMs. This is how you requested a song for your crush, sent birthday greetings to your Tita in another town, or found a long-lost relative. It's the sound of provincial afternoons, with a DJ reading your heartfelt (and sometimes cheesy) message on air. "Binabati ko po ang lahat ng nakikinig, from your listener friend, Jomar."
usage_notes: A compound term combining 'pahatid' (message) and 'radyo' (radio).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpadala siya ng **pahatid sa radyo** para batiin ang kanyang ina.","translation":"She sent a **radio dedication** to greet her mother."},{"sentence":"Narinig mo ba ang **pahatid sa radyo** kanina? Hinahanap ang may-ari ng isang aso.","translation":"Did you hear the **message on the radio** earlier? They're looking for the owner of a dog."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging walang-saysay, walang epekto, o hindi na balido ayon sa batas o kasunduan.
etymology: Mula sa `pagka-` (estado ng pagiging) + `walang bisa` (walang epekto o pagiging balido). Isang tambalang pangngalan.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your warranty when you try to DIY repair your phone. It's when a contract is voided, a law is repealed, or your free coupon has expired. It's the official "Sorry, 'di na 'to pwede" status. Parang 'yung pangako niya sa'yo, nag-expire na rin.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa mga kontekstong legal, pormal, o teknikal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Idineklara ng korte ang **pagkawalang-bisa** ng kanilang kasal.","translation":"The court declared the **nullification** of their marriage."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkawalang-bisa** ng kontrata ay dahil sa hindi pagtupad sa mga tuntunin.","translation":"The **invalidity** of the contract was due to non-compliance with the terms."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagak ng pera o ari-arian sa korte bilang pansamantalang garantiya upang makalaya ang isang akusado habang nililitis ang kanyang kaso.
original_explanation: This is what you do for a friend who got into some trouble. It's literally paying for their temporary freedom. 'Yung "Bes, nalintikan na, kailangan mo 'kong piyansahan!" text message na ayaw mong matanggap at 3 AM. It’s a financial and emotional rescue mission.
usage_notes: Can also be used figuratively to mean "to rescue someone from a difficult situation."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nilang maghanap ng malaking pera para **piyansahan** ang kanilang kapatid.","translation":"They need to find a lot of money to **post bail for** their sibling."},{"sentence":"Sino ang maglalakas-loob na **piyansahan** siya mula sa kanyang mga utang?","translation":"Who will dare to **bail him out** of his debts?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbuo ng isang palagay o pag-aakala tungkol sa isang bagay bago pa man magkaroon ng sapat na katibayan o impormasyon.
etymology: From Spanish 'presupuesto' (presupposition, assumption, budget). Note the meaning shift in Filipino context.
original_explanation: Basically, 'assuming lang'. It's when you jump to conclusions. You see your crush talking to someone else and you immediately 'nagpresupuwesto' that they're together. It's the root of all 'marites' gossip and 'sana all' moments. Don't assume, ask!
usage_notes: Less common than 'mag-assume' or 'maghinala', but more formal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag tayong **magpresupuwesto**; alamin muna natin ang buong kwento.","translation":"Let's not **presuppose**; let's find out the whole story first."},{"sentence":"**Nagpresupuwesto** siya na ayaw ko siyang kasama dahil hindi ako sumasagot sa tawag niya.","translation":"He **assumed** I didn't want to be with him because I wasn't answering his calls."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdaan nang higit pa sa isang takdang hangganan, lugar, o limitasyon.
original_explanation: When the jeepney driver doesn't hear your 'para!' and you end up two blocks away from your destination. Also, when you plan to spend only P500 on Shopee but your cart total is P2,500. Lumampas ka na sa budget.
usage_notes: Can be used for physical locations, abstract limits (like budget or authority), or time.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lumampas** ako sa bababaan ko dahil nakatulog ako sa bus.","translation":"I **went past** my stop because I fell asleep on the bus."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga katangian, sakit, o pag-aari na naipapasa mula sa mga ninuno patungo sa mga salinlahi.
original_explanation: It's when you get your mom's nose, your dad's temper, and your lola's talent for finding the best deals at the palengke. It's the reason why you're good at singing or why you have high blood pressure—'nasa lahi n'yo raw.' Can be a compliment or a curse, depending on what you inherited.
usage_notes: Often used with 'lang' as 'mana-mana lang' to mean 'it's just inherited'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang talento sa pag-awit ay **mana-mana** sa kanilang pamilya.","translation":"Her talent for singing is **hereditary** in their family."},{"sentence":"Sabi ng doktor, ang diabetes ay maaaring **mana-mana**.","translation":"The doctor said that diabetes can be **inherited**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang gawain ay ang pagsusulat, partikular na ang pagtatala o paglikha ng mga akda.
etymology: From taga- (doer of an action) + sulat (write).
original_explanation: The designated note-taker of the group. Sa BPO, sila yung agent na taga-document ng call. Sa barkada, sila yung taga-sulat ng group project na laging puyat. In short, the official 'taga-type'.
usage_notes: Can mean a professional writer (`manunulat`) but more often implies someone assigned the task of writing or taking notes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ako ang naatasang maging **tagasulat** ng minutes ng meeting.","translation":"I was assigned to be the **writer** of the meeting minutes."},{"sentence":"Ang mga sinaunang **tagasulat** ay gumagamit ng balahibo ng ibon bilang panulat.","translation":"The ancient **scribes** used bird feathers as pens."}]

meaning_filipino: Itawid o ihatid ang isang tao o bagay sa kabilang pampang gamit ang isang balsa.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'Grab' for crossing rivers in the province before bridges were cool. You and your stuff get on a bamboo raft, and Mang Kiko poles you to the other side. It's slow, scenic, and has a 100% chance of getting your feet wet.
usage_notes: Primarily used in rural or provincial contexts where rafts are a mode of transport.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **ibalsa** ang mga sako ng palay papunta sa kabilang baryo.","translation":"The sacks of rice need to be **transported by raft** to the other village."},{"sentence":"**Inibalsa** nila ang mga turista sa gitna ng lawa.","translation":"They **took** the tourists **by raft** to the middle of the lake."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagsasabi o paggawa ng isang bagay nang higit sa isang beses.
original_explanation: 'Ma, alis na po ako.' 'Sige, ingat.' 'Ma, alis na po.' 'Oo, ingat ka.' That's `pag-uulit`. It's what your teacher does during a review, what your favorite song does on loop, and what happens in a meeting that could have been an email. Sometimes it's for emphasis, sometimes it's just... a glitch in the matrix.
usage_notes: Can refer to repeating words, actions, or events.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pag-uulit** ng aralin ay mahalaga para sa pagkatuto.","translation":"The **repetition** of the lesson is important for learning."},{"sentence":"'Paulit-ulit na lang!' sigaw niya, sawa na sa **pag-uulit** ng parehong pagkakamali.","translation":"'It's just the same thing over and over!' she shouted, tired of the **repetition** of the same mistake."}]

meaning_filipino: Salitang balbal para sa pera.
etymology: Possibly a playful alteration of 'datu', implying that the 'datu' or boss has the money. Another theory is from Hokkien 'toa-chîng' (big money).
original_explanation: This is what you need to pay for your milk tea, your Grab ride, and your Netflix subscription. It's the 70s/80s slang for money that's still cool to use. When your friend asks, 'May **datung** ka ba?' they're not asking about a chieftain, they're asking if you're broke. It's the OG 'pera,' 'kwarta,' 'kweltz.'
usage_notes: Purely informal and slang. Do not use this in a formal paper unless you're writing about Filipino slang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pare, wala akong **datung** ngayon, sa susunod na lang ako manlilibre.","translation":"Bro, I don't have any **money** right now, I'll treat you next time."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang **datung** na napanalunan niya sa lotto.","translation":"He won a lot of **cash** in the lottery."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang panlabas na espasyo, karaniwang isang basketball court, na may bubong upang magbigay-proteksyon laban sa araw at ulan.
original_explanation: Hindi lang 'to basketball court, ito ang social hall ng barangay. Dito ginaganap ang lahat: liga ng basketball, zumba sessions, binyagan, kasalan, lamay, Christmas party, at vaccination drive. Ang sentro ng buhay-komunidad, umaraw man o umulan.
usage_notes: A standard feature in almost every Philippine barangay and school.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa barangay **covered court** gaganapin ang susunod na pagpupulong.","translation":"The next meeting will be held at the barangay **covered court**."},{"sentence":"Naglaro kami ng basketball sa **covered court** kahit umuulan.","translation":"We played basketball at the **covered court** even though it was raining."}]

translation: to have something built; to cause to be erected
meaning_filipino: Ipatayo o ipagawa ang isang estruktura o gusali. Hilingin sa iba na itayo ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: When you're the boss, the client, or the parent with the cash, and you tell someone else to do the actual building. "I want a condo here." You don't mix the cement yourself, you just `pabangunin` mo sa contractor. It's the verb for commissioning a project, from a sandcastle to a skyscraper.
usage_notes: This is a causative verb. The root 'bangon' means 'to rise' or 'to get up'. Here, it's used in the sense of making something rise, i.e., building it.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-iipon sila para **pabangunin** ang kanilang pangarap na bahay.","translation":"They are saving up to **have** their dream house **built**."},{"sentence":"Sino ang arkitektong pinili mong **pabangunin** ang gusaling iyan?","translation":"Who is the architect you chose to **have that building erected**?"}]

translation: to be hit; to be struck; to be affected
meaning_filipino: Ang maranasan ang pagtama o pag-abot ng isang bagay, pisikal man o metaporikal.
original_explanation: What happens when you get hit by Cupid's arrow ("**tamaan** ng pag-ibig"), a stray basketball, or a passive-aggressive comment from a coworker. "Ouch, **tamaan** ako dun ah." It's being the unwilling target of something.
usage_notes: The object-focused verb. "Tamaan ka sana ng kidlat!" is a common curse, meaning "May you be struck by lightning!"
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingat ka, baka **tamaan** ka ng bolang lumilipad.","translation":"Be careful, you might **be hit** by the flying ball."},{"sentence":"Mukhang **tinamaan** si Marco kay Jessica.","translation":"It looks like Marco has **been struck** (fallen for) Jessica."}]

translation: to make steeper; to make upright
meaning_filipino: Gawing mas matarik o mas nakatindig nang tuwid ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is what you tell the construction worker when the ramp they built looks more like a slide for penguins. It's about increasing the angle, making something stand up straighter or steeper. "Patarikin mo pa 'yang hagdan, masyadong banayad."
usage_notes: Can refer to literal steepness (like a hill or ramp) or making something stand up straight.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan niya ang mga trabahador na **patarikin** ang bubong.","translation":"He instructed the workers to **make the roof steeper**."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang **patarikin** ang poste na natumba ng bagyo.","translation":"He is trying to **make the post that fell during the typhoon stand upright**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang patpat na ginagamit sa pagtulak ng bola sa larong bilyar.
original_explanation: The magic wand used by Efren "Bata" Reyes. This is the stick you use at the local pool hall to show off your (probably non-existent) billiard skills. You chalk the tip, lean over the table, and hope for the best. "Pahiram ng tako, pare!"
usage_notes: Ang pagbigkas ay pareho sa 'tako' (wedge), kaya ang konteksto ang susi.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magaling humawak ng **tako** si Efren kaya siya naging kampeon.","translation":"Efren is great at handling a **cue stick** which is why he became a champion."}]

translation: to make narrow; to make tight
meaning_filipino: Gawing mas makitid o masikip ang isang espasyo o bagay.
etymology: Root word 'sikip' means tight or narrow. The affix 'pag- -in' turns it into a verb.
original_explanation: Ever tried to fit 15 people in a jeepney meant for 10? That's *pagsikipin* in action. It's what you do to your budget before payday, trying to stretch it out. Or when you're arranging furniture in a condo studio and you have to make everything fit. 'Pagsikipin mo pa, kasya pa isa!' (Make it tighter, one more can fit!) is the unofficial mantra.
usage_notes: This is a command or infinitive verb form. The noun form would be 'pagsikip' (the state of being tight) or 'paninikip' (the act of becoming tight, e.g., 'paninikip ng dibdib').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag nating **pagsikipin** ang daanan upang makalabas ang mga tao.","translation":"Let's not **make** the pathway **narrow** so people can exit."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **pagsikipin** ang lahat ng damit sa isang maliit na maleta.","translation":"He tried **to make** all the clothes **fit tightly** in one small suitcase."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang nagpapahiwatig ng kawalan ng katiyakan o posibilidad; baka sakali.
etymology: Its exact origin is debated among linguists, but it is treated as a whole adverbial unit in modern Tagalog.
original_explanation: This is your go-to word for when you're not sure if you're going to make it to the party, or if that Shopee parcel will actually arrive on time. 'Marahil darating siya.' is the polite way of saying '50/50 chance, don't get your hopes up.' It's the official adverb of 'bahala na'.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'baka'. 'Marahil' can sound slightly more formal or literary than 'baka'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Marahil** ay uulan mamayang hapon kaya magdala ka ng payong.","translation":"**Perhaps** it will rain this afternoon, so bring an umbrella."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko pa sigurado, ngunit **marahil** ay makakadalo ako sa pagtitipon.","translation":"I'm not yet sure, but **maybe** I can attend the gathering."}]

translation: to be enchanted; to be charmed by a supernatural being
meaning_filipino: Maging biktima ng engkanto o maligno; mabighani o mapahamak dahil sa kapangyarihan ng isang engkanto.
etymology: From `ma-` (potential verb prefix) + `engkanto` (supernatural being), which is from Spanish 'encanto' (charm, enchantment).
original_explanation: This is what your lola warns you about when you play too late outside or pee on a random mound of earth (nuno sa punso!). It's the supernatural explanation for getting sick after a trip to the province, or for suddenly falling for someone who is... suspiciously charming. "Baka na-engkanto ka na niyan!"
usage_notes: Deeply rooted in Philippine folklore and superstition. The user provided 'maingkanto', which is a common misspelling of the correct 'maengkanto'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayon sa matatanda, baka **maengkanto** ka kung mag-iingay ka sa gubat.","translation":"According to the elders, you might **be enchanted** (by a spirit) if you make noise in the forest."},{"sentence":"Nagkasakit daw si Ana pag-uwi galing probinsya; hinala nila ay naengkanto ito.","translation":"They said Ana got sick after coming home from the province; they suspect she was charmed by a supernatural being."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang alternatibong pagbaybay para sa 'Kristiyanismo', na tumutukoy sa relihiyong nakabatay sa mga aral ni Hesukristo.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na 'cristianismo', isang variant ng pagbaybay sa Filipino.
original_explanation: This is how you type 'Kristiyanismo' when you're texting fast and can't be bothered with the extra 'i'. It means the exact same thing, just the 'shortcut' version. Think of it as the difference between 'for real' and 'fr'.
usage_notes: Considered a common variant spelling of 'Kristiyanismo.' While widely understood, 'Kristiyanismo' is preferred in formal writing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paglaganap ng **Kristyanismo** ay isang mahalagang bahagi ng ating nakaraan.","translation":"The spread of **Christianity** is an important part of our past."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang damdamin o pagpapakita ng malalim at taimtim na paggalang, pagpipitagan, o pagsamba sa isang tao, bagay, o konsepto.
original_explanation: This is that deep, almost holy respect you give to your lola's secret adobo recipe, or the way K-Pop stans look at their idols. It's more than just 'respect'; it's a 'bow down, peasants' level of admiration. It's the feeling that makes you quiet and awestruck.
usage_notes: This is a deep or literary Tagalog word, not commonly used in casual conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinakita nila ang kanilang **pamintuhuan** sa mga bayani ng lahi sa pamamagitan ng isang minutong katahimikan.","translation":"They showed their **veneration** for the nation's heroes through a minute of silence."},{"sentence":"Ang **pamintuhuan** sa mga nakatatanda ay isang mahalagang bahagi ng kulturang Pilipino.","translation":"**Reverence** for the elderly is an important part of Filipino culture."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagtitipon ng mga kinatawan mula sa iba't ibang simbahang Kristiyano sa buong mundo upang talakayin at pagpasyahan ang mga usapin ng pananampalataya, doktrina, at disiplina.
original_explanation: Think of it as the ultimate crossover event for Christian churches. It's like the Avengers of theology, where leaders from different Christian denominations gather to discuss the "lore" and "canon" of the faith. A pulong sansinukob is a big deal in church history. 'Pulong' = meeting, 'sansinukob' = universe/the whole world. A universal meeting!
usage_notes: This is a very specific term used almost exclusively in a religious or theological context, particularly within Christianity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Ikalawang Konsilyo Vaticano ay isang mahalagang **pulong sansinukob** sa kasaysayan ng Simbahang Katoliko.","translation":"The Second Vatican Council was an important **ecumenical council** in the history of the Catholic Church."},{"sentence":"Pinag-usapan sa **pulong sansinukob** ang mga doktrina ng simbahan.","translation":"Church doctrines were discussed at the **ecumenical council**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtrato sa isang tao na parang alipin; ang pagmamaltrato, pag-abuso, o labis na pagpapahirap sa kapwa.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "busabos" (abject slave, wretched person).
original_explanation: Ito 'yung ginagawa ng mga kontrabida sa teleserye sa kanilang mga katulong. 'Yung tipong halos wala nang pahinga, pinapahirapan, at minaliit ang pagkatao. Sa office setting, ito yung feeling mo kapag 'yung boss mo, pinapagawa sa'yo ang trabaho ng tatlong tao for the price of one. Huwag maging ganito.
usage_notes: Isang napakatinding salita na nagpapahiwatig ng dehumanisasyon at matinding kalupitan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi tama na **busabusin** ang mga kasambahay.","translation":"It is not right **to maltreat** the household helpers."},{"sentence":"Pinagbawalan niya ang kanyang mga anak na **busabusin** ang kanilang mga katulong.","translation":"She forbade her children from **abusing** their helpers."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis na pagpikit at pagdilat ng mga mata; maaari ring tumukoy sa mabilis at paulit-ulit na pagliwanag at pagdilim ng isang ilaw.
original_explanation: The action your eyes do when you see your crush ('*wink wink*'), or when dust gets in them. It's also what a dying fluorescent light does before it finally gives up, much like my motivation on a Friday afternoon. And of course, the twinkling of stars is 'pagkisap ng mga bituin.'
usage_notes: Madalas na ginagamit sa pariralang 'isang kisapmata' (in the blink of an eye).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kisap** ng mga bituin sa langit ay napakagandang pagmasdan.","translation":"The **twinkle** of the stars in the sky is so beautiful to watch."},{"sentence":"Isang mabilis na **kisap** lang ng kanyang mga mata ang sagot niya sa akin.","translation":"A quick **blink** of her eyes was her only answer to me."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o katangian ng pagiging lubhang malungkot, mapait, o kahabag-habag.
etymology: Mula sa 'pagka-' (ang estado ng pagiging) + 'masaklap' (mapait, trahedya). Ang gitling ay minsan ginagamit para sa kalinawan.
original_explanation: This is the feeling when you studied all night for an exam, but it got postponed. It's when your online order arrives and it's completely wrong. It's the 'sana hindi na lang' moment, the universe playing a sad, ironic joke on you. The very essence of a tragic teleserye plot twist.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang bigyang-diin ang kapaitan o trahedya ng isang sitwasyon. Ang anyong may gitling na 'pagka-masaklap' ay karaniwan, ngunit ang 'pagkamasaklap' ay katanggap-tanggap din.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagka-masaklap** ng kanyang kapalaran ay nagdulot ng awa sa marami.","translation":"The **tragic nature** of her fate drew pity from many."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong kinikilala ng simbahan bilang may pambihirang antas ng kabanalan, kadalasang ginagamit bilang titulo para sa mga lalaking banal.
original_explanation: The guy version of 'Santa'. Every barangay has a fiesta for one. It's also that collection of statues your lola has on the altar that you were forbidden to play with as a kid. Often abbreviated as 'Sto.' like in 'Sto. Niño'.
usage_notes: The feminine form is 'Santa'. The abbreviation 'Sto.' is very common in place names (e.g., Sto. Tomas, Batangas) and names of saints (e.g., Sto. Niño). The word 'santo' can also refer to the religious statue itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **Santo** Niño de Cebu ay isang tanyag na imahen sa Pilipinas.","translation":"The **Saint** Child of Cebu is a famous image in the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Pista bukas ng aming patron, si **Santo** Isidro Labrador.","translation":"It's the feast of our patron, **Saint** Isidore the Laborer, tomorrow."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na lumipat at nanirahan sa ibang bansa na hindi niya sinilangan.
original_explanation: This is your tita in Canada who sends you a balikbayan box every Christmas, or your cousin in the US who suddenly has a strong accent after two years. They're living the dream (and dealing with the cold) for the family.
usage_notes: This is a loanword from English and is used commonly in both formal and informal contexts. The Tagalog equivalent is "dayuhan" or "mandarayuhan".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming Pilipinong **immigrant** ang matagumpay sa kanilang mga karera sa ibang bansa.","translation":"Many Filipino **immigrants** are successful in their careers abroad."},{"sentence":"Bilang isang **immigrant**, nahirapan siyang mag-adjust sa bagong kultura.","translation":"As an **immigrant**, he had a hard time adjusting to the new culture."}]

translation: To flinch; to recoil; to jump back
meaning_filipino: Biglaang pag-urong o pagkilos ng katawan dahil sa gulat, takot, o sakit.
original_explanation: That sudden body-jerk when a cockroach suddenly flies. It's your reaction when someone taps your shoulder from behind in a dark alley (or in the office when you're deep in focus). The physical manifestation of 'Ay, butiki!'
usage_notes: The root 'igtad' is rarely used alone. It is almost always found in its verb form, 'umigtad' (to flinch).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umigtad** siya nang biglang may pumutok.","translation":"She **flinch**ed when something suddenly exploded."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang matakot, pusa lang 'yan kaya ka **umigtad**.","translation":"Don't be scared, it was just a cat that made you **jump back**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtigil sa gawain o paggalaw upang mabawi ang lakas; ang paglalaan ng oras para sa pamamahinga sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: The most sacred phrase for any BPO agent, student during finals week, or anyone who's been adulting too hard. It's the future tense of "I give up... for now." It's the promise you make to yourself after finishing a mountain of work. "After this, magpapahinga na talaga ako." (Narrator: He did not.)
usage_notes: This is the future tense form of the verb "magpahinga" (to rest).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng mahabang byahe, **magpapahinga** muna kami.","translation":"After the long trip, we **will rest** for a while."},{"sentence":"Sabi ng doktor, kailangan kong **magpahinga** nang isang linggo.","translation":"The doctor said I need **to rest** for a week."}]

translation: to carry on the shoulder, to bear
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbuhat o pagdadala ng isang bagay na mabigat sa pamamagitan ng paglalagay nito sa balikat.
etymology: From `pasan` (to carry on the shoulder) + `-in` (verb-forming suffix).
original_explanation: The literal act of carrying something on your shoulder, like a sack of rice from the palengke or your drunk friend after a wild night out. "Pasanin mo 'to," says your boss, handing you a mountain of work on a Friday afternoon.
usage_notes: Can be used both literally for physical loads and figuratively for responsibilities.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pinasan** niya ang isang sakong bigas mula sa tindahan.","translation":"He **carried** a sack of rice on his shoulder from the store."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pasanin** ang problema ng buong mundo.","translation":"Don't **bear** the problems of the whole world."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malambot at sariwang keso na gawa sa gatas at krema, karaniwang ginagamit bilang palaman sa tinapay.
original_explanation: The official palaman of bagels and the secret ingredient to that burnt cheesecake you keep seeing on your feed. It's that tangy, creamy spread that makes you forget you're on a diet. Basically, the 'sosyal' version of Cheez Whiz.
usage_notes: Almost always spelled as two words or as 'creamcheese'. Pronounced locally as /krim-tsis/.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pabili ng isang box ng **cream cheese** para sa gagawin kong cheesecake.","translation":"Please buy a box of **cream cheese** for the cheesecake I'm making."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang pandesal na may **cream cheese** at bawang.","translation":"Pandesal with **cream cheese** and garlic is delicious."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng tiyaga, puwersa, o diin upang makamit ang isang layunin o mangyari ang isang bagay, kahit na may pagtutol o kahirapan.
original_explanation: This is your tita at a family reunion saying "Sige na, kumain ka pa! Ang payat mo!" even if you're already full. It's also you trying to fit into your pre-pandemic jeans. You can also 'magpilit' to wake up for your 8 AM shift after binge-watching a K-drama until 3 AM. It’s the art of 'push mo 'yan, teh!'
usage_notes: Can have a positive connotation (perseverance) or a negative one (being pushy).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magpilit** kung ayaw niya talaga.","translation":"Don't **insist** if they really don't want to."},{"sentence":"**Nagpilit** siyang tapusin ang trabaho kahit pagod na pagod na siya.","translation":"He **forced himself** to finish the work even though he was very tired."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-alis sa tahanan o isang lugar nang walang paalam, karaniwan dahil sa galit, pagtatampo, o pagsuway.
original_explanation: The classic teenage drama move. You pack your bag with three shirts and your favorite pillow, vowing never to return... until you get hungry an hour later. It's the ultimate 'I'm out!' but usually with a return ticket.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to running away from home or a place of responsibility, distinct from simply leaving ('pag-alis').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang madalas na **paglayas** ng bata ay senyales ng problema sa pamilya.","translation":"The child's frequent **running away** is a sign of family problems."},{"sentence":"Nagbanta siya ng **paglayas** kung hindi ibibigay ang kaniyang gusto.","translation":"He threatened **to run away** if his wants were not given."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglalaan, pag-aayos, o paggamit ng oras sa isang mahusay at planadong paraan.
etymology: From pag- (nominalizer) + sa- (causative) + oras (hour, time), from Spanish 'horas'.
original_explanation: This is the adulting skill you wish you learned in school. It's juggling your BPO night shift, your online selling side hustle, and still having time to binge a K-drama series. It's the art of arriving 'Filipino time' but making it look intentional. When your project manager asks for your 'pagsasaoras' plan, they mean your timeline, not your life story.
usage_notes: A somewhat formal or technical term for 'timing' or 'time management.' More commonly, people might just say 'pag-timpla ng oras' or 'pamamahala ng oras.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang tamang **pagsasaoras** sa paghahain ng mga reklamo.","translation":"Proper **timing** is important in filing complaints."},{"sentence":"Ang tagumpay ng proyekto ay nakasalalay sa mahusay na **pagsasaoras** ng bawat gawain.","translation":"The project's success depends on the efficient **time management** of each task."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na laging ginagawa o sinusunod na naging bahagi na ng pang-araw-araw na pamumuhay o kultura.
etymology: From 'gawi' (habit, manner), with the 'kina-' prefix and '-an' suffix, indicating a place or result of the action.
original_explanation: This is your personal 'factory settings.' It's the morning coffee you can't live without, the automatic 'po' and 'opo' to elders, or your body's instinct to check your phone the moment you wake up. It's the 'what you usually do' that defines your routine.
usage_notes: Often refers to long-standing habits or cultural practices.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kinagawian** na ng mga Pilipino ang magdaos ng salu-salo tuwing Pasko.","translation":"It has become a **tradition** for Filipinos to hold feasts during Christmas."},{"sentence":"Mahirap alisin ang masamang **kinagawian**.","translation":"It's hard to remove a bad **habit**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagdadalang-tao; isang babae na may dinadalang sanggol sa kanyang sinapupunan.
original_explanation: The state of being where you suddenly have cravings for green mangoes with bagoong at 3 AM. When someone is buntis, they get a pass for being moody ('paglilihi'), get the best seat on the MRT, and everyone suddenly becomes a health expert around them. 'Congrats, you're now eating for two!'
usage_notes: Can also be used as a noun ('Ang buntis') to refer to a pregnant woman.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinayuhan ng doktor ang babaeng **buntis** na magpahinga at kumain ng masusustansyang pagkain.","translation":"The doctor advised the **pregnant** woman to rest and eat nutritious food."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang unti-unting pagdidilim ng kalangitan dahil sa pagdating ng makakapal na ulap na tumatakip sa araw. Ito ang anyong pangkaganapan ng 'kulimlim'.
original_explanation: This is what the sky does right before a major downpour or a dramatic scene in a movie. The sun disappears, the clouds get thick and gray, and everything gets gloomy. It's the universe's way of saying, "Mag-ready ka na, bes. May drama/ulan na paparating." When the sky kumulimlim, you better have your umbrella or your feelings ready.
usage_notes: Past tense/completed aspect. Refers to the sky becoming cloudy and dark.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Biglang **kumulimlim** kaya't minadali naming isinara ang mga bintana.","translation":"The sky suddenly **became overcast**, so we rushed to close the windows."},{"sentence":"**Kumulimlim** ang paligid bago ang malakas na bagyo.","translation":"The surroundings **darkened** before the strong typhoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging mahina, malata, o walang lakas, tulad ng isang halamang nalanta o isang taong may sakit.
original_explanation: That feeling when the Wi-Fi is down, your phone is at 1%, and you haven't had coffee. You're not just tired, you're *lupaypay*. Your shoulders are slumped, your energy is zero, like a plant that hasn't been watered in a week. It's the human equivalent of a low-battery icon.
usage_notes: Often used to describe physical weakness due to heat, fatigue, or illness. Can also describe wilted plants.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lupaypay** ang mga dahon ng halaman dahil sa tindi ng sikat ng araw.","translation":"The leaves of the plant are **drooping** because of the intense heat of the sun."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam ko ay **lupaypay** ako buong araw dahil sa lagnat.","translation":"I feel **weak** all day because of the fever."}]

meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng kaukulang pagtingin, pag-iingat, o presyo ang isang bagay, tao, o konsepto.
original_explanation: It's what you do to your sweldo on payday before all the bills attack. It's also that thing your ex didn't do to you. Charot. "Pahalagahan mo naman ako" is the national anthem of the 'sana all' club. To give something its proper worth, whether it's a diamond ring or your 15-minute coffee break.
usage_notes: Often used in emotional or financial contexts. Can mean to literally put a price on something (appraise) or to emotionally/metaphorically cherish something/someone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat mong **halagahan** ang mga payo ng iyong mga magulang.","translation":"You should **value** the advice of your parents."},{"sentence":"Magkano mo **hahalgahan** ang lumang alahas na iyan?","translation":"How much will you **appraise** that old jewelry for?"}]

meaning_filipino: Bawat isa sa serye ng maliliit na buto na bumubuo sa gulugod (backbone).
original_explanation: 'Yung mga buto-buto sa likod mo na parang stack ng Pringles na nagpapatayo sa'yo. 'Pag sumakit 'yan, sign of aging na raw. Or baka sign na kailangan mo na ng bagong office chair.
usage_notes: Isang terminong medikal o siyentipiko. Ang anyong pangmaramihan ay "vertebrae."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napinsala ang kanyang pang-apat na **bertebra** sa aksidente.","translation":"His fourth **vertebra** was damaged in the accident."},{"sentence":"Ang gulugod ay binubuo ng maraming magkakadugtong na **bertebra**.","translation":"The spine is composed of many interconnected **vertebrae**."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubos na nakabihis o pormal ang kasuotan; ayos na ayos ang pananamit para sa isang okasyon.
original_explanation: Yung OOTD (Outfit Of The Day) mo na pang-rampa levels. Hindi ka lang nakabihis, bisting-bisti ka! Parang pupunta ka sa kasal o debut kahit sa mall lang naman ang punta. Yung tipong pinaghandaan mo talaga 'yung suot mo from head to toe.
usage_notes: Emphasizes being formally or elaborately dressed, more than just 'nakabihis'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bisting-bisti** si Ana para sa kanyang job interview.","translation":"Ana is **all dressed up** for her job interview."},{"sentence":"Bakit ka **bisting-bisti**? May lakad ka ba?","translation":"Why are you so **well-dressed**? Are you going somewhere?"}]

translation: to be overtaken by noon; to have a late lunch
meaning_filipino: Ang abutan ng katanghalian habang gumagawa ng isang bagay o nasa daan, na nagreresulta sa pagkahuli sa panananghalian.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're so busy with chismis or work that you look at the clock and it's already 2 PM. You've been 'overtaken by noon.' The stomach is grumbling, the hangry monster is awakening. It's the official term for 'I forgot to eat lunch on time.'
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ipaliwanag kung bakit hindi pa nakakakain ng tanghalian.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagmamadali siyang umuwi dahil ayaw niyang **matanghalianan** sa daan.","translation":"She hurried home because she didn't want **to be overtaken by noon** on the road."}]

translation: to take an examination or test
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkuha ng isang pagsusulit upang masukat ang kaalaman o kakayahan.
original_explanation: That moment of truth in class where you find out if your all-night Netflix binge was a better idea than studying. It's the formal term for taking a quiz or exam. 'Mag-e-exam' is more common in casual talk, but 'magsulit' is the classic school-speak that brings back memories of sweat and Scantron sheets.
usage_notes: A very common term in the Philippine academic context. It is a homonym of 'magsulit' which means 'to return/submit'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga mag-aaral ay **magsusulit** sa asignaturang Agham bukas.","translation":"The students will **take a test** in Science tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Hindi ako nakapag-aral nang mabuti, kaya kinakabahan akong **magsulit**.","translation":"I wasn't able to study well, so I'm nervous **to take the exam**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na mahusay at epektibong magsalita sa publiko; isang mananalumpati.
original_explanation: Ito yung kaklase mo nung high school na laging kinukuha para sa declamation at laging panalo. Sila yung mga taong kayang-kayang ibenta kahit ang buhangin sa disyerto gamit lang ang kanilang laway at galing sa pagsasalita. Think politicians, motivational speakers, or yung tito mong laging may speech sa family reunion.
usage_notes: Mas pormal kaysa sa "tagapagsalita" o "speaker". Nagpapahiwatig ng mataas na antas ng kasanayan sa retorika.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala si Jose Rizal bilang isang mahusay na manunulat at **orador**.","translation":"Jose Rizal is known as an excellent writer and **orator**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao o hayop na may tendensiyang maligaw o mawala sa daan.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'pa-' (nagpapahiwatig ng tendensiya o hilig) at salitang-ugat na 'ligaw' (nawawala, walang tiyak na direksyon).
original_explanation: 'Yung kaibigan mong kahit may Waze na, naliligaw pa rin? Siya 'yun, **paligaw**. Or 'yung aso ninyong laging nakakalabas ng gate tapos hindi na marunong umuwi. Describes someone or something that easily gets lost.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan ng isang katangian o hilig. Iba ang kahulugan nito sa 'manliligaw' (suitor).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang tutang **paligaw** ang nakita namin sa kalsada.","translation":"We saw a **stray** puppy on the street."},{"sentence":"Talagang **paligaw** si Ana, kaya laging may kasama kapag umaalis.","translation":"Ana is really **prone to getting lost**, so she always has a companion when she goes out."}]

meaning_filipino: Nauukol o ginagamit sa pagtuturo ng isang partikular na doktrina, prinsipyo, o sistema ng paniniwala.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `pan-` at salitang hiram sa Espanyol na `doctrina`.
original_explanation: Describes anything used for indoctrination. Think of the pamphlets, seminars, or training modules used to teach a specific set of beliefs, whether for a religion, a political party, or a multi-level marketing scheme. It's the 'how-to' guide for believing something very specific.
usage_notes: Madalas ginagamit sa konteksto ng relihiyon, pulitika, o anumang organisasyong may mahigpit na sinusunod na mga aral.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga aklat na ito ay **pandoktrina** at hindi para sa pangkalahatang mambabasa.","translation":"These books are **doctrinal** and not for the general reader."},{"sentence":"Sumailalim sila sa isang sesyon na **pandoktrina** bago maging miyembro.","translation":"They underwent a **doctrinal** session before becoming members."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubos na ipinagbabawal; walang anumang kapahintulutan.
original_explanation: This isn't just 'bawal', this is the final boss of 'bawal'. It's when your mom uses your full name.
