It's the difference between a "No Parking" sign and a "No Parking - Tow Away Zone" sign. If something is bawal na bawal, doing it will likely result in major consequences, a chancla, or a call to HR.
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang paraan upang patindihin ang konsepto ng pagbabawal sa Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bawal na bawal** ang gumamit ng cellphone habang nagmamaneho.","translation":"Using a cellphone while driving is **strictly prohibited**."},{"sentence":"Sa aming pamilya, **bawal na bawal** ang magsinungaling.","translation":"In our family, lying is **absolutely forbidden**."}]

translation: to reduce from; to give a discount
meaning_filipino: Alisin ang isang bahagi mula sa isang kabuuan; magbigay ng diskuwento o bawas sa presyo para sa isang tao o mula sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the verb you use when you're haggling at the palengke. "Ate, bawahan mo naman!" (Miss, give me a discount!). It's the act of reducing the price or taking a little bit off the top for someone. It's the financial version of "less is more."
usage_notes: Ang 'bawahan' ay nakatuon sa bagay o tao kung saan kinuha ang bawas. Ihambing sa 'bawasin', na nakatuon sa mismong bagay na binabawas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **bawahan** ninyo ang presyo ng bilihin.","translation":"Please, **reduce** the price of the goods."},{"sentence":"**Binawahan** niya ng sampung piso ang bayad ko.","translation":"She **reduced** my payment by ten pesos."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-aayos ng buhok ng isang tao gamit ang suklay.
original_explanation: The act of untangling the mess that is your hair, or someone else's. This is what your lola did to you as a kid, pulling a little too hard while telling you stories. It's a verb of care, but sometimes, a verb of slight pain. "Suklayan mo nga 'yang buhok mo, mukha kang bruha" is a classic mom-ism.
usage_notes: This is the directional/locational focus form of the verb from the root "suklay" (comb). "Suklayin" is the object-focus form (to comb a specific thing, like a knot), but "suklayan" is used for the general act on a person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig **suklayan** ng ina ang mahabang buhok ng kanyang anak.","translation":"The mother loves **to comb** her daughter's long hair."},{"sentence":"Pakisabi sa barbero na **suklayan** nang maigi ang gilid.","translation":"Please tell the barber **to comb** the sides well."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na binabayaran upang magbantay at magpanatili ng kaayusan at kaligtasan sa isang lugar o ari-arian.
etymology: Colloquial Filipinization of the English word 'security'.
original_explanation: Short for 'security guard'. Sila 'yung unang babati sa'yo ng 'good morning, ma'am/sir' sa mall, sa condo, o sa office. Sila rin ang expert sa logbook at pag-check ng bag na parang may hinahanap na kayamanan. They are the unsung heroes of our everyday safety.
usage_notes: A common and informal term for 'security guard'. 'Guwardiya' is the more formal equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtanong ako sa **sekyu** kung saan ang pinakamalapit na ATM.","translation":"I asked the **security guard** where the nearest ATM is."},{"sentence":"Laging nakangiti ang **sekyu** sa aming opisina.","translation":"The **security guard** in our office is always smiling."}]

meaning_filipino: Paggawa ng isang aksyon; paggalaw ng katawan o bahagi nito.
original_explanation: This is the opposite of "pabebe" or "pa-victim". It's taking action. 'Yung nanay mo na sumisigaw ng "Hoy, kumilos-kilos ka diyan!", 'yan 'yun. It's the "Just Do It" of the Filipino household. 'Wag puro salita, 'wag puro plano, kumilos ka!
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **kumilos** agad bago pa lumala ang sitwasyon.","translation":"We need to **act** immediately before the situation gets worse."},{"sentence":"Bakit hindi ka **kumilos** nang tawagin kita?","translation":"Why didn't you **move** when I called you?"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang kilos na isinagawa nang walang pag-aalinlangan, pag-aatubili, o pag-uurong-sulong.
etymology: Mula sa "wala" (none) at "gatol" (hesitation, stutter). Ang "gatol" mismo ay isang salitang bihira nang gamitin.
original_explanation: How you say "yes" when someone asks "libre kita?" (my treat?). It's acting instantly, without a second thought. Like when you see the last piece of chicken skin on the plate—you grab it, **walang-gatol**. No doubts, no regrets, just pure, decisive action.
usage_notes: "Gatol" itself is a rare word meaning hesitation or a stammer. The phrase 'walang-gatol' is more common than its root word. It functions as an adverb modifying a verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Walang-gatol** siyang tumulong sa mga nasalanta ng bagyo.","translation":"He helped the storm victims **without hesitation**."},{"sentence":"Sumagot siya nang **walang-gatol** sa tanong ng guro.","translation":"She answered the teacher's question **unhesitatingly**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtimbang o pagsukat ng isang bagay gamit ang yunit na kilo.
etymology: Mula sa 'kilo' + '-in'. Ang 'kilo' ay mula sa Espanyol 'kilo'.
original_explanation: This is what the tindera at the palengke does when you buy bigas, manok, or gulay. "Ate, kiluin mo nga 'tong isang kilong baboy." It's the official verb of market transactions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **kiluin** mo muna ang mga mangga bago ilagay sa bayong.","translation":"Please, **weigh** the mangoes in kilos first before putting them in the basket."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **kiluin** ang mga donasyon para malaman kung gaano kabigat ang lahat.","translation":"We need to **weigh** the donations in kilos to know the total weight."}]

translation: is assumed; is presumed; is considered
meaning_filipino: Itinuturing o kinikilala bilang; ang pag-aakala o pagpapalagay sa isang bagay o sitwasyon batay sa limitadong impormasyon.
original_explanation: This is the official word for 'assuming ka!'. It's what you think is happening, even without solid proof. **Ipinalalagay** mong may gusto siya sa'yo kasi nag-react siya sa MyDay mo. Spoiler: Baka napindot lang.
usage_notes: A more formal version of 'ipinapalagay'. Both are commonly used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ipinalalagay** ng marami na siya ang mananalo sa darating na halalan.","translation":"It **is assumed** by many that he will win the upcoming election."},{"sentence":"**Ipinalalagay** na ligtas ang lugar na ito mula sa anumang kapahamakan.","translation":"This place **is considered** safe from any harm."}]

translation: for a very long time; lengthily
meaning_filipino: Sa napakahabang panahon o paraan; pagpapahaba nang lubos.
etymology: Reduplication of `haba` (length) with the `-in-` infix, suggesting a process or state of being made long.
original_explanation: This describes that meeting that could have been an email, or that 'short' story your tita tells that spans three generations. 'Gaano katagal kayo nag-usap?' '**Hinaba-haba** rin, inabot kami ng madaling araw!'
usage_notes: Emphasizes the excessive or notable length of time or duration. Often used in the proverb 'Hinaba-haba man ng prusisyon, sa simbahan din ang tuloy.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hinaba-haba** ng paliwanag niya, pero hindi ko pa rin naintindihan.","translation":"His explanation was **very lengthy**, but I still didn't understand."},{"sentence":"**Hinaba-haba** man ng prusisyon, sa simbahan din ang tuloy.","translation":"No matter how **long** the procession is, it still ends up at the church."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagpapahid ng isang bagay, tulad ng gamot o kulay, sa isang rabaw na nag-iiwan ng marka o mantsa. Maaari ring tumukoy sa mismong ipinahid na bagay.
original_explanation: When you apply something messily. Like a kid putting lipstick all over their face, not just their lips—that's 'nagdampol.' Or when you apply a thick layer of ointment on a wound. It's the act of smearing or dabbing something on, often thickly and without much precision. Think of it as the opposite of 'blending'.
usage_notes: The verb form is 'magdampol' or 'dampulan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglagay siya ng **dampol** ng yerba sa kanyang bukol.","translation":"She put a **poultice** of herbs on her lump."},{"sentence":"Puro **dampol** ng putik ang kanyang damit pagkatapos maglaro sa ulan.","translation":"His clothes were covered in **smudges** of mud after playing in the rain."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **dampulan** ng kolorete ang buong mukha mo!","translation":"Don't **smear** lipstick all over your face!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang pambuhat na karaniwang yari sa kahoy o metal, na may dalawang mahabang hawakan at ginagamit ng dalawang tao upang magbuhat ng mabibigat na bagay o isang tao.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na "parihuela" (stretcher, barrow).
original_explanation: This is the OG 'delivery service' equipment, 'yung parang stretcher na kailangan ng dalawang tao para buhatin. Madalas makita sa palengke para sa sako ng bigas o sa construction site. Sa lumang pelikula, dito sinasakay 'yung bida na nasugatan. Think of it as a human-powered forklift.
usage_notes: Maaari ring tumukoy sa isang stretcher para sa maysakit o nasugatan, o sa isang kabaong na pasan-pasan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binuhat nila ang sako-sakong bigas gamit ang isang **parihuwela**.","translation":"They carried the sacks of rice using a **barrow**."},{"sentence":"Isinakay sa **parihuwela** ang sugatang sundalo upang madala sa pagamutan.","translation":"The wounded soldier was placed on a **stretcher** to be brought to the hospital."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng marahas na pagpasok o pagsalakay sa isang lugar, teritoryo, o kuta ng may masamang hangarin.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `pan-` (nagiging `panl-`) + pag-uulit ng unang pantig (`lu`) + salitang-ugat na `lusob` (salakay).
original_explanation: Think of it as your titas storming the buffet table during a family reunion. Or when there's a piso sale online and everyone crashes the app at the same time. It's a full-on, no-holds-barred attack.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa mga konteksto ng aksyong militar, mga makasaysayang kaganapan, o sa matalinhagang paraan para sa anumang agresibong kilos.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang biglaang **panlulusob** ng mga kaaway ay ikinagulat ng mga sundalo.","translation":"The sudden **invasion** by the enemies surprised the soldiers."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aralan sa kasaysayan ang **panlulusob** ng mga dayuhan sa ating bansa.","translation":"The **assault** of foreigners on our country was studied in history."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyon ng paghanga sa isang bagay, tao, o lugar na may kaaya-ayang itsura o istilo. Katumbas ng 'Ang ganda niyan' sa modernong balbal.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na 'aesthetic' at Filipino gay lingo na 'yarn' (isang baryasyon ng 'iyan').
original_explanation: A very Gen Z/gay lingo way of saying 'That's so pretty!' or 'Love the vibe!'. It's the verbal equivalent of a chef's kiss. You see your friend's new minimalist condo? 'Wow, aesthetic yarn!' Your officemate's latte art is on point? 'Aesthetic yarn!'
usage_notes: Popular na ekspresyon sa online conversations at sa gay lingo community.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tingnan mo 'yung pagkaka-ayos ng mga libro, **aesthetic yarn**!","translation":"Look at how the books are arranged, **so aesthetic**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang pandamdam na hiram sa Ingles na ginagamit upang ipahayag ang biglaang sakit, pagkadismaya, o pakikiramay sa kamalasan ng iba.
etymology: From English 'oof,' popularized by the death sound effect in the video game Roblox.
original_explanation: The sound you make when you see your friend's post about their ex getting engaged. It’s the universal internet reaction to something awkward, painful, or just plain cringey. It's a one-word comment that says, 'That's rough, buddy.' Originally from the Roblox death sound, it's now the soundtrack to digital secondhand embarrassment.
usage_notes: Extremely common in online chats and comment sections to express sympathy, cringe, or secondhand pain.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumagsak ako sa exam. **Oof**.","translation":"I failed the exam. **Oof**."},{"sentence":"Nakita niya 'yung jowa niya na may kasamang iba. Malaking **oof** 'yun.","translation":"She saw her partner with someone else. That's a big **oof**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos o kalagayan ng unti-unting pagiging kapansin-pansin o pagiging hayag ng isang bagay na dati ay tago.
original_explanation: Eto yung feeling na 'OMG, they know!' Yung sikreto mong pagkain ng madaling araw, nahahalata na kasi tumataba ka. Yung pagka-crush mo sa officemate mo, nahahalata na kasi ngingiti ka mag-isa. It's when your poker face fails and the truth starts peeking out.
usage_notes: Ang unlaping 'na-' at ang pag-uulit ng unang pantig ng salitang-ugat ('ha') ay nagpapahiwatig ng isang nagaganap at hindi kusang-loob na proseso.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nahahalata** na ang pagod sa kanyang mga mata.","translation":"The exhaustion in his eyes is **becoming obvious**."},{"sentence":"Uy, **nahahalata** ko na may gusto ka sa kanya, aminin mo na!","translation":"Hey, I'm **starting to notice** that you like her, just admit it!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng sandata na nagpapaputok ng bala o projectile sa pamamagitan ng pagsunog ng pulbura.
original_explanation: A more formal way to say 'baril' or gun. This is what the news reports say when they talk about firearms. It covers everything from a small pistol to a big rifle. It's literally a 'weapon that explodes.'
usage_notes: Teknikal na termino para sa mga baril.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mo ng lisensya para magmay-ari ng **sandatang pumuputok**.","translation":"You need a license to own a **firearm**."},{"sentence":"Isinuko niya sa pulisya ang kanyang hindi lisensyadong **sandatang pumuputok**.","translation":"He surrendered his unlicensed **firearm** to the police."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang parirala na tumutukoy sa isang babaeng may pambihirang ganda at pang-akit na nagsisilbing inspirasyon; isang diwatang may balani o magnetismo.
etymology: Tagalog. 'Balniin' ay isang makatang anyo ng pandiwa na may kaugnayan sa 'balani' (magnetism, charm). Ang 'paraluman' ay nangangahulugang muse o diwata.
original_explanation: The ultimate #WCW (Woman Crush Wednesday) of the pre-colonial and Spanish eras. She's not just beautiful; she's got that magnetic charm, that *balani*, that makes poets write sonnets and warriors fight battles. She's the inspiration, the muse, the one who launches a thousand carabaos.
usage_notes: A highly poetic and archaic phrase. 'Paraluman' by itself is more common (but still literary) than the full phrase.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang makata ay lumikha ng isang tula para sa kanyang **balniing paraluman**.","translation":"The poet created a poem for his **enchanting muse**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghimok o paghikayat sa isang tao na gawin ang isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pakiusap o pangangatuwiran.
original_explanation: This is the art of convincing someone, the 'pilit' game. It's your friend trying to get you to go out on a Friday night when you just want to binge Netflix. It's the vendor at Greenhills using every trick in the book to make you buy that 'authentic' bag. It's the low-key, often repeated effort to get someone to say yes.
usage_notes: Less common in everyday conversation than its verb form 'amukiin' or synonyms like 'himok' or 'hikayat'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa **amuki** ng kanyang mga kaibigan, sumali siya sa paligsahan.","translation":"Because of the **persuasion** of his friends, he joined the contest."}]

meaning_filipino: Suriin o beripikahin ang isang bagay; lagyan ng marka o tsek.
etymology: Mula sa salitang "tsek" (mula sa Ingles na "check") at hulaping "-an".
original_explanation: The act of verifying if your sweldo has come in, if your online order has shipped, or if your partner's 'I'm with my friends' story is legit. It's the verb form of 'tsek'.
usage_notes: A very common verb in modern, informal Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyong **tsekan** mo kung tama ang mga sagot ko.","translation":"Please **check** if my answers are correct."},{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **tsekan** ang presyon ng gulong bago umalis.","translation":"Don't forget **to check** the tire pressure before leaving."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpilit o paghikayat sa isang tao na gawin ang isang bagay laban sa kaniyang kalooban.
etymology: From "pilit" (force, insist). The "pan-" prefix becomes "pam-" and the first syllable of the root is reduplicated ("-pi-") to form a noun of action.
original_explanation: This is what your tita does when she says "Kain pa!" for the fifth time even if you're already about to explode. It's also the energy of a friend who won't take 'no' for an answer when they want you to go out on a Friday night. Low-key 'kulit' but on a more serious level.
usage_notes: Can range from gentle insistence to forceful coercion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa **pamimilit** ng kaniyang mga kaibigan, napasali siya sa kantahan.","translation":"Due to the **insistence** of his friends, he was roped into the singing session."},{"sentence":"Walang mabuting maidudulot ang **pamimilit** sa isang relasyon.","translation":"**Coercion** brings nothing good in a relationship."}]

translation: to get tired of each other
meaning_filipino: Ang sabay o parehong pagkakaroon ng pagkasawa o pagkaumay ng dalawa o higit pang tao sa isa't isa o sa isang sitwasyon.
original_explanation: This is the mutual 'I'm over it' stage in a relationship or friendship. It's when the constant bickering isn't cute anymore, and both parties are just... done. The magic is gone, the spark has fizzled, and you're both just going through the motions. It's the quiet, unspoken agreement to stop trying. The ultimate 'walang forever' verb.
usage_notes: Ang hulaping '-an' dito ay nagpapahiwatig ng parehong damdamin o kilos sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mukhang nagkaka-**sawaan** na ang magkasintahan.","translation":"It seems the couple is starting to **get tired of each other**."},{"sentence":"Para hindi kayo mag-**sawaan**, subukan ninyo ang mga bagong bagay.","translation":"So that you don't **get fed up with each other**, try new things."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging abot-tanaw o napapansin ng mata; ang kasalukuyang pagkilos ng pagtingin sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: What you hope your crush is doing when you walk past them. Also, "na-seen-zone." Can mean you are actively seeing something ("Nakikita ko ang bus!") or that something is visible ("Nakikita na ang aplaya!"). It’s the visual equivalent of 'available'.
usage_notes: Can be both active (I am seeing) and passive (is being seen/is visible). The context and actor/focus of the sentence determines the precise meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakikita** mo ba ang **nakikita** ko?","translation":"Are you **seeing** what I'm **seeing**?"},{"sentence":"Mula rito, **nakikita** ang buong siyudad.","translation":"From here, the whole city **is visible**."}]

translation: to be able to rise up from; to recover
meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang bumangon mula sa isang mahirap na kalagayan, tulad ng kahirapan, pagkakalubog sa utang, o matinding kalungkutan.
etymology: maka- (ability prefix) + ahon (to go up, ascend from water/poverty)
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "bangon" verb. It's not just getting up from bed; it's getting up from rock bottom. It's what every Filipino family strives for: "makaahon sa hirap." It's recovering from a financial crisis, a bad breakup, or a series of unfortunate events. It's the theme song of every teleserye protagonist.
usage_notes: Has a strong metaphorical sense of overcoming hardship, not just physically moving upwards.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsisikap siya sa trabaho para **makaahon** sa kahirapan ang kanyang pamilya.","translation":"He works hard so his family can **rise up from** poverty."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng bagyo, unti-unti na silang **nakakaahon**.","translation":"After the storm, they are slowly **recovering**."}]

meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng aldaba o trangka ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay pinto o bintana.
original_explanation: It's the action you do when your mom yells "Isara mo 'yang pinto, baka mapasok tayo!" You're not just closing it, you're securing it with the 'aldaba'. It's the verb form of making sure no one unwanted gets in.
usage_notes: A verb derived from the noun 'aldaba'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Aldabahan** mo ang pinto bago ka matulog.","translation":"**Latch** the door before you go to sleep."},{"sentence":"Inutusan siyang **aldabahan** ang lahat ng bintana dahil sa paparating na bagyo.","translation":"He was instructed **to latch** all the windows because of the approaching typhoon."}]

translation: straddled; riding on the back of another
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pag-upo na magkabila ang mga binti sa isang bagay, tulad ng sa likod ng isang tao o hayop, o sa isang sanga.
original_explanation: Yung pose mo kapag naka-angkas ka sa motor o sa likod ng kaibigan mo para sa piggyback ride. Para kang naka-split pero sa ere at may sinasakyan. It's the OG "angkas" before the app existed.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin bilang pandiwa (sumaklong, nakasaklong). Ang anyong pangngalan (noun form) ay tumutukoy din sa kilos ng pag-upo nang ganito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakasaklong** ang bata sa balikat ng kanyang ama para makita ang parada.","translation":"The child was **straddling** his father's shoulders to see the parade."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **sumaklong** sa sanga na iyan, baka mabali.","translation":"Don't **straddle** that branch, it might break."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng tahi sa isang sugat; o ang pagsasagawa ng diseksiyon sa isang bagay. Ito ay anyong pautos o tumutukoy sa bagay na tatanggap ng kilos.
original_explanation: This is the verb form. It's the command or the action to be done. 'Dok, tistisin n'yo na po!' (Doc, stitch it up already!). Or the dreaded instruction from your science teacher: 'Okay class, tistisin ninyo ang mga palaka.' (Okay class, dissect the frogs.)
usage_notes: This is the object-focus imperative/infinitive form of the verb from the root word 'tistis'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **tistisin** agad ang sugat niya para hindi ma-impeksyon.","translation":"His wound needs **to be stitched** up immediately to avoid infection."},{"sentence":"Inutusan kaming **tistisin** ang isda para makita ang mga panloob na bahagi nito.","translation":"We were instructed **to dissect** the fish to see its internal parts."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang alternatibong baybay o pinaikling anyo ng salitang "semento"; isang pulbos na gawa sa luwad at apog na kapag hinaluan ng tubig ay tumitigas at ginagamit sa konstruksiyon.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'cemento'. Ito ay isang kolokyal na pagpapaikli o baryasyon sa pagbaybay.
original_explanation: Ito yung version ng "semento" na parang nagmamadali ka i-type sa text. "Pabili ng sement!" Mabilis, pero lahat naman nakakaintindi. Basically, the shortcut version of 'semento', like using 'u' instead of 'you'.
usage_notes: Ang "sement" ay mas madalas gamitin sa pasalitang paraan at itinuturing na impormal o kolokyal kumpara sa "semento".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kulang pa ng isang sakong **sement** ang timpla.","translation":"The mixture is still short one sack of **cement**."},{"sentence":"Magkano ba ang isang supot ng **sement** ngayon?","translation":"How much is a bag of **cement** nowadays?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matinding puna, pagtuligsa, o pagsisi sa isang tao dahil sa isang nagawang mali.
etymology: From Sanskrit "upaśalya" (उपशल्य) meaning a minor vexation or trouble.
original_explanation: The formal word for what your tita gives you at a family reunion when she asks, "Tumaba ka yata?" It's a high-level, literary shade. The kind of criticism that comes with a side of disappointment.
usage_notes: A formal and literary word. Not used in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatanggap siya ng **upasala** mula sa konseho dahil sa kanyang mga kontrobersyal na pahayag.","translation":"He received **censure** from the council because of his controversial statements."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang akronim para sa "got to go," na ginagamit upang ipahiwatig ang pangangailangang umalis o tapusin ang isang pag-uusap.
original_explanation: Acronym for "Got To Go." The classic escape line sa group chat 'pag nag-uumpisa nang mag-away 'yung mga tita mo about politics, or when your boss DMs you at 7 PM. The digital version of "May pupuntahan pa pala ako."
usage_notes: Used in informal digital communication like chats and text messages.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sige, **gtg** na ako, tinatawag na ako ni mama.","translation":"Okay, I've **got to go** now, my mom is calling me."},{"sentence":"Nice catching up! **GTG**, may meeting pa.","translation":"Nice catching up! **GTG**, still have a meeting."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng hindi pag-alala o pag-alis sa isipan ng isang bagay, tao, o pangyayari. Ito ay nasa anyong pangnagdaan.
etymology: From the root word `limot`, meaning 'forget'. The infix `-in-` and suffix `-an` indicate a completed action done to an object or in a location.
original_explanation: The national anthem of exes and amnesiacs. This is what you do to your diet on cheat day, to your deadlines when a new K-drama drops, and what your crush does to your existence. "Bes, kinalimutan mo na naman 'yung payong, basa tuloy ang resibo ng pagiging aanga-anga mo." It’s the past tense of "seen-zoned."
usage_notes: Can mean both "someone forgot something" (active) or "something was forgotten" (passive). The context determines the subject.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kinalimutan** niya ang kaarawan ko.","translation":"He/She **forgot** my birthday."},{"sentence":"Ang payo ng aking ina ay hinding-hindi ko **kinalimutan**.","translation":"My mother's advice is something I never **forgot**."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa direksyon o gawing kanluran; patungo sa kanluran.
original_explanation: Similar to 'pakakanan', this is the formal way to say 'papuntang west'. You'd hear this in a documentary about migrating birds or an old sea captain's log. 'The ship sailed pakanluran.' For everyday use, we just say 'sa west' or point and say 'doon, sa paglubog ng araw'.
usage_notes: Primarily used in literary, formal, or geographical contexts. 'Kanluran' is the common noun; 'pakanluran' is the directional adverb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglakbay sila nang **pakanluran** hanggang sa marating ang dagat.","translation":"They journeyed **westward** until they reached the sea."},{"sentence":"Ang bagyo ay kumikilos nang **pakanluran** sa bilis na 20 kph.","translation":"The typhoon is moving **westward** at a speed of 20 kph."}]

translation: to dig, to excavate, to unearth
meaning_filipino: Isang kilos ng pag-aalis ng lupa o iba pang materyales upang makagawa ng butas, o upang mahanap ang isang bagay na nakabaon.
original_explanation: The action verb for 'hukay'. This is what you do when you're looking for buried treasure, planting a 'kamote' seedling, or more realistically, when your 'Marites' friend is trying to 'dig up' some old gossip. 'Hukayin mo ang past niya!' (Dig up his/her past!).
usage_notes: A transitive verb that requires an object to be dug. Can be used literally for soil or figuratively for information.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **hukayin** ang lumang tubo ng tubig para palitan.","translation":"The old water pipe needs to **be dug up** to be replaced."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan nilang **hukayin** ang mga detalye ng nakaraang iskandalo.","translation":"They tried to **unearth** the details of the past scandal."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubhang napakaliit; mas maliit pa sa karaniwan.
original_explanation: Yung sahod mo after all the bills and utang? Malinggit. Yung pasensya mo sa traffic sa EDSA? Malinggit din. Basically, anything that's 'cute size' but in a sad, depressing way.
usage_notes: Hindi gaanong karaniwan kaysa "maliit." Binibigyang-diin nito ang sukdulang kaliitan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kitang-kita niya ang **malinggit** na langgam sa ibabaw ng mesa.","translation":"He clearly saw the **tiny** ant on the table."},{"sentence":"Isang **malinggit** na butas lang ang kailangan para masira ang buong istraktura.","translation":"Just one **minuscule** hole is needed to destroy the whole structure."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na idinadagdag upang pahabain o pagkabitin ang dalawa o higit pang bahagi.
original_explanation: That extra piece you add to make something longer. Like an extension cord for your charger, or the "Part 2" of a chismis. "Ano'ng dugtong ng kwento?" (What's the rest of the story?).
usage_notes: Can refer to a physical extension or a continuation of a story or idea.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakihanap ng **dugtong** para sa alambreng ito.","translation":"Please find an **extension** for this wire."},{"sentence":"Ang bawat kabanata ay **dugtong** sa nakaraang pangyayari.","translation":"Each chapter is a **continuation** of the previous event."}]

meaning_filipino: Payagan o hayaan ang isang bagay, lalo na ang isang gawing mali o hindi kanais-nais, na mangyari nang walang parusa o pagtutol.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'sige na nga, bahala ka' move. It's what parents do when their kid wants to stay up late, or what you do when your friend makes another questionable life choice. You don't approve, but you're too tired to argue. You're enabling, bes. Stop it.
usage_notes: Often has a negative connotation, implying tolerance of something wrong or improper.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **kunsintihin** ang pagiging tamad ng kapatid mo.","translation":"Don't **condone** your sibling's laziness."},{"sentence":"Kinunsinti ng ilang opisyal ang ilegal na gawain kaya ito lumaganap.","translation":"Some officials **tolerated** the illegal activity, which is why it spread."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang makatanggap ng salapi o anumang uri ng pakinabang bilang kabayaran sa pagtatrabaho, serbisyo, o mula sa isang negosyo.
original_explanation: The ultimate goal of every "raket" and "side hustle." Ito 'yung dahilan kung bakit ka nag-o-overtime kahit gusto mo nang umuwi. Para **kumita** ng pera pang-check out sa Shopee cart mo.
usage_notes: Primarily refers to earning money, but can also be used figuratively to mean 'to gain' or 'to earn' something abstract, like respect (kumita ng respeto).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang **kinita** niya sa pagbebenta ng mga damit online.","translation":"She **earned** a lot from selling clothes online."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong magtrabaho para **kumita** para sa aking pamilya.","translation":"I need to work **to earn** for my family."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng hindi pagsasama o pag-iiwan sa isang bagay; isang bagay na nakaligtaan o hindi isinama.
original_explanation: Ito yung "sinadyang kalimutan". Parang nung tinanong ka ng nanay mo kung sino kumain ng huling piraso ng leche flan, at sa kwento mo, may "omisyon" ng part na ikaw pala yun. It's the art of leaving things out, whether by accident or... not.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroong malaking **omisyon** sa kanyang testimonya.","translation":"There was a major **omission** in his testimony."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang yunit ng sukat para sa bigat sa sistemang metriko, katumbas ng ikasanlibong bahagi ng isang kilo.
original_explanation: Ito yung unit na ginagamit sa pagbe-bake ng cake. O kaya pag bumibili ka ng ginto, per **gram** ang presyuhan. Yung isa pang 'gram' ay yung Instagram, pero iba yun, 'wag kang malito.
usage_notes: Ito ang Ingles na katumbas ng 'gramo'. Mas karaniwang ginagamit ang 'gramo' sa pang-araw-araw na usapan sa palengke.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng isandaang **gram** ng asukal para sa recipe.","translation":"I need one hundred **grams** of sugar for the recipe."},{"sentence":"Ilang **gram** ang isang kutsarita ng asin?","translation":"How many **grams** are in a teaspoon of salt?"}]

translation: is doing something alone; going solo
meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng isang bagay nang nag-iisa, hiwalay sa kasama o grupo.
original_explanation: When you finally get tired of waiting for your 'laging late' friends and just go to the cafe or movie by yourself. It's that feeling of independence, whether it's eating at a restaurant alone or a singer leaving a band to pursue a solo career. 'Me time' in verb form.
usage_notes: Can be used for activities, career moves, or even just being emotionally distant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hayaan mo siyang **magsolo** muna, kailangan niya ng space.","translation":"Let her **be alone** for a while, she needs space."},{"sentence":"Madalas akong **nagsosolo** sa coffee shop para makapagtrabaho.","translation":"I often **go solo** to a coffee shop to be able to work."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o pagiging sanhi upang tumigil o ihinto ang isang gawain, kilos, o pag-andar.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung sinisigaw ng nanay mo sa kapatid mong maingay habang may kausap siya sa phone: 'Hoy, **papaghintuin** mo nga 'yang kapatid mo sa kakatalon!' It's ordering someone to enforce a stop.
usage_notes: Causative form of 'hinto'. It means to command or cause a stop through an intermediary.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Papaghintuin** mo na ang makina kapag umabot na sa tamang temperatura.","translation":"**Have** the machine **stopped** once it reaches the right temperature."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **papaghintuin** ang mga bata sa paglalaro sa kalsada.","translation":"He tried to **make** the children **stop** playing on the street."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi matitinag o maikikilos mula sa kinalalagyan; matatag at hindi nagbabago ang paninindigan.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `di-` (hindi) at `matinag` (kayang igalaw), na galing sa salitang ugat na `tinag` (bahagyang galaw).
original_explanation: This is your lolo sitting in his favorite chair, watching TV, completely ignoring everyone—**di-matinag**. It's also your conviction that pineapple belongs on pizza, no matter what your friends say. It’s being so firm in your position, physically or mentally, that nothing can move you. Unbothered. Moisturized. In my lane. Flourishing.
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang ilarawan ang pisikal na di-paggalaw o, mas karaniwan, ang metaporikal na katatagan sa paniniwala, prinsipyo, o damdamin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa kabila ng mga pagsubok, nanatili siyang **di-matinag** sa kanyang pananampalataya.","translation":"Despite the trials, she remained **unshakable** in her faith."},{"sentence":"Ang malaking bato sa gitna ng ilog ay **di-matinag** kahit malakas ang agos.","translation":"The large rock in the middle of the river is **immovable** even with the strong current."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang yunit ng oras na katumbas ng ikaanimnapung bahagi ng isang minuto.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung pinakamabilis na unit ng oras, pero 'pag naghihintay ka ng reply niya, parang bawat segundo ay isang taon. Sa New Year's countdown, ito 'yung isinisigaw mo. Sa mga runner, bawat segundo ay mahalaga. Sa buhay, paalala na 'wag sayangin ang bawat sandali.
usage_notes: May pagkakaiba sa "segunda" (second-hand). Ang "segundo" ay tumutukoy sa oras.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hintayin mo ako, isang **segundo** lang ito!","translation":"Wait for me, this will only take a **second**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang dumi, mantsa, o bahid sa isang malinis na rabaw o ibabaw, lalo na sa mukha o damit.
original_explanation: Eto 'yung mantsa ng chocolate sa pisngi ng bata, 'yung uling sa noo mo pagkatapos mag-ihaw, or 'yung pen mark sa puting uniform mo. It's that small spot of imperfection that someone will always point out: "Uy, may buling ka sa mukha!"
usage_notes: Often refers to a small, easily removable spot of dirt, as opposed to a permanent stain ('mantsa').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **buling** ng putik ang kanyang pantalon.","translation":"There's a **smudge** of mud on his pants."},{"sentence":"Pahiran mo 'yang **buling** sa iyong pisngi.","translation":"Wipe that **dirt mark** off your cheek."}]

translation: to clench; to press firmly together
meaning_filipino: Mariing isara o pagdikitin ang mga bahagi ng katawan tulad ng bagang (panga), kamao (fist) o mga labi, karaniwan dahil sa galit, sakit, o pagpipigil.
original_explanation: This is the physical manifestation of 'pigil na galit' or trying not to cry. It's the action you do when your boss gives you more work at 5 PM on a Friday. You **clench** your jaw, smile, and say 'Okay po,' but your jaw is telling the real story.
usage_notes: Often used with a body part, such as 'magtiim ng bagang' (to clench one's jaw), 'magtiim ng kamao' (to clench one's fist), or 'magtiim ng labi' (to press one's lips together).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko siyang **magtiim** ng bagang dahil sa sobrang galit.","translation":"I heard him **clench** his jaw due to extreme anger."},{"sentence":"Napilitan siyang **magtiim** ng labi upang hindi maiyak sa harap nila.","translation":"She was forced **to press her lips together** so she wouldn't cry in front of them."}]

translation: to take up a course; to be attracted to
meaning_filipino: Pag-aralan ang isang kurso o asignatura; magkaroon ng pagtingin o pagkagusto sa isang tao.
etymology: From Spanish 'curso' (course) + '-hin' suffix. The romantic meaning is a colloquial extension.
original_explanation: This word lives a double life. The first is academic, like choosing your major: 'Gusto kong **kursuhin** ang engineering.' (I want to take up engineering). The second is for matters of the heart, a colloquial term for being attracted to someone. It's when your brain says 'take this course' but your heart says 'siya ang **kursuhin** mo'.
usage_notes: The primary meaning relates to academics. The secondary, romantic meaning is informal and often expressed as 'kursunada' (the thing/person one is attracted to) or 'kinukursunada' (is attracted to).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Plano niyang **kursuhin** ang abogasya pagkatapos ng kolehiyo.","translation":"He plans **to take up** law after college."},{"sentence":"Pasensya na, pero hindi talaga kita **kursuhin**.","translation":"Sorry, but I'm really not **attracted to** you."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malawak at bukas na lugar, karaniwang may mga puno, halaman, at bangko, na laan para sa paglilibang at pamamahinga ng publiko.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "parque," na nagmula sa Pranses na "parc." Ang Ingles na "park" ay isa ring direkta at karaniwang hiram na salita.
original_explanation: The default dating spot for high school students with no budget. It's where you jog, walk your dog, have picnics, or just people-watch. Think Luneta Park or Quezon Memorial Circle. Ang lugar kung saan maraming nabubuong love team at maraming nauubos na fishball. The alternate spelling "park" is also very common.
usage_notes: Ang baybay sa Ingles na "park" ay malawakang ginagamit at ipinagpapalit sa "parke" sa mga kaswal na usapan at sulatin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglakad-lakad kami sa **parke** kahapon.","translation":"We strolled in the **park** yesterday."},{"sentence":"Maraming bata ang naglalaro sa bagong gawang **parke**.","translation":"Many children are playing in the newly built **park**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggalaw ng ulo at mata upang tumingin sa paligid, karaniwang dahil sa pagtataka, pagkalito, o paghahanap.
original_explanation: 'Yung reaction mo kapag biglang may tumawag sa pangalan mo sa gitna ng crowded na mall, tapos hindi mo alam kung saan galing. Para kang meerkat na nagmamasid, pero mas confused lang.
usage_notes: Often implies a sense of confusion, being lost, or searching for something uncertainly.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Luminga**-linga ang turista sa estasyon ng tren, hindi alam kung aling platform ang sasakyan.","translation":"The tourist **looked around bewilderedly** at the train station, not knowing which platform to take."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakasalikop o pagkakabuhol ng isang lubid, sinulid, o anumang nababaluktot na materyal na mahirap kalasin.
original_explanation: That frustrating tangle in your earphones, the plot of a Filipino teleserye, or the state of your love life. If it's complicated, twisted, and hard to undo, it's a **buhol**. 'Ang gulo, parang buhol-buhol na sinulid!' is a classic Pinoy frustration line.
usage_notes: Can be literal (a knot in a rope) or figurative (a complicated problem or relationship).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko matanggal ang **buhol** sa sintas ng sapatos ko.","translation":"I can't remove the **knot** in my shoelace."},{"sentence":"Nasa gitna sila ng isang **buhol** ng pamilya na mahirap ayusin.","translation":"They are in the middle of a family **tangle** that is difficult to fix."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na pinaikli o binago mula sa 'tara na', na ginagamit sa pag-aaya o pagyaya.
etymology: Slang, believed to be a playful inversion or modification of 'tara', which itself is a contraction of 'tara na' (let's go).
original_explanation: The cooler, quicker version of 'Tara!' It's what you text your friends when the plan is finally set. 'Inuman na? Arat!' 'Movie night? Arat!' It's the official go-signal for any 'lakad' or 'gala'. Short, sweet, and gets the point across.
usage_notes: Highly informal and popular among younger generations. Often seen in text messages and social media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Arat** na sa mall, baka maubusan tayo ng sale.","translation":"**Let's go** to the mall, the sale items might run out."},{"sentence":"Gutom na ako, **arat** nang kumain!","translation":"I'm hungry, **c'mon** let's eat!"}]

meaning_filipino: Tinitingala o kinikilala dahil sa angking galing, kabutihan, o katangian.
etymology: From `hanga` (admiration) with the `-in-` infix and `-an` suffix, indicating the object/person being admired.
original_explanation: This is what you feel for your workmate who can finish all their tasks and still leave at 5 PM on the dot. Or for that celebrity who is both talented and unproblematic. It's the state of being the subject of someone's 'sana all' feels.
usage_notes: The object of admiration is the subject of the sentence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hinahangaan** ko ang mga OFW sa kanilang sakripisyo para sa pamilya.","translation":"I **admire** the OFWs for their sacrifice for their families."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang kabaitan, siya ay **hinahangaan** ng lahat.","translation":"Because of her kindness, she **is admired** by everyone."}]

translation: knows, finds out, is aware of
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng kaalaman o impormasyon tungkol sa isang bagay; pagiging mulat sa isang katotohanan.
original_explanation: Ito yung moment na nag-scroll ka sa social media at biglang may chismis kang nakita. "So, totoo pala!" 'Yan ang state of *nalalaman*. It's the process of knowing, the tea being spilled and received in real-time.
usage_notes: Present tense of 'malaman'. Can be used for both discovering something new or possessing existing knowledge.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya **nalalaman** na may surpresa kaming inihanda para sa kanya.","translation":"He **is not aware** that we prepared a surprise for him."},{"sentence":"Sa pagbabasa, marami kang **nalalaman** tungkol sa mundo.","translation":"By reading, you **find out** many things about the world."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tambilang na katumbas ng isang libong milyon (1,000,000,000).
original_explanation: This is the OG "billion." Before we all just started saying "isang bilyon," this was the formal way to say it. It's a compound of 'san' (isa, one), 'libo' (thousand), and 'angaw' (million). So literally "one thousand million." You'd use this if you were writing a very formal document or maybe trying to sound super smart, like explaining the national debt.
usage_notes: This is a formal and somewhat archaic term. "Isang bilyon" is far more common in modern usage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang populasyon ng mundo ay higit sa pitong **sanlibong-angaw**.","translation":"The world's population is over seven **billion**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malubhang sakit na nakakahawa na dulot ng bakterya, na karaniwang nakaaapekto sa mga lamad ng ilong at lalamunan.
original_explanation: Isa sa mga sakit na kasama sa "pentavalent vaccine" na kinakatakutan ng mga nanay at tita. Before COVID, ito 'yung mga tipo ng sakit na dahilan kung bakit may malawakang pagbabakuna sa mga barangay health center.
usage_notes: Isang terminong medikal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bakuna ay mabisang panlaban sa sakit na **dipterya**.","translation":"The vaccine is an effective countermeasure against the disease **diphtheria**."},{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng outbreak ng **dipterya** sa isang liblib na lugar.","translation":"There was an outbreak of **diphtheria** in a remote area."}]

meaning_filipino: Matinding kalungkutan, pighati, o pagsisisi na nararamdaman sa kaibuturan ng damdamin.
original_explanation: This is the "wasak na wasak" level of sadness. It’s not just being sad; it’s being emotionally wrecked. It's the feeling you get after a major breakup, a huge failure, or watching the dog die in a movie. The kind of heartbreak that requires a bucket of ice cream and a playlist of hugot songs.
usage_notes: A very evocative and deep phrase for emotional distress.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dama sa kanyang mga mata ang **pagkabagbag ng loob** dahil sa pagkawala ng alaga niyang aso.","translation":"You could see in his eyes the **deep sorrow** from the loss of his pet dog."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkabagbag ng loob** ay isang mabigat na pasanin.","translation":"**Heartbreak** is a heavy burden to carry."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uusap o pagkakalat ng mga kuwento tungkol sa ibang tao, na kadalasan ay hindi pa kumpirmado o pribado.
original_explanation: The act of 'spilling the tea' or sharing the latest 'Maritest' update. It's the unofficial national sport. When you magtsismis, you are actively participating in the sacred art of talking about someone who isn't there. It's a one-way broadcast of juicy info. 'Hoy, 'wag kang magtsismis nang malakas, baka marinig tayo!'
usage_notes: This verb implies a one-to-many or a one-to-one action of telling gossip. Compare with 'magtsismisan,' which is reciprocal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **magtsismis** tungkol sa buhay ng mga kapitbahay niya.","translation":"She loves to **gossip** about the lives of her neighbors."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniniwala agad, baka may gusto lang **magtsismis** sa kanya.","translation":"Don't believe it right away, someone might just want to **spread gossip** about him."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng pagkilala, papuri, o gantimpala sa isang tao o grupo dahil sa kanilang natatanging nagawa o katangian.
etymology: From `magpa-` (causative prefix) + `dangal` (honor). `Parangal` is a nominalized form.
original_explanation: This is what happens during awards night, whether it's for the Oscars or just the 'Best in Attendance' award in your office. To magparangal is to put someone on a stage (literally or figuratively) and say, 'You did a great job!' It's the act of giving props, but in a formal, trophy-and-certificate kind of way.
usage_notes: Commonly associated with ceremonies, awards, and formal recognition. The root word is 'dangal' (honor).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paaralan ay **magpaparangal** sa mga natatanging mag-aaral.","translation":"The school will **honor** the outstanding students."},{"sentence":"Isang malaking karangalan ang **magparangal** sa ating mga bayani.","translation":"It is a great honor to **give tribute** to our heroes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking uri ng sitrus na may makapal na balat at matamis o maasim-asim na lasa.
original_explanation: 'Yung higanteng orange na kulay green o yellow ang balat, at pink o puti ang laman. Ito 'yung prutas na kailangan mo ng 'patience is a virtue' para balatan, pero worth it naman 'pag nakain mo na. Perfect pang-dessert o pang-regalo sa Tita mong galing Davao. Also known as 'suha'.
usage_notes: Ang 'suha' ay ang mas karaniwang termino para sa pomelo sa karamihan ng lugar sa Pilipinas. Ang 'suwatan' ay maaaring gamitin sa mga tiyak na rehiyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tamis ng **suwatan** na nabili namin mula sa Davao.","translation":"The **pomelo** we bought from Davao is so sweet."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng hindi pagkakaroon ng kakayahang magkaanak o mamunga.
original_explanation: Medically, it's the inability to conceive. In the world of chismis, it's a topic whispered about over the back fence. It can also be used figuratively for creative block—when your brain feels 'baog' and can't produce any new ideas for your thesis or your next TikTok video.
usage_notes: Can refer to humans, animals, or even plants (not bearing fruit). Can also be used figuratively for lack of productivity or creativity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malaking pagsubok para sa mag-asawa ang kanilang **pagkabaog**.","translation":"Their **infertility** was a huge challenge for the couple."},{"sentence":"Tila may **pagkabaog** ang kanyang isipan at wala siyang maisulat.","translation":"It seems his mind is **barren** and he cannot write anything."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi makaihi, karaniwan dahil sa matinding takot, kaba, o pagkabigla.
original_explanation: You're walking down a dark alley late at night and suddenly a cat jumps out of a trash can. Sa sobrang gulat, para kang di-mapaihi. It's that physical reaction to extreme fear or shock where your body just freezes up, including your bladder. It's being literally "scared pee-less."
usage_notes: Halos palaging ginagamit upang ilarawan ang isang estado ng matinding takot o kaba. Ito ay isang kolokyal na ekspresyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halos **di-mapaihi** ako sa takot habang nanonood kami ng horror movie.","translation":"I was so scared I was almost **unable to pee** while we were watching the horror movie."},{"sentence":"Nang tinawag siya sa entablado, para siyang **di-mapaihi** sa kaba.","translation":"When he was called on stage, it was like he was **unable to urinate** from nervousness."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang taong nagsasagawa ng interbiyu at nagtatanong sa kinakapanayam.
original_explanation: The person holding the script to your future. They ask the questions you rehearsed in the shower, but they can smell your desperation from across the table. A good interbiyuwer makes you feel comfortable; a great one already knows you stalked them on LinkedIn.
usage_notes: The counterpart of the 'interbiyuwi' (interviewee).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakagaling ng **interbiyuwer**; gumaan agad ang pakiramdam ko.","translation":"The **interviewer** was very good; I immediately felt at ease."},{"sentence":"Siya ang magiging **interbiyuwer** para sa final round ng hiring process.","translation":"She will be the **interviewer** for the final round of the hiring process."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kabuuan ng mga paniniwala, kaugalian, batas, sining, moralidad, at kaalaman ng isang partikular na lipunan o pangkat ng mga tao.
original_explanation: It's the 'why' behind the 'what' we do. Why we say 'po' and 'opo', why we have 5-hour family reunions with karaoke, why we point with our lips, and why adobo has a thousand 'correct' versions. It's the shared software running in the background of a society.
usage_notes: Isang pormal at karaniwang salita na ginagamit sa mga kontekstong akademiko, panlipunan, at pang-araw-araw.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bahagi ng **kultura** ng Pilipino ang pagiging magiliw sa mga bisita.","translation":"Being hospitable to visitors is part of Filipino **culture**."},{"sentence":"Dapat nating pagyamanin at ipagmalaki ang ating sariling **kultura**.","translation":"We should enrich and be proud of our own **culture**."}]

translation: to receive a reward; to be rewarded
meaning_filipino: Ang tumanggap ng pabuya, parangal, o anumang kapalit para sa isang mabuting gawa, serbisyo, o tagumpay.
original_explanation: This is what you hope for after a month of OT and weekend work—the 13th-month pay! It's the trophy at the end of the competition, the "good job" from your boss, or the extra rice you give yourself after a successful diet day. It's getting the prize you deserve (or think you deserve).
usage_notes: Used in contexts of receiving a prize, award, or compensation for an action or achievement.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sinumang makahanap sa nawawalang aso ay **magkakagantimpala** ng limang libong piso.","translation":"Whoever finds the missing dog **will be rewarded** with five thousand pesos."},{"sentence":"Sana'y **magkagantimpala** ang lahat ng iyong paghihirap.","translation":"I hope all your hardships **will receive a reward**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang panahon ng malawakang kakapusan sa pagkain sa isang rehiyon na nagdudulot ng matinding pagkagutom at sakit.
original_explanation: This is what happens when your entire region has been on a "petsa de peligro" diet for way too long. It's not just being hungry; it's a large-scale crisis, a nationwide "walang ulam" situation. In modern slang, you might say "taggutom na, besh" when your wallet is empty and all you have are instant noodles.
usage_notes: A serious term for a widespread food crisis. Can be used hyperbolically in casual speech to mean extreme poverty or lack of food.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming namatay noong panahon ng **taggutom** pagkatapos ng digmaan.","translation":"Many died during the time of **famine** after the war."},{"sentence":"Grabe, parang may **taggutom** dito sa bahay, naubos agad ang pagkain!","translation":"Wow, it's like there's a **famine** here at home, the food ran out immediately!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malawakang kapahamakan o kalamidad na nagdudulot ng matinding pinsala sa buhay at ari-arian.
etymology: A phrase composed of `malaki` (big) and `sakuna` (disaster, accident).
original_explanation: When a typhoon has a person's name and it's all over the news, that's a malaking sakuna. It's a 'major disaster.' It's not just a power outage; it's a 'no power, no water, no internet, and your roof is gone' kind of situation.
usage_notes: Refers to large-scale disasters, typically natural (like typhoons, earthquakes) or man-made (like major industrial accidents), affecting a wide area or a large number of people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-iwan ng **malaking sakuna** ang pagputok ng bulkan sa maraming bayan.","translation":"The volcanic eruption left a **major disaster** in many towns."}]

translation: to be bleached, to be discolored
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkawala o pagbabago ng orihinal na kulay ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay dahil sa pagkabilad sa araw o paggamit ng kemikal tulad ng pangkula (bleach).
original_explanation: This is what happens to your favorite black shirt after you accidentally spill bleach on it, or after leaving it out in the sun for a week. It's the reason we have the phrase "Wais sa pag-laba" because one wrong move and your clothes will get "makula". It's the bane of every laundry day.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to discoloration, often fading or lightening, due to sun or chemicals.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-ingat siya sa paglalaba para hindi **makula** ang kanyang bagong damit.","translation":"She was careful with the laundry so her new dress wouldn't **be bleached**."},{"sentence":"**Nakula** ang kulay ng kurtina dahil laging nabibilad sa araw.","translation":"The curtain's color **faded** because it's always exposed to the sun."}]

translation: to be accidentally thrown away; to be exiled
meaning_filipino: Hindi sinasadyang maisama sa mga bagay na itatapon; o maipatapon sa ibang lugar bilang parusa.
original_explanation: The tragic fate of your favorite pen, the other sock, or the TV remote. You didn't mean to, but somehow it ended up in the trash. It's the 'Hala, nasama sa basura!' panic. In a more dramatic, telenovela sense, it means to be exiled, like a disgraced heir sent to a faraway province.
usage_notes: This word has two main meanings: the common one is 'to be accidentally thrown away,' and a more formal, literary one is 'to be exiled or banished'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nanghinayang siya sa singsing na **napatapon** kasama ng basura.","translation":"She regretted the ring that **was accidentally thrown away** with the trash."},{"sentence":"Noong unang panahon, ang mga criminal ay **napatapon** sa malalayong isla.","translation":"In the old days, criminals **were exiled** to faraway islands."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpulupot ng mga braso sa isang tao o bagay bilang pagpapakita ng pagmamahal, pag-aliw, o pagbati.
original_explanation: The physical manifestation of 'Sana all.' It's the act of hugging, whether it's a tight hug from your mom after a long day, a quick friendly hug with a barkada, or that *special* hug with your jowa. It's the cure for everything, from a bad day at work to a 'seen-zoned' message.
usage_notes: The `pag-CV-` form suggests a more intense, prolonged, or repeated act of hugging compared to the simpler `pagyakap`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mahigpit na **pagyayakap** ng mag-ina ay nagpaiyak sa mga nakakita.","translation":"The tight **embracing** of the mother and child made the onlookers cry."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang opisyal na himno o awit ng isang bansa na sumisimbolo sa kasaysayan, kultura, at pagkakakilanlan nito.
original_explanation: The song that makes everyone in the cinema stand up, put their right hand over their heart, and try not to think about what they're having for lunch. It's the final boss before the movie trailers begin.
usage_notes: In the Philippines, the national anthem is 'Lupang Hinirang'. It is legally required to be sung with fervor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumayo nang tuwid habang inaawit ang **Pambansang Awit**.","translation":"Stand straight while the **National Anthem** is being sung."},{"sentence":"Ang 'Lupang Hinirang' ang ating **pambansang awit**.","translation":"'Lupang Hinirang' is our **national anthem**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na pag-aalay ng isang bagay para sa isang partikular na layunin; ang paghirang sa isang tao sa isang posisyon o tungkulin.
etymology: From "pag-" (verbal noun prefix) + "talaga" (originally meaning 'to appoint' or 'to destine').
original_explanation: Think of it as leveling up. It's when you're officially "the one". Like when your boss finally promotes you, or when you dedicate your new song to your crush. It's the official announcement that something or someone is now set for a special purpose, like dedicating a new building or appointing a new cabinet secretary. It's the "Ikaw na!" moment, but with paperwork.
usage_notes: Can refer to dedicating a work of art, appointing someone to a position, or consecrating a place.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagtatalaga** sa kanya bilang bagong CEO ay ipinagdiwang ng kumpanya.","translation":"His **appointment** as the new CEO was celebrated by the company."},{"sentence":"Ito ay isang **pagtatalaga** ng kanyang buhay sa paglilingkod sa mahihirap.","translation":"This is a **dedication** of his life to serving the poor."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na inalis o sinisante sa trabaho; maaari ring mangahulugang naipadala o natapos na ang isang gawain o bagay.
original_explanation: When your boss says "You're fired!", in old-school Tagalog, you've been `despatsado`. It means you've been sent packing. Can also be used for things, like when a customer's order is finally shipped. "Okay, `despatsado` na ang J&T parcel mo, antayin mo na lang." So it can mean "you're out" or "it's out." Context is key!
usage_notes: Has two main meanings: being fired from a job (more common and older usage) and having something dispatched or sent (more modern, logistics-related usage).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming empleyado ang **despatsado** nang magsara ang pabrika.","translation":"Many employees were **fired** when the factory closed."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, **despatsado** na ang order mo kaninang umaga.","translation":"Don't worry, your order was **dispatched** this morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bata na ipinanganak matapos pumanaw ang kanyang ama.
etymology: A descriptive phrase combining 'isinilang' (was born), 'pagkamatay' (upon the death of), and 'ama' (father).
original_explanation: This is a real-life teleserye plot twist from day one. You're born into a story that's already missing a main character, starting life with a major 'hugot' moment. The English term is 'posthumous child,' which sounds very academic, but the Tagalog phrase hits you right in the feels.
usage_notes: This phrase functions as a descriptor for a person. A single-word equivalent, 'postumo' (from Spanish), is sometimes used but is much rarer.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Heneral Antonio Luna ay **isinilang pagkamatay ng ama**.","translation":"General Antonio Luna was **born after his father's death**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang unang bahagi o yugto ng isang pangyayari, gawain, o panahon; ang pinagmulan o simula ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: 'Yung "In the beginning..." ng buhay mo. Pwedeng 'yung first day sa bagong trabaho, 'yung unang episode ng K-drama na pagpupuyatan mo, or 'yung unang "Hi" ng magiging ahas sa buhay mo. It's the starting line, the Day 1, the Genesis of your next big adventure or "sana all" moment.
usage_notes: Often used more formally than 'simula'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap ang **pasimula** ng anumang proyekto.","translation":"The **beginning** of any project is difficult."},{"sentence":"Sa **pasimula** pa lang, alam ko nang magkakaroon ng problema.","translation":"From the very **start**, I knew there would be a problem."}]

translation: to make things fit; to reconcile (figures/accounts)
meaning_filipino: Pagsisikap na pagtugmain o pag-angkupin ang mga bagay, lalo na ang mga numero, datos, o kuwenta, upang maging wasto o magbalanse.
original_explanation: The official verb for accountants during closing period, or for anyone trying to make their budget fit until the next sahod. It's that stressful process of adjusting numbers here and there para lang 'mag-balance' ang spreadsheet. 'Bakit may P200 na sobra? Ah, i-magtama-tama na lang natin sa miscellaneous.'
usage_notes: A reduplication of "tama" (correct/hit), implying a repeated action of trying to make things "correct".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **magtama-tama** ng mga resibo para sa aking expense report.","translation":"I need to **reconcile** the receipts for my expense report."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan nilang **magtama-tama** ng kuwenta para malaman kung saan napunta ang nawawalang pondo.","translation":"They are trying to **make the figures fit** to find out where the missing funds went."}]

meaning_filipino: Ito ay may dalawang kahulugan: (1) Ang paggamit ng susi upang isara at tiyaking ligtas ang isang kandado. (2) Ang masusing pag-aaral, pagsisiyasat, o pag-iimbestiga sa isang bagay o pangyayari.
original_explanation: This verb has two personalities. The literal one is what you forget to do to your door, leading to a mini-panic attack. The figurative one is what your Marites friend does—they "investigate" or "look closely" into the latest chismis. "Magsusi tayo sa profile niya."
usage_notes: The meaning shifts from "to lock" to "to investigate" depending on context. "Magsusi ng pinto" (lock the door) vs. "Magsusi sa mga ebidensya" (investigate the evidence).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **magsusi** ng pinto bago umalis.","translation":"Don't forget to **lock** the door before leaving."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magsusi** nang mabuti sa kasong ito.","translation":"We need to **investigate** this case thoroughly."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng may pormal na pinag-aralan, nagpapakita ng mabuting asal, at may malawak na kaalaman.
original_explanation: She's not just book-smart, she's "may pinag-aralan" smart. An 'edukada' woman carries herself with class, knows her stuff, and won't fall for fake news on Facebook. She's the tita who corrects your grammar but also gives the best life advice. Think of your lola insisting you finish your studies to become an 'edukada' lady.
usage_notes: The feminine form of "edukado". Often implies not just academic learning but also good manners and breeding.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang babaeng **edukada** ang napangasawa ng pinsan ko.","translation":"My cousin married an **educated** woman."},{"sentence":"Kahit hindi nakatapos ng kolehiyo, lumaki siyang parang **edukada** dahil sa turo ng kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"Even if she didn't finish college, she grew up like an **educated** person because of her parents' teachings."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang bagay na may kulay o kintab na parang pilak; maaari ring tumukoy sa pagiging mayaman o maraming pera.
original_explanation: Literally, 'silvery.' But in classic Pinoy fashion, we also use it to describe someone who's loaded with cash. 'Pilak' is slang for money, so if you're 'mapilak,' you're not just shiny, you're rich, honey! You've got that 'pera'.
usage_notes: Can be literal (silvery) or figurative (wealthy). The figurative meaning is more common in modern slang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **mapilak** na buhok ng lola ay tanda ng kanyang karunungan.","translation":"The grandmother's **silvery** hair is a sign of her wisdom."},{"sentence":"Naging **mapilak** siya mula nang manalo sa lotto.","translation":"He became **rich** (abundant in money) ever since he won the lottery."}]

translation: having dark circles under the eyes
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng maitim na bilog o bahagi sa ilalim ng mga mata, karaniwang sanhi ng pagkapagod, puyat, o sakit.
etymology: Possibly a combination of a word related to 'ngalo' (withered) and 'mata' (eye).
original_explanation: The official look of every BPO agent on their 4th straight OT, the student cramming for finals, or anyone who just finished a K-drama marathon until 5 AM. It's the 'puyat is life' battle scar. Your eyes are basically telling on you.
usage_notes: The noun form, 'pangangalumata', refers to the condition of having dark circles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halatang puyat ka dahil **ngalumata** ka na.","translation":"It's obvious you lack sleep because you're already **having dark circles under your eyes**."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang takpan ng concealer ang kanyang **ngalumata** na mga mata.","translation":"She tried to cover her **eyes with dark circles** with concealer."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpalo o paghampas nang malakas gamit ang isang bagay na mahaba at nababaluktot, tulad ng latigo, sinturon, o sanga.
original_explanation: This is what happens when your nanay finds out you spent your pamalengke money on ML diamonds. It's the action of whipping something or someone, usually with a tsinelas, belt, or walis tingting. The OG disciplinary action.
usage_notes: Often implies a swift, sharp strike.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binalaan ng ama ang anak na **hahalibasin** niya ito ng sinturon kung hindi titigil sa paglalaro.","translation":"The father warned his child that he would **whip** him with a belt if he didn't stop playing."},{"sentence":"Parang **hinalibasin** ng hangin ang mga sanga ng puno sa lakas ng bagyo.","translation":"It was as if the wind **lashed** the tree branches with the storm's strength."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang halaga ng pera o ari-arian na ibinibigay ng isang tao bilang kanyang bahagi sa isang negosyo, kooperatiba, o samahan.
original_explanation: It's your 'skin in the game.' The money you put in to start a small business with your barkada, or your contribution to the office paluwagan. It's your share of the capital, hoping it turns into a big-time 'kita' (profit) later on.
usage_notes: A specific business or financial term used in the context of cooperatives and partnerships.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bawat miyembro ng kooperatiba ay kailangang magbigay ng kanilang **hulog-sapi**.","translation":"Each member of the cooperative needs to give their **capital contribution**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, pangyayari, o tao na nagpapakita o nagpapatunay sa isang pangkalahatang tuntunin o katotohanan; isang modelo o huwaran.
original_explanation: The OG 'For example...' bago pa nauso ang 'For instance...' at 'Sample!'. Ito yung binibigay ng teacher mo para maintindihan mo yung lesson, o yung resibo na kailangan mo para patunayang totoo ang chismis. 'Halimbawa, si Marites...'
usage_notes: Can also be used as a conjunction, 'Halimbawa,' meaning 'For example,'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magbigay ka ng **halimbawa** ng pang-uri.","translation":"Give an **example** of an adjective."},{"sentence":"Siya ay isang mabuting **halimbawa** sa kanyang mga kapatid.","translation":"He is a good **example** to his siblings."}]

translation: to make something shine or sparkle
meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng ningning o kintab ang isang bagay; pakinangin.
etymology: From `pa-` (causative prefix) + `luningning` (a variant of ningning, sparkle) + `-an` (locative/object-focus suffix).
original_explanation: Think of it as applying the ultimate highlighter or running your photo through a "kira-kira" filter. It's the verb for when you want something to be so shiny it could blind your haters. "Bes, **paluningningan** mo 'yang sapatos mo para pang-aura."
usage_notes: A more poetic or intense way to say "pakintabin" (to make shiny).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinabihan niya ang katulong na **paluningningan** ang sahig na gawa sa marmol.","translation":"He told the helper to **make the marble floor shine**."},{"sentence":"Nais ng reyna na **paluningningan** ang kanyang korona bago ang seremonya.","translation":"The queen wants her crown **to be made to sparkle** before the ceremony."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagdudulot ng inis, pagkayamot, o pagkagalit sa isang tao sa paraang paulit-ulit o sinasadya.
etymology: From `pang-` + reduplication of the first syllable of the root `buwisit` (`bu-`) + `buwisit`. The root is from Hokkien 'bo ui sit' (無衣食), meaning 'no clothes or food', implying bad luck or annoyance.
original_explanation: That feeling when the internet connection drops during a crucial Zoom meeting, or when your sibling keeps poking you for no reason. It's the act of being a professional-level irritant. The 'nakakainis' energy in noun form.
usage_notes: Describes the action of being a nuisance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itigil mo na ang **pambubuwisit** mo sa kapatid mo.","translation":"Stop your **act of annoying** your sibling."},{"sentence":"Araw-araw na lang ang kanyang **pambubuwisit** sa opisina.","translation":"His **pestering** at the office is a daily occurrence."}]

translation: to pickle; to preserve in brine or vinegar
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagbabad ng pagkain tulad ng gulay, prutas, o isda sa solusyon ng suka, asin, at iba pang pampalasa upang mapreserba ito at magkaroon ng kakaibang lasa.
original_explanation: Yung PBB ng mga pagkain. Ilalagay mo sila sa isang banga (bahay ni Kuya) na puno ng suka, asin, at asukal, tapos iiwan mo for a long time. Paglabas, iba na ang personality... at lasa! Burong mangga, atchara, burong isda — mga produkto ng pag-buruhin.
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang paraan ng pag-iimbak ng pagkain sa Pilipinas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais kong **buruhin** ang mga sobrang mangga mula sa aming puno.","translation":"I want **to pickle** the excess mangoes from our tree."},{"sentence":"Madali lang **buruhin** ang papaya para gawing atchara.","translation":"It's easy **to pickle** papaya to make atchara."}]

translation: to make something into three; to triple
meaning_filipino: Ang utos o gawain na hatiin sa tatlong bahagi o gawing tatlo ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is what you tell your friend when you're sharing one order of large fries: 'Pagtatluhin natin 'to!' (Let's split this three ways!). It's the verb for tripling something or dividing it into three equal parts. It's the mathematical operation for when a couple becomes a love triangle.
usage_notes: This is a command or infinitive form. 'Pagtatluhin mo' (You make it three).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pagtatluhin** ninyo ang perang ito para sa inyong tatlo.","translation":"**Divide** this money **into three** for the three of you."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **pagtatluhin** ang effort natin para matapos ang project.","translation":"We need to **triple** our effort to finish the project."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang anyo ng sining pampanitikan na gumagamit ng mga salitang may angking ritmo, tugma, at estetika upang ipahayag ang damdamin, kaisipan, o karanasan.
original_explanation: The OG hugot post. Long before Facebook statuses and Twitter threads, the 'tula' was where Filipinos poured out all their feels. From Balagtas's epic love sagas to today's spoken word poetry about coffee shops and heartbreak, it's the art of making words beautiful, even when the topic is ugly.
usage_notes: A major form of Philippine literature.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumulat siya ng isang **tula** para sa kanyang minamahal.","translation":"He wrote a **poem** for his beloved."},{"sentence":"Ang paborito kong **tula** ay ang 'Isang Dipang Langit' ni Amado V. Hernandez.","translation":"My favorite **poem** is 'Isang Dipang Langit' by Amado V. Hernandez."}]

translation: a measly amount; a tiny bit
meaning_filipino: Isang napakaliit o halos walang halaga na dami o bahagi.
etymology: From ka- (reduplication) + karampot (a very small amount).
original_explanation: 'Yung sahod mo na parang kakarampot na tuldok sa listahan ng mga bayarin mo. It's that comically small amount that makes you laugh and cry at the same time. The "is this it?!" of quantities.
usage_notes: Stronger and more informal than "kakaunti". Often implies that the amount is disappointingly or ridiculously small.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng lahat ng buwis, **kakarampot** na lang ang natira sa bonus ko.","translation":"After all the taxes, only **a measly amount** was left of my bonus."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, **kakarampot** lang naman ang kinuha kong kanin.","translation":"Don't worry, I only took **a tiny bit** of rice."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking superyor o pinuno sa isang monasteryo o relihiyosong orden, na mas mababa sa ranggo kaysa sa isang abad.
original_explanation: Think of him as the branch manager of a monastery. He's a religious leader, a figure you'd probably only encounter in history books, old movies about the Spanish era, or maybe if you visit a really old monastery. Not your everyday palengke encounter.
usage_notes: A very specific term related to the Catholic church hierarchy. Usually seen in historical or religious contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **priyor** ang namumuno sa mga monghe sa kumbento.","translation":"The **prior** leads the monks in the convent."},{"sentence":"Nakausap ng mga bisita ang **priyor** ng monasteryo.","translation":"The visitors were able to speak with the monastery's **prior**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginagamitan ng tali o anumang pampatibay upang hindi makawala o maalis sa kinalalagyan.
etymology: From `tali` (string, rope, tie). `Naka-` indicates the resulting state of being tied.
original_explanation: Literal na aso mong **nakatali** sa gate. O yung sapatos mong kailangan i-double knot. Metaphorically, ito yung feeling mo 'pag committed ka na sa isang relationship. **Nakatali** ka na, bes! Bawal na lumandi. Pwede ring sa trabaho, **nakatali** sa kontratang 'di mo na gusto.
usage_notes: Used both literally for physical tying and metaphorically for being bound by commitment, contract, or relationship.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bangka ay **nakatali** nang mahigpit sa pantalan.","translation":"The boat is **tied** tightly to the dock."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam niya ay **nakatali** siya sa isang trabahong hindi niya gusto.","translation":"He feels **bound** to a job he doesn't like."}]

meaning_filipino: Maging isang hadlang o balakid sa pag-usad o pagpapatuloy ng isang bagay, gawain, o proseso.
original_explanation: That one officemate who asks a question 5 minutes before the meeting ends. The un-skippable 30-second ad before a YouTube video. The chismis that ruins your focus. Anything that gets in your way and slows you down, 'yan ang sumasagabal sa'yo.
usage_notes: Implies causing a delay or making progress more difficult, rather than stopping it completely.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **sumagabal** sa daan, marami ang nagmamadali.","translation":"Don't **obstruct** the way, many people are in a hurry."},{"sentence":"Ang masamang koneksyon ng internet ay **sumagabal** sa aming online meeting.","translation":"The bad internet connection **hindered** our online meeting."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking at organisadong pangkat ng mga tao, karaniwan ay mga sundalo, na may layuning militar o para sa isang partikular na gawain.
etymology: Possible connection to Proto-Austronesian roots related to 'group' or 'gather'.
original_explanation: Your squad, but make it military. An army. It can be the literal AFP (Armed Forces of the Philippines), or it can be a 'hukbo ng mga tsismosa' (an army of gossipers) mobilizing in the neighborhood. Any large, organized group on a mission.
usage_notes: Can refer to a military army or, more broadly, any large group of people with a common purpose.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinadala ang isang **hukbo** ng mga sundalo sa lugar na apektado ng kalamidad.","translation":"An **army** of soldiers was sent to the calamity-stricken area."},{"sentence":"Isang **hukbo** ng mga boluntaryo ang tumulong sa paglilinis ng baybayin.","translation":"A **multitude** of volunteers helped clean the coastline."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging magkatulad o magkamukha sa anyo, uri, o halaga.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "parejo". Ang unlaping "pagka-" ay nagpapahiwatig ng kalidad o estado ng pagiging magkatulad.
original_explanation: 'Yung moment na pareho kayo ng suot ng officemate mo nang hindi sinasadya. Awkward! That **pagkapareho** can be a conversation starter or a reason to go home and change. Also, the reason you can't tell the difference between two milk tea shops – they're basically the same.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin para sa pisikal na pagkakahawig, pagkakatulad sa mga katangian, o pagkakapantay-pantay sa katayuan o halaga.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kitang-kita ang **pagkapareho** ng magkapatid na kambal.","translation":"The **similarity** between the twin siblings is very evident."},{"sentence":"Sa kabila ng kanilang **pagkapareho** sa pananaw, mayroon pa rin silang maliliit na di-pagkakasundo.","translation":"Despite their **sameness** in perspective, they still have minor disagreements."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapadala ng isang bagay, lalo na ng mensahe o datos, sa paraang elektroniko.
original_explanation: The modern-day 'sugo.' Before, it was about sending a letter via post office. Now, it's about hitting that arrow icon on Messenger, IG, or your email. 'Pa-send naman ng file.' is the battle cry of every student and office worker. Also used for G-Cash: 'Pa-send na lang, besh.'
usage_notes: Used primarily in informal, digital communication (Taglish). The formal Tagalog equivalent is 'ipadala' or 'magpadala'.
