usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**send** na lang sa email ko ang mga litrato.","translation":"Please just **send** the photos to my email."},{"sentence":"Na-**send** mo na ba 'yung G-Cash?","translation":"Have you **sent** the G-Cash?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamataas na ehekutibong opisyal na namamahala sa isang korporasyon o kumpanya.
etymology: Isang tambalang salita na binubuo ng "presidente" (mula sa Espanyol) at "kumpanya" (mula sa Espanyol na "compañía").
original_explanation: The big boss sa office. Sila 'yung may sariling parking spot, 'yung laging nasa board meeting, at 'yung nag-aapruba ng budget para sa Christmas party. Kung sa BPO, sila 'yung 'client' na laging kailangan i-please.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang kolokyal na pagbubuo. Ang mas pormal at karaniwang paraan ay "presidente ng kumpanya".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bagong **presidentengkumpanya** ay dating nagsimula bilang isang intern.","translation":"The new **company president** once started as an intern."}]

translation: manner of answering; the act of answering back
meaning_filipino: Ang paraan o akto ng pagtugon sa isang tanong o sitwasyon. Maaari rin itong tumukoy sa walang-galang na pagsagot sa nakatatanda.
original_explanation: This has two flavors. 1) The neutral one: how you answered the exam. 'Paano pagkasagot mo sa math test?' 2) The spicy one: talking back to your parents or boss. This is the 'sumasagot ka na ah!' moment. It's not about *what* you said, but the audacity of saying it. Your tone and timing turned a simple answer into an act of rebellion.
usage_notes: The meaning is highly contextual, often implying disrespect when used in a disciplinary context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinagalitan siya dahil sa kanyang **pagkasagot** sa nanay niya.","translation":"He was scolded for his **manner of answering back** to his mother."},{"sentence":"Ang bilis ng **pagkasagot** niya sa tanong ay ikinahanga ng lahat.","translation":"The quickness of his **answering** the question amazed everyone."}]

translation: to strike; to whip; to lash
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpalo o pagtama nang malakas sa isang bagay o tao, karaniwang gamit ang isang instrumento tulad ng pamalo, sinturon, o ang kamay.
original_explanation: The sound of a flying tsinelas (slipper) has a verb, and this is it. It's a forceful strike, often done out of anger or for discipline. Also used to describe waves crashing against the shore ('hampas ng alon'). 'Tigilan mo 'yan o ako'y **manghampas** na ng sinturon!' (Stop that or I'll start striking with a belt!)
usage_notes: Implies a strong, often repeated, hitting motion. The object being used for hitting is often specified, e.g., 'manghampas ng tsinelas'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagbanta ang matanda na **manghampas** ng baston sa mga batang maiingay.","translation":"The old man threatened **to strike** the noisy children with his cane."},{"sentence":"Parang may gustong **manghampas** sa pinto sa sobrang lakas ng hangin.","translation":"It's as if something wants **to lash** at the door because of the strong wind."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hudyat, kilos, o tunog na nagbibigay ng impormasyon, babala, o utos.
original_explanation: The reason you can't watch Netflix, make a call, or send a message. 'Walang sinyal!' is the modern cry of desperation. It can also be the subtle hint your crush gives you (or doesn't give you), leaving you to overthink for the next 3-5 business days.
usage_notes: Commonly refers to telecommunication signals (cellphone, Wi-Fi) but can be used for any type of signal. The word 'hudyat' is a more native equivalent. 'Sinyas' or 'senyas' are common variants.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahina ang **sinyal** ng Wi-Fi dito sa probinsya.","translation":"The Wi-Fi **signal** is weak here in the province."},{"sentence":"Nagbigay siya ng **sinyal** na oras na para umalis.","translation":"He gave a **signal** that it was time to leave."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pampublikong opisyal na may awtoridad na magsagawa ng mga partikular na legal na pormalidad, tulad ng pagpapatunay sa mga lagda sa mga dokumento, pagtanggap ng mga sinumpaang salaysay, at pagprotesta sa mga kasulatang maipagbibili.
etymology: Mula sa pariralang Espanyol na 'notario público'.
original_explanation: This is the person you go to para maging 'official' ang isang document. Yung pirma niya with the fancy seal, 'yan ang nagbibigay-buhay sa mga affidavit of loss mo para sa SIM card, deed of sale ng lupa ni lola, at iba pang papeles. Sila ang Tito/Tita mong legal eagle na nagsasabing 'This document is legit, pramis!'
usage_notes: Ginagamit bilang isang buong parirala. Ang pagpapaikli sa 'notaryo' ay karaniwan sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong ipanotaryo ang kontrata sa isang **notaryo publiko**.","translation":"You need to have the contract notarized by a **notary public**."},{"sentence":"Naghahanap ako ng opisina ng **notaryo publiko** para sa aking sinumpaang salaysay.","translation":"I am looking for a **notary public's** office for my affidavit."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng matinding kakulangan, lalo na sa mga pangunahing pangangailangan tulad ng pagkain at pera; karalitaan o kahirapan.
original_explanation: This is a deep, literary word for being broke. Not just 'petsa de peligro' broke, but truly, deeply in need. It's the kind of word you'd find in a Florante at Laura novel to describe extreme poverty. It's the 'wala nang makain, wala nang pag-asa' level of hardship.
usage_notes: A formal and literary term. In everyday conversation, 'kahirapan' or 'kakulangan' are more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming pamilya ang nagtitiis sa **kadahupan** sa mga liblib na lugar.","translation":"Many families endure **destitution** in remote areas."},{"sentence":"Ang **kadahupan** sa buhay ay hindi hadlang sa pag-abot ng pangarap.","translation":"Life's **poverty** is not a hindrance to reaching one's dreams."}]

translation: to sue, to file a complaint
meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na pag-akyat ng isang usapin sa hukuman sa pamamagitan ng pagsasampa ng kaso laban sa isang tao o entidad.
etymology: From Spanish 'hablar' (to speak), which evolved to mean legal pleading or filing a suit in this context.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'I'll see you in court!' move. When a chismis escalates, a contract is breached, or someone owes you a huge amount of money and won't pay up, this is the nuclear option. It's what happens when 'mag-usap tayo' fails and you bring in the lawyers. Think Raffy Tulfo in action, but the legal, official version.
usage_notes: The object-focused form is 'ihabla'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **maghabla** laban sa kumpanyang hindi nagbigay ng kanyang sahod.","translation":"He decided to **file a complaint** against the company that didn't give him his salary."},{"sentence":"Binalaan niya ang kapitbahay na **maghahabla** siya kung hindi titigil sa pag-iingay.","translation":"He warned his neighbor that he would **sue** if the noise didn't stop."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pakiramdam ng pagkabagot, pagkawalang-gana, o kawalan ng pasensya dahil sa matagal na paghihintay o kawalan ng magawa.
original_explanation: The feeling you get when the wifi is down, your phone is dead, and your friend is two hours late. It’s that soul-crushing boredom and impatience rolled into one. "Grabe ang inip ko sa pila, besh. Pang-isang season ng K-drama na ang hinintay ko."
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun (`ang inip`) or as a root for adjectives (`naiinip`) and verbs (`mainip`).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya maitago ang kanyang **inip** habang naghihintay.","translation":"He couldn't hide his **impatience** while waiting."},{"sentence":"Ang **inip** ay kalaban ng mga taong nag-aabang sa wala.","translation":"**Boredom** is the enemy of people waiting for nothing."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halamang-gulay na may mahahabang tangkay at mabangong dahon, karaniwang ginagamit bilang pampalasa sa mga lutuin tulad ng sopas at pansit.
original_explanation: That green leafy thing your mom forces into your sopas or arroz caldo to make it 'healthy.' It's the cousin of cilantro that didn't get invited to the Mexican food party but is the star of every pansit canton.
usage_notes: Madalas na tumutukoy sa 'Chinese celery', na may mas maninipis na tangkay at mas matapang na amoy at lasa kaysa sa Kanluraning kauri nito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang lagyan ng **kintsay** ang niluluto mong pansit para bumango.","translation":"Don't forget to add **celery** to the noodles you're cooking to make it fragrant."},{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng isang tali ng **kintsay** sa palengke.","translation":"Mom bought a bunch of **celery** at the market."}]

meaning_filipino: May sapat o matinding liwanag; madaling makita, maunawaan, o maintindihan.
original_explanation: Two kinds: 1) Yung ilaw ng Meralco pagkatapos ng brownout. 2) Yung explanation ng prof mo na finally gets mo na. It's the opposite of "malabo." Kapag "maliwanag pa sa sikat ng araw," it means it's super obvious, like your friend's feelings for their crush that everyone sees but them.
usage_notes: Can be literal (light) or figurative (understanding). When used figuratively, it's a synonym for 'malinaw' (clear).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayokong matulog nang **maliwanag** ang ilaw.","translation":"I don't like to sleep with the light **bright**."},{"sentence":"**Maliwanag** na hindi siya interesadong sumama.","translation":"It's **clear** that he is not interested in joining."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tao o pangkat na nagmamay-ari ng isang bagay, ari-arian, o negosyo.
original_explanation: The big boss. The one who signs the checks. The person you complain about when rent is due or the person you praise when there's free pizza. Whether it's the may-ari of the apartment you're renting, the company you work for, or the sari-sari store where you have a 'lista,' this is the person who holds the title.
usage_notes: A very common and fundamental word in contexts of business, property, and ownership.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **may-ari** ng asong ito?","translation":"Who is the **owner** of this dog?"},{"sentence":"Kausapin mo ang **may-ari** ng gusali para sa iyong mga hinaing.","translation":"Talk to the building **owner** about your complaints."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit at malakas na pag-apak o pagtapak sa isang bagay, lalo na sa putik o basang lupa, upang ito ay mapatag o masiksik.
original_explanation: This is the sound and action of feet stomping in mud. Imagine kids playing in the rain, making a mess of a muddy patch, or a farmer pressing down soil with their feet in the rice paddies. It's a messy, noisy, and kind of satisfying action. It's the onomatopoeia of 'squish-squash-stomp.'
usage_notes: The root 'yakyak' means to trample or stomp. 'Yakyakan' can be the place where stomping happens, or the act itself. The verb form is 'yakyakin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging isang malaking **yakyakan** ang laro ng mga bata sa putikan.","translation":"The children's game in the mud turned into a huge **act of stomping repeatedly**."},{"sentence":"Ang **yakyakan** sa palayan ay bahagi ng paghahanda sa pagtatanim.","translation":"The **act of stomping** in the rice field is part of the preparation for planting."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng materyal o bagay na hindi kayang tupukin o sirain ng apoy.
etymology: Mula sa `hindi` (not) + `masusunog` (will be burned), nasa anyong panghinaharap ng `masunog`.
original_explanation: This is the Daenerys Targaryen of materials, "Unburnt." 'Yung gamit na pwede mong iwan sa gitna ng bonfire at pagbalik mo, eh, andun pa rin, chill lang. Can also be your hard drive na puno ng "thesis" folder—sana **hindi masusunog** or macorrupt!
usage_notes: Ginagamit para sa mga materyales na lumalaban sa apoy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga mahahalagang dokumento ay nakatago sa isang kahang **hindi masusunog**.","translation":"The important documents are kept in a **fireproof** box."},{"sentence":"Dapat gawa sa materyales na **hindi masusunog** ang mga kurtina sa sinehan.","translation":"The curtains in a cinema should be made of **non-combustible** materials."}]

meaning_filipino: Lutuin ang isang sangkap, karaniwang karne, sa paraang asado na may sarsang gawa sa kamatis, patatas, at iba pang pampalasa.
etymology: From Spanish 'asado' (roasted), which evolved in the Philippines to refer to a specific type of stew.
original_explanation: When your mom tells you "asaduhin mo na 'yung manok," it means you're about to make that classic, saucy, tomato-based dish that's a staple in every handaan. It's the less sweet cousin of caldereta and the more tomato-y sibling of mechado. Don't mess it up or the whole pamilya will know.
usage_notes: 'Asado' in a Filipino context refers to a specific braised stew, not just any roasted meat as in the original Spanish. The verb form 'asaduhin' specifically means to cook this dish.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Balak kong **asaduhin** ang natirang baboy mula sa Pasko.","translation":"I plan **to cook the leftover pork from Christmas asado-style**."},{"sentence":"Masarap **asaduhin** ang manok na may kasamang atay.","translation":"It's delicious **to cook chicken asado-style** with liver."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagdaragdag ng luya sa isang bagay, karaniwan sa pagkain o inumin.
original_explanation: The verb form of tita-ing up your food. When the soup tastes like sad water, you need to `luyahan` it. It's the command your mom shouts from the living room while you're attempting to cook adobo for the first time. "Hoy, `luyahan` mo 'yan!"
usage_notes: A command or action word. The suffix '-an' indicates applying the root word to something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Luyahan** mo pa ang sabaw para mawala ang lansa ng isda.","translation":"**Add more ginger** to the soup to remove the fishy smell."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong masyadong **luyahan** ang paksiw, baka umanghang masyado.","translation":"Don't **add too much ginger** to the paksiw, it might get too spicy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging masungit o madaling magalit.
original_explanation: This is your boss on a Monday morning before coffee. It's your partner when they're 'hangry.' It's the *tindera* who looks at you like you're an inconvenience. *Sungit* is that aura of unapproachability and general grumpiness. If someone asks, 'May dalaw ka ba?' you're probably being *masungit*.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun ('ang sungit mo' - your grumpiness) or as an adjective ('masungit ka' - you are grumpy). The root word itself is often used as an exclamation or description.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na ang **sungit** mo, umaga pa lang.","translation":"Stop your **grumpiness**, it's still early in the morning."},{"sentence":"Bakit ang **sungit** ng mukha mo ngayon?","translation":"Why do you have such a **cranky** face today?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang damdamin ng pagiging mapagpasalamat; pagtanaw ng utang na loob.
original_explanation: 'Yan 'yung feeling mo 'pag may nag-abot sa'yo ng payong nung biglang umulan. O 'yung post mo sa Facebook na "Thank you, Lord!" after mong pumasa sa exam. It's 'pasasalamat' but make it more formal and deep. It's the "utang na loob" you feel.
usage_notes: Isang mas pormal na paraan ng pagsasabi ng "pasasalamat" o "utang na loob".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinakita niya ang kanyang **gratitud** sa pamamagitan ng isang liham.","translation":"She showed her **gratitude** through a letter."},{"sentence":"Puno ng **gratitud** ang aking puso para sa lahat ng tumulong.","translation":"My heart is full of **gratitude** for everyone who helped."}]

meaning_filipino: Matisod o madapa nang paulit-ulit; kumilos sa paraang nagmamadali, natataranta, at halos mawalan ng balanse.
etymology: magkanda- (prefix for repeated, clumsy action) + dapa (fall flat on one's face)
original_explanation: You, when you're 15 minutes late for your morning shift and can't find your keys, wallet, and dignity. It's moving with the grace of a baby giraffe on roller skates. Madalas nangyayari 'pag may biglaang chismis.
usage_notes: Often implies haste and panic, leading to clumsiness. The prefix 'magkanda-' is intensive and denotes a repetitive, clumsy, or sprawling action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagkandarapa** siya sa pagtakbo para maabutan ang huling biyahe ng bus.","translation":"He **scrambled** to run to catch the last bus trip."},{"sentence":"Sa sobrang taranta, **nagkandarapa** na siya sa pag-akyat ng hagdan.","translation":"In so much panic, she was **stumbling all over** while going up the stairs."}]

meaning_filipino: Gumamit ng wikang Tagalog sa pagsasalita o pagsusulat.
original_explanation: What your relatives from the US try to do during family reunions. It's also the default mode when you're trying to haggle in Divisoria or when you're explaining something passionately to a friend. "Wait, mag-Tagalog na lang ako, hirap i-explain in English eh!"
usage_notes: A very common verb used to refer to the action of speaking the Tagalog language.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit lumaki siya sa Amerika, marunong siyang **magtagalog**.","translation":"Even though he grew up in America, he knows how to **speak Tagalog**."},{"sentence":"Pwedeng **magtagalog** na lang tayo para mas madali?","translation":"Can we just **speak in Tagalog** so it's easier?"}]

translation: to become weak, to droop, to languish
meaning_filipino: Manghina ang katawan at espiritu; mawalan ng lakas o sigla, na tila lanta o bagsak ang anyo.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung itsura mo after a hell week sa office. 'Yung parang halaman na hindi nadiligan for a week. You're not just tired, you're physically and emotionally drained, drooping like overcooked spaghetti. Your battery isn't just low, it's at -1%.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan ng estado ng matinding panghihina o pagkapagod, kapwa pisikal at emosyonal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nanlupaypay** ang mga manlalaro pagkatapos ng limang set na laban.","translation":"The players **became weak** after a five-set match."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa matinding init, madaling **manlupaypay** ang mga halaman sa hardin.","translation":"Because of the intense heat, the plants in the garden easily **droop**."}]

translation: to cause a bad smell; to make something stink
meaning_filipino: Ang maging sanhi ng masamang amoy sa isang lugar o bagay.
original_explanation: The verb form of that one officemate who reheats their leftover tinapa in the pantry microwave. 'Bes, 'wag 'yan, makakabaho sa buong office!' It's the action of introducing a foul odor into an environment.
usage_notes: More commonly heard in its conjugated form 'nakakabaho' (causes a bad smell).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itapon mo na ang basurang iyan dahil baka **makabaho** pa sa buong kusina.","translation":"Throw that trash out because it might **make** the whole kitchen **stink**."},{"sentence":"Ang natapong kemikal ay nakakabaho sa buong laboratoryo.","translation":"The spilled chemical is **causing a bad smell** in the entire laboratory."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marubdob, masidhi, at malalim na damdamin o pananabik para sa isang bagay, tao, o layunin.
etymology: From ka- + dubdob + -an. 'Dubdob' means blaze or intense glow.
original_explanation: This is the 'gigil' level of passion. It's not just 'gusto', it's 'GUSTONG-GUSTO'. It's the fire in your belly when you're fighting for a cause, the intense emotion when you're writing a love letter, or the 'all-in' feeling of a die-hard fan. This is love or dedication on beast mode.
usage_notes: A deep, literary word. Not used in casual conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinakita niya ang **karubduban** ng kanyang pag-ibig sa pamamagitan ng isang tula.","translation":"He showed the **fervor** of his love through a poem."},{"sentence":"Ang **karubduban** ng kanilang pananampalataya ay hindi natinag ng pagsubok.","translation":"The **intensity** of their faith was not shaken by trials."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging walang bayad, gastos, o obligasyon.
original_explanation: The best state of being for any Pinoy. It's the 'free taste' in the supermarket, the 'libre sakay' van, the free wifi at the coffee shop. When you hear something is pagkalibre, you run, no questions asked.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively refers to being free of cost, not freedom in the political sense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa **pagkalibre** ng seminar, marami ang dumalo.","translation":"Because the seminar was **free**, many attended."},{"sentence":"Sinamantala niya ang **pagkalibre** ng konsultasyon sa doktor.","translation":"She took advantage of the **freeness** of the doctor's consultation."}]

translation: to boast about something; to show something off
meaning_filipino: Ipagmalaki o ipagyabang ang isang bagay, katangian, o nagawa sa paraang labis o nakakainis.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung flex culture bago pa na-imbento ang "flex". 'Yung tita mong 'di titigil ikwento 'yung achievements ng anak niya, or 'yung friend mong laging pino-post 'yung bago niyang gadget. "Sige, ipaghambog mo pa 'yang bago mong iPhone, 'di naman kami naiinggit. Charot."
usage_notes: Carries a negative connotation of excessive pride or arrogance. The object of the verb is the thing being boasted about.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hilig niyang **ipaghambog** ang kanyang mga mamahaling alahas.","translation":"She likes to **boast about** her expensive jewelry."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ipaghambog** ang mga bagay na hindi mo pinaghirapan.","translation":"Don't **show off** things you didn't work hard for."}]

meaning_filipino: Kainin nang may lubos na gana at bilis; o paluin o hampasin nang buong lakas.
original_explanation: The official verb of Pinoy fiestas and buffets. It's not just 'to eat' (kain), it's to attack the lechon, crabs, and everything on the table with gusto. 'Tara, lantakan na natin 'to!' is the battle cry before a feast. It can also mean to hit something hard, but let's be real, we use it for food 99% of the time.
usage_notes: This is an object-focus verb. The command form is 'Lantakan mo!' (Devour it! / Hit it!). It has two main meanings: eating voraciously and hitting forcefully.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mahiya, **lantakan** mo na ang mga handa.","translation":"Don't be shy, **devour** the food that's prepared."},{"sentence":"Nais niyang **lantakan** ng martilyo ang sirang pinto.","translation":"He wants to **strike** the broken door with a hammer."}]

translation: to give joy to; to please
meaning_filipino: Magdulot ng kaligayahan o kasiyahan sa isang tao.
etymology: From "bigyan" (to give) and "tuwa" (joy). Literally, "to give joy to."
original_explanation: This is your life's mission when your crush is around. Or when you bring home pasalubong for the family. It's the act of making someone happy, like when the GrabFood driver arrives earlier than expected.
usage_notes: A positive and heartwarming expression.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **bigyang-tuwa** ang kanyang ina sa pamamagitan ng isang sorpresa.","translation":"He tried to **give joy to** his mother with a surprise."},{"sentence":"Ang pagkapanalo ng pambansang koponan ay nagbigay-tuwa sa buong bansa.","translation":"The national team's victory brought joy to the whole country."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginagamit upang ipahayag ang pagiging malubha, matindi, o di-pangkaraniwan ng isang sitwasyon, katangian, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: The Swiss Army knife of Filipino expressions. It can mean "Wow!", "Oh my god!", "That's terrible!", "That's amazing!", or "You won't believe this!". The meaning completely depends on your tone. "Grabe, ang ganda mo!" (Wow, you're so beautiful!) vs "Grabe, ang traffic!" (Ugh, the traffic is terrible!). It's the one-word summary for any situation that's extra.
usage_notes: Can be used as an adjective (grabe ang sitwasyon), an adverb (grabeng ganda), or an interjection (Grabe!).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Grabe** ang init ng panahon ngayon!","translation":"The weather is **intensely** hot today!"},{"sentence":"**Grabe**! Nanalo ka sa lotto?","translation":"**Wow**! You won the lottery?"},{"sentence":"Napanood mo ba 'yung balita? **Grabe** 'yung nangyari.","translation":"Did you watch the news? What happened was **terrible**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng panulat na gumagamit ng maliit na bola sa dulo upang ikalat ang tinta.
original_explanation: Ang national treasure ng mga estudyante at office worker. Laging nawawala, laging hinihiram pero hindi na binabalik. May itim, blue, at red para sa mga masisipag mag-notes. Pag nawala 'to, parang nawalan ka ng isang kaibigan. #JusticeForMyBolpen
usage_notes: Ang pinakakaraniwang termino para sa isang ballpoint pen sa Pilipinas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pahiram naman ng **bolpen**, naiwan ko ang sa akin.","translation":"Can I borrow a **ballpen**, I left mine."},{"sentence":"Pula ang tintang ginamit niyang **bolpen** sa pagwawasto ng mga papel.","translation":"She used a red ink **ballpen** to correct the papers."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pagkain, partikular sa tinapay, na hindi na sariwa, matigas na, at mayroon nang di-kaaya-ayang lasa o amoy dahil sa katagalan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na "panes," ang pangmaramihang anyo ng "pan" (tinapay). Ang kahulugan ay nagbago upang tumukoy sa lumang tinapay.
original_explanation: That sad moment when you're craving pandesal for breakfast, but the one you bought yesterday now has the texture of a rock. It's food that's past its prime, basically saying 'wala na, finish na'. In slang, it's also used to mean 'owned' or 'beaten badly' in a game. "Panes ka sa akin!"
usage_notes: Bagaman ang teknikal na kahulugan ay para sa tinapay, malawakan itong ginagamit para sa anumang pagkaing sira na. Popular din ito bilang isang salitang balbal na nangangahulugang 'talo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang kainin 'yan, **panes** na ang tinapay.","translation":"Don't eat that anymore, the bread is **stale**."},{"sentence":"Amoy **panes** na 'yung ulam sa ref.","translation":"The viand in the ref smells **spoiled**."},{"sentence":"Sa wakas, natalo kita sa Mobile Legends! **Panes**!","translation":"Finally, I beat you in Mobile Legends! **Owned**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o taniman kung saan partikular na pinapatubo ang mga gulay.
original_explanation: This is your mom's pride and joy, or your 'Bahay Kubo' project in elementary school. It's where the magic happens, turning tiny seeds into the sitaw and kalabasa that you'll eventually be forced to eat. The original farm-to-table concept.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to a place for growing vegetables.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming tanim na talong at kamatis sa aming **gulayan** sa likod-bahay.","translation":"There are many eggplants and tomatoes planted in our **vegetable garden** at the backyard."},{"sentence":"Ang proyektong **gulayan** sa paaralan ay nakatulong sa mga mag-aaral.","translation":"The school's **vegetable patch** project helped the students."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghihintay o pag-aabang para sa pagdating ng isang tao, bagay, o pangyayari.
etymology: From 'hintay' with the '-in' suffix. A colloquial contraction of 'hintayin'.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'seen-zoned.' You're waiting for a reply that may or may not come. It's what you do for your sahod, for the 13th-month pay, and for the bus that seems to be taking the scenic route from another dimension. It's the promise of 'Wait for me,' but make it a command.
usage_notes: This is a very common colloquial form of 'hintayin'. Both are widely used and understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Antayin** mo ako sa labas ng sinehan.","translation":"**Wait for** me outside the cinema."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **antayin** ang resulta ng pagsusulit.","translation":"We need to **wait for** the exam results."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng grasa o langis sa isang bagay, karaniwan sa mga bahagi ng makina, upang mabawasan ang pagkiskis at mapadali ang paggalaw.
original_explanation: What your tito does to the squeaky gate, the bicycle chain, or the car engine on a Saturday morning. It's the ultimate 'tito move' to fix anything that makes a noise. Also, a metaphor for 'smoothing things over,' but mostly, it's about the actual sticky stuff.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nang **maggrasa** ng kadena ng bisikleta dahil tumutunog na ito.","translation":"The bicycle chain needs **to be greased** because it's already making a noise."},{"sentence":"Si Mang Berto ay abala sa **paggrasa** ng mga piyesa ng jeep.","translation":"Mang Berto is busy **lubricating** the jeepney parts."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng pagiging madaling matakot o kulang sa tapang.
original_explanation: This is your friend who jumps at every horror movie scene, screams when a cat passes by, and refuses to walk down a dark alley. They're the designated screamer of the group. If 'matakot' is a temporary state, 'matakutin' is a lifestyle.
usage_notes: Describes a personality trait, a disposition to be fearful, as opposed to 'matakot' which is the state of being afraid at a moment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masyado siyang **matakutin** kaya ayaw niyang manood ng mga horror movie.","translation":"She is too **easily frightened**, which is why she doesn't want to watch horror movies."},{"sentence":"Hindi pwedeng maging sundalo ang isang taong **matakutin**.","translation":"A **timid** person cannot be a soldier."}]

translation: strolling; sightseeing; going out for leisure
meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng paglalakad-lakad o pagpunta sa isang lugar para sa libangan, pagliliwaliw, o pagtingin-tingin sa paligid.
original_explanation: This is the official term for "gala". 'Yung tipong "Tara, mall tayo!" o "Lakad-lakad lang sa park." It's your weekend escape from adulting, kahit pa window shopping lang at hanggang tingin ka lang sa mga presyo. The national pastime.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paboritong gawin ng pamilya namin tuwing Linggo ay ang **pamamasyal** sa parke.","translation":"Our family's favorite Sunday activity is **strolling** in the park."},{"sentence":"Nag-ipon siya ng pera para sa kanyang planong **pamamasyal** sa Europa.","translation":"She saved money for her planned **sightseeing** trip in Europe."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang nakasulat na katibayan ng pagbabayad o pagtanggap ng isang produkto o serbisyo.
original_explanation: The official, paper kind. Yung hinahanap ng accountant mo para sa reimbursement. Yung laging nawawala kapag kailangan mo for warranty. "Ma'am/Sir, need po ng original receipt." The phrase that haunts every shopper.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa orihinal na anyong Ingles, ngunit binibigkas bilang /ri-SIT/. Madalas na ginagamit nang palitan sa salitang 'resibo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong iwawala ang **receipt** para sa warranty.","translation":"Don't lose the **receipt** for the warranty."},{"sentence":"Puwede po bang makahingi ng official **receipt**?","translation":"May I ask for an official **receipt**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng molusko na may dalawang kabibe, karaniwang matatagpuan sa tubig-alat, at kinakain bilang pagkain.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'pampagana' or aphrodisiac, especially when doused with vinegar and enjoyed with an ice-cold beer. It's that fancy seafood you order when you're feeling a bit bourgeois in a dampa-style restaurant. Best eaten fresh, unless you want to spend the next day regretting your life choices.
usage_notes: Often sold by the 'sako' (sack) in coastal areas. A popular 'pulutan' (bar chow).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap ang sariwang **talaba** na may suka at sili.","translation":"Fresh **oysters** are delicious with vinegar and chili."},{"sentence":"Nag-order kami ng tatlong dosenang **talaba** sa Dampa.","translation":"We ordered three dozen **oysters** at the Dampa (seafood market restaurant)."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hindi pagtupad o pagkukulang sa isang tungkulin o gawain; pagpapabaya.
etymology: Root word 'ligta' means to miss or omit.
original_explanation: This is that 'oops, I forgot' moment but with more serious consequences. It's failing to pay your Meralco bill on time, forgetting a major deadline at work, or not watering your tita's precious plants when she's away. It's an error of omission.
usage_notes: A formal term, often found in literature or formal speech. 'Pagpapabaya' is a more common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagkaligta** sa tungkulin ay nagdulot ng malaking problema.","translation":"His **neglect** of duty caused a huge problem."},{"sentence":"Walang puwang ang **pagkaligta** sa anumang detalye ng plano.","translation":"There is no room for **omission** in any detail of the plan."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang nababanat na materyal na nagmula sa katas ng ilang tropikal na halaman o gawa sa sintetikong paraan. Tumutukoy din ito sa gulong ng sasakyan.
original_explanation: That thing your car can't live without, and the reason you get stuck on the road ('na-flatan ng goma!'). Also, the main ingredient of your favorite tsinelas and the rubber bands you use to tie your 'baon'.
usage_notes: Can refer to the material (rubber) or more commonly, the object (tire). Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang palitan ang **goma** ng kotse dahil pudpod na.","translation":"The car's **tire** needs to be replaced because it's worn out."},{"sentence":"Ang tsinelas ay gawa sa **goma**.","translation":"The slippers are made of **rubber**."}]

translation: Act of reporting or telling on someone; denunciation
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-uulat o paglalantad sa isang tao sa awtoridad dahil sa isang nagawang pagkakamali o krimen.
original_explanation: This is the formal term for being a 'sumbungero'. It’s when you snitch on your co-worker for taking too many free pens from the supply room, or report a crime to the police. It's the act of being a whistleblower, a tattle-tale, or a concerned citizen, depending on your motive.
usage_notes: Carries a more formal and serious tone than 'sumbong'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang matapang na **pagsusuplong** ng saksi ang naging susi sa paglutas ng kaso.","translation":"The witness's brave **act of reporting** was the key to solving the case."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng hayop-dagat na may malambot na katawan, sampung galamay, at may kakayahang magbuga ng maitim na tinta bilang depensa. Ito ay karaniwang kinakain bilang pagkain.
original_explanation: The star of your favorite Calamares. This sea creature is famous for two things: being delicious when fried and shooting ink like a messy printer when it gets scared. It's the emo kid of the ocean.
usage_notes: Often distinguished from 'pugita' (octopus), which has eight arms, and 'kulambutan' (cuttlefish).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap ang adobong **pusit** lalo na kung sariwa.","translation":"Adobo-style **squid** is delicious, especially when fresh."},{"sentence":"Nagbuga ng tinta ang **pusit** kaya naging itim ang sabaw.","translation":"The **squid** released its ink, so the soup turned black."}]

translation: to block for someone, to support someone
meaning_filipino: Suportahan, tulungan, o ipagtanggol ang isang tao, lalo na sa pamamagitan ng pagharang sa panganib para sa kanila.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'sangga' at hulaping '-han'.
original_explanation: The verb form of being a 'sangga'. It's what you do when your friend is about to get scolded by their mom and you make up an excuse for them. 'Sige, ako na bahala, sasanggahan kita kay tita.'
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng mga laro (hal. basketball) o pagbibigay ng suporta sa isang alitan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sanggahan** mo ako para makatira ako sa basket.","translation":"**Block** for me so I can shoot at the basket."},{"sentence":"Kahit anong mangyari, **sasanggahan** ka ng iyong mga tunay na kaibigan.","translation":"Whatever happens, your true friends will **support** you."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kaalaman o kasanayang natamo mula sa pagmamasid, pakikilahok, o pagdanas ng mga pangyayari.
original_explanation: 'Yung bagay na wala ka raw nu'ng nag-apply ka para sa first job mo. O 'yung dahilan kung bakit ka 'single but not ready to mingle'—dami mo nang 'character-building' eksperyensiya.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with the native term 'karanasan', but 'eksperyensiya' is very common in contexts of work and qualifications.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **eksperyensiya** ang pinakamahusay na guro.","translation":"**Experience** is the best teacher."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng hindi bababa sa dalawang taong **eksperyensiya** sa trabaho.","translation":"At least two years of work **experience** is required."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aalaga, pag-aaruga, at pagbibigay proteksyon na may pagmamahal at malasakit.
original_explanation: This is more than just 'care.' It's that warm, fuzzy, protective feeling you get from your nanay when you're sick. It's how an OFW parent provides for their family from afar. It's the 'alaga' of a nurse, the guidance of a mentor, the whole vibe of a community looking out for each other. It's care with a capital 'C' and a whole lot of heart.
usage_notes: Madalas gamiting kasama ng 'pagmamahal'. Ang 'Kalinga' ay pangalan din ng isang lalawigan at pangkat-etniko sa Pilipinas, ngunit naiiba ito sa kahulugan bilang pangngalang pambalana.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mararamdaman mo ang **kalinga** ng isang ina sa kanyang mga yakap.","translation":"You can feel a mother's **care** in her hugs."},{"sentence":"Ang gobyerno ay dapat magbigay ng **kalinga** sa mga mahihirap.","translation":"The government should provide **protection** for the poor."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpalo o paghampas gamit ang puluhan o dulo ng isang riple o baril.
etymology: From Spanish 'culata', meaning 'butt of a gun'.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you run out of bullets in a Call of Duty game and have to get up close and personal. It's the act of using your firearm not for shooting, but as a very hard, very unfriendly club. Think of it as the ultimate "talk to the hand," but the hand is holding a rifle butt.
usage_notes: Often used in military, police, or action contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinamaan siya ng **kulata** ng sundalo sa likod.","translation":"He was hit by the soldier's **butt stroke** on the back."},{"sentence":"Isang malakas na **kulata** sa ulo ang nagpabagsak sa kalaban.","translation":"A strong **hit with the rifle butt** to the head brought the enemy down."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong namamahala o nagtatrabaho sa isang kantina. Ang anyong pambabae ay kantinera.
original_explanation: The unsung hero of the school/office. The kantinero knows your usual order, has seen you at your most 'gutom' and 'puyat', and holds the sacred power of giving you an extra scoop of rice. Be nice to them, they control your happiness for the day.
usage_notes: The female equivalent is 'kantinera'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala ng **kantinero** ang lahat ng estudyante sa kanilang pangalan.","translation":"The **canteen keeper** knows all the students by name."},{"sentence":"Tinulungan kami ng **kantinero** na mahanap ang nawawala naming wallet.","translation":"The **canteen worker** helped us find our missing wallet."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging nakahihigit, nakalalamang, o mas mataas ang antas o estado kaysa sa iba.
original_explanation: This is when you're "better" or "ahead" of someone else. Not just physically higher, but in terms of status, points, or progress. "Lodi, angat ka talaga!" (Idol, you're really on another level!). When your crush finally notices you over your rival, you are "angat." In gaming, if your team has more kills, "angat kayo." It's the state of being winning.
usage_notes: Madalas na ginagamit kasama ng "naka-" (nakaangat) upang ipahiwatig na "nakalalamang" o "nasa mas mataas na posisyon."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa lahat ng kandidato, siya ang **angat** sa karanasan.","translation":"Of all the candidates, she is **superior** in experience."},{"sentence":"Naka-**angat** na tayo sa kahirapan dahil sa pagsisikap.","translation":"We have now **risen** from poverty through hard work."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng manipis at malinaw na plastik na karaniwang ginagamit bilang pambalot, takip, o lalagyan, lalo na sa pagkain.
etymology: Possibly from the mineral "mica" which can be split into thin transparent sheets, or from a brand name that became generic.
original_explanation: This is the official take-out container for your birthday party spaghetti, pansit, at pichi-pichi. Ito rin yung ginagamit na cover sa mga ID noong unang panahon. Kung wala kang dalang tupperware sa handaan, ang mika ang iyong magiging savior.
usage_notes: In the Philippines, "mika" almost exclusively refers to the thin, clear plastic used for food packaging or as a transparent sheet, not the mineral.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakilagay na lang sa **mika** ang tirang pansit para maiuwi ko.","translation":"Please just put the leftover noodles in a **plastic container** so I can take it home."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking ibong mandaragit na may malakas na tuka, matatalas na kuko, at malinaw na paningin.
original_explanation: The national bird of the Philippines! The king of the sky. Madalas makita sa mga logo ng gobyerno, pera, at team name sa sports. Symbol of strength, power, and freedom. Parang 'yung boss mo na 'eagle-eyed' sa mga mali mo sa report.
usage_notes: Refers to the bird, but also used metaphorically for someone with sharp vision or a powerful presence. The Philippine Eagle is a critically endangered species.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **agila** ay pambansang ibon ng Pilipinas.","translation":"The **eagle** is the national bird of the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Napakataas ng lipad ng **agila** sa kalangitan.","translation":"The **eagle**'s flight is so high in the sky."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na pagpapahayag ng pagsang-ayon o pahintulot sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: The formal 'go signal'. It's the signature you need from your boss to go on leave, the 'yes' from your parents to go on a trip with friends, or the government permit you need to start a business. Getting that **aprobasyon** feels like winning the lottery, especially after a long wait. 'Wala pang **aprobasyon** sa budget, so tiis-tiis muna sa instant noodles.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinihintay pa namin ang **aprobasyon** ng pangulo para sa bagong proyekto.","translation":"We are still waiting for the president's **approval** for the new project."},{"sentence":"Nakuha na ba ninyo ang **aprobasyon** mula sa city hall?","translation":"Have you secured the **approval** from city hall?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kilos na ginawa nang mas maaga o bago pa man ang takdang oras; pauna.
original_explanation: 'Yung paghahanda mo bago pa ang "sakuna." Like, nag-baon ka na ng pagkain sa party kasi alam mong 'di masarap handa nila. Or nag-ready ka na ng sagot sa tanong na "Kailan ka mag-aasawa?" bago pa ang family reunion. It's being one step ahead. Pro-active, 'ika nga.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Antimano** siyang nag-empake ng gamit para hindi magahol sa oras.","translation":"He packed his things **beforehand** so he wouldn't be rushed."},{"sentence":"Salamat sa **antimano** mong paalala.","translation":"Thanks for your reminder **in advance**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang kilos ng pagpunta o paglalakbay patungo sa isang partikular na lugar, direksyon, o layunin.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'tungo' na nangangahulugang direksyon o patungo.
original_explanation: Your current Waze destination. It's where you're physically going, like "Saan ang tinutungo mo?" (Where are you headed?). It can also be your life goal, your career path. "Ano ba talaga ang tinutungo ng relationship natin?" is the ultimate DTR (Define The Relationship) question.
usage_notes: Ito ang anyong pangkasalukuyan ng pandiwang "tunguhin". Ang anyong naganap ay "tinungo" at panghinaharap ay "tutunguhin".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Aling landas ang **tinutungo** mo sa buhay?","translation":"Which path are you **heading towards** in life?"},{"sentence":"Nakikita ko na ang gusaling aming **tinutungo**.","translation":"I can now see the building we are **heading to**."}]

meaning_filipino: Salatin o hawakan ang katawan ng isang tao upang maghanap ng isang bagay na nakatago, o sa masamang kahulugan, bilang isang uri ng panghihipo.
original_explanation: Has two main vibes. 1) The security guard at the mall entrance patting you down for contraband. That's 'mangapkap'. 2) The creepy person on a crowded MRT who 'accidentally' touches people. That's also 'mangapkap', but the criminal, disgusting kind. The word itself is neutral—it's the context that makes it either a security procedure or a crime.
usage_notes: The meaning can range from a neutral act of searching (like by police) to a negative act of unwanted touching (groping). Context is crucial.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **mangapkap** ng guwardiya sa lahat ng pumapasok sa concert.","translation":"The guard has to **frisk** everyone entering the concert."},{"sentence":"Idinemanda niya ang lalaking nangahas na **mangapkap** sa kanya sa bus.","translation":"She sued the man who dared to **grope** her on the bus."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng may labis na kumpiyansa sa sarili o nag-aakala ng mga bagay na hindi naman totoo, lalo na kung ito ay tungkol sa atensyon mula sa iba.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Ingles na "feeling" at Espanyol na panlaping pambabae na "-era".
original_explanation: She's the girl who thinks the barista is flirting with her just because they drew a heart on her latte. She'll post a blurry selfie with the caption 'I woke up like this' when you know it took 37 tries and a filter. It's main character energy, but sometimes the movie is a flop. 'Feeling maganda,' 'feeling sikat,' 'feeling chinita'—the possibilities are endless.
usage_notes: Isang salitang nakabatay sa kasarian para sa isang babae. Ang katumbas nito sa lalaki ay 'feelingero'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong **feelingera**, hindi ikaw ang tinitingnan niya.","translation":"Don't be so **assuming**, he's not looking at you."},{"sentence":"Yung kaibigan mong **feelingera**, akala niya lahat ng lalaki may gusto sa kanya.","translation":"Your **conceited** friend thinks all the guys have a crush on her."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan ginagawa o kinukuha ang asin, karaniwan sa pamamagitan ng pagsingaw ng tubig-alat.
etymology: Nagmula sa salitang-ugat na "asin" na may hulaping "-an" na tumutukoy sa lugar.
original_explanation: Before fancy Himalayan pink salt became a thing, this was the OG source. An 'asnan' is basically a salt farm. Imagine shallow pools of seawater just chilling under the sun, waiting to evaporate and leave behind the good stuff. It's the place that makes our chicharon and mangga with bagoong possible. Respect the asnan.
usage_notes: The suffix "-an" denotes a place where the root word is found or made in abundance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala ang lalawigan ng Pangasinan sa kanilang malalawak na **asnan**.","translation":"The province of Pangasinan is known for its vast **salt beds**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga manggagawa sa **asnan** ay nagtatrabaho sa ilalim ng matinding sikat ng araw.","translation":"The workers at the **saltern** work under the intense heat of the sun."}]

meaning_filipino: Kasalukuyang kinakaharap o tinutugunan ang isang sitwasyon, problema, o tao.
etymology: From `harap` (front/face) with the `-in-` infix, indicating the object being faced.
original_explanation: This is you on a Monday morning, **facing** a mountain of emails. Or when you finally decide to confront your 'Marites' neighbor about the latest chismis. It's the present continuous tense of dealing with life's challenges, big or small.
usage_notes: The object being faced is the focus of the sentence. Present tense of 'harrapin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Anong pagsubok ang **hinaharap** mo ngayon sa trabaho?","translation":"What challenge are you **facing** at work right now?"},{"sentence":"Matapang niyang **hinaharap** ang bawat problema.","translation":"She bravely **confronts** every problem."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang posisyon o opinyon ng isang tao hinggil sa isang partikular na isyu; paninindigan.
original_explanation: 'Ano'ng stand mo sa issue?' Eto 'yung tanong kapag may mainit na chismis o political issue. It's your official, non-negotiable opinion. 'Yung pinaninindigan mo kahit i-cancel ka pa ng buong bayan.
usage_notes: Frequently used in discussions about opinions, politics, and social issues.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga na malaman ang **stand** ng bawat kandidato sa mahahalagang isyu.","translation":"It's important to know the **stand** of each candidate on important issues."},{"sentence":"Hindi nagbago ang **stand** ko, naniniwala pa rin ako sa kanya.","translation":"My **stand** hasn't changed, I still believe in him."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na nagpapahayag ng pagtanggi, pagsalungat, o kawalan; salungat sa positibo.
original_explanation: That one friend who always sees the bad side of things. "Bes, ang nega mo!" Also, 'yung result ng pregnancy test na hinihintay mo (or kinakatakutan mo). Or the result of a COVID test. It's the opposite of positive.
usage_notes: Ito ang Tinagalog na baybay ng salitang Ingles/Espanyol na "negative".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iwasan mo ang mga **negatib** na pag-iisip para hindi ka ma-stress.","translation":"Avoid **negative** thoughts so you don't get stressed."},{"sentence":"**Negatib** ang resulta ng kanyang medical test.","translation":"The result of his medical test was **negative**."}]

meaning_filipino: Sadyang umiwas o lumayo sa isang tao, bagay, o sitwasyon, karaniwan dahil sa takot, paggalang, o pag-iingat.
original_explanation: Eto yung "ghosting" bago pa na-imbento ang term na 'yan. Yung iniiwasan mo yung officemate mong laging nangungutang, o yung ex mo na nakita mo sa mall. You see them, you make a quick turn. You pangilagan them. It's the art of strategic avoidance.
usage_notes: Implies a deliberate act of avoiding someone or something, often out of fear, respect, or dislike.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat mong **pangilagan** ang mga taong may masamang impluwensya.","translation":"You should **avoid** people who are a bad influence."},{"sentence":"Mula nang mag-away sila, **pinangilagan** na niya ang kanyang dating kaibigan.","translation":"Ever since they fought, he has **shunned** his former friend."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong gumagawa ng mga bagay, kadalasan ay kontrobersyal o sukdulan, upang makakuha ng atensyon, impluwensya, o katanyagan sa social media.
original_explanation: Yung kaibigan mong biglang nag-post ng 'unpopular opinion' na super offensive para lang pag-usapan. O 'yung nag-comment sa issue ng may issue para lang sumakay sa trending topic. They live by the motto: 'Any publicity is good publicity.' The term 'clout chase malala' is used when the attempt is very obvious and desperate.
usage_notes: A derogatory term for someone perceived as desperate for online fame. The plural is 'cloutchasers'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang pansinin 'yan, isa lang siyang **cloutchaser** na gustong sumikat.","translation":"Don't pay attention to him, he's just a **cloutchaser** who wants to get famous."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sining, gawain, o propesyon ng isang anluwage; ang paggawa o pagkukumpuni ng mga bagay na yari sa kahoy.
etymology: From `anluwage` (carpenter). The `pag-` prefix and reduplication of the first vowel `a` indicate the act or profession of being a carpenter.
original_explanation: This is the OG DIY. Before YouTube tutorials and IKEA, there was the anluwage (carpenter) and their craft, pag-aanluwagi. It's the skill of turning a block of wood into a table, a chair, or that *silya de tumba* your lola loves. It’s basically adult LEGOs but with splinters.
usage_notes: A formal and rather rare term. "Karpinterya" or "pagkakarpintero" is the more common, Spanish-derived equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinakailangan ng tiyaga at husay sa **pag-aanluwagi**.","translation":"Patience and skill are needed in **carpentry**."},{"sentence":"Nais niyang pag-aralan ang sining ng **pag-aanluwagi** mula sa kanyang lolo.","translation":"He wants to learn the art of **carpentry** from his grandfather."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang magalang na salita na ginagamit sa paghingi ng paumanhin o pahintulot, lalo na kapag dadaan sa pagitan ng mga tao o sa mga lugar na pinaniniwalaang may mga espiritu.
etymology: Theorized as a contraction of 'sa inyo'y tabi' (roughly 'aside for you') or a similar polite phrase involving 'tabi' (side, aside).
original_explanation: The magic word you say so you don't get cursed by a 'nuno sa punso'. 'Sintabi po, makikiraan lang' is your supernatural insurance policy when walking past an old tree or an anthill. It's the old-school 'excuse me po,' mixed with a healthy dose of respect for the unseen. Also used when you need to pass between two people talking so you don't 'cut' their conversation.
usage_notes: Almost always used with 'po' for politeness: 'Sintabi po.' The phrase 'Tabi-tabi po' carries a very similar meaning, especially in folklore contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sintabi** po, dadaan lang kami sa inyong bakuran.","translation":"**With your permission**, we will just pass through your yard."},{"sentence":"Nagsabi siya ng **sintabi** bago pumasok sa madilim na gubat.","translation":"He said **'excuse me'** before entering the dark forest."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bahagi, kontribusyon, o ambag, karaniwang pagkain o bagay, na ibinibigay sa isang grupo o para sa isang okasyon.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'potluck.' When your tita says, 'Magdala ka ng amot mo,' she means bring your share, usually a Tupperware of spaghetti or a tray of leche flan for the fiesta. It's the physical form of 'ambagan.' No amot, no entry... or at least you'll get some side-eye from the other relatives.
usage_notes: Karaniwan sa maraming rehiyonal na wika sa Pilipinas na may pareho o katulad na kahulugan. Sa standard na Tagalog, mas karaniwan ang 'ambag', ngunit ang 'amot' ay malawak na naiintindihan, lalo na sa mga di-pormal na pagtitipon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang magiging **amot** mo para sa salu-salo sa Sabado?","translation":"What will your **contribution** be for the get-together on Saturday?"},{"sentence":"Ang bawat pamilya ay may dalang **amot** na pagkain para sa piyesta.","translation":"Each family brought a food **contribution** for the fiesta."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng hindi magkatulad na katangian, anyo, o kalikasan.
etymology: From `magka-` + `iba`, where `magka-` indicates a shared state of being different from one another.
original_explanation: The ultimate "opposites attract" word. It's you loving K-Pop and your partner loving heavy metal. It's pineapple on pizza vs. no pineapple on pizza. You're not the same, and that's okay. Sometimes.
usage_notes: A very common adjective to express difference between two or more things.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit kambal sila, **magkaiba** ang kanilang mga ugali.","translation":"Even though they are twins, their personalities are **different from each other**."},{"sentence":"**Magkaiba** ang pananaw namin sa pulitika kaya madalas kaming magtalo.","translation":"Our political views are **different**, which is why we often argue."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasalanan o pagkakamali na mayroon pang kakayahang patawarin o palampasin.
etymology: ma- (ability) + ipagpa- (causative) + pa- (future tense marker) + tawad (forgive)
original_explanation: This is the future tense of forgiveness. It’s the "maybe someday" of letting go of a grudge. When your friend cancels on you for the nth time, you sigh and say, "Hindi ko alam kung **maipagpapatawad** ko pa 'to." It’s the hope that you won't hold onto that 'sama ng loob' forever.
usage_notes: This is a future tense verb form. It implies a future possibility of forgiveness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana'y **maipagpapatawad** mo ang aking nagawang kasalanan.","translation":"I hope you **will be able to forgive** the wrong I have done."},{"sentence":"Ang ginawa niyang panloloko ay isang bagay na hindi basta-basta **maipagpapatawad**.","translation":"His deception is something that **will not be easily forgiven**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang lugar o posisyon na walang laman o hindi okupado.
original_explanation: That 'For Rent' sign on an apartment? That means the unit is bakante. That job opening your BPO friend told you about? It's a bakante position. It's the space waiting to be filled, whether it's a parking spot, a seat on the bus, or a spot in someone's heart (charot!).
usage_notes: Can be used for places, positions, or even time slots.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **bakante** pa bang upuan sa harap?","translation":"Is there still a **vacant** seat in front?"},{"sentence":"Naghahanap sila ng bagong manager dahil **bakante** ang posisyon.","translation":"They are looking for a new manager because the position is **vacant**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglilinis ng sugat gamit ang isang antiseptikong likido o maligamgam na tubig na may asin upang maiwasan ang impeksyon.
original_explanation: This is what your lola does when you get a 'gasgas' from playing too much. It's the OG way of disinfecting a wound before Betadine became a thing. You'd hear "Tiis ganda" or "Tiis pogi" while they **langgasin** your wound with that warm salt water solution that stings like heck.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **langgasin** ang sugat mo para hindi ito maimpeksyon.","translation":"Your wound needs to be **cleansed** so it doesn't get infected."},{"sentence":"**Langgasin** mo ng maligamgam na tubig na may asin ang hiwa sa iyong daliri.","translation":"**Cleanse** the cut on your finger with warm salt water."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang yunit ng tirahan na bahagi ng isang mas malaking gusali na karaniwang inuupahan.
original_explanation: The classic Pinoy starter pack for independence. It's smaller than a house, bigger than your childhood bedroom, and just right for accumulating Meralco bills and Shopee deliveries. Your landlord is either a sweet tita or your greatest nemesis. No in-between.
usage_notes: Bagama't may mga katumbas na salita tulad ng 'paupahan' o 'aksesorya', mas karaniwan at naiintindihan ang salitang 'apartment' sa modernong usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghahanap sila ng **apartment** na malapit sa kanilang trabaho.","translation":"They are looking for an **apartment** near their workplace."},{"sentence":"Maliit lang ang **apartment** ko pero sapat na para sa akin.","translation":"My **apartment** is small but it's enough for me."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan na ginagamit upang pigain o diinan ang isang bagay upang makuha ang katas o likido nito.
original_explanation: The gadget you use to get every last drop of juice from a calamansi or lemon for your pancit or iced tea. It's a tool for extraction, applying pressure to get the good stuff out. Think of it as the mechanical version of your strong tita's handshake.
usage_notes: Can refer to any tool used for squeezing, such as a citrus squeezer or a garlic press.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasaan na ba ang **panisil** ng bawang?","translation":"Where is the garlic **presser**?"},{"sentence":"Hiram muna ako ng **panisil** ng calamansi.","translation":"May I borrow the calamansi **squeezer**?"}]

translation: The act of scrubbing (with a brush)
meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng paglilinis sa pamamagitan ng pagkuskos gamit ang isang iskoba.
etymology: From `pag-` (nominalizer) + `iskoba` (scrubbing brush), which is from the Spanish `escoba` (broom). In Filipino, its meaning shifted to a hand-held brush.
original_explanation: This is the workout you didn't sign up for. It's the intense arm-day session when cleaning the bathroom tiles or scrubbing the kaldero with a week-old tutong. The sound of `pag-iiskoba` is the soundtrack of every Filipino household's general cleaning day.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to scrubbing with a brush, not just any kind of cleaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagod na pagod ako sa **pag-iiskoba** ng sahig sa banyo.","translation":"I'm so tired from the **act of scrubbing** the bathroom floor."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na tuwid, walang liko, o sa isang tao o gawa na tama, makatarungan, at naaayon sa moralidad.
original_explanation: This word has two vibes. Vibe 1: The physical 'straight' like a ruler or a freshly rebonded hair. Vibe 2: The moral 'straight' – being on the 'daang matuwid' (righteous path). It's about being upright, honest, and not cutting corners, whether you're drawing a line or living your life. The goal is to be as matwid as your lola's moral compass.
usage_notes: 'Matwid' is often used in a more poetic or moral sense than its root 'tuwid', which is more commonly used for physical straightness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagsasabi ng totoo ay isang daang **matwid**.","translation":"Telling the truth is a **righteous** path."},{"sentence":"Sikapin mong mamuhay nang **matwid** at marangal.","translation":"Strive to live a **just** and honorable life."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng de-latang karne na prinoseso at hinahalo, karaniwang ipiniprito at inihahain kasama ng kanin.
original_explanation: The king of 'pang-emergency' meals. That pinkish, salty block of mystery meat in a can that saved you during typhoons, pay-day droughts, and lazy Sunday mornings. Best fried until crispy on the edges and eaten with sinangag and a fried egg. It's not just food, it's a core memory.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to canned processed meat like SPAM, Maling, or local brands.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong almusal ang pritong **luncheonmeat** na may kasamang itlog.","translation":"My favorite breakfast is fried **luncheon meat** with an egg."},{"sentence":"Bumili ka ng dalawang lata ng **luncheonmeat** para may reserba tayo.","translation":"Buy two cans of **luncheon meat** so we have a reserve."}]

meaning_filipino: Kalingain at ituring na sariling anak ang hindi tunay na anak; kupkupin at bigyan ng pangangalaga.
original_explanation: It's what you do when you see a stray kitten, or when your favorite Tita who's 'single by choice' decides you're now her designated travel buddy and food trip companion. To take something or someone in and care for them as your own.
usage_notes: This is the verb form used when the object (the one being adopted) is the focus of the sentence. The root 'ampon' means an adopted child.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang mag-asawa na **ampunin** ang ulilang bata.","translation":"The couple decided to **adopt** the orphaned child."},{"sentence":"Sana may **ampunin** sa akin na mayaman,\" pabirong sabi niya.","translation":"I hope a rich person **adopts** me,\" she said jokingly."}]

meaning_filipino: Gagawin ang pagpapatunog sa isang kasangkapang pangmusika sa hinaharap; ang musikang pyesa na balak patugtugin.
original_explanation: The future tense of jamming. It's what you tell your friend when they ask what you're going to do with that new ukulele you bought online. "Ano'ng gagawin mo diyan?" "Ah, **tutugtugin** ko." It's the promise of a future concert, even if it's just for your cats.
usage_notes: This is the object-focus, future tense form of the verb 'tugtog'. It refers to the song or piece that will be played.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **tutugtugin** ng banda mamayang gabi?","translation":"What (song) **will** the band **play** tonight?"},{"sentence":"**Tutugtugin** niya ang paborito kong kanta sa piano.","translation":"He **will play** my favorite song on the piano."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang rehas na bakal o metal na pinapatungan ng pagkain upang ihawin sa ibabaw ng nagbabagang uling o apoy.
original_explanation: 'Yan 'yung metal grid na pinag-iihawan ng isaw, betamax, at hotdog sa tabi-tabi. The sacred altar for all things 'ihaw-ihaw'. Kung wala kang **parilya** sa family outing, kulang ang experience. Huwag kalimutan, 'yung part na may sunog-sunog, 'yun ang "flavor."
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa metal na rehas, ngunit madalas ginagamit para tukuyin ang buong ihawan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Linisin mo muna ang **parilya** bago tayo mag-ihaw ng liempo.","translation":"Clean the **grill** first before we grill the pork belly."},{"sentence":"Mainit na ang uling, ilagay mo na ang **parilya** sa ibabaw.","translation":"The charcoal is hot, place the **grate** on top now."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pahayag na hiniram mula sa isang tao o teksto; o isang pagtantiya ng presyo para sa isang serbisyo o produkto.
original_explanation: In the Philippines, 'quote' has two main battlegrounds. First, the 'hugot quote' you post on social media when you're feeling deep or heartbroken. Second, the 'quote' you get from a contractor for your home renovation, which is the opening line to a different kind of heartbreak. 'Magkano po pa-quote?' is a phrase that precedes either inspiration or perspiration (from seeing the price).
usage_notes: Used extensively in Taglish in both its meanings: a cited phrase and a price quotation. The Tagalog equivalent is 'sipi' (for a quotation) or 'pagtantiya' (for an estimate).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng **quote** na pinost mo sa Facebook kanina.","translation":"The **quote** you posted on Facebook earlier was beautiful."},{"sentence":"Humingi ako ng **quote** sa tatlong supplier para sa mga materyales.","translation":"I asked for a **quote** from three suppliers for the materials."}]

translation: To be looked up to; to admire
meaning_filipino: Maging isang huwaran o modelo na iginagalang at hinahangaan ng marami. Kadalasang ginagamit sa anyong 'tinitingala' o 'titingalain'.
original_explanation: Eto 'yung #Goals. 'Yung level na hindi ka lang tinitingala physically (kasi matangkad ka), kundi tinitingala ka for your achievements. Ikaw 'yung "Sana All" ng barkada. The opposite of being the "bad influence."
usage_notes: This is the metaphorical use of 'tingala' (to look up), meaning to admire or respect.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Dr. Jose Rizal ay isang bayaning **tinitingalaan** ng lahat ng Pilipino.","translation":"Dr. Jose Rizal is a hero **looked up to** by all Filipinos."}]

translation: to bury in oblivion; to forget completely
meaning_filipino: Ganap na kalimutan ang isang bagay, alaala, o pangyayari na para bang hindi ito kailanman umiral.
etymology: An idiomatic phrase combining 'ilibing' (to bury) and 'limot' (forgetfulness).
original_explanation: This is the "delete and block" for your brain. It's the ultimate 'move on' move. 'Yung mga masasakit na alaala, 'yung utang ng kaibigan mo, 'yung nakakahiyang moment mo nung high school — lahat 'yan, kailangan nang ilibing sa limot.
usage_notes: An expressive idiom for deliberate and complete forgetting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masakit man, kailangan na nating **ilibing sa limot** ang nakaraan.","translation":"Though it hurts, we need to **bury the past in oblivion**."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **ilibing sa limot** ang lahat ng alaala niya sa dating kasintahan.","translation":"She tried to **completely forget** all her memories of her ex-lover."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang banal na langis na binabasbasan ng obispo at ginagamit sa mga sakramento ng Simbahang Katolika, tulad ng binyag, kumpil, at pagpapahid ng langis sa maysakit.
original_explanation: The special, blessed oil used by priests for sacraments. It's the OG essential oil. Not for your diffuser, but for baptisms and anointing the sick. It's the spiritual equivalent of Vicks VapoRub for your soul.
usage_notes: Sometimes spelled as 'Santo Olyo' or 'Santuolyo'. It refers to the three types of holy oils: Oil of Catechumens, Oil of the Infirm, and Holy Chrism.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ng pari ang **Santu-Olyo** para sa pagpapahid sa maysakit.","translation":"The priest used the **Holy Oil** for the anointing of the sick."},{"sentence":"Ang **Santu-Olyo** ay binabasbasan tuwing Huwebes Santo sa Misa ng Krisma.","translation":"The **Holy Oils** are blessed every Holy Thursday during the Chrism Mass."}]

meaning_filipino: Laganap o kalat sa isang lugar; marami at matatagpuan kahit saan.
etymology: From Malay 'lipan' meaning 'centipede', implying something that spreads out like its many legs.
original_explanation: Parang chismis sa office, sobrang bilis kumalat. Or like that one K-drama everyone is suddenly watching. It's everywhere, you can't escape it. 'Lipana ang mga nagbebenta ng face mask noong pandemic.'
usage_notes: Often used to describe negative things like diseases, crime, or gossip, but can be neutral.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **lipana** ang sakit na dengue sa kanilang barangay dahil sa mga naipong tubig-ulan.","translation":"Dengue became **widespread** in their village because of the collected rainwater."},{"sentence":"**Lipana** ang mga pekeng balita sa social media, kaya mag-ingat sa pagbabasa.","translation":"Fake news is **rampant** on social media, so be careful what you read."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtamo ng sira, sugat, o anumang uri ng kapahamakan sa tao, bagay, o ari-arian.
original_explanation: The official status of your phone after it falls face down. The state of your friend's heart after a breakup. The result of a typhoon on a coastal town. It's the 'after' photo you don't want to see.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical damage to objects, injury to people, or abstract harm.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iniwan ng bagyo ang maraming bahay na **may-pinsala**.","translation":"The typhoon left many houses **damaged**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paghingi ng payo o impormasyon mula sa isang dalubhasa o eksperto.
original_explanation: This is what you do when WebMD says you have three days to live. You go for a 'kunsulta' with a real doctor. It's also what you do with your team lead before making a big decision at work, or with your 'mare' to dissect the latest chismis.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb root (e.g., 'kumunsulta', 'ikunsulta'). The more formal term is 'konsultasyon'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Libre ang unang **kunsulta** sa bagong klinika.","translation":"The first **consultation** is free at the new clinic."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng **kunsulta**, napanatag ang kanyang loob.","translation":"After the **consultation**, his mind was put at ease."}]

meaning_filipino: Gamitin sa pag-aahit ng buhok, balbas, o bigote.
original_explanation: This is the tool of the trade for that clean look. Your razor, your shaving cream, whatever you use to get rid of that 'bigote' or 'balbas' that's not quite working for you. It's the 'use this to shave' command. 'Ano'ng ipang-ahit mo? Ang kinis, ah!'
usage_notes: This is an instrumental verb, where the focus is on the tool or means used to perform the action of shaving. It can also function as a noun referring to the shaving implement itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lumang labaha ang kanyang **ipang-ahit** sa ulo.","translation":"The old razor is what he will **use to shave** his head."},{"sentence":"Wala na akong sabon na **ipang-ahit**.","translation":"I don't have any soap **to use for shaving**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong likas na masayahin, madaling malugod, at palaging may positibong pananaw sa buhay.
original_explanation: This is your friend who's a human Golden Retriever. They find joy in the little things, like free coffee refills or finding a 20-peso bill in their old jeans. They're the ones who say 'Good morning!' and actually mean it. A matuwain person is the opposite of your 'laging pagod' BPO friend.
usage_notes: Describes a person's general disposition, not just a temporary feeling of happiness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa pagiging **matuwain** at palangiti sa lahat.","translation":"She is known for being **cheerful** and always smiling at everyone."},{"sentence":"Kahit maraming problema, nananatili siyang **matuwain**.","translation":"Even with many problems, he remains **joyous**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sinasadyang paglanghap o di-sinasadyang maamoy ang hangin o anumang nasa hangin.
original_explanation: This is the general-purpose word for smelling or inhaling something. Unlike 'masamyo' which is for nice smells, 'masanghap' is neutral. You can 'masanghap' the fresh mountain air, but you can also 'masanghap' the usok from a jeepney or the unpleasant smell from the estero. It's the act of your nose doing its job, for better or for worse.
usage_notes: A more general term for smelling than 'masamyo' (fragrant) or 'maamoy' (can be good or bad).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong pumunta sa probinsya para **masanghap** ang sariwang hangin.","translation":"I want to go to the province to **inhale** the fresh air."},{"sentence":"Ayaw kong **masanghap** ang usok mula sa sigarilyo.","translation":"I don't want to **inhale** the smoke from the cigarette."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa halip na; bilang kapalit ng.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'en vez de'.
original_explanation: The classic Pinoy way of saying 'instead of.' 'Kumain ako ng kanin **embes** na mag-diet.' It's the word you use to justify your choices, good or bad. It's the colloquial, everyday version of the more formal 'sa halip na'.
usage_notes: Laganap sa pang-araw-araw na usapan. Madalas na ipinagpapalit sa 'imbes'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Embes** na mag-aral, nag-ML na lang siya buong gabi.","translation":"**Instead of** studying, he just played Mobile Legends all night."}]

translation: Spill the tea; tell the gossip
meaning_filipino: Isang modernong idyoma na nangangahulugang ibahagi o ikuwento ang mga tsismis, sikreto, o pinakabagong balita tungkol sa isang tao o sitwasyon.
etymology: From English slang, where 'T' stands for 'Truth'. Popularized by internet and drag culture.
original_explanation: This is the modern, social media-approved way of saying 'I-chika mo na!' It's the signal to share the juicy details, the drama, the latest scoop. When your friend says 'Spill the tea,' you better be ready with the screenshots and the whole backstory. The 'tea' is the chismis.
usage_notes: Used as a direct phrase in Taglish conversations. Often abbreviated to just 'Spill' or followed by 'sis.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uy, ano'ng nangyari sa kanila? **Spill the tea** naman diyan!","translation":"Hey, what happened to them? **Spill the tea**!"},{"sentence":"May chika ako sa'yo mamaya, sis. Get ready for me to **spill the tea**.","translation":"I have gossip for you later, sis. Get ready for me to **spill the tea**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pariralang pananong na ginagamit upang alamin ang haba ng oras o panahon ng isang pangyayari, gawain, o kalagayan.
original_explanation: The official question for impatient people, Pinoys waiting for their online shopping delivery, or anyone stuck in EDSA traffic. "Ma, **gaano katagal** pa?" is the childhood anthem of long road trips. In the world of love, it's the question you ask when someone says "Mag-usap tayo mamaya." How long is "mamaya"?!
usage_notes: Specifically asks about the duration of time.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Gaano katagal** ang biyahe mula Maynila hanggang Baguio?","translation":"**How long** is the trip from Manila to Baguio?"},{"sentence":"Tinanong niya ako kung **gaano katagal** ko siyang hihintayin.","translation":"He asked me **how long** I would wait for him."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang patag na parihabang espasyo na may tig-isang basket sa magkabilang dulo, na siyang lugar kung saan nilalaro ang basketbol.
original_explanation: The Philippines' real national stage. Every barangay has one, and it's more than just a place for sports. It's a community center, a venue for pageants, a place for zumba, an evacuation center during typhoons, and sometimes, a wake. The heart of the community.
usage_notes: Often shortened to 'court' in everyday speech. The formal Tagalog term 'palaruan ng basketbol' can be used but is less common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ang **basketball court** tuwing hapon.","translation":"The **basketball court** is full every afternoon."},{"sentence":"Magkita tayo sa **basketball court** mamaya.","translation":"Let's meet at the **basketball court** later."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na gumagamit ng karahasan, pananakot, o paninira upang maghasik ng takot sa publiko para sa layuning pampulitika o ideolohikal.
original_explanation: The ultimate kontrabida in news reports and action movies. Sila yung naglalagay ng bomba at naghahasik ng lagim. A very serious term you don't throw around lightly, unless you're joking about your friend who 'terrorizes' the group chat with endless memes.
usage_notes: A serious term with strong political and social connotations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahuli ng mga awtoridad ang pinaghihinalaang **terorista**.","translation":"The authorities captured the suspected **terrorist**."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-atake ay itinuturing na gawa ng isang grupo ng mga **terorista**.","translation":"The attack is considered the work of a group of **terrorists**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marahan at paunti-unting paghigop o pagsipsip ng isang likido.
original_explanation: Think of how you drink milk tea na malapit nang maubos, trying to get the last pearl—'yan ang pagsalipsip. It's a delicate, careful sip, not a chug. Parang pagkuha ng chismis, paunti-unti lang.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'sipsip' but can imply a more delicate, repeated, or widespread action (e.g., bees sipping from many flowers).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sinalipsip** ng bubuyog ang nektar mula sa bulaklak.","translation":"The bee **sipped** the nectar from the flower."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **sumalipsip** ng kape habang nagbabasa.","translation":"He likes to **sip** coffee while reading."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pag-aari, gawain, o katangiang bukod-tangi sa bawat isa sa isang pangkat.
etymology: Nagmula sa reduplikasyon ng "kaniya", na buhat naman sa "ka-" at "niya".
original_explanation: The official motto of potlucks and team buildings: 'Okay guys, kani-kaniya na lang ng ambag ha?' It's the polite way of saying 'Mind your own business' or 'You're on your own.' Pag narinig mo 'to, it means 'walang pakialamanan' or 'bahala ka sa buhay mo.'
usage_notes: Madalas ginagamit kasama ang 'kanya-kanyang' bilang pang-uri (hal. 'kanya-kanyang diskarte'). Ang 'kani-kaniya' ay panghalip.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng pulong, bumalik sila sa **kani-kaniya** nilang mga gawain.","translation":"After the meeting, they returned to their **respective** tasks."},{"sentence":"Sa huli, **kani-kaniya** tayong lahat sa pagharap sa ating mga problema.","translation":"In the end, we are all on **our own** in facing our problems."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pamamaga, pamumula, o pangangati ng balat na karaniwang sanhi ng iritasyon o alerhiya.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung reaction ng balat mo noong nalaman mong na-seen ka lang niya. Biglang may pangangati at pamumula, 'yan ang **talitis**. O 'yung kamay ng laging naglalaba, nagkakaroon ng **talitis** dahil sa matapang na sabon. It's that annoying skin rash from chemicals or, you know, emotional damage.
