usage_notes: Maaari ring tumukoy sa isang maliit na daloy ng tubig, ngunit mas bihirang gamitin sa kahulugang ito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng **talitis** ang kaniyang mga kamay dahil sa kemikal sa trabaho.","translation":"His hands developed **dermatitis** because of the chemicals at work."},{"sentence":"Pinayuhan siya ng doktor na gumamit ng espesyal na sabon para sa kaniyang **talitis**.","translation":"The doctor advised him to use a special soap for his **skin inflammation**."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang bagay o balat na may mga guhit, lukot, o tupi dahil sa pagtanda, pagkatuyo, o pagkakapiga.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your skin after years of marites-ing, to your clothes when you're too lazy to iron, or to your face when you see your ex with a new jowa. It's the opposite of 'smooth.'
usage_notes: Can describe skin, fabric, paper, or any surface that can be wrinkled.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mapagmahal pa rin siya sa **kulubot** na kamay ng kanyang lola.","translation":"He still loves the **wrinkled** hands of his grandmother."},{"sentence":"Ayusin mo ang **kulubot** na damit mo bago ka umalis.","translation":"Fix your **creased** shirt before you leave."}]

translation: to put inside; to let in; to enroll
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng isang bagay sa loob ng isa pa; ang pagbibigay-pahintulot sa isang tao na pumasok; o ang pagtatala ng pangalan sa isang paaralan o kurso.
original_explanation: The multi-tasking verb for getting things in. You magpasok your USB into the laptop, you magpasok the guest into the house ('Tuloy po kayo!'), or you magpasok your kid in a good school (which involves a lot of paperwork and parent-tita pressure). It's all about entry.
usage_notes: The meaning changes significantly based on context (object, person, institution).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**magpasok** ng mga damit sa aparador.","translation":"Please **put** the clothes **inside** the closet."},{"sentence":"Sino ang nag-utos na **magpasok** ng aso sa loob ng bahay?","translation":"Who ordered to **let** the dog **in** the house?"},{"sentence":"Gusto kong **magpasok** ng anak ko sa isang pampublikong paaralan.","translation":"I want to **enroll** my child in a public school."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang lasa; matabang.
etymology: Mula sa "wala" (none) + "-ng" (linker) + "latoy" (isang termino para sa lasa, bagaman bihira na itong gamitin nang mag-isa).
original_explanation: This is that sinigang your friend cooked that tastes more like "nilagang tubig na may kangkong." It's food that's so bland, it makes you sad. Parang 'yung ka-chat mo na "haha" at "ok" lang ang reply. Walang-latoy! It lacks the 'kick' or 'sarap' that makes things interesting.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit para sa pagkain at inumin. Maaaring gamitin nang patalinghaga para sa isang kuwento o pagtatanghal na walang kabuhay-buhay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko nagustuhan ang luto niya, **walang-latoy** ang adobo.","translation":"I didn't like her cooking, the adobo was **tasteless**."},{"sentence":"Dagdagan mo ng patis, parang **walang-latoy** ang sabaw.","translation":"Add some fish sauce, the soup seems **bland**."}]

meaning_filipino: Matapang o matindi ang amoy o lasa na bahagyang nakasusugat sa pang-amoy o panlasa.
original_explanation: Yung amoy ng durian o bagoong na pagbukas mo pa lang, alam na ng buong barangay. O yung sipa ng suka na sobrang tapang, mapapapikit ka. It’s that sharp, intense sensation that hits your senses hard, for better or for worse.
usage_notes: Primarily used for strong smells and tastes, often with a sharp or piercing quality.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **masigid** na amoy ng pabango ay kumapit sa kanyang damit.","translation":"The **pungent** smell of the perfume clung to her clothes."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang bagay, pamumuhay, o kaganapan na labis sa karaniwan, magastos, at puno ng karangalan o luho.
original_explanation: Think of the lifestyle of a celebrity in a Forbes Park mansion, a gown from a Michael Cinco fashion show, or that one tita who shows up to the family reunion dripping in gold jewelry. 'Marangya' is living the high life, extra-extra, and not being afraid to show it. It's the opposite of a minimalist aesthetic.
usage_notes: Describes anything from lifestyle ('marangyang pamumuhay') to objects ('marangyang sasakyan') to events ('marangyang handaan'). The word 'mararangya' is its plural form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghanda sila ng isang **marangya** na salu-salo para sa kanilang anibersaryo.","translation":"They prepared a **lavish** feast for their anniversary."},{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang magkaroon ng **marangya** na buhay balang araw.","translation":"She dreams of having a **luxurious** life someday."},{"sentence":"Ang mga politiko ay pinuna dahil sa kanilang **marangya** na paggastos.","translation":"The politicians were criticized for their **extravagant** spending."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita ng kahusayan o galing sa isang bagay sa paraang may halong pagyayabang upang mapansin o hangaan ng iba.
original_explanation: This is that one officemate who types really loud when the boss is around, or that friend who suddenly speaks in full English after watching one Hollywood movie. It's about making a spectacle of your 'skills' for clout. It's the "look at me, I'm so galing" energy, often just for show.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin na may bahagyang negatibong konotasyon, na nagpapahiwatig na ang pagpapakita ay higit na para sa palabas kaysa sa tunay na nilalaman.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang puro **pakitang-gilas**; ipakita mo ang tunay mong kakayahan.","translation":"Don't just be a **show-off**; show your real abilities."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang talumpati ay isang malaking **pakitang-gilas** lamang.","translation":"His speech was just a big act of **grandstanding**."}]

translation: to coincide; to happen by chance
meaning_filipino: Maganap o mangyari sa isang tiyak na panahon o pagkakataon nang hindi sinasadya.
original_explanation: The universe's way of playing a prank on you. It's when you bump into your ex while looking like you just rolled out of bed, or when your crush DMs you the exact moment you're about to log off. It’s the ultimate 'timing' moment, whether for good or for bad.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi namin sinasadya, **napataon** lang na pareho kami ng destinasyon.","translation":"We didn't plan it, it just **happened by chance** that we had the same destination."},{"sentence":"Sana ay huwag **mapataon** sa araw ng exam ang brownout.","translation":"I hope the power outage doesn't **coincide** with the exam day."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang protina sa dugo na nililikha ng sistemang imyuno bilang tugon sa isang partikular na antigen (tulad ng virus o bakterya), na may kakayahang neutralisahin ito.
etymology: Filipino phonetic spelling of the English word 'antibody'.
original_explanation: Your body's personal security guards or bouncers. When a virus (the uninvited guest) tries to enter the club (your system), the antibady squad shows up to kick it out. Getting a vaccine is like giving them a heads-up with a picture of the troublemaker so they're ready to block them at the door.
usage_notes: Became extremely common during the COVID-19 pandemic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bakuna ay tumutulong sa katawan na gumawa ng mga **antibady**.","translation":"The vaccine helps the body create **antibodies**."},{"sentence":"Sinuri ang kanyang dugo para malaman ang bilang ng kanyang **antibady**.","translation":"His blood was tested to determine his **antibody** count."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng sabaw na gawa sa pinakuluang karne, isda, o gulay. Karaniwang ginagamit bilang panimpla at pampalasa sa pagluluto, madalas sa anyong cube o pulbos.
original_explanation: The magic cube or powder that turns plain hot water into "sabaw." It's the ultimate cooking cheat code for when you want the flavor of chicken or beef stock without boiling bones for 8 hours. Knorr Cubes and Maggi Magic Sarap are its popular local avatars.
usage_notes: Used in culinary contexts. More commonly, Filipinos would use brand names like "Knorr cubes" or generic terms like "panimpla" or "sabaw cubes."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magdagdag ka ng isang **bouillon** cube sa nilaga para lumasa.","translation":"Add one **bouillon** cube to the stew to add flavor."},{"sentence":"Ang sikreto sa masarap na sopas ay ang de-kalidad na **bouillon**.","translation":"The secret to a delicious soup is high-quality **bouillon**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahabang salaysay na pampanitikan na nahahati sa mga kabanata, karaniwang naglalarawan ng mga tauhan at mga pangyayari sa isang masalimuot na banghay.
original_explanation: Officially, it's a novel, like Rizal's Noli Me Tángere. Unofficially, it's what you call your friend's super long, dramatic text message about their love life. 'Teh, **nobela** na naman 'yang chat mo!' It's any story, real or imagined, that's long enough to require a coffee break in the middle.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for a book or figuratively for a long, drawn-out story, explanation, or even a text message.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang *Noli Me Tángere* ay isang mahalagang **nobela** sa kasaysayan ng Pilipinas.","translation":"*Noli Me Tángere* is an important **novel** in Philippine history."},{"sentence":"Tinanong ko lang kung kumusta siya, pero **nobela** ang isinagot niya sa text.","translation":"I just asked how she was, but she sent a **novel** as a reply via text."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hindi pagtupad sa inaasahan o kagustuhan ng isang tao; ang pagdudulot ng pagkadismaya.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung ginawa sa'yo ng ex mo. 'Yung feeling na umasa ka sa wala. Parang nag-abang ka ng 13th-month pay pero na-delay, tapos nung dumating, kulang pa. Ultimate hugot fuel. To let someone down, big time.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of relationships, promises, and expectations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo sana akong **biguin** sa tiwalang ibinigay ko sa iyo.","translation":"I hope you don't **disappoint** the trust I've given you."},{"sentence":"**Binigo** niya ang pangarap ng kanyang mga magulang na maging doktor.","translation":"He **failed** his parents' dream for him to become a doctor."}]

translation: to be able to celebrate Christmas
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng pagkakataon o kakayahang ipagdiwang ang araw ng Pasko.
original_explanation: For OFWs, seafarers, and BPO agents on a night shift, this is the goal: to be able to spend Christmas with family. It's not about receiving gifts (that's 'makapamasko'), but about being present and celebrating the holiday itself. 'Sana makapasko ako sa Pinas this year.'
usage_notes: Distinguishable from "makapamasko". This verb is about the ability to participate in the celebration, not receive gifts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umuwi ang seaman para **makapasko** kasama ang kanyang pamilya.","translation":"The seaman went home to be **able to celebrate Christmas** with his family."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa trabaho, marami ang hindi **nakapasko** sa kanilang mga probinsya.","translation":"Because of work, many were not **able to celebrate Christmas** in their provinces."}]

translation: to stick; to paste; to attach
meaning_filipino: Ikabit o paglapatin ang dalawang bagay gamit ang isang malagkit na substansiya tulad ng pandikit, o sa pamamagitan ng pagdiin.
original_explanation: This is what you do with a poster on a wall, a sticker on your laptop, or yourself to your crush (kidding... mostly). It's the command to make something stick. "Bes, **idikit** mo na 'yung resibo sa logbook." It's the opposite of "tanggalin," and the reason why Scotch tape and Mighty Bond exist.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for adhesives or figuratively for becoming very close to someone, as in 'idikit ang sarili' (to attach oneself).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**idikit** mo itong anunsyo sa bulletin board.","translation":"Please **stick** this announcement on the bulletin board."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong masyadong **idikit** ang sarili mo sa mga taong may masamang impluwensya.","translation":"Don't **attach** yourself too closely to people with bad influence."}]

meaning_filipino: Tiyakin o patunayan ang isang bagay upang magkaroon ng katiyakan.
original_explanation: The official verb of your overthinking friend or your tita who needs to confirm your attendance for the 5th time. 'Bes, siguruhan mo lang ha, kasama ka ba talaga sa beach trip? Kasi nagbayad na ako ng van.'
usage_notes: Often used in imperative form ('Siguruhan mo!').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **siguruhan** mong nakasara ang pinto bago ka umalis.","translation":"Please **make sure** the door is locked before you leave."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **siguruhan** na tama ang lahat ng detalye sa kontrata.","translation":"We need to **ensure** that all the details in the contract are correct."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-uga-uga o pagiging hindi matatag ng isang bagay, tulad ng isang mesa, upuan, o gusali.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung puso mo pag nakita mo si ex na may kasamang iba—unstable. Or 'yung tuhod mo after leg day sa gym. It's the physical manifestation of 'I'm not okay.' Also applies to wobbly tables in a coffee shop that spill your P200 latte.
usage_notes: Can be used both literally for physical objects and figuratively for emotions, plans, or situations that are unstable or precarious.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paggiwang** ng tulay ay nagdulot ng takot sa mga tao.","translation":"The **swaying** of the bridge caused fear among the people."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa lindol, naramdaman ang malakas na **paggiwang** ng aming gusali.","translation":"Because of the earthquake, the strong **wobbling** of our building was felt."}]

meaning_filipino: Magsalita ng kasinungalingan o walang batayan laban sa isang tao upang sirain ang kanyang reputasyon o karangalan.
etymology: Compound word from manira (to destroy) and puri (honor, praise).
original_explanation: The national sport of Marites and chismosos everywhere. It's when you spread fake news about someone to ruin their good name. This can literally get you sued for libel. Kaya 'think before you click' at 'think before you speak'.
usage_notes: A serious accusation and a legal term (libel/slander). The root words are 'sira' and 'puri'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **manirang-puri** ay isang krimen na may kaakibat na parusa.","translation":"**Slander** is a crime with a corresponding punishment."},{"sentence":"Itigil mo na ang paninirang-puri sa kanya dahil wala kang ebidensya.","translation":"Stop your slander against him/her because you have no evidence."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga maling impormasyon o balita na sadyang ginawa at ipinakalat upang manlinlang, magdulot ng kalituhan, o mag-udyok ng tiyak na reaksyon mula sa publiko.
original_explanation: Ang paboritong 'ulam' sa feed ng marami. Ito 'yung mga balita na mas mabilis pang kumalat kaysa sa sahod mo. Usually starts with 'BREAKING:' and ends with you arguing with a relative in the comments section. The reason why you now have to fact-check if the sun will rise tomorrow.
usage_notes: A term popularized globally in the mid-2010s, it's now a staple in discussions about media, politics, and online information.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa pagbabahagi ng mga artikulo na maaaring **fake news**.","translation":"Be careful in sharing articles that could be **fake news**."},{"sentence":"Ang pagkalat ng **fake news** ay isang seryosong problema sa ating lipunan.","translation":"The spread of **fake news** is a serious problem in our society."}]

meaning_filipino: Panahon ng taon na may mataas na temperatura at kadalasang walang ulan; panahon ng tag-araw.
original_explanation: The official season of 'kili-kili power' tests, 3-in-1 coffee that's actually just ice, and electric fan duets. It's when your back becomes a map of the world in sweat stains and your only life goal is to find aircon. Beach season!
usage_notes: The Philippines has two main seasons: tag-init (dry season, roughly March-May) and tag-ulan (rainy season).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pupunta kami sa Boracay ngayong **tag-init**.","translation":"We will go to Boracay this **summer**."},{"sentence":"Napakainit talaga ng panahon kapag **tag-init**.","translation":"The weather is really hot during the **dry season**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghahanap o paghahangad ng isang babaeng nagdadalang-tao sa isang partikular na pagkain o bagay, na pinaniniwalaang makaaapekto sa magiging hitsura o katangian ng sanggol.
original_explanation: This is the Filipina's "Get Out of Jail Free" card during pregnancy. Suddenly want green mangoes with bagoong at 3 AM? Blame it on the **lihi**. Want to see your husband in a ridiculous costume? **Lihi**. It's the culturally accepted explanation for all the weird cravings and whims of an expectant mother, and everyone just has to deal with it.
usage_notes: Often used with the verb "maglihi" (to have pregnancy cravings). The object of the craving is "pinaglilihian".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglilihi si Anna sa maasim na mangga kaya iyon ang laging hinahanap niya.","translation":"Anna is having a **pregnancy craving** for sour mangoes, that's why she's always looking for it."},{"sentence":"Sabi ng matatanda, kung ano ang iyong **lihi**, iyon ang magiging kamukha ng iyong anak.","translation":"The elders say, whatever your **craving** is, that's what your child will resemble."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagdaragdag ng sangkap na maanghang sa isang pagkain o bagay.
original_explanation: To "anghangan" something is to give it a kick. You do this to your ramen, your sisig, or even your life choices. It's the act of adding that extra 'oomph'. "Bes, anghangan mo pa, kulang pa sa drama!"
usage_notes: This is a verb form, specifically an object-focus verb ('-an' suffix), meaning 'to add spice to something'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisabi sa kusinero na **anghangan** pa niya nang kaunti ang Bicol Express.","translation":"Please tell the cook to **make** the Bicol Express a little **spicier**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong masyadong **anghangan** 'yan, hindi kumakain ng maanghang si lola.","translation":"Don't **add too much spice** to that, grandma doesn't eat spicy food."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-usli o paglabas ng isang bagay mula sa kinalalagyan nito, partikular na tumutukoy sa mata.
etymology: From 'luwa' (bulging, protruding). The '-um-' infix indicates a verb.
original_explanation: This is your eyes' reaction when you see the total on your Shopee cart, or when your chismosa neighbor tells you the latest shocking gossip. Your eyes literally go 👀. It’s that cartoonish "eyes popping out of your head" moment, but in real life.
usage_notes: Most commonly used to describe eyes bulging due to shock, anger, or strain.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halos **lumuwa** ang mata ko sa gulat nang makita ko ang presyo.","translation":"My eyes almost **bulged out** in shock when I saw the price."},{"sentence":"**Lumuwa** ang mga mata ng bata sa galit nang agawin ang kanyang laruan.","translation":"The child's eyes **bulged** in anger when his toy was snatched."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga tao, wika, o kultura mula sa rehiyon ng Castile sa Espanya; karaniwang ginagamit bilang kasingkahulugan ng Espanyol.
original_explanation: The formal, almost historical, way of referring to Spaniards or the Spanish language. It’s what your lola called the Spanish friars in stories. Today, if you say you speak 'Kastelyano', you sound like you learned it from a 19th-century textbook, not from watching 'La Casa de Papel'.
usage_notes: Often capitalized. While it specifically means 'Castilian,' in the Philippines it's a common synonym for 'Spanish' in general.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang nobelang Noli Me Tángere ay orihinal na isinulat sa wikang **Kastelyano**.","translation":"The novel Noli Me Tángere was originally written in the **Spanish** language."},{"sentence":"Marami sa ating mga salita ay hiram sa mga **Kastelyano**.","translation":"Many of our words are borrowed from the **Spanish**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan na walang gulo, away, o alitan; tahimik at panatag.
original_explanation: The opposite of EDSA traffic on a Friday payday. It's that feeling you get at the beach with no one else around, or when you finally submit your last report for the quarter. It's the Zen mode we're all chasing. The ultimate #SanaAll.
usage_notes: Used to describe places, situations, or a person's state of mind.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais kong manirahan sa isang **payapa** na lugar.","translation":"I want to live in a **peaceful** place."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paghahanap at pagtuklas ng isang bagay na bago, nawawala, o hindi pa nalalaman.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'tuklas'. It's the action of finding that hidden gem of a coffee shop, or finally figuring out the 'chismis' about your neighbor. It's your personal mission to explore, to find, to know. "Tara, tuklasin natin ang best ukay-ukay sa Baguio!"
usage_notes: Implies an active search or exploration to find something new or hidden.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais ng mga siyentipiko na **tuklasin** ang lunas para sa kanser.","translation":"Scientists want **to discover** the cure for cancer."},{"sentence":"Panahon na para **tuklasin** mo ang iyong mga tunay na talento.","translation":"It's time for you **to discover** your true talents."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halamang ornamental (Coleus scutellarioides) na kilala sa makukulay na dahon nito at ginagamit din bilang halamang gamot.
etymology: The name of the plant, likely from a local Philippine language.
original_explanation: The official plantita/plantito starter pack! Before the Monstera craze, there was Mayana. It's that colorful, low-maintenance plant you see in your lola's garden. It became super trendy during the pandemic because it's easy to grow and looks great on Instagram. Some even use it for traditional remedies, like for bruises or coughs.
usage_notes: Refers to the plant species Coleus, popular in Philippine gardens.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtanim si Nanay ng maraming **mayana** sa aming hardin.","translation":"Mom planted a lot of **Coleus** in our garden."},{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng kulay ng mga dahon ng **mayana** mo.","translation":"The color of your **mayana** leaves is beautiful."}]

translation: to tell on someone; to report (an offense)
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uulat sa isang may kapangyarihan tungkol sa maling ginawa ng ibang tao.
original_explanation: 'Sumbong kita kay mommy!' The ultimate childhood threat. In the office, this is the person who forwards your 'for your eyes only' email to HR. It's the act of tattling or officially reporting someone's wrongdoing. The opposite of keeping a secret.
usage_notes: Can have a negative connotation (tattling) or a neutral/positive one (reporting a crime). Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang matakot **magsumbong** sa guro kung may nang-aapi sa iyo.","translation":"Don't be afraid **to report** to the teacher if someone is bullying you."},{"sentence":"Nag-away ang magkapatid dahil may gustong **magsumbong** sa kanilang nanay.","translation":"The siblings fought because one wanted **to tell on** the other to their mother."}]

translation: a type of plum-like fruit/tree (Terminalia microcarpa)
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng puno na karaniwan sa Pilipinas na nagbubunga ng maliliit at maasim-asim na prutas na kahawig ng sirwelas.
original_explanation: Ito yung pinsan ng duhat at sinigwelas na hindi masyadong sikat. Prutas na makikita mo sa probinsya na masarap isawsaw sa asin. Parang yung underrated friend mo na sobrang cool pala kapag nakilala mo.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa puno at sa bunga nito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Namitas kami ng **kalumpit** sa likod-bahay ni lola.","translation":"We picked **kalumpit** fruits at grandma's backyard."},{"sentence":"Maaasim ang hinog na bunga ng **kalumpit**.","translation":"The ripe fruits of the **kalumpit** are sour."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagsasagawa ng isang aksyon, gawain, o bagay; lumilikha.
original_explanation: The present tense of "to do/make." This is what you say you're doing ("**gumagawa** ng assignment") when you're actually scrolling through TikTok. It's the opposite of "nakatunganga." Also used for "making a way" or being resourceful: "**gumagawa** ng paraan."
usage_notes: Present tense of 'gawa'. Very common and fundamental verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Gumagawa** ako ng report para sa boss ko.","translation":"I am **making** a report for my boss."},{"sentence":"Sila ay **gumagawa** ng paraan upang makatulong sa mga nasalanta ng bagyo.","translation":"They are **finding a way** (lit. making a way) to help the typhoon victims."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang halaga ng salapi na katumbas ng isang produkto, serbisyo, o ari-arian.
original_explanation: 'Yung numerong tinitingnan mo bago ka mag-'add to cart'. Ito 'yung dahilan kung bakit ka nagtatanong ng 'Magkano po?' sa palengke at umaasang may 'tawad' pa. Sa hugot terms, ito 'yung 'halaga' mo na hindi dapat binabarat. Know your worth, bes!
usage_notes: Isang napakakaraniwang salita sa pang-araw-araw na transaksyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumaas na naman ang **presyo** ng gasolina.","translation":"The **price** of gasoline has increased again."},{"sentence":"Ano ang **presyo** ng sapatos na iyon?","translation":"What is the **price** of those shoes?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging makulimlim o madilim dahil sa mga ulap na tumatakip sa araw; kadiliman o kalungkutan.
etymology: From circumfix `ka- -an` + `kulimlim` (overcast, gloomy). The circumfix creates a noun denoting the state or quality of being gloomy.
original_explanation: That gray, gloomy vibe right before a heavy rain, when the sky looks like it's about to have a major "hugot" moment. It's the perfect weather for staying in, drinking coffee, and listening to sad OPM songs. It can also describe a somber mood, like the atmosphere in an office after a round of layoffs.
usage_notes: Refers to the dimness caused by overcast skies, but can also be used metaphorically to describe a sad or somber atmosphere.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dama ang **kakulimliman** sa paligid bago bumuhos ang malakas na ulan.","translation":"The **gloominess** in the surroundings was felt before the heavy rain poured."},{"sentence":"May **kakulimliman** sa kanyang mga mata na nagsasabi ng kanyang kalungkutan.","translation":"There is a **gloominess** in his eyes that tells of his sadness."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paggiba, pagwasak, o pagkuha ng mga bato o lupa mula sa isang bundok o malaking istraktura.
etymology: From `pag-` (verbal noun prefix) + reduplication of the first syllable of the root `ti-` + `tibag` (demolish/erode).
original_explanation: This is what happens to old buildings in Makati to make way for new condos. It's also what happens to a mountain for a quarry. Figuratively, it's the 'demolition job' someone does to your reputation with 'chismis'. 'Ilegal ang **pagtitibag** ng bundok na iyon.'
usage_notes: Refers to large-scale destruction or excavation, either of man-made structures or natural formations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagtitibag** ng lumang gusali ay nagdulot ng matinding alikabok.","translation":"The **demolition** of the old building caused a lot of dust."},{"sentence":"Ipinagbawal ng DENR ang **pagtitibag** sa protektadong lugar.","translation":"The DENR banned **quarrying** in the protected area."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gamot, pagkain, o inumin na nakatutulong sa pagpapalambot ng dumi at nagpapadali sa pagdumi, karaniwang ginagamit para sa mga hirap dumumi.
original_explanation: This is what you take when you're feeling... stuck. After eating way too much at a fiesta or during a long trip with an unfamiliar diet, you might need a little help from a 'pampadumi.' Think papaya, prunes, or that over-the-counter stuff from the pharmacy. It's the 'un-blocker' for your digestive system.
usage_notes: This is a medical or health-related term. 'Dumi' in this context specifically refers to feces.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang papaya ay isang epektibong natural na **pampadumi**.","translation":"Papaya is an effective natural **laxative**."},{"sentence":"Niresetahan siya ng doktor ng **pampadumi** dahil tatlong araw na siyang hindi makarumi.","translation":"The doctor prescribed him a **laxative** because he hasn't been able to defecate for three days."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay o sitwasyon na napakakumplikado, magulo, at mahirap unawain o lutasin.
etymology: From 'salimuot' (tangle, complexity), with the 'sali-' prefix indicating intensity or repetition.
original_explanation: Your love life status on Facebook? "It's complicated." 'Yan ang sali-salimuot. Parang 'yung plot ng K-drama na may amnesia, birth secrets, at nagkapalit na magkapatid. O 'yung pag-commute sa EDSA. Maximum level of gulo.
usage_notes: The repetition 'sali-sali' intensifies the meaning of 'salimuot' (complicated).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **sali-salimuot** na problema ng pamilya ay tila walang katapusan.","translation":"The **intricate** family problem seemed to have no end."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukang kalasin ng mangingisda ang **sali-salimuot** na lambat.","translation":"The fisherman is trying to untangle the **tangled** net."}]

translation: to be surprised; to be startled
meaning_filipino: Ang makaranas ng biglaang pagkabahala, pagtataka, o pagkatakot dahil sa isang di-inaasahang pangyayari.
original_explanation: That mini heart attack you get when someone sneaks up on you, or when your phone bill is way higher than expected. It's the "Ay, butiki!" moment. The adult version is getting a "for compliance" email from HR.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nabigla** ako nang bigla kang sumigaw.","translation":"I **was startled** when you suddenly shouted."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mabibigla** kung manalo tayo sa lotto.","translation":"Don't **be surprised** if we win the lottery."}]

meaning_filipino: Kalagayan ng pagkalito o pagkatuliro, karaniwang sanhi ng isang malakas na tama sa ulo, pagkalasing, o pagkakagulat.
original_explanation: That feeling when you wake up from a deep nap and don't know what year it is. Or after a long night out and your brain is still buffering. It's the 'loading... please wait' screen of the human mind. You're not drunk anymore, you're just... bangenge.
usage_notes: Can be caused by a physical blow, intoxication, lack of sleep, or shock.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naiwang **bangenge** ang boksingero matapos ang malakas na suntok.","translation":"The boxer was left **dazed** after the powerful punch."},{"sentence":"Gising na ako pero **bangenge** pa rin ang diwa ko dahil sa puyat.","translation":"I'm awake but my mind is still **groggy** from lack of sleep."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking lalagyan, karaniwang gawa sa metal o plastik, na ginagamit para sa pag-iimbak ng tubig.
original_explanation: Ang best friend ng bawat Pinoy tuwing may water interruption. Pag puno 'to, may kapayapaan sa bahay. Pag walang laman, aawayin ka ni nanay kasi hindi ka nag-ipon ng tubig.
usage_notes: Ang katumbas nito sa Filipino ay 'tangke ng tubig'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating linisin ang **watertank** bago dumating ang tag-ulan.","translation":"We need to clean the **water tank** before the rainy season arrives."},{"sentence":"Punuin mo ang mga **watertank** dahil may anunsyo ng water interruption.","translation":"Fill up the **water tanks** because there's an announcement of a water interruption."}]

translation: act of making a hole; perforation
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o kilos ng paglikha ng butas sa isang bagay.
etymology: From pag- (gerund prefix) + reduplication of the first syllable of the root (bu-) + butas (hole).
original_explanation: Literally 'the making of a hole.' Whether it's your dad with a power drill, getting your ears pierced at the mall, or what happens to your budget during a 12.12 sale. If there's a new opening where there wasn't one before, that's pagbubutas.
usage_notes: The pag- + reduplication form implies a continuous or professional action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagbubutas** ng kalsada ay nagdulot ng matinding trapiko.","translation":"The **drilling** of the road caused heavy traffic."},{"sentence":"Mahirap ang **pagbubutas** sa makapal na pader na ito.","translation":"The **act of making a hole** in this thick wall is difficult."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang likidong kemikal na ginagamit upang tunawin ang pintura; maaari ding tumukoy sa isang uri ng matapang na inuming nakalalasing.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "aguarrás", na ang orihinal na kahulugan ay 'turpentine', ngunit nagbago ang kahulugan sa Pilipinas upang tumukoy sa pulot-tubo.
original_explanation: The double-agent of liquids. It's either used by your Tito Boy to thin out paint for the house renovation, OR it’s the mystery moonshine he’s drinking that could probably also thin out paint. Use with caution, whether for painting or partying.
usage_notes: Ang orihinal na salitang Espanyol na "aguarrás" ay nangangahulugang 'turpentine', ngunit ang kahulugan nito sa Tagalog ay tumutukoy sa 'molasses' at iba sa "pulot-pukyutan" (honey).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit ka ng **agwaras** para linisin ang mga brush ng pintura.","translation":"Use **paint thinner** to clean the paint brushes."},{"sentence":"Matapang daw ang **agwaras** na tinitinda sa kanilang probinsya.","translation":"They say the local liquor sold in their province is strong."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkalat o pag-alpas ng matinding bango o samyo, karaniwan mula sa mga bulaklak, pabango, o nilulutong pagkain.
original_explanation: That amazing smell that hits you when you walk past a bakeshop, a sampaguita vendor, or your crush wearing their favorite pabango. It's not just a scent (amoy), it's a glorious, spreading fragrance. The opposite of the smell of durian in a closed room.
usage_notes: Used to describe a strong, pleasant, and spreading aroma.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **halibuyak** ng mga bulaklak sa hardin ay umaabot hanggang sa loob ng bahay.","translation":"The **fragrance** of the flowers in the garden reaches inside the house."},{"sentence":"Naalala ko ang lola ko sa **halibuyak** ng kanyang nilulutong adobo.","translation":"I remember my grandmother through the **aroma** of the adobo she used to cook."}]

translation: able to cut; causing a break
meaning_filipino: May kakayahang maghiwa, maghati, o magputol ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: Describes anything that can cut you off. A sharp knife, for example. Or 'yung mabagal na internet connection na nakapuputol ng momentum mo sa work. Or 'yung chismosa na nakapuputol ng usapan niyo para mag-share ng "breaking news".
usage_notes: The 'nakapu-' prefix here implies an ability or potential to cut. It's not just "cut" (putol), but "capable of cutting".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa bubog na iyan, **nakapuputol** ng paa.","translation":"Be careful with that shard of glass, it's **able to cut** feet."},{"sentence":"Ang biglaang pagkawala ng kuryente ay **nakapuputol** ng daloy ng trabaho.","translation":"The sudden power outage is **causing a break** in the workflow."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang alternatibong pagbaybay para sa 'bangus', ang pambansang isda ng Pilipinas (Chanos chanos).
original_explanation: This is basically a typo or an old-school/regional spelling of 'bangus'. If someone says 'bangos', they mean the bony, delicious national fish. Just think 'bangus'.
usage_notes: Ang 'bangus' ang pamantayan at mas karaniwang pagbaybay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng **bangos** sa palengke para sa hapunan.","translation":"Mom bought **milkfish** at the market for dinner."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan na may sandalan at karaniwang apat na paa, na ginagamit para sa pag-upo ng isang tao.
original_explanation: The throne of every Filipino household, from the monobloc plastic kind sa handaan to the fancy wooden one na bawal upuan. Kung saan ka nakaupo kapag naghihintay ka ng sahod o ng chat mula sa kanya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiabot ng isang **silya** para sa ating bisita.","translation":"Please get a **chair** for our guest."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong itungtong ang paa mo sa **silya**.","translation":"Don't put your feet on the **chair**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sining, hanapbuhay, o gawain ng isang karpintero; paggawa o pag-aayos ng mga bagay na yari sa kahoy.
etymology: From `pagka-` (denoting profession or state) + `karpintero` (carpenter), which is from Spanish `carpintero`.
original_explanation: The OG DIY. Before there were YouTube tutorials and IKEA flat-packs, there was just good old `pagkakarpinteriya`. It's the skill of turning wood into something useful, like a chair, a table, or a cabinet for all the stuff you bought online. It's a legit profession, not just a weekend hobby.
usage_notes: `Pagka-` is used to form nouns denoting profession or abstract quality, like `pagka-doktor` (being a doctor).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkakarpinteriya** ay isang marangal na trabaho.","translation":"**Carpentry** is a noble job."},{"sentence":"Natuto siya ng **pagkakarpinteriya** mula sa kanyang lolo.","translation":"He learned **carpentry** from his grandfather."}]

translation: to match, to suit, to adapt
meaning_filipino: Gawing angkop, akma, o tama para sa isang partikular na sitwasyon, tao, o layunin.
etymology: From the prefix 'i-' (causative verb marker) and 'bagay' (suitable, appropriate).
original_explanation: Like choosing the perfect filter for your IG post. It's not just about looking good, it's about making sure the vibe *matches*. 'Di lahat ng bagay, pwedeng ipilit. Kailangan **ibagay** mo sa sitwasyon, parang OOTD mo sa weather. It's about finding the right fit, whether for clothes, attitude, or jowa.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of fashion, design, behavior, or social interaction, implying a need for harmony or appropriateness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **ibagay** ang iyong pananamit sa okasyon.","translation":"You need to **match** your clothes to the occasion."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang **ibagay** ang kanyang sarili sa bagong grupo ng mga kaibigan.","translation":"She is trying to **adapt** herself to the new group of friends."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kumikilos bilang kinatawan o tagapamagitan para sa iba sa isang transaksyong pangnegosyo o legal.
original_explanation: The person who's always 'just checking in.' They could be selling you a condo you can't afford, insurance for your imaginary future, or a memorial plan when you're just 25. They're the masters of the follow-up call and the friendly 'Kamusta ka na, bes?' that ends with a sales pitch.
usage_notes: Can refer to a real estate agent, insurance agent, sales agent, or even a government/secret agent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinausap kami ng isang **ahente** ng real estate tungkol sa bagong condominium.","translation":"A real estate **agent** talked to us about the new condominium."},{"sentence":"Ang **ahente** ng gobyerno ay nag-iimbestiga sa kaso.","translation":"The government **agent** is investigating the case."}]

meaning_filipino: Nang walang bayad; libre.
original_explanation: The magic word. 'Pag narinig mo 'to, ibig sabihin, wala kang babayaran. "Libre" in a slightly more formal, almost Spanish-sounding way. "Buy one take one, so 'yung isa, gratis na!"
usage_notes: Madalas na ipinagpapalit sa salitang "libre".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Gratis** ang unang baso ng inumin para sa lahat ng bisita.","translation":"The first glass of drink is **free** for all guests."},{"sentence":"Nag-aalok sila ng **gratis** na konsultasyon sa mga bagong kliyente.","translation":"They offer **gratis** consultation to new clients."}]

translation: to urinate involuntarily; to wet oneself
meaning_filipino: Hindi sinasadyang mailabas ang ihi, kadalasan dahil sa matinding takot, tawa, o hirap sa pagpipigil.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'tatawa na sana ako kaso baka...' moment. It's what happens when your friend tells a joke that's too funny, or when a horror movie jump scare is too effective. It's an involuntary bathroom break you didn't sign up for.
usage_notes: Often used hyperbolically in a humorous or embarrassing context to describe extreme laughter or fear.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halos **mapaihi** siya sa kakatawa sa mga biro ng komedyante.","translation":"She almost **wet herself** from laughing so hard at the comedian's jokes."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa sasakyan, ito ang mekanismo para magpalit ng gear. Tumutukoy din ito sa sukli o baryang ibinabalik sa isang transaksyon ng pagbabayad.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'cambio', na nangangahulugang "pagbabago" o "pagpapalit".
original_explanation: Two meanings, one word. 1) Sa sasakyan, ito 'yung stick na parang joystick ng buhay mo sa traffic—'prima, segunda, tersera, atras!' Ito ang dahilan kung bakit masakit sa kaliwang paa ang EDSA. 2) Sa bayaran, ito 'yung hinihintay mong barya mula sa ₱1000 mo para sa isang C2. "Keep the change" is a myth; we need the kambyo for pamasahe.
usage_notes: Karaniwan sa dalawang magkaibang konteksto: pagmamaneho ng de-kambyo na sasakyan at sa mga transaksyong may kinalaman sa pera.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahirapan akong paganahin ang **kambyo** ng lumang kotse.","translation":"I had a hard time operating the **gear shift** of the old car."},{"sentence":"Itago mo ang **kambyo** para may pambayad tayo sa tricycle mamaya.","translation":"Keep the **change** so we have money to pay the tricycle later."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbabago, pagwawasto, o pag-aayos ng isang bagay (tulad ng teksto, larawan, o video) na naganap na.
original_explanation: 'Yung picture niyo sa beach na tinanggal mo 'yung basurahan sa background. O 'yung resume mo na dinagdagan mo ng "proficient in Microsoft Excel" kahit alam mo lang mag-add ng column. You nag-edit. It's the magic that turns a "meh" photo into an "IG-worthy" post.
usage_notes: A Tagalized verb in the past tense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **nag-edit** ng video para sa aming presentasyon.","translation":"He was the one who **edited** the video for our presentation."},{"sentence":"**Nag-edit** ako ng caption ng post ko kasi may mali akong spelling.","translation":"I **edited** the caption of my post because I had a wrong spelling."}]

translation: to mark, to note down, to remember
meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng marka o palatandaan ang isang bagay; isulat o ilista upang hindi makalimutan; isaisip nang mabuti.
etymology: From i- (causative verb prefix) + tanda (mark, sign, memory).
original_explanation: This is what you do when your crush says something important, and you mentally save it for future reference. "Itanda mo sa bato!" (Mark it on stone!) is the OG way of saying "screenshotting this for later." It's also what your nanay tells you to do with her instructions para hindi mo makalimutan bumili ng suka sa tindahan.
usage_notes: Can mean both physically marking something (like on a calendar) and mentally noting something to remember it.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Itanda** mo sa kalendaryo ang araw ng ating anibersaryo.","translation":"**Mark** the day of our anniversary on the calendar."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **itanda** sa isip mo ang lahat ng bilin niya.","translation":"You need to **keep in mind** all of her instructions."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang likas o natatanging kakayahan, husay, o abilidad sa isang partikular na larangan, tulad ng sining, musika, o palakasan.
original_explanation: Your 'special skills' section on your resume, but make it Pinoy. It's what you show off during the office Christmas party talent show or what your parents brag about to their friends ('May talento sa pagkanta ang anak ko!'). It's your 'God-given gift' that you hopefully use for more than just karaoke.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinamalas ni Sarah Geronimo ang kanyang **talento** sa pag-awit at pagsayaw.","translation":"Sarah Geronimo showcased her **talent** in singing and dancing."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong itago ang iyong **talento**; ibahagi mo ito sa mundo.","translation":"Don't hide your **talent**; share it with the world."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkuha o pag-ani ng bulaklak o bunga mula sa tangkay o puno nito gamit ang mga daliri.
original_explanation: The command form of 'pitas'. Ito 'yung sasabihin ng nanay mo, "Paki-pitasin mo nga 'yung mga sampagita sa hardin." Or when you see a really good-looking mango, you tell yourself, "Kailangan kong pitasin 'yan."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pitasin** mo na ang mga hinog na mangga sa likod-bahay.","translation":"**Pick** the ripe mangoes in the backyard now."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan isinasagawa ang pagkakarga at pagbababa ng mga kargamento.
original_explanation: 'Yung "Loading/Unloading Zone" sign na nakikita mo. 'Yan ang kargahan. Sa airport, ito 'yung lugar kung saan nilalagay 'yung mga maleta niyo sa eroplano. Sa pier, dito dinadala 'yung mga container van.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa isang lokasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit na ipinagbabawal ang pagparada sa **kargahan**.","translation":"Parking in the **loading area** is strictly prohibited."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng saging na karaniwang ginagamit sa pagluluto, tulad ng saging na saba. Maaari rin itong tumukoy sa hibla na nakukuha mula sa halamang ito.
original_explanation: This is a less common, more regional term for the saging na saba – the OG banana for banana cue, turon, and maruya. If someone from a specific province offers you '**bayas**', they're likely handing you a saba banana, not some exotic, unheard-of fruit. It's a "you say 'saba', I say '**bayas**'" situation.
usage_notes: Ang terminong ito ay hindi malawakang ginagamit sa Maynila at mas karaniwan sa ilang mga lalawigan, lalo na sa rehiyon ng Visayas. Ang 'saging na saba' ay ang mas karaniwang termino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap gawing minatamis ang saging na **bayas**.","translation":"The **saba banana** is delicious when made into a sweet preserve."},{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng isang piling na **bayas** sa palengke.","translation":"Mother bought a bunch of **saba bananas** at the market."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kondisyon ng paglalakad o pagsasagawa ng iba pang aktibidad habang nasa estado ng pagtulog. Ito ay isang varyant ng "somnambulismo".
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "sonambulismo". Ito ay isang varyant sa pagbaybay ng "somnambulismo".
original_explanation: Same as 'somnambulismo,' but this spelling is closer to the Spanish original. It's the "sosi" way of saying someone is sleepwalking. You'd probably see this in a medical journal or a very formal text rather than hear it at the palengke.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang hindi gaanong karaniwang varyant sa pagbaybay ng "somnambulismo" sa Tagalog, bagaman ito ang tamang baybay sa Espanyol. Karamihan sa mga Pilipino ay gagamitin ang salitang Ingles na "sleepwalking" sa pag-uusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-aaral tungkol sa **sonambulismo** ay sakop ng sikolohiya.","translation":"The study of **somnambulism** is covered by psychology."},{"sentence":"May mga kaso ng **sonambulismo** na nauugnay sa matinding stress.","translation":"There are cases of **somnambulism** linked to extreme stress."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng aswang o nilalang sa mitolohiyang Pilipino na sinasabing sumisipsip ng dugo ng tao, lalo na ng mga sanggol sa sinapupunan.
etymology: From 'dugo' (blood) with the prefix 'man-' and the infix '-ru-' (a form of reduplication indicating a profession or habit). Literally 'one who deals with blood.'
original_explanation: The 'mandurugo' is the original Filipino vampire, but way creepier. Forget sparkling vampires; this one might be your quiet neighbor by day who detaches their body at night to suck the blood of unborn babies through a long, proboscis-like tongue. It’s the reason your lola tells you to put garlic on the windows.
usage_notes: A specific creature in Philippine folklore, often used interchangeably with 'aswang' in general conversation, though it has a specific function (blood-sucking).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kuwento ng matatanda, may **mandurugo** na umaaligid sa baryo tuwing kabilugan ng buwan.","translation":"According to the elders, a **bloodsucker** roams the village during a full moon."},{"sentence":"Natakot ang buntis dahil sa mga bulung-bulungan tungkol sa **mandurugo**.","translation":"The pregnant woman was scared because of the rumors about the **bloodsucker**."}]

translation: to be used up, to be consumed, to run out of
meaning_filipino: Ang tuluyang pagkawala o pagkaunti ng isang bagay hanggang sa wala nang matira.
etymology: From ma- (involuntary/process prefix) + ubos (consumed, used up).
original_explanation: The tragedy that happens to your mobile data 3 days after you subscribe. It's when the ulam is gone but there's still a mountain of rice. It's the state of zero-balance for anything: food, money, patience, load. 'Naubos na pasensya ko sa'yo!' is a national anthem.
usage_notes: Extremely common verb used for a wide range of things that can be depleted.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-withdraw ka na, baka **maubos** ang cash mo.","translation":"You should withdraw now, your cash might **run out**."},{"sentence":"Ang bilis **maubos** ng pagkain kapag may bisita.","translation":"The food gets **consumed** so quickly when there are guests."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hintaying **maubos** ang pasensya ko.","translation":"Don't wait for my patience to **be used up**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang puwang o agwat sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang mga bagay, tao, o lugar. Tumutukoy din ito sa agwat ng panahon.
original_explanation: The "it's complicated" status between two people. It's the physical distance when you're in a fight, the awkward silence in a conversation, or the space you leave for Jesus on the dance floor. It's the gap, the in-between, the "may namamagitan ba sa inyo?"
usage_notes: Can refer to physical space, time, or relationships.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagyan mo ng **pagitan** ang mga halaman para lumago sila nang maayos.","translation":"Put a **space between** the plants so they can grow properly."},{"sentence":"May lamat na sa **pagitan** ng kanilang pagkakaibigan.","translation":"There's a rift in the **gap** of their friendship."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdaan nang mabilis na may kasamang mahinang tunog tulad ng hangin o isang mabilis na bagay; maaari ding tumukoy sa pagkalat ng isang balita o tsismis.
original_explanation: 'Yung bala na dumaan sa pelikula, may sound effect na *swoosh*. That's *haging*. Pwede rin sa chismis, 'yung "may **humaging** na balita sa akin" means may nakarating na juicy info sa'yo, parang dumaan lang sa hangin.
usage_notes: Can refer to both a physical sound of something passing quickly and the spread of a rumor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Humaging** ang bala malapit sa kanyang tainga.","translation":"The bullet **whizzed** past his ear."},{"sentence":"**Humaging** sa buong opisina ang balitang magkakaroon ng bonus.","translation":"The news that there would be a bonus **was rumored** throughout the office."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangunahing harapan ng isang gusali; ang unang pahina o pabalat ng isang aklat, magasin, o publikasyon.
original_explanation: Basically, the 'cover photo' of a building or a magazine. It's the first thing you see, the part that's supposed to impress you and make you say 'wow'. In relationship terms, ito 'yung 'best foot forward' look mo on the first date.
usage_notes: Can refer to the architectural facade of a building or the cover of a publication.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakaganda ng **pultada** ng lumang simbahan sa aming bayan.","translation":"The **facade** of the old church in our town is very beautiful."},{"sentence":"Siya ang nasa **pultada** ng sikat na magasin ngayong buwan.","translation":"She is on the **cover** of the popular magazine this month."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng pagiging hindi namamatay o pagkakaroon ng buhay na walang hanggan.
original_explanation: That thing vampires, gods, and cockroaches are. They just don't die. Also, how some politicians seem to be—they're always there, election after election. In pop culture, it's the goal of every supervillain and the curse of every tragic hero.
usage_notes: The native Tagalog equivalent "walang kamatayan" is more commonly used in everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naniniwala sila na ang mga diyos at diyosa sa mitolohiya ay **inmortal**.","translation":"They believe that the gods and goddesses in mythology are **immortal**."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-ibig ng ina ay sinasabing **inmortal** at walang kapantay.","translation":"A mother's love is said to be **immortal** and unparalleled."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kabuuan ng mga nasusulat na akda, lalo na ang mga itinuturing na may mataas na kalidad sa sining at kaisipan.
original_explanation: This is the formal word for all the stories, poems, and essays you had to read in school. It's the collection of all the 'hugot', 'marites', and 'sana all' moments of a culture, written down beautifully. The English equivalent is 'literature,' but 'literatura' just sounds more dramatic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayaman ang Pilipinas sa **literatura** na nakasulat sa iba't ibang wika.","translation":"The Philippines is rich in **literature** written in various languages."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan namin ang **literatura** ng Timog-Silangang Asya.","translation":"We are studying the **literature** of Southeast Asia."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marahas na pagyupi o paglukot ng isang bagay, tulad ng papel, gamit ang kamay.
original_explanation: That aggressive crumpling of paper after you fail an exam or get a frustrating email. It's not just folding; it's an angry, forceful scrunching into a tight ball. The physical manifestation of 'Ugh, I give up!' The verb form is 'lamukusin'.
usage_notes: The noun 'lamukos' refers to the act, while the verb 'lamukusin' means 'to crumple'. 'Nilamukos' is the past tense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **lamukos** lang ang ginawa niya sa sulat at itinapon ito sa basura.","translation":"He gave the letter just one **crumple** and threw it in the trash."},{"sentence":"Galit niyang **nilamukos** ang test paper na may bagsak na marka.","translation":"He angrily **crumpled** the test paper with a failing grade."}]

meaning_filipino: Opisyal na idineklara o ipinahayag sa publiko.
original_explanation: Parang sa eleksyon, after ng bilangan at matinding stress, ito na yung moment of truth. Kapag proklamado ka na, official ka nang nanalo. Pwede ring self-proklamado, tulad ng pagdeklara mo sa sarili mo bilang "Tita of the Year" dahil nagdala ka ng lumpia sa party.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng eleksyon, batas, o opisyal na anunsyo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Opisyal nang **proklamado** ang mga nanalong senador.","translation":"The winning senators have been officially **proclaimed**."},{"sentence":"Siya ay isang self-**proklamado** na hari ng social media.","translation":"He is a self-**proclaimed** king of social media."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang aklat o koleksyon, karaniwang may blangkong mga pahina, para sa pag-iipon ng mga larawan, selyo, lagda, o iba pang mga memorabilia. Maaari rin itong tumukoy sa isang koleksyon ng mga rekording ng musika.
original_explanation: Before Instagram and cloud storage, this was the original 'photo dump'. It's that thick, dusty book your mom pulls out to show your baby pictures to visitors. Also, what your favorite K-Pop group releases that you spend your sahod on, complete with a photocard you'd trade your left kidney for.
usage_notes: Used for both photo albums and music albums. The context usually makes the meaning clear.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno na ang **album** ng mga litrato mula sa aming bakasyon sa Palawan.","translation":"The **album** is full of photos from our vacation in Palawan."},{"sentence":"Inaabangan ng mga tagahanga ang bagong **album** ng kanilang paboritong banda.","translation":"The fans are waiting for the new **album** of their favorite band."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng manipis na telang koton na may makulay at nakaimprentang disenyo, karaniwang bulaklakin.
original_explanation: Isipin mo 'yung kurtina o punda sa bahay ng lola mo na puro bulaklak ang design. 'Yung tela na parang pang-lumang bestida. 'Yun ang sitsa. Bago pa nauso ang minimalist aesthetic, #SitsaCore muna. Vintage vibes!
usage_notes: Isang lumang salita na hindi na gaanong ginagamit sa kasalukuyan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang bestida ay yari sa makulay na **sitsa**.","translation":"Her dress was made of colorful **chintz**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng labis na pagmamataas, pagpapakita, o paghahambog sa sarili, kaalaman, o ari-arian.
original_explanation: The "Sana all" in reverse. Ito yung ugali ng kakilala mong laging nagpo-post ng "blessed" with matching picture ng bagong kotse, condo, or LV bag. Hindi masamang maging proud, pero 'pag sobra na, yabang na 'yan. The line is thinner than your patience during a traffic jam.
usage_notes: Can function as a noun (e.g., "Puno ng yabang") or an adjective (e.g., "Huwag kang yabang"). The adjective form is often "mayabang".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi maganda ang sobrang **yabang** sa katawan.","translation":"Too much **arrogance** is not good."},{"sentence":"Puro **yabang** lang pala ang alam niya, wala namang maipakita.","translation":"He's just full of **boastfulness**, but has nothing to show for it."}]

meaning_filipino: Iwasto ang isang pagkakamali; gawing tama o tuwid ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: What your teacher does to your test paper with a red pen. Or in hugot terms, 'Sana lahat ng pagkakamali, kayang itama.' (I wish all mistakes could be corrected.) It's the act of fixing an error, whether it's a typo or a past regret.
usage_notes: An object-focus verb where the mistake or error being fixed is the focus.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang **itama** ang lahat ng kanyang mga pagkakamali sa nakaraan.","translation":"He is trying to **correct** all his past mistakes."},{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **itama** mo ang spelling ng pangalan ko sa dokumento.","translation":"Please **correct** the spelling of my name on the document."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal para sa 'alternatibo' o 'pamalit', karaniwang tumutukoy sa isang alternatibong istilo, musika, o pananaw.
original_explanation: Short for 'alternative'. If you're not into mainstream pop and you listen to bands your friends have never heard of, you're probably into 'alt' music. It’s the edgy, non-conformist sibling of the mainstream. In gaming, it's your second character or 'alternate'. On social media, it's your 'other' account where you post your real, unfiltered thoughts (see also: 'alter').
usage_notes: Isang salitang balbal na popular sa mga kabataan at sa online communities.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang makinig sa mga **alt** rock band noong dekada '90.","translation":"He loves listening to **alt** rock bands from the '90s."},{"sentence":"Gagamitin ko ang **alt** account ko para mag-comment.","translation":"I'll use my **alt** account to comment."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o gawain na naging pangkaraniwan o nakasanayan na dahil sa paulit-ulit na karanasan.
etymology: From the root word `bihasa` (skilled, accustomed), via `mamihasa` (to get used to). The `kina-an` affixation denotes the thing or situation one has become accustomed to.
original_explanation: This is when "practice makes permanent." It's that thing you do automatically without thinking. Like navigating the EDSA bus carousel like a pro, ordering your go-to milk tea combo, or expertly dodging chismis from your tita. It's a habit that's been so deeply ingrained, it's now part of your system. You didn't just get used to it; you kinapamihasnan it.
usage_notes: A more formal and deeper version of "nakasanayan". It implies a long period of habituation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang hirap ng buhay sa siyudad ay **kinapamihasnan** na niya.","translation":"He has **become accustomed to** the hardship of life in the city."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa araw-araw na pag-eensayo, **kinapamihasnan** na ng atleta ang sakit ng katawan.","translation":"Because of daily training, the athlete has **gotten used to** the body aches."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng malalim na pag-iisip, pagmumuni-muni, o pagbubulay-bulay sa isang bagay o ideya.
original_explanation: ‘Yung moment na nakatitig ka lang sa kawalan, nag-iisip kung magre-reply ba si crush o kung ano ulam mamaya. It's your brain going into deep-dive mode, analyzing everything from your life choices to the latest chismis. Basically, overthinking level 99.
usage_notes: Often implies a solitary and deep thought process, distinct from simple thinking.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa kanyang **pagkukuro**, napagtanto niyang kailangan na niyang magbago ng landas sa buhay.","translation":"In his **contemplation**, he realized he needed to change his path in life."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pag-aalanganin, kawalan ng katiyakan, o pagdududa tungkol sa isang bagay na gagawin o desisyon.
etymology: From the nominalizing prefix 'pag-a-' + the reduplicated root 'agam-agam'.
original_explanation: This is the feeling you get when you're about to send a risky text. It's the 'Should I or shouldn't I?' playing on a loop in your head. It's that moment of hesitation before you click 'Add to Cart' on something you know you can't afford. It's a mental tug-of-war.
usage_notes: The root 'agam-agam' is a reduplication, which emphasizes the uncertainty. The prefix 'pag-a-' nominalizes it into the act or feeling of hesitation. It's a more formal and literary word than 'duda' or 'alinlangan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kitang-kita sa kanyang mukha ang **pag-aagam-agam** bago siya sumagot.","translation":"The **hesitation** was clearly visible on his face before he answered."},{"sentence":"Walang anumang **pag-aagam-agam** siyang tumalon sa tubig upang iligtas ang bata.","translation":"Without any **hesitation**, he jumped into the water to save the child."}]

translation: to lower; to bring down; to drop off (a passenger)
meaning_filipino: Ilagay sa mas mababang posisyon o lugar; ihatid at ibaba ang isang pasahero mula sa sasakyan.
original_explanation: What you yell at the jeepney driver when you're about to miss your stop: 'Manong, para! Dito na po ako magbababa!' Also, what happens to your standards when you're desperate to find a date.
usage_notes: Commonly used in the context of transportation for dropping off passengers. Can also mean to lower an object or a price ('magbaba ng presyo').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **magbaba** po kayo sa tamang sakayan at babaan.","translation":"Please, **get off** at the designated loading and unloading zones."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng sunod-sunod na pag-ikot o pagbaligtad ng katawan, karaniwang ginagawa bilang isang ehersisyo, paglalaro, o pagpapakitang-gilas.
etymology: From Spanish 'circo' (circus), referring to circus acrobatics. The reduplication implies a repeated or playful action.
original_explanation: Imagine a kid high on sugar at a Jollibee party, or a gymnast during their floor routine. That's `sumirko-sirko`. It's also a metaphor for doing everything you can to please someone, like a politician during campaign season. 'Gagawin ko ang lahat, kahit mag-sirko-sirko pa ako!'
usage_notes: The reduplication `sirko-sirko` emphasizes the repetitive or continuous nature of the tumbling. The un-reduplicated form `sumirko` (to do a somersault) is also common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **sumirko-sirko** ang bata sa damuhan dahil sa tuwa.","translation":"The child started to **do somersaults** on the grass out of joy."},{"sentence":"Kahit **sumirko-sirko** ka pa sa harap niya, hindi ka pa rin niya papansinin.","translation":"Even if you **do somersaults** in front of him/her, they still won't notice you."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng takip sa ulo na karaniwang gawa sa tela, isinusuot ng mga sanggol o bilang bahagi ng isang uniporme.
original_explanation: That cute little hat your mom forced you to wear as a baby for your baptismal pictures. Nowadays, it’s what you wear to hide a bad hair day or when you're too lazy to fix your hair for a quick run to the convenience store.
usage_notes: Less common than "sumbrero" or "cap". Often refers specifically to a soft cap, like a baby's bonnet or a chef's hat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang cute ng sanggol sa suot niyang puting **bunete**.","translation":"The baby is cute in his white **bonnet**."}]

meaning_filipino: Matinding pananabik o pagnanais na makabalik na sa sariling tahanan o bayan.
etymology: A phrase composed of 'sabik' (eager), 'sa' (to/for), and 'pag-uwi' (the act of going home).
original_explanation: The official feeling of every OFW, seaman, or anyone stuck in EDSA traffic at 8 PM on a Friday. It's that deep longing for your own bed, your family, and home-cooked meals. This phrase is pure 'homesick' energy.
usage_notes: A common set phrase. The object of eagerness can be changed, e.g., 'sabik sa pagkain' (eager for food), 'sabik sa iyo' (longing for you).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matapos ang isang taon sa abroad, siya ay **sabik na sabik sa pag-uwi**.","translation":"After a year abroad, she was **very eager to go home**."},{"sentence":"Kahit pagod sa trabaho, ang mga manggagawa ay laging **sabik sa pag-uwi**.","translation":"Even if tired from work, workers are always **eager to go home**."}]

translation: to reduce; to lessen; to subtract
meaning_filipino: Alisin ang isang bahagi mula sa isang kabuuan; bawasan ang dami, bilang, o sukat.
original_explanation: This is your New Year's resolution to 'lose weight' (magbawas ng timbang), your tita telling you to 'lessen your rice intake' (magbawas ng kanin), or what you have to do with your expenses when it's 'petsa de peligro' week. It's the universal adulting verb.
usage_notes: Can be used for tangible things (weight, food) and intangible concepts (expenses, workload).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **magbawas** ng gastos dahil malapit na ang bayaran ng matrikula.","translation":"I need to **reduce** my expenses because the tuition fee payment is near."},{"sentence":"Pinayuhan siya ng doktor na **magbawas** ng pagkain ng matatamis.","translation":"The doctor advised him to **lessen** his intake of sweets."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng lupa na malagkit kapag basa at tumitigas kapag tuyo, karaniwang ginagamit sa paggawa ng palayok at iba pang seramika.
original_explanation: The OG Play-Doh. Before slime kits and kinetic sand, there was luwad. It's the stuff used to make palayok (clay pots) that give dishes like sinigang a special, earthy taste. It’s messy, it’s earthy, and it's the foundation of some of the most iconic Filipino crafts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga banga ay gawa sa **luwad** na hinulma at pinatuyo sa araw.","translation":"The jars are made of **clay** that was molded and dried under the sun."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pananda (*) na ginagamit sa pagsulat o pag-imprenta upang tumukoy sa isang footnote, magpahiwatig ng pag-aalis ng salita, o bigyang-diin ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: The formal, English version of 'asterisko'. You use this when you're writing a formal paper. In conversations, it's the "but..." or "actually..." that comes after a compliment. "You're a great driver... *asterisk* for a beginner."
usage_notes: Used in more formal or English-heavy contexts. 'Asterisko' is more common in everyday Tagalog/Taglish.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagyan mo ng **asterisk** ang mga importanteng detalye sa report.","translation":"Put an **asterisk** on the important details in the report."},{"sentence":"May **asterisk** 'yung promo, ibig sabihin may hidden charges.","translation":"The promo has an **asterisk**, which means there are hidden charges."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kaswal at panandaliang pakikipagtalik na walang kasamang emosyonal na ugnayan o pangmatagalang pangako.
original_explanation: 'Yung akala mo "getting to know" stage, pero "getting to bed" stage lang pala. It's the "Netflix and chill" that actually means Netflix and chill, but then... not just chilling. No strings attached, no label, no problem? 'Yan ang sabi nila.
usage_notes: A very modern, informal term borrowed directly from English, primarily used by younger, urban speakers. It carries the same connotations as in Western culture.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Akala ko date, pero **hookup** lang pala ang hanap niya.","translation":"I thought it was a date, but he was just looking for a **hookup**."},{"sentence":"Hindi ako para sa **hookup** culture, gusto ko ng seryosong relasyon.","translation":"I'm not for the **hookup** culture, I want a serious relationship."}]

meaning_filipino: Alisin ang pagkatali o pagkakabuhol ng isang bagay; luwagan.
original_explanation: What you need to do to your shoelaces after a long day. Or what you wish you could do to your problems. 'Bes, paki-kalagan naman ng buhol sa puso ko.'
usage_notes: The object-focus verb form of 'kalag'. 'Magkalag' is the actor-focus form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**kalagan** mo nga ang tali ng sapatos ko.","translation":"Can you please **untie** my shoelaces?"},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **kalagan** ang mga kamay niyang nakagapos.","translation":"He tried to **untie** his bound hands."}]

translation: A specific type of Filipino grilled chicken (from Iloilo)
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng litsong manok na nagmula sa rehiyon ng Kanlurang Visayas, na ibinababad sa suka, calamansi, tanglad, at atsuete, at inihuhaw sa uling.
etymology: Ang salitang 'inasal' ay Hiligaynon para sa 'inihaw'. Ito ay naasimila sa Tagalog upang partikular na tukuyin ang putaheng ito.
original_explanation: The undisputed king of grilled chicken in the Philippines, hailing from Bacolod. It's that glorious, yellowish-orange chicken swimming in chicken oil over a mountain of rice. It's not just food, it's a 'kain-all-you-can-rice' challenge. The 'pecho' or 'paa' debate is a deep Filipino philosophical dilemma.
usage_notes: Bagaman ang 'inasal' ay teknikal na nangangahulugang 'inihaw' sa ibang diyalekto, sa pangkalahatang gamit sa Pilipinas, ito ay halos palaging tumutukoy sa 'chicken inasal' ng Bacolod.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tara, kumain tayo ng **inasal** na may unli-rice.","translation":"Let's go eat **Inasal** with unlimited rice."},{"sentence":"Kilala ang Bacolod sa masarap nilang manok na **inasal**.","translation":"Bacolod is known for their delicious **Inasal** chicken."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o kilos ng pagkalkula o pagtutuos gamit ang mga numero at operasyong matematikal.
original_explanation: Ito yung ginagawa mo sa sweldo mo pagdating ng a-kinse. Plus sahod, minus utang, minus bills, minus pang-treat sa pamilya... tapos ang ending, minus na rin ang bank account mo. It's just math, but with more feelings involved.
usage_notes: Often used in finance, science, and technology.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mali ang kanyang **komputasyon** kaya kulang ang sukli.","translation":"His **computation** was wrong, that's why the change was short."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang calculator para sa mabilis na **komputasyon**.","translation":"She used a calculator for a quick **computation**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng mamamayan ng Espanya.
original_explanation: The female version of Ispanyol. Think Penelope Cruz or a Flamenco dancer. Siya yung Señora o Señorita sa mga historical dramas na may dalang abaniko at laging may mataray na tingin.
usage_notes: Partikular na tumutukoy sa babaeng mula sa Espanya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang guro namin sa kasaysayan ay isang magandang **Ispanyola**.","translation":"Our history teacher is a beautiful **Spaniard** (female)."}]

translation: fellow adventurer; one who shares the same fate
meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kabahagi sa isang paglalakbay o pakikipagsapalaran; isang indibidwal na kahati sa parehong tadhana o kapalaran.
original_explanation: Your partner in crime, your fellow "bahala na" warrior. 'Yung kasama mong sumubok mag-apply sa BPO kahit 'di niyo alam ang gagawin, or 'yung kaibigan mong sinamahan kang akyatin ang bundok kahit pareho kayong walang experience. You share the same journey, the same "what-ifs," and the same "lagot!" moments.
usage_notes: Often found in literary or dramatic contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang aking naging **kasapalaran** sa paglalakbay sa ibang bansa.","translation":"He became my **fellow adventurer** in traveling to another country."},{"sentence":"Bilang mga **kasapalaran**, sabay nilang hinarap ang mga pagsubok.","translation":"As **partners in fate**, they faced the challenges together."}]

translation: to save; to rescue from danger
meaning_filipino: Iligtas o ipagtanggol mula sa isang panganib, kapahamakan, o kasamaan.
original_explanation: This is a very "Florante at Laura" or "dasal" kind of word. You use this when you're praying to be saved from a difficult exam, a terrible boss, or your 'marites' neighbor. "Lord, ipag-adya niyo po ako sa tukso!" It’s a formal, almost poetic way of saying "save me!"
usage_notes: Highly formal and literary. Rarely used in casual conversation. Common in prayers, poems, and old literature.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Idinadalangin kong **ipag-adya** ka ng Maykapal sa lahat ng masama.","translation":"I pray that the Creator **saves** you from all evil."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **ipag-adya** ang kanyang kaibigan mula sa kapahamakan.","translation":"He tried to **rescue** his friend from harm."}]

translation: to be able to detach or unstick
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang tanggalin ang isang bagay na mahigpit na nakadikit o nakakabit.
original_explanation: Ever tried peeling off an old sticker and it just leaves that annoying white residue? The goal is to 'makatkat' it cleanly. It's the ability to unstick something, like a stubborn label on a jar or your friend from a toxic relationship.
usage_notes: 'Katkat' as a root word is not very common on its own; 'makatkat' is the more frequent form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **makatkat** ko nang buo itong lumang sticker sa laptop ko.","translation":"I hope I can **detach** this old sticker on my laptop completely."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **makatkat** ang tuyong pintura sa sahig.","translation":"It's hard **to unstick** the dried paint from the floor."}]

translation: to get something using a pole
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkuha ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay prutas sa puno, sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng isang mahabang patpat o panungkit.
original_explanation: The official verb of every Filipino kid who's ever tried to get mangoes, santol, or aratiles from a neighbor's tree without climbing. You get a long bamboo pole (`panungkit`), maybe with a hook or a net at the end, and you poke and twist until the fruit falls. It’s a skill, a sport, and a core childhood memory.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to the action of using a pole or hook (`sungkit`) to retrieve an object, usually from a high place.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-aabang ang mga bata sa ibaba habang may **nanunungkit** ng mangga sa puno.","translation":"The children were waiting below while someone was **getting mangoes with a pole** from the tree."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **manungkit** ng bayabas dahil masyado nang mataas ang puno.","translation":"We need to **get guavas using a pole** because the tree is already too high."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi handa; walang anumang palamuti, dekorasyon, o paghahanda.
original_explanation: Showing up to a party in your *pambahay* (house clothes) when everyone else is in formal wear. It's a house with no Christmas decorations in December. It's being caught off-guard, like a surprise quiz you didn't study for. The state of being "as is" when "extra" is expected.
usage_notes: Can refer to a person's state of readiness or the plain appearance of a place or object.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumating ang mga bisita nang **walang-gayak** ang bahay.","translation":"The guests arrived when the house was **unadorned**."},{"sentence":"Nahuli siyang **walang-gayak** sa biglaang pag-uwi ng kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"She was caught **unprepared** by the sudden return of her parents."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na nangangahulugang matinding inasar, nilait, o pinahiya sa paraang nakakatawa o brutal.
etymology: From the English word 'roasted', used in the context of a 'roast' (an event where an individual is subjected to good-natured mockery).
original_explanation: When your friends make fun of you so badly, so accurately, and so hilariously that you have no comeback. You've been **roasted**. Parang lechon, luto ka sa pamba-bara nila. "Grabe, **roasted** si kuya sa comment section!"
usage_notes: A slang term borrowed from English and used frequently in online culture and among friends, synonymous with 'barado' or 'basag'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng talo nila, **roasted** ang buong team sa social media.","translation":"After their loss, the whole team was **roasted** on social media."},{"sentence":"Talagang **roasted** ka sa nanay mo 'pag nalamang 'di ka pumasok.","translation":"You'll really get **roasted** by your mom when she finds out you skipped class."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging mayabang; ang labis na pagmamataas sa sarili at pagmamaliit sa iba.
original_explanation: This is "flexing" gone wrong. It's not just being proud of your achievements; it's rubbing them in everyone's face, usually with a side of condescension. Think of that one officemate who won't shut up about their trip to Europe. That energy? That's kayabangan.
usage_notes: Carries a strong negative connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kayabangan** niya ang dahilan kung bakit iilan lang ang kanyang kaibigan.","translation":"His **arrogance** is the reason why he has few friends."},{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na ang **kayabangan** mo, wala kang mararating diyan.","translation":"Stop your **boastfulness**, you won't get anywhere with that."}]

meaning_filipino: Maglaan o magtabi ng isang bagay o lugar para sa isang partikular na tao o layunin.
original_explanation: It's what you tell your friend to do at your favorite samgyupsal place on a Friday night. "Uy, reserbahan mo na kami ng table, baka maunahan!" It's the act of claiming dibs on something—a seat, a concert ticket, or even a person's time.
usage_notes: The '-han' suffix indicates this is a benefactive verb, meaning the action is done *for* someone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Reserbahan** mo ako ng upuan sa harap, ha?","translation":"**Reserve** a seat for me in the front, okay?"},{"sentence":"Sana all, may **nirereserbahan** ng pag-ibig.","translation":"I wish everyone had someone **reserving** their love for them."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng puno na may bungang nakakain, na may balat na kulay rosas o berde at laman na maputi at matamis na may itim na buto. Ang bunga nito ay tila nakapulupot.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'guamúchil', na galing sa Nahuatl na 'cuamochitl'.
