original_explanation: Ito yung prutas na mukhang alien pod na pinipitas mo sa puno ng kapitbahay nung bata ka. Yung feeling na nag-aagawan kayo sa mga hinog na bunga? Parang cotton candy na may buto sa loob. Nostalgic snack bago pa nauso ang imported fruits.
usage_notes: Maaari ring baybayin bilang 'kamatsile'. Ang siyentipikong pangalan nito ay *Pithecellobium dulce*.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap papakin ang matatamis na **kamatsili** habang nagpapahinga sa ilalim ng puno.","translation":"It's nice to snack on sweet **Manila tamarind** while resting under a tree."},{"sentence":"Maraming puno ng **kamatsili** sa aming probinsya.","translation":"There are many **Manila tamarind** trees in our province."}]

translation: to title; to give a title to
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng pangalan o pamagat sa isang bagay, akda, o tao.
original_explanation: It's the verb form of 'titulo.' This is what you do when you've finished writing your masterpiece (or your term paper) and you need to name it. '**Tituluhan** mo na 'yang kwento mo.' It's also what happens when a queen confers a title upon a knight. You're basically bestowing a name or rank.
usage_notes: Object-focus verb. The past tense is 'tinuluhan' and the present tense is 'tinutuluhan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang naatasang **tituluhan** ang bawat kabanata ng libro.","translation":"He was assigned **to title** each chapter of the book."},{"sentence":"'Ang Huling El Bimbo' ang **tinuluhan** sa sikat na musical.","translation":"The famous musical was **titled** 'Ang Huling El Bimbo'."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang folder sa cloud storage (tulad ng Google Drive) na ibinabahagi sa ibang mga gumagamit, karaniwang naglalaman ng mga file na may temang pang-adulto o pribado.
etymology: English initialism for 'Shared Folder' or 'Story Feature'.
original_explanation: The digital version of "pasahan ng notes," but for... well, you know. It stands for "Shared Folder" (or "Story Feature" on IG), but 99% of the time, it's the modern-day, high-tech version of the forbidden cabinet. "Link?" is the password.
usage_notes: A highly colloquial term used in online chats and social media. Its meaning is heavily context-dependent and often implies adult or private content.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pahingi naman ng link sa **sf** mo.","translation":"Can I have the link to your **sf** (shared folder)?"},{"sentence":"Nag-post siya sa **sf** niya sa IG para sa mga close friends lang.","translation":"She posted on her **sf** (story feature) on IG for close friends only."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaikling salita para sa "nakakakaloka" o "kakakaloka," na nagpapahayag ng pagkabigla, pagka-inis, o pagkamangha sa isang bagay na tila nakababaliw.
etymology: Acronym/abbreviation of "kakakaloka", from the root "loka" (crazy woman) derived from Spanish "loca".
original_explanation: The official text-speak for when something is so unbelievably weird, annoying, or hilarious that it short-circuits your brain. Your friend cancels plans last minute? "kklk". The traffic in EDSA is somehow worse than yesterday? "kklk". You see a meme that's too real? "kklk". It's the ultimate expression of being overwhelmed by the sheer craziness of life, packed into four convenient letters.
usage_notes: Primarily used in text messages and social media. It conveys a mix of frustration, amusement, and disbelief.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Grabe ang pila sa bangko, **kklk**!","translation":"The line at the bank is terrible, it's **driving me crazy**!"},{"sentence":"Napanood mo na ba yung bagong episode? **Kklk** yung plot twist!","translation":"Have you seen the new episode? The plot twist is **so crazy**!"}]

translation: A place of plunder; a den of thieves
meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan nagaganap ang pandarambong o kung saan itinatago ang mga bagay na dinambong.
original_explanation: This is the headquarters for the bad guys, the secret warehouse where they count their loot. It's the villain's lair in a movie, or maybe that sketchy building everyone whispers about. It’s where the 'dambong' is stored.
usage_notes: A very rare word, more likely to be encountered in literature than in conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natunton ng mga awtoridad ang **dambungan** ng mga pirata.","translation":"The authorities tracked down the pirates' **den/hoard**."},{"sentence":"Ang kanilang mansyon ay tila isang **dambungan** ng mga nakaw na yaman.","translation":"Their mansion was like a **hoard** of stolen wealth."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan, karaniwang gawa sa kahoy o plastik, na ginagamit sa pagpulupot o pag-ikid ng sinulid, alambre, o anumang katulad na materyal upang hindi magkabuhol-buhol.
original_explanation: The OG cable organizer. Before cable ties and velcro strips, your lola had an 'ikiran' to keep her sewing thread from turning into a chaotic mess that looks like your life plans. It's the thing you wind yarn onto.
usage_notes: This is an older term, mostly associated with sewing, weaving, or fishing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiabot ng **ikiran** ng sinulid na pula.","translation":"Please hand me the **spool** of red thread."},{"sentence":"Ginagamit din ang **ikiran** para sa pamingwit.","translation":"A **reel** is also used for a fishing rod."}]

translation: state of being cut; severance; disconnection
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging hati, putol, o nahiwalay mula sa isang kabuuan; ang paghinto ng isang koneksyon.
etymology: Mula sa ugat na "putol" (hiwa, tigil). Ang unlaping "pagka-" ay tumutukoy sa estado o kondisyon ng pagiging putol.
original_explanation: 'Yung nawalan ka ng internet connection sa gitna ng online exam or Zoom meeting. That sudden **pagkaputol** is pure panic. Pwede ring sa love life, 'yung bigla ka na lang na-ghost. The **pagkaputol** of communication.
usage_notes: Maaaring literal (isang lubid na naputol) o makasagisag (isang relasyon o serbisyo na naputol).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nireklamo ng mga residente ang madalas na **pagkaputol** ng suplay ng kuryente.","translation":"The residents complained about the frequent **disconnection** of the electricity supply."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkaputol** ng puno ay nagdulot ng matinding trapiko sa kalsada.","translation":"The **state of the tree being cut** (and falling) caused heavy traffic on the road."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng sariling pangalan o marka sa isang dokumento bilang tanda ng pagsang-ayon, pagpapatunay, o pag-ako ng responsibilidad.
original_explanation: That moment of truth when you get your first job offer. "Pirmahan mo na 'yan!" Or when you're applying for a loan and you see the mountain of papers you need to sign. It's the adult version of "drawing a star" on your test paper.
usage_notes: Can also be a noun ('ang pirmahan') meaning a signing event. The context clarifies the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **pirmahan** ang kontrata bago ka magsimula sa trabaho.","translation":"You need **to sign** the contract before you start work."},{"sentence":"Saan ko po dapat **pirmahan** ang resibo?","translation":"Where should I **sign** the receipt?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtaas ng halaga, bilang, o sukat ng isang bagay; karaniwang tumutukoy sa dagdag na sahod.
original_explanation: Ang pinakahihintay ng lahat ng empleyado every year! 'Yung umento sa sahod na parang 'di mo maramdaman dahil sa inflation. 'Pag tinanong ka, "May umento ba?" 'yan ang universal code for "tumaas ba sweldo mo?"
usage_notes: Primarily used to refer to a salary increase.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Humihingi ng **umento** sa sahod ang mga manggagawa.","translation":"The workers are asking for a salary **increase**."},{"sentence":"Magkakaroon daw ng **umento** sa presyo ng gasolina sa susunod na linggo.","translation":"They say there will be an **increase** in the price of gasoline next week."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkapa o paghahanap ng isang bagay sa dilim o kapag hindi makakita, gamit ang mga kamay.
original_explanation: This is you trying to find the light switch in a strange bathroom during a brownout. Or you, trying to find your phone under the blankets at 3 AM. It’s the physical manifestation of "I don't know what I'm doing but I'm doing my best."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawalan ng ilaw kaya **ngumapa-ngapa** siya sa paghahanap ng kandila.","translation":"The power went out so he **groped around** looking for a candle."},{"sentence":"Para siyang bulag na **ngumapa-ngapa** sa dilim.","translation":"He was like a blind person **fumbling** in the dark."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang instrumental na komposisyon sa simula ng isang opera, oratorio, o dula, na kadalasang naglalaman ng mga pangunahing tema ng musika.
original_explanation: It's the musical trailer for a play or opera. Before the main characters start their drama, the orchestra plays the obertura to give you a taste of the feels—the suspense, the romance, the 'iyakan' to come. Think of it as the opening credits music for a major theatrical production.
usage_notes: Primarily used in musical and theatrical contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakaganda ng **obertura** ng opera na aming pinanood.","translation":"The **overture** of the opera we watched was very beautiful."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula ang palabas sa isang madamdaming **obertura**.","translation":"The show began with a dramatic **overture**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbabad o pagbuhos ng buong katawan sa tubig o anumang likido.
etymology: From `pag-` + reduplication of the first syllable of the root `lublob` (`lu-`) + `lublob`.
original_explanation: What you want to do in a tub of cold water after walking under the Manila sun. Pwede ring metaphorical, like 'paglulublob sa kalungkutan'—wallowing in sadness, listening to sadboi music, and re-reading old convos. It's an all-in kind of soaking, literal or emotional.
usage_notes: Implies full immersion, often with a sense of indulgence or desperation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paglulublob** sa malamig na batis ay paborito niyang gawin tuwing tag-init.","translation":"His favorite thing to do during summer is **immersing** himself in the cold spring."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lalaking kasama o kasabay ng isang magulang sa pagiging ninong o ninang sa isang binyag o kasal. Tumutukoy din ito sa matalik na kaibigan o kasama.
original_explanation: Your dad's drinking buddy who is also your godfather. He's the guy who gives you a crisp 100-peso bill on Christmas and calls you 'inaanák'. In modern terms, it's your 'pare' or 'bro' for life, sealed by Catholic rites and celebrated with lots of San Miguel.
usage_notes: The female equivalent is 'kumadre'. The system of relationships formed through this is called the 'compadrazgo system'. A more common colloquial spelling is 'kumpare'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si **kompadre** ang laging kasama ni Tatay sa pag-inom tuwing Sabado.","translation":"My dad's **buddy** is always his drinking companion every Saturday."},{"sentence":"Inimbitahan ko ang aking **kompadre** para sa binyag ng aking anak.","translation":"I invited my **co-sponsor** for my child's baptism."}]

translation: to blame; to find fault with
meaning_filipino: Ang paghahanap ng mali o kapintasan sa isang tao o bagay; ang pagbibigay ng sisi o paninisi.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "sisi" na may hulaping "-hin". Isang varyant ng "sisihin".
original_explanation: 'Yan 'yung ginagawa sa'yo 'pag may nawawala sa bahay. "Ikaw na naman 'di naglagay sa lugar!" Kahit hindi ikaw. Sa office, ito 'yung "blame game" kapag may pumalpak na project. Laging may isang taong sinisisi, at sana hindi ikaw 'yun.
usage_notes: Isang varyant ng mas karaniwang 'sisihin', at mas madalas marinig sa ilang partikular na rehiyon o sa mas matatandang tagapagsalita.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **sistihin** sa pagkakamaling hindi ko ginawa.","translation":"Don't **blame** me for a mistake I didn't make."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na umaalis sa kanyang sariling bansa upang manirahan nang permanente sa ibang bansa.
original_explanation: This is someone on their "leaving the country for good" arc. Unlike an OFW who plans to come back (in theory), an emigrante is packing up their whole life—magic sing, tabo, and all—to start fresh somewhere else. They're the ones you see in tearful airport goodbyes, heading to Canada, Australia, or the US. They are emigrants *from* the Philippines, and immigrants *to* their new country.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with "immigrant" in casual conversation, but "emigrante" specifically refers to the act of *leaving* one's country of origin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming Pilipinong **emigrante** ang naninirahan na ngayon sa Amerika.","translation":"Many Filipino **emigrants** now live in America."},{"sentence":"Bilang isang **emigrante**, hinahanap-hanap pa rin niya ang pagkaing Pilipino.","translation":"As an **emigrant**, he still craves Filipino food."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hindi inaasahan at hindi kanais-nais na pangyayari na nagdudulot ng pinsala, kapahamakan, o kamatayan.
original_explanation: Yung biglaang 'lagot!' moment na may kasamang bangga, sugat, o sira. Pwedeng banggaan ng sasakyan sa EDSA, pagkadulas sa basang sahig, o yung 'aksidente' kang na-in love sa best friend mo. The last one is the most dangerous.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng malubhang **aksidente** sa may kanto kaninang umaga.","translation":"There was a serious **accident** at the corner this morning."},{"sentence":"Ingat sa pagmamaneho para makaiwas sa **aksidente**.","translation":"Drive carefully to avoid an **accident**."}]

translation: to pass the buck; to evade responsibility
meaning_filipino: Isang idyoma na nangangahulugang pagpapasa-pasa ng responsibilidad o sisi sa ibang tao upang makaiwas sa pananagutan.
original_explanation: The ultimate corporate and government strategy. When something goes wrong, you see people magsaluhan ng bola like it's a hot potato. 'It's not my department.' 'Sir, si ano po ang may hawak niyan.' 'I'm just waiting for the email.' It's the national sport of avoiding accountability.
usage_notes: A highly idiomatic phrase. Literally 'to catch the ball for each other,' but it's used figuratively to mean passing responsibility around.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumigil na kayo sa **pagsasaluhan ng bola** at aminin kung sino ang may kasalanan.","translation":"Stop **passing the buck** and just admit who is at fault."}]

translation: to apologize; to ask for forgiveness
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-amin sa pagkakamali at paghiling ng kapatawaran o pag-unawa mula sa taong nagawan ng sala.
original_explanation: The hardest thing to do after a lovers' quarrel (LQ) or when you accidentally spilled coffee on your boss's laptop. It's saying "sorry na, please" with more syllables and more drama. The first step to fixing your mess, whether it's a broken heart or a broken appliance.
usage_notes: A formal and sincere way of saying "sorry". More formal than "pasensya na".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat kang **humingi ng paumanhin** sa kanya dahil sa iyong nagawa.","translation":"You should **apologize** to her for what you did."},{"sentence":"Nag-post siya sa social media upang **humingi ng paumanhin** sa lahat ng kanyang naapektuhan.","translation":"He posted on social media to **ask for forgiveness** from everyone he affected."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang yunit ng sukat para sa kadalisayan ng ginto (karat) o para sa bigat ng mga mamahaling bato tulad ng diyamante (carat).
etymology: Borrowed from English "carat"/"karat", from Middle French, from Italian carato, from Arabic qīrāṭ قيراط, from Ancient Greek kerátion κεράτιον ("carob seed").
original_explanation: The magic number that determines how much "sana all" your jewelry gets. For gold, 24k is the purest, most "mabilis mayupi" (easily bent) version. For diamonds, it's all about the weight – the higher the carat, the heavier the rock and the lighter your wallet.
usage_notes: In English, "carat" is for gems and "karat" is for gold purity. In Filipino, "karat" is often used for both.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang singsing na ito ay gawa sa 18-**karat** na ginto.","translation":"This ring is made of 18-**karat** gold."},{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang makatanggap ng isang 2-**karat** na diyamante.","translation":"She dreams of receiving a 2-**carat** diamond."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapanggap o pagkukunwari na may nararamdaman, ginagawa, o nalalaman na hindi totoo.
etymology: Derived from "balabala" (pretense). The verb form is created with the "-an" suffix.
original_explanation: The art of 'acting lang'. When you bala-balahan that you're busy on your phone to avoid talking to someone. Or when you pretend to be sick to get out of a meeting. It’s a low-level scam, a social white lie you tell with your actions.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of feigning an emotion or condition. E.g., bala-balahaning may sakit (to feign sickness).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bina-balabala** lang niya ang pagtulog para hindi mautusan.","translation":"He is just **pretending** to be asleep so he won't be asked to do an errand."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **bala-balahan**; alam kong gising ka pa.","translation":"Don't **feign** with me; I know you're still awake."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan o katangian ng pagiging tahimik, payapa, at walang anumang maririnig na tunog o gulo.
original_explanation: The vibe in the office when the big boss is walking around. It's the state of your house at 3 AM when you're sneaking to the fridge for a midnight snack. The opposite of a karaoke night with your titas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatulog siya agad dahil **walang-ingay** ang paligid.","translation":"He fell asleep immediately because the surroundings were **noiseless**."},{"sentence":"Pumasok siya sa silid nang **walang-ingay**.","translation":"He entered the room **silently**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-ipon o pagbuo ng dalawa o higit pang bagay, tao, o ideya sa isang grupo o kabuuan.
original_explanation: This is what you do with your laundry (whites and coloreds... maybe not). Or what your project manager does with different teams. 'Pagsamahin ang itlog, harina, at asukal.' It's the recipe instruction of life. Sa love life, ito yung pangarap mong gawin sa 'yo at sa crush mo: pagsamahin sa iisang lovelife. It's the ultimate 'ship' verb.
usage_notes: The root 'sama' here means 'together' or 'group'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **pagsamahin** ang lahat ng sangkap bago ilagay sa oven.","translation":"You need **to combine** all the ingredients before putting them in the oven."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng guro na **pagsamahin** sa isang grupo ang magkakaaway na estudyante.","translation":"The teacher tried **to put together** the feuding students in one group."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang opisyal na pangalan ng pangkat ng mga tagahanga (fandom) ng South Korean na grupong BTS (Bangtan Sonyeondan).
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na "ARMY", isang acronym para sa "Adorable Representative M.C. for Youth".
original_explanation: Hindi ito 'yung sundalo, besh. Ito 'yung fandom ng BTS. Sila 'yung mga nagpupuyat para sa comebacks, nag-iipon para sa concert tickets, at handang makipag-bardagulan online para ipagtanggol ang Bangtan Boys. The real **Army** that uses lightsticks instead of rifles.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa konteksto ng K-Pop at kulturang popular. Laging naka-capitalize ang unang titik upang maiba sa 'army' (hukbo).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isa siyang proud member ng **Army** mula pa noong 2015.","translation":"She has been a proud member of the **Army** since 2015."},{"sentence":"Nag-trending sa Twitter ang mga **Army** para sa kaarawan ni Jungkook.","translation":"The **Army** trended on Twitter for Jungkook's birthday."}]

meaning_filipino: Mahilig mag-usisa, mag-imbestiga, o magsiyasat nang malaliman upang matuklasan ang katotohanan o mga detalye.
original_explanation: Describes a person who, before buying something on Shopee, reads all 500 reviews, watches 10 YouTube unboxing videos, and compares prices across three different apps. Also your friend who can find your crush's entire family history from a single tagged photo. Basically a human NBI agent for everyday life.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil siya ay **masaliksik**, natuklasan niya ang lunas sa kakaibang sakit.","translation":"Because she is **inquisitive**, she discovered the cure for the strange illness."},{"sentence":"Ang isang mabuting mamamahayag ay dapat na **masaliksik**.","translation":"A good journalist must be **meticulous**."}]

meaning_filipino: Taong masipag, matiyaga, at patuloy na nagsisikap upang makamit ang isang layunin.
original_explanation: This is the student who's a scholar, a student leader, and has three side hustles. The BPO agent who works overtime to send money to their family. They embody the 'sipag at tiyaga' mantra. They're powered by coffee, dreams, and the fear of disappointing their parents.
usage_notes: A highly positive and admired trait in Filipino culture. It implies not just hard work ('masipag') but also perseverance and striving for a goal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil siya ay **mapagsumikap**, nakapagtapos siya ng pag-aaral habang nagtatrabaho.","translation":"Because she is **hardworking**, she was able to finish her studies while working."},{"sentence":"Ang isang empleyadong **mapagsumikap** ay tiyak na aasenso sa kumpanya.","translation":"A **diligent** employee will surely get promoted in the company."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang seremonya o proseso ng paglalagay sa isang yumaong tao sa kanyang huling hantungan, karaniwan sa ilalim ng lupa.
original_explanation: The final 'despedida.' It's the event where everyone wears black or white, there's a lot of crying, and your tita is judging everyone's level of grief. It's the culmination of the 'burol' (wake), followed by a slow-moving convoy that causes traffic, and ends with everyone throwing flowers and a handful of soil, saying their last goodbyes.
usage_notes: The act of burying. The place is 'libingan'. The verb is 'ilibing'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming tao ang dumalo sa **libing** ng yumaong alkalde.","translation":"Many people attended the **funeral** of the late mayor."},{"sentence":"Nakatakda ang **libing** sa Sabado ng umaga.","translation":"The **burial** is scheduled for Saturday morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o paghiling na isauli ang isang bagay sa pinanggalingan o sa may-ari nito.
original_explanation: The official verb for when you lend a friend your power bank and they 'forget' to give it back. 'Hoy, **ipabalik** mo na 'yung hiram mo!' Also what you do with a wrong Shopee/Lazada order. You file for a return and **ipabalik** mo sa seller.
usage_notes: A very common and straightforward word used in everyday situations involving borrowing, lending, or returning merchandise.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **ipabalik** mo ang aklat na hiniram mo sa library.","translation":"Please, **have the book you borrowed returned** to the library."},{"sentence":"Nagdesisyon siyang **ipabalik** ang biniling sapatos dahil mali ang sukat.","translation":"She decided **to have the shoes she bought returned** because it was the wrong size."}]

translation: just recently; only a short while ago
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang panahon na hindi pa nagtatagal mula sa kasalukuyan; kamakailan lamang.
etymology: Reduplication of the first syllable of `kailan` (when) + `lamang` (only/just). `ka-` + `kailan` -> `kaikailan`.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "fresh pa" or "bagong-bago lang" phrase. It's when something happened so recently, the "chismis" is still hot. "Kai-kailan lamang sila nag-break," means the wound is still fresh, the IG posts are probably still up. It's more emphatic than just "kailan lang."
usage_notes: An adverbial phrase of time. The hyphen is standard.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kai-kailan lamang** nang huli kaming magkita.","translation":"It was **just recently** that we last saw each other."},{"sentence":"Ang balitang iyan ay lumabas **kai-kailan lamang**.","translation":"That news came out **only a short while ago**."}]

translation: to cause to become blurry; to obscure
meaning_filipino: Magdulot ng pagiging malabo o hindi malinaw ng isang bagay, tulad ng paningin o isang usapin.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your vision after crying your eyes out over a K-drama finale. It's also what your friend does when they give a vague, non-committal answer about your 'situationship'—they're making things unclear.
usage_notes: A causative verb. It describes an action or substance that results in a loss of clarity, either literally (vision) or figuratively (understanding).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang usok mula sa sasakyan ay **makalabo** ng paningin.","translation":"The smoke from the vehicle can **blur** one's vision."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magsalita ng mga bagay na **makalabo** lang sa usapan.","translation":"Don't say things that will only **obscure** the conversation."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa paglagpas o pagtagos ng isang bagay sa isa pa, karaniwang may kasamang puwersa at ganap na paglusot.
original_explanation: Imagine trying to get on the MRT at 7 AM. The way you push through the crowd and somehow end up inside? That's 'dagos'. It's a forceful penetration, like when a nail goes straight through a piece of wood, or when a juicy chismis goes straight to your marites heart.
usage_notes: Often used to describe something sharp or pointed successfully and completely piercing a surface. Can also be used figuratively for concepts or emotions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **dagos** ang pako sa manipis na pader.","translation":"The nail **penetrated** the thin wall."},{"sentence":"**Dagos** hanggang buto ang lamig ng hangin.","translation":"The coldness of the wind was **bone-deep** (piercing to the bone)."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsapi o pagiging bahagi ng isang grupo, samahan, o kilusan na may partikular na paniniwala o layunin.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "maki-" (paglahok) at salitang ugat na "anib" (pagsapi, pag-sama).
original_explanation: This is more formal than 'sumali.' It's not just joining the office basketball team; it's joining a cause, a political party, or a fraternity/sorority. It has a vibe of commitment, like you're not just there for the free pizza, you actually believe in the 'org principles.'
usage_notes: May bigat at pormalidad ang salitang ito kumpara sa "sumali".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming kabataan ang nahikayat na **makianib** sa kanilang adbokasiya para sa kalikasan.","translation":"Many youths were convinced to **join** their advocacy for the environment."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang punong-guro o tagapamahala ng isang paaralan.
etymology: Isang tambalang salita mula sa "ulo" (head) at "guro" (teacher).
original_explanation: Before there was 'Ma'am Principal' or 'Sir Principal,' there was the ulungguro. This is the ultimate authority in the school, the final boss you get sent to when you've been too pasaway in class. It's a very formal, almost poetic term for the school head.
usage_notes: Isang pormal na termino na bihirang gamitin sa pang-araw-araw na usapan. Mas karaniwan ang 'punong-guro' o 'principal'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinatawag ng **ulungguro** ang mga magulang ng mag-aaral.","translation":"The **head teacher** summoned the student's parents."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kilos na tapos nang isagawa kung saan nilinis ang mga damit gamit ang tubig at sabon.
etymology: From Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *labaq. The 'nag-' prefix marks the completed aspect (past tense).
original_explanation: The ultimate adulting milestone. You know you're a responsible adult when your entire weekend plan is just this. '**Naglaba** ako buong Sabado, kaya pagod ako.' It's the sacred act of washing away the sins... and stains... of the previous week.
usage_notes: The completed aspect (past tense) of 'maglaba'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Naglaba** si nanay ng mga puting damit kaninang umaga.","translation":"Mom **washed** the white clothes this morning."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos niyang **maglaba**, nagpahinga na siya.","translation":"After she **did the laundry**, she finally rested."}]

meaning_filipino: Bilang pang-uri, tumutukoy sa isang bagay na walang bisa o hindi katanggap-tanggap ayon sa batas o tuntunin. Bilang pangalan, isang taong may kapansanan o hindi na kayang magtrabaho dahil sa sakit o pinsala.
original_explanation: As an adjective, it's that feeling when your promo code doesn't work: "Error: Code is **imbalido**." It means 'invalid'. As a noun, it's an old-school, and now often considered insensitive, term for a person with a disability (PWD). It's more common to hear it from older folks. So, it can be about a voided check or, in a more dated sense, a person who is physically incapacitated.
usage_notes: The use of 'imbalido' to refer to a person is now often replaced by more sensitive terms like 'taong may kapansanan' (person with disability). However, its use for 'invalid' (e.g., ticket, document) remains common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **imbalido** ang kanyang boto dahil sa maling pagpuno ng balota.","translation":"His vote became **invalid** due to improperly filling out the ballot."},{"sentence":"Inalagaan niya ang kanyang amang naging **imbalido** matapos ang aksidente.","translation":"She took care of her father who became **disabled** after the accident."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malapit at matalik na ugnayan o relasyon sa isang tao, na may kasamang pagtitiwala at pag-unawa.
original_explanation: This is that special connection you have with someone. Hindi lang kayo friends, you're *friends*. Yung tipong kaya mong utangan without feeling hiya. It's the opposite of 'social distancing'—it's 'emotional closeness.' The foundation of all marites sessions.
usage_notes: A compound phrase. 'Lapit' means closeness, 'loob' means inner self/will/disposition. Literally 'closeness of the inner self.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa **lapit ng loob** namin sa isa't isa, alam ko agad kapag may problema siya.","translation":"Because of our **close relationship**, I immediately know when she has a problem."},{"sentence":"Mahirap makamit ang **lapit ng loob** ng isang taong nasaktan na dati.","translation":"It's hard to gain the **intimacy** of a person who has been hurt before."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging laganap, karaniwan, o kalat na kalat ng isang bagay, gawi, o ideya.
original_explanation: This is when something goes viral, but in a more old-school, organic way. It's when a certain fashion trend, a piece of slang, or even a problem becomes so common that it's everywhere. 'Nung panahon ng pandemya, **namalasak** ang online selling.' It describes something becoming the new normal.
usage_notes: Often used to describe trends, problems, or phenomena. The present tense 'namamalasak' is more commonly encountered than the future tense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Noong dekada nobenta, **namalasak** ang mga OPM rock band.","translation":"In the nineties, OPM rock bands **prevailed**."},{"sentence":"Sa panahon ngayon, tila **mamalasak** ang paggamit ng pekeng balita upang manlinlang.","translation":"Nowadays, it seems the use of fake news to deceive **will become widespread**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kemikal na may maasim na lasa, may kakayahang mag-neutralize ng mga alkali, at karaniwang nagiging pula ang asul na litmus paper.
original_explanation: This is the Tagalog spelling for 'acid'. It's what gives suka its kick and what your ex's words might be full of. Not to be confused with 'asim', which is the taste, 'asid' is the actual chemical compound. Science, besh!
usage_notes: A technical or scientific term. 'Asim' is used for the taste in everyday language.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **asid** sa baterya ay mapanganib kung madidikit sa balat.","translation":"The **acid** in a battery is dangerous if it touches the skin."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan nila ang epekto ng iba't ibang uri ng **asid**.","translation":"They are studying the effects of different kinds of **acid**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapang yari sa kahoy o metal na may malapad at patag na dulo, ginagamit sa paggaod o pagpapatakbo ng bangka.
original_explanation: The original engine for your bangka before Yamaha came along. It's the thing you use to move a small boat when you're trying to have a romantic moment on a lake, or when you're desperately trying to get back to shore because you forgot the snacks. Think of it as the manual transmission of the sea.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawala ang isang **sagwan** kaya paikot-ikot na lang kami sa lawa.","translation":"One **paddle** was lost, so we just kept going in circles on the lake."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang **sagwan** para itaboy ang mga ahas sa tubig.","translation":"He used the **oar** to drive away the water snakes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang laruang yari sa magaan na balangkas na binalutan ng papel o tela, na idinisenyo upang paliparin sa hangin gamit ang isang mahabang tali.
etymology: From Spanish 'gorrión' (sparrow), likely due to its bird-like appearance when flying.
original_explanation: The classic Filipino kite, usually diamond-shaped, that you see flying high during windy seasons. It's the OG drone. Making one with 'tingting' (bamboo stick) and 'papel de hapon' is a core childhood memory for many Pinoys, right next to getting your kite stuck on a power line.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'saranggola', though 'saranggola' is more common. 'Guryon' can sometimes refer to a smaller, simpler type of kite.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtatakbuhan ang mga bata sa parang habang nagpapalipad ng **guryon**.","translation":"The children were running in the field while flying a **kite**."},{"sentence":"Ang taas ng lipad ng kanyang **guryon**!","translation":"His **kite** is flying so high!"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na nakabukas, nakalatag, o nakabukadkad nang husto. Sa modernong gamit, ito ay tumutukoy din sa hayagang pag-amin ng isang tao sa kanyang sekswalidad (pagiging out).
etymology: From the original meaning of 'to unfurl' or 'spread out', it has been adopted by the LGBTQ+ community to mean 'out of the closet'.
original_explanation: Like a banner, a flag, or your true self finally unfurled for the world to see. Think 'coming out of the closet.' When you stop hiding and just say, "This is me, mga beshie!" It's about being out and proud.
usage_notes: The meaning 'openly gay' or 'out' is a very common modern usage, derived from the original meaning of 'unfurled'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ladlad** na ang mga banderitas para sa pista.","translation":"The fiesta banners are now **unfurled**."},{"sentence":"Matagal na siyang **ladlad** sa kanyang pamilya at mga kaibigan.","translation":"He has long been **out** to his family and friends."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malakas na tunog na nalilikha ng pagbagsak ng isang mabigat at di-gaanong matigas na bagay, lalo na sa putik o tubig.
original_explanation: Yung tunog ng pagbagsak mo sa reyalidad pagkatapos mong umasa. O 'yung tunog ng hinog na langka na nahulog sa lupa. It's a heavy, 'squishy' kind of fall. Hindi matinis na 'kalabog', kundi isang mapurol na 'labog'.
usage_notes: Madalas na nagpapahiwatig ng pagkahulog sa isang bagay na malambot o basa, tulad ng putik.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **labog** ng niyog sa putikan.","translation":"I heard the **thud** of the coconut in the mud."},{"sentence":"Isang malakas na **labog** ang gumising sa lahat nang mahulog ang sako ng bigas.","translation":"A loud **thud** woke everyone up when the sack of rice fell."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang nakaplanong gawain, kadalasan ay may tiyak na layunin, na isinasagawa sa loob ng isang takdang panahon.
original_explanation: Ito yung group work sa school na isa lang ang gumagawa. O kaya yung "passion prodyek" mo na sinimulan mo noong 2019 pero hanggang ngayon, nasa "planning stage" pa rin. Sa gobyerno, ito yung "Build, Build, Build" na minsan "Delay, Delay, Delay".
usage_notes: Isang modernong hiram na salita na mas karaniwan sa kolokyal na usapan kaysa sa pormal na "proyekto".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong tapusin ang **prodyek** ko sa Science bago ang Biyernes.","translation":"I need to finish my Science **project** before Friday."},{"sentence":"Malaking **prodyek** ng barangay ang paglilinis ng ilog.","translation":"The river cleanup is a big barangay **project**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagbibigay ng kaligayahan, kagalakan, o kasiyahan sa pakiramdam.
etymology: From `siya` (joy, pleasure). The affix `nakasi-` denotes something that causes the feeling of the root word.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na sakto lang ang timpla ng kape mo, walang traffic sa EDSA, o biglang may nag-abot ng libreng Jollibee. That's **nakasisiya**. It's the simple joys, the small wins, the "Sana all" moments that actually happen to you.
usage_notes: A more formal and slightly more intense version of `masaya` (happy). It describes the thing *causing* the joy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakasisiya** talagang pagmasdan ang paglubog ng araw sa dalampasigan.","translation":"It is truly **delightful** to watch the sunset on the beach."},{"sentence":"Isang **nakasisiyang** karanasan ang manalo sa kompetisyon.","translation":"Winning the competition was a **satisfying** experience."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagluluto ng pagkain, karaniwan ay karne o isda, sa ibabaw ng nagbabagang uling o apoy. Ito ang anyong pangkasalukuyan ng pandiwang 'mag-ihaw'.
original_explanation: Future tense of 'ihaw'. That moment when your tito declares, "Ako na mag-iihaw!" at the family reunion, and you know you're about to have the best liempo of your life. This is the action you'll be doing. "Mag-iihaw kami mamaya sa beach."
usage_notes: This is the contemplated aspect (future tense) of the verb 'mag-ihaw'. The 'i-' prefix indicates it's often an object-focus verb, meaning the object being grilled is the focus.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Iihaw** ni Mang Berto ang mga isdang nahuli niya kanina.","translation":"Mang Berto **will grill** the fish he caught earlier."},{"sentence":"Ano ang **iihaw** natin para sa Noche Buena?","translation":"What **will we grill** for Christmas Eve dinner?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging api, inaalipusta, o minaliit ng iba.
original_explanation: This is "api" level 99. It's that feeling when you're the only one in the group project who did all the work, but everyone got the same grade. You feel 'amis'. It has a classic, literary flavor, like something you'd read in a Florante at Laura summary. You're not just sad, you're existentially stepped on.
usage_notes: A more literary or formal term for being oppressed or looked down upon. 'Api' is more commonly used in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa kahirapan, marami ang namumuhay nang **amis**.","translation":"Because of poverty, many live an **oppressed** life."},{"sentence":"Nadama niya ang pagiging **amis** sa kamay ng malupit na pinuno.","translation":"He felt **downtrodden** at the hands of the cruel leader."}]

meaning_filipino: (Pabalbal/Figuratibo) Naging bastos, magaspang, o bumaba ang antas ng pag-uusap, pagbibiro, o pag-uugali.
etymology: Figurative slang, from the idea of something falling 'into the gutter'.
original_explanation: When the "wholesome" group chat topic suddenly takes a dark, dirty, or R-18 turn. "Okay pa 'yung biruan namin kanina, tapos biglang kumanal nung dumating si Mark." Gutter humor, basically.
usage_notes: A modern slang term to describe conversations or humor turning vulgar or 'gutter-level'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-aasaran lang sila pero biglang **kumanal** ang usapan.","translation":"They were just teasing each other but the conversation suddenly **became crude**."},{"sentence":"Ayoko nang sumama sa kanila, laging **kumakanal** ang mga biro.","translation":"I don't want to hang out with them anymore, the jokes always **turn vulgar**."}]

meaning_filipino: May labis na taba sa katawan; malaman o mabilog ang pangangatawan.
original_explanation: The politically incorrect way to say someone's 'plus-sized' or 'thicc.' It's what your tita lovingly calls you after the Christmas Noche Buena feast. The phrase 'Uy, tumaba ka!' is a national greeting, not a compliment.
usage_notes: While descriptive, can be considered rude when referring to people. 'Malusog' (healthy) or 'malaman' (fleshy) are often used as more polite alternatives. Note the glottal stop at the end, distinguishing it from 'matabang' (bland).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **mataba** ang alaga kong pusa dahil sa sobrang pagkain at tulog.","translation":"My pet cat became **fat** from too much eating and sleeping."},{"sentence":"Pinayuhan siya ng doktor na mag-ehersisyo dahil medyo **mataba** na siya para sa kanyang edad.","translation":"The doctor advised him to exercise because he is already a bit **fat** for his age."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mamukadkad o umunlad, partikular na tumutukoy sa pagbukadkad ng bulaklak o sa pagganda at pag-unlad ng isang tao.
original_explanation: This is what happens after a major heartbreak, a career shift, or just finally getting enough sleep. You start glowing up, feeling good, and living your best life. Sabi nga nila, 'Nag-bloom ka!' It's the physical manifestation of 'I'm doing better now.'
usage_notes: Madalas ginagamit sa Taglish (e.g., 'nag-bloom') para ilarawan ang pagganda o pag-unlad ng isang tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Talagang nag-**bloom** si Ana mula nang mag-aral siya sa ibang bansa.","translation":"Ana really **bloomed** since she started studying abroad."},{"sentence":"Hintayin nating mag-**bloom** ang mga rosas sa hardin.","translation":"Let's wait for the roses in the garden to **bloom**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamataas na lalaking pinuno ng isang monarkiya o kaharian.
etymology: From Malay 'hari' (day). The semantic shift to 'king' or 'ruler' is a specific development within Philippine languages.
original_explanation: The ultimate boss, the big cheese, the numero uno. In the Philippines, we don't have a literal king anymore, but we use 'hari' to describe someone who's the best at something. 'Hari ng Sablay' (King of Fails), 'Hari ng Kalsada' (King of the Road, for jeepney drivers), or FPJ as the 'Hari ng Pelikulang Pilipino' (King of Philippine Movies).
usage_notes: The female equivalent is 'reyna' (queen). Commonly used metaphorically to denote mastery or dominance in a certain field.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Haring Felipe ang dating **hari** ng Espanya.","translation":"King Felipe was the former **king** of Spain."},{"sentence":"Tinagurian si Fernando Poe Jr. bilang **Hari** ng Pelikulang Pilipino.","translation":"Fernando Poe Jr. was dubbed the **King** of Philippine Cinema."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang agham at sining ng pag-aalaga, pagpaparami, at pamamahala sa mga alagang hayop para sa kapakinabangan, tulad ng pagkain o produkto.
etymology: From 'hayop' (animal). The circumfix 'pag- -an' and the repetition of the first syllable 'ha' ('pag-ha-hayup-an') creates a noun meaning the practice or industry related to animals.
original_explanation: It's basically running a farm for animals. Think piggery, poultry, or a cattle ranch. It's the business of raising animals not just as pets, but for meat, milk, eggs, or labor. It's the 'agri' part of 'agribusiness' that deals with creatures that moo, oink, and cluck.
usage_notes: A technical term used in agriculture and economics.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paghahayupan** ay isang mahalagang sektor ng agrikultura sa bansa.","translation":"**Livestock farming** is an important sector of agriculture in the country."},{"sentence":"Kumuha siya ng kurso sa **paghahayupan** upang mapabuti ang kanilang negosyo.","translation":"He took a course in **animal husbandry** to improve their business."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang estado ng pag-iisip kung saan ang isang tao ay hindi makapagpasya o may pag-aalinlangan.
original_explanation: The official status of your friend who can't choose where to eat. "Kahit saan" is their mantra. This is you, scrolling through Netflix for an hour and watching nothing. It’s that “It’s Complicated” relationship status. You want it, but you're not sure, but maybe you do? That's **hindi disidido**.
usage_notes: A common phrase to express uncertainty or indecisiveness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hindi disidido** pa ako kung anong kurso ang kukunin ko sa kolehiyo.","translation":"I'm still **undecided** about what course to take in college."},{"sentence":"Dahil **hindi disidido** ang mga tao, uulitin ang botohan.","translation":"Because the people were **undecided**, the voting will be repeated."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagsasagawa ng pag-aaral o pagsusuri sa isang bagay; isang taong nagbabantay sa isang pagsusulit.
original_explanation: The person you pay to cram a semester's worth of knowledge into your brain a week before the board exams. They're the coach for your mental Olympics, armed with highlighters and practice tests.
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of academic or professional review centers.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahusay ang aming **tagarepaso** sa review center kaya pumasa ako sa board exam.","translation":"Our **reviewer** at the review center was excellent, which is why I passed the board exam."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **tagarepaso** natin para sa darating na pagsusulit?","translation":"Who is our **reviewer** for the upcoming exam?"}]

meaning_filipino: Itaas o iangat ang ulo o paningin upang tumingin sa isang bagay o direksyon, karaniwan mula sa pagkakayuko.
original_explanation: When someone calls your name in the middle of doomscrolling, and you finally lift your head from your phone. That's 'itunghay'. It's the opposite of being 'nakayuko'. It's the "look up, child, there's a world outside your screen" command from your nanay.
usage_notes: Often used in a poetic or formal context, like lifting one's gaze to the heavens or in literature.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Itunghay** mo ang iyong mga mata at masdan ang ganda ng kalangitan.","translation":"**Lift up** your eyes and behold the beauty of the sky."},{"sentence":"Nang tawagin siya ng guro, dahan-dahan niyang **itinunghay** ang kanyang ulo mula sa pagkakayuko sa libro.","translation":"When the teacher called him, he slowly **lifted** his head from being bent over the book."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay, karaniwang damit o papel, na punit-punit, sira-sira, o laspag na sa gamit.
original_explanation: Your favorite 'pambahay' shirt that has more holes than fabric? That's **gulanit**. The distressed jeans you paid 2,000 pesos for? Also **gulanit**. It's the look of something that has been through a lot, whether it's an old flag after a storm or your notes after your dog decides they're a snack.
usage_notes: Describes a state of being extremely torn and worn out.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakasuot siya ng **gulanit** na damit habang namamalimos sa kalye.","translation":"He was wearing **tattered** clothes while begging on the street."},{"sentence":"Naging **gulanit** ang mga pahina ng lumang libro.","translation":"The pages of the old book became **torn to shreds**."}]

translation: slip of paper; ballot; small poster
meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na piraso ng papel na naglalaman ng impormasyon, paunawa, o ginagamit sa pagboto.
original_explanation: Think of it as the ancestor of the modern-day 'flyer' or 'brochure'. It's that small piece of paper handed out during election season with a candidate's face on it, or a slip for a raffle draw at the company Christmas party. A more formal, slightly vintage-sounding word than just 'papel'.
usage_notes: Often associated with voting (ballots) or official notices on small paper. It implies a small paper with a specific function or information.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ibinigay sa kanya ang isang **papeleta** para sa rifa.","translation":"He was given a **slip of paper** for the raffle."},{"sentence":"Maingat niyang pinunan ang kanyang **papeleta** sa loob ng voting booth.","translation":"He carefully filled out his **ballot** inside the voting booth."}]

translation: to excommunicate each other; to expel one another
meaning_filipino: Itakwil o alisin sa grupo o organisasyon ang isa't isa nang sabay-sabay o bilang ganti.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "you're dead to me" on a group level. It's when members of a church, a political party, or even a toxic barkada start kicking each other out. It's a messy, dramatic process of mutual excommunication. "Nagtiwa-tiwalag na sila sa grupo dahil sa pera." It's the organizational equivalent of a very bad breakup.
usage_notes: The "mag-" prefix with a reduplicated root often implies a reciprocal or mutual action. In this case, "to expel each other."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa matinding hindi pagkakaunawaan, nagsimulang **magtiwa-tiwalag** ang mga miyembro ng samahan.","translation":"Due to severe misunderstanding, the members of the organization began to **expel one another**."},{"sentence":"Ang pagtatalo sa pamumuno ay nauwi sa **pagtitiwa-tiwalag** ng mga opisyal.","translation":"The dispute over leadership ended with the officials **excommunicating each other**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mabangong sangkap na mula sa dagta ng mga halaman na sinusunog upang maglabas ng kaaya-ayang amoy, karaniwang ginagamit sa mga seremonyang panrelihiyon.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung usok na amoy-simbahan. 'Yung ginagamit ng pari na winawagayway at feel na feel mo ang kabanalan sa amoy. Sa labas ng simbahan, ginagamit din 'to for 'good vibes' or para paalisin daw ang masamang espiritu... o 'yung amoy ng piniritong isda.
usage_notes: Primarily associated with Catholic religious rites, but also used in other spiritual or aromatic contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang amoy ng **insenso** ay nangingibabaw sa loob ng lumang simbahan.","translation":"The smell of **incense** dominates the inside of the old church."},{"sentence":"Nagsunog siya ng **insenso** para sa mga yumaong kamag-anak.","translation":"He burned **incense** for his deceased relatives."}]

meaning_filipino: Maayos; may sistema; nakaplano nang mabuti ang bawat bahagi.
original_explanation: The opposite of your "tapon-dito-tapon-doon" bedroom. Ito 'yung friend mo na may planner at naka-color code pa ang notes. From a perfectly arranged closet to a well-planned event, 'pag **organisado**, everything just works. It's the life goal of every adult na pagod na sa gulo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging matagumpay ang proyekto dahil sa isang **organisado** na pangkat.","translation":"The project became successful because of an **organized** team."},{"sentence":"Laging **organisado** ang mga gamit niya sa mesa.","translation":"His things on the table are always **organized**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng pabago-bagong katangian, anyo, o kalagayan; hindi panatag o permanente.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'iba' na inuulit upang ipahiwatig ang pagkakaiba-iba o hindi pagiging pare-pareho.
original_explanation: Parang presyo ng gasolina o 'yong signal ng Wi-Fi mo. Minsan malakas, minsan wala. Ganyan din ang mood ng kaibigan mong laging may hugot. Ang tawag diyan, **nag-iiba-iba**.
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang ilarawan ang isang bagay na walang katiyakan o may maraming baryasyon sa paglipas ng panahon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Normal lang na **mag-iba-iba** ang iyong timbang sa loob ng isang linggo.","translation":"It's normal for your weight to **vary** within a week."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa pabago-bagong panahon, **nag-iba-iba** ang presyo ng gulay sa palengke.","translation":"Because of the changing weather, the price of vegetables at the market **varied**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pagsisisi sa nagawang kasalanan na nag-uugat sa takot sa parusa ng Diyos, sa halip na sa dalisay na pagmamahal sa Kanya.
etymology: From pagsisisi (regret) + hindi (not) + lubos (complete, perfect). A theological term.
original_explanation: This is the "I'm sorry I got caught" kind of regret. You're not really sorry for what you did, you're just sorry about the consequences. It’s like regretting cheating on an exam because you failed, not because you know it was wrong. In religious terms, it's being sorry because you're scared of hellfire, not because you genuinely feel bad for offending God.
usage_notes: Primarily a religious or theological term used in Catholicism.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinuturo sa katekismo ang pagkakaiba ng **pagsisising hindi lubos** at pagsisising lubos.","translation":"The catechism teaches the difference between **imperfect contrition** and perfect contrition."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang paghingi ng tawad ay tila **pagsisising hindi lubos** lamang.","translation":"His apology seemed to be just **attrition**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang makaligtas o makaiwas sa isang hindi kanais-nais na pangyayari, bagay, o tao.
original_explanation: Your superpower when you see your toxic tita at a family gathering and you suddenly need to go to the bathroom. It's the skill you use to dodge extra work your boss tries to give you at 5 PM on a Friday. "Paano ba maiwasan ang traffic sa EDSA?" is the great unanswered question of our time.
usage_notes: This is an object-focus verb, meaning the thing being avoided is the subject of the sentence. The past/completed form is 'naiwasan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paano kaya **maiwasan** ang magkaroon ng utang?","translation":"How can one **avoid** getting into debt?"},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang takbuhan ang problema, ngunit hindi niya ito **naiwasan**.","translation":"He tried to run from the problem, but he couldn't **avoid** it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng lalagyan, karaniwang may hawakan at bibig, na ginagamit sa pagsasalin ng likido tulad ng tubig o juice.
original_explanation: That big jug of water or iced tea sa gitna ng lamesa during family lunch. 'Yung 'pag ubos na, magtuturuan kayo kung sino'ng magre-refill. It's the designated hydration station of every Pinoy handaan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakilagyan mo ng malamig na tubig ang **pitser**.","translation":"Please fill the **pitcher** with cold water."},{"sentence":"Ang sarap ng iced tea na nasa **pitser**.","translation":"The iced tea in the **pitcher** is delicious."}]

translation: was broken, was damaged, got destroyed
meaning_filipino: Nawalan ng dating ayos, anyo, o silbi; nagkaroon ng pinsala o depekto.
original_explanation: This is the 'sira na' moment. Your phone after it falls face down. Your diet after seeing a lechon. Your trust after they lie to you. It's the past tense of things going wrong. It's the 'awit, lods' when your laptop decides to update in the middle of a presentation.
usage_notes: This is a very common verb indicating that something has been broken or damaged. It is in the completed aspect (past tense).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nasira** ang relos ko kaya huli na ako sa klase.","translation":"My watch **was broken** so I was late for class."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, lahat ng bagay na **nasira** ay maaaring ayusin o palitan, maliban sa tiwala.","translation":"Don't worry, everything that **gets broken** can be fixed or replaced, except for trust."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangkalahatang pakiramdam o kapaligiran na nagpapahiwatig ng pagiging mababang-uri, magulo, o hindi kaaya-aya.
etymology: A compound of the slang 'squammy' (from 'squatter') and the English word 'vibes'.
original_explanation: It's not just one thing, it's the whole *aura*. That feeling you get when you walk into a place and the combination of the loud, distorted music, the questionable color scheme, and the general chaos just screams "tacky." It's the total opposite of the clean, minimalist "aesthetic" vibes. If a place gives you "squammyvibes," you probably won't be taking any Instagram pics there.
usage_notes: A very contemporary slang term used to describe the atmosphere of a place or situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umalis na tayo dito, hindi ko gusto ang **squammyvibes** ng lugar.","translation":"Let's leave, I don't like the **tacky atmosphere** of this place."},{"sentence":"Yung party nila, imbes na maging masaya, nagkaroon ng **squammyvibes** dahil sa away.","translation":"Their party, instead of being fun, got **low-class vibes** because of the fight."}]

meaning_filipino: Salitang nagpapahayag ng kawalan, pagkaubos, o hindi pag-iral ng isang bagay, tao, o katangian.
etymology: Mula sa Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *walaq. Sa ibang wika, ito ay nangangahulugang 'umiral', ngunit sa Tagalog at iba pa, ito ay nag-evolve upang mangahulugang 'hindi umiral'.
original_explanation: This is the official word for "ghosting." When someone asks "Nasaan na siya?" and you reply, "Wala na," it's the sound of an empty chatbox. It's what's left in your wallet before payday. It's the answer to "May pake ba ako?" It is the void, the absence, the big fat zero.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamiting mag-isa bilang sagot. Madalas na sinusundan ng pangngalan upang ipahiwatig ang kawalan nito (hal., `walang tao`).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May pagkain pa ba? **Wala** na, naubos na lahat.","translation":"Is there any food left? There's **none**, it's all gone."},{"sentence":"**Wala** akong masabi sa galing mo.","translation":"I have **nothing** to say about your skill (I'm speechless)."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o gawain ng pagluluto ng bigas upang maging kanin.
original_explanation: The most fundamental Filipino life skill. If you don't know how to 'magsaing', are you even Filipino? 'Saing' is the ritual of washing rice, getting the water level 'one-knuckle' deep, and turning on the rice cooker. It's the foundation of every meal. "Wala pa tayong ulam, pero at least may saing na."
usage_notes: Often used with the prefix 'mag-' to form the verb 'magsaing' (to cook rice). The noun 'saing' itself can also refer to the rice being cooked.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tapos na ba ang **saing**? Nagugutom na ako.","translation":"Is the **rice cooked** already? I'm getting hungry."},{"sentence":"Sino ang taya sa **saing** ngayong gabi?","translation":"Who is assigned to **cook rice** tonight?"}]

meaning_filipino: Maging isang biyudo; mamatayan ng asawang babae.
original_explanation: This is the male version of `mabiyuda` (to become a widow). It's when a husband outlives his wife. It's a sad, life-changing event. You see this in teleseryes where the single dad struggles to raise his kids after his wife passes away.
usage_notes: Specifically for a man whose wife has died. The female counterpart is `mabiyuda`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maagang **nabiyudo** si Mang Kanor kaya mag-isa niyang pinalaki ang kanilang mga anak.","translation":"Mang Kanor **became a widower** early, so he raised their children by himself."},{"sentence":"Ayaw kong isipin na balang araw ay **mabibiyudo** ako.","translation":"I don't want to think that I will **become a widower** someday."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na hindi maaaring makuha, makamit, o mapasakamay.
etymology: Mula sa 'di' (not) + 'makukuha' (will be able to be gotten).
original_explanation: Like your crush who's already 'taken'. Or that 10/10 condo in BGC on an entry-level salary. Some things are just di-makukuha sa tingin, you have to work for them... or accept they're out of your league. Also, 'Di mo 'ko makukuha sa santong dasalan!' (You can't win me over with feigned piety!).
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa mga pisikal na bagay, layunin, o maging sa pabor ng isang tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para sa kanya, ang kaligayahan ay isang bagay na **di-makukuha** sa materyal na yaman.","translation":"For him, happiness is something **unobtainable** through material wealth."},{"sentence":"Ang promosyon na iyon ay tila **di-makukuha** kung hindi ka magsisikap.","translation":"That promotion seems **unattainable** if you don't work hard."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng puno o palumpong na may malalaki at karaniwang mapuputi o kulay-rosas na mga bulaklak.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na "magnolia", ipinangalan kay Pierre Magnol.
original_explanation: Besides being a famous ice cream and dairy brand in the Philippines that's basically part of our childhood, it's also a fancy flower. Think of it as the tita of flowers – elegant, classic, and smells amazing.
usage_notes: Mas kilala sa Pilipinas bilang pangalan ng isang brand ng pagkain kaysa sa bulaklak mismo. Ang Tagalog na baybay ay "magnolya".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May malaking puno ng **magnolia** sa kanilang hardin.","translation":"There is a big **magnolia** tree in their garden."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-aalis ng legal na kapangyarihan, pagiging epektibo, o katotohanan ng isang kasunduan, batas, o desisyon.
etymology: From pag- (nominalizer) + pa- (causative) + walang-bisa (ineffective, null). Lit. 'the act of making something null and void'.
original_explanation: This is the official term for 'cancel culture' in legal documents. Parang 'yung pag-cancel mo sa Grab booking mo, pero for contracts, marriage, or laws. Ito rin 'yung gusto mong gawin sa mga sinabi mo nung lasing ka.
usage_notes: A formal and legal term. Can also be written as 'pagpapawalambisa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghain sila ng petisyon para sa **pagpapawalang-bisa** ng kanilang kasal.","translation":"They filed a petition for the **annulment** of their marriage."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapawalang-bisa** sa kontrata ay nagdulot ng malaking problema.","translation":"The **invalidation** of the contract caused a huge problem."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang labis na pag-aatubili o pagbabantulot na gawin ang isang bagay, na kadalasan ay nagpapakita ng kawalan ng gana o takot.
original_explanation: This is the next level of `pag-aatubili`. It's not just hesitating; it's actively dawdling and finding excuses. It's the feeling when you're asked to wash the dishes, and you suddenly need to check your phone, fix a pillow, and stare into space for ten minutes before starting. It's procrastination in its purest, most annoying form.
usage_notes: A more intense and often irritating form of hesitation or reluctance. The root 'ulik' is rarely used on its own.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itigil mo na ang iyong **pag-uulik-ulik** at simulan mo na ang iyong takdang-aralin.","translation":"Stop your **dawdling** and start your homework."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o kalagayan ng pagguho, pagkasira, o pagwasak ng isang istraktura o samahan.
original_explanation: Think of it as a relationship status: "It's complicated, and now it's demolished." This is the complete and utter collapse. It could be a building after an earthquake, a political party after a scandal, or your self-esteem after seeing your ex's wedding photos. Total wasak.
usage_notes: Used for both literal structures (buildings, walls) and figurative entities (organizations, plans, alliances).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging sanhi ng malakas na lindol ang **pagkatibag** ng maraming gusali.","translation":"The strong earthquake caused the **collapse** of many buildings."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkatibag** ng kanilang samahan ay dulot ng panloob na alitan.","translation":"The **disintegration** of their organization was caused by internal conflict."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na mahilig sa sopas o sabaw, o sa isang pagkain na masyadong masabaw.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "sopero" (may kaugnayan sa sabaw; mahilig sa sopas).
original_explanation: Describes someone who can't live without sabaw. 'Yung kaibigan mong laging naghahanap ng sabaw sa bawat ulam, kahit sa prito. "Pahingi ng sabaw!" is their life's motto. It can also describe food that's too watery, like, "Ang sopero naman ng adobo mo, parang tinola na."
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin upang ilarawan ang isang tao (bilang pangngalan o pang-uri) o isang ulam.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Talagang **sopero** si Lolo, laging may sabaw ang kanin niya.","translation":"Grandpa is really **fond of soup**; his rice always has broth."},{"sentence":"Ayaw ko ng ganyang luto, masyadong **sopero** para sa akin.","translation":"I don't like it cooked that way, it's too **soupy** for me."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malalim at taos-pusong pagdadalamhati o pagka-konsensya dahil sa isang nagawang pagkakamali.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng `mataos` (taos-puso, malalim) at `pagsisisi` (paghingi ng tawad).
original_explanation: This isn't just saying "sorry" because you got caught. This is the "sorry" that keeps you up at 3 AM, replaying your mistakes. 'Yung pagsisisi na parang suntok sa dibdib, when you realize the gravity of what you've done and wish you could turn back time. It's the emotional equivalent of a thesis defense for your conscience.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang pormal at mabigat na parirala, madalas gamitin sa kontekstong legal, relihiyoso, o pampanitikan upang tukuyin ang isang napakalalim na antas ng pagsisisi.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinakita ng akusado ang **mataos na pagsisisi** sa kanyang ginawang krimen.","translation":"The accused showed **deep remorse** for the crime he committed."},{"sentence":"Ang tanging hiling niya ay kapatawaran, dala ng kanyang **mataos na pagsisisi**.","translation":"His only wish is forgiveness, brought by his **profound regret**."}]

translation: to reach; to arrive at (a time or place)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagdating o pag-abot sa isang tiyak na lugar, panahon, o kalagayan.
original_explanation: A slightly more formal or literary way of saying 'makarating'. You use this when you're talking about reaching a destination, a goal, or a certain point in time. 'Nawa'y makasapit tayo sa ating patutunguhan nang ligtas.' It has a slightly more dramatic or hopeful tone than just 'dumating'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagdarasal kong **makasapit** ka sa iyong kaarawan na malusog at masaya.","translation":"I pray that you **reach** your birthday healthy and happy."},{"sentence":"Sana ay **makasapit** tayo sa tuktok ng bundok bago dumilim.","translation":"Hopefully, we can **arrive at** the mountain's peak before it gets dark."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang likidong walang kulay, mabango, at siksik na ginamit bilang anestetiko at bilang isang pantunaw.
original_explanation: Ito yung pampatulog sa mga pelikula na tinatakpan sa panyo tapos ipapaamoy sa bida (o kontrabida). Sa totoong buhay, kemikal ito na may maraming gamit sa laboratoryo, pero 'wag mong gagayahin yung sa TV, delikado 'yan.
usage_notes: Madalas marinig sa mga pelikula o serye kaysa sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamitan ng **kloropormo** ang biktima upang mawalan ito ng malay.","translation":"The victim was subdued with **chloroform** to make them unconscious."}]

meaning_filipino: Isampay o ilatag ang mga damit o tela sa sampayan upang matuyo.
etymology: From i- (causative prefix) + hayhay (to hang clothes).
original_explanation: The official verb of Laundry Day. After 'paglalaba,' comes 'pag-ihayhay.' This is the act of hanging your newly washed clothes on the 'sampayan' (clothesline). You do this hoping it doesn't rain, and that your kapitbahay doesn't see the hole in your favorite pambahay shorts.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to hanging clothes or fabric to dry. The more common synonym is 'isampay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **ihayhay** ang mga damit bago umulan.","translation":"Help me **hang** the clothes **out to dry** before it rains."},{"sentence":"Maaga siyang naglaba para maaga ring makapag-**ihayhay**.","translation":"She did the laundry early so she could also **hang the clothes** early."}]

translation: A Filipino martial art focusing on kicks.
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng sining panlaban mula sa Pilipinas na nakatuon sa paggamit ng mga sipa bilang pangunahing atake.
original_explanation: It's the OG Filipino foot-fighting style. Think of it as Pinoy Taekwondo, but probably developed from watching chickens fight. It's a martial art where your legs do all the talking (and kicking).
usage_notes: Sikaran is a specific martial art originating from Rizal province. The term can also refer to the place of kicking, but it is primarily known as the martial art itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **sikaran** ay isang pamanang sining panlaban na dapat nating ipagmalaki.","translation":"**Sikaran** is a heritage martial art that we should be proud of."},{"sentence":"Nais niyang matuto ng **sikaran** upang maipagtanggol ang sarili.","translation":"He wants to learn **sikaran** to defend himself."}]

translation: to cause a collision; to be the reason for a crash
meaning_filipino: Ang maging sanhi ng pagbangga o pag-umpog ng dalawa o higit pang bagay, lalo na ng mga sasakyan.
etymology: Mula sa panlaping 'ika-' (panlaping sanhi) at 'bangga' (collide, crash).
original_explanation: The reason for a crash. It could be literal, like a stray dog on the road na ikinabangga ng tricycle. Or it could be figurative, like when your controversial opinion ikinabangga mo sa opinyon ng boss mo during a meeting. Awkward.
usage_notes: Isang pandiwang sanhi. Ang layon ng pandiwa ay ang tao o bagay na bumangga, at ang simuno ay ang sanhi.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang biglaang pagtawid ng pusa ang **ikinabangga** ng motorsiklo.","translation":"The cat's sudden crossing **was the reason for the motorcycle's crash**."},{"sentence":"Muntik nang **ikabangga** ng sasakyan ang pagmamaneho niya nang lasing.","translation":"His drunk driving almost **caused the car to crash**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang dalubhasang artesano na gumagawa ng mga bagay mula sa pilak.
original_explanation: The more 'sosyal' cousin of the 'panday-bakal'. Instead of making rough-and-tough 'itaks', the 'panday-pilak' creates delicate and expensive jewelry, religious artifacts, and fancy utensils. Think of the artisans in Baguio or Meycauayan, Bulacan. They're the ones you go to for a custom engagement ring or a 'pasalubong' that screams 'I have good taste and some money.'
usage_notes: Specific to working with silver. A 'panday-ginto' (goldsmith) is another related term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga alahas na gawa ng **panday-pilak** na iyon ay napakaganda.","translation":"The jewelry made by that **silversmith** is very beautiful."},{"sentence":"Kilala ang Baguio sa mga mahuhusay na **panday-pilak**.","translation":"Baguio is known for its skilled **silversmiths**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng pagiging madalas na lumalabag o hindi sumusunod sa mga batas, alituntunin, o kasunduan.
original_explanation: This describes someone who treats rules like suggestions. They're the ones who will park in a 'No Parking' zone 'saglit lang', cross the street when the pedestrian light is red, or try to sneak an extra item into the 10-items-or-less express lane. They have a rebellious streak, whether it's against the law or just office policy.
usage_notes: Often used in legal, formal, or religious contexts to describe someone who habitually breaks rules.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang taong **mapaglabag** sa batas-trapiko ay madalas na sanhi ng aksidente.","translation":"A person who is **fond of violating** traffic laws is often the cause of accidents."},{"sentence":"Pinarusahan ang mga empleyadong **mapaglabag** sa patakaran ng kumpanya.","translation":"The employees who were **transgressing** company policy were punished."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong kulang sa talino, pang-unawa, o pag-iisip; hangal. Ginagamit din bilang isang salitang mura na nagpapahayag ng galit o inis.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na "gago" na nangangahulugang "utal" o "nauutal," na nag-evolve upang mangahulugang "hangal" o "tanga."
original_explanation: This is the Swiss Army knife of Pinoy insults. It can be a term of endearment among bros ('Gago! Ang galing mo dun!') or a full-on declaration of war ('Gago ka ba?!'). It's the 'dude' that can also mean 'you absolute moron.' Context is everything. Not HR-friendly, but very common in traffic.
usage_notes: Itinuturing na isang salitang mura o nakakainsulto sa mga pormal na okasyon. Ang bigat ng kahulugan ay nag-iiba depende sa tono at relasyon ng mga nagsasalita.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **gago**, sundin mo ang batas trapiko.","translation":"Don't be an **idiot**, follow the traffic laws."},{"sentence":"Tawang-tawa ako sa'yo, **gago** ka!","translation":"You make me laugh so much, you **fool**! (affectionate)"}]

meaning_filipino: Naiintindihan o nauunawaan.
original_explanation: The Tagalized version of "understand." It's the confirmation you give your BPO team lead when they explain the new process for the fifth time. "Okay, gets na." It's faster than "Naiintindihan ko."
usage_notes: Isang kolokyal na salita na madalas gamitin sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Gets** mo ba ang sinasabi ko?","translation":"Do you **get** what I'm saying?"},{"sentence":"Ah, **gets** ko na kung bakit siya nagalit.","translation":"Ah, I **get** now why he got angry."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa maikling sandali lamang; pansamantala.
original_explanation: "Can I see you **pasaglit**?" is the official question of someone who needs to tell you some major chismis but only has a 5-minute coffee break. It's the Filipino version of 'just for a sec'. It implies a quick, temporary action, like dropping by a friend's house just to deliver something.
usage_notes: Often used as a polite way to request a small amount of someone's time or to indicate a brief action. Can be used interchangeably with "sandali lang".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumasok ako **pasaglit** sa opisina para kunin ang naiwan kong gamit.","translation":"I went into the office **for a moment** to get the thing I left behind."},{"sentence":"Maaari ba kitang makausap **pasaglit**?","translation":"May I speak with you **briefly**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Daglat para sa 'looking for group,' ginagamit sa mga online game upang maghanap ng mga makakasama sa isang laro o pangkat.
etymology: Daglat ng pariralang Ingles na 'looking for group.'
original_explanation: The gamer's classified ad. When you're tired of playing solo and getting bad teammates, you post 'LFG' in the chat, hoping to find a competent squad to help you rank up. It's the modern way of saying, 'Sino gusto kalaro?'
usage_notes: Tiyak na ginagamit sa mga komunidad ng online gaming.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**LFG** Valorant, need ko ng Sage main.","translation":"**Looking for group** for Valorant, I need a Sage main."},{"sentence":"Sawa na ako sa randoms, **LFG** na lang ako mamaya.","translation":"I'm tired of randoms, I'll just **look for a group** later."}]

translation: villager; person from a rural area
meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nakatira o nagmula sa isang nayon o pook rural.
original_explanation: The counterpart to the 'tagalunsod'. They wake up to the sound of roosters, not car horns. They know their neighbors' entire family history and probably get their food fresh from the backyard or the local market, not GrabFood. Often romanticized as living a 'simple life'.
usage_notes: Can be used interchangeably with 'tagabaryo' or the more general 'tagaprobinsya'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lahat ng **taganayon** ay nagtutulungan upang ihanda ang pista.","translation":"All the **villagers** are helping each other to prepare for the fiesta."},{"sentence":"Namangha ang mga **taganayon** sa bagong teknolohiya.","translation":"The **villagers** were amazed by the new technology."}]

meaning_filipino: Mayroong parehong bigat o timbang sa isang bagay na pinaghahambing.
etymology: From kasin- (variant of kasing-) + bigat. 'Kasin-' is used before roots starting with /b/ or /p/.
original_explanation: When your emotional baggage is kasimbigat ng bills mo for the month. Or when the chismis your friend is about to tell you is kasimbigat ng problema ng buong bansa. It's the ultimate 'same weight' comparison, for both literal and figurative burdens.
usage_notes: A comparative adjective used to equate the weight of two things.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang dala niyang sako ng bigas ay **kasimbigat** ng isang bata.","translation":"The sack of rice he was carrying was **as heavy as** a child."},{"sentence":"Para sa kanya, ang responsibilidad na ito ay **kasimbigat** ng mundo.","translation":"For him, this responsibility is **as heavy as** the world."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng post sa social media, karaniwan ay isang mapang-akit na larawan o video, na may layuning makakuha ng mga komento o mensahe na nagpapahayag ng pagnanasa.
etymology: Isang slang na pariralang Ingles, na pinagsasama ang "thirst" (pagnanasa) at "trap" (bitag), na nagpapahiwatig na ito ay isang bitag para sa mga taong 'uhaw'.
original_explanation: This isn't just bait; this is the whole fishing expedition with dynamite. A thirst trap is a photo or video posted with the *explicit* purpose of making people feel 'uhaw' (thirsty). Think post-workout pics with glistening sweat, 'woke up like this' selfies with perfect lighting, or any content that screams "I know I look good, now tell me about it." It's a power move in the digital world of 'landian'.
usage_notes: Isang napaka-karaniwang termino sa kultura ng internet upang ilarawan ang mga lantad na mapanuksong mga post.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **thirst trap** ang Instagram feed ng artistang iyon.","translation":"That celebrity's Instagram feed is full of **thirst traps**."},{"sentence":"Mag-po-post ako ng **thirst trap** mamaya para asarin ang ex ko.","translation":"I'm going to post a **thirst trap** later to annoy my ex."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong hinirang o inihalal upang kumatawan sa isang grupo, organisasyon, o bansa sa isang kumperensya, pulong, o pagtitipon.
original_explanation: The official "taga-attend ng seminar." Sila yung pinapadala ng office or school sa isang event, tapos pagbalik, sila ang tatanungin, "So, anong natutunan mo?" Sila rin ang may dalang free ballpen at conference kit.
usage_notes: May pambabaeng anyo, "delegada", ngunit madalas na ginagamit ang "delegado" para sa lahat ng kasarian sa modernong paggamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinadala ang isang **delegado** mula sa Pilipinas sa pandaigdigang pagpupulong.","translation":"A **delegate** from the Philippines was sent to the international meeting."},{"sentence":"Bilang **delegado**, tungkulin mong ipahayag ang saloobin ng iyong mga kinakatawan.","translation":"As a **delegate**, it is your duty to voice the sentiments of those you represent."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na para sa iisang tao lamang, o isang yunit. Sa balarila, ito ay tumutukoy sa anyong pang-isang bilang.
original_explanation: "Isahang kama" is a single bed. "Labanang isahan" is a one-on-one fight. It's the opposite of "para sa lahat" or group work. Think of it as the "solo mode" setting for things.
usage_notes: Describes something as being singular or intended for a single unit/person. Can also function as an adverb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas gusto niya ang **isahan** na kwarto kaysa sa dorm.","translation":"He prefers a **single** room over a dorm."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manunulat ng isang aklat, artikulo, o dokumento; ang lumikha o nagpasimula ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: Yung taong dahilan kung bakit ka napupuyat kakabasa ng libro o Wattpad story. Sila yung nag-imbento ng mga karakter na kinakikiligan o kinaiinisan mo.
