original_explanation: When things go from bad to worse. Yung ubo na naging lagnat, yung simpleng away na naging world war 3 sa family GC, or yung traffic sa EDSA na dati 1 hour lang, ngayon 3 hours na. 'Palala nang palala.'
usage_notes: Often used with 'nang' as in 'palala nang palala' (getting worse and worse).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Palala** nang **palala** ang sitwasyon dahil walang nakikinig.","translation":"The situation is **worsening** because no one is listening."}]

meaning_filipino: Lihim na patayin ang isang tao, karaniwan ay dahil sa krimen o alitan sa pulitika.
etymology: From 'i-' (causative prefix) + 'ligpit' (kept, stored), used euphemistically to mean "to put away permanently."
original_explanation: This is the darker, action-movie version of the word. When a witness in a movie "knows too much," the villain will order his goons, "Iligpit 'yan." It's a euphemism for assassination, a permanent way of 'tidying up' a problem.
usage_notes: This is a euphemism for "to kill" or "to assassinate," often used in the context of crime or conflict. It implies a clandestine, summary execution.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May utos daw na **iligpit** ang sinumang magiging testigo sa kaso.","translation":"There was supposedly an order to **eliminate** anyone who would become a witness in the case."},{"sentence":"Natatakot siyang baka siya ang isunod na **iligpit** ng sindikato.","translation":"He is afraid that the syndicate might **kill** him next."}]

translation: tilted; askew; inclined to one side
meaning_filipino: Nakahilig o nakatagilid sa isang direksyon; hindi tuwid o pantay ang pagkakatayo.
original_explanation: Like the Leaning Tower of Pisa, but for everyday things. A picture frame on the wall that's not straight is 'paling'. Your head when you're confused or trying to look cute in a selfie is 'paling'. 'Ayusin mo yung salamin mo, paling.'
usage_notes: Often used to describe objects that should be upright but are not. Can also describe a person's posture or head position.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **paling** ang poste ng kuryente dahil sa malakas na bagyo.","translation":"The electric post became **tilted** because of the strong typhoon."},{"sentence":"Napansin niyang **paling** ang pagkakalagay ng libro sa estante.","translation":"She noticed that the book on the shelf was placed **askew**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ritwal na sakramento sa Kristiyanismo, partikular sa Simbahang Katoliko, kung saan tinatanggap ang Banal na Ostiya bilang katawan ni Kristo.
original_explanation: This is that part of the Catholic Mass where you line up, looking your holiest, to receive the host. As a kid, it was the moment you'd try not to let the wafer stick to the roof of your mouth. It's the solemn 'snack time' in church, a key part of Catholic life and tradition.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to the Roman Catholic sacrament of Holy Communion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Unang **Pagkokomunyon** ay isang mahalagang yugto sa buhay ng isang batang Katoliko.","translation":"The First **Communion** is an important stage in the life of a Catholic child."},{"sentence":"Mahaba ang pila para sa **pagkokomunyon** tuwing Linggo ng umaga.","translation":"The line for the **act of taking communion** is long every Sunday morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na nasuri na at nabigyan ng katumbas na halaga o presyo.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "tasado" (appraised), mula sa pandiwang "tasar" (to appraise).
original_explanation: This is what happens to your family's old jewelry when you take it to a pawnshop. "Ma'am, tasado na po, ito po ang halaga." It's the official price tag slapped onto something after an expert looks at it. Think of it as the "official IG price" versus the "PM is the key" price.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng pagsasangla, pagbebenta ng ari-arian, o insurance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tasado** na ang mga alahas na isinangla niya.","translation":"The jewelry she pawned has been **appraised**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nauukol sa diplomasya; nagpapakita ng kasanayan sa pakikitungo sa mga tao nang hindi nakakasakit ng damdamin.
original_explanation: Yung kaibigan mong kahit anong chismis ang sabihin mo, ang sagot laging "I see," "interesting," or "may point ka diyan." Hindi kumakampi, hindi nakikipag-away, pang-United Nations ang peg. Ganyan maging diplomatiko.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng **diplomatiko** na paraan upang malutas ang alitan ng dalawang bansa.","translation":"A **diplomatic** approach is needed to resolve the conflict between the two countries."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa pagiging **diplomatiko** sa pakikipag-usap kahit sa mahihirap na kliyente.","translation":"He is known for being **diplomatic** in conversations even with difficult clients."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggalaw o paglipat mula sa isang posisyon o kinalalagyan patungo sa iba.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung ginagawa mo sa upuan mo 'pag nangangalay ka na, umiibag ka para humanap ng mas komportableng pwesto. O 'yung bato sa daan na biglang umibag nung natapakan mo. Medyo luma na 'tong salita, parang 'umalis' or 'gumalaw' na lang ang gamit ngayon.
usage_notes: A somewhat rare or literary word. 'Gumalaw' or 'umalis' are much more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umibag** ang bato nang bahagya nang masagi ito ng kanyang paa.","translation":"The rock **moved** slightly when his foot grazed it."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **umibag** diyan sa pwesto mo.","translation":"Don't **move** from your spot."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa butil ng palay na inalisan na ng ipa at balat, handa nang isaing upang maging kanin.
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino lifeblood before it hits the rice cooker. It's not kanin (cooked rice) yet, it's the raw, hard grains you buy by the kilo sa palengke. Having a sack of this at home is the Pinoy equivalent of a fully-charged power bank – it means you're prepared for anything. Staple food in its pre-glow up stage.
usage_notes: Tandaan na iba ang 'bigas' (uncooked rice) sa 'kanin' (cooked rice) at 'palay' (unhusked rice).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng isang sakong **bigas** sa palengke.","translation":"Mom bought a sack of **uncooked rice** at the market."},{"sentence":"Hugasang mabuti ang **bigas** bago ito isaing.","translation":"Wash the **uncooked rice** well before cooking it."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang agham at sining ng paghahanda, pag-iimbak, at pagbibigay ng mga gamot.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "farmacéutica," ang anyong pambabae na ginagamit para sa agham o larangan.
original_explanation: This is the "-ics" or the science/field of study behind the "parmaseutiko" (pharmacist). It's the whole industry and knowledge base of making and distributing medicine. Kung ang parmaseutiko ay ang chef, ang **parmasiyutika** ay ang buong culinary arts. It's the big, brainy word for the world of pharmaceuticals.
usage_notes: Naiiba sa "parmasya" o "botika," na tumutukoy sa pisikal na tindahan (drugstore/pharmacy). Ang salitang ito ay tumutukoy sa agham o industriya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang larangan ng **parmasiyutika** ay mabilis na umuunlad dahil sa teknolohiya.","translation":"The field of **pharmaceutics** is rapidly advancing due to technology."},{"sentence":"Kumuha siya ng kurso sa **parmasiyutika** sa unibersidad.","translation":"She took a course in **pharmacy** (the science) at the university."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkuha ng sabaw, kanin, o anumang pagkain gamit ang sandok.
original_explanation: The official verb for getting your fair share of sinigang broth or that mountain of rice. It's the action you do before asking "Pwedeng paabot ng patis?" The bigger the *sandok*, the happier the tummy.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to scooping with a ladle (*sandok*). The infix '-um-' indicates the actor-focus, completed aspect (past tense).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumandok** siya ng mainit na sabaw para sa may sakit.","translation":"He **scooped** some hot soup for the sick person."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **sumandok** ng huling kanin sa kaldero?","translation":"Who **scooped** the last of the rice from the pot?"}]

translation: act of shooing away; driving away
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpapaalis o pagtataboy sa mga hayop, insekto, o tao sa isang lugar.
etymology: From pag- (gerund prefix) + bugaw (shoo, drive away).
original_explanation: This is what you do to a fly that won't leave your halo-halo alone, or to that persistent suitor your parents don't like. It's the act of shooing something or someone away, with hand gestures, loud noises, or just a very pointed 'Umalis ka nga!' stare.
usage_notes: Be cautious as 'bugaw' can also refer to a pimp, although the context usually makes the meaning clear. 'Pagbugaw' specifically refers to the action of shooing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagbugaw** sa mga langaw ay naging trabaho ng bata.","translation":"The **shooing away** of flies became the child's job."},{"sentence":"Isang malakas na palakpak lang ang kailangan para sa **pagbugaw** sa mga ibon.","translation":"Just one loud clap is needed for **driving away** the birds."}]

translation: one who shares in grief; sympathizer
meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kasama o kaagapay sa panahon ng kalungkutan, pagsubok, o pagdadalamhati; taong nakikiramay.
original_explanation: This is your ride-or-die friend during tough times, especially during a wake or a major life problem. They're the one who brings you food when you're grieving, listens to your rants, and just sits with you in silence. Hindi lang sila "nakikiramay" sa text; andiyan sila, physically and emotionally. Sila yung totoong 'shoulder to cry on'.
usage_notes: Deeply cultural, associated with the Filipino value of 'pakikiramay' (sympathy, condolence).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **karamay** ang pamilya sa kanilang pagdadalamhati.","translation":"The family has many **sympathizers** in their time of grief."},{"sentence":"Sa oras ng pangangailangan, malalaman mo kung sino ang tunay mong **karamay**.","translation":"In times of need, you will know who your true **allies in hardship** are."}]

translation: a confounder; something that causes confusion
meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, pahayag, o sitwasyon na nagdudulot ng kalituhan o pagkaligaw ng isip.
original_explanation: This is that 'mixed signal' from your crush, the vague instructions from your boss, or the plot twist in a teleserye that makes no sense. It's anything designed to make you go 'Ha? Ano daw?' and short-circuit your brain. The ultimate 'paasa' move.
usage_notes: Used for things that are intentionally or unintentionally confusing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagbigay siya ng mga **pampalito** na sagot para hindi mahuli.","translation":"He gave **confounding** answers so he wouldn't get caught."},{"sentence":"Ang mga tanong sa exam ay may mga **pampalito**.","translation":"The questions on the exam had some **confounders**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pandiwa ng pag-kaykay; ang paghalukay o pagkalmot sa isang partikular na lugar o bagay.
original_explanation: This is the command form of "kaykay." It's what you tell your dog when you want it to dig for a hidden treat: "Kaykayin mo!" It's also what you do to that pile of laundry on your "chairdrobe" when you're looking for that one specific shirt. You're not just looking, you're actively digging and scratching through the pile.
usage_notes: Verb form. Conjugations: kinaykay (past), kinakaykay (present), kakaykayin (future).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kinaykay** ng aso ang lupa upang itago ang kanyang buto.","translation":"The dog **scratched** up the ground to hide its bone."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **kaykayin** ang bunton ng buhangin para mahanap ang kabibe.","translation":"You need **to dig up** the pile of sand to find the shell."}]

translation: will be made to lose weight; will become thin
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagbabawas ng timbang o ang maging sanhi ng pagiging mas manipis ng katawan.
original_explanation: Everyone's New Year's resolution. It's what happens (or what you hope happens) after weeks of gym, diet, and resisting milk tea. "Huwag mo akong papayatin sa stress, please lang." (Don't make me lose weight from stress, please.)
usage_notes: Future tense. Can be causative ("Papayatin ka ng sakit na 'yan" - That sickness will make you thin) or a goal ("Magpapayat ako" is more common for a personal goal, while "papayatin" is often something done to you).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sabi ng doktor, kailangan siyang **papayatin** para sa kanyang kalusugan.","translation":"The doctor said, he needs **to be made to lose weight** for his health."},{"sentence":"Ang bagong diet plan daw ang **papayatin** sa kanya.","translation":"They say the new diet plan is what **will make her become thin**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong kasuklam-suklam, walang kuwenta, o nagtataglay ng mga katangiang lubhang kinasusuklaman. Literal na nangangahulugang 'amoy dumi ng tao'.
etymology: Isang tambalang salita mula sa 'amoy' (smell) at 'tae' (feces).
original_explanation: When someone is so useless, treacherous, or just plain awful, they're not just 'plastic' or 'a snake', they're literally `amoytae`. It's the ultimate 'you're trash' insult, reserved for the worst of the worst, like a corrupt official or a backstabbing 'friend'.
usage_notes: Isang napakabigat at bulgar na panlalait. Gamitin nang may lubos na pag-iingat dahil ito ay lubhang nakakainsulto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala sa kanya, **amoytae** ang ugali ng taong 'yan.","translation":"Don't believe him, that person's character is **contemptible**."},{"sentence":"Tinawag siyang **amoytae** ng taumbayan dahil sa kanyang pagnanakaw sa kaban ng bayan.","translation":"The people called him **worthless** because he stole from the nation's treasury."}]

translation: to install a floor, to floor
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng sahig o patag na latag sa isang bahay, silid, o anumang istruktura.
original_explanation: Literally, to put a floor down. The adulting version of 'building your foundation.' Before you can buy the fancy furniture, you need to magsahig first. You can't just live on dirt, unless that's your aesthetic.
usage_notes: A specific construction term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpaplano silang **magsahig** ng kahoy sa kanilang bagong bahay.","translation":"They are planning to **install a wood floor** in their new house."},{"sentence":"Magkano ang singil para **magsahig** ng isang buong kwarto?","translation":"How much is the charge to **floor** an entire room?"}]

translation: To chip off; to hew; to trim by cutting.
meaning_filipino: Putulin o alisin ang isang bahagi ng isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng matalas na kasangkapan; pag-ukit sa pamamagitan ng pagtatagpas.
original_explanation: Like a sculptor chipping away at a block of stone, or when you try to trim your own bangs and accidentally tapyas too much. It's a more aggressive form of trimming, often with a blade. Also, what happens to your budget before payday.
usage_notes: Implies using a tool to cut or shape something, often stone, wood, or even hair.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais ng iskultor na **tapyasin** ang marmol upang makabuo ng isang obra.","translation":"The sculptor wants to **hew** the marble to create a masterpiece."},{"sentence":"Ingatan mong huwag **tapyasin** ang daliri mo habang nagpuputol ng kahoy.","translation":"Be careful not to **chip** your finger while cutting wood."}]

meaning_filipino: Nakakaramdam ng sukdulang kagalakan o kasiyahan; lubos na masaya.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `napaka-` (nagpapahiwatig ng sukdulang antas) at salitang ugat na `ligaya` (joy, happiness).
original_explanation: The feeling when your Shopee/Lazada package arrives. The joy of seeing your salary credited to your bank account. The kilig when your crush views your IG story. It’s not just 'happy', it’s pure, unadulterated, smiling-like-an-idiot kind of joy.
usage_notes: Expresses a deeper, more profound happiness than 'napakasaya'. 'Ligaya' often implies a state of bliss or deep contentment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Napakaligaya** ng mag-asawa sa pagdating ng kanilang unang anak.","translation":"The couple was **ecstatic** at the arrival of their first child."},{"sentence":"Isang **napakaligayang** alaala ang aming paglalakbay sa Palawan.","translation":"Our trip to Palawan is a **very happy** memory."}]

translation: to apply; to place on; to fit together
meaning_filipino: Paglalagay o pagdidikit ng isang bagay sa ibabaw ng isa pa nang may kaayusan at katiyakan. Maaari rin itong tumukoy sa pagbibigay ng isang bagay, tulad ng parusa o lunas.
original_explanation: This is the verb for when things need to fit perfectly or be applied just right. Like a 'first-aid' move: 'maglapat ng gamot sa sugat' (apply medicine to a wound). Or when you're a carpenter making sure two pieces of wood join seamlessly. It's also used for delivering something more abstract, like justice: 'maglapat ng parusa' (to apply a penalty). It's about precise contact and application.
usage_notes: Can be used for physical application (ointment, bandage) or for abstract concepts (justice, punishment).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **maglapat** ng yelo sa iyong bukol.","translation":"You need to **apply** ice to your bump."},{"sentence":"Ang hukom ang **maglalapat** ng karampatang parusa sa nagkasala.","translation":"The judge will **apply** the appropriate punishment to the guilty party."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang posisyon o antas ng isang tao o bagay sa isang sistema ng herarkiya o klasipikasyon.
original_explanation: This is your level sa Mobile Legends, your position sa office hierarchy, or your place in the social food chain. From Private to General, from Junior Dev to CTO, from 'seen-zoned' to 'in a relationship'—lahat 'yan may ranggo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano na ba ang **ranggo** mo sa laro?","translation":"What's your **rank** in the game now?"},{"sentence":"Mataas ang **ranggo** niya sa kumpanya kaya malaki ang responsibilidad.","translation":"He has a high **rank** in the company, so he has a big responsibility."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang yugto sa buhay ng isang tao kung saan pinagtutuunan niya ng pansin ang pagsasarili sa pananalapi, emosyon, at pamumuhay nang hindi umaasa sa iba.
original_explanation: This is when you're in your 'I can buy my own flowers' phase. You're focusing on your career, your finances, your glow-up, and you're not waiting for a jowa to make you happy. You pay your own bills, you fix your own problems, and your only 'sana all' is for more sleep. The 'independent woman era' is the more specific and popular version of this.
usage_notes: A popular social media term, especially on platforms like TikTok and Instagram, primarily used by young adults and women.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa **independent era** daw siya kaya puro trabaho at travel ang focus niya ngayon.","translation":"She says she's in her **independent era**, so her focus right now is all work and travel."},{"sentence":"Sabi ng nanay ko, tigilan ko na raw ang **independent woman era** ko at mag-asawa na.","translation":"My mom told me to stop my **independent woman era** and get married already."}]

translation: will be liked; will be found pleasing
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan kung saan ang isang bagay o tao ay magiging kalugod-lugod o kaibig-ibig sa panlasa o damdamin ng iba sa hinaharap.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `ma-` (potensyal na pandiwa) + pag-uulit ng unang pantig ng ugat `gu-` (panahong panghinaharap) + `gusto` (like/want) + hulaping `-han` (locative/benefactive).
original_explanation: What you hope your crush's parents think of you when you finally meet them. 'Sa tingin mo, magugustuhan kaya nila ako?' It's the future tense of being liked, filled with anxiety and the desire for approval. Also what you tell yourself about the weird dish you cooked: 'Sana magustuhan nila.'
usage_notes: Ito ay nasa pokus sa layon, panahong panghinaharap. Ang paksa ng pangungusap ay ang bagay na nagugustuhan, at ang gumaganap (ang nagkakagusto) ay karaniwang ipinapahiwatig ng 'ni' o 'ng'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sigurado akong **magugustuhan** mo ang bagong kanta ng Ben&Ben.","translation":"I'm sure you **will like** the new song by Ben&Ben."},{"sentence":"Ipinagluto ko siya ng adobo, sana **magugustuhan** niya.","translation":"I cooked adobo for him, I hope he **will like** it."}]

translation: to side with; to take someone's side
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpanig o pagkiling sa isang tao, grupo, o pananaw, lalo na sa isang alitan o kompetisyon.
etymology: From "kampi" + "-han" suffix. "Kampi" is from Spanish "campo" (camp, side).
original_explanation: This is what happens in every family gathering, office drama, or even sa national elections. It's choosing your team, your 'kakampi.' It's the 'you can't sit with us' of the adult world. 'Bakit mo siya kinakampihan? Dahil ba crush mo?'
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of conflict, debate, or competition. It implies choosing one side over another.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **kampihan** ang mali, kahit pa kaibigan mo siya.","translation":"Don't **side with** what is wrong, even if it's your friend."},{"sentence":"Sa debate, agad na nagkaroon ng **kampihan** ang mga manonood.","translation":"In the debate, the audience immediately started **taking sides**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang impormal na pagpapaikli para sa salitang "scandal" o "iskandalo," na tumutukoy sa isang kaganapan na nagdudulot ng galit o pagkasira ng reputasyon.
original_explanation: Short for 'scandal'. Kapag may bagong chismis, video, or issue na viral at pinag-uusapan ng lahat, 'yan ang "latest SC." From showbiz love triangles to political controversies, basta may drama at kahihiyan, may SC.
usage_notes: Commonly used in social media and online forums.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita mo na ba 'yung bagong **SC** sa Twitter?","translation":"Have you seen the new **scandal** on Twitter?"},{"sentence":"Laging may **SC** na lumalabas tuwing malapit na ang eleksyon.","translation":"A **scandal** always comes out whenever the election is near."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bulalas na nagpapahayag ng pagkagulat, pagtataka, o banayad na pagsaway.
etymology: Hindi tiyak ang pinagmulan ngunit karaniwang ginagamit bilang isang ekspresyon.
original_explanation: The verbal equivalent of a side-eye or a "Talaga ba?" It's what your mom says when you ask for more allowance right after getting it. "Abay, saan mo naman dinala ang pera mo?" It's less aggressive than "Hoy!" but carries that perfect blend of surprise and gentle disappointment.
usage_notes: The tone is crucial. It can be playful, surprised, or slightly annoyed. Often used at the beginning of a sentence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Abay**, nandito ka lang pala! Kanina pa kita hinahanap.","translation":"**Well**, so you're here! I've been looking for you."},{"sentence":"**Abay**, ang ganda naman ng suot mo ngayon!","translation":"**Hey**, your outfit looks really nice today!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang yunit ng timbang na katumbas ng 1,000 kilo o humigit-kumulang 2,204 libra.
original_explanation: Imagine mo 'yung bigat ng sama ng loob mo after ka i-ghost, tapos i-multiply mo by one thousand. 'Yan ang isang tonelada. O kaya 'yung bigat ng traffic sa EDSA tuwing Biyernes ng hapon. Ginagamit para sa sobrang bigat na bagay, literal man o figurative.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa pagtukoy sa napakabigat na bagay, literal man o matalinghaga.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **tonelada**ng bigas ang donasyon ng samahan.","translation":"The organization donated one **ton** of rice."},{"sentence":"**Tonelada**ng problema ang kinakaharap niya ngayon.","translation":"He is facing a **ton** of problems right now."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na nagpapahayag ng matinding paghanga o pagsang-ayon.
etymology: Slang, likely from the 1970s. Origin uncertain, but possibly an expressive, arbitrary term.
original_explanation: This is your tito's version of 'lit,' 'fire,' or 'slay.' Back in the 70s and 80s, if something was incredibly cool, it was 'Hanip!'. A cool car? 'Hanip!'. A great guitar solo? 'Hanip!'. It's retro cool, like bell-bottoms and VST & Co.
usage_notes: Considered dated or retro slang. Using it now might get you a knowing smile from older generations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hanip** ang galing mo sa gitara!","translation":"You're **awesome** at guitar!"},{"sentence":"Wow, **hanip** 'yang kotse mo, pare!","translation":"Wow, your car is **cool**, dude!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na responsable sa pamamahala at pagpapanatili ng kaayusan sa isang sambahayan, kasama na ang paggabay sa ibang mga katulong.
etymology: Isang parirala na pinagsasama ang 'tagapangasiwa' (administrator) at 'ng/sa bahay' (of/at the house).
original_explanation: This is the manager of the household staff. Not just the 'kasambahay', but the one who *manages* the kasambahays. Sila yung head of house, the majordomo, the one who makes sure the whole house runs like a well-oiled machine, from the cook to the driver to the gardener. Think of Alfred to Batman.
usage_notes: Isang mas pormal at mas mataas na antas na termino kaysa 'kasambahay' o 'katulong'. Nagpapahiwatig ng isang manedyeryal na tungkulin sa loob ng isang sambahayan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **tagapangasiwa ng bahay** ang nag-aayos ng iskedyul ng mga katulong.","translation":"The **house manager** arranges the schedule of the helpers."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang tiwala ng mag-asawa sa kanilang **tagapangasiwa sa bahay**.","translation":"The couple has great trust in their **housekeeper**."}]

translation: not picky; one who doesn't refuse or dislike anything
meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng tao na tumatanggap o gusto ang lahat ng bagay o pagkaing inihahain at hindi namimili.
original_explanation: The human equivalent of a stray cat you feed once. They'll eat anything you give them, from your mom's sinigang to that questionable street food. They're the best 'kain buddy' because they never say no. Zero arte.
usage_notes: Often used to describe someone's non-picky attitude towards food, but can also apply to tasks, people, or activities.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang paboritong bisita ni lola dahil **walang-inaayawan** siyang pagkain.","translation":"She is grandma's favorite guest because she is **not picky** with any food."},{"sentence":"Humanap ka ng empleyadong **walang-inaayawan** na trabaho, 'yung game sa lahat.","translation":"Find an employee who **doesn't refuse** any work, someone who's game for anything."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang ginagamit upang magpahayag ng pagkagulat, pagtataka, paghanga, o banayad na pagsaway.
etymology: Pinaniniwalaang nagmula sa sinaunang mga wika sa Pilipinas, ginagamit bilang panawag-pansin.
original_explanation: The Swiss Army knife of Filipino expressions. Can mean "Wow!" ("Aba, ang ganda!"), "Hey, what gives?" ("Aba, bakit mo kinuha 'yan?"), or "Of course!" ("Aba, oo naman!"). It's the ultimate 'tita' reaction word.
usage_notes: The meaning is heavily dependent on the intonation and context. It can express a wide range of emotions from pleasant surprise to mild indignation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Aba**, nandito ka na pala! Kanina ka pa namin hinihintay.","translation":"**Oh**, you're here already! We've been waiting for you."},{"sentence":"**Aba**, ang galing mo namang sumayaw!","translation":"**Wow**, you're such a great dancer!"},{"sentence":"**Aba**, bakit mo pinakialaman ang gamit ko?","translation":"**Hey**, why did you meddle with my things?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang isang maliit at partikular na bahagi ng isang kabuuan; mga tiyak na impormasyon tungkol sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: What your chismosa kapitbahay wants to know about your breakup. 'Anong nangyari? Give me the deets!' Also, what your boss asks for in a report when you thought you were already done. From the Spanish 'detalle'.
usage_notes: The verb form is 'detalyehin' (to detail something).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutan ang maliliit na **detalye** sa iyong ulat.","translation":"Don't forget the small **details** in your report."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ko pa ng karagdagang **detalye** tungkol sa proyekto.","translation":"I still need more **details** about the project."}]

meaning_filipino: Nauukol o tumutukoy sa mga rehiyon na malapit sa ekwador, na karaniwang may mainit at mahalumigmig na klima sa buong taon.
original_explanation: Eto yung klima natin sa Pinas. Yung tipong kahit December na, pawis na pawis ka pa rin. Perfect for the beach, pero challenge sa makeup. 'Tropical country' ang auto-reply natin 'pag may nagreklamo sa init.
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang ilarawan ang klima, prutas, halaman, o anumang bagay na nagmula o katangian ng mga tropiko.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **tropikal** na prutas sa Pilipinas tulad ng mangga at pinya.","translation":"There are many **tropical** fruits in the Philippines like mangoes and pineapples."},{"sentence":"Ang **tropikal** na klima ay nangangahulugang dalawang panahon lang: tag-araw at tag-ulan.","translation":"The **tropical** climate means there are only two seasons: dry season and wet season."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkalahatang katawagan para sa anumang isinusuot sa paa, tulad ng sapatos, tsinelas, o sandalyas, para sa proteksyon at kaginhawaan.
original_explanation: This is the formal, almost clinical term for anything you put on your feet. While you'd normally say 'sapatos' or 'tsinelas,' if you're writing a school report or a formal invitation with a dress code ('Pormal na kasuotan at angkop na sapin sa paa'), you'd use 'sapin sa paa.' It's the 'footwear' to your everyday 'shoes.'
usage_notes: A formal and general term encompassing all types of items worn on the feet.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagbabawal ang pagpasok nang walang maayos na **sapin sa paa**.","translation":"Entering without proper **footwear** is prohibited."},{"sentence":"Anong **sapin sa paa** ang bagay sa damit na ito?","translation":"What **footwear** matches this dress?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng de-latang gatas na dumaan sa proseso ng pag-aalis ng malaking bahagi ng tubig nito.
original_explanation: The formal name for 'evap'. You use this full term when you're reading a recipe from a cookbook or watching a formal cooking show. In the palengke or sari-sari store, it's just 'evap'. Using the full 'evaporated milk' in casual conversation is like calling your friend by their full government name—a bit too serious.
usage_notes: Often shortened to 'evap' in everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayon sa resipi, kailangan mo ng isang tasa ng **evaporated milk**.","translation":"According to the recipe, you need one cup of **evaporated milk**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marahas na pagbuka o paghiwalay sa isang bagay na nakasara o magkadikit, karaniwan gamit ang puwersa.
original_explanation: Imagine trying to open a can of sardines without a can opener, or forcing open a locked door. That's hiniklat. It’s a bit aggressive, like when you finally get your hands on a bag of chips and just rip it open without looking for the tear-here notch.
usage_notes: Often implies a sudden, forceful, and sometimes damaging action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Galit na **hiniklat** niya ang sobre na naglalaman ng masamang balita.","translation":"He angrily **pried open** the envelope that contained the bad news."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **hiniklat** ang kahon, baka masira ang laman.","translation":"Don't **pull open** the box forcefully, the contents might get damaged."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng tradisyonal na awit o tula na pasalaysay, partikular sa mga pangkat etniko tulad ng Maranao at Maguindanao, na kadalasang inaawit sa mga mahahalagang okasyon.
original_explanation: This is an epic chant, a traditional form of storytelling through song, especially in Mindanao. Think of it as the original Filipino rap battle or spoken word poetry, but with more cultural weight and history. It’s not your typical pop song; it's a performance art that carries the stories of a people.
usage_notes: Specific to certain ethnolinguistic groups in the Philippines, particularly the Maranao and Maguindanao peoples. It's a key part of their oral traditions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakinig kami sa isang matanda na umaawit ng **bayok** tungkol sa kasaysayan ng kanilang lahi.","translation":"We listened to an elder who was chanting a **narrative chant** about the history of their people."},{"sentence":"Ang **bayok** ay isang mahalagang bahagi ng kultura ng mga Maranao.","translation":"The **bayok** is an important part of the Maranao culture."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubos-lubos; ibinibigay ang lahat ng lakas, kakayahan, o pansin; walang anumang pagtitimpi.
original_explanation: This is 'todo' but on steroids. It's not just giving your all, it's giving your all, your cousin's all, and your dog's all. It's the level of effort you put in when cramming for an exam the night before, or when cleaning the house because your crush is coming over.
usage_notes: An emphatic form of 'todo', signifying extreme or maximum effort or intensity. It functions as an adverb describing how an action is done.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Todo-todo** ang pag-awit niya sa videoke, ramdam na ramdam ang hugot.","translation":"He/She sang **all-out** on the videoke, you could really feel the heartache."},{"sentence":"Nag-aral siya nang **todo-todo** para sa board exam.","translation":"He/She studied with **full force** for the board exam."}]

translation: to go through hastily; to rush through with difficulty
meaning_filipino: Pilit na dumaan o maglakbay sa isang mahirap na lugar o sitwasyon; magmadali sa paggawa ng isang bagay nang walang ingat.
original_explanation: Imagine running through a crowded palengke while it's raining, or trying to finish a 100-page report in one night. That's sumasagsag. It’s messy, rushed, and probably involves a lot of stress and coffee. It's the verb form of 'Hala, sige, bahala na!'
usage_notes: Implies haste, difficulty, and often a lack of grace or carefulness. Can be used for physical movement or for completing a task.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumagsag** ang motorsiklo sa makitid at maputik na eskinita.","translation":"The motorcycle **rushed through** the narrow and muddy alley."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **sumagsag** sa trabaho para makahabol sa deadline.","translation":"I need to **plow through** work to meet the deadline."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang direksiyong nasa pagitan ng hilaga at silangan.
original_explanation: The direction of the 'Amihan' winds that bring cooler, drier air from December to February. It's the reason you can finally wear that jacket you bought on sale. On the map from Manila, it's the general direction of provinces like Isabela and Cagayan.
usage_notes: An intermediate cardinal direction, often associated with the Amihan (Northeast Monsoon).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang hanging Amihan ay nanggagaling sa **hilagang-silangan**.","translation":"The Amihan winds come from the **northeast**."},{"sentence":"Ang Cagayan Valley ay nasa rehiyon ng **hilagang-silangan** ng Luzon.","translation":"Cagayan Valley is in the **northeast** region of Luzon."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bulalas na nagpapahayag ng matinding pananabik, pagkasabik, o determinasyon.
etymology: Acronym for the English phrase 'Let's fucking go.'
original_explanation: The upgraded, more intense version of 'Lezzgo!' This is what you scream (or type in all caps) when you finally get your concert tickets, your team wins, or you're about to do something epic. It's pure, unadulterated hype energy. The verbal equivalent of a shot of espresso mixed with Red Bull.
usage_notes: Lubhang impormal at naglalaman ng salitang may pagmumura. Ginagamit upang ipahayag ang matinding kagalakan o motibasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pasok tayo sa finals! **LFG**!!","translation":"We made it to the finals! **Let's fucking go**!!"},{"sentence":"Approved ang leave! Boracay, **LFG**!","translation":"My leave is approved! Boracay, **let's fucking go**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang supot o lalagyan, karaniwang yari sa katad, na isinusuot sa baywang o katawan para paglagyan ng baril.
original_explanation: The little leather pouch that every Pinoy action star from the 90s, from FPJ to Rudy Fernandez, had for their .45 caliber pistol. It's the fanny pack for guns.
usage_notes: Primarily used in contexts involving police, military, security personnel, or action movies.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakasabit sa kanyang sinturon ang **holster** na may lamang baril.","translation":"The **holster** containing a gun was hanging from his belt."},{"sentence":"Itinago ng pulis ang kanyang baril sa **holster**.","translation":"The policeman hid his gun in the **holster**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tradisyonal na palabas, na nagmula sa Espanya, kung saan ang isang torero (bullfighter) ay nakikipaglaban sa isang toro sa loob ng isang arena.
etymology: From Spanish 'corrida' (short for 'corrida de toros,' meaning 'running of bulls').
original_explanation: This is that sport in Spain where a bull keeps charging at a red cloth. Think matador versus a very angry bull. It's not common here in the Philippines, but we know the concept because of Spanish influence. It's like your fight with your partner: one is an angry bull, and the other is waving a 'red flag'.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to the Spanish-style bullfight.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napanood niya ang isang **korida** nang bumisita siya sa Madrid.","translation":"He watched a **bullfight** when he visited Madrid."},{"sentence":"Mapanganib at kontrobersyal ang isport na **korida**.","translation":"The sport of **bullfighting** is dangerous and controversial."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing higit o labis sa kung ano ang totoo o kailangan.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of being "extra." It's what you do when you're writing your resume and you turn "answered emails" into "managed and streamlined internal and external communication channels." You're not lying, you're just choosing to palabisin the details.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang **palabisin** ang kuwento, sabihin mo ang totoo.","translation":"Don't **exaggerate** the story anymore, just tell the truth."}]

translation: a cartful; the contents of a cart
meaning_filipino: Ang dami o kantidad ng mga bagay na kayang isakay o ilaman sa isang kariton.
etymology: From "kariton" + "-an" suffix, indicating a measure or quantity.
original_explanation: If "kariton" is the pushcart, "karitunan" is the *amount* of stuff you can cram into it. "Isang karitunan ng mangga" means a whole pushcart's worth of mangoes. It's the unit of measurement for when you're buying in bulk, palengke-style. It’s like saying a "truckload" but for the more humble kariton.
usage_notes: Used as a unit of measure.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili siya ng isang **karitunan** ng pakwan para sa pista.","translation":"He bought a **cartful** of watermelons for the fiesta."},{"sentence":"Isang **karitunan** na basura ang nakuha sa paglilinis ng kanal.","translation":"A **cartful** of trash was collected from cleaning the canal."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang maramdaman o mapansin ang isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pandama o emosyon.
original_explanation: That moment when you suddenly feel something, either physical (like a sudden chill) or emotional (like that familiar pang of "kilig" when your crush messages you). It's the ability to catch feelings, literally and figuratively. "Sana all nakakadama pa."
usage_notes: Often used for emotions, but can also be for physical sensations. `Makarandam` is a common variant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **makadama** ka rin ng pagmamahal na ibinibigay ko sa iyo.","translation":"I hope you can also **feel** the love I am giving you."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula siyang **makadama** ng pagod matapos ang mahabang lakaran.","translation":"He started to **feel** tired after the long walk."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong palaging umaasa o humihingi ng libre mula sa iba at bihirang magbigay ng sariling ambag.
etymology: Colloquial term, possibly a portmanteau or evolved slang. Exact origin is unclear.
original_explanation: That 'friend' who always shows up to the inuman or kainan but never contributes to the bill. Their wallet is always 'naiwan sa bahay' and their favorite phrase is 'Penge ako.' They have a Ph.D. in Freeloading from the University of Kapal-Muks.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun to describe a person or an adjective to describe behavior.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **buraot** sa handaan, mag-ambag ka naman.","translation":"Don't be a **moocher** at the party, contribute something."},{"sentence":"Lagi siyang sumasama pero hindi nagbabayad, napaka-**buraot** talaga.","translation":"He always joins but never pays, he's such a **freeloader**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pagtatanghal o panoorin na naglalaman ng mga eksenang mahalay, malaswa, o hindi angkop sa pangkalahatang manonood.
original_explanation: Anything that would make the MTRCB slap a big 'SPG' (Striktong Patnubay at Gabay) rating on it. Think burlesque shows, some raunchy stand-up comedy, or that movie your parents immediately changed the channel on.
usage_notes: 'Palabas' can refer to a live performance, a TV show, or a movie.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-raid ang mga pulis sa isang bar na may **bastos na palabas**.","translation":"The police raided a bar that had a **lewd performance**."},{"sentence":"Bawal sa mga bata ang manood ng mga **bastos na palabas**.","translation":"It is forbidden for children to watch **obscene shows**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nakaayos nang paakyat o pababa na parang mga baitang o hagdanan; isinasagawa nang paunti-unti o ayon sa antas.
original_explanation: Imagine the Banaue Rice Terraces – that's a perfect example of 'bai-baitang.' It can also describe a process, like a tutorial that's 'bai-baitang,' meaning it's step-by-step, easy to follow, from Level 1 to Boss Level. It's about gradual progression.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang mga tanawin (tulad ng mga hagdan-hagdang palayan) o mga proseso (tulad ng mga tagubilin).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga palayan sa Banaue ay **bai-baitang**.","translation":"The rice paddies in Banaue are **terraced**."},{"sentence":"Itinuro niya ang proseso sa paraang **bai-baitang** para madaling maintindihan.","translation":"He taught the process in a **step-by-step** manner so it would be easy to understand."}]

meaning_filipino: Sadyang sirain, hadlangan, o guluhin ang isang gawain, plano, o sistema, lalo na para sa politikal o personal na kapakinabangan.
etymology: From 'sabutahe' (sabotage), from Spanish 'sabotaje'. The verb is formed with the actor-focus infix '-um-'.
original_explanation: The act of being a snake. It's when you secretly mess things up for someone else. That coworker who 'accidentally' deleted your presentation? **Sumabutahe** 'yan. The friend who tells your crush you have a weird hobby? Sabotage! It's the ultimate backstab, the shady move done to make someone else fail. It's not 'teamwork makes the dream work,' it's 'I work to make your dream a nightmare.'
usage_notes: A strong word implying deliberate and malicious intent to cause failure or disruption.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May hinala silang may **sumabutahe** sa makina ng pabrika.","translation":"They suspect that someone **sabotaged** the factory's machine."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **sumabutahe** sa iyong mga pangarap ang negatibong komento ng iba.","translation":"Don't let the negative comments of others **sabotage** your dreams."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang halaga na kailangang bayaran; mga gastusin o obligasyong pinansyal.
etymology: From "bayad" (payment) + "-in" suffix (denoting an object to be acted upon).
original_explanation: Your adulting nightmare starter pack. **Bayarin** are all the bills that haunt you at the end of the month: Meralco, Maynilad, Wi-Fi, credit card, rent. It's the plural form of "sakit sa ulo." "Ang dami kong **bayarin**" is the national motto after payday.
usage_notes: Refers to the things to be paid (bills, debts, etc.). Often used in the plural form 'mga bayarin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumataas na naman ang ating mga **bayarin** sa kuryente at tubig.","translation":"Our electricity and water **bills** are increasing again."},{"sentence":"Unahin mong asikasuhin ang mga **bayarin** bago ka gumastos para sa luho.","translation":"Prioritize your **payables** before you spend on luxuries."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o resulta ng pag-imprenta ng teksto o larawan sa papel o iba pang materyales.
etymology: Root word 'limbag' means to print or publish.
original_explanation: This is the glow-up moment for any writer or artist. It's when your thesis, your first book, or your komiks finally goes from a Word doc to a physical copy. It's the smell of fresh ink on paper. Pagkalimbag means it's now official, it's out there, ready to be sold at a book fair or read by your proud nanay.
usage_notes: Refers to the act or state of being printed. 'Paglalathala' (publishing) is a related but broader term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inaabangan ng marami ang **pagkalimbag** ng kanyang bagong nobela.","translation":"Many are anticipating the **publication** of her new novel."},{"sentence":"Mataas ang kalidad ng **pagkalimbag** ng librong ito.","translation":"The print quality (lit: state of being printed) of this book is high."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nangongolekta ng mga bagay na may partikular na uri bilang isang libangan o propesyon.
original_explanation: Hindi lang 'yung naniningil ng utang. Sila 'yung mga taong ang motto sa buhay ay 'Gotta catch 'em all!' mapa-K-Pop photocard, Funko Pop, sapatos, o halaman (plantito/plantita). Ang kwarto nila, mukha nang museum o bodega, depende sa'yo.
usage_notes: Madalas na tumutukoy sa mga hobbyist. Para sa naniningil ng bayad, mas karaniwan ang 'kolektor' o 'maniningil'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang siyang **collector** ng mga lumang komiks.","translation":"He is a **collector** of old comic books."},{"sentence":"Bilang isang photocard **collector**, laging warzone ang pag-secure ng new album.","translation":"As a photocard **collector**, securing a new album is always a warzone."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng isang tao o bagay na mapanlinlang, hindi tapat, o gumagamit ng panlalamang.
original_explanation: 'Yung kalaro mo ng Monopoly na biglang may-ari na ng buong board, pero 'di mo naman nakitang bumili. O 'yung ex mong nagsabing "friends lang tayo" pero may jowa na kinabukasan. That's madaya. It’s when the rules of the game (or life) are bent for someone else's unfair advantage.
usage_notes: Can describe a person, an action, or a situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayokong makipaglaro sa kanya dahil siya ay **madaya**.","translation":"I don't want to play with him because he is **deceitful**."},{"sentence":"**Madaya** ang laban kung mas marami sila.","translation":"The fight is **unfair** if they have more people."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglampas o pag-abot sa isang tiyak na hangganan, punto, o sukat.
original_explanation: 'Yung moment na nakatulog ka sa jeep at nagising ka, dalawang kanto na ang layo mo sa dapat mong bababaan. You went past your stop. Pwede ring sa budget, "Lagpas na tayo sa budget, besh!" It means going over a limit, whether it's a place, a number, or a deadline.
usage_notes: Often used with "sa" (e.g., "lagpas sa linya" - beyond the line). It is nearly synonymous with 'lampas'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatulog ako sa bus kaya **lagpas** na ako sa bababaan ko.","translation":"I fell asleep on the bus so I'm already **past** my stop."},{"sentence":"Ang gastos natin ay **lagpas** na sa ating badyet.","translation":"Our expenses have **exceeded** our budget."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat ng mga tao na namumuhay sa iisang pook, na may magkakatulad na katangian, o may iisang interes.
original_explanation: Hindi lang ito lugar, ito ay a feeling. Ito yung mga kapitbahay mong nag-aabutan ng ulam, yung group chat niyo for DOTA or Mobile Legends, o yung fandom niyo sa K-Pop. It’s your tribe, your people, your Marites support group.
usage_notes: Can refer to a geographical area (a neighborhood) or a group with shared interests (the gaming community).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaisa ang buong **komunidad** upang tulungan ang mga nasalanta ng bagyo.","translation":"The entire **community** united to help the typhoon victims."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang naitutulong ng **komunidad** ng mga Pilipino sa ibang bansa.","translation":"The Filipino **community** abroad provides a lot of help."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lihim na pagkakasundo o pagpaplano ng dalawa o higit pang tao upang isagawa ang isang masamang balak o ilegal na gawain.
original_explanation: This is what happens in the group chat when you're all planning something sneaky. It could be a surprise party for a friend, or... plotting to overthrow the current team lead. It's the secret huddle, the whispered plans, the "kakuntsaba" vibes. The Mariteses are experts at this, conspiring to spread the latest chismis.
usage_notes: Carries a negative connotation of plotting something illicit or harmful.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nabisto ang **pagsasabuwatan** ng mga empleyado laban sa kanilang manager.","translation":"The employees' **conspiracy** against their manager was exposed."},{"sentence":"May hinala ang pulisya na may naganap na **pagsasabuwatan** upang itago ang krimen.","translation":"The police suspect that there was **plotting** to hide the crime."}]

meaning_filipino: Gumawa ng pagkilos ng pagtataksil, paglililo, o pagiging hindi tapat sa isang tao, pangkat, pinagkasunduan, o bayan.
original_explanation: The plot of 90% of Filipino teleseryes. To **magtaksil** is to commit the ultimate 'sira tiwala'. You thought you had a loyal jowa or bestie, tapos ahas pala. It's when your groupmate removes your name from the project credits. That's betrayal.
usage_notes: A strong word denoting a serious breach of trust.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya lubos maisip na kaya siyang **magtaksil** ng kanyang pinakamatalik na kaibigan.","translation":"She couldn't imagine that her own best friend could **betray** her."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay ng punda sa isang unan.
original_explanation: The domestic Olympics event that happens every laundry day. It's a struggle, especially with a fluffy new unan. You try to stuff it in, it fights back, you do the little shakey-shake dance. "Pundahan mo na 'yan, bilis!" is the battle cry.
usage_notes: The verb form of "punda".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyong **pundahan** ang mga bagong labang unan.","translation":"Please **put a pillowcase on** the newly washed pillows."},{"sentence":"Nahihirapan siyang **pundahan** ang malaking unan.","translation":"She is having a hard time **putting a pillowcase on** the big pillow."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang legal na karapatan ng isang tao, sasakyan, o barko na magpatuloy sa isang partikular na paraan nang unahin kaysa sa iba, ayon sa batas trapiko o nabigasyon.
etymology: From karapatan (right) and mauna (to be first).
original_explanation: In theory, it's the rule that decides who goes first at an intersection. In Philippine practice, it’s a myth, a legend. It's often replaced by "diskarte," the size of your vehicle, or how loud your horn is. The one with the most "lakas ng loob" usually wins.
usage_notes: A crucial concept in traffic laws, though its observance can be inconsistent in practice.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging tandaan kung sino ang may **karapatang mauna** sa mga interseksyon para maiwasan ang aksidente.","translation":"Always remember who has the **right of way** at intersections to avoid accidents."},{"sentence":"Kahit ikaw ang may **karapatang mauna**, mag-ingat pa rin sa mga kamote driver.","translation":"Even if you have the **right of way**, still be careful of reckless drivers."}]

translation: to stick one's tongue out at someone
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalabas ng dila bilang paraan ng pang-aasar, pagpapahayag ng pagkayamot, o bilang isang mapaglarong kilos.
original_explanation: This is the OG "bleh" face. Kids do this to annoy their parents, siblings do it to start a fight, and sometimes you do it to your boss behind their back after a stressful meeting. It's the universal sign for "I'm playfully (or not-so-playfully) defying you."
usage_notes: Often used in an imperative or command form, like 'Dilatan mo siya!' (Stick your tongue out at him/her!).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dilatan** mo nga 'yang kapatid mong nang-aasar sa'yo!","translation":"Go ahead, **stick your tongue out** at your sibling who's teasing you!"},{"sentence":"Bigla siyang **dinilatan** ng bata nang talikuran niya ito.","translation":"The child suddenly **stuck his tongue out** at him when he turned his back."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng metal na may kulay puting-pilak, mahalaga, at ginagamit sa paggawa ng alahas, barya, at kubyertos.
original_explanation: The fancy cousin of stainless steel. It's the metal for your lola's antique kubyertos that only come out during Noche Buena. In street slang, it can also mean money, as in the famous line 'Plata o Plomo' (silver or lead) - your money or your life.
usage_notes: While 'pilak' is the more common native term for silver, 'plata' is often used in contexts of jewelry, antiques, or wealth.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga kutsara't tinidor na ito ay yari sa purong **plata**.","translation":"These spoons and forks are made of pure **silver**."},{"sentence":"Maraming alahas na **plata** ang ibinebenta sa Baguio.","translation":"A lot of **silver** jewelry is sold in Baguio."}]

translation: to be accused (wrongfully), to be framed
meaning_filipino: Maging paksa o biktima ng isang bintang o akusasyon, na kadalasan ay walang sapat na batayan.
etymology: Mula sa `mapag-` (nagsasaad ng potensyal o pagiging biktima) + `bintang` (akusasyon) + hulaping `-an`.
original_explanation: Eto 'yung bigla ka na lang sinisi sa kasalanang hindi mo ginawa. 'Yung nawawala 'yung Tupperware sa office tapos sa'yo nakaturo ang lahat kasi ikaw huling nag-kape. It's that "Bakit ako?" moment when you're being framed. The ultimate "Maritess was here" moment, and you're the topic.
usage_notes: Isang pandiwa sa aspetong potensyal, na karaniwang nagpapahiwatig na ang akusasyon ay posible o nangyari na, at madalas ay hindi makatarungan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-iingat siya sa bawat kilos niya para hindi **mapagbintangan** ng kung anu-ano.","translation":"He is careful with his every move so as not **to be accused** of anything."},{"sentence":"Masakit **mapagbintangan** sa isang bagay na hindi mo naman ginawa.","translation":"It hurts **to be wrongfully accused** of something you didn't even do."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pahintulot o pagpayag na gawin ang isang bagay; kapahintulutan.
original_explanation: The old-school, more poetic way of saying "paalam" or "permission." It's what you needed from your lola before you could go out and play. Now, it's what your boss gives you (or doesn't) for that much-needed vacation leave. Very formal, very rare in casual chats.
usage_notes: Quite rare in modern conversation; more common in literature, formal speech, or religious contexts. 'Pahintulot' is the more common term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa **tulot** ng Maykapal, malalagpasan din natin ito.","translation":"With the **consent** of the Almighty, we will also get through this."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mo ang **tulot** ng iyong mga magulang bago ka sumama.","translation":"You need your parents' **permission** before you can go."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gagawing pagpapahayag o pagsasalita ng impormasyon, opinyon, o saloobin sa hinaharap.
etymology: From `mag-` + reduplication of the first syllable of the root `sa-` + `sabi` (say). This is the future tense of `magsabi`.
original_explanation: The ultimate threat every Filipino kid hears: 'Isusumbong kita sa nanay mo!' The person who will do the telling is the one who 'magsasabi.' Also the thing you promise your best friend you won't do with their secret, but you're secretly tempted.
usage_notes: Future tense of the verb `magsabi`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **magsasabi** sa kanya ng masamang balita?","translation":"Who **will tell** him the bad news?"},{"sentence":"Bukas ako **magsasabi** ng aking desisyon.","translation":"I **will say** my decision tomorrow."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pakiramdam sa balat na karaniwang nagdudulot ng pagtawa o bahagyang pagkairita kapag ginagalaw o dinadantayan nang magaan ang isang parte ng katawan.
original_explanation: That feeling that turns you from a functioning adult into a squealing, flailing mess. It's a weapon for annoying your siblings and a test of your jowa's patience. The ultimate 'Hala, tama na!' (Whoa, stop it!) moment.
usage_notes: Can refer to both the sensation and the act of tickling itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malakas ang **kiliti** ko sa talampakan.","translation":"I am very **ticklish** on the soles of my feet."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula sa **kiliti** ang kanilang masayang harutan.","translation":"Their playful roughhousing started with a **tickle**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkawala ng pakiramdam o kakayahang makaramdam sa isang bahagi ng katawan.
etymology: From the root 'manhid' (numb, insensitive) with the nominalizing prefix 'pamama-'.
original_explanation: That 'pins and needles' feeling when your leg falls asleep after sitting on it for too long during a long meeting? That's pamamanhid. It's also what the dentist gives you before pulling a tooth. Metaphorically, it's that emotional numbness you feel after a bad breakup, when you're just... 'manhid'. You're past the crying stage and have entered the 'stare at the ceiling' phase.
usage_notes: Can be physical (loss of feeling) or emotional (apathy, insensitivity).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang matagal na pag-upo ay maaaring magdulot ng **pamamanhid** sa mga binti.","translation":"Sitting for a long time can cause **numbness** in the legs."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng trahedya, nakaranas siya ng emosyonal na **pamamanhid**.","translation":"After the tragedy, she experienced emotional **numbness**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang estado ng pagiging natigilan at nalilito, na para bang hindi makapaniwala o hindi maintindihan ang nangyayari.
original_explanation: Mas matindi sa 'tulig'. Ito yung reaksyon mo nung nalaman mong yung crush mo, may crush din sa'yo. O kaya yung itsura mo kapag tinanong ka ng prof sa recitation at wala kang kaide-ideya sa sagot. You're not just stunned, you're mentally frozen. Parang nag-hang yung utak mo.
usage_notes: Katulad ng 'tulig' ngunit kadalasang nagpapahiwatig ng mas matinding pagkagulat o kawalan ng kibo dahil sa pagkabigla o pagkalito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napatingin na lang siya sa akin na **tulingag** matapos kong sabihin ang totoo.","translation":"He just stared at me, **dumbfounded**, after I told the truth."},{"sentence":"Naiwang **tulingag** ang lahat sa biglaang pag-anunsyo.","translation":"Everyone was left **stupefied** by the sudden announcement."}]

translation: to venture; to seek one's fortune
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsubok sa kapalaran sa pamamagitan ng pagpunta sa ibang lugar o paggawa ng isang bagay na may kasamang panganib at walang katiyakan ang resulta.
etymology: From makipag- + sapalaran (venture, adventure), which is derived from 'sa palad' meaning 'in the palm/fate'.
original_explanation: This is the official theme song of every OFW, probinsyano moving to Manila, or anyone who's ever said 'Bahala na si Batman!' before making a huge life decision. It's about taking a leap of faith, whether it's for a better job abroad or trying out a new, risky food cart business.
usage_notes: Often implies leaving one's home or comfort zone for an uncertain future, usually for economic reasons.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming Pilipino ang nangingibang-bansa upang **makipagsapalaran** para sa kanilang pamilya.","translation":"Many Filipinos go to other countries to **seek their fortune** for their families."},{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **makipagsapalaran** sa Maynila kahit walang kasiguraduhan.","translation":"He decided to **take a chance** in Manila even with no guarantees."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang magkaroon ng marka o mantsa, lalo na sa damit o tela, na mahirap alisin.
etymology: From Spanish "dejar" (to leave, to leave behind).
original_explanation: That horror when a drop of toyo from your siomai lands on your brand new white shirt. Your shirt has been madeha-han. It's the universe's way of marking your territory... on your clothes. From Spanish 'dejar' meaning 'to leave' (a mark).
usage_notes: A bit old-fashioned, 'mamantsahan' is more common today. Often seen in its inflected form 'madehan' or 'nadehan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-ingat siyang kumain ng spaghetti upang hindi **madeha** ang kanyang uniporme.","translation":"He was careful eating spaghetti so that his uniform would not **be stained**."},{"sentence":"**Nadehan** ng tinta ang paborito kong polo.","translation":"My favorite polo shirt **was stained** with ink."}]

meaning_filipino: Pumanig o sumama sa isang grupo o indibidwal; nagpakita ng suporta o pagkakasang-ayon sa isang panig sa isang alitan o usapin.
original_explanation: 'Yung moment sa away ng mag-jowa mong kaibigan na kailangan mong pumili kung kanino ka papanig. A very dangerous game. "Sa lahat ng tao, sa ex ko pa siya kumampi!" The ultimate betrayal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa halip na mamagitan, **kumampi** pa siya sa isa.","translation":"Instead of mediating, he even **sided with** one of them."},{"sentence":"Marami ang **kumampi** sa kanya dahil naniniwala silang nasa tama siya.","translation":"Many **took his side** because they believe he is right."}]

translation: to make happen; to hold (an event)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa o pagsasakatuparan ng isang plano, kaganapan, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: The official verb of the "event organizer" or the "project manager" of the friend group. When you say, "Tara, magpaganap tayo ng reunion!" it means you're not just suggesting it, you're volunteering to make it a reality. It's turning a "drawing" (a plan that never happens) into an actual event. It's the ultimate "let's make it happen" verb.
usage_notes: Often used for organizing events, projects, or making plans a reality.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sila ang **magpaganap** ng susunod na Christmas party sa opisina.","translation":"They are the ones who will **hold** the next Christmas party at the office."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **magpaganap** ng isang malaking proyekto kung kulang sa pondo.","translation":"It's difficult to **make a big project happen** if funds are lacking."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang batang baboy na sumususo pa sa kanyang ina.
original_explanation: The cute baby version of the animal that gives us lechon, sisig, and bacon. When you see a biik, you either go "Awww, ang cute!" or "Hmm, masarap 'to 'pag lechon de leche." It's the adorable prequel to a Pinoy fiesta.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to a very young pig. The adult is "baboy".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang inahing baboy ay may sampung **biik**.","translation":"The sow has ten **piglets**."},{"sentence":"Naglalaro sa putikan ang mga alagang **biik**.","translation":"The pet **piglets** are playing in the mud."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang gawain ay ang pagkakalat o pagtatanim ng binhi. Sa matalinhagang paraan, isang taong nagkakalat ng ideya, balita, o intriga.
original_explanation: Literally, a farmer scattering seeds. Figuratively, it’s that one Marites (gossiper) in your GC who loves to plant seeds of chismis. 'Ingat ka diyan, **manghahasik** ng lagim 'yan.' (Be careful with that person, they're a sower of discord/gloom.) It can be positive too, like a 'sower of knowledge'.
usage_notes: This word functions as a noun, referring to the doer of the action 'maghasik' (to sow). It is formed using the 'mang-' prefix, which often denotes a profession or a habitual doer.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **manghahasik** ay maagang pumunta sa bukid upang magtanim ng palay.","translation":"The **sower** went to the field early to plant rice."},{"sentence":"Tinagurian siyang **manghahasik** ng mabuting balita sa kanilang komunidad.","translation":"He was called a **sower** of good news in their community."}]

translation: to graze; to strike with a glancing blow
meaning_filipino: Tamaan nang bahagya o padaplis ang isang bagay o tao.
original_explanation: The action of making a 'daplis.' When you try to hit something squarely but you just manage to nick it. Like trying to swat a fly and you just barely brush its wing, and it flies away laughing at you.
usage_notes: The verb form of 'daplis'. It is an action performed on an object or person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang saksakin ang kalaban ngunit nagawa lamang niyang **daplisin** ang braso nito.","translation":"He tried to stab the enemy but only managed to **graze** his arm."},{"sentence":"Maingat niyang inihagis ang bato upang **daplisin** lamang ang lata sa ibabaw ng bakod.","translation":"He carefully threw the stone to only **graze** the can on top of the fence."}]

translation: to be stung by a 'lipa' plant
meaning_filipino: Ang maranasan ang pagdikit o pagtama ng halamang lipa sa balat, na nagdudulot ng matinding kati at pamamaga.
original_explanation: The verb form of "oh no, I touched the spicy plant." This is the unfortunate event of getting stung by the 'lipa' plant. It's an instant regret situation, followed by a frantic search for anything to soothe the intense, burning itch.
usage_notes: This is a very specific verb related to the 'lipa' plant (Dendrocnide meyeniana), a type of stinging nettle.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napasigaw siya sa kati nang siya ay ma-**lipakin** habang naglalakad sa bukid.","translation":"He screamed from the itchiness when he **was stung by a lipa plant** while walking in the field."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka, baka ka **lipakin** diyan sa dawagan.","translation":"Be careful, you might **get stung by a lipa plant** there in the thicket."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng dulo ng daliri, karaniwan ay ang hinlalato, upang bahagyang tamaan o paandarin ang isang bagay sa mabilis na paraan.
original_explanation: That thing your lola does to your ear when you're being makulit. It's not a full-on batok, just a quick, sharp *ting!* to get your attention. Also what you do to a bottle cap to launch it across the room. "Huwag mo akong pitikin!" is the battle cry of anyone with an annoying sibling.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a light, quick strike with a finger.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pitikin** mo nga 'yung langgam sa braso ko.","translation":"Can you **flick** the ant off my arm?"},{"sentence":"Gusto kong **pitikin** ang tenga ng kapatid ko sa sobrang inis.","translation":"I want to **flick** my brother's ear out of extreme annoyance."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang serye ng mga aralin sa isang partikular na paksa sa isang kolehiyo o unibersidad; direksyon o ruta na tinatahak.
original_explanation: The answer to the dreaded Tita question, 'Anong **kurso** mo, iho/iha?'. It's your major in college. It can also mean the path or direction something is taking, like 'ang **kurso** ng buhay mo' (the course of your life) after you realize you hate your chosen college course.
usage_notes: Most commonly refers to an academic course of study (e.g., a degree program). Can also mean 'route' or 'direction' in a more general or nautical sense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Anong **kurso** ang kinuha mo sa kolehiyo?","translation":"What **course** did you take in college?"},{"sentence":"Nawala sa **kurso** ang barko dahil sa malakas na bagyo.","translation":"The ship went off **course** because of the strong typhoon."}]

translation: to slip through; to slide off/down
meaning_filipino: Ang dahan-dahan o biglaang pagdulas o pagkahulog mula sa isang kinapipigilan o kinalalagyan, tulad ng damit na unti-unting bumababa.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na suot mo 'yung luma mong garter shorts tapos habang naglalakad ka, unti-unti itong namamalusbos. Awkward! It's that slow, gravity-assisted wardrobe malfunction. Can also mean slipping through a tight space or a small opening.
usage_notes: Often used for clothing that is loose or for something granular (like rice) slipping out of a container. It implies a slow, downward sliding motion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Biglang **namalusbos** ang pantalon niya dahil maluwag ang pagkakatali.","translation":"His pants suddenly **slid down** because they were loosely tied."},{"sentence":"Ingatan mong huwag **mamalusbos** ang mga barya mula sa butas mong bulsa.","translation":"Be careful that the coins don't **slip through** your pocket with a hole."}]

translation: (for eyes) to become sunken or hollow
meaning_filipino: Ang paglubog ng mga mata, karaniwang sanhi ng pagkapagod, puyat, sakit, o pagtanda.
etymology: A combination of `mang-` and `lumata`, which refers to the state of having sunken eyes.
original_explanation: The official look of every BPO agent during hell week, every student finishing their thesis, and every new parent. It's when your eyes have dark circles so deep they look like they're sinking into your skull. 'Girl, anyare? Nangalumata ka na!' is a common greeting among overworked friends.
usage_notes: Describes the appearance of the eyes, not an action. It's a state of being. Often used with 'na' (nangalumata na).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang puyat sa pag-aaral, nagsimula nang **mangalumata** ang estudyante.","translation":"From staying up too late studying, the student's **eyes** started **to become sunken**."},{"sentence":"Halata sa itsura niyang pagod na pagod dahil **nangalumata** na siya.","translation":"It's obvious from his appearance that he's very tired because his **eyes have become hollow**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na mamamayan o katutubo ng Gresya; tumutukoy sa wika, kultura, o anumang bagay na may kaugnayan sa Gresya.
original_explanation: Refers to anything from Greece. Think souvlaki, the Parthenon, those statues with missing limbs, and the philosophers who gave your high school teachers so many essay topics. Also, the origin of words that sound super smart, like 'philosophy' and 'democracy'.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun for a person or an adjective for something related to Greece. The word is capitalized when referring to the people or language as a proper noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming salitang **Griyego** ang hiniram sa siyensya.","translation":"Many **Greek** words are borrowed in science."},{"sentence":"Nakipag-usap ako sa isang **Griyego** na turista sa Boracay.","translation":"I talked to a **Greek** tourist in Boracay."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian, bagay, o punto na nagpapaiba sa isang tao, bagay, o sitwasyon mula sa iba; pagkakaiba.
etymology: From kakaiba + -han. It nominalizes the adjective 'kakaiba'.
original_explanation: If 'kakaiba' is the adjective, 'kakaibhan' is the noun. It's the 'what' that makes something different. It's the difference between your 'work-from-home' self and your 'going-out' self. It's the distinction between 'okay lang' and 'okay na okay!'.
usage_notes: More formal than 'pagkakaiba'. It emphasizes a unique or special distinction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **kakaibhan** ng dalawang produktong ito?","translation":"What is the **distinction** between these two products?"},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang pananaw sa buhay ang nagbibigay sa kanya ng **kakaibhan**.","translation":"His perspective on life is what gives him his **uniqueness**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang gawain o tungkulin ay magbigay ng aliw, saya, o libangan sa iba.
original_explanation: Your human stress ball, the life of the party, or the professional clown you hire for a kid's party. In modern terms, they're the content creators, the stand-up comedians, or that one friend who always has a funny meme ready when you're feeling down. Sila ang nagpapasaya ng feed mo.
usage_notes: Also commonly spelled as 'tagaaliw', though the hyphenated form is more formally correct to separate the prefix from the root word starting with a vowel.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **taga-aliw** sa perya ay laging nakangiti.","translation":"The **entertainers** at the fair are always smiling."},{"sentence":"Siya ang nagsilbing **taga-aliw** namin noong kami'y nalulungkot.","translation":"She served as our **comforter** when we were sad."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang internasyonal na samahang makatao na nagbibigay ng tulong sa mga biktima ng digmaan o sakuna, at nagtataguyod ng kalusugan at kapakanan ng publiko.
original_explanation: The heroes in red and white who show up during disasters with relief goods and first aid. They're the ones you call for blood donations or when you need first aid training. Basically, the real-life Avengers when a typhoon hits.
usage_notes: This is a proper noun, the official name of the organization in Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-abot ng tulong ang **Krus na Pula** sa mga nasalanta ng bagyo.","translation":"The **Red Cross** extended help to those affected by the typhoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghiwa ng isang bagay sa napakaliliit na piraso, karaniwan sa pagluluto; maaari ring tumukoy sa pagpuno o paglagay ng napakarami.
original_explanation: In the kitchen, this is what you do to garlic and onions until they're tiny bits for your 'gisa'. It’s chopping with a vengeance. Figuratively, it's what happens to a person's reputation during a 'chismis' session, or what happens to a basketball team's defense when the star player starts shooting threes from everywhere—tinadtad sila!
usage_notes: Can also be used metaphorically to mean being riddled with something, like bullets ('tadtad ng bala') or pimples ('tadtad ng tigyawat').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabusisi ang **pagtadtad** ng bawang para sa ginisang ulam.","translation":"The **mincing** of garlic for the sauteed dish is meticulous."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagtadtad** ng bala sa sasakyan ay nagpapahiwatig ng matinding galit ng mga salarin.","translation":"The **riddling** of the car with bullets indicates the perpetrators' intense anger."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malambot at maputing laman sa loob ng puno ng saging na maaaring kainin.
original_explanation: Think of it as the heart of the banana stalk. Before it becomes a meme-worthy "saging lang ang may puso" moment, the 'ubad' is the edible core. It's often used in dishes like 'kinilaw' or stews. It's the plant's hidden gem, kinda like that one quiet but super talented person in your group project.
usage_notes: Primarily used in culinary contexts, especially in certain regional cuisines like those in Aklan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap gawing ensalada ang **ubad** ng saging.","translation":"The banana **pith** is delicious as a salad."},{"sentence":"Naghanap si lola ng **ubad** sa kanilang bakuran para sa pananghalian.","translation":"Grandma looked for banana **pith** in their yard for lunch."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maranasan o madama ang kaligayahan o kasiyahan.
original_explanation: This is the feeling when your Shopee package arrives, or when the client finally approves the project, or when sahod day hits. It's the verb form of 'happy'. From a state of not-happy to happy. Yung moment na naging kayo ng crush mo? 'Yan, lumigaya ka 'non.
usage_notes: Ito ang pandiwang nagpapahiwatig ng pagbabago tungo sa isang estado ng kaligayahan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lumigaya** ang kanyang puso nang makita niyang muli ang kanyang pamilya.","translation":"His heart **became happy** when he saw his family again."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagdudulot ng matinding takot, pagkabigla, o pangingilabot.
original_explanation: This isn't just "nakakatakot." This is horror movie-level fear. 'Yung tipong mapapasigaw ka at magtatago sa ilalim ng kumot. A shadowy figure at the end of a dark hallway, a sudden loud noise in a quiet house, or seeing your "due date" sa Meralco bill. Lahat 'yan **nakasisindak**. It's the "Shake, Rattle & Roll" of adjectives.
usage_notes: The 'nakasisi-' prefix emphasizes the ability to cause terror. Stronger and more intense than 'nakakatakot'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang malakas at galit na boses ay **nakasisindak**.","translation":"His loud and angry voice is **terrifying**."},{"sentence":"**Nakasisindak** ang mga kuwento tungkol sa mga nawawala sa bundok na iyon.","translation":"The stories about the people who go missing on that mountain are **terrifying**."}]

translation: channeling the vibe of; embodying the essence of
meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na hiram sa Ingles na nangangahulugang nagpapakita o nagpapahiwatig ng katangian, kilos, o itsura ng isang partikular na tao, bagay, o konsepto.
etymology: From the English word "giving," popularized in LGBTQ+ ballroom culture and spread through social media platforms like TikTok.
original_explanation: The ultimate Gen Z / Millennial compliment (or insult). It's when your outfit is 'giving rich tita vibes' or your friend's dramatic story is 'giving main character energy'. It’s the 2020s version of saying 'parang,' 'mukhang,' or 'may dating na.' You're not just *like* something, you are *giving* its entire essence to the universe.
usage_notes: Almost always followed by a noun or noun phrase that describes the "vibe" being channeled (e.g., giving tita, giving BPO agent, giving sad girl).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naka-linen pants ka at may dalang reusable cup? Naku, **giving** tita vibes ka, girl!","translation":"You're wearing linen pants and carrying a reusable cup? Wow, you're **giving** tita vibes, girl!"},{"sentence":"Yung ex mo na biglang nag-post ng 'I deserve better'? **Giving** main character yarn?","translation":"Your ex who suddenly posted 'I deserve better'? Is that **giving** main character energy?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggalaw ng balakang at baywang sa paraang kaaya-aya at may ritmo, karaniwan sa pagsayaw.
original_explanation: Think TikTok dance challenge. 'Yung pag-indak na ang focus ay sa hips and waist. It's the signature move of beauty queens and your tita who loves zumba. 'Pag narinig mo ang "Otso-otso," automatic na 'yan, kailangan mong kuminding.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **kuminding** ang mga mananayaw nang tumugtog ang mabilis na musika.","translation":"The dancers started to **sway their hips** when the fast music played."},{"sentence":"Ang galing mong **kuminding**!","translation":"You're so good at **swaying your hips**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking sisidlan na yari sa magaspang na tela tulad ng lona o abaka, karaniwang ginagamit para sa paglalagay ng bigas, arina, o iba pang butil.
original_explanation: The OG eco-bag ng mga lola natin. Dito nilalagay ang isang kaban ng bigas, uling, o minsan, mga pusa na ililigaw (don't do this!). Sa school, ito yung ginagamit sa "sack race" tuwing sports fest. Iconic!
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagbuhat siya ng isang **sako** ng bigas.","translation":"He carried a **sack** of rice."},{"sentence":"Ginamit nila ang mga lumang **sako** bilang pananiman ng gulay.","translation":"They used the old **sacks** as planters for vegetables."}]
