meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng tela, karaniwang luma o retaso, na ginagamit sa paglilinis, pagpunas, o pagpapatuyo ng mga bagay.
etymology: From `basa` (wet) + the locative/instrumental suffix `-han`. Literally, "a thing for wetting/wiping."
original_explanation: The final form of your favorite, now hole-ridden, pambahay shirt. It's the unsung hero of every Filipino household, used for everything from wiping up spilled coffee to polishing the floor. "Ma, nasaan ang basahan?" is a question as common as "Anong ulam?"
usage_notes: Can also refer to old, worn-out clothes in a derogatory sense. The root word is 'basa' (wet).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha ka ng **basahan** at punasan mo ang natapong tubig.","translation":"Get a **rag** and wipe the spilled water."},{"sentence":"Ginawa na lang niyang **basahan** ang mga lumang damit.","translation":"She just turned the old clothes into **rags**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan sa pader na pinagkakabitan ng plaka ng mga de-kuryenteng aparato upang makakuha ng kuryente.
etymology: Mula sa "saksak" (to plug in, to stab).
original_explanation: The source of life for your phone, laptop, and other gadgets. Ito yung bagay na laging kulang sa mga coffee shop at laging may "battle royale" kung sino unang makakakuha. Ang modernong "watering hole" para sa mga low-batt.
usage_notes: Ito ay homonim sa "saksakan" (pang-abay) na nangangahulugang "sobra" o "labis".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Saan ang pinakamalapit na **saksakan**? Low-batt na ako.","translation":"Where is the nearest **outlet**? My battery is low."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong pagsabay-sabayin ang mga appliances sa iisang **saksakan**.","translation":"Don't plug in all the appliances into a single **socket**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pagkakaroon ng mataas na antas ng halumigmig o pamamasa sa hangin o sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: The default weather setting in the Philippines, especially during summer. 'Yung feeling na kaliligo mo pa lang pero malagkit ka na ulit? 'Yan 'yun. Dahil umido ang panahon, mabilis mamuo ang amag sa pader o sa loob ng cabinet.
usage_notes: Often used to describe weather or a damp environment. 'Maalinsangan' is a close synonym, often implying heat as well.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masyadong **umido** ang panahon ngayon kaya malagkit sa pakiramdam.","translation":"The weather is too **humid** today, which is why it feels sticky."},{"sentence":"Itinago niya ang mga damit sa isang lugar na hindi **umido** upang maiwasan ang amag.","translation":"She stored the clothes in a place that isn't **damp** to avoid mold."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalipunan ng mga pahinang papel na may nakalimbag na mga salita o larawan, na pinagsama-sama at karaniwang may pabalat.
etymology: Possibly from Arabic 'kitāb' (كتاب) meaning 'book', via Malay 'kitab'.
original_explanation: Before Netflix, TikTok, and endless scrolling, this was the OG source of entertainment and knowledge. It's that thing your parents tell you to read more of. Can be used as a source of wisdom, a paperweight, or something to hide your phone behind during class.
usage_notes: A general term for any bound set of pages. 'Libro' (from Spanish) is a common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang magbasa ng mga **aklat** tungkol sa kasaysayan.","translation":"He/She loves to read **books** about history."},{"sentence":"Nawawala ang paborito kong **aklat**.","translation":"My favorite **book** is missing."}]

meaning_filipino: Palasak; gamit na gamit o kalat na kalat; hindi na natatangi dahil sa madalas na paggamit o pagkakaroon.
original_explanation: When something is so common it's not special anymore. Like that 'pabebe wave' from a few years back, or that one 'sana all' comment you see under every sweet couple's post. It's the 'basic' of Tagalog. The plot of that teleserye where the protagonist gets amnesia? **Lasak** na 'yan.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'palasak'. Describes ideas, trends, or objects that have lost their novelty.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lasak** na ang ganyang istilo ng pananamit.","translation":"That style of clothing is already so **common**."},{"sentence":"Humanap ka ng bagong dahilan, **lasak** na 'yang palusot mo.","translation":"Find a new reason, your excuse is **overused**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pang-itaas na kasuotan para sa mga babae, karaniwang maluwag at may mga butones o iba pang pangkabit.
original_explanation: The official uniform for office workers, church-goers, and anyone who needs to look 'presentable.' Eto yung go-to top mo kapag may biglaang Zoom meeting at naka-pajama shorts ka lang. Business on top, party (or tulog) at the bottom. Ang blusa ang sagot sa 'Wala akong maisuot!'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng bagong **blusa** para sa kanyang kaarawan.","translation":"Mom bought a new **blouse** for her birthday."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong plantsahin ang **blusa** mo dahil lukot-lukot ito.","translation":"You need to iron your **blouse** because it's very wrinkled."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mahabang hawakan ng isang walis, karaniwang yari sa kawayan o kahoy.
original_explanation: The legendary multi-tool of every Pinoy household. It's a broom handle, a tool for getting things from high shelves, a pointer for your mom's sermon, a makeshift sword for kids, and the ultimate threat for misbehaving children. "Gusto mo makatikim ng tangkay ng walis?" (Do you want a taste of the broomstick?) is a phrase that has straightened out generations.
usage_notes: A specific and very common compound noun. While literally "stem of a broom," it's the standard term for a broomstick.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang **tangkay ng walis** para abutin ang bola sa bubong.","translation":"He used the **broomstick** to reach the ball on the roof."},{"sentence":"Nabali ang **tangkay ng walis** sa sobrang lakas ng paghampas niya.","translation":"The **broomstick** broke from the force of his strike."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian sa sining o panitikan na pumupukaw ng damdamin ng awa, lungkot, o habag.
original_explanation: This is a direct loanword. It's the secret ingredient in every Filipino drama that makes your tita cry. The sob story of the 'bida,' the dramatic slow-motion rain scene, the 'Maalaala Mo Kaya' episode that hits too close to home—that's patos. It’s the 'feels' that marketing agencies and film directors manipulate to get a reaction.
usage_notes: Primarily used in literary, academic, or rhetorical contexts. Not common in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit ng matinding **patos** ang manunulat upang makuha ang simpatya ng mambabasa.","translation":"The writer used intense **pathos** to get the reader's sympathy."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang talumpati ay puno ng **patos** at nakaantig sa puso ng marami.","translation":"His speech was full of **pathos** and touched the hearts of many."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian na nagdudulot ng matinding inis, pagkainis, o pagkabagot.
original_explanation: This is next-level "nakakainis." It's not just annoying; it's the kind of annoying that makes your skin crawl. It's the sound of someone chewing loudly with their mouth open, the slow internet during a Zoom call, or that one fly in the room that just won't leave you alone. It’s the feeling that makes you want to scream, "Huy, tigilan mo 'yan!"
usage_notes: The repetition in 'yamot-yamot' intensifies the meaning of 'yamot' (annoyance).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kayamut-yamot** ang ugali ng taong iyon, palaging may reklamo.","translation":"That person's attitude is **extremely annoying**; always has a complaint."},{"sentence":"Ang ingay mula sa construction sa tapat ay talagang **kayamut-yamot**.","translation":"The noise from the construction across the street is really **irritating**."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagiging maluwag at hindi siksik ng isang bagay, tulad ng lupa; paghiwa-hiwalay ng mga buhol o pagiging malambot.
original_explanation: This is what you do to the soil before planting your tita-approved herbs. It's also what happens to your hair after you take out your braids, or to kanin that's perfectly cooked and not sticking together. It's the opposite of siksik, liglig, and umaapaw. It’s giving things room to breathe.
usage_notes: Can be used for soil, hair, rice, or any texture that can be loosened or fluffed up.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumuhaghag** ang lupa matapos itong bungkalin.","translation":"The soil **became loose** after it was tilled."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **buhaghagin** ang kanin bago gawing sinangag.","translation":"You need to **loosen** the rice before making fried rice."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkakaroon ng utang o pananagutan sa isang tao, bangko, o institusyon.
original_explanation: That "due date" notification from your credit card company. The feeling you get when you see your friend who you owe money to. It's the state of being financially obligated to someone. Parang may invisible chain na nakakabit sa'yo hangga't 'di ka nakakabayad. "5-6" is the extreme sport version of this.
usage_notes: Ang `pagkakautang` ay tumutukoy sa akto ng pangungutang, habang ang `pagkautangan` ay tumutukoy sa estado ng pagkakaroon ng utang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa malaking **pagkautangan**, kinailangan nilang isanla ang kanilang bahay.","translation":"Because of their huge **indebtedness**, they had to mortgage their house."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang makaahon mula sa kanyang **pagkautangan**.","translation":"He is trying to recover from his **state of being in debt**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malubhang kondisyong medikal kung saan ang katawan ay may matinding reaksyon sa isang impeksyon na kumalat sa daluyan ng dugo.
original_explanation: This is the medical drama plot twist you see on TV. It's not just "lason" (poison) in the literal sense, but the body's over-the-top, life-threatening response to an infection. It's when a small "sugat" gets infected and then the whole system goes haywire. Pagkalason ng dugo is a medical emergency, the body's version of a total system failure.
usage_notes: A specific medical term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang hindi nalinis na sugat ay maaaring magdulot ng **pagkalason ng dugo**.","translation":"An uncleaned wound can cause **blood poisoning**."},{"sentence":"Isinugod siya sa ospital dahil sa mga sintomas ng **pagkalason ng dugo**.","translation":"He was rushed to the hospital due to symptoms of **sepsis**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtatala o pagsusulat ng mga bagay, pangalan, o datos sa isang organisadong paraan, karaniwan ay sunod-sunod.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you're about to go to the grocery and you don't want to forget the toyo, suka, and a specific brand of corned beef. It's the "making of the list" itself. Also applies to your list of "sana all" moments or your list of exes you'd rather not run into.
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of shopping, inventory, or any form of enumeration.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinimulan na ni Ana ang **paglilista** ng mga bisita para sa kanyang kaarawan.","translation":"Ana has started **listing** the guests for her birthday."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang maingat na **paglilista** ng mga gastusin upang makatipid.","translation":"Careful **listing** of expenses is important to save money."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan nagtatagpo ang dalawa o higit pang tao, bagay, o landas; ang akto ng sabay-sabay na pagtatagpo.
original_explanation: This is the designated 'kita-kits' spot. The 'See you at the entrance of SM' or 'Sa ilalim ng waiting shed.' It's the intersection, the junction, the rendezvous point where paths cross. Can be romantic (a lovers' meeting place) or stressful (EDSA-Ortigas during rush hour).
usage_notes: Different from 'salubong' (the act of fetching someone). 'Salubungan' is the location or event of meeting. It implies that both parties are moving towards each other.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanto ng Rizal at Mabini ang aming **salubungan**.","translation":"The corner of Rizal and Mabini is our **meeting point**."},{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng aksidente sa **salubungan** ng dalawang kalye.","translation":"An accident occurred at the **intersection** of the two streets."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sangay ng agham na nauukol sa istruktura ng katawan ng mga tao, hayop, at iba pang nabubuhay na organismo.
etymology: Hiram sa Espanyol na "anatomía," mula sa Griyegong "anatomē" (paghiwa, dissection).
original_explanation: What med students and aspiring artists have to study. For med students, it's memorizing every bone, muscle, and nerve. For artists, it's about not making your drawing look like a stick figure. For the rest of us, it's the reason we know the 'hip bone is connected to the thigh bone.' The more common English version 'anatomy' is used more often in everyday speech.
usage_notes: Mas karaniwang ginagamit sa pormal na agham o medikal na teksto. Sa pang-araw-araw na usapan, mas madalas gamitin ang Ingles na salitang "anatomy."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan sa klase ng **anatomia** ang iba't ibang bahagi ng katawan ng tao.","translation":"The different parts of the human body are studied in the **anatomy** class."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng isang siruhano ang malalim na kaalaman sa **anatomia**.","translation":"A surgeon needs a deep knowledge of **anatomy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaikling anyo ng 'ganyan,' na tumutukoy sa isang bagay, paraan, o sitwasyon na malapit sa kinakausap.
original_explanation: The shorter, more conversational, and slightly lazier cousin of 'ganyan.' You use it when pointing out how your friend's ex is acting, 'Tingnan mo, **ganan** na naman siya.' It's the 'like that' you say with a sigh or a knowing look.
usage_notes: Very common in informal, spoken Tagalog. It's the colloquial version of 'ganyan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ganan** ba talaga ang tamang paggawa nito?","translation":"Is it really done **like that**?"},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **ganan**, mag-usap tayo nang maayos.","translation":"Don't be **like that**, let's talk properly."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salita ng pagpapahayag ng pasasalamat o pagtanaw ng utang na loob para sa isang kabutihan, serbisyo, o pabor na natanggap.
etymology: From Arabic 'salāma' (سلامة), meaning 'safety, security, well-being', which entered Tagalog through Malay.
original_explanation: The magic word you say after someone gives you food, holds the door, or gives you their seat on the MRT. It's the minimum payment for your friend who listened to your rants for 3 hours. Short, sweet, and a basic requirement for being a decent human being.
usage_notes: The most common way to express gratitude. Can be intensified as 'Maraming salamat' (Many thanks).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Salamat** sa iyong tulong.","translation":"**Thank you** for your help."},{"sentence":"'**Salamat** po,' sabi ng bata sa nagbigay ng kendi.","translation":"'**Thank you**,' said the child to the one who gave the candy."}]

translation: to rush someone; to do something in a hurry
meaning_filipino: Pilitin ang isang tao na magmadali; gawin ang isang bagay nang mabilisan.
original_explanation: This is what your mom does when the whole family is going to church and you're still choosing your outfit. It's the verb form of panic. "Apurahan mo na 'yan!" is the official battle cry of impatient people everywhere, from project managers with a deadline to friends waiting for you to finish your kwento.
usage_notes: Can mean to rush someone else ('apurahan ang isang tao'), or to rush an action ('apurahan ang paggawa').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **apurahan**, baka magkamali ako.","translation":"Don't **rush me**, I might make a mistake."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **apurahan** ang paggawa ng report dahil malapit na ang deadline.","translation":"The report needs to be **done in a hurry** because the deadline is near."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit at pansamantalang estruktura o puwesto, karaniwang nasa labas o sa mga pampublikong lugar, kung saan nagbebenta ng mga produkto tulad ng diyaryo, pagkain, o tiket.
original_explanation: It's that small booth in the mall selling phone cases, the one in the park selling ice cream, or the lotto outlet on the street corner. A "kiyosko" is a small-time business dream in a box. It’s bigger than a "pwesto" on a "banig" but smaller than a full-blown store. The OG pop-up store.
usage_notes: Refers to a small, often standalone, booth or stall.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng yosi sa **kiyosko** sa kanto.","translation":"I bought cigarettes at the **kiosk** on the corner."},{"sentence":"Nagtayo sila ng isang **kiyosko** para sa information desk ng event.","translation":"They set up a **kiosk** for the event's information desk."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pagsasalita o pagsusulat na gumagamit ng kaunting salita; matipid sa pananalita ngunit malaman.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'lacónico', mula sa Latin na 'Laconicus', na tumutukoy sa mga taga-Laconia (Sparta) sa Gresya, na kilala sa kanilang matipid na pananalita.
original_explanation: Describes someone who's 'tipid magsalita'. They're not shy, they just get straight to the point. Your dad who just replies 'K.' to your long text message? That's a **lakoniko** response. It's the art of saying a lot by saying very little. The human version of a '.zip' file.
usage_notes: A formal or literary term. 'Matipid magsalita', 'maikli', or 'direkta' are more common in everyday conversation. The form 'lakonik' is also sometimes seen as a direct Anglicism.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala ang heneral sa kanyang **lakoniko** ngunit matatag na mga utos.","translation":"The general is known for his **laconic** but firm commands."},{"sentence":"Isang **lakoniko**ng tango lang ang naging sagot niya.","translation":"A **brief** nod was his only answer."}]

translation: a type of clay jar or pot
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng banga o tapayan na gawa sa putik, karaniwang ginagamit sa pag-iimbak ng tubig o pagkain.
original_explanation: Before the era of plastic containers and refrigerators, this was the OG food storage solution. Think of it as the rustic, aesthetic lola's jar in the corner of the kitchen, probably holding bagoong or suka.
usage_notes: This is a very specific and somewhat archaic term. Most people would just say 'banga' or 'tapayan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatago sa isang lumang **ango** ang mga sulat ng kanyang lolo.","translation":"The letters from her grandfather were hidden in an old **clay jar**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng musikang popular na nagmula noong dekada 1950, karaniwang gumagamit ng de-kuryenteng gitara, bass, at drums.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na "rock", pinaikli para sa "rock and roll".
original_explanation: "Tara, rock and roll to the world!" Ito yung tugtugan na napapa-headbang ka, kahit sa jeep lang. Not the 'bato' kind of rock, but the 'rakrakan na!' kind. Think Eraserheads, Parokya ni Edgar, o a tito's favorite band from the 70s.
usage_notes: Madalas ginagamit sa pariralang "rock and roll" o "rakrakan". Ang baybay na "rak" ay karaniwan din sa mga impormal na konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig si tatay sa mga **rock** band noong kabataan niya.","translation":"My father was a fan of **rock** bands during his youth."},{"sentence":"Rakrakan na! Patugtugin mo 'yung paborito kong **rock** song.","translation":"Let's rock! Play my favorite **rock** song."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong may pambihirang talino o kakayahan sa isang partikular na larangan; nagpapakita ng pambihirang katalinuhan.
original_explanation: Yung kaklase mong hindi nag-aaral pero laging perfect sa exam. O kaya yung nakaisip na lagyan ng cheese ang lahat ng pagkain. Sometimes used sarcastically for someone who did something obviously dumb. "Wow, genius ka talaga."
usage_notes: Ginagamit bilang pangngalan (isang henyo) at pang-uri (matalino). Madalas gamitin nang may bahid ng sarkasmo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **genius** ang nakaimbento niyan.","translation":"A **genius** invented that."},{"sentence":"**Genius** ang idea mo na magdala ng payong!","translation":"Your idea to bring an umbrella is **brilliant**!"}]

translation: Speck in the eye; foreign particle in the eye.
meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na bagay o dumi na napunta at nakairita sa mata.
original_explanation: That tiny little traitor that gets in your eye and makes you look like you're crying over your ex, but really, it's just dust. It's the universe's way of saying, 'Stop scrolling and blink for a second.'
usage_notes: Often used metaphorically to refer to a small but significant annoyance or a person who is a thorn in one's side.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naiiyak ako, hindi dahil sa drama, kundi dahil may **puwing** ang mata ko.","translation":"I'm crying, not because of the drama, but because I have a **speck** in my eye."},{"sentence":"Sa paningin ng kanyang biyenan, siya ay isang **puwing** sa pamilya.","translation":"In the eyes of her mother-in-law, she is a **thorn** in the family's side."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng marahas at walang-kontrol na pagsalakay o pagwawala dahil sa matinding galit o pagkabaliw.
etymology: From `pag-` + `hunusdili` + `-an`. An archaic and literary form. The root's origin is obscure.
original_explanation: This is what happens when your internet dies mid-finals, your food delivery gets cancelled, and you spill coffee on your white shirt all in the same hour. It's the ultimate 'amok' mode, a word so rare you only use it for a rage so epic it deserves its own mythological term.
usage_notes: This is a very deep and literary word, almost never used in casual conversation. It's the Filipino equivalent of "going postal" but with a more ancient, primal feel.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **paghunusdilian** ay nag-iwan ng takot sa buong baryo.","translation":"His act of **running amok** left the entire village in fear."},{"sentence":"Sa kuwento, ang **paghunusdilian** ng mandirigma ay dulot ng isang masamang sumpa.","translation":"In the story, the warrior's **berserk rage** was caused by an evil curse."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na nangangahulugang matagumpay, nakakatawa, o may magandang dating sa madla.
etymology: Mula sa gay lingo, hango sa salitang Ingles na 'have'. Pinatanyag sa industriya ng aliwan sa Pilipinas.
original_explanation: From the root word "have." As in, "it has it!" Kapag ang joke mo, bumenta. Kapag ang project mo, aprubado. Kapag ang OOTD mo, pak na pak. That's havey! The opposite is 'waley' from 'wala'.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang salitang balbal na ginagamit sa mga di-pormal na usapan, kadalasan sa kontekstong komedya o pagbibigay-puri.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Havey** na havey ang punchline ng komedyante kagabi!","translation":"The comedian's punchline last night was a **total hit**!"},{"sentence":"Sa tingin mo, **havey** ba itong sinulat kong tula?","translation":"Do you think this poem I wrote is **good** (a hit)?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang direksiyon o pook kung saan sumisikat ang araw.
etymology: From pa- + silangan (east). Silangan itself comes from silang (to rise, as in the sun).
original_explanation: Yung lugar kung saan unang sumisilip si haring araw, parang 'yung pag-asa na nakikita mo tuwing umaga bago ka pumasok sa trabaho. Dito raw nanggagaling ang liwanag, pero minsan dito rin nanggagaling ang traffic papuntang office. The opposite of 'kanluran' (west).
usage_notes: Often used in formal or literary contexts to refer to the East or the Orient.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang araw ay sumisikat sa **pasilangan**.","translation":"The sun rises in the **east**."},{"sentence":"Maraming kabihasnan ang nagmula sa **pasilangan**.","translation":"Many civilizations originated from the **Orient**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng nagbibigay ng serbisyong sekswal kapalit ng bayad; isang salitang may pampanitikang konotasyon.
original_explanation: This is a very old, almost poetic word for a prostitute that you'd find in classic Filipino literature, not in a modern-day teleserye. It sounds more like a name from a legend than a job description. Think of it as the vintage, pre-internet term before 'GRO' or 'escort' became common. Using it today might get you some confused looks.
usage_notes: Considered archaic or literary. More common words are 'prostituta', 'babaeng bayaran', or the slang 'pokpok'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa mga lumang nobela, ang tauhang **libay** ay madalas na may malungkot na kapalaran.","translation":"In old novels, the **prostitute** character often has a sad fate."},{"sentence":"Ang salitang **libay** ay bihira nang marinig sa kasalukuyang panahon.","translation":"The word **libay** is rarely heard in modern times."}]

meaning_filipino: Husto, sapat, at walang anumang bahagi na nawawala o kailangan pang idagdag.
original_explanation: 'Yung order mo sa Shopee na dumating na kumpleto lahat, may freebie pa. O 'yung sukli na binigay sa'yo ni manong sa jeep, eksakto. **Walang-kulang**. It's the feeling of completeness, when everything is present and accounted for. The opposite of "ay, kulang ng isa."
usage_notes: Can be used for tangible things (complete items) or abstract concepts (a perfect life).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinigurado niyang **walang-kulang** ang mga gamit na dadalhin nila sa biyahe.","translation":"He made sure that the things they would bring on the trip were **complete**."},{"sentence":"Salamat sa Diyos, ang ating pamilya ay buo at **walang-kulang**.","translation":"Thank God, our family is whole and **nothing is lacking**."}]

meaning_filipino: Gamitin ang isang materyales bilang pansahig.
original_explanation: This is what you say about the *material* you're using for the floor. If "sahigan" is the *action* of putting the floor *on* the house, "sahigin" is the *decision* on what material to use *as* the floor. "Maganda itong kahoy, pwede nating sahigin." It's a bit deep-cut Tagalog, like a B-side track from a classic OPM band.
usage_notes: The suffix "-in" here denotes using the root word (sahig) as the object or material for an action. This is less common than 'sahigan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga lumang tabla ng narra ay plano nilang **sahigin** sa kanilang bagong bahay.","translation":"They plan **to use** the old narra planks **as flooring** for their new house."},{"sentence":"Hindi mo pwedeng **sahigin** ang ganitong klaseng kawayan dahil marupok.","translation":"You can't **use this kind of bamboo as flooring** because it's brittle."}]

meaning_filipino: Nakararanas ng pagkaubos ng lakas o enerhiya, maging ito ay pisikal, mental, o emosyonal.
original_explanation: The official status after a long shift, a 3-hour commute on EDSA, or listening to your tita's unsolicited advice. The battle cry of every working adult and student in the Philippines. 'Pagod na 'ko' is a full sentence and a whole mood.
usage_notes: Actor-focus verb in the completed aspect. Can be used for physical, mental, or emotional exhaustion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Napagod** ako sa kakatakbo para habulin ang bus.","translation":"I **got tired** from running to catch the bus."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala kung **napagod** ka, magpahinga ka muna.","translation":"Don't worry if you **became tired**, just rest for a while."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagsasaad ng obligasyon, pangangailangan, o pagiging angkop at tama ng isang kilos o kalagayan.
original_explanation: The official word of Filipino parents, bosses, and your own conscience. It's the 'you should' that carries the weight of expectation, responsibility, and sometimes, a little bit of guilt-tripping. 'Dapat nag-aral ka.' 'Dapat on time ka.' It's the prelude to every lecture.
usage_notes: An extremely common and versatile word expressing obligation, propriety, or fitness. Can also function as an adjective meaning 'fitting' or 'proper'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dapat** kang mag-aral nang mabuti para sa iyong kinabukasan.","translation":"You **should** study well for your future."},{"sentence":"Ang suot niya ay hindi **dapat** sa okasyon.","translation":"What she's wearing is not **fitting** for the occasion."},{"sentence":"Alam kong **dapat** akong humingi ng tawad.","translation":"I know I **ought to** apologize."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-iiba o pagpapalit sa katotohanan, katulad ng pagbabaligtad ng isang salaysay o pangyayari upang mailigaw ang iba.
etymology: Mula sa "pan-" + pag-uulit ng unang pantig ng ugat na "baligtad". Tumutukoy sa kilos o pamamaraan ng pagbaligtad.
original_explanation: This is what happens when a chismis gets passed around and the story completely flips. It's the 'uno reverse card' move in an argument. 'Hindi, ikaw ang may kasalanan!'—that's a classic pambabaligtad technique. Some people are pros at this.
usage_notes: Madalas itong may negatibong konotasyon, na nagpapahiwatig ng panlilinlang o pagmamanipula sa katotohanan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dalubhasa siya sa **pambabaligtad** ng mga kwento para siya ang magmukhang biktima.","translation":"She is an expert in the **act of distorting** stories to make herself look like the victim."},{"sentence":"Ang ginawa ng abogado ay isang malinaw na **pambabaligtad** sa ebidensya.","translation":"What the lawyer did was a clear **reversal/distortion** of the evidence."}]

translation: a person with rizz; a charmer; a smooth talker
meaning_filipino: Isang taong may malakas na 'rizz' o karisma; isang taong magaling mambighani o mang-akit.
original_explanation: Ito yung kaibigan mong kahit saang party niyo dalhin, may maiuuwing bagong contact number. The master of 'diskarte', the king of 'pogi points'. Basically, a professional charmer. "Ingat ka diyan, kilala 'yang **rizzler** sa campus."
usage_notes: A derivative of the slang term 'rizz', used to describe a person who is skilled at charming others.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang tinaguriang 'The **Rizzler**' ng barkada dahil lahat ng crush niya, nagiging jowa niya.","translation":"He's dubbed 'The **Rizzler**' of the friend group because all his crushes become his girlfriends."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpapadala sa mga banat ng **rizzler** na 'yan.","translation":"Don't fall for the pickup lines of that **charmer**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagguhit o paglikha ng isang larawan o disenyo sa pamamagitan ng mga linya.
original_explanation: Your inner artist coming out. It’s the Tagalog-ized version of the Spanish 'dibujar'. When your friend is bored in a meeting and starts doodling on their notepad, *dumidibuho* sila. It’s what architects do before building, and what manga artists do for a living.
usage_notes: Less common than "gumuhit" but still understood. Often used in artistic or technical contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dumibuho** ang arkitekto ng isang magandang bahay.","translation":"The architect **drew** a beautiful house."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **dumibuho** ng mga mukha sa kanyang kwaderno.","translation":"He likes to **sketch** faces in his notebook."}]

meaning_filipino: Magdulot ng matinding kalungkutan o pighati sa isang tao.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung level-up sa "biguin." Hindi lang disappointment, kundi deep sadness. 'Yung feeling na nalaman mong ubos na 'yung paborito mong ulam, times a thousand. It's causing someone profound grief, like the emotional damage from a teleserye finale where the bida dies.
usage_notes: A very formal and literary term. Not common in casual conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang biglaang pagpanaw ay **nagbigay-dalamhati** sa buong pamilya.","translation":"His sudden passing **caused sorrow** for the whole family."},{"sentence":"Huwag nating **bigyang-dalamhati** ang ating mga magulang.","translation":"Let us not **grieve** our parents."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pakiramdam ng pagkahilo o pag-ikot ng paningin, karaniwang nararanasan kapag nasa matataas na lugar, habang bumibiyahe sa sasakyang pandagat, o sa sasakyang panghimpapawid.
original_explanation: That feeling you get when you look down from a high floor, or when you're on a ferry and the waves are rough. It's the world spinning when it shouldn't be. Also, the feeling you get when you see your Meralco bill after a month of WFH with the AC on 24/7.
usage_notes: Can be specified as 'lula sa taas' (fear of heights/vertigo), 'lula sa dagat' (seasickness), or 'lula sa biyahe' (motion sickness).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakararamdam ako ng **lula** kapag sumasampa ako sa matataas na gusali.","translation":"I feel **dizzy** when I go up tall buildings."},{"sentence":"Uminom ka ng gamot para sa **lula** bago tayo sumakay ng barko.","translation":"Take medicine for **seasickness** before we board the ship."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdating sa isang kalagayan na malapit na sa isang tiyak na resulta, lalo na sa kamatayan o kapahamakan.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na one wrong move ka na lang, either lagot ka sa nanay mo o bagsak ka sa exam. You're on the edge. **Bumingit** sa kamatayan ang pasyente pero nailigtas siya ng mga doktor. It's life hanging by a thread.
usage_notes: Actor-focus verb in the completed aspect. Present: bumibingit. Future: bibingit. Almost always used in the context of danger, death, or a critical point.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumingit** sa alanganin ang kanilang relasyon dahil sa selos.","translation":"Their relationship **was on the verge of** collapse because of jealousy."},{"sentence":"Maraming negosyo ang **bumingit** sa pagkalugi noong pandemya.","translation":"Many businesses **were at the edge of** bankruptcy during the pandemic."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang ginagawang kilos ng pag-alis ng kasuotan sa katawan. Ito ang pangkasalukuyang anyo ng pandiwang "maghubad".
original_explanation: When someone asks, "Asan ka na?" and you reply, "Naliligo na," the prerequisite step is **naghuhubad** pa lang. It's the first step to the long ritual of "pag-aayos" before a night out.
usage_notes: Present progressive tense of 'maghubad'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang pumasok, **naghuhubad** pa ako!","translation":"Don't come in, I'm still **undressing**!"},{"sentence":"Bakit **naghuhubad** ang bata sa gitna ng mall?","translation":"Why is the child **taking off his clothes** in the middle of the mall?"}]

translation: a type of medicinal plant (Lagerstroemia speciosa)
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng puno (Lagerstroemia speciosa) na may mga bulaklak na kulay rosas o lila, at kahawig ng puno ng duhat. Kilala rin sa pangalang banaba.
original_explanation: It's the 'duhat's' impostor cousin. It looks kinda like the duhat tree, but it's actually banaba, famous for its herbal tea benefits for diabetes. It's like your friend who's a dead ringer for a celebrity, but isn't actually them.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **duhat-duhatan** ay kilala rin sa pangalang banaba.","translation":"The **duhat-duhatan** is also known by the name banaba."},{"sentence":"Maraming gamit na panggamot ang dahon ng **duhat-duhatan**.","translation":"The leaves of the **Lagerstroemia speciosa** have many medicinal uses."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang impormal na pagdiriwang na ginagawa linggu-linggo upang gunitain ang isang anibersaryo, karaniwan ng isang relasyon.
etymology: Isang portmanteau o pinaghalong salita mula sa Ingles na 'week' at 'anniversary'.
original_explanation: Celebration ng mga bagong mag-jowa na sobrang in-love pa. Bawat linggo may milestone. After a few months, nagiging 'monthsary', tapos 'anniversary', tapos minsan... 'sorry'.
usage_notes: Isang modernong slang, lalo na sa mga kabataan at sa social media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Happy 3rd **weeksary**, babe!","translation":"Happy 3rd **weeksary**, babe!"},{"sentence":"May date sila mamaya para sa kanilang unang **weeksary**.","translation":"They have a date later for their first **weeksary**."}]

translation: to present; to state; to reveal
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalahad, pagpapaliwanag, o pagpapakita ng isang bagay, ideya, o impormasyon sa isang malinaw at organisadong paraan.
original_explanation: This is what you do during a school report, a business presentation, or when you're explaining your side of the story to your parents. It's not just talking; it's presenting facts or feelings in an orderly way. Think of it as laying your cards on the table, whether those cards are PowerPoint slides or your 'sama ng loob'.
usage_notes: Often used in formal or academic contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bawat grupo ay kailangang **maglahad** ng kanilang pananaliksik sa klase.","translation":"Each group needs to **present** their research to the class."},{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **maglahad** ng kanyang saloobin sa pulong.","translation":"He decided to **state** his opinion at the meeting."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pahayag, salaysay, o bagay na nagpapatunay sa katotohanan; katibayan o ebidensya.
original_explanation: Your 'resibo' (receipt) when you want to call someone out. It's the screenshot you saved, the video recording, the friend who can back up your story. In a religious setting, it’s sharing your 'testimony' of faith. For online shopping, it's the customer review with pictures that serves as patotoo that the product is legit (or a scam).
usage_notes: More common than 'patotohanan'. Can refer to both physical evidence and verbal testimony.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang malinaw na salaysay ay nagsilbing matibay na **patotoo**.","translation":"His clear statement served as strong **evidence**."},{"sentence":"Maraming nagbigay ng kanilang **patotoo** tungkol sa himalang naganap.","translation":"Many gave their **testimony** about the miracle that happened."}]

translation: to massage; to perform traditional healing
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalapat ng masahe o tradisyonal na panggagamot sa isang tao, karaniwan para maibsan ang sakit sa katawan, ayusin ang pilay, o bilang gawain ng isang komadrona.
original_explanation: This is what you ask your lola to do when you have a "pilay" (sprain) or just feeling "lamig sa likod" (coldness in the back). It's the OG Filipino deep tissue massage, sometimes involving mysterious oils and chants. It's also the verb for what a traditional midwife (komadrona) does.
usage_notes: Can refer to both a general massage and the specific practice of a traditional Filipino healer (manghihilot). The context usually clarifies the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marunong ka bang **maghilot** ng likod? Masakit kasi.","translation":"Do you know how to **massage** a back? Mine is aching."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating tumawag ng marunong **maghilot** para sa pilay ni Lito.","translation":"We need to call someone who knows how to perform a traditional **healing massage** for Lito's sprain."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang balbal na salita para sa "tao" (person). Ginagamit bilang pamalit sa pangalan ng isang tao, katulad ng "siya" o bilang pangkalahatang tawag.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Ingles na "person", na binago ang baybay sa paraang Swardspeak o gay lingo. Sumikat dahil sa isang viral social media clip.
original_explanation: This is the Swardspeak/Gen Z evolution of 'person'. Why say 'sino yung person na yun?' when you can say 'sino yung ferson na yun?' It adds a little ✨spice✨. It’s a playful way to refer to someone, like 'this ferson is asking for it' or 'iba din talaga yung confidence ng ferson na to'. It’s the verbal equivalent of a side-eye and a smirk.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin nang palitan sa 'fersons' ngunit ang 'ferson' ay pang-isahan. Popularized by a viral social media clip.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ba 'yang **ferson** na kasama mo kahapon?","translation":"Who was that **person** you were with yesterday?"},{"sentence":"Ibang klase mag-isip ang **ferson** na 'to.","translation":"This **guy/girl** thinks on another level."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katawagan ng paggalang o pagmamahal para sa ama o sa isang nakatatandang lalaki na itinuturing na parang ama.
original_explanation: A respectful and sometimes old-fashioned way to call your dad or lolo. It's the more formal cousin of 'Tatay' or 'Daddy'. You'd hear this more in provinces or in classic Filipino movies. If someone calls their dad 'Tatang', you know they were raised with a lot of 'mano po'.
usage_notes: Madalas ding ginagamit para sa lolo. Nagpapahiwatig ng malalim na paggalang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"\"Mano po, **Tatang**,\" bati ng apo sa kanyang lolo.","translation":"\"Bless you, **Father/Grandfather**,\" the grandchild greeted his grandfather."},{"sentence":"Si **Tatang** ang haligi ng aming tahanan.","translation":"**Father** is the pillar of our home."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapang panulat na may grapayt sa loob na nakabalot sa kahoy.
original_explanation: Before ballpens, before keyboards, before touchscreens, there was **lapis**. The OG writing tool. It's what you used to shade your crush's name inside a heart in your notebook. Also, the primary weapon in a game of 'Tusok-Tusok'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakihiram naman ng **lapis** mo, nawawala kasi ang sa akin.","translation":"Can I borrow your **pencil**? I can't find mine."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong tasahan ang **lapis** para maging matulis.","translation":"You need to sharpen the **pencil** to make it pointed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pakiramdam ng ganap na pagkakontento at katuparan, kung saan ang lahat ng inaasahan o ninanais ay natugunan.
original_explanation: The feeling after a successful 'samgyupsal' session where you ate your money's worth. It's the 10/10 rating on a customer feedback form. While 'kaligayahan' is about joy, 'kasiyahan' is about fulfillment and contentment. You've gotten what you wanted, and it was perfect.
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of service, achievement, or fulfillment of a need or desire.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aming layunin ay ang iyong **lubos na kasiyahan**.","translation":"Our goal is your **complete satisfaction**."},{"sentence":"Nakaramdam siya ng **lubos na kasiyahan** nang makapasa siya sa board exam.","translation":"She felt **full contentment** when she passed the board exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtanggi o pagsasabing hindi totoo ang isang paratang, pahayag, o katotohanan.
original_explanation: This is the official term for 'hindi ako 'yan!' or 'it wasn't me!' It's what politicians do when accused of corruption and what you do when your mom asks if you ate the last piece of leche flan. It's the art of saying 'nope' with conviction, whether you're telling the truth or not.
usage_notes: Often used in formal or legal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa kabila ng ebidensya, patuloy ang kanyang **pagbubulaan** sa mga akusasyon.","translation":"Despite the evidence, his **denial** of the accusations continues."},{"sentence":"Naglabas ng opisyal na pahayag ng **pagbubulaan** ang kumpanya.","translation":"The company issued an official statement of **refutation**."}]

meaning_filipino: Kasalukuyang isinasagawa ang paglilinis ng mga damit gamit ang tubig at sabon.
etymology: The prefix 'nag-' and the reduplication of the first syllable 'la-' marks the progressive aspect (present, ongoing action).
original_explanation: This is the 'in progress' status of your weekend. When your friends ask what you're up to, and your reply is, '**Naglalaba** ako, bes.' The sound of the washing machine is your background music. The smell of fabric conditioner is your air freshener.
usage_notes: The progressive aspect (present tense) of 'maglaba'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo muna akong istorbohin, **naglalaba** ako.","translation":"Don't bother me for now, I'm **doing the laundry**."},{"sentence":"Tuwing Sabado, maaga siyang gumigising habang **naglalaba** ang kapitbahay.","translation":"Every Saturday, she wakes up early while the neighbor is **doing laundry**."}]

translation: to have something dripped; to apply drops
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa ng pagbuhos ng likido nang paunti-unti o patak-patak.
original_explanation: This is what you do with eye drops when your eyes are red from binge-watching K-dramas all night. Or when you're adding just a little bit of patis to your sinigang. It's the act of carefully dispensing liquid one drop at a time. 'Dok, paano po ba magpatak ng gamot sa mata ng bata?'
usage_notes: Typically used for medicine (eye drops, ear drops), flavorings (soy sauce, fish sauce), or in scientific/laboratory contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magpatak** ng gamot sa iyong mata tatlong beses sa isang araw.","translation":"You need to **apply drops** of medicine to your eye three times a day."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong **magpatak** ng toyo; maalat na iyan.","translation":"Don't **drip** too much soy sauce; that's already salty."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging nasa mas mababang posisyon o lugar matapos ang isang paggalaw pababa; o ang pagkilos ng pag-alis mula sa isang sasakyan.
original_explanation: This is you after getting off the jeepney ('Para po!'). It's also your phone's battery status after scrolling through TikTok for 3 hours. It's the state of having moved from a higher to a lower position.
usage_notes: 'Nakababa' means the action of going down is complete. 'Bumaba' is the action itself. 'Nasa baba' means is located at the bottom.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tawagan mo ako kapag **nakababa** ka na ng bus.","translation":"Call me when you've **gotten off** the bus."}]

meaning_filipino: Paglalagay ng apoy sa isang partikular na bagay o lugar. Ito ay isang pandiwang pautos o pakiusap na gawin ang aksyon ng pagsisindi.
original_explanation: This is the verb you use when you're asking someone to do the 'sindi'. 'Pakisindihan mo 'yung kandila,' is what you yell during a brownout. It's the specific action of applying fire to something, from lighting the grill for a BBQ party to lighting the gasera because Meralco is at it again.
usage_notes: This is a transitive verb, meaning it requires an object. You 'sindihan' *something*.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sindihan** mo na ang mga parol para mas masaya ang Pasko.","translation":"**Light** up the Christmas lanterns now to make Christmas merrier."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **sindihan** ang sigarilyo sa loob ng kwarto.","translation":"Don't **light** the cigarette inside the room."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halamang-ugat (Manihot esculenta) na may malaki at nakakaing ugat na mayaman sa arina (starch). Karaniwang tinatawag ding kamoteng-kahoy.
original_explanation: The unsung hero of Filipino snacks. Before we had fancy potatoes, we had **balinghoy**, a.k.a. kamoteng-kahoy. This is the root of all good things: cassava cake, pichi-pichi with cheese, and even the tapioca pearls in your milk tea. It's the OG, the versatile carb that has been fueling generations of Filipinos.
usage_notes: The term 'kamoteng-kahoy' is more commonly used in everyday conversation, while 'balinghoy' might be considered more traditional or regional in some areas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap gawing keyk o pichi-pichi ang **balinghoy**.","translation":"**Cassava** is delicious when made into a cake or pichi-pichi."},{"sentence":"Nagtanim sila ng **balinghoy** sa likod-bahay para may makain sa panahon ng taggutom.","translation":"They planted **cassava** in the backyard to have something to eat during times of famine."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang partikular na paksa na masusing sinisiyasat, tinatalakay, o inaaral, karaniwan sa kontekstong akademiko o siyentipiko.
original_explanation: This is your thesis topic in all its glory. It’s what keeps you up at 3 AM, surrounded by books and instant noodles, questioning all your life choices. It's the official, formal name for that thing you're supposed to be an expert on by the time you graduate.
usage_notes: Isang partikular na parirala na ginagamit sa mga kontekstong akademiko at pananaliksik.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang epekto ng social media sa kalusugang pangkaisipan ang kanyang **paksang pinag-aaralan**.","translation":"The effect of social media on mental health is her **subject of study**."}]

meaning_filipino: Magdulot ng kiliti sa isang tao sa pamamagitan ng magaan na pagdantay o paggalaw sa isang bahagi ng kanyang katawan.
original_explanation: The action verb for causing temporary insanity via tickling. It's what you do when you want to get a reaction, whether it's laughter or a playful slap. 'Wag mo akong kilitiin, may kiliti ako diyan!' (Don't tickle me, I'm ticklish there!)
usage_notes: Object-focus verb. 'Kilitiin mo siya' (Tickle him/her).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **kilitiin** ang kanyang mga anak hanggang sa humagalpak sila ng tawa.","translation":"He loves **to tickle** his children until they burst out laughing."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **kilitiin** ang pusa ngunit siya'y kinalmot.","translation":"He tried **to tickle** the cat but got scratched."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagpapatakbo ng isang negosyo, kalakalan, o komersyo.
etymology: From Spanish "negocio" (business). The Filipino form involves the prefix "pag-" and reduplication of the first two syllables of the root ("ne-go" -> "ne-ne-go") to form a verbal noun indicating an ongoing action.
original_explanation: This is the hustle! It's the art of being a 'negosyante' or 'entrepreneur'. From selling things online, opening a samgyupsal place, to running a massive corporation. It's the process of turning an idea (and a lot of 'diskarte') into profit. It's the reason your friend is always busy and replies, "Sorry, nasa meeting."
usage_notes: Refers to the general, ongoing act or process of engaging in business.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagnenegosyo** ay nangangailangan ng sipag, tiyaga, at diskarte.","translation":"**Entrepreneurship** requires diligence, perseverance, and strategy."},{"sentence":"Naging matagumpay siya sa kanyang **pagnenegosyo** ng mga damit.","translation":"She became successful in her **business** of selling clothes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagsasagawa ng scam o panloloko upang makapanlinlang ng kapwa.
original_explanation: The person behind the "scam." Sila 'yung mga may pa-text na kamag-anak daw galing abroad na nanghihingi ng load, o 'yung ka-match mo sa dating app na biglang nanghihiram ng pera for a "family emergency." They are professional users... of other people's money.
usage_notes: The perpetrator of a 'scam'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"I-block mo na 'yang **scammer** na 'yan sa Facebook.","translation":"Block that **scammer** on Facebook now."},{"sentence":"Nahuli na sa wakas ang kilabot na **scammer**.","translation":"The notorious **scammer** was finally caught."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng legal na pagkuha sa isang bata upang palakihin bilang sariling anak; ang pagtanggap at pag-aalaga sa isang nangangailangan.
original_explanation: The act of choosing to make someone part of your family. This isn't just for kids; you can `ampon` a rescue dog, `ampon` a struggling friend, or `ampon` a new hobby. It's an act of love and acceptance.
usage_notes: Ang pagbigkas ay nag-iiba depende sa anyo ng pandiwa (e.g., /AM-pon/ for 'ampon', /am-pu-NIN/ for 'ampunin'). Ang salitang-ugat mismo ay may diin sa unang pantig.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang mag-asawa na **mag-ampon** ng isang sanggol.","translation":"The couple decided **to adopt** a baby."},{"sentence":"Inaanyayahan niya ang lahat na **amponin** ang adbokasiya para sa kalikasan.","translation":"She invites everyone **to adopt** the advocacy for the environment."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong nag-uulat ng mga balita o impormasyon para sa pahayagan, radyo, telebisyon, o online na plataporma.
original_explanation: Sila 'yung laging may hawak na mic at camera, humahabol sa mga politiko, artista, o kahit sinong sangkot sa chismis para makuha ang "scoop". Sila ang original Marites, pero with a press ID and a deadline.
usage_notes: A common loanword used in Filipino media and daily conversation. The native equivalent is "mamamahayag" or "tagapagbalita".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinanong ng **reporter** ang pangulo tungkol sa bagong batas.","translation":"The **reporter** asked the president about the new law."},{"sentence":"Naging viral ang video ng **reporter** na nadulas habang nag-uulat.","translation":"The video of the **reporter** who slipped while reporting went viral."}]

meaning_filipino: Madagdagan ang sukat ng lapad; maging mas malawak.
original_explanation: This is what happens to the roads during a government project, and also what happens to your waistline after the Christmas holidays. It's the process of expanding sideways. "Friend, parang lumapad ka?" is a question you should never, ever ask. Ever.
usage_notes: Used for physical objects, spaces, and metaphorically for one's understanding or perspective ("lumapad ang pang-unawa").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lumapad** ang kalsada matapos ang road-widening project.","translation":"The road **became wider** after the road-widening project."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa pag-eehersisyo, **lumapad** ang kanyang mga balikat.","translation":"Because of exercising, his shoulders **broadened**."}]

translation: to dismiss (from a job); to fire; to lay off
meaning_filipino: Alisin o tanggalin sa trabaho ang isang empleyado.
original_explanation: The BPO term for "You're fired!" or "We're letting you go." It’s that dreaded meeting with HR where they tell you your services are no longer required. The corporate version of getting broken up with: "It's not you, it's the company's financial restructuring."
usage_notes: Commonly used in a corporate or employment context. 'Magtanggal' is a more general term, while 'magsisante' is specifically for firing people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napilitan ang kumpanya na **magsisante** ng maraming empleyado dahil sa pagkalugi.","translation":"The company was forced to **lay off** many employees due to financial losses."},{"sentence":"Nagbanta ang manager na **magsisisante** siya ng mga taong laging huli sa trabaho.","translation":"The manager threatened that he **would fire** the people who are always late for work."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang tao, bagay, o ideya na nagdudulot ng problema, kumplikado, o may kaduda-dudang moralidad o etika.
original_explanation: The go-to label for that tito who makes sexist jokes at family reunions, that celebrity who tweeted something dumb in 2012, or that K-drama plot that just doesn't sit right with you. In the court of Twitter, being called 'problematic' is one step away from getting 'cancelled'.
usage_notes: A very common loanword in modern, online Filipino discourse, especially among younger generations. Used heavily in Taglish.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Medyo **problematic** ang mga naunang pelikula ng direktor na iyon.","translation":"That director's earlier films are a bit **problematic**."},{"sentence":"Ayoko na sa kanya, masyado siyang **problematic** kausap.","translation":"I don't like him anymore, he's too **problematic** to talk to."}]

translation: to be able to plant on/in
meaning_filipino: Magawang makapagtanim sa isang lugar o espasyo.
original_explanation: When your plantita/plantito dreams can finally come true because you found a patch of land, a pot, or even a recycled plastic bottle that can be planted on. It's the verb form of "May space pa!" for your succulent collection. Figuratively, it's finding a heart that's ready to be planted with love, #charot.
usage_notes: The -an suffix indicates the location where the action (planting) takes place.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malawak ang bukid kaya marami pa itong **matatamnan**.","translation":"The field is wide so a lot more **can be planted on** it."},{"sentence":"Sana ang paso na ito ay **matamnan** ko ng bagong bulaklak.","translation":"I hope I'll be able **to plant** a new flower **in** this pot."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang beses lamang; sa ilang pagkakataon; paminsan-minsan.
etymology: Isang pagpapaikli ng pariralang 'may isang' o 'isang beses'.
original_explanation: The official word for 'one time' or 'sometimes.' It’s the frequency of you cleaning your room (minsan lang), or how often you see your crush (paminsan-minsan). It’s also the start of many hugot lines: 'Minsan akala mo okay na, pero hindi pa pala.'
usage_notes: Ang 'minsan' ay nangangahulugang 'sometimes'. Ang 'isang beses' o 'minsan lang' ay nangangahulugang 'only once'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Minsan**, masarap mapag-isa.","translation":"**Sometimes**, it's nice to be alone."},{"sentence":"Isang **minsan** lang ako nagmahal nang ganito.","translation":"I have only loved like this **once**."}]

translation: to be sideswiped; to be grazed
meaning_filipino: Magalusan o masagi nang bahagya at mabilisan ng isang bagay na gumagalaw.
original_explanation: 'Yung muntik ka nang mabangga ng motor sa EDSA pero siningitan ka lang. 'Yan 'yung 'madagil'. It's that "Oops, sorry!" moment in traffic, but for your body. The physical version of a close call.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of minor accidents or close calls.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bahagya siyang **nadagil** ng traysikel kaya may gasgas ang kanyang braso.","translation":"He was lightly **grazed** by a tricycle, so his arm has a scratch."}]

translation: to let dangle; to swing something around
meaning_filipino: Hayaan o igalaw ang isang bagay sa paraang ito ay lalawit o babitin-bitin nang paulit-ulit.
etymology: Mula sa pag-uulit at paglalapi ng salitang `lawit`.
original_explanation: Imagine a kid bored in class, swinging their ID lace back and forth. 'Yan ang ginagawa niya, pinapalawit-lawit niya. It's the act of dangling something and letting it swing, often out of boredom or playfulness. It has a more active, repetitive feel than just 'palawit'.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang di-gaanong karaniwang anyo ng pandiwa na nagbibigay-diin sa pag-indayog o paulit-ulit na pagbitin ng isang bagay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **palawit-lawitin** ang iyong ID, baka mawala.","translation":"Don't **swing your ID around**, it might get lost."},{"sentence":"Nakakatuwang pagmasdan ang unggoy na **pinapalawit-lawit** ang buntot nito.","translation":"It's amusing to watch the monkey **dangling and swinging** its tail."}]

translation: dying; state of being near death; agony
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng isang tao na nasa bingit ng kamatayan, kung saan tila naglalaban ang buhay at kamatayan.
original_explanation: This is the most dramatic scene in any teleserye. The character is in the hospital, the heart monitor is beeping erratically, and the family is crying outside. It's the literal 'snatching of life'—a tug-of-war between life and death. The ultimate cliffhanger.
usage_notes: A compound noun. 'Agaw-buhay' can also be used as an adjective (e.g., 'Siya ay agaw-buhay'). 'Pag-aagaw-buhay' refers to the state or process itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matagal ang naging **pag-aagaw-buhay** ng matanda bago siya pumanaw.","translation":"The old man's **struggle with death** was long before he passed away."},{"sentence":"Nasaksihan ng mga doktor ang kanyang **pag-aagaw-buhay** sa emergency room.","translation":"The doctors witnessed his **fight for life** in the emergency room."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malawak na espasyo o lugar; isang hindi gaanong karaniwang baryasyon sa pagbaybay ng salitang 'bulwag'.
etymology: Possibly a variant or corruption of 'bulwag'.
original_explanation: Basically the same as 'bulwag,' but maybe said by your tita who spells things a little differently, like 'sine' vs 'cine'. You get the point, it's a big hall. 'Bulwag' is the more 'correct' term you'll see in books.
usage_notes: 'Bulwag' is the more standard and widely accepted spelling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maluwag ang **bulwang** ng kanilang bagong-tayong bahay.","translation":"The **hall** of their newly-built house is spacious."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga palagay o opinyon na walang matibay na batayan; mga tsismis o sabi-sabi.
original_explanation: This is 'haka' on steroids. It's not just one assumption, it's a whole universe of them. This is the stuff that fuels showbiz talk shows and family group chats. 'Totoo bang buntis si artista X?' 'Hala, haka-haka lang 'yan!' It's the official word for 'chismis that's trying to sound intellectual.'
usage_notes: More common in everyday speech than the singular 'haka'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala sa mga **haka-haka** na naririnig mo sa kanto.","translation":"Don't believe the **rumors** you hear on the street corner."},{"sentence":"Ang balitang iyon ay batay sa **haka-haka** at hindi sa katotohanan.","translation":"That news is based on **speculation** and not on facts."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi sinasadyang pagsasabi o pagpapahayag ng isang damdamin o saloobin nang biglaan at malakas.
original_explanation: That moment when you see the latest chismis and you can't help but shout, "Hala, totoo ba?!" That's mapabulalas. It's an involuntary verbal reaction, like when you accidentally see your crush or stub your toe. The opposite of being poker-faced.
usage_notes: The "mapa-" prefix signifies an involuntary or sudden action. It's an outburst of words driven by strong emotion like surprise, pain, or joy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nang makita niya ang resulta ng exam, **napabulalas** siya ng, 'Salamat, Lord!'","translation":"When she saw the exam results, she **exclaimed**, 'Thank you, Lord!'"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na pinili o itinalaga upang kumilos o magsalita para sa isa pa o para sa isang pangkat.
original_explanation: Sila 'yung "pambato" ng grupo n'yo. Sa Kongreso, sila 'yung boses ng distrito n'yo (sana). Sa group project, siya 'yung taga-report. Sa call center, sila 'yung kausap mo na laging may script na "I understand your frustration."
usage_notes: Common in political, legal, and formal business contexts. "Kinatawan" is the native Tagalog equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **representante** ng aming distrito ay naghain ng bagong panukalang batas.","translation":"The **representative** of our district filed a new bill."},{"sentence":"Sino ang ipapadala ninyong **representante** para sa pulong?","translation":"Who will you send as your **representative** for the meeting?"}]

meaning_filipino: Nakatuon ang buong pansin o atensyon sa isang bagay; nakatapat o nakaturo ang dulo ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're so into a K-drama that you don't even notice the house is on fire. Or when a hold-upper points a gun at you and says, "Akin na ang lahat." In both cases, you're *tutok*. One is by choice, the other... not so much.
usage_notes: Can describe both mental focus and the physical act of pointing something (like a gun or a camera) at a target.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tutok** na **tutok** siya sa kanyang trabaho kaya hindi niya namalayan ang oras.","translation":"He was so **focused** on his work that he didn't notice the time."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang malikot, may baril na naka-**tutok** sa'yo.","translation":"Don't move, there's a gun **pointed** at you."}]

translation: to take to heart; to internalize
meaning_filipino: Itanim sa isip at damdamin nang may pagpapahalaga; bigyan ng seryosong atensyon at damhin nang malalim.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'seryosohin mo, please' command. When someone tells you to isapuso something, it's not just about memorizing it. It's about letting it sink into your core, understanding its importance, and living by it. It’s what your lola tells you about her advice, what your manager says about the company values, and what your jowa hopes you do with their 'I love you.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Isapuso** mo ang bawat payo ng iyong mga magulang.","translation":"**Take to heart** every piece of advice from your parents."},{"sentence":"Dapat nating **isapuso** ang mga aral ng kasaysayan.","translation":"We should **internalize** the lessons of history."}]

translation: The sound of gushing or flowing water
meaning_filipino: Ang tunog ng mabilis at malakas na agos ng tubig, karaniwan sa mga sapa, ilog, o talon.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung soundtrip mo sa probinsya kapag umuulan tapos malakas ang agos sa kanal. It's the ASMR of a mini-waterfall or a really active bidet. Hindi 'yung pabulong-bulong na agos, kundi 'yung may energy at parang may sinasabi.
usage_notes: Isang onomatopoeic na salita na partikular na tumutukoy sa tunog ng tubig. Mas malakas kaysa sa 'agasas' o 'daloy'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **lagasaw** ng tubig mula sa di-kalayuang talon.","translation":"I heard the **gushing sound** of the water from the nearby falls."},{"sentence":"Ang **lagasaw** sa batis ay nakakarelax pakinggan tuwing hapon.","translation":"The **sound of the flowing stream** is relaxing to listen to every afternoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Inilagay sa mas mababang posisyon o lugar; binawasan ang halaga, presyo, o antas.
original_explanation: What your boss does to your performance rating when you've been 'quiet quitting.' Or when you finally put down that heavy bag of groceries (or emotional baggage). Also, what happens to gas prices... sometimes... if we're lucky.
usage_notes: This is the past tense of the verb 'ibaba' (to put something down).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ibinaba** niya ang hawak na sako ng bigas.","translation":"He **lowered** the sack of rice he was holding."},{"sentence":"**Ibinaba** ng pamahalaan ang alert level sa aming lugar.","translation":"The government **lowered** the alert level in our area."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na legal na kumukupkop at kumikilala sa isang indibidwal, karaniwang isang bata, bilang sarili niyang anak kahit hindi ito kadugo.
original_explanation: The ultimate hero in a teleserye who takes in the lost 'bida'. In real life, they're the ones with big hearts (and even bigger paperwork) who give a child a forever home. They're not just parents; they're chosen parents.
usage_notes: Also commonly spelled as 'tagaampon', though the hyphenated form is more formally correct.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghahanap ang ahensya ng mga mapagmahal na **taga-ampon**.","translation":"The agency is looking for loving **adopters**."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga **taga-ampon** ay itinuring siyang tunay na anak.","translation":"His **adoptive parents** treated him as their own child."}]

meaning_filipino: May ugaling mag-aksaya o magtapon ng mga bagay, lalo na ng pagkain o pera, nang walang pakundangan.
original_explanation: Describes someone who orders food for the 'gram but only takes two bites. The person who buys the latest iPhone every year even if their old one is perfectly fine. They live the 'YOLO' lifestyle, but their wallet and the environment are crying. Lola would definitely hit them with the 'Daming nagugutom sa mundo!' line.
usage_notes: A negative trait, often used to chastise someone for not being frugal or for disrespecting resources. Commonly used in the context of food or money.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinagalitan ng nanay ang anak niyang **mapagtapon** ng pagkain.","translation":"The mother scolded her child for being **wasteful** with food."},{"sentence":"Sa panahon ng krisis, hindi dapat maging **mapagtapon** ng pera.","translation":"In times of crisis, one should not be **wasteful** with money."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malawak at patag na anyong lupa na matatagpuan sa mataas na lugar.
original_explanation: 'Yung lugar na parang Baguio o Tagaytay. Umakyat ka na ng bundok, pero pagdating mo sa taas, patag naman pala. Perfect for your "I'm on top of the world" IG post, pero may space pa rin para mag-picnic.
usage_notes: A common term in geography (Heograpiya) classes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Lungsod ng Baguio ay matatagpuan sa isang **talampas**.","translation":"Baguio City is located on a **plateau**."},{"sentence":"Napakaganda ng tanawin mula sa tuktok ng **talampas**.","translation":"The view from the top of the **plateau** is magnificent."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang anyong lupa na nakausli at napapaligiran ng tubig sa halos lahat ng panig nito, maliban sa isang bahagi na nakakabit sa mas malaking kalupaan.
original_explanation: In geography class, it's that piece of land that's *almost* an island but still has attachment issues with the mainland. Think of Bataan or the Zamboanga Peninsula. It's land that wants to be free and explore the sea but is still connected to its roots.
usage_notes: A geographical term. The native Tagalog equivalent is 'tangway'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Bataan ay isang makasaysayang **peninsula** sa Pilipinas.","translation":"Bataan is a historical **peninsula** in the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Maraming magagandang baybayin sa Zamboanga **Peninsula**.","translation":"There are many beautiful coastlines on the Zamboanga **Peninsula**."}]

meaning_filipino: Inilaan o inaalok upang ipagbili.
etymology: From 'pam-' + 'benta' (sale), which is derived from Spanish 'venta'.
original_explanation: The sign you put on things you no longer need, from your old phone to your pre-loved clothes. On Facebook Marketplace, the default status of everything is 'pambenta, RFS: need funds'.
usage_notes: Often used as a noun phrase 'na pambenta' (that is for sale) or 'gamit na pambenta' (things for sale).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itong mga damit na ito ay **pambenta**, hindi pampamigay.","translation":"These clothes are **for sale**, not for donation."},{"sentence":"Nag-bake siya ng cookies na **pambenta** para kumita ng dagdag na pera.","translation":"She baked cookies **for sale** to earn extra money."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit o patuloy na paglalapat ng marahang haplos sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: This is the action of giving non-stop 'himas'. You're not just giving one pat; you're in it for the long haul. It's what you do to your pet while binge-watching a series. The repetition implies a continuous, soothing action.
usage_notes: The repetition of the root word emphasizes the continuous or repeated nature of the action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto niyang **himas-himasin** ang malambot na balahibo ng pusa.","translation":"He wants to **continuously caress** the soft fur of the cat."},{"sentence":"**Himas-himasin** mo ang likod ng sanggol para makatulog siya.","translation":"**Repeatedly stroke** the baby's back so he can sleep."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahalagang bahagi, elemento, o sangkap na nakakaapekto sa resulta o kalagayan ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: Ito yung mga 'dahilan' kung bakit nangyari ang isang bagay. Sa pagluluto, ito yung ingredients. Sa chismis, ito yung mga piraso ng kwento na pinagdugtong-dugtong. Sa project management, ito yung mga 'variables' na kailangan mong i-consider para 'di pumalpak.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa mga akademikong talakayan, siyentipikong pag-aaral, at pormal na pagsulat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kahirapan ay isa sa mga **salik** sa pagtaas ng krimen.","translation":"Poverty is one of the **factors** in the rise of crime."},{"sentence":"Maraming **salik** ang dapat isaalang-alang sa pagpili ng kurso sa kolehiyo.","translation":"There are many **factors** to consider when choosing a college course."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maging sanhi ng pagbagsak o pagguho ng isang bagay na nakatayo, tulad ng puno, pader, o tao.
original_explanation: This is what a strong typhoon does to banana trees and billboards. It's also what you accidentally do to a tower of Jenga or a stack of papers on your messy desk. In a fight, it's the goal: 'magtumba ng kalaban' (to knock down the opponent).
usage_notes: Implies an actor causing something to fall. The reflexive form 'matumba' means 'to fall over' by accident or force.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malakas ang hangin, baka **magtumba** ito ng mga puno.","translation":"The wind is strong, it might **knock over** the trees."},{"sentence":"Sa sobrang lakas ng suntok, naka-**magtumba** siya ng kalaban sa isang iglap.","translation":"With such a strong punch, he was able to **knock down** his opponent in an instant."}]

meaning_filipino: May ekspresyon na nakasimangot, magagalitin, o hindi palangiti.
original_explanation: The look on your face when you're forced to go to work on a Monday morning. That RBF (Resting B*tch Face) that makes people hesitate to talk to you. You look like you just ate a whole green mango with no bagoong.
usage_notes: Used to describe someone who looks perpetually unhappy, grumpy, or unapproachable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagi na lang **mukhang-maasim** ang boss namin tuwing umaga.","translation":"Our boss is always **sour-faced** every morning."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang sumimangot, nagiging **mukhang-maasim** ka tuloy.","translation":"Don't frown, you're becoming **grumpy-looking**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahinang dagundong o malagong na tunog, tulad ng kulog sa malayo o pag-uga ng isang bagay na may maluwag na laman sa loob.
original_explanation: It's the sound your stomach makes when you see your ex with someone new. Or the sound of the last piece of Choc-Nut rattling in the box when you desperately need a sugar rush. It's the sound of impending doom... or just a jeepney with a bad muffler.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **kalugkog** mula sa aparador ang gumising sa kanya sa kalagitnaan ng gabi.","translation":"A **rattling sound** from the cabinet woke him up in the middle of the night."},{"sentence":"May narinig akong **kalugkog** sa makina ng sasakyan.","translation":"I heard a **rumbling sound** from the car's engine."}]

translation: stubble field; place where reaping was done
meaning_filipino: Ang bukid o lugar kung saan naganap ang pag-aani o paggapas ng mga pananim tulad ng palay.
original_explanation: The aftermath of a harvest party in the province. It's the rice field post-Manny Pacquiao fight—kalbo na. This is the empty, stubbly field where the golden stalks of rice used to be. It can also refer to the stalks left behind.
usage_notes: Isang terminong pang-agrikultura na partikular na tumutukoy sa isang bukid pagkatapos ng anihan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpulot ng mga natirang palay ang mga bata sa **pinaggapasan**.","translation":"The children gleaned the leftover rice stalks from the **stubble field**."},{"sentence":"Tuyot na ang **pinaggapasan** dahil sa matinding sikat ng araw.","translation":"The **harvested field** is now dry because of the intense heat of the sun."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapahayag ng pahintulot, posibilidad, o kakayahan. Katumbas ng "puwede".
original_explanation: The Filipino "maybe" with a sprinkle of "yes." It's the word your parents use when they don't want to say a hard "no" to you going out. "Tingnan natin... `maaari`." It's the Schrödinger's cat of permission—both a yes and a no until the last minute.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'puwede', but 'maaari' can sound slightly more formal or polite.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Maaari** po bang magtanong?","translation":"**May** I ask a question?"},{"sentence":"**Maaari** tayong manalo kung magtutulungan tayo.","translation":"We **can** win if we help each other."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko akalain na **maaari** pala itong mangyari.","translation":"I didn't think this could possibly **happen**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tinambak o inipon sa paraang mataas na tila isang bundok.
original_explanation: Eto yung sandamakmak na labahin na naghihintay sa'yo sa sahig ng kwarto mo. It looks like a small mountain, 'di ba? That's 'binundok'. It can also describe a huge serving of rice, 'yung kaning parang Mt. Apo sa taas. Anything piled up so high it resembles a mountain.
usage_notes: Used to describe a very large pile of something, often hyperbolically.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Binundok** na mga damit ang kailangan niyang labhan ngayong Sabado.","translation":"A **mountain-like pile** of clothes is what she needs to wash this Saturday."},{"sentence":"Nagulat ako sa **binundok** na kanin na inihain sa akin.","translation":"I was surprised by the **piled-up** rice that was served to me."}]

translation: to pilfer from; to steal a small amount from
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng palihim na pagkuha ng maliit na bahagi mula sa isang kabuuan, tulad ng pera mula sa pitaka o paninda mula sa tindahan.
original_explanation: When you "borrow" a few fries from your friend's large order without them noticing. You're not stealing the whole thing, you just **kupitan** a little. It's a game of stealth and plausible deniability.
usage_notes: The focus is on the source from which something is stolen (e.g., 'kupitan ang kahon').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **kupitan** ang alkansya ng iyong kapatid.","translation":"Don't **pilfer from** your sibling's piggy bank."},{"sentence":"May nangahas na **kupitan** ang donasyon para sa mga biktima ng bagyo.","translation":"Someone dared to **steal a small amount from** the donation for the typhoon victims."}]

translation: the act of pulling out or unsheathing
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbunot o paghugot ng isang bagay mula sa kinalalagyan nito, tulad ng espada mula sa kaluban o baril mula sa taguan.
original_explanation: This is that dramatic movie scene where the hero pulls out his sword before a big fight. Or a less dramatic scene where you pull a weed from the garden. It’s the act of drawing something out from its container or sheath, usually with a quick, decisive motion.
usage_notes: Often used for weapons like swords or knives. Similar to "paghugot" or "pagbunot".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagulat ang lahat sa biglaang **paghagot** niya ng patalim.","translation":"Everyone was shocked by his sudden **act of pulling out** a blade."},{"sentence":"Ang bilis ng kanyang **paghagot** ng espada ay hinangaan ng mga manonood.","translation":"His speed in **unsheathing** the sword was admired by the audience."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang estado ng kawalan ng pag-asa, panlulumo, o pagkawala ng kumpiyansa at sigla.
original_explanation: This is when you lose the will to fight. After you failed an exam you studied hard for, got rejected for a job you really wanted, or when your crush says 'you're like a brother to me.' Your spirit is broken. You're not crazy, just deeply sad and discouraged. Your 'loob' (inner self) is 'sira' (broken).
usage_notes: An idiomatic expression describing a state of emotional and mental defeat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **sira ang loob** dahil lang sa isang pagkabigo.","translation":"Don't be **discouraged** just because of one failure."},{"sentence":"Naging **sira ang loob** ng koponan matapos ang sunod-sunod nilang pagkatalo.","translation":"The team became **demoralized** after their successive losses."}]
related: ["nawalan ng pag-asa","nanlumo","panghinaan ng loob","matibay ang loob"]

translation: dousing, splashing with a large amount of water
meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang pagbuhos o pagsaboy ng maraming tubig sa isang bagay o tao.
original_explanation: It's not just a splash (wisik) or a sprinkle (saboy). 'Sibog' is when you take a whole 'tabo' or bucket of water and douse someone with it. It's what happens during the 'basaan' on San Juan's feast day. It's an aggressive, full-on soaking. 'Sinibugan niya ng malamig na tubig ang natutulog na kapatid.' Savage.
usage_notes: Implies a larger volume of liquid than 'buhos' or 'wisik'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malakas na **sibog** ng tubig ang gumising sa kanya.","translation":"A strong **dousing** of water woke him up."}]

meaning_filipino: Ibaon sa lupa, lalo na ang isang patay, alinsunod sa isang seremonya o ritwal.
