original_explanation: The final act of saying goodbye. It's what happens at a funeral when the casket is lowered into the ground. On a less serious note, it's what you do with a secret or a memory you want to forget. "Bes, ilibing na natin 'yang feelings mo para sa kanya."
usage_notes: Primarily refers to burying the dead, but can be used metaphorically for burying objects, secrets, or feelings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bukas ng hapon **ililibing** ang yumaong alkalde.","translation":"The deceased mayor will be **buried** tomorrow afternoon."},{"sentence":"Naghukay sila sa hardin upang **ilibing** ang time capsule.","translation":"They dug in the garden to **bury** the time capsule."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay na nagpapalusog at nagpapataba sa lupa o halaman; pagkain o sustansyang nakapagpapataba sa tao o hayop.
original_explanation: For plants, ito yung inilalagay mo sa lupa para lumago sila, a.k.a. fertilizer. For people, ito yung extra rice, chicharon, at lahat ng masasarap na pagkain na sinisisi mo kung bakit masikip na ang pantalon mo. "Puro ka **pataba** kaya ka tumataba!"
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa pataba sa agrikultura o sa pagkaing pampataba para sa tao o hayop.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng mga halaman ang **pataba** upang lumaking malusog.","translation":"Plants need **fertilizer** to grow healthy."},{"sentence":"Ang kanin ay itinuturing na **pataba** ng maraming Pilipino.","translation":"Rice is considered a **fattening food** by many Filipinos."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga binibiling pagkain at iba pang pangangailangan sa bahay; isang tindahan kung saan nabibili ang mga ito.
original_explanation: The place where your sahod goes to die. It's the modern-day hunting ground for adults, stalking the aisles for the best deals on hotdogs, instant noodles, and that one specific brand of coffee. Can refer to the items themselves ('Ubos na ang grocery natin!') or the store ('Punta lang ako sa grocery.').
usage_notes: Used interchangeably with its Filipinized spelling 'groseri'. The English spelling is common in signs and formal writing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko nang mag-**grocery** para sa buong linggo.","translation":"I need to do the **groceries** for the whole week."},{"sentence":"Saan ba ang pinakamalapit na **grocery** dito?","translation":"Where is the nearest **grocery store** here?"}]

translation: To give alms; to beg for alms.
meaning_filipino: Magbigay ng tulong o abuloy sa mga nangangailangan; o, humingi ng abuloy.
etymology: From mag- (verb prefix) + limos (alms), from Spanish 'limosna'.
original_explanation: Two sides of the same coin. It can mean giving your spare change to the kid knocking on your car window ('nagbigay ng limos'), or it can be the act of asking for it ('nanglimos'). Context is key. It's the spirit of 'barya lang po sa umaga' in verb form.
usage_notes: The verb maglimos can ambiguously mean either to give or to ask for alms. The more specific verbs are magbigay ng limos (to give alms) and manglimos or manlimos (to beg for alms). However, in common usage, maglimos is often understood as giving.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing Biyernes, ugali niyang **maglimos** sa mga pulubi sa labas ng simbahan.","translation":"Every Friday, it's his habit to **give alms** to the beggars outside the church."},{"sentence":"Napilitan siyang **maglimos** sa daan para may maipakain sa kanyang mga anak.","translation":"He was forced to **beg for alms** on the street to have something to feed his children."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumibok nang malakas at mabilis, karaniwan ay tumutukoy sa puso dahil sa matinding damdamin.
original_explanation: That feeling when your crush walks by, and your heart goes from chill to a full-on drum solo. It's that sudden, strong beat, like when you chugged your third cup of coffee before a presentation. 'Yung puso mo, biglang nag-EDM festival.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a heart reacting to shock, fear, excitement, or love.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumikdo** nang malakas ang dibdib niya nang makita ang pangalan niya sa listahan ng mga pumasa.","translation":"His chest **throbbed** powerfully when he saw his name on the list of passers."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong gulatin, **sumisikdo** ang puso ko!","translation":"Don't startle me, my heart is **pounding**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-rolyo o pagbilot ng isang bagay na manipis at malapad, tulad ng banig, papel, o tela.
original_explanation: What you do to a banig (sleeping mat) after you wake up, or to a poster after a concert. You **likit** it. It's the act of rolling something up neatly. Parang pag-roll up ng feelings para 'di mahalata ni crush.
usage_notes: Used for items like mats, paper, posters, or anything that can be rolled into a cylinder.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**likit** naman ng banig at itabi sa sulok.","translation":"Please **roll up** the mat and put it in the corner."},{"sentence":"Nilikit niya ang liham at itinago sa kanyang bulsa.","translation":"He **rolled up** the letter and hid it in his pocket."}]

meaning_filipino: Sangay ng medisina na tumutukoy sa pangangalaga, pag-unlad, at mga sakit ng mga sanggol at bata.
etymology: From English 'pediatrics', adapted to Tagalog phonology.
original_explanation: The medical field for everything 'bata'. If your baby has a fever, your toddler has 'ubo't sipon', or your kid needs a check-up, you go to a specialist in pediatrics. The waiting room is usually chaotic, filled with crying kids, colorful toys, and parents who desperately need coffee. This is the Filipinized spelling of 'pediatrics'.
usage_notes: The doctor is called a 'pediatrician' or 'pedia' for short.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kapatid ko ay nag-aaral ng **pedyatriks** sa isang malaking unibersidad.","translation":"My sibling is studying **pediatrics** at a big university."},{"sentence":"Dinala niya ang kanyang anak sa doktor na espesyalista sa **pedyatriks**.","translation":"She brought her child to a doctor specializing in **pediatrics**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang kilos ng pagbuo ng mga titik, salita, o pangungusap sa isang papel, kompyuter, o anumang midyum gamit ang panulat o teklado.
original_explanation: Ito yung ginagawa mo 'pag may exam, 'pag nag-e-email sa boss, o 'pag nag-po-post ng long-form hugot sa Facebook. Before, love letters. Ngayon, DMs, captions, at code. Lahat 'yan ay pag-sumusulat.
usage_notes: This is the present tense form. Past tense is 'sumulat'. Future tense is 'susulat'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumusulat** ako ng tula para sa kanya.","translation":"I am **writing** a poem for her."},{"sentence":"Ang mga bata ay **sumusulat** sa kanilang mga kwaderno.","translation":"The children are **writing** in their notebooks."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagturo, pagbanggit, o pagkilala sa isang partikular na tao, bagay, o ideya.
original_explanation: That moment when someone asks, 'Who finished the ulam?' and all eyes suddenly turn to you. That's a 'tukoy' moment. It's the act of pointing someone out, a direct reference, the opposite of the 'Sana 'di ako mapansin' prayer.
usage_notes: Often used in verb forms like 'tukuyin' (to identify/specify) and 'matukoy' (to be identified).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **tukoy** niya ay ang babaeng nakapula.","translation":"Her **reference** was the woman in red."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **tukuyin** kung sino ang may sala.","translation":"It's hard to **identify** who is at fault."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang anak o guya ng baka.
original_explanation: A baby cow. Super cute, wobbly, and probably ends up as the star of your next bulalo. It's the "junior" version of the animal that gives us milk and, well, beef. Think of it as the "toddler" stage of a baka.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang inahing baka ay hindi humihiwalay sa kanyang bagong silang na **bisiro**.","translation":"The mother cow does not separate from her newborn **calf**."},{"sentence":"Ang cute ng maliit na **bisiro** sa bukid.","translation":"The small **calf** in the field is cute."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkuha o pagsamsam sa isang pag-aari sa pamamagitan ng kapangyarihan o awtoridad.
original_explanation: What happens to your phone when your teacher catches you texting in class, or what the MMDA does to a vendor's paninda on the sidewalk. It's the official, authority-backed version of 'Akin na 'yan!' (Give me that!).
usage_notes: This is the object-focus verb form (-in suffix). The actor-focus form is 'kumumpiska'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binalaan sila na **kumpiskahin** ang kanilang mga paninda kung hindi sila aalis.","translation":"They were warned that their goods would be **confiscated** if they did not leave."},{"sentence":"Maaaring **kumpiskahin** ng guwardiya ang anumang ipinagbabawal na gamit.","translation":"The guard can **confiscate** any prohibited items."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na sumusunod, naniniwala, o sumusuporta sa isang lider, ideolohiya, o simulain.
etymology: From taga- (doer of an action) + sunod (follow).
original_explanation: Your 'followers' on Instagram and TikTok, but in real life. Sila yung mga tropa mong game sa lahat ng kalokohan mo, from trying a weird food trend to joining a new fandom. The ultimate 'yes-man' or loyal supporter.
usage_notes: Can have a neutral meaning (follower of a leader), a positive one (loyal disciple), or a slightly negative one (a blind follower).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang isang mabuting lider ay may maraming tapat na **tagasunod**.","translation":"A good leader has many loyal **followers**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga **tagasunod** ng banda ay naghintay nang magdamag para sa tiket.","translation":"The band's **followers** waited overnight for tickets."}]

translation: to be able to curse; to unintentionally curse
meaning_filipino: Hindi sinasadyang makapagbitiw ng masasamang salita o sumpa, karaniwang dahil sa gulat, sakit, o galit.
original_explanation: That moment when you stub your toe on the leg of the table and a bad word just flies out of your mouth. Or when you see your ex's new post and you just can't help it. 'Napakamura ako nang makita ko ang presyo ng bilihin.'
usage_notes: Often used with 'napa-' (napakamura) to emphasize the involuntary nature of the action. Distinguish from 'magmura' which is intentional cursing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang magugulat at baka ka **makamura** sa harap ng mga bata.","translation":"Don't get startled or you might **unintentionally curse** in front of the kids."},{"sentence":"Halos **makamura** ako sa sakit nang maipit ang daliri ko sa pinto.","translation":"I almost **cursed** from the pain when my finger got caught in the door."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagmamaneho ng motorsiklo, partikular na tumutukoy sa mga nagtatrabaho sa mga delivery service.
original_explanation: The modern-day superheroes na nagliligtas sa'yo mula sa gutom, katamaran, at "wala nang stock" na moments. Sila 'yung tumatawid sa baha at matinding traffic para lang maihatid ang milk tea o 2-pc chicken mo. "Pa-star na lang po, Ma'am/Sir!" is their battle cry. A true hero of the gig economy.
usage_notes: Ang kahulugan nito sa Pilipinas ay malakas na nauugnay sa mga delivery service (Grab, Lalamove, FoodPanda, etc.) dahil sa kanilang pagiging prominente.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Parating na raw ang **rider** na may dalang pagkain natin.","translation":"The **rider** with our food is said to be on the way."},{"sentence":"Ingat sa pagmamaneho, Kuya **Rider**!","translation":"Drive safely, Mr. **Rider**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging tahimik o hindi pagsasalita; ang hindi pag-imik o pagkibo.
original_explanation: This is that heavy, awkward silence after someone drops a major 'chismis' bomb in the group chat. It's the 'seen-zone' in noun form. Or the vibe in the office when the boss is in a bad mood. The sound of nothing, but it speaks volumes.
usage_notes: Refers to the state of not speaking, often implying a deliberate choice or a heavy atmosphere, as opposed to 'katahimikan' which can be a more neutral or peaceful silence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nabalot ng **kawalang-imik** ang silid nang ianunsyo ang balita.","translation":"The room was filled with **silence** when the news was announced."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **kawalang-imik** ay mas malakas pa sa anumang sigaw.","translation":"Her **reticence** was louder than any shout."}]

meaning_filipino: May pagkiling o tendensiya sa pakikipag-away o paglikha ng alitan.
original_explanation: Describes someone who's always looking for a fight. That officemate who replies-all to critique your work, the tito at the family reunion who brings up politics, or just anyone whose default mode seems to be 'suntukan na lang o.' They approach situations in a paaway manner.
usage_notes: Describes a mode of action or a personality trait.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bakit ba **paaway** lagi ang tono ng pananalita mo?","translation":"Why is the tone of your voice always so **confrontational**?"},{"sentence":"Umiwas ka sa mga taong **paaway** kung ayaw mo ng gulo.","translation":"Avoid **quarrelsome** people if you don't want trouble."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita o nagpapahiwatig ng matinding kalungkutan, pangungulila, o pananabik.
original_explanation: This is the more poetic, dramatic cousin of 'malungkot'. It's not just sad; it's the kind of sadness you feel while staring out the window on a rainy day, listening to a sad OPM song, and thinking about your life choices. It's the official emotion of #hugot. It's a deep, quiet sadness.
usage_notes: More literary or formal than `malungkot`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **malumbay** na tugtugin ang kaniyang narinig mula sa kapitbahay.","translation":"He heard a **melancholic** tune from the neighbor."},{"sentence":"Naging **malumbay** ang kaniyang mga araw mula nang umalis ang kaniyang kasintahan.","translation":"Her days became **sorrowful** ever since her partner left."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang posisyon ng pag-upo sa mga sakong, na ang mga tuhod ay nakabaluktot at ang bigat ng katawan ay nasa mga paa.
original_explanation: The classic "tambay sa kanto" pose. Or when you're waiting for your laundry to finish at the laundromat and all the seats are taken. You just find a corner and go 'nakatigda'. It's the Asian squat, but make it Pinoy.
usage_notes: Similar to 'nakatingkayad' but 'nakatigda' often implies a more stable, flat-footed squat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang maupong **nakatigda** habang nagkakape.","translation":"He likes to sit **squatting on his heels** while having coffee."},{"sentence":"May mga batang **nakatigda** sa tabi ng kalsada at naglalaro ng teks.","translation":"There were children **squatting** by the roadside playing with trading cards."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa asal o gawi na parang sa isang bata; isip-bata.
original_explanation: When a full-grown adult throws a tantrum because their milk tea order was wrong. It’s that colleague who loves to pull pranks, or your tito who still collects action figures (which is cool, but still). It's the opposite of 'acting your age.'
usage_notes: Can be used as an adjective ('Siya ay kilos-bata') or a noun ('Hindi maganda ang pagiging kilos-bata mo.') to describe childish behavior.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit matanda na siya, **kilos-bata** pa rin kung magtampo.","translation":"Even though he's old, he's still **childish** when he sulks."},{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na 'yang pagiging **kilos-bata** mo, hindi na nakakatuwa.","translation":"Stop your **childish behavior**, it's not funny anymore."}]

translation: to be swarmed by a crowd; to be the center of a commotion
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging sentro ng atensyon ng isang magulo at maingay na grupo ng mga tao.
original_explanation: What happens when a celebrity is spotted in a mall, or when there's a 'Piso Sale' announcement. Everyone rushes in, creating chaos. You become the 'pinagkakaguluhan'. It's the human version of ants swarming a piece of candy.
usage_notes: The object of this verb is the person or thing causing the commotion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw ng sikat na artista na **pagkaguluhan** siya sa publiko.","translation":"The famous actor does not want **to be swarmed by a crowd** in public."},{"sentence":"Tiyak na **pagkakaguluhan** ng mga bata ang mga bagong laruan.","translation":"The new toys will surely **be the center of commotion** for the children."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manipis at patag na piraso ng bato, semento, o seramika na karaniwang ginagamit bilang pantakip sa sahig, dingding, o iba pang patag na ibabaw.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung tiles sa sahig ng bahay niyo. 'Pag malamig ang panahon, sarap higaan. 'Pag may nabasag kang baso dito, yari ka sa nanay mo. Ito rin ang dahilan kung bakit kailangan mong mag-tsinelas sa loob ng bahay kung ayaw mong magka-rayuma, sabi ng mga lola.
usage_notes: Sometimes used interchangeably with 'baldosa' or the English word 'tiles'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bagong palit ang **losa** sa aming kusina kaya makintab na ulit.","translation":"The **tiles** in our kitchen are newly replaced, that's why they're shiny again."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka, baka madulas ka dahil basa ang **losa**.","translation":"Be careful, you might slip because the **floor tile** is wet."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pagkain o ulam na inihanda para sa hapunan.
original_explanation: The main event of the day's food journey. Ito yung ulam na pinag-isipan mo buong araw habang nasa trabaho. "Ano kaya ang panghapunan namin mamaya?" is a national existential question asked around 4 PM.
usage_notes: Pangunahing tumutukoy sa mismong pagkain na inihahain para sa hapunan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Adobong manok ang ating **panghapunan** ngayong gabi.","translation":"Chicken adobo is our **dinner meal** for tonight."},{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng isda para sa **panghapunan**.","translation":"Mom bought fish for **dinner**."}]

translation: tied; bound (usually hands behind the back)
meaning_filipino: Nakatali ang mga kamay, karaniwan sa likuran, gamit ang lubid o posas.
original_explanation: 'Yung itsura ng kontrabida sa pelikula 'pag nahuli na siya ng bida. It's a specific kind of being tied up, usually with the hands behind the back. It’s what you feel like when you have too many deadlines and can’t do anything else—nakapugal sa trabaho.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to the hands being bound, often behind the back. More specific than just 'nakatali'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natagpuan ang suspek na **nakapugal** ang mga kamay.","translation":"The suspect was found with his hands **tied**."},{"sentence":"Iniwan siyang **nakapugal** sa isang madilim na silid.","translation":"He was left **bound** in a dark room."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng pataba o abono sa lupa upang mapabuti ang paglago ng mga halaman.
original_explanation: This is the plantito/plantita action verb. When your ornamental cabbage starts looking sad, it's time to **mag-abono**. It's the act of giving your plant babies their "vitamins" so they can grow big and strong, and you can post their glow-up on Instagram.
usage_notes: This meaning is specific to agriculture and gardening.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing umaga, si Lolo ay nagpupunta sa hardin upang **mag-abono** ng kanyang mga tanim na gulay.","translation":"Every morning, Grandpa goes to the garden to **apply fertilizer** to his vegetable plants."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang matigas na panlabas na balat o takip sa likod ng isang pagong na nagsisilbing proteksyon at tirahan nito.
original_explanation: The original mobile home. It's the turtle's built-in, portable shield against haters and life's problems. When things get tough, they just... go inside. We all need a 'bahay ng pagong' sometimes, especially during family reunions.
usage_notes: A descriptive phrase used literally to refer to a turtle's shell.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **bahay ng pagong** ay gawa sa buto at kartilago.","translation":"The **turtle's shell** is made of bone and cartilage."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagkakaroon ng pag-aalinlangan o kawalan ng katiyakan sa isang bagay; hindi makapagpasya agad.
original_explanation: That feeling when you've added to cart on Shopee but you're staring at the 'Place Order' button, thinking about your life choices and your wallet. It's the 'should I or shouldn't I?' moment.
usage_notes: Implies a sense of doubt or feeling that something is not quite right or appropriate.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mag-alangan** na magtanong kung may hindi ka naiintindihan.","translation":"Don't **hesitate** to ask if there's something you don't understand."},{"sentence":"Siya ay **nag-alangan** na tanggapin ang alok dahil masyadong malayo ang opisina.","translation":"He **was uncertain** about accepting the offer because the office was too far."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang rehiyon sa pinakahilagang bahagi ng daigdig, na sumasaklaw sa Karagatang Artiko at mga kalapit na lupain.
original_explanation: The polar opposite of the Philippines in every way. It's the land of polar bears, Santa Claus's workshop, and temperatures that would make your AC unit cry. While we complain about 35°C heat, they're chilling (literally) at -35°C.
usage_notes: Laging isinusulat na may malaking titik sa unahan dahil ito ay isang pangngalang pantangi (proper noun).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga polar bear ay matatagpuan sa rehiyon ng **Artiko**.","translation":"Polar bears are found in the **Arctic** region."}]

translation: to be able to make someone laugh
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang magdulot ng halakhak, aliw, o tuwa sa ibang tao sa pamamagitan ng salita o kilos.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `makapag-` (kakayahan), `pa-` (padahilan), at salitang-ugat na `tawa`.
original_explanation: This is your superpower when the group chat is dead, or when your friend is going through some major hugot. If you can make them laugh, you have the ability to 'makapagpatawa'. It's the skill of every stand-up comedian, the class clown, and that one tito who always has a corny joke ready for the family reunion.
usage_notes: Ang unlaping `makapag-` ay nagpapahiwatig ng kakayahan o potensyal na gawin ang isang aksyon. Ang `pa-` ay ginagawang padahilan ang pandiwa, na nangangahulugang ang paksa ang sanhi ng pagkilos ng iba (sa kasong ito, pagtawa).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit pagod sa trabaho, sinusubukan niyang **makapagpatawa** ng kanyang mga anak.","translation":"Even when tired from work, he tries **to be able to make** his children **laugh**."},{"sentence":"Sana **makapagpatawa** ako sa aking presentasyon para hindi antukin ang audience.","translation":"I hope I can **make** the audience **laugh** during my presentation so they don't get sleepy."}]

translation: to align, to put in a line
meaning_filipino: Ayusin ang mga bagay-bagay sa isang tuwid na guhit, hanay, o pila.
etymology: From the verb-forming prefix `i-` + `linya` (line), from Spanish `línea` (line).
original_explanation: That feeling of satisfaction when you **ilinya** your apps on your phone screen. It's what your teacher shouted during flag ceremony: 'Ilinya nang maayos!' It's about making things straight and orderly, whether it's shoes, cars in a parking lot, or your life goals (which is the hardest to **ilinya**, tbh).
usage_notes: Commonly used for physically aligning objects or people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **ilinya** ninyo ang mga silya bago magsimula ang programa.","translation":"Please, **align** the chairs before the program starts."},{"sentence":"Maayos niyang **inilinya** ang mga libro sa estante ayon sa kulay.","translation":"She neatly **lined up** the books on the shelf according to color."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng labis at hindi mapigilang emosyon o pananabik, lalo na sa isang grupo ng mga tao.
original_explanation: That moment when your favorite K-Pop group appears on stage and the whole arena loses its collective mind. Or when there's a piso fare sale and everyone's trying to book a flight at the same time. It's OA (over-acting) mode, but on a massive scale.
usage_notes: Describes an exaggerated or uncontrollable emotional reaction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng **histerismo** sa mga manonood nang lumabas ang sikat na artista.","translation":"The audience fell into **hysterics** when the famous celebrity came out."},{"sentence":"Ang biglaang anunsyo ay nagdulot ng **histerismo** sa merkado.","translation":"The sudden announcement caused **hysteria** in the market."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang propesyonal na may kasanayan sa pag-iingat, pagsusuri, at pag-uulat ng mga financial record o talaang pampinansyal.
etymology: From English "accountant." The Filipino equivalent, "tagatuos," is rarely used in modern conversation.
original_explanation: The person in the office who magically turns a mountain of receipts and spreadsheets into something that makes sense (or at least, something the BIR will accept). They are the guardians of the budget, the masters of Excel, and the reason you can't just claim your 10th milk tea of the day as a business expense. They live by the motto: "It's accrual world."
usage_notes: The English word "accountant" is used almost exclusively, even in Tagalog sentences.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating kumuha ng **accountant** para ayusin ang ating tax.","translation":"We need to hire an **accountant** to fix our taxes."},{"sentence":"Ang ate ko ay isang CPA, isang lisensyadong **accountant**.","translation":"My older sister is a CPA, a licensed **accountant**."}]

translation: to fill with content, to stuff
meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng laman o nilalaman ang isang bagay na walang laman o may puwang.
original_explanation: This is what you do to an empanada, a siopao, or a Thanksgiving turkey. It's the act of putting the 'palaman' (filling) inside. Figuratively, it can also mean to add substance or content to something, like 'palamnan mo naman ng datos ang report mo' (add some data to your report).
usage_notes: Used for both food and abstract concepts like reports or stories.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **palamnan** ang mga unan ng bagong bulak.","translation":"We need to **stuff** the pillows with new cotton."},{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **palamnan** ng keso ang pandesal.","translation":"Don't forget to **fill** the pandesal with cheese."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglikha ng mga salita, pangungusap, o teksto sa papel o anumang midyum gamit ang panulat, makinilya, o kompyuter.
etymology: Nagmula sa unlaping 'man-' at salitang-ugat na 'sulat'.
original_explanation: The act of writing. Not just texting 'k' or 'lol', but actually composing something. Whether you're a journalist, a novelist, or just someone writing a 'hugot' post on Facebook, you are practicing the art of **manulat**. It's turning your 'daldal' into something readable. The person who writes is a 'manunulat'.
usage_notes: Isang mas pormal o pampanitikang termino para sa 'sumulat'. Madalas itong tumutukoy sa pagsusulat bilang isang propesyon o seryosong gawain.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang **manulat** ng isang nobela balang araw.","translation":"She dreams of **writing** a novel someday."},{"sentence":"Si Jose Rizal ay isang tanyag na bayaning marunong **manulat**.","translation":"Jose Rizal was a famous hero who knew how to **write**."}]

translation: to reverse, to invert, to turn inside out
meaning_filipino: Ilagay sa posisyong salungat sa dati; gawing kabaligtaran ang ayos, direksyon, o kahulugan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang 'baligtad' (reversed, upside down) + hulaping pandiwa na '-in'.
original_explanation: Yung ginagawa mo sa t-shirt mo pagkatapos maligo para matuyo agad. O yung ginagawa sa'yo ng chismosa mong kapitbahay—ikaw na nga ang biktima, ikaw pa ang pinalabas na masama. They flip the script on you!
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin nang literal (pagbaligtad ng isang bagay) o matalinghaga (pagpihit sa isang kuwento o sitwasyon).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **baligtarin** ang kuwento para lang pagtakpan ang iyong pagkakamali.","translation":"Don't **twist** the story just to cover up your mistake."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **baligtarin** ang damit bago ito isampay.","translation":"You need to **turn** the shirt **inside out** before hanging it to dry."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kikil na may malalaki at magagaspang na ngipin, ginagamit para sa mabilis na pag-aalis ng materyal.
original_explanation: This is the 'brute force' version of the kikil tool. Not for fine-tuning, but for when you need to remove a lot of material fast. Think of it as the 'buraot' of files—it just takes and takes without finesse. It's for the initial, messy part of the job before you bring in the more refined tools.
usage_notes: A descriptive phrase combining 'kikil' (file) and 'magaspang' (rough, coarse).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mo ng **kikil na magaspang** para diyan dahil makapal ang kalawang.","translation":"You need a **coarse file** for that because the rust is thick."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi kaaya-aya sa paningin; may kapintasang pisikal.
original_explanation: The opposite of 'sana all'. It's that feeling when you take a selfie and the front camera betrays you. It can describe a bad haircut, a questionable outfit choice, or even a messy situation. "Ang pangit ng sulat ko, parang reseta ng doktor."
usage_notes: Can also be used to describe non-physical things like a situation, a performance, or a result (e.g., "pangit ang resulta," "pangit ang laro").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong sabihing **pangit** ang guhit niya, pinaghirapan niya 'yan.","translation":"Don't say his drawing is **ugly**, he worked hard on that."},{"sentence":"Naging **pangit** ang sitwasyon nang magsimula silang magsigawan.","translation":"The situation became **ugly** when they started shouting at each other."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pautos na anyo ng salitang 'ayusin', na nangangahulugang ipagawa sa iba ang pagsasaayos o pagkukumpuni ng isang bagay.
etymology: From `pa-` (causative prefix, meaning 'to ask someone to do') + `ayos` (order, fix).
original_explanation: The magic word you say when something's broken and you can't (or won't) fix it yourself. 'Paayos mo na 'yang tumutulong aircon!' is a classic household line. It's a command that's also a request, delegating the task of fixing something to someone else.
usage_notes: This is the imperative form, often used with 'mo' or 'ninyo'. It can be seen as a casual contraction of 'paki-ayos'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Paayos** mo naman itong relo ko.","translation":"Please **have** my watch **fixed**."},{"sentence":"Sino ang pwedeng tawagan para **paayos** ang internet?","translation":"Who can we call to **get** the internet **fixed**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtiklop o pag-ayos sa isang bagay, karaniwan ay damit o papel, upang maging mas maliit o mas maayos ang anyo.
original_explanation: The verb form of that chore you hate the most: folding laundry. "**Tutupin** ko na ba 'tong mga damit?" is a question filled with either genuine helpfulness or passive-aggressive dread. It’s the action that separates the clean clothes from the *clean and organized* clothes. Also applicable to folding love letters you'll never send.
usage_notes: An object-focus verb, often used as an imperative (command) or infinitive. The future tense is 'tutupiin', but 'tutupin' is commonly used in commands or statements of intent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **tupiin** mo nang maayos ang iyong mga damit.","translation":"Please, **fold** your clothes neatly."},{"sentence":"Ang dami ko pang labada na kailangang **tupiin**.","translation":"I still have so much laundry that needs to be **folded**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpasok at pamumuhay sa isang kumbento bilang isang madre o relihiyosa.
etymology: From Spanish 'monja' (nun), combined with the Tagalog verb prefix 'mag-'.
original_explanation: The ultimate "it's complicated" relationship status with the world. It’s when a woman decides to dedicate her life to religious service. Often used as a half-joking threat by parents to their daughters who have too many suitors, or by women who are tired of dating apps: "Ayoko na, magmo-mongha na lang ako!"
usage_notes: The male equivalent is "magpari" (to become a priest).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bata pa lamang siya ay pangarap na niyang **magmongha**.","translation":"Ever since she was young, it has been her dream to **become a nun**."},{"sentence":"Pagod na raw siya sa mundo kaya nagdesisyon siyang **magmongha**.","translation":"She said she was tired of the world so she decided to **become a nun**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pariralang papuri na nagpapahayag ng matinding paghanga sa galing, itsura, o pangkalahatang pagganap ng isang tao.
etymology: Kombinasyon ng Ingles na 'very' at slang na 'slay', na nagmula sa African-American Vernacular English (AAVE) at pinasikat ng kulturang popular at LGBTQ+.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate compliment from the Gen Z dictionary. When you look amazing, when your presentation was flawless, when you delivered the perfect comeback—you didn't just do well, you 'slayed.' Adding 'very' just amps it up. 'Your new haircut? Very slay!'
usage_notes: Isang napaka-impormal na ekspresyon na ginagamit bilang pinakamataas na papuri, lalo na sa mga online na komunidad at sa mga kabataan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita mo ba ang sagot niya sa Q&A? **Very slay**!","translation":"Did you see her answer in the Q&A? **Very slay**!"},{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng OOTD mo, mars! **Very slay**!","translation":"Your OOTD is gorgeous, girl! **Very slay**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na mangkok na yari sa bato, metal, o matigas na kahoy, na ginagamit kasama ng pandikdik (palo) para sa pagdurog ng mga sangkap.
original_explanation: The bowl part of the 'mortar and pestle' combo, 'yung partner ng 'palo' or 'pandikdik'. Ito ang OG food processor ng lola mo para durugin ang bawang, paminta, at mani. Kapag naririnig mo na ang tunog nito sa kusina, alam mong may masarap na niluluto.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'pandikdikan,' but 'almires' specifically refers to the bowl, while the pestle is the 'palo' or 'halo.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Durugin mo ang bawang at paminta sa **almires**.","translation":"Crush the garlic and pepper in the **mortar**."},{"sentence":"Ang bigat ng lumang **almires** na gawa sa marmol.","translation":"The old **mortar** made of marble is heavy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging magkakasama o nagkakaisa bilang isang grupo.
original_explanation: This is the official term for your barkada's "squad goals" moment. It's the feeling of unity when you're all cramming for an exam, sharing one bag of chips, or just chilling at a coffee shop. It's the opposite of "social distancing."
usage_notes: Emphasizes the collective state and feeling of unity within a group. Stronger than just 'pagsasama' (act of being together).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Pasko ay panahon ng **pagkasama-sama** ng pamilya.","translation":"Christmas is a time for family **togetherness**."},{"sentence":"Pinahahalagahan namin ang aming **pagkasama-sama** bilang magkakaibigan.","translation":"We value our **being together** as friends."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kilos ng pag-iyak na may kasamang malalim at putol-putol na paghinga, na gagawin pa lamang sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: Future tense of 'humikbi'. Eto 'yung mangyayari sa'yo 'pag napanood mo na 'yung ending ng paborito mong K-drama or 'pag nakita mong 1% na lang ang battery ng phone mo at walang powerbank. A quiet, shaky cry.
usage_notes: This is the future tense of 'humikbi' (to sob). A sob ('hikbi') is a more intense, often suppressed cry compared to a simple cry ('iyak').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang lungkot ng pelikula, alam kong **maghihikbi** na naman ako sa dulo.","translation":"The movie is so sad, I know I **will sob** again at the end."},{"sentence":"Tahimik siyang **maghihikbi** sa kanyang kwarto para hindi marinig ng iba.","translation":"She **will sob** quietly in her room so others won't hear."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paglalakbay na isinasagawa ng isang pangkat ng mga tao na may tiyak na layunin, tulad ng pagtuklas, pananaliksik, o digmaan.
original_explanation: Parang team building n'yo sa office, pero mas hardcore. Instead of trust falls, may chance na may ahas o maligaw kayo sa bundok. Ito 'yung OG 'Amazing Race' bago pa nauso sa TV.
usage_notes: Often used in historical or scientific contexts, referring to a journey with a specific, often challenging, purpose.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumama siya sa isang **ekspedisyon** sa Amazon upang pag-aralan ang mga bihirang halaman.","translation":"He joined an **expedition** to the Amazon to study rare plants."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng harang o linya sa isang lugar upang hindi ito mapasok o malapitan ng mga tao, karaniwang para sa seguridad o pag-iingat.
original_explanation: Ginagawa 'to ng pulis sa crime scene para 'di makapasok ang mga usisero't usisera. O kaya 'yung ginagawa ng nanay mo sa bagong linis na sahig gamit ang basahan at tingin na nagsasabing 'Subukan-mong-tumawid-diyan.'
usage_notes: Associated with security, police lines, or restricting access to an area.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang mga awtoridad na **magkordon** sa buong lugar pagkatapos ng pagsabog.","translation":"The authorities decided to **cordon off** the entire area after the explosion."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **magkordon** tayo sa paligid ng stage para sa kaligtasan ng mga manonood.","translation":"We need to **cordon off** the area around the stage for the safety of the audience."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahabang piyesa ng musika na karaniwang tinutugtog ng isang orkestra, na binubuo ng ilang magkakaugnay na bahagi o 'movements'.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "sinfonía," na mula sa Griyegong "symphōnia" (kasunduan ng tunog).
original_explanation: Imagine mo 'yung background music sa isang epic movie scene, 'yung may violin, cello, trumpeta, at lahat na, nagtutunugan nang sabay-sabay in perfect harmony. That's a simponia. It's the high-class, 'pang-Cultural Center of the Philippines' version of a band jamming. It's what you listen to when you want to feel dramatic or sophisticated while stuck in EDSA traffic.
usage_notes: A formal and somewhat rare word. The English word 'symphony' is more commonly used in casual contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakagandang pakinggan ang **simponia** na nilikha ng pambansang alagad ng sining.","translation":"The **symphony** created by the national artist is so beautiful to listen to."}]

translation: fiber (especially abaca or coconut husk fiber)
meaning_filipino: Himaymay o hibla mula sa mga halaman, partikular na mula sa abaka, bunot ng niyog, o katulad na materyales.
original_explanation: Before there was fiber optic, there was just *lanot*. This is the tough, stringy stuff you get from plants like abaca. It's used for making ropes, sacks (sako), and the *bunot* you use to polish the floor until you can see your reflection. It's the OG sustainable material.
usage_notes: Can refer to any coarse plant fiber.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **lanot** ng abaka ay ginagamit sa paggawa ng matibay na lubid.","translation":"The **fiber** of the abaca is used to make durable ropes."},{"sentence":"Matigas ang **lanot** ng bunot ng niyog.","translation":"The **fiber** of the coconut husk is tough."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng isang mahalagang bagay bilang garantiya o kolateral kapalit ng isang utang.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'kapit sa patalim' move. When petsa de peligro hits hard and you're fresh out of cash, you go to a pawnshop to 'isangla' your jewelry, your phone, or even your laptop. It's a temporary trade: your valuable item for quick cash, hoping you can get it back before the due date. It's the national sport during 'gipit' season.
usage_notes: The object being pawned is the focus of the sentence when using the 'i-' prefix. For example, 'Isangla mo ang alahas' means '(You) pawn the jewelry'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napilitan siyang **isangla** ang singsing na pamana ng kanyang lola.","translation":"She was forced **to pawn** the ring inherited from her grandmother."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **isangla** ang iyong kinabukasan para sa panandaliang ligaya.","translation":"Don't **mortgage** your future for temporary happiness."}]

translation: to spit out; to expel from the mouth
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-alis o pagpapalabas ng isang bagay mula sa bibig, na maaaring sinasadya o hindi.
original_explanation: What you do when you accidentally chew on a peppercorn in your sinigang. Metaphorically, it's what happens when you can't hold back a harsh comment. "Think before you speak, 'ika nga, para hindi ka magluwa ng masasakit na salita."
usage_notes: Different from 'dura' which means to spit saliva. 'Luwa' specifically refers to expelling a solid object or food from the mouth.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napilitan siyang **magluwa** ng buto ng pakwan.","translation":"He was forced to **spit out** the watermelon seed."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magluwa** ng pagkain sa hapag-kainan, hindi magandang tingnan.","translation":"Don't **spit out** food at the dining table, it's not pleasant to see."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ekspresyon o itsura ng mukha na nagpapahiwatig ng damdamin; ang sining o kilos ng paggaya sa pamamagitan ng galaw at ekspresyon ng mukha.
original_explanation: This is your face's "RBF" (Resting B*tch Face), "pabebe" smile, or "kilig" expression. It's the non-verbal cues you give off. When someone says "Ayusin mo 'yang mimika ng mukha mo," they're telling you your face is broadcasting your true feelings too loudly.
usage_notes: More commonly refers to facial expression rather than the art of pantomime.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kitang-kita sa **mimika** ng kanyang mukha ang labis na pagkadismaya.","translation":"The extreme disappointment was evident in the **expression** on his face."}]

translation: to break; to damage; to destroy
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagwasak, pagbasag, o pagdudulot ng depekto sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: The action that leads to the adjective. This is what your little sibling does to your new toy, what a typhoon does to houses, or what you do to your friend's trust when you spoil the ending of their favorite K-drama. 'Huwag mong sirain!' is a national cry.
usage_notes: The verb form. The pronunciation shifts stress to the second syllable: /si-RA-in/ for the command form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinong nag-**sira** ng remote control?","translation":"Who **broke** the remote control?"},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **sirain** ang tiwala ko sa'yo.","translation":"Don't **destroy** my trust in you."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang yugto ng panahon na katumbas ng 365 (o 366) na araw, o ang panahong kinakailangan ng Mundo upang makumpleto ang isang pag-ikot sa Araw.
original_explanation: The unit of measurement for how long you've been single, how long 'til your next salary increase, or how many years it's been since your favorite show ended. 'Isang **taon** na akong naghihintay sa promo, Lord!'
usage_notes: Very common. Used for age ('ilang taon ka na?'), dates, and duration.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magbabakasyon kami sa probinsya sa susunod na **taon**.","translation":"We will go on vacation to the province next **year**."},{"sentence":"Ilang **taon** ka nang nagtatrabaho dito?","translation":"For how many **years** have you been working here?"}]

meaning_filipino: Utos o pakiusap na magpahabi o ipagawa ang paglalala ng mga sinulid, hibla, o materyales upang makabuo ng tela, banig, o anumang katulad nito.
original_explanation: This is the boss-level command for weaving. You don't do the weaving yourself; you tell someone, "Hey, pahabiin mo nga itong mga hibla para maging banig." It's like ordering a custom-made item from a weaver. Think of it as the pre-industrial version of "paki-print" or "pa-photocopy."
usage_notes: A causative verb. The subject of the sentence causes the action of weaving to be done by someone else.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-order ang reyna na **pahabiin** ang pinakamagandang tela para sa kanyang bestida.","translation":"The queen ordered to **have the finest cloth woven** for her dress."},{"sentence":"Maaari mo bang **pahabiin** itong mga dahon ng niyog para gawing basket?","translation":"Can you **have these coconut leaves woven** to make a basket?"}]

meaning_filipino: Nakahiga na ang mukha o dibdib ay nakaharap sa sahig o lupa.
original_explanation: 'Yung position mo sa sahig 'pag sobrang pagod ka na from work, you just drop everything and lie face down. Or 'yung ginagawa ng mga sundalo sa training. Also the default position for a dramatic "I give up!" moment.
usage_notes: 'Nakarapa' is the state of being 'dapa' (to fall flat on one's face). It describes the resulting position.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natagpuan siyang **nakarapa** sa sahig, walang malay.","translation":"He was found **lying face down** on the floor, unconscious."},{"sentence":"Ang mga bata ay masayang naglalaro habang **nakarapa** sa damuhan.","translation":"The children were happily playing while **lying face down** on the grass."}]

meaning_filipino: Napakalakas na tunog na halos ikasira ng pandinig o magdulot ng pansamantalang pagkabingi.
original_explanation: Yung sound system ng kapitbahay mo tuwing may party, sobrang lakas, as in **makabingi**! Parang nasa loob ng speaker 'yung tenga mo. O 'yung tili ng kaibigan mo kapag nakita si crush, level 999 na **makabingi**.
usage_notes: The prefix 'maka-' indicates causation. In this context, 'makabingi' means 'able to cause deafness' or simply 'deafening'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Makabingi** ang katahimikan sa pagitan naming dalawa pagkatapos ng aming pagtatalo.","translation":"The silence between us after our argument was **deafening**."},{"sentence":"Nagsuot siya ng earplugs dahil sa **makabingi**ng ingay ng makina.","translation":"He wore earplugs because of the **deafening** noise of the machine."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang institusyon ng mas mataas na edukasyon kung saan itinuturo ang mga espesyal na kurso o larangan ng kaalaman; kolehiyo o instituto.
original_explanation: The place you go after high school to specialize. It's where you learn how to be a 'dalubhasa' (expert). Think of it as the training ground for future professionals, artists, and people who are experts at cramming for exams. This is where your baon allowance magically disappears.
usage_notes: A more formal or literary term for `kolehiyo`. It emphasizes the aspect of specialization.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtapos siya sa isang tanyag na **dalubhasaan** ng sining.","translation":"She graduated from a famous **college** of arts."},{"sentence":"Ang **Dalubhasaan** ng Agham ng Unibersidad ng Pilipinas ay nangunguna sa pananaliksik.","translation":"The **College** of Science of the University of the Philippines leads in research."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o pook kung saan isinasagawa ang mga laro ng pagkakataon o pustahan na may kinalaman sa pera.
etymology: Mula sa salitang 'sugal' (gamble) + '-an' (hulapi na nagsasaad ng lugar).
original_explanation: The place where your tito's 13th-month pay goes to die. It can be a high-end casino with flashing lights or just a makeshift table in a back alley for a game of tong-its. It's the Bermuda Triangle of money, where fortunes are made and, more often, lost.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinalakay ng mga pulis ang ilegal na **sugalan** sa kanilang barangay.","translation":"The police raided the illegal **gambling den** in their village."},{"sentence":"Maraming tao sa **sugalan** tuwing araw ng sahod.","translation":"There are many people at the **gambling place** during payday."}]

translation: to bump one's head against something
meaning_filipino: Sadyain o hindi sinasadyang ibangga ang ulo ng isang tao o sarili sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: What you want to do to your own head when you remember a cringey thing you did five years ago. Or what your kuya threatens to do to you when you steal the last piece of chicken.
usage_notes: Often used in the imperative form "Untugin mo!"
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **untugin** ang ulo mo sa pader sa sobrang inis.","translation":"Don't **bump** your head against the wall out of extreme annoyance."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagkuha o pag-angkin ng isang bagay o serbisyo kapalit ng pera o katumbas na halaga.
original_explanation: That moment of pure joy (or instant regret) when you finally click 'Add to Cart' and 'Checkout.' From the palengke run for groceries to splurging on a new phone, this is the core of our consumerist hearts. Ang pagbili online ang dahilan ng pagdami ng 'unnecessary' but 'makes me happy' items sa bahay.
usage_notes: Refers to the general act of purchasing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siya sa **pagbili** ng mga damit online.","translation":"She loves the **act of buying** clothes online."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagbili** ng bahay ay isang malaking desisyon.","translation":"The **purchase** of a house is a big decision."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hanay o linya, karaniwang binubuo ng mga pulis, sundalo, o anumang harang, na itinatag upang pigilan ang pagpasok o paglabas sa isang partikular na lugar.
original_explanation: That yellow tape with 'Police Line Do Not Cross' at crime scenes, that's a **kordon**. Or the human barricade of guards at a concert to stop you from getting backstage. Basically, it's the physical 'access denied' line.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of police, military, or emergency situations to secure an area.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtayo ng **kordon** ang mga pulis sa paligid ng lugar ng krimen.","translation":"The police set up a **cordon** around the crime scene."},{"sentence":"Mahirap makalusot sa **kordon** ng mga guwardiya.","translation":"It's hard to get past the guards' **cordon**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang pamalit na walang tiyak na kahulugan, karaniwang ginagamit sa kolokyal na usapan upang tukuyin ang isang bagay, lugar, tao, o sitwasyon na hindi maisip o ayaw tukuyin.
etymology: From Filipino gay slang (Swardspeak). A highly popular and versatile placeholder word.
original_explanation: The mother of all placeholder words. If your brain lags and you can't find the right noun, verb, or adjective, just insert "churva" and everyone will still probably get you. "Kunin mo 'yung churva sa ibabaw ng table." It's a testament to the Filipino talent for understanding the unsaid.
usage_notes: The quintessential 'bekimon' or gay slang word that has crossed over to mainstream colloquial Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkita kami sa **churva**... alam mo na, 'yung bagong coffee shop.","translation":"We met at the **whatchamacallit**... you know, that new coffee shop."},{"sentence":"Ano ba 'yung **churva** na pinag-usapan natin kahapon?","translation":"What was that **thingamajig** we were talking about yesterday?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggalaw o pag-imbay ng balakang at katawan sa isang ritmikong paraan, tulad ng sa pagsasayaw o paglakad.
original_explanation: That confident, rhythmic hip sway you see in beauty pageants or from your favorite TikTok dancer. It's the "Lava Walk" energy. It's how you walk when you know you look good and you want everyone else to know it too. The opposite of walking like a robot.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a graceful, sometimes seductive, way of walking or dancing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinangaan ng lahat ang **panginginday** ng mananayaw sa entablado.","translation":"Everyone admired the dancer's **hip-swaying** on stage."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa kanyang eleganteng **panginginday** habang naglalakad.","translation":"She is known for her elegant **swaying of the hips** while walking."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bilanggo na pinagkakatiwalaan ng mga awtoridad sa bilangguan at binibigyan ng mga espesyal na pribilehiyo o tungkulin.
original_explanation: Sila 'yung 'model student' sa loob ng kulungan. Dahil sa good behavior, pinagkakatiwalaan sila ng guards. Sila 'yung inuutusan na maglinis ng office ng warden o mag-distribute ng pagkain. May perks, parang may 'employee of the month' award pero sa Bilibid version.
usage_notes: Isang tiyak na termino sa loob ng sistemang penal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang mabuting asal, ginawa siyang **bilanggong-katiwala**.","translation":"Because of his good behavior, he was made a **prisoner trustee**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga **bilanggong-katiwala** ay may mas maraming kalayaan sa loob ng bilangguan.","translation":"The **trusties** have more freedom inside the prison."}]

translation: to act young; to be childish
meaning_filipino: Kumilos na parang bata; magpakita ng mga katangiang pambata sa kabila ng edad.
original_explanation: When a tito or tita suddenly busts out their old dance moves at a party or starts using Gen Z slang they don't understand. It's about letting your inner child out, for better or for worse. "Hayaan mo na si Daddy, minsan lang 'yan magpakabata at mag-TikTok."
usage_notes: Can be used positively (to be young at heart) or negatively (to be childish).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit may edad na si Lolo, mahilig pa ring **magpakabata** at makipaglaro sa mga apo niya.","translation":"Even though Grandpa is old, he still likes to **act young** and play with his grandchildren."},{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang **magpakabata** diyan, hindi na bagay sa iyo ang mag-tantrums.","translation":"Don't **be childish** there, throwing tantrums doesn't suit you anymore."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang palihim na pagkuha ng isang bagay na may maliit na halaga; pagnanakaw nang tingi-tingi.
original_explanation: This is low-level stealing. It’s not a full-on bank heist; it's taking a pen from the office, sneaking a piece of chocolate from your sibling's stash, or getting 'extra' suka from the Mang Inasal condiment station. It's the 'nawala lang, hindi kinuha' kind of theft.
usage_notes: Refers to petty theft, often done sneakily and for small items.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahuli siyang sinusubukang **mang-umit** ng kendi sa tindahan.","translation":"He was caught trying to **filch** candy from the store."},{"sentence":"'Huwag kang sanay na **mang-umit** ng gamit ng iba, maliit man o malaki,' sabi ni Nanay.","translation":"'Don't get used to **pilfering** other people's things, whether small or big,' said Mother."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, karaniwang babae, na kumikilos sa paraang malandi o nagpapakita ng labis na pagnanais na makuha ang atensyon ng iba, lalo na ng kalalakihan.
etymology: From 'ta-' (a prefix indicating habit or inclination) + 'landi' (flirt).
original_explanation: Old-school term for "flirt," a bit more intense than "pabebe" and more direct than "pa-cute." 'Yung tita mong laging may comment sa OOTD mo at sa love life mo, baka tinawag siyang **talandi** noong kabataan niya. It's a word that screams "Marites was here."
usage_notes: Often used pejoratively, but can also be used playfully among friends. The male equivalent is 'harot'. Can also function as an adjective (flirtatious).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinawag siyang **talandi** dahil sa kanyang paraan ng pananamit at pakikipag-usap.","translation":"She was called a **flirt** because of the way she dressed and talked."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, biro lang 'yung pagiging **talandi** niya.","translation":"Don't worry, her being **flirtatious** is just a joke."}]

translation: Genshin (referring to the game Genshin Impact)
meaning_filipino: Isang sikat na online action role-playing game na binuo ng miHoYo. Ang buong pamagat nito ay Genshin Impact.
etymology: Mula sa pamagat ng larong "Genshin Impact".
original_explanation: The game that will make you say "last quest na" at 2 AM. Kilala rin bilang 'gacha hell' kung saan uubusin mo ang pera mo para sa isang 5-star character na 'waifu' o 'husbando'. If you hear someone screaming "PULLED IT!", they're probably playing Genshin.
usage_notes: Pinaikling pangalan para sa larong "Genshin Impact".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maglalaro muna ako ng **Genshin** bago matulog.","translation":"I'll play **Genshin** first before sleeping."},{"sentence":"Naubos ang data ko kaka-download ng update sa **Genshin**.","translation":"My data ran out from downloading the **Genshin** update."}]

translation: to grow a mustache; to have a mustache
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon o pag-aalaga ng buhok sa itaas ng labi.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of having that 'Tito look' or trying to channel your inner Goyo. It's the act of cultivating that upper lip foliage. When you drink milk and get a white 'mustache,' you technically nagbigote for a few seconds.
usage_notes: Can mean both the state of having a mustache ('Siya ay nagbibigote') and the act of deciding to grow one ('Nagpasya siyang magbigote').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Balak kong **magbigote** para sa Movember.","translation":"I plan to **grow a mustache** for Movember."},{"sentence":"Hindi bagay sa kanya ang **magbigote**.","translation":"Having a **mustache** doesn't suit him."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging palakaibigan, mapagmahal, at malugod sa pakikitungo.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "pagka-" (estado ng pagiging) at "magiliw" (palakaibigan).
original_explanation: This is the default setting for Jollibee crew members. It’s that warm, fuzzy feeling you get from a tita who always gives you extra baon. The vibe of a golden retriever in human form. It's the opposite of "sungit" mode.
usage_notes: Isang positibong katangian na naglalarawan ng mainit at palakaibigang disposisyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala si Aling Nena sa kanyang **pagkamagiliw** sa lahat ng kanyang mga suki.","translation":"Aling Nena is known for her **friendliness** to all her regular customers."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paraan o akto ng pagbabawas o pag-aalis ng isang bahagi mula sa isang kabuuan, karaniwan ay tumutukoy sa pera o sahod.
original_explanation: That thing that happens to your sweldo before it even hits your bank account. SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, tax... that's *pagkakaltas*. It's the reason your gross pay and your net pay are in a very complicated relationship. It’s the "why is there so much month left at the end of the money?" feeling.
usage_notes: Most commonly used in the context of salary, payments, and finances.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang naging **pagkakaltas** sa sahod niya para sa buwis.","translation":"The **deduction** from his salary for taxes was large."},{"sentence":"Nagreklamo ang mga empleyado sa biglaang **pagkakaltas** sa kanilang benepisyo.","translation":"The employees complained about the sudden **deduction** from their benefits."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang magaspang, matigas, at nakatayong buhok o balahibo ng isang hayop.
original_explanation: Imagine the hair on a wild boar or the stiffest, most uncooperative strand of hair on your head that just won't be tamed. That's *balukag*. It's the kind of hair that stands on end when something is startled. Also, what your leg hair feels like when you haven't shaved in a while.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang balahibo ng hayop. Maaaring gamitin nang patalinghaga para sa magaspang na buhok ng tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtayuan ang **balukag** ng baboy-ramo nang may marinig itong kaluskos.","translation":"The wild boar's **bristles** stood on end when it heard a rustling sound."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang suklayin ang kanyang **balukag** na buhok.","translation":"He tried to comb his **bristly** hair."}]

translation: to be deafened; to become deaf
meaning_filipino: Mawalan ng pandinig, pansamantala man o permanente, dahil sa napakalakas na ingay o karamdaman.
original_explanation: What happens when your tita brings her karaoke machine to the family reunion and sings Whitney Houston at full blast. Or when you sit too close to the speakers at a concert. 'Bes, hinaan mo 'yan, baka mabingi ako!'
usage_notes: Can be used literally for hearing loss or hyperbolically for very loud noises.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halos **mabingi** ako sa lakas ng kulog kagabi.","translation":"I was almost **deafened** by how loud the thunder was last night."},{"sentence":"Ingatan mo ang iyong pandinig upang hindi ka **mabingi** sa pagtanda.","translation":"Take care of your hearing so you don't **become deaf** in old age."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng metal na may paikot na ukit o 'thread' at tulis na dulo, ginagamit upang pagkabitin o pagdikitin ang mga bagay sa pamamagitan ng pag-ikot nito.
original_explanation: The more high-tech cousin of the 'pako' (nail). You can't just hammer it in; you need a special tool (a 'disturnilyador' or screwdriver). It's what holds your IKEA furniture together, and also what you feel is loose in your head after a long week of adulting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng mas mahabang **turnilyo** para sa dingding na ito.","translation":"I need a longer **screw** for this wall."},{"sentence":"Lumuwag ang **turnilyo** ng upuan kaya umuuga ito.","translation":"The chair's **screw** loosened, that's why it's wobbly."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaghalong bunga, dahon ng ikmo, at apog na inihahanda para nguyain, na isang tradisyonal na gawain sa maraming kultura sa Asya.
original_explanation: The OG Filipino chewing gum. It’s that red-staining mix of areca nut and betel leaf that your lolo or lola might chew. It's a cultural stimulant that's been around way before energy drinks and espresso shots. The result? Red-stained teeth and a mild buzz.
usage_notes: The act of chewing it is 'pagnganga' or 'pagngangata'. The quid itself is the 'ngata'. The root 'ngata' can also mean 'to chew', which is where the verb 'ngatain' comes from.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghanda ng **ngata** ang matanda bago magkwento sa mga bata.","translation":"The old man prepared a **betel nut quid** before telling stories to the children."},{"sentence":"Pula ang kanyang mga ngipin dahil sa laging pagnguya ng **ngata**.","translation":"His teeth are red from always chewing **betel nut quid**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng isang masusing pag-aaral o pagsusuri upang alamin ang katotohanan o mga detalye ng isang bagay o pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is what your nanay does to your phone when she gets a hint you have a jowa. It's a full-blown investigation, more intense than the NBI. 'Magsiyasat na mabuti' is the level-up version, like when she cross-references your messages with your Facebook posts.
usage_notes: Often used in formal contexts like police investigations, academic research, or formal inquiries. The phrase 'magsiyasat na mabuti' emphasizes thoroughness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **magsiyasat** ang mga pulis upang matukoy ang tunay na salarin.","translation":"The police need to **investigate** to identify the real culprit."},{"sentence":"Pinayuhan siyang **magsiyasat** na mabuti bago pumasok sa isang kasunduan.","translation":"He was advised to **examine** thoroughly before entering an agreement."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis at hindi makontrol na paggalaw ng katawan dahil sa takot, lamig, sakit, o matinding emosyon.
original_explanation: That uncontrollable shaking when the aircon is set to 16°C, when you're about to do a big presentation, or when you see your crush walking towards you. It’s your body’s natural reaction to extreme cold, fear, or kilig.
usage_notes: Describes a physical reaction. Can be caused by cold, fear, excitement, or illness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi mapigilan ang kanyang **pangangatal** dahil sa matinding lamig.","translation":"His **shivering** could not be stopped due to the intense cold."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang **pangangatal** ng kanyang mga tuhod bago siya magsalita sa harap ng maraming tao.","translation":"She felt the **trembling** of her knees before she spoke in front of the crowd."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging mahinhin, malumanay, at banayad sa pagkilos, pananalita, at pag-uugali.
original_explanation: The Maria Clara vibe. Someone who speaks softly, moves gracefully, and probably doesn't rage-quit at video games. It's the opposite of your tita who shouts across the room to ask for the salt. Think less "scream" and more "soft-spoken whisper".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **mabinay** na ngiti ang kanyang isinukli sa akin.","translation":"She returned my gesture with a **gentle** smile."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa kanyang **mabinay** na pananalita.","translation":"She is known for her **mild-mannered** way of speaking."}]

meaning_filipino: Takpan ang butas o sira ng isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng paglalagay ng kapirasong materyal o tagpi.
original_explanation: This is a life skill for the 'wais' (street-smart). Got a hole in your favorite pambahay shorts? Don't throw it away, magtagpi ka! It's the act of covering a flaw, literally with a patch on your jeans, or figuratively, like when you try to patch up a weak excuse you just gave.
usage_notes: More specific than 'magkumpuni' (to repair). It specifically refers to using a patch to cover a hole or tear, usually in fabric or other surfaces.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natuto siyang **magtagpi** ng sarili niyang pantalon para makatipid.","translation":"He learned to **patch** his own pants to save money."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magtagpi** diyan sa butas sa bubong bago pa umulan.","translation":"You need to **patch** that hole in the roof before it rains."}]

translation: to entertain, to amuse, to distract
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aaliw o paglilibang sa sarili o sa iba upang maibsan ang pagkabagot o kalungkutan.
original_explanation: 'Libang' is what you do when your internet is down. You try to find something, *anything*, to keep yourself from going crazy. It's also what your friend does to you when you're going through a breakup—they try to **libang** you with K-dramas and milk tea so you forget about your ex for five minutes.
usage_notes: The root word itself is not often used alone; it's usually found in inflected forms like 'libangin', 'maglibang', 'nakalilibang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **libangin** ang sarili sa pamamagitan ng pagbabasa.","translation":"He tried to **amuse** himself by reading."},{"sentence":"Hayaan mong **libangin** kita para makalimutan mo ang iyong problema.","translation":"Let me **entertain** you so you can forget your problem."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng masusing paghahanap at paghahambing ng presyo, kalidad, o katangian ng mga produkto o serbisyo mula sa iba't ibang mapagkukunan bago bumili.
etymology: From pagka- + kambas, derived from English `canvass`.
original_explanation: The national sport of Filipino moms at the *palengke* or Divisoria. It's the art of asking "Magkano 'to?" at ten different stalls before buying from the first one. In the office, it's getting quotes from three suppliers. It’s the opposite of an impulse buy; it's a calculated, strategic mission to get the best deal.
usage_notes: Derived from the English word "canvass". Used in contexts of shopping, procurement, or surveying opinions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang tamang **pagkakambas** para makatipid sa gastusin.","translation":"Proper **canvassing** is important to save on expenses."},{"sentence":"Inatasan siyang magsagawa ng **pagkakambas** para sa mga materyales ng proyekto.","translation":"He was tasked to do the **canvassing** for the project materials."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pag-alis, paghihiwalay, o pag-aalis sa puwesto ng isang bagay o tao.
original_explanation: Pwedeng pagtanggal ng sapatos pag-uwi mo galing trabaho. Pwedeng pagtanggal ng ex mo sa friends list mo sa Facebook. O, sa mas malungkot na reality, pagtanggal sa trabaho. It's the act of un-friending, un-following, or un-employing. The opposite of 'add to cart' is 'remove from life'.
usage_notes: A very common and versatile word. Can be used for physical objects, digital items, or people from a position.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagtanggal** ng takip ay nangangailangan ng lakas.","translation":"The **removal** of the lid requires strength."},{"sentence":"Ikinalungkot niya ang **pagtanggal** sa kanya sa trabaho.","translation":"He was saddened by his **dismissal** from work."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tunog na nalilikha ng isang tao bilang pagpapahayag ng kagalakan, pagkasuklam, o iba pang damdamin, karaniwang kinasasangkutan ng mabilis at sunod-sunod na paghinga.
original_explanation: The sound you make when you see a hilarious meme, your friend trips over nothing, or you remember your crush actually replied to your DM. It's the best medicine, unless you're laughing alone in the dark, then it's just creepy. That's tawa.
usage_notes: Often combined with other words to specify the type of laugh (e.g., 'halakhak' for a loud laugh, 'ngisi' for a grin).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang malakas na **tawa** mula sa kabilang kwarto.","translation":"I heard loud **laughter** from the other room."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko mapigilan ang aking **tawa** sa kanyang biro.","translation":"I couldn't stop my **laugh** at his joke."}]

meaning_filipino: Sukatin ang bigat ng isang bagay gamit ang timbangan; Pag-aralan ang dalawang panig ng isang isyu o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: This is what you do at the palengke to make sure you're not getting ripped off on your kilo of tilapia. It's also what your mom does when she weighs the pros and cons of letting you go to that beach trip. 'Magtimbang ka muna ng desisyon mo, anak.'
usage_notes: Can be used literally for weighing objects or figuratively for weighing options or decisions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magtimbang** ng bigas para malaman kung sapat pa ito.","translation":"You need to **weigh** the rice to know if it's still enough."},{"sentence":"**Magtimbang** ka muna ng mga bagay-bagay bago ka magdesisyon.","translation":"**Weigh** things first before you make a decision."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang parirala na ginagamit upang humingi o magpakita ng kabuuang kasuotan ng isang tao, karaniwan sa social media. Maaari ring isulat na 'fitcheck'.
original_explanation: The modern-day runway walk, but for your phone camera. It's a command, a request, and a declaration: 'Show me what you're wearing!' Usually followed by a quick pan from shoes to shirt, showcasing the 'drip'. The official ritual before going out or posting an OOTD.
usage_notes: Extremely common on platforms like TikTok and Instagram. Can be written as 'fit check' or 'fitcheck'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Okay, guys, mabilis na **fit check** bago tayo umalis!","translation":"Okay, guys, quick **fit check** before we leave!"},{"sentence":"Nag-post siya ng **fit check** sa TikTok; ang ganda ng sapatos niya.","translation":"She posted a **fit check** on TikTok; her shoes are beautiful."}]

meaning_filipino: Sabay-sabay na uminom ng alak o anumang inumin, karaniwan sa isang pagtitipon.
original_explanation: The official verb for 'Tara, shot puno!' It's when the barkada gathers, the Red Horse or Emperador comes out, and everyone takes turns drinking from the same glass (the 'tagay' system). It's a sacred ritual of Filipino bonding and questionable life choices.
usage_notes: A very common term in the context of social drinking. The root 'tungga' means to gulp or drink in one go.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkayayaan ang magkakaibigan na **magtunggaan** pagkatapos ng trabaho.","translation":"The friends decided to **have a drinking session** after work."},{"sentence":"Huwag kayong **magtunggaan** hanggang madaling-araw, may pasok pa bukas.","translation":"Don't **drink together** until dawn, there's still work tomorrow."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagdaragdag ng likido, karaniwang tubig, upang bawasan ang tapang o konsentrasyon ng isang substansiya.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your free "iced tea" at a carinderia that's been sitting out all day. The ice melts, and boom, instant pagbabanto. It's the culinary equivalent of "stretching the budget," turning a strong coffee into just brown water.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of drinks, chemicals, or even figuratively for ideas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagbabanto** ng gasgas sa alak ay isang paraan upang makatipid ang mga tindahan.","translation":"The **dilution** of cheap liquor is a way for stores to save money."},{"sentence":"Inireklamo ng mga mamimili ang **pagbabanto** sa nabili nilang toyo.","translation":"The customers complained about the **dilution** of the soy sauce they bought."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar na nagsisilbing pansamantalang tirahan o tulugan, tulad ng isang otel, bahay-panuluyan, o inn.
etymology: Nagmula sa salitang-ugat na "tuloy" (to enter, to stay). Ang kabilaang panlaping "pa- ... -an" ay nagpapahiwatig ng isang lugar kung saan isinasagawa ang kilos.
original_explanation: Parang Airbnb o transient house. Yung lugar na tinutuluyan mo kapag nag-out-of-town ka with friends. O kaya yung bahay ng tita mo na nagiging **patuluyan** ng buong angkan tuwing Pasko. It's your official crash pad.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa isang lugar para sa pansamantalang paninirahan, hindi permanenteng tirahan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghahanap kami ng murang **patuluyan** sa Baguio.","translation":"We are looking for cheap **lodging** in Baguio."},{"sentence":"Nagsilbing **patuluyan** ng mga biktima ng baha ang evacuation center.","translation":"The evacuation center served as **temporary residence** for the flood victims."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng hangin mula sa timog-kanluran na karaniwang nagdadala ng malalakas na ulan sa Pilipinas, lalo na sa mga buwan ng Hunyo hanggang Oktubre.
original_explanation: The official sponsor of cancelled classes, epic floods, and "work-from-home" days in the Philippines. When PAGASA says "Habagat is here," you know it's time to stock up on instant noodles, charge your power banks, and prepare your "baha-couture" (aka shorts and tsinelas). It's the rainy season's main character.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang terminong meteorolohikal na kilala ng karamihan sa Pilipinas. Ang katapat nito ay 'amihan' (northeast monsoon).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagdeklara ng suspensiyon ng klase dahil sa malakas na ulan na dala ng **habagat**.","translation":"Classes were suspended due to the heavy rains brought by the **southwest monsoon**."},{"sentence":"Tumaas ang tubig sa ilog nang manalasa ang **habagat**.","translation":"The river water rose when the **southwest monsoon** hit."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang larawan, plano, o disenyo na nilikha sa pamamagitan ng pagguhit.
original_explanation: The blueprint, the sketch, the master plan. It's the first draft of a masterpiece or a building. In life, your "dibuho" is your game plan, the grand scheme you have for your career, love life, or how to get the last piece of lechon at a party.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinakita ng arkitekto ang **dibuho** ng ipapatayong gusali.","translation":"The architect showed the **design** of the building to be constructed."},{"sentence":"Isang simpleng **dibuho** lang ang kailangan ko para sa proyekto.","translation":"I just need a simple **sketch** for the project."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-unat ng leeg at pag-angat ng mukha upang masilayan ang isang bagay na may kahirapang makita dahil sa harang o layo.
original_explanation: What everyone does at a concert when they're in the Gen Ad section trying to see the artist. It's also the move you make in a crowded LRT trying to see which station is next. Short people problems.
usage_notes: A very specific term for stretching one's neck to get a better view, often in a crowd or over an obstacle. It is not commonly used in modern conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa dami ng tao, **pagdunghal** na lang ang nagawa niya para makita ang prusisyon.","translation":"With so many people, **craning his neck** was the only thing he could do to see the procession."},{"sentence":"Isang **pagdunghal** sa pader ang ginawa ng bata upang makita ang laro sa kabilang bakod.","translation":"The child did a **craning of the neck** over the wall to see the game on the other side of the fence."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paggamit ng matematika o lohika upang matukoy ang isang halaga, bilang, o resulta; pagtutuos.
original_explanation: What you do when you get your paycheck to see if you can afford both your bills and that 12.12 shopping cart. It's mentally computing if you have enough money for a fancy coffee or if you're stuck with 3-in-1 for the rest of the kinsenas. Can also be used for calculating risks, like, 'Kinalkula ko kung aabot pa ba ako sa office kapag dumaan ako ng EDSA ng 8 AM.' (Spoiler: you won't).
usage_notes: A direct loanword adaptation. 'Nagkalkula' is also a common form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **kumalkula** kung magkano ang lahat ng kanyang gastos ngayong buwan.","translation":"He tried to **calculate** how much all his expenses were this month."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **kumalkula** ng tamang badyet para sa isang malaking proyekto.","translation":"It's difficult to **calculate** the right budget for a big project."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-umbok o pamamaga ng balat, karaniwan dahil sa kagat ng insekto, sakit, o pagkakabugbog.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your face after a breakup crying session, or to your skin after you lose a fight with a lamok (mosquito). It's the body's natural way of saying 'aray ko po.'
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'mamaga'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **mamuga** ang kanyang braso matapos siyang kagatin ng bubuyog.","translation":"His arm started **to swell** after he was stung by a bee."},{"sentence":"Ayokong **mamuga** ang mata ko bukas kaya titigilan ko na ang pag-iyak.","translation":"I don't want my eyes **to be swollen** tomorrow so I will stop crying."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng marahas na paghila sa buhok ng isang tao, karaniwan ay dahil sa galit o sa gitna ng isang away.
original_explanation: The iconic move in every Pinoy teleserye catfight. It's the ultimate escalation, the point of no return in an argument. If words are bullets, 'pagsabunot' is going nuclear. Also, what you feel like doing to yourself when your internet connection dies during a crucial online meeting.
usage_notes: Almost always associated with a physical fight.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nauwi sa **pagsabunot** ang mainit na pagtatalo ng dalawang babae.","translation":"The heated argument between the two women ended in **hair-pulling**."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng mga guwardiya na awatin ang **pagsabunot** sa loob ng bar.","translation":"The guards tried to stop the **hair-pulling** inside the bar."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang unang pagliwanag sa silangan bago ang pagsikat ng araw; bukang-liwayway.
original_explanation: The time of day when roosters and BPO agents are at their most active. For some, it's the start of a new day. For others, it's finally time to go to sleep after a long night of work, gaming, or overthinking. It's more poetic than 'madaling araw'.
usage_notes: A more literary or formal term for dawn. 'Bukang-liwayway' is a more common native equivalent.
