usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula silang maglakad bago pa sumapit ang **alba**.","translation":"They started walking before **dawn** arrived."},{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng kulay ng langit pagsapit ng **alba**.","translation":"The color of the sky is beautiful at **daybreak**."}]

meaning_filipino: Kumuha at mag-imbak ng tunog, imahe, o datos sa isang midyum tulad ng tape, disk, o digital file.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa mo sa phone mo kapag may away sa kalye para may pang-post sa social media. Or 'yung utos sa'yo ng boss mo sa Zoom meeting: "Can someone please irekord this session?" From audio recordings to CCTV footage, this is the verb.
usage_notes: Can also mean 'to write down' or 'to make a note of', similar to 'itala'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **irekord** mo ang ating pag-uusap para may ebidensya tayo.","translation":"Please, **record** our conversation so we have evidence."},{"sentence":"Gusto niyang **irekord** ang sarili niyang kanta sa isang studio.","translation":"He wants to **record** his own song in a studio."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian o ugali ng pagiging mandaraya o mapanlinlang.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "pagka-" (estado ng pagiging) at "magdaraya" (isang taong nanloloko).
original_explanation: It's that "skill" your classmate has during exams, or your friend who peeks at your cards during a game of Tong-its. On a serious note, it's the quality of that person who promises to pay you back "next week" for the last six months. A major red flag in any 'ship.
usage_notes: Ito ay naglalarawan sa katangian ng isang tao na mahilig manlamang o manloko.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging dahilan ng kanilang paghihiwalay ang **pagkamagdaraya** ng kanyang kasintahan.","translation":"The **deceitfulness** of her partner was the reason for their breakup."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manipis at parisukat o parihabang piraso ng matigas na materyal tulad ng seramika, bato, o vinyl na ginagamit na pantakip sa sahig.
original_explanation: Ito yung tiles sa sahig ng bahay niyo. Specifically, 'yung luma, makintab, at malamig sa paa na parang sa bahay ng lola mo. Yung tipong kapag bagong lampaso, dulas-dulas pa. Hindi 'yung mga modernong 'porcelain' o 'granite' tiles, ito 'yung classic, Vigan-style floor tile.
usage_notes: Often refers to older, traditional types of floor tiles like Machuca tiles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinakintab niya ang mga lumang **baldosin** sa sahig.","translation":"He polished the old **floor tiles**."},{"sentence":"Maganda pa rin ang disenyo ng **baldosin** sa lumang bahay na iyon.","translation":"The design of the **floor tiles** in that old house is still beautiful."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na propesyonal o bihasang tumugtog ng piyano.
original_explanation: The person with magic fingers who can make a piano sing. Sila 'yung laging bida sa school programs o sa mga hotel lobby. Every Filipino family dreams of having a piyanista in the house, a sign of being "cultured" and "sosyal". They are the masters of the black and white keys.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang tanyag na **piyanista** ang nagtanghal sa Cultural Center of the Philippines.","translation":"A famous **pianist** performed at the Cultural Center of the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Nagsasanay siya araw-araw upang maging isang mahusay na **piyanista**.","translation":"She practices every day to become a great **pianist**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggalaw pataas o pababa sa nilalaman ng isang digital na screen upang tingnan ang impormasyon na hindi kasya sa isang display.
original_explanation: The mindless thumb exercise you do on your phone at 2 AM, hoping to find the end of the internet. It's how you consume an infinite buffet of memes, chismis, and bad news without actually moving. The modern-day 'doomscrolling' is its final form.
usage_notes: Filipinized verb forms are common, such as 'nag-scroll' (scrolled), 'nag-i-scroll' (scrolling), and 'mag-scroll' (to scroll).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinto na sa pag-**scroll** sa gabi para makatulog ka nang maaga.","translation":"Stop **scrolling** at night so you can sleep early."},{"sentence":"Mag-**scroll** ka lang pababa at makikita mo ang pangalan mo sa listahan.","translation":"Just **scroll** down and you will see your name on the list."}]

meaning_filipino: Mabilis na pag-ikot o pagdaloy ng hangin, tubig, o alabok na bumubuo ng hugis pabilog; maaaring tumukoy din sa matinding damdamin.
original_explanation: This is the feeling in your chest when you see your ex with someone new. Or the chaos in Divisoria during the Christmas rush. It's a swirling mess, whether it's dust, water, or your complicated feelings.
usage_notes: Often used poetically or figuratively to describe turbulent emotions like anger, jealousy, or passion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **umalipuyo** ang alikabok nang dumaan ang malakas na hangin.","translation":"The dust began **to swirl** when the strong wind passed."},{"sentence":"Sa kanyang dibdib ay tila may **umalipuyo** na galit at selos.","translation":"In his chest, anger and jealousy seemed **to whirl**."}]

translation: to get involved; to be implicated
meaning_filipino: Ang maging bahagi o madawit sa isang pangyayari, usapin, o problema, kadalasan nang hindi sinasadya.
original_explanation: The Tagalog equivalent of 'getting dragged into the drama.' It's when your friend has a fight with their jowa and suddenly you're the unwilling mediator. Or when a chismis starts and your name gets mentioned. 'Ayokong makasangkot sa gulo nila.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingatan mo ang iyong mga sinasabi para hindi ka **makasangkot** sa anumang isyu.","translation":"Be careful with what you say so you don't **get involved** in any issue."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya inasahan na **makakasangkot** siya sa imbestigasyon.","translation":"He didn't expect that he would **be implicated** in the investigation."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng mamamayan o katutubo ng bansang Ehipto.
original_explanation: The female version of an Egyptian. Think Cleopatra. If you meet a woman from Cairo, she's an Ehipsiya.
usage_notes: Ginagamit para tukuyin ang kasariang pambabae. Laging nagsisimula sa malaking titik bilang demonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Cleopatra VII ay isang tanyag na **Ehipsiya** na naging huling Paraon.","translation":"Cleopatra VII was a famous **Egyptian (female)** who became the last Pharaoh."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marahan at maindayog na paggalaw, tulad ng pag-ugoy o pag-indayog.
original_explanation: Imagine a drunk person trying to walk a straight line, but gracefully. Or the movement of a chandelier in a mild earthquake. It's the gentle swing of a hammock on a lazy afternoon, or the way a dancer moves their hips to a slow beat.
usage_notes: Describes a gentle, rhythmic, back-and-forth or side-to-side movement.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pag-undayon** ng mga puno ay senyales ng malakas na hangin.","translation":"The **swaying** of the trees is a sign of strong winds."},{"sentence":"Naaliw ako sa **pag-undayon** ng duyan.","translation":"I was amused by the **swinging** of the hammock."}]

meaning_filipino: Sabihin ang isang bagay sa mahinang tinig, karaniwan ay malapit sa tainga ng kausap, upang hindi marinig ng iba.
original_explanation: The official verb of chismis. "Psst, may ibubulong ako sa'yo." This is how secrets, gossip, and sweet nothings are transmitted. It's the low-volume, high-impact communication method used by your marites friends and romantic partners alike.
usage_notes: Focuses on the information being whispered. The object of the verb is the thing being said. Compare with 'bulungan' (to whisper *to someone*).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May mahalaga siyang **ibinulong** sa akin bago siya umalis.","translation":"He **whispered** something important to me before he left."},{"sentence":"**Ibulong** mo na lang sa akin ang sagot kung alam mo.","translation":"Just **whisper** the answer to me if you know it."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagwawasak, paglansag, o pagpapawalang-bisa sa isang samahan, kasunduan, o istruktura.
original_explanation: The official term for a group project that just got cancelled, or a loveteam that has officially broken up. It's the end of an era, the 'game over' for a partnership. Pwede ring mangyari sa kasal. Ouch.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **buwag** ng kanilang banda ay ikinalungkot ng maraming tagahanga.","translation":"The **dissolution** of their band saddened many fans."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng binti na nag-uugnay sa paa at sa mas mababang bahagi ng hita; ang kasu-kasuan sa pagitan ng paa at binti.
original_explanation: That bony part of your leg that swells up like a 'pan de sal' when you sprain it playing basketball. It's also where you'd wear an anklet to feel ~aesthetic~. Not to be confused with sakong (heel).
usage_notes: A specific body part. The more common term is 'bukung-bukong'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Namaga ang kanyang **buol** matapos siyang matapilok.","translation":"His **ankle** swelled after he stumbled."},{"sentence":"Hanggang **buol** lamang ang lalim ng tubig sa pampang.","translation":"The water on the shore is only **ankle**-deep."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kusang-loob na nag-alok ng sarili para sa isang gawain; o isang bagay na iniharap o ipinakita.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na ikaw yung 'chosen one' para sa isang task na ayaw gawin ng iba. 'Sino'ng mag-o-overtime?' Tapos bigla kang tinuro ng boss mo. You've been prisintado! Pwede ring ikaw mismo ang nag-volunteer, parang 'Ako na po, Ma'am/Sir!' para plus points.
usage_notes: Can be used to mean something was presented ('iprisinta') or someone volunteered ('nagprisinta'). The form 'prisintado' is often used as an adjective describing the person who volunteered.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay laging **prisintado** sa mga gawaing-bahay.","translation":"He always **volunteers** for household chores."},{"sentence":"Nag**prisintado** si Juan na maghugas ng mga plato.","translation":"Juan **volunteered** to wash the dishes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pag-ulan na may matinding dalas at dami ng tubig, na kadalasang nagiging sanhi ng pagbaha.
original_explanation: The other half of PAGASA's greatest hits. 'Malakas na ulan' is the universe telling you to cancel all your plans and just stay home. It's the cause of 'baha,' the reason your Grab fare triples, and the perfect excuse to make instant noodles and watch Netflix. The official start of cuddle weather.
usage_notes: Standard phrase for heavy rainfall. Often used in weather reports and daily conversation about the weather.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang umalis, may **malakas na ulan** sa labas.","translation":"Don't leave anymore, there's **heavy rain** outside."},{"sentence":"Ang **malakas na ulan** ay nagdulot ng baha sa maraming lugar sa Metro Manila.","translation":"The **heavy rain** caused floods in many areas in Metro Manila."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto o proseso ng pagkuha muli; pagpapanumbalik o pagbabalik sa dating kalagayan.
original_explanation: This is the 'what' to the verb's 'how'. When your friend loses badly in Mobile Legends and says "Kailangan ko ng bawi!", he's not just saying he needs to *do* the recovering, he's talking about the *act* of recovery itself—the sweet, sweet revenge match. It's the noun form of redemption.
usage_notes: Refers to the act or result of recovering something, often used in contexts of games, competitions, or making amends.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis ang **bawi** niya sa puhunan.","translation":"His **recovery** of the investment was quick."},{"sentence":"Walang **bawi** sa mga regalong naibigay na.","translation":"There are no **take-backs** for gifts that have already been given."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangnagdaang anyo ng pandiwa na tumutukoy sa pagkilos ng paggamit ng mata upang mapansin ang isang tao o bagay; natagpuan.
original_explanation: That "OMG" moment when you finally find your keys. Or that "Oh no" moment when you realize your boss **saw** you scrolling through Shopee. It's the past tense of a visual event. "Nakita ko ang ex mo na may kasamang iba." The ultimate Marites starter pack.
usage_notes: Past tense of 'makita'. Can mean "saw", "was seen", or "found" depending on sentence structure.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakita** ko siya sa palengke kaninang umaga.","translation":"I **saw** her at the market this morning."},{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **nakita** rin ang nawawalang pitaka.","translation":"Finally, the missing wallet **was found**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagpapatalas sa isang bagay, tulad ng kutsilyo o lapis. Sa makabagong gamit, tumutukoy rin ito sa pagtataya o ebalwasyon ng kaalaman o kasanayan.
etymology: From `pag-` (verbal noun prefix) + `tasa` (to sharpen). The meaning 'assessment' is a modern semantic extension, likening evaluation to the honing of skills or knowledge.
original_explanation: This word has two lives. On one hand, it's the old-school `pagtasa` ng itak bago ka mag-ani sa bukid. On the other hand, it’s the very modern, DepEd-style `pagtasa` (assessment) of your skills. So whether you're sharpening a pencil for an exam or taking the exam itself, you're dealing with `pagtasa`. One sharpens a blade, the other sharpens the mind (or gives you a headache).
usage_notes: The meaning depends heavily on context, distinguishing between the physical act of sharpening and the abstract act of evaluation. The latter is common in education and corporate settings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng **pagtasa** ang mga kutsilyo sa kusina.","translation":"The kitchen knives need **sharpening**."},{"sentence":"Ang National Achievement Test ay isang paraan ng **pagtasa** sa mga mag-aaral.","translation":"The National Achievement Test is a method of **assessment** for students."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang elementong kemikal na may simbolong 'Lu' at atomikong bilang na 71. Ito ay isang pilak-puting metal na bihirang matagpuan sa kalikasan.
original_explanation: This is that one element in the periodic table you probably forgot existed. It's the last of the lanthanide series, the introverted cousin of the more famous elements like Gold and Oxygen. You'll only ever hear this in a chemistry class or if you're a hardcore science nerd. Basically, it's the 'seen-zoned' element of the periodic table.
usage_notes: A scientific term. The spelling is based on Filipino orthography for the chemical element.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **Lutesyum** ay ginagamit sa ilang mga espesyal na uri ng metal alloys.","translation":"**Lutetium** is used in some special types of metal alloys."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan, karaniwang gawa sa plastik, kahoy, o metal, na may hugis ng balikat ng tao, na ginagamit sa pagsasabit ng damit.
original_explanation: The thing you have a million of but can never find when you need one. The primary weapon of choice for an angry Filipino mom. Also, the unsung hero that keeps your 'pang-alis' clothes from getting crumpled.
usage_notes: While "sabitan ng damit" is the formal term, "hanger" is used universally in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakikuha ng **hanger** sa aparador para sa bagong damit ko.","translation":"Please get a **hanger** from the closet for my new dress."},{"sentence":"Naubusan na kami ng **hanger** dahil sa dami ng labada.","translation":"We ran out of **hangers** because of so much laundry."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o paghiling sa isang tao na isara ang isang bagay, tulad ng pinto, bintana, o tindahan.
original_explanation: This is the command form. When you're comfy in bed and you see the door is open, you yell to your younger sibling, "Hoy, pasarahan mo nga yung pinto!" It's the ultimate 'tamad' or 'boss mode' command.
usage_notes: This is a causative command, asking someone else to perform the action of closing. It is different from `pasarhan` (/pa-SAR-han/) due to stress and meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pasarahan** mo na ang tindahan at gabi na.","translation":"**Have** the store **closed** now, it's already night."},{"sentence":"Maaari mo bang **pasarahan** ang bintana? Lumalamig na.","translation":"Can you please **have** the window **closed**? It's getting cold."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-inom ng alak o anumang inuming nakalalasing, karaniwan sa isang pagtitipon.
etymology: From the root word 'barik', which means to drink liquor.
original_explanation: The official verb of 'Tara, shot puno!' It's what happens when the stress of adulting hits and someone brings out the Emperador or Soju. The act of turning your liver into a battleground for fun and questionable decisions.
usage_notes: Often used in informal or colloquial settings. It's the action verb for 'inuman' (drinking session).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing Biyernes, mahilig **bumarik** ang magkakaibigan pagkatapos ng trabaho.","translation":"Every Friday, the friends like **to drink alcohol** after work."},{"sentence":"\"Huwag ka nang **bumarik** mamaya, may pasok ka pa bukas,\" paalala ng nanay.","translation":"\"Don't **go drinking** later, you still have work tomorrow,\" his mother reminded."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga alituntunin, kayarian, o anumang aspekto na may kaugnayan sa balarila o wastong paggamit ng wika.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "pan-" at salitang ugat na "balarila" (grammar). Ang /n/ sa "pan-" ay nagiging /m/ dahil sa kasunod na tunog na /b/.
original_explanation: Anything related to grammar. 'Kamaliang pambalarila' is a grammatical error—the kind your strict Filipino teacher would circle with a red pen. It's the reason you have to know your 'ng' from your 'nang'. It’s the rulebook for speaking and writing 'properly'.
usage_notes: Isang pormal at akademikong termino na may kaugnayan sa linggwistika at pag-aaral ng wikang Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marami pa ring mga isyung **pambalarila** ang pinagtatalunan ng mga dalubwika.","translation":"There are still many **grammatical** issues being debated by linguists."},{"sentence":"Ang aklat na ito ay tumatalakay sa mga tuntuning **pambalarila** ng Filipino.","translation":"This book discusses the **grammatical** rules of Filipino."}]

translation: a swarm; a mob; a throng
meaning_filipino: Isang malaking pangkat ng mga tao o hayop na sabay-sabay at magulong kumikilos patungo sa isang direksyon.
original_explanation: Picture mo 'yung 12.12 sale sa mall, o kaya 'yung BTS concert ticket selling. 'Yun ang dalumog! 'Yung dagsaan ng tao na parang may free-for-all. Parang langgam sa asukal.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a chaotic or disorderly crowd. The verb form is 'dumalumog'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **dalumog** ng mga mamimili ang sumugod sa mall para sa midnight sale.","translation":"A **throng** of shoppers rushed into the mall for the midnight sale."},{"sentence":"Naiwasan niya ang **dalumog** ng mga tagahanga sa labas ng istadyum.","translation":"He avoided the **mob** of fans outside the stadium."}]

translation: manner of foundation; the way something was established
meaning_filipino: Ang paraan o proseso ng pagtatayo o pagbuo ng isang organisasyon, institusyon, o samahan.
original_explanation: This is the 'origin story' of a group. Think of the founding of your high school barkada, the establishment of a new BPO company in the province, or how the local government was formed. It's about how something was built from the ground up. If you add 'na muli', it's the 're-founding' or 're-establishment', like when your favorite milk tea shop re-opens after a renovation.
usage_notes: The prefix 'pagkaka-' here describes the manner or way something was done. The phrase 'pagkakatatag na muli' means 're-establishment'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagdiriwang nila ang ika-50 anibersaryo ng **pagkakatatag** ng kanilang kumpanya.","translation":"They are celebrating the 50th anniversary of their company's **foundation**."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkakatatag** na muli ng samahan ay nagbigay ng bagong pag-asa sa mga miyembro.","translation":"The re-**establishment** of the organization gave new hope to its members."}]

translation: to shake something vigorously; to brandish
meaning_filipino: Igalaw-galaw nang mabilis at malakas ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay hawak sa kamay; ikampay o iwinagayway.
original_explanation: That thing you do with a wet towel before snapping it. Or how a majorette iwagawag her baton during a parade. It’s a more forceful, almost aggressive shake compared to a simple 'wagayway' (wave). Think of shaking a dusty rug with a vengeance.
usage_notes: Implies a stronger, more energetic shaking motion than `iwagwag` or `iwinagayway`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **iwagawag** ang bote, baka sumabog ang laman.","translation":"Don't **shake** the bottle **vigorously**, its contents might explode."},{"sentence":"Nagalit ang guro at **iniwagawag** ang patpat sa hangin.","translation":"The teacher got angry and **brandished** the stick in the air."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pares ng sako o bag na isinasabit sa likod ng isang hayop na pasan, tulad ng kabayo o kalabaw, upang paglagyan ng mga kargamento.
original_explanation: Basically, the OG GrabFood bag for your kabayo. Before Lalamove motorcycles, this was how you transported your paninda or kagamitan across towns. It's a pair of bags draped over a horse or carabao. You'll probably only hear this word from your lolo telling stories about 'noong unang panahon' or see it in a historical movie.
usage_notes: Isang salitang napakadalang nang gamitin sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap at maituturing na halos lipas na.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inilagay ng magsasaka ang kanyang mga ani sa **alporhas** ng kalabaw.","translation":"The farmer placed his harvest in the carabao's **saddlebag**."},{"sentence":"Puno ng mga paninda ang **alporhas** ng mangangalakal na naglalakbay.","translation":"The traveling merchant's **saddlebags** were full of goods."}]

translation: to be the cause of hardship/poverty
meaning_filipino: Maging sanhi ng pagdanas ng hirap, paghihikahos, o kahirapan sa buhay.
original_explanation: This is the 'petsa de peligro' life before payday. It's the investment scam that promises you'll get rich quick but does the opposite. It's the reason you're eating instant noodles for the fifth day in a row.
usage_notes: Points to the root cause of poverty, difficulty, or suffering.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang katamaran ay maaaring **ikahirap** ng isang tao.","translation":"Laziness can **be the cause of a person's hardship**."},{"sentence":"Maraming desisyon ang gobyerno na **ikinahirap** ng mga mamamayan.","translation":"Many government decisions **caused hardship** for the citizens."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang sangkap, tulad ng asin, paminta, o mga yerba, na idinadagdag sa pagkain upang mapahusay o magbigay ng partikular na lasa.
original_explanation: The magic dust that turns boring food into something edible. For Filipinos, this isn't just salt and pepper. It's a whole arsenal: toyo, suka, patis, bawang, sibuyas, and the all-powerful Magic Sarap. The 'secret ingredient' your lola won't tell you about.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kulang sa **pampalasa** ang adobo; dagdagan mo ng toyo at suka.","translation":"The adobo lacks **seasoning**; add more soy sauce and vinegar."},{"sentence":"Ang bawang ay isang mahalagang **pampalasa** sa lutuing Pilipino.","translation":"Garlic is an important **seasoning** in Filipino cuisine."}]

meaning_filipino: Kaagad; walang pagkaantala o pagtigil; tuloy-tuloy.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung utos ng nanay mo na, "Linisin mo 'yang kwarto mo, segida!" Ibig sabihin, ngayon na, 'wag nang mag-cellphone muna. It's the Pinoy version of "pronto" or "ASAP." Walang bukas-bukas, walang mamaya na.
usage_notes: Madalas marinig sa mga probinsya at sa mga nakatatanda. Medyo pormal o luma na ang dating sa ilang urban na lugar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nang marinig ang balita, **segida** siyang umuwi ng probinsya.","translation":"Upon hearing the news, he **immediately** went home to the province."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng makapal na papel na may nakasulat na mensahe; maaari ding tumukoy sa baraha.
original_explanation: Before DMs, Messenger, and email, there was the 'karta'. It's the OG way of telling someone 'I miss you' or 'Utang mo, bayaran mo na'. Also refers to playing cards, the source of many family arguments during reunions.
usage_notes: Can mean a formal letter ('liham'), a playing card ('baraha'), or even a menu ('karta ng pagkain').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatanggap siya ng **karta** mula sa kanyang kasintahan sa ibang bansa.","translation":"She received a **letter** from her sweetheart abroad."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mandaraya sa laro natin ng **karta**.","translation":"Don't cheat in our game of **cards**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng tela o papel na ginagamit sa pagpapatuyo o paglilinis sa pamamagitan ng pagpunas.
original_explanation: Your trusty sidekick after a shower, a swim, or when you accidentally spill your milk tea. It's the thing you use to wipe away your tears after a sad K-drama episode or your sweat after climbing the MRT stairs.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'tuwalya' (from Spanish 'toalla'). 'Pamunasan' is more native-sounding but 'tuwalya' is more common in everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha ka ng **pamunasan** at patuyuin mo ang iyong buhok.","translation":"Get a **towel** and dry your hair."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang **pamunasan** sa mesa para linisin ang natapong kape.","translation":"He used the cloth **towel** to clean the spilled coffee."}]

translation: to sell by retail; to sell in small portions
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbebenta ng mga produkto sa maliliit na bahagi o paunti-unti sa halip na bultuhan.
original_explanation: The business model of every sari-sari store in the Philippines. You don't buy a whole shampoo bottle, you buy a sachet. You don't buy a pack of cigarettes, you buy one stick. The store owner is asked to **ipagtingi** the goods. It's the art of breaking down the whole into affordable little pieces.
usage_notes: This verb is central to the concept of 'tingi-tingi' or retail culture in the Philippines. The focus is on the item being sold.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit anong paninda ay kaya niyang **ipagtingi** para lang kumita.","translation":"She can **sell any merchandise by retail** just to earn money."},{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **ipagtingi** mo na itong bawang para maubos na.","translation":"Please, just **sell this garlic by the piece** so we can get rid of it."}]

translation: regression, state of being made to retreat
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging sapilitang napaatras o napaalis mula sa isang posisyon.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you confidently answer a question in class, but the teacher says, "Are you sure?" and you immediately doubt yourself. It's the feeling of your progress getting a hard reset, like when your internet dies mid-download and you have to start over. It's a forced step back.
usage_notes: Often implies an external force causing the retreat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang biglaang **pagkakapaurong** ng mga sundalo ay ikinagulat ng lahat.","translation":"The sudden **state of being made to retreat** by the soldiers surprised everyone."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa takot, kitang-kita ang **pagkakapaurong** niya mula sa away.","translation":"Because of fear, his **regression** from the fight was very evident."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paglalarawan na tumutukoy sa pagiging magkakatulad ng lahat ng miyembro sa isang pangkat, grupo, o kalipunan.
original_explanation: When you ask your lola what she wants for Christmas and she says 'Kayo na ang bahala,' so you and your cousins all end up buying her the same floral duster. Also the foundation of the classic hugot line, 'Pare-pareho lang kayong mga lalaki!'
usage_notes: Ito ay ang plural o distributive form ng 'pareho', na nagbibigay-diin na ang bawat isa sa isang grupo ay magkakatulad.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pare-pareho** ang suot naming uniporme sa opisina.","translation":"We wear uniforms at the office that are **all the same**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong isipin na **pare-pareho** ang lahat ng tao.","translation":"Don't think that all people are **all alike**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tanyag na pagkaing Pilipino na karaniwang gawa sa tinadtad na parte ng ulo at atay ng baboy, at tinimplahan ng calamansi, sibuyas, at sili.
etymology: From Kapampangan "sisig," which originally meant "to snack on something sour." The modern sizzling dish is credited to Lucia Cunanan ("Aling Lucing") of Angeles City, Pampanga.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'putok-batok' pulutan. It's that sizzling plate of chopped pork parts that arrives at your table screaming 'extra rice, please!' and 'one more beer!'. It's the reason your diet failed last weekend.
usage_notes: While traditionally made of pork, there are now many popular variations like chicken, tofu, squid, and bangus (milkfish) sisig.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong order-in ang mainit na **sisig** na may itlog sa ibabaw.","translation":"My favorite thing to order is hot **sisig** with an egg on top."},{"sentence":"Tara, mag-**sisig** tayo mamaya pagkatapos ng trabaho.","translation":"Come on, let's have **sisig** later after work."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng isang biro o panunukso sa isang tao.
original_explanation: To 'tudyuhin' someone is to launch a friendly 'asar' attack. It's what you do when your friend gets a new haircut ('anong nangyari sa buhok mo, bes?'), or when your sibling is obviously texting their crush. It's the verbal equivalent of a playful nudge.
usage_notes: This is the verb form, indicating the action of teasing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang **tudyuhin** ang kapatid mo, baka mapikon na 'yan.","translation":"Don't **tease** your sibling anymore, they might get annoyed."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **tudyuhin** ako tungkol sa dati kong kasintahan.","translation":"He likes **to tease** me about my ex-boyfriend."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon at pagpapakita ng damdamin ng sama ng loob, hinanakit, o galit dahil sa isang kasalanan o pagkukulang na ginawa ng iba.
original_explanation: The official term for 'silent treatment'. It's when you reply 'K.' to long messages. It's the emotional baggage you carry that's heavier than your check-in luggage. The opposite of 'letting go'.
usage_notes: A very specific and somewhat rare noun form derived from 'hinanakit' (resentment). More common phrasing is 'pagkakaroon ng hinanakit'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi maganda ang laging **paghinanaktan** sa kapwa.","translation":"Constantly **feeling resentment** towards others is not good."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging mabilis o matulin sa pagkilos; tulin o bilis.
original_explanation: This is the scientific, slightly more formal cousin of 'bilis'. It's what you use to talk about the speed of your internet connection, the velocity of a moving car, or how quickly chismis spreads in the office. It's the noun form of 'mabilis'.
usage_notes: Less common in everyday conversation than 'bilis', but used in more formal or technical contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinusukat ng mga pulis ang **kabilisan** ng mga sasakyan sa highway.","translation":"The police are measuring the **speed** of vehicles on the highway."},{"sentence":"Humanga ako sa **kabilisan** ng kanyang pag-iisip.","translation":"I was amazed by the **swiftness** of his thinking."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng palitan ng kaalaman, mensahe, o impormasyon sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang tao o pangkat.
original_explanation: This is the formal term for "chismisan" but for a good cause. It's the two-way street of communication, not just a one-way "seen-zone." Think of a group chat that's actually productive, or a BPO team huddle where everyone actually listens and gives updates. It’s about making sure everyone is on the same page.
usage_notes: This is a more formal term than `komunikasyon` or `usapan`. It emphasizes the mutual aspect of sharing knowledge.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang malinaw na **pagpabatiran** sa pagitan ng pamahalaan at ng mamamayan.","translation":"Clear **mutual communication** between the government and the citizens is important."},{"sentence":"Ang epektibong **pagpabatiran** ay susi sa tagumpay ng anumang proyekto.","translation":"Effective **exchange of information** is the key to the success of any project."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpulupot ng mga braso sa isang tao o bagay bilang pagpapahayag ng pagmamahal, pag-aliw, o pagbati.
original_explanation: The universal cure for a bad day, a failed exam, or when your 'situationship' ends. It’s cheaper than therapy and more effective than a motivational quote. A tight 'akap' can sometimes feel like coming home.
usage_notes: Often used with 'mahigpit na akap' (tight hug). It's a very common term of endearment and comfort. Often used interchangeably with 'yakap'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng isang mahigpit na **akap** mula sa iyo.","translation":"I need a tight **hug** from you."},{"sentence":"Ang **akap** ng ina ay gamot sa kalungkutan.","translation":"A mother's **embrace** is a cure for sadness."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang deskripsyon sa daan o ibabaw na hindi pantay at may maraming butas o hukay.
original_explanation: The default setting of most roads outside the main highways in the Philippines. It's the reason your daily commute feels like a free, unwanted rollercoaster ride. Driving on a 'lubak-lubak' road is a skill, and avoiding the potholes is a national sport. Your car's suspension system is crying.
usage_notes: Very specific to roads and surfaces. A highly descriptive and common word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa pagmamaneho dahil **lubak-lubak** ang daan papunta sa probinsya.","translation":"Drive carefully because the road to the province is **bumpy**."},{"sentence":"Nasira ang gulong ng sasakyan dahil sa **lubak-lubak** na kalsada.","translation":"The car's tire was damaged because of the **pothole-filled** road."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng katawan mula sa baywang hanggang sa mga tuhod ng isang taong nakaupo. Sa mas malalim na kahulugan, ito ay tumutukoy sa sinapupunan o bahay-bata ng isang ina.
original_explanation: Literally, it's your lap—the perfect place for a laptop, a cat, or a sleepy toddler. Figuratively and more poetically, it's the womb, the "sinapupunan." It speaks of safety, origin, and motherly love. "Mula sa kandungan ng iyong ina..." sounds way more epic than "from your mom's womb."
usage_notes: Can be literal (lap) or figurative (womb, care, protection). The context determines the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inilagay niya ang sanggol sa kanyang **kandungan**.","translation":"She placed the baby on her **lap**."},{"sentence":"Siyam na buwan kang nanatili sa **kandungan** ng iyong ina.","translation":"You stayed for nine months in your mother's **womb**."}]

translation: entry; entrance; act of coming in
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpunta sa loob ng isang lugar, espasyo, o institusyon. Maaari rin itong tumukoy sa pagsisimula ng isang panahon o yugto, tulad ng sa trabaho o paaralan.
original_explanation: This is your daily grind. The act of swiping your ID to get into the office. The moment you step into the classroom. The start of the rainy season ('pagpasok ng tag-ulan'). It's the opposite of 'pag-uwi'. It’s the 'Hello, world!' of your day.
usage_notes: Very common word with multiple applications: entering a place, starting school/work ('pasukan'), or the beginning of a season.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang seguridad sa **pagpasok** sa gusali.","translation":"The security is strict upon **entry** into the building."},{"sentence":"Malapit na ang **pagpasok** ng mga estudyante sa eskwela.","translation":"The start of the school year for students is near."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na tumutugtog ng instrumento bilang saliw sa isang pangunahing mang-aawit o manunugtog.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'taga-' at salitang hiram sa Espanyol na 'acompañar' (sumama, samahan).
original_explanation: The unsung hero of every 'The Voice' audition. Sila 'yung nagpi-piano o gitara habang bumibirit 'yung contestant. The official 'supporter' in a musical performance.
usage_notes: Isang espesyal na termino sa larangan ng musika.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahusay ang **tagaakompanya** sa piyano kaya lalong gumanda ang kanta.","translation":"The **accompanist** on the piano was excellent, which made the song even more beautiful."},{"sentence":"Naghahanap sila ng **tagaakompanya** para sa kanilang koro.","translation":"They are looking for an **accompanist** for their choir."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagtatanggol o nagbibigay proteksyon sa iba; isang abogado na kumakatawan sa nasasakdal sa isang kaso.
original_explanation: The 'knight in shining armor' ng mga na-aakusahan. Sila 'yung tagapagtanggol mo sa korte, o 'yung best friend mong laging kumakampi sa'yo kahit alam niyang mali ka. Basically, your personal 'I got your back' person.
usage_notes: Bagama't nangangahulugang pangkalahatang tagapagtanggol, mas madalas itong tumutukoy sa isang abogado de depensa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha siya ng magaling na **depensor** para sa kanyang kaso.","translation":"He hired a great **defense lawyer** for his case."},{"sentence":"Itinuturing siyang **depensor** ng mga naaapi.","translation":"He is considered a **defender** of the oppressed."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng lutuing Pilipino na gawa sa dugo at lamang-loob ng baboy, na niluto sa suka, bawang, at iba pang pampalasa.
etymology: From 'dugo' (blood) with the suffix '-an', literally meaning 'made with blood'.
original_explanation: That one Pinoy dish that makes foreigners go "Wait, what's in it?" and makes Pinoys go "Extra puto, please!". It's savory, slightly sour, and a whole lot of deliciousness. Also called "chocolate meat" to trick your friends.
usage_notes: Often served with 'puto' (steamed rice cakes). Variations exist across different regions of the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap ang **dinuguan** kapag may kasamang puto.","translation":"**Pork blood stew** is delicious when paired with steamed rice cakes."},{"sentence":"Nag-uwi si nanay ng isang palayok na mainit na **dinuguan**.","translation":"Mom brought home a pot of hot **pork blood stew**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang taong taksil, hindi mapagkakatiwalaan, at madalas ay madaldal o masalita sa paraang walang kabuluhan.
original_explanation: This is a very dramatic, old-school word. It describes someone who is a traitor AND annoyingly talkative. Imagine that gossipy officemate who not only spreads rumors but also stabs you in the back to get a promotion. That's 'talipandas'. It's a word straight out of a Florante at Laura-esque drama, a perfect descriptor for a villain.
usage_notes: A literary and somewhat archaic word, carrying strong negative connotations of both betrayal and senseless talkativeness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinilala siya bilang isang **talipandas** na Hudas sa kanilang samahan.","translation":"He was known as a **treacherous** Judas in their group."},{"sentence":"Iwasan mo ang mga taong **talipandas** at hindi marunong magtago ng sikreto.","translation":"Avoid **garrulous and untrustworthy** people who don't know how to keep a secret."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay na bitbit o pasan; pasanin o bagahe.
original_explanation: Your 'dala' is everything you're carrying. Physically, it's your backpack, your groceries, your laptop bag. Emotionally? It's your 'hugot,' your baggage from your ex, the stress from your BPO shift. 'Ang bigat ng dala ko ngayon' can mean your grocery bags are heavy, or life is just... heavy.
usage_notes: Often used in the phrase 'mabigat ang dala' (the load is heavy), which can be literal or figurative.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang dami mong **dala**! Saan ka pupunta?","translation":"You have so much **baggage**! Where are you going?"},{"sentence":"Ang bawat isa ay may kanya-kanyang **dala** sa buhay.","translation":"Everyone has their own **load** to carry in life."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kilos na tumutukoy sa pagdurog o pagpino ng isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng paulit-ulit na pagpukpok o pagbayo, karaniwan sa isang lusong at pambayo.
etymology: From the root word 'dikdik' meaning to pound or pulverize.
original_explanation: Eto yung ginawa sa puso mo nung nalaman mong 'di ka niya gusto. Durog. Pinong-pino. Parang bawang at paminta na pinagsama sa almires para sa adobo. The process of being absolutely crushed, literally or emotionally.
usage_notes: This is the completed or past tense (perfective aspect) form of the verb 'dikdikin' (to pound).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dinikdik** niya ang bawang bago igisa.","translation":"She **pounded** the garlic before sautéing it."},{"sentence":"Para sa gamot, **dinikdik** ng albularyo ang mga tuyong dahon.","translation":"For the medicine, the folk healer **crushed** the dried leaves."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pariralang nagpapahayag ng pagkakaiba o hindi pagkakatulad ng isang bagay, tao, o konsepto kumpara sa iba.
original_explanation: The ultimate "I'm not like the other girls/guys" phrase. You use this to highlight uniqueness or contrast. "Yung ex ko? Ay, iba sa lahat. Iba siyang manakit." It's the go-to phrase for comparing your current coffee spot to Starbucks or explaining why your kind of "pagod" is different from everyone else's.
usage_notes: A common prepositional phrase.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang panlasa niya sa musika ay **iba sa** karamihan.","translation":"His taste in music is **different from** the majority."},{"sentence":"Ang naramdaman ko para sa kanya ay **iba sa** naramdaman ko dati.","translation":"What I felt for him was **unlike** anything I've felt before."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matatag at di-natitinag na paniniwala o opinyon. Sa legal na konteksto, ito ay ang pormal na pagpapahayag ng paghatol na ang isang tao ay nagkasala.
original_explanation: Two meanings, bes. First, it's that "I will die on this hill" feeling mo about something, like believing pineapple belongs on pizza. Second, it's what happens to a corrupt official when the Sandiganbayan finally does its job. From strong belief to a guilty verdict.
usage_notes: Can refer to a strong belief or a legal judgment. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May matibay siyang **kombiksiyon** na tama ang kanyang ginagawa.","translation":"He has a strong **conviction** that what he is doing is right."},{"sentence":"Nahaharap siya sa **kombiksiyon** para sa kasong pagnanakaw.","translation":"He is facing **conviction** for the crime of theft."}]

translation: to be exposed, to be revealed
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging hayag o kita sa publiko; ang paglabas ng isang bagay na dating nakatago o lihim.
original_explanation: This is what happens when your 'private' DMs get screenshotted and posted online. It's the 'tea' being spilled, the 'receipts' being shown. You thought it was a secret, but now everyone in the Marites group chat knows. You've been malantad.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of scandals, secrets, or vulnerabilities being revealed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang **malantad** ang kanyang kahinaan sa harap ng marami.","translation":"He doesn't want his weakness to **be exposed** in front of many people."},{"sentence":"Nang **malantad** ang katotohanan, gumuho ang kanyang mundo.","translation":"When the truth **was revealed**, her world collapsed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapatigil sa ingay, gulo, o sa isang taong nagsasalita; pagpapakalma.
etymology: From pag- (nominalizer) + pa- (causative prefix) + tahimik (quiet, silent).
original_explanation: This can be as innocent as a librarian shushing a noisy group, or as sinister as a movie villain 'silencing' a witness. It's the act of making someone or something quiet. It's what you try to do to your barking dog at 3 AM or to your chismosa tita who's about to spill the tea at a family reunion.
usage_notes: Can have a neutral meaning (to quiet down) or a negative, threatening connotation (to silence permanently).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapatahimik** sa mga bata ay naging hamon sa guro.","translation":"The **act of quieting** the children was a challenge for the teacher."},{"sentence":"May masamang balak ang mga kriminal na **pagpapatahimik** sa testigo.","translation":"The criminals have a sinister plan of **silencing** the witness."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubos na masaya; nagpapahayag ng sukdulang kagalakan o kasiyahan.
etymology: From the root 'ligaya' (joy), intensified by reduplication and the 'ka-' prefix.
original_explanation: This is not just 'happy'. This is "nanalo ka sa lotto while on your way to marry the love of your life on a perfect beach day" happy. It's the peak, the climax of joy. The kind of happiness that makes you want to spontaneously burst into a musical number.
usage_notes: An intensified form of 'maligaya' (happy). The prefix 'ka-' and the reduplication 'liga-' emphasize the supreme degree of happiness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ito na marahil ang **kaliga-ligaya**ng araw ng aking buhay.","translation":"This is probably the **most joyful** day of my life."},{"sentence":"**Kaliga-ligaya** ang kanyang ngiti nang makita niya ang kanyang pamilya.","translation":"Her smile was **extremely happy** when she saw her family."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkabawas o pagkakaltas mula sa isang kabuuan, halaga, o bilang.
etymology: From na- (verb prefix) + awas (to reduce, deduct).
original_explanation: That feeling of dread when you check your payslip and see all the deductions. "Ang laki ng sahod ko, pero ang liit ng take-home pay kasi ang daming naawas!" It's what happens to your sauce supply when your friend double-dips their fries.
usage_notes: Commonly used in financial contexts (salary, budget) or when talking about quantities. Often seen with 'ang' or 'yung' to denote what was deducted.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Naawas** ang buwis mula sa aking sahod.","translation":"The tax **was deducted** from my salary."},{"sentence":"Pakitingnan kung may **naawas** sa laman ng kahon.","translation":"Please check if anything **was reduced** from the box's contents."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga uri ng pagkain na karaniwang inihahanda at inihahain tuwing may mga espesyal na okasyon tulad ng pista, kaarawan, Pasko, at iba pang pagdiriwang.
etymology: Pagsasama ng salitang Espanyol na "fiesta" (pista) at salitang Ingles na "food" (pagkain).
original_explanation: Think lechon, spaghetti (the sweet Filipino kind!), pansit, lumpia, and fruit salad with that questionable amount of condensed milk. These are the Avengers of Filipino celebrations. You know it's a party when you see these dishes assembled on a table. 'Fiestafood' is a whole food group on its own, and the main side effect is a 'food coma' and the need for a nap afterwards.
usage_notes: Isang kolokyal na tambalang salita.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sarap kumain ng mga **fiestafood** lalo na kung libre.","translation":"It's so delicious to eat **fiesta food**, especially when it's free."},{"sentence":"Nag-crave ako bigla sa **fiestafood** tulad ng lechon at pansit.","translation":"I suddenly craved **fiesta food** like roasted pig and noodles."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumukoy sa paglikha ng isang matinis at paulit-ulit na tunog, karaniwan mula sa maliliit na bagay na metal tulad ng mga barya o susi.
original_explanation: That sound your spare change makes in your pocket when you're running to catch the jeep. It's the 'I'm broke but not *completely* broke' anthem. Parang tunog ng mga susi ng landlord mo kapag papalapit na siya sa pinto mo on the 15th.
usage_notes: Describes a light, high-pitched, metallic sound.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumalansing** ang mga barya sa kanyang bulsa.","translation":"The coins **jingled** in his pocket."},{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **kumalansing** na mga susi kaya alam kong parating na siya.","translation":"I heard the keys **jingling**, so I knew he was arriving."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kaliwang bahagi ng isang barko o sasakyang-dagat kapag nakaharap sa unahan (proa).
original_explanation: The nautical term for "left" that makes you sound like a legit sea captain, even if you're just on the Pasig River Ferry. It's the opposite of 'estribor' (starboard/right). Use this to impress your friends during your next beach trip on a bangka. "Lipat kayo sa babor, 'wag lahat sa estribor, baka tumagilid!"
usage_notes: A technical term used in maritime contexts. The average person might not know this.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Makikita ang isla mula sa **babor** ng barko.","translation":"The island can be seen from the **port side** of the ship."},{"sentence":"Inutusan ng kapitan ang mga tripulante na ihanda ang mga kagamitan sa **babor**.","translation":"The captain ordered the crew to prepare the equipment on the **port side**."}]

translation: to put something on a tray for someone
meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng isang bagay ang bandeha para sa isang tao.
original_explanation: Similar to `pabandeha`, but this focuses on the person receiving the tray service. It's the action of preparing the tray for them. "Anak, pabandehahan mo ng meryenda ang lolo mo." It's the verb form of being a good apo or a five-star hotel staff.
usage_notes: The object is the person for whom the tray is being prepared.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan ng manager ang waiter na **pabandehahan** ng komplimentaryong inumin ang VIP guest.","translation":"The manager instructed the waiter to **put complimentary drinks on a tray for** the VIP guest."},{"sentence":"\"Sige na, **pabandehahan** mo na ako ng hapunan, pagod na pagod na ako,\" biro niya sa asawa.","translation":"\"Come on, **put my dinner on a tray for me**, I'm so tired,\" he joked to his wife."}]

translation: to strive; to endeavor; to work hard
meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa nang may buong pagsisikap at tiyaga upang makamit ang isang layunin.
original_explanation: This is the official motto of every Pinoy parent trying to motivate their kids. "Mag-aral kang mabuti, anak, at **magsikap** ka sa buhay!" It's the hustle culture before "hustle culture" was a thing. It’s the energy you channel when you're juggling a full-time job, a side hustle, and still trying to have a social life.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of achieving long-term goals like education, career success, or improving one's life.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magsikap** para maabot ang iyong mga pangarap.","translation":"You need **to strive** to reach your dreams."},{"sentence":"Siya ay **nagsikap** sa pag-aaral kaya nakapagtapos siya nang may karangalan.","translation":"She **worked hard** in her studies, which is why she graduated with honors."}]

translation: to suppress, to quell, to subdue
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng kakayahang pigilan, kontrolin, o talunin ang isang bagay na malakas o mahirap pamahalaan, tulad ng isang rebelyon, damdamin, o sakit.
original_explanation: What you try to do to your 'kilig' when your crush walks by. Or what the government tries to do to a protest. It's about putting something down, keeping it under control, whether it's an army, a fire, or your urge to buy something on a 12.12 sale.
usage_notes: A formal word often found in news reports, historical texts, or when discussing control over strong forces or emotions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinikap ng mga bumbero na **masupil** ang malaking sunog.","translation":"The firefighters tried to **suppress** the huge fire."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **masupil** ang galit na nararamdaman niya.","translation":"It is difficult to **subdue** the anger that he feels."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsama o pag-isa sa isang grupo o puwersa; maaari ring tumukoy sa pagpasok ng isang espiritu sa katawan ng isang tao.
original_explanation: This verb has two vibes. Vibe 1: Corporate. When two companies merge, they *sumanib*. "Let's synergize our efforts!" Vibe 2: Horror movie. When a ghost enters a person's body, it *sumanib*. "The power of Christ compels you!" Choose your adventure.
usage_notes: Has a dual meaning: a neutral one (to merge/join forces) and a supernatural one (to be possessed). Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumanib** ang dalawang kumpanya upang palakasin ang kanilang negosyo.","translation":"The two companies **merged** to strengthen their business."},{"sentence":"Ayon sa kwento, **sumanib** daw ang isang masamang espiritu sa dalaga.","translation":"According to the story, an evil spirit supposedly **possessed** the young woman."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng tela na may natatanging disenyo at kulay, ginagamit bilang simbolo ng isang bansa, organisasyon, o kilusan.
original_explanation: The ultimate symbol of "#ProudToBePinoy." It's what we raise every Monday morning in school while trying to hit the high notes of "Lupang Hinirang." It's also what athletes wave when they win a gold medal. Figuratively, "magtaas ng bandera" means to bring honor to a group, like when you're the only one in your barkada who passes the exam.
usage_notes: Can be used for any flag, but most commonly refers to a national flag. The phrase 'itaas ang puting bandera' means 'to raise the white flag' or to surrender.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **bandera** ng Pilipinas ay may kulay pula, asul, puti, at dilaw.","translation":"The **flag** of the Philippines has the colors red, blue, white, and yellow."},{"sentence":"Itinaas nila ang puting **bandera** bilang tanda ng pagsuko.","translation":"They raised the white **flag** as a sign of surrender."}]

translation: to fulfill; to bring to fruition; to realize
meaning_filipino: Gawing ganap o maisagawa ang isang plano, pangarap, o pangako.
etymology: From `i-` (verb prefix) + `sa` (to/for) + `katuparan` (fulfillment), which is from the root `tupad` (to fulfill).
original_explanation: The ultimate 'make it happen' verb. This is for your big life goals, not just for your weekend plans. It’s what pageant winners promise to do, what politicians claim they will achieve, and what you tell yourself about your new year's resolutions. 'Sana ma-**isakatuparan** ko ang pangarap kong mag-travel sa buong mundo.'
usage_notes: A formal and profound word, often used for dreams, promises, plans, and laws.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinulungan niya akong **isakatuparan** ang aking mga pangarap.","translation":"He helped me **fulfill** my dreams."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **isakatuparan** ang isang batas kung walang suporta ng mamamayan.","translation":"It is difficult to **implement** a law without the support of the people."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng pagiging madaling magdamdam o magtanim ng sama ng loob sa kapwa.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `mapag-` at `hinanakit` (sama ng loob, sentimyento).
original_explanation: Ito yung kaibigan na 'di mo nireplyan ng 5 minutes tapos may "K" na sagot. Tapos after 3 years, isusumbat pa rin niya yun. Sila yung may listahan—written or unwritten—ng lahat ng kasalanan mo since 19-kopong-kopong. Master of the silent treatment and the art of "sumbat."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **mapaghinanakit** na tao ang mahirap patawarin at mahirap ding magpatawad.","translation":"A **resentful** person is hard to forgive and also finds it hard to forgive."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang huwag maging **mapaghinanakit** sa kabila ng mga nangyari.","translation":"She tries not to be **resentful** despite what happened."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paggalaw sa ibabaw ng anyong tubig tulad ng dagat o lawa, na nililikha ng hangin o iba pang puwersa.
original_explanation: The reason you go to La Union or Siargao. It's what you try to surf on, what crashes on the shore while you're having a 'hugot' moment, and what sometimes knocks you over when you thought you were strong enough. Life is like an 'alon', sometimes you're up, sometimes you're down.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin sa matalinghagang paraan, hal. 'alon ng buhay'. Ang pandiwang 'umaalon' ay nangangahulugang 'nagkakaroon ng mga alon'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lakas ng **alon** sa dagat kaya bawal maligo.","translation":"The **waves** in the sea are strong, so swimming is not allowed."},{"sentence":"Masarap pakinggan ang hampas ng **alon** sa dalampasigan.","translation":"It's nice to listen to the crash of the **waves** on the shore."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na silid sa bilangguan o piitan kung saan ikinukulong ang isang tao.
original_explanation: This is the 'cell' you don't want to be in. Hindi ito 'yung biological cell or cellphone. Ito 'yung kwarto sa kulungan. Parang pinakamaliit na studio-type unit na walang Wi-Fi at may kasamang rehas.
usage_notes: Ginagamit din sa metaporikal na paraan upang ilarawan ang isang nakakulong na sitwasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inilipat ang bilanggo sa mas mahigpit na **selda**.","translation":"The prisoner was moved to a more secure **cell**."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam niya ay nabubuhay siya sa isang **selda** dahil sa mahigpit niyang mga magulang.","translation":"She felt like she was living in a **cell** because of her strict parents."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na may malawak at natatanging kaalaman o kasanayan sa isang partikular na larangan.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung tita mo na 'eksperto' sa lahat ng bagay, mula sa pagluluto ng adobo hanggang sa love life mo. O 'yung ka-team mo sa work na laging tinatawag ng boss 'pag may sunog na kailangang apulain. Sila ang mga resident 'SME' (Subject Matter Expert).
usage_notes: The spelling "ekspert" is sometimes used, influenced by the English "expert", but "eksperto" is the standard form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinonsulta nila ang isang **eksperto** sa batas bago simulan ang kaso.","translation":"They consulted a legal **expert** before starting the case."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang yugto ng panahon na katumbas ng labing-apat na araw.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng 'dalawa' (two) at 'linggo' (week, mula sa Espanyol na 'domingo').
original_explanation: The official waiting time for your sahod (paycheck). It's the 'quarantine period' we all got too familiar with. It's how long you promise yourself you'll stick to a diet before giving up. Basically, 14 days, or a fortnight if you're feeling fancy.
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang yunit ng pagsukat ng panahon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magbabakasyon kami sa probinsya sa loob ng **dalawang linggo**.","translation":"We will be on vacation in the province for **two weeks**."},{"sentence":"Aabutin ng **dalawang linggo** bago dumating ang inorder mong gamit.","translation":"It will take **two weeks** before the item you ordered arrives."}]

translation: to be shuffled (like cards); to be disconcerted or worried
meaning_filipino: Magulo ang ayos o pagkakasunod-sunod, tulad ng sa baraha; mabagabag o hindi mapakali ang isip o damdamin.
original_explanation: This word has two vibes. 1) The literal: what you do to a deck of playing cards before a game of 'tong-its'. 2) The emotional: what happens to your feelings when your crush views your IG story but doesn't reply to your DM. You're 'nabalasa'—all mixed up, anxious, and unsettled.
usage_notes: The meaning of being worried or anxious is more common in modern conversation than the literal shuffling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **mabalasa** nang mabuti ang mga baraha bago mamigay.","translation":"The cards need **to be shuffled** well before dealing."},{"sentence":"**Nabalasa** ako sa balitang narinig ko kanina.","translation":"I **was disconcerted** by the news I heard earlier."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa mga paniniwalang Austronesian, ito ay isang puwersa o kapangyarihang espirituwal na maaaring taglayin ng isang tao, bagay, o lugar. Sa kontekstong biblikal, ito ay ang pagkaing ipinagkaloob ng Diyos.
etymology: From Polynesian languages, referring to a supernatural force. Also influenced by the biblical 'manna'. The two concepts have converged in modern pop culture usage.
original_explanation: Think of it as the original MP (Magic Points) or energy bar in video games. In RPGs like Mobile Legends or DOTA, mana is the resource you use to cast spells. 'Wala na akong mana!' means you can't use your skills anymore. It's that magical juice that lets you do cool stuff.
usage_notes: The 'magical power' meaning is almost exclusively used in the context of fantasy, video games, and RPGs. The biblical 'manna' is less common in everyday speech. Context makes the meaning clear from its homonym 'mana' (inheritance).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong bumalik sa base para mapunong muli ang aking **mana**.","translation":"I need to return to base to refill my **mana**."},{"sentence":"Sa Bibliya, umulan ng **mana** mula sa langit.","translation":"In the Bible, **manna** rained down from heaven."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa tubig sa ilalim ng lupa na kusang umaagos paitaas dahil sa presyon, o sa balon na pinagkukunan nito.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "artesiano," na tumutukoy sa rehiyon ng Artois sa Pransya kung saan unang naobserbahan ang mga ganitong balon.
original_explanation: "Poso negro" is for waste, but "posong artesyano" is the OG water source in the province before NAWASA or Maynilad became a thing. It's the free-flowing, manually pumped well that gives you cool, clean water. It’s also where all the neighborhood chismis happens while waiting for your turn to pump.
usage_notes: Most commonly seen in the phrase "posong artesyano" (artesian well).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha kami ng inuming tubig mula sa posong **artesyano**.","translation":"We got drinking water from the **artesian** well."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malaking puno (Afzelia rhomboidea) na may matigas at matibay na kahoy, karaniwang ginagamit sa paggawa ng muwebles at sa konstruksiyon.
original_explanation: Think of it as the ultimate Tita-approved wood for furniture. It's the kind of wood your Lolo would point to and say, "This table is made of **tindalo**, it will outlive all of us." It's the OG, premium, built-to-last material before IKEA flat-packs existed.
usage_notes: A specific type of Philippine hardwood, known for its durability and reddish color. Also spelled as 'tindalo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sahig ng lumang bahay ay yari sa makintab na **tindalo**.","translation":"The floor of the old house was made of shiny **Philippine ironwood**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hanay ng mga tao o bagay na nakaayos nang sunod-sunod, karaniwang naghihintay para sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: The national sport of the Philippines. Whether it's for the MRT, a milk tea shop, or getting "ayuda," you'll find a **pila**. It's a test of patience, a social gathering, and a place where you hear all the latest "chismis." The rule is simple: bawal sumingit!
usage_notes: A very common word used in daily life. `Pumila` is the verb form (to line up).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang haba ng **pila** sa sinehan!","translation":"The **line** at the cinema is so long!"},{"sentence":"Pumila ka nang maayos at huwag sumingit sa **pila**.","translation":"Line up properly and don't cut in **line**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kasama o kabalikat sa isang gawain, negosyo, o relasyon.
original_explanation: Your partner can be your 'partner in crime' for sneaking in extra rice, your business partner for that online selling hustle, or your life partner (a.k.a. jowa). It's the person you're stuck with, for better or for worse, in a project or in life.
usage_notes: A direct loanword from English, widely used in both formal and informal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang aking **partner** sa sayaw para sa school program.","translation":"He is my dance **partner** for the school program."},{"sentence":"Humanap ka ng maaasahang **partner** sa negosyo.","translation":"Find a reliable business **partner**."}]

meaning_filipino: Pinaikling anyo ng salitang "celebrity"; isang taong sikat o tanyag, lalo na sa larangan ng libangan.
etymology: Pinaikling anyo ng salitang Ingles na "celebrity".
original_explanation: Short for 'celebrity.' Sila 'yung mga artista, vlogger, influencer, o kahit sinong sikat na laman ng balita at social media feed mo. 'Yung buhay nila parang teleserye na sinusubaybayan ng buong bansa.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa impormal na pag-uusap at sa entertainment news.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang daming **celeb** na dumalo sa premiere night ng pelikula.","translation":"So many **celebs** attended the movie's premiere night."},{"sentence":"Naging instant **celeb** siya dahil sa viral niyang TikTok video.","translation":"She became an instant **celeb** because of her viral TikTok video."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng malalim na pagrerelaks at matinding konsentrasyon, na kahawig ng pagtulog, kung saan ang isang tao ay nagiging mas bukas sa mga mungkahi.
original_explanation: Yan yung ginagawa sa'yo ng crush mo kahit di mo alam. Isang tingin lang, para ka nang na-hipnosis, sunud-sunuran ka na. Or yung state mo pagkatapos ng 12-hour shift, zombie mode na, open to suggestions like 'isa pang kape?'
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa kontekstong medikal, sikolohikal, o pang-aliw (stage hypnosis).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ng terapista ang **hipnosis** upang matulungan siyang alalahanin ang nakaraan.","translation":"The therapist used **hypnosis** to help her remember the past."},{"sentence":"Para siyang nasa ilalim ng **hipnosis** tuwing nanonood ng kanyang paboritong serye.","translation":"It's like he's under **hypnosis** whenever he watches his favorite series."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi kayang pasukan o tagusan ng anumang bagay, lalo na ng likido o matutulis na bagay.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'di-' (hindi) at pandiwang 'tatagusan' (will be penetrated).
original_explanation: Like your friend's 'Marites-proof' earphones. Or your mom's heart when you ask for more allowance after you just got it yesterday. It's 'di-tatagusan'—nothing gets through.
usage_notes: Often used to describe materials or barriers.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang suot niyang baluti ay sinasabing **di-tatagusan** ng anumang patalim.","translation":"The armor he wears is said to be **impenetrable** by any blade."},{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng bubong na **di-tatagusan** ng tubig-ulan.","translation":"We need a roof that is **impermeable** to rainwater."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagluluto ng pagkain, tulad ng karne o isda, sa ibabaw ng nagbabagang uling o apoy.
original_explanation: The official verb of Pinoy family outings. Anong gagawin sa beach? **Mag-ihaw**. Anong handa sa birthday? **Mag-ihaw** ng liempo. Anong amoy sa kapitbahay tuwing Linggo? Amoy ng nag-iihaw. It's the scent of happiness.
usage_notes: Ito ang pawatas (infinitive) na anyo. Ang ibang anyo ay 'nag-ihaw' (naganap), 'nag-iihaw' (nagaganap), at 'mag-iihaw' (magaganap).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig si Tatay na **mag-ihaw** ng bangus tuwing may salu-salo.","translation":"Dad loves to **grill** milkfish whenever there's a gathering."},{"sentence":"Tara, **mag-ihaw** tayo ng hotdog at marshmallows!","translation":"Come on, let's **grill** some hotdogs and marshmallows!"}]

translation: to warn; to give a warning
meaning_filipino: Magbigay ng paunang paalala o impormasyon tungkol sa posibleng panganib, kamalian, o masamang mangyayari.
original_explanation: That thing your friend does before you make a bad life choice, but you do it anyway. 'Nagbabala na ako sa'yo tungkol diyan, 'di ba?' Also, what PAGASA does 24/7 during rainy season.
usage_notes: This is the more common meaning of 'magbabala'. It is distinct from the homonym related to loading bullets.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Patuloy na **nagbabala** ang mga awtoridad sa pagtaas ng tubig sa ilog.","translation":"The authorities continue to **warn** about the rising water level in the river."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sabay na pagkilos ng dalawa o higit pang tao na magkayakap sa isa't isa nang mahigpit.
etymology: From magka- (denoting a reciprocal or mutual action) + yapos (embrace).
original_explanation: That moment when you and your jowa are in a tight hug, parang ayaw niyo nang bumitaw. It's the physical manifestation of "sana all," especially when you see a couple being sweet in public. It's a deeper, more intentional hug than a simple 'yakap'.
usage_notes: "Magkayapos" implies a mutual, often prolonged and tight embrace, different from a quick "yakap".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita ko silang **magkayapos** sa ilalim ng puno ng mangga.","translation":"I saw them **embracing each other** under the mango tree."},{"sentence":"Kahit mainit ang panahon, gustong-gusto pa rin nilang **magkayapos** habang nanonood ng TV.","translation":"Even though the weather is hot, they still love **to embrace each other** while watching TV."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtayo mula sa pagkakaupo o pagkakahiga; ang pagbangon. Maaari ring tumukoy sa pag-angat o paglitaw ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: This isn't just "tayo." 'Tumindig' has more drama, more purpose. You stand up for the national anthem (tumindig para sa Lupang Hinirang). You rise against injustice (tumindig laban sa katiwalian). It's what your hair does when you watch a horror movie (tumindig ang balahibo). It's standing up with conviction.
usage_notes: Carries a more formal or dramatic connotation than "tayo" (to stand). "Tumindig ang balahibo" is a common idiom for getting goosebumps.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumindig** ang lahat nang pumasok ang pangulo.","translation":"Everyone **stood up** when the president entered."},{"sentence":"**Tumindig** ang aking balahibo nang marinig ko ang kakaibang tunog.","translation":"My hair **stood on end** when I heard the strange sound."}]

translation: to be blocked; to be clogged
meaning_filipino: Mahadlangan o masarhan ang isang daanan, na nagiging sanhi ng pagtigil ng daloy.
original_explanation: Your sink when you've washed too much pancit canton residue down it. EDSA at 5 PM on a payday Friday. Your friend's DMs when they post a fire selfie. Anything that's supposed to flow but can't. 'Mabarahan' is the Tagalog for 'Houston, we have a blockage.'
usage_notes: Used for both physical blockages (pipes, roads) and metaphorical ones (communication, creative flow).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumawag ka ng tubero dahil baka **mabarahan** ang ating lababo.","translation":"Call a plumber because our sink might **get clogged**."},{"sentence":"Sana hindi **mabarahan** ang daloy ng tulong para sa mga nasalanta.","translation":"I hope the flow of aid for the victims won't **be blocked**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay o tao na itinuring na hindi katanggap-tanggap o may mababang kalidad.
original_explanation: Sa Divisoria or factory outlet, ito yung mga damit na may slight, almost unnoticeable na sira pero binebenta nang mas mura. Sa love life, ikaw 'to nung 'di ka niya pinili. A term for being "basted" or not making the cut, whether for a job, a team, or a relationship. Ouch.
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang salitang Taglish. Maaaring gamitin bilang pangngalan ("Isang reject 'yan") o pang-uri ("Reject 'yang item na 'yan").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong bilhin 'yan, baka **reject** 'yan.","translation":"Don't buy that, it might be a **reject**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga damit na ito ay mga **reject** mula sa pabrika kaya mura.","translation":"These clothes are **rejects** from the factory, that's why they're cheap."}]

translation: to alleviate; to relieve; to ease
meaning_filipino: Bawasan o pagaanin ang tindi ng isang pasanin, sakit, o hirap.
original_explanation: That feeling when you finally take off your tight shoes after a long day? That's "maibsan." When you get your salary and your financial stress lessens a bit? "Maibsan." It's the relief you feel when a burden, physical or emotional, is made lighter. The "ahh, much better" moment.
usage_notes: Used for both physical pain (sakit) and emotional/abstract burdens (hirap, kalungkutan, problema).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uminom siya ng gamot upang **maibsan** ang sakit ng ulo.","translation":"He took medicine to **alleviate** the headache."},{"sentence":"Ang pakikipag-usap sa kaibigan ay nakatulong upang **maibsan** ang kaniyang lungkot.","translation":"Talking to a friend helped **ease** her sadness."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kuryente na dumadaloy sa iisang direksyon lamang, salungat sa salitang-daloy na kuryente (alternating current).
etymology: Isang neolohismo na binuo mula sa salitang "tahas" (tuwiran, direkta) at "tablay" (kargang kuryente).
original_explanation: Ito yung OG na kuryente, straight-to-the-point, walang pabalik-balik. Parang yung friend mong prangka, isang direksyon lang mag-isip. Hindi ito yung AC na pa-AC/DC, pabago-bago. DC is 'Diretso, 'tol!' Ginagamit sa mga baterya at electronics.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang terminong teknikal na karaniwang ginagamit sa larangan ng pisika, inhinyeriya, at elektroniks. Hindi ito pangkaraniwan sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga baterya ay karaniwang pinagmumulan ng **tahas na tablay**.","translation":"Batteries are a common source of **direct current**."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng mga mag-aaral ang pagkakaiba ng **tahas na tablay** at salitang-daloy na tablay.","translation":"The students are studying the difference between **direct current** and alternating current."}]

translation: to point a finger at someone accusingly
meaning_filipino: Ituro ang isang tao gamit ang daliri, karaniwan sa paraang nagpaparatang o nagbabala.
original_explanation: This is the singular version of `duruan`. It's that dramatic finger-pointing you see in teleseryes. "How dare you!" *sabay duro*. It's more intense than just `ituro` (to point). `Duruin` has that extra spice of accusation, warning, or "ikaw!" energy. It's the physical punctuation to a heated argument.
usage_notes: Carries a strong connotation of accusation, blame, or threat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **duruin** na parang ako ang may kasalanan!","translation":"Don't **point your finger at me** as if I'm the one at fault!"},{"sentence":"**Dinuro** niya ang magnanakaw habang sumisigaw ng tulong.","translation":"She **pointed at** the thief while shouting for help."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng maraming sabaw; malabnaw o hindi siksik sa nilalaman.
original_explanation: When your sinigang is more liquid than solid, that's `masabaw`. It's also used to describe a person who's all talk with no substance, or a joke that's corny and diluted. 'Ang `masabaw` mong joke, parang relasyon natin, malabnaw.' (Your soupy joke, like our relationship, is weak.)
usage_notes: Can be used literally for food or figuratively for ideas, jokes, or even people whose thoughts seem scattered.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko ng sinigang na **masabaw** para maraming mahigop.","translation":"I want a **soupy** sinigang so there's a lot to sip."},{"sentence":"Medyo **masabaw** ang mga ideya niya sa meeting kanina.","translation":"His ideas in the meeting earlier were a bit **unsubstantial**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan ang isang tao, pamilya, o hayop ay naninirahan; isang bahay o tahanan.
etymology: Nagmula sa salitang-ugat na 'tira' (manirahan) at hulaping '-han'.
original_explanation: This is what you fill out in forms under "Address". It's your home base, your "where do you live?". From a condo in BGC to a kubo in the province, as long as it's where you sleep and keep your Funko Pops, it's your **tirahan**. Also, the place where your Shopee and Lazada packages are supposed to go.
usage_notes: Ang salitang-ugat na 'tira' dito ay nangangahulugang 'manirahan', iba sa ibang kahulugan ng 'tira'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano po ang permanenteng **tirahan** ninyo?","translation":"What is your permanent **residence**?"},{"sentence":"Ang kagubatan ay **tirahan** ng maraming uri ng hayop.","translation":"The forest is the **dwelling** of many kinds of animals."}]

meaning_filipino: Naganap na ang kilos ng pagkonsumo ng pagkain. Ito ay ang anyong pangnagdaan ng pandiwang 'kain'.
original_explanation: The past tense of the most important Filipino verb. This is what you say after you've successfully conquered a buffet or demolished your baon. 'Have you eaten?' is the Filipino 'I love you,' so 'Kumain ka na ba?' (Have you eaten *already*?) is a critical question. This entry is for when the answer is 'Oo, kumain na ako.' (Yes, I've eaten.)
usage_notes: Ito ang perpektibong aspekto (pangnagdaan) ng pandiwa. Ang "kumakain" ay ang imperpektibong aspekto (pangkasalukuyan).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumain** ako ng almusal bago umalis ng bahay.","translation":"I **ate** breakfast before leaving the house."},{"sentence":"**Kumain** na sila kanina pang tanghali.","translation":"They already **ate** earlier this noon."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa paraan ng pagluluto kung saan ang pagkain ay direktang inilalantad sa init mula sa nagbabagang uling o apoy. Maaari rin itong tumukoy sa mismong pagkaing niluto sa ganitong paraan.
original_explanation: The official scent of every Filipino family outing. Kung may usok sa kapitbahay, malamang may nag-iihaw. From pork belly (liempo) to tilapia and hotdogs on a stick, 'pag inihaw, mas masarap! Best paired with toyo-mansi-sili and a mountain of rice.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pang-uri ('inihaw na manok') o pangngalan ('Ano'ng ulam? Inihaw.').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong kainin ang **inihaw** na liempo.","translation":"My favorite thing to eat is **grilled** pork belly."},{"sentence":"Bumili tayo ng **inihaw** na mais sa kanto.","translation":"Let's buy **grilled** corn at the corner."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pook o gusali kung saan inihahanda at inihahain ang pagkain at inumin sa mga customer kapalit ng bayad.
etymology: From Spanish 'restaurante', adapted into a Filipino phonetic spelling.
original_explanation: The 'official' Tagalog spelling you see in textbooks, but let's be real, most people just type 'restaurant' or 'restoran'. A 'restawran' is where you take your family after someone graduates, or where you have awkward first dates. From the fancy 'kainan' in BGC to the turo-turo with the questionable but delicious ulam, they're all technically 'restawran'.
usage_notes: 'Restoran' and 'resto' are more common in casual conversation and writing. 'Restawran' is a more phonetically Filipino spelling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkita tayo sa paborito nating **restawran** sa Sabado.","translation":"Let's meet at our favorite **restaurant** on Saturday."},{"sentence":"Maraming bagong **restawran** ang nagbukas sa aming lugar.","translation":"Many new **restaurants** have opened in our area."}]

meaning_filipino: Manangis o manambitan nang may matinding kalungkutan o pighati para sa isang bagay o tao.
original_explanation: This is next-level hugot. It's not just crying; it's a dramatic, poetic wail, like when your favorite K-drama character dies or when the internet goes down during a final exam. You don't just feel the sadness, you perform it.
usage_notes: A very literary and deep word, not used in everyday conversation. Found mostly in poems, songs, and classic literature.
