meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng pananampalataya o pagtitiwala sa isang bagay o tao sa nakaraan.
original_explanation: The past tense of "I trust you." 'Yung moment na sinabi niyang "ikaw lang" at umasa ka. Tapos nalaman mo na lang na may "ikaw lang... sa ngayon." It's what you did before you knew better. The act of having believed. #Marupok
usage_notes: Pangnagdaang panahunan (past tense) ng pandiwang 'maniwala'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis siyang **naniwala** sa mga matatamis na salita nito.","translation":"She quickly **believed** his sweet words."},{"sentence":"Dati, hindi ako **naniwala** sa forever, pero ngayon, iba na.","translation":"Before, I didn't **believe** in forever, but now, it's different."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang karagdagang kagamitan na hindi pangunahin ngunit nagpapabuti o nagpapaganda sa paggamit ng isang pangunahing bagay.
original_explanation: This is the 'extra' stuff you buy for your main gadget. The phone case, the pop socket, the cute keychains for your bag, the RGB keyboard for your PC setup. It's not essential for the thing to work, but it makes it *yours* and makes it look cooler. The reason why your Lazada cart is never empty.
usage_notes: A common phrase in tech, fashion, and retail.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng mga **dagdag na gamit** para sa bago kong cellphone.","translation":"I bought some **accessories** for my new cellphone."},{"sentence":"Maraming **dagdag na gamit** ang sasakyan niya kaya ito mahal.","translation":"His car has many **add-ons**, that's why it's expensive."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang karaniwang maling baybay o ponetikong pagkakaiba ng salitang 'Kuwaresma,' na tumutukoy sa panahon ng pagninilay sa Kristiyanismo.
etymology: Variant spelling of Spanish 'Cuaresma'. The phonological shift from /e/ to /i/ is common in Tagalog.
original_explanation: This is how many people mistakenly spell or say 'Kuwaresma' (Lent). It sounds a bit like 'karisma' (charisma), but it has nothing to do with being charming. It's just a common slip of the tongue or typo. If you see this written down, they mean Lent, they just need a little help from spellcheck.
usage_notes: Considered a non-standard or incorrect spelling of 'Kuwaresma,' but is widely understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa Biyernes Santo ng **Kuwarisma**, bawal daw kumain ng karne.","translation":"On Good Friday during **Lent**, they say you shouldn't eat meat."},{"sentence":"Napanood mo na ba ang mga palabas para sa **Kuwarisma**?","translation":"Have you seen the shows for **Lent**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sikretong plano o kasunduan sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang tao upang magsagawa ng isang ilegal o masamang gawain.
original_explanation: The plot of every Pinoy teleserye. It's that whispered conversation in a dark, expensive-looking room between the kontrabida and their sidekick, usually involving taking over the family business or ruining the bida's life. In real life, it's what you suspect your officemates are doing when they suddenly go quiet when you walk into the pantry.
usage_notes: A compound phrase. "Pakana" by itself already implies a scheme, but adding "lihim na" emphasizes its clandestine nature.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nabunyag ang **lihim na pakana** ng mga opisyal laban sa gobyerno.","translation":"The **secret plot** of the officials against the government was exposed."},{"sentence":"Akala nila hindi ko alam ang kanilang **lihim na pakana** para tanggalin ako sa pwesto.","translation":"They thought I didn't know about their **conspiracy** to remove me from my position."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita ng mga guhit o kulubot sa balat, lalo na sa noo, bilang tanda ng pag-aalala, pag-iisip, o di-pagsang-ayon.
original_explanation: 'Yung itsura ng noo mo kapag nakita mong 'seen' lang ang message mo sa kanya, or kapag narinig mo 'yung boss mo na may "urgent" task na naman at 5 PM on a Friday. Automatic, mangunot ang noo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nangunot** ang noo ng guro nang makita ang mababang marka ng kanyang estudyante.","translation":"The teacher's forehead **wrinkled** when she saw her student's low grade."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mangunot** diyan, baka pumangit ka.","translation":"Don't **frown** like that, you might get ugly."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mga kalakal o bagay na inilululan sa barko, eroplano, trak, o iba pang sasakyan para sa transportasyon.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung mga laman ng "kargada." 'Yung 12.12 haul mo from Lazada, 'yan ay isang kargamento. 'Yung container van na puno ng electronics galing China, 'yan ay isang malaking kargamento. Basically, the stuff being moved.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa komersyo at lohistika.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumating na sa daungan ang **kargamento** mula sa ibang bansa.","translation":"The **shipment** from another country has arrived at the port."}]

translation: at the same time; together with; accompanying
meaning_filipino: Ginagawa o nangyayari sa iisang panahon o pagkakataon; kasama sa isang gawain o paglalakbay.
original_explanation: This is your 'sabay tayo mag-lunch' buddy at work. It's when you and your bestie accidentally wear the same color shirt. It's also when your internet bill, water bill, and credit card bill all arrive on the same day. The universe loves to make things 'kasabay'.
usage_notes: Very common word. Can function as an adjective (e.g., "kasabay na pangyayari" - simultaneous event) or an adverb (e.g., "Dumating kami nang kasabay" - We arrived at the same time). Can also be a noun-like word referring to the person/thing one is with.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umalis kami nang **kasabay** papuntang opisina.","translation":"We left **at the same time** for the office."},{"sentence":"Siya ang **kasabay** kong lumaki sa probinsya.","translation":"He is the one I grew up **with** in the province."}]

translation: to make an exception; to express reservation
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapahayag ng pag-aalinlangan, pagtutol, o paglilinaw sa isang kondisyon bago sumang-ayon; paggawa ng eksepsiyon.
original_explanation: This is the formal way of saying 'Wait lang...' or 'Yes, but...'. It's what you do when you generally agree with a plan, but you have one very important condition. 'Okay, sasama ako, pero may pasubali: dapat 10 PM sharp, uwi na 'ko.' You're not totally killing the vibe, just adding a Terms & Conditions apply.
usage_notes: A formal and somewhat rare word. More commonly replaced with phrases like 'pero may kondisyon' or 'maliban kung'. The noun form 'pagpapasubali' (reservation) is more frequently used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumang-ayon siya sa panukala nang walang anumang **pagpapasubali**.","translation":"He agreed to the proposal without any **reservations**."},{"sentence":"Hindi ako **magpapasubali** sa iyong desisyon, kung iyan ang ikasasaya mo.","translation":"I will not **express any doubt** about your decision, if that is what will make you happy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking tropikal na prutas na may berdeng balat na matinik-tinik at dilaw na laman na matamis kapag hinog. Ang hilaw na bunga ay ginugulay.
original_explanation: The jack-of-all-trades fruit. When unripe (*hilaw*), it's the star of *ginataang langka*. When ripe (*hinog*), it's the sweet, distinct flavor in your halo-halo or turon. It's huge, sticky when you prep it, and has a smell that you either love or hate—no in-between. Vegans now call it "pulled pork," we've been calling it *ulam* for centuries.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong sahog sa halo-halo ang matamis na **langka**.","translation":"My favorite ingredient in halo-halo is sweet **jackfruit**."},{"sentence":"Nag-ulam kami ng ginataang **langka** kaninang tanghali.","translation":"We had **jackfruit** in coconut milk for lunch today."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang partikular na paksa o yunit ng pag-aaral na itinuturo sa isang klase o kurso.
etymology: From the root 'aral' with the suffix '-in', which can denote an object or a noun form of the action.
original_explanation: This is the specific 'topic' or 'chapter' in your textbook. If 'aral' is the general wisdom, 'aralin' is Chapter 5: The Krebs Cycle, which you'll probably forget after the test. It's the concrete stuff you have to memorize for school or work.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'leksyon'. It can also be a verb form meaning 'to study something' (e.g., 'Aralin mo ito').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **aralin** natin para sa araw na ito ay tungkol sa kasaysayan ng Pilipinas.","translation":"Our **lesson** for today is about the history of the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Mahirap intindihin ang huling **aralin** sa matematika.","translation":"The last math **lesson** was hard to understand."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kulay na tulad ng sa mga dahon at damo; luntian.
original_explanation: The old-school, poetic way to say 'green.' You'd find this in a Florante at Laura-type text, not in a group chat deciding on a color palette. It's the color of nature, envy, and sometimes, money. Basically, the more formal, less common cousin of 'berde'.
usage_notes: Largely replaced by 'luntian' or the Spanish-derived 'berde' in modern usage. Considered very poetic or archaic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bukirin ay nababalot sa **lungting** kulay.","translation":"The field is covered in a **green** color."},{"sentence":"Napakasarap pagmasdan ng **lungting** kapaligiran.","translation":"It is so wonderful to look at the **green** environment."}]

translation: to grant a request; to accept an invitation
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtugon o pagbibigay-pabor sa isang pakiusap, anyaya, o hiling.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of that classy invitation. When you 'paunlakan' something, you're graciously saying yes. It's not just "Okay, game." It's "I would be honored to attend." Parang 'pag in-invite ka ng crush mo, you don't just say 'sige', you say "Salamat sa pag-anyaya, siyempre, darating ako!" That's the energy of 'paunlakan'.
usage_notes: A very formal verb. Used to show respect and grace when accepting an invitation or granting a favor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay **paunlakan** ninyo ang aming paanyaya na maging ninong at ninang.","translation":"We hope you will **grant** our request to be the godparents."},{"sentence":"Malugod naming pinasasalamatan ang lahat na **nagpaunlak** sa aming imbitasyon.","translation":"We sincerely thank everyone who **accepted** our invitation."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sandata na yari sa nababaluktot na piraso ng kahoy o ibang materyales na pinag-ugnay ng isang tali sa magkabilang dulo, ginagamit upang magpakawala ng pana.
original_explanation: The OG weapon before guns were a thing. Think Katniss Everdeen in The Hunger Games, or Hawkeye from the Avengers. It's the 'B' in 'B & A' (Bow and Arrow). Not to be confused with the feeling of being full after a buffet, which has a different stress on the syllable (`bu-SOG`). This one is `/BU-sog/`.
usage_notes: The pronunciation is key to distinguish it from 'busog' (full). Here, the stress is on the first syllable: /BU-sog/.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga katutubo ay sanay gumamit ng **busog** at pana para mangaso.","translation":"The indigenous people are skilled at using a **bow** and arrow for hunting."},{"sentence":"Niregaluhan siya ng isang magandang **busog** para sa kanyang pagsasanay sa archery.","translation":"She was gifted a beautiful **bow** for her archery training."}]

translation: will go fishing (with a hook and line)
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghuli ng isda gamit ang bingwit o pamingwit sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: The future tense of your lolo's favorite weekend activity. Or, in modern terms, 'mamimingwit ng chismis' – fishing for gossip. 'Mamimingwit ng compliments' – posting a fire selfie and waiting for the likes and comments to roll in.
usage_notes: Future tense of 'mamingwit'. Specifically refers to fishing with a rod, hook, and line, as opposed to a net.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa Sabado, **mamimingwit** kami sa ilog kasama si Lolo.","translation":"On Saturday, we **will go fishing** at the river with Grandpa."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **mamimingwit** ng isda para sa ating hapunan?","translation":"Who **will fish** (with a line) for our dinner?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maging sanhi ng pagbigat o pagbagal ng daloy ng mga sasakyan sa isang kalsada o daanan.
original_explanation: This is what happens when a jeepney decides to load/unload passengers in the middle of the road, a car breaks down on EDSA during rush hour, or when everyone suddenly decides to go to the mall at the same time. It's the universe's way of telling you, 'You should have left earlier... or just stayed home and watched Netflix.' The verb form of the noun we all love to hate.
usage_notes: While 'trapik' (noun) is extremely common, the verb form 'magtrapik' is less common but understood. It's more common to say 'nagkakatraffic' (traffic is building up) or 'nakaka-traffic' (causes traffic).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang huminto diyan, **magtratrapik** ka lang.","translation":"Don't stop there, you'll just **cause traffic**."},{"sentence":"Ang aksidente sa C5 ay siguradong **magtratrapik** nang malala.","translation":"The accident on C5 will surely **cause** severe **traffic**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay na pagtawa ng isang grupo ng mga tao bilang tugon sa isang bagay na nakakatuwa.
original_explanation: The sound of a good barkada, a funny meme being passed around, or your family watching a Vice Ganda movie. It's that moment when everyone just gets the joke and erupts in laughter. The opposite of a corporate meeting.
usage_notes: A reciprocal verb implying a group of people laughing at the same time or at each other's jokes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula silang **magtawanan** nang marinig ang nakakatawang kwento ni Lolo.","translation":"They started to **laugh together** when they heard Grandpa's funny story."},{"sentence":"Ang sarap pakinggan kapag ang buong pamilya ay **nagtawanan** sa sala.","translation":"It's so nice to hear when the whole family is **laughing together** in the living room."}]

translation: to act like an expert; to specialize
meaning_filipino: Kumilos o magsalita na parang isang dalubhasa sa isang partikular na larangan; maging bihasa.
original_explanation: That one friend who watches a single YouTube tutorial and suddenly starts giving everyone unsolicited advice like they've been doing it for years. "Huwag kang magpakaeksperto kung isang beses mo pa lang naman 'yan nagawa." It can mean to actually become an expert, but it's often used for someone *pretending* to be one.
usage_notes: Can be used to mean genuinely striving to be an expert or sarcastically for someone acting like a know-it-all.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magpakaeksperto** sa iyong napiling propesyon.","translation":"You need to **specialize** in your chosen profession."},{"sentence":"Kakapanood lang niya ng isang documentary, **nagpakaeksperto** na agad sa pulitika.","translation":"He just watched one documentary and he's already **acting like an expert** in politics."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang unang pampublikong pagpapakilala o paglabas ng isang tao, lalo na ng isang dalaga sa lipunan sa kaniyang ika-18 kaarawan, o ng isang artista.
etymology: Mula sa Pranses na 'début', na nangangahulugang 'unang pagganap'.
original_explanation: That magical 18th birthday party that's basically a Pinoy Met Gala. It's the one night you're a certified princess, complete with 18 roses, 18 candles, and 18 treasures. The budget for this can range from 'merienda with friends' to 'a down payment for a condo.'
usage_notes: Commonly refers to a girl's 18th birthday celebration in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinaghahandaan na ng pamilya ang engrandeng **debut** ni Liza.","translation":"The family is preparing for Liza's grand **debut**."},{"sentence":"Naging matagumpay ang **debut** album ng bagong banda.","translation":"The new band's **debut** album was successful."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piyesa ng musika na binubuo ng mga pinagdugtong-dugtong na bahagi mula sa iba't ibang kanta.
original_explanation: The ultimate "throwback" weapon in a singing contest or family karaoke night. It's when you can't decide on just one Sharon Cuneta or Regine Velasquez song, so you sing a little bit of ALL of them. The transitions can be awkward, but the nostalgia hit is 100% guaranteed.
usage_notes: Primarily used in a musical context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghanda sila ng isang OPM **medley** para sa kanilang production number.","translation":"They prepared an OPM **medley** for their production number."},{"sentence":"Ang galing ng pagkakadugtong ng mga kanta sa **medley** na iyon.","translation":"The transition between the songs in that **medley** was so good."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkuskos sa isang bagay upang ito ay kuminis at kumintab.
original_explanation: What you do to a wooden floor with a 'bunot' (coconut husk) to make it shiny and slippery. Or polishing your shoes before going to the office to look professional even if you're sleep-deprived. It's all about making things shiny.
usage_notes: Often associated with floors (especially wooden ones), shoes, or metal objects.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan si Totoy na **magbuli** ng sahig.","translation":"Totoy was instructed to **polish** the floor."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **magbuli** ng kanyang mga sapatos na katad.","translation":"He likes to **polish** his leather shoes."}]

translation: to inculcate; to instill; to open one's eyes to
meaning_filipino: Ituro o ikintal sa isipan ng isang tao, lalo na mula sa pagkabata, upang maging bahagi ng kanyang kamalayan o paniniwala.
etymology: From i- (causative prefix) + pa- (causative prefix) + mulat (awake, aware).
original_explanation: This is what your parents try to do when they teach you values, or what a 'woke' friend does when they introduce you to a social issue. It's about opening someone's eyes to a reality or a certain way of thinking. Like when you finally realized that 'adulting' is a trap. That's the moment it was ipinamulat to you.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of teaching values, principles, or awareness from a young age or to a naive person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalagang **ipamulat** sa mga bata ang paggalang sa nakatatanda.","translation":"It's important **to instill** in children respect for the elderly."},{"sentence":"Ang kahirapan ang **nagpamulat** sa kanya sa tunay na kalagayan ng lipunan.","translation":"Poverty is what **opened his eyes to** the true state of society."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong dalubhasa sa larangan ng batas; isang eksperto sa pag-aaral, pagpapaliwanag, o paglikha ng batas.
original_explanation: Not just your everyday "Attorney!". A dalub-batas is the final boss of lawyers. They don't just argue cases; they write the books that other lawyers study. They're the ones who can find a loophole in your condo's "no pets" policy by citing a 19th-century provincial decree. Level 99 Abogado.
usage_notes: More formal and profound than `abogado` (lawyer/attorney). It implies a deep, scholarly understanding of the law itself, not just its practice.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinonsulta ng senado ang isang **dalub-batas** para sa bagong panukala.","translation":"The senate consulted a **jurist** for the new bill."},{"sentence":"Si Jose P. Laurel ay isang tanyag na **dalub-batas** sa kasaysayan ng Pilipinas.","translation":"Jose P. Laurel is a famous **legal expert** in Philippine history."}]

meaning_filipino: May mababang temperatura; hindi mainit. Maaari ring tumukoy sa kawalan ng sigla o pagmamahal.
original_explanation: The weather in Baguio. The halo-halo you crave on a hot day. The feeling you get from your partner when they're mad at you and give you the silent treatment. It's the absence of heat, literally and figuratively.
usage_notes: Can describe temperature, food, or a person's demeanor (unenthusiastic, unaffectionate).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Malamig** ang panahon ngayong Disyembre.","translation":"The weather is **cold** this December."},{"sentence":"Naging **malamig** ang pakikitungo niya sa akin pagkatapos ng aming pag-aaway.","translation":"His treatment of me became **cold** after our argument."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o pagawaan kung saan ang mga troso ay pinuputol at ginagawang tabla o iba pang kagamitang yari sa kahoy gamit ang mga lagari.
original_explanation: It's the place that smells like sawdust and fresh-cut wood. Where big logs go in and come out as dos-por-dos and plyboard. The home of the maglalagari (sawmill worker) and the source of your wooden furniture's ancestors.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala ang mga bagong putol na puno sa **lagarian**.","translation":"The newly cut trees were brought to the **sawmill**."},{"sentence":"Maraming manggagawa sa **lagarian** sa aming probinsya.","translation":"There are many workers in the **lumberyard** in our province."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pabalat o sisidlan, karaniwang gawa sa karton o plastik, na ginagamit upang itago at ayusin ang mga papel, dokumento, o sulatin.
original_explanation: The unsung hero of every student and office worker. This is where your thesis drafts, birth certificates, and unpaid Meralco bills go to live together in (dis)harmony. It comes in many colors, usually brown or a sad-looking manila, and is the physical manifestation of 'I'll get to this later.'
usage_notes: The 'F' sound is often replaced with 'P' in casual Filipino speech. "Folder" is also commonly used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakilagay ang lahat ng resibo sa loob ng asul na **polder**.","translation":"Please put all the receipts inside the blue **folder**."},{"sentence":"Nawawala ang **polder** na naglalaman ng aking mga grado.","translation":"The **folder** containing my grades is missing."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pag-unawa sa kahulugan ng mga nakasulat o nakalimbag na salita at simbolo.
original_explanation: The thing you're supposed to do with the Terms & Conditions but you just scroll down and click "Agree." Also, the low-key flex of finishing a book in one sitting.
usage_notes: Pronunciation is key to distinguish this from the act of getting wet, which has a different stress.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagbasa** ay nagpapalawak ng kaalaman.","translation":"**Reading** expands knowledge."},{"sentence":"Nahihirapan siya sa **pagbasa** ng sulat-kamay ng doktor.","translation":"He has difficulty **reading** the doctor's handwriting."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay o palitang pag-kagat ng dalawa o higit pang tao o hayop. Ang akto ng pag-aaway gamit ang mga ngipin.
original_explanation: The plural form of 'kagat' in action. Think two dogs fighting, or you and your siblings fighting over the last piece of chicharon. It's a mutual biting frenzy. 'Nagkagatan ang mga aso sa kalye.' It can also be used figuratively for intense arguments. 'Para silang nagkakagatan sa board meeting.'
usage_notes: A reciprocal verb form. Often implies conflict or a shared, sometimes competitive, act of eating.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag ninyong hayaang mag-**kagatan** ang mga alagang aso.","translation":"Don't let the pet dogs **bite each other**."},{"sentence":"Nag-**kagatan** ang mga bata sa iisang piraso ng mangga.","translation":"The children **competitively bit** at the single piece of mango."}]

meaning_filipino: Gumawa ng butas sa lupa o sa anumang ibabaw sa pamamagitan ng pag-aalis ng materyal.
original_explanation: What you do when you're looking for buried treasure, planting a tree, or trying to find old *chismis* on someone's social media profile from 2010. It's the act of digging, literally or figuratively. 'Huwag mo nang hukayin ang nakaraan!' (Don't dig up the past!)
usage_notes: Past tense of the verb. Infinitive is 'humukay', present is 'humuhukay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Humukay** ang aso sa hardin para itago ang buto.","translation":"The dog **dug** in the garden to hide its bone."},{"sentence":"Sila ay **humukay** ng balon bilang mapagkukunan ng tubig.","translation":"They **dug** a well as a source of water."}]

translation: hotel; motel (often with a connotation of a short-time stay)
meaning_filipino: Isang gusali na nag-aalok ng pansamantalang tuluyan na may bayad; karaniwang ginagamit na may konotasyon ng panandaliang paglagi o 'short-time'.
original_explanation: The Filipinized spelling of 'hotel'. While it can mean a regular hotel, it's more often used as a euphemism for a motel, the kind with the "themed" rooms and the 3-hour stay promos. The place you check into, not check out of. *wink wink*
usage_notes: Ang baybay na 'otel' ay may dalang mas kolokyal, at madalas na may pahiwatig, na tono kaysa sa 'hotel'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghanap sila ng murang **otel** para sa tatlong oras.","translation":"They looked for a cheap **motel** for three hours."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang isama sa social media post mo na sa **otel** kayo nag-check in.","translation":"Don't include in your social media post that you checked into a **motel**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglanghap at pagbuga ng singaw na nililikha ng isang electronic cigarette o katulad na aparato. Tumutukoy din sa mismong aparato.
original_explanation: The new-gen yosi. Instead of smoke, you get clouds of fruity, candy-smelling vapor. "Nag-vape" is the act, the "vape" is the device. It's the thing your tito who "quit smoking" is now doing, producing clouds thick enough to cause a low-visibility warning.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun (the device) or a verb (the action, often as 'mag-vape').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bawal mag-**vape** sa loob ng mall.","translation":"It's forbidden to **vape** inside the mall."},{"sentence":"Nawala ko ang **vape** ko kagabi.","translation":"I lost my **vape** last night."}]

translation: So that's the game; So that's your play
meaning_filipino: Isang modernong ekspresyon na ginagamit upang ipahiwatig ang pagkaunawa o pagkabunyag sa totoong plano, motibo, o 'diskarte' ng isang tao, kadalasan sa paraang may halong sarkasmo.
etymology: Combination of English loanword 'gamer' and Filipino slang 'yarn' (a stylized, often gay lingo, version of 'iyan').
original_explanation: When you finally figure out someone's hidden agenda or 'diskarte.' It's like saying, 'Ah, so that's your strategy!' Usually said with a mix of sarcasm, amusement, or mock surprise. Example: Your friend keeps being extra nice, then asks for a favor. You look at them and say, '**Gamer yarn**?' (So that's your game, huh?).
usage_notes: A very current internet/meme slang expression. 'Yarn' is a playful pronunciation of 'iyan' (that), popularized in online Filipino communities and gay lingo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-offer siyang ilibre ako, tapos nagpapatulong pala sa assignment. **Gamer yarn**?","translation":"He offered to treat me, but it turns out he just needed help with his assignment. **So that's the game**, huh?"},{"sentence":"Akala ko totoo, 'yun pala dare lang. **Gamer yarn**!","translation":"I thought it was real, but it was just a dare. **What a play**!"}]

translation: to be on fire, to burn; to be filled with passion
meaning_filipino: Ang literal na pagliliyab o pagkakaroon ng apoy. Sa matalinhagang paraan, ito ay tumutukoy sa matinding damdamin tulad ng galit, pag-ibig, o determinasyon.
original_explanation: Can be literal, like "OMG, the toaster is starting to mag-apoy!" Or it can be figurative, like when your crush walks by and your heart starts to mag-apoy. It's also that look in the eyes of an athlete before a championship game. It's fire, literally or emotionally. Pwedeng kilig, pwedeng galit.
usage_notes: Has both a literal meaning (to catch fire) and a common figurative meaning (to burn with emotion).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **mag-apoy** ang tuyong damuhan dahil sa matinding sikat ng araw.","translation":"The dry grass started **to catch fire** because of the intense heat of the sun."},{"sentence":"Dapat **mag-apoy** ang iyong puso sa pagnanais na makamit ang iyong mga pangarap.","translation":"Your heart must **burn with passion** in the desire to achieve your dreams."}]

translation: to become sour; to turn sour
meaning_filipino: Magbago ang lasa ng isang bagay tungo sa pagiging maasim, karaniwang dahil sa permentasyon o pagkasira.
original_explanation: What happens to your sinigang when you add more sampaloc mix. Also, what happens to your face when you see your ex with a new partner. Figuratively, it's when a good situation or relationship goes bad. 'Umasim na ang samahan nila.'
usage_notes: Used literally for food and drinks, and figuratively for relationships, moods, or situations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong iwan sa labas ang gatas at baka **umasim**.","translation":"Don't leave the milk outside or it might **turn sour**."},{"sentence":"**Umasim** ang mukha niya nang marinig ang balita.","translation":"His face **soured** when he heard the news."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hindi kanais-nais na sitwasyon o pangyayari na itinuturing na bunga ng tadhana o pagkakataon.
original_explanation: When the universe just isn't on your side. You studied for the wrong exam, your Grab driver cancelled, and your crush just got engaged. That's not just a bad day, that's 'masamang kapalaran'. It's when you feel like the main character of a tragic teleserye.
usage_notes: Refers to a series of unfortunate events or a general state of bad luck, often with a sense of fate or destiny involved.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tila sinusundan ako ng **masamang kapalaran** ngayong linggo.","translation":"It seems **misfortune** has been following me this week."},{"sentence":"Ang pagkawala ng kanyang trabaho ay isang **masamang kapalaran** na hindi niya inaasahan.","translation":"Losing his job was a **misfortune** that he did not expect."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang krus na may nakapakong imahen ni Hesukristo.
original_explanation: The OG religious bling. It's the cross with Jesus on it, usually seen hanging on walls in Filipino homes, worn as a necklace, or held by priests. It's not just a cross; it's the *story* of the cross.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa kontekstong panrelihiyon, lalo na sa Katolisismo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May malaking **krusipiho** na nakasabit sa itaas ng kanilang pinto.","translation":"There is a large **crucifix** hanging above their door."},{"sentence":"Mahigpit niyang hinawakan ang kanyang **krusipiho** habang nagdarasal.","translation":"She tightly held her **crucifix** while praying."}]

translation: to oppose, to contradict, to go against
meaning_filipino: Pagkilos o pagpapahayag ng pagtutol, pagkontra, o hindi pagsang-ayon sa isang tao, ideya, o patakaran.
original_explanation: This is your inner "kontrabida" coming out. When your parents tell you to clean your room but you binge-watch Netflix instead, that's you *sumalungat*-ing. It's the classic act of defiance, like telling your TL you can't render OT because you have "plans" (which is to sleep).
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of debate, rebellion, or simple disagreement. The prefix 'sum-' indicates an actor-focus verb in the past or completed tense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumalungat** siya sa desisyon ng kanyang mga magulang na mag-abroad.","translation":"He **went against** his parents' decision for him to work abroad."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **sumalungat** sa agos ng buhay, minsan kailangan mo lang mag-adjust.","translation":"Don't **go against** the flow of life, sometimes you just need to adjust."}]

meaning_filipino: Iaalay, ipagkakaloob, o iaabot ang isang bagay sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: The future tense of generosity (or obligation). This is you promising 'I will give you a treat' on payday, the company announcing it 'will give a 13th-month pay,' or a politician promising they 'will give jobs.' It's a word full of hope, promises, and sometimes, 'sana totoo.'
usage_notes: This is the future tense of 'magbigay' (to give).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pamahalaan ay **magbibigay** ng tulong sa mga nasalanta ng bagyo.","translation":"The government **will give** aid to those affected by the typhoon."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **magbibigay** ng pambungad na pananalita sa programa?","translation":"Who **will give** the opening remarks for the program?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng baboy na nasa hustong gulang, lalo na ang isa na nanganak na ng mga biik.
etymology: Combination of 'inahin' (female animal used for breeding, from 'ina') and 'baboy' (pig).
original_explanation: The original matriarch, the queen of the pig pen. She's the source of all the cute little biik that eventually become our beloved lechon and sisig. In human terms, it's sometimes used (not very nicely) to refer to the head of a household or a group who is... well, large and in charge.
usage_notes: A compound noun. 'Inahin' by itself refers to a mother animal of any species (e.g., inahing manok - mother hen).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malusog ang mga biik dahil masustansya ang gatas ng **inahing baboy**.","translation":"The piglets are healthy because the **sow's** milk is nutritious."},{"sentence":"Ibinenta sa palengke ang matabang **inahing baboy**.","translation":"The fat **sow** was sold at the market."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tunog na nalilikha ng isang bagay na malutong kapag kinakain, o ng isang bagay na luma o mahina kapag nagagalaw, tulad ng sahig na kawayan.
original_explanation: This is the ASMR of Filipino snacks. It's the satisfying *langutngot* of chicharon, kropek, or crispy pata. It's the sound of success! On the other hand, it can also be the creepy *langutngot* of your wooden stairs at 3 AM when you're home alone. Choose your *langutngot* wisely.
usage_notes: An onomatopoeic word that can refer to the sound of eating crispy food or the creaking of materials like wood or bamboo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Rinig na rinig ang **langutngot** ng chicharon habang kinakain niya.","translation":"The **crunching sound** of the pork rinds could be clearly heard while he was eating."},{"sentence":"May narinig akong **langutngot** mula sa lumang sahig.","translation":"I heard a **creaking sound** from the old floor."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaiba o pagbabago sa pagitan ng dalawang bagay, lalo na sa konteksto ng matematika, agham, o negosyo.
etymology: From the Greek letter Δ (delta), used in math and science to denote change.
original_explanation: Sa BPO at corporate world, 'pag sinabing "What's the delta?", ang ibig sabihin ay "Ano ang pinagkaiba?" o "Ano ang kulang?". Hindi ito 'yung airline o ilog sa Egypt. It's corporate-speak for 'the difference'.
usage_notes: Primarily used in corporate, IT, or BPO settings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **delta** sa pagitan ng target sales at actual sales natin para sa quarter na ito?","translation":"What's the **delta** between our target sales and actual sales for this quarter?"},{"sentence":"We need to analyze the **delta** to understand the performance gap.","translation":"Kailangan nating suriin ang **pagkakaiba** para maunawaan ang pagkukulang sa performance."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang nababaluktot na kordong de-kuryente na may plug sa isang dulo at saksakan sa kabilang dulo, ginagamit upang mapahaba ang abot ng isang de-kuryenteng kasangkapan.
etymology: Hiram na parirala mula sa Ingles na 'extension cord'.
original_explanation: The unsung hero of every Pinoy household and office. Ito 'yung nagliligtas sa'yo kapag ang layo ng saksakan sa pwesto mo. The real MVP during group projects, thesis nights, at sa mga coffee shop na iisa lang ang outlet. Life-saver, 'di ba? Also known as just 'extension'.
usage_notes: Madalas na tinatawag na 'extension' na lamang sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakihiram nga ng **extension cord**, hindi abot ang charger ko.","translation":"Can I borrow the **extension cord**, my charger can't reach."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa sobrang paggamit ng **extension cord** dahil maaaring maging sanhi ito ng sunog.","translation":"Be careful with overloading the **extension cord** because it can cause a fire."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pag-aalinlangan o kawalan ng katiyakan sa paggawa ng isang desisyon o kilos.
etymology: From `pag-` (gerund prefix) + `a` (euphonic liaison) + reduplication of the first syllable of the root `atubili`.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're about to send a risky text and your thumb hovers over the 'send' button for five minutes. It's the "should I or shouldn't I?" moment, the internal debate before you finally decide to either go for it or 'seen-zone' the opportunity. Parang 'yung crush mo, puro pag-aatubili, hindi ka tuloy ma-chat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **pag-aatubili**, naunahan na siya ng iba.","translation":"Because of his **hesitation**, others got ahead of him."},{"sentence":"Walang **pag-aatubili** niyang tinanggap ang alok na trabaho.","translation":"He accepted the job offer without **hesitation**."}]

translation: to break free; to escape from a hold
meaning_filipino: Ang makawala o makalaya mula sa pagkakatali, pagkakahawak, o anumang pumipigil.
original_explanation: This is the feeling when you finally get out of a crowded MRT train at your station. It's the fish escaping the net, the employee finally resigning from a toxic job, or you escaping your tita's interrogation about your love life during a family reunion. It’s a sudden, successful escape from a tight grip.
usage_notes: Implies escaping from a physical restraint or a difficult situation through a struggle.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng isda na **mahulagpos** mula sa lambat.","translation":"The fish tried **to break free** from the net."},{"sentence":"Sa wakas ay **nakahulagpos** siya sa masamang relasyon.","translation":"She was finally able **to escape** from the bad relationship."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sakramento sa Simbahang Katoliko kung saan ipinapahayag ng isang tao ang kanyang mga kasalanan sa isang pari upang makamit ang kapatawaran mula sa Diyos.
original_explanation: That moment in the church booth where you tell the priest all the tea, but it's about your own sins. It's like a spiritual 'Spill the tea' session, but with penance at the end instead of likes and shares. Also used figuratively for any dramatic admission of guilt, like finally admitting to your mom you're the one who broke her favorite vase.
usage_notes: Primarily used in a religious (Catholic) context. The verb form is 'magkumpisal' (to confess).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghihintay ang mga tao para sa kanilang pagkakataong mag-**Kumpisal** bago mag-Pasko.","translation":"The people were waiting for their turn for **Confession** before Christmas."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang liham ay parang isang **kumpisal** ng lahat ng kanyang pagkakamali.","translation":"His letter was like a **confession** of all his mistakes."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabago sa kalagayan ng isang likido patungo sa pagiging mas malapot o makapal.
etymology: From the root word 'lapot' (thickness, viscosity) + the '-um-' infix for verbs.
original_explanation: 'Yung gravy sa fast food na iniwan mo lang saglit, pagbalik mo, parang semento na. 'Yan, lumapot na. O kaya 'yung usapan niyo ng ex mo, nagsimula sa "kamusta," tapos biglang lumapot at naging seryoso. From liquid to solid real quick.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lumapot** na ang sarsa habang ito'y niluluto.","translation":"The sauce **thickened** as it was being cooked."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **lumapot** ang dugo sa isip mo; magpatawad ka na.","translation":"Don't let bad blood **thicken** in your mind; just forgive."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdanas ng matinding kalungkutan, pighati, o dalamhati.
original_explanation: This isn't just 'sad.' This is 'sana all chibog, pero ako lugmok' level of sadness. It's the deep, heavy feeling you get after a major loss, a breakup that hits different, or when you realize your SSS contributions won't be enough for retirement. It's a formal, almost poetic kind of sorrow. The OG 'sana'y di na lang' feeling.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pandiwa na naglalarawan sa kilos ng pagdaramdam o pang-uri na naglalarawan sa isang kalagayan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nahahapis** ang buong pamilya sa pagpanaw ng kanilang lola.","translation":"The whole family is **grieving** the passing of their grandmother."},{"sentence":"Isang **nahahapis** na ina ang humarap sa media.","translation":"A **sorrowful** mother faced the media."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglilinis gamit ang tubig at sabon sa hinaharap. Ito ang aspektong kontemplatibo ng pandiwang 'hugas'.
original_explanation: The national sport of every Filipino household after a fiesta. "Sino'ng maghuhugas ng pinggan?" is a question that can start a family feud. It's the future tense of your designated chore.
usage_notes: Commonly refers to washing dishes ('maghugas ng pinggan') or hands ('maghugas ng kamay').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ako na ang **maghuhugas** ng mga pinagkainan natin.","translation":"I **will wash** the dishes we used."},{"sentence":"Lagi kang **maghuhugas** ng kamay para makaiwas sa sakit.","translation":"You should always **wash** your hands to avoid getting sick."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglikha ng tupi sa isang bagay; tiklupin.
original_explanation: The chore you probably hate the most after laundry day. It's the act of making your clothes look presentable for the closet, only for you to mess them up again the next day looking for an outfit. 'Pakisuyo, tupiin mo na ang mga sinampay.'
usage_notes: Synonymous with 'tiklupin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **tupiin** nang maayos ang mga damit.","translation":"You need **to fold** the clothes neatly."},{"sentence":"Puwede mo bang **tupiin** ang papel na ito sa gitna?","translation":"Can you **fold** this paper in the middle?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng pagiging hindi normal o sapat ang paglaki o pag-unlad; maliit at hindi lumaki nang maayos.
original_explanation: The word moms use to scare you into drinking your milk or eating your vegetables. It means you didn't grow properly. It's not just short, it's *stunted*. Parang 'yung halaman na hindi naarawan at nadiligan, or 'yung career mo pag laging kang "seen-zoned" sa job applications.
usage_notes: Often used to describe people, animals, or plants. Can be considered offensive when used for people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **bansot** ang paglaki ng halaman dahil sa kakulangan sa sikat ng araw.","translation":"The plant's growth was **stunted** due to lack of sunlight."},{"sentence":"Pinayuhan ng doktor ang ina na pakainin nang tama ang anak upang hindi maging **bansot**.","translation":"The doctor advised the mother to feed her child properly so he won't be **stunted** in growth."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang namuong taba o mantika mula sa karne na lumalamig; maaari ring tumukoy sa mamantikang dumi sa balat o sa mga kagamitan.
original_explanation: That stubborn, solidified grease on your plate after eating adobo or sinigang that requires industrial-strength dishwashing liquid and hot water to remove. Also, the stuff that clogs your pores. Basically, the enemy of both clean dishes and clear skin.
usage_notes: Commonly refers to the hardened, often white, fat residue on cooled dishes or unwashed plates.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang hirap tanggalin ng **sebo** sa mga plato kapag malamig na tubig ang gamit.","translation":"It's hard to remove the **grease** from plates when using cold water."},{"sentence":"Puno ng **sebo** ang kawali pagkatapos magprito ng bacon.","translation":"The pan was full of **solidified fat** after frying bacon."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng tasa na may mga marka o sukat, ginagamit sa pagtakal ng mga sangkap sa pagluluto o pagbe-bake, tulad ng harina o likido.
etymology: Direct loan phrase from English "measuring cup".
original_explanation: That kitchen tool you can never find when you need it, so you just end up using a random coffee mug and hoping for the best. This is why your pandesal sometimes comes out as hard as a rock. In the hands of a lola, any 'tabo' or 'tasa' can be a measuring cup. The ancestors guide their measurements.
usage_notes: The English term is used almost exclusively. The Tagalog equivalent "panakal na tasa" is very rare.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gamitin mo ang **measuring cup** para eksakto ang sukat ng asukal.","translation":"Use the **measuring cup** so the measurement of the sugar is exact."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi maaaring pasinungalingan o itanggi; isang katotohanang hindi matututulan.
original_explanation: That CCTV footage of you sneaking a piece of cake from the office fridge at 3 AM? 'Yan ang ebidensyang di-mapabubulaanan. It's the ultimate "gotcha" moment, the solid proof that leaves no room for excuses. Resibo, kumbaga.
usage_notes: Isang pormal at matatag na salita na ginagamit upang bigyang-diin ang ganap na katotohanan o katiyakan ng isang bagay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagmamahal ng isang ina ay isang katotohanang **di-mapabubulaanan**.","translation":"A mother's love is an **undeniable** truth."},{"sentence":"May mga ebidensya siyang **di-mapabubulaanan** laban sa akusado.","translation":"He has **irrefutable** evidence against the accused."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal at magalang na tawag sa isang amo o sa isang taong may mataas na katungkulan o awtoridad.
etymology: From English "boss" + Filipino suffix "-ing" (often used for endearment or colloquialism).
original_explanation: The slightly more endearing, sometimes more *sipsip* version of 'boss'. It's what you call your actual boss when you're trying to be friendly, or what you call Vic Sotto. It has a lighter, more familiar feel than the straightforward 'boss'.
usage_notes: Primarily colloquial. Can be used for one's actual superior or as a general respectful term of address.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sabi ni **Bossing**, kailangan na nating tapusin ang report ngayon.","translation":"**The boss** said we need to finish the report today."},{"sentence":"Uy, **Bossing**! Kamusta na? Long time no see!","translation":"Hey, **Boss**! How are you? Long time no see!"}]

meaning_filipino: Kasama o bahagi ng isang pangkat o kabuuan.
original_explanation: This is the word for being 'in the group.' You're kabilang sa team, kabilang sa pamilya, or kabilang sa mga single ngayong Pasko. It’s the opposite of being 'OP' (out of place). It's the feeling of belonging, or at least, being counted.
usage_notes: Can function as a verb (to be included) or an adjective (belonging to).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay **kabilang** sa mga pinakamahuhusay na mag-aaral.","translation":"She is **among** the best students."},{"sentence":"Hindi ako **kabilang** sa listahan ng mga inimbitahan.","translation":"I am not **included** in the list of invitees."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang kaalaman o kamalayan sa isang partikular na bagay; inosente sa isang negatibong paraan.
original_explanation: That friend who's always the last one to get the joke. 'Yung tipong tapos na ang tawanan ng buong barkada, saka pa lang siya magtatanong, 'Ha? Ano 'yun?'. It's not about being unintelligent, but being hilariously out of the loop. Like living on airplane mode while everyone else is on 5G.
usage_notes: A Bisaya loanword that has gained some usage in Manila, especially among younger generations. It carries a slightly playful, less harsh connotation than 'bobo' or 'tanga'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **muang**, halata namang may gusto siya sa'yo.","translation":"Don't be **clueless**, it's obvious he/she likes you."},{"sentence":"Tawa kami nang tawa pero si Ana, **muang** pa rin sa nangyayari.","translation":"We were all laughing but Ana was still **clueless** about what was happening."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pandiwa na tumutukoy sa lugar o bahay na kasalukuyang pinanahanan o pinananatili ng isang tao o pamilya.
original_explanation: The place where you live. Your "address" when you're filling out a form, or the place your Grab driver is trying to find. It's the "where" in "where you at?". From the root word "tira" (to live/reside).
usage_notes: Often used to ask for or state an address. In a different context, from the root word 'tira' (hit), it can also mean 'being hit by' something (e.g., 'tinitirahan ng bato' - being hit by stones), but the primary meaning is 'residing'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bahay na **tinitirahan** namin ay malapit sa palengke.","translation":"The house we are **living in** is near the market."},{"sentence":"Saan po ang kasalukuyan ninyong **tinitirahan**?","translation":"Where is your current **residence**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hindi makontrol at mabilis na paggalaw ng katawan, karaniwang dahil sa sakit, matinding emosyon, o pangingisay.
original_explanation: You see this when a fish is out of water. Or when your friend who can't handle spicy food tries the 'level 5' Bicol Express. It's a dramatic, uncontrolled movement, a physical reaction to extreme stimulus, be it pain, spice, or seeing your crush with someone else.
usage_notes: Often has a negative or painful connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkisay** ng isda sa sahig ay senyales na bago pa itong huli.","translation":"The **writhing** of the fish on the floor is a sign that it was freshly caught."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan nilang pakalmahin ang pasyente sa gitna ng **pagkisay** nito.","translation":"They tried to calm the patient in the middle of his **convulsion**."}]

meaning_filipino: Gamitin bilang kasangkapan sa pagputol o paghiwa ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: The designated slicer. That one specific knife in the kitchen that's super sharp and perfect for tomatoes. Or the credit card you use to slice your birthday cake when you forget a knife. It’s the tool for the job of cutting. 'Ito lang ang kutsilyo nating matalim, kaya ito ang ipanghiwa mo ng sibuyas.'
usage_notes: An instrumental verb. The focus is on the tool being used to perform the action of slicing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masyadong mapurol ang kutsilyong ito para **ipanghiwa** ng karne.","translation":"This knife is too dull **to use for slicing** meat."},{"sentence":"Mayroon ka bang gunting na pwedeng **ipanghiwa** ng karton?","translation":"Do you have scissors that can be **used to cut** cardboard?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kabilang sa pangkat-etniko ng mga Malay, na pangunahing naninirahan sa Timog-silangang Asya; tumutukoy din sa kanilang wika.
original_explanation: Our cousins in the neighborhood! The ones we share a lot of words, food, and maybe some ancient history with. When you hear 'Bahasa,' think Malay. They are our fellow Austronesians from Malaysia, Indonesia, Brunei, etc.
usage_notes: The word 'malay' (ma-LAY) as a noun is distinct from 'malay' (MA-lay) which means consciousness or awareness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming salitang Tagalog ang hiram sa wikang **Malay**.","translation":"Many Tagalog words are borrowed from the **Malay** language."},{"sentence":"Ang mga ninuno ng maraming Pilipino ay pinaniniwalaang mga **Malay**.","translation":"The ancestors of many Filipinos are believed to be **Malays**."}]

translation: to take under one's care; to shelter; to adopt
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkuha at pag-aaruga sa isang tao o hayop upang bigyan ng proteksyon, kalinga, at tirahan.
original_explanation: The verb form of that "ampon" energy. When you see a stray dog and you don't just feel sorry for it, you actually take it home, give it a bath, and name it Bantay. That's when you **kupkupin** it. It's an active gesture of compassion.
usage_notes: This is the action word for providing 'kupkop'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Balak nilang **kupkupin** ang mga batang kalye sa kanilang lugar.","translation":"They plan to **take under their care** the street children in their area."},{"sentence":"Pinili niyang **kupkupin** ang lahat ng pusang gala sa kanilang barangay.","translation":"He chose to **shelter** all the stray cats in their barangay."}]

meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng palaman ang isang bagay, tulad ng tinapay o empanada.
original_explanation: The action of adding the good stuff. It's what you tell your mom to do with your baon: 'Palamanan mo po ng marami!' It's the verb form of making something not-boring.
usage_notes: This is the command or instruction to add a filling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sige, **palamanan** mo na ng manok ang mga empanada.","translation":"Okay, go **put the chicken filling in** the empanadas now."}]

translation: to make a hole in; to pierce
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglikha ng butas sa isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pagtusok, pagputol, o pag-ukit.
original_explanation: This is what you do to your wall to hang a picture frame, or to your ear for that new piercing. It's the verb form of creating a 'butas'. In the context of chismis, "butasan ng kwento" is finding a loophole or inconsistency in someone's story. "Sige, magsinungaling ka pa, bubutasan ko lahat ng alibi mo."
usage_notes: An action word derived from the noun 'butas'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **butasan** ang pader para maisabit ang orasan.","translation":"You need to **make a hole in** the wall to hang the clock."},{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **butasan** ang kanyang tainga para sa hikaw.","translation":"She decided to **pierce** her ear for an earring."}]

translation: to be able to move; to cause to move or act
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang igalaw ang isang bagay o tao; maging dahilan upang kumilos o gumawa ng aksyon ang iba.
original_explanation: This is about getting something or someone to move, literally or figuratively. Like a manager trying to mapakilos their lazy team members to meet a deadline. Or that feeling when your crush smiles at you and bigla kang hindi makakilos (can't move). The `mapa-` prefix implies you successfully made it happen.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical movement or motivating someone to take action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **mapakilos** ang natumbang puno ngunit masyado itong mabigat.","translation":"He tried **to be able to move** the fallen tree but it was too heavy."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang talumpati ay sapat na upang **mapakilos** ang mga botante.","translation":"His speech was enough **to cause the voters to act**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gawain, bagay, o sitwasyon na hindi naaayon o salungat sa mga umiiral na batas ng isang lugar o bansa.
original_explanation: Basically, anything that's 'bawal'. From jaywalking to major crimes. Yung ginawa ng ex mo na kinuha ang hoodie mo at hindi na binalik? Hindi man 'labag sa batas', pero 'labag sa' international humanitarian law of relationships.
usage_notes: A common phrase used in news, legal documents, and everyday conversations about rules.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagbebenta ng pekeng produkto ay **labag sa batas**.","translation":"Selling fake products is **against the law**."},{"sentence":"Itinuturing na **labag sa batas** ang pagmamaneho nang lasing.","translation":"Drunk driving is considered **illegal**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga salita, pananalita, o pag-uugali na hindi pormal, itinuturing na "pang-kalye," o labas sa pamantayan ng wastong wika.
original_explanation: Describes language that isn't exactly textbook-Filipino. Think 'lodi', 'petmalu', 'werpa'. It's the language of the streets, of memes, of your cool tito. Can also mean a bit rough or unrefined, like describing someone's manners as 'mabalbal na ugali'.
usage_notes: "Balbal" itself is the noun for "slang word". "Mabalbal" is the adjective form describing something as being slangy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko maintindihan ang usapan nila dahil masyadong **mabalbal**.","translation":"I can't understand their conversation because it's too **slangy**."},{"sentence":"May mga salitang **mabalbal** na katanggap-tanggap na ngayon sa ilang usapan.","translation":"There are **colloquial** words that are now acceptable in some conversations."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan na ginagamit para luwagan o higpitan ang mga tornilyo.
original_explanation: Ito yung tool ni Tatay na laging nawawala 'pag kailangan mo. Ang life-saver pag mag-a-assemble ka ng IKEA furniture. May dalawang klase 'yan, parang sa chismis: flat-head (negative) at Phillips (positive).
usage_notes: The more common term is the English word "screwdriver".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiabot mo nga ang **distornilyador** para mahigpitan ko ang hawakan ng pinto.","translation":"Please hand me the **screwdriver** so I can tighten the doorknob."},{"sentence":"May flat-head at Phillips na **distornilyador** sa toolbox.","translation":"There are flat-head and Phillips **screwdrivers** in the toolbox."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panggitnang uri ng lipunan na binubuo ng mga propesyonal, mangangalakal, at may-ari ng maliliit na negosyo na may sapat at matatag na kita, na hindi maituturing na mahirap o mayaman.
original_explanation: You're middle class if you can afford a Samgyupsal dinner, a new phone on installment, and a Grab ride when it's raining, but you still check the price tag on everything and your blood pressure spikes when you see your Meralco bill. You have just enough to be comfortable but not enough to stop complaining. The sandwich generation's battleground.
usage_notes: The term is used directly in both English and Taglish. "Panggitnang uri" is the formal Filipino equivalent but is less common in casual conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming pangarap ang pamilyang **middle class**, tulad ng sariling bahay at kotse.","translation":"A **middle class** family has many dreams, like their own house and car."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang parirala na tumutukoy sa pinto mismo kasama ang balangkas o kuwadro nito na tinatawag na baskagan.
etymology: Combination of 'pinto' (door) and 'baskagan' (doorframe). 'Baskagan' is less common now, with 'hamba' being more frequently used.
original_explanation: This is some old-school construction lingo, like something your Lolo na karpintero would say. It's the complete door package deal: not just the part that swings, but also the frame it's attached to. The whole shebang.
usage_notes: This is a rare, almost archaic phrase. 'Hamba' is the more common term for doorframe today.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinusukat ng karpintero ang kabuuan ng **pinto o baskagan**.","translation":"The carpenter is measuring the entire **door and doorframe** assembly."},{"sentence":"Kasama sa kontrata ang pagpapalit ng lahat ng **pinto o baskagan** sa bahay.","translation":"The contract includes the replacement of all **doors and doorframes** in the house."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng alimango o talangka na mas maliit kaysa sa karaniwang alimasag.
original_explanation: It's a crab, but not the big, meaty alimango you're dreaming of for your ginataang version. A 'talipa' is a smaller type of crab. Think of it as the younger sibling in the crab family. You'd probably find this at a local wet market, but it's not as famous as its bigger cousins.
usage_notes: Specific to a type of crustacean, smaller than an 'alimango' or 'alimasag'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap daw gawing torta ang **talipa**.","translation":"They say it's delicious to make an omelette with **talipa** crab."},{"sentence":"Nagtitinda sila ng sariwang **talipa** sa palengke.","translation":"They sell fresh **talipa crabs** at the market."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang alagad ng sining na lumilikha ng mga anyo o pigura mula sa kahoy, bato, o iba pang materyales sa pamamagitan ng pag-ukit o paglilok.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'mang-' at ang salitang-ugat na 'lalik' (pag-ukit sa kahoy gamit ang torno), na may pag-uulit ng unang pantig ng ugat ('la').
original_explanation: The OG 3D printer, but with more skill and fewer error messages. A 'manlalalik' is an artist who carves things, turning a boring block of wood or stone into something beautiful, like those amazing sculptures in Paete, Laguna or the bulul figures of the Ifugao. They have the patience of a saint and the hands of a surgeon.
usage_notes: `Lalik` specifically refers to turning on a lathe or carving wood. `Manlililok` is a more general term for sculptor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala ang Paete, Laguna sa mga mahuhusay na **manlalalik**.","translation":"Paete, Laguna is known for its skilled **woodcarvers**."},{"sentence":"Isang obra maestra ang ginawa ng **manlalalik** na iyon.","translation":"That **sculptor** created a masterpiece."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, larawan, o anumang nilalaman na sadyang ginagamit upang pukawin ang matinding pagnanasa o atensyon mula sa iba, partikular sa social media.
etymology: Isang modernong slang na pariralang Ingles, na pinagsasama ang "thirst" (pagnanasa) at "bait" (pain).
original_explanation: The appetizer to the main course that is the 'thirst trap'. It's that subtle post—a gym mirror selfie where the bicep is *accidentally* flexed, or a beach pic that's *supposedly* about the sunset but is 90% abs. It’s designed to make people comment "Sana all" or slide into your DMs. It's calculated, it's strategic, it's modern-day fishing for compliments.
usage_notes: Madalas na ginagamit upang ilarawan ang isang post na hindi kasing-lantad ng isang 'thirst trap' ngunit may parehong layunin na makaakit ng atensyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-post siya ng litrato na nagbabasa ng libro habang naka-topless; halatang **thirst bait**.","translation":"He posted a picture of him reading a book while topless; it's obvious **thirst bait**."},{"sentence":"Ang galing niyang mag-post ng **thirst bait** na mukhang wholesome lang.","translation":"She's so good at posting **thirst bait** that just looks wholesome."}]

translation: to the limit; to the maximum extent
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pag-abot sa pinakadulo, pinakailalim, o sukdulang hangganan ng isang bagay o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: When you push the toothpaste tube until it's flatter than your wallet before payday. When you're so emotionally drained, you're "sagad na sagad." It's the feeling of hitting rock bottom or reaching the absolute end of the line, whether it's your patience, your phone's memory, or the last drop of coffee.
usage_notes: Often repeated as 'sagad-sagad' or used with 'hanggang' (hanggang sagad) to emphasize the limit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pindutin mo ang buton nang **sagad** para gumana.","translation":"Press the button **all the way** for it to work."},{"sentence":"**Sagad** na ang pasensya ko sa iyo!","translation":"My patience with you is **at its limit**!"}]

translation: to have lights installed; to be lit up
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon o paglalagay ng ilaw sa isang lugar.
etymology: From `magka-` + `ilaw`, meaning to come to have light.
original_explanation: That moment when Meralco finally fixes the power outage and your whole barangay shouts for joy. Or when your sitio, which has been in the dark for decades, finally gets electricity. "Sa wakas, magkakailaw na rin kami!" It's a literal "let there be light" moment.
usage_notes: Used to denote the event or process of a place getting electric lighting, or for power to be restored after an outage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magkakailaw** na raw ang buong baryo sa susunod na buwan.","translation":"They say the whole village will **have lights installed** next month."},{"sentence":"Sana **magkailaw** na para makapag-charge na ako ng cellphone.","translation":"I hope the **power comes back on** so I can charge my phone."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na may hilig sa labis na pag-inom ng alak at madaling malasing.
original_explanation: This is your tito who is the life (and eventual problem) of the party, always looking for a 'tagay'. Every weekend is an 'inuman' session. They might say 'isang case lang,' but you know it's just the warm-up. Their blood type might as well be Red Horse.
usage_notes: Can range from describing someone who gets drunk easily to someone with a drinking problem. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mula nang magkaproblema, naging **mapaglasing** si Mang Tonyo.","translation":"Since he had problems, Mang Tonyo became **prone to getting drunk**."},{"sentence":"Pinayuhan siya ng doktor na iwasan ang alak dahil siya ay **mapaglasing**.","translation":"The doctor advised him to avoid alcohol because he gets drunk easily."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na mula sa ibang bansa o lahi; hindi katutubo sa isang lugar; banyaga.
etymology: From 'dayo' (to visit or go to another place) + '-han' suffix, literally 'one who comes from another place'.
original_explanation: Anyone who's not from 'Pinas. The tourist asking for directions to the nearest Jollibee, the expat in BGC, or even Superman (he's literally an alien). It's the standard, neutral term, unlike the more casual 'Kano' or the slightly dated 'banyaga'.
usage_notes: Can also mean 'stranger' or 'outsider' in a more local context, not necessarily from another country.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **dayuhan** ang namamasyal sa Palawan tuwing tag-araw.","translation":"Many **foreigners** visit Palawan during the summer."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam niya ay isa siyang **dayuhan** sa sarili niyang bayan.","translation":"He feels like a **stranger** in his own town."}]

translation: to break, to destroy, to ruin
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagdudulot ng pinsala sa isang bagay upang ito ay hindi na gumana, maging buo, o manatili sa orihinal nitong kalagayan.
original_explanation: The ultimate "Wreck-It Ralph" move. It's what you do to your diet on a weekend, what a toddler does to a perfectly built Lego castle, or what happens to your trust when someone breaks a promise. From gadgets to relationships, if it can be broken, you can "sirain" it.
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang pandiwa na ginagamit para sa mga pisikal na bagay at mga abstraktong konsepto tulad ng plano, tiwala, o araw ng isang tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **sirain** ang laruan ng kapatid mo.","translation":"Don't **break** your sibling's toy."},{"sentence":"Sinira niya ang tiwala ko nang magsinungaling siya.","translation":"He **ruined** my trust when he lied."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang artipisyal na bagay na sadyang inilagay sa orbit sa kalawakan upang magamit sa komunikasyon, pagmamanman, o pananaliksik. Pwede ring tumukoy sa isang natural na bagay na umiikot sa isang planeta, tulad ng buwan.
original_explanation: The reason you can watch Netflix, use Waze, and get a signal for your Cignal or G Sat. It's that thing in space that eavesdrops on everyone's data. Also, a term for a branch office in a BPO company that's not the main site. "Saan ka naka-assign?" "Sa satellite office lang sa Alabang."
usage_notes: An English loanword used directly in Tagalog, especially in technical and modern contexts. There is no common native equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglalagay sila ng bagong **satellite** para pabilisin ang internet.","translation":"They are launching a new **satellite** to speed up the internet."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng **satellite** dish para makasagap ng signal.","translation":"A **satellite** dish is needed to receive a signal."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtigil sa paggawa o paggalaw na natapos na, upang maibalik ang lakas.
original_explanation: This is the past tense of 'pahinga'. It's what you did last weekend after a hell week at work. You binged a series, ordered food, and didn't reply to work emails. You took a break. You deserved it.
usage_notes: This is the completed aspect (past tense) of the verb 'magpahinga'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng mahabang byahe, **nagpahinga** muna kami sa hotel.","translation":"After the long trip, we **rested** for a while at the hotel."},{"sentence":"**Nagpahinga** siya ng isang taon bago pumasok sa kolehiyo.","translation":"He **took a break** for one year before entering college."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang balangkas o listahan ng mga gawain, pagtatanghal, o bahagi ng isang pagdiriwang o kaganapan na nakaayos ayon sa pagkakasunod-sunod.
etymology: From 'pa-' + 'tunton' (trace, follow) + '-an', literally 'a guide to be followed'.
original_explanation: The piece of paper they hand you at a wedding, debut, or company Christmas party that tells you when to eat, when the boring speeches happen, and when you can finally go home. The 'what's next?' list.
usage_notes: Refers to the schedule of an event, not a TV/radio program (which is 'programa') or a computer program.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayon sa **palatuntunan**, ang susunod na bahagi ay ang sayaw ng mga debutante.","translation":"According to the **program**, the next part is the debutantes' dance."},{"sentence":"Nawala ko ang kopya ko ng **palatuntunan** para sa Pasko.","translation":"I lost my copy of the Christmas **program**."}]

translation: depletion; the state of being used up
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng lubusang pagkawala o paggamit ng isang bagay hanggang sa wala nang matira.
original_explanation: The state of the ulam after your kuya gets to it first. The state of your data allowance three days after it refreshed. The state of your patience during a 3-hour traffic jam on EDSA. That 'wala na, finish na' feeling is pagkaubos.
usage_notes: A very common word used for food, money, patience, resources, etc.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ikinalungkot niya ang mabilis na **pagkaubos** ng kanyang sahod.","translation":"He was saddened by the rapid **depletion** of his salary."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng pista, kitang-kita ang **pagkaubos** ng pagkain sa mesa.","translation":"After the feast, the **state of the food being used up** on the table was very evident."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na may malapit na ugnayan, pagtitiwala, at pagmamahal sa isa pa, na hindi pamilya o karelasyon.
etymology: From ka- + ibig + -an. Literally means 'one you share affection with' or 'co-lover' in a platonic sense.
original_explanation: Your human diary, co-conspirator sa kalokohan, tagasalo ng mga hugot mo, at ang unang taong tinatawagan mo para sa chismis. The one who will help you move, or more importantly, help you move on. Sila 'yung pamilya na pinili mo.
usage_notes: A universal and fundamental word. Can be used as a term of address.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Maria ang matalik kong **kaibigan** mula pagkabata.","translation":"Maria is my best **friend** since childhood."},{"sentence":"Salamat, **kaibigan**, sa iyong tulong.","translation":"Thank you, **friend**, for your help."}]

translation: to get a wound; to be wounded
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng sugat o pinsala sa balat o katawan dahil sa isang aksidente o pagkasakit.
original_explanation: That moment when you're just walking and suddenly, BAM, you trip over nothing and now you have a battle scar. It’s what happens when you try to open a can without a can opener or when your cat decides your arm is a scratching post. Time to bring out the Betadine and band-aids.
usage_notes: Refers to acquiring a single or a few wounds.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa paggamit ng kutsilyo para hindi ka **magkasugat**.","translation":"Be careful using the knife so you don't **get wounded**."},{"sentence":"**Nagkasugat** siya sa tuhod pagkatapos mahulog sa bisikleta.","translation":"He **got a wound** on his knee after falling from the bicycle."}]

meaning_filipino: Naging mas mahigpit, masinsin, o istrikto sa pagpapatupad ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na humigpit ang hawak niya sa kamay mo nung may dumaang pogi, or 'yung security sa mall na biglang humigpit pagdating ng Pasko. Pwede ring tumukoy sa traffic sa EDSA na lalong humigpit, parang pag-asa mong umuwi nang maaga.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Humigpit** ang yakap niya nang sabihin kong aalis na ako.","translation":"Her hug **tightened** when I said I was leaving."},{"sentence":"Simula nang magkaroon ng bagong manager, **humigpit** ang mga patakaran sa opisina.","translation":"Since the new manager arrived, the rules in the office **became stricter**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tanggapin na totoo o tunay ang isang bagay, pahayag, o konsepto.
original_explanation: What you do when your friend says "On the way na ako" but you know they're still in the shower. It's the act of having faith, whether it's in a higher power, in another person, or in yourself. "Bes, maniwala ka sa sarili mo, kaya mo 'yan!"
usage_notes: The root 'tiwala' means trust. 'Maniwala' is the verb form for believing something is true.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **maniwala** sa mga pangako niya.","translation":"It's hard to **believe** his promises."},{"sentence":"**Maniwala** ka't sa hindi, nanalo ako sa lotto!","translation":"**Believe** it or not, I won the lottery!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang yugto sa siklo ng buwan kung kailan ito ay ganap na bilog at naiilawan mula sa pananaw ng Daigdig.
original_explanation: AKA 'full moon.' This is when werewolves supposedly come out, and when your friend who's into astrology starts telling you that Mercury is in retrograde again. It's the ultimate backdrop for a romantic date, a horror movie scene, or just a really good night to drink outside. It's the moon in its most extra, show-off phase.
usage_notes: The full phrase is almost always used. Just 'kabilugan' can mean 'roundness' in general.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maliwanag ang gabi dahil sa **kabilugan ng buwan**.","translation":"The night is bright because of the **full moon**."},{"sentence":"May mga naniniwalang lumalabas ang mga aswang tuwing **kabilugan ng buwan**.","translation":"Some believe that mythical creatures come out during the **full moon**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang modernong ekspresyon na may sarkastikong tono, na pinagsasama ang 'OA' (overacting) at 'yarn' (isang kolokyal na bersyon ng 'iyan'), upang tukuyin ang isang bagay na labis o eksaherado.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng 'OA' (overacting) at 'yarn', isang gay lingo/internet slang na baryasyon ng 'iyan' (that).
original_explanation: Sassy Gen Z slang for calling someone out on their drama. The 'yarn' (a playful version of 'iyan' or 'that') adds a layer of playful mockery. It’s like saying, 'Oh, you're being dramatic about *that*? How cute.' Your friend complains about having to wake up at 8 AM? You hit them with the, 'OA yarn?'
usage_notes: Lubhang impormal at bahagi ng modernong internet/gay lingo. Ang 'yarn' ay nagdaragdag ng sarkastiko o mapanuksong tono.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umiiyak dahil walang data? **OA yarn**?","translation":"Crying because you have no data? **So dramatic, aren't we**?"},{"sentence":"Grabe ang reaksyon niya sa simpleng biro, **oa yarn**.","translation":"His reaction to a simple joke was too much, **so dramatic**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang organisasyon o gusali na itinatag para sa isang partikular na layunin, tulad ng edukasyon, pananaliksik, o pagsasanay.
original_explanation: Parang school pero mas pang-matalino pakinggan. Dito ginagawa 'yung mga research na hindi mo maintindihan pero importante daw para sa future ng humanity. Think TESDA training centers or specialized colleges.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtatrabaho siya bilang mananaliksik sa isang **instituto** ng agham.","translation":"She works as a researcher at a science **institute**."},{"sentence":"Ang **Instituto** Cervantes ay nagtuturo ng wikang Espanyol.","translation":"The Cervantes **Institute** teaches the Spanish language."}]

translation: to permit, to allow, to grant
meaning_filipino: Magbigay ng pahintulot o permiso para sa isang gawain o kahilingan.
original_explanation: The formal, almost divine, version of 'Sige, payag ako.' It's what you ask from your parents when you want to go on a trip: 'Sana'y itulot ninyo ang aking pag-alis.' It has a very 'grant me this wish' vibe, like you're petitioning a higher power (e.g., your boss for a vacation leave, or the heavens for no traffic on EDSA).
usage_notes: This is a formal and somewhat archaic word, often found in literature, prayers, or very formal speech. The common, everyday equivalent is 'payagan' or 'pahintulutan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawa'y **itulot** ng pagkakataon na magkita tayong muli.","translation":"May the occasion **permit** us to meet again."},{"sentence":"Hindi **itinulot** ng kanyang mga magulang ang kanyang pag-alis.","translation":"His parents did not **allow** him to leave."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging matalino sa paraang mapanlamang o mapaglalang; pagkakaroon ng abilidad na makaisip ng paraan para sa sariling kapakanan.
original_explanation: That officemate who always manages to get out of 'ambagan' for the birthday celebrant. Or the 'diskarte' of a jeepney driver navigating EDSA traffic. It's street smarts with a hint of mischief. That's pagkatuso.
usage_notes: Can have a negative connotation (deceitful) or a slightly admirable one (street-smart, resourceful).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa kanyang **pagkatuso** sa negosyo.","translation":"He is known for his **cunningness** in business."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang kanyang **pagkatuso** upang makalusot sa mahirap na sitwasyon.","translation":"She used her **slyness** to get out of a difficult situation."}]

translation: to send someone to school; to finance someone's education
meaning_filipino: Tustusan ang pag-aaral ng isang tao; bigyan ng pagkakataon at suporta upang makapag-aral.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate Filipino parent goal. It's when you work multiple jobs, maybe even go abroad as an OFW, just to 'papag-aralin' your kids. You are causing them to be able to study. It’s the verb form of every parent’s favorite line: “Edukasyon lang ang maipapamana ko sa’yo.”
usage_notes: A very common causative verb that holds significant cultural weight in the Philippines, emphasizing a benefactor's role in a person's education. Often used interchangeably with the simpler 'pag-aralin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gagawin ko ang lahat para **papag-aralin** ang aking mga kapatid hanggang kolehiyo.","translation":"I will do everything to **send my siblings to school** until college."},{"sentence":"Siya ang nagboluntaryong **papag-aralin** ang ulilang pamangkin.","translation":"He volunteered to **finance the education** of his orphaned nephew."}]

translation: to flirt, to sweet-talk, to show affection
meaning_filipino: Pagpapakita ng labis na paglalambing o pagmamahal sa isang tao, kadalasan sa paraang may pahiwatig ng panunuyo o romantikong interes.
original_explanation: This is your 'diskarte' mode activated. When you kumarinyo, you're laying on the charm thick, like a guy trying to get a girl's number or someone trying to sweet-talk their way out of a traffic ticket. It's the verbal equivalent of a 'landi' move. Think 'How to be you po?' but with more pa-cute.
usage_notes: Often implies a playful or romantic intent, distinct from general kindness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumarinyo** ang binata sa dalaga sa pag-asang mapapasagot niya ito.","translation":"The young man **flirted** with the young woman, hoping she would say yes to him."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **kumarinyo** sa guwardiya para makapasok nang walang bayad.","translation":"He tried to **sweet-talk** the guard to get in for free."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalawakan sa itaas ng mundo; ang himpapawid o atmospera na bumabalot sa daigdig.
etymology: Possibly from 'pawid' (nipa thatch) + -in, referring to the 'roof' of the world.
