original_explanation: This is the kind of word you use when you're feeling poetic or dramatic while looking at the sky. It's not just 'langit' (sky), it's the whole majestic, grand expanse above. "Tumingin ka sa papawirin, andiyan ang mga pangarap mo." It's the sky, but with a Master's degree.
usage_notes: A more literary or formal term for 'sky' or 'heavens', often used in poetry and literature.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga ibon ay malayang lumilipad sa malawak na **papawirin**.","translation":"The birds fly freely in the vast **sky**."},{"sentence":"Nagniningning ang mga bituin sa madilim na **papawirin**.","translation":"The stars are shining in the dark **heavens**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang parirala na nangangahulugang wala sa mga pagpipilian ang totoo, tama, o pinili.
original_explanation: The Tagalog for "None of the above." It's what you say when you're asked to choose between two exes or two equally bad job offers. "Gusto mo ba si A o si B?" Sagot: "Alinma'y hindi." (I choose self-love and peace of mind).
usage_notes: Used to negate all available choices. The '-y' is a contraction of 'ay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinanong siya kung alin sa dalawa ang salarin, ngunit **alinma'y hindi** raw niya nakita.","translation":"He was asked which of the two was the culprit, but he said he saw **neither**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang layunin, puntirya, o bagay na nais makamit, maabot, o tamaan.
original_explanation: Your BPO life in one word. It's the sales quota you need to hit para sa commission, the number of calls you need to take per hour, or the deadline your client set for yesterday. Outside the office, it's the "sana bago mag-30" life goals list. Basically, it's the finish line you're always running towards, whether for a project or for your life. A direct English loanword that has been fully adopted.
usage_notes: Pronounced with a Filipino accent. Widely used in business, personal goal-setting, and even in games.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating maabot ang ating sales **target** para sa buwang ito.","translation":"We need to hit our sales **target** for this month."},{"sentence":"Ikaw ang **target** ng mga biro niya kanina.","translation":"You were the **target** of his jokes earlier."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tradisyonal na kuwento na itinuturing na makasaysayan ngunit hindi pa napapatunayan; isang alamat.
original_explanation: The Spanish cousin of 'alamat.' It's the story of how a mountain got its shape or why a certain flower is colored that way. Think Maria Makiling or the legend of the pineapple. It's the original 'chismis' that got passed down for generations until it became a school lesson.
usage_notes: Ang 'alamat' ay ang mas karaniwang ginagamit na termino sa Filipino. Ang 'leyenda' ay may mas pampanitikan o pangkasaysayang dating.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **leyenda** ng Bulkang Mayon ay tungkol sa isang trahedya ng pag-ibig.","translation":"The **legend** of Mayon Volcano is about a tragic love story."},{"sentence":"Maraming **leyenda** ang bumabalot sa isla ng Siquijor.","translation":"Many **legends** surround the island of Siquijor."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit at manipis na patpat, karaniwang gawa sa kahoy o plastik, na ginagamit sa pag-alis ng pagkaing naipit sa pagitan ng mga ngipin.
original_explanation: The ultimate after-meal weapon against 'tinga'. It's that tiny stick you see your tito skillfully wield while watching TV, sometimes for hours after he's finished eating. It's also a status symbol of a satisfying meal.
usage_notes: Walang katumbas na isang salita sa Tagalog, kaya hinihiram nang buo. Ang "palito" ay maaaring gamitin ngunit mas pangkalahatan (e.g., palito ng posporo).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pahingi naman ng **toothpick**, may tinga ako.","translation":"Can I have a **toothpick**? I have food stuck in my teeth."},{"sentence":"Laging may dalang **toothpick** si Mang Berto sa kanyang bulsa.","translation":"Mang Berto always carries a **toothpick** in his pocket."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng pahintulot o pagsang-ayon sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: This is what you do when your friend asks, "Bes, pwede ba 'ko matulog sa inyo mamaya?" and you say "Sige." You're giving them the go signal. It’s the opposite of being a KJ (Kill Joy).
usage_notes: "Payagan" is a more common synonym and object-focus form. "Payahan" is less common in modern conversation but grammatically correct.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Payahan** mo na siyang sumama sa field trip.","translation":"Just **allow** him/her to join the field trip."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang abnormal na mabilis, malakas, o iregular na pagtibok ng puso, kadalasang nararamdaman dahil sa sakit, pagod, o matinding emosyon.
original_explanation: Yung feeling na nakita mo si crush na may kasamang iba, tapos biglang kumabog 'yung dibdib mo na parang may nagda-drum solo. Or 'yung epekto ng pangatlong baso mo ng kape para lang matapos ang BPO shift. That's **palpitasyon**. Your heart is doing the cha-cha when it should be doing a waltz.
usage_notes: Used in both medical and emotional contexts to describe a racing or irregular heartbeat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ako ng **palpitasyon** dahil sa sobrang kape na ininom ko.","translation":"I had **palpitations** because of the excessive coffee I drank."},{"sentence":"Tuwing kinakabahan siya bago mag-exam, nakakaramdam siya ng **palpitasyon**.","translation":"Every time she gets nervous before an exam, she feels **palpitations**."}]

translation: to attend to, to take care of, to manage
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng atensiyon at pag-aalaga sa isang tao, bagay, o gawain; ang pagsasaayos ng mga kailangan.
etymology: mag- (actor-focus verb prefix) + asikaso (from Spanish 'hacer caso' meaning 'to pay attention')
original_explanation: This is the official verb of the eldest daughter (panganay). It's what you do when guests arrive ('asikasuhin mo ang bisita'), what you do with your messy room, and what your boss tells you to do with a new project. It's adulting in one word.
usage_notes: A very common verb used for managing tasks, people, or responsibilities.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **mag-asikaso** ng mga dokumento para sa aking passport.","translation":"I need to **take care of** the documents for my passport."},{"sentence":"Siya ang nag-**asikaso** sa mga bisita habang abala ang lahat.","translation":"She was the one who **attended to** the guests while everyone was busy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng mataas na sombrero na may patag na tuktok at hugis silindro, karaniwang isinusuot sa mga pormal na okasyon noong unang panahon.
etymology: From Spanish "cilindro" (cylinder), but with a specialized meaning in Tagalog referring to the top hat, likely due to its shape.
original_explanation: That fancy top hat you see in old movies or worn by magicians. Think of Jose Rizal's iconic look, or the Monopoly man's headgear. It's the hat that says 'I'm either a 19th-century ilustrado or about to pull a rabbit out of this thing.'
usage_notes: This word specifically refers to a top hat. For the geometric shape or a mechanical part, 'silindro' is used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Makikita sa mga lumang larawan ang mga ginoong nakasuot ng **silinder**.","translation":"In old photographs, you can see gentlemen wearing **top hats**."},{"sentence":"Ang salamangkero ay may hawak na baston at may suot na **silinder**.","translation":"The magician was holding a cane and wearing a **top hat**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalawigan sa Pilipinas na matatagpuan sa rehiyon ng Gitnang Luzon, kilala sa mayamang kasaysayan at kultura.
etymology: Pinaniniwalaang nagmula sa salitang "bulak" dahil sa dating kasaganaan ng mga halamang bulak sa lugar.
original_explanation: The land of beautiful women, sweet pastillas, and the birthplace of heroes. Kung taga-dito ka, automatic tanong sa'yo, "Marunong ka mag-English?" dahil sa stereotype. Also, traffic capital 'pag pauwi ng norte on a long weekend.
usage_notes: Laging isinusulat na malaki ang unang titik dahil ito ay isang pangngalang pantangi.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming makasaysayang pook sa lalawigan ng **Bulakan**.","translation":"There are many historical sites in the province of **Bulacan**."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga kagamitan at kasangkapang metal tulad ng martilyo, pako, at turnilyo na ginagamit sa pagtatayo at pagkukumpuni. Tumutukoy din sa pisikal na bahagi ng isang kompyuter.
original_explanation: That one-stop shop where your tatay buys everything from pako (nails) to a new gripo (faucet) for his weekend DIY projects. It smells like paint, metal, and productivity. In the BPO/IT world, it's the physical stuff—the monitor, keyboard, CPU—that you threaten to throw out the window when the 'software' crashes for the 10th time.
usage_notes: The spelling 'hardware' is also widely accepted and used. 'Hardwer' is the Filipinized spelling. Can refer to both construction/tool hardware and computer hardware.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si Tatay ng martilyo sa **hardwer**.","translation":"Dad bought a hammer at the **hardware** store."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating i-upgrade ang **hardwer** ng computer para bumilis.","translation":"We need to upgrade the computer's **hardware** to make it faster."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga post sa platform na Twitter (ngayon ay X) na hayagang nagpapahayag ng matinding paghanga o pagnanasa para sa isang tao, kadalasan ay isang celebrity o public figure.
etymology: Nagmula sa social media platform na Twitter, pinagsasama ang "thirst" (pagnanasa) at "tweets" (mga post sa Twitter).
original_explanation: The public declaration of your 'pagka-uhaw' for everyone to see. These are those tweets you fire off at 2 AM about how you'd let your celebrity crush step on you. It's the digital equivalent of shouting your love from a rooftop, but hornier. Celebrities reading their 'thirst tweets' is a whole genre of internet content, and it's both cringe and gold.
usage_notes: Partikular na tumutukoy sa mga post sa Twitter/X. Ang mga katulad na komento sa ibang platform ay karaniwang tinatawag na 'thirsty comments'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binasa ni Chris Evans ang ilang **thirst tweets** tungkol sa kanya sa isang panayam.","translation":"Chris Evans read some **thirst tweets** about himself in an interview."},{"sentence":"Nagsulat siya ng sunod-sunod na **thirst tweets** para sa paborito niyang K-pop idol.","translation":"She wrote a series of **thirst tweets** for her favorite K-pop idol."}]

translation: to be erased; to be deleted
meaning_filipino: Matanggal o mawala ang isang marka, sulat, o datos mula sa isang ibabaw o sistema.
etymology: From 'bura' (erase). 'Ma-' prefix indicates an ability or accidental action.
original_explanation: That feeling of panic when you accidentally hit 'delete' on a super important file. Or when you try to forget your ex, pero parang permanent marker 'yung alaala niya—ayaw mabura. In the digital world, it's Ctrl+Z's worst enemy.
usage_notes: Can be used for physical erasing (like on a whiteboard) or digital deleting (files, messages). It can also be used metaphorically for memories or feelings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana'y **mabura** na sa isip ko ang lahat ng masasakit na alaala.","translation":"I wish all the painful memories could **be erased** from my mind."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka, baka **mabura** mo ang lahat ng files sa computer.","translation":"Be careful, you might accidentally **delete** all the files on the computer."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinong sapot na gawa ng gagamba, karaniwang matatagpuan sa mga sulok at lugar na bihirang linisin.
original_explanation: The official decoration of every haunted house and bodega. It's that sticky, dusty stuff in the corner that proves you haven't done general cleaning in ages. Finding an 'ulapot' in your room is a silent judgment from the universe (and from your mom) telling you to get the 'walis tingting'.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'agiw', though 'agiw' can also specifically refer to soot.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **ulapot** ang lumang bahay.","translation":"The old house is full of **cobwebs**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong alisin ang mga **ulapot** sa kisame.","translation":"You need to remove the **cobwebs** from the ceiling."}]

meaning_filipino: Maghiwa o magkatay ng malalaking piraso ng karne, karaniwang ginagawa ng isang magkakarne.
original_explanation: This is what the butcher at the palengke does with that huge slab of pork before you get your half-kilo of liempo. It's a primal, hardcore version of 'hiwa'. Think less of a delicate chef's slice and more of a "get the big cleaver" kind of action. Rarely used in everyday convo unless you're actually a butcher or describing a very gory scene.
usage_notes: An archaic or specialized term. More commonly, "magkatay" or "hiwain" is used. "Lapa" can also refer to the cut of meat itself (the flank).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang magkakarne ay sanay na **lumapa** ng baboy araw-araw.","translation":"The butcher is used **to cutting up** pigs every day."},{"sentence":"Pinanood ng bata kung paano **lumapa** ng baka ang kanyang ama.","translation":"The child watched how his father **butchered** the cow."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumungo o magpunta sa isang tiyak na lugar na malayo sa nagsasalita at sa kinakausap.
original_explanation: The formal, slightly dramatic way of saying 'go over there.' You won't hear this in a jeepney ("Manong, pumaroon lang po sa kanto!"), but you might see it in a historical movie or a classic novel. It's the opposite of 'pumarito' (come here).
usage_notes: Often used in formal or literary contexts. The more common, everyday equivalents are 'pumunta doon' or 'magpunta doon'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pumaroon** ka sa kaharian at sabihin sa hari ang masamang balita.","translation":"**Go there** to the kingdom and tell the king the bad news."},{"sentence":"Nais ng mga apostol na **pumaroon** sa kabilang ibayo.","translation":"The apostles wanted to **go there** to the other side."}]

translation: junction; fork (in the road); point of divergence
meaning_filipino: Isang punto kung saan ang isang daan, ilog, o anumang linya ay nahahati sa dalawa o higit pang direksyon; isang sangandaan.
original_explanation: That moment in your life when you have to choose between two job offers, or more importantly, between Jollibee and McDo. It's the 'two roads diverged in a yellow wood' moment, but in the Philippines, it's probably a fork in the road with a waiting shed and a sari-sari store. A literal or metaphorical point of decision.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'sangandaan', but 'pinagsangahan' can more specifically refer to the exact point of branching.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa **pinagsangahan** ng daan, lumiko ka pakanan.","translation":"At the **fork** in the road, turn right."},{"sentence":"Ang ilog ay may **pinagsangahan** patungo sa dalawang magkaibang bayan.","translation":"The river has a **junction** leading to two different towns."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aalaga, pagprotekta, o pagtingin sa isang tao, bagay, o lugar upang matiyak ang kaligtasan nito at maiwasan ang anumang panganib.
original_explanation: This is the job of the security guard at the mall, the 'sekyu' who checks your bag. It's what you do when you're babysitting your younger sibling. You `magbantay` your food at a party so no one else eats it. It's the ultimate 'paki-tingnan mo nga muna 'to' (can you watch this for a sec) verb.
usage_notes: Can be used for people, places, or things.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinakiusapan ko si ate na **magbantay** muna sa tindahan habang ako'y wala.","translation":"I asked my older sister to **watch over** the store for a while when I'm gone."},{"sentence":"Ang mga aso ay mahusay na **magbantay** ng bahay.","translation":"Dogs are excellent at **guarding** a house."}]

meaning_filipino: Nauukol o may katangian ng isang biograpia; naglalaman ng mga detalye tungkol sa buhay ng isang tao.
original_explanation: If a movie, book, or article is 'biograpiko', it means it's about a real person's life. Think of films like 'Heneral Luna' or 'Goyo: Ang Batang Heneral.' They're not 100% documentary, but they're based on historical figures. It's the adjective form, describing something that tells a life story.
usage_notes: Often used to describe films ("biographical film" or "biopic"), books, and articles. The Tagalized "bayopik" (from biopic) is more common in modern casual speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming aral ang mapupulot sa mga pelikulang **biograpiko**.","translation":"Many lessons can be learned from **biographical** films."},{"sentence":"Naglalaman ang aklat ng mga detalyeng **biograpiko** tungkol sa mga bayani ng Pilipinas.","translation":"The book contains **biographical** details about the heroes of the Philippines."}]

translation: to retaliate, to get revenge, to return (a favor)
meaning_filipino: Tumugon sa isang ginawang aksyon sa pamamagitan ng katulad na aksyon, ito man ay mabuti (pasasalamat) o masama (paghihiganti).
etymology: From the root 'ganti' (retaliation, return) with the infix '-um-'.
original_explanation: The clapback verb. It can be good, like returning a favor ('gumanti ng tulong'). But let's be real, it's mostly used for revenge. That moment when the teleserye bida, after being oppressed for 100 episodes, finally gets back at the kontrabida. That's pure, satisfying 'gumanti' energy.
usage_notes: The nature of the retaliation (positive or negative) is determined by the context or the object of the verb. 'Gumanti ng kabutihan' (to return kindness) vs. 'Gumanti sa kaaway' (to get revenge on an enemy).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nangako siyang **guganti** siya sa lahat ng nagtaksil sa kanya.","translation":"He promised he **would get revenge** on everyone who betrayed him."},{"sentence":"Gusto kong **gumanti** sa kabutihan mo sa pamamagitan ng pagtulong sa iyong proyekto.","translation":"I want to **return** your kindness by helping with your project."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang anumang pakinabang, kabutihan, o kalamangan na nakukuha mula sa isang bagay o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: The more formal, less corporate-y cousin of "benefits." This is what you get from drinking your veggies (good health), sleeping 8 hours (less eyebags), or breaking up with a toxic jowa (peace of mind). Any "what's in it for me?" question is answered by benepisyo.
usage_notes: Mas pangkalahatan ang saklaw kaysa sa salitang 'benefits' na kalimitang tumutukoy sa employment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **benepisyo** ng pag-eehersisyo araw-araw?","translation":"What is the **benefit** of exercising every day?"},{"sentence":"Malaki ang **benepisyo** ng bagong batas para sa mga magsasaka.","translation":"The new law has great **benefits** for farmers."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang marahas at mabilis na umiikot na kolumna ng hangin na may anyong embudo at umaabot mula sa ulap patungo sa lupa.
original_explanation: That thing you see in movies that picks up cows and houses. In the Philippines, it's more like a mini-tornado that makes yero sheets fly and your mom shout "Pasok na, may ipuipo!" Also a metaphor for a chaotic person or situation, like your love life.
usage_notes: Can also refer to a waterspout ('ipuipo sa tubig').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Winasak ng malakas na **ipuipo** ang ilang kabahayan sa probinsya.","translation":"A strong **tornado** destroyed several houses in the province."},{"sentence":"Para siyang **ipuipo** kung dumaan sa sala, lahat ng gamit nagulo.","translation":"He was like a **whirlwind** passing through the living room, all the things were in disarray."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa tradisyong Kristiyano, ito ang Huwebes bago ang Pasko ng Pagkabuhay na ginugunita ang Huling Hapunan ni Hesukristo kasama ang kanyang mga apostol.
original_explanation: The Thursday of Holy Week. This is the day for Visita Iglesia, where you try to visit seven churches, often getting stuck in traffic that tests your Christian patience. It's the official start of the long weekend where everyone either goes to the province or binge-watches on Netflix.
usage_notes: Part of the Holy Week (Mahal na Araw) observance in the Philippines. It is a public holiday.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsasagawa ng Visita Iglesia ang maraming pamilya tuwing **Huwebes Santo**.","translation":"Many families conduct the Visita Iglesia every **Maundy Thursday**."},{"sentence":"Walang pasok sa opisina mula **Huwebes Santo** hanggang Biyernes Santo.","translation":"There are no office workdays from **Maundy Thursday** to Good Friday."}]
related: ["Mahal na Araw","Biyernes Santo","Linggo ng Pagkabuhay","Visita Iglesia"]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghingi ng payo, opinyon, o impormasyon mula sa isang tao o pangkat na may sapat na kaalaman.
original_explanation: This is what you do when your own Googling skills aren't enough. Whether it's asking your manager for advice, seeing a specialist doctor, or even consulting the elders about pamamanhikan, it's the official act of saying, "Help, I need an expert!"
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagsangguni** sa abogado ay mahalaga bago pumirma ng anumang kontrata.","translation":"The **consultation** with a lawyer is important before signing any contract."},{"sentence":"Inirerekomenda ang **pagsangguni** sa isang espesyalista para sa iyong kondisyon.","translation":"A **referral** to a specialist is recommended for your condition."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng baging na may bunga na mayroong mapait na lasa, karaniwang ginagamit bilang gulay sa lutuing Pilipino.
etymology: Pinaniniwalaang nagmula sa salitang Sanskrit na 'karavella' sa pamamagitan ng Malay na 'peria'.
original_explanation: The official vegetable of people who can't be happy for others. Got dumped? Failed an exam? Your friend got a new phone? If your first reaction is bitterness, congrats, you're the human embodiment of `ampalaya`. Also, a very healthy vegetable your mom makes you eat.
usage_notes: Bukod sa pagiging gulay, malawakang ginagamit sa kolokyal na pananalita upang ilarawan ang isang taong 'bitter' o puno ng kapaitan at inggit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-uulam kami ng ginisang **ampalaya** na may itlog tuwing Biyernes.","translation":"We eat sautéed **bitter gourd** with egg every Friday."},{"sentence":"Hayaan mo na siya, parang **ampalaya** 'yan dahil hindi ka niya makuha.","translation":"Just ignore him, he's acting like a **bitter person** because he can't have you."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, karaniwang gamot o halamang-gamot, na may kakayahang magdulot ng pagkalaglag o pagkaagas ng ipinagbubuntis.
original_explanation: This is a serious one. It refers to anything—herbs, sketchy pills, folk remedies—that is taken to induce an abortion or miscarriage. It's a heavy topic, often discussed in whispers, and tied to desperate situations. Definitely not something you casually talk about.
usage_notes: This term is used in medical or folk medicine contexts and pertains to a sensitive and controversial subject.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-inom ng mga hindi resetadong gamot na **pampaagas** ay lubhang mapanganib sa kalusugan.","translation":"Taking non-prescribed **abortifacient** drugs is extremely dangerous to one's health."},{"sentence":"Nagbabala ang mga doktor laban sa mga halamang-gamot na sinasabing mabisang **pampaagas**.","translation":"Doctors warned against herbal medicines that are claimed to be effective **abortifacients**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panahon ng pagpapalit o pagluluno ng balahibo ng mga ibon, lalo na ng mga manok.
original_explanation: It's the 'bad hair day' season for chickens and birds. They're shedding their old feathers to grow new ones, so they look a bit rough, like you after a long week of OT. Sabungeros know this well; it's when the roosters are on a 'beauty break' and can't fight.
usage_notes: Isang partikular na termino na karaniwang ginagamit sa pag-aalaga ng manok o ng mga mahilig sa ibon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa panahon ng **tagulaway** ang mga alagang manok ni Mang Kardo kaya't matamlay ang mga ito.","translation":"Mang Kardo's chickens are in their **molting** season, which is why they are lethargic."}]

translation: manner of being dressed or prepared
meaning_filipino: Ang paraan ng pag-aayos sa sarili, lalo na sa pananamit, para sa isang okasyon; ang estado ng pagiging handa.
etymology: From `pag-` + `kaka-` + `gayak` (adornment, preparation). Describes the state or manner of being adorned or prepared.
original_explanation: This is your OOTD's final form. It's not just the clothes, but *how* you put it all together. 'Ang ganda ng pagkakagayak mo!' is a high-level compliment at a party. It's the state of being all dolled up, prepared, and ready to slay, whether for a wedding or just a trip to the mall.
usage_notes: Can refer to personal appearance (clothing, makeup) or the state of preparation for an event.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Humanga ang lahat sa marangyang **pagkakagayak** ng debutante.","translation":"Everyone was amazed by the debutante's splendid **way of being dressed**."},{"sentence":"Maayos na ang **pagkakagayak** ng lahat ng gamit para sa aming pag-alis.","translation":"All the things are now properly **prepared** for our departure."}]

translation: manner of use; the way something was used
meaning_filipino: Ang paraan o istilo kung paano ginamit ang isang bagay, kagamitan, o konsepto.
etymology: From `pag-` + `kaka-` + `gamit` (use). The `pagkaka-` affix denotes the manner or way something was done.
original_explanation: This is the 'how-to' or 'how-it-was-done' of using something. Think of it as the difference between using a new iPhone for TikTok vs. using it as a chopping board. The pagkakagamit was... questionable in the second case. It's the 'user story' of an object's life.
usage_notes: Often used to evaluate or describe the method or effectiveness of how something was utilized.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko gusto ang **pagkakagamit** mo sa pera na ipinadala ko.","translation":"I don't like the **way you used** the money I sent."},{"sentence":"Ang husay ng **pagkakagamit** ng direktor sa slow-motion sa eksenang iyon.","translation":"The director's **use** of slow-motion in that scene was brilliant."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang buto na nag-uugnay sa sternum (buto sa dibdib) at sa scapula (buto sa balikat), na kilala rin sa tawag na buto ng balagat.
original_explanation: That bone you can feel (and see, if you're skinny) between your neck and your shoulder. It's the one that makes you look "sexy" according to some, and the one that hurts like hell when you break it falling off your bike. It's the body's built-in hanger for your sando straps.
usage_notes: A technical/medical term. The common term is "balagat".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nabali ang kanyang **klabikula** nang mahulog siya sa hagdan.","translation":"His **clavicle** broke when he fell down the stairs."},{"sentence":"Ipinakita ng X-ray ang lamat sa kanyang kaliwang **klabikula**.","translation":"The X-ray showed a fracture in his left **collarbone**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang ginagamit upang mag-rekord at magpatugtog ng tunog sa pamamagitan ng isang disk o silindro.
original_explanation: The OG Spotify. This was the high-tech gadget of your great-grandparents, where they'd gather 'round to listen to kundiman songs from a big, spinning disc with a horn. Now, it's a prized possession for audiophiles and collectors who insist 'vinyl just sounds warmer.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May luma silang **ponograpo** sa kanilang bahay na pamana pa ng kanilang lolo.","translation":"They have an old **phonograph** in their house, inherited from their grandfather."},{"sentence":"Pinatugtog niya ang isang lumang plaka sa **ponograpo**.","translation":"He played an old record on the **record player**."}]

translation: a type of woody vine (Leucaena leucocephala)
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng puno o palumpong (Leucaena leucocephala) na may maliliit na dahon at mga bunga na parang patag na sitaw, karaniwang ginagamit bilang pagkain ng hayop. Kilala rin bilang ipil-ipil.
etymology: Named after Saint Helena (Santa Elena), but the reason for the plant being named after her is unclear.
original_explanation: This isn't about a saint named Elena. It's the plant we more commonly know as "ipil-ipil." Maybe it got its name because it's as common and widespread as towns named after a Santa Elena. Its seeds were used in necklaces and crafts back in the day. Now, it's mostly known as high-protein food for goats. So, it's holy chow for kambing.
usage_notes: More commonly known as `ipil-ipil`. The name `santa-elena` is less frequent in casual conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga kambing sa bukid ay kinakain ang mga dahon ng **santa-elena**.","translation":"The goats on the farm eat the leaves of the **santa-elena** vine."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na nakararanas ng kaunti o walang romantikong atraksyon sa iba.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung taong happy sa platonic love. Hindi sila "bitter" o "manhid," sadyang wala lang sa vocabulary nila ang kilig, harana, at monthsary. They can love people deeply—as friends, as family—pero 'yung romantic stuff? Pass. It's a valid orientation, not a phase or a problem to be fixed.
usage_notes: Isang modernong termino na nauugnay sa SOGIESC (Sexual Orientation, Gender Identity and Expression, and Sex Characteristics). Madalas na pinaikli bilang "aro".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bilang isang **aromantic**, mas pinahahalagahan niya ang pagkakaibigan kaysa sa romantikong relasyon.","translation":"As an **aromantic** person, they value friendship more than romantic relationships."},{"sentence":"Ipinaliwanag niya sa kanyang mga kaibigan kung ano ang ibig sabihin ng pagiging **aromantic** at asexual.","translation":"He explained to his friends what it means to be **aromantic** and asexual."}]

meaning_filipino: May sukdulang antas ng lamig; lubhang mababa ang temperatura.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `napaka-` (nagpapahiwatig ng sukdulang antas) at salitang ugat na `lamig` (coldness).
original_explanation: The feeling of the office AC on a Monday morning. The way your ex treats you now. The halo-halo you crave on a 40-degree summer day. It's the kind of cold that makes you question your life choices, like not bringing a jacket.
usage_notes: Can describe temperature, but also a person's demeanor or the state of a relationship (e.g., 'cold' treatment).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Napakalamig** ng tubig sa ilog kahit tag-araw.","translation":"The water in the river is **very cold** even during summer."},{"sentence":"Naging **napakalamig** ng pakikitungo niya sa akin pagkatapos ng aming pagtatalo.","translation":"His treatment of me became **very cold** after our argument."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi mapakali; balisa o puno ng pag-aalala; magulo ang isip o damdamin.
original_explanation: That feeling you get at 3 AM when you're overthinking everything from your deadlines to that awkward thing you said in 2015. You're tossing and turning, your mind is a web browser with 50 tabs open. That's being maligalig. You're not at peace, parang may utang ka na di mo mabayaran.
usage_notes: Describes a state of mental or emotional turmoil.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **maligalig** ang kanyang pagtulog dahil sa masamang balita.","translation":"His sleep became **restless** because of the bad news."},{"sentence":"Isang **maligalig** na damdamin ang bumalot sa kanya habang naghihintay ng resulta.","translation":"A **troubled** feeling enveloped her while waiting for the results."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-aalis ng marka, sulat, o datos; pagpawi o pag-alis nang tuluyan.
original_explanation: What you do to your search history after a questionable late-night internet deep dive. Also, what you wish you could do to your ex's memories, pero 'di pala gano'n kadali. It's the CTRL+Z of real life, or at least we wish it was.
usage_notes: Often used in verb forms like 'burahin' (to erase) or 'mabura' (to be erased). The noun for the object used to erase is 'pambura'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **bura** sa nakaraan ay hindi laging madali.","translation":"The **erasure** of the past is not always easy."},{"sentence":"Burahin mo na ang numero niya, 'yan ang unang hakbang sa pag-**bura** sa kanya sa isip mo.","translation":"Delete his number, that's the first step in **erasing** him from your mind."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang indibidwal na kabilang sa pangkalahatang populasyon, na walang espesyal na ranggo, yaman, o kapangyarihan.
original_explanation: This is "the masses," the "madlang people," the everyday Juan and Maria. They're the ones commuting on the MRT, lining up for a free concert, and making up 99% of the population. They're the main character of the country's story, even if they don't get the spotlight.
usage_notes: Often used in social or political contexts to refer to the general populace.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga isyu tulad ng pagtaas ng presyo ng bilihin ay direktang nakaaapekto sa **karaniwang tao**.","translation":"Issues like the rising prices of goods directly affect the **common person**."},{"sentence":"Dapat pakinggan ng gobyerno ang hinaing ng **karaniwang tao**.","translation":"The government should listen to the grievances of the **ordinary person**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na tawag sa isang kaibigang lalaki, katumbas ng 'bro' sa Ingles. Hango sa salitang 'brother'.
original_explanation: The universal Filipino term for a male friend, buddy, or pal. It's the shortened, cooler version of "brother." You use it when you're asking for a favor ("Brad, pa-utang."), greeting a friend ("Uy, brad, kumusta?"), or calling out to some random guy whose name you don't know. It's friendlier than 'pare' and less formal than 'kuya'.
usage_notes: Highly colloquial and informal. Used to address male friends.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Saan ang lakad natin mamaya, **brad**?","translation":"Where are we going later, **bro**?"},{"sentence":"Salamat sa tulong, **brad**! Malaking bagay 'to.","translation":"Thanks for the help, **bro**! This is a big deal."}]

meaning_filipino: Espesyal na kasuotang idinisenyo para gamitin sa paglangoy o pagligo sa dagat, ilog, o swimming pool.
original_explanation: Your beach OOTD. Whether it's a bikini for your Boracay trip, board shorts for surfing in Siargao, or even just a t-shirt and shorts combo for the resort swimming pool, this is what you wear when you're about to get wet. The official attire for 'vitamin sea.'
usage_notes: Can refer to any type of swimwear, from bikinis and one-pieces to trunks and board shorts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakalimutan kong dalhin ang aking **damit-pampaligo** kaya hindi ako nakalangoy.","translation":"I forgot to bring my **swimwear**, so I couldn't swim."},{"sentence":"Magsuot ka ng rash guard sa ibabaw ng iyong **damit-pampaligo** para hindi ka masunog.","translation":"Wear a rash guard over your **bathing suit** so you don't get sunburned."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang nagpapahiwatig na ang isang kinalabasan o desisyon ay nakasalalay o nababatay sa isang partikular na kondisyon, sitwasyon, o tao.
original_explanation: The ultimate non-committal Filipino answer. 'Tuloy ba tayo?' '**Depende**.' 'Mahal mo ba ako?' '**Depende**.' It's the verbal equivalent of a shrug emoji 🤷‍♀️, a safe space between a 'yes' and a 'no'.
usage_notes: Madalas na sinusundan ng 'sa' (hal. 'depende sa iyo').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Depende** sa panahon kung matutuloy ang ating lakad.","translation":"It **depends** on the weather if our trip will push through."},{"sentence":"Sasama ka ba? **Depende** kung sino ang kasama.","translation":"Are you coming? It **depends** on who's coming along."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghuli ng isda o anumang bagay sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng lambat.
original_explanation: The action word for using a 'lambat'. It's what you do when you want to catch a whole bunch of fish at once. In the digital age, it's what scammers do to your DMs, trying to 'catch' you with a phishing link. 'Huwag kang magpalambatin sa mga pekeng offer online.'
usage_notes: This is the verb form derived from the noun 'lambat'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **lambatin** ang mga paru-paro sa hardin.","translation":"He tried to **catch with a net** the butterflies in the garden."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **lambatin** ang mga isda sa lawa.","translation":"We need to **catch with a net** the fish in the lake."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bahagi ng sasakyan, tulad ng kotse o bisikleta, na nagsisilbing panangga sa putik at iba pang dumi mula sa gulong.
original_explanation: That part of your bike or car that does all the dirty work, catching the mud so your OOTD doesn't. It's the unsung hero of rainy days, the shield against the 'putik' of life.
usage_notes: A specific technical term for the part of a vehicle that covers the wheel.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nabasag ang **tapalodo** ng motor ko kaya tumalsik ang putik sa likod ko.","translation":"My motorcycle's **mudguard** broke, so mud splattered on my back."},{"sentence":"Magkano ang pagpapalit ng **tapalodo** sa harap?","translation":"How much is it to replace the front **fender**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglalabas ng hangin mula sa sikmura sa pamamagitan ng bibig na may kasamang tunog; gagawin sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: Future tense ng dighal. Ito 'yung warning mo sa katabi mo after uminom ng isang litrong Coke. 'Excuse me, parang **magdidighal** ako.' It's the body's natural way of saying 'Thank you for the food, ang busog ko!'
usage_notes: This is the future tense form. The root verb is 'dumighal'. 'Magdighal' is also a valid infinitive but less common than 'dumighal'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos niyang uminom ng soda, siguradong **magdidighal** siya.","translation":"After he drinks soda, he **will surely burp**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maingay, baka **magdidighal** ang sanggol.","translation":"Don't be noisy, the baby **might burp**."}]

translation: will fight with; will quarrel with
meaning_filipino: Sasali o makikisangkot sa isang alitan o pagtatalo sa hinaharap. Ito ang anyong panghinaharap ng pandiwang "makipag-away".
original_explanation: "Sige, subukan mo, makikipag-away talaga ako sa'yo!" (Go on, try me, I'll really fight you!). This is the future tense of picking a fight. It's the warning you give someone before things get messy, whether it's over a parking spot, a BPO account, or the last milk tea in the shop.
usage_notes: This is the future tense of `makipag-away`. It signifies an intention or a future action of engaging in a conflict with someone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang **makikipag-away** dahil lang sa maliit na bagay.","translation":"He doesn't want to **get into a fight** just because of a small thing."},{"sentence":"Talaga bang **makikipag-away** ka para sa prinsipyong iyan?","translation":"Are you really **going to fight** for that principle?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bantas (:) na ginagamit upang ihiwalay ang dalawang sugnay na magkaugnay o magpakilala ng isang listahan.
original_explanation: The punctuation mark that looks like it's perpetually surprised: The colon. In Filipino grammar, it's the "wait, there's more!" signal. You use a **tutuldok** before dropping a list, like your list of exes, your grocery list, or the reasons why you're still single. Halimbawa: Ito ang mga kailangan mo para sa masayang buhay: pera, pag-ibig, at good internet connection.
usage_notes: The name is derived from 'tuldok' (dot/period), essentially meaning 'two dots'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit ka ng **tutuldok** bago ilista ang mga sangkap.","translation":"Use a **colon** before listing the ingredients."},{"sentence":"Ang **tutuldok** ay isang mahalagang bantas sa pagsulat.","translation":"The **colon** is an important punctuation mark in writing."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit at makitid na puwang o bitak, tulad ng sa pader, pinto, o sa pagitan ng dalawang bagay.
original_explanation: That tiny gap in the curtains that lets the morning sun hit you directly in the eye. The small opening in the door your chismosa Tita peeks through. The crack in the wall where the ipis makes its grand entrance. It's a small space with big potential for annoyance or horror.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin nang literal para sa mga pisikal na puwang o metaporikal para sa isang maliit na pagkakataon, oportunidad, o kahinaan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May nakita akong anino na sumisilip sa **siwang** ng pinto.","translation":"I saw a shadow peeking through the **crack** of the door."},{"sentence":"Kahit maliit lang ang **siwang**, nakapasok pa rin ang lamok.","translation":"Even though the **opening** was small, the mosquito still got in."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na piraso ng papel na may marka o disenyo na idinidikit sa sulat bilang bayad sa serbisyong pangkoreo, o isang marka na iniiwan ng isang kagamitan upang magpatunay ng awtentisidad.
original_explanation: Before email and DMs, this was how you proved you paid to send your love letter. It's a postage stamp! It can also be the official 'taktak' or 'tatak' (stamp) from a government office that makes your document legit, often accompanied by the phrase 'for releasing.' In a metaphorical sense, 'selyado' means it's a done deal, sealed.
usage_notes: Can mean postage stamp, an official rubber stamp impression, or a seal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong lagyan ng **selyo** ang sulat bago ito ipadala sa post office.","translation":"You need to put a **stamp** on the letter before sending it to the post office."},{"sentence":"Wala pang opisyal na **selyo** ng munisipyo ang dokumento.","translation":"The document doesn't have the official municipal **seal** yet."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaikling anyo ng pariralang "hintay ka," na ginagamit upang hilingin sa isang tao na maghintay o huminto pansamantala.
original_explanation: The national pause button of the Philippines. Before any major decision, minor inconvenience, or just to gather your thoughts mid-chismis, you say "teka." It's the spoken equivalent of the buffering icon. "Teka, processing pa..."
usage_notes: Used informally in conversations. It's a command, a request, and a filler word all in one.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Teka**, ano ulit 'yung sinabi mo?","translation":"**Wait**, what did you say again?"},{"sentence":"**Teka** lang, may kinukuha lang ako.","translation":"**Hold on** a moment, I'm just getting something."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtuklap o pag-alis ng panlabas na balat, karaniwan ay dahil sa pagkasunog sa araw, sakit, o pagkatuyo.
etymology: From pa- + mam- (from ma- + balikaskas) + balikaskas. The root 'balikaskas' means 'peeled off' or 'flaked'.
original_explanation: That thing that happens to your skin after you get sunburnt at the beach and you start shedding like a snake? That's pamamalikaskas. It's your skin's dramatic way of saying 'You should have used more sunblock!' and hitting the reset button. Can also apply to peeling paint on an old wall.
usage_notes: Mostly used to describe skin peeling due to sunburn or dryness, or paint flaking off a surface.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit ka ng lotion para maiwasan ang **pamamalikaskas** ng iyong balat.","translation":"Use lotion to prevent the **peeling** of your skin."},{"sentence":"Ang **pamamalikaskas** ng pintura sa pader ay senyales na kailangan na itong pinturahan muli.","translation":"The **flaking** of the paint on the wall is a sign that it needs to be repainted."}]

meaning_filipino: Nilagyan ng sabaw ang isang pagkain. Maaari ring tumukoy sa isang ulam na maraming sabaw.
original_explanation: The ultimate life hack for extending ulam for one more meal. Got one piece of fried chicken left for a family of five? No problem, `sinabawan` with lots of water, Knorr cubes, and maybe some sad-looking pechay. Instant tinola! It's the culinary equivalent of "diskarte."
usage_notes: Can be a verb (action of adding broth, `Sinabawan ni nanay...`) or an adjective (describing a soupy dish, `ulam na sinabawan`).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sinabawan** ni nanay ang kanin para mas madaling kainin ng bata.","translation":"Mom **added broth** to the rice to make it easier for the child to eat."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang pritong isda, pero mas masarap kung may kasamang **sinabawan** na gulay.","translation":"Fried fish is delicious, but it's better with a side of **soupy** vegetables."}]

translation: to be cut; to be disconnected; to be severed
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkaputol, pagkahinto, o pagkatigil ng isang bagay na tuloy-tuloy, gaya ng linya, koneksyon, o daloy.
original_explanation: The official verb for when your WiFi dies mid-Zoom call, your Meralco connection gets cut, or your train of thought is interrupted by a chismosa neighbor. 'Nako, naputol ang internet, 'di ko na-submit 'yung report!' It's the universe's way of saying 'pause,' whether you like it or not. Also used for relationships ending: 'naputol ang ugnayan.'
usage_notes: Can refer to physical cutting or metaphorical disconnection.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Biglang **naputol** ang aming tawag sa telepono.","translation":"Our phone call was suddenly **disconnected**."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka at baka **maputol** ang lubid.","translation":"Be careful or the rope might **be cut**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng paggamit ng payong bilang proteksyon sa ulan o sa sikat ng araw.
original_explanation: A classic Filipino survival skill. You do this to avoid getting dark (ayaw umitim!), or to not get wet in the rain and ruin your hair. Ito yung moment na biglang uulan tapos may mag-ooffer sa'yo, "Gusto mo mamayong?" -- a simple act that can be the start of a rom-com scene.
usage_notes: This is a nominalized verb form. The verb form 'mamayong' (to use an umbrella) is more common in speech. 'Pamamayong' refers to the act itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa sobrang init, naging pangkaraniwan na ang **pamamayong** kahit hindi umuulan.","translation":"Because of the extreme heat, the **act of using an umbrella** has become common even when it's not raining."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula ang kanilang pagkakaibigan sa isang simpleng alok ng **pamamayong**.","translation":"Their friendship started with a simple offer of sharing an umbrella (literally: the **act of using an umbrella**)."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkaramdam ng matinding kalungkutan na may kasamang pag-iisa at kawalan ng pag-asa, karaniwan sa isang tahimik o tiwangwang na lugar.
original_explanation: This is sadness with an eerie, empty vibe. Imagine walking through a ghost town or an abandoned mall. That feeling of desolate loneliness? That's namamanglaw. It's sadness + isolation + a creepy, quiet atmosphere. Parang eksena sa horror film bago may lumabas na multo.
usage_notes: Isang napakalalim at pampanitikang salita para sa kalungkutan, kadalasang iniuugnay sa isang lugar o kapaligiran na nagdudulot ng pag-iisa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Namamanglaw** ang pakiramdam sa loob ng abandonadong bahay.","translation":"There is a **desolate** feeling inside the abandoned house."},{"sentence":"Mula nang iwan siya ng lahat, **namamanglaw** ang kanyang mga araw.","translation":"Ever since everyone left him, his days have been **forlorn**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang damdamin ng hindi mapalagay, pag-aalala, o takot, na kadalasang may kasamang pisikal na sintomas tulad ng mabilis na pagtibok ng puso o pagpapawis.
original_explanation: It's that 3 AM feeling when your brain decides to play a highlight reel of every mistake you've ever made. It's the 'Did I lock the door?' feeling, but for your entire life. It’s what you feel when you see 'We need to talk' or 'pumunta ka sa HR' in an email. It’s a mix of worry, fear, and a sudden urge to clean the entire house to distract yourself.
usage_notes: A common word to describe feelings of anxiety, worry, or unease. More internal and mental than 'kabalinuhan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang matinding **kabalisahan** bago ang kanyang job interview.","translation":"She felt extreme **anxiety** before her job interview."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang mag-meditate upang mabawasan ang kanyang **kabalisahan**.","translation":"He tries to meditate to reduce his **worry**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kumpletong landas na dinadaluyan ng kuryente. Sa mas malawak na kahulugan, isang regular na ruta o paglalakbay.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung Meralco bill mo, ito 'yung dahilan kung bakit may ilaw at WiFi ka. A 'sirkit' is the path electricity takes. Kapag 'short-circuited', 'yan 'yung parang relationship niyo, biglang nag-spark tapos biglang wala na.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa mga kontekstong teknikal o elektroniko. Ang 'sirkito' ay ang baryant na hango sa Espanyol at mas karaniwan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasunog ang **sirkit** ng telebisyon kaya hindi na gumagana.","translation":"The television's **circuit** burned out so it's not working anymore."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng electrician para ayusin ang depektibong **sirkit**.","translation":"An electrician is needed to fix the defective **circuit**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na globo ng hangin o gas na nabubuo sa loob o ibabaw ng isang likido. Maaari rin itong tumukoy sa makapal na kimpal ng mga bula na nabubuo, gaya ng sa sabon at tubig.
original_explanation: It's the magic stuff that appears when you wash dishes, do laundry, or take a bath. Also, a metaphor for something that looks good but is empty inside, like some promises. "Puro ka **bula**," means you're all talk, no action. Like a stock market bubble, it's exciting until it pops.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin nang literal para sa bula ng sabon o piguratibo para sa isang bagay na walang laman o saysay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig maglaro ng **bula** ang mga bata habang naliligo.","translation":"The kids love to play with **bubbles** while bathing."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga pangarap ay naglahong parang **bula**.","translation":"His dreams vanished like a **bubble**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang trabaho, libangan, o gawain ay ang pag-aalaga, pagsasanay, at paglalaban ng mga manok na panabong.
etymology: From `mag-` + reduplication of the first syllable of the root `sa-` + `sabong` (cockfight). The `magsa-` prefix denotes a profession or habitual doer.
original_explanation: Your tito who loves his roosters more than his own kids (kidding... maybe). He's the guy with the special 'vitamins' for his 'manok' and is always talking about 'kristo' and 'dehado' at the local 'sabungan'.
usage_notes: Refers to the person who engages in cockfighting, either as a hobby or profession.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala si Mang Jun bilang isang tanyag na **magsasabong** sa kanilang bayan.","translation":"Mang Jun is known as a famous **cockfighter** in their town."},{"sentence":"Maraming **magsasabong** ang dumayo para sa malaking derby.","translation":"Many **cockfighters** traveled for the big derby."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng legumbre na ang buto ay karaniwang kinakain bilang isang meryenda, na maaaring lutuin sa pamamagitan ng paglalaga, pagsasangag, o pagpiprito.
original_explanation: The ultimate pulutan and sinehan snack. Whether it's nilaga, adobo, or 'yung matamis na may balat, mani is a Filipino staple. Also, a slang term for something being "very easy." "Mani lang 'yan!" means "That's just peanuts!" or "That's a piece of cake!"
usage_notes: Stress is on the second syllable /ma-NI/ when referring to the food.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong pulutan ang nilagang **mani**.","translation":"Boiled **peanuts** are my favorite bar snack."},{"sentence":"Bumili ka ng **mani** sa may kanto.","translation":"Buy some **peanuts** at the corner."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng maraming sanga o dibisyon; ang paglawak sa iba't ibang direksyon o larangan.
original_explanation: Like a family tree that gets super complicated, or when a simple chismis (gossip) evolves into ten different dramatic subplots. It's also what your career does when you go from being an accountant to a vlogger to a plantito.
usage_notes: The repetition of 'sanga' implies multiple, complex branching. The infix '-um-' indicates the actor-focus, completed aspect (past tense).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang maliit na negosyo niya noon ay **sumanga-sanga** na sa iba't ibang industriya.","translation":"Her small business before has now **branched out** into different industries."},{"sentence":"Mula sa isang simpleng tanong, **sumanga-sanga** ang usapan namin hanggang madaling-araw.","translation":"From one simple question, our conversation **branched out** until dawn."}]

translation: severe thrashing; a place full of 'lipa' plants
meaning_filipino: Sa matalinhagang kahulugan, ito ay tumutukoy sa matinding pagpalo o bugbog. Sa literal na kahulugan, isang lugar na maraming tumutubong halamang lipa (Dendrocnide meyeniana).
original_explanation: Literally, a place you do NOT want to fall into, as it's full of the 'lipa' plant, the botanical equivalent of a thousand tiny needles. Figuratively, it's what your parents threatened you with when you were a kid. "Gusto mo ng lipakan?" meant "Do you want a severe spanking?" It's a beating so bad, it feels like you rolled around in a field of stinging nettles.
usage_notes: The literal meaning is rare in conversation. The figurative meaning of 'a severe beating' is more common, though somewhat old-fashioned.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binigyan siya ng **lipakan** ng kanyang ama dahil sa pagiging suwail.","translation":"He was given a **severe thrashing** by his father for being disobedient."},{"sentence":"Iwasan mong pumasok sa **lipakan** sa likod ng gubat.","translation":"Avoid entering the **place full of lipa plants** behind the forest."}]

translation: To change hands; to transfer ownership.
meaning_filipino: Ilipat ang pagmamay-ari o responsibilidad ng isang bagay mula sa isang tao patungo sa iba.
original_explanation: It's like 'pass the parcel' but with serious stuff like property titles, car registrations, or the family's secret adobo recipe. When a business is sold, it's said to maglipat-kamay. It's the official term for when something is no longer yours, for better or for worse.
usage_notes: A compound verb that is idiomatic. It literally means "to transfer hand" but signifies a change in ownership or control.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matapos ang ilang dekada, ang lumang bahay ay **naglipat-kamay** na sa bagong pamilya.","translation":"After several decades, the old house has **changed hands** to a new family."},{"sentence":"Mabilis na **naglipat-kamay** ang mga dokumento nang matapos ang bentahan.","translation":"The documents quickly **transferred ownership** after the sale was completed."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang napakaliit na kulisap o araknida, karaniwang isang uri ng kuto o garapata, na nabubuhay bilang parasito sa mga hayop o halaman.
original_explanation: It's that tiny, annoying pest you can barely see but definitely feel. Think of it as the micro-influencer of the insect world—small, but causes major irritation. Not the kind of 'tungo' (direction) you want to be headed towards.
usage_notes: This is a less common meaning than the preposition. The pronunciation differs, with stress on the second syllable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinakamot ng aso ang kanyang balahibo dahil sa mga **tungo**.","translation":"The dog is scratching its fur because of the **mites**."},{"sentence":"Kailangang linisin ang lumang kutson para mawala ang mga **tungo**.","translation":"The old mattress needs to be cleaned to get rid of the **mites**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng sapilitang pagkuha ng pera o anumang bagay na may halaga mula sa isang tao, kadalasan sa pamamagitan ng pananakot o paggamit ng kapangyarihan.
original_explanation: This is the "pahingi ako ng pera" that isn't a friendly request. It's when someone, maybe a corrupt official or a freeloader 'friend', consistently drains your wallet. It’s the ultimate ‘budol’ but with a hint of threat. "Grabe ang huthot ng buwaya sa gobyerno."
usage_notes: Carries a strong negative connotation related to corruption and exploitation. The root word for 'huthutan' and 'huthutin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang talamak na **huthot** ay isa sa mga suliranin ng bansa.","translation":"Widespread **extortion** is one of the country's problems."},{"sentence":"Biktima siya ng **huthot** ng mga sindikato.","translation":"He was a victim of **extortion** by syndicates."}]

meaning_filipino: Gamitin ang isang pagkain bilang pangunahing putahe na isinasabay sa kanin.
original_explanation: That moment of desperation when you open the fridge and there's nothing but leftover hotdogs. You shrug and say, "Puwede na 'to i-ulam." It's the verb form of turning literally anything edible—from last night's adobo to a pack of chicharon—into a partner for your rice. The ultimate Filipino survival skill.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano kaya ang masarap **iulam** sa sinangag?","translation":"What do you think is delicious to **use as a viand** with fried rice?"},{"sentence":"Kahit tuyo lang, basta't may **maiuulam** ay sapat na.","translation":"Even just dried fish, as long as there is something **to be used as a viand**, is enough."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing yari sa tanso o balutan ng tanso ang isang bagay.
etymology: From 'tanso' (brass) + '-in' (verb suffix). 'Tanso' itself is from Hokkien 'tâng-sú' (bronze).
original_explanation: It's like when you're so into that brass/bronze aesthetic for your condo, you want everything to have that metallic, slightly vintage look. 'Tansuin mo 'yang door knob para magmukhang antique.' It means to cover or make something out of brass.
usage_notes: Not a very common verb. It's more common to hear 'yari sa tanso' (made of brass).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan siyang **tansuin** ang mga plake para sa parangal.","translation":"He was instructed to **plate the plaques with brass** for the award."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapahayag ng paghanga, paggalang, o mabuting salita tungkol sa isang tao, bagay, o gawa.
original_explanation: The opposite of "mambasag." It's what you do when your friend's OOTD is on point ("Uy, ganda ng suot mo!"). It's also what you do to your boss right before asking for a leave. "Magpuri ka muna bago humingi ng pabor, 'yan ang technique."
usage_notes: A general act of giving praise. For mutual praise, see 'magpurihan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-atubiling **magpuri** sa kapwa mo kung may nagawa silang mabuti.","translation":"Don't hesitate to **praise** your fellow person if they have done something good."},{"sentence":"Likas sa kanya ang **magpuri** sa kagandahan ng kalikasan.","translation":"It's natural for him to **praise** the beauty of nature."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagdudulot ng matinding paghanga o panggigilalas; kahanga-hanga.
original_explanation: That feeling when you see the Mayon Volcano for the first time, or when your GrabFood arrives in under 10 minutes. It's something that makes you go 'Wow!' or 'Sana all!'. Truly makamangha.
usage_notes: Describes something that causes a sense of awe or wonder.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **makamangha** na tanawin ang paglubog ng araw sa Manila Bay.","translation":"The sunset at Manila Bay is an **amazing** sight."},{"sentence":"Ang galing ng bata sa pagkanta ay talagang **makamangha**.","translation":"The child's singing ability is truly **astonishing**."}]

meaning_filipino: Gumawa ng kilos ng pagganti laban sa isang tao o pangkat dahil sa isang naunang kasalanan o pinsala.
original_explanation: That feeling when you were ghosted, then they slide back into your DMs after two years and you just leave them on 'seen'. That's you, bumenggansa. It’s the ultimate 'the receipts are in' moment, but make it dramatic like a teleserye finale. The sweet, petty satisfaction of 'resbak'.
usage_notes: Often used in dramatic or formal contexts. The more common, everyday word is 'gumanti'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumenggansa** ang koponan sa kanilang mahigpit na karibal matapos ang masaklap na pagkatalo noong nakaraang taon.","translation":"The team **took revenge** on their bitter rivals after a painful loss last year."},{"sentence":"Sa huli, hindi siya **bumenggansa** at pinili na lang niyang magpatawad.","translation":"In the end, he did not **retaliate** and just chose to forgive."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa bilang, sukat, o tindi ng isang bagay; karamihan.
original_explanation: When your mom comes back from the palengke and you see bags of veggies, that's 'dami'. When you open your Meralco bill and scream, it's because of the 'dami' of the charges. It's the default Filipino exclamation for 'so much' or 'so many'. 'Ang dami!' can express joy (ang daming pagkain!), stress (ang daming trabaho!), or surprise (ang daming tao!).
usage_notes: Often used in exclamations 'Ang dami!' (So much/many!). Can function as a noun ('ang dami ng tao') or an adjective-like word ('daming tao').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko inasahan ang **dami** ng taong dumalo.","translation":"I did not expect the **quantity** of people who attended."},{"sentence":"Wow, ang **dami** mong libro!","translation":"Wow, you have **a lot** of books!"}]

translation: to be noticed; to be perceived; to become obvious
meaning_filipino: Ang mapansin o matuklasan ang isang bagay na sinusubukang itago o hindi ipaalam, gaya ng isang damdamin, lihim, o kalagayan.
original_explanation: That "Oh no, they know!" feeling. It's when you're trying to act cool around your crush but you're blushing like a tomato. O kaya 'yung pilit mong tinatago na ubos mo na sahod mo a-kinse pa lang, pero 'yung mukha mo, mukha nang petsa de peligro. Your poker face failed. Busted!
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin para sa mga damdamin, intensyon, o lihim na hindi sinasadyang mabunyag.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang ngumiti nang todo para hindi **mahalata** na kinikilig ka.","translation":"Don't smile too much so it won't **be noticed** that you're giddy."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang itago ang lungkot, ngunit **nahalata** pa rin sa kanyang mga mata.","translation":"She tried to hide her sadness, but it was still **perceived** in her eyes."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-angat ng ulo o mukha upang tumingin sa itaas.
original_explanation: The opposite of 'yuko.' It's what you do when you're looking for your kite, checking if it's going to rain, or admiring a tall building. It’s also a gesture of hope or prayer. But in the modern world, it's what you do when you hear a drone, an airplane, or when someone from the 5th floor calls your name. It's the physical act of aiming your gaze skyward.
usage_notes: The direct opposite of "yumuko" (to bow or look down).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumingala** siya sa langit at nagdasal.","translation":"He **looked up** at the sky and prayed."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang laging **tumingala**, baka may mahulog sa ulo mo.","translation":"Don't always **look up**, something might fall on your head."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang babaeng may malalim na pananampalataya, palasimba, at namumuhay ayon sa mga aral ng kanyang relihiyon.
original_explanation: She's the tita who posts "God is good" inspirational quotes every morning on Facebook. She never misses Simbang Gabi, and her default advice for any problem is "Ipag-pray mo lang 'yan, hija." While it can also refer to a nun, it's more commonly used to describe any woman who is very devout and makes sure you know it.
usage_notes: Ito ang pambabaeng anyo ng salitang "relihiyoso". Maaari ring gamitin bilang pangngalan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala ang lola ko sa aming bayan bilang isang babaeng tunay na **relihiyosa**.","translation":"My grandmother is known in our town as a truly **religious** woman."},{"sentence":"Naging mas **relihiyosa** si Ana mula nang sumali siya sa kanilang choir sa simbahan.","translation":"Ana became more **religious** ever since she joined their church choir."}]

meaning_filipino: May bilang o marka na numero; nakalista o inayos ayon sa pagkakasunod-sunod ng mga numero.
original_explanation: Like your crush's other admirers, you're just one of many, aka 'numerado'. You have a number and you're just waiting in line. Also, this is what you do with your laundry list of 'utang' sa sari-sari store.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit para sa mga bagay na bahagi ng isang serye, tulad ng mga bahay, pahina, o tiket.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lahat ng upuan sa sinehan ay **numerado**.","translation":"All the seats in the cinema are **numbered**."},{"sentence":"Pakisulat ang mga pangalan sa isang **numerado**ng listahan.","translation":"Please write the names on a **numbered** list."}]

translation: to strike, to hit, to lash
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpalo o pagtama nang may lakas sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'hampas.' This is what you do *with* the 'tsinelas' when your kid is being makulit. It's the command form: 'Hampasin mo 'yung lamok!' (Hit the mosquito!). It implies a swift, forceful action to make contact.
usage_notes: An object-focused verb. The action is done *to* the object.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Galit na **hinampas** niya ang mesa.","translation":"He angrily **struck** the table."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **hampasin** ang aso, hindi niya kasalanan.","translation":"Don't **hit** the dog, it's not its fault."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalagyan o lugar, karaniwang may gripo at paagusan, na ginagamit sa paghuhugas ng mga kamay, pinggan, o iba pang bagay.
original_explanation: The battlefield of every Filipino household. This is where the debate "Sino'ng taya sa hugas-plato?" happens. It's where you find a mountain of dishes after a fiesta, and where you secretly rinse a spoon you dropped on the floor (5-second rule!). It's the sink, the lababo, the epicenter of kitchen cleanliness.
usage_notes: Can also refer to the thing *to be washed* in some contexts, but its primary meaning is the place of washing (sink). The verb form is "hugasan" (to wash something). This noun form is less common than "lababo".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ilagay mo ang mga maruruming plato sa **paghugasan**.","translation":"Put the dirty plates in the **sink**."},{"sentence":"Barado na naman ang ating **paghugasan** sa kusina.","translation":"Our kitchen **sink** is clogged again."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lutuin, karaniwan ay isda, na pinirito at ibinabad sa isang sarsang matamis at maasim na gawa sa suka, asukal, at mga gulay tulad ng karot at bell pepper.
original_explanation: The Filipino sweet and sour fish that's a fiesta staple. It’s that brightly colored dish with fried fish swimming in a tangy, sweet sauce with carrots and bell peppers. It’s what happens when you want your fried fish to have a little more ~pizzazz~. Perfect with a mountain of rice.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa isang partikular na uri ng lutuin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-request si Lolo ng **eskabetse** para sa kanyang kaarawan.","translation":"Grandpa requested **escabeche** for his birthday."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang **eskabetse** kapag malutong pa ang isda.","translation":"**Sweet and sour fish** is delicious when the fish is still crispy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nasa ilalim ng pag-aalaga, paggabay, o proteksyon ng isang mas makapangyarihan o maimpluwensyang indibidwal.
original_explanation: Ito yung 'bata' ng isang boss sa office o sa pulitika. Siya yung laging may special treatment, unang napo-promote, at laging ligtas sa layoff kasi may 'backer' na malakas. Parang 'anak-anakan' sa trabaho.
usage_notes: Often has a slightly negative connotation, implying favoritism or nepotism, especially in a political or corporate context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya bilang **protehido** ng mayor kaya hindi siya natitinag sa puwesto.","translation":"He is known as the mayor's **protégé**, which is why he is unshakable in his position."},{"sentence":"Bilang isang mentor, tungkulin mong gabayan ang iyong **protehido**.","translation":"As a mentor, it is your duty to guide your **protégé**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maramihan o masidhing pagbabanggaan ng mga bagay, tao, o sasakyan.
etymology: From 'mag-' + 'ka-' + 'bunggo' + '-an'. The '-an' suffix often indicates a place or a more intense, reciprocal action.
original_explanation: This isn't just a simple bump. This is the EDSA-at-rush-hour, multiple-car-pile-up version of 'magkabunggo'. Think bumper cars but with real consequences and lots of shouting. It's the chaos of a palengke on a Saturday morning where everyone seems to be bumping into everyone else. It's plural, it's intense, it's a mess.
usage_notes: More intense and often involves more than two parties compared to 'magkabunggo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang dami ng tao sa concert, hindi maiwasang **magkabungguan**.","translation":"With so many people at the concert, it was unavoidable for them to **collide with each other**."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula ang gulo nang **magkabungguan** ang dalawang grupo ng manonood.","translation":"The trouble started when the two groups of spectators **collided with each other**."}]

meaning_filipino: Daglat para sa "Lover's Quarrel," na tumutukoy sa isang away o hindi pagkakaunawaan sa pagitan ng magkasintahan.
original_explanation: Stands for "Lover's Quarrel." It's that silent treatment phase, the one-word replies, the "K." text message. You're not breaking up, but the emotional climate is colder than the aircon in a BPO office. Usually solved by a good conversation or, let's be real, a milk tea peace offering.
usage_notes: A very common slang/colloquial term used by couples.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong kausapin, **LQ** kami ngayon.","translation":"Don't talk to me, we're having an **LQ** right now."},{"sentence":"Mukhang may **LQ** na naman sina Ben at Ana, ang tahimik nila.","translation":"It looks like Ben and Ana are having an **LQ** again, they're so quiet."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng isa o higit pang tadyak sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: When you give someone a 'tadyak'. "Huwag mo akong simulan, baka tadyakan kita papuntang Mars." Ito ang action word para sa paninipa nang malakas.
usage_notes: Ang '-an' sa hulihan ay nagpapahiwatig na ang aksyon ay direktang ginagawa sa isang tao o bagay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binalaan niya ang aso na huwag siyang lapitan o **tatadyakan** niya ito.","translation":"He warned the dog not to come near or he would **kick** it."},{"sentence":"Nagpambuno sila at nagsimulang mag-**tadyakan**.","translation":"They wrestled and started to **kick** each other."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bilang na kasunod ng labing-walo at bago ang dalawampu; katumbas ng 19.
etymology: From "labi" (excess, remainder) + "-ng" + "siyam" (nine), literally "excess of ten by nine". The 'g' in 'labing' is dropped and becomes 'n' before 's' for easier pronunciation.
original_explanation: The awkward year between being a legal adult and actually feeling like one. It's also the number of times you hit the snooze button before finally getting up for your 8 AM class.
usage_notes: Can be written as "labinsiyam" or "labing-siyam". The Spanish-derived "disinuwebe" is also used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Labinsiyam** na kandidata ang naglaban-laban para sa korona.","translation":"**Nineteen** candidates competed for the crown."},{"sentence":"Halos **labinsiyam** na taon na pala tayong magkaibigan.","translation":"We've been friends for almost **nineteen** years."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi pa ganap na hinog; bata pa o wala pa sa hustong gulang o pag-iisip.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping pang-uri na 'ma-' at ang salitang ugat na 'mura' (unripe, young).
original_explanation: Describes something that's not quite ready yet. Like that green mango that's super sour, or your younger sibling who still makes 'bata' decisions. It can also be a slightly polite way of calling someone immature. 'Medyo mamura-mura pa ang isip niyan.'
usage_notes: Madalas itong inuulit ('mamura-mura') upang ipahiwatig ang 'medyo' o 'bahagyang' mura pa. Ang anyong 'mamura' ay tumutukoy sa katangian.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Mamura** pa ang mga manggang ito para pitasin.","translation":"These mangoes are still **unripe** to be picked."},{"sentence":"Hayaan mo na siya, **mamura** pa ang pag-iisip kaya ganoon.","translation":"Just let him be, his thinking is still **immature**, that's why he's like that."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sangay ng agham na nag-aaral sa buhay at mga organismong may buhay, kabilang ang kanilang estruktura, tungkulin, paglaki, pinagmulan, ebolusyon, at distribusyon.
etymology: Isang neolohismo o salitang binuo mula sa "hanayan ng buhay". Hindi ito karaniwang ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
original_explanation: This is the Tagalog word for Biology, a purist term that didn't quite stick. Parang yung "Salumpuwit" for chair. It's the subject where you study plants, animals, and the human body. Basically, the science of 'buhay', which is ironic kasi minsan ito yung subject na papatay sa'yo sa high school.
usage_notes: Isang salitang akademiko at pampanitikan na nilikha upang maging katumbas ng "biology". Ang "biyolohiya" ay mas karaniwang ginagamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **haynayan** ay isang mahalagang asignatura sa pag-aaral ng mga natural na agham.","translation":"**Biology** is an important subject in the study of natural sciences."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kabuuan ng mga katangian, pag-uugali, paniniwala, at prinsipyo na bumubuo sa isang indibidwal; ang esensya ng pagiging isang tao.
original_explanation: This is your deep, core self. It’s what’s left when you strip away your job title, your social media profile, and your OOTD. It's your character, your values, your 'dignidad.' When someone says 'Winasak mo ang pagkatao ko,' it's the ultimate hugot line, meaning you've crushed their very soul, not just their feelings. It's heavy stuff.
usage_notes: A profound word that can mean 'personality', 'character', 'identity', or the abstract concept of 'humanity' or 'personhood'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga na pangalagaan ang iyong **pagkatao** at reputasyon.","translation":"It's important to take care of your **identity** and reputation."},{"sentence":"Ang tunay na sukat ng isang tao ay nasa kanyang **pagkatao**, hindi sa yaman.","translation":"The true measure of a person is in their **character**, not in wealth."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nag-aalaga, nagbabantay, at gumagabay sa isang kawan ng mga hayop, tulad ng tupa o kambing.
original_explanation: The original animal welfare advocate. Sila yung nag-aalaga ng mga tupa at kambing sa bukid. Sa Christmas, sila yung laging may dalang tupa sa Belen. The OG 'pet-sitter' for farm animals.
usage_notes: Partikular na tumutukoy sa isang pastol ng mga hayop. Bagama't kaugnay ng "pastor" (ng isang simbahan), ang "pastol" ay eksklusibo para sa pag-aalaga ng hayop.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pastol** ay dinala ang kanyang kawan ng tupa sa mas luntiang pastulan.","translation":"The **shepherd** brought his flock of sheep to a greener pasture."},{"sentence":"Sa kwento ng Bibliya, binisita ng mga **pastol** ang sanggol na si Hesus.","translation":"In the Bible story, the **shepherds** visited the baby Jesus."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang anyong panghinaharap ng pandiwang 'magsugal'. Tumutukoy sa gagawing pakikipaglaro na may pusta o taya, na nakadepende sa swerte.
original_explanation: This is the verb you use when you're about to risk it all—your sweldo, your baon, your dignity—on a game of chance. "Tara, magsusugal tayo!" is either the start of a fun night or a cautionary tale. It's the future tense of taking a chance.
usage_notes: This is the future tense of the verb 'magsugal' (to gamble). The infinitive form is 'magsugal'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magsusugal** na naman daw si Tiyo Roger.","translation":"They say Uncle Roger **will gamble** again."},{"sentence":"Nangako siyang hindi na siya **magsusugal** kailanman.","translation":"He promised that he **will** never **gamble** again."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasanib o pagdidikit ng dalawang bagay, karaniwan ay mga palad, bilang tanda ng pagkakaisa, pagdarasal, o pagbibigay-galang.
original_explanation: That moment in a wedding when the priest says, "Now, join your hands." That's magdaop. It's also what you do when you're praying really hard for your online shopping package to arrive on time. It’s a very formal "holding hands."
usage_notes: Often used in formal or ceremonial contexts, like weddings ('pag-iisang-dibdib' involves 'pagdadaop-palad') or prayer.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hiniling sa magkasintahan na **magdaop** ang kanilang mga palad.","translation":"The couple was asked to **join** their **palms**."},{"sentence":"Sila ay umupo nang tahimik at nag-antay, na **magkadaop** ang mga kamay.","translation":"They sat quietly and waited, with their hands **joined**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng harang sa isang daanan, espasyo, o tao upang hindi ito madaanan o makakilos.
etymology: harang + -an (suffix indicating the location or recipient of the action)
original_explanation: This is the action of putting up a barrier. It's what the MMDA does to a street for a road repair. It's what your sibling does with a pillow to mark their territory on the bed. 'Harangan mo yung pinto!' (Block the door!) is a classic line in Filipino action movies or when you're trying to hide from someone you owe money to.
usage_notes: Verb. The focus is on the place or path being blocked. 'Harangan mo ang daan.' (Block the path). It is distinct from 'harangin' which focuses on the person or thing being blocked from proceeding.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **harangan** ang daan para makalabas ang mga sasakyan.","translation":"Don't **block** the way so the cars can get out."},{"sentence":"**Hinaranagan** ng mga pulis ang lugar ng krimen.","translation":"The police **obstructed** (cordoned off) the crime scene."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapatunog sa isang maliit na kampana o batingaw.
original_explanation: This is the action you do to produce the 'kuliling' sound. You 'kulilingin' the bell at the front desk to get the receptionist's attention after they've been on their phone for 5 minutes. It's the verb for making that cute little bell sound, often done repeatedly to signal something or call someone.
usage_notes: The focus of the verb is the bell being rung.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **kulilingin** nang malakas ang kampana para marinig ka.","translation":"You need **to ring** the bell loudly for you to be heard."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **kulilingin** 'yan, baka magising ang sanggol.","translation":"Don't **ring** that, the baby might wake up."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o bagay na hindi nararapat na pagbintangan o iturong sanhi ng isang kamalian o masamang pangyayari.
etymology: Kombinasyon ng 'di' (not), 'dapat' (should), at 'sisihin' (to blame), mula sa ugat na 'sisi'.
original_explanation: This is your go-to defense when you're the 'pabida' who suggested a food trip, but the food turned out to be terrible. 'Uy, **di dapat sisihin** ang nag-suggest, sinubukan lang naman natin!' It's the 'don't shoot the messenger' of Filipino excuses.
usage_notes: Isang parirala na ginagamit upang alisin ang sisi sa isang tao o bagay.
