meaning_filipino: Mabigyan ng solusyon o kasagutan ang isang problema, suliranin, o katanungan.
original_explanation: This is the goal for every 'chismis' in the office—to get to the bottom of it. It's what you hope happens to your team's production bug before the client finds out. 'Sana malutas na 'to bago mag-release.'
usage_notes: Often used for problems, mysteries, or conflicts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umaasa ang lahat na **malutas** na ang krisis sa lalong madaling panahon.","translation":"Everyone is hoping the crisis will **be resolved** as soon as possible."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **malutas** ang problema kung hindi tayo magtutulungan.","translation":"The problem is hard **to solve** if we don't help each other."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang masidhi at tuloy-tuloy na paggamit ng masasamang salita o pagmumura laban sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: This is the verbal equivalent of a volcanic eruption. It's what happens when someone cuts you off in traffic on EDSA, or when your internet connection dies during a ranked game. A non-stop, expletive-filled rant. Think of it as the ultimate 'beast mode' of complaining.
usage_notes: Implies a loud, angry, and public display of verbal abuse, often sustained over a period.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig sa buong kalsada ang kanyang **pagtutungayaw** matapos siyang mabangga.","translation":"His **tirade** was heard all over the street after he got hit."},{"sentence":"Itigil mo na ang **pagtutungayaw** mo at huminahon ka.","translation":"Stop your **profuse cursing** and calm down."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging sanhi upang ang isang tao ay maglaway, karaniwan dahil sa matinding pagnanasa sa pagkain o sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the effect of food vlogs showing crispy lechon or cheese being pulled. 'Yung amoy ng bagong saing na kanin at adobo? It will **papaglawayin** you. It's to cause an involuntary, drooling reaction of desire.
usage_notes: Often used metaphorically to mean 'to make someone crave or desire something intensely', not just literally salivate.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang litrato ng mangga na may bagoong ay sapat na para **papaglawayin** ako.","translation":"The picture of mango with shrimp paste is enough to **make me drool**."},{"sentence":"Ipinakita niya ang bago niyang cellphone para **papaglawayin** sa inggit ang mga kaibigan.","translation":"He showed off his new cellphone to **make** his friends **drool** with envy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-awit ng mga awiting pag-ibig para sa isang nililigawan, karaniwan sa tapat ng bahay nito.
original_explanation: The infinitive form of the legendary Filipino courtship ritual. Instead of just sliding into DMs, you'd literally go to someone's house with a guitar and sing. 'Gusto ko sanang **mangharana** pero baka batuhin ako ng kapitbahay.' (I'd like to serenade someone, but the neighbors might throw rocks at me.)
usage_notes: This is the infinitive/base form of the verb. It is distinct from 'manghaharana', which is the future tense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang nawawalang tradisyon na ang **mangharana** sa ilalim ng bintana.","translation":"**To serenade** under a window is a disappearing tradition."},{"sentence":"Nagpaturo si Leo na tumugtog ng gitara upang **mangharana**.","translation":"Leo learned to play the guitar in order **to serenade**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na may hilig o tendensiyang ayusin ang mga gusot, alitan, o hindi pagkakasundo.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `mapag-` (na nagsasaad ng hilig) + `ayos` (pag-aareglo, paglutas).
original_explanation: Siya 'yung friend sa group chat na laging "Kalma lang guys," kapag may nag-aaway. The designated peacemaker. Sila yung ayaw ng gulo at laging naghahanap ng win-win solution para sa lahat. Kung may issue sa office, siya yung unang mag-aalok na mag-usap para ma-settle.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan sa papel ng isang tao sa paglutas ng sigalot.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Salamat sa pagiging **mapag-ayos** mo, kung hindi ay baka hindi na kami nag-uusap ngayon.","translation":"Thanks to your **conciliatory** nature, otherwise we might not be talking to each other now."},{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng lider na **mapag-ayos** upang magkaisa ang ating grupo.","translation":"We need a **conciliatory** leader to unite our group."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng paghingi o pagkolekta ng donasyon o abuloy, karaniwan para sa isang kawanggawa, proyekto, o para sa isang taong nangangailangan.
original_explanation: Eto yung formal term for "pa-ambag po" or "para sa project po namin." Yung may sobreng umiikot sa office para sa birthday ng boss, o yung mga estudyanteng kumakatok sa pinto niyo with a can for their "Linggo ng Wika" funds. That whole process is pangingilak. It’s the art of collecting money for a cause.
usage_notes: Commonly associated with charity drives, church collections, or community projects.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pangingilak** ng pondo ay para sa mga biktima ng bagyo.","translation":"The **fundraising** is for the victims of the typhoon."},{"sentence":"Naging matagumpay ang kanilang **pangingilak** para sa pagpapagawa ng bagong kapilya.","translation":"Their **solicitation of funds** for the construction of the new chapel was successful."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hangganan ng lupa at dagat; ang dalampasigan.
original_explanation: Your go-to place for summer outings, team buildings, or just some serious 'hugot' while staring at the sunset. It's where you take your aesthetic IG photos, build sandcastles, and contemplate your life choices. Boracay, La Union, Siargao... you get the picture.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'dalampasigan' or 'tabing-dagat'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglakad-lakad kami sa **baybay-dagat** habang papalubog ang araw.","translation":"We walked along the **seashore** as the sun was setting."},{"sentence":"Maraming resort na matatagpuan sa **baybay-dagat** ng Batangas.","translation":"There are many resorts found on the **coastline** of Batangas."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang pagbibigay ng matinding gulat o pagkabigla sa isang tao.
original_explanation: This is the action of making someone 'gulantang'. It's what your friend does when they jump out from behind a door shouting 'Boo!'. It's what a plot twist in a movie does to the audience. It's the verb form of dropping a bombshell chismis in the group chat just to see the chaos unfold.
usage_notes: The verb form of 'gulantang', meaning to cause someone to be in that state.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo siyang **gulantangin**; baka atakihin sa puso.","translation":"Don't **startle** her; she might have a heart attack."},{"sentence":"Nais nilang **gulantangin** ang buong mundo sa kanilang bagong imbensyon.","translation":"They want to **shock** the whole world with their new invention."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang estado ng pagkasira o dekomposisyon, lalo na sa pagkain; maaari ring tumukoy sa isang sistemang sira o korap.
original_explanation: 'Yung amoy ng saging na naging itim na sa sobrang hinog, o 'yung isda na iniwan mo sa labas ng ref. That's bulok. Figuratively, ito rin ang tawag sa sistema na puno ng corruption ("bulok na sistema") o sa palusot na hindi kapani-paniwala ("bulok na dahilan"). It's the ultimate descriptor for anything that's gone bad, literally or morally.
usage_notes: Isang napaka-karaniwang salita na may literal at matalinghagang gamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itapon mo na 'yang kamatis, **bulok** na.","translation":"Throw that tomato away, it's already **rotten**."},{"sentence":"Marami ang naniniwala na **bulok** ang sistema ng hustisya sa bansa.","translation":"Many believe that the justice system in the country is **corrupt**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita o pagmamayabang ng isang bagay na pag-aari, kakayahan, o tagumpay, karaniwan sa paraang mapagmataas o para ipaalam sa iba.
etymology: From English 'flex', meaning to show off one's muscles, which evolved into showing off anything of value.
original_explanation: 'I-flex mo lang' is the new 'Sana all.' It's when you post your new iPhone, your travel pics from La Union, or even your jowa on social media for the world to see and envy. It's the national sport of the 'blessed and grateful' crowd.
usage_notes: Commonly used in social media contexts. Often used with the prefix 'i-' (i-flex) to mean 'to flex [something]'. It can be used for proud, non-arrogant sharing (e.g., 'flexing' one's parents) or for pure boasting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang i-**flex** 'yang bago mong sapatos, baka magasgasan lang.","translation":"Don't **show off** your new shoes, they might just get scratched."},{"sentence":"Gusto kong i-**flex** ang mga magulang ko dahil sa lahat ng sakripisyo nila.","translation":"I want to **show off** (in a proud way) my parents for all their sacrifices."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang masalimuot na sitwasyon, gusot, o hindi pagkakasundo sa pagitan ng mga tao na nagdudulot ng samaan ng loob.
original_explanation: 'Yung may 'something' sa inyo ng ka-work mo na hindi niyo pinag-uusapan pero ramdam niyo pareho. That silent tension, 'yung gusot sa relasyon. It's the messy, tangled-up state of affairs, be it in office politics or family drama. Parang sinulid na nagkabuhol-buhol.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa mga kumplikadong problema o hidwaan sa pagitan ng mga tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **aligutgot** sa kanilang pamilya na kailangang ayusin.","translation":"There is a lot of **friction** in their family that needs to be resolved."},{"sentence":"Gusto kong iwasan ang anumang **aligutgot** sa opisina.","translation":"I want to avoid any **complications** at the office."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uunat ng mga kalamnan o bahagi ng katawan, karaniwan pagkatapos magising, matulog, o matagal na pag-upo.
original_explanation: That super satisfying, full-body stretch you do first thing in the morning, sometimes with a little groan. It's your body's way of rebooting after being idle, like a computer starting up. Also what you do in the office after a long meeting that could have been an email.
usage_notes: Ang pandiwa nito ay 'mag-inat' o 'umunat'. Ang 'inat' ay ang pangngalan para sa kilos mismo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malalim na hininga at isang mahabang **inat** ang ginawa niya pagkagising.","translation":"A deep breath and a long **stretch** was what she did upon waking up."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong mag-**inat** dahil nangangalay na ang likod ko sa pag-upo.","translation":"I need to **stretch** because my back is getting stiff from sitting."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamataas na bahagi, punto, o antas ng isang bagay; ang kalagayan ng pagiging suprema o pinakadakila.
etymology: From ka- + taas + -an, signifying the abstract quality or location of being 'high'.
original_explanation: Think of it as the 'boss level' of anything. Sa bundok, it's the summit where you take your profile pic. Sa career, it's the CEO position. Sa love life... well, 'yan 'yung level na sana all. The peak, the pinnacle, the 'you have arrived' moment.
usage_notes: Often used in both literal (physical height) and figurative (status, power) contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natanaw niya ang lawak ng lupain mula sa **kaitaasan** ng bundok.","translation":"He viewed the vastness of the land from the **summit** of the mountain."},{"sentence":"Narating na niya ang **kaitaasan** ng kanyang karera bilang isang aktor.","translation":"He has reached the **pinnacle** of his career as an actor."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang alinman sa dalawang buto na nag-uugnay sa sternum (buto sa dibdib) at sa mga balikat.
original_explanation: That bone that pops out when you're feeling 'payat' or when you pose for that 'angas' profile pic. It's the body's built-in hanger for necklaces. If you fall off your bike, there's a good chance you might break this.
usage_notes: A specific anatomical term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nabali ang kanyang **balagat** nang mahulog siya sa hagdan.","translation":"His **collarbone** broke when he fell down the stairs."},{"sentence":"Kitang-kita ang **balagat** ng modelo sa kanyang larawan.","translation":"The model's **collarbone** is very visible in her picture."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sumailalim sa pagbabago; magkaroon ng kaibahan mula sa dating anyo, katangian, o kalagayan.
original_explanation: That moment when your boss says, "The deadline has been moved," and your whole week's plan has to mabago. It's what happens to your relationship status from "in a relationship" to "it's complicated." It's the potential for something to be different, for better or for worse.
usage_notes: Refers to the possibility or actuality of something being changed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay **mabago** pa ang desisyon ng komite.","translation":"I hope the committee's decision can still **be changed**."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang pinagkaiba niya; hindi ko akalaing kaya niyang **mabago** nang ganoon.","translation":"He's so different; I didn't think he could **be changed** like that."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng pansin, interes, o paglahok sa isang bagay o usapin na maaaring hindi tuwirang saklaw ng isang tao.
etymology: From paki- (request/involvement) + alam (know). Literally, "to involve oneself in knowing."
original_explanation: The Filipino concept of 'giving a damn'. "Wala akong pakialam" is the iconic "I don't care," the verbal equivalent of shrugging your shoulders at someone's drama. It's what you feel when your tita asks about your love life for the nth time at a family reunion.
usage_notes: Often used in the negative form "walang pakialam" (to not care). The verb form is "makialam" (to meddle).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Wala siyang **pakialam** sa nararamdaman ng iba.","translation":"He has no **concern** for the feelings of others."},{"sentence":"Ano ba ang **pakialam** mo sa buhay ko?","translation":"What's your **business** in my life?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na sumasama sa isang maikling paglalakbay o pamamasyal para sa libangan, karaniwang kasama ng isang grupo.
original_explanation: Basically, isang turista o 'yung mga kasama sa field trip. 'Yung mga taong bumababa ng bus na may dalang camera, naka-matching t-shirt, at handang mag-picture sa bawat sulok. Sila 'yung mga ekskursiyonista.
usage_notes: Mas pormal na termino para sa turista o namamasyal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dagsaan ang mga **ekskursiyonista** sa Baguio tuwing Panagbenga Festival.","translation":"The **excursionists** flock to Baguio during the Panagbenga Festival."},{"sentence":"Naghanda ng meryenda ang lokal na pamahalaan para sa mga **ekskursiyonista**.","translation":"The local government prepared snacks for the **tourists**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang daanan na tumatagos o lumalagos mula sa isang lugar patungo sa iba, tulad ng tunel, pasilyo, o anumang maikling daan.
original_explanation: Ever tried to find a shortcut in a crowded mall like SM Megamall to avoid the sea of people? That's a lagusan. It's your secret portal, your life hack to get from Point A to Point B without losing your sanity. Parang sa buhay, we're all looking for a lagusan to our goals, pero minsan, traffic talaga.
usage_notes: Can refer to a physical tunnel or a metaphorical shortcut.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May lihim na **lagusan** sa ilalim ng lumang simbahan.","translation":"There is a secret **passageway** under the old church."},{"sentence":"Ginawa naming **lagusan** ang eskinita para makaiwas sa trapik.","translation":"We used the alley as a **shortcut** to avoid the traffic."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sining ng paglikha ng mga ilusyon o kaganapang tila imposible at hindi maipaliwanag ng agham, karaniwang para sa libangan.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung ginagawa ni Harry Potter. O 'yung ginagawa ng nanay mo para pagkasayahin ang 500 pesos na budget for one week. "Parang madyik!"
usage_notes: A direct loanword from English. Often used interchangeably with the Spanish-derived `mahika`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang manood ng mga palabas na may **madyik**.","translation":"He loves watching shows with **magic**."},{"sentence":"Para siyang may **madyik** sa pagluluto, laging masarap.","translation":"It's like she has **magic** in her cooking, it's always delicious."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang pagbalik o pagtalbog ng isang bagay na nabatak, napipi, o naiipit.
original_explanation: You know that feeling when you pull a rubber band too far and it snaps back at your fingers? That's *umigkas*. It's the sudden, violent recoil. It's also your body's reaction when you accidentally touch something super hot or slimy.
usage_notes: Often implies a sudden, forceful, and reflexive action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umigkas** ang goma ng tirador at tinamaan ang kanyang kamay.","translation":"The slingshot's rubber band **sprang back** and hit his hand."},{"sentence":"Parang **umigkas** ang katawan niya sa gulat nang marinig ang kulog.","translation":"His body seemed to **recoil** in shock when he heard the thunder."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi na nasa pinakamababang posisyon ng isang bagay o lugar.
original_explanation: The place where your coin, your phone, or your hopes and dreams go when they fall under the sofa. It's the space below something. 'Nasa **ilalim** ng mesa' (Under the table). It can also be used figuratively, like 'nasa **ilalim** ng stress' (under stress).
usage_notes: Often used with the preposition 'sa' (e.g., sa ilalim). Can be literal (under a table) or figurative (under pressure).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatago ang susi sa **ilalim** ng paso.","translation":"The key is hidden **under** the flowerpot."},{"sentence":"Ang mga minero ay nagtatrabaho nang malalim sa **ilalim** ng lupa.","translation":"The miners work deep **beneath** the ground."}]

translation: idol; a term of address for a friend
meaning_filipino: Isang baryasyon ng salitang "lodi," ginagamit bilang paraan ng pagtawag sa isang kaibigan o kakilala, na may pahiwatig ng paggalang o pakikipagkaibigan.
etymology: Isang pinaikling anyo o baryasyon ng "lodi," na mula sa baliktad na "idol."
original_explanation: The friendly, more casual cousin of 'lodi'. If 'lodi' is for a specific act of greatness, 'lods' is the everyday version you use to call your buddies. It’s the new 'pre', 'tol', or 'boss'. "Kamusta, lods?" is the 2020s equivalent of "What's up, dude?".
usage_notes: Napakakaraniwan sa online games, social media, at sa mga kabataan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uy, **lods**, anong laro natin mamaya?","translation":"Hey, **idol/dude**, what are we playing later?"},{"sentence":"Sige na, **lods**, payag ka na.","translation":"Come on, **dude**, just agree already."}]

translation: to halve; to divide into two
meaning_filipino: Ang paghahati sa isang bagay sa dalawang magkapantay na bahagi.
etymology: From 'ka-' + 'hati' + '-in' suffix, creating a transitive verb.
original_explanation: What you do with the last piece of chicharon when your friend gives you 'the look'. It’s the act of splitting something, whether it's the last Coke in the fridge or the workload for a group project. 'Kalahatiin natin 'to' is a peace treaty.
usage_notes: A transitive verb that requires an object to be halved.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **kalahatiin** mo ang mansanas para sa ating dalawa.","translation":"Please, **halve** the apple for the two of us."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **kalahatiin** ang iyong pagsisikap sa proyektong ito.","translation":"Don't just give **half** of your effort on this project."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapang may hawakan at isang mahabang metal na may dulo na ginagamit sa pagpihit o paghigpit ng mga tornilyo.
original_explanation: Ito yung tool na unang hinahanap ni Tatay kapag may sira sa bahay, tapos kasunod na yung martilyo. Essential sa bawat 'handyman' kuno na Pinoy. Kapag nawawala 'to, parang may world crisis sa bahay.
usage_notes: Karaniwang baybay sa Tagalog ng salitang Ingles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiabot ng **iskrudrayber** para maikabit ko itong pinto.","translation":"Please hand me the **screwdriver** so I can install this door."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong gamiting pambukas ng lata ang **iskrudrayber**.","translation":"Don't use the **screwdriver** to open cans."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng atensyon o pagkilala sa isang tao, bagay, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: That moment when your crush finally views your IG story. 'Hala, pumansin na siya!' It's the opposite of being 'seen-zoned'. When someone finally acknowledges your existence after you've been trying to get their attention forever.
usage_notes: Often used in the negative form 'hindi pumansin' (to ignore). The actor-focus form is 'pumansin' (someone noticed), while the object-focus is 'pinansin' (someone/something was noticed).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **pumansin** din ang gobyerno sa aming mga hinaing.","translation":"Finally, the government also **paid attention** to our complaints."},{"sentence":"Bakit hindi ka man lang **pumansin** noong tinawag kita?","translation":"Why didn't you even **notice** when I called you?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbibigay ng isang bagay bilang parangal, alay, o tanda ng paggalang at pasasalamat.
etymology: From 'handog' (offering). The prefix 'pag-' and the repetition 'ha' create a noun signifying the formal act of offering.
original_explanation: It's more than just giving a gift. It's the 'alay' in 'alay-lakad,' the flowers you offer at a hero's monument, or dedicating your thesis to your parents who funded your milk tea addiction. It's giving with a sense of ceremony and deep meaning.
usage_notes: Carries a formal or spiritual connotation. Used in religious contexts, ceremonies, or for dedicating artistic works.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang konsiyerto ay isang **paghahandog** sa mga frontliner.","translation":"The concert is a **dedication** to the frontliners."},{"sentence":"Ang **paghahandog** ng bulaklak sa altar ay bahagi ng kanilang ritwal.","translation":"The **offering** of flowers on the altar is part of their ritual."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang may pinakamatunog o pinakamataas na antas ng ingay o bolyum.
original_explanation: This is your neighbor's karaoke session at 1 AM, the thunder during a storm that makes your dog hide, or that one friend's laugh that can be heard across the mall. It's the sound that dominates all others. Yung tawa niya ang **pinakamalakas** sa buong sinehan.
usage_notes: Refers to sound volume. Homonymous with 'pinakamalakas' (strongest).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang hiyawan ng mga manonood ang **pinakamalakas** nang manalo ang kanilang koponan.","translation":"The cheering of the audience was at its **loudest** when their team won."},{"sentence":"Pakihinaan mo ang radyo, iyan na yata ang **pinakamalakas** na setting.","translation":"Please turn down the radio, that seems to be the **loudest** setting."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging angkop o madali para sa isang partikular na layunin o sitwasyon; kaginhawahan.
original_explanation: That thing you pay extra for sa 7-Eleven para hindi mo na kailangang mag-grocery. It's the "add to cart" button, the Grab delivery, the G-Cash payment. It's paying a premium para hindi ka ma-hassle sa buhay.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of services, locations, or products that save time and effort.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para sa **kombenyensiya** ng lahat, online na ang pagpaparehistro.","translation":"For everyone's **convenience**, registration is now online."},{"sentence":"Malaking **kombenyensiya** ang pagkakaroon ng tindahan sa tapat ng bahay.","translation":"Having a store across from the house is a great **convenience**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nakakulong o nakasupil sa isang maliit o masikip na lugar; hindi malaya.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're stuck in EDSA traffic for 3 hours, unable to move. You are, in essence, 'piit'. Also applies to being stuck in a toxic relationship or a dead-end job you can't quit. It's confinement, literal or metaphorical.
usage_notes: Often used to describe someone in jail or a state of being trapped. The verb form is 'ipiit' (to imprison).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pusang kalye ay **piit** sa loob ng hawla.","translation":"The street cat is **confined** inside the cage."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman niyang **piit** ang kanyang kaluluwa sa sitwasyong iyon.","translation":"He felt his soul was **imprisoned** in that situation."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na pagtatalo o pagpapalitan ng kuro-kuro tungkol sa isang partikular na paksa, kung saan ang magkabilang panig ay naglalatag ng kani-kanilang mga argumento.
original_explanation: It's the formal version of the arguments you have with your friends about basketball, politics, or who should pay for the milk tea. Except here, you use "therefore" and "I contend" instead of "basta!" and "ewan ko sa'yo!". It's a mental boxing match where the goal is to out-reason your opponent, not just out-shout them.
usage_notes: While 'debate' is common, the native term 'pagtatalo' is also widely used. 'Debate' often implies a more structured, formal setting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumali siya sa **debate** tungkol sa pagbabago ng klima.","translation":"He joined the **debate** about climate change."},{"sentence":"Naging mainit ang **debate** sa pagitan ng dalawang kandidato.","translation":"The **debate** between the two candidates became heated."}]

translation: to tie a knot on something
meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng buhol ang isang bagay; pag-ugnay-ugnayin sa pamamagitan ng buhol.
original_explanation: The action you do to create a 'buhol'. It's what you do to your shoelaces, to the plastic bag from the palengke, or to the loose ends of a story to make sure it's secure. Figuratively, 'buhulan ang dila' means to be tongue-tied.
usage_notes: The suffix '-an' here indicates that the action of tying a knot is done *onto* something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki **buhulan** nang mahigpit ang dulo ng lubid.","translation":"Please **tie a knot** tightly on the end of the rope."},{"sentence":"Para hindi makalimutan, **buhulan** mo ang panyo sa iyong daliri.","translation":"So you don't forget, **tie** the handkerchief **on** your finger."}]

translation: to finance, to support, to provide for
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng regular na suportang pinansyal o materyal sa isang tao, organisasyon, o proyekto.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of 'tustos'. It's what your generous tita from abroad does when she sends you money every month. 'Siya ang tumutustos sa pag-aaral ng kanyang mga kapatid.' It's the act of being the human ATM or sponsor for someone's needs.
usage_notes: The verb form of providing support. The actor-focus form is 'tumustos'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nangako siyang **tustusan** ang lahat ng pangangailangan ng kanyang pamilya.","translation":"He promised to **provide for** all the needs of his family."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **tumutustos** sa proyektong ito?","translation":"Who is **financing** this project?"}]

meaning_filipino: Kulang o walang kakayahang maghintay nang mahinahon; madaling mainis o magalit sa paghihintay.
etymology: Mula sa `walang` (without) + `pasyensya` (patience), na galing sa Espanyol na `paciencia`.
original_explanation: Ikaw 'yan 'pag 5 seconds pa lang 'yung loading screen ng laro pero gusto mo nang ihagis 'yung phone. O 'yung feeling mo sa pila sa bangko na parang isang taon na ang lumipas pero 5 minutes pa lang. Classic **walang-pasyensya** moment.
usage_notes: Ang 'walang-pasyensiya' ay isang alternatibong baybay ngunit ang 'walang-pasyensya' ay mas karaniwan sa modernong paggamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang magmadali, para kang **walang-pasyensya**.","translation":"Don't be in such a hurry, you seem so **impatient**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga taong **walang-pasyensya** ay madalas nai-stress sa traffic.","translation":"**Impatient** people often get stressed in traffic."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng isang sistema, kagamitan, o proseso na madaling gamitin at intindihin para sa karaniwang tao.
original_explanation: Basically, something that's 'bobo-proof.' It's an app your lola can figure out without calling you 10 times. It's a government website that doesn't make you want to throw your laptop out the window. It's so easy to use, it doesn't need a 50-page manual. The opposite of this is every SSS or PhilHealth online portal.
usage_notes: Used as is in Taglish/Filipino conversations, especially in tech and business contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat mas **user friendly** ang app na ito para mas maraming gumamit.","translation":"This app should be more **user-friendly** so more people will use it."},{"sentence":"Hindi **user friendly** ang proseso ng pagkuha ng lisensya.","translation":"The process of getting a license is not **user-friendly**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang patuloy na paggalaw sa isang paikot na landas o sa sarili nitong aksis. Maaari ring tumukoy sa paglilibot sa isang lugar.
original_explanation: This is what your world does after too many shots of Emperador. It's what the electric fan does on a hot day. It's also what you do when you're looking for parking at SM on a payday weekend—just going round and round. "Umiikot ang paningin ko" is the classic line for feeling dizzy.
usage_notes: This is the progressive form of *umikot*. It describes an ongoing action of turning or circulating.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umiikot** ang mundo sa araw.","translation":"The Earth **revolves** around the sun."},{"sentence":"Nahihilo ako, parang **umiikot** ang buong paligid.","translation":"I feel dizzy, it's like my whole surroundings are **spinning**."}]

translation: series of loud thuds, sound of heavy rain
meaning_filipino: Sunod-sunod na malalakas na tunog na nalilikha ng pagbagsak, pagyabag, o pagpatak ng malalaking bagay, tulad ng malakas na ulan sa bubong o yabag ng maraming tao.
original_explanation: Imagine the sound of a herd of kids running on the second floor of your house. Or the sound of super heavy rain on a yero (galvanized iron) roof. It's a loud, repetitive, thudding sound. Not just a 'tok tok' but a 'BLAGADAG! BLAGADAG!'.
usage_notes: This is an onomatopoeic word, describing a repetitive, heavy sound.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **lagapakan** ng mga paa sa itaas.","translation":"I heard the **loud thudding** of feet upstairs."},{"sentence":"Ang **lagapakan** ng ulan sa aming bubong na yero ay nakakaantok.","translation":"The **pattering sound of heavy rain** on our tin roof is sleep-inducing."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang lalaking nag-aaral sa kolehiyo o anumang bagay na may kaugnayan sa antas ng kolehiyo.
original_explanation: The guy version of 'kolehiyala'. Siya yung aabangan mo sa labas ng classroom niyo, yung varsity player, o yung laging nasa library (or computer shop). Basically, a male college kid.
usage_notes: Less common now than "college student". Often has a slightly dated or formal feel.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming pangarap ang binatang **kolehiyal** na iyon.","translation":"That young **male college student** has many dreams."},{"sentence":"Naging sikat siya sa kanilang liga bilang isang **kolehiyal**.","translation":"He became famous in their league as a **collegiate** player."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging bagsak o pagkawala ng balanse at pagguho mula sa pagkakatayo.
etymology: From Spanish "tumba" (tomb, or from the verb "tumbar" - to knock down).
original_explanation: "Tumba" is what happens to the Jenga tower when you pull the wrong block. It's you after a long day at work or a night out with friends—"Tumba na ako sa pagod." It's also that feeling when you're so sleepy you could just fall over right where you stand. In street games, it's what you do to the opponent's "lata" in Tumbang Preso.
usage_notes: Can be used as an adjective (e.g., "Tumba ang puno") or a noun referring to the state of being fallen.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumba** ang poste ng ilaw dahil sa malakas na hangin.","translation":"The light post is **toppled over** because of the strong wind."},{"sentence":"Isang bote na lang, **tumba** na siguro ako.","translation":"Just one more bottle, and I'll probably be **knocked out** (fallen drunk)."}]

translation: a competition of lowering; a race to the bottom
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kumpetisyon o paligsahan kung saan ang layunin ay maging pinakamababa, magkaroon ng pinakamababang puntos, o mag-alok ng pinakamababang presyo.
etymology: From `pa-` + `baba` + `-an` (a place or event for an action).
original_explanation: That office 'bardagulan' where different teams try to one-up (or one-down?) each other. It's a contest to see who can go the lowest. It could be a 'pababaan ng presyo' (price war) between telcos, or a 'pababaan ng ere' (a contest of humility, often sarcastic). It's a competition, but the goal is to be at the bottom.
usage_notes: Often implies a competitive or rivalrous context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng **pababaan** ng presyo ang mga tindahan noong Black Friday.","translation":"The stores had a **price-lowering competition** during Black Friday."},{"sentence":"Huwag nating gawing **pababaan** ng moral ang usapang ito.","translation":"Let's not turn this conversation into a **race to the bottom** of morals."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging kilala o popular ng isang tao, lugar, o bagay sa maraming tao.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `ma-` (na bumubuo ng pang-uri) + `tanyag` (kilala).
original_explanation: Eto 'yung level-up ng "sikat". Hindi lang basta vlogger na may 10k subscribers. Ito 'yung pang-Manny Pacquiao, Lea Salonga, o Jollibee level of fame. 'Pag sinabing **matanyag**, buong Pilipinas (at minsan, buong mundo) kilala ka. You've gone from viral to legendary.
usage_notes: Mas pormal kaysa sa "sikat". Madalas gamitin sa pagsulat, balita, o pormal na talumpati upang ilarawan ang isang taong tinitingala.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap ng maraming artista na maging **matanyag** sa buong mundo.","translation":"It is the dream of many actors to become **renowned** throughout the world."},{"sentence":"Si Jose Rizal ay isang **matanyag** na bayani ng Pilipinas.","translation":"Jose Rizal is a **famous** hero of the Philippines."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng tela o papel na ginagamit sa hapag-kainan upang ipampunas ng bibig at mga kamay habang kumakain.
original_explanation: Your best friend when you're eating something messy like BBQ or crab. It's that piece of paper or cloth na nagse-save sa'yo from looking like a toddler who just discovered spaghetti. Sa mga handaan, ito rin yung ginagawang pansamantalang lalagyan ng shanghai at hotdog na iuuwi mo. Don't deny it.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa papel (paper napkin) o tela (cloth napkin).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakilagay ng **serbilyeta** sa iyong kandungan habang kumakain.","translation":"Please place the **napkin** on your lap while eating."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sagisag ng pananampalatayang Katoliko, karaniwang dalawang maliit na piraso ng tela na may mga banal na imahen, na pinag-uugnay ng tali at isinusuot sa leeg.
etymology: From Spanish 'Carmen,' referring to Our Lady of Mount Carmel, from whom the devotion of the Brown Scapular originates. The full Spanish name is 'escapulario del Carmen'.
original_explanation: That brown necklace your lola makes you wear for protection. It's like a religious dog tag. You're not supposed to take it off, even when you shower, because it's believed to protect you from harm and shorten your stay in purgatory. It's the OG spiritual insurance policy.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to the Brown Scapular of Our Lady of Mount Carmel in a Filipino Catholic context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isinuot sa kanya ng kanyang lola ang isang **kalmen** bilang proteksyon.","translation":"His grandmother made him wear a **scapular** for protection."},{"sentence":"Maraming deboto ang nagsusuot ng **kalmen** tuwing pista ng Birhen ng Carmen.","translation":"Many devotees wear a **scapular** during the feast of Our Lady of Mount Carmel."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagsukat ng bigat ng isang bagay gamit ang timbangan. Sa matalinhagang paraan, ito ay ang pagsusuri o pag-iisip nang mabuti sa mga pagpipilian o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: On a literal level, 'timbangin' is what the vendor does to your chicken at the market. But on a 'hugot' level, it's what you do with your life choices. "Timbangin mo muna ang pros and cons bago ka mag-resign." It's about weighing your options, balancing the good and the bad, whether it's about your career, your love life, or deciding if that extra cup of rice is worth it.
usage_notes: Has both a literal meaning (to weigh on a scale) and a very common figurative meaning (to weigh options/assess a situation).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**timbang** nga po ng isang kilong baboy.","translation":"Please **weigh** one kilo of pork."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **timbangin** ang mga bagay-bagay bago ka gumawa ng desisyon.","translation":"You need to **weigh** things carefully before you make a decision."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pagkilos o pangyayari na naganap nang biglaan at walang anumang paunang babala o pasabi.
etymology: Mula sa "walang" (without) at dinobleng "ka-abiso" (mula sa Espanyol na 'aviso', notice). Ang pag-uulit ay nagdaragdag ng diin.
original_explanation: How your landlady shows up on the 15th of the month. How your boss gives you a rush project at 4:59 PM on a Friday. It's the 'surprise' in 'surprise quiz' that nobody likes. The ultimate 'biglaang-ganap'.
usage_notes: The reduplication "kaabiso-abiso" is for emphasis, meaning "absolutely no notice at all." The simpler form is "walang-abiso."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumating ang bagyo nang **walang-kaabiso-abiso**.","translation":"The storm arrived **without any notice whatsoever**."},{"sentence":"Umalis siya ng bansa nang **walang-kaabiso-abiso** sa kanyang pamilya.","translation":"He left the country **suddenly** without telling his family."}]

translation: is proving; is testifying; is confirming
meaning_filipino: Nagbibigay ng ebidensya o katibayan upang suportahan ang isang pahayag o katotohanan.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you show your receipts. Yung resibo ng Grab, yung screenshot ng convo, yung picture niyo together—lahat 'yan nagpapatunay na hindi ka nag-iimbento ng kwento. It's the act of showing proof, whether it's for a court case or just to win an argument with your 'marites' friends.
usage_notes: Present progressive tense. Indicates an ongoing action of proving something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga dokumentong ito ay **nagpapatunay** na siya ang may-ari ng lupa.","translation":"These documents **are proving** that he is the owner of the land."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga luha ay **nagpapatunay** ng kanyang kalungkutan.","translation":"Her tears **are testifying** to her sadness."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lugar o arena kung saan idinaraos ang mga laban ng sabong.
original_explanation: The Thunderdome for chickens. It's the official venue for the national pastime of 'sabong'. It's loud, crowded, and smells like a mix of testosterone, money, and feathers. This is where you'll find the 'kristo' (bet caller) masterfully taking bets with just hand signals. It's the 'tito' equivalent of a mall.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumunta siya sa **sabungan** para itaya ang kanyang manok na panabong.","translation":"He went to the **cockpit arena** to bet on his fighting cock."},{"sentence":"Bawat bayan ay tila may sariling **sabungan**.","translation":"Every town seems to have its own **cockpit arena**."}]

translation: To refuse; to turn someone down
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtanggi o hindi pagpayag sa isang hiling, paanyaya, o alok ng isang tao.
original_explanation: Ito yung ultimate 'seenzone' move sa personal. Inimbita ka sa birthday, pero bigla kang nagka-ubo. Niyaya kang mag-date, pero 'may gagawin ka.' Kapag ayaw mo, pero ayaw mong maging prangka, you pahindian them. It's the art of saying no without saying no, but they get the message anyway.
usage_notes: Carries a nuance of turning someone down in a social context, rather than just a simple negation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masakit para sa kanya na **pahindian** ng taong gusto niya.","translation":"It's painful for him to be **turned down** by the person he likes."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **pahindian** sa paanyaya kong ito.","translation":"Don't **refuse** me on this invitation."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na minamahal nang labis; isang tawag ng paglalambing sa isang kasintahan, asawa, o sinumang malapit sa puso.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'baby,' 'babe,' or 'mahal.' It's the word Jose Rizal would use in his love letters. Today, it sounds super poetic and romantic, like something you'd hear in a classic Filipino movie or a kundiman. Using this on your modern-day jowa might get you a 'sana all' or a 'Wow, ang deep!'
usage_notes: Highly poetic and archaic. Used in literature, songs, or for dramatic/romantic effect.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"O, **irog** ko, nasaan ka na?","translation":"Oh, my **beloved**, where are you now?"},{"sentence":"Isinulat niya ang tula para sa kanyang natatanging **irog**.","translation":"He wrote the poem for his one and only **darling**."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagkaing matamis na karaniwang inihahain pagkatapos ng pangunahing pagkain, tulad ng keyk, sorbetes, o prutas. Ang katumbas nito sa Tagalog ay panghimagas.
original_explanation: The reason you 'leave room' after a feast of sinigang and adobo. Whether it's halo-halo, leche flan, or that ube cheese pandesal you saw on TikTok, this is the 'final boss' of any Filipino meal. Remember, 'stressed' is 'desserts' spelled backward. Coincidence? I think not.
usage_notes: Very common loanword. The native Tagalog term is 'panghimagas'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **dessert** natin mamaya? Sana leche flan.","translation":"What's our **dessert** for later? I hope it's leche flan."}]

translation: to tell a story; to narrate
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasalaysay ng isang pangyayari, karanasan, o kathang-isip sa paraang pasalita o pasulat.
original_explanation: The national pastime. It's what you say to your bestie when you have fresh chismis: "Uy, may ikukwento ako sa'yo!" It's the engine of every Pinoy gathering, from family reunions to inuman sessions. To 'ikwento' is to share a piece of your life, or someone else's (lol). It's our version of a podcast, live and unfiltered.
usage_notes: A very common command form is "Ikwento mo!" (Tell me the story!).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito ng mga bata na **ikwento** ng kanilang lola ang mga alamat.","translation":"The children's favorite thing is when their grandmother **narrates** legends."},{"sentence":"Sige na, **ikwento** mo na kung bakit ka late!","translation":"Go on, **tell the story** of why you're late!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbuo ng mga hakbangin o estratehiya para sa isang layunin sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: The official verb of every "drawing" session with your barkada. "Tara, mag-beach tayo!" "Sige, magpaplano tayo!"... and then it never happens. It's the act of creating a detailed plan, whether for a vacation, a business, or how to get home during a transport strike. It's the hopeful first step before reality (and budget constraints) kicks in.
usage_notes: This form is in the future tense. The root word 'plano' is very common in both formal and informal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bukas kami **magpaplano** para sa aming Christmas party.","translation":"Tomorrow, we **will plan** for our Christmas party."},{"sentence":"Sila ang **magpaplano** ng buong programa.","translation":"They **will plan** the entire program."}]

translation: to end up; to result in
meaning_filipino: Ang pagdating sa isang tiyak na kalagayan, lugar, o resulta bilang wakas ng isang proseso o pangyayari.
original_explanation: 'Yung sinubukan mong mag-DIY ng haircut base sa YouTube tutorial, pero sa huli, humantong ka rin sa barbero para ipaayos. Or when your "one-shot" inuman session with friends humantong sa tatlong balde at videoke hanggang umaga. It's the final destination of your questionable life choices.
usage_notes: Implies a final outcome or destination, often one that was not originally planned.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanilang pag-aaway ay **humantong** sa hiwalayan.","translation":"Their fighting **resulted in** a breakup."},{"sentence":"Saan kaya **hahantong** ang lahat ng ating pinaghirapan?","translation":"Where will all our hard work **end up**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malagkit at mamasa-masang dumi na natural na nabubuo sa loob ng tainga.
original_explanation: That yellowish gunk you discreetly try to remove from your ear when no one's looking. It's the main reason cotton buds were invented (even though doctors say you shouldn't use them for that). Having too much **tutuli** is why you "can't hear" your mom asking you to do chores. "Ano po? 'Di ko marinig, barado yata tenga ko!"
usage_notes: A common, non-technical term for cerumen.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nilinisan niya ang kanyang tainga dahil sa dami ng **tutuli**.","translation":"He cleaned his ears because of the amount of **earwax**."},{"sentence":"Sabi ng doktor, huwag daw basta-basta mag-alis ng **tutuli** gamit ang matutulis na bagay.","translation":"The doctor said not to carelessly remove **earwax** using sharp objects."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pag-uugnay ng mga metal sa pamamagitan ng pag-init hanggang sa matunaw at magdikit; maaari ring tumukoy sa materyal na ginagamit sa prosesong ito.
original_explanation: Ito yung 'magic' na ginagawa ng soldador para pagdikitin ang dalawang bakal. Parang sa relasyon, kailangan ng matinding init (passion) at tamang proseso para maging matibay ang pagsasama. Pag pangit ang pagka-soldadura, 'break' agad.
usage_notes: Can refer to the act of welding or the material (solder) used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matibay ang pagkakagawa ng **soldadura** sa rehas.","translation":"The **welding** on the grill is sturdy."},{"sentence":"Naubusan kami ng tingga para sa **soldadura** ng mga kawad.","translation":"We ran out of lead for the **solder** for the wires."}]

meaning_filipino: Matagumpay na malampasan ang isang pagsubok, eksaminasyon, o pamantayan.
original_explanation: The word that brings either immense joy or crushing 'bagsak' feels. This is what every student prays for during finals week, what every board exam taker posts on Facebook ('Thank you, Lord! #Pumasa'), and what your parents ask about your grades. It can also mean to hand something over, like 'pakipasa ng asin'.
usage_notes: Can mean to pass a test, or to pass an object to someone. The context usually makes it clear. 'Pumasa sa exam' vs 'Ipinasa ang kanin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **pumasa** rin ako sa board exam pagkatapos ng ilang buwang review!","translation":"Finally, I **passed** the board exam after several months of review!"},{"sentence":"Sana **pumasa** ang lahat ng proyekto natin sa kliyente.","translation":"I hope all our projects **pass** the client's standards."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sitwasyon kung saan mayroong palitan ng malalakas na sigaw sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang mga tao.
original_explanation: This is when the shouting is no longer a one-way street; it's a full-blown traffic jam of yelling. A sigawan is a shouting match. Think of your neighbors having a 'discussion' at 2 AM, or the climax of a family reunion where old resentments are finally aired out... loudly.
usage_notes: This is a noun describing a mutual or collective act of shouting. Note the difference in stress from the verb form: /SI-ga-wan/ (noun) vs /si-ga-WAN/ (verb).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nauwi sa **sigawan** ang kanilang pag-uusap.","translation":"Their conversation ended in a **shouting match**."},{"sentence":"Narinig sa buong barangay ang **sigawan** ng mag-asawa.","translation":"The couple's **exchange of shouts** was heard throughout the whole barangay."}]

translation: A traditional Filipino game of catching pebbles.
meaning_filipino: Isang tradisyonal na larong pambata sa Pilipinas na gumagamit ng maliliit na bato o sigay, kung saan ito ay inihahagis paitaas at sinasalo.
original_explanation: This is the OG fidget spinner. Before mobile games, kids played siklot with pebbles or shells. It's a game of skill where you toss one 'pamato' (main stone) in the air and try to scoop up as many other stones as you can before catching the pamato again. It teaches you reflexes, coordination, and how to deal with losing your favorite shiny pebble.
usage_notes: The game is also sometimes called 'sintak'. The verb is 'mag-siklot' (to play siklot) or 'siklutin' (to snatch, derived from the game's motion).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marunong ka pa bang maglaro ng **siklot**?","translation":"Do you still know how to play **siklot**?"},{"sentence":"Ang mga bata sa probinsya ay naglalaro ng **siklot** sa ilalim ng puno.","translation":"The children in the province are playing **siklot** under a tree."}]

meaning_filipino: Kumukuha ng isang bagay mula sa iba na may intensyon at pangakong isauli ito sa takdang panahon.
original_explanation: Yung tropa mong laging humihiram ng pera pero 'nakalimutan' magbayad. Or when you're humihiram ng lakas sa kape para lang matapos ang work week. The official motto is 'pahiram muna, balik ko rin agad' (spoiler: hindi agad).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Humihiram** ako ng libro sa silid-aklatan.","translation":"I **am borrowing** a book from the library."},{"sentence":"Palagi siyang **humihiram** ng ballpen sa akin.","translation":"He is always **borrowing** a pen from me."}]

translation: to praise one another; to exchange praises
meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay o palitan na pagbibigay ng papuri ng dalawa o higit pang tao sa isa't isa.
original_explanation: This is what happens in a "plastikan" reunion. "OMG, you look so young!" "No, you're the one who hasn't aged a day!" Apir! 'Yan ang magpurihan. It's the comments section of your barkada's group chat when someone posts a new profile pic.
usage_notes: Implies a reciprocal or mutual action. The suffix '-han' denotes this reciprocity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula nang **magpurihan** ang dalawang panig matapos ang matagumpay na proyekto.","translation":"The two sides began to **praise one another** after the successful project."},{"sentence":"Nakakatuwang pagmasdan ang mga magkakaibigan na **nagpurihan** sa kanilang mga natamo.","translation":"It's heartwarming to watch the friends who were **exchanging praises** for their achievements."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos kung saan ang dalawa o higit pang tao ay sabay-sabay o halinhinang nagtutulak sa isa't isa.
original_explanation: The daily scene at the MRT entrance during rush hour. Or when there's a 50% off sale and everyone's trying to get to the discount rack. Figuratively, it's when officemates are blaming each other for a mistake ('pass the blame' kumbaga).
usage_notes: The 'pag- -an' affix with a reduplicated first syllable of the root indicates a reciprocal or collective action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkagulo sa pila dahil sa **pagtutulakan** ng mga tao.","translation":"There was chaos in the line because of people **pushing each other**."},{"sentence":"Itigil niyo na 'yang **pagtutulakan** ninyo!","translation":"Stop that **shoving one another**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan kumakain o maaaring kumain; isang pampublikong establisyimento na naghahain ng pagkain.
etymology: Nagmula sa salitang-ugat na "kain" at hulaping "-an", na nagpapahiwatig ng isang lugar.
original_explanation: This is any place you go to eat. It can be a fancy restaurant, a humble carinderia, or the dining area in your own house. "Saan ang pinakamalapit na kainan dito?" is the most important question to ask when you're hungry in a new place. It's the battleground for deciding where to eat with your friends: "Kahit saan." "Sige, sa Kainan ni Aling Nena." "Ay, ayoko dun."
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa isang komersyal na establisyimento (restaurant) o sa espasyo para sa pagkain sa loob ng isang bahay (dining area).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming masasarap na **kainan** sa Maginhawa Street.","translation":"There are many delicious **eateries** on Maginhawa Street."},{"sentence":"Pumunta tayo sa **kainan** para mag-almusal.","translation":"Let's go to the **dining area** to have breakfast."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkilos ng isang online platform na paghigpitan ang visibility ng isang user o ng kanilang mga post nang hindi nila nalalaman. Ang user ay hindi pormal na "banned" ngunit ang kanilang content ay hindi naipapakita sa iba.
original_explanation: When you're talking, but the algorithm puts a virtual 'piring' (blindfold) on you. You think you're shouting your hot takes into the social media universe, but you're actually just whispering to yourself in a corner. It's the internet's way of telling you to sit down and be quiet without actually telling you.
usage_notes: Used as a noun ('May shadowban ako') or a verb ('Na-shadowban ako'). A term born from social media culture.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kaya pala walang engagement posts ko, naka-**shadowban** yata ako sa Instagram.","translation":"That's why my posts have no engagement, I think I'm **shadowbanned** on Instagram."},{"sentence":"Ingat sa mga ginagamit na hashtag para maiwasan ang **shadowban**.","translation":"Be careful with the hashtags you use to avoid a **shadowban**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na ginagamit bilang pabigat upang maging balanse ang isang bagay; panimbang.
original_explanation: Think of the rocks the tindera at the palengke puts on the other side of the 'timbangan' (weighing scale). That's a pantuwas. In life, it’s that one responsible friend in the group who balances out the chaotic energy of everyone else. It's the 'pang-kontra' to keep things from tipping over.
usage_notes: From 'pan-' (for) + 'tuwas' (unbalanced, tipped to one side). It is the instrument to correct the 'tuwas'. Often used interchangeably with 'panimbang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghahanap siya ng bato na tamang-tama ang bigat para maging **pantuwas** sa timbangan.","translation":"He is looking for a rock with just the right weight to be a **counterweight** for the scale."},{"sentence":"Ang maliit na pabigat sa dulo ng lubid ay nagsisilbing **pantuwas**.","translation":"The small weight at the end of the rope serves as a **counterbalance**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng kataksilan; lilo; hindi mapagkakatiwalaan at nagkakanulo sa likuran.
original_explanation: This isn't just a simple liar. A 'sukab' is a next-level traitor. Think Brutus to Caesar, or that 'friend' who uses your Netflix account and then changes the password. It's the snake in the grass, the backstabber in your group project. It's a word so dramatic it belongs in a Florante at Laura-style teleserye.
usage_notes: A very strong and literary word for betrayal. Not commonly used in casual conversation, but understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinuring siyang **sukab** matapos niyang ipagkanulo ang kanyang sariling bayan.","translation":"He was considered **treacherous** after he betrayed his own country."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa mga **sukab** na kaibigan.","translation":"Be careful of **perfidious** friends."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan na ginagamit sa pagkayod o pag-alis ng dumi, lumot, o anumang nakadikit sa isang ibabaw.
original_explanation: The `panakyod` is that satisfying tool you use to scrape off stuff. It's the `paleta` for removing old paint, the squeegee for cleaning your aquarium, or even just a ruler you use to scrape off dried glue from your desk. In the kitchen, it's what you use for `kayod` to get all the coconut meat out of the shell. It's the official tool for "getting the last bit."
usage_notes: This is a general term. Specific scrapers might have other names (e.g., `kudkuran` for coconut scraper).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng **panakyod** para alisin ang lumang wallpaper sa pader.","translation":"He used a **scraper** to remove the old wallpaper from the wall."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng matalas na **panakyod** para linisin ang dumi sa sahig.","translation":"I need a sharp **scraper** to clean the dirt on the floor."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o bagay na hindi sumusunod sa pangkalahatang tuntunin o pamantayan.
original_explanation: 'Yung "exception to the rule." Halimbawa, lahat ng ex mo manloloko, maliban sa isa. Siya ang eksepsiyon. Or 'yung bawal ang maingay sa library, pero may eksepsiyon pag may emergency. It's that one thing that doesn't fit the pattern.
usage_notes: Halos kasingkahulugan ng 'eksemsyon' ngunit mas tumutukoy sa isang bagay na naiiba sa isang patakaran, habang ang 'eksemsyon' ay ang pagiging malaya mula sa patakaran.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lahat ay kailangang sumunod sa patakaran, walang **eksepsiyon**.","translation":"Everyone must follow the rule, no **exceptions**."},{"sentence":"Siya ang **eksepsiyon** sa aming pamilya na hindi naging doktor.","translation":"He is the **exception** in our family who did not become a doctor."}]

translation: to accidentally leave something behind; to be left behind by someone/something
meaning_filipino: Hindi sinasadyang makalimutang dalhin ang isang bagay; o malagpasan o iwanan ng isang umaalis na tao o sasakyan.
original_explanation: Two main scenarios. 1) The "Oh no, my wallet!" moment. "Naiwanan ko ang phone ko sa bahay!" You forgot to bring something. 2) The "Wait for me!" moment. When the jeepney starts moving just as you get there. "Naiwanan ako ng byahe!" You were the one who got left behind. It's the official verb of forgetfulness and poor timing.
usage_notes: This is transitive. It can mean to forgetfully leave an object somewhere ('Naiwanan ko ang payong') or for a person to be left by a moving vehicle or group ('Naiwanan ako ng bus').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutan ang iyong mga gamit at baka may **maiwanan** ka.","translation":"Don't forget your things, you might **leave something behind**."},{"sentence":"Nagmadali siyang tumakbo para hindi **maiwanan** ng huling bus.","translation":"He ran fast so he wouldn't **be left behind** by the last bus."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bunga ng langka na mura pa at binuro sa suka, asin, at iba pang pampalasa.
original_explanation: This is the glow-up of unripe langka. Before it becomes the sweet star of turon or halo-halo, it gets a sour, tangy makeover. It's basically 'burong langka', the side dish that adds a surprising kick to your fried fish, kinda like that quiet officemate who suddenly nails the karaoke high notes at the Christmas party.
usage_notes: A regional delicacy, not widely known in all parts of the Philippines. Often eaten as a condiment or appetizer.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap ipares ang prinitong isda sa **dalok**.","translation":"It's delicious to pair fried fish with **pickled unripe jackfruit**."},{"sentence":"Naghahanap si Lola ng murang langka para gawing **dalok**.","translation":"Grandma is looking for unripe jackfruit to make **dalok**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tiyak na halaga ng salapi na inilaan para sa isang partikular na gastusin o proyekto.
original_explanation: Ito yung official term para sa budget. Yung bagay na laging 'wala na' pag-petsa de peligro. Yung dahilan kung bakit ka nagtitimpla ng kape sa office pantry imbes na bumili sa Starbucks. The struggle is real.
usage_notes: A more formal term for 'badyet'. Commonly used in government and finance contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang aprubahan ng kongreso ang **laang-gugulin** para sa susunod na taon.","translation":"The congress needs to approve the **budget** for next year."},{"sentence":"Maliit lang ang aming **laang-gugulin** para sa bakasyon.","translation":"We have a small **budget** for the vacation."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasabihan sa internet na nagsasaad na ang pagiging delusional o pagtakas sa pantasya ay ang solusyon sa mga problema o sa malupit na katotohanan.
etymology: A rhyming internet maxim combining "delulu" (delusional) and a cute-ified "solulu" (solution).
original_explanation: When reality bites hard, just choose to live in your own world where everything is perfect. Can't afford concert tickets? Just imagine you're there. Crush doesn't know you exist? In your mind, you're already married. Why? Because delulu is the solulu. It's the ultimate coping mechanism for Gen Z.
usage_notes: Used as a mantra to justify or celebrate indulging in fantasies as a way to cope with reality.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ako papasa sa exam bukas, pero okay lang, **delulu is the solulu**. I-imagine ko na lang na A+ ang grade ko.","translation":"I won't pass the exam tomorrow, but it's okay, **delusion is the solution**. I'll just imagine my grade is an A+."},{"sentence":"Friend: 'Stop thinking about him!' Me: 'Sorry, **delulu is the solulu**.'","translation":"Kaibigan: 'Tigilan mo na kakaisip sa kanya!' Ako: 'Pasensya na, **delusion is the solution**.'"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o pamilya na naninirahan sa isang lupa o gusali na hindi nila pag-aari at walang legal na pahintulot mula sa may-ari.
original_explanation: In the Philippines, this term is more than just its legal definition. It's a loaded word associated with urban poverty, makeshift housing ("barong-barong"), and complex issues of land ownership and social inequality. While it's often used neutrally to describe informal settlers, it can also carry a negative, classist stigma, leading to the creation of slang like "squammy."
usage_notes: A term with significant socio-economic and political implications in the Philippines. "Informal settler" is the more formal and politically correct term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming pamilyang **squatter** ang nawalan ng tirahan dahil sa demolisyon.","translation":"Many **informal settler** families lost their homes due to the demolition."},{"sentence":"Ang proyektong pabahay ng gobyerno ay para sa mga dating **squatter**.","translation":"The government's housing project is for the former **informal settlers**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtugtog ng tambol sa pamamagitan ng pagpalo rito gamit ang kamay o patpat.
original_explanation: What you do on your desk when you're bored in a meeting. Or what your upstairs neighbor does at 2 AM. To magtambol is to create a beat, whether you're a pro drummer in a band or just a kid hitting pots and pans in the kitchen.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahusay siyang **magtambol** at miyembro siya ng isang banda.","translation":"He is good at **playing the drums** and is a member of a band."},{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **magtambol** ang mga tao sa kalye bilang bahagi ng parada.","translation":"The people started to **play the drums** on the street as part of the parade."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng interseksyon ng mga kalsada kung saan ang trapiko ay gumagalaw sa isang direksyon sa paligid ng isang gitnang isla.
original_explanation: That thing in the middle of the road that's supposed to make traffic flow better but sometimes just becomes a parking lot. Think Welcome Rotonda or the "Death Circle" in Eastwood.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to a traffic roundabout, also known as a rotunda.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa pagdaan sa **paikot** sa EDSA dahil maraming sasakyan.","translation":"Be careful when passing through the **roundabout** on EDSA because there are many vehicles."},{"sentence":"Ang monumento ay nasa gitna ng **paikot**.","translation":"The monument is in the middle of the **traffic circle**."}]

translation: to refute; to prove false; to belie
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapasinungalingan o pagpapatunay na hindi totoo ang isang pahayag, paratang, o paniniwala sa pamamagitan ng ebidensya o argumento.
etymology: Mula sa salitang 'bulaan' (hindi totoo) na may hulaping '-in' upang gawin itong isang pandiwa.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you bring out the receipts. It's the act of showing screenshots to prove your friend wrong. It's your lawyer's job in court, or your job during a performance review to dispute your boss's 'feedback'. 'I object, your honor! And I'm here to **bulaanin** the allegations!'
usage_notes: Ito ay isang palipat na pandiwa (transitive verb) na nangangailangan ng tuwirang layon (ang bagay na pinasisinungalingan).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **bulaanin** ang mga akusasyon laban sa kanya.","translation":"He tried to **refute** the accusations against him."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **bulaanin** ang ebidensyang iprinisenta ng piskal.","translation":"It's hard to **prove false** the evidence presented by the prosecutor."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagsasalita sa napakahinang tinig, na halos hangin lamang ang maririnig, upang hindi malaman ng iba ang sinasabi.
original_explanation: The official language of chismis (gossip). This is what your officemates are doing when you walk into the pantry. It's also what your crush's friend does right before they both look at you and giggle. It can be sweet, but 90% of the time, it's juicy gossip.
usage_notes: Present tense of 'bumulong'. Can also act as an adjective (e.g., 'ang bumubulong na hangin' - the whispering wind).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **bumubulong** sa likod ko pero hindi ko maintindihan.","translation":"Someone is **whispering** behind me but I can't understand."},{"sentence":"Ano 'yang **binubulong** ninyo diyan? I-share n'yo naman!","translation":"What are you guys **whispering** about over there? Share it!"}]

translation: to dehorn; to cut the tip off
meaning_filipino: Putulin o bawasan ang sungay ng hayop, o ang dulo o taluktok ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: It's what you do to a carabao's horns so they don't accidentally poke you. Think of it as giving something a 'flat top' haircut, but more permanent. Like when your mom cuts the tip off the *sili* before putting it in the *sinigang*.
usage_notes: Often used in agricultural or provincial contexts, referring to animals like carabaos or goats.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **pungusin** ang mga sungay ng kalabaw para hindi ito makasakit.","translation":"The carabao's horns need to be **dehorned** so it won't hurt anyone."},{"sentence":"**Pinungos** niya ang dulo ng lapis gamit ang kutsilyo.","translation":"He **cut the tip off** the pencil using a knife."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong ang iniisip lamang ay ang sariling kapakanan at hindi ang sa iba.
original_explanation: That friend who eats the whole pizza and leaves you with the box. They'll borrow your Netflix password but won't share their HBO Go. Their life motto is 'Me, myself, and I.' They always ask 'What's in it for me?' before doing anything. The opposite of 'mapagparaya'.
usage_notes: A common and straightforward negative trait. 'Makasarili' is a more common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap pakisamahan ang taong **mapagsarili**.","translation":"It's difficult to get along with a **selfish** person."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **mapagsarili**; ibahagi mo ang iyong biyaya sa iba.","translation":"Don't be **self-centered**; share your blessings with others."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang salitang-ugat para sa kilos ng pagtanggap, pagdakma, o pagkamit ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: The ultimate multi-purpose Filipino verb. Need to grab something? **Kuha**. Understand a joke? 'Na-**kuha** mo?' Take a picture? **Kuha** ng picture. It's the 'get' that keeps on giving. If you're learning Tagalog, you'll be using this word every five minutes.
usage_notes: A very common and versatile root verb. Often used with affixes like 'kumuha', 'kinuha', 'kukunin', 'makuha'. As a noun ('kuha'), it can also mean 'a photo' or 'a catch'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang utos niya ay **kuha** ka ng tubig.","translation":"His order was for you to **get** some water."},{"sentence":"**Kuha** mo ba ang ibig kong sabihin?","translation":"Do you **get** what I mean?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sagisag o simbolo na kumakatawan sa isang ideya, pamilya, organisasyon, o bansa.
original_explanation: It's a logo, but make it *classy*. Think of the sun and stars on the Philippine flag, the seal of your university, or the crest of a royal family from a fantasy series. It's a symbol that screams, 'This is who we are!'
usage_notes: Ginagamit para sa mga opisyal o simbolikong representasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang agila ay ang **emblema** ng katapangan at kapangyarihan.","translation":"The eagle is the **emblem** of courage and power."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na tuwiran, hindi paligoy-ligoy, at may partikular na tinutukoy.
original_explanation: This is the opposite of 'parinig'. When you're being 'tiyakan', you're not beating around the bush. You name names, you give specifics. It's direct to the point, no fluff. Like a 'tiyakang sagutan' (direct confrontation) instead of just subtweeting your enemy. It’s the "We need to talk" that actually leads to a clear conversation.
usage_notes: Often used in grammar to refer to the definite or specific form of a noun or in communication to mean 'direct'. For example, 'panaguring tiyakan' (definite object).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas gusto ko ang **tiyakan** na sagot, hindi 'yung paligoy-ligoy.","translation":"I prefer a **direct** answer, not one that beats around the bush."},{"sentence":"Nagkaroon sila ng **tiyakan** na pag-uusap tungkol sa kanilang problema.","translation":"They had a **specific** conversation about their problem."}]

meaning_filipino: Itransfer o isalin ang lahat ng nilalaman ng isang bagay, lalo na ang mga damdamin o sama ng loob, sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'hugot' move. When you can't take it anymore—be it office stress, love life drama, or family issues—you find a friend (or a social media post) and just ibunto everything. It's like a data dump, but for your feelings. "Sige na, i-spill mo na ang tea, ibunto mo na lahat!"
usage_notes: Often used for negative emotions like anger, frustration, or sadness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo sa akin **ibunto** ang galit mo sa boss mo.","translation":"Don't **vent** your anger at your boss on me."},{"sentence":"Sa pagsusulat niya **ibinunto** ang lahat ng kanyang kalungkutan.","translation":"She **poured out** all her sadness into her writing."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong madaling magkasakit o may mahinang pangangatawan.
original_explanation: That one friend who is always absent from the get-together because they have a fever, a cough, or some mysterious ailment. They're the human equivalent of a fragile phone screen—needs extra care. Their immune system is perpetually on vacation.
usage_notes: Often used to describe children or the elderly, but can apply to anyone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Noong bata pa ako, ako ay **sakitin** kaya palagi akong nasa bahay.","translation":"When I was young, I was **sickly** so I was always at home."},{"sentence":"Dahil **sakitin** siya, kailangan niyang uminom ng maraming bitamina.","translation":"Because she is **prone to illness**, she needs to take a lot of vitamins."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang biglaan at malakas na pagdaloy o pag-agos ng likido mula sa isang sisidlan o pinagmulan.
original_explanation: Isipin mo 'yung gripo na biglang bumigay, 'tapos biglang BWOOSH! 'Yung malakas na agos ng tubig. O 'yung pagbukas mo ng bote ng softdrinks na inalog, 'yun ang bulos ng bula. It's a sudden, uncontrolled, powerful rush of liquid. Parang emotions mo 'pag 'di mo na mapigilan.
usage_notes: Madalas ginagamit sa anyong pandiwa: bumulos (to gush out).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malakas na **bulos** ng dugo ang lumabas mula sa kanyang sugat.","translation":"A strong **gush** of blood came out from his wound."},{"sentence":"Nang mabuksan ang dam, bumuhos ang malakas na **bulos** ng tubig.","translation":"When the dam was opened, a powerful **spurt** of water poured out."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sukat ng potensyal na pagkakaiba ng kuryente sa pagitan ng dalawang punto; ang puwersang nagtutulak sa daloy ng kuryente.
original_explanation: 'Yung dahilan kung bakit kailangan mo ng AVR o transformer. 'Pag mali ang boltahe ng saksakan mo para sa gamit galing US, good luck sa appliance mo, baka mag-ala-New Year's firecracker. Ito rin 'yung 'high voltage' na drama sa pamilya kapag may away.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa konteksto ng kuryente at elektronika.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumaas daw ang **boltahe** ng kuryente kaya nasira ang kanilang telebisyon.","translation":"They said the **voltage** of the electricity surged, which is why their television broke."},{"sentence":"Siguraduhin mong 220 ang **boltahe** niyan bago mo isaksak.","translation":"Make sure that has a 220 **voltage** before you plug it in."}]

translation: to be able to scare; to cause fear
meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang magdulot ng takot o pangamba sa isang tao o hayop.
original_explanation: This is the goal of every horror movie, your friend hiding behind a door to jump at you, and your mom when she uses your full name. It's the ability to make someone's heart jump into their throat. 'Uy, 'wag kang mag-ganyan, nakakatakot!' becomes 'Huwag mong gawin iyan, baka makatakot ka ng bata.'
usage_notes: A very common verb for causing fear.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kwento mo tungkol sa multo ay sapat para **makatakot** ng kahit sino.","translation":"Your ghost story is enough **to scare** anyone."},{"sentence":"Hindi siya nakasuot ng costume dahil ayaw niyang **makatakot** ng mga bata.","translation":"He didn't wear a costume because he didn't want **to scare** the children."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbubukod-bukod o paglalayo sa isa't isa ng isang grupo ng mga tao, bagay, o ideya.
original_explanation: This is what a teacher does to noisy students, what you do with your laundry (whites and colors), or what happens to a barkada after graduation. It's the great divide. Can also be used for sorting things, like separating M&Ms by color because you're a monster, or sorting your feelings for your ex (it's complicated).
usage_notes: The root "hiwalay" is reduplicated to indicate that multiple items or groups are being separated. It's a command/object-focus form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **paghiwa-hiwalayin** ang mga basura sa nabubulok at di-nabubulok.","translation":"We need **to separate** the trash into biodegradable and non-biodegradable."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan silang **paghiwa-hiwalayin** ng tadhana, ngunit nanatili silang matatag.","translation":"Fate tried **to separate them**, but they remained strong."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pampang o tabing-ilog.
original_explanation: Not just the city with the famous river, but the OG Tagalog word for a riverbank. Before it was a location, it was... a location. Think of it as the place where you'd have a picnic by the water, or where the 'labanderas' used to wash clothes. Its modern use is almost entirely for the city name.
usage_notes: This definition is archaic as a common noun and is now almost exclusively known as the proper noun for Pasig City and the Pasig River.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa lumang kwento, ang mga dalaga ay naglalaba sa **pasig**.","translation":"In old stories, the maidens would do laundry on the **riverbank**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghahabla o pagsasampa ng kaso laban sa isang tao sa korte. Maaari ring mangahulugang pagtugis o pagpaparusa nang walang hustisya.
original_explanation: This is 'pag-usapan' with lawyers and a judge. It's taking a grievance to the next level—the legal level. When someone says 'I'm going to sue you!', this is the verb for it. On a darker note, it can also mean to relentlessly hunt or torment someone, like how your conscience 'persecutes' you after eating the whole cake.
usage_notes: This word has a strong legal or moral connotation. It can mean both legal prosecution and unjust persecution.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang gobyerno na **mag-usig** sa mga sangkot sa korapsyon.","translation":"The government decided to **prosecute** those involved in corruption."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **mag-usig** ka ng iyong konsensya.","translation":"Don't let your conscience **persecute** you."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pagluluto kung saan ang karne ay inihaw, nilitson, o pinirito nang dahan-dahan. Tumutukoy rin ito sa mismong putahe na niluto sa ganitong paraan.
original_explanation: This isn't just about the Mexican 'carne asada'. In the Philippines, 'asada' is a general term for roasting. It's the method behind lechon manok or that perfectly roasted pork belly. Think of it as the slow-and-steady cooking method that brings out all the juicy flavors. Yung tipong inihaw pero mas sosyal.
usage_notes: Mas karaniwang ginagamit ang mga tiyak na salita tulad ng 'inihaw' o 'litson', ngunit nauunawaan pa rin ang 'asada' lalo na sa konteksto ng mga putaheng may impluwensyang Espanyol.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paborito niyang lutuin ay manok na **asada**.","translation":"His favorite dish is roasted chicken (**asado**)."},{"sentence":"Natutunan niya ang paraan ng pag-**asada** mula sa kanyang lola.","translation":"She learned the method of **roasting** from her grandmother."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking tumatanggap ng pensiyon, karaniwan dahil sa pagreretiro sa trabaho o bilang benepisyaryo.
original_explanation: The male counterpart to the pensyonada. This is your lolo who spends his mornings reading the newspaper (or scrolling through Facebook), tending to his fighting cocks, or meeting up with his fellow retirees at the local coffee shop to solve the world's problems. His 'uniform' is often a sando, shorts, and a 'Good Morning' towel draped over his shoulder.
usage_notes: Ito ang panlalaking anyo ng 'pensyonada'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dating sundalo ang **pensyonado** na nakatira sa kanto.","translation":"The **pensioner** living on the corner is a former soldier."},{"sentence":"Tuwing umaga, nagkakape ang mga **pensyonado** sa parke.","translation":"Every morning, the male **pensioners** drink coffee at the park."}]

translation: to fix; to arrange; to settle
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay sa kaayusan; pagkukumpuni ng isang bagay na sira; paglutas sa isang problema o hindi pagkakaunawaan.
original_explanation: The ultimate "get your life together" verb. It can mean fixing a broken appliance ("Ayusin mo 'yung electric fan"), cleaning your messy room ("Ayusin mo 'yung kwarto mo!"), or settling a conflict ("Ayusin n'yo 'yang gulo n'yo!"). It's the go-to word for bringing order to chaos, whether it's a tangled headset, a messy spreadsheet, or a complicated relationship.
usage_notes: A very versatile verb with multiple applications: fixing, arranging, tidying, mediating, preparing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**ayusin** mo naman ang mga libro sa estante.","translation":"Please **arrange** the books on the shelf."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **ayusin** ang gusot sa pagitan nating dalawa.","translation":"We need to **settle** the conflict between us."},{"sentence":"Tatawag ako ng mekaniko para **ayusin** ang sasakyan.","translation":"I will call a mechanic to **fix** the car."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng may lihim na romantikong relasyon sa isang lalaking mayroon nang opisyal na kasintahan o asawa.
