original_explanation: The unofficial, un-postable, 'it's complicated' girlfriend. She gets the secret texts, not the public declarations of love. In the world of teleseryes, she's the character everyone loves to hate, the one who causes all the drama and gets a dramatic confrontation scene involving a lot of hair-pulling and sabunutan. Modern term for 'kabit' or 'kerida'.
usage_notes: A derogatory slang loanword. The Tagalog equivalents 'kabit' or 'kerida' are more common and carry a stronger negative connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nalaman ng asawa niya na may **sidechick** pala siya kaya naghiwalay sila.","translation":"His wife found out he had a **sidechick**, so they separated."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang papayag maging **sidechick** lang, girl. You deserve to be the main.","translation":"Don't agree to just be a **sidechick**, girl. You deserve to be the main one."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maamoy o malanghap ang isang mabango o kaaya-ayang halimuyak.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you walk past a bakeshop and the smell of pandesal hits you. Or when your crush walks by and you catch a whiff of their perfume. It's the more poetic, 'pang-harana' version of 'maamoy'. You don't just smell it; you *experience* the fragrance.
usage_notes: Used specifically for pleasant smells. You wouldn't say 'masamyo ang basura'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sarap **masamyo** ng mga bulaklak sa hardin tuwing umaga.","translation":"It's wonderful to **smell the fragrance** of the flowers in the garden every morning."},{"sentence":"Bigla kong **nasamyo** ang paborito kong pabango.","translation":"I suddenly **caught a whiff** of my favorite perfume."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marahas na pagtatagpo o pagtama ng dalawang bagay, lalo na ng mga sasakyan.
original_explanation: The sound your wallet makes after the 12.12 sale. Kidding aside, this is the literal crash. The 'OMG may nag-bangga sa EDSA kaya traffic' moment. It's the sudden, often destructive, meeting of two objects that weren't supposed to meet.
usage_notes: Primarily used for vehicular accidents but can be used for any forceful collision.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng malaking **bangga** sa kanto ng Ayala at Buendia.","translation":"There was a big **collision** at the corner of Ayala and Buendia."},{"sentence":"Ingat sa pagmamaneho para makaiwas sa **bangga**.","translation":"Drive carefully to avoid a **crash**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagnakaw nang malakihan at may kasamang dahas, karaniwan sa panahon ng digmaan o kaguluhan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang "dambong" (pananamsam) at ang gitlaping "-um-".
original_explanation: This is next-level pagnanakaw. Think pirates looting a ship or corrupt officials raiding the national treasury. It’s not just taking a pen from the office; it's large-scale, shameless robbery. The ultimate 'sana all' ng mga buwaya.
usage_notes: Ito ay tumutukoy sa malawakang pagnanakaw, kadalasan ay may kinalaman sa kapangyarihan o kaguluhan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinasabing **dumambong** ng yaman ng bayan ang mga tiwaling opisyal.","translation":"It is said that the corrupt officials **plundered** the nation's wealth."},{"sentence":"Ang mga pirata ay **dumambong** sa mga kalapit na isla para sa ginto.","translation":"The pirates **looted** the nearby islands for gold."}]

translation: to fit; to adjust; to make suitable
meaning_filipino: Ayusin, ibagay, o itugma ang isang bagay upang maging angkop sa sitwasyon, lugar, o sa isa pang bagay.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "i-" at salitang-ugat na "akma" (bagay, angkop, lapat).
original_explanation: The everyday version of 'iagpang'. It's what you do when your pants are too loose and you adjust your belt. Or when you change your attitude to fit the mood of the room. "Iakma mo naman ang ugali mo, nasa lamay tayo." It's all about making things 'sakto' or just right.
usage_notes: Napakakaraniwang salita para sa pag-a-adjust ng mga bagay, konsepto, o pag-uugali.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **iakma** ang iyong bilis sa pagmamaneho sa kondisyon ng kalsada.","translation":"You need to **adjust** your driving speed to the road conditions."},{"sentence":"Subukan mong **iakma** ang iyong sarili sa bagong patakaran ng kumpanya.","translation":"Try to **adapt** yourself to the company's new policy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mailimbag at maipamahagi sa publiko ang isang akda, balita, o anunsyo sa pamamagitan ng diyaryo, magasin, aklat, o iba pang midyum.
etymology: From ma- + lathala (publish). 'Lathala' itself is a portmanteau of 'dala sa tala' (carried to the stars/record).
original_explanation: Before 'going viral' or 'trending on Twitter,' this was the ultimate goal. It's having your work—be it a story, a research paper, or your angry letter to the editor—printed and distributed for everyone to see. It's the OG 'Share' button. In today's world, it also applies to being published online. It's the moment your thoughts are no longer just in your drafts folder but are out there for the world to read, critique, and turn into a meme.
usage_notes: A formal term associated with journalism, literature, and academic work.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap ng bawat manunulat na **malathala** ang kanilang aklat.","translation":"It is every writer's dream for their book **to be published**."},{"sentence":"Inaasahang **malathala** bukas sa pahayagan ang resulta ng pagsusulit.","translation":"The exam results are expected **to be published** in the newspaper tomorrow."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa lahat ng pagkakataon; nang walang patid o paghinto; palagi.
etymology: Posibleng mula sa pariralang 'para atî' (para dito/diyan), na nag-evolve ang kahulugan sa paglipas ng panahon.
original_explanation: Your go-to word for 'always.' It's the clingy ex of adverbs. 'Parati na lang akong iniiwan.' (I'm *always* the one being left behind.) 'Parati siyang late.' (He's *always* late.) It has a slightly more dramatic, almost complaining tone than 'palagi'. It’s the perfect word for your hugot lines.
usage_notes: Madalas na ipinagpapalit sa 'palagi', ngunit ang 'parati' ay may bahagyang diin sa pagiging paulit-ulit o walang tigil, minsan may kasamang himig ng reklamo o pagkadismaya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Parati** siyang nag-aaral kaya matataas ang kanyang mga marka.","translation":"She **always** studies, that's why her grades are high."},{"sentence":"Bakit **parati** na lang ako ang nauutusan mo?","translation":"Why am I **always** the one you ask to run errands?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng mag-aaral sa antas ng kolehiyo.
original_explanation: The classic 'dalagang Pilipina' in a university setting. Yung tipong naka-uniform, may dalang maraming libro, at laging may headphones. Sometimes associated with a certain social class or school (e.g., 'conyo girl' vibes), but really, it just means a female college student.
usage_notes: More common than 'kolehiyal'. Can sometimes carry connotations of being from a private, exclusive school.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pangarap niya ay maging isang matagumpay na **kolehiyala**.","translation":"Her dream is to be a successful **female college student**."},{"sentence":"Kilala ang mga **kolehiyala** mula sa unibersidad na iyon sa kanilang talino at ganda.","translation":"The **co-eds** from that university are known for their intelligence and beauty."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi pa lubos na luto; nasa estado sa pagitan ng pagiging hilaw at luto.
original_explanation: This is the state of your fried chicken when you're too hungry to wait—crispy on the outside, but still clucking on the inside. It's that medium-rare steak that's a bit too 'rare'. Or the rice that's still crunchy. When someone gives you unsolicited advice, you can say their opinion is taghilaw—not fully baked.
usage_notes: Can also be used metaphorically for something that is half-baked or not well-thought-out.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayokong kumain ng manok na **taghilaw** pa.","translation":"I don't want to eat chicken that is still **undercooked**."},{"sentence":"**Taghilaw** ang mga plano nila kaya hindi ito naaprubahan.","translation":"Their plans were **half-baked** so they weren't approved."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapang matulis ang dulo na ginagamit sa paggawa ng butas sa mga materyales tulad ng katad, kahoy, o papel.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na "punzón" (awl, punch).
original_explanation: The OG hole-puncher, but for serious business like leather or wood. Your friendly neighborhood sapatero (shoemaker) definitely has one of these. It’s the tool you use when a regular needle or 'butas' from your ballpen just won't cut it.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ng sapatero ang **punson** upang butasan ang bagong sinturon.","translation":"The shoemaker used the **awl** to punch a hole in the new belt."},{"sentence":"Ingatan mo ang paggamit ng **punson** dahil matulis iyan.","translation":"Be careful using the **punch** because it is sharp."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbebenta ng isang ari-arian, karaniwan sa pamamagitan ng subasta, dahil sa hindi pagbabayad ng utang.
original_explanation: This is when things get serious with your bank loan. If you don't pay up, your property (house, car, etc.) goes up for remata. It's basically a "for sale by force" event. For bargain hunters, it's a goldmine; for the original owner, it's a financial nightmare.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of real estate and bank loans.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa **remata** ang bahay nila dahil sa malaking pagkakautang.","translation":"Their house is up for **foreclosure** because of a large debt."},{"sentence":"Naghahanap siya ng murang sasakyan sa mga **remata**.","translation":"He is looking for a cheap car at **auction sales**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tradisyonal na instrumentong pangmusika sa Pilipinas na may dalawang kuwerdas, karaniwang hugis bangka at kalimitang matatagpuan sa mga katutubong pangkat.
original_explanation: The Filipino equivalent of a rockstar's guitar, but way, way older and more chill. It's a two-stringed, boat-shaped lute from places like Palawan and Mindanao. Think of it as the ultimate indigenous instrument for serenading or telling epic stories through music. The sound of pre-colonial Philippines.
usage_notes: A specific type of indigenous Philippine stringed instrument.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagtugtog ng **kudyapi** ay isang sining na ipinapasa sa mga henerasyon.","translation":"Playing the **kudyapi** is an art passed down through generations."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko ang isang tunay na **kudyapi** sa pambansang museo.","translation":"I saw a real **two-stringed lute** at the national museum."}]

translation: to be able to anger someone; to cause anger
meaning_filipino: Magdulot o maging sanhi ng galit sa isang tao.
original_explanation: That moment when you do something, intentionally or not, that pushes someone's buttons. Tipong nag-reply ka ng "K" sa long message niya. O kaya 'yung sinabi mong "calm down" sa isang taong halata namang hindi calm. Anything that can trigger the beast mode.
usage_notes: Often used in hypothetical or cautionary statements. "Nakagalit" is the past tense (caused anger).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iwasan mong sabihin 'yan dahil baka **makagalit** ka ng iyong ama.","translation":"Avoid saying that because you might **anger** your father."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko sinasadyang **makagalit**; nagbibiro lang ako.","translation":"I didn't mean to **cause anger**; I was just joking."}]

meaning_filipino: Simulan o buksan ang isang gawain, kaganapan, o proseso.
original_explanation: The go-signal. The 'Game na!' moment. What you tell your friend when they're still hesitating to spill the chismis. 'Umpisahan mo na, dali!' It's the official start of anything, from a meeting that could have been an email to a karaoke session that will last until 3 AM.
usage_notes: The '-han' suffix makes this a transitive verb, indicating that the action of starting is directed *at* something. 'Umpisahan mo ang kwento' (You start the story).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sige, **umpisahan** na natin ang miting para matapos tayo nang maaga.","translation":"Okay, let's **start** the meeting so we can finish early."},{"sentence":"Paano ko ba uumpisahan ang pag-amin sa kanya?","translation":"How will I start confessing to him/her?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kati o kakaibang pakiramdam sa lalamunan na nag-uudyok sa isang tao na umubo o tumikhim.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung feeling sa lalamunan mo na parang may dumaang langgam tapos na-stuck. Hindi siya sakit, pero super annoying. It's the reason you keep making that little 'ehem' sound during a quiet meeting. Ito 'yung nagpaparamdam na either uubuhin ka na o kailangan mo lang ng candy.
usage_notes: Espesipikong tumutukoy sa pakiramdam sa lalamunan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May nararamdaman akong **kalamkam** sa lalamunan ko, baka kailangan ko ng tubig.","translation":"I feel a **tickling sensation** in my throat, maybe I need water."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa **kalamkam**, hindi siya tumigil sa pagtikhim.","translation":"Because of the **tickle**, he couldn't stop clearing his throat."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan ang mga sasakyan o tao ay pansamantalang pinahihinto para sa inspeksyon, pag-verify ng mga dokumento, o pagpapatupad ng seguridad.
original_explanation: That thing that suddenly appears on the road, especially during ECQ, making you check if your driver's license is expired or if you forgot your face mask. Parang biglaang quiz sa kalsada. 'Dumaan kami sa tatlong checkpoint papuntang probinsya.'
usage_notes: Widely used, especially in news and during periods of heightened security or quarantine.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinarang kami sa **checkpoint** dahil sa coding.","translation":"We were stopped at the **checkpoint** because of the number coding scheme."},{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang mga pulis sa **checkpoint** kagabi.","translation":"The police were strict at the **checkpoint** last night."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa loob lamang ng maikling panahon o panandalian.
original_explanation: The official time unit of Filipino parents when they say "sandali lang." In reality, 'sasandali' could mean five minutes or two hours. "Lalabas lang ako sasandali" often means they'll come back with groceries for a week. It's the cousin of "on the way na ako" when they just woke up.
usage_notes: The 'sa-' prefix here is a reduplication of the first syllable of the root 'sandali', but it functions to mean 'for just a moment'. It's often used interchangeably with 'sandali lang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaari ba akong umupo rito nang **sasandali**?","translation":"May I sit here **for a moment**?"},{"sentence":"Hihinto muna kami nang **sasandali** para magpahinga.","translation":"We will stop **briefly** to rest."}]

translation: to spit out phlegm; to expectorate
meaning_filipino: Ilabas ang plema o malapot na laway mula sa lalamunan o baga sa pamamagitan ng pag-ubo.
original_explanation: That gross but necessary thing you do when you have a bad cough. It’s the sound your tito makes in the morning that echoes through the whole house. Not a pretty word, not a pretty action, but when you gotta idahak, you gotta idahak. Just please, not on the sidewalk.
usage_notes: 'Dahak' is the noun for phlegm. 'Idahak' is the action of spitting it out.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinabihan siya ng doktor na kailangan niyang **idahak** ang plema para gumaan ang kanyang paghinga.","translation":"The doctor told him he needs to **spit out the phlegm** to ease his breathing."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **idahak** ang plema kapag tuyo ang ubo.","translation":"It's difficult to **expectorate** phlegm when you have a dry cough."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matalinghagang katawagan para sa industriya ng pelikula o sinehan; ang malaking telang puti kung saan ipinapalabas ang mga pelikula.
original_explanation: A fancy, old-school term for the movies or the big screen. Parang 'Hollywood' pero pang-Pinoy. When you say someone is a star of the **puting-tabing**, you mean they're a movie star, not a TV star or a TikTok influencer.
usage_notes: Isang matalinghaga o pampanitikang termino para sa sinehan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming sikat na artista ang nagsimula sa **puting-tabing**.","translation":"Many famous actors started on the **silver screen**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bahagi ng isang mas malaking kabuuan na may maliit na sukat.
original_explanation: This is what you get when you ask for "pahingi" of your friend's chicharon. It's the last maliit na piraso of chocolate you've been saving. It can also be a tiny piece of information, like a chismis, or a fragment of a broken heart (charot).
usage_notes: Very common phrase. Can be literal (food, objects) or figurative (information, feelings).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigyan mo ako kahit **maliit na piraso** lang ng cake.","translation":"Give me even just a **small piece** of the cake."},{"sentence":"Ang baso ay nabasag at naging maraming **maliliit na piraso**.","translation":"The glass broke and turned into many **small pieces**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pandiwa ng pagkopya o pagnanakaw sa gawa ng iba at pag-angkin nito bilang sarili.
original_explanation: The action verb for when you're about to commit the academic crime of 'plahiyo'. This is what happens when you see a really good meme and post it without giving credit. "Huwag mong plahiyuhin ang thesis ko, bes!"
usage_notes: The verb form of 'plahiyo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binalaan ng propesor ang mga estudyante na huwag **plahiyuhin** ang kanilang mga sanaysay.","translation":"The professor warned the students not to **plagiarize** their essays."},{"sentence":"Mahirap patunayan na **plinahiyo** niya ang buong kanta.","translation":"It's hard to prove that he **plagiarized** the entire song."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang isa sa sampung pantay na bahagi ng isang kabuuan; ang ikapu.
original_explanation: This is the tithe you give to the church. Or the **ikasampung bahagi** of your 'sahod' that automatically goes to your milk tea addiction. It's that 10% slice of the pie, the portion you set aside for something important (or delicious).
usage_notes: A more formal and explicit way of saying 'ikapu' (tithe). It is literally 'tenth part'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglaan siya ng **ikasampung bahagi** ng kaniyang kita para sa kawanggawa.","translation":"He allocated **one-tenth** of his income for charity."},{"sentence":"Ang **ikasampung bahagi** ng populasyon ay nakatira sa lungsod na iyon.","translation":"A **tenth** of the population lives in that city."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang palapag o sahig na nasa pagitan ng mga pangunahing palapag ng isang gusali, karaniwang mas mababa ang kisame kaysa sa mga buong palapag.
original_explanation: Ito yung "half-floor" sa mga lumang bahay o sa mall. Parang 'yung state ng relationship niyo—hindi kayo pero hindi rin magkaibigan. Nasa gitna. Mezzanine level. Pwedeng bodega, pwedeng office, pwedeng tambayan.
usage_notes: Madalas makita sa mga lumang bahay na may impluwensyang Espanyol o sa mga modernong disenyo ng gusali at condo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginawang silid-aklatan ang **entresuwelo** ng lumang bahay.","translation":"The **mezzanine** of the old house was turned into a library."},{"sentence":"Nakatayo ang coffee shop sa **entresuwelo** ng mall.","translation":"The coffee shop is located on the **mezzanine** of the mall."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglaki o pag-umbok ng isang bahagi, karaniwan sa katawan, dahil sa pamamaga, pinsala, o pagkaipon ng likido.
original_explanation: Yung pisngi mo after bunutan ng wisdom tooth. Yung bukol mo after mauntog sa pinto. It's that puffy state that screams 'may nangyaring masama dito.'
usage_notes: Used as a noun ('ang pintog'). Can be used interchangeably with 'pamamaga' or 'bukol'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi humuhupa ang **pintog** ng kanyang paa.","translation":"The **swelling** of his foot is not subsiding."},{"sentence":"May **pintog** sa noo niya matapos siyang mauntog.","translation":"There is a **bulge** on his forehead after he bumped his head."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kabibe na karaniwang may butas sa gitna, popular na ginagamit sa paggawa ng mga alahas tulad ng kuwintas at pulseras.
etymology: From Hawaiian 'puka,' meaning 'hole.' The term was popularized in the Philippines and globally.
original_explanation: The official shell of the 90s beach-loving tito and the ultimate pasalubong from Boracay. These are those small, white, naturally-holed shells that scream 'I've been to the beach and all I got was this awesome necklace.' The name itself got so famous it's used internationally.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to the shell used in jewelry, named for the hole ('puka') in it.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili siya ng kuwintas na gawa sa **puka** bilang alaala ng kanyang bakasyon sa dagat.","translation":"He bought a necklace made of **puka** shells as a souvenir of his beach vacation."},{"sentence":"Naging uso noong dekada nobenta ang mga **puka** shell necklace.","translation":"**Puka** shell necklaces became trendy in the nineties."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng peryodiko o babasahin na may mga larawan at artikulo, karaniwang inilalathala nang lingguhan o buwanan.
original_explanation: Before Instagram and TikTok, this was your source for chismis, fashion tips, and celebrity posters. 'Yung binabasa mo sa waiting area ng dental clinic. Now, it's mostly a flat-lay prop for your coffee shop photos.
usage_notes: A direct loanword. Pronunciation is often Filipinized.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lumabas na ang bagong isyu ng paborito kong **magasin**.","translation":"The new issue of my favorite **magazine** is out."},{"sentence":"Nagbabasa siya ng **magasin** habang naghihintay.","translation":"He/She is reading a **magazine** while waiting."}]

translation: having the same name; being namesakes
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa dalawa o higit pang tao na may parehong pangalan.
etymology: From Tagalog 'magka-' (to have, to be with) and Spanish 'tocayo' (namesake).
original_explanation: When you're at Starbucks and they call your name, but someone else gets the coffee. 'Ay, magkatokayo pala kami!' It's the original identity theft, but with more caffeine involved.
usage_notes: This refers to people who share the same first name.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Parehong 'Jose' ang pangalan nila, kaya sila ay **magkatokayo**.","translation":"They are both named 'Jose', so they are **namesakes**."},{"sentence":"Nagkakilala kami sa isang event, at nalaman naming **magkatokayo** pala kami!","translation":"We met at an event, and we found out we **have the same name**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalakbay o paggalaw nang salungat sa direksyon ng hangin, agos ng tubig, o anumang puwersa.
original_explanation: Parang pag-commute sa EDSA rush hour—you're going against a massive force. O kaya parang pag-uwi mo ng probinsya nung Pasko, sungsong ka sa dagsa ng mga taong papuntang Maynila naman. It’s that feeling of struggling against the flow.
usage_notes: Often used in nautical or travel contexts, but can be used metaphorically for going against popular opinion or a powerful force.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **sungsungin** ang malakas na hangin habang nagbibisikleta.","translation":"It's difficult to **go against** the strong wind while cycling."},{"sentence":"Nais niyang **sungsungin** ang agos ng karamihan at ipaglaban ang kanyang paniniwala.","translation":"He wants to **go against** the current of the majority and fight for his beliefs."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang pautos na ginagamit upang anyayahan o tawagin ang isang tao na lumapit.
etymology: Contraction of "hali ka," with "hali" being an old root for "come."
original_explanation: The universal Filipino call to action. Your mom yells this when dinner is ready. Your friend whispers this when there's chismis. It's the singular, more personal version of "tara!" or "halikayo!" Used for one person only. **Halika**, kain tayo!
usage_notes: Used when speaking to one person (the 'ka' part). For multiple people, use "Halikayo."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Halika!** Samahan mo akong mamili sa palengke.","translation":"**Come here!** Accompany me to shop at the market."},{"sentence":"Narinig niya ang tawag ng ina, '**Halika**, anak, kakain na.'","translation":"He heard his mother's call, '**Come**, child, it's time to eat.'"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, tunog, o kilos na ginagamit upang itaboy o palayasin ang mga hayop, tao, o masasamang espiritu.
original_explanation: Your go-to tool for shooing things away. For stray dogs, it might be a 'walis tambo'. For annoying officemates, it might be your noise-cancelling headphones. For lamok, it's katol or bug spray. The ultimate pang-aboy for unwanted visitors? Pretending you're not home.
usage_notes: Maaaring isang pisikal na bagay, isang tunog, o kahit isang kilos.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha siya ng patpat bilang **pang-aboy** sa mga asong-gala.","translation":"He got a stick as something to **drive away** the stray dogs."},{"sentence":"Ang malakas na tunog ng kampana ay nagsisilbing **pang-aboy** sa masasamang espiritu, ayon sa paniniwala.","translation":"The loud sound of the bell serves to **repel** evil spirits, according to belief."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang puno o halaman na may maraming sanga. Sa matalinhagang paraan, ito ay nangangahulugang kumplikado o may maraming bahagi.
etymology: ma- (adjective prefix meaning 'having much of') + sanga (branch).
original_explanation: This is that tree in your backyard that's perfect for climbing because it has branches everywhere. Figuratively, it's your love life—'it's complicated.' Pwede ring plot ng K-drama na ang daming twists and turns, or yung family tree niyo na kailangan ng flowchart para maintindihan.
usage_notes: Can be literal (for trees) or figurative (for topics, stories, problems).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap akyatin ang puno dahil ito ay hindi gaanong **masanga**.","translation":"It's hard to climb the tree because it's not very **branchy**."},{"sentence":"Naging **masanga** ang usapan at napunta na sa iba't ibang paksa.","translation":"The discussion became **convoluted** and went into different topics."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging matanda o may edad; kahinugan sa karanasan o gulang.
original_explanation: That moment when you start saying 'Noong panahon namin...' or your back hurts from just sleeping. It's the state of being a 'Tito' or 'Tita' of Manila, not by relation, but by your life choices (e.g., preferring home over a party). It's not just about years, but about the wisdom (or body aches) that come with them.
usage_notes: Often used with prefixes like `pag-` (`pagtanda` - the process of aging) or `ka-` (`katandaan` - old age). The adjective form is 'matanda' (old). Homonym with 'tanda' (sign/mark).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga puting buhok ay senyales ng **tanda**.","translation":"White hair is a sign of **old age**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong ikahiya ang iyong **tanda**; dala nito ay karunungan.","translation":"Don't be ashamed of your **age**; it brings wisdom."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng isang tao na malimit mag-isip nang malalim o seryoso tungkol sa mga bagay-bagay.
original_explanation: This is your friend who is always in pensive mode, as if constantly thinking of a life-changing formula. They're not just overthinking your chat, they're just genuinely a deep thinker. The 'Why is the world round and not square?' level of thinking.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging **palaisip** si Ana tuwing papalapit na ang mga pagsusulit.","translation":"Ana is always **pensive** whenever exams are approaching."},{"sentence":"Isang batang **palaisip** si Jose, mahilig magbasa ng mga libro.","translation":"Jose is a **thoughtful** child; he loves to read books."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, pahayag, o kilos na nagbibigay-linaw o nagdudulot ng pag-unawa sa isang malabo o kumplikadong paksa.
etymology: From nakapag- (causative, ability) + pa- (causative) + liwanag (light, clarity).
original_explanation: The opposite of your friend who gives confusing directions. This is something that brings an 'aha!' moment. It's the diagram that finally makes sense of the data, the 'hugot' line that perfectly describes your feelings, or the tutorial video that saves you from a failing grade. It sheds light on things.
usage_notes: Can refer to a person explaining something, or an object/event that itself provides clarity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga larawang ito ay **nakapagpapaliwanag** kung ano talaga ang nangyari.","translation":"These pictures **explain** what really happened."},{"sentence":"Isang mahusay na guro ang **nakapagpapaliwanag** ng mahihirap na konsepto sa simpleng paraan.","translation":"A great teacher is one who **can explain** difficult concepts in a simple way."}]

translation: to take seriously; to make real; to fulfill
meaning_filipino: Gawing totoo, seryoso, o ganap ang isang bagay na sinabi, binalak, o ipinangako; isakatuparan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang 'totoo' na may mga hulaping '-han' at '-in'.
original_explanation: This is the 'put your money where your mouth is' verb. When someone tells you "Totohanin mo 'yan," they're challenging you to turn your words into action. It's what you tell your friend who keeps saying they'll start a business, or what you hope your crush does after all that landi. From 'sana all' to 'sana totoo.'
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang isang utos, pakiusap, o isang pahayag ng intensyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Akala ko biro lang, pero mukhang **totohanin** niya ang pag-alis papuntang Canada.","translation":"I thought it was just a joke, but it looks like he will **make good on** his plan to leave for Canada."},{"sentence":"Sige nga, **totohanin** mo yang banta mo!","translation":"Go on, **make** your threat **a reality**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang utos o pakiusap na kunin o sunduin ang isang bagay o tao mula sa isang lugar.
etymology: Isang baryasyon ng 'kunin', na nagmula sa salitang-ugat na 'kuha' at hulaping '-in'. Ang pagkawala ng 'h' at pagbabago ng patinig ay karaniwan sa ebolusyon ng wika.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of your mom yelling 'Pakikuha ng toyo sa ref!' but more direct. 'Kaunin mo 'yung kapatid mo sa school' is a classic errand. It’s the action of getting something or someone. Think of it as the command form for GrabExpress or Lalamove.
usage_notes: A variant of the more common word 'kunin'. Both are widely understood and used interchangeably in many regions, especially in spoken language. 'Kaunin' focuses on the object being fetched.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kaunin** mo ang mga sinampay dahil uulan na.","translation":"**Get** the laundry because it's about to rain."},{"sentence":"Sino ang pwedeng **kaunin** sa airport mamaya?","translation":"Who can be **fetched** from the airport later?"}]

translation: to be a godparent to; to beget a child with
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng anak sa isang tao; o tumayong ninong o ninang sa binyag o kasal ng anak ng iba.
original_explanation: This word has two major vibes. 1) The biological 'let's make a baby' context. 2) The more common social context: to become a godparent (ninong/ninang). It's the ultimate Filipino friendship upgrade. When a friend asks 'Pa-anak naman kami sa'yo,' they're not asking for your DNA, they're asking you to commit to giving aguinaldo every Christmas.
usage_notes: Ang kahulugan ay nakadepende nang husto sa konteksto. Ang 'Anakan mo' ay maaaring mangahulugang 'magkaanak ka sa kanya' o 'maging ninong/ninang ka sa anak niya', kung saan ang huli ay mas karaniwan sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Plano naming **anakan** si Lito sa binyag ng aming bunso.","translation":"We plan to have Lito **be the godparent** at our youngest's baptism."},{"sentence":"Sa alamat, **inanakán** ng diyos ang isang mortal.","translation":"In the legend, the god **begot a child** with a mortal."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga maliliit at mumurahing bagay na walang gaanong halaga o gamit; mga palamuti o abubot.
etymology: From Spanish 'chuchería' (trinket, trifle), pluralized. This is the direct source word for 'tsitsirya' as well, but this form retains the 'trinket' meaning while 'tsitsirya' shifted to 'snack food'.
original_explanation: This is the official term for all the cute but 'wala namang silbi' stuff you buy from Divisoria, a tiangge, or Miniso. Think tiny figurines, colorful pens you'll never use, and other small items that just 'spark joy' for a moment. It's the physical form of an impulse buy. Basically, a more formal-sounding 'abubot'.
usage_notes: 'Tsitsirya' (for snacks) and 'tsutserias' (for trinkets) both come from the same Spanish root 'chuchería', but have diverged in meaning in Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng kung anu-anong **tsutserias** ang kanyang kwarto.","translation":"Her room is full of various **trinkets**."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang mangolekta ng mga **tsutserias** mula sa kanyang mga paglalakbay.","translation":"She loves to collect **knick-knacks** from her travels."}]

meaning_filipino: Bawat isa sa mga karaniwang makulay at manipis na bahagi ng bulaklak na nakapalibot sa gitna nito.
etymology: Hindi tiyak ang pinagmulan ngunit isang katutubong salita sa mga wika sa Pilipinas.
original_explanation: This is the 'he loves me, he loves me not' part of the flower. The petal. 'Yung pinakamakulay at magandang parte ng bulaklak na umaakit sa mga bubuyog... at sa mga taong mahilig kumuha ng aesthetic photos for their IG feed.
usage_notes: Isang partikular na termino sa botanika na kilala rin ng pangkalahatang publiko.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nalaglag ang mga huling **talulot** ng rosas dahil sa malakas na hangin.","translation":"The last **petals** of the rose fell because of the strong wind."},{"sentence":"Ang bawat **talulot** ng sampaguita ay naglalabas ng matamis na amoy.","translation":"Each **petal** of the sampaguita releases a sweet fragrance."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinuno ng isang kolehiyo o fakultad sa loob ng isang unibersidad o pamantasan.
original_explanation: The final boss of a college department. They're the ones you see during graduation ceremonies or when a major issue happens in your college. You generally don't want to be called to the Dean's Office unless you're an honor student receiving an award. It's like being called to the principal's office, but for adults.
usage_notes: Ginagamit lamang sa konteksto ng akademya. Ang katumbas nito sa Kastila ay 'dekano' (lalaki) o 'dekana' (babae).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinausap ng mga magulang ang **dean** ng College of Engineering.","translation":"The parents spoke with the **dean** of the College of Engineering."},{"sentence":"Ang aming **dean** ay isang respetadong manunulat.","translation":"Our **dean** is a respected writer."}]

meaning_filipino: Kumawala mula sa pagkakagapos, pagkakakulong, o anumang uri ng paghihigpit.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na gusto mo nang umalis sa toxic na trabaho o relasyon. "I need to break free!" moment mo, parang si Freddie Mercury pero mas Tagalog. It's the urge to escape from something that's holding you back, whether it's literal ropes or metaphorical emotional baggage from your ex.
usage_notes: Often used in a dramatic or literary context, but can also be used for animals breaking free from a cage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng bilanggo na **mag-alpas** mula sa kanyang selda.","translation":"The prisoner tried to **break free** from his cell."},{"sentence":"Nais ng ibon na **mag-alpas** sa hawla upang malayang makalipad.","translation":"The bird wants to **escape** the cage to fly freely."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan na may mga istante at pinto para sa pag-iimbak ng mga bagay; isang pangkat ng mga tagapayo na bumubuo sa pangunahing sangay ng ehekutibo ng pamahalaan.
original_explanation: Has two main meanings. 1) The thing in your kitchen where you hide the good snacks from your siblings. 2) The group of high-level government officials who advise the President. Ironically, both types of kabinet are full of important stuff that you probably shouldn't mess with unless you know what you're doing.
usage_notes: The context usually makes the meaning clear (furniture vs. government).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itago mo ang mga baso sa **kabinet** sa kusina.","translation":"Keep the glasses in the kitchen **cabinet**."},{"sentence":"Nagpulong ang Pangulo kasama ang kanyang **kabinet**.","translation":"The President had a meeting with his **cabinet**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na humihingi ng bawas sa presyo ng isang produkto o serbisyo; isang mamimili na mahilig tumawad.
etymology: Mula sa `mang-` + `tawad` (bargain). Ang `mang-` ay nagiging `manan-` at inuulit ang unang pantig ng salitang-ugat.
original_explanation: The patron saint of the palengke and Divisoria. Ito 'yung nanay o lola mo na kayang-kayang tawaran 'yung 50-peso item para maging 45 pesos na lang, tapos ang laking tagumpay. Their motto: "Walang tawad? Sige, sa kabila na lang ako." The ultimate skill in Filipino shopping.
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang termino, lalo na sa konteksto ng mga palengke at impormal na komersyo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala ang nanay ko bilang isang dalubhasang **mananawad** sa palengke.","translation":"My mother is known as an expert **haggler** at the market."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubos na tanyag at pamilyar sa napakaraming tao; hindi na maikakaila ang kasikatan.
etymology: Repetition of the root word for intensification.
original_explanation: This isn't just 'known', this is 'OF COURSE, I know them!' level of fame. It's the "Sino 'yan? Ah, si ano pala!" moment turning into "Sino'ng hindi makakakilala sa kanya?". Think the OG artistas, the biggest loveteams, or that one chismosa neighbor na alam ang life story ng buong barangay.
usage_notes: The repetition of "kilala" serves to intensify the meaning, a common grammatical feature in Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kilalang-kilala** ang pamilya nila sa buong bayan dahil sa kanilang kabutihan.","translation":"Their family is **very well-known** throughout the town for their kindness."},{"sentence":"Ang Jollibee ay **kilalang-kilala** hindi lang sa Pilipinas kundi sa buong mundo.","translation":"Jollibee is **very well-known** not just in the Philippines but around the world."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng katangiang kaakit-akit o kahali-halina sa paningin; karaniwang tumutukoy sa isang babae o isang bagay na pambabae.
original_explanation: She's got 'the look'. When someone is described as 'atraktiba', they're not just 'maganda' (beautiful), they have a certain pull or charm. It's the 'head-turner' quality. This is the '-a' version, traditionally for females, but in modern usage, it's often interchangeable with 'atraktibo' even for things.
usage_notes: The feminine form of 'atraktibo'. While traditionally for women, modern usage is more flexible and can describe inanimate objects or concepts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming nagsasabi na **atraktiba** ang bagong aktres.","translation":"Many are saying that the new actress is **attractive**."},{"sentence":"Naging mas **atraktiba** ang alok na trabaho dahil sa mga benepisyo.","translation":"The job offer became more **attractive** because of the benefits."}]

translation: to give a gift to someone
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng isang regalo sa isang tao.
original_explanation: The action verb for the 'Receiving Gifts' love language. It's not just about the 'regalo' itself, but the act of being remembered. Also what you say to your friends hinting at what you want: 'Sana may mag-regalo sa'kin ng plane ticket!'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **regaluhan** ang iyong ina sa Mother's Day.","translation":"Don't forget **to give your mother a gift** on Mother's Day."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pamumuhay sa paraang marangya, magarbo, at sagana na tila isang taong mayaman.
original_explanation: This is what you do on payday weekend. You go to the mall, eat at a restaurant you can't really afford, buy that overpriced coffee, and basically pretend you're a "conyo" kid from a posh village. It's the act of living lavishly, even if it's just for a day, before you go back to eating instant noodles until the next sahod. #TreatYourself
usage_notes: Often used with a hint of irony or aspiration. The root is a compound word 'buhay-mayaman'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tara, **magbuhay-mayaman** tayo kahit isang araw lang at kumain sa buffet.","translation":"Come on, let's **live a rich life** for just one day and eat at a buffet."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o kumpanya na naghahatid ng mga mensahe, sulat, o pakete mula sa isang lugar patungo sa iba.
original_explanation: Ang ating mga modern-day bayani. Ang dahilan kung bakit napipindot mo ang "Add to Cart" nang walang pag-aalinlangan. Sila yung nag-tetext ng "Sir/Ma'am, andito na po ako sa labas," na mas kinakikiligan mo pa kaysa sa text ng jowa mo.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with "rider" or the specific brand name (e.g., "Lalamove", "Grab").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinihintay ko 'yung **courier** na magde-deliver ng inorder kong sapatos.","translation":"I'm waiting for the **courier** who will deliver the shoes I ordered."},{"sentence":"Paki-abot na lang ng bayad sa **courier** pagdating niya.","translation":"Please just hand the payment to the **courier** when he arrives."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasabi o pagpapahayag ng mga mangyayari sa hinaharap, kadalasan sa pamamagitan ng inspirasyon o kutob.
original_explanation: Like your tita who can **maghaula** that you're getting fat just by looking at your profile picture. Or that friend who, after seeing your crush's IG story, predicts, 'Nako, may ka-date 'yan, 'wag ka nang umasa.' Basically, anyone who acts like a manghuhula, with or without tarot cards.
usage_notes: Often associated with fortune-telling or making predictions about the future.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala sa mga taong nagsasabing kaya nilang **maghaula** ng iyong kapalaran.","translation":"Don't believe people who claim they can **predict** your fate."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **maghaula** kung sino ang mananalo sa eleksyon.","translation":"He tried to **predict** who would win the election."}]

translation: Ha! (expression of surprise, triumph, or inquiry)
meaning_filipino: Isang bulalas na nagpapahayag ng pagkagulat, pagtatanong, paghamon, o tagumpay.
original_explanation: The Swiss Army knife of Filipino reactions. Can mean "What did you say?", "I knew it!", "You think you can fool me?", or "OMG!". The tone is everything. A short "Ha?" is a question. A long "Haaaa..." is realization. A sharp "Ha!" is victory. It's the 'seen' of spoken conversations.
usage_notes: Ang kahulugan ay lubos na nakadepende sa tono at konteksto ng paggamit. Ang tandang padamdam (!) ay nagpapahiwatig ng diin, samantalang ang tandang pananong (?) ay nagpapahiwatig ng pagtatanong.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ha!** Akala mo maloloko mo ako, ano?","translation":"**Ha!** You thought you could fool me, huh?"},{"sentence":"**Ha?** Ano'ng sabi mo? Pakiulit nga.","translation":"**Huh?** What did you say? Please repeat it."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglilipat ng pagmamay-ari at kontrol ng isang pribadong industriya, kumpanya, o ari-arian sa pamahalaan o estado.
original_explanation: This is when the government says 'Akin na 'yan' to a private company. Imagine if a big telco or power company suddenly became government-owned. That's 'isabansa.' It’s a big, serious political and economic move, often debated in classrooms and Congress, not so much sa palengke.
usage_notes: Primarily used in political, economic, and historical contexts. The noun form is 'pagsasabansa' or 'nasyonalisasyon'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May mga panukala na **isabansa** ang industriya ng langis.","translation":"There are proposals to **nationalize** the oil industry."},{"sentence":"Matapos ang rebolusyon, maraming kumpanya ang **isinabansa** ng bagong pamahalaan.","translation":"After the revolution, many companies were **nationalized** by the new government."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsisimula ng paggana o pag-usad ng isang makina, sasakyan, o proseso sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: The moment of truth when you turn the key of a second-hand car. "Sana aandar." Also applies to your brain before your first cup of coffee: "Hindi aandar 'to hangga't walang kape."
usage_notes: Primarily used for machines, vehicles, or abstract processes. Less common for people or animals, where 'gagalaw' or 'uunlad' might be used instead.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **aandar** pa itong luma kong kotse.","translation":"I hope this old car of mine **will** still **run**."},{"sentence":"Hindi **aandar** ang proyekto kung walang pondo.","translation":"The project **will not function** without funds."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkuha o pagtala ng puntos sa isang laro, kompetisyon, o pagsusulit.
original_explanation: In basketball, it's what Ginebra fans scream for. In dating, it's a cringey old-timer term for getting someone's number (or more). In the office, it's finally getting your leave approved. "Sana mag-iskor ang pambato natin sa quiz bee."
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of sports, games, and tests. The colloquial, romantic meaning is dated but still understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang layunin ng bawat koponan ay **mag-iskor** ng mas maraming puntos kaysa sa kalaban.","translation":"The goal of each team is to **score** more points than the opponent."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan ni June Mar na **mag-iskor** malapit sa ring.","translation":"June Mar tried to **score** near the ring."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marahas na paninira o pagwasak sa isang lugar, karaniwang dulot ng natural na kalamidad tulad ng bagyo o malakas na hangin.
original_explanation: When a typhoon goes full beast mode and destroys everything in its path, that's 'manalasa'. It's the ultimate 'you shall not pass... without getting wrecked' moment from Mother Nature. Also what your mom does to your room when she's cleaning it and finds your secret stash of snacks.
usage_notes: Often used to describe the destructive force of typhoons, floods, or other disasters. Can also be used figuratively for a person causing chaos.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nanalasa** raw ang bagyong si 'Karding' sa buong Luzon.","translation":"They say typhoon 'Karding' **wreaked havoc** across all of Luzon."},{"sentence":"Ang mga alagang manok ay **nanalasa** sa taniman ng gulay.","translation":"The pet chickens **ravaged** the vegetable patch."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng opisyal na pahintulot, permiso, o kapangyarihan para sa isang bagay na maganap o gawin.
original_explanation: That thing your manager has to do before you can take a vacation leave or claim your expenses. Or when you need to `mag-autorisa` a credit card transaction that's suspiciously large (probably from your 11.11 shopping spree). It’s the adult version of asking for permission.
usage_notes: Commonly used in business, banking, and formal or bureaucratic settings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mo munang **mag-autorisa** ng pagbabayad bago maipadala ang iyong order.","translation":"You first need to **authorize** the payment before your order can be shipped."},{"sentence":"Hindi ako pwedeng umalis hangga't hindi **nag-a-autorisa** ang aking manager.","translation":"I cannot leave until my manager **authorizes** it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sukat ng temperatura sa Celsius scale, kung saan ang tubig ay nagyeyelo sa 0 digri at kumukulo sa 100 digri.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung 'C' na nakikita mo sa weather forecast (e.g., 35°C). 'Pag sinabi ng PAGASA na sobrang init, 'yan 'yung numerong sinisisi mo. Sa Pilipinas, sentigrado ang gamit natin. Hindi tayo Fahrenheit friends dito. Kapag 40 degrees sentigrado, alam mong impyerno na sa labas.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit kasama ang salitang 'digri' o 'grado' (e.g., 'digri sentigrado').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umabot sa 38 digri **sentigrado** ang temperatura kahapon.","translation":"The temperature reached 38 degrees **Celsius** yesterday."},{"sentence":"Pakuluan ang tubig sa 100 digri **sentigrado**.","translation":"Boil the water at 100 degrees **centigrade**."}]

meaning_filipino: Maramihang anyo ng balbal na salitang "ferson"; tumutukoy sa "mga tao" (people).
etymology: Mula sa salitang Ingles na "persons" (plural of person), na binago ang baybay sa paraang Swardspeak o gay lingo.
original_explanation: The plural of 'ferson'. You use this when you're talking about a group. 'Ang daming fersons sa pila!' instead of 'Ang daming tao sa pila!' It’s a bit more playful and trendy. It’s what you say when you enter a party and see the whole gang: 'Andito na pala lahat ng fersons!'
usage_notes: Pangmaramihang anyo ng salitang balbal na 'ferson'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang dami nating **fersons** dito, parang reunion.","translation":"There are so many of us **people** here, it's like a reunion."},{"sentence":"Para sa mga **fersons** na naghahanap ng sign, ito na 'yun.","translation":"For the **people** looking for a sign, this is it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit at mabilis na kislap ng liwanag; ang pagkindat o kislap ng mga bituin o iba pang malayong bagay na nagbibigay-liwanag.
original_explanation: 'Yung ilaw ng Christmas lights na parang may sariling buhay, 'yun ang kutitap. Parang mga mata ng crush mo kapag nakikita ka, biglang nag-sparkle. The OG fairy light aesthetic before it was cool.
usage_notes: Often used poetically to describe stars, lights, or even eyes full of emotion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng **kutitap** ng mga bituin sa probinsya.","translation":"The **twinkle** of the stars in the province is beautiful."},{"sentence":"Makikita mo sa mga mata niya ang **kutitap** ng pag-asa.","translation":"You can see the **glimmer** of hope in his/her eyes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang organisadong kumpetisyon o serye ng mga laro na may mga patakaran at mga kalahok na naglalayong manalo.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `pa-` (nagpapahiwatig ng sanhi) + `laro` (game, play).
original_explanation: Ito yung event sa school, barangay, o office kung saan naglalabasan ang competitive spirit ng lahat. Parang Hunger Games pero ang premyo ay bragging rights, tropeo, at minsan, cash prize. Dito mo makikita kung sino talaga ang pikon at sino ang aayaw na lang 'kasi laro lang naman.'
usage_notes: Madalas na tumutukoy sa mga organisadong kaganapan tulad ng Palarong Pambansa o intramurals sa mga paaralan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumali siya sa **palaro** ng basketball sa aming barangay.","translation":"He joined the basketball **games** in our village."},{"sentence":"Ang Palarong Pambansa ay isang taunang **palaro** para sa mga estudyanteng atleta.","translation":"The Palarong Pambansa is an annual **sports competition** for student-athletes."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lihim na pagmamanman o pagkuha ng impormasyon tungkol sa isang tao, grupo, o bansa.
original_explanation: What you do on your crush's social media profile at 2 AM. Or what your chismosa na kapitbahay does 24/7. "Huwag kang maingay, baka marinig tayo ng kapitbahay nating mahilig mag-ispiya."
usage_notes: Carries a strong sense of secrecy and covert observation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan ang ahente na **mag-ispiya** sa mga kilos ng kalabang bansa.","translation":"The agent was ordered to **spy** on the movements of the enemy nation."},{"sentence":"Nahuli niya ang kanyang kapatid na sinusubukang **mag-ispiya** sa kanyang diary.","translation":"She caught her sibling trying to **spy** on her diary."}]

meaning_filipino: Madaling makita, mapansin, o maunawaan; hindi maitatago at lantad sa paningin o pang-unawa.
original_explanation: When you say 'I'm fine' but your face looks like you just got a 500-page report due tomorrow. Bes, **halata** na. It's the opposite of subtle. It’s what you are when you keep glancing at your crush every 2.5 seconds.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Halata** sa mukha niya ang labis na pagod.","translation":"The extreme fatigue is **obvious** on his face."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi naman **halata** na kinakabahan ka.","translation":"Don't worry, it's not **noticeable** that you're nervous."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang kilos ng pagganap sa isang gawain o tungkulin, karaniwan para sa sahod o kabuhayan. Ito ay ang kasalukuyang anyo ng pandiwang 'magtrabaho'.
original_explanation: The default answer to "Kumusta ka?" when you're an adult. "Eto, nagtatrabaho." It's the daily grind, the 9-to-5 (or the graveyard shift for BPO peeps), the reason for your coffee addiction. It's the hustle to pay the bills and fund your Shopee/Lazada addiction.
usage_notes: Ito ang imperpektibong aspekto (present tense) ng pandiwang 'magtrabaho'. Tumutukoy ito sa kasalukuyang aksyon ng paggawa o sa estado ng pagkakaroon ng hanapbuhay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagtatrabaho** ako bilang isang guro.","translation":"I **work** as a teacher."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo siyang istorbohin, **nagtatrabaho** siya.","translation":"Don't disturb him, he **is working**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangyayari o lugar kung saan naganap ang isang pagbabanggaan, karaniwan sa pagitan ng mga sasakyan.
original_explanation: The chismis magnet on EDSA. When you see traffic suddenly stop, it's probably because of a 'bungguan'. It's the actual collision event or the place where it happened. It's the reason you're late for work, and your boss won't believe you until they see it on the news.
usage_notes: More specific than 'bunggo', often referring to a more significant accident, typically involving vehicles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagdulot ng matinding trapik ang **bungguan** sa may kanto.","translation":"The **collision** at the corner caused heavy traffic."}]

translation: toast (for drinking); a shot/serving of liquor
meaning_filipino: Isang pag-inom ng alak, karaniwang ginagawa kasama ang iba bilang tanda ng pagkakaisa o pagdiriwang; ang mismong inuming alak na ibinubuhos sa baso para sa isang tao.
original_explanation: This is the battle cry of every tito and tita on a Friday night. It's the act of raising your glass and saying "cheers!" before downing that shot of Emperador or that glass of Red Horse. "Tagay!" is the social glue that binds barkadas together over pulutan and karaoke. It's not just drinking; it's a ritual.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb, "tumagay" (to drink/toast), or as an exclamation. The act of sharing one glass among a group is called "tagayan".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **tagay** para sa mga pusong sawi!","translation":"One **toast** for the brokenhearted!"},{"sentence":"Pahingi naman ng isang **tagay** ng beer.","translation":"Can I have a **serving** of beer?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar na maaaring daanan o gamitin bilang ruta mula sa isang punto patungo sa iba; isang landas o pasilyo.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'daan' (way, path) na may panlaping 'pa-…-an', na nagpapahiwatig ng lugar kung saan isinasagawa ang kilos.
original_explanation: Think of it as a "way to have a way". It's the physical path you take. It could be the 'eskinita' (alleyway) you use as a shortcut, the hallway in your office building, or even a metaphorical path in life. It’s the space provided *for passing through* (para + daan + -an).
usage_notes: Maaari ring tumukoy sa isang paraan o metodo, bagaman mas karaniwan ang 'paraan' para sa kahulugang iyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Madilim ang **paraanan** patungo sa likod-bahay.","translation":"The **passageway** to the backyard is dark."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong harangan ang **paraanan**.","translation":"Don't block the **path**."}]

meaning_filipino: Naghanda ng pagkain sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng init. Ito ay nasa panahunang pangnagdaan.
etymology: From "luto" (cook) with the "nag-" prefix for the past tense.
original_explanation: The action is done, the food is (hopefully) ready. This is the past tense of making magic happen in the kitchen. When you tell your friends, 'Guys, nagluto ako,' it's an invitation to feast. It's the proof of your effort, now sitting on the dining table.
usage_notes: The past tense (perfective aspect) of the verb "to cook".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagluto** si tatay ng adobo para sa aming tanghalian.","translation":"Dad **cooked** adobo for our lunch."},{"sentence":"Salamat sa kaibigan ko, siya ang **nagluto** ng lahat ng ito.","translation":"Thanks to my friend, he's the one who **cooked** all of this."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghiram ng pera o bagay na may kasunduang ibabalik sa takdang panahon.
etymology: From `utang` (debt) with the `um-` infix and reduplication of the first syllable of the root.
original_explanation: The official state of being for many people before 'sahod' day. When your friend suddenly becomes extra nice and asks "Bes, kamusta?", they might be umuutang. It's the verb that powers '5-6' lending, credit cards, and the national economy. "Friendship over pag di nagbayad yung umuutang."
usage_notes: Specifically refers to borrowing, usually money, with the obligation to return it.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming tao ang **umuutang** para lang makabili ng bagong gadget.","translation":"Many people are **borrowing money** just to buy a new gadget."},{"sentence":"Nahihirapan siyang magbayad dahil palagi siyang **umuutang**.","translation":"He's having a hard time paying because he is always **getting into debt**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng hindi tamang interpretasyon o pag-unawa sa isang sinabi, ginawa, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: Nagsimula ang lahat sa isang maling pagkakaintindi. Akala niya 'K' lang reply ko kasi galit ako, pero low-batt na talaga ako, bes! It's not you, it's my battery.
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang parirala upang ipaliwanag ang mga hidwaan o pagkakamali sa komunikasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa **maling pagkakaintindi**, nagkaroon sila ng alitan.","translation":"Because of a **misunderstanding**, they had a conflict."},{"sentence":"Linawin natin ang lahat upang maiwasan ang anumang **maling pagkakaintindi**.","translation":"Let's clarify everything to avoid any **misunderstanding**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang makaranas ng hirap, pagsubok, o balakid sa paggawa o pagkamit ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung active state of being "mahirap" (difficult). When you're in the middle of that exam and you're sweating, that's you *nahihirapan*. When you're trying to explain something to your parents about technology and they just don't get it, *nahihirapan* ka. It's the process of struggling through something, the journey, not just the label.
usage_notes: Describes the experience of difficulty. The object of the difficulty is often introduced by "sa."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nahirapan** akong hanapin ang bahay mo dahil walang street sign.","translation":"I **had difficulty** finding your house because there was no street sign."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi ka namin hahayaang **mahirapan**.","translation":"Don't worry, we won't let you **struggle**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paggamit ng sagwan upang mapausad ang isang bangka o sasakyang-tubig.
original_explanation: It's literally paddling a boat. But metaphorically, it's the grind. It's you, trying to move your life forward, 'paddling' through deadlines, traffic, and adulting responsibilities. When someone says 'sagwan lang nang sagwan,' it means 'just keep going,' even if your arms (or your spirit) are getting tired. The original 'push lang' mantra.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakapagod ang **pagsagwan** nang malayo, lalo na kung mag-isa ka lang.","translation":"It's tiring to **paddle** far, especially if you are alone."},{"sentence":"Nanalo sila sa karera dahil sa kanilang sabay-sabay na **pagsagwan**.","translation":"They won the race because of their synchronized **rowing**."}]

translation: To pull out, to unsheathe, to draw out
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbunot o paghugot ng isang bagay mula sa kinalalagyan nito, tulad ng espada mula sa kaluban o ng halaman mula sa lupa.
original_explanation: This is the dramatic move you see in action movies when the hero finally draws his sword. Lagwatan mo 'yung itak! But in real life, it's more like trying to lagwatan your ATM card from a stubborn machine. The drama is real.
usage_notes: A more literary or archaic term for 'bunutin' or 'hugutin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis niyang ni**lagwatan** ang espada mula sa kaluban.","translation":"He quickly **drew** the sword from its sheath."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga latak o pinong tira na lumulubog sa ilalim ng isang likido, tulad ng kapeng barako o alak.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung "bonus" na makukuha mo sa ilalim ng tasa mo ng kapeng barako. Parang 'yung mga huling text message sa isang failed relationship—puro latak at pait. May gumagamit din nito para manghula. "Teh, ano'ng sabi ng gulapong? Magkakajowa na ba 'ko this year?"
usage_notes: Often associated with strong, unfiltered coffee (kapeng barako) and sometimes used in fortune-telling (tasseography).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong inumin ang **gulapong** sa ilalim ng tasa ng kape.","translation":"Don't drink the **dregs** at the bottom of the coffee cup."},{"sentence":"May naiwang **gulapong** sa bote ng lumang alak.","translation":"There were **sediments** left in the bottle of old wine."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalapat o pag-aalis ng isang bagay (gaya ng likido, dumi, o pamahid) sa isang ibabaw sa pamamagitan ng paghaplos o pagkuskos.
original_explanation: This is the OG "swipe." Before Tinder, there was `pagpahid`. Wiping tears away? `Pagpahid` ng luha. Spreading palaman on your pandesal? `Pagpahid` ng butter. Applying Vicks VapoRub on your chest when you have a cold? `Pagpahid` din 'yan. It's the gentle (or sometimes not-so-gentle) act of applying or removing something with a smear.
usage_notes: Can mean both applying (smearing on) and removing (wiping off). Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang malumanay na **pagpahid** ng ina sa noo ng anak ay nagpapakita ng pagmamahal.","translation":"The mother's gentle **wiping** of her child's forehead shows love."},{"sentence":"Isang **pagpahid** lang ng pampabango ay sapat na.","translation":"Just one **smear** of perfume is enough."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nananalangin o namumuno sa isang panalangin.
original_explanation: This is your lola at 6 PM, rosary in hand, ready for Oratio Imperata. Or that one person in your group project who, instead of contributing, just says "I'll pray for us." Anyone who prays can be called a magdarasal, especially if it's their designated role.
usage_notes: This noun form is less common than the verb form with the same spelling. It usually refers to a person with a specific role, like a prayer warrior or leader.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **magdarasal** ay nagtipon sa simbahan para sa isang prayer vigil.","translation":"The **prayer group** gathered at the church for a prayer vigil."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa komunidad bilang isang tapat na **magdarasal**.","translation":"She is known in the community as a faithful **person who prays**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halamang baging na may mga ugat na ginagamit sa paggawa ng inumin at gamot; tumutukoy rin sa inuming pampalamig na gawa mula rito.
original_explanation: The OG root beer. Before all the fancy craft sodas, there was 'sarsaparilya'. It's that classic, old-timey soft drink your lolo or lola probably remembers, often sold in those iconic brown bottles. Tastes like nostalgia and a bit like medicine, but in a good way.
usage_notes: Mostly known as a vintage soft drink brand in the Philippines (e.g., Sarsi).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Noong araw, paboritong inumin ng mga bata ang **sarsaparilya**.","translation":"Back in the day, **sarsaparilla** was a favorite drink of children."},{"sentence":"May kakaibang lasa ang **sarsaparilya** na hahanap-hanapin mo.","translation":"**Sarsaparilla** has a unique taste that you will crave."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang taong may sakit na ketong, o pagkakaroon ng katangian ng sakit na ito. Maaari ring tumukoy bilang pangalan sa taong may karamdaman.
original_explanation: This is what you call a person who has leprosy, or something afflicted by it. But be careful, this word carries a *lot* of historical baggage and can be super offensive, like calling someone a 'leper.' It's often used metaphorically to describe an outcast or someone people avoid. It's more of a word you'd hear in a historical drama than in a polite, modern conversation.
usage_notes: This term is now considered derogatory and stigmatizing. The preferred way to refer to someone with the disease is 'taong may ketong' (person with leprosy) or 'person affected by Hansen's disease.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa mga lumang nobela, madalas ituring na paria ang mga **ketongin**.","translation":"In old novels, people with **leprosy** were often treated as outcasts."},{"sentence":"Iwasan ang paggamit ng salitang '**ketongin**' dahil ito ay nakakasakit ng damdamin.","translation":"Avoid using the word '**leprous**' (or 'leper') because it is hurtful."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang pag-apaw ng likidong kumukulo; o ang biglaang paglaki at paglakas ng apoy.
original_explanation: Ever cooked something and turned your back for two seconds, only to find the pot boiling over and making a mess on the stove? That's sigbo. It's the sudden, violent overflow of a boiling liquid or the flare-up of a fire when you add oil. It's the kitchen's way of saying, 'You're not paying enough attention to me!'
usage_notes: Often used in its conjugated form, 'sumigbo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumigbo** ang niluluto kong gatas nang iwanan ko ito sandali.","translation":"The milk I was cooking **boiled over** when I left it for a moment."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa pagpiprito at baka **sumigbo** ang apoy sa mantika.","translation":"Be careful when frying as the fire might **flare up** in the oil."}]

translation: to be broken into pieces; to be fractured
meaning_filipino: Masira sa pamamagitan ng pagkaputol o pagkapira-piraso, lalo na ang mga bagay na matitigas tulad ng buto o sanga.
original_explanation: Imagine a tree branch in a super typhoon. It doesn't just bend, it snaps. That's 'mabalbal'. It's a more violent, splintering kind of break. Also applies to bones, which is why you listen to your mom when she says "Dahan-dahan, baka mabalbal 'yang buto mo!"
usage_notes: Often used for bones, branches, or similar rigid objects. It implies a snapping or fracturing break, as opposed to a clean cut.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingat sa pag-akyat sa puno, baka **mabalbal** ang sanga.","translation":"Be careful climbing the tree, the branch might **break**."},{"sentence":"Sa lakas ng pagkabagsak, **nabalbal** ang kaniyang braso.","translation":"From the force of the fall, his arm was **fractured**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbatak o pagkaladkad sa isang bagay o tao patungo sa direksyon ng gumagawa ng kilos.
original_explanation: This is what a tow truck does to an illegally parked car. It's what you do to your friend who's too drunk to walk. It's also what your 'toxic' ex does to your emotions—they keep pulling you back in. 'Hila' is the OG 'drag'.
usage_notes: The verb form 'hilahin' (to pull) is very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malakas ang **hila** ng kabayo kaya natumba ang kalesa.","translation":"The horse's **pull** was so strong that the carriage fell."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang **hila** sa kanyang damit.","translation":"He felt a **pull** on his clothes."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang materyal gaya ng lupa, bato, o buhangin na ginagamit bilang pampuno sa isang hukay, mababang lugar, o bilang pundasyon.
etymology: Nagmula sa unlaping 'paN-' (nagiging 'pan-') at sa salitang-ugat na 'tambak' (pile, heap).
original_explanation: The stuff used to fill a hole or level the ground. Think of it as the 'filler' episode in a teleserye—it's there to fill the space before the big dramatic climax. In construction, it's literally the mountain of dirt and rocks used for reclamation projects or to make a vacant lot buildable. It covers up the 'low points'.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng konstruksiyon at paghahanda ng lupa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng sampung trak ng **panambak** para sa itatayong bahay.","translation":"We need ten trucks of **filling material** for the house we're building."},{"sentence":"Ginamit na **panambak** sa reclamation project ang buhangin mula sa dagat.","translation":"Sand from the sea was used as **landfill material** for the reclamation project."}]

translation: to cause to become worse; to be the cause of ill-feeling
meaning_filipino: Maging dahilan ng paglala ng isang sitwasyon o kalagayan; maging sanhi ng sama ng loob.
original_explanation: When you bring up politics at a family reunion, that's the **ikasama** of everyone's mood. It's the 'why did you have to say that?' moment that ruins the vibe. It's the root cause of the 'tampo' (sullenness).
usage_notes: Can refer to the worsening of a situation ('ikasama ng panahon') or the worsening of a person's feelings ('ikasama ng loob').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-ulan ay tiyak na **ikasama** ng trapiko.","translation":"The rain will surely **cause the traffic to worsen**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magsalita ng ganyan, baka iyan pa ang **ikasama** ng loob niya.","translation":"Don't speak like that, it might **be the cause of her ill-feeling**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang marka o disenyo na inilalagay sa isang bagay bilang pagkakakilanlan ng gumawa, nagmamay-ari, o pinagmulan nito.
original_explanation: This is the old-school word for 'brand'. Before 'logos', there was 'tata'. Think of the mark burned onto cattle or the stamp on a sack of rice from a specific mill. It's the OG "trademark". "Anong tata niyan?" is the vintage way of asking "What brand is that?".
usage_notes: Hindi na gaanong karaniwan kumpara sa 'tatak' ngunit naiintindihan pa rin sa maraming rehiyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **tata** ng kalabaw ang bawat sako ng bigas mula sa kanilang bukid.","translation":"Every sack of rice from their farm has a **brand** of a carabao."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi sinasadyang matalsikan o mabuhusan ng likido.
original_explanation: When a jeepney speeds through a puddle and gives you an impromptu, dirty shower, you just got `masabuyan`. It's the universe's way of telling you that you should have worn darker pants. Can also be used for being splashed with insults or negativity.
usage_notes: The focus is on being the recipient of the splash, usually unintentionally.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naiinis ako dahil **nasabuyan** ako ng putik ng dumaang sasakyan.","translation":"I'm annoyed because I was **splashed** with mud by a passing vehicle."},{"sentence":"Iwasan mo ang mga taong iyan, baka **masabuyan** ka lang ng kanilang negatibong pananaw.","translation":"Avoid those people, you might just get **splashed** with their negative views."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang damdamin ng paninibugho o inggit sa tagumpay, pag-aari, o katangian ng ibang tao.
original_explanation: This is the 'Sana all' feeling but with a hint of bitterness. It's what you feel when your officemate gets promoted and you don't, or when you see your ex's happy travel photos with their new partner. It's the green-eyed monster, Pinoy version.
usage_notes: This is a less common, more literary synonym for 'paninibugho' or 'selos'. It carries a deeper, more intense connotation than the everyday 'selos'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kaselangan** ay maaaring sumira sa isang magandang pagkakaibigan.","translation":"**Jealousy** can destroy a good friendship."},{"sentence":"Dama sa kanyang mga mata ang **kaselangan** sa tuwing nakikita niyang magkasama ang dalawa.","translation":"The **envy** was felt in his eyes whenever he saw the two together."}]

translation: to have doubts; to be hesitant
meaning_filipino: Ang makaranas ng pag-aalinlangan, kawalan ng katiyakan, o pangamba tungkol sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're about to click "Place Order" on Shopee for something you don't really need. Or when your friend invites you out but you'd rather stay home and binge Netflix. That hesitation, that "should I or shouldn't I?" internal debate—that's `magkaagam-agam`. It's your inner Marites and your inner voice of reason having a showdown.
usage_notes: The root `agam-agam` means doubt or misgiving. The `magka-` prefix indicates having or experiencing this feeling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay **nagkaagam-agam** na tanggapin ang alok na trabaho sa ibang bansa.","translation":"He/She **had doubts** about accepting the job offer abroad."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magkaagam-agam** sa iyong kakayahan; kaya mo 'yan!","translation":"Don't **be hesitant** about your abilities; you can do it!"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kulay na hindi matingkad, kupas, o maputla.
original_explanation: Yung kulay ng favorite black shirt mo after 100 washes. Or yung kulay ng feelings niya para sa'yo, nag-fade na. It's the color equivalent of 'meh'. Hindi na vibrant, parang pag-asa mo sa 13th month pay pagdating ng March.
usage_notes: Often used to describe colors of fabric, skin tone (mapusyaw), or even the brightness of light.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **pusyaw** na ang kulay ng kanyang lumang maong.","translation":"The color of his old jeans has become **faded**."},{"sentence":"Mapapansin mo ang **pusyaw** na kulay ng kanyang mga labi dahil sa takot.","translation":"You can notice the **pale** color of his lips due to fear."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang empleyado sa isang tindahan, bangko, o establisyimento na responsable sa pagtanggap ng bayad at pagbibigay ng sukli.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'cajera' (babae) / 'cajero' (lalaki), na galing sa 'caja' (kahon/cash register).
original_explanation: The person you interact with last at the grocery store. They're the master of the barcode scanner beep, the one who asks "May BEEP card po ba?" or "Points po, ma'am/sir?". Pro tip: be nice to the **kahera**, they can make your day or break it by giving you all barya as sukli.
usage_notes: Ang 'kahera' ay para sa babae, at 'kahero' para sa lalaki. Mas karaniwang naririnig ang 'kahera' dahil tradisyonal na babae ang gumaganap sa papel na ito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahaba ang pila sa **kahera** dahil maraming namimili.","translation":"The line at the **cashier** is long because there are many shoppers."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon o pagdating ng isang panauhin o bisita.
original_explanation: That moment of panic when your mom yells 'Ayusin mo 'yang sala, may darating!' because you're about to 'magkabisita'. It's the act of having guests, which triggers a nationwide cleaning frenzy known as the 'pag may bisita lang naglilinis' phenomenon.
usage_notes: A very common expression. The future tense is 'magkakabisita', present is 'nagkakabisita', past is 'nagkabisita'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bukas kami **magkabisita** mula sa probinsya.","translation":"Tomorrow we will **have a visitor** from the province."},{"sentence":"Naglinis ako ng bahay dahil **nagkabisita** kami kahapon.","translation":"I cleaned the house because we **had a visitor** yesterday."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagkitil ng buhay ng isang nilalang, o ang pagpatay sa pinagmumulan ng kuryente, apoy, o ilaw ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'hugot' line: "Papatayin mo ba ako sa selos?" (Are you going to kill me with jealousy?). Also, what your mom shouts when you leave the room: "Papatayin mo 'yang ilaw!" (Turn off that light!). It's a word of extremes.
usage_notes: Future tense of 'patayin'. It has two common meanings: to extinguish life or to extinguish a light/appliance. Context is key to understanding the intent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **papatayin** sa susunod na episode ng paborito mong serye?","translation":"Who **will be killed** in the next episode of your favorite series?"},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutan, **papatayin** ang lahat ng ilaw bago umalis ng bahay.","translation":"Don't forget, **turn off** all the lights before leaving the house."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggalaw ng mga labi at pisngi upang ipahayag ang kagalakan, kasiyahan, o pagbati.
original_explanation: The universal cure for a bad day, and the best way to disarm a grumpy security guard. It's what you do when you see the food delivery guy arriving. It's cheaper than therapy and can sometimes get you a discount at the *palengke*. The purest form of human connection.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **ngumiti** kahit maraming problema.","translation":"Don't forget to **smile** even if there are many problems."},{"sentence":"**Ngumiti** siya sa akin kanina sa jeep, crush niya kaya ako?","translation":"She **smiled** at me in the jeep earlier, I wonder if she has a crush on me?"}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang bagay na nagtataguyod ng mabuting kalusugan at kapakanan, pisikal man o moral; malusog, malinis, at mabuti para sa isip at katawan.
original_explanation: Ito yung content na safe for the whole family, walang halong malisya o toxic vibes. Parang pamilya na nagpi-picnic sa park, o love team na ang holding hands ay aabutin ng 10 episodes. Ito yung kabaligtaran ng "Marites mode." Yung tipong mapapa-comment ka ng, "Sana all!" nang walang bahid ng inggit.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa Taglish upang ilarawan ang mga tao, relasyon, o media content na positibo at malinis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng pelikula, very **wholesome** at pampamilya.","translation":"The movie was great, very **wholesome** and family-friendly."},{"sentence":"Gusto ko yung mga **wholesome** na content sa social media, nakakagaan ng loob.","translation":"I like **wholesome** content on social media, it's heartwarming."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uugali ng pagtingin sa sarili bilang nakatataas o mas mahusay kaysa sa iba; kahambugan.
etymology: Mula sa `pag-` + `magmataas` (maging arogante), na mula sa `mataas`.
original_explanation: The feeling of being "the main character" in a bad way. It's when you think you're better than everyone else, and you make sure they know it. Parang kontrabida sa teleserye na laging nakataas ang kilay at minamaliit ang bida. Pride before the fall, ika nga.
usage_notes: Isang mabigat na negatibong termino para sa isang depekto sa pagkatao. Kasingkahulugan ng `kapalaluan` o `kahambugan`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagmamataas** ang naging dahilan ng kanyang pagbagsak.","translation":"His **arrogance** was the cause of his downfall."},{"sentence":"Walang lugar ang **pagmamataas** sa isang tunay na pinuno.","translation":"There is no place for **haughtiness** in a true leader."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kalagayan ng isang tao, karaniwan ay matanda na, na nagiging makakalimutin o nagpapakita ng paghina ng pag-iisip.
etymology: Mula sa `pagka-` (kalagayan ng pagiging) + `ulianin` (taong nagiging makakalimutin dahil sa edad), mula sa ugat na `ulian`.
original_explanation: This is your lolo or lola asking "Sino ka?" for the third time this morning.
