It's that stage where memories start to feel like a phone with only 1GB of RAM left – always lagging and randomly closing apps (memories). It's more than just being 'makakalimutin'; it’s the medical state of senility.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang mga matatanda. Ito ay maaaring ituring na isang sensitibong salita, kaya't dapat gamitin nang may pag-iingat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagiging **pagkaulianin** na si Lolo kaya kailangan niya ng masusing pag-aalaga.","translation":"Grandfather is becoming **senile**, so he needs careful attention."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkaulianin** ay isang hamon para sa pamilya ng maysakit.","translation":"**Senility** is a challenge for the family of the afflicted."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salita na may kapareho o halos kaparehong kahulugan sa isa pang salita.
original_explanation: That thing your Filipino teacher made you memorize in high school. It's basically having multiple ways to say the same thing. 'Maganda' and 'marikit' are synonyms. It's like having different outfits for the same 'you' – they all mean 'gorgeous'. The native Tagalog term is 'kasingkahulugan'.
usage_notes: The native Tagalog equivalent is 'kasingkahulugan'. 'Sinonimo' is used more in academic or formal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **sinonimo** ng salitang 'masaya' ay 'maligaya'.","translation":"The **synonym** of the word 'masaya' (happy) is 'maligaya' (joyful)."},{"sentence":"Magbigay ng tatlong **sinonimo** para sa salitang 'malaki'.","translation":"Give three **synonyms** for the word 'malaki' (big)."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangatnig na nag-uugnay ng sanhi at bunga; ginagamit upang ipakita ang resulta o konklusyon ng isang naunang pahayag.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "chismis" connector. "Umuulan kasi, KAYA pala basang-basa siya pagdating." (It was raining, THAT'S WHY he was soaking wet when he arrived.) It's the word that links the 'why' to the 'what happened'. The 'therefore' in the grand equation of life's daily dramas.
usage_notes: It introduces a result or consequence. Often starts a clause.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-aral siya nang mabuti, **kaya** nakapasa siya sa pagsusulit.","translation":"He studied well, **so** he passed the exam."},{"sentence":"Late ka na naman gumising, **kaya** nahuli ka sa klase.","translation":"You woke up late again, **that's why** you were late for class."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagdiriwang o pagtitipon upang gunitain ang isang mahalagang okasyon o kaganapan.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung dahilan kung bakit may handa. Birthday, Pasko, graduation, o kahit 'yung simpleng 'TGIF!'—lahat 'yan pwedeng maging selebrasyon. Basically, any excuse to eat, drink, and be merry with friends and family. Sa Pilipinas, ang selebrasyon ay hindi kumpleto kung walang spaghetti, lumpia, at videoke.
usage_notes: Ang katutubong katumbas ay 'pagdiriwang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malaking **selebrasyon** ang inihanda para sa kanyang kaarawan.","translation":"A big **celebration** was prepared for her birthday."},{"sentence":"Ang Pasko ang pinakamahabang **selebrasyon** sa Pilipinas.","translation":"Christmas is the longest **celebration** in the Philippines."}]

meaning_filipino: Pahiran o lagyan ng pintura ang isang ibabaw, karaniwan para sa proteksyon, dekorasyon, o pagbabago ng kulay.
original_explanation: More functional than 'ipinta'. This is the actual labor. This is what your dad asks you to do over summer break. '**Ipintura** mo na 'yang bakod, puro ka selpon!' It's about applying the physical paint, not necessarily creating a masterpiece.
usage_notes: Refers to the act of coating a surface with paint, like a wall or a fence. It's more about utility than artistry.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **ipintura** ulit ang mga pader dahil naninilaw na.","translation":"We need to **paint** the walls again because they are already turning yellow."},{"sentence":"Magkano ang singil mo para **ipintura** ang buong bahay?","translation":"How much do you charge to **paint** the whole house?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na pinagsamang 'bading' at 'bodyguard,' tumutukoy sa isang bading na nagsisilbing tagapagtanggol o kasama ng isang tao.
original_explanation: Your gay best friend who's always ready to defend your honor, check out your potential dates, and tell you 'hindi siya kawalan, girl!' They're your protector, your confidante, and your personal stylist all rolled into one. They provide security, but with more sass and better fashion advice than a regular bodyguard.
usage_notes: A playful and affectionate term within LGBTQ+ circles and their friends.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kasama ko ang aking mga **badigard** kaya 'wag kang ano dyan.","translation":"I'm with my **bodyguards** (gay friends), so don't you start anything."},{"sentence":"Si Paolo ang official **badigard** ni Sarah sa lahat ng party.","translation":"Paolo is Sarah's official **badigard** at all parties."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malakas na gamot na pampamanhid at pampakalma, karaniwang ginagamit sa medisina para sa matinding sakit, na nagmula sa opyo.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "morfina", na galing sa Aleman na "Morphin", ipinangalan kay Morpheus, ang Griyegong diyos ng mga panaginip.
original_explanation: Ito yung gamot na mas matindi pa sa breakup para makalimutan mo ang sakit. Pang-ospital level na pampamanhid, hindi pang-hugot lang. Seryosong bagay 'to, hindi paracetamol.
usage_notes: Isang terminong medikal na may mahigpit na regulasyon sa paggamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binigyan ng doktor ng **morpina** ang pasyente upang maibsan ang matinding sakit pagkatapos ng operasyon.","translation":"The doctor gave the patient **morphine** to alleviate the intense pain after the surgery."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malakas at biglaang pagpalo o paghampas, karaniwang gamit ang isang mabigat na bagay.
original_explanation: If 'hambalin' is a repeated whipping, 'hambalos' is that one solid, heavy hit. Imagine swatting a giant ipis with a tsinelas so hard it echoes through the house. That's one 'hambalos'. It's a powerful, resounding strike. 'Isang **hambalos** lang ng dos por dos, tulog ang kalaban.'
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun for the strike itself, or as a verb root (e.g., hambalusin - to strike forcefully).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang malakas na **hambalos** sa pinto.","translation":"I heard the forceful **whack** on the door."},{"sentence":"Tinamaan siya ng **hambalos** ng kahoy sa likod.","translation":"He was hit by a **strike** from a piece of wood on his back."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtama sa isang bagay gamit ang paa na magaganap sa hinaharap.
etymology: From "sipa" (kick) with the future tense aspect, formed by reduplicating the first syllable of the root word.
original_explanation: Future tense of 'kick.' This is what a football player will do to the ball, what a taekwondo athlete will do to their opponent, or what you threaten to do to your slow-ass laptop. 'Isa pa, sisipain ko na 'to!'
usage_notes: 'Susipa' is an alternative but less common future tense form. 'Tadyak' is a stronger, more forceful kick.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sisipa** siya ng bola mamaya sa laro ng football.","translation":"He **will kick** the ball later at the football game."},{"sentence":"Kapag hindi ka tumigil, **sisipa** ako.","translation":"If you don't stop, I **will kick**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalantad o pag-aalis ng takip sa isang bagay na lihim, nakatago, o hindi pa alam ng nakararami.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung ginagawa mo kapag may 'tea' ka at kailangan mo nang i-spill. 'Yung moment na may hawak kang resibo at ready ka nang mag-post ng 'expose thread' tungkol sa ex mong cheater. The ultimate 'the truth will set you free' moment.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng mga sikreto, katiwalian, o mga nakatagong katotohanan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **ibunyag** ang katotohanan sa kabila ng mga panganib.","translation":"He decided **to reveal** the truth despite the dangers."},{"sentence":"Panahon na para **ibunyag** ang mga anomalya sa gobyerno.","translation":"It is time **to expose** the anomalies in the government."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghinto o pagtigil sa isang gawain, kilos, o kalagayan, na kadalasan ay may konotasyon ng pag-aatubili o pagiging pansamantala.
original_explanation: That feeling when you want to give up on your thesis, but then you remember the tuition fee. It's the pause button on life's drama, a temporary stop to overthinking. It’s like your brain is buffering... but for your will to continue.
usage_notes: A formal and somewhat archaic word. 'Paghinto' or 'pagtigil' are the common modern equivalents. Often used in the negative 'walang-pagtutugot' to mean 'unceasing'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Walang **pagtutugot** ang kanyang pag-iyak nang malaman ang balita.","translation":"Her crying was **unceasing** upon learning the news."},{"sentence":"Dapat may **pagtutugot** ang paggastos nang walang kabuluhan.","translation":"There should be a **stop** to meaningless spending."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang marka sa balat na taglay na ng isang tao mula pa sa kaniyang kapanganakan.
original_explanation: That special mark on your skin you've had since birth. Sometimes it's cute, sometimes it's in a weird spot. In old Filipino superstitions, they say what your mom was craving while pregnant could cause one. Craved chocolate? You might get a brown balat.
usage_notes: The pronunciation stress shifts to the last syllable (/ba-LAT/) to distinguish it from skin (/BA-lat/).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroon siyang **balat** sa kanyang kanang pisngi.","translation":"She has a **mole** on her right cheek."},{"sentence":"Ang **balat** sa likod niya ay hugis puso daw.","translation":"They say the **birthmark** on her back is heart-shaped."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggamit ng isang likido upang linisin ang bibig o lalamunan; pagmumog.
etymology: Mula sa "mumog". Ang hulaping -an ay ginagawa itong pandiwa na nagsasaad ng kilos.
original_explanation: This is the action version of `mumog`. It's what you do with mouthwash, or with salt and warm water when you have a sore throat as per your lola's instructions. The verb form of swishing stuff in your mouth. 'Magmumog ka na!' is the battle cry of parents everywhere before bedtime.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa anyong pautos na "Mumugan mo" (Gargle with it) o "Magmumog ka" (You gargle).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Mumugan** mo ng maligamgam na tubig na may asin ang iyong lalamunan.","translation":"**Gargle** your throat with warm water with salt."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **mumugan** ang gamot na ito nang isang minuto.","translation":"You need to **gargle** with this medicine for one minute."}]

translation: is taking a bath, is bathing
meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang ginagawang kilos ng paglilinis ng katawan gamit ang tubig.
original_explanation: Ito yung isasagot mo kapag may tumatawag sa'yo pero 'di mo masagot ang phone. "Sorry, naliligo ako!" The perfect excuse, whether it's true or not. It's the present continuous tense of getting fresh.
usage_notes: Present progressive form of 'maligo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maingay, **naliligo** ang sanggol.","translation":"Don't be noisy, the baby **is taking a bath**."},{"sentence":"Bakit ang tagal mo sa banyo? Isang oras ka nang **naliligo**!","translation":"Why are you taking so long in the bathroom? You've **been bathing** for an hour!"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa, o may katangian ng, isang buong bansa o nasyon.
original_explanation: The official adjective for anything 'pang-buong Pilipinas'. National ID, National Hero, National Bookstore... basically, if it's a big deal and involves the whole country, you slap this word in front. It's the level-up from 'local' or 'regional'. It's when your barangay's chismis goes viral nationwide.
usage_notes: Used to describe things pertaining to the nation. 'Pambansa' is the more common and native-sounding equivalent (e.g., 'pambansang wika' for national language).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Sampaguita ay ang ating **nasyonal** na bulaklak.","translation":"The Sampaguita is our **national** flower."},{"sentence":"Ipinagdiriwang ngayon ang Araw ng **Nasyonal** na Watawat.","translation":"Today, we celebrate **National** Flag Day."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kulisap na karaniwang may mabalahibong katawan, kahawig ng paruparo, at naaakit sa liwanag, lalo na sa gabi.
original_explanation: That little insect that's hopelessly attracted to any light source, just like you to your crush's IG stories. They're the uninvited guests at your late-night study session, crashing into your lamp. Sila 'yung patay na patay sa ilaw.
usage_notes: Famously referenced in a fable told by Jose Rizal's mother, about a young moth that flew too close to a flame.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **gamugamo** ang bumbilya sa labas ng bahay tuwing gabi.","translation":"The lightbulb outside the house is full of **moths** every night."},{"sentence":"Ikinuwento ng ina ang pabula ng **gamugamo** at lampara sa kanyang anak.","translation":"The mother told the fable of the **moth** and the lamp to her child."}]

translation: to take out; to bring out; to release
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkuha ng isang bagay mula sa loob at paglipat nito sa labas; ang pag-publish o pagpapalabas ng isang produkto o likha.
original_explanation: The universal command when you need something. 'Maglabas ka ng pera' (Bring out some money). 'Maglabas ka ng pagkain' (Take out the food). For artists and companies, it means to release something new, like a new album, movie, or the latest iPhone model. It's also what your boss tells you when they want to see 'results'.
usage_notes: A very versatile verb. The specific meaning depends heavily on the object of the verb. 'Maglabas ng sama ng loob' means 'to vent out frustrations'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **maglabas** ka ng dalawang baso mula sa aparador.","translation":"Please, **take out** two glasses from the cupboard."},{"sentence":"**Maglalabas** ng bagong album ang paborito kong banda sa susunod na buwan.","translation":"My favorite band will **release** a new album next month."}]

translation: to be called; to be summoned
meaning_filipino: Maging paksa ng isang pagtawag; ang pagbanggit sa pangalan ng isang tao upang makuha ang atensyon o hilingin ang kanyang presensya.
original_explanation: The feeling of dread when you're chilling at your desk and you hear your boss's voice from their office. You're about to matawag. It's the passive form—you're not the one calling, you're the one *being called*.
usage_notes: This is the object-focus counterpart to 'tumawag' (to call). The subject of 'matawag' is the person or thing being called.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayokong **matawag** sa klase dahil hindi ako nag-aral.","translation":"I don't want to **be called** in class because I didn't study."},{"sentence":"Maaari ba akong **matawag** na 'Dok' kahit hindi pa ako doktor?","translation":"Can I **be called** 'Doc' even if I'm not yet a doctor?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bahagi o piraso na bumubuo sa isang mas malaking kabuuan; isang seksyon.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung part ng TV show na paborito mo, like 'yung "Juan for All, All for Juan" sa Eat Bulaga. O 'yung segmento ng balita tungkol sa showbiz chismis. It's just a fancy word for "part" or "section," whether sa work, sa show, o kahit sa orange na hinihiwa-hiwa mo.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa media, negosyo, matematika, at pangkalahatang usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang susunod na **segmento** ng programa ay tungkol sa kalusugan.","translation":"The next **segment** of the program is about health."}]

translation: to write to each other; to correspond
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng dalawa o higit pang tao na nagpapalitan ng liham o sulat.
original_explanation: The pre-internet version of a group chat or sliding into DMs. This is what pen pals did. It implies a reciprocal exchange of messages, like you and your work bestie messaging each other about your boss while in the same meeting. Social, not solo.
usage_notes: This is a social/reciprocal verb, indicating that the action of writing is done between two or more people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Noong wala pang internet, mahilig **magsulatan** ang mga magkasintahan.","translation":"When there was no internet yet, lovers were fond of **writing to each other**."},{"sentence":"Nagkasundo kaming **magsulatan** kahit na magkalayo na kami ng bansa.","translation":"We agreed **to correspond** even though we are in different countries."}]

translation: to let something rot, to cause to decay
meaning_filipino: Hayaan o maging sanhi na masira, mabulok, o dumaan sa proseso ng dekomposisyon ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay organikong materyal.
etymology: From 'mag-' (verb prefix) + 'pa-' (causative prefix) + 'bulok' (rotten). Literally 'to cause to become rotten'.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you buy a bunch of fresh veggies for your 'healthy lifestyle' goals and then forget about them in the fridge for two weeks. It can also be used figuratively, like when you let your skills get rusty or let a project die. 'Huwag mong pabulukin ang talento mo.' (Don't let your talent rot.)
usage_notes: Can be used literally for food/organic matter or figuratively for skills, plans, or systems.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **magpabulok** ang mga prutas sa mesa; kainin mo na.","translation":"Don't **let the fruits on the table rot**; eat them already."},{"sentence":"Mas mabuting gamitin ang pera kaysa **magpabulok** lang nito sa bangko nang walang interes.","translation":"It's better to use the money than to just **let it rot** in the bank without interest."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang lugar na may suplay ng kuryente o isang bagay na dinadaluyan ng kuryente.
original_explanation: The most beautiful phrase you can hear after a 12-hour brownout during a typhoon: 'Huy, **may-kuryente** na!' It means you can finally charge your phone, turn on the fan, and binge-watch Netflix again. It's the opposite of being 'offline'. Can also mean 'live wire,' so don't touch that thing your tito is 'fixing'.
usage_notes: Very common in everyday conversation, especially when talking about power outages.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa kawad na iyan, baka **may-kuryente**.","translation":"Be careful with that wire, it might be **live**."},{"sentence":"Salamat sa Diyos at **may-kuryente** na ulit tayo!","translation":"Thank God we **have electricity** again!"}]

meaning_filipino: Maliliit at pinong piraso ng kahoy na nalilikha mula sa paglalagari, pagbubutas, o pagpapakinis ng kahoy.
original_explanation: The glitter of a carpentry shop. It's the stuff that gets everywhere when your neighbor decides to do some DIY home improvement on a Sunday morning. Also used to stuff things, from pet beds to old-school boxing gloves.
usage_notes: This noun form is distinct from the verb 'kusutin' (to crumple/rub), which has a different stress pattern /ku-SUTIN/.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Punuin mo ng **kusot** ang sahig ng kulungan ng manok.","translation":"Fill the floor of the chicken coop with **sawdust**."},{"sentence":"Nagkalat ang **kusot** sa buong pagawaan ng muwebles.","translation":"The **wood shavings** were scattered all over the furniture workshop."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang itinalagang bahagi ng kalsada na may marka kung saan ligtas na makakatawid ang mga taong naglalakad.
original_explanation: Those white stripes on the road that are *supposed* to be a safe zone for crossing. In the Philippines, using a pedestrian lane is often an extreme sport. You make eye contact with the driver, say a little prayer, and hope for the best. It's the 'tawiran' for the conyo crowd.
usage_notes: Widely used and understood. The Tagalog word 'tawiran' is also very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumawid ka lang sa **pedestrian lane** para iwas-disgrasya.","translation":"Only cross at the **pedestrian lane** to avoid accidents."},{"sentence":"Pininturahan nila ulit ang mga **pedestrian lane** sa EDSA.","translation":"They repainted the **pedestrian lanes** on EDSA."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng matinding damdamin, sigasig, o init; nag-aapoy sa kasidhian.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `ma-` (nagpapahiwatig ng katangian) at salitang-ugat na `alab` (sidhi, init ng damdamin).
original_explanation: This is your energy level when your k-pop idols have a comeback. It's the "gigil" you feel for your passion project. Parang 'yung pag-ibig na hindi lang basta 'like', kundi 'fire emoji' level. All-out, walang preno, 110% effort.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang mga damdamin tulad ng pag-ibig, pagkamakabayan, o pagnanasa. Nagpapahiwatig ito ng nag-aapoy na intensidad.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagbigay siya ng isang **maalab** na talumpati tungkol sa pagbabago.","translation":"He gave a **fervent** speech about change."},{"sentence":"Ipinakita nila ang kanilang **maalab** na pagmamahal sa bayan.","translation":"They showed their **ardent** love for the country."}]

meaning_filipino: Isasagawa ang kilos ng pag-aalok ng produkto o serbisyo kapalit ng pera sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: This is the future tense of 'hustle.' It's your friend who's 'planning to sell' pre-loved clothes online, the tita who will sell homemade ube cheese pandesal next week, or the announcement that SM will have a 3-day sale. The anthem of every aspiring online seller.
usage_notes: This is the future tense form of 'magbenta'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magbebenta** raw si Aling Nena ng halo-halo simula bukas.","translation":"Aling Nena **will sell** halo-halo starting tomorrow, they say."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **magbebenta** ng tiket para sa konsiyerto?","translation":"Who **will be selling** the tickets for the concert?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto o proseso ng pangongolekta ng pera, bayad, o utang. Ito rin ay tumutukoy sa kabuuang halaga ng perang nakolekta.
original_explanation: Ito yung total earnings for the day. Para sa jeepney driver, ito yung kita sa pamamasada. Para sa tindera, ito yung benta. Para sa BPO agent, ito yung... ay wala pala, sahod 'yon. Basically, the cash you've collected. "Magkano kobransa natin ngayon, boss?"
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng negosyo, transportasyon, at pangongolekta ng bayad.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang **kobransa** ng mga sinehan noong Pasko.","translation":"The cinemas had a huge **collection** (box office earnings) last Christmas."},{"sentence":"Ibigay mo na sa dispatcher ang **kobransa** mo sa buong araw.","translation":"Give your day's **earnings** to the dispatcher."}]

translation: to collide with each other; to bump into each other
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtama o pagbangga ng dalawa o higit pang bagay, tao, o sasakyan sa isa't isa.
etymology: From 'magka-' (prefix indicating mutuality or accident) + 'bunggo' (bump, collide).
original_explanation: The classic scene in a Filipino rom-com where the leads meet. They're both rushing, they 'magkabunggo', papers fly everywhere, and boom—love at first sight. In real life, it's what happens in Divisoria when you're not looking, and instead of love, you just get a 'Sorry po!' and a lost slipper.
usage_notes: Implies a mutual or reciprocal action. If one party is stationary, 'makabunggo' (to accidentally bump into) or 'ibunggo' (to cause to bump into) is more appropriate.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagmamadali sila kaya sila **nagkabunggo** sa pasilyo.","translation":"They were in a hurry, that's why they **bumped into each other** in the hallway."},{"sentence":"Ingat sa pagmamaneho para hindi **magkabunggo**.","translation":"Drive carefully so you don't **collide with each other**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng metal na napakabihira, mahalaga, at may kulay pilak-puti, mas matibay at mas mabigat kaysa ginto.
original_explanation: The final boss of precious metals. If gold is for the rich, Platino (platinum) is for the ultra-rich. It's what your credit card becomes when you've reached peak tito/tita of Manila status. It's rarer, denser, and more low-key expensive than gold.
usage_notes: This is the specific term for the metal platinum. Not to be confused with 'platina' (stage). Often spelled with a capital 'P' when referring to the chemical element, but lowercase is fine for general use.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang singsing na iyon ay gawa sa **Platino** at may dyamante.","translation":"That ring is made of **Platinum** and has a diamond."},{"sentence":"Mas mahal pa sa ginto ang **Platino**.","translation":"**Platinum** is more expensive than gold."}]

meaning_filipino: Mag-away o magbangayan nang paulit-ulit at madalas tungkol sa maliliit o hindi gaanong mahalagang bagay.
original_explanation: This is 'magtalo' level 2.0. It’s the rapid-fire, back-and-forth arguing you see between siblings fighting over the TV remote or a couple arguing in IKEA about which shelf to buy. It’s less about winning a debate and more about getting the last petty word in.
usage_notes: Implies a more repetitive and often more childish or petty argument than 'magtalo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumigil na kayo sa **pagtaltalan** dahil sa isang pirasong tsokolate.","translation":"Stop **bickering** over a single piece of chocolate."},{"sentence":"Lagi na lang silang **nagtataltalan** tuwing magkasama sa kotse.","translation":"They always **squabble** whenever they are together in the car."}]

translation: can be endured; can be put up with
meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, gawain, o sitwasyon na kayang batahin o dalhin kahit na ito ay mahirap, hindi komportable, o hindi gusto.
original_explanation: Yung trabaho mong hindi mo passion pero 'pwede na' for the bills. Yung ulam na hindi masarap pero okay lang para hindi magutom. It’s the 'it is what it is' of situations—not ideal, but survivable. The feeling you have about your slow internet connection because you have no other choice.
usage_notes: Refers to a situation or thing that one can tolerate or endure, often out of necessity. It's in the future tense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa ngayon, ang maliit na sahod ay **mapagtitiisan** pa niya para sa pamilya.","translation":"For now, the small salary **can be endured** by him for his family."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang anumang dungis, dumi, o kasalanan; lubos na malinis at dalisay.
original_explanation: This is that level of clean that's almost mythical. Like your lola's white sofa that no one is allowed to sit on, or the state of your room for the 5 minutes after a major general cleaning before chaos reigns again. It's often used in a religious context (Immaculate Conception), but can also describe a perfectly white shirt or a flawless reputation. "Wow, **imakulada** ang pagkakaplantsa ng uniform mo!"
usage_notes: Strongly associated with the Catholic doctrine of the Immaculate Conception ('Imakulada Konsepsyon').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nanatiling **imakulada** ang kanyang puting bestida sa kabila ng maputik na daan.","translation":"Her white dress remained **immaculate** despite the muddy road."},{"sentence":"Ang debosyon sa **Imakulada** Konsepsyon ay malalim sa kulturang Pilipino.","translation":"The devotion to the **Immaculate** Conception is deep in Filipino culture."}]

translation: to be grazed; to be scratched lightly
meaning_filipino: Ang magtamo ng bahagyang gasgas o galos sa balat dahil sa pagdikit o pagdaan ng isang magaspang na bagay.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `ma-` + salitang ugat na `halas` (graze, scratch) + hulaping `-an`.
original_explanation: When something rough just barely scrapes you. It's that "daplis lang" feeling. Like when you're squeezing through a crowded MRT and your arm brushes against someone's zipper. It's not a full-on wound, just a "Wala 'to, galos lang" moment.
usage_notes: Ang 'halas' ay hindi gaanong karaniwan kumpara sa 'gasgas' o 'galos'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa pader na iyan at baka ka **mahalasan**.","translation":"Be careful with that wall, you might **get grazed**."},{"sentence":"**Nahalasan** ang braso niya sa matulis na sanga.","translation":"His arm **was scratched lightly** by the sharp branch."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang dalubhasa o eksperto sa larangan ng ekonomiks.
original_explanation: This is the person on the news who explains why the price of gas is so high using a lot of charts and words you don't understand, like "fiscal policy" and "GDP growth." They are the professional overthinkers of the country's finances. When they speak, your parents either get very worried or slightly hopeful about the future.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayon sa mga **ekonomista**, posibleng tumaas ang inflation rate sa susunod na buwan.","translation":"According to **economists**, the inflation rate might increase next month."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang patuloy o paulit-ulit na pagkilos upang hindi makaharap, makasalamuha, o tamaan ng isang bagay o tao.
original_explanation: The act of dodging something or someone. This is you when you see your chismosang kapitbahay, or when your ex walks into the same coffee shop. It's also what you do to avoid spoilers for the latest K-drama episode. In short, the art of the "seen-zone" but in real life. #iwaspusoy
usage_notes: Progressive form of *umiwas*. Describes the ongoing action of avoiding.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matagal na siyang **umiiwas** sa mga pagkaing matatamis.","translation":"He has been **avoiding** sweet foods for a long time."},{"sentence":"Bakit ka ba **umiiwas** sa akin? May nagawa ba akong masama?","translation":"Why are you **avoiding** me? Did I do something wrong?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging naresolba o pagkakaroon ng solusyon sa isang problema o suliranin.
original_explanation: That 'Aha!' moment when the Wi-Fi finally connects, or when you finally figure out the answer to a math problem you've been staring at for an hour. It's the sweet relief of a problem being solved, the end of the 'sakit sa ulo.'
usage_notes: Refers to the state after a problem has been resolved.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mabilis na **pagkalutas** ng kaso ay ikinatuwa ng lahat.","translation":"The swift **resolution** of the case pleased everyone."}]

translation: to feel envious; to be jealous
meaning_filipino: Makaramdam ng inggit o pananaghili sa tagumpay, pag-aari, o katangian ng iba.
original_explanation: That feeling you get when you see your friend's travel photos on IG while you're stuck in traffic on EDSA. "Sana all" is the battle cry of the 'naiinggit'. It’s wanting what they have, whether it’s a new gadget, a jowa, or clear skin.
usage_notes: Often used in the form `naiinggit` (present tense) or as an infinitive.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi mo kailangang **mainggit** sa iba, mayroon ka ring sariling galing.","translation":"You don't need **to be envious** of others, you have your own strengths too."},{"sentence":"Naiinggit ako sa mga taong kayang kumain nang marami pero hindi tumataba.","translation":"I am envious of people who can eat a lot but don't get fat."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang kagamitan na ginagamit sa pagsusulat, tulad ng lapis, bolpen, o panulat.
original_explanation: Anything you can use to write, from your trusty G-Tec pen for taking notes, to the Mongol pencil you used in elementary school, or even the marker for your whiteboard brainstorming session. If you can make letters with it, it's a `pansulat`. It's the weapon of choice for students, writers, and anyone who's ever had to sign a contract or a birthday card.
usage_notes: A general term. More specific terms like "bolpen" (ballpen) or "lapis" (pencil) are more common in everyday speech. "Panulat" is a common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pahiram naman ako ng **pansulat**, naiwan ko ang aking bolpen.","translation":"Can I borrow a **writing instrument**, I left my ballpen."},{"sentence":"Kumuha ka ng papel at **pansulat** para sa ating pagsusulit.","translation":"Get a piece of paper and **something to write with** for our test."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkakaroon ng mataas na temperatura; ang enerhiyang nagpapataas ng temperatura ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: That feeling when you see your ex with their new partner. Charot! It's literally heat, like the summer heat that makes you want to live inside a refrigerator, or the warmth from a good cup of kapeng barako. Also, "init ng ulo" is when you're angry or stressed out.
usage_notes: "Init ng ulo" is a common idiom for being angry or short-tempered.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Grabe ang **init** ng panahon ngayon.","translation":"The **heat** today is intense."},{"sentence":"Nararamdaman ko ang **init** ng yakap mo.","translation":"I can feel the **warmth** of your hug."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang natural na ahente na nagpapasigla sa paningin at ginagawang nakikita ang mga bagay; kaliwanagan o ilaw.
original_explanation: The ultimate frenemy of mga nagpupuyat. It's what you see when you finally have a brilliant idea ('Eureka!'). It's also what Meralco cuts when you forget to pay your bill. Metaphorically, it's the 'truth' you find out about your chismosa officemate, or the 'hope' you feel when it's finally payday. Ang liwanag sa dulo ng tunnel ay minsan sweldo, minsan tren.
usage_notes: Maaari ring tumukoy sa kaliwanagan ng pag-iisip o pag-unawa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Biglang nawalan ng kuryente kaya nawala ang lahat ng **liwanag** sa bahay.","translation":"The power suddenly went out, so all the **light** in the house was gone."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga salita ay nagbigay **liwanag** sa aking mga agam-agam.","translation":"His words brought **light** to my doubts."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga maliliit na pabilog na bagay na ikinakabit sa damit bilang pangkabit o palamuti.
original_explanation: Buttons. Yes, just buttons. But not just any buttons. This is the word your lola or your neighborhood mananahi (seamstress) would use. It feels more classic than the English word. If you lose one, 'Nawala ang **bitones** ng polo ko!' and it sounds 10x more urgent.
usage_notes: Used interchangeably with the English word 'button,' but 'bitones' has a more traditional or classic feel. The singular form is 'bitones' as well, though some may say 'isang bitones'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong tahiin muli ang natanggal na **bitones** ng aking amerikana.","translation":"I need to sew back the detached **button** of my coat."},{"sentence":"Gawa sa ginto ang mga **bitones** ng kanyang barong.","translation":"The **buttons** of his barong are made of gold."}]

translation: a type of medicinal climbing vine (Tinospora rumphii)
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng gumagapang na halamang gamot (Tinospora rumphii) na kilala sa mapait na lasa at sa kakayahang magpagaling ng iba't ibang sakit.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung halaman na pinapainom sa'yo ni lola 'pag may sakit ka. Sobrang pait, parang ex mo, pero effective daw. Its name literally means 'can give life,' which tells you how much our ancestors trusted this plant.
usage_notes: The name of the plant itself. It is well-known in Filipino traditional medicine for its bitter properties.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglaga si Lola ng tangkay ng **makabuhay** para sa kanyang rayuma.","translation":"Grandma boiled stems of the **makabuhay** vine for her rheumatism."},{"sentence":"Mapait ang katas ng **makabuhay** pero mabisa raw itong panlaban sa lagnat.","translation":"The extract of **makabuhay** is bitter but they say it's effective against fever."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang matinding pagpuna, paghamak, o pag-alipusta sa isang tao o bagay sa pamamagitan ng masasakit na salita.
etymology: From `pang-` + reduplication of the first syllable `u-` + `upasala` (scorn, vituperation).
original_explanation: This isn't just criticism; this is full-blown 'cancellation' mode with words. It's what happens in a toxic comment section or a heated 'bardagulan' on Twitter. It's the act of verbally tearing someone down, insulting their very soul until they feel worthless. It's a verbal beatdown.
usage_notes: A very strong, formal, and literary word. Not used in casual conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan na ang **pang-uupasala** sa mga taong iba ang pananaw.","translation":"Stop the **reviling** of people with different views."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang talumpati ay puno ng **pang-uupasala** sa kanyang mga kalaban sa pulitika.","translation":"His speech was full of **vilification** against his political opponents."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang biglaang paghaharap o komprontasyon na may kasamang tensyon, hidwaan, o labanan, na hindi pinaghandaan.
etymology: Isang parirala na binubuo ng "di-", "inaasahan" (mula sa ugat na "asa"), at "pagsasagupa" (mula sa ugat na "sagupa").
original_explanation: This is the upgraded, action-packed version of 'di-inasasahang pagkikita'. This isn't just bumping into an ex; this is bumping into your rival for the last piece of lechon at a party. It's the moment the protagonist and antagonist finally cross paths in a crowded palengke. More confrontation, less conversation.
usage_notes: Karaniwang nagpapahiwatig ng negatibong resulta o tensyon, di-tulad ng 'pagkikita'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nauwi sa **di-inasasahang pagsasagupa** ang protesta nang dumating ang mga pulis.","translation":"The protest led to an **unforeseen clash** when the police arrived."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pook o bagay kung saan isinasampay o isinasabit ang mga damit upang matuyo.
etymology: Mula sa salitang 'sampay' at hulaping '-an' na nangangahulugang gamit o lugar.
original_explanation: The stage for your freshly washed clothes. It could be a high-tech foldable rack from the department store, or a simple wire tied between two coconut trees. The sampayan is the silent witness to all your OOTDs and your favorite butas-butas na pambahay.
usage_notes: Ang hulaping '-an' dito ay tumutukoy sa kasangkapan o lugar kung saan isinasagawa ang kilos ng salitang-ugat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Biglang bumagsak ang **sampayan** dahil sa bigat ng mga basang maong.","translation":"The **clothesline** suddenly collapsed due to the weight of the wet jeans."},{"sentence":"Pakikuha ng mga damit sa **sampayan** dahil uulan na.","translation":"Please get the clothes from the **clothesline** because it's about to rain."}]

translation: to saw; to travel back and forth
meaning_filipino: Gumamit ng lagari upang pumutol ng isang bagay; tumutukoy din sa madalas at pabalik-balik na pagbyahe sa dalawang lugar.
original_explanation: This has two meanings. First, using a saw. Boring. The second one is the juicy one: it's what you call that friend who lives in Cavite but works in QC. They're constantly lumalagari on EDSA. It's the life of a commuter, a delivery rider, or someone in a long-distance relationship, always going back and forth like a human shuttle service.
usage_notes: The second meaning of traveling back and forth is more common in modern colloquial speech to describe commuting or frequent travel between two points.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lumagari** siya ng kahoy para panggatong.","translation":"He **sawed** wood for fuel."},{"sentence":"Araw-araw siyang **lumalagari** mula Bulacan hanggang Makati para sa trabaho.","translation":"He **travels back and forth** from Bulacan to Makati for work every day."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang grado o puntos na ibinibigay bilang pagtatasa sa gawa o pagganap ng isang mag-aaral; grado.
original_explanation: The number that defined your childhood happiness or doom every quarter. A high `markahan` meant extra allowance or a Jollibee treat. A low one meant a sermon and no computer games for a week. Also known as 'grado.'
usage_notes: Used interchangeably with 'grado'. 'Markahan' can also refer to a grading period (e.g., 'Unang Markahan' - First Quarter).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang nakuha mong **markahan** sa pagsusulit sa Math?","translation":"What **score** did you get on the Math exam?"},{"sentence":"Ibibigay na bukas ang kard na may mga **markahan** para sa unang kwarter.","translation":"The card with the **grades** for the first quarter will be released tomorrow."}]

translation: to snatch and run away with something, to grab swiftly
meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis at biglaang pag-agaw o pagdaklot sa isang bagay at kasabay na pagtakbo o pag-alis.
original_explanation: The classic "snatcher" move. Imagine walking in Quiapo, holding your phone, and *whoosh*—it's gone. The person who took it just did a *sumambilat*. It’s a grab-and-go, but for theft. It's faster than a Shopee flash sale checkout.
usage_notes: A very specific verb implying both grabbing and fleeing. More descriptive than just 'kinuha' (took) or 'ninakaw' (stole).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumambilat** ng bag ang isang magnanakaw mula sa babaeng naglalakad.","translation":"A thief **snatched** a bag from a walking woman and ran off."},{"sentence":"Muntik nang **masambilat** ang cellphone ko buti na lang mahigpit ang hawak ko.","translation":"My cellphone was almost **snatched**, good thing I was holding it tightly."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa wika na nagmula sa Inglatera; maaari ring tumukoy sa taong mamamayan o nagmula sa Inglatera.
original_explanation: The official language of BPO companies, job interviews, and trying to sound smart. It's what you use to order at Starbucks and what your parents force you to speak when relatives from the US visit. It can also mean the person, like that tourist who's sunburnt but happy in Boracay.
usage_notes: Can refer to the language or a person of English nationality.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong maging mahusay sa **Ingles** para sa trabahong iyon.","translation":"You need to be good in **English** for that job."},{"sentence":"May isang **Ingles** na naligaw habang naglalakad sa Intramuros.","translation":"There was an **Englishman** who got lost while walking in Intramuros."}]

translation: to obstruct, to use as an obstacle
meaning_filipino: Ilagay o ipuwesto ang isang bagay upang maging hadlang, sagabal, o balakid sa daan o sa isang gawain.
etymology: From the prefix 'i-' (causative verb marker) and 'balakid' (obstacle, hindrance).
original_explanation: Ever tried to walk in a straight line but someone left their size 12 shoes in the middle of the hallway? That's an **ibinalakid**. It's intentionally or unintentionally putting something in the way to trip you up or block your path. Parang 'yung mga 'di kailangang meeting na **ibinabalakid** sa schedule mo para 'di ka makauwi on time.
usage_notes: Often used in a literal sense of blocking a path, but can also be used figuratively for hindering progress, plans, or dreams.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May nagtangkang **ibalakid** ang isang malaking bato sa kalsada.","translation":"Someone attempted to **use** a large rock **to obstruct** the road."},{"sentence":"Huwag nating hayaang **ibalakid** ng takot ang ating mga pangarap.","translation":"Let's not allow fear to be **used as an obstacle** to our dreams."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng maraming laman; mayaman sa nilalaman, kahulugan, o sustansya.
etymology: Mula sa `ma-` (mayroon o nagtataglay ng katangian) + `laman` (nilalaman, unod).
original_explanation: Can describe a juicy piece of chickenjoy (fleshy), or a movie that's more than just explosions and actually makes you think (meaningful). It's the difference between a chismis that's just "Nakita ko sila" and one that has all the juicy details. It has substance.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin nang literal para sa pagkain o bahagi ng katawan, o sa matalinghagang paraan para sa mga ideya, kwento, o argumento.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas gusto ko ang **malamnan** na bahagi ng manok.","translation":"I prefer the **fleshy** part of the chicken."},{"sentence":"Isang **malamnan** na talumpati ang kanyang ibinigay, puno ng mga makabuluhang punto.","translation":"He gave a **substantial** speech, full of meaningful points."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi malalagyan ng anumang mantsa, dumi, o bahid; nananatiling puro at malinis.
etymology: From 'di-' (not) + 'ma-' (ability prefix) + 'babahiran' (will be stained) from the root 'bahid' (stain, trace).
original_explanation: Your 'work bestie's' reputation before the new chismosa intern arrived. Or your white sneakers on the first day you wear them, before stepping into a puddle. That pristine state is di-mababahiran.
usage_notes: Often used figuratively to describe reputation, honor, or purity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pilit niyang pinanatiling **di-mababahiran** ng anumang katiwalian ang kanyang pangalan.","translation":"He tried hard to keep his name **untainted** by any corruption."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang pagkatao ay tila isang puting tela, **di-mababahiran** ng kasamaan.","translation":"Her character is like a white cloth, **untainted** by evil."}]

translation: to make or eat sopas (creamy macaroni soup)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagluluto o pagkain ng sopas, isang uri ng sabaw na karaniwang may manok, gatas, at macaroni.
etymology: From Spanish 'sopa' meaning 'soup'. In the Philippines, 'sopas' specifically refers to the creamy chicken macaroni soup.
original_explanation: The official verb for rainy days. When the weather gets cold, your mom will declare, 'Magsopas tayo!' It's the ultimate comfort food move, a verb that means 'to make everything feel warm and okay by cooking/eating creamy chicken soup.'
usage_notes: A very specific verb tied to a particular Filipino dish. It implies both the act of cooking and/or eating it.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil umuulan, nagpasya si Inay na **magsopas** para sa aming meryenda.","translation":"Because it was raining, Mom decided to **make sopas** for our snack."},{"sentence":"Tara, **magsopas** tayo sa kanto, malamig ang panahon.","translation":"Let's go **eat sopas** at the corner, the weather is cold."}]

translation: to quaver; to become hoarse or shaky (voice)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabago ng tunog ng boses na nagiging paos, nanginginig, o basag, karaniwan dahil sa matinding emosyon tulad ng takot, galit, o pag-iyak.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your voice when you're about to cry during a confrontation, or when you're trying to give a speech and stage fright hits you hard. Your voice starts to crack and tremble. It's the audio equivalent of "I'm not crying, you're crying!"
usage_notes: Specifically refers to the quality of a voice.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Gumaralgal** ang boses niya habang nagpapaalam.","translation":"His voice **quavered** while saying goodbye."},{"sentence":"Nang subukan niyang sumigaw, **gumaralgal** lang ang kanyang tinig dahil sa takot.","translation":"When he tried to shout, his voice just **became shaky** out of fear."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghahanda ng pagkain sa pamamagitan ng init, tulad ng pagpapakulo, pagpiprito, o pag-iihaw.
original_explanation: The command you give when you're hungry and pointing at raw ingredients. "Itlog, lutuin mo" (Cook the egg). It’s the process of transforming sad, raw vegetables and meat into a glorious meal, or in some cases, into a carbonized offering to the fire gods if you get distracted by a TikTok video.
usage_notes: This is the object-focus form of the verb "to cook". The subject-focus form is `magluto`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **lutuin** ang bigas para sa hapunan.","translation":"Don't forget **to cook** the rice for dinner."}]

translation: to give attention to; to notice
meaning_filipino: Mag-ukol ng atensyon o pag-iisip sa isang tao, bagay, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: The opposite of being "seen-zoned." Ito 'yung pag-reply ni crush sa story mo. It's the act of taking notice, of paying attention to something or someone. When your boss praises your work in a meeting, he is giving it attention. It's acknowledging existence and importance, even for a moment.
usage_notes: A very common phrase used in all contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat nating **bigyang-pansin** ang mga isyung pangkalikasan.","translation":"We should **give attention to** environmental issues."},{"sentence":"Salamat sa **pagbigay-pansin** sa aking mungkahi.","translation":"Thank you for **noticing** my suggestion."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maranasan ang pagyanig o paggalaw ng lupa sanhi ng mga pwersang heolohikal.
original_explanation: The verb form of that moment when the whole world (or at least, your building) starts shaking and you have to decide whether to 'duck, cover, and hold' or run outside screaming. It's the Earth hitting the 'vibrate' button.
usage_notes: Actor-focus verb, completed aspect (past tense). The 'actor' is conceptually the earth or the event itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lumindol** nang malakas kagabi kaya't maraming nagising.","translation":"There **was a strong earthquake** last night, so many people woke up."},{"sentence":"Nang **lumindol**, nasa ika-sampung palapag kami ng gusali.","translation":"When the **earthquake happened**, we were on the tenth floor of the building."}]

translation: to sell; to put up for sale
meaning_filipino: Ialok at ipagbili ang isang produkto o serbisyo.
original_explanation: Your tita's side hustle. Whether it's frozen siopao, homemade ube pandesal, or pre-loved clothes, 'pag inilagay na niya sa Facebook Marketplace, she's going to 'itinda' it. It's the verb for making a sale, palengke-style or online.
usage_notes: Often used for goods sold in a store, market, or by an individual seller.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano-anong prutas ang plano mong **itinda** bukas?","translation":"What fruits are you planning to **sell** tomorrow?"},{"sentence":"Mas magandang **itinda** ang mga ito online para mas maraming makakita.","translation":"It's better to **sell** these online so more people can see them."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging mag-isa; kawalan ng kasama.
etymology: From `pag-` (nominalizer) + `isa` (one). The repetition `pag-i-isa` emphasizes the state or quality of being one.
original_explanation: That feeling when your whole barkada made plans without you. Or, on the flip side, that glorious moment when you finally have the whole house to yourself—no parents, no siblings, just you, Netflix, and a large pizza. Pwedeng malungkot, pwedeng masaya. It's the difference between 'lonely' and 'alone time.'
usage_notes: Can have both positive (solitude, peace) and negative (loneliness, isolation) connotations depending on context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Minsan, kailangan natin ng panahon para sa **pag-iisa** upang makapag-isip-isip.","translation":"Sometimes, we need time for **solitude** to reflect."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang itinalagang lugar para sa pagpaparada o pag-iwan ng mga sasakyan.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'parada' (a stop), mula sa 'parar' (to stop) + hulaping Tagalog na '-han' (lugar).
original_explanation: The Holy Grail of any mall-goer in Manila, especially on a payday weekend. A 'paradahan' is a parking lot. Finding a spot can feel like winning the lottery. It's derived from 'parada' (the Spanish word for stop, not parade) + '-han' (a suffix indicating a place). So, it's literally a "place for stopping/parking".
usage_notes: Ang salitang-ugat na 'parada' dito ay tumutukoy sa 'paghinto', hindi sa 'parada' na isang prusisyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno na ang **paradahan** ng mall.","translation":"The mall's **parking lot** is already full."},{"sentence":"Maghanap ka ng maayos na **paradahan** para hindi tayo mamultahan.","translation":"Find a proper **parking space** so we don't get a fine."}]

translation: hard up (for money), in a tight spot
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging nasa isang mahirap na sitwasyon, partikular na ang kakulangan sa pera o oras.
original_explanation: It's petsa de peligro. Sweldo is a week away, your wallet has 100 pesos, and your friend invites you out for samgyupsal. You can't go because you're **nagigipit**. It’s the official state of being for many people from the 10th to the 14th, and the 25th to the 29th of the month.
usage_notes: Can be used as a verb ('nagigipit ako') or an adjective ('panahong nagigipit'). Primarily refers to financial difficulty but can also refer to being cornered or pressed for time.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagigipit** ako ngayon, pwedeng sa susunod na linggo na lang ako magbayad?","translation":"I'm **hard up** right now, can I just pay next week?"},{"sentence":"Maraming Pilipino ang **nagigipit** dahil sa pagtaas ng presyo ng bilihin.","translation":"Many Filipinos are **in a tight spot** because of the rising prices of goods."}]

meaning_filipino: Malakas at hindi kaaya-ayang tunog na nakakagambala sa pandinig o katahimikan.
original_explanation: The soundtrack of the Philippines. It's the karaoke next door at 2 AM on a Tuesday, the unending tricycle engine revs, the 'taho!' vendor's morning call, and the collective chismis of your neighborhood marites. If there's no ingay, something is wrong.
usage_notes: Can also be used metaphorically for clamor, controversy, or 'buzz' (e.g., 'gumawa ng ingay' - to create a buzz).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, bawasan ninyo ang **ingay** dahil may natutulog.","translation":"Please, lessen the **noise** because someone is sleeping."},{"sentence":"Gumawa ng **ingay** sa social media ang kanyang bagong pelikula.","translation":"His new movie created a **buzz** on social media."}]

translation: to reach; to be able to get to
meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang makarating o makaabot sa isang partikular na lugar, layunin, o kalagayan.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na after 3 hours of traffic sa EDSA, marating mo na rin sa wakas 'yung office mo. Or 'yung pangarap mong maging K-pop star, sana balang araw marating mo rin. It's about reaching a destination, whether it's a physical place or a life goal.
usage_notes: Often used for both physical destinations and abstract goals or achievements.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **marating** natin ang tuktok ng bundok bago dumilim.","translation":"I hope we can **reach** the summit of the mountain before it gets dark."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **marating** ang tagumpay kung hindi ka magsisikap.","translation":"It's hard **to reach** success if you don't work hard."}]

meaning_filipino: Ipahayag sa publiko sa pamamagitan ng paglalathala o pagbabando, karaniwang isang utos o anunsyo mula sa awtoridad.
original_explanation: Before group chats and Facebook announcements, this was how you got the word out. A town crier, or `bandilyo`, would walk around shouting the mayor's new ordinance. "Hoy, hoy, hoy! Bawal magtapon ng basura dito!" That's `ibando`. It’s a public broadcast, old-school style.
usage_notes: A bit formal and dated, but still understood. Often associated with official government or town announcements.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinag-utos ng kapitan na **ibando** sa buong barangay ang bagong patakaran.","translation":"The captain ordered to **proclaim** the new rule throughout the entire barangay."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **ibando** na may pagpupulong mamayang gabi.","translation":"We need to **announce publicly** that there is a meeting tonight."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng matibay na paniniwala o paninindigan sa isang bagay dahil sa sapat na ebidensya o pangangatwiran.
original_explanation: That feeling when your friend finally presents enough 'receipts' (screenshots) to prove their chismis is true. You're no longer in doubt, you're 100% on board. 'Okay, fine, kumbinsido na ako!' is the verbal equivalent of a white flag in an argument. From Spanish 'convencido'.
usage_notes: Ang pambabaeng anyo ay 'kumbinsida', ngunit 'kumbinsido' ay karaniwang ginagamit para sa lahat ng kasarian sa modernong pag-uusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumbinsido** siyang mananalo siya sa patimpalak.","translation":"He is **convinced** that he will win the contest."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglilinis upang alisin ang mga mikrobyo; isagawa ang disimpeksyon.
original_explanation: This is the action word for "disimpeksyon". Kapag sinabing "disimpektahin mo 'yan," ibig sabihin, "wisikan mo ng alcohol 'yan, now na!" It's the command you give when someone sneezes near the food or when a package from Lazada arrives. The ultimate germ-killing action.
usage_notes: Ito ang pandiwa (verb) na kaugnay ng pangngalan (noun) na 'disimpeksyon'. Karaniwang ginagamit sa anyong pautos (disimpektahin) o bilang pandiwa (nagdisimpekta, magdidisimpekta).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **disimpekta**hin ang iyong mga kamay bago kumain.","translation":"You need to **disinfect** your hands before eating."},{"sentence":"Nag-utos ang mayor na **disimpekta**hin ang buong palengke.","translation":"The mayor ordered to **disinfect** the entire public market."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga bagay na itinatapon, dumi, o anumang walang silbi o halaga.
original_explanation: The stuff you throw away. Can be literal (like your food scraps) or figurative (like your ex's empty promises). Also, a major character in every Metro Manila flood story.
usage_notes: A very common word used daily. Can be used metaphorically to describe something of low quality or a person with bad character.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang itapon ang **basura** mamayang gabi.","translation":"Don't forget to take out the **trash** tonight."},{"sentence":"Ang pelikulang iyon ay **basura**.","translation":"That movie was **trash**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng labis na pagmamataas, kawalan ng galang, at pagiging palalo sa pakikitungo sa iba.
original_explanation: This is the vibe of someone who thinks they're a gift from the heavens and treats everyone else like ants. Yung tipong in-expect ka niyang mag-adjust para sa kanya, hindi siya sa'yo. It's not just being "mayabang" (boastful), it's the added layer of being rude and disrespectful about it. The "How dare you speak to me?" energy.
usage_notes: A strong, somewhat old-fashioned word to describe a particularly offensive type of arrogance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa pagiging **dunghal** at walang pakundangan sa damdamin ng iba.","translation":"He is known for being **arrogant** and thoughtless of others' feelings."},{"sentence":"Isang **dunghal** na sagot ang kanyang binitiwan sa matanda.","translation":"He gave a **haughty** reply to the old person."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang lugar na madalas makaranas ng lindol o pagyanig ng lupa.
original_explanation: Describes a place, not an event. The Philippines is a malindol country, thanks to the Pacific Ring of Fire. If you live in a malindol area, your emergency 'go bag' is always ready and you know the 'duck, cover, and hold' drill by heart. It's a geographical reality check.
usage_notes: Describes a location's characteristic of having frequent earthquakes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Japan ay isang bansang **malindol**.","translation":"Japan is a country **prone to earthquakes**."},{"sentence":"Dahil **malindol** ang aming lugar, matibay ang pagkakagawa ng aming bahay.","translation":"Because our area is **earthquake-prone**, our house was built to be sturdy."}]

translation: to be very frank with; to speak bluntly to
meaning_filipino: Kausapin ang isang tao nang buong katapatan at walang anumang pag-aalinlangan o pagtatago.
original_explanation: This is the upgraded version of 'tapatan'. It's when you're done with hints and subtleties. 'Look, tapat-tapatin na kita, amoy-araw ka na.' It's direct, no-filter honesty, often used when the situation is serious or you've run out of patience.
usage_notes: The reduplication adds emphasis, implying a higher degree of frankness or directness than 'tapatan'. It's an imperative to speak without holding back.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kung ako sa'yo, **tapat-tapatin** mo na siya tungkol sa iyong tunay na nararamdaman.","translation":"If I were you, I would **be very frank with** him about your true feelings."},{"sentence":"**Tapat-tapatin** na kita, kaibigan. Hindi bagay sa iyo ang damit na iyan.","translation":"Let me **be blunt with** you, friend. That dress doesn't suit you."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kumikilos o may kapangyarihang kumatawan sa iba; isang kinatawan o ahente. Maaari ring tumukoy sa isang puwersa o sangkap na nagdudulot ng pagbabago.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung friend mong laging nag-aalok ng insurance, condo, o kotse. Sila 'yung "agent" ng kumpanya. Pwede ring 'yung bida sa action movie na spy, tulad ni James Bond, a secret agent. Sa science, ito 'yung "active ingredient" na nagpapagana sa isang bagay, like "oxidizing agent".
usage_notes: Commonly used in business, real estate, insurance, and intelligence contexts. The Tagalog-assimilated form 'ahente' is also very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinausap ko ang **agent** ng insurance para sa bagong policy.","translation":"I spoke with the insurance **agent** for a new policy."},{"sentence":"Ang **agent** ng real estate ang nagpakita sa amin ng bahay.","translation":"The real estate **agent** showed us the house."}]

translation: to have someone look for something
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o paghiling sa isang tao na hanapin ang isang bagay o isang indibidwal.
original_explanation: This is what your mom yells when she can't find her glasses and is 100% sure you moved them. "Pahanap mo nga ako ng matinong ka-date!" is the single person's lament. It's the act of delegating a search party, whether for car keys or for a soulmate.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pahanap** mo nga sa bata ang tsinelas ko.","translation":"Please have the child **look for** my slippers."},{"sentence":"Nag-alala siya kaya nag-utos siyang **pahanap** ang nawawalang aso.","translation":"She was worried so she ordered someone to **look for** the missing dog."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na pagsubok sa kaalaman o kasanayan ng isang tao, karaniwan sa larangan ng akademya o propesyonal.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'judgement day' ng mga estudyante. Ito 'yung dahilan ng puyat, sandamakmak na kape, at dasal na sana lumabas sa eksamen 'yung mga inaral mo lang. Pag bagsak, may part 2 sa summer class.
usage_notes: Ginagamit din ang salitang 'pagsusulit' bilang katumbas nito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong mag-aral nang mabuti para sa **eksamen** bukas.","translation":"I need to study well for the **exam** tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Bumagsak siya sa huling **eksamen** kaya kailangan niyang umulit.","translation":"He failed the last **examination**, so he needs to retake it."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang makipag-usap o mag-alay ng papuri, pasasalamat, o kahilingan sa isang kinikilalang Diyos o mas mataas na kapangyarihan.
original_explanation: What you do before a major exam, during a bumpy flight, or when your salary is delayed. It's your direct line to 'the management upstairs.' Whether it's a full-on 'Ama Namin' or a quick 'Lord, help po,' you're manalangin.
usage_notes: The most common and respectful term for praying. 'Magdasal' is a synonym, often from the Spanish 'rezar'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **manalangin** bago matulog.","translation":"Don't forget **to pray** before sleeping."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang aspekto o panahunan ng pandiwa na nagsasaad na ang kilos ay hindi pa nangyayari at magaganap pa lamang sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: Ito ang "sana mangyari" o "plano" tense. 'Yung mga "Mag-aaral na ako mamaya," "Magda-diet na ako bukas," at "Babayaran na kita next week." Puno ng pag-asa, minsan napapako. Sa gramatika, ito yung mga verb na inuulit ang unang pantig ng salitang-ugat, tulad ng *ka*kain, *tu*tulog, *li*lipad.
usage_notes: Ang mas teknikal at karaniwang termino para rito ay "aspektong kontemplatibo."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang salitang \"aalis\" ay nasa **panahunang panghinaharap**.","translation":"The word \"will leave\" is in the **future tense**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha o paglabas ng mga kislap ng kuryente o apoy; biglaang pag-ilaw.
original_explanation: This is the spark you see when you plug something into a faulty outlet, or the flash of a transformer before a brownout. Metaphorically, it's that 'spark' you feel on a first date when the chemistry is just right. Kilig-level electricity.
usage_notes: A somewhat literary or technical term. 'Kislap' is more common in everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagdagitab** ng mga kawad ng kuryente ay nakakatakot.","translation":"The **sparking** of the electrical wires is frightening."},{"sentence":"Isang marahan na **pagdagitab** ang namuo sa pagitan ng kanilang mga kamay.","translation":"A gentle **spark** formed between their hands."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang diplomatikong kinatawan ng Santo Papa sa isang bansa, na may ranggo ng isang embahador.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na 'nuncio', na galing sa Latin na 'nuntius' (mensahero).
original_explanation: The Pope's official representative or ambassador to a country. Basically, he's the direct line to the Vatican, the ultimate 'Team Lead' for the Catholic Church in the Philippines. You see him during major church events.
usage_notes: Ang baybay na 'nunsiyo' ay ginagamit din ngunit hindi gaanong karaniwan. Tumutukoy ito partikular sa Papal Nuncio.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Apostolikong **Nunsyo** sa Pilipinas ay nagbigay ng mensahe mula sa Santo Papa.","translation":"The Apostolic **Nuncio** to the Philippines delivered a message from the Pope."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kusang-loob na nag-aalok ng serbisyo o tulong nang walang inaasahang bayad.
original_explanation: Ito yung mga taong may "main character energy" sa pagtulong. Hindi kailangan ng sahod, sapat na ang libreng T-shirt at fulfillment. Sila yung unang nag-sign up para sa community pantry, clean-up drive, o relief operations. Bayani points over sahod points ang motto nila. Kung sa group project, sila yung "Ako na gagawa," pero this time, para sa bayan.
usage_notes: Madalas ding ginagamit bilang pandiwa (mag-volunteer). Ang katumbas sa Tagalog ay "boluntaryo" o "magboluntaryo."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **volunteer** ang tumulong sa pag-repack ng relief goods para sa mga biktima ng bagyo.","translation":"Many **volunteers** helped repack the relief goods for the typhoon victims."},{"sentence":"Nag-**volunteer** siyang magturo sa mga bata tuwing Sabado.","translation":"He **volunteered** to teach children every Saturday."}]

translation: to endure, to suffer through, to bear
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtitiis o pagbata sa isang mahirap, masakit, o hindi kaaya-ayang sitwasyon.
etymology: Likely a variant of 'tiisin' from the root 'tiis' (to endure).
original_explanation: This is what you do during a 3-hour company town hall that could have been an email. It's enduring your tita's 'tumataba ka' comments during a family reunion. You just gotta **katiin** mo lang, bes. It's the verb form of 'tiis-ganda.'
usage_notes: 'Tiisin' is the far more common and standard verb. 'Katiin' is considered archaic, a misspelling, or a dialectal variant and is rarely used in modern Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **katiin** ang pambabatikos ng mga tao.","translation":"It's hard **to bear** the people's criticism."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglipat ng mga pahina ng isang aklat, magasin, o anumang babasahin na naganap na. Ito ay nasa pangnagdaang panahunan.
original_explanation: Past tense of that thing you do in a bookstore. "Kanina, nagbuklat ako ng libro tungkol sa 'adulting' tapos na-stress lang ako lalo kaya binalik ko." It's the completed action of flipping pages.
usage_notes: The past tense of "magbuklat." Refers to the completed action of turning pages.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagbuklat** siya ng ilang pahina bago niya ibinalik ang aklat sa estante.","translation":"He **leafed through** a few pages before returning the book to the shelf."},{"sentence":"Habang naghihintay, **nagbuklat** ako ng isang lumang magasin.","translation":"While waiting, I **browsed** an old magazine."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubhang mababa, maaaring tumukoy sa posisyon, halaga, antas, o kalidad.
original_explanation: Can refer to your grades after a tough sem, the sale price of your dream shoes during 11.11, your self-esteem after a rejection, or your energy level on a Monday morning. It's the floor, basically.
usage_notes: The 'napaka-' prefix is a superlative, used to mean 'very' or 'extremely'. Can be used for both literal (low position) and figurative (low value, low morale) meanings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Napakababa** ng nakuha niyang marka sa pagsusulit.","translation":"He got a **very low** score on the exam."},{"sentence":"Kahit **napakababa** ng sahod, nagtitiyaga pa rin siya para sa pamilya.","translation":"Even if the salary is **very low**, he perseveres for his family."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang makasaysayang napapaderang lungsod sa Maynila na nagsilbing sentro ng pamahalaan, relihiyon, at edukasyon noong panahon ng pananakop ng Espanya sa Pilipinas.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na "intramuros," na nangangahulugang "sa loob ng mga pader."
original_explanation: Yan yung go-to place for pre-nup shoots, school field trips, and ghost hunting. Ang ultimate throwback ng Pinas. Dito mo mararamdaman na #OldManila ang peg, with matching kalesa rides at cobblestone streets. Perfect for that "Maria Clara" vibe OOTD.
usage_notes: Palaging nagsisimula sa malaking titik dahil ito ay isang tiyak na pangalan ng lugar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Namasyal kami sa **Intramuros** noong nakaraang linggo.","translation":"We toured **Intramuros** last week."},{"sentence":"Maraming makasaysayang simbahan at gusali sa loob ng **Intramuros**.","translation":"There are many historical churches and buildings inside **Intramuros**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bilang na katumbas ng siyam na daan; ang kardinal na bilang na kasunod ng 899 at sinusundan ng 901.
etymology: A compound number from Tagalog 'siyam' (nine), the linker 'na', and 'raan' (a variant of 'daan', meaning hundred).
original_explanation: Literally 'nine hundred'. It's the price of a concert ticket that makes you think twice. It's that awkward amount you have left in your G-Cash after paying all your bills. 'May 900 pa ako... kaya pa 'to hanggang sahod.'
usage_notes: The 'na' linker is essential. In modern text, it's almost always written as the numeral '900'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang upa sa apartment ay **siyam na raan** na dolyar bawat buwan.","translation":"The rent for the apartment is **nine hundred** dollars per month."},{"sentence":"Nagkakahalaga ng **siyam na raan** na piso ang bagong labas na video game.","translation":"The newly released video game costs **nine hundred** pesos."}]

translation: to gargle, to rinse one's mouth
meaning_filipino: Ipagalaw ang tubig o anumang likido sa loob ng bibig nang hindi ito nilulunok, karaniwan para sa paglilinis.
original_explanation: The sound you make to prove to your mom you're actually getting ready for school. Also the secret weapon against 'bawang breath' after eating too much sinangag. It's the oral version of 'washing your hands of the situation'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinabihan ako ng dentista na **magmumog** ng maligamgam na tubig na may asin.","translation":"The dentist told me to **gargle** with warm salt water."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos kumain, laging **magmumog** para maiwasan ang tooth decay.","translation":"After eating, always **rinse your mouth** to prevent tooth decay."}]

translation: act of poking or tapping lightly
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pauli-ulit at marahang pagdiin o pagturo gamit ang daliri o isang bagay na may dulo.
original_explanation: This is that annoying but sometimes necessary poke. It's what you do to your sleepy friend to wake them up, what you do to your phone screen when it's lagging, or how you get your sibling's attention without talking. It's the physical version of 'uy, psst!'.
usage_notes: Can also mean 'to touch upon' or 'briefly mention' a topic in a discussion. It implies a repeated or light action, as opposed to a single, firm 'tusok' (stab/poke).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakairita ang **pagdutdot** niya sa tagiliran ko habang nanonood kami ng sine.","translation":"His **poking** on my side while we were watching a movie was irritating."},{"sentence":"Sa pamamagitan ng **pagdutdot** sa screen, maaari mo nang buksan ang application.","translation":"By **tapping** on the screen, you can now open the application."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagtiyak, pagpapatunay, o pag-alam kung ang isang bagay ay totoo, tama, o tiyak.
original_explanation: The classic 'double-check' or 'triple-check.' It's what you do before logging off your work computer, before sending a risky text, or when your mom asks 'Did you lock the door?' for the fifth time. *Pagsiguro* is the official sport of panganays and project managers everywhere. 'Para sigurado' is the national motto.
usage_notes: 'Siguro' by itself can mean 'maybe', but 'pagsiguro' or 'siguraduhin' means 'to make sure'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **pagsiguro** na kumpleto ang lahat ng dokumento bago mag-apply.","translation":"**Ensuring** that all documents are complete before applying is important."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang muling pagtawag ay isang **pagsiguro** lamang na natanggap ko ang mensahe.","translation":"His call back was just an **act of making sure** that I received the message."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malakas na unos o sigwa na may kasamang malakas na hangin at ulan, karaniwang nabubuo sa mga rehiyong tropikal.
original_explanation: In the Philippines, this is the national excuse for class suspensions and a valid reason to eat instant noodles with egg. A bagyo isn't just a storm; it's an event. It has a name (like 'Yolanda' or 'Ondoy'), it trends on Twitter, and it's when you find out if your roof has a leak. It's the ultimate test of your 'diskarte' (resourcefulness) and your supply of canned goods.
usage_notes: A very common word, especially during the rainy season (June-November).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Walang pasok bukas dahil sa paparating na **bagyo**.","translation":"There are no classes tomorrow because of the approaching **typhoon**."},{"sentence":"Nasira ang maraming pananim dahil sa lakas ng **bagyo**.","translation":"Many crops were destroyed due to the strength of the **storm**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpukpok o pagdiin sa isang bagay hanggang sa ito ay maging yupi o pipi.
original_explanation: The command form of 'pitpit'. It's what your mom tells you to do to the garlic before sautéing. "Pitpitin mo muna 'yung luya bago ilagay sa tinola." It's an act of controlled destruction in the kitchen, essential for releasing flavor or just taking out your frustrations on an innocent clove of garlic.
usage_notes: A common verb in cooking instructions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **pitpitin** ang mga buto ng paminta para mas lumabas ang anghang.","translation":"You need to **pound flat** the peppercorns to release more of their spiciness."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pitpitin** ang lata, ire-recycle pa natin 'yan.","translation":"Don't **flatten** the can, we are still going to recycle it."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pag-aalaga sa mga itlog, karaniwan sa pamamagitan ng pagbibigay ng init, upang mapisa ang mga ito at lumabas ang sisiw o anak.
original_explanation: This is the OG "startup incubator." It's literally making eggs hatch, whether it's a mother hen sitting on them or a high-tech machine doing the job. In modern slang, "pinapisa ang itlog" can be a crude way to say someone got someone pregnant.
usage_notes: This is a phrase acting as a noun. The core concept is 'pagpapapisa'. The object 'ng itlog' is almost always included. Be aware of the potential for slang/crude double meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang modernong **pagpapapisa ng itlog** ay gumagamit ng mga incubator machine.","translation":"Modern **hatching of eggs** uses incubator machines."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong may mataas na ranggo o posisyon sa pamahalaan o simbahan; isang importanteng tao.
original_explanation: The VIPs. The 'big-time' folks. These are the people who get the front-row seats, the police escorts, and the special catered food at events. Think presidents, ambassadors, cardinals, and that one super-rich tito who everyone tries to impress at the family reunion.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in formal, political, or religious contexts, especially in news reporting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumating ang mga dayuhang **dignitaryo** para sa isang pandaigdigang kumperensya.","translation":"The foreign **dignitaries** arrived for an international conference."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng palitan ng salita o ideya sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang tao.
original_explanation: The cure for (and cause of) all problems. It's what your partner says when you're in trouble: 'We need to talk.' It can be about chismis with your bestie, a serious meeting with your boss, or a heart-to-heart with your parents. The foundation of every relationship and every 'Marites' network.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **mag-usap** nang masinsinan tungkol sa problema.","translation":"We need to **talk** thoroughly about the problem."},{"sentence":"Masayang **mag-usap** habang nagkakape.","translation":"It's nice to **converse** while having coffee."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong may malawak na kaalaman sa panitikan; isang manunulat o alagad ng sining ng pagsulat.
original_explanation: Basically, a 'book person' or a writer, but with a fancier, old-school title. Think of Jose Rizal or Nick Joaquin. If someone calls you a 'literato' today, they're either being very formal or teasing you for being a bookworm who uses big words.
usage_notes: Medyo luma na ang termino at bihirang gamitin sa pang-araw-araw na usapan. Mas karaniwan ang 'manunulat'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinikilala si Lope K. Santos bilang isang dakilang **literato** ng Pilipinas.","translation":"Lope K. Santos is recognized as a great **man of letters** of the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Ang mga **literato** ay nagtipon para sa isang kumperensya.","translation":"The **literary people** gathered for a conference."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpapadala ng isang "private message" o pribadong mensahe sa isang tao sa isang social media platform.
etymology: From the English acronym 'private message', used as a verb.
original_explanation: The act of sending a private message. When someone asks "How much po?" on a public post, the seller's immediate response is "P-PM ko po kayo" to keep the price a secret and create a sense of exclusivity. It's the first step to any "mine" or "pa-reserve" transaction.
usage_notes: Can be conjugated like a regular Filipino verb using Filipino affixes: nag-pm, nag-pe-pm, i-pe-pm, etc.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**PM** mo na lang ako para sa mga detalye.","translation":"Just **pm** me for the details."},{"sentence":"Nag-**pm** ako sa kanya pero seen lang.","translation":"I **pm**'d him but he just left me on seen."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagsasabit ng mga damit o anumang tela sa isang sampayan upang matuyo sa pamamagitan ng hangin at sikat ng araw.
original_explanation: The OG way of drying clothes before the 'automatic' button on the washing machine. It's a race against the rain clouds and a test of your clothespin skills. The ultimate sign of an 'adulting' weekend is spending it doing laundry and saying 'kailangan kong magsampay.'
