usage_notes: Specifically refers to hanging items, usually laundry, on a line or rack (sampayan) to dry.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag ka munang **magsampay** dahil mukhang uulan.","translation":"Don't **hang the laundry** yet because it looks like it's going to rain."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos maglaba, kailangan mo nang **magsampay** agad.","translation":"After washing the clothes, you need to **hang** them to dry right away."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang masamang damdamin o bigat sa puso na nararamdaman para sa isang tao dahil sa isang nagawang kasalanan o di-pagkakaunawaan.
etymology: From sama (bad) + ng (of) + kalooban (inner self, will).
original_explanation: This is the emotional baggage you carry after a fight. It's the silent treatment, the passive-aggressive comments, the "Okay lang ako" when you're clearly not okay. It’s the hugot that fuels a thousand sad songs. You don't just 'get mad'; you accumulate 'sama ng kalooban' like bad cholesterol.
usage_notes: A deep-seated negative emotion, more profound than simple anger (`galit`).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon siya ng **sama ng kalooban** sa kaibigan niya matapos siyang pagtaksilan.","translation":"She developed **resentment** towards her friend after being betrayed."},{"sentence":"Dapat nating iwasan ang magkimkim ng **sama ng kalooban** para sa kapayapaan ng ating isip.","translation":"We should avoid holding a **grudge** for our own peace of mind."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malaking salagubang (Oryctes rhinoceros) na karaniwang itim, makintab, at may sungay na kahawig ng sa rinosero.
etymology: Katutubong salita sa mga wika sa Pilipinas.
original_explanation: This is that big, black, shiny beetle with a horn that looks like it's ready for a medieval joust. Kids in the province sometimes catch them, tie a string to them, and make them fight. It's the 'bodybuilder' of the beetle world. Not to be confused with 'uwang', which can be a more general term for any large beetle.
usage_notes: Often found in rural or provincial areas, especially near coconut trees. The term is more specific than the general 'salagubang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May nahuli kaming **uang** sa puno ng niyog kagabi.","translation":"We caught a **rhinoceros beetle** on the coconut tree last night."},{"sentence":"Kinatatakutan ng mga bata ang lumilipad na **uang**.","translation":"The children are afraid of the flying **rhinoceros beetle**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagtatasa sa emosyonal na estado o pangkalahatang 'vibe' ng isang tao, lugar, o sitwasyon.
etymology: Mula sa pariralang Ingles na 'vibe check', na naging popular sa internet.
original_explanation: It's a spontaneous, informal assessment of someone's mood or the general atmosphere. Bago ka mag-open up ng topic, you do a quick 'vibe check' to see if it's the right time. 'Kumusta ang vibe check sa party?' means 'Is the party fun or boring?' It's the social weather report.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pangngalan ('gumawa ng vibe check') o pandiwa ('i-vibe check mo siya').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Teka, **vibe check** muna tayo. Okay lang ba ang lahat?","translation":"Hold on, let's do a **vibe check**. Is everyone okay?"},{"sentence":"Parang bagsak ang **vibe check** sa opisina ngayon; tahimik ang lahat.","translation":"The **vibe check** at the office seems low today; everyone is quiet."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpapatunay na hindi totoo, mali, o walang batayan ang isang pahayag, paratang, o paniniwala.
etymology: From `pag-` + `pa-` + `bulaan` (liar, false). The act of making something be proven false.
original_explanation: This is the official term for 'calling someone out on their BS.' It's when you present facts, evidence, or a solid 'receipt' to prove that what someone said is fake news. The ultimate 'Objection!' in a debate or a Marites session.
usage_notes: Often used in formal contexts like debates, legal proceedings, or academic arguments.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglabas ng opisyal na pahayag ang kumpanya para sa **pagpapabulaan** sa mga akusasyon.","translation":"The company released an official statement for the **refutation** of the accusations."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang testimonya ay isang malinaw na **pagpapabulaan** sa sinabi ng unang saksi.","translation":"His testimony is a clear **disproof** of what the first witness said."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang babaeng asawa ng isang lalaki; isang pormal na pantawag sa isang babaeng may-asawa.
original_explanation: The CEO of the household. The 'boss' na laging tama. Your partner-in-crime, partner-in-utang, and the one who knows where you put your keys. Also used as a respectful term for a married woman, short for 'Mrs.'
usage_notes: A very common colloquial term for 'wife'. It can be used affectionately or as a simple descriptor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umuwi ka na, baka hanapin ka na ng **misis** mo.","translation":"Go home now, your **wife** might be looking for you."},{"sentence":"Magandang umaga po, **Misis** Reyes.","translation":"Good morning, **Mrs.** Reyes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na kubo na may mga tuldok sa bawat isa sa anim na mukha nito, na ginagamit sa mga laro.
original_explanation: Before Mobile Legends, there was 'dado'. This is the OG random number generator for board games like Snakes and Ladders or Monopoly. It's the little cube that decides your fate—whether you land on the property you want or go straight to jail.
usage_notes: The plural form is also "dado" in common parlance, though "mga dado" is grammatically correct.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-abot ng **dado** para makapagsimula na tayo sa laro.","translation":"Please pass the **dice** so we can start the game."},{"sentence":"Nawawala ang isang **dado** ng Monopoly.","translation":"One of the Monopoly **dice** is missing."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagiging bagsak, lupaypay, o nanghihina dahil sa matinding kalungkutan, pagod, o sakit.
original_explanation: That feeling after a 16-hour shift tapos na-cancel pa 'yung leave mo for the long weekend. Bagsak ang katawan, bagsak ang loob. Parang na-drain lahat ng energy mo, physically and emotionally. That's lugpo. It's the "wala-na-finish-na" state of being.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a state of extreme emotional or physical exhaustion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lugpo** ang katawan ng manlalaro matapos ang limang set na laban.","translation":"The player's body was **prostrate** after a five-set match."},{"sentence":"Naiwang **lugpo** si Ana nang malaman niyang hindi siya nakapasa sa board exam.","translation":"Ana was left **crestfallen** when she found out she didn't pass the board exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong kulang sa kasanayan, husay, o galing sa isang partikular na gawain o laro.
etymology: Possibly from Spanish 'vano' meaning vain or useless.
original_explanation: This is the gamer term for a "noob" before "noob" was a thing. If you keep dying in Mobile Legends or can't seem to get the mechanics of a game, your teammates will definitely call you bano. It's the opposite of a pro. Parang 'yung ka-team mo na auto-lock sa Marksman pero 0-10-0 ang score.
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of games (video games, sports, etc.). It's considered informal and can be insulting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala kung **bano** ka pa sa simula, lahat naman nagsisimula diyan.","translation":"Don't worry if you're still a **noob** at the start, everyone starts there."},{"sentence":"Tinawag siyang **bano** ng mga kalaro niya dahil palagi siyang talo.","translation":"His playmates called him **unskilled** because he always loses."}]

translation: to transfer; to translate; to pour
meaning_filipino: Ilipat ang isang bagay mula sa isang lalagyan, wika, o anyo patungo sa iba.
original_explanation: This word is a multitasker. You magsalin water from a pitcher to a glass. You magsalin a document from English to Tagalog (translate). A mother can magsalin her knowledge to her child (pass down). It's the OG 'copy-paste' but for liquids, languages, and legacies. It's all about moving something from one container to another, whether that container is a cup, a language, or a generation.
usage_notes: The specific meaning depends heavily on the context (what is being transferred and to where). It can mean to pour, to translate, to copy, or to pass down/on.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magsalin** ka ng tubig sa baso.","translation":"**Pour** some water into the glass."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan kong **magsalin** ng isang nobelang Hapon sa Filipino.","translation":"I am trying to **translate** a Japanese novel into Filipino."},{"sentence":"Ang mga tradisyon ay dapat na maisalin sa susunod na henerasyon.","translation":"Traditions should be **passed down** to the next generation."}]

meaning_filipino: Hilahin o unatin ang isang bagay upang ito ay tumigas, lumapad, o humaba.
original_explanation: The official term for what you do to a bedsheet to get rid of the wrinkles. It's also what your gym instructor tells you to do to your muscles before a workout. Figuratively, it's what you do to your budget before payday, or how you try to connect two distant points in your alibi. 'Banatin mo 'yang kwento mo, 'di kapanipaniwala.'
usage_notes: Can be used for physical objects (ropes, cloth) or abstract concepts (a story, a budget). Also related to 'bumanat' which can mean 'to hit' or 'to deliver a punchline'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **banatin** ang lubid para maging tuwid ito.","translation":"You need **to pull** the rope **taut** to make it straight."},{"sentence":"**Banatin** mo nang maigi ang kumot sa kama.","translation":"**Stretch** the blanket on the bed properly."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng pagkakahawig o pagkakapareho sa katangian, anyo, o kalagayan.
original_explanation: The OG 'same vibes' or 'same energy' word. You use this when comparing things, people, or situations. 'Katulad ka rin pala ng ex ko, mahilig sa drama.' (You're just like my ex, you love drama.) It's the go-to word for similes and pointing out resemblances, whether it's a compliment or an insult.
usage_notes: Often used with 'ng' (like) or 'ni' (like, for names). The phrase 'katulad ng paraiso' (like paradise) is a common expression.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang boses niya ay **katulad** ng sa isang anghel.","translation":"Her voice is **like** that of an angel."},{"sentence":"Marami kang makikitang magagandang tanawin sa Palawan, **katulad** ng mga lagoon sa El Nido.","translation":"You will see many beautiful sights in Palawan, **like** the lagoons in El Nido."}]

meaning_filipino: Alisin ang buhok sa ulo ng isang tao sa pamamagitan ng pag-ahit; gawing kalbo.
etymology: From 'anit' (scalp) + '-an' (verb suffix indicating action upon an object).
original_explanation: This is what happens when you lose a bet, or when a new ROTC recruit gets their 'welcome to the jungle' haircut. It's the ultimate 'tanggal pride' makeover, the kind of haircut that screams 'I've made some questionable life choices.' Think Britney 2007, but make it Pinoy.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of hazing, military/police training, or as a form of punishment or consequence for a lost bet.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Anitan** mo na 'yang bagong kadete para matuto ng disiplina.","translation":"**Shave the head** of that new cadet so they learn discipline."},{"sentence":"Kapag natalo ka sa pustahan, papayag ka bang **anitan**?","translation":"If you lose the bet, will you agree to have your **head shaved**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan ng hindi pagkibo o hindi pagsasalita, kadalasan dahil sa pagkagulat, pagkamangha, o matinding damdamin.
original_explanation: This is you when your crush finally talks to you and your brain just blue-screens. Or when you see the Meralco bill after a month of non-stop aircon. Zero words. Just stunned silence.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a state of shock or awe. Can also imply a quiet, reserved person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Walang-salita** siyang napatingin sa surpresang handaan para sa kanya.","translation":"He was **speechless** as he looked at the surprise party for him."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng anunsyo, ang buong klase ay **walang-salita**.","translation":"After the announcement, the whole class was **without a word**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bata na nasa pinakamaagang yugto ng buhay, mula sa kapanganakan hanggang sa humigit-kumulang isang taong gulang.
original_explanation: A tiny human whose main job is to eat, sleep, poop, and look cute. They are the official boss of the house, and their crying is the alarm clock you can't snooze. The reason why your Tita keeps asking, 'Kailan ka mag-aasawa?'
usage_notes: Partikular na tumutukoy sa isang sanggol, karaniwang mas bata sa isa o dalawang taong gulang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahimbing na natutulog ang **sanggol** sa duyan.","translation":"The **baby** is sleeping soundly in the cradle."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-aalaga sa isang **sanggol** ay isang malaking responsibilidad.","translation":"Taking care of an **infant** is a big responsibility."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na sinanay at binigyan ng kagamitan upang pumatay o apulahin ang mga sunog, at iligtas ang mga tao.
original_explanation: The real-life superhero who shows up when your "ay, may nasusunog na amoy!" turns into a full-blown emergency. They're the ones you call when things get too hot to handle, literally. Also, the reason why there are big red trucks with loud sirens.
usage_notes: The common term for firefighter in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis na rumesponde ang mga **bumbero** sa lugar ng sunog.","translation":"The **firefighters** quickly responded to the fire scene."},{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang maging isang **bumbero** paglaki niya.","translation":"His dream is to become a **firefighter** when he grows up."}]

translation: to have something fall from; to have a miscarriage
meaning_filipino: Ang hindi sinasadyang pagbagsak ng isang bagay mula sa isang tao o kinalalagyan; sa medikal na konteksto, ang hindi sinasadyang pagkawala ng ipinagbubuntis.
etymology: From 'laglag' (to fall, drop). The circumfix 'ma- -an' indicates an involuntary or accidental action affecting the subject.
original_explanation: This word has two major vibes. First, the clumsy one: 'Naku, **nalaglagan** ako ng barya sa bus!' (Oh no, a coin dropped from me on the bus!). It's when something accidentally falls from you. The second meaning is much more serious and sensitive: it means to have a miscarriage. So context is EVERYTHING. One is a minor inconvenience, the other is a profound loss. Handle with care.
usage_notes: The meaning depends heavily on context. Be sensitive when using or interpreting this word, as it can refer to a miscarriage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nalaglagan** ng pitaka ang lalaki habang tumatakbo.","translation":"The man **had** his wallet **fall from him** while running."},{"sentence":"Isang malungkot na balita na **nalaglagan** ang kanyang asawa.","translation":"It's sad news that his wife **had a miscarriage**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglala o pagiging mas masahol ng isang kalagayan, sitwasyon, o pakiramdam.
original_explanation: This is when things go from bad to worse. Yung 'pagsama ng panahon' right before your big beach trip. O yung 'pagsama ng ugali' ng ex mo after the breakup. It's the universe (or a person) basically saying, 'You think this is bad? Hold my beer.'
usage_notes: Derived from 'sama' meaning 'bad' or 'evil'. Pronunciation stress is on the second syllable, distinguishing it from the other 'pagsama'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ikinababahala ng mga doktor ang **pagsama** ng kanyang karamdaman.","translation":"The doctors are worried about the **worsening** of his illness."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa **pagsama** ng trapiko, nahuli siya sa trabaho.","translation":"Because of the **worsening** of the traffic, he was late for work."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging simple, hindi kumplikado, o hindi nangangailangan ng malaking hirap o pagsisikap.
original_explanation: This is the quality you wish all exams, job applications, and government processes had. The 'chill lang' version of any task. It's when something is so straightforward, even your friend who always asks 'paano?' can do it.
usage_notes: Refers to the quality of a task or concept being easy to do or understand. Homonym of 'pagkamadali' (hastiness).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagulat ang mga estudyante sa **pagkamadali** ng huling pagsusulit.","translation":"The students were surprised at the **easiness** of the final exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga gawain sa loob ng isang tahanan tulad ng paglilinis, pagluluto, at paglalaba upang mapanatili ang kaayusan nito.
etymology: Isang tambalang salita na binubuo ng 'trabaho' at 'pambahay' (mula sa 'bahay').
original_explanation: The work that never ends, has no salary, no benefits, and no day off. Your mom's main job, which she somehow does better than your paid one. The final boss is the mountain of unfolded laundry.
usage_notes: Madalas ding ginagamit ang katumbas na 'gawaing-bahay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit Linggo, napakarami pa ring **trabahong-pambahay**.","translation":"Even if it's Sunday, there's still so much **housework**."},{"sentence":"Tulungan mo naman ako sa **trabahong-pambahay**.","translation":"Please help me with the **chores**."}]

translation: a party game involving grabbing treats from a suspended basket
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng palaro sa mga pagdiriwang, lalo na sa kaarawan ng mga bata, kung saan ang mga regalo o kendi na nakalagay sa isang sisidlan ay ibinababa nang paunti-unti upang agawan ng mga kalahok. Tumutukoy din sa anumang bagay na pinakawalan o binitawan.
original_explanation: The original battle royale. Before PUBG and Mobile Legends, there was the 'pabitaw' at every Pinoy kid's birthday party. A bamboo grid or basket full of goodies is lowered, and it's every kid for themselves. It's the chaotic, glorious, and sometimes tear-filled climax of the party where you learn about competition and the value of a well-timed grab.
usage_notes: The game is also commonly called 'pabitin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsigawan ang mga bata nang simulan na ang **pabitaw** sa birthday party.","translation":"The children shouted when the **pabitaw** started at the birthday party."},{"sentence":"Ang dami kong nakuha sa **pabitaw**, puro kendi at maliliit na laruan.","translation":"I got so much from the **pabitaw**, all candies and small toys."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maputi at malapot na likidong nakukuha sa pagpiga ng kinayod na laman ng hinog na niyog.
etymology: Pinaniniwalaang mula sa pamilyang wikang Austronesian.
original_explanation: The lifeblood of Bicol express, laing, and ginataang bilo-bilo. It's that creamy, dreamy liquid that makes any dish 100x more comforting and delicious. The first squeeze ('unang piga') is the premium, full-fat version, like the director's cut. The second squeeze ('pangalawang piga') is the light, everyday version.
usage_notes: Madalas gamiting magkasingkahulugan sa 'gata ng niyog', ngunit ang 'gata' lamang ay sapat na at mas karaniwan sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap ang laing kapag maraming **gata**.","translation":"Laing is delicious when it has a lot of **coconut milk**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating pigain ang niyog para makakuha ng sariwang **gata**.","translation":"We need to squeeze the coconut to get fresh **coconut milk**."}]

translation: act of putting something in the mouth, feeding
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglalagay ng pagkain o anumang bagay sa loob ng bibig.
etymology: From `pag-` (nominalizer) + `su-` (reduplication of first syllable) + `subo` (put in mouth). The reduplication indicates a repeated or intense action.
original_explanation: The first step in any mukbang video. It's that critical moment when the spoon carrying a perfect ratio of rice, ulam, and sauce finally enters your mouth. For babies, it's putting literally *anything* in their mouth. For adults, it's a more calculated, delicious process. Pagsusubo is the gateway to flavor town.
usage_notes: Can refer to feeding oneself or another person. The simpler form 'pagsubo' is also used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahan-dahan ang kanyang **pagsusubo** ng mainit na sabaw.","translation":"His **act of putting** the hot soup into his mouth was slow."},{"sentence":"Ang ina ay matiyagang ginagabayan ang anak sa tamang **pagsusubo** ng pagkain.","translation":"The mother patiently guides the child in the proper way of **feeding** himself."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtutol, paglaban, o hindi pagsang-ayon sa isang bagay o kapangyarihan.
original_explanation: This is your 'Darna!' moment. It's the feeling of not wanting to get up on a Monday morning. It's the Katipunan fighting the Spanish. It's you saying 'no' to another optional OT. It’s the fight, the pushback, the 'ayaw ko na po'.
usage_notes: The general term for opposition, unlike 'resistans' which is specific to electricity. Can also refer to the body's immune resistance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpakita ng matinding **resistensiya** ang mga mamamayan laban sa bagong buwis.","translation":"The citizens showed strong **resistance** against the new tax."},{"sentence":"Bumaba ang kanyang **resistensiya** kaya siya madaling nagkasakit.","translation":"His **resistance** (immune system) weakened, which is why he got sick easily."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglagay o naglathala ng isang bagay sa social media na natapos na.
original_explanation: That moment of regret after you nagpost something at 2 AM and woke up to a "We need to talk" message from your jowa. It's the past tense of an online action that can have very real-world consequences. "Sana 'di ko na lang nagpost."
usage_notes: A Tagalized verb from English. Simple past tense, indicating a completed action of posting online.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagpost** siya ng \"Thank you for the birthday wishes!\" sa kanyang wall.","translation":"She **posted** \"Thank you for the birthday wishes!\" on her wall."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **nagpost** ng sikreto natin sa Twitter?","translation":"Who **posted** our secret on Twitter?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bantas (;) na ginagamit sa paghihiwalay ng dalawang sugnay na nakapag-iisa na magkaugnay ang diwa, o sa paghihiwalay ng mga aytem sa isang serye na naglalaman na ng mga kuwit.
original_explanation: Ito yung punctuation mark na parang nagsasabing, 'Hindi pa tapos ang storya natin, pero kailangan muna natin ng space.' Parang kayo ng ex mo, may connection pa pero hindi na pwedeng maging isa. Ginagamit sa grammar para hindi magulo, parang 'It's complicated' status sa Facebook.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa pormal na pagsulat upang pagdugtungin ang dalawang malapit na magkaugnay na sugnay na nakapag-iisa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang edukasyon; **tuldok-kuwit**, ito ang susi sa magandang kinabukasan.","translation":"Education is important; it is the key to a good future."},{"sentence":"Nagpunta siya sa palengke upang bumili ng mga sumusunod: mansanas, saging, at ubas; gatas, tinapay, at keso.","translation":"She went to the market to buy the following: apples, bananas, and grapes; milk, bread, and cheese."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking sasakyang pandagat na karaniwang pinatatakbo ng makina, ginagamit sa paglalakbay o paghakot ng kargamento sa karagatan.
original_explanation: The OG GrabCar of the sea. Before Cebu Pacific, this was how your lolo and lola traveled between islands. It's bigger than a 'bangka' but smaller than a cruise ship where you can get a buffet. Think of the Titanic, but hopefully with a happier ending.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakasakay ka na ba sa **bapor** patungong Cebu?","translation":"Have you ever ridden a **ship** going to Cebu?"},{"sentence":"Dumaong ang **bapor** na may dalang mga container van.","translation":"The **ship** carrying container vans has docked."}]

translation: Expenses; budget; something to be spent
meaning_filipino: Anumang halaga, salapi, o yaman na inilaan upang gamitin o gastusin para sa isang partikular na layunin.
original_explanation: This is your "gastos" money. Your allowance, your budget for the 12.12 sale, the cash you set aside for milk tea and GrabFood. When your parents ask "Saan napunta ang baon mo?" they're auditing your `panggugol`. It's the financial fuel for your "deserve ko 'to" moments.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of budgeting and finance. Interchangeable with 'gastos' or 'badyet'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkano ang inilaan mong **panggugol** para sa bakasyon ninyo?","translation":"How much **budget** did you allocate for your vacation?"},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating magtipid sa ating **panggugol** ngayong buwan.","translation":"We need to be frugal with our **expenses** this month."}]

translation: the act of proceeding; continuing; staying
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapatuloy sa isang gawain, pagpasok sa isang lugar, o pansamantalang paninirahan.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `pag-` at sa salitang ugat na `tuloy` (magpatuloy; pumasok; manirahan).
original_explanation: This word has a few vibes. 1) The "go lang nang go" vibe: continuing despite challenges ('pagtuloy sa laban'). 2) The "welcome, come in!" vibe: when someone arrives at your house ('pagtuloy sa bahay'). 3) The "check-in" vibe: staying at a hotel or a friend's place ('pagtuloy sa hotel'). It’s all about moving forward, entering, or staying put.
usage_notes: Ang kahulugan ay nakadepende sa konteksto. Maaari itong mangahulugang 'pagpapatuloy', 'pagpasok', o 'panunuluyan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpapasalamat kami sa inyong mainit na **pagtuloy** sa amin.","translation":"We are thankful for your warm hospitality in **having us stay**."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagtuloy** ng proyekto ay depende sa badyet.","translation":"The **continuation** of the project depends on the budget."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi lantad, nakakubli, o hindi hayag sa paningin o kaalaman ng iba.
etymology: From Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *taRuq 'to place, to keep, to hide'.
original_explanation: Like your browsing history, your 'other' social media account, or where you hide the good snacks from your siblings. It's the status of your feelings for your crush—'di mo masabi, 'di mo maamin. #TagoFeels
usage_notes: Describes a state. The verb form is 'magtago' (to hide).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **tago** siyang galit sa kanyang kaibigan.","translation":"He has a **secret** anger towards his friend."},{"sentence":"Nahanap ko ang **tago** na lagusan sa likod ng aparador.","translation":"I found the **hidden** passage behind the cabinet."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasulatan o dokumento na nagbibigay ng pahintulot sa isang tao na pumasok, lumabas, o dumaan sa isang partikular na lugar.
original_explanation: Your hall pass in school, your quarantine pass during the lockdown, or the VIP pass you wish you had for a concert. It's the piece of paper or ID that says 'Okay, pwede kang pumasok dito, 'di ka trespassing.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong ipakita ang iyong **pases** sa guwardiya.","translation":"You need to show your **pass** to the guard."},{"sentence":"Nakalimutan niya ang kanyang media **pases** kaya hindi siya nakapasok.","translation":"She forgot her media **pass** so she couldn't get in."}]

meaning_filipino: Magbigay ng partikular na pansin o kahalagahan sa isang salita, ideya, o punto.
original_explanation: This is the verbal equivalent of using bold, italics, AND underline. It's saying, "Listen up, this part is important!" Parang 'yung teacher mo na inuulit-ulit 'yung topic na siguradong lalabas sa exam. It's highlighting the main point so no one misses it.
usage_notes: Common in both spoken and written language, from casual conversations to formal speeches.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Binigyang-diin** ng tagapagsalita ang kahalagahan ng pagkakaisa.","translation":"The speaker **emphasized** the importance of unity."},{"sentence":"Gusto kong **bigyang-diin** na hindi ito kasalanan ninuman.","translation":"I want to **stress** that this is nobody's fault."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kemikal na pangkulay, lalo na para sa buhok.
original_explanation: This is what you use when you decide to go from black hair to blonde, or when you're trying to cover up those 'wisdom highlights' (a.k.a. white hair). It's the stuff in the box at Watsons that promises to change your life, or at least your hair color, for a few weeks.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used for hair dye in modern colloquial Tagalog. The more general word for 'dye' is 'tina'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpakulay siya ng buhok gamit ang pulang **tinte**.","translation":"She colored her hair using red **dye**."},{"sentence":"Anong tatak ng **tinte** ang maganda para sa buhok?","translation":"What brand of hair **dye** is good?"}]

meaning_filipino: Nauukol sa o may katangian ng teatro; labis na madamdamin o dramatiko sa paraan ng pagkilos o pagsasalita.
original_explanation: This is your friend who makes a huge scene out of everything. Stubbed their toe? Parang katapusan na ng mundo. Didn't get their milk tea order right? Cue the dramatic monologue. 'Teatral' is being extra, O.A. (overacting), the human version of a teleserye confrontation scene.
usage_notes: Can be used to describe a performance or a person's behavior. Often has a slightly negative connotation of being overly dramatic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **teatral** ang kanyang pag-iyak nang malaman niyang bagsak siya sa pagsusulit.","translation":"Her crying became **theatrical** when she found out she failed the exam."},{"sentence":"Mahusay ang **teatral** na pagganap ng pangunahing aktor.","translation":"The lead actor's **theatrical** performance was excellent."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpunta o pagkilos nang salungat sa direksyon ng agos, hangin, o daloy ng trapiko. Maaari ring tumukoy sa akto ng pagsalubong o pagtanggap sa isang taong dumarating.
etymology: From pag- (nominalizer) + sa- (repetition) + salungsong (against the current).
original_explanation: This is your life when you're late for the MRT and everyone's getting off while you're desperately trying to get in. It's the ultimate salmon move, whether in EDSA traffic or in a crowded mall. It can also be that grand gesture of meeting someone at the airport, like in the movies, running towards them as they exit.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for traffic/currents or figuratively for going against popular opinion. The 'welcoming' meaning is less common but still valid, often in a formal or literary context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagsasalungsong** sa agos ay isang mapanganib na gawain para sa maliliit na bangka.","translation":"**Going against the current** is a dangerous activity for small boats."},{"sentence":"Naging madamdamin ang **pagsasalungsong** ng pamilya sa kanilang OFW na ama.","translation":"The family's **welcoming** of their OFW father was emotional."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng dalawa o higit pang tao na magkakaroon ng pag-uusap o pagpapalitan ng salita sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: This is the dreaded "We need to talk" but in future tense. It can be good, like planning a barkada trip ("Mag-uusap tayo mamaya para sa outing!"). Or it can be serious, like resolving a conflict ("Kailangan nating mag-uusap para ayusin 'to."). It implies a two-way (or more) conversation, not a monologue. It's the verbal equivalent of a group chat planning session.
usage_notes: Future tense of `mag-usap`. Implies a reciprocal action between two or more people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bukas tayo **mag-uusap** tungkol sa mga plano para sa Pasko.","translation":"Tomorrow we **will talk** about the plans for Christmas."},{"sentence":"Kailan kaya sila **mag-uusap** para magkabati na?","translation":"I wonder when they **will talk** so they can make up?"}]

translation: to run; to function (for a machine)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsimulang gumana o gumalaw ng isang makina, sasakyan, o anumang mekanismo.
original_explanation: The opposite of 'ayaw gumana.' It's the sweet sound of your old aircon finally kicking in, the motorcycle starting on the first try, or the WiFi router blinking green again. When something 'umandar', it's working as it should. It can also be used for plans: 'Umandar na ang plano natin!' (Our plan is now in motion!).
usage_notes: Primarily used for machines, engines, and appliances. Can also be used figuratively for plans or processes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **umandar** na ang kotse pagkatapos kumpunihin.","translation":"Finally, the car is **running** after being repaired."},{"sentence":"Hindi **umandar** ang negosyo niya kaya nagsara ito.","translation":"His business did not **function** (succeed), so it closed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kawalan ng balanse sa paglakad o pagtayo; pagewang-gewang.
original_explanation: The walk of shame after a big night out with Emperador. Or how you walk on a moving bus during EDSA traffic. It’s that unsteady, wobbly movement when you're trying your best to go straight but your body has other plans.
usage_notes: Often used in its verb form, 'sumuray-suray' (to be staggering).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halata sa kanyang **suray** na galing siya sa inuman.","translation":"It was obvious from his **stagger** that he came from a drinking session."},{"sentence":"Nawalan siya ng balanse at napahawak sa pader dahil sa **suray**.","translation":"He lost his balance and held onto the wall because of the **wobble**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang magaang pagpalo o pagpukpok sa ulo gamit ang mga buko ng daliri.
original_explanation: The classic 'friendly' punishment from your kuya or your barkada. Hindi siya suntok, hindi rin batok. It's that specific tap on the head that says, 'Gising!' or 'Ano na naman kalokohan mo?' The physical form of 'loko ka talaga.'
usage_notes: Generally informal and implies a light, often playful or disciplinary, tap on the head with the knuckles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binigyan niya ng **kutos** ang kapatid niyang nakatulog sa klase.","translation":"He gave his sibling who fell asleep in class a **rap on the head**."},{"sentence":"Isang **kutos** ang aabutin mo sa akin kapag hindi ka tumigil.","translation":"You'll get a **rap on the head** from me if you don't stop."}]

translation: cheater; adulterer; one who will cheat
meaning_filipino: Isang tao na hindi tapat sa kanyang asawa o kasintahan at nakikipag-ugnayan sa iba.
original_explanation: The human version of 'You are the weakest link, goodbye.' That person who treats relationships like a buffet, sampling everything even when they're supposed to be on a diet with one person. The reason for trust issues and dramatic teleserye confrontation scenes.
usage_notes: Refers to someone who has cheated or is expected to cheat in a romantic relationship. The root 'kaliwa' means 'left', which idiomatically refers to doing something illicit or 'on the side'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bulung-bulungan sa opisina na ang bagong manager ay isang **mangangaliwa**.","translation":"It's rumored in the office that the new manager is a **cheater**."},{"sentence":"Ayokong magkaroon ng reputasyon bilang isang **mangangaliwa** kaya't wawakasan ko na ang relasyon na ito.","translation":"I don't want to have a reputation as a **cheater**, so I will end this relationship."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pag-ihaw ng isang buong baboy sa ibabaw ng nagbabagang uling, karaniwan sa pamamagitan ng dahan-dahang pag-ikot nito sa isang tuhugan.
etymology: mag- (verb prefix) + litson (from Spanish 'lechón', meaning 'suckling pig').
original_explanation: The sacred ritual that signals a major fiesta, Christmas, or a really, really good day. To 'maglitson' is to roast a whole pig until its skin is a crispy, golden-brown armor of deliciousness. It's a team effort that requires patience, lots of charcoal, and an unshakeable love for pork. The result is the centerpiece of every grand Filipino celebration: the lechon.
usage_notes: While it specifically means to roast a pig, it can be used more broadly for roasting other animals (e.g., 'maglitson ng manok').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang pamilya na **maglitson** para sa ika-50 kaarawan ni Lolo.","translation":"The family decided to **roast a pig** for Grandpa's 50th birthday."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **maglitson** kapag umuulan dahil namamatay ang baga.","translation":"It's hard to **roast a lechon** when it's raining because the embers die out."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapatalsik o pagbato ng isang bagay sa malayo gamit ang lakas ng braso.
etymology: From "pag-" + reduplication of the first syllable of the root "ha-" + "hagis". The reduplication suggests a more deliberate or repeated action compared to a simple "paghagis".
original_explanation: This is the act of yeeting something. Whether it's a basketball player's three-point shot, a frustrated person throwing their phone (don't do it!), or tossing garbage into the bin from across the room. It’s the act of making something fly through the air with force.
usage_notes: "Paghahagis" is more common in general use than the simpler form "paghagis".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahusay siya sa **paghahagis** ng bola sa basketball.","translation":"He is skilled at **throwing** the ball in basketball."},{"sentence":"Ang maling **paghahagis** ng basura ay may kaukulang parusa.","translation":"Improper **throwing** of trash has a corresponding penalty."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang paraan ng pagbili kung saan ang kabayaran ay hinahati-hati at binabayaran nang regular sa loob ng isang takdang panahon.
original_explanation: The magic word that lets you own a new iPhone or a 65-inch TV even if you don't have the cash upfront. It's the 'Buy Now, Pay Later' of traditional Filipino commerce. Your wallet might be crying every month, but at least your living room looks great.
usage_notes: Describes the payment method, not the item itself. Often appears as 'binili nang hulugan' (bought on installment).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hulugan** ang motor na binili ni kuya.","translation":"The motorcycle my brother bought is **on installment**."},{"sentence":"Maraming gamit ngayon ang mabibili nang **hulugan**.","translation":"Many appliances nowadays can be bought **on installment**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinaghalong bunga, dahon ng ikmo, at apog na nginunguya, na karaniwang nagiging sanhi ng pamumula ng bibig at lura. Ito ay tinatawag ding 'nganga'.
original_explanation: Lolo's old-school version of chewing gum or vape. It's a mix of betel nut, leaves, and lime that you chew, not swallow. The tell-tale sign is the red-stained teeth and the need to spit constantly. Think of it as a traditional Filipino stimulant.
usage_notes: This is a traditional practice, more common in rural areas and among older generations or indigenous communities. The act of chewing is 'pagmama'. Stress is on the second syllable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig pa rin sa **mama** ang matatanda sa probinsya.","translation":"The elderly in the province are still fond of chewing **betel quid**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa panlabas na bahagi, anyo, o katangian ng isang bagay; hindi panloob. Karaniwang ginagamit para sa mga pangngalang pambabae sa kontekstong Espanyol.
original_explanation: The 'pang-labas' version, but for a girl. Kidding aside, it's the female-gendered adjective for 'external' from Spanish. You'll barely hear this in daily convo unless someone's being super formal or quoting an old text. You're more likely to just hear 'panlabas' or 'external'.
usage_notes: Very rare in modern Tagalog. Usually replaced by 'panlabas' or the English 'external'. Its counterpart is 'eksterno'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kagandahang **eksterna** ay lumilipas.","translation":"**External** beauty fades."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng palitan ng sulat o mensahe sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang tao.
etymology: From 'sulat' (write), with reduplication and affixes to denote a reciprocal action.
original_explanation: Before DMs, Messenger, and email, there was 'pagsusuwatan'. This was the OG long-distance relationship tool. It's the slow, romantic, and often beautifully handwritten exchange of thoughts and feelings. Today, it's the official term for that flurry of emails between you and HR about your leave credits.
usage_notes: Often implies a mutual or reciprocal act of writing to each other. The root 'suwat' is an archaic form of 'sulat'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanilang **pagsusuwatan** ay nagpatuloy kahit sila'y magkalayo.","translation":"Their **correspondence** continued even when they were far apart."}]

meaning_filipino: Gamitin bilang lunas o gamot sa isang sakit o karamdaman.
original_explanation: This is your go-to remedy. It could be the paracetamol for your headache, the Vicks VapoRub your mom insists is a cure-all, or even that 'masarap na pagkain' you eat to cure your sadness. It's the 'use this to cure' verb. 'Ano ang mabisang ipanggamot sa ubo?'
usage_notes: This instrumental verb denotes the instrument or means for the action. In this case, the medicine or remedy used for `gamot` (curing).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang dahon ng bayabas ay mabisang **ipanggamot** sa sugat.","translation":"Guava leaves are effective **to use for treating** wounds."},{"sentence":"Mayroon ka bang perang **ipanggagamot** sa iyong ina?","translation":"Do you have money **to use for** your mother's **medical treatment**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maikli at matalas na tunog na nalilikha sa pagpindot ng isang bagay, tulad ng buton ng mouse, switch ng ilaw, o panulat.
original_explanation: That satisfying sound your ballpen makes. Or the sound of a camera shutter that means 'picture na!'. Or the sound the door makes when your parents get home and you were supposed to be asleep hours ago.
usage_notes: Widely used loanword for the specific sound.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **click** ng pinto kaya alam kong may pumasok.","translation":"I heard the **click** of the door so I knew someone entered."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng takip o talukbong sa ulo at mukha, karaniwang yari sa manipis na tela.
original_explanation: Think of the classic Maria Clara look, or what your lola wears to church. It's a head covering, like a veil or a shawl, used for modesty, protection from the sun, or just to complete the 'santo-santita' vibe.
usage_notes: Often associated with traditional or religious attire.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang babae ay nagsuot ng itim na **kulubong** sa misa.","translation":"The woman wore a black **veil** to the mass."},{"sentence":"Tinatakpan niya ang kanyang mukha gamit ang isang **kulubong** upang hindi makilala.","translation":"She covers her face with a **head covering** so as not to be recognized."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kilos o aksyon na labag sa moralidad, batas, o kabutihang-asal; kasamaan.
etymology: Mula sa `gawang` (isang anyo ng `gawa`, 'act of') at `masama` (bad, evil).
original_explanation: The opposite of your good deed for the day. This covers everything from petty theft to major crimes. It's the 'dark side' of the word `gawa`. Lahat ng bawal, lahat ng kasalanan, lahat ng ikahihiya mo sa nanay mo.
usage_notes: Isang pariralang pangngalan na tumutukoy sa isang negatibo o masamang gawain.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagsisisihan niya rin ang lahat ng kanyang **gawang-masama**.","translation":"He will eventually regret all his **wrongdoings**."},{"sentence":"Ang pagnanakaw ay isang halimbawa ng **gawang-masama**.","translation":"Stealing is an example of an **evil act**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kilos o bagay na nagbibigay ng dagdag na lakas, sigla, o kapangyarihan sa isang tao o bagay.
etymology: From nakapag- (causative, ability) + pa- (causative) + lakas (strength). A complex causative verb form.
original_explanation: That feeling you get after drinking coffee, seeing your crush smile back, or getting your sahod. It's your personal power-up, your life's 'energy drink' moment. Kapag may isang bagay na nagbibigay sa'yo ng motivation, 'yan ay nakapagpapalakas.
usage_notes: Often used to describe things, actions, or even feelings that provide strength, whether physically, emotionally, or mentally.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang masustansiyang pagkain ay **nakapagpapalakas** ng katawan.","translation":"Nutritious food is **strengthening** for the body."},{"sentence":"Ang suporta ng pamilya ay **nakapagpapalakas** ng aking loob.","translation":"The support of my family **strengthens** my spirit."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sangay ng agham na tumutukoy sa pag-aaral ng materya, enerhiya, at ang mga interaksyon sa pagitan ng mga ito.
original_explanation: Ah, 'pisika'. That high school/college subject that made you question your life choices. It's the science of why things fall down (gravity), why your phone charges (electricity), and why your world turns upside down when you see your crush (that's actually chemistry, but let's blame physics for the falling part). It's all about forces, motion, and energy.
usage_notes: Refers to the field of science, physics.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pisika** ay isa sa mga paborito kong asignatura.","translation":"**Physics** is one of my favorite subjects."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan sa **pisika** ang mga batas ng kalikasan.","translation":"The laws of nature are studied in **physics**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng pasta o panapal sa butas ng ngipin upang maibalik ang funksyon at hugis nito.
etymology: Mula sa "pasta" (sa diwa ng panapal) + hulaping "-han".
original_explanation: This is what you do at the dentist's office when you have a cavity. 'Doc, **pastahan** n'yo na po itong ngipin ko.' It's the dental version of 'palamanan'. Parang pagtatapal sa butas sa puso mo, pero ito, sa ngipin lang at may bayad.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa kontekstong dental na nangangahulugang "lagyan ng panapal ang ngipin".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong bumalik sa dentista para **pastahan** ang isa ko pang ngipin.","translation":"I need to go back to the dentist to **get a filling** for my other tooth."},{"sentence":"Ipinapastahan ni Ana ang kanyang sirang ngipin.","translation":"Ana is having her damaged tooth filled."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi mahalaga o kailangan; maaaring isantabi o huwag gawin.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung pagbili mo ng ika-sampung milk tea mo for the week. O 'yung pag-attend sa meeting na "could have been an email." It's extra, it's optional, it's something you can totally live without. In short, di-kinakailangan.
usage_notes: Ang kabaligtaran ng "kinakailangan" (necessary, required).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iwasan ang mga **di-kinakailangan**g gastos.","translation":"Avoid **unnecessary** expenses."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-aalala nang sobra ay **di-kinakailangan**.","translation":"Worrying too much is **not needed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging kuba o pagyuko, karaniwan dahil sa pagod, kalungkutan, o pagtuon sa isang bagay na nasa ibaba.
original_explanation: 'Yung itsura mo after 8 hours of coding or binge-watching a K-drama. Your back is screaming, your neck is MIA, and you're just a human question mark. "Uy, 'wag kang nakayukyok diyan, baka maging Lolo ka agad!"
usage_notes: Often implies a sense of weariness, sadness, or intense focus on something low, like a phone or a book.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Palagi siyang **nakayukyok** sa kanyang lamesa habang nag-aaral.","translation":"He is always **hunched over** his desk while studying."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko si Lolo na **nakayukyok** sa silya, tila malalim ang iniisip.","translation":"I saw Grandpa **stooped** in his chair, seemingly deep in thought."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marahas o hindi makatarungang paggamit ng kapangyarihan upang pigilan, supilin, o gipitin ang isang tao o pangkat.
etymology: From "sikil" (to suppress, to oppress), with the prefix "paN-" and reduplication of the first syllable.
original_explanation: This is some serious Martial Law-level stuff. It's when the powers-that-be actively crush dissent. Think of it as the ultimate 'cancel culture' but with real-world, often dangerous consequences. It's the act of silencing voices, not with a mute button, but with force and intimidation.
usage_notes: Carries a strong, negative connotation related to power abuse and human rights violations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinaglaban nila ang kalayaan mula sa **paninikil** ng mga mananakop.","translation":"They fought for freedom from the **oppression** of the colonizers."},{"sentence":"Ang **paninikil** sa malayang pamamahayag ay isang banta sa demokrasya.","translation":"The **suppression** of the free press is a threat to democracy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng isdang-tabang na karaniwang walang kaliskis at may mga "balbas" o barbels sa paligid ng bibig.
original_explanation: The fish, not the person pretending to be someone else online (though the 'whiskers' kinda look like a fake mustache, lol). This is the slippery, whiskered fish you often find grilled or fried in dampa-style restaurants. A staple in many provincial cuisines.
usage_notes: Refers to the freshwater fish *Clarias batrachus*.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap ang inihaw na **hito** na may sawsawang toyo't kalamansi.","translation":"Grilled **catfish** is delicious with a soy sauce and calamansi dip."},{"sentence":"Mahirap hulihin ang **hito** dahil madulas ito.","translation":"**Catfish** are hard to catch because they are slippery."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagsasalit-salit ng mga materyales tulad ng dahon ng niyog, buri, o pandan upang makabuo ng mga bagay tulad ng banig, sombrero, o bayong.
original_explanation: This is a traditional Filipino craft. It's the art of creating something beautiful and useful, like a banig (mat) or a bayong (woven bag), from strips of leaves. It's like braiding, but on an architectural scale. It requires patience, skill, and probably a good playlist to listen to.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to weaving with hands using wide strips of material like leaves, not thread on a loom (`maghabi`).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marunong si Lola na **maglala** ng banig gamit ang dahon ng pandan.","translation":"Grandma knows how **to weave** a mat using pandan leaves."},{"sentence":"Ang paglala ay isang sining na ipinapasa sa mga henerasyon.","translation":"Weaving is an art passed down through generations."}]

translation: to trade; to do business; to scavenge for junk
meaning_filipino: Sa pormal na kahulugan, ito ay ang kilos ng pangangalakal o pakikipagpalitan ng mga produkto o serbisyo. Sa kolokyal na gamit, ito ay tumutukoy sa paghahanap at pag-iipon ng mga bagay na maaaring ibenta, tulad ng mga bote, bakal, at papel.
etymology: Mula sa salitang ugat na "kalakal" (merchandise, trade).
original_explanation: This word has two vibes. The 'corporate' vibe: kumalakal is to trade stocks or do business deals in Makati. The 'street' vibe: it's what the guys with the kariton do, collecting 'dyaryo, bote, bakal' to sell at the junk shop. Both are about turning something into cash, just on very different scales. It's the art of the deal, Divisoria-style or BGC-style.
usage_notes: Ang kahulugan ay maaaring magbago nang malaki batay sa konteksto, mula sa pormal na komersyo hanggang sa impormal na pangangalakal ng mga bagay na maaaring i-recycle.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Noong unang panahon, ang mga Tsino ay **kumalakal** ng seda at porselana sa ating mga ninuno.","translation":"In ancient times, the Chinese **traded** silk and porcelain with our ancestors."},{"sentence":"Araw-araw siyang **kumakalakal** ng bote at plastik para may pambili ng pagkain.","translation":"Every day, he **scavenges** for bottles and plastic to have money to buy food."}]

translation: to be destroyed; to be shattered; to be wrecked
meaning_filipino: Ang tuluyang pagkasira, pagguho, o pagkapira-piraso ng isang bagay, istruktura, o kahit damdamin.
original_explanation: Can apply to your phone screen after it falls face down on the pavement, a building after an earthquake, or your heart after a painful breakup. It's not just 'sira' (broken), it's total annihilation. 'Yung 'di na kayang i-super glue o i-tape. The point of no return for broken things and broken hearts. "Wasak na wasak, beshie."
usage_notes: Can be used literally for physical destruction or figuratively for emotional devastation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming bahay ang **nawasak** dahil sa lindol.","translation":"Many houses were **destroyed** by the earthquake."},{"sentence":"**Nawasak** ang puso niya nang malamang may iba na ang kanyang minamahal.","translation":"Her heart was **shattered** when she found out her beloved has someone else."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-alis, paglisan, o pagtungo sa ibang lugar. Ito ay nasa pangkasalukuyang anyo.
etymology: Mula sa salitang ugat na 'alis' (leave) at panlaping '-um-'.
original_explanation: It's the 'Bye, Felicia!' of Tagalog verbs. That moment when you're heading out for work, leaving a party, or when your jowa ghosts you. 'Bakit ka umaalis?' is the prelude to many a dramatic teleserye scene. It's the action of going away, happening right now.
usage_notes: Anyong pangkasalukuyan ng pandiwang 'umalis'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umaalis** na ang bus papuntang Maynila.","translation":"The bus to Manila is now **leaving**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan isinasagawa ang pagsasanay sa pag-asinta at pagbaril sa isang target.
etymology: Nagmula sa salitang-ugat na `tudla` ('target' o 'aim'), na kinabitan ng unlaping `pan-` at hulaping `-an`, na tumutukoy sa isang lugar. Ang /t/ ng ugat ay nawala sa proseso.
original_explanation: The place you go to practice your aim, whether it's with a real gun or just NERF guns with your pamangkins. It's where you pretend you're in an action movie, but the only thing you're hitting is your wallet.
usage_notes: Isang teknikal na termino na hindi karaniwang ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpunta ang mga pulis sa **panudlaan** para magsanay sa pagbaril.","translation":"The police went to the **target range** to practice shooting."},{"sentence":"Isang modernong **panudlaan** ang itatayo sa loob ng kampo militar.","translation":"A modern **target range** will be built inside the military camp."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang halaga ng pera na inilalagak sa bangko para sa pag-iingat o upang kumita ng interes; isang paunang bayad para sa isang produkto o serbisyo.
original_explanation: Eto 'yung pera na nilalagay mo sa bangko para 'di mo magastos, or 'yung downpayment mo sa condo na pinapangarap mo. It's the 'I'm serious about this' money, whether it's for your savings account or for reserving that lechon for the fiesta.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa deposito sa bangko, security deposit sa pag-upa, o paunang bayad.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpunta ako sa bangko para maghulog ng **deposito**.","translation":"I went to the bank to make a **deposit**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng isang buwang **deposito** at isang buwang advance para sa inuupahang apartment.","translation":"A one-month **deposit** and one-month advance are required for the apartment for rent."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing isang kaugalian o palagiang gawi ang isang kilos o gawain.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of your New Year's resolution. "Ugaliin mong mag-gym," sabi mo sa sarili mo noong January 1. It's the act of trying to install new software into your personality's OS. It's what your parents tell you to do: "Ugaliin mong magsipilyo bago matulog!"
usage_notes: A command or suggestion to adopt a certain behavior.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ugaliin** ang pagbabasa ng libro araw-araw.","translation":"**Make a habit of** reading a book every day."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **ugaliin** ang pag-eehersisyo para sa mabuting kalusugan.","translation":"One must **make a habit of** exercising for good health."}]

translation: to bless, to inspire, to grant favor
meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng biyaya, pabor, o inspirasyon. Pagpalain ng Maykapal o ng isang may kapangyarihan.
etymology: From ka- + asi + -han. 'Asi' is an old Tagalog word related to mercy or grace.
original_explanation: This is what you hope your boss does to your leave request, or what you pray happens to your lotto ticket. It's like asking the universe, 'Sana all... kasihan.' It's the act of being granted favor, like when the Grab driver actually finds your hard-to-find address without calling.
usage_notes: Often used in a formal, literary, or religious context, especially in the phrase 'Kasihan nawa' (May you/it be blessed).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kasihan** nawa ng Panginoon ang iyong mga plano.","translation":"May the Lord **bless** your plans."},{"sentence":"Sana'y **kasihan** ako ng suwerte sa pagsusulit bukas.","translation":"I hope luck **favors** me in the exam tomorrow."}]

meaning_filipino: Kumain nang sabay-sabay o sama-sama bilang isang grupo. Ito ay ang anyong maramihan ng pandiwang 'kumain'.
etymology: From `mang-` + `kaon`. 'Kaon' is the Visayan word for 'eat', but this form is widely understood and used in many Tagalog-speaking areas.
original_explanation: This is the official verb for "Tara, kain tayo!" when everyone actually goes to eat. It's the plural form of 'kumain'. Think of a fiesta, a team lunch, or a family reunion where everyone descends upon the buffet table. That collective act of chowing down is 'mangaon'.
usage_notes: This is the plural verb for 'to eat'. The singular form is 'kumaon' (from 'kumain'). 'Mangaon' implies a group of people eating. The standard Tagalog plural is 'magsikain', but 'mangaon' is very common and often preferred for its brevity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Mangaon** na tayo sa Jollibee pagkatapos ng trabaho.","translation":"Let's all **go eat** at Jollibee after work."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis at biglaang pagbaba o pagbagsak mula sa isang mataas na lugar o posisyon.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung nangyari sa grades mo noong na-discover mo ang Netflix. O 'yung biglang pagbagsak ng presyo ng crypto pagkatapos mong mag-invest. It's the "weeeeeee... splat!" moment of life.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for physical falling or figuratively for prices, grades, or status.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubaybayan ng lahat ang **pagbulusok** ng eroplano sa karagatan.","translation":"Everyone watched the **plunge** of the airplane into the ocean."},{"sentence":"Nakakabahala ang **pagbulusok** ng ekonomiya ng bansa.","translation":"The **nosedive** of the country's economy is alarming."}]

translation: maid of honor, matron of honor
meaning_filipino: Ang pangunahing abay na babae sa isang kasal, na pinili dahil sa kanyang karangalan at malapit na ugnayan sa nobya.
original_explanation: This is the bride's MVP, her right-hand woman, the Head of Committee for all bridal things. She's the one who plans the bridal shower, calms down the bridezilla moments, and holds the bride's phone during the ceremony. She's basically the project manager for the bride's happiness on the big day.
usage_notes: The female equivalent of the "best man".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bilang **abay na pandangal**, responsibilidad niyang tulungan ang nobya sa lahat ng paghahanda.","translation":"As the **maid of honor**, it's her responsibility to help the bride with all the preparations."}]
related: ["maid of honor","matron of honor","abay na lalaki","best man"]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na naidugtong, naidikit, o na-install sa isa pang bagay o lugar.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'naka-' (nagsasaad ng estado) at salitang-ugat na 'kabit'.
original_explanation: Yung status ng extension cord sa saksakan, o 'yung poster ng K-pop idol mo sa pader ng kwarto mo. It's physically connected. Pwede ring status ng ex mong ayaw kang i-let go, 'nakakabit' pa rin sa'yo.
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang ilarawan ang pisikal na pagkakadugtong o pagiging naka-install ng isang bagay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakakabit** na ang bagong aircon sa aming opisina.","translation":"The new aircon is already **installed** in our office."},{"sentence":"May maliit na papel na **nakakabit** sa pinto.","translation":"There's a small paper **attached** to the door."}]

translation: to become paralyzed; to be crippled
meaning_filipino: Ang mawalan ng kakayahang igalaw ang isa o higit pang bahagi ng katawan, kadalasan dahil sa sakit o pinsala sa gulugod o utak.
original_explanation: A serious term for when someone loses the ability to move parts of their body. It's the medical condition your lola warns you about when you sit on a hot surface and then immediately splash yourself with cold water ("mapapasma ka!"). In a figurative sense, it can mean being crippled by fear or indecision, like when you're so anxious you can't even get out of bed. "Nalumpo ako sa takot."
usage_notes: Can be used literally for a medical condition or figuratively for being immobilized by an emotion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa aksidente, nanganganib siyang **malumpo**.","translation":"Because of the accident, he is in danger of **becoming paralyzed**."},{"sentence":"Tila **nalumpo** ang buong sistema ng gobyerno dahil sa korapsyon.","translation":"The entire government system seemed to have **been crippled** by corruption."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marahas na pagdiin ng isang bagay sa isang ibabaw; o ang sapilitang pagpapakain o pagsubo ng isang bagay sa bibig.
original_explanation: That awkward moment when your tita tries to force-feed you more food at a fiesta even if you're already full. "Hala, sige na, isang subo pa!" Can also mean aggressively pushing your phone charger into a crowded power strip.
usage_notes: Carries a connotation of forcefulness or insistence. It can be about food, or pressing an object into or against something else.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw ng bata ang **pagduldol** ng gamot sa kanyang bibig.","translation":"The child did not like the **force-feeding** of medicine into his mouth."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang **pagduldol** ng matigas na bagay sa kanyang likod.","translation":"He felt the **pressing** of a hard object against his back."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kulay na matingkad na pula, na hango sa tina na nagmumula sa insektong cochineal.
original_explanation: This is a fancy name for a deep, rich red color. Think of the color of a really good red velvet cupcake, a dark shade of lipstick, or the velvet curtains in an old theater. It's not just "pula," it's "pula" with a college degree. It's the color you'd use to describe something as luxurious or intense.
usage_notes: More common as a technical term for color or in literary descriptions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kulay ng kanyang labi ay tila **karmin**.","translation":"The color of her lips was like **carmine**."},{"sentence":"Pininturahan niya ang pader ng kulay **karmin**.","translation":"He painted the wall a **carmine** color."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging matabang o kakulangan sa lasa, lalo na sa pagkain at inumin.
etymology: From `tabang` (bland) with the prefix `ka-` and suffix `-an` to form a noun indicating a quality or state.
original_explanation: The official diagnosis for food that makes you sad. It's that lugaw with no toyo, that coffee that's more water than kape, that sinigang that forgot its asim. It’s the culinary equivalent of a boring movie, a text with no emojis, or a conversation that’s just "K."
usage_notes: Primarily used for food and drink, but can be used metaphorically for something dull or uninteresting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko nagustuhan ang sopas dahil sa **katabangan** nito.","translation":"I didn't like the soup because of its **blandness**."},{"sentence":"Lagyan mo ng patis para mawala ang **katabangan** ng sabaw.","translation":"Add some fish sauce to get rid of the **tastelessness** of the broth."}]

meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng liwanag o ilaw ang isang lugar, bagay, o tao.
original_explanation: It's what you do to a dark room, or what your crush does to your world. "You light up my world like nobody else," sabi ng One Direction. Pwede ring utos ng nanay mo, "Nak, ilawan mo nga 'tong dinadaanan ko, ang dilim!"
usage_notes: The '-an' suffix indicates that the object of the verb is the place or thing being lit. Compare with 'umilaw' (to give off light).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ilawan** mo ang daan para makita natin kung saan tayo pupunta.","translation":"**Light up** the path so we can see where we are going."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **ilawan** nang mabuti ang entablado para sa pagtatanghal.","translation":"The stage needs to be **illuminated** well for the performance."}]

translation: You're the one!; You're the best!
meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyon ng paghanga, pagkilala, o kung minsan ay sarkastikong papuri sa isang tao dahil sa kanyang pambihirang kakayahan, tagumpay, o katangian.
original_explanation: The ultimate Pinoy compliment (or sometimes, sarcastic jab). Your friend graduates summa cum laude? "Ikaw na!" Your officemate gets promoted after only 3 months? "Ikaw na!" You manage to book a Grab on a Friday payday rush hour? "IKAW NA TALAGA!" It's the verbal equivalent of a slow clap and a bow.
usage_notes: This is an idiomatic expression. The tone of voice is crucial in determining whether it's sincere praise or sarcasm.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nanalo ka na naman sa raffle? **Ikaw na**!","translation":"You won the raffle again? **You're the one**!"},{"sentence":"Lahat ng subject, perfect score ka. Sige na, **ikaw na** ang matalino.","translation":"You got a perfect score in all subjects. Okay, fine, **you're** the smart one."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kabuuang lakas militar ng isang bansa, kabilang ang lahat ng sangay nito tulad ng hukbong-kati, hukbong-dagat, at hukbong-himpapawid.
etymology: A compound of 'hukbo' (army) and 'sandatahan' (armed, from 'sandata' meaning weapon).
original_explanation: The whole package deal. The Avengers of the military. This isn't just one branch, but ALL of them combined: Army, Navy, Air Force, Marines. The 'Sandatahang Lakas ng Pilipinas' (Armed Forces of the Philippines or AFP). When you say 'hukbong-sandatahan', you're referring to the entire military might of the nation. The ultimate 'tropa.'
usage_notes: A formal and comprehensive term for a nation's entire military. Often used interchangeably with 'Sandatahang Lakas'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pangulo ang Commander-in-Chief ng **Hukbong Sandatahan**.","translation":"The president is the Commander-in-Chief of the **Armed Forces**."}]

translation: to dare, to be brave, to take courage
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita ng tapang o katatagan ng kalooban sa harap ng panganib, pagsubok, o kahirapan.
etymology: From `mag-` (verb prefix) + `lakas` (strength) + `loob` (inner self). Literally "to make the inner self strong."
original_explanation: This is your "Bahala na si Batman!" moment. It's when you finally decide to do something scary, like confessing to your crush, asking your boss for a raise, or trying the spiciest Bicol Express on the menu. It's the verb form of having "Lakas ng loob" (guts).
usage_notes: Often used to encourage someone to do a difficult or frightening task.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Maglakas-loob** kang sabihin ang totoo para matapos na ang problema.","translation":"**Be brave** and tell the truth so the problem can be resolved."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **maglakas-loob** na harapin ang iyong mga takot.","translation":"You need **to take courage** to face your fears."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpapakalma, pag-aayos ng gulo, o paghahatid ng kapayapaan sa isang sitwasyon o sa pagitan ng mga tao.
original_explanation: The designated "chill ka lang" person in the group. When your friends are fighting over the last piece of pizza or arguing about politics on Facebook, you're the one who steps in to be the peacemaker. It's the verbal equivalent of spraying a fire extinguisher on a heated argument.
usage_notes: Used in contexts of conflict resolution, from small arguments to larger disputes. The verb implies an active role in calming a situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng guro na **magpapayapa** sa nag-aaway na mga estudyante.","translation":"The teacher tried to **pacify** the fighting students."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **magpapayapa** sa kanilang alitan kung pareho silang matigas ang ulo?","translation":"Who will **bring peace** to their conflict if they are both stubborn?"}]

translation: to bump into; to collide with
meaning_filipino: Ang hindi sinasadyang pagtama o pagbangga sa isang tao o bagay habang gumagalaw.
etymology: From ma- (accidental verb prefix) + bunggo (bump, collision).
original_explanation: That awkward moment when you're texting while walking and you suddenly mabunggo a stranger. Or worse, your ex. Pwede ring car collision, "nagbungguan." It's the classic meet-cute trope in movies where the leads mabunggo each other, papers fly everywhere, and they fall in love. Sa totoong buhay, "Sorry po!" lang sapat na.
usage_notes: Can be used for people bumping into each other, or for vehicle collisions. More general than `mabundol`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagmamadali siyang lumakad kaya may na-**mabunggo** siyang matanda.","translation":"He was walking in a hurry, so he **bumped into** an old person."},{"sentence":"Ingat sa pagmamaneho para hindi ka **mabunggo** o makabunggo.","translation":"Drive carefully so you don't **collide with** something or cause a collision."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o pangkat na bahagi o kasama sa isang mas malaking organisasyon o samahan.
etymology: From `ka-` (denoting company or relationship) + `sanib` (to join, to merge).
original_explanation: Your day-one, your ride-or-die in a project or organization. Parang 'yung ka-opisina mong laging kasama mo sa lahat ng team building, from planning to the actual event. Kasanib mo sa hirap at ginhawa... ng corporate life. Or in politics, it's your ally.
usage_notes: Often used in formal contexts like organizations, religious groups, or political affiliations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si G. Reyes ay isang **kasanib** sa aming kooperatiba.","translation":"Mr. Reyes is an **affiliate** of our cooperative."},{"sentence":"Ang kanilang kumpanya ay **kasanib** ng isang malaking international corporation.","translation":"Their company is an **affiliate** of a large international corporation."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahina at tuloy-tuloy na tunog o ugong, karaniwang mula sa hangin, makina, o pulutong ng mga tao.
original_explanation: That sound your old ref makes at 3 AM. Or the collective chismis of your kapitbahay. It's a sound that fills the background, like the hum of a BPO office floor or the buzz of a fly you can't find.
usage_notes: Describes a low-frequency, resonant sound.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naririnig ko ang **hugong** ng mga bubuyog sa hardin.","translation":"I can hear the **buzzing** of the bees in the garden."},{"sentence":"Ang tanging maririnig sa gabi ay ang **hugong** ng hangin.","translation":"The only thing that can be heard at night is the **humming** of the wind."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagbabahagi ng kaalaman, kasanayan, o paggabay sa pagkatuto ng iba.
original_explanation: More than just what Ma'am/Sir does in school. It's your kuya showing you how to play Mobile Legends, your lola teaching you her secret recipe, or a YouTube tutorial explaining how to fix a leaky faucet. It's the transfer of knowledge, whether it's about the Pythagorean theorem or the best way to peel a mango.
usage_notes: While the root 'turo' can mean 'to point', 'pagtuturo' almost exclusively means 'teaching' or 'instruction'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagtuturo** ay isang marangal na propesyon.","translation":"**Teaching** is a noble profession."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang pasasalamat ko sa **pagtuturo** mo sa akin kung paano magluto.","translation":"I'm very thankful for your **teaching** me how to cook."}]

translation: to assign; to post (to a location)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtalaga sa isang tao sa isang partikular na lugar, tungkulin, o gawain, karaniwan sa konteksto ng trabaho o serbisyo.
original_explanation: 'Yung moment na sinabi ng BPO manager mo, 'Ididistino ka namin sa night shift for Q4.' O kaya sa pulis at sundalo, 'Ididistino ka sa Mindanao.' It's like being deployed for a mission, with matching travel allowance (sana).
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa pormal na konteksto tulad ng trabaho, militar, o gobyerno para sa pagtatalaga ng tauhan sa isang lokasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Plano nilang **idistino** ang mga bagong guro sa mga malalayong baryo.","translation":"They plan **to assign** the new teachers to the remote villages."},{"sentence":"Saan ka **idinistino** ng kumpanya pagkatapos ng training?","translation":"Where were you **posted** by the company after the training?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng palma na may mahahaba at nababaluktot na tangkay, karaniwang ginagamit sa paggawa ng muwebles, basket, at tungkod.
original_explanation: The OG material for your lola's rocking chair and the legendary disciplinary tool of old-school parents. 'Pag nakita mo si Nanay na hawak na ang yantok, alam mo nang may kasalanan kang malaki. Now, it's more for that 'tropical aesthetic' furniture.
usage_notes: Refers to both the plant and the processed material or stick.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga upuang gawa sa **yantok** ay matibay at maganda.","translation":"Chairs made of **rattan** are durable and beautiful."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghigop ng likido gamit ang bibig o isang kasangkapan; ang pagkuha at pag-iipon ng isang bagay (tulad ng kaalaman o likido); ang labis na pagpuri sa isang tao para sa sariling kapakanan.
original_explanation: This word has layers, like a good halo-halo. Level 1: Literally sipping your milk tea. Level 2: A sponge absorbing water. Level 3: The most common modern meaning—the "sipsip sa boss" or sucking up to your manager for a promotion. It's the art of being a teacher's pet or an office brown-noser.
usage_notes: The figurative meaning of "sucking up" is very common in modern colloquial Filipino. Context is key to differentiate from the literal meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naubos agad ang juice dahil sa mabilis niyang **pagsipsip**.","translation":"The juice was gone immediately because of his fast **sipping**."},{"sentence":"Hindi maganda ang sobrang **pagsipsip** sa mga nakatataas.","translation":"Excessive **sucking up** to superiors is not good."}]

translation: to doze off; to nod off
meaning_filipino: Hindi sinasadyang makatulog nang bahagya o sa maikling sandali, lalo na kung nakaupo.
original_explanation: That 2-minute power nap you accidentally take on the MRT or during a boring Zoom meeting. Your head starts bobbing, your eyes get heavy... next thing you know, you've 'mapaidlip'. It's the mini-siesta you didn't plan for but your body desperately needed.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to a light, short, and often unplanned sleep. Different from 'matulog' (to sleep) or 'umidlip' (to intentionally take a nap).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa haba ng biyahe, **napaidlip** ang pasahero sa bus.","translation":"Because of the long trip, the passenger **dozed off** on the bus."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang panghalip na ginagamit sa pagtatanong tungkol sa bilang o dami ng mga bagay, tao, o pangyayari na kayang bilangin.
original_explanation: The official question of every family reunion: '**Ilan** na ang anak mo?' (How many kids do you have?). Or when you're ordering food: '**Ilan** po lahat?' (How many in total?). It's the question word for quantity.
usage_notes: Used to ask about countable nouns. The answer is a number. Pronunciation stress is on the second syllable, distinguishing it from 'ilang' (wilderness).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ilan** ang gusto mong pandesal?","translation":"**How many** pieces of pandesal do you want?"},{"sentence":"Hindi ko alam kung **ilan** silang darating sa party.","translation":"I don't know **how many** of them are coming to the party."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaki na nagpapakita ng labis at hindi makontrol na emosyon.
original_explanation: The male version of 'isterika'. Ito yung tito mo na halos himatayin sa tuwa nung nanalo sa PBA ang paborito niyang team. Or yung kuya mong nagwawala kasi nag-lag yung internet habang nasa gitna ng ranked game.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit para sa lalaki. Ang katumbas para sa babae ay 'isterika'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **isteriko** siya sa galit nang malaman niyang natalo ang kanyang pusta.","translation":"He became **hysterical** with anger when he found out he lost his bet."},{"sentence":"Para kang **isteriko** kung makareak sa gagamba.","translation":"You're reacting like you're **hysterical** over a spider."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang inordenang pinunong espirituwal ng isang kongregasyong Kristiyano, lalo na sa mga denominasyong Protestante.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "pastor" (pastol, kura) at Ingles na "pastor".
original_explanation: The spiritual leader of a church, your go-to for guidance, prayers, and powerful Sunday sermons. Sila yung nagpapaalala sa'yo na 'God has a plan' kapag feeling mo 'di mo na kaya ang life. Hindi siya nag-aalaga ng tupa, kundi ng 'flock' or congregation niya.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa isang Kristiyanong lider-espirituwal, lalo na sa mga denominasyong Protestante o hindi Katoliko. Ang katumbas sa Katoliko ay "pari".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aming **pastor** ay nagbigay ng isang makabagbag-damdaming sermon noong Linggo.","translation":"Our **pastor** gave a moving sermon on Sunday."},{"sentence":"Humingi ako ng payo mula sa aming **pastor**.","translation":"I asked for advice from our **pastor**."}]

translation: to collide with; to bump into
meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang pagtama o pagbangga sa isang bagay o tao.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'bunggo'. This is what you do when you're trying to get someone's attention in a crowded mall, so you "accidentally" 'bungguin' them. Or what an angry driver wants to do to the car that cut them off. It implies intent, from a playful nudge to a full-on kamote driver move.
usage_notes: This is the object-focus form of the verb. The actor-focus form is 'bumunggo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **bungguin** ang pader, kakapintura lang niyan.","translation":"Don't **bump into** the wall, it was just painted."},{"sentence":"Muntik na niyang **bungguin** ang poste dahil sa antok.","translation":"He almost **collided with** the post due to sleepiness."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pang-uring pamilang na panunuran na tumutukoy sa posisyong kasunod ng ikaanim at bago ang ikawalo.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're the **ikapito** person in line for the last concert ticket. Or when it's the **ikapito** day of the week, Linggo na, and you realize may pasok na naman bukas. It's the number that screams 'almost there, but not quite'.
usage_notes: This is an ordinal number. The 'ika-' prefix turns a cardinal number (like 'pito' - seven) into an ordinal one (seventh).
