usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa **ikapito** siyang baitang nang manalo sa paligsahan.","translation":"She was in the **seventh** grade when she won the contest."},{"sentence":"Ito na ang **ikapito** kong tasa ng kape ngayong araw.","translation":"This is my **seventh** cup of coffee for the day."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapasya o paghirang sa isa o higit pa mula sa isang pangkat ng mga opsyon.
original_explanation: Ang ginagawa mo sa Shopee, sa Netflix, at sa mga manliligaw mo. The art of decision-making, from 'Ano'ng kakainin natin?' to 'Sino ba talaga, self?'. Madalas, aabot sa analysis paralysis.
usage_notes: Ito ang anyong pautos (imperative) o pandiwang-ugat (root verb).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pili** ka na ng damit na isusuot mo para sa party.","translation":"**Choose** the dress you'll wear to the party now."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **pili**in ang tama kapag pagod ka na.","translation":"It's hard to **choose** what's right when you're already tired."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng gulay na kalabasa na pahaba ang hugis, katulad ng upo.
original_explanation: It's that long, green vegetable that looks like a giant cucumber or a green baseball bat. Your lola probably puts it in soups like tinola or ginisa. It's the cousin of the kalabasa that didn't get the memo to be round.
usage_notes: This term is more common in certain regions. 'Upo' is a more widely used term for a similar gourd.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-ani si Lolo ng maraming **tabayag** mula sa kanyang hardin.","translation":"Grandfather harvested a lot of **long gourds** from his garden."},{"sentence":"Masarap isahog sa miswa ang hiniwang **tabayag**.","translation":"Sliced **long gourd** is delicious to add to misua soup."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-amin o pagpapahayag ng isang kasalanan, pagkakamali, o lihim sa isang pari o sa isang taong pinagkakatiwalaan.
original_explanation: That moment sa confession box, or sa harap ni bes, na finally inamin mo na, "Oo, ako umubos ng huling piraso ng pizza." It's spilling the tea, but with more guilt and maybe some Hail Marys. Or yung pag-amin mo sa crush mo na matagal mo na siyang tinititigan sa Zoom meetings.
usage_notes: Often used in a religious context (Catholic confession) but can also be used for confessing any secret or wrongdoing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **ikumpisal** ang lahat ng kanyang kasalanan sa pari.","translation":"He decided to **confess** all his sins to the priest."},{"sentence":"Bes, may **ikukumpisal** ako... ako yung kumuha ng charger mo.","translation":"Friend, I have something to **confess**... I was the one who took your charger."}]

translation: to have faith, to believe (in God)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng matibay at buong pusong paniniwala sa Diyos o sa isang doktrinang panrelihiyon.
etymology: From 'man-' + 'sampalataya' (faith). 'Sampalataya' itself is believed to come from Sanskrit 'sampratyaya' (trust, confidence).
original_explanation: This is the 'super saiyan' version of 'manalig'. It's not just trust, it's a full-on commitment to a belief system, usually a religious one. It’s the core verb you'll hear in church every Sunday. It’s the spiritual equivalent of betting all your chips on your chosen deity.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in a religious or spiritual context. More formal and intense than 'manalig'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **manampalataya** sa Diyos sa panahon ng kagipitan.","translation":"It is important to **have faith** in God in times of crisis."},{"sentence":"Ang mga **nananampalataya** ay nagtipon sa simbahan para magdasal.","translation":"The **believers** gathered in the church to pray."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang maliit na bahagi o piraso ng isang mas malaking buo.
etymology: Mula sa 'ka-' (unlaping pamilang na nangangahulugang 'isa') + 'piraso' (piece), na mula sa Espanyol na 'pedazo'.
original_explanation: The universal unit of measurement when you want "just a little bit." "Pahingi ng kapirasong cake," "Bigyan mo ko ng kapirasong papel." It's the polite way of saying 'gimme some' without sounding too greedy. It's the opposite of "isang buo."
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang humingi o maglarawan ng maliit na bahagi ng isang bagay. Gumagana ito bilang isang panukat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Humingi siya ng **kapiraso**ng tinapay para sa kanyang almusal.","translation":"He asked for **a piece of** bread for his breakfast."},{"sentence":"Mayroon ka bang **kapiraso**ng papel na pwedeng sulatan?","translation":"Do you have **a piece of** paper I can write on?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaikling katawagan para sa "voice call" o "voice chat," isang paraan ng pakikipag-usap sa pamamagitan ng internet gamit ang boses.
etymology: Acronym for English 'voice call' or 'voice chat'.
original_explanation: Stands for "voice call" or "voice chat." The go-to for gamers ("Tara VC sa Discord!") and long-distance lovers. It's the level-up from a regular chat when typing is too slow or you're too lazy. Also the perfect way to find out if your online friend's voice matches their profile pic.
usage_notes: Primarily used in online and gaming contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mamaya na tayo mag-usap, mag-**vc** tayo sa Discord.","translation":"Let's talk later, let's do a **voice call** on Discord."},{"sentence":"Ayokong mag-**vc**, ang ingay sa bahay.","translation":"I don't want to do a **voice chat**, it's noisy at home."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pook o kalagayan na patutunguhan o kahihinatnan ng isang paglalakbay, gawain, o proseso.
etymology: From ka- + reduplication of the first syllable of the root dating (da) + -an. The form is ka-da-dating-an, which morphs to kararatnan through phonological changes.
original_explanation: It's the "consequences of your actions" but in a more poetic, destination-focused way. It's where your life choices, good or bad, will eventually lead you. Your "kararatnan" could be a corner office, or it could be explaining to your parents why you failed a subject. It's the final stop on the train of your decisions.
usage_notes: Often used in a formal or literary context. It implies not just a physical destination but also a state or condition that one will arrive at.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Walang mabuting **kararatnan** ang iyong masamang balak.","translation":"Your evil plan will have no good **outcome**."},{"sentence":"Ang tagumpay ang **kararatnan** ng lahat ng iyong pagsisikap.","translation":"Success is the **end result** of all your hard work."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o akto ng paglikha ng tunog gamit ang tinig, lalo na sa pag-awit o pagsasalita.
original_explanation: This is the fancy term for your vocal warm-ups. 'Yung "Ma-me-mi-mo-mu" na ginagawa mo sa banyo bago ka kumanta sa videoke or mag-present sa work. It's the preparation para 'di ka sintunado sa "My Way" o mabulol sa harap ng boss mo. The art of making your voice ready for its performance.
usage_notes: A formal or technical term used in music, linguistics, and speech therapy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang tamang **bokalisasyon** para sa isang mang-aawit.","translation":"Proper **vocalization** is important for a singer."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan niya ang iba't ibang teknik ng **bokalisasyon**.","translation":"She is studying different **vocalization** techniques."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking likas na butas o espasyo sa ilalim ng lupa o sa gilid ng isang bundok o dalampasigan.
original_explanation: The OG condo. It's a natural cave, bigger and more dramatic than a 'lungga'. Think Batman's hideout, or where you go for spelunking adventures on a provincial trip.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'kuweba', but 'lungib' can imply a larger, deeper cavern.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May mga sinaunang pinta sa loob ng **lungib**.","translation":"There are ancient paintings inside the **cave**."},{"sentence":"Ginalugad ng mga turista ang madilim na **lungib**.","translation":"The tourists explored the dark **cavern**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng matibay na tela na karaniwang gawa sa lana o bulak, na may pahilis na mga guhit o habi.
original_explanation: This is that tito-core fabric. You know, the material of your dad's old-school office pants or that sturdy, slightly shiny trench coat he never wears. It's the textile equivalent of a reliable, no-nonsense employee who's been with the company for 20 years. Hindi basta-basta nasisira.
usage_notes: Refers to the specific type of woven fabric.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang uniporme niya ay yari sa telang **gabardin** kaya't matibay.","translation":"His uniform is made of **gabardine** fabric, that's why it's durable."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan, katangian, o pangyayari na naglalagay sa isang tao o bagay sa hindi kanais-nais na posisyon kumpara sa iba.
original_explanation: Being the only one in the friend group who hasn't watched the latest K-drama. You can't join the chika. That's the real **desbentaha**. It's anything that puts you at a disadvantage, like being short when playing basketball or having slow internet during an online game.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaking **desbentaha** sa isang aplikante kung wala siyang karanasan sa trabaho.","translation":"It is a big **disadvantage** for an applicant if they have no work experience."},{"sentence":"Nakita niya ang **desbentaha** ng pagiging bunso sa pamilya.","translation":"She saw the **disadvantage** of being the youngest in the family."}]

translation: a hard slap or punch, usually to the head or face
meaning_filipino: Isang malakas na sampal o suntok, karaniwan ay sa ulo o mukha.
original_explanation: This is that sound effect you hear in old Pinoy action movies. *SAPAK!* It's more of a forceful, open-palmed hit than a closed-fist punch (suntok). It's what your mom threatens you with when you forget to do the dishes. "Isa pang sagot, sasapakin kita!"
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malutong na **sapak** ang dumapo sa kanyang pisngi.","translation":"A crisp **slap** landed on his cheek."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pag-aaral o pagsusuri sa pagkakatulad at pagkakaiba ng dalawa o higit pang bagay, tao, o ideya.
original_explanation: The official term for what your tita does to you and your cousins every family reunion. 'Bakit si pinsan mo, engineer na? Ikaw, kailan?' That's an unsolicited hambingan. It's the act of putting things side-by-side to see what's what, for better or for worse. In school, it's a Venn diagram; in life, it's a source of anxiety.
usage_notes: Often used in academic or formal contexts. The more common active form is 'paghahambing' (the act of comparing).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **hambingan** ng dalawang nobela ay nagpakita ng magkaibang pananaw sa lipunan.","translation":"The **comparison** of the two novels showed different perspectives on society."},{"sentence":"Sa **hambingan** ng presyo, mas mura ang bilihin sa palengke kaysa sa supermarket.","translation":"In a price **comparison**, goods are cheaper at the wet market than at the supermarket."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng muwebles na may patag na ibabaw at karaniwang may mga kahon, na ginagamit para sa pagsusulat, pagbabasa, o paggamit ng kompyuter.
original_explanation: The altar where BPO agents, students, and WFH employees offer their souls (and their backs). It's where your coffee mug, laptop, tumbler, and 50 other 'essentials' live. Also known as 'lamesa' but 'desk' sounds more professional, 'di ba? 'Clean desk policy' is a corporate myth for most.
usage_notes: Direktang hiram na salita mula sa Ingles. Ang 'lamesa' ang mas tradisyonal na katumbas na hango sa Espanyol, ngunit ang 'desk' ay laganap sa konteksto ng opisina at paaralan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-ayos ng mga gamit sa **desk** mo.","translation":"Please organize the things on your **desk**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang daliri sa pagitan ng hinlalaki at ng gitnang daliri, na karaniwang ginagamit sa pagturo.
original_explanation: This is your "pointing finger." The one you use to pick your ulam at a carinderia, to press elevator buttons, and to accuse your sibling of eating the last piece of chocolate. It's literally the "pointing-pointing" finger.
usage_notes: Isang kolokyal o deskriptibong termino para sa hintuturo. Ang mas pormal na termino ay 'hintuturo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May hiwa ang kanyang **turuturo** kaya nilagyan niya ito ng band-aid.","translation":"He has a cut on his **index finger** so he put a band-aid on it."},{"sentence":"Itinaas niya ang kanyang **turuturo** upang magtanong sa klase.","translation":"She raised her **index finger** to ask a question in class."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga alagang ibon, tulad ng manok, pabo, bibe, at gansa, na inaalagaan para sa kanilang itlog o karne.
original_explanation: Basically, anything with feathers that you can raise in your backyard and eventually becomes tinola or fried chicken. It's the category your Jollibee Chickenjoy and the eggs for your breakfast silog belong to. The industry that keeps our cravings for 'manok' satisfied.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa mga kontekstong pang-agrikultura, pangnegosyo, at sa pagluluto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang naging epekto ng bird flu sa industriya ng **poltri**.","translation":"The bird flu had a huge effect on the **poultry** industry."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan, karaniwang ginagamit sa mga seremonyang panrelihiyon, para sa pagwiwisik ng banal na tubig.
original_explanation: This is the tool the priest uses to splash holy water on you during Mass or a house blessing. It's like a pangwilig but with holy intentions. Think of it as a holy water dispenser.
usage_notes: Mahigpit na nauugnay sa mga ritwal ng relihiyon (partikular sa Katolisismo). Ang "wisik" ay nagpapahiwatig ng pagtalsik, habang ang "wilig" ay maaaring mas pangkalahatang pag-spray o pagwiwisik.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hawak ng pari ang **pangwisik** na isasawsaw sa bendita.","translation":"The priest is holding the **aspergillum** to be dipped in holy water."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang isang palaspas bilang **pangwisik** ng tubig sa mga tao.","translation":"He used a palm frond as something **for sprinkling** water on the people."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng nagmula o mamamayan ng Espanya; tumutukoy sa anumang bagay na nauugnay sa babaeng Espanyol.
original_explanation: Ito yung counterpart ni Zorro, ang babaeng galing sa Spain. If a guy from Spain is 'Espanyol', a girl is **Espanyola**. Pwede ring adjective, like 'sayaw na Espanyola' (a Spanish dance). Think of flamenco dancers or Penélope Cruz.
usage_notes: Ang "Espanyol" ay para sa lalaki o pangkalahatan, habang ang "Espanyola" ay para lamang sa babae. Ang "Kastila" ay isang neutral na alternatibo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang magandang **Espanyola** ang bumisita sa aming bayan.","translation":"A beautiful **Spanish woman** visited our town."},{"sentence":"Hinahangaan niya ang mga katangiang **Espanyola** ng kanyang lola.","translation":"He admires the **Spanish** traits of his grandmother."}]

translation: to make (someone/something) move back; to cause to retreat
meaning_filipino: Pilitin o utusan ang isang tao o bagay na umatras o bumalik sa pinanggalingan.
etymology: From `pa-` (causative prefix) + `urong` (retreat, move back) + `-in` (object focus suffix).
original_explanation: 'Yung sinisigaw ng nanay mo sa tatay mo habang nagpa-park ng kotse: "Sige pa, atras pa! Ay, 'wag masyado, paurungin mo pa konti!" It's to make something go backward. Pwede ring gamitin sa arguments: when you present facts, you can make your opponent's weak argument retreat. Checkmate.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for physical movement or figuratively for arguments, plans, or progress.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Paurungin** mo nang kaunti ang sasakyan para magkasya ang motor.","translation":"**Move** the car **back** a little so the motorcycle can fit."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpapatalo; huwag kang hahayaang **paurungin** ka nila sa iyong mga prinsipyo.","translation":"Don't be defeated; don't let them **make you retreat** from your principles."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking yunit ng militar na binubuo ng ilang kompanya ng mga sundalo.
original_explanation: This is a whole squad, but make it military-grade. A battalion is a large group of soldiers. In modern slang, you might say your barkada is a "batalyon" when you roll deep into a party or a milk tea shop. "Dumating ang buong batalyon ni Jessica."
usage_notes: Primarily a military term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinamumunuan ng isang tenyente koronel ang buong **batalyon**.","translation":"A lieutenant colonel commands the entire **battalion**."},{"sentence":"Ipinadala ang isang **batalyon** ng mga marino sa lugar ng sakuna.","translation":"A **battalion** of marines was sent to the disaster area."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga katawang pangkalawakan na kumikinang at nakikita sa kalangitan sa gabi.
original_explanation: 'Yung mga kumukutitap sa langit 'pag gabi. Perfect for romantic stargazing dates or for when you're feeling poetic and deep. 'Look at the stars, look how they shine for you...' - Coldplay, probably while stuck in EDSA traffic.
usage_notes: The native word 'bituin' is more common, but 'stars' is also widely understood and used, especially in songs and poetic contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang daming **stars** sa langit ngayong gabi.","translation":"There are so many **stars** in the sky tonight."},{"sentence":"Nakahiga lang kami sa damuhan habang pinapanood ang mga **stars**.","translation":"We were just lying on the grass while watching the **stars**."}]

translation: to trace; to follow a path
meaning_filipino: Ang maingat na pagsunod sa isang bakas, landas, o gabay upang marating ang isang patutunguhan o matuklasan ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you're tracking your Shopee order online, following its every move. It's also what historians do when they trace our ancestors' story. Basically, you're being a detective following the clues, whether it's for a package or your family tree.
usage_notes: A formal and literary word for 'to follow' or 'to trace'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng mga pulis na **tumalunton** sa mga yapak ng magnanakaw.","translation":"The police tried **to trace** the footsteps of the thief."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang akronim para sa "not my type," na ginagamit upang ipahayag na ang isang tao ay hindi ang tipo o uri na gusto o hinahanap.
etymology: Acronym from the English phrase "not my type".
original_explanation: Acronym for "Not My Type." The polite (or sometimes not-so-polite) way of saying "pass." When your tita tries to set you up with her friend's anak, and you just whisper to your cousin, "**notp** talaga, besh." It’s the ultimate friendzone-level rejection without saying a full sentence.
usage_notes: Primarily used in informal, online, or spoken conversations, especially among younger people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gwapo siya, pero **notp** ko, masyadong mayabang.","translation":"He's handsome, but **not my type**, he's too arrogant."},{"sentence":"Sinabi niya sa akin na **notp** daw ako. Saklap.","translation":"She told me I'm **not her type**. How painful."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na sasakyang may dalawa o apat na gulong, karaniwang itinutulak o hinihila ng tao o hayop, para sa paghakot ng mga bagay.
original_explanation: 'Yung wooden pushcart na gamit sa palengke para buhatin yung isang sakong bigas at tatlong kilong galunggong na pinamili mo. Sa construction, ito 'yung wheelbarrow. Basically, the OG "add to cart."
usage_notes: Madalas makita sa mga palengke, konstruksyon, at bukid.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng mga gulay ang **kareta** na tulak-tulak ng magsasaka.","translation":"The **cart** being pushed by the farmer is full of vegetables."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang magalang na tawag o pantukoy sa isang babaeng may-asawa, mas matanda, o may mataas na katungkulan.
original_explanation: The formal, somewhat intimidating title for the matriarch, the boss lady, or the rich tita who gives the biggest aguinaldo. If you see her in a teleserye, she probably owns a hacienda and has a signature slap. 'Magandang umaga po, Senyora.' You say this with respect, and maybe a little bit of fear.
usage_notes: Always capitalized when used as a title before a name (e.g., Senyora Cruz). It implies respect and formality. The male equivalent is "Senyor".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumating na po ang bisita ninyo, **Senyora** Imperial.","translation":"Your guest has arrived, **Madam** Imperial."},{"sentence":"Ang **Senyora** ng bahay ang nag-utos na ihanda ang piging.","translation":"The **lady** of the house ordered the feast to be prepared."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pulbos na mula sa inihaw at giniling na mga buto ng kakaw, na ginagamit sa paggawa ng tsokolate.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'cacao', na mula sa Nahuatl na 'cacahuatl'.
original_explanation: Yung aamoy-amuyin mo tuwing malamig ang Pasko habang nakabalot sa kumot. Instant pampasaya, lalo na kung may kasamang pandesal. Partner ng puto bumbong sa Simbang Gabi.
usage_notes: Ang 'cocoa' ay karaniwang tumutukoy sa pulbos, habang ang 'kakaw' ay sa puno o bunga.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko ng mainit na **cocoa** ngayong gabi.","translation":"I want hot **cocoa** tonight."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang **cocoa** na galing sa Davao.","translation":"The **cocoa** from Davao is delicious."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggawa ng isang bagay sa mas mabilis na paraan; ang pag-apura. Ito ay nasa aspektong panghinaharap ng pandiwa.
original_explanation: This is the default setting for anyone commuting in Metro Manila during rush hour. It's the "future tense" of being late. "Magmamadali ako" is what you tell your boss when you're still at home fixing your hair 15 minutes before the meeting. It's the promise to rush, which may or may not actually happen.
usage_notes: This is the future/contemplative aspect of the verb 'magmadali'. The present tense is 'nagmamadali' (is rushing).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magmamadali** akong umuwi para maabutan ang paborito kong palabas.","translation":"I **will hurry** home to catch my favorite show."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magmamadali** sa pagsagot para hindi ka magkamali.","translation":"Don't **rush** your answer so you won't make a mistake."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang programa o proyekto na naglalayong magbigay ng tirahan, karaniwan para sa mga nangangailangan o walang sapat na kakayahan.
etymology: From 'pa-' + 'bahay' (house). Literally, 'for housing' or 'to cause to have a house.'
original_explanation: Ito 'yung project ng gobyerno or NGO na nagbibigay ng bahay at lupa, usually sa mga nasalanta ng bagyo o sa urban poor. Parang 'Pimp My Ride' pero imbes na kotse, bahay. Minsan, ito rin 'yung 'housing loan' mo sa Pag-IBIG na pinagdadasal mong ma-approve.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatanggap sila ng tulong na **pabahay** mula sa gobyerno.","translation":"They received **housing** assistance from the government."},{"sentence":"Maraming pamilya ang umaasa sa proyektong **pabahay** ng LGU.","translation":"Many families are hoping for the LGU's **housing project**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga araw ng Sabado at Linggo, ang katapusan ng sanlinggo ng pagtatrabaho at karaniwang panahon ng pahinga.
original_explanation: The holy grail. Ang pinakahihintay na 48 hours para mag-laundry, maglinis ng bahay, matulog, gumala, o mag-marathon ng K-drama. Usually ends with "Shet, Lunes na bukas."
usage_notes: Isang napakakaraniwang loanword sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Anong plano mo sa **weekend**?","translation":"What are your plans for the **weekend**?"},{"sentence":"Magkita tayo sa **weekend** para magkape.","translation":"Let's meet on the **weekend** for coffee."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pampublikong pagdiriwang o liwasan na may mga rides, palaro, at mga tindahan, karaniwang idinaraos tuwing may pista.
original_explanation: The OG Star City. Where you ride a rusty Ferris wheel, try to win a giant stuffed toy by shooting hoops (and fail), and eat questionably-colored street food. It's the highlight of every provincial fiesta. That temporary, magical, and slightly sketchy place of fun.
usage_notes: A staple of Filipino town fiestas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumunta kami sa **perya** para sumakay sa Ferris wheel.","translation":"We went to the **fair** to ride the Ferris wheel."},{"sentence":"Nanonood ng 'beto-beto' ang mga tatay sa isang sulok ng **perya**.","translation":"The fathers are watching 'beto-beto' (a dice game) in a corner of the **carnival**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang pampalangaw na ginagamit sa pagtawag sa isang batang babae o dalaga, na maaaring anak o hindi. Katumbas ng 'hija' sa Espanyol.
original_explanation: This is what your lola, tita, or any random older person calls you if you're a girl. It's the Pinoy version of 'dear' or 'honey' for a younger female. 'Kumain ka na ba, iha?' is the official sound of a Filipino household.
usage_notes: A term of endearment or a polite way for an older person to address a younger female.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Iha**, mag-ingat ka sa iyong pag-uwi.","translation":"**Dear**, be careful on your way home."},{"sentence":"Tinanong ng matanda, 'Ano ang pangalan mo, **iha**?'","translation":"The old woman asked, 'What is your name, **young lady**?'"}]

meaning_filipino: Masakit o mapanirang pananalita; paghamak o pag-insulto sa isang tao gamit ang mga salita.
original_explanation: This is what happens when a "friendly" argument turns into a full-blown bardagulan. It's the verbal ammo, the hurtful words thrown like knives. Think of a teleserye confrontation scene where someone gets called "walang utang na loob." That's peak alimura. Verb form: `alimurahin`.
usage_notes: A strong term for verbal insults. The verb 'alimurahin' means 'to insult or scorn someone'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya makalimutan ang mga **alimura** na binitiwan ng kanyang kaaway.","translation":"She could not forget the **insults** hurled by her enemy."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **alimurahin** ang kanyang pagkatao dahil lang sa isang pagkakamali.","translation":"Do not **scorn** his character just because of one mistake."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gamot na pampadumi o pampalaglag ng mga bulate sa tiyan.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'detox' before 'detox' was cool. It's the stuff your nanay gives you that results in a very, very productive day in the CR. Also used figuratively for getting rid of bad elements, like 'purging' fake friends from your social media.
usage_notes: Can refer to medicine for constipation (laxative) or for intestinal worms (dewormer).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binigyan ng doktor ng **purga** ang bata para sa kanyang mga bulate.","translation":"The doctor gave the child a **dewormer** for his worms."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mo ng **purga** kung lagi kang constipated.","translation":"You need a **laxative** if you are always constipated."}]

translation: to be able to connect; to be able to attach
meaning_filipino: Magawang pagkabitin o pag-ugnayin ang dalawa o higit pang bagay na magkahiwalay.
original_explanation: This is what you do when your phone charger is too short and you need an extension cord. You "maidugtong" the two. It's also what you do when you try to connect the current chismis to the chismis from last week to see the full picture. It's all about connecting the dots, literally or figuratively.
usage_notes: Can be used for physical connections (wires, ropes) or for abstract connections (stories, ideas).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng isa pang mesa para **maidugtong** dito.","translation":"We need another table **to attach** to this one."},{"sentence":"Subukan mong **maidugtong** ang mga pangyayari para maintindihan natin ang kwento.","translation":"Try **to connect** the events so we can understand the story."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubhang kasuklam-suklam o karapat-dapat sa matinding pag-alipusta o pagkutya.
etymology: Reduplication of 'ka-' + 'lait' (insult, scorn). The 'ka-' prefix here implies 'worthy of' and the reduplication intensifies the meaning.
original_explanation: Describes something so bad, it's begging for a roast. Like that one politician's excuse, the plot of a terrible teleserye, or someone who cuts in the LRT line. It's not just bad, it's *roast-worthy* bad.
usage_notes: A very strong adjective used to express extreme disapproval or disgust.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang ginawang pagtataksil ay isang gawang **kalait-lait**.","translation":"His act of betrayal was a **despicable** deed."},{"sentence":"**Kalait-lait** ang serbisyo sa nasabing ahensya ng gobyerno.","translation":"The service at the said government agency is **deplorable**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapatunay o pagpapatotoo sa katangian, kredibilidad, o pagiging maaasahan ng isang tao o bagay batay sa sariling kaalaman o karanasan.
original_explanation: Ito yung sinasabi mo kapag nirerekomenda mo ang isang kaibigan para sa trabaho: "Boss, I can **vouch** for this person. Solid 'to!" Parang pag-endorso sa isang produkto, pero ang produkto ay yung kaibigan mong kailangan ng character reference. Kapag nag-vouch ka, parang sinasabi mo, "Sagot ko 'to. Kung pumalpak 'to, kasalanan ko." High-stakes, bes!
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa mga impormal na usapan, lalo na sa konteksto ng trabaho o pagrerekomenda.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"I can **vouch** for his skills; he's one of the best programmers I know.","translation":"Maaari akong **managot** para sa kanyang kakayahan; isa siya sa pinakamahuhusay na programmer na kilala ko."},{"sentence":"Sino ang pwedeng mag-**vouch** na mabait talaga siya?","translation":"Who can **vouch** that he is really a good person?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, karaniwang lalaki, na hindi makahanap ng romantikong kapareha sa kabila ng pagnanais, at madalas ay nagpapakita ng sama ng loob sa mga kababaihan o sa lipunan.
etymology: Loanword from English, a portmanteau of 'involuntary' and 'celibate'.
original_explanation: Short for 'involuntary celibate.' This is the guy who's perpetually single, not by choice, and blames everyone else for it—especially women. He's the one you see in comment sections typing 'All women are the same' after getting rejected. It's a specific internet subculture that's gone mainstream, and not in a good way.
usage_notes: This term carries a strong negative connotation and is associated with online misogynistic communities.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-aalala ang marami sa pagkalat ng **incel** ideology online.","translation":"Many are worried about the spread of **incel** ideology online."},{"sentence":"Ang pagiging **incel** ay hindi dahilan upang maging bastos sa kapwa.","translation":"Being an **incel** is not an excuse to be rude to others."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga sangkap, lalo na ang mga pampalasa, na ginagamit sa pagluluto upang magbigay ng lasa sa pagkain.
original_explanation: The secret weapons of your lola's adobo. Ito yung mga bawang, sibuyas, paminta, toyo, suka, at kung ano-ano pang magic na inilalagay sa kaldero. Sa chismis, ang rekado ay yung mga juicy, spicy details na nagpapasarap sa kwento. "Ano'ng rekado? Spill the tea!"
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa lahat ng sangkap para sa isang ulam, ngunit mas karaniwang tumutukoy sa mga pampalasa at pampalasa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili ka ng kumpletong **rekado** para sa menudo sa palengke.","translation":"Buy the complete **ingredients** for the menudo at the market."},{"sentence":"Ang sikreto sa masarap na luto ay nasa tamang timpla ng **rekado**.","translation":"The secret to delicious cooking is in the right mix of **ingredients**."}]

translation: to be able to finish; to be able to graduate
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang wakasan o kumpletuhin ang isang gawain, proyekto, o isang antas ng pag-aaral.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `makapag-` (kakayahan) at salitang-ugat na `tapos`.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate goal of every Filipino student and their parents. The dream is to 'makapagtapos' of college and finally wear that toga. It's also the feeling of relief when you finally finish a huge project at work or even just a Netflix series you've been binge-watching. It's all about reaching the finish line.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng edukasyon na nangangahulugang 'makapagtapos ng pag-aaral' o 'to graduate'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsisikap siyang magtrabaho para **makapagtapos** ng pag-aaral ang kanyang mga kapatid.","translation":"He works hard so his siblings can **be able to graduate**."},{"sentence":"Kailan kaya tayo **makakapagtapos** sa proyektong ito?","translation":"When will we **be able to finish** this project?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mabango at kaaya-ayang amoy, karaniwang mula sa mga bulaklak, pabango, o pagkain.
original_explanation: This is the bougie version of 'amoy'. Hindi lang 'bango', it's 'fragrance'. Yung amoy ng sampaguita sa gabi, yung mamahaling pabango ng katabi mo sa MRT, o yung amoy ng bagong lutong pandesal. It's the scent that makes you take a deep, happy sniff.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used for pleasant smells. The opposite would be 'baho'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **halimuyak** ng mga bulaklak sa hardin ay kaaya-aya.","translation":"The **fragrance** of the flowers in the garden is pleasant."},{"sentence":"Naaamoy ko ang **halimuyak** ng niluluto mong adobo.","translation":"I can smell the **aroma** of the adobo you are cooking."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay o sunud-sunod na pag-ngiyaw ng maraming pusa.
original_explanation: The soundtrack to your subdivision at midnight. It's a cat party on your roof, and you're not invited. The sound of multiple cats arguing over territory, food, or love life drama.
usage_notes: The suffix '-an' denotes a collective or simultaneous action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagising ako sa ingay ng **ngiyawan** ng mga pusa sa aming bubong.","translation":"I woke up to the noise of the **caterwauling** of cats on our roof."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lihim na pagkakasundo o pagpaplano ng dalawa o higit pang tao upang isagawa ang isang ilegal, masama, o mapanlinlang na gawain.
etymology: From pakiki- (reciprocal action) + pag- (action noun) + sabwatan (to conspire with). Root is sabwat (conspiracy).
original_explanation: The "Marites" level of teamwork, but for evil. This is when the villains in a teleserye meet in a dark, empty warehouse to plot the hero's downfall. It's what you suspect your officemates are doing when they suddenly go quiet when you enter the pantry. It’s a secret, shady group project.
usage_notes: Always has a negative connotation, implying secrecy and malicious intent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahuli ang mga opisyal dahil sa kanilang **pakikipagsabwatan** upang magnakaw sa kaban ng bayan.","translation":"The officials were caught for their **conspiracy** to steal from the nation's treasury."},{"sentence":"May hinala siyang may **pakikipagsabwatan** laban sa kanya.","translation":"He suspects there is a **collusion** against him."}]

translation: to have two people marry each other; to arrange a marriage
meaning_filipino: Pagsamahin sa kasal ang dalawang tao, kadalasan sa pamamagitan ng pag-aayos ng mga magulang o ibang tagapamagitan.
original_explanation: The verb for 'arranged marriage.' This is what happens in historical dramas when the rich haciendero's daughter is forced to marry the son of another powerful family. You're causing them to become a married couple (mag-asawa). In modern times, it's what your tita tries to do when she introduces you to her friend's 'very successful and single' son.
usage_notes: Causative verb. To cause two people to become spouses ('asawa'). This term is strongly associated with the concept of arranged marriages.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Noong unang panahon, karaniwan na **papag-asawahin** ng mga magulang ang kanilang mga anak.","translation":"In the old days, it was common for parents to **have their children marry** each other."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagmamanman o pag-espiya sa isang tao o grupo upang makakuha ng lihim na impormasyon.
original_explanation: This is the verb 'to spy on someone'. 'Tiktikan mo nga kung ano pinag-uusapan nila.' (Go spy on what they're talking about.) It can also be a noun for the act itself, 'Nagkaroon ng tiktikan sa pagitan ng dalawang ahensya.' (There was espionage between the two agencies). This is what you and your work bestie do to figure out the office chismis.
usage_notes: As a verb, it is object-focus ('tiktikan ang target'). The noun form 'tiktikan' ('espionage') refers to the mutual or general act of spying.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan siyang **tiktikan** ang bawat galaw ng suspek.","translation":"He was ordered **to spy on** the suspect's every move."},{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang **tiktikan** sa pulitika kapag malapit na ang eleksyon.","translation":"The **espionage** in politics is intense when the election is near."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gitnang-gitnang bahagi ng isang target; ang tiyak na pagtama sa isang bagay; ang dulo ng isang kalye na sumasalubong sa isa pang kalye.
original_explanation: When you hit the nail right on the head, that's 'tumbok'! It's the 'saktong-sakto' moment. In street terms, it's the house at the very end of a T-junction, the one Feng Shui experts warn you about. 'Tumbok mo 'yung sagot!' means 'You got the exact answer!'
usage_notes: Can be literal (hitting a target) or figurative (getting something exactly right). Also used in geography/directions to refer to the end of a street that forms a 'T'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa **tumbok** ng kalye ang bahay nila kaya madaling mahanap.","translation":"Their house is at the **T-junction** of the street so it's easy to find."},{"sentence":"**Tumbok** mo ang sagot sa bugtong ko!","translation":"You hit the **bullseye** with the answer to my riddle!"}]

translation: favorite expression; catchphrase; talk of the town
meaning_filipino: Isang salita, parirala, o pangalan na palaging binabanggit o sinasabi ng isang tao o grupo; laging nasa bibig.
original_explanation: Your personal catchphrase. 'Yung linya mo na alam na ng lahat na sa'yo galing, like "sana all" or "charot!" If a person is the 'bukambibig' of the town, they're the talk of the town—for better or for worse.
usage_notes: Can refer to a phrase someone always says, or a person/topic everyone is talking about.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **bukambibig** na niya ang salitang 'ganern' sa araw-araw.","translation":"The word 'ganern' has become his daily **catchphrase**."},{"sentence":"Siya ang naging **bukambibig** sa buong barangay matapos manalo sa lotto.","translation":"He became the **talk of the town** in the whole barangay after winning the lottery."}]

translation: to color; to apply color to
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o paglalapat ng kulay sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is what you do to your adult coloring book to de-stress from your 9-to-5 job. It's the verb form of "kulay." To "kulayan" something is to bring it to life, whether it's a drawing, your hair, or giving a different meaning to a story. "Kulayan mo naman ang buhay ko," is a classic hugot line for someone feeling dull and lonely.
usage_notes: The object receiving the color is the focus. Contrast with 'magkulay' where the actor is the focus.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kulayan** mo ang drowing na ito ng pula.","translation":"**Color** this drawing red."},{"sentence":"Nais niyang **kulayan** ang kanyang buhok para sa Bagong Taon.","translation":"She wants **to color** her hair for the New Year."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, kumpanya, o bansa na nagpapadala ng mga kalakal o serbisyo sa ibang bansa upang doon ipagbili.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'tagapag-' (doer of action) at 'luwas' (to transport goods out of a place).
original_explanation: Sila 'yung mga beshie ng ekonomiya na nagpapadala ng mga produktong 'Made in the Philippines' sa ibang bansa. From dried mangoes to world-class talent, sila ang bahala. Think of them as the nation's official courier for good stuff.
usage_notes: Ang kasalungat nito ay 'tagapag-angkat' (importer).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Pilipinas ay isang pangunahing **tagapagluwas** ng niyog at saging sa mundo.","translation":"The Philippines is a major **exporter** of coconut and bananas in the world."},{"sentence":"Ang aming kumpanya ay naglalayong maging nangungunang **tagapagluwas** ng mga produktong gawang-kamay.","translation":"Our company aims to be the leading **exporter** of handmade products."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang kasiguraduhan; hindi alam kung ano ang mangyayari o kung totoo.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'di-' (hindi) at salitang-ugat na 'tiyak' (sure, certain).
original_explanation: The status of your relationship when they say "I like you" but also "I'm not ready for a commitment." It's 'di-tiyak'. It's that "See you later!" that could mean in 5 minutes or 5 years. It's the ultimate "it's complicated."
usage_notes: Refers to a state of doubt or lack of confirmation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Di-tiyak** kung kailan babalik sa normal ang lahat.","translation":"It is **uncertain** when everything will return to normal."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa **di-tiyak** na panahon, ipinagpaliban ang biyahe.","translation":"Because of the **indefinite** weather, the trip was postponed."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng matapang, malakas, at may kilos na panlalaki; hango sa mga mandirigmang babae sa mitolohiyang Griyego.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "amazona," na galing sa Griyegong "Amazōn," tumutukoy sa mitolohikal na lahi ng mga babaeng mandirigma.
original_explanation: Your gym-rat tita who can lift heavier than your kuya. A tough, no-nonsense woman who isn't afraid to speak her mind or get her hands dirty. Sometimes used to describe a tomboyish or very assertive woman. Think Wonder Woman, but maybe in a daster, running the local carinderia with an iron fist.
usage_notes: Minsan ay maaaring gamitin nang may bahid ng pagmamaliit, ngunit kadalasan ay may paghanga sa lakas at kalayaan ng isang babae.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa kanilang lugar bilang isang **amasona** dahil sa kanyang katapangan.","translation":"She is known in their area as an **amazon** because of her bravery."},{"sentence":"Hinahangaan ko ang mga atletang babae, mga tunay na **amasona** sa kanilang larangan.","translation":"I admire female athletes, true **amazons** in their field."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang indibidwal na lumilikha ng materyal na pang-aliw o pang-edukasyon para sa anumang midyum, lalo na sa mga digital na plataporma tulad ng YouTube, TikTok, o Instagram.
original_explanation: The modern-day *artista*. Sila yung mga vlogger, influencer, o TikTokerist na nagpapakahirap mag-isip ng content para sa views at likes. Pangarap ng bawat Gen Z at tita na 'work from home' lang pero kumikita ng malaki. 'Anak, mag-aral kang mabuti para maging... content creator!'
usage_notes: Isang modernong katawagan para sa mga taong gumagawa ng nilalaman sa internet. Madalas gamitin sa Taglish.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang maging isang sikat na **content creator** sa YouTube.","translation":"She dreams of becoming a famous **content creator** on YouTube."},{"sentence":"Bilang isang **content creator**, kailangan laging bago ang iyong mga ideya.","translation":"As a **content creator**, your ideas always need to be fresh."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sapilitang pagkuha ng isang ari-arian o bagay ng isang may kapangyarihan, alinsunod sa batas o regulasyon.
original_explanation: Remember in high school when the teacher takes your phone for using it in class? 'Yan, *nakumpiska*. Or when airport security takes your oversized bottle of shampoo? *Nakumpiska* rin 'yan. It’s when someone in authority takes your stuff because you broke a rule. The ultimate "lagot ka" moment.
usage_notes: Used in official contexts (police, customs, courts) and informal ones (school, home).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaaring **makumpiska** ang mga ipinagbabawal na gamit kapag dumaan sa airport security.","translation":"Prohibited items may **be confiscated** when passing through airport security."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang ginagamit sa pag-anyaya o pag-aaya sa isang tao o grupo na sumama; katumbas ng "halika" o "tayo na."
etymology: Possibly a colloquial shortening of "tayo na" (let's go now).
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino invitation. It's short, it's punchy, and it means 'Let's go!' or 'Come on!'. It can be a question ("Tara?") or a statement ("Tara!"). The one-word text you send to your barkada that could lead to an epic, unplanned adventure or just a quick milk tea run.
usage_notes: Highly colloquial and common in everyday speech. Can also be used as an adverb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tara**, kain tayo sa labas!","translation":"**Let's go**, let's eat out!"},{"sentence":"Gusto mo bang manood ng sine? **Tara**!","translation":"Do you want to watch a movie? **Let's go**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang propesyon o gawain ng pag-aalaga sa mga may sakit, sugatan, o matatanda, lalo na sa ilalim ng pangangasiwa ng isang doktor.
original_explanation: Ito yung kursong kinuha ng kalahati ng batch niyo nung college, na ngayon ay malamang nasa ibang bansa na at nag-aalaga ng mga lolo't lola. Sila ang mga modern-day heroes na ang superpower ay pasensya at pag-aalaga.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang maging doktor, kaya kumuha muna siya ng kursong **narsing**.","translation":"She dreams of becoming a doctor, so she first took up a **nursing** course."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ama ng ama o ina ng isang tao; isang lalaking nakatatanda na may mga apo.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na "abuelo", na pinaikli at inangkop sa ponolohiyang Tagalog.
original_explanation: The male counterpart of Lola. He's the one who slips you 100 pesos and says "Huwag mong sabihin sa lola mo." He's either quietly reading the newspaper, fixing something that isn't broken, or telling the same story about his youth for the 87th time.
usage_notes: Isang magalang na tawag sa lahat ng matatandang lalaki, kahit hindi kamag-anak.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **lolo** ko ay isang beterano ng giyera.","translation":"My **grandfather** is a war veteran."},{"sentence":"Tulungan mo si **Lolo** na buhatin ang mga iyan.","translation":"Help **Grandpa** carry those things."}]

translation: That's the tea; That's the gossip.
meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyong balbal na ginagamit upang kumpirmahin na ang isang impormasyon ay ang 'tsismis' o ang katotohanang pinag-uusapan.
etymology: Combination of English slang 'tea' (gossip) and a stylized form of Tagalog 'iyan' (that). Popularized on social media.
original_explanation: This is the Gen Z confirmation that the chismis is legit. It's like saying 'Ayan, 'yan 'yung chika!' or 'So 'yun pala 'yon!'. It's the sound of a Marites getting her daily dose of information validated. 'Ah, so nag-break na sila? Tea yarn!'
usage_notes: Highly informal and trendy. Used as a reaction or confirmation of recently received gossip.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sabi niya hindi na raw siya babalik. **Tea yarn**!","translation":"She said she's not coming back. **That's the tea**!"},{"sentence":"So siya pala yung umutang at hindi nagbayad? **Tea yarn**.","translation":"So he was the one who borrowed money and didn't pay? **That's the tea**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng hipon-dagat na may malalakas na pang-ipit na parang sa gagamba o tipaklong, kilala rin bilang tatampal.
etymology: From 'ulang' (prawn) and possibly 'tikatik' (a clicking or ticking sound).
original_explanation: This isn't your ordinary shrimp. The 'ulang-tikatik' is the Manny Pacquiao of the crustacean world. It has claws that can punch so fast they boil the water around them. It's a low-key badass you find in the palengke, sometimes called 'alupihang-dagat'. Handle with care, or you might get a knockout punch from your ulam.
usage_notes: Also known as 'alupihang-dagat' or 'tatampal'. It is a marine crustacean, unlike the freshwater 'ulang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa paghawak ng **ulang-tikatik** dahil matalas ang sipit nito.","translation":"Be careful when handling **mantis shrimp** because its claws are sharp."},{"sentence":"Ginataang **ulang-tikatik** ang ulam namin.","translation":"**Mantis shrimp** cooked in coconut milk was our viand."}]

meaning_filipino: Patungo sa isang lugar na mas mababa; sa direksyong paibaba. Tumutukoy rin sa pagbawas ng halaga, bilang, o antas.
original_explanation: The direction your bank account balance goes after payday. Or the direction you're headed on an escalator going down. It means 'downwards' or 'decreasing.' 'Pababa na ang presyo ng bilihin!' (The prices of goods are going down!) is something we all want to hear at the palengke.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical direction, or a decrease in value, price, or intensity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumakay kami sa elevator na **pababa**.","translation":"We rode the elevator that was **going down**."},{"sentence":"Mukhang **pababa** ang trend ng kaso ngayon.","translation":"It seems the trend of cases is **decreasing** now."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbuo ng isang bagay sa anyong pabilog o pabalumbon sa pamamagitan ng pagpulupot o pagbilot.
original_explanation: The action version of 'rolyo'. E.g., 'Rolyohin mo 'yung banig' (Roll up the sleeping mat). 'Rolyohin mo na 'yang lumpia' (Roll up the spring roll). It's the command you give when you want something flat to become a tube. Parang 'yung feelings mo for your crush, gusto mo na lang i-rolyo at itago.
usage_notes: Isang pandiwang palipat, nangangailangan ng tuwirang layon na irorolyo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Rolyohin** mo nang maayos ang diploma para hindi malukot.","translation":"**Roll** the diploma properly so it doesn't get crumpled."},{"sentence":"Tinuruan niya ako kung paano **rolyohin** ang sushi.","translation":"She taught me how to **roll** sushi."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahan ng isip na bumuo ng mga bagong imahe, ideya, o konsepto na hindi kaagad nararanasan sa pamamagitan ng mga pandama. Ito ay maaari ring tumukoy sa isang pangarap o ilusyon.
etymology: From Old Tagalog, possibly related to Sanskrit 'hrdaya' (heart, mind).
original_explanation: This is your mind's ability to dream, to imagine, to "manifest." It's the "sana all" you whisper to the universe. "Hiraya Manawari" means "may your dreams come true." It's the deep, ancient Filipino version of "The Secret."
usage_notes: A deep or archaic word, now popularized by the phrase "Hiraya Manawari", which means "may your dreams/wishes come true."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawa'y matupad ang iyong **hiraya**.","translation":"May your **vision** (dream) come true."},{"sentence":"Ginamit ng manunulat ang kanyang malikhaing **hiraya** upang buuin ang kuwento.","translation":"The writer used their creative **imagination** to build the story."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi konektado o walang relasyon sa paksang pinag-uusapan o sa isang partikular na bagay.
etymology: Mula sa "walang" (without) at "kaugnayan" (connection), na mula sa ugat na "ugnay" (connect).
original_explanation: 'Yung nag-uusap kayo tungkol sa work deadlines, tapos biglang may humirit ng, "Guys, alam niyo ba kung bakit basa ang tubig?" That's a **walang-kaugnayan** comment. It's a random thought that derails the convo, like a pop-up ad in the middle of a serious movie scene.
usage_notes: Used to dismiss information that is not pertinent to the current topic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang sinabi ay **walang-kaugnayan** sa aming pinag-uusapan.","translation":"What he said was **unrelated** to what we were discussing."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong isama ang mga detalyeng **walang-kaugnayan** sa ulat.","translation":"Do not include **irrelevant** details in the report."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang natunaw at tumigas na materyal mula sa isang kandila.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na 'esperma de vela'.
original_explanation: Yung luha ng kandila. Pagkatapos ng Undas o ng isang romantikong dinner (o brownout), ito 'yung kailangan mong kayurin sa platito o sa sahig. May art form din sa paghulma nito habang nagdadasal sa simbahan.
usage_notes: Karaniwang tumutukoy sa natunaw at tumigas na waks.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa tumutulong **esperma** mula sa kandila.","translation":"Be careful with the dripping **wax** from the candle."},{"sentence":"Puno ng **esperma** ang sahig ng simbahan pagkatapos ng prusisyon.","translation":"The church floor was full of **candle wax** after the procession."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar kung saan pansamantalang nanunuluyan ang mga tao, tulad ng mga sundalo o turista. Tumutukoy din ito sa isang panig o grupo sa isang debate o alitan.
original_explanation: Can be a literal place, like a military camp or a summer camp. But more often, it's about which side of the chismis you're on. 'Nasaang kampo ka? Team Bea o Team Julia?' It's your faction, your crew, your political alignment.
usage_notes: Has both a literal meaning (a physical camp) and a figurative one (a side or faction). The context determines the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtayo ng **kampo** ang mga sundalo malapit sa bundok.","translation":"The soldiers set up a **camp** near the mountain."},{"sentence":"Nahati sa dalawang **kampo** ang mga senador tungkol sa bagong batas.","translation":"The senators were divided into two **camps** regarding the new law."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal at masusing pagsusuri o pag-iimbestiga sa isang bagay o lugar upang matiyak ang kalidad, kaligtasan, o pagsunod sa mga regulasyon.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "inspección" o Ingles na "inspection".
original_explanation: 'Yung moment na biglang darating si boss sa desk mo para tingnan kung nagtatrabaho ka ba talaga o puro Shopee check out lang. O 'yung sa LTO, tinitingnan kung gumagana pa ba 'yung signal light ng motor mo. Judgement day, basically.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa mga opisyal na konteksto tulad ng gobyerno, engineering, at kalusugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng biglaang **ispeksyon** sa pabrika ang mga kinatawan mula sa DOLE.","translation":"Representatives from DOLE conducted a surprise **inspection** at the factory."}]

translation: to be able to reach; to be able to achieve
meaning_filipino: Magawang abutin, makuha, o marating ang isang bagay, lugar, o layunin.
original_explanation: Yung pangarap mong maging K-pop star, maabot mo 'yan basta't 'wag kang titigil sa pagpa-practice ng dance moves sa TikTok. Also, yung sahod mo, sana maabot man lang hanggang sa susunod na petsa de peligro.
usage_notes: Often used for both physical reaching and achieving abstract goals.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **maabot** ko ang mga pangarap ko para sa aking pamilya.","translation":"I hope I can **achieve** my dreams for my family."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko **maabot** ang asukal sa itaas ng estante.","translation":"I can't **reach** the sugar on the top shelf."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng busal o anumang bagay sa bibig ng isang tao o hayop upang pigilan itong magsalita o gumawa ng ingay.
original_explanation: This is the action version of "shush, please." It's what villains in movies do to their captives with a piece of cloth. In modern terms, it's what you want to do to your tita when she starts asking "Kailan ka ikakasal?" during a family reunion. Or when your friend is about to spoil the ending of a series. "Huy, 'wag mo i-spoil, busalan kita diyan!"
usage_notes: Can be used literally (to physically gag) or figuratively (to silence someone).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan nilang **busalan** ang testigo para hindi ito makapagsalita sa korte.","translation":"They tried to **gag** the witness so he couldn't speak in court."},{"sentence":"Parang gustong **busalan** ng gobyerno ang mga kritiko nito.","translation":"It seems like the government wants to **muzzle** its critics."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kilos na naglalayong dakutin, kapitan, o hipuin ang isang bagay o tao.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'hawak'. 'Pwedeng hawakan ang kamay mo?' is the question you ask before you become official. It’s also what the sign says sa museum: 'Please do not touch.'
usage_notes: Ang diin ay nasa ikalawang pantig (ha-WA-kan), na iba sa pangngalan na 'hawakán'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hawakan** mo ito sandali habang binubuksan ko ang pinto.","translation":"**Hold** this for a moment while I open the door."}]

meaning_filipino: Isda na pinatuyo sa ilalim ng araw at inasnan upang mapreserba.
original_explanation: The general term for dried fish, the smelly but beloved breakfast of champions (along with sinangag and itlog - #TuyoSilog). This is what makes your neighbors know exactly what you're cooking. From tuyo to daing to danggit, they all fall under the "bislad" umbrella. It's the taste of the sea, preserved with salt and sun, ready to be fried to a crisp.
usage_notes: While understood in many Tagalog regions, it is more common in Visayan languages. "Daing" or "tuyo" are more frequent synonyms in standard Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap na almusal ang sinangag na may kasamang pritong **bislad** at kamatis.","translation":"Fried rice with fried **dried fish** and tomatoes is a delicious breakfast."},{"sentence":"Nag-uwi siya ng isang balot ng **bislad** mula sa kanyang bakasyon sa Cebu.","translation":"He brought home a pack of **dried fish** from his vacation in Cebu."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng napakatigas na bato, tulad ng batong-pingkian, na ginagamit noong unang panahon upang makalikha ng apoy.
original_explanation: This is the OG power bank. Before matches and lighters, our ancestors used balatok to start a fire. Kiskis-kiskis lang, may apoy ka na. It's the Stone Age equivalent of "May I borrow your lighter?"
usage_notes: A historical term referring to flintstone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit sila ng **balatok** upang mag-apoy sa gitna ng kagubatan.","translation":"They used **flint** to start a fire in the middle of the forest."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o bagay na ginagamit bilang tuntungan o basehan sa paglundag.
etymology: From pa- prefix + lundag (leap, big jump) + -an suffix, denoting a place or device for the action.
original_explanation: Can be a literal trampoline at a kid's party, or the diving board at the public pool. Metaphorically, it's that first job you took that became your 'jumping-off point' for a better career.
usage_notes: Can be a literal object or a metaphorical starting point.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsisigaw sa tuwa ang mga bata habang naglalaro sa **palundagan**.","translation":"The children were screaming with joy while playing on the **trampoline**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbuhat o paglipat ng isang bagay na naganap na. Ito ay nasa pangnagdaang panahunan.
original_explanation: Past tense of bringing something. "Sino nagdala ng chismis?" (Who brought the gossip?). Also used when something had a big impact, like a performance. "Grabe, nagdala talaga si Regine sa concert!" It means she really carried the show, she delivered.
usage_notes: Past tense of "magdala". Can be used for literal carrying or for figurative "delivering" or "making an impact."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagdala** ako ng payong kasi mukhang uulan.","translation":"I **brought** an umbrella because it looks like it will rain."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang pagkapanalo ay **nagdala** ng karangalan sa buong bansa.","translation":"Her victory **brought** honor to the whole country."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na may malawak na pang-unawa, pasensya, at kakayahang umunawa sa kalagayan o damdamin ng iba.
etymology: From Spanish `entender` (to understand). `Mapag-` is a prefix indicating a tendency or inclination to do something.
original_explanation: Ito yung friend mo na kahit ilang beses ka nang nag-rant tungkol sa same ex, makikinig pa rin. Sila yung tipo na hindi ka ijajudge kahit nag-impulsive purchase ka na naman sa Shopee. The human version of "It's okay, valid 'yan."
usage_notes: Often used to describe a desirable trait in a partner, friend, or family member. It implies patience and empathy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Swerte ka kung ang partner mo ay **mapag-intindi** sa trabaho mo.","translation":"You're lucky if your partner is **understanding** of your work."},{"sentence":"Maging **mapag-intindi** tayo sa mga taong may pinagdadaanan.","translation":"Let's be **understanding** towards people who are going through something."}]

translation: to be able to skip or hop about; to start hopping suddenly
meaning_filipino: Biglaan o hindi sinasadyang makatalon-talon o makapag-iskip-iskip, kadalasan dahil sa tuwa, gulat, o sakit.
etymology: From 'maka-' (ability/involuntary action prefix) + 'kandirit' (a little hop or skip).
original_explanation: You know that little happy dance you do when your 13th-month pay comes in? Or when you're walking on hot pavement and you start hopping? That's you about to makandirit. It's the physical manifestation of 'OMG!' or 'Aray!'.
usage_notes: Describes a quick, often uncontrolled, hopping or skipping motion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halos **makandirit** siya sa tuwa nang malaman niyang nanalo siya sa raffle.","translation":"She almost **started hopping** in joy when she found out she won the raffle."},{"sentence":"Nang matapakan niya ang uling na may baga pa, napilitan siyang **makandirit**.","translation":"When he stepped on a live coal, he was forced **to hop about**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na nilikha o ginawa ng sariling kamay o pagsisikap, hindi binili o ginawa ng iba.
original_explanation: The battle cry of every DIY enthusiast and proud parent whose kid made a macaroni frame. It's "I made this!" with a Filipino accent. Whether it's a lovingly cooked adobo or a wobbly bookshelf you built yourself, if it's sariling-gawa, it automatically has +10 sentimental value.
usage_notes: Can describe an object (e.g., 'sariling-gawang keyk') or be the object itself (e.g., 'Ang keyk na iyan ay sariling-gawa ko').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagmamalaki niya ang kanyang hardin na **sariling-gawa**.","translation":"He is proud of his **self-made** garden."},{"sentence":"Mas masarap ang regalong **sariling-gawa**.","translation":"A **homemade** gift is much better."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng bungang-kahoy na may matigas na balat at nakakaing buto sa loob.
original_explanation: The general term for 'nut'. Think kasuy, mani (technically a legume, but we call it a nut), or the ones you see in fruitcake during Christmas. It's what you snack on while watching a movie or what your Tita warns you not to eat too much of, 'kasi mataas sa uric acid.'
usage_notes: Isang pangkalahatang termino. Ang mga partikular na nuwes ay madalas may sariling pangalan (hal. 'kasoy' para sa cashew, 'pili' para sa pili nut).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang kumain ng halo-halong **nuwes**.","translation":"He likes to eat mixed **nuts**."},{"sentence":"Ang food processor ay kayang dumurog ng matitigas na **nuwes**.","translation":"The food processor can crush hard **nuts**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng paggawa ng isang bagay nang walang pag-iingat, pagpipigil, o pagsasaalang-alang sa posibleng masamang resulta.
original_explanation: This is "YOLO" mode but make it destructive. 'Yung nanggugulo sa inuman na parang walang bukas. Or 'yung paggastos ng pera na parang hindi mo pinaghirapan. It's acting without a filter, without considering the consequences. The "bahala na si Batman" attitude on steroids.
usage_notes: Nagpapahiwatig ng kalabisan, karahasan, o kawalan ng kontrol na may potensyal na makapinsala.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinondena ng marami ang **kawalang-habas** na pagputol ng mga puno sa kabundukan.","translation":"Many condemned the **reckless** cutting of trees in the mountains."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **kawalang-habas** sa pagmamaneho ang naging sanhi ng sakuna.","translation":"His **recklessness** in driving caused the accident."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang magiliw na katawagan para sa isang minamahal, katulad ng asawa, kasintahan, o malapit na kaibigan. Hango sa salitang Ingles na "love".
etymology: Reduplication of a clipped version of the English word "love".
original_explanation: The cutesy, jejemon-era term of endearment that refuses to die. It's what you call your jowa when you want to ask for a favor. It’s the evolved form of "love ko ‘to." If your Tita calls you this, she probably has pasalubong for you.
usage_notes: Highly informal and affectionate. Often used in text messages and social media. Can be used for a romantic partner, a close friend, or even a pet.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"\"Uwi ka na, **lablabs**, di na ako galit.\"","translation":"\"Come home already, **love**, I'm not mad anymore.\""},{"sentence":"Hi **lablabs**! Kamusta ang araw mo?","translation":"Hi **sweetheart**! How was your day?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pagkaing Hapones na niluluto sa isang mababaw na kalderong bakal, na karaniwang binubuo ng manipis na hiwa ng baka, tofu, gulay, at noodles sa isang matamis na toyo-based na sabaw.
original_explanation: That fancy Japanese hotpot dish you order on payday or when you're trying to impress a date. It's the one with the sweet-savory broth, thin beef slices, and lots of veggies. Not to be confused with shabu-shabu, which is its more 'dip-and-swish' cousin. It's the "I-feel-rich-today" food choice at the mall.
usage_notes: A direct loanword from Japanese. Pronounced as it is in the original language.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-crave ako ng mainit na sabaw kaya nag-order kami ng **sukiyaki**.","translation":"I was craving hot soup so we ordered **sukiyaki**."},{"sentence":"Masarap isawsaw ang karne ng **sukiyaki** sa binating itlog.","translation":"It's delicious to dip the **sukiyaki** meat in a beaten egg."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng Misa sa tradisyong Katoliko kung saan ang mga bahagi nito, lalo na ang mga panalangin ng pari, ay inaawit sa halip na binibigkas lamang.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'misa cantada' ('inawit na misa').
original_explanation: This is the "musical" version of the Mass. Instead of just speaking, the priest sings his lines like he's in a holy opera. It's longer, more formal, and usually reserved for big fiestas or special occasions. Think of it as the "concert version" of your regular Sunday service.
usage_notes: Isang mas tradisyonal at pormal na uri ng Misa, naiiba sa Misa Resada (recited mass).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **Misa Kantada** ang idinaos para sa pista ng bayan.","translation":"A **Sung Mass** was held for the town fiesta."},{"sentence":"Mahal na mahal ng lola ko ang mga himno sa **Misa Kantada**.","translation":"My grandmother loves the hymns in the **Sung Mass**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang dalubhasa na kinukuhang-payo o opinyon hinggil sa isang partikular na paksa o larangan.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "taga-" (tagagawa) at salitang-ugat na "sangguni" (paghingi ng payo).
original_explanation: The person you pay big bucks to tell you what you already know but needed to hear from a 'professional'. In a barkada, they're the friend you run to for love advice, even if their own love life is a mess. The official 'consultant' of your life's problems.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa mga kontekstong propesyonal, legal, o pampamahalaan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha ang kumpanya ng isang **tagasangguni** sa pinansya upang mapabuti ang kanilang kita.","translation":"The company hired a financial **adviser** to improve their profits."},{"sentence":"Ang pangulo ay may mga tapat na **tagasangguni** sa iba't ibang larangan.","translation":"The president has loyal **advisers** in various fields."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggamit ng mata upang makita ang isang bagay; maaari ring tumukoy sa pananaw o opinyon tungkol sa isang paksa.
original_explanation: The Swiss Army knife of non-verbal communication. Pwedeng "tingin na nakakamatunaw" from your crush, "tingin na nakakamatay" from your mom, or "tingin ng paghuhusga" from a Marites. It's also your opinion, as in, "Sa tingin ko, aabutin tayo ng siyam-siyam dito."
usage_notes: A very versatile word. Context is key to differentiate between 'a look' and 'an opinion'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakatakot ang masamang **tingin** ng ale.","translation":"The lady's bad **look** is scary."},{"sentence":"Sa **tingin** ko, mas mabuting umuwi na tayo bago bumuhos ang ulan.","translation":"In my **opinion**, it's better for us to go home before the rain pours."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang lalaki o sa pangkalahatang bagay na nagmula, naninirahan, o may kaugnayan sa Roma.
original_explanation: The OG. The guy version of Romana. Think gladiators, Julius Caesar, and the entire Roman Empire. If your friend comes back from a trip to Italy speaking with his hands a lot, you can jokingly call him a 'Romano'.
usage_notes: Used for people, language, or culture related to Rome. Can also be a noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang sundalong **Romano** ang nagbabantay sa tarangkahan.","translation":"A **Roman** soldier was guarding the gate."}]

translation: to pray something; to recite a prayer
meaning_filipino: Bigkasin o sambitin ang isang partikular na panalangin o dasal.
etymology: From the noun 'dasal' (prayer), which is derived from Spanish 'rezar' (to pray).
original_explanation: This is the active form of praying. It's not just thinking about it, it's doing it. It's what your lola tells you to do before a big exam, a long trip, or when you've done something stupid. 'Dasalin mo ang rosaryo.' It's the verb form of sending a direct message to G (God).
usage_notes: Used when specifying what is being prayed (e.g., a specific prayer like the Rosary). Contrast with 'magdasal', which means 'to pray' in a general sense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **dasalin** ang 'Ama Namin' bago matulog.","translation":"Don't forget to **recite** the 'Our Father' before sleeping."},{"sentence":"Ano ang dapat kong **dasalin** para sa kaligtasan niya?","translation":"What should I **pray** for his safety?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng patag na materyal na may mga marka, ginagamit para sa mga laro tulad ng ahedres o dama; o ang panel ng mga instrumento sa harap ng drayber sa isang sasakyan.
original_explanation: The battlefield for chess, checkers, or Game of the Generals. It's where family feuds are settled over a game of dama. Also, the dashboard of a car where the speedometer lives and where jeepney drivers put their mini-altars and bobbleheads.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inilabas ni Lolo ang **tablero** ng dama pagkatapos ng hapunan.","translation":"Grandpa took out the checkers **board** after dinner."},{"sentence":"Huwag maglagay ng maraming gamit sa **tablero** ng kotse.","translation":"Don't put a lot of things on the car's **dashboard**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang makina na may umiikot na mga talim (blades) na pinapaandar ng daloy ng tubig, singaw, hangin, o gas upang makalikha ng kuryente o mekanikal na lakas.
etymology: From Spanish `turbina`, which comes from Latin `turbo` ('whirlwind, spinning top').
original_explanation: That giant, majestic pinwheel you see in places like Bangui, Ilocos Norte. They're not just for your IG feed; they're the things that spin like crazy to turn wind or water into the electricity you use to charge your phone and scroll through TikTok.
usage_notes: Primarily used in technical, scientific, or news contexts related to energy and engineering.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **turbina** ng hangin sa Ilocos ay isang tanyag na pasyalan.","translation":"The wind **turbines** in Ilocos are a popular tourist spot."},{"sentence":"Ang hydroelectric dam ay gumagamit ng **turbina** upang makalikha ng kuryente.","translation":"The hydroelectric dam uses a **turbine** to generate electricity."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang pangkusina na may malapad at patag na dulo, ginagamit sa pagbabaligtad, pag-angat, o paghahalo ng pagkain habang nagluluto.
etymology: From Hokkien Chinese 煎匙 (tsian-sî), literally 'frying spoon/ladle'.
original_explanation: That flat thingy you use to flip fried eggs, hotdogs, or pancakes. It's the official weapon of choice for moms threatening to discipline you ('Gusto mo paluin kita ng siyansi?'), but also the magic wand that brings you your perfectly cooked sunny-side up.
usage_notes: A very common household and kitchen term in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gamitin mo ang **siyansi** para baligtarin ang pritong isda.","translation":"Use the **turner** to flip the fried fish."},{"sentence":"Naiwan niya ang mainit na **siyansi** sa ibabaw ng plastic na lalagyan kaya natunaw ito.","translation":"She left the hot **spatula** on top of the plastic container so it melted."}]

translation: to scheme; to plot; to orchestrate
meaning_filipino: Lihim na magplano o mag-organisa ng isang bagay, karaniwang may masamang hangarin.
etymology: From `mag-` + `pakana` (scheme, plot). Unlike others with a `paka-` infix, this word's root is `pakana` itself, which is then conjugated.
original_explanation: The favorite activity of every teleserye kontrabida. It's about masterminding a plan, usually shady, like how to steal the hacienda or frame the bida. In real life, it's what your friends do to magpakana of a surprise birthday party for you.
usage_notes: Often carries a negative connotation of conspiracy, but can be used neutrally or positively for elaborate, secret plans like surprises.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sila ang **nagpakana** ng lahat para pabagsakin ang kanilang kalaban sa negosyo.","translation":"They were the ones who **schemed** everything to bring down their business rival."},{"sentence":"Ang magkakaibigan ay **nagpakana** ng isang sorpresang salu-salo para sa kanyang kaarawan.","translation":"The friends **orchestrated** a surprise party for her birthday."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng sandwich na binubuo ng isang nilutong patty—karaniwang gawa sa giniling na karne—na inilagay sa loob ng isang hiniwang tinapay o bun.
original_explanation: The go-to comfort food, from the 'buy-one-take-one' street-side stalls to the fancy gourmet ones that cost half your daily wage. It's the star of every 'cheat day' and the reason you say 'Diet starts tomorrow... again.'
usage_notes: A direct loanword, universally understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong kumain ng **burger** na may kasamang fries.","translation":"I want to eat a **burger** with fries."},{"sentence":"Saan ba ang masarap, Angel's **Burger** o Minute **Burger**?","translation":"Which is better, Angel's **Burger** or Minute **Burger**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaki at gayak na ilawan na may maraming sanga para sa mga bombilya o kandila, karaniwang nakasabit sa kisame.
etymology: From Spanish 'araña', meaning 'spider', due to the chandelier's web-like or leg-like branches.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'sosyal' lighting fixture. You see this in old churches, fancy hotel lobbies, or in the homes of teleserye villains. It's that giant, sparkly thing on the ceiling that looks like it's worth more than your life savings.
usage_notes: Primarily refers to a chandelier. Can also refer to a type of spider, though 'gagamba' is far more common for that meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kristal na **aranya** sa bulwagan ay napakaganda.","translation":"The crystal **chandelier** in the hall is very beautiful."},{"sentence":"Nanginig ang mga palamuti ng **aranya** nang yumanig ang lupa.","translation":"The **chandelier's** ornaments trembled when the ground shook."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtataas at pagbababa ng mga balikat bilang pagpapahiwatig ng kawalan ng alam, pagwawalang-bahala, o pag-aalinlangan.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'IDK' or 'K.' (K lang) move before it was cool. A pagkibitan ng balikat can mean 'I don't know,' 'I don't care,' or 'Whatever, bahala na si Batman.' It's the physical embodiment of non-committal Filipino energy.
usage_notes: The phrase is almost always used in this full form. 'Pagkibit' alone is less common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **pagkibitan ng balikat** lang ang isinagot niya nang tanungin kung saan siya galing.","translation":"Just a **shrugging of the shoulders** was his answer when asked where he came from."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagkibitan ng balikat** ay senyales na ayaw na niyang makipagtalo.","translation":"His **shrugging of the shoulders** was a sign that he didn't want to argue anymore."}]

meaning_filipino: Dilaan nang paulit-ulit ang isang bagay hanggang sa ito ay maubos o luminis.
original_explanation: This is what you do to an ice cream cone until there's nothing left. It's the act of licking something completely. Your pet cat 'himuhimod' its fur, but you 'hinuhimuran' the last drop of chocolate syrup from the spoon. 'Himurin' implies licking until finished.
usage_notes: This verb has an object focus (-in suffix), emphasizing the thing being licked until it is consumed or clean. Contrast with 'himuran', which focuses on the surface being licked.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gustong-gusto ng pusa na **himurin** ang platito ng gatas niya.","translation":"The cat loves to **lick clean** its saucer of milk."},{"sentence":"**Himurin** mo na lang ang natirang sorbetes sa apa.","translation":"Just **lick** the remaining ice cream on the cone."}]

meaning_filipino: Nauukol sa isang indibidwal lamang; hindi para sa iba; pribado.
original_explanation: This is the 'for my eyes only' folder on your laptop. The 'me time' you desperately need after a hell week. Your secret stash of snacks that you don't share with anyone. It's all about you. When someone asks 'Para kanino yan?' and you say 'Pansarili,' it's the polite way of saying 'Back off, this is mine!'
usage_notes: Emphasizes ownership, privacy, or personal use.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayroon siyang mga **pansarili** na dahilan kung bakit siya umalis.","translation":"He has his own **personal** reasons why he left."},{"sentence":"Ang diary ay isang aklat para sa mga **pansarili** mong saloobin.","translation":"A diary is a book for your **private** thoughts."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang parirala na ginagamit upang bigyang-diin ang pinakamahalagang punto o konsiderasyon sa isang serye ng mga ideya.
original_explanation: This is the mic drop phrase. It's the "And finally, the most important part..." used in speeches, presentations, and parental lectures. "Mag-aral ka, maging mabait, tumulong sa bahay, pero higit sa lahat, 'wag mo kaming bibigyan ng sakit ng ulo." It's the main event, the top priority, the final boss of your to-do list.
usage_notes: Used to introduce the most important point in a discussion or list.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marami akong pangarap, ngunit **higit sa lahat**, gusto kong maging masaya.","translation":"I have many dreams, but **above all**, I want to be happy."},{"sentence":"**Higit sa lahat**, ingatan mo ang iyong kalusugan.","translation":"**Most importantly**, take care of your health."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang punso o lungga, na karaniwang yari sa lupa o buhangin, kung saan naninirahan ang isang kolonya ng mga langgam.
