original_explanation: The original underground society. It's that little mound of dirt you accidentally step on, unleashing an army of tiny, angry tenants. A complex subway system and residential area for ants, proving they're better at city planning and teamwork than most humans.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with "punso," although "punso" can also refer to a termite mound and has superstitious connotations ("tabi-tabi po").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa **bahay-langgam** sa ilalim ng puno ng mangga.","translation":"Be careful of the **anthill** under the mango tree."}]

meaning_filipino: Biglaang paghila o pagbatak sa isang bagay o tao nang may puwersa.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na bigla kang hinila ng kaibigan mo palayo sa ex mong paparating. You were just 'nahiklat' to safety. Pwede ring 'yung aso mong biglang humatak sa tali kasi may nakitang pusa.
usage_notes: Often implies a sudden, forceful, and sometimes unexpected pull.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nahiklat** ang bag ko ng magnanakaw, buti na lang mahigpit ang hawak ko.","translation":"My bag **was yanked** by a thief, good thing I was holding it tightly."},{"sentence":"Bigla siyang **nahiklat** ng nanay niya palabas ng tindahan.","translation":"He was suddenly **pulled** out of the store by his mother."}]

translation: to graze; to brush against; to cross one's mind
meaning_filipino: Ang marahang pagdikit o pagtama sa isang bagay habang dumaraan. Sa metaporikal na gamit, ito ay ang biglaang paglitaw ng isang ideya o alaala sa isipan.
original_explanation: The physical version is that awkward moment in a crowded MRT when you accidentally bump into someone (nasagi). The mental version is when the memory of your ex suddenly hits you while you're listening to a specific song (sumagi sa isip). It's a light, fleeting touch—either by a person or a thought.
usage_notes: The verb forms are key: 'nasagi' (physically bumped/brushed against), 'sumagi' (crossed the mind). The root 'sagi' itself is rarely used alone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-sorry siya dahil **nasagi** niya ang aking kape.","translation":"He apologized because he **brushed against** my coffee."},{"sentence":"**Sumagi** sa isipan ko ang ating mga masasayang alaala.","translation":"Our happy memories **crossed** my mind."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng tela, karaniwang parihaba, na may natatanging disenyo at kulay, na ginagamit bilang simbolo ng isang bansa, organisasyon, o kilusan.
etymology: From Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *bata(bata) meaning banner or flag.
original_explanation: The ultimate symbol of national pride, especially during a Manny Pacquiao fight or a beauty pageant. This is the star of every school's Monday morning flag ceremony. Don't you dare wear it as a costume or let it touch the ground, or you'll get a lecture on patriotism. The most famous one, of course, is the Philippine watawat.
usage_notes: The primary word for 'flag'. 'Bandila' is a synonym, often used interchangeably, though 'watawat' can sometimes feel more formal or patriotic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinaas ang **watawat** ng Pilipinas sa seremonya.","translation":"The Philippine **flag** was raised at the ceremony."},{"sentence":"Ang bawat kulay sa ating **watawat** ay may mahalagang kahulugan.","translation":"Each color in our **flag** has an important meaning."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaikling salita para sa "rekomendasyon"; isang mungkahi o payo tungkol sa isang bagay na mabuti o angkop para sa isang partikular na layunin.
etymology: Pinaikling anyo ng salitang Ingles na "recommendation" o Espanyol/Filipino na "rekomendasyon".
original_explanation: The short and sweet term for "recommendation." "Penge reco ng masarap na kapehan sa QC!" (Give me a reco for a good coffee shop in QC!). It's the modern-day word-of-mouth, crowdsourced from your friends, influencers, or that one "suki" who knows all the best spots. Your 'reco' can make or break someone's samgyup experience.
usage_notes: Kadalasang ginagamit sa mga di-pormal na pag-uusap, lalo na sa social media at sa mga nakababatang henerasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **reco** ka ba na magandang series sa Netflix?","translation":"Do you have a **recommendation** for a good series on Netflix?"},{"sentence":"Salamat sa **reco** mo, ang ganda nga ng pelikula!","translation":"Thanks for your **recommendation**, the movie was indeed great!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging pinipigilan, inaapi, o pinagmamalupitan.
original_explanation: The feeling of being under a micromanager's thumb. It's the theme of every historical Filipino film about colonization. When you have to do a group project but one person dictates everything and takes all the credit—you are the 'siil' in that situation.
usage_notes: A strong, formal word used in contexts of social justice, history, and oppression. Can also function as a noun ('ang mga siil' - the oppressed).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **siil** na mamamayan ay nag-aklas laban sa mapang-aping pamahalaan.","translation":"The **oppressed** citizens revolted against the tyrannical government."},{"sentence":"Ipinaglalaban niya ang karapatan ng mga **siil**.","translation":"He fights for the rights of the **downtrodden**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng opisyal na pahintulot o pag-apruba upang gawin ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: Kapag may "authorized personnel only" sa pinto, ibig sabihin, hindi ka kasama dun. Kailangan mo ng permission, ng go-signal, ng pirma. Kung wala kang dalang authorization letter, hanggang tingin ka na lang sa labas. Basically, may basbas ka para gawin ang isang bagay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tanging mga **awtorisado** na tauhan lamang ang maaaring pumasok sa laboratoryo.","translation":"Only **authorized** personnel may enter the laboratory."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na dumadalaw o bumibisita sa isang lugar o sa ibang tao.
original_explanation: The reason your mom suddenly yells "Linisin n'yo 'yung sala, parating na 'yung mga bisita!" This is the person (or people) you have to be nice to, offer snacks (yung masarap, hindi yung para sa inyo lang), and let use the "special" plates. Whether it's your tita from the province or your crush coming over for a "group project," they are the VIPs of the household for a day.
usage_notes: This is also the root word for the verbs 'bisitahin' and 'bumisita'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maghanda tayo ng meryenda para sa ating mga **bisita**.","translation":"Let's prepare snacks for our **guests**."},{"sentence":"Mayroon tayong hindi inaasahang **bisita** kaninang umaga.","translation":"We had an unexpected **visitor** this morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking instrumentong pangmusika na may apat na kuwerdas, tinutugtog habang nakaupo at nakapatong sa pagitan ng mga tuhod ng manunugtog.
original_explanation: It's that big, classy violin you have to sit down to play. It's got that deep, rich sound you hear in dramatic movie scores or classical concerts. It's the 'I'm sophisticated' member of the string family.
usage_notes: A specific musical term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahusay siyang tumugtog ng **biolonselo**.","translation":"He plays the **cello** very well."},{"sentence":"Ang tunog ng **biolonselo** ay malalim at madamdamin.","translation":"The sound of the **cello** is deep and emotional."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang miyembro ng kapatirang internasyonal na kilala bilang Freemasonry, na may layuning itaguyod ang moralidad, pagkakawanggawa, at kapatiran sa mga kasapi nito.
original_explanation: Sila 'yung mga nasa history books natin like Rizal and Bonifacio. Isang secret society (na hindi na masyadong secret) na may mga cool na handshakes at simbolo. Sa modern times, sila 'yung mga tito na may singsing na may square and compass, at laging may mga charity projects.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa isang miyembro ng Freemasons. Palaging isinusulat na nagsisimula sa malaking titik.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming bayaning Pilipino, tulad ni Jose Rizal, ay kasapi ng mga **Mason**.","translation":"Many Filipino heroes, like Jose Rizal, were members of the **Masons**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga **Mason** ay kilala sa kanilang mga gawaing pangkawanggawa.","translation":"The **Masons** are known for their charitable works."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis at mababaw na paghinga na karaniwang ginagawa ng aso, lalo na kung pagod o naiinitan, na may nakalabas na dila.
original_explanation: The state of your dog after a 5-minute game of fetch. Also you, after climbing three flights of stairs because the elevator is broken again and you're late for your shift.
usage_notes: Used to describe the act of panting, almost exclusively for dogs, but can be used humorously for humans.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-umpisang mag-**halhal** ang aso pagkatapos naming magtakbuhan.","translation":"The dog started **to pant** after we ran around."}]

translation: to scrape; to make a scraping sound
meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng magaspang na tunog o pakiramdam dahil sa pagkiskis ng isang bagay sa isa pang ibabaw.
etymology: Mula sa salitang ugat na "kagaskas", isang onomatopeikong salita para sa tunog ng pagkiskis.
original_explanation: That cringe-worthy sound your chair makes when you drag it across the floor instead of lifting it. Or the sound of your brand new phone's screen after it meets the pavement. That sound that makes your teeth hurt? That's kumagaskas.
usage_notes: Inilalarawan nito pareho ang kilos ng pagkiskis at ang tunog na nalilikha.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumagaskas** ang mga kuko ng pusa sa sahig na kahoy.","translation":"The cat's claws **scraped** on the wooden floor."},{"sentence":"Narinig kong **kumagaskas** ang bumper ng kotse sa pader.","translation":"I heard the car's bumper **scrape** against the wall."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na malinis at libre sa anumang mikrobyo o bakterya. Maaari rin itong mangahulugang hindi may kakayahang magkaanak o magbunga.
original_explanation: When your hands are so clean with alcohol they could perform surgery, that's esteril. Also, what you call a hospital room, a lab, or sadly, a relationship that's not going anywhere and won't produce any... results. It's the opposite of your messy kwarto.
usage_notes: Has two main meanings: 1. hygienically clean, 2. infertile/barren.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **esteril** ang lahat ng gamit sa operasyon.","translation":"All instruments in the surgery must be **sterile**."},{"sentence":"Sinabi ng eksperto na **esteril** ang lupa kaya walang tumutubong halaman.","translation":"The expert said the land is **sterile** that's why no plants are growing."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang halal na opisyal na kinatawan ng isang distrito sa Konggreso o kapulungan ng mga mambabatas.
original_explanation: Your friendly neighborhood politician who shows up during fiestas, hands out calendars with their face on it, and promises to fix roads. Their job is to represent you in Congress, but sometimes it feels like they represent their tarpaulins more. Also known as "Rep."
usage_notes: Bagama't gender-neutral, madalas na isinasalin bilang 'congressman' sa impormal na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nangako ang **kongresista** ng tulong para sa mga nasalanta ng bagyo.","translation":"The **congressperson** promised aid for the typhoon victims."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **kongresista** sa inyong distrito?","translation":"Who is the **congressperson** in your district?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong miyembro o mang-aawit sa isang koro o pangkat ng mga mang-aawit.
original_explanation: Those people who sing in church every Sunday, usually in uniform. They're the ones who always have 'blending' practice and get scolded by the choir master when someone's off-key. Basically, a member of a choir. They provide the background music to your life, literally.
usage_notes: Used to refer to a member of any choir, whether in a church, school, or professional group.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang mahusay na **korista** si Maria sa kanilang simbahan.","translation":"Maria is a great **chorister** in their church."},{"sentence":"Nag-audition siya para maging **korista** sa sikat na Madrigal Singers.","translation":"She auditioned to be a **choir member** of the famous Madrigal Singers."}]

translation: food prepared for a feast; offering
meaning_filipino: Mga pagkain na inihanda para sa isang salu-salo, pagdiriwang, o bilang alay.
etymology: Possibly from Sanskrit 'haṇḍa' (large earthen water-pot), which evolved to mean 'vessel for cooking' and then the 'food cooked' itself.
original_explanation: The star of every Filipino birthday party, fiesta, or Noche Buena. It's the collection of spaghetti, lumpia, pansit, and fried chicken that makes any gathering a feast. "Ang daming handa!" is the best compliment an event host can receive. It's not just food, it's a love language.
usage_notes: Pronounced with stress on the first syllable /HAN-da/, distinguishing it from the adjective 'handa' (/han-DA/).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap ang lahat ng **handa** sa kaarawan ni Lola.","translation":"All the **food** at Grandma's birthday was delicious."},{"sentence":"Nagdala siya ng pansit bilang kanyang **handa** sa party.","translation":"She brought noodles as her **contribution to the feast** for the party."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, kumpanya, o organisasyon na tumatanggap ng serbisyo o payo mula sa isang propesyonal o negosyo kapalit ng bayad.
original_explanation: Sila ang dahilan kung bakit may sahod ang mga BPO agent, freelancer, at abogado. Sila 'yung nagbabayad para sa serbisyo mo, kaya sila 'yung 'boss' mo kahit hindi. Tandaan: 'The kliyente is always right... in their own mind.' Kailangan ng mahabang pasensya at maraming kape.
usage_notes: Ito ang mas karaniwan at tinatanggap na baybay kaysa 'kliente'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May pulong ako kasama ang isang mahalagang **kliyente** mamayang hapon.","translation":"I have a meeting with an important **client** this afternoon."},{"sentence":"Ang pagiging magalang sa **kliyente** ay susi sa magandang serbisyo.","translation":"Being polite to the **client** is key to good service."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o kinalabasan ng malawakang pagkasira o pagwasak.
original_explanation: Ito yung nangyayari sa diet mo kapag may dumaang nagbebenta ng taho o ice cream. Ang total-wreck, ang pagka-wasak. Pwedeng literal, tulad ng epekto ng bagyo, o emotional, tulad ng epekto ng ghosting sa puso mo.
usage_notes: A formal term. "Pagkasira" or "pagkawasak" are more common in everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-iwan ng malawakang **distruksiyon** ang nagdaang bagyo.","translation":"The recent typhoon left widespread **destruction**."},{"sentence":"Ang digmaan ay nagdudulot lamang ng **distruksiyon** at pagdurusa.","translation":"War only brings **destruction** and suffering."}]

translation: to catch (something falling); to take responsibility for
meaning_filipino: Saluhin ang isang bagay na nahuhulog. Sa matalinghagang paraan, ito ay ang pag-ako sa responsibilidad, kasalanan, o pasanin ng iba.
original_explanation: On one hand, **sapuhin** means to literally catch your falling phone. On the other, more 'hugot' hand, it's when you take the fall for your team's mistake at work. "Sige, ako na ang sasapo niyan." (Alright, I'll take responsibility for that.) It's the ultimate act of a hero or a martyr, depending on the situation.
usage_notes: The verb form of `sapo` (to catch). Can be literal (catch an object) or figurative (take the blame/burden).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **sapuhin** ang lahat ng gastusin para hindi na mamroblema ang kanyang mga kapatid.","translation":"He tried **to shoulder** all the expenses so his siblings would not have to worry."},{"sentence":"Bilisan mo! **Sapuhin** mo ang bata bago mahulog sa hagdan!","translation":"Hurry! **Catch** the child before he falls down the stairs!"}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng mataas na antas ng kultura, pag-unlad, at kaayusan sa lipunan.
original_explanation: This is the opposite of 'barbaric.' It's how you describe a society with laws, arts, and a system. It's also what your lola wants you to be when you eat at a fancy restaurant—'Anak, umayos ka, parang 'di ka may-kabihasnan!' (Act properly, as if you're not civilized!).
usage_notes: Used in historical and sociological contexts to describe societies, or colloquially to mean 'cultured' or 'well-mannered.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinatunayan ng mga artifact na ang ating mga ninuno ay isang lahing **may-kabihasnan**.","translation":"The artifacts proved that our ancestors were a **civilized** race."},{"sentence":"Kumilos ka na parang taong **may-kabihasnan**.","translation":"Act like a **cultured** person."}]

translation: to sue someone; to file a complaint against someone
meaning_filipino: Magsampa ng pormal na reklamo o kaso sa hukuman laban sa isang tao o entidad.
etymology: From Spanish 'hablar' (to speak), which evolved in Filipino to mean a legal complaint or suit.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "See you in court!" move. Kapag 'yung kapitbahay mong chismosa ay nag-level up na sa character assassination, at ready ka nang dalhin ang away sa barangay hall o mas malala pa. "Ipaghabla mo na 'yan, bes, para matauhan!"
usage_notes: A formal legal term. The object of the verb is the person being sued. `Ipaghabla mo siya.` (Sue him/her.)
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **ipaghabla** ang kumpanya dahil sa hindi makatarungang pagtanggal sa kanya sa trabaho.","translation":"He decided to **sue** the company for unjust termination."},{"sentence":"Pinag-iisipan niyang **ipaghabla** ang driver na nakabangga sa kanya.","translation":"She is thinking of **filing a complaint against** the driver who hit her."}]

translation: to wrestle with; to grapple with
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pakikipaglaban sa isang tao gamit ang pisikal na lakas na walang sandata, kadalasang may layuning pabagsakin o pasukuin ang kalaban. Ginagamit din sa matalinhagang paraan para sa mahihirap na sitwasyon.
etymology: From maki- (social prefix) + pag- (action prefix) + buno (wrestling, grappling).
original_explanation: Physically, ito yung wrestling o 'yung laro niyong magkapatid sa kama hanggang may umiyak. Figuratively, ito yung 'struggle is real' mo sa buhay—makipagbuno sa traffic sa EDSA, sa sandamakmak na deadlines, o sa sarili mong katamaran. It's the ultimate grapple, literal or metaphorical.
usage_notes: Can be literal (physical wrestling) or figurative (struggling with a problem, emotion, or difficult situation).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Araw-araw siyang kailangang **makipagbuno** sa kahirapan.","translation":"Every day she has to **grapple with** poverty."},{"sentence":"Gusto ng mga bata na **makipagbuno** sa kanilang ama bilang paglalaro.","translation":"The children want to **wrestle with** their father as a form of play."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbibigay ng isang bagay sa isang tao na may kasunduang ito ay ibabalik sa takdang panahon.
etymology: From pa- + pa- + hiram, meaning "the act of causing or allowing to borrow."
original_explanation: The ultimate friendship test. It starts with "Bes, pahiram ballpen," and can level up to "Pahiram pera, bayaran ko sa sahod." The act of pagpapahiram is a delicate dance between trust and the high probability you'll never see that item again.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bangko ay nag-aalok ng **pagpapahiram** ng puhunan para sa mga negosyo.","translation":"The bank offers **lending** of capital for businesses."},{"sentence":"Salamat sa iyong **pagpapahiram** ng libro.","translation":"Thank you for **lending** me the book."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagluluto ng pagkain sa mainit na mantika na gagawin pa lamang sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: That moment when you tell your mom you're hungry and she says, "Magpiprito ako ng itlog," and you know life is good. It's the future tense of making anything crispy and delicious, from hotdogs to galunggong (scad). The promise of a simple, yet satisfying meal.
usage_notes: This is the future tense of 'magprito'. The object of the verb is usually in the 'ng' form (e.g., magpiprito NG isda).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magpiprito** si Nanay ng isda para sa ating hapunan.","translation":"Mom **will fry** fish for our dinner."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **magpiprito** ng hotdog para sa mga bata?","translation":"Who **will fry** the hotdogs for the kids?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang magalang na pantawag o titulo para sa isang lalaki.
etymology: Possibly from a contraction of 'ginoong' from an older form. Related to the 'Gat' in Gat Jose Rizal.
original_explanation: The formal Filipino version of 'Sir' or 'Mister.' You use it for your boss, a government official, or that intimidatingly well-dressed tito at a family gathering. It's the word you use when you're trying to be extra polite, like when you're asking for a favor or when you've accidentally bumped into someone's car. The female counterpart is 'Ginang.'
usage_notes: A formal honorific for men, equivalent to 'Mr.' or 'Sir.' It precedes the name (e.g., Ginoong Cruz) or can be used alone as a form of address.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magandang umaga po, **Ginoo**.","translation":"Good morning, **Sir**."},{"sentence":"Para po kay **Ginoong** Santos ang sulat na ito.","translation":"This letter is for **Mister** Santos."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa anumang pagkain na inilagay at isinara sa loob ng lata upang mapreserba at tumagal.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "de" (of) at Tagalog na "lata" (can).
original_explanation: The official student/BPO employee survival kit. Pag petsa de peligro na, you turn to your trusty stash of de-lata like sardines, tuna, or corned beef. It's the "break in case of gutom" emergency food. Can also be a noun for 'canned goods'.
usage_notes: Can function as an adjective (pagkaing de-lata) or a noun (Bumili ako ng de-lata).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sardinas ay isang halimbawa ng pagkaing **de-lata**.","translation":"Sardines are an example of **canned** food."},{"sentence":"Laging may nakahandang **de-lata** sa aming bahay para sa biglaang pangangailangan.","translation":"There are always **canned goods** ready in our house for emergencies."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggamit ng telepono upang makipag-ugnayan sa isang tao; ang pagtawag sa telepono. Ito ay nasa panahunang pangnagdaan.
etymology: From Spanish 'teléfono'. The verb is formed with the '-um-' infix.
original_explanation: The past tense of making a phone call. This is what your parents did before 'nag-chat,' 'nag-DM,' or 'nag-video call.' If someone says they 'tumelepono,' it has a slightly formal, almost vintage vibe, like they used a landline with a curly cord.
usage_notes: Past tense of the verb 'to call'. The more common, modern equivalent is 'tumawag'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumelepono** ang tita mo mula sa Amerika kagabi.","translation":"Your aunt **called** from America last night."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **tumelepono** habang naliligo ako?","translation":"Who **called on the phone** while I was taking a shower?"}]

meaning_filipino: Simulang paganahin ang isang makina o sasakyan.
etymology: From `pa-` (causative prefix) + `andar` (to run, to function, from Spanish 'andar' meaning 'to walk') + `-in` (object-focus suffix).
original_explanation: The first command you give your car in the morning, your laptop when you start work, or the generator during a brownout. It's the "Let's get this show on the road!" moment for any machine. Also, what you do to your brain with a strong cup of coffee.
usage_notes: Used for machinery, vehicles, and appliances. Can also be used metaphorically for starting a process.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **paandarin** mo ang kotse habang naghahanda ako.","translation":"Please **start** the car while I get ready."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko alam kung paano **paandarin** ang bagong washing machine.","translation":"I don't know how to **make** the new washing machine **run**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malalim na pag-iisip, pagninilay-nilay, o pagmumuni-muni sa isang bagay.
etymology: Likely a reduplication of a root related to thought or reflection.
original_explanation: This is your "sana all" moment pero in deep thought. Yung nakatingin ka lang sa malayo, nag-iisip kung saan ka nagkamali, anong ulam bukas, o kung may pag-asa pa ba sa Pinas. It's the quiet, internal monologue before you post something dramatic online.
usage_notes: A more poetic or literary term for deep thinking. 'Pagninilay' is more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagdidilidili** sa tabi ng dagat ay nakakatulong upang gumaan ang kanyang pakiramdam.","translation":"**Contemplation** by the sea helps to lighten his feelings."},{"sentence":"Sa kanyang **pagdidilidili**, napagtanto niya ang kanyang mga pagkakamali.","translation":"In his **deep thought**, he realized his mistakes."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagiging marumi o ang pagdumi ng isang bagay. Ito rin ay tumutukoy sa pisyolohikal na proseso ng paglabas ng dumi mula sa katawan.
original_explanation: Two meanings, one vibe: messiness. First, it's when your white shirt gets a coffee stain. "Hala, dumumi!" Second, it's the more... *biological* meaning. The polite way your tita asks the toddler, "Gusto mo bang dumumi?" instead of saying "Jumejebs ka na ba?" It's the universal code for "nature calls."
usage_notes: The context usually clarifies whether it means "to become dirty" or "to defecate". The latter is a common, slightly formal/polite way to refer to the act.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maglaro diyan, **dudumi** lang ang damit mo.","translation":"Don't play there, your clothes will just **get dirty**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nang **dumumi** ng aso kaya inilabas niya ito.","translation":"The dog needed **to defecate** so he took it outside."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng paputok na lumilikha ng malakas na ingay kapag sinindihan.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "reventar," na nangangahulugang "sumabog" o "pumutok."
original_explanation: Ito yung pampaingay tuwing New Year's Eve na parang relationship status mo: maingay sa simula, tapos biglang wala na. The louder, the better daw sabi ng mga tito, para itaboy ang bad spirits (at ang tulog ng kapitbahay).
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit tuwing may pagdiriwang, lalo na sa Bagong Taon. Ang paggamit nito ay mahigpit na kinokontrol ng batas dahil sa panganib na dulot nito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-ingay ang mga bata sa pagsisindi ng **rebentador** sa kalsada.","translation":"The kids made a lot of noise lighting **firecrackers** on the street."},{"sentence":"Ipinagbawal ng lokal na pamahalaan ang pagbebenta ng malalakas na **rebentador**.","translation":"The local government banned the sale of powerful **firecrackers**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat ng mga estado o organisasyon na may sariling pamamahala ngunit pinag-isa sa ilalim ng isang sentral na awtoridad para sa mga partikular na layunin.
original_explanation: Imagine all the different student orgs in a university. Each org has its own projects and officers, but they all come together to form a student council or a 'pederasyon' for bigger, university-wide events. It's like an alliance, a supergroup of smaller groups. K-pop fans, think of it like SM Town or HYBE Family.
usage_notes: Used in contexts of sports, organizations, and politics.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **Pederasyon** ng mga Magsasaka ay nagdaos ng isang malaking pagtitipon.","translation":"The **Federation** of Farmers held a large gathering."},{"sentence":"Sumali ang kanilang koponan sa pandaigdigang **pederasyon** ng basketball.","translation":"Their team joined the international basketball **federation**."}]

translation: to stun; to daze; to bewilder
meaning_filipino: Gawing tulig ang isang tao; lituhin o guluhin ang isipan sa pamamagitan ng ingay, dagok, o anumang nakagugulat na aksyon.
original_explanation: Ito yung ginagawa sa'yo ng sunod-sunod na deadlines at a-attend-an na Zoom meetings. Or yung ginagawa sa'yo ng chismis na narinig mo tungkol sa sarili mo. Basically, to be mentally knocked out.
usage_notes: Ang pandiwa na nagsasanhi sa isang tao na maging 'tulig'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo siyang **tuligin** ng napakaraming tanong nang sabay-sabay.","translation":"Don't **bewilder** him with so many questions all at once."},{"sentence":"Tila **tinulig** ng malakas na suntok ang boksingero.","translation":"The boxer seemed to have been **stunned** by the strong punch."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na sinasamantala ang mga pagkakataon para sa sariling kapakinabangan, madalas nang walang pagsasaalang-alang sa etika o sa kapakanan ng iba.
original_explanation: Ito yung 'friend' mo na bigla lang nagpaparamdam 'pag may kailangan. Parang kabute sa pulitika, sumusulpot 'pag eleksyon para makisawsaw. Sila yung tipo na laging nag-aabang ng chance para umangat, kahit pa may matapakan.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng pulitika at panlipunang pakikipag-ugnayan na may negatibong konotasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinawag siyang **oportunista** dahil lumipat siya ng partido bago ang eleksyon.","translation":"He was called an **opportunist** because he switched parties before the election."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging isang **oportunista** sa iyong mga kaibigan.","translation":"Don't be an **opportunist** with your friends."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang tao na kulang sa tapang o lakas ng loob upang harapin ang panganib, takot, o kahirapan.
original_explanation: 'Yung tropa mong nagyayayang manood ng horror movie pero siya unang sumisigaw at nagtatakip ng mata. O 'yung gusto mo nang mag-resign pero takot ka sa unknown. It's not being a duwag outright, sometimes it's just being... careful. Very, very careful. But yeah, mostly **hindi matapang**.
usage_notes: Mas malumanay kaysa sa `duwag`. Sinasabi lamang nito ang kawalan ng katapangan at hindi direktang isang insulto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inamin niyang siya ay **hindi matapang** pagdating sa matataas na lugar.","translation":"He admitted that he is **not brave** when it comes to high places."},{"sentence":"Hindi porket **hindi matapang** ang isang tao ay duwag na siya kaagad.","translation":"Just because a person is **not brave** doesn't mean they are a coward."}]

translation: to make; to do; to create
meaning_filipino: Isang anyo ng pandiwang 'gumawa' na nagpapahiwatig ng paglikha, pagsasagawa, o pagbuo ng isang bagay. Madalas gamitin sa anyong pautos o sa pagtatanong.
original_explanation: Basically the same as 'gumawa'. It's the verb for getting things done. 'Maggawa ka ng assignment mo.' 'Maggawa ka ng paraan.' It's the command form your parents use when they're tired of your excuses. It’s less common in everyday conversation than 'gumawa' but still understood.
usage_notes: 'Maggawa' is a less common conjugation of 'gawa' compared to 'gumawa.' It's often used in imperative sentences or questions, sometimes carrying a slightly more forceful or deliberate tone. For example, 'Anong maggagawa natin?' (What can we do?).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **maggagawa** ko kung ayaw niyang makinig?","translation":"What can I **do** if he doesn't want to listen?"},{"sentence":"**Maggawa** na kayo ng inyong takdang-aralin.","translation":"**Do** your homework now."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maingay na tunog na nalilikha sa paghinga habang natutulog, karaniwang sanhi ng panginginig ng malambot na bahagi ng lalamunan.
original_explanation: The official soundtrack of your tito's afternoon nap. It's that human chainsaw sound that makes you question your love for the person sleeping beside you. Parang may nag-start ng two-stroke engine sa kwarto mo.
usage_notes: The verb form is 'humilik' (to snore).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lakas ng **hilik** ni Tatay kagabi!","translation":"Dad's **snore** was so loud last night!"},{"sentence":"Hindi ako makatulog dahil sa **hilik** ng kasama ko sa kwarto.","translation":"I can't sleep because of my roommate's **snoring**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-abot o paglilipat ng isang bagay sa pag-iingat o pagmamay-ari ng iba nang walang inaasahang kapalit.
original_explanation: The ultimate command during gift-giving season. '**Ibigay** mo na 'yan sa inaanak mo!' (Give that to your godchild!). It's what you do with your salary (to your bills), your effort (to your work), and your all (sa taong 'di ka naman gusto). *Ibigay mo ang 100% mo!*
usage_notes: Focuses on the object being given.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **ibigay** mo sa akin ang aklat na iyan.","translation":"Please, **give** me that book."},{"sentence":"**Ibinigay** niya ang lahat ng kanyang lakas para manalo sa laro.","translation":"He **gave** all his strength to win the game."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gusali o pook dalanginan na itinalaga para sa pampublikong pagsamba, lalo na sa relihiyong Kristiyano.
original_explanation: The go-to place for Sundays, weddings, baptisms, and when you need to pray for a miracle before your final exams. Also a classic landmark for giving directions: 'Kanan ka sa may simbahan.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkita tayo sa labas ng **simbahan** pagkatapos ng misa.","translation":"Let's meet outside the **church** after the mass."},{"sentence":"Ang lumang **simbahan** sa aming bayan ay itinayo pa noong panahon ng mga Espanyol.","translation":"The old **church** in our town was built during the Spanish era."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang larawan, video, o teksto na naglalaman ng katatawanan, na kumakalat nang mabilis sa internet at madalas na binabago para umangkop sa iba't ibang sitwasyon.
original_explanation: The universal language of the internet. Ito yung mga nakakatawang picture na may text, o short video clip, na pinapasa-pasa sa Messenger, FB, at TikTok. Kung hindi ka nakakarelate sa isang meme, baka kailangan mo nang mag-update ng social media life mo. Sila ang modern-day 'hugot' lines in picture form.
usage_notes: Pronounced as /mim/ in the Philippines, following English.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginawa nilang **meme** yung epic fail na pag-arte ng artista.","translation":"They turned the actor's epic fail performance into a **meme**."},{"sentence":"Tawa ako nang tawa sa mga **meme** tungkol sa work from home.","translation":"I was laughing so hard at the **memes** about working from home."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng tela o papel na ginagamit sa mesa para sa pagpunas ng bibig at kamay habang kumakain. Maaari ring tumukoy sa 'sanitary napkin'.
original_explanation: In the Philippines, 'napkin' has a double life. At Jollibee, it's for wiping your mouth after eating Chickenjoy. But if a girl whispers to her friend, 'May napkin ka?', she's not asking for something for the dining table. It's a code word for a sanitary pad. Context is key!
usage_notes: The meaning (table napkin vs. sanitary napkin) is highly dependent on context. The term 'sanitary napkin' is also widely used for clarity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiabot ng **napkin**, mayumit ako sa spaghetti.","translation":"Please pass the **napkin**, I got spaghetti sauce on me."},{"sentence":"Kailangan niyang bumili ng **napkin** sa tindahan.","translation":"She needs to buy a **sanitary napkin** at the store."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pakikisama o pakikipag-ugnayan sa isang grupo ng mga tao, karaniwan sa isang pagtitipon.
etymology: From 'halo' (mix) + 'bilo' (a type of rice cake, metaphorically 'to roll with').
original_explanation: The art of 'making chika' at a party. It's floating from one group to another, armed with a drink and a smile, trying to look like you belong. For introverts, this is the final boss. The verb form, 'makipaghalubilo', is what your tita tells you to do instead of just staring at your phone during family reunions.
usage_notes: Often used in the verb form 'makipaghalubilo' (to mingle). The noun 'halubilo' itself is less common but refers to the act.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahusay siya sa pakikipag-**halubilo** sa mga kliyente.","translation":"She is good at **mingling** with clients."},{"sentence":"Iniiwasan ko ang masyadong maraming **halubilo** sa mga party.","translation":"I avoid too much **socializing** at parties."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglilimpon o pag-aayos ng isang bagay, tulad ng damit o papel, sa pamamagitan ng paglalapat ng mga gilid nito, na naganap sa nakaraan. Ito ay halos kasingkahulugan ng 'nagtiklop'.
original_explanation: The simpler, more common cousin of 'nagtiklop'. This is what your mom told you to do with your clothes but you ignored it, and now your chair has a mountain of them. "Nagtupi ako ng isang daang papel na eroplano para sa project niya." It’s a basic life skill, right up there with knowing how to cook rice.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'nagtiklop' for folding clothes, paper, etc., but 'nagtiklop' is more common for businesses closing or people backing down.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos maglaba, **nagtupi** agad ako ng mga damit.","translation":"After doing the laundry, I immediately **folded** the clothes."},{"sentence":"**Nagtupi** siya ng sulat at inilagay ito sa kanyang bulsa.","translation":"He **folded** the letter and put it in his pocket."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal at mapagmahal na tawag sa isang pusa, katulad ng 'muning' o 'kuting'.
etymology: Posibleng mula sa mga wikang Bisaya kung saan ang 'misay' ay nangangahulugang pusa, o mula sa tunog na ginagamit sa pagtawag ng pusa.
original_explanation: It's what you call a cat when "pusa" feels too formal and "muning" is already taken. It’s like calling a dog "doggo" or a friend "bes." "Psst, misay!" is the universal Filipino sound to summon any feline within a 10-meter radius, usually for a quick head scratch or to shoo it away from your ulam.
usage_notes: Kolokyal at madalas gamitin sa paraang magiliw o nakakatuwa. Minsan ay ipinagpapalit sa 'muning'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aming **misay** ay mahilig matulog sa ibabaw ng TV.","translation":"Our **cat** loves to sleep on top of the TV."},{"sentence":"Hoy **misay**, huwag mong kainin 'yang isda!","translation":"Hey **cat**, don't eat that fish!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang grapikong representasyon ng datos o impormasyon, tulad ng talahanayan, grap, o diyagrama.
original_explanation: That thing your boss asks for in a BPO meeting that's full of confusing lines and bars, usually made in Excel. It's supposed to make things clearer, but sometimes it just gives you a headache. "Pakigawa ng chart ng sales performance, ASAP."
usage_notes: Used directly in business, academic, and medical contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tingnan mo ang **chart** para makita ang pagtaas ng ating benta.","translation":"Look at the **chart** to see the increase in our sales."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating i-update ang medical **chart** ng pasyente.","translation":"We need to update the patient's medical **chart**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagpapahayag, nagsasalaysay, o nagsasaad ng isang bagay sa pormal na paraan.
original_explanation: The official voice-over guy of a situation. In legal terms, they're the one making a sworn statement. In literature, they're the narrator telling the story. They're the ones who put things on the record. Sila ang nagsasabi kung ano ang totoo (o kung ano ang dapat mapatala bilang totoo).
usage_notes: Often used in formal, legal, or literary contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **tagasaad** sa dokumentaryo ay may malinaw at kapanipaniwalang boses.","translation":"The **narrator** in the documentary has a clear and believable voice."},{"sentence":"Sino ang pipirma bilang **tagasaad** sa sinumpaang salaysay na ito?","translation":"Who will sign as the **declarer** on this sworn statement?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sinaunang sistema ng pagsulat na nagmula sa Java at ginamit sa malaking bahagi ng Timog-silangang Asya, kabilang ang Pilipinas, mula ika-8 hanggang ika-16 na siglo.
etymology: From Old Javanese 'kawi', meaning 'poet' or 'literary language'.
original_explanation: Think of it as the great-great-grandparent of Baybayin. Kawi was the script used by ancient kingdoms in Southeast Asia for official documents, literature, and probably some serious ancient 'chismis' etched in copperplates. It's the 'alta' writing system of its time.
usage_notes: Usually capitalized as it is a proper noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng mga historyador ang mga inskripsyon na nakasulat sa **Kawi**.","translation":"Historians are studying the inscriptions written in **Kawi**."},{"sentence":"Ang Laguna Copperplate Inscription ay isang halimbawa ng dokumentong gumagamit ng sulat **Kawi**.","translation":"The Laguna Copperplate Inscription is an example of a document that uses the **Kawi** script."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paraang literal o eksakto sa orihinal na salita o teksto; isa-isang titik.
etymology: From Spanish 'letra por letra' (letter for letter).
original_explanation: When you translate something letra-por-letra, you're being super literal, word-for-word, no room for interpretation. It's like using Google Translate in the early 2000s and getting a hilariously wrong sentence. It's the opposite of 'getting the gist.' Sometimes you need to explain things this way to someone who isn't getting the message, 'Okay, letra-por-letra na ha: H-U-W-A-G.'
usage_notes: Used to emphasize literalness or a very careful, methodical process. Can also function as an adjective.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isinalin niya ang tula nang **letra-por-letra** kaya nawala ang orihinal na himig nito.","translation":"He translated the poem **literally**, so its original rhythm was lost."},{"sentence":"Binaybay niya ang pangalan, **letra-por-letra**, para siguradong tama.","translation":"She spelled out the name, **letter by letter**, to ensure it was correct."}]

meaning_filipino: Nilalaman sa internet, tulad ng artikulo o post, na sadyang ginawa upang magdulot ng galit o inis sa mambabasa para makakuha ng maraming reaksyon at komento.
original_explanation: 'Yung post sa Facebook na "Hindi lahat ng single mom ay biktima" or "May kasalanan din ang mahihirap kung bakit sila mahirap." Sinasadya 'yan para mag-away-away kayo sa comments section, at 'pag nag-comment ka ng galit, "congrats, you took the bait!" It's content designed to trigger your inner Marites.
usage_notes: Isang modernong termino na nauuso sa social media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang patulan 'yan, halatang **rage bait** lang 'yang post na 'yan para dumami ang engagement.","translation":"Don't engage with that, the post is obviously just **rage bait** to increase engagement."}]

translation: to rent out; to lease out
meaning_filipino: Pahintulutan ang iba na gamitin ang isang ari-arian, tulad ng bahay o sasakyan, kapalit ng regular na bayad o upa.
original_explanation: This is the verb for what landlords and business-minded Pinoys do. If you have an extra room, a condo you're not using, or even a high-end bike, you can **iupa** it for extra cash. It's the OG side hustle. "For rent" signs are basically saying "Pwedeng iupa."
usage_notes: The focus is on the thing being rented out. Contrast with 'umupa', which means 'to rent (from someone)'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya silang **iupa** ang isang kuwarto sa kanilang bahay para sa dagdag na kita.","translation":"They decided to **rent out** a room in their house for extra income."},{"sentence":"Balak kong **iupa** ang luma kong kotse.","translation":"I plan to **rent out** my old car."}]

translation: scraping; grating; to scrape; to grate
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkiskis nang mariin ng isang bagay sa isang magaspang na ibabaw, na karaniwang lumilikha ng tunog at nag-aalis ng panlabas na bahagi.
original_explanation: This is the sound and action of grating a coconut for "gata" using a "kudkuran." It's the sound of a metal shovel scraping against concrete. It’s also what happens when you trip and your knee decides to make out with the pavement. The result is a "gasgas" (scrape/abrasion), but the action is "kayog."
usage_notes: Similar to 'kayod' but often implies a rougher, more grating action or sound.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **kayog** ng pala sa semento.","translation":"I heard the **scraping** of the shovel on the cement."},{"sentence":"**Kinayog** niya ang niyog para sa gagawing bibingka.","translation":"She **grated** the coconut for the rice cake she was making."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang nakausling kartilago sa lalamunan ng tao, partikular sa mga lalaki, na kilala sa medikal na termino bilang 'laryngeal prominence'.
etymology: Possibly related to 'gulong' (to roll), referring to its movement during swallowing.
original_explanation: That bump on a guy's throat. Also known as the "lalagukan". It's the anatomical feature that moves up and down when someone is nervously swallowing their pride... or a large piece of chicharon.
usage_notes: A specific anatomical term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kapansin-pansin ang kanyang **gulunggulungan** kapag siya ay nagsasalita.","translation":"His **Adam's apple** is noticeable when he speaks."},{"sentence":"Gumagalaw ang **gulunggulungan** niya habang lumulunok.","translation":"His **Adam's apple** moves as he swallows."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtutulungan ng dalawa o higit pang tao o organisasyon upang makamit ang isang partikular na layunin.
original_explanation: Parang group project sa school, pero sa totoong buhay. Pwedeng sa office, sa isang art project, o kahit sa paggawa ng TikTok dance. Teamwork makes the dream work, 'ika nga.
usage_notes: Often used in business, arts, and academic contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tagumpay ng proyekto ay bunga ng mahusay na **kolaborasyon** ng bawat miyembro.","translation":"The project's success was the result of the excellent **collaboration** of every member."},{"sentence":"Naghahanap ang kumpanya ng **kolaborasyon** sa mga lokal na artista.","translation":"The company is seeking **collaboration** with local artists."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang agham na nag-aaral sa pisikal na estruktura at mga sangkap ng Daigdig, ang kasaysayan nito, at ang mga prosesong humuhubog dito.
original_explanation: The Earth's autobiography. It’s the science of rocks, volcanoes, earthquakes, and all the stuff under your feet that you usually ignore. It’s basically the planet's very, very, very long history book, written in stone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-aaral ng **heolohiya** ay mahalaga upang maunawaan ang mga natural na panganib tulad ng lindol at pagputok ng bulkan.","translation":"The study of **geology** is important for understanding natural hazards like earthquakes and volcanic eruptions."}]

translation: to have something put inside; to have someone admitted
meaning_filipino: Utos o pakiusap na ilagay ang isang bagay sa loob ng isang sisidlan o lugar, o payagang makapasok ang isang tao.
original_explanation: The command your mom gives you for the groceries, the command your boss gives you for the USB drive, or what you wish you could do with your feelings sometimes—just put them in a box. It's the opposite of 'ilabas' (take out), which is what you do with the trash, or with your *hugot*.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **ipasok** mo ang mga upuan dahil uulan na.","translation":"Please, **have** the chairs **brought inside** because it's about to rain."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na nagbago na ng landas sa buhay, karaniwang mula sa masama tungo sa mabuti.
original_explanation: Parang yung ex mong biglang naging religious after niyo mag-break. 'New life' daw, pero deep inside, umaasa pa ring babalikan mo. O kaya yung taong kalalabas lang ng kulungan at nangakong magiging mabuting mamamayan na. It's a second chance, a fresh start, your character's redemption arc.
usage_notes: Often used for former criminals, addicts, or anyone who has made a significant positive change in their lifestyle. A compound word from 'bago' (new) and 'buhay' (life).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mula nang makalaya, siya ay isa nang **bagong-buhay** at tumutulong sa komunidad.","translation":"Since being freed, he is a **reformed** man and helps the community."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang haba ng panahon o distansya; maaari ring tumukoy sa lugar kung saan pumupondo o humihimpil ang sasakyang-dagat (anchorage).
etymology: Possibly related to sea-faring terms, connected to the idea of a long voyage or a place to stay for a long time.
original_explanation: This word is all about how long something lasts. Parang 'yong paghihintay mo sa sahod, 'yon ang **lawig** ng pagtitiis. It can also mean 'anchorage', the place where a ship parks. So basically, it's about waiting or staying put, whether you're a ship or just a marites waiting for the next chismis to drop anchor.
usage_notes: Less common in everyday conversation, more poetic or formal. 'Tagal' is the more common word for duration.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi na matiis ng mga mandaragat ang **lawig** ng kanilang paglalakbay.","translation":"The sailors could no longer endure the **duration** of their voyage."},{"sentence":"Ang look na iyon ay isang ligtas na **lawig** para sa mga barko.","translation":"That bay is a safe **anchorage** for ships."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang magalang na parirala na ginagamit upang humingi ng paumanhin o pahintulot bago gawin ang isang bagay na maaaring makagambala, makasakit, o ituring na bastos.
etymology: Possibly from pagsinta (love, care) + tabi (side, aside), a poetic way of saying "with your kind permission". The `po` adds politeness.
original_explanation: The ultimate "get out of jail free" card for social situations. You say this before you squeeze through a crowded MRT, before you pass in front of elders, or before you say something that might be a little too real (TMI). It's the verbal equivalent of a polite bow, especially when you think you might be disturbing some unseen "engkanto" in the province.
usage_notes: A very polite and slightly formal/traditional expression. Often used when passing in front of people or in unfamiliar, rural places to show respect to spirits.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pasintabi po**, dadaan lang po ako.","translation":"**Excuse me**, I'm just passing through."},{"sentence":"**Pasintabi po** sa mga nakikinig, pero kailangan kong sabihin ang totoo.","translation":"**With all due respect** to those listening, I have to tell the truth."}]

meaning_filipino: Isa sa apat na pangunahing direksyon, partikular ang direksyon kung saan lumulubog ang araw.
etymology: Believed to be from `ka-` + `lunod` + `-an` (place of drowning/sinking), referring to the setting sun.
original_explanation: The direction of sunset, Manila Bay, and everything "Western." When your Lola talks about your relatives in America, she's talking about those in the Kanluran. It's the direction you face when you're dreaming of migrating, or just watching the sun go down with a bottle of beer.
usage_notes: A primary cardinal direction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang araw ay lumulubog sa **kanluran**.","translation":"The sun sets in the **west**."},{"sentence":"Nakatira sila sa bandang **kanluran** ng Maynila.","translation":"They live in the **western** part of Manila."}]

translation: to take off (an item of clothing)
meaning_filipino: Alisin sa katawan ang isang partikular na kasuotan.
original_explanation: This is what you do the moment you get home from work—kick off your shoes, peel off your tight jeans. Unlike 'hubaran' which is done *to* someone, 'hubarin' is about removing a specific *thing*. 'Hubarin mo ang sapatos mo,' not 'Hubaran mo ang sapatos mo.' Gets?
usage_notes: Ang pokus ng pandiwang ito ay ang damit o bagay na inaalis (object focus). Halimbawa, 'Hubarin mo *ang damit*.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisabi sa kanya na **hubarin** ang sumbrero sa loob ng bahay.","translation":"Please tell him to **take off** his hat inside the house."},{"sentence":"Ang hirap **hubarin** ng basang medyas.","translation":"It's hard **to take off** wet socks."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na bukas-palad sa pagbibigay ng tulong, materyal na bagay, o panahon sa iba.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `mapag-` (na nagsasaad ng ugali) + `bigay` (pag-abot, pagkakaloob).
original_explanation: 'Yung kaibigan mong laging "libre ko!" o 'yung tita mong galing abroad na may pasalubong para sa buong barangay. Sila 'yung hindi nagdadalawang-isip mag-share ng blessings. Sila 'yung nag-aabot ng pamasahe sa jeep kahit 'di mo hiningi. The "Share-lebrity" of the group.
usage_notes: Isang napakakaraniwan at positibong paglalarawan sa katangian ng isang tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Talagang **mapagbigay** si Aling Nena; lagi siyang namimigay ng pagkain sa mga kapitbahay.","translation":"Aling Nena is truly **generous**; she always gives food to the neighbors."},{"sentence":"Sana lahat ay maging **mapagbigay** ngayong Pasko.","translation":"I hope everyone becomes **giving** this Christmas."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit at mapilit na paghingi o pagtatanong tungkol sa isang bagay; ang pangungulit.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa ng kaibigan mo na ayaw tumigil mangutang. O 'yung telemarketer na tumatawag kahit sinabi mo nang 'not interested'. It's that next-level pangungulit, a persistent nagging that tests your patience to its limits.
usage_notes: Carries a negative connotation of being annoying or bothersome.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa **pag-ukilkil** ng bata, ibinili na rin siya ng nanay ng laruan.","translation":"Because of the child's **pestering**, the mother finally bought him a toy."},{"sentence":"Itigil mo na ang **pag-ukilkil** mo sa akin tungkol sa utang niya.","translation":"Stop **nagging** me about his debt."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang malaki ngunit hindi tiyak na bilang na nasa saklaw ng mga daan.
original_explanation: When "isang daan" is not enough to express the sheer number of chismis you heard, or the number of people lining up for a seat sale. It's not a precise number, it's a vibe. It's the "so many I lost count" of Filipino numbers.
usage_notes: Indicates a large, indefinite quantity in the hundreds.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Daan-daan** na mensahe ang natanggap niya sa kanyang kaarawan.","translation":"She received **hundreds of** messages on her birthday."},{"sentence":"Nagkakahalaga ito ng **daan-daang** piso.","translation":"This costs **hundreds of** pesos."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkuha ng isang bagay mula sa isang tao o pook na may balak na isauli ito sa takdang panahon. Ito ay tumutukoy sa pinagmulan o tao kung saan nanghiram.
etymology: From the structure ka- + hiram (borrow) + -an, indicating a locative or referential focus, i.e., the person/place from whom something is borrowed.
original_explanation: This is the person you run to when you're 'petsa de peligro' and need to borrow some cash. 'Uy, bes, pwedeng **kahiraman** muna ng pang-Grab? Bawi ako sa sahod.' It's the source of your temporary relief (or future utang na loob).
usage_notes: The '-an' suffix turns the verb into a locative form, indicating the person or place *from which* something is borrowed. Not to be confused with 'hiraman' which can mean 'to borrow something for someone'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Aling Nena ang lagi kong **kahiraman** ng asukal tuwing nauubusan kami.","translation":"Aling Nena is the one I always **borrow** sugar **from** whenever we run out."},{"sentence":"Maaari ba kitang **kahiraman** ng libro para sa aking takdang-aralin?","translation":"May I **borrow** a book **from** you for my assignment?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng matamis na hinurnong pagkain na karaniwang gawa sa harina, asukal, itlog, at mantikilya o mantika. Madalas itong inihahanda para sa mga espesyal na okasyon tulad ng kaarawan.
etymology: From English 'cake', respelled according to Tagalog phonetic rules.
original_explanation: It's just 'cake' but spelled the way a Filipino would write it phonetically. It's the star of every birthday party, the centerpiece that gets its own song before being sliced. Whether it's a fluffy chiffon from Goldilocks, a dense chocolate cake from a local bakeshop, or a colorful ube macapuno roll, the 'keyk' is a non-negotiable part of any Pinoy celebration.
usage_notes: A common, informal spelling for 'cake'. The English spelling is also widely used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang bumili ng **keyk** para sa kaarawan ni nanay.","translation":"Don't forget to buy a **cake** for mom's birthday."},{"sentence":"Paborito ko ang chocolate moist **keyk**.","translation":"My favorite is chocolate moist **cake**."}]

translation: to press upon; to put weight on
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng diin o bigat sa ibabaw ng isang bagay; pagpapatong na may kasamang puwersa.
original_explanation: This is like 'dagan' but less common, the indie version. Imagine you're trying to close an overstuffed maleta—you have to sit on it to zip it up. That's the spirit of dayan. You're applying steady pressure to keep something down or shut.
usage_notes: This word is rare in modern conversational Tagalog and is often replaced by 'dagan'. It might be encountered in older literature or specific dialects.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dayanan** mo ang takip para hindi bumukas.","translation":"**Press upon** the lid so it won't open."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-**dayan** sa sugat ay nakatulong upang tumigil ang pagdurugo.","translation":"**Putting pressure** on the wound helped stop the bleeding."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa o may kaugnayan sa tiyan at mga bituka.
original_explanation: The fancy, scientific-sounding way to talk about anything related to your 'tiyan' and 'bituka'. You'll hear this from your doctor, not your tita gossiping about her neighbor's health problems. "May gastrointestinal issues daw siya."
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa mga teknikal o medikal na talakayan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang endoscopy ay isang paraan upang suriin ang **gastrointestinal** tract.","translation":"An endoscopy is a procedure to examine the **gastrointestinal** tract."},{"sentence":"Nagrereklamo siya ng pananakit sa kanyang **gastrointestinal** system.","translation":"He is complaining of pain in his **gastrointestinal** system."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang damdamin ng pagsisisi o pag-ako sa isang pagkakamali; ang pagtuturo o pagbibintang sa iba bilang sanhi ng isang masamang pangyayari.
original_explanation: The star of the classic Filipino drama line: "Lagi na lang bang ako? Puro na lang sisi!" It's that heavy feeling you get after eating the whole pizza by yourself (regret), or what you do to your sibling when your mom asks who broke the vase (blame). Remember, "Nasa huli ang pagsisisi."
usage_notes: Maaaring mangahulugan ng panloob na pagsisisi o panlabas na paninisi. Ang pariralang 'Nasa huli ang pagsisisi' ay isang napakakaraniwang salawikain.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **sisi** ang kanyang puso matapos niyang iwan ang kanyang pamilya.","translation":"His heart was full of **regret** after he left his family."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong isalin sa akin ang **sisi** sa iyong mga pagkakamali.","translation":"Don't pass the **blame** for your mistakes onto me."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang pagkain, karaniwang karne, isda, o gulay, na isinasabay o ipinapares sa kanin sa isang kainan.
etymology: From Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *qulam, meaning 'side dish with rice'.
original_explanation: The eternal question every Pinoy asks at least twice a day: 'Anong ulam?' It's the star of the meal, the main event that makes your kanin (rice) not feel so lonely. Without ulam, life is just plain rice. It's the adobo, sinigang, or even the humble fried egg that gives your meal its identity.
usage_notes: A fundamental concept in Filipino cuisine. It refers specifically to the dish eaten with rice.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paborito kong **ulam** ay sinigang na baboy.","translation":"My favorite **viand** is pork sinigang."},{"sentence":"Sana masarap ang **ulam** natin mamayang gabi.","translation":"I hope our **main dish** is delicious tonight."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang labis na pagpapakita o pagpapahayag ng paghanga sa sarili; pagyayabang.
original_explanation: This is the "humble brag" level 9000. Yung friend mo na post nang post ng achievements niya with the caption "So blessed!" pero ang totoo, gusto lang ipamukha sa lahat na angat siya. It's the act of being your own number one fan, very loudly.
usage_notes: May dalang negatibong konotasyon, na nagpapahiwatig ng labis at kadalasang nakakainis na pagpupuri sa sarili.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Walang nakikinig sa kanyang **pagmamapuri** tungkol sa bago niyang kotse.","translation":"No one was listening to his **boasting** about his new car."},{"sentence":"Ang tunay na matalino ay hindi kailangan ng **pagmamapuri**.","translation":"A truly intelligent person doesn't need to **brag**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng labis na kalupitan, kabagsikan, o karahasan; hindi maamo.
original_explanation: This is the energy of your landlady on the 15th when you haven't paid rent. It's also how your mom looks at you when you come home at 3 AM. It's that 'don't-mess-with-me' vibe turned up to 11.
usage_notes: Often used to describe wild animals, but can be used metaphorically for people, actions, or situations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **mabangis** na tigre ay kinatatakutan sa gubat.","translation":"The **fierce** tiger is feared in the forest."},{"sentence":"May **mabangis** siyang tingin nang malaman niyang niloko siya.","translation":"She had a **ferocious** look when she found out she was cheated."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bagay o pook na abot ng tingin o nakikita mula sa malayo.
original_explanation: Your 'view from the top.' It's what you see from your condo window, the top of a mountain, or when you're stalking someone's IG story from afar. If you can see it, but it's kinda far away, that's your `tanaw`. It’s the visual equivalent of 'so close, yet so far.'
usage_notes: Often used with prepositions like 'abot-' (within view) or verbs like 'matanaw' (to be able to see from a distance).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mula sa aming bintana, **tanaw** namin ang buong siyudad.","translation":"From our window, the whole city is in our **view**."},{"sentence":"Abot-**tanaw** ko na ang tagumpay.","translation":"Success is already within my **sight**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagsasagawa o naniniwala sa espiritismo; isang medyum na nagsisilbing tagapamagitan sa mundo ng mga buhay at mga espiritu.
original_explanation: Yung tita o lola sa probinsya na kaya daw kausapin ang mga "hindi nakikita." Sila 'yung tinatawag kapag may nagpaparamdam o may nawawalang gamit na baka "kinuha ng nuno." Sila ang original na customer support ng other side.
usage_notes: Maaari ring tumukoy sa isang taong naniniwala lamang sa doktrina ng espiritismo, hindi kinakailangang isang medyum.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpatawag sila ng isang **espiritista** upang paalisin ang masamang espiritu sa bahay.","translation":"They called a **spiritist** to exorcise the evil spirit from the house."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa kanilang lugar bilang isang mahusay na **espiritista**.","translation":"She is known in their area as a skilled **medium**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtatakwil, pagtanggi, o pag-abandona sa isang tao, paniniwala, o responsibilidad.
original_explanation: This is major drama, like a scene from a teleserye where the rich father disowns his child for marrying someone poor. 'Itinakwil kita!' Pagsakwil is the act of doing that. It's more than just ignoring someone; it's actively casting them out of your life or renouncing a belief you once held. It's the ultimate 'You're dead to me' move.
usage_notes: Carries a strong sense of finality and rejection.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagsakwil** sa sariling anak ay isa sa pinakamasakit na desisyon para sa isang magulang.","translation":"The **disowning** of one's own child is one of the most painful decisions for a parent."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagsakwil** sa dati niyang mga prinsipyo ay ikinagulat ng lahat.","translation":"His **renunciation** of his former principles surprised everyone."}]

translation: tool for criticism; something used to critique
meaning_filipino: Isang paraan, salita, o kasangkapan na ginagamit sa pagpuna o pagbatikos sa isang tao, ideya, o gawa.
original_explanation: The ammo you use in a heated debate or during a 'constructive criticism' session that feels more destructive. Your keyboard can be your ultimate 'pambatikos' on social media.
usage_notes: This is a less common word, often found in formal or literary contexts related to debate, journalism, or art criticism.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang panulat ay nagsilbing **pambatikos** sa mga katiwalian sa gobyerno.","translation":"His pen served as a **tool for criticism** against corruption in government."},{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng matatalinhagang salita bilang **pambatikos** sa kanyang kalaban.","translation":"He used figurative words as a **critique** against his opponent."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang aklat na inilalathala taun-taon, karaniwang naglalaman ng mga larawan, kaganapan, at mga alaala ng nakalipas na taon sa isang paaralan o organisasyon.
original_explanation: The yearbook! That book you paid thousands for in high school/college just to see your awkward photo and a quote you now regret ('Live, Laugh, Love'). It's the physical version of your Facebook Memories from a specific year. Also known as 'taunang-aklat'.
usage_notes: This is a less common term for yearbook; 'taunang-aklat' or the English word 'yearbook' are more frequently used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatago pa rin sa baul ang **taunan** namin noong high school.","translation":"Our high school **yearbook** is still kept in the chest."},{"sentence":"'Pirmahan mo naman ang **taunan** ko,' sabi niya sa kanyang mga kaklase.","translation":"'Please sign my **yearbook**,' she said to her classmates."}]

meaning_filipino: Paggamit ng magaan na haplos o galaw sa isang bahagi ng katawan upang magdulot ng pangingilabot o pagtawa.
original_explanation: The ultimate weapon of titos and titas against their pamangkins. It's that playful torture that can make even the toughest person giggle uncontrollably. One moment you're chilling, the next moment someone's fingers are attacking your sides or feet and you're begging them to stop.
usage_notes: A very common action verb, especially in playful or family contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **mangiliti** ng kanyang mga kapatid hanggang sa mamula sila sa katatawa.","translation":"He loves to **tickle** his siblings until they turn red from laughing."},{"sentence":"Bawal **mangiliti** sa paa ko dahil malakas ang kiliti ko diyan!","translation":"You're not allowed to **tickle** my feet because I'm very ticklish there!"}]

translation: to lust after; to covet; to desire intensely
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng matindi at kung minsan ay masidhing pagnanais para sa isang tao o bagay, lalo na kung ito ay hindi sa iyo.
etymology: From the root "nasa" (desire, wish), with the prefix "pag-" and suffix "-an" to create a passive verb.
original_explanation: This is that intense "I want it, I got it" feeling, but maybe you *don't* got it... yet. It's more than just 'gusto'. It's the level of desire you have for the last piece of crispy pata, the latest iPhone, or your ultimate celebrity crush. It has a slightly naughty or forbidden connotation, like wanting something you know you shouldn't.
usage_notes: Carries a stronger, more intense, and sometimes negative or obsessive connotation than "gustuhin" (to like/want). The "-an" suffix indicates the object or person that is the target of the desire.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi tama na **pagnasaan** ang pag-aari ng iba.","translation":"It is not right **to covet** the property of others."},{"sentence":"Marami ang **pumagnanasa** sa kanyang yaman at kapangyarihan.","translation":"Many **lusted after** his wealth and power."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang biglaan at hindi sinasadyang pagkilos o paggalaw ng katawan, karaniwang sanhi ng gulat, takot, o sakit.
original_explanation: That involuntary jump you do when someone sneaks up behind you and shouts "BOO!" Or when you're half-asleep and you suddenly feel like you're falling. "Nagulat ako, grabe ang pitlag ko!" It's your body's built-in alarm system going haywire for a split second.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb 'pumitlag' (to flinch).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malakas na **pitlag** ang ginawa niya nang marinig ang kulog.","translation":"She gave a strong **flinch** when she heard the thunder."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman ko ang **pitlag** ng isda sa dulo ng aking pamingwit.","translation":"I felt the **twitch** of the fish at the end of my fishing line."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang pang-agrikultura na may mahabang hawakan at patag na talim na nakatayo nang pahalang, ginagamit sa pagbubungkal ng lupa at pag-aalis ng damo.
original_explanation: This is your tito's best friend in the garden. It's that tool for breaking up hard soil, getting rid of weeds, or pretending you're a warrior from a historical drama. Not to be confused with a shovel (pala) or a rake (kalaykay). This one's for chopping at the ground.
usage_notes: A specific farming/gardening tool, distinct from 'pala' (shovel) and 'piko' (pickaxe).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang **asarol** upang linisin ang damo sa kanilang bakuran.","translation":"He used the **hoe** to clear the weeds in their yard."},{"sentence":"Mabigat ang lumang **asarol** ni Lolo.","translation":"Grandpa's old **hoe** is heavy."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kabilang dako, panig, o pook.
original_explanation: This is your go-to word for anything 'on the other side.' The other side of the street, the other team in a game, or even the 'other woman/man' in a messy relationship drama. It's the ultimate word for division and separation. 'Sa kabila ng lahat' (despite everything) is the national anthem of a martyr.
usage_notes: Often used in phrases like 'sa kabila' (on the other side) or 'sa kabila ng' (despite).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa **kabila** ng kalsada ang tindahan.","translation":"The store is on the **other side** of the road."},{"sentence":"Sa **kabila** ng pagod, tinapos niya pa rin ang trabaho.","translation":"Despite the fatigue, he still finished the work."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang natural na pagtigil ng buwanang dalaw o regla sa isang babae, karaniwang nangyayari sa pagitan ng edad na 45 at 55.
original_explanation: Ito yung stage sa buhay ng isang babae na "end of an era" na ang period niya. Sabi nila, dito nag-uumpisa yung mga hot flashes, mood swings na level 999, at biglaang paghahanap ng aircon. Ito ang official "goodbye, monthly visitor" at "hello, new chapter" moment.
usage_notes: A medical term that has entered common parlance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nararanasan na raw ng tita ko ang mga sintomas ng **menopos**.","translation":"My aunt is said to be experiencing the symptoms of **menopause**."},{"sentence":"Ang **menopos** ay isang natural na bahagi ng pagtanda para sa mga kababaihan.","translation":"**Menopause** is a natural part of aging for women."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maging dahilan upang ang isang tao ay mabilanggo o maipakulong sa piitan.
etymology: Mula sa panlaping 'ika-' (panlaping sanhi) at 'Bilibid', ang pangalan ng pambansang bilangguan sa Muntinlupa, na naging pangkalahatang tawag sa kulungan.
original_explanation: The reason someone gets thrown in jail. It's the crime that gets you sent to Bilibid (the national penitentiary). "Yung pagnanakaw niya sa kaban ng bayan ang ikinabilibid niya." It's the ultimate "actions have consequences" verb.
usage_notes: Pandiwang sanhi. Ang salitang-ugat na 'Bilibid' ay tumutukoy sa pambansang bilangguan ng Pilipinas, ngunit ang paggamit nito ay naging pangkalahatan na para sa anumang kulungan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kasong estafa ang **ikinabilibid** ng negosyante.","translation":"The estafa case **was the cause of the businessman's imprisonment**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang gumawa ng masama na maaaring **ikabilibid** mo.","translation":"Don't do anything bad that could **cause you to be imprisoned**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang institusyon na nag-aalaga sa mga ulila, matatanda, o may malubhang karamdaman.
original_explanation: The local spelling of 'hospicio'. It's a place for the needy—orphans, the elderly, the terminally ill. It has a heavy, serious vibe, often associated with charity and last resorts. You'd say "ampunan" for an orphanage, but 'hospisyo' sounds more formal and all-encompassing.
usage_notes: This spelling is more common in modern Filipino than its Spanish counterpart "hospicio".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-alay sila ng donasyon sa isang **hospisyo** para sa mga batang may kanser.","translation":"They gave a donation to a **hospice** for children with cancer."},{"sentence":"Maraming boluntaryo ang tumutulong sa **hospisyo** tuwing Pasko.","translation":"Many volunteers help at the **asylum/orphanage** every Christmas."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang matindi, matalas, at paulit-ulit na sakit o hapdi, karaniwang pisikal.
original_explanation: Yung feeling 'pag na-seenzone ka. Or more literally, 'yung feeling 'pag nadapa ka at nagasgasan 'yung tuhod mo. It's that sharp, stinging pain, whether sa puso or sa balat.
usage_notes: Often describes a specific type of sharp, throbbing, or stinging pain, as opposed to a dull ache ('sakit').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Makirot** ang sugat niya sa braso matapos mahulog sa bisikleta.","translation":"The wound on his arm is **painful** after falling from the bicycle."},{"sentence":"Parang may tumutusok sa dibdib ko, sobrang **makirot**.","translation":"It feels like something is poking my chest, it's so **stinging**."}]

meaning_filipino: Maramihang anyo ng 'retweet'; tumutukoy sa kabuuang bilang ng mga pagbabahagi ng isang partikular na tweet.
original_explanation: The plural of RT. It's the currency of Twitter. The more **RTS** you get, the more 'viral' you are. It’s the digital equivalent of people nodding in agreement or shouting 'Amen!' in a crowd. 'Likes are for vanity, RTS are for sanity' (or for spreading the chismis).
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang tukuyin ang bilang ng interaksyon sa isang tweet.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Wow, umabot na sa 10,000 **rts** 'yung post mo!","translation":"Wow, your post already reached 10,000 **retweets**!"},{"sentence":"Mas mahalaga sa kanya ang **rts** kaysa sa likes.","translation":"**Retweets** are more important to him than likes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kondisyon ng mata kung saan ang mga ito ay hindi nakatuon sa iisang direksyon; banlag.
original_explanation: When your eyes are playing 'look here, look there' at the same time. One eye is looking at the person you're talking to, while the other is checking out the 'chismis' (gossip) at the next table. It's often used playfully, but it refers to the medical condition strabismus.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Medyo **duling** ang isang mata ng pusa.","translation":"The cat is slightly **cross-eyed** in one eye."},{"sentence":"Nagpanggap siyang **duling** para magpatawa.","translation":"He pretended to be **cross-eyed** to be funny."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghihiwalay o pag-alis mula sa pagsasama; ang pagputol ng ugnayan sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang tao.
original_explanation: The official term for 'it's over.' It's the source of countless 'hugot' posts, sad Spotify playlists, and late-night ice cream tubs. Whether it's a romantic breakup or just saying goodbye at the airport, it's that moment of untangling two lives that were once intertwined.
usage_notes: Can be used for romantic breakups, physical separation, or segregation of items.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masakit ang **paghihiwalay** ng magkasintahan.","translation":"The **breakup** of the couple is painful."},{"sentence":"Ang **paghihiwalay** ng basura ay mahalaga para sa kalikasan.","translation":"The **separation** of trash is important for the environment."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubos na pagkasira, pagkalito, o pagkabigla dahil sa isang matinding pangyayari, emosyon, o balita.
etymology: Origin is uncertain, but it has become a very popular colloquial term to describe a state of shock or devastation.
original_explanation: This is your state of being after you see your ex with their new partner, and they look... happy. Or when your sweldo arrives and then gets eaten by bills in 5 minutes. You're not just sad, you're not just shocked—you are emotionally and mentally wrecked. Your whole system just crashed. That's 'windang'.
usage_notes: Often used colloquially to describe a state of emotional or mental shock.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Windang** ang lahat nang malaman ang resulta ng eleksyon.","translation":"Everyone was **devastated** upon learning the election results."},{"sentence":"Naiwan siyang **windang** matapos siyang i-ghost ng ka-date niya.","translation":"She was left **shattered** after her date ghosted her."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang kilos ng pagtanggap ng salapi bilang kabayaran sa trabaho o serbisyo.
etymology: From 'kita' (earnings, profit). This is the present progressive tense of the verb 'kitain' (to earn).
original_explanation: This is the *action* of making money, the present tense of "to earn." It's the hustle. "Habang natutulog ka, ako'y kumikita." (While you're sleeping, I'm earning.) It's the verb form of your grind.
usage_notes: This is the active, ongoing process of earning money.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kinikita** niya ang pera sa marangal na paraan.","translation":"He/She **is earning** the money in an honorable way."},{"sentence":"Magkano ang **kinikita** mo bawat buwan?","translation":"How much **are you earning** each month?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang trabaho o tungkulin ay ang mangolekta ng bayad o utang.
etymology: From taga- (doer of an action) + singil (to collect a payment).
original_explanation: The person you both need and dread. Sila yung nagpapaalala sa'yo na may due date ang Meralco, credit card, at yung utang mo sa kaibigan mo. The modern-day tagasingil sends GCash reminders with a passive-aggressive "Hi, friend!"
usage_notes: Can refer to a professional debt collector, a cashier asking for payment, or even a friend you owe money to.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumating na ang **tagasingil** ng upa sa apartment.","translation":"The rent **collector** for the apartment has arrived."},{"sentence":"Ayokong maging **tagasingil** ng utang sa mga kaibigan ko.","translation":"I don't want to be the one **collecting** debts from my friends."}]

meaning_filipino: May bahid o taglay na maraming dugo; madugo.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'ma-' (mayroon) at salitang-ugat na 'dugo'.
original_explanation: Literally, 'bloody.' It's what a crime scene in a teleserye looks like. It can also describe a very intense, difficult, or violent situation. 'Ang exam sa Math ay marugo.' (The Math exam was bloody/brutal). It's the next level up from just 'mahirap' (difficult).
usage_notes: Can be literal (covered in blood) or figurative (extremely difficult/violent). 'Madugo' is a more common synonym.
