usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **marugong** labanan ang naganap sa Mactan.","translation":"A **bloody** battle took place in Mactan."},{"sentence":"Naging **marugo** ang operasyon ng pasyente.","translation":"The patient's operation became **bloody**."},{"sentence":"**Marugo** ang final exam namin sa abogasya.","translation":"Our final exam in law was **bloody** (brutal)."}]

translation: to be different; to make oneself different
meaning_filipino: Gawing iba ang sarili sa karaniwan; kumilos o mag-isip sa paraang hindi katulad ng nakararami.
original_explanation: This is for the "I'm not like other girls/boys" crowd. It's the conscious effort to stand out, to break the mold, or to just be your weird, unique self. Sometimes it's genuine self-expression, other times it's just trying too hard. "Gusto niya talagang magpakaiba, kaya laging kakaiba ang kulay ng buhok niya."
usage_notes: Can be neutral, positive (unique), or slightly negative (trying too hard to be different).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang matakot **magpakaiba** at ipahayag ang sarili mong opinyon.","translation":"Don't be afraid to **be different** and express your own opinion."},{"sentence":"Sa lahat ng magkakapatid, si bunso ang laging **nagpakaiba**.","translation":"Of all the siblings, the youngest is the one who always **makes himself different**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isara ang damit o anumang kasuotan sa pamamagitan ng pagpasok ng mga butones sa kaukulang butas nito.
original_explanation: That moment when your crush is walking by and you realize your polo shirt is wide open. You gotta ibutones that thing, stat! It can also mean 'to keep a secret' or 'zip it.' "Uy, ibutones mo yang bibig mo, baka marinig tayo!"
usage_notes: Can be used literally for clothing or figuratively for keeping quiet.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **ibutones** mo ang likod ng bestida ko.","translation":"Please, **button up** the back of my dress."},{"sentence":"Malamig sa labas, mas mabuting **ibutones** mo ang iyong dyaket.","translation":"It's cold outside, you should **button up** your jacket."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na hindi sarado o nakabukas; maaari ring tumukoy sa isang taong may bukas na isipan at handang tumanggap ng mga bagong ideya.
original_explanation: More than just "bukas." When a Pinoy says they're "open," it usually means they're open-minded ("open ako sa suggestions") or they're emotionally available ("hindi pa ako open to a new relationship, kakabreak lang namin"). It's the status you're hoping your crush is, but they're probably "it's complicated."
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa mga impormal na pag-uusap. Maaaring mangahulugang bukas (literal) o bukas ang isipan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Open** na ba ang bagong mall sa kanto?","translation":"Is the new mall on the corner **open** already?"},{"sentence":"Dapat laging **open** tayo sa mga bagong opinyon.","translation":"We should always be **open** to new opinions."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang opisyal na dokumento na inilalabas ng pamahalaan, na nagpapatunay sa pagkakakilanlan at pagkamamamayan ng isang tao, at nagbibigay-daan sa kanya na maglakbay sa ibang bansa.
original_explanation: The little blue (or maroon) book that holds your dreams of becoming a tita/tito in Japan, a student in Korea, or an OFW in Dubai. It's your ticket out of the country, and also the reason for the long lines at DFA. The ultimate "pangarap" booklet.
usage_notes: A direct loanword used universally in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang dalhin ang iyong **pasaporte** sa airport.","translation":"Don't forget to bring your **passport** to the airport."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong i-renew ang aking **pasaporte** bago matapos ang taon.","translation":"I need to renew my **passport** before the year ends."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng maraming katas o likido.
etymology: From ma- (adjective-forming prefix, meaning 'full of') + katas (juice, sap, extract).
original_explanation: That perfect slice of watermelon on a hot day. That perfectly cooked steak that drips when you slice it. The chismis you just heard that's so full of juicy details. "Uy, share mo naman 'yang chismis, mukhang makatas ah!"
usage_notes: Primarily used for fruits, but can be used metaphorically for gossip or stories.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap ang mangga kapag hinog at **makatas**.","translation":"The mango is delicious when it's ripe and **juicy**."},{"sentence":"Pinili niya ang pinaka-**makatas** na orange sa lahat.","translation":"She chose the **juiciest** orange of all."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagbati na nagpapahayag ng kagalakan o paghanga para sa tagumpay o magandang kapalaran ng isang tao.
original_explanation: The go-to word when someone passes the board exams, gets promoted, gets married, or finally gets their annulment papers. Usually followed by "pa-burger ka naman!" or "sana all!". The formal version of "Congrats!"
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin bilang isang pagbati (interjection). Ang anyong 'kongratulasyon' ay karaniwang ginagamit kahit para sa iisang pagbati.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kongratulasyon** sa iyong pagtatapos!","translation":"**Congratulations** on your graduation!"},{"sentence":"Isang malaking **kongratulasyon** ang ipinaabot ng buong kumpanya sa kanya.","translation":"The whole company extended a big **congratulations** to him."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggamit ng paa o isang kasangkapan upang kumayod o mag-alis ng isang bagay sa ibabaw, karaniwang sa lupa.
original_explanation: This is the classic chicken move. You know, 'isang kahig, isang tuka'—what you scrape is what you eat. It's the ultimate 'hustle' metaphor for a hand-to-mouth existence. Think of a chicken energetically scratching the dirt for worms; that's the raw, unfiltered energy of 'pagkahig'.
usage_notes: Most famously used in the idiom 'isang kahig, isang tuka' to describe a subsistence lifestyle.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita niya ang manok sa **pagkahig** nito ng lupa para maghanap ng bulate.","translation":"He saw the chicken in its **act of scraping** the ground to look for worms."},{"sentence":"Ang kasabihang 'isang **kahig**, isang tuka' ay sumasalamin sa buhay ng maraming naghihirap.","translation":"The saying 'one **scrape**, one peck' reflects the lives of many who are impoverished."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pang-abay na nagsasaad ng pagtatapos o pagtigil ng isang aksyon, kalagayan, o pangyayari na dati'y nagaganap.
original_explanation: The official phrase of moving on. "Mahal mo pa ba siya?" "**Hindi na**." The end of an era. 'Yung dati paborito mong milk tea, ngayon **hindi na** masarap. 'Yung dati mong 8 hours of sleep, ngayon pangarap **na** lang. It signifies a change, a stop, a full-stop.
usage_notes: Isang napakakaraniwang pananda sa pangungusap na nagpapahiwatig na ang isang estado na totoo sa nakaraan ay hindi na totoo sa kasalukuyan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hindi na** ako kumakain ng kanin sa gabi.","translation":"I **no longer** eat rice at night."},{"sentence":"Bakit **hindi na** siya tumatawag?","translation":"Why is he **not** calling **anymore**?"}]

translation: To parry; to block; to deflect
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagsangga o pag-iwas sa isang atake, suntok, o anumang paparating na panganib sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng kamay, braso, o isang bagay.
original_explanation: What you do when your mom is about to hit you with a 'tsinelas' (slipper). You parry! It's also what you do when your tita asks at a family reunion, 'Kailan ka mag-aasawa?' You 'salagin' that question with a quick topic change about how delicious the food is.
usage_notes: The '-in' suffix indicates that the object being blocked is the focus of the action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis niyang sinubukan na **salagin** ang bola.","translation":"He quickly tried to **block** the ball."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **salagin** ang mga masasakit na salita mula sa isang kaibigan.","translation":"It's hard to **deflect** hurtful words from a friend."}]

translation: to mesmerize; to attract; to magnetize
meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng balani o pang-akit upang mahikayat o maakit ang isang tao o bagay; ang paglalapat ng magnetismo sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: To put someone under your spell. It's what happens when your crush finally looks at you and smiles, and suddenly you forget your own name. "Nabalani" is the state of being mesmerized. This is the verb for when someone's charisma level is over 9000 and you're caught in their gravitational pull.
usage_notes: Used literally to magnetize an object, but more commonly used figuratively to mean mesmerize or captivate.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tila **binabalani** niya ang lahat sa kanyang galing sa pagkanta.","translation":"It seems she **mesmerizes** everyone with her singing talent."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpadala at hayaang **balaniin** ka ng kanyang matatamis na salita.","translation":"Don't give in and let yourself be **captivated** by his/her sweet words."}]

translation: Act of going up; filing (a case)
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-akyat sa isang mas mataas na lugar; o ang pormal na paghahain ng isang kaso o reklamo sa korte o kinauukulan.
original_explanation: Two meanings! 1) Literally climbing up something, like a tree or a jeepney. 2) The more stressful version: filing a lawsuit. 'Isasampa kita ng kaso!' is the grown-up version of 'I'm telling my mom!' It's the ultimate way to say, 'See you in court.'
usage_notes: The context (physical location vs. legal document) determines the meaning. 'Pag-akyat' is a more general term for climbing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahirapan ang matanda sa **pagsampa** sa matarik na hagdan.","translation":"The old man had difficulty with the **act of going up** the steep stairs."},{"sentence":"Nagdesisyon siyang ituloy ang **pagsampa** ng kaso laban sa kumpanya.","translation":"He decided to proceed with the **filing** of a case against the company."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o paghiling na ibaba ang isang bagay sa pisikal na lokasyon, o bawasan ang halaga, presyo, o antas nito.
original_explanation: Two main flavors: 1) The literal, "Paki-abot 'yung item sa taas, magpababa ako." (I'll have it brought down). 2) The one we all know and love at the palengke or tiangge: "Ate, magpababa naman ako ng presyo. Last price na po ba?" This is the art of "pagtawad" (haggling). You're asking the seller to lower the price. It's a national sport.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical lowering or reduction in value/price (haggling). The context clarifies the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magpababa** ka na lang ng gamit mula sa itaas na palapag.","translation":"Just **have the things brought down** from the upper floor."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **magpababa** ng presyo ng bilihin, pero ayaw pumayag ng tindera.","translation":"He tried to **ask for a lower price** for the goods, but the seller wouldn't agree."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gawain, salita, o sitwasyon na hangal, walang katuturan, at kadalasang nakakainis o nakakatawa.
etymology: From ka- + gago (stupid, fool, from Spanish 'gago' meaning stutterer) + -han suffix.
original_explanation: The general term for all stupid stuff. That prank your friends pulled on you, the ridiculously long queue for a freebie, the plot of a badly written teleserye. It’s the Filipino version of 'shenanigans,' 'bullsh*t,' or 'tomfoolery.' Can be used in anger ('Anong kagaguhan 'to?!') or in jest ('Tara, gawa tayo ng kagaguhan.').
usage_notes: A very common, informal, and versatile word. Its tone can range from angry and accusatory to playful and humorous depending on the context. Considered a mild curse word by some.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **kagaguhan** ang pinagsasabi ng politikong iyon.","translation":"That politician's speech is full of **foolishness**."},{"sentence":"Miss ko na ang mga **kagaguhan** natin noong college.","translation":"I miss our **shenanigans** back in college."}]

translation: to practice; to rehearse; to train
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uulit ng isang gawain o kasanayan upang mapabuti ang pagganap; ang pagsasanay para sa isang pagtatanghal, laro, o anumang aktibidad.
etymology: Hiram sa salitang Espanyol na 'ensayo' (rehearsal, practice) at nilapian ng unlaping `mag-`.
original_explanation: The "grind" before the "glow." Eto yung ginagawa ng P-Pop groups bago mag-comeback, ng basketball team bago ang finals, at ng choir niyo sa simbahan bago ang Pasko. It's the repetitive, often tiring, process needed for a flawless performance. Practice makes perfect, 'di ba?
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang salita para sa anumang uri ng pagsasanay, mula sa palakasan at musika hanggang sa mga presentasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pupunta kami sa court para **mag-ensayo** ng basketball.","translation":"We're going to the court to **practice** basketball."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **mag-ensayo** araw-araw para manalo sa kompetisyon.","translation":"We need to **rehearse** every day to win the competition."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging hindi permanente o madalas na pag-iiba-iba ng estado, isip, o damdamin.
etymology: From `pag-` + reduplication of the root `bago` (new), implying continuous or repeated change.
original_explanation: Describe your 'situationship' in one word. It's the weather in the Philippines: sunny in the morning, typhoon in the afternoon. It's the price of gasoline. It's your crush's mixed signals. 'Pabagu-bago' is the adjective, this is the noun for the whole messy phenomenon.
usage_notes: Emphasizes the repetitive or continuous nature of change, often with a negative connotation of being unstable or unpredictable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakalito ang **pagbabagu-bago** ng kanyang isip.","translation":"The **inconsistency** of his mind is confusing."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagbabagu-bago** ng panahon ay nagdudulot ng sakit.","translation":"The **fluctuation** of the weather causes sickness."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasara ng isang bagay, tulad ng pinto o kandado, gamit ang susi.
etymology: The root 'susi' is from Chinese Hokkien 鎖匙 (só-sî). The verb formation is native Tagalog.
original_explanation: That final step before you leave the house, patting your pockets and realizing you forgot where you put the keys. 'Isusi mo ang pinto!' is your mom's final reminder before you go out. It's the act of securing something, like your house from intruders or your diary from your nosy siblings. In the modern world, it's like putting a password on your phone—securing the goods.
usage_notes: The prefix 'i-' makes the key ('susi') the implied instrument and the thing being locked (e.g., 'pinto') the direct object.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **isusi** mo nang maigi ang pinto bago ka umalis.","translation":"Please, **lock** the door properly before you leave."},{"sentence":"Nakalimutan niyang **isusi** ang kahon kaya nakuha ang laman nito.","translation":"He forgot to **lock** the box, so its contents were taken."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan o aparato na sumusukat ng isang tiyak na haba ng oras o nagtatakda ng hudyat sa isang partikular na sandali.
original_explanation: This is the thing on your phone you set for your 15-minute power nap that turns into a 2-hour siesta. It's what you use for your instant noodles so they're perfectly cooked. In BPO lingo, it's the countdown for your break time. It's the modern-day taskmaster that dictates small chunks of our lives. "Set ka ng timer for 5 minutes, 'pag 'di pa siya nag-reply, move on na."
usage_notes: Isang direktang hiram na salita mula sa Ingles na malawakang ginagamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-set ako ng **timer** para hindi masunog ang niluluto kong itlog.","translation":"I set a **timer** so I wouldn't burn the egg I was cooking."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng prutas na hugis-kampana, karaniwang kulay pula o rosas, may makintab na balat, at malutong at matubig na laman. Ang puno nito ay Syzygium samarangense.
original_explanation: The OG thirst quencher before bottled water was a thing. It’s that bell-shaped, shiny red fruit that looks more like a Christmas ornament than food. It's crunchy, watery, and mildly sweet. Perfect for a hot summer day when you're too lazy to get a glass of water. Just grab a makopa from the neighbor's tree (with permission, of course!).
usage_notes: Also known as rose apple. It's a common fruit found in backyards in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong isawsaw sa asin ang hinog na **makopa**.","translation":"I love dipping ripe **wax apples** in salt."},{"sentence":"Namumunga na naman ang puno ng **makopa** sa aming bakuran.","translation":"The **wax apple** tree in our yard is bearing fruit again."}]

meaning_filipino: May hugis na parang itlog; habilog.
original_explanation: It's the shape of your face daw sabi ng mga beauty expert. Not quite round, not quite long, just... egg-like. Think of the perfect egg you're about to make into a sunny-side up. That's the shape.
usage_notes: Often used to describe face shapes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sabi ng barbero, **tabas-itlog** daw ang hugis ng mukha ko kaya bagay sa akin ang kahit anong gupit.","translation":"The barber said my face is **oval-shaped** so any haircut would suit me."},{"sentence":"Ang salamin na iyon ay may disenyong **tabas-itlog**.","translation":"That mirror has an **oval-shaped** design."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkubli o pag-iwas na makita ng iba. Ito ay ang kasalukuyang anyo ng pandiwang 'magtago'.
original_explanation: You, when the inaanak (godchild) visits on Christmas. Or when you see your officemate who owes you money walking towards you. It's the default state of introverts at a party. "Bakit ka nagtatago sa likod ng pinto?"
usage_notes: Ito ang imperpektibong aspekto (present tense) ng pandiwang 'magtago', na naglalarawan ng isang kasalukuyang ginagawang kilos.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pusa ay **nagtatago** sa ilalim ng mesa.","translation":"The cat is **hiding** under the table."},{"sentence":"Mayroon siyang sikretong **nagtatago** sa kanyang mga kaibigan.","translation":"He has a secret that he is **hiding** from his friends."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi nagwagi; natalo sa isang laban, paligsahan, argumento, o pusta.
original_explanation: The feeling after the 8-8 cutoff sa BPO. Or when you lose an argument with your mom even if you have all the facts from Google. You're just... **talo**. No questions asked, uwian na. It's the opposite of 'panalo', the mood when you check your bank account before payday.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a noun ('pagkatalo' - defeat) or a verb ('matalo' - to be defeated).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit **talo** ang paborito kong koponan, masaya pa rin ako sa napanood ko.","translation":"Even if my favorite team was **defeated**, I'm still happy with what I watched."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang malungkot kung **talo** ka ngayon, may bukas pa para bumawi.","translation":"Don't be sad if you're **defeated** today, there's still tomorrow to bounce back."}]

translation: to be crumpled, to get wrinkled
meaning_filipino: Magusot o magkaroon ng mga lukot at tupi.
original_explanation: This is the state of your shirt after you've used it as a pillow. It's also the state of a 100-peso bill you've kept in your pocket for a week. The verb form `malukot` means "to become crumpled". When your face does this because you tasted something super sour, that's also a form of `paglukot`.
usage_notes: Used for paper, cloth, and other materials that can be wrinkled. The adjective form is `lukot` or `gusot`. The verb form is `malukot` (infinitive) or `nalukot` (past tense).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingatan mong huwag **malukot** ang iyong diploma.","translation":"Be careful not to **crumple** your diploma."},{"sentence":"Madaling **malukot** ang damit na gawa sa linen.","translation":"Clothing made of linen gets **wrinkled** easily."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang binhi ng halamang kape na ginagamit sa paggawa ng inuming kape matapos itong anihin, patuyuin, at sangagin.
original_explanation: The holy grail for every BPO agent, student pulling an all-nighter, and basically every adult in Manila. This isn't just a 'seed', it's a magical bean that gets roasted, ground, and brewed into the liquid motivation we call coffee. The real 'pambansang buto'.
usage_notes: A common noun phrase. Refers to the bean in any state: raw, roasted, or ground.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-uwi siya ng isang sako ng sariwang **buto ng kape** mula sa Batangas.","translation":"He brought home a sack of fresh **coffee beans** from Batangas."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bulgar at lubhang mapanlait na paglalarawan sa isang taong itinuturing na napakapangit.
original_explanation: The nuclear option of Filipino insults about appearance. It's worse than 'mukhang-paa'. You don't just look bad, you look like... well, you know. This is what you mutter under your breath at the driver who cut you off in traffic. Never say this to someone's face unless you're ready for a full-blown away.
usage_notes: Extremely vulgar, offensive, and derogatory. To be avoided in almost all situations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang galit niya, nasabihan niya ito ng '**mukhang-tae**'.","translation":"In his extreme anger, he called him **shitty-looking**."},{"sentence":"Iwasan ang paggamit ng mga salitang nakakasakit tulad ng **mukhang-tae**.","translation":"Avoid using hurtful words like **feces-faced**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging magkalapit o magkatabi nang walang gaanong pagitan, o ang pagiging magkadugtong.
original_explanation: This is you and your crush riding the MRT during rush hour—zero personal space. It's also you and your bestie, inseparable since birth. Pwedeng literal na may pandikit, or pwede ring "sobrang close lang talaga kami."
usage_notes: Can be used literally for things stuck together or figuratively for people who are very close.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging **magkadikit** ang magkapatid na iyon saan man sila magpunta.","translation":"Those siblings are always **very close** (together) wherever they go."},{"sentence":"Ayaw matanggal ng sticker, **magkadikit** na talaga sila ng pader.","translation":"The sticker won't come off, they are really **stuck together** with the wall."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na nagbibigay-aliw, ginhawa, o pag-asa sa isang tao na nakararanas ng kalungkutan, pagkabigo, o sakit.
original_explanation: The "at least" prize of life. You didn't win the grand prize, but you get a "konsolasyon" prize. Your crush rejected you? "Konsolasyon mo na lang na at least, sinubukan mo." It's the emotional equivalent of a pat on the back and a free lollipop after getting a shot at the doctor's office.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of losing a competition ('consolation prize') or dealing with disappointment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit natalo, may natanggap pa rin siyang **konsolasyon** na premyo.","translation":"Even though he lost, he still received a **consolation** prize."},{"sentence":"Ang tanging **konsolasyon** niya ay ang suporta ng kanyang pamilya.","translation":"His only **consolation** is the support of his family."}]

translation: to walk a long way; to hike
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalakbay sa isang malayo o mahabang distansya sa pamamagitan lamang ng paglalakad.
etymology: A verbal phrase from maglakad (to walk) + nang (adverb marker) + mahaba (long).
original_explanation: This isn't just a simple walk to the store; this is a trek. This is what you do when you miss the last jeepney home and have no choice, or when you decide to go on a hike up a mountain. It’s the kind of walking that requires good shoes, a bottle of water, and maybe a hugot line about 'the long journey ahead.'
usage_notes: A common phrase used to describe a long walk or hike. It emphasizes the distance or duration of the walk.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinailangan naming **maglakad nang mahaba** dahil nasiraan ang bus.","translation":"We had to **walk a long way** because the bus broke down."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-akyat sa Mt. Pulag ay nangangailangan ng paghahanda para **maglakad nang mahaba**.","translation":"Climbing Mt. Pulag requires preparation to **hike**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkahilo o pagkalito; isang pakiramdam ng kawalan ng balanse o linaw ng isip.
original_explanation: You know that feeling after three bottles of Red Horse, or when you stand up too fast after binge-watching a series for 12 hours? That's kahiluhan. It's also the mental state you're in when your crush finally talks to you and you forget your own name.
usage_notes: While understandable, `pagkahilo` is the more common term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa tindi ng sikat ng araw, nakaramdam siya ng **kahiluhan**.","translation":"From the intense heat of the sun, he felt a **state of dizziness**."},{"sentence":"Ang **kahiluhan** niya ay dahil sa dami ng problemang iniisip.","translation":"His **confusion** is due to the number of problems he's thinking about."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pinong mineral, karaniwang puti at bahagyang nababanaag, na ginagamit sa pag-ukit at bilang palamuti.
original_explanation: That fancy white stone you see in museums or in your lola's house as a figurine. In poems, it's used to describe someone's skin as super flawless and white, 'kutis-alabastro.' The OG Gluta.
usage_notes: Often used in literary contexts to describe smooth, white skin, as in the phrase 'kutis-alabastro'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang kutis ay sinliwanag at sinkinis ng **alabastro**.","translation":"Her skin was as bright and smooth as **alabaster**."},{"sentence":"Yari sa **alabastro** ang mamahaling plorera.","translation":"The expensive vase was made of **alabaster**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng laro na nilalaro ng dalawang koponan na may labing-isang manlalaro bawat isa, kung saan ang layunin ay maipasok ang bola sa goal ng kalaban gamit ang anumang bahagi ng katawan maliban sa mga kamay at braso.
original_explanation: Yung sport na sikat sa buong mundo pero sa Pinas, mas sikat pa rin ang basketball. It's the Filipino spelling of 'football,' which almost always means soccer. Don't get it confused with American football, 'yun 'yung may helmet at parang nag-aaway lang sila para sa isang itlog na bola.
usage_notes: This is a direct, phonetic borrowing from English. 'Soccer' is understood but 'putbol' is more commonly used in casual Filipino conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig manood ng **putbol** ang tatay ko tuwing may World Cup.","translation":"My father loves to watch **football** whenever there's a World Cup."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang isang tao, bagay, o lugar na nahawahan o nalagyan ng mikrobyo, sakit, o anumang masamang elemento.
original_explanation: 'Pag may virus na yung laptop mo, impektado na 'yan. 'Pag yung kaibigan mong laging nega, baka impektado na rin ng bad vibes ang buong barkada. It's that feeling when you know something's been contaminated, whether it's a wound, a computer, or the group chat.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa kontekstong medikal o teknikal (hal. computer virus).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Agad na nilinis ng nars ang **impektado** na sugat.","translation":"The nurse immediately cleaned the **infected** wound."},{"sentence":"Babala: Huwag buksan ang email na ito dahil maaaring **impektado** ito ng virus.","translation":"Warning: Do not open this email as it may be **infected** with a virus."}]

translation: To be persuaded, to be cajoled, to be coaxed
meaning_filipino: Mapahinuhod o mapasunod sa pamamagitan ng malumanay at paulit-ulit na pakiusap o paglalambing.
original_explanation: When your friends convince you to go out on a Friday night even though you promised yourself you'd stay home and save money. 'Sige na, isang bote lang!' they say. It's the power of 'budol' but in a nicer, more persuasive way. It's how your mom gets you to do chores by using her 'lambing' voice.
usage_notes: Implies being won over by gentle persuasion, not by force or logic alone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Madali siyang **maamuki** basta't paborito niyang pagkain ang alok.","translation":"She is easily **persuaded** as long as her favorite food is the offer."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan siyang **amukiin** ng kanyang mga kaibigan na sumama sa paglalakbay.","translation":"His friends tried to **coax** him into joining the trip."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pandiwa sa nakaraang aspekto na nangangahulugang sinundan ang isang tao o isang account sa social media. Ito ay hango sa salitang Ingles na 'follow'.
original_explanation: The past tense of 'following' someone online. This is what you did right before you started stalking their old posts. 'OMG, nagfollow back sa akin si crush!' is the modern-day 'sinagot na niya ako.'
usage_notes: A very common Taglish verb used in social media contexts. This is the past tense (aspektong perpektibo).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagfollow** na ako sa'yo kahapon pa.","translation":"I already **followed** you yesterday."},{"sentence":"Bakit ka **nagfollow** sa kanya, 'di ba ayaw mo sa kanya?","translation":"Why did you **follow** them, didn't you say you don't like them?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na nakabitin o nakasabit bilang palamuti, tulad ng sa kuwintas, hikaw, o borlas sa gilid ng tela.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `pa-` at salitang ugat na `lawit` (nakabitin).
original_explanation: Yung sabit-sabit sa dulo ng kurtina ng lola mo, o yung agimat na pendant sa kwintas ni Cardo Dalisay. Anything that dangles for aesthetic purposes. It's the 'extra' hanging off your main outfit, bag, or even your jeepney's rearview mirror.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa mga palamuti sa alahas, mga borlas sa kurtina, o anumang pandekorasyon na bagay na idinisenyo upang nakabitin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng **palawit** sa bago niyang kuwintas.","translation":"The **pendant** on her new necklace is beautiful."},{"sentence":"Nilagyan niya ng **palawit** na ginto ang laylayan ng kanyang bestida.","translation":"She added a gold **fringe** to the hem of her dress."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gawain, obligasyon, o pananagutan na inaasahang gampanan ng isang tao dahil sa kanyang posisyon, propesyon, o katayuan sa lipunan.
etymology: From 'tungo' (direction, aim), suggesting a task directed towards a certain goal or purpose.
original_explanation: This is your 'job description' in life, whether you're the 'panganay na anak' whose tungkulin is to be the family's back-up retirement plan, or a BPO agent whose tungkulin is to stay calm while being yelled at. It’s what you *have* to do, not just what you *want* to do. Adulting is 99% tungkulin.
usage_notes: Often used in formal, professional, or familial contexts. The formal, full form is 'katungkulan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tungkulin** ng bawat mamamayan na sumunod sa batas.","translation":"It is the **duty** of every citizen to follow the law."},{"sentence":"Bilang panganay, ramdam ko ang **tungkulin** na tulungan ang aking mga kapatid.","translation":"As the eldest, I feel the **responsibility** to help my siblings."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mesa na may hilig na ibabaw at kadalasang may upuan, na ginagamit sa pagsulat o pagbasa, partikular sa paaralan.
original_explanation: Your lolo and lola's version of a work-from-home setup, but in a classroom. It's that classic wooden desk where you probably carved your crush's initials. Today, it’s the ancestor of your IKEA desk.
usage_notes: Primarily used in older contexts or in formal school settings. 'Mesa' is more common today.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inukit niya ang pangalan ng kanyang minamahal sa lumang **pupitre**.","translation":"He carved the name of his beloved on the old **desk**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga mag-aaral ay tahimik na nakaupo sa kanilang mga **pupitre**.","translation":"The students sat quietly at their **desks**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang haka-haka, opinyon, o paniniwala na tinatanggap bilang totoo nang walang sapat na katibayan; isang teorya o hinuha.
etymology: From `pag-` + `pa-` + `lagay` (state, condition, put). In this sense, it means 'to put forth an idea'.
original_explanation: "Assuming ka!" The noun version. It’s when you think someone has a crush on you because they smiled, or you conclude the project is due next week without checking the email. It's the mother of all "ay, sorry, akala ko" moments.
usage_notes: Often used in discussions, debates, or when forming a hypothesis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Batay sa aking **pagpapalagay**, hindi siya darating dahil sa masamang panahon.","translation":"Based on my **assumption**, he will not come because of the bad weather."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagpapalagay** ay napatunayang mali nang lumabas ang mga ebidensya.","translation":"His **supposition** was proven wrong when the evidence came out."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa ng isang pormal na pagpupulong, karaniwang may mga tagapagsalita, upang talakayin ang isang partikular na paksa.
etymology: From `mag-` (verb prefix) + `komperensiya`, which is from Spanish `conferencia`.
original_explanation: The corporate version of a 'team meeting,' but with better snacks and a lanyard. It's when a bunch of people in business attire gather to listen to PowerPoint presentations, network, and pretend to understand complex charts. Also, a good excuse to travel for work.
usage_notes: A formal term for a large meeting or assembly. A smaller, less formal meeting is usually called a `pulong`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magkokomperensiya** ang mga doktor mula sa iba't ibang bansa sa susunod na linggo.","translation":"Doctors from different countries **will hold a conference** next week."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magkomperensiya** upang pag-usapan ang mga bagong proyekto ng kumpanya.","translation":"We need **to have a conference** to discuss the company's new projects."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang aklat o listahan na naglalaman ng mga aytem na nakaayos sa isang sistematikong paraan, karaniwang may kasamang paglalarawan.
original_explanation: Before Shopee and Lazada, this was how you did your 'add to cart.' It's the Avon or Natasha brochure your tita leaves on the table. A list of things you want but probably don't need. The original 'budol.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumingin siya sa **katalogo** para pumili ng bagong sapatos.","translation":"She looked at the **catalog** to choose new shoes."},{"sentence":"Ang lahat ng aklat sa aklatan ay nakalista sa digital na **katalogo**.","translation":"All the books in the library are listed in the digital **catalogue**."}]

translation: To have a crush on someone who has a crush on you; mutual crush
meaning_filipino: Ang sitwasyon kung saan ang taong gusto mo (crush) ay may gusto rin sa iyo.
etymology: A portmanteau of "crush" and "back" (as in, to like someone back). A modern Filipino slang invention.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'sana all' moment. Ito yung plot twist sa K-drama ng buhay mo kung saan malalaman mong yung taong pinapangarap mo, pinapangarap ka rin pala. The opposite of being seenzoned. Kapag nag-crushback sa'yo si crush, may pag-asa!
usage_notes: A very specific slang term used to describe mutual admiration. Can be used as a verb ("Sana i-crushback niya ako") or a noun ("May crushback sila!").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paano kung i-**crushback** ka niya? Anong gagawin mo?","translation":"What if he/she **has a crush on you back**? What will you do?"},{"sentence":"OMG, totoo ba? May **crushback** sila sa isa't isa!","translation":"OMG, is it true? They have a **mutual crush** on each other!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pagkilos na walang sapat na pag-iingat o pag-iisip; pabigla-bigla.
original_explanation: This is your life mantra when you see "SALE" and buy things you don't need. Or when you send a risky text at 2 AM without thinking. It's the "act now, regret later" vibe. "Huwag kang padalus-dalos sa pag-resign, wala ka pang backup!"
usage_notes: The repetition (`dalus-dalos`) intensifies the meaning of being rash or hasty.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **padalus-dalos** na desisyon ay madalas pinagsisisihan sa huli.","translation":"A **hasty** decision is often regretted in the end."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng paltos o maliit na lesyon sa balat na may lamang tubig dahil sa pagkiskis, paso, o iba pang iritasyon.
original_explanation: The painful souvenir you get from wearing new shoes without socks to a party. Or after a 'fun' hike your friends dragged you to. Your foot didn't just get a blister, it 'nagpaltos'. The shoe itself can be described as 'nakakapagpaltos' (causes blisters).
usage_notes: This verb indicates the process of a blister forming. "Nagpaltos ang paa ko" means "My foot got a blister."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagpaltos** ang kanyang mga kamay dahil sa maghapong pagkakarpintero.","translation":"His hands **got blisters** from a whole day of carpentry."},{"sentence":"Siguradong **magpapaltos** ang paa mo kung isusuot mo ang masikip na sapatos na iyan.","translation":"Your foot will surely **get a blister** if you wear those tight shoes."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging labis na matipid o kuripot; ang pag-aatubili o pagtanggi na gumastos ng pera o magbahagi ng ari-arian.
original_explanation: This is the opposite of 'libre ko na.' This is your friend who uses a calculator to split the bill down to the last centavo, or your relative who reuses tea bags and gift wrappers from 1998. It’s the art of squeezing every last drop out of your peso, sometimes to a fault. It's being Ebenezer Scrooge, but Pinoy version.
usage_notes: A strong negative term. `Pagkamatipid` (frugality) is the positive or neutral version.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi siya gusto ng marami dahil sa kanyang **pagkamaimot**.","translation":"Not many people like him because of his **stinginess**."},{"sentence":"Ang labis na **pagkamaimot** ay maaaring maging sanhi ng pag-iisa.","translation":"Extreme **miserliness** can lead to loneliness."}]

translation: a sudden jerk; a flinch; a startle
meaning_filipino: Ang biglaan at hindi sinasadyang pagkilos ng katawan, karaniwang sanhi ng gulat, takot, o sakit.
etymology: From `pag-` + `pitlag`. `Pitlag` means a sudden twitch or jerk.
original_explanation: This is that mini-heart attack jump you do when your boss suddenly appears behind you while you're scrolling through Shopee. It's your body's "Alt+F4" reaction to a sudden "Marites" whisper or the classic "pusa sa bubong" sound at 3 AM. It’s a physical manifestation of being *gulat is you*.
usage_notes: Describes an involuntary physical reaction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya napigilan ang **pagpitlag** nang may biglang sumigaw sa dilim.","translation":"He couldn't stop his **flinch** when someone suddenly shouted in the dark."},{"sentence":"Ang malakas na tunog ng kulog ay nagdulot ng **pagpitlag** sa natutulog na sanggol.","translation":"The loud sound of thunder caused the sleeping baby to **jerk** suddenly."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na gawa sa artipisyal na materyales sa halip na natural; hindi tunay o likas.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung ngiti ng officemate mo 'pag Lunes—hindi totoo, gawa-gawa lang. 'Yung tela ng damit na galing sa fast fashion, 'yung leatherette na bag, o 'yung flavoring ng juice na lasang kemikal? Lahat 'yan sintetik.
usage_notes: Used to describe materials, chemicals, or even abstract concepts that are man-made or artificial.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gawa sa **sintetik** na katad ang sapatos na ito kaya mas mura.","translation":"These shoes are made of **synthetic** leather, that's why they're cheaper."},{"sentence":"Hindi maganda sa kalikasan ang mga **sintetik** na materyales.","translation":"**Synthetic** materials are not good for the environment."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, karaniwan ay karne o gulay, na hiniwa nang napakapino o giniling.
original_explanation: This is what happens to garlic and onions before they hit the pan. It's the "giniling" before it becomes giniling. Metaphorically, "tinadtad" is what happens to your report when your boss covers it in red marks and revisions. Or when someone gets multiple stab wounds in a crime show, "tinadtad ng saksak." It's all about being chopped into tiny little pieces, literally or figuratively.
usage_notes: Used as an adjective (e.g., "tinadtad na bawang") or a noun (e.g., "Ginamit niya ang tinadtad para sa lumpiang shanghai"). The verb form is "tadtarin".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magprito ka muna ng bawang na **tinadtad** bago ilagay ang baboy.","translation":"First, fry the **minced** garlic before adding the pork."},{"sentence":"Ang sisig ay gawa sa **tinadtad** na tenga at pisngi ng baboy.","translation":"Sisig is made from **finely chopped** pig's ears and cheeks."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mga gawain o katangian na masama, mapanlinlang, at maihahalintulad sa isang demonyo.
original_explanation: This is what your nanay calls your actions when you do something really naughty. It's the energy you bring when you plan a prank on your friends, or the 'kalokohan' you do when the boss isn't looking. Can range from playful mischief to actual evil deeds. 'Ano na namang kademonyuhan 'to?' is a classic Pinoy parent line.
usage_notes: Can be used seriously to mean 'evil' or hyperbolically to mean 'mischief' or 'naughtiness'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang gumawa ng anumang **kademonyuhan** habang wala ako.","translation":"Don't get into any **mischief** while I'm away."},{"sentence":"Ang mga krimen na iyon ay gawa ng purong **kademonyuhan**.","translation":"Those crimes are acts of pure **wickedness**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang instrumentong pangmusika na binubuo ng dalawang pirasong hugis-kabibe na gawa sa kahoy o ivory, pinatutunog sa pamamagitan ng pagpapatama sa isa't isa gamit ang mga daliri.
original_explanation: That clacky-clacky thingy you see flamenco dancers use. It's the Spanish-era fidget spinner. In school programs, they're usually made of two bottle caps (tansan) tied to a piece of cardboard. Resourcefulness!
usage_notes: A musical percussion instrument associated with Spanish dance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mananayaw ay mahusay na pinatutunog ang kanyang **kastanyetas** habang sumasayaw ng flamenco.","translation":"The dancer skillfully played her **castanets** while dancing the flamenco."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating bumili ng **kastanyetas** para sa presentasyon sa Filipino.","translation":"We need to buy **castanets** for the presentation in our Filipino class."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing tuyo o alisin ang pagkabasa o halumigmig ng isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pagpapahangin, pagbibilad sa araw, o paggamit ng tuwalya o ibang kagamitan.
etymology: From the causative prefix "pa-", the root word "tuyo" (dry), and the object-focus suffix "-in".
original_explanation: The official command given to the youngest sibling after washing the dishes. Also, what you try to do with your tears before your boss sees you crying over a spreadsheet. It's the act of making something wet become not wet, from laundry ('patuyuin ang sinampay') to a wound ('patuyuin ang sugat').
usage_notes: This is an object-focus verb. The object being dried is the grammatical subject of the sentence. Differentiated from 'patuyutin' which means to cause to wither.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **patuyuin** ang mga damit bago umulan.","translation":"The clothes need **to be dried** before it rains."},{"sentence":"**Patuyuin** mo muna ang buhok mo bago ka matulog.","translation":"**Dry** your hair first before you go to sleep."}]

meaning_filipino: Kumuha ng isang bagay na hindi sa iyo nang patago at karaniwang may maliit na halaga.
original_explanation: This isn't grand larceny. This is you "borrowing" a fry from your friend's McDo order when they're not looking. It's taking a small, almost insignificant thing without permission. "Sino ang umumit ng huling piraso ng pizza sa ref?"
usage_notes: Implies stealing something of small value or in small quantities, often sneakily.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahuli ng guro ang batang **umomit** ng krayola ng kanyang kaklase.","translation":"The teacher caught the child who **pilfered** his classmate's crayon."},{"sentence":"Mahirap magtiwala sa taong mahilig **umomit** kahit sa maliliit na bagay.","translation":"It's hard to trust a person who likes to **filch** even small things."}]

translation: to send; to convey; to cause to arrive
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapapunta o paghahatid ng isang bagay, mensahe, o tao sa isang tiyak na lugar o tao.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you want chismis to reach the intended person, but you don't want to be the one to say it directly. 'Pakisabi sa kanya...' is the starter pack. It's also what you do when you order from Shopee or Lazada – you're asking the seller to 'magparating' the item to your house.
usage_notes: The prefix 'magpa-' indicates causing someone or something to do the action of the root word. Here, it means to cause something/someone to 'dating' (arrive).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **magparating** ka ng balita kung ligtas kang nakauwi.","translation":"Please, **send** word if you arrived home safely."},{"sentence":"Nag-utos ang hepe na **magparating** ng tulong sa mga nasalanta ng bagyo.","translation":"The chief ordered to **send** aid to those affected by the typhoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapalabis o pagpapasobra sa paglalarawan ng isang bagay, pangyayari, o katangian.
original_explanation: ‘Yung sinabi mong "mamamatay ako sa gutom" kahit 15 minutes ka pa lang late kumain. O 'yung friend mong OA mag-react sa chismis, as in level 999 na eksaherasyon. It's the art of making a molehill into a Mount Apo.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit upang tukuyin ang sobrang paglalarawan o "OA" (over-acting) na reaksyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puro **eksaherasyon** lang naman ang mga kuwento niya para maging bida.","translation":"His stories are just full of **exaggeration** so he can be the hero."},{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na ang **eksaherasyon**, hindi naman ganoon kalaki ang problema.","translation":"Stop the **exaggeration**, the problem isn't that big."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paraan ng paggalaw, pagkilos, o pag-uugali ng isang tao o bagay. Ito ay maaaring tumukoy sa pisikal na galaw o sa kabuuang asal.
original_explanation: Your overall vibe in motion. It's your body language, your actions, your 'galawang-Breezy'. 'Ang kahina-hinala ng kilos niya.' (His/her actions are suspicious.) It's the non-verbal cues that tell you if someone is a potential friend, a marites in the making, or about to ask you for money.
usage_notes: A very versatile word. 'Kilos' can refer to a single movement or a general pattern of behavior.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagmasdan mong mabuti ang bawat **kilos** ng suspek.","translation":"Carefully observe the suspect's every **movement**."},{"sentence":"Nagbago ang kanyang **kilos** mula nang siya'y yumaman.","translation":"His **demeanor** changed ever since he got rich."}]

meaning_filipino: Simulan ang isang gawain, kaganapan, o proseso. Ito ang unang hakbang sa anumang pagkilos.
etymology: From `mag-` (verb prefix) + `umpisa` (start), which is from Spanish `empezar` (to begin).
original_explanation: What you tell yourself you'll do at 8 AM, but actually do at 10 AM after two cups of coffee and scrolling through TikTok. It’s the 'Game, na!' moment of any project. Also, the hardest part of writing a report or starting a diet.
usage_notes: A very common synonym for `magsimula`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailan tayo **mag-uumpisa** sa ating proyekto?","translation":"When will we **start** our project?"},{"sentence":"**Mag-umpisa** na tayong magluto para hindi tayo gabihin.","translation":"Let's **begin** cooking now so we won't be late into the night."}]

translation: to dress someone; to put clothes on someone
meaning_filipino: Suotan ng damit ang isang tao; lagyan ng kasuotan.
original_explanation: What parents do to their kids, what a stylist does to a celebrity, or what you do to your pet dog when it's cold. "Bihisan mo na 'yung bata, aalis na tayo." It's the act of putting clothes on another being.
usage_notes: This verb is transitive, requiring an object (the person/thing being dressed).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **bihisan** ang manika para sa kanyang parada.","translation":"Help me **dress** the doll for its parade."},{"sentence":"Maingat niyang **binihisan** ang kanyang lola na may sakit.","translation":"She carefully **dressed** her sick grandmother."}]

meaning_filipino: Madaling magkasakit o may mahinang pangangatawan.
etymology: Hindi tiyak ang pinagmulan, ngunit maaaring may kaugnayan sa "dala" (carry) na parang "may dalang" sakit.
original_explanation: This is your friend who always has a cough, a cold, or some mysterious ailment. Change lang ng weather, may sakit na. Uminom lang ng malamig, sinisipon na. Sila yung laging may baon na Vicks, Biogesic, at Katinko. The poster child for "bawal sa pagod".
usage_notes: Naglalarawan sa pangkalahatang estado ng kalusugan ng isang tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mula pagkabata ay **dalahikin** na si Ana kaya laging pinag-iingat ng kanyang ina.","translation":"Ana has been **sickly** since childhood, so her mother always tells her to be careful."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpuyat masyado at baka maging **dalahikin** ka.","translation":"Don't stay up late too often or you might become **prone to illness**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtatanim ng mga buto o binhi, karaniwan sa isang kamang taniman (seedbed) bago ilipat sa permanenteng lugar.
original_explanation: This is what your lola does with her tomato seeds before they get their own pots. It's like the "soft launch" of a plant's life. Sa negosyo, ito 'yung pag-invest ng maliit na capital sa isang idea, hoping it will grow into a big venture. Nagpu-punla ka ng good karma 'pag tinulungan mo 'yung officemate mong 'di marunong mag-Excel.
usage_notes: Often used in agriculture, but can be used metaphorically for ideas, values, or feelings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magpunla** ng mga bagong binhi para sa susunod na anihan.","translation":"We need to **sow** new seeds for the next harvest."},{"sentence":"**Nagpunla** siya ng pag-asa sa puso ng mga nawalan.","translation":"He **planted** hope in the hearts of the lost."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maranasan ang pagdaloy ng koryente sa katawan na nagdudulot ng biglaang pagyanig, sakit, o pinsala.
original_explanation: That zapping feeling when you touch a faulty appliance or a live wire you weren't supposed to touch. It's the universe's spicy way of telling you to call an electrician. Also used metaphorically for a sudden, shocking realization, like seeing your ex with your best friend. "Parang nakoryente ako nung nakita ko sila."
usage_notes: Primarily refers to a literal electric shock, but its metaphorical use for a sudden jolt of surprise or shock is also common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa pagsaksak niyan baka ka **makoryente**.","translation":"Be careful plugging that in, you might **get an electric shock**."},{"sentence":"Nanginginig pa rin siya matapos **makoryente** sa sirang plantsa.","translation":"He is still trembling after **getting an electric shock** from the broken iron."}]

meaning_filipino: Inanod o tinangay ng isang malakas na puwersa tulad ng hangin, alon, o agos patungo sa isang partikular na lugar.
original_explanation: This is you after payday, getting carried away by the currents of Shopee and Lazada sales until you're **ipinadpad** to the shores of 'petsa de peligro'. In a more dramatic sense, it's that feeling of being lost, where life just takes you. 'Saan na ba ako ipinadpad ng tadhana?'
usage_notes: Often used in literary or dramatic contexts to describe being carried by forces of nature or fate.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang maliit na bangka ay **ipinadpad** ng malakas na bagyo sa kabilang isla.","translation":"The small boat **was drifted** by the strong storm to the other island."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa pag-ibig, tila **ipinadpad** siya sa isang mundong hindi niya kilala.","translation":"Because of love, it was as if he **was carried away** to a world he did not know."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na mahilig mang-asar o mambiro sa iba sa paraang mapaglaro.
original_explanation: Ito yung tropa mong professional mang-asar. Hindi sila bully, pero expert sa friendly fire. Sila yung unang-unang pupuna sa bago mong gupit o sa suot mong damit, pero sila rin yung tatawa kasama mo. The life of the party, pero minsan gusto mo na ring batukan. Sila ang certified 'manunudyo' ng barkada.
usage_notes: Often used to describe someone who is habitually playful or a bit of a prankster. Can be seen as a slightly more formal version of 'mang-aasar'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala si Pedro bilang isang **manunudyo** sa kanilang klase.","translation":"Pedro is known as a **teaser** in their class."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong pansinin ang **manunudyo**, nagbibiro lang iyan.","translation":"Don't mind the **jester**, he's just kidding."}]

meaning_filipino: Dilaan ang isang ibabaw upang alisin ang nakadikit dito, tulad ng pagkain sa daliri o plato.
original_explanation: That moment when you've got some sweet condensed milk on your finger after making yema cake, and you lick it clean. That's himuran. It's licking something *off* a surface, usually your own fingers or a plate. It's the final act of 'sayang naman.'
usage_notes: This verb has a locative focus (-an suffix), emphasizing the surface from which something is licked. Contrast with 'himurin', which focuses on the object being licked clean.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **himuran** ang daliri mo sa harap ng mga bisita.","translation":"Don't **lick** your finger (to clean it) in front of the guests."},{"sentence":"Nasarapan ang bata kaya't halos **himuran** na niya ang plato.","translation":"The child enjoyed it so much he almost **licked** the plate clean."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mahabang sulating pananaliksik sa isang partikular na paksa, lalo na ang isinusulat para sa isang doktoral na antas sa unibersidad.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung final boss sa college, lalo na sa grad school. 'Yung isang libong pahinang document na puno ng dugo, pawis, at puyat mo. Ang disertasyon ay parang napakahabang love letter mo sa subject na pinag-aaralan mo, na sana ay basahin at aprubahan ng panel.
usage_notes: A formal, academic term. Often used interchangeably with 'tesis' (thesis), although 'disertasyon' is technically for a doctorate.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ilang taon niyang ginawa ang kanyang **disertasyon** bago makapagtapos.","translation":"He worked on his **dissertation** for several years before graduating."},{"sentence":"Ang paksa ng kanyang **disertasyon** ay tungkol sa kasaysayan ng wikang Filipino.","translation":"The topic of her **dissertation** is about the history of the Filipino language."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babae na kapareho ng pangalan ng iba; katukayo.
original_explanation: That moment in class when the teacher calls "Maria!" and three people look up. You're all tokaya to each other. It's a free pass to call someone "pangalan" (name) when you're feeling friendly. The masculine form is 'tokayo'.
usage_notes: The masculine form 'tokayo' is more commonly heard, but 'tokaya' is the correct form for a female namesake. Often used as a friendly term of address.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Ana at ang kanyang **tokaya** ay parehong magaling kumanta.","translation":"Ana and her **namesake** are both good at singing."},{"sentence":"Uy, **tokaya**! Kamusta ka na?","translation":"Hey, **namesake**! How are you?"}]

meaning_filipino: May kalakip na matinding pagmamahal, pagtingin, o pagkagusto na malumanay at magiliw.
original_explanation: How your lola looks at you when you visit her in the province. It's that warm, fuzzy, affectionate vibe, full of tenderness. It's less intense than "pagmamahal" and more about sweet fondness. Often seen in old love letters and haranas.
usage_notes: A somewhat formal or literary phrase expressing deep affection.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinanggap niya **buong paggiliw** ang alay na bulaklak ng binata.","translation":"She accepted the young man's flower offering **with full affection**."},{"sentence":"Inalagaan ng ina ang kanyang maysakit na anak **buong paggiliw**.","translation":"The mother cared for her sick child **with fondness**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pagsasaka kung saan ang mga puno at halaman sa isang bahagi ng kagubatan ay pinuputol at sinusunog upang gawing taniman ang lupa.
etymology: Ang etimolohiya ay hindi tiyak, ngunit ito ay isang katutubong salitang Austronesian.
original_explanation: This is the OG method of clearing land for farming, but it's now mostly known for being super illegal and bad for the environment. You chop down trees, burn everything, and then plant crops. It's the reason you see huge plumes of smoke from mountains sometimes. It's a hot-button environmental issue, literally.
usage_notes: Madalas na iniuugnay sa iligal na pagtotroso at pagkakalbo ng kagubatan. Ang mismong akto ay tinatawag na 'pagkakaingin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagbabawal ng batas ang pagsasagawa ng **kaingin**.","translation":"The law prohibits the practice of **slash-and-burn agriculture**."},{"sentence":"Ang malawakang **kaingin** ay isa sa mga sanhi ng pagbabago ng klima.","translation":"Widespread **slash-and-burn farming** is one of the causes of climate change."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aalok ng isang bagay, tulad ng bahay, sasakyan, o kagamitan, para sa pansamantalang paggamit kapalit ng bayad.
original_explanation: Your side hustle when you have an extra condo unit in Tagaytay or a van that isn't always used. You post it on Facebook Marketplace and **ipaarkila** it for a daily or monthly rate. It's the general term for making money off your stuff without selling it.
usage_notes: A more general term than 'ipaarenda'. Used for renting out things like vehicles, apartments, rooms, equipment, gowns, etc.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinasya niyang **ipaarkila** ang isang kwarto sa kanyang bahay para sa mga estudyante.","translation":"She decided **to rent out** a room in her house to students."},{"sentence":"Magkano ang **ipaarkila** ng van para sa isang araw?","translation":"How much is it **to have a van rented out** for one day?"}]

meaning_filipino: Inayos nang mabuti; nasa tamang pagkakasunod-sunod. Sa kontekstong panrelihiyon, ito ay tumutukoy sa isang taong pormal na itinalaga bilang isang pari o ministro.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'ordenado', na nangangahulugang 'maayos' o 'naordinahan'.
original_explanation: The state of your room for the 5 minutes after you clean it. It's Marie Kondo's favorite word. "Ordenado lahat ng files ko!" is something you say to impress your boss. It can also mean being officially made a priest, which is like being 'ordered' by God into service.
usage_notes: The 'neat/orderly' meaning is more common in general conversation. The 'ordained' meaning is specific to religion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ni nanay na laging **ordenado** ang mga gamit sa bahay.","translation":"My mother wants the things in the house to always be **orderly**."},{"sentence":"Siya ay **ordenado** bilang pari noong isang taon.","translation":"He was **ordained** as a priest last year."}]

translation: to gore, to butt with horns
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-atake o pagtulak gamit ang sungay, tulad ng ginagawa ng kalabaw, baka, o kambing.
original_explanation: The OG 'headbutt'. This is what a carabao or goat does when it's angry or feeling feisty. It's the animal equivalent of a 'suntukan sa labas' challenge, but with horns. You don't want to be on the receiving end of this.
usage_notes: This is the root word. The actor-focus verb form is 'sumuag' and the object-focus form is 'isuag' or 'suagin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-ingat ang magsasaka dahil baka **sumuag** ang alaga niyang kalabaw.","translation":"The farmer was careful because his pet carabao might **gore** him."},{"sentence":"Biglang sinuag ng kambing ang bakod.","translation":"The goat suddenly **butted** the fence."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng baril na may mahabang tubo at walang ukit sa loob (smoothbore), na karaniwang nagpapaputok ng maraming maliliit na bala (pellets) nang sabay-sabay.
original_explanation: That big gun you see in action movies that makes a loud 'BOOM' and can take out a whole group of zombies in one shot. Farmers in the province might have an old iskopeta to scare away wild boars. Definitely not your friendly neighborhood water gun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **iskopeta** ang sandata ng guwardiya sa bangko.","translation":"A **shotgun** was the weapon of the guard at the bank."}]

translation: to cause anxiety; to cause unease/worry
meaning_filipino: Ang maging sanhi ng pag-aalala, pagkabalisa, o hindi pagkapalagay ng loob ng isang tao.
etymology: Mula sa panlaping 'ika-' (panlaping sanhi) at 'bagabag' (worry, anxiety).
original_explanation: That feeling you get when your boss messages you "Can we talk?" on a Friday afternoon. Or when your partner says "We need to talk." 'Yun 'yung bagay na ikinabagabag mo buong weekend. It's the source of your low-key panic and overthinking.
usage_notes: Ang panlaping 'ika-' dito ay isang panlaping sanhi (causative prefix), na nagsasaad na ang isang bagay ang sanhi ng damdaming inilalarawan ng salitang-ugat. Madalas itong ginagamit sa anyong pangnakaraan/perpektibo na 'ikinabagabag'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang biglaang pagkawala niya ay **ikinabagabag** ng kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"His sudden disappearance **caused anxiety** for his parents."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ikabagabag** ang mga bagay na wala kang kontrol.","translation":"Don't let things you can't control **cause you unease**."}]

translation: to make heavier; to add weight to
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagdaragdag ng bigat o pabigat sa isang bagay, sitwasyon, o damdamin.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "bigat" (weight) at hulaping "-an".
original_explanation: Yung feeling na may problema ka na, tapos dinagdagan pa ng isa. 'Huwag mo nang bigatan ang dibdib ko!' is the classic hugot line. It's like you're already carrying your team in a game, tapos biglang nag-lag yung internet mo. You're adding weight to an already heavy situation.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin sa literal na pagdaragdag ng timbang o sa metaporikal na paraan para sa problema o emosyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang **bigatan** ang problema sa pamamagitan ng pagsisinungaling.","translation":"Don't **make the problem heavier** by lying."},{"sentence":"**Binigatan** niya ang dulo ng lambat para lumubog ito sa tubig.","translation":"He **added weight** to the end of the net so it would sink in the water."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat ng mga tao na nagtutulungan upang makamit ang isang karaniwang layunin, lalo na sa larangan ng palakasan, trabaho, o proyekto.
original_explanation: In the Philippines, 'team' is everything. It's your BPO team struggling to hit metrics, your basketball team sa kanto, your family group chat named 'Team Last Name,' or even the 'team building' you're forced to go on. It's the official word for 'samahan ng mga nagdadamayan (o nagtsitsismisan).'
usage_notes: Widely used in business, sports, and casual settings. Often used directly in Tagalog sentences.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan magtulungan ang buong **team** para manalo sa kumpetisyon.","translation":"The whole **team** needs to work together to win the competition."},{"sentence":"May team building kami sa Batangas sa susunod na buwan.","translation":"Our **team** has a team building in Batangas next month."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtindig o pagiging nasa posisyong bertikal; ang posisyon o paninindigan sa isang isyu.
original_explanation: This is the 'stand' in 'stand for your rights' or 'stand up straight!' Your lola will shout 'Tumayo ka!' when you're slouching. This is the root word for that action. It's the opposite of 'higa' (lie down) and 'upo' (sit).
usage_notes: The pronunciation is key: stress is on the second syllable /ta-YO/, unlike the pronoun 'tayo' /TA-yo/. This word is the root for verbs like 'tumayo' (to stand up), 'magtayo' (to build/establish), and nouns like 'pagtayo' (the act of standing).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **tayo** mo sa isyung ito?","translation":"What is your **stand** on this issue?"},{"sentence":"Nakakangawit ang **tayo** nang matagal sa pila.","translation":"It's tiring **standing** for a long time in line."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa katangian ng pagkain, lalo na ng karne, na mahirap nguyain o kainin dahil sa pagiging makunat o matigas.
original_explanation: The mortal enemy of anyone with dentures. It's that piece of steak you've been chewing for five minutes and it feels like you're chewing on a rubber slipper. Not hard like a rock, but tough and fibrous. That 'overcooked adobo' texture. Your jaw will get a workout. 'Bes, 'wag mo nang i-serve 'yung baka, sobrang ganit!'
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used to describe food, particularly meat that is difficult to chew.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **ganit** ang litson kawali dahil napasobra sa pagprito.","translation":"The fried pork belly became **tough** because it was over-fried."},{"sentence":"Ayokong kumain sa karinderyang iyon dahil laging **ganit** ang karne nila.","translation":"I don't like eating at that eatery because their meat is always **leathery**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng legal na pagsasakdal o paghabla sa isang tao sa korte; o ang malupit at walang-tigil na pagtrato dahil sa lahi, relihiyon, o paniniwala.
original_explanation: This is a heavy word. It's what happens when someone is relentlessly pursued, either legally (like a fiscal filing a case) or unjustly (like historical persecution). Think of it as the 'Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney' level of accusation, but with real-world, serious consequences. It's the opposite of being left alone.
usage_notes: Has a strong legal and historical connotation. Can mean both legal prosecution and social/political persecution.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pag-usig** sa mga suspek ay sinimulan na ng piskalya.","translation":"The **prosecution** of the suspects has been initiated by the fiscal."},{"sentence":"Maraming bayani ang dumanas ng **pag-usig** sa ilalim ng mga mananakop.","translation":"Many heroes suffered **persecution** under the colonizers."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lumang anyo ng salitang "bawat," na nangangahulugang isa-isa o lahat ng kasapi sa isang pangkat.
original_explanation: This is the lolo/lola version of 'bawat'. It's like saying 'thou' instead of 'you'. You'd probably only hear this in old movies or from a very, very traditional relative. It means 'each' or 'every'. Today, we just say 'bawat'.
usage_notes: Malaking bahagi na pinalitan ng 'bawat' sa modernong Tagalog. Ang pangunahing gamit nito sa ngayon ay bilang salitang-ugat, bagaman ang 'bawas' ang mas karaniwang kinikilalang ugat para sa 'bawahan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **bawa** isa ay may tungkulin.","translation":"**Each** one has a duty."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mensahe, senyas, o bagay na nagsisilbing panggising sa alaala tungkol sa isang bagay na dapat gawin o tandaan.
etymology: From `pa-` (causative prefix) + `alala` (remember). Literally, "something that causes remembering".
original_explanation: Your phone notification, the sticky note on your monitor, or your mom shouting "Magdala ka ng payong!" (Bring an umbrella!) before you leave. These are all forms of 'paalala'. It's the "friendly reminder" in a work email that's not actually friendly and means "do this now." It's also the "Babala" (warning) signs that serve as a 'paalala' not to do something stupid.
usage_notes: Very common in both formal (e.g., public announcements) and informal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-iwan siya ng **paalala** sa ref para hindi niya makalimutan ang bibilhin.","translation":"She left a **reminder** on the fridge so she wouldn't forget what to buy."},{"sentence":"Isang mahalagang **paalala**: magsuot ng face mask sa lahat ng oras.","translation":"An important **notice**: wear a face mask at all times."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gawain na isinasagawa para sa kasiyahan o pag-aaliw sa mga malayang oras.
original_explanation: Your **libangan** is your 'sana all' skill that you're actually good at. For tito's, it's golf or biking. For tita's, it might be 'plantita' duties or baking. For Gen Z, it's making TikTok videos or playing Mobile Legends. It's your personal stress-reliever that doesn't involve spending your entire 13th-month pay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paghahardin ang kanyang naging **libangan** ngayong pandemya.","translation":"Gardening became her **hobby** during the pandemic."},{"sentence":"Ano ang paborito mong **libangan**?","translation":"What is your favorite **pastime**?"}]

translation: to cure or smoke meat/fish; to make 'tapa'
meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pag-iimbak ng karne o isda sa pamamagitan ng pagpapatuyo, pag-aasin, o pagpapausok.
original_explanation: This is the OG Filipino food preservation technique. Before refrigerators, our ancestors would magtapa to make meat last longer. Now, it's the sacred process of creating the star of your favorite tapsilog breakfast. It's basically giving meat a smoky, salty spa day.
usage_notes: Refers to the process of making 'tapa', which is cured meat, usually beef.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig si Lola na **magtapa** ng baboy-ramo tuwing may nahuhuli si Lolo.","translation":"Grandma loves to **make tapa** from wild boar whenever Grandpa catches one."},{"sentence":"Naisipan nilang **magtapa** ng isda para hindi masira ang mga sobrang huli.","translation":"They decided to **smoke** the fish so the extra catch wouldn't spoil."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtungo o paglipat sa isang partikular na lugar, direksyon, o destinasyon.
original_explanation: The most basic 'Tara!' starter pack. It's the verb for when you're leaving your current spot to be in another. Whether it's 'punta sa mall,' 'punta sa office,' or 'punta na sa next life,' it's all about movement to a destination. Often used in commands or questions.
usage_notes: This is the root word form, often used in commands ('Punta ka doon!') or as a noun-like verb in questions ('Saan ang punta mo?'). The conjugated form is 'pumunta'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Punta** ka na sa palengke bago pa magsara.","translation":"**Go** to the market now before it closes."},{"sentence":"Saan ang **punta** ninyong magbabarkada?","translation":"Where are you and your friends **going**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi nag-iiba ang kalagayan, anyo, o katangian; nananatili sa dati.
original_explanation: 'The only thing that is constant is change,' but this word is the exception. It means 'unchanging' or 'stagnant.' It can be a good thing, like your friend's 'walang-pagbabagong' loyalty. But it can also be a bad thing, like your crush's relationship status na 'in a relationship' at 'walang-pagbabago' for years. Ouch.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mula noon hanggang ngayon, **walang-pagbabago** ang kanyang pagtingin sa iyo.","translation":"From then until now, his feelings for you are **unchanging**."},{"sentence":"Nananatiling **walang-pagbabago** ang presyo ng bigas sa palengke.","translation":"The price of rice in the market remains **constant**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ligaya, galak, o pang-akit (bihirang gamit, kadalasang ugat ng salitang maigaya).
Naglalarawan sa isang gawain na hindi madali o isang estado ng kakulangan sa yaman o pangangailangan.
original_explanation: Two meanings here. First, it's that feeling when you're trying to solve a math problem: 'Medyo may-kahirapan 'tong exam.' (This exam is a bit difficult). Second, it's the more serious, socio-economic reality: 'Isang pamilyang may-kahirapan sa buhay.' (A family experiencing poverty). It's a slightly more formal way of saying 'mahirap.'
usage_notes: Can refer to the difficulty of a task or the state of being poor. Context is key to differentiate between 'difficult' and 'impoverished'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagsusulit ay **may-kahirapan** kaya't kailangan mong mag-aral nang mabuti.","translation":"The test is **difficult** so you need to study well."},{"sentence":"Marami siyang pinagdaanan dahil lumaki siya sa pamilyang **may-kahirapan**.","translation":"He went through a lot because he grew up in an **impoverished** family."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan na ginagamit sa pagsakal o pagbitay sa isang tao, karaniwang binubuo ng isang pisi, kadena, o alambre na hinihigpitan sa leeg. Ginagamit din bilang pandiwa na tumutukoy sa akto ng pagsakal gamit ito.
original_explanation: This is some dark history stuff. Think Spanish colonial era execution method. It's the ultimate, brutal "I can't breathe." In modern, less literal terms, it's what you feel when you see your Meralco bill after a month of WFH with the aircon on 24/7.
usage_notes: Associated with historical execution methods in the Philippines, most famously with the Gomburza priests.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Gomburza ay pinarusahan sa pamamagitan ng **garote**.","translation":"The Gomburza were executed by means of the **garrote**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lalaking kamag-anak na kapatid ng ama o ina; pormal na tawag sa tiyo.
etymology: Mula sa "tiyo" at hulaping "-in", na nagpapahiwatig ng relasyon.
original_explanation: The formal, almost biblical way of saying 'uncle'. You'd probably read this in a textbook or hear it in a historical drama. It's what you call your 'tiyo' when you're writing a formal essay about your family tree.
usage_notes: More formal and less common in casual conversation than 'tiyo' or 'tito'. It's often used when referring to an uncle in the third person rather than as a direct address.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **tiyuhin** ay isang tanyag na doktor.","translation":"His **uncle** is a famous doctor."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga produktong pagkain na inilagay at isinara sa loob ng lata upang mapreserba.
original_explanation: The official food of typhoons, long weekends, and every Filipino student's dorm life. Sardinas, corned beef, luncheon meat—the holy trinity of 'yaring-lata'. Your go-to when you're too tired/broke to cook a proper meal.
usage_notes: Often used in its plural form 'mga yaring-lata'. Refers specifically to preserved food in cans.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-imbak kami ng maraming **yaring-lata** bilang paghahanda sa paparating na bagyo.","translation":"We stocked up on a lot of **canned goods** in preparation for the coming typhoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa kalagayan ng paghiga o pagpapahinga nang nakalapat ang katawan sa isang ibabaw.
original_explanation: The default state of a person on a Sunday, or after a long shift. 'Yung humihiga ka na lang sa sahig sa pagod at nag-iisip kung para saan ba lahat ng pinapasan mo. #AdultingIsHard. Ito rin 'yung ginagawa mo habang nag-i-scroll sa phone hanggang 3 AM.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagod na pagod si tatay kaya **humihiga** na siya sa sopa.","translation":"Dad is very tired, so he **is lying down** on the sofa now."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **humihiga** diyan sa sahig, madumi!","translation":"Don't **lie down** there on the floor, it's dirty!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na pumapalit sa tungkulin o trabaho ng iba para sa isang takdang panahon; pamalit.
original_explanation: The BPO and medical field's favorite word. Ito yung a-angle mo sa ka-team mo, "Uy, rilyebo muna, CR lang ako!" Your rilyebo is your savior, the person who takes over your post so you can finally take that much-needed break. Sila ang tunay na MVP ng shift.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang **rilyebo** mo mamayang gabi sa ospital?","translation":"Who is your **substitute** at the hospital tonight?"},{"sentence":"Hinihintay ko na lang dumating ang aking **rilyebo** bago ako umuwi.","translation":"I'm just waiting for my **relief** to arrive before I go home."}]

translation: to turn silver-colored; to become silver
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon o pagbabago tungo sa kulay na katulad ng pilak.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your parents' hair, and eventually yours. It's nature's way of giving you highlights for free. Also describes the moon's reflection on the water, giving it that romantic, movie-scene vibe.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa paraang patula o upang ilarawan ang pagtanda (pag-uban ng buhok).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula nang **magkulay-pilak** ang buhok ng aking ama.","translation":"My father's hair has started to **turn silver-colored**."},{"sentence":"Ang dagat ay tila **nagkulay-pilak** sa tama ng sinag ng buwan.","translation":"The sea seemed to **become silver** under the moon's rays."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginamit ang mga kuko, daliri, o isang bagay upang kudkurin ang balat, karaniwan dahil sa pangangati.
original_explanation: 'Yung automatic reaction mo 'pag kinagat ka ng lamok. O 'yung ginagawa mo sa ulo mo 'pag 'di mo masagutan 'yung math problem. "Hala, ba't ka kumamot ng braso? May allergy ka ba diyan sa ex mong bumabalik?"
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya napigilang **kumamot** sa braso dahil sa kagat ng lamok.","translation":"He couldn't help but **scratch** his arm because of the mosquito bite."},{"sentence":"**Kumamot** siya sa ulo habang nag-iisip ng tamang sagot.","translation":"He **scratched** his head while thinking of the right answer."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa lasa na maasim at mapait na nagdudulot ng tila pag-urong ng bibig, tulad ng lasa ng hilaw na prutas.
original_explanation: This is the taste that makes your face scrunch up. Think unripe mangoes or bananas. It's not just sour, it's not just bitter, it's that "dry" kind of bitterness. Figuratively, it's a bitter, sarcastic smile. "Isang mapaklang ngiti ang isinukli niya." It's the taste of disappointment.
usage_notes: Primarily used for taste, but also common in literature to describe a bitter or forced smile/laugh.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **mapaklang** lasa ng hilaw na saging ay hindi masarap.","translation":"The **acrid** taste of an unripe banana is not delicious."},{"sentence":"Tumawa siya nang **mapakla** nang malaman ang katotohanan.","translation":"She laughed **bitterly** when she learned the truth."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal at nakatutuwang paraan ng pagbaybay at pagbigkas ng salitang Ingles na 'videos'.
etymology: Isang mapaglaro at ponetikong pagbaybay ng salitang Ingles na 'videos'.
original_explanation: This is how your tita who just discovered TikTok says "videos." It's the jeje/beki-fied version, born from our love of phonetic spelling. You use this when you're being cute or funny online. "Pa-send naman ng mga **pideos** ng pusa mo!"
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa napaka-impormal, madalas na nakakatawa o 'cutesy' na konteksto sa online.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang dami kong tawa sa mga nakakatawang **pideos** na napanood ko sa Facebook.","translation":"I laughed so hard at the funny **videos** I watched on Facebook."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglubog o pagbabad ng isang bagay sa likido. Sa matalinhagang kahulugan, ito ay ang pakikialam sa usapan o gawain ng iba.
