original_explanation: Literally, it's what you do with your chicharon in vinegar or your pandesal in coffee. Figuratively, it's what you do when you butt into a conversation that isn't yours. "Huwag kang sumawsaw sa usapan ng may usapan!" is the polite way of saying "Mind your own business." The act of being a 'sawsawera/sawsawero'.
usage_notes: Has both a literal meaning (dipping food) and a common figurative meaning (meddling). The figurative use is often derogatory.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap **isawsaw** ang pritong manok sa gravy.","translation":"It's delicious to **dip** the fried chicken in gravy."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **sumawsaw** sa anumang tsismis na kaniyang marinig.","translation":"She loves to **meddle** in any gossip she hears."}]

translation: to feel inferior, to be overshadowed
meaning_filipino: Maramdaman ang pagiging mas mababa o mas dehado kumpara sa iba; malit o mapailalim sa kapangyarihan o galing ng iba.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're in a group project and there's that one "bibo kid" who does everything perfectly, and you just end up... there. You're not useless, but next to them, you feel like a side character in their "bida" story. That's mangilalim. It's the emotional equivalent of being stuck in the shadow of a much taller building.
usage_notes: Describes a psychological or social feeling of being less than someone else.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mangilalim** sa kanila; may sarili ka ring galing.","translation":"Don't **feel inferior** to them; you have your own talents."},{"sentence":"Sa sobrang galing ng kanyang kasama sa entablado, nagsimula siyang **mangilalim**.","translation":"Because his stage partner was so good, he started to **be overshadowed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang indibidwal na may masamang hangarin, gumagawa ng kasamaan sa kapwa, at walang mabuting kalooban.
original_explanation: The kontrabida in your life's teleserye. They borrow money and never pay it back, they spread fake chismis, they cut in line at the MRT. Basically, someone you wouldn't want to be stuck in an elevator with.
usage_notes: A direct and strong term for a person perceived as morally corrupt or wicked.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang magtiwala sa kanya, isa siyang **masamang tao**.","translation":"Don't trust him, he is a **bad person**."},{"sentence":"Hindi ako naniniwala na mayroong taong likas na **masama**; nagiging ganoon lang sila dahil sa mga karanasan.","translation":"I don't believe that there are inherently **evil people**; they just become that way because of their experiences."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginagamit upang magpakilala ng isang ideya na salungat o naiiba sa naunang nabanggit.
original_explanation: This is the formal, 'maka-Lolo Jose Rizal' way of saying 'actually...' or 'on the contrary...' It's the word you use to pivot and correct a statement. 'Hindi siya galit, bagkus nagtatampo lamang.' You won't hear this in everyday chismisan, but you'll see it in textbooks, legal documents, or a very dramatic formal speech.
usage_notes: A formal or literary conjunction. In casual speech, "kundi" or "sa halip" are more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi layunin ng batas na magpahirap, **bagkus** ay magbigay ng kaayusan.","translation":"The law's purpose is not to oppress, **but rather** to provide order."},{"sentence":"Hindi siya nagtagumpay dahil sa suwerte, **bagkus** ay dahil sa kanyang sipag at tiyaga.","translation":"He did not succeed because of luck, **on the contrary**, it was because of his diligence and perseverance."}]

translation: to pretend to be knowledgeable; to act like a know-it-all
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapanggap o pagkukunwaring may malawak na kaalaman sa isang paksa, kadalasan nang walang sapat na batayan.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `mag-` + salitang-ugat na `dunong` (kaalaman) + pag-uulit na `dunungan` na nagpapahiwatig ng pagkukunwari.
original_explanation: Eto yung tropa mong kakapanood lang ng isang YouTube tutorial, akala mo kung sinong expert na. Sila yung unang-unang nagko-comment sa Facebook posts na may "Well, actually..." kahit mali naman. The classic 'know-it-all' na bida-bida sa group project.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin na may negatibong konotasyon upang ilarawan ang isang taong mayabang o nakakainis dahil sa kanyang pagpapanggap na maraming alam.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magdunung-dunungan** sa harap ng mga tunay na eksperto at baka mapahiya ka lang.","translation":"Don't **act like a know-it-all** in front of real experts, you might just get embarrassed."},{"sentence":"Naiinis ako sa kanya kasi mahilig siyang **magdunung-dunungan** sa aming mga meeting.","translation":"I get annoyed with him because he likes to **pretend to be knowledgeable** during our meetings."}]

meaning_filipino: Malambot na pagkain, karaniwang lugaw o niligis na prutas at gulay, na ipinapakain sa mga sanggol o sa mga taong hirap ngumuya.
etymology: From Spanish 'papa' (potato), which was generalized to mean any soft, mashed food.
original_explanation: Baby food, basically. Before there was Cerelac, there was 'pap'. It's that mushy, bland-looking stuff you feed to someone who can't handle a steak just yet—either a baby or your lolo without his pustiso (dentures).
usage_notes: This word is becoming less common in urban areas, often replaced by brand names or more specific terms like 'lugaw' or 'baby food'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghanda si nanay ng **pap** na gawa sa kalabasa para sa bunso.","translation":"Mom prepared a **mush** made of squash for the youngest child."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mapatawan ng multa o parusang salapi dahil sa paglabag sa isang batas o regulasyon.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you get caught jaywalking, color-coding, or returning a library book late. It's the universe (or the MMDA) telling you, "You messed up, now pay up." It's the financial consequence of your actions, the adult version of having your allowance cut.
usage_notes: This is a passive verb form; the subject is the one receiving the fine. The active form is "magmulta" (to impose a fine).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tiyak na **mamumultahan** ka kapag nahuli kang walang face mask sa pampublikong lugar.","translation":"You will surely **be fined** if you're caught without a face mask in a public place."},{"sentence":"**Namultahan** ang drayber dahil sa ilegal na pagparada.","translation":"The driver **was fined** for illegal parking."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang takdang petsa o oras kung kailan kailangang makumpleto o maipasa ang isang gawain, proyekto, o tungkulin.
original_explanation: The most feared word by students and BPO employees alike. It's that imaginary line that, once crossed, unleashes the wrath of your boss or professor. The cause of countless sleepless nights, coffee overdoses, and prayers to saints you didn't even know existed. "Yung deadline na bukas, pero 'in progress' pa rin ang status mo."
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang salitang hiram na ginagamit sa mga opisina, paaralan, at sa pangkalahatang usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating habulin ang **deadline** para sa proyekto.","translation":"We need to rush to meet the **deadline** for the project."},{"sentence":"Ano ang **deadline** ng pagpasa ng mga papeles?","translation":"What is the **deadline** for submitting the papers?"}]

translation: to make someone carry a burden
meaning_filipino: Iatas o ipagawa sa isang tao ang pagdadala ng isang mabigat na bagay sa balikat o likod; o, atangan ng isang mabigat na responsibilidad o problema.
original_explanation: This is what your boss does when they go on vacation and leave you with all their work. You've been **papagpasanin**-ed. It's also what happens when you're the 'panganay' (eldest child) and suddenly you're responsible for your siblings' life choices.
usage_notes: Can be used for both physical burdens (e.g., a sack of rice) and metaphorical ones (e.g., problems, responsibilities).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **papagpasanin** ng lahat ng problema ang iyong mga magulang.","translation":"Don't **make your parents carry the burden** of all your problems."},{"sentence":"Ang mga kabayo ay **pinagpasan** ng mabibigat na sako ng bigas.","translation":"The horses were **made to carry** heavy sacks of rice."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaikling salita para sa "notipikasyon"; isang mensahe o babala na natatanggap sa gadyet o social media.
original_explanation: Short for "notification." Ito yung dahilan kung bakit di mo maiwan-iwan ang phone mo. That little red dot that gives you a mini-heart attack, hoping it's from your crush but it's just another Shopee sale update. "May notif ka from HR." Uh oh.
usage_notes: Used primarily in digital and social media contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno na naman ng **notif** ang cellphone ko galing sa group chat.","translation":"My phone is full of **notifications** again from the group chat."},{"sentence":"Hinihintay ko ang **notif** na 'Your order has been shipped'.","translation":"I'm waiting for the **notification** that says 'Your order has been shipped'."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagbabalik sa dating mabuting kalagayan, kaayusan, o relasyon.
original_explanation: This is the "Balikan na tayo" phase. It's the act of fixing something broken, whether it's a friendship after a big fight, restoring an old house, or bringing back the good old days. It's about making things whole again.
usage_notes: A formal and somewhat deep word. 'Panunumbalik' is a more common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapanag-uli** ng kanilang pagkakaibigan ay naganap pagkatapos ng isang matagal na pag-uusap.","translation":"The **reconciliation** of their friendship happened after a long conversation."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao o bagay na kaakit-akit sa pisikal na paraan; mayroong pang-akit na sekswal.
original_explanation: The ultimate compliment from your tita after you've lost 5 lbs. It's not just about looks, it can also be a vibe. "Ang seksi ng boses niya!" (His/Her voice is so sexy!) or "Seksi 'yang kotse mo!" (Your car is sexy!). It's the Filipino stamp of "hotness approval."
usage_notes: Isang salitang hiram na ganap nang bahagi ng wikang Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming nagsasabi na **seksi** si Anne Curtis.","translation":"Many say that Anne Curtis is **sexy**."},{"sentence":"Naging usap-usapan ang kanyang **seksi** na kasuotan sa party.","translation":"Her **sexy** outfit at the party became the talk of the town."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng isang kasangkapan upang hatiin o tanggalin ang isang bahagi mula sa kabuuan.
original_explanation: The command your mom gives you when she sees your long hair, or what you do to your ex out of your life. 'Mag-move on ka na, i-cut mo na communication!' It's also what you shouldn't do in class, unless you want to face your teacher's wrath.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magputol** ng mga tuyong sanga ng puno.","translation":"You need to **cut** the dry branches of the tree."},{"sentence":"Nagdesisyon siyang **magputol** ng ugnayan sa kanyang mga masasamang kaibigan.","translation":"She decided to **sever** ties with her bad friends."}]

translation: to end; to cut short; to kill
meaning_filipino: Wakasan o putulin ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay tumutukoy sa buhay, pag-asa, o pangarap.
etymology: From the root word "kitil" (to end, to kill).
original_explanation: "Kitlin" is the more dramatic, poetic cousin of "tapusin" (to finish). You don't just "kitlin" your report; you "kitlin" someone's dreams, hopes, or... well, their life. It's the word you use when you want to add a touch of tragedy. "Kinitil niya ang pag-asa ko" sounds way more heartbreaking than "Wala na akong pag-asa dahil sa kanya." It's the "hugot" version of ending something.
usage_notes: Often used in a figurative sense to mean "to crush" or "to extinguish," such as hopes or dreams.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **kitlin** ng iba ang iyong mga pangarap.","translation":"Don't let others **cut short** your dreams."},{"sentence":"Ang biglaang trahedya ay tila **kumitil** sa kanyang masayang kinabukasan.","translation":"The sudden tragedy seemed to **end** his happy future."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng hayop na mamalya (pamilya Viverridae) na karaniwang matatagpuan sa Asya at Aprika, kahawig ng pusa, at kilala rin bilang musang o alamid.
etymology: Unknown, likely a specific local name for the animal.
original_explanation: The animal famous for pooping out the world's most expensive coffee (Kopi Luwak). It's the OG coffee barista. Looks like a mix between a cat and a weasel with a 'what have I done' expression.
usage_notes: This is a homonym. This entry refers to the animal. It is more commonly known as 'musang' or 'alamid' in many regions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **tambuko** ang mabilis na tumawid sa kalsada.","translation":"A **civet cat** quickly crossed the road."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lumang yunit ng panukat para sa mga butil tulad ng bigas, na katumbas ng tatlong litro o isang 'ganta'.
original_explanation: Before weighing rice in kilos, our lolas bought it by the 'salop' or 'ganta' at the palengke. It's a wooden or metal container used to measure dry goods. Ask your parents, they'll probably have a story about being sent to the store to buy a 'salop' of rice. It's the OG 'pabili po'.
usage_notes: Primarily a historical unit of measure, roughly equivalent to 3 liters. It's rarely used today, having been replaced by the metric system (kilograms and liters).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si Inay ng isang **salop** na bigas sa palengke.","translation":"Mother bought one **ganta** of rice at the market."},{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng dalawang **salop** ng mais para sa mga manok.","translation":"We need two **gantas** of corn for the chickens."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang establisyimento na nagbibigay ng bayad na tuluyan sa mga manlalakbay, karaniwang panandalian.
original_explanation: A place you stay when you're on vacation, on a business trip, or when the aircon at home is broken and you need to "staycation" in a place with a pool. Also, the default venue for every major wedding, debut, and corporate event.
usage_notes: The word "otel" is a common, informal variant spelling/pronunciation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-book kami ng kwarto sa isang **hotel** malapit sa dagat.","translation":"We booked a room in a **hotel** near the sea."},{"sentence":"Gaganapin ang kumperensya sa Manila **Hotel**.","translation":"The conference will be held at the Manila **Hotel**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng isang pormal o taimtim na kahilingan para makamit o makuha ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: The active form of making a 'hiling'. Ito yung act of sending that risky text to your crush asking them out, or composing that very polite email to your prof asking for an extension. It's shooting your shot, but in a formal, hopeful way.
usage_notes: This is a transitive verb, meaning it requires an object. You 'hilingin' *something*.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **hilingin** ang iyong tulong para sa proyekto.","translation":"I want to **request** your help for the project."},{"sentence":"Ano ang gusto mong **hilingin** kay Santa ngayong Pasko?","translation":"What do you want to **ask for** from Santa this Christmas?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maranasan ang pagdurugo mula sa ilong.
original_explanation: The verb form of that stressful moment. It's what happens *to you*. 'Binalinguyngoy ako' means you've officially been victimized by your own nose, usually after trying to understand your crush's mixed signals or your telco bill.
usage_notes: Often used in the passive voice (e.g., binalinguyngoy).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong magbabad sa araw at baka ka **balinguynguyin**.","translation":"Don't stay under the sun for too long or you might **get a nosebleed**."},{"sentence":"Madalas siyang **balinguynguyin** noong bata pa siya.","translation":"He often **used to have nosebleeds** when he was a child."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng matinding pagod sa katawan o isipan.
original_explanation: This is more than just 'pagod'. This is 'pagod na pagod'. It's the exhaustion you feel after a week of OT, commuting through EDSA traffic, and dealing with adult responsibilities. It's the 'I-can't-adult-today' feeling in one word. A deep, soul-level tiredness.
usage_notes: Ang 'kapagalan' ay nagpapahiwatig ng isang estado o naipon na pagod, samantalang ang 'pagod' ay ang mas direktang pakiramdam.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ramdam na ramdam niya ang **kapagalan** matapos ang maghapong trabaho.","translation":"He really felt the **fatigue** after a whole day of work."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa **kapagalan**, nakatulog siya agad.","translation":"Because of **exhaustion**, he fell asleep immediately."}]

translation: to put inside; to place into a container
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng mga bagay sa loob ng isang lalagyan, silid, o anumang espasyo.
etymology: From 'mag-' (actor-focus verb prefix) + 'silid' (room, chamber; to put inside).
original_explanation: This is what you do when your mom says "Clean your room!" You take all the "kalat" and **magsilid** it inside your closet, under your bed, or anywhere out of sight. It's the art of organized chaos.
usage_notes: 'Silid' as a noun means 'room', but as a root for this verb, it means 'to put inside'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magsilid** ka ng mga damit mo sa aparador.","translation":"**Put** your clothes **inside** the cabinet."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos gamitin, kailangan mong **magsilid** ng mga gamit sa tamang lalagyan.","translation":"After using them, you need **to place** the things **into** their proper containers."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kendi na nakakabit sa isang patpat.
original_explanation: The ultimate "pampatahan" for a crying kid. It's the OG fidget spinner. Also, the thing you buy from the sari-sari store when you're 5 pesos short for a proper snack. Comes in flavors like "red," "orange," and "mystery."
usage_notes: Isang hiram na salita na ganap nang bahagi ng leksikong Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigyan mo ng **lolipop** ang bata para tumigil sa pag-iyak.","translation":"Give the child a **lollipop** so he'll stop crying."},{"sentence":"Paborito ko ang **lolipop** na may bubble gum sa loob.","translation":"I like the **lollipop** with bubble gum inside."}]

translation: to display a flag; to feature prominently
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagwawagayway ng bandila bilang simbolo ng pagkakakilanlan, pagdiriwang, o pagprotesta. Sa makabagong gamit, ito rin ay tumutukoy sa pagtatampok ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: Literally, it's what you do on Independence Day. Figuratively, it's when you 'flex' or proudly showcase something. For example, a news program might 'magbandila' a special report, or you might 'magbandila' your new relationship status on Facebook. It's about making something the headline.
usage_notes: Has a literal meaning (to raise a flag) and a common figurative meaning in media (to headline or feature). The object-focus form 'ibandila' is very common for the figurative meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing Araw ng Kalayaan, lahat ng tahanan ay inaasahang **magbandila** ng Pilipinas.","translation":"Every Independence Day, all homes are expected to **display the Philippine flag**."},{"sentence":"Ibinandila ng programa sa telebisyon ang kwento ng isang matagumpay na OFW.","translation":"The television program **featured prominently** the story of a successful OFW."}]

translation: to put something into one's mouth
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglalagay ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay pagkain, sa sariling bibig.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung moment na gutom na gutom ka na, tapos may isang pirasong lechon kawali sa harap mo. Hindi mo na hihintayin ang kutsara't tinidor, kakamayin mo na lang at diretso sa bibig. It's the verb form of 'OM NOM NOM'.
usage_notes: Ang 'suubin' ay paglagay sa sariling bibig. Ang 'subuan' ay pagpapakain sa ibang tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **suubin** nang sabay-sabay ang pagkain para hindi ka mabulunan.","translation":"Don't **put** the food **into your mouth** all at once so you don't choke."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-utos o paggawa ng paraan upang maging matalim ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay isang kasangkapang may talim tulad ng kutsilyo o lapis.
original_explanation: For your kitchen knives before mincing garlic like a pro. For your pencil before a big exam. Or metaphorically, for your mind ('magpatalas ng isip') before a debate. It's about getting that edge, literally and figuratively, so you're ready for action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala ni Mang Tonyo ang mga gunting sa panday para **magpatalas**.","translation":"Mang Tonyo brought the scissors to the blacksmith to **have them sharpened**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **magpatalas** ng lapis bago magsimula ang pagsusulit.","translation":"I need to **sharpen** my pencil before the test starts."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pagkaing Pilipino na gawa sa giniling na karne (karaniwang baboy), hinaluan ng mga sangkap tulad ng pasas, karot, at itlog, binalot sa aluminum foil at pinasingawan o niluto.
original_explanation: The VIP of Filipino handaans. It's that log-shaped meat thingy that looks fancy but is basically your tita's delicious, steamed meatloaf. It's not a party without the embutido, sliced into perfect little circles. It's the "I-brought-something-special" potluck contribution.
usage_notes: Often served during holidays, fiestas, and special occasions. It can be eaten cold or fried after steaming.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong ulam sa Pasko ang **embutido** na gawa ni Lola.","translation":"My favorite Christmas dish is the **embutido** made by Grandma."},{"sentence":"Pakiprito mo nga itong natirang **embutido** para sa almusal.","translation":"Please fry this leftover **embutido** for breakfast."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang anyo ng enerhiya na resulta ng pagdaloy ng mga electron; daloy ng karga ng kuryente.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na 'corriente', na nangangahulugang 'current'.
original_explanation: Ang dahilan kung bakit may Wi-Fi ka, malamig ang aircon mo, at nagcha-charge ang phone mo. Pero ito rin ang dahilan ng bill shock mo every month at 'yung biglang 'brownout!' sa kalagitnaan ng paborito mong Netflix series. Sa usapan, 'kuryente' din 'yung info na mali o 'yung joke na hindi bumenta. 'Tol, kuryente 'yang balita mo.'
usage_notes: Can also be used colloquially to mean 'wrong information' or a 'miss' (in a joke or story).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawalan kami ng **kuryente** kagabi dahil sa malakas na bagyo.","translation":"We lost **electricity** last night because of the strong typhoon."},{"sentence":"Akala ko ba may bonus? Ay, **kuryente** raw yung balita.","translation":"I thought there was a bonus? Oh, the news was apparently **wrong/a miss**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na para sa pangkalahatang gamit ng lahat ng tao, o may kinalaman sa komunidad at hindi pribado.
original_explanation: Yung opposite ng 'private'. Public school, public hospital, public transport... mga lugar kung saan mo masusubok ang iyong pasensya at makakahanap ng mga kwentong pang-MMK. A 'public' scandal is way juicier than a private one.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **publiko**ng transportasyon ay mahalaga sa mga manggagawa.","translation":"**Public** transportation is important for workers."}]

translation: a gossipy, untruthful person (literally: gossipy frog)
meaning_filipino: Isang mapanlait na pariralang balbal para sa isang taong sinungaling, tsismosa, o mahilig gumawa ng kwento.
etymology: Isang modernong pariralang balbal na pinagsasama ang "echosera" (babaeng mahilig sa echos) at "frog" (palaka), na marahil ay naging popular sa social media.
original_explanation: Level up ng 'echosera'. Ito yung kaibigan mong hindi lang nagkakalat ng 'echos', kundi ginagawa itong full-blown teleserye with sound effects. The 'frog' part adds that extra 'ribbit-ribbit' annoyance factor. It's a meme-ified insult for the queen of fake news in your GC.
usage_notes: Isang napaka-impormal at mapaglarong panlilibak.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang pansinin 'yan, isa 'yang **echoserang frog**.","translation":"Don't mind her, she's such a **gossipy, untruthful person**."},{"sentence":"Nagalit si Ana dahil tinawag siyang **echoserang frog** ni Ben.","translation":"Ana got mad because Ben called her an **echoserang frog**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nangangahulugang mayroong isa para sa bawat miyembro ng isang pangkat.
original_explanation: The rule when the food is *saktong-sakto lang*. When your mom brings home Jollibee Chickenjoy and says "Tig-isa lang ha," you know there's no room for negotiation or asking for a second piece. It's the ultimate test of self-control.
usage_notes: Denotes a strict one-to-one distribution.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binigyan kami ng aming lola ng **tig-isa**ng mansanas.","translation":"Our grandmother gave us **one** apple **each**."},{"sentence":"Okay, class, **tig-isa** lang ang coupon para sa free ice cream.","translation":"Okay, class, only **one for each** for the free ice cream coupons."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malambot at mamantikang tisyu na matatagpuan sa loob ng mga buto, na responsable sa paggawa ng mga selula ng dugo.
original_explanation: The ultimate prize when you're eating Bulalo or Kare-kare. That rich, fatty, cholesterol-packed goodness you slurp out of the bone. It's the 'bawal pero masarap' part of the meal that makes you say 'High-blood is waving, but I'm diving in!'
usage_notes: A compound noun from 'utak' (brain) and 'buto' (bone), literally 'brain in the bone'. Primarily used in culinary contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paborito niyang parte ng bulalo ay ang **utak sa buto**.","translation":"His favorite part of the bulalo is the **bone marrow**."},{"sentence":"Masarap higupin ang **utak sa buto** habang mainit pa ang sabaw.","translation":"It's delicious to slurp the **bone marrow** while the soup is still hot."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na sayaw, karaniwang tumutukoy sa mga sayaw panlipunan o 'ballroom' na may tiyak na mga hakbang.
original_explanation: Not your usual TikTok dance. This is the lola's-era, formal-attire, cotillion kind of dance. Think rigodon de honor, waltz, or tango. The kind of dance where you actually have to touch your partner and can't just wing it. From the Spanish 'danza'.
usage_notes: A more formal and somewhat archaic term for 'sayaw'. Often used in literary or historical contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging tanyag ang **dansa** sa mga sosyal na pagtitipon noong panahon ng mga Espanyol.","translation":"The **dansa** became popular in social gatherings during the Spanish era."},{"sentence":"Ang rigodon de honor ay isang uri ng **dansa** na isinasagawa sa mga mararangal na okasyon.","translation":"The rigodon de honor is a type of **formal dance** performed on stately occasions."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paraang palagian, hindi nagbabago, o matatag.
original_explanation: This is more common in Visayan languages, but used in Tagalog too. It's that one friend who's "pirme" late. Or your tita's "pirme" na tanong, "Kailan ka mag-aasawa?" It means consistent, fixed, for better or for worse.
usage_notes: While understood in Manila, it is much more frequently used in the Visayas and Mindanao. In standard Tagalog, 'palagi' (always) or 'permanente' (permanent) are more common. Can also function as an adjective.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko ng trabaho na **pirme** ang sahod at hindi pabago-bago.","translation":"I want a job with a **fixed** salary that isn't variable."},{"sentence":"**Pirme** siyang nagrereklamo tungkol sa trapiko.","translation":"He **always** complains about the traffic."}]

meaning_filipino: Tinanggal sa listahan ng mga sinusubaybayan sa isang social media platform.
original_explanation: That moment when your friend's posts become too cringey or puro political rants na lang, you hit that magic button. It's the digital equivalent of 'it's not you, it's me... but it's definitely you.' The silent ghosting of the social media world.
usage_notes: A modern, Taglish word used in the context of social media to indicate a past action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nag-unfollow** ako sa kanya kasi puro drama lang ang pino-post niya.","translation":"I **unfollowed** him because he only posts drama."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko sinasadyang **mag-unfollow** sa iyo, napindot ko lang!","translation":"I didn't mean to **unfollow** you, I just accidentally pressed it!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng puno (Aleurites moluccanus) na ang bunga ay pinagkukunan ng langis na ginagamit bilang ilawan o sa pagluluto.
original_explanation: This is the OG source of light before Meralco decided to bill us our souls. The nuts from this tree give oil. Think of it as nature's power bank, but for lamps. Also, its oil is used in some dishes, so it's a multi-tasker like a working student.
usage_notes: Ang buto mismo ay tinatawag ding 'lumbang'. Ang langis nito ay 'langis ng lumbang'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang langis mula sa **lumbang** ay ginagamit na panggatong sa mga lampara noong unang panahon.","translation":"The oil from the **candlenut** was used as fuel for lamps in the old days."}]

meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng kalinga, pagmamahal, at pag-aalaga ang isang tao, hayop, o bagay upang ito ay lumaki, gumaling, o mapanatiling maayos.
etymology: Mula sa salitang "aruga", na nangangahulugang kalinga o alaga.
original_explanation: This is what your nanay does when you have a slight cough and she suddenly brings you a feast of lugaw, Vicks, and a blanket in 30-degree weather. It's that next-level care, the kind that makes you feel safe and loved. Tulad ng pag-aalaga sa halaman mong ayaw mong mamatay o sa jowa mong may 'tampo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tungkulin ng mga magulang na **arugain** ang kanilang mga anak.","translation":"It is the duty of parents **to care for** their children."},{"sentence":"Dapat nating **arugain** ang ating kalikasan para sa susunod na henerasyon.","translation":"We must **nurture** our environment for the next generation."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang masusing paghahanap sa isang bagay o impormasyon na nawawala o mahirap matagpuan, madalas sa paraang apurahan.
original_explanation: 'Yung eksenang hinahanap mo 'yung phone mo habang kausap mo 'yung tao sa phone. O 'yung paghahanap ng matinong jowa sa dating apps. You **humagilap** for something that seems impossible to find.
usage_notes: Implies a more frantic or difficult search than 'humanap'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Humagilap** siya ng barya sa kanyang bulsa para pamasahe.","translation":"He **searched** his pocket for coins for his fare."},{"sentence":"**Humagilap** ng mga kasagutan ang mga mananaliksik tungkol sa biglaang pagbabago ng klima.","translation":"The researchers **searched for** answers regarding the sudden climate change."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pangkat etnolinggwistiko sa mga rehiyon ng Silangang Visayas (Samar at Leyte) sa Pilipinas, o sa kanilang wika.
etymology: From the Waray-Waray language, possibly from the word "waray" meaning "nothing," a common feature in the language's grammar.
original_explanation: This refers to the fierce and beautiful people from Samar and Leyte in the Visayas region. If someone says "I'm Waray," they're telling you about their proud heritage. Also refers to their language, which is distinct from Tagalog or Cebuano. Don't mess with a Waray; they are known for being brave ('matapang').
usage_notes: Capitalized when referring to the people or the language. The stress is on the first syllable, distinguishing it from the slang term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang nanay ko ay isang **Waray** mula sa Tacloban.","translation":"My mother is a **Waray** from Tacloban."},{"sentence":"Nagsasalita siya ng **Waray** at Tagalog.","translation":"She speaks **Waray** and Tagalog."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang labis o matinding pagtugon sa isang sitwasyon o pahayag, kadalasan sa paraang negatibo o sobra sa inaasahan.
etymology: Taglish, from English 'react' and Tagalog 'malala' (severe, intense).
original_explanation: The national sport of Pinoy netizens. When someone posts something mildly controversial and the comment section explodes. It's when your friend sees their crush with someone else and immediately goes into full-on drama mode. 'Besh, 'wag kang react malala, tinanong lang niya direksyon.'
usage_notes: A modern slang phrase popular on social media. The two words function as a single semantic unit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **react malala**, biro lang 'yon.","translation":"Don't **overreact**, it was just a joke."},{"sentence":"Nag-post lang ako ng pagkain, pero **react malala** ang mga kaibigan kong nagda-diet.","translation":"I just posted food, but my friends who are on a diet **reacted intensely**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gawain, responsibilidad, o bagay na ipinagkatiwala o iniatas sa isang tao; isang order para sa isang produkto o serbisyo.
original_explanation: Yung pakiusap ng nanay mo na "Pakibili ng suka sa tindahan," 'yan ang engkargo mo. O kaya 'yung pinapagawa sa'yo ng boss mo na "urgent" pero 5 PM na ng Biyernes. It's basically a task or an errand you've been entrusted with, whether it's a Shopee order or a divine mission.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa konteksto ng mga pakiusap, utos, o pag-order ng isang bagay na ipapagawa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **engkargo** sa akin ang lola ko mula sa probinsya.","translation":"My grandmother has a **task** for me from the province."},{"sentence":"Tinatapos ko lang itong **engkargo** sa akin ng kliyente.","translation":"I'm just finishing this **commission** from my client."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagyang paggalaw mula sa isang posisyon; ang pagkilos mula sa pagkakapirme.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're playing "statue dance" and you try your hardest not to move a muscle. 'Tuminag' is that tiny flinch or movement. It's often used in the negative, "hindi tuminag," to describe someone who is unfazed, stubborn, or literally frozen in place. "Sinigawan na siya, pero hindi man lang tuminag." It's the ultimate "unbothered" move.
usage_notes: Often used in the negative form "hindi tuminag" to emphasize stillness or being unaffected.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit anong yugyog, hindi **tuminag** ang natutulog na aso.","translation":"No matter how much it was shaken, the sleeping dog didn't **budge**."},{"sentence":"Nang marinig niya ang balita, ni hindi siya **tuminag** sa kanyang kinauupuan.","translation":"When she heard the news, she didn't even **move** from her seat."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang parte mula sa apat na magkakapantay na hati ng isang kabuuan.
original_explanation: A quarter. It's what's left of your sweldo one day after payday. Or it's the portion of the pizza you get when you're sharing with three other friends. "Akin na lang 'yung ikaapat na bahagi ng cake, diet ako." (Narrator: She was not on a diet.)
usage_notes: Ito ang pormal na paraan ng pagsasabi ng "one-fourth." Sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap, mas madalas sabihin ang "one-fourth" o "kapat" (mula sa Espanyol na 'cuarto').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mo ng **ikaapat na bahagi** ng isang tasa ng asukal para sa resipe.","translation":"You need **one-fourth** of a cup of sugar for the recipe."},{"sentence":"Ang **ikaapat na bahagi** ng populasyon ay nakatira sa kalunsuran.","translation":"A **quarter** of the population lives in urban areas."}]

translation: to pick up (a signal); to catch (a rumor)
meaning_filipino: Makuha o marinig nang hindi sinasadya, tulad ng signal ng radyo o isang usap-usapan.
etymology: From `ma-` (ability/potential prefix) + `sagap` (to scoop up from a surface, to pick up signals).
original_explanation: Before WiFi, it meant trying to get a clear radio station. Now, `masagap` is what you do when you overhear juicy chismis from the next table at a coffee shop. 'May **nasagap** akong balita, magre-resign na daw si boss.' (I **caught** some news, they say the boss is resigning.) It's the skill of a true Marites—picking up signals from the airwaves of gossip.
usage_notes: Used for both literal signals (radio, TV, wifi) and figurative information (news, gossip).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **masagap** ang signal ng selpon sa bundok.","translation":"It's hard to **pick up** a cellphone signal in the mountains."},{"sentence":"May **nasagap** ka bang balita tungkol sa bagong anunsyo?","translation":"Did you **catch** any news about the new announcement?"}]

translation: to meddle with, to fidget with, to mess with
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggalaw o paghimasok sa isang bagay nang walang pahintulot o sa paraang magulo.
original_explanation: What your mom tells you not to do to the Christmas decorations. 'Huwag mong likutin 'yan!' is the official tagline. It's the urge to press a big red button that says 'Do Not Press.'
usage_notes: Often has a negative connotation of annoying or meddlesome touching/moving of things.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **likutin** ang mga gamit sa mesa ko.","translation":"Don't **meddle with** the things on my desk."},{"sentence":"Bata, bawal **likutin** ang mga paninda.","translation":"Kid, it's forbidden **to mess with** the merchandise."}]

translation: raw (referring to food, especially seafood or meat)
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa paraan ng paghahanda ng pagkain, lalo na ang isda o karne, na hindi niluluto sa apoy kundi pinapahinog sa asim ng suka, kalamansi, o katulad na sangkap.
original_explanation: This is the OG Filipino ceviche. It’s food that's "cooked" not by heat, but by the acid trip you give it with vinegar or calamansi juice. It's the state of being raw but getting ready to be delicious. Think of it as the 'in a relationship' status of fish before it becomes 'married' to the vinegar as 'kilawin'.
usage_notes: Often used as an adjective-like noun, as in "pagkaing kilaw" (raw food prepared in vinegar). Can be used interchangeably with "kilawin" to refer to the dish, but "kilaw" more accurately refers to the method or state.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang isdang tanigue ay masarap gawing **kilaw**.","translation":"Tanigue fish is delicious when prepared **raw in vinegar**."},{"sentence":"Hindi lahat ay sanay kumain ng pagkaing **kilaw**.","translation":"Not everyone is used to eating **raw, vinegar-cured** food."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagpunta sa gubat o kakahuyan upang mamutol o manguha ng kahoy na gagamiting panggatong.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'probinsya life' activity. Before LPG tanks, there was this. It's the act of going into the woods to get firewood. Today, it might sound rustic and romantic, but for many, it's a daily chore. It’s the OG way of sourcing your fuel for cooking that sinigang.
usage_notes: The 'ng' in 'mangahoy' is a result of nasal assimilation where 'mang-' + 'kahoy' becomes 'mangahoy' (the 'k' is dropped).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maagang gumising si Tatay para **mangahoy** sa bundok.","translation":"Father woke up early to **gather firewood** on the mountain."},{"sentence":"Ipinagbabawal na ang **mangahoy** sa protektadong gubat na ito.","translation":"Gathering firewood is now forbidden in this protected forest."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay ng laman sa isang bagay hanggang sa ito ay maging sapat o umapaw. Ito ay ang pagkumpleto o pagbuo sa isang espasyo o kakulangan.
original_explanation: When you're the designated taga-refill ng ice sa water jug during a family reunion. You pumuno the jug. Also, what someone did to your heart, only to leave it empty again. #hugot
usage_notes: This is the completed or past tense form of the verb. The infinitive form is 'pumuno' and the present progressive is 'pumupuno'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pumuno** siya ng tubig sa timba.","translation":"He/She **filled** the pail with water."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **pumuno** sa listahan ng mga bisita?","translation":"Who **filled** out the guest list?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bilang na kasunod ng labing-tatlo at bago ang labing-lima; katumbas ng 14.
etymology: From "labi" (excess, remainder) + "-ng" + "apat" (four), literally "excess of ten by four".
original_explanation: The number of days you have to wait for your sahod after the 15th. It's also the age when you thought you were an adult but your parents still treated you like a kid.
usage_notes: Can be written as "labing-apat" or "labing apat". The hyphenated form is more common in formal writing. The Spanish-derived "katorse" is also used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **labing-apat** na estudyante sa klase.","translation":"There are **fourteen** students in the class."},{"sentence":"Tatakbo ako ng **labing-apat** na kilometro bukas.","translation":"I will run for **fourteen** kilometers tomorrow."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagpapaikli ng salitang "tsismis," na tumutukoy sa usap-usapan o kuwentong maaaring totoo o hindi, karaniwang tungkol sa pribadong buhay ng ibang tao.
etymology: Pagpapaikli ng "tsismis," na mula sa Espanyol na "chismes".
original_explanation: Short for "tsismis." Ito ang lifeblood ng mga Marites (Mare, anong latest?). 'Pag may nag-message sa'yo ng "May ts ako," alam mong kailangan mong i-drop everything at mag-focus. It's the tea, the chika, the lowdown. The shorter the message, the juicier the gossip.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa text messages o online chat. Binibigkas bilang "chis".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uy, anong latest na **ts**?","translation":"Hey, what's the latest **gossip**?"},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala diyan, **ts** lang 'yan.","translation":"Don't believe that, it's just a **rumor**."}]

translation: to make a hole; to pierce
meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng isang butas o siwang sa isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pagtusok, pagpunit, o pag-ukit.
original_explanation: What you do to your brand new pants to make them 'distressed,' what the DPWH does to the road for the 5th time this month, or what your tsismosa kapitbahay does to the wall to hear the latest chika. To create an opening, wanted or not.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **magbutas** ng karton para sa aming proyekto sa paaralan.","translation":"I need to **make a hole** in the cardboard for our school project."},{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **magbutas** ng tainga para sa isa pang hikaw.","translation":"She decided to **pierce** her ear for another earring."}]

meaning_filipino: Mabagal kumilos o gumalaw; makupad.
original_explanation: 'Yung internet connection mo 'pag 5 PM na at lahat ng kapitbahay mo nanonood ng Netflix. O 'yung feeling mo 'pag Lunes ng umaga at kulang ka sa tulog. It's that sluggish, can't-be-bothered-to-move-fast kind of vibe.
usage_notes: Describes slowness in movement or action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **malamba** ang pag-usad ng pila dahil sa dami ng tao.","translation":"The line's progress became **slow** because of the number of people."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **malamba** kumilos para hindi tayo mahuli.","translation":"Don't move so **sluggishly** so we won't be late."}]

translation: to make something sour; to add sourness to
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagdaragdag ng sangkap na pampaasim sa isang lutuin o inumin.
original_explanation: The magical command you give when the sinigang isn't sour enough. 'More sampalok, please!' It's the act of transforming a bland soup into a sour-faced masterpiece.
usage_notes: A command or infinitive form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong masyadong **asiman** ang sabaw, baka hindi magustuhan ng mga bata.","translation":"Don't **make** the soup too **sour**, the kids might not like it."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mo pang **asiman** ang sinigang para mas sumarap.","translation":"You still need to **add sourness** to the sinigang to make it more delicious."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babae na sekswal o romantikong naaakit sa kapwa babae.
original_explanation: A woman who loves women. It's the more formal term compared to 'tibo' or 'tomboy', which can sometimes be used playfully or, depending on tone, as a slur. Using 'lesbya' is often a more respectful and affirming choice, especially in formal discussions or within the LGBTQ+ community.
usage_notes: While 'tomboy' is more common in colloquial speech, 'lesbya' is often preferred in formal or academic contexts and by some members of the community for its directness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagdiriwang ng komunidad ng mga **lesbya** ang Pride Month tuwing Hunyo.","translation":"The **lesbian** community celebrates Pride Month every June."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang mekanikal o elektromekanikal na may mga tiklado na kapag pinindot ay naglilimbag ng mga karakter sa papel.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'maquinilla' (maliit na makina, makinilya).
original_explanation: The original keyboard warrior's weapon. Before laptops and mechanical keyboards, there was the 'makinilya'. This is what your lolo used to write love letters or what government offices used to type documents that required 10 carbon copies. That satisfying 'clack-clack-clack-DING!' sound is pure nostalgia.
usage_notes: Ngayon ay itinuturing na isang 'vintage' o antigong kagamitan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natuto akong mag-type gamit ang lumang **makinilya** ng aking ama.","translation":"I learned to type using my father's old **typewriter**."},{"sentence":"May koleksyon siya ng mga antigong **makinilya**.","translation":"He has a collection of antique **typewriters**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nauukol sa isang komunidad o samahan; pampamayanan o para sa gamit ng lahat.
original_explanation: Think of it as the 'group project' version of ownership. Yung community pantry, komunales 'yan. Yung videoke sa gitna ng kalye tuwing Pasko, komunales din 'yan (whether you like it or not). It's for the barangay, by the barangay.
usage_notes: Often refers to land, property, or activities shared by a community.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpulong ang mga residente tungkol sa pagpapanatili ng kanilang lupang **komunales**.","translation":"The residents held a meeting about maintaining their **communal** land."},{"sentence":"Ang paglilinis ng estero ay isang proyektong **komunales**.","translation":"Cleaning the creek is a **communal** project."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos o proseso ng hindi makatarungang paggamit sa isang tao o sitwasyon para sa sariling kapakinabangan.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung 'unli-OT, no pay' na policy. O 'yung nangyayari sa mga 'child stars' na pinagtratrabaho nang sobra. Basically, the noun version of getting played for someone else's gain.
usage_notes: A formal term used in discussions about labor rights, human rights, and social justice.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **eksplotasyon** ng mga manggagawa ay isang seryosong isyu sa lipunan.","translation":"The **exploitation** of workers is a serious societal issue."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang tungkulin o gawain ay ang pagpigil, pagkontrol, o pagpapakalma sa isang sitwasyon, kaguluhan, o damdamin.
etymology: From taga- (doer of an action) + sawata (to suppress, to quell).
original_explanation: The official 'killjoy' of the group. Sila yung laging nagsasabing, 'Kalma lang, guys,' kapag nagkakainitan na sa group chat o sa pamilya. The designated adult in the room, even if they're not the oldest.
usage_notes: Often used in formal contexts, like for someone who controls a riot or a fire.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga bumbero ay nagsilbing **tagasawata** ng malaking sunog sa pabrika.","translation":"The firefighters served as the **suppressors** of the large fire at the factory."},{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng isang **tagasawata** sa pagtatalo ng dalawang panig.","translation":"We need a **controller** for the argument between the two sides."}]

translation: to enter; to go to work/school
meaning_filipino: Magtungo sa loob ng isang lugar; tumungo sa trabaho o paaralan para gampanan ang tungkulin.
original_explanation: The daily grind verb. 'Pumasok ka na?' is the national morning check-in question. It means to enter a room, a house, or more importantly, to show up for your shift at the BPO or your 8 AM class. When you're late, you say 'Sorry, traffic!' even if you just woke up. That's the pumasok life.
usage_notes: Extremely common. 'Pumasok sa trabaho' (go to work), 'Pumasok sa eskwela' (go to school), 'Pumasok sa kwarto' (enter the room).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maingay, **pumasok** ka na sa opisina dahil may meeting.","translation":"Be quiet, **go to** the office now because there's a meeting."},{"sentence":"Maagang **pumasok** ang mga estudyante para sa kanilang field trip.","translation":"The students **came to school** early for their field trip."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian na hindi karaniwan, naiiba sa inaasahan, o lumilihis sa pamantayan.
etymology: From English 'abnormal', which is from Latin 'abnormalis'.
original_explanation: Basically 'weird' or 'not normal.' It's what your tita calls your fashion choices, the traffic on EDSA during a holiday, or how your crush is acting after you confessed. It's a loanword we use for anything that deviates from the expected.
usage_notes: A direct loanword from English, used in both formal (medical, psychological) and informal contexts. Pronunciation follows the English model.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinuturing na **abnormal** ang sobrang taas na lagnat.","translation":"An extremely high fever is considered **abnormal**."},{"sentence":"Parang **abnormal** ang kilos niya ngayon, hindi siya ganyan dati.","translation":"His behavior seems **abnormal** today, he wasn't like that before."}]

meaning_filipino: Panghalip na panao sa kaukulang paari na tumutukoy sa 'kami' at hindi kasama ang kausap.
original_explanation: The ultimate "squad goals" pronoun. It's "ours," but *not including you*. When your barkada says, "Sa amin 'to," about a table at a coffee shop, it means you can't sit there. It's the verbal version of a velvet rope. It's different from 'atin', which is inclusive ('ours', including you).
usage_notes: This is the 'exclusive we' possessive pronoun. It contrasts with 'atin' (inclusive we). 'Amin' is used when the speaker and their group own/are associated with something, but the listener is not part of that group.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Amin** ang bahay na iyan.","translation":"That house is **ours** (but not yours)."},{"sentence":"Ibigay mo sa **amin** ang bola.","translation":"Give the ball to **us** (referring to a group that doesn't include the listener)."}]

meaning_filipino: Lubos na kasiguraduhan; walang bahid ng anumang pag-aalinlangan.
original_explanation: This is the upgraded version of 'tiyak'. It's when you're not just sure, you're "I'd bet my 13th-month pay on it" sure. It's the confidence level you have when you know the 'chismis' is 100% verified from the source. "Tiyak na tiyak kong siya ang kumain ng last piece ng lechon."
usage_notes: A reduplication used for emphasis, to convey absolute certainty and remove any shred of doubt.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tiyak na tiyak** kong nakita ko siya sa mall kahapon.","translation":"I am **absolutely sure** I saw him at the mall yesterday."},{"sentence":"Kahit walang pruweba, **tiyak na tiyak** ang kanyang ina na siya ang may kasalanan.","translation":"Even without proof, his mother was **positively certain** that he was the one at fault."}]

meaning_filipino: Hati o may lamat; nahati sa dalawa o higit pang bahagi.
original_explanation: Parang puso mo pagkatapos niyang sabihing "friends lang tayo." O 'yung buko na hinati para sa buko juice. It's that state of being split open, whether it's your heart or a coconut.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagulat siya nang makitang **biyak** ang salamin.","translation":"She was surprised to see that the mirror was **cracked**."},{"sentence":"Ang puso niya ay tila **biyak** sa sobrang kalungkutan.","translation":"His heart seemed **split** from so much sadness."}]

translation: to patch; to apply a plaster to
meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng panakip o pantapal ang isang butas, sugat, o anumang sira.
original_explanation: That moment when your friend is having a bad day, and you try to 'patch things up' with milk tea and fries. Or literally, when your mom puts a medicated plaster on your back for your cough. "Tapalan mo na 'yan!"
usage_notes: Commonly used for fixing leaks, holes, or applying medicinal patches and poultices.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tapalan** mo muna ng panyo ang sugat habang naghahanap ako ng gamot.","translation":"**Patch** the wound with a handkerchief while I look for medicine."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **tapalan** ang butas sa bubong bago umulan.","translation":"The hole in the roof needs to **be patched** before it rains."}]

translation: To turn upside down; to switch sides; to betray
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabago ng posisyon mula sa tama patungo sa saliwa o pabaliktad. Sa matalinghagang gamit, ito ay nangangahulugang pagbabago ng panig, pagtataksil, o pag-atras sa naunang sinabi.
original_explanation: 'Bumaliktad' has layers. Literally, it's your tsinelas turning upside down. But the real drama is in its other meanings. It's the witness in a court case who suddenly changes their testimony. It's the politician who switches parties after an election. It's your friend who promised to have your back but then sided with your enemy. It's the ultimate act of turning—turning over, turning against, turning traitor.
usage_notes: Has both literal and figurative meanings, with the figurative ones (betrayal, changing one's story) being very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumaliktad** ang bangka dahil sa lakas ng alon.","translation":"The boat **turned upside down** because of the strong waves."},{"sentence":"Biglang **bumaliktad** ang pangunahing testigo at itinanggi ang lahat ng kanyang sinabi.","translation":"The main witness suddenly **switched sides** and denied everything he had said."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagkopya o pagnanakaw sa mga ideya, salita, o gawa ng ibang tao at pag-angkin nito bilang sarili nang walang tamang pagkilala.
original_explanation: That thing you were tempted to do in high school when the deadline for your term paper was 8 AM tomorrow. It's the "copy-paste" sin. In the age of the internet, it's easier to do, but also easier to get caught. Remember: Google is your friend, but Turnitin is your teacher's best friend.
usage_notes: A more formal, Spanish-derived term. 'Pangongopya' is more common in casual speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **plahiyo** ay isang seryosong kasalanang akademiko.","translation":"**Plagiarism** is a serious academic offense."},{"sentence":"Sinampahan siya ng kasong **plahiyo** dahil sa kinopyang tula.","translation":"He was charged with **plagiarism** for the copied poem."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng plantsa na gumagana sa pamamagitan ng koryente upang uminit.
original_explanation: The modern-day plantsa. Ito yung isinasaksak mo sa pader. Mas mabilis uminit kaysa sa ex mong biglang nag-chat. May settings para sa iba't ibang tela, pero aminin mo, laging nasa "cotton" lang 'yan kahit ano pa'ng tela ang plantsahin mo.
usage_notes: Madalas na pinaikli bilang "plantsa" sa modernong konteksto dahil ito na ang karaniwang uri.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas madaling gamitin ang **plantsang de-koryente** kaysa sa de-uling.","translation":"The **electric iron** is easier to use than the charcoal one."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang bunutin sa saksakan ang **plantsang de-koryente** pagkatapos gamitin.","translation":"Don't forget to unplug the **electric iron** after using it."}]

translation: to be swaying continuously, to be staggering repeatedly
meaning_filipino: Ang patuloy o paulit-ulit na paggewang-gewang o pagkawala ng balanse sa paglakad o pagtayo.
original_explanation: Eto na yung level up ng 'sumuray'. Hindi lang isang beses, kundi tuloy-tuloy ang pagka-out of balance. Parang yung emosyon mo 'pag 'di ka sure kung aalis ka ba o mag-stay sa isang relasyon. O yung internet connection mo 'pag umuulan, 'di mapakali.
usage_notes: The repetition of the root word `suray` indicates a continuous or repeated action. This is the completed action (past tense). Present tense is `sumusuray-suray`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumuray-suray** ang lasing na naglalakad sa kalsada.","translation":"The drunk person was **staggering repeatedly** while walking on the street."},{"sentence":"Matapos ang lindol, **sumuray-suray** pa rin ang mga tao dahil sa pagkahilo.","translation":"After the earthquake, the people were still **swaying continuously** due to dizziness."}]

translation: Act of sending on a mission or errand
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-aatas o pagpapadala sa isang tao upang gampanan ang isang tiyak na gawain o misyon.
original_explanation: This is what your mom does when she runs out of Magic Sarap and sends you to the sari-sari store. On a grander scale, it's like God sending an angel, or the CEO sending the top sales agent to close a big deal. You are the chosen one... to go buy suka.
usage_notes: Implies that the person being sent has a specific purpose or task to fulfill. Often has a formal or important connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagsugo** sa kanya sa malayong probinsya ay bahagi ng kanyang pagsasanay.","translation":"The **act of sending him** to a faraway province was part of his training."},{"sentence":"Pinag-iisipan ng hari ang **pagsugo** ng mensahero.","translation":"The king is contemplating the **sending** of a messenger."}]

meaning_filipino: Maliit na piraso ng pagkain, lalo na ang himaymay ng karne o butil, na sumisingit o naiipit sa pagitan ng mga ngipin.
original_explanation: The ultimate post-kain-sa-labas public enemy. It's that tiny piece of mango, lechon, or corn that lives rent-free in your teeth and ruins your perfect smile for a selfie. It's the reason why toothpicks are a national treasure and why your best friend will discreetly signal to you with a weird mouth gesture.
usage_notes: Very specific meaning. Not to be confused with general food debris (`mumo`).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **tinga** ka sa ngipin, kumuha ka ng palito.","translation":"You have **food stuck in your teeth**, get a toothpick."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagkatuklap o pagkatanggal ng isang manipis na bahagi mula sa ibabaw ng isang bagay, tulad ng balat, pintura, o balat ng kahoy.
original_explanation: Similar to 'lapnis', but think smaller scale. It's the tiny bit of skin you peel near your fingernail (a hangnail). Or when the paint on your wall starts chipping off. **Lapnit** is the start of the problem, 'lapnis' is when it gets serious.
usage_notes: Often describes a smaller or thinner piece that is peeling compared to 'lapnis'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong hilahin ang **lapnit** sa gilid ng iyong kuko, magdurugo iyan.","translation":"Don't pull the **peeled-off skin** at the side of your nail, it will bleed."},{"sentence":"Puro **lapnit** na ang pintura ng lumang pader.","translation":"The paint on the old wall is all **chipped off**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na hindi madaling magpahayag ng damdamin o saloobin; mahiyain o hindi palakibo. Maaari ding tumukoy sa isang bagay na nakalaan na para sa iba.
original_explanation: Two meanings here: 1. Yung friend mong tahimik lang sa isang sulok habang nag-iinuman, pero pag naka-one-on-one ka, ang lalim pala. They're not snobs, just introverts. 2. Yung upuan sa sinehan na na-book mo na online, o yung table sa resto na may sign na "Reserbado". Bawal umupo ang iba, parang puso ng taong taken na.
usage_notes: Maaaring ilarawan ang personalidad ng isang tao o ang estado ng isang bagay o lugar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Marco ay isang **reserbado**ng tao at bihirang makipag-usap.","translation":"Marco is a **reserved** person and rarely talks."},{"sentence":"**Reserbado** na ang mesang iyon para sa pamilya Reyes.","translation":"That table is already **reserved** for the Reyes family."},{"sentence":"\"Taken na ba siya?\" \"Oo, **reserbado** na 'yan.\"","translation":"\"Is he taken?\" \"Yes, he's already **reserved**.\""}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapang yari sa kahoy o metal na partikular na idinisenyo para sa pagpalo ng bola sa mga larong tulad ng baseball o softball.
original_explanation: This is the more specific, G-rated version of `pamalo`. It's what you use to hit a home run, not what your mom uses when you don't do your homework. Think Manny Ramirez, not Mama Ramirez. It's the essential tool for palaro, not pangaral.
usage_notes: A descriptive noun phrase that specifies the purpose of the 'pamalo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bigat ng **pamalo ng bola** na ito!","translation":"This **bat** is heavy!"},{"sentence":"Bumili siya ng bagong **pamalo ng bola** para sa laro nila bukas.","translation":"He bought a new **bat** for their game tomorrow."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang eksaktong gitna ng araw, karaniwang tumutukoy sa oras na ika-12 ng araw, kung kailan pinakamataas ang sikat ng araw.
original_explanation: The official start of your lunch break. It's that magical hour when the sun is at its most savage, your stomach starts rumbling louder than the EDSA traffic, and your brain cells collectively decide to go on siesta. "Tara, kain na, tanghali na!"
usage_notes: Often used in greetings like "Magandang tanghali."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tirik na tirik ang araw tuwing **tanghali**.","translation":"The sun is scorching hot every **noon**."},{"sentence":"Magkita tayo sa tapat ng simbahan mamayang **tanghali**.","translation":"Let's meet in front of the church later at **midday**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos sa nakaraang panahunan ng panonood o pag-broadcast ng media nang direkta sa internet.
etymology: Taglish, from English "stream" with Tagalog affix "nag-".
original_explanation: The past tense of our national hobby. This is what you say the next day at work when your boss asks why you have eyebags. "Sorry boss, nag-stream ako ng buong season kagabi." It's the digital footprint of your 'puyat' session.
usage_notes: Past tense of the Taglish verb "mag-stream". The present progressive is "nagsistream".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kagabi, **nagstream** ako ng concert ng paborito kong banda.","translation":"Last night, I **streamed** my favorite band's concert."},{"sentence":"**Nagstream** ba kayo ng bagong episode?","translation":"Did you guys **stream** the new episode?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na hindi nagsasabi ng katotohanan; sinungaling. Bilang pang-uri, ito ay naglalarawan sa isang bagay na hindi totoo, peke, o mapanlinlang.
etymology: Nagmula sa salitang 'bula' (sa metaporikal na kahulugan nitong 'walang laman') na dinugtungan ng hulaping '-an', na bumubuo ng pang-uri o pangalan para sa isang taong may taglay na katangiang iyon.
original_explanation: This is the official title for your friend who says "On the way na ako" but is actually still in the shower. It's the adjective for fake news, fake friends, and fake 'I love you's'. A certified Marites detector red flag.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang isang tao (bilang pangngalan, 'isang bulaan'), ngunit maaari ring ilarawan ang mga bagay tulad ng 'bulaang propeta' (false prophet) o 'bulaang saksi' (false witness).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala sa kanya, isa siyang **bulaan**.","translation":"Don't believe him, he is a **liar**."},{"sentence":"Nagkalat ang mga **bulaan** na balita sa social media.","translation":"There is a lot of **false** news spreading on social media."}]

translation: sprawled; spread out over a surface
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging nakakalat o nakalatag sa ibabaw ng isang bagay, kadalasan ay tumutukoy sa mga marka, sugat, o guhit sa balat.
original_explanation: Think of the welts on your skin after getting hit by a latigo (or your mom's belt, #classic). Or the pattern of veins on a leaf, or stretch marks. It's something that is spread across a surface, often in a linear or network-like pattern, and is very visible. It sounds a bit dramatic and poetic.
usage_notes: Often used in a literary or medical context to describe marks, scars, or rashes on the skin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Makikita ang mga peklat na **nakabalatay** sa kanyang likod.","translation":"The scars **sprawled** across his back could be seen."}]

translation: to mess up; to complicate; to cause chaos
meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang paglikha ng gulo, kalituhan, o kawalan ng kaayusan sa isang sitwasyon, lugar, o isipan ng tao.
original_explanation: 'Wag mo nang **paguluhin** ang isip ko! Ito 'yung sinasabi mo sa ex mong pilit bumabalik, o sa groupmate mong biglang binabago 'yung presentation 5 minutes before the report. The act of making things messy or complicated, intentionally or not.
usage_notes: A command or infinitive form. 'Gulo' means mess or chaos. A stronger version is 'guluhin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **paguluhin** ang mga papel sa mesa ko.","translation":"Don't **mess up** the papers on my desk."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang **paguluhin** ang simpleng plano.","translation":"He's trying **to complicate** the simple plan."}]

translation: to guide by the hand, to lead
meaning_filipino: Tulungan o suportahan sa paglakad sa pamamagitan ng paghawak sa kamay o braso; gabayan sa isang direksyon o landas.
original_explanation: This is what your friend does when you've had one too many San Mig Lights. It's also what a good mentor or leader does for their team—guiding them, not dragging them. Figuratively, it's about leading someone towards a better path, like 'akayin mo siya sa kabutihan' (lead them to goodness).
usage_notes: Can be literal (physically guiding someone) or figurative (guiding someone morally or intellectually).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **akayin** ang matanda sa pagtawid sa kalsada.","translation":"You need **to guide** the old person in crossing the street."},{"sentence":"Ina**akay** ng guro ang kanyang mga estudyante tungo sa tamang kaalaman.","translation":"The teacher **leads** her students towards the right knowledge."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar sa baybayin kung saan maaaring dumaong, magkarga, o magdiskarga ang mga sasakyang-dagat tulad ng barko.
etymology: From 'daong' (to dock, a large boat) + '-an' suffix (location).
original_explanation: It's the airport for boats. The place where ships 'park'. Whether it's a huge container ship from China or the ferry to Boracay, they all end up at a **daungan**. It's a place of hellos and goodbyes, full of OFWs, balikbayan boxes, and the smell of the sea.
usage_notes: Can refer to a small pier or a large international seaport.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghihintay ang pamilya sa **daungan** para sa pagdating ng barko.","translation":"The family is waiting at the **port** for the ship's arrival."},{"sentence":"Ang **Daungan** ng Maynila ay isa sa pinakaabala sa buong bansa.","translation":"The **Port** of Manila is one of the busiest in the country."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal para sa "pangit".
etymology: A playful alteration of 'pangit' (ugly), common in Filipino gay lingo (Swardspeak). The exact origin is unclear but follows the pattern of creating more 'stylish' sounding words.
original_explanation: Gay lingo for 'pangit' (ugly). Why say pangit when you can say 'shonda'? It has more flair. 'Shonda ang ugali niya' (His/her attitude is ugly). It's the kind of ugly that's not just physical but can also describe a situation or behavior.
usage_notes: Used in informal conversations and gay lingo (Swardspeak). Can be considered offensive if used maliciously.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ay, ang **shonda** naman ng design ng damit na 'yan.","translation":"Oh, the design of that dress is so **ugly**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi ka **shonda**, kailangan mo lang ng tulog.","translation":"Don't worry, you're not **ugly**, you just need some sleep."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o paghiling sa isang tao na magluto ng pagkain sa ibabaw ng nagbabagang uling o apoy.
etymology: From mag- (actor-focus verb prefix) + pa- (causative prefix) + ihaw (grill).
original_explanation: It's what you say when you're too lazy to stand over the hot coals yourself. "Pare, magpaihaw ka na ng liempo!" This is a staple verb during Filipino family outings, beach trips, and fiestas. You're not the one grilling (`nag-iihaw`), you're the one delegating the grilling. You're the project manager of the inihaw.
usage_notes: `Mag-ihaw` is to grill something yourself. `Magpaihaw` is to ask someone to grill something for you.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para sa handaan, **nagpaihaw** sila ng isang buong manok.","translation":"For the feast, they **had** a whole chicken **grilled**."},{"sentence":"Sino ang pwedeng **magpaihaw** nitong mga isda?","translation":"Who can I **ask to grill** these fish?"}]

translation: to discuss something; to talk something over
meaning_filipino: Pag-usapan o talakayin ang isang paksa o isyu sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang tao upang magkaroon ng pagkakaunawaan.
original_explanation: Ito yung "Let's talk" stage sa isang relasyon, pero for everything. Pwedeng sa project, sa away-bati niyo ng jowa mo, o sa usapang pampamilya. The goal is to adult properly and not just ghost each other. Kumbaga, "usap tayo, 'wag puro assume."
usage_notes: A command or suggestion form. The noun form is 'pag-uusap' or 'diyalogo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pagdialogohan** natin ang mga hindi pagkakaunawaan para maayos na natin ito.","translation":"**Let's discuss** our misunderstandings so we can fix them."},{"sentence":"Mas mabuting **pagdialogohan** ang budget bago mamili.","translation":"It's better **to talk over** the budget before shopping."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na labis ang pagkahilig o may adiksyon sa pagsusugal.
etymology: From 'sugal' (gamble) + '-ol' (a suffix indicating a person characterized by the root word, similar to -er in English).
original_explanation: Ito yung tropa mong laging nagsasabing "Pustahan tayo?" kahit sa pinakamaliit na bagay. Sila yung laging may dalang baraha, laging online sa e-sabong, o laging nag-aabang ng resulta ng lotto. For them, life is a game of chance, at madalas, talo sila sa buhay.
usage_notes: The suffix '-ol' is not productive but is found in a few words to denote a person with a habit or addiction (e.g., lasinggero from lasing).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala si Mang Karding sa buong baryo bilang isang notoryus na **sugarol**.","translation":"Mang Karding is known throughout the village as a notorious **gambler**."},{"sentence":"Sinabihan na siya ng asawa niya na tigilan ang pagiging **sugarol**.","translation":"His wife already told him to stop being a **gambler**."}]

translation: a Filipino breakfast meal with fried rice and egg
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pagkaing Pilipino, karaniwang pang-agahan, na binubuo ng sinangag (fried rice) at itlog (egg). Ang salita ay portmanteau ng "SInangag" at "itLOG".
etymology: Isang portmanteau o pagtatambal ng mga salitang SInangag (fried rice) at itLOG (egg).
original_explanation: The undisputed champion of Pinoy breakfast. It's not just a meal, it's a formula: (Ulam) + SI (Sinangag) + LOG (Itlog). Tapsilog, Longsilog, Tocilog... the possibilities are endless! It's the reason why you can eat rice for breakfast, lunch, and dinner without judgment. The ultimate comfort food after a long night out or for a long day ahead.
usage_notes: Palaging ginagamit bilang hulapi sa pangunahing ulam (hal. Tapsilog = Tapa + Sinangag + Itlog). Ang 'silog' mismo ay tumutukoy sa kombinasyon ng sinangag at itlog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong orderin sa karinderya ang tapsilog, kumpleto na ang **silog** sa tapa.","translation":"My favorite thing to order at the eatery is tapsilog, the **fried rice and egg** combo is complete with cured beef."},{"sentence":"Anong gusto mong **silog**? Mayroon kaming longganisa, tocino, at bangus.","translation":"What **silog** meal do you want? We have sausage, sweet cured pork, and milkfish."}]

translation: to fund; to allocate funds for
meaning_filipino: Maglaan o magbigay ng pondo o salapi para sa isang tiyak na layunin, proyekto, o gawain.
original_explanation: Think of it as the "add to cart" but for projects. When the government decides to build a new bridge, they need to ipundo it. When your barkada plans a beach trip, everyone has to ipundo their share. It's putting the money where the mouth (or the project plan) is.
usage_notes: 'Ipundo' is about allocating funds, while 'ipundar' is about establishing something with those funds.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **ipundo** ng gobyerno ang sapat na halaga para sa edukasyon.","translation":"The government needs **to fund** a sufficient amount for education."},{"sentence":"Magkano ang **ipinundo** ninyo para sa Christmas party?","translation":"How much did you guys **allocate** for the Christmas party?"}]

translation: to act, to behave, to swagger
meaning_filipino: Kumilos o gumalaw sa isang partikular na paraan, na kadalasan ay may pagpapakitang-gilas o pagpapanggap.
etymology: From Spanish 'actuar' (to act), with the Filipino connotation of 'to put on airs'.
original_explanation: Yung ka-officemate mong biglang nag-English accent pagkatapos ma-promote. Or yung friend mong kung maka-asta, parang may-ari ng bar, pero nakikibreak lang pala. It's to put on airs, to act a certain way, often pretentiously. "Ume-asta na namang bida-bida."
usage_notes: Often carries a negative connotation of being pretentious or showing off.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **umasta** na parang ikaw ang biktima dito.","translation":"Don't **act** like you're the victim here."},{"sentence":"**Umasta** siyang parang boss kaya sinunod siya ng lahat.","translation":"He **acted** like a boss, so everyone followed him."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-unawa nang lubusan sa isang bagay na malalim o mahirap intindihin; ang pagsukat sa lalim ng tubig o ng isang konsepto.
original_explanation: Trying to understand your crush's mixed signals? That's you, trying to tumarok their intentions. It's what you do when you're trying to figure out a deep movie plot or a friend's vague 'I'm fine'. It’s deep-level comprehension, a mental dive into the unknown.
usage_notes: A more profound word than 'umunawa' (to understand). It implies understanding something complex, deep, or abstract.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **tumarok** sa isipan ng isang henyo.","translation":"It's difficult **to fathom** the mind of a genius."},{"sentence":"Walang sinuman ang kayang **tumarok** sa lalim ng pagmamahal ng isang ina.","translation":"No one can fully **comprehend** the depth of a mother's love."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa teolohiyang Abrahamiko, ito ang huling araw kung kailan hahatulan ang lahat ng tao, buhay man o patay, batay sa kanilang mga gawa.
original_explanation: The ultimate deadline. The final performance review. That day when all your 'seen zones', ghosting, and 'utang na di binayaran' will be brought up. It's the universe's version of a tribunal council, and you're the main respondent.
usage_notes: Used in religious or eschatological contexts, but also metaphorically for a day of reckoning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayon sa banal na kasulatan, darating ang **Araw ng Paghuhukom**.","translation":"According to the holy scriptures, **Judgment Day** will come."},{"sentence":"Para sa mga kurakot na pulitiko, ang eleksyon ang kanilang **araw ng paghuhukom**.","translation":"For corrupt politicians, the election is their **day of reckoning**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o pagawaan kung saan isinasagawa ang pananahi o paggawa ng mga kasuotan.
etymology: From `pa-` + `tahi` (sew) + `-an` (locative suffix), literally 'a place for having things sewn'.
original_explanation: The magical place where your 'patahi' dreams come true. It's the workshop of a mananahi or sastre, usually filled with the sound of a sewing machine, colorful threads, and fabric scraps. The OG source of custom-fit outfits before online shopping and 'add to cart.'
usage_notes: The suffix '-an' here denotes a place. Compare with 'kainan' (eating place) from 'kain' (eat).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala ko ang tela sa **patahian** ni Aling Nena.","translation":"I brought the fabric to Aling Nena's **tailor shop**."},{"sentence":"Maraming **patahian** sa palengke na mura maningil.","translation":"There are many **dressmaker's shops** in the market that charge low prices."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghinto ng buhay; ang katapusan ng pag-iral ng isang organismo.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'log out' from life. It's when your phone battery hits 0% and there's no power bank in sight. The final 'Ayoko na, pagod na ako.'
usage_notes: The infinitive form. Often used to express the act or possibility of dying. The completed form is `namatay` (died).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw kong **mamatay** sa gutom sa gitna ng EDSA traffic.","translation":"I don't want to **die** of hunger in the middle of EDSA traffic."},{"sentence":"Lahat ng tao ay **mamatay** balang araw.","translation":"All people will **die** someday."}]

translation: to erase; to remove; to alleviate
meaning_filipino: Alisin o tanggalin ang isang bagay, tulad ng marka, sakit, o alaala.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na gusto mong i-delete ang isang ex sa isip at puso mo, pero walang Ctrl+Z. Ginagamit din 'to para sa pag-alis ng pagod, parang pag-inom ng malamig na softdrink after a long day. "Magpawi ka muna ng pagod."
usage_notes: Often used for abstract concepts like fatigue (`pagod`), sadness (`lungkot`), or memories (`alaala`).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinatanggal ng musika ang aking kalungkutan at tumutulong **magpawi** ng masasamang alaala.","translation":"Music lifts my sadness and helps **erase** bad memories."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong umupo sandali para **magpawi** ng pagod.","translation":"I need to sit for a moment to **alleviate** my fatigue."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtuon ng matindi at tuloy-tuloy na tingin sa isang tao o bagay sa loob ng mahabang panahon.
original_explanation: That moment when you see your crush and you can't help but **titigan** them from afar, hoping they don't catch you. Or when your team lead stares at you during a meeting, and you're not sure if they're impressed or if you just said something dumb. It's an intense, focused look, more powerful than a simple 'tingin'.
usage_notes: Titigan is the object-focus form of the verb 'to stare'. The actor-focus form is 'tumitig'. It implies a more intense and prolonged gaze compared to 'tingnan' (to look at).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **titigan** nang ganyan, baka matunaw ako.","translation":"Don't **stare at** me like that, I might melt."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **titigan** ang mga bituin sa gabi.","translation":"He likes to **stare at** the stars at night."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapalista o pagpapatala upang regular na makatanggap ng serbisyo, produkto, o impormasyon, na karaniwang may kaakibat na bayad.
original_explanation: Ito yung ginagawa mo sa Netflix, Spotify, at sa paborito mong YouTuber. "Don't forget to like, share, and sumuskribi!" 'Pag sinabing "sumuskribi ka na sa newsletter ko," ibig sabihin, ibigay mo na email mo para sa weekly dose of chika or updates.
