usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa ahas na iyan dahil ito ay **makamandag**.","translation":"Be careful with that snake because it is **venomous**."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga salita ay kasing **makamandag** ng tuklaw ng ahas.","translation":"Her words are as **poisonous** as a snake's bite."}]

translation: to beat up, to maul, to batter
meaning_filipino: Ang pandiwa ng pananakit sa isang tao o bagay sa pamamagitan ng paulit-ulit na pagpalo, pagsuntok, o paghampas.
original_explanation: If 'bugbugan' is the event, **bugbugin** is the action. It's what you do *to* someone or something. It's more intense than just 'suntukin' (to punch); this implies a thorough, severe beating. It's the verb for what happens to your wallet after a 12.12 sale, or what you feel like doing to your laptop when it crashes before you save.
usage_notes: A strong word indicating severe physical violence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagbanta ang lalaki na **bubugbugin** niya ang sinumang lalapit.","translation":"The man threatened that he would **beat up** anyone who came near."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **bugbugin** ang unan, masisira 'yan!","translation":"Don't **batter** the pillow, it will get ruined!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang posisyon ng pag-upo na ang bawat binti ay nasa magkabilang panig ng isang bagay, tulad ng sa kabayo o motorsiklo.
original_explanation: Imagine how you ride a motorcycle or a horse. That's nakabisaklat. You're straddling it. Also used for people who sit on railings or the armrest of a chair with their legs apart. It's the classic 'angkas' position.
usage_notes: Primarily describes a physical position.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kportable siyang **nakabisaklat** sa motorsiklo habang naghihintay.","translation":"He was comfortably **astride** the motorcycle while waiting."},{"sentence":"Bawal umupong **nakabisaklat** sa braso ng silya.","translation":"It is forbidden to sit **straddling** the arm of the chair."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa seryoso o kritikal na kalagayan; matindi ang tama o epekto.
original_explanation: This isn't just a simple "aray" or a minor inconvenience. This is "ER-level" serious. When your internet connection isn't just slow but completely dead during a final presentation, that's a **malubha** situation. When your "slight fever" turns out to be dengue, that's **malubha**. It’s the highest difficulty setting for problems.
usage_notes: Often used to describe illnesses, injuries, problems, or situations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa **malubha** siyang kalagayan sa ospital.","translation":"He is in a **critical** condition at the hospital."},{"sentence":"Naging **malubha** ang problema sa baha dahil sa walang tigil na ulan.","translation":"The flood problem became **severe** due to the non-stop rain."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng tropikal na prutas na may kulay kahel na laman, itim na buto, at berde o dilaw na balat. Kilala sa siyentipikong pangalan na *Carica papaya*.
etymology: From Spanish 'papaya', which originates from the Carib word 'papáia'.
original_explanation: The secret ingredient in tinola (sometimes). Also, the main ingredient in those soaps that promise to make you 'maputi'. It's that fruit you either love or think smells a little weird. A staple in any Filipino fruit salad.
usage_notes: The word is the same in English and Tagalog, but the pronunciation differs slightly, with the stress on the second syllable in Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gagawa si Nanay ng atsara gamit ang hilaw na **papaya**.","translation":"Mom will make pickled relish using unripe **papaya**."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang hinog na **papaya** para sa meryenda.","translation":"Ripe **papaya** is delicious for a snack."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kaganapan ng malawakang pagpatay o isang marahas na labanan na nagreresulta sa maraming namamatay.
etymology: From 'patay' (dead) + '-an' (suffix indicating an event or reciprocal action).
original_explanation: What happens in action movies when the hero finally confronts the main villain's entire army. Also, what your mom thinks is happening when you and your sibling fight over the last piece of chicken. 'Ano ba 'yan, may patayan na naman kayo diyan!'
usage_notes: Refers to a violent event involving killing, often mutual or widespread.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang balita ay puno ng mga ulat tungkol sa **patayan** sa iba't ibang bahagi ng mundo.","translation":"The news is full of reports about **killings** in different parts of the world."},{"sentence":"Nauwi sa **patayan** ang simpleng alitan ng dalawang pamilya.","translation":"The simple dispute between two families ended in a **massacre**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aksyon ng pagsunod nang malapitan sa likuran ng isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: This is what you do when your friend knows the directions to the party and you don't, so you stick to their car like glue. Also the move of a chismosa trying to overhear a juicy conversation. It's following someone, but with more focus and less personal space.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of driving or surveillance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May itim na kotse na **bumuntot** sa amin pauwi.","translation":"A black car **tailed** us on our way home."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagkain na mabilis ihanda at ihain, karaniwang ibinebenta sa mga restawran o tindahan na may serbisyong take-out o drive-thru. Ito ay madalas na tumutukoy sa mga hamburger, pritong manok, at french fries.
etymology: Direktang hiram mula sa Ingles na "fast food."
original_explanation: Eto yung sagot sa tanong na "Saan tayo kakain?" kapag pagod ka na, wala kang time, o petsa de peligro. Jollibee, McDo, KFC—ang mga patron saint ng mga estudyante at BPO employee. Mura, mabilis, at laging nandiyan para sa'yo, parang ex mong 'di ka makalimutan.
usage_notes: Isang napakakaraniwang salita sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap. Maaari ring gamitin bilang pang-uri (e.g., "fastfood restaurant").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng klase, dumaan kami sa isang **fastfood** para kumain ng burger.","translation":"After class, we dropped by a **fast food** place to eat burgers."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang manok sa paborito naming **fastfood** joint.","translation":"The chicken at our favorite **fast food** joint is delicious."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng isdang-alat na may pagkakahawig sa dalag ngunit nabubuhay sa dagat. Karaniwang tumutukoy sa mga isda tulad ng lapu-lapu.
original_explanation: Literally 'mudfish of the sea.' It's not an actual mudfish, but a saltwater fish that kinda looks like one. Think of it as the dalag's sophisticated, cosmopolitan cousin who lives by the beach. It's often another name for fish like the grouper (lapu-lapu). When you see it on a menu, expect a pricier, more 'sosyal' version of its freshwater namesake.
usage_notes: The term can refer to several different species of marine fish depending on the region, most commonly a type of grouper.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-uwi ang mangingisda ng isang malaking **dalag-dagat**.","translation":"The fisherman brought home a large **sea bass**."},{"sentence":"Pinapaksiw namin ang nahuling **dalag-dagat**.","translation":"We cooked the caught **grouper** in vinegar."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa pamamaraang naiiba sa naunang nabanggit o ginawa; isang alternatibong metodo o pagkilos.
original_explanation: The classic "It's not you, it's me" escape route. When your first plan fails (like trying to explain something to your parents), you pivot and say, "Okay, let me explain it **sa ibang paraan**." It's the verbal equivalent of turning on Waze when you're already lost.
usage_notes: Ipinapakilala ang isang alternatibong pamamaraan, paliwanag, o hakbang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kung hindi ito gumana, subukan natin **sa ibang paraan**.","translation":"If this doesn't work, let's try it **in another way**."},{"sentence":"Ipinaliwanag niya ang konsepto **sa ibang paraan** upang mas maunawaan namin.","translation":"He explained the concept **in a different way** so we could understand it better."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga katangian, kaugalian, salita, o paraan ng pamumuhay na tipikal sa isang lalawigan; hindi makabago o simple.
original_explanation: This describes the "probinsya vibe." Yung punto o accent mo na halatang-halata 'pag nasa Manila ka na. O 'yung pagiging simple at mahiyain, na minsan ay tinatawag na "promdi" (from the province). It's the opposite of being a "city-slicker." It’s the charm of the countryside, the slow pace, the fresh air—all wrapped up in one word.
usage_notes: Can sometimes be used with a slightly negative connotation to mean unsophisticated, but can also be used neutrally or positively to mean rustic or charming.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May punto siyang **lalawiganin** kaya alam mong hindi siya taga-Maynila.","translation":"He has a **provincial** accent so you know he's not from Manila."},{"sentence":"Na-miss niya ang simpleng buhay na **lalawiganin**.","translation":"She missed the simple, **rustic** life."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang biglaan at matinding pagsiklab ng galit, poot, o inis.
original_explanation: This is that 'snap'. That moment you go from 0 to 100 real quick. One minute you're calm, the next, you're fuming because someone spoiled the finale of your favorite K-drama. That sudden explosion of 'gigil' and 'inis' is **bugnit**. It’s a more intense, less common cousin of 'bugnot'.
usage_notes: A less common word, often found in literature. 'Siklab ng galit' is a more common equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa isang iglap, napuno siya ng **bugnit** at sumigaw nang malakas.","translation":"In an instant, she was filled with **sudden rage** and shouted loudly."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya napigilan ang kanyang **bugnit** nang makita ang sira-sirang proyekto.","translation":"He couldn't control his **outburst of anger** when he saw the ruined project."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumanggap ng sakramento ng kumpil sa simbahan, isang ritwal sa Kristiyanismo na nagpapatibay sa pananampalataya.
original_explanation: This is what your parents make you do before you're a teenager. It's the Catholic sacrament of confirmation, basically the church's way of saying, "Okay, you're officially part of the squad, here's some extra Holy Spirit." It's a big family event, which means... lechon.
usage_notes: Specifically used in the context of the Catholic sacrament of Confirmation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatakdang **magpakumpil** ang aking pamangkin sa susunod na buwan.","translation":"My nephew is scheduled to **get confirmed** next month."},{"sentence":"Maraming kabataan ang sabay-sabay na **nagpakumpil** sa parokya.","translation":"Many young people **got confirmed** at the same time in the parish."}]

translation: to have a mutual dispute or quarrel
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng hidwaan o pagtatalo sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang tao.
original_explanation: This is the action version of `magkaalit`. Kung sa group chat biglang nag-away-away dahil sa kung sino ang magbabayad ng pizza, 'yan, **nagkaalitan** na sila. It's the process of the quarrel itself, the back-and-forth, the drama unfolding.
usage_notes: Emphasizes the reciprocal action of quarreling among multiple parties. It's the verb form related to the noun 'alitan' (dispute).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagkaalitan** ang mga miyembro ng banda tungkol sa kanilang susunod na kanta.","translation":"The band members **had a dispute** about their next song."},{"sentence":"Madalas **magkaalitan** ang mag-asawa sa mga maliliit na bagay.","translation":"The couple often **quarrels** over small things."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa teolohiyang Katoliko, ito ay ang pagpapatawad sa temporal na kaparusahan ng mga kasalanan. Sa pangkalahatan, ito ay pagbibigay-kasiyahan sa sariling nais o pagnanasa.
original_explanation: Sa simbahan, ito yung "get out of purgatory free" card na binibigay under certain conditions. Sa totoong buhay, ito yung "cheat day" mo. Yung pag-order mo ng extra large milk tea with 100% sugar, extra pearls, at cream cheese kasi "deserve mo." Self-love, but make it sinful.
usage_notes: Primarily a religious term, but its secondary meaning of self-gratification is also understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagbisita sa pitong simbahan tuwing Mahal na Araw ay isang paraan upang makamit ang **indulhensya**.","translation":"Visiting seven churches during Holy Week is one way to gain **indulgence**."},{"sentence":"Ang pagkain ng isang buong cake ay isang **indulhensya** na bihirang-bihira kong gawin.","translation":"Eating a whole cake is an **indulgence** I very rarely do."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manunulat na dalubhasa sa pagsasalaysay ng talambuhay ng ibang tao.
original_explanation: The official, professional 'chismoso' or 'chismosa' of history. They're the ones who dig deep into someone's life—interviewing friends, reading old letters, stalking their (historical) social media—to write their life story. Sila ang gumagawa ng talambuhay na binabasa natin sa eskwelahan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Nick Joaquin ay isang tanyag na manunulat at **biyograpo** sa Pilipinas.","translation":"Nick Joaquin is a famous writer and **biographer** in the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Kinapanayam ng **biyograpo** ang mga kamag-anak ng pambansang bayani.","translation":"The **biographer** interviewed the relatives of the national hero."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging gising at hindi magawang makapahinga o makatulog, kadalasan dahil sa pag-aalala, ingay, o sakit.
etymology: Mula sa 'di' (not) at 'makatulog' (able to sleep), na galing sa ugat na 'tulog'.
original_explanation: The official state of being for anyone who just had three cups of coffee for their BPO night shift, is overthinking a 'k.' reply from their crush, or is waiting for the Shopee 12.12 sale to start. You're just staring at the ceiling, and your brain is playing a highlight reel of your most awkward moments.
usage_notes: Isang napakakaraniwang parirala upang ilarawan ang insomnia o isang gabing walang tulog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang kaba ko para sa exam bukas, **di makatulog** ako kagabi.","translation":"I was so nervous for the exam tomorrow, I was **unable to sleep** last night."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtayo sa dulo ng mga daliri ng paa upang maging mas mataas o maabot ang isang bagay, na naganap na.
original_explanation: The official move of every short person trying to get something from the top shelf. Also what you do during a concert or parade to see over the sea of heads in front of you. Basically, the analog version of "zoom in".
usage_notes: Completed aspect (past tense) of the verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumiyad** siya para makita ang prusisyon.","translation":"She **stood on tiptoe** to see the procession."},{"sentence":"Kinailangang **tumiyad** ni Ana para makuha ang libro sa itaas ng aparador.","translation":"Ana had to **stand on tiptoe** to get the book from the top of the cabinet."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hindi sinasadyang pagtama o pagkabit ng paa sa isang bagay na nagiging sanhi ng pagkawala ng balanse o pagkadapa.
original_explanation: That moment when you're walking confidently and your foot catches on a loose tile or an uneven part of the sidewalk. That brief, heart-stopping moment before you either recover or faceplant? That's **pagtakid**. It's the universe's way of saying, "Hey, slow down there, superstar."
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'pagkatisod'. 'Pagtakid' can sometimes imply a slightly harder trip.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging sanhi ng kanyang **pagtakid** ang nakakalat na laruan sa sahig.","translation":"The scattered toys on the floor caused his **stumbling**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang Monosodium Glutamate, isang pampalasa na nagbibigay ng 'umami' o malinamnam na lasa sa pagkain.
original_explanation: The secret ingredient of your lola's adobo and every Pinoy 'pampalasa' brand (Aji-no-moto, Vetsin). It's that magic dust that makes everything taste better, despite the 'nakakabobo daw' myths. The fifth flavor profile that runs in our veins.
usage_notes: Often referred to by brand names like Vetsin or Aji-no-moto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maglagay ng masyadong maraming **MSG** sa niluluto mo.","translation":"Don't put too much **MSG** in what you're cooking."},{"sentence":"Sabi nila, ang sikreto sa masarap na chichirya ay **MSG**.","translation":"They say the secret to tasty junk food is **MSG**."}]

meaning_filipino: Humanap o magbigay-diin sa mga kapintasan o pagkukulang ng isang tao, bagay, o gawa.
original_explanation: Ito yung hobby ng mga Marites at ng mga tita mo sa family reunion. "Uy, tumaba ka yata?" 'Yan, namimintas 'yan. It's the act of pointing out flaws, whether you were asked to or not (usually not).
usage_notes: May negatibong konotasyon ng pagiging labis na mapamuna o mapanuri.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **mamintas** ng gawa ng iba, pero hindi niya tinitingnan ang sarili niyang pagkakamali.","translation":"He/She loves to **criticize** the work of others, but doesn't look at his/her own mistakes."},{"sentence":"Kung wala kang magandang sasabihin, mas mabuting huwag ka nang **mamintas**.","translation":"If you have nothing good to say, it's better not to **find fault**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang muling paglala o pagbalik ng karamdaman ng isang tao na inaakalang magaling na o nagpapagaling pa lamang, kadalasan dahil sa hindi pagsunod sa payo na magpahinga.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "I told you so" from your nanay or lola. You just got over a fever, but instead of resting, you went out for milk tea, took a bath at night, or worked overtime. The next day, you're sick again. That, my friend, is **binat**. It's the universe (and your elders) reminding you that "pahinga is key." The medical community might be skeptical, but in the Filipino household, it's a very real diagnosis.
usage_notes: Isang konseptong kultural na may malalim na paniniwala sa Pilipinas, bagamat hindi ito isang pormal na terminong medikal. Ito ang konsepto sa likod ng mga pariralang 'relapse malala' sa lokal na konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag ka munang magpagod at baka ka ma-**binat**.","translation":"Don't tire yourself out yet or you might suffer a **relapse**."},{"sentence":"Kagagaling lang niya sa lagnat pero nag-basketbol agad, kaya ayan, nagkaroon ng **binat**.","translation":"He just recovered from a fever but immediately played basketball, so there, he had a **relapse**."}]

translation: to work hard for; to suffer for
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbuhos ng matinding pagsisikap, pagod, at sakripisyo upang makamit o makuha ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "no pain, no gain" verb. It's what your parents tell you about getting a diploma, what your gym instructor screams about getting abs, and what you tell yourself about enduring traffic on EDSA just to get to work. Anything worth having, you must **paghirapan**. It's the grind, the hustle, the tiis-ganda of life.
usage_notes: This is a verb in the object-focus form. "Paghirapan mo 'yan" means "You work hard for that."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **paghirapan** ang iyong mga pangarap.","translation":"You need **to work hard for** your dreams."},{"sentence":"Talagang pinaghirapan niya ang perang ipinadala sa pamilya.","translation":"He really **suffered for** the money he sent to his family."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagdudulot ng matinding hirap, sakit, o pagdurusa sa isang tao, hayop, o bagay, sa paraang pisikal o emosyonal.
etymology: From pa- + pa- + hirap, meaning "the act of causing hardship."
original_explanation: What you feel when the internet connection dies in the middle of a crucial online meeting or a Netflix cliffhanger. Also, what your "frenemy" does by posting their perfect vacation photos while you're stuck in traffic on EDSA.
usage_notes: Can refer to both physical torture and the act of making things difficult for someone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapahirap** sa mga bilanggo ay labag sa karapatang pantao.","translation":"The **torture** of prisoners is a violation of human rights."},{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na ang **pagpapahirap** sa sarili mo sa pag-iisip sa kanya.","translation":"Stop **tormenting** yourself by thinking about him/her."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bunga o resulta ng isang pangyayari, kilos, o proseso.
etymology: From `labas` (out, outside) with `ka-` and `-an` affixes. Literally, 'what comes out'.
original_explanation: This is the 'so, what happened?' part of the story. After all the drama, the effort, the chismis... ano ang kalabasan? It's the final score, the grade you get, whether you got the job or not. It’s the consequence of your actions, good or bad. 'Nag-aral ka ba? Tingnan natin ang kalabasan sa exam mo.'
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'resulta' or 'bunga'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang naging **kalabasan** ng inyong pag-uusap?","translation":"What was the **outcome** of your conversation?"},{"sentence":"Ang magandang **kalabasan** ng proyekto ay dahil sa pagtutulungan ng lahat.","translation":"The good **result** of the project was due to everyone's cooperation."}]

translation: to reunite, to get back together
meaning_filipino: Ang muling pagtitipon o pagbabalik sa pagiging magkakasama ng isang pangkat o grupo matapos ang isang panahon ng pagkakahiwalay.
etymology: From `sama` (together) and `muli` (again). The `-ng` is a linker, and the repetition of `sama` emphasizes the group nature.
original_explanation: That feeling when your high school barkada finally pushes through with the reunion after 10 years of being 'drawing'. It's the 'sana all complete' moment, but for real this time. The opposite of social distancing.
usage_notes: Often used for family reunions, batch reunions, or when a band gets back together. The repetition `sama-sama` emphasizes the collective and complete nature of the group.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inaasahan namin na **magsama-samang muli** ang buong pamilya sa Pasko.","translation":"We are hoping that the whole family will **reunite** this Christmas."},{"sentence":"Kailan kaya **magsasama-samang muli** ang paborito nating banda?","translation":"When will our favorite band ever **get back together again**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maikling talumpati o pagbati bago uminom bilang parangal sa isang tao o pagdiriwang sa isang okasyon, na sinusundan ng sabay-sabay na pag-inom.
original_explanation: The part of the party where someone gets a microphone (or just clinks a glass) and gives a speech, usually ending with "Cheers!" or "Tagay!". It's what happens right before everyone takes a synchronized shot. Not to be confused with the bread you eat for breakfast.
usage_notes: This is for the act of giving a speech before drinking. The verb form is often "mag-toast".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagbigay ng **toast** ang best man para sa bagong kasal.","translation":"The best man gave a **toast** for the newlyweds."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang buhok na tumutubo sa gilid ng mukha, sa may tapat ng tainga, na karugtong ng buhok sa ulo.
original_explanation: That strip of hair that connects your hair to your (potential) beard. Popularized by Elvis Presley, Jose Rizal, and your tito from the 70s. Kapag masyadong mahaba, mukha kang kontrabida sa pelikula ni FPJ.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"\"Ahitan mo nang maayos ang **patilya** ko,\" sabi niya sa barbero.","translation":"\"Trim my **sideburns** neatly,\" he told the barber."},{"sentence":"Mahaba ang **patilya** ng mga lalaki noong dekada sitenta.","translation":"Men's **sideburns** were long in the seventies."}]

meaning_filipino: Saktan sa pamamagitan ng paulit-ulit na pagpalo o pagsuntok; bugbugin.
original_explanation: The action version of "gulpi". This is what happens when you get caught cheating in a game, or worse, in a relationship. It's the physical manifestation of "lagot ka!" (you're in trouble!).
usage_notes: Often used to describe a physical assault or a severe beating.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binalaan niya ang magnanakaw na **gulpihin** ito kapag hindi isinauli ang gamit niya.","translation":"He warned the thief that he would **beat him up** if he didn't return his things."},{"sentence":"Ayaw kong **gulpihin** ka, pero sumusobra ka na.","translation":"I don't want to **beat you up**, but you're going too far."}]

meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng hindi pagkakaunawaan o hidwaan sa isa't isa.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung state ng dalawang tao na may "issue". Hindi pa full-blown away, pero may tension na. Think of it as the cold war phase of a friendship breakup or a family drama over the last piece of lechon. Sila ay **magkaalit**.
usage_notes: Refers to the state of being in conflict or at odds with someone. It is a less intense version of 'magkaaway'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matagal nang **magkaalit** ang dalawang magkapitbahay dahil sa hangganan ng kanilang lupa.","translation":"The two neighbors have long **been in a dispute** over their property line."},{"sentence":"Ayokong **magkaalit** tayo dahil lang sa pera.","translation":"I don't want us **to have a falling-out** just because of money."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o establisyimento kung saan gumagawa o nagbebenta ng tinapay at iba pang produktong panaderya.
etymology: Formed from "tinapay" (bread) + "-an" (location suffix), meaning "place of bread".
original_explanation: This is the source of all things good and holy at 5 AM—the place that smells like heaven and pandesal. The local "panaderya." It's where you get your fix of Spanish bread, kababayan, and the local chismis while waiting in line. The word itself sounds a bit old-school, like something your lolo would say. "Pupunta lang ako sa tinapayan."
usage_notes: A less common synonym for "panaderya". It specifically means "a place with/for bread".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maagang nagbukas ang **tinapayan** sa kanto para sa mga mamimili ng pandesal.","translation":"The **bakery** on the corner opened early for the pandesal buyers."},{"sentence":"Ang amoy mula sa **tinapayan** ay nakakagutom.","translation":"The smell from the **bakery** is appetizing."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng pagpipigil sa sarili, pagsunod sa mga alituntunin, at pagkakaroon ng maayos na kaasalan.
original_explanation: Ito yung kaklase mo nung high school na 8 PM pa lang tulog na, tapos lahat ng assignment on time. O yung officemate mong laging 15 minutes early at never nag-o-overbreak. Sila yung mga taong may 'willpower' na hindi mo alam kung saan humuhugot. Ikaw, 'pag sinabing 'diet,' hanggang lunch lang **disiplinado**.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang maging **disiplinado** ang mga sundalo sa kanilang pagsasanay.","translation":"The soldiers need to be **disciplined** in their training."},{"sentence":"Isang **disiplinado**ng manlalaro si Hidilyn Diaz.","translation":"Hidilyn Diaz is a **disciplined** athlete."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang unang antas ng pormal na edukasyon, karaniwang sumasaklaw mula sa una hanggang ikaanim na baitang.
original_explanation: The place where you peaked. You learned the multiplication table, played patintero during recess, and your biggest problem was forgetting your cartolina for a project. Also known as "mababang paaralan".
usage_notes: Maaari ring gamitin bilang pang-uri (e.g., "edukasyong elementarya").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtapos ako ng **elementarya** sa Mabini Elementary School.","translation":"I finished **elementary school** at Mabini Elementary School."},{"sentence":"Ang mga alaala ko noong **elementarya** ay masasaya.","translation":"My memories from **elementary school** are happy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bulalas na nagpapahayag ng pagkagulat, pag-aalala, pagkadismaya, o iba pang biglaang damdamin. Karaniwang pinaikling anyo ng "Ina ko!".
original_explanation: The Swiss Army knife of Filipino reactions. Spilled coffee? "Naku!" Forgot your wallet? "Naku po." Saw a cute dog? "Naku, ang cute!" It's the sound of mild panic, gentle exasperation, or sudden delight. The ultimate Tita/Tito sound effect.
usage_notes: Can be followed by 'po' for politeness ('Naku po!'). Its meaning is heavily dependent on the tone of voice.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Naku**! Nahulog ang baso!","translation":"**Oh no**! The glass fell!"},{"sentence":"**Naku** po, ang mahal naman pala niyan.","translation":"**Oh my**, that's quite expensive."}]

meaning_filipino: Gumamit ng sinsel o pait upang umukit, magbutas, o maghugis sa matitigas na materyales tulad ng bato o kahoy.
original_explanation: The OG way of carving something out before power tools existed. It's what sculptors do to turn a boring block of stone into a masterpiece, or what a construction worker does to make a precise hole in a concrete wall. It's all about that slow, deliberate, and often noisy removal of material.
usage_notes: Used in carpentry, sculpture, and construction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-ingat ang karpintero habang siya ay **nagsisinsel** sa matigas na kahoy.","translation":"The carpenter was careful while he was **chiseling** the hard wood."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **magsinsel** ng marmol kung wala kang tamang kagamitan.","translation":"It's difficult to **chisel** marble if you don't have the right tools."}]

meaning_filipino: Hayag, kita, o hindi nakatago; nasa labas at walang takip.
original_explanation: When the secret is out. Yung 'spill the tea' moment na naging headline na. It's being out in the open, no more hiding. Think of a politician's corruption getting exposed, or when your friend's secret relationship status suddenly becomes 'In a Relationship' on Facebook for everyone to see. Everything is *lantad*.
usage_notes: Maaari itong tumukoy sa isang bagay na pisikal na nakikita o sa isang impormasyon na naging pampubliko na.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lantad** na sa lahat ang kanyang masamang balak.","translation":"His evil plan is now **exposed** to everyone."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong iwanang **lantad** sa araw ang iyong pagkain.","translation":"Don't leave your food **exposed** to the sun."}]

meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang mag-ikid o magbigkis ng tali sa isang tao, hayop, o bagay.
original_explanation: This is about having the *ability* to tie something or someone. Like, "Kaya mo bang matalian 'yang baka?" (Can you manage to tie that cow?). It's a test of your knot-tying skills, whether it's for a boat, a gift, or your friend who's about to spill spoilers.
usage_notes: Focuses on the ability or success in performing the action of tying. The suffix '-an' here implies the object being tied.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko **matalian** nang mahigpit ang sapatos ko dahil sa haba ng kuko ko.","translation":"I can't **tie** my shoes tightly because of my long fingernails."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **matalian** ang mga kahon para hindi magkalat sa byahe.","translation":"You need **to be able to tie** the boxes so they don't get scattered during the trip."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian, karapatan, o pag-aari na inaangkin o taglay ng isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: This is what you call that special 'something' someone has. It's not a physical object, but a quality they 'own' or possess. "Ang galing niyang kumanta, 'yan talaga ang kaangkinan niya." It's their superpower, their special skill in the game of life. It can also be a claim to something, like that last piece of lechon you're eyeing.
usage_notes: Can refer to a right, a possession, or more commonly, a quality or talent that is inherently part of someone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagiging matapat ay isang **kaangkinan** na hinahanap ko sa isang kaibigan.","translation":"Honesty is a **characteristic** I look for in a friend."},{"sentence":"Ipinaglaban niya ang kanyang **kaangkinan** sa lupa.","translation":"He fought for his **claim** to the land."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng sangkap o paggawa ng paraan upang ang isang pagkain ay maging mas masarap.
original_explanation: The magic you do to instant pancit canton to make it gourmet. You add a fried egg, some calamansi, maybe even some leftover lechon kawali. "Pasarapan natin 'to!" is the battle cry before turning a simple meal into a feast. It's the art of the upgrade.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in a culinary context to mean enhancing flavor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pasarapan** mo pa ang adobo, lagyan mo ng kaunting asukal.","translation":"**Make** the adobo **more delicious**, add a little sugar."},{"sentence":"Ang sikreto sa pagluluto ay kung paano mo ito **papasarapin** gamit ang mga pampalasa.","translation":"The secret to cooking is how you **will make it more delicious** using spices."}]

meaning_filipino: Magtagumpay sa isang pagsusulit o pagsubok; o kaya ay maibigay o maiabot ang isang bagay sa iba.
original_explanation: The word that gives every Filipino student anxiety and relief. Before exams: 'Sana makapasa ako!' After results are out: 'Nakapasa ako!' It's the difference between a celebration and a long explanation to your parents. It can also mean 'to be able to hand something over,' like passing the salt ('pakipasa ng asin') or a document.
usage_notes: Has two common meanings: 1) to pass a test/standard, and 2) to hand over an object. The context usually makes it clear.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawa'y **makapasa** ka sa board exam.","translation":"I hope you'll be **able to pass** the board exam."},{"sentence":"Puwede bang **makapasa** ng bayad ko sa driver?","translation":"Can you **pass** my fare to the driver?"}]

meaning_filipino: Pagbibigay ng sagot o reaksyon sa isang tanong, pahayag, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: 'Yung sineen mo lang 'yung message niya for 3 hours tapos finally nag-decide kang tumugon. To reply, to answer, or to finally give in to your friend's constant "Tara, kape!" messages.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi kaagad **tumugon** ang ahensya sa mga tanong ng media.","translation":"The agency did not immediately **respond** to the media's questions."},{"sentence":"**Tumugon** ka naman sa tawag ko.","translation":"Please **answer** my call."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, salita, o kilos na nagdudulot ng pagkainis o galit sa isang tao.
etymology: From 'pang-' (instrumental prefix) + 'pa-' (causative prefix) + 'galit' (anger). Lit. 'that which is used to cause anger'.
original_explanation: This is your friend who acts like a friend, but their main goal in life is to test your patience. The one who always says 'joke lang!' after saying something offensive. The ultimate 'trigger' for your inner beast mode.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a person's annoying habit or a specific object/situation that is intentionally or unintentionally irritating.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong gawin 'yan, **pampagalit** talaga 'yang ugali mo.","translation":"Don't do that, your attitude is a real **irritant**."},{"sentence":"Ang walang tigil na pagtahol ng aso ay **pampagalit** sa gabi.","translation":"The dog's incessant barking is an **annoyance** at night."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ganap na pagsisisi sa kasalanan na bunga ng dalisay na pag-ibig sa Diyos na nasaktan dahil sa nagawang pagkakamali.
etymology: From pagsisisi (regret) + -ng (linker) + lubos (complete, perfect). A theological term.
original_explanation: The "I'm sorry because I hurt you" kind of regret. This is the highest level of being sorry. It’s not about fear of punishment; it’s about genuinely feeling terrible for disappointing someone you love (in this context, God). It’s the kind of regret that makes you want to be a better person, not just a person who avoids getting into trouble. It's the ultimate 'sana all' of apologies.
usage_notes: Primarily a religious or theological term used in Catholicism, the counterpart to 'pagsisising hindi lubos'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagsisising-lubos** ay itinuturing na sapat na para sa kapatawaran kahit bago pa man mangumpisal.","translation":"**Perfect contrition** is considered sufficient for forgiveness even before confession."},{"sentence":"Nakamit niya ang kapayapaan ng kalooban dahil sa kanyang **pagsisising-lubos**.","translation":"He achieved peace of mind because of his **perfect contrition**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang karagdagang halaga, benepisyo, o gantimpala na ibinibigay bukod sa inaasahan o sa regular na sahod.
original_explanation: Ah, the most beautiful word in the BPO and corporate world, especially in December. This is the 13th (or 14th, or 15th) month pay, the performance incentive, the extra cash that suddenly makes holiday traffic and endless meetings worth it. It's the financial equivalent of 'dasurv.'
usage_notes: A direct loanword from English, used ubiquitously in the context of employment and finance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Yehey! May **bonus** na kami sa Pasko!","translation":"Yay! We have a **bonus** for Christmas!"},{"sentence":"Gagamitin ko ang **bonus** ko para magbayad ng utang at bumili ng bagong cellphone.","translation":"I will use my **bonus** to pay off debts and buy a new cellphone."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang natatanging paraan ng pagbigkas ng mga salita na karaniwan sa isang partikular na tao, lugar, o bansa.
original_explanation: Eto yung tunog mo 'pag nagsasalita ka. Alam mo agad kung taga-Batangas, Iloilo, o conyo-from-the-south ka dahil sa punto mo. Parang seasoning sa salita.
usage_notes: Often refers to a regional accent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malakas ang **punto** niyang Bisaya kaya alam kong hindi siya taga-Maynila.","translation":"His Visayan **accent** is strong, so I know he's not from Manila."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng mga aktor ang tamang **punto** para sa kanilang papel.","translation":"The actors are studying the right **intonation** for their role."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-angkin o pagtanggap ng isang bagay na kasalukuyang ginagawa o nagaganap. Ito ang anyong pangkasalukuyan (present progressive) ng pandiwang 'kuha'.
original_explanation: This is the "-ing" form of "to get." It's what's happening right now. "Ano'ng ginagawa mo?" "Kumukuha ng pera sa ATM." It's the process, the grind. Like when you're still in college, you're "kumukuha ng kurso." You haven't gotten it yet, but you're working on it. The present struggle is real.
usage_notes: Present progressive aspect of the verb 'to get/take', indicating an ongoing action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumukuha** ako ng mga larawan para sa aming proyekto.","translation":"I **am taking** pictures for our project."},{"sentence":"Siya ang **kumukuha** ng mga order sa counter.","translation":"He/She is the one **taking** orders at the counter."}]

translation: to tie; to draw (in a game)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng parehong iskor o puntos sa isang laro o kompetisyon, na nagreresulta sa walang malinaw na panalo o talo.
etymology: From Spanish 'tabla' (board, table), which in the context of games means a draw or tie, with the Tagalog -um- infix.
original_explanation: The feeling when you and your ex both show up single to a reunion. Walang nanalo, walang natalo. It's the "it is what it is" of competition. In basketball, it's that heart-stopping moment before overtime. In chess, it's when you both run out of moves. In arguments, it's when you both agree to disagree.
usage_notes: Used specifically for games, contests, and competitions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumabla** ang laro sa iskor na 98-98.","translation":"The game **ended in a tie** with a score of 98-98."}]

translation: to look out from; to peer out
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtingin sa labas mula sa isang siwang o butas, tulad ng bintana, pinto, o anumang maliit na espasyo.
original_explanation: This is the verb for when a 'Marites' (gossip) discreetly peeks through her window to see what the neighborhood commotion is about. It's not just looking, it’s looking *from* an enclosure *outward*. Think of a turtle poking its head out of its shell, or you checking if the food delivery rider is already outside your gate.
usage_notes: Implies looking out from an enclosed space (window, door, hole).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **manungaw** sa bintana tuwing umaga.","translation":"She likes to **look out** the window every morning."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko ang isang pusang **nanungaw** mula sa ilalim ng kotse.","translation":"I saw a cat **peering out** from under the car."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagsakay o paggamit ng taxi bilang transportasyon.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'taxi'. It's what you do when you're late for work, umuulan, or just feeling extra and don't want to commute via jeepney. "Bes, taxihin na lang natin, pagod na ako." is the official slogan of the pagod-na-sa-buhay commuter club.
usage_notes: Isang kolokyal na pandiwa na nabuo mula sa pangngalang "taxi". Ang isa pang anyo ay "mag-taxi".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas mabilis kung **taxihin** na lang natin ang biyahe papuntang hotel.","translation":"It would be faster if we just **take a taxi** going to the hotel."},{"sentence":"Ayokong **taxihin** 'yan, baka malaki ang singil.","translation":"I don't want to **take a taxi** for that trip, the fare might be expensive."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangyayari o kilos na naganap nang hindi inaasahan at mabilisan.
original_explanation: The official word for when things go from 0 to 100, real quick. Your internet connection `bigla`ng nawala during a client call. Your ex `bigla`ng nag-chat ng "hi". The last piece of chicken joy `bigla`ng kinuha ng kapatid mo. It's the universe's way of saying "plot twist!" without any warning.
usage_notes: Very common adverb. Often appears as `biglang` before a verb or adjective, which is a combination of `bigla` + the linker `ng`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bigla** siyang umalis nang walang paalam.","translation":"He/She **suddenly** left without saying goodbye."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **bigla** magdesisyon nang hindi pinag-iisipan.","translation":"Don't **abruptly** make a decision without thinking it through."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng sukdulang kasanayan, kaayusan sa paggawa, at pangkalahatang kagalingan.
original_explanation: If 'napakagaling' is for a specific 'wow' moment, 'napakahusay' is for sustained, consistent excellence. It's for the BPO agent with the highest CSAT score for 6 months straight, or the chef whose every dish is a masterpiece. It implies a deep, well-honed skill. It's 'galing' with a college degree.
usage_notes: Often interchangeable with 'napakagaling', but 'napakahusay' can carry a stronger connotation of craftsmanship, competence, and well-executed work.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Napakahusay** ng pagkakagawa ng pelikulang ito, mula sa sinematograpiya hanggang sa pag-arte.","translation":"This film was **excellently** made, from the cinematography to the acting."},{"sentence":"Isa siyang **napakahusay** na abogado na laging nananalo sa kanyang mga kaso.","translation":"She is a **very competent** lawyer who always wins her cases."}]

translation: to act gay; to exhibit gay mannerisms
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos o pag-arte sa paraang "bakla" o pagpapakita ng mga gawi na itinuturing na pambakla, kadalasan sa paraang pabiro o eksaherado.
etymology: Derived from "accla" by treating it as a root word and adding verb-like English suffixes or using it in a verb context, typical of Taglish and gayspeak.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of being an "accla." When you're "accling," you're not just existing, you're *serving*. You're turning a simple walk to the sari-sari store into a runway show. You're making your coffee with a flourish. It's the act of infusing any activity with that signature flair, drama, and wit. "Stop accling!" is what your straight friends say when you're being too much (which is never).
usage_notes: Used humorously. Can also be used in a gerund form, "pag-accling."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan mo nga 'yang pag-**accling** mo, nasa harap tayo ng kliyente.","translation":"Stop **acting so gay**, we're in front of a client."},{"sentence":"He started **accling** the moment the camera was on him.","translation":"He started **acting gay** the moment the camera was on him."}]

translation: to quarantine; to be under quarantine
meaning_filipino: Ang paghiwalay o pagbubukod sa sarili o sa iba, karaniwan sa isang itinakdang lugar at panahon, upang maiwasan ang pagkalat ng nakahahawang sakit.
original_explanation: This word went from zero to hero during the pandemic. It's the official term for 'bawal lumabas ng bahay' (not allowed to leave the house) for 14 days or more. It's the ultimate 'social distancing' level-up, where your only companions are Netflix, food delivery apps, and your own slowly unraveling sanity.
usage_notes: While the root word is from Spanish, the prefix 'mag-' makes it a very common Filipino verb construction. Became extremely common during the COVID-19 pandemic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **magkuwarentenas** ng lahat ng uuwi galing sa ibang bansa.","translation":"Everyone returning from other countries needs to **quarantine**."},{"sentence":"**Nagkuwarentenas** ako sa kwarto ko nang dalawang linggo.","translation":"I **quarantined** in my room for two weeks."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang kilos ng pagsisimula ng isang gawain, pangyayari, o proseso.
original_explanation: That 'Day 1' feeling. Monday morning. The first page of a new notebook. The first 5 minutes of your diet before you see a Jollibee. It’s the opposite of 'sana matapos na 'to.' It’s the 'let's do this!'... for now. 'Pa-join ako mamaya, **nag-uumpisa** pa lang ang meeting namin.'
usage_notes: Present progressive tense of 'mag-umpisa'. Synonym of 'nagsisimula'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nag-uumpisa** pa lang ang palabas, huwag kang maingay.","translation":"The show **is just starting**, don't be noisy."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam ko, **nag-uumpisa** na ang ulan.","translation":"I feel like the rain **is starting**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isinagawa nang ayon sa sariling kagustuhan o pagkukusa; hindi pinilit o inutusan.
original_explanation: That rare, almost mythical moment your younger sibling washes the dishes without being told. It’s when you do something out of your own free will, often surprising everyone around you. 'Wow, **pakusa**?'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pakusa** siyang tumulong sa paglilinis ng kanilang silid-aralan.","translation":"He **voluntarily** helped in cleaning their classroom."},{"sentence":"Hindi mo na kailangang utusan si Ana, **pakusa** niyang ginagawa ang kanyang mga tungkulin.","translation":"You don't need to order Ana, she does her duties **of her own accord**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamataas na halal na opisyal o ehekutibong pinuno ng isang lalawigan o estado.
original_explanation: 'Yung "boss" ng isang buong probinsya. Siya 'yung may pinakamalaking tarpaulin 'pag may fiesta o Pasko, at 'yung pangalan niya nakalagay sa mga waiting shed at basketball court. The provincial chief executive.
usage_notes: Standard na termino para sa isang panlalawigang gobernador. Ang katumbas na pambabae ay 'gobernadora'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **gobernador** ang namuno sa pamamahagi ng tulong sa mga nasalanta ng bagyo.","translation":"The **governor** led the distribution of aid to the typhoon victims."},{"sentence":"Sino ang iboboto mong **gobernador** sa darating na halalan?","translation":"Who will you vote for as **governor** in the upcoming election?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang trabaho o gawain ay ang pagsusulsi o pag-aayos ng mga punit o butas sa damit o tela.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "man-" (tagagawa ng kilos) at salitang-ugat na "sulsi" (pagtahi sa punit).
original_explanation: This is your lola's superpower. Before fast fashion and Shopee hauls, there was the 'manunulsi' who could magically fix that tiny hole in your favorite uniform. They're the original clothing life extenders, the OG sustainability advocates.
usage_notes: Karaniwang tumutukoy sa isang propesyonal na mananahi o sinumang may kasanayan sa pag-aayos ng damit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala ko ang pantalon kong napunit sa **manunulsi** sa palengke.","translation":"I brought my torn pants to the **darner** at the market."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang talaan ng mga personal na karanasan at saloobin na isinusulat araw-araw; o isang pahayagan na inilalathala araw-araw.
original_explanation: Before social media, ito ang original na 'What's on your mind?'. Dito mo sinusulat ang 'Dear Diario...' para ilabas ang feels mo about your crush. Puwede ring tumukoy sa dyaryo na binibili ni Tatay tuwing umaga para sa balita at crossword puzzle.
usage_notes: Medyo luma na ang paggamit para sa 'diary' (mas karaniwan ang 'talaarawan' o 'diary' mismo), at 'dyaryo' naman para sa pahayagan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isinulat niya sa kanyang **diario** ang lahat ng kanyang mga lihim.","translation":"She wrote all her secrets in her **diary**."},{"sentence":"Nabasa ko sa **diario** na may paparating na bagyo.","translation":"I read in the **daily newspaper** that a storm is coming."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkaramdam ng matalas at parang nasusunog na sakit, karaniwan sa sugat na nalagyan ng gamot o sa balat na nabilad sa araw.
original_explanation: That moment when you put alcohol on a fresh cut and it humahapdi so bad you start seeing your ancestors. Parang 'yung katotohanang sinabi ng best friend mo tungkol sa jowa mong red flag—masakit pero kailangan.
usage_notes: Describes a specific type of sharp, burning pain, different from a dull ache.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Humapdi** ang sugat niya nang lagyan ng betadine.","translation":"His wound **stung** when betadine was applied."},{"sentence":"**Humahapdi** ang mga mata ko dahil sa usok.","translation":"My eyes are **stinging** because of the smoke."}]

translation: to be torn; to get ripped
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng punit o gisi dahil sa puwersa o aksidente.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your 100-peso bill when you try to stuff it in your wallet too fast. Or your favorite shirt when you snag it on a nail. Basically, the universe telling you, 'Oops, sira na.' It's the physical manifestation of your life falling apart after a 'seen' message with no reply.
usage_notes: Used for paper, fabric, and other thin materials. The actor-focus form is 'makapunit'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka at baka **mapunit** ang papel na iyan.","translation":"Be careful or that paper might **get torn**."}]

translation: to tunnel; to go through a tunnel
meaning_filipino: Gumawa o dumaan sa isang tunel o daanang nasa ilalim ng lupa o bundok.
original_explanation: It's what you do when you're stuck in EDSA traffic and you wish you could just dig your way to Makati. Or, it's literally just going through the SCTEX or Kennon Road tunnels. No drama, just infrastructure.
usage_notes: Often used literally for vehicles or people passing through tunnels.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magtunel** sa ilalim ng bundok para mas mabilis ang biyahe.","translation":"We need to **tunnel** under the mountain to make the trip faster."},{"sentence":"**Magtunel** na lang tayo para iwas traffic sa ibabaw.","translation":"Let's just **go through the tunnel** to avoid the traffic on the surface."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bilang na kasunod ng apatnapu't siyam at bago ang limampu't isa; katumbas ng 50.
original_explanation: The age you hit when you start getting senior citizen discounts but your knees feel like they're a hundred. Also, the price of a small milk tea, if you're lucky. From the Spanish 'cincuenta'.
usage_notes: Often shortened to 'singkwenta' in informal speech and text.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkakahalaga ng **singkuwenta** pesos ang isang kilong bigas.","translation":"One kilo of rice costs **fifty** pesos."},{"sentence":"May **singkuwenta** katao ang dumalo sa pagpupulong.","translation":"There were **fifty** people who attended the meeting."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong ang buong buhay at mga desisyon ay kontrolado ng paghahangad o pagpapanatili ng kayamanan, na isinasantabi ang ibang mahahalagang aspeto ng buhay.
original_explanation: 'Yung tita mong ayaw um-attend ng family reunion kasi sayang daw 'yung OT sa work. Or 'yung friend mong pinipili ang pera over friends, over love, over everything. That's an **alipin ng salapi**.
usage_notes: Isang idyoma na may negatibong konotasyon, tumutukoy sa pagiging materyoso o sakim.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming opisyal ang nagiging **alipin ng salapi** kaya nasasangkot sa katiwalian.","translation":"Many officials become a **slave to money**, which is why they get involved in corruption."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang opisyal na papel o dokumento na naglalaman ng mahahalagang impormasyon, kasunduan, o tala. Maaari rin itong tumukoy sa mga banal na aklat ng isang relihiyon.
etymology: From ka- + sulat (write) + -an (place/result of action). Literally 'a collection of writings.'
original_explanation: Ito 'yung papel na pinapapirmahan sa'yo bago ka mag-start sa trabaho—'yung contract. O 'yung titulo ng lupa ni lola. Basically, any important paper that proves something. Kung sa love life, ito 'yung 'marriage contract,' ang ultimate 'proof of relationship' na may pirma ni mayor.
usage_notes: Can refer to a single document or a body of writings, like the Holy Scriptures (Banal na Kasulatan).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinirmahan nila ang isang **kasulatan** na nagsasaad ng mga tuntunin ng kanilang negosyo.","translation":"They signed a **document** that states the terms of their business."},{"sentence":"Ang Banal na **Kasulatan** ay gabay sa buhay ng maraming mananampalataya.","translation":"The Holy **Scripture** is a guide for the lives of many believers."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong palaging nagbibigay ng matinding puna o negatibong komento laban sa isang tao, partikular na sa mga sikat na personalidad sa social media.
original_explanation: A 'basher' is someone whose full-time job seems to be leaving hateful comments online. They're the ones in the comments section saying 'Laos na 'yan!' or 'Retokada!'. They probably need a hug, or a hobby. Or both.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in the context of online and celebrity culture.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marami siyang **basher** pero marami rin siyang tagahanga.","translation":"She has many **bashers**, but she also has many fans."},{"sentence":"Hindi pinapansin ng artista ang kanyang mga **basher**.","translation":"The celebrity ignores his/her **bashers**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tulong, suporta, o ambag, lalo na ang materyal na tulong na ipinamamahagi ng pamahalaan o organisasyon sa mga nangangailangan, lalo na sa panahon ng krisis o kalamidad.
original_explanation: The magic word of the pandemic era. This is the government-provided goodie bag (or cash) that makes everyone suddenly best friends with the barangay captain. Waiting for ayuda became a national pastime, complete with memes, drama, and a listahan. It's basically "help," but with a political and social-media-frenzy flavor.
usage_notes: Became extremely common during the COVID-19 pandemic to refer to government aid.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghihintay ang mga residente para sa pamamahagi ng **ayuda**.","translation":"The residents are waiting for the distribution of **aid**."},{"sentence":"Ang isang sakong bigas ay bahagi ng **ayuda** mula sa LGU.","translation":"A sack of rice is part of the **aid** from the LGU."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng tawa o ngiti na hindi tunay at nagpapahiwatig ng pangungutya, pag-insulto, o kawalan ng paniniwala.
etymology: Compound of "tawa" (laugh) and "aso" (dog), literally "dog's laugh," possibly alluding to a dog baring its teeth in a way that resembles a grin but is actually a sign of aggression.
original_explanation: It's that fake, sarcastic laugh. You know the one. When your frenemy compliments your outfit, and you give them that tight-lipped smile that says "I know you're lying." That's tawang-aso. It's the laugh of a kontrabida in a teleserye.
usage_notes: Always carries a negative connotation of mockery or insincerity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **tawang-aso** lang ang isinagot niya sa aking paliwanag.","translation":"He just gave a **sarcastic laugh** in response to my explanation."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko ang **tawang-aso** sa kanyang mga labi nang mabigo ang katunggali niya.","translation":"I saw the **sneer** on his lips when his rival failed."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang araw na hindi pista opisyal o araw ng pahinga; isang tipikal na araw na may pasok sa trabaho o eskwela.
original_explanation: It's your Monday to Friday grind. The days you set your alarm for, battle the commute, and count down the hours until you can log off. Not a holiday, not a weekend, just the regular programming of your life.
usage_notes: Refers to a typical workday or school day, as opposed to a weekend or holiday.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas matindi ang trapik tuwing **karaniwang araw** kumpara sa Sabado at Linggo.","translation":"The traffic is worse on a **weekday** compared to Saturday and Sunday."},{"sentence":"Anong almusal mo sa isang **karaniwang araw**?","translation":"What's your breakfast on an **ordinary day**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tao o pangkat na nasa pinakahuling puwesto sa isang kompetisyon, paligsahan, o anumang uri ng pagraranggo.
original_explanation: Being 'kulelat' is the ultimate 'sana all' but in reverse. It's being the last one to cross the finish line, the team at the bottom of the UAAP standings, or the last one to get the joke. It’s a term of pity, sometimes playful teasing, for the one who came in last. Nobody wants to be the kulelat, but hey, at least you finished, right? ...Right?
usage_notes: Can also function as an adjective (e.g., 'siya ay kulelat'). It has a slightly negative and informal connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa kasamaang palad, ang pangkat namin ang **kulelat** sa paligsahan.","translation":"Unfortunately, our group was the **tail-ender** in the competition."},{"sentence":"Ayokong maging **kulelat** sa klase kaya nag-aaral ako nang mabuti.","translation":"I don't want to be in **last place** in class, so I study hard."}]

translation: poetic debate, verbal joust in verse
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng debate o pagtatalo na isinasagawa sa paraang patula. Ito ay ipinangalan kay Francisco Balagtas, ang ama ng panulaang Tagalog.
etymology: Named after Francisco Balagtas (Baltazar), a prominent Filipino poet, with the suffix "-an" denoting a place or event related to the name.
original_explanation: The OG Filipino rap battle, but with more 'makata' vibes and less diss tracks. Instead of beats, you have meter and rhyme (tugma at sukat). It's a formal debate on a topic, where two poets (mambabalagtas) try to out-rhyme and out-reason each other in front of a live audience. Think of it as the intellectual showdown of your Lolo's generation, usually held during a town fiesta.
usage_notes: A key element of Filipino literary tradition, often performed during Buwan ng Wika (National Language Month).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paksa ng **balagtasan** ay kung 'Dapat ba o Hindi Dapat Manligaw ang Babae?'","translation":"The topic of the **poetic debate** is 'Should or Should Not a Woman Initiate Courtship?'"},{"sentence":"Nanalo ang panig ng lakandiwa sa ginanap na **balagtasan** sa aming paaralan.","translation":"The moderator's side won the **poetic joust** held at our school."}]

meaning_filipino: Bumaon o tumagos sa isang bagay, karaniwang gamit ang isang matulis na kasangkapan.
original_explanation: Think of a barbecue stick expertly piercing through chunks of pork for the perfect inihaw. That's 'umulos'. It’s the action of a sharp object making its way through something. "Nang mahulog ang mangga, umulos ang sanga sa prutas."
usage_notes: Describes a piercing or thrusting motion, often with force.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umulos** ang matalim na pako sa kanyang tsinelas.","translation":"The sharp nail **pierced** through his slipper."},{"sentence":"Mabilis na **umulos** ang espada sa dibdib ng kalaban.","translation":"The sword quickly **thrust** into the enemy's chest."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagbabantay o pagmamasid nang maigi upang maprotektahan ang isang lugar, tao, o bagay.
original_explanation: This is the job of the security guard sa mall, the barangay tanod doing rounds, or you, watching your food delivery app like a hawk waiting for the rider to arrive. It's the act of being on high alert, keeping an eye out for anything sus. Your personal CCTV mode.
usage_notes: Often associated with security, vigilance, and protection.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang masusing **pagtatanod** sa gabi upang maiwasan ang pagnanakaw.","translation":"Vigilant **guarding** at night is important to prevent theft."},{"sentence":"Nagpalitan sila sa **pagtatanod** sa maysakit.","translation":"They took turns **keeping watch** over the sick person."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong nagtatrabaho sa pugon, karaniwan ay sa paggawa ng tinapay, palayok, o pagtutunaw ng metal.
etymology: From Spanish 'fogonero' (stoker, fireman), derived from 'fogón' (hearth, furnace).
original_explanation: The OG firebender of the workplace. Sila yung mga tito na sanay sa init, hindi dahil sa summer sa Pinas, kundi dahil sa trabaho nila sa harap ng pugon. Think of the guys making your pan de sal hot and fresh, or the unsung heroes in a pottery shop.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pugunero** ang tagabantay ng tamang init ng hurno para sa mga palayok.","translation":"The **kiln worker** is the one who monitors the correct heat of the kiln for the pots."},{"sentence":"Maaga pa lang ay gising na ang **pugunero** upang maghanda ng tinapay.","translation":"The **furnace operator** is already awake early to prepare the bread."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maliit at matamis na kahel (orange) na madaling balatan.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "mandarín", na tumutukoy sa prutas.
original_explanation: 'Yung orange na laging present tuwing Chinese New Year para daw swerte. Ito 'yung pinsan ng Dalandan at Ponkan na mas madaling hubaran. Perfect pang-baon kasi hindi messy.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa prutas na *Citrus reticulata*. Upang tukuyin ang wika, mas malinaw na gamitin ang "Wikang Mandarin".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng isang kilong **mandarin** sa palengke.","translation":"Mom bought a kilo of **mandarin oranges** at the market."},{"sentence":"Matamis ang **mandarin** na ito.","translation":"This **mandarin orange** is sweet."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal o Taglish na nangangahulugang tumanggap ng isang bagay. Ito ay nasa aspektong perpektibo.
original_explanation: The past tense of getting that Shopee/Lazada package you've been waiting for. It's the "OMG, andito na!" moment. Also used for when you finally got your 13th-month pay. "Guys, **nag-receive** na ako ng sahod! Tara, milk tea!"
usage_notes: This is a very common Taglish (Tagalog-English) code-switching word used in informal conversations, especially in office or online shopping contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **nag-receive** na rin ako ng email mula sa HR.","translation":"Finally, I **received** an email from HR."},{"sentence":"**Nag-receive** ka na ba ng parcel mo?","translation":"Have you **received** your parcel already?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang hindi patas na pagtrato o pagpapakita ng higit na pagkiling sa isang tao o grupo kaysa sa iba.
original_explanation: The system that powers the "teacher's pet" and the "anak ni boss" phenomenon. It's the unfair advantage someone gets just because they're the favorite. It’s why your officemate who just does 'pacute' gets the promotion while you, the OT-King/Queen, are still stuck. It's the dark side of 'pabor'.
usage_notes: Carries a negative connotation of unfairness or bias.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Talamak ang **paboritismo** sa kanilang kumpanya kaya marami ang nag-reresign.","translation":"**Favoritism** is rampant in their company, which is why many are resigning."},{"sentence":"Ang pagbibigay ng bonus base sa **paboritismo** ay labag sa polisiya.","translation":"Giving bonuses based on **favoritism** is against policy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa o pagtupad sa isang gawain, tungkulin, o plano.
original_explanation: This is the 'performance' part of your job description, yung actual na pag-trabaho mo. It's the moment of truth, the 'paki-execute' ng boss mo. In showbiz, ito yung acting performance ng artista. In Filipino grammar, it's the objective complement, the thing being acted upon. Basically, the 'doing' part.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of roles, duties, or artistic performances. Interchangeable with 'pagganap'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **paganap** bilang bida ay hinangaan ng lahat.","translation":"His **performance** as the lead actor was admired by all."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang tapat na **paganap** sa tungkulin.","translation":"Honest **fulfillment** of one's duty is important."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagpatay sa apoy, pagpigil sa paglala ng isang sitwasyon, o pagpapakalma sa matinding damdamin.
original_explanation: This is what firefighters do to a fire, what your friend does to your 'marupok' feelings for your ex, or what you do to a political flame war online by muting everyone. It's the act of stopping something from spreading.
usage_notes: Can be used for literal fire or metaphorical 'fires' like anger, rebellion, or gossip.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis ang **pag-apula** ng mga bumbero sa sunog sa palengke.","translation":"The firefighters' **extinguishing** of the market fire was quick."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **pag-apula** sa galit bago pa ito lumaki.","translation":"The **suppression** of anger is important before it escalates."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng molusko na may dalawang magkatakip na kabibe, karaniwang nabubuhay sa buhanginan sa tubig-alat o tubig-tabang.
etymology: Unknown, possibly a native Austronesian term.
original_explanation: The star of your favorite Tinolang Halaan. These are the small, tasty clams you buy by the kilo sa palengke. Don't confuse them with tahong (mussels) or talaba (oysters). Halaan are the ones that make your soup taste like the sea, in a good way. They're the reason you sometimes get a bit of sand in your sabaw, but it's totally worth it.
usage_notes: Refers to various species of clams, often used in soups like Tinola.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng isang kilong **halaan** para sa tinola.","translation":"Mom bought a kilo of **clams** for the tinola soup."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang sabaw ng **halaan** lalo na kung may luya at sili.","translation":"The broth of **clams** is delicious, especially with ginger and chili."}]

translation: state of being stunned or deafened
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging litó o pansamantalang pagkabingi dahil sa isang napakalakas na tunog o ingay.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling pagkatapos ng concert ng paborito mong rock band, o 'pag napagalitan ka ng nanay mo na parang may megaphone. Your ears are ringing, and you can't process anything. Yan ang pagkatulig.
usage_notes: Can refer to a literal deafening from sound or a figurative stunning from a shocking event or scolding.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang **pagkatulig** matapos ang malakas na pagsabog.","translation":"He felt the **state of being deafened** after the loud explosion."},{"sentence":"Halos isang oras ang kanyang **pagkatulig** dahil sa ingay ng makina.","translation":"His **state of being stunned by the noise** lasted for almost an hour due to the machine's sound."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pagluluto o pagtitinda ng bibingka, isang uri ng kakaning gawa sa galapong at gata ng niyog. Ito ay nasa aspektong panghinaharap.
etymology: From `mag-` (verb prefix) + `bibingka` (a type of rice cake).
original_explanation: This is what your tita does when the Christmas season is near. It means to make or sell that fluffy, charcoal-smelling rice cake we all love. If someone says they're going to 'magbibingka', you know your Simbang Gabi is about to be extra special. It's the verb form of holiday calories.
usage_notes: Can mean either making for personal consumption or selling as a business. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magbibingka** si Aling Nena para sa pista sa susunod na linggo.","translation":"Aling Nena **will make bibingka** for the fiesta next week."},{"sentence":"Ang pamilya niya ay **magbibingka** sa tapat ng simbahan ngayong Pasko.","translation":"His family **will sell bibingka** in front of the church this Christmas."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbaba o pag-alis ng lulan, karga, o pasahero mula sa isang sasakyan. Maaari ring tumukoy sa pagbabawas ng bigat o pasanin.
original_explanation: This is the moment of sweet release when you finally get to unload your groceries from the car after a palengke trip, or when you finally get off the jam-packed MRT. It can also be metaphorical, like 'pag-iibis ng sama ng loob'—unloading your emotional baggage on your bestie over a tub of ice cream.
usage_notes: Can be used for both physical unloading and metaphorical unburdening.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabagal ang **pag-iibis** ng mga kargamento mula sa barko.","translation":"The **unloading** of cargo from the ship was slow."},{"sentence":"Ang pakikipag-usap sa kaibigan ay isang paraan ng **pag-iibis** ng problema.","translation":"Talking to a friend is a way of **unloading** one's problems."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa heometriya, isang planong pigura na may hindi bababa sa tatlong tuwid na gilid at anggulo, at karaniwang may limang o higit pa.
etymology: From Spanish "polígono" or English "polygon", from Greek "polugōnon" (many-angled).
original_explanation: Remember that thing from high school math that you thought you'd never use again? Well, here it is. A poligon is just a fancy word for any closed shape with straight sides: triangles, squares, pentagons, hexagons, etc. It's the building block of everything in geometry and, let's be real, the reason for many headaches during exams. 'Sir, ano po ulit ang formula para sa area ng octagon?'
usage_notes: A technical term used in mathematics and geometry.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang parisukat at tatsulok ay mga halimbawa ng **poligon**.","translation":"A square and a triangle are examples of a **polygon**."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aralan namin sa klase kung paano kwentahin ang mga panloob na anggulo ng isang regular na **poligon**.","translation":"We studied in class how to calculate the interior angles of a regular **polygon**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpasok ng isang matulis na bagay, tulad ng karayom, sa isang ibabaw o katawan, karaniwan upang maglagay ng gamot o likido.
original_explanation: What nurses do that can make a grown man cry. It's getting your vaccine shot, your anti-rabies, or that gluta drip for the 'artistahin' glow. A moment of pain ('aray!') for a long-term gain.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis lang ang **pagturok** ng bakuna.","translation":"The **injection** of the vaccine is just quick."},{"sentence":"Takot siya sa **pagturok** ng karayom.","translation":"He is afraid of the **prick** of a needle."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang balbal na paglalarawan sa isang tao na labis na emosyonal, madamdamin, o malungkutin sa isang partikular na sandali.
etymology: Derived from the English "emo" subculture, but used as a verb ("nag-e-emo") or adjective to describe a state of being emotional.
original_explanation: When someone is being overly dramatic or sentimental, you say they're "nag-e-emo". It's the state of listening to sad songs in the rain, posting cryptic hugot lines, or just being generally moody. "Hayaan mo na 'yan, nag-e-emo lang 'yan kasi iniwan ng jowa." (Leave him be, he's just being emo because his girlfriend left him.)
usage_notes: Often used with the prefix "nag-" (nag-e-emo) to denote the action of being emotional.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong **emo**, problema lang 'yan.","translation":"Don't be too **emotional**, it's just a problem."},{"sentence":"Gabi-gabi siyang nag-e-**emo** habang nakikinig sa mga paborito niyang kanta.","translation":"Every night he gets **emo** while listening to his favorite songs."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng gamot na karaniwang ginagamit bilang pampaginhawa sa sakit (analgesic), pampababa ng lagnat (antipyretic), at anti-inflammatory.
original_explanation: The go-to cure-all for Pinoys, from headaches caused by traffic to heartaches caused by your crush. "Masakit ulo ko." "Uminom ka ng aspirina." "Masakit puso ko." "Uminom ka pa rin ng aspirina." It's the Tita's first line of defense.
usage_notes: A common household medicine name, often used generically for any mild pain reliever.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng **aspirina** para sa sakit ng ulo ko.","translation":"I need an **aspirin** for my headache."},{"sentence":"Nagdala si Nanay ng **aspirina** baka sakaling may lagnatin.","translation":"Mom brought **aspirin** just in case someone gets a fever."}]

meaning_filipino: Karapat-dapat isumpa; nagdudulot ng matinding galit o pagkamuhi na hahantong sa pagmumura o pagsumpa.
original_explanation: Imagine 'yung traffic sa EDSA on a payday Friday habang umuulan at may sale sa lahat ng mall. That situation is kasumpa-sumpa. It's so frustrating and infuriating you just want to curse at the universe. It's the feeling you get when your internet dies in the middle of a crucial online meeting.
usage_notes: An intensifier like 'kasuklam-suklam,' but specifically related to being worthy of a curse due to frustration or evil.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kasumpa-sumpa** ang sinapit ng mga biktima ng karahasan.","translation":"The fate of the victims of violence was **accursed**."},{"sentence":"Nagsimulang magmura ang tsuper dahil sa **kasumpa-sumpang** trapiko.","translation":"The driver started cursing because of the **damnable** traffic."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng magaspang at di-pinong telang bulak na karaniwang may kulay o disenyo.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'calicó', na hango sa Calicut, isang lungsod sa India kung saan orihinal na ginawa ang tela.
original_explanation: This is that T-shirt material you buy in Divisoria that feels a bit rough, the kind your tita uses for pambahay. It's not quite Japanese cotton, not quite silk, but it gets the job done for a budget-friendly price. Think of the fabric for bandanas or cheap curtains.
usage_notes: Karaniwang tumutukoy sa murang tela na yari sa bulak at may mga nakalimbag na disenyo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng ilang metrong **kaliko** para gawing punda.","translation":"Mom bought a few meters of **calico** to make pillowcases."},{"sentence":"Ang damit niya ay yari sa simpleng **kaliko** lamang.","translation":"Her dress is made of just simple **calico**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang itaas na bahagi sa loob ng bibig; ang ngalangala.
etymology: Kaugnay ng tunog na nililikha gamit ito.
original_explanation: Ito yung parte ng bibig mo na laging biktima ng bagong luto at sobrang init na pizza o sopas. The official name for the 'roof of your mouth.'
usage_notes: Ang salitang 'ngalangala' ay mas karaniwang ginagamit upang tukuyin ang 'palate' sa modernong pakikipag-usap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napaso ang kanyang **palatak** dahil sa mainit na kape.","translation":"The **roof of his mouth** was burned by the hot coffee."},{"sentence":"Ang mga tunog na /k/ at /g/ ay nililikha sa may malambot na **palatak**.","translation":"The sounds /k/ and /g/ are produced near the soft **palate**."}]

translation: to be adjacent; to border each other
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging magkatabi, magkadikit, o magkahangganan ng dalawa o higit pang lugar o bagay.
original_explanation: Think of your relationship with your work chismis buddy—your cubicles are probably `magkanugnog`. It means right next to each other, sharing a border. Like how Quezon City and Marikina are `magkanugnog`, or how the sinigang and adobo are on the buffet table. It's all about proximity.
usage_notes: Often used in geography to describe bordering towns, provinces, or countries. The adjective form is 'kanugnog'. 'Magkanugnog' is the verb describing this state.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magkanugnog** ang mga lungsod ng San Juan at Mandaluyong.","translation":"The cities of San Juan and Mandaluyong **are adjacent**."},{"sentence":"Pinlano nilang bumili ng mga lote na **magkanugnog** para maging magkapitbahay sila.","translation":"They planned to buy lots that **border each other** so they could be neighbors."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging puno o pagkasira dahil sa paninirahan o pagkain ng anay.
original_explanation: When the termites have officially won and your wooden aparador is now more like a pile of dust waiting to happen. 'Huwag mo nang bilhin 'yang silya, mukhang inanay na.'
usage_notes: Most commonly used in its past tense form, "inanay".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang palitan ang sahig dahil **inanay** na ito.","translation":"The floor needs to be replaced because it **is already infested with termites**."},{"sentence":"Sayang ang magandang aparador, **inanay** na ang likod.","translation":"It's a shame about the beautiful cabinet, its back has been **infested with termites**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang siyentista o dalubhasa na nag-aaral ng heolohiya, kabilang ang pisikal na estruktura at mga sangkap ng Daigdig, ang kasaysayan nito, at ang mga prosesong humuhubog dito.
original_explanation: A rock star, but literally. They're the experts you see on TV after an earthquake, explaining fault lines. They get excited about things that are millions of years old, which is also how you feel after a long week of work.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinapanayam ng media ang isang **heologo** mula sa PHIVOLCS matapos ang lindol.","translation":"The media interviewed a **geologist** from PHIVOLCS after the earthquake."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga bagay na may kaugnayan sa kalangitan, sansinukob, o sa mga espirituwal o banal na nilalang.
original_explanation: Anything na pang-outer space or pang-langit. Stars, planets, angels, gods—lahat 'yan selestiyal. 'Pag sinabing 'celestial body,' 'wag kang green-minded, hindi 'yan 'yung pang-gym. It means a planet or a star. It's the vibe of being heavenly or out of this world.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa panitikan, astronomiya, at relihiyosong konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng mga astronomo ang mga **selestiyal** na katawan tulad ng mga bituin at planeta.","translation":"Astronomers study **celestial** bodies like stars and planets."},{"sentence":"May **selestiyal** na ganda ang kanyang mukha na parang anghel.","translation":"Her face has a **celestial** beauty, like an angel's."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kilos ng pagsama o pag-angkop sa isang tao o grupo; o sa kalagayan ng pagiging magkakasama.
original_explanation: The opposite of FOMO (Fear Of Missing Out). When your friend says "Tara, kape!" and you say "Sama ako!" It's the foundation of every barkada trip, every "team building," and every chismis session. To be "sama" is to be part of the group, not left behind.
usage_notes: As a root word, it forms many verbs like `sumama`, `samahan`, `makisama`. Can also be used as a noun, 'kasama' (companion).
