usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sama** ka sa amin mamaya sa mall.","translation":"**Come with** us to the mall later."},{"sentence":"Lagi silang magka-**sama** sa hirap at ginhawa.","translation":"They are always **together** through thick and thin."}]

translation: piece by piece; bit by bit
meaning_filipino: Sa paraang paunti-unti at masinsinan, karaniwang tumutukoy sa pagkalap ng impormasyon o pagbuo ng isang salaysay mula sa maliliit na detalye.
original_explanation: How you assemble chismis. You get a small piece from Marites A, another bit from Marisol B, and a tiny screenshot from Kevin C. You're gathering info **piece by piece** until you have the full, glorious, and probably exaggerated story. It's investigative journalism, but for group chat drama.
usage_notes: Nagbibigay-diin sa isang mabagal at masusing proseso ng pagsunod sa mga pahiwatig.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tagu-tagunton** niyang binuo ang kwento ng nakaraan mula sa mga lumang sulat.","translation":"**Piece by piece**, he constructed the story of the past from old letters."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang manggagawa, lalo na ang gumagamit ng pisikal na lakas sa kanyang trabaho, tulad sa konstruksiyon o pabrika.
original_explanation: Your friendly neighborhood construction worker, the factory employee, the unsung heroes building our condos and roads. They're the backbone of the economy, the ones who literally get their hands dirty. Think 'manggagawa' but with a more classic, almost historical feel.
usage_notes: While 'manggagawa' is more common today, 'obrero' is still understood and used, often in historical or formal labor-related discussions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtipon ang mga **obrero** upang ipaglaban ang kanilang mga karapatan.","translation":"The **laborers** gathered to fight for their rights."},{"sentence":"Ang tatay niya ay isang marangal na **obrero** sa isang pabrika ng sapatos.","translation":"His father was an honorable **laborer** in a shoe factory."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng panlinis na gawa sa taba o langis at alkali, ginagamit kasama ng tubig upang magtanggal ng dumi sa katawan o sa mga bagay.
original_explanation: The OG life-saver for when you're feeling 'lagkit' or after a sweaty commute on the MRT. It's your first line of defense against germs, bad vibes, and the 'amoy-araw' that clings to you. Whether it's a beauty bar for that 'kutis-artista' look or a simple 'perla' for laundry, sabon is non-negotiable in the Pinoy household.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong bumili ng bagong **sabon** dahil paubos na ang nasa banyo.","translation":"I need to buy new **soap** because the one in the bathroom is almost used up."},{"sentence":"Ang **sabon** na ito ay mabango at maganda sa balat.","translation":"This **soap** is fragrant and good for the skin."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking gusali sa isang bukid na ginagamit na imbakan ng mga ani o silungan ng mga alagang hayop.
original_explanation: This word is basically just the English word 'barn' used in a Tagalog sentence. You'd probably only hear it if you're on a farm-themed resort in Batangas or watching a dubbed American movie. We'd more likely say 'bodega' for storage or 'kulungan' for animals.
usage_notes: Not a common word in daily Filipino conversation. 'Kamalig' or 'bodega' are more traditional equivalents.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinago ng magsasaka ang dayami sa **barn**.","translation":"The farmer stored the hay in the **barn**."},{"sentence":"May malaking pulang **barn** sa gitna ng bukid.","translation":"There is a big red **barn** in the middle of the field."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi sinasadyang mawala sa isip o alaala ang isang bagay, tao, o impormasyon.
original_explanation: This is the classic "Oops, I forgot" moment. 'Yung naiwan mo 'yung wallet mo sa bahay, or 'yung anniversary niyo. Unlike 'makalimot' (the ability to forget), 'makalimutan' is about a specific thing being forgotten, usually accidentally. "Sorry, na-traffic ako sa EDSA at sa sobrang stress, nakalimutan ko na 'yung pinapabili mo."
usage_notes: Focuses on the object or person being forgotten. It's the most common way to say "to forget."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **makalimutan** ang payo ng iyong ina.","translation":"Don't **forget** your mother's advice."},{"sentence":"Ay! **Nakalimutan** kong magdala ng payong, uulan pa naman.","translation":"Oh! I **forgot** to bring an umbrella, and it looks like it's going to rain."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong palaboy, walang permanenteng tirahan, at palipat-lipat ng lugar.
etymology: Hango sa wikang Espanyol na 'vagabundo' (vagrant, wanderer).
original_explanation: Your parents' worst nightmare for your future if you don't study hard. It's the classic term for a wanderer or a bum. Today, it can also be used half-jokingly to describe a travel blogger or someone who's always "laag" (wandering).
usage_notes: Can have a negative connotation, implying laziness or being a societal burden, but can also be used more neutrally for a wanderer.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Namumuhay siyang parang **bagamundo**, walang tiyak na patutunguhan.","translation":"He lives like a **vagrant**, with no certain destination."},{"sentence":"Kung hindi ka mag-aaral nang mabuti, baka maging **bagamundo** ka lang.","translation":"If you don't study well, you might just become a **vagabond**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang organulo sa loob ng mga selula ng halaman at alga na siyang lugar ng potosintesis.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "cloroplasto," mula sa Griyegong "khlōros" (berde) at "plastos" (nabuo).
original_explanation: Ito yung kitchen sa loob ng cell ng halaman. Dito niluluto ang pagkain niya (glucose) gamit ang sikat ng araw, tubig, at carbon dioxide. Kung wala ito, wala kang kanin at gulay, besh. Back to basics ng Science class.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa agham, lalo na sa biyolohiya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kloroplas** ang nagbibigay ng berdeng kulay sa mga dahon.","translation":"The **chloroplast** gives the green color to the leaves."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng mga katangian ng buhay; hindi patay.
original_explanation: The opposite of 'dedz'. That feeling when you get your 13th month pay, or when the chismis you're listening to is super juicy. 'Buhay na buhay ang dugo!' means you're super alert or worked up.
usage_notes: The stress shifts from the first syllable (BU-hay, noun) to the second syllable (bu-HAY, adjective).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Buhay** pa ba ang luma nating telebisyon?","translation":"Is our old television still **working** (lit: alive)?"},{"sentence":"Natagpuan siyang **buhay** at walang galos matapos ang aksidente.","translation":"He was found **alive** and unscathed after the accident."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang piraso ng papel o kard na nagpapatunay ng pagbabayad at nagbibigay ng karapatan sa isang tao na pumasok sa isang lugar, sumakay sa sasakyan, o lumahok sa isang kaganapan.
original_explanation: Your golden pass to everything from a chaotic bus ride to a sold-out K-Pop concert. It's that piece of paper (or QR code) you guard with your life. Sa Pinas, ang **tiket** ay hindi lang basta papel, ito ay pangarap—pangarap makauwi sa probinsya, pangarap makita ang idol mo, o pangarap lang na makalabas ng traffic violation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawala ko ang **tiket** ko sa bus pauwing probinsya.","translation":"I lost my bus **ticket** going home to the province."},{"sentence":"Sold out na agad ang mga **tiket** para sa concert.","translation":"The **tickets** for the concert were immediately sold out."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpunta o paglalakbay mula sa isang lugar patungo sa iba, karaniwan ay sa malayo o sa loob ng mahabang panahon.
original_explanation: What you wish you were doing instead of being stuck in traffic. It's the act of going on an adventure, whether it's a soul-searching trip to Sagada or just trying to navigate the MRT during rush hour.
usage_notes: The infinitive/past tense form. Present: 'umalakbay'. Future: 'aalakbay'. A more common form is 'naglakbay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Magellan ay **umalakbay** sa buong mundo.","translation":"Magellan **traveled** around the world."},{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang **umalakbay** at makita ang iba't ibang kultura.","translation":"It's her dream to **travel** and see different cultures."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na tumakas o umiwas mula sa pagkakakulong, pagkaalipin, o isang mapanganib o hindi kaaya-ayang sitwasyon.
original_explanation: The main character in every action movie who just broke out of prison. Or you, when you sneak out of the house to meet your friends even though your parents said no. In the BPO world, a 'takas' is someone who goes AWOL.
usage_notes: Can refer to a person who has escaped literally (a fugitive) or figuratively (someone who ran away from a responsibility).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinaghahanap ng mga pulis ang mga **takas** mula sa bilangguan.","translation":"The police are searching for the **escapees** from the prison."},{"sentence":"Para siyang **takas** sa mental hospital sa suot niya.","translation":"He looks like an **escapee** from a mental hospital with what he's wearing."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng bukas na kamalayan sa mga nangyayari sa kapaligiran, lalo na sa mga isyung panlipunan; maaari ring tumukoy sa pagiging dilat ng mga mata.
original_explanation: That moment you realize lumpia is not a health food. More seriously, it's when you're 'woke.' Hindi ka na basta-basta naniniwala sa chismis o fake news. You're socially aware, you know your rights, and you question the system. You've taken the red pill, Neo.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa literal na pagbukas ng mata, o sa metaporikal na pagiging mulat sa lipunan o pulitika.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa murang edad, **mulat** na si Jose sa kahirapan ng kanilang pamilya.","translation":"At a young age, Jose was already **aware** of his family's poverty."},{"sentence":"Layunin ng edukasyon na gawing **mulat** ang mga mamamayan sa kanilang mga karapatan.","translation":"The goal of education is to make the citizens **enlightened** about their rights."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paraang may pag-iingat; dahan-dahan at may pansin sa kaligtasan.
original_explanation: This is how your mom tells you to do things when you're handling something fragile or expensive. 'Hawakan mo 'yan nang paingat!' (Hold that carefully!). It's the opposite of being 'burara' or reckless. It’s moving with the precision of someone diffusing a bomb, or, more relatably, carrying a full bowl of hot sinigang to the dining table.
usage_notes: Often used with 'nang' to form an adverbial phrase: 'nang paingat'. It is a stylistic variation of 'nang maingat'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglakad siya nang **paingat** sa madulas na sahig.","translation":"She walked **carefully** on the slippery floor."},{"sentence":"Ibinaba niya nang **paingat** ang babasaging plorera.","translation":"He put down the fragile vase **with care**."}]

translation: to leave something for last; to deliberately be late for something
meaning_filipino: Itakda o ilagay ang isang gawain, tao, o bagay sa pinakadulong bahagi ng isang pagkakasunod-sunod; sinasadyang maging huli para sa isang layunin.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `i-` (nagsasaad ng sanhi), `pagpa-` (nagsasaad ng sanhi), at `huli` (last/late).
original_explanation: 'Yung sinasabi mong "save the best for last" sa buffet, pero sa totoo lang, inuuna mo lang 'yung mura. Or when you deliberately arrive late to an event para "grand entrance" ang dating. It's the act of intentionally putting something or someone at the very end.
usage_notes: Maaaring mangahulugang unahin ang isang bagay sa huli, o sadyang huliin ang isang tao/bagay para sa isang partikular na dahilan (ang dahilan ang siyang layon ng pandiwa).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ipagpahuli** ang pag-aaral para sa iyong mga laro.","translation":"Don't **leave** your studies **for last** in favor of your games."},{"sentence":"Bakit mo ba ako laging **ipinagpapahuli** sa mga plano ninyo?","translation":"Why do you always **include me last** in your plans?"}]

translation: to lead someone on; to give someone false hope
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng sadyang pagbibigay ng pag-asa sa isang tao nang walang balak na tuparin ang ipinapahiwatig o ipinapangako.
original_explanation: The verb form of being a relationship villain. This is what a `paasa` does. It's the act of sending those "good morning" texts, giving compliments, and making future plans (like "let's go out sometime") with zero intention of following through. It's emotional clickbait. If you do this, there's a special place in hell for you, right next to people who talk in the cinema.
usage_notes: This is the action performed by a "paasa". The person being led on is the one being "pinaasa".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na ang **paasahin** siya kung wala ka namang gusto sa kanya.","translation":"Stop **leading her on** if you don't even like her."},{"sentence":"Bakit mo ako **pinaasa** nang ganito katagal?","translation":"Why did you **give me false hope** for so long?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maingay na pagkain o pagnguya; mabilis at malakas na pagsubo ng pagkain.
etymology: Onomatopoeic. The sound of a mouth opening and closing noisily.
original_explanation: The sound your seatmate makes in the cinema while eating popcorn, making you question your life choices. It's chewing with your mouth open, with full sound effects. The opposite of "poise". Parang baka ngumuya.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb root (e.g., 'ngumabngab'). Often used with a slightly negative or humorous connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagsabihan mo nga 'yang kapatid mo, ang lakas ng **ngabngab** niya habang kumakain.","translation":"Can you tell your sibling, his **noisy chewing** is so loud while eating."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **ngumabngab** na parang baboy.","translation":"Don't **gobble** your food like a pig."}]

translation: to unstitch, to rip a seam
meaning_filipino: Tanggalin ang tahi sa isang kasuotan o tela; kalasin ang sinulid na nagdurugtong sa mga bahagi ng damit.
original_explanation: Before you can alter a pair of jeans or fix a dress, you have to magtastas first. It's the act of carefully undoing stitches, the opposite of sewing. It's a job for a seam ripper and a lot of patience. It’s the deconstruction phase before the reconstruction, like breaking up with someone before you can work on yourself. #hugot
usage_notes: Specific to undoing stitches or seams in fabric.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **magtastas** ng laylayan ng pantalon dahil masyado itong mahaba.","translation":"I need to **unstitch** the hem of the pants because it's too long."},{"sentence":"Maingat siyang **nagtastas** ng lumang burda upang palitan ng bago.","translation":"She carefully **ripped the seam** of the old embroidery to replace it with a new one."}]

translation: to be able to be reloaded; to be loaded with cargo
meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang malagyan o mapunuan muli ng karga, tulad ng sa isang sasakyan, baril, o anumang sisidlan.
etymology: ma- (ability) + re- (again) + karga (from Spanish "carga", meaning load) + -han (locative/benefactive suffix)
original_explanation: This sounds very specific, like something a BPO agent in a logistics account would say. "Sir, hindi po marekarguhan 'yung truck kasi over capacity na." It means to be able to be loaded up. Can also be used for reloading a gun or even putting load on your phone ('marekarguhan ng load'). It's about filling something up with its intended content, often for a second time.
usage_notes: A bit technical. The simpler form 'makargahan' (to be loaded) is more common. 'Marekarguhan' specifically implies reloading or a second loading.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **marekarguhan** ang barko bago ito umalis sa pantalan.","translation":"The ship needs **to be reloaded** before it leaves the port."},{"sentence":"Hindi **marekarguhan** ang baril dahil sira ang magasin.","translation":"The gun cannot **be reloaded** because the magazine is broken."}]

translation: to run away from home, to elope
meaning_filipino: Ang kusang pag-alis sa tahanan o sa isang lugar nang walang paalam, kadalasan dahil sa galit, pagsuway, o pagnanais na makatakas.
original_explanation: The ultimate teenage drama move. It's when you've had enough of your parents' rules and you pack your bags to "live with a friend." The phrase "maglayas ng babae" is the old-school term for when a man takes a woman to elope, a.k.a. "tanan". It's a classic telenovela plot twist. "Nag-away sila ng tatay niya, kaya nagbanta siyang maglalayas."
usage_notes: The phrase "maglayas ng babae" specifically means to elope with a woman, which is now more commonly called "itanan".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **maglayas** dahil lang sa maliit na pagtatalo.","translation":"Don't **run away from home** just because of a small argument."},{"sentence":"Noong unang panahon, malaking iskandalo kapag ang isang lalaki ay **naglayas ng babae**.","translation":"In the old days, it was a big scandal when a man **eloped with a woman**."}]

translation: prone to dizziness; easily gets dizzy
meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng isang tao na madalas o madaling makaranas ng pagkahilo.
original_explanation: This is your friend who can't ride a bus without a Katinko, can't look down from a high place, and definitely can't join you on a rollercoaster. They have a low tolerance for spinning, travel, or anything that upsets their equilibrium. The "-hin" suffix means they're susceptible to it.
usage_notes: Describes a person's tendency. Formed by adding the suffix '-hin' to the root 'liyo'. A common synonym is 'mahiluhin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dala ko lagi ang white flower oil dahil ako ay **maliyuhin** sa biyahe.","translation":"I always bring white flower oil because I am **prone to dizziness** during travel."},{"sentence":"Hindi siya sumama sa pamamangka dahil **maliyuhin** siya.","translation":"He didn't join the boating trip because he **easily gets dizzy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na may tulis o dulo na ginagamit sa pagdutdot, pagturo, o pag-indayog sa isang bagay.
etymology: Mula sa "pang-" (instrumento) + "dutdot" (pagpindot nang marahan at paulit-ulit).
original_explanation: Before the Apple Pencil, there was the OG pandutdot for your Palm Pilot or Nokia touch screen phone. Nowadays, it can be anything from a ballpen you use to press a reset button to a barbecue stick you use to check if the cake is cooked.
usage_notes: Ang kahulugan ay lubos na nakadepende sa kung ano ang dinudutdot.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawawala ang **pandutdot** ng luma kong cellphone.","translation":"The **stylus** of my old cellphone is missing."},{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng patpat bilang **pandutdot** sa uling.","translation":"He used a stick as a **poker** for the charcoal."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang babaeng uri ng usa, isang hayop na kilala sa pagiging mahinhin at mailap.
original_explanation: Think Bambi's mom. The symbol of grace and gentleness in the forest. In human terms, it's that crush of yours who's super quiet, elegant, and seems to gracefully glide away whenever you try to approach them.
usage_notes: A specific biological term used to distinguish the female deer from the male.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang magandang **usang babae** ang nakita naming nanginginain sa parang.","translation":"We saw a beautiful **doe** grazing in the meadow."},{"sentence":"Ang mga mata niya ay parang sa isang **usang babae**, malumanay at maamo.","translation":"Her eyes are like a **doe's**, gentle and tame."}]

translation: to strengthen; to stabilize; to establish
meaning_filipino: Palakasin, patibayin, o gawing matatag ang isang bagay, samahan, o pundasyon.
original_explanation: This is what you do after a major life 'plot twist' or a breakup. You pick yourself up and **magpatatag** ka. It's about strengthening your foundations, whether it's your career, your friend group, or your emotional well-being. It's the opposite of being 'marupok.' Also what engineers do to buildings after an earthquake.
usage_notes: Can be used for physical structures, organizations, or abstract concepts like relationships or one's spirit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bagong pamunuan ay nagsisikap na **magpatatag** ng ekonomiya.","translation":"The new leadership is striving to **stabilize** the economy."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng bagyo, kailangan nilang **magpatatag** ng kanilang mga bahay.","translation":"After the storm, they need to **strengthen** their houses."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kabuluhan, pakinabang, o halaga ng isang bagay, gawain, o pangyayari.
etymology: From `ka-` + `parak` + reduplication of `-ra-`. The root `parak` is an archaic term related to destination or purpose.
original_explanation: This is that Tita-level word for 'So what's the point?' or 'Anong mapapala ko dito?' When you're weighing if that unli-rice promo is worth the extra 50 pesos, you're questioning its kapararakan. It’s the ROI (return on investment) of your life choices, often used when there seems to be none.
usage_notes: Frequently used in negative constructions like 'walang kapararakan' to mean 'pointless' or 'useless'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tila walang **kapararakan** ang aming pagod kung hindi rin ito makikita ng hepe.","translation":"Our hard work seems to have no **worth** if the boss won't even see it."},{"sentence":"Ano ba ang **kapararakan** ng proyektong ito para sa komunidad?","translation":"What is the **benefit** of this project for the community?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaki na gumaganap sa tungkulin ng isang ama ngunit hindi tunay na ama sa dugo; pangalawang asawa ng ina.
etymology: Mula sa salitang 'ama' na may reduplikasyon at hulaping '-an', na nagpapahiwatig ng isang ginagampanang papel o pekeng bersyon.
original_explanation: This is your mom's new husband, your "stepdad." Not the OG dad, but he's in the picture now. The relationship can range from "best bud who teaches you to drive" to "that guy who sits in your real dad's favorite chair." It's complicated, like a teleserye plot.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabuti ang pakikitungo sa kanya ng kanyang **ama-amahan**.","translation":"His **stepfather** treats him well."},{"sentence":"Kahit **ama-amahan** lang ako, ituturing ko siyang tunay na anak.","translation":"Even if I am only a **stepfather**, I will treat him as my own son."}]

translation: to notice; to criticize; to point out
meaning_filipino: Makita o maobserbahan ang isang bagay, lalo na ang isang kamalian o kakulangan; punahin.
original_explanation: That thing your tita does at family reunions. 'Uy, tumaba ka.' Or when your boss spots the one typo in your 100-page report. It's the act of observing something and then—crucially—saying something about it. It's the opposite of 'seen-zoned'.
usage_notes: Can be neutral (to notice) or negative (to criticize). Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay walang **mapuna** sa aking presentasyon mamaya.","translation":"I hope no one will **point out** any flaws in my presentation later."},{"sentence":"Agad niyang **mapuna** ang pagbabago sa ayos ng silid.","translation":"He can immediately **notice** the change in the room's arrangement."}]

meaning_filipino: Manakit, mang-api, o gumawa ng masama sa kapwa sa paraang mapang-abuso at mapanliit.
etymology: From 'dusta' (afflicted, oppressed, miserable), possibly of Sanskrit origin.
original_explanation: This is what villains in teleseryes do. It's not just simple bullying; it's a whole level of oppressive, cruel behavior. Think of the evil stepmother, the corrupt haciendero, or that micromanager who enjoys making you feel small. To 'mandusta' is to crush someone's spirit with cruelty.
usage_notes: A very strong and formal word. 'Mang-api' is the more common term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinaglaban ng mga manggagawa ang kanilang karapatan laban sa mga naghahangad na **mandusta** sa kanila.","translation":"The workers fought for their rights against those who wished to **oppress** them."},{"sentence":"Hindi tama na **mandusta** ng kapwa dahil lamang sa kanilang katayuan sa buhay.","translation":"It is not right to **maltreat** others just because of their status in life."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtitipon o pagsasama-sama nang siksikan sa isang maliit na espasyo.
original_explanation: 'Yung eksena sa MRT tuwing rush hour. O 'yung mga tao sa palengke kapag may bagong dating na isda. O 'yung mga ka-chismisan mo 'pag may bagong tea. It's the opposite of social distancing.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin para ilarawan ang mga tao, ngunit maaari ding gamitin para sa mga bagay, hayop, o halaman.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bawal **magkulumpol** ang mga tao para maiwasan ang pagkalat ng sakit.","translation":"People are forbidden to **cluster** to prevent the spread of disease."},{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **magkulumpol** ang mga estudyante sa harap ng bulletin board para tingnan ang kanilang mga grado.","translation":"The students started to **crowd together** in front of the bulletin board to check their grades."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nag-aalok ng suhol o lagay upang makakuha ng pabor o impluwensyahan ang desisyon ng iba, lalo na ng isang taong may kapangyarihan.
original_explanation: The person who believes 'cash is king' and that anything can be solved with a little 'padulas.' They're the ones slipping a folded bill to the traffic enforcer or giving 'gifts' to an official to speed up a permit. A manunuhol operates on the principle of 'walang hindi nadadaan sa mabuting usapan... at konting pera.'
usage_notes: Carries a strong negative and illegal connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinuli ng mga pulis ang **manunuhol** na negosyante.","translation":"The police arrested the businessman who was a **briber**."},{"sentence":"Ang pagiging **manunuhol** ay isang krimen na may mabigat na parusa.","translation":"Being a **briber** is a crime with a heavy penalty."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang makaramdam ng matinding galit, pagkasuklam, o pag-ayaw sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: The feeling you get when you see your ex happily in a new relationship on Facebook. It's that intense 'gigil' you feel towards the kontrabida in a teleserye. It’s a level of dislike that's more than just 'ayaw ko,' it's 'I CANNOT.'
usage_notes: A very strong word expressing intense dislike or hatred.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **kamuhian** ang isang taong minsan mong minahal.","translation":"It's hard **to hate** a person you once loved."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang mga kasinungalingan, nagsimula siyang **kamuhian** ng mga tao.","translation":"Because of his lies, people began **to despise** him."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapahayag ng pagkakatulad o paghahambing sa isang tao, bagay, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: The ultimate comparison tool. 'Gusto ko ng jowa na kagaya ni Captain Ri.' 'Sana all, kagaya niya, may travel budget.' It's the word you use when you're pointing out a similarity, whether you're describing a doppelgänger or wishing for a life that's like someone else's.
usage_notes: Almost always used with 'ng' or 'ni' to connect to the object of comparison (e.g., 'kagaya ng', 'kagaya ni'). On its own, it is less common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang boses niya ay **kagaya** ng isang anghel.","translation":"Her voice is **like** an angel's."},{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng damit na **kagaya** ng isinusuot ng paborito kong artista.","translation":"I bought a dress **similar to** what my favorite actress wears."}]

meaning_filipino: Inamag; tinubuan ng amag o mga maliliit na halamang-singaw, karaniwan dahil sa pagkabilad sa halumigmig.
original_explanation: 'Yung hitsura ng tinapay na iniwan mo sa cabinet ng dalawang linggo. O 'yung amoy ng damit na hindi natuyo nang maayos nung tag-ulan. Basically, a food's or item's "expired" look. Not a good look, unless you're a scientist studying fungi.
usage_notes: A less common, literary word for 'moldy'. The word 'inaamag' is more frequently used in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **agihap** na ang tinapay na naiwan sa mesa.","translation":"The bread left on the table has become **moldy**."},{"sentence":"Itapon mo na 'yang pagkaing **agihap**.","translation":"Throw away that **moldy** food."}]

translation: to let someone go on vacation; to send someone on a vacation
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng pahintulot o pagkakataon sa isang tao na magbakasyon o mamahinga mula sa trabaho o tungkulin.
original_explanation: This is what every employee dreams their boss would say: 'Sige, pagbakasyunin na kita.' It's the act of giving someone the green light to go on that much-needed leave. It can also be what a rich tita does for her favorite pamangkin, 'I'll pay for your trip to Japan, pagbakasyunin kita!'
usage_notes: An object-focus verb (-in suffix) where the object is the person being allowed or sent to vacation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabait ang amo niya, kaya madali siyang **pagbakasyunin** kapag kailangan.","translation":"Her boss is kind, so it's easy **to get permission for her to go on vacation** when needed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pakiusap o utos na plantsahin o ituwid ang isang damit o tela gamit ang plantsa; tumutukoy din sa mga damit na nakatakdang plantsahin.
etymology: From 'plantsa' (clothing iron, from Spanish 'plancha') and the prefix 'pa-', indicating a request or an item intended for the action.
original_explanation: "Ma, paplantsa po ng uniform ko!" The battle cry of every student on a Sunday night. This is the act of asking someone to iron your clothes for you. It's a staple of household chores vocabulary. It can also be used as a noun, like "marami akong paplantsa" (I have a lot of clothes to be ironed).
usage_notes: Can function as a verb in a request ("Paplantsa ako nito") or as a noun referring to the clothes to be ironed ("Dala ko ang mga paplantsa").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Paplantsa** ko lang itong polo ko para bukas.","translation":"I'll just **have my polo shirt ironed** for tomorrow."},{"sentence":"Inipon niya ang lahat ng kanyang **paplantsa** para sa Sabado.","translation":"She gathered all her **clothes to be ironed** for Saturday."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang napakaliit na kulisap o kuto, karaniwang matatagpuan sa mga manok o iba pang ibon, na nagdudulot ng matinding kati.
original_explanation: Remember that super itchy feeling you get sometimes for no reason? Pwedeng 'hanip' 'yan! These are microscopic monsters, the ninjas of the insect world, often found on chickens. If someone says 'para kang may hanip,' it means you can't seem to stay still, like you're being bitten by invisible pests.
usage_notes: The primary meaning refers to the insect. The figurative use for restlessness is also common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nangangati ang buong katawan ko, parang kinagat ng **hanip**.","translation":"My whole body is itchy, as if bitten by **mites**."},{"sentence":"Tingnan mo ang mga manok, mukhang may mga **hanip**.","translation":"Look at the chickens, they seem to have **mites**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang matigas na materyal mula sa puno at iba pang halaman, na ginagamit bilang panggatong o sa paggawa ng mga gusali at kasangkapan. Maaari rin itong tumukoy sa mismong puno.
original_explanation: Before it was a minimalist aesthetic table from IKEA, it was a **kahoy** (tree). It's what your lolo's rocking chair is made of. In school, it's what you call your classmate who's a stiff or bad actor ('Ang **kahoy** mo umarte!'). It's both the source material and the insult.
usage_notes: While it can mean 'tree', 'puno' is more specific for a living tree. 'Kahoy' is more often used for the material (wood) or a felled tree. It's also used colloquially as an adjective to mean 'stiff' or 'unnatural' in acting or dancing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mesa ay gawa sa matibay na **kahoy** na narra.","translation":"The table is made of sturdy narra **wood**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong **kahoy** sumayaw, mag-relax ka lang.","translation":"Don't be so **stiff** when you dance, just relax."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang magkaroon ng pagkakataong magbigay ng isang bahagi; ang tumanggap ng isang parte o hati.
original_explanation: That feeling when a coworker brings a whole box of donuts and you're hoping you'll mabahagi-an. Or when you finally get the courage to share your chika with your bestie. It's about getting a piece of the pie, literally or figuratively.
usage_notes: Often used with the suffix `-an` (`mabahaginan`) to mean "to be given a share of." By itself, it can mean "to be able to share."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana'y **mabahagi** ko sa inyo ang aking mga natutunan.","translation":"I hope **to be able to share** with you what I have learned."},{"sentence":"Lahat ng empleyado ay umaasang **mabahaginan** ng bonus.","translation":"All employees are hoping **to be given a share** of the bonus."}]

translation: to fall with a thud; to fail (an exam)
meaning_filipino: Ang marahas na pagbagsak ng isang bagay na nagdudulot ng malakas na tunog. Sa kolokyal na gamit, nangangahulugan din itong hindi pagpasa sa isang pagsusulit o kurso.
original_explanation: Two meanings, both painful. 1) The sound of a durian hitting the ground. 2) The feeling when you see your grade is '5.00'. 'Bes, nalagpak ako sa exam!' is a cry for help that can only be cured by milk tea and a good cry session. It's the sound of gravity and your GPA hitting rock bottom.
usage_notes: Has both a literal meaning (to fall heavily) and a very common colloquial meaning (to fail an academic test or subject).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig kong **malagpak** ang mga mangga mula sa puno.","translation":"I heard the mangoes **fall with a thud** from the tree."},{"sentence":"Ayokong **malagpak** sa Math ngayong semestre.","translation":"I don't want **to fail** in Math this semester."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang kilos ng paglalagay o pagbibitay ng mga nilabhang damit sa sampayan upang matuyo. Ito ay nasa aspektong imperpektibo.
original_explanation: You, looking out the window, seeing your neighbor currently doing this chore, and thinking, "Ah, so hindi lang pala ako ang naglalaba ngayon." It's a silent bond between neighbors.
usage_notes: Present progressive tense (imperpektibo) of 'magsampay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Habang **nagsasampay** si Aling Nena, nakikipagkwentuhan siya sa kanyang kapitbahay.","translation":"While Aling Nena **is hanging clothes to dry**, she chats with her neighbor."},{"sentence":"Tingnan mo ang langit, mukhang uulan. Huwag ka na munang **magsampay**.","translation":"Look at the sky, it looks like it will rain. Don't **hang the clothes to dry** for now."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mataas na ranggo sa militar, mas mataas sa mayor-heneral at mas mababa sa heneral.
original_explanation: A super high-ranking military officer. This isn't the 'tenyente' you see in old Filipino movies patrolling the barrio; this one's a big boss with three stars on their shoulder. They're probably in charge of a whole army corps, not just a small platoon.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa konteksto ng Sandatahang Lakas ng Pilipinas at iba pang militar sa buong mundo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **tenyente-heneral** ang namuno sa operasyon laban sa mga rebelde.","translation":"The **lieutenant general** led the operation against the rebels."},{"sentence":"Itinaas sa ranggong **tenyente-heneral** si Heneral Santos.","translation":"General Santos was promoted to the rank of **lieutenant general**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang opisyal na yunit ng pananalapi sa Estados Unidos at iba pang mga bansa, ayon sa pamantayang ortograpiyang Filipino.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na 'dollar', na inangkin sa ortograpiyang Filipino.
original_explanation: The currency of your OFW relatives. This is what fuels the Balikbayan box economy and the reason why money-changers are always busy in December. The standard spelling, unlike its cousin 'dolar'.
usage_notes: This is the standard Filipino spelling for 'dollar'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumaas na naman ang halaga ng **dolyar** laban sa piso.","translation":"The value of the **dollar** against the peso has risen again."},{"sentence":"Ilang **dolyar** ang baon mo para sa biyahe?","translation":"How many **dollars** is your allowance for the trip?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang patuloy na pag-iyak o pagdaing nang mahina, karaniwang ginagawa ng isang aso o bata.
etymology: Mula sa reduplikasyon ng salitang-ugat na 'aing' (whimper) at unlaping '-um-'.
original_explanation: This is the sound your dog makes when it wants a piece of your chicharon but you're not giving in. It's that low-key, manipulative whining that pulls at your heartstrings. The audio equivalent of puppy dog eyes. Kids do this too when they want a new toy at the mall.
usage_notes: The reduplication 'aing-aing' implies a continuous or repeated action of whimpering.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kanina pa **umaing-aing** ang tuta dahil hinahanap nito ang kanyang ina.","translation":"The puppy has been **whimpering continuously** for a while because it's looking for its mother."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **umaing-aing** diyan, hindi kita bibigyan ng kendi.","translation":"Don't **whine** there, I won't give you candy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sistema o paniniwala sa politika kung saan ang isang pinuno o monarko ay may hawak ng ganap at walang takdang kapangyarihan.
original_explanation: 'Yung gobyerno na parang nanay mo noong bata ka: "Bakit?" "Kasi sinabi ko." Walang tanong-tanong, walang reklamo, a.k.a. one-man rule. From Spanish "absolutismo".
usage_notes: A political and historical term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aralan namin sa kasaysayan ang pagbagsak ng **absulutismo** sa Pransya.","translation":"We studied in history the fall of **absolutism** in France."},{"sentence":"Maraming tao ang tumutol sa **absulutismo** dahil nililimitahan nito ang kalayaan.","translation":"Many people oppose **absolutism** because it limits freedom."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malawak na anyong lupa na buhangin o bato sa tabi ng dagat, lawa, o ilog.
original_explanation: Your go-to summer destination for that perfect IG-worthy sunset pic. It's where you go to get a tan, a beer, and maybe some much-needed 'me time' away from the city traffic. Also the setting for 90% of Filipino rom-coms where the characters 'find themselves.'
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'dalampasigan', though 'dalampasigan' can feel more poetic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumunta kami sa **aplaya** ng Boracay para magbakasyon.","translation":"We went to the **beach** of Boracay for a vacation."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng gangrena; ang pagkabulok o pagkamatay ng himaymay (tissue) ng isang bahagi ng katawan dahil sa pagkawala ng suplay ng dugo o malubhang impeksyon.
original_explanation: This is a serious medical term, not your everyday hugot. When a wound gets super infected and the tissue starts to die, that's when it can `magkanggrena`. It's the body's version of "It's not you, it's me... I'm literally dying here." Usually heard in hospitals or in very dramatic teleseryes.
usage_notes: Strictly a medical or biological term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinayuhan ng doktor na putulin ang binti upang hindi na ito **magkanggrena** pa.","translation":"The doctor advised to amputate the leg so it would not **develop gangrene** anymore."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa diabetes, tumaas ang panganib na **magkanggrena** ang kanyang mga paa.","translation":"Due to diabetes, the risk of his feet **developing gangrene** increased."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mitsa o pabilo ng isang ilawan, kandila, o lampara na siyang sumisipsip ng panggatong upang magpaningas.
original_explanation: This is the little stringy thing in the middle of your birthday candle or your Lola's old-school gasera. It's the heart of the flame. No timsim, no light. Parang sa relationship, kung walang "spark" o "timsim" na nagkokonekta sa inyo, madilim ang future.
usage_notes: An older word, often associated with traditional lamps (gasera, ilawan).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napundi na ang **timsim** ng gasera kaya kailangan na itong palitan.","translation":"The **wick** of the oil lamp has burned out, so it needs to be replaced."},{"sentence":"Maingat niyang itinaas ang **timsim** para lumakas ang apoy.","translation":"He carefully raised the **wick** to make the flame stronger."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marka o sugat na dulot ng pagdiin ng mga ngipin sa isang bagay. Maaari ring tumukoy sa akto mismo ng paggamit ng ngipin upang putulin o hawakan ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: The OG action scene. Pwedeng kagat ng langgam, aso, o 'yung friend mo na nanghihingi ng 'isang kagat lang' sa Jollibee Chickenjoy mo pero kalahati na pala 'yung kinuha. It's the physical evidence of being bitten.
usage_notes: Often used to describe the result of biting (e.g., 'may kagat ng lamok'). The verb form is 'kumagat' or 'kagatin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **kagat** ng lamok ang kanyang mga binti.","translation":"Her legs are full of mosquito **bites**."},{"sentence":"Isang **kagat** lang, busog ka na sa sarap ng burger na ito.","translation":"Just one **bite**, and you'll be satisfied with how delicious this burger is."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto o paraan ng pagpapako sa krus bilang parusang kamatayan.
original_explanation: The ultimate sacrifice play. This refers to the act of being nailed to a cross, most famously associated with Jesus Christ's passion. In the Philippines, some devotees even re-enact this during Holy Week. It's intense, symbolic, and definitely not for the faint of heart.
usage_notes: Pangunahing tumutukoy sa pagpapako sa krus ni Kristo, ngunit maaari ring gamitin para sa sinumang sumailalim sa ganitong parusa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **krusipiksyon** ni Hesus ay ginugunita tuwing Biyernes Santo.","translation":"The **crucifixion** of Jesus is commemorated every Good Friday."},{"sentence":"May mga deboto sa Pampanga na nagsasagawa ng totoong **krusipiksyon** bilang panata.","translation":"There are devotees in Pampanga who perform actual **crucifixion** as a vow."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang institusyon ng mas mataas na edukasyon at pananaliksik, na nagbibigay ng mga akademikong digri sa iba't ibang larangan ng pag-aaral.
original_explanation: It's the place you go to after high school para 'hanapin ang sarili mo' but you end up just finding puyat, stress, and a mountain of readings. It's the final boss level of your education before you face the real final boss: adulting.
usage_notes: Madalas na pinapaikli bilang 'univ' sa kolokyal na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtapos siya ng medisina sa isang kilalang **unibersidad** sa Maynila.","translation":"He/She graduated with a medical degree from a well-known **university** in Manila."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng halaman (Chromolaena odorata) na may mga katangiang gamot. Sa ibang konteksto, ito ay nangangahulugang isang mahina at malungkot na daing o panaghoy.
etymology: The plant is *Chromolaena odorata*. The meaning 'moan' is likely onomatopoeic or related to the sound of wind through the plant's leaves.
original_explanation: This word is a two-for-one deal. It's the name of a plant your lola might use for *hilot* or to treat a cut (it's also called Siam weed). But it also sounds like a sad, low moan, like the sound you make when you see your Meralco bill. 'Hagunoy ng puso kong sawi.'
usage_notes: The plant meaning is more common in rural/botanical contexts. The 'moan' meaning is more poetic. It's important to distinguish from 'hagunot' (fast sound).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang dahon ng **hagunoy** para ipantapal sa sugat.","translation":"He used the leaf of the **Siam weed** to cover the wound."},{"sentence":"Sa katahimikan ng gabi, tanging ang **hagunoy** ng hangin ang maririnig.","translation":"In the silence of the night, only the **wail** of the wind could be heard."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pagkain na gawa sa harina, tubig, at kung minsan ay itlog, na hinuhulma sa iba't ibang hugis at karaniwang niluluto sa kumukulong tubig.
etymology: Mula sa Italyano na "pasta" sa pamamagitan ng Espanyol na "pasta".
original_explanation: Comfort food ng bayan! Spaghetti, carbonara, mac 'n' cheese—lahat 'yan **pasta**. Ito yung go-to handa sa birthday party ng mga bata, at yung craving mo kapag 'di ka makapili between rice meal at sandwich. Parang relationship, maraming shapes and sizes pero lahat masarap pag may tamang sauce.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa mismong ulam o sa mga noodles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magluluto ako ng **pasta** para sa hapunan.","translation":"I will cook **pasta** for dinner."},{"sentence":"Paborito ng mga bata ang Pinoy-style spaghetti, isang uri ng matamis na **pasta**.","translation":"Kids' favorite is Pinoy-style spaghetti, a type of sweet **pasta**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aalis ng mga mikrobyo, bakterya, o iba pang nakakapinsalang organismo sa isang bagay o lugar gamit ang kemikal.
original_explanation: It's what your mom yells at you to do with the groceries when you get home from the palengke, a.k.a. the COVID-19 pandemic's most overused verb. You do this to your phone, your hands, your doorknobs... basically everything except your ex's memories. You can't disinfect those.
usage_notes: The root 'disimpekta' is from Spanish. The 'mag-' prefix indicates an action done by the subject.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **magdisimpekta** ng buong bahay pagkatapos magkaroon ng may sakit.","translation":"The whole house needs **to be disinfected** after someone got sick."},{"sentence":"**Magdisimpekta** ka ng mga kamay mo bago kumain.","translation":"**Disinfect** your hands before eating."}]

translation: to make someone worship; to have someone worship
meaning_filipino: Utusan o hikayatin ang isang tao na magsagawa ng ritwal ng pagsamba o pagbibigay-galang sa isang itinuturing na banal o makapangyarihan.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of making someone go to church or pray. It's what your lola tells you to do every Sunday morning, or what you tell your friend to do when they're about to take a super hard exam—"Magdasal ka na, bes!"—and you're basically telling them to worship the gods of multiple-choice questions. It's about instigating the act of worship.
usage_notes: Used to command or cause someone to perform an act of worship.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pasambahin** mo ang mga bata sa Diyos tuwing Linggo.","translation":"**Have** the children **worship** God every Sunday."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng mga mananakop na **pasambahin** ang mga katutubo sa kanilang mga diyos.","translation":"The colonizers tried to **make** the natives **worship** their gods."}]

translation: to have a tantrum; to have a relapse; to act up
meaning_filipino: Biglaang pagbabago ng ugali, karaniwang patungo sa pagiging magagalitin o mahirap pakisamahan, o ang muling pag-atake o pagbabalik ng isang sakit.
original_explanation: This is what happens when your toddler suddenly throws a fit in the middle of the mall for no reason. It's also when a chronic illness, like asthma or arthritis, suddenly flares up. Even your Wi-Fi can 'sumumpong' when it suddenly stops working during an important video call. It’s the universe deciding to have an attitude problem at your expense.
usage_notes: Often used to describe unpredictable behavior in children, the recurrence of an illness, or the sudden malfunction of a device.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumumpong** na naman ang high blood ng tatay kaya pinagpahinga muna namin siya.","translation":"Dad's high blood pressure **acted up** again, so we had him rest."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maingay, baka **sumumpong** ang bata at mag-iyakan.","translation":"Don't be noisy, the child might **have a tantrum** and start crying."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng sapatos na mataas at karaniwang tumatakip sa paa at bukong-bukong, at minsan ay umaabot hanggang sa binti.
original_explanation: Ang pang-OOTD mo kapag malamig ang panahon or gusto mo lang mag-feeling rockstar. Also, the required footwear for construction sites or for wading through Baha-la-na-kayo-dyan levels of floodwater. From fashion statement to flood protection, the bota is versatile.
usage_notes: This is the singular form. The plural is often 'mga bota' or 'botas'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng bagong pares ng **bota** para sa aking pag-akyat sa bundok.","translation":"I bought a new pair of **boots** for my mountain climbing trip."},{"sentence":"Isinuot niya ang kanyang dilaw na **bota** para hindi mabasa sa ulan.","translation":"He wore his yellow **boots** so he wouldn't get wet in the rain."}]

meaning_filipino: May kakayahan o hilig na magdulot ng malawakang pagkasira sa mga bagay, ari-arian, o kahit sa relasyon.
original_explanation: Pwedeng literal, like a super typhoon na mapangwasak. Pwede ring figurative, like 'yung ex mong mapangwasak ng puso at pangarap. Or 'yung chismis na mapangwasak ng friendships. Anything that leaves a trail of chaos and wreckage in its wake. The human or natural equivalent of a wrecking ball.
usage_notes: Can be used for both literal physical destruction and figurative emotional or social destruction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bagyong iyon ay nag-iwan ng **mapangwasak** na epekto sa buong rehiyon.","translation":"That typhoon left a **destructive** effect on the entire region."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga salita ay naging **mapangwasak** sa aming pagkakaibigan.","translation":"His words became **destructive** to our friendship."}]

translation: to put someone in a difficult situation, to pressure
meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang paglalagay sa isang tao sa isang mahirap o alanganing sitwasyon, kadalasan para sa sariling kapakinabangan.
etymology: From `mang-` + `gipit` (in a tight spot, financially strapped).
original_explanation: This is what your landlord does when the rent is due. Or what loan sharks do. It's the act of cornering someone, leaving them with no good options. Think of it as the human version of a system error that says 'Insufficient Funds.'
usage_notes: Carries a strong negative connotation of exploitation or bullying.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong subukang **manggipit** ng mga taong naghihirap na.","translation":"Don't try to **pressure** people who are already struggling."},{"sentence":"May mga politikong mahilig **manggipit** sa kanilang mga kalaban.","translation":"There are politicians who like to **put their opponents in a tight spot**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa karne o pagkain na walang kasamang taba o mantika; puro laman.
original_explanation: This is what you order when you're on a diet but still want lechon kawali. It's the "healthy" version of your favorite ulam. The "puro laman, walang taba" is the battle cry of the health-conscious carnivore.
usage_notes: Primarily used in a culinary context to describe meat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pabili po ng isang kilong baboy, 'yung **walang-taba** sana.","translation":"I'd like to buy one kilo of pork, the **lean** kind please."},{"sentence":"Mas masarap daw ang adobo kapag hindi **walang-taba** ang karne.","translation":"They say adobo is tastier when the meat is not **fat-free**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao o bagay na mababa ang katayuan, walang gaanong halaga, o abâ.
original_explanation: This is the classic teleserye protagonist's starting point. 'Isang hamak na mangingisda lamang po.' It's a word that screams humility, sometimes genuine, sometimes false. It can also be used to belittle someone. 'Don't you dare talk to me, you're just a lowly employee!' - said the kontrabida before getting slapped.
usage_notes: Can carry a negative connotation of being worthless, or a positive one of being humble. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ako'y isang **hamak** na lingkod lamang.","translation":"I am but a **humble** servant."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong ituring na **hamak** ang iyong kapwa.","translation":"Do not treat your fellow person as **insignificant**."}]

translation: to be able to persuade/invite someone to come along
meaning_filipino: Mahikayat o mapapayag ang isang tao na sumama sa isang gawain, lakad, o lugar.
original_explanation: That magical power your one friend has. You promised yourself you'd stay home and save money, but they message "Tara, kape?" and suddenly you're out the door. Sila yung 'bad influence' na masaya kasama. "Hindi ko alam paano niya ako nayakag gumala, eh wala akong pera." It's the power of "libre kita" or "sige na, minsan lang."
usage_notes: Often used in its completed aspect "nayakag" (was able to persuade) or in questions like "Mayayakag mo ba siya?" (Will you be able to persuade him/her?). It implies successful persuasion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **mayakag** natin si Ana na sumama sa ating beach trip.","translation":"I hope we can **persuade** Ana to join our beach trip."},{"sentence":"**Nayakag** ako ng mga kaibigan ko na manood ng sine kahit pagod ako.","translation":"My friends **managed to persuade** me to watch a movie even though I was tired."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kasuotang pantulog na karaniwang binubuo ng maluwag na pang-itaas at pang-ibaba.
original_explanation: The official uniform for WFH, Netflix marathons, and Sunday morning pandesal runs. It’s socially acceptable to wear these outside, but only until 8 AM. Don't be surprised to see your neighbor watering plants in their favorite cartoon-character padyama.
usage_notes: The variant 'padyamas' is also extremely common, mirroring the English plural 'pajamas', but is often used even when referring to a single set.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsuot siya ng bagong **padyama** na terno.","translation":"She wore a new matching set of **pajamas**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang lalabas ng bahay nang naka-**padyama** lang!","translation":"Don't go out of the house wearing only your **pajamas**!"}]

translation: to tolerate, to allow, to let be
meaning_filipino: Hayaan o payagan ang isang gawain o sitwasyon na magpatuloy, kahit na ito ay maaaring hindi kanais-nais; magbigay ng konsiderasyon o kaluwagan.
etymology: From `pa-` + `buya` + `-an`. The root `buya` is possibly related to giving grace or favor, hence 'to give leeway' or 'to be gracious towards' an action.
original_explanation: This is the art of 'live and let live' or sometimes, 'picking your battles.' When your roommate leaves their mess in the sala for the third time, and you just sigh and walk away instead of starting a fight, you're choosing to **pabuyaan** them. It’s a calculated surrender for the sake of peace.
usage_notes: Often implies a degree of reluctance or putting up with something undesirable. Synonymous with 'pagbigyan' but can carry a slightly more passive or resigned tone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pabuyaan** mo na lang muna ang pagiging makulit ng bata, baka pagod lang.","translation":"Just **tolerate** the child's naughtiness for now, maybe they're just tired."},{"sentence":"Hindi dapat **pabuyaan** ang maling gawain ng mga opisyal ng gobyerno.","translation":"The wrongdoings of government officials should not be **allowed**."}]

translation: to go first; to lead the way
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkilos upang mauna sa iba sa isang lugar, gawain, o pila; ang pagiging lider o gabay sa isang pangkat.
original_explanation: In a Filipino family gathering, this is the polite thing to say before you attack the buffet table: "O, **magpapauna** na po ako!" (Okay, I'll go first!). It's a way of asking for permission to be the first one, whether it's getting food, entering a room, or starting a presentation. A slightly more formal "una na 'ko".
usage_notes: Often used as a polite way to state one is going ahead of others.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"\"Maaari po ba akong **magpauna**? Nagmamadali po kasi ako,\" sabi niya sa pila.","translation":"\"May I please **go first**? I'm in a hurry,\" he said in the line."},{"sentence":"**Nagpauna** ang mga scout upang suriin kung ligtas ang daan.","translation":"The scouts **went ahead** to check if the path was safe."}]

meaning_filipino: Mabalot ng dilim; ang pagdating ng gabi o ang pagkawala ng liwanag sa isang lugar.
etymology: From the root word 'dilim' with the suffix '-in'.
original_explanation: This is the verb form. It's what happens to your room when you finally give up on that last-minute report and just let the night take over. "Hayaan mo nang dilimin ang kwarto, tulog na tayo."
usage_notes: Often used in a passive or literary sense. 'Dinidilim' means 'getting dark'. 'Diniliman ng paningin' is an idiom for fainting or becoming enraged.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala kung **dilimin** man tayo sa daan, may flashlight ako.","translation":"Don't worry if we **are caught by darkness** on the road, I have a flashlight."},{"sentence":"Bigla siyang diniliman ng paningin at natumba.","translation":"His vision suddenly went **dark** and he collapsed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sangay ng biyolohiya na nag-aaral sa mga hayop, kasama na ang kanilang estruktura, pisyolohiya, pag-unlad, at klasipikasyon.
original_explanation: The science of animals. Basically, the "-ology" of the "zoo." Ito 'yung subject na kukunin mo kung gusto mong maging a la Steve Irwin o kung gusto mong malaman kung bakit mas tapat pa ang aso mo kaysa sa ex mo.
usage_notes: Ito ang pormal at akademikong termino. Sa pang-araw-araw na Filipino, maaaring sabihin lang na "pag-aaral tungkol sa mga hayop".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha siya ng kursong **soolohiya** sa unibersidad.","translation":"He took a course in **zoology** at the university."},{"sentence":"Ang **soolohiya** ay isang malawak na larangan ng agham.","translation":"**Zoology** is a broad field of science."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na may dalawang magkasalungat na epekto, isang positibo at isang negatibo; literal na tumutukoy sa isang sandata na may talim sa magkabilang gilid.
original_explanation: Parang social media. Pwedeng maging source ng saya at koneksyon, pero pwede ring maging source ng inggit at anxiety. O kaya parang pag-utang sa kaibigan—nakatulong sa'yo ngayon, pero baka masira ang friendship niyo bukas. May good side, may bad side. Choose your fighter.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa idyomatikong paraan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang katanyagan ay isang espadang **doble-talim**.","translation":"Fame is a **double-edged** sword."},{"sentence":"Isang kutsilyong **doble-talim** ang kanyang dala.","translation":"He was carrying a **double-edged** knife."}]

translation: very few; a little bit more than a little
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang maliit na bilang o dami na higit sa 'kaunting-kaunti' ngunit kulang pa rin para maituring na marami.
etymology: Nagmula sa pag-uulit ng unang pantig ng salitang 'kaunti' upang magpahiwatig ng katamtamang kagaanan o kababaan ng dami.
original_explanation: This is the 'sakto lang' or 'pwede na' level of 'kaunti'. Not 'kaunting-kaunti' (like your 13th-month pay after taxes), but just a bit more. Like when you ask for 'extra rice' and they give you exactly one extra spoonful. 'Ma, pautang.' 'O, eto kau-kaunti.'
usage_notes: Often used to express a modest or slightly insufficient amount. It implies a quantity that is more than the absolute minimum but still small.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kau-kaunti** lang ang natira sa sahod ko matapos magbayad ng bills.","translation":"Only a **very small amount** was left of my salary after paying the bills."},{"sentence":"Bigyan mo ako ng kanin, kahit **kau-kaunti** lang.","translation":"Give me some rice, even just a **little bit**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagpapakulo ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay pagkain tulad ng itlog, kamote, o saging, sa tubig hanggang sa ito ay maluto.
original_explanation: This is a kitchen staple verb. When you're too lazy to cook a full meal, you maglaga ng itlog (boil an egg) or saging na saba. It's the official cooking method for 'bahala na si Batman' dinners. Just add water, fire, and wait.
usage_notes: Distinct from 'magpakulo' which just means to boil water. 'Maglaga' implies something is being cooked *in* the boiling water.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gutom na ako, **maglaga** ka muna ng kamote.","translation":"I'm hungry, please **boil** some sweet potatoes for now."},{"sentence":"Madaling **maglaga** ng itlog para sa almusal.","translation":"It's easy to **boil** eggs for breakfast."}]

translation: to make something grow, to cultivate
meaning_filipino: Alagaan at paramihin ang isang halaman, hayop, o anumang bagay na may buhay upang ito ay lumaki at umunlad.
original_explanation: Your tita who became a 'plantita' during the pandemic? She loves to `magpatubo` of new monsteras. It's the act of playing God with a seed or a cutting and hoping it doesn't die on you. From munggo for a science project to a full-blown vegetable garden.
usage_notes: Refers to the act of cultivating plants, or sometimes raising small animals. Distict from 'magpatubo' which means to charge interest.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais kong **magpatubo** ng mga gulay sa aming bakuran.","translation":"I want to **grow** vegetables in our yard."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **magpatubo** ng halaman kung kulang sa sikat ng araw.","translation":"It's hard to **make a plant grow** if there's not enough sunlight."}]

translation: to do something at the same time; to go together
meaning_filipino: Gawin ang isang bagay nang magkasama o sa iisang panahon.
original_explanation: The ultimate group project, commute, or lunch out move. "Sabay na tayo!" is the Filipino's way of saying "Don't leave me behind!" Whether it's two people walking in the same direction or your deadlines and your problems arriving at the same time, that's magsabay.
usage_notes: Can be used for people, events, or actions happening concurrently.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto mo bang **magsabay** na tayo sa pag-uwi mamaya?","translation":"Do you want us **to go** home **together** later?"},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pagsabayin** ang pag-aaral at panonood ng TV.","translation":"Don't **do** studying and watching TV **at the same time**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagdaan o paglusot mula sa isang panig patungo sa kabila, na kadalasan ay may pagkasira o pagkabutas.
original_explanation: 'Yung bala na tumama sa pader at lumabas sa kabilang side. Or 'yung "hugot" na sobrang tindi, tagos hanggang buto! It means "all the way through." Pwedeng literal na butas, pwedeng sa feelings.
usage_notes: Often used with a verb like "tumagos". Can be used both literally and figuratively. When used as an adverb, it modifies the verb to mean 'through'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pako ay **lagos** sa kahoy.","translation":"The nail is **pierced through** the wood."},{"sentence":"Ang sinabi niya ay tumagos nang **lagos** sa puso.","translation":"What he said pierced **all the way through** the heart."}]

translation: to poke; to nudge with a fingertip
meaning_filipino: Ang pagdaiti o pag-abot sa isang tao o bagay gamit ang dulo ng daliri upang makuha ang atensyon o magbigay ng senyas.
original_explanation: It's that subtle poke you give your friend when your crush walks by. Not a full-on tap, just a light *psst* with your finger. Also what you do to someone sleeping in the jeepney when it's their stop. It's the physical version of "uy!"
usage_notes: Often used to get someone's attention without speaking. The verb form is often inflected, e.g., 'kinakalbit' (poking) or 'kalbitin' (to poke someone).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **kalbitin** habang nagmamaneho ako.","translation":"Don't **poke** me while I'm driving."},{"sentence":"**Kinakalbit** niya ako sa likod para manghingi ng papel.","translation":"He was **poking** me in the back to ask for paper."}]

translation: A place or session for gossiping.
meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o pagtitipon kung saan nag-uusap-usap ang mga tao tungkol sa buhay ng iba, kadalasan ay walang katotohanan.
original_explanation: The national sport of the Philippines. It's the OG social media feed, happening in real-time over the bakod, sa tindahan, or even sa office pantry. Before DMs, there was the 'PM is the key' of the tsismisan circle.
usage_notes: The suffix '-an' can denote either the act of doing something together (like a session) or the place where it happens.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang sasali sa **tsismisan** sa kanto, baka ikaw ang sunod na pag-usapan.","translation":"Don't join the **gossiping session** at the corner, you might be the next topic."},{"sentence":"Naging sentro ng **tsismisan** ang bagong kapitbahay.","translation":"The new neighbor became the center of the **gossip session**."}]

meaning_filipino: Dalhin ang isang tao o hayop sa doktor o manggagamot upang malunasan ang karamdaman.
original_explanation: This is the responsible adult verb. When your dog is sick, you ipagamot mo siya sa vet. When your friend is having a "sakit-sakitan" moment for the nth time, you tell them, "Ipagamot mo na 'yan!" It's the act of taking someone to get medical help, a core part of Filipino family care.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to seeking medical treatment for someone or something (like a pet).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **ipagamot** si Lola sa lalong madaling panahon.","translation":"We need to **have** Grandma **treated** as soon as possible."},{"sentence":"Saan magandang **ipagamot** ang alaga kong pusa na ayaw kumain?","translation":"Where is a good place to **have** my pet cat, who doesn't want to eat, **treated**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkuha ng dimensyon, kantidad, o kapasidad ng isang bagay gamit ang isang panukat tulad ng metro, ruler, o timbangan.
original_explanation: This is what the karpintero does before cutting wood, or what the sastre (tailor) does to get your body measurements. 'Manong, magsukat po muna kayo bago niyo putulin 'yan, baka sumobra!' It's the 'measure twice, cut once' verb.
usage_notes: Refers to the act of determining size, length, weight, volume, etc.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **magsukat** ng tela ang mananahi para sa gagawing bestida.","translation":"The dressmaker needs to **measure** the fabric for the dress she will make."},{"sentence":"Nag-utos ang inhenyero na **magsukat** muli ng lote.","translation":"The engineer ordered to **measure** the lot again."}]

meaning_filipino: Nauukol sa espiritu o kaluluwa at hindi sa mga pisikal na bagay; may kinalaman sa mga banal o relihiyosong usapin.
original_explanation: Describes your tita who collects crystals and talks about chakras, but also your lola who goes to church every single day. It's anything that feeds the soul, whether that's through prayer, meditation, or just staring at the sunset and having a 'main character moment'.
usage_notes: Ang baybay na 'espiritwal' ay karaniwan ding ginagamit at tinatanggap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paglalakbay niya sa India ay isang karanasang **espirituwal**.","translation":"Her journey to India was a **spiritual** experience."},{"sentence":"Naghahanap siya ng **espirituwal** na kapayapaan.","translation":"He is searching for **spiritual** peace."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng dalawa o higit pang tao na nagpapalitan ng mga biro o kantsawan sa isang magaan at palakaibigang paraan.
etymology: From the root 'biro' (joke). The circumfix 'pag-…-an' and reduplication 'bi-' indicates a reciprocal or social action of joking together.
original_explanation: This is the official sport of Filipino barkadas. It's how you show affection without being cheesy. If your friends aren't making fun of you, do they even love you? It's the 'asaran' that ends in laughter, not in a blocked contact.
usage_notes: Implies a reciprocal or mutual action between people. 'Pagbibiro' is the act of one person joking.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nauwi sa totohanang away ang kanilang **pagbibiruan**.","translation":"Their **mutual joking** ended in a real fight."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan ng pagkakaroon ng bahagyang pagkakahawig o pagkakatulad sa isang bagay o tao, ngunit hindi lubos na kapareho.
original_explanation: When you see someone who looks like a celebrity's 'Shopee version.' They're not a doppelgänger, but there's a definite resemblance. 'Uy, wangis-wangis ni Daniel Padilla yung barista!' It's for when 'kamukha' is too strong a word, but 'wala lang' is a lie.
usage_notes: A more poetic or literary way to say 'medyo kamukha' or 'may hawig'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga ulap ay **wangis-wangis** ng mga tupa na nagpapahinga sa langit.","translation":"The clouds are **somewhat similar** to sheep resting in the sky."},{"sentence":"May **wangis-wangis** ang kanyang ngiti sa yumaong lola.","translation":"Her smile has a **slight resemblance** to her late grandmother's."}]

translation: To make ten; to divide into ten parts
meaning_filipino: Gawing sampu ang bilang o dami ng isang bagay; hatiin sa sampung bahagi.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'ten.' When your manager says, 'You have 8 reports, sampuin mo na 'yan,' they mean 'make it ten.' It's the action of rounding up or completing a set to ten. Not a super common word, but it shows the flexibility of Tagalog verbs.
usage_notes: Isang pandiwa na nabuo sa pamamagitan ng pagdaragdag ng hulaping '-in' sa bilang na 'sampu'. Hindi ito karaniwang ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kulang pa tayo ng dalawa, **sampuin** na natin ang mga silya para sa bisita.","translation":"We're still short by two, let's **make it ten** chairs for the guests."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkawala ng kahinahunan at pagiging taranta o natataranta dahil sa pagkabigla, takot, o pagmamadali.
original_explanation: Your state of mind when the client calls and you haven't started their request yet. Or when your mom says 'May bisita!' and the house is a mess. It’s that headless chicken dance you do when the deadline is in 5 minutes.
usage_notes: Describes a state of frantic confusion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumaranta** ang lahat nang biglang tumunog ang fire alarm.","translation":"Everyone **panicked** when the fire alarm suddenly went off."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **tumaranta**; huminga ka nang malalim at mag-isip.","translation":"Don't **be flustered**; take a deep breath and think."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapaputok ng baril na ang puntirya ay isang tao, hayop, o bagay.
original_explanation: The verb form you see in action movies or hear in angry teleserye confrontations. 'Babrilin kita!' is the ultimate threat. In a lighter sense, it's what you do to the target in a carnival shooting game to win that giant stuffed toy you don't need.
usage_notes: An object-focus verb. The actor is marked by 'ng' or a pronoun like 'ko', 'mo', 'niya'. The object being shot is marked by 'ang' or a pronoun like 'siya', 'ito'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Barilin** mo ang mga bote para manalo tayo.","translation":"**Shoot** the bottles so we can win."},{"sentence":"Binalaan ng pulis ang magnanakaw na **babrilin** niya ito kapag hindi sumuko.","translation":"The police warned the thief that he would **shoot** him if he didn't surrender."}]

translation: to force someone into marriage; to entrap
meaning_filipino: Ang sapilitang pagpapakasal sa isang tao, kadalasan sa pamamagitan ng panlilinlang, pagbabanta, o paglikha ng isang sitwasyon kung saan wala na siyang ibang pagpipilian.
original_explanation: The classic teleserye plot device! Girl gets pregnant (or pretends to be) to force the rich heir to marry her. That's **pikutin**. It's trapping someone in a relationship, shotgun wedding style. It’s a checkmate move in the game of love, but like, the cheating kind.
usage_notes: Has a very strong, negative connotation related to forced marriage or relationship entrapment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayaman ang lalaki kaya plinano niyang **pikutin** ito.","translation":"The man was rich so she planned to **entrap him into marriage**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang papayag na **pikutin** ka ninuman.","translation":"Don't allow anyone to **force you into marriage**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mitolohikal na nilalang na may katawan ng babae mula ulo hanggang baywang at buntot ng isda mula baywang pababa.
original_explanation: The OG Dyesebel! The half-human, half-fish creature that fuels countless Filipino fantasy series. Every Pinoy kid grew up with stories of a beautiful 'sirena' luring fishermen with her enchanting voice. She's the ultimate beach fantasy, minus the difficulty of walking on land.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa mitolohikal na nilalang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paboritong palabas ng mga bata ang kuwento tungkol sa **sirena** at sa prinsipe.","translation":"The children's favorite show is the story about the **mermaid** and the prince."},{"sentence":"Ayon sa alamat, may mga **sirena** na naninirahan sa malalim na bahagi ng dagat.","translation":"According to legend, there are **mermaids** living in the deep parts of the sea."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga katangian, distribusyon, at ugnayan ng mga bagay at tao sa ibabaw ng mundo; nauugnay sa heograpiya.
original_explanation: Anything related to maps, locations, and why your Grab driver is taking the 'scenic route' through three different cities. It's about where things are, from the nearest milk tea shop to the tectonic plates causing all the drama.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan nila ang mga katangiang **heograpiko** ng kapuluan ng Pilipinas.","translation":"They are studying the **geographical** features of the Philippine archipelago."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtulo ng luha mula sa mga mata, karaniwang dahil sa matinding damdamin tulad ng lungkot, sakit, o saya.
original_explanation: The original 'unli-data' plan of your eyes when you watch a sad Filipino movie, get your heart broken, or see your electricity bill. It's the body's natural reaction to a plot twist in a teleserye or when your crush leaves you on 'seen'.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pandiwa sa anyong 'umiyak' (to cry) o 'iyakan' (to cry over something).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **iyak** ng sanggol sa kabilang kwarto.","translation":"I heard the **cry** of the baby in the other room."},{"sentence":"Napuno ng **iyak** at tawanan ang kanilang muling pagkikita.","translation":"Their reunion was filled with **crying** and laughter."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pulbos na gawa sa mineral na talc, karaniwang ginagamit sa balat upang mabawasan ang pamamasa at iritasyon.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na 'talcum', na mula sa Latin 'talcum'.
original_explanation: This is that white powder your lola puts on your back after a bath so you don't get 'bungang-araw' (prickly heat). It's the OG Johnson's Baby Powder before all the fancy skincare stuff came along. Smells like childhood and not being 'maalinsangan'.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang direktang hiram na salita mula sa Ingles. Ang mas karaniwang Filipino na termino ay 'pulbos'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagyan mo ng **talcum** ang likod ng bata para hindi mainitan.","translation":"Put **talcum** powder on the child's back so they don't feel hot."}]

meaning_filipino: Nauuna sa lahat sa pagkakasunod-sunod, oras, o kahalagahan.
original_explanation: `Primero`, you listen to the instructions, `segundo`, you ignore them and do it your own way. It's the 'first things first' of the Titos of Manila. When someone says this, they're about to give you a lecture or a multi-step plan, probably involving some kind of hand gesture.
usage_notes: Often used when enumerating steps or establishing priority. The native Tagalog equivalent is 'una'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Primero**, mag-aral ka muna bago ka maglaro.","translation":"**First**, you study before you play."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang isang tao o bagay na magdudulot ng pagkabigo o hindi pagtupad sa inaasahan sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: The classic line in a teleserye before a painful breakup: 'Ayokong mambigo, pero hindi na kita mahal.' It's the future tense of breaking someone's heart or not living up to expectations. The promise your internet provider makes and then breaks during your Zoom presentation.
usage_notes: This is the future tense form of the verb 'mamigo', meaning 'to cause failure or disappointment'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nangako siyang hindi **mambibigo**, ngunit hindi pa rin siya dumating.","translation":"He promised he **would not disappoint**, but he still didn't arrive."},{"sentence":"Sana'y hindi **mambibigo** ang bagong pamahalaan sa mga pangako nito.","translation":"Hopefully, the new government **will not fail** on its promises."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghamak, pagtuya, o pag-insulto sa isang tao o bagay sa pamamagitan ng salita o gawa.
original_explanation: This is what happens when your 'friends' see your old Friendster profile. It's the act of roasting someone, but not in a fun, friendly way. It's the 'ay, anyare?' comment on your failed cooking attempt posted on IG. It's low-key bullying, but with words.
usage_notes: Often carries a strong negative connotation of belittling someone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paglibak** sa kapwa ay hindi magandang ugali.","translation":"**Mockery** of others is not a good trait."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya pinansin ang **paglibak** ng mga kasamahan niya sa trabaho.","translation":"He ignored the **derision** from his colleagues at work."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng luntiang gulay na may malalapad na dahon at mapuputing tangkay, karaniwang ginagamit sa mga lutuing Filipino tulad ng nilaga at pansit.
etymology: Mula sa Hokkien na "pe̍h-chhài" (白菜), na nangangahulugang "puting gulay."
original_explanation: The default vegetable of the Philippines. If a dish needs some green in it, chances are, it's petsay. It's the hardworking, underpaid employee of the vegetable world—always there, reliable, and doesn't ask for much. Perfect for bulalo, nilaga, or stir-fry when you're on a budget before payday.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagdagdag si nanay ng maraming **petsay** sa nilagang baka.","translation":"Mom added a lot of **pechay** to the beef stew."},{"sentence":"Mas mura ang **petsay** sa palengke ngayon.","translation":"**Pechay** is cheaper at the market today."}]

translation: to be stunned, to freeze, to be brought to a standstill
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pansamantalang paghinto o pagkatulala dahil sa gulat, takot, o pagkamangha.
original_explanation: ‘Yung moment na nakita mo ‘yung crush mo tapos may kasama siyang iba, at bigla kang naging human statue. Or ‘yung feeling na nag-present ka sa work tapos biglang nag-freeze ‘yung PowerPoint mo at pati ikaw, nag-freeze din. That's 'natitigilan'. Your whole system just stops.
usage_notes: Ito ang pangkasalukuyang anyo ng pandiwa na may banghay sa -an, na nagpapahiwatig na may panlabas na sanhi ang paghinto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Natitigilan** siya sa tuwing nakikita niya ang magandang tanawin mula sa bintana.","translation":"He **is brought to a standstill** every time he sees the beautiful view from the window."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **matitigilan** sa mga pagsubok; magpatuloy ka lang.","translation":"Don't **be stopped** by challenges; just keep going."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinuno ng isang bayan o munisipalidad; sa makalumang gamit, maaari ring tumukoy sa tagapamahala ng isang bilangguan.
