original_explanation: The OG 'Yorme'. Bago pa nauso ang 'mayor', 'alkaide' na ang tawag sa kanila. Sounds more formal and a bit historical, like someone from a Jose Rizal novel. Today, you'd probably only hear this from your lola or in a history class.
usage_notes: Primarily an archaic term for 'mayor.' In some contexts, it can also mean 'warden.' The modern and common term is 'mayor' or 'punong-bayan.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **alkaide** ng San Diego ay isang iginagalang na tao noong panahon ng mga Kastila.","translation":"The **mayor** of San Diego was a respected person during the Spanish era."},{"sentence":"Itinalaga siya bilang **alkaide** ng piitan.","translation":"He was appointed as the **warden** of the prison."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng isang tao o bagay sa posisyon o lugar ng iba; ang pagpapalit.
original_explanation: That moment when your favorite character in a series gets killed off and they try to ihalip a new one, but it's just not the same. It's to substitute or replace. 'Sino ang ihahalip natin kay John sa basketball team habang injured siya?' It's finding a stand-in, a proxy, or a replacement.
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of positions, roles, or ingredients. 'Sa halip na...' (instead of...) is a very common related phrase.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Maria ang **inihalip** bilang pansamantalang pinuno.","translation":"Maria was **substituted** as the temporary leader."},{"sentence":"Maaari mong **ihalip** ang honey sa asukal para mas masustansya.","translation":"You can **substitute** honey for sugar to make it healthier."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng bakod o kulungan na yari sa kawayan o lambat na inilalagay sa tubig upang makahuli ng isda.
etymology: Unknown, possibly from a local dialect. Sometimes spelled 'buhiya'.
original_explanation: This is some deep-cut, lolo's-baul-level Tagalog. Think of it as the OG, analog version of a fish finder. It's a giant trap set in the water, like a maze for fish where the only exit is into a fisherman's net. You'd probably only hear this from someone who actually builds them. For everyone else, it's just 'baklad'.
usage_notes: A very rare or archaic term. 'Baklad' is the much more common word for a fish corral.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtayo ng bagong **buhia** ang mga mangingisda sa lawa.","translation":"The fishermen built a new **fish corral** in the lake."},{"sentence":"Maraming nahuli sa kanilang **buhia** kaninang umaga.","translation":"Many were caught in their **fish trap** this morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyon ng pagtataboy o pag-ayaw sa isang tao, bagay, o masamang espiritu.
original_explanation: This is the OG 'shoo!' or 'get lost!' Often said with a hand gesture to ward off bad vibes, evil spirits, or even just an annoying person. 'Puwera usog!' is what your lola says to protect a baby from mysterious ailments caused by strangers' greetings. It's a verbal anting-anting.
usage_notes: Often used in superstitious contexts like 'puwera usog' or 'puwera gaba' to ward off curses or bad luck. It functions as a command or exclamation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Puwera**! Layuan mo ako!","translation":"**Get away**! Stay away from me!"},{"sentence":"Ang cute ng bata! **Puwera** usog.","translation":"The baby is so cute! (A phrase to **ward off** unintentional hex)."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggalaw sa pamamagitan ng pag-usad ng katawan nang malapit sa lupa, karaniwang ginagamit ang mga kamay at tuhod.
original_explanation: This is how babies explore the world before they can walk. It's also you after a really, *really* long night out with friends, trying to get to your bed without waking up your parents. Or a soldier in training, moving silently under barbed wire. It's slow, low-to-the-ground movement.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for movement or figuratively for struggling to advance in life or a career ('maggapang sa hirap').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula nang **maggapang** ang sanggol sa sahig.","translation":"The baby started to **crawl** on the floor."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng pagkakaiba-iba sa katangian, anyo, o opinyon ng dalawa o higit pang tao, bagay, o ideya.
original_explanation: This is the formal way of saying 'magkaiba sila.' It's for when you're comparing your ex to your current flame, or when you realize your political views and your tita's are worlds apart. It emphasizes that *they* (plural) are the ones who are different from each other. It has a slightly old-fashioned, literary vibe.
usage_notes: The prefix 'mangagka-' is a plural form, indicating that the subjects of the verb are mutually different. It's less common in casual speech than 'magkaiba'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bagama't sila'y kambal, sila ay **mangagkaiba** sa ugali.","translation":"Although they are twins, they **differ from each other** in personality."},{"sentence":"Ang mga opinyon ng mga delegado ay **mangagkaiba** kaya't nagkaroon ng mahabang debate.","translation":"The opinions of the delegates **differed from each other**, which is why a long debate occurred."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mga ninuno o pinagmulan ng isang lahi o pamilya; ang mga nauna sa maraming salinlahi.
etymology: From the root word *nuno* (ancestor, grandparent) with the *ka- -an* affix, indicating a collective group or the very essence of ancestry.
original_explanation: This is your ultimate #ThrowbackThursday squad. Not just your lolo and lola, but their lolo and lola, and so on, all the way back to the folks who probably fought Lapu-Lapu. When you talk about *kanunu-nunuan*, you're going deep into your family tree, connecting to your roots and the ancient traditions they passed down.
usage_notes: A very formal and deep word for "ancestors." "Ninuno" is the more common term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagmamano ay isang kaugaliang minana pa natin sa ating mga **kanunu-nunuan**.","translation":"The 'pagmamano' is a custom we inherited from our **ancestors**."},{"sentence":"Ipinagdiriwang nila ang Araw ng mga Patay upang alalahanin ang kanilang **kanunu-nunuan**.","translation":"They celebrate the Day of the Dead to remember their **forebears**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginawa sa tatlong kopya o pinarami nang tatlong beses.
original_explanation: Ito yung level ng paperwork sa government office. Hindi sapat ang duplicate, dapat triplikado lahat ng forms mo, with matching photocopies of your soul.
usage_notes: Often used in legal, bureaucratic, or formal contexts referring to documents.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakipirmahan po ang lahat ng **triplikado** na kopya ng kontrata.","translation":"Please sign all **triplicate** copies of the contract."},{"sentence":"Naging **triplikado** ang bilang ng mga dumalo sa event kumpara noong nakaraang taon.","translation":"The number of event attendees **tripled** compared to last year."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagbibigay ng pagsusuri, pagtatasa, o kritikal na opinyon sa mga gawang sining, panitikan, pelikula, o anumang paksa.
etymology: Nagmula sa "man-" + pag-uulit ng unang pantig ng ugat ("su-") + "suri" (siyasatin/analisahin).
original_explanation: That friend who gives a 10-minute commentary after watching a movie, or the person online who writes a 5-paragraph review of the latest milk tea craze. They're the ones who look beyond the surface, whether it's for a thesis paper (akademikong manunuri) or just to tell you why your ex's new partner is a walking red flag (chismis-level manunuri).
usage_notes: Maaaring maging pormal (hal. kritiko sa panitikan) o impormal (hal. food reviewer).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinuri ng mga **manunuri** ang bagong pelikula ni Direk.","translation":"The **critics** praised the Director's new film."}]

translation: to endure; to bear; to suffer
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtanggap at pagtitiis sa isang mahirap na sitwasyon, pasanin, o damdamin nang walang reklamo.
etymology: From an old Tagalog root 'bati' meaning 'to suffer' or 'to endure'. This root is distinct from the more common 'bati' meaning 'greeting' or 'to mix'.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'tiis-ganda' or 'tiis-pogi' on an emotional level. It's when you take all the pain, the 'sakit', the 'pait', and just... absorb it. Like when your crush sees you only as a friend, and you just smile and say 'Okay lang.' That's you, silently *bathin* the friendzone.
usage_notes: This is a deep Tagalog word, often found in literature, poetry, and formal speech. It implies a sense of silent, stoic suffering. A more common synonym is 'tiisin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **bathin** ang pagkawala ng isang minamahal.","translation":"It is difficult **to endure** the loss of a loved one."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **bathin** ang lahat ng pagsubok para sa iyong pamilya.","translation":"You need **to bear** all the challenges for your family."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging magaan na galit o iritasyon dahil sa isang bagay na nakagagambala o hindi kaaya-aya.
original_explanation: The feeling you get when the internet connection drops mid-Zoom meeting, or when someone chews their food loudly beside you. It's not full-blown rage, just that "Lord, give me patience" level of irritation. The "gigil" that isn't cute.
usage_notes: Describes the state or feeling of being annoyed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kitang-kita sa mukha niya ang **pagkainis** dahil sa ingay.","translation":"His **annoyance** at the noise was very visible on his face."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko na maitago ang aking **pagkainis** sa mabagal na serbisyo.","translation":"I can no longer hide my **irritation** at the slow service."}]

meaning_filipino: Nauukol sa mga karaniwang mamamayan o sa kanilang mga karapatan at ugnayan, na hiwalay sa usaping militar o panrelihiyon.
original_explanation: Anything that's not military or religious. 'Kasal na sibil' (civil wedding) is when you get married in city hall, officiated by a judge, instead of in a church by a priest. 'Karapatang sibil' (civil rights) are the rights you have as a citizen. It’s the 'civilian' side of life.
usage_notes: Primarily used in legal, political, and social contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinili nilang magpakasal sa isang seremonyang **sibil**.","translation":"They chose to get married in a **civil** ceremony."},{"sentence":"Ang inhinyeriyang **sibil** ay mahalaga sa pagpapaunlad ng imprastraktura.","translation":"**Civil** engineering is important for developing infrastructure."}]

meaning_filipino: Itaya ang pera o anumang mahalagang bagay sa isang kaganapan na hindi tiyak ang kahihinatnan, tulad ng sugal o kompetisyon.
original_explanation: This is what your tito does during a Pacquiao fight or a sabong match. "Sampu, kay Pula!" But it's also used for friendly wagers, like, "Ipupusta ko ang lunch ko, mahuhuli si Mark sa meeting." It's putting your money (or your meal) where your mouth is.
usage_notes: The `i-` prefix focuses on the thing being bet (the wager).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ipusta** ang lahat ng pera mo sa iisang laro lang.","translation":"Don't **bet** all your money on just one game."},{"sentence":"Ang huling sahod niya ang **ipinusta** niya sa karera ng kabayo.","translation":"He **wagered** his last salary on the horse race."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang anyo ng wika na pinaghahalo ang mga salita at balarila mula sa Tagalog at Ingles.
etymology: A blend of Tagalog and English.
original_explanation: The default language of every Filipino trying to sound cool, explain something complicated, or just can't be bothered to think of the Tagalog word for 'aesthetic'. It's like, you know, when you're making chika with your friends, and you're like, 'OMG, grabe talaga!' That's it. You're speaking it now.
usage_notes: A very common sociolect in the Philippines, especially in urban areas and online.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap i-translate ang ibang salita sa **Taglish**.","translation":"It's hard to translate some words in **Taglish**."},{"sentence":"Araw-araw siyang nagsasalita ng **Taglish** sa opisina.","translation":"She speaks **Taglish** every day at the office."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi matatag ang pagkakapuwesto o pagkakakabit; madaling gumalaw o yumanig.
original_explanation: Describes your lola's favorite rocking chair, the cheap monobloc chair at a handaan that feels like a trust exercise, or your career plans during a quarter-life crisis. If it feels like it's about to give way, it's **mauga**.
usage_notes: Used to describe physical instability in objects.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingat ka sa pag-upo diyan, **mauga** ang silya.","translation":"Be careful sitting there, the chair is **wobbly**."},{"sentence":"Naging **mauga** ang tulay pagkatapos ng lindol.","translation":"The bridge became **unstable** after the earthquake."}]

translation: to attack, to invade, to charge
meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang pagsugod o pag-atake sa isang lugar o grupo ng mga tao, karaniwan nang may layuning manakop o manakit.
original_explanation: The ultimate "sugod mga kapatid!" moment. It's what you and your friends do to a buffet table. It's also what happens during a 12.12 sale when everyone tries to check out at the same time. "Ready na? Sa bilang ng tatlo, **lumusob** na tayo sa 'Add to Cart'!"
usage_notes: Strongly associated with military or aggressive action. Can be used humorously for non-violent "attacks" like on food or a sale.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga sundalo ay handa nang **lumusob** sa kuta ng mga kalaban.","translation":"The soldiers are ready to **attack** the enemy's fortress."},{"sentence":"Nang buksan ang pinto, **lumusob** ang mga mamimili sa loob ng mall para sa midnight sale.","translation":"When the doors opened, shoppers **charged** inside the mall for the midnight sale."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking nawalan ng karangalan, reputasyon, o pabor; sinawing-palad.
original_explanation: The male version of "disgrasyada," but it's used more broadly. It can mean a guy who lost his job, his reputation, or just had a major fall from grace. Think of a politician caught in a scandal or a CEO fired for corruption. They're not just unlucky; they're disgrasyado – their good name is toast.
usage_notes: Bagaman may panlalaking anyo, mas malawak ang sakop nito kumpara sa 'disgrasyada' at maaaring tumukoy sa anumang uri ng pagkawala ng pabor o reputasyon, hindi lamang sa kontekstong sekswal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Simula nang matanggal sa trabaho, pakiramdam niya ay **disgrasyado** siya sa paningin ng lahat.","translation":"Since he was fired from his job, he feels **disgraced** in everyone's eyes."},{"sentence":"Ang **disgrasyado** na pulitiko ay hindi na muling nahalal.","translation":"The **disgraced** politician was never elected again."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang butas, siwang, o daanan kung saan lumalabas ang singaw, hangin, o anumang gas.
etymology: From 'singaw' (steam, vapor) + '-an' (suffix indicating a place or device for something).
original_explanation: It's the little hole where steam escapes. Think of the whistle on a pressure cooker, the vent on a rice cooker, or even a small opening in a geyser. It's the designated exit point for hot air and pressure. In a 'hugot' sense, your friend who always listens to your rants is your personal 'singawan'.
usage_notes: Commonly used in cooking, mechanical, and industrial contexts. It is the place *where* steam ('singaw') comes out.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa **singawan** ng pressure cooker dahil mainit ang singaw na lumalabas diyan.","translation":"Be careful with the **vent** of the pressure cooker because the steam coming out of it is hot."},{"sentence":"May bara ang **singawan** kaya hindi gumagana nang maayos ang makina.","translation":"The **nozzle** is clogged, that's why the machine isn't working properly."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging masalita o mahilig makipag-usap nang walang tigil at madalas tungkol sa mga bagay na walang kabuluhan.
etymology: From ka- + daldal + -an, referring to the quality or state of being talkative.
original_explanation: Ito yung skill na meron ang best friend mo kapag may chismis. Endless, unli-data, non-stop talking. Minsan, ito rin yung dahilan kung bakit napapagalitan ka sa klase o sa meeting.
usage_notes: Often has a slightly negative connotation, implying excessive or aimless talking.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakilala siya sa buong opisina dahil sa kanyang **kadaldalan**.","translation":"She became known throughout the office for her **talkativeness**."},{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na ang **kadaldalan** mo at magtrabaho ka na.","translation":"Stop your **chattiness** and get to work."}]

translation: to refute; to deny; to prove false
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapatunay na hindi totoo o walang katotohanan ang isang pahayag, paratang, o paniniwala.
etymology: From pa- + sinungaling (liar). The verb form means to make something (or someone) out to be a lie (or a liar).
original_explanation: This is the "Objection, your Honor!" move in a conversation. It's when you actively debunk a chismis or a false accusation. Someone says, "Uy, may bago ka daw jowa?" and you reply with a detailed presentation of your single, lonely life to prove them wrong. That's `pasinungalingan`. It's not just denying; it's presenting your counter-evidence.
usage_notes: This is a verb, often seen in its infinitive or conjugated forms. The root word `sinungaling` means liar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **pasinungalingan** ang mga akusasyon laban sa kanya.","translation":"He tried to **refute** the accusations against him."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **pasinungalingan** ang isang bagay na may matibay na ebidensya.","translation":"It's hard to **prove false** something that has strong evidence."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang estado ng pagiging walang kabuluhan, importansya, o silbi.
original_explanation: The feeling you get when your crush leaves you on "seen." Ouch. It's the state of being irrelevant or useless. Parang 'yung lumang charger na hindi na gumagana pero tinatago mo pa rin. It's the ultimate "sana all... may halaga" hugot.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa materyal na bagay, konsepto, o sa damdamin ng isang tao tungkol sa sarili (feeling of worthlessness).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang matinding **kawalang-halaga** nang iwanan siya ng lahat.","translation":"She felt an intense **worthlessness** when everyone left her."},{"sentence":"Para sa kanya, ang pera ay may **kawalang-halaga** kumpara sa pamilya.","translation":"For him, money has **insignificance** compared to family."}]

translation: to set on fire; to burn
meaning_filipino: Sindihan o sunugin hanggang sa magliyab at maging abo.
original_explanation: The more dramatic, almost poetic way of saying "sunugin." This isn't just for burning trash (basura). You use this when you're burning old love letters in a fit of post-breakup rage, or when a villain in a teleserye wants to burn down the hacienda. It has main character energy.
usage_notes: A more literary or intense synonym for 'sunugin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagbanta siyang **apuyin** ang buong bahay.","translation":"He threatened to **set** the whole house **on fire**."},{"sentence":"In**apoy** nila ang mga tuyong dahon sa bakuran.","translation":"They **burned** the dry leaves in the yard."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto o proseso ng paghihiwalay o pagbabahagi ng isang buo sa dalawa o higit pang bahagi.
original_explanation: This is the 'OG' sharing is caring. It's when you cut the cake, split the bill, or divide the last piece of chicharon. It can be a simple 50/50 split or a more complicated division of assets 'pag naghiwalay kayo ng jowa mo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang pantay na **paghati** ng mana upang maiwasan ang alitan.","translation":"Fair **partition** of the inheritance is important to avoid conflict."},{"sentence":"Ang **paghati** ng cake ay ginawa ng debutante.","translation":"The **act of dividing** the cake was done by the debutante."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na gumagawa ng mga huwad o pekeng bagay, tulad ng dokumento, pera, o pirma, na may layuning manlinlang.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung expert sa "fake it 'til you make it," pero in a criminal way. Sila 'yung gumagawa ng mga pekeng ID sa Recto, mga "Class A" na sapatos na mukhang orig, o 'yung pirma ng nanay mo sa excuse letter nung high school ka. A **palsipikador** is a professional faker.
usage_notes: A formal and somewhat legalistic term. 'Mamepeke' is more common in everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahuli ng mga pulis ang **palsipikador** ng mga pekeng pera.","translation":"The police caught the **counterfeiter** of fake money."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya bilang isang mahusay na **palsipikador** ng mga lumang pinta.","translation":"He is known as a skilled **forger** of old paintings."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasapi ng klero; isang taong inordenan para sa serbisyong panrelihiyon, tulad ng pari, ministro, o pastor.
original_explanation: Ito yung mga 'Men in Black' ng simbahan, pero hindi sila ahente ng gobyerno na nagtatago ng aliens. Sila yung mga pari, pastor, at iba pang spiritual leaders na naglilingkod sa kanilang komunidad. Sila ang OG spiritual influencers.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa isang indibidwal na kasapi ng klero.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **klerigo** ay nagbigay ng basbas sa mga bagong kasal.","translation":"The **clergyman** gave a blessing to the newlyweds."},{"sentence":"Nag-aral nang maraming taon ang **klerigo** bago siya naordenan.","translation":"The **cleric** studied for many years before he was ordained."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagbabawas sa dami, bilang, o sukat ng isang bagay.
etymology: From pag- (nominalizer) + pa- (causative) + pa- (progressive aspect) + unti (little/few). Lit. 'the act of causing to become little'.
original_explanation: Yung ginagawa mo sa budget mo pag malapit na ang petsa de peligro. Biglang 'di na kailangan ng milk tea at samgyup. Ito rin 'yung unti-unting pagkawala ng pasensya mo sa traffic sa EDSA.
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of budget, resources, supplies, or even abstract concepts like patience.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapaunti** ng kanin sa plato ay bahagi ng kanyang diyeta.","translation":"The **reduction** of rice on the plate is part of his diet."},{"sentence":"Sinimulan ng gobyerno ang **pagpapaunti** sa mga hindi kinakailangang gastusin.","translation":"The government started the **reduction** of unnecessary expenses."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapang yari sa metal na may hugis-pilipit at ginagamit sa pagtanggal ng tapon (cork) mula sa bote, karaniwan ng alak.
original_explanation: That T-shaped thingy you frantically look for when you finally get a bottle of wine. Kung wala nito, magiging challenge ang inuman niyo. Minsan, aasa ka na lang sa YouTube tutorials on how to open a wine bottle with a shoe. Good luck, you'll need it.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiabot ng **tirabuson**, bubuksan ko na itong alak.","translation":"Please pass the **corkscrew**, I'm going to open this wine."}]

translation: to engage in animal husbandry, to raise livestock
meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng pag-aalaga at pagpaparami ng mga hayop bilang isang negosyo o propesyon.
original_explanation: This is the verb form for running a livestock farm. If your lolo decides to retire and spend his days taking care of pigs and chickens for profit, he's going to **maghayupan**. It's not just having pets; it's a full-on business.
usage_notes: This verb is less common than 'mag-alaga ng hayop' but is the specific term for doing it as a profession.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais niyang **maghayupan** pagkatapos niyang magretiro sa kanyang trabaho.","translation":"He wants to **raise livestock** after he retires from his job."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **maghayupan** kung wala kang sapat na kaalaman tungkol dito.","translation":"It's difficult to **engage in animal husbandry** if you don't have enough knowledge about it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gas na walang kulay, lubhang nasusunog, at ginagamit sa pagwe-welding at pagputol ng metal kapag hinaluan ng oksiheno. Ito ay alternatibong baybay ng "asetilen".
original_explanation: Same as 'asetilen,' pero ito yung mas Spanish-sounding na version. Parang yung Jollibee at yung 'Jollibee-with-an-e' sa ibang bansa. Same lang ang laman, iba lang ang label. Ito yung ginagamit sa weldingan para magkadikit ang mga bakal na pinaghiwalay ng tadhana.
usage_notes: Isang alternatibong baybay at pagbigkas para sa "asetilen". Parehong tinatanggap ngunit ang "asetilen" ay mas malapit sa internasyonal na termino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ubos na ang laman ng tangke ng **asetileno** kaya hindi matuloy ang trabaho.","translation":"The **acetylene** tank is empty, so the work cannot continue."},{"sentence":"Mapanganib ang singaw ng **asetileno** kung malalanghap.","translation":"The fumes of **acetylene** are dangerous if inhaled."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-apaw ng tubig at paglubog ng isang lugar, karaniwan dahil sa malakas na ulan o pagtaas ng antas ng tubig sa ilog o dagat.
original_explanation: The national sport of the Philippines during rainy season. When it rains for 30 minutes in Manila, expect it to bumaha. It's when streets turn into instant swimming pools and your commute becomes an extreme water adventure. Also used figuratively, like when your DMs bumaha with messages after posting a fire profile pic.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang pandiwang walang tiyak na gumaganap (impersonal verb) na tumutukoy sa kilos ng pagbaha.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumaha** sa maraming lugar sa Metro Manila dahil sa bagyo.","translation":"Many places in Metro Manila **flooded** because of the typhoon."},{"sentence":"Kapag malakas ang ulan, siguradong **babaha** na naman sa kanto.","translation":"When the rain is heavy, it will surely **flood** at the corner again."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbuga o paglabas ng usok, karaniwang mula sa isang bagay na nasusunog o mula sa isang makina.
original_explanation: What your neighbor's two-stroke tricycle does every morning. Or that ihaw-ihaw stand at the corner that makes the whole street smell like barbecue. It's the visual cue that something is either cooking, burning, or broken.
usage_notes: Do not confuse with 'aso' (dog), which has a different stress and pronunciation. This 'aso' refers to smoke.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **umaso** ang sinaing bago ito masunog.","translation":"The cooking rice began to **smoke** before it got burnt."},{"sentence":"**Umuaso** ang tambutso ng lumang dyip.","translation":"The old jeepney's exhaust pipe was **emitting smoke**."}]

translation: to go to; to head towards
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtungo o pagpunta sa isang tiyak na lugar o direksyon.
etymology: Unknown, possibly from an older Tagalog form.
original_explanation: A slightly more formal or poetic way of saying 'pumunta' or 'to go to'. You'd probably hear this in a historical drama or read it in a classic novel. It's like saying "let's proceed to" instead of "let's go to." Sounds more dramatic, like "Adyo tayo sa palasyo!" (Let's go to the palace!).
usage_notes: This is a very rare and somewhat archaic word. Most modern speakers would use 'punta' or 'tungo'. The conjugated form is often 'umadyo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga mandirigma ay **umadyo** sa larangan ng digmaan.","translation":"The warriors **went** to the battlefield."},{"sentence":"Nais niyang **adyo** sa malayong kaharian.","translation":"He wants to **go to** the faraway kingdom."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-alis sa isang tao o account mula sa listahan ng mga sinusubaybayan sa isang social media platform.
etymology: Hiram na salita mula sa Ingles na "unfollow", karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng social media.
original_explanation: The digital equivalent of saying "I've had enough of your drama/food pics/vague posts." It's the silent breakup of the 21st century. One click and *poof*, their updates are gone from your feed. It's not as harsh as 'unfriend' or 'block,' it's more of a "I'm curating my feed for my mental health" move.
usage_notes: Isang modernong termino na ginagamit sa konteksto ng social media tulad ng Instagram, Twitter (X), at TikTok.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**In-unfollow** ko na siya kasi puro nega ang posts niya.","translation":"I **unfollowed** her because her posts are all negative."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong i-**unfollow**, magpo-post na ako ng matitinong bagay, pramis!","translation":"Don't **unfollow** me, I'll start posting sensible things, I promise!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na idinadagdag sa iba upang ito ay makumpleto, mapabuti, o mapalakas. Karaniwang tumutukoy sa mga bitamina o karagdagang bahagi ng isang publikasyon.
original_explanation: That vitamin C you take so you don't get sick from working overtime. Or that extra section in the Sunday paper with the comics and lifestyle articles. It's the "add-on" to make something better or more complete, like adding extra rice to your chicken inasal meal.
usage_notes: Can refer to nutritional supplements, or a supplementary section of a book or newspaper.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umiinom siya ng **suplemento** na iron para sa kanyang anemia.","translation":"She takes an iron **supplement** for her anemia."},{"sentence":"Nasa **suplemento** ng dyaryo ang mga balitang pampalakasan.","translation":"The sports news is in the newspaper's **supplement**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ikalawang buwan ng taon, na may 28 araw maliban kung 'leap year' na may 29 na araw.
original_explanation: The month of love, 'sana all,' and overpriced flowers. It's when everyone suddenly becomes a relationship expert or a bitter single. Also known for the EDSA People Power Revolution anniversary, which is a holiday, and the start of the Panagbenga Festival in Baguio.
usage_notes: Always capitalized as it is a proper noun, referring to a month of the year.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipagdiriwang namin ang aming anibersaryo sa **Pebrero**.","translation":"We will celebrate our anniversary in **February**."},{"sentence":"Araw ng mga Puso tuwing ika-labing apat ng **Pebrero**.","translation":"Valentine's Day is on the fourteenth of **February**."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang sustansya, likido man o pulbos, na ginagamit upang magbigay o magpalit ng kulay sa isang bagay.
etymology: From `pang-` (instrument for) + `kulay` (color). Note the morphophonemic change where `k` is dropped and `ng` is used in assimilation.
original_explanation: It's the magic stuff that makes things less boring. From the food coloring in your ube ice cream, the dye for your 'tie-dye' project, to the 'atsuete' that gives your afritada its signature color. A pangulay is what you use when you want to tell the world, 'No, this isn't just plain white, this is *fiesta* level.'
usage_notes: The form 'pangkulay' is also very common and acceptable. 'Pangulay' is the result of natural assimilation in Filipino phonology.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng atsuete bilang natural na **pangulay** sa kanyang nilutong kare-kare.","translation":"She used annatto as a natural **colorant** for the kare-kare she cooked."},{"sentence":"Bumili ka ng **pangulay** sa buhok na bagay sa kulay ng balat mo.","translation":"Buy a hair **dye** that matches your skin tone."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamababang bilang ng mga kasapi ng isang kapulungan o samahan na kinakailangang dumalo sa isang pulong upang maging balido ang mga transaksyon.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "cuórum", na hango sa Latin.
original_explanation: That magic number of attendees you need for a meeting to be legit. Kung wala nito, drawing lang ang meeting. It's the corporate version of "Game na ba? Ilan na tayo?" in a group chat before a planned outing. If you don't have quorum, it's an "unofficial" meeting, aka chismisan.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng mga pormal na pagpupulong, batas, at organisasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi natuloy ang boto dahil walang **kuworum** sa Senado.","translation":"The vote did not proceed because there was no **quorum** in the Senate."}]

translation: to hack; to chop (with a heavy blade)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagputol o paghiwa sa isang bagay gamit ang malakas na puwersa, karaniwan sa pamamagitan ng isang malaking patalim tulad ng itak o palakol.
etymology: From 'taga' (a hack or chop) with the -um- infix.
original_explanation: This isn't your delicate kitchen chopping. This is provincial, heavy-duty action. Think clearing a path in the jungle with a bolo, or splitting firewood with an axe. It’s a powerful, swinging motion intended to cut through something tough. The verb form of "Bahala na si Batman!" when facing a giant coconut you need to open.
usage_notes: Implies the use of a heavy blade like a bolo, machete, or axe. It's a downward or sideways hacking motion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumaga** siya ng kawayan para gawing bakod.","translation":"He **hacked** some bamboo to make a fence."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na keyk na idinisenyo upang ihain sa isang tao, karaniwang niluluto sa isang manipis na papel o aluminum cup.
original_explanation: The smaller, cuter, and more socially acceptable version of eating an entire cake by yourself. It's the go-to pasalubong from that one tita who just came from a bake sale or the default birthday treat you bring to the office. Perfect for when you want dessert but are pretending to have self-control.
usage_notes: Isang direktang hiram na salita mula sa Ingles. Ang baybay at pagbigkas sa Ingles ay karaniwang pinapanatili.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng isang dosenang **cupcake** para sa party.","translation":"I bought a dozen **cupcakes** for the party."},{"sentence":"Paborito ng mga bata ang red velvet na **cupcake** na may cream cheese frosting.","translation":"The kids' favorite is the red velvet **cupcake** with cream cheese frosting."}]

translation: to go up on; to climb on
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-akyat o pagpunta sa ibabaw ng isang bagay, tulad ng mesa, hagdanan, o bubong.
original_explanation: What your mom yells at you not to do on the new sofa. "Huwag kang **umakyat** diyan!" It's also what you do when you need to change a lightbulb, or when the floodwaters are rising and the only safe place is the roof. From climbing trees to climbing the corporate ladder, it all starts with sampa.
usage_notes: Can be used literally (climbing a physical object) or figuratively (e.g., "sumampa sa kasikatan" - to rise to fame). Common forms are sumampa (past), sumasampa (present), sasampa (future).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumampa** ang pusa sa bubong para habulin ang ibon.","translation":"The cat **climbed** on the roof to chase the bird."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangyayari o okasyon; maaari ding tumukoy sa pagiging buo, kumpleto, o pagsasakatuparan ng isang bagay.
etymology: From `ka-` + `ganap` + `-an`, denoting an event or the state of being complete.
original_explanation: 'Kaganapan' is the main event, the 'what's happening?', the 'anong ganap?' It can be a concert, a fiesta, or a major plot twist in your favorite teleserye. It's also that feeling of fulfillment, like when your Shopee order finally arrives or when your crush finally notices you. It's the moment something becomes real or complete.
usage_notes: Has a dual meaning: an event/occurrence or the state of completeness/fulfillment. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming tao ang dumalo sa **kaganapan** sa plasa.","translation":"Many people attended the **event** at the plaza."},{"sentence":"Ang pagkapanalo niya sa lotto ang nagbigay **kaganapan** sa kanyang mga pangarap.","translation":"His lottery win gave **fulfillment** to his dreams."}]

translation: to cause to swell; to inflate
meaning_filipino: Gawing mapintog o maging dahilan ng pamamaga o pag-umbok ng isang bagay.
etymology: From the root word 'pintog' (swollen, turgid) and the verbal affix 'pa- -in', indicating causation (to cause to be...).
original_explanation: This is what happens when you get a mosquito bite and can't stop scratching it. Or when someone's ego gets too big after a little praise. "Huwag mo masyadong purihin, baka papintugin mo lang ang ulo niyan." It also applies to literally inflating something, like a balloon. It's the act of making something swell up, literally or figuratively.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of body parts swelling (pamamaga) or egos being inflated (paglaki ng ulo).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kagat ng surot ay kayang **papintugin** ang balat mo.","translation":"A bedbug bite can **cause your skin to swell**."},{"sentence":"Sinadya niyang **papintugin** ang lobo hanggang sa pumutok ito.","translation":"He intentionally **inflated** the balloon until it popped."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkasira ng isang buong bagay sa maraming maliliit na bahagi o piraso, kadalasan dahil sa pagkabagsak o malakas na puwersa.
etymology: From ma- (potential/involuntary action prefix) + piraso (piece), from Spanish 'pedazo'.
original_explanation: What happens to your heart after a breakup. Or what happens to your favorite mug when you drop it. It's the state of being shattered. "Ingat sa pagdala, baka mapiraso 'yang salamin!" Also applies to team projects where everyone wants to go their own way – the project might just get 'mapiraso'.
usage_notes: Used for things that break into multiple fragments, like glass, pottery, or even metaphorically, a group or a heart.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nabitawan niya ang plorera kaya ito'y **napiraso** sa sahig.","translation":"She dropped the vase so it **broke into pieces** on the floor."},{"sentence":"Huwag ninyong hayaang **mapiraso** ang ating pagkakaibigan dahil lang sa maliit na hindi pagkakaunawaan.","translation":"Don't let our friendship be **broken into pieces** just because of a small misunderstanding."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paraan ng pamumuhay ng isang tao, pangkat, o lipunan, kasama ang kanilang mga kaugalian, gawain, at antas sa buhay.
original_explanation: Your 'kapamuhayan' is your personal brand of living. Are you the "woke up like this, minimalist" type, or the "more is more, yolo" type? It's your daily grind, your weekend habits, how you spend your 13th-month pay, and your overall vibe. From "tipid-mode" to "sana-all," it's how you navigate life.
usage_notes: A more formal term for 'lifestyle' or 'paraan ng pamumuhay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang ipinagbago ng kanyang **kapamuhayan** mula nang manalo siya sa lotto.","translation":"His **way of life** changed a lot since he won the lottery."},{"sentence":"Ang simpleng **kapamuhayan** sa probinsya ay hinahanap-hanap ng marami.","translation":"The simple **lifestyle** in the province is longed for by many."}]

translation: to cause a loss to someone, to put at a disadvantage
meaning_filipino: Pagsamantalahan o dayain ang isang tao sa isang transaksyon upang siya'y malugi o mawalan ng kita.
original_explanation: That feeling when you get short-changed by the jeepney driver or when you buy something online and the item you receive is a cheap knock-off. "Nalugi ako" means you lost money on a deal. "Huwag mo akong lugihin" is a warning: "Don't you dare cheat me out of my money." It's the business equivalent of being played.
usage_notes: Used in the context of business, transactions, or any situation where there's an exchange and one party ends up with the short end of the stick.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan siyang **lugihin** ng ka-transaksyon niya, pero naging alisto siya.","translation":"His business partner tried to **cause him a loss**, but he was alert."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam ko ay **nilugi** ako sa bentahan ng kotse.","translation":"I feel like I was **put at a disadvantage** in the car sale."}]

meaning_filipino: Nauukol o kumakatawan sa buong bansa o nasyon.
etymology: From the prefix 'pam-' (a variant of 'pan-' used before 'b' and 'p') and the root word 'bansa', meaning 'country' or 'nation'.
original_explanation: The official label for anything representing the Philippines. Pambansang ulam? Adobo. Pambansang inumin? Kape. Pambansang third wheel? Your friend who's always with a couple. It’s the ultimate Pinoy identifier.
usage_notes: Used to describe things that are official or widely recognized as representing the entire country.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang adobo ay itinuturing ng marami na **pambansa**ng ulam ng Pilipinas.","translation":"Adobo is considered by many as the **national** dish of the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Ipinagdiriwang natin ang **pambansa**ng araw ng mga bayani tuwing Agosto.","translation":"We celebrate the **national** heroes' day every August."}]

translation: to have one's own; to become independent
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng sariling pag-aari, pamilya, o pamumuhay na hiwalay at malaya sa iba, lalo na sa mga magulang.
original_explanation: The ultimate adulting goal! It's when you finally move out of your parents' house, pay your own bills, and have your own life. You're no longer just a dependent; you're the main character of your own teleserye. It's about having your own space, your own rules, and your own stash of instant noodles.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of growing up and becoming independent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang **magkasarili** ng bahay at lupa bago siya mag-treinta.","translation":"Her dream is **to have her own** house and lot before she turns thirty."},{"sentence":"Dumating na ang panahon para **magkasarili** ka na at bumukod sa iyong mga magulang.","translation":"The time has come for you **to become independent** and move out from your parents."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na mahilig magmotorsiklo o sumasali sa mga grupo ng mga nagmomotorsiklo.
original_explanation: Hindi lang 'to yung angkas mo sa Joyride. Sila yung mga naka-full battle gear (leather jacket, helmet, boots) na parang laging may long ride to somewhere, kahit sa kanto lang bibili ng suka. Sila yung may sariling universe ng "rides," "chapters," at "kamote riders." The modern-day cowboys of the asphalt jungle.
usage_notes: Isang direktang hiram na salita mula sa Ingles na malawakang naiintindihan sa Pilipinas. Maaaring tumukoy sa mga mahilig sa motorsiklo at bisikleta, ngunit mas karaniwan sa nauna.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumama ang mga **biker** sa isang charity ride para sa mga biktima ng bagyo.","translation":"The **bikers** joined a charity ride for the typhoon victims."},{"sentence":"Kilala siyang **biker** sa kanilang lugar dahil sa kanyang malaking motorsiklo.","translation":"He is known as a **biker** in their area because of his big motorcycle."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na may masamang intensyon, hangarin, o pag-uugali; isang kriminal o taong gumagawa ng kasamaan.
etymology: Mula sa 'sama' (bad) at 'loob' (inside/will). Literal na 'bad inside'.
original_explanation: Ito yung kontrabida sa teleserye na laging may balak na masama sa bida. Pwede ring holdapper sa kanto, scammer sa text, o yung officemate mong laging naninira sa'yo sa boss. Basically, anyone with bad vibes and even worse intentions.
usage_notes: Often used to refer to criminals or antagonists. Can be used as a noun ('isang masamang-loob') or an adjective ('may masamang-loob na balak').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahuli ng mga pulis ang **masamang-loob** na nagnakaw sa bangko.","translation":"The police caught the **culprit** who robbed the bank."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa mga taong may **masamang-loob**.","translation":"Be careful of people with **evil intentions**."}]

translation: act of measuring by the yard
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso o kilos ng pagsukat ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay tela, gamit ang sukat na yarda.
original_explanation: This is what the tindera at the fabric store does. You say, 'Ate, pabili pong dalawang yarda,' and she whips out her meter stick (which is close enough) and does the 'pagyarda.' It's the specific action of measuring something out in yards.
usage_notes: Specific to measuring length, especially for fabric or land, using the imperial unit 'yard'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis ang kanyang **pagyarda** ng tela dahil sanay na siya sa kanyang trabaho.","translation":"Her **act of measuring the cloth by the yard** was fast because she was used to her job."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pariralang nagpapahayag ng walang tigil o tuloy-tuloy na pagkilos o paggawa ng isang bagay.
etymology: From Tagalog "sige" (go ahead) and "nang" (linker). "Sige" itself is from Spanish "sigue" (it follows / continue).
original_explanation: This is the "bahala na si Batman" of actions. When you're driving through EDSA traffic, working on a deadline, or eating at an unli-rice promo, you just keep going. No brakes, just sige nang sige. It's the mantra of the persistent, the tired, and the very, very hungry.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a relentless or sometimes thoughtless continuation of an action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sige nang sige** siya sa paglalaro ng computer games kahit hatinggabi na.","translation":"He **kept on** playing computer games even though it was already midnight."},{"sentence":"Kahit umuulan, **sige nang sige** ang mga bata sa paglalaro sa labas.","translation":"Even though it was raining, the children **just kept on** playing outside."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na rolyo o karetes na pinag-iikutan ng sinulid, alambre, o anumang katulad na materyal.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung maliit na bagay na laging nawawala sa sewing kit ni lola. The bulilyo holds the thread that makes the magic of sewing happen. Sa modern terms, para siyang mini power bank para sa sinulid. It's small but crucial!
usage_notes: Primarily used in sewing, weaving, or any craft involving thread or wire.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naubusan ng sinulid ang **bulilyo** ng makinang panahi.","translation":"The sewing machine's **bobbin** ran out of thread."},{"sentence":"Maingat niyang inikid ang alambre sa isang maliit na **bulilyo**.","translation":"He carefully wound the wire onto a small **spool**."}]

meaning_filipino: Magsagawa ng protesta sa labas ng isang lugar ng trabaho o gusali, karaniwan ay may dalang mga plakard, upang ipahayag ang mga hinaing o kahilingan.
original_explanation: When the employees' group chat escalates to real life. It's a protest, but with more placards and less anonymity than a Twitter rant. This is what happens when "pizza parties" are given instead of actual salary increases.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in the context of labor strikes, protests, and activism.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang unyon na **magpiket** sa harap ng pabrika upang ipaglaban ang mas mataas na sahod.","translation":"The union decided to **picket** in front of the factory to fight for higher wages."},{"sentence":"Ipinagbabawal ng batas ang pananakit sa mga manggagawang nais **magpiket** nang mapayapa.","translation":"The law prohibits harming workers who want to **picket** peacefully."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-asinta o pagtutok sa isang target bago magpakawala ng isang bagay tulad ng bala, pana, o bato.
original_explanation: That moment of intense focus before you shoot your shot—literally or figuratively. It’s what you do in a video game before a headshot, what a basketball player does before a free throw, or what you do when trying to throw your trash into the bin from across the room.
usage_notes: Can be used for literal aiming or metaphorical targeting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang tamang **pagpunteriya** sa pagbaril.","translation":"Proper **aiming** is important in shooting."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagpunteriya** sa mga layunin niya sa buhay ay kahanga-hanga.","translation":"His **act of aiming** for his goals in life is admirable."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumawa nang malakas, malaya, at kadalasang mula sa tiyan, na nagpapahiwatig ng matinding tuwa o libangan.
original_explanation: This isn't just 'haha' in chat. This is a full-body, no-holds-barred, 'hindi na makahinga' laugh you let out when your friend trips over nothing. It’s the sound of pure, unadulterated chismis being shared among besties. The opposite of a corporate email laugh ('lol').
usage_notes: Past tense. Describes a loud, hearty, and often unrestrained laugh.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Humalakhak** ang buong klase sa biro ng guro.","translation":"The whole class **laughed loudly** at the teacher's joke."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya mapigilang **humalakhak** habang nanonood ng comedy film.","translation":"He couldn't stop himself from **guffawing** while watching the comedy film."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malawak na pook na may magandang tanawin, karaniwang likas na yaman tulad ng bundok, dagat, o bukirin.
etymology: From `tanaw` (view) + `-in` (suffix indicating an object or place).
original_explanation: This is the upgraded, IG-worthy version of `tanaw`. It's not just a view, it's *the* view. Think Mayon Volcano, the Banaue Rice Terraces, or the beaches of Palawan. It's the kind of scenery that makes you say, 'Picture-an mo 'ko, dali!' It's what's on postcards and tourism ads.
usage_notes: `Tanawin` specifically refers to the scenery itself, while `tanaw` is the act or state of viewing from a distance. Can also be a verb `tanawin` (to look at from a distance), but the noun form is more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakaganda ng **tanawin** sa tuktok ng Bundok Pulag.","translation":"The **scenery** at the peak of Mount Pulag is so beautiful."},{"sentence":"Isa sa mga sikat na **tanawin** sa Bohol ang Chocolate Hills.","translation":"The Chocolate Hills are one of the famous **landscapes** in Bohol."}]

translation: to give a speech, to orate
meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na pagbigkas ng isang sanaysay o talumpati sa harap ng mga tagapakinig.
original_explanation: This is the formal version of 'may speech ka.' It's what politicians do during campaigns, what your valedictorian classmate did at graduation, and what you have to do when it's your turn for the reporting in class. Public speaking, but make it *Filipino formal*.
usage_notes: A formal word used for public speaking events.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Buong giting siyang **nanalumpati** sa harap ng libu-libong tao.","translation":"He bravely **gave a speech** in front of thousands of people."},{"sentence":"Ang susunod na **mananalumpati** ay ang ating kagalang-galang na panauhin.","translation":"The next one to **orate** is our honorable guest."}]

meaning_filipino: Patawan ng multa ang isang tao o entidad bilang parusa sa paglabag sa isang batas o regulasyon.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you get caught breaking the "bawal tumawid, may namatay na dito" sign. The MMDA officer will happily **papagmultahin** you. It's the government's way of saying, "Oops, you did it again," and then taking your money.
usage_notes: A formal term used in legal and official contexts. The active form is 'magpamulta'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Papagmultahin** ng LTO ang sinumang mahuhuling lumabag sa batas-trapiko.","translation":"The LTO will **impose a fine** on anyone caught violating traffic laws."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-overstay sa parking, baka ka **papagmultahin**.","translation":"Don't overstay in the parking lot, you might be **made to pay a fine**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, sitwasyon, o tanong na mahirap unawain, lutasin, o harapin; isang hadlang o suliranin.
original_explanation: The national capital of the Philippines. Charot. It's anything from "Walang wifi" to "Wala akong pera" to "Mahal ko pa ba ex ko?". A problema is the default status of any Filipino before coffee, after their commute, or when looking at their bills. The answer is always "Bahala na si Batman."
usage_notes: A very common word. Can be used for minor inconveniences to major life crises.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang trapik ang pinakamalaking **problema** tuwing umaga.","translation":"Traffic is the biggest **problem** every morning."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, lahat ng **problema** ay may solusyon.","translation":"Don't worry, every **problem** has a solution."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na seremonya kung saan iginagawad ang mga diploma o akademikong digri sa mga mag-aaral na matagumpay na nakatapos ng kanilang pag-aaral.
original_explanation: The big day! It's the culmination of puyat, pagod, photocopies, and parental pressure. It's a day of celebration marked by a toga that's always too hot, a cap that won't stay on, and endless picture-taking with the whole barangay. The Tagalog term is "Pagtatapos," but everyone just says graduation. It's the finish line you've been dreaming of... right before you start worrying about finding a job.
usage_notes: The English word is used directly. The native Tagalog equivalent is "pagtatapos," but "graduation" is extremely common in both formal and informal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Saan gaganapin ang **graduation** ninyo?","translation":"Where will your **graduation** be held?"},{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng bagong bestida para sa **graduation** ko.","translation":"Mom bought a new dress for my **graduation**."}]

meaning_filipino: Matubig ang timpla; kulang sa lasa o tapang dahil sa sobrang pagkahalo ng likido, lalo na ng tubig.
original_explanation: The ultimate betrayal for any coffee or juice lover. It's when your drink tastes like it just had a brief, awkward conversation with the flavor it was supposed to have. That iced tea that's 90% melted ice? That's **lasaw**. Your friend's lame excuse for being late? **Lasaw** din. It lacks punch, substance, and flavor.
usage_notes: Primarily used for drinks and sauces. Can be used metaphorically for weak arguments or uninspired performances.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayoko ng kape rito, laging **lasaw**.","translation":"I don't like the coffee here, it's always **watery**."},{"sentence":"Naging **lasaw** ang sinigang dahil naparami ang sabaw.","translation":"The sinigang became **bland** because too much broth was added."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang amoy ng isang tao na nagbabad sa ilalim ng sikat ng araw, karaniwang pinaghalong amoy ng pawis at alikabok.
original_explanation: This is the official scent of every Filipino kid after playing patintero outside all afternoon. It’s that distinct, slightly sour, dusty smell you get when sweat meets intense tropical heat. Your mom can detect this from a mile away and her first command will always be, 'Maligo ka na, amoy-araw ka na!'
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang ilarawan ang isang tao, hindi isang bagay. Ito ay isang napaka-karaniwan at naglalarawang ekspresyong Pilipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumasok sa bahay ang mga bata na **amoy-araw** at pawisan.","translation":"The children came into the house **smelling of the sun** and sweaty."},{"sentence":"Kahit naka-aircon sa opisina, pakiramdam ko'y **amoy-araw** pa rin ako dahil sa biyahe.","translation":"Even with the office aircon, I feel like I still **smell of the sun** because of the commute."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng kawani na ang pangunahing tungkulin ay tumulong sa mga gawaing pang-opisina, tulad ng pag-aayos ng mga dokumento, pag-iskedyul ng mga pagpupulong, at pagsagot sa mga tawag.
original_explanation: She's the gatekeeper of the boss. The one who knows the entire office's schedule, chismis, and where the good coffee is hidden. You need to be on her good side if you want your leave form signed. The real CEO of the office, TBH.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa isang babaeng kalihim. Ang katumbas na panlalaki ay "sekretaryo".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakibigay na lang po itong dokumento sa **sekretarya** ni Atty. Reyes.","translation":"Please just give this document to Atty. Reyes' **secretary**."},{"sentence":"Ang aming **sekretarya** ang nag-ayos ng lahat para sa Christmas party.","translation":"Our **secretary** arranged everything for the Christmas party."}]

translation: will be heard; will be heeded
meaning_filipino: Pakikinggan o bibigyang-pansin ang isang pakiusap, payo, o tunog. Ito ay nasa aspektong panghinaharap ng pandiwang 'dinggin'.
etymology: Mula sa "dinig" (marinig) + "-in" (hulapi) + pag-uulit ng unang pantig (di-) para sa aspektong panghinaharap.
original_explanation: Yung dasal mo na sana diringgin na ni Lord. O 'yung request mo for a raise na sana diringgin ng boss mo. It's the ultimate 'sana all' for requests and prayers, hoping they don't just enter one ear and exit the other.
usage_notes: Ito ang anyong panghinaharap ng pandiwang 'dinggin'. Ang salitang-ugat ay 'dinig'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana'y **diringgin** ng mga mambabatas ang hinaing ng taumbayan.","translation":"Hopefully, the lawmakers **will heed** the grievances of the people."},{"sentence":"Ang panalangin ng isang ina ay laging **diringgin** ng Maykapal.","translation":"A mother's prayer **will** always **be heard** by God."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paunti-unting pagpapakilala o pagpapahiwatig ng isang bagay, tulad ng isang bagong relasyon, sa publiko o sa social media, nang hindi ito direktang inaamin o inaanunsyo.
etymology: Hango sa pariralang Ingles na "soft launch", orihinal na mula sa marketing at tech.
original_explanation: The 'di-diretsahang pag-reveal' ng jowa. You post a picture of two coffee cups, a photo where their hand is visible, or an IG story where you can hear their laugh in the background. It’s for the marites to analyze. You're not officially announcing the relationship, just dropping clues para 'pag nag-break, hindi masyadong nakakahiya mag-delete. It's a trial period for your public image as a couple.
usage_notes: Habang orihinal na terminolohiya sa negosyo, naging popular ito sa konteksto ng mga relasyon sa social media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita mo ba yung IG story niya? Mukhang **soft launch** na nila ng bago niyang jowa.","translation":"Did you see her IG story? It looks like a **soft launch** with her new partner."},{"sentence":"Hindi pa kami official, pero parang nag-**soft launch** na siya sa akin sa Twitter.","translation":"We're not official yet, but it seems like he **soft launched** me on Twitter."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtatagpo o pagsalubong ng dalawang linya, daan, o landas sa isang punto.
original_explanation: Literal na 'X marks the spot.' Pwedeng 'dito nagkrus ang landas natin' moment na parang Fated To Be Yours ang drama. O pwedeng 'dito nagkrus ang tingin natin' na sign na para mag-away na kayo sa huling piraso ng lechon.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for roads intersecting or figuratively for paths of people meeting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay hindi na muling **magkrus** ang landas nating dalawa.","translation":"I hope our paths **never cross** again."},{"sentence":"Sa kanto kung saan **nagkrus** ang EDSA at Ayala Avenue, doon sila nagkita.","translation":"At the corner where EDSA and Ayala Avenue **intersect**, that's where they met."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na termino na tumutukoy sa pagiging sumpungin, madaling magbago ang kalooban, o pagpapakita ng hindi inaasahang pag-uugali. Ito ay isang paglalaro sa pariralang 'may toyo sa utak.'
etymology: From the idiom 'may toyo sa utak' (has soy sauce in the brain), implying something is amiss in the head.
original_explanation: This is the 'soy sauce in the brain' syndrome. When someone is being moody, unpredictable, or just plain weird for no reason, you say 'May toyo 'yan.' It's the Pinoy way of describing someone's sudden shift in mood, like when your friend is laughing one minute and then deadma the next. It’s the unofficial diagnosis for PMS, mid-life crisis, and random tantrums.
usage_notes: Highly colloquial and informal. Used to describe a person's erratic or moody behavior. Often used humorously.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo munang kausapin si boss, mukhang may **toyo** ngayon.","translation":"Don't talk to the boss yet, it seems he's **moody** today."},{"sentence":"Bakit ka ganyan? May **toyo** ka na naman ba?","translation":"Why are you like that? Are you being **temperamental** again?"}]

translation: to speak ill of; to bad-mouth
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapahayag ng mga negatibo, mapanirang-puri, o hindi kanais-nais na bagay tungkol sa isang tao, kadalasan kapag wala sila.
original_explanation: This is the tea, the chismis, the main event of any Marites gathering. It's when you talk behind someone's back. 'Uy, alam mo ba si ano...' is the national anthem for this activity. It's basically turning your tongue into a weapon of mass destruction for someone's reputation.
usage_notes: A common phrase used to describe gossip or slander. The object of the negative speech is often introduced with 'tungkol sa' or 'laban sa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi magandang ugali ang **magsalita nang masama** tungkol sa iyong kapwa.","translation":"It is not a good habit to **speak ill of** others."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpilipit o pagbabago ng anyo ng bibig at mukha dahil sa sakit, pait, asim, o pagkadiri.
original_explanation: That face you make when you accidentally drink your Lolo's suka thinking it's water, or when your officemate shows you their 'salamat, shopee' haul and it's... questionable. It's a silent, facial 'yuck!' or 'ouch!'.
usage_notes: Describes a facial expression, specifically the contortion of the mouth due to pain, disgust, or tasting something sour.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **pagngibit** ang naisagot niya nang matikman ang maasim na mangga.","translation":"A **grimace** was his response when he tasted the sour mango."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko ang **pagngibit** sa kanyang mukha nang masaling ang sugat niya.","translation":"I saw the **grimace** on his face when his wound was touched."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng kahinhinan, kababaang-loob, at pagiging pino sa kilos, pananalita, at pananamit.
original_explanation: The 'Maria Clara' vibe. It's the opposite of being loud and scandalous. Think of a dalagang Pilipina who is soft-spoken, dresses conservatively, and doesn't make a scene. It's a classic trait, but in today's world, it's more of a personal choice than a social expectation. Also, the surname of the 'Brains of the Revolution,' Apolinario Mabini.
usage_notes: Often associated with traditional Filipino feminine virtues.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinahangaan siya dahil sa kanyang **mabini** na pag-uugali.","translation":"She is admired for her **modest** demeanor."},{"sentence":"Isang **mabini** na ngiti lamang ang kanyang isinukli.","translation":"She only returned a **gentle** smile."}]

translation: to undergo steam inhalation; to be fumigated
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalanghap ng singaw o usok, karaniwan mula sa pinakuluang tubig na may halamang gamot, bilang isang paraan ng panggagamot o paglilinis.
original_explanation: This is lola's cure-all. Got a cold? 'Suob'. Feeling run down? 'Suob'. It’s the traditional Filipino practice of steam inhalation, where you put a towel over your head and inhale steam from a basin of hot water, often with salt or medicinal leaves. It’s like a DIY spa treatment and decongestant in one. It can also mean to fumigate a room to drive away pests or bad spirits.
usage_notes: Also known as 'tuob' in other dialects. The practice is a form of traditional healing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinayuhan siya ng kanyang lola na **sumuob** para guminhawa ang kanyang paghinga.","translation":"His grandmother advised him **to undergo steam inhalation** to ease his breathing."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **sumuob** sa silid para mawala ang mga lamok.","translation":"We need **to fumigate** the room to get rid of the mosquitoes."}]

translation: leading, to be first, to be at the forefront
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging una sa isang hilera, kompetisyon, o anumang uri ng pagkakasunud-sunod; pamumuno.
original_explanation: 'Yung laging top 1 sa klase, 'yung paboritong team mo sa UAAP na laging champion, o 'yung chismosa sa kanto na unang nakakaalam ng balita. It means being number one, taking the lead, being ahead of the pack.
usage_notes: Ito ang kasalukuyang anyo (present progressive) ng pandiwang 'manguna'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nangunguna** sa karera ang pambato ng Pilipinas.","translation":"The Philippines' representative is **leading** the race."},{"sentence":"Siya ang laging **nangunguna** sa aming klase.","translation":"He is always the one who is **at the forefront** in our class."}]

meaning_filipino: (Pangngalan) Ang antas ng kaalaman o edukasyon na natamo ng isang tao. (Pandiwa) Ang kilos ng pag-aaral o pagsusuri sa isang bagay na naganap na.
original_explanation: As a noun, ito yung "What's your educational background?" sa job interviews, or yung reason bakit ka pinapagalitan ng nanay mo para mag-aral mabuti. As a verb, ito yung ginawa mo sa ex mo bago mo i-accept ulit—you studied the situation. O yung ginawa mo sa menu ng resto for 15 minutes.
usage_notes: Can be a noun (educational attainment) or a verb (past tense of 'to study something'). Context is key. "May pinag-aralan" (has education) vs. "Pinag-aralan niya" (He/She studied it).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipakita mong may **pinag-aralan** kang tao.","translation":"Show that you are an **educated** person."},{"sentence":"**Pinag-aralan** niyang mabuti ang kontrata bago pumirma.","translation":"He **studied** the contract carefully before signing."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagkakaroon ng matindi at kung minsan ay di-makatwirang pagkahumaling o pagkasabik sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: Stage 5 clinger. Yung level of pagka-faney mo sa isang K-Pop idol na pati unan mo may mukha niya. O yung pagka-adik mo sa isang mobile game na hindi ka na naliligo. It's obsession with a hint of craziness. When you're 'haling na haling,' you're completely, utterly, no-turning-back gone for it.
usage_notes: Often intensified as 'haling na haling' to mean 'completely obsessed'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay **haling** sa pagbabasa ng mga libro.","translation":"She is **crazy about** reading books."},{"sentence":"Naging **haling na haling** ang mga tao sa bagong serye sa TV.","translation":"The people became **completely obsessed** with the new TV series."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto o proseso ng pagpapanumbalik sa dati o orihinal na kalagayan, anyo, o posisyon ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: Parang pag-restore ng factory settings sa phone mo. O kaya 'yung effort mong ibalik 'yung tiwala ng jowa mo after mo siyang 'di i-update. It's the act of making things right or whole again.
usage_notes: A less common word for restoration. 'Pagpapanumbalik' is more frequently used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap ang **pamuli** sa nasirang reputasyon.","translation":"The **act of restoring** a ruined reputation is difficult."},{"sentence":"Ang **pamuli** sa lumang gusali ay nangangailangan ng malaking pondo.","translation":"The **restoration** of the old building requires a large fund."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglaki o pamamaga ng isang bahagi ng katawan sanhi ng pinsala, sakit, o pagkaipon ng likido.
original_explanation: 'Yung itsura ng mata mo pagkatapos mong mag-marathon ng K-drama buong gabi. O 'yung pisngi mo pagkatapos bunutan ng ngipin. Also, 'yung pride ng ka-team mo na ayaw tumanggap ng feedback, "ang maga ng ego."
usage_notes: A very common word to describe inflammation or swelling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Maga** ang kanang paa niya dahil natapilok siya.","translation":"Her right foot is **swollen** because she sprained it."},{"sentence":"Umiyak siya buong gabi kaya **maga** ang kanyang mga mata.","translation":"She cried all night, that's why her eyes are **puffy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagsasama-sama o pag-uugnay ng iba't ibang bahagi, elemento, o indibidwal upang bumuo ng isang nagkakaisang kabuuan.
original_explanation: Parang pag-blend ng mango at graham sa blender para maging mango graham shake. O kaya 'yung pag-welcome sa bagong ka-team sa office at pag-include sa kanya sa lunch out at chismisan. It's making different things work together as one, from company departments to the ingredients in your sinigang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **integrasyon** ng mga bagong empleyado sa kultura ng kumpanya.","translation":"The **integration** of new employees into the company culture is important."},{"sentence":"Ang proyektong ito ay naglalayon ng mas malalim na **integrasyon** sa ekonomiya ng rehiyon.","translation":"This project aims for deeper economic **integration** in the region."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalakbay o pagbabakasyon ng bagong kasal pagkatapos ng kanilang kasal upang ipagdiwang ang kanilang pagsasama.
etymology: From 'pulot' (to pick up/gather) and 'gata' (coconut milk), a metaphor for the sweetness of the newlywed phase.
original_explanation: The OG 'travel goals' for newlyweds. It's that sweet period after the stress of wedding planning where you can finally 'collect the coconut milk' (the weirdly poetic literal translation). Basically, it's your first official vacation as a married couple, probably funded by ninongs and ninangs, before you have to deal with bills and in-laws.
usage_notes: This is an idiomatic expression. It is exclusively used to mean 'to go on a honeymoon'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa Palawan balak **magpulot-gata** ng bagong kasal.","translation":"The newlyweds plan to **have their honeymoon** in Palawan."},{"sentence":"\"Saan kayo **magpupulot-gata**?\" tanong ng lahat sa amin.","translation":"\"Where will you **go for your honeymoon**?\" everyone asked us."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtakip sa ulo o mukha gamit ang isang talukbong, belo, o anumang uri ng pandong.
etymology: Nagmula sa salitang 'talukbong' (veil) na may hulaping '-an', na nagpapahiwatig ng isang kilos.
original_explanation: This is the act of putting on a veil or any head covering. Picture a bride walking down the aisle, or your lola going to church with a mantilla. It's the action, not the object. 'Yung pagtatago mo sa likod ng face mask para 'di ka makilala ng nangungutang sa'yo, 'di 'yan talukbungan, pero gets mo na 'yung idea ng pagtakip.
usage_notes: Isang pormal at medyo makalumang pandiwa. Ang anyong 'magtalukbong' ay mas karaniwang naririnig.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tinalukbungan** ng nobya ang kanyang mukha bago pumasok sa simbahan.","translation":"The bride **covered her face with a veil** before entering the church."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **talukbungan** ang katotohanan ng mga kasinungalingan.","translation":"Do not **veil** the truth with lies."}]

translation: to dream of, to aspire to
meaning_filipino: Ang paghahangad o pag-asam na makamit ang isang bagay o marating ang isang kalagayan.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you're staring at the ceiling at 2 AM, thinking about your K-Pop bias or that beach trip to Palawan. To **pangarapin** is to want something so bad, it plays like a movie in your head. It's the verb form of your #goals.
usage_notes: This is the object-focused verb for "pangarap" (dream/ambition).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matagal na niyang **pinapangarap** na maging isang doktor.","translation":"She has long been **dreaming** of becoming a doctor."},{"sentence":"Ano ang **pinapangarap** mong trabaho?","translation":"What is your **dream** job?"}]

meaning_filipino: Walang karangalan; kahiya-hiya at hindi kagalang-galang ang isang gawain, pag-uugali, o pagkatao.
original_explanation: The act of taking credit for someone else's work, cutting in line, or posting fake news for clicks. It's any action that would make your lola shake her head in disappointment. Basically, behavior that belongs in the 'cancel culture' folder for being utterly classless.
usage_notes: A strong word used to condemn actions or behaviors that violate moral or ethical standards.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagnanakaw sa kaban ng bayan ay isang **di-marangal** na gawain.","translation":"Stealing from the nation's coffers is a **dishonorable** act."},{"sentence":"Itinuturing niyang **di-marangal** ang paninira sa kapwa para lang umangat.","translation":"He considers slandering others just to get ahead as **undignified**."}]

meaning_filipino: Lagyan ng pain o pang-akit ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay patibong o bingwit, upang makahuli.
original_explanation: This is what you do before you can catch fish, or a mouse, or even a potential customer. You put the 'pain' (bait) on the 'kawil' (hook). 'Painan mo 'yang bitag para mahuli 'yung daga.' In marketing, a freebie or a discount is the 'pain' you use to 'painan' your sales funnel.
usage_notes: 'Pain' (bait) + '-an' (locative/applicative suffix). To put bait onto something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Painan** mo ng bulate ang bingwit.","translation":"**Bait** the fishhook with a worm."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **painan** ang patibong para may mahuling baboy-ramo.","translation":"The trap needs to be **baited** to catch a wild boar."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pariralang balbal na naglalarawan sa isang bagay, kilos, o tao bilang sukdulang "bakla" o nagpapakita ng mga katangiang iniuugnay sa mga bakla.
etymology: From "bekimon" or gayspeak, a transformation of "baklang totoo" (true gay). "Bakla" becomes "accla," and "totoo" becomes "twoh."
original_explanation: The final evolution of "accla." "Acclang twoh" (from "baklang totoo" or "true gay") is the label for something that is unapologetically, undeniably, and fabulously gay. It’s the glitter on the eyelids, the death drop on the dance floor, the high note in a Mariah Carey song. It’s not just gay, it’s *gay* gay. The highest level of gayness you can achieve.
usage_notes: A very specific slang term used within the LGBTQ+ community. It's an intensifier.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Yung playlist mo puro Lady Gaga at Ariana Grande, **acclang twoh**!","translation":"Your playlist is all Lady Gaga and Ariana Grande, **so gay**!"},{"sentence":"Ang reaction niya sa chismis, **acclang twoh**.","translation":"His reaction to the gossip was **quintessentially gay**."}]

translation: to sort; to classify; to separate
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paghihiwa-hiwalay ng mga bagay ayon sa kanilang uri, katangian, o kategorya.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung ginagawa mo sa laundry—puti, de-kolor, at 'yung mga damit na may "sana all" feelings na ayaw mo nang labhan. Sa office, ito 'yung pag-sort ng tasks from "urgent" to "bahala na si Batman."
usage_notes: The command form of the verb. "Bukurin" is the imperative. "Pagbukurin" implies a more deliberate or comprehensive act of sorting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pagbukurin** mo ang mga basura sa nabubulok at di-nabubulok.","translation":"**Separate** the trash into biodegradable and non-biodegradable."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **pagbukurin** ang mga dokumento ayon sa petsa.","translation":"The documents need **to be sorted** according to date."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng paglilinis ng mga damit at iba pang tela sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng tubig at sabon.
original_explanation: The national sport every weekend. It's the never-ending cycle of sorting whites, coloreds, and 'pwede na 'to isama.' It's that magical process where one sock always goes missing. Whether you're doing it by hand (kuskos-kuskos) or by machine, it's the ultimate chore that prepares you for the week ahead.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing Sabado ang araw ng aking **paglalaba**.","translation":"Saturday is my day for **washing clothes**."},{"sentence":"Napagod siya sa maghapong **paglalaba**.","translation":"She got tired from a whole day of **laundering**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang supot ng balat na naglalaman ng mga itlog ng bayag sa mga lalaking mamalya.
original_explanation: The family jewels, the boys downstairs, the very things that make a 'tropa' meeting hilarious when someone accidentally gets hit there. It's often used in jest or as a mild curse word, but anatomically, it's the scrotum. "Mag-ingat ka sa bola, baka tamaan ang **bayag** mo!"
usage_notes: Considered vulgar or coarse in formal settings but is common in informal, male-centric conversations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagrereklamo ang pasyente dahil sa pananakit ng kaniyang **bayag**.","translation":"The patient is complaining of pain in his **scrotum**."},{"sentence":"Sa anatomya, ang eskroto ay ang panlabas na sako na bumabalot sa **bayag**.","translation":"In anatomy, the scrotum is the external sac that encloses the **testicles**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aalinlangan o pag-uurong-sulong sa paggawa ng isang desisyon o aksyon dahil sa kawalan ng katiyakan o takot.
original_explanation: 'Yung moment na nasa counter ka na ng fast food at tinanong ka, 'What's your order, ma'am/sir?' tapos bigla kang nag-freeze. You `mag-atubili`. Also applies to confessing your feelings to your crush. The ultimate 'Should I or shouldn't I?'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mag-atubili** na magtanong kung mayroon kang hindi naiintindihan.","translation":"Don't **hesitate** to ask if there is something you don't understand."},{"sentence":"Siya ay **nag-atubili** na sabihin ang totoo dahil natatakot siya sa magiging reaksyon mo.","translation":"He **hesitated** to tell the truth because he was afraid of your reaction."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hayop o nilalang na ang pangunahing pagkain ay karne.
original_explanation: A meat-lover, basically. In science, it's an animal that eats other animals. In real life, it's that friend who goes to a samgyupsal buffet and ignores all the side dishes except the meat. "Rice? No thanks, pass the liempo." That's a true karniboro.
usage_notes: Maaari ring gamitin bilang pang-uri (adjective) na "karniboroso" o sa pangungusap tulad ng "Ang leon ay isang hayop na karniboro."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang leon ay isang halimbawa ng **karniboro**.","translation":"The lion is an example of a **carnivore**."},{"sentence":"Itinuturing na isang **karniboro** ang buwaya.","translation":"The crocodile is considered a **carnivore**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kaganapan o pagtitipon kung saan ang mga tao ay sama-samang umaawit.
original_explanation: The main event of any Pinoy party. It starts with one person grabbing the mic, and ends with everyone screaming "My Way" at 3 AM. It’s the ultimate bonding experience, fueled by San Mig Light and a thick songbook. "Tara, kantahan na!"
usage_notes: Refers to the event or activity of singing together.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkayayaan ang magkakaibigan na magkaroon ng **kantahan** sa videoke bar.","translation":"The friends decided to have a **singing session** at the videoke bar."},{"sentence":"Hindi kumpleto ang Pasko kung walang **kantahan** at sayawan.","translation":"Christmas isn't complete without a **sing-along** and dancing."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marahas at hindi makontrol na panginginig ng buong katawan, karaniwang sanhi ng mataas na lagnat, matinding takot, o ginaw.
original_explanation: This is 'mangatal' on steroids. This isn't a cute little shiver. This is the full-body, teeth-chattering tremble you get from a 40°C fever, watching a horror movie alone at 3 AM, or getting caught in a monsoon rain without an umbrella.
usage_notes: Implies a more intense and often uncontrollable trembling compared to 'mangatal' or 'manginig'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **mangatog** sa ginaw ang bata dahil basang-basa siya sa ulan.","translation":"The child began **to shudder** from the cold because he was soaked from the rain."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng kawalan ng kakayahang makakita; maaaring pisikal o metaporikal na tumutukoy sa kawalan ng kaalaman o pag-unawa.
