original_explanation: Literally, not being able to see. Figuratively, it’s what happens when you have a crush. You ignore all the red flags, you think their toxic traits are 'cute quirks.' Pag-ibig nga naman. This is the official state of being for anyone who says, 'I can fix him/her.'
usage_notes: Ginagamit pareho sa literal na medikal na kondisyon at sa matalinhagang paraan para sa 'blind love', 'blind faith', atbp.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming sanhi ang **pagkabulag**, kabilang ang mga sakit at aksidente.","translation":"There are many causes of **blindness**, including diseases and accidents."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagkabulag** sa pag-ibig ang naging dahilan ng kanyang mga maling desisyon.","translation":"Her **blindness** in love was the reason for her wrong decisions."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na lumilikha at naglalathala ng mga video blog (vlog), na karaniwang ibinabahagi sa mga online platform tulad ng YouTube.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na "vlogger," pinaikling "video blogger."
original_explanation: Ito yung tropa mong "What's up, guys!" ang bati sa umaga, tanghali, at gabi. Lahat ng ganap sa buhay, mula paggising hanggang pagkain ng instant noodles, kailangang i-document. Sila ang dahilan kung bakit alam mo kung anong latest sa food trip, travel, o chismis, at kung bakit minsan napapabili ka ng mga bagay na 'di mo naman kailangan dahil sa "budol" nila.
usage_notes: Isang modernong hiram na salita na malawakang ginagamit at nauunawaan sa Pilipinas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging sikat na **vlogger** si Anna dahil sa kanyang mga travel video.","translation":"Anna became a famous **vlogger** because of her travel videos."},{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang maging isang full-time **vlogger** balang araw.","translation":"Her dream is to become a full-time **vlogger** someday."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitang metal na ginagamit upang buksan o isara ang isang kandado.
original_explanation: This is the old-school, hispanized word for 'susi'. Your lola might have used this term for the key to the aparador where she keeps the forbidden corned beef. It comes from the Spanish 'llave'. Nowadays, if you say 'Pakiabot ng **yawe**,' people might just give you a confused look before handing you the 'susi'.
usage_notes: Largely considered archaic or regional. 'Susi' is the universally understood and standard term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawawala ang **yawe** ng baul ng lola.","translation":"Grandma's chest key is missing."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mabilis at magaang na pagpalo o pagpitik gamit ang dulo ng daliri o isang maliit na bagay.
original_explanation: It's more than a tap, less than a slap. Think of flicking an ant off your table, or when your lola flicks your hand away from the Noche Buena table before midnight. It’s a quick, sharp 'get-off-me' motion.
usage_notes: The verb form is `pilandutin` (to flick something).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **pilandot** lang sa pisngi ang ginawa niya.","translation":"He just gave a light **flick** on the cheek."},{"sentence":"**Pinilandot** niya ang langgam sa kanyang braso.","translation":"He **flicked** the ant off his arm."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang halal na opisyal na bahagi ng lehislatura na may kapangyarihang gumawa, magbago, o magpawalang-bisa ng mga batas.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "tagapag-" (doer/agent of action) at sa salitang ugat na "batas" (law).
original_explanation: The people in Congress or the Senate you see arguing on TV. They're supposed to be making laws for the country, but sometimes it feels like they're just making content for their next campaign ad.
usage_notes: Isang pormal na termino. Ang "mambabatas" ay isang karaniwang kasingkahulugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tungkulin ng isang **tagapagbatas** na pakinggan ang hinaing ng kaniyang mga nasasakupan.","translation":"It is the duty of a **lawmaker** to listen to the grievances of their constituents."}]

translation: to make something spin; to rotate; to manage (money)
meaning_filipino: Ipagalaw ang isang bagay sa paraang umiikot ito sa sarili nitong aksis. Maaari ring tumukoy sa paggamit ng pera upang kumita.
original_explanation: This is the command form. 'Paikutin mo 'yung bote' for a game of spin the bottle. It also has a business meaning: using capital to generate more money. 'Kailangan kong paikutin itong puhunan para lumago.' It's the entrepreneur's mantra, making your money work for you, not just letting it sit in the bank.
usage_notes: Has a common literal meaning and a very popular figurative meaning related to deception or manipulation. The word 'paikitin' is a less common variant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Paikutin** mo ang trumpo.","translation":"**Spin** the top."},{"sentence":"Magaling siyang **paikutin** ang maliit na puhunan para maging malaking negosyo.","translation":"She is good at **managing** a small capital to become a big business."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtubo o pag-usbong ng isang bagong bahagi ng halaman, tulad ng dahon o bulaklak.
original_explanation: That feeling when a new idea pops into your head during a brainstorming session. Or when you see the first tiny green leaf on the monggo seeds from your kid's science project. That's 'sumuloy'. It's the start of something new and fresh.
usage_notes: Often used in a literary or poetic context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng ilang araw, **sumuloy** na rin ang mga butong itinanim ko.","translation":"After a few days, the seeds I planted finally **sprouted**."},{"sentence":"Isang bagong pag-asa ang **sumuloy** sa kanyang puso.","translation":"A new hope **sprouted** in his/her heart."}]

translation: to act like an animal, to be beastly
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-asal na parang hayop; ang pagpapakita ng kabangisan o kawalan ng tamang pag-iisip.
original_explanation: When someone cuts you off in traffic and you just want to go wild, that's the urge to **maghayop**. It's a very strong word, often used when someone is acting uncivilized, rude, or savage. 'Naghayop siya sa galit' means he went totally beast mode. It's the opposite of being a rational human being.
usage_notes: A very strong and often negative term to describe behavior. Can be used to mean 'to curse' or 'to rage.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula siyang **maghayop** sa galit nang malaman niyang niloko siya.","translation":"He started to **act like an animal** in anger when he found out he was cheated."},{"sentence":"Pinagsabihan siya na huwag **maghayop** sa harap ng mga bata.","translation":"He was told not to **behave savagely** in front of the children."}]

translation: fetid, foul-smelling (like stagnant water or urine)
meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa masangsang at mabahong amoy, karaniwan mula sa ihi o sa tubig na hindi umaagos.
original_explanation: You know that specific, sharp, nasty smell from a public CR that hasn't been cleaned in a week? Or the smell of a canal or estero during summer? That's **lantong**. It's a smell that attacks your nostrils and makes you want to hold your breath indefinitely. It’s the official scent of "napatayong ihi sa pader."
usage_notes: Specifically refers to the smell of old urine or stagnant, dirty water.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **lantong** na amoy mula sa eskinita ay hindi matagalan.","translation":"The **fetid** smell from the alley is unbearable."},{"sentence":"Nangangamoy **lantong** ang lumang banyo.","translation":"The old bathroom smells **foul** like stale urine."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hukay o kompartimento sa isang pader, karaniwan sa sementeryo o simbahan, kung saan inilalagay ang kabaong o urna ng isang yumaong tao.
original_explanation: Your final, minimalist condo unit. It's that drawer-like space in a cemetery's 'apartment building' style tomb. When land for traditional burials gets too expensive, the 'nitso' becomes the practical choice. It's a very Filipino way of dealing with the high cost of... well, leaving.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'puntod' or 'libingan' in a general sense, but 'nitso' specifically refers to the wall compartment for a coffin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglagay sila ng mga bulaklak at kandila sa harap ng **nitso** ng kanilang lola.","translation":"They placed flowers and candles in front of their grandmother's **tomb niche**."},{"sentence":"Nangungupahan sila ng **nitso** sa sementeryo para sa kanilang yumaong kamag-anak.","translation":"They are renting a **crypt** in the cemetery for their deceased relative."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagkain na binili mula sa isang restawran o kainan upang kainin sa ibang lugar at hindi sa loob ng establisyimento.
original_explanation: The default setting for Pinoys who are too tired to cook after a long day in traffic. It's the 'uwi na lang natin 'to' move. Also the reason why you have a mountain of plastic containers at home that you swear you'll reuse someday.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun ('Mag-takeout tayo') or an adjective ('takeout na pagkain'). Can also be spelled 'takeout'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-**take-out** na lang tayo ng hapunan, pagod na ako.","translation":"Let's just get **takeout** for dinner, I'm tired."},{"sentence":"Paki-balot po nito, para sa **take-out**.","translation":"Please wrap this, it's for **takeout**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang biglaan at masakit na paghilab o pamumulikat ng kalamnan, karaniwan sa binti o paa.
original_explanation: That sudden, evil pain in your leg, usually in the middle of the night, that makes you scream and question all your life choices. It's the universe's way of saying, "Hoy, uminom ka ng tubig at kumain ng saging!" That's pulikat. The mortal enemy of swimmers and sleepy people.
usage_notes: While it can refer to any muscle cramp, it's most commonly associated with leg cramps.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Aray! Bigla akong nagka-**pulikat** habang lumalangoy.","translation":"Ouch! I suddenly got a **cramp** while swimming."},{"sentence":"Inunat niya ang kanyang binti para mawala ang **pulikat**.","translation":"He stretched his leg to get rid of the **cramp**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng isang kasuotan na nakapalibot sa leeg.
etymology: Literal na pagsasama ng mga salitang "leeg" at "damit".
original_explanation: The part of your t-shirt that tells the world how old it is. Pag 'yan bacon na (wavy and stretched out), it's time to either downgrade it to "pambahay" (house clothes) or "basahan" (rag). A crisp leeg ng damit is a sign of a new shirt or a very careful owner.
usage_notes: Ang terminong "kuwelyo" (mula sa Espanyol na "cuello") ay mas madalas gamitin para sa mga pormal na damit na may kwelyo tulad ng polo shirt o formal shirt.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bacon na ang **leeg ng damit** mo, palitan mo na 'yan.","translation":"The **neckline of your shirt** is already wavy, you should change it."},{"sentence":"Mas gusto ko ang V-neck kaysa sa bilog na **leeg ng damit**.","translation":"I prefer V-necks over round **necklines**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-alis ng harang, takip, o sagabal upang magkaroon ng daan, makita ang nilalaman, o paganahin ang isang bagay.
etymology: From 'bukas' (open) + '-an' suffix, which creates an object-focused verb.
original_explanation: The magic word you say to your friend who brought snacks: 'Pre, buksan mo na 'yan!' It's the universal command for opening anything from a door, a jar of pickles, your heart (charot!), to a new GrabFood order.
usage_notes: Object-focused verb. The future tense is 'bubuksan', past tense is 'binuksan', and present tense is 'binubuksan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**buksan** mo ang pinto, may tao sa labas.","translation":"Please **open** the door, there's someone outside."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **buksan** ang isip mo sa mga pekeng balita.","translation":"Don't **open** your mind to fake news."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, karaniwang pagkain, na hiniwa nang manipis o maliliit na piraso.
original_explanation: This is what your nanay does to vegetables with expert-level speed. That perfectly shredded papaya for tinola, the thinly sliced onions that make you cry, the julienned carrots for lumpia. If it's been chopped up into bits, it's been ginayat.
usage_notes: Past tense of the verb 'gayatin' (to slice thinly). Often used as an adjective to describe the state of the ingredient.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglagay siya ng **ginayat** na repolyo sa pansit.","translation":"She added **shredded** cabbage to the noodles."},{"sentence":"**Ginayat** niya ang manggang hilaw para isawsaw sa bagoong.","translation":"She **sliced** the unripe mango to dip in shrimp paste."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong aktibo sa pulitika ng isang pamahalaan, karaniwang isang halal na opisyal o kandidato para sa isang pampublikong tanggapan.
original_explanation: Ah, the pulitiko. The person whose face is plastered on every lamppost during election season, promising everything from free Wi-Fi to eternal life. They're masters of speeches, handshakes, and, sometimes, "creative" budget allocation. Love 'em or hate 'em, they run the show.
usage_notes: Can have a slightly negative connotation depending on the context, implying someone who is cunning or opportunistic for political gain.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **pulitiko** ang nangangampanya na para sa susunod na halalan.","translation":"Many **politicians** are already campaigning for the next election."},{"sentence":"Kilala siyang isang tapat na **pulitiko** na walang bahid ng korapsyon.","translation":"He is known as an honest **politician** with no trace of corruption."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng pag-aalala at pag-aasikaso sa kapakanan o damdamin ng iba.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `ma-` at `alalahanin` (isipin o mag-alala para sa), na nagmula sa salitang-ugat na `alaala` (memorya, isipan).
original_explanation: 'Yung kaibigan mong mag-memessage ng "Kumain ka na?" o "Ingat ka pauwi." 'Yung officemate na may dalang extra kape para sa'yo. Basically, the opposite of seenzone. Sila 'yung mga taong may default setting na "care mode: on".
usage_notes: Inilalarawan nito ang katangian ng isang tao. Ipinahihiwatig nito hindi lang ang pag-alala sa mga bagay, kundi ang aktibong pag-iisip at pag-aaruga sa pangangailangan ng iba.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **maalalahanin** na anak si Jose, lagi niyang tinatawagan ang kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"Jose is a **thoughtful** son; he always calls his parents."},{"sentence":"Salamat sa regalo, napaka-**maalalahanin** mo talaga.","translation":"Thanks for the gift, you're so **considerate**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkatuyo at pagtuklap ng ibabaw na bahagi ng balat; balakubak sa katawan.
original_explanation: You know that feeling when you get a sunburn and your skin starts peeling off like a snake? That's *balukiskis*. It's also the dandruff on your shoulders, but for your whole body. It's the enemy of black shirts and the best friend of lotion.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa kalagayan ng pagbabalat o pagtutuklap ng balat ng tao o kaliskis ng isda.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon siya ng **balukiskis** sa braso dahil sa sobrang pagkatuyo ng kanyang balat.","translation":"He had **flaking skin** on his arm because his skin was extremely dry."},{"sentence":"Gumamit ka ng moisturizer para maiwasan ang **balukiskis**.","translation":"Use moisturizer to prevent **flaking skin**."}]

translation: to be able to dodge; to be able to evade
meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang makaiwas sa isang bagay na paparating o isang panganib sa pamamagitan ng mabilis na pagkilos.
original_explanation: What you do when a flying tsinelas from your nanay is headed your way. Or when you see someone from your downline at the mall and you're not in the mood for a 'kamusta, upline?' chat. It's the physical version of `maiiwasan`—a quick, skillful dodge.
usage_notes: Focuses on the physical act of dodging or evading something, often something moving towards the subject.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabilis siyang kumilos kaya niya **nailagan** ang bolang muntik nang tumama sa kanyang mukha.","translation":"He moved quickly so he was **able to dodge** the ball that almost hit his face."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan kong **mailagan** ang tanong niya tungkol sa aking lovelife.","translation":"I tried **to evade** her question about my lovelife."}]

translation: of a different kind; not of the same type
meaning_filipino: Hindi kabilang sa parehong uri, grupo, o klasipikasyon.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `di-` (hindi) at `kauri` (of the same kind).
original_explanation: In high school, this is the feeling of being a rocker kid in a sea of K-pop fans. Or being the only one in the friend group who hasn't seen the latest trending series. You're simply di-kauri. Not necessarily bad, just... different. You don't belong to the same category.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pang-uri na naglalarawan sa pangngalan, o bilang pangngalan na tumutukoy sa isang tao/bagay na may ibang uri.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga ibon at isda ay mga hayop na **di-kauri**.","translation":"Birds and fish are animals **of a different kind**."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam niya ay isa siyang **di-kauri** sa kanilang pamilya dahil sa kanyang mga interes.","translation":"He felt like an **outsider (one of a different kind)** in their family because of his interests."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng aspili na may takip sa dulo upang hindi makatusok at ligtas na maikabit sa damit o tela.
original_explanation: The OG life hack before double-sided tape became a thing. Your lola used this to fix your skirt, your tita used it to secure her malong, and you probably used it to attach your race bib. It's the 'just in case' item in every Filipino mom's purse.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha ka ng **perdible** sa panahian ni Nanay para isara itong butas sa bag ko.","translation":"Get a **safety pin** from Mom's sewing kit to close this hole in my bag."},{"sentence":"Isang malaking **perdible** ang ginamit niya para ipitin ang laylayan ng kanyang pantalon.","translation":"He used a large **safety pin** to hold up the hem of his pants."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang pagtatanghal ng isang musikero o banda, o sa isang pansamantalang trabaho o raket.
etymology: From English 'gig', of uncertain origin, popularized by jazz musicians.
original_explanation: Your "raket" or "sideline." For a musician, it's their tugtugan at a bar in Poblacion. For a BPO agent, it's that freelance writing project they do for extra cash. Having a "gig" means you're hustling, whether on stage or on your laptop.
usage_notes: Used in both the musical performance and freelance work contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **gig** kami mamaya sa 70s Bistro, manood ka.","translation":"We have a **gig** later at 70s Bistro, you should watch."},{"sentence":"Naghahanap ako ng extra **gig** para may pandagdag sa ipon.","translation":"I'm looking for an extra **gig** to add to my savings."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaloob ng basbas o pagpapala sa isang tao, bagay, o lugar.
original_explanation: This is the action verb form of *bendisyon*. It's what the priest does to your new car, your house, or even your pet hamster so it won't get bad vibes. It's also what your lola does to you before a big exam. "Sige na, lola, bendisyunan mo na po ako para pumasa!"
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinapunta nila ang pari upang **bendisyunan** ang kanilang bagong bahay.","translation":"They had the priest come over **to bless** their new house."},{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **bendisyunan** ang pagkain bago kumain.","translation":"Don't forget **to bless** the food before eating."}]

meaning_filipino: May kakayahang mailipat o maipasa sa iba, lalo na ang sakit.
etymology: From 'haway,' an older or regional term for contagion, related to 'hawa.'
original_explanation: This is the less common, slightly more formal cousin of 'nakakahawa'. It's what your doctor might say about the flu. But culturally, we also use 'nakakahawa' for non-illnesses. A yawn can be 'nakakahawa'. A good mood can be 'nakakahawa'. 'Nakahaway' is usually just for the medical stuff.
usage_notes: 'Nakahahawa' is much more common in modern conversation. 'Nakahaway' might be encountered in older texts or more formal/medical contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sakit na bulutong-tubig ay lubhang **nakahaway**.","translation":"The disease chickenpox is highly **contagious**."},{"sentence":"Pinayuhan siyang manatili sa bahay dahil **nakahaway** ang kaniyang ubo.","translation":"He was advised to stay home because his cough was **contagious**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagkuha ng kaalaman o kasanayan, karaniwan sa isang paaralan o sa pamamagitan ng pagbabasa at pagsasanay.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa mo (o dapat mong ginagawa) bago ang exam. 'Yung dahilan kung bakit ka puyat at dependent sa kape. When someone asks "Anong ginagawa mo?" and you're just scrolling through memes, the socially acceptable answer is "Nag-aaral ako."
usage_notes: Can refer to formal education (e.g., attending school) or the specific act of studying for a test or subject.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nag-aaral** si Maria para sa kanyang pagsusulit sa Math.","translation":"Maria **is studying** for her Math exam."},{"sentence":"Saan ka **nag-aaral** ng kolehiyo?","translation":"Where **are you studying** for college?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng isang imahe, ideya, o sitwasyon sa isipan na hindi totoo o hindi nangyayari sa kasalukuyan.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of 'guniguni'. It's the act of daydreaming, fantasizing, or just plain making stuff up in your head. When you're in a boring meeting and you start to *gunigunihin* you're on a beach in Palawan, that's the word. It's the mental escape hatch.
usage_notes: Object-focus verb. The actor-focus version is 'mag-guniguni'. Related to 'guniguni' (imagination/hallucination).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Subukan mong **gunigunihin** ang isang mundong walang gera.","translation":"Try to **imagine** a world without war."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **gunigunihin** ang mga bagay na hindi naman totoo.","translation":"Don't **fantasize** about things that aren't real."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang likido na naging malabo o marumi dahil sa pagkahalo ng mga latak o ibang bagay; maaari ring tumukoy sa isang ideya o plano na naging magulo.
original_explanation: 'Yung kape mong 3-in-1 na tinimpla mo tapos iniwan mo lang. Pagbalik mo, may 'bottom-level' na. That's nalabusaw. It can also be used for plans that get messed up. "Okay na sana 'yung usapan, kaso may sumali sa group chat, ayun, nalabusaw 'yung plano."
usage_notes: Often used for liquids with sediments that have been disturbed. Can also be used figuratively for situations or thoughts that become confused or unclear.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong galawin ang banga at baka **malabusaw** ang tubig.","translation":"Don't move the jar or the water might **become murky**."},{"sentence":"**Nalabusaw** ang isip niya dahil sa dami ng problema.","translation":"His mind **was muddled** because of so many problems."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglapit at paghinto ng isang sasakyang-dagat, tulad ng barko o bapor, sa isang daungan o pantalan.
original_explanation: This is the grand entrance of a ship, like when it finally 'parks' at the pier after a long journey. Think of it as the maritime equivalent of a plane landing or your Grab car finally arriving at your pickup point. It's the 'touchdown' moment for anything that floats.
usage_notes: Used specifically for ships, boats, and other sea vessels arriving at a port or pier.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inabangan ng marami ang **pagduong** ng barkong lulan ang mga balikbayan.","translation":"Many awaited the **docking** of the ship carrying the returning overseas Filipinos."},{"sentence":"Naging maayos ang **pagduong** ng malaking cruise ship sa kabila ng malakas na alon.","translation":"The **docking** of the large cruise ship was smooth despite the strong waves."}]

meaning_filipino: Mabilis na kumalat at naging tanyag sa internet, lalo na sa mga social media platform.
original_explanation: The dream of every TikToker and vlogger. One moment you're just a person dancing awkwardly in your room, the next, you're on everyone's feed and TV Patrol. It's the digital version of 'sikat ka na!' usually for reasons you didn't expect. 'Yung video ng pusang kumakanta, **nagviral** 'yun!'
usage_notes: Past tense. A very modern Taglish word. The present progressive would be 'nagva-viral'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagviral** ang post niya tungkol sa kanyang karanasan sa bus.","translation":"Her post about her experience on the bus **went viral**."},{"sentence":"Simula noong **nagviral** siya, dumami na ang kanyang followers.","translation":"Ever since she **went viral**, her followers have increased."}]

meaning_filipino: Eksakto o tiyak na sa paraang ito; walang labis, walang kulang sa ipinapakita o tinutukoy.
etymology: Reduplication of 'ganito' (like this) with the linker '-ng'.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'copy-paste' in conversation. When you're showing someone a dance move, a recipe, or how your boss looked at you, and you want to be precise. 'No, no, not like that... like THIS.' It's for when 'ganito' (like this) isn't specific enough. 'Ganitung-ganito 'yung itsura ng aso ko nung iniwan ko siya sa bahay.'
usage_notes: Used for emphasis to mean 'exactly like this,' often accompanied by a physical demonstration.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ganitung-ganito** ang paraan ng paggawa ng tamang adobo.","translation":"This is **exactly** the way to make proper adobo."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko sa CCTV, **ganitung-ganito** ang nangyari.","translation":"I saw it on the CCTV, this is **exactly what** happened."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gusali o silid na may simboryo sa kisame kung saan ipinapalabas ang mga imahe ng mga bituin, planeta, at iba pang bagay sa kalawakan para sa layuning pang-edukasyon o libangan.
original_explanation: Yung lugar kung saan ka dinadala ng school nung elementary para sa field trip. Dito mo unang na-realize na hindi lang ikaw ang center of the universe. Parang sinehan pero puro bituin, at mas malamang na makatulog ka habang nag-eexplain yung narrator.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumunta kami sa **planetáryo** para sa aming field trip noong Grade 5.","translation":"We went to the **planetarium** for our field trip in Grade 5."},{"sentence":"Nakakabilib ang palabas tungkol sa mga galaxy sa loob ng **planetáryo**.","translation":"The show about galaxies inside the **planetarium** was amazing."}]

meaning_filipino: Makaramdam ng matindi at biglaang sakit na parang tinutusok o kumikirot.
original_explanation: The feeling when you put alcohol on a fresh wound. Or when your friend's 'joke' hits a little too close to home. That sharp, 'Aray ko!' feeling, whether physical or emotional. 'Bes, umantak 'yung sinabi mo.'
usage_notes: Describes a sharp, piercing, or stinging pain, as opposed to a dull ache. Often used poetically for emotional pain.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umantak** ang hapdi sa sugat ko nang lagyan ko ng alcohol.","translation":"The pain in my wound **stung** when I put alcohol on it."},{"sentence":"Sa puso ko'y **umantak** ang bawat salitang binitiwan niya.","translation":"Every word she uttered caused a **sharp pain** in my heart."}]

translation: to refresh; to renew; to revive (memories)
meaning_filipino: Ang muling pagbuhay o pagbabalik sa isipan ng mga alaala, karanasan, o damdamin mula sa nakaraan.
etymology: Mula sa `pa-` + `sariwa` + `-in`. Isang pandiwa na nangangahulugang "gawing sariwa muli".
original_explanation: 'Yung moment na bigla kang nag-throwback. "Let's panariwain our college memories!" 'Yan 'yung ginagawa niyo sa reunion. O 'di kaya 'pag nakita mo 'yung picture ng ex mo, biglang nag-flashback lahat. You're refreshing the memory, for better or for worse.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit para sa mga alaala, damdamin, o kaalaman, hindi sa mga pisikal na bagay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto naming **panariwain** ang mga masasayang alaala ng aming kabataan.","translation":"We want **to revive** the happy memories of our youth."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **panariwain** ang isang pangakong matagal nang napako.","translation":"It's hard **to renew** a promise that has long been broken."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglapastangan, pagdungis, o pagbaboy sa isang bagay, lugar, o konsepto na itinuturing na banal, sagrado, o malinis.
etymology: From pag- (gerund prefix) + sa- (causative) + salaula (filthy, sordid).
original_explanation: It's what happens when someone leaves their trash on a pristine beach, or draws a mustache on a historical portrait. It's the act of making something pure or respected become dirty or cheap. Like turning a serious discussion into a cheap joke fest.
usage_notes: Carries a strong negative and often moral connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinuturing na **pagsasalaula** sa templo ang kanilang ginawang pag-iingay.","translation":"Their act of making noise was considered a **desecration** of the temple."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagsasalaula** sa pangalan ng pamilya ay isang malaking kasalanan para sa kanila.","translation":"The **defilement** of the family name is a great sin for them."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang literal na kahulugan ay hindi makalabas ng ihi. Sa matalinhagang paraan, ito ay tumutukoy sa isang tao na sobrang abala, takot, o kaba na hindi na makaalis sa kanyang kinalalagyan.
etymology: Mula sa "di-" (not/can't) at "maihi" (to be able to urinate), na galing sa "ihi" (urine).
original_explanation: Literal: 'Yung feeling na naiihi ka na talaga pero walang banyo. Figurative: 'Yung boss mo, binigyan ka ng 3 reports due EOD. Sa sobrang taranta at busy mo, di-maihi ka sa upuan mo. Stuck ka lang sa harap ng laptop mo, praying for a miracle.
usage_notes: The figurative sense is very common in informal and office settings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang kaba ko sa interview, pakiramdam ko ay **di-maihi**.","translation":"I was so nervous during the interview, I felt like I was **(figuratively) unable to move/pee**."},{"sentence":"Dinala siya sa ospital dahil ilang araw na siyang **di-maihi**.","translation":"He was taken to the hospital because he **couldn't urinate** for several days."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pakiusap na ilipat ang isang likido sa ibang lalagyan, isalin ang isang wika, o kopyahin ang isang sulatin o gawa.
original_explanation: The ultimate multi-purpose 'hustle' word. In school: "Pasalin naman ng assignment!" (Let me copy the assignment). In the kitchen: "Pasalin ng sabaw." (Please pour me some soup). To a bilingual friend: "Pasalin nga nito sa English." (Please translate this to English).
usage_notes: The specific meaning (pour, copy, translate) is highly dependent on the context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pasalin** naman ng tubig sa baso ko.","translation":"**Please pour** some water into my glass."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko maintindihan ito, **pasalin** naman sa Tagalog.","translation":"I don't understand this, **please translate** it to Tagalog."}]

translation: to extort from someone; to milk someone for money
meaning_filipino: Kunan ng pera o yaman ang isang tao sa paraang sapilitan o mapanlinlang.
original_explanation: "Huwag kang papayag na huthutan ka lang ng jowa mong walang trabaho." This is the verb form. It's the action of doing the 'huthot'. It's what happens when your 'kaibigan' only messages you when they need to borrow money... again. You're being milked dry.
usage_notes: The object of this verb is the person or entity being extorted.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan nilang **huthutan** ang mga negosyante sa palengke.","translation":"They tried to **extort from** the merchants in the market."},{"sentence":"Napagod na siyang **huthutan** ng kanyang mga kamag-anak.","translation":"She got tired of being **milked for money by** her relatives."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lihim na plano o balak, na karaniwang may masamang layunin; isang paraan o gimik.
etymology: From 'pa-' + 'kana'. The exact origin is debated, but it's related to planning or devising.
original_explanation: This is the Tagalog word for 'Marites-level' plotting. It's the secret plan your friends make to surprise you on your birthday, or the elaborate scheme a teleserye kontrabida cooks up to steal the family fortune. A 'pakana' can be harmless fun or pure evil, but it's always done with some sneaky, clever thinking. It's the 'How to Get Away with Murder' of the Filipino vocabulary.
usage_notes: Often has a negative connotation, implying deceit or trickery, but can also be used neutrally for a clever plan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malaking **pakana** ang lahat para pabagsakin ang kanilang kumpanya.","translation":"It was all one big **scheme** to bring down their company."},{"sentence":"Sino ang may **pakana** ng sorpresang ito?","translation":"Who is the **mastermind** behind this surprise?"}]

meaning_filipino: Sa iba't ibang lugar; kung saan-saan.
original_explanation: Like a Grab driver during rush hour, or your friend who's juggling two different jowas in two different cities. It means "everywhere," "all over the place," or "in various locations." You're basically scattered, like your attention span when your crush walks by.
usage_notes: An idiomatic phrase used to express being in multiple, often unspecified, places.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghahanap ako ng trabaho **dito at doon**, pero wala pa ring mahanap.","translation":"I'm looking for a job **here and there**, but I still can't find one."},{"sentence":"Nagkalat ang mga gamit niya **dito at doon** sa buong kwarto.","translation":"His things are scattered **everywhere** in the whole room."}]

translation: to suppress, to stop, to eradicate
meaning_filipino: Ang paghinto, pagpigil, o pagpuksa sa paglago o pagkalat ng isang bagay na masama, tulad ng krimen, sakit, o rebelyon.
original_explanation: This is what you do to problems. Sugpuin ang corruption! Sugpuin ang pagkalat ng fake news! Sugpuin ang pagnanasa mong mag-text sa ex mo at 3 AM! It's an active, forceful stop, like a superhero landing to halt a villain's evil plan.
usage_notes: This is a verb root. Common forms are 'sugpuin' (to suppress something) and 'masugpo' (to be able to suppress). This is a homonym of 'sugpo' (prawn).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Layunin ng pamahalaan na **sugpuin** ang kahirapan sa bansa.","translation":"The government's goal is to **eradicate** poverty in the country."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating magtulungan upang **sugpuin** ang epidemya.","translation":"We need to work together to **suppress** the epidemic."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghawak nang mahigpit sa isang bagay upang hindi ito mabitawan o mawala.
original_explanation: This is the 'kapit lang bes!' action. It's the way you grip the jeepney handrail during a sudden stop, the way you hold onto your phone in a crowded Divisoria, or the way you cling to your last bit of salary before 'petsa de peligro'. It’s holding on for dear life.
usage_notes: Implies a firm, secure grip. More poetic or literary than 'paghawak'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mahigpit na **pagtaban** niya sa lubid ang nagligtas sa kanya mula sa pagkakahulog.","translation":"His firm **grasp** on the rope saved him from falling."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapang pangkarpintero na hugis "L", ginagamit sa pagsukat at pagguhit ng mga anggulong 90-digri o tamang kanto.
original_explanation: This is your friendly neighborhood karpintero's special ruler. Hindi siya basta-bastang ruler, hugis 'L' siya para masigurong 'squared' o 'sakto sa kanto' ang ginagawa mong lamesa o bintana. It's for making sure things are perfectly angled, unlike your love life.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa karpinterya, konstruksiyon, at pagguhit na teknikal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ng karpintero ang **eskuwadra** upang matiyak na tuwid ang kanto ng kabinet.","translation":"The carpenter used the **try square** to ensure the corner of the cabinet was straight."},{"sentence":"Pakiabot ng **eskuwadra**, sabi ni tatay habang gumagawa ng lamesa.","translation":"Please pass the **L-square**, said dad while making a table."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa iba't ibang lugar; kung saan-saan.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng "dini" (isang lumang anyo ng "dito") at "doon" (there).
original_explanation: This is the more ~poetic~ version of "dito at doon." It's like when you're trying to find a specific item at the ukay-ukay, you look dini at doon. Or when you're telling a story about your travels: "Nagpunta kami dini at doon." It's the old-school way of saying "everywhere."
usage_notes: Ang 'Dini' ay isang luma/mas pormal/patula na kasingkahulugan ng 'dito'. Ang parirala ay hindi gaanong karaniwan sa kaswal na pag-uusap kaysa sa 'dito at doon' o 'kung saan-saan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkalat ang kanyang mga gamit **dini at doon** sa loob ng silid.","translation":"His things were scattered **here and there** inside the room."},{"sentence":"May mga bulaklak na tumutubo **dini at doon** sa parang.","translation":"There are flowers growing **here and there** in the field."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa maraming relihiyon at mitolohiya, ito ang lugar ng walang hanggang kaparusahan at pagdurusa para sa mga masasama pagkatapos ng kamatayan.
original_explanation: Yung sinasabi ng nanay mo na pupuntahan mo 'pag 'di ka sumunod. Figuratively, ito 'yung traffic sa EDSA tuwing rush hour, 'yung pila sa government office, o 'yung init ng panahon sa Pinas kapag summer. 'Grabe, parang **impyerno** sa init!'
usage_notes: Isang salitang may malakas na konotasyong relihiyoso at metaporikal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayon sa banal na kasulatan, ang mga makasalanan ay mapupunta sa **impyerno**.","translation":"According to the holy scriptures, sinners will go to **hell**."},{"sentence":"Naging **impyerno** ang buhay niya mula nang malulong siya sa droga.","translation":"His life became a living **hell** ever since he got addicted to drugs."}]

meaning_filipino: Kapangyarihan o karapatang mag-utos o mamahala. Maaari ring tumukoy sa pangangalaga o kustodiya sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: A Spanish-era word for 'power' that sounds like something a telenovela villain would say. 'Nasa aking mga kamay ang lahat ng poder!' Today, it's mostly used in legal or formal contexts, like when talking about 'power of attorney' or who has custody ('nasa poder ni...') of the kids after a messy breakup. It's the vintage version of 'kapangyarihan'.
usage_notes: Primarily used in legal jargon ('poder ng abogado') or very formal, somewhat archaic speech. The word 'kapangyarihan' is the more common and general term for 'power'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bata ay nasa **poder** ng kanyang ina.","translation":"The child is in the custody (lit. **power**) of his mother."},{"sentence":"Ibinigay sa kanya ang buong **poder** upang pamunuan ang kumpanya.","translation":"He was given full **authority** to lead the company."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa isang kompetisyon, ito ang yugto o laban bago ang kampeonato o pinal na labanan. Ang mananalo rito ay aabante sa finals.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na 'semifinal', na binaybay sa paraang Filipino.
original_explanation: The "malapit na pero hindi pa" stage of any competition. Dito pinakamatindi ang kaba kasi isang panalo na lang, finals na! Parang sa love life, ito yung "exclusively dating" stage. Hindi pa kayo opisyal, pero malapit na. The ultimate "sana all" moment is getting past the semipaynal.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng palakasan (sports), mga patimpalak (contests), at mga palabas sa telebisyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napasok ng Gilas Pilipinas ang **semipaynal** ng FIBA Asia Cup.","translation":"Gilas Pilipinas made it to the **semifinals** of the FIBA Asia Cup."},{"sentence":"Sino kaya ang maglalaban sa **semipaynal** ng singing contest?","translation":"I wonder who will compete in the **semifinal** of the singing contest?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapatirapa o paglalagay ng isa o dalawang tuhod sa sahig o lupa, karaniwan bilang tanda ng paggalang, pagsamba, o pagsusumamo.
original_explanation: What you do when you're proposing (sana all!), begging your parents to let you go to that concert, or praying to pass your exams kahit 'di ka nag-review. It's the ultimate gesture of "please" or "sorry na po."
usage_notes: Can be an act of worship, respect, proposal, or punishment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagluhod** ay tanda ng kanyang taos-pusong pagsisisi.","translation":"His **kneeling** was a sign of his sincere repentance."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging may batayan, lohikal, at naaayon sa tamang pangangatwiran.
etymology: Nagmula sa `pagka-` (katangian ng) at `makatwiran` (may katwiran), na galing sa salitang `katwiran` (rason), na ugat sa `tuwid` (straight).
original_explanation: Ito yung 'make it make sense' moment mo. Yung ability mong mag-explain sa nanay mo kung bakit ka ginabi nang hindi siya nagagalit. It's the logic behind your 'budol' buys ('Kailangan ko 'to for self-care!'). When you're arguing with your jowa, and you try to find the logic (the pagkamakatwiran) in their 'tampo', but sometimes, there's none.
usage_notes: Malapit na kaugnay ng `pagkamakatarungan` ngunit mas nakatuon sa lohikal na batayan o rason kaysa sa pagiging patas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Walang **pagkamakatwiran** ang kanyang mga akusasyon.","translation":"There is no **reasonableness** in his accusations."},{"sentence":"Timbangin natin ang **pagkamakatwiran** ng bawat panig.","translation":"Let's weigh the **rationality** of each side."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao, bagay, o serbisyo na nakatali sa isang kontrata para sa isang tiyak na panahon.
original_explanation: Ito yung status mo sa trabaho na parang 'it's complicated'. May trabaho ka for 5 months, pero after that, 'Thank you, next!'. Walang benefits, walang security of tenure, pero at least may sahod... for now. The reality of 'endo' (end of contract).
usage_notes: A politically and socially charged term in the Philippines due to labor issues surrounding 'endo' or end-of-contract practices. Can also function as a noun referring to the worker.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bilang isang **kontratado** na manggagawa, laging may pangamba na hindi ma-renew ang kanyang kontrata.","translation":"As a **contractual** worker, there is always the fear that his contract will not be renewed."},{"sentence":"Ang serbisyong ito ay isinagawa ng isang **kontratado** na ahensya.","translation":"This service was performed by a **contracted** agency."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang anyong lupa na napapaligiran ng tubig.
original_explanation: Ang rason kung bakit 7,107 (or 7,641 na daw) ang bilang sa Pilipinas. Ito yung ultimate travel goal mo tuwing summer—Boracay, Palawan, Siargao, name it! Kapag sinabing "Tara, mag-isla tayo," hindi ibig sabihin bibili ka ng lupa, kundi magbe-beach trip.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Pilipinas ay binubuo ng libo-libong magagandang **isla**.","translation":"The Philippines is composed of thousands of beautiful **islands**."},{"sentence":"Pangarap kong tumira sa isang tahimik na **isla** pagtanda ko.","translation":"It's my dream to live on a quiet **island** when I get old."}]

translation: a feud; a mutual fight; a brawl
meaning_filipino: Isang sitwasyon ng palitan ng away o hidwaan sa pagitan ng mga grupo o indibidwal.
original_explanation: This is the '-an' suffix doing its magic, implying a reciprocal or mutual action. It's not just a one-sided fight; it's a full-on feud where everyone's involved. Think Montagues vs. Capulets, but make it barangay level. Or that legendary fan war between two K-pop groups online. That's an 'awayan'.
usage_notes: Implies a recurring or mutual conflict, often involving more than two people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matagal na ang **awayan** ng dalawang pamilyang iyon.","translation":"The **feud** between those two families has been going on for a long time."},{"sentence":"Sana ay matigil na ang **awayan** sa social media.","translation":"I hope the mutual **fighting** on social media stops."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging maawain at may habag sa kapwa; ang pagpapakita ng awa at pag-unawa sa paghihirap ng iba.
original_explanation: This is your inner Angel Locsin or your friend who always says "libre ko na" when you're broke. It's that feeling that makes you adopt a stray cat, give your last piece of chicharon to a friend, or forgive someone who ghosted you. It's having a soft heart in a world that's often hardcore.
usage_notes: Carries a strong, often religious or deeply moral connotation. It's a level above simple pity (`awa`).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinakita niya ang kanyang **pagkamahabagin** sa pamamagitan ng pagtulong sa mga nasalanta ng bagyo.","translation":"He showed his **compassion** by helping the victims of the typhoon."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkamahabagin** ay isang birtud na dapat taglayin ng lahat.","translation":"**Compassion** is a virtue that everyone should possess."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marahan at magiliw na paghaplos sa isang bagay, tao, o hayop.
original_explanation: This is that gentle, loving touch. Like when you're petting your doggo and he's super happy, or when your lola strokes your hair. It's the S.O. version of 'haplos'. The verb form of "there, there."
usage_notes: Implies a gentle, often affectionate, stroking motion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **humimas** sa balahibo ng kanyang alagang pusa.","translation":"She likes to **stroke** the fur of her pet cat."},{"sentence":"**Humimas** siya sa likod ko para pagaanin ang aking loob.","translation":"He **caressed** my back to comfort me."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maliit na mamal na may mahahabang tainga, maikling buntot, at kilala sa mabilis nitong pagdami.
original_explanation: The OG pet na mabilis dumami, parang chismis sa office. Before cats and dogs dominated your feed, these fluffy creatures were the stars of every kid's birthday party magic show. Cute, but high-maintenance, just like your standards in dating.
usage_notes: Ang 'kuneho' ay isang karaniwang alternatibong baybay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang alaga niyang **koneho** ay napakabilis tumakbo.","translation":"His pet **rabbit** runs very fast."},{"sentence":"Maraming **koneho** sa bukid ng lolo niya.","translation":"There are many **rabbits** in his grandfather's farm."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa sandali ring iyon; agad-agad; walang pagkaantala.
original_explanation: This is the 'shala' or high-falutin' way of saying 'agad'. You won't hear this in the palengke, but you'll see it in old books, the Bible, or maybe in a Lolo's story. It means 'right away, no questions asked'. Think of it as the formal, literary version of 'ASAP'.
usage_notes: Itinuturing na pormal o pampanitikan. Ang 'agad' ang karaniwang katumbas sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kapagdaka**'y tumayo ang binata at umalis.","translation":"**Immediately**, the young man stood up and left."},{"sentence":"Nang marinig ang utos, **kapagdaka** siyang kumilos.","translation":"When he heard the order, he acted **at once**."}]

meaning_filipino: Gumawa ng isang maikli, matinis, at paulit-ulit na tunog, tulad ng pagpapatunog ng mga daliri, pag-aapoy ng kahoy, o pag-type sa keyboard.
original_explanation: The sound effect verb! It's making that 'tiktik' or clicking noise. Think of the sound of your knuckles cracking, the sound of firewood popping in a fire, or even the sound of your ballpen being clicked repeatedly during a boring meeting. That's 'magpalagitik'. It's the sound of impatience or a good campfire.
usage_notes: An onomatopoeic word, where the word itself imitates the sound it describes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magpalagitik** ng daliri, nakakairita.","translation":"Don't **make a clicking sound** with your fingers, it's irritating."},{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **magpalagitik** ang tuyong kahoy sa apoy.","translation":"The dry wood in the fire started **to make a snapping sound**."}]

meaning_filipino: Paramihin ang bilang sa pamamagitan ng pagdaragdag ng paulit-ulit; magparami.
original_explanation: The official term for when chismis spreads like wildfire in the office group chat. One person tells two friends, and then they tell two friends... It's also what your expenses do right after payday.
usage_notes: A more formal or technical term for 'multiply' compared to 'magparami'. Often used in mathematical or scientific contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **magmultiplika** ng ating efforts para maabot ang quota.","translation":"We need to **multiply** our efforts to reach the quota."},{"sentence":"Ang bacteria ay mabilis na **magmultiplika** sa mainit na panahon.","translation":"Bacteria will **multiply** quickly in hot weather."}]

translation: to be unlucky; to experience misfortune
meaning_filipino: Ang makaranas ng kamalasan, kasawian, o hindi magandang kapalaran.
original_explanation: This is when you leave the house and it starts raining, you miss your jeep, your data runs out, and you realize you left your wallet at home. You're not just unlucky, you're 'nagmamalas'. It's the universe deciding to throw you a series of unfortunate events, Filipino-style. The kind of day that makes you say, 'Lord, what did I do?'
usage_notes: Often used to describe a string of bad luck or a particularly unfortunate event.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naku, mukhang **magmamalas** ako ngayong araw, naiwan ko ang wallet ko.","translation":"Oh no, it seems I'm **going to be unlucky** today, I left my wallet."},{"sentence":"**Nagmalas** ang buong team sa huling laro nila.","translation":"The whole team **experienced misfortune** in their last game."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malakas na tunog o epekto na dulot ng pagsabog, pagkasira, o biglaang pag-igting ng isang bagay. Sa kolokyal na gamit, tumutukoy din ito sa masamang amoy ng kili-kili.
original_explanation: Can mean a literal explosion, like a firecracker ('paputok'). But in modern Filipino slang, it's the *other* kind of explosion: body odor, specifically from the armpits. 'May putok ka' is the not-so-subtle way of saying someone needs a stronger deodorant. It's a social grenade you never want thrown at you.
usage_notes: Maaari ring tumukoy sa 'bitak' sa ibabaw ng isang mahusay na pagkalutong tinapay, tulad ng pandesal. Ang slang na kahulugan para sa amoy-kili-kili ay napakakaraniwan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang malakas na **putok** mula sa kabilang kanto.","translation":"I heard a loud **explosion** from the other corner."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, **putok** lang iyon ng gulong.","translation":"Don't worry, that was just a tire **bursting**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mo na atang gumamit ng deodorant, amoy **putok** ka.","translation":"I think you need to use deodorant, you have **body odor**."}]

translation: not really, not exactly, on the contrary
meaning_filipino: Isang panagot na ginagamit upang magbigay ng banayad na pagtutol, paglilinaw, o pagkontra sa isang naunang pahayag o inaasahan.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng 'hindi' (not) at 'naman' (isang kataga na ginagamit para sa diin, pagkontra, o paggalang).
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino soft "no." It's how you politely disagree without being confrontational. "Maganda ba 'yung movie?" "Uhm, **hindi naman**..." It's the verbal equivalent of a shrug and a slight head tilt. It's not a hard 'no', it's a 'no' with a side of 'it's complicated' and 'I don't want to hurt your feelings'.
usage_notes: Lubhang karaniwan sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap. Ang kahulugan nito ay lubos na nakadepende sa tono at konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"\"Galit ka ba?\" \"Ay, **hindi naman**.\"","translation":"\"Are you angry?\" \"Oh, **not really**.\""},{"sentence":"Akala ko mahirap ang exam, pero **hindi naman** pala.","translation":"I thought the exam would be hard, but it turns out it was **not really**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan na ikinakabit sa dulo ng baril o tambutso ng sasakyan upang bawasan ang ingay na nalilikha nito.
original_explanation: That thing you see in action movies that makes a gunshot go "pfft" instead of "BANG!" Also refers to the muffler on a car or motorcycle that keeps it from sounding like a beast waking up the whole neighborhood at 3 AM. If your officemate is too loud, you wish you could put a 'silensyador' on them.
usage_notes: Used for both firearms and vehicle exhausts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng **silensyador** ang tambutso ng motor mo dahil sobrang ingay.","translation":"Your motorcycle's exhaust pipe needs a **muffler** because it's too noisy."},{"sentence":"Gumamit ng baril na may **silensyador** ang kontrabida sa pelikula.","translation":"The villain in the movie used a gun with a **silencer**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na termino para sa isang bata o kabataan na nagmula sa isang napakayamang pamilya.
original_explanation: 'Yung kaklase mong laging naka-Starbucks, ang baon ay credit card, at ang "commute" ay GrabCar papunta sa driver niya. Sila 'yung nagrereklamo na "boring sa bahay" kaya mag-a-out of town, habang ikaw nagrereklamo na "boring sa bahay" kaya lilipat ka lang sa kabilang upuan.
usage_notes: Ginagamit bilang isang impormal na paglalarawan at maaaring may dalang inggit, paghanga, o bahagyang pangungutya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tingnan mo ang sasakyan niya, halatang **richkid**.","translation":"Look at his car, he's obviously a **rich kid**."},{"sentence":"Hindi lahat ng **richkid** ay mayabang.","translation":"Not all **rich kids** are arrogant."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tiyak na lugar, panig, o direksyon.
original_explanation: A more poetic way of saying "lugar" or "pwesto." Parang sa Waze, instead of "turn left," it's "sa **dako** roon." It sounds more formal, like something you'd hear in a fantasy movie or from your lola. "Saang **dako** ka man ng mundo, 'wag mo akong kalimutan." #Hugot
usage_notes: Often used in phrases like "sa lahat ng dako" (everywhere) or "sa dakong iyon" (in that place/direction).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagmula sila sa iba't ibang **dako** ng Pilipinas.","translation":"They came from different **parts** of the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Pumunta ka sa **dako**ng iyon at hanapin mo ang nawawalang aso.","translation":"Go in that **direction** and look for the missing dog."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang grapikong representasyon ng datos na gumagamit ng mga linya, tuldok, o bar upang ipakita ang ugnayan sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang baryabol.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung drawing na may X at Y axis na nagpapakita kung paakyat (sales), pababa (grades mo), o stagnant (love life mo) ang isang bagay. Favorite visual aid ng mga boss sa BPO at ng mga teacher sa Math.
usage_notes: A formal or academic term. 'Graph' or 'chart' is more common in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinakita sa **talangguhit** ang pagtaas ng kaso ng dengue.","translation":"The **graph** showed the increase in dengue cases."},{"sentence":"Gumawa ka ng **talangguhit** para mas madaling maintindihan ang datos.","translation":"Make a **chart** so the data is easier to understand."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian o kalagayan ng pagiging magalang; pagpapakita ng paggalang o kortesiya.
original_explanation: The opposite of 'bastos.' It's using 'po' and 'opo,' not interrupting when someone's speaking, and generally not being a jerk. It's the formal behavior you switch on when meeting your partner's parents for the first time. The noun form of 'magalang.'
usage_notes: Often used in formal contexts to describe the quality of being respectful. 'Paggalang' is the act of respecting, while 'kagalangan' is the quality of being respectful.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinakita niya ang kanyang **kagalangan** sa pamamagitan ng pagmano sa mga nakatatanda.","translation":"He showed his **respectfulness** by doing the 'mano' gesture to the elders."},{"sentence":"Ang **kagalangan** ay isang mahalagang birtud na dapat ituro sa mga bata.","translation":"**Courtesy** is an important virtue that should be taught to children."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matining at malakas na tunog o sigaw, karaniwang dahil sa takot, tuwa, o sakit.
original_explanation: The sound a fangirl makes when she sees her K-pop bias. Also the sound your brakes make when you suddenly stop. Or the sound you make when you see a rat in the kitchen. A high-pitched scream that's 50% excitement, 50% terror.
usage_notes: Often used with a verb like 'umirit' (to shriek) or as a root in 'napa-irit' (caused to shriek).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malakas na **irit** ang narinig mula sa mga nanonood ng horror movie.","translation":"A loud **shriek** was heard from those watching the horror movie."},{"sentence":"Napa-**irit** siya sa tuwa nang makita ang regalo.","translation":"She let out a **squeal** of joy when she saw the gift."}]

translation: To entertain; to give attention to (often negative)
meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng pansin o pag-aksayahan ng panahon ang isang tao, bagay, o sitwasyon, na kadalasan ay may negatibong konotasyon o itinuturing na hindi ka-lebel.
etymology: From `patol` (to engage, to deal with) + `-an` (locative/object-focus suffix).
original_explanation: The classic advice from your nanay when someone's being an idiot online: "Huwag mo nang patulan." It means don't stoop to their level, don't engage, don't feed the trolls. To patulan something is to give it your precious time and energy, which it probably doesn't deserve.
usage_notes: The root word 'patol' is rarely used on its own. The verb 'patulan' is very common, especially as a command in the negative ('huwag patulan').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit anong pamba-bash ang gawin nila, hindi ko sila **patutulan**.","translation":"No matter how much they bash me, I won't **give them any attention**."},{"sentence":"Bakit mo pa kasi **pinatulan** ang tsismis? Lalo lang lumaki ang gulo.","translation":"Why did you even **entertain** the gossip? The conflict just got bigger."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pagkain na gawa sa namuong gatas ng balatong (soybean) na karaniwang piniprito o isinasahog sa iba't ibang lutuin.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Hokkien na "tāu-koa" (豆干), na nangangahulugang "dried bean curd".
original_explanation: The OG plant-based protein ng Pinas. Before all the hipsters discovered it, we were already frying it, dousing it in soy sauce for Tokwa't Baboy, or throwing it in lugaw. It's the chameleon of the palengke, absorbing whatever flavor you throw at it.
usage_notes: Isang pangunahing sangkap sa lutuing Pilipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pabili po ng isang bloke ng **tokwa**.","translation":"Can I buy one block of **tofu**, please?"},{"sentence":"Masarap ang **tokwa**'t baboy na pulutan.","translation":"**Tofu** and pork is a delicious appetizer."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na may positibong pananaw sa buhay at laging umaasa sa magandang kahihinatnan ng mga bagay-bagay.
original_explanation: Ito yung kaibigan mong kahit na-ghost na, sinasabi pa ring, 'Baka low-batt lang siya.' Kahit traffic sa EDSA, 'At least may time mag-isip.' Sila yung laging 'good vibes lang' ang mantra at naniniwalang may silver lining kahit sa pinakamadilim na ulap ng anxiety mo.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap, madalas sa pormang Ingles nito. Ang katumbas sa Tagalog ay "taong may positibong pananaw."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit maraming problema, nananatili siyang isang **optimist**.","translation":"Despite many problems, she remains an **optimist**."}]

translation: to cause to stagger; to make someone wobble
meaning_filipino: Gawing hindi matatag o alanganin ang pagtayo o paglakad ng isang tao; paganapang-goyin.
original_explanation: Imagine you're in a packed MRT and it suddenly brakes. That feeling of almost falling over? You were *pinasuray*. It's also what happens after one too many shots of tequila. Your walk becomes a "dance" – you're being *pinapasuray* by the alcohol.
usage_notes: The root word `suray` is not very common on its own, but `pasurayin` or `sumuray` are understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang isang malakas na suntok ay sapat na upang **pasurayin** ang boksingero.","translation":"One strong punch is enough **to make** the boxer **stagger**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpadala sa mga problema na maaaring **pasurayin** ang iyong pananampalataya.","translation":"Do not give in to problems that can **make** your faith **wobble**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang magalang na tawag para sa isang babaeng wala pang asawa; isang dalaga.
original_explanation: Ito ang formal na "Miss" bago pa nauso ang "Ma'am/Sir". Ito ang itatawag sa'yo sa mga formal events, sa mga beauty pageant (hello, Binibining Pilipinas!), o ng lolo mong makata. It's the classy way to address a young woman, giving off major dalagang Pilipina vibes.
usage_notes: Used as a title of respect, similar to the English "Miss". It is the counterpart to "Ginoo" (Mr.) and "Ginang" (Mrs.).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magandang umaga, **Binibini** Cruz.","translation":"Good morning, **Miss** Cruz."},{"sentence":"Siya ang pambato ng aming bayan para sa titulong **Binibining** Pilipinas.","translation":"She is our town's candidate for the **Miss** Philippines title."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang walang tigil o labis na pagsasalita, kadalasan tungkol sa mga bagay na hindi gaanong mahalaga.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you have too much coffee and the chismis is piping hot. It's that one person in the Zoom meeting who just won't stop talking. It's the verbal equivalent of a machine gun firing words instead of bullets. Basically, being a daldalero/daldalera on steroids.
usage_notes: Has a slightly negative connotation, implying that the talking is excessive or annoying.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumigil ka na sa ka-**pagdudumaldal** at tapusin mo ang iyong trabaho.","translation":"Stop **chattering** and finish your work."},{"sentence":"Kapag nagsama ang magkaibigan, tiyak na **magdudumaldal** sila buong araw.","translation":"When the friends get together, they will surely **talk excessively** all day."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglalagay ng gawgaw o almirol sa mga damit upang ito ay tumigas kapag natuyo at naplantsa.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'almidonar' (mag-almirol), na nagmula sa 'almidón' (gawgaw o starch).
original_explanation: This is the OG way of making your school uniform collar and polo stand up straight, stiffer than your strict tito. It's the secret weapon of nanays everywhere to make clothes look crisp and new, like you're ready for a job interview even if you're just going to the sari-sari store. It's basically fabric hairspray.
usage_notes: Ang pandiwa ay 'almirulan' (gawing may almirol ang isang bagay). Ang pangngalan para sa starch ay 'almirol' o 'gawgaw'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Almirulan** mo ang kuwelyo ng polo ko para magandang tingnan.","translation":"Please **starch** the collar of my polo shirt so it looks good."},{"sentence":"Ang mga damit na in**almirulan** ay mas madaling plantsahin.","translation":"Clothes that have been **starched** are easier to iron."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nakatalaga upang magbantay o magprotekta sa isang lugar, tao, o bagay; isang tanod.
original_explanation: Your friendly neighborhood guwardiya at the village gate or the BPO building entrance. They're the ones who check your ID, log your temperature, and sometimes know more about the office chismis than anyone else.
usage_notes: A more formal or literary term for a guard. 'Guwardiya' or 'tanod' are more common in everyday speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang matapat na **balantay** ay hindi natulog buong gabi.","translation":"The loyal **sentinel** did not sleep the whole night."},{"sentence":"Naglagay sila ng **balantay** sa tarangkahan ng palasyo.","translation":"They placed a **guard** at the palace gate."}]

meaning_filipino: Isa pang kolokyal at balbal na anyo ng salitang 'ganoon,' na may kahulugang 'sa ganoong paraan.'
etymology: A colloquial corruption of 'ganoon' (like that), existing as a popular alternative to 'ganern' in internet and youth culture.
original_explanation: The slightly more 'pabebe' or cuter cousin of 'ganern.' If 'ganern' is a smirk, 'ganoin' is a wink. It's used in the exact same way, just with a different flavor of sass. Often used in a playful, almost teasing manner. 'Ay, in-unfriend ka niya? Hurtful ganoin.'
usage_notes: Highly informal and interchangeable with 'ganern.' The choice between them is purely stylistic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kunyari ka pa, pero kinikilig ka naman. **Ganoin**!","translation":"You're just pretending, but you're actually giddy. **Like that**!"},{"sentence":"Mag-aaral daw siya mabuti, pero naka-online games. **Ganoin**?","translation":"He said he'd study hard, but he's playing online games. **Is that how it is**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paggisi o paghiwa sa isang bagay, karaniwan ay papel o tela, gamit ang mga kamay.
original_explanation: The OG stress reliever before fidget spinners. It's the sound your ex's love letters make, or what you do to a parking ticket in your mind. Also, the first step in making *pabalat* for your school books.
usage_notes: Refers to the action itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang marahas na **pagpunit** niya sa sulat ay nagpakita ng kanyang galit.","translation":"His violent **tearing** of the letter showed his anger."},{"sentence":"Maingat ang kanyang **pagpunit** ng resibo.","translation":"His **act of tearing** the receipt was careful."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit, magaspang, at matigas na bukol sa balat na karaniwang sanhi ng isang uri ng virus.
original_explanation: That unwanted skin guest that pops up and refuses to leave, like a 'Marites' neighbor. It's not a pimple; it's tougher and more stubborn. Sometimes associated with folklore, like getting one from pointing at rainbows or playing with frogs.
usage_notes: A common, non-technical term for a wart. 'Kulugo' is a more common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May tumubong **butig** sa kanyang daliri.","translation":"A **wart** grew on his finger."},{"sentence":"Sabi ng matatanda, huwag daw ituturo ang bahaghari para hindi ka magka-**butig**.","translation":"The elders say you shouldn't point at a rainbow so you won't get a **wart**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang halaman na itinanim at pinalalaki sa loob ng isang lalagyan na tinatawag na paso.
original_explanation: The perfect solution for condo dwellers and people with zero backyard space who still want to join the Plantita/Plantito craze. It's a plant with its own personal, portable real estate. You can move it around to "chase the sun" like it's some kind of celebrity.
usage_notes: A descriptive phrase, not a compound word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno na ng mga **halaman sa paso** ang kanyang balkonahe.","translation":"Her balcony is now full of **potted plants**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nangangahulugang ganap, buo, walang kulang, o husto.
original_explanation: The 100% of Tagalog. It's not 99.9%, it's not 'almost there'. It's the full charge, the whole package, the 'I-give-my-all' of words. When you trust someone 'lubos,' you're giving them access to your Netflix and your FB password. It’s total commitment.
usage_notes: Often precedes an adjective or verb to signify completeness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lubos** ang aking pasasalamat sa iyong kabutihan.","translation":"My gratitude for your kindness is **absolute**."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko pa **lubos** na nauunawaan ang sitwasyon.","translation":"I do not yet **fully** understand the situation."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paghahanda at paggamit ng lupa para sa pagtatanim; ang proseso ng pagpapayaman o pagpapaunlad ng isip, sining, o kasanayan.
original_explanation: The process of making something better, whether it's land or your mind. In farming, it's tilling the soil and planting seeds. In life, it's the 'grind' – reading books, learning a skill, developing good habits. It's the 'how' you get to be 'kultibado'.
usage_notes: Used in both agricultural and intellectual/personal development contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang tamang **kultibasyon** ng lupa para sa masaganang ani.","translation":"Proper **cultivation** of the land is important for a bountiful harvest."},{"sentence":"Ang **kultibasyon** ng kaalaman ay isang panghabambuhay na gawain.","translation":"The **cultivation** of knowledge is a lifelong task."}]

translation: to send word; to have news spread
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapahatid ng isang mensahe o impormasyon sa iba, o pagiging sanhi na kumalat ang isang balita.
original_explanation: Like when you ask your Marites friend to "accidentally" let your ex know you're doing great. You're not the one spreading the chismis, you're just *magpabalita* through a designated agent. It's strategic information dissemination, 2026 style.
usage_notes: Can mean to actively send news or to passively cause news to be known.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagpabalita** si Aling Nena sa kanyang mga anak na uuwi na siya mula sa abroad.","translation":"Aling Nena **sent word** to her children that she is coming home from abroad."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang gagawa ng iskandalo kung ayaw mong **magpabalita** sa buong barangay.","translation":"Don't cause a scandal if you don't want to **have news about you spread** throughout the whole village."}]

meaning_filipino: May kakayahan o kapangyarihang makahikayat o makapagpabago sa pag-iisip o kilos ng iba.
original_explanation: Sila 'yung mga "influencer" sa social media, o 'yung tita mong laging may "recommendation" kung sinong doktor ang magaling. Kung kaya niyang i-convince ang buong barkada na kumain sa isang lugar na siya lang ang may gusto, maimpluwensiya siya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isa siyang **maimpluwensiya** na negosyante sa aming bayan.","translation":"He is an **influential** businessman in our town."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga sinulat ay naging **maimpluwensiya** sa maraming kabataan.","translation":"His writings became **influential** to many young people."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng higaan na yari sa lona o matibay na tela na nakabitin sa isang balangkas na maaaring itiklop.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'tijeras' (gunting), marahil dahil sa itsura nitong nagkrus na mga paa na parang gunting kapag itinitiklop.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung kama ng mga bisita na bigla na lang sumusulpot pag may darating na kamag-anak from the province. O kaya 'yung higaan mo sa evacuation center. It's the "I wasn't expecting you, but here's a bed" of Filipino hospitality. Folds up neatly for when the drama is over.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha ka ng **tiheras** sa bodega para may matulugan si Tita mo.","translation":"Get the **cot** from the storage room so your Aunt has a place to sleep."},{"sentence":"Ayokong matulog sa **tiheras**, masakit sa likod.","translation":"I don't want to sleep on the **cot**, it hurts my back."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bahagi ng sasakyan na hugis bilog at ginagamit ng drayber upang kontrolin ang direksyon nito.
original_explanation: What the driver holds onto in a jeepney to keep you from crashing. It's like your life—you should be holding the 'manibela' to control where you're going. Don't let someone else drive your future! Unless it's Waze, then maybe listen.
usage_notes: A common loanword used in the context of any vehicle with a steering wheel.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang kapit niya sa **manibela** habang nagmamaneho sa matarik na daan.","translation":"He had a tight grip on the **steering wheel** while driving on the steep road."},{"sentence":"Ang init ng **manibela** dahil nababad sa araw ang kotse.","translation":"The **steering wheel** is so hot because the car was left out in the sun."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasama o kaibigan sa pag-eehersisyo, lalo na sa pagbubuhat ng mga pabigat sa gym.
etymology: From 'batak' (to pull, to stretch, slang for workout) with the prefix 'ka-', denoting a companion or partner in an activity.
original_explanation: Your official spotter, not just for weights, but for life's burdens. Sila yung kasama mong mag-reklamo na 'ang sakit ng katawan ko,' pero bukas, nasa gym na naman. Your 'accountabili-buddy' for achieving that 'goal bod' or just for taking mirror selfies post-workout.
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of fitness and gym culture. A modern, informal term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumunta ako sa gym kasama ang **kabatakan** ko.","translation":"I went to the gym with my **workout partner**."},{"sentence":"Si Mark ang lagi kong **kabatakan** tuwing umaga.","translation":"Mark is always my **gym buddy** every morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbaluktot ng katawan upang takpan o protektahan ang isang bagay; ang paglikom o pagyakap sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: Imagine a mother hen spreading her wings to cover her chicks, or you hunching over your phone on the jeepney to hide your screen from the chismosa beside you. That act of covering, arching over, or enveloping is 'kulukob'.
usage_notes: Used in its inflected forms like 'kinukulukuban' (is covering) or 'kulukubin' (to cover).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kinukulukuban** ng inahing manok ang kanyang mga sisiw.","translation":"The mother hen **is stooping over** her chicks."},{"sentence":"**Kulukubin** mo ng iyong katawan ang bata para hindi mabasa ng ulan.","translation":"**Envelop** the child with your body so they don't get wet from the rain."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpunta sa mas mababang posisyon, lebel, o halaga; o ang resulta ng naturang akto.
etymology: The `pag-` prefix nominalizes the root `baba` (down, low).
original_explanation: That feeling when your sweldo is gone five days after payday—that's the rapid **pagbaba** of your bank account. It's also what happens to your social battery after a long family reunion, or the sudden drop in your WiFi signal during an important Zoom call.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical descent, getting off a vehicle, or a decrease in value, level, or quantity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ramdam na ramdam ang **pagbaba** ng presyo ng bilihin.","translation":"The **decrease** in the prices of goods is very noticeable."},{"sentence":"Naging mabilis ang kaniyang **pagbaba** mula sa tuktok ng bundok.","translation":"His **descent** from the top of the mountain was fast."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa dalawa o higit pang tao na may magkasamang pagmamay-ari o interes sa isang negosyo, proyekto, o ari-arian.
etymology: From "mag-" (prefix indicating plurality/reciprocity) + "ka-" (prefix indicating companionship) + "bakas" (share, contribution).
original_explanation: Parang kayo ng business partner mo sa milk tea shop niyo. Magkakabakas kayo sa puhunan, sa pagod, at sa kita. It's like being shareholders in a venture. Hindi pwedeng isa lang ang kumikita, dapat hati kayo. Teamwork makes the dream work... or makes the business bankrupt.
usage_notes: The root "bakas" in this context means a share or stake, not a trace or footprint.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magkakabakas** kami sa maliit na tindahan sa palengke.","translation":"We are **partners** in a small store at the market."},{"sentence":"Bilang **magkakabakas**, dapat pareho nating pagdesisyunan ang mga susunod na hakbang.","translation":"As **joint owners**, we should both decide on the next steps."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na hatol o parusang ipinapataw ng isang korte sa isang taong napatunayang nagkasala.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung final verdict, 'yung 'game over' na hatol ng judge. Kapag sinabing 'Guilty!', ang kasunod na tanong ay, 'Ano ang sentensya?' Ito 'yung bilang ng taon sa kulungan, o 'yung multa na babayaran mo. The ultimate resibo from the court.
usage_notes: Ginagamit lamang sa konteksto ng batas at paglilitis.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matinding **sentensya** ang iginawad sa kanya dahil sa bigat ng krimen.","translation":"A heavy **sentence** was imposed on him due to the gravity of the crime."},{"sentence":"Umapela ang kanyang abogado upang mapababa ang **sentensya**.","translation":"His lawyer appealed to have the **sentence** reduced."}]

meaning_filipino: Isusulat o itatala sa isang listahan o talaan ang mga bagay, pangalan, o impormasyon. Ito ay ang gagawing pagtatala sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: This is what you do when your mom sends you to the palengke with a super long list. 'Isang kilong bawang, sampung sibuyas, suka, toyo...' You **will list it down** para walang kalimutan, or else magagalit si mother. It's the future tense of being organized.
usage_notes: This is the future tense of 'magtala' (to list). It specifically refers to the future action of making a list or record.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magtetela** ako ng lahat ng ating gastos para sa buwan na ito.","translation":"I **will list down** all our expenses for this month."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **magtetela** ng mga pangalan ng mga dadalo sa pagpupulong?","translation":"Who **will record** the names of the attendees for the meeting?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaki at matibay na poste o haligi, karaniwang yari sa semento, bakal, o kahoy, na ibinabaon sa lupa upang magsilbing pundasyon ng isang gusali o istruktura.
original_explanation: The unseen hero of every high-rise building in BGC and Makati. These are the giant concrete or steel 'stilts' driven deep into the ground to make sure the building doesn't just tip over. It's the ultimate 'support system' for any major construction project.
usage_notes: A technical term used in construction and engineering.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng matitibay na **pilote** upang masuportahan ang itatayong tulay.","translation":"Strong **foundation piles** are needed to support the bridge that will be built."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang yugto o bahagi ng isang kompetisyon, laro, o aktibidad; isang serye ng inumin na inililibre para sa isang grupo.
original_explanation: When your boss says "Next round is on me!" at the company party, that's the best use of this word. It's also used in boxing ("Round 3!") or in job interviews ("This is your final round of interviews"). It’s a segment, a stage, a turn. Basically, it's the part where you either level up or get knocked out.
usage_notes: Used as a direct loanword in specific contexts like drinking, sports, games, and competitions. It is not used as an adjective for "circular" (the word for that is 'bilog').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sige, isang **round** pa ng beer!","translation":"Okay, one more **round** of beer!"},{"sentence":"Natalo siya sa ikalimang **round** ng laban.","translation":"He was defeated in the fifth **round** of the match."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malawakang labanan o armadong tunggalian sa pagitan ng mga bansa, estado, o magkakalabang pangkat.
original_explanation: That thing your lola always brings up when she wants you to finish your food ("Noong panahon ng giyera..."). Also, the state of the living room after a 12.12 online sale unboxing, or what happens between two fandoms on Twitter over a ship.
usage_notes: Can be spelled as 'gera'. Used both for literal armed conflict and metaphorically for intense conflict or chaos.
