usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming buhay ang nawala noong kasagsagan ng ikalawang digmaang pandaigdig o **giyera**.","translation":"Many lives were lost during the height of the second world **war**."},{"sentence":"Para kang galing sa **giyera** sa gulo ng buhok mo.","translation":"You look like you came from a **war** with how messy your hair is."}]

translation: to make a shallow cut on; to score
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng mababaw at pahilis na hiwa o marka sa ibabaw ng isang bagay, karaniwan sa pagkain bago lutuin.
original_explanation: What you do to a fish before frying it so the seasoning gets in, or to a hotdog to make it look fancy. In hugot terms, it's making a small mark on someone's heart—not deep enough to be a wound, but a mark nonetheless. 'Huwag mo akong gilitan ng pag-asa.'
usage_notes: Commonly used in a culinary context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Gilitan** mo ang isda bago iprito para maluto ang loob.","translation":"**Score** the fish before frying so the inside cooks well."},{"sentence":"Mas masarap ang pritong manok kapag **ginitan** muna bago timplahan.","translation":"Fried chicken is tastier when it's **scored** first before seasoning."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malawak at bukas na espasyo sa loob ng isang gusali, karaniwang nagsisilbing pasukan, hintayan, o lugar para sa mga pagtitipon.
original_explanation: The grand entrance hall of a building, like the lobby of a fancy hotel (Solaire, Okada) or the main hall of the National Museum. It's that 'wow, ang laki naman dito' space you first walk into, perfect for dramatic entrances or just waiting for your Grab.
usage_notes: Often used for large, formal halls like in government buildings, museums, or universities (e.g., 'Bulwagang Palma' in UP).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghintay ang mga bisita sa **bulwag** ng pambansang museo.","translation":"The guests waited in the **hall** of the national museum."},{"sentence":"Gaganapin ang pagtatanghal sa **Bulwagang** Nicanor Abelardo.","translation":"The performance will be held at the Nicanor Abelardo **Hall**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na sobra, reserba, o hindi pangunahing ginagamit.
original_explanation: The "just in case" item. 'Yung "ispeir" na gulong sa kotse na sana hindi mo kailanganin. O 'yung "ispeir" na jowa... joke lang! Basically, the backup plan for anything, from car parts to ballpens.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin bilang pangngalan (e.g., "May ispeir ka?") o pang-uri (e.g., "ispeir na gulong").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagi akong may dalang **ispeir** na baterya para sa aking cellphone.","translation":"I always bring a **spare** battery for my cellphone."}]

translation: to ride pillion, to ride on the back
meaning_filipino: Sumakay sa likuran ng isang tao o sasakyan, lalo na sa motorsiklo, kabayo, o bisikleta.
original_explanation: The official term for being the 'backride' in a motorcycle relationship. It's you, holding on for dear life sa bewang ni crush habang bumibiyahe sa EDSA, pretending the traffic isn't giving you trust issues.
usage_notes: Often used for motorcycles, but can also be for horses or someone giving a piggyback ride.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umangkas** ako sa motorsiklo ng kaibigan ko papuntang opisina.","translation":"I **rode on the back** of my friend's motorcycle to the office."},{"sentence":"Gusto mo bang **umangkas**? Maluwag pa sa likod.","translation":"Do you want to **hitch a ride**? There's still space at the back."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang modernong baryasyon ng 'charot' o 'chos', na nagpapahiwatig na ang naunang sinabi ay isang biro o hindi dapat seryosohin.
etymology: A modern, likely internet-driven, evolution of 'charot' and 'chos'.
original_explanation: It's like "charot" went to finishing school and came back with a slightly more ✨aesthetic✨ vibe. Used by the younger crowd to soften a spicy take or a self-deprecating joke. "Ang ganda ko ngayon, chour!"
usage_notes: Popular among Gen Z and in online spaces. It carries the same function as 'charot' but with a more current feel.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Feeling ko yayaman ako next year, **chour**.","translation":"I feel like I'm going to get rich next year, **just kidding**."},{"sentence":"Diet na ako bukas, **chour**!","translation":"I'm starting my diet tomorrow, **as if**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbukas ng talulot ng isang bulaklak; ang pag-unlad at pagyabong sa buong ganda o potensyal.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'glow up' verb. It's what flowers do in spring, and what you do after a bad breakup. From a closed-off bud to a fully-realized, beautiful being. 'Ganda ka, ghorl? Nag-mamukadkad!'
usage_notes: Used literally for flowers and figuratively for a person's development or 'glowing up.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula nang **mamukadkad** ang mga rosas sa hardin.","translation":"The roses in the garden have started **to bloom**."},{"sentence":"Mula nang iwan niya ang toxic niyang jowa, tila lalo siyang **namukadkad**.","translation":"Ever since she left her toxic boyfriend, it seems she has **blossomed** even more."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaghalong harina, itlog, gatas o tubig, at iba pang sangkap na karaniwang ginagamit sa pagluluto ng mga keyk, pancake, o bilang pambalot sa ipiprito.
original_explanation: That goopy mix for your hotcakes, banana cue, or fried chicken. It's the secret to making everything crispy and delicious. Kung sa BPO, ito yung 'blended' account, halo-halo ang LOB. Kung sa love life, 'mixed signals'.
usage_notes: A loanword used in culinary contexts. The spelling and pronunciation are retained from English.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong haluing mabuti ang **batter** para walang buo-buong harina.","translation":"You need to mix the **batter** well so there are no lumps of flour."},{"sentence":"Isawsaw ang manok sa **batter** bago iprito.","translation":"Dip the chicken in the **batter** before frying."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na pagtatasa o pagsusuri sa isang bagay, tulad ng libro, pelikula, o pagganap sa trabaho. Maaari ring tumukoy sa muling pag-aaral ng mga aralin.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa mo bago ka mag-check out sa Shopee o Lazada—tinitingnan mo 'yung 1-star at 5-star comments. Ito rin 'yung dahilan ng puyat mo bago ang exam. At 'yung kinakatakutan mong "performance review" sa BPO.
usage_notes: Isang Filipino-ized spelling at pronunciation ng salitang Ingles. Karaniwang ginagamit sa impormal na konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong mag-**ribyu** para sa board exam sa susunod na buwan.","translation":"I need to **review** for the board exam next month."},{"sentence":"Maganda ba ang mga **ribyu** ng bagong pelikula ni Direk?","translation":"Are the **reviews** for the new movie of Direk good?"}]

translation: to lend; to allow to borrow
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng pahintulot sa iba na gamitin ang isang bagay na pagmamay-ari mo sa loob ng isang takdang panahon, na may kasunduang ito ay ibabalik.
etymology: From mag- (actor-focus verb prefix) + pa- (causative prefix) + hiram (borrow).
original_explanation: This is what you do when your friend is short on cash before payday. "Pahiram muna, bes, bayaran ko sa 15th!" It's the foundation of many friendships and the cause of many "seen-zoned" messages when it's time to pay up. It's basically a trust fall with your money or belongings.
usage_notes: `Magpahiram` is when the owner allows someone to borrow. `Humiram` is when someone borrows. The focus is on the lender.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puwede ka bang **magpahiram** ng libro mo sa akin?","translation":"Can you **lend** me your book?"},{"sentence":"**Nagpahiram** si Ana ng pera kay Marco dahil sa emergency.","translation":"Ana **lent** money to Marco because of an emergency."}]

meaning_filipino: Kontrolin o impluwensyahan ang isang tao o sitwasyon sa paraang hindi tapat o mapanlinlang upang makuha ang sariling nais.
original_explanation: What your ex did to you. It's when someone plays with your emotions like a puppet master, making you dance to their tune. Classic toxic trait. "Huwag mo akong sinusubukang manipulahin, alam ko na ang mga galawan mo."
usage_notes: A transitive verb that requires an object to be manipulated.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **manipulahin** ka ng sinuman.","translation":"Don't let anyone **manipulate** you."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **manipulahin** ang resulta ng eleksyon.","translation":"He tried to **manipulate** the election results."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang babaeng labis ang pagpapahalaga sa sariling kaanyuan at itsura; hambog.
original_explanation: She's that friend who can't pass a mirror or a reflective Jollibee glass window without checking herself out. She's always camera-ready, her OOTD is always on point, and her IG feed is life goals. A little **banidosa**, but you gotta admit, she looks fabulous. The male version is 'banidoso'.
usage_notes: This is the feminine form. The masculine form is 'banidoso'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa pagiging **banidosa** dahil hindi siya umaalis ng bahay nang walang makeup.","translation":"She is known for being **vain** because she never leaves the house without makeup."},{"sentence":"“Huwag kang masyadong **banidosa**,” biro ni Ana sa kaibigang panay ang pag-selfie.","translation":"\"Don't be too **vain**,\" Ana joked to her friend who was constantly taking selfies."}]

translation: to like; to want; to approve of
meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na nangangahulugang gusto, nagugustuhan, o sinasang-ayunan ang isang bagay, tao, o ideya.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Ingles na "bet," na ginagamit sa konteksto ng pagsang-ayon o paggusto, na posibleng naimpluwensyahan ng pariralang "you bet!".
original_explanation: Pag sinabi mong "bet" mo, ibig sabihin type mo, gusto mo, aprub! "Bet mo ba 'yung bagong kanta ng BINI?" "Bet!" It's the ultimate seal of approval from the council of marites and cool kids. Pwede ring gamitin as a challenge: "Bet, P500 'di mo kaya ubusin 'yan."
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa mga pariralang "Bet ko 'yan" (I like that) o bilang isang salitang sagot na "Bet!" (I'm in! / I like it!).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bet** ko talaga ang style niya manamit.","translation":"I really **like** her fashion style."},{"sentence":"Gusto mo bang sumama sa beach? **Bet**!","translation":"Do you want to come to the beach? **I'm in**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong bahagi ng subkultura na karaniwang nakikilala sa madilim na pananamit, partikular na istilo ng musika, at malalim na pagpapahalaga sa sining at panitikan.
original_explanation: Yung kaibigan mong laging naka-black, mahilig sa The Cure, at parang laging may pinagdadaanang existential crisis. Hindi sila masamang tao, sadyang mas intense lang sila mag-emote kaysa sa'yo tuwing Monday morning. Parang laging may kasamang fog machine ang aura.
usage_notes: Ginagamit bilang slang, lalo na sa mga kabataan at sa social media, upang ilarawan ang isang tao o istilo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **goth** ng outfit mo ngayon, may event ba sa sementeryo?","translation":"Your outfit is very **goth** today, is there an event at the cemetery?"},{"sentence":"Mahilig siya sa mga banda na parang pang-**goth**.","translation":"He/She likes bands that sound like they're for **goths**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pansamantalang pamalit o solusyon na ginagamit upang punan ang isang kakulangan, madalas ay hindi ang pinakamainam na pagpipilian.
etymology: Compound of Tagalog 'takip' (cover) and 'butas' (hole). Literally, 'hole cover.'
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'hugot' word. It's when you feel like you're just a rebound, a 'panakip-butas.' You're the substitute player called in because the main character wasn't available. You're the instant coffee when they really want a brewed one. Basically, you're the second choice, the temporary fix. Aray ko beh.
usage_notes: Highly idiomatic. Used to describe people, things, or solutions that are merely temporary or second-best.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayokong maging **takip-butas** lang habang hinihintay mo siyang bumalik.","translation":"I don't want to be just a **placeholder** while you wait for him to come back."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-utang para bayaran ang isa pang utang ay solusyong **takip-butas** lamang.","translation":"Borrowing money to pay another debt is just a **stopgap** solution."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa o pagganap ng isang pagdiriwang, pulong, o anumang mahalagang okasyon.
original_explanation: This is the 'may ganap' moment. It's the act of making the event happen. From planning the debut to the actual party, from organizing the barangay meeting to the actual meeting itself. It's the 'how' behind every 'sana all' picture on social media.
usage_notes: Often used for formal events like conferences, ceremonies, and official celebrations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging matagumpay ang **pagdaraos** ng kanilang anibersaryo.","translation":"The **celebration** of their anniversary was successful."},{"sentence":"Pinaghahandaan na ang **pagdaraos** ng taunang pista sa aming bayan.","translation":"Preparations are underway for the **holding** of the annual town fiesta."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa masamang amoy, partikular na ang amoy ng ihi.
original_explanation: That unmistakable, sharp, and disgusting smell you find in poorly maintained public restrooms, underpasses, or that one dark alley. If a place smells `panghi`, you walk faster. It's the official scent of "dito bawal umihi."
usage_notes: Isang napaka-espesipiko at Matingkad na salita para sa amoy ng ihi.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakasakit sa ilong ng **panghi** sa eskinita.","translation":"The **urinous stench** in the alley is very sharp."},{"sentence":"Bakit amoy **panghi** ang banyo? Hindi ba nilinis?","translation":"Why does the bathroom **stink of urine**? Wasn't it cleaned?"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa anumang bagay na may kaugnayan sa, o nagmula sa, Inglatera, sa wika nito, o sa mga tao nito.
original_explanation: This describes anything from the 'English' breakfast at the hotel buffet (which is mostly just bacon and eggs) to your friend's weird 'English' accent after a two-week vacation in London.
usage_notes: Adjectival form. For example, 'wikang Ingles' (English language), 'pagkaing Ingles' (English food).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito niyang inumin ang tsaa na **Ingles** tuwing hapon.","translation":"Her favorite drink is **English** tea every afternoon."}]

translation: something used to fight or compete; countermeasure; entry (in a contest)
meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, tao, o paraan na ginagamit sa pakikipag-away, pakikipagkompetisyon, o bilang proteksyon o solusyon laban sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: Your "pambato" or bet in a competition. "Siya ang **panlaban** natin sa Miss Universe!" It can also be your secret weapon, like that killer presentation deck for a client pitch. Or more literally, it's your Off! lotion as a **panlaban** sa lamok. It's anything you use to go up against something else, from a rival company to a pesky mosquito.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun ("ang panlaban") or an adjective ("gamit na panlaban").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bagong bakuna ang itinuturing na mabisang **panlaban** sa sakit.","translation":"The new vaccine is considered an effective **countermeasure** against the disease."},{"sentence":"Ipinasok niya ang kanyang pinakamagandang obra bilang **panlaban** sa patimpalak sa pagpipinta.","translation":"He entered his best masterpiece as his **entry** in the painting contest."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang instrumentong pang-orkestra na hinihipan at yari sa kahoy (woodwind) na may dalawang piraso ng manipis na kawayan (double reed) na pinagtutunog upang makalikha ng isang matinis at tumatagos na tono.
original_explanation: The 'bibo kid' of the orchestra's woodwind section. The obo is that long, black instrument that looks like a clarinet but sounds a bit more... nasal? It's famous for playing that 'A' note that the whole orchestra tunes to before a concert. So, basically, it's the one that tells everyone else, 'Okay guys, ganito dapat ang tono natin.'
usage_notes: A highly specific musical term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang pangunahing manunugtog ng **obo** sa Philippine Philharmonic Orchestra.","translation":"She is the principal **oboe** player in the Philippine Philharmonic Orchestra."},{"sentence":"Mahirap pag-aralan ang pagtugtog ng **obo** dahil sa 'double reed' nito.","translation":"It's difficult to learn to play the **oboe** because of its double reed."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang akronim para sa "Work From Home"; isang paraan ng pagtatrabaho kung saan ginagampanan ng isang empleyado ang kanyang mga tungkulin mula sa bahay sa halip na sa opisina.
etymology: Acronym for the English phrase 'Work From Home'.
original_explanation: The 2020s career goal. It means your commute is from your bed to your desk (which might also be your bed). You're 'on a call' but you're actually muted while cooking adobo. The uniform is a professional-looking top and pambahay shorts. 'Sorry, my connection is unstable' is the new 'I'm stuck in traffic.'
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun (e.g., 'Naka-WFH ako') or an adjective (e.g., 'WFH setup').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bukas, naka-**WFH** ako kaya puwede tayong mag-usap sa hapon.","translation":"Tomorrow, I'm on **WFH** so we can talk in the afternoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng ibong mandaragit na karaniwang aktibo sa gabi, na may malalaking mata, patag na mukha, at may kakayahang paikutin ang ulo nito nang malayo.
etymology: From Spanish "cuajo", which has a complex history, but likely influenced by the sound the owl makes and folk etymology. The more direct Spanish word for owl is "búho".
original_explanation: The official mascot of the BPO industry and anyone who works the night shift. In Filipino folklore, they're often seen as spooky omens, but today, they're more of a symbol for being a 'night owl.' If you're awake at 3 AM scrolling, congratulations, you're a modern-day kuwago.
usage_notes: Often associated with wisdom, night, and sometimes bad omens in Philippine folklore.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May narinig kaming huni ng **kuwago** kagabi sa labas ng aming bintana.","translation":"We heard the hoot of an **owl** last night outside our window."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang trabaho sa gabi, para na siyang **kuwago** na gising sa gabi at tulog sa umaga.","translation":"Because of his night job, he's like an **owl** who is awake at night and asleep in the morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar, sisidlan, o gusali kung saan itinatago at iniimbak ang mga bagay para sa hinaharap na paggamit.
original_explanation: Your 'bodega', your closet full of things you "might need someday", the 'baul' of your lola, or even the Downloads folder on your computer. An 'imbakan' is any place you dump stuff into. It could be a giant warehouse for rice (NFA imbakan) or that one kitchen drawer that has everything from batteries to old receipts.
usage_notes: The suffix '-an' denotes a place where the action of the root word ('imbak' - to store) is done.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno na ang **imbakan** ng bigas dahil sa magandang ani.","translation":"The rice **warehouse** is full because of the good harvest."},{"sentence":"Ginamit nilang **imbakan** ng mga lumang gamit ang espasyo sa ilalim ng hagdan.","translation":"They used the space under the stairs as a **storage area** for old things."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-usog o pagpunta sa gilid upang magbigay-daan o umiwas sa sagabal.
original_explanation: "Tabi-tabi po!" The action version. It's what you do when a motorcycle suddenly uses the sidewalk in Manila, or when your crush is walking towards you and you panic. "Girl, **gumilid** ako bigla, dumaan si crush, di ako prepared!"
usage_notes: This is the completed aspect (past tense) of the verb. Often used as a command: "Gilid!" (Move aside!).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Gumilid** ka muna at may dadaan na sasakyan.","translation":"**Move to the side** for a moment, a vehicle is about to pass."},{"sentence":"Agad siyang **gumilid** nang makita ang paparating na bulto ng tao.","translation":"He immediately **moved to the side** when he saw the crowd of people approaching."}]

translation: trinket; small gift; token of appreciation
meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na handog o regalo bilang tanda ng paggunita, pagpapahalaga, o pasasalamat.
etymology: Mula sa 'para-' (for) + 'gala' (travel/stroll), na nagpapahiwatig ng isang bagay na nakuha mula sa isang paglalakbay.
original_explanation: That little souvenir you buy from Baguio (like the tiny barrel man) that you give to your officemates as 'pasalubong'. It's not about the price, it's the 'naalala kita' thought that counts.
usage_notes: Kadalasang tumutukoy sa mga pasalubong o maliliit na alaala mula sa isang paglalakbay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-uwi si nanay ng mga **paragala** mula sa kanyang pagbisita sa Cebu.","translation":"Mother brought home some **trinkets** from her visit to Cebu."},{"sentence":"Isang simpleng **paragala** lang ang hiling ko, kahit key chain lang.","translation":"I'm only asking for a simple **token**, even just a key chain."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang nilagang itlog ng pato na mayroon nang nabubuong sisiw sa loob, isang kilalang pagkain sa Pilipinas.
etymology: Mula sa salitang 'balot' (to wrap), dahil ang sisiw ay 'nakabalot' sa loob ng itlog.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'fear factor' food for foreigners, but a national treasure for Pinoys. It's the litmus test of your Pinoy-ness. Best enjoyed with a sprinkle of salt and a swig of spicy vinegar, usually sold by a vendor shouting 'Baluuuut!' at night.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy lamang sa pagkaing ito. Ang bigkas ay may diin sa huling pantig /ba-LOT/.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong kainin ang sabaw ng **balot** bago ito balatan.","translation":"My favorite part is sipping the **balut** soup before peeling it."},{"sentence":"Bumili tayo ng **balot** at penoy sa kanto.","translation":"Let's buy **balut** and penoy at the corner."}]

meaning_filipino: Igalaw ang katawan sa saliw ng tugtugin; isama ang isang tao sa pagsasayaw o gamitin ang isang bagay bilang paksa ng sayaw.
original_explanation: That feeling when your crush asks you to dance, and you're like, "OMG, is this the prom scene from a movie?" Also what you do to a baby to put them to sleep, or what you do with your problems—you just dance them away. "Isayaw mo na lang 'yan!"
usage_notes: Can be used to mean 'to dance with someone' (Isayaw mo siya) or 'to perform a specific dance' (Isayaw mo ang tinikling).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **isayaw** mo ang ating bisita.","translation":"Please, **dance with** our guest."},{"sentence":"Ang tinikling ay mahirap **isayaw**.","translation":"The Tinikling is difficult **to dance**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagsasagawa ng pagsusuri o awdit sa mga talaang pampinansyal ng isang indibidwal, negosyo, o organisasyon.
original_explanation: The person you try to befriend when they visit your office, hoping they don't find that 'miscellaneous' expense for a team-building... in Boracay. They are the official 'resibo pls' person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumating na ang **awditor** mula sa Commission on Audit (COA).","translation":"The **auditor** from the Commission on Audit (COA) has arrived."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bihirang anyo ng 'numerado'; nangangahulugang may mga numero o bilang.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na 'numeroso' (numerous), ngunit ginagamit sa Pilipinas sa kahulugan ng 'numerado' (numbered).
original_explanation: This is the slightly more 'extra' cousin of 'numerado'. It's not wrong, but it sounds a bit old-fashioned or like someone trying to sound fancy. Think of it as the difference between 'iPhone 15' and 'the fifteenth iPhone'.
usage_notes: Itinuturing na hindi pamantayan o makalumang anyo ng 'numerado'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga pahina ng lumang aklat ay **numerodos**.","translation":"The pages of the old book are **numbered**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay ng permanenteng marka o disenyo sa balat sa pamamagitan ng tinta.
etymology: From English "tattoo", which is from Polynesian languages.
original_explanation: That thing you tell your parents you're "thinking about" but you've already booked the appointment. It's either a deep, meaningful symbol of your journey or a random drawing you saw on Pinterest. No in-between. "For my birthday, I will get a tattoo."
usage_notes: Future tense of "magtatu". A colloquial and direct way to say "magpapatattoo".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magtatatu** ako ng pangalan ng aso ko sa aking braso.","translation":"I **will get a tattoo** of my dog's name on my arm."},{"sentence":"Sigurado ka na bang **magtatatu** ka? Hindi na iyan mabubura.","translation":"Are you sure you **will get a tattoo**? That's permanent."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng respeto, konsiderasyon, at pag-iisip sa kapakanan o damdamin ng iba.
original_explanation: A rare Pokemon in the world of commuting and office politics. This is the person who won't eat chicharon in a quiet library, offers you their seat on the bus, or asks "Okay ka lang?" before unloading all their problems on you. The opposite of "walang pakialam." Be this person.
usage_notes: The "mapag-" prefix turns the root concept ("alang-alang" - for the sake of) into a character trait. Describes a person who habitually shows consideration.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana lahat ng tao ay **mapag-alang-alang** sa damdamin ng kanilang kapwa.","translation":"I wish all people were **considerate** of the feelings of others."}]

translation: to stumble and fall flat, to fall on one's face
meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang pagkadapa o pagbagsak nang padapa, karaniwang dahil sa pagkatapilok o pagkawala ng balanse.
etymology: From 'ma-' (potential/accidental action prefix) + 'dapa' (to lie face down).
original_explanation: That super embarrassing moment when you're walking confidently, maybe even checking someone out, and then your foot catches on nothing and you suddenly find yourself kissing the pavement. That's 'marapa'. It’s a specific kind of fall – face-first. The universe's way of saying 'stay humble, bes.'
usage_notes: 'Marapa' is an accidental, sudden action. It's different from 'dumapa' which is the intentional act of lying down on one's stomach. 'Marapa' implies a loss of balance leading to the fall.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa paglalakad diyan at baka ka **marapa**.","translation":"Be careful walking there or you might **stumble and fall flat**."},{"sentence":"Nang makita niya ang presyo, halos **marapa** siya sa gulat.","translation":"When he saw the price, he almost **fell over** in shock."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang batang kambing, lalo na ang lalaki.
original_explanation: This is the baby boy goat, a kid. The male counterpart to 'kabrita'. Also, this is the star of the dish 'kalderetang kabrito'. Poor little guy.
usage_notes: More known in culinary contexts than in animal husbandry conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap daw ang kalderetang **kabrito** sa restawran na iyon.","translation":"They say the **kid** (young goat) stew at that restaurant is delicious."},{"sentence":"Pinakain niya ng damo ang **kabrito**.","translation":"He fed the **kid** some grass."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang anyo ng sining pampanitikan na gumagamit ng mga piling salita na may angking aliw-iw, ritmo, at talinhaga upang magpahayag ng masidhing damdamin o malalim na kaisipan.
original_explanation: The Spanish-sounding, more 'conyo' cousin of 'tula'. You use 'poesiya' when you want to sound intellectual or you're talking about Neruda. You use 'tula' when you're writing your high school crush a cheesy rhyme for Valentine's. Both are about feelings, but 'poesiya' feels like it needs a glass of wine.
usage_notes: The native and more commonly used term is 'tula'. 'Poesiya' is often used in academic, literary, or more formal discussions about the art of poetry as a whole.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga akda ay puno ng malalim na **poesiya**.","translation":"His works are full of deep **poetry**."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan namin ang **poesiya** ng mga makatang Espanyol.","translation":"We are studying the **poetry** of Spanish poets."}]

meaning_filipino: Pinong-pinong mga partikulo ng lupa o iba pang bagay na umaalialigid sa hangin at namumuo sa mga ibabaw ng bagay.
original_explanation: That stuff that magically appears on your bookshelf two days after you cleaned it. It's the universe's way of telling you, "Nice try, but I'm still here." Also, the primary ingredient of a "maalikabok" na daan.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'alikabok', but 'gabok' can refer to finer dust, while 'alikabok' often implies dust kicked up from the ground.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-punasan mo ang **gabok** sa ibabaw ng mesa.","translation":"Please wipe the **dust** off the table."},{"sentence":"Puno ng **gabok** ang mga lumang libro sa bodega.","translation":"The old books in the storage room are full of **dust**."}]

translation: to sue, to file a case against
meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na paghahain ng sakdal o kaso sa korte laban sa isang tao o entidad.
etymology: From Spanish 'hablar', meaning 'to speak', which evolved in legal contexts.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'I'll see you in court!' threat. When a chismis gets too out of hand or someone scams you online, the next level is to ihabla them. It's turning a personal away into a legal battle. 'Kapag 'di mo binalik pera ko, i-ha-habla kita!'
usage_notes: A legal term that has entered common parlance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **ihabla** ang kumpanya dahil sa hindi makatarungang pagtanggal sa kanya.","translation":"She decided to **sue** the company for unjust termination."},{"sentence":"Pinagbabantaan siyang **ihahabla** ng paninirang-puri.","translation":"He is being threatened with being **sued** for libel."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong sanay at bihasa sa pakikipaglaban o pakikidigma; isang kawal.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `man-` (tagagawa ng kilos) + `digma` (giyera) + `-r-` gitlapi.
original_explanation: Hindi lang ito 'yung may hawak na espada at kalasag. Mandirigma din 'yung BPO agent na sumasabak sa graveyard shift, 'yung nanay na nag-aalaga ng tatlong anak, at 'yung student na nag-cocommute ng 3 hours para makapasok. Lahat tayo, may pinaglalaban.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin nang literal para sa isang mandirigma sa kasaysayan o pantasya, o patalinghaga para sa sinumang nagpapakita ng tapang at katatagan sa harap ng mga hamon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Lapu-Lapu ay isang magiting na **mandirigma**.","translation":"Lapu-Lapu was a valiant **warrior**."},{"sentence":"Ang bawat OFW ay isang **mandirigma** ng modernong panahon.","translation":"Every OFW is a modern-day **warrior**."}]

meaning_filipino: Maiikling video na nililikha at ibinabahagi sa mga platform ng social media tulad ng Instagram at Facebook, na kadalasang may kasamang musika, epekto, at mga trending na audio.
etymology: Hiram na pangalan ng brand/feature mula sa Instagram/Facebook, na bahagi na ng pangkalahatang leksikon ng social media.
original_explanation: The Gen Z and Millennial's answer to TikTok, but on Instagram and Facebook. It's that 30-second video of your friend pointing at floating text while dancing badly to a trending song. It's where you see "A Day in My Life," GRWM (Get Ready With Me), and food hacks you'll never actually try. If you haven't wasted an hour scrolling through an endless stream of Reels, are you even living in the 2020s?
usage_notes: Isang napaka-modernong salita na direktang nauugnay sa paggamit ng social media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-viral ang ginawa niyang **Reels** tungkol sa kanyang alagang aso.","translation":"The **Reels** she made about her pet dog went viral."},{"sentence":"Gagawa ako ng **Reels** ng ating bakasyon para may alaala tayo.","translation":"I'll make a **Reels** of our vacation so we have a memory."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglikha ng tela mula sa sinulid o panali sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng isang kawit na tinatawag na gantsilyo.
original_explanation: This is what your lola does to make those little coasters for the dining table or that cute beanie you never wear. It's the art of turning a ball of yarn into something useful (or at least decorative) using a single hook. The ultimate 'tita' hobby, now making a comeback with the 'cottagecore' aesthetic.
usage_notes: The verb form of 'gantsilyo' (crochet hook/the craft itself).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais kong matutong **gantsilyuhin** ang isang kumot para sa aking pamangkin.","translation":"I want to learn to **crochet** a blanket for my nephew."}]

translation: taller than a person; above human height
meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng taas o haba na humihigit sa karaniwang sukat o taas ng isang tao.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're trying to describe how high the floodwaters were. 'Bes, lampas-tao 'yung baha sa amin!' It's the ultimate measurement for things that are way, way taller than you, like a basketball player, a huge wave, or the pile of laundry you've been ignoring.
usage_notes: Often used to describe the height of floodwaters, overgrown grass, or very tall structures.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lampas-tao** na ang mga talahib sa bakanteng lote.","translation":"The cogon grass in the vacant lot is now **taller than a person**."},{"sentence":"Umakyat ang tubig-baha nang **lampas-tao** kaya nagsilikas ang mga residente.","translation":"The floodwater rose **above human height**, so the residents evacuated."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sistema para sa pagpapadala ng mga imahe na may kasamang tunog sa malayo at ang pagpapakita nito sa isang screen; ang aparato na ginagamit para dito.
original_explanation: The OG Netflix. Ito 'yung kahon sa sala na sentro ng pamilya tuwing gabi para manood ng "FPJ's Ang Probinsyano" or "It's Showtime". Dito mo unang narinig ang "Marimar, au!" at "I am sorry". Ngayon, baka smart TV na 'yan, pero ang tawag pa rin natin, TV o telebisyon.
usage_notes: Often shortened to 'TV' (tee-vee) in casual conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Manonood kami ng paborito naming teleserye sa **telebisyon**.","translation":"We will watch our favorite drama series on **television**."},{"sentence":"Patayin mo ang **telebisyon** kung hindi mo naman pinapanood.","translation":"Turn off the **television** if you're not watching it."}]

translation: to adapt; to adjust; to make fit
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagbabagay o pag-aakma sa isang bagong sitwasyon, kapaligiran, o pangangailangan.
original_explanation: This is the adulting version of 'to fit in'. It’s moving to a new city and learning the commute, starting a new job and learning the office politics, or trying to fit all your stuff into a tiny condo unit. 'Mag-agpang' is the skill of making things work, of adjusting yourself or the situation until it clicks. It's the opposite of forcing a square peg into a round hole.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'umagpang' or 'iagpang'. It has a sense of making two or more things compatible.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **mag-agpang** sa mga bagong patakaran ng kumpanya.","translation":"We need **to adapt** to the new company policies."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **mag-agpang** sa buhay sa ibang bansa kung sanay ka sa Pilipinas.","translation":"It's difficult **to adjust** to life in another country if you're used to the Philippines."}]

translation: will be in a tight spot, will be short of money
meaning_filipino: Mararanasan ang kakulangan, lalo na sa pananalapi, o malalagay sa isang mahirap na sitwasyon.
original_explanation: The official state of being during 'petsa de peligro' (the days before payday). 'Yong 'di ka na makasama sa gala kasi puro instant noodles na lang ang kaya ng budget mo. "Pass muna, guys, **magigipit** ako."
usage_notes: Ito ang anyong panghinaharap na nagpapahiwatig ng darating na kakapusan o kahirapan, karaniwan sa aspetong pinansyal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kung hindi ka mag-iipon, siguradong **magigipit** ka sa oras ng pangangailangan.","translation":"If you don't save, you **will surely be short of money** in times of need."},{"sentence":"Mukhang **magigipit** kami sa budget dahil sa biglaang pagtaas ng mga bilihin.","translation":"It looks like we **will be in a tight spot** with the budget because of the sudden increase in prices."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na utos, kahilingan, o listahan ng mga bagay na nais bilhin o ihanda.
original_explanation: This is your go-to word for everything from telling your younger sibling what to do, to your boss giving you a task, to telling the Jollibee crew "One C3, please". It's the ultimate 'pabili po' and 'gawin mo 'to' rolled into one English word we just can't live without. Pwede ring "out of **order**" 'pag sira ang ATM.
usage_notes: Ginagamit din bilang pandiwa (hal. mag-order, umorder). Lubos na karaniwan sa pang-araw-araw na usapan, lalo na sa mga sitwasyong komersyal at sa opisina.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **order** mo sa restawran?","translation":"What's your **order** at the restaurant?"},{"sentence":"Nag-**order** ako ng bagong sapatos online.","translation":"I **ordered** new shoes online."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng habag o awa sa kapwa; may malambot na puso at handang tumulong sa mga nangangailangan.
original_explanation: That tita who always gives you extra baon money 'kasi kawawa ka naman, pagod sa school.' It’s the person who adopts stray cats and dogs. Being maawain is having a heart that's not calloused by the world, always ready to give a second chance or a helping hand.
usage_notes: A highly valued positive trait in Filipino culture.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa kanilang lugar bilang isang taong **maawain** at matulungin.","translation":"She is known in their area as a **compassionate** and helpful person."},{"sentence":"Ang **maawain** na hukom ay nagbigay ng mas magaan na parusa.","translation":"The **merciful** judge gave a lighter sentence."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang labis na pagbibigay ng luho, kaginhawahan, o anumang naisin ng isang tao; ang kalagayan ng pagiging sanay sa karangyaan at hindi sa hirap.
original_explanation: This is the 'spoiled brat' starter pack. It's the feeling of being treated like royalty—getting everything you want without lifting a finger. Think 'panganay na apo' treatment. A little 'layaw' is a spa day; too much 'layaw' and you become a 'palamunin'.
usage_notes: Can be both positive (a well-deserved treat) and negative (being spoiled to the point of helplessness).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lumaki sa **layaw** ang bata kaya hindi marunong sa gawaing-bahay.","translation":"The child grew up with too much **pampering**, so they don't know any household chores."},{"sentence":"Bigyan mo naman ng kaunting **layaw** ang iyong sarili pagkatapos ng mahabang linggo ng trabaho.","translation":"Give yourself a little **indulgence** after a long week of work."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit o katamtamang-laking sasakyang-dagat na pinapatakbo ng motor, karaniwang ginagamit sa pagtawid sa pagitan ng mga isla o sa mga ilog.
original_explanation: Before there were ROROs and fast crafts for your Boracay trip, there was the humble **lantsa**. It's a motorboat, bigger than a 'bangka' but smaller than a 'barko'. It's the workhorse of inter-island travel, the GrabCar of the sea. It’s what you take when the destination is too far to swim but too near for a massive ferry.
usage_notes: A very common term in coastal and island communities in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumakay kami ng **lantsa** para makarating sa kabilang isla.","translation":"We rode a **motorboat** to get to the other island."},{"sentence":"Ang mga mangingisda ay gumagamit din ng **lantsa** para sa kanilang pangingisda.","translation":"The fishermen also use **launches** for their fishing."}]

translation: to have a falling out with someone; to become enemies
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng alitan, hidwaan, o samaan ng loob sa isang tao na humahantong sa pagkasira ng relasyon.
original_explanation: This is what happens when the "tampo" levels up to an epic "away." It's the social equivalent of unfriending, blocking, and muting someone in real life. One minute you're sharing chismis, the next you're the subject of the chismis. The opposite of 'makipagbati'.
usage_notes: Implies a mutual or reciprocal state of being angry with each other.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw kong **makipagkagalit** sa aking matalik na kaibigan dahil lang sa pera.","translation":"I don't want to **have a falling out** with my best friend just because of money."},{"sentence":"Sila ay nag-**makipagkagalit** matapos ang mainit na debate.","translation":"They **became enemies** after a heated debate."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nag-aaral sa isang paaralan, kolehiyo, o unibersidad.
original_explanation: Ang official title ng mga taong laging puyat, laging naghahabol ng deadline, at ang allowance ay parang bula na lang nawawala. Sila rin ang may PhD in 'Procrastination and Heavy Cramming'.
usage_notes: Very common word. The native Tagalog equivalent is 'mag-aaral'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging maraming assignment ang mga **estudyante** sa panahong ito.","translation":"**Students** always have a lot of assignments these days."},{"sentence":"Bilang isang **estudyante**, responsibilidad mong mag-aral nang mabuti.","translation":"As a **student**, it is your responsibility to study well."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpasok o pakikialam sa isang bagay, lugar, o usapin nang walang pahintulot o karapatan.
etymology: From pang- (instrumental/nominalizing prefix) + reduplication of the first syllable of the root + pasok (enter). The 'p' in 'pasok' assimilates to 'm' after 'pang-'.
original_explanation: This is when someone oversteps their boundaries. Like your tita asking why you're still single at the family reunion, or when a country meddles in another's affairs. It's the ultimate "sawsaw" move, but on a more serious level. Unsolicited advice on your life choices? That's low-key panghihimasok.
usage_notes: Often used in formal contexts like politics (territorial intrusion) or legal matters (trespassing). Can also be used for personal relationships to describe meddling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **panghihimasok** ng ibang bansa sa ating teritoryo ay isang seryosong usapin.","translation":"The **intrusion** of other countries into our territory is a serious matter."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko gusto ang **panghihimasok** niya sa personal kong buhay.","translation":"I don't like his **meddling** in my personal life."}]

translation: to clear one's name; to be acquitted
meaning_filipino: Paglalahad ng katwiran upang mapawalang-sala o malinis ang pangalan mula sa isang akusasyon.
original_explanation: This isn't about unloading boxes. This is about unloading yourself from a legal mess. It's what a lawyer helps you do when you're 'Maritess-ed' (gossiped about) into a corner. You present your 'diskargo' to clear your name. Think of it as the legal version of 'showing receipts'.
usage_notes: A formal or legal term, distinct from 'magdiskarga' (to unload cargo). It's about clearing responsibility or a charge.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghanda ang abogado ng mga ebidensya para **magdiskargo** sa kanyang kliyente.","translation":"The lawyer prepared evidence **to acquit** his client."},{"sentence":"Kailangan niyang **magdiskargo** sa korte upang patunayang wala siyang kasalanan.","translation":"He needs **to clear his name** in court to prove his innocence."}]

translation: to piece together; to connect multiple things
meaning_filipino: Pag-ugnayin o pagkabit-kabitin ang maraming hiwa-hiwalay na bahagi upang makabuo ng isang kabuuan.
original_explanation: Your tita's job during a family reunion—connecting all the plot points of everyone's love life. It's also what a detective does with clues, or what you do with your leftover sweldo until the next payday.
usage_notes: This is the intensified or plural form of 'pagdugtungin', implying connecting multiple, often scattered, pieces.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng imbestigador na **pagdugtung-dugtungin** ang mga ebidensya.","translation":"The investigator tried **to piece together** the evidence."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **pagdugtung-dugtungin** ang mga retasong tela para makabuo ng kumot.","translation":"We need **to connect the multiple** scraps of fabric to make a blanket."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong may hilig sa pagsusuri; mapanuri at mahilig mag-obserba nang malaliman.
etymology: Mula sa `pala-` (unlaping nagsasaad ng hilig) + `suri` (analyze, examine).
original_explanation: Ito yung kaibigan mong overthinker level 99. Bago gumawa ng desisyon, may pros and cons list, SWOT analysis, at kinonsulta na ang buong angkan. Sila rin yung mahilig mag-analyze ng mga pelikula at series, 'Alam mo, yung foreshadowing kanina...' Minsan, nakakapagod kasama, pero madalas, sila ang savior ng grupo.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan sa katangian o hilig ng isang tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil siya ay isang abogadong **palasuri**, napansin niya ang maliit na detalye sa kontrata.","translation":"Because he is an **analytical** lawyer, he noticed the small detail in the contract."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong **palasuri** sa lahat ng bagay, minsan kailangan mo lang mag-enjoy.","translation":"Don't be too **critical** of everything, sometimes you just need to enjoy."}]

translation: act of standing up; rising; taking a stand
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtayo mula sa pagkakaupo o pagkakahiga; ang pagpapakita ng paninindigan sa isang isyu o prinsipyo.
original_explanation: This isn't just getting up from your chair. It's what you do when you see injustice and decide to speak up. It's having a 'spine'. On a less serious note, it's also the struggle of getting out of bed on a Monday morning. 'Ang **pagtindig** para sa tama ay hindi laging madali.'
usage_notes: Carries a strong connotation of principle and conviction, beyond the physical act of standing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang marangal na **pagtindig** ng mga bayani ay dapat tularan.","translation":"The noble **stance** of the heroes should be emulated."},{"sentence":"Nagulat ang lahat sa bigla niyang **pagtindig** at pagsigaw.","translation":"Everyone was surprised by his sudden **act of standing up** and shouting."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang numerong kumakatawan sa isang bahagi ng isang buo, ipinapakita bilang isang bilang na hinati sa isa pa (hal. 1/2, 3/4).
original_explanation: That thing in math that gave you a headache in grade school. It's literally 'part-number'. Like, when you only get half of your 13th-month pay on time, you got a *bahagimbilang* of your bonus.
usage_notes: A specific mathematical term. The English loanword 'praksyon' is more commonly used in casual conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang 'kalahati' o 1/2 ay isang uri ng **bahagimbilang**.","translation":"'Half' or 1/2 is a type of **fraction**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaki at pormal na pagpupulong ng mga tao, karaniwan sa isang unibersidad o kolehiyo para sa isang seremonya.
original_explanation: The university event that's not quite graduation, but you still have to wear something nice for it. It's like the opening ceremonies of the school year where they welcome the freshmen and make everyone feel important before the hell of exams begins.
usage_notes: Primarily used in academic settings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kombokasyon** para sa mga bagong mag-aaral ay gaganapin sa gymnasium.","translation":"The **convocation** for new students will be held at the gymnasium."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging naabala o naistorbo sa isang gawain o sa kapayapaan.
etymology: From `pag-` + `ka-` + `ka-` (reduplication) + `gambala`. The prefix `pagkaka-` refers to the state of being disturbed.
original_explanation: The state of being disturbed. It's what you feel when you're in deep focus mode ("naka-headset na, 'wag istorbohin") and someone asks you a question that could've been a chat. It's the unexpected "taho!" shout during your 9 AM Zoom call. It's the opposite of "peace and quiet."
usage_notes: Can refer to the state of being disturbed or the act of causing a disturbance itself. Often preceded by 'paumanhin sa...' (apologies for...).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paumanhin po sa **pagkakagambala** sa inyong pag-uusap.","translation":"My apologies for the **interruption** to your conversation."},{"sentence":"Ang ingay mula sa construction ay sanhi ng aming **pagkakagambala**.","translation":"The noise from the construction is the cause of our **disturbance**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagtatala o paglilista ng lahat ng mga ari-arian, paninda, o kagamitan sa isang lugar.
original_explanation: That dreaded end-of-month task at your retail job. It's also what you do to your fridge before going to the grocery to see if you really need another bottle of ketchup. "Kailangan nating mag-imbentaryo sa bodega para malaman kung ano ang kulang."
usage_notes: A formal word used in business, logistics, and accounting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan kami ng manager na **mag-imbentaryo** ng lahat ng gamit sa opisina.","translation":"The manager ordered us **to make an inventory** of all the office equipment."},{"sentence":"Taun-taon silang nagsasara para **mag-imbentaryo**.","translation":"They close annually **to do an inventory**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging nakahiga o nakalagay nang pahalang sa isang daanan, na nagsisilbing hadlang o sagabal.
original_explanation: Picture that truck that broke down sideways on EDSA during rush hour. Or a huge fallen tree blocking a provincial road after a typhoon. That's nakabalagbag. It's not just in the way, it's *aggressively* in the way, blocking everything and everyone.
usage_notes: Implies a large object lying transversely or horizontally, causing an obstruction.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malaking puno ang **nakabalagbag** sa kalsada pagkatapos ng malakas na bagyo.","translation":"A large tree was **lying across** the road after the strong typhoon."}]

translation: state of being in light contact; adherence
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng bahagyang pagdikit o paglapat ng dalawang bagay sa isa't isa.
etymology: From `pag-` + `ka-` + `ka-` (reduplication) + `diit`. The prefix `pagkaka-` indicates the state of light contact.
original_explanation: That brief, accidental touch with your crush in a crowded jeepney that sends 10,000 volts through your body. It’s the state of two things lightly pressed together, like a sticker that's barely hanging on or two people squished together on the MRT during rush hour.
usage_notes: Implies a light, surface-level contact, not a strong bond. It is more delicate than 'pagkakadikit'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa **pagkakadiit** ng kanilang mga balikat, nagsimula ang kanilang pag-iibigan.","translation":"Because of the **light contact** of their shoulders, their romance began."},{"sentence":"Tingnan mo kung maayos ang **pagkakadiit** ng selyo sa sobre.","translation":"Check if the stamp is **adhering** properly to the envelope."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paligsahan ng bilis, tulad ng sa pagtakbo o pagmamaneho; maaari ding tumukoy sa propesyon o larangang pinagkadalubhasaan ng isang tao.
original_explanation: Two meanings, one word. Pwedeng 'yung literal na takbuhan ng kabayo o F1. Or, 'yung "anong course mo?" na naging "anong work mo?" - 'yan ang career path mo. Yung pinagpupuyatan mo sa BPO, 'yan ang karera mo. Yung pag-akyat mo sa corporate ladder, karera din 'yan. The ultimate rat race.
usage_notes: Ang kahulugan ay nakadepende sa konteksto ng pangungusap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumaya siya sa **karera** ng mga kabayo at nanalo ng malaki.","translation":"He bet on the horse **race** and won big."},{"sentence":"Matagumpay ang kanyang **karera** bilang isang abogado.","translation":"Her **career** as a lawyer is successful."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa o pagpapahintulot na isailalim sa prosesong medikal ang isang tao o hayop upang hindi na magkaroon ng anak o supling.
original_explanation: This is what responsible pet owners do. When you take your askal or puspin to the vet para hindi na sila dumami nang dumami, you *magpabaog* them. It's the "snip-snip" verb. Also used in agriculture for plants or clinically for humans.
usage_notes: Commonly used in the context of animal neutering or spaying (pagpapakapon).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang adbokasiya ng city vet ang **magpabaog** ng mga alagang aso at pusa nang libre.","translation":"It's an advocacy of the city vet to **have pet dogs and cats sterilized** for free."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malaki at matibay na puno o kahoy na matatagpuan sa Pilipinas, kilala sa pagiging matatag at ginagamit sa konstruksiyon.
original_explanation: The 'Hulk' of Philippine woods. If narra is the elegant, respected elder, yakal is the buff, super-strong *tito* you'd trust to build your house. It's so famously tough that its name is sometimes used to describe someone who is physically or emotionally resilient. 'Tibay-yakal' means built to last.
usage_notes: Often mentioned in contexts of construction, furniture, and Philippine ecology.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sahig ng lumang bahay ay gawa sa makikintab na tabla ng **yakal**.","translation":"The floor of the old house is made of shiny **yakal** planks."},{"sentence":"Kasing tibay ng **yakal** ang paninindigan niya.","translation":"His conviction is as strong as **yakal**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang karaniwan at hindi mahal na metal, salungat sa mga mahahalagang metal tulad ng ginto o pilak. Ito ay madaling mag-oxidize o masira.
etymology: Isang tambalang salita mula sa 'saligan' (base, foundation) at 'metal' (mula sa Ingles).
original_explanation: Ito yung mga metal na hindi pang-pawnshop. Hindi sila ginto, silver, o platinum. Sila yung tipo ng metal na 'pag nabasa, kinakalawang. Parang sa pagkakaibigan, ito yung 'acquaintance' lang, hindi yung 'best friend' na precious metal.
usage_notes: Isang teknikal na termino sa kimika at metalurhiya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tanso at bakal ay mga halimbawa ng **saligang metal**.","translation":"Copper and iron are examples of **base metal**."},{"sentence":"Ginamit ang isang **saligang metal** para sa pundasyon ng istraktura.","translation":"A **base metal** was used for the foundation of the structure."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang miyembro ng Order of Augustinian Recollects, isang relihiyosong orden sa Simbahang Katoliko.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na "Recoletos" (pangmaramihan ng "Recoleto").
original_explanation: The priests who often run schools like San Sebastian College. They're a specific squad or 'barkada' of priests within the larger Catholic church, known for their focus on community and prayer. Think of them as a specific brand of pari.
usage_notes: Laging naka-kapital dahil ito ay tumutukoy sa isang tiyak na pangngalang pantangi, ang orden ng relihiyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Simbahan ng San Sebastian ay pinamamahalaan ng mga paring **Rekoleto**.","translation":"The San Sebastian Church is administered by the **Recollect** priests."},{"sentence":"Nag-aral siya sa isang paaralang itinatag ng mga **Rekoleto**.","translation":"He studied in a school founded by the **Recollects**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mensahe o paskil sa social media na nagpapahayag ng pasasalamat, paghanga, o pagpapahalaga sa isang tao, bagay, o karanasan.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na pariralang "appreciation post", na naging popular sa social media.
original_explanation: The modern-day 'thank you' card, but for everyone on your feed to see. It's that long, heartfelt Facebook status with 10 tagged photos dedicated to your jowa, your barkada, or even your favorite Grab driver. Usually starts with 'Hindi ko alam paano magsisimula...' and ends with a promise of 'more memories to come'. #Blessed.
usage_notes: Ginagamit lamang sa konteksto ng social media at modernong komunikasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumawa siya ng **appreciation post** para sa kanyang mga magulang noong graduation niya.","translation":"She made an **appreciation post** for her parents during her graduation."},{"sentence":"Ang sweet naman ng jowa mo, may **appreciation post** kaagad para sa'yo.","translation":"Your partner is so sweet, they immediately made an **appreciation post** for you."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kalagayan ng boses na paos, magaspang, o hirap lumabas dahil sa pamamaga ng lalamunan o labis na paggamit nito.
original_explanation: This is the official voice of call center agents after a 12-hour shift, KTV champions the morning after, and teachers at the end of the school week. Your voice sounds like a rusty gate hinge, and every word is a struggle. It's when you try to say 'good morning' but what comes out is a low, gravelly croak that scares small children. The cure? Salabat, water, and shutting up for a while.
usage_notes: Synonymous with 'paos'. 'Malat' is very common in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Malat** ang boses ko dahil sa kakasigaw sa concert kagabi.","translation":"My voice is **hoarse** from shouting at the concert last night."},{"sentence":"Uminom ka ng salabat para mawala ang pagka-**malat** mo.","translation":"Drink some ginger tea to get rid of your **hoarseness**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ipinadala upang maghatid ng mensahe, kumatawan, o magsagawa ng isang partikular na misyon para sa isang pinuno, pangkat, o bansa.
original_explanation: Before Grab or Lalamove, we had the sugo. They're the original couriers, but for more high-stakes stuff like royal decrees or declarations of war, not just your milk tea order. In religious contexts, they're the chosen ones, the prophets. Today, it could be the office intern sent to buy coffee for the bosses—the humble sugo of the pantry.
usage_notes: Often has a formal, official, or religious connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinadala ng hari ang kanyang pinagkakatiwalaang **sugo** sa kabilang kaharian.","translation":"The king sent his trusted **envoy** to the other kingdom."},{"sentence":"Naniniwala sila na si Hesus ay ang **sugo** ng Diyos.","translation":"They believe that Jesus is the **messenger** of God."}]

translation: to confess, to be honest, to admit
meaning_filipino: Sabihin ang katotohanan; umamin sa isang bagay, lalo na sa isang kasalanan o damdamin.
original_explanation: The verb that launches a thousand teleserye plot twists. This is when you finally decide to spill the tea, come clean, or confess your undying love. It's that heart-pounding moment before you say, 'May aaminin ako sa'yo...' It’s the opposite of being 'marupok' and hiding your feelings; it’s about being brave and honest.
usage_notes: Often used for confessing feelings (love, guilt) or revealing a secret.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya siyang **magtapat** ng kanyang pag-ibig sa kanyang matalik na kaibigan.","translation":"He decided to **confess** his love for his best friend."},{"sentence":"Mas mabuting **magtapat** ka na sa iyong mga magulang tungkol sa nangyari.","translation":"It's better to **be honest** with your parents about what happened."}]

translation: will be made to restore; will be caused to be restored
meaning_filipino: Pagsisikapang ibalik sa dati o orihinal na kalagayan, anyo, o kondisyon ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: Imagine your lola's precious vase breaks. Your mom tells you, "**Papanag-uliin** ko sa'yo 'yan!" It means you will be made to restore it to its former glory, piece by tiny piece. Good luck with the super glue! It's a very formal and rare word; you'd more likely hear "ipapaayos" or "ibabalik mo sa dati".
usage_notes: A very formal and rare term for causing something to be restored to a former state. 'Panunumbalikin' or 'ipapaayos' are more common substitutes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang nasirang mural ay **papanag-uliin** sa tulong ng mga lokal na alagad ng sining.","translation":"The damaged mural **will be restored** with the help of local artists."}]

translation: to make a vow; to perform a religious devotion
meaning_filipino: Ang paggawa ng isang solemne o banal na pangako, karaniwang sa Diyos o sa isang santo, bilang bahagi ng isang debosyon na isinasagawa nang paulit-ulit.
original_explanation: This is your sacred promise, your holy 'pamatay' na deal with the heavens. It's walking on your knees to the altar, not eating meat during Lent, or joining the Black Nazarene procession every year. It's a spiritual contract you fulfill, often in exchange for a favor asked or granted. It's leveling up from a simple promise to a full-blown spiritual commitment.
usage_notes: Strongly associated with religious practices, particularly in Filipino Catholicism. It implies a regular, repeated act of devotion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming deboto ang **nagpapanata** sa Quiapo tuwing Biyernes.","translation":"Many devotees **perform their religious vow** in Quiapo every Friday."},{"sentence":"**Nagpanata** siyang mag-ayuno bilang pasasalamat sa paggaling ng kanyang ina.","translation":"He **made a vow** to fast as a sign of gratitude for his mother's recovery."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na pahayag o salaysay ng mga pangyayari, natuklasan, o imbestigasyon.
original_explanation: Sa school, ito yung pinapagawa ng teacher na kailangan mong i-present sa harap ng klase. Sa office, ito yung Excel file na kailangan mong i-submit sa boss mo bago mag-end of day. Sa social media, ito yung ginagawa mo sa mga fake news peddlers at online trolls. It's the ultimate "paki-explain" document.
usage_notes: A very common English loanword used in schools, offices, and online. Often conjugated with Filipino affixes (e.g., 'i-report', 'nag-report').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong tapusin ang **report** ko para bukas.","translation":"I need to finish my **report** for tomorrow."},{"sentence":"**I-report** mo sa pulis ang anumang kahina-hinalang aktibidad.","translation":"**Report** any suspicious activity to the police."}]

translation: to be destined for, to pertain to, to be allotted
meaning_filipino: Ang maging laan, tadhana, o tungkol sa isang partikular na tao, bagay, o layunin.
original_explanation: This is a deep cut, a bit old-school. Think of it as the universe's pre-assigned Jira ticket. If a task or destiny is meant for you, it will "**maukol**" sa'yo. It's like saying "This is meant for you" but with more gravitas and less of a modern "meant to be" vibe. You'd probably hear this from a historian or in a classic Filipino film.
usage_notes: Primarily used in formal or literary writing. Not common in everyday conversation. Often seen in the phrase "nauukol sa" (pertaining to).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang parangal na ito ay **nauukol** sa mga bayaning nagbuwis ng buhay para sa bayan.","translation":"This award **is for** (pertains to) the heroes who gave their lives for the country."},{"sentence":"Sana ang sweldo ko ay **maukol** sa pagbabayad ng bills at hindi lang sa utang.","translation":"I hope my salary will **be allotted** for paying bills and not just debt."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng katawan sa pagitan ng tuhod at sakong.
original_explanation: The part of your leg that gets all the attention during a long walk, a tough workout, or when a mosquito decides to have a feast. It's the "pamatay" part of a beauty queen's walk. In basketball, 'pag pagod ka na, "nangangawit na ang binti."
usage_notes: Specifically refers to the lower leg (shank/calf area). The word for the entire limb from the hip down is "paa," but "paa" can also mean "foot." "Hita" is the thigh. "Binti" is between the knee and ankle.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masakit ang aking **binti** pagkatapos ng mahabang takbuhan.","translation":"My **leg** hurts after the long run."},{"sentence":"May kagat ng lamok ang kanyang makinis na **binti**.","translation":"There's a mosquito bite on her smooth **leg**."}]

translation: to perform a ritual for anitos (spirits/deities)
meaning_filipino: Magsagawa ng isang ritwal o seremonya ng pagsamba o pag-aalay sa mga anito o espiritu ng mga ninuno.
etymology: From Tagalog 'mag-' (verb prefix) + 'anito' (ancestral spirit, nature deity, idol).
original_explanation: This is the OG Filipino spiritual practice, way before your lola started lighting candles to saints. It's about connecting with ancestral spirits or nature deities ('anito'). Think of a 'babaylan' (priestess) leading a community ritual, offering sacrifices, and asking for a good harvest or protection. It’s a deep dive into pre-colonial Philippine history and spirituality.
usage_notes: A historical and anthropological term. Not used in the context of modern, everyday actions but to describe historical or indigenous spiritual practices.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga babaylan ay nagtitipon upang **mag-anito** bago magsimula ang panahon ng pagtatanim.","translation":"The priestesses would gather **to perform a ritual for the spirits** before the planting season began."},{"sentence":"Pinaniniwalaan na ang **pag-anito** ay paraan ng pakikipag-usap sa mga espiritu ng kalikasan.","translation":"It was believed that **performing the anito ritual** was a way to communicate with nature spirits."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang nasa pinakamasamang kalagayan o may pinakamatinding epekto, karaniwang tumutukoy sa sakit, pinsala, o problema.
original_explanation: This is when a situation goes from 'bad' to 'Code Red.' It's not just a cough, it's pneumonia. It's not just a traffic jam, it's EDSA on a payday Friday rain. It's the 'worst-case scenario' actually happening. When a doctor says the patient's condition is **pinakamalubha**, it's time to be seriously concerned.
usage_notes: Almost always used in a negative context, referring to the severity of an illness, injury, problem, or situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa **pinakamalubha** siyang kalagayan kaya kailangan siyang isugod sa ospital.","translation":"He is in the **most severe** condition so he needs to be rushed to the hospital."},{"sentence":"Ang pagbaha ang naging **pinakamalubha** niyang problema sa taong ito.","translation":"The flood became his **worst** problem this year."}]

translation: to be moved, to be shaken, to be disturbed
meaning_filipino: Ang maapektuhan, magalaw, o mabago mula sa isang matatag na posisyon o paninindigan, pisikal man o emosyonal.
original_explanation: Imagine trying to convince your Lola that her old-school remedies are not scientifically proven. If she doesn't change her mind, she's 'di matinag.' It's that unshakeable quality, like your friend who's still a solid fan of a celebrity even after all the cancel culture drama. Can be physical (like a building in an earthquake) or emotional/mental.
usage_notes: Often used in the negative form 'hindi matinag' to mean unshakeable or firm.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit anong pilit, hindi **matinag** ang kanyang desisyon.","translation":"No matter how they insisted, his decision could not **be shaken**."},{"sentence":"Sana'y hindi **matinag** ang ating pananampalataya sa gitna ng pagsubok.","translation":"Hopefully, our faith will not **be shaken** amidst trials."}]

translation: to get fat; to gain weight
meaning_filipino: Ang pagdagdag ng timbang o paglaki ng katawan dahil sa akumulasyon ng taba.
original_explanation: The official result of saying "diet starts tomorrow" for 365 days straight. It's what happens after the holidays, after a breakup feast, or after discovering the magic of unli-rice. A verb that is often used with a mix of 'hugot' and 'handa'.
usage_notes: The verb is in the completed aspect (past tense). The infinitive is 'tumaba', present is 'tumataba', and future is 'tataba'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tumaba** ako nang limang libra pagkatapos ng Pasko.","translation":"I **gained** five pounds after Christmas."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala kung **tumaba** ka, ang mahalaga ay malusog ka.","translation":"Don't worry if you **got fat**, what's important is that you're healthy."}]

translation: to be sued, to be charged in court
meaning_filipino: Maging paksa ng isang pormal na sakdal o akusasyon sa hukuman; ang kasuhan.
etymology: Hango sa salitang Espanyol na 'hablar' (magsalita), na tumutukoy sa pagsasalita o paglalahad sa isang legal na paglilitis.
original_explanation: The moment your 'Amalayer?' or 'You're road?' argument escalates to a legal battle. It's when you receive a formal invitation (a subpoena) to star in your own courtroom drama. The opposite of settling things 'amicably'.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa mga legal o pormal na konteksto. Ang tinutukoy ng pandiwa ay ang taong sinasakdal o kinakasuhan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaari kang **mahabla** kung hindi mo babayaran ang iyong mga utang.","translation":"You can **be sued** if you do not pay your debts."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang masinsinan at paulit-ulit na pagtatanong o pagsisiyasat sa isang bagay upang malaman ang buong katotohanan o detalye.
original_explanation: This is what your chismosa Tita does when she senses you're hiding something about your love life. It's not just asking; it's digging, probing, cross-examining, and connecting dots you didn't even know existed. "Sino 'yun? Taga-saan? Anong trabaho? May kotse ba?" The verbal equivalent of an archaeological dig.
usage_notes: The repetition of "uka" implies a thorough, persistent, and almost invasive level of questioning or investigation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang **uka-ukain** pa ang nakaraan, mag-move on ka na.","translation":"Don't **probe** into the past anymore, just move on."},{"sentence":"**Inuka-uka** ng imbestigador ang bawat detalye ng krimen.","translation":"The investigator **persistently questioned** every detail of the crime."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paraang nagkukunwari o nagpapanggap; tila totoo ngunit hindi naman.
original_explanation: The official word for 'acting lang'. It's when you pretend to be busy when your boss walks by, or when you act surprised by a birthday party you already knew about. 'Kunwari ka pa!' is what you say to a friend who's being pa-humble but is secretly proud. It's the foundation of all childhood 'bahay-bahayan' games.
usage_notes: A very common word to describe pretense or a hypothetical situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-usap sila **kunwari** hindi sila magkakilala.","translation":"They talked, **pretending** they didn't know each other."},{"sentence":"**Kunwari** masakit ang ulo niya para hindi siya mautusan.","translation":"**Supposedly** his head hurts so he won't be asked to run errands."}]

translation: to be able to cause panic or confusion
meaning_filipino: Magdulot o maging sanhi ng pagkabahala, pagkalito, o pagkasindak sa iba.
original_explanation: That one friend who screams "SUNOG!" as a joke, causing everyone to freak out. Or when a sudden "urgent" email from the boss at 4:59 PM causes the whole team to go into headless chicken mode. That's how you makataranta. "Huwag kang sumigaw, baka makataranta ka ng mga tao."
usage_notes: The "maka-" prefix here is causative, meaning "to cause" the state of the root word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang maling balita ay maaaring **makataranta** sa publiko.","translation":"False news can **cause panic** among the public."},{"sentence":"Naisip niyang baka **makataranta** lang siya kung sasabihin niya agad ang problema.","translation":"He thought that he might just **cause confusion** if he immediately stated the problem."}]

translation: Act of getting wet, being drenched
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging nababad sa tubig o anumang likido.
original_explanation: That feeling when you forget your umbrella and a sudden downpour hits during your commute. It’s the universe's way of saying, "Surprise! You're taking a shower now." Often leads to the phrase, "Basang sisiw."
usage_notes: While "pagbasa" can be used colloquially, "pagkabasa" is more precise for denoting the state of being wet.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang biglaang **pagbasa** ng ulan ay naging sanhi ng kanyang pagkakasakit.","translation":"The sudden **drenching** from the rain caused his sickness."},{"sentence":"Iwasan ang **pagbasa** ng cellphone upang hindi masira.","translation":"Avoid the **wetting** of the cellphone so it won't get damaged."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang estado ng pagiging hilaw o hindi pa ganap na luto o hinog. Tumutukoy din sa kawalan ng karanasan o pagiging bata pa.
original_explanation: This is the state of being 'green'—literally for fruits, figuratively for people. It's that intern who accidentally hits 'Reply All' on a company-wide email. It's the mango that's more sour than your ex's heart. It's a vibe of 'not yet ready for primetime'.
usage_notes: Can refer to food (unripe fruit, uncooked meat) or people (inexperienced, immature).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo munang pitasin ang mangga, kitang-kita pa ang **kahilawan** nito.","translation":"Don't pick the mango yet, its **unripeness** is still very obvious."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **kahilawan**, marami pa siyang dapat matutunan sa trabaho.","translation":"Because of his **immaturity** / **inexperience**, he still has much to learn at work."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, kumpanya, o bansa na lumilikha, gumagawa, o naglilinang ng mga produkto, kalakal, o palabas sa sining tulad ng pelikula o telebisyon.
original_explanation: In showbiz, they're the "money-person" who makes the movie or teleserye happen. They're the one Vice Ganda thanks profusely at the end of every film. In business, they're the ones making the stuff you add to your Shopee cart at 3 AM. Basically, the person with the capital P, whether that's Pera or Power.
usage_notes: A direct loanword used commonly in business, media, and entertainment contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **producer** ng pelikula ang naghahanap ng pondo para sa proyekto.","translation":"The **producer** of the movie is the one who looks for funding for the project."},{"sentence":"Ang Pilipinas ay isa sa mga nangungunang **producer** ng niyog sa buong mundo.","translation":"The Philippines is one of the leading **producers** of coconut in the world."}]

meaning_filipino: Gumagamit ng kamay upang mahigpitan ang kapit sa isang bagay; may kontrol o kapangyarihan sa isang sitwasyon.
original_explanation: What your mom is doing to her purse in Divisoria. What you are doing to your phone 24/7. What you wish your crush was doing to your hand. It's the act of holding on, whether it's to your last 100 pesos before sweldo or to a 'situationship'.
usage_notes: Present progressive tense of 'humawak'. Can mean physically holding or metaphorically being in control.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit siyang **humahawak** sa kamay ng kanyang ina habang tumatawid.","translation":"She **is holding** tightly to her mother's hand while crossing the street."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **humahawak** sa proyektong ito ngayon?","translation":"Who **is holding** (in charge of) this project now?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapang panggupit na binubuo ng dalawang talim na pinagdudugtong sa gitna at may mga butas sa kabilang dulo para sa mga daliri.
original_explanation: The ultimate tool for cutting things, whether it's paper for your kid's project, your bangs during a quarantine crisis, or ties with a toxic ex. 'Guntingin na natin ang communication,' as they say.
usage_notes: Used for general cutting. Can also refer to the act of cutting in some contexts, but more often the tool itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiabot ng **gunting**, puputulin ko lang itong sinulid.","translation":"Please hand me the **scissors**, I'll just cut this thread."},{"sentence":"Nawawala na naman ang **gunting** sa kusina.","translation":"The **scissors** in the kitchen are missing again."}]

translation: one who tends to take back what is given
meaning_filipino: Isang taong may ugaling bawiin ang mga bagay na naibigay na niya, literal man o sa usapan.
original_explanation: You know that friend who treats you to lunch then brings it up for the next 5 years? Or someone who gives you a gift and then asks for it back when they get mad? That's a classic palabawi. It's the ultimate "walang bigay-bawi" violator. They give with strings attached, and those strings are bungee cords.
usage_notes: Describes a negative personality trait.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayokong humingi ng pabor sa kanya kasi **palabawi** 'yun.","translation":"I don't want to ask for a favor from them because they're the type to **always take things back**."}]

translation: to give or take an enema
meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit o pagsasagawa ng labatiba, isang pamamaraang medikal ng pagpasok ng likido sa tumbong at malaking bituka upang linisin ito.
original_explanation: Okay, let's be mature about this. This is the verb for using an enema. It's that medical procedure you hope you'll never need, often used for constipation or before certain surgeries. It's the ultimate 'pampadumi' when all else fails. Not exactly a topic for the dinner table, but a word you should know for... emergencies.
usage_notes: A medical term. Not used in everyday casual conversation unless discussing health issues.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inutusan ng doktor ang nars na **maglabatiba** sa pasyente bago ang operasyon.","translation":"The doctor instructed the nurse to **give an enema** to the patient before the operation."},{"sentence":"Kailangan daw niyang **maglabatiba** dahil sa matinding konstipasyon.","translation":"They said he needs to **take an enema** due to severe constipation."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa balarila, tumutukoy ito sa uri ng pangngalan na hindi tiyak at karaniwan, tulad ng 'aso', 'lugar', o 'tao'. Ito ay nagsisimula sa maliit na titik maliban kung ito ay nasa simula ng pangungusap.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "pan-" at salitang "balana" (everyone, the public). Ang /n/ sa "pan-" ay nagiging /m/ dahil sa kasunod na tunog na /b/.
original_explanation: Remember your Filipino class? This is the opposite of 'Pantangi' (proper noun). 'Pangngalang Pambalana' is your 'common noun'. It's the 'aso' (dog) not 'Bantay', the 'babae' (woman) not 'Maria Clara'. It’s generic, not specific. The 'anybody' in a sea of 'somebodies'.
usage_notes: Ito ay isang terminong pang-gramatika at halos eksklusibong ginagamit sa konteksto ng pag-aaral ng wika.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang salitang 'lapis' ay isang halimbawa ng pangngalang **pambalana**.","translation":"The word 'pencil' is an example of a **common** noun."},{"sentence":"Itinuro ng guro ang pagkakaiba ng pangngalang pantangi at **pambalana**.","translation":"The teacher taught the difference between proper and **common** nouns."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang laman o karne mula sa isang batang baka, na karaniwang mas malambot at mas maputla kaysa sa karne ng baka na nasa hustong gulang.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "carne" (karne) at Tagalog na "guya" (batang baka o kalabaw).
original_explanation: Fancy meat! This is the meat from a baby cow. You usually find this in high-end restaurants, not your typical karinderya. It's like the "intern" of the beef world – young, tender, and hasn't seen much of the world (or the pasture).
