usage_notes: Isang uri ng karne na hindi gaanong karaniwan sa pang-araw-araw na lutuing Pilipino ngunit ginagamit sa mga espesyal na okasyon o sa mga restawran na naghahain ng lutuing Kanluranin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-order siya ng **karne ng guya** para sa kanilang anibersaryo.","translation":"He ordered **veal** for their anniversary."},{"sentence":"Mas mahal ang **karne ng guya** kaysa sa ordinaryong karneng-baka.","translation":"**Veal** is more expensive than regular beef."}]

translation: to cause numbness; to act numb
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging sanhi ng kawalan ng pakiramdam sa isang bahagi ng katawan; o ang pagpapanggap na walang nararamdaman o walang pakialam.
original_explanation: Two kinds: 1) The dentist version, where they inject something to make your face feel like a block of wood. 2) The 'hugot' version. This is what you do after a breakup. You go emotionally numb, pretending you don't care while binge-watching Netflix. It’s the emotional equivalent of anesthesia.
usage_notes: Can refer to literal, physical numbness (e.g., from cold or anesthesia) or figurative, emotional numbness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglagay siya ng yelo sa pasa para **magpamanhid** ng sakit.","translation":"He put ice on the bruise to **cause numbness** to the pain."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng lahat ng pinagdaanan niya, pinili niyang **magpamanhid** na lang sa halip na umiyak.","translation":"After everything she went through, she chose to just **act numb** instead of crying."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagbago o nasira ang orihinal na anyo, hugis, o itsura; may kapansanan sa pisikal na kaanyuan.
original_explanation: When something is so messed up, its original shape is gone. Like your face after an intense boxing match, or that doll from your childhood that your younger sibling 'gave a haircut' to. It can also be used for things, like a 'dispiguradong' box that got crushed in transit.
usage_notes: A strong word used to describe significant physical alteration or damage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naiwan siyang **dispigurado** dahil sa malubhang aksidente.","translation":"He was left **disfigured** due to a serious accident."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal para sa isang isyu, reklamo, drama, o anumang pinagkakaabalahan o pinag-uusapan nang may himig ng pagkadismaya o pagkaaliw.
etymology: A popular slang term, likely originating from gay lingo, possibly as a playful alteration of 'ano as in...?' or 'hanapbuhay', which evolved to mean 'what's your issue/business?'.
original_explanation: Your daily dose of drama or chismis. It's that thing your friend rants about for 30 minutes straight. "Ano na namang hanash 'yan?" is the Filipino way of saying "What's the tea now?" It can be a minor annoyance or a full-blown issue. Basically, any situation that makes you go "Hay nako."
usage_notes: A very common slang term, especially among younger generations and in the LGBTQ+ community. Can also be used as a verb 'mag-hanash' (to rant or complain).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang dami mong **hanash** sa buhay, mag-relax ka nga.","translation":"You have so much **drama** in your life, just relax."},{"sentence":"May bagong **hanash** na naman si Marites tungkol sa kapitbahay.","translation":"Marites has new **gossip** again about the neighbor."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang troli na itinutulak ng mga mamimili sa loob ng supermarket o pamilihan upang paglagyan ng kanilang mga pinamili.
original_explanation: The official vehicle of your tita during a 50% off sale at the grocery. It's what you use to hoard toilet paper and corned beef. Also, the thing you always get with a wonky wheel that makes a loud noise all over the supermarket.
usage_notes: Partikular na tumutukoy sa shopping cart. Ang 'troli' (mula sa 'trolley') ay ginagamit din minsan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Punuin na natin ang **kart** at magbayad na sa cashier.","translation":"Let's fill up the **cart** and pay at the cashier."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbebenta ng isda bilang hanapbuhay. Ito rin ay tumutukoy sa hinaharap na kilos ng pagtitinda ng isda.
original_explanation: This is what your suki at the palengke does for a living. Also, it's what you'll do this weekend if your tita from the province sends you a whole cooler of bangus. "Uy, mag-iisda muna ako sa FB Marketplace, ang daming bigay ni Tita!"
usage_notes: This is the future tense or contemplative aspect of the verb 'mag-isda' (to sell fish).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Mag-iisda** si Aling Nena sa palengke bukas ng umaga.","translation":"Aling Nena **will sell fish** at the market tomorrow morning."},{"sentence":"Plano kong **mag-iisda** para may dagdag na kita.","translation":"I plan **to sell fish** for extra income."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang halaga ng pera o bagay na hiniram na kailangang isauli o bayaran sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: The national pastime. 'Yung bagay na mas madaling kunin kaysa bayaran. Parang 'yung feelings mo for your crush na 'di masabi-sabi, laging pending. Sa Pilipinas, may utang ka sa bumbay, sa 5-6, sa kapitbahay, at sa gobyerno via taxes.
usage_notes: Can refer to monetary debt, a favor, or a debt of gratitude (see utang-na-loob). The concept is deeply embedded in Filipino social dynamics.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang **utang** ko sa bangko dahil sa pinapatayong bahay.","translation":"I have a large **debt** to the bank because of the house I'm having built."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutan bayaran ang **utang** mo sa akin.","translation":"Don't forget to pay your **debt** to me."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormat ng file para sa mga imahe na sumusuporta sa parehong di-gumagalaw at gumagalaw (animated) na mga larawan.
original_explanation: That moving picture you send in your group chat when words are not enough to express your reaction. Whether you pronounce it "gif" or "jif," it's the lifeblood of internet memes and Messenger reactions. It's how you show you're laughing, crying, or cringing without typing a single letter.
usage_notes: The pronunciation debate ('hard G' vs 'soft G') exists in the Philippines as it does elsewhere, though 'hard G' is more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-send ka ng **gif** para mas masaya 'yung usapan.","translation":"Send a **gif** so the conversation is more fun."},{"sentence":"Tawang-tawa ako sa **gif** na pinost mo sa Facebook.","translation":"I was laughing so hard at the **gif** you posted on Facebook."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pahayag, pasulat o pasalita, na naglalarawan sa isang tao, bagay, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: That block of text on Shopee or Lazada under the product picture? That's the `deskripsiyon`. It's supposed to tell you what you're buying, but sometimes it feels like a creative writing project. "High-quality, elegant, life-changing phone case." Okay, sure.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Basahin mong mabuti ang **deskripsiyon** ng produkto bago ka mag-check out.","translation":"Read the product **description** carefully before you check out."},{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng **deskripsiyon** niya sa tanawin, parang nandoon na rin ako.","translation":"Her **description** of the scenery was so beautiful, it's as if I were there too."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng sasakyang panghimpapawid na may malalaking umiikot na talim (rotor blades) sa itaas na nagbibigay-daan dito upang lumipad nang patayo, paurong-sulong, o manatili sa isang lugar.
etymology: Hiram na salita mula sa Ingles na "helicopter", na isinunod sa baybaying Filipino.
original_explanation: 'Yung sasakyan sa pelikula na laging dumadating for a dramatic rescue or escape. Sa totoong buhay, ito 'yung naririnig mo sa taas 'pag may V.I.P. na dadaan at na-traffic ka na naman sa EDSA. Helicopter parent? 'Yan 'yung magulang na laging naka-hover sa'yo.
usage_notes: Isang modernong sasakyang panghimpapawid.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ang **helikopter** sa paghahatid ng tulong sa mga lugar na nasalanta ng bagyo.","translation":"The **helicopter** was used to deliver aid to the areas devastated by the typhoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang alituntunin o sistema ng mga alituntunin na kinikilala ng isang bansa o komunidad bilang regulasyon sa mga kilos ng mga miyembro nito.
original_explanation: The high-falutin' Spanish word for 'batas.' You'll hear this from old-school lawyers or in historical dramas. It's like the OG 'rules of the game' before it was cool to just call it 'batas.'
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa mga legal o pangkasaysayang konteksto. Ang 'batas' ay ang mas karaniwang termino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **ley** militar ay isang madilim na kabanata sa kasaysayan ng Pilipinas.","translation":"Martial **law** is a dark chapter in Philippine history."},{"sentence":"Ayon sa **ley**, ang lahat ay pantay-pantay sa mata ng batas.","translation":"According to the **law**, everyone is equal in the eyes of the law."}]

translation: to make a vow for; to make a devotion of
meaning_filipino: Gawing isang panata o taimtim na pangako ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay may kinalaman sa relihiyon o isang malalim na paniniwala.
original_explanation: This is leveling up your promise to a sacred vow. It's what devotees do during Holy Week, walking for miles as a 'panata'. Or when you swear to yourself, 'Ipanata ko na hindi na ako kakain ng fast food for a month' after seeing your weight. It’s a promise with spiritual or deeply personal stakes.
usage_notes: Strongly associated with religious or solemn vows.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Taon-taon niyang **ipinapanata** ang pag-akyat sa bundok bilang pasasalamat.","translation":"Every year, he **makes a devotion of** climbing the mountain as a form of thanksgiving."},{"sentence":"**Ipanata** mo sa iyong sarili na magiging mas mabuting tao ka.","translation":"**Make a vow** to yourself that you will become a better person."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na nangyayari o kailangan nang mabilisan at walang pagpapaliban.
original_explanation: Describes something that needs to happen NOW. A 'kagyat na pangangailangan' is an urgent need, like needing WiFi before a Zoom call. A 'kagyat na desisyon' is a snap decision, like impulse-buying something from a Shopee flash sale.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kagyat** na tulong ay ipinadala sa mga biktima ng bagyo.","translation":"**Immediate** aid was sent to the victims of the typhoon."},{"sentence":"Isang **kagyat** na pagpupulong ang ipinatawag ng manager.","translation":"An **urgent** meeting was called by the manager."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng kalayaan sa isang tao, hayop, o bagay na nakakulong, nakatali, o nasa ilalim ng kapangyarihan ng iba.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'let go' move. Whether it's releasing a bird from its cage, freeing a nation from colonizers, or finally letting go of that toxic ex. It's the act of un-caging, un-chaining, and un-following in real life. 'Friend, it's time to **magpalaya**... ng sama ng loob.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga bayani ay lumaban upang **magpalaya** sa bansa.","translation":"The heroes fought to **liberate** the country."},{"sentence":"Panahon na para **magpalaya** ka mula sa masamang nakaraan.","translation":"It is time for you to **set yourself free** from the bad past."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na bula sa balat na naglalaman ng likido, sanhi ng pagkiskis o pagkasunog. Maaari ring mangahulugang pagkakamali o hindi pagtama.
original_explanation: **Paltos** is what you get on your feet after wearing new shoes to a party without socks. It's that bubble of pain and regret. Figuratively, it's also a 'miss' or a 'failure.' 'Yung nag-effort ka mag-shoot ng basura sa trash can from a distance, pero sumablay? That's also a **paltos**. A physical ouch or a metaphorical one.
usage_notes: Used both literally for a skin blister ('lintos' is a synonym) and figuratively for a miss or failure ('sablay' is a synonym).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ako ng **paltos** sa paa dahil sa bago kong sapatos.","translation":"I got a **blister** on my foot from my new shoes."},{"sentence":"**Paltos** ang lahat ng kaniyang mga tira sa basketball ring.","translation":"All his shots at the basketball ring were a **miss**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang institusyon na nagbibigay ng panggagamot at lunas sa mga may sakit o nasugatan, na pinamamahalaan ng mga doktor at nars.
original_explanation: The place you end up after eating too much isaw from that one street vendor. It's where your PhilHealth card suddenly becomes your most prized possession. Also, the default setting for the climax of many Filipino teleseryes.
usage_notes: Isang napakakaraniwang salita. Maaaring baybayin na 'ospital' o ang mas lumang 'hospital'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isinugod siya sa **ospital** matapos ang aksidente.","translation":"He was rushed to the **hospital** after the accident."},{"sentence":"Nagtatrabaho ang nanay ko bilang nars sa isang malaking **ospital**.","translation":"My mother works as a nurse in a big **hospital**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pormal at hayagang pag-aanunsyo sa publiko ng isang romantikong relasyon, karaniwang ginagawa sa social media.
etymology: From the English phrase 'hard launch,' originally used in marketing for a product's official, full-scale release.
original_explanation: The opposite of a 'soft launch' where you only show your jowa's hand holding a coffee cup. A 'hard launch' is the full-face reveal, the 'ito na siya, mga marites!' post on Facebook or Instagram. It's changing your relationship status from 'Single' to 'In a Relationship' and waiting for the 'Sana all!' comments to pour in.
usage_notes: A very recent slang term adopted from English social media culture, primarily used by younger generations (Gen Z, Millennials) to describe making a relationship public.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-**hard launch** na sa wakas si Bea at Dominic sa kanilang Instagram.","translation":"Bea and Dominic finally did a **hard launch** of their relationship on their Instagram."},{"sentence":"Hintayin ko muna mag-one year kami bago ako mag-**hard launch**.","translation":"I'll wait until we're one year in before I do a **hard launch**."}]

translation: to find something smelly; to be affected by a foul odor
meaning_filipino: Ang maramdaman o maapektuhan ng masamang amoy mula sa isang bagay, tao, o lugar.
original_explanation: That feeling when your officemate opens their baon of bagoong or kimchi and suddenly the whole pantry smells like it. You've been 'mabahuan'. It's an olfactory assault that makes you question your life choices and your proximity to the microwave.
usage_notes: Often used to express disgust or discomfort due to a bad smell. Can be used in both a passive sense (being subjected to a smell) and an active sense (perceiving a smell as bad).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayokong pumasok sa kwartong iyon dahil baka **mabahuan** lang ako sa mga medyas niya.","translation":"I don't want to enter that room because I might just be **overwhelmed by the foul smell** of his socks."},{"sentence":"**Nabahuan** ako sa isda kaya hindi ko na kinain.","translation":"I **found the fish smelly**, so I didn't eat it anymore."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga bagay o nilalang na nabibilang sa iisang grupo, klase, o kategorya.
etymology: From `mag-` (prefix indicating relationship/reciprocity) + `ka-` (prefix indicating being part of a pair/group) + `uri` (type, kind).
original_explanation: Parang mga Funko Pop sa collection mo, kahit iba-iba ang character, lahat sila Funko Pop pa rin. O kaya 'yung mga kaibigan mong lahat mahilig sa K-Pop, kayo ay magkakauri ng fans.
usage_notes: Used for classification of objects, people, or concepts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinagsama-sama niya ang lahat ng prutas na **magkakauri**.","translation":"He grouped together all the fruits that are **of the same kind**."},{"sentence":"Ang mga aso at lobo ay **magkakauri**.","translation":"Dogs and wolves are **of the same type** (of the same family)."}]

meaning_filipino: Patawan ng parusang kamatayan sa pamamagitan ng pagbigti.
original_explanation: A very heavy word, straight out of a history book or a dramatic movie. This refers specifically to execution by hanging, like what happened to Gomburza. Not a word you use lightly. It's the ultimate 'game over' in the most brutal way.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to the act of capital punishment by hanging.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga traydor sa kaharian ay hinatulang **mabitay**.","translation":"The traitors to the kingdom were sentenced **to be hanged**."},{"sentence":"Si José Rizal ay hindi **nabitay**, kundi binaril sa Bagumbayan.","translation":"José Rizal was not **hanged**, but was shot in Bagumbayan."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na may tungkulin o pananagutang gawin ang isang bagay dahil sa batas, kasunduan, o moral na dahilan.
original_explanation: That feeling when your tita asks you to sing at the family reunion. You don't want to, but you feel 'utang na loob' so you're ubligado. It's the social contract that makes you do things, from giving 'pasalubong' to helping a relative find a job. You're not legally bound, but socially, you're cornered.
usage_notes: Often used to express a sense of social or moral duty rather than a strict legal one.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ubligado** kang tulungan ang iyong mga magulang sa kanilang pagtanda.","translation":"You are **obliged** to help your parents in their old age."},{"sentence":"Hindi ako **ubligado** na sundin ang lahat ng gusto mo.","translation":"I'm not **obliged** to follow everything you want."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang opisyal na nagtatakda ng halaga ng ari-arian para sa layunin ng pagbubuwis. Maaari ring tumukoy sa isang tagapayo.
original_explanation: Sila yung mga taga-city hall na nagsasabi kung magkano ang value ng lupa't bahay mo. 'Pag tumaas ang assessment nila, tataas din ang babayaran mong amilyar. Sila ang dahilan kung bakit napapakamot ka sa ulo 'pag dumating ang tax declaration.
usage_notes: Isang opisyal na termino sa gobyerno, lalo na sa mga lokal na yunit ng pamahalaan (LGU).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **asesor** ng lungsod ang nag-apruba sa bagong halaga ng aming ari-arian.","translation":"The city **assessor** approved the new value of our property."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong magsumite ng mga dokumento sa opisina ng **asesor**.","translation":"You need to submit the documents to the **assessor's** office."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lalaking baboy na hindi pa kapon at karaniwang ginagamit sa pagpapalahi.
original_explanation: Sa farm, siya 'yung 'The Man.' Siya 'yung alpha male pig na taga-gawa ng mga cute na biik. Sa office, 'yan 'yung officemate mong laging nagyayabang, parang siya ang hari. 'Feeling bulugan.'
usage_notes: Specifically refers to a male pig for breeding purposes. Can be used metaphorically to describe a virile or domineering man, sometimes pejoratively.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si Mang Tasyo ng bagong **bulugan** para sa kanyang babuyan.","translation":"Mang Tasyo bought a new **boar** for his piggery."},{"sentence":"Malakas at malusog ang **bulugan** na iyon.","translation":"That **stud pig** is strong and healthy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaikling salita para sa "picture" o litrato.
etymology: Pinaikling anyo ng salitang Ingles na 'picture'.
original_explanation: The short and sweet version of 'picture.' It's what you say when you're in a hurry to capture a moment. 'Uy, pic tayo!' is the universal call to action for a group photo. It's faster to type, faster to say, and gets the job done. In the world of DMs, it's also the polite (or not-so-polite) way to ask for a photo: 'Send pic.'
usage_notes: Lubhang karaniwan sa impormal na usapan, parehong pasalita at pasulat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pa-send naman ng **pic** natin kanina.","translation":"Can you send our **pic** from earlier?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na labis na umaasa o nahuhumaling sa isang partikular na substansiya, gawain, o bagay, na kadalasan ay may masamang epekto.
original_explanation: Originally for drug users, but now it's for anyone obsessed. "Adik sa K-drama," "Adik sa milk tea," "Adik sa ML (Mobile Legends)." It's the Pinoy way of saying you're super into something, whether it's a substance or your latest online shopping haul from Shopee.
usage_notes: While it can still refer to drug addiction, its colloquial use for general obsession is very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **adik** siya sa paglalaro ng video games kaya napabayaan niya ang pag-aaral.","translation":"He became an **addict** to playing video games, so he neglected his studies."},{"sentence":"Hala, **adik** ka na sa kape, pang-apat mo na 'yan!","translation":"Wow, you're a coffee **addict**, that's your fourth cup already!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na nakasulat na kahilingan, karaniwang nilagdaan ng maraming tao, na naglalayong mag-apela sa isang partikular na awtoridad hinggil sa isang partikular na layunin.
original_explanation: Ito yung group project niyo para pilitin ang isang tao o kumpanya na gawin ang gusto niyo. Parang online "change.org" pero sa papel, na may kasamang pagod sa pagkuha ng pirma. 'Pag galit na ang buong barangay sa Meralco, gawa na ng petisyon!
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglunsad sila ng isang **petisyon** upang itigil ang pagputol ng mga puno sa kanilang komunidad.","translation":"They launched a **petition** to stop the cutting of trees in their community."},{"sentence":"Libu-libong pirma ang nakalap ng **petisyon** para sa mas mataas na sahod ng mga guro.","translation":"The **petition** for higher teacher salaries gathered thousands of signatures."}]

translation: to gnaw; to chew on something hard
meaning_filipino: Ngatngatin o kainin nang may kahirapan ang isang bagay na matigas, tulad ng buto, tubo, o matigas na kakanin.
original_explanation: What a dog does to a bone, or what you do to the last bit of meat stuck on a chicken wing. It's the determined, slightly desperate act of getting every last bit of flavor. Also, what you do to the end of your pen when you're stressed about an exam.
usage_notes: Often implies a persistent, slow, and sometimes noisy chewing or gnawing action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatutuwang panoorin ang aso habang ito ay **nag-uungot** ng buto.","translation":"It's amusing to watch the dog while it **gnaws** on a bone."},{"sentence":"Nahirapan siyang **mag-ungot** ng matigas na candy.","translation":"He had a hard time **chewing on** the hard candy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong hindi nakikinig sa payo o pangaral; matigas ang ulo at hindi tumatanggap ng opinyon ng iba.
original_explanation: Literally 'blocked ears.' This is your friend who keeps going back to their toxic ex even after you've given them a 10-slide PowerPoint presentation on why it's a bad idea. They hear you, but the information just bounces off. Sila yung tipo na, 'Oo, gets ko,' pero a-ayun, ginawa pa rin.
usage_notes: Functions as a descriptive phrase for a person. Often used with a sense of frustration by the speaker.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit anong pangaral ang gawin mo, **harang ang tainga** ng batang iyan.","translation":"No matter how much you advise him, that kid is **deaf to advice**."},{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang magsayang ng laway, **harang ang tainga** niyan sa opinyon ng iba.","translation":"Don't waste your breath, he's **stubborn** and doesn't listen to others' opinions."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paraan o kilos ng pagkuha, pag-amin, o pag-ako sa isang bagay na ibinigay, ipinagkaloob, o nangyari.
etymology: From "pag-" (manner of) + "ka-" (abstract noun prefix) + "tanggap" (to receive, to accept).
original_explanation: How you react when you get a package you ordered from Shopee vs. how you react when you get your credit card bill. That's pagkakatanggap. It's also about how you handle feedback—'yung pagkakatanggap mo sa "constructive criticism" ng boss mo, even if it feels more like "destructive." It's your reception, your take, your vibe upon receiving something.
usage_notes: Can refer to the physical act of receiving or the emotional/mental act of accepting a situation or idea.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iba ang naging **pagkakatanggap** niya sa balita kumpara sa inaasahan namin.","translation":"His/Her **manner of acceptance** of the news was different from what we expected."},{"sentence":"Pinirmahan niya ang dokumento bilang patunay ng **pagkakatanggap** ng sahod.","translation":"He/She signed the document as proof of **receipt** of the salary."}]

translation: to weaken; to become quiet; to decrease in intensity
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbaba ng lakas, ingay, o sigla; ang pagiging mahina.
original_explanation: This verb covers everything that's losing its power. Your WiFi signal when you move to the kitchen? 'Humihina'. The chismis volume when the boss walks by? 'Humihina'. Your motivation on a Wednesday afternoon? 'Humihina'. Your love life? Uh oh...
usage_notes: A very versatile word used for physical strength, sound volume, signal strength, economic activity, feelings, etc.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Humina** ang boses niya dahil sa ubo.","translation":"Her voice **became weak** because of her cough."},{"sentence":"Pakilakasan ang TV, **humihina** na naman.","translation":"Please turn up the TV, it's **getting quiet** again."},{"sentence":"Simula nang mag-resign siya, **humina** ang benta ng kumpanya.","translation":"Ever since he resigned, the company's sales **weakened**."}]

translation: to join, to participate, to enter (a contest)
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagiging bahagi ng isang grupo, gawain, paligsahan, o organisasyon.
original_explanation: The official verb of every Filipino 'tita' asking her 'pamangkin': "Why don't you 'sumali' in the family parlor games?" It's what you do when you see a 'pa-raffle' on Facebook, or when your office crush joins the company fun run and you suddenly become a fitness enthusiast.
usage_notes: A very common verb used for joining anything from a club to a conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **sumali** sa basketball team ng paaralan.","translation":"I want **to join** the school's basketball team."},{"sentence":"Sino'ng gustong **sumali** sa aming laro?","translation":"Who wants **to participate** in our game?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hanay o hilera ng mga bagay na nakaayos nang patong-patong o magkakasunod, tulad ng mga upuan sa sinehan o istante.
original_explanation: Think of it as the levels in a game, but for real-life stuff. The different layers of a wedding cake, the rows of seats at the Araneta Coliseum, or the shelves in your cabinet where you hide your snacks from your siblings. 'Nasa itaas na andana yung mga imported na corned beef.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ang lahat ng **andana** ng upuan sa teatro.","translation":"All the **tiers** of seats in the theater were full."},{"sentence":"Inayos niya ang mga de lata sa tatlong **andana** ng estante.","translation":"She arranged the canned goods on three **levels** of the shelf."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa kalagayang sarado, lalo na ang mga pinto, bintana, o anumang maaaring isara.
original_explanation: 'Yung pinto ng kwarto ng teenager na ayaw magpapasok. O 'yung isipan ng ka-debate mo na kahit anong ebidensya ang ipakita mo, 'di na magbabago. It's more formal and final than just "sarado." It's sealed shut.
usage_notes: A more formal or literary word for "sarado" (closed).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging **nakapinid** ang mga bintana ng matandang bahay na iyon.","translation":"The windows of that old house are always **shut**."},{"sentence":"Mananatiling **nakapinid** ang aking mga labi tungkol sa sikretong iyon.","translation":"My lips will remain **sealed** about that secret."}]

translation: a type of large lift net (for fishing)
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malaking lambat na ginagamit sa pangingisda, na ibinababa sa tubig at pagkatapos ay mabilis na inaangat upang makahuli ng isda.
original_explanation: The OG 'group project' of fishing. Imagine a giant, square mosquito net (kulambo) on a bamboo raft. You lower it, wait for the fish to have a party on top, then you and your buddies lift it up. Sapyaw is all about teamwork and timing, kind of like trying to get a group picture where everyone looks good.
usage_notes: A specific term in fishing, primarily known in coastal communities.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming nahuling isda ang mga mangingisda gamit ang kanilang **sapyaw**.","translation":"The fishermen caught a lot of fish using their **lift net**."},{"sentence":"Kinukumpuni nila ang nasirang **sapyaw** bago pumalaot muli.","translation":"They are repairing the damaged **sapyaw** before going out to sea again."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mga kanais-nais na pag-uugali, gawi, at kilos na naaayon sa pamantayan ng lipunan at moralidad.
original_explanation: What your lola and your Grade 1 teacher tried to drill into you. Saying 'po' and 'opo', not talking with your mouth full, and offering your seat on the MRT to the elderly. It's the social currency that proves you were raised right. The lack of it is a favorite topic for 'Marites' everywhere.
usage_notes: A core concept in Filipino values, often taught in schools under 'Good Manners and Right Conduct' (GMRC).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagpapakita ng **mabuting asal** ay tanda ng paggalang sa kapwa.","translation":"Showing **good manners** is a sign of respect for others."},{"sentence":"Tinuturuan ng mga magulang ang kanilang mga anak ng **mabuting asal**.","translation":"Parents teach their children **good conduct**."}]

meaning_filipino: May katangian ng pagiging maliit, makinis, o malinis ang pagkakagawa; tumutukoy din sa magandang asal o pagiging mahinhin.
original_explanation: Can refer to two things: 1) The texture of something, like 'pinong buhangin' at the beach in Boracay. It's the opposite of 'magaspang' (rough). 2) A person's character. A 'pinong' person is refined, well-mannered, probably doesn't shout 'Darna!' in the middle of traffic. Think Maria Clara but with a 2026 mindset.
usage_notes: Can describe both physical texture and a person's demeanor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang **pinong** asukal para sa keyk.","translation":"She used **fine** sugar for the cake."},{"sentence":"Isang **pinong** dalaga si Maria, mahinhin kumilos at magsalita.","translation":"Maria is a **refined** lady, graceful in her movements and speech."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-eendorso o pag-aanunsyo ng isang produkto, serbisyo, o kaganapan, lalo na sa paraang di-pormal o sa kalagitnaan ng ibang usapan.
etymology: From English 'plug' (in the sense of promotion).
original_explanation: That 'by the way' moment your friend uses to promote their new online shop, YouTube channel, or 'for sale' posts. To 'mag-plug' is to shamelessly (and sometimes skillfully) insert a promotional message into a conversation. 'Ang ganda ng blouse mo! Speaking of ganda, please follow my makeup tutorial page...'
usage_notes: A modern, informal term derived from English. Often spelled with a hyphen 'mag-plug'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bago matapos ang interview, gusto ko lang **mag-plug** ng bago kong album.","translation":"Before the interview ends, I just want **to plug** my new album."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mahiyang **mag-plug** ng business mo sa group chat natin.","translation":"Don't be shy **to plug** your business in our group chat."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng duyan na yari sa tela, lambat, o lubid, na itinatali sa pagitan ng dalawang puno o poste upang higaan.
original_explanation: The official gear for beach trips and provincial siestas. That thing you tie between two coconut trees and pretend you don't have deadlines. It's the ultimate symbol of 'pahinga muna, bes' and the 'sana all' life.
usage_notes: Also commonly spelled as 'hammock' in modern Filipino text, but 'hamaka' is the traditional Filipino spelling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap matulog sa **hamaka** sa ilalim ng puno ng niyog.","translation":"It's nice to sleep in a **hammock** under a coconut tree."},{"sentence":"Nagdala sila ng **hamaka** para sa kanilang camping trip sa tabing-dagat.","translation":"They brought a **hammock** for their beachside camping trip."}]

translation: to cover with something concave (like a lid or dome)
meaning_filipino: Takpan ang isang bagay gamit ang malukong na pantakip tulad ng takip ng kaldero o mangkok.
original_explanation: That specific action of putting a lid on a pot, or covering a plate of food with another bowl to keep the flies away. It's a very specific kind of 'cover'. Think of it as putting a dome on something. 'Pakitingnan kung kumukulo na, tapos **isaklob** mo ulit.'
usage_notes: Differentiated from `takpan` (to cover in general). `Isaklob` specifies a dome-shaped or concave cover.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **isaklob** ang kawali para mas mabilis maluto ang adobo.","translation":"Don't forget to **cover** the pan with a lid so the adobo cooks faster."},{"sentence":"**Isaklob** mo ang mangkok sa natirang kanin.","translation":"**Cover** the leftover rice with the bowl."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng natural na pamamahinga ng katawan at isipan, kung saan ang kamalayan ay pansamantalang natitigil o nababawasan.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `pag-` at sa salitang ugat na `tulog` (kalagayan ng pamamahinga).
original_explanation: The most precious, most elusive commodity for BPO agents, students during finals week, and new parents. It's our favorite hobby that we never have enough time for. The best part of the day and the cure for almost everything: stress, pagod, sama ng loob. "Idaan mo na lang sa pagtulog."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mo ng sapat na **pagtulog** para lumakas ka.","translation":"You need enough **sleep** to get strong."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdating sa katapusan o hantungan ng isang bagay, pangyayari, o panahon.
original_explanation: This is the dramatic ending of a teleserye, the final chapter of a book, or the end of an era. It’s more formal and final than `matapos`. When a story `nagwakas`, it means "and they lived happily ever after"... or not. It’s the "fin" at the end of a French film. It carries a sense of finality and destiny. Parang 'yung relasyon n'yong bigla na lang... `nagwakas`. Ouch.
usage_notes: Carries a more formal, literary, or dramatic tone compared to `matapos`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dito na **magwawakas** ang ating kuwento.","translation":"Our story **will end** here."},{"sentence":"Sana'y hindi pa **magwakas** ang ating pagkakaibigan.","translation":"I hope our friendship doesn't **end** yet."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paggamit ng kaisipan upang bumuo ng ideya, opinyon, o desisyon.
original_explanation: What you do when your boss asks 'any questions?' and you're trying to sound smart. Also the state of your brain trying to calculate if you have enough money for milk tea until the next sahod. 'Wait lang, nag-iisip ako.' is a valid excuse for almost anything.
usage_notes: The progressive form of 'mag-isip', indicating the ongoing action of thinking.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malalim ang **iniisip** niya kaya hindi ka niya napansin.","translation":"He is **thinking** deeply, that's why he didn't notice you."},{"sentence":"**Nag-iisip** pa ako kung ano ang magandang iregalo sa kanya.","translation":"I'm still **thinking** about what would be a good gift for her."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salita o gawa ng pangungutya, paghamak, o pag-alipusta sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: This is high-level pambabara. Hindi lang simpleng asar, ito 'yung pang-iinsulto na may kasamang pagmamaliit sa pagkatao mo, sa lahi mo, o sa estado mo sa buhay. Ito 'yung ginagawa ng kontrabida sa teleserye sa api-apihang bida. It's the kind of insult that cuts deep. Pang-Florante at Laura levels of shade.
usage_notes: A deep, literary word. 'Pangungutya' or 'panlalait' are more common synonyms.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya pinansin ang **aglahi** ng kanyang mga kaaway.","translation":"He ignored the **scorn** of his enemies."},{"sentence":"Puno ng **aglahi** ang mga binitawan niyang salita.","translation":"The words he uttered were full of **mockery**."}]

translation: viscous fluid; oily substance; slow flow of a thick liquid
meaning_filipino: Isang malapot na likido, tulad ng langis o pulot, na dahan-dahang dumadaloy.
original_explanation: Imagine the slow, thick drip of honey or condensed milk. That's 'lanay'. It's the opposite of your sweldo which flows out of your bank account way too fast. 'Lanay' is that satisfyingly slow, thick, and rich flow.
usage_notes: This is a less common word, often found in literature. It specifically describes the quality and movement of viscous liquids.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **lanay** ng langis ay kumalat sa sahig.","translation":"The **oily substance** spread on the floor."},{"sentence":"Pinanood niya ang dahan-dahang **lanay** ng pulot sa kutsara.","translation":"She watched the slow **flow** of the honey on the spoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamababang halaga, antas, o sukat na posible o pinahihintulutan.
original_explanation: The bare minimum. It's the effort your ex gave, the lowest passing grade, or the required balance to keep your bank account open. Sa GrabFood, ito yung 'minimum order' na kailangan mong abutin para magamit ang voucher. The floor, not the ceiling.
usage_notes: Used interchangeably with the English 'minimum' in modern Taglish.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sampung piraso ang **minimo** na kailangan mong bilhin.","translation":"Ten pieces is **the minimum** you need to buy."},{"sentence":"Ginawa niya ang **minimo** para lang makapasa.","translation":"He did **the minimum** just to pass."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng kaisipan upang bumuo ng ideya, opinyon, o solusyon; pagmunimuni.
original_explanation: What you do for 5 hours before sending a one-sentence reply. Also, the command your mom gives you before you make a life decision she won't approve of. "Mag-isip-isip ka muna bago ka mag-checkout sa Shopee."
usage_notes: Often repeated as "mag-isip-isip" to mean "to think carefully" or "to reflect deeply".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigyan mo ako ng isang araw para **mag-isip** tungkol sa alok mo.","translation":"Give me a day to **think** about your offer."},{"sentence":"Bago ka sumagot, **mag-isip** ka munang mabuti.","translation":"Before you answer, **think** carefully first."}]

meaning_filipino: Maglapat ng lunas o gamot sa isang sakit, sugat, o karamdaman.
etymology: From the root 'gamot' (medicine) with the infix '-um-'.
original_explanation: Playing doctor. It's what you do when your friend has a headache and you give them paracetamol, or when your mom puts Vicks on everything from a cough to a broken leg. It's the active process of applying a remedy.
usage_notes: This verb implies the person is the one administering the treatment, not necessarily a professional doctor. A doctor 'nanggagamot', while a person can 'gumamot' by applying first aid.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **gumamot** sa sugat ko pagkatapos akong madapa.","translation":"She was the one who **treated** my wound after I fell."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **gumamot** sa sarili gamit ang mga halamang herbal.","translation":"He tried to **medicate** himself using herbal plants."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang maisuot o magkasya sa isang kasuotan.
original_explanation: The moment of truth in the fitting room. "Kaya ko pa bang **masuot** 'tong jeans ko from college?" It’s the verb for that victory feeling when an old favorite shirt still fits, or the mild panic when it doesn't.
usage_notes: Often used in questions or statements about whether a piece of clothing fits.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **masuot** ko pa itong luma kong bestida para sa party.","translation":"I hope I can still **wear** this old dress of mine for the party."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko na **masuot** ang sapatos dahil masikip na.","translation":"I can't **wear** the shoes anymore because they're too tight."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-ilaw o pagkinang nang paandap-andap o bahagya.
original_explanation: The OG "Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star." Ito yung basic sparkle. Yung isang bituin sa malayo, yung isang sequin na nalaglag sa damit mo, o yung pag-spark ng idea sa utak mo. Less dramatic than kumuti-kutitap, more of a solo performance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumukutitap** ang mga bituin sa langit.","translation":"The stars are **twinkling** in the sky."},{"sentence":"May isang ilaw na **kumukutitap** sa bintana ng abandonadong bahay.","translation":"There's a light **sparkling** in the window of the abandoned house."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng pagiging hindi regular, hindi tiyak, o pabago-bago sa kilos, pag-uugali, o direksyon.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung Wi-Fi connection mo 'pag umuulan – pabago-bago, hindi mo maasahan. Or 'yung mood ng jowa mo na hindi mo maintindihan. One minute masaya, next minute galit. "Bakit ang **eratiko** ng ugali niya ngayon?"
usage_notes: Isang mas pormal na alternatibo para sa 'pabago-bago'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **eratiko** ang takbo ng sasakyan bago ito bumangga.","translation":"The car's movement became **erratic** before it crashed."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **eratiko** na pag-uugali, mahirap siyang pakisamahan.","translation":"Because of his **erratic** behavior, he is difficult to get along with."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagrerekord ng isang palabas sa telebisyon, pelikula, o radyo para sa pagpapalabas sa hinaharap, sa halip na ito ay i-broadcast nang live.
original_explanation: That magical, often 24-hour-long process where artistas look fresh on cam but are running on coffee and pure will to live off cam. 'Call time 5 AM, pack-up 5 AM the next day.' #TapingLife
usage_notes: Used specifically in the context of media production (TV shows, vlogs, etc.).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puyat na naman ang mga artista dahil sa **taping** ng bago nilang teleserye.","translation":"The actors are sleep-deprived again because of the **taping** for their new TV series."},{"sentence":"Kailan ang **taping** para sa susunod na episode ng vlog mo?","translation":"When is the **taping** for your next vlog episode?"}]

meaning_filipino: Iinom ng kape.
original_explanation: The official verb of the BPO industry and college students during finals week. It's not just 'will drink coffee,' it's a declaration of survival, a ritual to summon brain cells, and the answer to 'tara, ano'ng gagawin natin?'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magkakape** muna ako bago ako magsimula sa trabaho.","translation":"I **will drink coffee** first before I start work."},{"sentence":"Sino ang gustong **magkakape** mamaya pagkatapos ng klase?","translation":"Who wants to **have coffee** later after class?"}]

meaning_filipino: Paglalarawan sa isang bagay na paikot na nakapulupot o nakapalibot sa isa pang bagay.
original_explanation: Like a snake around a branch, or your earphones in your pocket (kahit inayos mo na). It can also be your jowa's arms around you, which is cute, or 'yung utang sa credit card na nakalikaw sa leeg mo, which is not.
usage_notes: Often used to describe ropes, snakes, vines, or anything long and flexible wrapped around something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malaking ahas ang **nakalikaw** sa sanga ng puno.","translation":"A large snake is **coiled** on the tree branch."},{"sentence":"Maingat niyang inalis ang baging na **nakalikaw** sa kanyang binti.","translation":"He carefully removed the vine that was **wound around** his leg."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pagtupi o pagsasara na gaya ng sa isang panaklong na kutsilyo o balisong; may kakayahang matiklop.
etymology: From pa- prefix indicating manner + tiklop (fold).
original_explanation: Think of a folding chair, a foldable phone, or a balisong. It's designed to fold onto itself. Parang 'yung feelings mo for your ex, akala mo naka-move on ka na, pero isang "hi" lang niya, **patiklop** ka na naman.
usage_notes: Describes an object that folds in on itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili ako ng upuang **patiklop** para madaling itago.","translation":"I bought a **folding** chair so it's easy to store."},{"sentence":"Ang mga bagong telepono ngayon ay **patiklop** na.","translation":"The new phones nowadays are **foldable**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang daglat para sa pariralang Ingles na "I don't care," na nangangahulugang kawalan ng interes, pag-aalala, o pakialam.
etymology: From the English abbreviation 'IDC' (I Don't Care).
original_explanation: The official battle cry of the "bahala na" generation, but in English shorthand. When your friend asks for the 10th time if you should get milk tea or coffee, and you've lost the will to live, you just text back "idc". It's the text-speak version of a shoulder shrug.
usage_notes: Primarily used in informal, digital communication like text messages and social media. It is pronounced by spelling out the letters in English.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"\"Saan tayo kakain?\" \"Kahit saan, **idc**.\"","translation":"\"Where should we eat?\" \"Anywhere, **I don't care**.\""},{"sentence":"Sabi niya **idc** daw siya, pero halata namang apektado siya.","translation":"He said he **doesn't care**, but it's obvious he's affected."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtatago o pagdadala ng galit o sama ng loob sa isang tao sa mahabang panahon.
original_explanation: Literally "carrying anger". This is when you can't let go of a grudge. Parang may dala-dala kang mabigat na bag ng sama ng loob everywhere you go. Your friend forgot your birthday 5 years ago? And you still bring it up? You're dalang-galit. It's the emotional equivalent of "I will never forget this."
usage_notes: Isang idyomatikong ekspresyon na naglalarawan sa emosyonal na kalagayan ng isang tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nanatili siyang **dalang-galit** sa kanyang kaibigan matapos ang kanilang pag-aaway.","translation":"He remained **resentful** towards his friend after their fight."},{"sentence":"Mahirap mabuhay nang may **dalang-galit** sa puso.","translation":"It's hard to live while **bearing a grudge** in your heart."}]

translation: to legislate; to enact as law
meaning_filipino: Gawing isang batas ang isang panukala o alituntunin sa pamamagitan ng prosesong lehislatibo.
original_explanation: What senators and congressmen are *supposed* to do. It's the process of turning a 'bright idea' (or a really questionable one) into something everyone has to follow. It's like when your mom declares 'Bawal mag-cellphone sa hapag-kainan!'—she just ibinatas a new house rule.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa konteksto ng pamahalaan, batas, at pormal na paggawa ng mga alituntunin. Ang 'isabatas' ay isang mas karaniwang kasingkahulugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ng kongreso kung dapat bang **ibatas** ang pagbabawal sa plastic.","translation":"The congress is studying whether the ban on plastic should be **legislated**."},{"sentence":"Matagal nang isinusulong na **ibatas** ang National ID system.","translation":"They have long been pushing to **enact as law** the National ID system."}]

meaning_filipino: Linisin sa pamamagitan ng kemikal upang maalis o mapuksa ang mga mikrobyo, partikular na ang mga nagdudulot ng sakit.
etymology: Mula sa ugat na 'desimpekta', na hango sa Espanyol na 'desinfectar' (to disinfect).
original_explanation: The official theme song of the pandemic era. Ito yung action word na sinisigaw ng nanay mo bago ka pumasok ng bahay galing sa labas. 'I-desimpektahan mo 'yang mga pinamili mo!' Basically, giving everything the alcohol or Lysol treatment. From your hands to your Shopee delivery packages.
usage_notes: Isang pandiwa sa pokus sa layon (may hulaping -han). Ang salitang ugat na 'desimpekta' ay bihirang gamitin nang mag-isa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **desimpektahan** ang sugat upang maiwasan ang impeksyon.","translation":"The wound needs to be **disinfected** to prevent infection."},{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **desimpektahan** ang iyong mga kamay palagi.","translation":"Don't forget to **disinfect** your hands always."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng tela na makinis, makintab, at madulas ang isang panig, na karaniwang gawa sa sutla, nylon, o polyester.
etymology: From English 'satin', from Old French 'satin', from Arabic 'zaytūnī', named after Zaytun (modern Quanzhou) in China.
original_explanation: The go-to fabric for prom gowns, bridesmaid dresses, and fancy 'pantulog' (pajamas) that make you feel like a kontrabida in a teleserye. It's smooth, shiny, and looks expensive, but be warned: it shows every drop of sweat and is super slippery. Perfect for that "I woke up like this" look, even if you just slid off your bed.
usage_notes: A loanword from English, widely used in fashion and textiles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bestida niya ay gawa sa mamahaling **satin**.","translation":"Her dress is made of expensive **satin**."},{"sentence":"Gusto ko ng punda na **satin** para hindi magusot ang buhok ko.","translation":"I want a **satin** pillowcase so my hair won't get frizzy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang buwis o taripa na ipinapataw sa mga kalakal na inaangkat o iniluluwas sa isang bansa.
original_explanation: That surprise fee that hits your Shopee or Amazon package from overseas, turning your 'great deal' into just a... deal. It's the government's way of saying, "Nice haul you got there. It'd be a shame if something... happened to it in our warehouse." This is why your tita from the US has to get creative when sending you a balikbayan box.
usage_notes: A specific type of tax related to international trade.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang **bayad sa adwana** para sa mga imported na sasakyan.","translation":"The **customs duty** for imported cars is high."},{"sentence":"Kinailangan niyang maglaan ng pera para sa **bayad sa adwana** ng kanyang online order.","translation":"She had to set aside money for the **tariff** on her online order."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalanan o krimen ng pagpapakasal sa ibang tao habang legal pang kasal sa iba.
original_explanation: This is when someone tries to collect spouses like they're collecting Funko Pops. It's a legal no-no, basically having a 'main' and a 'backup' spouse officially, which the law frowns upon. Parang nag-multitask sa relationships pero sa level na may kasamang demanda.
usage_notes: Isang legal na termino na bihirang gamitin sa pang-araw-araw na usapan ngunit mahalaga sa konteksto ng batas pampamilya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ay kinasuhan ng **bigamiya** matapos matuklasan na mayroon siyang dalawang asawa.","translation":"He was charged with **bigamy** after it was discovered he had two wives."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mas malawak na konsepto ng isip na sumasaklaw sa kamalayan, damdamin, at pananaw ng isang tao.
original_explanation: If 'isip' is the computer, 'isipan' is the entire network—your consciousness, your worldview, your entire vibe. It's the "state of your mind." Kaya may "bukas na isipan" (open-minded) for people who are cool with new ideas, and "makitid na isipan" (narrow-minded) for those who are... well, not.
usage_notes: More abstract and broader than 'isip'. Often refers to a person's entire mindset or consciousness. Can also be a verb form 'to think about something'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating magkaroon ng bukas na **isipan** sa mga bagong ideya.","translation":"We need to have an open **mindset** to new ideas."},{"sentence":"Ang mga alaala ng kahapon ay nananatili sa kanyang **isipan**.","translation":"The memories of yesterday remain in his **consciousness**."}]

translation: please greet/say hi to someone for me
meaning_filipino: Isang pakiusap na ipaabot ang pagbati sa isang tao.
original_explanation: The classic Filipino social proxy move. When you see a friend who's going to see another friend, you say "Pabati kay [name]!" It’s the verbal equivalent of a forwarded message or a social CC. It's how you maintain social connections without actually being there. The ultimate low-effort, high-impact social gesture.
usage_notes: Used as a standalone phrase or within a sentence. It's a request.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uy, pupunta ka pala sa kanila! **Pabati** na lang kay Tita, ha?","translation":"Oh, you're going to their place! Just **say hi** to Tita for me, okay?"},{"sentence":"Pakisabi sa kanya, **pabati** mula sa dati niyang katrabaho.","translation":"Please tell him, **greetings** from his former colleague."}]

meaning_filipino: Nag-aalab o parang apoy; puno ng sidhi ng damdamin o entusiyasmo.
original_explanation: Describes something that's literally on fire, or more often, a person's feelings or speech. Think of a fiery 'bardagulan' online, a passionate speech from a politician, or the intense 'I love you' in a teleserye finale. It's got heat, energy, and a whole lot of drama.
usage_notes: Used both literally (fiery) and figuratively (passionate, ardent, intense).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagbigay siya ng isang **maapoy** na talumpati na pumukaw sa damdamin ng mga nakikinig.","translation":"He gave a **fiery** speech that stirred the emotions of the audience."},{"sentence":"Ang kanilang **maapoy** na pagmamahalan ay hinahangaan ng marami.","translation":"Their **passionate** love is admired by many."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar o pook na binubuo ng magkakatabing mga bahay; ang kabuuan ng mga kapitbahay sa isang lugar.
etymology: From 'kapitbahay' + '-an' (suffix denoting a place or a collective).
original_explanation: This is the whole 'hood. The subdivision, the barangay, the entire street. It’s where the community pantry pops up, where the Christmas lantern competition happens, and where everyone knows everyone's business. Think of it as the setting for your local 'teleserye'.
usage_notes: Refers to the collective area or community, not just one person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malinis at tahimik ang aming **kapitbahayan**.","translation":"Our **neighborhood** is clean and quiet."},{"sentence":"Nag-ikot ang mga tanod sa buong **kapitbahayan**.","translation":"The village watchmen patrolled the entire **neighborhood**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lutuing Pilipino na may impluwensyang Tsino, na binubuo ng mga pinaghalong ginisa na gulay tulad ng repolyo, carrots, at bell pepper, na kadalasang may kasamang karne, atay ng manok, o pagkaing-dagat.
etymology: From Chinese (Cantonese) 雜碎 (zaap6 seoi3), meaning 'mixed pieces' or 'odds and ends'.
original_explanation: The official 'para magka-gulay naman' dish at every Filipino gathering. It's a stir-fry medley that's supposed to make you feel healthy amidst the lechon, crispy pata, and spaghetti. The name itself, which means 'mixed bits,' perfectly describes the dish and sometimes, the chaotic but wonderful mix of people at the party.
usage_notes: A staple dish in Filipino cuisine, especially during fiestas, parties, and other celebrations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong ulam ang **chopsuey** na luto ni nanay.","translation":"My favorite dish is the **chop suey** cooked by my mom."},{"sentence":"Magluto ka ng **chopsuey** para may gulay tayong kakainin.","translation":"Cook some **chop suey** so we have vegetables to eat."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking ang trabaho o gawain ay magluto ng pagkain, lalo na sa isang propesyonal na kapasidad.
original_explanation: Siya ang hari ng kusina. Pwedeng ang tatay mo na special move ang sinangag with matching hotdog on a Sunday, o 'yung professional chef sa isang restaurant. Ang female version ay 'kusinera'. Sila ang mga alchemist na ginagawang masarap na ulam ang laman ng ref.
usage_notes: The female counterpart is 'kusinera'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magaling na **kusinero** ang tatay ko, lalo na sa pagluto ng sinigang.","translation":"My father is a great **cook**, especially when it comes to cooking sinigang."},{"sentence":"Nag-aral siya sa ibang bansa para maging isang sikat na **kusinero**.","translation":"He studied abroad to become a famous **chef**."}]

meaning_filipino: Pilit na ipasok o isiksik sa isipan ng isang tao ang isang ideya, paniniwala, o kaisipan.
original_explanation: This is what your parents do when they keep telling you to "mag-asawa ka na" or "mag-ipon ka." They're trying to hammer that idea into your brain until you give in. It's the ultimate 'kulit' mode, but for ideas. It’s the verbal equivalent of a jackhammer.
usage_notes: The object being insisted upon is the focus of the verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paulit-ulit niyang **iniuukilkil** sa amin ang kahalagahan ng pagboto.","translation":"He repeatedly **insists upon** us the importance of voting."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **iukilkil** ang iyong opinyon kung ayaw nilang makinig.","translation":"Don't **forcefully insist** on your opinion if they don't want to listen."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ipinanganak na pisikal na karugtong o kadikit ng kanyang kapatid; maaari ring tumukoy sa anumang bagay na magkadikit o magkapares.
original_explanation: Think of it as 'BFFs since birth,' but literally. *Kalambal* refers to conjoined twins. In a less literal sense, you can use it to describe two things that are inseparable, like you and your phone, or two best friends who are always seen together. 'Parang kalambal kayo!'
usage_notes: While the primary meaning is 'conjoined twin', it can be used figuratively for things or people that are closely paired and inseparable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isinilang na **kalambal** ang mga sanggol.","translation":"The babies were born as **conjoined twins**."},{"sentence":"Ang dalawang gusaling iyon ay parang **kalambal** dahil sa kanilang disenyo.","translation":"Those two buildings are like **conjoined twins** because of their design."}]

translation: to reek; to give off a foul smell
meaning_filipino: Ang paglabas o pagkalat ng isang masamang amoy, karaniwan ay mula sa isang bagay na nabubulok o marumi.
original_explanation: The smell that hits you when you open a lunch box you forgot in your bag over the weekend. It's the scent of the Pasig River on a hot day, or your brother's gym socks. It's a smell that doesn't just smell, it announces its presence with authority.
usage_notes: Describes a strong, pervasive, and unpleasant odor.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **umalingasaw** ang amoy mula sa basurahan.","translation":"A foul smell started **to reek** from the trash can."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong iwan ang isda diyan at baka **umalingasaw** sa buong bahay.","translation":"Don't leave the fish there or its smell might **reek** throughout the whole house."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong kaanib sa Simbahang Katolika na kumikilala sa Santo Papa sa Roma bilang pinakamataas na pinuno ng pananampalataya.
original_explanation: This is your lola's official religion on any government form. It's the default setting for many Filipinos, involving Simbang Gabi, fiestas, and a healthy fear of divine retribution if you don't finish the food on your plate.
usage_notes: Madalas na pinaikli sa "Katoliko" lamang. Ang "Romano" ay idinadagdag para sa pormal o tiyak na pagkilala mula sa ibang mga ritong Katoliko.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bilang isang **Katoliko Romano**, dinarasal niya ang rosaryo araw-araw.","translation":"As a **Roman Catholic**, he prays the rosary every day."},{"sentence":"Marami sa mga tradisyon sa Pilipinas ay nag-ugat sa pananampalatayang **Katoliko Romano**.","translation":"Many traditions in the Philippines are rooted in the **Roman Catholic** faith."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang hanapbuhay ay may kaugnayan sa dagat, tulad ng pangingisda o paglalayag.
original_explanation: Your modern-day Aquaman, but with more bills to pay and less talking to fish. Sila 'yung mga BPO (Barko-based Pinoy Overseas) at 'yung mga bayani sa palengke na nagdadala ng fresh seafood sa atin. The original OFWs, risking rough seas so we can have our sinigang na hipon. Salute to all **mandaragat**!
usage_notes: A general term for anyone who works at sea. It can refer to a fisherman ('mangingisda'), a sailor ('manlalayag'), or a modern seaman ('marino').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ama niya ay isang matapang na **mandaragat**.","translation":"His father is a brave **seafarer**."},{"sentence":"Bumibili kami ng sariwang isda direkta mula sa mga **mandaragat**.","translation":"We buy fresh fish directly from the **fishermen**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga produkto, lalo na ang pagkain, na itinanim o inalagaan nang hindi gumagamit ng mga artipisyal na pataba, pestisidyo, o kemikal.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung label sa gulay na nagsasabing, "Mas mahal ako, pero promise, walang lason." The food your health-conscious friend insists on buying. **Organik** means it grew up 'au naturel', like how your lola's backyard veggies did, before "pesticide" was even a thing. It's the "clean living" version of food.
usage_notes: Malawak na ginagamit sa konteksto ng agrikultura, pagkain, at malusog na pamumuhay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas mahal ang mga **organik** na gulay sa palengke.","translation":"**Organic** vegetables are more expensive in the market."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtalikod o pagtatakwil sa isang dating pinaniniwalaang relihiyon, pananampalataya, o prinsipyo.
etymology: From 'pagka-' (state of being) + 'balariid' (apostate). The root itself is very rare.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "unfriending" of a religion or major belief system. It's not just skipping church; it's a conscious, formal break-up. It's the spiritual equivalent of deleting your old account and starting a new one under a different philosophy. Very rare and heavy word.
usage_notes: An extremely rare and formal word, mostly found in old religious or literary texts. The common term is 'pagtalikod sa pananampalataya'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkabalariid** ay itinuturing na isang malaking kasalanan sa ilang sinaunang kasulatan.","translation":"**Apostasy** was considered a great sin in some ancient texts."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aralan niya ang kasaysayan ng **pagkabalariid** sa iba't ibang kultura.","translation":"He studied the history of **apostasy** in different cultures."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pampublikong daanan sa isang lungsod o bayan, karaniwang may mga gusali o bahay sa magkabilang gilid.
original_explanation: It's the street. The road. Dito nangyayari ang lahat. Dito ka nag-aabang ng jeep, dito naglalaro ng tumbang preso 'nung bata ka, dito mo nakikita ang mga nagtitinda ng fishball. "Street smarts" is "diskarte sa kalye." It's the artery of daily Filipino life.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maingay sa aming **kalye** tuwing umaga.","translation":"It's noisy on our **street** every morning."},{"sentence":"Tumawid ka sa tamang tawiran sa **kalye**.","translation":"Cross the **street** at the proper pedestrian lane."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto o paraan ng pagluhod, karaniwan bilang tanda ng pagsusumamo, paggalang, o pananalangin.
etymology: Nagmula sa unlaping 'pan-' at salitang-ugat na 'luhod', na may gitlaping '-ik-' na nagpapahiwatig ng paraan ng pagsasagawa ng kilos.
original_explanation: This is the dramatic act of kneeling, usually when you're begging for forgiveness, praying for a miracle (like passing an exam you didn't study for), or proposing marriage. It's the physical manifestation of "Lord, kayo na po ang bahala." The panikluhod is a classic move in teleseryes.
usage_notes: Nagpapahiwatig ng malalim na kababaang-loob, desperasyon, o pagpipitagan. Mas matindi ang diin nito kaysa sa simpleng 'pagluhod'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa pamamagitan ng kanyang **panikluhod**, ipinakita niya ang kanyang taos-pusong pagsisisi.","translation":"Through his **act of kneeling in supplication**, he showed his sincere repentance."},{"sentence":"Ang **panikluhod** sa harap ng altar ay tanda ng malalim na pananampalataya.","translation":"The **act of kneeling** before the altar is a sign of deep faith."}]

meaning_filipino: Linisin ang isang bagay gamit ang tubig o anumang likido.
original_explanation: The command your mom yells from the kitchen right after a feast. It's the act of facing the consequences (the dirty dishes) of your delicious actions. "Maghugas ka ng plato" is the national anthem after every meal.
usage_notes: This is the object-focus form of the verb 'hugas'. Use it when the thing being washed is the subject of the sentence. Contrast with 'maghugas' (actor-focus).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hugasan** mo na ang mga pinagkainan para hindi pamahayan ng ipis.","translation":"**Wash** the dishes now so cockroaches don't make a home there."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **hugasan** ang mga gulay bago iluto.","translation":"The vegetables need to be **washed** before cooking."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sawikain para sa kalagayan ng pagiging malayo ang diwa, hindi nakapokus, o nag-iisip ng ibang bagay.
original_explanation: The official status of your brain during a boring meeting or a long lecture. It's when you're physically present, but your mind is on vacation in Palawan, replaying a K-drama scene, or deciding what to eat for lunch. You're not dumb, your mind just booked a flight without you.
usage_notes: Literally translates to 'the mind is flying'. A very common idiom.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, madalas talagang **lumilipad ang isip** ko kapag pagod.","translation":"Don't worry, my **mind often wanders** when I'm tired."},{"sentence":"Tinawag ng guro si Ana dahil **lumilipad ang isip** niya sa klase.","translation":"The teacher called on Ana because she was **daydreaming** in class."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng batong sedimentaryo na pangunahing binubuo ng calcium carbonate. Karaniwan itong nabubuo mula sa mga labi ng mga organismong pandagat at ginagamit sa paggawa ng semento at apog.
original_explanation: The foundation of old-school Philippine architecture. Think of the walls of Intramuros or those ancient, massive churches in the provinces. This is the rock that, when processed, becomes the 'apog' (lime) used for construction. It's the historical building block of the Philippines, literally.
usage_notes: Ang `apog` mismo ay tumutukoy sa lime, kaya't ang `batong-apog` ay naglilinaw na ito ang anyong bato.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga pader ng lumang simbahan ay yari sa **batong-apog**.","translation":"The walls of the old church are made of **limestone**."}]

translation: for the sake of; in consideration of
meaning_filipino: Isang parirala na nagpapahiwatig na ang isang kilos ay ginawa dahil sa paggalang, pagmamahal, o pagbibigay-halaga sa isang tao, bagay, o prinsipyo.
original_explanation: The official tagline for every Filipino martyr moment. "I'll do it, but make no mistake, it's 'alang-alang sa 'yo.'" It's what you say when you agree to go to a K-Pop concert with your niece, or when you let your friend choose the movie even if you hate horror. It's the noble justification for doing something you don't necessarily want to do.
usage_notes: Functions as a preposition to introduce the reason or motivation for an action, which is often a sacrifice or a difficult choice.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Alang-alang sa** bayan, isinakripisyo ng mga bayani ang kanilang buhay.","translation":"**For the sake of** the country, the heroes sacrificed their lives."},{"sentence":"Tumahimik na lang ako **alang-alang sa** pagkakaibigan namin.","translation":"I just kept quiet **in consideration of** our friendship."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sinaunang salita na tumutukoy sa isang pamayanan, bayan, bansa, o lupain. Sa kasalukuyang gamit sa ilang wikang Bisaya, nangangahulugan itong 'bayan' o 'lungsod'.
etymology: From Proto-Philippine *banua, meaning 'inhabited land, settlement, country.' Cognates exist across Austronesian languages.
original_explanation: This is an OG term, like, pre-hispanic OG. Before there was 'bayan' or 'nasyon,' there was 'banwa.' It means your community, your turf, your people. Today, you'll mostly hear this in Visayan languages where it just means town or city. In Tagalog, it's a throwback word you'd find in history books or epic poems.
usage_notes: Considered archaic in modern standard Tagalog but is a common word in many Visayan languages (e.g., Hiligaynon, Cebuano).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga datu ang namumuno sa sinaunang **banwa**.","translation":"The datus led the ancient **community**."},{"sentence":"Sa mga epiko, madalas binabanggit ang katapangan ng mga bayani ng **banwa**.","translation":"In epics, the bravery of the heroes of the **land** is often mentioned."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang nilalang sa mitolohiyang Pilipino na may katawan ng tao at ulo at mga paa ng kabayo, na kilalang naninirahan sa mga puno ng balete at nagliligaw ng mga manlalakbay.
original_explanation: The original prankster of Philippine folklore. This tall, creepy horse-man will lead you in circles in the forest until you wear your shirt inside out to break the spell. Think of it as the ultimate "wrong turn" GPS from hell.
usage_notes: A well-known figure in Philippine mythology. Often used to scare children from wandering off alone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayon sa alamat, kailangan mong baligtarin ang iyong damit para hindi ka maligaw ng **tigbalang**.","translation":"According to legend, you need to wear your shirt inside out so you won't be led astray by a **tigbalang**."},{"sentence":"Kinatatakutan ang mga puno ng balete dahil diumano'y tirahan ito ng mga **tigbalang** at iba pang engkanto.","translation":"Balete trees are feared because they are said to be the home of **tigbalangs** and other supernatural beings."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pintura na nag-iiwan ng makinis, matibay, at makintab na balot kapag natuyo; maaari ding tumukoy sa pangkulay ng kuko.
original_explanation: This is the fancy word for nail polish or any glossy paint. Ito yung 'kuko's best friend' na nagbibigay kulay sa buhay mo, or at least sa mga daliri mo. Pwede rin itong pintura para sa gate o appliances para mukhang brand new at 'di kinakalawang, parang puso mong matibay.
usage_notes: Mas karaniwang ginagamit ngayon para tumukoy sa nail polish (pangkulay ng kuko) kaysa sa enamel paint.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si Ana ng pulang **esmalte** para sa kanyang mga kuko.","translation":"Ana bought red **nail polish** for her nails."},{"sentence":"Pininturahan niya ng puting **esmalte** ang lumang ref para magmukhang bago.","translation":"He painted the old fridge with white **enamel** to make it look new."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagkakaroon ng higit na kalamangan o benepisyo kaysa sa iba, na kung minsan ay sa hindi patas na paraan.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're in a competition (or just arguing with a sibling) and you're winning. 'Palamang na ako!' But it can also be negative, like when someone is being opportunistic or exploitative. 'Huwag kang palamang sa kapwa.' It’s the state of having the upper hand.
usage_notes: Can be neutral (leading in a game) or negative (exploitative). The context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Palamang** na ang kanilang koponan ng limang puntos.","translation":"Their team is now **leading** by five points."},{"sentence":"Ayaw ko sa mga taong **palamang** sa kanilang mga manggagawa.","translation":"I don't like people who **take advantage** of their workers."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malinaw at malapot na likido sa loob ng isang itlog na pumapalibot sa pula ng itlog (yolk), na nagiging kulay puti at solido kapag naluto.
original_explanation: 'Yung part ng itlog na iniiwasan ng mga nagda-diet sa cholesterol pero hinahabol ng mga bodybuilder para sa protein. It's the clear, goopy part that turns white when you cook it. Perfect for making meringue or for that 'healthy' omelette kuno.
usage_notes: Isang tambalang pangngalan (compound noun).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng **puti ng itlog** para gawing mas malutong ang empanada.","translation":"She used **egg white** to make the empanada crispier."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pahayag na nagsasaad na mayroong gaganaping pagpupulong o pagtitipon para sa isang partikular na layunin.
original_explanation: The three words every BPO agent or corporate slave dreads hearing on a Friday afternoon. "Uwi na tayo?" "**May pulong** daw, biglaan." It's the official reason why you can't go home yet. Can also be used for barangay meetings or even a serious family talk ("Upo kayo, mga anak, **may pulong** tayo.").
usage_notes: "Pulong" can refer to formal meetings (corporate, government) or informal gatherings (family, community).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ako makakasama sa pananghalian dahil **may pulong** kami kasama ang kliyente.","translation":"I can't join for lunch because we **have a meeting** with the client."}]

translation: was made into a small ball (usually of dough)
meaning_filipino: Hinugis na parang bola, karaniwang tumutukoy sa galapong o masa para sa mga kakanin tulad ng bilo-bilo.
original_explanation: That moment in the kitchen when you're making ginataang halo-halo and you're rolling the sticky rice dough between your palms. 'Yan, 'binibilo' mo 'yung galapong. It's the past tense form, so kung tapos ka na, binilo mo na.
usage_notes: Primarily used in a culinary context, especially for making "bilo-bilo" for desserts like ginataan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Binilo** niyang mabuti ang masa bago ito inihulog sa kumukulong gata.","translation":"She **rolled** the dough into balls carefully before dropping them into the boiling coconut milk."},{"sentence":"Ang daming galapong ang **binilo** para sa pista bukas.","translation":"A lot of rice flour dough **was made into balls** for the fiesta tomorrow."}]

translation: the way something is hung; state of being left hanging (cliffhanger)
meaning_filipino: Ang paraan ng pagkasabit o pagkapulupot sa isang bagay; maaari ring tumukoy sa kalagayan ng pagiging hindi tapos o walang kasiguraduhan.
etymology: From `pag-` + `ka-` + `ka-` (reduplication) + `bitin`. The prefix `pagkaka-` can mean the manner of doing something or the state of being something.
original_explanation: Two meanings! 1) Literally, how something is hanging—like your parol at Christmas. 2) The more common, "hugot" meaning: a cliffhanger! That feeling when the Netflix episode ends right at the most crucial part. Or when your crush replies "haha" and you're left wondering what it means. It's the ultimate "Ano na, bes?" moment.
usage_notes: Can be literal (hanging) or figurative (cliffhanger, feeling of being unsatisfied or left hanging). The context determines the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayusin mo ang **pagkakabitin** ng kurtina para pantay.","translation":"Fix the way the curtain is **hung** so it's even."},{"sentence":"Nakakainis ang **pagkakabitin** ng huling episode ng serye!","translation":"The **cliffhanger** at the end of the series' last episode is so annoying!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang pagdudulot ng pagkalugi o pagkabangkarota sa isang tao, negosyo, o entidad.
original_explanation: This is the action verb for financial ruin. 'Yung sinadya mong ubusin 'yung budget ng department niyo sa mga non-essential team buildings para lang inisin 'yung boss mo. It's the "I will ruin you" but make it corporate.
usage_notes: An object-focused verb indicating the act of causing someone or something to go bankrupt.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May mga tsismis na balak nilang **bangkarotehin** ang kanilang kakumpitensya.","translation":"There are rumors that they plan **to bankrupt** their competitor."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na umuupa ng isang silid sa isang bahay o gusali, na kung minsan ay may kasamang pagkain.
original_explanation: Eto yung estudyante o BPO agent na nangungupahan malapit sa school o office. Ang buhay ng isang boarder ay umiikot sa paghahanap ng murang carinderia, paglalaba tuwing weekend, at pag-asa na hindi maingay yung katabing kwarto. Sila ang mga modern-day nomads ng siyudad.
usage_notes: Ang 'bedspacer' ay isang kaugnay na termino na tumutukoy sa isang taong umuupa lamang ng espasyo para sa kama sa isang shared na silid.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghahanap ang tiyahin ko ng babaeng **boarder** para sa bakanteng kwarto sa bahay niya.","translation":"My aunt is looking for a female **boarder** for the vacant room in her house."},{"sentence":"Dati akong **boarder** sa Maynila noong nag-aaral pa ako sa kolehiyo.","translation":"I used to be a **boarder** in Manila when I was still studying in college."}]

meaning_filipino: Ilagay o isilid sa loob ng isang bote.
original_explanation: The process of putting liquids (or your feelings) into a container with a narrow neck. 'Bes, 'wag mo na lang i-chat, i-tweet, o i-post. Ibote mo na lang 'yang galit mo.' Also, what you do with homemade tuba or bagoong.
usage_notes: This is the command/infinitive form of the verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **ibote** ang bagong timplang suka.","translation":"We need to **bottle** the newly mixed vinegar."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos anihin, **ibote** agad ang gatas ng kalabaw.","translation":"After harvesting, **bottle** the carabao's milk immediately."}]

meaning_filipino: Nangangahulugang malapit na sa kabuuan, pagiging ganap, o sa isang tiyak na bilang o antas; hindi pa lubos.
etymology: Malay 'halus' (fine, subtle), with a semantic shift in Tagalog.
original_explanation: The official word for 'muntik na'. When you're *halos* on time for work but your boss is already staring at you. When you're *halos* tapos na sa project, but the client wants 'one small revision'. It's the story of our lives: so close, yet so far.
usage_notes: Commonly precedes verbs, adjectives, or nouns (with a quantifier like 'lahat'). Examples like 'halos lahat' (almost all) and 'halos pigil' (almost holding one's breath) are common phrases derived from this word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Halos** mahulog ako sa hagdan kanina.","translation":"I **almost** fell down the stairs earlier."},{"sentence":"Gabi na nang dumating ang **halos** lahat ng bisita.","translation":"It was already night when **almost** all the guests arrived."},{"sentence":"**Halos** mag-iisang oras na akong naghihintay.","translation":"I've been waiting for **almost** an hour."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng panganganak kung saan nauuna ang paa o puwit ng sanggol sa halip na ang ulo.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'doing things the hard way' from day one. When a baby decides to come out feet-first, that's 'suhi'. It's a term every lola knows and often uses to explain why someone is particularly stubborn or 'pasaway'—'Suhi kasi 'yan pinanganak!' It's a built-in origin story for anyone who defies convention.
usage_notes: Also used figuratively to describe someone who is contrary, rebellious, or goes against the grain. This figurative use is very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap ang naging panganganak ng nanay niya dahil **suhi** ang bata.","translation":"Her mother had a difficult childbirth because the baby was in a **breech position**."},{"sentence":"Palibhasa'y **suhi**, laging kontra sa lahat ng sinasabi ko!","translation":"Because he's a **contrarian** (lit. born breech), he always objects to everything I say!"}]

translation: to have a duet with someone
meaning_filipino: Magsagawa ng isang pag-awit o pagtugtog kasama ang isa pang tao.
etymology: From English "duet" + the suffix "-uhan". A Taglish construction.
