original_explanation: The act of singing a duet, usually in a videoke session. It's when you and your tita fight over who gets to sing the Sharon Cuneta part and who gets the Regine Velasquez part. "Tara, duetuhan natin 'yung 'Bakit Ngayon Ka Lang'."
usage_notes: Primarily used in informal and musical contexts. 'Mag-duet' is also a common alternative.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **duetuhan** si Sarah Geronimo sa isang konsiyerto.","translation":"I want to **have a duet with** Sarah Geronimo in a concert."},{"sentence":"**Nag-duetuhan** sila sa kasal ng kanilang kaibigan.","translation":"They **sang a duet** at their friend's wedding."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang sapat na paghahanda; hindi nakahanda para sa isang gawain, sitwasyon, o pangyayari.
original_explanation: The official state of being for 90% of students during a surprise quiz. It's you, when your boss suddenly says 'So, any updates on your project?' and you were just scrolling through memes. It's showing up to a party and realizing there's a theme and you're not wearing it. Basically, 'na-surprise attack.'
usage_notes: Can also be used as an adverb 'nang di-handa' (unpreparedly).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahuli siyang **di-handa** sa biglaang pagsusulit.","translation":"He was caught **unprepared** for the surprise quiz."},{"sentence":"Dahil **di-handa** ang komunidad, maraming naapektuhan ng bagyo.","translation":"Because the community was **unprepared**, many were affected by the typhoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Maglagak o mag-ingat ng pera o mahalagang bagay sa isang bangko o anumang tiyak na lugar para sa kaligtasan.
original_explanation: That sacred trip to the bank after payday, trying to save a portion of your salary before Lazada and Shopee temptations attack. It's the adult version of putting coins in a piggy bank, but with longer lines and more paperwork.
usage_notes: Primarily used for depositing money in a bank, but can also be used for depositing items for safekeeping.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pupunta ako sa bangko mamaya para **magdeposito** ng sahod ko.","translation":"I will go to the bank later **to deposit** my salary."},{"sentence":"Mas mainam na **magdeposito** ng pera sa bangko kaysa itago lang sa bahay.","translation":"It is better **to deposit** money in the bank than to just keep it at home."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa pagkaing mayaman sa lasa, masarap, at kalugod-lugod sa panlasa.
original_explanation: This is the highest praise you can give to your tita's spaghetti or the lechon from the fiesta. It's beyond 'masarap.' It's that umami-packed, mouth-watering flavor that makes you say 'extra rice please!' It's the taste of a perfectly seasoned adobo or sinigang. Malinamnam is the goal of every Pinoy cook.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to savory flavors, not usually for sweet desserts. It implies a deep, rich, and satisfying taste.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakasarap at **malinamnam** ang sabaw ng bulalo.","translation":"The soup of the bulalo is very delicious and **savory**."},{"sentence":"Mas **malinamnam** ang pagkain kapag bagong luto.","translation":"Food is more **flavorful** when freshly cooked."}]

translation: to make something whiz or zoom
meaning_filipino: Maging sanhi upang ang isang bagay ay gumawa ng mabilis at matunog na pagdaan o paggalaw, tulad ng isang bala o mabilis na sasakyan.
original_explanation: This is what you do with a toy car on a smooth floor. You **pasagitsitin** it! It's the action of making something go 'whoosh' or 'vroom' really fast. Also applies to the sound of bacon sizzling in a pan ('pinasagitsit ang bacon'). It's all about that satisfyingly fast sound and motion.
usage_notes: Describes causing a fast, often noisy, movement.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ng bata na **pasagitsitin** ang kanyang bagong laruang kotse sa sahig.","translation":"The child wants **to make** his new toy car **zoom** across the floor."},{"sentence":"**Pinasagitsit** niya ang gulong ng motor bago umalis.","translation":"He **made** the motorcycle's tires **squeal** before leaving."}]

translation: to use up completely, to exhaust a supply
meaning_filipino: Maubos nang walang anumang natitira; ubusin hanggang sa kahuli-hulihang piraso o patak.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your 13th-month pay by December 26th. It's when you scrape the last bit of Nutella from the jar, or when the ulam is so good, even the sauce on the plate is gone. "Na-masimot ang sahod" is a national tragedy every 'a-kinse' (15th) and 'katapusan' (end of the month).
usage_notes: Often used to describe the depletion of resources, especially food or money. The verb form is typically 'masimot' (future/infinitive) or 'nasimot' (past).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa sobrang sarap ng ulam, agad itong **nasimot** ng mga bata.","translation":"Because the dish was so delicious, it was immediately **devoured** by the children."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi **masisimot** ang pagmamahal ko sa'yo.","translation":"Don't worry, my love for you will not **be exhausted**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan kung saan hindi umiiral o hindi ipinaiiral ang katarungan; paglabag sa karapatan ng iba.
etymology: From `ka-` (marker for abstract nouns) + `walang` ('without') + `katarungan` ('justice'). Literally 'the state of being without justice'.
original_explanation: That feeling when you get blamed for something your sibling did. Or on a larger scale, the systemic issues that make you want to join a protest or just post angry rants on social media. It's the "unfair!" of the adult world.
usage_notes: A formal and serious term often used in legal, political, and social contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malaking **kawalang-katarungan** ang nangyari sa pamilya niya.","translation":"A great **injustice** happened to his family."},{"sentence":"Lumalaban sila sa **kawalang-katarungan** sa lipunan.","translation":"They are fighting against the **injustice** in society."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaikling salita para sa "lokasyon" o "lugar," na tumutukoy sa isang partikular na punto o posisyon.
original_explanation: Short for 'location'. It's what your Grab driver asks for when the pin is wrong, or what your friends message in the group chat: "Send loc!". It’s the modern-day "where you at?", but with GPS coordinates attached.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa impormal na pag-uusap, lalo na sa text o online chat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pre, send **loc**. Papunta na kami.","translation":"Bro, send your **location**. We're on our way."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagkakaroon ng kakayahang kumilos o igalaw ang isang bagay, bahagi ng katawan, o posisyon.
etymology: From 'i-' (causative prefix) + 'galaw' (move) with '-na-' and repetition for progressive aspect.
original_explanation: That feeling of relief when your leg was asleep (naninigas) and you can finally wiggle your toes again. 'Yes, naigagalaw ko na paa ko!' Also applies to that one stubborn screw on your new furniture that you can finally turn. It's about overcoming resistance to motion.
usage_notes: The 'na-' prefix here indicates ability or potential. 'Naigagalaw' means 'is able to be moved' or 'can be moved.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit masakit pa, **naigagalaw** ko na ang aking braso.","translation":"Even if it still hurts, I **am now able to move** my arm."},{"sentence":"Hindi **naigagalaw** ang mabigat na aparador kahit dalawa na kaming nagtutulak.","translation":"The heavy cabinet **cannot be moved** even with the two of us pushing."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na ginagamit sa pagtuturo, tulad ng patpat o ang kamay ng orasan. Tumutukoy din sa nangunguna sa isang karera o kompetisyon.
original_explanation: That stick your terror teacher used to point at the map, or the little hands on a clock that tell you you're late for work again. In sports or any competition, it's the person or team in the lead. Basically, anything that points or leads the way.
usage_notes: Can refer to a physical pointer, a clock hand, or the leader in a competition.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ng guro ang **puntero** para ituro ang Pilipinas sa mapa.","translation":"The teacher used the **pointer** to point to the Philippines on the map."},{"sentence":"Sila ang **puntero** sa kasalukuyang liga ng basketball.","translation":"They are the **frontrunner** in the current basketball league."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang damdamin ng matinding pighati, hapis, o pag-iisa na nararanasan dahil sa isang hindi kanais-nais na pangyayari o kawalan.
original_explanation: The official feeling of "sana all" season. Ito yung nararamdaman mo kapag ghosted ka, kapag umuulan at mag-isa ka lang, o kapag nakita mo yung presyo ng bilihin. It's the default background music of adulting. The opposite of "awra."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya maitago ang **kalungkutan** sa kanyang mga mata.","translation":"She could not hide the **sadness** in her eyes."},{"sentence":"Ang musika ay nakakatulong na maibsan ang kanyang **kalungkutan**.","translation":"Music helps to ease his **sorrow**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang nilalang na may buhay, karaniwang may kakayahang gumalaw at tumugon sa kapaligiran, at hindi isang halaman o tao. Ginagamit din bilang isang ekspresyon ng matinding emosyon tulad ng galit, paghanga, o pagkagulat.
original_explanation: Literal meaning: animal. But in the Philippines, this word is a Swiss Army knife of expressions. "Hayop ka!" can mean "You're an animal/jerk!" or "You're a beast/awesome!". It all depends on the tone. "Ang galing mo, hayop!" (You're awesome!). "Manloloko ka, hayop!" (You're a cheater, you animal!). It's the ultimate emotional amplifier.
usage_notes: Ang kahulugan bilang ekspresyon ay lubos na nakadepende sa tono at konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming uri ng **hayop** ang makikita sa kagubatan.","translation":"Many kinds of **animals** can be seen in the forest."},{"sentence":"**Hayop** sa ganda ang bago mong kotse!","translation":"Your new car is **beastly** beautiful!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na nangangahulugang hindi pinansin, binalewala, o sadyang hindi inintindi.
original_explanation: The art of pretending someone doesn't exist. It's when you see your ex in the mall and suddenly become very interested in a random houseplant. It's the ultimate 'seen zone' but in real life. Derived from 'dead malice.'
usage_notes: A very common slang term. Can be used as an adjective ('Dedma siya sa akin.') or as a root for verbs like 'dinedma' or 'dedmahin.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bakit parang **dedma** lang siya sa pagbati ko?","translation":"Why does he seem to have just **ignored** my greeting?"}]

meaning_filipino: Pukawin o paganahin ang pagtibok o pagpintig, karaniwan ay tumutukoy sa puso.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate goal of every harana, K-Drama marathon, or a well-timed "good morning" text. You want to make someone's heart beat faster. "Siya lang ang may kakayahang **patibukin** muli ang puso kong sawi." It's the verb form of kilig.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in the context of a heart, either literally (in a medical sense) or figuratively (in a romantic sense).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kape ay kayang **patibukin** nang mabilis ang iyong puso.","translation":"Coffee can **make** your heart **beat** faster."},{"sentence":"Isang ngiti mo lang, sapat na para **patibukin** ang puso ko.","translation":"Just one smile from you is enough to **make** my heart **beat**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit at mariing pagdiin o pagtusok sa isang bagay, karaniwan gamit ang daliri o isang matulis na bagay.
original_explanation: It's that annoying thing your little cousin does—poking you again and again saying "Kuya, kuya, kuya." Or you, trying to get your old phone to work, "dumudutdot" ka sa screen hoping it responds. It’s more insistent than a simple "sundot" (poke) and more irritating than a "pindot" (press). It's the physical version of being makulit.
usage_notes: Implies repetition and sometimes annoyance. Can be used for poking a person, an object, or pressing a button repeatedly.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **dumutdot** sa sugat, baka maimpeksyon.","translation":"Don't **poke repeatedly** at the wound, it might get infected."},{"sentence":"**Dumutdot** siya sa doorbell hanggang sa may magbukas.","translation":"He **insistently pressed** the doorbell until someone opened up."}]

translation: a type of native orange (Citrus aurantium)
meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng sitrus na karaniwang kulay berde ang balat kahit hinog na, at may maasim-asim na tamis ang lasa.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "naranja" (orange), na may metatesis o pagpapalit ng posisyon ng tunog.
original_explanation: The OG Filipino orange. It's green on the outside but orange on the inside. It's the fruit that teaches you not to judge a book by its cover. Perfect with a sprinkle of salt, or squeezed into a refreshing juice on a hot day. It’s not as sweet as an imported orange, but it has that distinct 'asim-kilig' flavor we love.
usage_notes: Isang napakakaraniwang prutas sa Pilipinas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong pamatid-uhaw ang bagong pigang katas ng **dalandan**.","translation":"Freshly squeezed **dalandan** juice is my favorite thirst quencher."},{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng isang kilong **dalandan** sa palengke.","translation":"Mom bought a kilo of **native oranges** at the market."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang gusali o lugar na may itsura, karangyaan, o kalakihan na katulad ng isang palasyo.
original_explanation: Describes a house that's so big and fancy, you wonder if the owner is a secret tycoon, a politician, or just won the lottery. It's the kind of house you see in teleseryes where the rich family lives, complete with a grand staircase perfect for dramatic entrances.
usage_notes: The 'mala-' prefix is common and means 'like' or '-ish'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatira sila sa isang **malapalasyo** na bahay sa isang eksklusibong subdibisyon.","translation":"They live in a **palatial** house in an exclusive subdivision."},{"sentence":"Ang lobby ng hotel ay **malapalasyo** sa ganda at laki.","translation":"The hotel lobby is **palace-like** in its beauty and size."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging nasa ilalim ng kontrol, pigil, o kapangyarihan ng iba; hindi malaya.
original_explanation: Imagine your desire to buy something on Shopee during the 12.12 sale, but you force yourself not to because "ipon muna." Your urge is now *supil*. It's being held back, controlled, or put in its place, like a rebellion that was quickly squashed.
usage_notes: Often used with verbs like "masupil" (to be suppressed) or "supilin" (to suppress). As an adjective, it describes a state.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nanatiling **supil** ang mga mamamayan sa ilalim ng diktador.","translation":"The citizens remained **suppressed** under the dictator."},{"sentence":"Sinikap niyang gawing **supil** ang kanyang galit.","translation":"He tried to keep his anger **subdued**."}]

translation: to stay behind; to let oneself be left behind
meaning_filipino: Ang sinasadyang desisyon na manatili sa isang lugar habang ang mga kasama ay umaalis.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `mag-` (gumanap ng kilos), `pa-` (pagpapahintulot), at salitang-ugat na `iwan` (to leave).
original_explanation: The ultimate FOMO trigger. When your barkada goes out and you can't join, you have to `magpaiwan`. It’s also the classic scene in dramas where the hero tells everyone to go on without them. 'Mauna na kayo, susunod na lang ako,' is the official script for someone who will `magpaiwan`. Sometimes it's a choice, sometimes you just have a deadline from your BPO job.
usage_notes: Nagpapahiwatig ng isang may kamalayang desisyon na hindi sumama sa grupo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang sumama sa outing kaya nagdesisyon siyang **magpaiwan** sa bahay.","translation":"She didn't want to join the outing so she decided to **stay behind** at home."},{"sentence":"Sino ang gustong **magpaiwan** para magbantay ng mga gamit?","translation":"Who wants to **stay behind** to watch over our things?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging tapat, direkta, at walang paligoy-ligoy sa pagsasalita.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "franco" (tapat, bukas). Ang unlaping "pagka-" ay nagpapahiwatig ng kalidad o estado ng pagiging prangka.
original_explanation: Same as 'pagkaprangka', but the "o" ending is often used when referring to a male person. It's that guy friend who'll tell you straight up, "Pre, 'wag mo nang i-text 'yan." His **pagkaprangko** saves you from making bad life choices at 2 AM.
usage_notes: Ang "pagkaprangka" at "pagkaprangko" ay halos magkapalitan, bagaman maaaring gamitin ng ilang tagapagsalita ang "prangko" para sa mga lalaki at "prangka" para sa mga babae, na sumasalamin sa pinagmulang Espanyol. Mas karaniwan ang "pagkaprangka" sa pangkalahatan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinangaan ko ang **pagkaprangko** ng lider sa pag-amin ng kanilang mga pagkakamali.","translation":"I admired the leader's **frankness** in admitting their mistakes."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagkaprangko** ay isang katangiang parehong kinatutuwaan at kinaiinisan sa kanya.","translation":"His **candidness** is a trait that is both liked and disliked about him."}]

translation: to reflect on; to ponder deeply
meaning_filipino: Ang masusing pag-isipan o pag-aralan ang isang bagay; ang pagmumuni-muni nang may kalaliman.
original_explanation: This is what you do at 3 AM when you can't sleep, thinking about your life choices, that awkward thing you said in 2012, or if you should finally use your leave credits for a beach trip. It's the verb form of 'deep thoughts,' often fueled by coffee, deadlines, or a major life crossroad. 'Bes, pagnilay-nilayin mo muna bago ka mag-resign.'
usage_notes: A command or suggestion to contemplate something carefully. The reduplication `nilay-nilay` emphasizes the depth and duration of the reflection.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **pagnilay-nilayin** ang mga pagpipilian mo bago magdesisyon.","translation":"You need **to reflect on** your options before making a decision."},{"sentence":"**Pagnilay-nilayin** mo kung ano talaga ang mahalaga sa iyo sa buhay.","translation":"**Ponder deeply** on what is truly important to you in life."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng hayop-dagat na may malambot at mala-gulaman na katawan, at mga galamay na maaaring makapaso.
etymology: Possibly from Malay `dekia` or a Chinese dialect.
original_explanation: The squishy, gelatinous creature at the beach that can ruin your whole summer vacation with one sting. They're the "look but don't touch" (or better yet, "don't even go near") celebrities of the sea.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa mga **dikya** kapag lumalangoy sa dagat.","translation":"Be careful of **jellyfish** when swimming in the sea."},{"sentence":"Napaso ako ng **dikya** noong isang linggo.","translation":"I was stung by a **jellyfish** last week."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagdating o pagparito sa hinaharap; sasapit.
original_explanation: This is the official word for 'Filipino time.' When someone says 'darating na,' it could mean they're 5 minutes away, 30 minutes away, or still in the shower. It's a word full of hope, suspense, and sometimes, a little bit of frustration. It's the promise of a Grab delivery, a Gcash transfer, or your crush finally noticing you.
usage_notes: Future tense of the verb 'dumating' (to arrive).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Darating** na raw ang inorder nating pizza.","translation":"They said the pizza we ordered **will arrive** soon."},{"sentence":"Kailan kaya **darating** ang sweldo?","translation":"When **will** the salary **come**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kalagayan ng pagiging bukas o paglatag ng isang bagay, karaniwan sa mga bulaklak na namumukadkad o mga pakpak na ibinubuka.
original_explanation: 'Yung moment na 'yung sampaguita sa garden ni Lola, nag-bloom na. It's that "reveal" moment. Pwede ring 'yung payong mo, finally na-figure out mo kung paano i-open. From a closed state to a beautiful, open one.
usage_notes: Often used for flowers, wings, or fans.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng mga rosas na **bukad** na sa hardin.","translation":"The roses that have **opened** in the garden are beautiful."},{"sentence":"Nakatayo ang pabo na **bukad** ang makulay na buntot.","translation":"The turkey stood with its colorful tail **spread out**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa ika-3 sa isang pagkakasunod-sunod; ang sumunod sa ikalawa.
original_explanation: You're not the first, you're not the second, you're the **pangatlo**. In a friend group, this is the one who didn't get the main love story. In a race, it's the bronze medalist. In a family, it's the middle child who might be a bit "extra" to get noticed.
usage_notes: An ordinal number. The `ika-` prefix can also be used (`ikatlo`), which is more formal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **pangatlo** sa pila.","translation":"He is **third** in line."},{"sentence":"Ito na ang **pangatlo** mong babala.","translation":"This is your **third** warning."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng iskoba upang linisin o kuskusin nang mariin ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay sahig, damit, o iba pang ibabaw.
etymology: From Spanish "escoba", meaning broom or brush.
original_explanation: The ultimate workout before the gym was a thing. This is what your mom made you do to the bathroom tiles until they were sparkling clean, usually with a dramatic "Hindi ka lalabas hangga't 'di 'yan tapos!"
usage_notes: Specifically refers to scrubbing with a stiff-bristled brush, not just any cleaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **mag-iskoba** ng sahig sa banyo dahil madumi na.","translation":"I need to **scrub** the bathroom floor with a brush because it's already dirty."},{"sentence":"Pinagalitan ako ni Lola kapag hindi ako marunong **mag-iskoba** ng puting damit.","translation":"Grandma scolds me when I don't know how to **scrub** white clothes with a brush."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hayop na likas na nanghuhuli at kumakain ng ibang hayop upang mabuhay.
etymology: Likha mula sa "hayop" at "maninila" (mula sa ugat na "sila", nangangahulugang biktima o prey).
original_explanation: These are the alpha predators of the animal kingdom. The lions, tigers, and eagles. Sa office setting, sila yung mga nang-aagaw ng credit sa project mo. Sa love life, sila yung mga ahas na umaaligid sa jowa mo. The key is the 'maninila' part, from 'sila', which means prey. They hunt.
usage_notes: Isang deskriptibong parirala.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang agila ay isang halimbawa ng **hayop na maninila**.","translation":"The eagle is an example of a **predatory animal**."}]

meaning_filipino: Magbasa nang mabilis, hindi gaanong malalim, o paulit-ulit nang bahagya upang makuha lamang ang pangkalahatang ideya ng isang teksto.
etymology: From `basa` (to read) with reduplication of the first two syllables, indicating a lighter, less intense, or repeated action.
original_explanation: It's what you do to your ex's new posts—you're not really reading, just scanning for drama. It's the "I have an exam tomorrow but I'm on TikTok" level of reading. You just basa-basahin the terms and conditions before clicking "Agree."
usage_notes: Often used to describe casual reading, browsing, or skimming a text without deep analysis. The root word is 'basa' (to read).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mo lang **basa-basahin** ang mga headline para malaman ang balita.","translation":"You just need to **browse** the headlines to know the news."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **basa-basahin** lang ang kontrata, intindihin mo bawat salita.","translation":"Don't just **skim** the contract, understand every word."}]

meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng malinaw na pagkaalam at pag-intindi sa kahulugan, layunin, o katotohanan ng isang bagay, ideya, o sitwasyon.
etymology: From 'unawa' (understanding, comprehension). The 'ma- -an' affix turns it into a verb meaning 'to be able to understand something'.
original_explanation: More than just "to know." This is the "gets ko na!" moment. It's deeper than just hearing the words; it's about grasping the 'why' behind the 'what'. 'Yung tipong finally naintindihan mo na 'yung plot twist ng K-drama or 'yung resibo ng nanay mo. It's the goal of every "We need to talk" conversation.
usage_notes: A more formal and deeper synonym for 'maintindihan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay **maunawaan** mo ang aking sitwasyon.","translation":"I hope you can **understand** my situation."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **maunawaan** ang aralin kung hindi ka nakikinig.","translation":"It's hard **to understand** the lesson if you're not listening."}]

meaning_filipino: Itago ang isang impormasyon o pangyayari mula sa kaalaman ng iba; hindi ipaalam.
original_explanation: 'Bes, secret lang natin 'to, ha?' a.k.a. the start of all chismis. This is what you do when you buy something from Shopee and don't want your parents to know, or when you have a secret crush. You **keep it a secret**, hoping Marites and her friends don't find out.
usage_notes: The focus is on the action of concealing information from someone. The object of the verb is the secret being kept.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ipaglihim** sa akin kung may problema ka.","translation":"Don't **keep it a secret** from me if you have a problem."},{"sentence":"Napagdesisyunan nilang **ipaglihim** muna ang kanilang relasyon.","translation":"They decided to **keep** their relationship **a secret** for now."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdanas at pagpapakita ng matinding kalungkutan o pighati dahil sa isang pagkawala o masamang pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is the opposite of `ipagbunyi`. It’s the deep, soul-crushing sadness you feel for a specific reason. It’s not just being sad; it’s mourning. You ipagdalamhati the passing of a loved one. You ipagdalamhati a great national tragedy. It's the verb for when your heart is truly broken by an event. It's the 'condolence' emotion turned into an action.
usage_notes: A deep and formal word for grieving. The focus is on the cause of the grief.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang buong bansa ay **nagdaramhati** sa pagpanaw ng dating pangulo.","translation":"The whole nation is **grieving** the passing of the former president."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **ipagdalamhati** ang isang pag-ibig na hindi naman naging sa'yo.","translation":"It's hard to **grieve for** a love that was never yours to begin with."}]

translation: to fix; to arrange; to put in order
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay sa tamang kalagayan, pagkakasunud-sunod, o kaayusan ng mga bagay; pag-aareglo ng isang gulo o problema.
original_explanation: The verb for "Marie Kondo-ing" your life. It's what you do to your room when your mom yells "Ang gulo ng kwarto mo!" It's also what you do to your life after a major heartbreak or when you realize your finances are a mess. From fixing a tangled headset to fixing a broken heart, magsaayos is the first step.
usage_notes: A very versatile word. Can mean to physically arrange things, to fix something broken, to settle a dispute, or to get one's life in order.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **magsaayos** ng mga gamit ko bago ako lumipat ng bahay.","translation":"I need to **arrange** my things before I move to a new house."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **magsaayos** ng gusot sa pagitan ng magkapatid.","translation":"He tried to **fix** the conflict between the siblings."}]

translation: to widen, to expand, to broaden
meaning_filipino: Ang paglaki o pagdagdag ng saklaw, espasyo, o sukat ng isang bagay.
etymology: From the root word 'lawak' (width, scope, area) + the '-um-' infix.
original_explanation: That moment when EDSA goes from 2 lanes to 5 lanes, tapos traffic pa rin. That's space lumawak. Or when your knowledge about K-Pop group members lumawak from one to twenty. It's about getting bigger, wider, or more comprehensive.
usage_notes: Can be used for physical spaces (e.g., a road) or abstract concepts (e.g., knowledge, understanding).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lumawak** ang kanyang pang-unawa sa mundo mula nang maglakbay siya.","translation":"His understanding of the world **broadened** since he started traveling."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa baha, **lumawak** ang ilog at umabot sa mga kabahayan.","translation":"Because of the flood, the river **widened** and reached the houses."}]

translation: unrest; lack of peace of mind
meaning_filipino: Ang estado ng pagkabalisa, hindi mapakali, o kakulangan ng kapayapaan sa isip at damdamin.
original_explanation: The feeling you get when you've sent a risky text and the other person is "typing..." for five minutes. It's the "Did I lock the door?" anxiety at 3 AM. It’s the opposite of chill; it's your inner peace going on an unannounced vacation.
usage_notes: Describes a state of mental or emotional distress.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kawalan ng kapanatagan** sa trabaho ay nakakaapekto sa kanyang kalusugan.","translation":"The **lack of peace of mind** at work is affecting his health."},{"sentence":"Nagdulot ng **kawalan ng kapanatagan** sa komunidad ang sunod-sunod na krimen.","translation":"The series of crimes caused **unrest** in the community."}]

translation: to focus on; to aim at
meaning_filipino: Pag-ukulan ng masusing pansin; itapat o ituro ang isang bagay sa isang tiyak na direksyon o target.
original_explanation: This is 'tutok' in verb form. It's what your boss tells you to do with the priority project: "**Tutukan** mo 'yan." It's also what a director tells the cameraman: "**Tutukan** mo 'yung bida." It's the command to give your undivided attention, whether to a spreadsheet or to a celebrity's face.
usage_notes: An object-focus verb, often used as an imperative (command) to direct attention or to point something towards a subject.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **tutukan** ang iyong pag-aaral para makapasa.","translation":"You need to **focus on** your studies to pass."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **tutukan** ng flashlight sa mata.","translation":"Don't **aim** the flashlight at my eyes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pagpapasya sa pamamagitan ng paghagis ng barya, kung saan ang isang panig ay "kara" (mukha) at ang kabilang panig ay "krus" (krus).
etymology: From Spanish `cara` (face) and `cruz` (cross), referring to the two sides of old Spanish coins.
original_explanation: The OG way of settling disputes in the Philippines, from who pays for the movie tickets to who gets the last piece of chicken. "Kara" is for the side with a face (like Jose Rizal's), and "krus" is the other side. It's the ultimate game of chance, 50/50, bahala na si Batman.
usage_notes: A very common phrase used when initiating a coin toss.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-**kara-krus** tayo kung sino ang unang titira.","translation":"Let's do a **coin toss** to see who goes first."},{"sentence":"Nanalo ako sa **kara-krus**, kaya ako ang pumili ng kakainin natin.","translation":"I won the **heads or tails**, so I got to choose what we'll eat."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang yunit ng sukat ng lupa na katumbas ng sampung libong metro kuwadrado (10,000 m²).
original_explanation: Ito yung unit of measurement na ginagamit ng mga mayayaman para sa lupa nila. Pag sinabi ng tita mo na may "isang hektarea" silang taniman ng mangga, alam mo nang big-time. For the rest of us, ang kaya nating sukatin ay "isang platitong kanin."
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa agrikultura, real estate, at pagpaplano ng lupa. Ang "ektarya" ay isang karaniwang varyant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binili niya ang limang **hektarea** ng lupain para gawing resort.","translation":"He bought five **hectares** of land to turn into a resort."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging magkatulad o magkamukha sa isa't isa sa anyo, ugali, o iba pang aspeto.
etymology: From the Spanish word 'parejo' (even, equal), adopted into Tagalog as 'pareho'. The 'pagkaka-' prefix forms a noun meaning 'the state or quality of being similar'.
original_explanation: When you and your workmate show up wearing the same Uniqlo shirt. That's 'pagkakapareho'. It can be about looks, ideas, or tastes. 'Grabe ang pagkakapareho namin, pati sa paboritong K-drama!' (Our similarities are crazy, even our favorite K-drama is the same!).
usage_notes: A very common word. 'Pagkakatulad' is a close synonym. 'Pagkakaparehas' is also used colloquially.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita agad ang **pagkakapareho** ng magkapatid.","translation":"The **similarity** of the siblings was immediately seen."},{"sentence":"Sa kabila ng kanilang mga pagkakaiba, marami rin silang **pagkakapareho**.","translation":"Despite their differences, they also have many **similarities**."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagsama-samahin ang mga halaga o bilang upang makuha ang kabuuan.
original_explanation: Parang pag-compute ng total ng inorder niyo sa GrabFood, or yung pag-calculate mo ng lahat ng gastos mo for the month tapos mapapa-'sana all mayaman' ka na lang. To sumahin is to get the total, the grand total, the 'damage' sa wallet mo.
usage_notes: This is a command or an infinitive form. The completed action form (past tense) is 'sinuma'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**sumahin** mo lahat ng ating gastusin para sa buwang ito.","translation":"Please **total** all our expenses for this month."},{"sentence":"Nang **sumahin** niya ang mga puntos, nalaman niyang panalo ang kanilang koponan.","translation":"When he **summed up** the points, he found out their team had won."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng may kakulangan sa talino o pang-unawa; hangal. Tumutukoy din sa mga bilog at kenyong sangkap na gawa sa gawgaw na inihahalo sa mga inumin.
etymology: From Spanish 'boba' (foolish female). The food meaning comes from Taiwanese Hokkien 'bōbà', a slang term for the large tapioca balls.
original_explanation: This is the feminine version of 'bobo'. But let's be real, in 2026, it's more famous as the tapioca pearls in your milk tea. 'Extra boba, please!' is a national prayer. So, are you talking about a person or a drink? Context is key, bes.
usage_notes: When used for a person, it is an offensive term for a female. It is also the common term for tapioca pearls in bubble tea.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpanggap na **boba**, alam kong naintindihan mo.","translation":"Don't pretend to be **stupid**, I know you understood."},{"sentence":"Gusto ko ng maraming **boba** sa milk tea ko.","translation":"I want a lot of **boba** in my milk tea."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong (babae) mahilig magtanong o mag-usisa tungkol sa buhay o gawain ng iba.
original_explanation: The official title of the neighborhood 'Marites'. An usisera is the human version of a CCTV camera, always monitoring the comings and goings, and always ready with a follow-up question. The male version is 'usisero'.
usage_notes: Feminine form. The masculine form is 'usisero'. Carries a slightly negative connotation of being meddlesome.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala ang kapitbahay naming si Aling Nena bilang isang tunay na **usisera**.","translation":"Our neighbor Aling Nena is known as a truly **nosy person**."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa pagiging **usisera**, alam niya ang lahat ng chismis sa aming barangay.","translation":"Because of being **nosy**, she knows all the gossip in our village."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paraang hindi nakikita, nalalaman, o napapansin ng iba; palihim.
original_explanation: How you eat the last piece of cake from the fridge at 2 AM. How you check your crush's social media profile. It's doing something on the down-low, away from prying eyes (aka the neighborhood chismosa). The official 'ninja mode' of the Filipino language.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Patago** siyang kumuha ng pagkain sa ref habang tulog ang lahat.","translation":"He **secretly** got food from the ref while everyone was asleep."},{"sentence":"Nagkita sila nang **patago** upang hindi malaman ng kanilang mga magulang.","translation":"They met **stealthily** so their parents wouldn't find out."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang dalubhasang manggagawa na nagpapatakbo ng mga makina, lalo na sa paggawa ng mga piyesa mula sa metal o iba pang materyales.
original_explanation: Sila 'yung mga tito na kayang-kayang ayusin 'yung makina ng owner-type jeep n'yo o gumawa ng custom na parts para sa kung anuman. Think of them as the wizards of the metal shop, turning blocks of metal into useful things.
usage_notes: Commonly used in technical and vocational contexts. Spelled as borrowed from English.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng isang mahusay na **machinist** para sa proyektong ito.","translation":"We need a skilled **machinist** for this project."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi nakakapukaw ng interes o atensyon; walang sigla o kabuhay-buhay.
original_explanation: Ito yung 3-hour company meeting na pwedeng i-summarize sa isang email. Or yung movie na puro salita at walang action. It's the official word for "boring." If something is di-kawili-wili, you'd rather be scrolling on TikTok.
usage_notes: Direktang negasyon ng salitang "kawili-wili" (interesting).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para sa akin, **di-kawili-wili** ang palabas na iyon.","translation":"For me, that show was **uninteresting**."},{"sentence":"Nakatulog siya sa gitna ng **di-kawili-wili**ng talumpati.","translation":"He fell asleep in the middle of the **dull** speech."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang oras sa dapit-hapon kung kailan ang araw ay naglalaho sa abot-tanaw sa kanluran.
etymology: Literally translates to "sinking of the sun". A phrase combining `paglubog` (sinking) and `araw` (sun).
original_explanation: The OG aesthetic shot. The official signal to start your 'sana all' posts while looking at happy couples on the beach. Perfect for dramatic IG stories with sad songs, or just chilling with a beer after a long day's work.
usage_notes: A very common phrase. Synonymous with 'takipsilim'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakagandang pagmasdan ang **paglubog ng araw** sa Manila Bay.","translation":"It's so beautiful to watch the **sunset** at Manila Bay."}]

translation: To hammer; to strike; a strike
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paulit-ulit na pagpalo o paghampas sa isang bagay gamit ang martilyo o anumang matigas na bagay. Maaari rin itong tumukoy sa tunog na nalilikha nito.
original_explanation: The sound your neighbor makes at 7 AM on a Sunday. 'Pukpok' is the act of hammering or striking something repeatedly. It's what a carpenter does to a nail, what a judge does with a gavel (but we call that 'pukpok ng maso'), and what your head feels like after a long night out. 'Pukpok ka nang pukpok!' (You keep on hammering!).
usage_notes: Can be a noun (the act or sound of striking) or a verb (to strike).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang martilyo para **pukpukin** ang pako sa dingding.","translation":"He used the hammer to **strike** the nail into the wall."},{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **pukpok** mula sa ginagawang bahay sa kabilang kalsada.","translation":"I heard the **hammering** from the house being built across the street."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pakiramdam sa balat na nag-uudyok sa isang tao na kamutin ito, kadalasang sanhi ng kagat ng insekto, alerdyi, o sakit sa balat.
original_explanation: That annoying feeling you get from a mosquito bite that makes you want to scratch it like there's no tomorrow. Pwede ring "kati" ang tawag sa friend mong malandi, as in "makati"—someone who's "itching" for a romantic partner (or five).
usage_notes: The adjective form "makati" (itchy) is extremely common and is also used colloquially to mean "flirtatious" or "promiscuous".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko matiis ang **kati** sa aking likod.","translation":"I can't stand the **itch** on my back."},{"sentence":"Nawala ang **kati** nang pahiran ko ito ng gamot.","translation":"The **itchiness** went away when I applied medicine to it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang matulis na bahagi ng kawil o palaso na nakabaluktot paatras upang hindi matanggal kapag tumusok. Ginagamit din bilang pain.
original_explanation: Ito yung 'the catch' sa isang bagay. Parang sa fishing, ito yung maliit na hook na kapag kumagat na yung isda, wala nang kawala. In dating, ito yung 'pa-fall' move ng isang tao para ma-hook ka. Pwede ring tumukoy sa mismong pain or 'lure'.
usage_notes: Can refer to the physical barb of a hook or arrow, or to the bait used for fishing. Metaphorically, it can mean a trap or lure.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tiyakin mong may **sima** ang iyong kawil para hindi makawala ang isda.","translation":"Make sure your hook has a **barb** so the fish won't escape."},{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng bulate bilang **sima** sa pamingwit.","translation":"He used a worm as **bait** for the fishing rod."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita o nakakaramdam ng matinding hindi pagkagusto, pagkadiri, o pagkayamot sa isang tao, bagay, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: 'Yung mukha mo 'pag nakakita ka ng ipis sa pagkain mo. Or 'yung reaction mo sa isang cringey na post sa social media. It's that mix of "yuck," "eww," and "I'm so done." The female form is "disgustada."
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang ilarawan ang damdamin ng pagkadiri o pagkayamot. Mayroon ding pambabaeng anyo na 'disgustada'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Disgustado** siya sa napanood niyang balita tungkol sa korapsyon.","translation":"He was **disgusted** by the news he watched about corruption."},{"sentence":"Naging **disgustado** ang mga customer dahil sa mabagal na serbisyo.","translation":"The customers became **displeased** because of the slow service."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangalawang pinuno o opisyal na may ranggong kasunod ng kapitan, lalo na sa isang barangay o barko.
original_explanation: Basically the VP of the barangay. If Kap is the main character, the segundo kapitan is the reliable best friend who gets things done when the star is busy. They're the one you talk to for the *real* chismis.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng pamamahala sa barangay o sa mga lumang terminolohiya sa barko.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinausap ng mga residente ang **segundo kapitan** tungkol sa problema sa basura.","translation":"The residents spoke to the **vice-captain** about the garbage problem."},{"sentence":"Habang wala si Kap, ang **segundo kapitan** muna ang mamamahala.","translation":"While the Captain is away, the **vice-captain** will be in charge for now."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang dalubhasa sa topograpiya; isang taong ang trabaho ay sukatin at ilarawan ang mga katangian ng isang lugar o rehiyon upang makagawa ng mapa.
original_explanation: Siya yung taong professional na tiga-measure ng lupa, parang high-tech na agrimensor. Sila yung nakikita mo sa gilid ng kalsada na may parang camera na nakatayo sa tripod (theodolite), tinitingnan kung gaano kataas o kababa ang isang lugar. Sila ang dahilan kung bakit alam ng Waze kung saan may bundok at kung saan may ilog.
usage_notes: Isang teknikal na termino na ginagamit sa larangan ng heograpiya at inhinyeriya sibil.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinuha ang serbisyo ng isang **topograpo** para sa paggawa ng plano ng bagong subdibisyon.","translation":"The services of a **topographer** were hired to create the plan for the new subdivision."},{"sentence":"Ang mga **topograpo** ay mahalaga sa pagpaplano ng mga imprastraktura tulad ng mga kalsada at tulay.","translation":"**Topographers** are essential in planning infrastructure like roads and bridges."}]

translation: his; hers; to him; to her
meaning_filipino: Panghalip paari o palayon sa ikatlong panauhan na tumutukoy sa isang tao.
etymology: A contraction of the preposition *kay* and pronoun *niya*, or from *sa* and *iya* in older forms.
original_explanation: The ultimate pronoun for when you're talking about someone else's stuff or giving them something. "Is this your charger?" "No, it's **hers** (*sa kanya*)." "Who should I give this to?" "**To him** (*sa kanya*)." It's the linguistic equivalent of pointing at someone else's lane and saying, "That's their business."
usage_notes: A very common pronoun. It is gender-neutral. Often used with "sa" (sa kanya) or "para sa" (para sa kanya). Can also mean "possession" in some contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ibigay mo **kanya** ang sulat na iyan.","translation":"Give that letter **to him/her**."},{"sentence":"Ang librong ito ay hindi sa akin, **kanya** ito.","translation":"This book is not mine, it's **his/hers**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng kasapi o tagasunod ng Simbahang Katoliko Romano.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na 'católica' (Katoliko, pambabae).
original_explanation: She's the Tita who reminds you to go to mass on Sundays and probably has a Sto. Niño collection that can rival a museum's. A woman who is a member of the world's biggest Christian church.
usage_notes: Ang anyong pambabae ng 'Katoliko'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aking lola ay isang debotong **Katolika**.","translation":"My grandmother is a devout **Catholic**."},{"sentence":"Lumaki siya sa isang pamilyang **Katolika**.","translation":"She grew up in a **Catholic** family."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtanggap o pagharap sa isang taong dumarating, o ang pagdiriwang para sa isang mahalagang okasyon na paparating.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate Filipino welcome. Yung pagdating ng kamag-anak from abroad, buong barangay andun sa airport? That's a grand pagsalubong. Also applies to how we meet the New Year with fireworks, food, and lots of noise. It's not just a 'hello', it's an event.
usage_notes: Can refer to welcoming people (e.g., at an airport) or welcoming an event (e.g., New Year).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging emosyonal ang **pagsalubong** ng pamilya sa kanilang OFW na ama.","translation":"The family's **welcoming** of their OFW father was emotional."},{"sentence":"Handa na ba kayo para sa **pagsalubong** sa Bagong Taon?","translation":"Are you ready for **welcoming** the New Year?"}]

meaning_filipino: Pagsasama o paghahalo ng isang bagay sa iba upang maging bahagi nito; sangkap.
original_explanation: It's like when you're making adobo and the soy sauce, vinegar, and garlic *langkap* together to create that perfect flavor. It's the fusion, the perfect blend. In life, it's when your personality and your partner's just click—*langkap na langkap* ang mga ugali ninyo. It can also mean 'possessed by a spirit' (nilangkapan), which is a totally different, more terrifying kind of blend.
usage_notes: Often used in cooking or when describing things that are perfectly mixed or integrated. The spiritual meaning of 'possession' (e.g., 'nilangkapan ng masamang espiritu') is also a common usage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bawang ay mahalagang **langkap** sa maraming lutuing Pilipino.","translation":"Garlic is an important **ingredient** in many Filipino dishes."},{"sentence":"**Langkap** sa kanyang pagkatao ang pagiging matulungin.","translation":"Helpfulness is **incorporated** into his personality."}]

translation: to put to bed, to arrange in a bed
meaning_filipino: Ilagay o ihanda sa higaan o kama ang isang bagay o tao.
original_explanation: Ito yung action na ginagawa mo sa lasing mong tropa para siguraduhing 'di siya sa sahig matutulog. Or when you finally get your sweldo and you just want to ikama your money and roll in it (figuratively, of course... unless?). Also, 'pag pagod na pagod ka na, gusto mo na lang 'ikama' ang sarili mo.
usage_notes: A less common but understood term. More common ways to say this would be 'ihiga sa kama' (to lay on the bed).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahan-dahan niyang **inikama** ang natutulog na sanggol.","translation":"He slowly **put the sleeping baby to bed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maranasang tamaan sa mukha gamit ang palad, karaniwang dahil sa galit o bilang parusa.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'you crossed the line' moment in any Pinoy drama. It's when you get a face-full of someone's hand, usually accompanied by a dramatic gasp. 'Pag na-realize mong mali ka ng sinabi sa nanay mo at nakita mong tumaas na kamay niya, this is what you're about to experience. The physical manifestation of 'How dare you?!'.
usage_notes: The verb is in the object-focus form. The subject of the sentence is the one who gets slapped.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang **masampal** kaya nanahimik na lang siya.","translation":"He didn't want to **be slapped**, so he just kept quiet."},{"sentence":"Halos **masampal** ko siya sa inis.","translation":"I almost **slapped** him out of annoyance."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na likas na mahilig magbiro o magpatawa.
original_explanation: Your dad with his dad jokes, your officemate who sends memes all day, or that tito who always has a corny joke ready for any occasion. A palabiro is the designated court jester of the family or barkada. Not all their jokes land, but they get an A for effort.
usage_notes: Generally a positive or neutral trait.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala si Mark bilang isang **palabiro** sa aming klase.","translation":"Mark is known as a **jokester** in our class."}]

translation: to be lucky; to get lucky
meaning_filipino: Ang makaranas ng suwerte o maging mapalad sa isang sitwasyon o pangyayari.
etymology: Salitang ugat na 'suwerte' na may panlaping '-in'.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'sana all.' Ito yung dasal mo bago ka tumaya sa lotto, bago mag-exam, o bago ka umamin sa crush mo. 'Sana **suwertihin** ako ngayon!'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay **suwertihin** ka sa iyong bagong trabaho.","translation":"I hope you **get lucky** in your new job."},{"sentence":"Bihira siyang **suwertihin** sa mga laro ng pagkakataon.","translation":"He is rarely **lucky** in games of chance."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging mahinahon, kalmado, at hindi madaling magalit o mataranta sa gitna ng kaguluhan o problema.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'sana all' state of mind. It's having 100 unread emails, a deadline in an hour, and your boss is looking for you, but you're still sipping your coffee calmly. It's the opposite of 'panic mode'. It's the Zen-like state you aspire to have when stuck in EDSA traffic. It’s your inner Tito/Tita telling you to just breathe.
usage_notes: Refers to a state of being calm and composed, especially under pressure.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit sa gitna ng gulo, nanatili ang kanyang **pagkahinahon**.","translation":"Even in the midst of chaos, he maintained his **composure**."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkahinahon** ay isang mahalagang katangian para sa isang lider.","translation":"**Calmness** is an important trait for a leader."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng pagkakataong makita o makatagpo ang isa't isa.
original_explanation: The classic 'kita-kits!' verb. It's what you say when you're making plans with the barkada that might or might not actually happen (a.k.a. 'drawing'). It can be a planned meeting at a coffee shop or a surprise encounter with your ex at the mall. Awkward.
usage_notes: Often used in the future tense `magkikita` (will meet). `Magkita` is the infinitive or command form. `Magkita-kita` is used for groups of more than two.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Saan tayo **magkikita** mamaya?","translation":"Where will we **meet** later?"},{"sentence":"Sana **magkita** tayong muli sa lalong madaling panahon.","translation":"I hope we **meet** again very soon."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang aklat kung saan itinatala ang mga transaksyong pampinansyal o iba pang mahahalagang impormasyon sa isang organisadong paraan.
original_explanation: The ancient ancestor of Microsoft Excel. This is the notebook your sari-sari store-owning tita uses to list down everyone who has 'utang'. Every line item is a potential source of 'chismis' or future collection efforts. "Nasa talaang-aklat ko lahat ng nangutang ng empanada."
usage_notes: Formal term. In everyday conversation, 'listahan' or 'notebook ng utang' is more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maingat na isinulat ng tesorero ang bawat gastos sa **talaang-aklat**.","translation":"The treasurer carefully wrote every expense in the **ledger**."},{"sentence":"Ang lumang **talaang-aklat** na iyon ay naglalaman ng kasaysayan ng aming negosyo.","translation":"That old **record book** contains the history of our business."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na termino para sa pagbili, pagkuha, o pagkakaroon ng isang bagay, lalo na ang isang bagay na kanais-nais o uso.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-lansangan (slang) sa Ingles na "cop", na nangangahulugang "to get" o "to acquire".
original_explanation: The hypebeast way of saying 'bumili.' Hindi ka lang bumibili, you 'cop' the latest drip, the new kicks, the limited edition merch. 'Did you cop the new Jordan release?' sounds way cooler than 'Nabili mo ba yung bagong sapatos?' It's all about the hype.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit ng mga kabataan, lalo na sa kultura ng sneakers at streetwear.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong i-**cop** yung bagong labas na t-shirt ng paborito kong banda.","translation":"I want to **cop** the new t-shirt release from my favorite band."},{"sentence":"Ang hirap mag-**cop** ng sapatos na 'yun, laging sold out!","translation":"It's so hard to **cop** those shoes, they're always sold out!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na may halaga, tulad ng pera o gantimpala, na ibinibigay sa isang tao bilang kapalit ng isang serbisyo, tulong, o impormasyon.
etymology: From the prefix `pa-` and `buya`, an old word related to grace or favor. A 'pabuya' is something given as a favor or reward.
original_explanation: This is the cash prize for finding a lost dog or for the capture of a notorious criminal. It's the "Wanted: Dead or Alive" money. In the office, it might be the bonus for the top-performing agent. It’s the universe (or your boss) saying "Salamat sa effort, eto cash."
usage_notes: Often refers specifically to a monetary reward for a specific deed or for providing information, such as a bounty.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May malaking **pabuya** na nakalaan para sa sinumang makakapagturo sa kinaroroonan ng mga suspek.","translation":"There is a large **bounty** for anyone who can pinpoint the whereabouts of the suspects."},{"sentence":"Natanggap niya ang **pabuya** matapos isauli ang nawawalang pitaka.","translation":"He received the **reward** after returning the lost wallet."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bahagi ng puno o halaman na tumutubo mula sa puno (trunk) o sa mas malaking sanga. Ginagamit din ito upang tukuyin ang isang dibisyon o lokal na yunit ng isang mas malaking organisasyon.
original_explanation: A *sanga* is a branch. Literally, it's what you see on a tree. Figuratively, it's that BDO or Jollibee branch near your office. It's the family *sanga* in Cebu that you only see during Christmas reunions. It represents both growth and division—things spreading out from a central source, just like *chismis*.
usage_notes: Highly versatile, used in both natural and organizational contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May pugad ng ibon sa **sanga** ng puno ng mangga.","translation":"There is a bird's nest on the **branch** of the mango tree."},{"sentence":"Magbubukas sila ng bagong **sanga** ng bangko sa aming bayan.","translation":"They will open a new **branch** of the bank in our town."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal o Taglish na nangangahulugang kasalukuyang nag-iipon (ng pera) o nagliligtas (ng isang bagay o tao). Ito ay nasa aspektong imperpektibo.
original_explanation: What you tell your friends you're doing when they ask you to go out, but you're really just broke. "**Nagsasave** ako para sa future." (Future = the next 12.12 sale). Also, what you do every 5 seconds in a Word doc to avoid a thesis-ending disaster.
usage_notes: A Taglish word with two common meanings: saving money (mag-ipon) or saving a file/data (i-save). The context clarifies the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagsasave** ako ng pera para makabili ng bagong cellphone.","translation":"I **am saving** money to buy a new cellphone."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong kausapin, **nagsasave** ako ng importanteng file.","translation":"Don't talk to me, I **am saving** an important file."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan na ginagamit upang sukatin ang bigat o masa ng isang bagay.
etymology: From 'timbang' (weight) + '-an' (noun suffix indicating a place or instrument).
original_explanation: The 'timbangan' is your frenemy at the 'palengke' (wet market). You use it to make sure the vendor isn't cheating you on your kilo of pork. It's also that thing in the bathroom you avoid after the holidays. From checking your baggage allowance at the airport to measuring ingredients for baking, the 'timbangan' is the ultimate judge of weight. "Patingin sa timbangan, ate!"
usage_notes: Refers to any kind of scale, from a small kitchen scale to a large industrial one.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ilagay mo ang mga isda sa **timbangan** upang malaman ang bigat.","translation":"Put the fish on the **weighing scale** to find out the weight."},{"sentence":"Ayokong tumuntong sa **timbangan** pagkatapos ng Pasko.","translation":"I don't want to step on the **weighing scale** after Christmas."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpayag, pagkakasundo, o pagpapakita ng katulad na opinyon o damdamin sa iba.
original_explanation: The 'samedt' or 'I agree' of formal Filipino. It's the nod you give in a meeting when the boss says something smart. It's the opposite of being a 'kontrabida'. Getting your parents' pagsang-ayon to go on a trip with friends is a major life achievement.
usage_notes: A formal word for agreement. 'Pagpayag' is more about permission, while 'pagsang-ayon' is more about alignment of opinion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ang **pagsang-ayon** ng lahat ng miyembro bago simulan ang proyekto.","translation":"We need the **agreement** of all members before starting the project."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang pananahimik ay hindi nangangahulugan ng **pagsang-ayon**.","translation":"Her silence does not mean **consent**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bagay, proyekto, o negosyo na pinaglalaanan ng puhunan o kapital sa kasalukuyang kilos.
etymology: From the root 'puhunan' (investment, capital), with verbal affixes 'pina-' and '-an', and root duplication 'mu-'.
original_explanation: The thing you're pouring your time, money, and maybe even tears into, hoping for a good ROI. It could be your small online business, your sibling's education, or that condo unit you're paying for monthly.
usage_notes: Refers to the object or entity receiving the investment. A complex verb form indicating an ongoing action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang start-up na ito ang **pinamumuhunanan** ng maraming dayuhang kumpanya.","translation":"This start-up **is being invested in** by many foreign companies."},{"sentence":"Malaki ang tiwala niya sa proyektong kanyang **pinamumuhunanan**.","translation":"He has great faith in the project he **is investing in**."}]

translation: to shine; to sparkle; to glitter
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbuga o pagpapakita ng matinding liwanag o kintab.
original_explanation: This is what you tell yourself in the mirror before a big presentation or a first date: "Kailangan kong magningning!" It's the ultimate goal of your highlighter, the twinkle in your eye when you see your crush, or how a star is born (literally and figuratively). Be the ✨main character✨.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin sa literal na paraan (para sa mga bituin, alahas) o sa metaporikal na paraan (para sa talento, tagumpay).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais ng bawat bituin sa showbiz na **magningning** ang kanilang pangalan.","translation":"Every star in showbiz wants their name to **shine**."}]

meaning_filipino: Manindigan sa isang paniniwala, karapatan, o pahayag; ipilit ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is your 'I said what I said' moment. It's when you stand your ground, whether you're arguing for your rights, defending your opinion in a heated debate, or just really, really insisting that pineapple belongs on pizza. It's the verbal version of planting your feet and refusing to be moved.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of rights, opinions, or arguments.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Patuloy niyang **igigiit** ang kanyang karapatan bilang isang manggagawa.","translation":"He will continue to **assert** his rights as a worker."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **igiit** ang gusto mo kung ito ay makakasama sa iba.","translation":"Don't **insist** on what you want if it will harm others."}]

translation: to have something thrown away; to have someone exiled
meaning_filipino: Utos na alisin at ilagay sa basurahan ang isang bagay na hindi na kailangan; o utos na palayasin o ilayo ang isang tao sa isang lugar bilang parusa.
original_explanation: Your mom's daily command for the trash bag. Also, what you want to do with your ex's memories (and their hoodie). In history class, it's what they did to Rizal in Dapitan. One word, two levels of drama: household and historical.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Luma na ang sapatos na iyan, mas mabuting **ipatapon** na lang.","translation":"Those shoes are old, it's better to just **have** them **thrown away**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pampublikong lugar na nag-aalok ng akses sa internet, karaniwang may bayad kada oras, kasama ang mga serbisyo tulad ng pag-print at paglalaro ng mga computer games.
original_explanation: The holy ground for Filipino gamers and students rushing a last-minute project. It smells of air conditioning, instant noodles, and teenage angst. Before everyone had WiFi at home, the internet cafe (or 'comshop') was the community center where you could play DOTA, chat on YM, and print your thesis with a 'RUSH ID' sign on the side. A cultural landmark.
usage_notes: Often colloquially called 'comshop' (computer shop).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkita tayo sa **internet cafe** mamaya para maglaro ng Valorant.","translation":"Let's meet at the **internet cafe** later to play Valorant."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong magpa-print sa **internet cafe** dahil sira ang printer ko.","translation":"I need to print at the **internet cafe** because my printer is broken."}]

meaning_filipino: Maglaan o gumamit ng puhunan o salapi para sa isang negosyo o proyekto.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of what your tita who's an OFW does to start her milk tea shop. It's taking your 'puhunan' (capital) and putting it into a business, hoping it turns into more money. It’s the act of betting on yourself (or someone else) with cold, hard cash.
usage_notes: Almost exclusively used in business, finance, or economic contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **mangapital** sa teknolohiya para lumago ang kumpanya.","translation":"We need to **invest capital** in technology for the company to grow."}]

translation: to show a sample; to gesture to someone
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbibigay o pagpapakita ng isang muwestra (halimbawa o senyas) sa isang tao.
original_explanation: This is the action version of 'muwestra'. It's what you do when you need to show, not just tell. You muwestrahan your friend with the correct dance step. The traffic enforcer will muwestrahan you to stop or go. The tindera will muwestrahan you with the different cuts of pork. It's a very active, demonstrative word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Muwesrahan** mo nga ako kung paano gawin 'yang bagong TikTok dance.","translation":"**Show me** how to do that new TikTok dance."},{"sentence":"**Minuwestrahan** ng pulis ang mga sasakyan na tumuloy na.","translation":"The police officer **gestured** for the cars to proceed."}]

translation: to sway gently, to rock repeatedly
meaning_filipino: Marahan at paulit-ulit na gumalaw nang pabalik-balik; mag-ugoy nang may paglalambing o dahan-dahan.
original_explanation: This is the 'chill' version of 'umugoy'. The repetition of the root word 'ugoy' implies a gentler, more continuous, and often more deliberate action. It's not the violent sway of an earthquake, but the gentle rocking of a boat on calm water, or a mother lulling her baby to sleep. It’s 'ugoy' with extra tenderness.
usage_notes: The duplication of the root word ('uguy-ugoy') indicates a continuous, repeated, or diminutive action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Habang kumakanta ng oyayi, marahang **umuguy-ugoy** ang ina sa kanyang sanggol.","translation":"While singing a lullaby, the mother gently **rocked** her baby."},{"sentence":"Masarap matulog sa duyan na **umuguy-ugoy** sa tabi ng dagat.","translation":"It's nice to sleep in a hammock that is **swaying gently** by the sea."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong ang trabaho ay maglinis at magmantina ng isang gusali, tulad ng paaralan, opisina, o ospital.
original_explanation: The unsung hero of every office, school, and mall. Sila yung nag-aayos ng kalat na iniwan mo, yung nagmo-mop ng sahig na tinapunan mo ng kape, at yung taga-ensure na hindi mukhang dumpster fire ang workplace. Often more reliable than your office WiFi. Give them a smile and a 'thank you, kuya/ate!'
usage_notes: Filipinized spelling of the English word. The word 'tagalinis' is a more native equivalent but 'diyanitor' is very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinulungan kami ng **diyanitor** na buksan ang naka-lock na pinto.","translation":"The **janitor** helped us open the locked door."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng malaking isdang-alat na karaniwang nahuhuli sa malalalim na bahagi ng dagat, kilala rin bilang atún.
etymology: From Spanish 'barril' (barrel), referring to the fish's barrel-shaped body.
original_explanation: This is the big fish that ends up as sashimi in Japanese restaurants or canned tuna in your pantry. In General Santos City, the "Tuna Capital of the Philippines," a giant barilis can be a status symbol for a fisherman. It's the heavyweight champion of the sea.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'atun', but 'barilis' is more common in Visayan-influenced areas like Mindanao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sariwa ang huling **barilis** mula sa General Santos.","translation":"The newly caught **tuna** from General Santos is fresh."},{"sentence":"Mahal ang kilo ng **barilis** sa palengke ngayon.","translation":"The price per kilo of **tuna** in the market is expensive today."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawin o mangyari sa ikalawang pagkakataon o nang panibago; umulit.
original_explanation: Like hitting the 'replay' button on life's dramas. "Nag-away na naman sila? Hay, magmuli na naman ang teleserye." It's the feeling when you have to re-do your work because you forgot to save. Ulit?
usage_notes: Can imply a return to a previous state or a simple repetition of an action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, **magmuli** kang babangon mula sa pagkakadapa.","translation":"Don't worry, you will rise **again** from your fall."},{"sentence":"Sana'y **magmuli** ang ating pag-iibigan.","translation":"I hope our love will happen **again**."}]

translation: to put a hat on someone
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagpapatong ng sumbrero sa ulo ng isang tao.
original_explanation: That moment when your mom forces a hat on you before you go out to play. "Sumbreruhan mo 'yung kapatid mo, baka masunog!" It's an act of caring, even if it messes up your hair.
usage_notes: The '-an' suffix indicates the location or recipient of the action. In this case, the person whose head the hat is being put on.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumbreruhan** mo ang bata para hindi mainitan.","translation":"**Put a hat on** the child so they don't get hot."},{"sentence":"Nagpumilit siyang **sumbreruhan** ako kahit ayoko.","translation":"He insisted on **putting a hat on me** even though I didn't want to."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagtitipon kung saan ang pangunahing gawain ay ang pag-inom ng alak hanggang sa malasing; inuman.
original_explanation: This isn't just a casual drink. This is a drinking *session*. The 'walwalan' night. It's where the pulutan is endless, the playlist is a mix of OPM rock and hugot songs, and the 'isang case pa!' chant is inevitable. It's where secrets are spilled, friendships are tested, and hangovers are born.
usage_notes: Implies a more intense or focused drinking event compared to a simple 'inuman'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagyaya si Mark ng **lasingan** sa bahay nila sa Sabado.","translation":"Mark invited us for a **drinking session** at his house on Saturday."},{"sentence":"Napagalitan siya dahil umuwi siyang madaling-araw galing sa **lasingan**.","translation":"He got scolded because he came home at dawn from a **drinking binge**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang partikular na oras, karaniwan sa gabi o madaling araw, kung kailan ang isang tao ay mas madaling mag-isip ng mga pantasya o malalayong imahinasyon.
etymology: A phrase derived from the slang "delulu."
original_explanation: It's that 3 AM mood when you're staring at the ceiling, imagining your whole life with your crush after they liked your post from two weeks ago. When the world is quiet, your imagination gets loud. Welcome to delulu hours.
usage_notes: Used to describe a specific time, usually late at night, for indulging in delusional thoughts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Open na naman ang **delulu hours** ko, ini-imagine ko na mag-reply siya.","translation":"My **delulu hours** are open again, I'm imagining that he will reply."},{"sentence":"Magpatulog ka na, hindi 'yung puro ka **delulu hours** diyan.","translation":"Go to sleep already, instead of just indulging in **delulu hours**."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang ibabaw na hindi pantay at may maraming umbok o bukol.
original_explanation: 'Yung kalsada sa probinsya na hindi pa sementado. 'Yung gravy na hindi mo hinalo nang maayos. 'Yung kutson mo na luma na. Anything that isn't smooth and has multiple bumps is 'bukul-bukol.' The opposite of 'makinis'.
usage_notes: The repetition of the root word 'bukol' indicates plurality or intensity, meaning 'many lumps' or 'very lumpy'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bukul-bukol** ang daan kaya dahan-dahan lang ang takbo ng sasakyan.","translation":"The road is **bumpy** so the car is running slowly."},{"sentence":"Naging **bukul-bukol** ang pintura dahil hindi ito naipakalat nang maayos.","translation":"The paint became **lumpy** because it wasn't spread properly."}]

translation: to do; to make; to create
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasakatuparan ng isang kilos, paglikha ng isang bagay, o pagtupad sa isang gawain.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate Filipino verb. From 'gumawa ng assignment' (do homework) to 'gumawa ng paraan' (find a way), it's all about action. It's the Pinoy's answer to Nike's "Just Do It." When there seems to be no solution, a Filipino will always find a way to 'gumawa ng paraan'. It's the verb of diskarte and creativity.
usage_notes: An extremely versatile and fundamental verb in Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Gumawa** siya ng isang magandang tula.","translation":"He **made** a beautiful poem."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **gumawa** ng paraan para malutas ito.","translation":"We need to **do** something (find a way) to solve this."},{"sentence":"Ano ang **ginawa** mo buong araw?","translation":"What did you **do** all day?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkain nang may kasibaan, mabilis, at sa malaking kantidad.
original_explanation: The only acceptable way to eat at a samgyupsal buffet. You don't just 'kumain', you lumamon. It's a sport, a lifestyle. 'Tara, lumamon tayo ng unli-wings!'
usage_notes: An informal and more intense version of 'kumain' (to eat). It implies a lack of grace and a huge appetite.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng laro, gutom na gutom ang mga manlalaro kaya sila ay **lumamon**.","translation":"After the game, the players were so hungry that they **devoured** their food."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babae na malapit nang ikasal o nasa akto ng pagpapakasal.
original_explanation: The star of the show, the main character, the woman about to change her civil status and (possibly) her last name. She's the reason for the expensive glam team, the traffic-causing wedding entourage, and the fifty-strong ninong/ninang list. Basically, the queen for a day.
usage_notes: A compound noun from 'babae' (woman) and 'ikakasal' (will be wed). The male equivalent is 'lalaking ikakasal' (groom).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakaganda ng **babaing ikakasal** sa kanyang puting bestida.","translation":"The **bride** is so beautiful in her white dress."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kamay na nakatikom nang mahigpit, na ang mga daliri ay nakabaluktot paloob sa palad.
etymology: From Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *kaməl, with a similar meaning.
original_explanation: It's your hand balled up, ready for a fist bump with a friend or, you know, for more 'intense negotiations'. It's the symbol of fighting spirit, like when Manny Pacquiao raises his kamao after a win, or when activists raise theirs during a protest. It's 'suntukan' mode activated.
usage_notes: Also used figuratively to represent struggle, resistance, or power.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinaas niya ang kanyang **kamao** bilang simbolo ng paglaban.","translation":"He raised his **fist** as a symbol of resistance."},{"sentence":"Tinamaan siya ng malakas na **kamao** sa mukha.","translation":"He was hit by a strong **fist** on the face."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso, sining, o kakayahan ng paggabay, pamamahala, at pag-impluwensya sa isang grupo ng mga tao upang makamit ang isang karaniwang layunin.
etymology: From `puno` (leader, head, chief). The `paN-` prefix (manifesting as `pam-`) and reduplication creates a noun for the act or state of being a leader.
original_explanation: The thing everyone in your group project is trying to avoid, until one person (the bida-bida or the real leader) finally steps up. It's the difference between a company that gives 13th month pay on time and one that... doesn't. It's what you hope your barangay captain, your manager, and the president of the Philippines actually have.
usage_notes: Refers to the quality or act of leadership, while 'pinuno' refers to the leader themselves.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinakita niya ang kanyang galing sa **pamumuno** sa panahon ng krisis.","translation":"He showed his skill in **leadership** during the time of crisis."},{"sentence":"Ang mabuting **pamumuno** ay nagsisimula sa pakikinig sa nasasakupan.","translation":"Good **leadership** starts with listening to your constituents."}]

meaning_filipino: Isa pang balbal na anyo ng salitang "pare," na hango sa "repa" at dinagdagan ng hulaping "-kol" para sa karagdagang diin o istilo.
original_explanation: This is 'repa' on steroids. It's the level-up version you use when 'repa' or 'pare' just doesn't have enough punch. It’s got that extra ‘oomph’, like adding extra rice to your siomai meal. Often used with a friendly slap on the back.
usage_notes: Very informal and often used for comedic or emphatic effect among close friends. The '-kol' suffix adds a layer of rugged, street-smart affection.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Repakol**, ang ganda ng bagong motor mo!","translation":"**Dude**, your new motorcycle is awesome!"},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, **repakol**, sasamahan kita.","translation":"Don't worry, **buddy**, I'll go with you."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang lugar na may gumagamit o tao na; o sa isang tao na maraming ginagawa at walang libreng oras.
original_explanation: 'Yung status ng CR sa Jollibee pag long weekend. O 'yung sagot ng kaibigan mo kapag niyayaya mo gumala pero ayaw ka lang niya talagang kasama. 'Sorry, okupado ako' is the new 'It's not you, it's me.'
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa isang taong abala o sa isang lugar/bagay na ginagamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pasensya na, **okupado** ang linya ng telepono.","translation":"Sorry, the telephone line is **busy**."},{"sentence":"Laging **okupado** si nanay sa mga gawaing-bahay.","translation":"Mom is always **busy** with household chores."},{"sentence":"May tao ba sa banyo? **Okupado** ba?","translation":"Is someone in the bathroom? Is it **occupied**?"}]

translation: to be enough, to fit, to suffice
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng sapat na espasyo upang magkasya; maging sapat sa bilang o dami.
etymology: From the adjective "kasya" (can fit, enough). "Kasiya" is often used in verb conjugations, though the verb "magkasya" is more common.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'kasya'. This is what you pray for when you're trying to fit all your pasalubong into one carry-on bag. 'Sana **kasiya** lahat!' It's also used for budget: 'Will my salary be enough until the next payday?' The eternal Filipino question.
usage_notes: While it can stand alone in some contexts, it's more frequently seen as part of a conjugated verb like "magkasiya" or in the phrase "kasiya pa" (still fits). The adjective "kasya" is more common than this verb form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi **kasiya** sa isang van ang buong pamilya kaya kumuha kami ng isa pa.","translation":"The whole family will not **fit** in one van so we got another one."},{"sentence":"Tingnan mo kung **kasiya** pa ang mga ito sa kahon.","translation":"See if these will still **fit** in the box."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maikling dibisyon ng isang kabanata sa Bibliya o anumang banal na kasulatan; isang linya ng tula.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung linya sa Bible na pino-post mo sa IG story mo 'pag feeling blessed ka or 'pag may pinagdadaanan. 'Yung "Jeremiah 29:11" na laging bukambibig. Pwede ring linya sa kanta o tula.
usage_notes: Karaniwang tumutukoy sa mga linya sa Bibliya, ngunit maaari ring gamitin para sa mga linya sa tula o awit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paborito kong **bersikulo** sa Bibliya ay ang Juan 3:16.","translation":"My favorite **verse** in the Bible is John 3:16."},{"sentence":"Bawat **bersikulo** ng tula ay puno ng damdamin.","translation":"Every **verse** of the poem is full of emotion."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa dalawa o higit pang mga gumagamit ng social media (tulad ng Twitter, Instagram, o TikTok) na parehong naka-follow sa isa't isa.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na "mutuals", pinaikling "mutual followers".
original_explanation: In the digital palengke of social media, your 'mutuals' are your suki. You follow them, they follow you back. It's a silent agreement of 'I see your content, you see mine.' They're your online kapitbahay who see your latest chika, hugot posts, and food pics. Hoping your crush becomes your mutual is a modern-day love story.
usage_notes: Ginagamit halos eksklusibo sa konteksto ng social media. Madalas ding tawaging 'moots'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang saya, isa sa mga paborito kong artist ay **mutuals** ko na sa Twitter!","translation":"So happy, one of my favorite artists and I are now **mutuals** on Twitter!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kapistahang Kristiyano na ginugunita ang pagdalaw ng Tatlong Mago sa batang Hesus. Kilala rin bilang Pasko ng mga Hari, ito ay sumisimbolo sa paghahayag ni Kristo sa mga Hentil.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'Epifanía', na mula sa Griyegong 'epiphaneia' na nangangahulugang "pagpapakita" o "paghahayag".
original_explanation: Eto yung official end ng Christmas season sa Pinas, 'yung Pasko ng Tatlong Hari. Last chance mo nang mangaroling at kumain ng mga natirang handa. After nito, balik na sa totoong buhay at tanggalin na ang Christmas tree. Ang pangalang "Epipania" ay classic name din para sa mga lola.
