usage_notes: Madalas tumutukoy sa relihiyosong kapistahan. Ang 'Epipania' ay isang baryasyon sa pagbaybay na ginagamit din, lalo na bilang pangalan ng tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagdiriwang ng **Epipaniya** ay tuwing unang Linggo pagkatapos ng Bagong Taon.","translation":"The celebration of the **Epiphany** is on the first Sunday after New Year."},{"sentence":"Si Lola **Epipania** ang nagluto ng masarap na biko.","translation":"Lola **Epipania** cooked the delicious sweet rice cake."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagdudulot ng matinding damdamin na nagiging sanhi ng pagluha o pag-iyak, maaaring dahil sa kalungkutan, galak, o awa.
etymology: From `naka-` (causative prefix) + reduplication of the first vowel `i-` + `iyak` (cry).
original_explanation: The ending of 'Heneral Luna' or 'Goyo'. That viral Jollibee commercial. Or when you see your phone bill after using data roaming. It's anything that hits you right in the feels and makes you reach for the tissue, whether from sadness or from seeing your bank account.
usage_notes: Describes something that evokes a strong emotional response, leading to tears. Can be from sadness, happiness, or being touched.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nakaiiyak** ang mga eksena sa pelikulang 'Miracle in Cell No. 7'.","translation":"The scenes in the movie 'Miracle in Cell No. 7' are **tear-jerking**."},{"sentence":"**Nakaiiyak** ang presyo ng bilihin ngayon.","translation":"The price of goods today is enough **to make you cry**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang puwersang pisikal na nagdudulot ng pagkahalina o pag-atras ng mga bagay (magnetismo). Sa matalinhagang paraan, ito ay tumutukoy sa di-pangkaraniwang pang-akit o karisma ng isang tao.
etymology: From Malay 'berani' (courageous), which may have influenced the sense of 'attraction'. In physics, it's the direct term for magnetism.
original_explanation: The "it" factor. The force that makes you stare at your crush from across the room. It’s the invisible string that pulls you towards someone or something, like how you're pulled towards the last piece of leche flan. It’s the scientific term for 'landi' or 'karisma'.
usage_notes: Can be used both literally for physical magnetism (magnetismo) and figuratively for personal charm or charisma.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan sa siyensya ang **balani** ng mga batubalani.","translation":"Science studies the **magnetism** of magnets."},{"sentence":"May kakaibang **balani** ang kanyang mga mata na nakakabighani.","translation":"There is a strange **allure** in his/her eyes that is captivating."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangalawa sa huli sa isang serye, partikular na ang pangalawa sa huling pantig ng isang salita.
etymology: Mula sa Latin na 'paenultima,' mula sa 'paene' (halos) + 'ultima' (huli).
original_explanation: This is the 'sana all' of the finish line. Not the winner, but also not the last place. It's the second to the last episode of your favorite K-drama, the second to the last day of the work week (Thursday!), or the second to the last piece of lechon on the platter. It's that moment of anticipation right before the end. In linguistics, it's where the stress usually falls in Filipino words (e.g., ma-GAn-da), making it a low-key MVP of pronunciation.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa mga konteksto ng linggwistika at panitikan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang diin sa salitang 'tao' ay nasa **penultima**.","translation":"The stress in the word 'tao' is on the **penult**."},{"sentence":"Siya ang **penultima** sa pila kaya matagal pa siyang maghihintay.","translation":"He is **second to the last** in line, so he still has a long wait."}]

meaning_filipino: Madalas magbago; hindi permanente o matatag sa isang kalagayan, desisyon, o damdamin.
original_explanation: Describes your 'situationship,' the weather in the Philippines, or your friend who can't decide where to eat. It means inconsistent, fickle, or always changing. 'Pabago-bago ang isip niya' (His/Her mind is always changing) is the ultimate hugot for anyone dealing with an indecisive person.
usage_notes: The reduplication emphasizes the repetitive or continuous nature of the change.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ako makapagplano dahil **pabago-bago** ang isip mo.","translation":"I can't make plans because your mind is so **fickle**."},{"sentence":"Normal lang na **pabago-bago** ang panahon sa Pilipinas.","translation":"It's normal for the weather in the Philippines to be **inconsistent**."}]

meaning_filipino: Sining ng paggawa ng mga kahanga-hangang kilos ng katawan tulad ng pagtalon, pag-ikot, at pagbalanse, na kadalasang ginagawa sa himpapawid.
original_explanation: This is the fancy word for all the 'pa-impress' moves you see in a circus, a fiesta performance, or even in action movies. Think of it as the OG parkour. It's the art of flipping and twisting your body in ways that make your mom say 'Nako, baka mabalian ka!'
usage_notes: Can also refer to a single acrobatic feat. Sometimes used to describe showy or flashy movements in martial arts or dance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Humanga ang mga manonood sa ipinakitang **silambang** ng mga artista sa sirko.","translation":"The audience was amazed by the **acrobatics** shown by the circus performers."},{"sentence":"Bahagi ng kanilang pagsasanay sa martial arts ang pagsasagawa ng **silambang**.","translation":"Performing **aerial maneuvers** is part of their martial arts training."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa kalipunan ng mga bagay na may iba't ibang uri, anyo, o katangian; halo-halo.
original_explanation: This is the official adjective of the Filipino household drawer where you find everything from old batteries, a random button, a single chopstick, to your birth certificate. It's the "etc." in spoken form. "Ano laman ng bag mo?" "Sarisari... alam mo na, pambayad, resibo, lip balm, at tatlong takip ng ballpen na walang ballpen."
usage_notes: Almost always used before a noun, as in 'sari-saring bagay' (miscellaneous things). The hyphenated form 'sari-sari' is also very common and interchangeable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May tindahan siya ng **sarisari**ng paninda sa palengke.","translation":"She has a store with **assorted** goods in the market."},{"sentence":"Napag-usapan namin ang **sarisari**ng paksa, mula politika hanggang showbiz.","translation":"We talked about **various** topics, from politics to showbiz."}]

translation: to make into kilawin; to cure in vinegar
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagbabad ng hilaw na pagkain sa suka o anumang maasim na likido upang ito ay maluto nang walang apoy.
original_explanation: This is the action part! It's the verb form of making that awesome pulutan. When your tito says "Kilawin mo na 'yang isda!", he's giving you the sacred task of transforming raw fish into a party-ready dish using the magic of vinegar.
usage_notes: The verb form is less common in everyday conversation than the noun, but is standard in recipes and cooking instructions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kilawin** natin ang nahuling tuna para mamaya.","translation":"Let's **make kilawin** out of the caught tuna for later."},{"sentence":"Ituro mo sa akin kung paano **kilawin** ang pusit.","translation":"Teach me how to **cure squid in vinegar**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalapat ng marahang haplos sa isang tao o bagay; ang pandiwang anyo ng himas.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'himas'. It's the command or the action. "Himasin mo 'yung pusa." (Pet the cat.) It's the direct act of applying that gentle stroke. Simpler than 'himas-himasin', it just means to do the action once or as a general instruction.
usage_notes: Object-focused verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais kong **himasin** ang iyong buhok.","translation":"I want to **caress** your hair."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutan na **himasin** ang alaga nating aso.","translation":"Don't forget to **pet** our pet dog."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pananalita na gumagamit ng mga salitang kabaligtaran ng tunay na kahulugan upang mangutya o manlibak.
etymology: Nagmula sa Proto-Philippine na *uyam* na nangangahulugang 'kutyain' o 'pagtawanan'.
original_explanation: This is the high-falutin' word for sarcasm. It's that 'Wow, ang galing mo talaga' you say to your friend who just tripped on a flat surface. Uyam is the art of throwing shade with a smile. It's the spice in many Pinoy jokes and 'parinig'.
usage_notes: Mas karaniwan sa mga pampanitikan o pormal na konteksto kaysa sa pang-araw-araw na pananalita, kung saan mas ginagamit ang 'sarcasm' o 'pamba-bara'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **uyam** ang kanyang mga papuri.","translation":"His praises were full of **sarcasm**."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya napansin ang **uyam** sa boses ng kausap.","translation":"He didn't notice the **mockery** in the person's voice."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang elementong kemikal na may simbolong Ra at atomikong bilang na 88. Ito ay isang radyaktibong metal.
original_explanation: Isa sa mga OG na 'glow-in-the-dark' na materyales bago pa nauso ang neon lights. Sikat dati sa orasan, pero nalaman nilang delikado pala. Basically, the original 'forbidden' glow stick.
usage_notes: Isang salitang pang-agham.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang elementong **radyum** ay natuklasan ni Marie Curie.","translation":"The element **radium** was discovered by Marie Curie."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng tulong, paglilingkod, o pagganap ng tungkulin para sa kapakanan ng iba, ng isang komunidad, o ng bansa.
original_explanation: This is a big word. It's what politicians promise to do during campaign season. It's also what you do when you work in the BPO or a restaurant—you provide service. From "public service" to "customer service," ang goal ay magserbisyo.
usage_notes: Can refer to public service, military service, customer service, or any act of serving others.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pangarap niya ay **magserbisyo** sa bayan bilang isang sundalo.","translation":"His dream is **to serve** the country as a soldier."},{"sentence":"Tungkulin ng mga opisyal ng gobyerno na **magserbisyo** nang tapat sa mga mamamayan.","translation":"It is the duty of government officials **to serve** the citizens honestly."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng isang tao na nagtataksil, hindi tapat, o mapanlinlang, lalo na sa isang kaibigan o pinagkakatiwalaan.
etymology: The root 'lamara' is not commonly isolated, but the word itself is well-understood. It implies betrayal and deceit.
original_explanation: This is the classic 'ahas' or snake in the friend group. The one who smiles at you but is secretly screenshotting your convos to send to your ex. They're the Brutus to your Caesar, the co-worker who takes credit for your work. Super kontrabida vibes.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a person who betrays trust in a dramatic or harmful way.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa mga taong **palamara** na kunwari'y kaibigan.","translation":"Be careful of **treacherous** people who pretend to be friends."},{"sentence":"Ang **palamara** niyang ginawa ay habambuhay kong hindi malilimutan.","translation":"I will never forget the **traitorous** thing she did."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng isdang tabang na karaniwang matatagpuan sa mga palayan at putikan, kilala sa kakayahang mabuhay kahit sa labas ng tubig nang panandalian.
original_explanation: The OG survivor fish. This is the fish you see wriggling in the palengke that refuses to accept its fate. It can live in muddy, low-oxygen water, making it a symbol of resilience. If your friend is tough and can thrive anywhere, you can say, 'Para kang dalag, kahit saan buhay!'
usage_notes: A common freshwater fish in the Philippines, often used in local cuisine like sinigang or pesa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap gawing sinigang ang sariwang **dalag**.","translation":"Fresh **mudfish** is delicious for sinigang."},{"sentence":"Nakakahuli sila ng **dalag** sa mga bukirin pagkatapos ng ulan.","translation":"They can catch **snakehead fish** in the fields after it rains."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pandiwa ng pag-aalis ng dumi sa isang partikular na lugar o ibabaw gamit ang walis. Ang diin ay nasa lugar na nililinis.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'adulting.' It's not about what you're sweeping, but *where* you're sweeping it. 'Walisan mo yung kwarto' means clean the whole room, not just the pile of chichirya crumbs. It's about taking responsibility for a messy space, whether it's your floor or your life choices.
usage_notes: Focus is on the location being swept. Contrast with 'walisin' (to sweep something away).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyong **walisan** mo ang sahig ng kusina pagkatapos mong magluto.","translation":"Please **sweep** the kitchen floor after you cook."},{"sentence":"Tuwing umaga ay wina**walisan** ni Aling Nena ang kanilang bakuran.","translation":"Every morning, Aling Nena **sweeps** their yard."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging mahiyain o kimi; ang pag-aatubili sa pakikisalamuha sa ibang tao dahil sa kakulangan ng kumpiyansa sa sarili o pag-iwas sa atensyon.
original_explanation: This is that moment when your crush looks at you and you suddenly become an expert at studying the floor. It's the 'dalagang Pilipina' mode, where you can't make eye contact, your voice becomes a whisper, and you wish you had an invisibility cloak. It’s the opposite of being a 'bibo kid.'
usage_notes: The form `pagkamahihiyain` is a reduplicated version that emphasizes the trait, but `pagkamahiyain` is more commonly used and understood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **pagkamahiyain**, hindi niya nasabi ang kanyang nararamdaman.","translation":"Because of his **shyness**, he wasn't able to say what he felt."},{"sentence":"Subukan mong bawasan ang iyong **pagkamahiyain** upang magkaroon ka ng maraming kaibigan.","translation":"Try to lessen your **shyness** so you can have more friends."}]

translation: to be able to draw (a lot); to be able to pull out
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang humugot o kunin ang isang bagay mula sa kinalalagyan nito, karaniwan sa pamamagitan ng palabunutan o raffle.
original_explanation: Yung kaba mo sa Christmas party exchange gift habang nagbubunutan. 'Sana pangalan ko **makabunot** ni boss!' O 'yung swerte mo kung ikaw ang **makabunot** ng grand prize sa raffle.
usage_notes: The 'maka-' prefix indicates the ability or potential to perform the action of 'bunot' (to pull out, to draw lots).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino kaya ang suwerteng **makabunot** ng nanalong numero sa raffle?","translation":"I wonder who will be the lucky one **to be able to draw** the winning number in the raffle?"},{"sentence":"Hindi ko **makabunot** ang tinik na bumaon sa aking daliri.","translation":"I can't **pull out** the splinter that got stuck in my finger."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang kilos ng paglilipat ng datos (tulad ng larawan, video, o dokumento) mula sa isang lokal na kompyuter o aparato patungo sa isang sentral na server o sa internet.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa mo sa TikTok, IG, at Facebook para makita ng buong mundo ang bago mong selfie, 'yung kinain mong lunch, o 'yung sayaw na pinraktis mo ng isang oras. If you're not nag-a-upload, did it even happen? Minsan, mas mabilis pa 'yung chismis kaysa sa internet connection na nag-a-upload ng video mo.
usage_notes: A clear example of code-switching and borrowing from English, fully integrated into modern Tagalog with Filipino verb affixes (nag-a-).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bakit ang bagal ng internet? Kanina pa ako **nag-a-upload** ng video sa YouTube.","translation":"Why is the internet so slow? I've been **uploading** a video to YouTube for a while now."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maingay, **nag-a-upload** ako ng mahalagang file para sa trabaho.","translation":"Be quiet, I'm **uploading** an important file for work."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang grupo ng mga indibidwal, karaniwang binubuo ng mga pari, pastor, at iba pang opisyal, na nangangasiwa sa mga gawain at doktrina ng isang simbahan o kongregasyon.
original_explanation: The OG admin team of the church. They're the ones leading the mass or service, organizing the fiesta, and giving spiritual advice. When they make an announcement, everyone in the parish listens, especially the 'Marites' of the community.
usage_notes: Refers to the governing body of a religious congregation, not just a single leader.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang desisyon ay nagmula sa **pamunuan ng simbahan**.","translation":"The decision came from the **church leadership**."},{"sentence":"Nakipag-ugnayan ang alkalde sa **pamunuan ng simbahan** para sa isang proyektong pangkawanggawa.","translation":"The mayor coordinated with the **church leadership** for a charity project."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na nakabitin at maluwag na gumagalaw o hindi nakaunat nang maayos.
original_explanation: Imagine your lolo's old favorite shirt, the collar is definitely 'nakalawlaw'. Or that feeling when you've been working overtime for 3 straight days and even your chin feels like it's sagging. Also, 'yung dila ng pagod na aso.
usage_notes: Often describes clothing, skin, or anything that has lost its firmness or tightness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto na niyang palitan ang kanyang lumang T-shirt dahil **nakalawlaw** na ang kuwelyo nito.","translation":"He wants to replace his old T-shirt because its collar is already **sagging loosely**."},{"sentence":"**Nakalawlaw** ang dila ng aso matapos tumakbo nang malayo.","translation":"The dog's tongue was **dangling** after running a long distance."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang reptilya, na karaniwang napakalaki, mula sa Panahong Mesozoic na ngayon ay wala na.
original_explanation: Yung mga lolo at lola ng mga butiki na nag-expire na. Also, a term for someone or something na super luma na, or out of touch sa modern times. "Ang tech mo, pang-dinosauro pa!"
usage_notes: The English word 'dinosaur' is very commonly used and understood in the Philippines, often more so than 'dinosauro'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito ng mga bata ang mga laruang **dinosauro**.","translation":"Toy **dinosaurs** are a favorite among children."},{"sentence":"Natuto kami tungkol sa mga **dinosauro** sa klase ng agham.","translation":"We learned about **dinosaurs** in science class."}]

translation: to give a ride (on a motorcycle/bicycle)
meaning_filipino: Pahintulutan o isama ang isang tao na sumakay bilang pasahero sa likod ng motorsiklo, bisikleta, o katulad na sasakyan.
etymology: ipag- (benefactive prefix) + angkas (to ride as a passenger on a two-wheeled vehicle)
original_explanation: This is the official verb for saying "be my backride." When you see your friend with a motorcycle and you need a lift, you ask, "Ipag-angkas mo naman ako!" It's the ultimate solution for beating traffic, Filipino style. It's not just a ride; it's an experience of trust (and holding on for dear life).
usage_notes: Used to ask for or to give someone a ride on a two-wheeled vehicle. The simpler form 'iangkas' is also very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mabait si kuya, **ipinag-angkas** niya ako hanggang sa sakayan ng bus.","translation":"The guy was kind, he **gave me a ride** on his motorcycle up to the bus stop."},{"sentence":"Pwede mo ba akong **ipag-angkas** papuntang palengke?","translation":"Can you **give me a ride** to the market?"}]

translation: to borrow (money), to take a loan
meaning_filipino: Ang paghiram ng pera sa isang tao o institusyon na may kasunduang ito ay ibabalik, kadalasan na may kasamang interes.
original_explanation: The national sport during "petsa de peligro" (the days before payday). 'Pag 'yung kaibigan mo biglang super bait sa'yo, tapos may kasunod na "P're, baka pwedeng...", malamang uutang 'yan. Also the origin story of many friendship breakups.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to borrowing money or sometimes, by extension, favors that create a debt of gratitude ("utang na loob"). For borrowing objects, "humiram" is used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinailangan niyang **umutang** sa bangko para sa pagpapaaral ng kanyang anak.","translation":"He needed **to take a loan** from the bank for his child's education."},{"sentence":"Mas mabuting mag-ipon kaysa palaging **umutang**.","translation":"It is better to save than to always **borrow money**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagsipsip ng likido mula sa isang lalagyan o pinagmulan.
original_explanation: This is the verb form you use when you're telling someone *where* to slurp from. 'Higupan mo 'tong mangkok' (Sip from this bowl). It's object-focused, but the object is the source, not the liquid itself. Perfect for when you want to share your bulalo but not the actual meat.
usage_notes: The focus of this verb is the container or source from which one sips. Contrast with 'higupin', which focuses on the liquid being sipped.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayokong **higupan** ang tasa na ginamit mo na.","translation":"I don't want to **sip from** the cup that you already used."},{"sentence":"Ang mangkok na ito ang paborito niyang **higupan** ng sabaw.","translation":"This bowl is his favorite one to **sip from** when having soup."}]

translation: to suspect; to wrongly accuse; to mistake someone for
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibintang o paghinala sa isang tao nang walang sapat na batayan; ang pagkakamali sa pagkilala o pag-unawa sa tunay na katangian o intensyon ng isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: 'Huwag mo akong pag-akalaan!' is the classic line when your mom thinks you ate the last piece of leche flan (but it was really your sibling). It's being the 'sus' in a game of Among Us. It's when your friend assumes you're galit, but you're really just hungry. It's the verb form of 'assuming makes an ass out of u and me.'
usage_notes: Often carries a negative connotation of wrongful judgment or misidentification.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo siyang **pag-akalaan** na magnanakaw dahil lang sa kanyang itsura.","translation":"Don't **suspect** him of being a thief just because of his appearance."},{"sentence":"Madalas akong **pag-akalaan** na mas matanda kaysa sa tunay kong edad.","translation":"I am often **mistaken for** being older than my actual age."}]

translation: to have someone baptized; baptismal party
meaning_filipino: Bilang pandiwa, ito ay ang akto ng pag-organisa o pagsasagawa ng binyag para sa isang tao. Bilang pangngalan, ito ay tumutukoy sa salu-salo o pagdiriwang pagkatapos ng seremonya ng binyag.
original_explanation: There are two meanings. 1) The verb: 'Pabinyagan na natin si baby!' means 'Let's have the baby baptized!' 2) The noun: 'Saan ang pabinyagan?' means 'Where's the baptismal party?' This is the reception after the church ceremony, where the ninongs and ninangs are expected to show up and the main event is often the lechon.
usage_notes: The noun form is very common and refers specifically to the reception/party, not the religious rite itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Plano nilang **pabinyagan** ang kanilang anak sa susunod na buwan.","translation":"They plan to **have** their child **baptized** next month."},{"sentence":"Inimbitahan kami sa **pabinyagan** sa isang sikat na restaurant.","translation":"We were invited to the **baptismal party** at a famous restaurant."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghiwa nang manipis at pahilis sa isang bagay, tulad ng isda.
original_explanation: The verb form of making a 'hilis'. This is the action. 'Hilisin mo yung isda' means slice the fish diagonally, not just any old chop-chop. It's a command for a specific, slightly fancy cut. Ito ang utos ng nanay mo bago ka paglutuin ng sinigang.
usage_notes: A command or action word for preparing food.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyong **hilisin** mo ang bangus para sa paksiw.","translation":"Please **slice** the milkfish diagonally for the stew."},{"sentence":"Kailangang matalas ang kutsilyo para madaling **hilisin** ang karne.","translation":"The knife needs to be sharp to easily **slice** the meat."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagsuri sa katotohanan ng mga impormasyon o pahayag upang matiyak ang kawastuhan nito bago paniwalaan o ibahagi.
original_explanation: The most important skill to have kapag 'yung tita mo sa Facebook nag-share na naman ng 'remedy' sa lahat ng sakit gamit ang bawang at sibuyas. Bago ka maniwala sa chismis na may holiday bukas, mag-**fact-check** ka muna sa official sources. It's the digital anting-anting against fake news.
usage_notes: Became extremely relevant and widely used due to the proliferation of misinformation online.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalagang i-**fact-check** ang lahat ng balitang nababasa online.","translation":"It's important to **fact-check** all the news you read online."},{"sentence":"Sino ang mag-aakala na kailangan nating i-**fact-check** pati ang sinasabi ng mga kamag-anak sa family GC?","translation":"Who would have thought we'd need to **fact-check** even what our relatives say in the family group chat?"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa labis na palamuti o paggamit ng maliligoy na salita sa pagsusulat o pagsasalita.
etymology: Metaphorical extension from the dish, which has many toppings ('palamuti').
original_explanation: This is the writing equivalent of the noodle dish - too many toppings! When someone uses big, complicated words to sound smart but doesn't really say anything, that's "puro palabok." It's verbal garnish. Think of a politician's speech that's long but has no substance. "Ang daming palabok, ano ba talaga ang punto?"
usage_notes: Used to describe language, writing, or speech that is unnecessarily embellished. Usually has a slightly negative connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tanggalin mo ang mga hindi importanteng detalye, masyadong maraming **palabok** ang sanaysay mo.","translation":"Remove the unimportant details, your essay is too **flowery**."}]

translation: to be piled up; to be swamped with
meaning_filipino: Maipon o magkapatong-patong ang maraming bagay sa isang lugar; magkaroon ng labis na dami ng isang bagay, lalo na ang gawain.
original_explanation: This is you every Monday morning, staring at your inbox. "Natambak na naman ang work!" It's that feeling of being buried, not by soil, but by deadlines, laundry, or unread messages. It's the physical manifestation of "sana all tapos na."
usage_notes: Often used to describe being overwhelmed with work, chores, or debt.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **matambak** ang mga labahin mo.","translation":"Don't let your laundry **pile up**."},{"sentence":"Mukhang **matatambak** na naman ako ng trabaho pagbalik ko mula sa bakasyon.","translation":"It looks like I'll be **swamped** with work again when I get back from vacation."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang napakahabang yugto ng panahon na sumasaklaw sa maraming sanlibong taon.
original_explanation: The amount of time it feels like you've been waiting for your crush to text back. Or the time it takes for a government project to finish. It's the ultimate time-based exaggeration for anything that takes forever. "It's been libu-libong taon!"
usage_notes: A common phrase to denote a very long period, often used in historical, geological, or hyperbolic contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga pyramid sa Ehipto ay nakatayo na nang **libu-libong taon**.","translation":"The pyramids in Egypt have been standing for **thousands of years**."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam ko'y **libu-libong taon** na akong naghihintay sa pila na ito.","translation":"I feel like I've been waiting in this line for **thousands of years**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang utos o sigaw na nag-uudyok na umusad o sumugod pauna.
original_explanation: The battle cry of every Filipino mom trying to get the family out the door on a Sunday morning. It’s what you yell at your screen during a Mobile Legends clash when your team is hesitating. "Ano pa hinihintay niyo, Pasko?! Sulong!"
usage_notes: Always used as a command or exclamation. Often carries a sense of urgency or aggression. Often translated as 'Charge!' in a military context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sulong**, mga kapatid! Ipaglaban ang ating karapatan!","translation":"**Forward**, my brethren! Fight for our rights!"},{"sentence":"Sigaw ng heneral, '**Sulong**!'","translation":"The general shouted, '**Charge**!'"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng ang hanapbuhay o libangan ay ang pagbuburda o paglalagay ng palamuting disenyo sa tela gamit ang karayom at sinulid.
original_explanation: The OG artisan before DIY vlogs were a thing. She's the tita or lola who can turn a plain panyo or barong into a masterpiece with just a needle, thread, and a whole lot of patience. The male version is 'burdador'.
usage_notes: The root word is 'burda' (embroidery). The male counterpart is 'burdador'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala ang Lumban, Laguna sa kanilang mahuhusay na **burdadora**.","translation":"Lumban, Laguna is known for its skilled female **embroiderers**."},{"sentence":"Ang lola ko ay isang dating **burdadora** ng mga Barong Tagalog.","translation":"My grandmother was a former **embroiderer** of Barong Tagalogs."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, lalo na isang istraktura, na itinayo upang magsilbing paalala sa isang tao o kaganapan. Maaari ding tumukoy sa isang serbisyo o seremonya para sa pag-alaala.
original_explanation: Ito yung parang "in loving memory of..." na moment. Pwedeng building (like a memorial park chapel), isang plaque sa pader, o isang service para alalahanin ang isang yumao. Sa Pilipinas, madalas itong i-associate sa mga 'memorial plan' na kukunin mo para 'di mamroblema pamilya mo 'pag time mo na. #Adulting101
usage_notes: Often used in the context of funeral services or insurance plans ('memorial plan').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtayo sila ng isang **memorial** para sa mga bayaning nasawi sa digmaan.","translation":"They built a **memorial** for the heroes who died in the war."},{"sentence":"Kasama ba sa **memorial** plan ang cremation?","translation":"Is cremation included in the **memorial** plan?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbuo ng isang balangkas o serye ng mga hakbang na gagawin upang makamit ang isang partikular na layunin.
original_explanation: The official sport of the barkada before any trip. To 'magplano' is to create a detailed itinerary for a vacation, a party, or even just a simple lunch out. It's that exciting phase of endless chats and Google Docs that may or may not actually happen. The opposite of this is 'drawing', which is when the plan never materializes.
usage_notes: A very common verb used in all contexts, from casual to formal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magplano** nang maaga para sa ating bakasyon sa Palawan.","translation":"We need **to plan** early for our vacation in Palawan."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **magplano** kapag hindi lahat ay sumasagot sa chat.","translation":"It's hard **to plan** when not everyone is replying to the chat."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit at bilog na prutas na sitrus, karaniwang berde na nagiging kahel kapag hinog, at may napakaasim na lasa. Kilala rin bilang kalamansi.
etymology: From Spanish 'limoncito,' meaning 'little lemon.' In the Philippines, this term is almost always used to refer to calamansi (Citrus × microcarpa).
original_explanation: This is the real MVP of Filipino kitchens. The 'sawsawan' superstar. Toyo? Needs limonsito. Pancit? Needs limonsito. Inihaw na baboy? Needs limonsito. It's the small but terrible fruit that can cure a sore throat or make your sinigang extra kickin'. Basically, it's calamansi, but with a Spanish-sounding name to make it sound a bit more... quaint.
usage_notes: While it literally means 'small lemon,' in the Philippines, 'limonsito' is a common synonym for 'kalamansi'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pigaan mo ng **limonsito** ang pansit para sumarap.","translation":"Squeeze some **calamansi** on the noodles to make it taste better."},{"sentence":"Gagawa ako ng toyo na may sili at **limonsito**.","translation":"I will make soy sauce with chili and **calamansi**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malalim at masusing pag-iisip sa isang bagay, ideya, o karanasan.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you're staring at your coffee on a rainy day, thinking about your life choices. It's the 'sana all' moment but for deep thoughts, not just relationships. The intellectual version of 'hugot'.
usage_notes: Often used in religious, spiritual, or academic contexts. It implies a deep, personal pondering.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Semana Santa ay panahon ng **pagninilay**.","translation":"Holy Week is a time for **reflection**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng oras para sa **pagninilay** tungkol sa aking kinabukasan.","translation":"I need time for **contemplation** about my future."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kagamitan, karaniwang yari sa lona na may dalawang poste sa magkabilang gilid, na ginagamit sa pagbuhat at paglipat ng maysakit o sugatang tao.
original_explanation: This is what you see in movies when someone dramatically gets injured and the paramedics rush in. It's that portable bed they use to carry people into an ambulance. Think of it as the Uber for people who can't walk to the hospital.
usage_notes: Isang partikular na terminong medikal o pang-emergency.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dinala ang pasyente sa ambulansya gamit ang **anggarilyas**.","translation":"The patient was brought to the ambulance on a **stretcher**."},{"sentence":"Nagmamadaling kinuha ng mga rescuer ang **anggarilyas** mula sa sasakyan.","translation":"The rescuers hurriedly got the **stretcher** from the vehicle."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kinikilala at binabati ngunit hindi itinuturing na isang malapit na kaibigan.
etymology: From 'bati' (to greet) with the circumfix 'ka- -an', here used to denote a person with whom one shares the action of greeting.
original_explanation: The human version of the 'Seen' feature on Messenger. You know them, you say 'hi' to them in the hallway or give them the classic Filipino eyebrow raise, but you don't know their Wi-Fi password. They're the people you're friends with on Facebook but would never actually message.
usage_notes: Refers to someone you are on greeting terms with, implying a level of familiarity less than a 'kaibigan' (friend) but more than a stranger.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ko siya kaibigan, **kabatian** ko lang sa opisina.","translation":"He's not my friend, just an **acquaintance** at the office."},{"sentence":"Marami siyang **kabatian** pero iilan lang ang tunay na kaibigan.","translation":"She has many **acquaintances** but only a few true friends."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na termino para sa isang babaeng tagahanga o "fangirl."
original_explanation: Combination ng "faney" at "girl". Ito yung ate, tita, o kaibigan mong todo-suporta sa K-drama oppa o P-pop idol niya. Siya yung may lightstick, naka-abang sa ticket selling, at alam lahat ng trivia tungkol sa bias niya. A proud **faneygirl**!
usage_notes: Mas tiyak kaysa sa "faney" at tumutukoy sa kasarian ng tagahanga.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bilang isang certified **faneygirl**, puno ang kwarto niya ng posters ng SB19.","translation":"As a certified **fangirl**, her room is full of SB19 posters."},{"sentence":"\"Okay lang maging **faneygirl** kahit may asawa't anak na!\"","translation":"\"It's okay to be a **fangirl** even if you're already married with kids!\""}]

meaning_filipino: Mga kagamitan, sangkap, o materyales na kinakailangan sa pagbuo o paglikha ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: Ito yung listahan ng bibilhin mo sa National Bookstore para sa school project ng anak mo (na ikaw din ang gagawa). O yung mga tela, sinulid, at butones para sa ipapatahi mong damit. Basically, the 'stuff' you need to make other 'stuff'.
usage_notes: Often used to refer to raw materials or components for a project.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili kami ng mga **panggawa** para sa aming proyekto sa sining.","translation":"We bought **materials** for our art project."},{"sentence":"Kumpleto na ba ang mga **panggawa** mo para sa cake?","translation":"Are your **ingredients** for the cake complete?"}]

translation: To be chosen, to be appointed
meaning_filipino: Ang mapili o matukoy para sa isang partikular na posisyon, tungkulin, o karangalan.
original_explanation: This is what you call getting picked for something important. Not just "eeny, meeny, miny, moe" picked, but chosen for a role. Like when you get appointed as the project lead, or when your crush finally chooses you (sana all). It's the verb in the first line of the Philippine National Anthem, "Bayang magiliw, perlas ng silanganan, alab ng puso, sa dibdib mo'y buhay. Lupang hinirang, duyan ka ng magiting..."
usage_notes: Has a formal and often official tone. Associated with positions of honor or responsibility. The past tense "hinirang" is very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **nahirang** na bagong pangulo ng aming samahan.","translation":"She was the one **chosen** as the new president of our organization."},{"sentence":"Isang malaking karangalan ang **mahirang** bilang kinatawan ng ating bansa.","translation":"It is a great honor to **be appointed** as the representative of our country."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng inumin na may alkohol, karaniwang ginawa mula sa proseso ng permentasyon ng mga prutas, butil, o asukal.
original_explanation: The official fuel for Friday nights, fiestas, and forgetting your ex. It's the reason for "shot puno!" and the source of your Sunday morning "hangover". Whether it's gin, beer, or a fancy wine, it's the social lubricant of the Philippines.
usage_notes: Isang pangkalahatang tawag para sa anumang inuming may alkohol.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bawal uminom ng **alak** ang mga menor de edad.","translation":"Minors are prohibited from drinking **liquor**."},{"sentence":"Nagdala siya ng isang bote ng **alak** para sa salu-salo.","translation":"He brought a bottle of **alcoholic beverage** for the party."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang senado o ang isa sa dalawang kapulungan ng lehislatura sa isang bikameral na sistema ng pamahalaan, karaniwang binubuo ng mas kaunting miyembro kaysa sa Mababang Kapulungan.
etymology: Isang calque o salin-hiram ng terminong Ingles na "Upper House." Binubuo ng `mataas` (high) + `na` (linker) + `kapulungan` (assembly, mula sa `pulong` o 'meeting').
original_explanation: This is the formal name for the Philippine Senate. Think of it as the "Titas and Titos" of Congress. They're fewer, often older, and their decisions have a huge impact on the country. It's where laws get a final look-over, and where some of the most intense political drama unfolds. It's the real-life House of Cards, Pinoy version.
usage_notes: Isang pormal na termino na ginagamit sa gobyerno, balita, at agham pampulitika. Madalas na ipinagpapalit sa "Senado."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinasa na ng **Mataas na Kapulungan** ang panukalang batas.","translation":"The **Upper House** has passed the bill."},{"sentence":"Ang mga senador ay miyembro ng **Mataas na Kapulungan** ng Kongreso.","translation":"The senators are members of the **Upper House** of Congress."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng kaukulang pansin, proteksyon, at pag-aalaga sa isang tao, bagay, o sitwasyon upang mapanatili itong ligtas, maayos, at buo.
original_explanation: What your mom tells you every time you leave the house: "Mag-ingat ka." This is the verb form. It's what you do with your sweldo (so it lasts till the next payday), your heart (para 'di masaktan), or that 'huling piraso ng lechon' sa handaan. Handle with care!
usage_notes: This is in the imperative or infinitive form. 'Ingatan mo' means 'Take care of it.' 'Pag-ingatan mo' is a slightly more formal or emphatic version, often used as a command or strong advice.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat mong **pag-ingatan** ang mga gamit na ipinahiram sa iyo.","translation":"You should **take care of** the things that were lent to you."},{"sentence":"**Pag-ingatan** mo ang iyong puso, iisa lang 'yan.","translation":"**Take care of** your heart, you only have one."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng pagiging may kakayahang gumawa ng himala o mga bagay na hindi maipaliwanag ng karaniwang pang-unawa.
original_explanation: This describes something so amazing it feels like a miracle. For example, yung sweldo mo na umabot pa hanggang sa susunod na sahod. That's mapaghimala! O kaya yung pag-abot mo sa office on time kahit 30 minutes ka lang natulog at dumaan ka pa ng EDSA on a Monday. Truly miraculous.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa paraang hyperbole upang ilarawan ang isang bagay na kamangha-mangha o hindi inaasahan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinasabing ang imahen ng santo ay **mapaghimala**.","translation":"It is said that the statue of the saint is **miraculous**."},{"sentence":"Ang paggaling niya sa malubhang sakit ay tunay na **mapaghimala**.","translation":"His recovery from a serious illness was truly **miraculous**."}]

translation: to hang oneself; to commit suicide by hanging
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkitil sa sariling buhay sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng lubid o anumang katulad nito na ipinupulupot sa leeg at itinatali sa isang mataas na bagay.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "ayoko na" move, but seriously, don't. It's when someone decides to end it all by hanging. If you're feeling this way, please reach out. This isn't the kind of "hanging out" anyone should do.
usage_notes: A very serious and sensitive word. Often used in news reports or dramatic contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa matinding depresyon, nagtangkang **magbigti** ang lalaki.","translation":"Due to severe depression, the man attempted to **hang himself**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magsalita ng ganyan, para ka nang magbibigti.","translation":"Don't talk like that, you sound like you're about to commit suicide by hanging."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tiyak na kilos ng paghiwa sa isang bagay upang makabuo ng maninipis na piraso o gayat.
etymology: From 'gayat' (slice) + '-in' suffix, creating a transitive verb.
original_explanation: The command form of 'gayat'. 'Hoy, bunso, gayatin mo na 'yung bawang at sibuyas!' (Hey, youngest, slice the garlic and onions now!). This is your official task when you're assigned kitchen duty. It's a specific instruction: not chopped (tadtad), not diced, but *sliced thinly*.
usage_notes: A transitive verb requiring a direct object. Specific to slicing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **gayatin** mo ang manok para sa chicken sandwich.","translation":"Please **slice** the chicken for the chicken sandwich."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **gayatin** nang pahilis ang carrots para magandang tingnan.","translation":"You need to **slice** the carrots diagonally so they look good."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang patag na ibabaw o sahig ng isang sasakyang-dagat tulad ng bapor o barko.
original_explanation: The 'floor' of a ship. It's where you go to do the classic Titanic "I'm flying, Jack!" pose, or where you go to get some fresh air when you're starting to feel seasick from the 2-Go ferry ride to Cebu.
usage_notes: Isang partikular na gamit ng 'palapag' sa kontekstong pandagat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkita-kita ang mga pasahero sa itaas na **palapag** ng bapor.","translation":"The passengers met on the upper **deck** of the ship."},{"sentence":"Nilinis ng mga tripulante ang **palapag** pagkatapos ng bagyo.","translation":"The crew cleaned the **deck** after the storm."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng kababaan ng loob at hindi nagmamataas sa kapwa.
original_explanation: The opposite of your tita who always brags about her kids' achievements abroad. This is the person who gets a promotion but still eats at the same karinderya with everyone. They're the ones whose 'blessed' caption is genuine, not just a humble brag.
usage_notes: A highly valued positive character trait in Filipino culture. It is formed from 'mapag-' (inclined to be) and 'pakumbaba' (the act of being humble).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit sikat na siya, nanatili siyang **mapagpakumbaba** sa kanyang mga tagahanga.","translation":"Even though she is famous, she remains **humble** to her fans."},{"sentence":"Ang tunay na karunungan ay laging may kasamang pusong **mapagpakumbaba**.","translation":"True wisdom always comes with a **humble** heart."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng hindi pagtulog sa gabi o pagiging gising nang lampas sa karaniwang oras ng pamamahinga.
original_explanation: That thing you do for work, for studies, or for a K-drama marathon. It's the official sport of BPO agents, college students during finals week, and anyone who just discovered a new series on Netflix. The next day, you'll be powered by coffee and regrets.
usage_notes: Refers to the act or state of being sleepless, often intentionally for a specific purpose.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang labis na **pagpupuyat** ay masama sa kalusugan.","translation":"Excessive **staying up late** is bad for one's health."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa **pagpupuyat** kagabi, halos nakatulog ako sa opisina.","translation":"Because of **staying up late** last night, I almost fell asleep at the office."}]

translation: Finger food; Appetizer (served with alcoholic drinks)
meaning_filipino: Pagkaing kinakain bilang pampagana o kasabay ng pag-inom ng alak.
etymology: From 'pulot' (to pick up with fingers) + '-an' (locus suffix). The food you pick at.
original_explanation: Ito yung life of the party, a.k.a. yung sisig, chicharon, o mani na kasama ng malamig na beer. Hindi kumpleto ang inuman session kung walang pulutan. It's the reason why your 'isang bote lang' turns into a whole-night affair.
usage_notes: Strictly used in the context of drinking sessions. Not to be confused with a regular appetizer ('pampagana') for a meal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-order tayo ng crispy pata para gawing **pulutan**.","translation":"Let's order crispy pata to have as our **finger food**."},{"sentence":"Naubos na ang **pulutan**, pero marami pa tayong beer.","translation":"The **pulutan** is all gone, but we still have a lot of beer."}]

meaning_filipino: Atasan o pilitin ang isang tao na magbigay ng sagot o mananagot para sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: When your friend is being evasive about who they're texting, you look them in the eye and say, "Hoy, **pasagutin** mo nga ako, sino 'yan?" This verb is about compelling a person to give an answer. It can be a simple question, or it can be about making someone take responsibility. "We need to **pasagutin** the person responsible for this mess." It has a stronger, more direct force than 'pasagot'.
usage_notes: The focus of this verb is the person who is being made to answer. It implies a degree of authority or insistence from the speaker.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan ng guro na **pasagutin** ang tahimik na estudyante.","translation":"The teacher tried **to make** the quiet student **answer**."},{"sentence":"Dapat nating **pasagutin** ang mga opisyal na sangkot sa korapsyon.","translation":"We must **hold accountable** the officials involved in corruption."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis na pagpikit at pagdilat ng mga mata.
original_explanation: That thing you do with your eyes thousands of times a day without thinking. Also, what you fail to do during a staring contest. "Huwag kang kumurap!" is the battle cry. Metaphorically, it means something happened so fast, "sa isang kurap lang," it was over.
usage_notes: Can also mean 'to flicker' when referring to a light source.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **kumurap** o matatalo ka sa titigan.","translation":"Don't **blink** or you'll lose the staring contest."},{"sentence":"Sa isang iglap, **kumurap** ang ilaw at biglang nawalan ng kuryente.","translation":"In an instant, the light **flickered** and the power went out."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng matinding kalungkutan, panghihina ng loob, o kawalan ng sigla; malungkot na malungkot.
etymology: Reduplication of 'lugo' (to be downcast, to suffer a loss).
original_explanation: This is the look of someone who just got 'seen-zoned' by their crush. It’s that droopy, mopey, 'walang gana kumain' vibe. Imagine a dog with its tail between its legs, or you after checking your bank account post-payday. It's sadness you can see in someone's posture.
usage_notes: Describes a visible state of sadness or dejection.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bakit ka **lulugu-lugo** diyan? May problema ba?","translation":"Why are you so **downcast**? Is there a problem?"},{"sentence":"**Lulugu-lugo** siyang umuwi matapos malamang hindi siya nakapasa sa exam.","translation":"He went home **crestfallen** after finding out he didn't pass the exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na isinama, isinapi, o naging bahagi ng isang mas malaking kabuuan, tulad ng isang korporasyon o organisasyon.
original_explanation: When your small startup finally gets its SEC registration, it's now 'ingkorporada'. It's the official term for "level up" in the business world. From a side hustle to a legit company with HR and mandatory fun-runs.
usage_notes: A formal, legal, or business term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aming kumpanya ay **ingkorporada** na at may legal na personalidad.","translation":"Our company is now **incorporated** and has a legal personality."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hakbang o paraan na maaaring gawin upang makakuha ng tulong, proteksyon, o solusyon sa isang mahirap na sitwasyon; pag-apela.
original_explanation: Your 'Plan B' or your 'Who you gonna call?' option. When your request gets denied, your next rekurso is to talk to the manager. When you lose a court case, your rekurso is to appeal to a higher court. It's the move you make when you refuse to take 'no' for an answer.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa legal o pormal na konteksto para mangahulugang apela o remedyo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang huling **rekurso** na lang nila ay ang pagdulog sa Korte Suprema.","translation":"Their only remaining **recourse** is to appeal to the Supreme Court."},{"sentence":"Wala na siyang ibang **rekurso** kundi ang humiram ng pera sa kanyang mga kaibigan.","translation":"He had no other **recourse** but to borrow money from his friends."}]

translation: to kick forcefully; to start (an engine); to throb
meaning_filipino: Ang marahas na pag-angat o pagtadyak ng paa; ang pagsisimula ng takbo ng makina; ang malakas na pagtibok o pag-igting.
original_explanation: Has multiple personalities. 1) The literal "donkey kick" you do when you're super annoyed. 2) The way you start an old-school motorcycle. 3) That "kick" you feel when the caffeine or alcohol hits your system. "Wow, sumikad na yung kape!" 4) How your heart feels when you see your crush—a strong, sudden throb.
usage_notes: Context is key for this word. It can mean a physical kick, the starting of a mechanism, or the sudden effect of a substance or emotion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumikad** ang kabayo kaya nahulog ang sakay nito.","translation":"The horse **kicked forcefully**, causing its rider to fall."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng ilang subok, **sumikad** din sa wakas ang makina ng motor.","translation":"After several tries, the motorcycle's engine finally **started**."},{"sentence":"Biglang **sumikad** ang kaba sa dibdib ko.","translation":"A feeling of nervousness suddenly **throbbed** in my chest."}]

translation: to live; to reside; to stay
meaning_filipino: Ang pananatili o paninirahan sa isang tiyak na lugar o tahanan.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "tirar" sa diwa ng "to tend towards" o "to be situated".
original_explanation: This is the "stay" version of 'tira'. When someone asks "Saan ka tumitira?" they're asking "Where do you live?". It's the root word for 'tirahan'. Not to be confused with hitting something or leftovers. This one is about having a home base for your Grab deliveries.
usage_notes: Ito ang salitang-ugat para sa 'tirahan' (tirahan) at 'tumira' (manirahan).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Saan ka **tumitira** ngayon?","translation":"Where are you **living** now?"},{"sentence":"Balak nilang **tumira** sa probinsya pagkatapos magretiro.","translation":"They plan **to live** in the province after retiring."}]

meaning_filipino: Mag-ayos o maghanda ng mga gamit na ilalagay sa loob ng maleta o iba pang uri ng sisidlan para sa isang paglalakbay.
original_explanation: The act of deciding which 5 outfits to bring for a weekend trip, but ending up packing 15 'just in case.' It's the pre-travel ritual filled with anxiety: 'May nakalimutan ba ako?' It's also a metaphor for emotional baggage. 'Bago ka pumasok sa bagong relasyon, dapat wala ka nang dala-dalang emotional baggage. So, **magbagahe** ka muna ng mga issues mo.'
usage_notes: Verb form of the noun "bagahe" (luggage). Often used interchangeably with "mag-empake".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maaga pa lang ay nagsimula na siyang **magbagahe** para sa kanyang flight bukas.","translation":"He started **to pack his luggage** early for his flight tomorrow."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pampahid sa tinapay na gawa sa langis ng halaman, na nagsisilbing pamalit sa mantikilya.
original_explanation: The OG palaman for pandesal before Nutella and cookie butter came along. Margarina is that yellow stuff in a tub (Dari Creme or Star Margarine, anyone?) that you slather on hot bread, sometimes with a sprinkle of sugar. It's the budget-friendly cousin of butter.
usage_notes: The brand names 'Star Margarine' or 'Dari Creme' are often used interchangeably with the generic term 'margarina'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-abot ng **margarina** at asukal para sa pandesal.","translation":"Please pass the **margarine** and sugar for the pandesal."},{"sentence":"Mas gusto niyang iprito ang itlog gamit ang **margarina** kaysa sa mantika.","translation":"She prefers to fry eggs using **margarine** instead of cooking oil."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng panloloko o pandaraya, lalo na sa usaping pampinansyal, kung saan ang isang tao ay nakakakuha ng pera o ari-arian mula sa iba sa pamamagitan ng panlilinlang.
original_explanation: This is the OG scam. Before phishing emails and text message spams, there was 'estapa'. It's when someone convinces you to "invest" in a "business" that doesn't exist. It's the reason why your Tita warns you about people who are 'masyadong mabait' and offer deals that are too good to be true. The crime is so common it has its own legal term in the Philippines: 'estafa'.
usage_notes: Often used in legal and news contexts. The person who commits estafa is an 'estapador'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsampa siya ng kasong **estapa** laban sa kanyang dating kasosyo sa negosyo.","translation":"She filed a case of **fraud** against her former business partner."}]

translation: to punch each other; to scuffle
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapalitan ng suntok o pisikal na sakitan sa pagitan ng dalawa o higit pang tao; magsuntukan.
original_explanation: Like a scene from an action movie, but it's just you and your sibling fighting over the last piece of chicharon. It's a mutual exchange of (usually not-so-playful) blows. Think less professional boxing, more chaotic family reunion.
usage_notes: Implies a mutual or reciprocal action of hitting or punching.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **magbuntalan** ang dalawang lalaki sa gitna ng kalsada dahil sa alitan sa trapiko.","translation":"The two men started to **scuffle** in the middle of the road because of a traffic dispute."},{"sentence":"Huwag kayong **magbuntalan** dito sa loob ng bahay, baka may mabasag kayo!","translation":"Don't **punch each other** here inside the house, you might break something!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng prutas na karaniwang hugis-kampanilya, may manamis-namis na lasa at malagranulang tekstura.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'peras' (pangmaramihan ng 'pera,' na nangangahulugang peras).
original_explanation: The fruit you always see in the fruit basket during Christmas, right next to the apples and grapes. It's not as popular as mango or banana for everyday eating, but it's a staple for Noche Buena and media noche celebrations. Eating a 'peras' feels a bit fancy, like you're in a hotel buffet. It's the fruit equivalent of wearing a nice shirt for a Zoom meeting—looks good, feels a bit formal.
usage_notes: Ang salitang Tagalog ay madalas na ginagamit para tumukoy sa isang peras o maramihang peras, dahil sa impluwensya ng pinagmulan nitong salitang Espanyol na pangmaramihan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bumili si nanay ng isang kilong **peras** sa supermarket.","translation":"Mom bought a kilo of **pears** at the supermarket."},{"sentence":"Ang **peras** ay masarap gawing juice o isama sa fruit salad.","translation":"A **pear** is delicious when made into juice or included in a fruit salad."}]

translation: to stay; to remain; to dwell
meaning_filipino: Ang pananatili sa isang lugar o kalagayan sa loob ng mahabang panahon.
original_explanation: This is more than just 'staying.' It's settling in. It's that feeling when you visit a province and you love it so much you decide to live there. It's also that friend who was supposed to visit for a weekend but is still on your couch two weeks later. 'Sana **mamalagi** ang pagmamahalan natin.' (Hope our love will last.) It has a sense of permanence.
usage_notes: Has a more permanent or long-term connotation than 'manatili' or 'tumira'. Often used in a more formal or poetic sense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais niyang **mamalagi** sa probinsya kung saan payapa ang buhay.","translation":"He wants to **dwell** in the province where life is peaceful."},{"sentence":"Hangad ko na **mamalagi** ang kapayapaan sa ating bansa.","translation":"I hope that peace will **remain** in our country."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paraan ng pagluluto ng karne sa pamamagitan ng pag-ihaw o paglalagay sa hurno.
original_explanation: The verb for when you're making lechon manok or liempo. It's the act of roasting something, usually meat, until it's cooked through and delicious. This is the action behind your favorite 'Andok's' or 'Baliwag' order.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'mag-ihaw,' but 'mag-asada' can also imply oven-roasting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Balak naming **mag-asada** ng manok para sa Noche Buena.","translation":"We plan **to roast** a chicken for Christmas Eve dinner."},{"sentence":"Sino ang taya sa **pag-asada** ng baboy sa handaan?","translation":"Who is in charge of **roasting** the pig at the feast?"}]

translation: to shake; to cause to tremble
meaning_filipino: Ang marahas na paggalaw o pag-uga sa isang bagay, lugar, o tao; lumikha ng pagyanig o lindol.
original_explanation: This is what happens when your crush finally notices you, and your whole world starts shaking. O 'pag nalaman mong may biglaang quiz. 'Nang yanigin ng balita ang buong office, lahat napatakbo sa pantry para mag-kape at mag-chismis.' It’s to be shaken, literally or figuratively.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of earthquakes ('Niyanig ng lindol...') or strong emotional impact.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kayang **yanigin** ng isang malakas na lindol ang buong gusali.","translation":"A strong earthquake can **shake** the entire building."},{"sentence":"**Yayanigin** ng kaniyang talumpati ang mga manonood.","translation":"His speech will **shake** the audience."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na pagdedeklara ng Simbahang Katoliko na ang isang yumaong tao ay isang santo. Sa pangkalahatang gamit, ito ay ang pagkilala sa isang bagay bilang opisyal o may awtoridad.
etymology: From Spanish `canonizar` (to canonize). The root is formed by dropping the '-r' and adding '-hin' to make it a verb.
original_explanation: The ultimate glow-up. It's when the Catholic Church officially declares someone a saint. "Balang araw, baka kanonisahin si San Pedro Calungsod." In modern slang, it's when a fandom decides a certain theory or character pairing is so good it *should* be official. "The fans are trying to kanonisahin their favorite ship."
usage_notes: Primarily used in a religious context, specifically Catholicism.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matagal ang proseso bago **kanonisahin** ng simbahan ang isang beato.","translation":"The process is long before the church **canonizes** a blessed person."},{"sentence":"Noong 2012, **kinanonisa** si San Pedro Calungsod.","translation":"In 2012, Saint Pedro Calungsod **was canonized**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na nangyayari, ginagawa, o binabayaran nang isang beses sa loob ng isang buwan.
original_explanation: Parang yung sahod mo, dumarating once a month (kung swerte ka at hindi twice a month). O yung bills ng Meralco at PLDT na siguradong darating, gusto mo man o hindi. Also, yung 'dalaw' na laging on time... or not.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong bayaran ang aking **menswal** na upa.","translation":"I need to pay my **monthly** rent."},{"sentence":"Mayroon kaming **menswal** na pagpupulong sa opisina.","translation":"We have a **monthly** meeting at the office."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang walang-tigil at madalas na walang-kabuluhang pagsasalita o pagdaldal.
etymology: From reduplication of the first syllable of the root `ka-` + `satsat`. This `ka-` + `reduplicated syllable` + `root` pattern denotes recent, continuous, or excessive action.
original_explanation: This is the sound of your Marites neighbor giving you the "latest chika." It's non-stop, often pointless, talking. Parang 'yung friend mong hindi nauubusan ng kwento, from their breakfast to their boss's new haircut. It's the verbal equivalent of spam messages. "Diyan ka naman magaling, sa kasasatsat!" is a classic mom-scolding line.
usage_notes: Often used with a slightly annoyed or negative tone. It's the noun form of the action. E.g., "Dahil sa kasasatsat mo..." (Because of your constant chattering...).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Walang natapos na trabaho dahil sa **kasasatsat** ninyo.","translation":"No work was finished because of your **constant chattering**."},{"sentence":"Napagalitan siya ng guro dahil sa **kasasatsat** sa klase.","translation":"He was scolded by the teacher because of his **incessant talk** in class."}]

translation: to feel nauseous; to be disgusted by
meaning_filipino: Makaranas ng alibadbad o pagkarimarim sa isang bagay, tao, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: Verb version of alibadbad. When you see your office mate na sipsip sa boss, 'Nako, inaalibadbaran ako sa pag-uugali niyan.' It's when something makes your stomach turn, either literally from bad food or figuratively from bad vibes.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin para sa pisikal na pagduduwal o sa metaporikal na pagkadiri o pagkasuklam.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Inaalibadbaran** ako sa amoy ng durian.","translation":"The smell of durian **makes me feel nauseous**."},{"sentence":"Talaga namang **maalibadbaran** ka sa sobrang kasinungalingan niya.","translation":"You will really **be disgusted** by his excessive lies."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maliit at malutong na biskwit na gawa sa galapong, asukal, at gata. Ito ay tuyo at parang pulbos kapag kinagat.
etymology: Mula sa Tagalog na 'puto' (steamed cake) at Espanyol na 'seco' (tuyo).
original_explanation: The 'dry puto.' These are small, white, powdery cookies that literally explode into dust in your mouth. They're super light, airy, and mildly sweet. Perfect for when you want a snack but also want to feel like you're eating a cloud of sugar and rice flour. Just don't inhale while taking a bite. Rookie mistake.
usage_notes: Ang pangalan ay literal na nangangahulugang 'tuyong puto'. Ang mga ito ay isang uri ng cookie o biskwit, hindi isang steamed cake. Madalas ibinebenta sa mga garapon bilang pasalubong. Ang baybay na 'putuseko' ay ginagamit din.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig kumain ng **puto seko** ang lola ko habang nagkakape.","translation":"My grandmother loves to eat **puto seko** while drinking coffee."},{"sentence":"Nag-uwi si tatay ng isang garapong **puto seko** bilang pasalubong.","translation":"Dad brought home a jar of **puto seko** as a souvenir gift."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng paputok na mabilis na tumataas sa himpapawid bago sumabog nang may kulay at ingay.
original_explanation: This is that New Year's Eve firecracker that goes "fweeeeeee" up into the sky before it goes "BOOM!". The 'skyrocket' type. It's the one your tito buys to show the neighbors who has the best fireworks display. The name itself sounds like the "whoosh" it makes.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to a skyrocket-type firework, not all fireworks in general (which is 'paputok').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakagandang pagmasdan ang mga **palusi** sa kalangitan tuwing Bagong Taon.","translation":"It's so beautiful to watch the **skyrockets** in the sky every New Year."},{"sentence":"Nag-ingat ang lahat sa pagsisindi ng **palusi** upang maiwasan ang disgrasya.","translation":"Everyone was careful in lighting the **skyrockets** to avoid accidents."}]

meaning_filipino: Dalhin ang isang tao o bagay sa pamamagitan ng paglalagay nito sa baywang o sa ilalim ng braso.
original_explanation: The verb form. 'Bes, kilikin mo muna 'tong bag ko, mag-reretouch lang ako.' (Friend, carry this bag for me, I'll just retouch my makeup.) It's the official request to turn your friend into a temporary coat rack or baggage counter.
usage_notes: The object-focus form of the verb 'kilik'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kilikin** mo muna ang iyong kapatid habang nagluluto ako.","translation":"**Carry** your sibling **on your hip** for a while as I cook."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko na kayang **kilikin** ang lahat ng problemang ito.","translation":"I can no longer **carry** all these problems."}]

meaning_filipino: Dinala o inilipat ang maraming bagay nang sabay-sabay o sunod-sunod.
original_explanation: This is what you do during a 'lipat-bahay' (moving house), carrying boxes back and forth. It's also what happens during a 12.12 sale when the delivery riders have to carry all your 'add to cart' items. 'Uy, **hinakot** mo lahat ng pagkain sa buffet ah!'
usage_notes: Implies carrying a large volume of items, often in multiple trips.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hinakot** ng mga bumbero ang mga gamit mula sa nasusunog na bahay.","translation":"The firefighters **carried out** the belongings from the burning house."},{"sentence":"Lahat ng paninda ay **hinakot** ng mga mamimili sa unang araw ng sale.","translation":"All the merchandise **was carried away** by shoppers on the first day of the sale."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing paksa ng laro o libangan ang isang bagay; manloko o paglaruan ang damdamin ng isang tao.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'ghosting' or 'breadcrumbing.' It's what you do to a video game, or unfortunately, what someone does to your heart. 'Huwag mo akong **laruin**' is the national anthem of the almost-but-not-quite relationship.
usage_notes: May dalawang pangunahing kahulugan: ang literal na paglalaro ng isang laro, at ang metaporikal na paglalaro sa damdamin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **laruin** muli ang Mobile Legends mamayang gabi.","translation":"I want **to play** Mobile Legends again later tonight."},{"sentence":"Nakiusap siya sa kasintahan, 'Pakiusap, huwag mong **laruin** ang puso ko.'","translation":"She pleaded with her lover, 'Please, don't **toy with** my heart.'"}]

meaning_filipino: Gamitin ang isang bagay bilang unan o patungan ng ulo sa pagtulog o paghiga.
original_explanation: That moment in a long bus ride when you're desperate for sleep and your backpack suddenly looks comfy. "Uunanin ko na lang 'tong bag ko." It's the verb form of making anything and everything your pillow—a lover's arm, a stack of books, your dog who didn't consent.
usage_notes: Ang 'unanin' ay ang anyong pautos/pawatas. 'Inunan' ang anyong pangnagdaan. 'Inuunan' ang pangkasalukuyan. 'Uunanin' ang panghinaharap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **unanin** ang mga bagong labang punda.","translation":"Don't **use** the newly washed pillowcases **as a pillow** yet."},{"sentence":"**Inunan** niya ang mga braso ko kagabi habang nanonood kami ng pelikula.","translation":"She **used my arm as a pillow** last night while we were watching a movie."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay ng katawan sa posisyong nakaupo na gagawin pa lamang sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: This is your game plan for the weekend after a hell week of work: 'Uupo lang ako sa sofa at manonood ng Netflix.' It's the future tense of chilling. It's the promise of rest. In a meeting, it's what you say when you're looking for a chair: 'Saan ako uupo?'
usage_notes: This is the actor-focused future tense. The subject is the person who will perform the action of sitting.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Saan ka **uupo** mamaya sa programa?","translation":"Where **will you sit** later at the program?"},{"sentence":"**Uupo** muna ako habang hinihintay kita.","translation":"I **will sit** for a while while waiting for you."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagpapakalat o nagpapalaganap ng impormasyon, balita, o minsan ay mga tsismis.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "tagapag-" (doer/agent of action) at sa salitang ugat na "kalat" (spread, mess).
original_explanation: The human version of a 'Share' button. This is your tita at the family reunion who knows everyone's business, or that officemate who delivers 'breaking news' faster than any news agency. The original social media algorithm.
usage_notes: Maaaring magkaroon ng negatibong konotasyon, lalo na kung ang ikinakalat ay tsismis ('tagapagkalat ng tsismis') o maling impormasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala diyan, kilala siyang **tagapagkalat** ng tsismis sa opisina.","translation":"Don't believe that, he's known as a **spreader** of gossip in the office."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang parirala na nagsasabing ang isang naunang sinabi o ginawa ay isang biro lamang at hindi dapat seryosohin.
etymology: Mula sa Ingles na "prank" at mga salitang Tagalog na "lang" (just/only) at "pala" (it turns out).
original_explanation: The ultimate "get out of jail free" card for when your joke lands badly. It's the verbal equivalent of hitting 'undo'. Also the most disappointing plot twist after you've already had a full-blown emotional reaction. "Nanalo ka sa lotto!"... "prank lang pala". The emotional whiplash is real.
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang parirala na ginagamit sa social media at ng mga nakababatang henerasyon, madalas pagkatapos ng isang praktikal na biro.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Akala ko totoo na, **prank lang pala**.","translation":"I thought it was real, but **it was just a prank**."},{"sentence":"Sinabi niyang aalis na siya, pero **prank lang pala**!","translation":"He said he was leaving, but **it was just a prank**!"}]

translation: to intensify (a color); to make more vivid
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapalala o pagpapalinaw sa kulay, anyo, o katangian ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: What you do with the saturation and contrast sliders on your photo editor to make your beach photos pop. 'Bes, **magpatingkad** ka ng lipstick, 'yung pang-rampa!'
usage_notes: While it primarily refers to color, it can be used metaphorically to mean 'to emphasize' or 'to make something stand out.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit siya ng ibang uri ng pintura upang **magpatingkad** sa kulay pula ng kanyang obra.","translation":"He used a different kind of paint to **intensify** the red color of his masterpiece."},{"sentence":"Ang pagdaragdag ng sili ay **nagpapatingkad** sa anghang ng Bicol Express.","translation":"Adding chili **intensifies** the spiciness of Bicol Express."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto o proseso ng pagbawi sa isang bagay na naisanla o pagpapalaya sa isang bihag sa pamamagitan ng bayad; ang pagliligtas mula sa kasalanan.
original_explanation: This is your glow-up after a major heartbreak or failure. It's paying off your credit card debt down to the last centavo. It's the hero's final act that makes up for all their past mistakes. It can be literal, like getting your 'nasangla' (pawned) alahas back, or spiritual, like finding salvation. It's the ultimate "Bawi-tayo" moment.
usage_notes: Has strong connotations in both finance (pawning, paying off a debt) and religion (redemption from sin).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkatubos** ng kanyang mga kasalanan ang kanyang tanging dalangin.","translation":"The **redemption** of his sins is his only prayer."},{"sentence":"Matagumpay ang negosasyon para sa **pagkatubos** sa mga bihag.","translation":"The negotiation for the **ransoming** of the hostages was successful."}]

meaning_filipino: Nakakaramdam ng bahagyang galit o pagkayamot dahil sa isang tao, bagay, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: That feeling when the Wi-Fi is so slow you can feel your patience thinning. Or when your officemate keeps clicking their pen. You're not angry, not yet. You're just... naiinis. It's the low-level boss fight before the final boss, which is 'galit na.'
usage_notes: Present tense. Describes an ongoing state of annoyance. It's milder than being angry (galit).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Naiinis** ako sa ingay ng mga kapitbahay.","translation":"I **am getting annoyed** by the noise from the neighbors."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo siyang kulitin, halatang **naiinis** na siya.","translation":"Don't keep bothering him, it's obvious he's already **irritated**."}]

translation: to be completely entangled; to be in a tangled mess
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging lubhang magkakabuhol-buhol at magulo ng maraming bagay na magkakasama.
etymology: From 'magka-' + reduplication of the first two syllables of the root 'salabid'.
original_explanation: This is 'magkasalabid' on steroids. It's not just your earphones; it's your earphones, your charger, your house keys, and three old receipts all forming a modern art installation in your bag. A total, chaotic mess. Imposibleng ayusin 'to, **magkasala-salabid** na ang mga alambre!
usage_notes: An intensive form of 'magkasalabid', emphasizing a higher degree of entanglement and chaos.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng bagyo, **nagkasala-salabid** ang mga poste ng kuryente at sanga ng puno.","translation":"After the storm, the electric posts and tree branches **were completely entangled**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong pagsamahin ang mga kuwintas at baka **magkasala-salabid** lang ang mga ito.","translation":"Don't put the necklaces together or they might just **get into a tangled mess**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na sanay at mahusay sa mga gawaing pisikal, lalo na sa mga isports o palakasan.
original_explanation: An "atleta" is someone who's physically fit and competes in sports, from the barangay basketball league star to an Olympian like Hidilyn Diaz. They're the ones who wake up at 4 AM to train while the rest of us are still scrolling through TikTok. In a family, the "atleta" is the one who eats the most during Noche Buena but somehow never gains weight.
usage_notes: The word is gender-neutral in Filipino usage, although its Spanish origin is masculine. It is used for both male and female athletes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang pambansang **atleta** ang kumatawan sa Pilipinas sa Olympics.","translation":"A national **athlete** represented the Philippines in the Olympics."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng disiplina upang maging isang mahusay na **atleta**.","translation":"Discipline is needed to become a great **athlete**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pag-uusap sa telepono. Sa konteksto ng trabaho, ito ay maaaring isang tawag mula sa isang customer o isang naka-iskedyul na pagpupulong sa telepono.
original_explanation: For BPO agents, this is their lifeblood—taking one **call** after another. 'Naka-long **call** ako, bes,' is the modern excuse for not replying. In corporate life, it's the 'Zoom **call**' that could have been an email.
usage_notes: Ginagamit halos eksklusibo para sa mga tawag sa telepono o internet. Ang katutubong salita sa Tagalog ay "tawag".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **call** ako mamayang 3 PM kasama ang kliyente.","translation":"I have a **call** later at 3 PM with the client."},{"sentence":"Grabe, sunod-sunod ang **call** sa pila kanina.","translation":"Wow, the **calls** in the queue were one after another earlier."}]

meaning_filipino: Umpisahan ang isang gawain, pangyayari, o proseso.
original_explanation: This is the "Go!" button of life. From starting a new series on Netflix to finally starting that diet you promised yourself you'd do last Monday. It's the opposite of "saka na" or "bukas na lang."
usage_notes: The base form of the verb, often used as a command or infinitive. The command form is 'Magsimula ka na!' (Start now!).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko nang **magsimula** ng bagong buhay sa probinsya.","translation":"I want to **start** a new life in the province."},{"sentence":"Paano ba **magsimula** ng isang maliit na negosyo?","translation":"How does one **begin** a small business?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng gatas ng baka na inalisan ng tubig at dinagdagan ng asukal, na nagreresulta sa isang malapot at matamis na produkto.
original_explanation: Ah, the nectar of the Filipino gods. Not to be confused with its angry cousin 'Letse!', letse-kondensada is pure, sweet, sticky joy in a can. It's the star of leche flan, the secret weapon in your Bicol express, and the heart of your halo-halo. It’s the reason why Filipino desserts can send you into a diabetic coma, and you'll be smiling the whole time.
usage_notes: Often shortened to 'kondensada'. A staple in Filipino pantries.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong palaman sa tinapay ang **letse-kondensada**.","translation":"My favorite bread filling is **condensed milk**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpalo o paghagupit nang malakas sa isang tao o hayop, karaniwan gamit ang latigo, sinturon, o anumang kahalintulad na bagay.
etymology: From a distinct root 'hambal' meaning 'to whip', not to be confused with 'hambal' meaning 'sorrow'.
original_explanation: This is an old-school word for a serious spanking or whipping. The kind of punishment lolo would tell stories about from his time. It's not just a simple palo; it implies a forceful, repeated striking. 'Hahambalin kita!' is a threat you don't want to hear from your nanay holding a belt.
usage_notes: An archaic word for corporal punishment. Not commonly used in modern speech but understood in certain literary or historical contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Noong unang panahon, kinatatakutan ng mga bata na sila ay **hambalin** ng kanilang mga magulang.","translation":"In the old days, children were afraid of being **whipped** by their parents."},{"sentence":"Binalaan niya ang magnanakaw na **hahambalin** niya ito kapag nahuli.","translation":"He warned the thief that he would **flog** him if caught."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging baluktot, liko, o hindi matuwid, kapwa sa pisikal na anyo at sa moral na pag-uugali.
original_explanation: This is the reason why you can't have nice things. It's the crooked logic used to justify corruption, the twisted reasoning behind a bad decision, or literally a road so poorly made it looks like a snake. It's the moral 'baluktot' (bent) state of a system or a person who chooses the wrong path even when the straight one is right there.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for physical crookedness but is more often used metaphorically for moral or ethical corruption.
