usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat labanan ang **kabaluktutan** sa gobyerno.","translation":"We must fight the **corruption** in government."},{"sentence":"Nakikita ang **kabaluktutan** ng daan mula sa itaas ng bundok.","translation":"The **crookedness** of the road is visible from the top of the mountain."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng sombrero na malapad ang paligid, karaniwang yari sa mga nilalang dahon tulad ng anahaw o nipa, na ginagamit bilang proteksyon sa araw at ulan.
original_explanation: This is the iconic farmer's hat you see in every Amorsolo painting. It's the ancestor of the modern baseball cap, but way more eco-friendly and with better ventilation. Perfect for shielding yourself from the tropical sun while looking authentically provincial.
usage_notes: Similar to a 'salakot', but 'salukot' can sometimes refer to a more conical or pointed variant. The terms are often used interchangeably.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang magsasaka ay nakasuot ng **salukot** habang nag-aararo sa bukid.","translation":"The farmer was wearing a **wide-brimmed hat** while plowing the field."},{"sentence":"Gawa sa dahon ng anahaw ang kanyang **salukot**.","translation":"His **hat** is made from anahaw leaves."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi kayang maunawaan o maarok ng isipan dahil sa sobrang lalim, lawak, o pagiging kumplikado.
etymology: Mula sa 'di' (not) + 'malirip' (can be fathomed or comprehended).
original_explanation: Trying to understand quantum physics, the sheer size of the universe, or why someone would put raisins in empanada. These are concepts that are di-malirip. It’s beyond 'di-maintindihan'; it’s so deep your brain can't even begin to process it. It's a mental 404 error.
usage_notes: Isang malalim at pampanitikang salita na ginagamit para sa mga malalalim na konsepto, misteryo, o damdamin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-ibig ng isang ina ay may lalim na **di-malirip**.","translation":"A mother's love has a depth that is **unfathomable**."},{"sentence":"Para sa akin, **di-malirip** ang dahilan ng kanyang biglaang pag-alis.","translation":"For me, the reason for his sudden departure is **incomprehensible**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang papel na ginagampanan ng isang aktor sa isang dula, pelikula, o anumang pagtatanghal.
original_explanation: Your 'role' in the drama of life. In showbiz, it's the character an actor plays. 'Galing ng **ganap** niya bilang kontrabida!' (Her performance as the villain was amazing!). In real life, it's the persona you put on, like your 'ganap' as the responsible eldest sibling or the 'kalog' one in the friend group.
usage_notes: Commonly used in the context of acting, theater, and by extension, social roles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napanalunan niya ang parangal para sa kanyang mahusay na **ganap** sa pelikula.","translation":"She won the award for her excellent **performance** in the movie."},{"sentence":"Ano ba ang **ganap** mo sa buhay, aber?","translation":"So what's your **role** in life, huh?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang artista na gumaganap sa pamamagitan ng mga kilos ng katawan at ekspresyon ng mukha nang walang salita; isang sining ng pag-arte na walang diyalogo.
original_explanation: 'Yung kaibigan mong nag-kkwento pero puro actions lang, walang sound. Parang 'yung mga nakikita mo sa park na nagpapanggap na nasa loob ng invisible box. They are masters of silent comedy and drama.
usage_notes: A rare word. The English loanword "mime" or the concept "pantomime" is more common in modern conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang mahusay na **mima** ang nagtanghal sa plasa.","translation":"A talented **mime** performed in the plaza."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging nasa tugatog ng tagumpay, kasikatan, o kapangyarihan; ang kilos ng pag-angat o paglipad nang mataas.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'payagpag' (to flap wings to fly high).
original_explanation: This is when you're not just winning, you're SLAYING. 'Yung K-Pop group na laging sold out ang concert, 'yung love team na lahat ng pelikula blockbuster, o 'yung business mo na sunod-sunod ang pag-open ng bagong branch. It's your "unbothered, moisturized, happy, in my lane, focused, flourishing" era.
usage_notes: Often used figuratively to mean success or dominance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuloy-tuloy ang **pamamayagpag** ng mga atletang Pilipino sa buong mundo.","translation":"The Filipino athletes continue to **reign supreme** around the world."},{"sentence":"Ang dekada '90 ang panahon ng **pamamayagpag** ng mga bandang alternative rock sa Pilipinas.","translation":"The 90s was the era of the **flourishing** of alternative rock bands in the Philippines."}]

translation: To cause to branch out; to ramify
meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha o pagpapalabas ng mga sanga mula sa isang pangunahing katawan o pinagmulan; ang paghati sa iba't ibang direksyon.
original_explanation: Think of it as making a single road split into two. Or when one piece of chismis leads to five other different chismis. 'Pagsangahin mo yung kwento' means to add more branches and details to a story, making it more complex.
usage_notes: A command form of the verb. Can be used literally for plants/roads or figuratively for stories/topics.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **pagsangahin** ang mga tubo ng tubig papunta sa bawat bahay.","translation":"The water pipes need **to be branched out** to each house."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang **pagsangahin** pa ang usapan, manatili tayo sa paksa.","translation":"Don't **cause the conversation to branch out** any further, let's stick to the topic."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o bagay na ginagamit bilang batayan, pinagkukunan ng impormasyon, o halimbawa para sa pagpapatunay o paglilinaw.
original_explanation: In a job hunt, this is your 'character witness' – that tita or former boss you pray will say good things about you. In a thesis, it's the list of books you 'read' to prove you didn't just make things up. "Sir, pwede ko po ba kayong gawing **reperensya** sa resume ko?"
usage_notes: Commonly used in academic ('citation'), professional ('character reference'), and general contexts ('point of reference').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakilagay ang lahat ng iyong **reperensya** sa dulo ng iyong sanaysay.","translation":"Please put all your **references** at the end of your essay."},{"sentence":"Naghahanap ako ng trabaho at kailangan ko ng personal na **reperensya**.","translation":"I am looking for a job and I need a personal **reference**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangatnig na pananhi na ginagamit upang ipaliwanag ang dahilan o sanhi ng isang pangyayari o kilos. Katumbas ng 'dahil'.
original_explanation: This is the formal, slightly old-school way of saying 'dahil'. Think of it as the 'whereas' or 'forasmuch as' to the simple 'because'. You'd use this when you're writing a thesis, or maybe when you're explaining to your lola why you're still single, para mas dramatic. "Sapagka't ang tunay na pag-ibig ay mahirap hanapin, Lola."
usage_notes: Mas pormal at madalas gamitin sa panitikan kaysa sa pang-araw-araw na usapan, kung saan mas karaniwan ang "dahil".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi siya nakarating **sapagka't** malakas ang ulan.","translation":"He could not come **because** the rain was heavy."},{"sentence":"Pinili niyang manatili sa bahay **sapagka't** pagod na siya.","translation":"She chose to stay home **because** she was already tired."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang partikular na anyo o bersyon ng isang inilathalang teksto, tulad ng libro, magasin, o pahayagan.
original_explanation: Parang 'version' ng isang bagay. May "First Edisyon" ang libro na sobrang mahal na ngayon. May "Limited Edisyon" na sapatos na pinag-aagawan. At siyempre, may "Special Edisyon" ng chismis galing sa kapitbahay na may kasama nang bagong detalye.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghahanap ako ng unang **edisyon** ng Noli Me Tángere.","translation":"I am looking for a first **edition** of Noli Me Tángere."},{"sentence":"Ang balita ay nasa pang-umagang **edisyon** ng pahayagan.","translation":"The news is in the morning **edition** of the newspaper."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sitwasyon, lalo na sa pampublikong sasakyan o isang lugar, kung saan wala nang maupuan at tanging espasyo para sa pagtayo na lamang ang magagamit.
etymology: From 'pan-' (for the purpose of) and the reduplicated 'tayu-tayo' (just standing), from the root word 'tayo' (to stand).
original_explanation: The classic MRT/LRT experience during rush hour. You're packed like sardines in a can, holding on for dear life. It's an extreme sport disguised as a daily commute. Also applies to sold-out concerts where you paid good money to not have a chair.
usage_notes: Often used to describe crowded public transport or venues.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil rush hour, **pantayu-tayo** na lang ang abot namin sa bus.","translation":"Because it was rush hour, we only got **standing room only** on the bus."},{"sentence":"Punuan na ang jeep, kaya **pantayu-tayo** ang drama ng mga huling sumakay.","translation":"The jeep was full, so it was a **standing room only** situation for the last passengers to get on."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagpapaikli ng pariralang "ang wika niya" o "sabi niya," na ginagamit upang iulat ang sinabi ng isang tao.
etymology: A contraction of the phrase "ang wika niya" (his/her language/saying).
original_explanation: The OG 'sabi niya'. It’s the formal, literary version of quoting someone. You'll see this in Noli Me Tángere or your lola's old komiks. In modern terms, it's like saying 'According to my source...' but the source is just one person. It's the #Marites classic, but with a diploma.
usage_notes: Primarily used in literature, formal writing, and reported speech. Less common in casual conversation where "sabi niya" is preferred.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maganda raw ang pelikula, **aniya**.","translation":"The movie is good, **he/she said**."},{"sentence":"**Aniya**, hindi na siya babalik pa.","translation":"**He/she said**, they will never come back."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan na ginagamit sa pagbubukas ng mga pagkaing de-lata.
original_explanation: 'Yung life-saver mo kapag puro de-latang sardinas, tuna, at corned beef na lang ang laman ng pantry mo bago ang sahod. Minsan, mas mahirap pa itong hanapin kaysa sa forever. Mula sa Espanyol na "abrelatas".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawawala na naman ang **abrilata**, paano natin bubuksan itong sardinas?","translation":"The **can opener** is missing again, how will we open this can of sardines?"},{"sentence":"Pakihanap ng **abrilata** sa kusina.","translation":"Please find the **can opener** in the kitchen."}]

translation: to use as a pattern; to model after
meaning_filipino: Gamitin bilang isang huwaran, modelo, o gabay sa paggawa ng isang bagay na katulad.
original_explanation: It's like when you see a really cool outfit on Pinterest and you show it to your mananahi, 'Gayahin mo 'to, 'day!' You're asking them to use the original as a template. Basically, to copy or model something. Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V in real life.
usage_notes: The spelling 'padrunin' is a common colloquial variant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **padronin** ang disenyo ng damit na nakita ko sa magasin.","translation":"I want **to model** it after the dress design I saw in the magazine."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **padronin** ang masamang ugali niya.","translation":"Do not **use** his bad behavior **as a model**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na pagsusuri ng isang kaso sa harap ng hukom upang matukoy ang katotohanan at maglapat ng katarungan.
original_explanation: This is the main event in a legal drama. It's the courtroom scene where lawyers object, witnesses testify, and the judge bangs the gavel. When you say 'nasa litis,' it means someone's fate is literally being decided. It's the climax of any 'demanda' story.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula na ang **litis** para sa kasong isinampa laban sa kanya.","translation":"The **trial** for the case filed against him has begun."},{"sentence":"Maraming tao ang dumalo sa **litis** upang marinig ang hatol.","translation":"Many people attended the **hearing** to hear the verdict."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-akyat at pagbaba; pagbabago-bago o hindi panatag na estado.
original_explanation: Parang presyo ng gas, o yung mood swings ng jowa mo. One minute okay, the next minute, ewan. Also, the ultimate leg day workout: squats.
usage_notes: Formed by combining 'taas' (up) and 'baba' (down). Often used to describe unstable movement or prices.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakahilo ang **taas-baba** ng sinasakyan naming barko.","translation":"The **up and down** movement of the ship we're on is nauseating."},{"sentence":"Laging **taas-baba** ang presyo ng dolyar.","translation":"The price of the dollar always **fluctuates**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa kalagayan ng kakulangan, kawalan, o pagiging dukha sa isang bagay, lalo na sa yaman o pangangailangan.
original_explanation: Ito yung state ng wallet mo bago sumahod. Parang love life mo, salat sa pagmamahal. It's when you're running on empty, whether it's cash, feelings, or your data plan.
usage_notes: Often used to describe poverty or a lack of resources. Can also be used figuratively for a lack of emotions or qualities.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming pamilya ang **salat** sa pagkain ngayong panahon ng krisis.","translation":"Many families are **lacking** food during this time of crisis."},{"sentence":"Kahit **salat** sa yaman, masaya pa rin ang kanilang pamilya.","translation":"Even if **poor** in wealth, their family is still happy."}]

translation: The act of brushing against; a passing thought
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng bahagyang pagdikit o pagtama sa isang bagay habang dumadaan; ang panandaliang paglitaw ng isang ideya o alaala sa isipan.
original_explanation: Ever been in a crowded MRT and someone just brushes past you? That's the physical 'pagsagi'. The more common use, though, is for thoughts. 'Pagsagi sa isip' is when an idea, a memory, or the face of your ex suddenly pops into your head while you're in the middle of a Zoom meeting. It's a mental photobomber.
usage_notes: Often used with 'sa isip' or 'sa isipan' to mean 'to cross one's mind'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman ko ang **pagsagi** ng isang tao sa aking likuran.","translation":"I felt someone **brush against** my back."},{"sentence":"Hindi maiwasan ang **pagsagi** sa isip ko ng aming mga masasayang alaala.","translation":"I can't stop the happy memories we had from **flashing through** my mind."}]

translation: to hold a class; to have class
meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa ng isang aralin o sesyon ng pag-aaral, o ang pagdalo dito.
etymology: From `mag-` (verb prefix) + `klase` (class), which is from Spanish `clase`.
original_explanation: Can mean two things: for teachers, it's the main event. For students, it's the thing you have to wake up for after a late-night Mobile Legends session. 'May prof ba? Magkaklase ba siya?' (Is the prof here? Is he/she going to hold class?) is the most important question of the morning.
usage_notes: This can be used from the perspective of the teacher (to conduct a class) or the student (to attend/have a class). Context determines the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi **nagklase** ang guro dahil may sakit siya.","translation":"The teacher did not **hold class** because she was sick."},{"sentence":"Maaga akong pumasok para **magklase**.","translation":"I went to school early **to have class**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang lugar kung saan idinaraos ang burol o paglalamay; maaaring isang punerarya, kapilya, o ang tahanan ng yumaong tao.
original_explanation: The "venue" for the wake. Pwedeng sa bahay, pwedeng sa isang dedicated na building. Dito nagaganap ang lahat: ang iyakan, ang tsismisan, ang kainan ng libreng kape, at siyempre, ang 24/7 na sugalan. Basically, the event space for the final farewell party.
usage_notes: Ang "-an" na hulapi ay nagpapahiwatig ng isang lugar kung saan nangyayari ang kilos ng salitang-ugat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatayo ang kabaong sa gitna ng **burulan**.","translation":"The coffin stood in the middle of the **wake venue**."},{"sentence":"Maraming bulaklak ang ipinadala sa **burulan**.","translation":"Many flowers were sent to the **funeral home**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng isang doktor o propesyonal sa kalusugan ng pormal na tagubilin para sa isang gamot o paggamot.
original_explanation: What a doctor does after listening to you describe your ubo and sipon for 5 minutes. They whip out a piece of paper with handwriting you can't read and magreseta something you can't pronounce. Also what your lola does, but instead of medicine, she'll magreseta Vicks VapoRub for literally any ailment.
usage_notes: Primarily used in a medical context. Can also be used figuratively to mean "to recommend a solution."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang doktor lang ang maaaring **magreseta** ng antibiotic.","translation":"Only a doctor can **prescribe** an antibiotic."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang basta-basta iinom ng gamot na hindi **nireseta** sa iyo.","translation":"Don't just take medicine that wasn't **prescribed** to you."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sukat ng haba mula sa dulo ng hinlalaki hanggang sa dulo ng hintuturo o kalingkingan kapag nakaunat ang mga daliri.
etymology: From ka- + dangkal. The prefix ka- can indicate a unit of measurement.
original_explanation: The OG unit of measurement before the metric system came to the Philippines. It's how your lola measures fabric at the palengke or how you'd check if a table can fit through a door. "Isang karangkal na lang, kasya na!" It's the ancestor of 'eyeballing it'.
usage_notes: An informal but widely understood unit of measurement for short distances, roughly the distance from the tip of the thumb to the tip of the little finger.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sukatin mo nga ng **karangkal** kung gaano kalapad ang libro.","translation":"Can you measure with a **handspan** how wide the book is?"},{"sentence":"Kulang pa ng isang **karangkal** ang haba ng tela.","translation":"The length of the fabric is still short by one **handspan**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-ako sa pagbabayad ng isang partikular na bagay, serbisyo, o utang.
original_explanation: This is the verb form that focuses on the *what* you're paying. While 'bayaran' focuses on *who* you pay ("Bayaran mo si Pedro"), '**bayarin**' focuses on the bill itself ("Bayarin mo ang utang mo kay Pedro"). It's the command you give yourself when you see that Lazada notification: "**Bayarin** mo na 'yan!"
usage_notes: The object of the verb is the thing being paid for (the bill, the debt, the item). Contrast with 'bayaran' (to pay someone).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino ang dapat **bayarin** ang mga pinamili natin?","translation":"Who should **pay for** our groceries?"},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **bayarin** ang matrikula mo bago ang deadline.","translation":"Don't forget to **pay for** your tuition before the deadline."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang impormal na pag-uusap o pagkukuwentuhan, karaniwan sa pagitan ng mga magkakaibigan o magkakakilala.
original_explanation: The official term for 'chismisan' but with less negative baggage. It's the long, winding conversation you have with your barkada over coffee or a beer. The agenda is... there is no agenda. Just pure, unadulterated kwentuhan about life, work, and that weird thing your officemate did.
usage_notes: 'Hunta' is the root, but 'huntahan' is more commonly used to refer to the activity itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napunta sa malalim na **huntahan** ang aming simpleng kamustahan.","translation":"Our simple greeting turned into a deep **chat session**."},{"sentence":"Ang paborito naming gawin ay magkaroon ng **huntahan** sa ilalim ng puno ng mangga.","translation":"Our favorite thing to do is have a **casual conversation** under the mango tree."}]

translation: is able to teach; is able to point
meaning_filipino: May kakayahang magbahagi ng kaalaman o kasanayan sa iba; o may kakayahang ipahiwatig ang isang direksyon o bagay.
etymology: From nakapag- (ability) + duplicated first syllable of root tu- + turo (teach/point). Present/imperfective 'can' form.
original_explanation: This word has two personalities, like a Grab driver who's also a life coach. First, it's about being able to teach (e.g., your lola who can teach you secret recipes). Second, it's about being able to point at something (e.g., Waze, which is able to point you to the nearest milk tea shop).
usage_notes: The meaning depends entirely on context: 'teach' for knowledge, 'point' for direction or location.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang karanasan, **nakapagtuturo** siya ng tamang diskarte sa negosyo.","translation":"Because of his experience, he is **able to teach** the right business strategies."},{"sentence":"Ang modernong teknolohiya ay **nakapagtuturo** ng eksaktong lokasyon ng isang lugar.","translation":"Modern technology is **able to point** to the exact location of a place."}]

translation: to be replaced; to be substituted
meaning_filipino: Ang mapalitan ng iba sa isang posisyon, gawain, o lugar.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `ma-` + salitang ugat na `halili` (substitute) + hulaping `-an`. Ang `-n-` ay isang epentetikong katinig.
original_explanation: The feeling when you're on a BPO shift and your reliever finally arrives. "Yes, I can finally go home!" It's being replaced, but in a good way (most of the time). It can also be the "hugot" version: being replaced in someone's heart. "Sana all, may kapalit. Ay, wait..."
usage_notes: Ang ibig sabihin ng pandiwa ay may ibang tao na kukuha ng iyong pwesto o tungkulin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko nang umuwi, sana ay may **mahalinhan** na sa akin sa pagbabantay.","translation":"I need to go home, I hope someone can **replace** me on duty."},{"sentence":"Nang magretiro ang dating manager, agad siyang **nahalinhan** ng kanyang assistant.","translation":"When the old manager retired, he was immediately **replaced** by his assistant."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-iwas o pagpipigil sa pagkain ng ilang uri ng pagkain o paggawa ng isang bagay, karaniwan dahil sa relihiyosong dahilan.
original_explanation: This is the religious version of "self-control." Think of it as your Lenten sacrifice—no meat on Fridays, no social media for 40 days. It's the original "detox," but for your soul. It's when your lola reminds you, "Hoy, Biyernes Santo ngayon, bawal ang karne!"
usage_notes: Often associated with religious practices, particularly during Lent in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang **pangingilin** ng pamilya nila tuwing Mahal na Araw.","translation":"Their family's **abstinence** is strict during Holy Week."},{"sentence":"Ang **pangingilin** sa masasamang bisyo ay isang malaking hamon.","translation":"**Abstaining** from bad vices is a big challenge."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-alis o pagpunta sa mas malayo; paglikha ng distansya sa pagitan ng sarili at ng isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: The 'ghosting' starter pack. It's the slow fade. Fewer texts, more 'seen' messages. It can be physical, like moving to another city for work, or emotional, like what you do when you realize your 'friend' is actually toxic. The opposite of 'paglapit'.
usage_notes: Can be physical, emotional, or social distancing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging sanhi ng kanilang **paglayo** sa isa't isa ang isang hindi pagkakaunawaan.","translation":"A misunderstanding caused them **to drift apart** from each other."},{"sentence":"Ang **paglayo** niya sa siyudad ay para makahanap ng kapayapaan.","translation":"His **moving away** from the city was to find peace."}]

meaning_filipino: Himukin o hikayatin ang isang tao na maniwala o gumawa ng isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng argumento o ebidensya.
original_explanation: Ito yung ginagawa mo para makuha ang gusto mo. 'Ma, payagan mo na 'ko, please!' habang nagpapa-cute. O yung effort mong kombensihin ang tropa na sa Samgyup kumain kahit gusto nila sa Jollibee. It's the art of persuasion, a skill needed for sales, debates, and getting your parents' permission.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'kumbinsihin'. The object of the verb is the person being convinced.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **kombensihin** ang kanyang mga magulang na payagan siyang sumama sa biyahe.","translation":"She tried **to convince** her parents to let her join the trip."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **kombensihin** ang isang taong sarado na ang isip.","translation":"It's hard **to convince** a person who is already close-minded."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian na naglalarawan sa isang bagay na walang-wala pang gamit, sariwa, o kararating o kagagawa pa lamang.
etymology: Reduplication of the root word 'bago' (new), with the linker '-ng'. This form intensifies the meaning.
original_explanation: That feeling when you peel the plastic off a new phone? That's bagung-bago. The smell of a new car or a fresh pair of shoes. It's so new, it still has the 'amoy-tindahan' (store smell). It's the superlative form of 'bago'—not just new, but *brand-spanking* new.
usage_notes: Used to emphasize the newness of an object.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagmamalaki niya ang kanyang **bagung-bagong** sapatos.","translation":"He is showing off his **brand new** shoes."},{"sentence":"Amoy pintura pa ang bahay dahil **bagung-bago** pa ito.","translation":"The house still smells of paint because it's **brand new**."}]

meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng pagkakaiba; magbago mula sa dating kalagayan, anyo, o katangian.
original_explanation: You and your barkada all agreed to wear black, but you show up in neon pink. You just had to **maiba**. It's the urge to be unique, to stand out, or simply to change. Can be a good thing (innovation) or a bad thing (KJ, KillJoy). 'Para **maiba** naman' is the official slogan of someone tired of the same old routine.
usage_notes: Can mean 'to be different' or 'to become different/change'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto niyang **maiba** sa lahat kaya pininturahan niya ng kulay ube ang buhok niya.","translation":"She wanted to **be different** from everyone so she dyed her hair purple."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi **maiiba** ang pagtingin ko sa'yo.","translation":"Don't worry, my feelings for you won't **change**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang impormal na termino para sa isang tao na lihim na hinahangaan o mayroong romantikong pagtingin; katumbas ng salitang Ingles na 'crush'.
etymology: From the English word 'crush', re-interpreted through the Tagalog word 'durog' (crushed), likely as a playful calque or pun.
original_explanation: This is the slang version of 'crush'. 'Sino durog mo sa kabilang section?' (Who's your crush in the other section?). It's that person who makes your heart go from 'buo' to 'durog' (in a good way, hopefully). It's a playful, slightly more 'kalye' (street) way to talk about your secret love.
usage_notes: This is a modern slang usage, popular among younger generations. It's a pun on the English 'crush' and the Tagalog 'durog' (crushed).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **durog** ng bayan sa campus namin.","translation":"He is the campus heartthrob (lit. the **crush** of the town) at our campus."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maingay, baka marinig ng **durog** ko!","translation":"Be quiet, my **crush** might hear you!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagbubudbod ng asin sa pagkain o anumang bagay.
original_explanation: The solution to every matabang (bland) dish. What your tita tells you to do when the sinigang isn't quite right. "Anak, mag-asin ka pa, kulang sa lasa." It's the most basic kitchen command.
usage_notes: Can also mean to preserve something in salt.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang masyadong **mag-asin** sa ulam, masama sa kalusugan.","translation":"Don't **add too much salt** to the dish, it's bad for your health."},{"sentence":"Tinuruan niya ako kung paano **mag-asin** ng isda para gawing tuyo.","translation":"He/She taught me how to **salt** fish to make dried fish."}]

translation: to be able to endure; to be able to tolerate
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang batahin ang hirap, sakit, o anumang hindi kaaya-ayang sitwasyon nang hindi sumusuko o nagrereklamo.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `makapag-` (kakayahan) at salitang-ugat na `tiis`.
original_explanation: This is the skill you learn when you're stuck in EDSA traffic for 3 hours. Or when your internet is buffering during the series finale. Or when you're on a diet and everyone around you is eating lechon. 'Makapagtiis' is the Filipino art of patience and endurance. It’s practically a national sport.
usage_notes: Madalas itong iniuugnay sa pagharap sa kahirapan, pagsubok, at pagpapakita ng katatagan ng loob.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **makapagtiis** sa hirap ngayon para sa magandang kinabukasan.","translation":"You need **to be able to endure** hardship now for a good future."},{"sentence":"Hindi na siya **makapagtiis** sa sakit ng ngipin kaya pumunta na siya sa dentista.","translation":"He could no longer **tolerate** the toothache so he went to the dentist."}]

meaning_filipino: Itrato o kilalanin ang isang tao o bagay sa isang partikular na paraan; magpalagay.
original_explanation: This is the verb for when you're in that awkward 'Ano ba talaga tayo?' stage. 'He treats me like a sister,' is the classic friendzone line. Or, 'Parang kapatid na ang turing ko sa'yo.' It's how you define a relationship, officially or unofficially. It's all about perception and labels.
usage_notes: Often used with 'bilang' (as) or 'na parang' (as if). The forms 'turingin' (to treat someone as) and 'pagturing' (the act of treating) are very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat kang **magturing** sa lahat ng tao nang may respeto.","translation":"You should **treat** all people with respect."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **magturing** na kaibigan sa isang taong hindi tapat.","translation":"It's hard **to consider** someone a friend who is not sincere."}]

translation: manager; administrator; one who is in charge
meaning_filipino: Isang tao na may tungkuling mangasiwa, magpatakbo, o mag-alaga ng isang negosyo, ari-arian, o gawain.
original_explanation: 'Yung taong laging may 'urgent' at 'paki-rush' sa email. Sila 'yung nag-a-approve ng leave mo, pero sila rin 'yung nagtatanong bakit ang dami mong leave. The mamamahala is the one who holds the power (and the deadlines).
usage_notes: The agent form of the verb 'mamahala'. The prefix 'mamaN-' indicates a profession or habitual role.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kausapin mo ang **mamamahala** ng gusali para sa iyong mga hinaing.","translation":"Talk to the building **administrator** regarding your complaints."},{"sentence":"Bilang **mamamahala**, responsibilidad niyang tiyakin ang kapakanan ng kanyang mga empleyado.","translation":"As a **manager**, it is his responsibility to ensure the welfare of his employees."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng laging maayos at maganda ang pananamit; mahilig magpaganda.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "postura" na nangangahulugang 'tindig' o 'ayos'.
original_explanation: The OG 'OOTD Queen'. Siya yung friend mong laging naka-full makeup at perfect ang outfit kahit sa palengke lang bibili ng toyo. She's always serving looks, ready for the 'gram. Hindi pwedeng hindi 'slay'.
usage_notes: The feminine form of `pusturyoso`. Often used to describe someone who pays great attention to their appearance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging **pusturyosa** si Maria, kahit sa bahay lang ay nakaayos.","translation":"Maria is always **well-dressed**, even when she's just at home."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa opisina bilang ang pinaka-**pusturyosa** sa lahat.","translation":"She is known in the office as the most **stylish** of all."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain, tungkulin, o posisyon ng isang patnugot; ang proseso ng paghahanda, pagwawasto, at pagsasaayos ng isang sulatin, pelikula, o anumang materyal para sa publikasyon o pagpapalabas.
original_explanation: This is the art of being a "grammar police" professionally. Ito 'yung trabaho ng editor-in-chief sa isang magazine, 'yung nag-a-approve ng articles sa school paper, o 'yung director na sumisigaw ng "Cut!" sa movie set. Sila ang may final say, ang huling titingin kung 'pasa' o 'palpak' ang isang gawa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa ilalim ng kanyang **pamamatnugot**, umani ng maraming parangal ang pahayagan.","translation":"Under his **editorship**, the newspaper reaped many awards."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang masusing **pamamatnugot** upang matiyak ang kalidad ng aklat.","translation":"Thorough **editing** is important to ensure the quality of the book."}]

meaning_filipino: Luhuran ang isang tao o bagay bilang tanda ng matinding paggalang, pagsamba, o pagsusumamo.
etymology: Nagmula sa salitang 'panikluhod' at hulaping '-an', na ginagawa itong isang pandiwa na tumutukoy sa lugar o tao kung kanino isinasagawa ang kilos.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of the dramatic kneeling. It's what you *do* to someone or something. You don't just kneel, you kneel *to* them. "Gusto ko siyang panikluhuran para lang patawarin niya ako." It's the ultimate "I'm sorry" or "Please" move. In historical dramas, people do this to the king. In modern life, you might do this to your partner after you forgot your anniversary.
usage_notes: Isang napormal at matinding salita na nagpapahiwatig ng malalim na pagpapasakop o paggalang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Handa niyang **panikluhuran** ang kanyang mga magulang para sa kanilang kapatawaran.","translation":"He is ready to **kneel before** his parents for their forgiveness."},{"sentence":"Pinanikluhuran ng mga alagad ang kanilang pinuno.","translation":"The followers **knelt before** their leader."}]

meaning_filipino: Pandayin o pag-ipunan ng maraming tao o insekto; dumugin.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na parang langgam na dinudumog ang asukal. Parang 'yung mga tao sa Divisoria 'pag 13th month pay na, 'yun 'yung kulumusin. O kaya 'yung mga chismosa sa kanto pag may bagong issue, nagkukulumpon sila.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a large crowd or insects gathering around something.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong iwanan ang matamis na pagkain sa mesa dahil **kulumusin** 'yan ng mga langgam.","translation":"Don't leave the sweet food on the table because it will be **swarmed** by ants."},{"sentence":"Kinulumos ng mga mamamahayag ang sikat na artista paglabas niya ng korte.","translation":"The famous artist was mobbed by the press when he came out of the court."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking apoy o sunog; matinding init na dala ng apoy o ng sikat ng araw.
original_explanation: This isn't just 'apoy'. This is the kind of fire that makes headlines. A massive, raging inferno. Also used for the intense, nakakalusaw-ng-makeup heat of the Philippine sun at 12 noon. Yung tipong paglabas mo, feeling mo nasa oven ka. That's dalahit.
usage_notes: Isang malakas at deskriptibong salita para sa apoy o init. Mas pampanitikan kaysa sa "sunog" o "init".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinupok ng **dalahit** ang buong gusali sa loob lamang ng isang oras.","translation":"The **blaze** consumed the entire building in just one hour."},{"sentence":"Hindi matagalan ng mga magsasaka ang **dalahit** ng araw sa bukid.","translation":"The farmers could not endure the **intense heat** of the sun in the fields."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan ng kilos o direksyon patungo sa mas mataas na lugar o posisyon.
original_explanation: This describes your journey on the MRT during rush hour, the price of gasoline, and your career path (hopefully!). It's the direction of every hike to a scenic viewpoint. "Uy, **paakyat** 'yung daan, kaya mo pa?" (Hey, the road is **going up**, can you still make it?). It can also describe something on an upward trend, like your data usage near the end of the month.
usage_notes: Can function as an adverb modifying a verb (e.g., `tumatakbo paakyat`) or as an adjective describing a noun (e.g., `daang paakyat`).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagod na ako sa paglalakad nang **paakyat** sa bundok.","translation":"I'm tired from walking **upward** on the mountain."},{"sentence":"Ang presyo ng bilihin ay laging **paakyat**.","translation":"The price of goods is always **going up**."}]

translation: to insist, to force, to compel
meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng lakas, kapangyarihan, o matinding pangungumbinsi upang makuha ang isang bagay o mapasunod ang isang tao laban sa kalooban nito.
original_explanation: What your tita does when she wants you to sing at the family reunion. "Sige na, isang kanta lang!" It's that "no means yes" energy, whether it's about eating more rice or joining them for another round of drinks.
usage_notes: Completed aspect (past tense). Present: `pumipilit`, Future: `pipilit`. Can have a negative connotation of coercion or a more neutral one of strong persuasion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kahit ayaw ko, **pumilit** pa rin siyang isama ako sa party.","translation":"Even though I didn't want to, she **insisted** on taking me to the party."},{"sentence":"**Pumilit** siyang tapusin ang proyekto kahit hatinggabi na.","translation":"He **forced** himself to finish the project even though it was midnight."}]

meaning_filipino: Hugasan nang mabilisan o bahagya gamit ang tubig upang alisin ang dumi o sabon; banlawan.
original_explanation: This is the final step in your 'labada' journey, the moment you wash away the soap (and your sins). It's also what you do to the dishes before the final 'punas' stage. If your relationship feels 'malabo', maybe it just needs a good 'anlawan' to see things clearly.
usage_notes: Synonymous with "banlawan," which is more commonly used in many regions. "Anlawan" can sometimes imply a quicker, less thorough rinse.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **anlawan** nang mabuti ang mga damit para hindi mangamoy-kulob.","translation":"Don't forget to **rinse** the clothes well so they don't get a musty smell."},{"sentence":"Pakidalian mo at **anlawan** mo na lang 'yang mga plato.","translation":"Please hurry up and just **rinse** those plates."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay na ginagamit na pain o panudyo upang makahuli ng isda o hayop; pagkain para sa mga alagang hayop.
original_explanation: This is the stuff you use to lure something in. It could be the actual worms you put on a hook to catch fish, or the pellets you give your chickens. Metaphorically, it's the "free webinar" that's really just a sales pitch, or the "sample" that gets you hooked on a product. It's the bait, and you, my friend, are the fish.
usage_notes: Pronunciation is key to distinguish this from the verb. For the noun, the stress is on the first syllable (PA-kain). For the verb, it's on the second (pa-KA-in).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating bumili ng **pakain** para sa mga manok.","translation":"We need to buy **feed** for the chickens."},{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang hipon bilang **pakain** sa pamingwit.","translation":"He used shrimp as **bait** for the fishing rod."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang duda; sigurado; kumpirmado at hindi magbabago.
original_explanation: This is your friend's answer when you ask "Tuloy ba tayo?" and they reply, "Tiyak!" It's the opposite of "drawing" or "asa pa". In a world of uncertainty, 'tiyak' is that 100% confirmed plan, that feeling when you know you aced an exam, or the certainty that traffic will be bad at 5 PM on a Friday.
usage_notes: Can function as an adjective (e.g., 'isang tiyak na bagay' - a sure thing) or an adverb (e.g., 'Tiyak na darating siya' - He will surely come).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tiyak** ang pag-unlad kung lahat ay magtutulungan.","translation":"Progress is **certain** if everyone works together."},{"sentence":"**Tiyak** na mananalo ang paborito kong koponan.","translation":"My favorite team will **surely** win."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi makayanan o matiis dahil sa tindi ng sakit, hirap, o sama ng loob.
original_explanation: The feeling of being in a crowded MRT train at 7 AM on a Monday with no aircon. The heat, the smell, the crushing weight of humanity... it's all di-mabata. Also, your sibling's singing in the shower.
usage_notes: Can describe physical pain, emotional suffering, or an annoying situation. The root 'bata' here means 'to endure', not 'child'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Di-mabata** ang sakit ng kanyang ngipin kaya nagpatingin na siya sa dentista.","translation":"The pain in his tooth was **unbearable**, so he went to see a dentist."},{"sentence":"Para sa akin, **di-mabata** ang kanyang kayabangan.","translation":"For me, his arrogance is **unbearable**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kondisyon ng pananakit o discomfort sa tiyan, karaniwang pagkatapos kumain, na sanhi ng hirap sa pagtunaw ng pagkain.
original_explanation: Ito yung feeling mo pagkatapos mong ubusin yung pang-isang linggong supply ng pagkain sa isang upuan lang sa fiesta. Parang may nag-aaway na Jollibee at McDo sa tiyan mo. The official term for 'empacho'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang kumain nang masyadong mabilis para iwasan ang **indihestyon**.","translation":"Don't eat too quickly to avoid **indigestion**."},{"sentence":"Inatake ako ng **indihestyon** dahil sa dami ng nakain kong lechon.","translation":"I got an attack of **indigestion** because of the amount of roasted pig I ate."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtawa nang mahina at pigil, na may kasamang tila nanginginig na tunog mula sa lalamunan.
original_explanation: The sound you make when you see a funny meme in a quiet office and you're trying not to get caught. It's a suppressed laugh, like you're a kettle that's about to whistle. The classic 'tita' giggle.
usage_notes: Onomatopoeic. Describes a suppressed, high-pitched laugh, often from amusement or mischief.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi niya napigilang **umalik-ik** habang nanonood ng comedy film.","translation":"She couldn't help but **giggle** while watching the comedy film."},{"sentence":"Narinig ko siyang **umalik-ik** sa kabilang kwarto, tiyak na may ka-chat na naman.","translation":"I heard her **chuckle** in the other room, she's surely chatting with someone again."}]

meaning_filipino: Mga bala, bomba, at iba pang kagamitang pumuputok na ginagamit sa mga baril at artilerya.
original_explanation: Not just bullets! This is the general term for anything that goes "bang" in a weapon. You hear this a lot in action movies or news reports about military operations. It's also used metaphorically, like when a debater is "running out of munisyon" (arguments).
usage_notes: 'Munisyon' is the singular/collective form. 'Munisyones' is the plural form, though 'munisyon' is often used for both in casual speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naubusan ng **munisyon** ang mga sundalo sa gitna ng labanan.","translation":"The soldiers ran out of **ammunition** in the middle of the battle."},{"sentence":"Dapat itago sa ligtas na lugar ang mga baril at **munisyon**.","translation":"Guns and **ammunition** must be stored in a safe place."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mapili sa isang posisyon o tungkulin sa pamamagitan ng pagboto o halalan.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `ma-` (potensyal na pandiwa) + `halal` (to elect).
original_explanation: The feeling of winning in the elections, whether for class president or for a national position. It's the moment your campaign jingle and free t-shirts pay off. The opposite is "natalo" or "'di-pinalad."
usage_notes: Halos eksklusibong ginagamit sa konteksto ng pulitika at eleksyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino kaya ang **mahalal** na susunod na pangulo?","translation":"Who do you think will **be elected** as the next president?"},{"sentence":"Umaasa siyang **mahalal** bilang senador sa darating na eleksyon.","translation":"He is hoping to **be elected** as a senator in the upcoming election."}]

translation: feeling nauseous, wanting to vomit; feeling disgusted
meaning_filipino: Nakakaramdam ng duduwalin o kagustuhang isuka ang laman ng sikmura; pagkaramdam ng matinding pandidiri o pagkayamot.
original_explanation: Two flavors: 1) The physical feeling after eating 'isaw' from the wrong vendor or riding the spiral slide at the perya. Your stomach is doing the cha-cha. 2) The emotional feeling when you see your ex's cheesy new couple photos. It's the ultimate 'eww' or 'kadiri' reaction, making you want to figuratively (or literally) puke.
usage_notes: Has both a literal, physical meaning (nauseous) and a figurative, emotional one (disgusted). Context is key. Not to be confused with its root 'suka' (vinegar), which is a noun with a different stress pattern /SU-ka/.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Buntis yata si Ana kasi palagi siyang **nasusuka** tuwing umaga.","translation":"Ana might be pregnant because she always **feels nauseous** every morning."},{"sentence":"**Nasusuka** ako sa pag-uugali niyang mapagkunwari.","translation":"I'm **disgusted** by his hypocritical behavior."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na buhaghag, hindi siksik, o madaling madurog.
original_explanation: Like soil that's perfect for planting, or a cookie that crumbles the moment you look at it. It's the opposite of that 'siksik' feeling in the MRT. It's also how your hair feels after a day at the beach without conditioner.
usage_notes: Often used to describe soil, sand, or dry, brittle things.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kalagkag** ang lupa kaya madaling magtanim dito.","translation":"The soil is **loose**, so it's easy to plant here."},{"sentence":"Naging **kalagkag** ang tinapay dahil naiwan sa labas.","translation":"The bread became **brittle** because it was left outside."}]

translation: to ignite; to cause to burst into flame
meaning_filipino: Pagsindihan o palakihin ang apoy hanggang sa ito ay magliyab nang malaki; pasiklabin.
original_explanation: This is what you tell your friend to do with their passion, their dreams... or literally, the charcoal for the barbecue. It's about taking a small spark and turning it into a full-blown inferno. Can be used for feelings, too, like 'Huwag mo nang pagningasin ang galit niya,' meaning don't add fuel to the fire.
usage_notes: Can be used both literally for fire and figuratively for emotions, passions, or conflicts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumuha siya ng gasolina upang **pagningasin** ang sinindihang siga.","translation":"He got some gasoline **to ignite** the bonfire he had lit."},{"sentence":"Huwag nating hayaang mamatay ang alab ng ating pagiging makabayan; sa halip ay **pagningasin** pa natin ito.","translation":"Let's not let the flame of our patriotism die; instead, let's **cause it to burst into flame** even more."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na namamagitan o nangangasiwa sa isang talakayan, debate, o online forum upang matiyak na ito ay maayos at sumusunod sa mga alituntunin.
original_explanation: The "taga-awat" of the internet. Sila 'yung nagde-delete ng mga offensive comments sa Facebook group at nag-a-approve ng membership mo. Sa totoong buhay, sila 'yung host ng debate na laging nagsasabi ng "Time's up!" bago pa man magkasuntukan ang mga kandidato. The unsung hero of civil discussions.
usage_notes: A direct loanword used in contexts of meetings, debates, and online communities.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **moderator** ng debate ay nanatiling kalmado sa gitna ng mainit na usapan.","translation":"The **moderator** of the debate remained calm amidst the heated discussion."},{"sentence":"Naging **moderator** ako sa isang online forum.","translation":"I became a **moderator** for an online forum."}]

translation: to have a tooth knocked out
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkawala o pagkatanggal ng isa o higit pang ngipin, kadalasan dahil sa aksidente o malakas na tama.
etymology: From ma- (accidental verb prefix) + bungi (gap-toothed, missing a tooth) + -an (locative/referential suffix).
original_explanation: Ito 'yung resulta kapag sumabak ka sa suntukan at natalo ka. O 'yung aksidenteng nadulas ka at tumama 'yung bibig mo sa sahig. Pag-gising mo, may bintana na sa ngiti mo. "Hala, na-mabungian si kuya!"
usage_notes: Specifically refers to losing a tooth/teeth, usually due to impact or accident, resulting in a gap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natakot siyang baka siya ay **mabungian** sa laban ng boksing.","translation":"He was afraid he might **have a tooth knocked out** in the boxing match."},{"sentence":"Ingat sa pagkain ng matitigas na kendi, baka ka **mabungian**.","translation":"Be careful eating hard candy, you might **lose a tooth**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkahulog o paglubog sa isang malambot na bagay o ibabaw, tulad ng putik o kumunoy.
original_explanation: Imagine mo 'yung paa mo nung umulan tapos dumaan ka sa damuhan, tapos biglang 'squish!'—lumubog. 'Yan ang pagka-bulsot. Parang puso mo lang nung nalaman mong 'di ka niya pala type, biglang lumubog.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a person or object sinking or getting stuck in mud, soft soil, or a similar yielding surface.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bulsot** ang gulong ng traktora sa maputik na bukid.","translation":"The tractor's wheel is **sunken** in the muddy field."},{"sentence":"Nag-ingat siyang maglakad para hindi **mabulsot** sa putikan.","translation":"He walked carefully so he wouldn't **fall into** the mud."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-ikot o paggalaw sa pamamagitan ng pag-ikot sa sarili nitong aksis, tulad ng isang bola o gulong.
original_explanation: Ever dropped a 20-peso coin in a jeepney? The frantic search that follows is because of **paggulong**. It's the motion of anything round—a basketball, a log, or yourself in bed when you can't find a comfy spot. It's physics in action, often leading to 'Saan na napunta 'yun?!'
usage_notes: Can refer to an object rolling or a person rolling over. It can also be used figuratively to mean the 'unfolding' or progression of events.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinanood ng bata ang **paggulong** ng bola pababa ng burol.","translation":"The child watched the **rolling** of the ball down the hill."},{"sentence":"Ang mabilis na **paggulong** ng mga pangyayari ay ikinagulat ng lahat.","translation":"The fast **unfolding** (lit. rolling) of events surprised everyone."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapahiwatig ng malaking antas, sukat, o epekto sa isang kilos o kalagayan.
original_explanation: This is how much your electricity bill went up during summer. It's how much you've changed (for better or worse) since high school. 'Nagbago ka na... *nang malaki*.' It's the go-to phrase to quantify something in a big, non-specific way.
usage_notes: A very common and versatile phrase to indicate a significant degree or amount.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatulong **nang malaki** ang donasyon mo sa mga biktima ng baha.","translation":"Your donation helped the flood victims **greatly**."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng malakas na puwersa, kapangyarihan, o diin; maaaring tumukoy sa pagiging sapilitan.
etymology: From ma- (adjective prefix) + puwersa (force), from Spanish 'fuerza'.
original_explanation: Describes something with a lot of 'oomph' or force. It can be a good thing, like a 'mapuwersa na suntok' ni Pacquiao, or a bad thing, like a 'mapuwersa na paghingi ng ambag' ng officemate mo para sa birthday ng boss. It has that 'no choice ka' energy.
usage_notes: Can have a negative connotation of being forced or coerced.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamitan niya ng **mapuwersa** na argumento ang kanyang kalaban sa debate.","translation":"He used a **powerful** argument against his opponent in the debate."},{"sentence":"Naging **mapuwersa** ang pagkuha sa kanya ng mga awtoridad.","translation":"His arrest by the authorities was **forceful**."}]

translation: to burst into flames, to flare up
meaning_filipino: Biglang pag-apoy o pagliliyab nang malaki at malakas.
original_explanation: When a small spark becomes a huge fire, literally or figuratively. It's what happens to a 'chismis' in the office—starts with a whisper, then by lunchtime, the whole department is on fire. Also, that moment when a calm argument suddenly escalates into a full-blown 'World War III' at home. That's 'sumilab'.
usage_notes: Used for both literal fires and figurative flare-ups of emotion or conflict.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Biglang **sumilab** ang tuyong damuhan dahil sa init ng araw.","translation":"The dry grass suddenly **burst into flames** because of the sun's heat."},{"sentence":"**Sumilab** ang galit niya nang marinig ang kasinungalingan.","translation":"His anger **flared up** when he heard the lie."}]

translation: to have pity on, to show mercy to
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita o pagbibigay ng awa o habag sa isang tao.
original_explanation: It's the verb form of mercy. When you're begging your prof to accept your late submission, you're hoping na 'kahabagan' ka niya. It's asking for grace, for someone to cut you some slack. 'Lord, kahabagan mo po ako sa traffic sa EDSA.'
usage_notes: Often used in a formal, prayerful, or pleading tone. The root verb is 'habagin'. 'Kahabagan' is in the potential/abilitative aspect.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay **kahabagan** tayo ng panahon at hindi umulan sa araw ng ating kasal.","translation":"Hopefully the weather **will have mercy on** us and it won't rain on our wedding day."},{"sentence":"**Kahabagan** mo ang mga taong nagugutom at walang tirahan.","translation":"**Have pity on** the people who are hungry and homeless."}]

translation: retreat; the act of moving back
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-urong, pagbalik sa pinanggalingan, o pag-iwas sa isang sitwasyon.
etymology: From Spanish "atrás" (back, behind). The prefix `pag-` nominalizes the action.
original_explanation: That moment you see your ex with their new partner at the mall and you do a 180-degree turn. That's "pag-atras." It's backing out of a deal, a fight, or a really awkward conversation. In traffic, it's what you wish the car in front of you would do.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for physical movement or figuratively for backing down from a decision or commitment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pag-atras** ng mga sundalo ay isang estratehikong hakbang.","translation":"The soldiers' **retreat** was a strategic move."},{"sentence":"Walang **pag-atras** sa mga pangakong binitawan mo.","translation":"There's no **backing out** of the promises you made."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinuno o punong-bayan ng isang munisipalidad o lungsod.
etymology: Isang tambalang salita mula sa "ulo" (head) at "bayan" (town).
original_explanation: This is the OG 'boss' of the town, the one you see on tarps during fiestas and elections. Think of them as the CEO of your city, responsible for everything from traffic to basketball courts. It's a bit of an old-school term; you'd more likely hear 'mayor' today.
usage_notes: Isang pormal at medyo lumang termino para sa 'mayor'. Mas karaniwang ginagamit ang salitang hiram na 'mayor' o ang katumbas nitong 'punong-bayan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **ulung-bayan** ang nanguna sa pagdiriwang ng pista.","translation":"The **mayor** led the town fiesta celebration."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang paggawa ng isang bagay upang magdulot ng pagkayamot o bahagyang galit sa ibang tao.
original_explanation: The national sport of siblings. It's what your little brother does when he keeps poking you, or what your officemate does when they keep humming off-key. It's the act of deliberately pushing someone's buttons. "Huwag mo akong inisin, mainit ang ulo ko ngayon."
usage_notes: The infinitive form of the verb. Other forms include `iniinis` (annoying), `in-inis` (annoyed someone).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **inisin** ang kanyang nakababatang kapatid.","translation":"He likes **to annoy** his younger sibling."},{"sentence":"Pakiusap, tigilan mo na ang pag-iingay, huwag mo akong **inisin**.","translation":"Please, stop making noise, don't **irritate** me."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang gawain o trabaho ay ang magplantsa ng mga damit.
original_explanation: The official unsung hero of your OOTD. Sila yung dahilan kung bakit hindi mukhang kumot na ginamit ng sampung taon yung bagong laba mong damit. Your personal wrinkle-remover.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko nang kumuha ng **tagaplantsa** dahil tambak na ang mga lukot na damit ko.","translation":"I need to hire an **ironer** because my wrinkled clothes are piling up."},{"sentence":"Ang nanay ko ang aming **tagaplantsa** tuwing Linggo.","translation":"My mom is our designated **ironer** every Sunday."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng impeksyon sa bituka na nagdudulot ng matinding pagtatae na may kasamang dugo o mucus.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung sakit na ayaw mong makuha 'pag nag-food trip ka sa kung saan-saan. Basically, your stomach declares war on you. Ito 'yung dahilan kung bakit laging sinasabi ni nanay na 'uminom ka lang ng bottled water!'
usage_notes: A medical term. The more common phrase is 'pagtatae na may dugo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakuha niya ang **disenteria** mula sa maruming tubig na nainom niya.","translation":"He got **dysentery** from the dirty water he drank."},{"sentence":"Ang **disenteria** ay isang seryosong sakit na nangangailangan ng agarang atensyong medikal.","translation":"**Dysentery** is a serious illness that requires immediate medical attention."}]

translation: to stain; to tarnish; to make dirty
meaning_filipino: Gawing marumi o lagyan ng dungis ang isang bagay; siraan ang pangalan o reputasyon ng isang tao.
original_explanation: Literally, it's making something dirty, like getting mud on your new white shoes. Figuratively, it's what chismis does to someone's reputation. It's staining a good name, bes. To make something dirty, either physically or metaphorically.
usage_notes: Can be used both literally for physical dirt and figuratively for reputation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **padungisin** ng putik ang iyong bagong sapatos.","translation":"Don't let your new shoes **be stained** with mud."},{"sentence":"Ang layunin ng tsismis ay **padungisin** ang kanyang malinis na pangalan.","translation":"The goal of the gossip is **to tarnish** her good name."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglubog o paglalagay ng isang bagay sa likido sa loob ng mahabang panahon.
original_explanation: What you do to your clothes with tough stains, or what you do to chicken in a mix of soy sauce, vinegar, and garlic before it becomes adobo. Figuratively, it's you doing a Netflix marathon—**pagbabad** sa harap ng TV—until your eyes hurt.
usage_notes: Used for cooking (marinating), laundry (soaking), or figuratively for immersing oneself in an activity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sikreto sa masarap na manok ay ang matagal na **pagbabad**.","translation":"The secret to delicious chicken is the long **marination**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng damit ng **pagbabad** para matanggal ang mantsa.","translation":"The clothes need **soaking** to remove the stain."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang tao na mayroong maraming pangarap, mithiin, o ambisyon sa buhay.
original_explanation: This is you at the start of the year, listing down New Year's resolutions like 'mag-gym,' 'mag-ipon,' and 'travel more.' It describes someone who's always looking to the future with big plans. The opposite of 'bahala na si Batman.' This person has a vision board, for sure.
usage_notes: Generally a positive trait, describing someone with aspirations. Can sometimes be used to mean "daydreamer" if the person doesn't act on their dreams.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **mapangarap** na bata si Jose, nais niyang maging doktor balang araw.","translation":"Jose is a child **full of dreams**; he wants to be a doctor someday."},{"sentence":"Kahit sa gitna ng kahirapan, nanatili siyang **mapangarap**.","translation":"Even in the midst of poverty, she remained **ambitious**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang magalang na salita na ginagamit sa paghiling ng pabor o tulong.
etymology: From paki- (polite request prefix) + suyo (to ask for a favor, to court).
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'paki-' word. It's the polite, almost formal way of asking for a favor, a level up from the basic 'paki'. When someone starts their sentence with 'Pakisuyo...', you know they're about to ask for something important, and they're being super respectful about it. It's the 'I would be ever so grateful if you could...' of Tagalog requests.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'paki-', but can sound slightly more formal or earnest. It can also stand alone as 'Please do this favor for me.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pakisuyo** naman, pakiabot mo ang baso.","translation":"**As a favor**, please pass the glass."},{"sentence":"May **pakisuyo** sana ako sa iyo.","translation":"I'd like to **ask a favor** of you."}]

translation: let me touch; allow to be touched
meaning_filipino: Isang pakiusap na pahintulutan kang hipuin o damhin ang isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng kamay.
original_explanation: When you buy a new gadget and your friend asks, "Wow, bago! Pasalat naman!" It's the Pinoy way of saying "Let me feel the glorious newness of your item." Also what you say to someone checking if you have a fever: "Eto, pasalat ng noo ko."
usage_notes: Often used as a one-word request: "Pasalat!"
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng tela, **pasalat** nga.","translation":"The fabric is beautiful, **let me touch** it."},{"sentence":"Ayaw niyang **pasalat** ang bago niyang cellphone.","translation":"He doesn't want his new cellphone **to be touched**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pagprito ng itlog kung saan ang pula (yolk) ay nananatiling buo, malambot, at nakalabas sa ibabaw, na parang sumisikat na araw.
original_explanation: The official breakfast of champions (or ng mga puyat sa BPO). Ito yung itlog na hindi binaligtad, so the yolk is still runny and perfect for dipping your pandesal or mixing with sinangag. Kapag sinabi mong "itlog" sa karinderya, 90% chance **sunnysideup** ang darating.
usage_notes: A direct loanword. Often spelled as "sunny side up". Used as both a noun (e.g., "Gusto ko ng sunnysideup") and an adjective (e.g., "itlog na sunnysideup").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong almusal ang tapsilog na may **sunnysideup**.","translation":"My favorite breakfast is tapsilog with a **sunny-side up** egg."},{"sentence":"Lutuin mo ang itlog na **sunnysideup**, huwag mong baligtarin.","translation":"Cook the egg **sunny-side up**, don't flip it over."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi o punto kung saan nagtatagpo ang dalawa o higit pang linya, gilid, o ibabaw.
original_explanation: Yung spot sa kanto ng kalye kung saan nag-aabang ng jeep ang mga BPO employee. O 'yung paboritong pwesto mo sa kwarto kapag gusto mong mag-emote at mag-isip-isip. "Meet me at the panulok near the 7-Eleven."
usage_notes: Often refers to a street corner or an inside corner of a room.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghihintay si Maria sa **panulok** ng kalsada.","translation":"Maria is waiting at the street **corner**."},{"sentence":"Ilagay mo ang mesa sa **panulok** ng silid.","translation":"Place the table in the **corner** of the room."}]

translation: act of pouring liquid from one container to another; decanting
meaning_filipino: Ang maingat na pagsasalin ng likido mula sa isang sisidlan patungo sa iba, karaniwang ginagawa upang ihiwalay ang latak.
etymology: From `pag-` (verbal noun prefix) + reduplication of the first syllable of the root `ti-` + `tigis` (to pour carefully).
original_explanation: This is the art of transferring 'tuba' or homemade vinegar without disturbing the gunk at the bottom. It's a slow, careful pour. Think of a bartender delicately pouring a layered drink. 'Kailangan ng pasensya sa **pagtitigis** ng lambanog.'
usage_notes: Implies a careful, steady pouring to decant a liquid, separating it from sediment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa pamamagitan ng dahan-dahang **pagtitigis**, naiwan ang mga dumi sa ilalim ng banga.","translation":"Through the slow **act of pouring**, the sediments were left at the bottom of the jar."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagtitigis** ng alak ay isang sining.","translation":"The **decanting** of wine is an art."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-atras, pagbalik, o pag-alis mula sa isang posisyon, plano, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na aamin ka na sana sa crush mo, tapos bigla siyang may sinamang iba. Ayun, urong ka bigla. O 'yung pag-order mo sa mamahaling coffee shop, tapos nakita mo 'yung presyo. Urong! It's that sudden 'nope, never mind' moment.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical movement or a change of mind/decision.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang maling hakbang lang, baka kailanganin nating mag-**urong**.","translation":"Just one wrong step, and we might need to make a **retreat**."},{"sentence":"Walang **urong** sa laban na ito.","translation":"There's no **withdrawal** in this fight."}]

meaning_filipino: Maliban sa; bukod sa.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'except for...' word. 'Okay lang ako, puwera na lang kung aalis ka.' (I'm okay, except if you leave). It's the disclaimer, the fine print in your feelings, the one condition that changes everything. It's the 'but wait, there's more' of exclusions.
usage_notes: Used to introduce an exception to a statement. Not to be confused with the interjection 'Puwera!'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lahat sila ay pumasa, **puwera** kay Juan.","translation":"They all passed, **except** for Juan."},{"sentence":"Wala akong ibang gusto **puwera** sa kapayapaan.","translation":"I want nothing else **besides** peace."}]

meaning_filipino: May kakayahang magdulot ng kamatayan; mapanganib sa buhay.
original_explanation: The ultimate warning label. That snake in the grass? **Nakamamatay**. That unli-rice promo combined with your high blood pressure? **Nakamamatay**. Also used for extreme exaggeration, like a "nakamamatay na tingin" (a death glare) from your boss, or "nakamamatay sa ganda" (drop-dead gorgeous).
usage_notes: Used literally for things that can cause death (poison, disease, accidents) and figuratively to describe something of extreme intensity (beauty, anger, cuteness).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kagat ng ilang uri ng ahas ay **nakamamatay**.","translation":"The bite of some types of snakes is **deadly**."},{"sentence":"Binigyan niya ako ng **nakamamatay** na tingin.","translation":"She gave me a **fatal** glare."}]

meaning_filipino: Itaas at itupi ang laylayan ng manggas ng damit o ng pantalon, karaniwan bilang paghahanda sa paggawa o pagbaha.
etymology: From the root word 'alilis' which means to roll up.
original_explanation: The official signal that things are about to get serious. Whether you're about to wash a mountain of dishes, join a street basketball game, or wade through a flooded Manila street, the first step is always to 'mag-alilis'. It's the 'let's do this' gesture.
usage_notes: Specific to rolling up sleeves or pant legs.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nag-alilis** siya ng manggas at sinimulan nang maghugas ng mga plato.","translation":"He **rolled up** his sleeves and started washing the dishes."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **mag-alilis** ng pantalon dahil mataas ang baha.","translation":"You need **to roll up** your pants because the flood is high."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtama o pagbangga sa isang tao o bagay, karaniwan ay hindi sinasadya ngunit may puwersa.
original_explanation: 'Yung moment na naglalakad ka sa mall habang nagce-cellphone tapos may nabangga ka. 'Yun ang pagbundol. Hindi kasing-lala ng "bangga" (crash), pero sapat na para masabi mong, "Ay, sorry po!"
usage_notes: Implies a less severe impact than 'pagbangga' (crash). Often used for person-to-person or person-to-object collisions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natisod siya dahil sa biglaang **pagbundol** ng isang lalaki sa kanyang likuran.","translation":"She stumbled due to the sudden **bumping** of a man from behind her."},{"sentence":"Iwasan ang **pagbundol** sa mga gamit na nakakalat sa sahig.","translation":"Avoid **bumping into** the things scattered on the floor."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang taong tuso, mapanlamang sa kapwa, at may kakayahang gumamit ng katusuhan upang makuha ang gusto.
etymology: From `ma-` (adjective-forming prefix) + `gulang` (age, maturity). The meaning evolved from 'mature/experienced' to 'wily/cunning'.
original_explanation: This isn't your mom or dad. This is that vendor in Greenhills who can sell you a 'genuine' LV bag for 500 pesos. It's your officemate who always manages to avoid work but gets the credit. It’s being street-smart but on the dark side. Think 'diskarte', but with a hint of scam.
usage_notes: Has a strong negative connotation. Not to be confused with the noun `magulang` (parent). Pronunciation is key: /ma-GU-lang/ for 'cunning', /ma-gu-LANG/ for 'parent'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa taong iyan, kilala siyang **magulang** sa negosyo.","translation":"Be careful with that person, he is known to be **cunning** in business."},{"sentence":"Ginamitan niya ako ng **magulang** na pamamaraan para makuha ang pera ko.","translation":"He used a **sly** method on me to get my money."}]

meaning_filipino: Ilagay o ipatong ang isang tao o bagay sa kandungan.
original_explanation: This is peak "lolo/lola's favorite apo" action. Or what your cat does to you when you're trying to work from home. It's an act of affection, comfort, or sometimes, just a practical way to fit more people in a tricycle. "Tara, ikandong na lang kita, para kasya."
usage_notes: Used for people (especially children) or objects.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig niyang **ikandong** ang kanyang pusa habang nanonood ng TV.","translation":"She likes to **place her cat on her lap** while watching TV."},{"sentence":"**Inikandong** ng ina ang kanyang umiiyak na anak.","translation":"The mother **placed her crying child on her lap**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pananatili sa isang lugar o kalagayan hanggang sa dumating ang isang tao, bagay, o pangyayari na inaasahan.
original_explanation: The national pastime of the Philippines. From waiting for your Shopee delivery, to waiting for your friend who's "on the way" (pero nasa bahay pa), to waiting for them to love you back (ouch). Maghihintay ka. 'Yan ang sport ng mga Pinoy.
usage_notes: This is the future tense of 'maghintay' (to wait).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Maghihintay** ako sa'yo sa labas ng sinehan.","translation":"I **will wait** for you outside the movie theater."},{"sentence":"Kahit gaano katagal, sinabi niyang **maghihintay** siya.","translation":"No matter how long it takes, he said he **will wait**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglilipat ng salita o datos mula sa isang anyo patungo sa iba, lalo na ang paglilipat ng sinasalitang wika sa nakasulat o nakalimbag na anyo.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "transcripción" at Ingles na "transcription".
original_explanation: This is what happens when your BPO friend listens to an angry customer call and has to type out every single word, including the curses. It's also what you do when your prof talks too fast and you try to write down everything for your notes. Basically, turning audio into text.
usage_notes: Ang "transcript" ay mas karaniwang ginagamit para sa opisyal na dokumento tulad ng "transcript of records" mula sa isang paaralan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng korte ng opisyal na **transkripsiyon** ng pagdinig.","translation":"The court needs an official **transcription** of the hearing."},{"sentence":"Mahirap ang trabahong medical **transkripsiyon** dahil sa mga teknikal na termino.","translation":"Medical **transcription** work is difficult because of the technical terms."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pahabang gulay na may luntiang balat at maputing laman, karaniwang kinakain nang hilaw sa mga ensalada o bilang pampapresko.
original_explanation: The chillest vegetable. It's 90% water, just like your tear ducts during a sad K-drama. Perfect for salads, atsara, or for putting over your eyes to reduce puffiness after an all-night BPO shift.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghiwa siya ng manipis na **pipino** para sa kanyang sandwich.","translation":"She sliced thin **cucumbers** for her sandwich."},{"sentence":"Malamig at masarap ang **pipino** juice sa tag-init.","translation":"**Cucumber** juice is cold and delicious during the summer."}]

translation: penmanship; typography; manner of being written
meaning_filipino: Ang paraan ng pagsulat o pag-imprenta ng mga letra; ang estilo ng pagkakasulat.
original_explanation: This is all about the font, but in real life. It's your handwriting ('ganda ng pagkakatitik mo, pang-doktor!'), the way a document is typed, or the specific lettering on a signage. In the digital age, it's your choice between Arial and Comic Sans. It describes how the letters are physically formed.
usage_notes: Refers to the style, quality, or manner of writing or typing letters.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Madaling basahin ang libro dahil malinaw ang **pagkakatitik** nito.","translation":"The book is easy to read because its **typography** is clear."},{"sentence":"Hinangaan ko ang **pagkakatitik** ng luma niyang liham, para itong kaligrapya.","translation":"I admired the **penmanship** of his old letter, it was like calligraphy."}]

translation: place to go for help, resort
meaning_filipino: Isang lugar, tao, o tanggapan na nilalapitan para sa tulong, payo, o saklolo.
original_explanation: Your 'in case of emergency, break glass' person or place. It's the friend you call at 3 AM for hugot sessions, the government office you run to for 'ayuda', or that one 'kakilala' who knows a guy who knows a guy. It's your last resort, your lifeline.
usage_notes: Refers to a person, place, or institution one can turn to for assistance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang barangay hall ang naging **dulugan** ng mga nasalanta ng baha.","translation":"The barangay hall became the **place to go for help** for the flood victims."},{"sentence":"Siya ang aking laging **dulugan** kapag may problema ako sa pera.","translation":"He is always my **resort** whenever I have money problems."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangatnig na ginagamit bilang katumbas ng salitang 'noong' upang tukuyin ang oras o panahon na naganap ang isang kilos.
original_explanation: This 'nang' is your time-traveling buddy. It means 'when' in the past tense, like 'noong'. 'Natutulog ako *nang* dumating ka.' (I was sleeping *when* you arrived). It sets the scene, like a flashback in a movie. It's the 'nang' that points to a specific moment in time.
usage_notes: This usage is synonymous with 'noong'. For example, 'Nang dumating siya' is the same as 'Noong dumating siya' (When he/she arrived).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa eskwelahan ako **nang** lumindol.","translation":"I was at school **when** the earthquake happened."},{"sentence":"**Nang** umalis siya, doon ko naramdaman ang lungkot.","translation":"**When** she left, that's when I felt the sadness."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng ibon na karaniwang kulay abo o puti, kilala sa ugali nitong mamirmihan sa mga lungsod at bilang simbolo ng kapayapaan.
etymology: From Sanskrit 'kapota' (कपोत), meaning pigeon or dove.
original_explanation: The official bird of Plaza Miranda and every public park in the Philippines. They're the OG 'tambay.' They're cute symbols of peace and love in weddings, but in the city, they're the ones who'll judge you while you eat your fishball and might just swoop in for a piece. Also, a term of endearment, 'kalapati ko,' for someone you love.
usage_notes: 'Kalapati' is the general term for both 'pigeon' and 'dove', although 'batubato' is sometimes used for the wild rock dove/pigeon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpakawala sila ng mga puting **kalapati** sa kanilang kasal.","translation":"They released white **doves** at their wedding."},{"sentence":"Puno ng **kalapati** ang liwasang-bayan tuwing umaga.","translation":"The town plaza is full of **pigeons** every morning."}]

meaning_filipino: Angkop, tama, o wasto para sa isang partikular na layunin, tao, okasyon, o sitwasyon.
etymology: From na- + dapat (should, must), with reduplication of the first syllable of the root.
original_explanation: It's the 'adulting' word. It's what you *should* do, not what you *want* to do. Like, 'nararapat' na mag-save for retirement, pero 'gusto' mong mag-travel to Korea. It's the standard, the right thing, the one that won't get you judged by your titas.
usage_notes: Often used in formal contexts to mean 'what is right or just'. It carries a stronger moral or ethical weight than just 'tama' (correct).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **nararapat** na parusa ay dapat igawad sa mga nagkasala.","translation":"The **appropriate** punishment should be given to the guilty."},{"sentence":"Hindi **nararapat** ang kanyang ugali sa isang pormal na pagtitipon.","translation":"His behavior is not **fitting** for a formal gathering."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay ng laman o mga bagay sa loob ng isang sisidlan.
original_explanation: The verb form. It's what you do to the lunch box before school, what the gas station attendant does to your car's tank, or what you do to your brain with new information (or chismis). It's the act of putting something *in* something.
usage_notes: This is the command form. The object of the verb is the container being filled. To say 'fill it with X', you'd say 'lamanan mo ng X'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**lamanan** mo ng tubig ang pitsel.","translation":"Please **fill** the pitcher with water."},{"sentence":"**Lamanan** mo na ang mga kahon para makapag-empake na tayo.","translation":"**Fill** the boxes already so we can start packing."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa kalagayan ng mga mata na bukas na bukas o malaki ang pagkakamulat, karaniwan dahil sa gulat, takot, o pagkamangha.
original_explanation: Your reaction when you see the Meralco bill. Your face when you hear the latest chismis about your officemate. Your look when you realize you sent the wrong screenshot to the wrong person. Mulat is just open eyes, dilat is open eyes with *EMOTION*.
usage_notes: Often used as an adjective (e.g., 'matang dilat'). Also serves as a root word for verbs like 'dumilat' (to open one's eyes) and 'idilat' (to open the eyes wide).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Dilat** ang kanyang mga mata sa pagkamangha sa ganda ng tanawin.","translation":"His eyes were **wide open** in amazement at the beauty of the scenery."},{"sentence":"Nakatitig siya sa akin, **dilat** ang mga mata sa takot.","translation":"He stared at me, his eyes **wide** with fear."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng legal na pagpapawalang-bisa sa kasal ng isang tao.
original_explanation: The verb form of ending the legally-binding "sila na." It's the action of filing the papers and going through the whole process to officially call it quits. "Gusto ko na siyang diborsyuhin!" is the dramatic line in many a teleserye set in the US.
usage_notes: This is an object-focused verb. The person being divorced is the object of the sentence.
