usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagdesisyon si Ana na **diborsyuhin** ang kanyang asawa pagkatapos ng maraming taon.","translation":"Ana decided **to divorce** her husband after many years."},{"sentence":"Hindi mo basta-basta pwedeng **diborsyuhin** ang isang tao nang walang sapat na dahilan sa ibang bansa.","translation":"You can't just **divorce** someone without a valid reason in other countries."}]

translation: Looks old; having an aged appearance
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng hitsura na mas matanda kaysa sa tunay na edad.
original_explanation: The result of stress, puyat (lack of sleep), and forgetting your skincare routine. It's what your tita says about you when you haven't seen her in a year and you've been working OT in a BPO. 'Hala, iho/iha, you're **mukhang matanda** na!' is the unofficial greeting.
usage_notes: A common descriptive phrase. Can be considered rude if said directly to someone, but often used in gossip or as a self-deprecating comment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa stress sa trabaho, pakiramdam ko **mukhang matanda** na ako.","translation":"Because of work stress, I feel like I **look old** already."},{"sentence":"Puyat ka ba? Medyo **mukhang matanda** ka ngayon.","translation":"Are you sleep-deprived? You **look a bit old** today."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay, gamot, o paraan na ginagamit upang magdulot ng katahimikan o magpakalma sa isang tao o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: This can be anything from a baby's pacifier ('tsupon'), a chill playlist on Spotify, or that look your mom gives you that instantly shuts you up. In a more serious context, it can be a sedative. Basically, it's the 'mute button' for chaos, whether that chaos is a crying baby or your own noisy thoughts at 3 AM.
usage_notes: Can refer to a physical object (like a baby's pacifier), a substance (like a sedative), or an action/thing that brings quiet.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigyan mo ng **pampatahimik** ang bata para tumigil sa pag-iyak.","translation":"Give the child a **pacifier** to stop it from crying."},{"sentence":"Ang musika niya ay nagsisilbing **pampatahimik** sa aking magulong isipan.","translation":"His music serves as a **calming agent** for my chaotic mind."}]

translation: to travel to/through a place, to journey across
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtahak o paglalakbay sa isang partikular na lugar, ruta, o distansya.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of "lakbay." It's what you *do* when you travel. "Gusto kong lakbayin ang buong Pilipinas." (I want to travel the entire Philippines). It has a more epic, grander feel than "puntahan" (to go to). You don't just "lakbayin" the sari-sari store; you "lakbayin" a province, a country, or even the journey of life itself (charot).
usage_notes: Nagpapahiwatig ng isang mas malawak o makabuluhang paglalakbay kumpara sa simpleng pagpunta lamang sa isang lugar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Plano naming **lakbayin** ang mga isla ng Palawan sa susunod na taon.","translation":"We plan **to travel to** the islands of Palawan next year."},{"sentence":"Marami kang pagsubok na dapat **lakbayin** sa buhay.","translation":"You have many trials **to journey through** in life."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang uri ng likido na maaaring lunukin o isubo, tulad ng tubig, gatas, o katas ng prutas.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "inom" na may hulaping "-in".
original_explanation: Anything liquid you can drink. From your morning kape, to the buko juice that saves you from the 3 PM heat, to the 'isa pa ngang beer' that you'll regret tomorrow. It's the other half of 'kain at inumin'.
usage_notes: Ito ay tumutukoy sa bagay na iniinom. Ang diin ay nasa huling pantig, na iba sa pandiwang 'inumin' (/i-NU-min/).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang gusto mong **inumin**?","translation":"What **drink** would you like?"},{"sentence":"Tubig ang pinakamainam na **inumin** para sa katawan.","translation":"Water is the best **beverage** for the body."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang may pinakamataas na antas ng kabutihan; higit sa lahat sa pagiging mabuti o angkop.
original_explanation: The 'best' option, like choosing sleep over another 'one more episode' on Netflix. It's the choice your future self will thank you for. When someone asks 'Sino'ng a-attend sa team building?' and you say 'Si Ma'am Tess,' you're saying she's the **pinakamabuti** choice to organize it because she gets things done.
usage_notes: The superlative form of 'mabuti' (good). Often used to describe the best course of action, a moral choice, or the most beneficial option.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-aaral nang mabuti ang **pinakamabuti** mong gawin para sa iyong kinabukasan.","translation":"Studying well is the **best** thing you can do for your future."},{"sentence":"Sa lahat ng payo niya, ito ang **pinakamabuti**.","translation":"Of all his advice, this is the **best**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malawakang kapahamakan, sakuna, o paghihirap na dulot ng kalikasan o gawa ng tao.
etymology: From "ka-" + "salanta" (crippled, afflicted by disaster) + "-an", meaning 'the state of great misfortune'.
original_explanation: When life gives you lemons, and then a typhoon, an earthquake, and a pandemic all at once. It's that series of unfortunate events that makes you say, "Ano na, 2026? Kalmahan mo lang." It's the reason for donation drives and the "Bangon, Pilipinas!" spirit.
usage_notes: A formal and strong word for widespread disaster or hardship.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming pamilya ang naapektuhan ng **kasalantaan** na dulot ng bagyo.","translation":"Many families were affected by the **calamity** brought by the typhoon."},{"sentence":"Nagkaisa ang buong bayan upang tulungan ang mga biktima ng **kasalantaan**.","translation":"The whole town united to help the victims of the **adversity**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagpapatalas sa isang bagay, tulad ng kutsilyo, o pagpapahusay sa isang kasanayan o kakayahan.
etymology: From 'hasa' (sharpened, skilled). 'Pag-ha-hasa' is the act of making something sharp or skilled.
original_explanation: It's sharpening your lola's kitchen knife on a 'hasaan' (whetstone). But it's also what you do when you attend workshops, practice your public speaking in the mirror, or grind in a video game to level up your character's skills. It's the training montage of your life.
usage_notes: Used both literally for tools and figuratively for skills and talents.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang araw-araw na pagsasanay ay isang **paghahasa** ng kanyang talento.","translation":"Daily practice is a **honing** of his talent."},{"sentence":"Maingay ang **paghahasa** ng mga itak sa palengke.","translation":"The **sharpening** of machetes in the market is noisy."}]

translation: to become strong; to become louder; to intensify
meaning_filipino: Tumaas ang antas ng lakas, puwersa, ingay, o bisa.
original_explanation: This word is for anything that goes from level 1 to level 10. The rain that was a gentle drizzle and is now a typhoon? Lumakas. The wifi signal that was one bar and is now full? Lumakas. Your feelings for your crush after they were nice to you? Lumakas. It's the verb for leveling up.
usage_notes: Very versatile. Can refer to physical strength, volume of sound, intensity of a storm, signal strength, feelings, influence, etc. Its antonym is `humina` (to weaken).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lumakas** ang hangin bago bumuhos ang ulan.","translation":"The wind **grew stronger** before the rain poured."},{"sentence":"Pakisabi sa kanila na **lumakas** ang tugtog at hindi kami magkarinigan.","translation":"Please tell them the music **got louder** and we can't hear each other."},{"sentence":"Simula nang mag-gym siya, unti-unting **lumakas** ang kanyang katawan.","translation":"Since he started going to the gym, his body gradually **became stronger**."}]

translation: act of pulling a trigger; strumming lightly; nudging with a finger
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng bahagyang paghila o pag-angat gamit ang dulo ng daliri, tulad ng sa gatilyo ng baril, kuwerdas ng gitara, o pag-abót sa isang tao.
etymology: From `pag-` (verb prefix indicating action) + `kalbit` (to touch lightly, to pull a trigger).
original_explanation: This is a word of small, quick actions. It's the pagkalbit ng gatilyo (pulling the trigger) in an action movie. It's the gentle pagkalbit sa gitara (strumming the guitar) when you're trying to remember a song. It's also that subtle "psst!" gesture you do with your finger to get your friend's attention, a light poke or nudge. It's a finger-flick of an action.
usage_notes: The meaning changes significantly based on the object of the action (trigger, string, person).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **pagkalbit** lang sa gatilyo ang nagpasimula ng gulo.","translation":"Just one **pull** of the trigger started the chaos."},{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang marahang **pagkalbit** niya sa mga kuwerdas ng kanyang ukelele.","translation":"I heard his gentle **strumming** on the strings of his ukelele."},{"sentence":"Isang **pagkalbit** sa braso ang ginawa niya para makuha ang atensyon ko.","translation":"He gave a light **nudge** on my arm to get my attention."}]

translation: to be infested by pests, to be plagued by
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging apektado o sinasalakay ng mga peste (insekto o hayop); ang pagdanas ng malawakang problema o sakit.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'peste'. Used literally when your rice field is attacked by locusts, or figuratively when your life is attacked by a series of unfortunate events. 'Pineste ng utang,' for example.
usage_notes: Can be literal (for crops) or figurative (for problems).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kapag hindi inalagaan, maaaring **pestehin** ang iyong mga pananim.","translation":"If not cared for, your crops might **be infested by pests**."},{"sentence":"**Pineste** ng mga daga ang buong bodega.","translation":"The entire warehouse **was infested** by rats."},{"sentence":"Tila **pineste** ng malas ang pamilya nila ngayong taon.","translation":"It seems their family **was plagued** by bad luck this year."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na pabaya, marumi, at walang ayos sa sarili, sa gamit, o sa gawain.
original_explanation: This is your roommate whose side of the room looks like a typhoon just hit it. They leave clothes on the floor, dishes in the sink for a week, and their work files are a mess. It's not just messy, it's a lifestyle of 'bahala na si Batman' applied to cleanliness and order.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang kakulangan ng isang tao sa kalinisan o kaayusan sa kanyang personal na gawi at mga gamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinagsabihan ng nanay ang anak niyang **taong burara** dahil sa magulong kwarto nito.","translation":"The mother scolded her **sloppy** child because of their messy room."},{"sentence":"Mahirap magtrabaho kasama ang isang **taong burara** dahil hindi maayos ang kanyang mga papeles.","translation":"It's hard to work with a **slovenly person** because their paperwork is not organized."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang takdang haba ng panahon; ang buwanang regla ng isang babae.
original_explanation: The ultimate "periodt" moment, literally. It can mean a period of time, like your probation period sa work. But 99% of the time, it's the code word for menstruation. "May piryod ako" is the universal signal for "bring me chocolate, don't annoy me, and yes, masakit ang puson ko."
usage_notes: While it can mean a span of time, it is overwhelmingly used to refer to menstruation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **piryod** siya ngayon kaya masungit.","translation":"She has her **period** today that's why she's grumpy."},{"sentence":"Ilang araw ang karaniwang **piryod** ng pag-aaral para sa pagsusulit?","translation":"How many days is the usual **period** of study for the exam?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang patuloy na pagbabasa o pagtingin sa masasamang balita sa internet, kahit pa ito ay nagdudulot ng kalungkutan, pagkabalisa, o pagkatakot.
original_explanation: Yung scroll ka nang scroll sa social media para maghanap ng updates, pero puro nega news at chismis lang nakikita mo hanggang sa ma-drain ka na. Parang toxic relationship, alam mong masakit pero 'di mo maiwan. 'One more scroll,' sabi mo, pero 2 AM na.
usage_notes: Isang neolohismo na naging popular noong panahon ng pandemya. Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng social media at balita.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na 'yang **doomscrolling** at baka ma-high blood ka.","translation":"Stop that **doomscrolling** or you might get high blood pressure."},{"sentence":"Puyat na naman ako kagabi dahil sa **doomscrolling**.","translation":"I stayed up late again last night because of **doomscrolling**."}]

translation: to pay a salary; to receive a salary
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay o pagtanggap ng kabayaran, karaniwan ay sa takdang panahon, para sa ginawang serbisyo o trabaho.
original_explanation: That glorious moment every 15th and 30th of the month. 'Pag oras na para magsuweldo, biglang nagiging best friends mo ang ATM, ang app ng bangko mo, at yung mga taong pinagkakautangan mo. It's the payday verb that fuels the nation's milk tea and Shopee addictions.
usage_notes: The verb can be used from the perspective of the employer (to pay a salary) or the employee (to receive a salary). Context determines the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailan daw **magsuweldo** ang kompanya?","translation":"When will the company **pay salaries**?"},{"sentence":"Yehey! Oras na para **magsuweldo**!","translation":"Yay! It's time to **receive our salary**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdanas ng malalim na kalungkutan o pananabik, kadalasang may kasamang pangungulila.
original_explanation: This is the "sana all" feeling but on a poetic, rainy-day-staring-out-the-window level. It's a quiet, deep sadness, like listening to a sad OPM song alone in your room at 3 AM. More profound than just being sad; it has a touch of longing.
usage_notes: Mas makatao at malalim kaysa sa 'nalulungkot'. Kadalasang nagpapahiwatig ng isang estado ng pagkatao sa halip na isang reaksyon sa isang partikular na kaganapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Madalas siyang **nalulumbay** tuwing naaalala niya ang kanyang yumaong asawa.","translation":"She often feels **melancholic** whenever she remembers her late husband."},{"sentence":"Ang makata ay nagsulat ng tula tungkol sa isang pusong **nalulumbay**.","translation":"The poet wrote a poem about a **sorrowful** heart."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na kusang-loob na ibinibigay o inihahandog bilang tanda ng paggalang, pagsamba, o pagmamahal.
original_explanation: That thing you give up for a greater good. Like your sleep for a K-drama marathon ('Alay para sa oppa!'), or your diet for a slice of ube cheesecake. It’s also used in a super serious way, like offering your life for your country, or in OPM songs about offering your love to someone who probably won't accept it. #Hugot
usage_notes: Can be both a noun (an offering) and a verb (to offer, 'mag-alay'). Has a deep, often solemn connotation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagdala sila ng mga bulaklak bilang **alay** sa dambana.","translation":"They brought flowers as an **offering** to the shrine."},{"sentence":"Ang kantang ito ay **alay** ko sa lahat ng mga sawi sa pag-ibig.","translation":"This song is my **dedication** to all the brokenhearted."}]

translation: to be able to be signed
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagda o paglalagay ng pirma sa isang dokumento upang maging opisyal o balido ito.
etymology: From ma- (ability prefix) + pirma (signature, from Spanish 'firma') + -han (locative suffix).
original_explanation: The final boss of any BPO or corporate job: getting that contract or clearance form signed. "Pabalik-balik ako sa HR, hindi ko mapirmahan 'yung papeles ko!" It's the act of getting a signature, the sacred scribble that makes everything official, from a marriage contract to a delivery receipt.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to the act of signing a document.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong bumalik bukas para **mapirmahan** ng manager ang tseke.","translation":"I need to come back tomorrow to get the check **signed** by the manager."},{"sentence":"Sana **mapirmahan** na ang batas para sa mas mataas na sahod.","translation":"Hopefully, the law for higher wages will be **signed** soon."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na may romantikong ugnayan sa isa pa; katipan o nobyo/nobya.
etymology: From "sinta" (love, affection) with the prefix "ka-" and suffix "-an", denoting a reciprocal relationship.
original_explanation: Your jowa, bebe, bae, or whatever you call the person you're 'in a relationship with' on Facebook. The one you send 'good morning' texts to and fight with over where to eat. It's a bit more formal than 'syota' and less clinical than 'significant other'.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with "nobyo/nobya" (boyfriend/girlfriend). "Kasintahan" can feel slightly more formal or serious, sometimes implying a long-term or engaged relationship.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinakilala na ni Ana ang kanyang **kasintahan** sa kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"Ana finally introduced her **sweetheart** to her parents."},{"sentence":"Sila ay mag-**kasintahan** na sa loob ng limang taon.","translation":"They have been a **couple** (sweethearts) for five years."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maingat na pag-alis o pagkuha ng maliliit na bagay na nakadikit o nakasabit, gamit ang daliri o isang maliit na instrumento.
original_explanation: Your dentist does this to get the tinga out of your teeth. It’s also what you do to that one annoying piece of dirt on your phone screen. 'Huwag mong kukutin 'yung sugat mo, baka maimpeksyon!' is the classic mom-line.
usage_notes: Often used for picking at scabs, food stuck in teeth, or small, embedded dirt. Implies using a fine tool or fingernails.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinabihan ako ng dentista na huwag **kukutin** ang tinga gamit ang palito.","translation":"The dentist told me not **to pick at** the food stuck in my teeth with a toothpick."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya mapigilang **kukutin** ang balat ng prutas gamit ang kanyang mga daliri.","translation":"She couldn't stop herself from **picking at** the fruit's skin with her fingers."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang ikalabindalawa ng gabi; ang gitna ng gabi (12:00 AM).
original_explanation: 12:00 AM. The official start of 'overthinking hours.' It's when you're either deep in your K-drama marathon, grinding for a deadline, having a deep talk with your friends, or just staring at the ceiling wondering about your life choices. It's the witching hour, the Cinderella deadline, and the time all the best 'sana all' moments seem to happen online.
usage_notes: Can also be spelled with a hyphen, `hating-gabi`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Umuwi siya ng lampas **hatinggabi** na.","translation":"He went home past **midnight**."},{"sentence":"Nag-umpisa ang party noong **hatinggabi**.","translation":"The party started at **midnight**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, bagay, o sitwasyon na nagdudulot ng problema, abala, o alalahanin.
original_explanation: This is the noun form of 'sakit ng ulo.' It's not the pain in your head, but the person or problem *causing* the figurative pain. Your jowang selosa? Sakit-ulo. Bills? Sakit-ulo. Your groupmate na pabuhat? Ultimate sakit-ulo.
usage_notes: This is the figurative version only, referring to a problem or a nuisance. It is a compound word. Compare with 'sakit ng ulo,' which can be literal or figurative.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang anak mong pasaway ay isang malaking **sakit-ulo**.","translation":"Your troublesome child is a big **nuisance**."},{"sentence":"Iwasan natin ang mga hindi kinakailangang **sakit-ulo** sa proyekto.","translation":"Let's avoid unnecessary **problems** in the project."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagtatrabaho, lalo na sa isang gawain na nangangailangan ng pisikal na lakas o kasanayan; isang manggagawa.
original_explanation: This refers to any worker, but it often brings to mind the hardworking folks in construction, factories, or farms – the people who literally build the country. It’s a term of respect for the 'blue-collar' workforce. Sila ang mga bayani ng Araw ng Paggawa.
usage_notes: While it can mean any worker, it often carries the connotation of a manual or skilled laborer.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **trabahador** sa konstruksyon ay nagpapahinga sa ilalim ng puno.","translation":"The construction **workers** are resting under the tree."},{"sentence":"Dapat itaas ang sahod ng bawat **trabahador** na Pilipino.","translation":"The salary of every Filipino **laborer** should be increased."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa paghupa o pagbaba ng tindi, gaya ng sa pamamaga, galit, o bagyo.
original_explanation: That feeling when your anger finally simmers down after a major "tampo." Or when a pimple's swelling finally goes down before a big event. It's the "chill" after the "beast mode," the calm after the storm, the quiet after your mom's sermon. "Hintaying lumubag ang galit niya bago ka magpaliwanag."
usage_notes: Often used in the context of emotions (anger), physical conditions (swelling, fever), or natural phenomena (storm). The root itself is less common than its inflected forms like 'lumubag'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi pa **lubag** ang pamamaga ng kanyang bukung-bukong.","translation":"The swelling on his ankle has not **subsided** yet."},{"sentence":"Nang lumubag na ang kanyang galit, saka niya ako kinausap.","translation":"When his anger **calmed down**, that's when he talked to me."}]

translation: to wipe, to smear, to apply (by wiping)
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pag-aalis ng isang bagay sa isang ibabaw sa pamamagitan ng pagdadaiti at paggalaw dito, karaniwan gamit ang kamay, tela, o anumang kagamitan.
original_explanation: This is the action of putting something on a surface, like spreading palaman on pandesal, applying lotion, or wiping away your tears after watching a sad K-drama. It's the 'swipe' action before 'swipe right/left' was a thing. 'Ma, paabot ng Vicks, **magpapahid** lang ako sa dibdib.'
usage_notes: Can mean to have someone wipe something for you (causative), but is more commonly used to mean applying something to oneself, like lotion or ointment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **magpahid** ng sunblock bago lumabas.","translation":"Don't forget to **apply** sunblock before going out."},{"sentence":"**Nagpahid** siya ng mantikilya sa tinapay.","translation":"He **smeared** butter on the bread."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng mga katangian, kilos, o itsura na tulad ng isang hari; maringal at kagalang-galang.
original_explanation: That feeling when you get your 13th-month pay and you can finally afford to eat somewhere other than the office pantry. You walk in with that malahari vibe, like you own the place. It's having a 'royal' aura, whether it's your bearing, your outfit, or your generosity for one glorious payday.
usage_notes: Describes a majestic or royal quality in a person's appearance, demeanor, or in an object's grandeur.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **malahari** siyang tindig na kahanga-hanga.","translation":"He has a **kingly** posture that is admirable."},{"sentence":"Ang lumang gusali ay may **malahari** pa ring anyo sa kabila ng edad nito.","translation":"The old building still has a **majestic** appearance despite its age."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng damit pambabae na isinusuot sa ilalim ng bestida o pang-itaas na damit, karaniwang gawa sa manipis na tela.
original_explanation: It's the OG undergarment lola and nanay wore under their daster or bestida, parang sando but for dresses. Before Uniqlo Airism, there was the humble kamison. It's that thin layer that prevents your main outfit from being 'bakát' (showing outlines).
usage_notes: Primarily refers to a woman's slip or underdress.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsuot siya ng **kamison** sa ilalim ng kanyang baro't saya.","translation":"She wore a **chemise** under her baro't saya."},{"sentence":"Mainit ang panahon kaya **kamison** lang ang suot niya sa bahay.","translation":"The weather is hot so she's just wearing a **slip** at home."}]

translation: to show off someone/something; to make someone/something famous
meaning_filipino: Ipagmalaki o ipakilala ang isang tao o bagay sa publiko upang sumikat o mapansin.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `i-` (nagsasaad ng sanhi), `pagpa-` (nagsasaad ng sanhi), at `sikat` (famous, sun's rays).
original_explanation: This is what stage mothers do. Or when you bring your super talented friend to a party and you tell them, "Kantahin mo 'yung 'Bohemian Rhapsody' dali!" You're not showing off for yourself, you're making *someone else* the star of the show. It's being a hype man for a person or a thing.
usage_notes: Ang pokus ay sa pagpapasikat o pagpapapansin sa *ibang* tao o bagay, hindi sa sarili (bagaman maaaring makasarili ang motibo). Ang taong/bagay na ipinagpapasikat ay ang tuwirang layon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto niyang **ipagpasikat** ang kanyang anak na magaling kumanta.","translation":"She wants to **show off** her child who sings well."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **ipagpasikat**, nahihiya ako!","translation":"Don't **put me in the spotlight**, I'm shy!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kasuotan sa ulo na karaniwang may palibot na labi, ginagamit bilang proteksiyon sa araw o ulan, o bilang palamuti.
original_explanation: The OG sunblock. Whether you're a farmer, a beach-goer, or just trying to hide a bad hair day, the sumbrero is your best friend. It's the crown you choose for yourself.
usage_notes: While 'sumbrero' is the general term, specific types of hats often have their own names (e.g., salakot).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutan ang iyong **sumbrero** dahil napakainit sa labas.","translation":"Don't forget your **hat** because it's very hot outside."},{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng **sumbrero** na suot ng lola mo.","translation":"The **hat** your grandmother is wearing is beautiful."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maikling pako o aspili na may malapad at patag na ulo, idinidiin gamit ang daliri upang magkabit ng papel sa isang ibabaw tulad ng pader o bulletin board.
original_explanation: The tiny cousin of the 'pako'. It's what you use to post announcements on the office bulletin board, or to hang your kid's 'Best in Coloring' award on the corkboard. It's the "ouch!" you feel when you accidentally step on one barefoot.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit niya ang **pakong-aspili** para idikit ang anunsyo sa pader.","translation":"She used a **thumbtack** to stick the announcement on the wall."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa pagiging makatotohanan, makatuwiran, at nakabatay sa karanasan o aktwal na paggamit sa halip na teorya.
original_explanation: This is the official motto of every nanay in the palengke. Why buy the branded stuff when the generic one works the same for half the price? It's choosing the 'jeep' over Grab because, hey, traffic is the same anyway. Being praktikal is the art of adulting in the Philippines without going broke.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa mga usapan tungkol sa pera, pagdedesisyon, at pang-araw-araw na buhay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas **praktikal** na magbaon ng pagkain sa opisina kaysa laging bumibili.","translation":"It's more **practical** to bring packed lunch to the office than to always buy."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating maging **praktikal** sa paggasta ngayong may krisis.","translation":"We need to be **practical** with our spending now that there's a crisis."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaikling paraan ng pagsulat ng salitang "baby" o "babe," na karaniwang ginagamit sa text messaging at social media bilang tawagan sa isang minamahal o malapit na kaibigan.
original_explanation: The ultimate text-speak shortcut for "baby" or "babe". It's what you call your S.O. when you're too lazy to type the other two letters. It's efficient, cute, and a little bit low-effort, just like some modern relationships. "Good morning, bb!" is the new "I love you."
usage_notes: Primarily used in informal, digital communication. Can be used for a romantic partner or a close friend.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kamusta araw mo, **bb**?","translation":"How was your day, **bb** (babe)?"},{"sentence":"See you later, **bb**! Ingat ka.","translation":"See you later, **bb** (babe)! Take care."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng pahintulot o pagsang-ayon sa isang mungkahi, kahilingan, o kondisyon.
original_explanation: When your parents finally say yes to your travel plans after a 2-hour PowerPoint presentation on your itinerary and budget. Or when your crush finally agrees to go out for coffee. 'YES! Pumayag siya!'
usage_notes: A very common word used in everyday conversation. The opposite is `hindi pumayag` or `tumanggi`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa wakas, **pumayag** din siyang sumama sa party.","translation":"Finally, she **agreed** to come to the party."},{"sentence":"Hindi ako **pumayag** sa alok niya dahil masyadong mababa.","translation":"I did not **agree** to his offer because it was too low."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng bahagyang paghugas o pagbanlaw, karaniwan ng mga kamay, paa, o mga kagamitang pangkain, gamit ang tubig.
original_explanation: This is not the full-on 'hugas' with soap and everything. This is the quick rinse you do before eating with your hands (magkamay). It's the 'padaanin lang sa tubig' move for your feet after walking in slippers outside. It’s the bare minimum of washing, parang 'seen' sa chat – may acknowledgment, pero hindi full commitment.
usage_notes: Often used for rinsing hands, feet, or utensils. It implies a less thorough wash than 'hugasan'. The noun form 'langgas' refers to the act or the liquid used for rinsing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Langgasan** mo muna ang mga kamay mo bago kumain.","translation":"**Rinse** your hands first before eating."},{"sentence":"Pakidala nito sa lababo at **langgasan** mo.","translation":"Please bring this to the sink and **rinse** it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng araknid na may walong paa at karaniwang gumagawa ng sapot upang makahuli ng pagkain.
original_explanation: That eight-legged creature that suddenly appears in your shower, making you question all your life choices. Also, the inspiration for Spider-Man, but the real ones are less friendly and don't pay rent.
usage_notes: Can also refer to a cobweb ('bahay ng lawalawa' or simply 'lawalawa').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May malaking **lawalawa** sa sulok ng kisame.","translation":"There's a big **spider** in the corner of the ceiling."},{"sentence":"Tinanggal niya ang mga **lawalawa** sa bintana.","translation":"She removed the **cobwebs** from the window."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagsusulat at nagpapanatili ng isang blog, isang online na dyornal o website na naglalaman ng mga personal na karanasan, opinyon, at impormasyon.
original_explanation: Dati, sila yung may mga online diary. Ngayon, sila na yung mga 'content creator' na nakakatanggap ng PR packages, libreng travel, at kumikita sa pagsusulat tungkol sa buhay nila. Sila yung nag-umpisa ng 'influencer' culture bago pa nauso ang TikTok.
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang tukuyin ang mga manunulat sa internet.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang sikat na food **blogger** ang nag-review ng bagong bukas na restaurant.","translation":"A famous food **blogger** reviewed the newly opened restaurant."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula siya bilang isang personal **blogger** bago naging isang vlogger.","translation":"She started as a personal **blogger** before becoming a vlogger."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa asal, pananamit, o pananalita na karaniwang iniuugnay sa mga taong tumatambay sa kanto; maaaring may negatibong konotasyon ng pagiging magaspang o walang pinag-aralan.
original_explanation: The vibe of the 'tambay sa kanto'. Think cheap gin, a guitar, and conversations that get louder past 10 PM. 'Pangkanto' humor is often raw and unfiltered. 'Pangkanto' fashion might mean sando, shorts, and tsinelas. It's the opposite of 'conyo', the raw, unfiltered culture of the street corner.
usage_notes: Can be derogatory, implying someone is rough, uncultured, or a loiterer. However, it can also be used neutrally or even humorously to describe something as "street."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayabang ang dating niya dahil sa **pangkanto** niyang pananalita.","translation":"He comes off as arrogant because of his **street-style** way of speaking."},{"sentence":"Kinanta nila ang mga awiting **pangkanto** na sikat noong dekada nobenta.","translation":"They sang the **street-corner** songs that were popular in the nineties."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bahagi ng damit na pumapalibot sa leeg; isang paha o tali na isinusuot sa leeg ng isang hayop.
original_explanation: Ito yung kwelyo ng polo mo na pilit mong tinitiklop nang maayos para presentable sa Zoom meeting. O kaya yung isinusuot sa aso mo na may pangalan at contact number, para 'pag nawala, alam ng makakakita na hindi siya 'askal' (asong kalye) kundi 'furbaby' na may nag-aalalang 'furparent'.
usage_notes: Can refer to the collar of a shirt ('kwelyo') or a collar for a pet.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayusin mo ang **kolyar** ng iyong polo bago ka umalis.","translation":"Fix the **collar** of your polo shirt before you leave."},{"sentence":"Nawala ang **kolyar** ng aso namin kaya bumili kami ng bago.","translation":"Our dog's **collar** got lost so we bought a new one."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi humihinto; tuloy-tuloy at walang puwang o agwat sa pagitan.
original_explanation: Parang chismis ng kapitbahay mo, **walang-patlang**. Or 'yung pag-ulan 'pag may bagyo, dire-diretso. Pwede ring 'yung boss mo magbigay ng tasks, sunod-sunod, **walang-patlang**.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang mga kilos o pangyayari na tuloy-tuloy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsalita siya nang **walang-patlang** sa loob ng isang oras.","translation":"He spoke **continuously** for an hour."},{"sentence":"Ang **walang-patlang** na pag-ulan ay nagdulot ng baha.","translation":"The **non-stop** rain caused flooding."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabago o pagdaragdag sa isang batas, panukala, o dokumento upang ito ay mapabuti o maiwasto.
original_explanation: This is the 'PS: I love you' of legal documents. It's that 'Wait, one more thing...' moment in Congress. When a law isn't quite right, you don't throw it out; you perform a pagsusog. Think of it as patching a video game to fix a bug or adding a new feature. It's the formal way of saying, 'Oops, let's correct that.'
usage_notes: Primarily used in legal, legislative, or formal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng mainitang debate tungkol sa **pagsusog** ng konstitusyon.","translation":"There was a heated debate about the **amendment** of the constitution."},{"sentence":"Iminungkahi ng senador ang ilang **pagsusog** sa panukalang batas.","translation":"The senator proposed several **amendments** to the bill."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalaro ng tenis sa mesa, isang isports na ginagamitan ng maliliit na raketa at isang magaan na bola.
original_explanation: It's what you and your officemates do in the pantry to de-stress after a toxic meeting. Or that game you play at a resort where the ball flies everywhere except on the table. It's a fast-paced game that requires more agility than you'd think. "Game, **magpingpong** tayo! Talo-libre-meryenda."
usage_notes: A direct loanword that has been adapted into a Tagalog verb using the 'mag-' prefix.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig **magpingpong** ang magkapatid tuwing hapon.","translation":"The siblings love to **play table tennis** every afternoon."},{"sentence":"Niyaya niya akong **magpingpong** pero tumanggi ako dahil hindi ako marunong.","translation":"He invited me to **play ping-pong** but I declined because I don't know how."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtusok o pagdiin sa isang bagay gamit ang dulo ng daliri, karaniwang madiin.
original_explanation: It's that aggressive poke your tita gives you in the side while saying 'Uy, tumataba ka!' (Hey, you're getting fat!). It's more forceful than a 'kalabit' (gentle tap) and is basically the physical version of an exclamation point.
usage_notes: The verb form is 'duruin'. Can also refer to the act of pointing accusatorily.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malakas na **duro** sa tagiliran ang gumising sa kanya.","translation":"A strong **poke** in the side woke him up."},{"sentence":"Galit niyang dinuro ang dibdib ng kaaway.","translation":"He angrily **jabbed** his finger at the enemy's chest."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa paulit-ulit at mabilis na pagkinang o pag-ilaw ng isang bagay, tulad ng mga bituin o maliliit na ilaw.
etymology: Reduplication of the first two syllables of the root word 'kutitap', meaning 'sparkle' or 'twinkle'.
original_explanation: Think Christmas lights in Ayala Triangle, or the stars in a provincial night sky. It's that magical, on-and-off sparkle. 'Wow, parang mga alitaptap na kukuti-kutitap ang mga ilaw sa Christmas tree!' It’s the visual equivalent of 'sana all may sparkle'.
usage_notes: A highly descriptive and somewhat poetic word used to describe flickering lights.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga mata niya ay tila **kukuti-kutitap** na mga bituin sa dilim.","translation":"Her eyes were like **twinkling** stars in the dark."},{"sentence":"Mahilig akong manood ng mga **kukuti-kutitap** na ilaw tuwing Pasko.","translation":"I love watching the **twinkling** lights during Christmas."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na nangyayari, ginagawa, o umiiral sa bawat araw; pang-araw-araw.
original_explanation: The daily grind. Commuting via EDSA, drinking 3-in-1 coffee, dealing with your boss's mood swings, and checking your crush's IG stories. If it happens Monday to Sunday (or Monday to Friday for the lucky ones), it's 'araw-araw'.
usage_notes: Can function as both an adverb (modifying a verb) and an adjective (describing a noun).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Araw-araw** akong nag-e-ehersisyo.","translation":"I exercise **everyday**."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-commute ay parte ng aking **araw-araw** na buhay.","translation":"Commuting is part of my **daily** life."}]

translation: Junk food; snacks (usually savory and processed).
meaning_filipino: Anumang uri ng pagkaing pangmerienda o pampalipas-oras na karaniwang nakabalot, tulad ng mga sitsarón, kropek, o chips.
etymology: From Spanish 'chuchería' (trinkets, sweets, knick-knacks), which also gave us 'tsutserias'. The meaning diverged to refer specifically to snack foods.
original_explanation: The lifeblood of any Pinoy kid's childhood and the go-to for a movie marathon. It's that crunchy, salty, sometimes sweet, and always 'nakaka-guilty' treat you buy from the sari-sari store. Your mom probably warned you about getting a sore throat from eating too much of this.
usage_notes: Often used to refer to any packaged snack, not just "junk food" in the negative sense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno na naman ng **tsitsirya** ang baunan mo.","translation":"Your lunchbox is full of **junk food** again."},{"sentence":"Bumili tayo ng **tsitsirya** at soft drinks para sa panonood ng pelikula.","translation":"Let's buy some **snacks** and soft drinks for the movie."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghahati ng isang buong bagay sa dalawang magkasinlaking bahagi.
etymology: 'pa-' + 'la-' + 'hati' + '-an'. A complex formation. 'Hati' is 'half/divide'. 'Palahati' is 'half of each'. The verb form 'palahatian' means 'to make something half for each'.
original_explanation: The ultimate act of fairness (or forced fairness). 'Palahatian natin 'tong Lays, para walang away.' (Let's split this bag of Lays in half, so there's no fight). It's what you do with the last piece of pizza, the last sip of Coke, or the bill on a first date (sometimes).
usage_notes: The verb form. The noun is 'kalahati' (half).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Palahatian** natin ang bayad sa taxi.","translation":"Let's **split** the taxi fare **in half**."},{"sentence":"Niyaya niya akong **palahatian** ang kinita namin sa proyekto.","translation":"He invited me to **divide our project earnings in half**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na laging nagnanais na maging sentro ng atensyon o ang bida sa anumang sitwasyon, kadalasan sa paraang nakakainis sa iba.
etymology: From `pa-` (to act like) + `bida` (protagonist/hero), from Spanish `vida` (life, but adopted in Filipino theater to mean protagonist).
original_explanation: The person in your group project who does the least work but presents the most. The friend who always has a "better" story to tell right after you share yours. It's someone who loves the spotlight a little *too* much. In the office, they're the one who CCs the entire C-suite on a minor email. "Hayaan mo na siya, pabida talaga 'yan."
usage_notes: Almost always used with a negative connotation. Can also be used as an adjective.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **pabida**; hindi lang ikaw ang magaling dito.","translation":"Don't be a **show-off**; you're not the only one who is good here."},{"sentence":"Laging eepal 'yung **pabida** naming kaklase tuwing may recitation.","translation":"Our **attention-seeking** classmate always butts in during recitation."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pag-aaral at pagpapahusay ng isang kasanayan o kaalaman sa pamamagitan ng paulit-ulit na paggawa, pag-eensayo, o pagtuturo.
original_explanation: Your BPO life in one word. It's the endless drills before a sports competition, the 'practice makes perfect' mantra of your music teacher, or that week-long seminar before you're allowed to touch the company's system. It's the grind before the glory.
usage_notes: A broad term used in sports, academics, professional development, and military contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ng masusing **pagsasanay** bago sumabak sa isang marathon.","translation":"Thorough **training** is needed before joining a marathon."},{"sentence":"Ang araw-araw na **pagsasanay** sa pagtugtog ng gitara ay nagbunga ng kanyang galing.","translation":"Daily **practice** in playing the guitar resulted in his skill."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos o kalagayan ng pagtigil o paghinto mula sa paggalaw, pagkilos, o pag-iral.
etymology: From `pagka-` (denoting an abstract quality or state resulting from an action) + `hinto` (stop).
original_explanation: 'Yung biglang preno ng bus sa EDSA, 'yun ang pagkahinto. O kaya 'yung biglaang pagtigil ng usapan niyo nung dumaan si crush. Awkward. It's the sudden stop, the abrupt end of motion or conversation.
usage_notes: Often used to describe the moment or the manner of stopping. Can be used for physical stops or the cessation of an activity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagulat ang lahat sa biglaang **pagkahinto** ng sasakyan.","translation":"Everyone was surprised by the sudden **stopping** of the vehicle."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkahinto** ng ulan ay hudyat na para lumabas kami.","translation":"The **cessation** of the rain was a signal for us to go out."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi labis at hindi rin kulang; nasa gitnang antas o sukat; sapat lamang.
etymology: From ka- + tamtam (a reduplication of a root related to taste or measure, possibly related to tama - correct/enough).
original_explanation: The Goldilocks of Tagalog words. Not too hot, not too cold, but 'just right.' When you order coffee, it's not 'strong' or 'weak,' but katamtaman. Your crush's feelings for you? Hopefully not katamtaman. It's the 'sakto lang' vibe. The perfect level of spiciness in your Bicol Express.
usage_notes: Can function as both an adjective (describing a noun) and an adverb (modifying a verb/adjective), often as 'nang katamtaman'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko ng kape na **katamtaman** lang ang tapang.","translation":"I like coffee that is of **medium** strength."},{"sentence":"May **katamtaman** siyang taas para sa isang Pilipino.","translation":"He has an **average** height for a Filipino."},{"sentence":"Umuulan nang **katamtaman**.","translation":"It is raining **moderately**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking nagpapaupa ng bahay, silid, o gusaling apartment.
original_explanation: Siya yung tito na laging may 'for da singil' moment sa'yo. Minsan strict sa rules ('Bawal maingay after 10 PM!'), minsan naman cool at iinom pa kasama ng mga tenants.
usage_notes: The female counterpart is 'kasera'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakausap mo na ba ang **kasero** tungkol sa sirang gripo?","translation":"Have you talked to the **landlord** about the broken faucet?"},{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang **kasero** namin sa pagbabayad sa tamang oras.","translation":"Our **landlord** is strict about paying on time."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa heograpiya, isang kathang-isip na bilog na linya sa ibabaw ng mundo na dumadaan sa North Pole at South Pole, na ginagamit sa pagsukat ng longitude.
original_explanation: Yung linya sa globe na natutunan mo sa Araling Panlipunan nung high school pero nakalimutan mo na. Ito yung kasama ng 'latitude' sa pag-define kung nasaan ka sa mundo. Parang sa buhay, kailangan mo ng reference point para hindi ka maligaw. This is the Earth's version of a 'landmark'.
usage_notes: Primarily used in scientific or academic contexts like geography. The Tagalog equivalent 'meridyano' (from Spanish) is also used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Prime **Meridian** ay matatagpuan sa Greenwich, England.","translation":"The Prime **Meridian** is located in Greenwich, England."},{"sentence":"Ginagamit ang mga linya ng **meridian** upang matukoy ang longitude ng isang lugar.","translation":"**Meridian** lines are used to determine the longitude of a place."}]

translation: to wade; to splash around lightly
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalakad o paglalaro sa mababaw na tubig, karaniwang nagdudulot ng bahagyang tilamsik.
original_explanation: That cute thing kids (and kids-at-heart) do at the beach, just dipping their feet in the shallow part and making little splashes. It's not a full-on swimming commitment; it's the 'testing the waters' phase of a relationship, but with actual water.
usage_notes: Implies shallow water and gentle splashing, not vigorous swimming. Often used interchangeably with 'tampisaw'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masayang **tumapsaw** sa ilog ang mga bata tuwing hapon.","translation":"The children happily **wade** in the river every afternoon."},{"sentence":"Gusto ko lang **tumapsaw** sa dalampasigan at hindi lumangoy.","translation":"I just want **to splash around lightly** on the shore and not swim."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang kasangkapan na may talim na ginagamit para sa pagputol o paggupit, tulad ng gunting o nail cutter.
original_explanation: The official term for "gunting" or "nail cutter." It's any tool you use for cutting. The scissors you use to open a bag of chips, the clippers for your nails, or the shears the barber uses to give you that questionable "summer cut." If it snips, it's a `panggupit`.
usage_notes: A general term. 'Gunting' is more specific for scissors, while 'panggupit' can also refer to clippers.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pahiram naman ng **panggupit** mo, puputulin ko lang itong sinulid.","translation":"Can I borrow your **cutting tool** (scissors), I'll just cut this thread."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng bagong **panggupit** ng kuko.","translation":"I need new nail **clippers**."}]

translation: to expel; to excommunicate; to fire
meaning_filipino: Alisin sa pagiging kasapi ng isang samahan, organisasyon, o trabaho dahil sa isang paglabag o kasalanan.
original_explanation: This is the formal way of saying "You're fired!" or "You're kicked out of the group chat." It's what happens when you break the rules so bad, they have to officially remove your name from the roster. Think of it as being voted off the island, but for your job or your church.
usage_notes: Often used in formal contexts like legal, corporate, or religious settings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang komite na **patiwalagin** ang miyembrong napatunayang nagnakaw ng pondo.","translation":"The committee decided to **expel** the member who was proven to have stolen funds."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kosmetiko na ipinapahid sa labi upang magbigay-kulay dito.
original_explanation: The ultimate weapon in your kikay kit. That tube of color you put on when you need to feel powerful, whether for a job interview or just a trip to the mall. 'On-call ka? Mag-lipistik ka para mukhang gising!'
usage_notes: A direct loanword, commonly used and understood by all.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang magdala ng **lipistik** para sa iyong retoke mamaya.","translation":"Don't forget to bring **lipstick** for your retouch later."},{"sentence":"Nawawala ang paborito kong pulang **lipistik**!","translation":"My favorite red **lipstick** is missing!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang anak na lalaki ng iyong anak.
original_explanation: Lolo's official 'taga-abot ng tools' and designated heir to his old-school wisdom, whether it's about basketball, fixing things, or life in general. He's the one tasked to carry on the family name and lola's secret adobo recipe.
usage_notes: The standard way to specify the gender of a grandchild.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tinuturuan ng lolo ang kanyang **apong lalaki** na mag-bike.","translation":"The grandfather is teaching his **grandson** how to ride a bike."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang buwis na ipinapataw ng pamahalaan sa mga inaangkat o iniluluwas na produkto.
original_explanation: That surprise fee you have to pay when your Shein or Amazon package finally arrives from abroad. It's the government's way of saying, 'Nice haul, pa-share naman kami diyan.' It's the reason your 'budol' from overseas ends up being more expensive than you thought.
usage_notes: A formal, economic term. Not commonly used in casual conversation. 'Taripa' is a more common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpataw ng mataas na **aransel** ang gobyerno sa mga imported na sasakyan.","translation":"The government imposed a high **tariff** on imported cars."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan ang pagbaba ng **aransel** sa mga produktong agrikultural.","translation":"They are studying the reduction of **tariffs** on agricultural products."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabago ng lasa ng isang bagay tungo sa pagiging matamis.
original_explanation: This is what happens to a mango as it ripens. Or when your crush finally smiles back at you, and suddenly, the whole world seems to 'tumamis'. It's the process of something going from bland or sour to delightfully sweet.
usage_notes: Often used figuratively to describe a situation or expression becoming pleasant or endearing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hayaan mong mahinog pa ang mangga para ito ay **tumamis**.","translation":"Let the mango ripen more so it will **become sweet**."},{"sentence":"**Tumamis** ang ngiti sa kanyang mga labi nang makita niya ako.","translation":"The smile on her lips **became sweet** when she saw me."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat o grupo na binubuo ng tatlong tao o bagay.
original_explanation: A group of three. Your barkada's 'power trio'. In a BPO setting, this could be a team huddle with you, your TL, and the QA. In a game, it means 'by threes'. 'Tatluhan ang pila!' (Line up in threes!).
usage_notes: Can also be used as an adverb to mean 'by threes' or 'in a group of three'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aming grupo ay isang masayang **tatluhan**.","translation":"Our group is a happy **trio**."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-uwi ay ginawang **tatluhan** sa bawat sasakyan.","translation":"The ride home was arranged **in groups of three** for each car."}]

meaning_filipino: Sapat sa pangangailangan; tama o wasto; akma o lapat.
original_explanation: The most satisfying word when paying for something with exact change. "Bayad po, husto." It's also your mom's answer when you ask how much salt to put in the adobo: "Yung husto lang" (Just enough). It's that "just right" Goldilocks feeling – not too much, not too little. The opposite of "kulang" (lacking) and "sobra" (excessive).
usage_notes: Very versatile. Can mean 'enough', 'correct', 'exact', or 'fitting'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Salamat sa bayad, **husto** lang po ito.","translation":"Thanks for the payment, this is the **exact** amount."},{"sentence":"Sa tingin ko ay **husto** na ang kanin na ito para sa ating lahat.","translation":"I think this rice is **enough** for all of us."},{"sentence":"**Husto** sa katawan niya ang bagong damit.","translation":"The new dress **fits** her body perfectly."}]

translation: The sound of heavy raindrops; rattling sound
meaning_filipino: Malakas at sunod-sunod na tunog ng pagpatak, tulad ng malakas na ulan sa yero, o pagkahulog ng maraming maliliit at matitigas na bagay.
original_explanation: 'Yung tunog ng P500 na barya na nalaglag mo sa sahig at nagkalat. Or 'yung sound ng malakas na ulan sa bubong ninyong yero na parang may nagma-marching. It's a chaotic, percussive sound. Hindi 'yung gentle pitter-patter, ito 'yung 'OMG, the sky is falling!' na patak.
usage_notes: Isang onomatopoeic na salita. Naglalarawan ito ng mas mabigat at mas natatanging tunog ng pagbagsak kaysa sa simpleng 'patak'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lakas ng **lagatak** ng ulan sa aming bubong na yero kagabi.","translation":"The **pattering sound** of the rain on our tin roof last night was so loud."},{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **lagatak** ng mga bato na gumulong sa dalisdis.","translation":"I heard the **rattling** of stones rolling down the slope."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na tama, wasto, o bagay para sa isang partikular na layunin, tao, okasyon, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: This is the Filipino word for 'it fits the vibe.' It's when your outfit is naaakma for the party's theme. It's the comment that is naaakma for the serious discussion. It's the salary that is naaakma for the job description (we wish!). The opposite is 'hindi akma', like wearing a gown to the palengke or making a 'sana all' joke at a funeral.
usage_notes: Ito ay nasa progresibong anyo ng pandiwang "umakma" ngunit madalas na gumagana bilang isang pang-uri.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang kasuotan ay **naaakma** sa pormal na okasyon.","translation":"Her attire is **suitable** for the formal occasion."},{"sentence":"Pumili ka ng mga salitang **naaakma** sa iyong mga kausap.","translation":"Choose words that are **appropriate** for the people you are talking to."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang direksyong kardinal na katapat ng timog, at siyang nasa kaliwa ng isang tao kung nakaharap sa silangan. Karaniwang tumutukoy sa hilagang bahagi ng isang lugar o bansa.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'norte', na nangangahulugang 'hilaga'.
original_explanation: It's the direction you point to when someone asks where Ilocos is. 'Tara, road trip sa Norte!' usually means Baguio, La Union, or Vigan. It's the opposite of 'South' kids, basically. If your life is going south, maybe it's time to head 'Norte' for a change of scenery.
usage_notes: Kadalasang ginagamit sa mga pangalan ng lugar (hal. Ilocos Norte, Camarines Norte) at sa pagbibigay ng direksyon, lalo na sa mas pormal o heograpikal na konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming magagandang tanawin sa **Norte**, tulad ng mga dalampasigan sa Ilocos.","translation":"There are many beautiful sights in the **North**, like the beaches in Ilocos."},{"sentence":"Ang hangin ay umiihip mula sa **Norte**.","translation":"The wind is blowing from the **North**."}]

translation: to be molded; to be shaped; to be formed
meaning_filipino: Ang mabigyan ng anyo, hugis, o katangian ang isang bagay o isang tao sa pamamagitan ng pagtuturo, pagsasanay, o karanasan.
original_explanation: This is what your parents, teachers, and life experiences do to you. You start as a lump of clay (or a fresh grad) and then life happens. You get shaped by deadlines, BPO night shifts, heartbreaks, and your lola's advice. "Dito ako nahubog" (This is where I was molded) is what you say about your first toxic job that taught you everything.
usage_notes: Can be used for both physical objects and abstract concepts like character, personality, or skills.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa pamamagitan ng masusing pagsasanay, **nahubog** ang kanyang talento sa pagpipinta.","translation":"Through careful training, her talent in painting **was molded**."},{"sentence":"Ang ating pagkatao ay **nahuhubog** ng mga karanasan natin sa buhay.","translation":"Our character **is shaped** by our life experiences."}]

translation: to show respect, to be respectful
meaning_filipino: Magpakita ng paggalang o pitagan sa isang tao, lalo na sa mga nakatatanda o may katungkulan.
etymology: Mula sa `mang-` at salitang ugat na `pitagan` (respect).
original_explanation: This is the opposite of being a 'bastos'. It's using 'po' and 'opo', doing the 'mano po', and generally not being a savage. It's the core of Filipino politeness that your lola insists you practice. "Mamitagan ka sa mga nakatatanda sa iyo."
usage_notes: Isang pormal at malalim na salita para sa pagpapakita ng paggalang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat kang **mamitagan** sa lahat ng oras, lalo na sa harap ng iyong mga guro.","translation":"You should **be respectful** at all times, especially in front of your teachers."},{"sentence":"Ang paggamit ng 'po' at 'opo' ay isang paraan ng **pamimitagan**.","translation":"Using 'po' and 'opo' is a way of **showing respect**."}]

translation: therefore; in that way; so that
meaning_filipino: Ginagamit bilang pang-ugnay upang ipahiwatig ang resulta, konklusyon, o layunin ng isang naunang pahayag.
etymology: Mula sa "sa" at "gayon" (like that/in that manner).
original_explanation: This is the formal "so" or "that's why" you use when you want to sound smart in a Filipino essay. "Nag-aral siyang mabuti; **sa gayon**, nakakuha siya ng mataas na marka." It connects cause and effect with a bit of class. It’s the "therefore" you use when you're trying to prove a point, whether in a debate or just explaining to your mom why you need a higher allowance.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa pormal na pagsulat at pananalita. Maaari itong palitan ng "kaya naman" o "dahil doon" sa impormal na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating magtipid **sa gayon** ay may magamit tayo sa oras ng kagipitan.","translation":"We need to save **so that** we have something to use in times of emergency."},{"sentence":"Umuulan nang malakas; **sa gayon**, ipinagpaliban muna ang laro.","translation":"It was raining hard; **therefore**, the game was postponed."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mas pinalambing at pinahabang bersyon ng "bebe," na pinagsamang "bebe" (baby) at "labs" (love). Ito ay isang matamis na tawagan para sa isang minamahal.
etymology: A portmanteau of 'bebe' (from baby) and 'labs' (a cutesy form of 'love').
original_explanation: The final evolution of 'baby'. It's when 'baby', 'bb', and 'bebe' are just not enough to contain your affection. 'Bebelabs' is 'bebe' + 'loves'. It’s the kind of term that makes other people in the jeepney roll their eyes. Use with caution and only with your certified ka-bebelabs.
usage_notes: Considered extremely sweet or sometimes cringey, depending on the context and the people involved.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Happy anniversary, **bebelabs**!","translation":"Happy anniversary, **baby love**!"},{"sentence":"Uwi ka na, miss na kita, **bebelabs**.","translation":"Come home already, I miss you, **bebelabs**."}]

meaning_filipino: Pilitin o utusan na huminto sa isang gawain, paggalaw, o operasyon.
original_explanation: This is what your mom yells when you and your sibling are fighting: "Patigilin niyo 'yan!" It's what you want to do to the alarm clock in the morning. It's the command form of "stop". The ultimate "awatin" move. "**Patigilin** mo na 'yang ka-drāma-han mo, please."
usage_notes: A very common causative verb. It means to cause something or someone else to stop, often with a sense of authority or urgency.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Patigilin** mo ang bata sa pag-iyak.","translation":"**Make** the child **stop** crying."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **patigilin** ang pagkalat ng maling impormasyon.","translation":"We need **to stop** the spread of false information."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang nagmula sa internet na tumutukoy sa "Skibidi Toilet," isang serye ng mga maiikling video na nagtatampok ng mga ulong lumalabas sa inidoro. Ginagamit din upang ilarawan ang anumang bagay na kakaiba, magulo, o walang katuturan na nauugnay sa meme.
etymology: Nag-ugat sa kantang "Skibidi" ng grupong Little Big, na kalaunan ay ginamit sa viral na serye sa YouTube na "Skibidi Toilet" ni DaFuq!?Boom!.
original_explanation: If you know, you know. It's the Gen Alpha/Z codeword for chaotic, nonsensical internet humor. It started as a YouTube series about singing toilet heads and became a global phenomenon that baffles millennials and boomers. "Anong pinapanood ng pamangkin ko? Puro Skibidi na lang!" It's the 2020s version of "Pen-Pineapple-Apple-Pen" – you don't understand it, but it's everywhere.
usage_notes: Isang napakabagong salitang slang na nauunawaan lamang ng mga pamilyar sa partikular na internet meme. Ang kahulugan nito ay lubos na nakadepende sa konteksto ng meme.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginagaya ng mga bata ang sayaw ng **Skibidi** Toilet.","translation":"The kids are imitating the dance from the **Skibidi** Toilet."},{"sentence":"Ang gulo ng video, parang **skibidi**.","translation":"The video is so chaotic, it's like **skibidi**."}]

translation: to show; to display; to demonstrate
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapamalas o paglalantad ng isang bagay upang makita o malaman ng iba.
original_explanation: The classic hugot line: "**Ipakita** mo, 'wag mong sabihin." It means "show me, don't just tell me." It's what you do with your new phone, your new haircut, your new skills, or your *resibo* (receipt/proof). It's the verb for "pics or it didn't happen."
usage_notes: A very common and versatile verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ipakita** mo sa akin ang ginawa mong proyekto.","translation":"**Show** me the project you made."},{"sentence":"Sa pamamagitan ng kanyang gawa, **ipinapakita** niya ang kanyang pagmamahal.","translation":"Through his actions, he **shows** his love."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng palabas na nagtatampok ng komedya, sayaw, at kadalasang may kasamang paghuhubad bilang paraan ng sining at aliwan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Ingles na "burlesque," na nagmula sa Italyanong "burlesco," na nangangahulugang "biro" o "panunuya."
original_explanation: Parang sexy dancing... but with *art*. Ito yung performance na pinagsasama ang comedy, sayaw, at a bit of tease. Hindi ito bastos, ito ay isang porma ng pagpapahayag. Think less "club dancer," more "Dita Von Teese sa isang napaka-eleganteng bathtub ng champagne."
usage_notes: Madalas na nauugnay sa mga palabas noong unang bahagi ng ika-20 siglo at kasalukuyang nakikita ang muling pagsikat bilang isang anyo ng sining.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging tanyag ang mga **burlesk** dancer noong dekada '50 sa Maynila.","translation":"**Burlesque** dancers became famous in the 1950s in Manila."}]

meaning_filipino: May kakayahang kumapit o dumikit nang mabilis at walang kahirap-hirap sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: This can be literal, like a good quality sticker or tape. Or it can be figurative, like that new officemate who instantly becomes your best friend after one coffee break. It can also be a 'hugot' term for people who get attached too easily: 'Bes, huwag kang masyadong madaling dumikit, baka masaktan ka lang.'
usage_notes: A descriptive phrase. Can be used literally for objects or figuratively for people's emotions or attachment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa pintura, **madaling dumikit** iyan sa damit.","translation":"Be careful with the paint, it's **easy to get on** (lit. easy to stick on) clothes."},{"sentence":"May mga taong **madaling dumikit** ang loob sa iyo, kahit kakakilala pa lang.","translation":"There are people who **get attached** to you easily, even if you've just met."}]

translation: aunt; a term of address for an older woman
meaning_filipino: Isang magalang na pantawag sa isang babaeng mas matanda, katumbas ng 'tiya' o 'ale'. Maaari ring tumukoy sa isang kamag-anak na kapatid na babae ng magulang.
original_explanation: Parang 'Tita' pero more classic and provincial feels. Ito 'yung tawag mo sa tindera sa palengke o sa kapitbahay mong laging may handang meryenda. 'Pabili po, Ali!'
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin bilang paggalang sa isang babaeng mas matanda, hindi kinakailangang kamag-anak. Maaaring ipagpalit sa 'ale'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magandang umaga po, **Ali** Maria.","translation":"Good morning, Ms. Maria."},{"sentence":"Patawad po, **Ali**, hindi ko po sinasadya.","translation":"I'm sorry, Ma'am, I didn't mean it."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hiram na salita na tumutukoy sa isang tao na lantad na o hayag na ang isang lihim, partikular na ang oryentasyong sekswal o pagkakakilanlan.
original_explanation: When the cat is out of the bag, or more specifically, when someone is no longer in the closet. "Out na si accla!" means your friend's secret is finally revealed, or they've come out. It can be about being gay, but also about a secret relationship, or who stole the last piece of leche flan.
usage_notes: Used in Taglish slang, often in the context of LGBTQ+ identity ('coming out') but has broadened to mean any kind of reveal or exposure of a secret.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huy, **out** na pala si Mark sa pamilya niya.","translation":"Hey, Mark is apparently **out** to his family now."},{"sentence":"Nang dahil sa tsismis, na-**out** tuloy na may jowa na si Sarah.","translation":"Because of the gossip, it was **revealed** that Sarah actually has a boyfriend."}]

translation: to play the guitar for someone; to serenade with a guitar
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtugtog ng gitara para sa isang tao o bagay; ang paggamit ng gitara sa pag-awit o pagharana.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you want to impress your crush, old-school style. Forget sending a Spotify playlist, you **gitarahin** them! It's the classic harana move. "Gitarahin mo nga ako ng paborito kong kanta." It can also mean to just play a song on the guitar.
usage_notes: Ang hulaping '-hin' ay ginagawang pandiwa ang pangngalang 'gitara', na tumutukoy sa kilos ng pagtugtog nito, kadalasan para sa isang tao o bagay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Balak niyang **gitarahin** ang nililigawan niya sa ilalim ng bintana nito.","translation":"He plans to **serenade** his crush with a guitar under her window."},{"sentence":"Puwede mo bang **gitarahin** 'yung bagong kanta ng Ben&Ben?","translation":"Can you **play** the new Ben&Ben song on the guitar?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bukas na istrukturang pabilog o hugis-itlog na may mga baitang ng upuan na nakapalibot sa isang gitnang espasyo, ginagamit para sa mga pagtatanghal o palabas.
original_explanation: Think of a concert venue, but make it ~classic~. It's that open-air place with seats going up in tiers, perfect for dramas, concerts, or even a university's graduation ceremony. The UP Diliman Amphitheater is a classic example.
usage_notes: Kadalasang tumutukoy sa mga malalaking panlabas na tanghalan, lalo na sa mga unibersidad at parke.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginanap ang konsiyerto sa sikat na **ampiteatro** ng unibersidad.","translation":"The concert was held at the university's famous **amphitheater**."},{"sentence":"Maraming tao ang nanood ng Lantern Parade sa **ampiteatro** ng UP.","translation":"Many people watched the Lantern Parade at the UP **amphitheater**."}]

meaning_filipino: Alisin o ibaba ang isang bagay o tao mula sa isang sasakyan.
etymology: From the root 'ibis' (to unload from a vehicle).
original_explanation: The official term for 'baba na po!' when you're getting off the jeepney and need to get your bayong of veggies from the roof. It's the act of unloading cargo, whether it's balikbayan boxes from a van or your friend who's had too much to drink from a Grab car.
usage_notes: This is the command/infinitive form. The root word 'ibis' (to unload) is a homonym of 'ibis' (the bird).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakisuyo, **ibisin** mo na ang mga kahon mula sa trak.","translation":"Please, **unload** the boxes from the truck."},{"sentence":"Saan natin **ibibisin** ang mga pasahero?","translation":"Where will we have the passengers **disembark**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ibaba o alisin ang karga mula sa isang sasakyan, lalagyan, o sistema.
original_explanation: Ito yung utos na 'Ibaba mo na 'yan!' in a more formal, Spanish-derived way. 'Hoy, **diskargahin** n'yo na 'yang mga gulay sa truck!' Pwede ring gamitin sa feelings: '**Diskargahin** mo na lahat ng galit mo, makikinig ako.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **diskargahin** ang mga pinamili mula sa kotse.","translation":"Help me **unload** the groceries from the car."},{"sentence":"Kailangang **diskargahin** ang lahat ng laman ng bodega para sa imbentaryo.","translation":"All the contents of the warehouse need to be **unloaded** for the inventory."}]

translation: to flee; to scram; to take off
meaning_filipino: Ang biglaang pag-alis o pagtakas mula sa isang lugar, karaniwang upang iwasan ang isang responsibilidad o problema.
etymology: From 'sibat' (spear), possibly alluding to the quick, straight motion of a thrown spear, hence a quick departure.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate "I'm out" move. It's when you sneak away from a boring family gathering, or when your friend disappears right when the bill arrives. "Saan na si Mark?" "Ayun, sumibat na, may utang pa naman sa 'kin." It’s the art of the ninja exit.
usage_notes: Carries a slightly informal, sometimes negative connotation of escaping or ditching.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sumibat** agad ang magnanakaw nang makita ang pulis.","translation":"The thief immediately **fled** when he saw the police."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **sumibat** sa iyong mga responsibilidad.","translation":"Don't **run away** from your responsibilities."}]

meaning_filipino: Madaling makita, mapansin, o mahalata; napakalinaw o lantad.
original_explanation: Like that one relative in a bright orange shirt at a funeral. Or the new pimple on your nose on the day of your big date. It's something that screams for attention, whether you want it to or not. 'Yung ugali niyang mayabang, litaw na litaw kahit sa chat lang.
usage_notes: The repetition of 'litaw' intensifies the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Litaw na litaw** ang pula niyang buhok sa gitna ng karamihan.","translation":"Her red hair was **very prominent** in the middle of the crowd."},{"sentence":"Sa kanyang mga kilos, **litaw na litaw** ang kanyang pagiging magalang.","translation":"In his actions, his politeness was **very visible**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking yunit pang-administratibo ng isang bansa, karaniwang nasa labas ng sentrong kalakhan o kabisera. Tumutukoy rin sa mga lugar sa labas ng Maynila na may mas payak na pamumuhay.
original_explanation: The place you dream about during a toxic week in Manila. It's the land of fresh air, fresh buko juice, and your lola asking why you're still single. It’s both a geographical location and a state of mind associated with rest, family, and a slower internet connection.
usage_notes: Often used in contrast to 'Maynila' or 'the city'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Uuwi kami sa **probinsya** para sa Pasko.","translation":"We will go home to the **province** for Christmas."},{"sentence":"Masarap ang buhay sa **probinsya**, payapa at hindi magulo.","translation":"Life in the **province** is good, it's peaceful and not chaotic."}]

translation: being two-timed; act of being unfaithful to two or more people
meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay na pagkakaroon ng romantikong ugnayan sa dalawa o higit pang tao, na nagdudulot ng panloloko o kawalan ng katapatan.
etymology: From pag- (gerund prefix) + sa- (repetition) + salawahan (unfaithful, two-timer), which comes from dalawa (two).
original_explanation: When your 'main' finds out about your 'side-chick', or when you're caught juggling two job offers and they both rescind. It's the messy, complicated art of playing the field and getting caught. Classic teleserye plotline.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to infidelity involving more than one other partner, or a pattern of it. 'Salawahan' is the adjective for a person who does this.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagsasalawahan** ang naging sanhi ng kanilang paghihiwalay.","translation":"His **act of being unfaithful with multiple partners** was the cause of their separation."},{"sentence":"Hindi na ako magtataka kung mahuli siyang muli sa **pagsasalawahan**.","translation":"I won't be surprised if he gets caught **two-timing** again."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paglalagay ng lason sa pagkain, inumin, o sa anumang bagay na may layuning makapinsala o pumatay.
original_explanation: The evil villain verb. It's what you do when you want to poison someone's drink in a telenovela. Figuratively, it means to poison someone's mind with bad ideas or lies. 'Nilason mo ang isip niya!' (You poisoned his mind!).
usage_notes: An object-focus verb. The object is the person or thing being poisoned.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May masamang balak siyang **lasuhin** ang hari.","translation":"He has an evil plan to **poison** the king."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **lasuhin** ng inggit ang iyong puso.","translation":"Don't let envy **poison** your heart."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pormal na talumpati o aralin na ibinibigay sa isang grupo ng tao, karaniwan sa isang akademikong tagpuan, upang magturo ng isang partikular na paksa.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'lectura' o Ingles na 'lecture'.
original_explanation: Ito yung 1.5 hours na monologo ng prof mo na kailangan mong i-record kasi antok ka na pero may quiz next meeting. O kaya yung sermon ng nanay mo pag-uwi mong madaling araw, 'yun ang ultimate 'lektyur'.
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang hiram na salita na ginagamit sa mga akademikong at pormal na tagpuan. Madalas na binabaybay bilang 'lecture' sa kaswal na pagsulat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi ako nakapasok sa klase, kaya hihiramin ko na lang ang notes mo sa **lektyur**.","translation":"I couldn't attend the class, so I'll just borrow your notes from the **lecture**."},{"sentence":"Ang **lektyur** tungkol sa quantum physics ay masyadong malalim para sa akin.","translation":"The **lecture** about quantum physics was too deep for me."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang modernong katawagan para sa isang lalaki na nagpapakita ng emosyonal na sensitibidad at interes sa sining at kultura, ngunit kadalasan ay ginagamit ito upang manipulahin ang damdamin ng iba para sa pansariling kapakinabangan, partikular sa romantikong konteksto.
original_explanation: He's not the typical 'bad boy'. He's the guy who quotes poetry, loves indie films, and sends you 'kamusta ka?' texts at 2 AM. He seems deep and sensitive, but 'yan ang style niya ng panlalandi. He'll make you feel special with his emotional vulnerability, then ghost you when he gets what he wants. It's emotional manipulation with a tote bag and a ukulele. Ingat, sis!
usage_notes: A modern slang term used in dating and social media culture. Carries a negative connotation of manipulative behavior disguised as sensitivity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Akala ko mabait siya, pero isa lang pala siyang **softboy**.","translation":"I thought he was nice, but he turned out to be just a **softboy**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala sa mga matatamis na salita niyan, baka **softboy** 'yan.","translation":"Don't believe his sweet words, he might be a **softboy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o gawain na nagpapakita ng pagiging delusyonal o pag-iisip na malayo sa katotohanan; hango sa salitang balbal na 'delulu'.
etymology: A recent coinage from the English slang 'delulu' (delusional) + the Filipino circumfix ka-...-an.
original_explanation: This is the official noun form of being 'delulu'. It's the whole universe you've created in your head where your crush likes you back, you've won the lottery, and you're the main character. 'The delulu is the solulu' is the motto. It's your entire vibe when you're manifesting something a little too hard.
usage_notes: Very new, Gen Z slang. Used exclusively in informal, online, or very casual conversations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na 'yang **ka-deluluhan** mo, hindi ka niya talaga gusto.","translation":"Stop your **foolishness** (delusions), he/she doesn't really like you."},{"sentence":"Ang dami niyang **ka-deluluhan** sa buhay, akala niya mananalo siya sa lotto.","translation":"He has so many **absurd ideas** in life, he thinks he'll win the lottery."}]

translation: to have pity on; to feel compassion for
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkilos ng pagpapakita o pagdama ng habag o awa para sa isang tao o bagay.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'habag' at hulaping '-in'.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of 'habag'. It's what you do when you see your officemate na puyat na puyat sa OT. You don't just feel bad, you might actually buy them coffee. "Habagin mo naman, pagod na 'yan." It’s turning that "kawawa naman" feeling into a small act of kindness.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa anyong pautos o pakiusap, na humihiling sa isang tao na magpakita ng awa.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Habagin** mo ang pulubing nanlilimos sa daan.","translation":"**Have pity on** the beggar asking for alms on the street."},{"sentence":"Panginoon, **habagin** mo po kami.","translation":"Lord, **have mercy on** us."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglalagay ng palaman o pinaghalong sangkap sa loob ng isang pangunahing pagkain, tulad ng manok, isda, o sili, bago ito lutuin.
original_explanation: The ultimate "it's what's on the inside that counts" of Pinoy cooking. You take a perfectly good chicken or fish, debone it like a pro (or a contortionist), and then stuff it with a delicious mix of ground meat, raisins, and whatever else is in the pantry. It's the Noche Buena star player that requires a PhD in patience to prepare.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to stuffing food items, often for special occasions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpaturo si Ana sa kanyang lola kung paano **magrelyeno** ng bangus.","translation":"Ana asked her grandmother to teach her how to **stuff** a milkfish."},{"sentence":"Para sa Pasko, plano nilang **magrelyeno** ng manok.","translation":"For Christmas, they plan to **stuff** a chicken."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga bagay, katangian, o gawain na angkop, dinisenyo, o laan para sa mga babae.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "pan-" at salitang ugat na "babae". Ang /n/ sa "pan-" ay nagiging /m/ dahil sa kasunod na tunog na /b/.
original_explanation: Anything labeled 'pambabae'—from clothes to scents to that specific CR sa mall. It's the opposite of 'panlalaki'. Think pink, floral, or anything society has decided is 'for girls only', even though we know anyone can rock a floral shirt.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May hiwalay na linya para sa mga **pambabae** na damit sa department store.","translation":"There's a separate line for **women's** clothing at the department store."},{"sentence":"Ang pabango na ito ay may amoy na medyo **pambabae**.","translation":"This perfume has a scent that is a bit **feminine**."}]
