meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa hindi kanais-nais na amoy o lasa ng lumang mantika, gata, o anumang pagkaing matagal nang nakaimbak at nagkaroon ng kemikal na pagbabago.
original_explanation: That weird, funky smell your cooking oil gets when it's been sitting in the pantry since the last presidential election. It's the flavor profile of 'Ay, sayang itapon' but your taste buds are screaming 'WHY?!'. It's the reason your lola can tell if the adobo is fresh just by sniffing the air.
usage_notes: Often used for oils, coconut milk (gata), and fatty foods that have gone bad.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Amoy **anta** na ang mantikang ginamit mo kahapon.","translation":"The oil you used yesterday smells **rancid** already."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo nang kainin 'yan, may lasang **anta** na.","translation":"Don't eat that anymore, it has a **stale** taste."}]

meaning_filipino: Maghagis o magtapon ng likido, tulad ng tubig, sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: What happens during the San Juan festival when everyone has a water gun or a bucket. It's also what a passing bus does to you on a rainy day when you're waiting for a jeep. It's a more forceful, directed version of `magsabog`, but for liquids.
usage_notes: Specifically used for splashing liquids.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula ang mga bata na **magsaboy** ng tubig sa isa't isa.","translation":"The children started **to splash** water at each other."},{"sentence":"Nag-ingat siyang huwag **magsaboy** ng mainit na sabaw habang inihahain ito.","translation":"She was careful not **to splash** the hot soup while serving it."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang mapanirang insekto o hayop na umaatake sa mga pananim, hayop, o tao; isang malawakang nakakahawang sakit; isang salitang bulalas na nagpapahayag ng pagkayamot.
original_explanation: Can mean three things: 1) The actual pests like ipis and daga you want to obliterate with Baygon. 2) A historical plague, like the Black Death. 3) The most common use: A mild curse you shout when you stub your toe, your wifi dies during a Zoom call, or your crush leaves you on 'seen'. 'Peste!' is the cleaner cousin of P.I.
usage_notes: Very versatile. Its meaning is highly dependent on context, from literal agricultural pests to a common, mild expletive.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Peste**! Naiwan ko ang wallet ko sa bahay!","translation":"**Darn it**! I left my wallet at home!"},{"sentence":"Maraming **peste** ang sumisira sa mga palayan.","translation":"Many **pests** are destroying the rice fields."},{"sentence":"Ang Itim na **Peste** ay kumitil ng milyun-milyong buhay sa Europa.","translation":"The Black **Plague** claimed millions of lives in Europe."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang patag na piraso ng kahoy, metal, o salamin na nakakabit sa dingding o bahagi ng isang kabinet, na ginagamit bilang patungan ng mga bagay tulad ng libro, palamuti, o pagkain.
original_explanation: It's where you put your books to pretend you read them, your Funko Pops to show your personality, or your collection of condiments in the kitchen. The 'estante' is the unsung hero of home organization, fighting a never-ending battle against 'kalat'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiayos ang mga libro sa **estante**.","translation":"Please arrange the books on the **shelf**."},{"sentence":"Puno na ng palamuti ang kanyang **estante** sa sala.","translation":"Her **shelf** in the living room is full of decorations."}]

translation: to strike, to hit, to punch
meaning_filipino: Ang pagtama o paghampas nang malakas sa isang tao o bagay, karaniwan gamit ang kamao.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'buntal' at gitlaping '-um-'.
original_explanation: ‘Yung eksena sa action movie na biglang sinuntok ng bida ‘yung kontrabida. That's `bumuntal`. It's a forceful hit, usually a punch. Not to be confused with `tumapik` (a light tap) or `dumampi` (a gentle touch). This one has force.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa isang malakas na pagtama, madalas gamit ang kamao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Galit na galit ang lalaki kaya't **bumuntal** siya sa pader.","translation":"The man was so angry that he **punched** the wall."},{"sentence":"Nagulat ang lahat nang bigla siyang **bumuntal** sa mesa.","translation":"Everyone was shocked when he suddenly **struck** the table."}]

meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng pisikal na kakayahan o ng pagkakataong mangusap o gamitin ang bibig upang bumigkas ng mga salita.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `makapag-` (kakayahan) at salitang-ugat na `salita`.
original_explanation: This is what happens after your dentist gives you anesthesia and your mouth is numb for hours. 'Kailan kaya ako ulit makapagsalita nang maayos?' It can also be about having the opportunity to speak in a meeting ('Wala na ba akong chance makapagsalita?'), or mustering the courage to speak up for yourself. It’s about the ability—physical or situational—to use your voice.
usage_notes: Naiiba ito sa `makapagsabi` na tumutukoy sa pagsasabi ng isang *partikular* na bagay. Ang `makapagsalita` ay tumutukoy sa pangkalahatang akto o kakayahan ng pagsasalita.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa sobrang gulat, hindi siya **makapagsalita**.","translation":"Due to extreme shock, she couldn't **speak**."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng operasyon, matagal bago siya muling **nakapagsalita**.","translation":"After the operation, it was a long time before he **was able to speak** again."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng putong o takip sa ulo na binubuo ng isang mahabang tela na ibinabalot sa ulo, karaniwang isinusuot ng mga lalaki sa ilang bahagi ng Timog Asya at Gitnang Silangan.
etymology: From Persian `dulband` via Turkish `tülbent` and English/French `turban`.
original_explanation: More than just a fashion accessory for your 'bad hair day'. It's a significant cultural and religious headwear for many, like our Sikh friends. But also, yes, it's what you wear to look chic while doing your skincare routine.
usage_notes: A direct loanword, used in both formal and informal contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga Sikh ay kilala sa pagsusuot ng **turban**.","translation":"Sikhs are known for wearing a **turban**."},{"sentence":"Bumili siya ng isang makulay na **turban** para sa buhok niya.","translation":"She bought a colorful **turban** for her hair."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging simple, hindi kumplikado, payak, o walang labis na palamuti.
etymology: From ka- + simple + -han. 'Simple' is a loanword from Spanish 'simple'.
original_explanation: It's the Jollibee chickenjoy—no fancy sauces needed. It's wearing pambahay all day. It's finding joy in a cup of 3-in-1 coffee. Kasimplihan is the beauty in the uncomplicated, the opposite of your friend's dramatic love life. It's the 'less is more' aesthetic before it was cool.
usage_notes: Refers to the quality of being simple, either in appearance, character, or complexity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinahangaan ko ang **kasimplihan** ng kanyang pamumuhay sa probinsya.","translation":"I admire the **simplicity** of her life in the province."},{"sentence":"Sa kabila ng kanyang yaman, nanatili ang **kasimplihan** sa kanyang puso.","translation":"Despite his wealth, **simplicity** remained in his heart."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pananalita na gumagamit ng mga salitang kabaligtaran ng tunay na kahulugan, karaniwang may layuning manlibak, mangutya, o magpahiwatig ng paghamak.
original_explanation: Ito yung "Wow, ang galing mo talaga!" na sinasabi mo sa kaibigan mong na-late ng isang oras. It's the language of savage friends and disappointed parents. The tone is everything. It's verbal side-eye.
usage_notes: Isang uri ng berbal na kabalintunaan (verbal irony). Ang tono at konteksto ay mahalaga upang maunawaan ito bilang sarkasmo.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **pang-uuyam** ang kanyang mga komento tungkol sa gobyerno.","translation":"His comments about the government were full of **sarcasm**."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko maintindihan kung seryoso siya o puro **pang-uuyam** lang ang sinasabi niya.","translation":"I can't tell if he's serious or if what he's saying is just pure **mockery**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na hiwa, ukit, o marka na ginawa sa isang ibabaw, karaniwan ay gamit ang isang matalim na bagay. Maaari ring tumukoy sa pagaspas na tunog ng paghiwa.
etymology: Likely onomatopoeic, from the sound of scratching or cutting.
original_explanation: Imagine you're a prisoner counting the days by scratching lines on the wall. Each one of those lines is a 'gutgot'. It's also the sound your rusty gate makes, or the sound of a saw cutting wood. It's that gritty, scratchy, friction-filled action or its result.
usage_notes: Can refer to the mark itself or the sound/action of making the mark. 'Ginutgot' (verb) means to have made a notch or incision.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May mga **gutgot** sa puno na nagsasabing may mga nauna nang umakyat dito.","translation":"There are **notches** on the tree indicating that others have climbed it before."},{"sentence":"Ang ingay ng **gutgot** ng lagari ay umalingawngaw sa buong baryo.","translation":"The sound of the **saw's serration** echoed throughout the village."}]

meaning_filipino: Maging matamis ang lasa o katangian.
etymology: From 'amis', an archaic or regional term for sweetness, distinct from the more common 'tamis'.
original_explanation: A rare, almost poetic way to say something turned sweet. Think of it as the vintage filter version of 'tumamis.' You'd use this to describe a fruit ripening on the vine, or perhaps a person's bitter attitude finally softening. It's got that old-timey, probinsya charm.
usage_notes: This is a rare and somewhat literary word. The more common term is 'tumamis'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa paglipas ng mga araw, ang hilaw na mangga ay unti-unting **umamis**.","translation":"As the days passed, the unripe mango gradually **became sweet**."},{"sentence":"**Umamis** ang kanyang ngiti nang makita niya ako.","translation":"Her smile **turned sweet** when she saw me."}]

meaning_filipino: Labis na masama; sukdulan sa kasamaan o pagkakaroon ng negatibong katangian.
original_explanation: When someone steals your lunch from the office fridge, or when the wifi dies during a crucial online meeting. That's not just 'masama', that's **napakasama**. It's the final boss level of bad vibes.
usage_notes: A strong word used to denote extreme negativity in character, quality, or effect.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagtatapon ng basura sa ilog ay isang **napakasamang** gawain.","translation":"Throwing trash in the river is a **very bad** habit."},{"sentence":"**Napakasama** ng ugali niya kaya walang may gustong makipagkaibigan sa kanya.","translation":"His attitude is **so bad** that no one wants to be friends with him."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kardinal na bilang na kasunod ng labing-anim at bago ang labing-walo, na isinusulat bilang 17.
etymology: Mula sa `labi` (sobra) + `na` + `pito` (pito). Pinaikli sa `labing-pito` at naging `labimpito`.
original_explanation: The number 17. The awkward teenage year. It's one more than sweet sixteen, one less than being legal. In Tagalog numbers, it's just "ten and seven" mashed together.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Labimpito** na siya sa darating niyang kaarawan.","translation":"She will be **seventeen** on her upcoming birthday."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang istrukturang tinitirhan ng isang kolonya ng mga pukyutan (laywan), kung saan sila gumagawa at nag-iimbak ng pulot-pukyutan.
original_explanation: The headquarters of the hardest working BPO employees in the animal kingdom. It's a factory, a nursery, and a palace for the queen, all in one. Don't mess with it unless you want to be on the receiving end of a thousand tiny, flying security guards. The original 'buzz-y' workplace.
usage_notes: "Bahay-pukyutan" is a more common synonym. "Laywan" itself is a less common term for bee than "pukyutan" or "bubuyog".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May malaking **bahay-laywan** na nakasabit sa sanga ng puno.","translation":"There is a large **beehive** hanging from the tree branch."}]

translation: to have someone give birth; to act as a midwife for someone
meaning_filipino: Tulungan, pangasiwaan, o asistihan ang isang ina sa kanyang proseso ng panganganak.
original_explanation: This is what a midwife (hilot or kumadrona) or an OB-GYN does. They don't give birth themselves, but they cause the birth to happen successfully by assisting the mother. It's the ultimate 'group project' where you're the project manager for a baby's arrival.
usage_notes: Causative verb. To cause someone to have a child ('anak'). It implies facilitation or assistance in the birthing process.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang sikat na doktor na iyon ang **papag-anakin** sa aking asawa.","translation":"That famous doctor is the one who will **assist my wife in giving birth**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isara ang isang pinto, kahon, o anumang bagay gamit ang kandado upang hindi mabuksan.
original_explanation: The adult version of "close the door." It's what you frantically do at night while remembering all the horror movies you've watched. It's also what you do to your heart after a bad breakup. #KinandadoAngPuso
usage_notes: Can refer to locking with a key, a padlock, or any locking mechanism.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **magkandado** ng pinto bago ka umalis.","translation":"Don't forget to **lock** the door before you leave."},{"sentence":"**Nagkandado** siya sa kanyang kuwarto at ayaw lumabas.","translation":"She **locked** herself in her room and doesn't want to come out."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pakiramdam ng pagkasawa o pagkasuya sa lasa ng isang pagkain, lalo na kung ito ay matamis o mataba, dahil sa labis na pagkain nito.
original_explanation: That feeling you get after the 5th piece of leche flan or the 10th slice of lechon. It was delicious at first, but now you can't even look at it. That's 'umay'. It's food-related burnout. It can also be used figuratively for being sick of a person, a song, or a situation. "Nakaka-umay na 'yang K-drama na 'yan, paulit-ulit ang plot!"
usage_notes: Primarily used for food but is now widely used figuratively to express being sick and tired of anything repetitive. The verb form is 'naumay' and the adjective is 'nakakaumay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Grabe ang **umay** ko sa lahat ng matatamis na handa sa Pasko.","translation":"I have an intense **cloying satiety** from all the sweet dishes served during Christmas."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman ko ang **umay** sa sobrang pagkain ng cake.","translation":"I felt **palate fatigue** from eating too much cake."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pangkalahatang kalagayan ng panahon sa isang lugar sa loob ng mahabang panahon, kasama ang temperatura, hangin, at pag-ulan.
original_explanation: Hindi ito 'yung 'weather' na pabago-bago na parang mood ng jowa mo. Ang klima ay 'yung overall personality ng panahon sa isang lugar. For example, tropical ang klima sa Pinas, kaya laging mainit at humid—parang laging may free sauna session paglabas mo ng bahay.
usage_notes: Madalas ipagkamali sa 'panahon' (weather), na tumutukoy sa kondisyon sa mas maikling panahon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagbabago ng **klima** ay isang seryosong isyu sa buong mundo.","translation":"**Climate** change is a serious global issue."},{"sentence":"Ang Pilipinas ay may tropikal na **klima**.","translation":"The Philippines has a tropical **climate**."}]

translation: to cause to drag or scrape on a surface
meaning_filipino: Hayaang humagod o kumiskis ang isang bagay sa isang ibabaw, lalo na sa lupa o sahig.
original_explanation: That cringey feeling when you drag something heavy and it makes that horrible scratching sound on the floor. Or when you're wearing a long gown and you have to be careful not to isayad the hem in the mud. It's the act of something touching and dragging along a lower surface. Also what happens to the bottom of a lowered car on a hump. *krrrrk*
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-angat mo 'yang sako, huwag mong **isayad** sa sahig.","translation":"Please lift that sack, don't **drag** it **on the floor**."},{"sentence":"Nag-ingat siyang huwag **isayad** ang bago niyang sapatos sa putik.","translation":"He was careful not to let his new shoes **scrape** on the mud."}]

translation: to make (it) more tense; to make taut
meaning_filipino: Gawing mas mahigpit o mas matindi ang pagkakabanat ng isang bagay tulad ng lubid o alambre; pataasin ang tensyon.
original_explanation: This is a deep cut. It's like tightening a guitar string to get the right note. 'Pabagtingan mo pa ang tali' means 'Make the rope more taut.' Metaphorically, when the boss enters the room during a chismis session, the atmosphere can 'pabagtingan'—become more tense. It's a rare word but very precise.
usage_notes: A less common word, often used in technical or specific contexts like music (tuning strings) or construction (tightening ropes/wires). Can also be used metaphorically for emotional or situational tension.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **pabagtingan** ang mga kawad ng kuryente para hindi lumawag.","translation":"The electric wires need **to be made more taut** so they don't sag."},{"sentence":"Ang pagdating ng hindi inaasahang bisita ay lalo pang nagpa**bagting** sa sitwasyon.","translation":"The arrival of the unexpected guest made the situation even more **tense**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marahan at maingat na pagdampi at paggalaw ng kamay sa ibabaw ng isang bagay o balat, karaniwang nagpapahiwatig ng pag-aalaga, pag-alo, o pagpapakalma.
original_explanation: This is that gentle back rub your mom gives you when you're not feeling well. It's how you pet a cat to make it purr. It’s a gesture of comfort, affection, or soothing. It's the physical form of "there, there."
usage_notes: Connotes gentleness and care. Similar to 'haplos' but can also mean to apply something thinly, like oil.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatulog ang bata dahil sa marahang **paghagod** ng ina sa kanyang likod.","translation":"The child fell asleep because of the mother's gentle **stroking** of his back."},{"sentence":"Isang **paghagod** sa buhok ang paraan niya ng pagpapakita ng pagmamahal.","translation":"A **caress** of the hair is his way of showing affection."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang doktor na dalubhasa sa pag-aalaga ng mga buntis, sa proseso ng panganganak, at sa kalagayan ng ina pagkatapos manganak.
original_explanation: Same as 'obstetrician', but this is the 'Tagalized' version. This is how we spell it when we're trying to make it fit our own alphabet. The go-to doctor for every 'mom-to-be'.
usage_notes: This is the common, Filipinized spelling. Often used interchangeably with the English spelling and the abbreviation 'O.B.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinayo ng **obstetrisyan** na magpahinga ang buntis.","translation":"The **obstetrician** advised the pregnant woman to rest."},{"sentence":"Magaling ang napili naming **obstetrisyan** para sa panganganak ni misis.","translation":"The **obstetrician** we chose for my wife's delivery is very good."}]

meaning_filipino: (1) Maramihan ng butones; mga piyesang ginagamit upang isara ang damit. (2) Isang taong nagtatrabaho sa otel na tumutulong sa mga bisita, lalo na sa pagbubuhat ng bagahe.
original_explanation: (1) The plural of your shirt's best friend. Sila yung mga kumakapit 'pag tumataba ka na. (2) The guy in the hotel lobby with the cool uniform. He's your first point of contact for help with your luggage, basically the frontliner of guest services. From the Spanish word for bellboy.
usage_notes: This word has two distinct meanings, both from Spanish. The context usually makes it clear which is meant. The "bellboy" meaning is less common now, with "bellboy" being used directly.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayusin mo ang mga **botones** ng polo mo.","translation":"Fix the **buttons** of your polo shirt."},{"sentence":"Tinawag ng manager ang **botones** para tulungan kami sa mga maleta.","translation":"The manager called the **bellboy** to help us with the suitcases."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang makapal at mahiblang balat ng bunga ng niyog na ginagamit sa pagpapakintab ng sahig.
original_explanation: The OG floor polisher. Before vacuum cleaners and mops, we had the bunot. It's the reason many Pinoys have strong legs and shiny floors. It's basically a CrossFit workout and house cleaning rolled into one. You skate on it to make the floorboards gleam.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gamitin mo ang **bunot** para kuminis ang sahig na kahoy.","translation":"Use the **coconut husk** to polish the wooden floor."}]

translation: to pull the trigger; to strum lightly; to nudge
meaning_filipino: Ang bahagyang paghila o pagpindot gamit ang dulo ng daliri, tulad ng pagkalabit sa gatilyo ng baril, kuwerdas ng gitara, o pagsundot sa isang tao upang makuha ang atensyon.
original_explanation: The action your finger does right before you send that risky 'u up?' text. Or what you do to a guitar string to see if it's in tune. It can be a gentle nudge to get your friend's attention, or the much more serious act of pulling a trigger. It's all about that quick, decisive finger movement.
usage_notes: Has multiple contexts: firearms (pulling a trigger), musical instruments (plucking a string), and getting someone's attention (nudging/poking).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nanginginig ang kanyang kamay nang **kumalbit** siya ng gatilyo.","translation":"His hand was shaking when he **pulled** the trigger."},{"sentence":"**Kumalbit** siya sa balikat ko para makuha ang atensyon ko.","translation":"He **nudged** my shoulder to get my attention."}]

translation: to test; to try on; to prove
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagsasagawa ng pagsubok o pagpapatunay sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: Basically the same as 'prubahan', just a different spelling based on 'pruweba'. It's like choosing between 'color' and 'colour'. You use this when you want to sound a bit more... specific. "Sige, pruebahan natin kung totoo nga yang sinasabi mo."
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang variant ng 'prubahan'. Ang kahulugan ay magkatulad.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **pruebahan** ang iyong sarili sa bagong trabaho.","translation":"You need to **prove** yourself at the new job."},{"sentence":"Gusto mo bang **pruebahan** itong sapatos?","translation":"Do you want to **try on** these shoes?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan kung saan wala nang natitira sa isang bagay na dati'y mayroon; pagkaubos ng isang suplay.
original_explanation: The official feeling of panic when the Grab driver says "Ma'am/Sir, maubusan na po tayo ng gas." Or that tragic moment at the buffet when you see the last piece of leche flan get taken right before you. It's the "OMG, wala na?!" of the Filipino experience.
usage_notes: Often used to express that a supply of something has been depleted, affecting the subject. The focus is on the person/entity experiencing the lack.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumila kami nang matagal para sa bigas, pero **naubusan** pa rin kami.","translation":"We lined up for a long time for the rice, but we still **ran out** (of supply before our turn)."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpapagabi sa palengke at baka **maubusan** ka ng sariwang isda.","translation":"Don't go to the market late or you might **run out** of fresh fish to buy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kasuotang pang-itaas na gawa sa makapal na tela o niniting na sinulid, karaniwang isinusuot para sa proteksyon laban sa lamig.
original_explanation: The official uniform in BPO offices and movie theaters because the AC is set to 'Antarctica'. Also your go-to outfit for Baguio trips and for hiding the fact that you've gained a bit of holiday weight.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magdala ka ng **sweter** kung manonood tayo ng sine, dahil sobrang lamig doon.","translation":"Bring a **sweater** if we're going to watch a movie, because it's super cold in there."}]

meaning_filipino: Magkaloob ng awtoridad, kakayahan, o karapatan sa isang tao o grupo upang kumilos o magpasya.
original_explanation: This is what happens when the boss makes you the team lead for a project. You're given the power! It's the official act of giving someone the authority or the means to do something. Parang special power of attorney, or when your parents leave you in charge of the house (and the remote control). To empower, to greenlight, to give the keys to the kingdom.
usage_notes: Used in legal, political, corporate, and social contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang batas ay naglalayong **bigyang-kapangyarihan** ang mga kababaihan sa lipunan.","translation":"The law aims to **empower** women in society."},{"sentence":"**Binigyang-kapangyarihan** ng CEO ang manager na pumirma ng mga kontrata.","translation":"The CEO **authorized** the manager to sign contracts."}]

translation: I give up!; Say it already!
meaning_filipino: Isang kolokyal na ekspresyon na nangangahulugang pagsuko sa isang hulaan o paghiling sa isang tao na sabihin na ang isang lihim o sagot.
etymology: Hango sa salitang Espanyol na 'ceder' (sumuko), na inangkop sa isang mapaglarong ekspresyong Tagalog.
original_explanation: The ultimate "I give up!" in a guessing game. It's what you scream when your friend is being pabitin with the chismis and you just can't take the suspense anymore. "Ano na, spill the tea! Sirit na!"
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa mga laro tulad ng Pinoy Henyo o kapag sinusubukang kumuha ng tsismis mula sa isang tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayoko nang manghula, **sirit na**! Ano ba talaga ang sagot?","translation":"I don't want to guess anymore, **I give up**! What is the answer, really?"},{"sentence":"Ang tagal mo namang sabihin ang chismis. **Sirit na**!","translation":"You're taking so long to tell the gossip. **Say it already**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang pag-ilag o paglayo sa isang tao, bagay, o sitwasyon.
original_explanation: The verb form of your ninja moves. This is what you do to toxic people, your ex, or that one piece of chicharon when you're on a diet. 'Iwasan ang stress' is easier said than done, especially in Manila traffic.
usage_notes: The object-focused verb form of 'iwas'. `Umiwas` is the actor-focused form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat mong **iwasan** ang mga taong nagdudulot sa iyo ng stress.","translation":"You should **avoid** people who cause you stress."},{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang **iwasan** ang matatamis na pagkain.","translation":"He/She is trying to **avoid** sweet foods."}]

meaning_filipino: Mamagitan sa isang hindi pagkakasundo upang malutas ito; gampanan ang papel ng isang arbitro.
original_explanation: When your two besties are fighting and you're the designated peacemaker. Your job is to listen to both sides of the chismis, weigh the evidence (screenshots, mostly), and try to make them friends again. 'Arbitrahan mo nga sila' is the official request to become the group's UN peacekeeper.
usage_notes: A formal term used in legal, business, or diplomatic contexts, but can be used informally for mediating any dispute.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangang **arbitrahan** ng Department of Labor ang isyu sa pagitan ng mga manggagawa at ng kumpanya.","translation":"The Department of Labor needs to **arbitrate** the issue between the workers and the company."},{"sentence":"Sino ang mag-a-**arbitrahan** sa away ng mag-asawa?","translation":"Who will **mediate** the couple's fight?"}]

translation: To ride on; to go along with
meaning_filipino: Tumuloy o sumakay sa isang sasakyan. Ginagamit din sa matalinghagang paraan para sa pagsang-ayon o paglahok sa isang usapan o kalakaran.
original_explanation: This is what you do to a jeep, bus, or MRT when you're late for your BPO shift. It's also what your friend does to your 'hugot' or joke—they 'ride along' with it. 'Sakyan mo na lang ang trip niya' means just go with their flow, even if it's weird.
usage_notes: The -an suffix makes the object (the vehicle or the topic) the focus of the action. It implies participation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sakyan** mo na ang huling biyahe ng bus pauwi.","translation":"**Get on** the last bus trip going home."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **sakyan** ang mga tsismis na naririnig mo.","translation":"Don't **go along with** the rumors you are hearing."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang alternatibong baybay para sa 'magnetiko'; nagtataglay ng katangian ng isang magnet.
original_explanation: This is the "shortcut" or sometimes "conyo" spelling of 'magnetiko'. It's like choosing 'pre' instead of 'pare'. It means the same thing—having that attractive pull—but with a slightly more modern, English-influenced flavor.
usage_notes: A less common, alternative spelling of 'magnetiko'. 'Magnetiko' (from Spanish) is generally considered more standard in formal Filipino, while 'magnetik' (from English) is also understood and used, especially in technical or casual contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating pag-aralan ang '**magnetik** field' ng mundo.","translation":"We need to study the world's '**magnetic** field'."},{"sentence":"Ang '**magnetik** levitation' ang prinsipyo sa likod ng ilang modernong tren.","translation":"**Magnetic** levitation is the principle behind some modern trains."}]

meaning_filipino: Magbigay ng tugon o kasagutan sa isang tanong, tawag, sulat, o anumang anyo ng komunikasyon.
original_explanation: The most basic action in any conversation, chat, or recitation. But it has levels. There's the quick 'Yes?' to a call, the thesis-level explanation in an exam, and the dreaded 'K' your partner sends. Lahat 'yan, technically, ay pag-sagot.
usage_notes: A fundamental verb in Tagalog. Can also mean 'to take responsibility for' or 'to shoulder the cost of' in certain contexts (e.g., 'Ako ang sasagot sa lahat ng gastusin.').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bakit hindi ka **sumagot** sa tawag ko kanina?","translation":"Why didn't you **answer** my call earlier?"},{"sentence":"Hindi lahat ng tanong ay kailangang **sumagot** agad.","translation":"Not all questions need to be **answered** immediately."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang laman ng mga hayop na ginagamit bilang pagkain ng tao.
original_explanation: The star of every Filipino fiesta! Whether it's baboy (pork), baka (beef), or manok (chicken), "karne" is the main event. It's the reason your adobo, sinigang, and lechon exist. If a Filipino dish doesn't have rice, the second question is "Anong karne?" It's the foundation of our ulam-centric universe.
usage_notes: A general term for meat. Specific types are usually mentioned, e.g., "karne ng baboy" (pork), "karne ng baka" (beef).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkano ang isang kilo ng **karne** ng baka sa palengke?","translation":"How much is one kilo of beef **meat** at the market?"},{"sentence":"Hindi siya kumakain ng **karne** tuwing Biyernes Santo.","translation":"He/She does not eat **meat** during Good Friday."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang sanay, hindi hasa, o magaspang ang kilos o gawa. Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na ginawa nang walang paghahanda o kasanayan.
original_explanation: You know that feeling when you're forced to dance at a family reunion and you have the grace of a broken washing machine? That's `biglaw`. It's the opposite of 'practice makes perfect.' It's the 'bahala na' approach to a performance, resulting in an awkward, unrehearsed mess. Think of a first-timer trying to cook adobo without a recipe.
usage_notes: Naglalarawan ng isang kilos o pagganap na magaspang at kulang sa pag-eensayo o kasanayan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halatang **biglaw** ang kaniyang pagsayaw dahil hindi siya nag-ensayo.","translation":"His dancing was obviously **clumsy** because he did not practice."},{"sentence":"Isang **biglaw** na talumpati ang kanyang binigkas, na walang paghahanda.","translation":"He delivered an **unrehearsed** speech, without any preparation."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mga natirang sapal o hibla ng isang bagay, tulad ng tubo o prutas, matapos itong nguyain o katasin upang makuha ang katas.
original_explanation: The stuff you spit out after chewing on sugarcane. It's all the fiber-y goodness minus the juice. Also applies to what's left of the 'bunga' (betel nut) after a good long chew by your friendly neighborhood security guard.
usage_notes: Often used for sugarcane ('tubo') or betel nut ('bunga'/'nga-nga'). It specifically refers to the chewed, fibrous waste.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinapon niya ang **sapa** ng tubo pagkatapos sipsipin ang katas.","translation":"He threw away the **bagasse** of the sugarcane after sucking out the juice."},{"sentence":"Puno ng **sapa** ng nganga ang sahig.","translation":"The floor is full of betel nut **residue**."}]

translation: to render meaningless; to make futile
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-alis o pagbabawas ng kahulugan, saysay, o silbi ng isang bagay, gawain, o konsepto.
original_explanation: This is a more profound version of `magpawalang-halaga`. It's not just devaluing something, it's making it completely pointless. It’s what happens when you work hard on a project, then the boss cancels it. Your efforts are rendered meaningless. "Ang kanyang mga kasinungalingan ay nagpawalang-kabuluhan sa lahat ng kanyang pangako."
usage_notes: A more formal and deeper term than 'magpawalang-halaga'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang isang maling desisyon ay maaaring **magpawalang-kabuluhan** sa lahat ng iyong pinaghirapan.","translation":"One wrong decision can **render meaningless** all that you've worked for."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan nilang **magpawalang-kabuluhan** sa isyu upang makalusot.","translation":"They are trying to **make the issue seem trivial** in order to get away with it."}]

meaning_filipino: Patalasin ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay isang kagamitang may talim tulad ng kutsilyo o gunting, sa pamamagitan ng pagkiskis nito sa hasaan.
original_explanation: This is what you do to a knife before chopping onions, or to your mind before a board exam. Pwedeng literal, like 'ihasa mo 'yung itak,' or figurative, like 'ihasa mo ang utak mo sa Math.' It's all about making something sharper and more effective, whether it's a blade or your brain cells.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for tools or metaphorically for skills, intellect, or talents.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **ihasa** ang kutsilyo bago maghiwa ng karne.","translation":"I need to **sharpen** the knife before slicing the meat."},{"sentence":"Magbasa ka ng libro para **ihasa** ang iyong isipan.","translation":"Read a book to **sharpen** your mind."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang posisyon o katayuan na mas mataas kaysa sa iba sa isang organisasyon o sistema batay sa haba ng serbisyo o antas ng awtoridad.
etymology: From `taas` (high) with the prefix `ka-` and suffix `-an` (denoting quality or state), plus `ng ranggo` (of rank).
original_explanation: This is the "nauna siya sa'yo" card in the office. It's why your boss, who might still think 'email' is a new thing, gets the bigger desk. It's the reason why in family gatherings, Tito Boy gets the first piece of lechon—he's the eldest. It's the corporate or family hierarchy in action.
usage_notes: Often used in military, corporate, or formal settings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang **kataasan ng ranggo**, iginagalang siya ng lahat ng sundalo.","translation":"Because of his **high rank**, he is respected by all the soldiers."},{"sentence":"Ang promosyon ay iginawad batay sa **kataasan ng ranggo** at hindi sa personal na pabor.","translation":"The promotion was awarded based on **seniority** and not on personal favors."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na laging nakikita ang masamang bahagi ng mga bagay o inaasahan ang pinakamasamang resulta; nauukol sa pagiging negatibo sa pananaw.
original_explanation: Your friend who, when you say 'Kaya natin 'to!', replies with 'Paano kung hindi?'. They're the one who brings an umbrella on a sunny day 'just in case'. The official member of the 'Sana All' no more, 'Wala Nang Pag-asa' club. The opposite of an 'optimist'.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun to describe a person or an adjective to describe a characteristic or outlook.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **pesimist**, isipin mo na magtatagumpay ka.","translation":"Don't be **pessimistic**, think that you will succeed."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya bilang isang **pesimist** sa aming grupo.","translation":"He is known as a **pessimist** in our group."}]

translation: in groups of four; four by four
meaning_filipino: Sa paraan ng pagpapangkat na may tig-aapat sa bawat grupo.
original_explanation: How your strict teacher wants you to line up, or how you count your money when it's all in 20-peso bills and you're trying to see if you have enough for milk tea. "Bilangin mo 'yang mga itlog, apat-apat para mabilis."
usage_notes: Naglalarawan ng paraan ng pamamahagi o pag-aayos.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pumasok sila sa sinehan nang **apat-apat**.","translation":"They entered the cinema **in groups of four**."},{"sentence":"Ibinigay ng titser ang mga libro nang **apat-apat**.","translation":"The teacher gave out the books **four by four**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang biyaya, pabor, o kaloob mula sa Diyos o sa sinumang may kapangyarihan; isang bagay na nagdudulot ng kabutihan at kaligayahan.
etymology: From `pag-` + `pala`. The root 'pala' is archaic and means grace or favor.
original_explanation: It's when you get the last piece of crispy pata, find an empty seat on the MRT during rush hour, or your 13th-month pay arrives just when your Shopee cart is full. It's the universe saying, "Sige na, deserve mo 'to."
usage_notes: Primarily used in a religious or spiritual context, but also for any significant good fortune.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinuturing niyang isang malaking **pagpapala** ang pagkakaroon ng mabuting pamilya.","translation":"She considers having a good family a great **blessing**."},{"sentence":"Nawa'y umulan ng **pagpapala** sa inyong bagong kasal.","translation":"May **blessings** rain upon you, newlyweds."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gawain ng paglilinis ng ngipin gamit ang sipilyo at toothpaste.
etymology: From pag- + si- + sipilyo (toothbrush, from Spanish 'cepillo').
original_explanation: The daily ritual your dentist begs you to do three times a day. It's that two-minute buffer between you and the world in the morning, and the final boss you have to defeat before collapsing into bed at night. The success of your pagsisipilyo determines if your breath is "mabango" or if people will practice social distancing around you even without a pandemic.
usage_notes: A very common, everyday word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutan ang **pagsisipilyo** pagkatapos kumain.","translation":"Don't forget the **brushing of teeth** after eating."},{"sentence":"Ang tamang **pagsisipilyo** ay mahalaga para sa kalusugan ng gilagid.","translation":"Proper **tooth brushing** is important for gum health."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtulad o pagkopya sa kilos, pananalita, anyo, o gawa ng iba.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you see a viral TikTok dance. Or when your younger sibling copies everything you say just to annoy you. From fashion trends to accents, panggagaya is the sincerest form of flattery... or the most irritating.
usage_notes: Can be neutral, positive (emulation), or negative (mockery).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa kanyang mahusay na **panggagaya** sa boses ng mga sikat na mang-aawit.","translation":"He is known for his excellent **imitation** of the voices of famous singers."},{"sentence":"Ang **panggagaya** ay isang anyo ng paghanga, sabi nila.","translation":"**Imitation** is a form of flattery, they say."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikas o pag-alis mula sa isang lugar na may panganib o sakuna patungo sa isang mas ligtas na lokasyon.
original_explanation: The OG 'GTFO.' When there's a super typhoon, a volcanic eruption, or a conflict, this is the command to pack your essentials (and maybe your pet cat) and run for your life to the nearest school gym or community center. The people who do this are called 'bakwit'.
usage_notes: 'Bakwit' is a Filipinized term from the English word 'evacuate'. It can refer to the act of evacuating or the evacuees themselves.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinailangang **magbakwit** ng mga residente dahil sa pagtaas ng baha.","translation":"The residents had to **evacuate** due to the rising floodwaters."},{"sentence":"Naghanda na sila ng go-bag para kung kailangang **magbakwit** bigla.","translation":"They already prepared a go-bag in case they need to **evacuate** suddenly."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangatnig na ginagamit upang ipahayag ang sanhi, dahilan, o katwiran ng isang pangyayari o kilos.
original_explanation: This is the 'why' that justifies everything. 'Bakit ka late?' 'Dahil traffic.' 'Bakit ka single?' 'Dahil 'di pa 'ko ready.' It's the word that connects an action to its reason, the excuse to the consequence. It's the start of every good explanation (and every bad alibi).
usage_notes: Often used in the phrase 'dahil sa' (+ noun) to mean 'because of'. The pronunciation /DA-hil/ with stress on the first syllable is key for this meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi siya nakapunta **dahil** umuulan.","translation":"He wasn't able to come **because** it was raining."},{"sentence":"Nagtagumpay siya **dahil** sa kanyang pagsisikap.","translation":"She succeeded **because** of her hard work."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay na nilikha, ginawa, o inimbento; isang nilalang.
original_explanation: Ito yung ultimate "It's alive!" moment. Mula sa paggawa ng Diyos sa mundo (the OG 'lalang') hanggang sa pag-imbento mo ng bagong recipe ng adobo na may twist. Lahat ng 'yan ay produkto ng pagiging creative. Parang 'yong artist na gumawa ng obra maestra, o 'yong programmer na bumuo ng app. Sila ay lumalang.
usage_notes: Often used in a religious or artistic context to mean "to create" or "creation." The verb form is "lumalang" (to create).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tao ay isang kahanga-hangang **lalang** ng Diyos.","translation":"Man is a wonderful **creation** of God."},{"sentence":"Isang bagong **lalang** sa sining ang kanyang ipinakita.","translation":"He showed a new **creation** in art."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng hindi pagkakaroon o pagpapakita ng emosyon, simpatiya, o pagmamalasakit.
original_explanation: The "dead inside" mood. Parang 'yung ex mong nakita kang umiiyak tapos ang tanong, "Umuulan ba?" It's the absence of feels, the emotional equivalent of a dial tone. Perfect for surgeons, maybe not so much for relationships. It's being manhid to the highest level.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa isang pansamantalang estado (emotional numbness) o isang permanenteng katangian ng isang tao (apathy).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakabahala ang ipinapakita niyang **kawalang-damdamin** sa pagdurusa ng iba.","translation":"His displayed **apathy** towards the suffering of others is alarming."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng trahedya, dumanas siya ng pansamantalang **kawalang-damdamin**.","translation":"After the tragedy, she experienced a temporary **lack of feeling**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang lalaking nagmula o mamamayan ng Europa, o sa anumang bagay na may katangiang panlalaki na mula sa Europa.
original_explanation: The male version of Europea. The guy you see in travel vlogs exploring the Philippines, often looking a bit lost but happy in a sando and shorts. 'Uy, may bisita tayong Europeo!'
usage_notes: Gender-specific (masculine). The gender-neutral term is 'taga-Europa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **Europeo** ang turistang nagtanong ng direksyon.","translation":"A **European** (male) was the tourist who asked for directions."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangyayaring astronomikal kung saan ang isang bagay sa kalawakan ay pansamantalang natatakpan ng isa pang bagay o ng anino nito. Karaniwang tumutukoy sa pagtatakip ng buwan sa araw (solar eclipse) o pagdaan ng buwan sa anino ng mundo (lunar eclipse).
original_explanation: Remember when your lola told you not to go outside or the *bakunawa* (a mythical serpent) would eat the sun? That's an *eklipse*. It's nature's most dramatic "new profile pic" moment for the sun or moon. Everyone suddenly becomes an amateur astronomer, buying special glasses or using a *planggana* (basin) of water to watch. It’s that rare celestial event that gets everyone to stop scrolling on their phones and actually look up.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming tao ang nag-abang sa rooftop para masaksihan ang lunar **eklipse**.","translation":"Many people waited on the rooftop to witness the lunar **eclipse**."}]

translation: to be overtaken by night; to be benighted
meaning_filipino: Ang maabutan ng gabi sa isang lugar o habang gumagawa ng isang bagay, kadalasan ay sa paglalakbay.
original_explanation: A more common and slightly more formal version of "gabi-gabihan". This is your mom's warning: "Umuwi ka nang maaga para hindi ka **gabihin** sa daan." It’s the state of being out and about when nighttime has already fallen, especially when you were supposed to be home before dark. It's the reason for a dozen missed calls from nanay.
usage_notes: The form "ginabi" (past tense) is extremely common. "Magpagabi" means to intentionally let night fall.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ginabi** na kami sa daan dahil sa matinding trapik.","translation":"We **were overtaken by night** on the road because of the heavy traffic."},{"sentence":"Bilisan mo ang paglalakad para hindi tayo **gabihan**.","translation":"Walk faster so we won't **be overtaken by night**."}]

translation: candle lighting stand; place for lighting candles
meaning_filipino: Isang lugar, karaniwan sa simbahan o sementeryo, na itinalaga para sa pagsisindi at paglalagay ng mga kandila bilang panalangin o pag-alaala.
etymology: Mula sa "tirikan" (place to erect) + "ng kandila" (of a candle).
original_explanation: The designated "prayer hotspot" in every Catholic church. Dito mo inilalagay yung P5 na kandila mo habang humihiling na sana pumasa ka sa exam, manalo sa lotto, o mapansin ni crush. It's the original "thoughts and prayers" but with a small flame.
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang tanawin sa mga simbahan sa Pilipinas at tuwing Undas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno na ng mga natunaw na kandila ang **tirikan ng kandila**.","translation":"The **candle lighting stand** is full of melted candles."},{"sentence":"Naghanap siya ng bakanteng espasyo sa **tirikan ng kandila**.","translation":"He looked for a vacant space at the **place for lighting candles**."}]

meaning_filipino: May ugali o tendensiyang maging hadlang, sagabal, o pumigil sa mga plano o gawain ng iba.
original_explanation: Ito yung kontrabida sa mga pangarap mo. Yung 'di ka pa nga nagsisimula, sinasabi na agad, "Ay, mahirap 'yan," "Sure ka ba diyan?" o "Baka 'di mo kaya." They are the human version of a "No Entry" sign on your road to success. Sila rin yung kamag-anak na haharang sa pinto 'pag aalis ka na, para lang magtanong kung saan ka pupunta.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang isang **mapaghadlang** na pananaw ay hindi makakatulong sa pag-unlad.","translation":"An **obstructive** perspective will not help with progress."},{"sentence":"Huwag nating hayaan ang mga **mapaghadlang** na tao na sirain ang ating mga pangarap.","translation":"Let's not allow **obstructive** people to destroy our dreams."}]

meaning_filipino: Maghanda ng isang bagay (karaniwan ay pagkain) para sa kapakinabangan o pagdating ng isang tao.
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino love language. Hindi "I love you" kundi "Kumain ka na?" 'Pag sinabing "Ipaghanda mo ako ng kape," it's more than just coffee. It's care, it's service, it's paglalambing. This is what your mom does when your favorite ulam is on the menu because you're coming home.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of preparing food or things for a person. `ipaghanda ng pagkain` (to prepare food for someone). The focus is on the beneficiary.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **ipaghanda** mo ng hapunan ang mga bisita natin.","translation":"Please, **prepare** dinner **for** our guests."},{"sentence":"Gusto kong **ipaghanda** ang pamilya ko ng isang espesyal na salu-salo.","translation":"I want to **prepare for** my family a special feast."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lubos at kapansin-pansing pagbabago sa hitsura, anyo, o katangian ng isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: This is the 'Glow Up' of the dictionary. Think of a caterpillar turning into a butterfly, or your friend after a breakup who suddenly hits the gym, gets a new haircut, and is now a total hottie. It's the 'Extreme Makeover' edition of 'pagbabago'.
usage_notes: Implies a more drastic and visible change than the simple `pagbabago`.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagbabagong-anyo** ng uod tungo sa pagiging paruparo ay kamangha-mangha.","translation":"The **metamorphosis** of a caterpillar into a butterfly is amazing."},{"sentence":"Dumaan siya sa isang malaking **pagbabagong-anyo** matapos manalo sa lotto.","translation":"He underwent a huge **transformation** after winning the lottery."}]

translation: to top with something; to place on top
meaning_filipino: Lagyan o patungan ng anuman sa ibabaw.
original_explanation: The magic instruction you give when ordering halo-halo: 'Paibabawan n'yo po ng maraming leche flan at ube.' It's the act of adding the finishing, glorious touch on top of something. The cherry on top, literally and figuratively.
usage_notes: A command or request to add a layer or topping. Commonly used in cooking and food preparation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **paibabawan** ng keso ang spaghetti.","translation":"Don't forget to **top** the spaghetti with cheese."},{"sentence":"Mas masarap kung ito ay **paibabawan** ng ice cream.","translation":"It's more delicious if you **place** ice cream **on top** of it."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paggawang gusot o hindi patag sa isang bagay, tulad ng papel o tela.
original_explanation: This is what you do to your test paper after seeing your score. You grab it, squeeze it into a ball, and wish it would disappear. That action is 'pag-lukot.' It's an act of frustration, anger, or sometimes, just being messy. 'Huwag mong lukutin 'yan!' is what your mom yells when you mistreat new clothes.
usage_notes: Common verb forms are "lukutin" (to crumple something, object-focus) and "malukot" (to become crumpled, subject-focus).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, huwag mong **lukutin** ang liham.","translation":"Please, don't **crumple** the letter."},{"sentence":"Mabilis **malukot** ang ganitong uri ng tela.","translation":"This type of fabric **wrinkles** easily."}]

translation: to undress; to take off clothes
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-aalis ng damit o anumang saplot sa katawan.
original_explanation: What you do the second you get home after a long day of work, traffic, and adulting. It's the first step to taking a shower or changing into your 'pambahay'. Not to be confused with 'mag-open up,' although sometimes, revealing your true self can feel just like this.
usage_notes: 'Maghubad' refers to taking off one's own clothes. 'Hubaran' means to undress someone else.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **maghubad** ng sapatos bago pumasok sa bahay.","translation":"You need to **take off** your shoes before entering the house."},{"sentence":"Pagdating niya mula sa trabaho, agad siyang **naghubad** ng uniporme at nagsuot ng pambahay.","translation":"When he arrived from work, he immediately **took off** his uniform and wore house clothes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaking naninirahan sa isang dormitoryo.
original_explanation: The guy version of a dormitoryana. His room probably smells like socks and instant pancit canton. An expert in "sahod-buhay" budgeting, borrowing your charger, and playing mobile games until 3 AM.
usage_notes: Ang katapat nito para sa babae ay 'dormitoryana'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging maingay sa kwarto ng mga **dormitoryano** dahil sa paglalaro ng video games.","translation":"It's always noisy in the **male dormers'** room because of them playing video games."},{"sentence":"Ang mga **dormitoryano** ay nag-ambagan para sa kanilang Christmas party.","translation":"The **male dorm residents** chipped in for their Christmas party."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang anyo ng sining o biswal na representasyon na karaniwang ginagamit sa paglilimbag, kompyuter, o iba pang midya upang maghatid ng impormasyon o palamuti.
original_explanation: 'Yan 'yung mga imahe, disenyo, o drawing sa computer na ginagawa ng graphic designer mo para sa social media post ng business ninyo. O 'yung itsura ng video game na nilalaro mo. "Ang ganda ng grapik ng bagong laro!"
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng disenyo, sining, at teknolohiya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating pagandahin ang **grapik** ng ating presentasyon.","translation":"We need to improve the **graphics** of our presentation."},{"sentence":"Siya ay isang mahusay na artist na gumagawa ng mga digital na **grapik**.","translation":"She is a talented artist who creates digital **graphics**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang gusali o silid na ginagamit para sa pag-iimbak ng mga kalakal o gamit.
original_explanation: It's that room in the house where things go to be forgotten. The Christmas decors, your old Nokia 3310, your high school projects, and maybe even your broken dreams. It's the Filipino equivalent of the Bermuda Triangle. You put something in, and good luck finding it ever again.
usage_notes: A very common term for any storage area, from a small room in a house to a large commercial warehouse.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itago mo muna ang mga lumang gamit sa **bodega**.","translation":"Keep the old things in the **storage room** for now."},{"sentence":"Dumating na ang kargamento at nasa **bodega** na ng kumpanya.","translation":"The shipment has arrived and is now in the company **warehouse**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o pagpapahintulot sa isang tao o kumpanya na magdala ng produkto o kalakal mula sa ibang bansa papasok sa sariling bansa.
original_explanation: This is when you tell someone, "Bes, pa-order naman ako niyan sa Shopee International." It's the act of causing importation, whether it's for your business that needs supplies from China or just you wanting that K-Pop merch that's not available locally. You're not the one doing the importing, but you're making it happen.
usage_notes: The `magpa-` prefix indicates that the subject is causing or asking someone else to perform the action of the root word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpasya ang gobyerno na **magpaangkat** ng bigas upang mapunan ang kakulangan.","translation":"The government decided to **have rice imported** to fill the shortage."},{"sentence":"Gusto kong **magpaangkat** ng mga pyesa ng kotse mula sa Japan.","translation":"I want to **have car parts imported** from Japan."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapatawa o pagsasabi ng mga bagay na hindi seryoso, kadalasan upang magbigay-aliw o subukin ang reaksyon ng isang tao.
original_explanation: When your tita asks, 'O, kailan ka ikakasal?' at a family reunion, she's not being serious... or is she? That's the art of 'mambiro'. It's the national sport of Filipino family gatherings, somewhere between joking and light roasting.
usage_notes: Can range from light-hearted joking to more pointed teasing ('panunukso' or 'pang-aasar'). Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hilig talaga ni Lolo na **mambiro** sa kanyang mga apo.","translation":"Grandpa really loves **to joke** with his grandchildren."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang basta-basta **mambiro** tungkol sa kanyang timbang; baka mamasamain niya.","translation":"Don't just **tease** about her weight; she might take it badly."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagbuo ng isang buod o konklusyon mula sa iba't ibang impormasyon o detalye; paglalahat.
etymology: From `panl-` + reduplication of the first syllable `la-` + `lagom` ("summary, gist"). This formation indicates the process of doing the action.
original_explanation: This is what you do after a two-hour chismis session with your bestie: "So, in short, break na sila?" It's the TL;DR (Too Long; Didn't Read) of Filipino nouns. In a more formal setting, it's the executive summary of a report or the conclusion of your thesis. The art of getting to the point.
usage_notes: Refers to the action or process of summarizing, while `lagom` is the summary itself (the noun/product). `Paglalagom` or `pagbubuod` are more common synonyms.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahusay ang kanyang ginawang **panlalagom** sa mahabang talakayan.","translation":"His **act of summarizing** the long discussion was excellent."},{"sentence":"Ang **panlalagom** ay isang mahalagang kasanayan sa akademikong pagsulat.","translation":"**Summarizing** is an important skill in academic writing."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang bagay o sitwasyon na nasa mabuting kalagayan, katanggap-tanggap, o walang problema.
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino "it's all good." When someone asks "Kumusta?", a simple "Ayos lang" can mean anything from "I'm genuinely fine" to "My life is a mess but I don't want to talk about it." It's the verbal equivalent of a thumbs-up.
usage_notes: Often used as a one-word answer to mean "okay" or "fine." Can be intensified as 'ayos na ayos'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ayos** lang ako, huwag kang mag-alala.","translation":"I'm **fine**, don't worry."},{"sentence":"**Ayos** ba ang lahat sa opisina?","translation":"Is everything **okay** at the office?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagsusulong ng mga pagbabago o reporma sa isang sistema, batas, o lipunan.
original_explanation: The person who looks at a broken system and says, "Teh, ayusin natin 'to." They're not content with "pwede na 'yan." They want to change the game, whether it's in government, an organization, or even just the family group chat rules.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Jose Rizal ay isang dakilang **tagareporma** na gumamit ng pluma upang imulat ang mga Pilipino.","translation":"Jose Rizal was a great **reformer** who used the pen to awaken the Filipinos."},{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng mga tunay na **tagareporma** sa gobyerno.","translation":"We need true **reformers** in the government."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagluha dahil sa matinding damdamin tulad ng kalungkutan, sakit, o kagalakan. Ito ay nasa aspektong kontemplatibo o panghinaharap.
etymology: Mula sa panlaping i- (panandang pandiwa sa hinaharap) at salitang-ugat na 'iyak'.
original_explanation: The future tense of crying. It's what you promise yourself you won't do after a breakup, but end up doing at 3 AM while listening to sad songs. "Sige, iwan mo 'ko, tingnan natin sino'ng iiyak sa huli." (Spoiler: ikaw pa rin.)
usage_notes: Ito ang anyong panghinaharap ng pandiwang 'umiyak'. Ang panlaping 'i-' dito ay pananda ng hinaharap, na may pag-uulit ng unang pantig ng salitang-ugat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Iiyak** na naman ang bata kapag hindi mo ibinigay ang laruan niya.","translation":"The child **will cry** again if you don't give him his toy."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi ako **iiyak** sa harap mo.","translation":"Don't worry, I **will not cry** in front of you."}]

translation: to cock (a gun); to set up; to prepare
meaning_filipino: Ihanda ang isang bagay para sa paggamit, tulad ng pag-angat ng martilyo ng baril, pag-aayos ng isang plano, o pagbuo ng isang kaso.
etymology: From Spanish 'cazar' (to hunt) or 'casar' (to fit, to match), which evolved in Filipino to mean setting a mechanism.
original_explanation: This is what you do before a 'bardagulan' online. You **ikasa** your arguments and screenshots. In old action movies, it's the sound before the hero says his one-liner. 'Ready, aim, fire!' starts with **ikasa**.
usage_notes: While its primary meaning relates to firearms, it is widely used metaphorically to mean 'to prepare' or 'to file' a case or plan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maingat niyang **ikinasa** ang baril bago pumasok sa madilim na silid.","translation":"He carefully **cocked** the gun before entering the dark room."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka, may plano silang **ikasa** na kaso laban sa iyo.","translation":"Be careful, they have a plan to **set up** a case against you."}]

translation: the act of burying or embedding
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglalagay ng isang bagay sa ilalim ng lupa o pagtatanim nito nang malalim sa isang ibabaw.
original_explanation: This is what you do with secrets, feelings for your crush, or literally, a time capsule. It's the act of hiding something deep down, whether it's treasure in the backyard or your 'hugot' in your journal. 'Yung pagbabaon mo sa limot ng utang ng kaibigan mo.
usage_notes: Differentiated from the other 'pagbabaon' (provisions) by context. This one relates to burying, hiding, or embedding something physically or emotionally.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagbabaon** sa mga poste ng kuryente ay isinasagawa upang maging mas ligtas ang kalsada.","translation":"The **burying** of electric posts is being done to make the road safer."},{"sentence":"Mahirap ang **pagbabaon** sa limot ng masasakit na alaala.","translation":"The **act of burying** painful memories in oblivion is difficult."}]

translation: to sell on a small scale; to dabble in selling
meaning_filipino: Magbenta nang paunti-unti, hindi regular, o bilang isang maliit na libangan o pangkabuhayan lamang.
original_explanation: This is the side hustle version of selling. You're not a full-blown tycoon yet. It's selling baked goods to your officemates, or having a small 'garage sale' on Facebook. It's the 'testing the waters' of the business world.
usage_notes: The repetition implies that the action is done in a small, non-continuous, or casual manner.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para may pandagdag sa gastusin, nagpasya siyang **magtinda-tinda** ng kakanin sa hapon.","translation":"To supplement her expenses, she decided to **sell rice cakes on a small scale** in the afternoon."},{"sentence":"Habang nag-aaral, siya ay nag**tinda-tinda** ng mga school supplies.","translation":"While studying, he **dabbled in selling** school supplies."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang estado ng pag-aapoy o pagliliyab nang may malakas na ningas o apoy.
original_explanation: Think of a bonfire at a beach party, or yung feelings mo for your crush na 'di mo maamin. It's burning brightly! Can also be used for passion or anger, like 'nagniningas na galit' (burning anger). It's fire, but make it poetic.
usage_notes: Often used both literally for fire and figuratively for strong emotions like love, passion, or anger.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagniningas** ang apoy sa kalan habang nagluluto si nanay.","translation":"The fire was **blazing** on the stove while mother was cooking."},{"sentence":"**Nagniningas** sa galit ang kanyang mga mata.","translation":"His eyes were **burning** with anger."}]

translation: to surpass, to overcome, to prevail
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging higit o mas mahusay kaysa sa iba; ang pagtagumpayan ang isang pagsubok o hadlang.
original_explanation: This is that "look at me now" moment. It's when the underdog wins the championship, when your small startup beats the giant corporation, or when you finally prove your bashers wrong. It's the ultimate "in your face" victory, but in a more poetic, Darna-esque way. "Ang kabutihan ay laging nagdadaig sa kasamaan."
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of competition, morality, or overcoming challenges.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawa'y **magdaig** ang katotohanan laban sa kasinungalingan.","translation":"May the truth **prevail** against the lies."},{"sentence":"Walang sinuman ang makapag-aakala na kaya niyang **magdaig** sa pinakamagaling na manlalaro.","translation":"No one thought he could **surpass** the best player."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bansa, teritoryo, o nasasakupan na pinamumunuan ng isang hari o reyna.
etymology: From `ka-`...`-an` (denoting a place or domain) around `hari` (king).
original_explanation: The OG 'territory.' Before there were condo associations or barangay captains, there were kingdoms. Today, you use it to describe your room which is your personal **kaharian** where you rule, or your lola's kitchen, which is *her* **kaharian** and you better follow her rules or face the wrath of the chancla.
usage_notes: Used for literal kingdoms in history/fantasy and metaphorically for one's personal domain or area of expertise.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napanood mo na ba ang bagong serye tungkol sa mga sinaunang **kaharian**?","translation":"Have you seen the new series about the ancient **kingdoms**?"},{"sentence":"Ang aking kuwarto ang aking munting **kaharian**.","translation":"My room is my little **kingdom**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinong pagpapakalat ng maliliit na patak ng isang likido sa isa pang likido kung saan ito ay hindi natutunaw o naghahalo.
original_explanation: Isipin mo 'yung mayonnaise. Oil at egg yolk 'yan na hindi dapat maghahalo, pero dahil sa "magic" ng pag-whisk (emulsification), naging creamy sauce sila. Ganun ang emulsyon. Parang 'yung dalawa mong kaibigan na "oil and water" ang personalities, pero 'pag kasama ka, nagkakasundo sila. Ikaw ang emulsifying agent.
usage_notes: Ang "emulsiyon" ay isang alternatibong baybay, ngunit mas karaniwan ang "emulsyon".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mayonesa ay isang halimbawa ng **emulsyon** ng langis at itlog.","translation":"Mayonnaise is an example of an **emulsion** of oil and egg."},{"sentence":"Gumamit ang pintor ng pinturang may oil-based **emulsyon**.","translation":"The painter used a paint with an oil-based **emulsion**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging magkakalayo o pagkakawatak-watak ng mga kasapi ng isang grupo o pamilya.
original_explanation: The saddest part of any barkada outing. You arrive at the mall together, then one wants to go to Uniqlo, another to the food court, and another to the arcade. After 30 minutes, nagkahiwa-hiwalay na kayo. It's the group splitting up, whether for a few hours in a mall or, more dramatically, after graduation when everyone goes their own way. The repeated "hiwalay" emphasizes that everyone is going in different directions.
usage_notes: The duplication of "hiwalay" indicates that a group of three or more entities became separated from each other, dispersing in different directions. For just two, "magkahiwalay" is more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nang lumindol, **nagkahiwa-hiwalay** ang magkakaibigan sa loob ng mall.","translation":"When the earthquake struck, the friends **became separated from one another** inside the mall."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng graduation, **nagkahiwa-hiwalay** na ng landas ang aming barkada.","translation":"After graduation, our group of friends **went our separate ways**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagtaas o pag-angat ng isang bagay mula sa mas mababang posisyon patungo sa mas mataas.
original_explanation: The verb for when you're trying to get a better signal and you lift your phone up to the sky. Or when you help your friend lift a heavy box of their ex's stuff. It's the physical act of moving something upward.
usage_notes: Salitang-ugat. Maaaring banghayin: umangat (to rise), iangat (to lift something).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**angat** naman ng kahon na ito.","translation":"Please **lift** this box."},{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **iangat** ang takip ngunit masyadong mabigat.","translation":"She tried to **lift** the lid but it was too heavy."}]

translation: to be stunned into stillness; to be shocked
meaning_filipino: Biglaang matigilan o hindi makakilos dahil sa matinding pagkabigla, pagtataka, o takot.
original_explanation: The human equivalent of a computer freezing. That moment when you see your crush walking towards you, or when you check your bank account after a 12.12 sale. You're just... stuck. Buffering. Loading... please wait.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Napatigagal** siya nang marinig ang balita.","translation":"She **was stunned into stillness** when she heard the news."},{"sentence":"Ang lahat ay **napatigagal** sa biglaang pagsabog.","translation":"Everyone **was shocked** by the sudden explosion."}]

translation: to shred, to tear to pieces
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpira-piraso o pagdurog sa isang bagay gamit ang kamay o ngipin hanggang sa ito ay maging maliliit na bahagi.
original_explanation: This is what your heart feels like after a breakup—shredded into a million tiny pieces. It's also what you do to that leftover lechon manok to make chicken sandwich spread. Total emotional and culinary carnage.
usage_notes: Often used to describe the violent tearing of paper, cloth, or even food. Can also be used figuratively for emotions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **lamurayin** ang sulat na iyan, importante 'yan!","translation":"Don't **shred** that letter, it's important!"},{"sentence":"Gusto niyang **lamurayin** ang lahat ng alaala nila.","translation":"He wants to **tear to pieces** all their memories."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging bagsak o pagkakaupo sa sahig dahil sa matinding pagod, sakit, o kawalan ng pag-asa.
original_explanation: Ever felt so defeated you just... plop down on the floor? That's lupasay. It's the physical manifestation of 'I give up.' Picture a toddler after a tantrum, a gamer after a 12-hour raid, or you after seeing your credit card bill. You're not just sitting, you're *lupasay*.
usage_notes: Connotes helplessness, exhaustion, or defeat. Can also be used as an adverb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natagpuan siyang **lupasay** sa sahig, umiiyak dahil sa masamang balita.","translation":"She was found **prostrate** on the floor, crying because of the bad news."},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng marathon, **lupasay** ang lahat ng mananakbo sa finish line.","translation":"After the marathon, all the runners were **down and out** at the finish line."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaikling salaysay ng mga mahahalagang pangyayari sa nakaraan ng isang tao, lugar, o bagay.
original_explanation: This is the TL;DR version of a chismis. It's the 'long story short' before you explain why you broke up with your ex or why you quit your last job. It gives just enough context without turning into a full-blown history lecture.
usage_notes: A noun phrase used to refer to a summary of past events.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigyan mo ako ng **maikling kasaysayan** ng relasyon ninyo.","translation":"Give me a **brief history** of your relationship."},{"sentence":"Ang unang kabanata ng libro ay isang **maikling kasaysayan** ng Pilipinas.","translation":"The first chapter of the book is a **short history** of the Philippines."}]

translation: to gush out, to spurt, to burst forth
meaning_filipino: Biglaan at malakas na paglabas ng isang likido o anumang bagay mula sa isang sisidlan o pinagmulan.
original_explanation: Imagine shaking a can of Coke and then opening it. That explosive mess? That's bumugalwak. It's the water from a busted pipe, the tears you held in all day that finally burst, or the 'di-mapigilang' feelings for your crush. It's sudden, messy, and hard to control.
usage_notes: A very descriptive and onomatopoeic-sounding word. Often implies a sudden, forceful, and somewhat messy release.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Bumugalwak** ang tubig mula sa nasirang tubo.","translation":"Water **gushed out** from the broken pipe."},{"sentence":"Nang buksan niya ang bote, **bumugalwak** ang champagne.","translation":"When he opened the bottle, the champagne **spurted** out."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kulungan o espasyo na may bakod, karaniwan para sa mga alagang hayop tulad ng baboy, manok, o kambing.
original_explanation: The animal version of a condo unit. It's the 'bahay' of the manok in the backyard or the 'babuyan' in the province. It's where the animals hang out before they become... well, lechon or tinola.
usage_notes: Distinct from 'kulungan' (cage), as 'kandang' usually implies a larger, often outdoor, fenced area.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inilipat ni Mang Teban ang mga baboy sa mas malaking **kandang**.","translation":"Mang Teban moved the pigs to a bigger **pen**."}]

translation: timing; act of setting a time limit
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtatakda ng oras, paglalagay ng hangganan sa panahon, o pagbibilang ng oras na ginugol sa isang gawain.
original_explanation: This is the act of putting a timer on something, like when your mom tells you "Maghugas ka ng pinggan in 15 minutes, kundi wala kang internet." It's that feeling of pressure because there's a deadline, whether it's for a project or for finishing your chores before the next teleserye starts. It's the ultimate "beat the clock" challenge, Filipino style.
usage_notes: Often used in contexts of setting deadlines or time limits for tasks. The `pag-o-` prefix indicates a repeated or continuous action, but in this case, it functions more like a standard gerund.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang **pag-ooras** ng aming guro sa pagsusulit.","translation":"Our teacher is strict with the **timing** of the exam."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng tamang **pag-ooras** sa pagluluto ng leche flan para hindi masunog.","translation":"Proper **timing** is needed in cooking leche flan so it doesn't get burnt."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagdaiti o pag-abot sa isang tao gamit ang daliri o isang bagay upang makuha ang kaniyang atensiyon. Ito ang anyong pangkaganapan ng 'kuhit'.
original_explanation: This is that subtle move you do in a meeting to wake up your seatmate who's dozing off. Or when you want to gossip with your friend in church, you kumuhit them. It's a light poke, usually with a finger, to say "Psst!" without actually saying "Psst!"
usage_notes: Past tense/completed aspect of 'kuhit'. Often done with the index finger to get someone's attention discreetly.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumuhit** siya sa akin para ipasa ang bayad sa jeep.","translation":"He/She **poked** me to pass the fare in the jeepney."},{"sentence":"May **kumuhit** sa likod ko habang nakapila ako.","translation":"Someone **nudged** me from behind while I was in line."}]

word: taong tinawag sa pagsusundalo o pagmamarino
meaning_filipino: Isang mamamayan na sapilitang inatasan ng pamahalaan na maglingkod sa sandatahang lakas, partikular bilang isang sundalo o marino.
etymology: From `tao` (person) + `tinawag` (called) + `sa` (to) + `pagsusundalo` (act of being a soldier) + `o` (or) + `pagmamarino` (act of being a marine/sailor).
original_explanation: This is the person who gets a 'You're in the army now' letter from the government, whether they like it or not. Think mandatory ROTC but for real, national-level service. It's the ultimate 'walang choice' moment, where your country calls and you have to answer.
usage_notes: This concept (conscription) is not currently active in the Philippines but is often discussed in historical or political contexts. The term is a direct, descriptive phrase.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Noong panahon ng digmaan, maraming **taong tinawag sa pagsusundalo o pagmamarino** upang ipagtanggol ang bansa.","translation":"During the war, many people were **conscripted into the army or navy** to defend the country."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na may masamang bisyo o gawi, tulad ng labis na pagsusugal, pag-inom ng alak, o paggamit ng ipinagbabawal na gamot.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'vicioso' (vicious, full of vice).
original_explanation: This is your tito who spends his 13th-month pay at the casino or the neighbor who's always 'nanginginig na ang laman' for a shot of cheap gin. They live by the motto 'YOLO' but in the most self-destructive way possible. Their vice is their master.
usage_notes: Ang 'bisyesto' ay panlalaki. Ang pambabae ay 'bisyesta', ngunit sa kolokyal na usapan, madalas gamitin ang 'bisyesto' para sa lahat ng kasarian.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Iwasan mo ang mga **taong bisyesto** dahil baka mahawa ka sa kanilang masamang gawi.","translation":"Avoid **people with vices** because you might be influenced by their bad habits."},{"sentence":"Maraming pera ang nasayang dahil sa pagiging **taong bisyesto** ni Mang Kanor.","translation":"A lot of money was wasted because Mang Kanor was a **person with vices**."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang kilos na ginawa nang walang pag-iingat, walang galang, o walang pagsasaalang-alang sa damdamin o kapakanan ng iba.
original_explanation: This is that person who cuts you in line at the MRT, blasts music on their phone in a jeepney, or posts spoilers for the new Marvel movie on release day. They act with zero f—cks given, completely **inconsiderate** of everyone else. Walang preno, walang hiya.
usage_notes: Isang matapang na salita na nagpapahiwatig ng kawalan ng respeto at tamang asal. Maaaring gumana bilang pang-uri na naglalarawan sa isang tao o pang-abay na naglalarawan sa isang kilos.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **walang-pakundangan** na pag-uugali ang dahilan kung bakit marami ang naiinis sa kanya.","translation":"His **brazen** behavior is the reason why many are annoyed with him."},{"sentence":"Pumasok siya nang **walang-pakundangan** sa kwarto ng kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"He entered his parents' room **inconsiderately**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang awit ng papuri, paggalang, o pagsamba, karaniwang para sa Diyos o sa bayan.
original_explanation: That song you have to stand up for at the beginning of a movie ('Lupang Hinirang') or the one you sing in church that isn't a 'praise and worship' pop song. It's the formal, serious music for God and country.
usage_notes: Often refers to a national anthem ("Pambansang Imno") or a religious hymn.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang 'Lupang Hinirang' ang pambansang **imno** ng Pilipinas.","translation":"'Lupang Hinirang' is the national **anthem** of the Philippines."},{"sentence":"Kinakanta ng koro ang isang **imno** ng pasasalamat tuwing Linggo.","translation":"The choir sings a **hymn** of thanksgiving every Sunday."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng paggawa kung saan ang mga tao o bagay ay nagpapalitan sa isang gawain o posisyon nang sunud-sunod.
original_explanation: This is your BPO team's life on a graveyard shift, taking turns on coffee runs. Or when you and your siblings had to share one Game Boy, so you played **hali-halili**. It's the art of alternating, so everyone gets a turn and no one (hopefully) gets left out.
usage_notes: The repetition of "hali" emphasizes the continuous and repeated nature of the turn-taking.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hali-halili** silang nagbantay sa ospital para sa kanilang maysakit na ina.","translation":"They **took turns** watching over their sick mother at the hospital."},{"sentence":"Ang araw at gabi ay **hali-haliling** dumarating.","translation":"Day and night arrive **alternately**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagbibigay ng katumbas na halaga para sa isang produkto, serbisyo, o utang sa hinaharap.
etymology: Future tense object-focus form of the verb "bayad" (to pay).
original_explanation: The magic word your friend says when they borrow money: "Promise, babayaran kita sa sweldo." It's also what you whisper to your cart full of Shopee items at 3 AM. The future tense of "adulting."
usage_notes: Object-focused verb. The thing being paid for is the focus. "Magbabayad" is the actor-focus equivalent ("will pay").
