meaning_filipino: Ang mataas na kapulungan ng lehislatura o kongreso sa isang bansa, na binubuo ng mga inihalal na senador.
original_explanation: The upper house of the Philippine Congress. Ito yung lugar kung saan maraming 'in aid of legislation' na hearing na minsan nagiging national TV drama series. Dito nagdedebate ang mga senador tungkol sa mga batas na huhubog sa kinabukasan ng bansa... o kung ano man ang trending topic for the week.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinagtibay na ng **Senado** ang panukalang batas para sa mas mataas na sahod.","translation":"The **Senate** has approved the bill for a higher wage."},{"sentence":"Mainit ang naging debate sa **Senado** kahapon.","translation":"The debate in the **Senate** yesterday was intense."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng propesyonal na nagtuturo sa mga mag-aaral, karaniwan sa isang paaralan.
original_explanation: Si Ma'am. Ang pangalawang nanay mo sa school na nagbigay sa'yo ng stars sa kamay at nagturo sa'yo ng "Lupang Hinirang." Sa modern times, sila 'yung nag-a-adjust sa online class at nagpapa-submit sa Google Classroom.
usage_notes: The feminine form of `maestro`. `Guro` is the gender-neutral term and is more commonly used in formal contexts today, but `maestra` is still widely understood and used, especially for older teachers.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **maestra** namin sa Filipino ay napakagaling magpaliwanag.","translation":"Our **female teacher** in Filipino is very good at explaining."},{"sentence":"Si Gng. Reyes ang paborito kong **maestra** noong elementarya.","translation":"Mrs. Reyes was my favorite **female teacher** in elementary school."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pakikipaglaban o pakikipagtunggali, maaaring sa paraang pisikal o sa ibang anyo ng pagpupunyagi.
etymology: From `pag-` + `baka`. The root `baka` (fight, struggle) is archaic and distinct from `baka` (cow) and `baka` (maybe).
original_explanation: This is the 'struggle is real' mood, but in a more formal, epic way. It's you fighting the urge to sleep at your desk during a long meeting. It's the intense action scene in a historical movie. It's the high-level concept of 'laban'—not just a single fight, but the ongoing, noble struggle.
usage_notes: More formal or literary than `pakikipag-away` or `laban`. It often implies a more significant or prolonged struggle, such as for freedom or principles.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kasaysayan ng Pilipinas ay puno ng mga kuwento ng **pagbabaka** para sa kalayaan.","translation":"The history of the Philippines is full of stories of **struggle** for freedom."},{"sentence":"Ang kaniyang **pagbabaka** sa sakit ay nagbigay inspirasyon sa marami.","translation":"His **fight** against the illness inspired many."}]

translation: to do something extra; to put in extra effort
meaning_filipino: Ang pagdaragdag ng higit pa sa karaniwan o inaasahan; ang paggawa ng karagdagang gawain o pagsisikap.
original_explanation: Yan 'yung BPO agent na kahit tapos na ang script, umekstra pa para lang ma-resolve ang issue ng customer. O 'yung friend mo na nagdala ng ulam, tapos umekstra pa, nagdala na rin ng dessert. The opposite of 'bare minimum'.
usage_notes: Commonly used in informal contexts to mean going the extra mile.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umekstra** siya sa pag-aasikaso sa mga bisita kaya natuwa sila.","translation":"He **put in extra effort** to take care of the guests, which is why they were pleased."},{"sentence":"Kahit hindi na kailangan, **umekstra** pa rin si Ana sa kanyang report.","translation":"Even though it wasn't necessary, Ana still **did something extra** on her report."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong labis ang pagpapahalaga sa sarili at madalas pag-usapan ang sariling mga nagawa o katangian; mayabang.
original_explanation: This is the person, the actual human embodiment of 'egotismo'. The 'egotista' is that officemate who turns every meeting into a monologue about their achievements. They're the friend who, when you share a problem, somehow makes the conversation about them. In short, may 'main character syndrome'.
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun to refer to the person or an adjective to describe them.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **egotista** ang bagong manager kaya walang may gusto sa kanya.","translation":"The new manager is an **egotist**, that's why nobody likes him."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **egotista** at pakinggan mo rin ang opinyon ng iba.","translation":"Don't be **egotistical** and listen to the opinions of others as well."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malalim at matinding damdamin ng kalungkutan, pighati, o pamimighati, na kadalasang may kasamang pangungulila.
original_explanation: This isn't just sad; this is 'listening to Moira dela Torre on a rainy day while staring out the window' sad. It's the *hugot* you feel after getting ghosted. *Kalumbayan* is a poetic, deep-seated sadness, the kind that makes for great OPM songs or spoken word poetry.
usage_notes: Carries a more profound and poetic weight than the common word 'lungkot' (sadness).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nababalot ng **kalumbayan** ang buong bayan sa pagpanaw ng kanilang lider.","translation":"The whole town is enveloped in **sorrow** over the passing of their leader."},{"sentence":"Makikita sa kanyang mga mata ang di-maipaliwanag na **kalumbayan**.","translation":"An inexplicable **melancholy** can be seen in his eyes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang utos o pakiusap na bigyan ng pagkain ang isang tao o hayop. Katumbas ng "pakain" sa Tagalog, at karaniwang ginagamit sa mga wikang Bisaya.
original_explanation: This is what happens when your Tagalog-speaking friend visits Cebu. They ask, 'Anong Tagalog ng 'pakaon'?' and you say, 'pakain.' It's the act of feeding someone, whether it's your pet, your 'jowa', or the 'chismis' you're feeding your friends.
usage_notes: While understood in many areas due to media and migration, 'pakain' is the standard Tagalog term. Using 'pakaon' often indicates a Visayan language background.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **pakaon** sa mga alagang aso.","translation":"Don't forget **to feed** the pet dogs."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagkakaroon ng mabuting kalooban o intensyon; pagiging mapagbigay at matulungin nang walang hinihintay na kapalit.
original_explanation: This is a level-up from 'kabutihan'. It's not just being good, it's being *good from the inside*. It's the 'goodwill' you show when you volunteer for a community pantry or treat your team to milk tea just because. It’s the core of Filipino hospitality. Think of it as 'goodness of the inner self.'
usage_notes: More specific than 'kabutihan', it emphasizes the internal disposition and genuine intent behind a kind act.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagpapasalamat ako sa iyong **kabutihang-loob**.","translation":"I am thankful for your **kindness**."},{"sentence":"Ipinakita niya ang kanyang **kabutihang-loob** sa pamamagitan ng pag-ampon sa mga ligaw na pusa.","translation":"She showed her **benevolence** by adopting stray cats."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa mga bagay, paraan, o kaisipan na naaayon sa nakaraang panahon at hindi na moderno.
etymology: ma- (having the quality of) + ka- (associative) + luma (old)
original_explanation: Your lola's way of thinking about courtship (no boyfriend-girlfriend, dapat harana agad!). O 'yung friend mo na naka-Nokia 3310 pa rin in 2026. "Ang makaluma naman ng style mo, parang galing sa baul ni lola!" It's not always negative, sometimes it's classic.
usage_notes: Can be used to describe objects, ideas, or people. Can have a slightly negative (outdated) or neutral/positive (classic, traditional) connotation depending on context.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas gusto pa rin niya ang mga **makalumang** awitin kaysa sa mga bago.","translation":"He still prefers **old-fashioned** songs over new ones."},{"sentence":"May **makalumang** paniniwala ang kanilang pamilya tungkol sa pag-aasawa.","translation":"Their family has **traditional** beliefs about marriage."}]

meaning_filipino: Gumamit ng puwersa upang maigalaw ang isang bagay palapit sa sarili o sa isang direksyon (anyong pangnagdaan).
original_explanation: Yung moment na humila ka ng upuan para maki-chismis. Or 'yung ex mong biglang nag-chat, parang humila sa'yo pabalik sa nakaraan. Wag kang papahila, bes! Move on!
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Humila** siya ng isang silya at umupo sa tabi ko.","translation":"He **pulled** a chair and sat beside me."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **humila** ng lubid nang napakalakas?","translation":"Who **pulled** the rope so hard?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasuotang panloob na mahigpit na isinusuot sa katawan, lalo na ng kababaihan, upang hubugin ang baywang at suportahan ang dibdib.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'corsé', na mula sa Pranses na 'corset'.
original_explanation: The original 'shapewear' before Skims became a thing. Your lola probably wore one, and it's what historical drama characters use to achieve that 'I can't breathe but at least my waist is snatched' look. In modern times, it's more of a fashion statement or what you wear to feel like a character from Bridgerton.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang pagkakatali ng kanyang **korset** para sa kanyang kasuotan.","translation":"Her **corset** was tied tightly for her costume."},{"sentence":"Ang mga **korset** ay sikat na kasuotan noong ika-19 na siglo.","translation":"**Corsets** were popular garments in the 19th century."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagdadalamhati dahil sa pagpanaw ng isang mahal sa buhay, karaniwang ipinapakita sa pamamagitan ng pagsusuot ng itim na damit.
original_explanation: This is the state of grieving, often visually represented by wearing black clothes (or a black pin) for a period of time after someone passes away. It's a sign of respect and sorrow. Parang 'yung puso mo 'pag nalaman mong may jowa na 'yung crush mo—pero ito, seryoso at mas malalim.
usage_notes: Describes a person's state of grieving. The traditional mourning period and attire (usually black) are associated with this word.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang taon nang **nakaluksa** ang buong pamilya.","translation":"The whole family has been **in mourning** for a year."},{"sentence":"Naka-itim siya ngayon dahil **nakaluksa** pa rin siya sa pagpanaw ng kanyang lola.","translation":"She is wearing black today because she is still **in mourning** for her grandmother's passing."}]

meaning_filipino: Utusan o pilitin ang isang tao na iangat ang paningin o tumingin sa itaas.
etymology: From pa- (causative prefix) + tingala (to look up) + -in (object-focus suffix).
original_explanation: The act of telling someone, "Uy, tingnan mo yung fireworks!" or when your friend is feeling down and you tell them to chin up, but literally. It's the command form for making someone raise their gaze, whether to see something amazing or to stop staring at their shoes in sadness.
usage_notes: Used to command or request someone to look upwards. It is the object-focus form of the verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Patingalain** mo siya para makita niya ang mga bituin sa langit.","translation":"**Make him look up** so he can see the stars in the sky."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maling paniniwala, ideya, o pag-aakala; isang bagay na mapanlinlang sa pandama o isipan.
original_explanation: That feeling when you think your salary will last until the next payday. Or when you think your crush likes you back just because they reacted to your MyDay. It's something that seems real but isn't. Parang magic trick, pero sa feelings.
usage_notes: Used for both sensory illusions (magic tricks) and false beliefs or hopes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng ginawa niyang **ilusyon** sa entablado.","translation":"The **illusion** he performed on stage was beautiful."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mabuhay sa **ilusyon** na babalikan ka pa niya.","translation":"Don't live in the **illusion** that he will still come back to you."}]

meaning_filipino: May ginagawa o hindi libre; mayroon nang gumagamit o naninirahan.
original_explanation: The classic sign on the CR door you desperately need to use. It’s your status from 9 to 5 (or 9 to 9 if you're in BPO). It's also your crush's relationship status, as in 'Sorry, taken na.' It's the Filipino-Spanish way of saying 'I have no time for your chika right now, bes.'
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with the English 'occupied' or the Tagalog 'abala' or 'may ginagawa'. Common in signs for restrooms.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pasensya na, **ukupado** ang banyo.","translation":"Sorry, the bathroom is **occupied**."},{"sentence":"Lagi siyang **ukupado** sa trabaho kaya wala siyang oras para sa pamilya.","translation":"He is always **busy** with work so he has no time for his family."}]

meaning_filipino: Itabi o iukol ang isang bagay, lugar, o oras para sa isang partikular na tao o layunin.
etymology: From i- (benefactive prefix) + pag- + reserba (from Spanish 'reserva', meaning 'reservation').
original_explanation: This is your go-to move when planning a date night or a team lunch. "Uy, ipagreserba mo na kami ng table sa Samgyupsal place!" It's the act of calling dibs on something for someone else, ensuring you don't end up waiting in line like a pleb.
usage_notes: Commonly used for booking tables in restaurants, tickets for events, or securing slots.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **ipagreserba** mo ako ng isang upuan sa harapan.","translation":"Please, **reserve** a seat **for me** in the front."},{"sentence":"**Ipinagreserba** ko na si nanay ng tiket para sa eroplano.","translation":"I already **reserved** a plane ticket **for** mom."}]

meaning_filipino: Bahagi ng katawan ng isang hayop na karaniwang mahaba at malambot, tulad ng sa pugita, na ginagamit sa paghawak o paggalaw. Sa makabagong gamit, ito rin ay tumutukoy sa isang kasabwat o tauhan sa isang samahan, lalo na sa masamang gawain.
original_explanation: Originally, it's the tentacles of an octopus or squid. But in the Philippines, 'galamay' is what you call a powerful person's network of minions or 'fixers' who get things done, often shadily. "Malakas 'yan, maraming galamay sa gobyerno." It's the human network equivalent of an octopus's reach.
usage_notes: The metaphorical sense of 'henchman' or 'network' is very common in political and social commentary.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **galamay** ng pugita ay mahigpit ang kapit.","translation":"The octopus's **tentacles** have a tight grip."},{"sentence":"Nahuli ang isa sa mga **galamay** ng sindikato.","translation":"One of the syndicate's **henchmen** was caught."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang makapal na guwantes na isinusuot upang protektahan ang kamay mula sa init kapag humahawak ng mainit na bagay mula sa oven o lutuan.
original_explanation: The official hand-armor for battling hot trays and pans. In the absence of a proper oven mitt, the Filipino "tita" will expertly use a folded "basahan" (rag) or pot holder. Resourcefulness is key!
usage_notes: The two words are almost always used together as a compound noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka, gamitin mo 'yung **oven mitt** para hindi ka mapaso.","translation":"Be careful, use the **oven mitt** so you don't get burned."},{"sentence":"Nawawala ang kapares ng **oven mitt** ko.","translation":"The other pair of my **oven mitt** is missing."}]

translation: coarseness, rudeness, vulgarity (in action or speech)
meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging magaspang, bastos, o walang pinong pagkilos o pananalita.
etymology: From `ka-` + `gaslaw` + `-an`, signifying the quality or state of being coarse.
original_explanation: This is the opposite of 'kagandahang-asal'. It's being clumsy, tactless, and generally uncouth. Think of someone who makes green jokes at a funeral, burps loudly during a formal dinner, or dances like a wacky inflatable tube man without a care in the world. It’s action or speech that lacks finesse and grace.
usage_notes: Refers to a lack of grace or refinement in movement, speech, or behavior. It can range from simple clumsiness to outright vulgarity.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinagsabihan siya dahil sa **kagaslawan** ng kanyang mga biro.","translation":"He was reprimanded for the **coarseness** of his jokes."},{"sentence":"Ang **kagaslawan** sa pagkilos ay maaaring ituring na kawalan ng respeto.","translation":"**Rudeness** in action can be considered a lack of respect."}]

meaning_filipino: (Balbal) Isang uri ng katatawanan na magaspang, bastos, o nakasentro sa mga paksang itinuturing na mababang-uri o hindi angkop sa pormal na usapan.
etymology: Combination of Tagalog 'kanal' (gutter, low-brow) and English 'humor'.
original_explanation: The type of comedy that makes you laugh but also makes you feel a little bit guilty. Think green jokes, slapstick that's a bit too painful, and memes that would get you cancelled if you posted them on your main account. It's the humor of the masses, unfiltered and often politically incorrect.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'kanalhumor' (one word), which is also used as a hashtag.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siya sa **kanal humor**, kaya tawa siya nang tawa sa mga jokes mo.","translation":"He's a fan of **gutter humor**, that's why he's laughing so hard at your jokes."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paghabol o paghahanap sa isang tao o bagay na nais hulihin o abutin.
original_explanation: This is straight out of an action movie. 'Pagtugis' is the police chasing the bad guys, or you chasing the last bus home. It implies a sense of urgency and determination. In a more 'hugot' sense, it can be the 'pagtugis ng pangarap' (pursuit of dreams), which is a much more dramatic chase.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of law enforcement, hunting, or achieving a goal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagresulta sa maaksyong **pagtugis** ang pagnanakaw sa bangko.","translation":"The bank robbery resulted in an action-packed **chase**."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagtugis** sa katarungan ay hindi madali.","translation":"The **pursuit** of justice is not easy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdikit at paggalaw nang paulit-ulit sa ibabaw ng isang bagay, na nagdudulot ng priksyon o kaskasan.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa ng pusa sa binti mo para magpalambing. O 'yung ginagawa mo sa pila ng MRT para lang makasingit. "Excuse me po," sabay **kumiskis** sa likod ng nasa unahan mo.
usage_notes: Can mean a gentle rub (like a cat) or a rough scrape (like a vehicle against a wall). The context and intensity are key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig **kumiskis** ang alaga naming pusa sa aming mga binti.","translation":"Our pet cat loves **to rub against** our legs."},{"sentence":"**Kumiskis** ang gilid ng tricycle sa pader kaya nagasgasan.","translation":"The side of the tricycle **scraped** against the wall, so it got scratched."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng araknid na may walong paa at karaniwang gumagawa ng sapot upang makahuli ng kanyang pagkain.
etymology: From Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *kawa-kawa 'spider', possibly with reduplication and phonetic shifts.
original_explanation: That eight-legged creature that makes you question if you should burn the house down or just move to another country. Also, a popular childhood game involving fighting captured spiders in a matchbox. "Tara, pa-derby tayo ng gagamba!"
usage_notes: A general term for any spider.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May malaking **gagamba** sa sulok ng kisame.","translation":"There's a big **spider** in the corner of the ceiling."},{"sentence":"Takot na takot siya sa mga **gagamba**.","translation":"She is terrified of **spiders**."}]

translation: to tumble; to turn upside down somersault-style
meaning_filipino: Itiwarik o itumba nang patiwarik; gawing baligtad na ang itaas ay nasa ibaba.
original_explanation: This is a more dramatic version of `ibaliktad`. Think gymnastics, or what happens to your life when you suddenly lose your job and your Jowa in the same week. Everything just tumbles over. It's the action of flipping something over completely, like a car in an action movie.
usage_notes: Implies a more forceful or complete overturning than 'ibaliktad'. Can be used for acrobatic movements.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa lakas ng hangin, halos **maibalintuwad** ang maliit na bangka.","translation":"With the strength of the wind, the small boat almost **tumbled over**."},{"sentence":"Kayang **ibalintuwad** ng atleta ang kanyang katawan sa ere.","translation":"The athlete can **tumble** his body in the air."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang makapal na takip sa sahig na gawa sa hinabing tela, ginagamit bilang palamuti o para sa kaginhawahan.
original_explanation: That floor blanket in your rich tita's house that you're not allowed to step on with your shoes. It's also the thing that magically collects all the dust, crumbs, and lost coins in the house. The VIP area of the floor.
usage_notes: Refers to wall-to-wall carpeting or large area rugs. For smaller rugs, 'karpeta' or 'basahan' might be used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nang linisin ang **karpet** sa sala.","translation":"The **carpet** in the living room needs to be cleaned."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-alis o paglisan mula sa isang tiyak na lugar o pook, kadalasan dahil sa panganib o pagbabago.
etymology: From the root "likas" as in "lumikas" (to evacuate). The verb "likasan" is the object-focus form, meaning to evacuate or depart from a specific place.
original_explanation: The dramatic version of "umalis." You don't just 'likasan' your office after your shift. You 'likasan' a place that has been hit by a typhoon, or a home full of bad memories. It implies a more significant, often permanent, departure. It's the verb for when you ghost everyone and move to a new city to start over.
usage_notes: "Likasan" (object-focus) means to leave a place. "Lumikas" (actor-focus) means to evacuate or flee. The place being left is the object.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinailangang **likasan** ng mga residente ang kanilang mga bahay dahil sa pagbaha.","translation":"The residents had **to leave** their homes because of the flood."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **likasan** ang bayang iyong sinilangan.","translation":"It is difficult **to depart from** the town where you were born."}]

translation: to point at something with one's lips
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagturo sa isang bagay o direksyon sa pamamagitan ng pag-usli ng mga labi.
original_explanation: The action of using the Filipino GPS (your lips). It's a verb! You don't just have a 'nguso', you actively 'ngusuan' things. "Ngusuan mo nga kung nasaan yung bilihan ng yosi." It's efficient, hands-free, and a core skill for any Pinoy.
usage_notes: This is the object-focus verb form. The action is directed *at* something. It can also mean 'to pout at someone'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ninusuan** niya ang lalagyan ng asukal nang tanungin ko kung nasaan ito.","translation":"She **pointed with her lips** at the sugar container when I asked where it was."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **ngusuan**, magsalita ka nang maayos.","translation":"Don't **pout at** me, speak properly."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kasama sa parehong klase sa paaralan o anumang institusyong pang-edukasyon.
etymology: From English 'classmate'. A direct loanword that has been fully adopted.
original_explanation: The person you share notes with, group projects with, and secretly compete with for the top spot. They are your first allies and rivals. Years later, you'll see them on Facebook and think, "Uy, classmate ko 'to dati!" before checking if their life is more or less successful than yours.
usage_notes: Used interchangeably with the native Tagalog term 'kaklase'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Classmate** ko siya mula elementary hanggang high school.","translation":"He was my **classmate** from elementary to high school."},{"sentence":"Humingi ako ng notes sa **classmate** ko.","translation":"I asked for notes from my **classmate**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sitwasyon kung saan may posibilidad ng pinsala, sakit, o kapahamakan; panganib.
etymology: Isang karaniwang maling baybay ng 'peligro', na hiram sa Espanyol na 'peligro'.
original_explanation: The non-standard, 'palengke' spelling of 'peligro'. Ito yung sigaw ng nanay mo 'pag umaakyat ka sa puno o 'pag sumasama ka sa maling barkada. It's the feeling you get when your phone is at 1% and you're waiting for an important message. Danger zone!
usage_notes: Ito ay isang kolokyal at di-pormal na baryant. Ang pormal at tamang baybay ay 'peligro'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging may **piligro** sa pagtawid sa abalang kalsada.","translation":"There is always **danger** in crossing a busy road."}]

meaning_filipino: Hayag, lantad, o opisyal na ipinahayag at alam na ng lahat.
original_explanation: Ito yung status na "in a relationship" pero on a whole new level. Hindi lang kayo, kundi alam na ng buong barangay. Parang 'pag sinabing "deklarado na holiday," alam mong walang pasok at walang kokontra. It's official, no-take-backs, and probably posted on social media.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Deklarado** na silang magkasintahan sa harap ng kanilang mga pamilya.","translation":"They are a **declared** couple in front of their families."},{"sentence":"Isang **deklarado** na special non-working holiday ang araw ng eleksyon.","translation":"Election day is a **declared** special non-working holiday."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang taong nagbago na ng landas mula sa masama tungo sa mabuting pamumuhay; isang panibagong simula o buhay.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'glow-up' story. Think of someone who went from 'pasaway' to 'model citizen'. It's the ex-convict who now runs a charity, or the person who quit their vices and is now a fitness guru. It’s the "new life, who dis?" energy, but in a really positive, reformed way.
usage_notes: Often has a moral or spiritual connotation of reform and redemption.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mula nang makalaya, isa na siyang **bagumbuhay** at tumutulong sa komunidad.","translation":"Since being freed, he is now a **reformed person** and helps the community."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kilos o aksyon na lubhang masama, imoral, o nakapipinsala.
etymology: A phrase combining 'napakasama' (very bad/evil) and 'gawa' (deed, work).
original_explanation: This is what your lola warns you about. It's not just 'masamang gawa' (a bad deed) like stealing a piece of candy; this is the final boss of bad deeds. Think major betrayals, grand theft, or voting for the wrong person in a group project. 'Ang pagtataksil sa bayan ay isang napakasamang gawa.'
usage_notes: A formal and strong condemnation of an action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-agaw ng lupa ng mga mahihirap ay isang **napakasamang gawa**.","translation":"Seizing the land of the poor is a **very evil deed**."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa balarila, ito ay isang panagano ng pandiwa na nagpapahayag ng isang katotohanan, opinyon, o isang katanungan.
original_explanation: Ito yung 'default setting' ng mga pandiwa. 'Yung nagsasabi lang ng totoo, kung ano ang nangyari, nangyayari, o mangyayari. Walang drama, walang 'what if'. Straight to the point, parang resibo ng 7-Eleven. "Kumain ako." Indicative 'yan. Hindi 'yan "Sana kumain ako" o "Kumain ka!".
usage_notes: Isang terminong pang-gramatika na bihirang gamitin sa pang-araw-araw na usapan ngunit mahalaga sa pag-aaral ng wikang Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pandiwang \"naglakad\" sa pangungusap na \"Naglakad si Maria\" ay nasa **panaganong paturol**.","translation":"The verb \"walked\" in the sentence \"Maria walked\" is in the **indicative mood**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang manatili sa isipan o alaala ang isang bagay, tao, o pangyayari sa hinaharap.
original_explanation: What your mom says before you leave the house: 'Matatandaan mo lahat ng bilin ko, ha?' (You will remember all my instructions, okay?). Also, the hugot line: 'Sana matatandaan mo pa rin ako kahit may bago ka na.' (I hope you will still remember me even if you have someone new). It's the future tense of memory.
usage_notes: Future tense of the verb 'tandaan' (to remember).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang araw na ito ay **matatandaan** bilang isang makasaysayang sandali.","translation":"This day **will be remembered** as a historic moment."},{"sentence":"Siguradong **matatandaan** kita dahil sa iyong kabutihan.","translation":"I will surely **remember** you because of your kindness."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lugar, kasangkapan, o kagamitan na ginagamit upang magbigay o magdagdag ng init sa isang bagay.
etymology: From `pa-` (causative prefix) + `init` (heat) + `-an` (locative suffix, indicating a place or instrument).
original_explanation: This could be your microwave oven (*microwavable painitan*), the office water dispenser's hot tap, or that spot sa ilalim ng araw where you dry your laundry. It's any place or thing you use to banish the cold, whether from your food, your body, or your lonely heart.
usage_notes: Can refer to a device (like a water heater) or a location (like a spot under the sun).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ilagay mo ang ulam sa **painitan** para hindi mapanis.","translation":"Put the viand in the **heater** (e.g., microwave) so it doesn't spoil."},{"sentence":"Sira ang aming **painitan** ng tubig kaya malamig ang panligo namin.","translation":"Our water **heater** is broken, that's why our bathwater is cold."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghiga na nakaharap paitaas ang dibdib at mukha.
original_explanation: The official position of someone who just got home from a long day, ate a huge meal, and is now contemplating their life choices while staring at the ceiling. It’s the "I give up on today" pose. Also how you sleep when you're feeling zero threats and maximum chill.
usage_notes: The opposite is 'dumapa' (to lie on one's stomach).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagod na pagod siyang **tumihaya** sa kama pag-uwi niya galing trabaho.","translation":"He was so tired that he **lay on his back** on the bed when he got home from work."},{"sentence":"Masarap **tumihaya** sa damuhan habang pinapanood ang mga bituin.","translation":"It feels good to **lie on one's back** on the grass while watching the stars."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mga huling tagubilin, kahilingan, o pamana ng isang taong malapit nang pumanaw o aalis nang matagal.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'pahabol' request. It's the dramatic final instruction in a teleserye before someone dies, or your mom's non-stop list of reminders before you leave for a trip. 'At 'wag kalimutan mag-charge ng power bank!'
usage_notes: Often used in legal contexts (last will and testament) or dramatic, personal situations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **huling-habilin** ng lola ay ipamahagi ang kanyang mga alahas sa lahat ng apo.","translation":"Grandma's **dying wish** was to distribute her jewelry among all her grandchildren."},{"sentence":"Nakasulat sa papel ang kanyang **huling-habilin** bago siya umalis.","translation":"His **final instructions** were written on paper before he left."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang babaeng kambing.
original_explanation: Simple. It's the female goat, the mama goat. While 'kambing' is the general term, 'kabra' is specifically for the 'girl' goat.
usage_notes: Less common than the general term 'kambing'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang gatas ng **kabra** ay masustansya raw.","translation":"The milk of a **she-goat** is said to be nutritious."},{"sentence":"Nanganak na ang alaga naming **kabra**.","translation":"Our pet **she-goat** has given birth."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkakaroon ng bulati sa tiyan o bituka.
etymology: From 'bulati' (worm) + '-hin' (a suffix indicating a condition or affliction).
original_explanation: Eto 'yung sinasabi ng nanay mo kapag payat ka pero malakas kang kumain. "Baka bulatihin ka na, anak!" Usually, this is followed by a trip to the botika for some deworming meds. It's the classic Pinoy parent diagnosis for any kid who's not chubby.
usage_notes: Primarily used in a medical or health context, often when talking about children or pets.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinainom ng gamot ang aso dahil **bulatihin** ito.","translation":"The dog was given medicine because it **has worms**."},{"sentence":"Madalas, ang mga batang **bulatihin** ay may maputlang itsura.","translation":"Often, children who **have worms** have a pale appearance."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng matinding pagkagutom o pananabik sa isang bagay, lalo na sa pagkain. Maaari ring tumukoy sa masidhing pagnanasa.
original_explanation: This is next-level gutom. Hindi lang 'I'm hungry,' but 'Gutom na gutom na ako, parang isang linggo akong 'di kumain' level. Yung tipong makakita ka lang ng picture ng pagkain sa IG, naglalaway ka na. Pwede ring for non-food things, like "hayok sa kapangyarihan" (power-hungry) or "hayok sa pagmamahal" (desperate for love).
usage_notes: Nagpapahiwatig ng desperasyon o kawalan ng kontrol.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Hayok** na **hayok** ang mga bata mula sa maghapong paglalaro.","translation":"The children were **ravenously** hungry from playing all day."},{"sentence":"Tila siya ay **hayok** sa atensyon kaya't kung ano-ano ang ginagawa.","translation":"It seems he is **starved** for attention that's why he does all sorts of things."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng binti ng tao sa pagitan ng balakang at tuhod.
original_explanation: The upper part of your leg. For chicken, it's one of the best parts. For humans, it's what gets sore after leg day at the gym or after a long commute standing up in the MRT.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masakit ang **hita** ko dahil sa pag-akyat sa bundok.","translation":"My **thighs** are sore from climbing the mountain."},{"sentence":"Ang paborito niyang parte ng manok ay ang **hita**.","translation":"His favorite part of the chicken is the **thigh**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang produkto na ginawa sa malakihang paraan sa loob ng isang pabrika, karaniwang gumagamit ng makinarya.
original_explanation: The opposite of yaring-kamay. This is mass-produced stuff. Consistent, cheap, and available everywhere. Think of your instant noodles, your generic white t-shirts, and most of the things in a supermarket. It lacks the 'soul' but gets the job done.
usage_notes: Hyphenated compound adjective.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas mura ang mga damit na **yaring-pabrika** kumpara sa mga pasadyang tahi.","translation":"**Factory-made** clothes are cheaper compared to custom-tailored ones."}]

meaning_filipino: Usap-usapan o balita na kumakalat na hindi tiyak ang katotohanan; tsismis.
etymology: From 'bulong' (whisper), reduplicated to imply a widespread, collective whispering.
original_explanation: This is the noun. The chismis itself. 'Yung 'tea' na pinapasa-pasa sa office group chat. "Narinig mo na ba ang bulung-bulungan? Magre-resign na daw si boss!" It's the stuff that travels faster than the office WiFi.
usage_notes: Carries a strong connotation of unverified information or gossip. It is the product of 'bulungan' (the act of whispering).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **bulung-bulungan** na magkakaroon daw ng bonus sa Pasko.","translation":"There's a **rumor** that there will be a bonus for Christmas."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala sa mga **bulung-bulungan**; alamin mo muna ang totoo.","translation":"Don't believe in **hearsay**; find out the truth first."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang simula, ugat, o sanhi ng isang bagay, pangyayari, konsepto, o lahi.
original_explanation: Your 'origin story.' 'Yung sagot sa tanong na 'Saan ka ba galing?' na hindi lang tungkol sa lugar, kundi sa history mo, sa pamilya mo, sa lahat ng hugot mo sa buhay. It's the 'backstory' in your life's teleserye. The root of all chismis, problems, and successes.
usage_notes: A fundamental word used in a wide variety of contexts, from history and science to personal stories.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalagang balikan ang ating **pinagmulan** upang maunawaan ang kasalukuyan.","translation":"It is important to look back at our **origins** to understand the present."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pinagmulan sa panig ng ama** ay mula sa Cebu.","translation":"His **roots on his father's side** are from Cebu."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang ekspresyon na pinagsasama ang "OMG" (Oh my God) at "eme" (isang salitang bakla para sa "biro lang" o "kunwari"), na nagpapahiwatig ng pagkagulat na may kasamang biro o hindi kasiguraduhan.
etymology: Pagsasama ng 'OMG' (acronym ng Oh my God) at 'eme' (salitang balbal).
original_explanation: Ito yung reaction mo pag may nakitang chismis na sobrang wild, pero di ka sure kung totoo. It's the "OMG, is this for real?!" but with a hint of "charot!" on the side. Ginagamit para mag-react sa isang bagay na shocking pero baka joke lang pala.
usage_notes: Karaniwan sa online chat at social media, lalo na sa mga kabataan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**OMG eme**, totoo ba yang balita na yan?","translation":"**OMG just kidding**, is that news actually true?"}]

translation: to touch lightly; to brush against
meaning_filipino: Ang marahan o bahagyang pagdikit o pagtama sa isang bagay o tao.
original_explanation: That kilig moment in a rom-com when the leads' hands accidentally magdampi while reaching for the same coffee cup. It's a touch so light, parang hangin lang, but it feels like an electric shock. The opposite of a slap.
usage_notes: Conveys a gentle, often fleeting touch. Can be used for physical objects or people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman kong **magdampi** ang aming mga balikat sa siksikang bus.","translation":"I felt our shoulders **brush against** each other in the crowded bus."},{"sentence":"Nag-ingat siyang huwag **magdampi** ang basang pintura sa pader.","translation":"He was careful not to **touch lightly** the wet paint on the wall."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagkakalat ng maliliit at pulburadong bagay sa ibabaw ng isang bagay, tulad ng asin, asukal, o pampalasa.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you're trying to achieve that perfect "Salt Bae" moment in your kitchen. Whether it's cheese on your spaghetti, sugar on your kutsinta, or chismis sa kapitbahay, the act of sprinkling it just right is to `magbudbod`. It's the finishing touch that makes all the difference.
usage_notes: Often used in cooking contexts. Can also be used metaphorically for spreading things like rumors.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **magbudbod** ng keso sa ibabaw ng iyong spaghetti.","translation":"Don't forget to **sprinkle** cheese on top of your spaghetti."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **magbudbod** ng tsismis sa opisina.","translation":"She likes to **scatter** gossip in the office."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maramdaman ang matinding galit o pagkasuklam para sa isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of hate. It's when you direct that 'gigil' or 'inis' towards a specific person, thing, or situation. 'Kinapopootan ko ang traffic sa EDSA.' That's the feeling. It's a stronger, more formal version of 'ayaw ko' or 'naiinis ako.'
usage_notes: An object-focus verb derived from the root 'poot' (hatred).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kinapopootan** niya ang mga taong sinungaling.","translation":"She **hates** people who are liars."},{"sentence":"Bakit mo ba ako **kinapopootan** nang ganito?","translation":"Why do you **hate** me this much?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay o paglilipat ng gawain, tungkulin, o kapangyarihan sa ibang tao.
etymology: Mula sa salitang "delegado" na may hulaping "-han".
original_explanation: This is what your boss does on a Friday afternoon. Yung lahat ng trabahong ayaw niyang gawin over the weekend, ipapasa sa'yo. "Pakigawa na lang nito, ha?" is the classic way to **delegahan** ka ng tasks. Effective teamwork... daw.
usage_notes: Isang pandiwa na tumutukoy sa akto ng pag-aatas ng gawain sa isang tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **delegahan** ng mga gawain ang iyong mga kasama upang mapabilis ang proyekto.","translation":"You need **to delegate** tasks to your colleagues to speed up the project."},{"sentence":"Dinelegahan ng manager ang team leader na mamahala sa bagong account.","translation":"The manager **assigned** the team leader to handle the new account."}]

translation: to crumple; to rub vigorously (especially eyes)
meaning_filipino: Ang marahas na paggulo o pagkayas sa isang bagay, tulad ng paglukot ng papel o paghilod sa mata.
original_explanation: What you do to your face when you wake up for an 8 AM meeting after a late-night K-drama binge. It's also what you do to a piece of paper right before you shoot it into the trash bin like a basketball star. The physical manifestation of 'Ugh, another revision?'
usage_notes: This is the root word for the verb. Common forms are 'kinukusot' (rubbing) and 'kinusot' (rubbed). The stress is on the second syllable, unlike the noun 'KÚSOT' (sawdust).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **kusutin** ang iyong mga mata, baka maimpeksyon.","translation":"Don't **rub** your eyes, you might get an infection."},{"sentence":"**Kinusot** niya ang papel at itinapon sa basurahan.","translation":"He **crumpled** the paper and threw it in the trash."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay, puwersa, o paraan na ginagamit sa pagsalakay, paglusob, o pag-atake.
original_explanation: This has big 'Marcos declares Martial Law' energy. It's a very formal, almost military term for an invading or attacking force. You won't hear this at the palengke, but you'll see it in history books describing a blitzkrieg. The vibe is aggressive, swift, and overwhelming.
usage_notes: A formal and literary word often used in military or historical contexts. Can be a noun (assault force) or an adjective (for assault).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang hukbong **pandaluhong** ay mabilis na sinakop ang bayan.","translation":"The **assault** force quickly occupied the town."},{"sentence":"Naghanda sila ng mga sandatang **pandaluhong** para sa napipintong giyera.","translation":"They prepared **assault** weapons for the impending war."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagprotekta o pag-iingat sa isang tao, bagay, o karapatan laban sa panganib, pag-atake, o kritisismo.
original_explanation: This is your 'ride or die' instinct kicking in. It's when you jump into a comments section to defend your favorite celebrity, or when an older sibling stands up to a bully for their younger sibling. It's what lawyers do in court and what soldiers do for the country. It's the act of saying "Subukan mong saktan 'yan, kami ang makakalaban mo." (You try to hurt them, you'll have to go through us).
usage_notes: Can be physical (defending against an attack), verbal (defending an idea), or legal (defending a client).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagtatanggol** sa sarili ay isang karapatan.","translation":"Self-**defense** is a right."},{"sentence":"Humanga ako sa kanyang matapang na **pagtatanggol** sa mga inaapi.","translation":"I admired his brave **advocacy** for the oppressed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pandiwang ugat na nangangahulugang manlamang, mang-abuso, o magmalupit sa kapwa.
original_explanation: This is the root word for the action of being the kontrabida. When you 'apihin' someone, you're being a bully. It's what happens when someone takes the last piece of chicken joy and they know you wanted it. That's pang-aapi.
usage_notes: Bilang salitang-ugat, nilalapian ito upang makabuo ng mga pandiwa tulad ng 'apihin', 'mang-api', at pangngalan tulad ng 'pang-aapi'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang kasalanan ang **mang-api** ng kapwa.","translation":"It is a sin **to oppress** others."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **apihin** ang iyong nakababatang kapatid.","translation":"Don't **maltreat** your younger sibling."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagkakaroon ng unawaan, pagkakaisa, at kawalan ng alitan o hindi pagkakaunawaan.
original_explanation: After the "tampuhan," when you and your jowa finally talk things out and make up. That peaceful resolution is pagkakasundo. It's when you and your sibling finally agree on how to split the last piece of pizza, or when two warring factions in the office call a truce. It's the "bessy na ulit tayo" moment.
usage_notes: Can refer to a formal settlement (like in a legal case) or an informal understanding between people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng **pagkakasundo** ang dalawang panig matapos ang mahabang negosasyon.","translation":"The two sides reached a **settlement** after a long negotiation."},{"sentence":"Ang mahalaga sa magkapatid ay ang kanilang **pagkakasundo**.","translation":"What's important between siblings is their **harmony**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto o proseso ng pag-aayos at pag-aantabay para sa isang tiyak na layunin o kaganapan.
etymology: From 'handa' (ready). The prefix 'pag-' and the repetition of the first syllable 'ha' ('pag-ha-handa') indicates a continuous or formal act of preparing.
original_explanation: This is what you do before a big presentation, a first date, or when your in-laws are visiting. It's the opposite of 'bahala na si Batman.' Think meal prep for the week, reviewing for an exam, or putting on your 'pamasok' clothes for a Zoom call. Maximum effort before the main event.
usage_notes: Often used for events, meals, projects, and personal readiness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paghahanda** para sa pista ay maagang sinimulan.","translation":"The **preparation** for the fiesta started early."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang **paghahanda** sa isip at katawan bago ang isang maraton.","translation":"Mental and physical **preparation** is important before a marathon."}]

meaning_filipino: Mag-alok at magbenta ng mga produkto o serbisyo kapalit ng pera.
original_explanation: The hustle! Whether you're selling fishballs in a cart, pre-loved clothes on IG, or insurance plans to your friends, you're 'nagtitinga.' The backbone of the Philippine economy, from the palengke to the online sellers.
usage_notes: A general term for selling goods.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naisipan niyang **magtinda** ng yema cake para kumita ng extra.","translation":"She thought of **selling** yema cake to earn extra money."},{"sentence":"Saan ka ba nagpa-planong **magtinda** ng mga damit na ito?","translation":"Where do you plan to **sell** these clothes?"}]

translation: to appoint; to choose; to select
meaning_filipino: Ang pormal na pagpili o pagtatalaga sa isang tao para sa isang katungkulan o karangalan.
original_explanation: The action of making someone 'The One.' This is what the President does to his cabinet, or what a pageant committee does to the new Miss Universe. It's the verb form of making a 'hirang.' Hindi ito basta 'pumili,' may weight, may formality, may press release. When you 'hirangin' someone, you're basically saying, 'Out of all the choices, it's you.'
usage_notes: A formal verb. "Piliin" is the more common, everyday equivalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pangulo ang may kapangyarihang **hirangin** ang mga kasapi ng kanyang gabinete.","translation":"The president has the power to **appoint** the members of his cabinet."},{"sentence":"Siya ang napili upang **hirangin** bilang kinatawan ng mga mag-aaral.","translation":"She was chosen to be **appointed** as the student representative."}]

translation: parental love; a parent's love for a child
meaning_filipino: Ang natatanging uri ng pag-ibig, pag-aaruga, at pagsasakripisyo na ipinadarama ng isang magulang sa kanyang anak.
etymology: A compound word from pagmamahal (love) + anak (child).
original_explanation: This is that special kind of love that makes a mother wake up at 4 AM to cook baon, or a father work abroad for 20 years just to send his kids to college. It's unconditional, often involves a lot of sacrifice, and is the reason for the 'utang na loob' dynamic in many Filipino families. It's the 'aalagaan kita hanggang pagtanda' promise in noun form.
usage_notes: A specific compound noun that is more descriptive and emphatic than just 'pagmamahal ng magulang' (love of a parent).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Walang kapantay ang **pagmamahal-anak**.","translation":"A **parent's love for a child** is unparalleled."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang tunay na **pagmamahal-anak** nang isakripisyo ng kanyang ina ang lahat para sa kanya.","translation":"She felt true **parental love** when her mother sacrificed everything for her."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa ng mga organisadong gawain upang makamit ang isang partikular na layunin, lalo na sa politika o pagbebenta.
original_explanation: That time of year when your street is suddenly full of posters with smiling faces, and free t-shirts and calendars appear out of nowhere. It's the act of trying to win votes, or in a non-political sense, trying to promote something. Your friend who's trying to get everyone to watch a new K-drama is technically nangangampanya.
usage_notes: Most commonly used in a political context, but can also be used for marketing or advocacy campaigns.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bawal **mangampanya** sa araw mismo ng eleksyon.","translation":"It is forbidden **to campaign** on the day of the election itself."},{"sentence":"Sila ay **nangangampanya** para sa mas malinis na kapaligiran.","translation":"They are **campaigning** for a cleaner environment."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagkayod o paggayat ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay niyog, gamit ang isang kasangkapang may matatalas na ngipin.
original_explanation: That repetitive motion your tita makes with a coconut on a spiky metal stool. The result is the fresh coconut shavings for your biko or palitaw. It's an arm workout, pre-CrossFit edition.
usage_notes: Often refers specifically to the act of grating coconut using a traditional Filipino grater ('kudkuran').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakapagod ang **kudkod** nang **kudkod** ng niyog para sa piyesta.","translation":"It's tiring to continuously **grate** coconut for the fiesta."},{"sentence":"Ang sariwang **kudkod** ng niyog ay mahalaga sa paggawa ng gata.","translation":"The fresh **grating** of coconut is essential for making coconut milk."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat o grupo ng mga bulaklak, bunga, o anumang magkakasamang bagay na nakaayos nang siksikan.
original_explanation: Parang barkada niyo lang, laging magkakasama. Or yung bouquet ng bulaklak na binigay sa'yo nung nanliligaw pa lang siya, 'yun ang talumpon. Ngayon, ni isang tangkay wala na. Hugot!
usage_notes: Often used for flowers, fruits, or even a small group of people huddled together.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **talumpon** ng rosas ang iniwan niya sa aking mesa.","translation":"He left a **bunch** of roses on my table."},{"sentence":"Ang sarap tingnan ng mga **talumpon** ng ubas sa puno.","translation":"The **clusters** of grapes on the vine are lovely to look at."}]

translation: to be able to hit (a target); to get right; to win (a lottery)
meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang matamaan ang isang puntirya, makuha ang tamang sagot, o manalo sa isang sugal o lottery.
original_explanation: It's that feeling of pure victory when you shoot your crumpled paper into the trash can from across the room. Or when you guess the plot twist of a movie correctly. Or, the ultimate dream, when your lotto numbers finally hit the jackpot. 'Sana all, makatama sa lotto!'
usage_notes: Versatile word. Can mean hitting a physical target, getting a correct answer, or winning a game of chance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **makatama** ako sa pagsusulit kahit hindi ako nag-review.","translation":"I hope I can **get the answers right** on the exam even if I didn't review."},{"sentence":"Isang beses lang siyang tumira pero nagawa niyang **makatama** sa bullseye.","translation":"He only took one shot but he managed **to hit** the bullseye."},{"sentence":"Ang pangarap niya ay **makatama** sa lotto para makatulong sa pamilya.","translation":"His dream is **to win** the lottery to help his family."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagkain o pagpatay sa isang hayop para gawing pagkain, na ginagawa ng isang maninilang hayop.
original_explanation: The National Geographic action verb. It's what a lion does to a zebra, or what an eagle does to a snake. In the urban jungle, it's what a 'buwaya' (corrupt official/person) does to the public funds, or what a scammer does to an unsuspecting victim. It means to viciously go after your target.
usage_notes: The root 'sila' (with stress on the second syllable, /si-LA/) means prey. This is different from 'sila' (/SI-la/), meaning 'they'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inabangan ng buwaya ang usa upang **silain** ito sa pampang.","translation":"The crocodile waited for the deer to **prey on** it at the riverbank."},{"sentence":"Ang maliliit na negosyo ay takot na **silain** ng malalaking korporasyon.","translation":"Small businesses are afraid of being **devoured** by large corporations."}]

translation: to save; to rescue; to deliver from danger
meaning_filipino: Iligtas mula sa kapahamakan, panganib, o paghihirap; tubusin.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping "i-" at salitang-ugat na "adya" (pagliligtas).
original_explanation: This is the Darna-level of saving someone. It's not just helping you cross the street; it's pulling you out of a burning building or saving you from a great evil. Very dramatic, very biblical. You'd usually hear this in prayers, like "Iadya mo kami sa lahat ng masama."
usage_notes: Isang pormal at medyo makalumang salita. Karaniwang ginagamit sa panitikan, panalangin, at mga pormal na talumpati.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nanalangin siya na **iadya** ang kanyang pamilya sa anumang sakuna.","translation":"He prayed to **save** his family from any disaster."},{"sentence":"\"O, Panginoon, **iadya** mo po kami sa tukso.\"","translation":"\"Oh, Lord, **deliver** us from temptation.\""}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kabuuan ng mga katangian, pag-uugali, at kalikasan na inaasahan o iniuugnay sa isang lalaki; ang estado ng pagiging isang lalaki.
original_explanation: This is the essence of being a "tunay na lalaki," but what that means is always up for debate. Is it about having muscles and a deep voice? Is it about being a provider? Is it about not being afraid to cry? Pagka-lalaki is the whole package of masculinity, both the traditional stereotypes (strong, silent type) and the modern, more nuanced versions. It’s the "macho" in machismo, but also the "gentle" in gentleman.
usage_notes: Often used in discussions about gender roles, identity, and societal expectations. The hyphen is often used to distinguish it from `pagkalaki` (the way something grew).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinamon niya ang **pagka-lalaki** ko nang sabihin niyang duwag ako.","translation":"He challenged my **manhood** when he said I was a coward."},{"sentence":"Ang tunay na **pagka-lalaki** ay hindi nasusukat sa lakas, kundi sa respeto at pananagutan.","translation":"True **masculinity** is not measured by strength, but by respect and responsibility."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maasim na likidong ginagamit bilang pampalasa o preserbatibo, na resulta ng permentasyon ng etanol.
etymology: From Sanskrit śukra ('clear, bright') or through Malay cuka.
original_explanation: The lifeblood of Filipino sawsawan. From the spicy pinakurat to the simple white vinegar with garlic and chili, 'suka' is the sour counterpoint to everything rich and fatty. It's what makes adobo adobo, and what you dip your chicharon in. It's the acid trip you actually want.
usage_notes: The pronunciation /SU-ka/ with stress on the first syllable distinguishes it from `suká` (vomit).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pahingi ng **suka** na may sili para sa chicharon.","translation":"Can I have some **vinegar** with chili for the pork rinds?"},{"sentence":"Ang adobo ay niluluto sa toyo at **suka**.","translation":"Adobo is cooked in soy sauce and **vinegar**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay ng isang piraso ng materyal, tulad ng tela, upang takpan ang isang butas o sira sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is what your lola does to your favorite butas-butas na shorts. It's the ultimate act of "pwedeng-pwede pa 'to!" It's basically putting a band-aid on your clothes. "My budget is tight this month, so I'll just magtatagpi these jeans."
usage_notes: Future tense of "magtagpi".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Magtatagpi** ako ng butas sa aking pantalon gamit ang lumang tela.","translation":"I **will patch** the hole in my pants using an old cloth."},{"sentence":"Si nanay ay **magtatagpi** ng mga sirang damit mamayang hapon.","translation":"Mother **will patch** the torn clothes later this afternoon."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng mataas na pamantayan sa pagpili; hindi basta-basta tumatanggap o nasisiyahan sa anumang bagay.
original_explanation: How your parents describe you when you're still single at 30. It's being meticulous with your choices, whether it's for a jowa, a job, or the perfect ripe mango at the palengke. You're not just settling for anything. Some call it picky, you call it having standards. 'Ang arte, ang mapili!'
usage_notes: Can have a slightly negative connotation (picky) or a neutral one (selective).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masyado siyang **mapili** sa pagkain kaya laging konti lang ang nakakain niya.","translation":"She is too **choosy** with food so she always eats just a little."},{"sentence":"Hindi naman sa pagiging **mapili**, gusto ko lang makasiguro sa desisyon ko.","translation":"It's not about being **selective**, I just want to be sure of my decision."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagdudulot ng hapdi, kirot, o hirap sa katawan o damdamin.
original_explanation: The feeling you get when you see your crush with someone else. Or when you stub your toe on the leg of a chair. Or when your data plan runs out mid-binge-watch. Basically, it's the universal "Aray!" in word form, whether for your body or your puso.
usage_notes: Can describe physical pain (masakit ang ulo - headache) or emotional pain (masakit na salita - hurtful words).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Masakit** ang ulo ko dahil sa init ng panahon.","translation":"My head is **aching** because of the hot weather."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magsalita ng **masakit** sa iyong kapwa.","translation":"Don't say **hurtful** things to others."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang gagawing pagkakalat o pagkakalatag ng mga buto sa lupa upang tumubo. Sa matalinghagang kahulugan, ito ay ang pagpapalaganap ng isang ideya, damdamin, o kalagayan.
original_explanation: Literally, what farmers do with seeds. Figuratively, what your chismosa neighbor does with rumors. 'Maghahasik ng lagim' (will sow terror) is the classic headline for a horror movie or a news report about a criminal. It's about spreading something, whether it's good vibes, good seeds, or fake news on social media.
usage_notes: Future tense of maghasik. Often used figuratively to mean 'to spread' something intangible like fear, discord, or news.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang magsasaka ay **maghahasik** ng palay sa susunod na linggo.","translation":"The farmer **will sow** rice seeds next week."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **maghahasik** ng maling impormasyon sa social media.","translation":"Do not **spread** false information on social media."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi isinama o pinansin; lumampas sa isang bahagi o hakbang.
original_explanation: That feeling when you're reading a Terms & Conditions and you just scroll to the bottom and click 'Agree'? You just lumaktaw. It's skipping a question on an exam, fast-forwarding through the boring part of a movie, or ignoring a step in a recipe and wondering why it failed. It's the art of the shortcut.
usage_notes: Can be used for physically jumping over something, but is more commonly used for skipping items in a sequence, list, or process.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lumaktaw** siya sa ilang pahina ng libro dahil nababagot na siya.","translation":"He **skipped over** a few pages of the book because he was getting bored."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **lumaktaw** ng kahit anong hakbang sa proseso.","translation":"Don't **skip** any step in the process."}]

translation: to be able to disturb; to cause inconvenience
meaning_filipino: Ang maging sanhi ng gambala, istorbo, o pagkaantala sa gawain o kapayapaan ng iba.
original_explanation: That feeling you get when you're about to ask a question but you start with "Sorry kung makaaabala ako..." It's the national pastime of being overly polite. It's what the videoke next door is doing at 2 AM. It's the "unexpected item in the bagging area" when you're in a hurry.
usage_notes: Often used in polite requests, sometimes in the form "nakaaabala" (present/completed tense) or "makakaabala" (future tense).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayokong **makaabala** sa iyong pag-aaral.","translation":"I don't want **to disturb** your studies."},{"sentence":"Pasensya na kung **nakaabala** ako sa inyo.","translation":"I'm sorry if I **disturbed** you."}]

translation: Maidenhood; state of being a young, unmarried woman
meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o panahon sa buhay ng isang babae kung kailan siya ay bata pa, wala pang asawa, at itinuturing na isang dalaga.
original_explanation: This is the girl's 'single and ready to mingle' era, but make it traditional. It's the period of being a 'dalaga'— a young woman. Think of it as the time before 'misis,' filled with debut parties, harana (back in the day), and your lola constantly reminding you to act like a 'dalagang Pilipina.' It's the state of being, not just the age.
usage_notes: Carries traditional and sometimes conservative connotations about a young woman's life before marriage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Inaalala niya ang masasayang araw ng kanyang **pagkadalaga**.","translation":"She reminisces about the happy days of her **maidenhood**."},{"sentence":"Ang pag-aaral ang prayoridad niya sa kanyang **pagkadalaga**.","translation":"Her studies are her priority during her time as a **young woman**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsasagawa o pagdalo sa seremonya ng Unang Komunyon sa relihiyong Katoliko.
original_explanation: A major life event for Filipino Catholic kids. It's when you get to wear a cute white dress or suit, learn a bunch of prayers, and finally receive the host. It's a solemn event followed by a not-so-solemn party with spaghetti, fried chicken, and a "My First Holy Communion" tarpaulin.
usage_notes: A specific cultural and religious term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa susunod na Linggo na **magpriprimera-komunyon** ang pamangkin ko.","translation":"My nephew will **have his First Communion** next Sunday."},{"sentence":"Saan ka **nagprimera-komunyon**?","translation":"Where did you **have your First Communion**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging biktima ng panloloko o pandaraya, karaniwan ay may kinalaman sa pera o ari-arian, sa pamamagitan ng tusong pamamaraan.
etymology: From na- (verb prefix) + budol, from the "Budol-Budol Gang," a type of swindling syndicate. The term itself is slang.
original_explanation: From the classic "budol-budol gang" scam. Now, it's used for everything! Got tricked into buying something you don't need from an online ad at 2 AM? "Nabudol ka!" Your friends convinced you to go out for "one drink" that turned into an all-nighter? "Nabudol!" It's the modern Filipino term for being expertly fooled, whether by a con artist or a Shopee sale.
usage_notes: Originally referred to a specific scam, but its meaning has broadened to include any instance of being tricked or swindled, often in a playful or minor way.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Akala ko totoo, **nabudol** lang pala ako ng pekeng seller online.","translation":"I thought it was real, I just **got scammed** by a fake seller online."},{"sentence":"Tara, kain tayo sa labas. Sige na, **magpabudol** ka na sa akin.","translation":"Come on, let's eat out. Go on, let me **convince/trick** you."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bahagi sa harap at likod ng sasakyan na idinisenyo upang sumalo sa epekto ng maliliit na banggaan.
original_explanation: The part of your car that's first to get a scratch in Manila traffic or a tight parking spot. It's basically a battle scar magnet. Also, a term sometimes used for a beer belly that sticks out. "Uy, lumalaki na 'yang bamper mo ah!"
usage_notes: A colloquial, direct loanword. The formal term might be 'depensa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May gasgas ang **bamper** ng kotse pagkatapos kong pumarada.","translation":"The car's **bumper** has a scratch after I parked."},{"sentence":"Magkano kaya magpaayos ng yuping **bamper**?","translation":"How much would it cost to fix a dented **bumper**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay, karaniwan ay daan o landas, na maraming kurba, liko, o paikot-ikot; hindi tuwid.
original_explanation: Parang daan paakyat ng Baguio o 'yung kwento ng kaibigan mong maraming side-story bago marating ang point. 'Yung usapan niyo, likaw-likaw bago naging kayo. Ganon. It's the opposite of 'straight to the point'.
usage_notes: Reduplication of 'likaw' (coil, curve) to intensify the meaning.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **likaw-likaw** na daan sa kabundukan ay nagbibigay ng magandang tanawin.","translation":"The **winding** road in the mountains offers a beautiful view."},{"sentence":"Nalito ako sa **likaw-likaw** niyang paliwanag.","translation":"I got confused by his **meandering** explanation."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na hayop na mabilis dumami, karaniwang itinuturing na peste, at may mahabang buntot.
original_explanation: The uninvited tenant in your house that doesn't pay rent. The reason you suddenly hear scratching sounds in the ceiling at 3 AM. In the Philippines, seeing a 'daga' can range from a minor annoyance (small house mouse) to a major problem (a rat the size of a kitten). It's also a classic insult for someone who is sneaky or a thief ("mukhang daga").
usage_notes: The term covers both rats and mice, although "maliit na daga" can be used to specify a mouse.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May nakitang **daga** sa kusina kaya kailangan nating maglinis.","translation":"A **rat** was seen in the kitchen so we need to clean."},{"sentence":"Takot na takot siya sa **daga**.","translation":"She is terrified of **mice**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malalim na pag-unawa o pag-alam sa kahulugan, dahilan, o kalikasan ng isang bagay na mahirap intindihin.
original_explanation: This isn't just 'gets ko na'. To 'tarok' something is to understand it on a soul-deep level. It's when you finally understand your parents' sacrifices, or when you finally grasp a complex philosophical concept after weeks of study. It's the "Aha!" moment on steroids. "Hindi ko matarok ang lalim ng kanyang pag-iisip" means "I can't fathom the depths of his thoughts." It’s a word for hugot lines and deep talks over coffee.
usage_notes: Almost always used in its conjugated forms, such as 'matarok' (to be able to fathom), 'tarukin' (to try to fathom), or 'di-matarok' (unfathomable).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap **tarukin** ang tunay niyang intensyon.","translation":"It's difficult to **fathom** his true intentions."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko **matarok** kung bakit niya ginawa iyon.","translation":"I cannot **comprehend** why he did that."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging manhid; kawalan ng pakiramdam, pisikal man o emosyonal.
original_explanation: That feeling when your crush walks by and you pretend you don't care, but deep inside, you're screaming. It's the 'seen-zone' energy personified. The emotional equivalent of your foot falling asleep.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa pisikal na pamamanhid (hal. mula sa anestisya) o emosyonal na kawalang-interes.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagkamanhid** niya sa harap ng trahedya ay nakababahala.","translation":"His **apathy** in the face of tragedy is worrying."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman ko ang **pagkamanhid** ng aking binti matapos maupo nang matagal.","translation":"I felt the **numbness** in my leg after sitting for a long time."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tanyag na pagkaing Koreano na binubuo ng isang mangkok ng mainit na kanin na may sahog na mga gulay, karne (karaniwang baka), gochujang (chili pepper paste), at itlog.
original_explanation: That Korean rice bowl you order when you want to feel a *little* healthy because of all the veggies, but you know you're just there for the samgyup experience. It's the "I want K-BBQ but I'm eating alone" meal. You mix it all up like your feelings after watching a K-drama finale.
usage_notes: A loanword. The spelling is retained from the original Korean.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong orderin ang **bibimbap** sa restawran na iyon.","translation":"My favorite thing to order at that restaurant is **bibimbap**."},{"sentence":"Haluin mong mabuti ang **bibimbap** bago kainin.","translation":"Mix the **bibimbap** well before eating."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o organisasyon na bumibili ng mga produkto o serbisyo mula sa isang tindahan o negosyo.
original_explanation: The person who is always right, even when they're asking for the manager because their ice is too cold. In the palengke, they're your 'suki'. In a BPO, they're the reason you need another cup of coffee. They hold the money, so you flash your best 'customer service' smile.
usage_notes: The word "customer" is widely used in business and retail settings in the Philippines. "Kostumer" is the Filipinized spelling. "Suki" refers to a regular, loyal customer. "Kliyente" is more for professional services.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat laging magalang sa **customer**.","translation":"You should always be polite to the **customer**."},{"sentence":"May reklamo ang **customer** tungkol sa natanggap niyang produkto.","translation":"The **customer** has a complaint about the product they received."}]

meaning_filipino: Ilubog nang bahagya at sandali ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay pagkain, sa isang likido tulad ng sarsa o suka.
original_explanation: The sacred act of giving your food its soulmate. Whether it's to isawsaw your french fries in ketchup, your chicharon in vinegar, or your pandesal in coffee, it's that quick plunge that adds a whole new dimension of flavor. The golden rule: don't double-dip, especially if the sawsawan is communal!
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **isawsaw** ang isaw sa maanghang na suka.","translation":"Don't forget to **dip** the isaw in the spicy vinegar."},{"sentence":"Paborito niyang **isawsaw** ang biskwit sa mainit na gatas.","translation":"Her favorite thing is to **dip** biscuits in hot milk."}]

meaning_filipino: Magtinda ng balut, isang uri ng pagkain na nilagang itlog ng pato na may nabuo nang sisiw sa loob.
original_explanation: The job of the iconic nighttime street vendor, whose cry of 'Baluuuut!' echoes through Filipino neighborhoods. They are the purveyors of the Philippines' most famous (or infamous) street food and late-night snack.
usage_notes: Refers to the occupation or act of being a 'balut' vendor. Not to be confused with 'magbalot' which means 'to wrap'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gabi-gabi siyang umiikot sa aming lugar para **magbalot**.","translation":"He goes around our area every night to **sell balut**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng naninirahan sa isang dormitoryo.
original_explanation: The girl living her best (or most broke) life in a dorm. Master of instant noodles, budgeting her baon until the next "padala" from her parents, and sharing chismis with her roomies. Her natural habitat is a bunk bed surrounded by books and drying laundry.
usage_notes: Ang katapat nito para sa lalaki ay 'dormitoryano'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bilang isang **dormitoryana**, natuto akong maging independent.","translation":"As a **female dormer**, I learned to be independent."},{"sentence":"Nag-reunion ang mga dating **dormitoryana** ng St. Agnes Dorm.","translation":"The former **female dorm residents** of St. Agnes Dorm had a reunion."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang indibidwal na may tungkuling mamahala, mangasiwa, o magpatakbo ng isang institusyon, ari-arian, o negosyo.
original_explanation: The more formal, almost-boomer version of "admin". This is the tito who manages the family hacienda or the building manager who tells you off for loud parties. Sounds more official and less techy than just 'admin'.
usage_notes: More formal than "admin". Often used for estate managers, building managers, or heads of institutions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **administrador** ng gusali ang nag-aapruba ng mga renovation permit.","translation":"The building **administrator** is the one who approves renovation permits."},{"sentence":"Siya ang itinalagang **administrador** ng naiwang ari-arian ng kanyang mga magulang.","translation":"He was appointed as the **administrator** of the properties left by his parents."}]

translation: to get scratched; to have scratches
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng mga guhit o marka sa isang ibabaw dahil sa pagkiskis o pagtama ng isang matulis na bagay.
etymology: From `magka-` (prefix indicating having or acquiring something) + `gasgas` (scratch).
original_explanation: This is what happens to your phone when you put it in the same pocket as your keys. Or your car after squeezing through a tight spot in the parking lot. Or your heart after a situationship. Basically, 'pag may damage na, pero hindi pa totally sira.
usage_notes: Often refers to superficial damage on a surface.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ingatan mo ang bagong kotse para hindi **magkagasgas**.","translation":"Take care of the new car so it doesn't **get scratched**."},{"sentence":"Ayokong **magkagasgas** ang screen ng cellphone ko.","translation":"I don't want my cellphone screen **to get scratched**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpatay o pananakit sa pamamagitan ng pagsakal o pagpigil sa paghinga mula sa labas na presyon sa leeg o lalamunan.
original_explanation: A very dark and serious word you'd hopefully only encounter in crime documentaries or news reports. It's the act of choking someone, usually with criminal intent. Not to be confused with 'nabulunan' (choking on food). This one is external and violent.
usage_notes: A medical and forensic term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Estranggulasyon** ang sanhi ng pagkamatay ng biktima ayon sa mga forensik.","translation":"**Strangulation** was the cause of the victim's death according to the forensics."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan sa medisina ang mga panganib ng **estranggulasyon**.","translation":"The dangers of **strangulation** are studied in medicine."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-usli ng ibabang labi, karaniwang tanda ng pagtatampo, pagkalungkot, o pagiging malapit nang umiyak.
original_explanation: The official facial expression for 'tampo.' It's that subtle (or not-so-subtle) pout you make when your Jollibee order is wrong, or when your SO forgets your monthsary. The paglabi is a silent weapon, a visual cue that says 'You better fix this, or else...'
usage_notes: Specifically refers to pouting as an expression of displeasure or sadness, distinct from just having prominent lips.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **paglabi** lang ng bata, alam na ng ina na may gusto itong hingin.","translation":"Just one **pout** from the child, and the mother already knows it wants to ask for something."},{"sentence":"Napansin ko ang kanyang **paglabi** nang hindi siya pinayagang sumama.","translation":"I noticed her **pouting** when she wasn't allowed to come along."}]

translation: to leave something for someone (e.g., food)
meaning_filipino: Ang sadyang paglalaan o hindi pag-ubos ng isang bagay, karaniwan ay pagkain, upang may matira para sa kapakinabangan ng iba.
original_explanation: The ultimate act of love in a Filipino household. When there's a delicious ulam, someone will shout, '**Ipagtira** n'yo si bunso!' which means 'Save some for the youngest!' It's the direct opposite of the tragic 'naubusan ka' (you missed out). This verb is the foundation of family food dynamics.
usage_notes: Most commonly used for food, but can also be used for other resources. It's a benefactive verb indicating something is saved for someone else.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag ninyong ubusin ang adobo, **ipagtira** ninyo ang tatay ninyo.","translation":"Don't finish the adobo, **leave some for** your father."},{"sentence":"Lagi niya akong **ipinagtitira** ng paborito kong keyk.","translation":"She always **saves** my favorite cake **for me**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang lugar, tulad ng ilog o kalsada, na hindi maaaring tawirin dahil sa panganib, harang, o kawalan ng daanan.
original_explanation: That feeling when EDSA is at a total standstill during rush hour—that's walang-tawid. Or a flooded street during a typhoon that even the bravest Grab driver won't dare enter. It's a literal or figurative "you shall not pass" situation.
usage_notes: Used to describe physical barriers that prevent crossing from one side to another.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **walang-tawid** ang ilog dahil sa malakas na agos.","translation":"The river became **uncrossable** due to the strong current."},{"sentence":"Sa sobrang traffic, halos **walang-tawid** na ang kalsada.","translation":"With so much traffic, the road is almost **impassable**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang detalyadong panukala o pamamaraan para sa paggawa o pagkamit ng isang bagay; isang balangkas, disenyo, o guhit.
original_explanation: Ito yung bagay na laging "drawing". Yung "tara, kape tayo" na hindi natutuloy. O kaya yung New Year's resolution mong mag-gym. Sa project management, ito yung blueprint. Sa barkada, ito yung "See you guys!" na alam mong forda-cancel din sa huli.
usage_notes: Maaari ring gamitin bilang pandiwa: "magplano" (mag-plano).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **plano** natin para sa bakasyon sa susunod na buwan?","translation":"What's our **plan** for the vacation next month?"},{"sentence":"Ang arkitekto ay nagpakita ng **plano** ng itatayong gusali.","translation":"The architect showed the **plan** of the building to be constructed."}]

translation: to cry one's heart out; to cry excessively
meaning_filipino: Umiyak nang labis-labis o paulit-ulit dahil sa matinding damdamin.
etymology: From `mag-` + `paka-` + `iyak-iyak` (reduplication of `iyak`). The reduplication signifies repeated or prolonged action.
original_explanation: That moment after a breakup when you're in your room, listening to a Moira dela Torre playlist on loop, and just letting it all out. It's not just crying; it's an Olympic-level crying event. "Nang iwan siya ng jowa niya, tatlong araw siyang nagpakaiyak-iyak sa kwarto."
usage_notes: Emphasizes the intensity and duration of crying.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagpakaiyak-iyak** ang bata nang hindi mabilhan ng laruan.","translation":"The child **cried and cried** when he wasn't bought a toy."},{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang **magpakaiyak-iyak** diyan, hindi na siya babalik.","translation":"Don't **cry your heart out** there, he/she is not coming back anymore."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paniniwala o doktrina na naniniwalang posibleng makipag-ugnayan ang mga nabubuhay sa mga espiritu ng mga pumanaw, karaniwan sa pamamagitan ng isang medyum.
original_explanation: Yung practice ng pakikipag-usap sa mga multo at kaluluwa, pero hindi via Messenger. Ito 'yung ginagawa sa mga horror movie kung saan may bilog na mesa, kandila, at isang medyum na biglang mag-iiba ang boses. Think "Spirit of the Glass" pero mas seryosohan at may sariling pilosopiya.
