usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming kontrobersya ang bumabalot sa paniniwalang **espiritismo**.","translation":"There are many controversies surrounding the belief of **spiritism**."},{"sentence":"Ang **espiritismo** ay naging popular noong ika-19 na siglo.","translation":"**Spiritism** became popular in the 19th century."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng barko na ginagamit sa paghila o pagtulak ng iba pang malalaking sasakyang-dagat na hindi makagalaw nang mag-isa sa masikip na daungan.
etymology: From Spanish 'lancha' (launch, boat) and Tagalog 'panghila' (for pulling).
original_explanation: The small but mighty barko that does the heavy lifting, like that one friend who always carries the group project. It's the BRP (Barkong Rume-rescue sa Project) of the port, pulling giant container ships like a pro.
usage_notes: This is a compound noun. 'Lantsa' means a launch or motorboat, and 'panghila' specifies its function.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ang **lantsang panghila** upang i-dock ang dambuhalang cargo ship.","translation":"The **tugboat** was used to dock the giant cargo ship."},{"sentence":"Maliit man, malakas ang makina ng **lantsang panghila**.","translation":"Although small, the engine of the **tugboat** is powerful."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang posibilidad ng pagharap sa panganib, pinsala, o kawalan.
original_explanation: That feeling when you send a risky text and turn off your phone. O kaya 'yung pag-invest mo sa crypto kasi sabi ng tropa mo "to the moon!" daw. Risko is the Tagalog for "YOLO," the potential for either great reward or epic failure. Every "bahala na" moment is powered by a calculated (or not-so-calculated) risko.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang **risko** sa negosyong pinasok niya.","translation":"There is a big **risk** in the business he entered."},{"sentence":"Kahit may **risko**, itinuloy pa rin niya ang kanyang plano.","translation":"Even with the **risk**, he still pushed through with his plan."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pagkain na gawa sa malagkit na bigas na niluto sa maraming tubig hanggang sa lumambot at lumapot.
original_explanation: The ultimate Filipino comfort food. It's what your nanay makes when you're sick. It's the go-to cheap meal after a night out. Plain lugaw is the base, but add toppings like tokw'a, baboy, chicharon, and a hard-boiled egg, and it becomes a "goto" or "arroz caldo." Lugaw is life. As they say, "sa panahon ng kagipitan, lugaw is the key."
usage_notes: Often associated with being sick or as an affordable meal. The phrase "Leni Lugaw" was a political pejorative, but her supporters reclaimed it.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masarap kumain ng mainit na **lugaw** kapag malamig ang panahon.","translation":"It's delicious to eat hot **rice porridge** when the weather is cold."},{"sentence":"Naghanda si nanay ng **lugaw** dahil may lagnat ako.","translation":"Mom prepared **rice porridge** because I have a fever."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang estado ng pagiging walang anumang gawain, tungkulin, o aktibidad na kailangang isagawa.
etymology: Mula sa "wala" (none) at "gagawin" (will do), ang hinaharap na anyo ng pandiwang "gawin".
original_explanation: The official mood for Sunday afternoons. That feeling when you've scrolled through all your social media feeds, watched everything on your Netflix list, and now you're just staring at the ceiling, wondering about your life choices. It's the opposite of being busy, the national sport of the *tambay*.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a state of boredom or free time. Can be used interchangeably with 'walang ginagawa', but this one can specifically refer to a future lack of plans.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Walang-gagawin** ako bukas, kaya pwede tayong lumabas.","translation":"I have **nothing to do** tomorrow, so we can go out."},{"sentence":"Nakatunganga lang siya dahil **walang-gagawin** sa opisina.","translation":"He was just staring blankly because he had **nothing to do** at the office."}]

translation: Habanero; a native or inhabitant of Havana, Cuba
meaning_filipino: Isang taong likas na naninirahan o nagmula sa Havana, ang kabisera ng Cuba.
original_explanation: Honestly, you'll probably only hear this word in a history class or a very specific quiz bee. It's the Filipino word for someone from Havana. Think old cars, cigars, and salsa music. Not to be confused with 'Hapon' (Japanese) or 'habang' (while). It's a "pang-flex ng vocabulary" kind of word.
usage_notes: Bihira nang gamitin sa pang-araw-araw na usapan. Mas karaniwan sa mga aklat ng kasaysayan o heograpiya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **Habanes** ay kilala sa kanilang masiglang kultura at musika.","translation":"The **Habaneros** are known for their vibrant culture and music."},{"sentence":"Isang **Habanes** ang nagwagi sa patimpalak sa paggawa ng tabako.","translation":"A **Habanero** won the cigar-making competition."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis at patagong pagkuha o pag-agaw sa isang bagay na hindi sa iyo, karaniwan ay maliit na halaga.
etymology: The origin is uncertain, but it is a widely understood colloquial term.
original_explanation: This isn't a grand heist. *Pagsikwat* is low-key, small-time theft. It's snatching the last piece of chicken joy when no one's looking. It's the art of getting free office supplies for your kid's school project. It's faster than 'pagnanakaw' (stealing) and has a more mischievous, less criminal vibe, but make no mistake, it's still taking something that isn't yours.
usage_notes: A colloquial or slang term for petty theft.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nahuli sa CCTV ang **pagsikwat** niya ng cellphone sa loob ng tindahan.","translation":"His **act of swiping** a cellphone inside the store was caught on CCTV."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa **pagsikwat** ng pagkain mula sa mga plato ng kanyang mga kaibigan.","translation":"He is known for **pilfering** food from his friends' plates."}]

meaning_filipino: May hangganan; hindi malawak o marami; may takdang bilang o sukat.
original_explanation: "Sorry, **limitado** lang po ang slots." The story of every Filipino trying to get a government ID, a concert ticket, or a seat at a popular samgyupsal place. It means there's a boundary, a cap, a "hanggang dito na lang." Your data plan can be **limitado**, your patience can be **limitado**, and yes, the "unli-rice" promo might actually be **limitado**.
usage_notes: Very common in both formal and informal settings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Limitado** lamang ang mga tiket na ibebenta para sa konsiyerto.","translation":"Only a **limited** number of tickets will be sold for the concert."},{"sentence":"Pasensya na, **limitado** ang aking kaalaman tungkol diyan.","translation":"I'm sorry, my knowledge about that is **limited**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang makabagong termino para sa matinding pagtatalo, pag-aaway, o pagpapalitan ng masasakit na salita sa pagitan ng mga indibidwal o grupo sa internet, partikular sa social media.
etymology: Combination of English 'online' and Filipino slang 'bardagulan' (brawl, chaotic fight).
original_explanation: The national sport of the Philippines, now with a digital arena. This is when a simple comment section on Facebook turns into a no-holds-barred war of words, complete with ad hominem attacks, screenshots of old posts, and the classic 'Respeto lang po.' It's the modern-day *sabong* (cockfight), but the chickens are our online personas.
usage_notes: A very popular term to describe comment section wars on platforms like Facebook, X (Twitter), and TikTok.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula sa isang simpleng post, nauwi sa **online bardagulan** ang dalawang kampo ng fans.","translation":"It started with a simple post, but it ended in an **online clash** between the two fan camps."},{"sentence":"Huwag ka nang sumali sa **online bardagulan**, masasayang lang ang oras mo.","translation":"Don't join the **flame war**, you'll just waste your time."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na ang hanapbuhay ay ang pag-aalaga at pagbebenta ng baboy, o ang lugar kung saan inaalagaan ang mga baboy.
original_explanation: Literally, someone who raises pigs. Calling someone this can be a bit tricky. In a rural context, it's a respectable job. In a city context, if you say 'Ang kalat mo, para kang **magbabuyan**,' you're probably talking about their messy room, not their career choice.
usage_notes: Can refer to the person (pig farmer) or the place (piggery). Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May malaking negosyo ang tiyuhin ko, isa siyang **magbabuyan** sa Batangas.","translation":"My uncle has a big business, he is a **pig farmer** in Batangas."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagiging mas malaki sa sukat, dami, o tindi; nasa proseso ng paglaki.
original_explanation: Describes something that's in the process of getting bigger. It can be 'Wow, **palaki** na ang tiyan mo!' (Your belly is getting bigger!) to a pregnant woman, or '**Palaki** na nang **palaki** ang utang mo' (Your debt is growing and growing). It's the '-ing' form of 'laki' (big).
usage_notes: Often repeated as 'palaki nang palaki' to emphasize continuous growth.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Palaki** na ang mga alaga naming tuta.","translation":"Our pet puppies are **getting bigger**."},{"sentence":"Habang tumatagal, **palaki** nang **palaki** ang problema.","translation":"As time goes on, the problem is **growing** bigger and bigger."}]

translation: was treated as an errand boy; was bossed around
meaning_filipino: Tinrato bilang isang utusan o taga-utos na walang paggalang; ginawang parang alila.
original_explanation: When your boss, tita, or jowa treats you like a personal Grab delivery, Shopee courier, and all-around "boy" rolled into one. "Pakikuha ng kape." "Pakibili ng yosi." "Paki-print nito." You're not an employee or a partner, you're just being biniboy.
usage_notes: Often used humorously or with frustration to describe being taken for granted and ordered around for menial tasks.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayoko nang sumama sa kanila, lagi lang akong **biniboy** para bumili ng yelo.","translation":"I don't want to go with them anymore, I'm always just **treated like an errand boy** to buy ice."},{"sentence":"Sa opisina, hindi ako ang intern, ako ang laging **biniboy** ng buong team.","translation":"At the office, I'm not the intern, I'm the one who's always **bossed around** by the whole team."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagkapit at pagbitin o pagbaba mula sa isang bagay, karaniwang gamit ang mga kamay o paa.
original_explanation: Think Spider-Man, but less graceful. It's what kids do on monkey bars, or what you do when you're trying to reach the last can of sardines on the top shelf. It's also a metaphor for your job security during a company-wide "restructuring." Holding on for dear life!
usage_notes: Often implies a swinging or swaying motion while hanging. It can also refer to the dangerous practice of hanging off the back of public vehicles like jeepneys.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig ang mga bata sa **paglalambitin** sa mga sanga ng puno.","translation":"Children are fond of **dangling** from tree branches."},{"sentence":"Delikado ang **paglalambitin** sa likod ng mga dyip.","translation":"It's dangerous to **hang** onto the back of jeepneys."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang babaeng wala sa tamang pag-iisip; o sa kolokyal na gamit, isang babaeng may ginawang kakatwa, katawa-tawa, o di-inaasahan.
original_explanation: The feminine version of 'loko'. This is what you call your bestie when she suggests a spontaneous trip to La Union at 10 PM, or when she buys another pair of shoes she doesn't need. It can range from "clinically insane" to "adorably quirky." Often said with affection, as in, "Ay, loka-loka ka talaga!" followed by laughter.
usage_notes: Can be used as an adjective (e.g., "babaeng loka") or as a noun/term of address (e.g., "Hoy, loka!"). The intensity depends heavily on tone.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniwala diyan, **loka** 'yan!","translation":"Don't believe her, she's **crazy**!"},{"sentence":"Ang **loka**, biglang sumayaw sa gitna ng mall!","translation":"That **silly girl** suddenly danced in the middle of the mall!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagpapatakbo, pamamahala, o paggabay sa isang organisasyon, proyekto, o gawain.
etymology: From `pang-` + `asiwa`. `Asiwa` itself can mean awkward or clumsy, but in this context, the affixation transforms it into management.
original_explanation: This is what the team lead does when they're not just approving your vacation leave. It's the art of juggling tasks, people, and resources to make sure the project doesn't crash and burn. Think of it as being the 'nanay' or 'tatay' of the office, making sure everyone is fed (with tasks) and everything is in order.
usage_notes: A formal term used in business, government, and organizational contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mahusay na **pangangasiwa** sa kumpanya ang dahilan ng tagumpay nito.","translation":"The excellent **management** of the company is the reason for its success."},{"sentence":"Siya ang naatasan sa **pangangasiwa** ng buong proyekto.","translation":"He was assigned to the **administration** of the entire project."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang istilo sa pananamit o estetika na nagtatampok ng mga damit at aksesorya na karaniwang matatagpuan o binili mula sa ukay-ukay, kadalasang may 'vintage' o kakaibang dating.
etymology: From Tagalog 'ukay' + English '-core' (a suffix used to denote a type of aesthetic, e.g., 'cottagecore').
original_explanation: It's not just wearing thrifted clothes, it's a whole vibe. Think mismatched patterns, vintage silhouettes, and a general look that screams 'I have a unique personality and I didn't get this from a fast-fashion megastore.' It's the aesthetic of sustainable, budget-conscious, and creative fashionistas.
usage_notes: A Gen Z internet term to describe a specific fashion subculture.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang buong Instagram feed niya ay puro **ukaycore**.","translation":"Her entire Instagram feed is pure **thrift store aesthetic**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian o kalagayan ng pagiging walang gana o ayaw na magtrabaho, kumilos, o mag-isip; kakulangan sa sipag.
original_explanation: This is the official state of being on a rainy Sunday afternoon. It's that 'pwede bang humiga na lang all day?' feeling. It's the force that makes you order food delivery instead of cooking, watch Netflix for 8 hours straight, and say 'mamaya na' to all your responsibilities. It’s the enemy of productivity and the best friend of your bed.
usage_notes: A very common word to describe a state or a personality trait. 'Katamaran' is a more formal synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Labanan mo ang iyong **pagkatamad** at simulan mo na ang iyong mga gawain.","translation":"Fight your **laziness** and start your tasks."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkatamad** ay hindi magdadala sa iyo sa tagumpay.","translation":"**Laziness** will not lead you to success."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bahagi ng ibabaw na mas mababa kaysa sa mga nakapaligid dito; isang lubog na lugar.
original_explanation: Parang pisngi mo after puyat week, medyo may humbak sa ilalim ng mata. O yung itsura ng kalsada sa Pinas na dinaanan ng overloaded na truck, may 'battle scars' na. Ito rin yung nangyayari sa kama mo sa part na lagi mong hinihigaan.
usage_notes: Can refer to depressions in the ground, on a surface, or even sunken cheeks.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-iwan ng malaking **humbak** sa kalsada ang malakas na ulan.","translation":"The heavy rain left a large **depression** on the road."},{"sentence":"Kitang-kita ang **humbak** sa kanyang mga pisngi dahil sa pagkapayat.","translation":"The **hollows** in his cheeks were very visible due to his weight loss."}]

translation: to shred, to tear into small pieces
meaning_filipino: Ang marahas na pagpunit o pagpilas sa isang bagay hanggang sa maging maliliit na piraso.
original_explanation: This is what happens to your important documents in a shredder, or what your dog does to the tissue roll. It's a more violent, chaotic version of 'pumunit'. If your paper is just torn, 'napunit.' If it looks like it went through a blender, it was *ginutay*.
usage_notes: Implies destruction and being torn into many small, often unrecognizable, pieces. Can be used figuratively for emotions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Gumutay** ang puso niya nang marinig ang masamang balita.","translation":"Her heart was **torn to pieces** when she heard the bad news."},{"sentence":"Ang pusa ay **gumutay** sa lumang pahayagan.","translation":"The cat **shredded** the old newspaper."}]

translation: to have a devotion; to be devoted
meaning_filipino: Mag-ukol ng natatanging panata, pananampalataya, o paglilingkod sa isang banal na entidad, gawain, o tao.
original_explanation: It's that intense loyalty you show, whether it's to the Black Nazarene every January, to your favorite K-Pop group during a comeback, or to your S.O. by bringing them their favorite milk tea without them asking. It's commitment level 9000.
usage_notes: Commonly used in a religious context but can be used hyperbolically for intense dedication to anything.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Taon-taon siyang pumupunta sa Quiapo para **magdebosyon** sa Itim na Nazareno.","translation":"Every year he goes to Quiapo to **have a devotion** to the Black Nazarene."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magdebosyon** sa pag-aaral kung gusto mong makapasa sa board exam.","translation":"You need to **be devoted** to your studies if you want to pass the board exam."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-alis ng kasuotan sa katawan. Ito ang nakaraang anyo ng pandiwang "maghubad".
original_explanation: What you do the moment you get home from a long day at work, especially when you've been wearing tight jeans. You just want to get rid of everything and wear your pambahay. That's the freedom of **naghubad**.
usage_notes: Past tense of 'maghubad'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Naghubad** siya ng sapatos bago pumasok sa bahay.","translation":"He/She **took off** his/her shoes before entering the house."},{"sentence":"Pagdating sa beach, agad siyang **naghubad** ng t-shirt at tumakbo sa tubig.","translation":"Upon arriving at the beach, he immediately **took off** his t-shirt and ran to the water."}]

translation: to do one's best; to excel
meaning_filipino: Gawin ang isang bagay sa pinakamagaling na paraan; pagbutihin nang husto ang sarili o ang gawa.
original_explanation: The ultimate "galingan mo" advice from your parents before a competition, exam, or job interview. It's the command to unleash your inner overachiever and not settle for "pwede na." It's about giving it your 110% to make the family proud. "Anak, magpakahusay ka sa presentation mo bukas, ha?"
usage_notes: A very positive and encouraging term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging bilin ng aming guro na **magpakahusay** sa pag-aaral.","translation":"Our teacher always reminds us to **excel** in our studies."},{"sentence":"**Nagpakahusay** siya sa pagtugtog ng gitara kaya nanalo siya sa paligsahan.","translation":"He **did his best** playing the guitar, that's why he won the contest."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng sili (Capsicum annuum) na mahaba at karaniwang berde ang kulay, hindi gaanong maanghang kumpara sa siling labuyo, at ginagamit sa mga lutuin tulad ng sinigang at dinuguan.
original_explanation: Ito yung sili na 'for display purposes only' sa sinigang. Hindi siya yung tipong papaiyakin ka sa anghang tulad ng ex mo, mild lang. Perfect pang-garnish o kapag gusto mo lang ng amoy ng sili pero takot ka sa anghang. Partner-in-crime ng dinuguan at Bicol Express.
usage_notes: Kadalasan ding tinutukoy bilang 'siling pangsigang' o 'siling berde'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglagay si nanay ng tatlong pirasong **siling-haba** sa sinigang para pampabango.","translation":"Mom put three pieces of **long green pepper** in the sinigang to add aroma."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong durugin ang **siling-haba** kung ayaw mong umanghang masyado ang Bicol Express.","translation":"Don't crush the **long green pepper** if you don't want the Bicol Express to be too spicy."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na lugar o bahagi ng isang silid na may mga kagamitan para sa pagluluto, karaniwang mas maliit kaysa sa isang buong kusina.
original_explanation: It's that tiny "kitchen" in your condo or studio apartment that's basically just a sink, a microwave, and maybe a single induction cooker. It’s where you perfect the art of cooking rice, frying hotdogs, and heating up leftovers, all within arm's reach of your bed. The "I'm an independent adult but my budget is tight" kitchen.
usage_notes: A direct loanword. The spelling "kitchenette" is also common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May maliit na **kitsenet** ang inuupahan niyang studio unit.","translation":"The studio unit he's renting has a small **kitchenette**."},{"sentence":"Sapat na ang **kitsenet** para sa mga simpleng lutuin.","translation":"The **kitchenette** is enough for simple dishes."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang plano o pamamaraan upang makamit ang isang tiyak na layunin, lalo na sa isang labanan, laro, o debate.
original_explanation: Paraan para manalo sa Mobile Legends, sa presentation sa office, o sa puso ng crush mo. Diskarte 2.0. Hindi lang 'basta-basta', dapat may plano.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng negosyo, laro, o anumang sitwasyon na nangangailangan ng estratehiya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng bagong **tactics** para matalo ang kalabang koponan.","translation":"We need new **tactics** to defeat the opposing team."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang galing sa **tactics** ang nagpanalo sa kanila sa debate.","translation":"His skill in **tactics** made them win the debate."}]

translation: to divert, to deflect, to lead astray
meaning_filipino: Baguhin ang direksyon o patutunguhan ng isang bagay; ibaling ang usapan o atensyon sa ibang paksa.
original_explanation: When your tita asks, 'Kailan ka mag-aasawa?' and you suddenly start talking about the weather. That's you trying to **ilihis** the topic. It's the art of strategic redirection, like a politician avoiding a tough question or you changing the channel when your parents walk in on a kissing scene.
usage_notes: Can be used for both physical direction (e.g., a car) and abstract concepts like conversations or attention.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **ilihis** ang usapan nang tanungin siya tungkol sa kanyang sahod.","translation":"He tried to **divert** the conversation when he was asked about his salary."},{"sentence":"**Inilihis** ng tsuper ang manibela upang maiwasan ang aso.","translation":"The driver **turned** the steering wheel to avoid the dog."}]

translation: act of going against the current or wind
meaning_filipino: Ang paggalaw o paglalakbay nang salungat sa direksyon ng hangin, agos ng tubig, o anumang gumagalaw na puwersa.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate 'Laban!' move. It's sailing your bangka against the strong waves. Figuratively, it's what you do when you defy expectations, challenge the status quo, or commute via EDSA during rush hour. It's the opposite of just going with the flow.
usage_notes: A less common word, often used in nautical or metaphorical contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap ang **pagsungsong** sa malakas na agos ng ilog.","translation":"**Going against** the strong river current is difficult."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang tagumpay ay bunga ng **pagsungsong** sa lahat ng pagsubok.","translation":"His success is a result of **going against** all challenges."}]

meaning_filipino: Bilang pangngalan, isang ritmiko at magkakasabay na paglakad, karaniwan ng mga sundalo o grupo. Bilang pandiwa (magmartsa), ang kilos ng paglakad nang pa-martsa.
original_explanation: That synchronized walking you see in parades or with soldiers. It’s the 'left, right, left!' of movement. Also, it's what you do when you're super determined (or angry) and walking with a purpose. 'Nag-martsa siya palabas ng kwarto pagkatapos ng away.' (She marched out of the room after the fight.)
usage_notes: Can be a noun ('ang martsa') or a verb, typically inflected as 'magmartsa' or 'ummartsa'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsanay ang mga sundalo para sa **martsa** sa Araw ng Kalayaan.","translation":"The soldiers practiced for the **march** on Independence Day."},{"sentence":"Nag-**martsa** ang mga aktibista upang iprotesta ang bagong batas.","translation":"The activists **marched** to protest the new law."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng paglalagay sa isang tao o bagay sa isang pagsubok upang malaman ang kalidad, kakayahan, o katatagan nito.
etymology: From 'subok' (test, try). The '-in-' infix and reduplication of the first syllable ('su-') indicate the present progressive tense.
original_explanation: This is what life does to you right before payday. It's also what your partner does when they ask, "Sino 'yung ka-chat mo?" even though they already know. It's a test, a trial, a challenge to your patience, wallet, or relationship status.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of challenges, tests (in school or in life), or trying something new.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sinusubok** lang talaga tayo ng panahon, pero kakayanin natin 'to.","translation":"Time is really just **testing** us, but we'll get through this."},{"sentence":"**Sinusubok** ko kung gumagana pa ba itong lumang radyo.","translation":"I'm **testing** if this old radio still works."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mabuting balita tungkol kay Hesukristo, lalo na ang nakasulat sa unang apat na aklat ng Bagong Tipan. Tumutukoy din ito sa pangkalahatang aral o doktrina ng Kristiyanismo.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "evangelio", mula sa Griyegong "euangelion" (mabuting balita).
original_explanation: The "Good News" according to Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John. Ito 'yung part ng Misa na tatayo ang lahat para makinig sa kwento ng buhay ni Hesus. It's the OG source material for all Christian faiths, the ultimate "resibo" of the religion.
usage_notes: Palaging naka-capitalize kapag tumutukoy sa mga aklat ng Bibliya.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Binasa ng pari ang **Ebanghelyo** ayon kay San Juan.","translation":"The priest read the **Gospel** according to St. John."},{"sentence":"Ang pagpapalaganap ng **Ebanghelyo** ang misyon ng mga apostol.","translation":"Spreading the **Gospel** was the mission of the apostles."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng isang tao, bagay, o lugar sa ilalim ng kapangyarihan ng mahika o kababalaghan.
etymology: From Spanish 'encantar' (to enchant), adapted with Tagalog verb suffix '-hin'.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you catch the eye of that crush from across the room and suddenly you forget your own name. Para kang in-engkanto. It's the act of putting someone under a spell, whether by an actual 'engkanto' or just by someone's killer smile. The 'jowa' effect.
usage_notes: The object-focus form of the verb related to 'engkanto'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Baka **ingkantuhin** ka ng diwata kung hindi ka magbibigay-galang pagdaan sa gubat.","translation":"The nature spirit might **bewitch** you if you don't show respect when passing through the forest."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang transaksiyon ng pagpapalitan ng pera para sa isang produkto o serbisyo; ang pagbili.
original_explanation: This is the root word, the OG concept of buying. When someone asks "Ano'ng bili mo diyan?" they're asking "How much did you buy that for?". It can also mean the thing you bought, as in "Patingin ng mga bili mo!" (Let me see your haul!). It's the noun form of every shopping spree.
usage_notes: Can refer to the act of buying, the price of purchase, or the purchased item itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magkano ang **bili** mo sa relo mo?","translation":"How much was your **purchase** price for your watch?"},{"sentence":"Ipakita mo sa akin ang iyong mga **bili** mula sa 11.11 sale.","translation":"Show me your **purchases** from the 11.11 sale."}]

meaning_filipino: Panahon ng taon na malimit at malakas ang pag-ulan, karaniwang mula Hunyo hanggang Nobyembre sa Pilipinas.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'tag-' (nagpapahiwatig ng panahon) at 'ulan' (rain).
original_explanation: The official season for cuddle weather, baha sa EDSA, and a sudden craving for champorado. It's when your laundry refuses to dry for days and your commute becomes an extreme water sport. Also, the perfect excuse to 'work from home'.
usage_notes: Kabaligtaran ng 'tag-araw' (dry season/summer).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magdala ka ng payong, **tag-ulan** na naman.","translation":"Bring an umbrella, it's the **rainy season** again."},{"sentence":"Masarap humigop ng mainit na sabaw tuwing **tag-ulan**.","translation":"It's nice to sip hot soup during the **rainy season**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kapatid na babae ng ama o ina ng isang tao; o ang asawa ng kapatid na lalaki ng ama o ina.
original_explanation: Your 'tita'. She's the one who asks "May boyfriend/girlfriend ka na?" at every family reunion, gives you the best 'pamasko' (Christmas cash), and probably has a collection of essential oils or expensive bags. The official gatekeeper of family 'chismis' (gossip).
usage_notes: Often replaced in casual conversation by the more affectionate 'Tita'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **tiya** ko ang nag-alaga sa akin noong bata pa ako.","translation":"My **aunt** took care of me when I was young."},{"sentence":"Pupunta kami sa bahay ni **Tiya** Susan sa Linggo.","translation":"We are going to **Aunt** Susan's house on Sunday."}]

translation: to be able to punch upwards; to uppercut
meaning_filipino: Ang kakayahang makapagbigay ng isang suntok na paitaas, karaniwang tinatama ang panga o baba ng kalaban.
original_explanation: This is that classic move you see in boxing or street fights in movies. It's not just a regular punch; it's an upward jab, often a knockout blow. Think Manny Pacquiao's training montage. It's the 'shoryuken!' of Pinoy brawls.
usage_notes: A specific term used in fighting, boxing, or brawling contexts. Less common in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malakas na suntok lang ang kailangan niya para **makasunok** at manalo.","translation":"He only needed one strong punch to be able **to uppercut** and win."},{"sentence":"Inaral niya kung paano **makasunok** nang tama sa kanyang boxing class.","translation":"He studied how to properly **deliver an uppercut** in his boxing class."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aaral sa posisyon at paggalaw ng mga bituin at planeta sa paniniwalang mayroon itong direktang impluwensya sa mga pangyayari sa mundo at sa kapalaran ng mga tao.
original_explanation: It's the "What's your sign?" science. It's why you blame your bad day on Mercury being in retrograde. For many Pinoys, astrolohia is a fun guide, a conversation starter, and a convenient scapegoat for our own questionable life choices. "Sorry, Scorpio ako eh."
usage_notes: Often considered a pseudoscience. It's the practice performed by an 'astrologo'. Not to be confused with 'astronomiya' (astronomy).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang magbasa tungkol sa **astrolohia** at mga zodiac sign.","translation":"She loves to read about **astrology** and zodiac signs."},{"sentence":"Hindi ako naniniwala sa **astrolohia**, pero nakakatuwang basahin ang horoscope.","translation":"I don't believe in **astrology**, but it's fun to read the horoscope."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging malandi; ang kilos o gawi ng labis na paglalambing, pagpapapansin, o pakikipagharutan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na 'landi' (flirt) at panlaping 'ka- -an'.
original_explanation: The art of 'pabebe' and 'pa-cute' with a purpose. Ito 'yung energy na nilalabas mo kapag andyan si crush. It's the extra sway in your walk, the higher pitch in your voice, the 'Ay, nahulog ang panyo ko' move from the 1950s but make it 2026. Can be cute, can be cringe, depends on execution. It's a skill, a lifestyle, a choice. Charot!
usage_notes: Maaaring magkaroon ng negatibo o mapaglarong konotasyon depende sa konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na ang iyong **kalandian** at seryosohin mo ang iyong pag-aaral.","translation":"Stop your **flirtatiousness** and get serious with your studies."},{"sentence":"Puro **kalandian** lang ang alam ng karakter niya sa teleserye.","translation":"Her character in the soap opera knows nothing but **flirtatiousness**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maikli at makabuluhang kasabihan na naglalaman ng payo, aral, o katotohanan na batay sa karanasan ng mga ninuno.
etymology: Possibly from a combination of an archaic word related to 'sala' (thought) and 'wika' (language).
original_explanation: These are the original 'hugot lines' from our Lolos and Lolas. They're like ancient Filipino memes passed down through generations. "Ang hindi lumingon sa pinanggalingan..." is a classic salawikain that’s basically the OG 'stay humble' tweet.
usage_notes: Often quoted in schools and by elders to impart wisdom. Differs from 'sawikain' (idiom).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang paborito kong **salawikain** ay 'Kung may tiyaga, may nilaga.'","translation":"My favorite **proverb** is 'If there is perseverance, there is stew (reward).'"},{"sentence":"Maraming aral sa buhay ang makukuha sa mga **salawikain**.","translation":"Many life lessons can be learned from **proverbs**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng community quarantine kung saan may bahagyang pagluluwag sa mga restriksyon kumpara sa Enhanced Community Quarantine (ECQ), ngunit mas mahigpit kaysa sa General Community Quarantine (GCQ).
etymology: Acronym for the English phrase 'Modified Enhanced Community Quarantine'.
original_explanation: Ah, the "Quarantine Purgatory" level. It's not quite the "stay-at-home-or-else" vibe of ECQ, but you're also not free to roam like in GCQ. It’s that confusing phase where you ask, "Pwede na ba lumabas? Pwede pero bawal? Ano na?!" The ultimate "it's complicated" status with the government.
usage_notes: A term that gained widespread use in the Philippines during the COVID-19 pandemic.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ibinalik sa **MECQ** ang buong Metro Manila dahil sa pagtaas ng kaso.","translation":"The entire Metro Manila was placed back under **MECQ** due to the rise in cases."},{"sentence":"Ano-ano nga ulit ang mga alituntunin kapag **MECQ**?","translation":"What are the rules again during **MECQ**?"}]

translation: to cling, to hold on tightly
meaning_filipino: Ang mahigpit na pagkapit o paghawak sa isang bagay, lalo na sa pag-akyat o upang maiwasan ang pagkahulog.
original_explanation: Parang 'yung kapit mo sa sahod mo bago mag-petsa de peligro. Or 'yung pag-mangunyapit mo sa jeep kapag siksikan at biglang nag-preno si Manong driver. Kapit-bisig sa reyalidad ng buhay commuter.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kinailangang **mangunyapit** ng bata sa likod ng kanyang ina para hindi siya mahulog.","translation":"The child had to **cling** to his mother's back so he wouldn't fall."},{"sentence":"Para siyang pusang **nangungunyapit** sa puno.","translation":"He's like a cat **clinging** to a tree."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang napakatinding damdamin ng kaligayahan, galak, o pananabik.
original_explanation: The feeling you get when your crush finally messages you back. Or when the GrabFood driver arrives with your milk tea order. It's that 'on top of the world' feeling, pure, unadulterated bliss. (Note: Also a street name for a drug, but the primary meaning is the feeling).
usage_notes: Can refer to a state of extreme happiness or, in modern contexts, the illicit drug MDMA. The dictionary focuses on the former.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nasa estado ng **ekstasi** ang mga tagahanga nang manalo ang kanilang paboritong banda.","translation":"The fans were in a state of **ecstasy** when their favorite band won."},{"sentence":"Purong **ekstasi** ang naramdaman niya nang makapasa sa board exam.","translation":"She felt pure **ecstasy** when she passed the board exam."}]

translation: A flat fall; a splat or thud
meaning_filipino: Ang biglaan at malakas na pagbagsak nang padapa o pasubsob; ang tunog na likha nito.
etymology: Likely onomatopoeic, imitating the sound of a wet, heavy impact.
original_explanation: That epic fail moment when you trip and land face-first on the floor. The sound it makes? That's the 'sagpak'. It's the physical manifestation of 'aruy!' and the reason your friends will never let you forget it. A total wipeout.
usage_notes: Often used with 'bumagsak' (to fall) as in 'bumagsak nang pasagpak' or as a verb 'sumagpak' (to fall flat).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napakalakas ng pagka**sagpak** niya sa putikan.","translation":"The way he **fell flat** into the mud was so forceful."},{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **sagpak** ng nahulog na bayabas.","translation":"I heard the **splat** of the fallen guava."}]

meaning_filipino: Paglalarawan sa isang tao na mukhang pagod na pagod, puyat, o may pinagdaanang hirap, na makikita sa kanyang itsura.
original_explanation: The official look of every BPO agent after a graveyard shift, every parent of a newborn, and every student during finals week. 'Yung itsura mong 'di na kayang itago ng concealer. 'Yung "pagod" na umabot na sa mukha. "Haggard" is not just a feeling, it's a look. The opposite of "blooming".
usage_notes: Isang napakakaraniwang salita sa Taglish, na halos itinuturing nang bahagi ng wikang Filipino sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Grabe, mukha na akong **haggard** dahil sa dami ng trabaho.","translation":"Wow, I already look **haggard** because of so much work."},{"sentence":"Kahit **haggard** ka na, maganda ka pa rin.","translation":"Even if you look **worn-out**, you are still beautiful."}]

translation: giving one's all; going all out
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng buong lakas, kakayahan, o sigla sa isang gawain; ang paggawa ng isang bagay sa pinakamatinding paraan.
original_explanation: That moment you decide to stop holding back. It's the "all-in" or "beast mode" of Tagalog. It's singing your heart out at the karaoke even if you're out of tune, dressing up for a party like it's the Met Gala, or cramming for an exam with the energy of three energy drinks. When you 'pagtodo', there are no half-measures. Go big or go home.
usage_notes: This is a colloquial or slang term, a Taglish construction from 'pag-' (gerund-forming prefix) and the Spanish word 'todo'. It can also function adverbially.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Galing ng **pagtodo** niya sa sayaw, panalo!","translation":"His **giving his all** in the dance was amazing, a winner!"},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating mag-**pagtodo** sa huling proyekto para makapasa.","translation":"We need **to go all out** on the final project to pass."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-umbok o paglaki ng isang bahagi ng katawan dahil sa pinsala, impeksiyon, o sakit.
etymology: From pa- + reduplication of the first syllable of the root 'maga' (-ma-). The pa- -ma- formation creates a noun denoting the state or result of the root word's action.
original_explanation: What happens to your ankle after a bad fall, your face after getting a wisdom tooth pulled, or your ego after being proven wrong. It's your body's way of saying "Ouch, something's not right here!" It's the physical proof that you shouldn't have played basketball in flip-flops.
usage_notes: A very common medical and everyday term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nilagyan niya ng yelo ang bukung-bukong niya upang mabawasan ang **pamamaga**.","translation":"She put ice on her ankle to reduce the **swelling**."},{"sentence":"Ang **pamamaga** ng gilagid ay senyales ng impeksyon.","translation":"The **inflammation** of the gums is a sign of infection."}]

translation: to profit from; to make money from
meaning_filipino: Ang kumita o magkaroon ng tubo mula sa isang negosyo, transaksyon, o puhunan.
original_explanation: The verb of every 'raket' and business venture. When you buy something cheap and sell it for a higher price, your goal is to 'pagtubuan' it. It's the core of 'diskarte' in business, from the 'tindera' in the palengke to the big-time CEO. 'Magkano ang pinagtubuan mo diyan?' is the Filipino way of asking 'What's your ROI?'.
usage_notes: A key verb in business and finance discussions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong masyadong **pagtubuan** ang mga paninda mo para balik-balikan ka ng customer.","translation":"Don't **profit too much from** your goods so that customers will keep coming back."},{"sentence":"Maliit lang ang **pinagtutubuan** niya sa bawat piraso, pero malakas naman ang benta.","translation":"He only **profits** a little from each piece, but his sales are strong."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagkuha ng karapatan na pansamantalang gamitin ang isang bagay, lugar, o serbisyo kapalit ng regular na bayad.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'rent'. 'Yung ginagawa mo kapag kailangan mo ng gown para sa JS prom, ng sasakyan para sa road trip, o ng condo unit kasi malayo ang office. Basically, using something you don't own by paying for it. 'Pwedeng alkilahin ang puso mo?' - a classic hugot line.
usage_notes: Refers to the act of renting something *from* someone. The counterpart is 'paalkila' (to rent something *out*).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **alkilahin** ang isang van para sa outing ng buong pamilya.","translation":"We need **to rent** a van for the whole family's outing."},{"sentence":"Magkano kung **alkilahin** ang buong resort para sa isang araw?","translation":"How much is it **to rent** the entire resort for one day?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpindot sa "Haha" na reaksyon sa isang post o komento sa social media, na nagpapahiwatig ng pagtawa o pagiging nakakatawa ng nilalaman.
etymology: A loan phrase from English, specifically from Facebook's 'React' feature introduced in 2016.
original_explanation: The ultimate passive-aggressive tool on Facebook. Pwedeng genuine na tawa, pwedeng pang-asar sa kaaway mo, o pwedeng 'I see your ridiculously dumb post and I will not engage, but I will laugh at you.' The modern 'ha-ha-ha, buti nga sa'yo.'
usage_notes: Can be used as a noun ('Daming haha react ng post mo!') or a verb ('I-haha react mo nga 'to.').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puro **haha react** ang natanggap ng selfie niya.","translation":"His selfie received nothing but **\"Haha\" reacts**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong i-**haha react**, seryoso ako!","translation":"Don't give me a **\"Haha\" react**, I'm serious!"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na binalutan o pinahiran ng manipis na patong ng nikel upang maging makintab at hindi kalawangin.
original_explanation: The OG 'chrome' finish before 'chrome' was cool. Think of those shiny, silvery parts of an old jeepney, a classic revolver in a Pinoy action movie, or the hardware on your lola's antique aparador. It's the process of giving something a 'bling' makeover with a protective layer of nickel. It says 'I'm fancy and I won't rust easily.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang baril ay **nikelado** kaya't napakakintab.","translation":"The gun is **nickel-plated**, that's why it's so shiny."},{"sentence":"Pinalitan niya ang mga hawakan ng pinto ng mga **nikelado**.","translation":"He replaced the door handles with **nickel-plated** ones."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pinaghalong pulbos ng iba't ibang pampalasa tulad ng turmerik, kumin, at coriander, na ginagamit sa pagluluto ng curry.
original_explanation: The magic yellow dust you buy in a small bottle that instantly makes your kitchen smell like an Indian restaurant. It's the cheat code to making curry when you don't have the time (or patience) to grind 15 different spices yourself.
usage_notes: Sold in most supermarkets in the Philippines.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kulang tayo sa **curry powder**, kailangan nating bumili.","translation":"We're out of **curry powder**, we need to buy some."},{"sentence":"Isang kutsaritang **curry powder** lang ang ilagay mo para hindi masyadong matapang ang lasa.","translation":"Just put one teaspoon of **curry powder** so the flavor isn't too strong."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapan, karaniwang tela o papel, na ginagamit sa pag-alis ng dumi, basa, o alikabok sa isang ibabaw sa pamamagitan ng pagpahid.
etymology: From `punas` (to wipe). The `paN-` prefix (manifesting as `pa-` in this case) turns the verb into a noun representing the tool used for the action.
original_explanation: The unsung hero of every Filipino household. It can be a legit, store-bought "Basahan," a retired Good Morning towel, or your dad's old sando. There's a hierarchy: one for the table (pamunas ng mesa), one for the dishes (pamunas ng pinggan), and the floor-level one that you wouldn't touch with a ten-foot pole.
usage_notes: A general term. Specificity is added with 'ng + [object]', e.g., 'pamunas ng mesa' (table wipe) or 'pamunas ng pinggan' (dish towel).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakikuha ng **pamunas** at may natapong kape sa sahig.","translation":"Please get a **rag** as there's spilled coffee on the floor."},{"sentence":"Ito ang **pamunas** ng pinggan, huwag mong gamitin sa mesa.","translation":"This is the dish **towel**, don't use it on the table."}]

meaning_filipino: Pagtugtog ng isang instrumentong pangmusika batay lamang sa pakikinig at hindi sa pagbabasa ng nota; pag-alam sa isang bagay batay sa narinig lamang.
original_explanation: The musical equivalent of 'suntok sa buwan' or 'bahala na si Batman'. It's when you can play "Canon in D" on the piano after just hearing it at a wedding, without ever seeing the sheet music. It's the ultimate 'galing' flex for musicians. "Wala akong pormal na training, oido lang lahat."
usage_notes: Primarily used in the context of music to describe playing an instrument without formal training or reading sheet music. Can be used as an adjective or adverb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natuto siyang mag-gitara nang **oido** lang.","translation":"He learned to play the guitar just **by ear**."},{"sentence":"Kahanga-hanga ang kakayahan niyang tumugtog nang **oido**.","translation":"His ability to play **by ear** is amazing."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kasuotan na isinusuot sa pang-itaas na bahagi ng katawan upang magbigay ng init, karaniwang gawa sa lana o makapal na tela.
original_explanation: The official uniform for Baguio trips, Christmas season, and any office with an overzealous aircon setting. Kahit 35 degrees Celsius sa labas, may dala kang **sweater** 'just in case' manlamig ka sa sinehan o sa BPO office floor.
usage_notes: Bagama't may salitang 'pangginaw', mas karaniwang ginagamit ang 'sweater' o 'dyaket' sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magdala ka ng **sweater** dahil malamig sa Baguio.","translation":"Bring a **sweater** because it's cold in Baguio."},{"sentence":"Naiwan ko ang paborito kong **sweater** sa bus.","translation":"I left my favorite **sweater** on the bus."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sisidlan, karaniwang yari sa metal o porselana, na nilalagay sa sahig upang duraan, lalo na ng mga taong ngumunguya ng tabako o buyo (nga-nga).
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "escupidor", nangangahulugang "spitter" o "isang bagay na dinuduraan".
original_explanation: This is the lolo's version of an ashtray, but for spit. Back in the day, when chewing tobacco (nga-nga) was the vape, you'd see this pot in corners of old houses or offices. It's a 'duraan'. Kinda gross, but very vintage. Now, it's a prime antique find.
usage_notes: Isang bagay na halos lipas na at makikita na lamang sa mga lumang bahay, museo, o sa mga pelikulang pangkasaysayan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa isang sulok ng lumang bahay, may nakitang tansong **eskupidor** ang mga bisita.","translation":"In a corner of the old house, the visitors saw a brass **spittoon**."},{"sentence":"Madalas linisin ng kasambahay ang **eskupidor** ng don.","translation":"The house helper frequently cleaned the master's **cuspidor**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang marahas na pagkain, pagpunit, o pagpatay sa pamamagitan ng pagkagat at pagkalmot, karaniwang ginagawa ng mababangis na hayop.
original_explanation: Imagine a lion with a zebra, or you with a bucket of Jollibee chicken after a long day. It's that no-holds-barred, 'gutom na ako' level of eating. Can also mean to get mauled, which is what happens to your wallet during a 12.12 sale.
usage_notes: Used as a root word for actions like 'lapain' (to devour something) or 'nilapa' (was devoured).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakita nila kung paano **lapa**-in ng buwaya ang isang baboy-ramo.","translation":"They saw how the crocodile **devoured** a wild boar."},{"sentence":"**Nilapa** ng aso ang natirang pagkain sa mesa.","translation":"The dog **devoured** the leftover food on the table."}]

translation: to feel small, to be belittled, to shrink
meaning_filipino: Ang maramdaman ang pagiging maliit o mababa, kadalasan dahil sa hiya, takot, o paghamak ng iba.
original_explanation: That feeling you get when your boss calls you out in a meeting, or when you realize you wore your t-shirt inside out the whole day. You just want to shrink and disappear. 'Manliit sa takot' (to shrink in fear) is the next level—it's shrinking out of fear, like when you check your bank account after a 12.12 sale. You feel so small you could fit in a thimble.
usage_notes: Often used with a cause, like 'manliit sa hiya' (to feel small from shame) or 'manliit sa takot' (to feel small from fear).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais niyang **manliit** sa hiya nang tawagin siya sa entablado.","translation":"She wanted to **shrink** in embarrassment when she was called on stage."},{"sentence":"Tila siya'y nanliit sa takot nang makita ang dambuhalang aso.","translation":"He seemed to shrink in fear when he saw the giant dog."}]

meaning_filipino: Prangka, direkta, o walang paligoy-ligoy sa pagsasalita; tuwiran.
original_explanation: This is your friend who tells you, "Uy, may tinga ka," without hesitation. They're not being mean, they're just being 'taros'—blunt and straight to the point. No sugarcoating, no pabebe wave. It's the communication style of someone who values efficiency over feelings, like a surgeon giving a diagnosis. Sometimes it hurts, but you always know where you stand. The opposite of 'pasikot-sikot'.
usage_notes: Can also be used as a verb root, e.g., "Tinaros niya ako ng tanong" (He asked me directly/bluntly). Synonymous with 'prangka'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Taros** kung magsalita ang matanda, pero laging may katwiran.","translation":"The old man speaks **bluntly**, but he always has a point."},{"sentence":"Sa isang **taros** na sagot, sinabi niyang ayaw na niya.","translation":"In a **direct** answer, she said she doesn't want to anymore."}]

translation: to charge; to rush forward; to attack
meaning_filipino: Ang mabilis at biglaang pag-abante o pagsulong, karaniwan upang salakayin ang isang bagay o isang tao.
original_explanation: The way people rush towards the MRT doors the moment they open. Or when you see a '70% OFF' sign at the mall. It's a chaotic, full-force rush forward with a clear target. No hesitation, just pure forward momentum.
usage_notes: More intense and chaotic than 'tumakbo' (to run). It implies a collective, aggressive forward movement.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nang bumukas ang pinto ng mall, **nagsumugod** ang mga tao para sa midnight sale.","translation":"When the mall doors opened, the people **charged** in for the midnight sale."},{"sentence":"Handa nang **magsumugod** ang mga sundalo sa utos ng kanilang heneral.","translation":"The soldiers are ready **to attack** on their general's command."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katumbas na halaga ng pera ng isang bansa kapag ipinagpalit sa pera ng ibang bansa.
original_explanation: This is the number that makes OFWs and BPO workers either very happy or very sad. It's the "Peso-Dollar Exchange Rate" you see on the news. When the halaga ng palitan is high (e.g., ₱58 to $1), your dollar remittance goes a long way. When it's low, you might have to skip the extra large fries. It's the magic number that dictates the purchasing power of your hard-earned foreign currency.
usage_notes: A specific economic term. Often seen in news reports, banks, and money exchange centers.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tumaas na naman ang **halaga ng palitan** ng dolyar laban sa piso.","translation":"The **exchange rate** of the dollar against the peso has increased again."},{"sentence":"Laging binabantayan ng mga OFW ang **halaga ng palitan** bago sila magpadala ng pera.","translation":"OFWs always monitor the **exchange rate** before they send money."}]

translation: killing it; looking fabulous; doing great
meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang kilos ng paggawa ng isang bagay sa napakahusay na paraan; pagiging nasa estado ng kahusayan o kaakit-akit na anyo.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Ingles na "slaying," ang kasalukuyang pandiwari (present participle) ng "slay."
original_explanation: This is the "-ing" form of 'slay' but used as a state of being. It’s not just that you DID something well (slay), it's that you are CURRENTLY in the process of being awesome. It's a continuous state of fabulousness. Your friend posts a selfie from their vacation in El Nido. You don't just comment 'slay', you comment 'Slaying!' to describe the whole vibe.
usage_notes: Used as a standalone exclamation or an adjective. Often interchangeable with 'slay' but emphasizes the current, ongoing nature of the awesomeness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lagi siyang **slaying** sa mga OOTD niya sa Instagram.","translation":"She's always **slaying** with her OOTDs on Instagram."},{"sentence":"Bagong gupit, bagong kulay ng buhok? **Slaying**!","translation":"New haircut, new hair color? **Slaying**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang malisyosong pagpapahayag ng kasinungalingan o maling paratang laban sa isang tao upang sirain ang kaniyang reputasyon.
original_explanation: Ito yung chismis na may kasamang legal action. Level up na paninirang-puri na pwedeng mauwi sa demandahan. Parang "tea" na sobrang pait at pwedeng makasama sa'yo sa korte.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa pormal na usapan, lalo na sa kontekstong legal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pagkakalat ng maling balita ay isang uri ng **kalumniya**.","translation":"Spreading fake news is a form of **calumny**."},{"sentence":"Nagsampa siya ng kaso para sa **kalumniya** laban sa kanyang mga kritiko.","translation":"He filed a case for **calumny** against his critics."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa posisyong tuwid, patayo, o hindi nakahiga. Partikular na tumutukoy sa sikat ng araw sa katanghalian o sa mga mata na dilat na dilat.
original_explanation: Yung buhok mo noong high school na sinabuyan mo ng isang buong bote ng gel. O kaya yung mata mo kapag nakakita ka ng multo o ng presyo ng bilihin. "Eyes wide open" mode. Ito rin ang state ng araw kapag 12 noon, yung tipong ayaw mong lumabas kasi nakakatunaw.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang mga mata, buhok, o ang araw sa tanghali.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tirik** ang sikat ng araw tuwing tanghali.","translation":"The sun's rays are **directly overhead** at noon."},{"sentence":"**Tirik** ang mga mata niya sa gulat.","translation":"His eyes were **wide open** in shock."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging kilala o pagpapahayag sa isang partikular na pangalan, titulo, o bansag.
original_explanation: This is the old-school way of saying 'to be called' or 'to be nicknamed.' Think of how historical figures got their titles, like how Lapu-Lapu was 'mamansag' as a great warrior. It’s about being proclaimed or earning a certain reputation or title. A bit too formal for your barkada's new nickname for you, though.
usage_notes: Formal and somewhat archaic. Used in historical or literary contexts to mean 'to be proclaimed' or 'to be known by a title'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Andres Bonifacio ay **mamansag** na \"Ama ng Katipunan\".","translation":"Andres Bonifacio is **known as** the \"Father of the Katipunan\"."},{"sentence":"Sino ang susunod na **mamansag** na pambansang alagad ng sining?","translation":"Who will be the next to **be proclaimed** as a national artist?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-alis sa isang lugar, lalo na kung ito ay may bahid ng kalungkutan, pinalidad, o pagtatapos ng isang kabanata.
original_explanation: This isn't just "pag-alis." This is the dramatic, slow-motion, often tearful kind of leaving. It's the OFW's departure at the airport. It's the "I'm leaving this town and never coming back" scene in a movie. It has a sense of finality and poetry to it. It’s what you call the act of leaving when you want to sound deep and full of hugot.
usage_notes: A more formal, literary, or emotional word for "leaving" compared to the more common "pag-alis".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malungkot ang naging **paglisan** niya patungong ibang bansa.","translation":"His **departure** to another country was sad."},{"sentence":"Ang **paglisan** sa tahanang kinalakihan ay hindi madali.","translation":"The **act of leaving** the home one grew up in is not easy."}]

translation: extremely; very; to the utmost degree
meaning_filipino: Isang pang-abay na nagpapahiwatig ng kasukdulan o kalabisan ng isang katangian.
etymology: Mula sa "saksak" (to stab, to stuff), na may konotasyon ng pagiging puno hanggang sa sukdulan.
original_explanation: This is the word you use to add extra drama. Hindi lang "maganda," kundi "saksakan ng ganda." Hindi lang "mahal," kundi "saksakan ng mahal." It's the "very," "so," or "super" before it was cool. The OG intensifier.
usage_notes: Karaniwang sinusundan ng "ng" at isang pang-uri. Halimbawa: saksakan ng guwapo, saksakan ng talino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang presyo ng bilihin ngayon ay **saksakan** ng mahal.","translation":"The price of goods today is **extremely** expensive."},{"sentence":"Bakit ka umiiyak? Dahil **saksakan** ng ganda ng pelikula.","translation":"Why are you crying? Because the movie is **extremely** beautiful."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maingay at magulong pagtatalo o away-away, karaniwang tungkol sa maliliit o hindi gaanong mahalagang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the sound of siblings fighting over the TV remote, a couple arguing about where to eat, or your titas debating politics on the family Viber group. It's a low-level, high-volume conflict that's more annoying than destructive. It's the background noise of any Filipino family gathering.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nauwi sa **pagbabangay** ang simpleng usapan ng magkapatid.","translation":"The simple conversation between the siblings ended in **bickering**."},{"sentence":"Sawang-sawa na ako sa walang katapusang **pagbabangay** ng mga politiko.","translation":"I am fed up with the endless **wrangling** of politicians."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panonood o pakikinig ng media (tulad ng video o audio) nang direkta mula sa internet nang hindi muna ito ganap na dina-download.
original_explanation: This is how you watch your favorite series on Netflix or listen to a new album on Spotify. It's also what your gamer pamangkin does on Twitch for 8 hours straight. 'Mag-stream tayo ng K-drama marathon mamaya!' is a solid weekend plan.
usage_notes: Widely used in conversations about digital media consumption.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Saan ba pwedeng **mag-stream** ng bagong episode ng paborito kong anime?","translation":"Where can I **stream** the new episode of my favorite anime?"},{"sentence":"Balak niyang **mag-stream** ng kanyang laro mamayang gabi sa Facebook Gaming.","translation":"He plans to **stream** his game tonight on Facebook Gaming."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang taong magiliw, madaling lapitan, at mahilig makipag-ugnayan o makipagkaibigan sa iba.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping 'pala-' (fond of) at salitang-ugat na 'kaibigan' (friend).
original_explanation: 'Yung ka-opisina mong lahat ng guard at taga-canteen ay kilala sa pangalan. Sila 'yung bumubuhay sa party at kayang makipag-usap kahit kanino. Basically, the human version of a Golden Retriever. Sila 'yung hindi nauubusan ng social battery.
usage_notes: Habang ang direktang salin ng 'extrovert' ay hindi karaniwan, ang 'palakaibigan' ang isa sa pinakamalapit na katangian na naglalarawan dito.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala si Ana sa pagiging **palakaibigan** kaya marami siyang kakilala.","translation":"Ana is known for being **friendly**, that's why she knows a lot of people."},{"sentence":"Maging **palakaibigan** ka sa mga bagong dating para hindi sila mailang.","translation":"Be **sociable** to the newcomers so they won't feel awkward."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinagmulan o dahilan ng isang pangyayari, kilos, o kalagayan.
original_explanation: The 'why' behind the 'what.' In chismis, it's the reason why nag-break si ano at si ano. In traffic, it's the car accident three kilometers ahead of you. In life, it's the reason you're ordering extra rice. It's the ultimate 'kasi...'
usage_notes: Often paired with 'bunga' (effect/result) in the classic Filipino lesson phrase 'sanhi at bunga' (cause and effect).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **sanhi** ng biglaang pagbaha sa inyong lugar?","translation":"What is the **cause** of the sudden flooding in your area?"},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan sa agham ang **sanhi** at bunga ng mga penomeno.","translation":"Science studies the **cause** and effect of phenomena."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng mataas na antas ng pag-iisip, kaalaman, at kakayahang umunawa o mangatwiran.
original_explanation: This is your classmate who never studies but aces the exam. Or you, when you figure out the fastest way to get to the food at a party. Being 'matalino' isn't just about book smarts; it can also be street smarts (diskarte). The opposite of someone who shares fake news on Facebook.
usage_notes: One of the most common adjectives in Tagalog.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Jose Rizal ay isang **matalino** at magiting na bayani.","translation":"Jose Rizal is an **intelligent** and brave hero."},{"sentence":"**Matalino** ang desisyon mong mag-ipon para sa kinabukasan.","translation":"Your decision to save for the future is **smart**."}]

translation: to be able to earn a profit; to be able to grow
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang kumita o magkaroon ng tubo sa isang negosyo; o ang kakayahang magpatubo o magpalago ng isang halaman.
original_explanation: This word has two vibes. First, the business tita/tito vibe: "How much can I 'makatubo' from this investment?" (to profit). Second, the plantita/plantito vibe: "Will this cutting 'makatubo'?" (to be able to grow/sprout). It's all about getting something to grow, whether it's your bank account or your succulent collection.
usage_notes: The context (business or gardening) clarifies the meaning. 'Tubo' can mean profit or sprout.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang tsansang **makatubo** ka kung magbebenta ka ng palamig ngayong tag-init.","translation":"There's a big chance you'll **be able to earn a profit** if you sell cold drinks this summer."},{"sentence":"Kahit sanga lang, basta't alagaan mo ay maaaring **makatubo** at maging puno.","translation":"Even if it's just a branch, as long as you take care of it, it can **grow** and become a tree."}]

translation: to set aside for Christmas; to use for Christmas
meaning_filipino: Itabi o ireserba ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay pera o pagkain, para gamitin o gastusin sa araw ng Pasko.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `i-` (nagsasaad ng sanhi), `pag-` (nagsasaad ng kilos), at `Pasko` (Christmas).
original_explanation: 'Yung bonus mong natanggap ng November pero bawal pa galawin kasi "para sa Pasko." O 'yung bagong damit na binili mo ng October pero di mo pa sinusuot kasi pang-Noche Buena. It's the act of earmarking something specifically for the Christmas festivities.
usage_notes: Isang napaka-espesipikong pandiwang kultural na nauugnay sa panahon ng Kapaskuhan sa Pilipinas. Ang bagay na itinatabi ay ang tuwirang layon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itong natirang pera sa sahod ko ay **ipagpapasko** ko na.","translation":"This remaining money from my salary, I will **set aside for Christmas**."},{"sentence":"Ang lechon de leche na ito ay **ipinagpasko** namin.","translation":"We **saved** this roasted suckling pig **for Christmas**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng lutuin kung saan ang karne ay dahan-dahang pinakuluan sa sarsa o sabaw sa loob ng mahabang oras upang lumambot.
etymology: Mula sa salitang Espanyol na 'estofado', na nangangahulugang 'nilaga' o 'stewed'.
original_explanation: Think of it as the Pinoy version of beef bourguignon, but probably with more toyo and suka. It's that slow-cooked, fall-off-the-bone ulam that your lola makes for fiestas. It's the 'low and slow' method of cooking, like how you slowly fell for your crush who eventually friend-zoned you.
usage_notes: Isang partikular na uri ng ulam, na kadalasang tumutukoy sa isang estilo ng pagluluto sa halip na isang tiyak na resipe.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito niyang lutuin ang **istupadong karne** na may patatas at karot.","translation":"Her favorite dish to cook is **stewed meat** with potatoes and carrots."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang taba o itlog na matatagpuan sa loob ng alimango o talangka, na karaniwang kulay kahel.
original_explanation: The 'gold' inside a crab. 'Yung orange-y stuff na masarap ihalo sa mainit na kanin. Ito 'yung dahilan kung bakit ka napapa-'extra rice, please!' kahit naka-diet ka. The delicious enemy of your cholesterol levels. Also known as 'taba ng talangka'.
usage_notes: Maaari ring baybaying 'aligue'. Itinuturing itong isang espesyal na pagkain o 'delicacy' sa Pilipinas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong papakin ang **aligi** ng alimango.","translation":"My favorite is to eat the crab **fat** by itself."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa pagkain ng maraming **aligi** kung mataas ang iyong presyon.","translation":"Be careful eating too much **crab roe** if you have high blood pressure."}]

translation: to be a die-hard fan of; to strongly support
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita ng labis na paghanga at suporta sa isang partikular na sikat na tao, grupo, o konsepto.
etymology: From the 2000 Eminem song 'Stan', about an obsessive fan.
original_explanation: 'We stan a queen!' Ibig sabihin, sobrang suportado mo 'yung tao o 'yung ginawa niya. It's the highest form of digital praise. You don't just like it, you stan it.
usage_notes: Used as a verb to express strong approval or fandom. Often used with affixes like 'i-stan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"I-**stan** mo ang BINI, hindi ka magsisisi.","translation":"You should **stan** BINI, you won't regret it."},{"sentence":"We **stan** a hardworking and unproblematic artist.","translation":"We **stan** a hardworking and unproblematic artist."}]

translation: to strike or cut with a bolo
meaning_filipino: Pagtaga o paghiwa gamit ang isang tabak.
original_explanation: What you do to the overgrown talahib in your backyard. In action movies, it's what the hero does to the villain's minions. 'Wag mo akong subukan, baka tabakin kita!' (Don't try me, or I might strike you with a bolo!) - usually said as a joke... hopefully.
usage_notes: A very direct and somewhat aggressive-sounding verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang dumaan diyan, baka ka **tabakin** ng baliw.","translation":"Don't pass there, you might get **struck with a bolo** by the crazy person."},{"sentence":"**Tabakin** mo na 'yang mga sanga na nakaharang sa daan.","translation":"**Cut** those branches blocking the path **with a bolo**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang detalyadong panukala para sa paggawa o pagkamit ng isang bagay; isang balak o layunin.
original_explanation: That thing your friend group makes on Friday morning and cancels by Friday afternoon. "Drawing" is its mortal enemy. "Ano plan niyo mamaya?" is the national anthem of the hopeful, while "See you when I see you" is the unofficial response. Also refers to your mobile data subscription that's always 'ubos na'.
usage_notes: Used interchangeably with the Spanish-derived 'plano'. 'Plan' is more common in casual, Taglish speech.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang **plan** natin para sa weekend?","translation":"What's our **plan** for the weekend?"},{"sentence":"Laging nasisira ang **plan** dahil sa biglaang trabaho.","translation":"The **plan** always gets ruined because of sudden work."},{"sentence":"Mag-subscribe ako sa bagong mobile **plan**.","translation":"I will subscribe to a new mobile **plan**."}]

translation: to correspond with; to exchange letters
meaning_filipino: Ang pakikipag-ugnayan sa isang tao sa pamamagitan ng pagpapalitan ng mga liham o sulat.
etymology: From makipag- + sulat + -an. The -an suffix here adds the idea of reciprocity or a place/means of action.
original_explanation: The OG way to slide into someone's DMs. Before email, Messenger, or even text messages, this was how you kept in touch with your long-distance jowa or pen pal. It involved paper, a pen, and a lot of patience waiting for the mailman. Today, it might mean 'to exchange long emails.'
usage_notes: While it literally means exchanging physical letters, it can be used more broadly for exchanging emails or long written messages.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig si Lola na **makipagsulatan** sa kanyang mga kaibigan sa probinsya.","translation":"Grandma loves to **correspond with** her friends in the province."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula ang kanilang pag-iibigan nang sila ay magsimulang **makipagsulatan**.","translation":"Their romance started when they began to **exchange letters**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagpaplano kung paano gagastusin ang pera; paglalaan ng pondo para sa mga partikular na pangangailangan.
original_explanation: Ah, adulting 101. This is the art of stretching your sahod until the next payday. It's making an Excel sheet of your expenses, crying a little, then ordering milk tea anyway. When someone says they need to **magbadyet**, it means they're one online purchase away from eating instant noodles for a week.
usage_notes: A verb from the English loanword "budget".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan kong matutong **magbadyet** nang maayos para makaipon.","translation":"I need to learn **to budget** properly so I can save money."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang panahon ng pagninilay-nilay at pananalangin, karaniwang ginagawa sa isang tahimik na lugar; pag-alala sa mga nakaraang pangyayari.
original_explanation: This is that thing your Catholic high school forced you to do before graduation. You go somewhere quiet (like Tagaytay), write letters to your parents you'll never send, and cry with your classmates. It's a spiritual 'team building' before you face the real world. Also means to remember something, like trying to remember your ex's password.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit sa konteksto ng relihiyon para sa isang 'spiritual retreat'. Ang kahulugan nito bilang 'memorya' ay hindi gaanong karaniwan ngunit naiintindihan pa rin.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga senior high school students ay sasama sa isang **rekoleksiyon** sa susunod na linggo.","translation":"The senior high school students will join a **retreat** next week."},{"sentence":"Sa aking **rekoleksiyon**, hindi siya ang unang nagsalita.","translation":"In my **recollection**, he was not the first one to speak."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng ibon (pamilya Ardeidae) na karaniwang may mahahabang binti at leeg, at aktibo sa gabi sa panghuhuli ng isda.
original_explanation: Not to be confused with 'baka' (cow/maybe). This is a night bird, a type of heron. Think of it as the BPO worker of the bird world – it's most active at night, looking for its next meal (fish, not free office coffee).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May nakita kaming **bakaw** na nakatayo sa tabi ng ilog kagabi.","translation":"We saw a **night heron** standing by the river last night."},{"sentence":"Ang tunog ng **bakaw** ay isa sa mga palatandaan ng papalapit na takipsilim.","translation":"The call of the **night heron** is one of the signs of approaching dusk."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pariralang kolokyal na tumutukoy sa labis na pagbibigay ng reaksyon, lalo na sa social media, tulad ng paggamit ng maraming 'Haha,' 'Angry,' o 'Care' reacts sa isang post.
etymology: Isang modernong pariralang balbal na pinagsasama ang Taglish na 'OA' (mula sa 'overacting') at Ingles na 'reacts' (tumutukoy sa mga reaction button sa social media).
original_explanation: This is 'OA' for the digital age. It's when someone doesn't just 'like' your post, they hit you with the Haha, the Care, the Angry, and the Wow react all at once. It's the social media equivalent of someone laughing, crying, and getting angry at your story in the span of five seconds. 'OA sa reacts si accla!'
usage_notes: Isang napakamoderno at internet-specific na pariralang balbal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-post lang ako ng pusa, pero **oa sa reacts** 'yung mga kaibigan ko.","translation":"I just posted a cat, but my friends were **overreacting on social media**."},{"sentence":"Bakit galit na galit ka? **OA sa reacts** ah!","translation":"Why are you so mad? You're **overreacting**!"}]

translation: to do something little by little; to conserve; to make something last
meaning_filipino: Ang unti-unting paggawa o paggamit ng isang bagay upang ito ay magtagal o hindi maubos kaagad.
etymology: Reduplication of the root "inot" (scrimping, being frugal).
original_explanation: How you use your 13th-month pay. It's also how you eat that expensive cake you bought, taking tiny bites to make it last the whole week. This is the official verb for "petsa de peligro" survival mode.
usage_notes: Connotes frugality, patience, or careful consumption.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **mag-inut-inot** sa paggastos dahil malayo pa ang sahod.","translation":"We need to **be frugal** with our spending because payday is still far away."}]

translation: to oppress; to scorn (variant of dustain)
meaning_filipino: Isang baryasyon ng salitang 'dustain'. Nangangahulugang hamakin, alipustain, o tratuhin nang walang paggalang at may pagmamaliit.
etymology: A common spoken variant of `dustain` where the 's' is dropped.
original_explanation: This is basically `dustain` but with a slight lisp or a regional accent. It's a less common variant, kind of like the "off-brand" version of the word. You'll hear it sometimes, and people will know exactly what you mean, but `dustain` is the standard, "published in the dictionary" spelling.
usage_notes: Considered a non-standard variant of 'dustain'. It is better to use 'dustain' in formal writing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi tama na **dutain** ang kapwa dahil lamang sa kanilang katayuan sa buhay.","translation":"It is not right to **look down upon** others just because of their status in life."},{"sentence":"Naramdaman niyang siya ay **dinuduta** ng kanyang mga katrabaho.","translation":"He felt that he was being **scorned** by his colleagues."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang lalaki na may kaakit-akit na anyo o hitsura; makisig.
original_explanation: The male version of 'ganda.' It's what your tita calls you even if you just woke up and haven't brushed your teeth. It's the highest compliment for a guy's looks, the reason for 'pogi problems,' and the adjective used for every single male celebrity from Daniel Padilla to Piolo Pascual. The feminine form is 'guwapa.'
usage_notes: Exclusively used for males. The female equivalent is 'guwapa'. Often used interchangeably with 'pogi'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sabi ni lola, ang **guwapo** raw ng nobyo ko.","translation":"Grandma said my boyfriend is **handsome**."},{"sentence":"Magbihis ka nang maayos para magmukha kang **guwapo** sa party.","translation":"Dress nicely so you'll look **handsome** at the party."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-apak sa pedal ng bisikleta, makina, o anumang kasangkapan upang ito ay umandar o gumana.
etymology: From the English/Spanish word 'pedal' with the Tagalog suffix '-an'.
original_explanation: The verb for what you do on a bike. 'Pedalan mo pa, malapit na tayo sa 7-Eleven!' It's the grind, the hustle, the continuous effort to move forward, whether you're on a bicycle trying to beat traffic or on a sewing machine trying to beat a deadline.
usage_notes: Used for bicycles, sewing machines, or any foot-operated lever. Can be used interchangeably with 'padyakan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pedalan** mo nang mabilis para maabutan natin sila.","translation":"**Pedal** fast so we can catch up to them."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **pedalan** ang makinang panahi para gumana ito.","translation":"You need **to pedal** the sewing machine for it to work."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbebenta ng isang bagay sa isang partikular na tao o entidad. Ito ay isang pandiwang tumutukoy sa direksyon ng transaksyon patungo sa mamimili.
etymology: Mula sa 'bili' (buy/sell). Ang hulaping '-han' ay nagpapahiwatig ng lokasyon o tagatanggap ng kilos.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of your 'suki' relationship. 'Ate, pagbilhan mo nga ako ng isang kilong bigas.' It's not just 'to sell' (magbenta), but specifically 'to sell TO someone.' It's the command you give the tindera at the sari-sari store when you're pointing at what you want.
usage_notes: This is a locative/benefactive focus verb. The object of the verb is the person *being sold to*.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo siyang **pagbilhan** ng alak dahil menor de edad siya.","translation":"Don't **sell** alcohol **to** him because he is a minor."},{"sentence":"'**Pagbilhan** nga po ng suka,' sabi ko sa tindera.","translation":"'Please **sell** me some vinegar,' I said to the storekeeper."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kabuuan ng mga nasusulat na akda, lalo na ang mga itinuturing na may mataas na kalidad na pansining, ng isang partikular na wika, bansa, o panahon.
etymology: From 'pala-' (indicating a system or study) + 'titik' (letter) + '-an' (place or collection). It signifies a collection or system of letters/writing.
original_explanation: All the required readings from your Filipino class—from Noli Me Tángere to the works of Nick Joaquin. It's the 'greatest hits' collection of a country's written masterpieces. The stuff that makes you say 'Wow, ang lalim!'
usage_notes: This term is formal and primarily used in academic and literary discussions. 'Panitikan' is a more common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mayaman ang Pilipinas sa **palatitikan** bago pa man dumating ang mga mananakop.","translation":"The Philippines was rich in **literature** even before the colonizers arrived."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan sa kursong Filipino ang iba't ibang anyo ng **palatitikan** ng bansa.","translation":"Different forms of the country's **literature** are studied in the Filipino course."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa sukdulang antas ng pag-aalala o pagiging di-mapakali; labis na nababagabag.
original_explanation: This is 'balisa' on steroids. This is when you've moved past 'seen' and are now contemplating if you should call them, or if you should just throw your phone into the Pasig River and start a new life as a hermit. This is peak anxiety, the final boss of 'kaba'. You're not just worried, you're walking back and forth, checking your phone every 5 seconds, and questioning all your life choices.
usage_notes: An intensified form of 'balisa' created by reduplication. Common in spoken language to add emphasis.
