usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Balisang-balisa** ang ina dahil hindi pa umuuwi ang kanyang anak.","translation":"The mother was **very anxious** because her child had not yet come home."},{"sentence":"Naiwan akong **balisang-balisa** matapos ang aming pag-uusap.","translation":"I was left **extremely restless** after our conversation."}]

translation: to leave something for someone; to leave something at a place
meaning_filipino: Mag-iwan ng isang bagay para sa isang tao o sa isang partikular na lugar.
original_explanation: When you leave the last piece of pizza for your sibling (para hindi ka masabihang madamot). Or when your ex iwaan ka ng emotional baggage. It's the act of leaving something behind, intentionally, for someone or at some place. The "-an" suffix implies a recipient or location.
usage_notes: `Iwanan` is a more common synonym. `Iwaan` can sometimes sound more poetic or dated.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **iwaan** mo ako ng kaunting kanin.","translation":"Please **leave** me a little rice."},{"sentence":"Saan ko ba dapat **iwaan** ang mga dokumento?","translation":"Where should I **leave** the documents?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paghahatid o pagsasabi ng isang impormasyon, kaganapan, o anunsyo sa iba.
original_explanation: The OG 'spill the tea'. Whether you're a news anchor on TV Patrol or the designated 'Marites' of your group chat, your job is to deliver the facts (or the chismis). "Friend, magbalita ka, anong latest?"
usage_notes: Can refer to formal news reporting or informal sharing of information.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si Noli de Castro ay **nagbalita** tungkol sa paparating na bagyo.","translation":"Noli de Castro **reported** about the upcoming typhoon."},{"sentence":"**Magbalita** ka naman kapag nakarating ka na sa bahay ninyo.","translation":"**Inform** me when you've arrived at your house."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kulang pa sa karanasan o kaalaman sa isang partikular na gawain, sining, o propesyon.
etymology: From 'bago' (new) + '-han' (suffix indicating a person characterized by the root).
original_explanation: This is the 'newbie' in the office who still asks where the restroom is, or the 'first-timer' in the gym who has no idea how the machines work. It's that "patience, please, I'm new here" phase of life. In short, the opposite of a 'veteran'.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a person's skill level. Can be used as a noun (a beginner) or an adjective (amateurish).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bilang isang **baguhan** sa pagluluto, sunog ang una niyang sinaing.","translation":"As a **beginner** in cooking, his first attempt at rice got burnt."},{"sentence":"Huwag mo siyang pagtawanan, **baguhan** pa lang siya sa trabaho.","translation":"Don't laugh at him, he's still a **novice** at the job."}]

meaning_filipino: Patunugin ang isang instrumento pangmusika o isang kanta gamit ang isang aparato.
original_explanation: Your personal DJ command. 'Alexa, itugtog mo ang 'Raining in Manila'!' or telling your friend who knows guitar, 'Pre, itugtog mo naman yung paborito kong kanta.' It's the act of bringing music to life, whether you're shredding a guitar solo or just hitting 'play' on Spotify.
usage_notes: Refers specifically to playing music, either on an instrument or from a device. It is not used for playing games (laruin) or playing a role (ganapan).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **itugtog** mo ang paborito kong awitin sa piano.","translation":"Please, **play** my favorite song on the piano."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **itugtog** nang malakas ang radyo sa gabi.","translation":"Don't **play** the radio loudly at night."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na nagbibigay ng proteksyon, kanlungan, o pananggalang laban sa panganib o pinsala. Maaari ring tumukoy sa pagtangkilik o pag-ampon ng isang makapangyarihang tao.
original_explanation: This is your human shield, your "backer," your "may pinanghahawakan." Parang yung feeling na safe ka kasi kasama mo si kuya na siga sa inyo, o kaya may kakilala kang VIP. In short, may "padrino" ka. It's having that invisible force field because you're under someone's wing.
usage_notes: Isang luma o pampanitikang salita. Hindi karaniwang ginagamit sa modernong pakikipag-usap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nananatili siyang ligtas sa ilalim ng **kambil** ng makapangyarihang pinuno.","translation":"He remains safe under the **protection** of the powerful leader."},{"sentence":"Ang pananampalataya ang kanyang naging **kambil** sa gitna ng mga pagsubok.","translation":"Faith became his **shield** amidst the trials."}]

translation: to get a lump; to hit someone to cause a lump
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon o paglitaw ng isang bukol sa katawan. Maaari ring tumukoy sa akto ng pananakit na nagreresulta sa bukol.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung aftermath ng suntukan o 'pag nadapa ka sa hagdan. 'Nagrambulan sila kaya ayun, nagka-bukulan.' It's the state of being covered in lumps and bumps. Also used as a subtle threat: 'Gusto mo bukulan kita?' (Do you want me to give you a lump?).
usage_notes: The meaning can shift based on context. 'Nagka-bukulan' means they got lumps (reciprocal/resultative). 'Bukulan kita' means I will give you a lump (active).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-away ang dalawang bata at nagka-**bukulan** sa katawan.","translation":"The two kids fought and **got lumps** on their bodies."},{"sentence":"Baka **bukulan** ka ng nanay mo kapag nalamang bagsak ka.","translation":"Your mom might **hit you and cause a lump** if she finds out you failed."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang samahan o organisasyong pangkalakalan na binubuo ng mga tao para sa isang partikular na layunin, karaniwan ay para kumita.
original_explanation: This is where you send your resume hoping they offer a signing bonus and free coffee. It's your 9-to-5 life, your BPO mothership, the reason you have 'team building' in Tagaytay. Basically, the place that gives you sahod and stress in equal measure.
usage_notes: The spelling 'kumpanya' is more widely used in modern writing. 'Kompania' is an older but still valid spelling.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naghahanap ako ng trabaho sa isang malaking **kompaniya**.","translation":"I am looking for a job in a big **company**."},{"sentence":"Ang **kompaniya** namin ay magkakaroon ng Christmas party sa susunod na linggo.","translation":"Our **company** will have a Christmas party next week."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng maliit at lumang kanyon o artilerya, karaniwang yari sa tansô.
etymology: Mula sa Malay na 'singga', na tumutukoy sa mga maliliit na baril o kanyon.
original_explanation: The OG 'pew-pew' device from the time of Lapu-Lapu. Before there were high-powered rifles, there was the **singga**, a small cannon that was probably a huge flex to own back in the day. Think of it as the 16th-century equivalent of having the latest iPhone model, but for defending your barangay.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga mandirigma ay naghanda ng kanilang mga **singga** at lantaka para sa paparating na laban.","translation":"The warriors prepared their **culverins** and cannons for the upcoming battle."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mala-halayang sangkap sa loob ng isang selula na pumapalibot sa nukleyus at naglalaman ng iba't ibang organelo.
etymology: Hango sa Ingles na "cytoplasm", na mula sa Griyegong "kytos" (lalagyan, selula) + "plasma" (nabuo, hinulma).
original_explanation: Kung ang cell ay isang bahay, ang sitoplasma 'yung hangin at espasyo sa loob kung saan nakalutang lahat ng gamit (organelles) mo. Parang 'yung gelatin sa fruit salad, 'yun ang sitoplasma, tapos 'yung mga prutas ang organelles. Science!
usage_notes: Isang terminong pang-agham (biyolohiya).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga organelo ng selula ay matatagpuan sa loob ng **sitoplasma**.","translation":"The cell's organelles are found within the **cytoplasm**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mga natatanging kalidad, ugali, o pagkakakilanlan na taglay ng isang tao o bagay na nagpapaiba rito sa iba.
original_explanation: This is your "special power" or your unique quirk. It’s what makes you, you. Maybe your sariling katangian is that you can sleep through any noise, or you can perfectly reheat rice in the microwave every single time. It’s your personal brand, your defining feature that would be listed on your character sheet in a video game.
usage_notes: A neutral term used to describe the unique qualities of a person, place, or thing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bawat tao ay may **sariling katangian** na dapat nating igalang.","translation":"Every person has their **own unique traits** that we should respect."},{"sentence":"Ang pagiging masayahin ay isa sa kanyang mga **sariling katangian**.","translation":"Being cheerful is one of his **personal characteristics**."}]

meaning_filipino: Bigyan ng kalayaan ang isang tao, hayop, o bagay mula sa pagkakakulong, pagkakagapos, o anumang uri ng restriksyon.
original_explanation: Ito yung ultimate 'let go' mo sa kanya. Whether it's freeing a bird from a cage, releasing a prisoner, or finally moving on from a toxic ex. The goal is to grant freedom. 'Kung mahal mo, **palayain** mo.' The national hugot anthem.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin sa literal na konteksto (pagpapalaya mula sa bilangguan) o sa matalinghagang paraan (pagpapalaya sa isang tao mula sa isang pangako, emosyonal na kalayaan).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakiusap ang mga mamamayan na **palayain** ang mga bilanggong pulitikal.","translation":"The citizens pleaded to **free** the political prisoners."},{"sentence":"Panahon na para **palayain** mo ang sarili mo sa mga takot na humahadlang sa'yo.","translation":"It's time to **set yourself free** from the fears that are holding you back."}]

meaning_filipino: Panghalip na panao sa unang panauhan na tumutukoy sa taong nagsasalita at sa isa o higit pang taong kausap.
original_explanation: The ultimate 'kasama ka' pronoun. Unlike 'kami' (we, exclusive), 'tayo' means you, me, and everyone in the GC is included. It’s the 'we' in 'Walang iwanan, beshie, sa hirap at ginhawa, tayo ang bida!'
usage_notes: 'Tayo' is inclusive, meaning it includes the person(s) being spoken to. In contrast, 'kami' is exclusive and does not include the listener.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Saan **tayo** kakain mamaya?","translation":"Where will **we** eat later?"},{"sentence":"Para sa ating lahat ito, kaya dapat magtulungan **tayo**.","translation":"This is for all of us, so **we** should help each other."}]

meaning_filipino: Usap-usapan o kuwentong kumakalat na hindi kumpirmado ang katotohanan, karaniwang tungkol sa pribadong buhay ng ibang tao.
original_explanation: The national sport of the Philippines. It's the tea, the chika, the 'what's the latest?'. From your kapitbahay's love life to a celebrity scandal, if it's being talked about in hushed (or not-so-hushed) tones, it's tsismis. It's the OG social media feed.
usage_notes: 'Tsimis' is a common alternative spelling, but 'tsismis' is the standard form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniniwala sa mga **tsismis** na naririnig mo.","translation":"Don't believe the **gossip** you hear."},{"sentence":"Kumalat ang **tsismis** na magre-resign na raw ang manager.","translation":"The **rumor** spread that the manager is allegedly resigning."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng sarsa na karaniwang gawa sa kamatis, suka, asukal, at mga pampalasa. Sa Pilipinas, popular din ang bersyon na gawa sa saging.
etymology: From English 'ketchup', which itself has a complex origin possibly from Chinese 'kê-tsiap' or Malay 'kicap'.
original_explanation: In the Philippines, when you say 'ketchup,' you gotta specify: tomato or banana? Banana ketchup is the default sawsawan for everything from fried chicken to tortang talong. It’s sweet, it’s red (thanks to food coloring), and it’s the lifeblood of every Pinoy kid's meal. Tomato ketchup is for the bougie folks or for french fries at fast-food chains.
usage_notes: The banana variant is often sweeter and is a staple in many Filipino households and restaurants. The spelling 'ketsap' is also common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakiabot ng **ketchup**, isasawsaw ko lang itong pritong manok.","translation":"Please pass the **ketchup**, I'll just dip this fried chicken."},{"sentence":"Mas gusto ng mga bata ang banana **ketchup** kaysa sa tomato ketchup.","translation":"Kids prefer banana **ketchup** over tomato ketchup."}]

translation: to throw something at each other; to pass blame
meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay o paulit-ulit na paghahagis ng mga bagay sa isa't isa. Sa matalinghagang kahulugan, ito ay ang pagpapasa-pasa ng sisi o responsibilidad.
original_explanation: This is a food fight, but with anything. Or more commonly, a blame game. When a group project fails, the "itsahan ng sisi" begins. "Hindi ako! Siya 'yun!" "Sabi niya tapos na 'yung part niya!" It's the corporate version of "turo-turo," where everyone points fingers until the manager gets tired.
usage_notes: The metaphorical sense of "blame-throwing" (itsahan ng sisi) is very common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimula sa asaran hanggang sa nauwi sa **itsahan** ng putik.","translation":"It started with teasing until it ended with them **throwing** mud **at each other**."},{"sentence":"Tigilan na ninyo ang **itsahan** ng sisi at magtulungan na lang tayo.","translation":"Stop **throwing blame at each other** and let's just help one another."}]

translation: to match; to make things correspond
meaning_filipino: Ang gawing magkatugma, magkabagay, o magkaugnay ang dalawa o higit pang bagay.
original_explanation: The verb for when you're playing matchmaker. This isn't just for people ('Bes, bagay kayo!'), but for everything. Trying to 'pagtugmain' your OOTD? Your schedule with your friend's? The color of the curtains with the sofa? It's the art of finding the perfect pair or combination. When things just click, 'swak na swak', that's successful 'pagtugmain'.
usage_notes: Used for matching items, ideas, schedules, colors, etc.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinusubukan niyang **pagtugmain** ang kanyang iskedyul sa bakasyon ng pamilya.","translation":"She is trying **to match** her schedule with the family's vacation."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **pagtugmain** ang teorya at ang tunay na nangyayari.","translation":"It's difficult **to make** the theory and reality **correspond**."}]

translation: to make one's presence felt; to haunt
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapahiwatig o pagpapakita ng presensya sa isang tao, kadalasan sa paraang hindi direkta o sa pamamagitan ng multo.
original_explanation: What your ex does when they suddenly like your IG story from 24 weeks ago. Also, what ghosts in horror movies do before the big jump scare. 'Magparamdam ka naman!' is the modern cry for 'seen-zoned' people.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin para sa mga taong buhay (pagpaparamdam/pagkontak) at sa mga multo (pagmumulto). Karaniwang ginagamit sa anyong 'magparamdam'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Matagal ka nang hindi nagpa**paramdam**, kumusta ka na?","translation":"You haven't **made your presence felt** in a while, how are you?"},{"sentence":"Sabi nila, nagpa**paramdam** daw ang dating may-ari sa lumang bahay na iyon.","translation":"They say the former owner **haunts** that old house."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang balbal na salita na nangangahulugang masarap.
etymology: Balbal (slang) from reversing the syllables of 'sarap'.
original_explanation: This is the cooler, more street way of saying 'masarap'. When the sisig is sizzling perfectly, or your mom's adobo hits just right, you don't just say it's delicious. You say, 'Wow, rapsa!' It's the sound of pure foodie satisfaction. It's a syllabic reversal of 'sarap'.
usage_notes: Highly informal, commonly used in everyday conversations, especially among younger people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Rapsa** talaga ng luto ni lola!","translation":"Grandma's cooking is really **delicious**!"},{"sentence":"Tara, kain tayo sa karinderya na 'yun, **rapsa** daw ang mga ulam.","translation":"Let's go, let's eat at that eatery, they say the dishes are **tasty**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isulat o i-encode ang mga titik at simbolo gamit ang isang keyboard ng kompyuter, makinilya, o telepono.
original_explanation: The verb that runs the BPO industry and powers your late-night 'where u at?' texts. It's what you do all day at work on a computer, and what you do all night on your phone. 'Pa-type naman ng report ko' is the modern cry for help from a college student. A very direct loanword.
usage_notes: A direct Tagalized version of the English verb 'to type'. Universally understood in the modern Philippines. The root is the English word itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-**type** mo na lang ang mensahe mo para mas malinaw.","translation":"Please just **type** your message so it's clearer."},{"sentence":"Mabilis siyang mag-**type** kahit hindi nakatingin sa keyboard.","translation":"She can **type** fast even without looking at the keyboard."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang hanay ng mga alituntunin, patakaran, o batas na dapat sundin sa isang partikular na lugar, sitwasyon, o organisasyon.
etymology: From the root 'tunton', an old word meaning 'to trace' or 'to follow a path', implying rules are paths to be followed.
original_explanation: The 'Terms and Conditions' you scroll past and click 'Agree' on without reading. From your condo's 'Bawal maingay after 10 PM' policy to the unwritten 'Bawal umutang sa katapusan' rule among friends, these are the guidelines that keep things from turning into chaos. Or at least, that's the plan.
usage_notes: Often used in plural form 'mga tuntunin'. A more formal synonym is 'alituntunin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahigpit ang mga **tuntunin** sa loob ng aklatan.","translation":"The **rules** inside the library are strict."},{"sentence":"Dapat nating sundin ang mga **tuntunin** sa tamang pagtapon ng basura.","translation":"We should follow the **regulations** on proper waste disposal."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagsasagawa ng pagbigti sa isang partikular na lugar o ang paglalagay ng silo para sa isang tao o hayop.
original_explanation: This is the verb form focusing on the location or the act itself, often with a sinister or historical context, like a public execution. 'Saan siya binigtihan?' (Where was he hanged?). It's the verb you'd use in a history textbook talking about capital punishment, not in everyday conversation. It has a heavy, 'place-of-action' feel to it.
usage_notes: Ang hulaping '-an' ay madalas na tumutukoy sa lokasyon o lugar ng isang aksyon. Ang pormang ito ay hindi gaanong karaniwan kaysa 'bigtihin' o 'magbigti'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang plasa ang lugar kung saan nila **binigtihan** ang mga kriminal noong unang panahon.","translation":"The plaza was the place where they **hanged** the criminals in the olden days."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-alis nang palihim kasama ang isang minamahal upang magpakasal nang walang pahintulot ng mga magulang; pagtakas.
original_explanation: The OG "sana all" for forbidden lovers. Bago pa nagkaroon ng "Sana ay 'di na lang kita nakilala" hugots, mayroon nang pagtanan. It's the ultimate romantic (or desperate) act of choosing love over family approval. Think Romeo and Juliet, but with a jeepney ride to the next town.
usage_notes: Often associated with young lovers escaping disapproving families. Can also mean 'running away' in a more general sense, but the elopement connotation is stronger.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagtanan** ng magkasintahan ay naging malaking usapin sa kanilang baryo.","translation":"The **elopement** of the couple became a big issue in their village."},{"sentence":"Pinaplano nila ang **pagtanan** dahil tutol ang mga magulang sa kanilang relasyon.","translation":"They are planning to **run away together** because their parents are against their relationship."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pamimili kung saan nagsasama-sama ang isang grupo ng tao upang umorder ng produkto nang sabay-sabay, karaniwan upang makatipid sa bayad sa pagpapadala o makakuha ng diskuwento.
original_explanation: The 'pasabay' culture leveled up for the digital age. This is what you do when you and your officemates all want milk tea but only want to pay one delivery fee. One person, the designated 'tita' or 'kuya' of the group, takes everyone's orders (and money), places the order, and becomes the hero of the 3 PM slump. The ultimate test of friendship and trust.
usage_notes: A very modern term that became extremely popular with the rise of food delivery apps and online shopping.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sino'ng sasali sa **grouporder** natin para sa tanghalian?","translation":"Who's joining our **group order** for lunch?"},{"sentence":"Mas makakatipid tayo sa shipping fee kung mag-**grouporder** tayo ng K-pop merch.","translation":"We'll save more on the shipping fee if we make a **group order** for the K-pop merch."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na hindi nag-aalala o hindi binibigyang-pansin ang mga problema, responsibilidad, o opinyon ng iba.
original_explanation: That friend who is 'go with the flow' to the extreme. Bills are due? 'Bahala na.' Project deadline tomorrow? 'Chill lang.' The world could be ending and they'd just be sipping their milk tea, completely unbothered. The epitome of 'dedma.'
usage_notes: Can have a positive connotation (carefree, easygoing) or a negative one (irresponsible, apathetic).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko maging katulad niya na **walang-iniintindi** sa buhay.","translation":"I want to be like him, **carefree** in life."},{"sentence":"Mahirap siyang kasama sa grupo dahil **walang-iniintindi** kundi ang sarili niya.","translation":"It's hard to have him in a group because he is **unconcerned** with anyone but himself."}]

translation: to take one's time intentionally; to delay
meaning_filipino: Sadyain ang pagpapabagal o pagpapatagal sa isang gawain o proseso.
etymology: From the prefix `magpaka-` (to deliberately cause oneself to be) and the root `luwat` (slowness, long time).
original_explanation: This is you when your boss gives you a task at 4:55 PM on a Friday. You magpakaluwat so you can officially clock out before you even have to start. Also applies to finishing the last piece of pizza to see who gives in first.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinadya niyang **magpakaluwat** sa palengke para hindi maabutan ang mga bisitang ayaw niya.","translation":"She deliberately **took her time** at the market so she wouldn't have to face the visitors she dislikes."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magpakaluwat** sa pag-aaral ng iyong mga leksyon.","translation":"Don't **delay** in studying your lessons."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na ginagamit upang mag-iwan ng marka, tanda, o palatandaan sa isang lugar o bagay.
original_explanation: Anything you use to mark your territory. It can be a bookmark for your novel, a highlighter for your notes, a dog-ear on a page, or even that 'tuldok' you send in chat to mark a conversation you'll get back to... eventually. It's the 'I was here' tool.
usage_notes: A very general term. Can refer to a physical object ('bookmark') or a conceptual one ('a sign').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ginamit ko ang resibo bilang **pantanda** sa aklat na binabasa ko.","translation":"I used the receipt as a **bookmark** for the book I'm reading."},{"sentence":"Maglagay ka ng **pantanda** sa mapa para hindi tayo maligaw.","translation":"Put a **marker** on the map so we don't get lost."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing patiwarik o baligtarin ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the action version of 'patiwarik'. It's what you do to a bottle to get the last drop of ketchup. It's also what a new manager with crazy ideas does to your team's "perfectly fine" workflow. You take something and intentionally flip it over.
usage_notes: The object receiving the action is the focus.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **patiwarikin** ang bote at matatapon ang laman.","translation":"Don't **turn** the bottle **upside down** or the contents will spill."}]

meaning_filipino: Ginagamit bilang pang-uri upang ilarawan ang dalawang panig o dako ng isang pangngalan.
original_explanation: This is the adjective version of 'magkabila'. Think 'magkabilang pisngi' (both cheeks) getting pinched by your Tita, or 'magkabilang dulo ng LDR niyo' (both ends of your LDR). It's the 'both' that comes *before* a noun, like the 'magkabilang' earphones you use to tune out the world (or your boss).
usage_notes: This is the form used to modify a noun directly. The '-ng' linker attaches to 'magkabila'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hawak niya ang bulaklak sa **magkabilang** kamay.","translation":"She was holding flowers in **both** hands."},{"sentence":"May sugat siya sa **magkabilang** tuhod.","translation":"He has wounds on **both** knees."}]

meaning_filipino: Malalaking kalibre ng mga baril na ginagamit sa digmaan sa lupa; isang sangay ng hukbo na gumagamit ng mga naturang baril.
original_explanation: The heavy-hitters of the battlefield. These aren't your friendly neighborhood paltik. We're talking cannons, howitzers... the kind of firepower that makes a big boom. Think of it as the army's "death metal" section, while infantry is the main rock band.
usage_notes: A collective noun for large-caliber weapons.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang ingay mula sa **artilyeria** ng kaaway ay yumanig sa buong bayan.","translation":"The noise from the enemy's **artillery** shook the entire town."}]

translation: to distribute; to give out a share
meaning_filipino: Ibigay o ipamahagi ang isang bagay sa iba't ibang tao bilang kanilang parte o bahagi.
original_explanation: This is what companies do with their 13th-month pay, or what you do with the chicharon you bought as pasalubong. The root word is 'bahagi' (part/share), so 'pamahagi' is literally "to make something into parts for others." It’s the ultimate "sana all" moment when you're the one giving out the blessings.
usage_notes: 'Ipamahagi' is the more common object-focused form.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang gobyerno ay nagplanong **pamahagi** ng tulong sa mga nasalanta ng bagyo.","translation":"The government planned to **distribute** aid to the typhoon victims."},{"sentence":"Oras na para **pamahagi** ang mga regalo sa mga bata.","translation":"It's time to **give out** the gifts to the children."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang landas o daan na tinatahak o patutunguhan; ang punto kung saan nakaturo o gumagalaw ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: Yung tinatanong mo kay Manong drayber ng jeep, "Manong, anong direksiyon nito?" para sure na hindi ka mapunta sa maling "I love you." Puwede ring 'yung 'direction' ng buhay mo na lagi mong tinatanong sa sarili mo tuwing hatinggabi. One Direction? Wrong Direction? No Direction? Ikaw bahala.
usage_notes: Maaaring isulat din bilang 'direksyon'. Ang pagbaybay na 'direksiyon' ay mas pormal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakituro naman kung saang **direksiyon** ang pinakamalapit na istasyon ng tren.","translation":"Please point me in the **direction** of the nearest train station."},{"sentence":"Nawawala ang **direksiyon** ng ating usapan.","translation":"The **direction** of our conversation is getting lost."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na tumutukoy sa isang bagay na peke, hindi totoo, o huwad.
etymology: Etymology is unclear, likely a slang coinage.
original_explanation: Slang for anything fake or imitation. 'Gura 'yang sapatos mo, 'no? Halata sa tahi.' It's the Greenhills special, the Class A, the 'inspired by' item. Basically, it's not the real deal.
usage_notes: Primarily used in informal, street-level conversations. Can also function as a noun ('puro gura').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang bibili diyan, puro **gura** ang tinda nila.","translation":"Don't buy from there, all their goods are **fake**."},{"sentence":"Mukhang orig pero **gura** lang pala ang relo niya.","translation":"His watch looks original but it's just a **counterfeit**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao na may mahinahon, banayad, at hindi malakas na boses.
original_explanation: The opposite of your tita who talks like she's using a megaphone 24/7. A soft-spoken person is someone you have to lean in to hear, even when there's no noise. They don't shout when they're angry; they just get quieter, which is honestly scarier. They're the Maria Clara of speaking voices.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit para ilarawan ang personalidad o paraan ng pananalita ng isang tao.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya bilang isang **soft-spoken** na lider, ngunit matatag ang kanyang mga desisyon.","translation":"He is known as a **soft-spoken** leader, but his decisions are firm."},{"sentence":"Dahil **soft-spoken** siya, minsan ay hindi siya marinig sa maingay na silid.","translation":"Because she is **soft-spoken**, sometimes she can't be heard in a noisy room."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang magalang na pahayag ng papuri, paghanga, o paggalang.
original_explanation: Ito yung sinasabi ng tita mo na 'Uy, tumaba ka!' na hindi mo sure kung kompliment ba o insulto. Pero ideally, ito yung 'Ang ganda mo ngayon!' na nagpapakilig sa'yo buong araw.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'papuri'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Salamat sa iyong **kompliment**.","translation":"Thank you for your **compliment**."},{"sentence":"Isang simpleng **kompliment** ay sapat na para pasayahin ang kanyang araw.","translation":"A simple **compliment** is enough to make her day."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagbukas ng bibig nang malaki at lumanghap ng hangin, karaniwang senyales ng pagkaantok o pagkabagot.
original_explanation: The body's way of saying 'Low batt na ako, bes.' O 'yung involuntary reaction mo sa meeting na dapat ay isang email lang. Bigla ka na lang humikab sa gitna ng presentation ng boss mo. Awkward.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bigla siyang **humikab** sa gitna ng klase dahil sa antok.","translation":"He suddenly **yawned** in the middle of the class because he was sleepy."},{"sentence":"Nang **humikab** ang isa, lahat kami ay nahawa na rin.","translation":"When one **yawned**, all of us were infected by it too."}]

translation: to set aside, to put aside
meaning_filipino: Ang paghiwalay o paglalagay sa isang tabi ng isang bagay para sa isang partikular na layunin, para hindi makasagabal, o para itabi pansamantala.
original_explanation: What you do with your feelings when you need to be professional at work. 'Hugot? Magsaisang-tabi mo muna 'yan, may deadline.' It's also what you do with a portion of your sahod for your 'ipon goals' before you spend it all on milk tea.
usage_notes: Can refer to physical objects, money, or abstract things like feelings or problems.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **magsaisang-tabi** ng pera para sa ating kinabukasan.","translation":"We need to **set aside** money for our future."},{"sentence":"Pilit niyang **isinantabi** ang kanyang mga problema upang makapag-focus sa trabaho.","translation":"He forced himself to **put aside** his problems to focus on work."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kalagayan kung saan ang bibig ay nakabukas nang malaki, kadalasan dahil sa pagkamangha, pagkatulog, o pagkapagod.
etymology: From "pala-" (prefix indicating a tendency or state) + "nganga" (state of having the mouth open).
original_explanation: This is your face when you see the latest chismis, when you see your crush, or when you fall asleep during a commute with your mouth wide open. It’s the default expression of shock, awe, or being completely knocked out. The fly-catcher look.
usage_notes: Describes a state, often involuntary. Can be used humorously or to describe someone in awe.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naiwan siyang **palanganga** sa sobrang gulat.","translation":"He was left **gaping** in utter surprise."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang matulog na **palanganga** sa bus, baka manakawan ka.","translation":"Don't sleep with your mouth **wide open** on the bus, you might get robbed."}]

meaning_filipino: Kasalukuyang naghahanda ng pagkain sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng init, gaya ng pagprito, paggisa, o pagpapakulo.
etymology: From "luto" (cook) with the "nag-" prefix and "-lu-" infix (reduplication of the first syllable of the root).
original_explanation: The source of that heavenly adobo or sinigang smell wafting from the kitchen. When someone is nagluluto, it means food is coming soon! It's the sound of sizzling garlic and onions, the bubbling of soup, and the promise of a full stomach. 'Amoy-luto ka!' is what your friends say when you come from a house where someone was nagluluto.
usage_notes: Very common verb for the act of cooking in the present progressive tense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang nanay ko ay **nagluluto** ng paborito naming sinigang.","translation":"My mother is **cooking** our favorite sinigang."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **nagluluto**? Ang bango ng amoy!","translation":"Who is **cooking**? It smells so good!"}]

translation: To kill; to turn off; to extinguish
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkitil sa buhay ng isang tao, hayop, o halaman; ang paghinto sa paggana ng isang bagay tulad ng ilaw o makina.
etymology: From 'patay' (dead) + '-in' (object-focus verbal suffix). The user requested 'patayain', a less common variant, so this entry uses the standard form 'patayin'.
original_explanation: The verb form of 'cancel culture' when taken to its most extreme, literal, and illegal conclusion. It's also what you do to the lights before a 'Netflix and chill' session, or what you do to your alarm clock in a fit of rage. Context is everything. 'Gusto kitang patayin... sa pagmamahal' is the cheesy pickup line version.
usage_notes: A very common verb with both literal (to kill) and figurative (to turn off) meanings. The specific meaning is determined by the object of the verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Patayin** mo ang ilaw pag-alis mo.","translation":"**Turn off** the light when you leave."},{"sentence":"Bawal **patayin** ang mga hayop sa loob ng reserbasyon.","translation":"It is forbidden **to kill** the animals inside the reservation."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kapatid na lalaki ng asawa, o ang asawa ng kapatid na babae.
original_explanation: This is your sister's husband or your wife's brother. He's the guy you're obligated to invite for inuman sessions and family gatherings. He's either your best buddy or the reason for some family drama. 'Kuya Bayaw' is the default title.
usage_notes: The female counterpart is 'hipag' (sister-in-law).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pupunta kami sa bahay ng **bayaw** ko para sa Pasko.","translation":"We are going to my **brother-in-law's** house for Christmas."},{"sentence":"Si Marco ang paborito kong **bayaw** dahil pareho kaming mahilig sa basketball.","translation":"Marco is my favorite **brother-in-law** because we both love basketball."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang kalagayan ng matinding kakulangan o kahirapan sa mga pangunahing pangangailangan.
original_explanation: This is beyond 'petsa de peligro.' This is when your wallet has cobwebs and your bank account is giving '404 Not Found.' **Dahop** is a state of extreme scarcity, whether it's in finances, resources, or even love life. 'Dahop sa pag-ibig.' See? Hugot.
usage_notes: A strong word for poverty or lack. More formal than 'mahirap'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming pamilya ang namumuhay nang **dahop** sa mga liblib na lugar.","translation":"Many families live **destitute** in remote areas."},{"sentence":"Ang kanilang komunidad ay **dahop** sa malinis na tubig.","translation":"Their community is **lacking** in clean water."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang katangian ng pagiging mabagal, makupad, o hindi mabilis sa pagkilos, pag-iisip, o pag-unlad.
original_explanation: This is the state of your brain before your first cup of coffee. It's the speed of government processing on a Monday morning. It's the WiFi connection when everyone in the house is streaming Netflix. *Kalumatan* is the official mood of '5 more minutes' of sleep.
usage_notes: An old or literary word. 'Kabagalan' is the more common term for slowness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kalumatan** ng pag-usad ng pila ay nagdulot ng inis sa marami.","translation":"The **slowness** of the line's movement annoyed many."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa kanyang sakit, ramdam niya ang **kalumatan** ng kanyang katawan.","translation":"Because of his illness, he felt the **sluggishness** of his body."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang solidong bahagi ng ibabaw ng mundo na hindi sakop ng tubig. Ito rin ay tumutukoy sa teritoryo o lupain at sa materyal na ginagamit sa pagtatanim.
original_explanation: The stuff you walk on, the stuff your condo is built on, and the stuff your parents keep telling you to buy ('Bumili ka na ng lupa!'). It's both the dirt in your garden and the ultimate Filipino adulting goal: owning a piece of it.
usage_notes: A fundamental and versatile word. Can refer to soil, land as property, or the planet Earth.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan natin ng matabang **lupa** para sa ating mga pananim.","translation":"We need fertile **soil** for our crops."},{"sentence":"Tumataas na ang presyo ng **lupa** sa siyudad.","translation":"The price of **land** in the city is increasing."}]

translation: to do laundry; to wash clothes
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglilinis ng mga damit at iba pang tela sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng tubig at sabon.
original_explanation: The national weekend sport of the Philippines. It's the sacred ritual of turning your 'labahin' (dirty laundry) into fresh, sun-dried clothes. Whether by hand ('kusot-kusot'), washing machine, or dropping it off at the local labandera, this is the ultimate act of adulting. The opposite of 'tambak.'
usage_notes: A very common household chore. Can refer to hand-washing or machine-washing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tuwing Sabado ako **naglaba** ng mga damit namin.","translation":"I **do our laundry** every Saturday."},{"sentence":"Sino ang taya para **maglaba** ngayon?","translation":"Whose turn is it to **wash the clothes** today?"}]

translation: to lessen, to decrease, to become few
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbaba o pagkabawas sa dami, bilang, o sukat ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: Ito yung nangyayari sa sahod mo five minutes after payday. Biglang umunti na lang na parang magic. Pwede ring feelings niya for you, bes. Aray.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with "kumaunti" from the root "konti".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Umunti** ang bilang ng mga dumalo sa pagpupulong dahil sa malakas na ulan.","translation":"The number of attendees at the meeting **lessened** because of the heavy rain."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, **uunti** rin ang mga problema mo.","translation":"Don't worry, your problems will also **decrease**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pampalasa at pangkulay sa pagkain na mula sa buto ng punong Achiote (Bixa orellana), na kilala sa Pilipinas bilang atsuete.
etymology: From Spanish 'annatto', which is derived from a Carib language term.
original_explanation: Ah, the official colorist of Pinoy cuisine! This is the secret ingredient that gives kare-kare, palabok, and tocino their signature reddish-orange glow-up. It's the food-grade makeup that makes dishes look more 'masarap' and IG-worthy. Filipinos almost always call it 'atsuete'.
usage_notes: The word "annatto" is used in English or formal culinary contexts. In everyday Filipino life and cooking, the Hispanicized term "atsuete" is exclusively used.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"The recipe calls for **annatto** powder to give the chicken a vibrant color.","translation":"Ang resipe ay nangangailangan ng pulbos na **atsuete** upang bigyan ng matingkad na kulay ang manok."},{"sentence":"Para sa mas natural na kulay, gumamit ng **annatto** seeds na ibinabad sa mantika.","translation":"For a more natural color, use **annatto** seeds soaked in oil."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapatala o pagpapalista upang regular na makatanggap ng isang produkto, serbisyo, o nilalaman, karaniwan ay may kaakibat na bayad.
original_explanation: Yung ginagawa mo sa YouTube channel ng paborito mong vlogger para hindi ka mahuli sa pinakabagong chismis o life update. 'Pa-subscribe naman diyan, besh!' ay ang modernong 'Amen' ng mga content creator.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa konteksto ng social media, streaming services, at iba pang digital na plataporma.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang mag-**subscribe** sa aming channel para sa mga bagong video.","translation":"Don't forget to **subscribe** to our channel for new videos."},{"sentence":"Nag-**subscribe** ako sa Netflix para mapanood ang paborito kong serye.","translation":"I **subscribed** to Netflix to watch my favorite series."}]

meaning_filipino: Nauukol sa sining o kasanayan ng pagtatalumpati sa publiko.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na 'oratorical' na nangangahulugang nauukol sa oratoryo o pagtatalumpati.
original_explanation: The fancy word for that "Buwan ng Wika" speech contest vibe. It's that dramatic, over-the-top way of speaking, complete with hand gestures and intense facial expressions, that makes you a champion in Sabayang Pagbigkas or a student council presidential candidate. "Ang galing ng delivery, pang-oratorikal!"
usage_notes: Used in formal or academic settings, especially related to public speaking competitions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nanalo siya sa patimpalak na **oratorikal** dahil sa kanyang madamdaming pagbigkas.","translation":"She won the **oratorical** contest because of her emotional delivery."},{"sentence":"Ang kanyang istilo ay masyadong **oratorikal** para sa isang simpleng pag-uusap.","translation":"His style is too **oratorical** for a simple conversation."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pag-ipit sa balat o laman gamit ang dulo ng hinlalaki at hintuturo.
original_explanation: The OG Filipino way of showing affection or discipline. Your tita does this to your cheeks when she says you've gotten fat ("Ang taba-taba mo na!"). Your mom does this to your side ("tagiliran") when you're misbehaving in public. It can be cute, it can be painful, but it's always memorable.
usage_notes: Can also be used metaphorically, e.g., "kumurot sa puso" (to tug at the heartstrings).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumurot** ang nanay sa pisngi ng kanyang cute na sanggol.","translation":"The mother **pinched** the cheek of her cute baby."},{"sentence":"Talagang **kumurot** sa puso ko ang napanood kong pelikula.","translation":"The movie I watched really **tugged** at my heartstrings."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na kasangkot sa politika bilang isang propesyon o may hawak na katungkulan sa pamahalaan.
original_explanation: The person whose face is on every lamppost, calendar, and water bottle during election season. They're the ones who make promises, kiss babies, and attend every fiesta. Can be a noble public servant or... well, you know. The main character (or kontrabida) in the teleserye of 'politika'.
usage_notes: Ang termino ay maaaring neutral, ngunit madalas na may bahagyang negatibo o mapanuyang konotasyon sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap, depende sa konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nangako ang **politiko** na aayusin niya ang mga kalsada sa kanilang bayan.","translation":"The **politician** promised to fix the roads in their town."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lababo o lugar na partikular na ginagamit para sa paghuhugas, karaniwan ng mga kamay o pinagkainan.
original_explanation: The official tambayan of dirty dishes. The place where you contemplate your life choices while scrubbing the kaldero from last night's adobo. Also known as the 'lababo'.
usage_notes: While 'lababo' (from Spanish 'lavabo') is more common for the modern kitchen sink, 'pahugasan' is also widely understood and used, especially for more traditional or outdoor washing areas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ilagay mo na lang ang mga maruruming plato sa **pahugasan**.","translation":"Just put the dirty plates in the **sink**."},{"sentence":"May gripo sa tabi ng **pahugasan** sa likod-bahay.","translation":"There is a faucet beside the **wash area** at the backyard."}]

meaning_filipino: Paghagis o pag-alis ng isang bagay na hindi na kailangan o gusto; itabi sa basurahan.
original_explanation: The official verb of 'decluttering.' It's what Marie Kondo tells you to do with things that don't spark joy. From your ex's old photos to the styrofoam cup from your last milk tea, the act of yeeting something into the trash is to magtapon. Just remember: 'Bawal magtapon ng basura dito!'
usage_notes: The most common verb for disposing of trash.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magtapon** ng basura sa kalye.","translation":"Do not **throw** trash on the street."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ko nang **magtapon** ng mga lumang damit na hindi ko na isinusuot.","translation":"I need to **throw away** the old clothes I no longer wear."}]

translation: to have something served on a tray
meaning_filipino: Ang pag-uutos o paghiling na ilagay at ihatid ang isang bagay, karaniwan ay pagkain o inumin, gamit ang isang bandeha.
original_explanation: Feeling like a VIP or a sick person in a telenovela. "Can you bring me coffee?" is one thing, but when you *magpabandeha* ka ng kape, it means you want it delivered to you on a tray. It's the "I'm not getting out of bed" level of service request.
usage_notes: Implies a request for service or being in a position to command service.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil may lagnat siya, **nagpabandeha** na lang siya ng hapunan sa kanyang kwarto.","translation":"Because she had a fever, she just **had her dinner served on a tray** in her room."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa dulo ng isang bagay na bilugan, mapurol, at hindi matalim.
original_explanation: Think of the opposite of 'matulis' (sharp). It's that pencil you've been using for 3 hours straight without sharpening. Or the tip of a used-up ballpen. Not sharp enough to be dangerous, just annoying.
usage_notes: Often used to describe the point of a writing instrument or a tool that has become blunt. Can also be used as a noun to mean 'a blunt point'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Tulsok** na ang lapis ko, kailangan ko nang tasahan.","translation":"My pencil's point is **dull**, I need to sharpen it."},{"sentence":"Naging **tulsok** ang dulo ng pako kaya hindi na bumaon.","translation":"The tip of the nail became **blunted** so it wouldn't go in anymore."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang partikular na uri ng sitsaron na gawa mismo sa balat ng baboy, na karaniwang may kasamang kaunting taba.
etymology: Tambalang salita ng "sitsaron" (mula sa Espanyol na "chicharrón") at "baboy".
original_explanation: This is the OG, the classic, the "putok-batok" king. While other chicharons exist (like chicken or fish skin), 'sitsarong baboy' is the one that comes to mind when you hear the word. It's the crunch that launched a thousand food comas. The 'laman' (meat and fat) to 'balat' (skin) ratio is a topic of serious debate among connoisseurs.
usage_notes: Ito ang pinakakaraniwang uri ng sitsaron. Sa pang-araw-araw na usapan, ang "sitsaron" ay madalas nang tumutukoy sa "sitsarong baboy" kahit hindi na banggitin ang "baboy".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas masarap ang **sitsarong baboy** na may laman kaysa sa puro balat lang.","translation":"**Pork rinds** with some meat attached are more delicious than just the skin."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha ng mga tunog na musikal gamit ang boses, na may tiyak na himig at ritmo.
original_explanation: 'Yung ginagawa mo sa videoke after three bottles of Red Horse, kahit sintunado ka pa. Or 'yung bigla kang napapa-sample sa "Torete" kapag umuulan. The act of singing, whether you're the next Regine Velasquez or just trying to annoy your siblings.
usage_notes: Verb in the completed aspect (past tense). The infinitive is 'kumanta', present is 'kumakanta', and future is 'kakanta'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kumanta** siya ng paborito niyang OPM song sa party.","translation":"She **sang** her favorite OPM song at the party."},{"sentence":"Sino ang **kumanta** ng theme song ng seryeng iyon?","translation":"Who **sang** the theme song of that series?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang anyo ng 'nariyan' na nagbibigay-diin sa tiyak na pagkakaroon o kinalalagyan ng isang bagay o tao sa lugar na malapit sa kausap.
etymology: From na- + ri- (reduplication) + iyan (that, near you). A more emphatic form of 'nariyan'.
original_explanation: It's like 'nariyan' but with extra feelings. When you're on a video call and you ask your friend, 'Where's the cat?' and they point just off-screen and say, '**Naririyan** lang, natutulog.' It means 'right there,' with a little more emphasis, as if to say 'see? I told you.'
usage_notes: 'Naririyan' is used for something near the person being spoken to. It's more emphatic than 'nariyan'. It's the intermediate point between 'narito' (here by me) and 'naroroon' (over there, far from both of us).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, **naririyan** lang ako sa tabi mo.","translation":"Don't worry, I'm right **there** by your side."},{"sentence":"Ang libro mo? **Naririyan** sa mesa sa harap mo.","translation":"Your book? It's right **there** on the table in front of you."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay, tao, o pook na naging paksa ng mga alamat; tanyag at madalas na pinag-uusapan sa paglipas ng panahon.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `ma-` (nagpapahiwatig ng katangian) at salitang-ugat na `alamat` (legend).
original_explanation: 'Yung kuwento ng pinya. O 'yung chismis sa office na sobrang unbelievable pero pinapasa-pasa pa rin for years. It's the stuff of legends, whether it's about Bernardo Carpio or 'yung co-worker na naka-10 years sa company without taking a single sick leave.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin para sa mga tunay na alamat at mito, o bilang hyperbole para sa mga bagay o tao na sikat o may matagal nang kuwento sa likod nila.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang Bundok Makiling ay isang **maalamat** na lugar sa Laguna.","translation":"Mount Makiling is a **legendary** place in Laguna."},{"sentence":"Naging **maalamat** ang kuwento ng kanilang pag-iibigan.","translation":"The story of their romance became **legendary**."}]

translation: to eat voraciously; to pig out
meaning_filipino: Kumain nang marami at walang tigil, kadalasan sa paraang mabilis at tila nagugutom.
original_explanation: The official verb for your 'unli-rice' mode. It's not just eating; it's a full-on, no-holds-barred assault on the buffet table. Think of how you eat after a long day of fasting, or how your barkada demolishes a bilao of pancit. That's maglantakan. Food coma is the likely endgame.
usage_notes: Often used in a very informal, almost crude way to describe intense eating. It can be used for a group or an individual.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tara, **maglantakan** tayo ng samgyupsal mamaya!","translation":"Let's go **pig out** on samgyupsal later!"},{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng laro, **naglantakan** ng pizza ang buong team.","translation":"After the game, the whole team **devoured** pizza."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang magtamo ng pinsala sa kasukasuan, karaniwan sa paa o kamay, dahil sa biglaang pagka-baluktot o pagka-unat nito.
original_explanation: What happens when you try to do a TikTok dance challenge your body isn't ready for. Or when you wear high heels on the bumpy sidewalks of Manila. The result is a painful 'aray' and a week of limping, armed with a bottle of Omega Pain Killer.
usage_notes: A common injury. The 'ma-'-'-an' construction indicates an unintentional or accidental occurrence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa pagbaba ng hagdan at baka ka **mapilayan**.","translation":"Be careful going down the stairs or you might **get a sprain**."},{"sentence":"**Napilayan** ang manlalaro kaya hindi siya nakasama sa finals.","translation":"The player **got a sprain** so he couldn't join the finals."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng prinosesong karne ng baka na inimbak sa asin, karaniwang inilalata at ginigisa kasama ng sibuyas at patatas para sa almusal.
original_explanation: Ang pambansang ulam ng mga nagmamadali at mga single. De-lata na pwedeng i-partner sa sinangag at itlog. Pag ginisa na may kasamang patatas at sibuyas, instant gourmet na ang feeling. The ultimate "I don't know what to cook" breakfast solution.
usage_notes: Almost always refers to the canned, shredded variety popular in the Philippines, not the deli-style brisket.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paborito kong almusal ang **corned beef** na may sinangag at itlog.","translation":"My favorite breakfast is **corned beef** with fried rice and egg."},{"sentence":"Pakigisa naman 'yung isang lata ng **corned beef** para sa mga bata.","translation":"Please sauté the can of **corned beef** for the kids."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng laro na gumagamit ng maliliit na raketa at isang magaan na bola, nilalaro sa ibabaw ng isang mesa na may net sa gitna.
original_explanation: Ito yung sport na akala mo madali lang pero pag sineryoso mo, para kang nag-Zumba sa liit ng space. Kilala rin bilang table tennis. Perfect 'to para sa mga ayaw maarawan pero gusto pawisan.
usage_notes: Ginagamit bilang direktang pangalan para sa larong table tennis. Itinuturing na isang salitang-ugat sa Tagalog kahit ito ay hiram na salita.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Magaling maglaro ng **pimpong** si Mang Tonyo.","translation":"Mang Tonyo is good at playing **table tennis**."},{"sentence":"Bumili kami ng bagong set ng **pimpong** para sa opisina.","translation":"We bought a new **table tennis** set for the office."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malawakang pagkalat ng apoy na tumupok sa malaking lugar o maraming ari-arian.
original_explanation: This is when the fire isn't just in your neighbor's house, but the entire block. It's a 'big fire' that requires more than one fire truck and becomes the main topic in the barangay group chat for weeks.
usage_notes: Used to describe a fire of significant scale, often one that requires a major response from firefighters and results in substantial property damage.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **malaking sunog** ang sumiklab sa isang pabrika sa Valenzuela.","translation":"A **big fire** broke out in a factory in Valenzuela."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pangkat ng mga sundalo na nakikipaglaban habang nakasakay sa kabayo.
original_explanation: The original 'fast and furious' squad. Before tanks and fighter jets, if you needed to send in the elite, fast-moving troops, you called the kabalyeria. Think of them as the GrabExpress of ancient warfare, delivering swords and spears instead of food.
usage_notes: A historical military term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **kabalyeria** ng Espanya ay kinatatakutan noong unang panahon.","translation":"The Spanish **cavalry** was feared in the old days."},{"sentence":"Nilusob ng **kabalyeria** ang kampo ng mga kaaway.","translation":"The **cavalry** charged the enemy camp."}]

translation: Peak; height (of an event); thick (of an event)
meaning_filipino: Ang kasukdulan, pinakamatindi, o pinakaabala na bahagi ng isang pangyayari, panahon, o gawain.
etymology: From 'sagsag' (to be busy, to go on relentlessly).
original_explanation: It's the 'kasagsagan' of the 12.12 sale when everyone's adding to cart and the website is about to crash. It's the 'kasagsagan' of summer when it's so hot you can fry an egg on the pavement. It's the primetime, the rush hour, the most intense part of anything.
usage_notes: Almost always used with the prefix 'ka-', forming 'kasagsagan', to mean 'the very peak/height of'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sa **kasagsagan** ng bagyo, nawalan kami ng kuryente.","translation":"At the **height** of the storm, we lost electricity."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang pupunta sa mall sa **kasagsagan** ng Christmas rush.","translation":"Don't go to the mall in the **thick** of the Christmas rush."}]

meaning_filipino: Bumuo ng isang malinaw na larawan sa isip; gunigunihin o isipin ang isang bagay na wala pa, hindi pa nangyayari, o kathang-isip lamang.
etymology: From 'haraya' (imagination, illusion), a word of Austronesian origin.
original_explanation: This is your brain on 'what if' mode. It's daydreaming about your crush, planning your future beach house, or thinking about what you'd do if you won the lottery. It's the power to create worlds, scenarios, and 'sana all' moments in your head. The root word 'haraya' means imagination. A very poetic way to say 'imagine.'
usage_notes: A more literary or deep word for 'to imagine'. 'Isipin' or 'gunigunihin' are more common in everyday conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Subukan mong **harayain** ang isang mundong walang kahirapan.","translation":"Try **to imagine** a world without poverty."},{"sentence":"**Hinaraya** niya ang kanyang sarili bilang isang matagumpay na arkitekto.","translation":"She **envisioned** herself as a successful architect."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pag-aalaga, pagkalinga, o pag-ampon sa isang tao, lalo na sa isang hindi tunay na anak.
etymology: Sinaunang salitang Tagalog na may hindi tiyak na pinagmulan, ngunit may kinalaman sa konsepto ng pangangalaga.
original_explanation: This is a deep, old-school word for taking someone in and raising them as your own, even if you're not related by blood. It's the ultimate 'ampon' energy. Think of a Darna story where a kind old couple finds a baby in a crater. That's **anduka**. It’s the OG 'found family' trope, full of kalinga and aruga.
usage_notes: Napakadalang sa modernong pag-uusap. Malamang na makikita ito sa mga klasikong panitikan, mga tekstong pangkasaysayan, o malalim na tula.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **anduka** sa mga ulila ay isang marangal na gawain.","translation":"The **foster care** of orphans is a noble deed."},{"sentence":"Lumaki siya sa **anduka** ng kanyang mga tiyahin.","translation":"He grew up under the **nurturing** of his aunts."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang kilos ng paglalagay ng pambalot sa isang bagay, tulad ng papel o plastik, upang ito ay takpan, protektahan, o gawing regalo.
original_explanation: What you're doing at 2 AM on Christmas Eve with a mountain of gifts, tape, and gift wrappers. Also, 'yung tita mong nagbabalot ng pagkain sa party para may take-out. "Huwag kang mahiya, nagbabalot din ako." It's a sign of a true Pinoy party.
usage_notes: The verb form of 'balot' (wrap). Not to be confused with the noun 'balut' (fertilized duck egg), though they have the same spelling. Context is key.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Si nanay ay **nagbabalot** ng mga regalo para sa Pasko.","translation":"Mom is **wrapping** gifts for Christmas."},{"sentence":"Siya ang laging **nagbabalot** ng tirang pagkain pagkatapos ng handaan.","translation":"She is always the one **wrapping** leftover food after the feast."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa bahagi, daan, o pinto na nasa likod. Maaari ring tumukoy sa isang bagay na ginagamit para sa likod.
original_explanation: This is the 'backdoor' entry, literally and figuratively. The 'pinto sa panlikuran' is where you sneak in late at night. It can also refer to anything 'for the back,' like a back scratcher ('pangamot na panlikuran'). In office politics, it's the unofficial channel or the backroom deal.
usage_notes: Commonly used in 'pintong panlikuran' for 'back door'. Can also be a noun referring to the rear area.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dumaan sila sa daanang **panlikuran** para hindi sila makita.","translation":"They passed through the **rear** path so they wouldn't be seen."},{"sentence":"Nakasara ang pintong **panlikuran** ng bahay.","translation":"The **back** door of the house is closed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang bahagi ng katawan ng tao o hayop na karaniwang nasa itaas at naglalaman ng utak, mata, bibig, ilong, at tainga.
original_explanation: The thing on top of your neck that carries your brain, your face, and all your bad decisions. It's also used figuratively. 'Malaki ang ulo' means you're arrogant, not that you need a bigger hat. 'Matigas ang ulo' means you're stubborn. And 'ulo ng balita' is a headline, the 'head' of the news.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for the body part or figuratively for arrogance ('malaki ang ulo'), intelligence ('may ulo'), stubbornness ('matigas ang ulo'), or leadership ('ulo ng pamilya').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumasakit ang **ulo** ko sa dami ng iniisip.","translation":"My **head** hurts from thinking too much."},{"sentence":"Lumaki na ang **ulo** niya simula nang sumikat siya.","translation":"He's gotten a big **head** (become arrogant) since he became famous."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang titulo ng nobilidad sa Europa na mas mataas sa baron ngunit mas mababa sa konde o earl.
original_explanation: A title you'd only encounter in history class, romance pocketbooks, or maybe a Netflix series like 'Bridgerton'. A biskonde is a nobleman, somewhere between a baron and an earl on the chismis ladder of European royalty. In the Philippines, the closest we have are probably hacienderos or maybe that one classmate whose family owns a bus line.
usage_notes: Extremely rare in modern conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pangunahing tauhan sa nobela ay isang mayamang **biskonde**.","translation":"The main character in the novel is a wealthy **viscount**."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aaralan nila ang herarkiya ng mga nobilidad, kasama na ang titulo ng **biskonde**.","translation":"They are studying the hierarchy of nobility, including the title of **viscount**."}]

translation: to become cheap, to decrease in price
meaning_filipino: Bumaba ang presyo o halaga ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: The moment every tita at the palengke is waiting for. "Kailan kaya magmumura ang sibuyas?" is a question of national importance. It's the opposite of inflation and the reason for "SALE!" signs.
usage_notes: This refers to a decrease in price. The root word 'mura' (cheap) is pronounced with stress on the first syllable: /MU-ra/. The verb form often retains this stress pattern /MAG-mu-ra/.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana **magmura** na ang presyo ng gasolina.","translation":"I hope the price of gasoline **becomes cheaper**."},{"sentence":"Aabangan ko na **magmura** ang mga bilihin bago ako mamili para sa Pasko.","translation":"I will wait for the goods to **decrease in price** before I shop for Christmas."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay na nagbibigay-ginhawa o aliw sa isang taong malungkot o nabigo.
original_explanation: 'Yung "at least" moment mo. Talo sa contest? "At least, may free food." Binasted ka? "At least, naging honest ka sa feelings mo." 'Yung maliit na silver lining o pampalubag-loob. The konsuwelo prize is the classic example.
usage_notes: Often used as 'konsuwelo de bobo' (a fool's consolation), a small, almost meaningless comfort.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang panalo niya sa raffle ay nagsilbing **konsuwelo** matapos ang masamang araw.","translation":"His raffle win served as a **consolation** after a bad day."},{"sentence":"Kahit natalo, may **konsuwelo** prize naman para sa lahat ng sumali.","translation":"Even though they lost, there was a **consolation** prize for all participants."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paglalagay ng kulay sa isang bagay, lalo na sa tela, buhok, o iba pang materyales, gamit ang isang pangkulay o tina.
original_explanation: This is what you do when you're going through a phase and decide to get pink hair. Or when you want to revive an old white shirt by making it tie-dye. "Tinain" is the verb form of adding color. Parang sa buhay, minsan kailangan mong 'tinain' ang mundo mo para 'di maging boring at black and white lang.
usage_notes: The root word "tina" means dye. "Tinain" is the command/infinitive form. "Tinina" is the past tense.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **tinain** ng asul ang aking buhok para sa bakasyon.","translation":"I want to **dye** my hair blue for the vacation."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong kalimutang **tinain** ang mga puting tela para sa proyekto natin.","translation":"Don't forget to **dye** the white fabrics for our project."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang paraan ng pagpapahayag o komunikasyon na ginagamitan ng pagsusulat; isang bagay na nakasulat.
etymology: The `pa-` prefix indicates manner or way + `sulat` (write).
original_explanation: The opposite of 'sabi-sabi lang.' This is the 'get it in writing' mode. If it's not pasulat, it's just chismis. Your resignation, your love letter, your promissory note to your friend—they all carry more weight when they are pasulat. It's the official, no-take-backsies way of communicating.
usage_notes: Often used as an adverb ('sa paraang pasulat') or an adjective.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong magsumite ng **pasulat** na pahintulot mula sa iyong mga magulang.","translation":"You need to submit a **written** consent from your parents."},{"sentence":"Idaan mo na lang sa **pasulat** ang iyong reklamo para pormal.","translation":"Just course your complaint **in writing** to make it formal."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi maliwanag, malabo, o mahirap unawain, makita, o marinig.
original_explanation: Like your situationship status: 'Ano ba talaga tayo?' That's di-malinaw. Or your boss's instructions that sound like a riddle. Or that 240p YouTube video from 2008. Or your future. Charot. If it's hazy, confusing, or hard to make out, it's di-malinaw.
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa paningin (malabo), tunog (mahina), o mga konsepto (hindi tiyak).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Di-malinaw** ang mga tagubilin kaya nagkamali kami.","translation":"The instructions were **unclear**, that's why we made a mistake."},{"sentence":"Naging **di-malinaw** ang kanyang paningin dahil sa pagod.","translation":"His vision became **blurry** due to fatigue."}]

translation: to be coiled by, to be entangled by
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging palibutan o pagapangan ng isang bagay, tulad ng baging o ahas, sa isang partikular na obheto o lugar.
original_explanation: Imagine being the tree and 'yung ahas ay 'yung utang mo sa credit card, slowly wrapping around you until you can't breathe. Or 'yung pagiging clingy ng jowa mo. 'Yan 'yung feeling na pinamumuluputan ka.
usage_notes: This is an object-focus verb form. It describes the thing that is being wrapped around.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **pamuluputan** ng utang ang iyong buhay.","translation":"Don't let your life **be entangled by** debt."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula nang **pamuluputan** ng baging ang mga haligi ng lumang bahay.","translation":"Vines have started **to coil around** the pillars of the old house."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng pagpapagaling, pag-iwas, o pagharap sa isang karamdaman.
original_explanation: This is the battle against anything from the common cold ('trangkaso') to more serious illnesses. It's taking your meds, drinking lots of water, and resting, even if your boss is messaging you. Eto yung moment na ang ultimate weapon mo ay Berocca, Vicks, at ang mainit na sabaw ni nanay.
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang parirala sa mga kontekstong pangkalusugan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang tamang nutrisyon ay mahalaga sa **laban sa sakit**.","translation":"Proper nutrition is important in the **fight against sickness**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagsisiksikan o pag-ipit sa isang masikip na espasyo upang makasingit o makakuha ng puwesto.
original_explanation: That feeling sa MRT pag rush hour, 'yung kailangan mong maging sardinas para lang makasakay. You have to **paggitgit** your way in. It's the physical version of 'pa-insert po sa group chat.'
usage_notes: Often used to describe crowded situations like public transport, concerts, or lines where people are pushing to get ahead.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **paggitgit** ng mga tao sa pila ay nagdulot ng gulo.","translation":"The **jostling** of people in the line caused chaos."},{"sentence":"Nahirapan siyang makapasok dahil sa **paggitgit** sa pinto ng tren.","translation":"He had a hard time getting in because of the **squeezing in** at the train door."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagpapakita ng katangiang hindi matatag o palaging nag-iiba, partikular sa desisyon, damdamin, o kalagayan.
original_explanation: Describes your 'situationship' status, the weather in Manila, the price of gasoline, or your friend who can't decide where to eat. One minute it's this, the next it's that. It's the official mood of anyone stuck in EDSA traffic.
usage_notes: Often used to describe something or someone's disposition as being inconsistent. The reduplication of 'bago' emphasizes the repetitive or continuous nature of the change.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap magplano kapag **napagbabagu-bago** ang isip ng kasama mo.","translation":"It's hard to make plans when your companion's mind is so **fickle**."},{"sentence":"Talagang **napagbabagu-bago** ang panahon ngayon, kanina'y maaraw, ngayon ay umuulan.","translation":"The weather is really **erratic** today; it was sunny a while ago, now it's raining."}]

meaning_filipino: Napakaliit, napakanipis, o napakapino na katulad ng isang hibla ng buhok.
etymology: From 'buhok' (hair) with the prefix 'mala-' (like/similar to). Literally 'hair-like.'
original_explanation: Yung pasensya mo sa Monday morning traffic, **malabuhok** na lang. Or yung pag-asa mong magre-reply si crush. It's something so thin and fine, like a single strand of hair. It can describe a crack, a thread, or your chances of winning the lottery.
usage_notes: Used to emphasize extreme thinness or fineness.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **malabuhok** na sinulid lamang ang nagdurugtong sa butones.","translation":"Only a **hair-like** thread was connecting the button."},{"sentence":"Nakita niya ang isang **malabuhok** na lamat sa salamin.","translation":"She saw a **very fine** crack in the mirror."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglikha o paglabas ng bula, karaniwan mula sa sabon at tubig o sa likidong kumukulo.
original_explanation: The action of soap when you mix it with water and rub it. It's also what happens to your mouth when you're so mad at your Mobile Legends teammate, 'nagbubula na sa galit' (frothing in anger).
usage_notes: Can also be used figuratively to mean "to froth at the mouth" in anger.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magbula** nang husto ng shampoo sa iyong buhok.","translation":"You need to **lather** the shampoo well in your hair."},{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **magbula** ang kumukulong sabaw.","translation":"The boiling soup started to **foam**."}]

translation: to mock; to scorn; to belittle
meaning_filipino: Ang paghamak, paglibak, o pagmamaliit sa isang tao sa pamamagitan ng salita o gawa.
etymology: Possibly related to 'hayop' (animal), implying treating someone like an animal.
original_explanation: The act of being a verbal bully or a savage keyboard warrior. When you ayupin someone, you're not just disagreeing, you're actively putting them down, making them feel small. It's what happens in toxic comment sections or family reunions when a tita comments on your weight. It's shade, but with more bite.
usage_notes: A strong, negative word. Not commonly used in casual conversation but appears in more formal or literary contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Masakit marinig na **ayupin** ka ng sarili mong kaibigan.","translation":"It's painful to hear your own friend **mock** you."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **ayupin** ang kanyang kakayahan dahil lang sa kanyang itsura.","translation":"Don't **belittle** his abilities just because of his appearance."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa paraan ng pagluto, lalo na ng itlog, kung saan ito ay hindi lubos na luto at ang pula ay nananatiling malambot o bahagyang likido.
etymology: Possible borrowing from Spanish 'mal asado' (badly roasted/cooked), adapted into Tagalog to mean half-cooked. The direct root in Tagalog is 'lagata'.
original_explanation: How do you like your eggs? If your answer is 'runny yolk, firm whites,' then you want it **malagata**. It's the perfect state for dipping your pandesal. It's the 'in-between' of cooking—not raw, not well-done. Parang 'almost lover' sa status ninyo, hindi pa fully cooked ang relationship.
usage_notes: Primarily used for eggs. The Spanish-derived term 'malasado' is a common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko ng itlog na **malagata** para sa almusal.","translation":"I want a **soft-boiled** egg for breakfast."},{"sentence":"Mas masarap isawsaw ang pandesal sa itlog na **malagata**.","translation":"It's more delicious to dip bread in a **half-cooked** egg."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, pangkat, o puwersa na pumipigil, sumusugpo, o nagpapatahimik sa kalayaan, karapatan, o pag-unlad ng iba sa pamamagitan ng lakas o kapangyarihan.
etymology: Nagmula sa "man-" + pag-uulit ng unang pantig ng ugat ("su-") + "supil" (sugpuin/pasukuin).
original_explanation: The ultimate kontrabida in a historical drama or a political rally. This is the entity—be it a person, a government, or a system—that says "You can't do that!" and has the power to back it up. Think of a micromanager boss, but on a national or historical scale.
usage_notes: Isang pormal at mabigat na salita, madalas gamitin sa mga kontekstong pampulitika o pangkasaysayan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga bayani ay lumaban sa mga **manunupil** na dayuhan.","translation":"The heroes fought against the foreign **oppressors**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng pagiging likas na mapagmahal, mabait, at palakaibigan.
original_explanation: This is a slightly more intense or inherent version of 'magiliw'. If 'magiliw' is how a Jollibee crew acts, 'magiliwin' is the Golden Retriever of people. It's not just an act, it's their whole personality. They're just naturally sweet and friendly.
usage_notes: While very similar to 'magiliw', 'magiliwin' emphasizes the inherent nature or tendency of a person to be affectionate. It's less about a single action and more about a core personality trait.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Talagang **magiliwin** ang mga Pilipino sa mga dayuhan.","translation":"Filipinos are truly **affectionate** towards foreigners."},{"sentence":"May pagka-**magiliwin** siyang pusa, laging gustong magpakarga.","translation":"He is a rather **affectionate** cat, always wanting to be carried."}]

translation: to tire oneself out; to work very hard
meaning_filipino: Sadyain ang pagbuhos ng matinding pagsisikap sa isang gawain hanggang sa maramdaman ang kapaguran.
etymology: From the prefix `magpaka-` (to deliberately cause oneself to be) and the root `pagod` (tired).
original_explanation: This is what you do when you're trying to prove a point. "O, ayan, nagpakapagod ako maglinis ng buong bahay, sana naman mapansin niyo!" It's the art of getting tired on purpose, either for a noble cause (like for your family) or just to be petty.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi mo kailangang **magpakapagod** para sa mga taong hindi ka pinapahalagahan.","translation":"You don't have to **tire yourself out** for people who don't value you."},{"sentence":"Nagpakapagod siya sa pag-eensayo para manalo sa kumpetisyon.","translation":"He **worked very hard** in training to win the competition."}]

meaning_filipino: Sa paraang may mataas at matalas na anggulo ng pagtaas o pagbaba; napakatarik.
original_explanation: Driving in Baguio or Antipolo be like... That feeling when your Waze takes you through a road that feels like a 90-degree angle and you start praying to all the saints. That's **patirik**. It's the 'OMG, aatras ba tayo?' kind of steep.
usage_notes: Often used to describe roads, mountains, or climbs. Synonymous with 'matarik'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Patirik** ang daan paakyat sa tuktok ng bundok kaya ingat sa pagmamaneho.","translation":"The road going up to the mountain's peak is **steeply** inclined, so drive carefully."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang tunog na nililikha ng sabay-sabay na pagpalo ng mga palad; isang masigabong pagbati.
original_explanation: The sound of success, or at least the sound of the show ending. A loud 'palakpakan' is what every performer, speaker, and even your tita who just finished her karaoke song hopes to hear.
usage_notes: Refers to the collective sound or event of clapping.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig sa buong teatro ang malakas na **palakpakan**.","translation":"A loud **applause** was heard throughout the theater."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang aralin na itinuturo o pinag-aaralan; isang karanasang nagbibigay ng mahalagang kaalaman o babala.
original_explanation: Can be the literal **leksyon** your teacher gives in school. But more importantly, it's what life gives you when you mess up. Nagpautang ka sa kaibigan mong di nagbabayad? **Leksyong** natutunan. Nag-reply ka sa 'hi' ng ex mo? Malaking **leksyon**. It's the Tagalog for 'lesson learned the hard way.'
usage_notes: Can refer to both an academic lesson and a life lesson.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap ang **leksyon** natin sa Math ngayon.","translation":"Our **lesson** in Math today is difficult."},{"sentence":"Sana ay maging **leksyon** ito sa iyo na huwag basta-basta magtiwala.","translation":"I hope this becomes a **lesson** for you not to trust easily."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kamalig o imbakan, karaniwang yari sa kawayan at nipa, na itinatayo nang may mataas na haligi upang paglagyan ng mga inaning butil tulad ng palay.
original_explanation: The OG G-Cash for farmers. Before banks, this was where you stored your wealth—your harvested rice. It’s a stilted hut that’s basically a panic room for palay, designed to keep it safe from floods, pests, and probably chismosas wanting to borrow a cup of rice.
usage_notes: A traditional agricultural term, not common in urban settings. Often raised on posts to protect grains from moisture and rodents.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng palay ang **tambubong** pagkatapos ng anihan.","translation":"The **granary** is full of harvested rice after the harvest."},{"sentence":"Itinayo ang **tambubong** sa gitna ng bukid.","translation":"The **granary** was built in the middle of the field."}]

meaning_filipino: Kanin na iniluto muli sa pamamagitan ng paggisa sa bawang, mantika, at kung minsan ay asin.
original_explanation: The official resurrection of yesterday's rice. `Sinangag` is the star of the -silog breakfast empire (Tapsilog, Longsilog, etc.). It's proof that leftovers can have a glorious second life. That *tutong* (burnt rice at the bottom) isn't a mistake; it's a crunchy, delicious feature. The more garlic, the more power!
usage_notes: Specifically refers to garlic fried rice, a staple of Filipino breakfast.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang almusal ko kanina ay longganisa, itlog, at maraming **sinangag**.","translation":"My breakfast earlier was longganisa, egg, and lots of **garlic fried rice**."},{"sentence":"Gamitin mo yung bahaw sa ref para gumawa ng **sinangag** para bukas.","translation":"Use the leftover rice in the ref to make **garlic fried rice** for tomorrow."}]

translation: to point at someone simultaneously with others
meaning_filipino: Sabay-sabay na ituro o tudlain ang isang tao o bagay, karaniwan sa paraang nagpaparatang.
original_explanation: This is the physical version of getting "called out" by the whole group chat. Imagine everyone in the room suddenly pointing their finger at you because you're the one who ate the last piece of pizza. "Sino umubos ng lechon?" *sabay duruan kay kuya*. It's a group point-out, a physical "J'accuse!" moment.
usage_notes: Often implies accusation or singling someone out by a group.
