translation: to slice into many pieces; to chop; to dice
meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit na paghiwa sa isang bagay upang maging maliliit na piraso.
etymology: From the reduplication of 'hiwa' (slice) + '-in' (object-focus suffix), indicating a repetitive action.
original_explanation: This is what your mom tells you to do to the onions and garlic, making you cry. It's not just slicing, it's slicing repeatedly until you have tiny bits. Think of it as the "chopping" level in a cooking game.
usage_notes: The repetition of "hiwa" implies multiple, often small, cuts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **hiwa-hiwain** nang pino ang mga sibuyas para sa ginisar.","translation":"You need to **finely chop** the onions for the sauté."},{"sentence":"**Hiwa-hiwain** natin ang karne bago ilagay sa adobo.","translation":"Let's **slice the meat into pieces** before putting it in the adobo."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang natatanging katangian o pagkakakilanlan ng isang tao o bagay na nagpapaiba rito sa iba.
etymology: From ka- + kanya (his/hers) + -han. It literally means the quality of 'his/her-ness' or 'its-ness'.
original_explanation: This is your 'personal brand'. It’s what makes you, you. It's your unique mix of personality, quirks, and talents. It's the reason why your friends can say 'That's so you!' It's the deep, philosophical version of 'be yourself.'
usage_notes: A formal and profound word used in discussions about identity, culture, and personality.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahalagang panatilihin ang ating **kakanyahan** bilang isang bansa.","translation":"It is important to maintain our **identity** as a nation."},{"sentence":"Ang bawat tao ay may sariling **kakanyahan** na dapat igalang.","translation":"Every person has their own **individuality** that must be respected."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sining, aplikasyon, at kasanayan sa paglikha ng mga imahe sa pamamagitan ng pagrekord ng liwanag, maging sa paraang elektroniko sa pamamagitan ng sensor ng imahe, o kemikal sa pamamagitan ng materyal na sensitibo sa liwanag.
original_explanation: The art of making your friends look good for their profile pics and making your food look 10x more delicious for Instagram. It's the reason why everyone with a DSLR or a new iPhone suddenly calls themselves a "photographer." From capturing epic travel moments to taking a hundred selfies to find the perfect one, that's potograpiya in the 21st century.
usage_notes: Ito ang moderno at karaniwang baybay para sa "photography" sa Filipino.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging libangan ko ang **potograpiya** simula nang magka-smartphone ako.","translation":"**Photography** became my hobby since I got a smartphone."},{"sentence":"Mananalo ka sa patimpalak ng **potograpiya** dahil maganda ang kuha mo.","translation":"You will win the **photography** contest because your shot is beautiful."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng baril na gawa sa bahay, karaniwang yari sa mga tubo ng metal, at ginagamit bilang sandata.
original_explanation: The OG Pinoy DIY project for self-defense (or offense). It's the kind of thing you hear about in gritty crime news reports. Think MacGyver, but instead of a paperclip and gum, it's a pipe and some gunpowder. Definitely not something you bring to show-and-tell.
usage_notes: Madalas na iniuugnay sa krimen sa kalye o sa mga impormal na pamayanan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakakumpiska ang mga pulis ng isang **sumpak** sa isinagawang raid.","translation":"The police confiscated an **improvised gun** during the raid."},{"sentence":"Delikadong magmay-ari ng **sumpak** dahil ito ay ilegal at hindi matatag.","translation":"It's dangerous to own an **improvised gun** because it is illegal and unstable."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit na pang-iinis o panggugulo sa isang tao sa maliit ngunit patuloy na paraan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang 'surot' (bedbug), na tumutukoy sa paulit-ulit at nakakainis na katangian ng kagat nito.
original_explanation: Parang yung officemate mong laging nanghihingi ng tissue o yung kaibigan mong panay ang tanong kung kailan ka mag-aasawa. Nakaka-high blood in a low-key way. Sila yung expert sa pang-**surutin**.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin upang ilarawan ang mga maliliit ngunit tuloy-tuloy na panggugulo o pang-aasar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mo akong **surutin** ngayon, masama ang gising ko.","translation":"Don't **pester** me right now, I woke up on the wrong side of the bed."},{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **surutin** ang kapatid niyang bunso.","translation":"He likes to **annoy** his youngest sibling."}]

translation: to put up or install curtains
meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay o pagkakabit ng kurtina sa bintana, pinto, o anumang bukasan.
original_explanation: The verb that signals you're officially "tita-fying" or "adulting". When you spend a weekend choosing, washing, and hanging up new drapes, you're not just decorating, you're 'nagkukurtina'. It's also the action you do at night to tell the chismosa neighbor, "The show is over."
usage_notes: A very direct and literal verb.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tulungan mo akong **magkurtina** sa sala bago dumating ang mga bisita.","translation":"Help me **put up the curtains** in the living room before the guests arrive."},{"sentence":"Oras na para **magkurtina** dahil tirik na ang araw.","translation":"It's time to **draw the curtains** because the sun is glaring."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapatirapa o pagyukod nang lubos bilang tanda ng matinding paggalang, pagsamba, o pagsuko.
original_explanation: This is a very dramatic bow. It's not just a nod. It's the 'we're not worthy!' bow you do to your K-Pop idol, or what you feel like doing to the one person who approves your vacation leave. It’s an act of deep respect or surrender.
usage_notes: A formal and somewhat archaic word. Often found in religious or historical texts. More intense than 'yumuko'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga alagad ay **yumukdo** sa harap ng kanilang pinuno.","translation":"The followers **bowed down** before their leader."},{"sentence":"Sa sobrang pagod, para siyang **yumukdo** sa sahig.","translation":"From extreme exhaustion, it was as if he **prostrated** on the floor."}]

translation: To coax; to wheedle; to cajole
meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng matatamis na salita o papuri upang himukin o hikayatin ang isang tao na gawin ang isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the 'sipsip' move you pull on your boss for a promotion, or when you sweet-talk your friend into treating you to milk tea. It's the art of persuasion, but with extra sugar coating. 'Uy, ang galing mo talaga! Pautang naman...'
usage_notes: Often implies a slightly manipulative but generally harmless form of persuasion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **mang-ulok** ng mga botante sa pamamagitan ng mga imposibleng pangako.","translation":"He tried to **cajole** the voters with impossible promises."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpadala sa mga taong sinusubukang **mang-ulok** sa iyo para sa kanilang sariling kapakanan.","translation":"Don't be swayed by people who try to **wheedle** you for their own benefit."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang kagamitan o kasangkapan na ginagamit sa pakikipaglaban, pag-atake, o pagtatanggol sa sarili.
original_explanation: Can be a literal weapon like a knife or gun. But in the modern world, your best 'sandata' could be your diploma, your skills, or your sharp tongue for office politics and marites battles. 'Edukasyon ang aking sandata sa kahirapan.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagbabawal ang pagdadala ng anumang **sandata** sa loob ng gusali.","translation":"Bringing any kind of **weapon** inside the building is prohibited."},{"sentence":"Ang kaalaman ay isang mabisang **sandata** laban sa kasinungalingan.","translation":"Knowledge is an effective **weapon** against lies."}]

translation: to defile one's honor; to rape; to dishonor
meaning_filipino: Isang idyomatikong ekspresyon na nangangahulugang pagsira sa karangalan o kabanalan ng isang tao, lalo na ng isang babae, sa pamamagitan ng sekswal na pang-aabuso.
etymology: Kumbinasyon ng pandiwang "ilugso" (mula sa "lugso", pagguho) at pangngalang "puri" (karangalan, kalinisan).
original_explanation: This is a very heavy and formal phrase, straight out of a classic Filipino movie or a historical drama. It means to violate someone's honor, specifically in a sexual manner (to rape). 'Puri' means honor or chastity, and 'ilugso' means to cause to collapse or crumble. So literally, 'to make one's honor crumble.' You won't hear this in everyday chismisan; it's reserved for very serious, often legal or literary, contexts.
usage_notes: Isang napakaseryoso at pormal na parirala na may malalim na kultural na konotasyon. Madalas itong gamitin sa panitikan, pelikula, at pormal na diskurso tungkol sa krimen.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kontrabida sa nobela ay nagtangkang **ilugso ang puri** ng dalaga.","translation":"The villain in the novel attempted **to defile the honor** of the maiden."}]

translation: to make someone blink; to dazzle
meaning_filipino: Maging sanhi ng mabilis o sunud-sunod na pagpikit at pagdilat ng mga mata ng isang tao, karaniwan dahil sa matinding liwanag, alikabok, o biglaang paggalaw.
original_explanation: Ever had a friend shine their phone's flashlight directly in your face? 'Pinakurap' ka nila. It's the verb for what a bright light, a cloud of dust, or even a stunningly beautiful person does to your eyes—makes them blink uncontrollably. 'Grabe ang ganda niya, napapakurap ako!'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong itutok ang ilaw sa mata ko, baka mo ako **pakurapin**.","translation":"Don't point the light at my eyes, you might **make me blink**."},{"sentence":"Ang alikabok mula sa kalsada ay kayang **pakurapin** ang sinumang dumaan.","translation":"The dust from the road can **make** anyone who passes by **blink**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng kabinet o aparador na may mga kahon at salamin, karaniwang ginagamit sa silid-tulugan para paglagyan ng damit at mga personal na kagamitan.
original_explanation: That big piece of furniture in your lola's room that smells like mothballs and holds a million secrets, plus your baptismal clothes. It's the OG 'get ready with me' station, complete with a giant, slightly-cloudy mirror.
usage_notes: Often found in older houses. Modern equivalents are often just called 'dresser' or 'cabinet'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakatago sa ilalim ng **tukador** ang mga lumang litrato ng aming pamilya.","translation":"The old family photos are hidden under the **dresser**."},{"sentence":"Ayusin mo ang mga damit sa loob ng **tukador**.","translation":"Arrange the clothes inside the **dresser**."}]

meaning_filipino: (Pang-uri) Pinakamaliit sa lahat. (Pangalan) Ang katangian o kalagayan ng pagiging maliit.
etymology: From 'ka-' + 'liit' + '-an', a form often used for superlatives or abstract nouns.
original_explanation: This is the 'bunso' of the group, the smol one. As an adjective, it means the absolute smallest, no questions asked. As a noun, it's the very essence of being small, like the 'kaliitan' of your sahod after all the bills are paid. It's the opposite of "Sana all malaki."
usage_notes: Can function as a superlative adjective ('the smallest') or a noun ('smallness'). When referring to siblings, it often implies 'youngest'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **kaliitan** sa aming magkakapatid.","translation":"She is the **smallest** (youngest) among us siblings."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong maliitin ang sinuman dahil sa kanyang **kaliitan**.","translation":"Do not belittle anyone because of his/her **smallness**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na sapat lamang upang mapanatili ang buhay o makaraos sa pang-araw-araw na pangangailangan; gamit sa kritikal na sitwasyon upang iligtas ang buhay.
etymology: Mula sa "pang-" (para sa) + "agaw" + "buhay", na literal na nangangahulugang "para sa pag-agaw ng buhay" (mula sa kamatayan).
original_explanation: This is the 'kapit sa patalim' mode. It's the instant noodles at the end of the month before payday. It's that 'raket' or sideline you take just to make ends meet. It's the first aid you give to someone while waiting for the ambulance. It's the bare minimum to keep things going.
usage_notes: Maaaring mangahulugang "nakapagliligtas-buhay" sa medikal na aspeto, o "pantawid-gutom" sa ekonomikong aspeto. Ang konteksto ay mahalaga.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang maliit niyang sahod ay **pang-agaw-buhay** lamang sa kanyang pamilya.","translation":"His small salary is **barely enough for his family to survive** on."},{"sentence":"Ang kaalaman sa first aid ay mahalaga bilang **pang-agaw-buhay** sa oras ng sakuna.","translation":"Knowledge of first aid is important as a **life-saving** measure during accidents."}]

meaning_filipino: Puno ng usok; may maraming usok na nagmumula sa isang bagay.
etymology: From 'usok' (smoke). The 'ma-' prefix means 'full of' or 'characterized by'.
original_explanation: The vibe of a provincial kitchen with a wood-fire stove, a classic Pinoy ihawan session, or EDSA during rush hour. It's when the air is thicker than your lola's hot chocolate. Can be good (barbecue!) or bad (secondhand smoke, pollution). The perfect adjective for that one friend's car that looks like it's trying to send smoke signals.
usage_notes: Can describe a place (e.g., 'mausok na kwarto' - a smoky room) or a thing (e.g., 'mausok na tambutso' - a smoky exhaust pipe).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Lumabas ka muna, sobrang **mausok** dito sa loob ng kusina.","translation":"Go outside for a bit, it's very **smoky** here inside the kitchen."},{"sentence":"Ipinagbawal ang mga **mausok** na sasakyan sa lungsod.","translation":"**Smoky** (smoke-belching) vehicles were banned in the city."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bakod o kulungan para sa mga alagang hayop tulad ng baka, kabayo, o baboy.
original_explanation: The original parking lot for farm animals. It's where you keep the future lechon or the kabayo for the next kalesa ride. Think of it as a gated community for livestock.
usage_notes: Karaniwang binabaybay na "kural" sa makabagong Filipino upang maiwasan ang kalituhan sa "koral" (coral) na mula sa dagat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipasok mo ang mga baka sa **koral** bago dumilim.","translation":"Put the cows inside the **corral** before it gets dark."},{"sentence":"Nililinis ni Mang Tonio ang **koral** ng kanyang mga baboy.","translation":"Mang Tonio is cleaning his pig **pen**."}]

translation: act of ignoring; giving the silent treatment; apathy
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng hindi pagpansin, pagwawalang-bahala, o pananahimik sa isang bagay na karaniwang nangangailangan ng tugon o aksyon.
original_explanation: This is the ultimate Pinoy passive-aggressive move. When your mom gives you the silent treatment after you come home late, that's pagsasawalang-kibo. It's ignoring a problem, a person, or a political issue, hoping it goes away. The national sport of 'bahala na' and 'dedma.'
usage_notes: A compound word that signifies a deliberate choice to be silent or inactive. It can imply indifference, disapproval, or strategic silence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang **pagsasawalang-kibo** sa isyu ay binatikos ng marami.","translation":"His **act of ignoring** the issue was criticized by many."}]

translation: to join; to connect; to attach
meaning_filipino: Pagdugtungin o pagkabitin ang dalawa o higit pang bagay, ideya, o bahagi upang maging isang buo.
original_explanation: It's like connecting two LEGO pieces, joining two water pipes, or what you do when the WiFi extender needs to be linked to the main router. It's about making things meet and become one. Can also be used for ideas, like trying to **ihugpong** two unrelated concepts to make a point during a presentation.
usage_notes: Often used for physically joining things end-to-end. 'Idugtong' is a more common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **ihugpong** ang dalawang putol na kawayan.","translation":"He tried to **join** the two broken bamboo pieces."},{"sentence":"Mahirap **ihugpong** ang lumang istorya sa bagong kabanata ng nobela.","translation":"It's difficult to **connect** the old story to the new chapter of the novel."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking singsing o bilog na metal, kahoy, o iba pang materyales, na karaniwang ginagamit bilang hawakan, palamuti, o sa mga laro.
original_explanation: Think of those giant rings gymnasts use, or the hoop in basketball, but make it old-school Tagalog. It's also that big, round handle on an old baul (treasure chest) or a carabao's nose ring. Not to be confused with your bling-bling singsing.
usage_notes: Can refer to various types of rings or hoops, from door knockers to curtain rings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isinabit niya ang kurtina sa mga **argolya**.","translation":"She hung the curtain on the **rings**."},{"sentence":"Ang **argolya** sa ilong ng kalabaw ay ginagamit para gabayan ito.","translation":"The **ring** in the carabao's nose is used to guide it."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpapahinto sa isang tao upang tanungin, sawayin, o bigyan ng babala, karaniwang ginagawa ng may awtoridad.
original_explanation: That moment when the guard at the mall entrance stops you, 'Sir, excuse me po, saan po ang face shield ninyo?' even though it's 2026. Or when your team lead messages you 'pa-check ng email ko' right after you log in late. It's a gentle but firm 'Hey, you!'
usage_notes: Can range from a gentle call-out to a formal reprimand.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa **pagsita** ng guro, natahimik ang mag-aaral.","translation":"Because of the teacher's **reprimand**, the student became quiet."},{"sentence":"Hindi niya inasahan ang biglaang **pagsita** ng pulis.","translation":"He did not expect the sudden **accosting** by the police."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paraan ng paghiling na maisakay o makisabay sa isang sasakyan.
original_explanation: Ito yung state of being mo kapag nakatayo ka sa kalsada, kumakaway sa mga jeep o kaibigang may kotse, at umaasang may magpapatigil para sa'yo. Para kang nag-aapply for a temporary slot sa sasakyan nila. "Boss, pasakay hanggang kanto!"
usage_notes: Used to make a request. Often said directly to the driver or a friend. Can also function as a noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sumigaw siya ng '**pasakay** po!' sa paparating na jeep.","translation":"She shouted '**can I get a ride**!' at the approaching jeepney."},{"sentence":"Nakita ko si Ana na naghihintay ng **pasakay** sa tapat ng opisina.","translation":"I saw Ana waiting to **get a ride** in front of the office."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malawak na lugar o lupain na tinutubuan ng maraming damo.
etymology: From "damo" (grass) + "-han" (suffix indicating a place where something abounds).
original_explanation: Your front yard, the park where you have picnics, or that empty lot next door that's overgrown with talahib. Basically, any place that's more grass than soil. "Huwag ka diyan sa semento, doon tayo sa **damuhan** maglatag ng banig." Perfect for chilling, basta walang red ants.
usage_notes: Can refer to a manicured lawn or a wild, grassy field. 'Kaparangan' is a synonym for a wider, more open field or meadow.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naglalaro ang mga bata sa malawak na **damuhan**.","translation":"The children are playing on the wide **lawn**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nang gupitin ang damo sa **damuhan** sa harap ng bahay.","translation":"The grass on the **lawn** in front of the house needs to be cut."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagdakip at pagpigil sa isang tao sa pamamagitan ng legal na kapangyarihan o utos ng hukuman.
original_explanation: When the pulis finally catches up to you for downloading pirated movies. It's the "Huli ka, balbon!" moment but with handcuffs. Also, what your mom threatens you with when you stay out too late: "Umuwi ka na kundi ipapa-aresto kita!"
usage_notes: Often used in the context of law enforcement and crime. The verb form is 'arestuhin'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May utos ng **aresto** laban sa suspek.","translation":"There is an arrest warrant for the suspect."},{"sentence":"Ang paglabag sa curfew ay maaaring magresulta sa **aresto**.","translation":"Violating the curfew can result in an **arrest**."}]

meaning_filipino: Lumagpas na sa itinakdang panahon o petsa para sa pagbabayad, pagpasa, o pagtupad sa isang obligasyon.
etymology: Isang idyomatikong parirala na binubuo ng 'lampas' (beyond) at 'taning' (term/deadline).
original_explanation: The status of your Meralco bill, your project submission, or that book you borrowed from a friend two years ago. This phrase gives every student and employee a mini heart attack. 'Bes, lampas sa taning na 'yung utang mo sa'kin. Singilin na ba kita via Gcash?'
usage_notes: This is an idiomatic phrase. 'Taning' means a set period or deadline.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May multa na ang bayarin mo dahil **lampas sa taning** na.","translation":"Your bill already has a penalty because it's **past the deadline**."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang maging **lampas sa taning** ang pag-amin mo sa kanya.","translation":"Don't let your confession to him/her become **overdue**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagganap sa isang tungkulin, gawain, o layunin; ang pagbibigay ng serbisyo o paglilingkod.
etymology: From 'mag-' (actor-focus verb prefix) + 'silbi' (service, use, function), from Spanish 'servir'.
original_explanation: This can mean "to serve" as in a waiter serving food, but it's more often used in a deeper sense, like "to serve the country" (**magsilbi** sa bayan). It can also mean "to function as," like when your plastic chair suddenly has to **magsilbi** as a ladder. Resourcefulness 101.
usage_notes: Has a wide range of use from formal service (public service) to informal utility (serving a purpose).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang **magsilbi** sa gobyerno bilang isang tapat na opisyal.","translation":"It is his dream **to serve** in the government as an honest official."},{"sentence":"Ang lumang kahon ay maaaring **magsilbi** bilang imbakan ng mga laruan.","translation":"The old box can **function as** storage for toys."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng aparador o kabinet na may salamin sa harap, karaniwang ginagamit upang itanghal ang mga babasagin, porselana, o kristal na kagamitan.
original_explanation: That fancy glass cabinet in your lola's house that you're not allowed to touch. It holds the 'special occasion' plates and glasses that are only used when the Pope visits. It's the museum of the dining room.
usage_notes: Often used to refer to a specific type of china cabinet or display case for fragile items.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maingat na inilagay ni Nanay ang mga bagong baso sa **kristaleria**.","translation":"Mother carefully placed the new glasses in the **glassware cabinet**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng pagkaing kalye na gawa sa giniling na isda, hinulma nang pabilog, pinirito, at karaniwang isinasawsaw sa matamis, maanghang, o maasim na sarsa.
original_explanation: The OG street food that fuels students, BPO agents, and everyone in between. Its true power lies in the 'sawsawan'—sweet, spicy, or a mix. The ultimate test of friendship is sharing the last stick or double-dipping. Don't be that person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pabili po ng sampung pisong **fishball**.","translation":"I'd like to buy ten pesos worth of **fishball**."},{"sentence":"Yung **fishball** sauce talaga ang nagpapasarap dito.","translation":"The **fishball** sauce is what really makes it delicious."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao o grupo ng mga tao na nagnanakaw o gumagawa ng karahasan sa dagat, karaniwang mula sa isang barko.
original_explanation: Basically, the OG 'holdupper' of the high seas. Before there were scammers on social media, there were these guys with scary flags and a love for treasure chests. Think Jack Sparrow, but probably with less eyeliner and more 'tabo' for bailing water.
usage_notes: The root word 'tulisan' means bandit or outlaw.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kwento ng mga **tulisang-dagat** ay sikat sa mga lumang pelikula.","translation":"The story of **pirates** is popular in old movies."},{"sentence":"Natakot ang mga mangingisda dahil sa balitang may mga **tulisang-dagat** sa kanilang lugar.","translation":"The fishermen were scared because of news about **pirates** in their area."}]

translation: an allusion; an indirect remark or hint
meaning_filipino: Isang salita, pangungusap, o gawaing nagpapahiwatig ng isang bagay na hindi tuwirang sinasabi; isang patama o pasaring.
etymology: Nagmula sa "pa-dinig", kung saan ang /d/ ay nagiging /r/ kapag nasa pagitan ng dalawang patinig.
original_explanation: This is a less common spelling of 'parinig'. It's the act of throwing shade, Filipino style. Ito 'yung "Sana all..." post mo na may specific na taong pinatatamaan. It's a high-art form of communication where you say everything by saying nothing directly.
usage_notes: Ang "parinig" ang mas karaniwan at pamantayang baybay. Ito ay isang baryasyon lamang.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puno ng **paringig** ang mga sinabi niya kanina sa miting.","translation":"What he said earlier in the meeting was full of **indirect remarks**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagtatamo ng tagumpay, karaniwan sa pamamagitan ng pagsisikap, abilidad, at determinasyon.
etymology: From English "achiever." Widely adopted into Filipino, especially in academic and professional contexts.
original_explanation: That classmate who was president of every club, had perfect attendance, and still had time to tutor you in Math. In the office, they're the "Bida ang Saya" employee who always hits their KPIs and volunteers for extra work. They're the reason your parents would ask, "Bakit si [Achiever's Name], kaya niya? Ikaw, hindi?" (Why can [Achiever's Name] do it? But you can't?). They're basically walking, talking LinkedIn profiles.
usage_notes: Often used to describe students with high grades or employees with excellent performance. Can sometimes have a slightly negative connotation of being overly ambitious or a teacher's pet.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Laging top 1 sa klase si Maria, isa siyang tunay na **achiever**.","translation":"Maria is always top 1 in class, she's a true **achiever**."},{"sentence":"Puro **achiever** ang mga anak ni Aling Susan.","translation":"All of Aling Susan's children are **achievers**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging kalat-kalat, hindi maayos, o watak-watak.
original_explanation: Your hair after a motorcycle ride without a helmet. Your thoughts during a really hard exam. Your things all over the room when your mom suddenly says 'may bisita!' This word perfectly describes a state of chaotic distribution. It's the physical version of the 'This is fine' meme where everything is on fire.
usage_notes: Describes a state of disarray. Can refer to physical objects, hair, or even abstract things like thoughts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sabug-sabog** ang mga gamit niya sa sahig pagkatapos ng lindol.","translation":"His things were **scattered** all over the floor after the earthquake."},{"sentence":"Galing ka ba sa laban? **Sabug-sabog** ang buhok mo!","translation":"Did you come from a fight? Your hair is **disheveled**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang mataas at patulis na seremonyal na takip sa ulo na isinusuot ng mga obispo at ilang mga abad sa tradisyonal na Kristiyanismo.
original_explanation: That tall, pointy hat a bishop wears during a big mass. It's the ultimate "I'm the boss" accessory in the Catholic Church. It looks a bit like a fish head, which is kind of a religious inside joke if you think about it.
usage_notes: Exclusively used in a religious, specifically Catholic, context to refer to a bishop's headdress.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isinuot ng arsobispo ang kanyang gintong **mitra** para sa espesyal na misa.","translation":"The archbishop wore his golden **miter** for the special mass."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paraan ng paghahati-hati ng isang salita sa mga bahagi o yunit ng tunog na tinatawag na pantig.
etymology: From the root 'pantig' (syllable), with the 'pagkaka-' prefix to denote the method or system of something, in this case, syllabication.
original_explanation: Flashback to your Grade 1 Filipino class. This is how you chop up words to pronounce them correctly, like 'Ma-gan-da.' It's the fundamental building block of speaking, and the reason you sometimes clap your hands while learning a new, long Tagalog word.
usage_notes: A linguistic term used in phonology and education.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Itinuro ng guro ang tamang **pagkakapantig** ng mga mahihirap na salita.","translation":"The teacher taught the correct **syllabication** of the difficult words."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagkakapantig** ng salitang 'pamahalaan' ay pa-ma-ha-la-an.","translation":"The **division into syllables** of the word 'pamahalaan' is pa-ma-ha-la-an."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kasalukuyang ginagawang kilos ng paglilinis gamit ang tubig. Ito ang pangkasalukuyang anyo ng pandiwang "maghugas".
original_explanation: That moment your mom calls you and you're in the middle of a game. "Ano'ng ginagawa mo?" you shout back, "**Naghuhugas** po ng pinggan!" even if you're just about to start. It's the sound of responsibility (or pretending to be responsible).
usage_notes: Present progressive tense of 'maghugas'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang laging **naghuhugas** ng aming mga pinagkainan.","translation":"He/She is always the one **washing** our dishes."},{"sentence":"Ma, **naghuhugas** pa po ako ng kamay, saglit lang.","translation":"Mom, I'm still **washing** my hands, just a moment."}]

translation: to argue with; to dispute with each other
meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapalitan ng magkasalungat na opinyon o pananaw sa isang tao; pagdedebate o pagtatalo nang masidhi.
etymology: From maki- (social prefix) + pag- (action prefix) + reduplication of the first syllable of the root tutol (objection) + -an (social suffix).
original_explanation: Ito yung nangyayari sa comment section ng Facebook. Endless 'debate' na nauuwi sa personalan. Sa pamilya, ito yung hindi kayo magkasundo kung anong channel ang papanoorin. It's arguing, but with a 'reciprocal' vibe, like you're both really into the fight.
usage_notes: Implies a reciprocal argument or a mutual act of opposing each other's points. More intense than 'makipagtalo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw kong **makipagtutulan** sa iyo tungkol sa pulitika.","translation":"I don't want to **argue with** you about politics."},{"sentence":"Madalas silang **makipagtutulan** kahit sa maliliit na bagay.","translation":"They often **dispute with each other** even over small things."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpapakulo ng isang bagay sa tubig hanggang sa ito ay maluto o lumambot. Ito ang anyong pangnagdaan ng pandiwang 'lagain'.
original_explanation: The action version. This is what you did to the eggs for breakfast, the kamote for merienda, or the beef until it's fall-off-the-bone tender. It's the simplest cooking method: just add water and heat.
usage_notes: As a verb, this is the past tense of 'to boil something'. It is a synonym of 'pinakuluan'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nilaga** niya ang mais sa loob ng dalawampung minuto.","translation":"She **boiled** the corn for twenty minutes."},{"sentence":"Sapat na ba ang lambot ng karneng **nilaga**?","translation":"Is the meat that was **boiled** tender enough?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na mahilig o magaling sa isport. Tumutukoy din sa isang taong nagpapakita ng patas na paglalaro at magandang asal sa kompetisyon, manalo man o matalo.
original_explanation: Not just the athlete (atleta), but the one who plays fair. 'Yung hindi pikon pag natalo. He's the guy who shakes hands after the game, even if he got dunked on. Siya rin 'yung nag-aabot ng tubig sa kalaban na na-cramps. The opposite of the player who calls a foul on every possession.
usage_notes: Ang baybay na 'isportman' ay isang hindi gaanong karaniwang variant. Ang 'isportsman' ay mas malawak na ginagamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dapat maging isang mabuting **isportsman** ang bawat manlalaro.","translation":"Every player should be a good **sportsman**."},{"sentence":"Ipinakita niya ang pagiging tunay na **isportsman** nang tulungan niya ang kalabang natumba.","translation":"He showed true **sportsmanship** when he helped the opponent who fell."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang makalumang katawagan para sa isang bagong dating na mandarayuhang Tsino sa Pilipinas.
etymology: Mula sa Hokkien na 新客 (sin-kheh), na nangangahulugang 'bagong panauhin'.
original_explanation: An old-school term from your lola's history books. A **singki** was a "new guest" from China trying to start a new life here. Think of them as the OG entrepreneurs, setting up sari-sari stores and building futures from scratch. The term itself comes from Hokkien "sin-kheh" (新客).
usage_notes: Ito ay isang makasaysayang termino at bihirang gamitin sa modernong pag-uusap. Maaaring ituring na lipas na.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **singki** ang nanirahan sa Binondo noong panahon ng mga Kastila.","translation":"Many **new Chinese immigrants** settled in Binondo during the Spanish era."}]

translation: to cause someone to get tired of or fed up with something
meaning_filipino: Ang pagdudulot sa isang tao ng pagkasuya o pagkaumay sa isang bagay dahil sa labis na pagbibigay o pag-uulit nito.
original_explanation: This is what happens when your favorite song becomes your alarm clock sound. At first, it's great. After a month, you hate it. The song didn't change, but you were overexposed. You can also do this to people. Keep giving someone their favorite food every single day, and eventually, you'll "magpasawa" them. It's the act of turning a 'want' into an 'ugh, not again' through over-saturation.
usage_notes: A causative verb. The subject of the verb is the one causing the feeling of being "sawa" (fed up) in someone else.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong araw-arawin ang pagluto ng adobo, baka **magpasawa** ka sa pamilya mo.","translation":"Don't cook adobo every day, you might **cause your family to get fed up** with it."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit at mapilit na paghingi o pagtatanong tungkol sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: This is the 'kulit' level-up. It's that telemarketer who won't take 'no' for an answer, or your friend who keeps asking "Are we there yet?" every five minutes. It's insisting on something with the energy of a kid demanding a toy in the middle of SM.
usage_notes: Carries a slightly negative connotation of being annoying or bothersome.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **mag-ukilkil** sa kanya dahil abala siya ngayon.","translation":"Don't **pester** him because he is busy right now."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong **mag-ukilkil** sa HR para makuha ang aking backpay.","translation":"I have to **persistently follow up** with HR to get my backpay."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagbabago-bago ang ugali o damdamin nang walang malinaw na dahilan; hindi palagian o pabigla-bigla.
etymology: From `pa-` + reduplication of `sumpong` (tantrum, whim, mood swing).
original_explanation: This is your friend who says "Game!" to a beach trip, then cancels an hour before because they "don't feel like it." It's also the Wi-Fi signal that's super fast one minute and then suddenly dies in the middle of your Zoom presentation. It's the emotional rollercoaster of being "seen-zoned." Moody, unpredictable, inconsistent.
usage_notes: Often used to describe a person's mood, a machine's performance, or even the weather. The spelling `pasumpung-sumpong` is a common variant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahirap hulaan ang desisyon niya dahil **pasumpong-sumpong** ang ugali niya.","translation":"It's hard to predict his decision because his attitude is **temperamental**."},{"sentence":"Ayoko na sa internet provider na ito, **pasumpong-sumpong** ang koneksyon!","translation":"I don't like this internet provider anymore, the connection is so **erratic**!"}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na pangmatagalan, hindi nagbabago, o mananatili sa loob ng mahabang panahon.
original_explanation: The opposite of your 'thing' with that person you're just 'casually seeing.' It's the Sharpie marker on a white shirt, the tattoo your friend got on a whim, or that coveted 'regular' status at work after months of being a contractual employee. It's supposed to last forever... or at least until you decide to get laser removal.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko na ng isang trabahong **permanente** at hindi laging kontraktuwal.","translation":"I want a **permanent** job and not always be on a contract."},{"sentence":"Ang peklat na iyan ay magiging **permanente** na.","translation":"That scar will now be **permanent**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-usad o paggalaw pauna; pag-unlad o pagbuti ng isang kalagayan.
original_explanation: This is the "forward" button in life. When your boss says, "We need to move this project forward," they mean "isulong." It’s the opposite of "urong." It’s what you do when the traffic light turns green, or when you finally decide to file that leave you've been putting off.
usage_notes: Often used as a root for verbs like 'sumulong' (to advance) and 'isulong' (to push forward an agenda/item).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **sulong** ng teknolohiya ay mabilis.","translation":"The **advance** of technology is fast."},{"sentence":"Mahalaga ang pagkakaisa para sa **sulong** ng bayan.","translation":"Unity is important for the **progress** of the nation."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang miyembro ng pamilya na kumikita ng pera upang suportahan ang buong sambahayan.
original_explanation: The designated 'pambansang bayani' of the Filipino family. Often the eldest child (panganay) or one of the parents, this is the person whose salary magically pays for the bills, the groceries, the tuition of younger siblings, and the pasalubong requests from relatives. Their motto is 'Work lang nang work.'
usage_notes: A very common concept in Filipino family dynamics, often linked to the 'panganay' (eldest child) responsibility.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Bilang panganay, siya ang naging **breadwinner** ng kanilang pamilya.","translation":"As the eldest, she became the **breadwinner** of their family."}]

translation: to become well-behaved; to straighten up
meaning_filipino: Ang pagbabago ng ugali tungo sa pagiging mabuti, maayos, o matuwid.
original_explanation: This is what every Pinoy parent wishes for their pasaway na anak. "Sana naman tumino ka na!" It's to stop being a troublemaker and start acting right. It's the character development arc from being a "sakit sa ulo" to finally having good judgment. It’s when you finally stop making bad life decisions and start adulting properly.
usage_notes: Often used as a command or a hope for someone to improve their behavior or judgment.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Simula nang magkatrabaho siya, medyo **tumino** na ang buhay niya.","translation":"Since he got a job, his life has **straightened up** a bit."},{"sentence":"Kailan ka ba **titino** at mag-aaral nang mabuti?","translation":"When will you ever **become well-behaved** and study properly?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang elementong kemikal na may simbolong 'He' at atomikong bilang na 2. Ito ay isang walang kulay, walang amoy, at walang lasa na noble gas.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol "helio" o Ingles "helium", na hango sa Griyegong "helios" (araw), dahil unang natuklasan ito sa spectrum ng araw.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung dahilan kung bakit lumulutang ang mga lobo sa birthday party at kung bakit nagiging parang chipmunk ang boses mo. 'Yung feeling na sobrang gaan mo after payday? Para kang lobong puno ng helyum.
usage_notes: Ginagamit sa mga lobo, airship, at bilang isang cooling agent sa siyentipikong pananaliksik. Bilang pangalan ng elemento, ito ay isang pangngalang pantangi (proper noun).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinuno ng **Helyum** ang mga lobo para sa kaarawan ng bata.","translation":"The balloons for the child's birthday were filled with **Helium**."}]

translation: to go along with; to happen to be at the same time
meaning_filipino: Hindi sinasadyang makasama sa isang gawain o paglalakbay; maganap sa parehong oras o pagkakataon.
original_explanation: The 'sabit lang' verb. When your friends are going out for milk tea and you just happened to be there, so you get invited. You **napasabay**. Or when you plan to leave the office at 5 PM sharp, but your boss calls a meeting at 4:59 PM, so your uwi **napasabay** sa rush hour traffic. It's the accidental tag-along.
usage_notes: Implies a sense of coincidence or unplanned participation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pauwi na sana ako nang may mag-aya, kaya **napasabay** na lang ako sa kanila.","translation":"I was about to go home when someone invited me out, so I just **went along with** them."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, baka **mapasabay** ka sa susunod na byahe.","translation":"Don't worry, you might **happen to join** the next trip."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit o di-gaanong malubhang pinsala sa balat na dulot ng init, kemikal, o alitan.
original_explanation: That little 'ouch' moment when hot oil from the pritong isda jumps at you. It's not a third-degree, hospital-worthy burn, just a 'first-degree' burn that needs a dab of toothpaste (the Pinoy remedy, but please don't do it!).
usage_notes: 'Bahagya' means slight or minor, and 'paso' means burn.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagtamo siya ng **bahagyang paso** sa kamay dahil sa mainit na kawali.","translation":"She got a **minor burn** on her hand from the hot pan."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang makaramdam ng selos o inggit patungkol sa isang tao o bagay; gawing dahilan ng selos ang isang tao o bagay.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of that green-eyed monster, 'selos.' It's when you see your partner liking someone else's photos and you feel that pang. 'Bakit mo pinagseselosan 'yung work friend ko?' (Why are you getting jealous of my work friend?) It's the action of directing your jealousy towards a specific target.
usage_notes: An object-focused verb. The object of the verb is the person or thing that is the target of the jealousy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hindi mo dapat **pagselosan** ang tagumpay ng iyong kaibigan.","translation":"You shouldn't **be jealous of** your friend's success."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang elektronikong aparato para sa pagpapatugtog ng tunog na gumagamit ng dalawa o higit pang channel upang lumikha ng impresyon ng tunog na nagmumula sa iba't ibang direksyon.
original_explanation: Your tito's pride and joy back in the 90s. That massive black box with two giant speakers that could shake the whole barangay during family reunions while blasting VST & Co. or Apo Hiking Society. Now it's probably just collecting dust, or you're using its Bluetooth-enabled descendant.
usage_notes: Can also be used as an adjective (e.g., "estereo sound").
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang lakas ng tunog ng **estereo** ng kapitbahay namin tuwing umaga.","translation":"The sound of our neighbor's **stereo** is so loud every morning."},{"sentence":"Bumili si Papa ng bagong **estereo** para sa kotse.","translation":"Dad bought a new **stereo** for the car."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na bahagi ng isang kabuuan o pangkat; isang kasama sa isang organisasyon, departamento, o grupo.
etymology: From the prefix `ka-` (denoting a shared relationship) and `buo` (whole, complete).
original_explanation: This is like your 'work-fam' or 'team-mate'. You might not be best friends, but you're part of the same project, department, or organization. You share the same 'kabuuan' (wholeness) of the group. It’s more formal than 'barkada' but less intimate than 'kapatid'.
usage_notes: Not a very common word in everyday speech, more likely to be found in formal or organizational contexts like memos or official meetings.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga **kabuo** sa aming departamento ay nagtulungan para matapos ang ulat.","translation":"The **colleagues** in our department helped each other to finish the report."},{"sentence":"Siya ay isang mahalagang **kabuo** ng ating samahan.","translation":"She is an important **fellow member** of our organization."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapakita ng labis na lakas, tapang, o gilas sa isang paraan na may kasamang pagyayabang.
original_explanation: This is the OG Filipino 'flex'. Yung bagong-bago ang sapatos, ipapang-apak mo talaga sa putik para mapansin. O yung bodybuilder sa gym na sumisigaw habang nagbubuhat ng mas mabigat pa sa mga problema mo. It's showing off your power or skills, often in a loud, look-at-me way.
usage_notes: Often carries a negative connotation of arrogance or showing off unnecessarily.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Napansin ng lahat ang kanyang **panggigilas** nang buhatin niya ang mabigat na sako.","translation":"Everyone noticed his **show of force** when he lifted the heavy sack."},{"sentence":"Hindi maganda ang labis na **panggigilas** sa harap ng mga kasamahan.","translation":"Excessive **flaunting** in front of colleagues is not good."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pag-aalay ng salita o gawa upang pagaanin ang damdamin, pawiin ang galit, o alisin ang pag-aalala ng isang tao.
etymology: From `magpa-` (causative prefix) and the compound word `lubag-loob` (calmness of inner self), from `lubag` (to subside) and `loob` (inner self, will).
original_explanation: This is the act of damage control. When you forget your anniversary, you need to 'magpalubag-loob' with flowers and a fancy dinner. When your friend is having a 'hugot' moment, you 'magpalubag-loob' with milk tea and a listening ear. It's about calming a storm, whether it's anger, sadness, or disappointment. It's the verbal or physical equivalent of patting someone's back and saying, "There, there."
usage_notes: A causative verb aimed at changing someone's negative emotional state to a more positive or neutral one.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sinubukan niyang **magpalubag-loob** sa kanyang nagtatampong kasintahan.","translation":"He tried **to appease** his sulking girlfriend."},{"sentence":"Isang taos-pusong paghingi ng tawad ang tanging paraan para **magpalubag-loob** sa kanya.","translation":"A sincere apology is the only way **to console** him."}]

translation: to be able to teach; to be able to point
meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng kakayahang magbahagi ng kaalaman o kasanayan sa iba; o ang kakayahang ituro ang direksyon o lokasyon ng isang bagay gamit ang daliri o anumang panuro.
original_explanation: The "maka-" prefix gives this two common meanings. 1) To be able to teach: "Sana makaturo ako sa mga bata sa probinsya balang araw." (I hope to be able to teach kids in the province someday). 2) To be able to point: "Makaturo ka lang kung nasaan ang CR, okay na ako." (Just be able to point where the restroom is, and I'll be fine). The ultimate GPS or mentor verb.
usage_notes: The context usually makes it clear whether it means teaching or pointing.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang malaking biyaya ang **makaturo** sa susunod na henerasyon.","translation":"It is a great blessing **to be able to teach** the next generation."},{"sentence":"Pakiusap, **makaturo** ka ba kung saan ang pinakamalapit na istasyon ng tren?","translation":"Please, can you **point** to where the nearest train station is?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang walang-ingat at labis na paggasta o pag-ubos ng pera, ari-arian, o yaman.
original_explanation: This is what you do with your 13th-month pay on 12.12 sales. It's spending money like you have a money tree in your backyard, only to cry 'sana all may ipon' a week later. To 'lustayin' is to squander resources with the energy of a one-day millionaire.
usage_notes: Almost always has a negative connotation, implying irresponsible spending.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong **lustayin** ang perang pinaghirapan ng iyong mga magulang.","translation":"Do not **squander** the money your parents worked hard for."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay na may pisikal na anyo, maaaring mahawakan, o maging paksa ng pag-iisip; isang kagamitan o entidad.
original_explanation: The ultimate placeholder word when you can't remember the name of something. "Pakikuha nga yung... ano... yung bagay sa ibabaw ng mesa." It's the Filipino equivalent of "thingamajig" or "whatchamacallit."
usage_notes: A very general and versatile noun. Pronunciation is key to differentiate from the adjective form; for the noun, the stress is on the first syllable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang dami mong **bagay** na nakakalat sa kuwarto.","translation":"You have so many **things** scattered in your room."},{"sentence":"Isang mahalagang **bagay** ang natutunan ko ngayon.","translation":"I learned an important **thing** today."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paggamit ng sandata, karaniwan ay yari sa yantok o kahoy, bilang isang sining ng pakikipaglaban o depensa sa sarili, na kilala rin bilang Arnis o Kali.
original_explanation: This is the verb form of our national martial art. Think of action stars like Coco Martin or a classic Lito Lapid movie where they fight with rattan sticks. It's not just whacking each other; it's a whole system. When you 'mag-eskrima', you're either training or in a serious situation that requires you to channel your inner Pinoy warrior.
usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 'mag-arnis'. Eskrima is a specific form of Filipino Martial Arts (FMA).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais niyang matutong **mag-eskrima** para maprotektahan ang kanyang sarili.","translation":"He wants to learn to **practice eskrima** to protect himself."},{"sentence":"Nag-eensayo silang **mag-eskrima** sa gym tuwing Sabado.","translation":"They practice **doing eskrima** at the gym every Saturday."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang taong inuupahan upang mag-alaga ng mga bata sa isang pribadong tahanan.
original_explanation: The superhero without a cape in many Filipino households. She's the one who feeds the kids, helps with homework, and knows all the family chismis. A **yaya** is more than just a nanny; she often becomes a second mother or an 'ate' (older sister) to the children she cares for. She's the real MVP when both parents have to work.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aming **yaya** ay kasama na namin sa pamilya sa loob ng sampung taon.","translation":"Our **nanny** has been with our family for ten years."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang kasangkapang pambahay o komersyal na idinisenyo upang mapanatiling nagyeyelo ang mga pagkain sa pamamagitan ng pagpapanatili ng temperatura na mas mababa sa zero degrees Celsius.
original_explanation: 'Yung part ng ref kung saan nakatira ang ice, hotdog, tocino, at 'yung ulam mula nung Pasko na hindi mo pa rin natatapon. It's the time capsule of your kitchen. Dito rin itinatago ang ice cream para ilayo sa mga kapatid. A sacred space.
usage_notes: A direct loanword, extremely common in everyday language.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakilagay mo naman itong karne sa **freezer** para hindi masira.","translation":"Please put this meat in the **freezer** so it won't spoil."},{"sentence":"Puno na ang **freezer** namin ng ice cream at yelo.","translation":"Our **freezer** is already full of ice cream and ice."}]

translation: to be swarmed by flies; (figurative) deserted, empty
meaning_filipino: Inilalarawan ang isang lugar o bagay na dinudumog o maraming langaw. Sa matalinhagang paraan, nangangahulugang walang katao-tao o walang pumapansin.
original_explanation: Literally, when a place is so fly-infested it could be their kingdom. Figuratively, it's the sad state of your DMs, or that new restaurant that nobody goes to. 'Kumusta ang party?' 'Langawin.' Meaning, it was so dead, the only guests were probably flies. It's the opposite of 'dagsaan'.
usage_notes: The literal meaning is common, but the figurative meaning (empty, unpopular) is also widely understood. Can also be a verb ('nilangaw').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag mong iwanang nakabukas ang basurahan para hindi **langawin**.","translation":"Don't leave the trash can open so it won't be **swarmed by flies**."},{"sentence":"**Nilangaw** ang sinehan dahil hindi maganda ang pelikula.","translation":"The movie theater was **deserted** because the film wasn't good."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paraan ng pagkain nang may malakas na tunog, katulad ng sa isang baboy; pagsubo ng malalaking piraso ng pagkain nang walang-ingat.
original_explanation: How you eat when you're super 'gutom' and no one's watching. Think of someone eating chicharon with gusto. It's messy, it's loud, and it's probably delicious. The opposite of 'fine dining.' Your mom would probably tell you, 'Huwag kang mag-ngubngob, anak!'
usage_notes: Often used as a verb root (e.g., 'ngumungubngob'). As a noun, it refers to the act itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Rinig na rinig ang **ngubngob** niya sa kabilang kwarto habang kumakain ng mansanas.","translation":"His **noisy chewing** could be heard from the other room while he was eating an apple."},{"sentence":"Tigilan mo 'yang pag-**ngubngob** ng buto, nakakairita.","translation":"Stop that **gobbling** of the bone, it's irritating."}]

translation: to contemplate; to reflect upon; to ponder
meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng malalim na pag-iisip o pagsasaalang-alang sa isang bagay; pagnilayan nang mabuti.
original_explanation: This is the active verb form of 'dili-dili'. It's what you do when you're trying to make a big life decision, like whether to accept that job offer abroad or finally break up with your toxic jowa. It's about turning an idea over and over in your mind, weighing the pros and cons until you get a headache or a breakthrough.
usage_notes: A more formal and literary word for 'pag-isipan' (to think about).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **dilidilihin** nang mabuti ang mga pagpipilian mo sa buhay.","translation":"You need **to reflect upon** your life choices carefully."},{"sentence":"Gabi-gabi niyang **dinidilidili** ang kanyang mga nagawang pagkakamali.","translation":"Every night, he **ponders** on the mistakes he has made."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nakikilala ngunit hindi gaanong malapit o matalik na kaibigan.
etymology: From `ka-` + `kilala` (to know, known). The `ka-` prefix here indicates a shared relationship or a fellow person who is known.
original_explanation: This is your "Facebook friend" in real life. You know their name, you might nod at them in the mall, but you don't know their dog's name or their deepest, darkest secrets. They're the people you add on LinkedIn but wouldn't necessarily invite to your birthday party. Not a stranger, but not a BFF either. The in-between zone of social connections.
usage_notes: Differentiated from 'kaibigan' (friend), which implies a closer relationship.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Marami siyang **kakilala** sa industriya, kaya madali siyang nakahanap ng trabaho.","translation":"He has many **acquaintances** in the industry, so he easily found a job."},{"sentence":"Siya ay **kakilala** ko lang, hindi kami matalik na magkaibigan.","translation":"She is just an **acquaintance** of mine, we are not close friends."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang tao o bagay na marumi sa katawan, sa pananamit, o sa pangkalahatang anyo; hindi malinis o marungis.
original_explanation: The opposite of 'kinesa' (clean/smooth). This is your friend who, even after a fresh shower, somehow still looks like they just wrestled in a mud pit. It's the vibe of not knowing how to take care of oneself. "Huy, mag-ayos ka nga, ang dugyutin mo tingnan!"
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **dugyutin** sa iyong pamamahay.","translation":"Don't be **slovenly** in your home."},{"sentence":"Pinagsabihan niya ang bata na ang **dugyutin** ng itsura nito.","translation":"She told the child that his appearance was **filthy**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang panahon o kilos pagkatapos mamitas o mangolekta ng mga bunga, gulay, o anumang tanim. Maaari din itong tumukoy sa paraan ng pag-aani.
original_explanation: This is the "salamat sa ani" moment. Literally, it's what happens after you pick the mangoes from the tree. Figuratively, it's the feeling after payday, when you've "harvested" your salary. It can also mean the result of your hard work, like "pagkaani ng mga pinaghirapan" (after reaping what you've sown).
usage_notes: Can refer to the time immediately after harvesting or the way the harvesting was done.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pagkaani** ng palay, agad itong ibinilad sa araw.","translation":"**After harvesting** the rice stalks, they were immediately dried under the sun."},{"sentence":"Ipinakita niya ang tamang **pagkaani** ng kape.","translation":"He showed the proper **way of harvesting** coffee."}]

translation: To be possessed (by a spirit); to join a group
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagpasok ng isang espiritu sa katawan ng isang tao; o ang pag-anib o pagsali sa isang samahan o grupo.
original_explanation: Has two main vibes. 1) The horror movie kind: when your friend suddenly speaks in a weird voice and asks for a blood sacrifice, they might be 'sinasapian'. 2) The org fair kind: when you finally decide to join that anime club or fraternity, you 'sumasapi' or ask to 'sapian' their group. It's about being entered or entering.
usage_notes: The context is crucial to distinguish between the supernatural and social meanings. The root 'sapi' means 'to join' or 'to affiliate'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang mag-alala, hindi ka **sasapian** ng masamang espiritu dito.","translation":"Don't worry, you won't **be possessed** by an evil spirit here."},{"sentence":"Pinag-iisipan kong **sapian** ang kooperatiba sa aming barangay.","translation":"I am thinking of **joining** the cooperative in our village."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang laruang pampalipad na gawa sa magaan na balangkas na binalutan ng papel o plastik, at pinatataas sa himpapawid sa pamamagitan ng sinulid habang humahangin.
original_explanation: The original Filipino drone. Before DJI, we had the saranggola. Made of bamboo sticks and papel de hapon, it's the ultimate symbol of a carefree Pinoy childhood summer. The goal? Fly it higher than your kalaro's, or better yet, get into a kite fight and cut their string. It's a high-stakes game.
usage_notes: Often associated with summer and childhood games in the Philippines. 'Guryon' is a common synonym.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsama-sama ang mga bata sa bukid upang magpalipad ng **saranggola**.","translation":"The children gathered in the field to fly a **kite**."},{"sentence":"Ang ganda ng disenyo ng **saranggola** ni Pepe, hugis agila ito.","translation":"Pepe's **kite** has a beautiful design, it's shaped like an eagle."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng metal na may paikot na uka at matulis na dulo, ginagamit upang pagkabitin o pagdikitin ang dalawang bagay.
original_explanation: That little metal thingy you need a screwdriver for. It's the reason your IKEA furniture is either a masterpiece or a wobbly disaster. Also, a metaphor for someone with a 'loose screw' (may 'tornilyo sa ulo').
usage_notes: Often used metaphorically to mean someone is crazy or eccentric ('may tornilyo sa utak'). A common variant spelling is 'turnilyo'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan ko ng mas mahabang **tornilyo** para sa estanteng ito.","translation":"I need a longer **screw** for this shelf."},{"sentence":"Humigpit ang **tornilyo** sa bisikleta kaya hindi na umuuga.","translation":"The **screw** on the bike was tightened, so it doesn't wobble anymore."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang elementong kemikal na may simbolong K at atomikong bilang na 19. Ito ay isang mahalagang mineral at electrolyte para sa katawan ng tao.
original_explanation: 'Yung dahilan kung bakit ka pinapakain ng saging ng nanay mo para 'di ka pulikatin. It's that mineral that keeps your muscles from going on strike and your heart beating properly. Think of it as the body's internal powerbank for your cells.
usage_notes: Ito ang Filipinisadong baybay ng elementong kemikal. Ang simbolo nito sa agham ay 'K'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang saging ay isang prutas na mayaman sa **Potasyum**.","translation":"Banana is a fruit that is rich in **Potassium**."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng katawan natin ng sapat na **Potasyum** para sa maayos na paggana ng mga kalamnan.","translation":"Our body needs enough **Potassium** for proper muscle function."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng kawalan ng tiwala o katiyakan tungkol sa isang bagay, tao, o sitwasyon; ang pag-aalinlangan.
original_explanation: This is the default setting of your jowa when you say 'may meeting lang kami.' It's that feeling you get when your friend says 'libre kita,' but you know they left their wallet at home. It's the 'sure ka na ba diyan?' of emotions.
usage_notes: Can express both general doubt and specific suspicion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **magduda** sa kakayahan mo.","translation":"Don't **doubt** your own abilities."},{"sentence":"Nagsimula siyang **magduda** sa asawa niya nang makita niya ang mga text message.","translation":"She started to **suspect** her husband when she saw the text messages."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalaman ng panlilinlang, pandaraya, o hindi katapatan.
original_explanation: That feeling when you lose in a card game and you just *know* someone cheated. Or when the weighing scale at the palengke seems a little too friendly to the vendor. It's the 'scam' in 'scammer,' the 'magic' in 'magic-timbang.' Anything that feels unfair and shady is probably may-daya.
usage_notes: Describes a situation, action, or thing that involves cheating or fraud.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayoko nang sumali sa larong iyan, laging **may-daya**.","translation":"I don't want to join that game anymore, there's always **cheating**."},{"sentence":"Napatunayan na ang transaksyon ay **may-daya**.","translation":"It was proven that the transaction was **fraudulent**."}]

meaning_filipino: Magkaroon ng matinding hidwaan o galit sa isa't isa; hindi magkasundo.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung level up ng `magkaalit`. Hindi na lang 'to simpleng tampuhan. This is full-on "I-unfriend-kita-sa-lahat-ng-social-media" level. When two people are **magkaaway**, they are enemies. May it be over a boy, a girl, a promotion, or the last piece of chicken in the bucket. The drama is real.
usage_notes: A stronger term than 'magkaalit'. It implies a more serious or prolonged state of conflict. Can be used as a verb or an adjective.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Simula noong eleksyon, **magkaaway** na ang magkaibigan.","translation":"Since the election, the friends have **been enemies**."},{"sentence":"Bakit ba laging **magkaaway** ang pusa at aso?","translation":"Why are cats and dogs always **enemies**?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng ligaw na tubo (Saccharum spontaneum) na karaniwang matatagpuan sa mga tabi ng ilog.
original_explanation: Not the tubo you see in haciendas for making sugar. This is the wild cousin, the one that grows freely by the riverbanks, often used for thatching or just being... wild. It's the "talahib" of the sugarcane world.
usage_notes: A botanical term, not common in everyday conversation unless you're a botanist or live in a rural area where it's prevalent.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming tumutubong **pugahan** sa pampang ng ilog.","translation":"There's a lot of **wild sugarcane** growing on the riverbank."}]

meaning_filipino: Usap-usapan o kuwento tungkol sa buhay ng ibang tao na hindi pa kumpirmado ang katotohanan.
original_explanation: The Philippines' unofficial national sport. It's the 'tea', the 'scoop', the 'what's the latest?'. Chismis can range from harmless updates about a neighbor to career-ending scandals. It's the social currency that binds and sometimes breaks communities. Remember: 'It's not chismis if it's true, it's balita (news).' - a chismosa, probably.
usage_notes: Can be used as a verb 'nag-chi-chismis' (gossiping). The person who gossips is a 'chismosa' (female) or 'chismoso' (male). Often spelled as 'tsismis'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ano ang pinakabagong **chismis** tungkol sa mga artista?","translation":"What's the latest **gossip** about the celebrities?"},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maniniwala agad sa **chismis**, alamin mo muna ang totoo.","translation":"Don't believe **rumors** right away, find out the truth first."}]

translation: to be shaken; to be rocked
meaning_filipino: Makaranas ng pag-uga o paggalaw, karaniwan ay dahil sa lindol o malakas na puwersa.
etymology: From `ma-` (prefix indicating ability or potentiality) + `yanig` (tremor, shake).
original_explanation: That feeling when an earthquake hits and you're on the 20th floor. Or, metaphorically, when a huge office scandal breaks out and everyone's job is suddenly on the line. It's about being shaken, literally or figuratively. 'Mayanig sana ang mundo ng mga ex nating 'di nag-effort.'
usage_notes: Often used in the context of earthquakes (`lindol`) but can also be used metaphorically for shocking events.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsigawan ang mga tao nang **mayanig** ang buong gusali.","translation":"The people screamed when the whole building **was shaken**."},{"sentence":"Maaaring **mayanig** ang kanyang posisyon sa kumpanya dahil sa isyu.","translation":"His position in the company might **be rocked** because of the issue."}]

meaning_filipino: Walang tiyak na anyo, hugis, o porma.
original_explanation: Like a blob, a cloud, or me after the Christmas holidays. It describes something that lacks a defined shape or structure. Pwedeng abstract, like a plan that has no details, or literal, like a very loose, oversized 'daster'.
usage_notes: Can be used for physical objects or abstract ideas.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang putik ay isang masang **walang-hubog** bago ito gawing banga.","translation":"The clay is a **shapeless** mass before it is turned into a jar."},{"sentence":"Sa simula, ang kanyang mga ideya ay tila **walang-hubog** at magulo.","translation":"At first, his ideas seemed **formless** and chaotic."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagbibigay ng suporta, asistensya, o saklolo sa isang tao o gawain.
original_explanation: The OG 'bayanihan' spirit in verb form. This is what you do when your friend is moving apartments, or when your officemate is drowning in deadlines. It’s a simple act of kindness, but sometimes people say 'Huwag kang mag-alala, tutulong ako,' then they just watch you suffer. That's called 'drawing'.
usage_notes: A general verb for helping. For mutual help, 'magtulungan' or 'magtulung-tulong' is more common.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **magtulong** sa mga nasalanta ng bagyo.","translation":"I want to **help** the typhoon victims."},{"sentence":"Sino ang pwedeng **magtulong** sa akin na buhatin ito?","translation":"Who can **help** me lift this?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang elementong kemikal na may simbolong Li at atomikong bilang na 3. Ito ay isang malambot, kulay-pilak na puting alkali metal.
original_explanation: The power source of your life. Literally. It's in your phone battery, your laptop battery, your power bank. Kung wala ang Lityum, back to Nokia 3310 days tayo. It's the silent MVP that keeps your digital life and chismis group chats running.
usage_notes: Isinusulat na may malaking titik sa simula bilang pangalan ng elemento, ngunit maaaring maliliit na titik sa pangkalahatang paggamit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang mga baterya na gawa sa **Lityum** ay mas matagal gamitin kaysa sa mga luma.","translation":"Batteries made of **Lithium** last longer than the old ones."}]

meaning_filipino: 1. Tumutukoy sa bagay na may mataas na presyo o halaga. 2. Naglalarawan ng matinding pagmamahal, pagpapahalaga, o pagtingin sa isang tao.
etymology: Ang dalawang kahulugan, "dear" at "expensive," ay magkaugnay, katulad sa salitang Ingles na 'dear'. Ang isang bagay na may malaking halaga (expensive) ay kadalasang itinuturing na mahal (dear).
original_explanation: The most versatile word for your wallet and your heart. One 'mahal' drains your bank account (e.g., 'Ang mahal ng iPhone!'), the other fills your heart (e.g., 'Mahal kong nanay'). Sometimes, the person who is 'mahal' to you is also 'mahal' to maintain. #TheStruggleIsReal
usage_notes: Ang konteksto ang susi upang maiba ang dalawang kahulugan. Ang kahulugang pampinansyal ay ginagamit sa komersyo, habang ang emosyonal na kahulugan ay ginagamit sa mga relasyon.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **mahal** ang lahat ng bilihin pagkatapos ng bagyo.","translation":"All the goods became **expensive** after the storm."},{"sentence":"Siya ang aking **mahal** na kaibigan mula pa pagkabata.","translation":"She is my **dear** friend since childhood."}]

translation: to be burnt to a crisp; to be charred
meaning_filipino: Maging ganap na sunog hanggang sa umitim at maging kahawig ng uling.
original_explanation: What happens to your toast when you forget it in the toaster oven. Or what happens to your skin when you stay at the beach from 10 AM to 3 PM without sunscreen. It's the ultimate "sunog" level, beyond golden brown. Used for overcooked food, severe sunburn, or things completely destroyed by fire.
usage_notes: An idiomatic expression used to describe something that has been severely burned.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naiwan niya ang sinaing sa kalan kaya ito ay **naging uling**.","translation":"She left the rice cooking on the stove so it **was burnt to a crisp**."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat ka sa apoy, baka **maging uling** ang bahay.","translation":"Be careful with the fire, the house might **turn to charcoal** (be completely burned down)."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang indibidwal na napatunayang nagkasala o may pananagutan sa isang pangyayari.
original_explanation: The person everyone points at when the WiFi suddenly dies. Sila yung 'salarin', 'the chosen one' for all the blame. In a group project, sila yung pinag-contribute ng lahat ng sisi.
usage_notes: Often preceded by 'ang' to mean 'the culprit' or 'the guilty party'. The hyphen is often dropped when used as a noun.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hinahanap ng pulisya kung sino ang **maykasalanan** sa krimen.","translation":"The police are looking for the **culprit** of the crime."},{"sentence":"Sa huli, umamin din ang tunay na **maykasalanan**.","translation":"In the end, the real **guilty one** confessed."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kapatid na lalaki ng ama o ina, o ang asawa ng tiya.
etymology: Mula sa salitang 'ama' na may hulaping '-in' na nagpapahiwatig ng relasyon.
original_explanation: The formal, almost literary word for "uncle." You probably call him "Tito" in real life. "Amain" sounds like something you'd read in a Florante at Laura summary for Filipino class. If you call your tito "amain" to his face, he might check if you're feeling okay.
usage_notes: Hindi gaanong karaniwan sa pang-araw-araw na pag-uusap kumpara sa 'tito' o 'tiyo'. Itinuturing itong mas pormal o pampanitikan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang aking **amain** na si Roberto ay kapatid ng aking ina.","translation":"My **uncle** Roberto is my mother's brother."},{"sentence":"Sa kuwentong-bayan, ang masamang **amain** ang nagpahirap sa bida.","translation":"In the folktale, the evil **uncle** was the one who made life difficult for the protagonist."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan o katangian ng pagiging malabo o hindi malinaw.
etymology: Mula sa Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *labuʀ na nangangahulugang 'malabo, maulap'.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung status ng relasyon niyo. Hindi 'in a relationship', hindi 'single', pero may something. The official term for 'ano ba talaga tayo?' Ito rin yung dahilan kung bakit kailangan mo ng bagong salamin sa mata.
usage_notes: Tumutukoy sa mismong estado o kalidad ng pagiging hindi klaro.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa **labo** ng tubig, hindi makita ang mga isda.","translation":"Because of the **murkiness** of the water, the fish cannot be seen."},{"sentence":"Ayoko na sa **labo** ng ating sitwasyon.","translation":"I'm tired of the **obscurity** of our situation."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang relihiyon na batay sa buhay at mga turo ni Hesukristo, na kinikilala bilang anak ng Diyos at tagapagligtas ng sangkatauhan.
etymology: Mula sa salitang 'Kristiyano' at hulaping '-ismo', na hango sa Espanyol na 'cristianismo'.
original_explanation: The OG religion for most Pinoys. It's why you have a Sto. Niño in your car, why Simbang Gabi is a national sport, and why your December is booked with Christmas parties. It's the spiritual backbone of the country, influencing everything from politics to family values.
usage_notes: The standard and formal spelling. 'Kristyanismo' is a common, but less formal, variant.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Malaki ang naging impluwensya ng **Kristiyanismo** sa kultura at kasaysayan ng Pilipinas.","translation":"**Christianity** has had a great influence on the culture and history of the Philippines."}]

translation: to have someone explain; to make something understood
meaning_filipino: Hilingin sa isang tao na ipaliwanag ang isang bagay sa paraang maiintindihan ito ng iba.
original_explanation: The manager's job. When the client's instructions are as clear as mud, you tell your team lead, "Ipaunawa mo nga sa team kung ano talaga ang gusto ng client." It's the act of delegating the task of explaining.
usage_notes: A causative verb focused on the goal of making someone else understand, often by delegating the explanation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **ipaunawa** sa kanila ang bigat ng sitwasyon.","translation":"You need to **make them understand** the gravity of the situation."},{"sentence":"**Ipaunawa** mo sa akin kung bakit ito nangyari.","translation":"**Have someone explain** to me why this happened. (Or: Make me understand why this happened.)"}]

meaning_filipino: Oras na inilalaan ng isang tao para sa kanyang sarili, malayo sa mga tungkulin at stress, para sa pagpapahinga at personal na kasiyahan.
etymology: Direct loan phrase from English "me time".
original_explanation: That glorious, sacred period when you can finally mute the group chat, ignore your emails, and just binge-watch Netflix without anyone asking you for anything. It's self-care 101, whether that means going to the spa, reading a book, or just staring at the ceiling and questioning your life choices. Essential for surviving the BPO night shift or a week of deadlines.
usage_notes: Used ubiquitously in modern Taglish conversation to refer to personal relaxation time.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng exam week, kailangan ko talaga ng **me time**.","translation":"After exam week, I really need some **me time**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na nagsisikap na mapabilang sa mas mataas na antas ng lipunan, kadalasan sa pamamagitan ng pakikipagkaibigan sa mga maimpluwensiyang tao.
etymology: Hango sa pariralang Ingles na "social climber".
original_explanation: That "friend" who suddenly appears when you get a promotion or win the lottery. Sila yung laging present sa mga "alta" party, nagpapa-picture with celebrities, at ginagamit ang connections mo for their own gain. Sila yung nag-a-add sa'yo sa Facebook pag nalaman nilang mayaman ka. Basically, they're climbing the social ladder using other people as steps. A classic character in every Pinoy teleserye.
usage_notes: Madalas na may negatibong konotasyon at ginagamit bilang isang insulto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw siyang kaibiganin ng marami dahil sa tingin nila ay isa siyang **social climber**.","translation":"Many don't want to befriend her because they think she is a **social climber**."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maging **social climber**; mahalin mo ang mga kaibigan mo nang totoo.","translation":"Don't be a **social climber**; love your friends genuinely."}]

translation: to be internalized; to be taken to heart
meaning_filipino: Maisapuso o maisaisip nang malalim ang isang aral, damdamin, o karanasan.
original_explanation: This is when a lesson or a 'hugot' line hits you so hard it becomes part of your system. When your crush says 'friends lang tayo' and you really, truly, deeply understand and accept it in your soul, you have **napasaloob** the concept of the friend zone. It's to internalize something completely.
usage_notes: Refers to the cognitive and emotional process of making an external idea or feeling an internal part of one's self.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay **mapasaloob** ng bawat isa ang kahalagahan ng pagkakaisa.","translation":"I hope everyone **internalizes** the importance of unity."},{"sentence":"Tila **napasaloob** na niya ang lahat ng sakit na kanyang dinanas.","translation":"It seems he has **taken to heart** all the pain he has experienced."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang estruktura o balangkas na may mga patungan o baitang para sa pagsasalansan o pagpapatong-patong ng mga bagay.
original_explanation: It's that thing you use to organize your life. The shoe rack is a salansanan. The dish rack is a salansanan. That wobbly wooden shelf where your lola puts her plants? Also a salansanan. If you can stack things on it in layers, it's a salansanan. The mortal enemy of clutter.
usage_notes: The noun form of 'salansan' (a pile/stack). 'Salansanan' is the place or tool used for stacking.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ilagay mo ang mga bagong hugas na plato sa **salansanan**.","translation":"Put the newly washed plates on the **rack**."}]

translation: to grope; to feel around for something
meaning_filipino: Ang paghahanap sa isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng pagsalat o paggamit ng kamay, lalo na sa dilim o kapag hindi makakita.
original_explanation: The official verb for when the power goes out (brownout!) and you're trying to find your phone or a candle. It's that awkward, clumsy patting on tables, walls, and floors. You're not seeing, you're *feeling* your way through the world.
usage_notes: Often implies searching in the dark or without the ability to see. It differs from 'kumapkap' which is to frisk a person.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawalan ng kuryente kaya **kumapa** ako sa dilim para hanapin ang flashlight.","translation":"The power went out so I **groped** in the dark to find the flashlight."},{"sentence":"**Kumapa** siya sa loob ng bag niya para sa kanyang mga susi.","translation":"She **felt around** inside her bag for her keys."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtatali o pagbubuklod ng mga bagay nang magkakasama; maaari ring tumukoy sa pagkakaisa ng mga tao para sa isang layunin.
original_explanation: This is tying things together, like a bundle of firewood or a 'walis tingting' (broomstick). Metaphorically, it's about unity. It's the 'Avengers, assemble!' moment for a community or a nation—coming together to be stronger, like a well-made walis tingting that can sweep away all the dirt (or problems).
usage_notes: Used both literally for tying objects (e.g., a wound, a bundle of sticks) and figuratively for uniting people.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang EDSA Revolution ay isang simbolo ng **pagbigkis** ng mga Pilipino.","translation":"The EDSA Revolution is a symbol of the **unification** of Filipinos."},{"sentence":"Ang **pagbigkis** sa mga sugat ay kailangan upang tumigil ang pagdurugo.","translation":"The **binding** of the wounds is necessary to stop the bleeding."}]

meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang bagay, tao, o sitwasyon na nang-aakit, nang-eengganyo, o nag-uudyok na gumawa ng isang bagay, na kadalasan ay mali o hindi dapat. Maaari ring tumukoy sa pagbibiro o pag-aasar.
