original_explanation: That slice of cake when you're on a diet. That "add to cart" button during the 12.12 sale. Or that crush who gives you a smile that makes you question your life choices. It's anything that whispers, "Go on, just one little... it won't hurt." It's a test of your self-control.
usage_notes: Maaaring mangahulugang "nakakaakit" sa seryosong paraan (kasalanan, bisyo) o "mapagbiro" sa isang mapaglarong paraan. Ang konteksto ang susi.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **mapanukso** na alok ng dayuhan ay tinanggihan ng matapat na pulis.","translation":"The **tempting** offer of the foreigner was rejected by the honest cop."},{"sentence":"Mayroon siyang **mapanukso** na ngiti na kinakikiligan ng marami.","translation":"She has a **teasing** smile that many find charming."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa anumang bagay na nauukol, nagmumula, o may kaugnayan sa isang lunsod o siyudad.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `pan-` na nagiging `panl-` dahil sa asimilasyon sa salitang-ugat na `lunsod` (siyudad).
original_explanation: Anything "for the city." Your city hall is a `gusaling panlunsod`. The ordinance against loud karaoke after 10 PM is a `kautusang panlunsod`. It's the official hashtag for anything run by or happening within the city's jurisdiction. #UrbanLiving
usage_notes: Madalas ginagamit bilang pang-uring naglalarawan sa isang pangngalan (hal. `pamahalaang panlunsod` - city government, `kalusugang panlunsod` - city health).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang bagong ordinansa ay isang batas **panlunsod**.","translation":"The new ordinance is a **city** law."},{"sentence":"Ang Sangguniang **Panlunsod** ang nagpasa ng resolusyon.","translation":"The **City** Council passed the resolution."}]

translation: to quarrel with each other, to argue
meaning_filipino: Ang sabay na pagkakaroon ng hidwaan, pagtatalo, o hindi pagkakasundo ng dalawa o higit pang tao.
original_explanation: What happens when two people both want the last piece of lechon, or when siblings fight over the TV remote. **Mag-alitan** is a group activity; you can't do it alone. It's the verbal sparring you see in a heated UAAP game thread, or between *titas* debating the best way to cook sinigang.
usage_notes: This is a reciprocal verb, meaning the action is done by the subjects to each other. It always implies more than one person involved.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Madalas **mag-alitan** ang magkapatid dahil sa maliliit na bagay.","translation":"The siblings often **quarrel with each other** over small things."},{"sentence":"Sinabihan sila ng kanilang ina na tigilan na ang pag-aalitan.","translation":"Their mother told them to stop quarreling."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na piraso ng kahoy, metal, o plastik na ginagamit upang pagdugtungin o patatagin ang dalawang bagay. Sa kolokyal na gamit, ito ay may bulgar na kahulugan para sa ari ng lalaki.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol na "tarugo" (wooden peg, blockhead).
original_explanation: Officially, it's that wooden pin you use to assemble IKEA furniture. Unofficially, and how you'll probably hear it on the street, it's a crass word for a guy's private parts. Context is everything, so don't ask your friendly hardware store staff for a 'tarugo' with a weird smirk.
usage_notes: Ang salita ay may karaniwang bulgar na kahulugan bilang slang. Gamitin nang may pag-iingat.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit ang karpintero ng **tarugo** para pagkabitin ang mga tabla ng silya.","translation":"The carpenter used a **dowel** to connect the chair's wooden planks."},{"sentence":"Mag-ingat sa paggamit ng salitang iyan dahil may bastos na kahulugan ang **tarugo**.","translation":"Be careful in using that word because **tarugo** has a vulgar meaning."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paulit-ulit at sukdulang pagmumura o pagsasabi ng masasamang salita sa isang tao.
original_explanation: This is what happens when you get into a road rage incident in EDSA. It's not just one 'putangina'; it's a whole litany, a creative string of curses delivered with passion. It's the verbal equivalent of a machine gun, used when someone really, REALLY pisses you off. Think angry gamer rage or a customer service call gone horribly wrong.
usage_notes: The 'paka-' prefix and the reduplication of 'mura' both serve to intensify the action, meaning to curse repeatedly and excessively.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Halos **pakamura-murahin** niya ang tsuper na biglang kumabig sa harap niya.","translation":"He almost **cursed out profusely** the driver who suddenly swerved in front of him."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **pakamura-murahin** ang kausap mo sa telepono, kahit gaano ka pa kainis.","translation":"Don't **curse out** the person you're talking to on the phone, no matter how annoyed you are."}]

meaning_filipino: Anumang bagay na ginagamit bilang panakip o pansara sa isang butas o sisidlan.
etymology: Likely a native Austronesian word. Compare with Malay 'tetap' which has a sense of fixing or setting in place.
original_explanation: Not the delicious breakfast food! This is the 'tapa' your lola tells you to find for the boiling pot of adobo. It's the piece of wood you nail over a hole in the wall. It’s the 'pamatong' or 'takip.' If you ask for this 'tapa' in a restaurant, you'll get a very confused look.
usage_notes: The pronunciation is different from the food. For the cover, the stress is on the second syllable: /ta-PA/. For the meat, it's on the first: /TA-pa/.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nawawala ang **tapa** ng kaldero.","translation":"The **lid** of the pot is missing."},{"sentence":"Lagyan mo ng **tapa** ang butas sa pader.","translation":"Put a **patch** on the hole in the wall."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang malaking pangkat ng mga magkakamag-anak na nagmula sa isang ninuno; lipi o pamilya.
original_explanation: Your "angkan" is your squad, but like, the one you're born into. It's your entire family tree, from your lola who makes the best adobo to that tito who only shows up for free food. It's the reason for massive family reunions where you meet "cousins" for the first time. Think of it as your dynasty, even if your only family heirloom is a magic-sing microphone.
usage_notes: Refers to a large, extended family or clan, more formal and broader than 'pamilya'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagmamalaki ng aming **angkan** ang aming mga ninuno.","translation":"Our **clan** is proud of our ancestors."},{"sentence":"Taun-taon, nagkakaroon ng malaking pagtitipon ang **angkan** ng mga Reyes.","translation":"Every year, the Reyes **clan** has a grand reunion."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng ibon na may mahahabang binti at leeg, karaniwang puti ang balahibo, at madalas makita sa mga basang lugar tulad ng bukirin at latian.
original_explanation: The official bird of the rice fields. The elegant, white, long-legged model posing on the back of a carabao. They're the OG 'unbothered, moisturized, in my lane, flourishing' icons of the palayan.
usage_notes: Specifically, the species often seen with carabaos is the Cattle Egret (Bubulcus ibis).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang kawan ng puting **tagak** ang payapang nagpapahinga sa likod ng kalabaw.","translation":"A flock of white **egrets** is peacefully resting on the carabao's back."}]

translation: to have someone take care of something; to safeguard
meaning_filipino: Ipagkatiwala sa iba ang pag-aalaga o pagprotekta sa isang bagay o tao mula sa pinsala o kapahamakan.
original_explanation: This is a command or a plea. 'Paingatan mo ang puso ko,' is the ultimate hugot line. It's what you say when you entrust something valuable to someone—a secret, a pet, your laptop, or your heart. It’s a level up from just 'ingatan'; the 'pa-' adds a sense of having it done by someone, a request for care.
usage_notes: The 'pa- ... -an' affix here means 'to cause care to be applied to something', often by someone else.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Paingatan** mo sana itong mga alahas na pamana pa ng lola.","translation":"Please **take good care of** this jewelry inherited from grandmother."},{"sentence":"Ipinagkatiwala ko sa kanya ang aso ko para **paingatan** habang nasa bakasyon ako.","translation":"I entrusted my dog to him to be **taken care of** while I'm on vacation."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang salitang balbal na baryasyon ng 'pagod,' na nangangahulugang lubos na pagkaramdam ng kapaguran.
etymology: A playful, possibly gay lingo, elongation of 'pagod.'
original_explanation: A more ~extra~ way to say you're tired. It's 'pagod' but with a bit of a dramatic flair. It sounds fancier, like you're not just tired, you're *exhausted, darling*. 'Don't talk to me, I'm so **pagoda** from all the chika.' It's the Tita-of-Manila version of 'pagod.'
usage_notes: Informal and playful. Used to add emphasis or humor to the feeling of being tired. Homonym with the architectural term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ay, **pagoda** na ang lola mo! Dami nating ginawa today.","translation":"Oh, your girl is **tired**! We did so much today."},{"sentence":"After ng 12-hour shift, **pagoda** is an understatement.","translation":"After a 12-hour shift, **tired** is an understatement."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pananakot o pagbabanta upang mapasunod o mapilit ang isang tao na gawin ang isang bagay laban sa kanyang kalooban.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung galawan ng boss mo na dadaan lang sa cubicle mo at tititigan ka, para lang iparamdam na kailangan mo nang mag-overtime. Hindi niya kailangan magsalita, pero ramdam mo 'yung pressure. That's intimidasyon BPO-style.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **intimidasyon** ay isang anyo ng bullying.","translation":"**Intimidation** is a form of bullying."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang magpadala sa **intimidasyon** niya.","translation":"Don't give in to his **intimidation**."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang likido, karaniwan ay tubig, na idinaan sa proseso ng distillation upang alisin ang mga dumi at mineral.
original_explanation: The 'sosyal' water. It's the water that went through a whole spa treatment (boiling, steaming, condensing) to become pure. Your Tita who only drinks 'distilled water' knows what's up. It's the water equivalent of a celebrity who had all impurities removed.
usage_notes: Almost always used as an adjective for water ('tubig na distilada').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Tubig na **distilada** lamang ang iniinom ng sanggol.","translation":"The baby only drinks **distilled** water."},{"sentence":"Kailangan ng **distilada**ng tubig para sa ilang eksperimento sa laboratoryo.","translation":"**Distilled** water is needed for some laboratory experiments."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng sandatang pumuputok na karaniwang isinasanib sa balikat, ginagamit laban sa mga tangke o sasakyang pandigma.
original_explanation: That giant, shoulder-fired weapon you see in action movies that makes things go BOOM. The Filipino spelling is just a direct, phonetic loanword. Not to be confused with 'basura' (trash) or 'suka' (vinegar). Please don't mix them up.
usage_notes: This is a direct loanword and is used in contexts involving military or warfare.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gumamit sila ng **basuka** upang pasabugin ang pader.","translation":"They used a **bazooka** to blow up the wall."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamataas na bahagi o dulo ng isang bundok, burol, o anumang mataas na estruktura o bagay.
etymology: Mula sa Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *taluktuk, na nangangahulugang 'tuktok' o 'rurok'.
original_explanation: This is the top of the mountain! The summit. 'Yung lugar kung saan ka mag-se-selfie after a long, tiring hike to prove na 'naka-akyat' ka. It can also be used figuratively for the peak of your career, the height of your success, or ang taluktok ng katangahan when you text your ex.
usage_notes: Maaaring gamitin para sa literal na bundok at para sa matalinghagang rurok ng tagumpay o anumang kalagayan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nakarating sila sa **taluktok** ng Bundok Apo bago pa sumikat ang araw.","translation":"They reached the **summit** of Mount Apo before sunrise."},{"sentence":"Nasa **taluktok** na siya ng kanyang karera bilang isang mang-aawit.","translation":"She is now at the **peak** of her career as a singer."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang uri ng binurong karne, karaniwang baboy, na may matamis na lasa at mamula-mulang kulay dahil sa atsuwete o food coloring.
etymology: From Spanish 'tocino', which originally means "bacon" or "cured pork belly". The Filipino version evolved into a distinct sweet cured meat.
original_explanation: That iconic red, sweet, and savory pork dish that's a staple in Filipino breakfast. It's the 'To' in 'Tocilog'. Frying it until the sugar caramelizes and the edges get a bit crispy is a national sport.
usage_notes: While pork is the most common, chicken tocino also exists and is widely available.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nag-uwi si nanay ng isang kilong **tocino** mula sa palengke.","translation":"Mom brought home one kilo of **tocino** from the market."},{"sentence":"Ang sikreto sa masarap na **tocino** ay ang tamang pagpapakulo nito bago iprito.","translation":"The secret to delicious **tocino** is to boil it properly before frying."}]

meaning_filipino: Kumuha o sumalok, karaniwan ay tumutukoy sa tubig mula sa isang balon, ilog, o poso.
original_explanation: Before Grab delivery and bottled water, you had to 'kaon' water from the well. It's the act of fetching something, usually a liquid, with a container. It's the provincial life equivalent of a water cooler run. Now it's a rare word, you'd more likely hear 'igib' or just 'kuha'.
usage_notes: Pangunahing ginagamit para sa pagkuha ng tubig. Kasingkahulugan ng 'igib' o 'salok'. Bihirang marinig sa mga urban na lugar.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagising siya nang maaga upang mag-**kaon** ng tubig sa balon.","translation":"He woke up early to **fetch** water from the well."},{"sentence":"Paki-**kaon** mo ako ng isang basong tubig.","translation":"Please **get** me a glass of water."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, karaniwang inumin, na nilagyan ng yelo upang lumamig.
original_explanation: The default setting for any drink order in the Philippines because it's hot 365 days a year. 'Coke, may-yelo.' 'Tubig, may-yelo.' 'Kape, may-yelo.' It's how we survive the tropical heat without melting into a puddle.
usage_notes: Very common in food and beverage contexts. It's the standard way to ask for a cold drink.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas masarap ang juice kapag **may-yelo**.","translation":"Juice is more delicious when it's **iced**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao, bagay, o sitwasyon na misteryoso, palaisipan, o mahirap unawain.
etymology: Mula sa Espanyol/Ingles na "enigma", na mula sa Griyegong "ainigma".
original_explanation: Yung ka-opisina mong tahimik lang pero alam lahat ng chismis. 'Yung babaeng hindi mo maintindihan kung gusto ka ba niya o gusto ka lang niyang utangan. 'Yung plot ng isang Christopher Nolan film. An enigma is a person or thing that's a walking, talking Rubik's cube—nakakaintriga pero nakaka-frustrate din intindihin.
usage_notes: Isang salitang pampanitikan o mas pormal. Hindi karaniwan sa pang-araw-araw na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang biglaang pag-alis ay nananatiling isang **enigma** sa aming lahat.","translation":"His sudden departure remains an **enigma** to us all."},{"sentence":"Isa siyang **enigma**; walang sinuman ang tunay na nakakakilala sa kanya.","translation":"She is an **enigma**; no one truly knows her."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na nahulog mula sa kinalalagyan nito; o sa isang taong hindi nakapasa sa isang pagsusulit, kompetisyon, o pagsubok.
original_explanation: The state of your phone after it slips from your hand (and your heart stops for a second). Also, the feeling when you don't make the cut for a job, a team, or sa puso ng crush mo. 'Laglag sa exam' is a classic student nightmare. It's the universe saying 'Oops, try again.'
usage_notes: Maaaring maging pangngalan (ang bagay na nahulog), pang-uri (naglalarawan sa isang bagay na nahulog), o ugat ng pandiwa (malaglag, ilaglag). Mayroon din itong slang na kahulugan na nahuli o nabisto, lalo na sa mga ilegal na gawain ('laglag-bala').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Maraming **laglag** na bunga ng mangga sa ilalim ng puno.","translation":"There are many **fallen** mango fruits under the tree."},{"sentence":"Nalungkot siya dahil **laglag** siya sa huling panayam para sa trabaho.","translation":"He was sad because he **failed** the final job interview."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong iiwan ang pitaka mo diyan, baka **laglag**-bala ang mangyari sa'yo.","translation":"Don't leave your wallet there, you might become a victim of the **bullet-planting** scheme."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang katangian ng pagiging malalim mag-isip, palagiang nagninilay-nilay sa mga bagay-bagay, o may hilig sa pagninilay.
etymology: Mula sa unlaping `mapag-` (na nagsasaad ng tendensiya) at `dili-dili` (magnilay, mag-isip nang malalim).
original_explanation: This is your friend who stares at their coffee for 10 minutes before drinking, probably contemplating the meaning of life or if they should have gotten a grande instead. Sila yung 'deep' sa grupo, mahilig sa hugot, at laging may philosophical take sa lahat, from traffic to TikTok trends.
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa mga akdang pampanitikan o sa pormal na konteksto.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **mapagdilidili** na manunulat ang kumatha ng nobelang iyon.","translation":"A **contemplative** writer created that novel."},{"sentence":"Sa kanyang pag-iisa sa bundok, naging mas **mapagdilidili** si Anton.","translation":"In his solitude on the mountain, Anton became more **reflective**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sitwasyon o pahayag na naglalaman ng magkasalungat na katotohanan, o kung saan ang resulta ay salungat sa inaasahan.
original_explanation: This is the universe's ultimate 'lol'. It's the traffic enforcer getting a ticket, the fire station burning down, or posting 'I hate social media' on Facebook. It's that moment of cosmic side-eye when what you expect to happen is the exact opposite of what actually goes down. It's the hugot of logic itself.
usage_notes: A literary and philosophical term. Less common in everyday conversation but used in formal writing and academic discussions.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Isang **kabalighuan** na ang pinakamayaman sa nayon ang siya pang pinakamaraming utang.","translation":"It's an **irony** that the richest person in the village is the one with the most debt."},{"sentence":"Pinag-aralan nila ang **kabalighuan** sa tula ni Jose Corazon de Jesus.","translation":"They studied the **paradox** in the poem of Jose Corazon de Jesus."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kalagayan ng pagiging walang saysay, kabuluhan, o layunin.
original_explanation: That existential dread you feel on a Monday morning staring at your work emails. It's when you ask "What's the point?" and the universe just sends you a "seen" receipt. The feeling of doing the same tasks over and over without a clear purpose.
usage_notes: Used in philosophical, psychological, or deeply emotional contexts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naramdaman niya ang **kawalan ng kahulugan** ng kanyang buhay matapos ang trahedya.","translation":"He felt the **meaninglessness** of his life after the tragedy."},{"sentence":"Para sa iba, ang sining na 'abstract' ay tila isang **kawalan ng kahulugan**.","translation":"For some, abstract art seems like a **lack of meaning**."}]

translation: to taste; to experience; to savor
meaning_filipino: Ang maranasan o matikman nang may buong pandama, lalo na ang isang bagay na kaaya-aya o isang tagumpay.
original_explanation: This is more than just tasting food. It's about fully experiencing something, usually something awesome. Think of finally getting your 13th-month pay and feeling that sweet, sweet victory—that's 'malasap ang tagumpay.' Or when you finally eat that Jollibee Chickenjoy after a long diet. You don't just eat it, you *savor* it. You 'malasap' every crispy, juicy bite.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for taste or metaphorically for experiences like victory, freedom, or suffering.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nais niyang **malasap** ang tamis ng tagumpay matapos ang maraming taon ng paghihirap.","translation":"She wants to **taste** the sweetness of victory after many years of hardship."},{"sentence":"Sana'y **malasap** ng lahat ang tunay na kapayapaan.","translation":"May everyone **experience** true peace."}]

meaning_filipino: Nagtataglay ng maraming buhangin o may katangiang tulad ng buhangin.
original_explanation: Describes your shoes, car, and entire house after a weekend trip to the beach. Also, a good description for poorly-cooked rice (kanin) that feels gritty. 'Yung feeling na pag-uwi mo galing beach, mas mabuhangin pa yung kama mo kaysa sa shore.'
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko ang mga **mabuhangin** na dalampasigan ng Palawan.","translation":"I like the **sandy** shores of Palawan."},{"sentence":"Naging **mabuhangin** ang sahig pagkatapos naming maglaro sa labas.","translation":"The floor became **sandy** after we played outside."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkakaroon ng sigla, pagnanais, o malikhaing ideya na gumawa ng isang bagay, karaniwang dulot ng isang tao, pangyayari, o damdamin.
original_explanation: 'Yung feeling na pagkatapos mong manood ng K-drama, gusto mo na ring maging CEO ng isang malaking kumpanya... o kaya humanap ng oppa. Ganyan ka 'pag may crush ka, biglang sinisipag mag-aral o mag-gym. #SanaAllInspired
usage_notes: Ang pambabaeng anyo nito ay 'inspirada', ngunit madalas na ginagamit ang 'inspirado' para sa lahat ng kasarian sa kolokyal na usapan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **inspirado** siyang magsulat ng tula dahil sa ganda ng tanawin.","translation":"He became **inspired** to write a poem because of the beautiful scenery."},{"sentence":"Mukhang **inspirado** ka ngayon, sino ba ang dahilan niyan?","translation":"You look **inspired** today, who's the reason for that?"}]

meaning_filipino: Ang paglalagay ng patong o panloob na suson sa isang bagay para sa proteksyon, disenyo, o dagdag na kapal.
original_explanation: Before you put the hot kaldero on the dining table, your mom shouts, 'Magsapin ka!' It means put something underneath. It's also what you do when you wear an undershirt ('sando') under your uniform. It's the art of adding layers, whether it's a placemat, a coaster, or another layer of clothing.
usage_notes: Can be used for clothing, furniture protection, or even in construction/crafts.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **magsapin** ng dyaryo sa sahig bago ka magpinta.","translation":"You need to **layer** the floor with newspaper before you paint."},{"sentence":"Huwag kalimutang **magsapin** ng karton sa ilalim ng kahon para hindi mabasa.","translation":"Don't forget to **put a lining** of cardboard at the bottom of the box so it doesn't get wet."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamahalaga o pinakamaraming sangkap sa isang lutuin, produkto, o pinaghalong bagay.
original_explanation: This is the star of the dish. For adobo, it's the soy sauce and vinegar. For your 'marites' friend group, it's the 'chismis'. It's the one thing you can't remove, or else the whole thing falls apart or becomes something else entirely.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Toyo at suka ang **pangunahing sangkap** ng adobo.","translation":"Soy sauce and vinegar are the **main ingredients** of adobo."},{"sentence":"Ang tiwala ay ang **pangunahing sangkap** sa isang matatag na relasyon.","translation":"Trust is the **key component** of a stable relationship."}]

translation: to cover one's head or face (with a cloth)
meaning_filipino: Takpan ang ulo at/o mukha gamit ang isang piraso ng tela, belo, kumot, o anumang katulad nito.
original_explanation: The classic move when you see someone you owe money to at the mall. Also when you go out with no makeup and don't want to be seen. It's the original 'incognito mode' before smartphones. Also used traditionally for prayer or to show modesty.
usage_notes: The object used for covering is often a loose piece of cloth, like a shawl ('alampay'), veil ('belo'), or blanket ('kumot').
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagsimulang **magtalukbong** ng belo ang mga babae bago pumasok sa simbahan.","translation":"The women started **to cover their heads** with veils before entering the church."},{"sentence":"Bigla siyang **nagtalukbong** ng kumot nang may kumatok sa pinto.","translation":"She suddenly **covered herself** with a blanket when someone knocked on the door."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang taong maluho, magastos, at walang pag-iingat sa paggamit ng pera o ari-arian.
original_explanation: A 'buhalhal' person treats their sweldo like it's an expiring coupon. They're the friend who orders the most expensive item on the menu, buys things on '3-months-to-pay' they don't need, and whose motto is "YOLO!" before every checkout. They live the 'sana all' lifestyle today, and eat instant noodles for the rest of the month.
usage_notes: A negative descriptor for someone's spending habits.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa pagiging **buhalhal** kaya laging walang natitirang ipon.","translation":"She is known for being **wasteful** that's why she never has any savings left."}]

translation: to regret the loss of; to feel sorry about something wasted
meaning_filipino: Ang maramdaman ang pagkabigo o lungkot dahil sa isang bagay na nasayang, nawala, o hindi nasamantala.
original_explanation: That feeling when you see your ex thriving and you think, "Sana all... sana ako na lang ulit." It's the "what if" that keeps you up at night, the missed opportunity, the sayang moment. Parang 'yung last piece of pizza na hindi mo kinain, tapos kinuha ng iba. You panghinayangan that pizza for the rest of your life.
usage_notes: Often used to express regret over a missed chance or a wasted resource.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Panghinayangan** mo ang mga pagkakataong hindi mo sinubukan.","translation":"You will **regret** the chances you didn't take."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **panghinayangan** ang perang ginastos mo para sa edukasyon.","translation":"Don't **feel sorry about** the money you spent on education."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagsasagawa ng isang pormal na pagtatasa, pagsusuri, o muling pag-aaral sa isang bagay.
original_explanation: The verb form of your pre-exam puyat or your pre-purchase paranoia. Ito 'yung action na "i-check muna natin ang comments" o "basahin ulit natin 'yung chapter 3." Basically, the act of not wanting to fail—whether it's an exam or a bad online purchase.
usage_notes: Pandiwang anyo ng salitang "ribyu".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sige, **ribyuhin** mo muna ang report bago ipasa kay Ma'am.","translation":"Okay, **review** the report first before submitting it to Ma'am."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating **ribyuhin** ang ating mga lumang aralin para sa finals.","translation":"We need to **review** our old lessons for the finals."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagsusuot ng pulseras bilang palamuti sa braso o galanggalangan.
original_explanation: It's the verb form of accessorizing your wrist. Whether it's a friendship bracelet from your bestie, a fancy gold one from your tita from the US, or a beaded one you bought at a beach trip, the act of putting it on is mamulseras. It's the simpler, less dramatic cousin of "mag-alahas" (to wear jewelry).
usage_notes: A less common verb. People are more likely to say "magsusuot ng pulseras" (will wear a bracelet).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahilig siyang **mamulseras** ng iba't ibang kulay para bumagay sa kanyang damit.","translation":"She likes **to wear bracelets** of different colors to match her outfit."},{"sentence":"Hindi ako sanay **mamulseras** dahil nabibigatan ako.","translation":"I'm not used **to wearing a bracelet** because I find it heavy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang makabuo ng isang palagay, hula, o opinyon batay sa hindi kumpletong impormasyon; ang maghinala.
original_explanation: Ito yung 'feeling ko...' or 'I have a hunch...' mo. When you don't have all the facts, but you connect the dots based on what you see. Parang Marites mode: 'Nakita ko si ano may kasamang iba, nasapantaha ko agad na may something.' It's making an educated (or sometimes, very uneducated) guess about a situation. It's the verb form of being a detective in your own mind.
usage_notes: A slightly formal or literary word for 'mahulaan' or 'mahinala'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mula sa kanyang mga kilos, **masasapantaha** mong may problema siya.","translation":"From his actions, you can **surmise** that he has a problem."},{"sentence":"Hindi ko **masapantaha** kung ano ang tunay niyang motibo.","translation":"I cannot **suspect** what his true motive is."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maliit na bintana o lagusan, karaniwang ginagamit sa mga takilya, tanggapan ng gobyerno, o bangko para sa transaksyon.
original_explanation: That small opening where you transact with the world. Paying your Meralco bill, getting a train ticket, renewing your driver's license at LTO – you do it all through a bintanilya. It's the official window of bureaucracy, often with a slightly annoyed person on the other side.
usage_notes: Specifically refers to a small service window, not a general window in a house.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mahaba ang pila sa **bintanilya** ng SSS kaninang umaga.","translation":"The line at the SSS **teller window** was long this morning."},{"sentence":"Idinaan niya ang bayad sa maliit na **bintanilya** ng sinehan.","translation":"He passed the payment through the small **ticket window** of the cinema."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lalaki na mahilig magkalat o makinig sa mga usap-usapan tungkol sa ibang tao.
original_explanation: The male counterpart to the chismosa, proving that gossip knows no gender. He might be a little more subtle, dropping intel during an inuman session or a basketball game. He's the guy who knows the office drama, the political intrigues, and who's getting promoted. The modern version might be called a 'Chismoso Tito' or male 'Marites'.
usage_notes: The female counterpart is 'chismosa'. Often spelled as 'tsismoso'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Akala mo mga babae lang, pero ang dami ring **chismoso** sa opisina.","translation":"You'd think it's only women, but there are also a lot of **male gossipers** in the office."},{"sentence":"Narinig ko lang sa mga **chismoso** sa kanto.","translation":"I just heard it from the **gossipers** at the corner."}]

meaning_filipino: Hindi kayang maabot o makamit, literal man o matalinghaga.
original_explanation: When you're short and the item you need is on the top shelf at the supermarket. Also, your standards, according to your crush. Pangarap na di-abot. That feeling of wanting something (or someone) you know you can't have. #Hugot
usage_notes: Maaaring tumukoy sa pisikal na distansya o sa mga matalinghagang layunin at pangarap.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Para sa isang bata, ang bumbilya sa kisame ay **di-abot**.","translation":"For a child, the lightbulb on the ceiling is **out of reach**."},{"sentence":"Ang pangarap niyang maging astronaut ay tila isang bituing **di-abot**.","translation":"Her dream of becoming an astronaut seems like an **unreachable** star."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagtutupi o pagsasara ng isang bagay sa pamamagitan ng paglalapat ng isang bahagi nito sa ibabaw ng isa pa, na naganap sa nakaraan. Maaari ring tumukoy sa pagsasara ng negosyo o pagsuko.
original_explanation: The past tense of folding something, like your laundry... or your business. "After one month of low sales, nagtiklop na yung milk tea shop sa kanto." It can also mean giving up or backing down in an argument. "Akala ko lalaban pa siya, pero nagtiklop din nung pinakita na yung ebidensya."
usage_notes: Can be used literally for folding objects or figuratively for a business closing down or a person giving up.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **nagtiklop** ng lahat ng damit na nilabhan.","translation":"He/She was the one who **folded** all the washed clothes."},{"sentence":"Dahil sa pandemya, maraming negosyo ang **nagtiklop**.","translation":"Because of the pandemic, many businesses **folded** (closed down)."}]

meaning_filipino: Bigkasin, ipahayag, o ilahad ang isang kaisipan, mensahe, o saloobin.
original_explanation: The verb for when you just gotta let it out. 'Ano'ng gusto mong sabihin?' (What do you want to say?). This is the verb you use for your 'hugot' lines, for confessing your feelings, or for telling your team lead you need a vacation. It focuses on the *message* being delivered.
usage_notes: Focuses on the thing being said. 'Sabihin mo ang totoo' (Tell the truth). Contrasts with 'sabihan', which focuses on the recipient of the message.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang matakot na **sabihin** ang iyong nararamdaman.","translation":"Don't be afraid to **say** what you feel."},{"sentence":"Ano ba ang dapat kong **sabihin** sa kanya pag nagkita kami?","translation":"What should I **say** to him when we see each other?"}]

translation: The act of falling or collapsing
meaning_filipino: Ang kilos o estado ng pagbagsak mula sa pagkakatayo, karaniwan dahil sa kawalan ng balanse, lakas, o suporta.
original_explanation: This is the dramatic fall. Not just a simple trip, but a full-on *bagsak*. Think of a boxer getting knocked out, a building crumbling in an earthquake, or you after seeing your crush with someone else. The 'buwal' part adds that extra oomph of total collapse.
usage_notes: Often used for large objects or a dramatic human fall.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang biglaang **pagkabuwal** ng puno ay nagdulot ng takot sa mga residente.","translation":"The sudden **collapse** of the tree caused fear among the residents."},{"sentence":"Naging sanhi ng kanyang **pagkabuwal** ang sobrang pagod at gutom.","translation":"His **collapse** was caused by extreme fatigue and hunger."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang sabay-sabay at malakas na ingay tulad ng sunod-sunod na putok ng baril, paputok, o ang pag-ungol ng manok (pagputak).
etymology: Mula sa salitang-ugat na "putak", ang tunog na ginagawa ng manok.
original_explanation: The sound of your chismosa titas when they see someone's controversial new boyfriend. It's a sudden, noisy outburst. Can also be the sound of legit gunfire or a series of firecrackers on New Year's Eve. Basically, any rapid 'pok-pok-pok' or 'tska-tska-tska' sound. Think of it as the official soundtrack of Marites.
usage_notes: The meaning depends on the context. It can be the cackling of hens, a volley of gunfire, or even a verbal outburst.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig sa buong baryo ang **putakan** ng mga manok nang may pumasok na ahas sa kulungan.","translation":"The **cackling** of the chickens was heard throughout the village when a snake entered the coop."},{"sentence":"Bigla na lang nagkaroon ng **putakan** ng baril sa kalapit na kanto.","translation":"Suddenly there was a **burst of gunfire** at the nearby corner."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang metaporikal na sukat ng enerhiya ng isang tao para sa pakikisalamuha sa iba.
etymology: Hango sa pariralang Ingles na "social battery".
original_explanation: Your capacity to deal with other humans. Pag full-charge, game ka sa party, chismisan, at family reunion. Pag low-batt, gusto mo na lang mag-hibernate sa kwarto with Netflix and a bag of chips. Para sa mga introvert, mabilis ma-drain ang social battery nila, parang cheap na power bank. "Sorry, 'di ako makakasama, low-batt na ako." is the ultimate Gen Z excuse.
usage_notes: Isang modernong konsepto na popular sa mga nakababatang henerasyon, lalo na sa konteksto ng mental health at introversion.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng buong linggong meeting, ubos na talaga ang **social battery** ko.","translation":"After a whole week of meetings, my **social battery** is completely drained."},{"sentence":"Kailangan kong mag-recharge ng **social battery** ko ngayong weekend.","translation":"I need to recharge my **social battery** this weekend."}]

translation: to bequeath to, to leave an inheritance to
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagbibigay o pag-iiwan ng pamana sa isang tao o pangkat.
etymology: From `pa-` + `mana` + `-han`. The `-han` suffix often denotes location or the recipient of an action.
original_explanation: This is the verb form. It's what your rich tita from the US does in her will. "Pamanahan mo naman ako ng chika, friend!" is the modern version for asking for gossip. It's the action of passing down the goods, whether it's a condo in BGC or your mom's collection of Tupperware.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of wills and testaments. The object of the verb is the person receiving the inheritance.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Pamanahan** mo sana ng kahit kaunting lupa ang iyong mga anak.","translation":"You should **bequeath** even a small piece of land to your children."},{"sentence":"Sino kaya ang **pamanahan** niya ng kanyang malawak na koleksyon ng libro?","translation":"I wonder who he will **leave** his vast book collection **to**."}]

translation: orderly, neat, proper, in good condition
meaning_filipino: Nasa tamang kalagayan, malinis, organisado, o walang anumang gusot o gulo.
etymology: From the prefix 'ma-' (indicating a quality) + 'ayos' (order, arrangement).
original_explanation: Your life when you finally do your laundry, clean your room, and have more than 50 pesos in your wallet before payday. It's the opposite of 'gulo', the state of your friend's love life. 'Ayusin mo buhay mo!' is the command, and 'maayos' is the goal. Can refer to a person ('maayos kausap' - sensible), a place ('maayos na bahay' - tidy house), or a situation ('sana maging maayos na ang lahat' - hope everything will be alright).
usage_notes: A very versatile adjective. 'Maayos na pagkain' means a proper meal. 'Maayos ang isip' means clear-headed or sane.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto ko ng **maayos** na kausap, hindi yung paasa.","translation":"I want someone **proper** to talk to, not someone who leads me on."},{"sentence":"Pakilagay ang mga libro sa isang **maayos** na hilera.","translation":"Please put the books in a **neat** row."},{"sentence":"Siguraduhin mong **maayos** ang sasakyan bago tayo umalis.","translation":"Make sure the car is in **good condition** before we leave."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagpapawalang-bisa, pagtigil, o pag-urong sa isang kasunduan, plano, o kaganapan.
original_explanation: That moment when your friend texts "OTW na!" but 5 minutes later, you get the dreaded "Sorry, 'di na ako tuloy." That's the kanselasyon of your friendship. Also, the feeling when your flight gets cancelled and you're stuck at NAIA.
usage_notes: Commonly used in formal and informal contexts, from flight cancellations to cancelling plans with friends.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa masamang panahon, nag-anunsyo sila ng **kanselasyon** ng lahat ng klase.","translation":"Due to the bad weather, they announced the **cancellation** of all classes."},{"sentence":"Ang biglaang **kanselasyon** ng konsiyerto ay ikinadismaya ng mga tagahanga.","translation":"The sudden **cancellation** of the concert disappointed the fans."}]

meaning_filipino: Kaskasin o kudkurin ang balat gamit ang mga kuko, karaniwan upang maibsan ang kati.
original_explanation: The verb you do when a mosquito bites you and you can't take the itchiness anymore. Or what your cat does to the sofa when you're not looking. 'Huwag mong kamutin 'yan, magsusugat!' (Don't scratch that, it will become a wound!)
usage_notes: This is the object-focus form. The actor-focus form is 'kumamot'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Gusto kong **kamutin** ang likod ko dahil sa kati.","translation":"I want **to scratch** my back because it's itchy."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **kamutin** 'yang kagat ng lamok.","translation":"Don't **scratch** that mosquito bite."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang mababa at nagbabantang tunog na ginagawa ng isang hayop, tulad ng aso, bilang babala.
original_explanation: "Angil" is the sound your aspin makes right before it decides your visitor's ankles look suspicious. It's the animal equivalent of "Subukan mo lang." Figuratively, it's the low, threatening tone your boss uses before asking why you were late again. It's a warning that something's about to go down.
usage_notes: Primarily used for animals, but can be used figuratively for humans showing anger. The verb form is 'umangil' (to growl).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **angil** ng aso sa labas kaya hindi ako lumabas ng bahay.","translation":"I heard the dog's **growl** outside so I didn't leave the house."},{"sentence":"Isang mahinang **angil** ang kumawala sa kanyang lalamunan nang makita ang karibal.","translation":"A low **growl** escaped his throat when he saw his rival."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang nakakahawang sakit na viral na nagdudulot ng pamamaga ng mga glandula ng laway, lalo na ang mga parotid gland sa magkabilang gilid ng mukha.
etymology: Hindi tiyak, posibleng may kaugnayan sa ibang mga salita sa Austronesian para sa pamamaga.
original_explanation: Ito yung sakit na ginagawang chipmunk o siopao ang mukha mo. Yung parang nag-ipon ka ng sama ng loob sa magkabilang panga. Usually, dinadaan lang sa pahinga at bawal maligo (sabi ng mga lola). The OG face filter before Snapchat.
usage_notes: Isang karaniwang termino para sa kondisyong medikal na mumps. Minsan ay tinatawag ding 'beke'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Nagkaroon ng **biki** si Ana kaya hindi siya nakapasok sa eskwela.","translation":"Ana had the **mumps** so she couldn't go to school."},{"sentence":"Pinayuhan ng doktor na magpahinga ang batang may **biki**.","translation":"The doctor advised the child with **mumps** to rest."}]

translation: to be beaten to it; to be preempted
meaning_filipino: Malampasan o magawa ng iba ang isang bagay bago pa man magkaroon ng pagkakataong gawin ito.
etymology: From 'una' (first), with the 'ma- -han' affix creating a verb meaning 'to have something done to you first by another'.
original_explanation: The ultimate "sayang" moment. Like when you were about to ask your crush out, but your friend got to them first. Or when you saw the last seat on the MRT, but someone faster snagged it. It's the "na-seen-zone ka na, na-unfriend ka pa" of life's little competitions, from getting the last piece of chicken to getting that promotion. You snooze, you lose.
usage_notes: Implies a competition or a race against time, whether explicit or implicit.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Akmang bibili na ako ng tiket, pero **naunahan** ako ng babae sa pila.","translation":"I was about to buy a ticket, but the woman in line **got to it before** me."},{"sentence":"Mag-isip ka na ng bagong idea para hindi ka **maunahan** ng kalaban mong kumpanya.","translation":"Think of a new idea so you won't **be preempted** by your rival company."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang karaniwang matamis at makatas na produkto ng isang puno o halaman na naglalaman ng buto at maaaring kainin bilang pagkain.
original_explanation: The healthy stuff your mom forces you to eat. From the saging in your baon to the mangga you pair with bagoong. Also, a term of endearment, "Hi, prutas!"... wait, no, that's not right. Just stick to the edible kind.
usage_notes: Ginagamit bilang pang-isahang pangngalan sa Tagalog, sa kabila ng pinagmulan nitong pangmaramihan sa Espanyol. Upang gawing pangmaramihan, sinasabing "mga prutas".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kumain ka ng **prutas** araw-araw para maging malusog.","translation":"Eat **fruit** every day to be healthy."},{"sentence":"Paborito kong **prutas** ang mangga.","translation":"My favorite **fruit** is mango."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang estetika sa internet na nagroromantisa sa buhay sa kanayunan, na nagtatampok ng mga simpleng gawain tulad ng paghahardin, pagbe-bake, at paggawa ng mga kagamitang pangkamay.
original_explanation: Yung pangarap mong iwanan ang magulong siyudad at manirahan sa isang maliit na bahay kubo sa probinsya, pero make it aesthetic. May kasamang pagbe-bake ng tinapay, pag-aalaga ng halaman, at pagsusuot ng flowy dress. Basically, your "plantita" dreams on steroids.
usage_notes: An internet aesthetic popular among younger generations.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Naging **cottagecore** ang feed ko sa Instagram dahil sa dami ng tanim kong bulaklak.","translation":"My Instagram feed has become **cottagecore** because of the many flowers I planted."},{"sentence":"Ang pangarap niya ay isang **cottagecore** na buhay, malayo sa stress ng trabaho.","translation":"Her dream is a **cottagecore** life, far from the stress of work."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang walang-tigil at malakas na pagsasalita, karaniwang nagpapahayag ng galit, reklamo, o pag-sermon.
etymology: From "bunganga" (a large, cavernous mouth, often used pejoratively).
original_explanation: Ah, the classic soundtrack to a Filipino childhood. This is your mom's final form when you haven't cleaned your room or when your dad comes home late. It's a verbal machine gun of complaints, sermons, and 'noong panahon namin...' stories. It's basically a one-person TED Talk on everything you're doing wrong, powered by love and frustration.
usage_notes: Highly informal and somewhat pejorative, implying loud and incessant talking.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Rinig sa buong bahay ang **pagbubunganga** ni Aling Nena sa kanyang asawa.","translation":"Aling Nena's **nagging** at her husband could be heard throughout the house."},{"sentence":"Tigilan mo na ang **pagbubunganga** mo, wala namang nakikinig sa'yo.","translation":"Stop your **ranting**, nobody is listening to you anyway."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang inumin na gawa sa katas ng mga prutas o gulay.
original_explanation: That colorful liquid in a pitcher at every Pinoy party, usually next to the Red Horse and Coke. It's often a super-sweet powder mix (pineapple or orange flavor, for sure) that you just add water to. The "healthy" option your mom insists you drink before letting you have soft drinks. Also, a slang for gossip ("What's the juice?").
usage_notes: Widely used and understood. Can also refer to gossip or inside information in a slang context, borrowed from English.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Paki-abot ng pitsel ng pineapple **juice**.","translation":"Please pass the pitcher of pineapple **juice**."},{"sentence":"Mas masarap ang **juice** kung sariwang prutas ang ginamit.","translation":"**Juice** is more delicious if fresh fruit is used."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kabuuan ng mundo, kasama ang lahat ng bansa, tao, at bagay na naririto; ang uniberso.
original_explanation: That feeling when your crush ghosts you and your whole world collapses. 'Gumuho ang aking sandaigdigan!' It's also what you promise your jowa during the honeymoon phase: 'Ibibigay ko sa'yo ang sandaigdigan.'
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa mga pampanitikan o pormal na konteksto para sa "buong mundo."
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang pag-ibig ay isang wika na naiintindihan sa **sandaigdigan**.","translation":"Love is a language understood throughout the **whole world**."},{"sentence":"Nais niyang maglakbay sa buong **sandaigdigan**.","translation":"He wants to travel the entire **world**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang anak na babae ng iyong anak.
original_explanation: She's lola's favorite fashion model for the new dress she just sewed and lolo's little princess. She holds the family's collective heart in her tiny hands.
usage_notes: The standard way to specify the gender of a grandchild.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ipinagmamalaki ng lolo ang kanyang **apong babae** na nagtapos na may karangalan.","translation":"The grandfather is proud of his **granddaughter** who graduated with honors."}]

translation: please reduce the price; a little less
meaning_filipino: Isang pakiusap na bawasan ang halaga, dami, o bigat ng isang bagay.
original_explanation: The national anthem of the Filipino palengke-goer. It's the hopeful question you ask the tindera after she names the price. "Pabawas naman, ate!" It's a mix of haggling, charm, and a silent prayer. Success means you walk away feeling like a financial genius. Failure means you just pay the original price. No harm in trying!
usage_notes: Used as a request, often in a market or transactional setting. It's the verb form of asking for a 'tawad' (discount).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ate, sampung kilo kukunin ko, **pabawas** naman sa presyo.","translation":"Miss, I'll take ten kilos, **please reduce** the price a bit."},{"sentence":"Suki, wala na bang **pabawas** 'yan?","translation":"Regular customer, can't you give a **discount** on that anymore?"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na may ugaling bawiin ang isang bagay na naibigay na, maging ito man ay materyal na bagay, salita, o pangako.
original_explanation: This is your friend who gives you a gift for your birthday, but after a fight, says 'Akin na 'yang binigay ko sa'yo!' It's also that ex who asks for the Netflix password back after you break up. The opposite of a cheerful giver.
usage_notes: Can also be the future tense of the verb `mambawi` (to take back), but is commonly used as a noun to describe a person with this trait. The negative connotation is strong.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayokong makipagkaibigan sa taong **mambabawi**.","translation":"I don't want to be friends with someone **who takes back what they've given**."},{"sentence":"Kilala siya sa pagiging **mambabawi** ng mga pangako.","translation":"He is known as **one who takes back** his promises."}]

translation: Act of beating someone up; mauling
meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng paulit-ulit at malupit na pananakit o paghampas sa isang tao o hayop.
etymology: From 'pang-' (used to form nouns of action) + 'gulpe', from Spanish 'golpe' (a hit/blow).
original_explanation: This is what happens in action movies when the main character is outnumbered 10 to 1. It's the act of a severe beatdown. Think less of a single "suntok" and more of a sustained, brutal attack. It's the noun form of "gulpihin." Also, what you feel like doing to your laptop when it crashes before you save your work.
usage_notes: A strong word indicating severe physical violence.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang biktima ay nagtamo ng maraming pasa dahil sa **panggugulpe** ng mga salarin.","translation":"The victim sustained many bruises from the **mauling** by the culprits."},{"sentence":"Kinondena ng lahat ang nag-viral na video ng **panggugulpe** sa isang matanda.","translation":"Everyone condemned the viral video of the **beating** of an old person."}]

meaning_filipino: Isama o ihalo ang isang sangkap sa isang lutuin o timpla, karaniwan bilang karagdagang pampalasa o pampakapal.
etymology: From the prefix 'i-' (causative verb marker) and 'bahog' (a mix, usually for animal feed, extended to human food).
original_explanation: The culinary equivalent of 'it's complicated.' When you **ibahog** something, you're mixing it into the main dish. Think of adding cheese to your instant noodles or chismis to a friendly conversation. Once it's in there, it's part of the whole delicious (or disastrous) mess.
usage_notes: Primarily used in cooking. It implies mixing something into a larger mixture, often something wet or semi-solid, to become an integral part of it.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Ibahog** mo na ang itlog sa binabating harina.","translation":"**Mix in** the egg into the flour batter."},{"sentence":"Masarap kung may kaunting giniling na karneng **ibabahog** sa sopas.","translation":"It's delicious if there's a little ground meat to be **mixed into** the soup."}]

translation: to be choked; to be strangled
meaning_filipino: Mahirapan sa paghinga o mamatay dahil sa pagkakabara o pagkakadiin sa lalamunan o leeg.
original_explanation: Literally, what happens when you eat too fast and the food goes down the wrong pipe. Figuratively, it's how you feel when your boss gives you three urgent tasks at 4:59 PM on a Friday. 'Nasasakal ako sa dami ng utang!' It's the feeling of being suffocated, by a person, a situation, or a piece of chicken.
usage_notes: Can be used literally for physical choking or figuratively for feeling suffocated or overwhelmed by a situation. Completed aspect is 'nasakal'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Muntik nang **masakal** ang bata sa kinakain niyang candy.","translation":"The child was almost **choked** by the candy he was eating."},{"sentence":"Pakiramdam niya ay **nasasakal** na siya sa sobrang pagiging selosa ng kanyang nobya.","translation":"He feels like he is **being suffocated** by his girlfriend's extreme jealousy."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang akto ng pagtatabas o pagpuputol ng mga sanga, dahon, o sobrang bahagi ng isang halaman upang mapabuti ang paglago nito.
original_explanation: It's like tidying up a plant's 'haircut' so it grows better. Or when you 'unfollow' toxic people from your social media feed to improve your mental health. You're trimming the unnecessary.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of gardening and agriculture.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagpapalispis** ng mga lumang dahon ay kailangan para sa malusog na puno ng mangga.","translation":"The **pruning** of old leaves is necessary for a healthy mango tree."}]

translation: to be surprised; to be startled
meaning_filipino: Makaranas ng biglaang pagkabigla o pagkagimbal dahil sa isang hindi inaasahang pangyayari.
original_explanation: The feeling when your phone bill arrives. Or when your crush suddenly messages you. Or when someone sneaks up behind you and yells. It's that "OMG!" moment, the sudden intake of breath, the widening of the eyes. Can be good-surprised or bad-surprised.
usage_notes: This is a patient-focus verb. The actor-focus equivalent is "manggulat" (to surprise someone).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Nagulat** ako sa bigla mong pagdating.","translation":"I **was surprised** by your sudden arrival."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang maingay para hindi siya **magulat**.","translation":"Don't be noisy so that he won't **be startled**."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pamamaga ng malaking bituka (colon), na maaaring magdulot ng pananakit ng tiyan, pagtatae, at dugo sa dumi.
original_explanation: Ito 'yung LBM na nag-level up. Hindi lang basta masakit ang tiyan, may 'inflammation' na. Parang 'yung relationship niyo, hindi lang away-bati, 'inflamed' na at kailangan na ng seryosong intervention. If you have kolitis, you need a doctor, not just Diatabs.
usage_notes: A specific medical term.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang stress ay maaaring magpalala ng sintomas ng **kolitis**.","translation":"Stress can worsen the symptoms of **colitis**."},{"sentence":"Pinayuhan siya ng doktor na magbago ng dieta dahil sa kanyang **kolitis**.","translation":"The doctor advised him to change his diet because of his **colitis**."}]

translation: to roll up (like a mat or paper)
meaning_filipino: Ang pagrorolyo o pag-ikid ng isang bagay, tulad ng banig, papel, o tela, upang maging silindriko ang hugis.
original_explanation: That satisfying feeling of rolling up a poster you just bought, or the banig (sleeping mat) after your tita from the province visits. It's the action of turning something flat into a tube. Think lumpia wrapper before frying.
usage_notes: Distinct from 'magbilog' (to make round/spherical). 'Magbilot' means to make into a roll/cylinder.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pagkatapos ng piknik, nagsimula na kaming **magbilot** ng aming banig.","translation":"After the picnic, we started to **roll up** our mat."},{"sentence":"Maingat niyang sinimulang **magbilot** ng lumang mapa na kanyang natagpuan.","translation":"He carefully started to **roll up** the old map he found."}]

translation: to make a mistake; to err
meaning_filipino: Gumawa ng pagkakamali o maging mali sa isang pasya, kilos, o pahayag.
original_explanation: Happens when you reply "ok po" to your boss but you actually sent it to your ex. Or when you confidently answer a question in class, only to be corrected by the teacher. It's the universe's way of saying "Oops, try again!" Tao lang, nagkakamali.
usage_notes: The 'magka-' prefix here denotes an unintentional or accidental action.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Patawarin mo ako, **nagkamali** ako ng hatol sa iyo.","translation":"Forgive me, I **made a mistake** in judging you."},{"sentence":"Kahit sinong matalino ay maaaring **magkamali**.","translation":"Even any smart person can **make a mistake**."}]

meaning_filipino: Gawing walang bisa, saysay, o legal na batayan ang isang bagay tulad ng kasunduan, dokumento, o damdamin.
original_explanation: This is what you do to someone's argument when you pull out the receipts. O kaya yung ginagawa ng HR sa sick leave mo kung wala kang medical certificate. Biglang "Sorry, but your feelings/claims/excuses are not valid here." It's the official "cancel" button for anything formal.
usage_notes: Karaniwang ginagamit sa mga pormal o teknikal na konteksto tulad ng batas, kontrata, o proseso sa opisina. Popular din sa social media para tukuyin ang pagbalewala sa damdamin ng iba.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kailangan mong **i-invalidate** ang lumang ticket para makakuha ng bago.","translation":"You need to **invalidate** the old ticket to get a new one."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong hayaang **i-invalidate** ng iba ang nararamdaman mo.","translation":"Don't let others **invalidate** your feelings."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na gumaganap sa entablado, sa pelikula, o sa telebisyon; isang taong lumilikha ng sining, tulad ng pintor o iskultor.
original_explanation: In the Philippines, this almost always means "celebrity" or "actor/actress." The person you see on billboards, in teleseryes, or in noontime shows. While it *can* mean a painter or sculptor (the "fine arts" kind), 99% of the time, when a Pinoy says "artista," they're talking about someone who's probably been in a love team.
usage_notes: In Philippine colloquial usage, it overwhelmingly refers to a screen or stage performer rather than a visual artist. The term is gender-neutral.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pangarap niyang maging isang sikat na **artista** balang araw.","translation":"She dreams of becoming a famous **actress** someday."},{"sentence":"Maraming **artista** ang dumalo sa premiere night ng pelikula.","translation":"Many **celebrities** attended the movie's premiere night."}]

meaning_filipino: Mahusay at malinaw magpahayag ng mga ideya; may kakayahang manghikayat o magpaliwanag nang epektibo sa pamamagitan ng pananalita.
original_explanation: 'Yung kaklase mo na laging class president kasi ang galing niyang mambola sa teacher. Or that officemate who nails every client presentation. Sila 'yung mabuting magsalita. They can sell ice to an Eskimo, or in a local context, convince you to buy another piece of life insurance you don't need.
usage_notes: Describes a person's skill in public speaking or conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang pinili naming lider dahil siya ay **mabuting magsalita** at kayang ipaglaban ang aming mga karapatan.","translation":"We chose her as our leader because she is **a good speaker** and can fight for our rights."},{"sentence":"Kailangan mong maging **mabuting magsalita** kung gusto mong maging isang politiko.","translation":"You need to be **eloquent** if you want to become a politician."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang nakikitang masa ng mga maliliit na patak ng tubig o kristal ng yelo na nakalutang sa atmospera.
original_explanation: The original 'cloud storage' before it was cool. In the Philippines, it's the thing you stare at while daydreaming, the thing that tells you if uulan ng malakas (it will rain hard) or if it's a perfect beach day. It's also where your head is when you're in love or 'lutang' (spaced out) during a meeting. 'Nasa alapaap' is the OG Filipino way of saying you're on cloud nine.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Puting-puti ang mga **ulap** sa langit.","translation":"The **clouds** in the sky are very white."},{"sentence":"Mukhang uulan dahil maitim ang **ulap**.","translation":"It looks like it will rain because the **clouds** are dark."}]

translation: to be disturbed; to be bothered
meaning_filipino: Makaranas ng pagkaabala o pagkagambala mula sa isang tao o pangyayari.
etymology: From `ma-` (potential/accidental prefix) + `istorbo`, which is from Spanish `estorbo` (hindrance, nuisance).
original_explanation: That moment when you're in a deep focus state at work, and someone asks "Busy ka?" Bro, if you have to ask, the answer is yes, and you just proved it. "Pasensya na kung maistorbo kita, pero kailangan ko 'to for the report." It's the polite Filipino way of interrupting someone.
usage_notes: Can be used in both potential ("Pwede ba kitang maistorbo?") and accidental ("Naku, naistorbo kita.") contexts. The prefix 'ma-' here signifies either an ability to disturb or the state of being disturbed.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ayaw kong **maistorbo** ang tulog niya kaya dahan-dahan akong pumasok.","translation":"I didn't want **to disturb** his sleep, so I entered quietly."},{"sentence":"Paumanhin kung ikaw ay aking **naistorbo**.","translation":"My apologies if I **disturbed** you."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tala o paliwanag na inilalagay sa ibabang bahagi ng isang pahina, karaniwang tumutukoy sa isang partikular na bahagi ng teksto sa itaas.
original_explanation: The fine print of your life's thesis. It's that extra info your prof requires you to add to prove you didn't just copy-paste from Wikipedia. In conversations, it's the 'nga pala...' or 'by the way...' that adds crucial, often juicy, context.
usage_notes: A compound word from 'tala' (record) and 'baba' (low). Used in academic writing, legal documents, and formal reports.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pakitingnan ang **talababa** para sa pinagkunan ng datos.","translation":"Please see the **footnote** for the source of the data."},{"sentence":"Nakalimutan kong ilagay ang **talababa** sa aking research paper.","translation":"I forgot to put the **footnote** in my research paper."}]

meaning_filipino: Nasa kabaligtarang posisyon; ang itaas ay nasa ibaba, ang loob ay nasa labas, o ang unahan ay nasa likuran.
original_explanation: Yung t-shirt mo na sinuot mo nang nagmamadali para sa 8 AM Zoom call, tapos sa kalagitnaan ng meeting, sinabi ng boss mo na **baliktad** pala. It's also the state of the world when chismis is treated as fact, and facts are dismissed as chismis. Everything's just... upside down.
usage_notes: Can be spelled as 'baligtad'. It is very versatile and can describe physical orientation (upside down, inside out) or a reversed situation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Natawa ang lahat nang mapansin nilang **baliktad** ang suot niyang medyas.","translation":"Everyone laughed when they noticed he was wearing his socks **inside out**."},{"sentence":"Teka, **baliktad** yata ang pagkakabit mo ng mapa.","translation":"Wait, I think you put the map up **upside down**."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang pagpapahayag ng kawalan ng kasiyahan, pagtutol, o reklamo, karaniwang sa mahinang boses o sa paraang nagpapakita ng pag-aatubili.
original_explanation: This is the low-key grumble you make when your boss gives you another task at 4:59 PM on a Friday. It's not a full-blown "reklamo" (formal complaint), but a muttered "Hay nako..." under your breath. It’s the sound of silent protest, the "reklamo ng mga duwag." When your mom asks you to wash the dishes and you sigh heavily, 'yan ang angal.
usage_notes: Madalas na nagpapahiwatig ng isang pabulong o paungol na reklamo sa halip na isang pormal. Ang anyong pandiwa nito ay "umangal".
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Wala akong narinig na **angal** mula sa kanya, kaya akala ko ayos lang.","translation":"I didn't hear any **complaint** from him, so I thought it was okay."},{"sentence":"Tigil na sa ka-a-**angal** at gawin mo na lang ang trabaho mo.","translation":"Stop **grumbling** and just do your job."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang sesyon ng pagsasanay o paghahanda para sa isang pagtatanghal, presentasyon, o anumang gawain na nangangailangan ng pag-eensayo.
original_explanation: The official term for 'practice.' That thing you do before the actual presentation, the dance number for the Christmas party, or the big performance. It's the time for all the mistakes, missed cues, and 'isa pa, isa pa!' moments. The more chaotic the ensayo, the better the final performance... hopefully.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May **ensayo** kami para sa dula mamayang hapon.","translation":"We have a **rehearsal** for the play this afternoon."},{"sentence":"Kailangan nating pagbutihin ang ating **ensayo** para manalo sa kompetisyon.","translation":"We need to improve our **practice** to win the competition."}]

translation: having many eggs; full of roe
meaning_filipino: Naglalarawan sa isang isda, alimango, o iba pang hayop na may maraming itlog sa loob ng katawan.
original_explanation: The highest praise you can give an alimango (crab) at a dampa restaurant. "Uy, tignan mo, maitlog!" means you hit the jackpot. It's the crab equivalent of being thicc and rich. You know it's gonna be a good, cholesterol-heavy meal.
usage_notes: Primarily used in a culinary context to describe seafood like fish, crabs, and shrimp that are bearing eggs (roe), which is often considered a delicacy.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mas mahal ang alimangong **maitlog** kaysa sa karaniwan.","translation":"A crab that is **full of roe** is more expensive than a regular one."},{"sentence":"Pumili ka ng isdang **maitlog** para mas masarap ang sinigang.","translation":"Choose a fish that is **full of eggs** so the sinigang will be more delicious."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang tao na dumaranas ng karamdaman o anumang uri ng diperensya sa kanyang atay.
original_explanation: Medically, it's a serious condition like hepatitis or cirrhosis. Culturally, it's what your Tita might diagnose you with if you're always irritable or 'mainitin ang ulo' (hot-headed). Based on old humoral theories, the liver was linked to anger, so being 'liverish' meant being grumpy. 'Lagi kang galit, baka may sakit ka sa atay!'
usage_notes: Can be a literal medical diagnosis or a figurative expression for someone who is perpetually angry or irritable.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Pinayuhan ng doktor ang pasyenteng **may-sakit sa atay** na iwasan ang mga matatabang pagkain.","translation":"The doctor advised the patient **with liver disease** to avoid fatty foods."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang maikling yugto ng panahon; saglit.
original_explanation: The Filipino unit of time that can mean anything from an actual second to 'I'll get to it when I feel like it.' When someone says 'Sandali lang,' you better grab a snack. It's the polite way of saying 'Hold up, I'm in the middle of something' (like finishing a level of Mobile Legends).
usage_notes: Madalas gamitin sa mga pariralang "Sandali lang" (Just a moment) o "Teka sandali" (Wait a moment).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Sandali** lang, may kinukuha lang ako sa loob ng bahay.","translation":"Just **a moment**, I'm just getting something inside the house."},{"sentence":"Maghintay ka ng **sandali** at darating na ako.","translation":"Wait for **a short while** and I'll be there."}]

translation: to oppose, to contradict, to go against
meaning_filipino: Ang pagkontra, pagtutol, o pagsuway sa isang utos, batas, o pananaw. Ito ay isang mas pormal o pampanitikang katumbas ng 'sumalansang'.
original_explanation: This is the spirit of your inner 'kontrabida' when your boss gives a terrible idea in a meeting, and you just have to speak up. It's going against the flow, like swimming upstream in a river of 'oo na lang po'. It is a slightly more formal, almost poetic version of the more common 'sumalansang'.
usage_notes: A more formal or literary term for 'to oppose'. 'Sumalansang' is more commonly used in modern conversation.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang kanyang mga ideya ay **sumalangsang** sa nakagawian ng kumpanya.","translation":"His ideas **went against** the company's traditions."},{"sentence":"Huwag kang **sumalangsang** sa payo ng iyong mga magulang.","translation":"Do not **go against** the advice of your parents."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pinakamataas na antas na naaabot ng tubig-dagat sa dalampasigan; ang pagtaas ng tubig.
original_explanation: The ocean's daily glow-up. It's when the sea comes closer to your beach blanket, forcing you to move your stuff unless you want your chichirya to get soggy. The opposite of 'hibas' (low tide).
usage_notes: Ang kasalungat nito ay 'kati' (low tide). Madalas na maling nababaybay bilang 'taeb'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Mamayang hapon pa ang **taib**, kaya mababa pa ang tubig.","translation":"The **high tide** isn't until this afternoon, so the water is still low."},{"sentence":"Nag-aabang ang mga mangingisda sa pagdating ng **taib**.","translation":"The fishermen are waiting for the **high tide** to come in."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang proseso ng paghihiwalay o pag-aalis sa pagkakasama-sama ng mga tao, bagay, o ideya.
original_explanation: Ito yung LDR stage ng relationship niyo, pero on a more formal, almost biblical level. Parang Moses separating the Red Sea. Hindi lang basta "hiwalay," may kasamang finality. Pwede ring paghihiwalay ng magkakadikit na pagkain, like separating conjoined hotdogs.
usage_notes: A more formal and less common word for separation than 'paghihiwalay'.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **pagbunlag** ng mag-asawa ay nagdulot ng kalungkutan sa kanilang mga anak.","translation":"The **separation** of the couple brought sadness to their children."},{"sentence":"Naging mahirap ang **pagbunlag** sa magkakadikit na pahina ng lumang libro.","translation":"The **separation** of the stuck pages of the old book was difficult."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang maramihang anyo ng "BFF," tumutukoy sa isang grupo ng pinakamatalik na magkakaibigan.
original_explanation: When your squad is so tight, you're not just a 'tropa' or 'barkada', you're BFFs. This is the group chat that never sleeps, the people you plan out-of-town trips with that never happen, and the ones who will roast you but fight anyone else who tries.
usage_notes: Ginagamit upang tumukoy sa isang grupo ng dalawa o higit pang matatalik na magkaibigan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Kaming tatlo ay **bffs** at laging magkasama.","translation":"The three of us are **bffs** and are always together."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang pagkuha at paggamit ng mga armas upang lumaban, mag-aklas, o ipagtanggol ang sarili; paglulunsad ng armadong pakikibaka.
original_explanation: This is the historical drama/RPG hero moment. When peaceful protests fail and the oppressed have had enough, they *sumamsam ng sandata*. It's the transition from dialogue to action, from holding placards to holding bolos or rifles. It's the "Let's get ready to rumble!" of a revolution.
usage_notes: A formal and somewhat literary phrase used to describe rebellion, revolution, or armed struggle.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Dahil sa pang-aapi, napilitan ang mga katutubong **sumamsam ng sandata** laban sa mga mananakop.","translation":"Because of oppression, the natives were forced **to take up arms** against the colonizers."},{"sentence":"Ito ang sigaw ng mga rebolusyonaryo: '**Sumamsam ng sandata** at ipaglaban ang kalayaan!'","translation":"This is the cry of the revolutionaries: '**Take up arms** and fight for freedom!'"}]

meaning_filipino: Isang lihim na salita o parirala na ginagamit bilang pagkakakilanlan o para makapasok sa isang lugar, grupo, o sistema.
etymology: Mula sa Italyano na 'parola' (word), na ginamit sa konteksto ng militar bilang 'watchword'. Naiiba sa Espanyol na 'farola' (lighthouse).
original_explanation: Before '123456' became your WiFi password, this was the OG password. 'Yung secret code niyo ng tropa para malaman kung sino ang kasama sa team at sino ang espiya. 'Anong **parola**?' 'Langit.' 'Sige, pasok!'
usage_notes: Ang paggamit na ito ay mas bihira na ngayon para sa mga digital password (kung saan 'password' ang ginagamit) ngunit naiintindihan pa rin sa konteksto ng mga lihim na code, mga salita sa militar, o sa mga akdang pampanitikan/pangkasaysayan.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Hiningi ng bantay ang **parola** bago sila pinapasok sa kampo.","translation":"The guard asked for the **password** before letting them into the camp."},{"sentence":"'Pag-ibig' ang **parola** ng mga rebolusyonaryo.","translation":"'Love' was the **watchword** of the revolutionaries."}]

meaning_filipino: Ang kilos ng pagpapahayag ng saloobin, impormasyon, o utos sa isang tao. Ito ay nasa aspektong perpektibo o naganap na.
original_explanation: The source of all chismis. "Sino **nagsabi**?" is the national question before believing any juicy gossip. It's the past tense of spilling the tea.
usage_notes: The completed aspect of 'magsabi'. Often interchangeable with 'sinabi', but 'nagsabi' focuses more on the person who initiated the act of saying.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Siya ang **nagsabi** sa akin na may pagpupulong ngayon.","translation":"He/She was the one who **told** me there's a meeting today."},{"sentence":"**Nagsabi** na ako kay nanay na uuwi ako nang late.","translation":"I already **told** mom that I would be coming home late."}]

translation: to come true; to be true to one's word
meaning_filipino: Ang pagiging totoo o ang pagsasakatuparan ng isang bagay na sinabi, ipinangako, o hinulaan.
original_explanation: When your horoscope says you'll receive unexpected money and you find 20 pesos in your old jeans—that's "nag-totoo"! It's when a prediction, a promise, or a dream becomes reality. Also means to be true to yourself or your word. "Sana magtotoo lahat ng New Year's resolutions ko this time."
usage_notes: Can refer to a prophecy/dream coming true or a person being truthful.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Sana ay **magtotoo** ang lahat ng iyong mga hiling sa kaarawan mo.","translation":"I hope all your birthday wishes **come true**."},{"sentence":"Bilang isang lider, mahalagang **magtotoo** ka sa iyong mga pangako.","translation":"As a leader, it's important that you **be true** to your promises."}]

meaning_filipino: Tumutukoy sa isang bagay na kinuha o sinamsam ng isang taong may awtoridad bilang parusa o dahil sa paglabag sa isang patakaran.
original_explanation: What happens to your phone when you're caught playing Mobile Legends in class. It's the fate of the oversized 'bagoong' jar in your luggage at the airport. Kompiskado means 'it's mine now,' said the teacher/guard/customs officer. You're not getting it back without a 'pakiusap' session or a parent.
usage_notes: Used as an adjective to describe a state. The verb form is 'kinompiska' (confiscated by someone) or 'magkompiska' (to confiscate).
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Kompiskado** ang mga pekeng produkto na ibinebenta sa bangketa.","translation":"The fake products being sold on the sidewalk were **confiscated**."},{"sentence":"Lahat ng laruan niya ay **kompiskado** dahil hindi siya nag-aral.","translation":"All his toys were **confiscated** because he didn't study."}]

translation: the manner of staring; the way one stares
meaning_filipino: Ang paraan o tagal ng pagtingin nang tuwid at walang kurap sa isang bagay o tao.
original_explanation: That intense, unblinking stare. It's how you look at your crush from across the room, how your boss looks at you when you're late, or how you look at the last piece of lechon. It's not just a glance; it's a full-on, high-definition, sometimes-creepy, sometimes-romantic stare. The 'pagkaka-' implies the specific way it's done—was it a loving stare, an angry one?
usage_notes: 'Pagkakatitig' emphasizes the quality or manner of the stare, while 'pagtitig' is the act of staring itself.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"May kahulugan ang **pagkakatitig** niya sa akin kanina sa kantina.","translation":"There was meaning in the **way he stared** at me earlier in the canteen."},{"sentence":"Nakakatakot ang **pagkakatitig** ng pusa sa madilim na sulok.","translation":"The **stare** of the cat at the dark corner is scary."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang bagay, lugar, o punto na pinupuntirya o nais tamaan, lalo na sa pag-asinta gamit ang pana, baril, o anumang ipinupukol.
original_explanation: Your 'tudlaan' is your goal, your crush's heart, or the last piece of chicken joy at the dinner table. It's what you're aiming for, whether it's hitting your sales quota or successfully landing a witty comeback in an argument. 'Yung bullseye sa dartboard ng buhay mo.
usage_notes: Often used in the context of shooting, archery, or figuratively, for goals and objectives.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Ang **tudlaan** ng pana ay ang pinakagitna ng bilog.","translation":"The **target** of the arrow is the very center of the circle."},{"sentence":"Ikaw ang naging **tudlaan** ng lahat ng biro niya kahapon.","translation":"You became the **target** of all his jokes yesterday."}]

translation: to get tired of; to be fed up with
meaning_filipino: Ang makaramdam ng pagkainis, pagkabagot, o pagkasuya sa isang bagay, tao, o sitwasyon dahil sa paulit-ulit na karanasan.
original_explanation: 'Yung paulit-ulit na lang 'yung ulam niyo for one week. Adobo Monday, Adobo Tuesday... by Friday, for sure **nanawa** ka na. "Ma, iba naman please!" Or 'yung kaibigan mong puro na lang hugot about sa ex niya. Nakakasawa, bes. That feeling is 'umay' or 'manawa'.
usage_notes: Synonymous with 'magsawa'. 'Manawa' can sometimes feel slightly more formal or literary.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Huwag kang **manawa** na gumawa ng mabuti sa iyong kapwa.","translation":"Don't **get tired of** doing good to others."},{"sentence":"**Nanawa** na ako sa kaniyang mga walang katapusang dahilan.","translation":"I've **gotten fed up with** his endless excuses."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang partikular na pag-uusap, kasunduan, o ang paksang pinag-uusapan ng dalawa o higit pang tao.
original_explanation: This is the actual chismis session. It's the 'So, anong latest?' It can be a simple chat with friends over coffee, or a serious 'We need to talk' moment with your S.O. It can also mean a deal or agreement, like 'Ang usapan natin, 8 AM, 'di ba? Anong oras na?' (Our agreement was 8 AM, right? What time is it now?). The ultimate Filipino time-check.
usage_notes: Very common. Can mean the act of conversation, the topic, or a prior agreement.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"Narinig ko ang **usapan** nila tungkol sa bagong manager.","translation":"I overheard their **conversation** about the new manager."},{"sentence":"Tuparin mo ang **usapan** natin, ha?","translation":"Fulfill our **agreement**, okay?"}]

translation: To add to; to mix in
meaning_filipino: Ang pandiwa ng pagdaragdag o paghahalo ng isang bagay sa isang umiiral na timpla o grupo.
original_explanation: The command form of adding something. It's your mom telling you, 'Lahukan mo ng patis 'yang sinigang.' Or your friend at a party saying, 'Lahukan mo na kami dito sa kwentuhan!' It's the action of adding an element to a bigger thing.
usage_notes: This is a verb form derived from the root 'lahok', typically used in the imperative mood.
usage_examples: [{"sentence":"**Lahukan** mo ng kaunting asukal ang kape para tumamis.","translation":"**Add** a little sugar to the coffee to make it sweet."},{"sentence":"Huwag mong **lahukan** ng personal na isyu ang usapang trabaho.","translation":"Don't **mix in** personal issues with work matters."}]

meaning_filipino: Isang panulat, lalo na ang mga lumang uri na gumagamit ng balahibo ng ibon (quill) o ang mga modernong 'fountain pen' na may tinta. Sa pangkalahatan, tumutukoy sa anumang uri ng panulat.
